评语:
Decided to come to the Public Market for lunch. This was my first time here, and was kind of overwhelmed by the choices. First saw the ice cream and wanted to go there, but I guess we had to eat lunch first. After walking around, Empty Bowl looked the most promising. 

This place is smack dab in the middle of the Marketplace and has limited bar seating. So if you plan on eating here, you may have to wait a bit for people to leave. If not, you can always order to go. I hope it's common knowledge that you shouldn't sit and chat after you've finished your meal ^_^

I ordered the Pad Thai. It came out nicely plated and I couldn't wait to dig in. They give you a fork, but there are tins of chopsticks on the bar. My dish was delicious.. not too sweet and the noodles had a good texture. The peanuts, spice, and bean sprouts are served on the side of the dish, so you can add to your liking. Obviously, I added everything except the additional bean sprouts. The Pad Thai was tasty and I wanted to eat it all! (I didn't and took home a doggy bag). 

While you wait for your food, you can watch the employees behind the bar. A guy was making Thai Tea right in front of us, which prompted a discussion about my mother wanting to try and make Thai Tea. The employees were super nice and friendly. 

It's no mystery that you should visit the ice cream place after you've finished your delicious meal here.

I'm only giving this place one star because I have to. 
When going there over the weekend we were the only customers in the entire place. When receiving the service we did we quickly realized why. There are 6 or more tvs in the establishment and we asked the manager Austin if he would put the baseball game on for us. He said no in the rudest and most unprofessional way and when asked if it was because he for some reason couldn't or if it was just simply because he didn't want to? His response was he just didn't want to. My friends and I said back that we would just leave then, after already had ordered drinks and food, so we couldn't even leave right away. He didn't try to make anything better just shrugged his shoulders and said ' I don't care, leave then.' We literally felt like we were in the presence of high schoolers at a home gathering rather than a business talking to a professional.... 
Our server that was working there was silent during all of this and never even came to check on us once after ordering, just avoided us all, and being that we were the only customers you can imagine how obvious this was. 
I finally managed to get his attention and asked for the names of the restaurant owner and the manager. And after giving me the owners name and the managers name he said quickly after, "But if you're thinking about writing a bad review its just going to be a complete waste of time, the owner Matt and the manager Austin have been best friends since kindergarten." 
So after he said that, and after I looked them up to write a review I see that this advice is most likely true. I should have known by all the horrible reviews and the fact we were the only customers there during dinner rush time, that it was most likely not a great place to go. 
I've never experienced such immaturity and unprofessionalism like this from a business ever in my life. 
My friends and I will never be returning.

Gangchu chicken and beer is a cool hang out concept utilizing the popular Korean fried chicken craze! They also have a few "bar" type Korean food - bulgogi, bulgogi cheesesteak, rice cakes, ban Chan etc.

Service 5/5: our hostess and server were great! We were sat immediately and our server was very friendly / knowledgeable!

Cocktail 5/5: Clifton was so good! Citrus soju and gin work so well each other. seventh sun collaborated with gangchu to create K-hop which was refreshing and paired great with chicken.

Food 2/5: lots of kinks to still work out. We got the gojuchang Buffalo sauce on the boneless wings and they were complete mush. Nothing was crispy. I've had Korean fried chicken in Ktown in NYC, Orlando, etc- typically it's double fried and hot (temperature wise) and this was luke warm and the skin was soggy. We got the yuzu pepper on the bone in wings and that was slightly crispier but still needs work. Loved the yuzu pepper sauce though! We received our last order which was the kimchi fried rice and it came out cold. They apologized and gave us a brand new order/Compensated us which we appreciated. 
Lastly their ban Chan was interesting.. Kimchi was watered down and the bean sprouts were chopped into little bite size pieces - it tasted like mush. 

Overall, would come back for the yuzu pepper sauce. Maybe in a few months when the food improves and the kitchen get more training...loved the concept and menu ideas but execution was lacking.

Worst bakery ever. The bakery is filthy and the cupcakes are stale. While I was there, I saw a roach run across the floor. I left immediately. I recommend you try one of the other bakeries in the area. I have never had a worse experience with a bakery. And to add to it all, the staff are extremely rude! Grab a box mix cake and make it at home. At least it won't be stale and baked in filthy conditions.

This review is specifically about happy hour.  If you offer happy hour, and accept a reservation from a happy hour Meetup group, you need to be flexible. 
Upon arrival, on a Quiet Thursday evening, you won't seat part of a group of 20 until half arrive. Accepted. Went to the Patio Bar. (It's 95 Degrees, no problem, but also, no crowd) Bartenders Super, drinks well made and reasonably priced. Great Job. We achieve a quorum and get seated. Sorry! No split checks.  Unacceptable. It's 2017. We've been to 50 bars and restaurants in the Philly burbs and this is the ONLY one that refused.  No problem. We'll order from the bar, pay as we go and MAKE IT EASY FOR THEM. Sorry, No. You can't order from the bar and bring it to a table.  "Can we speak to a manager?"  Out comes the Wicked Witch of the East.  WE HAVE RULES!  WTF. You can accommodate separate checks and food orders at the bar but not at tables 10 feet away?  Sorry. We all left. If it weren't for the great bar service, this would be a 1 star.

I really wanted to love this place and support their reopening but I just can't. Burgers were cooked incorrectly and it was very expensive in my opinion. $50 for three burgers (one a child's) and baked potatoes is a bit much. If you want anything on your potato you pay for every topping which is excessive. The patties are very thick and when over cooked it's hard to eat. I'm usually willing to give restaurants a few tries (especially when they are first opening) but not for their prices.

As I was outside almost around the corner leaving the premises a guy in regular clothes comes up to me and asks me for my wrist band.  I was a bit confused and said no thanks buddy and said im leaving bye.  He then yelled at me to give him my wrist band.  When I said no im leaving again he yoked me up against the wall and 2 other guys came over and put me in a restraint, picked me up and tossed me to the sidewalk.  These guys are in fact employees of mad river.  They have absolutely no right to touch me especially when I am not inside of their establishment.  Even if I was they have no right to put their hands on me.  Why and how this is tolerated and accepted by most people is beyond me.

This is unacceptable and I will be going to the proper authorities to make my complaint.

Geno's Steaks are A-OK!

Having missed Geno's the first time I vacationed in Philly, I knew i had to make it there this time around. As a tourist- I wanted to try Geno's. As a Yelper- I realized there were probably better options in town. I had to try for myself. 

Of all the cheesesteaks I tried in Philly, Geno's packed the least punch. It seemed light on the steak, light on the cheese, and heavy on the bread. HOWEVER, it was still a tasty ass cheesesteak and deserves at least 3 Stars!! You Philly Yelpers have it so lucky if you consider Geno's to be on the lower end of the 'cheesesteak totem pole'- because I'd love to have a place like Geno's where I'm from!

Overall A-OK, light on the steak, light on the cheese, tourist destination #1.

Pat's Steaks were damn good.

As a tourist, I did the rounds of several major cheesesteak spots and can say I thoroughly enjoyed Pat's. Their cheesesteaks were packed! The meat was chopped and packed thick- and it was dripping cheesy goodness! I'm not from Philly, so I can say this without any bias- Pat's was legit.

I'm aware that Pat's is considered a tourist cheesesteak shop, but this is one tourist shop I'll keep coming back to. Out of all the cheesesteaks I tried in Philly, this one was the fattest and cheesiest- I loved it.

Searching Yelp for somewhere to have dinner and I stumbled across DD Mau and after reading several reviews, decided I had to give them a try. And, I'm super glad that I did!  It's a bright and airy restaurant that is more "fast casual" than full service restaurant. I was warmly welcomed by both women working the front and they happily answered all of my questions and then I asked one to recommend a Bao bun & Pho. She recommended the pork as the best bun and the special Pho (rare beef, brisket & meatballs). She was SO on point! That was the best Bao bun ever. Soft & pillowy and filled to the brim with juicy pork & toppings and I chose spicy mayo as the icing on top. Could not love it more. 

I can honestly say that their Pho is also amazing. The broth is deeply flavorful without being too salty and I normally add a ton of hoisin & chili, but this broth really didn't need it. I added just a bit of each along with the usual accoutrements- fresh bean sprouts, fresh Thai basil, cilantro & lime.  Portions are huge so I have more than enough for lunch tomorrow too. Sweet! 

Lastly, I had the iced Matcha Green Tea Latte and it was good, but a tad too grassy for me. More Latte, less Matcha for me next time. I like a more subtle flavor, but if you like it strong you'll love it.  

A lot of people came in for take out as well, so it seems like they are doing really well for a 1 year old business. Can't wait to bring friends here! I'm craving another pork Bao Bun already. LOL!
the chai tea is made with a powder mix... i could feel the powder in my mouth with each sip. i paid $5.50 for that shit!!!!

I don't normally write reviews because anywhere I go to with high reviews on Yelp is worth it, but this was the worst service I've ever experience. (And I travel a lot). Our server completely ignored us and had a horrible attitude. The place wasn't even crowded. 

There are so many great places in Nashville, so don't waste your time here. If I could review 0 stars I would have. So disappointed. Never coming back.

(Note: written on take-out only experience during COVID-19 social distancing measures.) 

I went to The Parish years ago for a friend's birthday and remembered enjoying it a lot, and had been meaning to go back for ages. Obviously, the current shut-down of dining in at restaurants put a wrench in that plan, but last night I ordered take-out to treat my parents (one of whom is a hospital worker) to a socially-distant but delicious meal. 

I'm in what I've taken to calling "quaranTREAT YO SELF" mode, so I went all in on multiple appetizers along with my dinner. The Hushpuppies are perfect -- slightly sweet, buttery, balls of absolute happiness. The dipping sauce that comes with them is great as well and provides a slightly herbacious tang. The Black & Blue Brussels are delicious as well! The glaze on them is a lovely blend of sweet and subtly spicy, and the candied pecans provide little crunchy nuggets of additional sweetness. 

For my entree, I got the Drunken Angel (angel hair with crawfish and shrimp in a saffron red pepper cream sauce). It's so rich and satisfying! I particularly enjoyed the way the flavors came together when sopping up the sauce with some garlic bread. My parents ordered the Smokin' Angel (angel hair with spinach, goat cheese, and garlic in a smoked tomato sauce) and the Shrimp & Grits (shrimp in Creole BBQ sauce on white cheddar grits with greens). Though I wasn't able to try their dishes, both enjoyed their meal a great deal. Both enthusiastically praised the bright, bold flavors and hearty portions. We all agreed that we'd love to dine in with them as soon as we're able! 

On top of the great food, I really appreciate what they're doing to support the community during this time with discounts for a number of groups including healthcare workers, first responders, grocery-store workers, and more. They will definitely have my continued patronage!

(Note #2: I don't have any photos because I didn't feel like a take-out container is a fair representation of how their dishes would usually look.)

Wow -- one visit was enough to make me a Kiwami Ramen devotee! 

I got the Kiwami Kuro, which is their signature pork broth ramen with black garlic oil. The ramen has pork char siu, egg, mushrooms, bamboo, bean sprouts, scallions, and, of course, noodles. The broth is intensely rich and flavorful, but still light enough to sip without feeling greasy or heavy. The pork is also very well-seasoned and tender, which I enjoyed a lot. I thought it was some the best in-ramen pork I've had!

Along with the various ramens, they also have rice bowls and poke, both of which I plan to try soon. For appetizers, they offer steam buns, gyoza, takoyaki, and more. 

I also like that they have a drive-through! It's a unique bonus feature that feels ideal for social distancing.

This is without question the best brewery in Nashville. We did our best brewery crawl, and TBW was by far and a away the best spot. They use local ingredients to make sure their beers are representative of Tennessee. Also, the food is amazing. Just like the ingredient for beer, they make sure the food is locally sourced and delicious.

Very lovely and cozy place next to a museum in downtown Santa Barbara. It is actually among many other wine tasting rooms in that little alley. This one is out in the front, very easy to spot.

There was this little cute dog in there, she is unbelievably adorable! It was amazing she doesn't run out at all, just stands at the front door and ppl watching, very well trained dog, so lovely!

Mostly they have red tastings, I can't drink red wines, so I just ordered a glass of white, hubby had two whites and two reds tasting. We sat at the sofa bench in the corner, so relaxing in a late afternoon. We enjoyed our wine tasting time so much, I picked a candle too, it smells so nice, I am loving it. 

A pleasant wine tasting experience, I especially loved how they made a tasting room look like a home, it makes ppl just want to spend so much time there to try different kind of wines. Too bad I am not a fan of wines, or I would have stayed longer and tried more wines. 

Ps. They wave the $15 tasting fee if you purchase 2 bottles of wines, or remember to check in on yelp for 5% off one single purchase!

A little drama coming here for our birthday dinner, our reservation was canceled after I called to confirm in the afternoon, said something went wrong on open table. But they finally managed to squeeze us in anyways, handled it very professionally, great job! 

A small French restaurant, the seatings were really cramped, but our corner booth was kind of private. Brought our own Moet champagne, they waved cork and cake cutting fee as the nice gesture to make it up for messing up the reservation. Well technically it wasn't entirely their fault. Menu was simple and neat, very easy to order. A few bottles of Badoit sparking water to sip on while deciding on what to eat. 

For starters we shared special tomato salad, French onion bread bowl soup, two orders of crab cakes and Pan seared foie gras. Crab cakes were one of the best, we all loved it. Tomato salad was very fresh and tasty. Only hubby loved that savory foie gras, it melted in his mouth right away, so soft and buttery. Chef made us something like crostini with goat cheese and fruit on it, they were very yummy. 

For entrees we had ribeye in medium rare and rare plus, Mary's chicken with risotto, sea bass with shrimps and yellowfin tuna in rare. Ribeye was cooked to perfection, especially hubby's rare plus, the sauce was bomb. My tuna was so fresh and light, loved the olives in it. Sister loved her chicken, just the risotto was a bit salty. Parents didn't like the sea bass too much, said it was a bit hard and bland. I had a few bites, I liked it for some reason. 

Food portions were pretty big for French food, prices were fair. The service was over the top, our server was very friendly and attentive. We had our own birthday cake as dessert to end the pleasant birthday dinner. 

Everything was PERFECT, we enjoyed this family dining experience so much!

FOR EVERY MINUTE YOU WAIT, IT IS WORTH EVERY BITE YOU TAKE.
That should be the motto for Ruby Slipper Cafe.

A recommendation from my good friend Gina P. from Yelp Fort Lauderdale that Ruby Slippers Cafe is the BEST breakfast place in the French Quarter, but beware of long lines!!!  She was right on both fronts!!!

Regarding the line,  my wife and I had learned once we got to the hostess stand which is just right in the doorway for the restaurant with a lovely, patient hostess, that you can either put your name in at the door or use the Yelp App to put your name in and track where you are in line to be seated.  We put our name in with the hostess and used the Yelp App to track where we were in line to get seated.

As we were waiting I had a chance to look inside.  Plenty of seating, but quite the busy place. A large U shaped breakfast bar in the middle, surrounded by 2 top tables on the left and a larger dining room to the right of the bar with 4 top tables and booths. There is also outdoor seating in the front and side of the restaurant. 

After looking at the menu, and seeing the great breakfast dishes all around me, I can definitely see what all the hype is all about. People were PATIENTLY waiting outside like this was "the attraction". And it certainly was.

When our name was called, we thankfully got seated a the breakfast bar which I preferred.  There is a lot to see sitting there and recommend it if you can wait for that.  We were greeted by our vibrant and friendly server, Nicole C. (she never gave us her last name) when I asked.  We immediately knew she was from the midwest and had some fun with that when talking to her.

Coffee Anyone?  Here, like many places in New Orleans, they have the BEST coffee.  We had to have the NOLA roasted coffee which was served in the special Ruby Slippers red Coffee Mugs.  Delicious.

Just looking at the Specials for the day posted on the Specials Board,  which included Spiced Pumpkin Pancakes and Nutella & Raspberry French Toast and looking at the menu, this was going to be a tough choice.  The choices of 7 different "Eggs Traodianary" Eggs Benedict dishes and "Momma can't make this" Specialties alone had my head spinning.  At least my wife was with me so we could both order something different and share.  

It was no surprise that she ordered the Spiced Pumpkin Pancakes. There was no doubt that I was going to choose one of the Benedict dishes, but I was torn between Chicken St. Charles and the Eggs Cochin. Of course, Ruby Slippers had a dish called THE PEACEMAKER, which definitely gave me a piece of mind to be able to get combo of both dishes. The Chicken St. Charles is one of the most popular dishes here; Fried Chicken breast over a buttermilk biscuit topped with 2 poached eggs and a delicious sauce to top it off.  The chicken was a tender chicken breast, definitely fried Southern Style.  Juicy and tender and that Buttermilk Biscuit, well, let's just say, you would remember it after leaving here. The reason for the Eggs Cochin?  I love pulled pork, and to have that on top of the buttermilk biscuit served Benedict style with Hollandaise put me in Heaven. Between the 2 of these, I was in "food mode", for sure. 

My wife's portion of Spiced Pumpkin Pancakes was HUGE, thankfully, topped with a powdered sugar and some special sauce drizzled on top. Amazing amazing, amazing.  I could smell the Pumpkin as soon as Nicole put it down in front of us. 

The menu choices on the Momma Specials can also make your head spin, but as I learned from a gentleman sitting beside me, they have a dish called the Trifecta which allows you to combine 3 of he dishes.  Clever for a menu like this to offer that. Every dish is better than the next and to be able to try 2 of the Benedict dishes or 3 of the Specials is a smart option.

For every minute you wait, it is worth every bite you take here.  The atmosphere is lively with a lot of happy diners.  Nicole C. made our experience special and there is no doubt that a whole lot of love was put into the menu and food preparation.  

ABSOLUTELY the place to go when I come to NOLA, and will again and again. After all, there I a whole lot more to try here.

My wife and I took a short trip up to the Indianapolis area to see some lifetime friends who live in the small, beautiful country town of Jamestown, Indiana located just a small distance northwest of Indianapolis. There are many small farm communities along the way with very little great dining spots around. There are mostly fast food restaurants and small town diners and pubs. 

After a great day of catching up with each other accompanied with a couple bottles of good wine we left it up to them to go to one of the few great restaurants in the area. This beautiful large cozy dining experience ended up to be in Brownsburg, Indiana called Boulder Creek Dining Company. Leave it to me the: the first thing I noticed as we walked in was a bright Yelp sticker on the window that said "Yelp loves us."  Was impressed already!!!   As we walked in we were greeted by 2 friendly young gentlemen who handed over the menus and wine list to a girl who kindly seated us and we were immediately introduced to one of our servers who worked as a team with who later would be our waitress, Taylor. As we were walking to the table I immediately noticed the beautifully lit bar that wrapped around the attached dining room areas. Boulder Creek has surprisingly a large dining area and since the bar follows the dining areas on both sides , you can see the bar from wherever you are sitting. In the back of the restaurant there was a large open kitchen you can see also from wherever you are sitting.  The atmosphere had a very northern feel to it because of the dark wood and brick which warmed this place up.   I was very impressed about the immediate attention we received as Taylor helped us decide on the wine selection and answered some questions about the appetizers and entrees. The service was actually the first great attribute to Boulder Creek as it appeared that this dining experience will be timed perfectly and we would not be rushed. Taylor was  extremely friendly, knowledgeable and outgoing.  We ordered a great bottle of Concha Y Toro Gran Reserva which surprisingly was very reasonably priced.  

After we started on the wine, we were served an amazing Sour Dough bread loaf with a remarkable red pepper sauce.  I knew at that point we were in for a treat with their food as well.

We started out with the Heirloom Tomatoes and Mozzarella. Different from the normal Caprice Salad, the mozzarella was served lightly fried over fresh tomatoes which were topped with arugula. Sprinkled over the dish was a balsamic glaze, combined with the fried mozzarella, gave this dish a tremendous flavor.  We also shared the Ahi Tuna.  So fresh and flavorful, the tuna was perfectly seasoned. I could of made a sushi meal out of this dish.  My wife had a real great house salad which she loved.  

I ordered my entrée, which was highly recommended by Taylor; Double Cut Pork Chop.  The pork chop was so thick and so lean. It was grilled and charred on the outside and was very tender on the inside as it was cooked medium.  The way they charred and seasoned the outside of this thick pork chop gave this dish the best flavor and tenderness. You can taste it at the start and finish of each bite.  The side was a baked potato which went with this perfectly.  The wine was also tasting better too by the way.  My wife had grilled Salmon.  She is picky about Salmon which is one of her favorite fish dishes and she loved it. Now here is an unusual dish I've never seen which my friend ordered; Lobster Risotto and filet medallions.  He loved it and I decided that this is what I will order the next time I come here.  

We all decided to split an unusual ice cream desert, the Graeters Ice Cream Trio. The desert was served in 3 small attached glass bowls, and included  Cappuccino Chip and Mint Chip Ice Cream which surrounded a raspberry ice cream in the middle. It was served with fresh Basil and whipped cream. Glad we shared this because I would of eaten this great dessert by myself.  

Boulder Creek has a tremendous feel to it.  There is also outdoor dining as you walk into the front of the restaurant. The mild weather here would make outdoor dining easy, as we are used to heat and humidity in Florida which sometimes makes it difficult to do.

This was a perfect evening with friends in a restaurant that had all sorts of surprises.  Five stars for atmosphere, PERFECT service and a top menu with culinary perfection.  I really hope we can come back soon.

This place is my favorite lunch spot or rainy evening bowl of warm goodness. Obviously it's a noodle forward place and both the ramen and udon noodles always tastes fresh and perfectly cooked. Next the broth, my staple has been the spicy Dosunco, it's so rich and complex that fills your belly up right. Finally tried the vegetarian Udon and wow for a vegetarian broth it packs flavor. The standard bowl is good but I always add more bamboo shoots and seaweed. Save room for a sweet bite of the delish mochi ice cream. I love the green tea. 

And during the CV19 outbreak they serve everything separate and you fill the bowl with the broth and it comes out perfect at home. Great for takeout as well

What a pleasant surprise! Starving after a full day at Busch Gardens, we went on our way to find some food that didn't cost us an arm and a leg (like theme park food).   Low and behold- Fuzzy's Taco Shop.  This place rocks!  The decor is extremely vibrant and fun. They have funny quotes in the bathrooms and on the walls.  Seating room is wide open and airy feeling.  

My husband, son and I shared an order of pulled pork nachos and another order of ground beef tacos. Holy cow-- the servings are HUGE!!!! They really don't skimp on toppings.  The nachos come topped with pico de Gallo, queso, feta and garlic sauce (in addition to the protein of  choice).  I was a major fan of their original "Butt Burnin'" hot sauce.  

My younger son had an order of grilled fish tacos and absolutely loved it.  I didn't get a taste, but I trust his opinion.  He's a fish taco connoisseur :-)

I'm stoked I actually have a Fuzzy's in my area... sad I haven't given it a chance earlier!

I have been a loyal customer of Dolce Carini  for the past year. I have time and again shelled out almost $8 for 6 mozzarella sticks with a smile. Simply because Dolce has the best sticks in a 5 block radius, and I don't get much time for lunch. 
However, today is the last time I will step foot into this overpriced- over hyped pizza joint. I called in my order of Mozzarella sticks, I waited till 1:45, so I could avoid the lunch rush. When I went to pick my order up, I was on the receiving end of some of the worst service I have ever received. At the counter no one asked me how could they help me. I stood there for about 2 minutes and finally got the attention of the woman at the counter. I told her my name and my order. After getting that information from me, she proceeded to turn around to her computer and answer the phone. Now understand that a restaurant can be busy, so I waited a few minutes. Still she didn't get my order, but proceeded to tend to her computer screen and take calls. Another woman working there walked by and I asked fro her help. She was ABOUT to help me but the first lady told her that she was helping me. At that point she turned back to her computer and phone AGAIN. So I told her that I had to go back to work, and I just needed to pay for my order. She goes to get the order, hands it to me, takes my $20, and then answers the phone, and gets back on her computer.  She finally hands me my change, and when I told her that this was very poor customer service she said something that I wont write here. At that point I said I want my money back. I will not allow you to treat me poorly and take my money. Lets just say it took me another 7 minutes to get my money back. I asked the lady what her name was, she refused to tell me. Them I asked for a manager. She said she was the manager. I was appalled at such behavior.

We were hankering for ramen and had bookmarked this place on Yelp before heading out to Nashville. 

It's a bit difficult to find, as it's in a plaza area and the addresses aren't obvious. Walk towards the back of the plaza and it's on your left hand side with an outside patio. 

The hostess wasn't too happy when she greeted us, but that's cool. Perhaps she was tired. 

We were starving after a long day and immediately started ordering. Everything looked so good, but not everything was delicious. 

Yellowtail and jalapeno sashimi: fish tasted a bit too fishy and chewy. Pass.

Salmon sushi: delish and very good quality. 

Yellowtail sushi: my friend said this was much better than the yellowtail sashimi

Wagyu shortrib yakitori: best dish of the night! The beef was perfectly cooked and not chewy at all. 

Chicken ramen: meh, this was just okay. Too salty for me and I wasn't fond of the thicker noodles. The soft boiled egg was a redeeming factor. 

Pork ramen: my friend ordered this and I only had a taste of the broth. It was so much better than the chicken!! It also came with the thinner noodles that I would have preferred. 

Service was pretty good, as we got served by three different waiters. I was a bit disappointed when we tried to order another round of the beef skewers because the kitchen closed at 10 pm on the dot. Wish they had given us some kind of notice. 

I would recommend this place if you're in the area. Get the pork ramen, beef skewers and sushi! Good eclectic mix of Japanese food.

When I was working in Philly a few years ago, I made it a point to get my fill of Philly cheesesteak sandwiches...................so I made a list of places to hit up on, and they were -

1. Tommy DiNic's
2, Geno's Steaks
3. Pat's King of Steaks
4. Carmen's Famous Italian Hoagie

Located in south Philly...........finding Geno's wasn't too hard for me, but finding parking to get to Geno's was the biggest challenge! There is no private parking for this place, so you have to roll the dice & hopefully find some metered street parking. Lucky for me, I was able to find some street parking that wasn't too far, so I was able to hit up both Geno's & Pat's at the same time, as both rival business are just across from each other.

When you walk up to the ordering counter, make sure you're ready to order your cheesesteak as they like to keep the line moving.............there is only outside seating, as this place is like a grab & go kinda place.

Upon ordering, I ended up getting my cheesesteak sandwich with American cheeese & onions. Just a tip gang............don't do the American cheese, get the Wiz instead.......as that's the real way of eating a cheesesteak sandwich! I also noticed Geno's cuts their meat in whole slices, vs. Pat's that cuts up their meat in small little pieces.

What can I say about my sandwich? The bun was good, but the meat was rather on the dry and chewy side...........I was thinking to myself - "what is all the hype about this place?" Granted, I am not a Philly cheesesteak connoisseur...........but I know what I like as far as taste, and Geno's was just okay for me. 

I know Geno's has been around for a long time (founded in 1966 by Joey Vento), so I'm sure they have their loyal fans. 
Still worth it to make the trip out here, because if you don't try it.......you'll never know right?

I came to Pat's right after I left Geno's..........after all, it was just a hop, skip, & jump away from each other.............and being that this Hawaii boy made it all the way to Philly for work, by George, I had to have me my Philly cheesesteak sandwiches!!!

Pat's has been around even longer than Geno's, as Pat's King of Steaks was founded in 1930 by Pat Olivieri. He originally sold hot-dogs from a hot-dog stand, but one day decided to make a steak sandwich which caught the eye of one of his loyal customers who was a cabbie............after that, the steak sandwich was born!

Pat's has a similar set up like Geno's.........you go to the ordering counter, & order your sandwich. Please note the ordering sign, as they have instructions on how to order your sandwich to keep the line moving. 
Upon getting your sandwich, there are a few outdoor tables & seats, as this place is basically a grab & go kinda place too.

Upon ordering my sandwich, I got my cheesesteak with onions and American cheese. Just a tip gang.........don't do American cheese..........get the "Whiz" instead, as that's the true way to eat a cheesesteak sandwich. 
I guess I'm not a fan of cheese whiz, and that is why I did the American cheese..........but the American cheese didn't really go too good in the sandwich..............so get da Whiz! No can go wrong!

I liked the fact that Pat's cuts up their meats for their sandwiches...........as the meat tasted less chewy than Geno's, but overall..........it was just okay for me as I've had better at other places.

Loved the history about this place, as Pat's King of Steaks is well know in Philly.

I came to the Reading Terminal Market due to a recommendation from a friend, as he told me to check out DiNics for their famous Roast Pork, & Roast Beef sandwiches.
Upon seeing DiNics on a T.V. food channel, I made it a point to check out the Reading Terminal Market over the weekend. 

What can I say about the Reading Terminal Market?

Well, the best way to describe this place is - it's like a GIANT mega food court & store!!! 
You name it, they probably have it here...........all kinds of ethnic foods can be found here, as well as fresh farm produce, meats & poultry, finest seafood items, baked goods & confections.

My mission when I had visited the Reading Terminal Market was to try the sandwich from DiNics (which I accomplished), as I ended up eating both the roast pork, & roast beef sandwiches.............I really enjoyed both sandwiches, but between the two...........I gave the thumbs up to the roast pork!

While walking around the mall, I ran into another sandwich shop called - Carmen's Famous Italian Hoagie & Cheesesteaks. 
The time when I was there, I saw our island son - Barack Obama come to Carmen's to eat a cheese steak, so I figured if it was good enough for President Obama, it was a must for this island son to also give it a try too! Lol!

There is a very long history about the Reading Terminal Market, as I read a brochure about this place.............let me share a little of what I read.

Apparently back in 1892 the Reading Railroad opened the Reading Terminal Market below the tracks of their massive new train shed. The 78,000 sq. foot market held nearly 800 spaces for vendors & was touted as the "greatest food market" in the world!
By 1971, the Reading Railroad went bankrupt & the Reading Terminal Market started to decline & be in disrepair. 
Beginning in the 1980's, the Reading Company renewed attention to the market & began a turnaround of the facilities, and by 1984 trains stopped running to the station above the market and the city's commuter rail system was re-routed to bypass the old Reading Terminal. 
By 1990 the historic building was sold to the Pennsylvania Convention Center Authority, who rebuilt the market to strict historic preservation standards, and also set up a non-profit management company to run the market and maintain the historical integrity of this place.

I must say, if you're ever in Philadelphia, take sometime to check out the  Reading Terminal Market, as you should put it in your "must" list of things to do! 
Visiting the market has a lot of very cool historical value, as well coming here to try the various types of food...........it's basically a foodie lovers paradise!!!

I've only heard good things about this place, and I had the opportunity to check it out last weekend. And I have to say it was nothing but a series of disappointments.

- Incredibly slow service. As in 4 hours of slow service. We were a party of 8, so I could understand a slower service. But this was absolutely ridiculous.

- In addition to the slow service, they were absolutely terrible with drinks. My boyfriend and I were the last to arrive, and no one asked us if we wanted a drink. We had to ask for drinks. When mine was finished, no one asked if I wanted another. I also have to ask twice for my water to be refilled. My parents also went yesterday and experienced the same problem with drinks. The wine meant for a certain part of the meal was being served after that portion of the meal had already been eaten and cleared from the table.

- Again, the service...we have easily 5 different servers bringing us our food or clearing the table. With that many servers revolving, no one was actually giving us proper attention (like say to our empty drink glass, for example)

- The price is absolutely ridiculous and not worth it. I've had better meals that I didn't have to cook myself for less money.

The food itself was mostly enjoyable, which is why it gets 2 starts, but I think you can tell by my review that I will not only never go back but I will actively discourage others from going. For more than $100 per person, I have had better meals and more attentive service, and left sooner than 4 hours after starting my meal.

Not the cheapest in town but perhaps the swankiest customers. 

Great food, convenient location but parking can be tricky at this hotel restaurant and bar. The feel is casual and easy going with locals and guests the blend. This is not your usual hotel bar.

Being in a hotel, the prices can climb but they're worth it. How to Beat the High Co$t of Living? Hit up their Happy Hour M-F 4-6. Yes! A Friday HH. The menu changes but you can't beat the $10, Two Bit Burger and $7 Mules. If they bring the spareribs or spicy peppers back, dive in!

Brunch offers up a bottomless Mimosa option for $10 + $1 each refill on the weekends from 8-2:30 and will go a long way, my friend. Opt in for this while you scarf some $14 Huevos Rancheros or my favorite, the $17 Short Rib Hash.

Friendly people serving up nice cocktails, good wine and nice food. I'll be seeing you at the bed of the bar. 

Cheers

Another winner for Carlos and Santa Barbara!

From the team that keeps your bellies filled at Los Agaves and the margaritas flowing at Santa Mezcal, the beach is in view for Floe de Maiz. 

Location
Location
Location
Will only get you in the door. The food and service will bring you back. 

Two patios, bright and airy bar, delicious food and a competitive Happy Hour will find me coming back. 

I love sitting at the bar. Easy to meet new friends, quick service, and always someone to talk with. A bonus is Marcos behind the bar. You may remember him from Santo Mezcal and now he's moved down the street to rock our world at the beach. 

The margaritas flowed and I throughly enjoyed the Tacos De Pulpo Almendrado $18. I have a talent for ordering the best item on the menu on the first visit. The down side is branching out to eat my way through the rest. It's a challenge I'll take on. 

The Happy Hour is great but confusing. You may want to write it down:
Sunday - Monday 11:00am - 9:00pm
Tuesday - Thursday 12:00pm - 6:00pm
Friday - Saturday 2:00pm - 6:00pm

Who knows, of we're lucky, we'll meet at the bar. 
Cheers and say "hello" to Marcos for me!
Salute

Mr. Foreperson, have you reached a verdict? Yes we have. 

This is truly a neighborhood, greasy spoon. A locals hangout for sure. Regulars walking in receive warm greetings from the staff and other happy eaters. With room for 30ish at tables and side booths and another 6 at the bar, parties from 1 to 8-10 for yourself or family. 

Craving Chicken-fried Steak and Eggs I ordered ordered my eggs easy with hashbrowns and sourdough. The meat is as expected. Maybe a little thin. The gravy is definitely thin despite all the air bubbles trapped by what I guess is overuse of Xanthan gum to thicken it. I don't see how this could be home made brown gravy. Even with the steak submerged, the breading is dry. I'll pass on this next round. But don't let this ruling sway your vote. The salsa served was great. Better than some of the so called Mexican food restaurants. The eggs were spot on and the hashbrowns delicious with perfect toast. The portions were smaller than others but so were the prices. Preparing for my breakfast choice, I when in prepared to be stuffed. I was pleasantly surprised and appreciate the reasonable portion. Thanks for looking out for my waistline and pocket book. 

While I was not impressed with the chicken-fried steak and its gravy bath, I throughly enjoyed the feel and friendliness of JFYC. I will be adding this gem to my usual, breakfast haunts in hopes I will be accepted into this family.

Acquitted

Rushed, Old & Sad. Garrett's has not aged well.

A Santa Barbara institution that has forgotten it's a restaurant here to serve the people. This little, greasy spoon misses the breakfast spot for me with lousy service, bad attitude and food that would be better anywhere else. 
Our waitress was not a happy camper and wanted us to order as soon as we sat down. "I can't turn my tables" she said and was pushy for us to finish and leave. The hashbrowns, eggs, bacon and toast were fine but the attitude ruined the experience.

The following day I was at another breakfast diner with a line out the door and 35min wait quoted. Sitting at the counter the server said to the gentlemen next to me "there's no rush" when handing him the bill. That the way it's supposed to be

Ruben together with Chef Robert Perez just served up the best meal I've had in Santa Barbara!

While already a fan of this cute, quaint little spot a 1/2 block off State Street with it's creative and fresh menu and having sampled most, if not all of it, it was not until four of us sat down for the family style Tasting Menu at a very reasonable $45ea that I can honestly say I was blown away.

Since it's Chef's selection, the flow of food you see may vary. While it's difficult to highlight the best of the best. I'll keep it short and well, sweet.

*Grilled Watermelon was warm as expected but the juices flowed. What a fun idea and a must try on your next visit.
*White Anchovies are my favorites. These little crostini suckers were lightly oiled with a citrus freshness. Simple and easy, they're a delicious mouthful.
*Uni Shooter. EAT ME/DRINK ME! Nothing more to say.
*Bone Marrow Bruschetta. So good it should be illegal. I'll confiscate another plate, please. Put a dab of the whole grain mustard on top and melt into your seat. Winner of the Most decadent award, for sure. You'll wish for more.
*Niman Ranch Beef Short-ribs & braised pork belly is out of this world. First, the short-ribs are moist and fall apart in your mouth. Aint need to teeth to eat this meat. Delicious! The pork belly is a favorite of mine and always order it if on a specials menu.

Sure you can order off the menu, add you should. Many of the regulars have highlighted our top picks. For me, and if there's a small group of 3 or 4, I'm signing back up for the Tasting Menu. What a great way to eat your way through menu the way the Chef sees it. 

Already planning my next visit.
Cheers

It's like drinking wine with your friends, in their home. Good wine and good friends. 

Making a delicious offering of quality wines at a fair price is only part of it. For me to want to spend my money, you must sell me on the story. The dream. There are many great wines in Santa Barbara county so why do I love Sloan? Kym and Jamie with the help of Sophie, their lovable Havanese fur companion, make it great. These owners pour their heart into every bottle. Charismatic, smiling and ready with a story about themselves, how they're learning and discovering new aspects of the winemaking business or just to talk about you. This is more than a wine tasting room, it's a wine tasting experience. And they are more than purveyors, they are people you'll want to have a friends. 

The tasting room is more than convenient, across the street from De Le Guerra Plaza. You know, the place with the bands during Fiesta. A block off State Street and almost a mile from the Funk Zone, it's a perfect stop in the newly named, Wine Collection of El Paseo. With 6 tasting rooms to chose from, this is the more "adult" wine tasting adventure as opposed to the younger Funk Zone.

If I had a Spanish/California/Santa Fe inspired home, my den would look like Jamie Slone Wines Tasting Room. The special details put into the design, the free flowing feel, the personal touch. It's comfortable. It's easy for groups of 2 or more at the bar, 4-8 in the den by the fireplace or sitting around the large table for a more "private" setting. You will want to swing in for a glass and say "hi".

For the wine. Well, that's very subjective. I'm enjoying the whites and the reds certainly stand on their own compared to others in Santa Barbara County. I have a few bottles of the 2013 Pinot Noir from Santa Rita Hills in my wine fridge now. The Aloysius Chardonnay is crisp, not too oaky and perfect for hot summer days on the Central Coast. You're sure to enjoy the playful blend of the BoRific. Wonder where these names come from? Aloysius, BoRific, Mrs. B Grenache Blanc, another refreshing white, you'll need to ask. There's a story behind every pour and that's the magic here, folks.

Kym and Jamie Sloan have invited us into their home, their lives and their joy of the wine world. But don't take my word for it. Although you should. Stop by one afternoon soon and see for yourself what sets Jamie Slone Wines apart from the rest. And tell them I said "hi". Oh wait, I'm probably already there.

Cheers

Loud. Crowded. Poor Parking. Mediocre Food.
I expect a better burger from a Culinary Hall of Fame inductee.

They say location location location. 
That's the number one talking point of MB and what will keep this burger hut alive. The captive, family audience of the Mesa is hungry for quality food with family in a casual and fun atmosphere.
If you're on the Mesa, you've probably already been. If you're on the East side, you might not cross the line to visit. I don't think I would. 

Full of family's being loud. 
The concrete floors and hard tables do nothing to absorb the chaos. It's crazy from the mini-van and SUV/Crossover filled parking lot, through the ordering and eating process and not until you are comfortably on your way home are you relaxed. This is an event and not intended for a quiet night out. Hangovers stay away. This is not your comfort food.

The wait is not bad at all when you put it in perspective
13min from walking in the door, through the queue and placing our orders. You can wait longer for a table on State Street. It just feels long with nothing to occupy your time other than wondering if there will be a chair open and who you'll sit next to at the community tables. 
34min from walking in, we have our food. That's good! This is not fast food. It's fresh ingredients made just for you. Don't believe me? See for yourself as you watch the kitchen prep as you wait in line. But is the wait worth it?

Food is passable. 
The Funk Zone Burger was as juicy as a medium burger can be. Topped with a trendy sunny side up fried egg some applewood bacon, mushrooms, BBQ sauce, cheddar and tomato for $13, it's a great deal. The meat was too cooked for me. I'm a medium rare guy. If you like more time on the fire. You're in luck. Oh, and it comes with fries. Cold and not amazing. As I was eating them, I asked my dining partner "where where those great fries I had the other day? Because these are not those." Like meats cooking temp, fries are very subjective. You may love them. I did not. 
My partner had the Sandspit that came out medium-well, cold and without kalamata olives. But you can read all about it on Yelp. 

Thank you Cat Cora for investing in Santa Barbara. It's fun to name drop celebrity chefs in our little town. I'm sure you will do well with family on the way home from soccer practice, picking up to-go orders for a family Netflix night or even a bite to take down to the beach. I wish you the best. 
For me, I'll pass on dinning in and think hard about buying the burger, any flavor. The price point is good but the food is ok. 

So what do you do?
Go. Give Mesa Burger a shot. It may be exactly what you're looking for. Sadly, it was not good for me. I may call in an order for the beach for a second try but skip the fries. It's a 2.5 but not a 2.6 so I'll sadly round down.

Not the direction to take.

After a few visits since their opening, it's clear to me Convivo does not care about local business. Perhaps the guests at Santa Barbara Inn will keep them afloat.

Lets talk about the good to mediocre first. 

Patio is warmed with heaters from above and inviting. The fire side is smaller, more intimate apposed to the side closet to the rooms, filled with chatter and big parties. Both will pair nicely with your evening. No need to squint to read the fine print, the lights are bright. Too bright. 

What did we eat?
*Lamb meatballs - delicious, pink balls
*Prawns - the sauce was great
*Gnocchi- nestled up with the porkbelly and squash is great. Distinct flavors from the salty pork, sweet and drying squash and fluffy gnocchi play well together
*Quadrati rigati with veal bolenega- not amazing, in fact, bland and wet. The under cooked quadrati pasta was too heavy meaty, wet sauce. The liquid lay in the bottom of the bowl 
Focaccia- yummy fluffiness. Add on to any meal.

The Palmina Nebbiolo was a good pairing of Santa Barbara County little Italy and Convivo's take on the meal. The wine list is on the high side but this is Santa Barbara and a hotel so it's expected. 

Experience
Empty starter plates sat in their space at the edge of the table when the pasta arrived. It was not until I staked 3 plates and 1 bowl on top of each other before they were cleared and not by anyone we had seen. At last we had our space back.

My water was never refilled. 

The music is not appropriate for the crowd or the menu price. This is more a NYC, 40-something, trying to be hip, hotel lobby soundtrack.

Vin Santo, 2 to choose from, actually.  No Biscotti. Instead a round cookie that looks like a sausage was provided to dip in my wine. The complementary chocolate cookie was a nice touch.

Now for the follow up visits...
My first dinning experience was not too long after the opening and I wanted to give Convivo some time to mature. Apparently this is the Curious Case of Convivo Button. The service has gone down to the point where, on my last visit, we planed drinks at the bar first but the experience was painful and we left. With 3 behind the bar, I felt we were serving ourselves. Asking about wines on tap, the bar "tenders" were reluctant to provide details. After a disappointing attempt at finding a wine, we decided to go with a beer and cocktail. We pursued the menu but were never asked if we wanted something to eat. In fact, the head bartender kept his back to us most of the time. It was not a fun adventure and we decided to pay the tab and have dinner elsewhere. 

Convivo's potential to amaze or crash and burn is equal. My request to you would be, pay more attention to your customers. Especially the locals. You'll need us come winter.

Beautiful inside and out, the service, food and atmosphere will keep you coming back. It works for me.

Located in a quaint, 1872 Victorian house, it's right off the 101 and across from the Andree Clark Bird Refuge and on a quiet street, you might not even know it's there. You should. With it's multiple rooms seating small and larger groups, it's a perfect brunch spot for 2, a private dinner for 10, or a small wedding reception. Whatever to choose, Stella Mare's has you covered. For me, it's all about the greenhouse and it's fireplace.

*Applewood Bacon Eggs Benedict $17.95 is ok but I feel there are better benedicts in Santa Barbara (Boathouse Signature) and too many other options here.
*Omelette Ratatouille $16.25 with it's light and fluffy eggs is delicious and a great portion, not too big.
*Escargot $9.25 is always fun. Think of it as a mushroom with lots of butter and garlic. Who does not what to soak bread in that?
*Stella Burger $14.50 is delicious but can be overpowering with all the blue cheese. Ask for 1/2 the usual portion and leave no fry behind.
*Coq Au Vin $14.95/$24.95 lunch/dinner is my #2 pick and perfect afternoon or evening. The portion is bigger and I usually take some home for a perfect, cold snack. 
*Cassoulet $27.95 topped with duck confit is my #1 and "go to" whenever Chef Ironside adds it to the menu.

Happy Hour: Tuesday-Sunday from 5-7 with $3 bubbles. Yep, THREE DOLLAR BUBBLES! Now you'er in. In addition, $4 select wines and cocktails with food specials starting at $4 with plenty under $10. 

Did I mention live music every Wednesday starting at 7pm? Well, now I have.

Stella Mare's is a delightful restaurant with solid menu and beautiful soundings. It's a bit of an older crowd who come in early and leave the place quite by 7:30, mid-week. I'm ok with that. More like being at home than out on the town. Especially when you're on the sofa in front of the fire, drinking a well priced glass of Côtes du Rhône.

Make an Opentable for date night, 6 for Happy Hour/Dinner on Wednesday for live music in the Greenhouse or a lovely brunch this Sunday. Whatever you choose, Stella Mare's will deliver.

#1 in my heart and stomach. At Mony's, I'm family. 

Already my favorite Barbacoa and Tripas (moist and slightly crispy but not fried to hell) tacos, I was in. It too long ago, when I walked in and Mony told me to try the Tortas. I laughed to myself thinking "of course I'll eat whatever you tell me". "What kind?" I asked. "The Barbacoa" was Monica's reply. Since I do what I'm told, I told her son, Carlos, who was working the register "Your mom told me I had to eat the Barbacoa Tortas today". We laughed. 

Wow! Best Tortas in town. 
The bread is quality to begin with. Not falling apart and cheap. The cold avocado floats atop the moist and hot barbacoa. Good thing for the paper wrapping. It catches the escaping juices allowing the lightly toasted bread to soak it up. You don't want to waste anything here.

Monys prides themselves on great customer service and quality food served up at a fair price. If I did not believe in this family's ability to constantly deliver, I would not be a regular. If you need a second opinion on their greatness, ask Chef Aarón Sánchez of Taco Trip on The Cooking Channel.

I think I'll head there now.

Why do we come here? The staff does not seem to want us.

I've pooped into Seven many times but always as an afterthought. Sometimes earlier in the evening and others on the way home. I never get a warm and fuzzy feeling when I'm there. It's almost like they don't want me to be.

Recently 3 of us walked over to Seven for some snacks. We scored the table by the piano with the windows open for a great cross breeze. There were no stools available but at least we had a place to eat. One guest sat on the piano bench and was told to get up, that it's not a place to sit. Odd. I'm pretty sure that's exactly what it's for. Oh well. A smorgasbord of appetizers came out with sliders, fries and some very dry steak bites. We ate and left. 

The food is mostly good and the prices fair.
Pulled-Pork Sliders $10 are moist and delicious
Parmesan & Truffle Fries or overplayed. Their Classic Fries for $7 are just fine by me.
The Classic Burger for $13 is my favorite with the Mac & Cheese a hit or miss. 

A robust Happy Hour gains Seven a star
Monday - Thursday 5-7, Friday 4-7 and yep, they have weekends with Saturday & Sunday 12-3. You get a few food and drink specials that make it worth my while. 
The back patio is a nice escape and great later in the evening. 

My experience with service woes is not limited to the piano bench incident. Most of my time is spent sitting at the bar and being ignored. Regardless of how busy the place is. Maybe I pissed off the wrong person and there's a picture of me on the wall in the back. Regardless, the thought of poos service lingers in the back of my head and therefore, Seven rarely makes it to the top of the list and will remain in the postscript.

This actually is the best steak in town!

Tee Off is a place like none other in Santa Barbara. 
Sure their steaks are the amazing (prime rib and bone in rib-eye) but it's the little things that make the short list for date nights, birthday dinners, family in town and just Tuesday. 

First off it's dark. REALLY dark. There are no windows and it was years before I realized how green the place is. I mean, it's golf themed but this place is all green. 

A long bar, which is where you'll find me, is tended mostly by Todd and Matt. Both will shake up a killer martini while a bottle of big, bold red wine sits ready for the main event. The dining room is split with high backed booths up front with a very loungey feel and tables in a back room where there is more light. Also a great room for a surprise birthday party (thank you Sarah S). 

Bring your appetite!
Enjoy a cocktail while you pursue the menu. As mentioned, I suggest red meat but more on that in a moment. The meal starts with a cold veggie tray then it's feeding time!

'Big Bertha' $49 is a massive bone-in ribeye (I leave off the garlic marinade) that comes with Soup (prime rib soup!!!) or Salad, Rice or Potato, Fresh Seasonal Vegetables & Fresh Baked Sourdough Rolls. This is pretty much the only thing I order. Perfect for 2 and you'll have leftovers. Through Covid I've called in a take out a few times and it travels well too. Buyer beware. You'll need a big cutting board to carve this one up. 

Prime Rib $35-54 is the house specially, while they last. Multiple cuts for multiple appetites and again, I dare say, the best in Santa Barbara. Some pork, chicken and a fish or two too but come on. You know why you're here...COW. Moo. 

This is a locals joint where you and team know each other by name and the kitchen crew says "hi" when you walk by. It's on the small side and people tend to linger and enjoy their time so make a reservation on weekends and holidays to ensure you have a seat. If you're lucky, you can slide into the bar and make some new friends. 

Cheers and I'll see you at the Tee Off.

I've never felt compelled to leave a review about any place because I'm pretty easy going and being in the industry myself I understand how things can get when the bar is non stop, but what I experienced today was a blatant display of disrespect for the customer. 

To begin this is not a review on the restaurant end, I've always enjoyed the brunch and have always left satisfied with what I've ordered and the service has always been great. This concerns more with the bar side and the outrageous $20 cover to enter the pool only to leave minutes later because the amount of people was the equivalent to all the people you see in a wave pool at a water park and god knows what's going on beneath the surface. 

I have never seen such a lack of urgency with the bartenders both in the front and in the pool area as was displayed today. I understand what it means to be in the weeds but when your staff is dragging or in their case dancing and having casual conversations with other patrons while there are other people waiting to be served and showing no recognition of how long one individual has been waiting there to order vs. someone who just walked up is frustrating as a customer who was just looking to relax. Staffing wasn't the issue, there was more than enough bartenders to handle the crowds both in front and in the back bar. The issue was bartenders who showed zero lack of customer awareness and were rude to customers when voicing their displeasure at the amount if time they've had to wait. 

I have always enjoyed the Country Club and have often recommended it to people who want to try something different while visiting out here. After what I witnessed today I think that may change.

Upon entering Jilly's, you're "greeted" by staff rudely yelling, "You want brunch or just cupcakes?" Just cupcakes.  Thanks. 

The secret to winning Cupcake Wars? Giant, unwieldy cupcakes lacking flavor, topped with a weirdly fluffy icing that has a greasy but thin mouthfeel.  I expected something special, something of high quality, but these were pretty lame.  The base of the cupcake tasted like overcooked, storebought cake mix.  Maybe Sandra Lee was the judge of the Cupcake Wars finale?

Ok locals casino. Wife and I visit there often. Usually, it's not bad until yesterday. One of their ticket redemption machines shorted me $100. Told them what happened and they couldn't find out if the machine actually shorted me or not or malfunctioned. The machine said it spit out the correct amount, but guess what? It was missing $100. Course being a casino they didn't want to give me my money. So be careful of their ticket redemption machines. And always count what it gives before you walk away. Guess this place doesn't care if their machines malfunction.

It's been a while since I've been here, but I'm glad I came back. Service is always great, food is really good and good portions. Fish n chips is prob the best you'll find in a cafe. The breakfast burrito is also another fav. Might be a short wait when it's busy, but usually there's no wait. Great place to eat!

Let me start by saying, I don't usually complain when I get my meal and I don't like it. I suffer through, eat it, then pay for it. 
       We ordered the gator bites for an appetizer and it was delicious. We had two choices for an entree, either grouper or snapper. We could either get it blackened or fried. I chose blackened (because, normally, it is lightly spiced  and I normally don't eat fried food.) When it came out I had a bite and it was BEYOND spicy. I couldn't stomach it to eat it. When the waitress came out, I asked her if I could have something different because those was very spicy for me. The waitress said "we don't do that. We aren't going to bring that back. You have to eat it." I replied "I just want something different, it is really spicy. Can I at least have Tartar Sauce to calm down the spice?" The waitress replies "we don't have Tartar sauce here. I'll go get the manager." 
     She leaves and the manager comes out. Let me say, I have never been treated SO RUDELY in my life by a manager. I can't even open my mouth to explain myself before she starts scolding me. She yells "you don't know what you're talking about. This isn't spicy. Everyone else doesn't think it's spicy. You're the only one. We will NOT be giving you anything else. You will eat this and pay for it. You don't know what you're talking about. This is not a chain restaurant, that fish cost me $20." I tried to explain that it was just too spicy and I wanted something different. She then says "if you won't pay for this I will call the sheriff on you and you'll go to jail!" Before I could even respond, she storms off. 
     Five minutes later, the POLICE show up to the restaurant!!!!! She actually called the police...... 
She showed the officer to my table, I explained the situation to the sheriff; I was very calm. I told him "I will pay for my glass of wine, I will pay for the appetizer that I ordered, but I just wanted something different because the fish was entirely too spicy for me. I'm not asking for anything for free, but if they won't just exchange the fish I would like this taken off of my bill." I also told him "I own a produce stand at home and if a customer comes in with a complaint about the fruit they brought home, I exchange it and give them something different or give them their money back. I never treat them as I was treated tonight in this restaurant." At the table next to us the man was making comments such as "they are probably scam artists and do this all the time." If I was a scam artist, I would have just left without paying. I waited until the sheriff got there, obviously not a scam artist. 
    The sheriff then left to speak to the owner and came back to inform me "you either can pay your bill or come with me." I am the stubborn type of person that says "take me to jail". My friend that was dining with me (this was our mothers get away weekend, we both have 3 kids and this was our weekend away). My friend paid the bill so I wouldn't go to jail. 
     It's truly sad that a restaurant would treat their customers this way when they really do have good food. I've never experienced this kind of treatment in my life. Please, do not go here, they don't deserve to have nice customers when they call the police on their customers for asking to exchange their meal that was too spicy.

I was meeting up some friends for dinner in Philadelphia, but I got here pretty early. So I decided to stop by and walk around the downtown area for a bit. A bit of exploring of the streets adjacent to Independence Hall led me to this interestingly decorated coffee shop.
I walked in to find that I was the only customer there at the time. I went to order a cappuccino from the barista, and made a quick pit stop while I waited for my drink. I saw some pretty cool decor, and I could tell that the owner of this place really likes movies.
As I walked out of the restroom, I kept spotting interesting decor along the way. The best part about the decor: I spotted Wilson! (For those that don't know, watch the movie Cast Away).
The coffee was pretty good, and the barista was nice. We had a short conversation about the area. Apparently, Philadelphia was voted the rudest city in the US a few years back. I didn't see that while I was here, but that's probably because I'm from LA, and we have a similar reputation.
This coffee shop is nice, come here for a cup of Joe and take a break from Philly's winter weather.

Since I was in town for an interview, I called up some friends who are locals to the area. They suggested this place, so I made my way over here after checking out Independence Hall.
If you come to this restaurant, I recommend parking inside the lot that sits just across the street. The lot is safe, and the price is reasonable.
When I walked in, the restaurant was packed. I asked the hostess if we needed reservations, and she told me it was not required but advisable. Since we had none, I put my name down and sat at the bar while I waited for my friends.
At the bar, I ordered some seared fish tacos and a custom drink. The drink consisted of cold brew, whiskey, and a bit of Irish coffee. The tacos were pretty good, and the drink got me going fast.
Once my friends got there, we were sat at our table and ordered our food. I went with grilled salmon, coconut rice, and had some water on the side. The plate was pretty good! Although the coconut rice was not to my taste.
The customer service was alright here, the waitress was quick to get our order processed. 
Aside from the coconut rice, everything else was great.

After dinner, we went out looking for a nice bar. After checking out other establishments, we decided to hang out here. 
We sat at a round table near the front entrance, and ordered our drinks. I ordered another coffee/booze drink, but they didn't do a good job of making it. For starters, the drink should be over ice, not hot. I ordered a cup of ice from the waitress, and that was that.
The drink was so-so. But since this was a custom drink, I gave them a pass. Some of my friends got their orders mixed up, but the waitress was friendly about it and fixed the situation.
We mingled here for a few hours before we called it a night. It was great catching up with old friends over drinks. This place was an alright place to finish the night. It was cozy and lively. They actually had a live band playing upstairs, but we didn't take the time to check it out. Maybe the next time I find myself in Philly, I'll check out their live music.

I was on my way back to LA from Philly, and I was looking for good breakfast options before boarding my flight. I found this place a few hundred meters away from my gate. I had the craving for sushi, but I was told that they don't serve it until after 10:30 AM. They did, however, have breakfast options that sounded appealing. So I went with that and sat down for my meal here.
I ordered some water while I waited for my meal. Ten minutes later, my meal comes out. I got eggs with tuna and home fries. The plate had pretty big portions, and food was pretty good. It was not too heavy, and sat well in my stomach.
Once I was done, I paid for the check, then made my way to my gate. The food here made my morning. The customer service was great, and the decor was pretty nice. I'd repeat.

We walked along Gulf Blvd. looking for a lunch spot. My wife noticed a pretty good crowd outside, usually a good sign, It did not disappoint. Definitely a local spot. We sat inside, wanting the AC. Our server was the nicest guy I think we have ever met in service industry.  We started with rum runners and salsa and chips. Drinks were very good. I ordered the Ricky T's Fish Sandwich. Fried cod, with Cole slaw. My wife had the fish tacos, I think it was also Cod. 3 tacos, Both Dishes were $13.99. We both thought our lunch was delicious. My wife's friend met us late, so we ordered 3 more rumrunners to go, and a  home made clam chowder for her. She enjoyed her chowder as well. Great lunch place, glad we stopped in.

On the way home from our Treasure Island vacation , we stopped in the Frog for a bite to eat before our 4 hour ride home. Are we glad we did. Packed house when we arrived around 11am., but we got a table right away. Great service and great food. I ordered the Monte Cristo Omelette, 
Ham, turkey and Swiss cheese. My wife ordered the vegetable omelet, spinach, mushroom and cheddar. Huuuge portions. My omelet was filled with shaved turkey and ham, not just a slice or two, or chopped as usual with other breakfast places. Also my potatoes were cooked perfectly. Our server gave us their homemade strawberry jam, which was so good , we bought a jar to take home. We were so full, we barely ate dinner that night. Do yourself a favor if your in the area , stop in, you will not be disappointed, and try the jam.

Excellent burgers on South 5th Street, just where Passyunk intersects with the 5. Design your own using the three computer stations, or go to the counter to talk with the people working there. Either way you get a standard double patty complemented any way you choose. If you don't want to think that much about it, the menu offers several great combinations that are bound to make you happy. 

Just the right amount of grease, potato or pretzel roll, natural sugar carbonated beverages, Bassett ice cream based shakes, and fresh fruit smoothies, all surround the ultimate comfort food for your indulgence. 

Prices that won't break the bank just off the hippest street in town. 

If there is something to improve upon, it is that it appears that every burger is finished to well done regardless of how you request it. Still, they are so juicy I almost didn't notice.

Northern Liberties now has a fair share of interesting and comfortable places to eat, drink and hang out over cups of good coffee.  One of the earliest pioneers that continues to pump out java and decent bakery snacks is Higher Grounds on North 3rd Street.  This converted row house draws a local crowd, as well as longstriders from farther south in Center City, and the occasional visitor from farther afield.  It is attractive in a Salvation Army Store furniture kind of way, with a lot of art, crafts, and a vast variety of tchotchkes to catch your attention.  It is cozy and worn, like an old couch or settee should be.  

The caffeine options are decent, but by comparison to other jumpin' joe joints in the vicinity, not in the vanguard in terms of coffee quality, nor barista excellence. Our sampling of hot chai latte and cappuccino left us feeling like we had tasted better elsewhere recently.  Still, the lemon pound cake was tasty, and the ability to sit back and watch this part of the Universe go by was a pleasant timeout.  Just wish we were holding ceramic rather than paper cups to enhance to quality of the experience. 

There are ever more coffee outlets in the expanding urbansphere, and they all try to outdo each other with service, product, and atmospherics. Higher Grounds has the advantage of being an early provider in this neck of the woods, but also the disadvantage of staking its claim before cafes became more popular and the customers more demanding.  

If it was open to suggestion, a gentle makeover with heavy cleaning, fresh paint, and a competition to select the best available local roasted coffee, would raise the expectations here to better account for the changing java life in Philadelphia.

The old furniture is reminiscent of grandma's house, and should stay.

Devil's Acre Tavern is a very attractive reuse of an old roadhouse along Easton Road (Rt. 611), Plumsteadville, PA. It takes it name from the nearby Devil's Half Acre, originally a stone tavern built in the 18th Century close on the Delaware River that sold alcohol and other services to the river traffic navigating upstream and down in a time the the river was the primary means of transportation in this part of colonial America. In fact, they had no license to make nor sell alcohol, and the joint was a place where violence and shady characters abounded. Legend and history say there were many people killed there and buried in the backyard. 

Perhaps, to lessen the reliance on that unsavory history, the name was chosen without the word "Half," but the connection is not lost on those aware of these facts. Still, it appears often enough in the menu and on the walls of the establishment to hint at the local lore. 

Luckily, this house is totally legit. Ownership has created an attractive utilitarian space, German American in nature, with excellent cross section of Deutsch brews, quality cocktails, reasonable happy hour choices and a strong kitchen. We stopped in on Saturday afternoon at the start of HH, and thoroughly enjoyed the entire experience. After a little confusion with our new server about availability of happy hour and where to sit to capture those prices, everything was resolved quickly and we waited for delivery to our dining room table of Three Onion Soup, Dragon Wings and Pierogi of the Day apps/sides, and two DHA Burgers and a DHA Dog. 

Everything was very good to terrific. My stepson wouldn't share his potage, so it must have been great. We all sampled the wings @$.50 per. They were not too big, but were amply meaty with a good sweet/hot glaze with sesame seeds sprinkled on top. The pierogi were the weak link. The dough was thick, too chewy and dominated the flavor of the seasoned veggies within. Ate one and took the rest home. Maybe sour cream would have helped. 

The burgers were huge with double patties, bacon, lettuce, red onion, and their DHA sauce. Both were past the medium well finish requested, but there was still plenty of flavor and moisture. I loved the double dog with chopped red onion, dark mustard and well done bacon in a fresh crisp torpedo roll. Great taste and texture. @$5 HH price it was a star of the show. 

Devil's Acre Tavern is a 35 minute drive from home, but when in the mood for German beer and cuisine it is well worth the trip. Tuesday Burger Night sounds like a winner, too.

From its straight ahead name, to its gimmicky "Club" orientation, to the free coffee, and its semi-secret spot along the Delaware River in New Hope, Pa., Fred's Breakfast has it going on! 
It took me long enough to get there and check it out, but now that I've been, I have to say, I really like their style (or lack of it).  

There are no signs out front announcing its presence, yet the place was full on this Saturday morning at 9 am.  The front door was locked for non-members, but everyone knew that the world was invited.  Just wait for someone to open the door and go in.  Put your first name on the legal pad in the foyer and wait for it to be called.  In the meantime, pour yourself a mug of hot coffee (on the house), and look around.  There's a bakery in the corner with good looking housemade goodies, and T Shirts for sale with their logo House Labrador Retriever.  Check out the wood burning stove, and look out the large windows at the Mighty Delaware and Lambertville, NJ across the narrow truss bridge.  Plenty to keep you entertained while you wait for one of the 31 stools around the large room to become available.  Even on this crowded morn, we had adjoining spinners in about 20 minutes.  That's just the first act.

The menu is pretty much standard morning fare, with the major exception that everything is made in house.  Very tempting to try old standards and see what Fred's does with them.  So, we ordered Scrambled Eggs & Corned Beef Hash, and a Ham, Egg & Cheese on English Muffin.  The second came with a side of Hash Browns.  This is more or less a French kitchen, where everything is prepared in front of you.  It is easy to watch the staff do its thing, from making pancake batter, to buttering the toast.  Everyone knows their job and there is constant movement and teamwork.

My Corned Beef Hash was far more colorful than the normal variants.  This one had multi-colored peppers sliced into the mix, along with onion, potato and the meat.  The freshness was outstanding, and the taste a delight to my taste buds.  The scrambled were nothing special, but with a splash of hot sauce they were fine.  The English muffin was supersized and full of nooks and crannies.  It held its contents well, despite the load of sliced grilled ham, fried egg and American cheese.  Strong flavor along with the crunch.  Thomas's could learn a thing or two about improving their product.  The hash browns were plentiful and well cooked, with enough dark nibs and tenderness to be a textural as well as a tasteful side. 

The house closes at 11.  Plan accordingly.

Vault Brewing Co., as the name suggests, sits in a former bank on Main Street, Yardley, Pa. 
It has been in operation for a while, and it really seems to have its act together when it comes to the art of brewing beer, and making interesting dishes in the kitchen.  It is often crowded at happy hour, but when I arrived for lunch with a friend, we had the entire vault room to ourselves, and the bar was not busy.  Sadly, because this was also a business lunch, we did not indulge in their golden liquids, but did enjoy their house made root beer.  

Service was very good, with knowledgeable and affable dude, who gave us the time needed to chat as we perused their menu.  I ordered the chicken sandwich, although the pizza offerings were tempting.
