We started with the dumplings which were cooked perfectly and really tasty.  Since I was there for the burger, I decided to try the Waygu burger - "The Rebellion."  Wow, it was really amazing.  Best burger I have had for some time.  I asked for it to be cooked medium rare and low and behold, it was cooked perfectly medium rare!  I find that rarely can I get something perfectly medium rare.  (Ha!  Pun intended.)  The bun, the aioli and even the fries were all perfect!  I was exceedingly impressed.  My friend had a spicy noodle dish and loved it although it was really spicy to him and he likes spicy food.  He raved about the flavor.

The service was similarly outstanding all along.  Definitely a solid staff and we felt very welcomed.  All in all, you MUST give it a try!  Now I understand they are awaiting their liquor license (or a liquor order - they didn't have any today) but for a new place, I understand that.  If you like the fusion cuisine(check the menu online if it is there) that involves the gastro pub idea and eastern/Thai food (Pho!), definitely give this place a try before it is SLAMMED for lunch and happy hour.  I will be back soon and often!!

One of my all time favorite Indy restaurants. Bluebeard has done an incredible job throughout the pandemic of keeping their staff safe while adapting to outdoor dining only. After over a year of their dining rooms being closed, they've reopened their indoor dining at limited capacity and the food and service did not disappoint.

The skirt steak was by far my favorite thing we had. It was seasoned and cooked to perfection on a bed of delicious couscous. Other standouts were the baby octopus and the bread pudding for dessert. We tried a few different cocktails and they were all equally good. Truly it's hard to go wrong with anything on the menu here. 

They do not take reservations and there can be a wait on the weekends but we stopped by at around 8pm on a Wednesday and were seated immediately. I would highly recommend checking them out if you haven't already!

I came here a few days after Fat Tuesday for breakfast. We sat at the bar and I asked the friendly bartender for a breakfast cocktail based mainly on bourbon. He thought for a moment, then whipped up a milky concoction that had a hint of vanilla and nutmeg. It was fantastic! On to the food (see photos)... I had the Eggs Blackstone ("A duo of poached eggs, tomato and bacon on biscuits, finished with housemade Hollandaise sauce"). It was delicious.. I'd like to confirm that the bacon was crispy! My gf got the Ruby Slipper Club ("Slow-roasted turkey breast, ham, bacon, arugula, tomato, avocado, swiss cheese & mayo, served on brioche") and that was very good, too... what a great combo of ingredients! We shared a chocolate pancake for desert... yummy. To top it off, who would have known, but the bartender was a pretty good photographer, too! He took one photo of us, then he was like "oh wait, gotta take another one to be sure!". Photos came out great! haha. So all in all, a great breakfast spot that shouldn't be too overly crowed since it's semi off the main street.

This place is awesome, the service is excellent, the food is great and... oh, the beer, yeah that's pretty fantastic as well! The staff went above and beyond to ensure my out of town guests and I were well taken care of and had the opportunity to try every beer available. 

From light Pilsner style beers to big heavy porters, this place has a beer for every type of beer lover and had some great food to satisfy your appetite.

The staff made sure to treat us right and also let us go home with a few growlers of things we loved that weren't even on the board, I highly recommend this place to beer novices, and connoisseurs alike! Happy beer tasting! :)

I'm currently staring at my phone craving the goat cheese salad I am about to tell you about. 

It was love at first sight. The grilled chicken was juicy, the goat cheese was plenty, and the sliced apples were crisp and decorated the plate. And to my pleasant surprise, I found tortellini dispersed within the salad! Now the dressing... even someone like me who (attempts to) avoid extra calories succumbed to using most of it. Ya I have tried a lot of different goat cheese salads in my life but none have come close to this.

The only reason I'm giving 4 stars is because the fried cheese and jalapeño pierogies were mediocre.

Happy hour 4-7, everyday. Graffiti bar, sampan and double knot share a kitchen so they basically have the same menu, at least for happy hour. Keep reading because it gets better. 

Sampan is ALWAYS packed for HH. My friend and I were lucky enough to walk in as two seats at the chef's table opened up. The open kitchen was a neat view because we saw everything made right in front of us! 

My friend ordered a ming mule and we shared chicken bao buns, the Vietnamese chicken satay, edamame dumplings, the Kung pao chicken wings, and the vegetarian fried rice ( secret HH item cause it's not on the menu). My favorite items are the edamame dumplings and the fried rice. The wings were average but best bang for your buck because you get about 7 wings per order. Towards the end of our meal, I laid eyes on mini ice cream cones being made for someone else. So naturally, I got one of each flavor: Vanilla latte and Nutella.

Final price with tax for 1 drink + 5 plates + 2 mini ice cream cones = $33. 

See, I told you it gets better.

I have been wanting to come here for about 2 years now. I finally got a chance the other day to come here. It's practically down town Nashville. 

Menu items ordered:  I got their fried chicken, macaroni and cheese, and baked beans. I enjoyed my chicken. I mean it was great. But, it was not the best chicken I ever had. The best chicken I have had, still goes to (Chattanooga's) Champys Fried Chicken. Champy's is down town Chattanooga just Hattie Bs is down town Nashville. Now to put this into perspective:  This is my taste of the two chicken restaurants and my personal opinion. 

On Scene:  I had to pay $8 for parking behind the restaurant because there is a parking problem here. Also, there was an annoying long line just as I turned the corner while walking up to stand in line. I was in this line for 1 Hour. Plus it took another 15 minutes to receive my order after ordering. Also, my chicken dinner was about $18. So, if you include parking, the total costs was about $25.

I have eaten here twice. I would eat here more if it wasn't so far from my work or home. I have noticed that they were busy both times that I visited. I had to park across the street both times because their parking lot was full. 

The best part about this restaurant are their "vittles" or fixins that they bring you. The vittles are the sides that they bring you which includes; onion, pickles, hush puppies, white northern beans and coleslaw. It's worth coming here just for them. 

I ordered the catfish.  It was absolutely delicious. The catfish was cooked just right. They brought some tarter sauce to dip the catfish in.  I also had catsup for hush puppies. Altogether, I really enjoyed my catfish plate and sides. 

As far as customer service is concerned. I was very well taken care of, on both visits by my waitresses.  They checked on me several times and kept my drink full at all times with sweet tea. They also bought me more of the vittles that I wanted that I was out of. These vittles or "fixins" are all you can eat. 

Tip:  One tip I would give is to come here on Sundays because this is when they have their fried chicken special. You can save money on this day if you like fried chicken. Tuesdays are when they have their catfish special. They advertise all you can eat on both these days and of course they come with the fixins or vittles.

Great customer service from the bartender. I was walking by and was surprised that this place was open. I have been seeing them working on it for about 3 months now since I been coming down town Nashville. 

I sat at the bar and was immediately waited on by the bartender. I ordered a drink and she brought it to me with a smile. I could tell she liked working here. Then, I had to ask if Kid Rock has ever been there and she said at least two times within the last two weeks. She said one of those times was on a Friday both times were unannounced. 

Information:  They are open Daily from 11am to 3am. Their phone number is 615-248-2706.  This is called Kid Rock's Big Ass Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse. Yes, I know that is a great big name but,  that is what it says on the sign outside, and on their menu that they gave me.  They listed their address as 217 Broadway on their Facebook page. However, I saw the numbers 221 stamped above their door at the front entrance. So, that was confusing but this place is big and may have taken up two old previous businesses. 

Music Venue:  They have bands that play here even during week days in the middle of the day. I was here on a Tuesday about 3pm and they had a band playing. They were great too. They played some hits of today's entertainment society too.

Wow it's unbelievable how much of a disappointment this hotel was. We wouldn't even expect this from a 3-star hotel, much less from the Ritz Carlton Bacara which is a 5-star hotel with rates over $1k for a weekend night. This is the first time we ever spent this much on a hotel, but one of the worst hotels we've ever stayed at.

1. Bell boy LOST my Chanel shoes which were on the bed of the luggage cart and did not notice. When I asked the hotel to check their footage, they found that they delivered my shoes to the wrong room!!
2. Our shower drain was completely clogged and took the maintenance person 2 hours to fix. We could not shower until 10PM and the water pressure was also very weak. 
3. Two separate hotel restaurants messed up our reservations for dinner and breakfast. They even confirmed our breakfast reservations then told us our time was 4 hours later when we arrived.
4. At the restaurants, multiple staff members were wearing ill-fitting cloth masks that slid off and exposed their noses, which made us very uncomfortable amidst the pandemic. We picked this hotel hoping at the very least, COVID precautions and cleanliness would be upheld to a higher standard. 
5. The sheet was stained (see picture) and so was one of the bath towels.
6. MOLD on the sink faucet!! (See picture)
7. Pull-out sofa bed was in terrible condition and the springboard was unusable. Parts of the springs were broken and hurt to lie on. A bed in this condition should be replaced at any hotel!!

Overall, we left incredibly disappointed and disheartened at what a complete waste of money and time it was to stay at the Ritz Carlton Bacara. We will not be returning and do not recommend this hotel at all.

WOW love this place! Not only do they have a private parking lot, making it easy to access, but the food is amazing!

This restaurant is beautifully decorated including a cool fun bar, which is lite up with blue neon lighting, giving the place a sense of excitement! You have the option to either sit inside or outside. Outside seating includes either bar seating or table seating, in which, the lattice roof allows for open sky views. They also have fans located outside, for those warm Florida days.

They are open:

Monday 11am-10pm
Tuesday-Thursday 11am-11pm
Friday & Saturday 11am-1am
Sunday 11am-10pm
Brunch 11am-3pm, Saturday & Sunday

From the menu there were several plates ordered for sharing, including:

Chips Y Trio: Chile con queso, Salsa Veracruz, and freshly made Salsa

Colossal Lump Crab Cake: Pan seared & served with a spicy sweet honey Sriracha sauce, onion, cilantro & red bell pepper

Goat Cheese Balls: Rolled in breadcrumb seasoning & flash-fried, served over Guajillo marinara sauce, then topped with Mexica crema & cilantro.

Seafood Stuffed Avocado: Half an Avocado, fresh or tempura fried stuffed with blue lump crabmeat & shrimp. Topped with remoulade sauce, then garnished with red bell pepper, red onion & jalapeno. Severed on a bed of arugula.

Surf & Turf tacos: Flour tortilla with blackened shrimp, steak & potato topped with queso fresco, salsa cruda & cilantro

I must say Every dish was extremely Fresh and Delicious, if I lived in Tampa i would visit this place frequently, as the Margaritas were tasty as well! hehee...They also offer a -5 degree tequila shot, which sounds awesome and I definitely plan to try next time. ;D

I definitely would like to experience Brunch here, as it seems like it would be lots of fun and I KNOW the food and drinks will be great! 

So if you find yourself in Tampa, this is a must!
The only thing I liked about the restaurant is they offer uni in this area, which is a rare found, but rest of them are bad cuz seaweed are too soft and rice are not firm.

This is definitely a good place to stop in Santa Barbara for a great meal. I have only been here twice but I have been very satisfied with both of my experiences here. It's a nice location with seating for indoor or outdoor dining. I have done both. I have to say that if you can, go for the outside seating. It's quite nice. The food is well made and it's well, great! They have a large menu with many items to choose from. So everyone in your group should be able to find something that works for them. The staff is prompt with good, friendly service too. I would recommend making a reservation just in case. It may not always be necessary but, it's definitely good to plan ahead. Give it a try. I think you will enjoy it!

Gourmet tacos and some of the best I have ever had.  They have so many different types .  I liked the braised short ribs and fish tacos the best.  The cauliflower was interesting too.  Give that a try for something different.  Stop by here if you are in the area it is worth it for a snack or meal.  Not expensive and casual.

Beautiful store with lots of middle eastern desserts.  Tried some baklava and Turkish delight.  I was a little disappointed in the baklava.  It didn't have the honey flavor plus it was soggy.  Everything was just okay.

I was definitely really excited to try out the new taco place in town. Kirkwood just doesn't have as many good, non-chain options to get food other than your typical burger/pub type of joint. Located right in the heart of town, it was definitely a different vibe than I expected. The first thing- loud pumping music outside. Loud enough that you couldn't really talk to the person you were with. I guess they were not kidding with the "Club" part of "Club Taco.

You order the tacos up at the counter and then they bring them out to you. I think they are still figuring out logistics but the staff there were attentive. A nice touch was that they offered to bring us some hot sauce and did, which we liked. The folks were all very friendly and answered my wife's questions. 

They had several unique taco options that we tried. Yes they are pricier, but these aren't typical tacos. And in fact if you wanted cheaper ones like a traditional chicken/steak tinga taco, they had those for $3. The chicken tinga, while simple, ended up being one of my favorites; had a ton of flavor and the chicken was moist. But yes, other options are more expensive between $4-6/taco. When you order a korean style taco with kimchi on it or a shrimp one with fried avocado, those ingredients are more expensive. Roll with it. If you don't want to pay that, go to Taco Bell.

Overall the tacos were good, nice to see some unique flavors. The Korean style one was a bit of a miss for me compared to other Korean places in the area. They had a veggie one with portabellas that we thought was very good and would get again. The pork belly taco was excellent. I'm excited to try some of the other ones out in a future visit like the Carnitas. I also recommend trying the corn casserole side, grilled sweet corn with queso. Yum.

A cool feature about this place? The walk up window to get beers or cocktails. That's kind of neat. But... just a little out of place? The music was just too loud. The party guy part of of me really likes this place and would do this on a weekend with some drinks and friends. The part of me that wants to bring my wife and kid for a more relaxing chill weekday evening says, maybe not so much. Kudos to these folks for trying out a new concept; I look forward to seeing how it goes and will be back.

I'm a pretty regular patron at PB's, and haven't had anything to complain about until the day before yesterday - minor or not, it lost my business.

I went there with my boyfriend for a quick bite to eat, and was quickly greeted by a male server who said he would be with us in a few minutes.  More than "a few minutes" go by, so I ask the hostess if she can do me a solid and grab the male server who greeted us.  An older female server comes up and says she'll be right with us and that she's our server - miscommunication much?  I've worked in many a restaurant and was under the impression that servers had sections.  

Anyways, we order our beer and food - the latter of which was awful.  How can you screw up a grilled cheese sandwich?  The chef at PB's has written the book on it.  Last time I checked the cheese should be melted and not still in squares (see attached picture).  This is one of the easier sandwiches to make, and you think it's acceptable to it send out to a table half-cooked and luke warm?  Thank god I did't order anything with meat or it might have been undercooked, too.

Not worth the time!!! Had a large group of people here for lunch during the week, service was poor and manager was rude. Try to up charge me from prices on special menu provided to our group, which had a very limited selection!! Don't waste your time or money at this soon to go out of business place, unless service and management change.

Poor service, over priced food!! Poor management!!

So my family came here for my Mom's Birthday last week and the experience was not good.  

The New York strip steak was too oily, because they slathered oily mushrooms all over the top of it.  I'm confident a steak from my grill would have been better.

The fresh fish was also caked in spices that was too overpowering.  I'm not sure if the choice was to celebrate the spices, or the fish.

Lastly, the icing on the cake or, in this instance, lack there of - is that although we told the waitress it was my Mom's birthday (and granted we didn't order desert because they were already upset with the meal) the waitress brought back a Plank of wood with a candle on it.  What restaurant brings a plank of wood?  It's like at least substitute a cookie or something.  Ugh *facepalm.

One of my new favorite places.

This place was amazing, no scratch that, it was ah-may-zing! The food, the drinks, the atmosphere - it was all perfection. We came at about 7 p.m. on a Thursday and it was hopping! You know that when a place is in the middle of nowhere and busy on a Thursday night that it has to be good.

FLIGHTS - You can pick your own beers to make your own flight! I'm not a beer connoisseur so it is hard for me to speak to the beers, but I made a flight of all dark beer and I enjoyed every single one. 

FOOD - We got the Carmelized Beer Nuts, Ahi Poke tuna, BBQ Falafel Balls, IPA Steamed Mussels, Kung Pao Jumbo Chicken Wings, and the Big Storm Sliders. We were four girls and guy after Zumba, we needed our nourishment. Everything was delicious! The fries are shoestring, which is my favorite. The mussels were great and came with bread to soap up the butter. The Ahi Poke Tuna has a wasabi sauce which adds a nice kick. Literally, everything was delicious and even though I know this is a brewery, I would come back here for the food. 

SERVICE - The service is slow. There is no designated waiter for the tables so it is a bit of a free for all. Come here to relax and spend time with friends, don't come here when you're on a time crunch (or if you are, tell one of the servers upfront). 

This is one of my new favorite places in the area. If you want to check out a brewery that has awesome food and great beer, look no further.

Treat yourself to some pie!

I'm going to start by admitting I thought this place was like In N Out Burger - you have a basic menu of burger, fries, and milkshakes. In reality, this place is like a diner! However, because I wanted to taste test what they are known for best, I went with a burger and pie.

This restaurant has a great indoor outdoor flow. I hope they've thought through the summer months, but in April it was absolutely perfect. It gives the space a great feng shui. 

We sat right next to the pie display and man did it make me jones for something sweet. That's how I ended up ordering a burger and pie. Yes, that is not a typo, I did not order a burger and fries, I ordered a burger and pie. And I'm still patting myself on the back for doing so.

I went with the original burger and it was good. It tasted exactly how a burger should. It's not huge, but I also think we, as Americans, have warped views on the size of meals, so I appreciated the burger size. The Butterscotch Pie is amazing. It is super sweet, so if you are on the fence about sugar, don't get it, but if you love your sweets, dive in! It was fluffy and creamy in all the right places. I want to taste test all the pies!

I came at about 4 p.m. on a Friday and it was pretty empty. If you tried to come before and was deterred by the line, it's time to try again. I think the crazy hype has died down and now you should be able to find a seat!

A little pricey, but the frosting is where it's at.

I am a huge sugarholic and I love frosting. Cake has to be really really good to tickle my fancy, so the fact that these cupcakes are about half frosting really appeals to me. I have to be honest, I don't buy dessert that often. I have surprisingly strong willpower when I have to purchase something sweet. At home, where I have a ton of sugar, I have no willpower (I've already taken a break from writing this review to eat two types of Ben and Jerry's Ice cream and Ghirardelli chocolate). Now that I've tried these cupcakes, I'm pretty screwed, because they were a solid hit for me and I see myself returning every time I'm in the area.

I love that they have mini cupcakes and they are probably better for my waistline, but when I get dessert I go big so the normal sized cupcakes are for me. I did try the mini version of the red velvet and it was great. However, my love is reserved for the salted caramel cupcake. Holy mackerel was it amazing. Warning, it will give you diabetes, immediately. 

I love the combination of salt and sweet. If you don't love (like really love) sweet things, do not get the salted caramel. It is extremely sweet, but the salted part makes sure it doesn't get cloyingly sweet. If you like things a little less sugary, the dark chocolate has the slight bitter flavor of dark chocolate. For dark chocolate fans, like myself, it is a welcome relief. I've also tried a cookie cupcake and it was also exceptional - very sweet like the salted caramel. 

So, although I've enjoyed every cupcake I've gotten, I'm going to have to go back time and time again to the salted caramel. These cupcakes are about half frosting and half cupcake. This is the perfect ratio to me. I'm a huge frosting fan. 

The cupcakes are on the pricier side, but the way I can tell they are worth it to me is I would definitely buy it again. I will be back for my salted caramel cupcake.

Five stars for their selection and hot deli sandwiches.

I can see how this place gets crowded. We went for lunch on a Wednesday. When we got there at about 11:45 p.m. there was space at the deli counter to order. By noon when we got the sandwiches it was turning into elbow people to get through territory. I can't even imagine what this would be like on a weekend! 

First of all, the deli section is CHEAP. My friend got some sides and I thought they were $11 for a small container, I misread it, they were a little over ONE dollar. Mind. blown. The sandwiches were $6 each. Anywhere else it would be over $10. Five stars for the price. 

I tried four sandwiches, the Caprese, the Reuben, the Philly, and the Meatball. My ranking is I liked the Caprese best, then the Philly, the Reuben and then the Meatball. My dad liked the Reuben, the Philly, the Caprese, then the Meatball. We both liked the Meatball so that tells you how spectacular the other sandwiches were. This also shows you that each person will have their particular tastes, but all the sandwiches are spectacular. 

I loved the Caprese because the mozzarella was so dang fresh. I wish I bought balls of it to bring home now. The Philly had a great amount of cheese. The Reuben slathered on the thousand island dressing and was super flavorful. The Meatball had giant meatballs. All the sandwiches are incredibly filling. The bread really put these sandwiches over the top. I eat a lot and one of these sandwiches would fill me up. 

The way it works is you grab a number at the deli, they call your number so you can order, then they call your number again when it is ready, then you take it outside to pay. You can't buy grocery items at the outside check out line. There is a covered patio with mist spraying where you can sit and eat.

The market itself is really impressive. They have so much cheese, wine, fresh pasta, etc.

Great vegetarian options that fulfill my fast food cravings without making me feel terrible.

Currently, my unborn child does not like meat. Once we found out I was having a boy my husband immediately told me I needed to start eating meat to sustain his son. Hard pass. So when I was hunting for a restaurant to grab a meal before a Yelp Event I needed one with vegetarian options. 

It's super hit or miss right now about what seems appetizing. For example I am currently eating a lunch of trail mix. South Howard has a couple solid vegetarian options, but the moment I thought of a vegetarian burger and fries from EVOS I was sold. 

First of all, I feel pretty comfortable that EVOS takes its commitment to healthy food seriously. I've spoken with the owner and he makes my love of health and fitness look like child's play. Right now I am super aware of what I'm putting in my body (which means every bad food decision I make, I make deliberately. I'm not going to lie and say I'm eating super clean and healthy but at least I see and acknowledge the good food and then say nope). Sometimes I just want a burger and fries and I know that EVOS will give me a healthier version than your average fast food place.

I also have to point out I don't mind paying for quality. My burger and fries (no drink) came out to about $9. I was actually happy that my fries size was a small portion. I shouldn't be stuffing my face full of fries anyways. Yes, it is on the pricier side than your average "fast food", but this ain't your average fast food. I walked in knowing I'd be paying a little more. Also, pro tip, they have some awesome deals happening, like their meatless Monday BOGO deal, so if you want to save some moula then check them out on a certain day.

The place is really clean and the walls are decorated in a bright happy mural. I was there at about 4:30 p.m. (I eat at weird times when I have Yelp Events), and I was one of two tables. 

Ok, so I wrote all of this without discussing the food. The vegetarian burger was phenomenal. I have to say I don't eat many vegetarian burgers (this whole vegetarian thing is new to me), but it really hit the spot. I also enjoyed the fries. Was it as delicious as your fried in hot oil version? No, but I thought it was a good substitute. There are also a couple different ketchup options. I went with the garlic one and loved it. Even the ketchup containers are portion controlled! I had to go back to get more ketchup. (I see you, one ketchup should have been enough decision, and I respectfully decided to get more). 

They really need a location closer to where I live. You better believe I'm going to be capitalizing on meatless Mondays!

Tender meat, delicious sides, huge portions - you better clear your calendar for the rest of the day, because you will be sleeping this meal off.

Thank you, Yelp for finding me this juicy BBQ. I was meeting an old coworker for lunch and to be nice I looked up restaurants near his place of work. I wasn't picky about what type of food, I just wanted it to be good and cheap! Up popped Konan BBQ. I had never heard of it before and I used to work in one of the International Plaza Corporate Buildings. Heck, my old coworker had never heard of this before and he drives on Lois every day on average four times a day! (The building is a street removed from Lois.)

I called my coworker to let him know I was running a couple minutes late. (He doesn't have unlimited texting. Come into the 21st century, Chris!) He told me to hurry up, because he might get shot. I didn't really register that comment until I turned the corner onto Hubert. You probably won't get shot (don't hold me liable if you do), but I think there is a solid chance you could score drugs around here - hard drugs. Semi-joking aside, this is not the nicest neighborhood. There are groups of young men hanging outside in the middle of the workday, however, I never felt like I was in any danger, so chalk it up to the authenticity of the place.

There is seating inside and you probably never have to worry about finding a seat, because most people take their BBQ to go. You don't even really have to worry about parking, because even though it is a small lot, most people are from the neighborhood and just walk in. It is a random, remote location, but it works, because it has the support of the locals.

This is not the place for a business lunch. Dirt doesn't both me. Darkness (we didn't know that we were allowed to turn on lights until someone did halfway through our meal) isn't a problem. Noise - think blaring Jay Z and Beyonce - could make hearing your dining companion a little problematic. Since I was with a friend, we had no problem shouting over the music, however, if you are trying to impress a business companion/client, this could be an issue. You have been warned.

The food is cheap and delicious. I got the Chicken Dinner with sides of collard greens and coleslaw. My friend got Ribs Dinner with sides of mac and cheese and potato salad. Guess who got to try four different sides! I love when my dining companions order different choices. My total was $9.90. I don't really understand why, since on the menu it is $10, unless tax works backwards here, but this seems like a go with the flow place so I chalked it up, again, to authenticity. 

Environmentalists beware, even if you eat here you will receive plastic cutlery and a Styrofoam container and cup. This hurts my heart a little.

Pro tip: get the BBQ sauce on the side. They slather it on. The chicken was amazing enough without it. It was super juicy and tender. The collard greens were a little salty and the coleslaw was on the sweet side, but when I paired it altogether it complemented each other nicely. Both the mac and cheese and potato salad were solid choices. None of them outright wowed me, so I'd probably try two other sides next time. You get two pieces of wonder bread with your meal.

This joint definitely rivals all the best BBQ places in town. You have to check it out.

Writing a review for the best past - the beer.

Long story short for the background, I chose a place in Ybor for brunch and upon getting there we found out it doesn't open till noon. It was 11 a.m. We decided to go to TBBC to drink until noon. This ended up being a great idea.

One random thing is they have a full bar, but they don't have a liquor drink list. This is a bit diva of me, but I don't like creating my own drinks. I like reading a menu and deciding which delightful cocktail really speaks to my soul at the moment. This doesn't work if I'm just ordering a vodka cran. I totally understand why a place known for their beer doesn't create a drink menu so it doesn't bother me, I just find it funny. You do you, TBBC! 

I don't drink beer a ton, but when I do I go for a chocolate stout. They had two options so I tried both and went with the hazelnut espresso one. It was really good! It was a fun time just sitting at the bar chatting with a friend while sipping a good beer. 

The bartender seemed like a great guy. He was friendly, chatted every so often, but didn't try to insert himself in our conversation. 

I really like this place to just grab a beer.

Future Christina, get the yellow curry with coconut cream.

I'm very happy with my choice of dishes. I asked my friend, who's pregnant and nauseous, what she felt like eating since she was coming over to help me go through baby clothes. (Yes, I'm pregnant, my friends are pregnant, basically everyone is pregnant.) She said she was able to eat Vietnamese right now. Being that I've eaten at Thinh Anh almost every week (no lie) I decided to branch out and suggest Pho Quyen. Hence, here we are.

The majority of the day I thought I was going to go with the beef and rice dish. I made a last minute decision to go with the yellow curry with coconut cream. I'm usually not so impulsive, but I had a hunch. Also, Uber Eats told me that it was a popular dish (which I can see why). I also got an avocado smoothie with boba. 

This is one of those dishes that I think ok, I'll eat half of it and put it away. I ate almost all of it. It's that good. I did save some of it and ate it about an hour ago cold and it was still delicious. I should always remember how much I love coconut curry dishes. I got it with chicken (which Uber Eats did not have highlighted as a popular choice of meat, but I rebelled) and it was amazing. There were huge chunks of chicken in it. I even ate the bell peppers and I normally hate bell peppers. 

The avocado smoothie was also delicious, but I haven't met an avocado smoothie I disliked yet. 

Uber Eats delivered it 10 minutes ahead of schedule. I will definitely order from here again and soon.

A dream for someone with food restrictions.

I have to admit, I was not that aware of how sensitive places are to people with food allergies until I had my baby and have to cut out dairy and soy. Fun fact, dairy and soy are in pretty much everything. I now mainly eat salad with no dressing. (Totally kidding, I think I've actually gained weight since he was diagnosed with the food sensitivity because I found all the chips that are soy/dairy free, but I digress.) I've been very wary about eating out because I'm worried about hidden dairy and soy. Turns out FK caters to people like me and my eyes are now opened to the endless possibilities of eating there on a dairy/soy free diet.

Their menu already reflects if something is dairy free, gluten free, sugar free, and vegan friendly. This alone is amazing. I had to ask what was soy free, but the people serving the food were super knowledgeable. 

I couldn't get the sweet potato noodles because it has soy, but they said everything else that is dairy free was also soy free for the bases. I chose kale slaw and cauliflower mash. For veggies, my only choice was the buffalo cauliflower and roasted mushrooms so that made it easy. Proteins I got the baked almond chicken and the chia seed tuna poke (turns out their tuna isn't soy free, so don't make that mistake if you are on a soy free diet. If you aren't, it is still delicious), and all their sauces are soy free (holla) so I got the creamy white ginger. I felt like I was cheating my diet everything was so delicious! The only thing I was on the fence about is the buffalo cauliflower, but that's because it has a kick to it and I don't like spice at all. Next time I'll go double roasted mushrooms and there will definitely be a next time because I am in love. I wish I could just order platters of the baked almond chicken and dip it in the creamy white ginger sauce. My mouth is watering just thinking about it. 

It was moderately busy on Saturday at lunch time. I thought this place might be only busy on the weekdays when the work crowd is around, but it seems like people are willing to drive to eat here (for good reason.) It was still super quick to go through the line and get my bowl. The huge parking lot in the back is a plus. I managed to find a spot in the front and it was pretty easy pulling out, I just had to wait for the cars to get a red light at Westshore. 

For someone like me who has been super paranoid about going out to eat, this place is amazing. I thought dairy free/soy free would mean I had to eat super bland food, but that's not the case at all. I would definitely recommend this place to people with or without food allergies.

Impressive array of sugary sweets!

I actually came here for ice cream. We had just eaten a giant lunch at Yummy House South but they were out of egg tarts. They said it would take about 20 minutes to make more (and I bet we sat there for about 19 minutes talking before we decided to leave). Anyways, the point is I didn't get anything sweet to end my meal. 

Now, normally this isn't an issue, but since I'm pregnant I've taken on the viewpoint that I should never be deprived of anything.  I told my husband that I wanted ice cream and who would argue with a pregnant person.  I pulled up Yelp because I don't like going to chain places when I can help it. I saw that Dough was nearby and had ice cream so I pulled it up on maps and we took off.

Spoiler alert, I didn't end up getting ice cream. They only have a couple flavors, which really isn't that big an issue, but none of them appealed to me. I like ice cream that contains different ingredients like nuts, fudge, chocolate chips, etc. Ice cream that is all one consistency doesn't really do it for me. I'm sure having limited options ensures all their choices are spectacular, but I decided to forgo the ice cream.

Luckily, they have a huge selection of doughnuts as well! I think this is actually what Dough is known for. I have a confession to make, I am a huge apple fritter fanatic. There was a time when I was in high school where I wrote into the Houston Chronicle (newspapers were a thing back then) asking for recommendations about where I should go to get an apple fritter. I then dragged three friends to make a forty-minute road trip to get apple fritters at 7 a.m. (I heard they run out fast). When I saw that Dough had apple fritters I was both intrigued and frightened. I already have such a huge bar set for apple fritters was it worth trying it from here and rating the place based on a pastry that is held so dear to my heart?

Yes, I got the apple fritter. I usually like my apple fritters more crispy than doughy, but this one really impressed me. It was doughy but it wasn't dry at all. I'm not about to wax poetics about this apple fritter because it would get weird fast, but just know that Dough does dough well. 

I would definitely suggest coming here and trying something made of dough. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

Great sushi and hibachi dinner.

My husband's boss graciously bought us dinner to reward my husband for how hard he has been working. I gave my husband three options and he chose this one. This is what we ordered:

Spring roll appetizer - came three to an order and it was nicely fried. It was crispy and there wasn't a lot of excess grease. 
Make your own hibachi combo with chicken and filet mignon medium, salad, and added extra yum yum sauce - We decided this wasn't the best we've had, but not the worst. It was pretty average for hibachi. 
Side of fried rice - I really liked their fried rice. I'm glad we got an extra order. 
Philly roll - this is your basic philly roll. Nothing eye opening, but then again, when is it ever?
Pinky Dragon Roll - It's hard to judge rolls with tempura shrimp in it since it had to be delivered. I think this would be pretty amazing when fresh, but it was still good. 
Amazing Roll - This was my favorite roll. I will definitely get it again. I thought there was shredded crab on top, but when I went back to look at the menu it's topped with seared tuna. Whatever the ingredients are, it is absolutely delicious.
Salmon sashimi - again, hard to judge since it was delivered and packaged in the same box as a cooked roll, but it was still good. 

Since it is locally owned, it is $0 delivery fee if you use UberEats. That's how I'm deciding where I order from, I want to make sure the restaurant is owned locally. 

Once I feel safe eating in restaurants, I want to go here to try the sushi fresh!

Top notch place to get brunch.

First of all, shout out to our server. What's pretty funny is I was going to spell her name Katia, but upon reading my friend's reviews we have so far spelled her named Cadea, Caddea, and Cadia. At least they have the excuse that they were drinking bottomless mimosas. I was completely sober, being pregnant, and I'm probably the most off in terms of spelling. Mad props to our server for deftly handling a group of eight girls drinking and celebrating a birthday. Even though we were there for a long time, I never felt rushed and we were constantly checked upon.

I had a long time to look at the menu. Not only do I study menus before arriving at a restaurant, but the birthday girl got there about 45 minutes after us because it was a surprise birthday so she didn't see any reason to rush. I bounced back between so many different dish choices during that time. I love a menu where I want to try many different things and you will find that here. That's also what saved us when it turns out they ran out of tater tots. It was a little disappointing because people rave about their tots, but with such a large menu it is easy to find something else you'll enjoy. 

I ended up being healthy, you're welcome unborn baby, and I went with the egg white scramble. I thought for the price the dishes would end up being on the smaller side. Not true. Although the egg white scramble looked a bit small at first, it ended up being exceptionally filling. I was starving and I left full! Everyone else's dishes looked big and they all raved about them.

The real reason you need to check this place out is it is locally owned and operated. I love supporting local businesses. I ended up purchasing a gift card for my contact at The Don CeSar because this is exactly the type of business that Yelp supports. 

Unfortunately, living in Westchase, Chill is about 45 minutes from me. However, if anyone ever asks for a suggestion of a place to eat near St. Pete Beach or if we are ever in the area, you better believe we will stop by.

Delicious, made with love, and cheap!

For less than ten dollars you will come out full and happy. I feel like I can just end the review here and that should convince you to go. Not convinced? Fine, I'll give you more details.

The woman who was working the counter, presumably one of the owners, is a joy. She continuously had a smile on her face as she put out menus on the table. I thought we would be ordering at the counter, but I guess since there was only one other table and we were dining in they gave us personalized service. If every waitress was as jolly as her then I would always be a happy camper. 

My friend and I split the Falafel sandwich meal (which came with fries) and the Chicken Shawarma Bowl. The food came out pretty quickly. I loved both immensely. If you put a gun to my head and asked me to choose one over the other, I would probably go with the Chicken Shawarma Bowl. The rice was so good (which probably means it wasn't healthy for me). There was a generous portion of chicken too. The Falafel came with a cucumber, tomato salad. My friend asked if it was pre made because he doesn't eat cucumbers. I'm not sure if it is or not, but they made one special for him without the cucumbers! Top notch service.

This place is on the smaller side, but it wasn't busy at all during prime time lunch rush on a Thursday. I loved this place so much that I recommended it to a friend and she went the next day and loved it to! (Although, tbh, if a friend goes to a place that you recommend and doesn't like it, would she really say anything? I'm betting she's being honest because this place is awesome).

I chose this place based on Yelp reviews and I'm adding to them so others recognize what a fantastic place this is. Thanks Yelp for bringing me here!

Huge portion sizes for cheap.

Major four takeaways (this actually started as major two takeaways but as I wrote the review I kept remembering more important facts), the outside looks super sketch (it is much nicer inside), bring cash because your meal may cost less than $10 (which is their credit card minimum), service can be slow, just don't be afraid to flag people down (and in my case, we loved the slow service because we were catching up) and the pho is huge and satisfying.

One major lesson I learned is even though it is only 75 cents to get a large, if you aren't going to eat that much just don't do it. I ate all the meat and took home the noodles and broth for lunch the next day. It does not taste as good the next day. Of course, this isn't their fault since they make it hot and it should be eaten right away, but now I know that I don't like leftover pho!

OUTSIDE: If you have friends who are afraid about being mugged, give them a heads up that it is much nicer inside than outside. I told my friends this (since I read all your reviews like a good Yelper does) and I STILL received a text saying that the outside looked scary when my first friend pulled up. She did send a second text saying that the inside was much better. Maybe it wasn't my best life choice to choose this place to meet a friend who has a two-year-old, but once you get inside you'll feel better! I'm helping to build that two-year-old's character.

SERVICE: Yes, service can be slow. Honestly I didn't notice because we were a super slow table. I loved that we could just sit here forever and chat and they would never bring us the check until we ask. I didn't feel rushed at all. On the flip side if you are looking to get in and out this may be a negative, but it didn't bother me one bit. Just come in with eyes wide open that this is the price you may have to pay for good pho.

PHO: It's huge. Like two meals huge. I did upgrade 75 cents for the large, but like I said at the beginning I probably won't do that again because I've learned that pho isn't made to be leftovers. I did take a picture of the large and regular side by side so you can see. The regular is perfectly big enough. The pho was great. I got the number 11 (please don't make me type out the name) and it was amazing. I loved all the meet that was included. Yes, there was tons of fat on certain pieces, but I am a huge fat lover. 

PRICE: It's cheap! For $11 (including tip) I got a large bowl of pho that lasted me two days. That's legit.

I really like this place. It is definitely high on my list to go to when I need a pho fix!

Mediocre food, but a ton of variety.

My husband has been dying to come here since we moved to Tampa Bay. I have to be in the right mood for a buffet, so I kept vetoing his suggestion. Finally, he just put it on my calendar. No joke, he called it "The Feast" and scheduled us to be here for three hours. No to the three hours part, but I accepted that I couldn't avoid coming here any longer. I ended up being pleasantly surprised.

We came here for lunch. It was $9.99 a person. Reading other reviews and seeing that it is $17 a person, I don't think I could stomach that price for the quality of food here. However, $9.99 was reasonable and deserving of four stars to me. 

I actually took photos of every station they had during lunch. It was a pretty awesome variety. I started with the sushi stations, which had a ton of options, made my way to the cooked food, and ended with dessert. Ok, I ended with two plates of dessert. It's very random, but they have egg tarts and chinese doughnuts with the non dessert food. They also have a station of fruit. 

Nothing really stood out to me. Everything was mediocre, but I honestly wasn't expecting anything amazing. It was all solid. I did enjoy the coconut shrimp and krab and cheese (I know, in my head the krab and cheese sounds disgusting, but it was oddly enjoyable). They also have a hibachi station where they make it on the spot, but we missed seeing it. It's right next to the sushi. 

Even though nothing was really good, nothing was bad either. I ate everything I put on my plate. The egg tart tasted weird, but I still finished it, which means I didn't hate it. 

It wasn't that busy on a Saturday around noon so there were no lines at all. 

The price is right for what it offers. If my husband suggests coming here again, I'd be fine going.

Delicious buffet with great options.

This is one of those reviews that I'm writing right away because I'm pretty sure if I go a couple days I won't remember what I ate. Even now, I can't tell you the real names of the dishes, but I'll describe them the best I can. Should I have taken pictures of all the name cards? Yes, if I was a better Yelper I would, but sometimes I do get a little self conscious of snapping a million pictures especially when I'm with non Yelpers so I toned down the photos. (You should never do what I do and instead go ahead and get all the pictures!)

I'm been avoiding meat since getting pregnant because the baby seems to be a budding vegetarian so that ruled out a pretty good chunk of the dishes. I was definitely still pleased with my options afterwards. I stuck to a main three - a dahl that was my absolute favorite, a yellow vegetarian dish that tasted like coconut, and a red curry paneer. Usually I always see palak paneer at buffets, which is my go-to, but they didn't have it here (I'm pretty ignorant on regions and types of food so please forgive me if palak paneer is only served in certain regions). These three dishes more than made up for that fact. They even had coconut rice which was an awesome complement to the normal basmati rice, which they also had. They had a fried onion patty type thing which I also enjoyed and I grabbed some naan. This was my ideal meal and every time I come I'm sticking to it!

We got here a little after opening and it was pretty empty. By the time we left at about 12:30 p.m. it was getting more crowded, but not to the point that you'll have trouble finding a seat. There are plenty of tables.

This is now one of my favorite Indian buffets in Tampa Bay. I think the fact that the three dishes I ate were so unique in flavor really stood out to me. Also that coconut rice is pretty clutch. 

The service was fantastic. I've never been checked on so often (don't worry, it wasn't an annoying amount) and my water never got low. 

If anyone wants to try this Indian buffet, I'm in!

Great variety of meat.

I have to write this review comparing it to Terra Gaucha. They are two major churrasco, Brazilian steakhouses, in the area. When I gave Terra Gaucha five stars I realized I needed to come back and give Texas de Brazil five stars, because my husband and I agreed that all things considered we like this place a smidge better.

My husband loves Brazilian steakhouses. If I ever ask him where he wants to eat he will say a Brazilian steakhouse. Therefore, I'd say we have quite a few experiences to compare this one to. 

Where Terra Gaucha beats Texas de Brazil: Variety of meats. We noticed that they brought out a diverse set of meat pretty quickly. It wasn't just cow, cow, different type of cow, cow. They had lamb, chicken heart, sausage, etc. 

Where Texas de Brazil beats Terra Gaucha: The price is about the same, but Texas de Brazil now includes unlimited coke products and dessert and their dessert is pretty dang good. I know, you think who can eat dessert after all that meat. Well, I can, and you can also bring it home and eat that giant carrot cake later. 

Also, Texas de Brazil has the best scalloped potatoes. I actually enjoy their salad bar better. There is just more food I want to eat on their salad bar. I can forgo the meat at Texas de Brazil and spend less to just eat the salad bar. At Terra Gaucha I felt like I had to have the meat too to make it a complete meal. 

So, if you come mainly for the meat, Terra Gaucha should be your pick. If you like the extras, Texas de Brazil wins.

Solid breakfast/diner food.

I enjoy diner food. A greasy heaping of eggs, potatoes, and meat is all I really need in life and the cheaper the better. Skyway Café definitely fulfills my requirements. 

I heard this place can get really busy, but at 11:30 a.m. on a Tuesday there were still plenty of tables available. There were people in shorts and t-shirts and people in business casual clothes - there's really no dress code. 

I went with the Vegetable Skillet with a biscuit. Next time I think I'll try the cornbread. The biscuit was fluffy, whereas I enjoy my biscuits a little more flakey and dense. The Vegetable Skillet was a great portion of potatoes, eggs, and vegetables. It was a hearty meal and I ended up with some to take home! My friend got pancakes with blueberries and bananas and they looked huge and so fluffy! I had food envy looking at it. If you're a pancake person, you should definitely try it here. 

They bring you your check but you take it to the counter to pay. Our server was great - my water glass was never empty. 

Overall, I like this place and will come here to get my breakfast food fix!

Great new addition to this strip.

I have to be honest, I never went to any of the restaurants that occupied this space before. We live about five minutes away, but none of them ever appealed to me. I think since I heard good things about the Crabby Bill's in Clearwater Beach that I was more open to trying here. I am definitely glad I did. 

Since I wasn't eating dairy or soy at the time, I had to be very picky about what I tried. Our waiter, Alex, was fantastic. I felt like the kitchen wasn't doing a good job helping him figure out what I could eat, so he went above and beyond with his own deductive reasoning and asking other waitstaff. If you have dietary restrictions I wouldn't suggest eating here because it took a lot of questions to figure out that I couldn't eat the octopus salad. Luckily this doesn't pertain to a huge percent of the population so eat away!

I ended up going with the Boiled Shrimp starter since it was just shrimp and Old Bay seasoning. Sounds meh, right? It was delicious! I feel like this is a dish I should be able to make, but will never figure out. The Old Bay added the perfect spice and the shrimp were nice and plump. 

I like that they have daily specials. If I was there one day before I could have saved $4 on my shrimp! The menu had a ton of great options that I want to try after I can eat everything again - stone crab chowder anyone? I will definitely be coming back.

Ok Korean food, but the prices are a little high.

I came for dinner. Maybe if I came for lunch I wouldn't feel this way, but at dinner the prices are definitely on the higher side. 

Like other reviewers have mentioned, if you ask for recommendations, make sure you pay attention to pricing. Anything you add is extra. My friend got the Dolsat Bi Bim Bap and added bulgogi. The addition of the bulgogi came out to $6. That seems a little steep to me. I didn't want to risk it so I went with the Galbi Tang exactly the way it is listed on the menu.

It was pretty empty on a Friday night. I do like supporting locally owned and operated businesses so I hope they are fuller for lunch. I would say it is a medium sized restaurant. It has a good amount of seating (although my perspective might be skewed since it was pretty empty). They have limited parking. Again, wasn't an issue because not many people were there.

There were nine dishes of banchan. I thought this was a generous amount. My favorite was the fish cakes (but my favorite is always the fish cakes). 

I thought the Galbi Tang was ok. There really wasn't a lot of beef on the beef short ribs. I felt like it was used more for seasoning the soup. I felt like the ratio of broth and ingredients (e.g. noodles, egg, beef, etc.) was skewed too much towards the broth. 

This place is definitely a solid three to me. I didn't find anything glaringly wrong and I like the people who own it, but I don't think I'll be back any time soon.

Great concept with tons of variety for people on a restricted diet. 

If you've ever been to Fresh Kitchen you'll know what to expect from Taco Dirty. You walk through a line where you can choose bases, veggies, proteins, sauce, etc. I'm going to throw out there that I am a huge fan of Fresh Kitchen. I actually went to Fresh Kitchen a couple days before and a couple days after going to Taco Dirty. To me, and this is completely my personal taste, Taco Dirty ranks lower than Fresh Kitchen. I cannot handle spice and I managed to choose some spicy options (I think it was the chilled avocado and mole noodles.) Also, my choices didn't blend together as seamlessly as at Fresh Kitchen. Part of that could be what I chose, but I also would assume everything should taste great together (it tasted good, but not great.) I still give this place five stars because being on a soy free/dairy free diet, when I go out to eat I'm usually super limited, but here I can eat almost everything!

This is a new restaurant so the workers weren't fully aware of what is soy free. However, they are super helpful and the guy grabbed a book and walked me through every single item and if it was soy free. This was even with a line forming behind me. The people behind me may have suffered but I really appreciated that. This is what I ended up getting:

Avocado citrus rice, chilled avocado and mole noodles
Sweet potato hash and avocado crispy broccolini
Grilled lime and sour orange chicken, bbq tinga chicken
Pickled pineapple onions and warm vegan cauli queso
Orange guac sauce

Like I said earlier, everything on its own was great, it just tasted kind of weird together. I would definitely forgo the noodles next time because I think that was what gave it the kick. I loved the pickled pineapple onions and would definitely get it again. The warm vegan cauli queso is cool in theory, but I didn't feel like it really added to my dish so I'd skip it next time. Same with the orange guac sauce. I want to find a sauce I love here as much as the creamy ginger sauce at FK.

I was also able to eat the chips and salsa! I definitely enjoyed that. 

The décor is really neat - avocados everywhere! There is limited indoor and outdoor seating, but the entire time we were here it never seemed like people didn't have a seat as long as they were willing to sit outside. The music is really loud inside. I had to raise my voice to be heard, but that is the atmosphere they are going for, young, hip, and trendy (I'm old now.)

I would definitely recommend this as a healthy, fast option for anyone in the area!

Awesome lunch menu.

I used to live less than five minutes from here so of course it took moving thirty minutes away to make me try this place. I had heard that they had a really good lunch menu and it is definitely true. Most dishes are between $10 and $20 and there is a great variety of soups, salads, seafood, and, of course, steak.

This is definitely a place where people go for a business lunch. I really enjoyed the ambiance, it's classy without feeling stuffy.

Even though we were at a steakhouse, I couldn't get steak, since I love it rare, but I was pregnant. The gestational diabetes stopped me from trying any of their sandwiches (too many carbs), so I settled on the Seafood Cobb ($19). I do want to come back to try their lobster roll and fries. The fries are steak fries and they looked like they were perfectly fried.

The Seafood Cobb is like a deconstructed salad. It had a heaping of blue cheese, a heaping of crab, hardboiled egg, two shrimp, and a scoop of lobster on top. This is the type of salad where it would be weird to ask for the dressing on the side. It was absolutely delicious. It had a great amount of lobster. I felt healthy and satisfied after eating it.

The service was great. My friend and I were there for about two hours catching up and I never felt rushed. 

If you're looking for a reasonable lunch in the area, I would highly suggest coming here!

Great food, not a chain, fun atmosphere.

I really enjoy having The Grind close to where I live. I'm actually surprised I haven't reviewed it before, because I've had a couple different experiences here already. Every time I've walked away satisfied.

I've ordered take out to bring sandwiches to feed people before an event. I think their wraps are absolutely delicious. I got a Mediterranean one and it exceeded my expectations. However, since this was about half a year ago I'm going to glaze over specifics and focus on my most recent experience.

I came here to meet a friend for lunch. Although it wasn't packed, all tables except for one were taken because people like to come here and work for a bit. This doesn't bother me at all since I do the same thing and if the table in the back wasn't open we could have always shared one of the large tables up front with someone.

I ordered the Westchase Classic. The potatoes are what blew me away. Whatever seasoning they put on that is like crack. It is salty and so delicious. I was trying to scrape some of that seasoning on my eggs and toast! The prices here are super reasonable for what you get. You won't be breaking the bank with this lunch. 

I'm a fan of this place - you get healthy, fresh food for relatively cheap. I will always choose coming here over any chain coffee shop in the area!

I like this place, but the acidity of the poke rice can be hit or miss. 

I know, that's a very specific opening statement, but that sums up my feelings about this place. When I visited a while back, I gave it three stars because the rice acidity made the dish unenjoyable. I decided to give it another chance and ended up ordering the same dish twice in the course of a week. 

Time one: My friend came over and we ordered UberEats. I got the Salmon Poke Doke and she got a pork ramen. The broth came separate, which is good so it doesn't make all the food soggy. She ended up asking me for some soy sauce because she found the ramen kind of bland. 

I got the Salmon Poke with extra salmon, which is the way to go. It's definitely worth the $3 extra. This time, I absolutely loved my dish. It was satisfying and had a great taste to it. I liked it so much I got it again a couple days later. If I had stopped here, I would have given this place five stars.

Time two: This time I got my husband a chicken teriyaki bowl and my son the karaage. I got the Salmon Poke Doke bowl again because I liked it so much the first time. This time, the rice tasted too acidic again. I ended up eating all the salmon and toppings and leaving most of the rice. 

I love the chicken karaage. It was perfectly fried. The menu says it's spicy, but it comes with spicy aioli on the side, so the chicken isn't spicy at all. I'll definitely get it again.

The teriyaki chicken was very similar except it was tossed in a teriyaki sauce. I also thought it was delicious. 

Overall, I'm increasing it a star, because one of the times I didn't find the rice too acidic and I do love their chicken. I think this place will be a bit hit or miss with me, but as long as I always order the chicken karaage to go with it, I'll be happy.

We tried a ton more dishes for Father's Day (clearly the men in this house chose where they wanted to get takeout). We ended up ordering TWELVE dishes and it came out to around $115 (not including tax and tip). How's that for a great deal?! Here are my favorites in order:

Squid black bean sauce: They finally had squid available and I loved it! I don't know why I didn't expect to see black beans in the black bean sauce (duh), but there are and the sauce is delicious. There were so many pieces of squid. I will get this every time.

Seafood chow fun: I love their chow fun. The first time I walked away a little meh about it, because it tasted kind of doughy to me, but now that I've had it three more times, I have to say I love it. That first time might have been an off day. 

Satay chicken sticks: They do meat on a stick well. I liked the chicken sticks just a smidge better than the beef teriyaki sticks (which I totally disagree with Brett N. giving the beef teriyaki sticks four stars, they're five for sure).

Beef teriyaki sticks: see above

Sesame chicken: I love their sesame sauce. I tried their sesame tofu in the past, which is a great option if you avoid meat, but I do like the sesame chicken better. They give you huge chunks of chicken, not just the little balls of it. So good.

Beef fried rice: Ok, this is going to be a bit weird, but I love the beef in the beef fried rice. They don't give you a lot of it, which is sad, but I take all the beef and the men get the fried rice. 

Beef with broccoli: I really do like their beef if you can't tell. The broccoli tastes fresh and not soft at all. Of course, the beef is delicious.

We also got boneless spare ribs (which my husband loves, but I don't eat pork), dim sum (which is shumai, but for some reason is on their menu just as dim sum. Again, I didn't touch it because I thought there might be pork, but my dad said it was good. This definitely doesn't seem to be the frozen ones you get at the Asian grocery store like we experienced at another restaurant), beef lo mein (being that there were a million other dishes I didn't touch this one, but now that I'm writing this, I might go looking for the beef), egg rolls (my husband loves them) and they gave us free donuts.

With the free donuts, they asked us what we'd want for free. I think the choices were wonton soup, crab rangoon or chinese donuts. I got the donuts to see if my son would eat them, which he didn't, so I'd probably try something else next time. I don't know if they always do this or if it's just because we always order such a crazy amount of food. 

Like I wrote before, their sanitation efforts are top notch, which is why I let my family eat here. When they're busy it can take up to an hour and a half for your food to be ready. This time it was ready in thirty minutes. 

This is definitely our go to place. It's now three days later and we are still making our way through leftovers!

I love everything about this place.

Ask me any question about this restaurant and the answer will be it's the absolute best. Quality? It's the best. Quantity? It's the best. Price? It's the best. Cleanliness? It's the best. Friendliness? It's the best. My review is done.

If you want more details, I went here with my dad and one-year-old son at the off hours of 5 p.m. on Sunday for an early dinner. We were the only ones in the restaurant, which is great when my son starts to lose it. 

FOOD: We started with plantain chips. Look at the pictures, these are not cookie cutter plantains, they look like the real deal. They are also absolutely amazing. The tomato sauce it comes with is so fresh and delicious. It's a must get.

I got the La Vieja sandwich which comes with fries. The sandwich was perfection. It has a hint of sweetness from the sweet plantains and the cuban bread is sturdy, yet fluffy. The fries are the shoestring fries that are so addicting. When you come here, you should definitely get a sandwich.

We ended the meal with a dessert that wasn't on the menu. It was a chocolate cake with coffee flan and ice cream. Like everything else it was superb. 

PRICE: Everything above plus another sandwich came out to $27. Mind blowing. I can't believe that amount of food cost that little.

CLEANLINESS: I really pay attention to the cleanliness of a place now that my son likes to try to pick up everything. This place was spotless. You'd be surprised how many places has little pieces of trash on the floor. The owners really pay attention to detail.

FRIENDLINESS: Our server, which I think is also the owner, was so friendly. Her son, who is five, entertained my son by playing on his Mighty Morphin Power Rangers device. This place is family owned and operated and the owners are just so nice.

I want to come back to try more of their menu since I'm so impressed with what I had. I'm definitely a new fan.

A great place to get a sushi kick for lunch!

I'm a little surprised, but all the sushi places around me are closed for lunch. I was looking on a Sunday so maybe they are open for lunch other times, but this was shocking to me. Luckily Shogun opens at 12:30 (which I still find a little late, but I'll take late sushi instead of no sushi). 

I put in an Uber Eats order that morning for it to arrive between 12:30 p.m. and 1 p.m. (which I thought might be pushing it since the restaurant opens at 12:30 p.m., but hey, it was an option). The food ended up arriving at 1:07 p.m., which I'm not mad about, close enough. 

We ordered: Sushi and sashimi for two, Honey Roll appetizer, Agedashi tofu appetizer, one order of Mackerel, one order of Tobiko and Steak and Chicken Hibachi. It came out to about $150 including tax and tip, but it was a ton of food.

The sushi and sashimi for two was huge. I love the color dragon roll, I thought that was a great inclusion to balance out all the raw fish. They do salmon really well, I found the salmon to be super fresh, which is my favorite fish. For me, it ended up being too much raw fish (I know, is there really a thing?) so I definitely fulfilled my raw fish craving. Next time I'll go back to rolls. 

I finally found the honey salmon roll I had before. It turns out it is under sushi appetizer. I remember absolutely loving it last time. I still liked it, but I found it a bit too sweet. Maybe my taste buds have changed. It was good, but not a must get for me. 

The agedashi tofu was really good. It is sliced thinly and lightly fried. I actually got it to see if my son who is a super picky eater would like it. He spit it out, so that was a no go, but that's more for me. 

My husband liked his hibachi. I mistakenly said this was from the same place we got last time (which now looking at Yelp reviews, turns out it's not) and he said this time it was better. Score 1 for Shogun. If future Christina is reading this, next time Brandon wants to try the steak and shrimp.

Everything was packaged beautifully. I just wish they would put the hot stuff and the cool stuff in separate bags, but I noticed every place does this, so they're not unique with how they put it all together.

Five stars for the food, three stars for the service.

Food: The Kobe Fajitas are to die for. The meat is so tender and perfectly charred. The Cajun Ceviche is also very good. I love the option to have it on guacamole instead of tortilla chips! The stand out to me has to be their tortillas. I got to try both the flour and the corn and man could I have just eaten those for my entire meal. I loved the flour tortillas. The Kobe Fajitas comes with corn so next time I'm going to ask for flour instead. 

Service: I was basically a server's nightmare since I was off of dairy/nuts/egg/soy. I had actually called on a separate occasion and learned that I couldn't eat the chips because it had soy. After rattling off what I couldn't eat to the server he later came back and told me he thought I could eat the chips. I double checked with another server and learned nope, still can't eat the chips. Later that same server asked me if I could eat the tortillas. These are things I was hoping he would find out (and find out correctly because these things are important!) This put a bit of a damper on the service for me. He later joked when he brought my meal that it was taste free. Luckily for me it was actually delicious, but I was definitely not his biggest fan.

They have a VIP room which is a separate room. You can sit there if you have a large enough party (we had 12), no kids, and were spending over $250. 12 people was a bit of a squeeze. I think 10 would be the perfect size for that room. However, since we are such a boisterous bunch that room was perfect for us. 

If you have no food restrictions, this place is amazing. However, until I can eat everything again I don't feel comfortable eating here.

They have a bottomless mimosa brunch on a Saturday.

I'm on a hunt to try every restaurant that serves bottomless mimosas on a Saturday. Why should Sunday have all the fun (is it because it rhymes with fun day)? I like knowing I have all of Sunday to recover if a Saturday of day drinking carries over into the night. Let's be real, if you're starting with bottomless mimosas this is normally the case.

I was tasked with finding a brunch place in DTSP before our pedal pub appointment. After doing extensive research on yelp, as one does, I narrowed our options down to a couple restaurants and presented to the group. After determining they did not care, I chose Thirsty First. On the online menu, it says they have bottles of champagne with seasonal fruit juice for $20. I called, confirmed, and made a reservation for eight. 

Day of, right before I walk into the restaurant I see a chalkboard that says bottomless mimosas for $15. I ran in and quizzed the poor waitress to make sure that the chalkboard in front of the restaurant was indeed for Thirsty First. It was! They now offer bottomless mimosas and bottomless bromosas. What is a bromosa, you may ask, as we did about three different times? I can now say with authority that it is champagne, vodka, peach schnapps and orange juice. If you really want to start your day with a bang, you can get unlimited bromosas for $20. Since none of us really felt like falling off a pedal pub later in the day, we decided to stick with mimosas. 

Now, many people dislike bottomless mimosas because they claim the bar waters down their drink. You don't have to have any fear of that here, because after your first mimosa, they will bring the champagne bottle and orange juice carafe straight to your table. Go for it, you crazy kids. Fill your glass to the brim with champagne and add a splash of orange juice. This is a recipe for success.

Although I am inclined to stop my review here, I suppose you may care about having a side of food with your alcohol. Be aware that the portion sizes are on the smaller size, but that mainly speaks to the quality of ingredients. This is not Dennys. I got the Basic B, which includes eggs, hash browns and a cheddar chive biscuit. My friend wanted to get egg whites instead of eggs, but learned that the eggs come out of a carton, so she was unable to do that. The eggs and the biscuit were decent. I'm not in love with this biscuit, although I have very high standards for biscuits, so I'd probably try something else next time. The hash browns were pretty salty. That a can be easily rectified, however, and I didn't dislike them enough to send them back. My husband enjoyed his wings. He is a fan of what he calls "breakfast wings", which is essentially ordering Buffalo wings at brunch, because he doesn't like traditional brunch fare. Luckily, you are able to order off the brunch or lunch menu here. I enjoy their menu choices and I would like to come back to try different food.

This restaurant is right next to the Sundial Parking Garage. That means, unless there is a special event going on, it is only $1 to park on the weekend. If there is a special event, like how we encountered the Reggae Festival, it is $5. Either way, it is worth avoiding the hassle and just parking in the garage.

I like the vibe of this place. It is clean, hip, and laid back. I think it is a great addition to DTSP and I would definitely come back.

Might be newly opened pains, but I wasn't a fan.

It's tough to write a review based on one experience, but with so many awesome restaurants in Tampa Bay if I dislike a meal I am very unlikely to ever go back. I really disliked the black bean burger - it was to the point that I ate around the patty and basically left it sitting on my plate. It was incredibly dry. I let others I was with try it and they agreed that it wasn't good. I did really like the Yucca fries. They were on the heavier side of fried, but they were still pretty good. I heard someone else ask for a cilantro dipping sauce and now I wish I got it too. The fries don't come with any type of sauce so definitely remember to request it (reading other reviews, I think they will charge you extra, but I think it would be worth it)!

Ordering was also a little odd. You order at a window and it is unclear whether the line starts from the left or from the right. While I was standing waiting for my food I actually saw it shift from starting on the left to starting on the right. These are all kinks that they will probably work out and if it was a longer line I bet it would be obvious which way to go. The wait time seemed a little long, my husband got his pizza from AVA before I got my order, but my friends who ordered at Graze waited a whole lot longer. Probably if I was able to sit down it wouldn't be bad, but then I wouldn't be able to hear my name be called so I had to wait by the window. However, this is true for all the places so it is definitely not a negative, just an observation to be aware of!

I know most people don't go to a Cuban place and get a black bean burger so you can definitely take this review with a grain of salt. That being said, if you are looking for a vegetarian option, I would suggest looking elsewhere.

Still one of my favorite places to eat in the Westshore area.

It's a little embarrassing that I haven't updated my review since 2015, especially when I love this place so much. Here are the main reasons this continues to be a staple in my restaurant rotation.

GUACAMOLE - The table side made guacamole is superb. The chunks of avocado give me life and it is perfectly seasoned. It's a good amount for 2-3 people, if you order it and think uh I think that feeds more than 3 people, Christina, I'm a fatty, what can I say. 

Pair it with the superbly thin and well-salted chips and it is a recipe for addiction. They do not hold back with the salt, and I am here for it. 

FREE CHIPS AND SALSA - It hurts my heart when I go someplace and they don't give free chips and salsa. Please always do this.

CAMARONES SALAD - Yes, I continuously get the same salad. When I have so much other turmoil in my life, I'm looking at you my one-year-old son, I don't like to branch out with food anymore. This salad is delicious and nutritious. I'm so happy to have a light option when eating at a Mexican restaurant, because I know I'm eating all my calories with those chips and guac. 

SERVICE - You can get in and out in less than an hour. They know how to get food out during lunch hours. You would think this would be standard at any business during the week, but you'd be surprised. 

ICE TEA - They bring out the ice tea and give you a little carafe (well, it actually looks like a Patron tequila bottle, but carafe sounds classier), so you can replenish your own tea. They even bring sweetener to the table. I love this.

DESSERT - Free churros to round out the meal. It's the perfect amount of sweet to finish lunch.

The one negative is the parking situation. It continues to be impossible to find parking in the lot in front! This is a mall so of course you will find parking close by, but you might have to walk a bit. I ended up sucking it up and valeting (which was $5 not including gratuity), because I circled the parking lot once and then said screw it. There's nothing you can do about this, but add in five minutes to your drive time!
