I had to lower it a star because the brisket I had was subpar.

I hate giving 4 Rivers anything but five stars because I have had some absolutely delicious meals here, but I was very unimpressed by their brisket on my last visit. 

I choose places to go very wisely these days since I have a baby and don't want to waste a meal. There are multiple bbq places that are closer, but I wanted to have the best. Also, my dad was in town from Houston and I wanted him to experience my favorite BBQ place. Unfortunately, it did not live up to its hype.

I have to say, I was very disappointed with the brisket - it was mushy and tasteless. We like to sous vide meat and if I left the meat in the sous vide for too long, this is what I would guess it would taste like. I also had to douse it in bbq sauce to give it some taste, which I know from past experience isn't the case. 

I wasn't a huge fan of the mac and cheese or baked cheese grits. Both were bland to me. However, I was a huge fan of the fried okra. It's seasoning is amazing. I also enjoyed the bread pudding and corn. My baby chowed down on the sweet potato. 

My dad's pulled chicken was pretty good, but I wouldn't run here to eat it like the brisket. I'm disappointed that they got rid of the brontosaurus rib. I loved that before!

I now look at this place and love how kid friendly it is. It's already big and loud so my child blabbing away doesn't disturb anyone and they have high chairs. 

I'll definitely come back because I'm hoping this is a one time issue with the brisket!

Huge menu with lots of great options.

I remember in Psychology 101 (or whatever asinine number it was assigned in college) learning that when given too many options, people will freeze and not choose anything. In this case, I found the abundance of choices a boon. I'm trying to eat healthy and there were so many different dishes I could have gone with that it didn't seem like a downer at all! They literally hand you two menus because all the choices couldn't fit on a large front/back sheet. There's your traditional sushi, poke bowls, sushi burritos, curry, salad, etc. It seems like they went to some millennials and asked what is the hip food right now and bam, it's on the menu. 

I got a salad with mango, cashews, shrimp, and ginger dressing. The shrimp was on point! It was grilled perfectly and they were big, succulent pieces. Could I make this salad at home? Yeah, probably. But would I have been creative enough to think up this combination on my own? Definitely not. 

My friend got a curry and another got a poke bowl so we ran the gamut of options. They both seemed to really enjoy their dishes as well, so it seems like even though this restaurant wears many hats they wear them well.

Our server was really friendly. She even took the time to answer our questions before we left, we were mainly interested in whether this is the same ownership as the last restaurant (it isn't) and why there are so many guitars all over the place (the owner made them). 

The restaurant was almost full on a Friday night, so it was busy but there wasn't a wait for a table. I enjoyed my meal so I definitely would come back!

Not my favorite place, but a solid choice for the family.

My husband likes Tijuana Flats. I am not a huge Mexican/Tex-Mex fan, so it isn't my number one go to. However, we had a coupon so we decided to check it out.

I do really like the decor of these places. It's bold and fun. 

My husband got a Megajuana + Wet Burrito. It was supposed to come out smothered in queso, but they forgot. It wasn't a huge deal, since they just brought out queso in a cup. We got a Beef Quesadilla for my son. It was huge! It looks like a normal size quesadilla to me, but for a fraction of the price. I'm glad we planned for me to share that quesadilla, because there is no way my 15 month old was going to eat that. 

The actual food is just ok to me. I found the burrito kind of dry and the quesadilla was standard, nothing special. I asked my husband what he thought of the burrito and he was a huge fan. It really does show you that everyone has different tastes. 

Portion sizes are large and that is reflected in the calorie count. The calories are on the menu, which is great if you are watching your waistline, but terrible if you are watching your waistline and eating here. Just figure nothing is low calorie.

Service here is phenomenal. They actually come around and ask if everything is ok. I felt like the chips didn't have enough seasoning and they actually brought me out a side of the salt mix! I was debating going up to say something, but they made that decision for me by coming to me! It was much appreciated. 

It weirds me out that there are no garbage cans. I like to clean up after myself. I'm glad they mentioned this at the Yelp Event or else I would have spent so much time searching for the garbage! 

Overall, I think this is a good place to grab a quick bite.

The prime rib was exactly what I wanted. 

I've been craving prime rib, which apparently is not a popular meat for higher end restaurants to cook. I've wrote this on an Instagram story (and multiple Yelp reviews), that I like my meat like I like my men. A friend responded "pink?". Yes, my husband is quite pale, but what I meant was fat. (It is a total joke, I do love my meat fatty, but I'm often trying to get my husband to get on the peloton, which he is adamantly against). 

Anyways, I found it difficult to find prime rib on many menus that offer steak. Flamestone was actually the only one near me. I went with the classic cut with campfire mixed vegetables and mashed potatoes. My husband got a filet with campfire vegetables and mashed sweet potatoes (I chose the sweet potatoes side for him to get so I could try it) and my son got the kids chicken tenders with fries. 

The prime rib was perfect. I got it medium since I'm pregnant (I hate getting meat that is cooked more than rare, but I gotta do what I gotta do for this fetus). The meat was still tender and juicy with huge chunks of fat. I loved it. I also devoured the mashed potatoes and both my husband and I agreed that the vegetables were superb. I probably wouldn't get the mashed sweet potatoes again, but honestly I'm not a huge fan of sweet potatoes so it takes a lot to wow me. (Time and time again I think maybe I like sweet potatoes more than I think.)

The kids chicken tenders were solid. My son didn't touch any of it, but that's just him. 

I called at about 4:30 p.m. on a weekday and my order was ready in 15 minutes. Much faster than a pizza. It was empty inside save for one couple at the bar and one table. The bartender was super nice. I will definitely order takeout from here again.

Loved the brisket and pig powdered fries.

Let me set the scene. I had to change my baby's diaper on the floor of a tiny bathroom and I still loved the food enough to give this place five stars. 

When I pulled up I realized my baby needed a change of diaper...and clothes. Luckily my two friends were already here - shout out to a trio of on-time mom's including Tina S. and Michelle M. - so I was able to order food and go straight to the restroom. They don't have a changing table and the restroom is pretty tiny. Luckily, my baby is tiny so I pulled out his changing pad and changed his diaper, and clothes, on the ground. Yes, it was difficult, but these are the things you do as a mother. 

When I reappeared from the bathroom my food was on the table, which was awesome. I got the brisket and pig powder fries. The pig powder fries are fries with seasoning on it and omg is it delicious. It has a hint of sweetness to it and I devoured all the fries. I had to stop myself from licking the seasoning off the platter. I already want to go back with my husband, so he can hold the baby, just so I can eat those fries. I would argue I don't even care about the meat those fries were so good, but luckily the meat was good too. 

I feel like the mark of a good brisket is will I eat it without sauce, and this one I most definitely would. When I was ordering I asked what sauce wasn't spicy and would go well with the brisket. The employee mentioned the original bbq sauce and the florabama white sauce so I said the original sounded fine. She ended up giving me both to try! I thought they were both delicious, but I really only used a little since I loved the meat by itself. It was tender and had the perfect amount of fat. 

It was definitely on the pricier side, my total came out to a little over $17. I'm open to paying that for quality meat, but this isn't going to be an everyday thing. 

Parking seems to be on the small side, as you would expect in South Tampa. I made a mistake and parked at So Gourmet. Luckily you can walk between the places. 

Overall I really enjoyed this place so I will be back.

If you're on a diet, the salads are fine, but not great. 

I was at a crossroads, for my own health I should get a salad, since I was trying to fatten up my baby I should get a pizza to feed him the crust. I decided to help us both I ordered an appetizer of half pretzel and the spinach salad. 

First of all, how is a half serving of the pretzel appetizer three whole pretzels! I thought I was going to get half a pretzel. That is utterly insane. It was so much pretzel! It made me wonder who is getting the full serving. It was cheap too - only $4.99. I killed my diet eating those pretzels. I know I got them for my son, but he didn't seem to want them and, well, carbs. I'd give the pretzels a 4/5. They satisfied my need for carbs and were warm, but they were lacking that extra doughiness or butteriness to push them over the edge. 

I got the spinach salad and it came with cheese, candied pecans, craisins, apples, and a balsamic vinegar dressing. That dressing is strong. I'm glad they put it on the side so I could ration it myself. I ended up taking most of it home because my son was losing it. I'm glad I did because I was able to add turkey. It lacked protein to me. The salad was fine, but I don't think I'd get it again. 

Overall I still like this place for its options, but now I know to stick with what they do best - pizza.

Five stars for the fact that they have Yelp Waitlist!

We wanted to introduce my son to the beach for the first time, so we decided that the best time to go would be right after he woke up, which would be 6:30 a.m. We made it to the beach by 8 a.m. and by 8:45 a.m. we decided we were done with the beach and it was time to eat. 

Places like Frenchy's wouldn't open until 11 a.m. so that was out. I pulled up Yelp and looked for what was open and found Clear Sky Cafe. What's even better is they have Yelp Waitlist! I put us in line and it told us to get there in the next fifteen minutes.

We walked over and there was actually a wait! Yes, at 9 a.m. on a Sunday there was people waiting for tables. It isn't huge inside, but we could also tell this is a popular place for breakfast/brunch. Their Yelp Waitlist wasn't syncing up with their system yet, but the hostess immediately gave us the next table because of the fact that I used Yelp Waitlist. Once they get that fixed, it's going to be so clutch. I mean, why leave the beach to wait at a restaurant for a table? 

They were busy, but our waitress was super attentive. Random, but when we left at 10 a.m. they had open tables. I guess 9 a.m. is just a busy time for them!

I ordered the lobster bennie and my husband ordered the chicken and waffles. I got a side of grits to try to feed my ten month old son. 

The people who eat here are super friendly. My son was losing it so I had to walk him around and people kept smiling and waving to him. I guess if you're spending your day at the beach life is good.

I liked the lobster bennie. It had a ton of lobster. The gouda grits were ok, but next time I'd try something else. My husband loved his chicken and waffles. He wasn't a huge fan of the sausage gravy, but to each their own. The chicken had an interesting breading to it. It's hard for me to describe, but I honestly really liked it. My son did too and actually ate some chicken, and he doesn't eat anything. 

We were in and out in 45 minutes, which when you're dining with a small child, this is great. I would definitely suggest this place to anyone who is going to the beach!

Chewy hunks of deliciousness - gotta love their bagels.

I am unabashedly a carboholic. If you give me the choice between a juicy steak or buttery croissant, I would choose the croissant nine times out of ten. I always am acutely aware that my butt seems to expand the more bread I eat, so I am very picky about the carbs I consume. I will glady eat these bagels. 

If you go to their website you can get a coupon for one free bagel or doughnut the first time you go in. I signed up for this over six months ago, but I finally had a chance to redeem it. Now I'm upset I didn't go in sooner.

BAGEL - these bagels are amazing. They are chewy with bold flavors. I got the sundried tomato bagel and I couldn't be happier. If you order cream cheese they put a huge dollop of cream cheese on your bagel. It's worth it.

SANDWICHES - I got the Strange Bird with a salt bagel and it was amazing. The cream cheese and cranberry sauce perfectly complemented the turkey. The salt bagel has a huge amount of salt. I'm a salt fiend so it worked well for me, but I think if I had the bagel alone it may have been too much salt. I would go for this sandwich every time. 

ATMOSPHERE - It was really easy to find a parking space at 10 a.m. on a Monday (although I think I may have made my own parking space). There are about four tables and seats at a counter. It was pretty full when we got there. When we left at about 10:45 a.m. there were about five people in line. It's not crazy busy but it is busy enough that you realize you've struck bagel gold.

If you want a bagel, skip the chains and come here. You can satisfy all your carb needs.

Still five stars worthy and I've eaten more of the menu.

I now drive thirty minutes to get here and I do so lovingly, because it is that good. Here are a couple menu items I have tried since my original visit.

TL:DR - get some sort of croissant and the homemade french fries!

Almond croissant - I get this every time. It is monstrous and sweet. This is more of a gooey croissant than a flakey one. Make sure you ask them to heat it for you, because it makes it infinitely better and I learned they don't automatically do this.

Chocolate croissant - I liked the almond croissant better, but my sister liked this one better. It is a flakier croissant and the chocolate has an almost nutella like quality to it in terms of texture. 

Croissant french toast - it will give me diabetes, but I love it. One of my favorite things on the menu.

Quiche - When you feel carbed out, the quiche helps balance this out. I had one with goat cheese and it was superb. The french fries are made in house so make sure you get them!

Smoked salmon and brie omelet - Same idea with the quiche, when you start feeling like you're on a carb overload, this is a good balance. They add a good amount of smoked salmon and brie in it. 

Tropezienne - The only thing I've ever disliked here. The brioche bread tasted stale. I will definitely avoid this from here on out. 

I wish I lived closer but then I would weigh ten pounds heavier. I guess it is a trade off.

They say they have the best breakfast in Tampa Bay and I believe them!

Even at 1:30 p.m. on a Sunday, this place is slammed. There was about a twenty-minute wait. Even if it looks super busy it is worth waiting because the line moves fast. This also gives you time to peruse their giant menu. Even though I looked at their menu online ahead of time, after studying it before getting a seat I changed my mind - twice. 

With a lot of the breakfast plates you get a free Danish basket to start off. They could honestly give a basket per table, but we each got our own! It has cream cheese pastries, chocolate cake, coffee cake, etc. You basically start breakfast with dessert. I took a bite of everything and then put it away because I knew it would ruin my appetite.

I decided to go with the Corned Beef Hash. This came with two eggs, which I got scrambled, and a choice of either pancakes or two sides. I went with the home fries and grits. If you're counting, that's a lot of food. So much food, in fact, that after I ate it all (hey, I was hungry and pregnant) I didn't eat for the rest of the day. I literally did not get hungry again until about lunch the next day. The Corned Beef Hash was amazing. I think next time I'd get the home fries without onions, but that's a personal preference. I wasn't a huge fan of the grits. It didn't have any taste to me, so I added my own butter and salt. With so many good options, I'll try something else next time. 

This is one of my new favorite restaurants. My friend and I determined that we will have to come here once a month. We'll just need to come hungry and prepare not to eat for a week afterwards.

They have a 15% off check in offer so make sure you check in on Yelp!

I didn't realize that this check in offer existed until after I ordered. Now I know, and I could share this fun tidbit with Yelpers who read my review.

I don't live anywhere close to The Haus, which is a shame, because it is a great place to get work done. They have fast, free wifi, both tables and couches, and it is fairly empty during the day, but still full enough that you don't feel like a creep for staying. There were actually a couple other tables of people getting work done, so I was in good company.

I got a matcha latte with almond milk, a croissant egg, steak, and cheese sandwich, a peanut butter bar, and a key lime cookie. The matcha latte is unsweetened. If you are getting sweets like I did, you will be glad for the balance. 

The croissant sandwich was my favorite of what I ordered. The croissant is buttery and the rest is very satisfying. I actually wasn't a huge fan of the peanut butter bar or key lime cookie (I mean, I still ate it all, because I don't let food go to waste, but I've had better). They have a variety of baked goods that they say comes from a bakery down the street, so I'll just try something else next time. 

I'm not exactly sure what it was about the baked goods that I didn't enjoy. The cookie was moist and chewy, but I think both weren't as decadent as I'm used to. The peanut butter topping also had a lightness to it, as if they were backing off on the peanut butter flavor, that I wasn't a fan of. Again, neither were bad, just neither knocked my socks off. 

They have an actual changing table in the restroom. Five stars right there. 

The employees are friendly and it seems like some of the people that come in are regulars. I will be back everytime I'm in the area.

Still a great place to grab a quick bite.

I am a huge fan of their curry chicken salad. It reminds me of the chicken salad sandwich at Barrows in Tampa, which is also absolutely delicious. They have a great amount of golden raisins, which really makes this salad.

Additionally, I got to try their Turkey Burger (yes, you are reading that correctly, I ordered a Turkey Burger and got a side of chicken salad). It seems a little pricey at $11, but it is really filling. I was a little worried because I saw the word jalapeno and was afraid it would be spicy, but that is not the case. The guacamole they put on it gives it a unique flavor. 

I'm going to keep trying to eat my way around this store. Nothing has disappointed me yet.

Fantastic service, but I found the food to be a bit bland.

I'm not a huge expert on Ethiopian food. I've had it once in Ann Arbor, a couple times in Houston, once in Orlando, once in Los Angeles and once at another place in Tampa. I was disappointed with the other place in Tampa, so I was excited to try this one. Since I'm not an expert in the food I tend to judge it based on did I enjoy it. 

I always love getting the sampling platter so I got the Vegetarian combination. I found a majority of the options to be pretty tasteless. They all seemed very healthy, but bland. I did really enjoy the red lentil, but one out of five isn't a great ratio. 

I think there might be other dishes that are more flavorful, but I technically tried five dishes and wasn't a huge fan. 

The reason I gave them three stars is because it is locally owned and operated and our server was so nice. There were only three tables full on a Thursday night so we never felt rushed to leave. We were actually there chatting for two hours. 

I wouldn't say no if someone wants to come here, but I'll let them do the ordering!

Fun place to chill, but I wasn't super impressed with the food.

I'd probably come back here to drink and enjoy the décor, but I, and my tablemates, found the food lacking. Safety Harbor has a ton of highly rated restaurants, but it is hard to find one that is large enough that you don't have to worry about wait and is kid friendly. That was why I chose this one - we had two toddlers in our group. I don't regret my decision because it is a nice place to hang out and catch up, but the food left something to be desired.

I got the lobster roll, but since I was not eating carbs I asked for it to be on lettuce. When I ask for lettuce, I usually expect it on big leaves of lettuce so it replaces a bun. In the past if a restaurant doesn't have that type of lettuce they let me know. Here, they brought it out on shredded lettuce (like the type of lettuce you have in tacos). That was definitely a bit bizarre. I got double the cole slaw instead of chips. I thought the cole slaw was pretty good, but they are tiny portions. I know the $15 price tag is for the lobster, but if they include sides they should up their game a little. They were solid chunks of lobster, but I found it a little rubbery. My friend got chicken tacos and she said she didn't really like them. So, overall, we found the food a bit lacking.

I do really love the décor of the place. It is tropical and beachy. I would love to come back for drinks one day. Also, the service was great. Our server was really nice so there were no issues there. 

I would definitely come back, but I would try something else on the menu and only bring friends who aren't huge foodies. Otherwise, there are other great restaurants in Safety Harbor still left to try.

Just go here. 

I actually had a pretty terrible experience getting this food and even I would eat here again - that should tell you how great the food is. 

Let me get the bad out of the way, we ordered delivery on one of the delivery apps and the time kept getting pushed back. It said the driver was there but our food wasn't ready. We knew the restaurant had started on the order because they contacted us to let us know that certain items were out, so I don't know what ended up taking so long. I was basically starving and angry by the time it came. They didn't even give us forks and napkins and messed up one of the orders. It started off bad. 

Therefore, the fact that I loved the food so much to give it five stars means the food is probably worthy of six stars. First, I thought how can I get full off of a single arepa, it doesn't come with sides? No sides necessary, this arepa is super filling. I got the pink floyd (which is shrimp) and dang was it good. The sauce was delicious and it had a good amount of shrimp. I also got the green juice and it was amazing as well. I honestly thought it was going to be disgusting, but healthy, and it turned out to be super refreshing. 

I've learned that this restaurant can call my baby ugly and I would still eat here. I plan to come back next time I'm in St. Petersburg.

Great selection of food with a beautiful view.

Whoever chose the businesses that got to occupy the spots at Sparkman Wharf did a great job. In my opinion, there isn't a dud in the bunch. I love that none of them are huge chains and they are all Tampa locals. There is also a great variety of food choices so everyone can find something. 

We went at a kind of random time on a weekday, but since school was out there were tons of families just chilling. I would be more wary about going here when it is hot, but I'm not going to speculate on that without experiencing it first hand. 

There is a ton of seating. Almost all of it was taken, but the grass looks like a nice place to pop a squat and enjoy some food. My husband went for tacos and I went with an acai bowl. The acai bowl was on par in terms of cost about what I pay at a normal brick and mortar store. The tacos were on the more expensive side, so I don't feel like I can say that you'll pay a premium here until I experience more vendors. 

I love being right on the water. It's nice to stand and look out. 

We didn't have to deal with parking since we are Aquarium members. That's another positive to Sparkman Wharf. You can walk to so many places! We walked to the Aquarium and we also went to walk the Riverwalk a bit. It is so centrally located to a lot of fun happenings. 

This is definitely a place that I will take guests when the weather is good.

One of my favorite places for Italian food in Tampa Bay.

Two things you should know right off the bat, 1. They do not allow children, 2. They will not seat you until you entire party is present. I can understand both points. They are a small place, so it makes sense that you don't have people sitting in prime real estate waiting for their party. I'm pregnant, I had to wait about fifteen minutes for my husband in the chairs outside before we could be seated, and it didn't bother me. Just be aware of this before you go and if you hate waiting then make sure your entire party arrives together. The no children thing doesn't bother me either. Sometimes, you want a childfree atmosphere. There are tons of restaurants in Tampa Bay so if either of these facts bother you then go somewhere else so I have an easier time getting a table here.

We came at about 5:45 p.m. on a Friday because I didn't want to have to wait for a table (even though I ended up waiting for my husband). I probably jumped the gun a bit on that one because there were empty tables the entire time we were there. This might not be the standard for them, and since it is such a tiny place I probably will continue to go before any sort of rush.

My husband always orders a chicken parmesan which is not on the menu. He says it is his favorite chicken parm in Tampa Bay. It came with asparagus and penne pasta in their pink sauce. I went with the lobster ravioli. It also comes in the pink sauce which I absolutely love. I use the bread to scoop up every last bite of that pink sauce. I also like the olive dip that the complimentary bread comes with. If you love olive, you'll love the dip. 

Osteria Natalina does decadent dishes well. I don't feel weighed down or sluggish after eating one of their cream dishes. I'm sure they are calorie laden, but I still walk out feeling good. That's why this place deserves five stars to me. 

If you want a romantic evening where you know the food will always be good, this is your place.

Good sushi and one of the better hibachi places we have been to.

My husband requested we go to a hibachi place for his birthday. A friend reminded me that Kobe always sends a free meal coupon and I brought that up to him. In the end we decided we rather support local and the Kobe nearest to us has a less than four star rating - wow am I getting elitist on where I eat. I'm actually glad we chose here, because it was pretty empty so we didn't have to worry about my son's crazy antics and the food was good!

FOOD - I always worry that hibachi will be too greasy. Not here! My husband got noodles, fried rice, vegetables, shrimp and steak. All of it was delicious. I really enjoyed the noodles. 

I ended up going with the Salmon Sushi Entree. I really enjoy that they have these combinations of sushi to order - theres a whole page of it. It was about $20 for a salmon roll, spicy salmon roll, and three pieces of salmon sushi. I feel like that combination a la carte would be less than $20, but I didn't get a chance to price it out. It is a little on the pricier side, but every piece of sushi was delicious.  The salmon tasted fresh and not fishy. 

We started with shrimp shumai steamed. Honestly, it seemed to me like the type you could get frozen at the Asian market. I didn't dislike it, but I wouldn't get it again. 

ATMOSPHERE - from the outside this place looks pretty run down. It's in a random location as kind of close to the movie theater, but not walking distance. I guess it is a testament to the food that it has survived so far. Inside it is much nicer. It is split between the sushi side and the hibachi side. Both sides are pretty large. On a Monday night there were only a couple tables occupied.

SERVICE - It is slow. This is not a get in get out restaurant. It takes a while for them to start the hibachi - maybe they are hoping that more people will come to share the table. Our server was nice though so I don't knock them for this. Just don't come here if you are in a rush. 

Overall I liked this place. It is hard to find someplace that both my husband and I will eat, but this is one of them. We will definitely return.

Good ramen in a minimalistic, hip environment.

I'm going to have to write this review comparing Buya to Ichicoro. Both are great ramen additions to the Tampa Bay area, so it is impossible to try one without thinking of the other. In terms of food, I'm a little divided. I enjoyed the broth at Ichicoro more, but I enjoyed the noodles and noodle to broth ratio at Buya. My sister often makes fun of me that I tend to have an entire bowl of broth left over at the end of my meal, because I pick out all the other ingredients to eat. At Buya, there is a hearty amount of noodles and less broth, so I actually ended up eating it pretty equally.

If this was my husband's review, he would say he loves Ichicoro more hands down. He wasn't that impressed with the pork belly at Buya. He said it had a lot more fat than the one at Ichicoro. This is not my husband's review, however, and he refuses to write any himself, so out of familial obligation I'm including this little paragraph to appease him. His constant stream of thought about how he prefers Ichicoro more than Buya did end up affecting this review, which is why I give this place four stars and Ichicoro five. He disliked the pork belly so much that he ended up leaving most of it. Taste is definitely subjective, so I don't want this to stop anyone from trying the Pork Belly Ramen. 

I really wanted to try the Duck Ramen or the Short Rib Ramen, but since it is in tonkatsu broth and I don't eat pork, it was not to be. Instead, I tried the Seafood Ramen. It had huge shrimp and a good portion of scallops. The broth was good, but the ramen noodles really stole the show for me.

We came at 8:15 p.m. on a Wednesday and it was fairly empty. No issue getting a table whatsoever. This may be where Buya has an advantage over Ichicoro. It has a much larger space, so you don't have to wait for a table. The restaurant is one huge room. It's a little dark and cold for my taste, but I guess that's what the hip people like. The temperature convinces you to get ramen even if you weren't planning to because it will warm you up.

Overall, I enjoyed this place and wouldn't hesitate to come back.

The burger and chips might give you a heart attack, but it would be worth it. 

I was nervous about giving this place a try. I know overall it has 4 1/2 stars, but some of my trusted Elites were rating it closer to 2 - 3, and I don't have time for a bad meal. I finally decided to give this place a try, because my husband could find something on the menu and there was no place around here that I really wanted to check out. I guess you can say we came here by default. 

This place was pretty empty on a Thursday at lunch. No huge lunch rush from the neighboring businesses yet. This was great for us, because it means we had no problem getting a seat. 

I decided that this was no time to go healthy and I went full carnivore on the Omg 2.0 burger with chips. This is not a lean burger - my husband remarked he saw the grease ooze out when I took my first bite. Did I gain five pounds? Yes. Did I regret it? Absolutely not. It was crazy delicious. This is not the type of burger I can replicate at home on the grill, did I mention the grease? The chips were superb as well. They reminded me of Datz chips, with a hint of sweetness. Again, these chips clogged up my arteries, but I think it was worth it. 

I got a juice to try to balance out the menu. It had beet and apples and was quite refreshing. It was also very cute, so your nonalcoholic friends can sip something that looks like your drink. 

Based on what I got, I loved this place. I could go back, get something else, and not be impressed, but I adored the burgers and chips.

Review of take out.

My friend probably eats here about once a week. That means when I visit we usually get take out from here for dinner. We've done it about four times now so I feel like I can safely comment on quality of the food. It's always the same order, two orders of Palak Paneer, one Chana Masala, naan, and garlic naan. 

If you are vacillating between the naan and the garlic naan, go for the garlic naan. To me, it is vastly better. They do not skimp on that garlic and it really adds the flavor. 

The Palak Paneer has a generous helping of cheese. The paneer is my favorite part and they gave you a huge heaping of it. Also, it is very thick, which I enjoy. 

Both the Palak Paneer and the Chana Masala are spicy! Even if you ask for it baseline mild (no spice at all please!) it still has a kick. The Chana Masala is usually spicier than the Palak Paneer. However, to my spice phobic taste buds, I would prefer both with less spice, but it won't stop me from eating here. Maybe they are slowly killing my taste buds and I'll eventually find it not spicy.

It is super easy to place an order for pickup. I would highly recommend it if you want an easy dinner in.

Update: There is now seating next door where their smoothie bar is, so you can get out of the heat.

I was spending the day outside so sitting outside during a break was not particularly appealing to me. I was going to suck it up just so we could go to Bodega, but low and behold there is air conditioned seating next door! There are no tables, but there are stools at bars, which is good enough for me!

I have to confess, I might not actually know what tempeh is. Wikipedia tells me it is a soybean product from Indonesia, but personally I always associated it with tofu. I got the Tempeh Sandwich and it tasted more like beans. The slaw that it came with was good, but I wasn't an actual fan of the tempeh. I'm still wracking my brain trying to figure out if that is what tempeh always tastes like. The bread, as always, was phenomenol and even though I was underwhelmed by my main filling, I still scarfed the whole thing down.

I got the Hibiscus soda and cortadito (a cafecito or cortadito is free with a check in!) Both were amazing! The hibiscus soda had just the right amount of sweetness (whereas my friend got the Watermelon Pear and it was lacking in flavor). The cortadito was smooth and packed a caffeine punch.

We came at an off hour (at about 3 p.m.) and it was still moderately busy. I can't imagine what the wait will be during peak times! If you're looking for a quick bite, this isn't it, but if you are willing to wait for quality food, hit this place up!

Huge portions ftw.

It is almost four hours past when I ate lunch here and I am still stuffed. I even took home half the meal to go. What type of wizardry is this that they charge around $10 for a "medium" size plate and you get a meal that could feed you, your significant other, your sister, your parents, and your dog. Ok, probably not that many people, but my eyes did bug a little when the plate came out. I usually opt for a small size whenever ordering anything because I'm dainty like that (ok, usually I go home and eat more food), but today I decided I wanted to try the Pad See Ew and the Green Curry which put me squarely in the court of trying a Medium Plate. I figured I could take the rest home, which I did. 

It is a super easy ordering system. Small = one entrée, Medium = two entrees, Large = three entrees, all come with one side. Since a Medium was about $1.50 more I figured I would indulge my gluttony and allow myself to try two entrees. I should have gone with the small, but at least I have dinner tonight. 

We started with the Chicken Potstickers. They were crispy and good. The entrees definitely stole the show. The Green Curry has a little bit of a kick to it. If you decide to go with a curry you may want to choose rice as your side. I ended up eating my curry more as a soup and I'll make rice later (since I still have half of it). The Pad See Ew portion was humongous. I didn't even feel like I ended up making a dent! I went with tofu as my "meat". I think it was fried. It had a sturdy texture to it. 

They also have sushi and boba drinks. I want to come back to try both of them.

Service is phenomenal. They are an order at the counter restaurant and yet they still managed to make sure my glass of water was never empty! I could have refilled it myself, but since they kept coming around offering, who am I to say no! 

This is now one of my favorite places to eat in this area. I will definitely be back.

Their desserts really hit the spot!

I owe Chris W. a review of all the goods I tried so this is jumping the line and getting written next. I sent my sister to get a plethora of baked goods for TWO people. She came back with EIGHT different pastries. It's as if she thinks we are both 300 lbs. Sure, she runs and does spin, but I gave birth a week ago and currently am not moving, so my calorie intake is much smaller. But I digress.

I really liked everything, but my favorite was the cross cream bun (not it's actual name. Since she got everything, I'm going by description). There was so much cream in it! It was absolutely delicious. There is a coconut bun that has cream down the middle (we also got that one), but I much prefer this one. The more cream the better.

Next by a slim difference was the chocolate crepe cake. Again, tons of cream and the layers were so light and fluffy. I devoured it (I'm pretty sure my sister only got a bite).

After that was the matcha mousse cake. I love mousse cake because it's not dry. Regular cake can often dry out, but this mousse one stayed moist for days. 

I also enjoyed the matcha sponge cake. It has a spiral of cream, in my opinion it could have more cream! It might have been a tad dry because it took three days for me to get to it. 

The egg tart was nice and flaky. My sister liked it and she's comparing it to LA Asian baked goods.

She said the pineapple tart was really good. She also got a pastry that had pork in it (so I couldn't try it) and said next time she would pass on that one. 

I counted, that was all eight. I'm just happy our Asian bakery stacks up to my sister's LA ones. She said if this was in LA she'd give it a four, but it's a five for Tampa for sure. Hey, I'll take whatever I can get. Now just bring one to Westchase.

This time I found some of the dishes hit or miss, but still overall a very enjoyable experience.

Remembering that the last time we ate here my husband and I waxed poetics about how my dad would really like this place, we decided to bring him here for his birthday dinner. (I think they bring out sparklers, with a complimentary dessert?, when you are celebrating a birthday because we saw it happen at two tables, but even though I mentioned in our reservation that we were celebrating a birthday there were no sparklers to be seen. If you really want those sparklers, make sure you make it obvious to your waiter that you are celebrating something).

The menu does change almost every month to the disappointment of my husband. He came prepared wanting to eat what he got last time. None of those plates were on the menu other than the baguette service, which I couldn't eat because I had gestational diabetes. I don't think he enjoyed anything as much as he liked what we got the first time.

Dishes we liked: Randomly, my favorite was the side of grilled cabbage that came with the quail breast. I've been trying to replicate it at home with our grill but haven't got it down. The quail breast was nice and tender too. My second favorite was the octopus. I should have just doubled down and ordered a plate just for myself. It was super tender. The rest of the dishes fell into the category of good but nothing I'm craving to have right away. That included the skirt steak and the mushroom and swiss burger (I found the chips that came with the mushroom and swiss burger too greasy). My dad got the beef tartar, but since I was pregnant I couldn't partake. He said it was very good. It comes with a raw egg on top. 

Dishes I didn't like: I recently had a very good beef tongue taco from Loli's Mexican Craving. I've been all about that beef tongue ever since. I really didn't like it here. The cut makes it lean and I didn't enjoy the flavor. I wouldn't get it again.

Service was fantastic. They do a good job at hiring waitstaff that is attentive but not overbearing. The waitstaff also seem to have a great knowledge of the menu and genuinely enjoy talking about the food and drinks. 

Expect a huge mark up on wines. The bottle my dad chose was $115, which in the store is normally $65. They have a solid scotch collection and will send someone over to help you choose one. 

You will definitely need a reservation on a Saturday night unless you want to sit at the bar. I never saw people waiting, but we originally had a table outside but since it was raining we asked to be moved indoors. They didn't think they'd have a table ready for us till about an hour later, but then someone left so we got it. I guess they operate on the cusp of having a wait list.

My new favorite spot close by.

I've been to Shaker & Peel now twice. Yes, they've only been open for about two weeks, but I loved it so much I had to go again. The first time was for a Westchase Moms Club event and the second was when my sister was in town. 

I could probably write a novel about this place so I'm going to try to keep it, relatively, short.

DRINKS: Have you seen the Salt Aire Margarita? There is a cloud of salty puff (best way I can think to describe it) floating on top of the drink. I saw a lot of people stop others to ask what it was, so I'm letting you know. I got the Pineapple Turmeric Margarita. It was a solid drink, but I'm excited to try other things on the menu. The drink menu is seriously stellar - I want to try it all.

FOOD - I got the Kale and Chicken salad twice, that's how much I loved it. It is the perfect salad for me. The amount of chicken, pistachios, and dressing is all so satisfying and delicious. I also tried the Miso Happy Shrimp Wok, which was also very good. The waitress warned us that it would be spicy, but I was pleasantly surprised that it wasn't, because I can't handle spice.

I also tried the General Tso's Cauliflower and the Flower Power taco. The Flower Power was my favorite of the two, but they were both good. The General Tso's was spicy. 

Finally, we tried the Duck, Fig, and Brie Dumplings. You really can't taste the brie. We actually asked the waitress if they forgot the brie, because it was so subtle. I wouldn't order it again, but it still tasted pretty good.

SERVICE - I just mentioned how we were surprised by the dumplings, well, the waitress took it off our bill! We were so amazed by that. My sister still ate the dumplings and we didn't say we disliked it, so this was stellar customer service. Even though our waitress was slammed getting three tables at once, she was efficient and friendly. It's been a while since I've loved a place equally for the food and service.

WAIT TIME - It is busy. We thought we'd avoid the rush by getting there at 5:25 p.m on a Sunday. It was a 20 - 25 minute wait, which was accurate. When I came with the Moms Club on a Wednesday night at 7:30 p.m. it was about half an hour wait. It's popular and I know why! Just be prepared. 

ATMOSPHERE - The whole place is decorated in blues and yellows. It's clean and modern looking. This is the perfect place for a date night. It is casual yet polished, which is my favorite type of place.

If anyone wants to check this place out, I'm willing to go a third time! There is so much more on the menu I want to try, but I will always get my Kale and Chicken salad, so I need buddies to go with!

The epitome of simplicity at its finest.

You will want to call ahead for seating. This place is small - maybe seats about 30 - and it does get busy. Normally, getting a table for four on a Tuesday doesn't seem like a difficult task, but this place is popular! Don't let that deter you from coming here. This place is worth it. 

THE ATMOSPHERE: If I was looking to fall in love, I would come here. This place screams romantic date night. There is both indoor and outdoor seating. It's intimate, warm, and welcoming. Heck, I would suggest coming here no matter what, because even if your date ends up being terrible, at least you'll get good food. If you need to impress a group, look no further, this is your restaurant.

THE FOOD: If you like octopus, you need to try it here. The night I went they had octopus two ways and a special octopus dish. Both were phenomenal. The octopus had the right amount of chewiness. I'm not going to repeat what others have said about the burger because honestly, they've said it all. I think I may have been the only person who has taken home part of my burger, so I can comment that eating this burger cold the next day is mind blowing. I may or may not have been crying with joy as I sat in my pajamas eating a cold burger. It was as if the flavors intensified. I'm lucky I work remote. The upgrade to truffle fries is totally worth it. Fries and truffle need to get married. It's going to happen one day. 

THE SERVICE: The service is great. I sat at the bar while I waited for the rest of my party and the bartender chatted with me even though I wasn't drinking anything. Our waitress was on point as well. This is the charm of a small restaurant - great service!

This is one of my favorite restaurants in St. Petersburg. You will not regret coming here.

They know how to make a mean sandwich!

We were preparing for an event all day so we needed to get take out from someplace that would keep us full for a while! Shout out to Brett N. for finding this place. Other than the star rating, one of the major draws to him was he could order online. Well, jokes on him because even though we were only a couple miles from the restaurant we were still outside their range of delivery. Just assume that you're outside their range of delivery and be pleasantly surprised if you aren't. However, since he was the one who had to deal with that, it didn't bother me. 

I decided to get a meatball sandwich. I called to verify it didn't include pork and was assured it is made with beef. Now, these sandwiches aren't for the faint of heart. Any other time I would have eaten half the sandwich and been full, but since I knew I wouldn't have that much time to eat later on I persevered and conquered the whole sandwich! I barely was able to eat any other bites the rest of the day because it filled me up. This is the type of sandwich where the filling is overflowing. You won't have to worry about a sad sandwich with too much bread for too little innards here. It was messy, it was delicious, it was everything I'd want a sandwich to be. 

I will definitely stop by here to get a sandwich every time I'm in the area.

Just an overall good experience. 

Brett N. was moving to Houston and I couldn't make his going away party because it was the first day of potty training my toddler (IYKYK). Instead I told him I'd meet him for a meal. Who knew he'd choose one that was 25 minutes away from my house. When I asked him if he had any other restaurants on his bucket list to try before he left he said no, just this one. Fine, I'll go here with you. In the end, I commend his choice. 

Brett gave this place four stars, but I'm going with five stars. Mainly because I rank atmosphere and experience above everything else. Yes, the food and drinks still have to be good, but if the food is good (not great), but the service and drinks are through the roof, five stars all around.

FOOD: We shared all the dishes and didn't actually try any of the BBQ. This is because we didn't turn over the menu to see that there was more. I don't regret this, because I've had good BBQ elsewhere and would rather try their unique dishes.

PB&J Wings: This was actually my least favorite dish we got. It mainly tastes like thai peanut sauce flavored wings. I'm not saying it isn't good, it is good, it just wasn't great. I would have appreciated more of a jelly taste, whereas it was overwhelmingly peanut butter.

Chicken and Waffles: We got the spicy glaze on the side, so maybe that's why it was lacking some flavor. However, the waffle was perfectly made. How was it so crisp? I would eat a million of the waffles and I usually avoid carbs. Another dish that I thought was good, but would probably pass.

Lobster corn fritters: Both my and Brett's favorite dish. The flavors were just superb. If you like lobster and you like corn fritters, try it.

Burnt Ends mac and cheese: My second favorite dish. I found the brisket to be very tender and the noodles weren't overcooked. I'd get it again.

DRINKS: The drinks are where this place shines. I wanted to try all the cocktails. I went with the Peaches and Cream which was amazing. I could drink five of them. I actually had the hardest time deciding what to drink there were so many good options. 10/10 would recommend going here for drinks.

SERVICE: Zach was AMAZING. Request him to be your server. He has such an incredibly deep knowledge of the menu and he isn't afraid to give strong recommendations. If I lived closer, I would learn his schedule and only come when he's working. 

This place's atmosphere is just cool. It was pretty busy on a Monday night and when it's not raining there's a good sized outdoor patio. They have a parking lot so parking is easy. 

I'd like to say this isn't good bye, but see you later, to Brett, but unless he comes back to Tampa, it's totally good bye. But, I'll always see him on Yelp.

Hip, yet non pretentious restaurant.

I have a confession to make. I know that Seminole Heights is considered up and coming, but I'm almost never there. I've heard of the Rooster and Till before, but I didn't want to make the trek. Up and coming to me still doesn't mean it is there. I enjoy DTSP, because I can walk from place to place. Heck, even if I don't have a destination in mind I can take a walk without a worry after eating in dtsp. Here, not so much. I still lock my car doors as I drive to the Rooster and Till. The real question is, is it worth the drive? Depends who you ask. My sister would hands down give this place five stars and come back. Too bad she lives in Santa Monica. I thought it was good, but it is as if we had two different experiences. This really epitomizes how food really is a personal experience. I liked the food, but I wasn't blown away enough that I would make the drive to return.

We spent a full day shopping at the outlets. We skipped lunch, so I was thrilled when I called and found out that they were open at 4 p.m. (some places it says 5 p.m. so I'm glad I called and asked!) My sister had wanted to try this place, because she researched farm-to-table restaurants in the Tampa Bay and this one stuck out to her. (Honestly, it was probably one of our only farm-to-table restaurants). It is in a rather barren location. Since we were there at such an odd hour, it was pretty easy to get a parking spot in front. Once you are inside, it is easy to forget where you are. They have an open kitchen so I would suggest either sitting at the bar or sitting in the seat that faces the bar. Unfortunately, I got stuck with my back to the bar so I missed out on all the action.

Our waitress was superb. She was very knowledgeable of the menu and pretty engaging. She suggested getting three plates and we agreed. It is a limited menu, but that's because everything is fresh. They bring out dishes as they are ready. We got the cheese plate, braised short rib gnocchi, and chicken thigh with tostones. If you read the menu, they do a much better job describing the components of the plate, but that's what stuck out to me. (I actually took a picture of the menu so I could remember all the ingredients, but I like my descriptions...or I'm just too lazy to look at my phone). The menu does change quite frequently. We were told the gnocchi is the only thing that's been on the menu for three years. It was also my sister's favorite dish. I always think gnocchi is made out of potatoes. I was craving potatoes. Not true in this case. It was made out of pate a choux dough. It was melt in your mouth, but when I was expecting a hearty potato piece, it was a bit of a shock. My sister said she would keep coming back here just for this, but honestly I was missing my potato. This is a classic to each its own. It was similar with the tostones. I was just in Puerto Rico and had some amazing tostones there. These are breadfruit tostones instead of made out of plantains (I had both while I was in Puerto Rico). Again, my sister loved it, but she had no expectations since she has never had a tostone before. I thought it was good, but a little too hard for my liking. However, the chicken was phenomenal. It was perfectly cooked and tender. We both agreed that we loved the cheese plate. We sent a picture to my dad and his comment was, "that's a lot of cheese". It was the perfect size for the two of us. Heck, I would love to have that cheese plate all to myself. The additional food complemented the cheese perfectly. There were salted almonds, honeycomb, jam, olives, and a fig bar. I was surprised by how little bread it came with. However, without us asking, our server asked if we'd like more bread. I feel like the lack of bread is more presentation than anything else. Don't be afraid to ask for more.

I feel the need to emphasize that this place is very food tolerant. Dishes are marked as Vegetarian or even Vegetarian Friendly, which means they can make a Vegetarian version! Same with Pesceterian. I don't eat pork, so even though neither of these truly pertains to me, it was very helpful while perusing the menu. 

Overall, I thought the meal was good, my sister thought the meal was great. However, since this is my yelp account, I'm giving it four stars. Ask her and she'd give it five plus. This is two people, eating the same food at the same time with very similar genes. It's all relative.

Solid menu options for a great brunch.

I don't eat pork so I'm a little more limited to what I can order, but I was still divided when trying to decide what to get. There were four different dishes I was debating between - yes four. That's when you know you have an appealing menu. 

When we were there, they had a 2 for $7 mimosa deal. The Asian mathematician in me is dying for making this mistake, but we ordered a champagne bottle for $27 to make our own mimosas. If there wasn't the deal, this would be great, because it came out to about six mimosas. However, with the deal six mimosas would have been $21. This is totally our fault and not the restaurant, but I'm writing this to stop anyone from making the same mistake! 

I would suggest making a reservation using Yelp. It got pretty busy quickly. We were there at 11 a.m. on a Sunday and by about 12:30 p.m. I saw some people waiting. 

Service was top notch. Our server continued to fill our glasses and was knowledgeable about the menu. She even made sure my friend was happy with a poached egg based on prior experience when people didn't realize the yolk would be so runny. Super proactive.

I got the Everyday People. The only reason I'm giving this place four stars instead of five is because I found my dish to be overly salty. The fried okra and the grits were heavily salted, and I love my salt. My friend got the Southern Hospitality and kept raving about it. She said the pork belly was absolutely amazing. If you eat pork, I would recommend getting it just from watching her devour her dish. 

In the end, with tax/tip, the entire meal came out to about $40. Knowing that the brunch buffet is $35 I would strongly consider it next time. It's definitely pricier than my average brunch, but I think the quality of the food warrants this price tag. 

The atmosphere is hip and the clientele seems to be groups of young professionals. I would definitely recommend it.

Quiet, unassuming restaurant with great food.

We were the only ones here for a majority of our meal on a Saturday at lunch. Maybe it is more busy during the week since it is right by the university, but I think it is a shame it wasn't busier. The food here is definitely worth checking out!

It is a small restaurant. There is one restroom. Again, since it wasn't busy this wasn't an issue at all.

We got a falafel platter and a vegetarian mixed plate. If I had to pick between the two, I would probably go with the falafel platter. Those lightly fried balls were absolutely delicious. However, I also enjoyed the vegetarian mixed plate. I'm not a huge fan of tabouli so I could have done without that, but everything else was delicious. I haven't been a huge fan of hummus lately, but I really enjoyed this one.  I particularly enjoyed the pita bread that came with the veggie plate. I think they butter and toast it so it is amazing. I could just sit and eat that pita bread. 

All the food tasted fresh and delicious. This is a great place to grab a healthy meal but still leave satisfied.

Pizza and Chinese food - weird combination, but it works.

My husband was furious at me for not taking him here earlier. To be honest, I had no idea this place existed until a coworker, Jonathan T., visited and myself and Brett N., my boss/last Tampa Bay CM, came up with places to take him. The email exchange went like this:

J: I'm planning to eat healthy while in Tampa.
B: We need to go get Chinese pizza.
J: Hell yeah we do.

When I brought up the ridiculousness of this exchange, I was basically met with, but it's Chinese pizza! Who was I to argue, I wasn't planning to eat healthy, so we put it on our list to check out. 

Saturday afternoon, about 12:30 p.m., and we are the only table in the restaurant. If you have little kids, they only have one high chair. I was victorious in getting it and I heard families after me ask and be told there were no more high chairs. It's a small place, so the one high chair thing isn't the most ridiculous thing ever, just a little surprising. 

It's in a strip mall and the restaurant itself is a little jank, but the food is legit. They make fresh dumplings on the weekend so we had to try that. We also got a scallion pancake and this stuffed with chive dish that I could never understand what the waitress was calling it. Then we finished this order with a Mapo Tofu pizza, Chicken Terriyaki pizza, and General Tso pizza. 

I couldn't try the dumplings because they had pork, but everything else was amazing. Admittedly, the Mapo Tofu pizza was everyone's least favorite, but it was still good. I wasn't a fan because I don't like spicy food. The Chicken Terriyaki and the General Tso pizza were amazing. It has a sweetness to it, even in the crust. The combination just works. They also do not skimp on the cheese. The best part, these pizzas are only $10! For 7 people we walked away paying $70 not including tip and we were stuffed. We basically took home over half of the Mapo Tofu pizza. 

For the price, quality, and novelty, this place cannot be beat. I'm lucky it is about half an hour from my house or else my husband would easily be 10 lbs heavier.

If you haven't eaten here, you're missing out.

It must be an unwritten rule that the best Italian restaurants in Tampa Bay are in nondescript locations. I have yet to eat in an Italian restaurant that astounds me that is in the middle of all the action. I could spend this whole review speculating on the why behind this or I can give the people what they want - a review of the food.

BURRATA: I searched the menu online to give you the proper name, but I can't find it. It was a special that our amazing waiter, Eric, showcased, so it may not be an every night option. It should be because it is absolutely divine. The addition of truffle to the burrata brought it to the next level. The crostini that came with the dish was buttered and crisped to perfection. I couldn't eat the prosciutto that came with the dish (no pork), but my tablemates devoured it.

BREAD AND SOUP/SALAD: Every meal comes with bread and either a soup or salad. The bread is solid, but like Eric warned us, don't fill up on it, because you'll be sorry when the entrée comes (rookie mistake that I make almost every time. I love my carbs). I opted for a soup, which was either Clam Chowder or Minestrone. The Clam Chowder was relatively light and definitely creamy. It was a good choice.

POLLO ALLA SESTO CON PENNE: First, I have to say, I have high standards for pasta. I will not eat it if it isn't made fresh because mediocre pasta kills my soul. You do not have to worry about that here. They get their pasta made fresh from literally down the road and you can tell from the taste. I was not hungry by the time my entrée came. As you can see above, I pretty much pigged out beforehand, however, my body had a mind of its own. The moment I started eating, I couldn't stop. It was a party in my mouth. The sauce was so creamy and delicious. I cannot recommend a pasta dish more highly. If you come to this restaurant you have to try the pasta, which lucky you, is in almost every dish (if not every dish). I will publicly shame you if I find out you came here and did not try the pasta. 

ATMOSPHERE: Random fact, when I was younger I used to accompany my parents to a lot of really nice restaurants. My dad is a wine fanatic, so we had to follow the bottle to places that have world-class options. I used to judge how nice a restaurant was by the restrooms. I found there was an odd correlation that if the restroom was super nice and paid attention to details, the restaurant was often stellar. The restroom here has a chandelier above the mirror. I love it. As for the restaurant itself, it will transport you to Italy. You will not believe you are in Pinellas Park once you step inside. 

RESERVATIONS: Pro tip, if you are coming on a popular night of the week, think Friday or Saturday night, make a reservation. This place was hopping by 6 p.m. on a Friday! It's a testament to how good the food is, that people come here, try it, and constantly come back. 

This is the place that you tell your friends about because you know it won't disappoint (believe me, I have). Try it yourself and thank me later.

Huge portion of Pad Se-ew.

I had the flu and it sucked, but that also meant that my husband was in charge of keeping me alive. This meant take out every night, which meant pad se-ew three nights in a row. After eating this dish for three nights, this is what I learned.

1. The portion size is huge! It could sustain me for three smaller meals or two large meals. I usually ate it for dinner and then breakfast the next day. On the third day I decided not to be a pig and ate more normal portion sizes and ended up eating it for dinner, breakfast, and then lunch. Pat on the back for figuring out how to not be a pig by the third day.
2. It's on the sweeter side. Randomly I found that if I was craving something sweet I could eat the Pad Se-ew instead of reaching for chocolate. This may just be my taste buds, but that's my experience.
3. I liked the tofu more than the squid. You will end up with a lot of whatever protein you choose to put in this dish. I got sick of the squid by the end (I know! Who gets sick of squid). I ended up ordering tofu the next two times and loved it.

I realize I need to branch out and try other places for Pad Se-ew, but this place definitely has my recommendation. I mean, I ate take out from here three days straight! If that's not an endorsement I don't know what is.

Good sandwich, but to me it didn't live up to the hype.

I really debated between giving this place three or four stars - crazy, I know. This place is absolutely beloved in Tampa. I finally settled on four because if there wasn't crazy hype surrounding this place I would have viewed it as four star worthy. I think I was just a little disappointed that it didn't blow my mind.

So where did this sandwich lose me? I got the roast beef without making any changes. I think I expected the pumpernickel to be heartier slices and there to be a ton more roast beef. Yelpers rave that the sandwiches are huge. I didn't feel like mine was that big - no huge amount of roast beef piled high. Afterwards I wish I got a side to go with it. I also tried my husband's turkey sandwich on cuban and I didn't think the cuban bread was that good. The roast beef was delicious though - thinly sliced and perfectly rare. It was definitely a solid sandwich, but I expected more. 

At 2:30 p.m. on a Saturday there was still a long line. It went all the way to where the line starts. I read some reviews that the line moves quickly, but I didn't find that to be the case. We waited for about half an hour. My husband did say that this is a lot faster than before they renovated. The steps are you wait in line until a sandwich maker is open, they make your sandwich, then you go pay. It's different than most places where you order and then pick up your sandwich later. I actually think I prefer ordering and picking up later because then you can sit down as a group and wait instead of standing for a while in line. Next time I'll definitely phone in an order and then pick it up.

I do have to give major props to their iced tea. The orange spice tea is amazing. They also have raspberry and mango which were pretty good. I also gulped down their sweet tea. Next time, I'm going to do an orange spice team/sweet tea combo. 

There are tons of seating. That's another positive to this place. 

Overall I don't think I'll be rushing to go back here. It was a solid meal, but it didn't blow me away.

Huge servings for pretty cheap.

I had to go to another meeting after eating here, so I powered through, but man you can get enough food for two meals if you eat here!

We started with the calamari and bruschetta appetizers (each $9). When they came out my jaw dropped. The bruschetta had six large pieces! Both were good, but not great. The calamari was seasoned well, but a little too fried for my liking. The bruschetta was also good, but I like it when I can taste the fresh tomatoes and this one used other seasonings/oils to mask the tomatoes a bit. 

But then my entree came. I got the Cajun Seafood Salad and I have to just say it was perfection. The seasoning to the dressing, all of it was absolutely delicious. I would 100 percent come back to get this again. Also, I feel like it was relatively healthy. The best part? It was only $11. That's insane! 

Both Sarah S. and Sarah R., got the chicken parm and wow it was huge! They didn't even look like they made a dent. This is the type of place my husband would love. For $16 you get at least two meals. 

There was only one waitress at lunch, so it took a little while. We were in and out in about an hour and 15 minutes. This might not be fast enough for professionals on a lunch break, but it's fine for anyone not in a rush! 

It is definitely an unassuming restaurant, but that added to the charm for me. I really enjoyed this place and I'd come back.

Fun place to grab a drink with friends.

I was shocked when I pulled up M.Bird on my phone walking up to the building and saw it had an average of three stars. I usually don't go anywhere that is less than 4, 3 1/2 if I'm really pushing it, but I was going to the second stop of a girl's night out (Mom's night out, actually, but that makes me feel old and lame to say) so I was stuck. 

I have to say, I think this place deserves more than four stars. These were my major takeaways. 

PROs - I love all things rooftop. We made a comment that there was a nice breeze going until we realized it was an artificial breeze created by fans. This bar knew that in Tampa, it gets hot! 

I feel like when getting drinks, atmosphere is everything and this place had a nice, trendy vibe to it. That alone is worth four stars to me.

CONs - They told us if we sat we would have to be served by a waitstaff and could only have a maximum of four tabs. There were twelve of us all paying separately. This was no issue at The Hall on Franklin, which was our first stop. This meant, we couldn't sit. I found that four tab maximum to be super weird. It was a Wednesday night so there were tons of empty seating, but we couldn't sit anywhere. 

I wasn't a huge fan of my drink. I got the I Left My Wallet at La Segunda, even without reading Brett N.'s review and finding out that's what he got and enjoyed. I think I expected a more fruity, tropical drink, and instead I felt like it was heavy handed on the rum. It is a beautiful drink though.

Overall I had a good experience here, so I would recommend it. Maybe it's because I didn't have food and experienced it as a drinks only place, but I found it to be enjoyable.

If you only get the BBQ it probably deserves a 2-3 star rating, but the Korean Philly is amazing.

I have to admit, I was going to get the brisket until I was standing in line reading Yelp reviews. The line was so long everywhere that I told my husband to choose a place and I would figure it out. I immediately regretted this when I saw this business had 3 stars after he chose it.

When I read Caitie S.'s review that said the Korean Philly is fire, I decided I had to try it. Thank God I did because I agree, it is amazing whereas my husband's chicken was tasteless. 

He also got fries, which would have tasted a lot better if it had some sort of seasoning. It definitely needed more salt. The coleslaw was also pretty tasteless.

My Korean Philly was delicious. It's filled with melted cheesey goodness. No, it is not healthy and I immediately felt like I had to go on a run, but I enjoyed it immensely.

The line was super long and slow, but every line was long. I rather not go back, but if I'm forced to I'll go with the Philly.

This is a perfectly acceptable Panera Bread.

I would have probably never gone here if my boss didn't ask to meet here for lunch. We were supposed to go to Curry Leaves, which is right down the street, but he was a little under the weather and didn't feel like Indian. Which is a shame, because I love Curry Leaves. 

I texted my former boss, Yelper Brett N., to ask can I refuse to meet here? In a foodie elitist fashion, I am not a huge fan of chains. Panera Bread, Starbucks, Cracker Barrel, they're all fine and will do in a pinch, but it's never my first choice to go to eat. 

As always, I looked online to see my choices and decided to go with a Baja Grain Bowl. It seemed healthy enough, yet still satisfying. It was exactly how I imagined it - a solid choice, but nothing exciting. I need to remember to choose something else next time.

The restaurant itself is clean and has plenty of seating. It looks pretty popular, we were there at about 1 p.m. and it was still fairly busy. I was worried there wouldn't be any parking, but the lot seems to be big enough for the businesses, so I had to walk a little, but at least there were options. 

They have self order kiosks, which is nice. Nobody seemed to be using them (we didn't either), but next time I come I probably will.

Again, there is nothing wrong with this Panera Bread, but I rather eat local when I can.

What I ordered was good, but I think I know the food that would have been great. 

Before child, I used to write super long reviews about everything I thought of a restaurant. Now, I basically write so future Christina knows what she should or shouldn't order. Here we go with the bare basics (sorry, my reviews are no longer meant to help out anyone but myself, but if you benefit from these, great!)

Since Big Ray's is about thirty minutes from my house, I sent my husband to pick up food from here for my birthday lunch (when else can you convince your husband to drive an hour round trip for food he's not excited about?) In the future, I think I'd want to consume it on property. Unfortunately, the fries and onion rings were lukewarm and soggy by the time it got home. Not Big Ray's fault at all, but good to know for future me. 

I got the Grouper Reuben. Next time I should get the Grouper sandwich (blackened). The thousand island dressing and the swiss cheese overpowered the fish IMO. The fresh fish really is the star of the show here, so there's no need to dress it up. I also found the onion rings oddly bland. It could have used some seasoning and see above about how it doesn't travel well. 

They were out of fish dip, so I went with conch fritters instead. Love these! I still want to try the fish dip next time if it's available, but I thought the conch fritters were super tasty and filled with conch. I did get a grease headache from my meal, so next time if I do get conch fritters I should forgo the onion rings (and maybe even the fries). 

Husband got the hot chicken sandwich. He did not like the dressing (it smelled like thousand island, but I didn't taste it and my own thousand island might have just been overpowering all other smells). He ended up wiping it off, but he really liked the sandwich. The chicken portion was huge. It came with parmesan fries. Next time get the sandwich sans sauce.

We got my son the kid's corn dog. I was reading reviews about a lobster corn dog and kind of thought the corn dog might randomly turn out to be lobster. I don't think the lobster dog is on the menu anymore, his corn dog was definitely a hot dog. But it was a solid hot dog. My husband gives his corn dog two thumbs up (my son barely nibbled on it, but that's him). My son did eat his fries. The kids meal is huge, so if you have a picky eater, you can probably share. 

I'm not going to go out of my way to come here, since the food doesn't really travel well, but if I'm in the area, this is top of my list to eat at.

Pasta is delicious, but heavy.

I finally decided to branch out and try something other than the Portobello Mushroom Salad. I'm sure it should be the other way, but ever since getting pregnant, I've been less concerned about gaining weight (ok, that part makes sense because it is inevitable, but I should still be healthy!) I've turned into quite the carboholic because it made me feel better when I had morning sickness. All of that is a long way of saying I finally tried the pasta.

At 6 p.m. on a Tuesday there was tons of seating. It looks like they've opened the dirt lot adjacent to the parking lot for people to park in, which is great because their parking lot is way too tiny! (I once tried to park there, couldn't find space, and ended up going somewhere else. 

This time service was a little spotty. We almost had to accost our waiter as he was walking by to get something because he never made eye contact with our table. We also had to ask for bread (always ask for bread with crack sauce. This is one of those breads that is worth filling up on) whereas it looked like it was brought automatically to the other tables. 

We started with the calamari. It was nice and lightly fried. It could have used some more salt, but there is salt on the table! 

I got the Baked Ziti with Eggplant and my friends got the Cibo's Primavera and Bianco and Spinaci Pizza. It was all supremely delicious but very heavy. Everything was super rich. Now that might be your version of heaven, and this is where taste is subjective, but I like leaving a restaurant without a food coma. I was in a serious coma after this meal. 

The Baked Ziti with Eggplant was absolutely smothered in cheese. The Spinaci Pizza had a generous heaping of ricotta on each slice. Again, all of this is delicious, but I only made it through half my dish (ok, granted I ate three pieces of bread with crack sauce, but shh) and I still felt super sluggish. 

This is the only reason I'm bumping it down to four. Don't come at me with pitchforks because taste is supremely subjective and I'm sure my husband wouldn't even register the richness of the meal. I think the perfect meal would be to split the Portobello Salad and a pasta dish. Now that sounds divine.

Phenomenal service and food.

I'm pretty sure Sue is going to get a shout out from every member of our party in our reviews because she is just that amazing. I've had great servers before, but this was even a step above. I wasn't eating soy/dairy/nuts/eggs, which made me a server's nightmare. Not to Sue. She not only didn't bat an eye when I rattled off the ungodly amount of ingredients I couldn't consume, but she laid down mad knowledge about hidden soy and eggs in dishes. Imitation crab has egg white and ikaru has soy, who knew?! Well, obviously Sue did and she saved me. 

Everything is made to order so on top of adapting a rainbow roll for me, again Sue with the knowledge reminding me that the eel has soy, they made a roll not on the menu just for me. It was delicious. I also got the hamachi-kama without ponzu sauce. Sue brought out a mix of spices, but honestly just a squirt of lemon made this dish shine. Even when I can eat everything I will get this dish again.

Sue was also on top of refilling everyone's glasses. Yes, I'm starting to see that this review is really just an ode to Sue. Even though I was only drinking water, my glass was never empty. Those drinking wine were having a really good night by the end. 

I loved Samurai Blue before, but I love it even more now. Although if Sue ever leaves she better let us know where she goes because I will follow her.

Great brisket and sides!

I love BBQ. Since my body tends to reject carbs (whether it's because of gestational diabetes or just the fact that my body clings to the carbs and makes me gain weight so I look like a oompa loompa), I'm a huge meat lover. I was meeting some friends in Brandon so after reading reviews I decided this would be a great place to try.

ATMOSPHERE: It is hot inside! I asked my friends if it was always like this and they said yes. I have to disclose that when I went I ran hot because I was pregnant, but it was still on the steamy side. We chose the tables at the end near the fan. I'm not telling you this to dissuade you from trying this place, but I would suggest grabbing food to go.

BBQ: I got the brisket. They chop it up into little pieces and pour BBQ sauce on it. I loved it. It had the perfect amount of moistness and fat to it. It's definitely presented differently than most brisket I've eaten, but I really enjoyed it.

SIDES: I got the collard greens and the cole slaw. I wanted to try the fritters, but they have pork in them (and they don't count as a side). Both sides were delicious. I really enjoyed the collard greens and felt relatively healthy eating it (please don't tell me if it isn't actually healthy).
