We went at 6 p.m. on a Wednesday night and there was no line. After we sat down to eat there were some people coming in and out, but it never really got that busy. It seems like lunch time is when they get their rush. 

If I'm ever back in the Brandon area, I will definitely come back to this place. But, like I said, I will definitely do take out!

Absolutely delicious japchae and kimchi pancake.

You know a meal is good when during every bite you think, this is a delicious meal. A friend was coming over and asked what food I'd like her to pick up. After a quick Yelp search I saw that this place opened close to her. Can I just say, dang is she lucky. I would be eating here constantly if it was close to me. 

I got the japchae and like I said, absolutely delicious. There's not a lot of beef in it, but really in Asian cuisine there aren't huge portions of beef so this wasn't surprising to me. It wasn't greasy and the sweet potato noodles were so good. They don't taste like sweet potatoes at all if you're wondering. (I'm not a huge fan of sweet potatoes so I feel like that's worth pointing out). 

The one random thing is with their banchan they give you a potato salad instead of fish cakes. I would have preferred the fish cakes, but oh well. The kimchi is very good, not too spicy.

I also tried the kimchi pancake and it was amazing. Next time I'm getting the seafood pancake for sure. It's a huge serving though, so it could be a meal or be prepared to share. 

My friend got the vegetable dumplings and she said it had meat in them. Definitely check on that if you're a vegetarian. She did eat all of them and said they are delicious. 

Basically I'm telling you if you're anywhere in the area, try this place. It's now one of my favorites.

Great outdoor dining for lunch.

When they say they open at 11:30 a.m. on a Saturday, they mean it. I tried to open the door at 11:29 a.m. and it was locked. They ended up opening it at 11:31 a.m., but whose counting. Don't be fashionably early for your lunch reservation if it's when it just opens.

They aren't doing valet due to COVID so you can park in the valet lot next to the restaurant for free. You have to follow the small signs to find the place or just follow your GPS. Don't go to the main hotel or else you are in the wrong place! I'm glad I read that before going. They suggest calling them if it's your first time to get directions.

Reservations can be made on Open Table, making the process super simple. I just wrote in the notes that we wanted outdoor dining. It's covered so even in the heat of the summer it's not bad. 

They have a fun cocktail list. I got a Sapphire Margherita (not that it went with my meal, but I wanted to try it). It wasn't very sweet and I'd try something else next time, but it was enjoyable. 

For lunch I got the Burrata Salad with Salmon added. Salmon is an additional $18 and came on the side. It was good and I think well worth the price. I find it funny that at places like this the scallops and shrimp are charged by the piece so you specify how many you want. My friend got shrimp last time and said they were huge, so worth the $3.50 each price tag. 

I really enjoyed my Burrata Salad. It had a good amount of burrata. The additional salmon was definitely needed, I wouldn't have been full without it. I enjoyed my entire meal.

The bread they bring out before the meal is very good. We devoured it. 

Overall this was a good meal with a beautiful view. It's expensive, but the quality is there. Service was also very good. I would absolutely do another meal here.

I love what this place stands for, but the meal fell a little short for me.

This is a really odd review for me to write. If my husband was here he would give it 2-3 stars. I personally found it between 3-4 stars, and I bet my friend who I dined with would give it between 4-5 stars. Why the discrepancy between everyone?

1. It was hot! I tend to run cold, but I was actually sweating in this restaurant. I mean the type of sweat that you see on your seat when you stand up! I was surprised I didn't read about this in any of the other reviews so I asked one of the employees if the AC was broken. She said because of the size of the place it is usually this temperature but would see if she could turn it down. I would highly advise take out if it is normally this hot. My husband, who runs hot, would have walked out (so thank god I wasn't with him.) My friend and I decided to suck it up and make the best of it. 

2. The pasta isn't made fresh, even though they have classes about making fresh pasta. I think I may have inadvertently insulted the server (who I also think is either an owner or the father of an owner of the restaurant) when I asked if the pasta is fresh. He basically told me it is impossible for them to make fresh pasta (that's an extremely shortened version because I got a speech about the difficulty of making pasta), however, there were two dishes that day with fresh pasta. One of them was a Frangozzee and the other was a Gnocchi. The regular menu features meals that are $10 and the specials are $20. Since I don't like consuming pasta unless it is freshly made, I went with a special. This is where my experience differs from my friend. For $10, her carbonara was a steal! It was exactly what she wanted and delicious. For my $20 I was disappointed with the Frangozzee. It kind of tasted like bean stew. I don't eat bacon (and I didn't realize there was bacon in it since it wasn't listed in the ingredients.) Luckily, the server came back and asked if I ate bacon. I wonder if they replaced the bacon with more beans because it was overwhelmingly covered in beans! The mussels in the dish were delicious, but even the fresh cooked pasta was underwhelming. 

If you are dining on a weekend evening, you need to make a reservation. There is a total of six tables and everyone was reserved (I did make a reservation!)

The people who own this place are lovely and the normal pasta dishes seem like a good deal. I think I just had an off dish, which is why I'm still rating this place highly. My major advice is to get take out!
Remember here (Cash is king).Ya I waited in line about 20 minutes who cares !!! the food is delicious. I will say no more BEST cheese steak in town.
Came here for happy hour.  Got a few dishes and drinks. The food was delicious and service was great. The ambiance was also very nice would definitely recommend this place.
Great spot for every occasion.  They have 4 levels and the roof top has an awesome view.  I would definitely recommend it and will be coming back.

Came here with happy expectations.  Computers were down and had to wait about 15-20 min to get started. Drink service was ok from the first server. Then we got another do to a shift change and service was very slow. Had empty drinks constantly and when we got the bill they tried charging  us for two hours of game play. We had only been there for 1.5 hours and some of that time we spent waiting on them to get the computer running. Customer servuce sucked.

I must say, this restaurant did not live up to its reputation.  Food tastes fine, but is basically 3 choices of protein braised in various (6) sauces.  Rice and beans are inedible.  Tortillas are like cardboard. Plating is, to my mind, messy.  2/3 of the plate is a  deconstructed salad (mostly lettuce and jicama). which is difficult to eat without drowning the salad in whatever sauce is on your chicken or beef.

The waitress was beyond horrible.  Since there are no menus (cute?) you are forced to listen to your 6 choices and she raced through the descriptions at breakneck speed and showed annoyance at being asked to speak more slowly.  She brought the plate with an undressed salad and never pointed out a cruet of dressing on the table .  (Oh, and did I say it is crazy dark). Never asked if we wanted wine or another margarita until the meal was finished.

In a city full of good Mexican food, this restaurant does not deserve a try..skip it...

I've been here a few times and mostly have the food delivered using the Yelp app. The ordering process is pretty easy and the food generally arrives in a timely fashion. I usually order a bowl and this time I tried the Bulgogi Bibim-bab bowl. It comes with a cup of Miso soup and a sauce of your choice, I'm a big fan of the spicy mayo. The bowl was good and had lots of veggies, rice and meat. In the past I would get the large bowl but I don't think it's worth it anymore as the regular is pretty filling and the large isn't that much larger.

If you haven't tried it yet give it a try.

My first time having Pho in Pennsylvania. I'm from the West Coast so I was a bit afraid how the taste like since there isn't much of a Vietnamese population here. When you first arrive at the place the outside looks like a traditional small restaurant. Walking in the place is small but has good amount of seating. The waiter sat us three by the window near the front so I didn't get to see the back seating area. 

We ordered the shrimp spring rolls, egg rolls, and Pho Dax Biet ($9.95) Overall, I was surprised on how excellent the quality of the food was. It probably tasted exactly similar to the west coast pho Vietnamese restaurants. It only came in one size bowl but it was enough for me to take home for left overs! I'm glad I was able to try this place because my boyfriend said he's been here multiple times and he was never disappointed.

This is my first time attending at cat cafe at all. I was really impressed. You have to book an reservation online and it costs $11 for 1 hour in the kitty room. I think it is actually reasonable price and time limit. Plus all the money goes for the cats for adoption. At least it's not just 30 minutes. The cats are so cute! The only down side was that we were the first group after their nap time so all the cats were sleeping still when we came in. It took a while until they finally woke up and started to play. I also like the idea of drinking coffee, tea or even a milkshake while playing the cats. My friend ordered the unicorn milkshake and it was delicious! It was a mix of lucky charms marshmallows and birthday cake mix! The room is super cute with pink and white decorations. The room is small because they only allow 10 people per time. Overall I was really happy with this cafe!

This place is cute. I like how you have the option to dine in or take out. If you dine in, you just sit at any table and a lady will come and take your order. They even deliver the dessert to you. If you want to go order, you can order from the cash register and they will call your order and give it to you. The customer service is really friendly and nice. I like how they keep it professional with their uniforms.

For the dessert i would probably say 9/10. It has a wide variety of desserts and drinks to choose from. If you like green tea or matcha this is the place to go! But I'm not a fan of that so it was hard for me to choose from. The desserts are a bit on the smaller side but still pretty good. They have some unique looking desserts too. My friend got one that was lychee with cheesecake. It turned out pretty good. The drinks were not bad either. I got the passion strawberry lemonade green tea. That one tasted okay to me only because I didn't like the strong taste of the tea part. My friend also got the tangerine dessert and they make it look so real but you were able to cut into it like cake in which I was pretty impressed.

The place is small but they offer a lot of seating. I came here on a Saturday so it was pretty packed. Luckily a group before us at the table left so we were able to sit down. The prices for the dessert is pretty expensive for just a small amount. But overall the place itself is not too bad.

Old school Italian Gem in Lawrenceville!  If your looking for authentic Italian cuisine this is your place!  It's well worth the drive as these type of restaurants in NJ are sparse.  This restaurant is an almost an hour south from me, but I have no problem making another trip for delicious authentic Italian food like my grandma from Sicily would cook for me.  Enzo's was everything I'd hope it would be, but even better!  I started with the eggplant rollatini, and it was hands down one of the best eggplant rollatini I ever ate!  It's a must order here!  I was debating between a few different entrees as there was such a large selection here, and I decided to go with a dish I couldn't get anywhere in my area.  I picked the homemade tagliatelle with braised chicken, figs, and walnuts.  It's an authentic Italian dish my grandma made, but I haven't found it at any restaurant since dining here tonight.  I absolutely loved it!  I also ordered a side of meatballs which I enjoyed too!  For dessert I had the white chocolate and blueberry bread pudding, and it was very good!  I would recommend they make the sauce on top a touch more sweeter for it to be even more delicious.  Nonetheless, I'd still order it again!  There was only one thing disappointing about tonight.  I ordered a s'mores cookie to take home and it was hard and dry.  I'm not sure if I would of had it at the restaurant if it was suppose to be warmed up to taste good.  I'd inquire about it before I order the s'mores cookie.  I highly recommend dining at Enzo's in Lawrenceville!  I'd make the hour trip to dine here again in a heartbeat!

If I were rating Under The Moon Cafe from my first time dining here I would of given it 5 stars!  Unfortunately, when I dined here 4 days later that day I would of given it 3 stars.  I came in here on a Sunday for the first time, and I absolutely loved it!  I ordered the empanadas for an appetizer, and they are DELICIOUS!  One of the best empanadas I ever had!  The meat inside was seasoned to perfection!  For entree I had the Dirty Gnocchi which was very good!  The gnocchi tasted like soft pillows of heaven!  I highly recommend ordering it!  For dessert I had the brownie and the Dulce de leche pie.  The brownie was ok/good, but it tasted like it was made a few days prior.  The Dulce de leche pie was OUTRAGEOUS!  I loved the restaurant so much I came back 4 days later which was a Thursday.  The first thing I noticed was the dessert display case since I'm a huge dessert lover!  They had the same desserts in the display case as Sunday with everything almost gone!  Unfortunately, they were the same desserts they were trying to still get rid of from Sunday!  When they should of been tossed out by this time!  That day I had the artichoke rice balls which tasted horrible!  It didn't taste  like your traditional Italian rice balls.  They had a bad taste, and it was topped with disgusting sauce!  Skip them!  For entree I had the ropa vieja which was very good, but it came with more tostones than actual meat!  The dish would of been better paired with plantains.  For dessert I had the banana chocolate chip bread pudding, but when I received it, it was stiff because it was sitting in the case from 4 days ago.  I asked the waitress to heat it up more to soften it.  Then it was Delicious!  I also took a chocolate nut crepe to go.  The chocolate nut crepe ended up being stale!  The crepe layers were all dried out and stiff.  Crepe cakes should be served within 2 days since the layers are delicate.  It goes bad fast, and the one I received tasted like it was made a week ago!  Any desserts you order ask what day it was made!  If there is only a few pieces left of something avoid ordering it here!  I still recommend dining here as it's such a cute restaurant plus the first time I came everything was Amazing!  I still plan on coming back, and hopefully it's just as good as my first experience!

Dined at La Fourno last night with a Travelzoo voucher.   I've dined here before, and it wasn't  anything to write home about, but last night was just... bad.

Started with the Pizzette special of the day - Pizza with duck prosciutto, gorgonzola, and balsamic. Sounded like it should have been amazing. In my husband's words, "It smells like wet dog." Despite the off-putting scent, we dove in, as we were starving. I must say that the crust of the pizza was very, very good. The mox of toppings, however, was an epic fail. The owner came over to check on us when we were 1/2 way through and we told him it wasn't out favorite. His response was, "Well, it's a recipe straight from Florence." As if we were idiots for not enjoying it. Remind me not to order this next time I'm in Florence, either.

Next came our entrees -- Penne a la Vodka for me and Calamari Fra Diavolo for husband. Both were flavorful and we enjoyed them. Only point worth noting is that the pasta was so hot that I have to assume that Chef Mike (AKA the microwave) had a hand in the cooking process. The food, however, isn't the reason that I won't be returning to La Fourno.

After our leftovers were packed, I watched as the food packer/table setter lady "washed" her hands in a bucket of water next to the bar. I'm not a germophobe, but I was appalled and disgusted. Also, the fail to mention that if your bill is less than $50 (which ours was, since we had the voucher), they do not accept credit/debit cards. Thank goodness we had some cash on us. Add to that the owner reprimanding servers on the floor, and I've got three good reasons not to return.

Formosa Seafood Buffet is owned by the same people who own 8 China Buffet, just up the road.  It's shiny and brand new right now, and obviously meant to go head-to-head with Journey for the higher-priced buffet market.  The theme, at least in the room we were in, was astrological; there was a large image of a bridge of stars and two Chinese mythological figures on one wall, and smaller plaques of the Western zodiac signs around the room.

The waitstaff are of more varied ethnicity than I'm used to at an Asian buffet, friendly, and fast-moving.  Upon arriving at our table we were greeted by a woman with a cart of various soups such as congee (a personal favourite).  There were also a few carts of dim sum items going around.

I feel bad that we weren't hungry enough to do the place justice on this trip.  The food was varied and kept refreshed, and there was a long counter with a wide variety of sushi rolls.  My personal favourite for sheer novelty was what appeared to be kappa uramaki topped with slices of kiwi fruit and a dot of strawberry sauce on each slice!  The buffet items were about what you'd expect; fried items, main dishes, various shellfish, roast meats, salad, pastries, fruit/vegetables, and a large cooler table full of ice cream.  The food that we tried was good and kept refreshed, with a good balance of buffet standards and more unusual items.

It was very good overall, and we're definitely going to come back on a day when we're a little hungrier!

I have hemmed and hawed about writing this review for about a month now.  If you look at the breakdown of my reviews, I tend to only review places I like, and generally I'm pretty easy to please.  Having read all of the excellent reviews for this place, my office decided to get take out for lunch from here and I volunteered to go pick it up.  I ordered the Tie Dye Stew and a Plain Jane baked potato from their online menu.  According to this menu, the Plain Jane Baker is topped with butter and sour cream only.  When I went in to pick up the food, the girl behind the counter had to look up the prices for all of the items we ordered in the menu.  She was nice enough, but I really feel that getting the prices on the ticket should probably have been done before I arrived.  In any event, I got my food and drove the 15min back to my office.  

This is where my real disappointment begins.  
I hand out everyone else's food and when I get to mine, my potato is covered in cheese and bacon.  As I am vegetarian, this was a pretty big problem for me.  I called them up to tell them what happened, and the woman on the phone sounded put out that I had even called with the problem and asked if I wanted a credit or another potato.  As it was my lunch, I told her I would like another potato and would be driving the 15min back to pick it up.  I reiterated that I had ordered the Plain Jane Baker from their menu, and she acted like it was the first she had ever heard of it.  I also received no apology for the error or for the time and gas that I would be wasting to get another potato.  So I drive back to the restaurant.  When I arrive, a woman tells me that my potato isn't done yet, that they were out of baked potatoes and mine was in the microwave.  MICROWAVE?!  How is that baked?  At this point, I just needed to get some food and get back to work as I'd wasted all of my lunch hour driving back and forth, so I didn't argue...but really, microwaved?  I stood and waited close to 10 minutes for this potato.  The entire time I was waiting, no one offered me a glass of water, a seat, a cookie...nothing at all.  I'm not looking for a handout, I didn't ask for the potato and credit, I still paid full price for the damned thing.  Really, I would have been happy with any sort of sincere apology, but all I got was an "oh, sorry 'bout that" when I came back in.  I finally got my potato and drove back to work.  The potato was alright, I guess, for a microwaved potato, but the stew (now cold) wasn't good at all.  It was tomato based and the vegetables in it tasted frozen.  I only ate half.  

Having worked in restaurants for years as a server, bartender and manager, I'm very forgiving of mistakes.  Slow service?  The kitchen is probably backed up.  Waitress looks overwhelmed?  It's cool, I don't mind waiting a bit for my refill.  However having worked those jobs, I also understand how mistakes should be handled, and this was not it.  I really wanted to like this place, and felt really let down by the entire experience.  I will not be returning.

We got carry out lunch from Tlaolli the second day they were open and oh mama were these tamales good!  Please note - this place is very vegan and vegetarian friendly!  I tried the vegetarian cheese poblano tamale, as well as the vegan bean tamale - both were amazing.  I also tried the salsa verde, which comes with a small portion of chips, and it was great as well.  Extra good with the bean tamale.  They also have a sandwich made with soy chorizo - I can't wait to try it out!

The customer service here was also exceptional.  A co-worker went to pick up lunch for three of us, and when she got there she found out they were not yet accepting credit card (the form of payment we had sent with her).  Instead of having her leave to get cash, they insisted she take the order and just come back with payment ($18 for three meals!) the next day.  They wanted us to be able to enjoy our lunch on that day, and not worry about our food getting cold, so they went with the honor system.  If the food hadn't won me over, that move certainly would have.  

Five thumbs up for this new east side gem!

The area surrounding 1st and Limberlost was lacking sit-down/takeout oriental food. Not anymore! Dao Tai Pan's takeover in the unusual-looking small building complex dishes out Vietnamese, Thai, and Chinese food. They expanded to a second location as they operated their east side location for many years. 

Great customer service. In fact, it was almost too much customer service. It's a little too invasive, but I rather have that problem than having the bare minimum attention. They are very nice and friendly. You'll be greeted right away upon entering the restaurant. 

Pho is always my "go to" when eating Vietnamese food. I echo Brad H's advice that large is the way to go. It will fill you up and leave you satisfied. My other piece of advice is to take some noodles out of the pho, put it on a plate, squirt some hoisin sauce on it, and eat it with chopsticks. Delicious! 

In the afternoon, the sun really sits in on the restaurant. I hope they get some shields to place on the windows because it was too bright inside. If they don't get it, just be sure to sit at a table opposite of the sun. That or you'll be wearing sunglasses inside. 

The atmosphere is neat. The place was clean, the decorations are cool, and the layout is very open. You can see most of the employees, whether it's the servers or the chefs. I always prefer that over barely getting to see anyone except for the person serving the food.

Check this place if you're in the area, and make your own conclusions about this place. My experience was very good!

I was pretty excited to come to Whatever Pops ... Until I got here then I was overwhelmed! So many choices... Given my allergy restrictions however it narrowed it down but still I was so impressed with what they had to offer! I wish they had some coconut milk or almond milk ice creams or gluten free waffles on a stick.

Yep that's right waffles on a stick the place is impressive and a gourmet ice cream experience. Or if you want to stay on the healthier side they offer Gluten Free acai bowls that are pretty tasty. Definitely a place worth trying out if you haven't yet!

Everyone isn't focused on the right things when it comes to PYT. It isn't about the TERRIBLE, god-awful service - it's about the   Horrendous burgers piled so high with junk that you can't even eat them. Sure, you'll be able to take a photo for Instagram and show everyone what you ordered, but when it comes to eating the stuff you'll be sorry. PYT represents the great catch-22 of burger restaurants: you order something because it sounds "cool" and "krazy", but then you actually try to eat it and it's so cool and krazy that you can't even wrap your mouth around it. Oh, and if you do manage to eat your burger you'll find a distinctive note of "tastes bad" with the slightest hint of overcooked.

Also, the service sucks.

The worst mexican food I've ever had in my life. I am from San Diego, I'm visiting Tennessee and was craving mexican food. Mexican food here is nothing compared to San Diego mexican food. 

The chips and salsa were good, the guacamole was very bland. Margaritas were great and a good price for the pitcher. 

The food was terrible. The chicken in the crunchy taco had absolutely no flavor and tasted old. The taco itself was tiny, it hardly had any toppings on it and the shell was not crunchy. The cheese enchilada was very bland and the sauce they used was tasteless. The chilie relleno was odd, normally they have cheese in them but this one had chicken. Even though I did not order that. The chille itself was not bad but like I said the chicken here is flavorless. Surprisingly the rice and beans were the worst thing on the plate. The beans had such an odd flavor that I couldn't even take 2 bites of it. The flavor completely ruined my appetite. 

Overall, I'm sure if you're from the south this food might be authentic to you. If you're from San Diego or anywhere where they have authentic delicious mexican food you will not like this.

So fun!!! Bought a Groupon and I'm so glad I did, this place had great food! 

They have different combos to choose from, then you order your sauce and spice level. I got the combo number 3 which came with so much seafood! All of the food tasted very fresh and was cooked perfectly. 

They give you bibs and gloves to wear as well, but I ended up not using the gloves because it made it a bit difficult to open up the crab. It was fun getting messy otherwise! There was tons of sauce, plenty to dip all your food in. The corn was so good! The dungeons crab was huge and absolutely delicious. 

The service was great! I had a text and couldn't open it because my hands were so messy. Our amazing waitress comes over and puts my phone to my face to unlock it! Now if that isn't great service I don't know what is! 

Overall really delicious, fun experience and phenomenal service this is definitely a place to come check out!

It was so great to find this hidden treasure! My date and I were in the mood for Thai and Yelp turned up Lemongrass as a Vietnamese restaurant that was good for vegetarians. It had good reviews and Vietnamese sounded like a perfect change of pace for us. 

Since I'm a vegetarian I am immediately intrigued when a restaurant touts itself as vegetarian. It's a loose description and I have often felt mislead once asking questions about the menu. For example, the soup has only vegetables but when pressed about the broth I am told it is made with chicken. 

To my vegetarian delight Lemongrass was an excellent experience all around including their vegetarian options. As soon as we were seated a nice woman came over and asked if we were vegetarians. I let her know I was but my date was not. She handed me a vegetarian menu! Yes, a list of all the things I can eat! Not a list of things that they can modify if needed. Hurray- this was a good sign! My date was handed the standard meat eaters menu and a "Winter's Specials" menu. 

We selected the vegetarian rolls to share and were satisfied with the price and item. For two tasty rolls with a side of peanut sauce it cost $4. We weren't feeling as adventurous as usual so we both ordered Sweet & Sour, chicken for him and tofu for me. We had a choice of jasmine or brown rice, we went for the jasmine. While we waited for the food we discussed how we were probably missing out on some great food by selecting something we could get at a local Chinese take out joint. 

When our food arrived we were happily surprised. There was no bright red, gloppy sauce with deep fried chunks of protein. Instead the sliced chicken/tofu was mixed with chunks of barely done onion (I love it this way!) and slivered red bell pepper. There was the slightest look and taste of seared/caramelized pieces. The sauce was brownish and topped with chopped cilantro. The sauce was thin but had body, delicate but full of flavor. The jasmine rice must be discussed, too. This is not Chinese take out rice, this is jasmine rice cooked perfectly. So rarely can I use chopsticks to eat rice because it's not cooked to stick together. This rice broke off into my chopsticks in beautiful chucks and withstood being lightly dipped into the sauce. It was satisfying!

The water seemed better than most places, I'm thinking it must be filtered. The ice cubes looked like mushrooms. I don't know if this is on purpose but I was amused! I ordered Thai Iced Tea and was again pleasantly surprised by the flavor. Typically Thai Iced Tea is sweet, very sweet. At Lemongrass the Thai Iced Tea was potent. It had a strong tea flavor with a light sweetness. Very different from what I am used to but delicious none the less. 

Our meal came out under $33. A steal as far as I am concerned. 

Service was kind and friendly. However, the place was busy and having only one server had us waiting on the edge of too long at certain points. 

Verdict? Go here, soon. It's a great place for a reasonably priced meal. Food is high quality and delicious. I will definitely return soon. See you there!

My mom and I ate here yesterday and had a great experience. We sat on the patio. Our server was very friendly. He took our drink order and just a minute later brought them out. The drink I had was called White Lightning, it was delish. We got one of the burgers and it had a fried green tomato on it, row sauce, and chow chow.. So good!! We had a side of fries and Brussels with bacon. Everything was really good and came out fast. The live entertainment was great too. Would definitely come back here if I make it back to Nashville again.

P.S. If you're a beer lover they have a huge selection of beers.

Oat Milk? In Reno? At a drive thru? Color me addicted!!!! Whoa. 

After hearing about this coffee shop in the local BLM group, I decided to stop by to show support. I have tried the pomegranate iced tea, which I would recommend getting sweetened! This morning I got an iced oat milk vanilla latte, and as a former barista I can be a bit of a snob on coffee. WHOA. Perfectly sweet without being nauseating, and the espresso was excellent. The oat milk was excellent, and the coffee / tea prices were so cheap! 

I also got a bagel. The bagel was a little undercooked, but I should've asked for it extra toasted since I am a godless heathen who would rather choke than eat raw bagel. The cream cheese was freaking AWESOME! I think it may have been made in house, but I'm not sure. I got the jalapeño flavor and good lordt, it was phenomenal. I'm looking forward to coming back again and again!

I went for lunch last Saturday. Let me count the ways this place sucked.

1. No management anywhere to be found. People were working without direction, and service was crap to say the least.

2. Our hostess took our drink order and food order and checked in on us time to time as our server should have. Our server came one time just before the bill arrived. We ended up tipping the hostess cash and the server 0. 

3. The food was no better than I could get at any grocery store. The mac and cheese for my daughter was inedible. We got the shrimp basket and I swear I get the same thing out of a bag. 

4. The bathrooms were the worst thing I have seen in a long time. Inches deep of standing piss in 2 out of 4 urinals. 

5. Arguing between the hostess and one of the servers. I suspect because the hostess was just trying to help people the server didnt like it and feared she would take tips away. The hostess was berated in the middle of the dining area by a  blonde waitress for well over a minute. How embarrassing. 

This is the 2nd time we have gone to Hotrods. We like the concept and the layout of the area, but both times, the service sucked, and the food was meh, at best.

This place deserves 3.5 stars (come on yelp hint hint). We came here on a Sunday afternoon after the Chestnut Hill's petapalooza. When we walked up to it we weren't sure if it was open or closed since there are no windows or signage etc... When we open the door it seemed to be pitch black inside and it took a few moments for our eyes to adjust. This is most definitely a pub! Dark, wood, beer. 
   We ordered the schmitter which you totally must get if you've never had one before. My only wish is that they put an extra slice of salami. The combo of the salami, meat, onions, cheese, and thousand island dressing (at least that's what it tasted like to me) was really good and unlike anything I've had before. I wish that it came with fries but chips did the trick.
   Two smitters and two beers will set you back only $30. They had tv's playing a soccer match (that's a plus). My favorite part of the restaurant was a waitress/bartender. She was the sweetest most attentive woman. She made you feel like if you were in her home. You can tell she truly loves what she does. If we're ever in that area we'd stop by again.

Ignore Dawn.

This place is great. The food was amazing, the menu was very modern. Out server was excellent. I agree the staff has strong enthusiasm which did seem like they were really trying to win you over desperately, but I think they're genuinely excited for their new look. The decor is beautiful and the projector that comes out of the patio deck to play the game on the outdoor wall is brilliant.

This place is still priced right for the blue collar residents that Dawn is talking about. But Dawn, just because you are blue collar (as am I) doesn't mean you have to settle for sitting in a place that looks like a blue collar dive. 

Taylor's has revamped their look, attitude and menu keeping the same neighborhood prices. I think it's a brilliant step in the right direction and a change of pace that the neighborhood needed. Hopefully more places in Roxborough can follow suit so that Ridge can liven up from its run down looks.

I've been to several different Flowing Tide locations in town, and I remember liking them, but I was never being a big enough fan to go out of my way to dine or drink there. Now that I have one in my neighborhood though, I frigging LOVE it!  This is a great local chain of neighborhood bars with the Happiest Hour(s) in town- 2:00-6:00 AND 10:00-midnight daily! Service is always fast and friendly, and I appreciate that the staff remembers me when I come in. It's totally a "Cheers" kind of place.

The food is standard pub fare and while it's not the greatest, it is always tasty, satisfying, and affordable. I come in specifically for their quesadilla packed with not just gooey cheese, but all kinds of delicious veggies! I wish they were a little more generous with the guac, but I understand that avocados are pricey...Add-ons (i.e. cheese on a salad =$1.39, guac = $3.00) are a little overpriced in my book, and I wish they didn't have a surcharge for takeout orders, but this is a locally-owned business and I'm sure it's priced that way for a reason. Everything else is so dang affordable that I don't really mind coughing up a little extra to have my meal just the way I like it. I still might not travel out of my way to visit Flowing Tide, but I am grateful to have one in my neighborhood and I fully take advantage of that!

A solid 4.5 stars for Naan & Kabab!  Naan & Kabab is the first full-service Mediterranean restaurant to come to Reno.  There were a few small counter service Mediterranean restaurants, but none of them offered a full dining experience.  Of course, there are a few more Mediterranean restaurants these days, but we wouldn't have those without Naan & Kabab leading the way.  Located across from the Peppermill (and next to Ruby River), it may be a little easy to miss.  They have a huge sign, but it has very light coloring and may be a little easy to miss if you aren't actively looking for it.  I have never had anything less than fantastic service in this cozy restaurant.  The moment you walk in, you will be greeted with a warm, genuine welcome.  The wonderful aromas of saffron and spices will delight your sense of smell and will make you start salivating for this wonderful cuisine before you even peek at the menu.  Chef Maurice is always there at dinner, and he visits with each table to ensure that his guests are satisfied.  He is a very warm, genuine man- always offering a handshake and coupon for a free Awesome Dude on your next visit.  He is very passionate and loves what he (and his team, particularly Tom and Sam) does, and you can taste that love (and freshness!) in the food.  

The Awesome Dude is definitely awesome!  The pistachios in the saffron-vanilla ice cream balance out the sweetness of the baklava nicely, making the dessert a nice way to finish your meal without being too sweet.  It is also an ideal portion- not too much, not too little.  However, I ALWAYS get the Vegetable Combination appetizer and rarely have room for dessert.  Seriously guys, Naan & Kabab has the best dolmades (stuffed grape leaves) in town!  Ditto for their falafel, hummus and tzatziki.  The naan is freshly grilled, brushed with garlic and baby dill-infused E.V.O.O. and is the perfect texture.  The dipping sauce that accompanies it (I believe it is called torshi, but forgive me if I am mistaken!) is the perfect partner for this delicious naan.  I have never ordered anything at Naan & Kabab that I have not thoroughly enjoyed.  It is a wonderful date for an intimate dinner with friends and loved ones, offering excellent food at very affordable prices.  It's not really set up for large parties, though they can easily accommodate 6-8 patrons without a reservation.  They also cater!  Do yourself a favor and check it out!  (And make sure you check in on yelp for a free Awesome Dude on your visit!)

Hellfire Saloon is an unexpected delight! I have lived in the neighborhood for a few years, but I never figured that there was a decent hangout spot in the shopping center at S. McCarran and Mira Loma...Boy, was I wrong! A few different businesses have occupied the space over the past few years, and when I noticed Hellfire's sign last year, I just figured it was a divey biker bar. 

Don't get it twisted, I love me some dive bars, but I was pleasantly surprised to discover how clean, open, and family-friendly Hellfire Saloon actually is! The restaurant is open, friendly, well-lit, and smoke-free, with ample room for parties. They have live music several nights per week, and offer full bar and restaurant services at VERY affordable prices! This bar is so much nicer than it looks from the outside, and the waitstaff is great! Our server was so attentive, friendly, and anticipated our needs better than Miss Cleo! (I know, I'm dating myself here, but I hope you're old enough to know to whom I'm referring...) I got so into the music (Lawdog Marks), that I didn't even catch my excellent server bussing my empty cocktail and when I turned my head back to my friends at the table, Presto Chango! A brand new drink was right in front of me! Excellent service!!!

I am withholding a star because I ate dinner before visiting Hellfire, and I want to taste their food! Some nearby patrons were noshing on simple caesar salads, and I could smell the deliciousness from my adjacent table...It says a lot about food quality when a simple salad smells that good! My only caveat is that the bartender was a little pissy when I ordered my last call drink. Last call had already been ordered, and the bartender was busy closing checks, so he didn't notice me for a few minutes. He totally gave me an attitude and said it was past call when I ordered, but I politely said that I was waiting for him to turn around and notice me. He had no problem filling the last call orders of other patrons that were right beside me (who had been likely ordering all night), and he didn't give any of them a hard time. He still filled my order, but he definitely watered it down. Whatever, it was the end of the night, and I understand wanting to close down. I just don't get why it's more acceptable to fill one patron's order over another's, especially when you're still filling orders. We're all human though, and this hiccup is no reason to downgrade Hellfire. I'm totally excited to come back and taste their menu!

How did I not know that South Reno has its very own awesome gas station sandwich shop, and that it has been there for 10 years?? Located inside of the Jackson's gas station on S Meadows Pkwy is a loaf of deliciousness known as The Sandwich Factory...Offering 15 different types of fresh bread (Basil Parm & Pesto Mozz FTW!) baked fresh daily and all the usual sandwich suspects you'd expect (salads, wraps, soup, etc.), Sandwich Factory is a very tasty way to fill that void in your belly. Their ingredients are super fresh and delicious, and always refreshing.

On my first visit, my mind and tastebuds were blown because I had no expectations, and I was completely wowed! I was literally thinking about my sammie the next day, it was that good. Now that I have a few more visits under my belt though, my tastebuds have come back down to earth, and I feel I can give a more grounded review of The Sandwich Factory. I still love the flavors of the sammies, but they do run a little thin, and $11 and change is just too pricey for a thin 8" sammie in my book. I understand that it's locally owned and operated, which I love, and will continue to support as a treat every now and again, but it's too much for me to treat myself to on a regular basis. 

I would still give them 4 stars, if it wasn't for their soup. Given how fresh everything else is, I was disappointed to see that they just microwave their cold soup, rather than having a vat of hot, fresh soup available for consumption. When I tried my nuked broccoli cheddar soup, it was lukewarm and had the consistency of gravy rather than creamy soup...Bummer. That being said, I will totally return to Sandwich Factory and I highly encourage you to give it a taste, too!

PRO TIP: Go on Mondays to get a double-punch on your punch card to earn that free sammie sooner, rather than later!

Eggs...From my head down to my legs...I love the incredible, edible Peg's!  There are many excellent breakfast spots in town these days and while Peg's was one of the first of its kind, I am happy to say that it still is one of the best!  I've never met a dish I didn't like here...The portions are generous and the price point is very affordable.  Love their signature huevos ranchero- golden fried eggs served on a lightly fried corn tortilla topped with delicious ranchero (tomato-chili) sauce accompanied by seasoned pintos, slaw, pico, diced jalapeños and bomb-diggity hash browns!  It's definitely my new favorite.  I don't know how I haven't had it before now...My husband had his go-to dish, the breakfast burrito, which was bursting with scrambled eggs, ham, onions, green chilies and melted cheddar, topped with the aforementioned yummy ranchero sauce.  

I've been to a few different Peg's locations (Sparks, Downtown Reno and now S. Meadows), and the quality of the food and service has always been on point across the board.  The staff seems to be happy working here, and you can taste that in the food.  While there are now several Peg's locations, this is not a chain restaurant!  Peg's has been locally owned and operated by the same family ("Pops" and "Peg" are retired, but their children (and some of their grandchildren) are at the helm these days).  It's great to see a local business like this expand and grow as Peg's has.  Regardless of which location you go to, there is usually a long wait, especially on the weekends.  But the staff here is efficient and friendly, and they are able to turn tables very quickly, without rushing their guests.  The wait is definitely worth it!

India Kabab & Curry is truly one of my favorite restaurants in town!  They were in existence long before the incredible foodie movement that we're enjoying now.  The $7.95 (now $8.95) buffet that they are so well-known for is merely the tip of this flavorful, delicious iceberg.  It's such a great deal and is so much better than the soup/salad/etc deals you can find at corporate restaurants.  

If you're unsure/intimidated by Indian food, the buffet is a great place to start teasing your palate (and learning the names of some of these wonderful dishes!).  However, please don't judge them solely on the quality of the buffet food.  The buffet food is good, but it's just not in the same league as a freshly made, individual order of the same dish.  The tandoori chicken is a prime example of this.  Tandoori ovens are borderline magical in my eyes.  They just give food the most incredible, indescribable flavor...I frequently order the vegetable tandoori.  There are literally 3-4 different flavors in each bite.  Eat slowly and savor the smooth transitions and clean finish.  If you're afraid of heat, don't worry!  Each dish is made to order (mild, medium, hot).  If you've never tried Indian food, start with mild heat and progress your way up the scale.  I grew up on Indian food, so I absolutely love all the rich flavors that warm you from the inside out.  However, I understand how the names and spices can be intimidating to newcomers...Don't let the Ben Stiller scene from "Along Came Polly" prevent you from exploring this wonderful territory!  You can never go wrong with samosas, vegetable pakoras, tikki aloo, malai kofta, aloo chole, or any tandoori dish.  (See what I mean about the intimidating names?)  The tomato-coconut soup (most of the soups are vegetarian) is absolutely to die for!  

They also have some nice dinners for 1 (or 2) at a variety of prices.  This is a nice way to try several dishes by yourself (or with someone special).  Since the dishes are freshly prepared, they are higher quality than what you'll get at the buffet.  It is well worth the extra money and is a more pleasurable dining experience!  While India Kabab & Curry has a full bar, I definitely encourage you to try a lassi!  It's like a yogurt shake/smoothie.  You can order it sweet, salty or mango-flavored.  Definitely go with the mango!  

Service is always pleasant, attentive and professional, though you may have difficulty in communicating when you'd like to modify a dish.  (In my case, I order the vegetarian appetizer platter with double vegetable pakora instead of cheese pakora.  Indian cheese just isn't my thing, but boy, do I love that chickpea batter!)  I have never had an issue when receiving my dish, but sometimes there's a communication barrier when I try to explain what I want.   

If management ever happens to read this, please bring back the ginger ice cream!!  It is simply otherworldly!

We were walking along South street, around 8pm on a weekday night.  We were just looking for a nice pizza and some wine.  When we stopped by La Fourno to check out their menu displayed, we were cordially invited inside by a staff member.

The restaurant was completely empty, but the staff made a couple of jokes about where to sit.  We laughed and took a seat.  Apparently, they have upstairs seating, and some customers dining up there.

What started off as a friendly meal, quickly turned otherwise.  After being seated, our server came up to tell us " I just got shit from the kitchen, and you need to put your order in ASAP.  The kitchen is closing in 15 minutes."

We put in an order for a pizza, a beer and a glass of wine.  We were politely and abiding.

After being getting our drinks, the entire restaurant began it's clean up for the night.  The music was cut off, and it became so noisy with the clatter of cleaning, that I had to struggle to hear the person across from me talking.

Our pizza arrived and it was pretty pathetic.  Basically, frozen vegetables  with a can of tomatoes thrown on top.  The thin crust turned soggy in all of the water from the toppings.  We attempted to enjoy this, while smelling Windex and 409, which was being used to clean the bar behind us.

I politely inquired if the music could be turned back on, since we were eating.  

After that, our server laid on the sarcasm quite thickly.  After dinner, I ordered an espresso martini as an after dinner drink.  (It was one of the worst martini's I think I've ever had, unfortunately).

As we were leaving, our server said to me, "Have a good night, and watch the alcohol.  Don't drink too much."

Uh, what?

Overall, their initial friendliness turned in to unprofessional sarcasm.  Couple that with a rude staff that can't wait 20 minutes for their lone customers in that section to finish a meal, and with unimpressive food and it's just not worth it.

I'd think, since we are in a recession they'd be happy to have us for a meal and be polite in order to get us to return.

Next time frankly, I'll get a frozen pizza next time and a bottle of wine from the store.  The food and the service would be far superior.

I can't say no to a man with tattoos and my experience at Pod was purely orgasmic.

The food at Pod is amazing and reasonably priced, if not underpriced. It is economical bliss.  I expected to pay way more and for appetizers, sushi, drinks and desserts for two. Our bill topped at $84 bucks. Not too bad. Killer ambiance and surprise after surprise, I find myself thinking about Pod time and time again.

Pod is futuristic, offers everything traditional with a twist and is unpretentious. The place is like an outer space playground with ever changing colored lights, bubble ceilings, and white on white interior. The sushi boat is a world of its own and if you fancy anime, the screens are like windows of cartoons.  I saw waitresses carry out birthday desserts with sparklers. It was like Fourth of July. The service is excellent (welcoming, accommodating, quick, and knowledgeable). Everything thumbs up.

The ultra hot weather called for mocktails, one Cucumber and Apple Spritzer and one White Peach and Mint Soda. Both were refreshing and full of fresh fruit. We ordered the special Lobster Ramen appetizer, Tonkatsu Sandwich, and the Rockin Spicy Tuna. The Lobster Ramen was not soupy but had a creamy rich broth-like dressing. The lobster chunks were huge and tender, the vegetable medley offered crunch and the ramen was very fresh and not over cooked. The Tonkatsu Sandwich could easily rival David Chang's pork steamed buns. The Rockin Spicy Tuna was haute sushi. Sprinkled with black sesame seeds and prepared like little works of art, the spicy tuna was like a sushi hors d'oevre. It was topped with popcornlike tempura rock shrimp and microgreens. This all created for a filling meal but without hesitation we ordered dessert.

If Pod's tactic to get people to order dessert was to send in a tattooed dessert man instead of our friendly waitress, then it surely worked. We were set on Chocolate Chocolate Chocolate (chocolate toffee bread pudding, chocolate shot with salted rim, and chocolate tart) but when the tattoo guy told us about the special Chocolate Flan we had to make our dessert choice Chocolate times 4. The tattooed guy was evil in a good way. Death by chocolate all the way at Pod. No worries, you will live to tell the tale of sweet decadence. I could easily devote a whole review to these desserts. Instead, just trust the smile on my face that they were all exquisite. I will add that the Chocolate Flan was light rather than rich and was complimented by an Early Grey Tea coulis and black cherries.

I'd make a two hour trip to Philly from NYC just to indulge at Pod. It was really that good.

For the formal writeup on Pod: http://spamisbetterfried.blogspot.com/2011/03/after-all-these-years-pod-is-still.html

It was a dark and stormy night. With torrential rain battling our car and the streets of Rittenhouse Square, there was no way we were going to make it across town to our reservation at Pod. We passed by Alma de Cuba, brought our car to a halt and went inside.

It was a gorgeous and sexy restaurant and we had no idea we were in for such a treat. From the almond stuffed dates wrapped in bacon and the NY Strip Steak to the lechon plate and Chocolate Cigar on fire dessert we were in awe with the taste and presentation. Little did we even know that Alma de Cuba was also a Stephen Starr restaurant. Score.

I recently went back with a group of friends to Alma de Cuba. From what I observed they were impressed with the drinks and food. Alma de Cuba is great for groups and the service is more than accommodating.

We started off with a trio of ceviche for each couple. I thought it might be a bit much but this tasting is the perfect portion for two people. We chose the Sea Scallop, Yellowtail Kingfish, and Long Island Fluke. With ingredients like pomegranate seeds, yuzu, soy and ginger, along with some heat, each ceviche had a different flavor. The Kingfish was my favorite. I'd gladly eat them all again and would like to try the Lenguado 'Al Fuego' next time. SUPER HOT with habanero!

The waiter described the Lechon Asado as a commitment. Yes it is as it is a hefty plate and enough to share with a whole family. I got it since I remembered it being so good last time. It was but as I was eating it I kind of wish I had went for a fish to be on the lighter side (had to leave room for dessert of course!). The other entrees are quite outstanding, if not better than the Lechon. Rum Cured Duck Breast, Vaca Frita, and Sugarcane Tuna I am looking at you! Have you ever had fish that look like lollipops? Tastes better and looks better than you can imagine. Five star gourmet right there! (A small portion too while you're at it.)

Always leave room for dessert as the pastry chef does not disappoint. I got my rich and decadent chocolate cigar as well as the key lime panna cotta with banana ceviche. Of course, the highlight was when they light the cigar matches on fire. It's all sort of mesmerizing.

Prepare to spend about $40/head at the very least.

I never liked cheesesteaks in Philly before going to Dalessandro's. I tried to like them and each time on my visit to Philly I spit out blech and it was gross, tough, hard meat, dry, and flavorless.

And now all I can do is dream about Dalessandro's juicy, tender, and flavorful sandwiches that hit the spot. Dalessandro's is a neighborhood cheesesteak shop. Apparently all cheesesteaks are judged by area. Well I don't care for Pat's, Geno's, or Jim's. I'd rather go beyond them and into the outskirts/residential areas.

Dalessandro's is not a place for big groups. Dining at Dalessandro's is all counter seating. I sat there with cheesesteaks larger than life in front of me, one of which was a chicken cheesesteak. "Chicken?!" everyone gasps and yells at me when I tell them this. Yes, I am a big fan of chicken cheesesteaks and stand by them. They are good and a new sort of thing. Ask Ishkabibble.

The cheesesteaks can be dolled up with peppers which are in giant jars and plastic containers on the counter. This is great since you can decided how sweet, how spicy, and how you want your sandwich. Start there and then just go for the grease.

When you're a tourist, everything at Reading Terminal has a certain amount of fame. You can walk around discombobulated, lost, and confused at what to eat. You will want to eat EVERYTHING!

The thing I like about The Famous 4th Street Cookie is that if you go early in the morning (10 AM), the cookies are fresh out of the oven, nice and warm. They have that chewy, gooey, sweet taste and really, you don't have to eat it then and there on the spot. I took three to go and chipped away at it over two days. They were excellent through the very last bite.

Cookies are sold at $10 per pound. My three cookies cost about $5 and were worth every dollar. They were richer than Mrs. Fields (we're talking loads of butter here) and less raw than Levain in NYC. I picked chocolate chip with pecans, oatmeal raisin, and peanut butter. I think the lady messed up because my chocolate chip had no pecans in it. It's alright, I will go back! Every cookie had a distinct taste and richness. I can't even say which one was my favorite but the chocolate chip ranked high. 

Famous 4th Street Cookie is a must when in Philly. I stand by their buttery goodness and am amazed that there were no grease stains leaking through the bag. Hmmmm.

Some say a big cocktail or stiff drink will start you right in NOLA. I go straight for the sweets.

Cafe Beignet was on our list and it was a nice destination in the French Quarter before the French Quarter got too crazy. Even at 11 AM there were loads of people in the cafe already. We waited in line for a bit and that gave us time to soak in the vibes of Cafe Beignet and drool over the many options. I thought we were just going to get beignets but then we decided it would be smart to fill our bellies with real food as well. A crawfish omelette with grits and French bread is what we ordered as our first taste of NOLA.

Great choice. The omelette was filled with seasoned crawfish! The grits were buttery and the bread was soft and fluffy. And then the beignets. They were super sized and topped with what looked like a whole box of powdered sugar. Oh my. So good. During our trip to NOLA we actually never made it to Cafe du Monde. I have no other comparison for beignets but that's okay because I am 100% satisfied and happy with Cafe Beignet. Go for it!

Customizable cheesesteak? Grilled onions? Where do you think you are? Burger King? In-N-Out? Starbucks? I told my cousin to not be the annoying tourist. My bad, after reading the reviews and listening to him order, apparently you can have it your way. Just tell the guy what you want. 

I just got a cheesesteak provolone. I'm not too keen on cheesesteaks and wanted to keep it basic. I should have added onions to mine because it was bland. We added salt and pepper to our sandwiches. The meat was chopped up this time (yay!) and not at all greasy (surprisingly). The bread was real good, soft and doughy. I liked the vibe at Jim's. It felt local as opposed to Pat's and Geno's which is like standing in line at a theme park or carnival. 

Jim's sandwiches are far better than Pat's and Geno's but still not what I thought cheesesteaks were gonna be like. As Mari H explains, maybe I just don't 'get it' yet. I also highly doubt my tastebuds are more refined than hers. After all, I am a Steak-umm kinda gal. So with that said, perhaps the city of Philly has more refined tastebuds than me.

And like a cheesesteak whore, I'm on to the next one. Hello Tony Luke!

PS- There is plenty of seating upstairs but they don't let you loiter.

I didn't think a grocery store could be as bad as 2 stars. But yelp was right. AVOID THE FRESH GROCER. It is at best 1 star (solely for existing)

The aisles are disorganized, chaotic, and narrow. You should be given a helmet at the door to fight your way trough the aisles. The selection isn't great for anything-coffee, dairy products, soy milk, eggs, chips, breads, etc. 

Everyone we encountered here appeared to hate life. (The seafood counter guy was just mean.) But the kicker was the employee at checkout named DACIA (yes, I checked my receipt) who attempted twice to tell me to bag my own groceries (I had a baby with me!) and when I refused proceeded to throw our groceries haphazardly into bags. Frozen items were mixed with chips, eggs with apples...no effort was made. All my fruit was bruised when I got home. She should be fired. I will never return here even though it is the closest grocery store to my house.

Way to lose thousands of dollars in purchases, Dacia & Fresh Grocer...We won't be back!

We came in to this gem for the first time during Devour Indy, and we'll definitely be back. The Devour special included an appetizer, four meats, four sides, cornbread, and dessert for two people for $35. We were STUFFED by the end of our meal and had to take dessert to go. 

We got the pretzels and beer cheese as our appetizer which was fairly standard. We chose ham steak, brisket, rib tips, and pulled pork as our meats. The brisket was my favorite because it was so tender, but the rest were great, too. The 7 Pepper Mustard sauce was hot in the best way. It had a kick to it but wasn't too spicy. The side portions seemed small for two people at first, but there was so much food that we didn't even finish. We chose green beans, mac n cheese, fried apples, and potato salad. The potato salad was the best of the sides. 
The meal was delicious, the atmosphere has a great casual, dive bar feel, and the service was excellent, especially for current times. We'll be back!

This was our first time to Ca 'Dario and we had a lovely evening.  The restaurant is charming inside with an Old World feel.  We had Salmon, the Roasted Chicken and a Chicken Pasta at our table and all were delicious.  The Caesar Salad was also very good and the bread, wonderful!
The restaurant is not large so a reservation is recommended.  It was a little noisy once all the tables were filled but the ambiance was enjoyable. The service was good and we never felt rushed.

Good food fast!  Taze sits in the middle of the Central West End on Euclid - a great location.  It's a build your own bowl or pita type of place.  Pick your bowl, pick your protein, pick your sauce and finally pick your toppings.  If you don't like what you get, it's your fault since you made it.

I give them a solid 4-star rating because:

Food- flavorful, fresh, and healthy portions.

Atmosphere- space has been completely remodeled. Nice clean and laid back.  Also, they have a patio.

Location- conveniently located in the CWE.

Service- all of the employees have been very nice  and helpful.

Merchandise - they have a few items you can purchase (spices mainly).

Last... they serve wine and beer! :)

Since my husband and I moved to New Tampa seven years ago we've been to Wolf's Den enough where everybody who works there knows me. 
Yesterday the restaurant was crowded. I saw open booths but not not the people on the side . Often people on the side are waiting for take-out but I backed off when I learned that they're waiting for booths. A waitress told me that I could sit at a communal table. At first I started to head to take a seat but turned to wait for a booth. A waitress thought that I was trying to jump the 

 line, raised her voice and SCOLDED ME. Treated like she never saw me before, like a child, not like the polite person who always says please, thank you and tips well. My husband and I were seated but I was trembling. Angry and  sad I got up and walked out. Once outside i started to cry. I seriously have an issue with someone who takes the liberty to treat me with so little respect.

Who: my husband and I. We're from California, we've never had a Philly cheesesteak. Clearly tourists, no idea where to start. But we knew going to Pat or Gino's was not the answer. 

When: Sunday November 18th, at around 11:50am. Small line of about 4 people in front of us. Moved along perfectly fine. I liked watching everyone customize their cheesesteak. 

Conundrum: how do you choose which place to goto?! Read reviews and try to find the most passionate positive reviews. 

Where do I begin. The location: so much rich history and character, the epicenter of icons: Creed, Kevin Hart and all the hard working citizens of Philly. The staff: fun, full of life, friendly, edgy, great! 

THE CHEESESTEAK: Served Hot, super fresh, loaded, custom made however you like. Gigantic. I'm dying for the provolone cheese, beef, peppers, mayo, lettuce and tomato combo. They come in a half size or small, about 12 inches, and a large size or whole order about 24 inches. My husband and I shared a large. They were able to apply mayo to my half (12") and not to his. I really appreciate that touch. The meat was juicy, perfectly cooked-- tender, not dried up and over fried like a lot of other places do. They use sirloin steak. It's all good. 

Once you order you can eat there at their bar next door that is connected. We ordered slushy's and water.

There is nothing to be afraid of, it is not very sketchy. People are respectful. There weren't any loitering beggars nearby, everyone was there to eat! I would go in the daytime simply just to give the food enough time to digest. Maybe night time is a different story. But truly it's a busy intersection, just a stones throw away from temple university and it's really quite safe. Check out the fresh mural of Kevin hart. 

Bonus: I took my philly friend here and her friends were so happy we went because they all swear by it being the best cheesesteak. 

Private parking lot with tons of spots for Max's. Cash only. About a $8 Lyft for two from 30th street station.

If you have read my review of Datz, and judging by the lack of compliments, you haven't, you will know that I love everything the owners do.  Datz has to be one of my favorite restaurants in Tampa, so that when we found out they were opening up a creole restaurant in a city that doesn't have them, we were thrilled (we is me and my girlfriend - her review will be better than mine).

Anyway, we were in New Orleans earlier in the year, and were anxious to find some creole food or at least creole inspired cuisine somewhere.  Yelp had an event at Roux a couple of months ago where we got to sample a few items, and everything was amazing.  Well, now that the restaurant is complete, we got to try a whole meal.

I loved it.  However, I am taking a star away for a couple of reasons.  One, it is not as good as Datz.  It is cuter than Datz, but the food at Datz is better.  Secondly, I am not sure it is worth the prices they are charging. Those are my only two complaints, so lets get onto the good stuff.

First, the decor.  It's very cute.  Brick facade walls with gas lamps.  Keeps it romantic and looks a lot like a smaller, but higher end restaurant from New Orleans.  Great place for a special occasion, first date, etc.

Second, the service.  Our server, good ole' washisname, was fantastic, especially since we sat down about 15 minutes before close.  We didn't know.  We called to find out what time they were closing at about 9:30, and we were told 11:00 by the hostess.  Once we arrived, sat down and ordered, we find out they close at 10:00.  So, even though we screwed the kitchen and server, they treated us very well - much better than I would have acted if someone did that to me when I waited tables.

Finally, the food.  The menu is a bit intimidating.  Really creole inspired.  Rabbit, alligator, and other weirdness.  I ordered an andouille sausage and alligator pasta.  I didn't care for alligator last time I had it, but I figured mixed with sauce and sausage, maybe I'd like it.  It came out all ground up in an awesome marinara sauce, so that I wasn't sure if I was eating the sausage or the alligator, and it was delicious, mixed up like that.  

We finished with a baked alaska.  They had given us some to try at the yelp event I mentioned, and they were very good.  This one wasn't as good - kind of disappointing actually.  I think it was a raspberry flavor, but I am not positive about that.  Anyway, it was the only one they had that night, or at least, the only one they had left, and we didn't love it.

All in all, it's worth checking out.  The menu is very different, and not something any Tampa or Florida native would expect.  The owners really tried to bring something new and different to the restaurant scene, and for the most part, they did a very good job.  Prices are a bit high, menu is a bit intimidating, but we enjoyed ourselves and are happy they finally opened.

I couldn't disagree more with the 2 star reviews on here so far.  I understand if this isn't your cup o' tea, but the food, service and environment is worth at least 3.5 or 4.

Dear all of you people not giving Datz its due because you don't like something during the soft opening. Please delete your yelp account. IT'S THE SOFT OPENING!!!!  There are supposed to be kinks to work out. We came for brunch. Was service perfect?  No, of course not, but it was fine and it was the SOFT OPENING. Did our food take a really long time to come out?  Yes, but it was the SOFT OPENING. Good lord people, calm your negativity and be a little understanding that the soft opening is meant to be a time while the staff figures things out.   

We have been waiting for Datz to open in st pete forever. It is our favorite American moderately priced restaurant in Tampa and while Dr BBQ was a great start by the Datz folks in St Pete, we wanted the real thing, and we finally got it. 

Came for brunch and we will do so again. We will also come back for lunch and dinner and brinner and linner and cocktails and appetizers. Got the breakfast burrito - tortilla stuffed with pork belly and potatoes and rice and black beans and covered in queso and it was freakin awesome. My favorite breakfast burrito in st pete used to be the El Gordo at Red Mesa Cantina-no longer. I say good day to you, El Gordo. I loved this. My lovely fiancé got their avocado toast and loved hers too. Everyone enjoyed their drinks. I just had coffee but they serve huge mugs of delicious coffee. 

So what went wrong?  Well, we wanted to get something sweet too and had intended to split some pancakes or something, but our meal took so long to come out, that we ran out of time. They also ran out of almond milk for the coffee. Big whoop. And they messed up our friend's biscuit and gravy by leaving on the scallions when she asked they leave it off. No one died. Server forgot a couple of things but nothing that really affected our enjoyment of the meal and also IT WAS THE SOFT OPENING!!!!

Datz is in a great location on the "terrace" level of the James Museum. It's very bright even though because of the placement, it's always shaded. They have a large dog friendly patio that thanks to the shade, stays pretty cool too (for a given Florida definition of cool). 

So, people, calm your inner trollness and rejoice in the fact you have Datz. You never have to drive over a bridge to go to Datz ever again. It is wonderful. It is amazing. It is Datz. Enjoy it. And stop going to soft openings if you can't give them a little more rope. 

Thank you for coming here Datz. Took you freakin long enough!

I really enjoyed District Tavern.  It has the look and feel of what a gastropub should be.  Open and spacious with lots of TVs and seating and good food.

Melissa and I came before the Billy Joel concert, whom we hadn't seen For the Longest Time (see what I did there).  Now, you might think that before such a concert, we should have a bottle of red, or ooooooooo, a bottle of white, but that wasn't the kind of mood we were in that night. No, on another night, You May be Right, but not tonight.  Tonight, me and my Uptown Girl just needed a quick bite, maybe a drink, and we had to run to the arena, where you'd think I would be a Big Shot, but no.  They treat me like I'm The Stranger.

I ordered a simple whiskey and water and a southwest chicken bowl - I don't recall the name and can't really be bothered to look it up right now.  However, it came with quinoa (or rice, but I went healthy) and blackened chicken and it was very good.  Don't recall what Melissa got, but I am fairly certain she enjoyed it too.

This is a great place for a pre-show meal for a couple of reasons.  First, it is within walking distance.  Second, because it is off the beaten path a bit, it was not nearly as busy as the places in Channelside or Fergs Live, or even some of the other pubs and restaurants in the business area of downtown Tampa.  We were surprised how easy it was to get a table.

That said, a number of reviews complained about the service, and while our server was friendly and everything was fine, service was slow.  Normally, I would consider deducting a star for it, but it wasn't so bad that it screwed up our evening.  Still, you should plan on needing some extra time all the same.

And so it goes, and so it goes, and you're the only one who knows.

Had Dinner there last month with the wife. Both of us got ill later. Reading their last health inspection report recently, brought the memory back in nauseating detail.

"What the inspector saw: Eight critical violations identified on July 17, including potentially hazardous foods stored at incorrect temperatures, flies observed around food-prep area, cook observed using same tongs to touch raw salmon and ready-to-eat chicken, cook observed picking up dropped piece of eggplant from the floor with tongs, then using tongs for other food".

Yay! Thank you Little Korea for giving me a little taste of home! I have been longing for some good Korean food for so long and they totally satisfied the craving. The banchan was tasty and they kindly offered some more kim chee without us having to ask. 

The mandoo wasn't quite what I'm used to (the wrapper was different), but it was hot, the filling was good, and the sauce was tasty. The bibimbap was wonderful. I mean really. There is something about getting that bit of cruchy rice at the bottom that reminds me of only good memories. The bulgogi was seasoned well and the bf enjoyed his kalbi. I had enough food left for the next day, which was also a bonus. In my eagerness for bibimbap, I didn't see sundubu on the menu. So we'll definitely have to come back on a cold day in the future. I'd also like to their dukboki (another fav I haven't had in a while). 

It was our fault for not looking at the price of the mochi ice cream. I'm glad they had azuki bean (bf's fav), but 2 pieces should not cost $6 or 7. The box it comes in costs that much and there are usually 6 pieces if I remember correctly. For that price, looks like we'll be going back to the Orange Cough for our ice cream mochi fix from now on in the city... That's honestly not that big of a deal, just want other peeps to be prepared when they see their bill. 

Small criticism: the decor needs a bit of help. The plastic table covers on the side of the restaurant we sat on don't seem to be doing well with the heat and weight of the stone bowls. Additionally, some of the paint is peeling off the walls. Those are easy fixes that don't detract from the food or the service. 

Tips: we don't really care for metal hashi (chopsticks), so they were kind and accommodated with wooden when we asked. They also don't serve pho anymore. Don't be afraid of spice, it's good for the soul.

I've come twice now and am very happy with both experiences! So glad that the eatery that took over from Dis and Dem's old location is so amazing! 

I would 100% recommend the lemongrass chicken tacos. 3 of them are enough for a full meal and $8 certainly will not break the bank! So far, the burgers have also been phenomenal (tried the fharmacy burger and Dr. Seuss - both are $12 and well worth the price, plus each burger comes with fries). Oh boy are their fries totally work the calories also. 

The staff there is so accommodating and kind. They consistently went out of their way both times to make sure the tables were taken care of. Several of my coworkers have been back since and consistently have the best things to say (they are a hard group to impress!). 

Pro-tip: order ahead for pick-up for lunch if you don't have the time to wait.

Review for the happy hour only...
You should go if you like cheap sushi and drinks! They have a great happy hour menu, that is good for a quick bite. The quality of how the sushi is made isn't the best, but you certainly can't be $4 for unagi/avacado roll. Despite how cheap the rolls were, the fish was fresh and brought out in a timely manner. 8 of us headed up there on a Wednesday to take advantage of the pretty much all day happy hour. We weren't disappointed and everyone left feeling full with less than $20 tabs that included drinks. 

The service could be improved a bit and I don't really understand the need for 2x hostesses. There's a small lot next door that is very convenient to park on since Oak St can get a bit full. While I'm not into trendy sushi places (this place certainly qualifies as that), I am into a good cheap bite. I probably won't be back for the regular menu, since it seems a bit overpriced. However, I will certainly be back for the happy hour menu! 

Happy hour: Wed 4pm-12am, Mon-Sat 4-6pm, Mon-Tues 10-11pm, Wed-Thurs 11-12pm, Fri-Sat 12am-1am

This is the best Chinese buffet I've found on the north side!  We go almost every week with the kids.  The food is freshest during typical lunch & dinner times but they're open all afternoon.  The price is reasonable (includes fountain drinks & desserts) and you can order off the menu if you prefer.

Well, I've officially been to this restaurant dozens of times now. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner, the service was almost consistently very good and the food was incredibly delicious and absolutely worth the price. 

My only complaint (and believe me, I wish I didn't have any complaints) is about how awful the manager/owner has made our experience at Stone House, multiple times. Besides the fact we've heard her blatantly yelling at/whining at her staff with her nasty tone in public, our worst experience with her in person actually made us decide to leave the restaurant before we got a table. So, overall, I would like to say I recommend eating at this wonderful restaurant, but also, perhaps you don't need to eat here.

Hot Doggin' It Up!

Florissant is much like any other Suburb town, but some things stand out about this fairly large city in North County Saint Louis.  We have local staples:  Old Town Donuts, Pirrone's Pizza, Fritz's Frozen Custard, Pearl Cafe, etc.  However, there's a new dog in Flo Town, and he might be added to the list of staple, Dog 'n Frys!

I constantly drive by this little place, tucked quietly in a shopping center on the corner of Charbonier and Paul Ave.  I've been meaning to check it out, but the opportunity arose when my dad had some coupons for the place.  I wouldn't miss my chance!
