The setup is pretty simple.  You walk in and order at a the counter, and the rest of the room has seats surrounding the perimeter and picnic style tables in the center.  

DNF covers all areas of the palate, from sweet and savory to hot and spicy.  My dad ordered a Chicago style dog, but I went with a new menu item, The Dude!  It was a beef frank, covered with gravy, bacon, onion straws, and green onions.  My dog might seem out of your element, but as far as I'm concerned, The Dude Abides!

Also, big shout out for the seasoned hand-cut fries!  I was digging those spuds.

That little shopping center has seen many things come and go, but here's hoping DNF can stand the test of time!

You're the man now, dog!

Steve Ewing is well known in St. Louis for fronting The Urge, a StL band that gained national acclaim in the mid-nineties.  We love our Urge!  But Steve isn't just a rock 'n' rolla . . .

I've been to both Steve's Hot Dogs.  The Hill location has been around for quite some time now.  However, the Tower Grove is still a fairly recent addition to the area, and it's just as good as the original.

Both locations seem to follow the same format and have the same specials.  However, The Hill is more of a lunch spot. TG keeps later hours because it is connected to Tick Tock Tavern.  So you can have a few drinks next door and then soak up some of that alcohol with Steve's dogs or mac 'n' cheese bowls.  Either way, you really can't go wrong.

Steve's doesn't make its own dogs, using Nathan's brand as his base for most concoctions.  However, his brats and sausages come from all over, including local area establishments.  Nonetheless, you get a quality dog and dress it up to your liking.

As I mentioned in my Hill review, follow Steve's on social media, specifically Facebook and Instagram.  They post a secret word every day that will give you a dollar off your order.  The word used to be Star Wars themed, but they've branched off in recent years to other cool stuff.  

You need to try Steve's for yourself.  Eat those dogs!

I can't take the peer pressure!

The Shaved Duck has received some pretty high praise from the Yelp community.  Some of my Yeeps have even gone so far to say that this place is the best for BBQ.  However, after my first visit, I can tell you it's the good to the great.

I don't know why it took so long for me to get over there.  Frankly, it's down the street.  However, it did take me some time, but on a weekday afternoon, I finally went to this acclaimed soul food joint.

Right around noon, I was surprised by the lack of patrons.  Only a few tables were taken up.  When the waiter took our drink order, I asked my dreaded question about drink specials, of which they had none.  The Bud was $3.50, and anything craft was five or more.  The drink menu was impressive but pricey for lunch on a Wednesday.  So I declined.

As far as food prices, I wouldn't say Shaved Duck is too expensive.  In fact, the BBQ sandwiches were pretty well on course with other places.  The pulled pork with one side was ten; the brisket with one side was eleven.  I went with the brisket.

I must have been in a que mood last week because I had just been to Bogart's on Monday and had their brisket.  If you're going to serve the que, then be prepared for comparison.  The prices were similar.  The Duck won the side wars (fries and mac n cheese), but as far as the brisket, Bogart's blew them away!

The brisket itself was pretty smokey, almost too smokey for my preference.  Also, I wouldn't say that it was particularly tender.  The sandwich was quality, but when lined up with the big boys, it just didn't bring it home.

Overall, the meal was very good.  Not overly expensive and the sides were pretty tasty.  However, if I'm going to pay ten plus for que, I'm going elsewhere in The Lou.

Valhalla!

I don't usually get all worked up over a chain coming into town, but how many chains promise 80 different craft beers on tap?

My first experience at a Fying Saucer was in Little Rock, Arkansas.  My friend had recently moved there, and he insisted that we go to this draught emporium.  I was smitten with this place right away.  When I started hearing murmurs of a location coming to Saint Louis, right down the street from Baseball Heaven, I just about flipped my wig!

After a pint at iTap, we were still in the mood for some craft beer, so we wandered down to Flying Saucer.  And we picked a good night!  All day Monday most draft beer is three dollars.  They have a markings system on the beer menu to help understand what's eligilble for three dollars, what's not, and what's in bottles.

Our bartender was awesome!  After continually poor service at iTap, it was nice to have someone patient enough to walk us through the specials and the menu.  I could tell that she was still trying to figure everything out, since they just opened last week.  However, she was attentive and super helpful.

And the samples!  The bartender poured us several small samplings, almost to the point where we felt bad for the amount of tasters we had on the counter.  However, she explained that FS wants their patrons to enjoy their selections and that allowing for samples insures that there will be less "comped" pints in the process.  And it helped us choose our pints wisely.  

Flying Saucer has embraced local talent.  Schlafly, Civil Life, Perennial, 4 Hands, Charleville, O'Fallon, and 2nd Shift all have taps, some multiple, at FS.  However, if you're looking for Bud and Bud Light, you might need to go elsewhere.  Fying Saucer is not your scene, man.

I'm excited that the Fying Saucer has landed in the StL.  More revenue downtown.  Another great place to hang before and after Cardinal victories!

A Great Addition to the Craft Beer Scene!

Over the past five years, Saint Louis has experienced a flourish of local breweries and establishments dedicated to craft beer.  As you can imagine, I already have my preferred tap houses around town, but Brew Hub Taproom just made that list!

Located in front of the Hampton Inn on Oakland Avenue, BHT is unique to the scene because it carries beer outside of our distribution range.  The majority of the tap wall was foreign to me, much of the beer coming from places like Florida and even Korea.  They also brew their own beer!  Fortunately, you can grab a flight of four and try as much of the wall as possible.

Their food menu is quite impressive.  I try to be mostly plant-based in my diet, and they had several meatless options.  Last night I tried a tofu kabob and spicy cauliflower.  The tofu was pretty good, but the cauliflower was especially great.  My friends and I were all snacking on it pretty happily.  They have tacos, kabobs, sandwiches, and other assorted pup fare.

I've been in twice since they opened, but the service was incredible both times.  Sarah, our bartender, was very knowledgeable of the tap wall and the menu, and was very attentive to our questions about the beers. 

I will definitely come back to Brew Hub Taproom.  The unique beer, extensive menu, and great service will not disappoint you.

Small portions with big flavor!

At first glance, you may be curious why the tacos at Taco Circus are kind of small.  However, if you look at the prices, it all starts to make sense.

Mikey Carrasco is a fascinating individual.  If you ever have the chance to meet him, take a minute to chat with him.  You will need it!  A former employee of the Bailey people, Mikey, along with business partner Christian Ethridge, has set out on his own and exudes passion for his new project.  His determination and charisma made me want to try Taco Circus.

It didn't disappoint.  The tacos range from $1.49-$1.99.  You choose your shell (flour, corn, hard) and your protein (beef, chicken, pork, steak).  They also have vegetarian and breakfast options.  I tried beef, chicken, and pork.

Initially, I was a little thrown by the portion, but considering tacos at Mission are three plus dollars, I could technically get more if I doubled my portion.  Three tacos seemed like just enough to satisfy, but I could see me ordering four or five tacos next visit.

You've persuaded me, Mr. Carrasco.  I am definitely a fan of Taco Circus.  Come support your local taco hut.  They've got something special going on in Bevo Mill!

Dam!  I wish you were my burger.

As much as I eat out at local restaurants, my experience with burgers has been pretty hit or miss.  Don't get me wrong.  I love a good burger, but it's not the first thing that I think about when dining out.  However, if you're looking for a damn fine burger, then The Dam might be your place.

The Dam lies on a little strip of Morganford that most people would probably be unaware of existing.  You won't find a strip mall with a Little Caesar and a Target, next to a McDonald's.  What you will find is locally owned business, restaurants, and pubs.

And if you're looking for a pub, The Dam just happens to be next to one.  They even take your orders next door!  If you're not looking for a pint, the place does have limited seating, or you can take it to go.

Cheap is not a word that I would use to describe this joint.  In fact, you will probably spend around ten dollars for burger, fries, and maybe more with a drink.  You can build your own burger, with some toppings extra, or you can try one of their signature concoctions.  I've done both.

I tried The Animal, a triple cheeseburger with jalapenos, grilled onions, bacon, and BBQ sauce.  This baby was smoking!  Literally.  I struggled to eat this burgers because I didn't give it time to cool.

It was a good burger, but my second trip was more to my liking.  I just ordered a double with cheese, mayo, and onions.  Simplicity worked better for me, and I would definitely order a burger that way again.

As for the service, expect some surliness at The Dam.  The owner was waiting on us, and she had no problem saying whatever she felt like, which doesn't bother me, but if you're a blessed soul that can't handle a little language and needs to be coddled, then you should probably eat your burgers at home.

The Dam has me sold.  I look forward to my next damn burger!

Can a cupcake be savory?

Or perhaps the question is whether or not a cupcake should be savory.  Well, I can tell you, my Yeeps, that a cupcake most certainly can!  And this cupcake resides at The Sweet Divine.

We were doing laundry at Soulard Soap.  Normally, we drop off our loads and find something to eat and/or drink.  The laundromat owner suggested Sweet Divine across the street, having opened since our last trip to the mat.  Cupcakes for lunch?  That's crazy, right?  More like crazy sexy cool!

The Sweet Divine is a simple shop, nothing that really stands out about it.  However, the flavors are unique.  Single cupcakes start at three dollars, similar to the Cup in the CWE.  However, four cupcakes cost ten dollars.  We wanted to get a sample, so we went with Red Velvet, Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough, Banana Cream Pie, and the Drunken Pig!

They were all solid efforts, but nothing compared to the Drunken Pig!  Here's the wesbites description:  Newcastle Beer & sharp cheddar cheese cupcake, sharp cheddar cream cheese frosting, topped with BACON!!  Frankly, it sounds gross.  I love all these elements separately, but together?  

Unless you're a vegetarian, this cupcake is absolutely perfect.  It was more like breakfast than a cupcake.  The Drunken Pig gives off a muffin vibe, but it's still semi-sweet.  And the texture was still very cupcake-like, lacking the graininess of a muffin.  What struck me most was how the Newcastle didn't make it bitter.  I don't know how else to describe it.  However, I wanted another one almost instantaneously!

I will be coming back later this week.  I'm really impressed.

Slow service, dirty tables everywhere, long wait on the food (which is cold), and just boring! First star is for having a bar and the second was for the 20 plus tv's in plain sight.. The second star was lost because "Chef" came out to top off his Coors Light draft after my wife and friends waited over 30mins for 3 sandwiches. Never again!

I've been to Pho Long, Kim Ngan, and Pho Grand, and this is by far my favorite pho restaurant in St. Louis.  Walking in, you see a dingy, tiny restaurant, but that, in my opinion, is the sign of amazing pho.  I've had the Pho Tai, Pho Tai Chin, Bun Bo Hue, and Hu Tieu. I've have no complaints about any of them.  All the dishes have a home-y taste to them that I can't quite put into words.  Portions may be on the smaller size, but its is cheaper than some of the other Pho restaurants in the area.  
Service is minimal, but in my opinion, you pay for the food.

UPDATED AT BOTTOM.

seemed pretty disorganized right off the bat. we were there to celebrate a birthday and had reservations made earlier in the week for 20 people. the hostess seemed to have no record of the reservation. this ended up fine, they split us into 2 tables of 10 that were across from each other in the picnic table area when you first walk in. 

we had two servers assigned to our party, though I think our table only saw the one, who was super enthusiastic and spoke loudly, in your ear. thanks. for that. 

taking our first drink order and food order went fine. but took forever for our drinks to actually arrive, and I want to say she was only 80% accurate with what she brought out and some of the pints were 1/3 foam - this might be the fault of the bartender, but don't bring that shit out to the table. or take $2 off each pint for excessive foam. 

future drink orders took 20+ minutes to come out. and our food took forever to come out too. I realize that 10 people at each table may be a lot, but get organized. it shouldn't take 15 minutes to get everyone at one table their food. 

after the food was dropped, i think we were kind of forgotten about. to the point where I was individually buying beers from the bar, because the server never came back. 

All in all: food was ok, and beers were too. service was terrible, and the staff seemed super disorganized. the place wasn't even that busy, there were so many empty tables throughout the night. 



UPDATE: Owner leaves me a message here, publicly, on a Thursday, wanting to hear about my experience and resolve. I respond back via email as requested and hear nothing for 2 days. I hear from the assistant wanting to schedule a call. I give availability. I wait 3 days and no response. What a waste. Posting pictures of the exchange.

Don't try and save face and then make virtually no attempt to follow through.

I came here when I was visiting Santa Barbara a couple of months ago. I was excited to try it because it was highly recommended by a friend.

I left feeling disappointed. The food itself is really good and I'd give it 5 stars. However, the portions were tiny and I had to order more food to fill up. By the end of the meal, I spent over $30 - this included a juice, bell pepper and avocado toast. I ordered the "large" bell pepper and after they served it, I had to double check that it was in fact the large size because it was so small. Makes me wonder how big the "regular" size is?

The worst part was the service - extremely rude. I called in advance to ask what would be the latest time I can come in, keeping in mind that they close at 5, and they said 4:30. So, that's when I came. The person taking the order was nice, but new, so when I asked a question about the food, she'd ask the manager who was a young girl sitting on a couch with a guy and who couldn't crack a smile if you paid her! In fact, she seemed annoyed. After I ate the pepper (which was really good, to be fair), and still being hungry, I went back to the front and asked if I could order avocado toast. It was 10 min till 5. They said yes and I assumed I could eat it there. They brought it out to me in a to-go container and said that I wanted to eat it there, after which they reminded me that they close at 5. Ummm, that's why I made sure to call ahead of time and asked if I could add this second thing to my order?? I felt extremely rushed, didn't enjoy the toast at all because I was stuffing it down while they picked up my napkins and silverware and kept poking their head in the room where I was sitting! I have never felt so unwelcome anywhere!!!

When I told the manager on my way out, she was extremely rude and wouldn't even acknowledge anything they did wrong. Wow, that left a really bad taste in my mouth. Acknowledgment and a sincere apology could have gone a long way!

In my opinion, Bo Fung is probably the best Chinese food in the city. They have great pot stickers, fried rice, etc. Their lo mein is probably the best I have ever had at a Chinese restaurant. The place kind of looks like a hole-in-the-wall from the outside, so I probably would have never tried their food if one of my friends hadn't highly recommended them.

After hearing rumors and seeing pictures of a cannoli donut we had to go on the hunt. We found the bakery sitting on a corner tucked away in a neighborhood. After walking in and smelling the fresh donuts we new we were in for a treat. The place is small but their food packs a big punch. They specialize in donuts and pastries and they are the creator of the famous cannoli donut. 

We ordered a lobster tail and two of the cannoli donuts. First we tried the lobster tail, the shell was nice and flakey, and the custard filling was very tasty and creamy. Next for the big anticipation we dove into the cannoli donut. The donut was soft and fresh and the cannoli filling was silky and had fantastic flavor. Wow! This just might be my favorite thing ever! Yes if you are a fan of cannoli's you just might fall in love with this creation.

While walking around the 9th street Italian market we had to take a small detour a couple of blocks and stop in and try their award winning pastries. Inside, the place is small, but they pack a big punch with a huge assortment of pastries, cakes, cannoli and so much more. 

We opted to try their Sfogliatella (lobster tail) and a cannoli. The lobster tail was nice and crispy, great flavor and a nice flavorful custard filling. The cannoli was outstanding! The shell was fresh and crisp, the filling was so light and airy not overly sweet, just perfect! If these two options were great I can just imagine how exceptional all the other offerings will be.

Okay. I'm starting out with apologies. We should have never eaten here. This review is our fault...Driving up we could tell it's not the kind of place we were looking for, but the reviews, and the press about this place were so good. I mean, 4.5 stars! Owner has studied with a pit master! How could we go wrong? 

Well, I'll tell you how we went wrong. This place is a BBQ hipster tragedy. In an upscale strip mall, trendily decorated, $15 a plate and filled with people that may not (saying may here, not trying to be offensive) have eaten awesome BBQ before. Drinks located in the front of the line you wait in and before you pay.....If you hadn't been there before, you would have never known to get yourself some libations. In a busy place like this, that often has lines (for some reason) that's just straight up, a goofy idea.  Like much of this place.....Trendy and in my opinion, not hitting the BBQ mark. We had tri-tip and pulled pork which was dry and flavor-less. Not an ounce of smokey goodness, moist meat or delicious-ness to be found on either of our plates in the meat department. Sides were ok, just above chain grade to me, with the exception of the potato salad, which was OUTSTANDING. 

People who like this place might just be afraid to go into the places that serve the best BBQ in the world. Which to me is moist, flavorful, fall apart in your mouth meat, smoked to perfection that leaves you wondering where you are after you've taken a bite. It's the kind of food that transcends the moment and makes you question if you REALLY are eating something THIS good. If that's the experience you are looking for, and you've had awesome BBQ before, this is not the place for you. If you like to feel the smoker before you get there, sense the BBQ magic in the air, and want an authentic BBQ experience with a sweaty guy putting his heart and soul into the food he's about to serve you, this is not the place for you. 

So, this review is definitely not SugarHouse's fault. It's our fault...It's not a bad place. We never should have set foot in this place, and if you are looking for what we look for, maybe you shouldn't either. If you happen to be in Nashville TN, head on over to some of the best BBQ in your life, Papa Turney's. You'll dream of being back there eating their food instead of writing a review on a joint that definitely has it's place in the hearts of others, but just not in yours.

Of all the places we've dropped a lot of cash for a swanky dinner, this was one of my favorites.  Definitely enjoyed this more than Stella or Commander's.  I've been here twice now, once for lunch and once for an over-the-top, wildly decadent anniversary dinner.

My first visit was my birthday lunch. At lunchtime, they feature dishes of long-gone New Orleans classic restaurants. My birthday this year happened to fall on a Wednesday,which is the day they do oyster spaghetti bordelaise. This was outstanding. We also split a salad which was ok but overpriced. The white chocolate bread pudding with apricots and pistachios was unique, beautiful and delicious. I also had some cucumber-St. Germain cocktail that was quite nice.

Last night, we visited again. Since it was our anniversary, I started out with a $16 glass of cava.  Our team of servers really were a highlight of the meal. They were informative about the food, gave great suggestions (even UNDER-SELLING us a few times) and gave us a history lesson to boot. We started out with the solo meat board (plenty for two if you're doing other courses). The pate was my favorite, oh and all those pickled vegetables. Fantastic. Second course was espresso-crusted venison carpaccio and sweetbreads with an Herbsaint reduction.  If we weren't already stuffed, I had a lamb shank with squash, sage and pistachios and the husband has a beautiful veal chop with bone marrow sauce.  I was quite full at that point when they brought us an anniversary treat (pate choux filled with ice cream, chocolate drizzle), plus my husband wanted the chocolate souffle. The souffle was really rich but wonderful (way better than the one we had at Le Foret). Finally, they brought over a little jewelry box that had several drawers you could open to reveal little sweet treats. Adorable. The only thing I didn't like was a house-made ratafia. Way too sweet for me.

It was really a lovely evening and although I may not ever be hungry again, I'd definitely be into going back for more!

Delicious beers! Crazy beers! Tired Hands is the place to get them. They brew some solid traditional styles that I really enjoy like the saisons, English mild, maibock, and IPAs. But then they have the super modern trending styles such as milkshake IPAs and super tropical fruity hopped double IPAs. The ones with crazy names. Space Food Cotton Candy Pina Colada Space Cookie Double Milkshake IPA. It said that on the side of my can.

They really do have some awesome tasting beers. And their can art is psychedelic and otherworldly. They regularly have can releases which they announce on Instagram and if you want to grab some fantastic beers and take them home, follow them there for current release dates. This is actually what brought me here for the first time. I was new to Philly and looking up local breweries, checking their Instagram pages, and following them. After a couple months of seeing announcements for can releases of tasty sounding beers, I decided I had to make the trek. I drove up after work and picked up a few 4 packs of tall cans from the line outside at the garage door on the side of the brewery. Then I headed inside to grab some food for dinner. 

They have a nice selection of tacos and I chose carnitas. I eat this taco everywhere that I ever eat tacos at. The cost is $12 for two tacos which does seem high but they put a lot of meat into those two tacos. And the carnitas was really good. My only lament is that the tortillas did not appear to be toasted at all and that is definitely a letdown.

I did of course drink a few beers. I'm always happy when a brewery serves half pours, ranging from 6 - 8 oz, and the Fermentaria does just that. I'm not a big fan of the small size that comes in a flight because I find it's usually not big enough to really enjoy the beer. The half pour is big enough to allow that while still being small enough to allow me to drink a few without getting drunk.

I will definitely return. I will absolutely drink more beer. And eat more tacos.

I'm not even kidding when I say that the bacon mac and cheese is one of the top 10 best things I've ever eaten. Seriously amazing. I can't even handle how good it is-- I had to come back a second time for more, even though I was only in Nashville 4 days.

The pimento cheese, fried green tomato and bacon (!!) sandwich is NOT to be missed. Simply amazing. I wonder if I can recreate it somehow at home...

If you don't get the fried pickles, you're crazy. And the beer selection is to die for. A Beer Named Sue, Straight to Ale Monkeynaut, Turtle Anarchy... were all fantastic. 

I won't even mention the dry chicken BBQ sandwich, bc the other things outweighed the dry sandwich. Actually, I give this place 7 stars, but I'll take off 2 for the dry sandwich. 

Don't miss this place if you're in Nashville.

Overrated at this point big-time...... 
Waitresses act like you are bothering them at any requests..... 
Burgers are way to greasy and the bottom of bun always falls apart.....
All fried foods are over breaded and fried to long......
They charge for ALL soda refills. 
They have done nothing, zero, zilch to upgrade the food, kitchen, atmosphere in years and its really just caught up with them in a very bad way. So, so sad to see this huge decline in a restaurant I used to enjoy. They don't even have a website, not sure anyone working there could utilize or run it anyway honestly. 
There are 5 WAY better burgers/service within 2 miles-Harvey's, Sunset Grille, Burger Monger, The Avenue, and Engine #9.

Nice little bakery.  Stopped-in and chose some items.  All were good (cookies, cupcakes)

Little concerned that the responses from the owner to negative reviews were nasty, and that they couldn't have cockroaches because they get exterminated weekly.  Yuck.  Maybe this is a norm for bakeries at least in the area?

The greatest bar in America.  Simple as that.

ToC was probably the first bar I visited after I turned 21.  It was awesome then.  It's continues to be awesome today.

Why?  Because it's casual, unpretentious, and -- most of all -- SO MUCH FUN.

ToC is practically an amusement park, with something for everyone.  The main level has a piano bar with some of the best tunes in town.  The bartenders are sweethearts, the drinks are cheap, and there is *never* a cover.  Want to sing showtunes all night with a bunch of drunk strangers?  I can't think of anywhere else to do it.

The bottom level is Terra, their in-house restaurant.  It already has its own listing on Yelp (http://www.yelp.com/biz/terra-philadelphia), so I won't go into the details here.  Needless to say, Chef Eric's food is superlative, and the staff (especially bartender Tony!) are the coolest guys in the 215.

The top level is the nightclub (its latest moniker: the Ascend Lounge).  On a Wednesday night, I played a naughty version of Family Feud with a bunch of friends.  On a Friday night, I danced 'til close.  The space is small, but the mirrored walls make it feel spacious.  The music and deejays are my favorite -- mostly pop tunes but with an excellent beat.  The bartenders keep the complimentary shots flowing.  It's just heaven.

ToC is my desert-island bar.  If I could just have one bar to take with me, please let it be ToC.  Pretty please?

I can't think of a single place in Philly that I was more eager to try than Federal Donuts.

Don't believe me?  When one of the other customers immediately pegged me as a non-regular and asked where I was from and what I was doing there, I told her that I had just flown 3000 miles for a FedNuts donut.  And she knew I wasn't entirely joking.

FedNuts may be a little hole-in-the-wall in a far-flung corner of town, but it's worth visiting no matter how far you have to travel to get there.  

Why?  Because these are THE MOST DELICIOUS DONUTS IN THE ENTIRE UNITED STATES.

Hyperbole much?  I don't think so.

I tasted the Indian cinnamon, Apollonia spice, and vanilla lavender donuts.  Each one had a texture and flavor that was no less than sublime.  Unlike your run-of-the-mill yeasty ("doughy") donuts, these are cake-based donuts, which are much fluffier and more delicate.  They were doused in exotic combinations of sweet and savory spices that were unlike anything I've ever had before.

Are donuts not enough?  Let me also add the FedNuts serves up THE MOST DELICIOUS FRIED CHICKEN IN THE ENTIRE UNITED STATES.

Still no hyperbole here, by the way.

To turn donuts into a meal, I was able to enjoy them with a sampler plate of their specialty fried chicken: two piece of Harissa spice fried chicken, and two pieces of chile/garlic-glazed fried chicken.  They were cooked exquisitely, with a perfectly crisped outside, a juicy interior, lots of punchy flavor, and not a speck of unwanted grease.  The homemade pickles were an excellent complement.

Have I convinced you to come here yet?  

No?  

Well, here's another motivation: I personally guarantee that Blake F. will give you a hug when you enter.  If that doesn't make you want to visit FedNuts, I don't know what will.

Few places make me happier than the PMA does.

Is it the biggest art museum around?  Well no -- the Met is bigger.

Is it the most accessible?  Not really.  The wings with medieval and Renaissance art are baffling to me most of the time.

But -- is it my favorite art museum in the world?  YES.

I have so many wonderful memories here.

I started coming to the PMA when I moved to Philly to go to school, at the not-so-ripe age of 18.  Whenever life would stress me out, I'd take a weekend afternoon and come to the PMA to wander through the galleries and forget about the outside world.  I had a museum membership at the time, so I never worried about whether I could afford to go as often as I would like.  The highlight of my day would be racing up the Rocky steps, taking in the breathtaking view of the Philly skyline, wandering in to receive my little admission pin, and enjoying the spectacle of the massive statue of Artemis welcoming me into my home away from home.

I don't care how touristy they are -- the Rocky steps are amazing and worth the kitsch.

There's just so much to wander through.  You have ancient art... Renaissance art... contemporary art... Western art... Eastern art... permanent exhibitions... rotating exhibitions... in a sprawling and gorgeous space.   Each of the wings had little hidden rooms, which were easy to miss if you weren't in the know.  Ever wanted to know what it was like to live in a Baroque French parlor?  The PMA provides.  Ever wanted to see Monet's Japanese Footbridge in the flesh?  The PMA has that too.

--- Flash forward 10 years ---

I no longer live within walking distance of the PMA, so I make a point of revisiting it every time I come to town.  

Some things have changed.  The front-door security seems to have gotten stricter, for example.  Paradoxically, they've gotten laxer when it comes to photography inside the museum.  They used to forbid it, but I suppose they've taken a "if you can't beat 'em, join 'em" attitude in this era of iPhone cameras. 

(Absolutely no flash, of course.)

The gorgeous interior and serene vibe of the place haven't changed a bit, however.

The highlight of my most recent visit was the special exhibit of Zoe Strauss photography.   Quite a powerful collection of everyman photos that the artist plastered onto billboards all over the tri-state area.  This exhibit is definitely worth seeing if you have an opportunity.  I'm usually not big into souvenirs, but I ultimately succumbed to my temptation to take a a postcard home with me.

Few cities in this hemisphere have as much cultural richness as Philly.  And the PMA is the proverbial crème de la crème.   It doesn't manner whether you're a local or a tourist -- the PMA is not  to be missed.  Get up off the couch and GO!

Certain people have informed me that I eat out too much -- and those haters are probably right.

But you know what I do very rarely?  Dine.

Let's face it: dining can be pricey and requires a bit more gussying up than I'm used to.  But it's worth it, because an evening of fine dining can be life-changing -- an adventure for all the senses and an experience to remember for years afterward.

That's what my evening at Sycamore was like.  Fine dining perfection.

Five friends and I congregated at Sycamore on a blisteringly cold and desolate Sunday night.  On the fringes of Philly in the suburb of Lansdowne, Sycamore is an oasis, with a warm, cozy, and inviting vibe.  It's a BYO, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that several of my dinner companions had brought wine.

After we were seated, my partners-in-dine reminded me that we wouldn't need menus.  It turns out Sunday night is the night of Chef Sam's prix-fixe tasting menu -- and that's what everyone at the table was having.   My eyes lit up.

The tasting is much more exciting than a preset list courses.  Instead, it's carte blanche for Chef Sam and his crew to prepare for us whatever they were in the mood for -- and all of us could receive something different and share with everyone else.  Had I died and gone to heaven?

The breadth and depth of Chef Sam's menu were on full display that night.  I have absolutely no idea how many different dishes were brought out for the six of us.  Here's a (totally abridged) list of what I tasted:

1) Smoked trout amuse bouche
2) Artisanal cheese, fruit, and preserves plate
3) Charcuterie plate
4) Radicchio and beet salad
5) Cream of rutabaga soup
6) Seared black bass
7) Onion crepe with porcini mushroom béchamel
8) Rib-eye steak
9) Wild mushrooms on toast with a fried egg 
10) Seared scallops with onion fritter
11) Pork loin with sauerkraut
12) Banana and dulce de leche tart
13) Bread pudding
14) Rum butterscotch budino

There's no point in trying to describe it all.  I'd have to write a novel.  Simply put: absolutely everything -- from the amuse bouche to the appetizers to the entrees to the desserts -- was heaven.  Somehow each dish that was brought out managed to out-do the previous one.  I have no idea how the staff of Sycamore pulls off miracles like these in the kitchen.  Even that servers were incredibly gracious, introducing every dish to all of us, whisking the empty ones away, and ensuring that the vegetarians in our group were properly taken care of. 
 
After nearly 4 hours of wining, dining, and chatting, our entire group found itself wonderfully tipsy, full, and jovial.  In other words -- in a state of total bliss.

Sunday night at Sycamore was one of the most memorable gastronomic experiences of my life.  Sycamore is a Philly gem that deserves all of the accolades that it receives on Yelp and elsewhere.  Next time I'm in town, the first thing I'm doing is making reservations in order to eat -- I mean "dine" -- here again.

The Habit makes one of my favorite burgers so I knew I would be happy with a stop here to relieve my nighttime hunger pangs. 

This location is actually a walk-up window.  There is no interior seating but there is patio seating both out front along State Street and also to the rear. I ordered a double char burger with cheese and a Coke. You're handed a pager to let you know when to come to the pickup window.

The Habit is consistently delicious no matter what location I visit. Here was no exception.

The downside to this location? No restrooms.

Absolutely loved the wine tasting experience here and walked out with two bottles.

We came in on a Monday afternoon - a slow time I'm sure - and were the only customers during our tasting time. I wish I knew the name of the woman who poured because she deserved a star of her own. The best wine tasting experiences happen when the wine is great and the person serving is personable and makes it all the more enjoyable. Such was the case here. Generous pours and insight into each wine were provided. This was a person who genuinely liked the wine. She was attentive to us yet knew when to give us space to just relax and enjoy the wine. And at the end of our tasting, when asked about recommendations for a place to grab a bite to eat, she took the time to handwrite a list of nearby eateries and what dishes she thought were best at each location. I loved this woman.

When we arrived we were given a list of 5 wines for our tasting. The space is like a garage that someone set up a bar in; comfortable but unassuming. I liked all of the wines we tried but the Pinot Noir and Merlot were standouts. I am not much of a white wine drinker but even their 2016 Chardonnay was enjoyable. I was enamored with the Petite Syrah as well. 

I'm not sure if this is their usual offer but by buying two bottles of wine we got one of our tastings free.

Great wine. Great space. Great hostess. Oreana nailed every aspect of a wonderful wine tasting experience.

Finally a place that is hip, alternative and chill.  A hangout/restaurant/bar/art gallery like The Bricks in Tampa is long over due.  And the fact that it is vegan/vegetarian friendly just takes this place over the edge!

 I discovered The Bricks just walking by one day while out in Ybor.  It was packed.  We stopped in to check it out and were sold on the menu.  Come on?  A Peanut Butter Bar.  Need I say more?  

Tonight was date night, and I'm happy to say, both my husband and I have agreed these place is a keeper!  

For $24 plus tip, we got an excellent meal that was healthy, light, yet still very filling.  

For our appetizer we had chips & salsa.  No frills, but tasty chips and a solid salsa.  

My husband had the portabelly which he enjoyed.  I had the goodness on mixed grain bread.  It was delicious.  Also a shout out to the amazing house dressing on the salad.  Yum.

For dessert we had the "brickin' nuggets" off the breakfast menu.  WOW! I would have licked the plate if I wasn't in public.  

If you are looking for a place with great food, a chill atmosphere, and just the coolest place I've been in Tampa in awhile... then head to The Bricks in Ybor City.  

Happy Vegan Dining!

Eat well,
Carolyn

My wife and I wanted to explore someplace new and we had driven by this place many times.  Time to stop in.  not knowing how busy it would be we used OpenTable to make a reservation but when I arrived we saw that we did not need it.

We were quickly greeting by the hostess.  You walk past the bar to the dining area.  There are 'taller' tables around the bar.  She passed us off to our waitress who handed us our menus, dropped off water, and gave us a drink menu.  I noticed the hand written menu on the wall and wanted something off it it.

When she came back (Jenny) she took our drink order.  My wife ordered wine and I was torn between two drinks. I asked her for a recommendation and since she didn't try either before she went and talked to the bar tender.   I ended up with the one with Larceny Bourbon.  Yum.  (They were out of the Jalapeños used for the kicker).

My wife ordered the vegetarian lasagna and I the meat loaf.  They came out quickly.  We could have ordered one and split them for the portions were large!  I managed to finish my meatloaf, mashed potatoes, and green beans.  My wife ended up taking 1/2 of hers home (which my daughter quickly consumed!).  

The waitress and bartender were very personable.  Jenny kept our water full, brought us spare napkins, and visited just the right amount.  She is an asset to that place.  The bartender as well (though I don't recall her name).  

We enjoyed it and plan to head back another night.  There was no live music and no piped in obnoxious music.  Nice date night all around.

Again they handled our large group from work with ease.  We had a party of 22 and the ordering went smooth.  Funny how a place takes orders 'in order' but then sends out the food doing what someone coined 'auctioning off the food' ("Ok, who had the whatis burger with blue cheese?")  Guess they take it in order so not to miss anyone.

A few minor kitchen errors but no show stoppers and no where near enough to make us NOT to choose this for a event.

I also like to come here for movies and beer.  They have some great movie nights and support charities at the same time.  

I always leave with a 6 pack of something... even when there for a work lunch thing.

My wife and I stopped by because (a) we had never been here before and (b) it was close to where we were while out on errands.

We got there at a slightly off (early) dinner hour so it wasn't too crowded or loud.   We were quickly greeted and then seated.  The seating is a bit cozy and not a lot of room to walk around (for staff!).  We were at a table and not at a booth with a tap.

Our waitress, Ashley, greeted us and gave us the run down of the place.  We learned about all the beers, wines, and specials.  She didn't seem to be in a hurry to move on to another customer but instead making sure we had no questions before we were left to decide what to order.

I had a beer and my wife had wine.  I ordered the Rise and Shine burger while she got a Cali Chicken wrap.  The food didn't take a long time to come out and our waitress had visited just enough to make sure our drinks were never too empty.  She was always willing to chat about the place and anything else we had on our mind.  

The burgers, though small, were wonderful.  I found out that you could actually order more patties (each is 3.5 oz) with any burger.  Good thing I didn't do it then... don't know where it would have led!  My wife's wrap was also very good.  Neither of us left anything on the plate.

We had no room for dessert but will be back!

I'm not one to give out 5 stars easily, but I think Lemongrass is worth it for several reasons..

1) First and foremost; the food is excellent. I have now ordered most items on the menu, and I have YET to be disappointed with anything in any way. The food is fresh, tasty, the cold stuff is cold, and the hot stuff is hot. I've traveled extensively throughout Asia, and I'm a fan of MOST regional cuisines; Vietnamese is my favorite and this place does it right. I suggest going frequently and trying everything, but the grilled meats roll (pork) is amazing as is the Deconstructed Bahn Xeo (which was on the specials menu this week)

2) Easy to get into. I've never made a reservation, and because of the hidden gem factor, I've been seated immediately every time. I want this place to stay forever and the owners to benefit from the success, but part of me selfishly wants this gem to remain hidden :) It won't be hidden for long; its that good

3) Service is awesome, friendly, perfect. No complaints ever. You feel like family when dining with them.

4) Cost: forgive me for saying this, but its inexpensive, its a BYOB, and I'd gladly pay 2X what they charge for their food (don't get any ideas, haha) My wife and I can leave satisfied for $50 bucks.

5) NOT overwhelming. The menu is adequate, and they change up the specials, but there aren't so many choices that I'm left confused or with remorse. Its a simple, concise, and appealing menu.

I absolutely love this place - it's in my top 3 for the entire Philadelphia area, and I'd cross the bridge for it if I lived in Philly.

The slow roast in green curry is nothing short of delightful. There is nothing to compare this dish to. The various herbs and spices compiled together to bring a great flavor along with a slight kick. The roti was very tasty as well, compliments the lamb also helps with the spice.

I finally got to try out The Row for brunch and definitely plan to come back. The outdoor patio was great, there was no wait, its pretty inexpensive, and it was a really relaxed atmosphere where we were able to hang out for a couple hours. 

The food: Check in on Yelp and you get a free fried pickle appetizer! These were really good, and the sauce that comes with them was even better. (May or may not have started eating the sauce by itself when waiting for my meal, and I think I spotted my friend lick his plate). The biscuits and jam starter was also another winner, the tomato jam was surprisingly good; pro-tip - you can ask for a side of gravy and get the best of both worlds. Our entrees were tasty as well, and the hot chicken seemed to be the best choice. 

The service: I would give The Row five stars because it meets all of my qualification for hangover curing brunches, but the service was questionable. Our waiter was friendly and chatty but could not remember a single thing to save his life, I got the feeling he was hitting the peace pipe in the back instead of putting our order in. No surprise, our food took a while to come out. Fortunately we were enjoying ourselves on the patio so it was not a huge concern, and they did apologize for the wait. 

The Row is one of the least crowded places in midtown for Sunday morning brunch with about the same quality of food as everywhere else. I was a big fan, and am looking forward to trying out their drink menu at the next brunch.

With a name like Full Belly Deli how can you not check this place out? When going to this place dont drive too fast or you will miss it because it is kind of situated in an industrial type building and the parking is lot is small. The suite they are in is not all that big either with about 8 small tables. I came in around 11:30 and was lucky to grab a table after ordering at the counter.

What I got was a Tri Tip Sandwich ($9.50) on sourdough. Was contemplating whether or not I should of got chips for I didnt know how big the sandwich was. The lady behind the counter said the sandwich is huge and it will fill me up. When your order is done they call your name at the other end of the counter towards the front of the restaurant.

The sandwich itself was not all that big. The tri tip was thinly sliced. I have had tri tip sandwiches at other places before and the meat was not thinly sliced so I wasn used to this style. According to their menu the tri tip is dry rubbed. I didnt really taste any seasonings. Also comes with carmelized onions, blue cheese, and spinach. I substituted the blue cheese with cheddar because cheese that is flavored with mold is just not my thing. I had to put cholula on it to give it more flavor with a kick.

So in the end I was not really impressed even though the lunch rush was almost out the door. I just dont get the hype. The sandwich got rid of my hunger but I was not full to the point that I could of still ate something on the side. I paid a total of 12 bucks and change for a sandwich and a drink. Kind of pricey if you ask me. On a funny note, when you get your drink from the soda machine, there is a picture of Ice Cube on the ice dispense button and a picture of Ice Tea on the ice tea dispense button. You dont see that everyday. Well, unless you work or eat here everyday. Hours are Monday through Friday 7 am to 3 pm. Saturday and Sunday 10 am to 3 pm. I will probably eat here again because there are lots of other choices. Maybe the next sandwich I get will be much better.

Yelp 2016 Review #15 
588 overall

I'm surprised at the high ratings for Brick, which prompted us to try something new last night.  The price point is ridiculously high for the quality of the food.  We were offered the specials of some kind of risotto, lobster thermador, and caprese salad.  We then heard two other tables close to us hear about specials such as elk chops, salmon, and venison, which made us really suspicious.  Are the wait staff assessing what we would order?  And if so, they were absolutely wrong.  We were put off by this aspect alone.  

The wine list is okay, nothing to write home to Mom about.  We had high hopes after selecting the Manhattan Lobster chowder, even though it was not a chowder, but a soup, it was nicely layered flavored with vegetables cooked to the right tenderness.  From there it went downhill.  I ordered the filet mignon, which was, honestly, about 1/3 of the thickness that most filets are cut, cooked okay, but lacked seasoning.  The garlic whipped potatoes were a misnomer, perhaps they waved a clove of garlic over the potatoes at some point in the cooking process, that was the only essence of garlic I tasted (after being told by our server that it was really garlicky, I was sorely disappointed).  My husband had the rib eye, and it, too, was not the thickness of a normal ribeye, and it was more toward the black-and-blue rare than the medium-rare he ordered.  For plates over $30, this felt like robbery.  His fries were clearly frozen-from-a-bag, and the ketchup was commercial.  Really, how hard is it to make homemade fries in a restaurant that charges these prices?  

We skipped dessert, we'd had enough disappointment for the night.  In a town with amazing restaurants, you can't afford to be this average and charge these prices.

I love this place and there's not even a single thing I can eat here besides the bread. 

Right now, I have some deep regrets. Like how I took late afternoon/early evening HHs for granted, when we'd spend a couple hours sitting at the bar with frozen French 75s (you get a large for the price of a small), brains slowly going numb and frozen. Thumbing our noses at the oppressive heat and humidity outside. It's a mood.

And now, this is a first stop for us when we're back in town. I cherish these visits. Last month on the Saturday before Mardi Gras, we spent a couple hours here, enjoying the festive scene around us, despite parades being done for the day. So many New Orleanians in the holiday spirit. There's nothing like it.

And honestly, Superior can always feel this way, on any given day. It's such a local treasure.

With several visits back to Magasin, my conclusion is that it has worked out all the growing pains from the winter and is now a serious contender for my favorite eateries on Magazine Street. But that's why I gave it four stars to begin with.

So, the aforementioned issues with slightly confused/overwhelmed counter service and long waits? A thing of the past. We were greeted immediately, whisked to the counter when we told the gal we wanted take out instead of being seated. Within 10 minutes our order was brought out to us by the nicest lady ever. 

Oh besides the bun and veg spring rolls, I suggest you get the garlic tofu banh mi if you're looking for something hearty with good value ($4...really? Really.) I even ate *all* the bread. That's rare for me when it comes to po-boys (and I consider most of the banh mi  to be like delicious Vietnamese versions of this New Orleans staple). Crusty, chewy goodness. It could stand to have more vegetables, but that's a small quibble.

I almost look forward to the cold weather so I can finally try the vegetarian pho!

That I have no love lost for less than a perfectly-executed Pimm's Cup has nothing to do with my rating of Lost Love Lounge. That I have no love lost for cigarette smoke has nothing to do with my rating of the Lost Love Lounge, either. And, that I especially have no love lost for a unisex bathroom with questionable latching device has nothing to do with my rating, either.

I'm not making sense (yet again). Four stars, you're scratching your head, why, then? Best motherfucking bar food in town. After throwing back a couple cocktails, I can't think of anything more satisfying than a huge bowl of vermicelli, tofu (three different vegetarian options, but I'm all about the tamarind-encrusted), fresh veggies and hot sauce. And a spring roll. You can keep your cheese fries, your nachos and your jalapeno poppers. Grilled cheese? Hell no. I'll take a Banh Mi. Yep, it's official, I'm hitting up Lost Love for real food when I plan to tie one on.

(and I just really like this bar anyway. Yet more reason for me to plan to move to the Marigny one day. I need a neighborhood bar like this one).

The entire operation is a friendly one, too. From the bartendress to the regulars to the folks serving up chow in the back.

I was recently asked by someone where they should stay in New Orleans. Options are so overwhelming! You could stay in an AirBnB in a cool neighborhood, but if you don't really know the neighborhoods of this city, it could mean you're in a less desirable/safe area (AirBnB is illegal in some parts of town, including the French Quarter). You could stay in a small local hotel in the Quarter. For the most part, I don't particularly love these as I haven't had the best experiences in them (weak service and amenities). Locally-owned bed & breakfasts are a great option but book quickly. Posh hotels are awesome but $$$ and trendy hotels like the Ace (my favorite) are great but also book quickly as they are smaller so if you're coming during Mardi Gras or JazzFest, you better book ahead. That leaves the solid chains like the Hilton, Hyatt, and of course Marriott. You can't go wrong really!

I was in town during Mardi Gras and couldn't stay in my own house, so we ended up staying here. At $350 a night, it wasn't cheap, but it was literally Mardi Gras weekend leading into Fat Tuesday itself and it could have been a lot worse.

The best part about this Marriott, other than its edge of the FQ location, is the lobby action. Seriously! It's an attraction within itself. During Mardi Gras you need a wristband to get in to see these sights, as it's right on Canal, the major parade route. Each evening, we'd wind down in the lobby bar. It's expensive for New Orleans and there are better hotel bars out there, but the characters that found their way in and out of here... you can't put a price on people watching. 

There's also a(n expensive) coffee bar serving Starbucks if you need your fix before leaving the hotel, and a very convenient little grocery & souvenir shop that serves liquor, too (no mini bar in the room, which is fine with me because that removes the temptation to dig into a $6 mini can of Pringles. Get me?)

Our room was small but clean and comfortable. There's a fridge for your leftovers. There's a coffee maker and huge TV. Beds are comfy and you get a robe, too. 

I usually work out when traveling but not this time. I checked out the gym anyway and it's small but does the trick (although it's a pretty dark/depressing gym like in most NOLA hotels. It's such an afterthought and I get it, "who works out when they are on vacation in New Orleans" but still... put in a Peloton bike. It would be such a game changer). 

The pool is really a decent size for a French Quarter hotel and affords a view over (not so pretty at most times of year) Canal Street.

The New Orleans Marriott is, as I mention above, a solid choice. It's not the most charming nor does it have that oh-so-gorgeous old timey New Orleans vibe, but you also likely won't have a giant palmetto bug making its way into your room. And if you're as phobic of these monsters as I am, that's peace of mind right there :)

If you're on the search for coffee in the upper Quarter, skip PJs and Starbucks and hit French Truck instead. They provide the very BEST cold brew in town. It's silky smooth and gives you just the icy burst you need to revive your day. I usually drink it black, but they have a variety of non dairy milks if you so desire!

I was thrilled to see that they opened a cute little cafe in the French Quarter close to the Marriott on Canal where I was staying during Mardi Gras. It's set up so that you can easily grab and go. They also have a decent amount of tables if you need to take a break, though I wouldn't say it's the most conducive spot to set up shop for working all day. The space is very open and with the doors open to the bustling French Quarter streets, there are so many distractions. Sometimes, you just need to devote a day to vacation, even if you live here.

Yes, you're reading this correctly: I, Joi B, mostly raw vegan chick, not only went willingly to a steak house, but I'm giving this steak house 5 glorious stars, yo!

It's old school as you can get. The kind of place where even someone like Yours, Truly, is compelled to order a steak and a martini. While that didn't actually happen, what I did order made me extremely happy, not to mention the attentive and friendly service, and the environment within this boisterous old jernt. 

My friends and I got in on one of those fabulous curtained booths. I love private booths, what can I say? So, they had me there. I was dubious about what I'd be served here, I can't lie. And I was ragingly hungry after having worked up quite the appetite at the ostrich and zebra races earlier (yes, yes, I realize I was not a very good vegetarian on Saturday. I might as well have worn leather shoes while I was at it. Oh wait...)

A perusal of the menu had me ordering sides of spinach, mushrooms and German potatoes. I also indulged in some of my friends' garlic bread, though I've pretty much sworn off all kinds of white bread. It was impossible to resist because seriously, this garlic bread is perfection, pure comfort food and like I said, I was starvin' marvin.

And I had a glass of wine, a decent pinot noir (they have a very respectable list of wines by the bottle and glass). 

And then I gorged on the side orders I mention above. Whereas I expected reheated dishes of frozen monstrosities, I received: *fresh* baby spinach leaves, *fresh* whole mushrooms  and freshly sliced/flash fried potato rounds. Granted the spinach had been sauteed in butter, but not overly so, and the mushrooms were served in a butter broth (oh come on, like who the hell could resist that?), but it wasn't overpowering. I prefer olive oil to butter any day, but this restaurant is, like I said, old school, and hey, they treat vegetables right! I ate all of it. ALL. Of. It.

After dinner, I commenced upon cigars and brandy.

The Good:
-enormous salads with better-than-decent lettuce choices (mixed greens, spinach, romaine... Iceberg if you must)
-the tempeh/tofu/vegan cheese as well as G/F options (this should be classified under "The Outstanding") 
-the menu features fantastic variety

The Meh:
-the lemonade cocktail I had once was so sweet, I couldn't taste anything but sugar in it (stick to wine. They have a decent Malbec)

-The "Margherita"(?) pizza

I was bamboozled. I'll go so far as to say, it's impossible that I was served anything resembling a Margherita pizza as this was loaded with your typical low moisture mozzarella (the menu stated it contained fresh mozzarella. I wasn't expecting Buffalo, but come on... Not to mention there wasn't a sliver of basil to be found, and it contained perhaps 5 slices of orange tomatoes. I also had asked for mushrooms to be added on. I counted about 10 stems and tiny slivers on the entire small pizza, which is pretty stingy. The crust is also just not right--spongy and thick. I really should have sent it back, but how could I when our waitress was nowhere to be found.

-On that note, the service

The apologies kept coming and yet our waitress spent more time socializing with one of her tables than paying attention to the fact that we were all but flagging her down after several minutes. Our food was brought by a different server and isn't it customary for your regular server to come by and make sure you have everything you need? Encourage more drinking? Nope.

I left the majority of my small pizza behind and had no desire to bag it up for leftovers as I didn't want to waste the box. I knew I wouldn't be finishing that pizza.

The above may seem kind of harsh, but I'd been raving about Mellow Mushroom because my previous visits were great (hence the three stars. I would have put past visits at 4 and my most recent at 2). 

I'll give it another shot and stick to MM's salads and sandwiches, rather than pizza, unless they come out with a thin crust option. I'm sure the sub par service was an isolated incident as well. It happens.

New Orleans doesn't have a ton of later night options (that is, after 10pm), so it's cool that Kebab, being on the St. Claude strip (it's sort of a strip. Don't nitpick please), is open til 11pm weeknights and midnight on weekends.

So this is the thing: by all appearances, you think this will be a cheap a$$ good Doner dive. I don't eat kebob, but I always know that there are options for me there in the form of hummus, falafel and the like. These are some of my favorite things, often consumed late late at night, typically under the influence of too many libations, but there it is. These places are lifesavers (and thank you for noting what can be made vegan-- **but please see note below, fellow vegans/vegetarians) and there can never be too many of them.

I didn't eat here late at night, though, so that sort of wine goggle haze wasn't coloring my opinion that the hummus here is extremely bland (I ordered a plate, which comes with a lot of bread, plus olives and cucumbers). I also didn't love that it's swimming in olive oil rather than spices. They were out of their house made habanero sauce but not even a bottle of Tabasco was to be found. In New Orleans? Kinda weird. So I had absolutely nothing to spice it up a bit (the person taking our order was nice enough but didn't suggest any alternatives). Texture of the hummus is nice and creamy and the pillowy bread that I see a lot of people complaining about was insanely good in my opinion. I'm not a fan of dry, tasteless pita so this is an appreciated alternative. But the lack of flavor would make me think twice about ordering that hummus again.

Somehow a gyro kebob, a small side of fries, two waters and hummus plate came to a little over $27.00 which is steep for a divey/casual, almost fast food type of place. (I do understand that the meat items, being that they are not factory-farmed, will be pricier than what one would typically pay, but $8.50 for a small paper plate of hummus is still expensive). Plus even though this is counter service, I can't not tip 20%, as in, I'm physically unable to do so especially at this time of year when the service industry is hurting. Note that the small fries at 3.50 comes with aioli but the large fries at 6.50 comes with aioli *and* ketchup. Huh? Not sure why they are so stingy with condiments, but I am not digging it at all. I'm more than willing to pay the .75 for house made sauces (even though there are plenty of places that don't make you pay for house made condiments) but if you're out of something, at least have bottles of Tabasco and maybe even Louisiana to make up for it.

**Vegetarians be aware: I'm just noticing in the "about the business" section here on Yelp that the frites are fried in animal fat. This absolutely should be written clearly on the menu especially considering that they are cool about noting what can and can't be made vegan. Also there are plenty of people who would avoid fries made in animal fat even if they do eat meat. Not saying they need to alter how they make their food, just that when things are clearly noted on the menu as to what is and isn't vegan, it sucks that I ate two fries made in animal fat off my boyfriend's plate because I didn't think I'd have to inquire as to the oil in a place like this. This is pretty disappointing as was the majority of my experience here.

Lilly's about saved my life last week! With temps dropping to the point of actual *icicles* forming, I still had to be out and about (not such a bad thing as pretty much anywhere is going to be warmer than my old drafty house) and although our intention was to get one of the amazing salads at nearby HiVolt, all I had to do was walk by Lilly's and change my mind because... well, vegan phó. 

Some of you are going to stop reading right here and that's OK, I don't blame you. I'm pretty certain that meaty phó is a whole other ballgame, what with the meat drippings seeping into the soup and adding that bit of unctuousness you're never going to get with a vegan version. But there I was freezing cold and do you know how hard it is to get a big bowl of vegetarian soup in this city?

Started with the spring rolls, because I can't ever pass those up. Vietnamese spring rolls are in my top 20 things to eat, seriously. And then came the enormous bowls of soup that warmed our souls that chilly afternoon. Flavor is light and I have to add tons of spice (wish they had sambal chili paste rather than sugary Sri Racha, just a note), but dang if that soup didn't make the rest of the day and frigid night bearable. 

And it was crazy cheap, too. Lunch for 2 (both of us had spring rolls and phó) was less than $30. True story.

Add in the sweetest, most attentive service (our waitress told us we "did good" as she took the bowls away) and Lilly's is definitely one of my favorite lower magazine eateries.

The eternal (yelper) question: Does this- insert iconic establishment- even need another review, when they already have X hundred reviews? To this I say, uh, yeah they do. You can never have too many positive reviews. Plus I look at it as a note to myself upon returning (ie, see my note below).

Yo Mama's is one of those places that was always on my itinerary when I'd visit NOLA. Truthfully, though, once I moved here, I have not been back since yesterday. And I also had only drank here, back in the days before they even had veggie burgers. 

So, it had been a long day of drinking and no eating. A parade day... By 6, or was it 7 or 8pm, I was really feeling it. I hate being hungry in the French Quarter because I don't have tons of options here (that aren't dress-up places, that is). I remembered Yo Mama's famed burger list and immediately was craving some crazy veggie burger piled high with whatever other crazy concoction they could come up with and insisted we make an immediate beeline (er, crooked, inebriated beeline). My friends and I were relieved to find an empty booth and slid on in. I love the atmosphere here-- just a cozy FQ bar with all kinds of characters hanging around. I remembered the bartenders always being pretty damn nice and that still holds true. You might have to wait a bit for service, but that's how it goes and it's never too long. The bartender also waits the tables. Something to keep in mind. 

While the veggie burger here isn't anything special, the way it's dressed up makes a plain girl into a vixen. And that giant baked potato is her perfect not-to-be ignored accessory (you can get these all dressed up too, if you'd like!) I had the Mexican version with salsa, avocado and jalapeños. While I agreed to have it dressed, I think next time I'll have them leave off the mayo because it didn't go with the salsa at all (that's my note to self, in case you were wondering). The baked potato is perfect, by the way. 

Drinks are cheap and good. I'm glad that I have another go-to for a cheap, casual and quick meal when crawling the Quarter.

I'm possibly the only person in America who has never stepped foot inside a PF Chang's, but I read up on their fairly decent amount of vegan options and thought I'd give it a try next time I was desperate for Chinese food. 

Verdict: Vegetarian lettuce wraps are everything here. If I ever do find myself coming back, I'm sticking to these and not ordering anything else. 

My entree (Buddha's Delight) was thoroughly tasteless and the vegetables actually did not taste good (the broccoli was downright awful). The tofu was rubbery and had no flavor. I don't understand how one dish can be so good and the other so bad, but there it is. A possible save would be to order the vegetables steamed instead of smothered in tasteless sauce, but I don't know.

Those lettuce wraps, tho... (wish they used romaine rather than iceberg which has no nutritional value). They are good enough to beg a return, not to mention they have a full bar and what appear to be decent cocktails and wine.

Love!!!! (I mean, ¡Me encanta!)

I'm a tapas fanatic, it seems. My favorite types of dinners involve a table covered with small plates. Order up a bunch and then wait for them to arrive at the table at any point, a new surprise. More ordering. More drinking. Next thing you know, you're at a three hour dinner. As it should be.

Barcelona Tapas is such a sweet spot to spend your evening with date and/or friends. This cozy house is warm and welcoming and you feel like you just happened upon a secret locals joint somewhere off the beaten path of Barri Gòtic in Barcelona (possibly my favorite European city). 

We started off with that superb sangria. Believe the hype. My fear with sangria is that it will be too sweet. Not the case here, as it's just... perfect. Not too sweet, nor, heaven forbid, too sour. Slightly fruity, definitely alcoholic... and two pitchers later, we were feeling it! Better order more food?

My favorite small plate here the other night was easily the patatas bravas. The *best* version of this dish I've ever had! Was the peppery aioli liberally drizzled on top? In fact, I believe my dinner date did not get to even try them because I gobbled it all up like whoa. The asparagus (also comes with aioli, vegans take note) is simple and delightful. Similarly, the lentil soup is a healthy, hearty option if you're trying to avoid all the mayo-tastic treats. Oh and the pesto dip... don't skip it. Ah, the memories... they make me hungry. Be sure to bring people who can share in the fun and so that you can try as much as possible.  

One other happy-making note: prepared for garlic galore on just about anything, but especially the crimini mushrooms (as it should be). The tomato bread with cheese allows for you to put a half clove on top. Daaaaang. 

In short, I'll be back at Barcelona Tapas in no time, I suspect. ¡Bring on the platos!

During finals time in December, it seemed it was next to impossible to get a seat in a coffee shop with free Wifi, no less a seat near a precious outlet. I happened upon Luna after seeing my regular shop completely packed (That is, CC's Coffeehouse. I only go to PJs as a last resort). What a sight for (computer-bleary) sore eyes! 

Luna is an actual coffee*house* and I love that. With a large front porch, where, although there are no outlets, you can probably work in the most idyllic environment imaginable  (the most idyllic environment that isn't say, on a shady beach in Costa Rica or Hawaii). Venture inside and you will find a small front room with outlets and a power strip. Past that is the counter where you'll order from a menu of sandwiches, pastry and espresso/drip/tea. The guy who works there is the nicest man I've ever encountered in a coffeehouse (I assume him to be the owner. I once owned a coffeehouse/bar and believe me, I could have taken attitude and customer lessons from this guy). 

Also be sure and check out the room past the counter/bar! Plenty of space to spread out and plug in while sipping on some brew and working your day away.

And now for an update on the new additions to the cocktail menu!

To be perfectly honest, lately I've been avoiding hard liquor and although I come here regularly and that gorgeous tiki drink menu tempts me, I stick to sparkling wine (I know. Killjoy). But when we came here for dinner the other night, our waiter told us about the new drinks on the menu, the Deadbeat Daiquiri (described as a not overly sweet Piña Colada) and a punch (forgot the name and the online menu hasn't been updated) that sounded like it had tons of booze in it, so I went for the Daiquiri.

This is the best daiquiri I've ever had *and*  (I'm gonna call it like it is) the best damn Piña Colada I have ever had. I absolutely "get" why they don't call it that because true Piña lovers are going to be cranky about the lack of tooth ache sweetness and phony baloney sugary drink mix. But this Daiquiri is divine! It has a rich, fresh coconutty flavor. It's blended, but not a super icy texture like most daiquiris are in this city. It just fucking delicious. And perfectly strong.

My guy had the punch and naturally I had to try it. I'm so not shying away from it next time! It's strong, yes, but the tropical flavors are so fresh and I love that passionfruit seems to dominate. It's also not sickeningly sweet.

On that note, the drinks here are crafted so that you're getting such good quality spirits and juices, that your days of suffering the dragon bowl hangover the next day are over. You get me here. 

I didn't know I could love Latitude 29 even more, but there you have it.

Time to eat my words. Ignore my previous quibbles about the not-so-great veggie dogs here, for Dat Dog is now serving really delicious vegan sausages (that I believe are Field Roast) for vegetarians! They have two kinds, but I recommend the spicy chipotle (it's not that spicy, just incredibly delicious). One other thing: get that doggie loaded up... toppings are gratis! I was a bit conservative yesterday, but next time I'm going to town on that dog.

This is pretty thrilling news, I must say, because sometimes you're ready to eat lunch after the dreaded 3pm closing time that's common in this city (this was the case yesterday). And sometimes, you just want to sit on an enormous patio with an outdoor bar and sip some Prosecco on a warm fall afternoon. You can do all of this at Dat Dog. 

Also tipping my hat to the really friendly staff. Do they take happy pills? They are just the best.

One slightly weird thing: they had a cocktail list up at the bar (order drinks separately from food) but the bartender couldn't make any of them! He was extremely nice (like the rest of the good folks at Dat Dog), and I saw they had bubbly, so all was forgiven, but... in a cocktail-focused city, this kind of is a bummer. I mean::: Fall. Cocktails. Who can resist? I'll be back for more and hopefully this time they can keep their promise of a Pear Collins.

I encountered the motherload of all things awesome and Asian here the other day. WoWowoW. Groceries were made, oh yes.

The produce section is enough to make me weep. I mean, 1.19 ea. for young coconuts that run you three times at that Whole Paycheck? There's an entire freezer section of exotic fruits, like bread fruit and duriyan (one day), if you can't find what you're looking for. I picked up a couple packages of frozen lotus root just cuz I love it and have never seen anywhere in a grocery store. 

If, like me, you're a saucy girl or guy, you may lose yourself in the hot sauce aisle. Dozens of varieties beyond sambal, Sri Racha and the like. Soy sauce... are you kidding? I've never seen so many different varieties. Although I tend not to buy premade curries and the like, there is scores of these too. 

There was something I was hoping to find: I would sell my soul to find bean curd skin, aka, yuba, and sadly was not able to find it the other day, but I'm sure it has to be somewhere here. If you're a fan of gluten and soy meats, you'll find an aisle devoted to this stuff (it's dried and you add water). Personally, I was more taken by the varieties of tofu in the fridge area. Mucho miso paste varieties right over there, too. Again, insanely cheap compared to WF. 

I'll be back soon and report more on this grocery paradise.

Why I'd opt to go to Rouses over Whole Foods:

1. It's Louisiana-owned
2. They have Cajun hot nuts
3. Related to the above, they have an array of other NOLA specialty items (tourists, buy your foodie souvenirs here rather than the FQ)
4.They play New Orleans music rather than hippy dippy crap
5. Their employees are nice without making you feel like you've committed a sin by asking for plastic (to be fair, the cashiers at WF aren't nearly as self-righteous as the floor staff who seem like they'd spit on you if you ask for something that is against WF puredom, like artificial sweetener. Not that I'd ever ask for it, but a friend once had the audacity to do so and was met with a lecture).
6. Kick ass olive bar
7. They just have a lot more grocery items, and more affordable options at that
8. Not everything has to be gourmet specialty foods and products. They have those, but sometimes you want a bag of Zapps chips or a harsh cleaning product for eff's sake!
9. Nowhere nearly as pretentious (for example, you probably don't notice, but WF has plenty of produce that's from Mexico, California and other places).  
10. Aeroponic rooftop garden! How cool is that?
11. Phenomenal booze/wine/beer selection

Issues with this particular Rouses that would have me head to WF instead:

1. The oils area is confusing not only to shoppers but to employees as well. I had three different employees attempt to find me a vessel in which to pour truffle oil from the jug thingamajig and no one could help me. Not their fault as apparently they had just changed all that around, but no one clued the staff in. 
2. There's just not enough organic produce. It would be ideal as well, if the organic stuff wasn't all mixed in with the other stuff.
3. Not enough produce in general (uh, dino kale shouldn't be that rare).
4. Lack of gourmet whole bean coffee


Numbers 2-4 have double weight, as I'm all about the organic produce selection. A fine whole bean coffee i(extremely dark roast that I grind myself) is what gets me through a morning. I realize not everyone is as particular as me, but there you have it. Supermarket shopping is painful enough, I'd rather not have to go to more than one store per week.

Other things to note:

-gourmet and deli sections in this Rouses is really outstanding and similar to WF. I didn't check out the prepared food section too much, so I can't report on that just yet. 
-the staff really did go out of their way to find me an oil vessel. 
-that wine selection blows WF's out of the water

Expect review updates!

This review is for the pool... And for the nekkid good times.

I jest. I didn't get anywhere near nekkid this past weekend at the Country Club. But I could have if wanted to and really, isn't that the important thing here? 

+no judgements
+pretty cool environment
+sometimes thar will be eye candy
+sometimes you'll see things that remind you how the human body is a pretty interesting creation
+don't let your stare linger too long
+just get with the nekkid good times
+sitting poolside with a Bloody Mary on a Sunday evening

In all seriousness, whether you want to show off that hot new bathing suit or let it all hang out, you're welcome at the Country Club. As you can gather from other reviews, this ain't your Uncle Thurston's Country Club. Maybe it's more like your cousin Gilligan's (heyyyy, "lil buddy" wink wink).

The staff here are so dang nice! Especially Mr. Smooth there on the mic announcing dinner orders to p/u from the bar. He's the gatekeeper and gets you all signed in. Ditto for the cool bartender inside (ear plugs, hat and tattoos). 

I look forward to come back for brunch and report back on that!

I like the concept of doing just a few things and doing them well. That's an understatement for Crescent Pie & Sausage.

So, you know the name, you know the deal. There are a variety of pies: savory, sweet and pizza, my favorite kind of pie (right above key lime, which they make when it's the season).
