The pesto schmear is a flavor blast, as are the marinated tomatoes. I added on avocado (recommend!) and they give you a half of one. Nice. They top it off with fresh cucumber slices. It's been hours and I'm still full.

Add in shady sidewalk café seating on a warm, breezy Saturday afternoon and you've got serious idyllica (I made that up) going on.

Except for the no booze part. Not that I'm complaining, but if I were in that brunchy kind of mood, I'd be wishing for Bloody Marys. 

Props to the cook/runner who hails from Jersey!

The simply-named Tavern offers up some mighty simple comfort food pleasures (White Trash hash, anyone?) and elevated junk food game bites. 

That said, I'm not sure this is quite the weekend brunch place for me, due to the TVs providing all of the background noise. I'm not a fan of big TVs blaring games -- to me, this is the worst kind of ambiance. BUT... for those of you seeking a place to watch local sports and cheer on with a crowd, Tavern is the spot for you, especially if your tastes are a bit more high brow than your typical nachos. I mean, they have nachos, but Tavern's come with pistachio and goat cheese. Nice! 

I'd easily return on a non game day (or even to sit on the shaded side patio) for more of that White Trash Hash. Think tater tot casserole. I mean, really. Goodbye hangover. The egg white omelet I had was kinda blah, as the tomatoes made it seem extra watery.The "Wicked" Bloody Mary was hardly wicked, more like gentle, despite the vodka being infused with pickled things that you'd hope for on your glass. They don't automatically garnish the way you'd think. Or at least the way a New Orleanian would think. I mean... just a lime? Nu uh. Our very lovely server came out with some olives for us, which was nice. But a Bloody without beaucoup d' garnish is a naked Mary, indeed.

Extra props for three bottles of hot sauces on the table, marked X, XX and XXX. Go for the orangey habanero, as it's the tastiest of the bunch (it might be the XX). Don't be fooled by the warnings. They are there for the bland American palate.

**This review is for the bar only!

Often, a bartender makes the bar. Anyone who has tended bar (8 years under my belt), knows there's a science behind it and by "science," I don't mean mixology, I mean people-handling. You're part therapist, part entertainer, part conversationalist, and more. You need to be able to read your customers within seconds or risk them leaving after one drink. You want to keep them there. You want them to tip you. You want them to become regulars (unless they are jerks).

I recently stayed at the Omni thanks to an unheard of rate of $135/night. This rate included two complimentary holiday cocktails at the Rib Room bar. We went to use them at around 10:30 on Monday night and the bartender apologetically told us that the recipes hadn't yet been given to the bartenders. She offered to make something holiday-ish on the fly for us, or we could have pretty much any drink we wanted. Uhhh, when Moet sparkling rose is an option, I can do without the overly sweet holiday drink, so SCORE! Let me note that my stay at the Omni was not a good one and this weird mistake on their part to offer up holiday drinks and then not even share a holiday drink menu with their own hotel bar staff was just par for the course at this point.

Getting back to our fabulous bartender. She was the best! I wish I has asked her name, but she's blonde and works Monday nights, so that should narrow it down for you. Go on a Monday night! Sit at the bar! She knows how to make you feel at home, chat a bit if you want, or leave you to your conversation with your partner. That's a skill, people. She even honored my third drink coupon when I suggested I should just buy one (also so I could tip on a CC)... actually she insisted. Pretty cool. That sparkling rose doesn't come cheap! I made sure to take care of her (note: when drinks/food are comped, one should tip generously). 

I am not a regular at any hotel bar, even though NOLA has some amazing hotel bars, but I can easily see myself returning here often as I am in the Quarter. The environs is plush, the bartendress is awesome and you also get a nice street view thanks to floor to ceiling windows.

Mondays are rough in New Orleans. It seems like everything is closed with the exception of Vietnamese, which, luckily is one of my favorite types of cuisine. I needed a break from my Lily's habit recently, so my friend and I landed at Namese.

It's definitely in an odd/unexpected spot, across from my old storage unit at Fountainbleu. They've somehow turned what was probably not the nicest building into something really special. There's a patio out front and if weather permits, do sit at one of the large woven booths. Inside reminds me of a really hip 1960s steak house as weird as that sounds. It's not your typical Vietnamese joint! Unlike Lily's, they have a full bar, too. And the rumors are true: you can add booze to your bubble tea smoothies!

But. It's not like they hand you a drink menu at any point. This was one of several service misses, I'm afraid. Don't get me wrong. Our server was nothing but nice and it had been a long, packed day for her. And a lot might have been beyond her control. Things like not getting our bubble teas until long after our app came out (to her credit, she kept coming by promising they'd come out soon). She also wasn't too familiar with what vegan meant. It's all over the menu ("vegan pho" "vegan crepe") and I'm not sure if they're trying to be trendy, but if they are aware of vegan diets, their waitstaff should be aware, too. If you are vegetarian or vegan, whatever you order, don't assume that if you are asking about something being vegan that they'll check for your entire order, either. Make sure for each item you're ordering. In other restaurants, I'm just used to them checking for me on everything once I identify myself as being vegan. On a positive note, she did make sure they gave me vegan peanut sauce with my spring rolls. She tried her best. I think they should train waitstaff a little bit better, that's all.

I liked, didn't love the food. Veg spring rolls could have used some protein and more avocado. Most places in NOLA make them with a hearty slice of fried tofu. I also ordered the veggie sotca, which was tasty, but without adding tofu to the mix, you, like me, may be left a little unsatisfied. 

When my mango bubble tea arrived, it came... without bubbles. I should have canceled the order, but I sent it back for the bubbles because that's kind of the whole point. That said, it's way too sweet. Way.

Later after we paid, we were hanging around talking for quite a bit, so we asked another waiter for a drink menu. They must be uniformly against liquor sales or something because that drink menu never came. There were at least 2-3 servers there and I don't know, it seemed they were overworked but I couldn't figure out why. I won't get too into it because like I said, no one was anything but nice to us which really is the most important thing.

This is a super complain-y review. I do like Namese, but I'm not sure I'd return, unless I was itching for a really great atmosphere when going out for Vietnamese.

I do not like casinos. I do not like gambling. But I loved staying at the Ameristar. For those of you who have read my reviews of hotels, you know it's a big deal when I rate a hotel over 3 stars. 

Rooms are suites with a sunken living room. Yes, you read that right. Sunken. Living. Room. Ours overlooked the gorgeous indoor/outdoor pool. I didn't bring my suit, so I had to content myself with just looking (pressing my nose against the glass. I did so delicately, of course). I took a walk around the patio area, which lends itself well to poolside libations.

Rooms have three flat screen TVs, one by the beds, one in the sunken living room, and one in the bathroom *suite* which is convenient if you end up taking a bath in the fabulously deep tub. I just adore the privacy this bathroom affords you. The toilet is in a separate room off the sinks, tub and shower. Thinking back to some pricey hotels that have those ridiculous sliding doors on the bathroom that allow for no privacy whatsoever (W, I'm looking at you), I really appreciated this. 

Is three TVs excessive? Sure. But I kept thinking this would be great for families with little kids who could have their own TV to watch (I mean, at night when winding down. I just don't want anyone to think I advocate dulling developing minds with the idiot box).

I never used to care about sound proofing, until I stayed in a room next to someone who emitted the loudest snores known to man. Ameristar has good sound proofing so you don't hear your neighbors (but you can hear loud people in the hallway, see below).

Other good things: small fridge (no mini bar) and a coffee maker. Decent gym. I was the only one using it, which of course is the way I like it.

The not so good:
Smoking in common areas. C'mon St. Charles, catch up with the year 2011. Smoking is even more difficult to bear in public places, yet every single restaurant we went to in this town has smoking sections which make the entire place REEK!!! And this hotel is no better. As soon as you open your hotel door, you're hit with the smell of a dirty ashtray.

Sound in the hallways at all hours... I mean, screaming. Ugh. Not the hotel's fault, as I'm sure late night revelry is common in a casino hotel.

Beds are comfy, although I think the bedding is pretty average. There's this brown throw that neither soft nor warm. For a laugh, check out the "for your convenience" pricing list should you even think about walking off with one of the "luxury" (hardly) neck pillows for 100 dollars or "luxury" bath towels that you can get for 10 bucks anywhere but will set you back 100 here. They do not give you a bathrobe, although the pricing for it is on the list.

Though I have a lot of nostalgia attached to Mona Lisa, as my last review states, I can't keep my review at five stars when I recently had a pretty sub par experience. 

As always, I ordered a pizza since I felt like splurging and eating cheese, which is rare these days. After eating half of a small one, I gave in and didn't even take the rest home for leftovers. From the bland sauce the the thick, doughy crust, it was mediocre all over. And I was pretty damn hungry. I can't in good faith recommend the pizza after that experience. The other issue was my friend who's on a limited diet made the grave, grave error of asking for a substitution (broccoli, rather than cheese) on her salad... which, judging by the amused look our server gave us, is a big no-no. That's fine, I get it, chefs hate substitutions. She then asked if she could just pay for broccoli to be added to her salad. Again, no. You can't even order a side of broccoli. This kind of thing I don't get, seeing as you can add broccoli as a pizza topping, so, what gives? Not sure if that was on the server (he said he'd ask the kitchen, but then never gave an answer one way or another, nor did broccoli ever appear). I don't mean to say he gave us poor service, because otherwise he was attentive and pretty cool. 

If this were my first visit here, I don't know if I'd return between the frowning on any kind of altering stuff off the menu and the mediocre pizza. I've loved Mona Lisa for so long, yet I'm not sure if I'm going to opt to come here instead of say, Italian Barrel or Domenica (whose pizza in a whole other league and if you're going to splurge, might as well do it right).

Great atmosphere, ruined by the overwhelmingly meh crowd.

The clientele on Friday night consisted of what appeared to be characters straight out of a Bret Easton Ellis novel... possibly including Patrick Batemen himself, seated right next to us, going on about how dare teachers bitch about their salaries when they get three months off a year (what teachers does *he* know, pray tell? Maybe the one he butchered the night before?) So, I'm not going out on a limb here to say that his group of friends who were cheering him on deserve to be deemed thoroughly despicable. I won't make such sweeping generalizations about the rest of the crowd but it seemed like they'd all be cronies forever, with regular gatherings on a giant yacht somewhere, (if not perpetually haunting the poor Columns Hotel). 

Forced to go inside for drinks because the waitress seemed taken with the table of dumbasses next to us, I overheard dudes everywhere trying to impress the ladies, going on about how successful they are (I don't think I saw a single person over 23, so I wonder how this can be, unless Daddy's in oil). Major ick factor everywhere. But it's just so so nice! I mean, Pretty Baby was shot here! The aesthetic may still be Storyville bordello but all I could see around me was American Psycho. Not right. Not cool. Bring back the cheap whores! At least they dressed better. And most likely were not Republicans.

I can't imagine why the Columns Hotel has to be overrun with such a crowd. It pains me to write this review because I had such high hopes for it. I mean, the expansive front porch and side patio areas make for idyllic sipping of beverages. Should be a great place for a date, right? No. Not unless you're both under 25 and voting Romney.

I just want to scream, "Darling!" across the room to whomever is listening as I sit in this joint. So Moulin Rouge fabulous. So Zsa Zsa. So me.

I had a most incredible vegetarian crêpe here, the Provençale. Truth be told, there are a couple ingredients in ratatouille that I don't really love (bell peppers. onions), so I never order it, but I devoured this crêpe in 5 minutes or less. It's a light dinner. And it makes the wine taste even better. 

I look forward to regular appearances here. 

Note: they take closing time seriously. If you order right before the hour, be prepared for clean-up to occur as you sit (ie, don't linger). I am not complaining. We were the only table in there for over a half hour and I've worked in the service industry far too long to not understand.

Hoooray for Mojo's new location on Freret! Being that I'm a Downtown dweller these days, you may be wondering what I'm cheering about because realistically, at about a 15-30 min commute depending on traffic, it sure ain't gonna be my neighborhood coffee joint! I give Mojo's the honor of being a *destination coffee joint* 

Why?

-delicious iced coffee
-almond milk options
-accepts cards unlike the Magazine location
-has extremely nice staff (a note on the staff on Magazine: I've stopped going due to a certain male barista who made my drink wrong the last two times and when I corrected him, he didn't look at me, didn't say anything, merely dumped my coffee down the drain and sullenly made me a new one. Call me neurotic but once I think a barista hates me, I never return to a coffee shop. I'm seriously a nice person who always tips, I swear!)
-TONS of outlets
-plenty of seating
-spacious
-lots of natural light
-clean, amazing bathrooms
-delectable-lookin' baked goods that I understand are as good as they look

Really, it's everything I need in a coffee shop. WTG MOJO!!!

I had a po' boy as big as my ARM yesterday, for serious. That is, it was placed in front of me and then I ate half. These things are ridiculous... stuffed with stuff.  I opted for fried green tomatoes because I love 'em (maybe even slightly obsessed) and I'm a vegetarian (there are a couple options for us). It comes piled with whatever you choose and if you get it dressed, it'll come loaded with lettuce, tomato and... PICKLES. Holy crap. 

Nothin' po about these boys. Not a damn thing. Pricey, but could possibly fill you up for the entire day, depending.

It's not like I want to write this review update, but with so many check-ins and so many sub par experiences lately, I feel like I can't keep up a five star review or people won't trust me anymore. 

Take this as you will, for I used to really dig most of the staff here and even the ones that weren't as kick ass were at least nice. My visits lately have been pretty lackluster or downright bad. Last week, I almost threw out a lukewarm iced coffee with almond milk that was all separated and gross looking (this is purely aesthetic, though-- the milk is not actually bad when this happens)... I should have handed it back, but I didn't want to rock the boat after my guy had the audacity to ask for an espresso milkshake. "WHO ORDERS THAT?" I've said to him before. He's like, "someone does, it's on the menu" but still. Ok, fine, order the milkshake. And when he did, I braced myself, because I knew what the response would be. "That's going to take 10 minutes," in not the nicest tone. I mean, it was clear the chick didn't want to make it. I would have said forget it, but this inspired him to take her up on the 10 minute milk shake challenge (sigh). 

Look, I used to have this job. I used to be a grouchy barista at times, too and I regret it. I probably shouldn't have been working on those days where I was coming to work straight from another job and the last thing I wanted to do was throw anything in a blender. I admit it! I've learned from my mistakes, though. I've spent years waiting tables, making coffee and bartending. We can't always be shiny happy people for the masses.

But it's not an isolated incident and so, I'm not going back. There are too many other coffee shops where I don't feel like I'm a nuisance when I"m walking through the door. Especially when two coffee drinks with tip amounts to about 10 dollars. I'm fine with spending that when I'm not brewing at home, but I don't want to deal with grumpiness on top of that.

Since my last visit, Graze changed their menu a bit, so an update is warranted! With much enthusiasm, I bring tidings of food joy.

I'm going to start not with how I started the meal, but how I ended it. Because see that photo of the tiramisu there? It doesn't do it justice (and I think it's quite lovely, don't get me wrong). I'm not sure my *words* can do this majestic concoction justice. Here I thought the best vegan tiramisu to be had was at NYC's Blossom, but nope. Graze has Blossom beat. It's an enormous piece of wonder and should probably be shared, but heed my advice, you will not want to share. The cake is moist. The cream is the most dairy-like non dairy cream I've ever had. The flavor would have Jesus weeping. I'm a little out of breath here. It's a marriage of chocolate and espresso flavored manna from Heaven. End scene.

Before that, I had the seitan steak and I don't know how they do it, but the seitan is prepared so that you feel like you're eating a well done cut of steak. It's slightly charred on the outside, chewy on the inside and has incredible flavor. Some places just get seitan all wrong and when it's wrong, it's oh so sadly wrong. Inedible, in fact. I love that this plate comes with just the right amount of mashed potatoes, gravy, and salad + steamed broccoli too.  Perfection! 

And to start... the chickpea cakes with Bay seasoning. The flavor is good, but the inside of the cake is a little too ponderous (let's just say a mushy texture) and overall, they might benefit from being a thinner cake so that they are more crispy. I prefer the hot tempeh that they used to have, but it's not like I'd throw these off the table or anything. 

I'd happily graze here all night, every night if I could! Leftovers the next day were just as divine and I hate leftovers!

I'll be honest. I hate buffets. I despise the concept with every ounce of my being. I can write an entire diatribe on the evils of buffets, but that wouldn't be appropriate here. With that in mind, I bring you my review for Panda Garden. By the way, I understand that on weekends they have dim sum and a nice restaurant offering up fine dining to the side. I'd like to go back and try that.

In light of the fact that I don't eat meat, this review is a bit skewed. If you do eat meat, you will be happy to see that there's tons of it. If you are trying to eat healthy, there is the hibachi option with calamari, chicken, shrimp and red meats that I can't remember. At lunch, it's insanely cheap (with tax, our bill came to about 18 bucks).

Although I was tempted to try Tan Dinh for lunch while stopping at the amazing Hong Kong Market, I really just wanted a pile of steamed veggies and figured that would be easier to find at a Chinese restaurant, so here we landed. My friend, on a similar mission, although she eats meat, too, was pretty happy to see they have a hibachi grill. I didn't realize at first that this meant you can pick your protein and a ton of fresh vegetables and have them make it to order, thereby allowing you to skip the scores of unhealthy trays of grease and sugar-laden "Chinese" favorites.  Once I did, I was hopeful. Until I took a bite and it was clear that they put sugar in the sauce they cook it with. I could not eat it and ended up wasting an entire plate of vegetables. So it goes with buffets. Waste or eating to excess. What are you going to do? Next time, I'll just say no sauce and it should be fine. I actually think I will go back now that I know I'm not limited to one tray of (actually really good) crispy Chinese broccoli in sesame oil and one tray of extremely overcooked "steamed" vegetables (steamed, my ass! I know I saw some kind of oil lurking around in there). 

What else? There is sushi (rolls only) and I was pretty happy to see an avocado cucumber roll on there-- my favorite. It's not bad, either. Seaweed salad too (sadly, it contains imitation crab in it. Ick). A huge salad bar. Chinese donuts and other interesting-looking desserts that I didn't try. Soft serve ice cream. Oh and my favorite thing had to be the condiment area where they had a bunch of different hot sauces (chili oil! Sambal!). 

And then of course, there's the entire row of fried horrors. I'm sorry, but fried food in Chinese restaurants seems more disgusting than anywhere else. I remember as a kid thinking that even the french fries tasted like egg rolls. But this is "Chinese" food only in the Western world. Make it stop!

I've been a longtime fan of Surrey's Café Uptown (healthy, hearty breakfast, brunch and lunch!) and just recently made a visit to this location. It's a lot smaller and there's no outdoor seating, so it helps to not arrive fiending for food first thing because you're probably going to wait. It's worth the wait... but... We arrived about an hour before closing, which I hate to tell you is the best time to go, but there it is.

What I prefer about this location is that the staff is awesomely prompt, attentive and just plain nice. I haven't been to the Uptown location in over a year, but I do recall feeling service left a bit to be desired. That said, the food is just so damn good that I really didn't care at all about that. The food at this Surrey's is just as good as Uptown. I had the special juice of the day, The Sweet Cuban (apple, kale, cucumber, celery, cilantro, ginger) and it tasted amazing. Not to mention, it's very fairly priced. Juice can often be hella $$ (just the other day I paid 10 bucks for 16 ounces elsewhere which, I'm sorry, is crazy).

The tofu breakfast with sautéed vegetables is SOLID! It comes over rice, but I substituted grits because 1. I love grits about 10x more than rice and 2. Surrey's grits are amazingly rich and delicious. Just a note that I'm pretty sure their grits ain't vegan because only butter, maybe even a touch of cream, can turn grits into breakfast decadence. Wow, seriously. It's breakfast time right now and I'm craving my half healthy, half richly divine concoction, but sadly I'm about 800 miles away, so no Surrey's tofu and grits for me. Thanks for the memories...

Six years without an update on Slice? That's just not right.

I was a longtime fan of their Uptown Magazine St. location because it's larger and typically more convenient to park, but that's now a Juan's (same restaurant group) and I've been coming to this location on St Charles a lot recently.

There's a dedicated vegan option (Sicily Ana), which features spicy sauce, Kalamata olives, capers (mmmm all that saltiness), eggplant and arugula. Easily the healthiest slice you're going to get in NOLA! I may be crucified for this, but I prefer this vegan slice to any vegan slice offered by the pricier Pizza Delicious. 

What would make this next level awesome? A couple more vegan slice options, perhaps one with vegan cheese. Daiya is acceptable, but it's so easy and cheap to make a cashew cheese or even tofu ricotta that I'm surprised more places don't just do this, given the increasing number of vegans or average health-conscious people (to say nothing of all those folks who are allergic to dairy). 

Just a tiny suggestion that I feel is worth mentioning. In the meantime, of course, I'm happy with the Sicily Ana and I always have to note my appreciation for their wine list (Chianti and Prosecco!) and fun cocktail list that typically has some type of frozen offering.

And of course, their staff couldn't be nicer!

Being a diehard Bacchanal fan, it has taken me several years to go outside my comfort zone and visit Bayou Wine Garden and damn, what took me so long? This place is pretty spectacular!

One of the best elements is the fact that you have the best of both worlds here. My guy is a beer drinker; I don't touch the stuff. While I enjoy the occasional cocktail, I am a diehard wine drinker. The solution is here. We entered through Bayou Beer Garden, where he got a pint of some kind of pilsner and then we walked through the gardens with outdoor bar (you'll never go thirsty here) + BBG's typical bar food offerings and huge screens showing March Madness stuff over through Bayou Wine Garden's outdoor bar and fairy-lit paradise complete with a huge fountain onto the porch where we grabbed a seat and I went inside the former shotgun home turned  to glimpse the wine list. There are a good selection of $5 glasses, including a sparkling rosé. WTH? Was I dreaming? They also have different wines on tap inside and out. And a selection of small plates. Inside is dark, charming and cozy and if it wasn't such a gorgeous evening, I would have sat inside.

We had a glorious time here. At first the game night crowds were a little off-putting, but given what was going on last night, it was pretty tame, overall friendly and welcoming. Sometimes, you just have to get over yourself, right? Also, we ran into a friend. I think this is that kind of place where you're bound to run into someone you know. It's a good thing.

So, I love Bayou Wine Garden. I just wish (here it comes) that there could be a vegan option on the menu, something similar to Mimi's (or Effervescence or Bacchanal), but there's nothing besides olives. I'll just keep it to wine drinking and I'm OK with that. But the potential for edibles would keep me drinking here longer!

Let me start off by saying I love Saint Louis. Lovely city. Really great food, bars, architecture, etc. And, you know, it has several things that Kansas City does not. An internationally recognized and iconic landmark/symbol. A baseball team that locals are proud of and adore. A subway. An authentic Little Italy neighborhood. Benson. Nelly...

But its historical landmark "train station"... has no trains! WTF? 

I've traveled a fair portion of the world and cities' train stations all have trains in them, so silly me for making such an outlandish assumption when attempting to take Amtrak home yesterday. It boggles my mind that St. Louis' train station is instead something that is trying to be a mall.

This would be fine, really. If only they would warn idiot visitors like me. Like, with signs pointing out that you will not find Amtrak here, but several blocks away, tucked back by the highway underpass that is a long walk (and nearly impossible to find). What's more? Not one employee in Union "Station" (more like a sad mall) could help point me in the direction of where one might find an actual train. Today, I found information booth so that I could get a cab to take me the hell out of there, so that was nice.

See, I missed my train yesterday, after frantically running all over this lame excuse for a mall that has maps and signs for the shops and food courts (all of them really quite sad and deserted... not one decent coffee shop to be found, not even Starbucks), but not ONE SIGN FOR WHERE ONE MIGHT FIND TRAINS IN THE TRAIN STATION!!!

That's right. And like I said, everyone looked at me like I had a second head when I asked where the trains were. One "transit" worker (that's what his jacket indicated) outside by the commuter rail barely grunted at me and pointed in the vague vicinity of where the small Amtrak/Greyhound station actually exists.

Before I could make it there, I had to drop my fifty pound bag and decompress by the highway underpass. At that point, I was approached by a fatherly type asking me basically WTF I was doing standing on a corner practically crying because by then I had missed the last train back to KC. Then there was the red mini van that kept slowly following me. How Christiane F can you get? 

I really don't know what the point of Union Station in Saint Louis is, besides a pathetic excuse for a tourist attraction for Marriott guests in the attached hotel. And next time I hear anyone complain about Kansas City's far superior Union Station, which is not only a gorgeous structure that makes you feel like you're stepping back in time, but is an operating train station, I'm going to virtually slap them.

And someone really needs to reevaluate the "transportation" description above in the Yelp listing.

Sometimes, you want to feel like a bambino again, and props to La Divnia Gelateria for making this a possibility.

My friend noted that another joint in town won't allow us "grown ups" to order anything smaller than a "small," and let's be real, is there anything akin to an actual size "small"  these days? Y'know, some of us prefer to eat a smaller amount of something that consists mainly of heavy cream and sugar, especially if you have health issues that don't permit it. 

Although you can go to the website and see this information, I'm going to draw attention to it here, anyway (also to highlight the incredibly reasonable prices!):

Bambino  2 oz. 2.00
Piccolo  4 oz. 3.75
Medio  6 oz. 4.85
Grande  8 oz. 

Onto the more delicious information. The flavors! They do vary according to what's in season, but the other night I had a free taste of the sour cherry. This small spoonful resulted in intense flavor epiphanies in my mouth, brain and possibly my soul. Yes, expect the ecstasy to last beyond the spoonful.

Really, does not one need more than 2 oz of this? You know what they say about too much of a good thing...

In the *spirit* of Tales of the Cocktail, the time has come for me to at long last review Arnaud's French 75 after several visits. 

It won't come as any surprise to any of you that I'm going to mention that this place is really just perfect as they come. Let's review what I love most about a cocktail bar:

-swanky surroundings (check)
-expertly mixed cocktails (check)
-expertly mixed *classics* (check)

add on incredibly affordable prices for those expertly mixed cocktails and swanky surroundings and you've got the 5th star.

Chris Hannah and his compadres behind the bar are a class act. You already knew that. It stands repeating. 

The whole operation conjures up the sophistication of the King Cole Room in the St. Regis sans the snooty NY East Side 'tude. Well, this is New Orleans and there is no place for that! Come as you are and thrill in the vibe... it's a friendly place, too.

What is the core of delicious Pho?
Broth.

And this place gets it right.
Now, everything else was ok too--veggies and noodles.
Fresh toppings and sauces rounded off the meal.

Solid place for pho.

I have always enjoyed Ciccio in St. Pete, so I was excited to see one in Riverview.

Always love the clean, fun, bright atmosphere.
Brightly colored vegetable items with SO much flavor and ridiculous portion sizes.

This location has great outside seating, perfect for brunch, and sometimes even live music.

Ciccio is positioned close to several popular places, so I don't think parking on the grass would be unusual.

Great pride in the cooking done here.
It shows in presentation and flavor.
Really great portion sizes and prices as well.
Well done!

So very disappointed!
I ordered massaman tofu curry to go. 

The experience was pleasant over the phone--I was told detailed information about the dishes to make sure my order was correct.

My food was ready when I arrived. 
The fresh rolls and sauce was perfect.

The flavor and texture of the curry was also perfect!
What really killed the dish was potatoes that were not fully cooked.  The first bite of potato was hard in the middle, and barely chewable.  I thought it was just an outlier, but all the other potatoes in the dish were the same.  
 
I was so looking forward to perfectly cooked potatoes with the amazing curry, but that did not happen.   The potatoes are what I especially enjoy with this dish! 

Such a shame too, because if the potatoes were fully cooked, the dish would have been perfect!

So, here's the thing.

Once you visit an exceptional WF, (Clearwater, Davie in FLL, Orlando-Dr. Phillips, Altamonte Springs for example)  all others are held to that standard.

And when a WF is ok, totally acceptable, but not exceptional, it falls short.

And that's what is happening here.

It's clean, the people are friendly, selection is nice.
If I ever have a problem with WF, it's the inconsistent food bars.

This location:
Selection is very small.
Seems as if it has stayed out too long.

I'm sure consistency is a nightmare for those managing stores. 

Space size varies.
Number of customers vary-- hard to gauge how much to prepare without wasting.
Regional influences vary (hamburger mac n cheese on the food bar in Jacksonville and not in other WF. . .I pray never again in a WF).

I'm sure it's complicated to get it right, and I do appreciate how challenging it must be, but disappointing nonetheless for WF regulars.

Went for breakfast and dinner -- simply amazing. For breakfast, my house-baked croissant with a perfectly fried egg, gruyere cheese, jambon de paris (ham), and arugula was breakfast excellence.

My noodle bowl with duck was absolutely delicious as well for dinner. One of my friends got the Asian-style Beef Stew which may have been the best thing on the table, it was that good.

One thing to note is their wine list -- a great eclectic selection with amazing prices.  Their wines by the bottle seem to be priced with a retail markup, not the usual restaurant-gouging price.  Some fabulous finds on this list -- try the Sancerre it absolutely sings with the food here.

And yes, the prices here are ridiculously cheap, for such well-made, thoughtfully-prepared food.  My noodle bowl was one of the most expensive things on the menu at just 9 dollars. For dinner. 

Keep in mind this is not a "Vietnamese" restaurant -- on the menu it notes that it is a fusion of the three owner's backgrounds, French, Vietnamese and Chinese.

11/24/17

Just a stand at the open market.  They have basic breakfasts and sandwiches, and some Greek salads.  Nothing particularly interesting here except that they spell Muffuletta 2 different ways here (menu is Muffuletta, but a sign in front says "Muffaletta 3 Meats 2 Cheeses, House Made Olive Salad").

Oh, yeah, I've had the Central Grocery (supposedly the inventor of this famous New Orleans sandwich).  Unfortunately I can't remember much about it, given I tasted it like 5 years ago, except that it was hella dry and it's a death sentence if you try to slam it down your throat without some drinks nearby.  But I guess that's the traditional way to make this sandwich.

1. Muffuletta 1/4 $5.44, 1/2 $9.06:  So, not much different here either.  Quite basic.  You got that dry bread, Italian meats, cheese, and "olive salad."  If you made it at home, this would be how it would taste.  Somewhat expensive for what they give you.  5/10

Have a nice day!

We needed breakfast and this place was one of the few open so early, and was really close to our hotel in the French Quarters.  Otherwise, honestly, it's quite unremarkable.  Well, I do want to say thought that our server was really great to us and even took time to teach us the wonders of Crystal, which she believed was better in Tobasco because of the lack of a lingering taste (though as a foodie I'd personally want as long of a lingering taste of everything as possible, but to each his/her own.)

1. Coffee $2.50

2. Orange Juice Large $4.50

3. Eggs Stella $18.50 "cornmeal-crusted soft-shell crab, poached eggs, Canadian bacon, and hollandaise on toasted English muffin":  Soft shell crab eggs benedict?--sounds amazing to me! We actually saved what we thought would be one of the best meals for very last.  On the very last day, last hour even!, on the way to the airport we jumped outta the Uber, luggage and all, and took our place in the line stretching out the side of the building.  It was actually already 2pm on a Mon, so I can only imagine how ridiculous the line would be at peak hours.

Anyway... what we THOUGHT would be one of the best meals... was really actually totally disappointing.  Can't come to the South and not get real Southen Fried Chicken right?--well, sadly, this place embodied the opposite of what I thought a famous and well loved Southern restaurant would be like, which was totally different than all the other meals we've had in New Orleans previously...

One.  Our waitress was rude to my gf.  She first ordered fried veal, to which the waitress sternly said, "No, we're out."  Then she asked for lemonade.  Curtly, "No, out."  Like seriously?--you're out of lemonade?  All of this with a frown, as if it were my gf's fault for even asking.

Two.  As I was walking through the restaurant I had to get out of the way of all the bus boys and waiters.  At one point a waiter walked towards me food in hand and I moved aside for him to pass, then he stopped right in front of me and turned around to chat with another waiter.  Yes, while I stood there like an idiot.

Three.  The bus boys gave us our neighbor's dish.  Then later, the waitress gave our check to our neighbor.  Wtf.

FOUR...  The waitress came over and knocked my glass of Coke over and it spilled all over our neighbor.  After she stood there for a little bit, she kinda half assed an apology then made some joke that I couldn't remember.  Then finally asked if the dude wanted some napkins to clean himself up.  Um... YES HE WANTS SOMETHING to mop up all the black liquid you spilled on him!!!  And....... get this: she didn't refill my Coke that she emptied.  W haaat T hheeee FFFFFFFFFFF???????

AND LAAAASTLY....  After I signed the bill and tipped, the waitress came over and took it.  I've only ever had that happen at Asian restaurants.  Never in an "American" place--pretty damn rude if you ask me.

And then there's the food...

1. Diet Coke $2.50

2. Cornbread Muffins $0.75 (I know it says "muffins" but they really mean $0.75 each):  Pretty basic cornbread.  Not all that moist.  Pretty dense.  Not bad, but not what I expected of such a highly praised restaurant either.  4/10

3. Fried Okra $5.00:  Very very very standard.  Cornmeal crust.  Small bites.  The okra was actually a tad old and dry.  4/10

4. Fried Chicken Mixed $10.00 "3 pcs. mixed served with your choice of one side":  So here's the deal--the meat itself is DRY AS HELL.  Both the white and dark meat.  Seriously, they can't even touch KFC on juiciness, let alone Costco chicken.  BUT, ....

BUUUUT....... HOLY MUTHA OF FRIED FOOD GODS!!!!!.... the batter is OUT OF THIS DAMN WORLD!  I've NEVER had batter this good at any traditional American fried chicken place.  The only restaurants with batter like this would be the best of the Korean Fried Chicken places.  And even then, I might be inclined to say the batter here is the Best I've Ever Had, other than what my gf makes at home.  Soooooo AIRY and CRISP.  It was like eating FRIED AIR!!!  Event the bits of raw batter was creamy and delicious!  Pretty spicy even.  Man.....

So I have no clue how to score this.  The meat was like 3/10, but the batter +++10/10.... you decide...

5. Red Velvet Cake $7.00:  Soooo, I would totally have given this restaurant 2/5 stars but well, this cake was so amazing that I guess combined with the epic chicken batter... sure, I'll give them one more star.  Yeah, this Red Velvet Cake........ top 2 I've ever had for sure.  The only other one I liked as much was the Blue Velvet Cake from Milk in SoCal.  It was soooo moist that you can see the bread bleeding juice!  And so sweet and creamy, both the cake and the frosting.  Man, it was so packed with moisture the surface glistened like dew on morning grass sparkling under the rising sun.  EPIC.  10/10

So........ not counting the food, our experience was just utter crap.

But food-wise, mostly substandard except absolutely divine Red Velvet Cake and chicken batter... so ridiculously good I think this palace is a must-try, so resurrected from the dead...

11/25/17

The courtyard dining area is something out of fairy tales at night!  Lit by glistening lights you'd pass the water fountain and plenty of pretty green plants and flowers before reaching the host.  It reminded me of the amazing meals we had in France, served among the sumptuous gardens.

There's even a beautiful singer outside the walls singing the most enchanting and romantic music!  I do not think she's an employee but wow, the music was otherworldly!  Unfortunately, once we got seated the house music of rock and roll somewhat drowned her out and was far less romantic.

We walked along the red bricked cobblestone to our wrought iron table...

1. Junta Superior $12 "Fortaleza blanco tequila, ancho verde chili liqueur, lillet, lime, pineapple habanero syrup":  Delicious!  It is as you would imagine with so many ingredients suggesting spice and heat.  Definitely has a kick but this spicy lemon drink is perfectly balanced, though that heat totally builds after sip after sip.  Loved it!  9/10

2. Glass of Kessler $9

3. Chicken and Andouille Gumbo $8:  Ultra salty, but otherwise thick and flavorful.  I also liked the big pieces of andouille sausage.  7/10

4. Cajun Country Poutine $10 "oven fries, mozzarella and cochon":  I think this was actually better than the real Canadian poutine we had in Canada!  Now... unfortunately some of the fries were significantly burnt.  But there was tons of flavor packed in.  The chicken was very dry though and again, it was ultra salty.  7/10

5. Oven Roasted Double-Cut Pork Chop $27 "over creamy old mill grits and green beans":  Well, I think if you follow my reviews you know what I am about to say:..... that's right.  It was DRY DRY DRY.  Why the F do chefs not test their pork chop recipes???  I really don't get it.  It ain't that hard.  When my gf makes it at home it's perfect.  These are pros right?  Get this--I even told the waiter to make sure it ain't dry!  He said it'll be cooked medium, but clearly it was super well done!  It was a shame cause it had great flavor and the grits were yummy.  Sadly... 3/10

6. Shrimp Cafe Pasta Special $26:  The pasta was overcooked, but still acceptable.  The sauce was spicy, kinda like a Cajun marinara.  The shrimp was just okay.  6/10

7. Rekorderlig Strawberry Lime Cider $5 "Sweden, 12 oz can 4.5% ABV":  Like a wine cooler heavy on strawberry.  Very smooth.  I'd say for what it is... 8/10

8. Illy Decaf Americano $4

9. Carlos VII Amontillado Sherry $9:  Very much like PX.  Plenty of raisins, but tastes light.  Very viscous with a very strong caramel taste.  Actually goes well with the super sweet cake, bringing out the citrus notes.  9/10

10. Doberge Cake $10 "thin cake layers with dessert pudding":  GODDAM.  Out of this world!  Loads of almond flavor in the crust.  Tons of caramel flavor.  And that salt on top just finishes it all perfectly.  The best kind of sin!  10/10

I loved eating in the gardens.  Unfortunately the food wasn't as great as the surroundings.  But still, if you want a special dinner without spending too much to get those love juices flowing, this would be a good choice.

4/5

If I were a rich man a very very very rich man, I would be giving it more stars.
To build a burger, looks simple but, the but is, it all adds up.  So the double graze burger with cheese $9.75,(not bad) oh yeah going grass $2.00 feed, bacon $1.25, add fries and drink $4.00 = $18.36 for a burger fries and a drink. 
This is not a restaurant for sitting and conversing, this is a side step from Whataburger.  So while I really liked it, I am going to slow it down in the future with all the bells and whistles. Oh yeah I forgot the couple of bucks I threw into the tip jar $20.36 for a 20 to 25 minute burger.

And the veggie pho is delicious...in case you were wondering, as is the spicy tofu appetizer.  

I've also tried their grilled shrimp items and YUMMY.  Love that the place is so low key and that you are greeted like you've just arrived at your favorite aunt's house.

Great new space in a pretty ordinary strip mall. The inside makes you think upscale tavern (even though they don't have a liquor license yet). The menu was broad enough to have a little something for everyone but small enough to do each item well.

I couldn't resist the fish of the day which was sheepshead with a succotash underneath and some citrus/fennel salad on top. DELICIOUS...but a bit pricey for lunch at $16. My coworkers each got a burger and fries and enjoyed them. We started with fried pickles which were OK but not great. I think the pickle to batter ratio was off.

The staff was lovely and the service was good. I'll definitely be back to sample that pimento grilled cheese.

I checked out this sushi joint because it was the 2nd closest to my brother's house (the closest served me fish the wrong color last time) and because Naomi P recommended it.

Naomi did not steer me wrong. The location is a bit difficult but they do have 2 reserved parking spots in front of the restaurant.  I tried a variety of rolls and everything was top notch.  The little nieces enjoyed the shrimp fried rice and I even got them to eat some of the cooked rolls.  My cucumber salad was delish and the noodle salad was also tasty...and not as mayonaissey as it is other places.  The server was also great to the little ones, even making them custom starter chopsticks.

The rainbow roll was smaller (and didn't use spicy crab) then I've had in other places, but the fish was beautifully interwoven.  Definitely worth checking out.

Y'all they have this veggie wrap that is AMAZING. Filling and delicious and the mushrooms are sauteed with something nice and fire-y so there's some heat.

I've dined in once and then picked up takeout another time (lunchtime). And both times the food was speedy both times. By the way their french fries are addictive. The only problem with calling in my order is that I don't know what the daily special is and they often sound delicious. My fellow diners have had the burger and the lemongrass chicken wrap which also got raves. 

I need to pass by after work for a cocktail and some dinner soon. And I need to try their tots. Definitely in the regular work rotation.

So like a silly girl, I started drinking at 3 pm and ate a few snacks and was STARVING. My time was limited and I had to pick up the lovely Lindsay A. I started yelping for a nearby foodtruck and instead saw Kukhnya which I've been wanting to go to for months. Last time I stopped by they were closed. So I crossed my fingers and prayed to the Slavic Mary and YAY!

I ordered the pierogies and an asparagus polboy (for me and Miss Lindsay). OMG delicious. Seriously those pickled onions on the sammich were AMAZING, sliced thin  and piled on... It ended up being so much food that Joi was gifted 1/2 of our polboy.  

Definitely will be back soon.I can't wait to have my Polish co-worker experience the yumminess...plus there's the entertainment in seeing her inside Siberia.

Wow! Since Harahan is part of my old stomping grounds, I kidnapped Lindsay and we stopped in for dinner to celebrate St. Joseph's day.  And I ordered all the foods because the menu looked so amazing.

I started with the caesar salad which was yummy and very garlicy, in a good way. Then had a seafood antipasto dish which was also delicious but small for the $11...but I get it because the seafood was amazing. THEN the verdure pizza and after the first bite I was all "this olive oil is amazing" and Lindsay thought I had lost my mind until she took a bite and said the same thing. THEN I had the pasta parpardelle  (I'm sure I'm spelling that wrong) which was also delicious and now I need to learn to make homemade past because...oh so good.  

Yep, it's an old Popeye's where one of my HS besties worked. And the space is small but they've done a good job making it clean and elegant. The night I was there it wasn't too noisy but I could see how it could get loud. Our service was fine...attentive to distracted depending on the tables around us. I'll definitely be trekking out here again and am recommending it to all my friends in the area.

Interesting place. It's not really a traditional sushi restaurant.  But more of an Asian restaurant that also sells sushi.  Very important items to note it has INARI which is really hard to comeby in NOLA and I love it.  It also has a vegetarian sushi or sashimi plate which is again rare. 

We had the specialty strawberry something roll and while I was hesitant, it was delicious. Another standout was the dessert tempura blueberry something. So tasty

The specialty cocktail menu was interesting and they had a good selection of high end sakes.

The service is still uneven but it's a new restaurant. I did feel the staff was trying...just confused.

I had a big bunch of limits from various family members for Easter Sunday lunch and the Peppermill fit the bill. We made reservations (a must for a busy day like Easter) a few days before and were seated promptly. Easter had a limited menu but there were easily enough selections to keep us all happy. 

Sundays have the dinner menu at lunch time which is really appropriate since this is a *very* old school restaurant. Old but solid. All 5 of us were very pleased with our meals. I loved that the salad dressing are made in house. And we had the veal with seafood, the redfish almondine and the stuffed crabs. We didn't peruse the wine list or order drinks so not really sure about that.

This spot does offer 3 meals a day so that's unusual for an independent spot and my brother has been here for breakfast meetings and says the food is good. 

We also sampled the desserts; a carrot cake - cheesecake, caramel custard and lemon meringue pie. All were delicious.

The server was on point. The food came out quickly and the tables turned over quickly, despite that we were in a room with a table set up for groups of 20.

Some friends and I were just talking about Adolfo's, their nephew had just discovered the restaurant and was raving...my friend announced that it was where she went with her husband on their first date 20+ years ago. So definitely staying power.

I used to go to Adolfo's all the time and it's still delicious. The restaurant is tight so don't bring your giant purse (or suitcase) here. Also it's easier to get seated with a smaller party.  The service has always been a bit hit or miss. They actually have a liquor license now so you can get a drink without walking downstairs to the bar like we had to back in the 90s. 

I usually get the Canneloni and the tomato cream sauce is my favorite. Most of the folks at my table got fish specials last Thursday and they looked tasty too. However we had to wait for over an hour and that's just a nope from me. But it's what my out of town friends wanted. 

The building.... it could use some love. The whole place is extra NOLA grungy so be aware if that is going to be an issue for you. The cash only thing is weird since this is not the cheapest place to eat... of course, they have an ATM in case you didn't know which charges beaucoup fees. 

As for the block, whew it was a disaster early on a Thursday night. I hadn't been down to this part of Frenchmen and in awhile and I have to admit I preferred it before. #getoffmylawn

I was lucky enough to dine at Trinity for a friend's birthday a couple of weeks back and the entire staff made our table feel like VIPs! Multiple staff members greeted us and wished my friend a happy birthday. The bartender came up with a custom cocktail for her based on her clearly defined likes & dislikes. She liked it so much she had 2!

And the food OMG. The food. We started with the baked oysters trinity. And they were amazing, each flavoring complementing but so different than the one before. We then split a couple of appetizers among the 3 of us...I know one was the ricotta gnudi. So different from what I was expecting but super tasty. Then the 3 of us split the vegetarian polenta dish and the linguine seafood dish. OMG they were both simply amazing. Really really delicious.  Did I mention that the bread was simply amazing too? It's made by the inhouse pastry chef. I tried to hoard all of it but I friends made me share. 

After our meal, our birthday girl had bread pudding with a candle in it... At this point I thought I might explode. So of course, we ended up concluding with small glasses of port. 

The staff was on point and super helpful and patient with our birthday silliness. The renovation is gorgeous!!! I have not eaten in this space since the 90s and I cannot believe it's the same place. So light and gorgeous and yes, still an open kitchen. 

Definitely a great spot for a special occasion or just because you deserve some delicious food. Now I want to stop by on a regular night for a cocktail and app...

Um yum! When you're hungry but you want to be healthy, this is the perfect spot. 

It's an assembly line and you decide exactly what you want in your bowl. Hate cilantro, skip it. Love macadamia nuts, yep you can have those. Just beware that a few ingredients are an extra cost, avocado, crab salad and, of course and extra scoop of your protein.

I wasn't big on the spicy tuna (but then again I never am) and I thought the tofu could have more flavor. That's right, tofu so you can definitely have a vegetarian meal here. 

The space is light and airy but I usually get my bowl to go. Staff is friendly and efficient. And OMG the watermelon agua fresca is delicious!

Bacchanal really is a lovely slightly bohemian place to share a bottle of wine and chat with friends. Yes the mosquitos are ridiculous and it is nice that there are bottles of bug spray scattered about...but how about hanging some sort of deterrent devices around the perimeter? I would love to see an old school purple bug zapper. (Do they even make those anymore?)

The wine selection is good and the food is tasty and diverse.  I'm also grateful for the diversity of non-alcoholic beverages that can be purchased for the non-drinker/underaged patron.

My only other bit advice is be careful with some of the chairs which are perhaps not as sturdy as one would like, even for the slightly built.

Um so it can't be called Camellia Grill because of a contract dispute with the original owners, but the decor, the menu, the staff, it's all Camellia.

The food is the same as the original uptown location which is reliable diner food. In the past month, I've had a tuna salad sandwich (and stole fries from a friend) and then a late night pecan waffle...although they did break my heart by not having cane syrup to go with the waffle. C'mon people.

The chocolate freeze is still delicious and, yes, I gave myself a headache. Plus points for excellent ice in their ice teas & cokes.

Long overdue review: The combo with the beer garden means that there is something for everyone at these sister establishments. The food is a bit more elevated on the wine garden side and the wines on tap or by the glass are numerous and tasty. If your companions want draft beer, then they just wander over the beer side and get that. Same for a basic burger.

On the wine side the menu is a bit fancier... and yummier in my opinion, their mac-n-cheese is tasty (currently artichoke and spinach but I've had crawfish before too) as are the stupidly addictive garlic-parm fries. The roasted cauliflower side is delicious. The only miss for me has been the fried avocado taco. But I think I'm just not a fan of that preparation. Live and learn.

The happy hour prices for wine, sangria, beer and a couple of batched cocktails are quite reasonable and run until 6:30pm. Plus when it's warm out, there's usually frose! Just like the beer garden, there are 2 bars one inside (dark and sexy) and one outside (sort of like drinking at a cabana club). 

Small parking lot behind the outdoor area, but it fills up fast. The outdoor areas are dog friendly. And the private party space is available too.

Fun times and making everyone happy. I like it.

Came here for a late night snack because it was recommended by the locals. Ordered the things they were known for and have to say my only disappointment was the Mac and cheese, it was bland. Everything else was delicious. Those pub loaded fries were outstanding. Fries perfectly cooked with the right amount of sauce and meat - so good. The cheeseburger egg rolls served with the pickles on the side and this special sauce - taste like you are eating a real cheeseburger - I liked it! It was something I never had before. The tikka chicken masala was like eating at an Indian restaurant - they hit that one out of the park. I don't know if I would visit this place that late again, it was next to a wild pub and you can't use their restroom at night which is no bueno but kudos on the delicious food!

Haha...Yaaasss! Finally! One of those hipster spots where the food is actually good!! Very Eccentric place! The venue is actually much bigger than it looks from the outside. A very unusual venue; with a bar style seating area in the middle, flanked by booths on two sides, a small lounging area with a couple of TV's inside and a large open space to pick up orders. Then there is the outside; space for live music, along with a Ping Pong table and a Foosball table. 

Now onto the food:
- Shredded Chicken Nachos - 4.5/5: Yaaasss!! I got the Wed special, where it was like a $1 cheaper or something to that extent. Generous Portions, juicy white chicken meat with flavorful sauces, cheese & Cilantro. It just works! 
- House Brewed Ice Tea - 4/5: Good stuff! Unlike a few other places the Teas was not too sweet and I didn't have to dilute it with regular tea or water, I could actually drink it straight up.   
- Better Chicken Chili - 4.5/5: Perfect deliciousness!!! If I didn't know better, I'd have thought that they specialize in chili! Hearty, but not too heavy, tasty, but not too spicy...very well balanced.    
- Jalapeno Bacon Mac N Cheese - 4/5: Very tasty, the small side portion is hearty, don't let the little dinky cup fool you. It's not all that easy to put away if you are chowing down on other sides as well. 
- MacNByrd - 4.5/5: One of the juiciest chicken sandwiches I had the pleasure of devouring. I opted for the Buttermilk Fried Chicken. I was a bit skeptical about the Potato Bun, but it just works...delicious. 
- Last but not least, lets not forget the fresh made to order doughnuts. The doughnuts are small, with a delicate balance of doughy on the inside and slightly crispy on the outside. The sauces and the toppings are what gives the doughnuts the desired flavor. IMHO they are a bit pricey, I'll skip these in the future. 

No...I am not a porker...OK well maybe I am...well I tend have an unusually large appetite...still, I didn't eat all this at once, this was over the course of a couple of visits. 

I'm starting to think the menu was crafted by someone who really knows what they are doing...somebody with a culinary background perhaps...BRAVO! On the plus side, nothing was disappointing. On the bad side, I now intend to try everything else on the menu! Especially at the listed price points. Great job Better Byrd! Need less to say...I'll be back!

I really really want to like...love this place.

This is one hipster spot...I'll give you that. the bar seems to be a very popular attraction. As far as I can tell, there is plenty of foot traffic that exclusively frequents the bar...plenty of patrons that come her just for a drink and don't actually eat here.

I found this place on Yelp and had some what high expectations based on the reviews. Sadly, they were not met. I came here to eat some Ramen. I ordered the Crispy duck Ramen. The entire bowl of Ramen was actually perfect...except for one tinsy winsy issue...well it's actually a very big issue. The broth was just bland, it had NO flavor, not something you could just drink by itself...it tasted like clear and flavourless stock of some kind. 

Unfortunately, the broth is an integral part of Ramen, you have to get that right. A good broth can make or break the reputation of Ramen Joint. Perhaps I'm just spoiled...coming from the West Coast, where Ramen joints are a dime a dozen and the fierce competition tends to bring out the best in all and the losers do not survive. Like I said the rest of the Ramen bowl was brilliant! The Crispy pieces of duck meat, although not all that generous in portions, they were perfectly done, Crispy on the outside, juicy and succulent on the inside. The noodles were also perfectly done, along with half the egg, mushrooms, shoots etc. 

I would let the broth pass, since the rest of Ramen was basically perfect, but then comes the price point. At $16 a bowl, this is one of the more expensive Ramen places I've visited anywhere, therefore value is a afterthought. If the flavor matched the price point, Buya Ramen would be an excellent spot to frequent on a regular basis. The service was excellent, my waitress was attentive and regularly checked up on me. 

Not so sure I would return...

So I found this place on Yelp...um duh! where else do you think I would look?! To nobody's surprise...of course it was fantastic! There is a reason this place has an incredible amount of good or great reviews. The food here was just brilliant.

This place quite popular and gets busy early, and stays busy...so come as early as possible in order to avoid the long wait. I was impressed by the techno savvy hosts & hostess that were running the place. They take your number and text you when your table is ready in addition to calling your name out loud. My friend and I got lucky, I think we waited for less than 15 minutes, while we were told it was going to be about 45 minutes. Maybe, because we were OK with sitting at the bar.  

So guess what...we sat at the bar and had the pleasure of being entertained by one of the bartenders; Jacob, real personable, genuine and helpful guy...apparently into fishing as well. 

To start I got a Bloody Mary Bacon. Excellent choice! One of the best Bloody Mary's I had! The  Bloody Mary mix is made in house, perfectly balanced...salty, spicy, tangy...pretty much how an excellent Bloody Mary should taste, topped with a piece of Bacon! BACON!!! 

I got the Gulf Fish 'St. Peter' - The fish of the day was a Big Red Drum also called  Channel Bass, Redfish, Spottail Bass, or simply Red (Information was from Jacob...free of charge). Its a local Atlantic fish, which happened to be exactly what I was looking for...something local. The Pan Seared Fish was excellent, light flakey perfectly complimented by the mustard sauce. I only wish the piece of fish was a bit more generous. Never had a Cheesy Grit cake before, this was something foreign to me...tasted like a lighter hash-brown, the inside was softer.

My buddy got the BBQ Shrimp & Grits. I got to sneak a taste of his dish. This was simply amazing...pretty much perfection! This is exactly how I pictured Shrimp & Grits in my head. Fresh local plump and juicy sautéed gulf shrimp with creamy flavorful grits! Yaassss! Even the buttermilk biscuit was delicious, light fluffy and full of flavor...bravo!  

Big fan of this place, I will endeavor to return here every time I visit NOLA

I really am unsure as how to proceed. How to relate to others the absolute disdain I have for this restaurant and especially the wife of the Owner. This woman is basically the "soup nazi" in pumps...
I have made reservations for every foray into this place and have tried to give them every benefit of the doubt. However, even though we had reservations for a particular time one evening, it was never written down and I even explained to her to whom I had spoken. It didn't matter; it was the middle of winter and she asked us to go outside and wait until she called us. Reluctantly, we did this and waited outside for 15 minutes and then just left. It happened again last night where I had called, made reservations and showed up on time. She treated us with pretension, condescension, and arrogance, so we left yet again. And in her passive aggressive way she was happy to say "goodbye"...mean girl syndrome.

The food in this establishment is good (if you like undercooked vegetables)but the setting is extremely problematic. The reception area is cluttered, crowded and virtually unworkable.
In addition, previously, on two separate occasions, we made our way to our table, our waiter came and gave us water and then disappeared. After about 25 minutes we complained and asked what happened to him. We were told"oh, he went home."
Basically, if you expect service and promptness in your waitstaff you're in the wrong place. However, if you enjoy a crowded,cluttered,chaotic environment where the owner thinks she's doing you a favor by letting you in...it should be a perfect experience.

We go to restaurants four times a week and over the course of many years in Tucson I've seen the same attitude with a number of other different restaurants who are no longer in business. I hope this will be the next one to go; it may take a little time but this attitude will catch up with them sooner or later.
The one bright spot for us and one of the reasons we kept coming back was because when things went right a girl name Amber was our waitress and she always did a good job.

Great food and "WOW" customer service!

So I was very honored to receive an invitation from Dave Fuller, the director of service excellence at the Peppermill Resort Spa Casino, to come back in and give Oceano another opportunity to show us a quality dining experience! 

At the hostess station, we were being greeted with a genuine smile by the beautiful host Rosa! After she walked us to the sushi bar, the sweet Katie Duran, the Manager, came to us, apologized for our poor experience and introduced us to Chef Russell! She was kind enough to offer us some wine but we were fine with the water. 

Chef Russell wanted to make sure to show us his love for sushi and how he is passionate about it so he started by asking us about our favorite fish! Brilliant start! Then, he kept impressing us with his special unique sushi combinations, creative rolls and classic nigiri! Each piece of flavorful fresh fish cut was laid out very beautifully! He really knows how to serve the right texture and the exotic flavors that go with it which totally satisfied our sushi craving! 

Our server was a fantastic young man! He came and very politely introduced himself to us when he took our order. Bummer, I can't remember his name. He kept checking on us to see if everything is OK and to make sure our water were full in a timely basis. Then, he topped it off with lemon hot towels to freshen up at the end of the meal!! 

We were pleasantly satisfied with both the quality and the quantity of our meal! The hospitality and the service were on point! Thank you Oceano! We really appreciate such a great dining experience!

What do you think of when you hear the words "Mediterranean - Middle Eastern Food"?

Huge portions of fresh, rich and aromatic food with unique flavors....Yah vast array of SPICES and HERBS!! From staples like cumin, coriander, turmeric, Nutmeg, Sumac and mint to exotic blends like Bharat and Za'atar. 

As a start of my homework, I posted asking about Naan & Kabab in Reno Foodies group on FB and had a tons of good thoughts, so of course I went back to Yelpers! I was amazed by some well-rounded Yelpers and their true appreciation of ethnic cuisines from different countries around the world. However, knowing Tariq K personally and his cultural background made me consider his review.

Our 1st impression was casual service, cozy room and an argument....Oh never mind, They were just Arabic people in a friendly happy conversation who didn't even bother to notice us.

For an appetizer,  we had the (maze) Vegetable Combination for two and I totally got Tariq's point of view, especially in his expression "It is edible and clean but plain."

SPICE IT UP!!!  Give it more interesting lively flavors... 

Baba Ghanoush: More and more eggplant kick and with little chili and garlic and spices to deliver that zing. 
Hummus: More tahini, lemon juice, little garlic and more spices for that rich flavor.
Dolmades: less rice, lemon juice, lots of spices and herbs with a nice fold and roll.

For the main course, we had the Combination Chicken & Beef Koobedeh. It was a good choice. Very fresh tasting and perfectly cooked. More spices and herb will turn it to the Real Deal!  Definitely, people will be impressed by the quality of food. However, the name of the plate is a little confusing. The word "Koobedeh" in Arabic means "liver" but the description of the plate sounds like Kabab. 

The Awesome Dude is "The ascent of Middle Eastern flavors in a dessert."  thumbs up!! 

Coming to The hard part, the SERVICE. I would suggest to hire someone to help the poor waitress  who was taking care of 3 other tables beside us, and in the middle of taking our order she apologized to go answer the phone, she was also the cashier and the host. I wasn't comfortable with the whole situation and I literally offered my help. Seriously, I won't mind at all rather than watching an elderly woman really struggling with all that. It was really sad. The people on the table beside us had the same feeling and started to encourage her and show her appreciation for her effort. When it came to the tip, I tipped her just because I felt sorry for her although the service was so bad and I can totally see it is not her fault. 
SHE CAN'T HANDLE IT.

Unfortunately Chef Maurice wasn't there. I was looking forward to meeting him and sharing my opinion with him. 

I was expecting an outstandingly good authentic food for the value, good service and a pleasant feeling.  I'm not sure if I will be a returning customer.

Monster Meaty Sandwiches!!

Bold sandwiches for those people who have a teenage boy's huge appetite! Bigger than your mouth with a giant portion of meats that require both hands, fork and knife! 

The hearty hot Pastrami on grilled sourdough with a big serving of garlic fries was what my Kat enjoyed very much! The Sourdough bread came hot with a high pile of smoky, well seasoned and nicely caramelized meat with sauerkraut and cheese! The thin-cut garlic french fries were golden, crispy and flavorful enough to be a meal of their own!

My Open-Face REUBEN sandwich with rye bead was so rich, tangy, meaty! Huge amount of corned beef, sauerkraut, and melted cheese! My orzo salad was meh. 

Quick and OK service.

As often, the leftovers were more enjoyable than the meal itself! Yes will be back!

I scream, You scream, We all scream... 

WHY don't you step outside of your classic vanilla, chocolate or strawberry flavor comfort zone and try something CRAZY!!
 
Ever try a Banana Curry ice cream? Or Toasted Sesame? How about Mango Chile Lime sorbet?  What!  You haven't heard of these?  Well, in that case you should check out these innovative bizarre ice cream flavors!! 

As weird as it may sound, these flavors are so good in a cool way possible!!  Uncommon and tasty ingredients mixed in with local cream, and, in the end, this surprisingly refreshing flavors are a little bit salty, a little bit spicy but definitely very unique.

I played it safe and got Mango Chile Lime sorbet, Chocolate Smoked Sea Salt and Banana Curry. Next time, I'll expand my horizons and get new things. 

So get out there, test out some of the more unconventional flavors and get ready for an unimaginable interesting ice cream taste sensation!

Gr8 Food 4 A Good Cause! 

Little cozy restaurant locally owned and operated by super sweet friendly couple. They serve the most insanely delicious and perfectly cooked pizza with fair prices!  They hire people with various physical and mental health disabilities to live more independent lives in our community. Hat off to Walter and Judy!

Did I mention the BEST mouthwatering fresh-out-of-the-oven pies in town! 

The crust was very thin, not too soggy, not too crispy, not full of air pockets and holds a fold very well. The red sauce was really flavorful, tangy and unique!  The light fresh mozzarella cheese was my favorite part not rubbery or chewy or overdone. The ingredients were crazy fresh! It was like eating happiness mixed with joy!

Did I mention that visit was so special to my heart?

Yes, I just picked my mom and my sister from the airport after almost 21 hours trip! Walter and Judy were very welcoming and attentive. They kept checking up on us and asking if things are good or if we need anything else. I really appreciate their kindness toward my mom. They kept welcoming her and having those sweet talk with her about her trip from Saudi to Reno, how she feels about visiting here and if she likes it here in Reno or not! They accepted and respected her even with Islamophobia. They even gave her a hug good bye! I was in seventh heaven seeing my mom that happy and ate that well! It was a great experience. We left with a full stomach and a cheerful mind. Everything was superior! 

Yes ... it is our humanity that keeps us alive

Quaint Italian restaurant that felt like Lady and the Tramp dining!! 

We always come here to celebrate our very special occasions! Our anniversary and Valentine's Day were very romantic and lovely! We had a truly warm and wonderful experience! 
 
Recently, Chef. Kevin posted on his private FB page their COVID -19 policy and all the pieces and parts regarding this matter so we decided to celebrate my BF Bday there! I called to reserve a table for 3 and I didn't hesitate to ask if the waitress/waiter will be wearing masks (was not trying to be rude but I'm a vulnerable person with Asthma). Judy was super kind and friendly! She did confirm that YES all the front/back of the house staff are wearing masks! On the other hand, she asked that we wear masks until we are seated and anytime we leave our table. 

Phenomenal job Zozo's for ramping up safety measures!!! Over 1/2 the tables in their dining room were removed to serve the social distancing purpose! Plenty of space between tables! Becky our amazing waitress seated us with a big smile on her face which her mask couldn't hide! Ugh...the signature red and white checkered table cloths were removed too. She handed us new laminate menus and kept 6 feet away from the table and explained that they clean and sanitize the menus and the tables between each use! I forgot to mention that she was wearing gloves too! 

We usually kick off our dinner party in style with one or two of the absolutely divine starters! The Calamari and Zozo's Meatballs were good but the Shrimp & Artichoke Fritta and the Lobster Ravioli were the big hit! The Chicken Parmesan always kicks it up the notch! The New Zealand Grouper and the Halibut were WONDERFUL! The Seafood Linguini and the Sausage Lasagna were excellent and authentic! The Garlic Bread is da best garlic bread we've had ever tasted!

Although we are in a pandemic and they just reopened, it felt so enjoyable and comfortable inside the restaurant! The atmosphere and the hospitality didn't change a bit! Another memorable night for us! Way to go ZOZO's!

Came here for a little very early date with my bestie!

Little restaurant. 
Cafe style decor. 
Cozy atmosphere! 
Very nice and welcoming host and service!

I started with Cappuccino.... Nothing to write home about. I wouldn't bother ordering it again. 

The Hen house was OMG! Great flavor of a creamy mixture of chicken breast strips, sautéed spinach, mushrooms, caramelized onions, tomatos and cheddar cheese which filling these soft, elegant and moist crepes that topped with two perfect over easy eggs and served with my choice of house salad!

We will be back to try some more .......

Sushi is Sushi, right? Not quite...

You are a sushi lover ... so you should add "Hinoki Sushi" to your "The Must" list!

Just sit at the sushi bar and watch those talented chefs using only a sharp knife and a bamboo rolling mat and keep them sending you their unique sushi combinations, creative rolls and classic nigiri. Trust me, Rodrigo and Gerson really know how to serve you the right texture and the exotic flavors that go with it which totally satisfy your sushi craving! Be happy and smile so you'll be lucky enough to be treated with the chef specials, you're most welcome!

Personally, everything was super delicious! Each piece of flavorful fresh fish cut was laid out very beautifully! We were most pleasantly satisfied with both the quality and the quantity of our dishes. The hospitality and the service were on point!  

Will be back because Hinoki really floats our sushi boat!

Me and my Kat were passing by this fast food casual spot so we decided to give it a try. 

The food was meh for us. My beef burrito was very soggy. Unpleasantly moist mess, I wasn't able to enjoy it. Kathy got the Carne Asada Torta. It looked and cooked correctly but didn't have much flavor. The seasoning was way off. It was very bland. 

Nothing to write home about so there is no need for us to go back.

Monster Meaty Sandwiches!!

Bold sandwiches bigger than your mouth with a giant portion of meats require both hands, ton of napkins and ... I know that sounds clunky but I would say, fork and knife! So yah be prepared with a teenage boy huge appetite!

Dirka Dirka on Jalapeño cheddar bread was what the lady on the cashier recommended to me! 
A pile of griddled, tender and nicely caramelized corned beef and pastrami draped with a thin slice of melty swiss cheese and topped with seasoned Jalapeño coleslaw, fresh pickles and a splash of yellow mustard on a nice crust and chewy inside tasty baguette! Is this the longest sentence ever or what!!

My Kat got the Sicilian on sourdoug while my sister got the Steak and cheese on blue cheese bread!  "It taste good!" .. that's what they said!

Freshness .. is the key here! Large selection of fresh breads, meats, cheeses, condiments and toppings for cold cuts sandwiches and hot options like phillys and meatballs is a big plus! 

Quick and friendly service! They don't skimp on on the portions/quality and charge a fair price!

Full Belly Deli is absolutely on the right track!

Mmmmmm TACOS !!

Authentic Mexican food is not popular in Saudi Arabia, where I grow up, so my idea of Mexican food is the Tex-Mex Taco Bell style. Taco is any kind of meat mixed with a packet of taco seasoning, chopped lettuce, diced tomatoes, all shoved in a tortilla and topped with shredded cheddar cheese, salsa and sour cream.
