Guess what, THESE ARE NOT TACOS.

Real tacos by Mexican standards!!! 

Mexican restaurant locally owned and operated by a happy friendly Mexican American family, not a chain restaurant (the word taquería is always a good sign).

Those soft traditional tacos, full of the flavors of Mexico, very simple corn tortillas, hot, moist, GENEROUS portion of meat topped with CILANTRO and finely diced WHITE ONION plus slices of fresh LIMES as condiments.

Make your choice between the Lengua (beef tongue), Al pastor (spicy pork), Asada (Steak), Cabeza (beef head), Carnitas (pork), Pollo (chicken), Al Pastor (spicy pork), Chicharron (pork skin), Carne Desebrada (shredded beef), Bistec Ranchero (steak ranchero), Chile Verde (pork in green chile) and Chorizo at around $1.50 each.

MEXICAN TACOS ARE NOT SPICY. 

You make them as spicy as you want, so choose between their house specialties salsa the mild (green) or to burn-your-mouth (red).

Now lemme get this straight, they are so good. Like really good. I tried different kinds of tacos:  Chorizo, Asada, Pollo,Carne Desebrada in addition to the lingua (my favorite).

So get out there, try some authentic 'street' taco flavor and turn your day into a fiesta !!!

Let's be honest, Who doesn't crave pizza and what could be better than having Guilt - Free Pizza!

I'm just done with my whole warm pie and I feel great!

I mean, how cool to be able to have around 12-inch pizza that you can choose your crust, pick your sauce, pile on as much as you want of your favorite toppings (without any extra charge) and get ready to chow down! So the idea that you can play around and have fun with this cool concept and make your own pie! There are no rules about the kinds of toppings you put on your pizza.It is totally all up to you! Go vegetarian, Gluten - Free, low - calories, ...... Remember, it is your pie!

I decided to go healthier (not %100) but I'm proud to say Linda's pie was extraordinarily flavorful and great oven-baked-to-perfection pie! 

The place was clean and has a comfortable family oriented atmosphere. The staff were doing their job and the owner of the place baked my pie! 

Definitely will be back for more "My Very Own Pizza Nutrition Game".

So when it comes to Korean food, I really trust the yelper Jeana R 's word!  After reading her review, I decided to give the CLASSIC BULGOGI BiBiM-BAB a shot!

It was a really delicious colorful"Healthy Simple Fix"! It came with a complementary Miso soup ... extra bounce! I upgraded to brown rice and added shredded kimchi and got a kimchi appetizer! Yah I'm a big kimchi fan! And just a heads up, the super hot sauce is SUPER HOT! They Aren't Kidding Around! 

I really loved the idea that whenever I feel like "guilt-free" fast food, I come here to get a "healthy grab with an Asian twist", power up with protein and boost my veggie intake!

The dinning area was spotless and neat! The young employees were quick and friendly! Please show them some appreciation and make their day! 

Will definitely be back to try their delicious Korean wings!

Nasty surprise!

My Kat was craving something sweet. This bakery is just a block from us so after reading the reviews, she decided to give it a shot.

The place was empty. Only one employee on the phone. No welcome or Hi or anything. Kat was in the mood of flavorful pumpkin pie and a rich cheesecake! 

The pumpkin pie was meh and the cheesecake was hard to the touch. it had an "off" smell and unpleasant flavor Yuck! So we went back and Kat asked the cashier Krystal M to taste it. She offered to give her a new one. After we took another look at the display, everything looked not fresh and had obviously been refrigerated. I asked her how often they bake the goods and she said every other day. Yah Right! The pastries we had were definitely over two days old if not longer. We asked for a refund and she issued it.

Shame on you Haven on Earth for keeping expired food in the fridge. Never again!

Phenomenal job Trader Joe's! 

Being a vulnerable person with Asthma in this nightmare really restricts my life. I have to be totally quarantined! My man usually does the grocery shopping and all the other essential tasks but I decided to tag along to TJ since I heard about their good policy of applying the social distancing and all the precautions to prevent the spread of the virus! 

Upon arrival, we were asked to create a line which we were promised that it will move fast! Also, we were asked to follow the floor marks to map out the distance that we should be keeping from each other. While we were waiting two of the employees were fully cleaning and sanitizing the shopping carts. Before the entrance, a friendly employee greeted us, handed the clean cart and informed us that they only allowing a certain number of customers in at once. She also encouraged us to fill up our cart to avoid making unnecessary trips and keep in mind the people who are waiting outside to get in. Loved how she also reminded us to take out our list and use the phone before wearing the gloves to avoid the cross contamination! 

It felt so good and comfortable Inside the store. Plenty of space between people and no crowded isles. At the cashier there are no lines! An employee guided us to a certain cashier once another costumer was done and left the building! 

All in all, very relaxing experience! Kudos TJ for ramping up safety measures in stores!! You guys earned our trust and loyalty

Fun show of upper crust ice cream! 

So after we picked our desired flavors, the ice cream girl poured a cup of milk on to an extremely cold and big steel surface circle. Then she used what looks like a paint scraper to chop the toppings onto the base. Once the creamy texture spread thinly, she pushed it down and created the ice cream rolls! Finally, the rolls were arranged in cups and topped with whipped cream, caramel sauce and CHOPSTICK!!

The Matcha and the salted caramel ice cream were not too sugary and the matcha/caramel flavors were well balanced with the milk! 

Definitely pricey for what you get so for me, it will be a luxurious indulgence here and there.

My favorite Indian Food Spot!

I highly recommend their lunch buffet! For only $9 you can enjoy a good variety of India's rich culinary flavors. Each item in it does the cuisine justice mainly because of the fresh ingredients, healthy vegetables, beans and fragrant spices. You just can't get enough of that delicious and pillowy garlic naan. The hot and spicy condiments are amazing! Fresh cilantro, mint, yogurt, hot chili peppers, garlic, lemon, ginger and tomato, I mean what more can you ask for!  With the Indian music in the background, Bollywood dance on the screens, all those different exotic aromas, colors and tastes, you would feel like you are celebrating the traditional Hindu spring festival of Colors!! JUST BE THERE BY 11AM, YOU'RE WELCOME!

If you are not a buffet person, you will be happy with the off the menu choices. So far we enjoyed, the boneless chicken pieces Tandoori Chicken, Tikka Masala, Chicken Korma, Murg Coc Korma and the incredibly flavorful Gosht Biryani.

The Mango Lassi is always a treat! It is between a smoothie and a milkshake and is absolutely heavenly!

Service is good and the owner is always making sure that everyone is having a good time.

India Kabab and Curry nailed a big shout out for its spectrum of exotic flavors of delicious foods and fantastic Indian beer at Yelp's Far East Street Eats - Reno Bites Signature Event. 

I was honored to attend 2016 Diwali, festival of lights celebration, which took place at the Paradise Ball Room in Atlantis Casino Resort. The yummy authentic food buffet was catered by India Kabab and Curry! According to India Association Of Northern Nevada (IANN), they received numerous compliments and calls praising the food. Indian know best ;)

The only reason why this place is even getting one star is because we called and told them we were running late and they were very accommodating. 

On the other hand the food was bland and flavorless they didn't even have honey mustard nor blue cheese for the chicken wings. The wings were cold and dry and just not good. The menu is very limited maybe because of corona as a result I got a burger for my entree thinking they couldn't possibly mess up on a burger. But I was wrong the burger meat was tasteless and had little cheese. My friends ordered ice teas and it tasted like vinegar straight vinegar. 

Now on to the service our waiter was terrible. He hardly was around we didn't even see him when we wanted our check another waiter actually gave us our check and  bring us the different things we requested. 

Overall I kinda knew this place was going to have issues because I read the reviews on various platforms but because of corona sitting at different places were limited and this place allowed our group to all sit together.

They have Rosa de Jamaica!!!!! And the tacos are SO FREAKIN DELICIOUS omg. 

I tried 7 out of the 12 or so taco meat choices. Each taco is $2 and comes with plenty of meat. My favorite was the cabeza (beef). All the meat choices were cooked perfectly, so tender, juicy! 

They have a full menu of other dishes like fajitas, tortas, huaraches, rice and beans etc. Its a grocery store when you first walk in, and the restaurant section is in the back. I loved the variety of baked goods, flan, tres leche they had too. 

Funny story: I LOVE rosa de jamaica drink. I have a hard time finding it and most places call it "hibiscus tea" which usually is so tart and not exactly Jamaica. So when our server told me they have "Rosa de Jamaica" I HAD TO GET IT. And it was exactly like I remembered- nectar of the gods hahaha, sweet and oh so yummy! Since they're also a grocery store, they sold the Jamaica dried flowers!!!! Now I can make it at home too- I was so happy :))) 

So yes, go here! I only came for the tacos, but had the best time ever :D

The service is excellent! 5 stars. During the gradual reopening of COVID, its reservations only. And they use paper menus for single use.

Get the Chef's Board, the cheese and meat selections change. When we went, it was a cheddar harissa (I CRIED IT WAS SO GOOD). Soft blue cheese and a hard smoked gouda. 

The oxtail fried rice was really yummy. The octopus was super tender and had a citrusy dressing with grilled peppers and tomatoes. 

Haven is a part of Bern's Steakhouse. Which meannnss, their steak options are from Bern's including the aged Delmonico yay! Haven has a modern feel and the decor is upscale and elegant.

This Sushi place is a Special kind of place. , not your local sushi place, special meaning, their seafood comes from Japan. They make such unique rolls, the employees, owners are great!! I stopped by here Friday night, met up with dinner buddy, the Volcano roll was spicy-yum..got Wasabi fries, ended with fried bananas with green tea ice cream.Mmmmm-mm!! Great atmosphere-decor. They are consistently great all the time.

What a great experience this was. We went there on a Sunday for a Mexican Brunch with my soon to be mother in law, sister in law and auntie in law. 
The place was packed, always a good sign, we didn't have to wait long for a table, we were seated promptly. 
Our waiter was very polite and took the time to let us know about the specials and of course he recommended their margarita, supposed to be so good it has won awards, so I had to make sure they were good indeed ;) , and yes they were!!! Not too sweet and they had a punch!!! I had to pace myself!!!

They gave us some chips and salsa, that were absolutely homemade, the salsa was made with roasted tomatoes and chillies, it was just like none I've had before, I wish I could've taken a bottle of that, it had the perfect kick as well, I was surprised to see my mother in law going to town with it :P, 
didn't get to try all the dishes that were ordered but I tried what my fiancé had, the beef flautas, I had only a couple of bites but they were yummy! 
I ordered huevos con chorizo, the ratio chorizo to eggs was not even! Lol it felt I had more chorizo than eggs, not complaining, it had a very nice kick, I kept making pauses in between and sipping on my margarita ;) .
We also had some desserts that tasted homemade.
Our experience was great, and if you ever find yourself in Tampa, go ahead give them a chance! You will love these guys!!

We went here for a nice dinner and the place was very busy as it is small inside with not a lot of seating. The food was very tasty and priced right. The wait times were long but it was busy. The service was friendly. The food arrived hot and looked good. This eatery is located in an older sort of run down strip mall, and you have to look for it as its off the side road not the main hwy in front. The serving sizes were plentiful, and overall things went well. I will eat here again.

Nice mom-n-pop hippy restaurant that throws you back to the 1960's with it's wall art and table decor. The tables are covered in tie dye designs and the walls covered in posters and signs from rock bands and other memorabilia from this long past, but not forgotten era in time. 

The floor could use some major deep cleaning as it looks very worn, and has lost its shine. Maybe updating from the red and white checkered tiles, that seem to clash with the rest of the decor would be an ever better idea than deep cleaning them. But on a mom-n-pop budget and not a corporate budget with tons of money to throw behind decorating a new store, I understand their slowness in replacing a floor, ha. 

I was greeted when I walked in the door by Jessie, who asked how many in my party, and told me to sit anywhere I wanted. She was nice, and she also was my server. The place was very slow when I was there, maybe one other table was eating there. 

The layout of the restaurant is kind of odd, maybe it was the way they did it 40 years ago, but now-days seems things are not in their proper place, not that this is a bad thing, just different. Such as the Coke dispenser machine is next to the front entrance door as soon as you walk in, you almost think you walked into the employee area, ha. 

The owners desk with computer, printer, etc is right next to the side entrance door, and out in the open, no private office area, or separation from the dining area. The kitchen is in the rear, where about 3 employees kept busy prepping and cooking. 

She gave me time to browse the menu and gave a few recommendations, and also noted that the Tuesday Tenderloins, were no longer just Tuesday, but now are available Everyday, as she said they are very popular. 

I ordered the Lave Lamp Wings for my appetizer as I scanned the extensive menu, where everything was named for something from the old days, ha. They arrived in a timely manner and looked great. 

They were of normal size and has a normal hot flavor to them, that was very good. they were properly covered in sauce and full of flavor. The server actually brought me more napkins for the messy hot wings, without me even having to request them, as I normally must do at 9 out of 10 places, ha. 

I then ordered the biggest burger on the menu to give it a try, it's called the Lights Out Lytle Burger, and it comes with three 10oz patties on it and whatever else you want to add. 

It's a huge almost 2 pound triple burger! I ordered mine with cheese, and when it arrived it was amazing looking with a big steak knife sticking out the top. Which was perfect because there was no way to pick up and eat this like a sandwich, so I used the knife and cut it like a steak. 

The three perfectly cooked medium well, Angus beef, char grilled burgers tasted amazing! They tasted like a steak, I almost asked the server for some A1 sauce, as the meat was so juicy and full of flavor. And after several minutes, yes, I did eat the entire burger. I just couldn't stop myself as my taste buds continually demanded more, more, more! 

The server kept checking up on me and was friendly the entire time. I had a great meal that was very filling, and although it was a expensive for what I ate, wings $7.95 and burger $15.95, for a total of about $26, this would have been a meal for 2 or 3 normal eaters, I am a big guy and can eat a lot, haha. 

Overall above average tasting hot wings, excellent tasting gigantic triple burger, very good service, decent decor, and priced a bit on the expensive side. 
Nice place to stop in and have a bite to eat.

Wow! This place has amazing tasting food! If you are not certain what some of the authentic German made dishes are, then the friendly server will be happy to answer any questions you may have. I have tasted several items from this location and everything has tasted great! Prices are average for a sit down restaurant and affordable. The place can get busy quickly during peek eating times. 

This is a place I will eat at and take others to eat at for a choice different than all the American or Mexican places all over town. We're lucky to have such a skilled cook, making these dishes for us in this area. Some days they also have live music. Don't pass up this strip mall gem!

My food was spot on for flavor, I had the salmon and it was delicious. I will be back to get more! Prices are as expected for this type restaurant, wait times normal, and overall a nice place for a great meal.

This location was pretty busy so we sat at the bar inside and had a couple beers, it was buy one get one free day on beers. Which explained why the place was so busy, lol. 

The service was fast and friendly, and the food here is pretty good. They are always changing their menu, so that keeps lots of fresh and new items to try. All went well and was good during this visit. 

The half price appetizers during certain hours are a good deal.

Cozy restaurant with lots of flashing lights on the ceiling, and lit up water falls on the wall. Very nice decor, tables, chairs, elegant, but no overly fancy. Menu's are well laid out, and very nice with their book like hard covers. The drinks are prepared and delivered in a very cool way. 

The food came out in a timely manner and was excellent in taste. For a Friday evening they were not overly busy, but by the time we left the place was starting to get crowded. This seems to be a local favorite hot spot for some great sushi. 

The food presentation was excellent, very appealing and displayed with artistry on the plates. The Edamame appetizer, California rolls,  Alligator Bites, Spider man, and Dragon Fire were all very well prepared and very tasty. The service was also excellent. The drinks were kept full, and the servers checked on us often. 

They have a wide variety of unique and create own sushi. They are open long and late hours. The entire staff was professional acting, well dressed, and you would not know this was a restaurant in a small strip mall. Excellent all the way around, food, service, fair prices, presentation, and decorations. Great place for a great dining experience.

Great shop to stop in for a fresh made sandwich. They offer many combinations and types of sandwiches, soups, and desserts, all at a fair price. Service is friendly and helpful, and they can get you in and out quickly if your on lunch break and limited on time. 
The soup was tasty, hot, and full to the top of the cup, drinks are self serve, so refills are included. Plenty of parking in the large lot, and if there during lunch rush hour, don't worry, the staff is fast and can get to you quickly. Glass counter full of tasty sugar treats awaits those with a sweet tooth.

I have eaten here many times and although there are several authentic Mexican restaurants in the area, including many food trucks, this place seems to provide some of the most consistently best tasting food, with good service. I have had many items from burrito's, taco's, to quesadilla's and it's all tasty! 

You can dine in the bar area at a high top table, outside on the patio, or in the main dining room. There is sometimes a wait on weekends or during peak dining hours, which is expected for any popular restaurant. But most of the time I have eaten here I have been able to walk in and get seated immediately.

This is a great waterfront place to eat outside and be right on the sandy beach. The service for our group was great, all drinks were kept full and the food arrived in a timely manner. The food was presented well and had a nice taste to it. Overall this was a nice beach front bar and restaurant to grab a quick bite to eat and be on our way. I will eat here again. 

I did take advantage of my Yelp free order of onion rings when eating here. The server didn't know what the mobile coupon was, but the manager came out and she knew. So that went smooth here, as some places don't like to honor the Yelp check in discounts.

When it's May in Indy, you will hear about the Indy 500 on a daily basis. This is a huge worldwide event that is attended by race fans from around the globe. 

They also host several other racing events, and even had the Rolling Stones play a first ever concert here. Bring friends and family, but on certain days you might want to leave the small kids at home, as the crowds can get a bit rowdy and tend to love to drink... and drink a lot, haha. It's all about racing and having fun here at the IMS.  

This is a historic place and this year (2016) celebrates the 100th running of the Indy 500. So come and be a part of history and create some great times!

Very upscale on the inside looking place, clean, well kept, organized, nice fixtures, and overall very attractive place to go for a nice meal. Plenty of parking around the building, which sits sort of by itself, where once there was a large strip mall behind it. 

The service was average to slow at times, but was friendly and nice. We did have to search for our server as once we were finished eating we could not find her, so I got up and searched the place, but she was better at hiding than Waldo, so I sat back down and continued to wait, until she returned. the food prep was very nice, presentation was good, taste was above average, and prices are on the higher side as expected. If it wasn't for the 15 minute wait to get my bill so we could leave I would have given 1 more star. The place was not busy when I was there this day either. 

I will go again, and hopefully won't have to wait for my bill, as that's 1 pet peeve of mine, because when I am done and ready to leave a place, I do not like waiting extra long times for the server to finally take my payment, ha.

I like this old fashioned greasy spoon type diner, and I know what to expect when I eat here. My food was prepared fast and hot and as ordered, it was a large portion so I needed to take some with me. All around great place for anytime of the day, especially late nights! I'll be back.

Great pizza at an expected price! Everything was excellent and this is a place to get a very large sized pizza, if needed for a large group. Nice alternative to the national pizza chains. All went well. I will eat here again.

I have not been to an Outback Steakhouse in some time, as they seemed to blend in with many of the other steak houses. But this night it was our selection, and amazingly enough it was an excellent choice. It was a Monday evening during dinner hour, the place was half full, so the noise level was low, and we were able talk easily. 

We sat at a booth in the bar area, and our server was there as soon as we sat down, took our drink order and was back in a flash with the drinks. She was very talkative and in a great mood. She really seemed to enjoy her job. 

Our food came out in a timely manner, and the server was always there as needed to check up on us. The chicken tortilla soup was very hearty, filled with lots of white chicken, veggies, and very little soup, ha. Many places give you lots of soup and very little chicken and veggies, this was the opposite. And it tasted great!

The grilled salmon and broccoli was cooked perfectly, tender, pink, and melted in your mouth. This dining experience really made me take a 2nd look at Outback, as I rarely give 5 stars to chain places, but I could not think of any reason this place did not deserve 5 stars. Food, service, ambiance, cleanliness of the restroom and entire restaurant was excellent, and we even had very close parking. 

This is not as great as some of the steak houses that charge 3 times the price in the area, but for the cost and what we received this place was awesome the night we had dinner! Great job Outback! We will be back!

Don't be fooled by this location, as it is not in the fancy part of town, but once you enter, you can see the place is very nice, and has a huge selection of wine, many foreign beers, and other drinks, along with a South American ambiance. 

I met and talked to the owner, Renzo, for a short minute, and he is a genuinely nice guy, who wants to take care of his customers, and make certain they have an excellent experience while in his establishment. 

They serve several meals as authentically prepared in Argentina and Uruguay. We tried the highly recommend and popular Ultimate Renzo sandwich, which came out on about a 10 inch white bread sub bun, and mine had steak, ham, bacon, 2 fried eggs, cheese, lettuce, tomato, green olives, and I think that's all. 

My friend had the same, except instead of steak he had grilled chicken. These come with large cut french fries, and substitutions are not allowed. The sandwiches were very healthy in size and tasted fresh and pleased my taste buds. 

We also tried and enjoyed the $2 empanada appetizers. I had two; beef and chicken, and my friend had spinach. They offered us two types of sauces for dipping, both were good. 

The large dinners made for 2 or more looked excellent on the menu, but that will be for another time. They have a good sized wine room for the connoisseur. At the rear of the restaurant you can see inside the butcher's glass counter, the exquisite cuts of meat available for the choosing.

The service, presentation, and food were all excellent. I will return here for more! The restaurant was kept clean, and well organized. All was very good!

On a side note, this hidden gem was discovered because we went a couple doors down in the same strip mall to the Happy Foot Chinese Massage business for 90 minute massages, which were also great! Men, take note, this is a great combo for a date; get a very relaxing massage, then come here for a wonderful dining experience. Bam! Winner, winner!

Was in the area and heard good things about this place so we stopped in for some breakfast. Saw lots of bicycles parked outside, as it's on the Monon trail, and the parking lot was pretty full too. Which is all a good sign that the food may be tasty. 

The meals were large and everything tasted good. The inside was very clean and has a bright colorful look to it. The service was not the quickest, but was okay, as they were busy. They offer inside and outside dining both. 

Very cool small sized mom-n-pop restaurant locally owned and operated. If in the area this is a place you will want to try the breakfast, as they have many options to choose from. Prices were a bit on the higher side, but the food was very good, so it was worth it.

I can't believe I have never reviewed Mango, one of my favorite restaurants in STL! You must try the grilled beef heart on skewer, the Ceviche Mixto, and the signature Peruvian dish Lomo Saltado. Really you can't go wrong with anything here. Wash down your food with a Pisco Sour or its fruitier cousin Mango Sour. If you like ginger beer, get the Chilcano too. 

The restaurant is beautiful, airy on the inside, with some patio seating. It makes for a great celebration dinner destination. Service is not always consistent but the food makes up for it. 

Peruvian food is never cheap. Go to a decently-decorated Peruvian restaurant in any city, you will likely have people complain of high prices. But if I'm getting cold-cured fish, I would rather pay a little extra $$$ to make sure it's fresh and properly-prepared. 

Last but not least, I have been to Peru and have eaten at many Peruvian restaurants in my travels, this is still one of the best Peruvian places in the United States. For people who like to use qualifiers such as "good enough for St. Louis" or "good enough for the midwest", no, just no. Didn't anyone ever tell you it's rude to label an entire city or part of the country as having unsophisticated taste buds? Get off the high horses already, seriously.

There are certain things I genuinely HATE about this place. To me, this is a restaurant that has been banking on its food network fame and goes out of its way to inconvenience diners. So if you are from out of town, skip! Especially if you have a group bigger than 2 people, it's not worth the trouble. 

I guess to start with what's decent: I find the food to be on the average to high quality range. Everything is pricier than they should be but the entrees have decent flavors. On our last visit, we had a fairly large party. I tried a sample of others' food. The side of green beans with bacon was WAY too peppery/salty; the Monte Cristo dogs were interesting. I'm a sucker for jellies so I enjoyed it. My friend's side of barley was completely cold when it came on the table and it also tasted funky. She left it sitting after one bite. The dessert peanut butter blaster was fantastic and it was a large slice, perfect for sharing. 

I also do not have any major complaints about the service on my visits. It's fair; the servers could be more attentive, but the place is always packed and busy that any lapse in attention is justifiable to me. 

What I find to be extremely distasteful is all these creative ways they come up to make a few bucks. $2 cold/grocery store bread; $3 split check fee (really? Is there really a need to charge $3 per check when people are dropping upwards of $30 for a meal?); no seating until everybody in the party shows up (which means even though 11 of our party of 13 were present, they will not let us sit and we all have to awkwardly stand around the bar trying to stay out of others way. We were gonna order appetizers first anyway so I don't see why the wait for two late-comers)....seriously? When are they gonna start charging for re-fills? And why do they need all these restrictions and surcharges? To up keep the restaurant that's in a seedy part of town? Puh--lease!!

Because of their "we don't give a shit about you or your convenience" attitude (and their "we don't give a shit about writing more descriptions on our menus cause we'd rather our over-worked waiters explain everything if and when he/she finally makes his/her way to your table"), Iron Barley is the most over-rated restaurant in STL in my opinion. For your hard-earned $$s, you can have an equally delicious if not more enjoyable meal, and that means not just good food, but great service, and actually be treated like your business matters. A good restaurant should at least make the simplest attempts to cater to a diner's not-so unreasonable needs. But apparently at Iron Barley, they are too famous to worry about that.

Well we are in our fifth week of being home and quarantine. The hubby and I are going stir crazy so we decided it was date night time. What should we do? So we called in an order for takeout at Zozo's swing by picked it up curbside. The staff was so lovely and gracious and the service spot on .... as always!  I got the mushroom ravioli and hubby ordered the chicken sausage.  Both came with salad and bread yummm. We then decided to drive to Windy Hill and enjoy our dinner overlooking our beautiful city.   

Thank you ZoZos for making our date night memorable!  We can't wait to be back !

We love this place! There is a good variety of food on the menu....beware of the tater tot entree...it's super hard to share it despite the large portion. Home brewed beer is wonderful and there is a fine assortment of cocktails too.  We prefer the tap room over the restaurant. Not as crowded and accommodates more friends.  On a cold night they light the fire. 

Bonus... the guys who own this are the nicest people and donate back to our community.  Any local business with such heart always has our business. 

Please check it out!

I have heard so much about Santa Barbara's fish n' chips. My parents had them at Moby Dick's and Harbor Restaurant since the '80's. Since we wanted to take it to-go, we decided to order from Char West. Their sign advertised their Fish N' Chips so we figured it had to be their best item. And with that view, it was the perfect set-up.

Right? Wrong. It was sincerely disappointing and given the dish, it was an expensive disappointment. For $15, we got two large pieces of fish and a basket of fries with tartar sauce. Overall, the fish was not good. It was watery, which means it was frozen. There was a noticeable amount of grey meat, which means it was probably a carp (like tilapia, catfish, swai) and not cod, haddock or halibut - the best choices of fish for this dish. Yes, the meat was thick and a great portion, but the quality was not great. It also had a very fishy smell, which you may think, "Duh" but this is the smell that comes from either old or defrosted fish. Not appetizing. We did not finish the dish, split among three people.

On the bright side, the fries were crispy and the tartar sauce was good. The fried coating was great, crispy and golden - a good sign that the oil was changed often. Staff was not friendly but they were efficient at grinding out food fast. 

I saw that there are not many options on the wharf so if you really really need food fast, I understand if you end up here. However, if you want good fish n' chips, I would go elsewhere. Admittedly, I did check their Yelp rating while I was in line to order, but gave them the benefit of the doubt. #regrets
Don't be like me. Be better.

Highly overrated seafood restaurant in Santa Barbara. 
My parents and I took a day trip to SB and, obviously, made plans to have seafood. I know SB is somewhat known for their delicious fish and chips, but for the non-fried route, we wanted to up the ante and splurge on a well-known spot. 

We were quoted 1 hour wait for our party of 3 but 30 minutes of waiting later, we were seated outside (by request) so we could enjoy the view of the marina. Partial sun (which was fine by my left shoulder is burned lol) but the breeze was amazing coming through the harbor. 

We waited a good 15 minutes until anyone decided to even take our drink order. I had waited that long to flag someone down to give them the benefit of the doubt since it was busy. However, plenty of servers were helping tables right next to us, but somehow, we were invisible. Very interesting. My family and I tend to stick out like a sore thumb in predominantly non-POC communities like SB. 

After a while, my parents started to get concerned, so I did what I do best and flagged someone down. Hey, thanks, water please! My mom got their mai tai. Slightly annoyed at this point. But service was good after that.

We all have somewhat small appetites (read: my dad has a small appetite, my mom and I do not) so we ordered 2 dishes and an appetizer to share. Mom went with the blackened seabass with a cup of New England Chowder, ya girl went with the hot combo appetizer as my entree. For our appetizer, we shared the oysters Rockefeller since it seems to be iconic American seafood. It's also in the hot combo so we ordered a lot of them unintentionally. My mom liked her seabass just fine, great texture and tasted fresh! But rice pilaf was undercooked so it was hard and rubbery. 

For the hot combo, the clams, steamed and baked, were overcooked. They were rubbery and bland - difficult to chew so I ended up not eating quite a few. The mussels were just fine but... bland. The shrimps were also flavorless and it kind of sucked that the shells were left on. Cocktail sauce was served on the side which was pretty good, but for shrimps that size, they're usually already shelled ready for a dip. I didn't want to get my hands dirty so I ate them whole. Sigh not a great mouth experience! I'm paying good money for good seafood. Please don't make me work.

I was let down after reading so many great reviews here! On our way out, I saw a man had ordered a whole order of the steamed clams. Poor man... you ain't ready for that sore jaw! I don't recommend this spot unless you enjoy overcooked flavorless seafood. The price tag is not worth what you get. Pass.

Yes, my loyal fans, this was my shortest review to date. It was done as draft on my iPhone...so sorry...Yelp seems to have dispensed with drafts & they go right into a review. I really do not know how anyone can effectively type a proper review on an iPhone. I surely can't. It is especially annoying with all the spell checking or typos.
Anyway, here is the original draft...

"Great Hyatt buffet breakfast with made to Order omelets. Can get egg white omelets. Buffet includes bagels& lox, fresh local strawberries, & the usual good Hyatt fare. Friendly service with a great ocean view."

Which addresses that Hyatt's quite nice Breakfast Buffet which they were really nice enough to comp since I am a Loyal Hyatt groupie. 

I have over 600,000 Hyatt points, a Hyatt Credit Card, a Hyatt clock, a Hyatt glass, Hyatt underpants, Hyatt nasal spray, Hyatt sock monkeys, Hyatt Bitcoins....OK....only the first line is true...but you get the idea.

As for this Hyatt, the high points are great location & service.  The Ocean view (with an avenue in between) is great as you pig out at the Buffet.  Then you can walk it off & can extend your walk/or rental bike ride all the way to the pier. 

As for the hotel, it is rather dated, but does the trick.  The baths are clean & fairly modern, but the rooms are rather boring.  The AC/ Heater is the usual noisy affair, but that did help to drown out my relative's snoring. They do have a small frig in the room, & good sized TV. The pool is just OK.

We always have a good time here, despite the drawbacks of the dated stuff.
The staff are almost all extremely friendly & helpful.  They are very responsive to any requests & bring stuff to your room in record time. Managers are great & will go the extra mile to please you.

Anyway, it is also a great place to do a day trip to the Outlet Stores in Camarillo.

This is the 3rd time we have stayed here & with my Hyatt Card, it was free this time.
 
On the way back home, we stopped at Solvang, which while very touristy, was kind of fun.  There are a few really neat shops there.  Do not bother with the food, you better wait till you get to the Pismo/ SLO town area.

Excellent food. Seriously, almost every bite was incredible. Table favorites were: the sushi roll, krabby patties, the eggplant miso entree, the shrub soda drink, and the chocolate-covered dates. 

BUT the service was super awkward, bordering on rude. And with so many other good choices for food these days, I won't tolerate that.

Examples: I asked for help making a decision between three entrees and was curious what the server would recommend. His reply was: "I don't want to be responsible for you not liking something... you're an adult, be an adult and choose." Then, a friend asked what one dish was like and he replied: "it tastes exactly like it sounds. Read the description." There were so many more zingers from the server that we just had to laugh it off and roll our eyes to not have the whole evening ruined. 

And finally, even though I called ahead of time and asked if they could take a party of 7, one hour before closing time (to which the restaurant replied "yes, we're slow right now, please come."), we were seated and immediately and heard grumblings from multiple employees about how they sent most of their kitchen staff home and how the chef was frustrated a big party came in late, etc... 

So next time save me the trouble.  

If your restaurant can't handle a 7-top without making it known to the customer how understaffed you are, how pissed off your chef is about us being there an hour before closing, and without an incredibly rude and awkward server making us cringe every time he opened his mouth... just tell us you're busy. Tell us you're booked. Tell us not to come because you just let your sous chefs went home and without anyone to prep you can't handle the rush. Then at least I'd understand. 

I would much rather be turned away than be invited in and made to feel incredibly uncomfortable while trying to enjoy a nice meal. So please, next time, save someone the trouble of incredibly awkward quips and some extremely rude and unprofessional behavior from your wait staff. 

The food was great. Understaffed or not, the chef pulled it together and send out some incredible dishes. Which is really too bad, because with the front of the house acting like they did, displaying a total lack of regard for the customer experience and consistently delivering such rude and unprofessional  service you can guarantee I will never be back.

I definitely love a Burger Me burger.  And Burger Me fries.  This is just a great place.  I soooo wish they would put another location in South Reno, but it's definitely worth the trip to the Northwest - especially since they're conveniently located right off the freeway.

My personal favorites: the Southwest Turkey Burger, the Lamb Burger, and the Ahi Burger.  I have tried lots of them, and they're all great, juicy, fresh burgers with tons of toppings...but those are definitely my favorites.  But I can't have a Burger Me burger without fries.  It's always a hard decision between the garlic fries and the sweet potato fries, so do yourself a favor and go with a friend and order both!  And don't forget to order a variety of dipping sauces!  Your car might smell like garlic for a couple of days because they definitely don't skimp on the garlic...but it's totally worth it!

The service at Burger Me is also fast and friendly.  The last time I went through the drive-through, I ordered and moved forward in line and regretted not ordering 1 more basket of fries for the group I was meeting.  I called on my cell phone while in line, and the cashier laughed as I added another basket of fries to my order, and had everything ready for me by the time I got up to the window.  

The restaurant is great, and the food truck is equally as great.

Great crab cakes, garlic Parmesan fries and cheesy rice with veggies. I haven't had breakfast here in awhile so I can't give a honest review but from what I remember it was good. Food isn't cheap here, but not too pricey.

We really enjoy eating at Ulele. Actually it made our trip wonderful! 
I did not disappoint, rustic atmosphere and the food was great. Amazing service! Covid friendly tables and everything was super clean.
we had the wedge salad and wow! It was the perfect combination of the salty, with sour and then the sweetness from the corn hitting your taste buds right at the right time. Amazing. That risotto... woah! Outstanding job as always!
Overall, it was a great experience! I look forward to my next visit to try another item of theirs.

I've been driving up and down Delmar for over a year and looking for a reason to stop in at this interesting looking restaurant/store.  I read a very positive article about it in the Ladue News this morning and my wife and I decided we were going.  I see that other reviewers have had a very positive experience but mine was somewhat less so.

First, when we got there, there is no indication that you have to walk to the rear of the restaurant, place your order at a counter and then seat yourself.  We waited a few minutes near the entrance for someone to assist us and none of the staff at the restaurant suggested we walk to the back and order our food.  Eventually we figured it out and walked to the back.  When we got to the counter, the young woman behind the counter did not acknowledge us or invited us to place our order....she just stood there....I initiated the conversation and asked about vegetarian options....there was something on the counter called a Torte Rustica (sp?) that looked delicious and the young woman explained that it was vegetarian and not vegan which demonstrated that she was knowledgeable about the issue (I appreciate that).  I ordered it with a side salad.  My wife ordered chicken salad.  I ordered a diet coke and the woman asked me to go get it for her from the nearby cooler so she could ring it up.  If she had taken two steps (literally), she could have done it hersefl.  My wife ordered a Latte and the woman behind the counter handed us a number for us to put on our table so they would know where to bring the food out.

We sat at our table for a few minutes which seemed like a long time without the Latte so I walked back up to the counter and found it sitting there.  Apparently, you are responsible for picking up your coffee but they bring the food to you.  They did not tell us that and it would have not been a problem if we had known to hang out by the counter while they made the Latte.

A few minutes later, the server brought our food.  They correctly brought the chicken salad but the server was carrying two Torte Rustica's.  She gave me the one without the salad by mistake but I didn't recognize that when she put it down....after a moment or two, I did realize it and flagged down the waitress.  she said she had inadvertently given my plate with the salad to a different table and I had someone elses.  She took the plate on my table and went over to another table and did a switch.  To be honest, I think the proper thing to do would have been to bring me the missing salad.  There is a little "yuck" factor in getting food that has been on someone elses table that you don't know.

While the flavor was very good, the Torte Rustica was barely warm.  As I was eating it, I realized that I had little bits of paper in my mouth.  I turned the Torte over and there was parchment paper from baking it stuck to the bottom in a few places.  I just peeled it off and finished eating it.  It was pretty tasty.  My wife said her chicken salad was excellent.

The server who brought our food came back and thoughtfully picked up the dishes we were finished with and then began refilling the small vase on our table with the silverware rolled up in a napkin for the next guests who would sit there.  I appreciate her picking up the dishes but perhaps she could have waited until we were finished or had left before restocking the table for the next people.

Though there were small problems with the food, it wasn't enough to keep us from coming back.  Now that we know how things work there, our next visit should be much smoother.  However, in my mind, the real issue was the detached attitude of the staff.  Everyone there is very young and could use a refresher course in customer service.  The staff at this restaurant reminded me of the bored/lightly trained college students that used to staff the restaurants in the community where I went to school.  No one was rude to us but the lack of hospitality was obvious.  If you look at my other reviews, I'm not a stickler for service....just the lack of it at this restaurant made it stand out.

We are going to go back because the food is good.  Sure hope the staff seems more interested in us when we do return.

I can't tell you how excited I am that this great new restaurant, SIU Korean BBQ opened up in my neighborhood.  My house is just a couple of blocks away and I'm excited to see Sparks grow up and class up. The interior of this place is almost unrecognizable from what it was and from what you'd imagine from the outside. It's absolutely stunning. They have a nice small bar area too. 

Korean BBQ was a new experience for us so we needed some direction.  If you are also new to the concept here is how it works. The menu gives you two price choices (other than the cocktail menu)  All you can eat lunch and all you can eat dinner.  Around $18pp for lunch and around $27pp for dinner.  Similar to sushi joints in the area.  Obviously this is dictated by what time it is when you decide to go.  After that there are many choices on the menu as to what will be YOUR all you can eat. Since we were pretty new to the concept we told our server (Matthew?) and he asked some questions about what we liked and chose our menu for us. 

He brought out Korean appetizers,  a few starters including kimchi,  fried dumplings with spicy soy sauce, sweet potato fries, fried Oysters, spicy rice cake,  a shareable green salad and a few other yummy things to get us started. 

There is a small gas grill with a nonstick surface built into the center of the table and while we ate our appetizers the server fired up ours. He explained that we would be able to grill our own meat, chicken, fish, and vegetables as they brought it out.  You're given a few sets of tongs and scissors as tools to cook and cut your meats and veggies. Then they bring out raw marinated meat, onions and whatever veggies you ordered. They also bring out a few sauces and spices for cooking with, dipping or whatever you feel you'd like to do with it.  We also each had a small cup of rice.

We ended up trying a variety of meats that We let Our server choose for us. Spicy chicken, which was marinated in spicy Korean chili, Chicken Bulgogi (Bulgogi is the most popular variety of Korean barbecue. Before cooking, the meat is marinated with a mixture of soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and pepper)  and Chicken Satay.  We also tried a couple of beef dishes, Tri-Tip Bulgogi, and my favorite of the night, Galbi (Bone-in prime short rib marinated with Siu sauce).   All are thin cut and are easy, quick and fun to cook at your table. It was all delicious.  When I go back I know that I'd like to try some seafood and more vegetables too next time. 

It was day two of being open for them. So we were prepared for kinks. There really weren't any. Our table side fire went out once but they were super quick to re light it. Our service was impeccable, prompt, very helpful and friendly on every levels. Even the bussers and expediters were extra friendly, well spoken and very helpful to us. 

I plan to be a regular over here and since I can walk over that won't be too hard. I actually need to walk there and back. We were stuffed when we left.  Let me know if you're heading over. I might meet you there.

Best and most gluttonous breakfast in Sparks!   This is the place to go for the cheat meal of all cheat meals.  At least if you cheat at breakfast you still have the whole day to work it off, right?  The Sparks Marina is just down the road. Planning for at least a stroll right after breakfast wouldn't hurt anyone. I'm sure there is a way to go light here but I personally wouldn't try it at this place. 

BJ's BBQ, not to be confused with the BJ's Brewhouse chain of restaurants, has been around since I was a teenager. I actually worked in the same shopping center as them at an Ice cream shop that's no longer there and I remember taking lunch or dinner breaks there from time to time.  I was 16 or 17 back then.    They only started offering breakfast a few years ago after their big move to their location on Victorian Avenue.  While I am a fan of their lunch and dinner BBQ menu, this review is all about breakfast.

The Words from their own website say "Our breakfast offerings are house made, handmade and fresh" and there is nothing but truth in that boast. This is a true country style, stick to your ribs home style breakfast that reminds me so much of my own dearly missed but long gone from this earth, Arkansas born and raised- truly Southern Grandma Ora.  This is the kind of breakfast she would have and did serve us in her farmhouse. Yes, she lived in a small farmhouse on a walnut orchard. She was the epitome of a southern farmhouse granny. 

They've got the Reno breakfast vibe down too. Mimosas, Bloody Mary's, champagne and even beer are on the breakfast and brunch menu. If you're going to Glutton Town you might as well go all in,  maybe save that marina walk and head over to the Galaxy Theater Recliners first. 

The fluffy house made buttermilk biscuits with a cup of gravy on the side made me think of my grandma after one bite and the tender, breaded and perfectly seasoned chicken fried steak was served hot with a thick country gravy that's to die for. I try chicken fried steak at least once (rarely twice) at almost every breakfast place and this one is my favorite.  You can get this a la carte or you can get the full breakfast which also includes eggs, mine were scrambled and so fluffy and soft and some killer seasoned crispy home fries or you can get grits!

The skillet breakfasts are also absolutely wonderful, all large and full of the best tasting ingredients they could find. 

This is a great place for sharing, or taking a box home,  everything is huge.  It's also great for meeting family members, groups, kids, special occasions or just everyday.   It is not a great place for diets or calorie counting. You could pull it off but it wouldn't be as fun. It is perfect for a cheat day. Because it's worth the cheat. 

Expect to wait on the weekends. The breakfast awesomeness isn't so secret anymore.

This place was disguising! You should drop the east coast name because that is a disgrace to east coast food. Trying to pull off a steak um ( which is frozen poor quality meat) as a steak in cheese is cheap and shameful. Than load on lettuce and veggies to make up for the small amount of meat. Not only that garbage loaded up in the back near the kitchen. Too lazy to get rid of it? How clean is your kitchen then? Don't go there. You can get the same quality in the frozen food section at your local super market but better. Shameful!

The best bacon, egg, and cheese sandwich in West Philly. The steaks are pretty good, too. Cash only, but you get a little extra something (chips or a slice of cake) if you use their ATM. I only wish they were open on Sunday.

This place was in the Marina upstairs! Busy, loud! The food was fantastic! I loved the oysters and chowder and the Halibut! My wife liked her salad with shrimp and crab! I don't think I would go back only because it's so noisy! There are so many different flavors and restaurants that you can really eat day and night until you drop! The service was good plenty of help everywhere  if you needed something!

Being from Spain, I always look forward to trying new Spanish restaurants and Loquita did not disappoint! From the quality of the food and service to the ambiance, everything is a plus! My husband and his family surprised me with a dinner here for my birthday.

The exceptional service definitely stood out. From the very beginning, we felt cared for. Our server explained the menu for us in detail and was attentive refilling our drinks. They also brought a lovely birthday dessert and postcard for me which was very thoughtful.

It is hard to choose favorites because everything we tried was excellent. In terms of drinks, I ordered the Costa Blanca and the Ibiza. While the Costa Blanca was very refreshing and beautifully presented (definitely picture worthy!), I personally preferred the Ibiza. I ordered it without the firewater bitters and it was everything I was hoping for! The spray of mezcal was perfect and did not overpower the drink. 

Moving onto food, we ordered pulpo, jamón ibérico, patatas bravas, croquetas, and Manchego and Mahón cheeses to share. The plate with the cheeses came with membrillo, raisins, and pistachios. The croquetas were super tasty and I loved that they added jamón on top. We also had the paella mar y tierra which was a favorite of our party. This is the first time I've tried a paella with socarrat in California! This is the traditional way to cook paella in Cataluña/ Comunidad Valenciana where they leave a toasted and crispy layer of rice at the bottom of the pan. These are definitely my favorite bites!

Last but not least, the ambiance of their outdoor patio was very intimate and relaxing. I feel like Loquita is a must for anybody visiting Santa Barbara!

Omg omg omg..... I've read the reviews for this place and all I see are great ones. I thought, hmmm you can never have all great reviews for one place. Brunch had the most. Being a person that LOVES brunch, I was very curious as to what I would find here. #Pricey
....AND THEY HAVE UNLIMITED MIMOSAS!!!! Omg 

So today I decided to take myself out for Brunch, and when I got there I was greeted by the cutest lil hostess. I told her I wanted to be seated outside, since the view was another hot point mentioned
 She sat me in thee most perfect spot. I'm already loving this place. While walking through the dining area, there was 2 gorgeous gentlemen playing the acoustic guitar and it was such a beautiful sound...UGHHH I'm in love and I haven't even eaten yet.
So now, I'm sitting in a great spot and the mimosas are about to get started....Cranberry and Pineapple mix together....Yummyyyyy 
I make my way to the dining area after my sip of course, and OoooEmmmGeeee I was blown away. The spread was absolutely lost. I don't really remember it all, but here's to name a few:
Desserts 
Fresh Cheeses 
Caviar 
Seafood 
Create your own omelets w/ all kind of fixins, to include quail eggs...
Pasta
Salads
Sushi
...and the list goes on.

Yeah its a bit pricey, but not for all that you get... $55 
I would definitely pay that anytime for a spread like this....
I will ABSOLUTELY HANDS DOWN be back here again....

What do you get when you take a bunch of old shipping containers, paint them in bright happy colors, fill them with yummy food, and place them on a big plot of land right on the waterfront? That's Sparkman Wharf - a unique urban renewal idea that, based on the number of people who were there late on a weekday afternoon, really works.

Let's start with that plot of land, which is now a really nice green space where friends and family can hang out in lounge chairs, play cornhole toss, or enjoy a round or two of shuffleboard. There's quite a few food offerings, including an entry from Mise en Place, one of Tampa's best restaurants. (If you haven't been to the original Mise en Place, add that to your 'must do' list!) The beer garden brings 'Fermented Reality' to Sparkman Wharf, offering a wide variety of beers on tap, and to satisfy your sweet tooth, its Whatever Pops to the rescue.

This is a great option for both families with kids on a nice spring day, as well as for getting together with friends in the evening for some drinks under the stars. Indeed a cool concept, something uniquely Tampa - and, for me, I'd give this the thumbs-up over Ybor City, definitely more hip!

I was in the mood for a burger, so I headed down the street from my hotel to Commoner and sat at the bar, perusing the various bourbons on display while I waited... and waited... and waited. I was one of only three people sitting at the bar (the other two already eating their entrées), so it should be pretty noticeable when someone new sits at the long, open bar.

Despite two of these people coming within handshake distance of me several times, there was no greeting, no "Hey, we'll be with you in just a minute", no nothing. They were all so absorbed in what they were doing that I just couldn't get their attention or flag them down.

About ten minutes pass, still with no acknowledgment, so with the realization that I'm not going to be served anytime soon, it was obviously time to get up and leave -- and so I did. 

One of the biggest turnoffs to any diner is indifference by the staff. Bottom line: if you don't respect your customers time and aren't appreciative that they've walked through your doors, they you don't deserve the business, plain and simple.

Truly one of our (well, mine anyway--but I'm a lamb nut) fave spots.  
They never disappoint. The whole vibe says "you've left Clearwater..." (tongue-in-cheek here. I love where I live but let's face it, CW has improved a lot but has a ways to go before it's the Foodie Capital Of The World...).
When we are feeling like an upgrade to our date nights, we'll head over to The Little Lamb and treat ourselves.
Good news: it's not a budget increase particularly, relative to other date night joints. (Now I'm starting to wonder why we don't go here for all our date nights.  Could have something to do with wifey not being the creature of habit I can be. )
Try their homemade chicharrónes (pork rinds). Super tasty (and very keto if you're into that).
Their sides are always full of flavor and creativity, too. 
Anything on the menu is going to be delicious. They put their heart into it. You can tell.
Just can't say anything bad about The Little Lamb, especially now that they have more than doubled the size of their seating area.  
Suffice to say we'll continue being Frequent Eaters and are looking forward to our next date night there (don't tell my wife).

I've been hearing how great this place is from friends and coworkers for close to 20yrs but will admit that hearing it was in a gas station put me off from trying them out.  I regret that I had doubts!  
They have a variety of fresh baked breads and their meats are top notch in flavor.  These are very generous sandwiches, my Italian sub almost had too much meat.  The favorite would be their version of the Cuban.  The Carnitas used for the roast pork plus the Salami and Ham made for such a cravable sandwich.  They seem pricey but the medium sandwich will feed two adults generously, generally a mini would suffice for an average appetite imo, but you'll probably want to get a "small (5 inch)" at least just because they are so delicious!

lovely quaint little house serving up equally lovely crepes and a small selection of baked goods.  Once word gets out I can see them having an issue of space like their other venture Sup.  They do have a nice patio area set up once the weather warms up, and it looks promising.  They have a paved brick area separated by sculptural metal planters that I imagine will be planted with a lovely assortment of flowers and greens that will make the space very cozy.  The inside of the house is very sunny and clean, with an interesting glazed but "undone" floor and some local art decorating the walls. 

I had the Farmhouse crepe and opted for salad and a side of country potatoes.  The presentation is very pretty (in fact I overheard Kasey explaining to another customer how the appearance of the food is important to her, and I agree.  "you eat with your eyes first")  The portions are light, but not "small" imo.  Actually I think it's just right to satisfy but not make you feel grossly stuffed and heavy after breakfast, but I can see those with bigger appetites, namely men, complaining that there isn't enough food.  The crepes are tender and made with a golden eggy batter as opposed to the thin crispy batter you'd get with a Japanese style crepe a la Van Nam.  I first had savory crepes in San Francisco, and these aren't the same type.  Those are usually very large folded crepes, these are smaller more delicately rolled ones.  One thing I really enjoyed is that the bacon was crispy!  I hate soggy or chewy bacon.   The flavors are clean and straightforward.  Good textures and freshness throughout.  I wasn't crazy about the side of potatoes, they were pan fried potatoes with onion and cheese on top.  The onions were a little underdone and not really caramelized enough.  I'd like it with no cheese but maybe some other savory vegetables in lieu (mushrooms, green pepper?),  I didn't order any sweets, but sampled the coffee cake and the 7 layer bar.  The 7 layer bar is a decadent but easy to make pan cookie.  The coffee cake was moist and had great cinnamon sugar flavor.  I really want to try their Earl Grey Brulee, but didn't bring the appetite for it this time.  

I will be back, and bringing others.  Their price range is extremely reasonable for the quality and low enough that I may become a regular without guilt.

I walked in this place a little bit skeptical.  Partially because Nashville doesn't do fancy as well as they do dive-y.  Mostly because when Nashville does do fancy, it's hit or miss with the snooty-factor.  This place definitely did right by Nashville!  And by my visiting mother, who was looking for a nice night with a decent cocktail and a light meal.

I arrived expecting a somewhat emtpied out restaurant, with 20-somethings crowding the bar.  I was shocked to find a pretty wide ensemble of people, and a crowded date-night scene.  The bar was open, so we sat there and got right down to brass tacks.  The drink menu.

Great selection of wines, and a lovely little list of martinis and refreshing cocktails.  I went with a dry, nutty Shiraz, while boyfriend took on a deliciously spicy and fruity Syrah.  My mom went for the gold and beat us both with her Pumpkin Martini.  All were delicious!

The food is no sham either.  We each enjoyed a delicious meal, all sporting very different flavors and varieties.  I had the Chilean sea bass, my mom enjoyed the salmon, and boyfriend took it home with the pot pie.  Spectacular plates.

I thoroughly enjoyed my experience.  Cheers to the wonderful bartenders!

For starters, to allay any confusion, this is not a gay bar. Its right in the middle of the grove, which has a lot of LGBT establishments, but this one is unaffiliated.

I have come here on a few occasions, mainly for late night (its open til 3 am) and once for trivia. On every occasion, I've had an awesome time. Its a very cool space, with a large indoor bar area and an outdoor patio. 

They have an awesome beer selection and great specials (if you check on yelp you get $1 off your first drink :)).

There typically is a small cover when coming out here on the weekend and the place is converted to a large dance party (mostly), whereas during the week its a reasonably mild mannered hipster bar/restaurant.

I have yet to eat here, but apparently they have great russian food and pizza. 

However, I can firmly endorse it as a solid late night spot (i'd probably only 2nd to Talayna's) and for their impressively challenging thrusday night trivia.

I've been to NOLA many times but on this trip we wanted to learn more about the dark secrets of its past. We did a ghost and vampire tour and thought it would only be fitting to eat here after. It came highly recommended by our tour guide. I thought for sure they all work together and he sends everyone here, so I set my expectations low. With Covid protocols, we were asked for vaccine cards and tables were far apart from each other. The place had a cool, dark vibe to it and it fit the theme of the name of the place. Dario was our most excellent server and he did an awesome job from start to finish. 

We started off with drinks. The drink menu has cool names of different blood types. I had to go with a blood bag cocktail because it just looked cool. Come to find out, their drinks were very well crafted and very tasty. I couldn't make up my mind about going for a burger or a proper entree, but Dario said the Dracula Burger was where it was at. He was not wrong. Hands down one of the best burgers I've had. I've thought about it since I've been back home. I'm not a blue cheese fan but was told all the flavors worked together and they did. The house made chips that came with it was outstanding as well. We shared an order of duck fat fingerling potatoes and Brussels sprouts as well and they were so good too. Dario also took care of my birthday girl as we were ready to leave. He heard it in passing that we were celebrating and he made us wait for a special shot and we got to serenade her before we left. Special touch that goes a long way in my book!

I will definitely make this a must stop every time I'm in town. I don't do that for many places on vacay, but this place won me over!

Vacationing in New Orleans, I thought I bookmarked all the food that I wanted to try.  The Ruby Slipper somehow slipped right by me.  After a night of walking the night before, I did not want to make a far trek to breakfast.  This particular location happened to be just a block over on Canal.  It was a Thursday morning so we thought there would not be a crowd, but we did have to wait about 20 minutes, which seemed to be our wait at almost every place we tried.  This city is definitely a foodies paradise.  We got seated and our waited Justin greeted us.  Within a couple of minutes, our drink orders were delivered and he took our orders.

We had a table of 7, and everyone ordered different things.  Benedicts were the popular choice, and the Peacemaker allows you to pick 2 of their 6 benedicts.  Between all of us, we had all of them except the Corned Beef Benne.  I had the Chicken St. Charles and the Eggs Blackstone.  The chicken dish had a perfectly seasoned, crispy chicken breast on top of a fluffy biscuit, with a perfectly poached egg on top, then topped with a delicious cream sauce.  The Eggs Blackstone was bacon and tomato on top of a biscuit, with a poached egg on top of that, then finished with a creamy hollandaise sauce.  Both benedicts were out of this world good!  We all passed our plates around and every single dish was great.  The favorite among the table was the Banana Foster Pain Perdu that my daughter ordered.  It had the taste of New Orleans that was all loved.  

From start to finish, we were extremely satisfied with the service, as well as the food here.  Being lazy that day paid off!

All the birthday girl wanted was a nice brunch before we headed back home to Houston. The problem was, we waited too long to make reservations thinking we could get lucky while we were in town. Come to find out, NOLA really loves brunch!  All the popular spots were booked or had crazy waits. We decided to just walk the French Quarter and hopefully find a hidden gem. After a few misses, we found this spot. It looked nice and quaint and there was no wait. I saw the not so great reviews but decided to give them a chance anyways. That's where I went wrong. Never go against Yelpers advise!!  This place was a disaster. Service was super slow and the server was just going through the motions. Our food came out and it looked really good, but most of the food was just barely warm. My platter was fried seafood and only one thing was piping hot. Flavors were there on my plate, but totally missed the mark with temps. For flavor alone I bumped them up to two stars. We sent back plate after plate which I absolutely hate doing. Definitely skip this place if you are in the Big Easy!

Great place with very personable owners and managers. Went for a birthday last week September 19,2015, and had a great time. Musician outside was great. Everything was quaint and the food was very good. Would go back to again as well as recommend!

Normally when I think of dining out I don't think a driving up into a strip mall and going into someplace with a rather exotic name, but that's just what happened one night last week.

I opted to sit outside, which was basically some chairs and tables on the sidewalk pretty much in the parking lot, yeah I know this sounds like it's going to be an interesting review!

The server was a wonderful and attentive woman with a personality, and sense of humor, which I can always appreciate.

The menu had a lot of good things to choose from and the portions were big enough that I ate all I could, and took quite a bit of it home!

My suggestion to you is that you go at night so that your surroundings do not remind you that you're sitting in a parking lot of the strip mall , and it's a bit quieter, as the traffic slows down off the Main Street.

Um, yeah. Noisy, and like being in college with a bunch of underaged kids just trying to get drunk. The dj music is too loud and the karaoke, is downright obnoxious!

As as grownup, this place is annoying, best bet is to find a more age appropriate place. First daters? You won't get a word in at all!

Really cool place. However the food is awful. Looked terrible. The tomatoes were fake as fuck, how do I know- tomatoes have seeds- theirs had no seeds. Took a few bites and I bit into something rock like in my sandwich. I could fee the minerals of whatever I bit get wedged into the crevices of my teeth. I'd go with the tenders. Fantastic customer service and great atmosphere- god awful food. Your choice. Way over priced for the quality, I could have made a better sandwich for 16 dollars

I love Uchi Sushi! It's the most delicious sushi! We've been coming here since it was Little Tokyo and it's actually where my husband and I first came for our first date! 
We come here all the time and the sushi is impeccable! We recently went to a wedding a couple of weeks ago that actually had Johnny (the owner) there making sushi for everyone! How great! A sushi bar at a wedding plus it being my favorite sushi place! 
We went last night for Hibachi (and some sushi) to mainly keep our toddler and baby entertained while we eat and service was great from the ladies, but the Hibachi came out a little slowly. I do love coming here because all the ladies love our babies! Tip: If you have a baby at your table, then you might get better service! 
Anyway, the food was fantastic, our kids ate everything and so did we and all the sushi is so fresh. We will consistently always come back here. I'm giving it a 4 stars because sometimes the service is a little slow (if you don't bring your baby).

You want a good hot dog? You got a good hot dog.

Here it is folks - the best dog with all the best toppings you could ever want. I will definitely be coming here again. I drive past this little corner strip mall regularly and now I will be tempted every time. Just great.

I got the buffalo chicken dog and mac n cheese fry, with some root beer (great brand by the way). The dog was cooked nicely so it's not dry or too mushy, and then the topping was shredded chicken that's got all those tasty sauces your heart desires. My frys were crispy and not floppy, piled with mac n cheese with bacon bits on top. My mouth is watering again...

And oh the choices! The menu is as tall as me. There's seriously something for everyone here. Unless you can't eat meat or fried things... then you might be SOL. Highly recommend!

Went here for Downtown Restaurant Week recently and this place is definitely worth another visit. We had great service, the food and drinks were delicious, and I'm liking the vibe here. Love the big booths!

I had the chicken satay with peanut sauce for the starter (on their regular menu). The chicken came skewered and grilled, not very moist, but great flavor. The peanut sauce was the bomb-dot-com and I will have my eye out for this again - sweet and creamy.

Main course was miso salmon with herbs pesto, roasted cauliflower, and radish (most similar to their grilled salmon on their regular menu). The salmon was perfectly cooked so not too dry and it was super tender - even the scales!

Dessert was the coconut tapioca pudding with mango compote and toasted coconut flakes (not on their typical menu but their Vietnamese coffee ice cream has the coconut flakes). The tapioca was awesome and I wasn't a super big fan of the crispy coconut flakes in contrast but overall still a delicious dish.

Love this place! They serve delicious Perc coffee, espresso drinks, and some beer and wine. The food is great - I've had one of the loaded toasts and would definitely get it again. The atmosphere is modern hipster and there are bluegrass bands that play on the weekends. My only complaint about this is that they are LOUD. I can barely carry on a conversation when they have music sometimes. It's a great addition to the neighborhood and is filling a need the Shaw neighborhood wants - a great cafe and great coffee. I'll be coming here many times in future and I can't wait for their patio to open!

I can hardly believe I neglected to review one of my favorite sweet shops in Reno! 

I stopped in to pick up a treat for my wife who loves the chocolate covered coffee beans but my order didn't stop there! I spied a few bags of the peppermint bark which we both fell in love with over the month of December. I think each of us consumed 2 bags all on our own. I got us a bag to share, it is almost demoed already! This stuff is the perfect thickness and has a perfect amount of peppermint flavor. The milk and white chocolate melt in your mouth and it's a treat we found ourselves reaching for repeatedly in December. I was thrilled to luck into another bag this late in January. I can guarantee this will be a stocking stuffer treat yearly now. 

Dorinda- please keep carrying this!

I also picked up a few truffles. The lemon is one of my favorites. I also got a peppermint one which was equally delicious. The best treat from this trip was the peppermint chocolate melt-a-way. It was incredibly decadent in the best way possible. I hope they will continue carrying this all year because it has become my new favorite treat from Dorinda's.

This place is a perfect spot to grab sweets for your sweet, yourself, and any friends visiting the area. It has a little something for every sweet tooth.

For once I found myself on this side of town early enough to get a cronut. These things sell out quickly so they are hard to catch. I decided to grab one for myself and one for the wife. I also ended up with a random donut thanks to their check-in offer to get one for free. 

I have to say that the customer service would lend me to giving them a 2 star review. I wasn't greeted when I walked in. The person who I gave my order to didn't say anything to me at all. I had to ask her to go over the cronut flavors with me. She was obviously not thrilled to have to do this. Why can't they just put signs in front of them like those fancy bakeries? The cashier wasn't rude but definitely wasn't pleasant either. She huffed after I paid and didn't leave a tip. I might have considered tipping had I actually received any customer service that was worth rewarding. I didn't.

The products deserved a 4 star but that didn't raise my rating review due to the lack of customer service. I wouldn't even bring this up if it weren't a constant problem. I haven't ever had good customer service here. I keep coming back because I like the product and I keep hoping the customer service will improve. It hasn't.

The cronuts are really good. I've had a variety of different flavors but honestly, the simpler the better. The triple chocolate with raspberry jelly was just too much. It doesn't need all of that. I would have been happy with just the chocolate drizzle on top. The jelly made the interior ring of the donut mushy and slimy. The regular chocolate frosted donut was dry and nothing to write home about. I can get a better one at several other places in town. 

If you want regular donuts, go elsewhere in town. Trust me. If you want designer donuts, be prepared for a good product but crappy service. Don't say I didn't warn you.

I would have breakfast for every meal of the day if my wife would let me! Stonehouse is one of our favorite local spots in town and was my first choice when my wife asked where I wanted to have my birthday breakfast. I love the wonderful french toast and was very excited to hear about their latest special,the  2 and 2, which is two pieces of french toast and two eggs with bacon or sausage. I love to balance my early morning sugar intake with some protein so this special was right up my alley. I really hope it sticks around because it's now my new favorite breakfast. Our server was fantastic, as was the meal. We will definitely be back again soon. The french toast cravings have already begun!
