I was looking for a place to have brunch with a friend and stumbled upon Half & Half on Yelp. We were fortunate to arrive in time to avoid the wait as we sat on the counter with a view of the open kitchen and the rest of the dining area. The white-colored walls and tiled floors presented a pristine, airy look. The makeup complemented nicely within the well-lit venue filled with a mix of artificial and natural sunlight. The noise level was high, but the vibe was inclusive with the elderly, couples, hipsters, and families with young children bursting at all corners.

The Salmon Hash ($14) was served in a piping hot skillet filled to the brim with two sunny side up eggs, potatoes, chives, spinach, capers, and hollandaise sauce. The mix of salmon and potatoes were chunky, buttery, and flavorful. Adding to the mix was a handful of spinach and capers that brought a backdrop of sweet and salty olive-like sensibilities to the dish. We asked for one of the eggs to be well done and the other ooey gooey soft and goodie in the middle and they were perfectly executed. We also asked for the hollandaise sauce to be served on the side, and it was custard thick, creamy, and sinfully delicious. The concerts of all the flavors made the hollandaise unnecessary but still much appreciated since I'm a big fan of the sauce.

The Clara Cake ($9.50) arrived with a stack of pancakes piled high and wide adorned with granola on top, fresh raspberries in between, and a load of creamy mascarpone at the core that oozed out at will as I cut into the stack with tremendous ease. The raspberries came with lots of seeds that made it difficult to bite into, but all flavor and fluffy textures made it a wonderful pick. The quality of their pancakes was topnotch so next time I would love to give their Blueberry Pancakes ($8.50) a chance. 

Many of the reviewers have complained about their handcrafted coffee, but their Orange Juice ($3.75) was squeezed on site loaded with freshness and spurts of wow factor here and there. The only complaint I had was the Doughnuts ($4.50) that were also known as beignets in St. Louis. They turned out to be fat pieces of Mexican churros embodied with a hint of citrus on the inside and laden with sugar on the golden brown exterior. The churros were soggy and the form and flavor didn't keep very well. I brought them back to the hotel to share with my Mexican friends and they were not impressed. 

All was forgiven, as service was attentive, friendly, and personable. We were offered refilled for our drinks and the used dishes were constantly replaced with new ones so the counter was kept clean and comfortable throughout the visit. By this time we were entering their peak hours, but the owner still stopped by to introduce himself and invited us back to try their new dinner menu with a focus on Mexican cuisine.

Fortunately, we didn't have to go through the complaints that were experienced by other reviewers regarding the long wait, expensive coffee, or the lack of service. I do agree that the prices were slightly higher than expected, especially the churros, but the number of wow factors and ginormous portions made the visit worthwhile. As someone who has experienced a lion share of rubbery boring pancakes, I would love to come back again. 4.5 stars for the overall experience.

Twenty-five of us were looking for a late night eatery, and a quick search on Yelp led us to this Chinatown restaurant. Initially, the server said over the phone that they are able to host a group of this size, but the interior turned out a lot smaller than we had envisioned. Upon entering, you will see a score of small tables tightly stacked together and two larger ones in the back. Seated elbow to elbow, we easily took over this hole in the wall for several hours on this very late evening.

Shrimp Wonton Soup ($15.75/4 people serving size): Great size of pork and shrimp wontons, perfectly thin wrapper, firm shrimp textures, and light tasting soup. One of the best wontons I have tasted. Plenty of wontons for four, but the price was way too high.

Seafood Tofu Hotpot ($13.50): The seafood was plump and juicy. Among the seafood, I enjoyed the large slices of fish filets and scallops. The fried tofu cubes were silky soft on each bite. This is my favorite dish of the night. I could sit there and eat the tofu all day. 

Chicken with Black Bean Sauce ($9.50) Great black bean stir-fry. Juicy and moist chicken. Great addition of onions and scallions to layer on top of the deepening black bean flavor. 

Shredded Chicken Black Bean Pan Fried Noodles ($8.50): The noodles were crisp and softened by the black bean stir-fry. The taste of the chicken was nicely integrated and flavorful. The same can be said about the House Pan-Fried Noodles with Shrimp, Chicken, and Beef ($14.50), as there was a good amount of toppings to go around, and the noodles were crisp and soft in all the right places. 

Beef with Scallion and Ginger ($10.50): The scallion and ginger stir-fry had good form to add to the tender and flavorful slices of beef. This was one of the highlights of the night.

Vegetarian Singapore Noodles with Tofu ($10.50): Nice curry flavor, and the noodles were fried to dry with good separation. However, I thought the additional $2 charge on the tofu was a rip off. Since we ordered so much food, I didn't like how they nickled and dimed us on this particular plate.

Beef Ho Fun ($9.50): The thick flat noodles were slippery and easy to separate. The beef again was tender and flavorful with good chew. This was another highlight for us.

Asparagus Chicken ($12.95): Nice thick and firm asparagus and the thick chicken slices were easy to bite into. They seemed to be able to bring out the flavors in simple dishes in complicated way.

Shrimp Fried Rice ($7.95): Wok fried rice with eggs, onions, and bean sprout. Nice texture coming from the onions and bean sprouts as the rice was airy and dried. The scrambled egg added a finesse element, and the wok fried flavor made it delicious.

Overall, the flavors on each dish were surprisingly tasty, had good form steeped in Cantonese traditions, nice wok fry wow factor, and tremendous food temperature. In addition to my complaints about the prices, each dish also came out one at a time, prompting those who ordered last to get their food when everyone else had already finished. Structurally, this was probably not the most ideal place for a group of our size. Given the number of competitions in the area, I would only return for late night small gatherings, and all food, no-frills experiences.

A group of us came to grab BBQ in St. Louis and a quick check on the Yelp App led us to The Shaved Duck. This is one of the few restaurants that were open till 10pm and the vibe was hipsterish with a gastropub set up. There was a full bar that faced the entrance followed by a dim-lit dining area culminated by red brick walls and photos and paints of all shapes and sizes. The wait was 40 minutes long so we spent a good amount of time chatting by the bar before getting seated. 

The menu was filled with smokehouse specialties so I decided to get the Big Jimmy Sampler ($19.00) that came with three ribs, beef briskets, pulled pork, pulled chicken, garlic bread and my choice of mac n' cheese on the side. All the options came with a hint of smoke and the ribs and pulled pork were particularly appetizing. The meat was tender with a hint of sweet smoky undertone. Too bad the brisket and pulled chicken weren't a match as the texture was dry and rough so they didn't make the grade. Portions were fabulous but I was expecting better quality from this sampler. 

Another disappointing part of the meal was the BBQ sauce. The flavors from the three options were really watered down and not as spicy, bold, or innovative as they could be.

The mac n' cheese came highly recommended by the server and interestingly the texture was firm and rather delicious. I wasn't keen on the cream sauce with which was embedded in, and would have preferred something cheesier that gives me the baked stringy effect.  I also had the chance to try my friend's coleslaw and it tasted more like raw vegetables than a true slaw. In all, I'd say 3 stars for the food.

The dessert happens to be the turning point as the Pumpkin Pie with Vanilla Ice Cream ($6.50) was truly outstanding. The presentation was not striking but the flavor was creamy delicious with a rich pumpkin flavor from start to finish. The ice cream was outstanding too. Unlike those watery versions I've encountered in the past, it was thick, rich, and pointed with vanilla bean flavor. Nothing fancy, but the entire baseline expectations were covered with the pie carrying the wow factor from one spoon to the next.

The Apple Cobbler with Vanilla Ice Cream ($6.50) was equally outstanding. It was served hot with a giant scoop of Vanilla Ice Cream that refused to melt. The Cobbler was sweetened by fresh apples with a degree of finessed subtle flavors and a nice touch of texture. The executive chef's mom had made these desserts so I wasn't surprised at how the dessert was able overshadow the main course. 

Without the desserts, Jethro's is still the better choice for BBQ. Service was friendly and adequately attentive. I enjoyed the festive atmosphere and would be interested in coming back for their live music. Many reviewers seem to like their smoked meatloaf so that might be the better thing to get for those interested. With mixed results, 3 stars for the overall experience.

I was taking a stroll in Chinatown looking to grab lunch and the Yelp App led me to this Szechuan restaurant. From left to right, the med-size banquet style seating arrangement was eye-pleasing, and included two rows of lazy Susans and booths vertically stacked. The lunch crowd was minimal with a quiet atmosphere. It's a fitting place for lunch or dinner for small and large groups alike.

The Conch Meat with Hot Oil ($12.95) came with fresh and crunchy conch, thinly sliced, and seasoned with Szechuan ma la spicy hot sauce. I loved the thickness of the conch and the way it was cut. It came with fresh crunchy textures, and the numb and spicy effect was on point and not intolerable. The shaved green onions were sharp and sweet to cut the spiciness in-between bites. Price was very good considering the amount of conch I got. This is a dish I would love to have again.

The Sauteed Black Fungus and Squash ($10.95) came with plenty of wood ear and Chinese squash stir-fried to perfection. The core of the squash was still firm, and crunchy wood ear added further textures. The dish was flavorful and the overall taste had form.

Service was the only downside on this visit. The server had a hands-off approach and no one seemed particularly friendly and warm. Otherwise, the complimentary tea and sauteed peanuts were very nice gestures. It was an outstanding meal. I'd be very interested in coming back to try their hot pot, mapo tofu, and other Szechuan flavors.

Just a note: I never tried the food here so this review is for the bar, staff, and venue itself.

This is a very classy looking joint. I could envision taking a hot date (aka La Novia) to a place like this. The bartender was talkative and friendly, but not particulary knowledgable on beer brands. He had no idea there was an alternative to Negra Modelo, which is the lighter colored version called Modelo Especial. 

The beer selection here was limited, but the Negra Modelo hit the spot.

My uncle insists I need to come back and try the food. Based on the price of the beer, the food might be pricey.

I hope he is paying.

Just a note: I never tried the food here so this review is for the bar, staff, and venue itself.

This was part of a bar/pub/restaurant crawl I went on with my dad and uncle in Philadelphia. As my uncle lives in Philly, he wanted to show us around town and where he usually hangs out, drinks and womanizes. Hey, I guess it runs in the family.

This place is a classy looking joint, with a nice set up, cool looking basket chairs that hang from the ceiling on the upper level of the restaurant, and a gorgeous outside terrace overlooking the nicer area of Philadelphia up on the second floor.

The bartenders were nice and cheerful. The Guinness was delicious. And it tasted so much better in the fabulous 70-degree weather out on the terrace.

When I come back to Philly, I will need return here to try the food while sitting in one of those basket chairs.

In all of my travels, this is one of the better restaurants I have dined in since it offers such a unique experience every time you eat here due to the menu changing every day. So instead of reviewing what I had for dinner that you probably will not see on your menu, I will instead review my experience. Each and every day, the chef comes up with a pre fixe menu where you can pick three to four courses from four to six different menu items. Sometimes you can pick between two apps, two entrees, and two desserts. But unlike whether you choose to pull out or not, there is no wrong choice to be made on this menu. Each dish ranges from really good to really great. 

For those that learn visually, the daily menu will sort of looks like this:

Course 1:

or

Enjoy!

For my 600th review, I have opted to skip a few New York joints on my recent east coast trip and flash forward over to my super fun and freakin' fantastic Philadelphia food experience at Fogo de Chao.

This is a Brazilian steakhouse that is made for people with huge appetites and zero remorse for eating animals. So with that said, my uncle took my dad and I here for my dad's birthday.

For $55 person, before tax & tip, you get this:

1) A trip to an amazing salad bar that features all kinds of good stuff, namely aged cheese, shitake mushrooms, and some of the best asparaghus you will ever have. But don't spend too much time here as you will not have enough room in your stomach for part 2.

2) An all you can eat meat extravaganza. Flip over your card from "red" to "green" and the meat cutter server guys start to come by with all kinds of Brazilian style meats, such as picanha (top sirlion), bacon wrapped filet mignon (amazing), and the orgasm inducing, beef ancho (prime of rib eye).

FDC also features killer fraldihna (bottom sirloin), yummy costela (ribs), super excellent and fresh cordero (lamb), very juicy and savory frango (chicken), tasty costella de porco , exceptional lombo (pork loin), and above average linguica (sausage). 

If you are a first timer, I suggest asking the servers for small cuts so you can figure out what you like most and request more later. My favorites were the picanha, bacan wrapped filet mignon, beef ancho, cordero, and frango. 

3) Tasty side dishes like garlic mashed potatoes, buttery bread, and caramalized bananas

4) You also receive spectacular service. The guys working that night were friendly, fast, and efficient. One server said:

"Hey, when you aren't taking orders, you have no excuse for screw ups."

Also, the guys are very attentive. I think they heard me say, "happy birthday" to my dad when we first started eating and at the end of the meal, the guys presented my dad with an amazing flan that was on the house.

5) A smile on everyone's face after dinner as they rub their bellies.

So if you have a huge appetite, and are looking for a wonderful meat eating experience, you should head to Fogo de Chao, which has several locations across the United States and Brazil.

Now if only they would open one up in the Bay Area!

Every single time I visit a new city outside of the Bay Area, I need to do at least three things. 

1) See the sights.
2) Try a signature dish or food item from that particular city.
3) Karaoke.

So #2 is why I came here. The line to eat here went out the door and circled around the corner. But in the end, this place is a tourist trap.

The cheesesteak sandwich here is mediocre. Nothing is fresh. The beef is bland and tasteless, the bread is a bit soggy, the peppers and mushrooms are canned, and the staff is surly and rude. 

One guy that was more rude than the rest was the guy bussing tables upstairs in the seating area barely wiped the table I was going to eat on. He was definitely too fat to bend over and wipe it properly. And at the end of the meal, he got mad at me for not putting a can on top of the garbage for them to recycle it. He pointed to a different bin that said "CANS" but it was so scratched up it looked like it said "CRAP" to me. Sure, he has a job to bus tables and clean up litter in that upstairs area, but he is too fat and lazy to get up and put the can in the right spot. He'd rather place his body against the wall and take out his frustration on me. Get up, fat boy, and do your damn job!

Philadelphia is a great city and they invented the cheesesteak sandwich; but in the end, they just taste better in the Bay Area since we have fresh produce and can use fresh mushrooms and peppers.

I love reviews that say "just ignore every bad review."  Yeah, right.

I am half-expecting to see Ellendale's on an upcoming episode of Kitchen Nightmares.  It has all the elements - a once bustling restaurant with some semblance of history has fallen into disrepair.  Guest counts are declining as word gets out about how it "isn't as good as it used to be."  Management starts trying to save money by carrying less staff, buying cheaper ingredients and putting off necessary repairs, wondering how they can reverse the decline and worrying about what the coming months have in store.

The venue is nice enough and the staff is well-meaning, but the food is rough.  Came for Sunday brunch - they opened late, most stations were not ready, and some of the food was downright inedible.  The catfish, for example, should have been called 'semi-fried grease with fish texture.'  

The meal was salvaged by a made-to-order omelet, but this place needs to find its way out of its death spiral.

This was my first time trying PGC and overall the food was so good. 

I got the California Love (Chicken and Waffles) and my favorite part about the dish wash the creamy PGC sauce. It was so sweet and savory that I wanted more! Everything about this dish was savory and deelishis. The chicken was fried perfectly and the piece was huge. The waffle was fluffy and freshly made in front of me. I used the PGC sauce to spread on top of the waffle.

Service was good. Our waiter was attentive and because we sat at the bar, the women cooking even came over to check on us. 

The only downside was they charge for water. Didn't realize that until after the fact. Our bill was $100 between the three of us so expect to spend some money compared to other popular brunch locations. I still plan to try dinner next.

I recently read online that the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino had just completed a $700 million dollar expansion, so of course my curiosity got the best of me and forced me to visit.  I hadn't been by the place in a good six months, and just wanted to take it all in with the sole intention of giving my two cents (never in a million years would I ever think about indulging in drinking, or betting actual money in this sinner's paradise, as I am a wholesome, god fearing Christian that lives my life on the straight and narrow). The promo card I received in the mail for a free $15 comp also may have played a rather small part in my attendance. 
     My best friend is a frequent guest, so when I suggested that we go take a gander, he was more than accommodating as he had already seen the new digs and wanted to give me a personal tour. Well folks, I have to say that I was more than impressed. If you've been to the "Hard Rock" before, you'd know that it was a cool place and was more than adequate with it's gaming and entertainment value. Think of those past experiences, and multiply them by 100. The place is almost unrecognizable. The level of detail and nuance is amazing. The entire layout has been upgraded, and really resembles a high end Las Vegas casino (yes, I've been to Vegas many times). 
     A bunch of new specialty shops, a high end desert shop with incredible pastries, cakes, and gelatos. A cigar shop with a crazy array of selections and humidors. A high end wine store, again with a large selection of mid to upper level bottles, including a sommelier on staff for those posh individuals who need attention and help spending lavish amounts of money. A handful of new restaurants including an Italian eatery that had a couple of either wood or coal fire pizza ovens blazing as you walked by. And on top of all these new amenities, a giant new 550-room hotel (dubbed the "East hotel tower", as opposed to the existing hotel known as the West hotel tower). I was honestly blown away with how nice and spanking new everything was, hell even the old food court looked great!
     Of course (and there's always an "of course"), you need to be careful with your wallet because your green backs can fly away rather quickly, so make sure you take everything in knowing that your visit should only come when you have a decent amount of disposable cash that you can afford to spend/lose. The food and fun come at a high price, but there's always that chance you get lucky, so my advice is go for it Rock! At the very least you will have a great time seeing all of the new digs, as well as all of the colorful characters. This place was built for people watching, and because it's the size a few airport terminals, you can easily blow a few hours just walking around.

The beauty of YELP is that no matter where you are, you have the local culinary world at your fingertips. With that in mind, I was recently in Plant City dropping off a friend who had a "legal" appointment (I'll stop at legal because that is an entirely long story in and of itself). I had about an hour to kill while waiting for said friend, and because it was close to lunchtime I figured I'd take a gander at what Plant City had to offer in relation to my appetite. 
     If you're from the Tampa Bay Area, you've heard of Plant City, mostly because it is known as the Winter Strawberry Capital of the World and hosts the annual Florida Strawberry Festival, which is absolutely amazing and definitely a bucket list destination, but I digress. Most of Plant City is an old farming community, so where oh where was I going to find some good grub in a town named after a railroad pioneer? There in lies why YELP is such an incredible app. 
     After a quick scan, I was excited to see a place that I'd read about years ago as having one of the best Cuban sandwiches in the country. I can't recall the article (definitely some foodie site), but the Strawberry Hut was listed as being in the top 10 in the U.S. as a sandwich destination, not a bad reputation to have in tiny little Plant City! I quickly plotted the address into my WAZE app, and was there in 10 minutes. If the monarch to never judge a book by its cover was ever true, this was the place. It honestly looks like the remnants of an old drive-thru movie theater snack bar (yes, I realize I'm dating myself here, so you millennials will need to Google that reference). 
     The menu is small, and all of the sandwiches are referenced as Cuban style (Turkey Cuban, Cheeseburger Cuban, Veggie Cuban), but they also have soup, salads, and shakes, and a really killer looking breakfast menu. I ordered a regular Cuban of course, and feeling cheeky, also got a Philly Cuban. To say I was more than impressed would be an understatement. The bread was pressed perfectly, nice and crispy with that buttery flavor on the outside, but still perfectly chewy on the inside. The entire sandwich just melted in my mouth and was just delicious, so much so that I almost ordered another one to go. The Philly was also delicious, again with the perfectly pressed bread, but my only gripe would be that there wasn't much meat on it (give me more of that awesomeness!!!). 
     It's probably a good thing that this place is about 35 minutes from my house, as I could easily see myself here once or twice a week, but I promise I will be back! (Okay, maybe just twice a month). Do yourself a favor and make the trip out if you're in the Bay Area. the "Hut" is the freaking BOMB!

And thanks for the all breakfast you don't have.

As I was ready to ordered, I was greeted by one of the barista here. Ordered an hot mocha. I must say the mocha I got was pretty strong. Really like how strong it was, woke me up throughout the day during my day off from work. 

Service here was pretty good. Very nice baristas here. And it was fast too. Seating area was pretty decent, some college students hang out with their laptop to do some studying. And there's some outlets too if you want to charge your electronics.

Christopher M.
