Food and service were standard. If you've been to one OG then you've been to them all. The franchise prices are high in my opinion.

We seated ourselves at the bar and were placed with plates, chopsticks, and a warmed moist towelette (common in actual Japanese restaurants!)

They started us with complimentary edamame and miso. The edamame was pretty clearly defrosted from frozen as it had a mushy bite, but the miso was tasty and had a good temperature.

We ordered a Philly roll, Vegas roll, spider roll, and naked scallop roll. We also had the Thai chicken wings, which were just fatty baked wings with a side of Thai sweet and tangy dipping sauce. Everything was made quickly came out in less than 5 minutes. The rolls were 3-star caliber in my opinion. 

The bill was a bit on the mid to expensive side but great service all around. Our waiter was very attentive and friendly.

Top golf is popping up in every major American city and Tucson is now fortunate to have one! 

This location is the best I've ever been to in terms of wait time. We were assigned a bay within 5 minutes of registering. Most times, we'd have to wait 45 min-2 hours and just kill time in the restaurant or playing pool in the complimentary game room. 

The menu has something for everyone. It's American pub food at a decent price. The Cobb salad was an appropriate to large serving size. I very much recommend their flatbread pizzas! Their desserts are also very very good. 

I was pleasantly surprised that heaters were installed. It was a beautiful day to be outdoors but a little chilly for Tucson so the warmth was a welcome addition.

The player console is very user friendly and offers several very fun games to play with your party. I'd recommend at least 3-4 guests to make the stay worth your money because it's $25 an hour. They also offer their own sets of men's and women's clubs. You are welcome to bring your own if you prefer.

After browsing several Tucson Valentine menus, I decided to make a reservation for my fiance's birthday which also happens to fall on Valentine's Day. Their dishes seemed right up my alley. I've had my choices lined up for almost two weeks.

In hindsight Valentine's Day probably wasn't a great night to come. The restaurant was (hopefully abnormally) swamped; we weren't getting great attention from our waiter but I understand she had multiple tables to which she had to attend. Every table was occupied. The chairs were decorated with helium valentine colored balloons. 

I started with the lobster bisque which had only minute bites of lobster meat. It was flavorful and had lots of textures including croutons, fried leeks, and potato chunks. I made the mistake of choosing paella for my entree. The rice was overcooked and soggy and the seafood was rubbery. To their credit presentation of my plate and everything else I saw coming out of the kitchen was great. Finally dessert was the cinnamon donuts which were excellent. I received two including the holes. Not greasy and perfectly bathed in cinnamon and paired with a sweet and tart fruit parfait. This was my favorite part of the meal. 

So was it good? Yes. $55 prix fixe per person good? Probably not.

Yummyyyyy! 

For the first time ever I had to wait in line and had a chance to actually look at the menu. I've been fortunate that I usually get to order immediately and, because my eyes are bigger than my stomach, I get the first thing that looks amazing, which is everything here! 

I found out that I don't have to get a massive scoop, I can order a kids scoop which is probably a more appropriate serving for an adult. I also learned they serve "nachos" which are waffle cone pieces surrounding a massive scoop of ice cream topped with hot fudge. One of these days I'm going to order the farmhouse - 8 scoops and unlimited toppings!

I recommend the honeycomb, cookies and cream, and I recently tried rough seas (candied nuts with honey swirl and pretzel). I think some flavors are only available for a limited time because I didn't see my beloved cowboy cookie. 

The only thing I can (barely) complain about is that their handmade waffle cones are thin and fragile. They're delicious and sugary but the tips are not tightened so ice cream always inevitably drips out. I recommend the cone by all means, but ask for a bowl to hold it!

The  menu offers a modest selection of Italian appetizers and brick oven pizzas. You can also order from the dinner menu at lunch. 

Entrees come out with a delicious complimentary house salad. Pizza came out quickly and was piping hot! There's only one size available but 6" is plenty for 1 person or good enough for 2 people. They do not skimp on the toppings here.  Our server (I think her name is Kayla) was friendly, attentive, and efficient.

Overall, a great choice for lunch in north Tucson.

Ginza is very close to Sabino Canyon and a tempting choice after a long hike. The restaurant is clean and modern with an extensive wine beer and cocktail list.

Service is a 5 but food is a 3. We really liked our very friendly waiter. He bared with us through lots of confusing requests and didn't bat an eye. I could see him juggle multiple tables but his attention did not feel divided.

The menu offers lots of Japanese items beyond your regular selection of sushi and nigiri, ex. ramen and izakaya fried foods. My 3 friends and I ordered the ginza boat at $70. I would say the food was good but nothing special. Quite expensive for the portions in m opinion.

This is apretty small restaurant in a poorly maintained lot off Kolb and Broadway. Both the interior and exterior are nothing special to look at.

This place is so popular for good reason but it means you will likely have to wait for a seat. They offer both indoor and outdoor tables, and outside is cooled by swamp coolers so effectively that I was shivering on a 100 degree day.

Their daily specials are delectable but you'd be foolish to come here and not try one of their sweet pancakes. We had the cinnamon roll pancake which was topped with cream cheese icing. I don't say this lightly- this pancake is BETTER THAN cinnabon. I feel like a traitor for admitting that. I also had the corned beef hash which was served on a bed of hashbrowns and topped with hollandaise sause (a little weird? But not bad). The corned beef was fatty and flavorful. I sincerely wanted to come back for breakfast the next day but my fiancee wanted to try something different.

Great restaurant and I will be back! The only drawback is that it's a very small space that's easily congested so I didn't enjoy the atmosphere.

I know I seem like a flip flopper with these updates but I have to at least give credit to the owner who saw my review and proactively offered me another chance at Roadhouse. Unfortunately, by the time he comped tickets for me, Ladybird was no longer playing and I wasn't thrilled by any alternative showings. I'm still disheartened that I missed the one movie I've been looking forward to in a year. 

If it means anything, thank you for your effort at customer service! It was a simple kind gesture that shows you clearly care for your patrons.

I've had this restaurant on my radar for a while & I finally had the opportunity to visit. Stopped by on a Saturday night for dinner. The spot was busy with friendly staff & quick service. I ordered a combination of rice & beans, a plantain stuffed with refried bean & fried yuca. Everything was affordable & delicious. I look forward to visiting again.

As I was recently introduced to First Watch through Yelp I was excited to bring my entire family to dine at the restaurant. Visited with a party of 6 and was immediately seated. The staff were polite and our server was excellent. I opted for several menu items as the food is fairly priced & delicious. The multigrain banana granola crunch pancakes were fluffy, huge and delicious, the potatoes were tasty and crispy. The avocado (zaboka) toast was loaded with fruit and the bread was soft and warm. I am a fan of First Watch & plan on visiting often.

Visited on a Saturday night for late dinner. The decor is modern and the restaurant has low lighting, it definitely sets the mood for an intimate dining experience. 
I had the Lobster BLT - the sandwich had lobster pieces sprinkled on the top and tomato in the center. I felt cheated as the sandwich was 50% bread, 20% lobster and 30% tomatoes. I also had the brussel sprouts which had a great flavor and chunks of bacon. The server great and  helpful. As for cocktails the Old fashioned is one of the best in the city.

My new favorite lunch spot in downtown Tampa. The restaurant has modern decor & the staff is friendly. There are inexpensive daily lunch specials & the food is delicious. My favorite items are the vegan pho & avocado roll.

Visited on a busy weekday for lunch. I was excited to have a hearty, healthy meal. The greek salad was described by a staff member a salad with lot's of olives, beets, tomatoes and cucumbers. The salad was a HUGE disappointment, I received one sliver of beet, a sprinkle of tomato and  tons of hard lettuce core. Actually, most of my salad was the hard, unappetizing lettuce core pieces. After nibbling on the few edible items of my salad I was disappointed & still hungry.

Visited on a Saturday afternoon for dinner. There is outdoor and indoor seating available and at the time of my visit there was a large party in the outdoor space. I had paneer (cheese) in tomato sauce with coconut rice. The food was very flavorful and perfectly spiced. The staff were busy and provided great service. I would certainly visit again.

Visited for dessert on a Friday night. Bake'n Babes is beautifully decorated and the bright pink colors and neon signs drew me in like a moth to a flame. I had a chocolate chip cookie and slutty brownie. I've had both in the past and the recipe seems to be a bit different. The brownie could've been more moist and less firm. The cookie was okay.

Visited Spinners for my surprise Birthday dinner. My husband planned a wonderful afternoon for us to dine and spin the night away. The restaurant is located in the Grand Plaza Hotel - a dated, art deco styled hotel. It was a sunny afternoon and the restaurant offered a beautiful roof top view of the ocean and St. Pete beach. The service was impeccable, my server was attentive & very friendly, other service staff I interacted with were also pleasant. 

Food
I started with the house salad that came with a mango salsa, it was a great introduction to Spinners as the greens were crispy and fresh. However, when it came to dinner, I was extremely disappointed. I had the Cajun Gulf Snapper - pan seared served with jalapeno grits. The meal quite bland, the Snapper was dry and lacked elements of basic seasoning. My husband's meal was also quite flavorless. For desert I had the chocolate cake - a rich, thick slice of chocolate goodness - good.

I have mixed feelings about my experience as the ambiance is lovely & service is excellent but the food is subpar.

I visited Mama's for Sunday brunch with a large group. Our orders for beverages were immediately taken as we were seated. The food appeared shortly after ordering. I ordered the grilled catfish however, the restaurant was out of grilled catfish so I opted for ordering a combination of side dishes. The service was excellent and the staff worked as a cohesive team.

Taste:
I had baked beans, black eyed peas, hush puppies, rice and gravy and potato salad. 

Hush puppies excellent
Baked beans: tasted like tomato sauce and were overly sweet 
Black eyed peas were a hard (undercooked) and lacked flavor
Potato salad: tasted more like sugar mayonnaise dressing with potatoes.
The lemonade is sugar laden with an artificial lemon flavor.
Red velvet cake: was overly sweet and tasted like sugared food coloring. 

Mama's seems to be a favorite for some but it wasn't my cup of tea.

Visited as I was interested in trying Szechuan cuisine. I started the meal with the spike potato, the spices were intense & delicious - imagine fries laden with a prominent peppercorn flavor. I had the vegetable hot bowl, the broth was hot in both heat & flavor. The staff appeared to family oriented & were extremely friendly. I thoroughly enjoyed my first visit & so I returned two weekends in a row, I look forward to my next visit.

Visited Revolutionary Ice Cream on a hot Saturday afternoon with a large group. The shop was packed. I had the Drunken Brownies - chardonnay caramel ice cream with brownie bits. The brownie bits tasted more like chocolate chips & the ice cream was 3 star worthy.

Visited on a Saturday afternoon as a colleague suggested I give NMM a try. The corner street restaurant is quite large and has games including Jenga,
ping pong, shuffleboard & corn hole. The staff was friendly and helpful. Though this place has been around for only 6 months, there appeared to be regulars.The menu was a mashup of American, Indian, Korean & Mexican favorites. I opted for the messy fries and the charred corn, both were good.

Visited on a Saturday afternoon for lunch. Mitmita is nestled in a little plaza that is easy to overlook while driving. The server who I believe was also the owner was happy & had a genuine smile. I started with the vegetable sumbusa - a fried pastry stuffed with lentil peas. I also had the yellow lentil entree and the complimentary lemonade. Overall, wonderful experience & I plan on visiting again soon.

Sparkman Wharf is a great addition to the Tampa bay area. Visited on a sunny Sunday afternoon & the space has a relaxing vibe as it's near the water & has lots of shaded seating space. I enjoyed a bite sized veggie taco from Gallito Taqueria. The taco was tasty and left me craving for more. I also enjoyed the Original Sin rose from the Fermented Reality Biergarten, it was refreshing & perfect for the hot summer day. Hopefully more restaurants will be added soon. I look forward to visiting again.

Visited on a Saturday morning for breakfast with the family. The staff were friendly & appeared to have excellent relationships with each other & customers. The decor is vintage & adds to the warm family atmosphere. I had french toast and fries, both items were good & relatively priced. Glad I tried this local favorite.

Visited Sugar Factory during its opening week and was impressed. The ambiance at the space was fun and bright! There are neon signs, floral decor and smoke filled drinks all around. The staff puts on a performance and dance to certain songs ever so often, it's a spectacle that all guests enjoy. The drinks are oversized, tasty and strong - just the way I like them. As for food I had the veggie burger and I considered it to be overpriced. Sugar Factory is certainly a space for a good entertaining evening.

I am a HUGE fan of restaurant week and was happy to find Buya on the list of 2018 restaurant week participants. I also a HUGE ramen and I have had ramen in different Providences in Japan. I understand each restaurant/chef prepares ramen differently and I am always open different variations of the dish.

Food:
The blistered shishito peppers are an excellent combination of spicy and sweet. It's a combination of fire blistered (grilled) peppers, brown sugar, sea salt and sesame. The peppers were mostly not overly spicy however, toward the end of the meal I bit into a blazing hot pepper, the brown sugar calmed the burn though. I also had the Edamame - perfectly salted and a great starter.

I had the Mushroom ramen which greatly needed flavor. The ramen was extremely bland and the noodles tasted like cardboard in hot water. I was very disappointed with the dish. I added chilli oil and chilli sauce to make it edible. I was highly displeased with this dish. 
My partner had the Crispy Duck Ramen which was incredible! I had a few bites of his dish and I immediately regretted my order. The duck was flavorful and had an amazing crunch. The broth was flavorful and hearty. 

Dessert
The chocolate mouse and creme brulee were excellent - rich in consistency and taste. Hopefully, there will be an upgrade to the mushroom ramen soon and I can make another visit.

Visited on a Sunday for drinks and eats. The decor is beautiful and there is indoor and outdoor seating. The restaurant was very busy and due to the extended wait time for service the manager on duty offered my partner and I complimentary appetizers or dessert. I opted for dessert but when the bill arrived the dessert was charged. In addition, the server spilled a large portion of my cocktail and told me that he would replace it. A refreshed beverage was not received. My visit to Whiskey Cake was filled with broken promises and terrible customer service. Overall, I had a very poor experience and would not recommend.

During my visit to the big easy I had Merchat bookmarked as a breakfast option and I'm glad I made it. The space is modern with beautiful large windows facing the street. There is also a hallway space with additional seats. 

Eats: 
I had a french vanilla latte which was absolutely delicious. I also had the apple cinnamon sugar crepe which was okay, if I visit again I'll probably try something else. Good vibes.

Visited for lunch on a hot summer day and as luck would have it the air conditioning was broken. The restaurant was extreemly stuffy and felt like a sauna. There is outdoor seating available however, it was entirely too warm to entertain the idea of eating outside. I ordered the lentil soup to go; the soup didn't have much flavor or taste and the consistency was extremely watery. With the high slection of eateries in downtown Tampa I'm not sure if I am willing to risk visiting again.

Visited on a busy Friday evening. The restaurant is dimly lit & has a romantic ambiance. Had my go to cocktail an old fashioned, the beverage was potent & well made. Great service & friendly bartenders, looking forward to my next visit.

Visited on a Sunday evening to celebrate a birthday and enjoy birthday dinner. The service were delightful and the Crab rangoon was a highlight of the meal, the rangoon had a light pastry with a moist cheesy filling. I look forward to visiting again.

Visited as I was in desperate need for some hot soup. I had the veggie Pho, it was served with beef broth (vegetarians and vegans) beware. The Pho was delicious and filling.
I also had the mint mango tea. The tea was very good but a very small serving for the price. It was about 12 ounces of tea for $5 YIKES!

Visited Shelly's for Sunday breakfast & had the Shelly's French Toast - toast topped with bananas, strawberries, blueberries & powdered sugar. The toast had a great texture and was reasonably priced. The staff were attentive & friendly. The space is small & the decor is the style of a modern diner. I enjoyed my experience & look forward to visiting again.

Visited Mediterranean Chickpea and had a variety of food items. The restaurant has a variety of hummus selections, by far the beet hummus was the most unique and delicious. The falafel was some of the best I've ever had.
Visited on a Saturday night for an evening treat. Had the rum raisin gelato & the turtle cheesecake. Both were good and fulfilled my sweet tooth craving.

I've visited on several occasions and I've enjoyed the experience every time. This vegetarian restaurant has delicious Indian cuisine that include rice dishes, roti & soups. The staff is friendly. Would highly recommend.

I've seen multiple people on both yelp and on paid media outlets discuss how there is "no good Chinese food in Tucson" and talk about how they're on some kind of "quest" to find the good stuff out here.  You guys need to calm down.  Tucson does have its places and some of them even rival restaurants in the more Chinese-heavy areas of California.

The twist?  It's all Szechuan food.  I haven't found any specifically southern Chinese restaurants yet and I don't have a palette for Americanized Chinese food.  If you're willing to try some of the real stuff without straying too far from things from Panda Express, China Szechwan happily serves both, with a little bit of Cantonese dinner cuisine thrown in.

THE GIST: Guests receive two menus, one of which contains most of the authentic dishes / Excellent roast pork

FOOD HIGHLIGHTS

Roast Combo: They have a combo that has a combination of roast duck, roast pork, and BBQ pork that I highly recommend to people of any background visiting this restaurant.  The roast pork in particular was fatty (like it's supposed to be) and the skin was incredibly crispy and tasty.

Western Lake Beef Soup: Very tasty, very savory, good portion.

Fish in Chili Oil: Very tasty and with generous amounts of fish, they don't "Americanize" the quality of the spices here so be aware if you're not used to hotter stuff.

Walnut Shrimp, Twice Cooked Pork: Highly recommended to those who are used to going to Panda Express, the latter is actually an authentic dish but very common in America.  Loved the walnuts in the shrimp and the pork was very full of flavor while being only slightly dry.

CONCLUSION

China Szechwan wouldn't stand out among the masses in cities like NYC, San Francisco, or anything in the San Gabriel Valley, but for a city that's apparently know for its lack of Chinese cuisine, it's excellent.  As far as this whole "quest for good Chinese food" goes, it only took me one night of browsing yelp for pictures to find this one.  Tucson might not have the variety that other cities have but it's not devoid of decent Chinese food.

I'm very surprised that I found the food to be as good as it was here as I had a bit of a bias going in because I'm not the biggest fan of Superior Grill's food (Superior Grill is a Tex-Mex place owned by the same people that opened this place).  I just sat at the bar and sampled a few appetizers with low expectations as they had so recently opened.  They have a nice looking raw oyster bar in here and the grilled and raw oysters really were fantastic and among the best I've ever had.  The crab cake seemed to actually be 99% crab and was great.  I also had ordered a gumbo and they accidentally brought me crawfish etouffe which was tasty but they quickly realized their mistake and brought me my gumbo which was good but not fantastic.  They make their own potato chips and some kind of dip and even those were good.  The location is perfect and this will certainly be a popular spot during Mardi Gras for parades.  

They have done a fantastic job of renovating the old Copeland's space and it is both very comfortable and aesthetically pleasing.  I have eaten here several times now and the appetizers and oysters remain the stars of the show with the entree options being less pleasing.  If everything else can reach the level of the appetizers and they maintain standards I will be glad to have this addition to the neighborhood.

Tip:  They have a fantastic daily happy hour with 50 cent oysters, $3 draft beers, 2 for 1 frozen drinks along with half off glasses and bottles of wine.

VERY disappointing!  I have been waiting in great expectation since October for this place to open and had the most disappointing Vietnamese meal of my life here.  This place is very popular at the moment and it was packed full of people in the small space like a sardine can and I was sat in the tiniest baby chair I've ever attempted to sit in within the most cramped space I've ever attempted to eat in. This place looks a lot like a trendy gastropub and what a surprise they also serve stupid SMALL portions of food just like a stupid gastropub too.  I was served the smallest serving of pho I've ever had in my life anywhere!  They have one bowl size and it is smaller than the small size at all the other places in the area.  If the size of the serving wasn't bad enough they dished out the bean sprouts and greens like they were made of gold and then only ONE slice of jalapeno.  

So after this tiny snack I attempt to pay my bill and noticed that when I got my credit card slip back that somehow they added on TWO special coffee drinks to my tab that I didn't have.  It took three times longer to take care of my bill than it did to eat and in the end all they could figure out was to just give me cash for the difference they had charged to my card.  I don't like small portions and dainty little snacks and I don't like being crammed into a sardine can and then forced to sit in a baby chair.  I'd be betting I probably won't be returning to eat the micro pho here so do yourself a favor and get a real bowl of pho elsewhere.

Out of all the new Vietnamese places that have opened on Magazine recently this is by far the best.  They have a selection of nine different types of pho including a rare (at least in NOLA) spicy shrimp one.  They have a good selection of spring rolls and egg rolls along with bun (noodle dishes), rice dishes and salads.  They have beef, chicken, pork, and tofu banh mi (po boys).  

The only three things I didn't like about the place is that they don't fill your bowl of pho to the top like they do at Westbank and Metairie pho places and they made me share my sprouts, greens, and peppers with my friend I was eating with.  I'm a very selfish person when it comes to my pho fixings grrrrr I don't want to share and I want my own plate of stuff grrrr!  I also thought the price at $8.25 for most of the pho's was a bit much for a non-full bowl compared to other places.  

The seating was far more comfortable and service was far faster than at the other two new Vietnamese places so if you want some good Vietnamese on Magazine this is your best option.  And yes for you freaky vegetarians they did have some tofu pho but I don't know if the broth is vegetarian :)

Fantastic food in a decent space with ambiance that tends towards more fun and casual than fine dining.  The downstairs dining room is a bit narrow and cramped with the tables rather near each other.  Service is excellent but not necessarily the most friendly and engaging.  The dress code is business casual but that rule doesn't seem very well enforced as it seems more tourist casual.  This is a very tourist heavy spot but it still has food that should appeal to the high standards of any local.  
Certainly one of the top restaurant gems in NOLA that should be on your must do list for the experience of Paul Prudhomme's legendary cuisine.

Tip: The bread basket is great with carrot bread, corn bread, cheese bread and regular bread etc. with plenty of butter.

I've consistently heard that dinner here is fantastic but very overpriced and not really worth it when compared to other spots in town.  My experience at lunch was similar except that the food was just good and not fantastic.  I had high expectations but the lunch menu seemed rather limited on choices when compared to other fine dining restaurants in the area.  They really fell short here in the service department.  I was offered no sherry with my turtle soup and getting my iced tea refilled was really inconsistent.  I was especially displeased when my empty glass of iced tea was taken away and I was left with only water prior to my dessert course even arriving and was never asked if I wanted coffee.  I'm not sure if it is a training issue or what but the staff here all seem very overly obsessed with commenting about their house filtered iced water and they were so focused with asking if I wanted more house filtered water every time they were around they really forgot to take care of my iced tea and other service needs.  If the restaurant had been crowded I might have been more understanding but there were only a handful of tables when we arrived and only a few more as we left.  I had turtle soup (which was quite overpriced at $10), Gulf Fish and then the best part of the meal the chocolate cake for dessert.  Of course no inquiry was made if I wanted coffee with my dessert.  For the price, clumsy service and overall experience I just don't think I would return for lunch.  I would definitely consider returning for dinner as it is a nice space but probably only if somebody else was buying.  

There are certainly aspects of this place I like but they really need to get the service aspect better organized as I really would have had a much better time and far more enjoyable meal by just turning the other direction on Bienville Street and going to Arnaud's instead.

I had the beef ramen and it was a good bowl of soup but it was a bit over priced at $10 as it was the same size as a small bowl of pho at most Vietnamese joints where you can get a large bowl of pho for less than $10.  The worst sticker shock was the $3.25 iced tea which I passed on and just had water and I was also a bit sad that they had no Abita Amber in their very small beer selection.  I had the blueberry & peach pie and I thought the crust was quite nice but it was a bit tough and I didn't find that I liked the combo of peach and blueberry as the flavor didn't really work for me.  

The interior of this place has been made into a very bright orange so all the Tennessee and Auburn fans can find themselves right at home but I find it a bit glaringly bright.  The seating is not very comfortable and didn't encourage me to linger around and enjoy myself.  The music was way too loud and not very good so that definitely could have been turned down a whole lot.  This place definitely has zero New Orleans vibe about it and could have been ripped out of Austin or someplace in California or New York.  I liked the ramen but the rest of the scene was trying way too hard to be way too hipster.  I would definitely return for the soup but I'm not sure about the rest of the food and the ambiance is just not pleasant.  

So in summary the ambiance is awful, the prices are a bit expensive, the ramen is really good and the pie has potential.

They actually do have watermelon here along with watermelon punch, Obama punch, and Michelle punch (but for some reason no Ray Nagin chocolate punch).  This is mainly a chicken wing focused joint with the addition of chicken gizzards, red beans, jalapeno bombers, fries and the namesake watermelon.  They also offer the infamous 100 piece chicken.

Cash only!

I've eaten here many times and had many private events here.  I have always had a great time with outstanding service and food.  Muriel's has some amazing gumbo and they usually have a special for around $30 for a 3 course meal.  Some people don't know you can usually get a drink downstairs and go and enjoy the balcony upstairs and this is one of the best places to people watch all the interesting things going on down around Jackson Square below.  They also have an interesting "Egyptian" themed room upstairs. Always a great place to go with a group, book an event, or just eat by yourself at the bar.

I had high hopes for a worthy competitor to the Joint having possibly arrived.  I was happy with the larger selection of items on the menu and especially pleased to see beef ribs.

The BAD:  

Service was not up to even keeping my iced tea refilled and I was sitting at the bar at around 4:30 pm with few other customers around which makes that situation even worse.  (on my next visit the service was much improved when we were sitting outside at a picnic table and the manager even came by twice to check on us so looks like they are addressing that service issue fast).

Quantity on the brisket plate was less meat than the Joint.

No toast or pickles came with my brisket plate.

Mac n Cheese isn't an official side dish so you have to order it separately for like $6!  MAD INSANITY ya gotta include smaller serving sizes of the various mac n cheese options as a side!!!

Crazy pricing scheme on their menu for biscuits as I thought I was getting 5 for $2 but actually they are $5 for 2 biscuits which is crazy overpriced for plain biscuits that most places give out free with meals.  The biscuits were also so dry and crumbly I couldn't really spread the butter on them without them just falling apart.

Texas Toast and corn bread are each counted as a side so you can buy one slice of their house-made Texas Toast for $3 or also get some corn bread for $3... That price is like at least one whole loaf of bread or a whole pan of corn bread and this might be the worst value on the entire menu.

Their brisket chili comes with beans in it... Texans don't put beans in their chili and then even though this place isn't Texas they still shouldn't put beans in a chili that is going on my hamburger as I don't want beans on my burger as that reeks of Vegan too much for me.

Price was a poor value as with tip I rang up a $29.50 bill so that is approaching Commander's Palace 3 course lunch price that also gets me 25 cent martinis!!!  This is also double the price of the Joint for less meat (Joint includes toast and pickles so I wouldn't have needed to also order the rip off $5 crumbly biscuits to satisfy my appetite too).

The GOOD:

The bar area is a pretty nice setup and could be a good space for watching games.

Heinekens and several other beers are just $3 and then they also have the expensive super hipster beers too along with quite a selection of cocktails. 

The brisket was decent and is probably about in third place to my taste preference in the NOLA area currently.

They have 3 BBQ sauces (and one additional white sauce for those weirdo Alabama folks that put that crazy white sauce on their meat).

Beef ribs!!!  This looks to be the only place that will be able to constantly serve beef ribs in the area (Black Label is the only other option but they have never had it every time I tried to order it so I have given up on them).

Burgers are decent here and they are a filling size served with a side of fries. 

Overall I hope they get this new bbq spot up and going full speed ahead and get all the kinks out to make it a viable competitor to the Joint in quality, quantity and value.  I would also suggest they take a hint from some of the awesome BBQ joints of Austin, TX and set up a condiment bar space with pickles, sliced onions and hot peppers along with serving the plates with toast/bread and they might need to outsource their house-made Texas Toast to one of our great local bakeries if they can't price it better than $3 a slice.

I had great times at old Pravda and liked that joint.  This new incarnation has nothing in common with the bar formerly known as Pravda and I don't like it.  Another fancy cocktail bar that ignores the needs of beer drinkers with a very limited selection of overpriced beers.  There is nothing Russian or Slavic about this joint so the name makes absolutely no sense.  I have absolutely no reason to return to this establishment.

For some reason I could never get Yelp check in to work here?

I was excited to try this place and when I walked in it looked and smelled fantastic to further excite my palate.  My party ordered the pastrami sliders, swallow cloud soup and General Lee's Chicken.  Sadly I was really disappointed in how bland everything ended up tasting and I would have rather have gone to any other Chinese or Vietnamese place for better tasting food.  

The General Lee's Chicken came out first and it is a HUGE portion so you get a lot of food for your money with this entree but I found it just didn't have a lot of flavor or spice to it while it sure looked pretty.  Next came out the swallow cloud soup (which didn't seem to have any greens in it as described on the menu) while the dumplings in it had some meat that did actually have some good flavor the broth was pretty bland to me and the noodles seemed to be the same type you get in a cheap ramen noodle packet.  Finally the sliders came out and they were the most disappointing item of the night as they were just like Vietnamese tacos but with far less on them and the main flavor on the sliders came from the kimchi while the cubed pastrami didn't do much for me.  I really wanted to like this place but it seems like some bland food loving Yankees were in charge of the flavoring for for the night as so much of my meal was just in need of much more spice.

Food inspired by the Yucatan with drink prices inspired by New York City with $4.50 Abita Amber, $5.50 Negra Modelo, $8 house margaritas (served in a small glass) and $8 for a glass of sangria. Food service is fast and the flavor of most things is good. The drink prices are too expensive and while the food is good the prices are a bit too much for what you get.  The spider theme of the interior decor is too year round Halloween for this section of town and doesn't seem to contribute anything other than scaring young children. 

My part of the bill came out to $27.16 (before tip) which was for the 3 tacos with 2 sides combo, a shared tamale, an iced tea and one house margarita.  Mexican food is cheap peasant food with most things wrapped in some form of tortilla and no valid reason to be pricey and the same goes for Mexican beer and house margaritas.  There are as good or better Mexican options in the city for a much better value on food and drinks so I'm not confident in the longevity of this place and I probably won't make many return visits.  

Tip: the à la carte seafood tacos are probably one of the better values on the menu.

Hint:  The main competition in the area for this joint is Rum House.  The drinks at Rum House are substantially cheaper and larger.

This is a really great Italian joint in Rivertown that offers a lot of bang for your buck.  There was another Italian restaurant right next door to this one several years ago that wasn't such a hit so if you are recalling hearing about less than good Italian in Rivertown it will be that now closed establishment and not this great spot.  The space is pleasing with classic Italian themed music and attentive service.  The huge meatballs here with their very affordable and amazing "Meatball Gendusa" appetizer being one of the stars of the show will certainly please the largest of appetites.  The po boys are very nice here and priced at a great value.  The pizza is done very well and they have really nice roasted garlic as one of their toppings that will cure what craving you might need in the hunger and flavor department along with a more than fair price.  

Overall this is fantastic food at a fantastic price in a nice restaurant in the cool area of Rivertown.

Gendusa's Italian Market video review:

https://youtu.be/a8Q-y4jAXIk

Sunday doesn't seem to be the most fun day to get crawfish here.  I've never had so many uneatable mudbugs anywhere in my life as I received in my serving here and I soon learned why.  It seems they had boiled a huge amount the day before and they were mixing in the old crawfish with the fresh crawfish which unfortunately had the effect of overcooking the older crawfish making it mushy and inedible.  I would've been fine with having some of the older crawfish being mixed in with the fresh but they could've just mixed them together AFTER pulling the newbies out of the water and letting them cool down a good bit before combining them and pushing the day olds into an overcooked mush zone.

Friday and Saturday would seem to be a safer bet for the best crawfish here.  I also didn't find the spice overly strong but I like it spicy while I did really miss the fact that they don't use garlic in their boil.  Overall I would probably say you would get a three star or above experience here but my Sunday experience was quite a disappointing batch of crawdaddies as the majority of them were good but far too many of them were bad. Nice folks running the place but for my money I still very much prefer Big Fisherman as my go to spot for consistently awesome boiled crawfish and shrimp (with lots of garlic).

I accidentally came across Rick's Reef while looking for parking on a Sunday afternoon beach day. My friend noticed the "$2 Bloody Mary" sign and we immediately decided to stop here. What a fantastic decision that turned into! Rick's Reef is an amazing, laid back beach bar right on Gulf Blvd. There is outdoor and indoor seating, but I must say that the best spot is at the bar. The bartender was extremely friendly and watching the locals come in and out is amazing (this is a true beach bar). 

The Bloody Marys were strong and very tasty. We ordered an appetizer of potato skins for $8...which turned out to be gigantic and fully loaded with cheeses and bacon. The menu was priced really reasonably and all of the food looked amazing as I saw it being served around the bar. The draft beer selection is notable...both local craft and domestics. But really...those $2 Bloody Marys will keep me coming back! A great little discovery on Gulf Blvd!!!

I teetered between 4 and 5 stars on this one, but I am going with 5...why? Because I didn't order a ton of stuff, I went on a holiday and everything was good as it can get for that setup! I stopped by with some friends for brunch on Labor Day around the time they opened and the service was really good. We sat at the bar and the staff was very attentive, moving quickly to make sure everyone was doing okay (even those who had to stand when the crowd built). 

I LOVE a dark bar. I don't know what it is, but it just seems cozy to me. The Galley is covered in wood and has that pirate ship feel to it. There is outdoor seating as well and you can bring your pups with you. Everything is really clean and it's an open seating layout. You can call ahead for reservations too though! 

For drinks, I had a Bloody Mary ($5) and a couple of Mimosas ($3). This was brunch pricing and everything was made well. For those of you who know me, the color of my mimosa was not orange....it was more on the clear side! I ate the Florida Nuggets - Gator ($9) as my meal and this may be the best version I've had in a really long time. Simply because the gator was more prominent than the breading! Delicious!!

Overall a cool bar right off of central with a fun crowd. Good specials, parking on the street nearby and a great staff. I'll be back!

I really enjoyed my first visit to McAlister's Deli this passed weekend! I've past by this deli many times and had figured it was just another Westshore business lunch spot. But I ended up here on a Saturday afternoon. It was very quiet, with just a few patrons and plenty of open tables. I went with the pick 2 menu option and got half of a Turkey Cobb sandwich with a half sized portion of the Savannah Chopped Salad. Both of these choices were fantastic! The Turkey Cobb had bacon, gorgonzola, guacamole, mayo and ranch. It had plenty of each ingredient and was on squishy nine grain bread. I am not normally a fan of salads with fruit in them but I really liked this one! It had chicken, cranberries, gorgonzola (I love cheese on everything), almonds and a balsamic type of dressing on the side. It was around $8.50 total and well worth the price in my opinion. It was more than enough food and everything was extremely fresh. 

There is plenty of parking out front as this restaurant shares a parking lot with Eddie V's. The staff was very friendly and seemed like they enjoyed their jobs. The restaurant is really clean and your food is brought to your table. I could not find a garbage can to use, but the food is served on glass and there are real utensils that are collected by the staff when you are done. A really good place to stop for lunch if you are looking for a nice place to have a sandwich or salad.

I've lived in Tampa for a long time and I hadn't been to Hattrick's yet. Just never made it, but this past Saturday I finally got around to it! Disclosure: I went the day of the River O'Green Fest and it was ridiculously packed. On top of that, there was a Lightning Game at Amelie that night as well. My friends and I showed up around 2:30pm and waited almost an hour to find a seat (they didn't have a hostess so we resorted to hawking and hovering over tables that looked like they were ready to leave). Oh, and basketball was on so no one wanted to leave. We were HUNGRY! 

Anyhoo, once we were able to grab a table our waitress came right over and looked super stressed - understandably! Regardless, she was accurate, professional and moved as fast as she could to help us. We started off with fried pickles and some drinks. Drinks were small but it was also an especially busy day so I get that. They were served as spears and were piping hot. Tasty and I'd recommend if you love pickles. They are way better than pickled chips like other places serve because you actually get a lot of pickle! I ordered the wings with IRA sauce which were really stinking delicious. Meaty, cooked well and had good flavor. 

The restaurant is dark and there are tons of TVs that you can see from any angle which is awesome. The bar has plenty of seating and they have a pretty good looking happy hour, which I'd return to try (drink specials everyday and 85 cent wings caught my eye). The bathrooms are exceptionally nice and were really clean despite the crowd. Prices are very fair for the location and the food is good quality for being a sports bar. This place has been around for a long time for a reason. Looking forward to going back during a more quiet time!

Went here during the soft opening after following them on Facebook for quite some time. I honestly didn't realize that they weren't fully 'open' yet but decided to stop by on this past Sunday evening. The location is really weird...in a strip mall that is being completely remodeled (there's a Youfit next door and a massive non denominational church being constructed...which I think was a Winn-Dixie at one time). Parking is obviously easy because the lot is massive and there aren't many businesses in this mall. The brewery itself is very dark and simple. The brewing takes place in the back and is open to see. The bar is a pretty decent size with plenty of stools and there are many wooden tables scattered around. It has a factory feel to it with very high ceilings and concrete floors. 

The wall murals were the most impressive part of this brewery. You are supposed to feel like you are inside of a shark's mouth and there is a big white square that will be used to project movies in the future. I like the dark lighting and the way the bar is lit up. They have usb plugs in abundance but no purse hooks yet. The bathrooms are still under construction but the sinks are located outside of the bathrooms and are set up like kegs. Super cool! Plus it keeps traffic moving out of the bathrooms and you can tell who doesn't wash their hands! Stay sanitary people.

As for the beers, they only have a core list of 6 beers right now. The best in my opinion is the Ramble On Raspberry Ale. All beers are low ABV and the IPA needs some work in my opinion. The beertenders were super cool and they offered me a mix of the raspberry and stout which was tasty. Beers are $5/$6. I'm excited to see what they offer in the future since i was told that they will have guest taps down the road. 

There was a food truck outside and i imagine they will have a rotating food truck gathering after their official opening. I also expect a larger selection of beers once they get going. I totally support this brewery, because it is the first in the immediate area and they have a large space to expand. Good luck 81Bay!!!!!

This is one of those places that deserves WAY more than 5 stars and for so many reasons!!! I have been wanting to stop by here since it opened and just never got the chance. So I snagged a reservation this evening to treat my boyfriend to an awesome birthday dinner and it was absolutely perfect. The owner is a super busy dude, so anyone who has rated this place based on being 'slow' or 'rude' has misunderstood the concept of a small and intimate restaurant. There are less than 10 tables (for 2, which they will push together if there's a bigger group coming in). This is not fast food and you can't expect it to run like a chain restaurant. You need a reservation and should plan to enjoy your evening with time set aside. The owner was fantastic in my experience tonight - polite, helpful, quick and efficient. We ordered Burrata as an appetizer, Carbonara and Puttanesca for dinner and Tiramisu for dessert. Everything was ridiculously delicious and was so much tastier than other Italian food I've had in Tampa. No salt or extra cheese needed (it's not on the table for a reason). The prices can't be beat. Especially since you can also bring your own wine or beer - no corkage fee. The owner even helped us open our bottle up after some technical difficulty LOL! Phenomenal place. I can't wait to go back!! Parking lot has about 8 spaces and it's shared with 2 other stores. Might need to park in the next lot over if it's a busy night. It used to be a hidden gem, but the cat's out of the bag. GO. JUST GO.

This was my second visit to The Butcher Bar, but first time for brunch. My boyfriend and I split the Butcher Mimosa, which supplied two small drinks each to us. My brother and friend had the Spicy Butcher Bacon Bloody. I ordered the Breakfast Toast and a side of roasted potatoes; boyfriend had the BLT; brother had the poached eggs; and friend ordered the special which was make-your-own salmon, lox, and cream cheese bagels.

I also had the Blackberry Brunch Potion and do not recommend. It wasn't mixed (which I thought was intentional since it did not come with a straw or stirrer), but really did not taste good un-mixed. And even when I did mix it up, it still tasted too syrupy. Adding some water helped a little but I still did not enjoy it. 

I love how the back patio is set up. At first we were very comfortable and warm, and then the heaters actually became too hot (which was easily fixed when a server turned it down for us). But overall, the service was great, we felt COVID-safe, and enjoyed our experience.

Sweet feathery jesus, people!  Here's my Geno's review.. It was good.  Not the second coming or anything, but good.  Let's put it this way, I'm not the best person to review this, as Cheese steaks are meh in my book.  I know, this will be met with some disdain, but hey, we all have our own passions.  Cheese steaks are not one of mine.   
That said, the onions, the cheese and the bread - all yummy.  The steak was a bit chewy, hence the three stars.  If I just ate the bread, onions, and cheese, I'd have probably given it four stars.  But then it wouldn't have been a cheese steak.. 
Ok, so there's my review.  Let the hate comments begin.  Sorry I can't be part of your little cheese steak clique.  I'm not worthy..

Reading - pronounced "Redding" apparently, as I was corrected quite often.   My savior in Philly.  Want something healthy?  Tasty?  Sinful?  Across the street from my hotel?  
Every lunch I had was spent here - getting freshly carved turkey breast from "The Original Turkey", salad from "Tootsie's salad bar", sushi from "Tokyo Sushi Bar" - this sushi chef was the fastest I've ever seen, and the sushi was amazing.   If I wanted to stay with my healthy eating choices, I'd also stock my hotel fridge with fresh fruit from Iovine Brothers Produce - they also made the BEST fruit salad.  I kid you not.  Ripe, succulent, and juicy.  (Insert dirty joke here)
If I wanted to be naughty, oh it was easy to be downright perverse here.. The cornbread from Delilah's - the best I've ever eaten in my entire life hands down.  Melt in your mouth, buttery goodness..
And the grand finale...Ir-freakin-resistable cookies from The Famous 4th Street Cookie Co.  Oh holy hell.  I had to have one every day, if not only for one bite and then hand it off to one of my friends who cursed me for giving them the additional calories, but silently blessed me for leading them to cookie heaven.  I tried every flavor.. All were delectable.  But if I had to choose?  The peanut butter chocolate chip and the white chocolate macadamia nut.  
Can't we move this to Los Angeles?  Please?

Went here with friends who are locals and they picked this restaurant. Well great choice upon arriving they have free parking out front. We had a choice of sitting outside or inside with the AC. We chose the later. The service was good and I ordered the frozen margarita. Nice size only needed one and it was delicious not too tart. 

We got the usual chips and salsa as well as ordered a side of queso. It was a pale white color not the bright yellow that you find in most places. It was good but not too thick. For my main course I had the Chile Releno my favorite. Two poblano peppers one hot one not. There's was prepared a little unusual as they but a red pizza sauce on top. Not needed and thankfully not too much as Italian meets Mexican didn't work. The rice was good as well. 

Would definitely come back but ask they hold the pizza sauce next time.

A group of friends makes this a regular hangout on Tuesday evenings, and I sometimes join them for a drink. It's been awhile since I've eaten anything here aside from an appetizer (Scotch Eggs) maybe once or twice a year, but the service in the bar is good, the beer list rotates often, and they sometimes have New Day Meadery Mead available, when the handle isn't broken.

During the warmer months, they open up the doors out front so you can get a nice breeze inside the bar or interact with people as they walk up and down Mass Ave. It can get busy, especially on Friday and Saturday nights, so don't plan on getting a table in the bar area right away. Tuesday evenings are much calmer (usually) and it's a good place to celebrate making it through two days of work.

First time here for brunch but definitely not the last. This place hasn't caught on yet, so we were the only ones here at 10:30 on a Sunday morning when we arrived. Our group of 10 got seated immediately.

Lots of options for brunch along with a full bar. The more popular cocktails are on the brunch menu, but they'll make others that are on the dinner menu if you have a favorite. 

I did the full order of cornmeal thyme biscuits with gravy and should have gone with a half order side instead. Served with a side of potatoes, there is a lot of kick in the gravy and it's very filling. Biscuits were good but a little dry in my opinion. 

It won't take long for this place to catch on and become a brunch hot spot, so get in now while you can without a wait!

I was fortunate enough to stumble across A Taste of Havana today while driving through Broadripple and thought I'd give it a try. Ohmigosh, I'm so glad that I did!

Having only been open for two weeks, A Taste of Havana is a family owned business. The family? Two. Father and Daughter. I can't imagine the number of hours they must put in each week, and hope they hurry up and get someone else in before the public catches on how good the food is. The decor is what you would expect to find in the cuban shops in Miami; and seeing how they did it all themselves, it's about as authentic as you can get. 

The food: When trying a cuban restaurant for the first time, I always go for the same thing; Cuban Sandwich and plantains. It's like the cheeseburger at an American place; if they can't get it right, why bother? Boy.. they got this one right. The El Cubano was layered with roast pork, ham, swiss cheese, pickles and yellow mustard. Even better, it came in three sizes: El Especial ($10.99), El Regular ($8.49) and El Mini ($6.50). I chose the El Regular, which was the perfect size for me. Add an extra $2.49 to make it a combo with a fountain drink and your choice of a side. 

I'll admit that I had a few bites of roast pork that were too tough to eat, but the flavors were outstanding, and the size of the tough pieces of pork were too small to worry about. Trust me: the meats on this sandwich were piled high. 

Dessert? Well, sure; only because I was writing this review and had to make sure you knew what to expect (your welcome.) Menu items includes assorted pastries, flan and tres leches cake. I ordered flan, which they were out of. I instead opted for a guava and cream cheese pastry, which they heated and served hot out of the oven. Fantastic. If they don't make them in house, they've fooled me.

During dessert they brought around complimentary cuban coffee, which they quickly pointed out doesn't happen often, but since they weren't very busy, they went ahead and made some. This review is powered by said coffee right now. Whoa was it strong. In my mind I was transported back to South Beach sipping cuban coffee at the little cuban restaurants. 

I have very high predictions for this place, assuming they get the staffing they need and don't burn out first. It's a tiny place, so I hope the lines don't get too much for them, and that Broadripple appreciates how awesome it is that a place like this has opened up.

My first review of Ivy's was in 2012 and my second was in 2014. Today marked my 235 check in on Yelp, so I kind of consider myself a "regular" at the place.

English Ivy's has gone through a change of owner in the past few months and the new owner seems to be having some trouble establishing some level of consistency with inventory and even servers. I've turned a blind eye to this, telling myself things these things happen when businesses change hands, but I've about hit my limit. As always, the opinions of this reviewer are just that.. opinions of one person, but since I'm the one typing and you're the one reading, here goes..

Let's start with what they're doing right:
-The frozen, soggy "steamed" vegetables have been replaced with much a much better quality of vegetables that are delicious.
-The glass bottles of catsup are gone, replaced with squeeze bottles
(struggling to think of more positives)
Sorry. That's it... I can't think of anything else.

Now, let's turn to the items that could use a little work:
-Actually have food that is advertised available. It's sometimes easier to ask what they have than what they don't. I feel bad for the servers who have to deal with the negativity because they're trying to earn a living and provide service when nothing's really there to provide. An alarmingly high number of items on the menu have been covered up with "New Items Coming Soon" stickers. Pretty soon I expect them to just take the menus away.
-Portions have gotten smaller. Prices have gotten higher.
-Specials aren't so special. Heck, they didn't even have the special today. We were told that they were working in the kitchen and forgot to make the specials. A few weeks ago they forgot to order the chicken for the Thursday chicken special. Today's soup special was a bowl of emptiness because they ran out at lunch. No bacon for the eggs and bacon weekend breakfast. 
-Servers are turning over like crazy. Sometimes attrition is positive. Usually it isn't when everyone has left.
-I've waited over 1 hour and 15 minutes for an omelette.
-This used to be my go-to place with a friend for late night dessert. Now they have so few items on the dessert menu that it hardly seems worth it.

I'm hoping that Ivy's can recover from this, but it's going to take some focus and determination from the new owner to actually get things moving in the direction they should be. From what I can tell, it's more about how the owner is trying to change everything at once and failing miserably rather than the local management and servers fault. They were here before the change.. things seemed okay then.

I'll quit ranting now.. I might need to start looking for a new place for my weekend brunch and weekday dinners because.. well.. having food to actually eat is kind of important for a restaurant.

I watched this place get built and have been excited to try it, so this morning, after a nice springtime snowstorm, I headed over to give it a try.

This is a cute little place with the menu written in chalk along the wall. You walk to the rear of the place to order at the counter, are given a number a coffee cup (if you ordered coffee) and grab a seat. Plenty of interesting signs line the wall, and there was a movie playing on an overhead against the wall that I watched for the 90 seconds I was seated before my food came out.

I ordered the spicy mushroom biscuits and gravy to eat. A heaping plateful of gravy came out with little bits of biscuit placed underneath. More mushrooms than spicy, this was a pretty filling breakfast even for me, and I'm a fairly good eater. I left about a third of it on the plate.

Would I eat it again? Yes.. well, maybe. A half portion would have been the perfect size for me, and if I would have seen an option to add an egg to it, I would have jumped at the opportunity. I might have missed it.. there is a lot of stuff on the menu!

Yeah, I'll give this place a try again, although the prices were a tad higher than I would have prefered. But hey, you only live once.. it's only money, and #welcometomassave!

Picture it.. Indianapolis. 2014. A dreary Saturday afternoon. A group of friends sit around a communal table, candles going. The room is decorated in whites. To the left, a fireplace roars next to the Christmas tree. The friends laugh and talk about their weekend plans while sipping coffee and tea and nibbling on carmel and chocolate cakes, just happy to be with one another and enjoying each others company.

A dream? No. One of Sophia's "picture it" stories from The Golden Girls? No, although I did hear her voice as I wrote that. No sir.. this was real, and it happened to me yesterday at the Cake Bake Shop in Broadripple.

The cakes that are being made by these fine folks are outstanding. Delicious.. yes. Beautiful.. absolutely! The sheer beauty of these cakes makes it hard to even think about cutting into them, but one you have your first bite, you won't be able to stop.

Although I'm certainly above just having cake for lunch, I thought it best to try their soup special: homemade mushroom soup. Made fresh daily, this vegetarian soup is made with mushroom stock (no chicken) and was simple yet lovely. The presentation was nice too.. a crock of soup, some crusty bread for dipping and a tiny pad of butter all served together on a small rectangular plate.

The real star here was the Carmel Cake. I think I counted 6 layers.. maybe 7. The flavors were deep and rich, and I didn't put my fork down until it was gone! If there wasn't a line, I would have gone back for more.

My "meal" consisted of soup, carmel cake and an Americano and totaled $19 and some change. This place isn't cheap, but it's definitely worth checking out for a special evening.. or an afternoon among friends.
Possibly THE most grand, and beautifully situated building in America, but the exhibits themselves are just so-so. My favorite part is still the Rocky statue out front :P

Every once in awhile you inadvertently slam up against the limits of a restaurants capabilities. Dining here the other night with a group of friends, that "limit" hit us hard. I'll cut to the chase. This place is great if you want a good burger, beer, or sandwich at a cheap price. Eat at the bar and maybe order a glass of wine as well, and you're fine.
However, go beyond that, and order some of the main dish entrees, and things can get ugly fast. While our server was very pleasant, the service on an early Friday evening was painfully slow. And tables were served well out of order, so that multiple tables who arrived after us were served first. It took over an hour to get our food. Totally unacceptable and the  manager/hostess did nothing to make up for it. Comp us a drink? Nah. Free dessert or coffee even? Nope. 
Since I brought my 5 friends here for the first time, it was kind of embarrassing. None of them will go back, I'm quite sure.
The food itself was also mediocre. My GF had the grilled chicken sausage. The potatoes were good but the sausage was over cooked and nothing special. My wild pacific salmon was extremely bland and had almost no flavor. Rice was slightly underdone and the nice looking green beans were nearly raw. Yikes. The only satisfied customer was my friend who ordered the turkey burger. And I think that's the lesson here. Order a burger & beer, you'll be fine --- happy even. But given the very slow service and very mediocre entree quality, go beyond that and you may ask yourself why you came.
This is a big drop from my previous rating but I've noted some other recent poor reviews as well. Maybe somethings up in the kitchen? Idk but I prob won't be back to find out. There are too many other great choices in Lambertville to put up with this.

First, I love Korean food. I would eat Korean food every day if I could. I wish I was Korean. :) that being said this restaurant is fabulous. 

The space is clean and beautifully decorated. There are plenty of tables and booths - and high chairs if needed. Speaking of high chairs, they were super friendly and accommodating with my friends 1 year old. 

Next, they knew we were new to the restaurant and were super helpful! They let us sample everything ahead of time to ensure our meal was awesome. Everyone I was with ordered the dolsot bibimbap. I had already planned on it before arriving but a patron in the restaurant highly recommended it as well!

The food was prepared just as ordered and looked wonderful when served. It tasted even better!! I live quite far from Carmel but definitely plan on making the trek back as often as possible to order this dish. 

I also ordered ginger honey tea. It was served with freshly grated ginger and an extra kettle of hot water so I could refill several times. Awesome and unexpected for a restaurant with "fast" in the title. 

Finally, the service was friendly and prompt. Everything was done with a smile and each employee went the extra mile for us. It truly was a pleasure all the way around.

This may be my new favorite restaurant. The salad bar is delicious, potatoes are great and you cook your own filet, so seriously if you don't like it, it's probably your own fault. I will say that the experience does "sort" of depend on what server you get... But for the most part it's good food for a great price! Also we just went last night, which was a Thursday and they had line dancing. It was so fun to watch them!!!

I believe we have another entry for "If Pinterest Opened A Restaurant, it Would Look Like This".  It's airy, lots of white and blonde wood, high ceilings with exposed painted ductwork, open kitchen.

I arrived for lunch on a gorgeous afternoon, one of those rare winter days that reminds us that spring is coming.   As I entered on the right hand side was a table with artfully displayed artisan chocolate bars and t-shirts.  To the right of that were comfy sofas and an open drink case.

This is self-seat, self-serve except for coffees that they make for you, and there are communal long tables for you to eat at.  The self-serve food had a mix of some sandwiches, salads, some croissants/sticky buns, soups and all you can eat toast bar.  You take what you want then as you leave you tell someone what you had and you pay.  Kind of the honor system I guess?

I picked up my tray - a butcher block board - and selected the broccoli creek salad along with a chicken couscous soup.  Both were displayed nicely in white crocks.  They looked delicious, but they were both very bland. I questioned whether there was actually dressing on the salad, they assured me there was. OK.  The soup looked gorgeous but lacked flavor.  

I headed back for something more flavorful and snagged the last pecan sticky bun. This is most definitely worth getting.  Nutty, cinnamon, sweet, gooey, deliciousness.  This,  my friend, is sticky bun perfection.

The staff were nice, the place is gorgeous. I think when I have an occasion to go again I will stick to the sticky buns (see what I did there?) and some nice brewed tea or coffee.  It's that kind of place.

There's something wonderful about a spontaneous lunch with a good friend.  Fellow Yelper Dee M happened by right at lunchtime on a beautiful spring day where I actually didn't have back-to-back meetings.  Yay!  We decided to check out the newly opened Nam Phuong Bistro.  I've been hoping to find good Vietnamese food since the closing of Saigon Harbor in Havertown last year.  

The restaurant is located in the old bar section of the now-defunct Gullaine's, a long time Ardmore place.  The other half of that restaurant was demolished to make way for new development.  The space has been beautifully renovated , taking advantage of existing high ceilings and exposed brick walls.  We arrived shortly after the 'lunch rush' and found the place to be very clean and comfortable.   

We were greeted warmly and our drink orders taken.  I chose the Vietnamese fried rice with chicken (I know, not authentic, but I love the dish) and Dee chose the beef sautéed with vegetables.  As an appetizer we got vegetable spring rolls.  The spring rolls were good, crunchy and not greasy, not the very best but good.  My fried rice was...fine.  A little on the mushy side, and missing that sweet zing that Saigon Harbor's had.  I'll let Dee tell you about her beef dish in her review :)  

Service was very good and prices were reasonable for lunch.  I wavered between 3 and 4 stars, opting for 4 based on the atmosphere and service.  It's not my favorite Vietnamese restaurant, however it's very good for the suburbs.  It's a quick 2 block walk from the Ardmore Train Station and 1 12 blocks from the bus station, very accessible by public transit!  I am hoping that the ongoing construction all around the restaurant - both across the street and next door - do not impede the success of this place as it's a great dining spot in our little village of Ardmore.

Anthony's has been one of those places that we see and think "we should go there sometime" then never remember when we think "where should we go to eat?"  I have no idea why, but it happens - until finally we said one night "hey, why don't we go there?" So we did.

The restaurant is clean, casual and has it's own 'feel'.  All around you see that their pizzas are "well done" which of course is a play on words: they are both well done as in very good and well done as in you will see little crispy black burnt spots on the crust because of the coal-fired oven. 

We were exceptionally hungry and also eager to sample so we got a large pizza, calzone, salad and the chicken wings.  Both the NMT and the Rev were skeptical of the wings because they're not drenched in some kind of hot spicy or sweet sauce.  As it turns out, the wings are so delicious putting a sauce on them would be  food crime. They loved them.  The wings are clearly the rockstar item of the night.

Pizza is huge, very thin crust, nice balance of sauce and cheese and yes, little spots of black from the coal firing.  It was very good.  Calzone was typical, overloaded with cheese and some meats, also by the way huge.  Salad was fine. Nothing to shout to the rooftops over.  Acceptable.

 Service varied between our clearly assigned to the table server who was very minimally present and seemed bored and others who brought out the food, clearly helping out, who made a big deal of serving the pizza and overall being enthusiastic and interested in whether we were enjoying our visit.  This likely is a training or front-of-house management issue, as we felt the presentation was annoyingly inconsistent.  

Much of our food went home with us, and weathered well as leftovers.  We'd definitely go again.

I have a confession to make...I don't like their beer.  Yes, I realize I am likely the only person in Philly who feels this way.  I get it.  To be clear, though, it's not their beer in particular I don't like. I don't like "IPAs", which are currently popular.  I'm a pilsner gal, simple and true. 

So when I was invited to join a group at Tired Hands, i went figuring I'd be drinking water.  I got there early, and fellow Yelper Dee M and I sat at the bar.  Then I had a lovely conversation with John, our bartender, confessing my dislike and assuring him it's not personal.  He was great, working with me, giving me samples of different brews until I found one I liked decently, Huzza!

Cue the rest of the UYE folks' arrival, and off to a long table we went.  The Fermentaria is a working brewery, as others have mentioned, and it has an industrial hip atmosphere, almost like you're eating in the employee cafeteria that's really nice. The building housing it is an old trolley shed that they brought back to life, with broadly sloping high ceilings and such.  It's cool, casual, not overly fancy.

The food was very good - we went for small bites and I got the pretzels, which were quite yummy, yeasty and warm with just the right amount of salt.

I give them props for knowing who they are and at the same time working hard to find me a happy place. I would definitely go again when others plan.

They closed January 20, 2020.  Lease expiration.  We went there often when my son was a wee one - it was kind of a hub for families in our community.  They had great milkshakes, good good and a model train circulating above the dining room.  

I have a sad. 

https://www.inquirer.com/food/rubys-diner-closed-ardmore-suburban-square-burger-fries-shake-20200121.html?outputType=amp

Who can miss the glittering jewel that is the new Bam Bam Kitchen in Ardmore?  Located on Lancaster Avenue, right by the Ardmore Music Hall, the restaurant positively glows with sparkle and color.  

The NMT, Panda and I went to Bam Bam for lunch one weekend afternoon, slightly after the 'main' lunch time.  We were greeted warmly and seated in a sunny alcove.  Our server actually offered water right away, which is a rare thing in restaurants these days.  

We ordered the Seafood Stone Bowl, Bulgolgi Stir Fry, seafood pancake and the Kan Phong (Deep Fried) shrimp.  The seafood pancake was loaded with seafood and the guys loved it.  The Stone Bowl was very good, very hot at first though and took a while to cool enough to eat.  The rockstar item was the deep fried shrimp: the sauce was an amazing combo of sweet and spicy and savory, I'm not sure how they got all that in but it was YUM even without the shrimp (I am allergic).  The bulgogi stir fry should really I think be called a bulgogi fajita presentation, as it arrived on a sizzling plate with caramelized onions, with white rice served on the side.  It was nicely presented and tender, but this is the sole place where I think they fell short as I found the bulgogi to be rather bland.   

Overall, it was a good experience, with good food and good service.  They need to think about putting pillows or cushion on the upright banquette seating as bare walls get hard on the back.   Where I worry is in the pricing, especially for lunch.  The three of us spent almost $80 on lunch, which is high for this area, and there are many places in Ardmore who serve equal or better quality food for less.  My hope is that they will adjust to this locale and offer a lunch menu that will allow them to be competitive in a wonderful restaurant area.  

I may be back, but only when I want to 'splurge'.

FDC is most definitely a Francophile.  She studied at the Sorbonne.  Her degree is in French Literature. So, when her half-century birthday came, I made a point to stop at Delice et Chocolat for their macaroons.  They are her favorite.

The shop is tucked in a row of c 1900-1925 storefronts directly next to the Ardmore Train Station.  The space is bright and sparkling, not cluttered, with bakery cases not so full of items by the time I got there because they make everything by hand each morning.  When it's sold, there are no freezer cases full of more inventory to sell.  This is the real deal, so get there early.

They were as nice as could be in helping me select a variety of macaroons for FDC, and my order was packaged nicely.  They've recently expanded to the next storefront over (where Radio Shack was for many years) and are now serving lunch items.  

Price was not inexpensive but reasonable for quality hand - made fresh baked goods. Parking is not the easiest, however for a fairly quick dash in on a weekend I was able to park in the train station lot. There's some metered parking on the street and a public lot 1/2 a block away.  Also, the train is literally right there as are the bus stops, so very transit friendly.

FDC was ecstatic, said theirs are the closest she's had to when she was studying in France.  I'll definitely be back.

What can I say about Isgro that hasn't been said already?  This is one of the Italian 'traditional' bakeries in South Philadelphia for generations.  By 'traditional' I mean that my 83 year old fathers' birthday cake came from them, the cookies served at my christening 32 years later came from them, and the cannoli served at my nephew's first holy communion came from them.  

As with any South Philadelphia business that has stayed in business this long, Isgro knows what they do well, and they do that continuously. So when my dear friend and I were down in South Philly and craved cannoli, we knew where to go.

Typical for South Philly is that the parking is challenging and it's not unusual to find 'creative' parking solutions (double parking, maybe that could be a spot).  We found a spot about a block away though, which was nice.  Going in is like going back in time, it's very unchanged from years ago, and there's a comfort in that. It smells of flour and cake baking, which is comforting.   I ordered a pound of assorted cookies for a shiva call I was making the next day and we both got a cannoli. The service was as usual, they were very busy, staff was efficient and businesslike. 

The cannoli were heavenly, not overly sweet, nice crisp shell that collapsed nicely as the treat was eaten.  Yum. The cookies were received well and I managed to get a couple too, again not overly sweet with a texture that almost dissolves in my mouth.  Yeah, that good.

I am looking forward to enjoying Isgro over and over again.  They're a pillar of delicious tradition in a sea of constant change. Here's to another 100 years and more generations of our family incorporating their treats in our lives.

What do Colonial Williamsburg and Peddler's Village have in common?  Well, both are largely reconstructions of "colonial era" villages, both are basically in the countryside, both are tourist destinations, including a hotel on site, and both are decently well done.  

Yes, folks, Colonial Williamsburg, except for the Governor's House, is a reconstruction built in the 50s.  I'm surprised at how often people don't know that.

But I digress...

I had heard many times about Peddler's Village over the years, noticing also that the Patriarch's Senior Center regularly offered bus trips there, and thought, hm, some day I should go there and check it out.

Lion and I visited the weekend before Christmas, taking the chance to stretch our legs after a long day of driving. Despite it being a very busy weekend we had no trouble parking and even with the crowds never felt it was 'too much'.  The stores were all decorated as was the interior common area. It was daytime so no lights were on but we could see it would be quite pretty at night.

The shops were, for the most part, pretty much what we'd expect from a tourist shopping destination.  Unique were the German store, which had beautiful clocks and steins, a 'man cave' store that had mostly design documents for rooms and a fixtures store that reminded me of Restoration Hardware.

There are a few restaurants, a candy store and a popcorn place for food. Given that it was a crowded day we opted to go elsewhere in the area to eat.  

Overall I think they've done a nice job and it's an enjoyable day. I can't say I'd make a special trip to go there, however if I were in the area again I would stop again.
