Sometimes, life throws you a curve ball and you hit the ball well.  Such is the case when the place where I originally intended to meet a friend for lunch turned out to open later on weekends.  My bad, I should have checked. We decided to head over to Brittingham's Pub for a drink, that turned into lunch and good time too.  

I've driven past this place hundreds of times. Often with FDC she recalls fondly, if a little fuzzily, good times in college. The original part of the building dates to the 1700s when RBI's was an inn in a main thoroughfare.  It's now a well kept, if rambling, restaurant & bar, with some lovely patio seating in the rear.  

We were provided drink menus quickly and our drinks were poured expertly.  The bar area is comfortable and bright, with an abundance of natural light.  There are TVs above the bar showing various games.  The spillover dining areas are TV free.  

The drink menu was pretty standard and, compared to what I'm used to, has less variety in beers.  Still it was adequate and we both got a beer we enjoyed.  The drinks were of substantial size.  

As time went on we were enjoying the place so much we decided to stay there & get a light lunch.  Menus were provided.  We ordered the calamari, Korean spring rolls, pretzel rivets & I got a wedge salad.  I am a big fan of the wedge.  

We decide to move to a long wood slab table to eat.  Our food comes reasonably quickly.  I didn't have the calamari because of my seafood allergy.  My friend reported them to be fine.  Of the others the rock star was the Korean Spring Rolls.  They were fresh and mixed some interesting flavors and textures.  We loved them.  The pretzels were average.  Wedge was above average with plenty of bacon and bleu cheese.  Pretty yummy. 

Our bartender/served was friendly and knowledgeable, she checked often to make sure we were happy.  

Overall it was quite pleasant, nothing like the college watering hole my sister recalled.  I'd love to go back sometime soon to check out their dinner menu.

Made a pilgrimage yesterday.  

In all seriousness, I'm a suburban dweller, and Stocks' is in an old part of the city where parking is...creative.  I've always gotten my fix through satellite bakery locations or fundraisers.  

Yesterday, though, I decided to go to the source.  I needed to go someplace nearby.  What the heck.  

First, it's easier to get to than it seems.  Do not follow Google Maps.  Their directions are nuts.  95-Aramingo- Lehigh.  

Second, they have a "loading zone only" curb right out front.  Easy parallel pull in except if someone decides to creatively park.  Expect creativity, this is Philly.  

Third, they have an employee outside who staggers entry and tells you which of 3 stations to go to.  Wasn't crowded so no wait.  

The place is so so so typical of a Philly row home bakery, it was like stepping back in time.  Glass cases, "marbled" Formica countertops, linoleum floors.  Clean, and smells like heaven. 

They have plastic barriers up across the counter and you hand your money through a slot.  Purchase is placed in a corral at the end of the row.  

Cash only.  

The pound cake super fresh from the oven is absolutely not shareable.  I don't care who you are.  It's fantastic.  Mine, my precious!  All mine!  Gets your own, I says!

The food and service are always spot on here at Oasis. The Burrito's are my favorite choice for takeout and their Fish Tacos with Mahi-mahi an excellent choice and my go-to for eat-in meal. Try one of their daily specials, they are a great choice as well and arr creative and delicious. Prices are reasonable for the quality and portions and the service is always friendly and helpful. Be sure to check out Taco Tuesday here.

The restaurant space is small but smartly decorated and inviting and comfortable.  They have tables available outside in the warmer weather.  Don't forget to bring your Corona's or other favorite beer or wine as Oasis like all of Collingswood restaurants, is a BYOB.

Finally had an opportunity to visit Central Taco & Tequila, the 23rd restaurant operated by PJW Restaurant Group. This location was formerly the Irish Mile.

I really like the open and spacious industrial look and feel of the interior restaurant with plenty of large windows amplifying the 150 seat space. They have an outdoor deck off the back side of the restaurant with some seating and plenty of tables and umbrellas setup out front in what used to be the parking lot pre-pandemic.

The food was decent with some great menu options and service was excellent, but based on my first visit, I would frequent more for the impressive tequila list (91 total) and margaritas then the food.  More visits and tasting needed to fully review the food.

Dinner Review: I bookmarked this restaurant after seeing in on a local TV show that highlights area eateries.  My main attraction to the Hash House was for the breakfast meals which I thought they served all day. After arriving late afternoon, we found out that the breakfast menu was no longer being offered :(  Missed it by that much  . . .!

We order up a few cocktails and browsed the dinner menu since we had been scouting the breakfast menu previously.  After checking the menu and referencing Yelp reviews on the dinner menu items like any good Yelper, we decided on Andy's  World Famous Sage Fried Chicken & Waffles, a Cesar Salad and a side of mac & Cheese.  The platter sizes are large, 2 of us split the Fried Chicken & Waffles and it was just the right amount. Loved the bacon slices cooked into the waffles. 

The service was spot on, our server Paul was on his game, helpful, pleasant and professional. The restaurant is spacious, smarty decorated with comfortable seating options including outdoor seating

I perceived this restaurant as being primarily a breakfast place, why else name it Hash House?  The food was decent enough, but I would not have come in for the dinner menu and definitely wont come back for it, there are too many other great options for dinner out there.  That said, I will come back to try out breakfast.  I was torn on the rating between 2-3 stars.  The service put it over the top.

The Kettle & Grille is a family run neighborhood restaurant focused on casual American cooking. Owner Peter Savva's father ran the Harvest Diner in Cinnaminson. Their menu is full of American classics, along with a some international favorites from the owners.  They have a huge selection of food to chose from, there is a meal for everyone.

They get busy on weekends for breakfast and do not accept reservations. Expect a small wait, they turnover quickly and have booths large enough for 6.  The service is friendly and efficient and the restaurant is kept sparkling clean. 

I have not had lunch or dinner here, but enjoy the breakfast.  My goto is the SOS. There is plenty of parking in the shopping center lot and cover from the rain outside if you have to wait for a table.

If you like beer and burgers, this is the place to go.  Daily board specials list current beer on tap selections, be sure to check these out on your visit. A must get on the appetizer menu is the Cheese fries with short rib gravy.  This is a great app to share with your crew on your visit.

For burgers, my favorite is the Second Coming, 100% dry aged sirloin, chopped overnight tomatoes, roasted garlic aioli, gruyère cheese, shoestring fries and a pickle.  This is the burger you want when your crav'n a Burger!  For those not into beef, they have Turkey, Black Bean and Wasabi Tuna burgers, all great choices.

If your not in a burger mood, be sure to try one of their awesome sammys, like the Grilled  Chicken & Mushroom sandwich with gruyère, candied bacon, sautéed 'shrooms, onion straws, garlic aioli, toasted sourdough or their Short Rib Melt sandwich with short rib, vermont white cheddar, pickled onion, garlic almond aioli, sourdough bread. 

Wednesdays feature buck-a-shuck oysters, they have daily app and beer specials and be sure to try the She Crab soup if you are here on a Friday.

The foodie in me is really excited about this restaurant opening so near my work. Stopped in for lunch today & got the Rebellion Ramen, and walked out almost a new man. Every component of this dish had its own intriguing flavor and texture (especially texture), and when combined together made for an unforgettable bowl of food. Will think about this one for a while... Until I go back & get another one, that is. Can already tell that the kitchen is doing amazing things.

I don't know what I just experienced. The owner/chef must be going through a tough time.  He seemed very out of sorts.

My wife and I ate there in the evening and it was a bizarre affair. The chef asked us what we ordered no less than 5 times. Every few minutes he would yell  at us from the kitchen asking what we had ordered. Yet he managed to get my order wrong.

The food was ok. I had the rabbit and my wife had puttanesca with sausage. Both dishes were palatable. 

The forgetting of the order wouldve seemed weird, maybe quirky, if the chef hadnt turned to yell at a pair of men who seemed to be minding their own business. It's a very small place so the cursing and the raising of his voice had maximum impact. They promptly left. The atmosphere quickly became extremely uncomfortable.  A couple who appeared to be on a date were also repeatedly asked what their order was, we wished them good luck before we left.

I don't know what happened but the owner is clearly going through some issues. Hopefully he figures things out because this little place has so much potential.

Enterprise Fish Co offered up an excellent meal, and good times! Refreshing red sangria to start, and we kept them flowing throughout our meal, perfect for a hot summer day in Santa Barbara. 

The lobster bisque with puff pastry was exquisite, and a must get. Velvety and deep. 

The entire menu looked so appealing that it made it difficult to make a choice. I finally decided to create a makeshift surf and turf: chimichurri steak (appetizer size) and the mixed seafood grill. It was a terrific creation, if I do say so myself! The seafood grill was a skewer with salmon, scallops and shrimp, and I think halibut: gigantic pieces of fresh and juicy seafood. I highly recommend it.

I was really satisfied with every part of my meal and experience! I don't understand the 3.5 star rating? Maybe it has something to do with the night you're there, or maybe they're really inconsistent, but this happened to be an excellent Thursday night for me.

Thanks to Angela R. for the superb recommendation! :-)

Fresh...fast...and its not Subway or McDonalds? Yes, please! If you've not had the chance to check off Korean cuisine from your "List of Ethnic Foods to Try", Omoni is a great place to start. Their menu is relatively simple, the food IS fresh and fast, and of course delicious.

I was looking for all of the above in Carmel one Friday evening, but wasn't feeling the usual Panera. Then I remembered I had bookmarked Omoni! My friends and I came in the early dinner hour so we had the place to ourselves. The space is setup similar to the likes of Q'doba (et al) -- you walk up to the counter and order your main dish and then go down the line of fresh and cooked ingredients to add to it. Because we got there early, we had a chance to speak with the owner about his business. All of his dishes are his mother's original recipes and are made fresh daily. I loved hearing this and he seemed so excited to be bringing some culture and delicious food to Carmel!

My vegetarian buddy and I ordered the Chap Chae, sweet potato-based noodles with optional tofu swap for the beef, while our other friend nabbed the Dolsot Bibimbap, beef in a hot stone bowl with crispy rice. The Chap Chae was a little bland at first. But, mixing in some veggies, hot sauce, and soy sauce doctored it up. I would have preferred it to have a little more sauce to it, but perhaps that is just the nature of the dish. The Bibimbap was so delicious, complete with hot egg on top! It takes a little longer to cook than the other dishes, but so worth it. And all of those veggies on the line...mmmm...the daikon radishes, pickled cukes, and kimchi were my fave. So fresh!

We finished our meal off with some yummy mochi ice cream! I highly recommend the red bean flavor.

I agree with a lot of other reviews for this place that it has a few little kinks to work out, but I really do hope Omoni sticks around and continues to bring something new and different to Carmel. The service is great and the food is definitely different from anything you'd normally associate with "fast food".

First let me start by saying, do the wine membership! If you're local to SB then you definitely get a ton of use out of it and who can complain about free tastings? 

With that being said, Corks is one of my favorite Funk Zone tasting room for the sheer fact they always have good wines from smaller wineries. They are a tasting room but not affiliated with a winery.

Service is meh but they have a great collection of wines especially from the CentralCoast. There has only been one shipment in the past three years that I haven't loved!

Nick Morello is their GM and is a wine maker. His Morello Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon are always a good one to fall back on and is my go to gift for out of towners. The rose's tastings are perfect during the hot summer months and hit the spot.

Grab a drink and chill on the patio and people watch in the funk zone or grab a spot in front of the fire place on a cold day.
This is a great place.  The staff was friendly and prompt. We had the tater tots and they were great.  Beer is solid and really clean.  Great work.

Update-3/30/2013:  I'm back because of the NASTY emails I received because of my review (below).  Notice a trend on the reviews: either 5 stars or 1 star... nothing in between.  I can't prove it and I will leave it up to Yelp to decide, but I suspect the 5 star reviews come from friends, family, and people associated with the restaurant.  I stand by my review as is.
Review: 
Just got home from dinner at Elaia, after first driving thru McDonalds.  I'll explain that in a moment.  First let me say that my wife and I enjoy the wonderful St Louis restaurants like Copia, Frazers, Sydney Street Cafe, Savor,  Modesto, Barcelona, Prime 1000, etc.  We also like the modest and fun places like Seamus McDaniels, Pats, Tuckers, Crown Candy, Benton Street Cafe.  
Elaia is a nice little restaurant.  Modestly decorated and friendly, attentive staff.  The food was well prepared.  Our problem was with the rediculously small portion sizes.  And this was not the tapas side of the restaurant, Olio.  The eggplant appetizer was one slice of eggplant so thin you could see the plate through it.  My wife ordered the Pasta and Scallops.  It should have been called "and Scallop".  One scallop on a small portion of pasta ( on a very big plate though!)  I ordered the "Beef"  dish.  I asked first and was told it was strip steak with potatoes and mushrooms.  Hmmm, not quite.  It was two very small slices off of a strip steak and two fingerling potatoes.  My guess is they cook one steak and get 3 to 4 servings from it.  Not sure.  
My point is that for entrees in the high $20's these portion sizes are not good.  Maybe it is a trendy chef a little too full of himself.  This place will never last.  Sorry.

Went in for a friends birthday on a Tuesday night.  Made reservations for 10 people, wound up being about 16, and that's when the everything started going sideways.. 

It's a Tuesday night.  You'd think that 16 people walk in interested in a lot of booze and food would be appreciated and bring at least a "B game"....well, you're wrong.  We spent about $300 or so just at the bar...but that didn't stop the manager coming up to my wife and start complaining that "If we'd known, we would have done a minimum price contract....you should have let us know."  Wait, can you not handle large groups?  And why is it OUR problem?  We actually did have reservations for 10 already, sorry it was a bit more.  And who signs a contract for dinner?  I have NEVER signed an agreement for dinner with a restaurant unless they are privately catering an event.  Her attitude was insulting and basically made it seem like we were putting her out.

Then when we were seated, they told us "don't crowd the people sitting in the same section."  Wait...it's an almost empty restaurant....we don't care where we sit and why are you assuming we're going to be jerks?  They didn't try to put any tables together, and the service still sucked even though they added an obligatory 20% gratuity.  We weren't demanding, but for the prices that they were charging I would think the waitress would know what seasonal beers are on tap and not have us wondering "hey, did she forget about us?" when she left halfway through taking drink orders at our (separate from the main table) table.

Food itself: so so.  The appetizer was good, but the actual sushi was mediocre.  The unagi nigiri was something like eel jerky, and the spicy tuna itself wasn't actually spicy...just jalapenos. 

We spent about $1000 overall.  Did we get our money's worth?  Absolutely not.  If you want sushi in the CBD...I'll have to say that you have to go somewhere else.

NOTE:  Emailed the owner/manager who basically said she was working that location that night and didn't recall you.  She tried to defend signing a contract to (paraphrase) that they have experienced servers on hand and the "kitchen doesn't get overwhelmed."  If that's what they consider a small kitchen, I'm stunned and don't know what to say and have to question their size standards.  That kitchen is open, and HUGE!!!!  

She also said that the "spicy tuna doesn't have jalepenos" which now kind of scares me...I tried the fish seperately and it was bland tuna, and the peppers were definitely providing the heat.

Now I'm wondering what they served me???  I really feel ripped off now.

Foods always been good. I've had dinner and brunch here multiple times before. Outdoor seating where you can see their herb gardens growing. Good variety of beer. Frequent live music. Service has been great every time I've been here except once.

You know, sometimes you've just gotta trust your instincts. All the years I've lived on this beach and nothing about Caddy's has ever impressed me.  I've spent lots of time and money here and each time swore I would never return.  I gave this place another shot over the weekend with friends and regretted it immediately.

Not only was the service STILL lousy, but l swear, it was worse than before.  I stood at a mostly empty bar waiting to order a beer while the bartenders (one of whom, I must add, is related to the owner) talked to each other .  No smile or hello even.  I had a brain fart and ordered food.  I figured a salad was safe, right?  Tough to mess THAT up, right?   The pitiful looking thing was full of wilted ( and I am generous with this term) lettuce and the other ingredients were equally yucky.  It looked like it had been sitting out on the counter all day.  I did not even attempt to eat it, nor did I complain.  It would do no good.  They just don't care.  My peeps had well done (not by choice) burgers which they ignored, too. We were all a bit undone over the food, although we knew what to expect.  Somehow, you hope you'll be wrong...   

However, having said this, I want to say that Jerry, the manager, is a really nice guy.  He has his hands full with all the ding dongs who work there and really, he does the best he can with what he has to work with.  I used to laugh it all off, but come on, it's just not funny anymore. 

I'm not trying to be pissy britches.  I swear.  I HATE fussing.  Maybe it's just me.  Maybe I'm missing a gene that allows me to hang out here and have fun.  Maybe I'm just too old (NOT!).  No, I  guess it's just one of those places that caters to drunk, young, A-holes who only come out for the eye candy (which I must say was lacking this day).  I'm over it. 

The beach takes a beating from this place, as I mentioned previously, and the addition of a half dozen or so porta potties is the straw that broke the camel's back.  Now you can sit on a dirty beach and smell the stinch of outdoor restrooms.  Does it get any better than that?  Caddy's sucks.

My wife and I stopped in Tucson during our honeymoon road trip and decided to find a nice spot for NYE to have dinner. The reviews seemed okay but the service and the food was some of the worst I have experienced in a long time. 

There was a preset three course dinner that we ordered. We waited 20-25 minutes for our first course only to be greeted by a new server who said they did not actually have the oysters app, and asked if I would be okay with shrimp instead. That was fine by me, but we then had to wait a long time to receive our food. When we did eventually get it, the obviously improvised shrimp dish was beyond too salty. When I told the server she simply said okay and took it away. No offer to sub it out or anything. 

We got the entrees pretty quickly and those were decent...however, after the entrees we waited again for 20-25 minutes to have anyone approach us about dessert. I ended up having to hail down a server and ask if we could just skip the last part of the dinner and get the check. They then attempted to charge us for the entire thing including the dessert & champagne we didn't want.. nearly 100 dollars. We didn't want to even attempt the last part of their meal because it had already been such a terrible experience.

The chef came over to apologize for the huge fail in the kitchen, which was nice of him to do. They then took off 20 bucks to make up for it.. not nearly enough for this catastrophe of a night on NYE. Afterwards you would expect them to expedite the checking out process to get us out quickly after such an unpleasant experience...but of course not. We waited a long time for a server just to run our card. And it was NOT that busy.

Bad experience, never again!

EDIT:
The response we received back was EXTREMELY rude. Such a poor experience & ownership. It is ridiculous for the owner to comment about my wife making it "abundantly clear" because she stated that we were good and ready to leave. No one tried to remedy the mishaps that happened through out the night until the chef came out.

Also, your "best efforts" were weak. I am not a professional reviewer by any means, but you are supposed to be a professional so act like it and quit with the passive aggressive, petty responses and show some class. The chef self-admittedly said it wasn't their best work this evening. Maybe take it from him and just admit when you've had a bad night.

Never again.  The crab rangoon was decent, but sesame chicken is definitely not traditional Chinese.  I thought I received the wrong order, but apparently Ming's does not serve their version in a sauce.

Everything was delicious. Our server Sofia was very attentive and efficient. The service was upto par as well as the food. 

Authentic and freshly made Mexican food... The chicken was a little dry... But everything else was delicious. Can't wait to come back. 

Happy hour makes you nothing but happy.
Sangria is so refreshing!

Try it out!

A local gem fresh on the Mid-town scene. 

Don't let the size fool you, there is more than meets the eye here and it's all good! 

I've been here twice since I discovered it last week and both times were equally great experiences that inspired me to add this place to my rotation of local favorites.

The vibe: is welcoming and chill, with comfy seating, good music and cool decor. Each time I sat at the bar along side other locals who stopped in to  enjoy their favorite dish and unwind with a cocktail or two.

The food selection has something for everyone....including VEGAN!!! Yay! 
I had the portobello mushroom dish, brussels sprout appetizer and red lentil falafel! The attention to flavor detail in each dish was on point and you can taste that they use farm fresh ingredients :)
  
My ultimate favorite was the falafel! Best in town thus far and I plan to return many times for that one. The avocado sauce and marinated veggies add a perky twist to the unbelievably tender falafel....so good. Next up is the jackfruit tacos, as I hear they are the bomb! 

The drinks: strong and delicious!! Homegrown Gastropub has a full bar with wine, a selection of draft beers and amazing craft cocktails made with the freshest ingredients. My favorite is the Whisky Social. Super refreshing! Upscale drinks without the upscale price. 

The service: I sat at the bar both times and Spencer  (owner) nailed it with the food, drinks and service. He took the time to explain their vegan options and went the extra mile with each customer at the bar to ensure a good experience. The waitresses were very welcoming and attentive. They also took the time to explain menu options to people and offer suggestions. I enjoyed seeing how well the staff interacted with each other and they seemed happy to be part of such a great pub. It made for a great vibe. 

Their prices are moderate and very fair compared to other local healthy restaurants. 

Besides the food and drinks, the best part about this place is, they serve food until 2am! I'll be back for sure and I highly recommend popping in to check em out :)

So many beers, so few livers!  They seriously have more taps than I've ever seen and what a great beer selection! The location is kinda odd but I really dig the patio and my favorite table shaped like the state of Nevada. They don't do food which is the only real downside, but there are many places in the shopping center you can grab a bite.  If you're a beer lover, or just want a cool place to hang out you should check it out. Keep an eye out for thier tap takeovers and trivia nights!

A carnivore's delight!  Dined here last night w/35 folks in a private room for the 65th b'day of a Meetup's organizer. Opened in October, the prices have already been increased. It's located @the Tucson Mall in the location of the former Twigs restaurant. The price for the salad bar + freshly grilled meats is $41.95 and tax & tip. The unlimited salad bar is above average w/offerings such as squash soup. black beans, cheese, salami & procuitto, chicken salad, olives & sun-dried tomatoes. Meat, meat & more meat: the 'gauchos' constantly come around w/12 cuts of meat to include top sirloin, beef & pork ribs, bacon wrapped chicken & filet mignon, sausage, leg of lamb & lamb chops. You will be asked how done U prefer ur meat & it is top quality, nicely charred and seasoned simply w/salt. Garlic mashed spuds, caramelized sweet plantains & cheese rolls are served @the table. The service is outstanding w/a team leader, someone circulating w/water and bussing tables + the polite & efficient gauchos (waiters). When I asked for a particular cut of meat, it appeared very quickly. A nice addition to the Tucson culinary scene & ideal for special celebrations.

Just around the corner from my 'working class neighborhood' street in U-City is Winslow's home.

I woke up this morning and thought "I want an omelette, but there are no diners around here I bet."

Yelp tells me Winslow's home is a diner (it's decidedly not - yelp shouldn't classify it as such.) and they have omelettes on the menu (no, they don't, actually)

So I hike on down there and walk in and get directed like a detainee at a camp through the whole Winslow's experience. 

"Order there, then come back here. You may sit at one of the two small tables, or a single person table. No not THAT small table that seats four, that's for a group. Sit at this table that seats 8 (what?)."

I asked about the omelettes, I was told they don't make those except as a special sometimes, and then told I should order a breakfast sandwich, which I did, with OJ and a Machiatto.

The service was abysmal. Rudeness abounds. I guess I needed to have the REI/Gap/Old Navy uniform on instead of jeans and a t-shirt.

Other patrons were rude too - while I'm standing there looking at the menu (which is scribbled on dry erase boards) I practically got shoved out of the way by some granola-yuppie.

It's great to hear with every order how organic and awesome Winslows Home is:

"Fresh squeezed orange juice (which is gross)"
"Sugar in the Raw, and would you like Soy with that?"
"How about a shade tree grown bamboo stick up your bum? We all have one!"


The Machiatto sucked. The OJ was bland and had not only pulp but orange rind in it.
The breakfast sandwich was palatable, I will admit.

I feel I wasted a perfectly good Thursday morning at Winslow's when I would have gotten better treatment amongst my fellow 'commoner's' at Saint Louis Bread Co.

Wear your yoga pants and your sense of entitlement, and leave your manners, good taste, and sense of value at home. That's the best way to make yourself feel at 'Home' here.

Del Frisco's is home to one of the great bars in Philadelphia.   It's vast expanse is mesmerizing, and it becomes more vast with every delicious cocktail you quaff.  

Del Frisco's also is the place to been seen; even on a random Wednesday night, the place was jammed with glitterati, politicos and movers and shakers.   One suspects the bar has become a magnet in the aftermath of the the Four Seasons Hotel's closure and the Ritz-Carlton's precipitous decline post-Chef Ripert. 

At a recent outing, we cut a wide swath through the menu.   Everyone raved about the cheesesteak lollipops, the jumbo shrimp cocktail, the steak tartare, the wedge salad and the composed salad of beefsteak tomato and red onion.  As to the latter, the dressing was superb but the salad would be improved if the onions were soaked to reduce their pungency.

The table's entrees included various cuts of steak, the lamb chops and the veal.  The carnivore chorus sang their elation in perfect harmony.  Although not on the menu, I enjoyed a dinner portion of filler-free jumbo lump crab cakes.  The best crab cakes I have had outside of Annapolis.  

Standouts among the sides were the garlic spinach and the lobster mac and cheese.   Our friends singled out for praise the potatoes au gratin (far too dense with cheese for me), the asparagus (with sliced almonds) and the mushrooms.   I surmise the onion rings were not a favorite inasmuch there was no positive commentary.  

The table's desserts received also rave reviews.   The misnamed "chocolate soufflé" was actually a lava cake accompanied by the most gorgeous vanilla ice cream with chocolate chunks.  The other crowd-pleaser was the butter cake.   The table's cake-eaters declared it "delicious."  

There is no question that we will return.

Our $14 chicken cheesesteaks were an abomination.   The chicken was soggy and tasteless (as if it had been steamed) and it was served partially shredded and partially in ginormous chunks.   Perversely, the sandwich including a mix of what-appeared-to-be boiled pearl onions, wet chopped peppers and charred mystery vegetation.  Whomever was manning the kitchen clearly had no idea about the anatomy of a proper Philadelphia cheesesteak (chicken or otherwise).  The sandwiches were a disgusting and heartburn-inducing tepid mess.   To add insult to injury, the formerly delicious hand-cut shoestring fries have been replaced by cold kettle chips.   

Who knew that a rooster could lay an egg? Sadly, this one can!!

Some culinary treasures are simultaneously obvious and obscure.  Chef Vargas' restaurant is one of them.  It's on York Road in Elkins Park in an impossible to miss multi-building apartment complex (I know!) but behind what-appear-to-be service doors at the south end of the complex. The restaurant's only external signage is a small sandwich board outside of the service doors. 

The Mister had the huevos rancheros, which he pronounced "delicious" and requiring a return visit for more, while I had the Caribbean Benedict.  My breakfast consisted of a pile of beautifully seasoned pulled pork sitting atop the most delicious, caramelized maduros I have ever had.  Completing the plate were two flawlessly  poached eggs, a lovely latinized Hollandaise, and crispy-on-the-outside, creamy-on-the-inside home fries.  Next time we visit, I may very well order a bowl of those fantastic maduros.  

Chef Vargas' restaurant is worth seeking out if you are a fan of authentic Latin cuisine.  In addition to the delicious, freshly made food, the restaurant's prices were reasonable, the service was charming and attentive and the coffee was outstanding.

In connection with a social gathering at our home, we recently had a butter cookie taste test and Swiss Haus Bakery came in second place.  The competition included butter cookies from Rilling's, Feasterville Family Bakery, Leonardo's, and Desserts by Design.   Chosen as for the test was the flower-shaped butter cookie with the chocolate center, which all of the bakeries offer.     

First place honors went to Rillings for its cookie's relatively soft crumb and clear butter flavor.   Our quibble was that the center dollop of chocolate was a bit sweet and hard, but overall it was a good cookie.   The other first place winner was Feasterville, whose cookie is very delicate and nearly disintegrates on the tongue (like any great shortbread).  One has to carefully transport Feasterville's cookies because they easily crumble in transit.  Again, the chocolate center was a bit sweet and hard.   Both Rilling's and Feasterville could elevate these cookies to epic status by replacing the chocolate frosting with a bittersweet ganache.

Second place went to Swiss Haus Bakery, whose butter cookies are a perennial household favorite.   The Swiss Haus version is much firmer than either than Rilling's or Feasterville's and it is less sweet.  To its credit, the Swiss Haus cookie's chocolate center is neither as sweet nor as hard as the first place bakeries' versions.  Swiss Haus's cookies are sufficiently hearty to transport with little breakage.    

Desserts by Design had a credible entry, which earned them third place.   The cookie had a delicate crumb but lacked any butter flavor.   Where these cookies failed was an unattractive milk-chocolate-looking center that was not a consistent color throughout and was irregularly shaped.   It also was far too sweet and hard.

Much to our chagrin, Leonardo's version ended up in fourth place.   While Leonardo's makes exquisite rustic breads and phenomenal cannoli, its butter cookies are just too hard and lack any butter flavor.

Though i have driven past many, many times... International Whiskey Day drew me into this great spot. I thank you for hosting our Yelp community for a wonderful event. I couldn't leave without trying a brew and some eats. 

First... i love the ambiance. This spot appears deceivingly small. We were seated upstairs, every floor is gorgeous and the staff are all amazing. Every person i encountered was friendly, accommodating, and made me feel like i was VIP. The venue for the event... impressed doesn't even begin to cover it.  Being with a whiskey fanatic, i am in love with the large party area and think i have found my reception venue. 

The food!!!! The servings are very generous. I had nachos and my friend has steak and chips... we split the macaroni. All from the appetizer menu. I was pleasantly surprised.... the nachos are not your typical texmex fare. The heat is minimal, but the flavor is on point!!!! My friends steak was PERFECT, flavorful, and the chops were obviously hand made. That macaroni tho!!!! I was hesitant about the smokes salmon as it can be over powering, but it was perfectly balanced. 

My only negatives... the complimentary corn bread fritters were liquid raw at the center, but the honey coating OMG!!!! The macaroni was a bit dry, i know with fried macaroni it tends to be dry. I would suggest a little more bechamel to counter. 

Overall.... from the libations, brews, to the food... a success that definitely has my attention.

ABSOLUTELY the perfect quick dining lunch spot. The other Sauce (SOTS) restaurants are also outstanding with flavorful and fresh food that is custom prepared very fast. Great for groups or just a solo lunch. Come hungry and ready for some superb flavors all around. Located in the Magnolia hotel. Great area, great food, fast and superb quick lunch spot. Probably great for dinner, but I work nearby so I go for lunch.

Ask about the options for the Calzones and sauces at the counter and get something unique. 

Who thought CALZONE's could be so fun! Reminds me of the Seinfeld episode.

I had always loved going to to this coffee shop, until today. I have never been treated with such disrespect by a person in the service industry. The very "hard" looking barista barked at me and my friend upon entering, rolled her eyes at us when we asked for a second to look over the menu, and harassed my friend due to her milk allergy. Then, after spreading negativity to the entire shop, she slammed my change down on the counter while very obviously pointing at the tip jar. I have never encountered a barista with as much agression before going to this coffee place. I will never step inside of this business again after her extremely rude, unwarranted, and unnecessary attitude.


On top of all of this, the drink she prepared tasted disguisting. She almost ruined my day with her negativity and agression

I have eaten at a lot of nice restaurants and several Mortons.  This was not a great experience at Mortons in downtown Nashville.  First, a bad attitude from the hostess and our waitress.  Sure, I just arrived for my meeting and wanted to eat without making a big dress up event.    Dinner,  Lobster bisque,  1 star.  very spicy, overwhelming and the lobster was grizzly,  I had to spit out a hunk of cartilage.  What the heck?  I had the beef steak tomatoes for salad. sort of ok, didn't impress me.  Bread, burnt onion?  my wife wouldn't eat it.  6 oz Fillet, cooked correctly at medium rare, but they must have basted it in an onion broth.  It tasted like I was eating it with french onion soup poured on it.  I eat Fillet because I like it.  I don't want it to taste like something else.    Molten chocolate for dessert. Tasted ok, but then the waitress didn't come back so I could take part of back to my room. After waiting 5 minutes or so, we left.   My recommendation is don't eat here.

Up until 2005, Koch's would have been an easy five stars.   But in 2005 Bob Koch, last of the Koches, passed away, and the business was sold to someone else.

The food is not the same; the cold cuts are poorer quality and the sandwiches are not assembled with the same care.  Can't anyone put together a sandwich?  Maybe it sounds silly to say it, but no.  The Koches really knew sandwiches.  They were sandwich masters.  And they really cared about what they did.  The new guy, not so much.

The experience isn't the same either, because the Koch brothers aren't there.  Last time I went in, while I was waiting, I had my laptop open.  "What are you doing?" asked the owner.  Just working, I said.  "Well, it looks kind of suspicious," he said.  Yeah, and screw you too.  

The shop still has the same sign, and it still says "Koch's", but it's a lie.  Koch's is closed.

Addendum 2011-09-20: I came home from work last week and my wife said "I'm never going to Koch's again".  She had taken my daughter I. and my daughter's friend Z. to Koch's for sandwiches.  The counter guy smiled at I. and said that he liked little girls.  Then he scowled at Z. and said "But I don't like little boys."  Z. was very hurt.  He is only five.

I really wanted to love Jillys, because what's not to love about cupcakes?  But sadly, I was very disappointed.

Firstly, they're EXPENSIVE.  I understand these are gianormous cupcakes, but I think $5+ is above market value for cupcakes in the Midwest.  Maybe I would be willing to pay that price if the cupcakes were "so good I'm going to float away bathed in sheer bliss" good.  Maybe.  I tried the peanut butter and chocolate cakecup and it was a moist and tasted ok, but to me, it was great or something that I would go out of my way to eat again.

What really left a bad taste in my mouth was the service.  It was very impersonal, rather unhelpful and borderline rude.

I know a lot of people love this place, but its just not for me.

Food is gross. Posted Reviews are from 3-4+ years ago. 

The owner seems to be very insecure about the food that is served at the restaurant. The professionalism of the owner is directly correlated to the quality of the food. 

My girlfriend and I came by and had a couple of plates. Notable ones were the mushrooms and the bruschetta. Mushrooms were slimy and gross, could very easily tell they were not fresh as noted. Bruschetta was surprisingly bad. It's Simply tomatoes on bread... Some of the bread came soft some came hard. 

Ordered a couple drinks, got a huckleberry cocktail and a beer. Beer, hard to mess up a bottle of beer. Cocktail was gross. Based off reviews and owners own words, it is the best selling cocktail. Best selling? To who the senior center? 

We had to send the food back because we simply couldn't eat it. I know it is a selfish thing to do, but I asked if it could be taken off the bill because it was inedible. Was told that there was nothing wrong with it and we were in the wrong. 

So just like many other patrons, paid the bill in full, and left to get a slice of pizza across the street. 

Have you guys seen Kitchen Nightmares where the owner refuses to hear out anyone because the food is the best thing ever? Exact thing that is happening here. Place is very clean, has a great location,  and seems like it's well run, but ego is the issue. 

Please just take the review of your customers as feedback and things you can improve on. Instead of insulting them in Yelp Replies, maybe try the suggestions provided. If not maybe the only customers that will dine here in the future will be the early bird 3pm dinner seniors. 

Take the tip I left you and get one of those huckleberry cocktails, and then try the food, you're going to need it.

I get asked a lot for restaurant recommendations.  After awhile, I feel like a broken record, always suggesting the same places.  I'm happy to say that after my fabulous meal at High Street on Market, I finally have a great place to recommend to my foodie family and friends.

So why 5 stars?  High Street on Market is just an overall great dining experience.  The restaurant itself is casual, yet classy.  It is a very comfortable space- like sitting in the dining room/living room of a friend who has really good taste.  I especially like the open kitchen-   it really makes you feel like you are at someone's house.

Service was impeccable, cocktails were amazing (I had some sort of spicy grapefruit margarita- whatever it was, it worked!) and the food... well, the food was absolutely delicious.  They offer a $50 tasting menu.  This would be an EXCELLENT place for a group dinner- it's definitely in the back of my mind for future group outing.  This visit, however, my husband and I decided to just order a few dishes, since we weren't too sure about the portion sizes.  We tried:

crispy broccoli- really simple dish of lightly fried broccoli with a spicy/tangy cabbage-like garnish.    

brussel sprouts-  I order brussel sprouts EVERYWHERE and I have to say this was one of my favorite versions I've ever had in Philly.  The secret was dollops of creamy goat cheese- wow!
 
charcoal grilled squid- I really liked this dish (although it could have been a tad bigger).  I didn't realize it was served with roasted cauliflower- that really made the dish spectacular.

angry crab spaghetti- this was probably my least favorite dish, but I still thought it was excellent.  A bit on the spicier side with lots of crab (some reviewers said they didn't get a ton-- I thought it was the perfect amount)

pumpkin tortellini- my favorite dish of the night... well maybe tied with those sprouts.  The homemade pasta melts in your mouth and the creamy pumpkin filling and sauce on top... amazing!

Overall, I thought the price was just right for the quality of food.  Prices are on the higher side but you get what you pay for here.  I really loved my meal here and will continue to recommend it to everyone I know who loves a great meal!

Was a fantastic meal. The flavor palette was similar to Scandinavian, but distinctly Jewish diaspora inspired. Very fresh ingredients, tasty, and thoughtfully designed. Nice plating, good sizes (I was actually quite full after the 3 courses). The menu is very accessible if you're not used to these flavors, and there's something for everyone. Though the menu has less for vegetarians, I'm sure they could pull something delicious together. I actually like Abe Fisher quite a bit better than Zahav.

Our waiter was also phenomenal. Took care of everyone's dietary restrictions, brought a free dessert specially prepared for our vegan friend, recommended a good wine, and super friendly.

Rolled into Vango after getting a tip from the bartendress at the other spot we were at a few doors down from Vango. Our bartendress, Lauren, I believe that's her name, directed us here so we could chill and listen to some music 

Hip Hop 'til you drop in the bar/lounge area where most of the younger locals were hanging. The upstairs rooftop bar, which I guess is called Skybar, offers nice scenic city views, with beds available to be reserved with the addition of bottle service. As an alternate, comfortable benches and chairs were also available. 

Chilled. Danced. Drank. Enjoyed the view, music and drinks. No complaints.

A local Philadelphian Yelper provided me with the 411 on all that's good in the downtown Philadelphia area and it's surroundings. One of her suggestions guided me here to Grubhouse. 

We arrived right before noon on a weekday and found parking to be a bit of a challenge, but eventually found a space directly across the street. We were the only patrons and within a short time three other patrons walked in. Grubhouse has the look of an old timey type diner with a flick of modern and an inviting environment. Even before being seated, I already had my mind set on ordering the Baconcakes after being enticed by all the Yelp reviews. 

Our waitress was pleasant and took our orders swiftly. A short time after our breakfast beverages were served our orders arrived. My thin, crisped edge, moist pancakes were redundant in bacon; griddled in bacon fat, with large pieces of bacon infused within the pancakes and then bacon strips served atop the Baconcakes and then lightly dusted with powdered sugar...wow!! And there you have Baconcakes, a bacon lovers bacon overload...absolutely mmm, mmm, good!

Aside from the wonderful Baconcakes Grubhouse's menu has other interesting options. For instance, the bacon wrapped jalapeño tater tots, Salted Caramel French Toast or Pancakes, Breakfast Egg Rolls, Grubhouse Big Philly Omelete, and some vegan items to name a few. I really wanted to take advantage and order the bacon wrapped tater tots which were free with the Yelp check-in, but that would've had me on the verge of bacon gluttony, so I forcefully refrained. 

I considered this my off the beaten path find as its not in the touristy downtown area of Philly. If in Philly and you have the time, I suggest you check out Grubhouse as its menu has a bit of a creative flare not similar to your regular diner fare. An additional bonus in taken this short excursion to this side of Philly is that there's a cheesesteak spot directly across the street, a perfect combination win. 

I have to end this review by saying, thank you Sari M. for your guidance!

I've stayed at the Valley Forge Casino Resort twice so far. Their rooms are large with a small living room area, bedroom, and a decent sized bathroom with a walk in shower. There is always a long line to check in, I've noticed that they usually have issues checking people in that book through Hotwire.

One thing that I love about this place is the parking | they have a huge space of free parking. No need to worry about lugging your baggage for too long because everything is a short distance. Being on the road a lot I've noticed that not many hotels offer free parking so this is definitely a perk!

I've had my run of bad luck in this Casino | It's better for me to hang out in my room instead of on the floor, but who knows maybe my luck will change one day! There is a huge selection of machines and tables with a decent sized bar in-between it all.

I came here with my daughter and a friend (my friend-not hers) on Sunday night and was thoroughly impressed! It's a relatively small restaurant, but we were there at 5:30, so it wasn't super packed. Side note: Happy Hour is 'til 6 Thursday-Sunday! Score! 

Our server was friendly and especially kind to my 15 month-old, who wasn't exactly on her best restaurant behavior. She asked what my daughter's name was and spent some time chatting with her each time she came to the table.  That is something I really appreciate, because a lot of times when we go out to eat, servers just kind of ignore her (I mean I know she's a baby-but hello! she's a person too).  But I digress, I got two rolls (Cortaro & Tootsie) both were delicious and completely satisfied my sushi craving! We will definitely be coming back soon for great sushi and superior service!

Love this sushi spot, I always forget about it!! I'm not sure how I forget because the food is really good! For an appetizer, I got the pan fried dumplings which were pretty good and flavorful . For dinner I got the dragon roll and the upside down roll which was still sizzling (in a good way) when it came out . It was a special and when the waitress described it I knew I had to get it! The waitress was so sweet, everything came out in a timely manner. There didn't seem to be too much of a crowd when I went,  but as I was there business started to pick up. Lots of people seemed to be doing take out. I felt comfortable being there, Covid restrictions were being followed. I cannot wait to go back and have their hibachi !

We had booked reservations for a Saturday for my husband's 40th birthday party. We all dressed up in wigs and glitter. We got put in the very back, dark room at a awkwardly high table with chairs with no backs. It took a half an hour to get our drink order in. The waitress forgot two of our drinks. There were colored lights and a wayyy better show in the main room it looked like, we were just in the back and got the very end of every little walk by of Brooklyn Heights. The service wasn't good. A few people in our party didn't even have forks or knives. Never saw our waitress to ask for more utensils. The frier oil really needs to be changed. That fried chicken our party had was over cooked and just not good. The waitress didn't even know what was in any of the drinks, so when asked, no one knew. 

Suggestions: knock down all of the walls in there. One big room. Build a stage. Get better food. Get better waitresses. More drag queens. Shouldn't be called a drag brunch with only one drag queen with over 100 people in there.

We poured in by the dozen reconfiguring the tables of half the bar so we could all chomp with each other while the staff looked on in amusement. They could handle us, sweet. I immediately felt at home. Hip and funky but understated, I came to learn from my local hosts that it provided refuge of cool in the Olde City landscape of trendy and wannabe upscale. 

Still new to historical architecture in the public domain, I was impressed with the ionic columns at the entrance, and the expansive high ceilings which allowed our sizable crowd to be boisterous without drowning each other out. This could have happened very easily with their $3 Yuenlings for those who aim to get as tipsy for as little as possible, as well as tempting brews for the aficionados. I was pleased to see a white ale Hitachino (go owls!) and nursed it accordingly.

Then marched the eats: piled high nachos, burgers (a little too overdone), veggie burgers (a wee bit too salty), paired with thick wedge, yummy fries. By the end of the meal we were all smiling and satiated. Mission accomplished!

Took both of our daughters here for their birthday. This was a family trip to Clearwater and a celebration of birthdays. Everything that we tried was excellent. A little pricey but well worth it. Do not eat too much that you cannot try any of the desserts.

Hands-down probably one of the best waffles I have ever tasted in my life. I cannot describe it it's almost eating a piece of cake that has been perfectly cooked and crunchy. The chicken was amazing. Be prepared to Want to order everything on the menu. We ordered so much stuff we could barely eat everything.
It was ok, I didn't think the gumbo was that good at all. I thought the house salad was plain. This to me would be like bar food. Service was a little slow.

The food was OK. We came in the evening and they really only had three servers working in the entire restaurant. We sat outside so it was already kind of hot, and we were exhausted. It took us over an hour to get our food. When it came it wasn't the best.  If I return back to Clearwater this place I would not eat out again.

I'm not sure how many fine-dining establishments are in New Orleans, but Restaurant R'Evolution is definitely one of them. I came here on Halloween night and it was quite a sight to see everyone in costumes eating at a multi-course meal. 

The restaurant is very spacious with several rooms spread out, there is also a door leading outside to this little garden walkway (I couldn't really explore because it was pouring outside). 
The ambience was romantic; quiet and clean. 

My favorite dish was the snapping turtle and deviled quail egg soup. The quail eggs was a flavorful twist on the classic deviled eggs and enhanced the flavor of the soup. I'm not a native of "N'awlins" but I felt that this creole snapping turtle soup had the essence of the city with the exotic meat and spiced broth. Pungent but not overwhelming. Also, snapping turtle just tastes like ground beef.  

The tuna crudo had bits of caviar on the tuna which didn't really add much to the overall flavor but was a nice touch. The pickled vegetables on the side must've been for decorative purposes only because the tartness of the pickled dishes didn't pair well with the fishy, saltiness of the caviar and tuna. A nice dish, but I wouldn't order it again. 

I also enjoyed the Creole Bouillabaisse but the portion was a bit small. Again, the broth was spiced but not overwhelming. 

The dinner ended on a playful note with a complimentary petite fours box.


Overall, I really enjoyed Restaurant R'evolution and would definitely come again. This was my favorite restaurant that I had visited during my weekend in NOLA.

Dear Old town, the name suits you well, you're old and washed up. 
I think rating you one star gives you too much credit. 

The moment I sat down a was approached by (which I didn't know at the time) was the owner - she almost forced me to buy a coffee and when I said I just wanted a water to start she scolded me and walked away - she came back and told me in disgust that I really should buy a coffee - as I started to explain that I was waiting for friends to arrive she walked away.

lame place.

There's an abundance of Thai food in Philadelphia, especially in West Philly where I live, so I came to JJ Thai with somewhat low expectations. I came in just before 6 PM on a Saturday night and almost every table was already full - except one table for 2 (yes!) I was greeted upon walking in and was asked if I had made a reservation - which neither I nor my friend had (oops, n00b move especially on a Saturday night). I kept eyeing the table for 2 while waiting for my friend and luckily the lady saved the table for us because when he walked in 10 minutes after me (they didn't know we were together) they told him it was a 30 minute wait! So whew. 

Food:
Trio Appetizer ($15) - a little overpriced imo but it was probably because of the filet mignon. My friend had both while I had both of the shrimp and crab rolls while we both split the duck salad (which was my favorite of the three). A little on the salty side but the crispy wonton bowl it came in and the veggies balanced it out really well. Shrimp and crab roll was pretty bland but they gave a really fragrant mint chutney that my friend l o v e d. He ate it plain and definitely scraped that plate clean haha.
Chicken Pad See Ew ($13) - first thing I noticed was that the portion size was large! I eat Pattaya's chicken pad see ew all the time so when compared to that, this chicken pad see ew was comparable. I wouldn't say it's anything special per se, but they didn't mess it up which was good! 
Chicken Pad Thai ($13) - I tried a little of the chicken pad Thai and it seemed pretty average to me. Again, good portion size and standard pad Thai.

Both my friend and I had heard good things about this restaurant and agreed that we should try our standard go-to Thai dishes before trying other stuff on their menu. I'll definitely be back, as I'm quite interested in their fusion dishes like lamb chops and others... stay tuned for an update!

The only thing this place has going for it, is the fact that they're on the water. And boy are they holding onto that tight. The food is not good it's cheaply prepared and not good quality! Extremely overpriced. 
I expected to pay for the atmosphere but I also expected to get good seafood. 
We had the Cuban, the Grouper sandwich, and the Getaway. The server asked us what kind of sides we wanted without mentioning they were not included with our sandwiches. I felt pretty dumb when the check came. 
There's so many better places in St.Pete and Tampa! Save your money and time and go somewhere else!!

Bobby's is simply excellent. On summer evenings and nights you can expect long lines out front but don't worry, they're great at forming multiple lines and working customers through quickly. Bobby's has been a local staple to the maryville, edwardsville, Collinsville area for many years and they've continued to improve. On any given night you can find "Bobby" himself and his wife both in store, working right along all the other workers to turn out delicious frozen custard. Last time I was there (I grew up just down the street) Bobby was walking through the parking lot scraping gum up to keep everything tidy and clean. 

Their bright and colorful lights are easy to spot from a mile away although you'll have to be ready to fight the bugs at the ordering window because everything is lit up so brightly. This place does close down around Halloween and usually reopens the first or second weekend of March. 

Also if any of their specials sound remotely good to you, GO FOR IT! They have excellent feature flavors and concretes and help support another local business (bakery) for all of their key lime pies, peach cobblers, brownies, and other baked goodies they add to their creamy custard. 

I would absolutely recommend the PEANUT BUTTER BLAST. It's one of my favorites with, half vanilla&half chocolate custard- Reece's peanut butter & Reece's pieces mixed in.

Finch & Fork is located inside the Canary Hotel, the restaurant is quite spacious and in the sedate downtown area nearby Paseo Nuevo, so you are likely to have no issues securing a table last minute. 

Finch & Fork is one of the long-standing establishments in the Santa Barbara dining scene. Creative menu designed by Executive Chef James Siao, it has consistently been in the top SB restaurants to visit when you are in the area.

I took my boyfriend here for his Birthday brunch since it always had an unerring way of surprising us with it's delicious dishes, their beautiful intimate-lit dining room was another plus to our experience.

THE STAFF-

Our server Ling-Ling was amazing in terms of comfort, wit, and alertness for our stay. Each order came out great and the execution of plating was exemplary. There is an extensive Italian-centric wine selection as well as some solid cocktail offerings here, although, I had blindly asked her for a good Pinot, she hand picked the G1s Alpha Omega II ($18.00), which was quite bland and a little leddy. She surely made up with her cunning taste in cocktails!


THE FOOD-

I had ordered their Deviled Eggs ($8.00 for four) to start with, which consisted of smoked trout, olive relish, and pickled shallots that gave a bit of a crunchiness that was very delightful to the soft eggs which I was marveled with. We had no problem finishing the bite sized starters in a matter of seconds.

Although their Market Fish Tacos ($12.00) weren't on their brunch menu, we just had to get our hands on them. The tacos had a combination of Jicama & avocado salsa on top which created a unique flavor and texture mixed in with the pickled cabbage.

My boyfriend ordered their F&F Burger, cooked medium ($18.00), with a side of their Mac & Cheese ($11.00) for a mighty meal to conquest. The baked mac & cheese which had aged cheddar and bacon was a little bland, but had a nice top layer of bread crumb crust. For the burger, the beef was more or less perfectly cooked, and the combination of aged cheddar, b & b pickles, and Bacon fig jam provided plenty of flavor munitions that made the burger so rich and complex. And, while I'm not ready to call Finch & Fork's burger the best in the city, it was definitely one of the better ones I've had the chance to taste recently.

For my main dish I ordered their Roasted Pork Belly Benedict ($17.00), which consisted of poached eggs, caramelized onions, English muffin, chipotle hollandaise, and their home fries. After cutting the middle of the very well executed poached egg, and watching the yolk just lather on top of the English muffin and caramelized onions - it was as if the Gods had spoken, just absolutely beautiful! 
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

With unique craft cocktails, a huge wine list, delectable food, and a beautiful back drop for it all, it's no surprise that Finch & Fork is a local fan favorite. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone who hasn't yet had the chance to dine here. A definite staple in Santa Barbara!

The Bacara is one of the best Resorts I've stayed at in California in terms of location and spectacular service. A must if you are in need of a small vacation and want to relax.

My boyfriend booked two nights at this hotel during 'Old Spanish Days' weekend to get away from all the confetti mess; and, it was also a late birthday gift for me.  

We arrived at the hotel with the very friendly staff and valet greeting us, but seeing how there is no underground parking, the valet staff parked our car out in the sun during our stay, we figured next time we come here, we are taking an Uber since we are SB locals, that way we don't ruin our car or pay a hefty parking fee. 

As we entered the beautiful lobby, we were greeted with complimentary champagne flutes and wonderful service from the staff. Although we were a few hours early before check-in, the staff helped us with a walk-around of the property and showed us the way to the pool while we waited (which was perfect since we had our bathing suits on under our clothes.).

We booked a gorgeous Ocean View Suite in building 10 (probably the best building there is at the resort), which had a view of the ocean and sweeping views of mountains. The room was set at a very accommodating temperature on arrival and we were surprised to receive a complimentary wine bottle of Pinot Noir. Our suite had beautiful his & her sinks, a walk-in rain shower, and a bath tub (I wish it had jets though) that separated the bathroom from the bedroom, and our bags were placed nicely near the closets by the wonderful staff.

The Bacara has two pools, and one Adults only pool (next to the fitness center) which I sadly did not get to take advantage of at the time. The view from the pool that everyone was in was spectacular, but, one thing I did not care for was that there is a sandy area for the kids to play in near the pool, and a bunch of the kids were rolling in the sand and racing to jump into the pool, getting the floors all sandy, and not to mention - some kid shat in the pool, it was closed for a night and I don't think they drained it lol. 

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

In short, I would definitely recommend staying here (and definitely ask if you could get a suite in building 10!). The pool was wonderful, just don't come on a Sunday - It's kid city!

This is my new favorite spot for heavenly divine Spanish styled tapas and drinks!

My boyfriend and I love coming here for a little wind down and dine after work. We love sitting next to each other instead of across from one another so we always get a nice seat at either the chef's table, the gorgeous heated outside patio area with a cozy fireplace, or the very shabby-chic corner with the fur seats!

STAFF -

The staff is usually very astute and welcoming whenever I'm here.

Although on our recent visit, our waitress was not too knowledgeable on the wine selection, giving her young appearance I would suspect her to be of inexperience to it, she was very sweet and even ran out to us after we paid our bill with the take-out bag that we forgot at our table. She did fall a little short when being needed but she was quite helpful.

FOOD -

We usually order from their Pintxos menu as appetizers. I would highly recommend the Brusselas and the Manchegos!

For Tapas we really enjoyed their Pulpo which is a Spanish octopus and potatos underneath, or their Cerdo which is a delicious pork belly with butternut squash and apple churney.

For Paella I love eating seafood, but I do love my rabbits, we ordered their Valenciana which consisted of chicken, rabbit, blue lake and gigante beans, saffron, and tomatos.

I would definitely recommend coming back here again! Very good food and ambiance.

How many wine bars are in Santa Barbara? I honestly don't know and wouldn't even take a plunge to guess. But Corks n' Crowns is one of the best tasting rooms I've been to in terms of service, comfort, and ambiance for Downtown Santa Barbara.

They have an amazing check-in offer of a "1 free Bonus Pour with check-in" that I always take advantage of each time I visit for a drink.

They have many great local wine selections that are very limited which makes it an exceptionally unique place to purchase wines. When I go here I usually just order a bottle to go and wine glass of my favorite 'Gold Moon sparkling Muscat' or if I'm with friends I get their Diamond or Platinum flites which never disappoint. 

This place has a nice little porch outside where you can proudly take your drinks out to and enjoy the fresh air and people watch, or you can enjoy your drinks inside; although, it can get quite busy on the weekends, when there's not a lot of people there it's very comfortable to sit inside on their comfy chairs, I always choose the big blue chair!

I would definitely recommend this wine tasting room for the locals or anyone visiting Santa Barbara for the first time!

**Parking was a bit hard to find; and at the time, there were three parking spots open in front of the restaurant but only for valet to the jewelry store next door which I thought was very silly**

No restaurant greatly represents the quintessential Montecito vibe better than Tre Lune, an authentic Italian restaurant led by chef Soemi Caramel.

As my boyfriend and I entered Tre Lune, we were immediately looked over by a room filled with pretentious patrons' prying eyes, but was warmly welcomed by an astute hostess that accommodated us to an already reserved table that seats four which was greatly appreciated.

THE STAFF-

As we sat down, to my understanding was our waiter, trying to sell us only the most expensive dishes to be their "most recommended dishes". $95 for a truffled pasta? Give me a break. 

When it came to us asking our waiter what wine bottle he'd recommend for the meal, he frantically flipped through the pages and pointed straight to the $400 and $600 wine bottles. We ordered a very simple pinot noir which didn't exceed more than $70 and my boyfriend said it tasted like $5 Trader Joe's wine Lol go figure.

THE FOOD-

We ordered their Vellutata di broccoli ($9),  which is essentially broccoli soup in vegetable broth as an appetizer for myself; it was topped with freshly crushed pepper but it still lacked basic flavor. It seemed to be a very underwhelming dish to start with.

My boyfriend had ordered the Fettucine Mare e Monte ($25.50), which was fettucine drenched in delicious safron-tomato sauce, and served with fresh lobster meat and Porcini mushrooms. 

I went and ordered their Pollo Saltimbocca ($27.50), which was very delectable chicken breast sauteed with mouthwatering prosciutto, melted Fontina cheese, sage, and Marsala wine. 

The pinot noir we ordered paired very well with my boyfriend's pasta which was very enjoyable and surprisingly the softest pasta I've ever tried.

We ended our meal with a few glasses of their tastiest sherry and a caffe desert.
_______________________________________

Tre Lune is sophisticated yet approachable, and I can't wait to try other dishes at this restaurant on my next visit.

Three Michelin star Chef Vincent Lesage, of Angel Oak created a unique menu, combining classic American hearty meals with a sense of approach. Chef Lesage emphasized when opening Angel Oak that he wanted to focus more on the quality of his food rather than to experiment with ingredients and new techniques.

***Stop reading while you're ahead and reserve a table now, you won't regret it!***

My boyfriend took me to Angel Oak for a birthday dinner, and I must say, it was magnificent. From the complimentary Birthday champagne flute, amazing craft cocktails, cozy yet minimalist dining area, and also the gorgeous view! What could make or break the evening all boils down to the meal, which is phenomenal. 

THE FOOD-

I started the meal with French Onion Soup ($17) and Braised Octopus ($21). Both dishes were absolutely superb, with soft texture of bread from the soup, it was as if one of my most memorable childhood dishes were brought back to life! The tender octopus had a somewhat balanced flavor but the octopus itself didn't feel cooked thoroughly to give an excellence level of structure.

My boyfriend ordered their Pan Seared Foie Gras ($25), and to my liking, it was a hit; I was a huge fan of the Foie Gras. 

For my main course I ordered the Abalone from our neighbor ($39) which had house made cappellini pasta, which was perfectly cooked Al dente, and the lemon beurre blanc on top pulled in all the flavors.

My boyfriend ordered the Alaskan Halibut ($34) for his main course, and he thoroughly enjoyed it. The Halibut was glistening and cooked to perfection, the fireball salami created intense flavor with the fish and also added a nice kick which is exactly what he wanted.

We ordered a lot of sides, the Angel Oak tator tots ($12), Brussels ($11), and  Gnocchi ($12). Although I'm not a huge fan of gnocchi in general, this gnocchi dish was really delicious, with excellent texture (not overly soft). I absolutely loved the side of Brussels, it had a very pleasant sauce that they marinated them in and it was very palatable to my tastes.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

I was genuinely impressed with the food that was gliding out of the kitchen that night, one course after the next. Superb meal, amazing wait staff. I couldn't have asked for a better birthday!

**After having the most terrible first time dining experience here I really wanted to give Stella Mares a second chance**

I took my boyfriend to Stella Mares one sunny afternoon; and although the restaurant wasn't filled with guests, it still had a cozy and lively ambiance to it. 

We sat in the glass room dining area which had a weirdly placed bar and a very eclectic mix of random outdoor furniture like what seemed to be a dirty old beat-up boxy leather couch in front of a dusty fireplace with random trinkets of "bonjour" and "benoit" signs around.

As we were served complimentary bread and butter, our silverware was in a dreadful state. I asked our waiter for new plates and his excuse on the misfortune was that the roof of that particular dining room "rarely gets sweeped, therefore you have bugs falling off and onto the plates". Pretty icky if you ask me!

THE FOOD-

We decided to quickly order, and as we've been here before we were quite familiar with the menu. 

My boyfriend decided on getting the Los Patos burger ($15.75) which is their one of a kind ground Duck burger that had goat cheese and black cherry gastrique. It's a must if you're a burger lover! He had the choice on how it was cooked and chose medium rare.

I ordered their Truite Rouge Almandine ($27.75), which is essentially a very crispy ruby red trout that had a very tasteful sweet potato purée and sauteed haticots verts, with charred cauliflowers.

I absolutely love duck dishes, especially if it's cooked at a level where it's juicy and tender, but after taking the first bite of my boyfriend's duck burger I was wondering whether the kitchen mistakenly brought a well-done burger because the texture of it was a bit underwhelmingly tough that I had fixated more on my Trout that was accompanied by it's seasonal vegetables. 
____________________________________

If you're looking for a French bistro to try authentic French cuisine in Santa Barbara, Stella Mares is a very viable option!

Renaud's is one of the greats that Santa Barbara has to offer for a grand breakfast/brunch/ or even coffee on the go. I've always enjoyed coming in as they open to get my hands on their freshly made macarons and cakes.

Starting in 2008, Co-founder and Executive Pastry Chef, Renaud Gonthier, has brought exceptional French flair to Santa Barbara's desire for (and previous lack of) a quality French pastry and croissant venue.

Although this Renaud's is right next to a bar where a lot of the shadier local riff raff type of people like to hang, a lot of them come out for a few smokes too which was a bit off putting (I feel like the location here in general is a bit sketchy, there are bums lurking near cars with open door windows and drunks that don't know when enough is enough as they go gallivanting across the streets.) The patio is just so picturesque with the striped parisian sunbrellas and beautiful iron dining sets, how could you not?

THE FOOD-

I ordered their Crooque Madame ($12.50) which was delightful, the eggs were creamy and bread at a certain crisp I dreadfully needed that wakening day. The croque madame also comes with a side salad which never disappoints. I love when salad is a bit on the softer side, especially when lathered in dressing - absolute perfection! The cafe latte that they serve here is one of the best in Santa Barbara, they make it stronger than most cafes in Santa Barbara.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------

This location is more for the older locals, parking is very easy to find. SB has a Renaud's on lower state street too, but far smaller, and doesn't quite have the charm as this one. I would recommend Renaud's to every local in Santa Barbara.

Empty Bowl Gourmet Noodle is a Santa Barbara staple, located in the Public Market, even after all of the switch outs of the many little eateries in the Public Market, Empty Bowl has stood on top. 

Owners and Chefs Nui Pannak, Jerry Lee, and Emre Balli infused street foods in their own way from Thailand and Taiwan all the way to Santa Barbara, changing the way people see the culinary status of SB. Interesting enough, Co-owners Jerry and Emre are Certified sommeliers. They offer an exclusive wine pairing with their handmade dumplings which are delightful.

THE FOOD-

Every time I come here, I always start off with their Spring Rolls ($9.95), the peanut sauce that is presented with the rolls is excellent and make it such a good starter.

As far as their ramen goes, I usually order their Bangkok Street Noodle ($14.95), or their Long Tail Boat Noodle ($14.95)

For pastas, I like to order their Tom Yum Noodles ($13.95), and their Hangover Noodles ($13.95).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is a go-to spot for anyone that loves ramen and noodles. I would definitely recommend Empty Bowl to everyone. Five stars all the way.

Shalhoob meats owner, Jeff Shalhoob created The Funk Zone Patio, one of the few successful family owned businesses in Santa Barbara, serving top notch burgers all locally sourced at unbeatable costs. 

Although they are a bit off the beaten path (at the start of gray street), The Patio is a very well known spot for every burger lover and enthusiast in Santa Barbara. I always try to share SB with my out-of-town friends, and this place is at the top of the list.

The Funk Zone Patio is literally in my backyard, I wake up every morning to the smell of their fresh bacon tempting me to be "bad" for the day.

The Patio is one of the staples that I always treat my friends to, after a long haul from the lovely wine trail in the Funk Zone.

THE FOOD-

My go-to burgers are the Bacon Jam Burger ($12), Santa Barbara styled Burger (with added bacon and avocado $16), and their Fried chicken sandwich ($12)

They have a lovely beer and wine list, I usually order their local Syrah ($10) or IPA's that are on tap.

-----------------------------------------------

The Patio is where it's all at if you're into supporting seriously great local businesses with amazing service and burgers!

The aura of great authenticity that Ichiban surpasses is beyond me. From the darling Japanese styled seating area, to the swords decorating the entryway, Ichiban is the most authentic Japanese dining experience I've had in Santa Barbara.

THE STAFF- 

The first few times I visited here I would use either an Axxess deal or a Groupon and the way the waitress would calculate the receipt would always be off by a few $$. I do think businesses should honor their deals, and it's a shame on their part because it would have been five stars.

Other than receipt miscalculations for deals, their staff are very quick and insightful, I'm never having to track down a waiter or if I'm at the Sushi bar, I never feel like I'm pressed for time.

THE FOOD- 

Lately I've been begining my sushi endeavours with fresh-water eel ($8.00) sashimi or nigiri, and it always falls palatable to the start of my meal.

I really enjoy their Mesa roll ($12.95), 007 roll ($13.95), and their mouthwatering Chef Special roll ($18.75). All of them come with a lot of spicy mayo so there's really no need to ask for a side of it. 

---------------------------------------------------

Ichiban is one of the best Japanese restaurants in SB, in terms of food quality, and real Japanese authenticity. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone!

** Very long overdue review **

One of the saddest closings of a Santa Barbara restaurant throughout my culinary journey was Julienne. With the classiest establishment representing the combination of sophisticated French dishes with a twist of old school Americano. 

Late Owner/chef Justin West created an amazing menu, although I felt as if it didn't really have a distinct identity to it, it had a lot of fan favorites with a heavy focus on meat.
