My boyfriend pointed me to this establishment when I first came to Santa Barbara saying it's very "date-worthy", "boundary-pushing haute cuisine", and also was one of his favorite restaurants for fine dining. I wanted to see if all the hype surrounding this place was worth it. I'm pleased to say Julienne had the BEST wine pairings with their prix fixe menu.

THE STAFF- 

To my surprise, Chef Justin was in the restaurant working the kitchen; not sure if he was expediting or what, but he came to our table after our meal and showed his gratitude for us coming in that night. It truly made that our stay feel special.

THE FOOD-

My boyfriend and I both ordered their five course tasting with wine pairing ($210 for both).

For starters we received a delicious Wild baby Arugula salad ($12) that was tousled in stone fruit with toasted oats, house ricotta, and onions with lemon oil. I was most impressed with how the lemon oil added a tart flavor to the stone fruit. 

After the starters, we received a delicious duck dish ($25 on menu) that had boneless confit, lentil risotto, bok choy, and plum sauce that was drizzled on the side. Although duck is definitely an acquired taste to most, the duck that we received was glistening and perfectly cooked, I'm sure anyone new to duck would fall in love!

We had the Roasted Ocean Trout ($26 on menu) which consisted mostly of lentils, artichoke, garlic, and dashi broth. The dashi broth and artichoke gave a very rich and aromatic flavor that was very palatable to my tastes.

We received the Fettuccine ($24 on menu), which consisted of tomatoes, fresh pork sausage, basil and Parmesan cheese. It must have been in season for the tomatoes because they were juicy and delicious. I was extremely impressed with the refined flavor of the dish which was very savory and didn't come out too heavy as one would normally expect from the typical fine dining French restaurant.

The Bone Marrow (not on menu) was my boyfriend's favorite part of the meal. I'm not even a huge fan of Bone Marrow, but the one I had at Julienne just had immaculate texture that gave me joy in every bite, it was absolutely phenomenal.

To finish off our meal, my boyfriend and I chose separate dishes. I had the Foie Gras & Donuts ($18 on menu) which had Torchon of foie, sourdough donuts, and strawberry balsamic preserves. My boyfriend had their sherbet I believe, and I know he liked it.

--------------------------------------------------------------

I haven't the clue to how much time and energy chef Justin put into his restaurant, but I wish the magic that I experienced at Julienne comes back to Santa Barbara soon!

I took my boyfriend to Yoichi's on a Sunday which to my surprise was the same day where Chef Yoichi was celebrating his Birthday; he and his family were having dinner here which was refreshing since he prides his restaurant so much he'd eat there too!

 I reserved for a booth at 8:30 for two and the sweet lady that served us knew I was Marina who had requested a table.

In terms of location, Yoichi's is off the beaten path, two and a half blocks from state street. You would need to look up the address to find it, otherwise the common tourist wouldn't be familiar about the location. Also, parking is side street and rarely is there parking on the same block (we had to walk a full block to get there!).

SERVICE -

Service was amazing in terms of Santa Barbara, the best I've had. As we entered the quaint little restaurant with lights flowing down the building, everyone bowed at us and was very kind. Our server was very nice and attentive, she kept checking on us regularly.  She was quite knowledgeable about every dish on the menu, I had felt like I was quizzing her as I asked about the different assortments of the foods and I think she was very good. 

FOOD -

My boyfriend and I have similar tastes but wanted to try other dishes to have more of a variety when we dined so we both ordered the Kaiseki 7 course meal. The restaurant has a nice selection of sake as well as wine. I ordered a bottle of their Gasanryu Hazuki Sake (which was very smooth and had a soft texture with a bold and fruity flavor as if it were freshly squeezed), and it surprisingly worked very well with the Kaiseki courses. 

We had the following: Zensai's (assorted appetizers) of Mozuku seaweed and jelly fish with shiso sauce, the simmered abalone, the deep fried tofu and vegetable balls siimmered in bonito broth, the shansho pepper sauce glazed grilled on wagyu beef, and the braised pork belly with moromi miso. 

For the Owan (second course/soup) we tried both soups of clear soup with sea eel, and egg cake; and, my boyfriend had the clear soup with whole steamed tomato.

For our Yakimono (grilled dish) we had the choice of the grilled, miso marinated black cod and the sweet soy sauce marinated grilled duck breast.

For our Mushimono (steamed & simmered dish) I ordered their Japanese rock fish simmered in sweet broth and my boyfriend's choice was of the gorgeous Arima Sansho pepper marinated sweet fish with Its roe inside.

And lastly for the Kanmi, or dessert we both ordered their sweet Green tea ice cream with a wedge of dried but tasty persimmons, I had the chance to eat both of them!

My boyfriend's favorite was the pork belly, because of the consistency and rich flavor. His clam soup was delectable too and also the Cod, he says he could have eaten that all day long! My boyfriend ordered their wagyu for his main course, and while his wagyu was nicely cooked, I felt the seasoning was somewhat uneven.

My favorite was the sweet soy sauce marinated grilled duck breast because the sweet soy sauce was rich and yet rustic without being overwhelming to my palate. While the duck breast was just a little bit on the salty side, I did really like the texture of the meat, which worked very well with the soy sauce and garnish on top. 

I would definitely recommend coming here again. I think that Yoichi's is the best Japanese restaurant in Santa Barbara if you're looking for legitimate sushi food that wouldn't be too westernized like what is usually seen on state street. Yoichi's is the crème de la crop of what Santa Barbara has to offer in terms of an authentic Japanese meal.

The dining experience was fair enough in this winery-esque Parisian-Olive Garden styled Restaurant, the food on the other hand was a bit negligent. 

The Oyster Rockefellers were pretty much the only dish I enjoyed even though it was played with multitudinous butters and cheeses.

My salad had mixed tastes, from bitter mixed greens to almost too sweetened of a Crouton wrap around.  Wasn't pleasant.

My Salmon with Mango was unsatisfactory and had no sensation of flavor.  I mean, I get what they were doing but, it was poorly executed on that note;  I wouldn't recommend the Salmon!  

At the end of the dinner we were greeted by an upstanding man who asked if we enjoyed the meal, I replied with a "No,  I've tasted better Salmon at a Costco free sample stand".  He looked away and put his hands on his hips and said "well if you'd like, I can put on my funny chef hat and go do it myself". Not cute, just a bit unprofessional. 

And don't get me started on the bathrooms! Ick!

I think I'd give it another chance, maybe it was a bad night?

First time there,  I ordered a portabella mushroom burger, the wife ordered a classic medium.  We ordered fried pickles for an appetizer.  The pickles, not sure if that was how they were supposed to be, but not quite right (breading falling off / nuclear hot) but they were ok,  The portabella mushroom burger arrived at about room temperature, it was not foul but it really was not special.  The fries were not cold, but not warm.  The last edible temperature you would touch them.  My wife's burger was not how she ordered it / it was well done, and just warmish when it arrived.  Fries were also not cold but not right.

At the end of the meal, it was expensive, not very good.  Not something I would ever go back for.  I'll point out at this point both of us thought they might just have had a bad day.  We left disappointed but not angry.

4 hours later, my stomach is pretty much in a knot, possibly from them not cooking the portabella enough / prepping it in a meat area, perhaps not.  It could just be something I picked up, but that burger now haunts me.  Signed up for Yelp just for this.  My wife mentioned that a burp 4 hours later also seemed tastier than her Classic.

So yeah, take a review from a vegetarian and a carnivore, neither fare there was worth repeating.  It's not the worst place I've ever been, but on a 1-5 scale where 2 is "meh".  I'd just say buyer beware, reading the reviews I'd 1) make them make your burger like you order it, 2) not accept not-warm food.

The waitstaff was pretty friendly,  The place was clean. If the food was better I would go back, but it wasn't.

This was a tough establishment for me to review.  Here's why...

This restaurant chose to meld bubble tea counter service, with sit down restaurant / waiter service.  What you get is confusing and extremely inconsistent service.   If you have somewhere to be, and time is of the essence, DO NOT come here!  Our experience was bitter-sweet in many ways; I'll break it down so you can judge each category for yourself (ranked from 1-10, 10 being the best)...

Bubble tea drinks:  9+ Topnotch!  Boba was sweet / flavorful (and cooked to perfection), and teas were prepared expertly with unique / pure flavors.

Food:  9+ Wonderful ramen dishes - super soft pork belly and beef, with a soft boiled egg and just the right saltiness; you can actually drink the broth without sodium overload!  One of the best ramen bowls I've eaten.  They also have rice bowls if you want your sushi fix!

Venue / decor:  10 - WOW, they found one heck of an interior designer with fashion sense; the environment is playful, fresh, and comforting, with spring colors, tables and chairs that match the wall decor, a jaw-dropping butterfly mural, soothing contemporary music humming in the background, and lots (and LOTS) of stuffed pigs for a cuteness factor.  

Now, here's the SAD SAD news...

Service:  2 - yes, it was that bad, unfortunately.  It was so sad to see this establishment suffering from untrained and inadequate service.  

My wife and I entered and waited...and waited...to be seated.  Finally, I asked the person at the counter if we should just find a table and sit.  With a host desk set up at the entrance, you would expect someone to seat you - my suggestion is to have a sign that directs people to either seat themselves, or wait for a hostess to seat you.

Once seated, the waiter did take our orders quickly - yay!  However, our drinks didn't arrive until we were halfway through eating our ramen, and we even reminded them twice - first time, we got the response, "Oh...it's coming, but there's a line of orders ahead of you."  Come to find out that our drink was sitting on a counter, and never got delivered.  Once they did give us the drinks, we discovered there was no boba in our drinks.

As a side note, a couple next to us sat for 30 min, until a waiter approached them, and asked if they ordered food; they said yes and repeated the order again.  The waiter then showed their order slip to the person behind the counter, and the counter personnel hurriedly walked into the kitchen to START their order!

After we were finished eating, we asked for the bill - their response: "Oh...you need to go to the counter to pay for your order."  Again, goes back to the confusing meld between bubble tea counter service and restaurant service.  So, we happily went to the counter only to find 5 people in line ordering their bubble tea drinks.  So, we had to wait in line just to pay for our dinner.  Our suggestion would be for the waiter to enter the order into the register, and deliver it to the table...like a restaurant should.  If we sit down to be served, we shouldn't have to get in the same line as bubble tea counter customers just to pay our bill.

There's potential for GREATNESS in this establishment...IF they fix their service flaws, and they are, unfortunately, BIG flaws.  Please train your staff to focus on customer service and consistent / timely delivery of drinks / dishes.  Go the extra mile and actually deliver the bill to tables!  I will be back again in hopes that their service improves.  Once it does, I would happily change this rating to 4-5 stars      

Good luck, Hi Tea - we're rooting for you!

Gave this place two chances, and after numerous problems, WOB is dead to me.

First visit: Friday lunchtime, pretty busy.  Was in a party of three, got a table, got served beers and put in our food order.  When the food came to the table, I was informed that what I'd ordered was 86'ed.  Really??  They didn't know that until my companions got their food?  Our server was struggling and apparently hadn't thought ahead to bring me a menu so I could make another selection.  Another delay.  Ordered and got my food by the time my companions were more than 1/2 way thru their meals.

Ordered a second beer from the menu and the server returned to inform me that what I'd ordered was not available.

By the time we got our check, we discovered that we had been charged for a $10.50 beer that we had not even ordered!

Second visit:  Thursday lunchtime, far enough thru the lunch rush that they weren't very busy at all.  Sat at the bar for a full 15min without anybody taking my order or offering me a food menu.  Got up and left without ever being acknowledged by anyone working there.

I will not be returning here.  When people from work (which is very nearby) suggest it, I'll push for Pour House or TJ's Everyday instead.

We heard great things about Pho Grand so we had a couple of meals here and tried different things from their large menu.  

Pros:

The restaurant, housed in an old building, is elegantly decorated and way nicer than your typical Viet hole-in-the-wall.   Great atmosphere.

The service is fast and efficient.  Servers are definitely competent in English, which may make a difference for some in terms of dish descriptions or food allergies.

They make tasty beef broth for pho.

Cons:

They don't provide soup spoons when you order pho.  You have to ask for one.  Yes, I'm serious.

They are downright skimpy with their fresh vegetables.  Not nearly enough lettuce and cilantro accompany their deep fried Vietnamese eggrolls.  The condiment plate for pho contains only a little cilantro and basil, and no jalapenos at all.   Again, you have to know that you have to ask.

They don't serve enough rice in their rice dishes, or noodles in their noodle dishes.  This may be in response to Caucasian food preferences but it sure doesn't please us Asians.  On that note, where is the little bowl of clear broth that usually accompanies rice platters?

Prices are higher and portions are smaller than what I'd normally expect for this type of Viet food.

We stumbled upon Cafe Mochi entirely by accident, and were so glad we did!  We originally thought this was a dessert place and passed it by, only to double back when the neon sushi sign in the window lit up.

This place serves solid, unpretentious fare at reasonable prices.  You get very good value for your money.  Specials during lunch and happy hour make it even more affordable.  We had shrimp and vegetable tempura, udon noodles, grilled lemongrass salmon, unakyu roll, Alaska roll and spicy tuna roll.  Portions were generous, and everything was fresh and tasty.

We had a great dinner and decided to return for lunch the next day.  The staff recognized us and the food was just as delicious.  If we lived in St. Louis, we would be regulars.

Loved our lunch experience at the Shaved Duck today.  The dark, intimate, cosy decor.  The irresistable smoky, barbecuey smell that hits you just as you are led into the dining room.  The "didn't-have-to-ask-for-a-single-thing" service.

And of course, the food.  Smothered fries, pulled pork sandwich, St. Louis style ribs, three types of bbq sauces.  So delicious.  Ribs were a tad dry, but I'll give them the benefit of the doubt as this was our only visit.  Definitely one of the best meals we've had in St. Louis!

We figured in keeping with the fowl... it would be perfect. Service is counter style; there is a special and they could use one of the chalkboards to list what it is. I always kind of dislike when a special is listed on the menu and you have to ask instead of it being transparent somewhere. It was some sort of burger this day... not chicken ? I came for chicken! My husband and I split the Fried Deviled Eggs ($7) for 6 .. with our college daughter. We expected more on flavor and just MORE for the price ! Eggs are cheap for quack sake .. oh wait. I have Oregon in my mind. My husband and I split The Heart Attack : Chicken Strips ; Mashed Potatoes & Gravy ; Bacon ; a Fried Egg placed between two fat waffles. We got this chicken in spicy but I only tasted spice on the last bite. The chicken itself was good. My daughter got The Classic Chicken and Waffle Sandwich which she liked but didn't like the Cider infused Maple Syrup and when she asked for plain we sensed a little attitude from the one girl who works the counter and runs the food ; which wasn't hot on delivery.. and that's my 3 , I like hot food .. the chicken actually was hot but the waffles were not even warm; I also don't so much  like attitude. It's a cute place tho on 4th Avenue in the arts district with several beers on tap. A small and somewhat tight place but the potential is there ; chicken  and waffles is always good for a splurge.. maybe this was an off Sunday or maybe she was an Oregon fan..?

I should have reviewed this so long ago.. considering that my wedding was at The JW Marriott Starr Pass a year ago and The Signature Grill was the place that catered the most important day of my life! We had the private dining room for our closest , nearest and dearest .. It overlooked the stunning resort grounds with a view of the golf course and mountains. The balcony overlooked the tee box in which we got married ! I was literally blown away at the impeccable attention to detail Signature Grill and its staff provided to me , prior to the wedding day/ evening , and during. The food was amazing !! The decor was too even though I had florals brought in for the tables and my own decor from my grandparents' wedding. The planner had passed that off to the staff. They piped our pre wedding photos from our dating years , childhood , etc. over a plasma television over the fireplace that was perfect and ambient to the setting of the evening. We also wanted music played that was our own.. I mean, 'Come Fly With Me ', is life! Done and done. The Rat Pack played all night! My Dad would be so proud that I'm such a Sinatra fan. Our menu was tailored to my allergies and to our budget and wants. Little menu cards adorned white China.. and it was unique and delicious! NOT like the wedding food you sometimes get that seems pre-made and dry! The best part: THE cake! I did want a wedding cake that I had seen, on , where else, The Knot via Pinterest! Chef Chris made it happen ! It was a showstopper and not only that.. it was delicious! I loathe cakes with fondant, as you can't eat the stuff and have it really taste good.. he made this cake happen without fondant! The champagne and flowed ; the staff never let a request go without attention , and let me say some of my group is , well .. High maintenance! After the wedding , we moved outside to the adjoining bar, Salud, where a corner kiva fireplace and more champagne had been set up for our guests. JB, our waiter and his staff boxed up all the extra cake; the decor; my wedding flowers, including my bouquet; even my Badgley Mischka's wedding stillettos and had them sent up to our wedding suite! A few nights later, after our guests had left the resort, we returned to Signature Grill, well, we were treated like VIP's again! JB, was once again our waiter.. well, our favorite Pinot Noir from the wedding appeared tableside and in the room!!! I can't even tell you how much we love the staff here at this place .. it will always hold such a place in my heart.. and it's a great place too. The patio isn't too fancy , but it's scenic , has a cool fire pit and for breakfast is amazing too! On weekends the brunch, although the buffet is $25, runs to 1400pm. If you opt for the menu, the Huevos Rancheros is off the charts. For dinner, ask for JB! I can't sing his praises enough :)

This was some of the best mexican food I have had in the US. Not only that, its a fun place with mariachis that travel around and act genuinely like they love playing music for the patrons! The place is colorful and transports you to a place on the beach in Mexico with all it's vibrance and color! We drove out of our way recently to have dinner here while on a weekend visit in Tucson. I will warn you, YOU will wait on a weekend night. So put your patience pants on and deal with it. OR do as we did.. head into the bar where the VERY, friendly bartenders are happy to serve up ginormous margaritas that are freshly made in front of you while you await your table. You can even eat at the bar, the one side part of that... the mariachis don't really fit into that area! You can hear them though. Besides the expansive drink menu of freshly made margaritas that will make you take an Uber or the wonderful fresh Sangria that the bartender also made fresh right in front of me and loaded up with fruit, THE salsa lady! She rolls up this table of goodies to make FRESH salsa right before your eyes with as much or as little spice as you like. Literally. BEST salsa ever. The bowl its served in was bigger than my head! For dinner I have always wanted to try a Molcajetes: a steaming hot lava bowl that is filled with large shrimp, tomatoes, mexican spices, lightly fried peppers and onions and cheese! It is served with corn or flour tortillas that are house made and piping hot. As if that isn't enough, because honestly that was a lot of food in the lava bowl!, it comes with beans and rice. I was so bummed I wasn't able to stuff my face more with all of this wonderful shrimp, as we were in a hotel and had a day loaded the next day and it was gonna go to waste. Literally, I can't think of a more amazing mexican meal I have had and that salsa was off the charts! Writing this review makes me want to go to Tucson now just for the salsa alone!

This is one of those places that exists purely on the lucky geographical location; that and the fact that there are no other places to eat a sit down dinner in Flourtown. 

The food is really pretty good. The prices are reasonable.
The time that you have to wait to get served negates the first two things that I just mentioned. 

The bar is kinda fun in a smoky old man sort of way.

I like to think of myself as a fairly adventurous eater, in the sense that I'll eat nearly anything except for foods slathered in mayonnaise. To take that idea further, I'm also a sucker for "interesting" dishes featuring exotic ingredients, layered/nuanced flavors, innovative preparation, artful plating, or any combination thereof. Parade these plates in front of me in the form of a multi-course tasting menu, and that's the formula for a meal I will always remember. 

There are two seatings per evening, at a bar that offers a full view of the kitchen. A seat at the table doesn't come cheap, at $150 per person, but keep in mind that this is going to be an experience of at least 12 courses. Viewed from that perspective, I'd bet that many have probably spent more, for lesser quality or quantity. Beverage pairing options are available, for an extra charge - many around us opted for the $100 "Sommelier Pairing" option, but we still had to eat and drink our way around Louisiana for a few more days, so we decided to pass, in the interest of saving some money. 

Here's a brief rundown of some of our more memorable dishes, but keep in mind that these will probably be subject to change:

The "magical muffuletta" was a play on the classic New Orleans sandwich, but instead of using something so pedestrian as bread, the "loaves" were little savory meringues.

My favorite plate of the evening was likely the "Southern picnic," which was fried chicken cotton candy with mustard seeds and fried okra. The plate itself was striking in presentation, but what made this tops for me was the dense chicken flavor of the cotton candy, which induced a bit of delicious cognitive dissonance. 

Another awfully cool plate was the "passion fruit pisco," a play on the pisco sour cocktail. I wish all pisco sours tasted like this. This dish was comprised of some cardamom apple, fennel and liquid nitrogen passion fruit with a nicely tart/sweet yuzu meringue on top. 

The most well-executed dish was the lobster chilaquiles. These came stocked with a nice bit of Mr. Pinchy, green salsa, lobster mole, queso fresco and onion ash. While I love lobster, I'd have to say that the green salsa and mole sauces really made this dish, with complex layers of sweet, spicy and smoky flavors. 

For dessert, there were a few bites, but the one that most stood out to me was a tarragon cake with satsuma ice cream and fresh satsuma, topped with a milk chocolate honey cremeaux. It wasn't overwhelmingly sweet, instead driven by the light herbal flavors of the cake and mild tart satsumas. 

This is just a sampling of the dishes I liked best....there were quite a few more courses! While they were all excellent, I cannot honestly say that the others were as memorable. Even so, this is still an easy 5 stars. I'd also like to note the pacing of the meal. Some of these multi-course tasting menus can drag out for a long time, while others feel rushed. For me, Square Root hit that sweet spot, allowing more than enough time to fully savor each special course, but without feeling like the night was dragging. Any waits in between courses were spent observing the kitchen staff work, which is fascinating in its own right. 

No boring meal, this. I'd recommend it to any serious eater.

Like most brewery tours, distillery tours tend to not be very distinctive. For the most part, if you've seen one, you've seem 'em all. What set this distillery tour apart for me was the quality of our tour guide, a salty, entertaining older gentleman whose name I sadly do not recall. Sure, we toured all the barrels, pipes, and vats that are essential to the distillation and maturation processes, but what made this tour much more fun than most were all the colorful stories and little bits of history that our guide would pepper in among his explanations of the more prosaic aspects of a distillery. 

And then, of course, there was the sampling. Our welcome cocktail was a simple, but effective combination of their spiced rum, and sweet tea. I don't usually think of rum and tea as going together, but here the combo was addictively refreshing. I think this has more to do with the unique cayenne/cinnamon/ginger/clove spicing going on in Old New Orleans' very tasty spiced rum....dumping some Bacardi into a jug of sweet tea would not fare as well. 

After the tour, we tasted all the rums on offer, by themselves. They are obviously outstanding rums for cocktails, but they are also smooth enough as to be sipping rums, should one be so inclined. This distillery also makes a product called Gingeroo. This is a bottled rum cocktail with ginger juice, cayenne, and cane syrup - a definite must for anyone who loves a good ginger bite as much as I. 

Service is exceptional as well. I wanted to bring a few bottles home, but had no room in our luggage. No problem - I was able to purchase 2 bottles of the spiced rum, plus a bottle of the Gingeroo, and they shipped the bottles to my office in Miami. Shortly after returning home, I was enjoying Old New Orleans' spiced rum in my own cocktail creations. Highly recommended for visitors of the Crescent City and locals alike.

Wow. Short bald waiter was embarrassingly rude. I brought all my friends here last night and was really looking forward to it. I have never been so offended by a waiter who treated us like shit from the moment we got there. Refused to tell us how much the cocktails cost, then snidely told me that the food runner "only has two hands" when I politely inquired about my missing food when everyone else had been served. Really? Thats how you talk to your customers? Everyone at the table was shocked. Throughout the evening he was a miserable snobby bitch about every single question and I hope he gets fired. He truly doesn't belong in the service industry. It was a real bummer because I liked the food.

This review is only for the charbroiled oysters!!  We  came here for a few drinks and some oysters, the wait time was about an hour or so. We were starving...they did give you 1 drink ticket each for the bar upstairs. We were able to snag some seats at the oyster bar. Now be prepared, you may end up smelling like charcoal but Greg, who prepares and cooks the oysters is AMAZING. 
The restaurant is definitely understaffed. No question. We were on our second dozen of the oysters before they even came over to take our drink orders. 
We ordered po' boys and some char broiled oysters for dinner. Po boys were fine, nothing to write home about ! We had the BBQ shrimp po boy, it's a huge sandwich and they literally scoop these little
Shrimp into a hero.  No lettuce or anything, but the sauce is good. But the oysters were AMAZING! They are by far the best ones I have had in NOLA. Just come here for those around lunch if possible but skip the dinner here ! Not worth the wait time 
If it were just a review on the oyster bar, I would say 5 stars but the service and po boy were a 3 star.

"Let's just stay for one more drink..." Oh man, famous last words indeed. I believe I said that about eight times during my night at Robert's, although by the end it probably sounded more like "SHOTS!!!!" ...even so, it's safe to say that you WILL have a good time at Robert's Western World.

I get that it's for the tourists mostly, but I was a tourist and it was one helluva night. The place was pretty packed, but I'd call it comfortably packed. The Mr and I made our way to the balcony area and had a perfect spot overlooking the whole floor and the band, plus there's a bar up there that's far less crowded. 

The crowd here is awesome, everybody is in a great mood and ready for a good time. We made friends with some random European tourists and, well, that's when I started saying "Just onnnne more drink..." And the drinks are cheap and cold. And the band is fantastic. And I can't tell you much else because, well... SHOTS.

Super charming little coffee shop tucked into the middle of Wells Ave! Met a friend here for coffee and brekkies for the first time this morning...how have I missed this place?
I can only attest to some breakfast offerings, but the bakery case had some beautiful muffins and pastries, and this lovely goddess of breakfast, their Avocado Toast! Avocado Toast is literally my FAVE thing for brekkie, and Walden's has outdone itself! Savory, crunchy amd creamy...so delish. 
Great coffee, nice cozy ambiance, amd friendly smiling staff makes this place a quaint stop for breakfast faves from sweet to savory!

My office has a view of Phaya Thai, and I've been waiting for opening day since their "coming soon" sign appeared. This morning my colleagues and I noted the big "open" banner outside, and knew what we were doing for lunch! We walked over and there was already a line, and many patrons sitting with their food. It's cafeteria style, you can select one two or three entrees with steamed rice, and add a spring roll, eggroll or crab rangoon. I had a pork eggplant dish and green curry with steamed rice, and one crab rangoon. The line moved a bit slowly, but they're still working out all the kinks- it's only their first day. I grabbed a glass of water and some hot sauce (just in case my food needed any extra boost). The crab rangoon actually tasted like crab, and not just cream cheese which was a nice treat. The pork dish was delicious, sweet and savory and perfectly cooked. The green curry was spicy, but not too spicy once I added the rice to the bowl. The portions were perfect for lunch. I didn't leave feeling like I was going to enter an afternoon food coma. The staff was friendly and though they were busy, still smiled and seemed excited to see how many people were coming to their first day of business. I hope that they remain that busy- it looks like everyone in the fort ben area was ready to have a good thai option.

Paladar was one of the participating restaurants for KOP Restaurant Week. I've participated in Center City's Restaurant Week many times, but it was nice to venture somewhere different yesterday and enjoy a fine meal at Paladar. A portion of the proceeds benefit Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

We had a reservation for lunch at 1:30. We arrived and 1:15 and the reservation was honored early. Our waiter was Miguel. He was so kind and helpful. He told us about the three menus they were offering; brunch, lunch and Restaurant Week. For $15, you get an appetizer, entree and dessert for lunch, $30 for dinner. Drinks are not included on the RW menus, but they did have a $3 mimosa just in case you wanna get crunk on the cheap. Miguel told us his favorite way of customizing his guac; that's another thing I loved about Paladar. You can create your own guac with however many ingredients you wish. We added goat cheese and mango salsa in our guac and it was heavenly. 

Started my afternoon off right by ordering a charred pineapple mojito. So flavorful and strong! 
I selected the Mushroom Escabeche Salad and my friend ordered the Mole Chicken Tostones. Those were the only two options for appetizers. The salad was huge! I was expecting it to be a much smaller portion since it was on RW menu. 
For my meal, I went with the Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Sweet Potato tacos... again, so much flavor! It came with a side of rice and beans which I don't care for but the tacos were fantastic.

Finally, dessert was between the Guava and Cheese
pastelito or a seasonal sorbet. Both of us got the pastelito. Reminded me a bit of Baklava. 

The reviews here weren't the best, but I enjoyed the food and service at Paladar. I'll be returning!

I had to swing by my office and was craving something sweet so I placed an order for pick-up at Sweet Box on my way home this afternoon. This place has been on my bookmarks/bucket list for a hot minute. My co-workers have been raving about their cupcakes, but I personally wanted to try the "Jawn" because it's one of their most popular items. 

My order was placed through DoorDash, but Sweet Box is also listed on Caviar. Ordering was a breeze. You can choose what time you'd like to pick up and you receive an e-mail confirmation. I also received a text message when my order was ready. The cupcakes of the day are listed on their Instagram page. I decided to get the "Jawn" and a banana pudding. 

When my friend and I arrived, a woman was at the front unpacking some boxes and she asked for our names and handed us our orders. Fairly easy transaction. We asked if it was absolutely necessary to place the order on DoorDash (we know DoorDash makes a small profit off of the business and it sucks) but to our surprise, she said the cupcakes she had on display were still available and we don't necessarily have to order through the app if we know what we want when we stop in. She was very warm and welcoming and thanked us for stopping in. It was a little cramped in there, but I understand their working conditions must be tough right now with the pandemic going on. It's a strange time for everyone. 

The banana pudding was smooth and creamy. I'd love it if it came in a bigger size, but I was so satisfied with the flavor and I devoured it in 5 minutes. Haven't tried the "Jawn" yet but I'm super pumped to give it a whirl tomorrow! I could almost see rays of sunshine leaving the box as I opened it to snap a picture. Five stars all the way for Sweet Box! Can't wait to visit again.

Great atmosphere, great spot, great beer, and most importantly delicious food! I do not know how I have not been to Twenty Tap before, but I'm glad somebody finally dragged me along to it. I have been to Fat Dan's right next door and the Fresh Market across the street numerous times. We had about a 30 minute wait on a Sunday night, but it was during the NFL playoff games and their bar area is a good place to hangout and wait for your table. 

First off, they obviously have 20 beer taps, as well as wine and bottled beer. The pint of the day was their house dubbel and it was actually really good. Not quite Taxman's quality of a dubbel, but then again that is their thing. The price of $3.50 a pint was great though and I enjoyed their beer. I was surprised that they brewed beer in-house and I will have to go back and try more. 

The food was top notch for a brewpub. Our groups tarted out with the cheese curds with the chimichurri and garlic dipping sauces. Really, the curds did not need to be dipped, they were tasty on their own. We didn't use much of the dipping sauces and actually saved them for dipping the seasoned fries into with our main course. Our group got a couple of the Tex burgers and the Blue Cheese Burger (I can't remember the name), but they were both good! I personally had the Tex and like it better than the blue cheese. It is a messy burger so be warned, but messiness is goodness in this case. The BBQ oozed out of the bun, and the onion rings and provolone paired very well. Awesome burger!

The service was quick, friendly, and helpful. Our server asked what kind of beers we were into and gave his recommendations for us to try. 

Overall I had a great time, and this place quickly became one of my local favorites!

I'm not a chef, I am just a normal person like most of you. I am not a food critic, just a person who likes food and will do my best to guide you with the most honest answers to a place due to my experiences.

I hate to be the first person to give this a 3 star rating but I rate hard on good food and service. You need both to execute a perfect meal and a perfect overall experience.

I love ramen and have eaten it through many cities in award winning restaurants.

I am stoked that in the past year St. Louis has added specialty ramen places from Nami to Robata to Midtown, etc and still more to come in the year.

I was super excited to try Vista being that it just opened a few weeks ago so I headed down to from the counties to make a trip to another part of the Lou.

Overall...

If the ramen was on point at Vista, 5 stars for sure. Otherwise a solid 4 all around.

Vista takes a lot of styles and puts them together in one location. The decor and size of the restaurant is no bigger than an average ramen/sushi place which is pretty small to start off with. Few tables and counter sitting for the most part. Added a small bar in the corner of the place that makes contemporary style drinks, also serving fusion American and Asian style sides and starters along a contemporary hipster vibe and feel from the neighborhood and you are bound to get a hit.

Service was on point, cooks, servers, every worker in the place seemed well educated over the menu and the ingredients going into every dish. They were also very attentive and friendly. 5 stars easily for service and ambiance as well.

Vista's ramen dish is called the Vista and that was what I order along with some Thai sausage. My friends also got a Vista ramen, some Korean chicken sliders and Korean pancakes. The starters were delicious visually and taste wise but the ramen fell through hard. If you read my Nami review you will see why I go hard on ramen reviews.

The broth lacked flavor tremendously, very bland and lacking any seasoning.
The noodles were under cooked but were hand made at least.
The pork was thick and large but was mostly fat and was not seasoned right.
The only good part of the ramen was the perfectly poached egg in the soup.

I know this place is new and it takes a while for certain new places to get it right so I will be back to update my review in a few months. Nami improved and I hope this place can as well. Places like this in St. Louis are rare and I want them to thrive by giving them repeat business but it is hard to repeat business if the main course is not good. 
A friend asked me to rate the ramen from a scale of 1-10 and I gave it a 2. I know that is harsh but I know my ramen and I am not trying to duplicate my experience from really good ramen shops but just enjoy my food at every or any location I go to without disappointment.

This was place will certainly thrive being it's location but the main reason you go to Vista is for the RAMEN! everything else in the restaurant is just a supporting cast to the main star.

dp

I might be going in a couple of different directions here so bare with me.

One of my friends Li Pan wrote a 1 star review on this place and I was like, "What! she has to be out of her mind for slamming this place," it is only the second legit Ramen place to open up in the 314/636 in forever and whoever is making a play for legit Ramen has to be getting it right, right?

She wasn't though and after my experience I can see why this place is getting 2 or less stars if not none. I will be focusing on the food because service was good and the ambiance was legit. I like the family style seating and the stools to tall tables, it gives a very modern feel to the restaurant.

I also want to say to you other yelpers, stop comparing this place to Japan or NY style ramen, yes we know Nippon is legit in New York but this is St. Louis. Factor in the culture and diversity before putting any ramen joint in St. Louis on a pedestal. I know Robata opened and by far their broth is so much better, not the best ramen in the world, but not the worst.

And yes I will be updating my review because I will come back to try other ramens to see if they are better than the one I had.

First the ramen is overpriced. People say it because it is located in the heart of a Clayton, but Chipotle has the same price in Clayton as it does in the county. I can get past the overpriced ramen. We don't have ramen spot in St Louis so I am willing to pay a little extra for something I can't get unless I travel to Chicago.

Second, to whoever owns this place, read your reviews! The biggest thing that is hurting you is your broth. It sucks, it is bland and has no flavor. Granted the pork or eggs or vegetables might have given it a extra hint of something, the broth is what makes your ramen, RAMEN! 
Almost every other review on Nami is about your broth lacking flavor. I shouldn't need to add siracha or more pepper or salt to any ramen dish. A perfect ramen comes out flavorful. I got the ROASTED BLACK GARLIC TONKOTSU and I barely tasted any garlic. Garlic is suppose to be the main theme of the dish but honestly the eggs were. The pork was excellently cooked but it lack balance with the bland broth. Fix the broth. You had like 7 people on the line. Even Munsok, the owner of Drunken Fish was there with one of his executive cooks while I was eating, hopefully giving you tips on how to spice up your broth!

Third, I tried the BAO, braised pork belly and braised pulled pork. The buns were not fluffy and the braised pork was horrible. It is like you were trying to upset me on purpose by giving me that can pieced of meat. Nothing braised of flavorful about the pork. The pork belly, decent but not executed to perfection due to the lack of fluff in the bun.

Damn, I felt like I wrote a story but I am willing to change this review on my second of third times around at Nami.

Also don't take this as an attack to whoever owns this place. I want you to succeed and be the best spot in town to go get ramen. I want to tell all my people that we have an official ramen spot in town for them to go to,
I know you are a new spot and because of that you will get business but as the months go by people will realize how crappy your broth and bao are and you can't have legit ramen without the broth.

dp

YES!

My kid and I have been long time fans of the original location, so imagine our excitement when we saw that we were getting a Hiroba on our side of town!  

My daughter and I actually stopped by 3 times before they were opening (hoping they were open) because we just couldn't calm the heck down over it.

Long story short - this location did NOT disappoint!  The sushi is just as amazing as the original location and the staff has the same, warm greeting when you enter.  My favorite is still the Kwon and they have the best salmon nigiri in town!

THANK YOU Hiroba for bringing happiness to Sparks.

If I had a dollar for every time someone asked me if I wanted to try Pho...........I wouldn't be writing this review.  I'd be paying someone to do it for me while I eat the most expensive lobster I could find on my yacht sailing somewhere in France with champagne...................but I don't have a dollar for every time I resisted, so here I sit, writing this by myself.

After years and years of turning down invites from a large variety of people, I finally let my boyfriend take me to Pho.  He chose Pho 777 boasting about their great food and environment.

Michael T......... ( My Yelp Idol ) is right about the pro-tip parking.  Park in the Cal-Neva, walk  1/2 a block and call it good.  Easy Peasy. 

When we walked in, the manager gave us the "hand wave" and showed us where to sit.  Easy Peasy again.  We sat down and I assessed my situation.  The décor is simple if almost non-existent.  Beige walls and a few live plants throughout the room.  It's not super huge but not super tiny. Comfortable, would be a good way to describe it.  We were given water very quickly and later even given our own pitcher since we were going through it so quick - that was appreciated.

The menu will confuse you if you have not had Pho before.  It's written in Vietnamese as well as English for first timers like me who haven't the single clue as to what they are looking at.  I ordered the #21 and we also got spring rolls and a won ton order.  My order consisted of crunchy noodles, pork, meat loaf and a bunch of other meats along with shrimp and a side of broth.  

I'll admit defeat to my years of defiance against Pho right here and right now.  It was damn tasty.  It really was.  I enjoyed the flavors that combined when the broth hit the noodles and the Won Tons were wonderful.  I think my favorite part about the dish was the pork - it was very tender and full of flavor.  I'm obviously not a Pho connoisseur since this was my first experience but I was impressed, so that's gotta point in favor for Pho 777.

Overall the environment was great, the customer service was pretty top notch and the food was great.  I'm pretty mad at myself for being such a stubborn, foot stomping baby over Pho for so many years, but at least my man finally got me to partake and now we can go back and enjoy some more.

Thanks Pho 777!

This is America, and we have the right to free speech, one of the many freedoms that make this country great.  That being said, I'm going to exercise my free speech and say that the "This is America, when ordering, speak English" sign, and the numerous other signs (yes, last I checked they are still up there) outside Geno's are hypocritical, RACIST and flat out ignorant.  Plus their steaks are sh*t. 

Congratulations, Geno's, you've added nothing to this community but hate-mongering propaganda and crappy hoagies. Bravo.  I mean "well done." Sorry.

This is an update to my earlier 'Incredibly Rude!!' review.
A few days ago I received an email from Daughters Cafe.  When I saw it in my inbox I imagined they had seen the error of their ways and emailed to apologize for how they treated me. This is what I'm sure most other restaurants would do. However, Daughters decided to make excuses, blame living social and say that my concerns weren't their concerns. If there is one party that is definitely not to blame for this situation it is the customer and daughters need to learn this. So now not only were they rude to me in person but they even took the time to be rude to me by email. This just illustrates how completely unprofessional they are. Shameful!!!

We read Brian Ries's review and went here on our way from the beach. Simply said: what a find - great and delicious food, wonderful atmosphere, great service and very reasonable prices. Definitely a restaurant worth going out of your way for. My wife and I visited on 7-25-11 and had the Pho, which is very flavorful (the first time I drank the broth out of the bowl) and the Banh mi sandwich - just right. You miss something  if you don't visit this charming place.

We will be back.

Thank you Argento's for the incredible custom rainbow layer cake for my virtual sprinkle this past Saturday.   It was wonderful, both aesthetically as well as being delicious. We also tried the chocolate shelled cannoli, chocolate cake cheesecake, the raspberry crumb cheesecake as well as some assorted Italian cookies. What a true delight! All of the pastries were excellent and gave us a taste of home (Long Island, NY). Bravo Argento's!! We can't wait to try your food!

Bricks had a limited but interesting menu.  The wine list was also limited but very adequate.  Our food was very good.  The  bruschetta appetizer was as good as it gets, the toasted bread was still warm and the tomatoes, fresh basil and fresh mozzarella were cold - superior presentation and taste.  Key lime pie was third on my all time list.  Entrees were very good and the service was good.  We sat in a NY style booth that was divided by glass partitions. The group next to us had one woman whose voice was so loud you could have heard her on the East Coast and she was trying to impress everyone within hearing distance with her travel exploits.  I almost gave Bricks a 2 star rating just because the loud mouth spoiled what was an otherwise excellent meal.

The happy hour here is probably the best happy hour in the city, one it is SEVEN DAYS a week happy hour and two the food is an amazing deal.  I've gotten everything on the menu several times.

My usual items are: Pork Ban Mi (perfectly toasty and seasoned, goes amazingly well with Siracha), the bbq wings, the giant bowl of kim chi fried rice, fried and balsamic vinegar tossed brussel sprouts.


You can either sit at the regular bar, or the bar facing the kitchen, back in the graffiti bar, or even outside on sansom street.


The drinks are $4 for the beer of the day, $5 for the cocktails.  The beers are not that special, maybe a blue moon, etc but your coming here mainly for the food vs the drinks.

The epitome of "doing too much".

It's a club, restaurant, and speakeasy?

We skipped the food which looked decent, yet small. 

The basement lounge needs a password to get into - which is cute, but slightly tacky. 

The bartender in the basement was excellent at half of his job - making drinks - but had a bit of a cocky attitude and ended up ruining what would've been a great bartender/bargoer relationship. 

Both cocktails were fantastic. The second one I ordered was priced at 20$, steep by any reasonable standard. After ordering, I received the blunt question, "that one is twenty dollars, can you afford it?". Underdressed and relatively younger than the rest of the clientele, I couldn't tell if he was kidding. I called him out on it. I could afford it, and I paid for it, but I left afterwards with a sour taste.

This place is in our 'hood, and we had been there for food truck night when they were under construction. After many months of seeing them being not quite open, we were excited to finally go! 

We tried to attend Tino's Pizza night and found that not only was the pizza gone before the scheduled end of the event, but kids are not allowed anywhere on the premises after 3 PM. We had our tweenager with us, so we left. What a shame - they have a great garden, perfect for kids, and we don't generally go for beers before 3pm. 

The place was fairly empty and the barkeep not too welcoming.

Crossing that one off our list...maybe we'll go back on a no-kid night. We want Three Canyons to be good, but spouse thinks the no-kid rule is a killer (insurance?) Time will tell I suppose...

Hands down, Forsythia has immediately climbed out of my gut and into my heart as my all-time Philly favorite. With a server like Seth, you'll feast and be treated like royalty.

Must get: foie gras, Panisse (chickpea) w/cheese, agnolotti, sea bream, omelet, clams, mushroom
Meh: wagyu beef
Missed: pigtail, cocktails, rabbit leg

Forsythia has only been open for 2 months, but it has already garnered a cult following. From the high set ceiling with its unique decor, to the immaculate attention and care by its waiters (Seth was an amazing rockstar), and the reasonably priced food, Forsythia is ideal from dates, socialization, or a business meal.

When it comes to the food, most of my Philly fine dining has been riddled with strong accented dishes that tried too hard to overwhelm and wow you. But it was clear from the moment I saw how Chef Kearse plated his Panisse w/the raclette cheese or how airy and fluffy the omelet tasted and even how better it married the fresh crab within its eggy goodness, I knew I was in for a treat. In short, everything just...worked, all notes were in harmony. For example, the smoked ricotta was just tantalizing next to the hunk of mushroom; the smoked sea bream skin contrasted so much with the celery root puree, or how the clam broth was so delectable that we got 3 servings of the sourdough bread just to soak it all up! Everything was perfect!

My only beef, pun intended, was the wagyu, in which I failed to taste the intricacies of the wagyu, but enjoyed the malt vinegar and broccoli combination. The raclette cheese was a bit salty for the already perfect and instantaneously dissolving Panisse and the agnolotti was just too...rich, with both the cheese and lamb neck causing all sorts of delicious regret on the walk home.

At the end of the night, we truly had a marvelous night and hope that Forsythia alters their menu per the season so we can revisit!

Food/ambiance/service/price: 5 stars

While shopping on the other side of the city with favorite daughter and her friend from DC, we decided to give her friend the Philly treatment by treating her to a cheese steak.   Out of all the cheese steaks in the city we went with Ishkabibble's.   We'd had been shopping and didn't want to move our car to drive to South Street which parking can be a bear so we took an Uber instead.

Ishkabibble's is nothing fancy but the cheese steaks are the bomb.  They offer more than just streaks but why get anything else but maybe some fries.  Lol

We ordered chicken and regular cheese steaks with fries and a couple bottles of water.  The meat was chopped up on a nice large soft roll, which is what I like.  The roll is what makes it even more special.  

The service was quick and polite.  The restaurant is a dive but clean enough to eat in.  Would come here again in a heartbeat.

I used to come here often... decided to come back today because I was craving some dim sum and Chinese dishes. Guess this will be my last because there are little cockroaches crawling on the wall by our table, I freaked out. And saw another one that I accidentally killed with my cup, ON MY TABLE!!!!!

The best place for boba in Tucson! The taste is very authentic and they have more than just boba toppings to choose from. My favorite topping is the house-made egg pudding. 

You can get almost any drink hot which is great for fall, even though fall falls barely below 80F in Tucson. 

You can also adjust sweetness level so your drink is unique to your tastes. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a place to hang out and get tea. It can get a little loud so I don't recommend doing homework here without headphones.

I can fix this food at home. You come here only for atmosphere. Period. It's in an old Victorian home full of the owner's ancestor's antiques.  Good wine list.  Really good wine list.  But I don't like to drink a bottle of Caymus with previously frozen fish.  I would like more focus on the quality of the food and less on the house.

My first visit to Bacchanal was a little confusing and, frankly, a little intimidating.  

I didn't know how the cheese, wine, or food worked.  I ended up sitting on a very uncomfortable empty keg (seriously, this was a seating option).  It was a Friday and too busy to ask anyone for help. 

My subsequent visits to Bacchanal have been a googolplex times better.

If you are a newbie, here is how it works: 

To your left when you first walk in is a cooler with excellent cheese where you can pick out a few wedges. Find a bottle of wine or opt for the by the glass options listed on the board behind the register.  

Pay with cash or credit at the register and ask for the cheese board (+$5, totally worth it).  Three cheeses and a nice bottle of wine will cost $30-35. They take your cheese, open your wine, and give you glasses.  

Go outside (now with no kegs in sight!) and choose a table or go upstairs to sit on the balcony or in the swanky new inside area.  Within minutes, your cheese board will arrive on a pizza pan, complete with assorted pickles, olives, nuts, fruit, and bread. It is enough food for dinner for two.

If you desire more substantial nourishment, there is a kitchen in the back with excellent options, including delightful desserts--cash only. Check out the menu online.

Tips:  
1. They provide bug spray.  Use it.
2. At dusk, watch out for the adorable frogs hopping around.
3. There is live music most nights, so sit outside.

You WON'T be disappointed!

My wife and I wanted to go to Mo's downtown for our anniversary. When I called, they said "Thank you for calling J. Hamman Prime, formerly Mo's". I was a little disappointed that we wouldn't be eating at Mo's, but I figured we'd give it a shot.

We arrived earlier than our reservations, and they went ahead an seated us anyways. Our menu's had "Happy Anniversary" printed on them. Which we thought was VERY cool. (We're pretty simple people, lol). The hostess then asked if we wanted our picture taken, we said "sure". She took our picture, and then about 15 minutes later arrived with the picture in a frame, and placed it on the table. A neat touch.

We started with the scallops wrapped in prosciutto. Amazing

For the main course, we had the 8oz filet's. One with peppercorn topping and one with spicy crab topping. Both amazing. The steaks were cooked perfectly. We ordered the broccolini and white cheddar mashed potatoes on the side. Both cooked to perfection.

At the end of the night, they brought our their signature bread pudding, (on the house).

It was the perfect night in my opinion, and I wanted to give major props to the management and wait staff for making our experience one to remember!

My wife and I visited Tennessee Brew Works on a muggy Tuesday afternoon during our trip to Nashville. The bar area/tasting room was not crowded and had a relaxed atmosphere. Meanwhile the tank room was a hub of activity, and it was interesting to see the brewers at work.

My wife wasn't drinking, but I ordered a flight of beers. I really appreciated the wide variety of styles that TBW offered for their flights. I feel like some of the breweries in California have become a little too IPA-centric so it was nice to see a good mix of options. 

I chose the Southern Wit, Cutaway Rye IPA, 1927 IPA, City Winery Abbey Strong Ale, and the Chestnut Brown Ale. All of the beers were great but I especially enjoyed the City Winery Strong Ale as it had a tart cherry taste that made me feel like I was drinking Pinot Noir. 

Overall, we really enjoyed the beer and the chill vibes (although I'm sure this place is probably packed on a Friday night). We would definitely recommend stopping in and trying a few beers.

Wow!!! I was a little weary when my friend chose this place for our happy hour get together after work, it's located in the parking lot of the croydon train station, but let me tell you... I was pleasantly surprised and will definitely be going back!! What an awesome place!!! It's small, and very hip. We sat at a high top table in the bar area, happy hour is from 4:30-7pm which is quite a long duration for a happy hour, which is another plus for this place! Most happy hours last only one hour, this time frame worked out well. If you are a fan of bloody Mary's this is the ultimate place to order one!!!!! For only $6 a glass, the famous Bloody Mary is served in a mason jar and it is unbelievable!!! I can't fully put into words how amazing it was! The taste was unlike any other Bloody Mary I've ever had before and I usually order this drink everywhere I go. Hands down.... Best Bloody Mary ever!!! You will never order one from anywhere else, after drinking one from dog and bull. Overall this is an awesome place and a must visit!!!!!

We visited Pappy's smokehouse on a trip to St Louis. Of course being in St Louis we had to have St Louis ribs which were the best ribs we have ever had. Don't let the long line or difficulty in finding parking scare you. The staff at Pappy's is super organized, friendly and persistent. 

We ordered half a rack of ribs and made it a combo by adding pulled pork. For the sides we got fried corn and baked beans. The beans were delicious, the corn...not so much. The corn was intensely greasy and had no seasoning to it. After taking a few bites, I had to stop as it felt like I was literally drinking cooking oil. Regardless of the corn, we'll be back and order a different side instead. Thanks Pappy's for filling our bellies while in Saint Louis!

Review #14 of 2017

I am not sure I understand the hype of this place.  Coming from the bay area where we are saturated with chains, we always try to hit up local spots while on road trips.  You can tell the Spot is local, however their prices and food just don't compute to amazingness.  We shared a burger and a chocolate shake which came out to $8+.  My other half was craving a chocolate chip shake and we were ready to be wow'd.  There isn't much shade around on the patio which is dog friendly. The orders come pretty quick.  We received our order a few minutes after placing it. Unfortunately the wow never happened.  The shake tasted like melted vanilla ice cream and we couldn't find any chocolate chips until we drank all the shake.  They sunk to the bottom. It seemed like they were dropped to the bottom of the cup before the shake was poured, and not blended in.  The burger was not anything exceptional and at $4+ I found it to be quite expensive for something that didn't seem of high quality. While it's a decent place to go if there's nowhere else open, I don't think we'd come back to the spot.

Unlimited hibachi?  Where do I sign?

This is essentially your standard Japanese hibachi restaurant, with a twist.  Pay $17.95, and you get unlimited food.  Yes, you read that right, unlimited, with a few caveats.

First, you entire party must decide to order a'la carte (as you would normally) or unlimited.  This is to prevent sharing, and seems fair - if perhaps inconvenient depending on the makeup of your party.   The unlimited price for kids is much lower, $5 for the younger ones.  

Once you've decided on the unlimited, you can order pretty much anything from the menu as much as you'd like.  Some items - filet mignon, for example - are at an extra charge ($5 for the filet).   But if you order hibachi shrimp as your entree, for example, you can still order as much chicken, shrimp, or even sushi as you'd like. 

The other caveat - if you do not finish what you order beyond your entree, you will be charged for it.   It's not a horrible charge, and roughly commensurate what you'd pay if you ordered it a'la carte - again, reasonable and fair.   Of course, if you are all ordering unlimited, you can share - so if the kid doesn't finish that California roll, you can.   And, of course, you can just order something to share intentionally.

Two things keeping this from being a 5-star review - both fixable by the restaurant:

1.  Limited hibachi tables mean that you might have a long wait.  However, you can get the same food at a conventional table.  

2.  Sometimes, the wait to get more food is a bit long.  Other times, it comes out quickly.  

The service is good, the staff is friendly, and you can eat as much or as little as you like for a reasonable price.

One thing that irks me  when your food arrives cold and you're one of 15 people in the entire place.  

When asked if they had  a guacamole tostada. The answer was a definitive no! It didn't seem like the waitress was too happy to be there.  And yes both items were cold. I had them redo the enchilada.

If you want below par service this is the place. Ugh so disappointed! I expected more considering I drove across town to get here.

They do know how to make it hot because my second enchilada was piping hot as opposed to the 1st!.

Sorry for the poor review...

Uhm, super awesome bubble tea place! Really, calling it a bubble tea cafe doesn't do it justice because they serve so much more.  It was a bit overwhelming when I first walked in because there are just so many combinations you can get.  But they have something for any mood you may be in, from creamy to fruity to chocolaty to tea-y? Once you decide on a drink, you then have the option of boba, grass jelly, pudding, coconut jelly, rainbow jelly, coffee jelly, or red beans as toppings (for $ 0.50 each).  Also, for all you lactose intolerant (or vegan) folks, the "milk" is not milk, but rather, non-dairy creamer.  I really couldn't tell until I was told. Perhaps my favorite feature is the ability to customize the sweetness (0%, 30%, 50%, 80%, regular sweetness)! I always hate when a drink is too sweet. Things are often far too sweet for me because my threshold for sweetness doesn't match that of the general population. Now if my drink is too sweet, I can only hate on myself. 

I finally decided, with help from the barista, on the brown rice green milk tea with half bubbles and half pudding at 50% sugar. It was everything I was hoping for and tasted exactly as I had imagined! It was delightfully creamy with a hint of toasted nuttiness from the brown rice which nicely balance the green tea. The sweetness was on point. The pudding and pearls were lightly sweetened and added a fun variety of textures. Unfortunately, the boba was a wee bit under --you know, with that overly chewy/hard inner core. Kinda a no-no for a boba place, but I'll overlook it this time. 

The lounge area is nice and chill. It was super quiet while I was there, except for the country music that was blasting... but seems like a good place to hang out and chill with friends. 

Overall, awesome bubble teas (plus juices, smoothies, mousses, coffees and more) with many complex flavors and cool customizable features (especially the sweetness level!!). Be sure to check in on Yelp for a discount and get a punch card to earn a free drink!

If you love waiting 90 minutes for a cold, messed up order, this is the place for you!

Basically, horrible delivery service. We ordered online but sbmenus wasn't letting us add boba to our drinks so we called and asked them to add boba which they ok'd AND even left a note on the order to remind them but there was no boba. We also ordered two half chicken half beef bowls but we got one chicken and one beef. I called after we got the food. They would only give us free drinks the next time we visit. We'll see if they remember. I just want my money back.

There is no doubt in my mind that Soulard Farmer's Market is a treasure in the city of St. Louis! 

First Star: I can always find fresh produce. It's a combination of local and shipped in products sold by local vendors, and it's typically decently priced (bring cash, because not all vendors are set up for cards). There aren't as many organic producers as I would like, but you can find them. There are also meats, baked goods, and other fun non-food items. I love browsing the aisles and being inspired by my shopping finds. So I always bring a bag and fill 'er up!

Second Star: Nestled close to the Mississippi River, the market is rooted in St. Louis history. It can trace its beginnings back to the 18th century. Structurally built like old European "H style" markets (central core with four legs or wings for vendors), its origin was an open air field for farmers to sell produce, livestock, and dairy. Why shop in a new brick box store when you can wander the historical paths of Soulard?!?

Third Star: Speaking of wandering, enjoy as you walk. Purchase a baked good from the several bakery spots, or grab a fresh made tamale. Imbibe with the hair of the dog that bit ya with a Bloody Mary, or sample a tasty bite if one of the vendors is offering. Grab a hot fresh mini-donut, or locally made pork rinds. They say you eat with your eyes first, and at Soulard you'll have the chance to see it and actually eat it while you shop!

Fourth Star: I love that you'll hear live music from the banjo players who seem to have a permanent residence at the end of one of the halls. You'll also be entertained by street performers from time to time and characters galore. It can get crowded on event weekends. So whether your vibe is to partake or avoid the crowds, you can check their website for updates. 

http://www.soulardmarket.com/soulard_market_002.htm

Which leads me to the Fifth Star:  It's a melting pot of fun people watching and interaction. You never know who (or what) you'll see! To me a visit to the market is like feeling the heartbeat of The Lou. So whether you're a local or a visitor, Soulard Farmer's Market has a lot to offer and is definitely worth the visit!

Comfort food and dining 101:

-Delicious food
-Great ambiance (bonus points for real fireplace)
-Decent alcohol list
-Excellent staff service

We had our recent International Supper Club dinner here. The staff easily accommodated 20ish people, helpfully adding chairs for our plus ones. 

They had decorated for Christmas, and the large trees next to the immense fireplace set the mood for a rustic and festive holiday party. I was amazed that the hall did not have a smokey smell, despite the crackling wood fire. They kept it cherrily blazing away the whole evening, without fuss or distraction.

The food was amazing - I ordered a dish similar to beef stroganoff, but baked, called Voldistana. I was only able to eat about 1/3 of the dish and enjoyed yummy leftovers the next day. 

I also enjoyed a beautiful pear brandy from their beverage list, thanks to the staff who were helpful in with their suggestion. I confess to another indulgence - Baklava. It was crisp and delightfully sticky with honey. It was the perfect compliment to the brandy.

I would be remiss if I didn't mention the wonderful basket of Bosnian bread that they brought to our table before we ordered. I honestly don't know why, but Bosnian bread is the most delicious. It's soft and not yeasty, and oh so good. It made my day to see a basket of that warm bread and soft butter appear. The staff brought extra servings as we quickly demolished our portion. Oh, how I wish I knew how they made that baked goodness - until then and my next Grbic visit, I can buy it at my local Schnucks!!!

I highly recommend Grbic! I'll be back to further explore their Bosnian menu and Eastern European specials...and bread!

Ohhhh, organic pickles.....and organic mayo.....and organic ketchup..to eat with your organic fries, after which you wipe your fingers with an organic/recycled napkin that came from a sustainable tree which was planted by a guy who drives a Prius that he bought after a PETA rally.......well, you get the point.

Bottom line, it's reasonably priced for the great quality, fries were on point, and I left happy. Sure, it loves to remind you how organic it is, like your vegan friend who reminds you how much they love quinoa, or your other friend who reminds you of how cultured they are because they spent a semester abroad....but whatever.

At this point, it's just good.....

But I have one point of contention:  You call the place "Graze" based on the idea that the beef is grass fed.  Neat, fine and dandy..then why the hell do I pay an extra $1 for grass fed beef?  Make it all grass fed!

I had an excellent experience dining at Blue Corn. The service was good, fast and very professional. We tried an array of dishes, that all came at the same time. 

The blue corn tacos and the tacos pibil were flavorful and complex, maybe missing a bit of salt but that's the only fault I can find. 

Their prices are very good for the quality of food they are offering and I would surely visit again to try more from their menu.

Tried SB's newest restaurant, Relais de Paris, last night - FAB! Perfect portion sizes, light and simple flavors, amazing signature sauce and the best mussels I have tasted EVER. The salad just sang with every bite, and the French Fries were very tasty. Everything was local and very, very fresh and delicious. The dining room was classic and elegant, and the owner, Skye McGinnes, was seated at a table nearby chatting with customers. We didn't have a reservation but got in within minutes on a Saturday night around 8pm. Great bar while you are waiting. My new favorite place to dine!

The food is very good!  It's also authentic at least according my friend who is Korean.  His mom used to make authentic Korean dishes for him growing up, and he said this is the real deal.  The food here is delicious, the restaurant is clean, and the staff is very friendly.  

The food is also very reasonably priced.  I can eat a lot, but I find myself making two meals out of what I buy.  That often means I can eat great food for under $5 a meal.

If you like Korean food, you should definitely check out Omoni.

Hello, I love libertine! First of all it is in a basement on mass ave which gives it a cool, secretive vibe. This place is perfect for starting or ending your weekend night. It has a relaxed vibe and some of the most creative cocktails I have seen. If you were hoping to have a boozy bourbon drink with a marshmallow on fire in the actual glass then look no further! I got this drink a couple of weeks ago and It was delicious. I came here with a friend and we sat at the bar - comfortable seats! There are plenty of tables and chairs which is nice. However it did fill up quickly as the night went on so keep that in mind if you're hoping to snag a seat. This place is a lot of fun and I look forward to coming here more and more! The bartenders are friendly and personable. Pricing is reasonable. Libertine, I will be back!

I guess this is what I get for reading reviews made by non-Asians (no racist). I say this because the food here was very Americanized. I was very disappointed because of this.

First off, this establishment does not have any Sriracha sauce. I've never been to a restaurant that sells pho and not have Sriracha. To this moment, I still can't wrap my head around that. Instead, when I asked for Sriracha sauce, the waitress handed me a silver container of chili sauce that does not even resemble it. This sauce was fine with my dipping sauce for the egg rolls but is not ok with my pho.

Now, the pho. The only veggies you will find in your bowl of pho is red onions and green onions. And maybe a pinch of cilantro. Real Vietnamese pho has bean sprouts, Thai basil leaves, green onions, cilantro, and sliced jalapeno peppers. So as you can tell, I was very confused when I dove into my bowl of imitated pho. The broth was a little too sweet for me and there was no soy sauce around for me to fix it. There was only sliced beef in it as well. No meatballs (which are my favorite) or tendons. 

Other than pho, my friends are I ordered the fried egg rolls, summer rolls, and onion soup. The egg rolls and onion soup were delicious. The egg rolls were cooked to perfection and the meat (I believe pork) were flavorful. Onion soup was the bomb diggity. Summer rolls were good. Can't really go wrong there. I liked the peanut sauce and of course with these type of dishes, the sauce is everything.

Service was good. A little slow, considering there was not a lot of customers at the time and they had plenty of workers around. I guess the only time I would come back is to try the desserts and pastries. Hopefully those won't let me down.

I'm so surprised that anyone would give less than 5 stars for their sushi. Literally phenomenal. To give you a comparison, Ken Sushi is my favorite spot for high quality sushi but Umai really takes it for quality and price. 

I got the Sunshine roll, sake nigiri, hamachi nigiri and escolar nigiri. The quality and just how fresh the sushi is mind blowing. The fish melts in your mouth. My favorite out of then all would be the hamachi. I will probably literally just order a whole plate of that next time. I devoured my food in less than 15 minutes.

The Sunshine rolls is nice take on the Rainbow roll except there's spicy tuna inside. Very, very good. I will definitely be back!

that frosting was BOMB! super dope, magnificent, delectable, mouth watering.. and oh yeah tasty! 

it's the cutest little shop ever... tiny tiny tiny though..and that I do not like.. with lots of annoying people in the way .. that is other customers in the way of me eating every  non chocolate cupcake in the place..

I appreciate their approach to customer service.. they immediately greeted me when I entered... then gave me a chance to look around.. I did so .. and when I was ready they came from behind the counter and packaged my cupcake.. they were very well informed about the product.. sooo passionate about it while explaining it to me.. I like that.. 

there are cupcakes and other things.. I bought a red velvet..I ate the icing babygirl had the cupcake.. and I also has a vegan pumpkin spiced one.. both were delicious! I like that they have vegan selections.. especially ones that are truly delicious 

I did eat them on day 2.... and they had endured a lot in that bag before they even made it home.. and were still very fresh the next day

cool thing.. when I left I noticed that you can see into their kitchen as you walk down 12th street... so I saw the guy in the back baking up a batch of cupcakes... I like seeing the process.. so out in the open like that.. it lets you know that they really do make them there.. fresh.. and that they aren't shipped from somewhere else... 

so basically .. I'm IN!

I was at first nervous about what to expect since some of the reviews were mixed, and all I can say is that I'm genuinely confused. I'm a picky enough person that I don't usually dine at buffets, and I was blown away by the quality here. Yes, the price is higher on the weekend when they have lobster and crab legs-- but I think the reviewers who complained about that should think about it reasonably. 

There is a full, all-you-can-eat sushi bar on top of crab legs and lobster. All you can eat sushi anywhere is at least $20. And that doesn't come with the option to enjoy a full buffet with crab, oysters, and lobster, desert, etc. 

I watched the sushi chef at the bar to figure out if the sushi was old, and what I observed is that he was constantly making new rolls and putting out about 8 pieces at a time which were pretty much immediately taken by people. Very fresh.
