As far as the buffet, they seem to put out small portions of each dish to make sure it's not a huge pile of aging food. There was a lady replacing dishes nonstop, so they clearly have standards on how long food can be out. 

Lunch during the week is $9.95, so even without the crab and lobster, having access to the buffet plus all you can eat sushi is an incredible value. My server was super kind and he was clearly working hard. He kept our table cleared and drinks full as we gorged. I will be back for sure. 

*I've been Yelping for a while and know we shouldn't discredit other Yelpers reviews, but I would just add that I think some people have low scores despite the excellent food because they went on a day when they had the lobster and were expecting to pay less. I would recommend checking this place out and knowing the price range options for the week.

(My first review of this place was 5/2008 - I gave them 5 stars at the time. Now that it's 4/2010 I want to revise my review and give them 10 stars if I could)

Oh Yoko! is Cherry Hill's hidden gem. If you are in the mood for friendly staff, a warm and inviting dining experience and food soooo fresh it'd have you believing they sent someone out to catch your dinner just minutes after you place your order... than this place is for you. Did I mention it is BYOB?? Can it get any better than that? Yes.

The sashimi and sushi is literally without a doubt a five star palate retreat. We always find ourselves going there and instead of ordering the rolls we know we like, we actually live outside our bounderies and will ask the friendly staff what they recommend and 5 times out of 5 times they will recommend what is on special. Special meaning soooo fresh it's a sin not to try it because you're missing out! We had sea urchin flown in from japan and received that very morning it was alive and still breathing, OMG it was soooo good. The owners recommended we try it, the staff recommended we try it and I am sooo happy we listened. We also had other recommendations of Sashimi and the filets of raw fish were so fresh and delicately sliced it was as if we were biting into pieces of buttery goodness. Like I said, when we go to Oh Yoko! we never order our usual rolls, we live a little on the wild side and order whatever they recommend and it's worked out for us still 2 years later. 

If you want to taste what real sushi and sashimi should taste like than this is the place. I grew up in a household with a father who went deepsea fishing every weekend so I know what meat just minutes out of a fish should taste like and Oh Yoko! does a really good job meeting up to that. It's a sin to have anyone try to rate this any lower than 5 stars. They are the friendliest bunch of staff you'll be soooo lucky to have met and I am honored to have been introduced to such wonderful food. 

I hope they live long and prosper.

Went here after being on a business trip. Went here and got the lobster burger. Smelled terrible and I don't think it was fresh seafood at all!

The service was terrible. Workers are too cool for school. Very mediocre and one bartender was actually nice

Won't return again with there non fresh food!

Finally leaving a hype review because they rock! We went here at the beginning of all this and they were still rocking it! Making sure we were safe as customers, they had a menu on a screen outside of the business. There were wipes and sanitizer mostly everywhere in the shop. 

They served their full menu but we were there for breakfast. The Bac n egg n ched sammie is a MUST along with the eye opener! They have ice cream and juices too! Hours are 8 AM to usually 8 PM so you definitely could come for lunch, dinner and dessert!

Simply put, Ruth Chris is not what it used to be. If you want a posh meal, there are many other options that will serve your tastebuds and wallet better.

Basically, read Todd B.'s review. His review tells you everything you need, but long story short - the venue sells this place, the service is standard good and the food is mediocre. 

The venue is great because you're in downtown St Pete and there is a good size patio where you can people watch. The interior is your typical chain steakhouse - refined and dark.

The best part of my meal was the Caesar salad! My boyfriend was unimpressed with the steak and the lobster was way over cooked. That should not happen when you are paying over $100 for two people for dinner. 

Why I am going so harsh with 2 stars is because for the price you are paying you could pay the same or less for much better food. The Birchwood has the same prices or less and the food is better and their patio is across from the water. Don't fall into the name brand trap - don't go to Ruth Chris because you know the name ; look at Yelp do better than this.

The name of this place is a bit deceiving but thats okay, hopefully it will keep the crazy crowds away. Lolitas sells wine of course but it is so much more than a market. It is your wine and charcuterie spot and your brunch spot! 

Yes, lolitas offers an awesome under the radar boozy brunch. Of course the mimosas are typically strong and bubbly thanks to the great palate of the chef. The breakfast menu is very limited but it hits the high marks by including both omni and vegetarian options. 

My avocado toast was sooooo good! Lots of thick fresh dreamy creamy avocado on hearty wholesome bread. Lolitas turns a breakfast staple that sounds simple into something artisan.

Inside is cute. It has a fee windows so you get that lovely good morning sunshine feeling when you eat. There are a few small tables and then 1 or 2 long community tables. 

Here is the only honest to goodness downside: it is too small and no outdoor tables. Thankfully the crowds havent caught on, so the small size hasnt been a huge issue if you get there as soon as it opens, but once people catch on i think they will outgrow their loc. No outside dining which sucks so we cant come as often since we typically take our dog everywhere.

Fast, fresh, delicious Vietnamese/Japanese fusion food is what you get here at this cute  spot in Downtown. I came on the recommendation of fellow Yelper Kylie K and she's was right on.

I ordered the tofu Bahn mi and the avocado summer rolls (these are a must!). There's a variety of Bahn mi for both the meat eaters and vegetarians - I really appreciate the variety which makes this one of the best lunch spots in downtown for office lunches. 

I loved this sandwich, plenty of vibrant fresh cilantro, thin carrots and some cucumber (could have used some more of that). The tofu was really razzed up with spices and i think it was sautéed, but I forgot to ask before I devoured it.

They have a variety of summer rolls but I went with the avocado. Huge chucks of avocado! Yay! And the dipping sauce, oh man, I wanted to order a pint to go.

The place is casual, bright and clean. Plenty of spots to eat solo at the window table bar or at a table with a group. 

The service was prompt and friendly. 

I will definitely be back.

For a restaurant to succeed, they need to be great at two things: the service and the quality of food. If they suffer in one, they can usually makes up the slack in the other. Unfortunately, Ampersand 27 failed at both! 

I was there a couple of weeks ago for a weekday birthday lunch with eight others, and we sat for nearly an hour before our orders were even taken! There were very few others dining at this time, many of whom came and left during this period. 

Remember the two things? Well, the service was beyond poor, but perhaps the food would be worth the wait, right? 

Wrong! I ordered the Plain, Simple & Beautiful flatbread pizza (Tomato, Basil, Mozzarella) for $15.00. It was overly greasy, a little overcooked and perhaps too plain and simple....but definitely nothing to write home about.

At the end of the meal, as is customary for large groups, we were each charged the 18% gratuity - unearned by all means, but it certainly explains the waiter's lackadaisical effort. Hooray for all of us!

So, if it wasn't yet clear, I won't be back any time soon. There are plenty of other restaurants in Edmonton that offer better service AND better food! Ampersand 27 has a long way to go on both aspects.

After hearing (and reading) rave reviews about this place, my husband and I were super excited to give the place a try. While I knew this would be 'Asian fusion'--and that I shouldn't expect traditional Ramen--I still left both disappointed and, frankly, disgruntled.

1) The wait: I get it. It was a Friday night, the place was poppin and as Prof Roger K wrote, "exotic fares were being prepared." But we waited an hour and a half. What. While that was not a deal breaker for me at all, albeit a minor inconvenience, what proceeded next was the worst...

2) The service: So, after waiting for an hour+ (and by the way neither of us were upset at this point) we were stuffed at the bar, despite a table for two clearly being open and already cleaned. The hostess rudely tossed down the menu and walked away. Awesome. Despite the chilly welcome, despite another couple after us getting seated at the open table, we were still eager to try the food and proceeded to order the Black Garlic Wings, Brisket noodles, and hand torn noodles. Not a bad selection, we thought. 

3) The food: In fact, the wings took about 10 minutes to arrive and they were spot on delicious. No complaints there. Both sweet and tangy, they had a nice crunch to it without being overly fried. We ordered another round of drinks, happier, much more optimistic than before; after all, maybe someone just pissed in the hostess's cheerios. But then came the next round of

4) The wait: Forty minutes went by. Forty. 4-0. I timed it (I had on my handy calculator wrist watch; and, yes, they still make them). At this point, I was starving. No, literally: I felt my stomach involuting. I was probably catabolizing all my muscle mass at this point. After forty minutes went by, after watching other couples who arrived after us get their food--the same order, FYI--my husband finally got his Brisket noodles. Slightly salty, but not mad. Ha, the noodles, not us. 'We have food now; this isn't so bad. Okay, well, at least one order,' I thought. But no, once his ramen came then came another round of

5) The wait: Yes, folks, it did not end there. Another twenty minutes rolled by without me getting anything: nary a peek at my food nor an explanation from the waitress/hostess/staff/kitchen. Just side-eyes from the surrounding tables, people wondering why my husband was guiltily eating while I had nothing in front of me. Finally, I took about ten deep breaths and calmly asked the waitress about the status of my order. Not only did she snap back at me with something exquisitely curt and snarky she went on to gossip/complain about me to the hostess. Before you think I'm delusional and semi-paranoid a la Remi Malek from Mr Robot, there was no need for me to deduce or even speculate that they were talking about me since they did it right. in. front. of. me. No secrets there, people. It was within earshot. Pretty clear, if you ask me. 

I know what you're thinking at this point, and, yes, I am crazy enough to be spending this much time writing a review; yes, I have dedicated thirty minutes of my life, time that I will never get back, to let you know the context in which I received my mediocre bowl of not-worth-it noodles; and yes, I can't believe I wrote a veritable war treatise on this place, what the heck am I thinking; 

but no, I am not ever, ever, ever crazy enough to go back to that place and re-hash the hipster hell that was Cheu Noodle. Ever. Because at the very least I am sane enough to recognize that the hostess/waitress was very much like my noodles that night: frigid. And a bit salty.


**UPDATE 10/22/15** The owner of Cheu Noodle reached out to me regarding my review and was very kind and extremely professional. While I was not impressed with my initial experience there, he really went above and beyond.

Truly disappointing experience - I had been really looking forward to my experience at Ciro's.  I made a reservation for 915 PM on a Friday night, I was called early in the day by the restaurant on Friday to confirm my reservation at which time I asked if I could move up my reservation to 845 and was told it would be no problem. 

We arrived at the restaurant at 830 (yes we were a little early) and checked in.  They still had me as a 915 reservation and when I mentioned that they had ok'd the 845 time she said that the wait wouldn't be long.  We said we'd go to the bar and she pointed at an open area with available chairs.  We ordered drinks and then waited till 930 to be seated (there were many patrons that went ahead of us while we were waiting). 

When the hostess finally came to get us, she took us a to a small high top table next to the bar, and when we said that we made reservations and were expecting a booth, she stated "Oh well you have to request that when you are making a reservation, most first timers never know it, but you'll get it next time" Well I'm not sure that there is going to be a next time. 

Our waitress was nice, a little overly peppy, but that's fine.  We already had our drinks, so we perused the menus and she told us about the specials. We opted for the Lobster Deviled Eggs, Duck Fat Fries, Slider Trio, and a Steak Special.  

The Deviled Eggs came out first.  There were 5 pieces (so really 2.5 eggs.....) and they were pretty good, but not GREAT and I didn't even taste any chunks of Lobster... 

Then came the Duck Fries, for something that the waitress said EVERYONE loves....I was super disappointed.  Some of the fries were really dark and some light and most were broken into small pieces.  They also tasted SOOO greasy, like they didn't get the temperature right on the fryer.  I sent them back.  The second batch at least came out with full fries and were hot, but still very greasy.  

The Slider Trio was probably the best dish we had.  The flavors were nice, but honestly for $16, 3 tiny little sliders did not fit the bill.  

Finally came the Steak Special.  I expect when I order Steak at a restaurant who charges thirty plus dollars for the entree that the Steak is good.  Well let's say that we struggled to make it through this dish.  The waitress did not even ask us the temperature we wanted for the steak, luckily it came medium rare.  Unluckily, it was like chewing rubber...I have never had meat SO TOUGH before at a restaurant.  Especially one that is supposedly High End.  If it were not for the fact that my boyfriend was starving and we wanted to get out of here, we would have sent this back as well.  Also the steak was swimming in this orange sauce, overloading the dish with sauce is unnecessary if you have a good quality Steak.

The waitress also seemed to be displeased when we opted not to order another round of drinks.  Overall disappointing experience, the highlight of our visit was the amusing conversation we had with the valet and doorman prior to entering the restaurant.

We were expecting a long wait on a Saturday morning. There aren't many places that do a Saturday brunch. To our surprise we had table in less than 10 minutes. Service was great as always. I had the Spinach and Ham Eggs Benedict. I love that their Hollandaise sauce is thick and rich. Delicious! I ate every bite. We were celebrating an engagement so champagne was a requirement.  I'll have to try one of the French toasts on my next visit.

The location is great, especially when seated in the outdoor patio area where we were allowed to have our dogs. It was nice and shaded and the view is excellent. The service is very good. The food was not exceptional however. The clam chowder was lumpy but did have lots of clams and was not over salted like many places will tend to do. The mixed fried seafood platter was bland, the fish had no taste and did not seem to be made from fresh fish. They do feature fresh fish so we made the assumption. I would ask if I were you and choose to eat here.

This restaurant is nicely done and has a cute outdoor patio that allows dogs. The caesar salad was very good. The fish and chips was excellent, so flavorful and fresh was the fish that it did not have to be eaten with condiments. The service is good and friendly. I would have given more stars if my muscles had been good, but the mustard, wine and cream broth was too picante from too much dijon mustard, the mussels were not very sweet and plump. However, I am giving them the benefit of the doubt and rating at least 4.

We ate here for breakfast with our dogs each morning on the pleasant patio in front of the cafe. Great coffee, excellent croisants that are crusty, flakey but soft and buttery inside. The omelets done perfectly moist and flavorful. Great way to start out a beautiful day.

Caffe Aldo has been around for years...and years...and has always been one of the "better" places for awesome Italian (and Northern Italian) food.  

The decor and ambiance is a definite 5-star and the service is always top-notch.  This is a place that you can actually get "dressed up" if you want and you don't stand out (unlike many other restaurants these days).  

They have a great little bar area that is set apart from the dining area so you feel like you're in a little lounge of your own.  They also have banquet rooms for weddings, functions, events, etc.

I actually had my wedding reception here years and years ago.....and a baby shower was given to me at this same place.  I still have the baby but not the husband.  One out of two isn't bad....so it wasn't totally bad luck!

I'm giving Falora an updated rating and review.  My original write-up of our (1-star) experience was enough to get the attention of the owner, Ari, who wrote me personally to apologize.  He explained, in detail, the events that lead up to our experience that night, and--suffice it to say--Falora has had an incredibly rough opening week.  Again, having worked in the industry, I definitely understand the situation.  I get the impression that these past two weeks have been a bit of a learning curve, but the learning is happening, which is a good thing!

After reading my critique, Ari invited my friends and I to come back and have dinner on him, which I thought was very generous and humble.  He knows that he's got some kinks to work out, but he IS paying attention to his customers when they tell him that things aren't up to par.  Some people don't care about feedback, but he clearly does.  I know that I said in my review that I wouldn't return, but anyone who is gracious enough to reach out to his customers and ask for a second chance deserves just that.

We're looking forward to coming back within the next couple of weeks, and I'll be sure to update my rating again.  This time, I'll be able to base it on the food and drinks at the restaurant, instead of just walking through the front door!

THIS REVIEW IS DURING COVID-19. One of the first places my family decided we wanted to get takeout from during this covid-19 pandemic. We waited until May 1, 2020 to order good (yup 1.5 months after the lockdown)

The family decided we wanted that huge pizza I've been telling them about so we made it happen.

Now at that time in May you had to place tour take our orders online (you will need to check if this is still true) the third party app said it would take 35 minutes for the pizza to be ready but in reality it look about 20.

I parked my car, walked over to the man at the front, told him my name and he grabbed my order for me - even offered to help me put the pizza in my car (I have a Honda CR-V and we opted to just put it in the trunk with the seats down lol)

The pizza was delicious! It was actually so large that one slice is good enough. We froze the leftover pizza to eat later and it did great heating up in the oven.

I would come here again, maybe buy smaller pizzas so we could try different flavors but we were super excited and wanted to try out this HUGE PIZZA!

Next time I want to order the pepperoni pizza.

Ever since my company moved down town I've been a glutton for this place! Great lunch - check. Great cocktails - check. Great cookies - check. Great coffee - check.

In fact. The cookies are why I am all about this place. I literally take lunch break walks just to justify the delicious cookies and treats.

Check out my photos to see how beautiful their beet salad is!

Sorry, Starbucks. Pie Lady Cafe serves La Colombe coffee and delicious homemade pastries. My go-to Saturday morning treat. Looks like they're expanding and it should be bigger soon with more room to sit inside. Try a freshly baked scone, all flavors are worth the calories. Surprisingly I haven't tried the pies yet, but I'll report back when I do.

I've only been to Kensington Quarters a couple of times for a libation. I've never sampled the food, so this review is for the aesthetic and cocktails only. My go to cocktail is the Canela- tequila, st germain, and lime topped with freshly grated cinnamon. Wine is available on tap, which is pretty cool! The downstairs bar is never crowded and a great dimly-lit spot for a drink with your date... just don't look behind you if you're squeamish about seeing freshly butchered meats. If you want to spoil your pup, grab some hearts and livers on the way out- they sell as dog food for an affordable price.

Celebrated some good news yesterday with a few treats from cake life and realized that I haven't reviewed one of my Fishtown staples yet! HUGE portions and fair prices considering the portions. If you like lemon bars, try a citrus bar. A buttery cookie crust with a lemon/lime/grapefruit curd, this is like a lemon bar on steroids. The fig walnut scones are a must try (all of their scones are delicious), especially warmed up for a few seconds. Almond, chocolate, and plain croissants are all excellent choices. Savory items like pepperoni pizza croissants are to die for!

Though I still think that Whipped has the best cupcakes in the area, Cake Life has the best variety of pastries and savory items. Flaky croissants, chicken pot pies, even dog treats for the pup... amazing variety of sweet and savory decadence.

I'm on a Fishtown review kick... I can't believe I've never written about Heffe!  The late night hours are great for drunk munchies, especially if you dont feel like walking all the way to the food trucks at Frankford and Girard. The fat man burrito is a drunk's dream. Chicken tenders, bacon, and the traditional burrito fixins. The octopus tacos (Kraken) are a MUST TRY even when you're sober. Stop by for lunch while you're walking through the neighborhood. Convenient, quick, and decent prices make me a fan.

I have been here a few times when the two original chefs were still in the house (Chef Eric and Chef Josh), and this place has fell far from grace.  I'm aware you cannot please all of your customers, but several of our dishes was beyond salty to the brink of not being editable.  I did not want to compare the chefs because they each have their own style, but it's hard when you're paying about $200/person and leave unhappy (I had a party of 3 tonight).  I don't mind paying good money for good food, but tonight was beyond a disappointment. 
Cons:
It's fun to eat with your hands, but when you're asking me to eat ground beef tartare with my hands without warning and refuse to give me a fork?!..brownie points will be taken away.  The beef tartare is not ground all at once and stored in a fridge ready for service..it is ground per dinner service.  Therefore, there's residual beef in the grinder sitting for maybe an hour or so..what does that mean?  When we got our tartare (we were also the last service of the night), yes we saw the man grind the beef in front of us, but it was also mixed with the beef sitting in the grinder from the previous service..my sister and I had a taste of sour beef. We all stopped eating it.  Raw meat sitting in a warm grinder produces harmful bacteria faster!  When you pay $200/person for food, I don't expect a buffet because I know it's a tasting menu.  However, I do expect more proteins incorporated in my dinner that makes it "seem" worth my money. Our proteins tonight consisted of an oyster, maybe 1/2 of an ounce of crab meat, a ham spread (a twist on pigs in a blanket), and a slice (yes ONE slice) of a chewy (in a bad way) duck breast, that's not $200 worth of anything. In our opinion, the nonalcoholic beverage pairings didn't enhance or pair well with the food as it has with the previous chefs..save your $30. We are generous tippers.  In fact, we've always added more on top of the 20% Catbird automatically charges, but the service was pretty bad this time around.  When you're forced to pay 20% gratuity to people who don't want to talk to you/act annoyed when you try to strike up a conversation, ignore you, and leave dirty dishes piled up in front of you from your previous courses..the experience won't be pleasant anymore.  I'm not sure what happened tonight we aren't rude people whatsoever, but it's such a shame to see this establishment make a turn for the worse.  Obviously first timers to this restaurant have a "blast" with Chef Trevor, but honestly I won't be returning to Catbird until a new chef takes over again.

I stopped by here for the first time on a Sunday night at 9 pm with a friend.  When we parked, we weren't sure that the restaurant was open, as we could see that there were no customers inside and an employee was mopping the floor.  The sign on the door said they were open until 10:00 pm, so we forged ahead, expecting to be informed that they were closing soon and they we no longer taking orders.  But we were pleasantly surprised when we were warmly greeted by all three employees present, including the one mopping the floor.  

We were asked if it was our first time there, and then we were givien a thorough explanation of the menu, and how to place our orders.

The service was excellent.  Even though you order at the counter,  employees serve your food and stop by your table frequently to check on things, and to offer refills on drinks.   

Our calzones were a perfect balance of crust, cheese, and ingredients.  Calzones I have had at other restaurants were mostly too doughy, with too much bread and few ingredients.  But these were excellent, the crust was golden brown with just the right amount of vegetables and cheese.  Mine was the Garden, and it contained spinach, eggplant, snow peas, onions, zucchini, roasted garlic, ricotta and mozzarella.   

There is a recommended sauce for each but you can choose any sauce or sauces you would like.  I chose the BBQ ranch which was excellent.  

And the calzones were huge!  I ended up taking home half of mine, mostly because we wanted to try a dessert. 

The dessert we decided on was the Caramel Apple Pie. Even sharing it we could only eat half as it was huge too.  Good thing there are takeout boxes stacked near the soda machine.

This pie featured hot apples with cinnamon, graham crackers and a delicious crumbly crust.  Ghirardelli caramel sauce was on top.  This was one excellent apple pie!  I would stop here just for dessert.

The craft sodas are unique and a nice change from the usual Coke or Pepsi products.  And the glasses are real glass, not paper or Styrofoam.  And the plates are real, too, as well as the silverware which is wrapped in napkins on the tables.    

I'm a fan!  Excellent service, nice atmosphere, delicious food and so many options to try, I will be back soon, and often.

This is the Rouladen (one-day special item) with spätzle and braised red cabbage for $18 at Berlin's Doener, my first time ever eating authentic German food.

Somewhere far far away, there lies a haven...a proverbial oasis where the people are kind, the gravy is thick, and the cabbage is pickled. You may not know how to pronounce what you are eating, but the taste and the smiles lull you into a sense of security. This is Berlin's Doener.

Immediately upon entering, you are greeted by both of the owners and their jovial grins - the wife who runs the front of the house and the husband who runs the kitchen. Can the start of a dining experience at a literal mom and pop establishment be any more genuine than that? The server that took care of me seemed genuinely excited to meet me and the way she spoke about the food was spectacularly exciting. It was because of her that I upgraded my order by more than twice the cost, because when, and I quote, "Everybody here is eating the Rouladen today, it's a fan favorite and if you want the true German food experience, this is the dish to get"....well...you get the dish.

Rouladen is made of thinly sliced beef wrapped around onions, pickles, mustard, and bacon; then positively drowned in gravy. I expected the beef to be similar to a sirloin and the insides to be tangy and flavorful with many interesting textures. I was surprised to find it was all soft and melded together into one overarching flavor that permeated the beef, making the beef more flavorful, but the textures less numerous. It seemed a bit more like a stuffed meatloaf. I do enjoy me some good meatloaf, though, and the gravy added a richness and earthiness to round it all off. My only concern was that it was clearly slow-cooked, but it came out about 5-10 minutes after I ordered it. No idea how they managed that, it the food quality didn't suffer so I had no complaints!

This spätzle was comprised of noodles, chopped into 1-2 inch pieces, appearing to be freshly sautéed in a mildly flavored oil, making them go along very well with the stronger flavors of either the gravy or the cabbage. The cabbage was yet another surprise because the only  "special" cabbages I'm aware of are either sauerkraut or kimchi, both of which are extremely tangy. This cabbage was somehow earthy and had a more subdued flavor - not at all overwhelming like the other two cabbages would have been for inexperienced foodies like me. When I did want a kick, there was a very large container of mustard sitting on the table that called my name.

The establishment as a whole was spotless. I normally don't comment on that because cleanliness is expected but I literally saw not a single speck of dirt anywhere on any surface that I glanced at. Even the bathroom, as simple as it was, was spick and span. I also love how they maximized the very limited space behind the restaurant, making it an actual pleasure to eat there despite the fact that it's only yards away from a major road.

A quick trip to their Facebook, unlike most other business social media accounts, gives you an actual reason to follow the page. Their special dishes, which can not be found on their regular menu and are constantly changing, are a wonder to behold to someone like me who only knows sausage of the Jimmy Dean variety. I don't even know what a schnitzel is, but now I know where to go to find out how best to eat one! I can appreciate that they give the chef this opportunity to spread his culinary wings instead of just having him making the same doener all day!

I am very fortunate to live right behind this gem and I hope to come back many times. They have nailed down many of the tiny details that most other places don't bother to put effort into. For me, that effort makes all the difference and it shows in everything that Berlin's Doener has done. 5 out of 5 quacks for sure!

- Tampa Bay Food Duck

Waiter was rude, cream of portobello soup was excellent, caprese salad would have been good if it didn't have hot house tomatoes, meatballs were those tiny FROZEN ones, thats just not acceptable! The cheesecake was awful. The chairs were stained. 
The pork chops were excellent. Worth going back.? NO!!. I can get good cream of mushroom soup in Kennett Square, and if I wanted a frozen meatball, I would go to Costco. To top it off, we had a $70 gift certificate, our bill was $59. and the guy made sure to tell us the tip would not be included on the certificate. He did not give us the balance, so he got the $11 extra plus the tip!

I understand that this location is going through some growing pains as I don't think they anticipated the volume of business. That being said with wait times being announced as 2 hrs I found it odd that the table next to where we were seated was left empty for 40 mins before people were seated there. Along with other tables we saw empty for long periods of time. 

I've had giordanos before in Chicago but this just didn't hit the spot. 

Best deep dish in indy still has to be BIG Mikes cafe on 96th and college. I would and will suggest people try their pizza before ever waiting 2 hrs at this location.

Like so many others have already posted, we too had a terrible experience. We went tonight to give it a try.


We were seated quickly about 9pm on a Friday which was a good start. After a long wait for a server, a waitress came over and her first question was did we speak Spanish. We said no and that was the end of our service- literally! No other server was ever sent over to our table to wait on us so we got up and left. 

The Spanish speaking waitress never even brought us water for our wait (we assumed she was going to send over another server who spoke English to serve us or at least take our order but that never happened).
Based upon the reviews of others, this is common level of service for the restaurant.

Save your time and just go to another restaurant where you can at least grab a glass of water !

You may not even know Ellie's in there as it is at the end of a shopping center, but once you've been, you'll be back! 
Ellie's is like going to mom's for a homemade BLT lunch or hearty weekend breakfast. 
The menu is large and even includes a Greek touch with Gyros and Greek salads.
The portions are a good size so you may even have some leftovers, like if you go for a breakfast skillet. 
It does have a diner feel to it and you may be served  by multiple people if it is busy. 
A solid choice with quality food.

Let's sum up my night.

I walked in, sat at a table and was told I needed bottle service.  Then I was told I needed 2 bottles because we had 7 people.  I said no and the waitress told me too bad I need to charge you.  I said no way, she went back and gave me my card.  2 days later i get an alert from amex that there was a suspicious 630 dollar charge on my card.  Sure enough, the stole from me.

Last year I visited The Chef & I at their Brentwood location, and was very excited to learn that it moved to the Gulch in January! Yes. We ventured out on a Friday night after snagging a last minute reservation for 7:45 at the counter and were excited to see what they had to offer! 
First of all, the space is amazing! The large open kitchen was definitely the focal point with plenty of seating, but they also have large high top tables and a bar for drinks on the side of the building. I love that its not too big but is a simple, awesome ambiance focused on the action in the kitchen. 
Our bar seats were perfect. There are two different cooking areas and we sat in the middle and were able to interact with both of them, which is something they encourage and was such a cool experience. I love an open kitchen with chef interactions! We were starving and decided that we needed to go with the 5 course tasting with a wine pairing. You only know the main ingredient of the dish and they create an awesome dish with that ingredient. The great thing about this menu is that the main ingredient may stay the same but they create new dishes almost every day! 
We started our meal with a complementary amuse-bouche, crostini with goat cheese and their homemade bacon. 
1st course: Scallops - with onion on a sweet potato puree - Delicious 
2nd course: Pork - ground pork loin with a fried egg and sauerkraut (not a fan) but I'm not big on heavy brauts and kraut
3rd course: Mushrooms - Pasta with balsamic glaze. So good!!
4th course: Tuna - with avocado - delicious 
5th course: Rabbit - Ravioli on a strange salsa type mixture. 
There were two courses that needed work... I really didn't like the Pork dish and left most of it on my plate. But some of this might be personal preference though since my BF enjoyed it. While we loved the rabbit ravioli it was on a bed of what tasted like jarred/canned salsa mixture. It did not taste fresh and had an odd flavor. While those two dishes were a let down, overall the experience was wonderful and the wine pairing was perfect.
I heard they are working on a lunch and late night menu, and am so excited that they are in Nashville proper!

Can I just say how amazing it is that we have so many new restaurants to look forward to? Nashville is on it. 

After being lucky enough to sample some bites at a Yelp event, I was even more excited and anxious for the opening. It did not disappoint. The space looks fantastic. When you step inside it's like you are transported somewhere else and I love the Indian decor and lighting. The vibe is awesome. I could not decide what I wanted to eat, so we asked for some recommendations from our very helpful and good-humored server. First things first:

The drinks. OMG.

I couldn't stop ordering the Rising Star with vodka and coconut milk foam. Wowzer. It was delicious without being overly sweet. If whiskey is more your thing, the Southern Belle was also delicious and a big hit with the guys. Do yourself a favor and at least get one cocktail. 

The food. Double OMG.

Just order the kale pakora appetizer. It's lick the plate good. For an interesting and delicious dish, try the gol guppa shots. MMMM. And lastly. Pork belly....a million times yes. For entrees most everyone tried the desi tiffin which was a very casual nod to the meat and 3. It comes out in a stacked tin and I loved the chicken korma and whatever magic that was put in the cabbage dish was out of this world good. I had the "make your own" dish with paneer and a coconut curry. It was very good, but I definitely was stealing a lot of bites from the chicken korma. Also, the garlic Parmesan naan... order that guy.

In summary....everything here was incredible. Presentation, flavors, creativity. A+ all around. And the service was just the perfect cherry on top. Don't walk, RUN to Chauhan!

There is a lot of potential at Pearl Diver. The interior is gorgeous and well-themed and the outdoor space makes you feel that you are transported to an island. Plus I love the cabanas and the overall vibe is really cool and interesting. 
However, there were some pretty significant issues. First, you have to order at the bar or window connected to the outdoor space. I definitely had more luck at the bar, but just come here planning to wait to order. That alone isn't a dealbreaker though. I'm fine to wait if I'm getting some interesting drinks and delicious food. Unfortunately Pearl Diver didn't deliver there either. While the port to port cocktail was delicious, it only tasted like fruit juice and was very weak. If I'm paying $12 I want it to taste like an adult beverage. I tried the Paloma later and it was better but also very weak and mostly ice. I was excited about the food but bummed when the mushroom and shishito peppers came out with a laughable amount. There were seriously 5 of them on a skewer and the mushrooms were a huge let down and not worth $9 for these items. Luckily the dumplings and dipping sauce were good so it wasn't a total waste. 
At the end of our night we enjoyed talking to the bartender and sampled a shot of the daiquiri which was delicious and what I should have ordered instead of the other fruit heavy beverages I sampled. The bottom line is that I paid $50 leaving hungry and completely sober which makes me grumpy. Luckily I was hanging out with an awesome group of ladies so it wasn't a total loss but I'm not rushing back, especially since it's the new place to be and super popular. Maybe they know something I don't?

We had a party of 4 that luckily snagged reservations on their first night. I absolutely love the interior. It's gorgeous, modern, and left me feeling like I was in a NY or Vegas restaurant (the light fixtures..omg). Plus, I am SO glad they aren't doing the farm to table thing and there wasn't a flannel shirt in sight. Yes!

We had a very tough time deciding on what to order, but started small with the cocktail list. I had the honey and thyme with gin and it was absolutely delicious. The jimberly and southern belle were hits at the table as well. However, be prepared that they are $13.00 each, but also very well made. 

Our server was sure to tell us about the appetizers and sold us on what he called "an appetizer platter" (whatever you do, DON'T order this, but more later) which included short ribs, quail, octopus, and sausage. I also had to try the spicy lobster gnocchi. The appetizers were all good minus the octopus. No one liked it; it was cold and rubbery and we didn't even finish it all. But the quail...wow. Probably my favorite from the appetizers. 

They were out of the mushrooms and trout for the evening, so we all ended up ordering red meat; steak and the lamb osso bucco. All of them were great, but the sides were really outstanding. The crispy sweet potatoes I couldn't stop eating and I didn't even order them! But I can speak highly of the foie gras home fries with garlic mayo and grilled brussels were extremely good as well. All around a spectacular meal. 

With one big problem: 

Remember that appetizer platter that was sold to us at the beginning of the meal? They charged us for each individual item, and the sausage alone was $25. That's right. the cost of an entree. The grand total for our appetizer platter of 4 items (one of which we didn't eat) SEVENTY dollars. You read that correctly $70.00! OUCH. We felt completely duped. In fact, we didn't stop talking about it the rest of the evening. We talked to our waiter and he apologized but then made the fantastic comment: "We were told not to say the price." Baffled, we asked for the octopus to be taken off. He took them off without any push back, so that was nice, but we still were in shock about our bill. Ridiculous. 

So. Prima is great, but whatever you do, don't order the appetizer "platter" and make sure you know the price before ordering!

I had a decent experience at Mortons happy hour, but wouldn't rush back. 

A couple things that I wasn't a fan of:

-NO drink specials. Really Mortons? Give us house wine discounts or something. Even a couple dollars off would be nice.
-Overcooked/flavorless filet mignon sandwiches on the happy hour menu
-Super crowded bar, and we couldn't move into the dining room; didn't make for a high end experience

I did enjoy the crab cake sliders, tuna tacos, and truffle parmesan fries from the menu, and I know the waiter did the best he could with such a packed bar. But our happy "hour" was more like two and we rushed to get to the ballet. 

I liked it ok, but nothing really blew me away from the experience or the food.

BOTTOM LINE: The drink menu is great, the food is better than average, and the prices are average. HOWEVER, THE SERVICE WAS BAD, and I will not be going back, considering that there are so many places these days offering great beer and great food.

DRINKS: Great beer selection that is competitively priced ($6 for most pours - with 16oz for cheaper beers and 12oz for better beers).  Since we came for the drinks, we were pretty happy with this.

FOOD: All-in-all, I thought the food was better than average.

I had the tortellini soup, which was okay, but should probably be skipped.  My fiancee had a side salad to start, which was pretty standard, but not worth the $5.50 price tag for not much to it.
I had the vegetarian panini for dinner, which was so-so (lacked salt and savoriness).  However, my fiancee had the crab cake sandwich, which was more than excellent.  The fries were very good, too.

SERVICE: This really made me unhappy and is what destroyed the experience.  We came in and sat at the bar, and I felt like the bartender was being rude and giving me the cold shoulder all night.  My fiancee and I both thought she was kinda mean and didn't check up on us.  We had never been there before, and we got the impression that a number of other people at the bar were regulars.  The bartender spent almost all of her time chatting with other diners/ drinkers at the bar whom she seemed to know.  At one point, when she walked by, I asked for water, and she just said "yeah sure" over her should as she continued on her way to talk to other patrons for a while.  She didn't even bother to look at me.  Eventually, she came back with just one glass of water.  I figured it wasn't worth it to ask for another one for my fiancee.  The same kind of rudeness occurred when I asked for the check.  She eventually dropped it off, and I had to flag her down so I could give the check back to her with the payment 5-10 minutes later (although I could see her a few feet away chatting with some regulars the whole time).  I left her a 20% tip on the bill, but she didn't deserve it.  She lost our patronage.

They take great pride in their craftsmanship, as a truly great spot should.

Case in point: Garden Shears - a seasonal drink made with housemade strawberry simple syrup. My wife may have had the last two of the season as the bartender showed us the bottle and said it was the very last of it. The notes of basil did not overwhelm. It was a very thoughtful and tasty drink.

The Kentucky is one of their signature drinks and it's easy to see why they sell so many of them. Manattanish with a touch of citrus notes; it really hits the spot.

The Negroni is your basic mixture of gin, Campari and sweet vermouth, but the bartender says he puts his own special twist on it, which was lost on my plebeian palate. Nonetheless, it was well-executed.

Lest I forget the nosh: They seem to switch up the rather limited menu but offer things like chevre and crackers, olives, nuts and, when they don't run out, they have cookies from Sugar Sweet bakery across the street.

They have some beers on tap as well as wine, but if you don't order a cocktail here, you are doing yourself a disservice.

One of the more unique spots in town. Most of these cool places are going in downtown. It's nice to know we have a midtown spot to have a nice grown-up cocktail.

This is hard to explain. I love pizza (who doesn't?) and when I read the menu online I had it in my mind that I just wouldn't like this place because of the limited meat options. I have a special relationship with meat and any place that doesn't make it a star is not likely to be high on my list. BUT, in the interest of expanding my horizons, I really wanted to try it.... glad I did.

My wife and I stopped in for lunch. The place was not packed and we were not greeted when we walked in so we assumed it was seat yourself, which we did. Almost immediately a server came over to us and asked us to move because they save tables for bigger groups. He directed us to a long communal table that had patrons at both ends already. I am not a fan of this format, so right away, this experience is going downhill.

We order the only meat option (the Cura) and I am looking at the El Pato can with flowers on the table. Huh? Between  this and the carafe of room temperature water served with no ice I am really starting to have my doubts about this place.

Then came the pizza... the first bite begin to lift my mood. Each bite of the crust made from imported Caputo flour and topped with sauce made from San Marzano tomatoes, Kalamata olives, sopressata, whole garlic cloves, mozzarella and parmiggiano cheese and kissed with chili oil is toe curling. By the time we finished our pizza, I was back in a happy place (the Peroni I downed with our pizza could also have contributed).

Short story long... go with a group so you get your own table; go for the hip atmosphere complete with a turntable and pile of vinyls to choose from; go for the bare brick walls with wood on display for the wood burning pizza oven; go for the pizza. Just go!

Vodka is the story here. But I ain't talking about that sad little bottle in your freezer you pull out and mix up the occasional Cosmo with. We are talking vodka infused with everything from herbs to bacon... yes I said bacon. How the heck do you even do that? I have yet to have a drink with bacon vodka from Elliott's but you can bet it's on my list.

The drinks I have had I have thoroughly enjoyed: 

Jalapeno Vodka Rita - spicy, limey, salted rim giving it just enough Margaritaishnous... mmm, mmm, mmm. This has become my go to drink here.

Bloody Mary - Your sort-of-standard-but this-is-Elliot's-and-standard-is-for-the-weak Bloody Mary but with hold on... horseradish infused vodka.

I had something else like a Minterini with citrus mint vodka and sweet tea vodka. 
A little sweet, but an ass-kicker nonetheless.

My wife had some sort of a lemonade with another infusion and a Pumpkin Russian (pumpkin infusion) on our couple of visits. All these infusions....  when will the madness stop?

Oh yes, I must mention that their specialty drinks are $3 during happy hour. $3? Are you kidding me?

On top of that, their food menu is almost as inventive. When you see duck on the menu, you definitely do a double take. Duck sliders and duck club were the two I spotted. I did not order them because our server suggested the Buffalo Soldier. Basically a wrap with chicken and buffalo sauce. Seems pretty standard but done well, especially when placed alongside a pile of thin, crispy parmesan garlic fries. These fries are the stuff heart attacks are made of. Tossed in garlic butter and dusted with parmesan... what a way to go.

My wife's dish was one of their signature dishes: pasta with tomato vodka (what else?) sauce made with basil infused vodka and topped with bacon. Sadly, it was just a little disappointing for her. I tasted it and agree.

All in all... originality is key here. There is no other place like Elliott's in town. We will be back... again and again.

I am going to file this whole experience under - not sure what I thought.

The ambiance was what I expected. The decor was not. For being open less than a year, things seemed unkempt. Wobbly tables, dirty windows and, when we entered through the back door, things in the hallway on the floor. When you walk into a place, first impressions are very important. They need to clean some things up. OK... Martha Stewart moment over. Let's talk about food and drink.

If I was not sure about things, neither were they. The beer I ordered (HopKnot IPA) was listed at two different prices: $6 on the board above the bar and $5.25 on the menu. Happy hour pricing would save me a buck. I figured I would be charged the higher price so I chose something a little less pricey for my second beer, a lowly lager. I was charged $4 for each beer. GRRRR...

I ordered the fish tacos ($2.50 each at happy hour), my wife ordered the BLTA flatbread and we ordered a basket of fries to share. They were handcut and the spicy Chubasco mayo was good, but $5 for fries? The flatbread was very rich. The combination of the lime aioli, bacon, avocado and cheese almost ended up being too rich for my wife to eat. I tasted it and my instantly collapsing arteries agreed with her assessment. The fish tacos were good. The fish was crispy and there was a hint of lime in the pico, which is a must. A dash of the Chubasco sauce they placed on the table added even more kick. I hunt for good fish tacos and, in terms of flavor combination, these are some of the better ones I have had.

The wings look imaginative with combinations like coconut/pineapple, pineapple/habañero and even a departure-from-the-beach-theme-decidedly-desert-driven prickly pear. 

Overall, this place has me intrigued enough about the rest of the menu that I will be back. I just hope they can get their hallway and their pricing cleaned up.

I have been DYING to try this place. Let me set the scene... We passed this place on the way to a friend's house and I told my wife, maybe after their party we can stop here on our way home." She says, "OK, we'll see if they are still open"... and to my utter happiness THEY WERE!

We got our food to go and the whole trip home I had to resist the urge to just pull over and start tearing into the food. My jowls ached from holding back the waterfall inside my jaw.

After AN ETERNITY, we get home and open the food. I am not disappointed. I ordered us each a carne asada quesadilla, which the guy corrected me to call them caramelos. Call them what you want. For $3.75, they are little meat filled blankets of love. I made it a point to take as many offerings as I could from the plentiful salsa bar. I am sure they watched in amazement as I left with my bulging bag-o-salsa-bar. Don't judge - I wanted to try it all.

I also had a Sonoran dog. Although I just don't think I am a fan of Sonoran dogs in general, this was probably the best I have had. The caramelos were, altogether, another story. My wife actually said they were too cheesy. WAT? No, they had the perfect amount of cheese and LOTS of tasty carne asada, I adorned each bite with a different kind of salsa, liquid cheese, pickled onions and cucumbers from my bag-o-salsa-bar, Each bite was better than the last.

Long story short - OK you already got the long version - the best $10 I have spent on this amount of food in a very long time.

I find myself writing a lot of updates these days. Maybe it's because, once you find someplace that's good, cheap and fast, you just continue to go back. That's exactly the kind of place Taco Giro is.

The star dish of this place for me is their chile verde. Read about it in my other review if you like... http://www.yelp.com/biz/taco-giro-tucson#hrid:KpZFAIBwnyPxo2MJjMH1Xw

Now, let's talk about their lunch menu. You can get a shredded beef or chicken burrito, wet, stuffed with rice and beans for $4.99. No, that's not a typo. It really says $4.99. If you want your rice and beans on the side it's another buck. Normally, this would annoy me, but even at $5.99, the amount of meat you get in your burrito is unbelievable. It's beyond me how they can offer a meal like this for that price.

The last time I went I sliced off the butt end of my burrito and tasted it. I am a salt fiend. I freely admit it.The next thing I did was surgically split my burrito down the middle to expose the guts so I could add salt. What I saw next blew me away. Not only was there enough meat for nearly another burrito, there was actual beef that looked like it had been cooked by a real person. If you don't understand, it's because I am making no sense. If you do understand, wow you're as twisted as I am, we should hang out sometime . The point I am trying to make is there appears to be actual cooking going on in the kitchen at Taco Giro... the kind of cooking you do at home but spending far more than $4.99 to make the same plate of food. 

IMO, Taco Giro's food, compared to similar places, tends to be under-seasoned but I already made my seasoning preference known. Maybe the lack of salt is not a bad thing as Mexican food in this town can lean the other way, with other places I know going loco with the sodium. The food is fresh and high quality, so take my comments about seasoning with a grain of salt... or two.

OK... I like spicy food. Yeah, everyone says that, but I think I am more of a capsicum head than most. If you have ever ordered something "Thai spicy" you:

A. Are Thai
B: Never made that mistake again

So I will classify this visit under the B category since I know A definitely does not apply.

I ordered the Pad Thai, extra spicy, The girl at the counter asked how spicy, from 1 - 10. I said, "not Thai spicy, but spicy". She offered up a 6, but I countered with a 7. I was skeptical I was going to get a real 7, as many places offer extra spicy, but for Western palates. I got a real 7... and it was worth every scorched taste bud. It not only had heat, but flavor, The ingredients were fresh, it was not greasy and, just generally, very good. My daughter had lo mein, which she said was "really good". We also split a tempura shrimp sushi roll, which was surprisingly good also.

The decor is kind of funky, which is one of the reasons this place does not get five stars. If they can just decide if they want to be fast food or sit-down, it's five stars waiting to happen. 

The other kind of strange thing was that the entire staff sat two tables over and feasted on a table full of food while we were in the place. I really can't decide if that's a good or bad thing, I mean is it tacky or is it a good sign that they are willing to eat the food they prepare? 

All the items we had were $5.99 apiece. They offer no lunch specials, but with reasonable prices like this and good food to boot , I'll be back. Maybe I will go for 8 next time.

CIBO has excellent Italian sandwiches served up by a friendly staff.  I've been back several times now trying the Chicken Toscani, Chicken Fagioli, and the spaghetti and meatballs. All were extremely solid, and you get a lot of sandwich for your money. You won't leave hungry! It's also a joy to eat in, the deli has a great New York style decor and any time you go in you'll hear old Brooklyn jazz standards playing over the radio.  There is definitely something to be said for chowing down on spaghetti and meatballs while listening to Frank Sinatra.

I've eaten at this Mellow Mushroom several times.  Food is always good, and up to MM's quality. I appreciate the vegetarian options on the Mellow Mushroom menu.   I love the old building it is in.  The beer selections are super.  I highly recommend eating here.

This was a highlight of my last trip to SB.  Normally I'm not much into fancy places but this place seemed more small and bistro like and the fact that they had some vegetarian options peaked my interest. The person I was with was not vegetarian so this place seemed perfect. 

First off the ambiance of this place is really cool.  Kind of dark interior but very modern and small so you felt super comfortable.  Also the service here is really good.  They staff are all very helpful to explain the menu and go over what each dish was made of and suggestions of their most recommended dishes.  They have a good selection of beers and wine, I didn't see any beer taps but the menu had over 40 different kinds some local and some international.  I decided to go with wine since it seemed to pair better with the dishes they offered.

The menu is very eclectic in that they have everything to exotic dishes of sweetbreads to bone marrow, some fish and seafood dishes, and what my eyes were on which were some vegetarian and even a few vegan offerings.  The dishes are all unique and there seemed to be something for everyone to chose from.

Now the menu is kind of small in the restaurant but they actually make more items that you need to ask for.  Case in point I had their dish called Fuel de Brick which is a vegan phyllo dough stuffed with  farmers market vegetables, red quinoa and other things.  They make a version with goat cheese also if you want.  This was  a very unique dish and was beautifully presented.  It loved the texture of the crunchy crust and the inside which had a lot of flavor even though it was very simple.  It came with spiced candied carrot puree to go with the dish which was excellent. I also had the beet salad which comes with goat cheese which I normally don't eat but I got it on the side to sample.  The beets where really good and the goat cheese was probably the best I've ever had, it was super mild and creamy and went well with the beets.

Overall hats of to this place for a great time and it was reasonable I thought considering how upscale it was.  Hope to come back and hope they add a few more veggie options because the ones I had were excellent.

DT Santa Barbara drives me crazy.  The kids who hang out here are up to no good.  A bunch spoiled children.  Shoppers walk around like they need to frenetically spend their 1000's of cash in their designer purses and wallets.   IF I'm going to set foot down here it better be good.

Thank goodness that Green Table has opened up, they are keeping me sane in DT SB.  Green Table is a very health conscious restaurant that doesn't just cater to vegans but they provide nourishing juices and food for an affordable price. 

First off the staff who work here are beyond nice.  Like 10 stars of niceness.  They help you with the menu, make suggestions, talk about transforming people's health in the area.  We need more people like this in our fragile world. 

First thing you need to do is check in and get your free dessert.  I could not help myself with just one and I have a zero sweet tooth.  I could not believe the choices here.  The Matcha balls are amazing.  They have a strawberry banana bread, delish.  Brownie is also rich and awesome.  You can't go wrong with any of the deserts.

Next is the food  and drinks they serve.  I tried the spicy lady juice with berry macha and a side of ginger shot because spicy is never spicy enough for my taste buds.  I don't think they charged me for the shot probably because that's how nice these people are.  It was super tasty.  I also got the raw wrap which had a dehydrated burger in a coconut tortilla with all kinds of fresh veggies.  When I saw the wrap I thought I would need to order two to get filled.  Wow how wrong I was with this little guy.  Each bite was so much more filling than any veggie giant burrito out there.  It is a cold dish so if you don't like raw foods then you might not like but I loved it.  They do have more normal dishes like a lasagna dish that has goat cheese that is made with almond noodles.  I heard it's very popular dish.  They told me that they try to vary the menu so it's more inclusive to people's different tastes.  Very cool idea IMO. Just make sure you ask because they do use cheese in some dishes that can't be modified. 

Thank you for making me sane in Santa Barbara.  See you next time.

I've had mixed feelings about Handlebar at their other location downtown but not here.  In fact I think this is my go to spot to get coffee drinks as it's consistent and I'm rarely let down.  I also like the outdoor seating here and I'm never rushed so I can get some work done or just sit out in the sun to enjoy life's little pleasures. 

This place reminds me of a like a Napa Valley specialty foods shop and coffee bar all in one.  If you want to check out some of the most advanced brewing equipment I've ever seen before this is your place   They sell interesting bottles of red and white locally made wines.  The produce they sell is pretty eclectic and is fun to brows through.  I saw pasta, different balsamics, gluten free flours and brownie mixes, bags of rice,  alternative milks in cases, and even some locally made vinegars of sorts.  They also have a whole line of their cups and mugs.  I bought one as I like the shape of it and it fits in my car smaller size coffee cup holder:)

My go to here is an Americano and I add an extra shot with half water and half steamed almond milk. I ask for cinnamon on top as I go nuts for cinnamon in everything.  Normally they use 2 shots for their medium coffee so when you add an extra shot they double that taking it to 4 shots total.  Trust me it's worth adding the extra shot.  I've also had their Dirty Chai and Macha, and Charcoal Latte and  all have been outstanding.  They do get busy and have a lot of staff working so they have once in a while messed up my order but that is rare.  Also note is I recommend you ask for extra hot if you're like me and like to have your drink stay warm for longer. I have had to one time have them remake my drink because it was lukewarm:(  I also bring a thermal mug to store mine so it even lasts longer but that's just me.

Service is always pretty efficient here even though lines can go out the door.  But there is always tables so that's good and you can also kill time browsing their stuff while you wait for your drink.  Also note their is some interesting food options that are inside the coffeehouse, most are not vegan but they have a Avo toast and salads you can modify.  They house a pop up of modern Asian Korean food but have never checked out but saw they make a maitake mushroom Bao that looked interesting.  

If you want to find good quality coffee/tea drinks that are a little spendy but well made and a fun place to hang out then this might be the place for you!

I thought when I went to this place that there would be tons of vegetarian and vegan options because of all the reviews.  Turns out people are slightly wrong and ordering things without knowing what's in them.  That said if you ask the right questions they steer you to what they can make for you and when they do that they deliver big time.

First off this place is located in the public market which houses many small joints of different foods such as Thai, sushi and others.  It's a small little spot that has only a few tables and a bar area in front of the kitchen .  Basically you order from  the menu and then go to the salsa bar and then pick a spot and wait for your order.  The line was pretty long when I was there but it moves pretty quickly.  

The menu is a pretty simple but at the same time kind of hard to read in the sense that I still had to ask a lot of questions.  I first wanted to get the cauliflower tacos because people raved about them but then I was told that they are vegetarian but not vegan so I asked for a basic burrito with veggies.  Turns out the rice is not vegetarian so I was almost ready to give up and go to one of the other stalls.  The manager came over and said that they make a vegan quesadilla  with veggies which was odd because it had no cheese in it.  But was happy to try it out and got some chips to go with it.

Got my number and went directly to the salsa bar and man did these salsa's look fresh and spicy.  They had a green one, two red ones one called cruda and one called La Mugro which looked roasted.  They had  a habanero salsa that was labeled extra spicy.  They also had a peanuts, pickled onions and limes. 

Chips were really fresh and salsas were off the hook good and spicy.  You can see them cut up the tortillas before they make the chips which is pretty cool.  The quesadilla I got was a large blue corn tortilla filled with different veggies and jalapenos and then topped with beans and tomatoes and a spicy salsa that was great.  It really was more of a giant taco and it was pretty messy to eat but it was 5 star good.   So good I am still thinking about it a week later lol.  

The only reason for the 4 stars was to put the vegan items on the menu and force a little pressure on the owner to veganize the rice and the cauliflower tacos so there are more options for us veggie folk.

Thank You!  It's definitely Corazon Cocina...thump thump..

I have been to backyard bowl numerous times when I'm in SB and always had 5 star experiences.  What I normally remembered is the acai being being super firm but yet creamy meaning it didn't melt quickly and the toppings added were both fresh and plentiful. Finally I remembered great service of passionate young people enthused with there jobs.  Well this place has really missed the mark this last time and the final product left me a bit disappointed on the experience overall. 

First off when you walk in there is only one menu on a pedestal at the entrance and so only one group at a time can even see what's on the menu.  This becomes problematic when there is a family who is on the fence whether they want pitaya or acai bowl or just a smoothie.  While they were holding everyone else from ordering the entire staff were doing nothing so I went to where the lady was taking orders and asked for another menu since I knew what I wanted just forgot name of the bowl.  Sorry she said there are no other menus. No sorry no asking how she could help nothing just a blank look.. wtf.  So I said give me that bowl with more acai in it.  You know??  She replies that all the bowls have the same amount of Acai.  Had to push further saying that they used to have a bowl with double the packets of Acai..?? Like you don't offer that anymore?? Finally the light bulb went off and she said oh the backyard bowl yes that has more acai but you only can get a large?  Yes yes that one and yes large is fine.  Then I'm like having to drill her on what's in it as I wasn't looking at the menu.  Basically she said it comes with strawberries blueberries and bananas with goji berries and bee polen on top.  Asked to sub out bee polin and replace with nibs instead.  Paid the $13 which seemed high but whatever.

Finally the menu opened up and I glanced at what I ordered and noticed they put honey on top of the bowl. Forgot to to take that out so went back to change. it kind of would be nice for them to ask you what you want versus the customer have to drill down their  orders...

Bowl came out and first thing I noticed was tons of strawberries but hardly any blueberries and no goji berries at all.  Went back again to ask what where the gojis are and got a basic ok give me your bowl and I'll put some on top.  No sorry anything else just put a spoon of them on top.

Took a bite and overall the taste was good but the consistency was much more watery than I remembered.  It was melting pretty much immediately as and felt I had to rush to eat my bowl.  Felt the bananas were over ripe and it needed more blueberries and nibs.  By the time I finished the bowl the acai was all melted.  

Still not t a horrible bowl but really felt disappointed with the way the service and bowl was not up to the past 5 star standards. Let's hope this is an anomaly as BB was always my to go place for all things acai.

A friend of mine has been telling me for a while about how this is one of her new favorite spots to eat, so we decided to go here for lunch together this week.

It was noon on a beautiful Friday when we arrived and luckily there was outdoor seating available. The patio seating here is great, especially on a nice sunny day. They have big umbrellas over the tables, fans to keep cool and a fun corn hole/jenga area to keep kids and big kids alike entertained.

We were sat and greeted right away. The server was informative, friendly and happy to answer all our questions. They had a ton of local craft beer on tap, but my wallet liked the sound of a $2 draft happy hour, so I went with a cold Yuengling.

Since my friend is the pro here, I let her guide the way on ordering the food. She insists the brussel sprouts and ahi tuna nachos are the bomb here, so that's what we got. I also ordered the grown up mac n cheese, despite her telling me that the 1st 2 things we got would be more than enough food.

Brussel sprouts came up first. It was a "miss" for me. I love brussel sprouts, but these were burnt to hell. It was like a black pile of mush, and for $9 for a SMALL portion, totally overpriced. I'd skip those next time.

The STAR of the show was the ahi tuna nachos. Holy moly those things were DEEEEE-LICIOUS. I love me some ahi tuna, and these nachos were fabulously made. A portion bigger than your head, piled high with chips, guac, seaweed salad, ahi tuna, seeds, etc. They were some of the best nachos I've had, hands down. 

The mac n cheese was so-so. It had too many veggies in it for my liking (even though I do like veggies, just didn't care for these). I could have done without that too.

All in all, service was great, environment is really nice, happy hour specials are excellent and the ahi tuna nachos are take a bite and go to heaven good!!! 

I would come here again, now that I know what to order - or what not to order. A great addition to downtown PH.

Yep, this place is a two thumbs up winner. 

I absolutely love Thai food and was excited to see a place with such great reviews had opened up close to my house. My mom and I came here for lunch on a sunday afternoon and grabbed a spot at one of the booths along the wall. Right away we noticed the nice bright, airy feel and the decor was appealing as well. The server was friendly and did a good job considering he was the only server for every table in there.

Our server brought by menus for us to take a look at and we noticed that they offered a lunch combo option, including soup, small thai roll and a wide variety of options all for $7.95 This was impressive to me because even most restaurants that DO offer a lunch special don't have it on the weekend, so that was a definite plus.

We started off with a Mexican roll just so we could try the sushi and see how we liked it. Theirs was spot on -- perfectly crunchy, great flavor, very fresh. We scarfed that down in 2 minutes flat. Next came our meals. My mom got the veggie delight with chicken and i chose the rama sama long (or is it rama song long, or rama lama song? I can NEVER remember) which is chicken in peanut sauce with rice, cabbage, carrots and broccoli. WOW! It was so tasty, reminded me of the "amazing" chicken from other local Thai places.

Between the soup, sushi and a few bites of my meal, I was stuffed, so had enough to bring home for leftovers. The server kindly boxed them up for me and brought it back to my table, that wins big points in my book too.

We thoroughly enjoyed our experience, between the ambience, service and fantastic Thai food. All of this was included for very reasonable prices. I will most definitely be a repeat customer here.

I had hoped to walk here from my hotel - a nice 2 mile stroll.  Exercise, sightseeing, and art; perfect right?  Except for the rain that foiled my one woman parade.  Instead I got a quick cab ride with a blink and you'll miss it view of the Rocky steps (you know I was going to run up them and do big champion arms at the top, right?), some streaks of green lawn, and a few fearing for my life "Philly drivers are insane" moments.
The museum was well worth it.  The lobby reminded me of the one at the Met, while the museum itself could've easily been one of the dozens I visited in Europe.
I agree with Heather wholeheartedly on her advice for the special exhibits - although I'll warn that weekdays are no better.  The exhibits should really be limited to  a certain number of people at a time rather than a flow, and I think if they changed the way they sold tickets they could manage that.  Say, only 30 people can buy tickets for the 1pm slot, and they have, oh 20 - 30 minutes to go through, and then the next group can go at 1:30 and so on. . . . life would be grand.  Shoving past people once you'd like to move on while they look at you like you're the rudest thing they've ever seen (as they shove back to try to take the space your body left open before someone else can) is not my idea of fun.  I love Frida's work and it is so detailed sometimes that I really want to get up close.  Plus, I'm not a huge fan of crowds.  That said, the exhibit was great, and I even bought a bunch of souvenirs at the end which I don't typically do. 
The rest of the museum was lovely, although I only had about 15 minutes to kill before it was my turn to line up for the special exhibit so I didn't get to see as much as I would've liked.  
** aside - Thanks to David for noticing (as always) that this is review #500.  Thanks to the museum and its kick ass Frida exhibit for making such a happy review memory.  I'd also like to thank my mom and dad, without whom none of this would've been possible.  Thank you to my . . . * music swells and drowns out typing . . *

As I begin this review, I'm not sure I can still identify the worst part of last night's dinner...the lackluster service, the underwhelming culinary offering, management's thinly veiled indifference to our dissatisfaction, or that I was robbed of one of a precious few date nights I get each year. I think of everything, which I will list momentarily, the one thing that rose above all of this was the server being argumentative with my husband over his order. Listen, doll, if anyone is going to give that man a hard time, it is me. Over the last 21 years, I have earned it and finely-honed my skills, so I say to thee, "how dare you?"

And, now, some comments:

* Yelp, I gave just one star, not because they didn't deserve two but because the 2-star rating indicated that my experience wasn't DISMAL and it was. "I've experienced better?" Yes, I've experienced a better treatment of beef at Krystal. At 2 a.m.

* Mike Kelly, you should be ashamed of yourself. Your family worked hard to bring this restaurant to life and survive in the cutthroat food industry for 7 decades. Take some time away from leaning on the bar and watching a replay of a Devils-Kings game from 2 nights ago to walking around your restaurant. Visit with your guests and when one goes so far as to indicate that the evening is not going well, delve a little deeper and find out what's going on. Walk through the kitchen throughout the night and let them know that you care and you're watching. Have someone come in and give those restrooms a thorough cleaning. Watch as appetizers are being sent back and entrees are leaving tables with more than half of the food still on them. Mike, that's YOUR name out there on the sign. Defend it. You were here in Nashville before any of those other steakhouses. It's your birthright. Bring back the Jimmy Kelly's that Nashvillians know, and love and respect.

* To our server, whom I did not get your name but I think you have to stand out as one of, if not the only, female servers at Jimmy Kelly's. Was last night your first night? Just tell me that. You greeted us and tried to take our drink orders. You asked if we would like some wine when we hadn't been given a wine menu yet. When I asked if you had sweet tea, you answered "yes.  Well, it's unsweet and I can bring you some sugar." Baby, this is the south. Tea is sweet and it's equal parts -- 1 cup of sugar to 1 tea bag. Plain and simple. When my husband complained that his steak wasn't right, did you know right then that you had keyed in the order wrong or did you discover that later? We all make mistakes but man up and accept it when you do. My husband gave you a tip last night. Partly because he's a nice guy. I also suspect he did this merely so we could go and salvage the last few minutes that we had a babysitter. Here's my tip for you:  find one of your fellow co-workers in a white dinner jacket and follow him around for a week or two. Learn the ropes from these veterans. 

* To Fred, another server at the restaurant who was assigned to an adjacent table.  We watched you throughout the evening, smiling and happy and providing top notch service to your table while we floundered in the corner with our gal. We watched you be attentive without hovering. We watched you glide in a beautiful minuet as you showered that other table with drinks, playful banter, corn cakes and impeccable service. And at the end, when everything blew up, it was you who stepped in and showed concern. Not our server. Not the house manager. And not that guy whose name is on the sign. No, it was you, Fred, who apologized for our experience and who implored us to give the restaurant another chance. You said you've been there for 45 years. My, the stories you must have. It was a pleasure meeting you last night.

* To the cow(s) that offered my husband's and my steaks last night, I'm sorry. I'm sorry they did that to you. A little salt and pepper goes a long way but they denied you.
