* And, finally, to Jason and Valerie, the hapless diners in last night's saga. We were given MULTIPLE red flags and dismissed, scoffed and laughed our way past each one. We chose to be impressed by the restaurant's website and ability to make a reservation online rather than heeding other reviews here on Yelp. We walked through a near empty dining room on a Friday night at 7 and didn't think a thing about it. We didn't take the cue from our server that this evening was doomed when she was giving pretty clear signals from the moment we sat down and placed our drink order. And, still, when the 1st appetizer was sent back, instead of asking for the check and cutting our losses, we persevered. We pushed on stubbornly. Hopefully, we'll be smarter next time.

I visited La Teresita on a quest to find a good Cubano sandwich. I bookmarked them based on a friend's suggestion. We arrived on a Monday during lunch hour and all dining areas were packed! (Note: There are at least four dining spaces on the compound!) Luckily, extra booths opened up in the ground floor dining room. We got our name in and obtained seats within minutes.

I ordered a small Cubano sandwich, Tostones, and a Ham croquetta. The Cubano was satisfactory. The bread was pressed to my liking (nice and flat) with a good ratio of ham to cheese. Definitely better from other Cubano sandwiches I've had in the past. Tostones were on the greasy side but mainly decent. The ham croquetta was probably the worst thing I ordered here. The croquetta was slightly shorter than a mozzarella stick and the breading was burnt. The ham filling overall was lackluster. Save your money and skip the croquetta. Honestly, I wasn't over the moon on my first visit to this restaurant but I'd like to give them a second chance and try an entree (Boliche Mechado) in the future. If you're in the area and looking for a cheap eat, La Teresita is worth the stop.

Everyone who knows me, knows my love for Mexican food... so when I saw the amount of ratings on this place, I was excited to try it out. Unfortunately, this place wasn't up to par for me. 

 I'll start with the positives:

-Loved their chips!! Hot, fresh, light and salty!! The salsa was sooo good and I loved their traditional guacamole. Slightly OD on the lime but it was fresh and delicious!
-My mom ordered their build your own steak tacos...the steak was amazing!! The seasoning on it was great and it came over grilled peppers and onions! The sides were avocado, sour cream, cheese, spicy sauce and pico de gallo. I would definitely recommend this dish! She also order a side of rice and beans which I was really impressed with. 
-I wasn't too impressed with their chicken tacos, it just fell short. Thank God for the spicy sauce that came with the steak fajitas or I wouldn't of ate them at all. 

Now onto the negatives:

-I understand it was a Saturday night, but a 2 & 1/2 hour wait for a table of 3 at 6:30pm is ridiculous. I felt most of the tables, people were just hanging out after they ate. They should think of an effective way to reduce the time. 
-Their menu is beyond limited. Salads, enchiladas, guacamole and tacos is the gist of it. They do have some appetizers and 3 entrees (the entrees I wouldn't consider traditional Mexican dishes). They're missing a bunch of plates: fajitas, chimichangas, flautas/taquitos, sopas, and tamales. I personally would remove the entrees and consider these as good alternatives. 
-Nothing in the decor screams Mexican restaurant...they could literally close down, change nothing, reopen as a new restaurant and it wouldn't make a difference. Even the margaritas didn't come in their traditional glass!

Overall, some of the food was good, our server was quick but not very attentive, but the wait here isn't worth it at all.

CALLING ALL FOODIES!!!! This place is HEAVEN on Earth for food lovers!! I can't believe this past weekend was my first time here after being to Philly a few times!! Anything you could possibly want to eat in one place!! I did my homework beforehand since our time was limited and I wanted to make sure I tried nothing but the best!!

-Beck's Cajun Cafe: Hands down my favorite!! They were serving bright and early...couldn't pass up on trying the award winning Trainwreck sandwich...WOW!! My mouth is salivating as I type! I also tried their fried mac & cheese balls which were delish!! Staff was friendly and helpful!! 
- By George!: BEST Stromboli I've ever had!! We shared the Italian, phenomenal! 
-Valley Shepard Creamery & Meltkraft: shared the Somerset Grilled cheese which was good. Awesome for cheese and olive lovers!
-Old City Coffee: much needed booster after feasting!! 
-Flying Monkey Bakery: AMAZING SERVICE!! So friendly and sweet!! We actually came here Saturday and Sunday! Not a dessert person but my daughter loved their whoopies! 

Sadly, I could've done without :
-Sang Kee Peking Duck's shrimp dumplings...sauce was great, but wasn't a fan! 
-Fox and Son Fancy Corn dogs was terrible!! I went with the cheese and jalapeno corn dog...really wish I hadn't...sauce was gross and jalapenos were dried up and tasteless. 

But hey you live and you learn!   

TIPS:
-COME EARLY!! Some places don't start serving their heavier foods till 10:30-11am...I still recommend you get here as early as possible to avoid the lines. I got to the terminal at 8:30am and was able to grab some food, eat at a table with no wait, digest, and repeat once the the other places started serving. 
-Crowd starts coming in around by 11am, making the table seating limited.
-Come with a friend(s)!! It's so much more fun when you can try out a bunch of spots and just split it with friends. 
-A lot of the merchants are closed on Sundays (Amish thing) so if you're coming on the weekend, Saturdays is your day!

Reading terminal,  until we meet again!

Great ambience.  Amazing food.  Felt like a nice family dinner with the chef/owner walking around (along with his adopted dog and nice wait staff). Romantic music (mixture of Louis Armstrong and Frank Sinatra).  Open kitchen with wonderful smells wafting through! We ordered vegan puttanesca and vegan eggplant Parmesan followed with vegan cannoli.  Best eggplant Parmesan ever!  (Even better than my non vegan days of eggplant parmesan).  Definitely going back to this restaurant!  Oh also everything is available gluten free!

You know, it's so typical of New Orleans people to not give a place a decent rating because they don't serve fucking alcohol. It's like, do you not know how to eat a fucking taco unless you're halfway drunk? Sure, you may like to have a cold cervesa with your enchiladas sometimes. So what do you do? You go to the friendly bar next door and pick up a beer, supporting two local businesses at once. Congrats. 

Popular, equally priced New Orleans restaurants and brunch spots should really look to this place for some tips. They have the dining trifecta that New Orleans hot spots don't really understand. Taqueria Guerrero has, Friendly and attentive staff, great homemade fresh food, OH and get this, their restaurant is clean! You go to brunch spots like Gott Gourmet, Slim Goodies and Surreys GD and the staff is rude, inattentive and the dining area is just plane dirty.  

This place is a hidden gem in the midst of a lot of popular restaurants with not much to account for. I highly recommend this place on all accounts.

Like being in an
Abusive relationship
I keep going back

If you cook at all, this place will leave you tearing your shopping list into thousands of pieces in frustration. In the past year I've developed a laundry list of complaints about South Square, and yet I still go once a week. It's the proximity and convenience factor. Simply, it is the closest grocery to me that's larger than a 7-11. They have the essentials and it's okay if you're trying to stock up on canned stuff. They also have a deli counter with a decent selection of meats, and a cold case with some great cheeses and meats from DiBruno Brothers. Otherwise, you're better off getting a zip car and going to the Pathmark on Gray's Ferry. It's cheaper, larger and higher quality.

So, why I don't like South Square. It smells, sometimes like wet dog, sometimes like vomit. Always faintly, but always noticeable. Their produce selection is okay, but they always opt for huge, fake looking stuff that comes from California, Florida, or wherever they make the garish window decorations for Pottery Barn. They don't sell large packages of meat, and every time I do buy meat there I am underwhelmed with the flavor and quality. It's always bland!

The big problem that I have here is that every time I have gone in with a small grocery list (15-20 items), 3-5 of the items on my list were nowhere to be found. Simple things like dry yeast or feta cheese. These are not specialty items by any stretch. And yet I can never seem to find a few of the items on my list, meaning I have to change plans for what I'm making or go somewhere else to supplement. Easily the most frustrating thing about South Square.

And yes, it's more expensive than other places. Whole Foods is a better deal, I swear. The Fitler Square Farmers Market has better meats and produce for less money that hold up better all week than the stuff they sell here.

The end result is that I will still go here as the need arises for things I KNOW they have like pasta, canned items or pizza cheese. I will also continue to gripe mightily about it to anyone who will listen.

Horrible service !!!! Staff are bitches and act like you are bothering them. We left at half time for a LSU game. 
Bartenders were rude, slow, unappreciative, had to keep asking them to wait on us. 
Burgers shrunk in size 
Never again will I go back

Last Sunday my boyfriend and I went looking for a yummy brunch. We live close to mid town and there are so many great places to choose from. I wanted to go somewhere new.... We googled and Yelp'd. This place came up with more than four stars so we figured BINGO
We arrived at nearly noon. Plenty of parking right in front of the restaurant too... I was getting excited. We walk in and it wasn't busy. No one waiting in front of us, numerous stools open at their bar area AND three open tables. First timers we were all smiles taking in the atmosphere while we waited to be seated. We were promptly greeted and told them it was our first time. We were hungry and eager to 'experience' the place. She asked how many and of course we answered two . She told us we could sit at the bar.... the bar had stools with no backing, looked very Uncomfortable & UNSundayBrunch like. We are Foodies and just love to relax and explore menus and new places. We asked if we could sit at one of the three open tables that were calling our name...lol. The answer was No.  I was shocked! I questioned why we were unable to sit down at an actual table. We were told that they might get a four top and so we could not take any of those tables since we are only two people. Again she tried to get us to sit on those uncomfortable stools at the bar OR we could wait for a table that only had two chairs. To me, that was it! That seemed like very greedy thinking. Because we are only two people, we aren't good enough to be seated. They wanted to bet on four people coming in that door and would rather seat them. It totally turned me off. I was so disappointed. If they had any professional sense at all, they would have invested or SHOULD invest in numerous two top size table that are easy to move together OR apart to accommodate CUSTOMERS. 
Instead, we discovered Daughters Cafe! OMG!! It was amazing, unique AND ... they were busy and the only table open was a six top.... GUESS Where We Sat?!?! THE Freaking Six Top... NO PROBLEM not snobbiness and we even made friends with another couple that asked if they could share our table on the end. Creme's mistake was our good fortune! Perhaps they shouldn't be so greedy & perhaps they should rethink their dining room! 
We won't be back... there are too many options in MidTown to choose from. This place is a big thumbs down.

This is a rare 5-star review from me.   This is the type of place you would expect to see on the East Coast.    From the outside, it's more than a little non-descript.   It's in a strip mall at the southwest corner of 75th and Shadeland with Starbucks and Donato's.   The only reason I even found out about it was because it's right next to a title company where I had to drop a check off.

From the outside it looks like one of those greasy spoon fried fish joints that you see around town.   However, from the moment you step inside, you realize you've come across something special.

For one, the place is hoppin' at lunch.   Try to get there before noon or expect to stand in line to place your order at the single register.

Then you see the massive seafood cases that run the length of the space.   Inside there are all manners of fish, crab, lobster, shrimp, etc., as well as several containers with their seafood salads and dips.

And the ostentatious display is not just for show.   The time I was there about half the patrons were just buying fresh seafood and/or seasonings (these are littered around the cases and on shelves).   This place is half-fishmonger, half-diner for sure.

On the wall behind the seafood cases, you will see the menu.    It's a seafood lover's dream.   Lots of different fish sandwiches, and fish entrees.   I'm not sure they serve anything but seafood here (for you non-seafood folks).    On second thought, I may have seen a chicken dish.

If you prefer, they will prefer any of their fresh seafood to your liking (not sure of the pricing for this service).

When you're ready, step up to the register and order from the owner himself.   Really friendly guy who has a passion for seafood.   In fact, he will special order any fresh seafood for you.

I ordered the lobster roll which came with 2 sides.   I chose the mac & cheese (I asked the owner how good his mac & cheese was and he said it was his mother's recipe so there's no turning back after that) and collard greens (you rarely see those on a menu in Indiana).     After you pay, he gives you a number and you find a place to sit.   After a few minutes, you're in culinary heaven.

The lobster roll was absolutely perfect.   The bread was grilled - crunchy on the outside and soft and chewy on the inside.    The lobster was obviously super-fresh, not too much mayo, and the perfect amount of celery to add just a bit of snap.

The owner was right about the mac & cheese, too.   Creamy, cheesy, and the macaroni was not overcooked.

I will definitely be returning soon to work my way through their menu.

I'm going to make a statement that is a really big deal for me. Restaurant R'evolution is the best dining experience we've had in the United States.  Alinea in Chicago is more of a culinary adventure.  Spoon in Dallas certainly offers a memorable and beautifully crafted seafood experience.  I've done all the Daniel Boulud, Tom Colicchio and David Burke establishments in NYC and they each have their memorable qualities.  Love eating in Charleston as well as Etch, Husk, Margot and Lockeland Table in Nashville. We've done the best of San Diego, LA, San Francisco, Napa and Sonoma. I love the work of Bobby Flay and especially Marc Forgione. While I lived in Southeast Asia I had many memorable dinners.  We've certainly had meals in France and Italy that would be at the top of the list for food alone. However, for us the efforts of Chefs Tramonto and Folse and their staff will be the standard that all future fine dining establishments are held to.

First, there was a mix up with our reservation.  When they realized it was their mistake they immediately went to work to make sure we were not disappointed.  When they said they could seat us I thought, "two top by the bathroom". NO, we were in a lovely dining room looking out on to the courtyard of The Royal Sonesta Hotel.

We were seated side-by-side in a banquette...instantly making us (gay couple) the Stars of the room. In a matter of seconds we met "our staff"...all three of them...Alejandro, John and Luke. However, in the course of the evening we had no less than eight servers, including two managers and Chef Folse making sure we were having a perfect evening.  (Side note) As we departed Alain Ducasse at The Plaza Athenee in Paris we were asked how we enjoyed our evening.  We responded," the food was only second to the beauty of the servers".  Well, not all of our servers were runway model beautiful (they were in Paris) but their work was like a well rehearsed ballet and their demeanor was the pinnacle of professionalism.  The food was absolutely standard setting in composition as well as flavor profiles.  We had two appetizers, a salumi board, two entrees and a bottle of wine and the check was only $200. I've spent a lot more money for not nearly the dining experience we enjoyed.  Who has ever heard of a jar of duck liver mousse that was like Thai Silk being $5 and coming with four condiments, nuts, dried fruits and grilled bread...WHAT?!?!?!  We are still reeling over what an incredible place this is.

Y'all. Go to this place. Seriously. I've heard amazing things about it so I've been wanting to try the food here for a whole year and I finally made it. And boy was it worth the wait!

They have so many options - everything from cookies to tres leches, chocolate cake to quesitos, HUGE loaves of bread to guava pastries (my favorite!). They have tons of different sandwiches (their Cuban sandwich is absolutely amazing - probably the best I've had). They have meat pies, empanadas, Cuban coffee - you name it! Everything is extremely reasonably priced so that means you can get lots of yummy treats for relatively cheap.

They have quite a bit of parking. It's not the easiest to get into but dang is it worth it! Right now, they're only letting a certain number of people in at a time so there's a line outside but it was a nice day and at least it gave us the time to decide what we wanted to get, right? All the staff is wearing masks and masks are required to go in. Once you've ordered, you go back outside to wait for your food to come out. It was really busy when we went and it was still pretty quick.

We couldn't even wait to get home before we started sampling the goodies we had bought. It was so yummy - there aren't even words.

Trust me, just go here and thank me later.

This place is AMAZING!

I went for a late lunch and was not disappointed. It's not the fastest place to grab a bite, but it's worth the wait for sure. With as many people as were in there, I thought it would take a long time, but I ended up leaving in about 15 minutes with a yummy sandwich in tow!

I wish I had taken a picture of my sandwich, but I was way too excited to be delayed. I got the Monte Christo, which is a double decker sandwich with ham, salami, Jarlsberg cheese, pickles, and their signature mustard sauce - piled high and grilled to perfection. It was huge and hugely delicious!

You can get sides (pasta salad, potato salad, chips, etc.) and dessert (cupcakes, cake slices, cookies). They also have salads if you're looking for something a little healthier.

I didn't get it this trip, but their cake is incredible - just a plain vanilla cake with chocolate frosting. There's something incredible about a simple classic done well, and Wright's has that down pat!

The place is easy to find and has tons of parking - the parking lot was packed when I got there, but still found a spot!

I can't wait to go back and try something else on their extensive menu!

Cafe Adelaide has been on my list of Brennan's restaurants to visit for awhile, so I decide while not go during their highly recommended recommended. It was my birthday and those 25 cent Martinis just seem like too good of a deal to pass by. As soon as I was walked in I was greeted by the hostess with a jingle bell Cafe Adelaide necklace and promptly seated. 

The restaurant did not disappoint in regards to excellent service, ambiance and cuisine. My waitress brought a piping hot loaf of French breach within moments of me being seated. I tried the Commanders Martini for lunch with my meal. The sweet blue martini packed punch and I would definitely order it again. 

I ordered the Lemongrass Drum Succotash for my entrees. The fish was masterfully prepared and tasted excellent. The succotash was composed of local root vegetables and I did not enjoy it. I'm not a fan of beets and I the beets to overpowering. I also found the succotash to be quite bland.

(pre-COVID)

I've always had a pleasant experience here especially during Mardi Gras season. Their chargrilled oysters are delicious and there seldom is a large wait time. I love how attentive the staff is and of course the free bread.

Every dish I've had has always been pleasant.

I'm excited they've now opened up to have 25% dining so I'm certain I'll be in to give them my support.

PS- be careful the freshly baked bread is super addicting.

WTF. Finally a coffee shop in the city I now know of that is not only open late but serves coffee and sandwiches into the night. This has been one of my gripes moving to New Orleans as I missed coffee spots that were open beyond 8pm. Sometimes you need to work, work, work, work, work as RiRi would belt out.

The cold brew is superb and I love how there's outdoor and indoor seating.

Prices are super reasonable and if the weather permits make sure to sit outside!

Damn Sofia, I had such a great time at brunch that I needed a few days to figure out how to properly give y'all justice. My sister was in town visiting with one of our family friends and we were all in the mood for a hearty and rich in flavor brunch. We wanted a mix of a fun and great environment, amazing and decadent dishes, but the casualness of wearing jeans and a sweater.

Clearly we weren't asking for too much lol.

Well Sofia came to mind and after showing them a few pics from yelp (woot woot) it was finalized that this was our brunch destination for that day.

We had a bit of a late start for brunch which worked out in our favor because we were promptly seated. Our table started off with a round of drinks including a fresh grapefruit juice mimosa, and some bloody mary's that were the right amount of spice!

For those of us who may not always be in the mood for a typical brunch item, they offer many of their signature dishes WHICH I SO APPRECIATE.

If y'all have a hardcore sports fan in the group assure them their game can be streamed here as they have plenty of tvs all around. The bar area is really beautiful and a great spot to enjoy a drink and an app.

Before I talk about the dishes, I have to give y'all some deets on the resto itself.

Sofia is a living altar to Sophia Loren and it's everything. The Andy Warhol moment of her eating pasta is my spirit animal and how I myself want to be captured. There's so much homage to her and her iconicness. That beauty of hollywood and class is something I wish was still around but I digress.

There's also a pizza oven that looks like a living art installation and found out it was actually imported from Italy. BAD ASS. I creepily walked over to where they make their fresh pizzas just to see the process and it's super neat. You really can taste the difference on the crust alone because of this oven. Kinda like a lifesize sculpture tbh.

Anyways back to the food!

Order the garlic bread. Then order a second round of garlic bread. This bread was so delicious I wanted to cry when we kept killing the plates. Compliment it with an order of their meatballs. Best starter plate combo.

The pizza was delicious and always go for a margherita.

The table was in full carb mode. So we opted for the blue crab risotto (fave at the table), cacio e pepe (proper dish staple) and the bolognese. Each dish featured a proper flavor and were delicious.

We all loved the dishes and our server was amazing. Thanks Tedrine!

A cute little coffee house off of Magazine St within close proximity to Whole Foods. They support a lot of community endeavors by featuring a community wall where you can glance at all of the local happenings and shows. You can also purchase most of the artwork on the walls and they conveniently list the artist and price.

There are a few baked goods to enjoy if you're hungry but I honestly enjoyed the coffee a bit. 

I really enjoy the outdoor seating and it's so calming and the large trees outside! If you have a perfect weather day make sure to sit outside.

I enjoy this tiki bar quite a bit and I enjoy the bites and drinks. Latitude 29 was my very first tiki bar experience in the city courtesy of Joi. The drinks are unique and I really like the plastic stirrers they put in their drinks. I can't wait to go back when it's possible and show them so patronage once able to.

I've been adding this location of Revelator to my rotation of coffee shops to work out of and for in-person meetings within the city. I'm an iced coffee junkie who pretends to be in Zoolander with his iced latte amongst all the iced orange mocha frappucinos! 

Revelator's iced coffee game is strong and will make you want to become a lyricst and say something dorky like Revelator Coffee Percolator. (IDK if they offer that style of coffee btw)

For those of us who like a little flavor in our life and want to spice up our life, you need to try one of their in-house syrups. They're always rotating and you should give them a try. They currently had a honey cinnamon, vanilla, [something] cake, and another option I couldn't remember.

I personally like mixing the honey cinnamon and vanilla with an oat milk latte because it taste like horchata.

There's plenty of seating and the wifi is strong. You'll also find two gender neutral bathrooms for use here.

If you're in the area I highly recommend swinging by!

Their grilled cheese. Ugh just so damn cheesy and filled with goodness. St. James uses Hook's 2 year aged cheddar on sourdough. The perfect crisp in every bite. Comes with salad or chips for your side. 

I totally recommend adding protein to your sandwich for a small fee. I've done it with bacon and prosciutto and my personal favorite is with prosciutto. The saltiness of the prosciutto gives it a nice touch.

Right now during the pandemic they have created some outdoor dining which I really hope they keep!

I'll definitely be coming back to St. James when I'm craving a grilled cheese.

LUCA eats is perfect for lunch and breakfast and I have gladly sent my friends on a guilt trip to pick up food from here. Everything tastes delicious and the owners are super sweet. You can't go wrong here with a to go order. Check my original review for my continuous 5 star experience.

I'm a fan of DDSB (District Donuts) and am spoiled enough to have quick access to both of their locations on Magazine. The one near Whole Foods is more of a to-go location as this one has proper seating including a bar top to sit down.

They not only offer coffee but plenty of savory and sweet options.

I love the donut creations here and the face you can grab a full bakers dozen or simply one donut and all of their orders are packaged properly in a little to-go branded box.

Ordering is super easy and their fried chicken sliders are worth checking out as well!

Solid local spot and happy to support them.

----
Re: COVID-19
They are offering options to ensure proper practices of social distancing so reach out ahead of time. I super appreciate they are offering a campaign to send donuts to healthcare providers and those at the front line. Check out their instagram page for more details. Snag a few donuts for yourself and send a few to those who are on the front lines currently.

Thank you District Donuts for what you're offering.

After a mouth-watering plate of Surrey's shrimp and grits, my friend and I were walking down Magazine St and came across some eclectic yet colorful rugs.

We were walking around them when all of a sudden a guy outside the shop informed us we could walk on them. (BTW we soon learned this rugs are meant to be there to capture folks' attention). As we passed by we soon realized it was an ice cream shop and being the true fatties we were we decide to head inside.

The same gentleman walked behind the counter whom we soon learned was the co-owner of the place with his cousin.

On the opposite end of the ice cream is a mini market where you can purchase beer and liquor to go. You're not allowed to drink it inside due their class of liquor license. 

They also serve sandwiches and a few other items but our main focus was their ice cream!

He was awesome enough to let us try multiple flavors including basil, Oreo, and white chocolate mint. The home run for the both of us was their raspberry pop tart and it was the best!

They're super passionate about their place and I'm so glad we decided to walk in.

My review is solely on the pool experience and for a quick $15 entry you gain access to their "backyard" which has lounge chairs, a large pool that can comfortable hold a plethora of folks, a food/drink cabana, pool-side service, showers, bathrooms, and a jacuzzi. (I believe there's a sauna but I can't guarantee it)

Drinks and pool food were very reasonably priced and I had no problem paying whatsoever.

It's a great way to spend a day underneath the sun and a place I'm certain I'll be visiting again sooner than later.

After attending a Holiday Soiree, we needed to continue chatting business and decided to hit up Longway Tavern. Lucky for us we were able to grab a spot at the bar quite easy since it was later in the evening during a weeknight. 

Morgan F and I decided to opt for the Old Again Cocktail, a bourbon based cocktail, with Apple Jack, sugar, and bitters. I seriously could've knocked back like 4 of these because it tasted like a boozy apple pie. The touch of fresh green apple slices also made me think I was healthy as I shamelessly munched on the garnish.

Since we were getting a tad hungry we placed a random but successful tasting of their signature bread and lardo butter, as well as, their Chocolate Dessert.

The butter. OMG the butter was divine. I wanted to just scoop it out and eat it with a spoon. I'm not sure if that's too much but by-golly was it delicious. You can also order extra bread (totally recommend it) but be aware you'll get charged. The bread is made in-house and complimented the butter perfectly.

Now the highlight of my visit was dessert. I have a sweet tooth like no other and I will always be that person at the table who will grab a dessert when everyone is trying to leave already. I'd apologize but I'm not sorry...

Their Chocolate is a mousse based desert and reminded me of a gourmet, deconstructed smores. Every bite had me wanting more. From the roasted marshmallow to the pieces of the smokey graham cracker, you'll go crazy for it too. I totally got a spoon and cleaned out the edges of the bowl to get one last bite.

If you're in the FQ for any reason I recommend coming here for cocktails and a small nibble!

One of my favorite spots to place an order for delivery and it's for my all time fave dish, french toast monte cristo. It's savory and sweet and has all of the most important food groups a foodie wants. Carbs, protein, delicious flavors, cheese, and more carbs. Grab extra jelly and just know you're mouth and belly are in for a delicious treat.

Situated on Magazine closer to downtown and French Quarter, this is a great spot for folks whether your local or playing tourist in New Orleans. This location of Mojo is a lot bigger than their location on Freret but still the same great coffee and vibes. Mojo has one of the best iced lattes IMHO but perhaps it's their use of oat milk and their in-house signature syrup of vanilla.

I was stationed at this spot for a few hours and had the chance to eat their hummus flat bread. There was a plentiful serving of shaved cucumbers and carrot with the spread. Personally it wasn't for my taste but I can see a lot of folks enjoying this!

Looking forward to trying their mermaid bowl in the near future but by golly, come give Mojo a shot!

A delicate little shop located in Jackson Square. A beignet is a classic dessert which is fried dough slathered in powdered sugar. 

Yes it is a touristy spot. 
Yes the lines are stupid crazy. 
This is one of those spots where you just have to try at least once.

The tables are open seating so if you see one treat it like the Black Friday specials and grab it because seating is scarce! 

I recommend grabbing a bag of beignets with their hot chocolate and sit on the steps adjacent to this shop. 

If you're not planning to sit there there is a to go line on the side.

This review has been sitting in my draft inbox for way too damn long. 

Oh Chef Nina Compton,

Thank you. Thank you for sharing your beautiful mind with us. Thank you for letting us indulge in your creations. Thank you for helping shape the city.

I first tried CL a few years back when I was in town for work and we reserved a tasting for about a group of 12. We honestly said we'll take Chef's recommendations, gave our allergens, and away she went.

It was beautiful. The spread was gorgeous and so varied. I remember taking bites and finding out what the dishes were, floored I had tried so-and-so.

Chef Compton knows her stuff and there's a reason why folks make this a destination of places to eat from out of town and locals alike.

I've been here during HH a few times and it's great to get her signature bites while enjoying a cocktail (or five) at the bar.

*must add to your foodie list!!!

King Cake King Cake King Cake

I don't need to go into a full story because their cream cheese cheesecake is a blessing for your tastebuds. You'll have one slice, say one more, and before you know it you find yourself scooping up the bit of cream cheese on the box with your finger.

I'm not ashamed to say I've done it. These king cakes can be ordered in advance but place it once they open up for reservations. If you want one in a last minute crunch they're available in some spots around the greater New Orleans area; however, you can wait in line the morning of and hope you snag one or three of them (max you can snag).

If you haven't had their cheesecake I'm sorry for your loss...

Solid spot if you're in the area and around for breakfast/early lunch. I've been to their other location but I recently had the chance to enjoy their french toast king cake and it was not only beautiful but delicious! Big of the Toast family and their menu is divine. It's a beautiful spot to enjoy a meal and then explore the quarter.

#thankyouthursday 

I have to say. CCPW is still one of my fave pizza spots throughout the city. Their pizza combinations are EVERYTHING. And that's that I've had them drunk and sober so HAH!

The bbq pulled pork one is probably one of my fave creations ever. I can't get enough of it. It has cinnamon apples, provolone, mozzarella, and baby ray bbq sauce. The savory and sweet combination is divine.

I probably grab 3 slices (they're hella big) whether I'm sober or tipsy. That's how good it is.

They're really good for catering services as I've also used them for large scale events. They're pretty passionate about non-profits and I'm thankful for their community endeavors.

I'm crossing fingers they one day open up an Uptown location.

Amazing service and adaptability from Lula during COVID-19! Earlier this Summer I had reached out asking if they could accommodate a larger table while it still being respectful of the city guidelines.

They were superb and had us in a socially distant area. Food was superb, drinks were flowing (their gin drinks are SUPERB), and the service was on-point.

We were allowed to bring in our own cake which was really nice of them.

Some things that still stand out to me are the blueberry glaze ribs, crawfish queso, and fried pickles.

I'll definitely be back!

I've been sleeping on La Carreta and also how am I just now finding out about this spot?!

So I have to yell for the folks in the back. Use the Yelp Check-In Offer! Better yet use the offer and ask for the bean dip. It's a bowl of queso with refried beans in it! Mix it around with your fresh tortilla chips and hot damn you'll be delighted. Now cheese is an important food group for any diet (don't fact check me) so make sure to order this alongside their queso fundido (melted cheese in a mini skillet with big chunks of chorizo). The queso fundido is oh so gooey and drips everywhere. JUST THE WAY I LIKE IT.

Ask for extra bowls of chips and salsa btw, you're going to kill them very very easily.

Now they have a happy hour that's pretty competitive y'all. We went on a Sunday and they were offering $4 margaritas that had a nice punch to them. I'm not sure when exactly it ends but we went later in the evening so I'm fairly certain it's at least until 6/7pm. I had their frozen margaritas with fresh mango and I'm craving one right now as I'm typing this.

The bar is actually set up pretty cool as it's actually a converted produce truck so pay attention to all the details. I also found it fun how they placed all those frames on the wall.

If you're a sports fanatic they have plenty of tv's around so you can catch your team of choice.

I ordered the barbacoa tacos with black refried beans and Mexican rice. My plate was absolutely delicious!! I ate everything off the plate and contemplated ordering more.

I'm officially giving this my stamp of approval to help with my Mexican food cravings as it's one of the closest things I've had to the food back home in El Paso, Tx and San Antonio, Tx since moving here.

An update is due when you catch yourself drooling over the thought of their wing combinations, don't blink an eye for delivery orders or smile everytime you pass by their restaurant. I love the flavor offerings and the chance to do a double down( (that's what I call it lol) and can get your wings wet and then add a dry rub or another sauce on it. These wings are freaking delicious and everyone needs to try them. Great I just drooled over my laptop typing this... I'm ordering some this week.

What more in life do you need other than fries and pies? Aside from a cocktail in hand of course!

I'm  a fry addict and will always make room for them. So when we were inside the bar and saw someone munching on fries I immediately put on my detective hat and had to find out where they got them.

Thankfully I was told they got them in the back so I, without much work, got my group to head out and order food with me.

Whether you have the tipsy munchies or you're simply having a foodie moment, y'all need to come here. I ended up getting two orders of their hamburger fries and was not disappointed. Wasn't planning to order the second one but realized I made the mistake of sharing with my friends and couldn't have them all to myself. Every bite had a heaping amount of burger meat, cheese, lettuce, literally the works. Your tastebuds will thank you.

I need to come back and start trying the rest of their menu.

If Mais Arepas utilized a food delivery service, I WOULD BE SCREWED. Do you know how often I'd be eating here at home. There wouldn't be any self control.

I'm obsessed with their menu y'all. This slice of heaven serves some of the best Colombian food you'll ever grace your mouth and belly with. You'll stare at your plate and cry tears of joy. You won't be polite at the table and have someone else take the last bite. You'll most likely order a second plate of something because one wasn't enough.

That is how amazing Mais Arepas is.

During COVID-19. they require reservations ideally (although they do allow walk-in's for super small tables ie 2 people) and masks must be worn throughout the establishment. Their team does  a great job trying to make dining as safe as possible!

May I also add that two signature cocktails will get you feeling A-OK and I'm not complaining.

As for the food, you really can't go wrong with anything here. Order extra maduros, chorizo and papas bravas. You can thank me later. My fave arepa is the mechada.

I've had the luxury to dine in at Mambo's, grab drinks on their beautiful rooftop bar that overlooks Bourbon St., and have utilized them for catering and large to-go orders.

Y'all their prices ARE RIDICULOUSLY AFFORDABLE. Best part? The food is well worth more and you're getting it for a steal.

Their gumbo, charbroiled oysters, carnival pastas, and a few other dishes are delish. What I respect and appreciate so much about Mambo's is how attentive they are whether it's dining in-person or working with them for catering needs.

Don't let their location fool you, it's a restaurant worth exploring and it really doesn't feel like you're on Bourbon.

Solid spot and right now during COVID-19 they're offering takeout and delivery.

Time to update!

Had the chance to visit during COVID-19 and I was very pleased with the safety regulations the entire team implemented. Everyone was wearing masks, all tables were socially distant, and they were cleaning in-between diners.

I went with a friend and had some small bites and champagne. They actually have a champagne bottle for $20 and it definitely paired nicely with their creme brulee.

I've had a few visits pre-covid and my updated review was long overdue.

Whether I'm under the weather or simply had a few too many drinks the night before, Pho from Mint will always make me feel a bit better.

I've had a few different variations and have had it dining in or to-go. It's always a delicious moment. As it says within the name, this is definitely a little bit more modern than the traditional presentations of Vietnamese dishes. But my goodness do i crave it often. The broth is so tasty and the servings are plentiful. I also appreciate the way they package everything for Togo orders.

You also have to try a lychee mule and get your mind blown away.

I've had a few of their small bites including the pork steamed buns with pickled carrots. Make sure to grab those.

Being able to grab pho at the 8 o'clock hour with a late night craving is everything for me. I'm not sure why I haven't had Le's before but I'll def be back! My to-go order was ready in about fifteen minutes and there was plenty of ample parking. 

Ordered a large rare steak pho with extra protein and the broth was delicious. As with any pho takeout order you should always reheat the broth! The broth was the star of the show and they followed all instructions which was greatly appreciated. I'm not a big fan of onions and they made sure not to include them.

They make their baguettes in-house and I made sure to order one on the side to dip into the broth. So light and fluffy. I'll be back when I need a warm hug in the form of food.

Damn I'm sorry Courtyard Brewery. It shouldn't have taken me this long to write a review about y'all. You are a total mood and one that I'd wish I could relish in any day, any moment, any reason. Your beer selection slaps so hard (in. a good way).

I love the outdoor space and how it feels like you're drinking at a friends house. So laid back but inviting for some great conversation.

Whether it's grabbing a beer to go or to hang out for a bit. Courtyard Brewery you never dissapoint.

This review needs some major updates but please take a look at my original review to get the full picture...

Ok. You know it's time to revamp your review and give it a facelift like the Bravo stars do with botox because it's long overdue and it doesn't truly reflect how you feel on the outside.

Faubourg deserves five stars. I'm addicted and it's bad. I can't get enough of their food and pretty sure I'm just now making excuses to find a reason to swing by.

The kitchen is open late which is a score but honestly the food itself holds up on its own. I'll continue being a loyal patron with many more visits to come.

Solid spot if you're in the area for a quick bite during the afternoon. Make sure to take advantage of their daily HH from 3-6pm which features beer, $5 cocktails, and select small pizzas for $7.

Their garlic knots are actually pretty fresh and it comes with a bit of fresh garlic!

You can build your own but I do enjoy their Saltimbocca which has garlic sauce, chicken, prosciutto, lemon juice and spinach + capers.

Their house rose is $8 but a solid pour.

Overall enjoyed it but I am a loyal patron of the Audubon location.

Definitely a destination drive if you're coming from uptown but it's so worth it!! Parking is limited so be patient and you may have to take a lap around.

I had an ube latte and it was so good. The flavors here are unique and it's definitely a social media spot with their neon sign.

Ube reminds me of birthday cake flavor so I was all for it. You'll definitely have some rich flavors kicking down your taste buds but I loved it.

I'm a Felipe's junkie tbh. I've been here after work events, for HH, and have even uber eats a few meals from here for various reasons. It's consistent and always has me feeling happy. Their frozen mango margaritas are LIFE.

They make all of their own purees fresh in-house and you can totally taste the difference.

I love how easy it is to order and they make everything right in front of you.

Take advantage of their mini quesadillas and add some chorizo to it.

It's a solid spot of mine and one that I frequent quite often.
(Hello queso with chorizo!)

Take your experience at Vals with a grain of salt, they're in their first few weeks of opening so there are always going to be growing pains. It's exciting to see them in the neighborhood, but I definitely can see the love and appeal of Vals for the city in the future.

They are doing their best to ensure COVID-19 safety practices. No reservations are allowed ahead of time, there is a checkpoint station, "no masks, no margs" rules for entry, and tables have a decent amount of space between them.

I enjoy the ability to have a cocktail or beverage at the drink window whilst waiting for your table. They have some patio tables available solely for drinking which was a nice touch.
////
The gentleman on the evening of Friday, August 21st at the "cocktail window" was a little condescending  and had an attitude that really wanted to make me take more of a sour approach. 

During these times though, it's already hard for local businesses to stay open, but I suggest to the management team at Vals to remind their employees they are not working at a gastronomic-based restaurant in Paris, Mexico City, Toronto, London, New York, or even Los Angeles for that type of attitude.

It's a little off-putting when it's your first time there discovering the menu and your first impression of the service is him scoffing about your drink inquiries with simply questions like what type of beers do y'all have and if the frozen margaritas have any fresh fruit purees.

Just a heads up it's quite common to have fresh mango purees and such available in restaurants with Hispanic/Latinx based roots, as well as, Dos XX as a beer option. 

The refreshing watermon juice cocktail was DELISH.
////
Our server for the table was divine and wonderful, I have to say. We felt bad since she had so many tables to oversee but understood the scenario. Just expect some delayed times between serving and a few more minutes to check out. 

Food is all great, just know the menu outlines the prices and not the qty. It was a good chuckle at the table. Every food item is a la carte, and is very similar to ordering at a sushi restaurant. You "tick mark" what you want to order and everything is brought out to you as it's ready.

Be aware though substitutions and such are not really encouraged, I do wish they were a bit more detailed on their menus for ingredients included. After dining though, I'll make sure to note to avoid the heavy use of onions on the tacos.

The tacos, charro beans, tostada chips, elotes, and queso fundido were all delicious. Not a big fan of all the onions in the queso fundido, but it was refreshing to have them serve it the proper dishware with a charred film.

I'm definitely going to have to give them a second try for an overall opinion, but I'm not opposed to it.

A great lunch spot that will sure to please you! Make sure to start with their hummus with the fried cauliflower and pomegranate sauce. It is so dang tasty and the table will love it.

Seating was fairly easy during their lunch hour and there is street parking adjacent to Lebanon's. Decor is stunning and take the time to adore the wall decorations.

I really enjoyed the stuffed grape leaves which had basmati rice, beef, and vegetable inside them. As for my main dish I decided to go with a kabob plate that had a few different meats.

The beef shawarma looked delicious and I will definitely be grabbing that dish on my next visit.

Must try if you're in the mood for Middle Eastern cuisine!

I appreciate the concept because I'm very familiar with the idea of a gourmet build-your-own-salad spot (they also sell wraps and a few other items), but dang the price in ratio to the salad itself is a bit extreme.

I had a salad in a to-go container come out to over $20 and the toppings weren't all that fresh. The pears were wilted, scoops were super small, and the variety of toppings was lackluster. If you're going to charge this amount which I don't mind paying I expect a wide variety of toppings. There are a few other concepts who charge about $13-$18 a salad with double protein and it had UNLIMITED toppings.

Even upon getting into line I stressed it was my first time here and there was no initiative to explain everything to me or how I'm going to pay for a base of lettuce to say and then get charged per scoop. The customer service here was lackluster and it even came off like they were doing me a favor...

BTW -- Paying for protein per scoop is not an issue with me. The scoop size is though.

I've been to places like Lemonade and Salata plenty of times in my visits around a few cities in the states and you definitely get more bang for your buck with a wide variety of toppings, unique offerings, and the produce is just way more fresh.

It's a great idea but I'll hold off from really coming back here.

I did like they had roasted sweet potato though!

Put me in a setting that'll provide live music and enjoy some signature craft beers and I'll be certain I've died and gone to heaven. The location of TBW is signature and I love how it's in a location that's so industrial and raw. It's a gem and a sense of a reward once you arrive at Tennessee Brew Works.

The patio in front is beautiful with dark wood and steel structures. As a double decker patio, you can find plenty of seating inside and out. Immediately as you walk in you'll be basked in the sounds of Nashville's live music scene and the artists TBW features were fantastic! Pretty sure my friends had to drag me out of the scene as I couldn't get enough.

For those that have a thirst to quench you'll find a bar downstairs and up. Their flavors are fun and unique which they take great pride in their brews. It's possible to grab a tour at a small cost and the tasting room is situated inside the brewing room which is a score! From board games to darts you can get lost for hours as your sipping on a hop and grabbing a bite to eat at the brewery. My favorite was the Southern Wit ( A Belgian White Ale) which had a great palette of flavors but they have a beer for your personal preferences.

You truly can't go wrong with Pizza Dominica! Not only can you place an order for delivery through a third party service; however, you can enjoy your food for carry out or now dine-in (since it's COVID and all).

I love their garlic knots and the burrata dipping sauce.

Their pizza sauces are delicious and I'm definite I'll be back.

I needed to get my Italian fix which was long overdue and I like to tell myself that carbs do not exist on the weekend; although, my waistline tells me elsewise.

My friend and I got there later in the evening and we were lucky enough to score a table without a reservation. This place was packed and from their photos on Yelp, I knew I was in for a treat.

We started off with calamari which had a nice crisp within the breading. Their red sauce had a nice flavor and between two people we cleaned the plate. What I loved most about Vincent's is how personable the staff was and how attentive the upper management was. Our waiter was a little overwhelmed with some minor hiccups but it wasn't anything that spoiled the experience.

The two dishes we enjoyed was the seafood medallion dish yet we upgraded it to feature veal instead of eggplant. There is a difference of sauces served between the featuring of veal and eggplant. I loved the veal and it was so easy to chew into. Our other dish for the table was the lasagna which is a staple for the restaurant. I loved both dishes! These dishes both came with a salad but there was a slight misunderstanding so I wasn't able to get one. By the time we were able to grab our waiter's attention I honestly was willing to build my appetite for the main course haha.

Not sure if the table was supposed to be served bread or not but we didn't get it. 

I'm definitely coming back and can't wait to show friends and family from out of town when they come visit. There are a few dishes I have on my "must try" list!

Unlike Michael Jackson, Willa Jean can be my lover any day y'all!

I had the pleasure of checking out this bakery/restaurant for lunch with a friend and we were quickly sat down during lunch traffic. This open space restaurant has great natural lighting and I enjoyed the stainless steel meets Southern Kitchen aesthetic.

If you're looking for a few baked goods then you can go up to the bakery counter and order. The lunch menu has a wide variety but I was craving a burger and boy did they not disappoint. The burger was so juicy and flavorful that I had to pace myself from scarfing it down in mere minutes.

The appetizer that everyone must try is their cornbread! This was honestly some of the best cornbread I've ever had. Definitely check out WJ if you have the chance.

Have had the pleasure of hanging out at Bacchanal on multiple trips before I moved here and now that I live here, it's on my frequent rotation list. There's something whimsical about this spot and i honestly have a great time every visit I make here.

You can select a bottle of wine to enjoy on their outdoor patio that's covered with trees with plenty of shade, not to mention, under the sounds of some amazing local talent with their live music.

The music is what steals my heart each and every single time. The artists and bands are so unique and you'll love hearing them in the back as you're catching up with friends and family.

If you don't like wine or rosé, you can grab a cocktail or beer at their full liquor bar on the second floor. You can access it outside from the staircase.

If you're not bent on purchasing a bottle (they're super reasonably priced btw!) you can always order by the glass.

Don't forget to select a few cheeses and build out a charcuterie board, which they present and make for you. Also love they bring it out to your table.

Always make sure to tip the live music and help support the arts. Many of them have venmo so NO EXCUSES!

Tip- if there is a long ass line for the bathrooms outside, sneak upstairs and use one of the bathrooms. They're for everyone and anyone and aren't labelled.

Dear Ruby Slipper Family,

I'm sorry it's been like three years and I'm just now realizing I never gave you five stars. Y'all are basically family at this point for my brunch needs and I even enjoy your food delivered or for pickup. I'll be honest- there's times when I want y'alls delicious french toast or seasonal pancakes, crispy bacon, your low calorie (don't correct me) homemade biscuits in the comfort of home. Y'all are a guaranteed spot for my hosting needs and tbh being able to make a reservation on Yelp is the syrup on top of my pancakes.

Sincerely,
A forever fan!

It's been a moment since I've left a restaurant with a foodgasm smile and hot damn, Morrow, y'all have reinvigorated my foodie cravings and excitement.

I'm still processing the wonderful meal (linner to be exact, lunch + dinner) with my friend and we both left proclaiming our love for Morrow's. Morrow's is neatly tucked on the corner and upon entering you are immediately given warm and woodsy vibes with all of the stained wood and the bar, oh my goodness, is it gorgeous.

"Morrow of the story..."

The fluorescent neon pink sign with a backdrop of foliage is stunning. In a pre-COVID world, I could picture myself being at the bar having multiple cocktails taking plenty of photos for the 'gram.

Reality currently had us waiting patiently for a table since they are really implementing social practices! THANK YOU. You have to wear a mask upon entry, they have a table blocking the entrance so folks can't simply go in-n-out, and there is a host to greet and make sure everyone is practicing safety and social distancing. Plenty of hand sanitizer all around.

We were eventually seated and absolutely no anxiety because they are so conscious about spacing of the tables. It honestly felt a little exclusive tbh. All of the staff was wearing masks and very, very friendly.

Onto the dishes we ordered...

Crawfish Bread: I literally wanted to cry tears of happiness because it was so good that I would've allowed someone to throw water in my face if it meant I would get a second plate of these for free. JUST GET THE DAMN APPETIZER.

Fried Chicken: Every crunch had the most flaky bite of fried chicken, I've had in SUCH a long time. I was sad when we realized we ate all of the fried chicken.

Charbroiled Oysters: Piping hot with the cheese drip. So fresh and the seasonings were divine. ORDER A DOZEN.

Crawfish Pasta: We asked for extra bread to slop up the sauce. ORDER EXTRA BREAD and you too will be happy you did. I legit had to make sure our server didn't take the dish until everything was eaten. I don't even like catfish, and I ate one of the two strips so fast I forgot to mention I hate catfish to my friend. The crawfish sauce had a nice spice (but not too spicy) and the pasta was al dente and cooked perfectly.

10s 10s 10s across the board. Make a trip to Morrow's ASAP!

Mojo you'll forever be home to my Iced Vanilla Oat Milk Latte with a splash of cinnamon aka my horchata coffee!

Right now during COVID-19, they are doing an amazing job implementing safety practices to ensure coffee drinkers, like myself, are getting our caffeine fix.

There are about 2/3 tables available outside but focusing on the ordering system...

Mojo currently has a one way entry system so visitors aren't coming in through both entrances. You enter through the main door then exit through the side door.

There is plexiglass between you and the Mojo Team and they have a big ol' bottle of hand sanitizer for you to utilize.

You can place any coffee order (they also have food still) and it comes out promptly.

There's probably like a total of 4 coffee drinkers spaced out throughout their whole space.

All the tables and chairs are piled up and they have blocked the use of the bathrooms. (Which I totally get)

Thank you Mojo for keeping your doors open!

With recent string of events, I wanted to let everyone know that their iconic shrimp and grits holds amazing well for to-go! This is one of my favorite dishes and seriously is a must try for every single person who comes to visit me. They also make a bit of their bread and juices from scratch so add them to the order. Their biscuits and gravy to go holds up amazing too.

Cute morning/lunch spot that is open until 2pm to help kickstart your day (no matter if you're a morning or early-afternoon bird gets the worm). They make a lot of their own baked goods including their signature bagels. If you prefer something with more substance they have a full menu available and I recommend their french toast. It's so good!

Plenty of seating that stretches down and outlets.

Such an adorable spot and I can't wait to go back and continue getting a better sense of The Chloe with a stay and pool pass to full encompass The Chloe.

My partner and I made a reservation for Monday evening the day of and were super appreciative they were able to squeeze us in. We initially asked for an 8/8:30pm timeslot, but they only had 6:45pm as their latest availability.

The Chloe is a super boutique hotel hosting only 14 rooms within their estate right off of St. Charles and has such a whimsical vibe. The darker, muted tones makes it blend in yet stand out amongst the other properties in this area. I love their pantone colors of choice and it's just so damn perfect. There's a courtyard they utilize for waiting space and all of the tables in the front are part of their dining area for their F&B program. They offer indoor and outdoor dining.

I learned within my dining experience they have a shorter menu for the pool area as it doesn't feature everything from their F&B program.

During our dinner I had two of their signature vodka cocktail, the Good Destruction. Made with vodka, peach, orange, cranberry, and galliano this cocktail is great for the warmer months and refreshing. Very easy to down to be honest.

We started off with the Shrimp Étouffée Dumplings and their Smoked Pork Belly & Shiso. 

The dumplings had a crushed chili and ginger based sauce that was divine. The crunchy elements was a great balance, not to mention, the ample amount of protein in each dumpling. Easy to share between 2-3 people. 

The smoked pork belly itself was delicious and each piece rested on a piece of bib lettuce, drizzled with an aioli-based sauce. Not my fave but I did enjoy it.

My partner and I split their Twin Stack Burger and Striped Bass since we both wanted to try the two. Now these were f*&king home runs y'all. The bass had a wonderful crunch coat, yet the fish itself was flaky and would easily cut with the least amount of effort with your fork. Surround by little pillows of rice dumplings bathed in that sauce, ugh just seriously a foodgasm for the soul. I also loved the oysters in their as well. (I kept dunking everything in the sauce tbh)

The burger had a poppyseed bun and it seriously blows my mind how this simply yet staple menu item took us by surprise. Simply topped with lettuce, tomato, and pickles, this burger wasn't able to hide behind a wall full of various toppings and flavors. It's such a cocky and confident bold statement, that you better make damn sure it's up to par. Welp, The Chloe knows their shit because that burger is literally making me drool as I'm typing this right now. I can't put my finger on it but if The Chloe had to sell their soul they rightfully made the right choice. I'll be back for this alone.

Our server was super polite and informative and we actually discovered they had a day of program where you can utilize and snag a pool pass valid for 4 people at $80 for 4 hours between 5-9pm. Not a bad way to cool off with the hotter months upon us.

My partner and I actually talked about the idea of utilizing this as a special occasion venue space and renting out the hotel so all of our families can stay with us. There's something special about the ambiance here where you know it's a hotel (explore the lobby, EXPLORE THE LOBBY) yet it feels like you're visiting someone's house whom you've known your whole life.

I'll definitely be back.
//
BTW this place is very LGBTQIA+ friendly and open to all. They also have gender neutral bathrooms!

I'm pissed at myself for sleeping on Cupcake Collection for so long. I had it bookmarked for such a long time and now I've upsetted the foodie gods for just now realizing the decadent taste of perfection from Cupcake Collection.

To think my freak out is over their cake and not their cupcakes yet tells me I'm swinging by sooner than later. 

Yelp Hack: They have the "Sweet Potato Cupcake Challenge". I HIGHLY recommend y'all go in to their shop and check it out. There's a reason why it's an award-winning cupcake and one you'll soon be ordering on a frequent basis.

So it was a friends birthday and I wanted to order a cake for the special occasion. After stalking their Instagram profile for such a long time, I decided to opt for their strawberry cake. *I kept debating between the red velvet, strawberry, and sweet potato for the day.*

What sold the deal was when I called the manager and she told me the strawberry icing and cake had no artificial colors or flavors! The pink hues from the cake was from real strawberries. Say whaaaa???? Done. Gimme the damn cake and sell it to me lol.

I placed the order and a six inch cake went for $65. I was able to choose the style of icing and opted for the rose petals.

OMGoodness. Every bite I took had my eyes getting larger and larger. The cake was not only fluffy but the icing was the right amount of sweetness. The table at the restaurant was super quiet because the cake was damn good. I had no shame sneaking a second slice because it was some of the best cake I have ever had.

If this was my first experience, I am excited to complete my unofficial Cupcake Collection flavor tour!

#SupportBlackOwnedBusinesses

I'm going to write a review based on the service and the food--maybe one of the few.  There are a lot of reviews that discuss what a great time they had at LSU, and how this brings back memories.  If you're looking for a trip down memory lane, read their reviews.  Not mine.

No, I'm not a tourist.  I lived in NOLA for quite a long time and still have work and friends there.  I was frustrated and disappointed that Smith & Wollensky's did not reoccupy the building after Katrina.  Hearing that someone did, I was thrilled to see something come back and provide an eating establishment in the CBD.

It's kind of the same as your generic sports bar fare, but with a bit of a South Louisiana twist.  And the usual price point and ridiculous portions.  I tried the Ahi Tuna "perfection" and it was ok, though I found the spices weren't' that spicy and the sweet & sour sauce served with it didn't float my boat.  We also had the Onion Mountain.  It's a Mountain, alright.

For starters, I think anytime you have a job and take your lunch hour and you *wait a FULL hour* before your lunch is set in front of you, you just can't recover.  I understand they have been open less than a month, but with the amount of brands and locations these guys have opened I would expect them to hit the ground running.

The killer though was the Gristle Salad.  Well, to be fair, not a lot of cartilage, but it's like the "Steakhouse" salad, which advertised Ribeye on it, was 50% fat.  I mean, don't you guys trim the meat you throw on a salad?  Oh, I guess that way when they overcook it, it's not tough.  But after cutting away all the fat myself (which is nigh impossible when it's served to you diced up), I was left with a underwhelming amount of lean meat and a Mountain of Lettuce (to go with Mt. Onion).  And another person ordered a Gristle Salad, it came out the same way, so clearly it's not an anomaly.

I may be back, but not of my own volition, and if they work out the kinks they deserve an update.  But for now, I'd steer clear.  And if you don't, don't get the Steakhouse.

My go-to place for pozole.  Always made fresh, tender pieces of pork with hominy in a flavorful broth.  Kick it up a notch with the included hot sauce.  It's a big portion, the picture below is just half the order.  Everything I've ordered here is fresh and full of flavor. 

There are 3 locations, so if you're ordering pickup, make sure you're calling the right one.  My ordering experiences have been hit or miss, as they get busy and you find yourself calling back frequently as the calls roll to a voicemail that is full.  Keep in mind, the good places are always busy.  The Maeanne location has plenty of parking, but the seating is limited (as stated, we usually order pick up).  Service is efficient and friendly.  All around good value for a decent meal.

We visited here again to meet with some friends and have a meal together. I arrived early to make sure we could get a table. Good thing I did, the place was packed! There was one table available, and we swooped it right up!

When our friends arrived, we greeted, sat down, and began enjoying each other's company over a couple of beverages. 

Audrey was our server, and she was spectacular! Of course, she thinks I'm very handsome! That made her even more awesome! 

She had to come by several times to make sure our beverages were full and cold, and to check on us to see when we would like to order our food. She was very patient, kind, and, like I said earlier, had a hard time keeping her hands off of me! I am used to that! Happens all the time!...(sorry, I digress!).

When we decided to order, there was a quesadilla, two buckets of clams, Two caprese salads, A bacon cheeseburger, and I ordered the prime rib dip. The cheeseburger and prime rib dip both came with fries.

My friends both ranted and raved about the quesadilla, caprese salad, and the clams! My prime rib dip was fabulous! The au jus was like nothing I have had before! They packed on the thinly sliced prime rib, and even the roll was tasty! The french fries were crispy, fresh, and seasoned perfectly!

After having our fill, Audrey promptly took care of our bill, and we even spent time sharing baby pictures! Her beautiful baby girl, and my beautiful-er granddaughter. Now that's how you get a good tip!

Audrey's service was impeccable. She even took our order without writing anything down! I have to carry my ID in my wallet, just to remember my own name!

If you haven't been out here yet, you are missing out! I know there is a new restaurant down the street, but don't count this one out!

We came here for dinner on our anniversary after visiting the distillery next-door. It was a Saturday night and the place was full! A new found friend pointed out the community table in the back, And we were able to sit down.

Our server, Shontel immediately brought us menus and took our drink order. I ordered a Truckee River red. Once again, it was delicious!

I ordered the tri-tip sandwich on a jalapeño cheese roll with a side of onion rings. The onion rings were crunchy, warm and perfect! The tri-tip sandwich had an ample supply of meat, and had a nice smoky barbecue flavor.

The community table soon filled up with other folks, and we had a wonderful time visiting with everyone! People here were just happy! 

Why three stars? I'm so glad you asked! After visiting with everyone for awhile, I got up to use the restroom. It is a gender neutral restroom. Actually it's more like a gas station restroom! It needed someone to clean it up! I am not one that goes around taking pictures of restrooms, but I appreciate those that do. This place was dark and smelled like stale urine. Fortunately, I wasn't in there to socialize. I did my biznis and bailed!

Other than that, this place is a very cool place to hang out, and no doubt I will be back soon!

We were Heading home for the evening and I asked "what would you like for dinner?"
We just happened to be passing Rick's Pizza Beer & More at that moment, and that was the reply she gave me... "Pizza, beer, and more!"

I turned the ship around and pulled into Rick's parking lot. There is a side door into the place from the parking lot. There is also, I suppose, a front door.

When we entered, we saw the bar counter and a fellow named Scott behind the bar smiling and greeting us with a friendly wave and a "Hi! Anywhere's good!". We bellied up to the bar and asked for a menu, and also asked if we were too old to be there. Scott replied that we were good for another couple of weeks... School's about to start again!

We decided on the uncle's boy pizza, an order of wings, and a couple of blondes from the draft selection. The uncle's boy pizza was fantastic! The wings, were devoured! The blondes, of course, were only made better by the second ones we ordered!

We had pizza to take home, we were full to the brim, and had some wonderful conversation while there! It just so happens, that Tuesdays are all day happy hour prices! I highly recommend that you head on over there on a Tuesday, and take advantage of the happy hour prices! I have no complaints! Thank you Scott!

After trying to have brunch at another nearby restaurant which had a 30 minute wait, we decided to try this place.

When we entered Jack's we were greeted and seated immediately. A fellow brought us coffee and menus within seconds. They have an extensive menu for breakfast and brunch, with American dishes as well as Mexican fare.

I ordered the Huevos rancheros and ask for a side order of jalapeños. When my plate arrived, there were no jalapeños. I asked my server again if she could bring me a side order of jalapeños. Again, she did not. Finally, the young man refilling coffee cups walked by and I ask him for a side order of jalapeños. He asked if I would like them grilled or sliced, and I stated that either way would be fine. Within seconds I had my jalapeños! Thank you young man!

The Huevos rancheros was all sweet, no heat! I do like a little heat with my meal! Actually, I like a lot of heat with my meal! This dish didn't really have a lot of flavor. It had some, just no pop! I suppose they have plenty of dishes that are spectacular, but unfortunately mine wasn't. 

I'm sure I will be back to try other dishes. The young man with the coffee earned them an extra star for his service, so they get another opportunity to impress me. A follow-up review will follow.

I'm loving this place! Having been here a few times now, I can tell you why.

This little place has been open for several years and I believe is family run. They specialize in making tacos, hence, the name.

The meats are very Tijuana style - beef tongue, head, tripe, pork stomach are but a few to choose from. The tortillas are made right there and you get to watch your meal being built right in front of you!

Tacos are $2 and they have other items as well. Mula and Vampiro were new dishes I'd never had, so of course I had to try them. They are $4 each. There are three french fries items that go for $10 each, but I haven't tried them yet...

The meat is prepared perfectly and these folks don't scrimp on the meat! It tastes fresh and is delicious!

A typical lunch for me would be:
1 taco de chorizo 
1 taco de asada
1 Vampiro al pastor
1 Horchata

I have had many other items and have not been disappointed with any of them. 

They have a chilled jalapeño, radish, and lime bar. You can ask for grilled Jalapeños and onions also! YUMMM!!

My only complaint is that there was a couple that was entering the restaurant and pestering the customers and really making everyone uncomfortable and it took several complaints before the manager finally shooed them off. Not good... 

I highly recommend this place for a very affordable lunch and even a casual dinner. They are open late also. Give 'em a try!

After reading many reviews, we decided to give this place a try. It was a Saturday afternoon, and we had a little time on our hands.

I ordered the smoked tri-tip with a side of crinkle fries and sweet potato tots. The tri-tip was delicious! The meet was tender and deliciously flavored. The crinkle fries taste just like the ones you get in the freezer section at Winco. They were dry, a little stale, and tasteless. The sweet potato tots on the other hand, we're awesome!

While waiting for our meal, I ordered the Truckee River red. It was nice and cold, creamy and yummy!

The place has several TVs spread about the restaurants. About 12 of them I believe. That's nice if they are playing what you want to watch. 

Overall, we had a great time! Our server was professional, congenial, and on point! She made us feel very special! This is definitely someplace I look forward to coming again!

Thought we would go north and check out someplace new and Hometown Cafe showed up when I Yelped BRUNCH in the north valleys area.

They were easy to find using the handy dandy map directions on the always awesome Yelp app!

Located in a kinda mini strip mall, there's plenty of parking (and gas next door in case you're low on fuel). 

Inside there's lots of room for seating and for good reason... the place was packed! We found a cozy little table near the counter which has about 8-10 seats as well. We were greeted at the door and immediately after sitting down also. 

We were served coffee within 1 minute of sitting down! Did I mention the place was packed?  We got service like we were the only ones there! Our server stopped by twice just to see if we were ready to order.

I finally settled for the chorizo and eggs with home fried potatoes and flour tortillas. I also ordered two grilled jalapeños! Yummm! The boss got chicken fried steak and eggs with home fries and toast.

The chorizo and eggs was good inside a warm tortilla and even better with a nice big bite of grilled jalapeño! I like mine spicy and the only problem was that they only had Tabasco for hot sauce. No bueno! If Tabasco flips yer skirt up then you'd like it here. I'm not a Tabasco guy and would have enjoyed my meal more with a bit more heat. Wife's chicken fried steak was a decent version of the standard breakfast item. Gravy was tasty. 

Our server was great and stopped by to ensure all was well and our coffee cup was full several times. 

The entire staff really seems to enjoy their job and it shows. They all were smiling and having fun and getting everyone served promptly! A well oiled machine! 

The total was about $26. Of course they received a generous tip as well! I really like good service! 

A fifth star awaits when I find they've added some different hot sauces to the mix. Solid place!

I love getting my groceries at Winco foods! I have not found any grocery store that is  cheaper in all of Reno!

They have a large produce section Full of seasonal fruits and vegetables, a great selection of coffee beans that you can grind there, or take the whole beans home. They have a wonderful assortment of all the favorites: beer, chips, paper products, etc. 

They have their own in-store  bakery. The bagels, muffins, bread and donuts are all fresh daily! They have delicious pre- buttered garlic French bread that is very inexpensive!

I gave them four stars, because I'm not a big fan of their meats. I will purchase their ground meat, chicken, packaged meats, and sausages, but their steaks seem to lack a bit in quality from some of the other stores in Reno. 

They have a great selection in their bulk foods area. They are also well stocked with Asian and Mexican staples.

It is a great feeling to walk out of there having spent $150 in groceries, especially knowing that elsewhere I would probably have spent $250! Yes, I really like Winco!

I never post reviews, but this was such a bad experience, I couldn't help myself. Let me start off by saying, I am a resident of downtown Tampa and I make it a point to frequent and support local businesses and restaurants. I have frequented cork and crumble numerous times in the past and I have never been overly pleased or disappointed, yet I continued my patronage because it was a convenient wine bar in downtown Tampa. Today, cork and crumble utterly disappointed me to the point that I feel it is absolutely necessary to share with locals. This is how my evening started, I went there with a girlfriend, expecting more girlfriends to come, and we debated ordering a bottle of wine, but wanted to sample some of their selections first.
