We ordered a glass of wine, that was offered at $8.00 a glass on the menu and was informed by our very nice waitress (by the way, this bottle of wine sells for $7.99 at any local store) that the management decided they didn't want to pour me a glass of wine because opening the bottle would potentially cause them spoilage of this entire bottle, if it wasn't all used that night, and the waitress told me, per the management I needed to order a different glass of wine. Why offer a glass of wine, if you don't intend to offer a glass of wine? 
As if this wasn't insulting enough, (a fellow frequent patron wasn't entitled to a glass of wine, as advertised on their menu) we requested a glass of water while we considered the other wines, we were informed by the waitress (who was instructed by the owner) that cork and crumble does not serve tap water because the salt from the tap water ruins their glasses. I have never been told that city water is too salty so that it is unsafe to sell it to consumers. 
While our waitress was very helpful and felt terrible, the management and ownership (who were informed of this matter)  did nothing to ameliorate the matter. After requesting to speak with the owner, the manager came to speak with us. Despite, our experience, the manger told us that he would be happy to buy us a glass of wine on our next visit? Who ever said there would be a next visit? 
People wonder why business in downtown Tampa is suffering... Perhaps they should reevaluate their business practices. 

Then we went to Anise and had an amazing experience.

I haven't reviewed in a while, but Jet City's newest location has inspired me to come out of Yelp hiding. First, let's talk about Jessica, the owner. I think most of us aspire to the level of passion and happiness Jessica cultivates every day. Her welcoming enthusiasm and always genuine graciousness makes visiting her cafe a 5-star experience the second you walk through the door. If you don't feel like part of her family after just a few visits, you haven't had enough of their wonderful espresso concoctions ;) Add another Borgia and you will certainly be convinced. 

The new location offers the same inspired coffee classics my girlfriend and I have been falling in love with since we started visiting her South Tampa location. I personally prefer the Chai latte made with almond milk. If you enjoy powdered donuts, you will love the somehow healthful liquid form. Also making a yummy reappearance at this location, her gorgeous, well balanced (and often surprisingly healthy) paleo and gluten-free treats. I love watching my girlfriend, a celiac sufferer, happily choose amongst the offerings (finally she has options!!). We are waiting to see if her gluten free paleo chocolate lava cake makes an appearance. This is hands down the best chocolate cake I have had in a very long time, across the board. 

The thing that really sets this location apart is the damn near perfect salads and sandwiches. Jessica outdoes herself daily with salads that contain just about everything you are reading about in your health magazines. No dressing necessary for these mixes of hearty lettuces, perfect slow cooked chicken, seeds, and extras like spaghetti squash and exotic rice. I recently had her portobello Gouda melt on a gluten free wrap---amazing. Next, I'm heading for her fish tacos. I am confident they will deliver in freshness, flavor, and wellness. 

A major win for Jet City, Jessica, and her team.

I finally made it down to Twisted Ranch the other day. I was meeting up with some friends in Soulard for the afternoon and made the recommendation we grab lunch . I am so glad I decided to try Twisted Ranch because it really was delicious! 

When we arrived around 2 pm on a Saturday the place was packed! As in, not a seat available anywhere! People seemed to be enjoying their meals and the food looked great. Since we had a party of 5 we opted to wait outside since there isn't much of a waiting space inside. That's the only reason I removed 1 star. The place is tiny. In colder months I don't know where people will be able to wait since standing outside is not really an option in winter months. However, when we were waiting outside it was a beautiful fall day and the sun was out so it wasn't too bad. 

After about 10 minutes of waiting a server came out to grab our group and brought us to our table. It was a high top table in the center of the room; I was almost sitting on top of the person at the table next to me. Seemed like community seating to me! 

Anyways, our server came over to get our drink orders and then gave us some time to review the menu. When she came over to deliver our drinks my group wanted to order a few appetizers; they ordered the nachos and the chicken dip. The appetizers came out fairly quickly and looked great. My friends all seemed to enjoy the food and recommended I give the apps a 5 star review! 

Our server came back over while appetizers were being eaten and took our orders. I ordered the turkey wrap (no bacon) and I asked for the pesto ranch to be included in the wrap and then I ordered fries with garlic ranch. Those are the 2 best sounding dips to me! I know my fiance ordered the burger, and I think there was a gyro wrap and 2 grilled cheeses ordered as well. Everything sounded so good! 

We each ordered another round of drinks and waited for our food. Within 15 minutes all of our food was brought out and looked fantastic. Unfortunately, the server forgot to say "no bacon" to the kitchen with my wrap, but kudos to her because she realized it as soon as she saw the plate. She immediately brought it back to the kitchen and had them make a new one without bacon. No biggie! I had fries and garlic ranch to snack on in the meantime. 

Overall, I am very pleased with Twisted Ranch and I really do want to go back! The only downfall is that the space is so tiny and with it being a packed house it was hard to really have room to myself. They definitely have a good business going and I look forward to seeing how they are doing in few weeks! 

Go check them out! Yum.

Yes, Salt + Smoke is probably my new favorite place for BBQ in the Lou! My sister was in town last weekend and when I asked her where she wanted to go for dinner Friday night she asked for some BBQ. I thought about the places we had been in the past, but decided to bring her to S+S instead because we wanted to try something different. What a good choice it was! 

When leaving my house I used the No Wait app and checked us in. There was a 45 minute wait and like 30 something parties ahead of us! Wow, it was busy! By the time we arrived there was still about 15 minutes left for the wait so I went ahead and let the hostess know I was there. She told me to just hang out because we would be seated soon. We decided to grab a drink at the bar and we were actually able to snag the last 2 chairs and my husband just stood behind us which was fine. We each ordered a drink and paid our tab. Moments later I was getting a text to let me know our table was ready! That was fast. 

We were brought over to our table and started looking over the menu. Our server came over to tell us about the specials and then gave us some time to decide. When we were ready to order I did ask if they had any popovers without the bacon in which she told me no. I kind of wish they would offer just a cheese or herb popover since I don't eat the bacon, but I guess I can't complain too much since it was a BBQ place. Anyway, I think we all ordered a plate with 2 meats and 2 sides. The special that night was smoked turkey so I ordered that and some chicken with the sweet potato fries and the mac and cheese. My sister ordered some other meats with her sides and my husband ordered meats with his sides. 

By the time our food came out I was ready to eat! My turkey was delicious and the chicken was pretty tasty too! But the winner of the meal was the mac and cheese (obviously)! I should have ordered a tub of that to go! I tried the sweet sauce and enjoyed it with my meat and after eating like 1/3 of my meal I needed a to go box. It was all so tasty and perfectly cooked. I think we all took some food home that night and reheated it the next day and it still tasted just as good to me. 

We paid our bill and were on our way, but I think we were all stuffed and happy! Thanks S+S for the enjoyable meal and for the best mac and cheese in the city!

Whisk is still a great bakery and I do visit often. I get my hair cut just up the street, so I have no excuse not to visit Whisk at least once every 8 weeks! Today I was shopping local in support of small business Saturday.  I was debating between a popsicle or a baked good. Once I saw the cookie that had peanut butter, pretzel, chocolate chip and caramel I knew I had to have it. The guy behind the counter was friendly and told me the cookie was a good choice (as if there is a bad choice at whisk)! I paid and was on my way. 

The cookie is salt and sweet and I have enjoyed every bite of it. I'll continue to support Whisk and look forward to my next visit.

I have found the best pizza place in Saint Louis (for real this time)! I was craving a pizza and wanted to try something new and after reading a few Yelp reviews I had to come try the Corner Bistro; and I am glad I did! 

I arrived with my bf around 5 on a Saturday and we were able to pick a table since so many were available. There were 2 other tables in the dining room when we arrived. The server came over ( she may be the owner too) and took our drink orders. They do not have a liquor license so I opted for soda. We looked over the menu for a bit and then when she came back with our drinks we ordered. I went with the margherita pizza and the bf ordered a sandwich. While our order was being made in the kitchen I noticed how busy this bistro can get. The phone was ringing non-stop and guests were coming in pretty steadily to pick up their to-go orders. The server was making her rounds and checking on tables; she was staying busy. 

By the time our food came out I was starving just thinking about it. I cut off a slice of pizza and tasted it and it was heavenly. I don't know how to best describe it, but all I can say is that the crust was soft and chewy and crisp all at the same time. The sauce tasted just right and the amount of cheese was perfect. I honestly enjoyed that first piece so much. I ate another and then another...it was that good. While eating it I was already thinking about ordering from them again. 

While we were enjoying our meal another table was ordering dessert. The desserts are definitely homemade from the looks of them. She even has a cake saver to keep the desserts in for freshness. I wish I would have ordered some for myself. I guess I will just have to go back for that. 

Our server made sure our drinks were refilled often and she checked in on us a few times. Very friendly and even made some friendly jokes with us. I knew I was going to need a box so I asked for one and she brought it right over.

We paid the bill which was about $20 for 2 people, what a steal! I will definitely be back and I can't wait to order another pizza for carry-out. Maybe I will do that this weekend!

Avoid this place.  It is not worth dealing with the poor customer service, flies, long wait, or, as I experienced, the horribly rude manager. This is quite possibly the longest review ever written, but I'd read it in its entirety if you are considering a place to eat in Ybor.

I visited this place for the first (and only) time approximately two weeks ago, after two of my friends found groupons online.  I had a similar experience as another yelper.  The customer service was the worst I have experienced and there were only about 4 other customers in the entire small restaurant.  I'd comment on the taste of the soup, but I wouldn't know since I never got what I ordered...

1) It took approximately 20 minutes to order drinks.  Nobody got refills on water the entire time.  I asked once and never got it.

2) The waiter (who bless his heart was actually a nice guy) did not write down our orders, which of course included four of the 4-soup-samplers.  I would have been extremely impressed if all of the orders were correct, but almost all of the orders were wrong.

3) The orders came out staggered over the course of an hour.  There is no "waiting for your friends to get their food" with soup because you don't want your soup to get cold.

4) The chilli cheese fries were not good.

5) I never got my soup sampler.  Thank goodness I also ordered the chilli cheese fries.

6) We were sitting near the open front door and there were flies in the air.  There was also a fly that landed in my friend's wine glass.

7) After two of my friends informed the waiter that one of their four soup samplers were not what they ordered, he graciously apologized, as he should have done.  BUT, then the manager came over, clearly agitated, asking what the problem was with us and our orders in an unacceptably RUDE tone, we responded that the waiter got our orders down wrong.  There was no apology, no sensitivity, no decency - and, even more shocking, became agitated at me when I said I had not even gotten my meal!!!!  He rudely walked away.  Shortly after, the waiter (again, bless his heart) came up and explained that they had not yet made that many soup samplers at one time and their kitchen was not ready for it.  He said that they would comp me a bowl of soup. I politely said, no thank you, as we had already been there two hours.  This was something the manager should have done, not the waiter.

8) At the time the checks came, we asked that they be split.  Yes, no server ever wants to do this.  We've all waited tables at some point in our lives, but there was nothing on the menu disallowing this, and the waiter did not ask this when he first greeted the table.  The manager became even more visibly agitated.  Given that almost everyone ordered the same thing, it's not rocket science.  Any functional restaurant should be able to handle this request without issue.  Instead, it turned into another 25 minute ordeal.  I think by this point our quick soup night had turned into a nearly 2.5 hour debacle.  I was late to a birthday party that night and had not had my soup.

9) When I got my bill, they did not comp anything.  Wah wah I know - but you'd think if I didn't get my meal they could at least cut out a $1.25 coke!!! :)

10) After we cleared out, I went to use the rest room one last time.  I heard the manager say in a horrible tone to the waiter, "sweep up a bit, wipe the table, and then get the f**k out of here."  Completely unacceptable, whether or not he knew there was a customer in the bathroom.  You are the manager.  Learn how to run your business, implement protocols for your servers, expect that a party over 2 is going to come in and order multiple soup samplers, and be gracious to them especially when you are a new business.

11) I believe the majority of us still tipped the waiter 15% because we felt so bad for him having to work there - although, a tip reflecting the quality of the service would be much much lower.  The whole experience was horrible.  There are way too many good places to go, to waste your time here.

2 stars for the food, 5 stars for the service. 

I really wanted to love this place. They had all my favorites: guacamole, mules, Chimichangas and enchiladas. So, what did my girlfriend and I order? All of the above, of course. 

While doing my research on a good place to eat, I found this place. They had a free corn appetizer for checking in on Yelp and a deal where you can purchase a coupon worth $50 for just $25. This deal is what really drew me in.

When we arrived, we were allowed to pick our own spot to sit. Word of advice: Don't sit in a 2 seater table of there are only 2 people! The tables are small and they have a huge condiment dish that takes up too much room. The host (I think she was actually the manager) pulled up another table next to us so we had more room. 

Once we ordered, it was just a short wait till our food started to arrive. We were first given a huge dish of complimentary chips and awesome salsa. Then our guacamole came.. I wasn't impressed. I am a big guacamole lover and was dissatisfied with the lack of salt and lime... then the corn came. YUM! I think this was the highlight of the meal! Our drinks were fine.. my Mexican mule was good, I just wish it was in a copper mug, it does make a difference. 

The food finally showed up. The beans weren't fully cooked but the Chimichanga was really good. The lady I assumed was the manager recommended the cheese sauce on top.. good recommendation! I almost wished the sauce came as a dipping sauce for some chips.

The price of $25 for $50 is worth it, just make sure you leave a nice tip for the waitstaff. They do a great job.

Cheapies.  I dig this place when I have cash (it is cash only) and want a banging chicken cheesesteak with some greens on top or a breakfast sammich.  Employees are so nice, so quick, and very attentive.  Always people in there, though there's limited space for sit-down eating.  Yes, they have coconut water.  Fresh baked goods too...uhhhh who woulda thunk?

We had to stop here, right?? This is the place that put Nashville Hot Chicken on the map after all. Honestly I was pretty impressed with their Covid precautions and there was no line (which was a clear sign to go). 

The medium spiced chicken tenders were definitely all the spice I needed. There are 2 more heat levels above that but, medium gave me all I could handle. Their chicken is honestly quite good. Pimento Mac & Cheese and coleslaw were my 2 sides of choice and neither excited very much. The chicken is definitely the star. 

We ate on the patio and there was everything we needed to sanitize our table & chairs before they brought out our food. It's definitely up to the customer to do this because the outdoor tables turn over so much. There was also plenty of hand sanitizer.

After a few hours of sightseeing I needed a boost, came across this place and it lived up to my expectations.

Initially CC's Coffee House reminded me of Starbucks but once I really checked it out I came to appreciate the differences. Originating from Baton Rouge, Community Coffee (the coffee roaster) has been around for ~100 years and various blends are available in some grocery story. In 1995 they began opening retail coffee shops throughout Louisiana, Texas and Alabama. The shops outside of Louisiana struggled due the establish places (i.e. Starbucks, Dunkin' Donuts, etc). In 2013, as an attempt to expand both inside and outside the state of Louisiana 2013, Community Coffee spun off the retail coffee shop business into a separate company named CC's Coffee House. 

As for this location, the space has a nice layout and while it's part of the CC's Coffee House chain, it felt more like a one-off local coffee shop. There was plenty of table seating, a few comfy chairs/sofa seats along with a few bar-height communal tables. With the steady flow of people coming/going, finding a seat was never an issue on my visits. Even more important, was the abundance of those power outlets available. Spend time in a coffee shop and one quickly learns how the seats near the power outlets are coveted. The staff was very friendly and super helpful. They assisted me a couple of times in deciding what I wanted to drink (I knew it in Starbucks lingo but it wasn't the same on their menu.  

While all of that is important, the primary reason for visiting a coffee shop is for the product. I used to brew Community Coffee at home and always enjoyed the bold but smooth flavor. For my first visit (yes, I visited it more than once) I went with a plain cup of coffee. It was as tasty as I remember.  and that's what I had on my first visit. On subsequent visits I tired some of their specialty drinks. All were made per order and were delicious. 

If you're in the area and need a boost stop in here for one of their many options. And while you're there, have a seat, charge your device and chill for a few minutes. I plan to do just that on future visits to this area.

I purposely arrived to Tampa earlier than I had to - for the simple fact that I like to eat. I asked this dude that kinda knows his way around town (you know, the Tampa Yelp CM - Brett N) and he recommended Anise, which was near our hotel.

The place was empty when we arrived - that's cool, just means we sit down faster. We took a seat and the server brought over the menus. I got a beer (AH! Pissed I can't remember the name of it, but it was great. It was unfiltered, which was my first time ever having an unfiltered beer, but it was ice cold and delicious).

We started off with the truffle tater tots. There is something about tater tots that make me feel like a kid - maybe cause I used to have them in elementry school - or maybe cause you eat them with your hands...but these...these are adult tots for sure. With a little truffle oil and a cream sauce (I would of prefered another, more flavorful sauce, but I get they keep it simple so the truffle stands alone). They were gone in seconds as me and the wife tag teamed the basket to the final crumb.

I ended up going with the buns after reading numerous reviews. Not sure why they are called Stinky Bunz but they are. And they smell delicious. I got two pork belly and one shrimp. The pork belly was awesome - BUT I really regretted not getting two shrimp instead. The shrimp was massive and blended with the sauce it was just better. The pork belly is still a viable contender for space in my belly - but maybe 2 shrimp and one PB next time.

Service was great! We were in and out of there super fast (which was good, we had places to be) and everyone was smiling. Great spot for a quick lunch - or a nice dinner - when in Tampa!

I get to go to Tampa Bay at least once a year for work and on my last trip I finally made it to Dough. It's been a while, and this draft has been sitting in my drafts, waiting to be finished. But I can't wait to drop back in when I'm there in November.

I just had brunch next door and came over to Dough for a sweet treat for my ride back home. I was immediately greeted by Bridgette. She was amazing - everyone needs employees like this! She is upbeat, excited about the product and so nice. Asking her for recommendations, she was so genuine is rattling off her favorites. You could see her smile as she named something, signifying that she ACTUALLY loves that.

So. I went with an iced coffee and a box of treats. A few donuts, a peanutbutter brownie and a cake pop. All of them were divine. Admittedly, most didn't make it back from the 4(ish) hour trip

I might of found my second favorite brewery. Yeah, I did.

After going to Tampa in September and missing out on visiting Rapp, I made sure during my latest trip I made it out to pay them a visit.

Rapp is in a super industrial area (aren't all breweries?!) - parking was a synch...and inside it's super clean...off to one side they have a ton of seating and on the other side some seating and the bar to order.

They have small batch brews...and immediately my eyes went to the chalk board with 20 brews on it! What a great visual. Even more impressive is that the dude behind the bar KNEW EVERY BEER BY NUMBER.

"Tell me about (inset whatever number)"
"Oh well....here's the history of it...has subtle notes of...it's our take on the traditional whatever...." Super detailed about each and every brew. I really think that makes a huge difference, especially for a first timer. I've been to plenty of other breweries where the staff doesn't take the time to explain the beers - granted we were there late, and it was somewhat empty, but he seemed to take great pride in the beers.

I got a flight of course.

Some that I remember:

2016 Pumpkin Ale - I love the reasoning behind this name....they can claim they released their new Pumpkin Ale before anyone else did! Oh, those other breweries are serving 2015 Ales? Well, we've got the 2016 ale available. haha love that

Chocolate Peanut Butter Stout - If you have a beer my wife actually likes you've hit a home run in my book. This was delicious! Perfect balance taste of chocolate and peanut butter....took 2 growlers of this to go!

Smoked Porter - WHOA! Nice porter....with a heavy smoky flavor...it was different. Not my favorite but perfect for a flight.

Really, everything was good. I liked some more than others...but they've got some great brews here!

Flights can be done by 6 or 9 brews - I honestly wouldn't mind going with someone else and trying all 20 in one shot lol

So yea, I'll be back for a couple of growlers when in town. Cheers!

TLDR: I'm not a fan of "fancy" Mexican food.
___
Man. I hate writing reviews that aren't stellar, but Yelp's all about sharing our experiences...so here I am. 

I've been to Miguel's twice now, and honestly wouldn't have returned after the first visit, but we had a work dinner here and thus, I was back.

We had a nice private room. The acoustics weren't the best and with 10+ people chatting it got a little loud and hard to hear at times.

This place is really nice. I however, am not a fan of "fancy" Mexican food. 
I much prefer authentic Mexican, and while this is supposed to be TexMex, I just don't get it. Maybe it's not for me.

Lobster Fajitas - Not good. This was just lobster. On a plate. With fajita fixings. No real flavor to the lobster. 

Steak Fajitas - these were a bit better. But still lackluster.
They have upgrades like Kobe beef. Not something I'd expect at at a Mexican joint.

Queso - This was good, and the first thing that came out so we all attacked it. 

Margaritas were good - and large.

Service also left something to be desired. One server for a large group - and he was a bit rude when I asked him something. He was visibly in over his head.

*Read on if you want to know about one of the best burgers (and overall meals) I've ever had.


Working for Yelp I get the MAJOR perk of knowing a local expert in every major city in the US. I  can guarantee I can travel to any city - and find the absolute best food there thanks to my colleagues. This sounds like a TV show I need to pitch - just me traveling around seeing my friends and having them take me to dinner at their favorite spots.

 So when I found out we'd be headed to St. Pete for our regional confrence, I was a little bummed we weren't going to Tampa, as all I remember of St. Pete is the tourist traps my old job used to take us to on our confrence (man, what a difference that company was to this one).....but then I remembered what a perfectionist our boss is. And there was no way he wasn't going to deliver a gastronomical adventure like no other. No seriously, he was under A LOT OF PRESSURE. Luckily, he delivered.

So, large 9 person party - what do they do? Give us a private room. I will point out the room was nice...but we sat in office chairs. That was the most bizarre thing ever. A super nice room, dim lighting...and office chairs with wheels.....ok?

If you've read this far, you are probably thinking...when is this dude going to get to the food...he said he had the most amazing burger and he's talking about office chairs?! Ok, here goes.

The B&M Burger is one of the best burger I've ever had. I've had many, many, many burgers. It was one of the best. Maybe the best. But that's a BOLD statement. I'll deff say it's TOP 5. It's juicy, greasy (in a very great way), and just perfectly done. I want you to try it because I can't do it justice. The truffle fries were a nice touch as well that complimented the burger perfectly.

While the burger was the star of the show - there were many co-stars....all capable of being starts if you decide to cast them...

Carpaccio - Man I love me some carpaccio and this one was a home run! 
 
Octopus - Perfectly cooked, with a little char on it, but still tender and not at all chewy. Also, it photographed amazing for the gram!

Polenta- creamy and amazing - I missed out on the meatballs, but heard they were amazing - well I figured they were by the way my colleagues eyes were rolling back in their heads.

I washed it all down with some beers from the local brewer, Cycle Brewing. Had a couple Cream & Sugar Please which is a delicious coffee stout.

Thanks to B&M for an incredible dinning experience - and to our host for choosing this place as our final dinner in town.

Maybe I was starving... maybe I was tired... maybe I had a few drinks... na, eff that this sushi really was THAT good. Good enough that we ordered about 18 different rolls for the table (of 18 people) and shared everything. I am now convinced that the ONLY way to go to a new sushi restaurant is to go with 18 of your closest friends, order basically everything off the menu and then share.

I really can't remember everything we had - especially after a sake bomb - but here were the highlights:

Blue Crab Rangoon - Lump Crab, Cream Cheese & Chives in a Crispy Wonton Wrapper. Amazing! Get these to start!

Tempura Lobster Roll - Cant remember what all is in it - but this was possibly my favorite of the night. I can say that was my first time having lobster on a sushi roll - and it was amazing - get it!

Blue Moon Roll - Lump crab meat, cream cheese, asparagus and scallions (tempora). Get it! Seemed to be in everyone's top choices at the table.

My wife got a Geisha Roll (Sweet Potato Tempura and Avocado, inside out with Sesame Seeds) - she said it was the best vegetarian roll she has ever had! 

From there it got a little fuzzy and unfortunately I forgot the names of all the other ones. BUT I must say I didn't have a single bit I didn't enjoy. It's safe to say everything on the menu is good.

Aside from the awesome food - the service was impeccable. Within minutes the staff whipped a few tables together for our large group (with no reservation and a pretty packed house) - and the servers took great care of us, bring everything out promptly and splitting the check for us an obscene amount of ways - never even flinching.

The location itself is pretty interesting as well. It's on the second floor and the ceiling is extremely high - and has exposed brick (love seeing exposed brick, since we don't have much of that down here in South Florida!) 

I'll deff make it back next time I am in Tampa!

The garlic fries should come with a warning but they are so good!   They are loaded with garlic. Just don't have them if you are planning on kissing anyone.  I like their chicken and beef burgers on the wheat buns.  Delicious!  The regular sized burger is quite large so my Mom and I usually split one and order a side of garlic fries. They have a drive through which is convenient but slow.  My only reason for 4 and not 5 stars is because while dining in the restaurant in the summer we've seen several flies buzzing around.  So I only eat there in the non-summer months.

The service in this restaurant leaves much to be desired. Before I was even finished my lunch a very thin lady - possibly the owner's mother asked if I was finished and abruptly took the plate away. She didn't even wait for a reply. There is no excuse for this even if they might have been trying to push people out to accommodate more people. No customer deserves this treatment. The restaurant is small and very noisy. Food is nothing to brag about and even if it was superior, this does not make up for the server's rude demeanor. I'd give it zero stars if I could.

The two star rating is purely for the weekend shopping experience at this TJ's.  Hey TJ's marketing team - NOLA has outgrown its one small location.  We need a second one, stat.

I'm from Cali, so I'm no stranger to TJ's.  I've been shopping at this chain for 20+ years, even in the 90s when this was the one place I could get a Toberlone bar before chain grocery stores started carrying them.  I remember when two buck Chuck, was actually $2 and not $2.99.

The produce selection and grab-and-go packaging beats the other local grocery stores, hands down.  Crimini mushrooms, riced cauliflower, chopped kale, rainbow carrots, and green goddess salad dressing?  Yes, please.  I also love the frozen section, with the cauliflower fried rice, Thai shrimp dumplings, Bolognese sauce, cioppino, and eggplant parm as my go-to dishes.  All the sauces and seasonings are not to be missed, as they can jazz up any bland weekday dinner.  Oddly enough, I don't shop for wine or liquor here like I used to back in Cali.  This is Louisiana, where alcohol can be found anywhere.

I mainly shop on the weekends, which is where the rating comes from.  I haven't SHOPPED at this TJ's.  On the weekends, you're running a gauntlet, hoping to grab your staples and get out in one piece.  There is no shopping and discovering new products.  It's one huge melee as shoppers run over each other to throw items in their carts and the employees are working furiously to re-stock, leaving pallets and boxes of merch in the middle of the already congested aisles.  It's so busy, they're always running out of key products.  I think the NOLA metro market has proven itself; can we have another one now?

I want to like this place. I have some mixed feelings. I've been here twice now. The first time I ordered a burrito, and that thing was MASSIVE.
I went on my lunch hour, on a Friday, it was pretty dead which worked for me, as the service was great, and food was great.

The next time I went in after work on a Thursday about 4:45. The service was mediocre at best. I ordered a house wine, and a friend met up with me. I asked the person behind the bar closest to me for another glass of wine, she said that she wasn't the bar tender, but poured it anyway.
We ordered some food, and it just wasn't great. I had tri-tip tacos, and they were cold. Cold cheese, warmish meat, cold taco shell. 

I walked to the restroom at one point and 2 servers were standing near the kitchen, in the path of walking to the bathroom and they seemed annoyed that I had to walk in between them to get to the bathroom.

It was a bit painful to try and get anyone's attention for a refill on drinks, or even get our check.

Like I said I want to like this place, it has a good vibe. I just feel like if you're not a regular, they don't really want to wait on you.  Jury is out on this one, I'll update if I go again.

Noble Pie is hands down my favorite wing and pizza place in Reno.  And the Midtown location is pretty amazing.

It's a LOT bigger than the down town location.  Plenty of places to sit.  I love the outdoor area, it's great for a warm spring day.  

The staff at Noble Pie is always on point, and I enjoy coming down and chatting with them all.  

Brunch is pretty darn good here.  Bottomless Mimosas, yes please!  Brunch slice, um YUM.  Get it with some sausage on it.  So darn good.  And the french toast, brie, apples, dish is AHHMAZING!  I couldn't get enough of it.

Really any time of day is a good time to hit up Noble.  You won't be sorry.

Great music, but they were out of like half the items on the menu.  Not good.  For that reason alone we won't be back.

Then, after that, they got our order way wrong- like not even close.  And no silverware, no napkins, nothing.

Damn, I really wanted to be obsessed with Java house. It's not that it's not bad - it's just still in the growing pain process.

The Good:
- The Nitro was great! It's an extra $1 but worth it. Splurge on the larger size. Much better than Starbucks!
- The inside is roomy and very aesthetically appealing. 
- Service was quick and fast
- You can rent a private meeting room for $15 an hour 
- You can purchase their pods on-site. I LOVE their cold brew coffee. It's fantastic!

The Bad:
- The plug situation is lackluster. If you are planning on needing an outlet for your stay, I suggest bringing an extension cord if possible. 
- No food. I heard that they are considering bringing in some small bites. Even if they just had a something from a local baker to snack on... that would be nice. Otherwise, you feel awkward staying past when your drink is gone. 

The Ugly:
- The internet situation is dumb. I consider myself extremely tech-savvy and I had to ask the barista how to connect. You click "accept terms" but then you're still not able to connect to the internet. They require you to enter in either your phone number, Instagram handle, facebook or email. I'm not a fan of that type of data farming, so I stuck with the good ol 867-5309. I highly recommend they make changes to this asap

I am looking forward to seeing the growth of Java House in the future.

The meal started with lousy bread, so I was not shocked when pizette appetizer also had  a dry gritty crust. Way too much dressing on the sald. I was terribly disappointed in the veal parm, not sure how they got voted best 6 years in a row, maybe it was just an off night. The pasta was overcooked  which didn't help either. For that kind of money, try La Scala.

While we are talking about a cheesesteak spot, this place is heavily hyped.  Bright lights, features on the Food and Travel channels....the whole nine.  How can you not think that you're in for an amazing Philly cheesesteak experience?  One that makes you want to start running up the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art and jumping around in victory like Rocky Balboa.

Yeaaaaaaaaaa.......NO!  I came on a Sunday evening to check out and compare Philly's finest in comfort food.  I realize that nothing could match up to my beloved chicken finger sub but I'm an open minded person when it comes to deciding what would finish in 2nd place.  

Service was shoddy.  Order taker was very nonchalant and disinterested.  I'm a city boy myself so I get it in terms of the blue collar attitude for a blue collar meal but still.....etiquette?

The cheesesteak itself was pathetic in terms of appearance.  It looked haphazardly tossed together, cheese whiz slopped onto it.  Another glaring thing was it was missing.....the rest of the meat!!!  Cheesesteaks are known for being packed with meat are they not?  Did a badger manage to get to mine before it reached my hands?  If I had a voice like the narrator from "Unsolved Mysteries" we could sho' nuff figure this thing out. 

Alas, I took my measly little sub and ate.  Meh....meh.......MEH!  It was ok and I'm probably being generous.  Very bland and not very fulfilling.  Relatively inexpensive ($6-$7).  Good thing I had other spots to check out because otherwise I would've left Philly a sad and hungry person.  So much for brotherly love!

Charlie's major sins:  

1. The drinks are good, but lots of ice and mint leaves for a flat fee of 12$ for any drink. You are paying for the ambiance, but that is mostly worth it, so make sure you grab a seat at the bar to really enjoy this place as it should be. Order the "5 year plan" as your first drink. 

2. Sadly no IPA's on tap for the enthusiasts. 

3. Try the beet dumplings, but don't bother with the crab cakes or the chickpea fries. Money better spent at El Vez or Barbuzzo for a meal at the same price. 

4. Great small vegan plates, but many are overly priced bites that fall short of expectations.

We dined there today with our grandchildren, and everyone had so much fun! Miranda was our server, and she was excellent. I don't know why they have so many low reviews. Our food amd service were very good.

My husband and I went for lunch on a weekday. The place was beautiful but chaos prevailed. We sat at the main bar for 30 minutes and no one waited on us. We then left and sat at the outside bar, ordered, had delicious salsa and queso and two ice teas. Then we waited well over an hour... no food, no nothing. They are totally understaffed and have NO idea how to run this restaurant.
I called over the manager, explained that we just couldn't wait anymore for the food we ordered. She comped our bill and was very apologetic. 
But PLEASE! They should close for a month, get their act together...hire lots more staff, train the cooks and all employees and have management that are experienced in running  a properous and efficient restaurant. They got a good location, but off to a terrible start. Ugh.

I bought a groupon for Charlottes and used it on a Thursday night. We won't go ever again. We spoke with the owner when we arrived and told him we were using a groupon. My husband and I each ordered their most expensive entrees (29.00 each) and a bottle of wine. Thursday nights are 1/2 price bottles of wine. When our check came, the waiter said he couldn't honor the wine special because we were using a groupon. The groupon clearly stated "good for food only." If alcohol was not included, why couldn't we get the 1/2 price wine. But, the worst part of the evening was the owner calling us "cheap" after we both had their most expensive entrees. If he didn't want to participate with groupon, he should never have agreed to it. As a business owner, you certainly don't call your patrons "cheap" after they purchase a groupon you agreed to participate in. I believe the whole reason you do that is to bring in new customers. Well he brought us in, called us cheap, and wouldn't honor his wine special. Needless to say, we won't every go back and will be happy to let everyone we know how bad customers are treated.

Since we are all on Social Distancing many of our local restaurants are closed. Thankfully, Washoe Public House is not and even after the Reno ordinance goes through to close restaurants, bars and more on Friday, their food is still available for take out. We also purchased a gift card for future use. Come support your local business!

I went with four of my friends. We arrived at 4:00pm and were seated by a cheerful hostess. That's where the fun pretty much ends. After being seated, it was at least 8 minutes until we were even ASKED if we would like beverages. Water should always be brought to the table immediately. Nobody should have to sit around and wait for a drink order to be taken to get water, especially when everyone gets it by default. I don't care how busy a restaurant is.

Three in our party ordered Strongbow cans and got them almost immediately. However, the other two members of the party ordered milkshakes.  I have gone to plenty of diners and burger joints and never in my life have I had to wait so long for so little. Not only was the whipped cream on the top warm and starting to sag by the time we got our shakes, the bottom of the shake was completely liquid. That is simply unacceptable. The shake was $5, which doesn't seem unfair at all until you realize that unlike every other place that has ever served milkshakes since the dawn of time at a cheaper price, PYT doesn't give you the mixer in which the shake was created with bonus milkshake happiness. I understand that ice cream is expensive and all, but when one of your major selling points is milkshakes, you should live up to at least what your local corner diner can supply. 

The burgers were very delicious, albeit smaller than you'd expect or even make for yourself at home, and cooked to the proper temperature and with enough VERY fresh toppings to partially satisfy my hunger. However, I felt as though charging $1 for adding a tablespoon of hot peppers to the burger was a bit excessive and i almost missed seeing the two meager pieces of bacon on my burger.

Then came the side item: kettle cooked chips. Like a pair of seasoned burger vets, two members of the party expected kettle cooked style hot potatoes or, at least, homemade kettle-cooked chips. What we got was prepackaged potato chips. I can see getting potato chips with a cold deli sandwich, but a burger NEEDS fries included on the side. It's not like it's more expensive to get potatoes in bulk than it is to get potato chips in bulk. 

The onion rings were advertised as some of the best, but they were pretty mediocre. The batter was delicious, but was often barely sticking to or properly coating the onions, so there were bits of burnt onion tainting the experience. They were also WAY too salty.  

After being spoiled rotten by Butcher & Singer's $5.95 lunch special and rapid fire service all summer and having made countless 'gourmet' burgers of my own in my life, I have to say that PYT doesn't really live up to all the hype going around about it. The service, while friendly, was too slow and the food, while tasty, wasn't really as filling. I am used to hyperbole and clever marketing when it comes to dance parties and club events, but that's the last thing I want when I am trying to get something good to eat.

Now that I'm done reviewing, here are some suggestions.

- Get a stand for the hostess. I know that sounds like a petty gripe, but it's pretty much standard fare for a restuarant so that people aren't wandering around trying to find someone to seat them. 

- Put all matching furniture outside. It's tacky when furniture is mismatched, especially when there are 3 different kinds of chairs at a table and only 2 of those chairs actually match the table. 

- Change your server assignment chart. Servers shouldn't have to run between the outdoor and  indoor areas. Keep them to a section of the restaurant so that they can keep an eye on all of their tables at one time

- Get your food and drinks out faster. It takes about 10 minutes to make a burger. 20 minutes is entirely too long for a burger of that size with no french fries. Add another bartender to the staff so that milkshakes don't come out with warm whipped cream and liquid at the bottom.

I eat at Rotiers a lot - the food is always up to par and the wait staff is always good. The reason I'm giving Rotiers a poor review is because of the smart alec attitude the owner Charlie shows to his guests. He's polite to people's faces but he won't hesitate to make comments behind their backs. I have an 81 year old father who has trouble with manual skills now that he's older, I really loved how he rolled his eyes as my father left and said something to people at the cash register!

A restaurant owner should expect his staff to show respect to his customers - not set a bad example.

I'm always reluctant to try a new Thai place. Is it going to approximate the real deal or is it going to be a glorified stir fry joint? I know what the real deal is - my cousin married a Thai and he happens to know how to cook. So with a great deal of reluctance we tried Siam Cafe tonight. 

Parking was tight but available - we were greeted immediately upon entering. We decided to order off the menu - I ordered the pla mug prao prig (squid with jalapeno pepper,onion and chili pepper) and I asked for it spicy with a side of rice. My father ordered the lad nah (flat rice noodles with broccoli and gravy - his choice of protein was chicken.) The main course was served with a large spoon and I was glad about that - the jalapeno and onion was sliced and the spoon enabled me to get a scoop of sauce with each bite. The heat level I would describe as three alarm; I will not have to use baby powder in the morning. (By comparison Prince's extra hot chicken is so hot that it will curdle milk and strip bark off of trees.)

Service was prompt and excellent, although my impression was that the server was fairly new. Pre-bussing was good although I must admit that I'm a slow eater so my plates were still on the table when we left. The only negatives were that the AC was low and the server forgot my drink order. She was very pleasant and when I asked her for a Diet Coke she immediately brought one back. 

In conclusion, we will be going back to Siam Cafe. The star of the show was the food - give it a try y'all.

Really enjoyed this brewery... Not only good draft beer, but great atmosphere to consume tasty beverages! The outside seating was great, plenty of activities, such as darts, board games, live music and sports on TV.  My favorite Brewery to visit.

Mostly a review for the beloved CBB. She ain't a looker, but boy was the flavor amazing. It's pretty much an eggs benedict and the biscuit is drenched in this delicious jalapeno cheese sauce with lots of Cajun flavor. I can't even accurately describe it and do it the justice it deserves. Our eyes literally widened upon first bite and we were scraping every last drop of it off the plate when we were done. I've never had or seen anything like it.

We ordered another more average plate of grits, ham, and eggs but the CBB stole the show. The service here is also amazing! The staff is so friendly and they seem genuinely happy interacting with their customers and each other. Very homey, welcoming vibe. We came here for breakfast on a whim and found this to be one of the most memorable meals we've had in New Orleans. Thanks Majoria's!

Meh. 
Gimmicky. 
Pretentious. 
Overpriced. 
Hipsters. 
Pizza is good. 
Not a value. 
Poor service. 
He creates his own demand. 
In Philly, people are too smart. 
Similar quality elsewhere at 2/3 the cost. 
The staff are just weird. 
And, despite what they think, they aren't cooler than me.

Terrible, my least favorite cheesesteak ever.

Even shouting "whiz wit" at the lady, and she gave me attitude. Everyone looked mean inside.

While I'm a fan of chopped, I'll give this place a try, but it was oily and with no flavor. I think the super extreme blind patriotism kind of bothers me. They made a big deal about "ordering only in English." With how much they love America, isn't it weird since it's a supposed town of brotherly love, a country founded by immigrants???

Political rant aside, you're better off going the other side of the street.

Sure, sure, the Rocky Steps & his statue greeting you, tempting you to mimic him & tackle this feat - which many cheesy tourists were certainly doing....the Philadelphia Museum of Art has so much more to offer 

( we did not tackle the stairs as it was 90+ degrees & we had just walked forever to get there ) 

Pricey for sure but nice collection of Impressionists paintings & etchings... who knew Degas, Renoir & Pissarro did etchings?? 

Mary Cassatt, Degas, Renoir, Monet, Manet, Cezanne, Van Gogh.....WOW! 

Wished we had had more time to check out the Chagall works...ah, next time 

$16 to get in; $22 for special exhibit 

Pictures ARE allowed...just make sure the flash is turned off

Eating vegetarian in the Big Easy isn't all that easy - and knowing this from our 12+ years of visits, we spent a lot of time before this year's vacation, researching our options & luckily we found Bayona!

Jazz Fest dinner on the docket.....you *definitely* want to get rezzies ahead of time!

Since there was no "real" veggie entree on their menu, even before we could wonder, our waiter was nice enough to make a special trip over to review their entire menu & what they would be able to offer as entrees for us veggies ( we had let them know ahead of time about our restrictions )

Started out w/ drinkys - included the Stormy Morning w/ elderflower & violet liqueur & sparkling water. Mr had the Smoking Jacket & while we both liked the whiskey & blueberry & chocolate tones, we felt this would have been a perfect after dinner drink. The elderflower was much more of a refreshing starter drinky

Split a couple of appies - 1st was the Chilled Tomato & Beet Soup. Very pungent tomato but the beets totally held their own.  A few bites into this soup we were loving it but after a few more, it started to taste like ketchup - you might want to split this soup to keep on the refreshing-side of things

2nd split was the Mushroom Crouton - all kinds of awesome. Piece of toast w baked goat cheese on it & served w marsala-marinated mushrooms

My entree was Lentil Salad w/ tomatoes & creamy goat cheese dressing. Nice vinegar taste & refreshing on such a warm night

Mr chose the Asparagus Risotto w/ Smokey Mushrooms, Zucchini, Yellow Squash. This is usually a side dish served w/ their steak option but they were kind enough to leave out the meat and we didn't have to pay the meaty price!

Creamy & lightly flavored w/ the asparagus, I found myself skeptical about the mushrooms.......they tasted to me like they had been cooked in a beefy sauce - but I will also admit that smoky flavorings always trigger my meaty-paranoia, so while this may have been a truly veggie dish, I had my doubts & did not ask to confirm

Best dessert wine EVER was the '09 Muscat Alicante Casta Diva.  I am so totally tracking this down!!! Sweet, fruity & a huge honey base. This was heaven in a glass & went perfectly w/ the strawberry buttermilk cake w homemade pistachio semifreddo

Thanks Bayona for kicking off our New Orleans visit in the yummiest way!

After a fab dinner at Circles, our nice waiter guided us to SPTR for a nightcap 

There was a great beer selection & we got to try some things we normally wouldn't have chosen - fun to experiment! Awesomely nice waitstaff! 

German birthday buddy tried his first IPA.....a SF IPA.....he wasn't a fan. I'm not an IPA fan either & warned him but I thought it was awesome he at least was adventurous enough to give it a try 

I tried their Apple Cider & it was okay - tasted kinda vinegary at first but left a somewhat sweet aftertaste. Don't think I'd get it again 

Next tried a Royal Porter - kinda too hoppy for my taste - I like a smoother finishing beer 

So although we didn't find our fermented nirvana we had a great time perusing the menu & taking a stab in the dark & that makes for an A-OK joint to me 

Joy Division playing inside - I knew this place was way cool! Their menu looked extremely Pub-like & promising w/ lots of veggie options & I expect a star upgrade after we get to enjoy their foodie wares!

Eating Vegetarian in New Orleans requires planning ahead & as we researched possible veggie options before our latest getaway, Cafe Abyssinia was a must

We arrived around 8pm & were practically the only ones there but by the time we left, the place was hopping

Started w/ the Sambusa - spicy mix of cabbage & carrots in a Samosa-like pastry shell. It was outstanding!

Dinner consisted of the Veggie Combo - just the 1 & we split it - glad we read the Yelp review ahead of time about this dish being enough for 2 people b/c it was huge......& delish!

Mild Yellow & spicy red lentils, collard greens w garlic & onion, cabbage & carrots, & potatoes & carrots.....loved how the milder veggies paired perfectly w the spicy & the injera bread was the perfect vehicle with which to eat it

Very laid back & nice neighborhoody kind of feel - this will def make our list of repeats for our next trip!

The best advice I can give anyone wanting to come to The Lark?  Make reservations!  I'm a planner & I get rezzies everywhere we go & this is the exact reason.  As we were approaching the hostess stand, they were turning away group after group, saying they were fully booked for the evening.....& now we know why

Serving both small & large plates, our waiter advised he would be happy to let us know if we were ordering not enough or too much & we ended up w/ the perfect amount.....he also steered us towards the veggie options which was awesome b/c you never know what's been fried in what these days!

Also to note, dishes are meant to be shared & come out as they're prepared, so you're constantly treated w/ flavor & delights

We shared:
Pimento Cheese Fritters - Gouda, provolone, pickled serrano chilies, grilled bread - OMG we wished we had ordered like 3 more of these.....SO good & just the right amount of spice

Smoked Persimmon & Burrata - Never would have thought to pair persimmon with burrata but this was likewise incredible

Acorn & Kuri Squash - served with chestnut mousse, vanilla poached cranberries, pumpkin seeds - the squashes did all the talking & we loved the creamy & wintry flavors

Chickpea Tagine - served w/ radicchio, rainbow carrots, goat butter, apricots & almonds - again loved the mix of flavors and had a lovely complexity of flavors

Washed it all down with a lovely local red ( can't remember which ) but this was another recommendation from our server & he certainly knew his stuff

Not ones to pass up dessert, we asked our server for his recommendation & were steered towards their banana bread pudding - WOW.  This was the special of the season & the bread pudding was spongy, the caramel sauce & ice cream made it that much gooier 

If in the area again, first thing I'd do is make a reservation!  This is an experience to repeat!!

A true foodie's heaven! You'll want to come here hungry! 

There is absolutely something for everyone here... and then some! 

Chocolates, cheeses, coffees, cookies, cheesesteaks, pizzas, meats, seafood, gelato, pastries, not to mention all the specialty foods 

Everything is extremely fresh & there's no wrong place to start digging in 

Snagged some local cinnamon honey & chocolates.....we got there too late to try the famous Apple Dumplings & they were closed Memorial Day Monday - boo! 

But next time, my pretties.....for sure!! The plan will be to come for breakfast & eat my way through dinner!

This was one of those meals that was perfect from the moment you walk into the restaurant up until you leave completely stuffed and satisfied.

I had my eye on this place for a number of reasons:
- I saw it on Best Thing I Ever Ate for the Blackened Drum, which also interested me since I never heard of nor tried Drum fish before.
- I saw they had Turtle Soup, which I also always wanted to try, mainly just so I could say "tonight I dine on turtle soup" like Shredder.
- of course, lots of high yelp reviews.

K-Paul definitely did not disappoint. They start you off right with a massive bread basket, with 5 or 6 different types of bread, all piping hot and therefore delicious. The excellent waitress cheerfully offered us a second basket after we quickly polished off the first one, and we had no choice but to accept.

Then came the soups to start - we got the Chicken and Andouille Gumbo ($7) and the Turtle Soup ($8), which both tasted about the same somehow. They were very tasty, but I would skip them in favor of the bread and the amazing entrees.

I almost panicked when perusing the menu, as I didn't see the highly touted Blackened Drum on the menu. But all was ok when the waitress told us the specials, which included an awesome Surf & Turf deal, which included the Blackened Drum as the Surt half. The other half was their also excellent Blackened Steak. This entree went for $43, which wasn't bad considering how delicious each bite was and how much food it included. There could have been a bit more steak, but they give you a nice sizable piece of the Drum, which lived up to the hype, and a nice portion of creamy delicious mashed potatoes.

For our other entree we shared the Fried Rabbit with Tasso Cream Pasta ($33). This was also amazing and worth every penny of the seemingly high price tag. This was one of the richest and most satisfying dishes I've ever had. The rabbit was amazing and fried lightly and not too overwhelming. The pasta on the other hand, was pretty overwhelming due to the cream sauce and the copious amounts of tasso ham, but it was worth every bite too. This dish is an excellent choice (it is actually supposed to come with shrimp, but as another sign of the excellence of this restaurant, the waitress was happy to allow me to choose any substitute for the shrimp since I have a shellfish allergy).

The food was so good we were able to forgive the fact that it took an incredibly long time for it to arrive. After the soups, we probably had to wait at least 30-40 minutes for it to finally come out. But as yet another sign of the reason this is a top restaurant, the friendly, attentive waitress came by and apologized and let us know they would give us dessert on the house since we had to wait so long.

Never one to turn down dessert, especially when it's free, we were happy to share the Bread Pudding ($6), another New Orleans staple. This was an excellent rendition, though I prefer having some nice cold ice cream to offset the warm, gooey bread pudding, and here they give you a huge dollop of cream on top instead. Still delicious, but a little too heavy after that huge meal (you know you're a fatso when you wish for some ice cream to provide some refreshment after a large meal).

I would add K-Paul's to the list of must try restaurants if you are visiting New Orleans and want to experience food that is both delicious and typical of New Orleans cuisine, in a nice, romantic ambience with good service.

Luckily I saw in the news a week earlier that Jimmy Fallon stopped by here for cheesesteaks for some reason, or I probably wouldn't have ventured over here to get one of the best cheesesteaks I've ever had.

This is more like John's than it is like Pat's/Geno's/Jim's - it's a tiny little shop that is frequented by way more locals than tourists. There are a few cramped seats at a counter inside, with a few more tables outside. There is gruff, yet somehow friendly service, that moves quickly to handle the crowds.

Most importantly, the cheesesteak was really incredible. I got it the way the lady recommended, with American cheese and fried onions, which is also my favorite way (I'm not as into that neon whiz). The sandwich was huge, with a ton of delicious chopped up steak. It wasn't heavily seasoned, but it still tasted great.

Whenever I go to a place like this or John's, which are crowded and still have small wait times, I'm baffled at why people wait in lines down the block at Jim's. Sure, the cheesesteaks at those places are good, but they're either as good as or not as good as these tiny local places.

Do yourself a favor and skip the insane lines at the obvious places - come here instead for one of the best cheesesteaks in Philly (and therefore, the world).

Decent food, but definitely not one of the best places for fried chicken in America.

Again, maybe this hype ruined it for me. It also might be that I'm just not a fan of this type of skin for my fried chicken - they apparently use a wet batter or something, which makes it very shiny and greasy, but not at all crispy enough. The meat itself is very juicy and tasty though. WARNING: if you don't make the request for "extra white meat", you will get NO white meat. The normal fried chicken plate ($10) comes with three pieces of dark meat, which is mad weak. If you order the "extra white meat", you get one breast and two pretty worthless, nearly meatless pieces of dark meat (I think a leg and a wing).

Other than the fried chicken, the rest of the food here was pretty underwhelming. The fries were pretty good actually, and were nice and crispy, but the red beans and rice were pretty standard and not really worth it. We figured we should split one other entree, so we also got the Country Fried Pork Chop ($8.50), which was definitely a mistake. It was pretty flavorless, so even though I always prefer variety, I would highly recommend just getting more of the fried chicken if you come here and plan to get more than one entree.

As stated in some other reviews, my wife and I had the advantage of being a small party of two, which allowed us to jump over pretty much the entire line, which was filled with several large groups of tourists dining together. This was a relief since the line was halfway down the block of this vacant, desolate area. Unfortunately, once we ordered, it took an unreasonably long time for our food to come (around half an hour).

The place itself is full of the southern charm and good service typical of most of the places I ate at during my visit. It's also packed full of the other aspect I was so used to, plenty of tourists. It's also pretty funny considering that the place is in a pretty rough neighborhood. It was humorous watching the poor, toothless old men sitting on their porches conversing unintelligibly with the middle-aged white women in their fanny packs on their way to binge on some beige.

I don't think it's quite worth the trek out here, especially if you make your way by foot like we did. If you want some excellent fried chicken, you are better off staying in the French Quarter where the action is and hitting up Coop's.

This is a must stop every time you are either passing through or staying in Philly for any amount of time.

No matter what your mood, there is always something here for you, with endless options for sweet and savory foods.

For the best savory bite, you should head over to Tommy DiNic's for the Roast Pork Sandwich with broccoli rabe and provolone. Featured on Man vs. Food as well as his show on the Best Sandwiches in America, it really is an amazing sandwich and worth the sometimes huge line in this chaotic market.

My favorite sweet things include The Famous 4th Street Cookie Company right by the entrance, serving hot, freshly baked excellent cookies, and the Apple Dumpling from Dutch Eating Place, which is so sweet it will make you shake. Don't forget to try Hope's Cookies also though - located all the way in the back, they have some really amazing cookies and tons of other chocolates and sweets.

Whether you want some authentic Philly eats, or you are one of those Chinese families that must eat Chinese food no matter where you are, or you want an overload of excellent dessert options, Reading Market's got you covered.

VEGAN EATERS HERE.   Remarkable veggie burger, toothsome, pickled onions, fresh greens and sauce the a side of similarly great, salty, peppery fries on the side ordered a side of panko crusted onion rings that were amazing for the tenderness of the onion itself. Easily the best non-meat burger we've had, probably ever. 

Why the four stars then? Not able to ascertain it was vegan as opposed to vegetarian and, bun was probably brioche which means egg. We were in a hurry, so didn't want to be as specific as usual. It would be easy for this stylish spot to remedy and they should, judging from the comments from many people who have tried it. 

The other reason for the four stars is the price, $12.00 is a hefty price for a veggie burger no matter how good. Service was tops and as mentioned previously, Mesa Burger is REALLY attractive and convenient. We will be back, no question.

Those who live in Tucson are VERY LUCKY to have Bubb's Grub!!!! SERIOUSLY LUCKY!!!!!! 

I love BBQ and search for joints in every city I visit. I've been lucky enough to have dined numerous times on some of the finest Texas BBQ in Austin, Texas- Stubs, Rudy's...etc 

Bubb's Grub is REAL DEAL Texas BBQ! I'm from SoCal and can't find REAL Texas bbq here.....some good bbq, but nothing that brings back memories and flavors of Texas. I was visiting Tucson last week and drove north just wandering around......I saw a small restaurant in the middle of nowhere (ok, I'm from SoCal.....this seemed like the middle of nowhere) it had a big sign that said "WORLD CHAMPION BBQ" with a big painting of Texas on it...... I went back to my hotel and told the wife that we were having bbq for dinner. If you see a restaurant that says "World Champion".....YOU MUST STOP AND EAT. My order was take out so my review is for the food only. It turns out they were world champion for their bbq sauce and pulled pork....I think in 1998, forgive me if I'm wrong. 

The pride and joy of Texas bbq is brisket.....this was some of the best brisket I have EVER had; almost tender enough to cut with my plastic fork, a nice amount of fat running thru the meat, incredibly juicy, and the smokey flavor, spice, and crust was out of this world...BRAVO Bubb's!!!! YOU ROCK!!!! You must be proud of your brisket to offer "burnt corners and pieces" as an appetizer! Oh I wish I had 2 stomachs that night! I also had the pulled pork.....Fantastic, and the bbq chicken....Fantastic... The beans were great, smokey, and spicy, not sweet. Their bbq sauce is just wonderful, their spicy bbq sauce is wonderful, and their mustard bbq sauce is wonderful. Some say a bbq sauce is truly special when you would consider drinking it just by itself......Bubb's is pretty damn close! 

The menu is huge and has so much variety....but since I had only one chance I ordered the staples to test their Texas authenticity. There are plenty of sandwiches, appetizers, salads, and sides. The staff was very friendly and helpful with all my nerdy bbq questions. I loved Bubb's so much that I would certainly pay to overnight their food to my home in SoCal. I've done this once before from a North Carolina bbq joint....that's how much I love bbq! They even serve Texas toast!! 

I just feel like cursing right now.....F&^K YEAH Bubb's! 

If you live in Tucson and eat here all the time....I ask you to slap yourself once in a while before you sit down at Bubb's to appreciate and remember how lucky you are to have this quality of bbq in your home town. AMAZING! I WILL BE BACK!!!!!!!!!! Thanks Bubb's!

I had called this hotel in advance to ask them if it was okay to do an early check-in and they were okay with it.  They also said the room would be ready by the time I got there.

When we got there to check in, Denver was helping us and he was going to put us in the back hotel not even affiliated with Hyatt.  That made zero sense, especially since I'm a Gold Hyatt passport member.  I was clearly upset, because I was not expecting to use my Hyatt points to stay in what appeared to be a 2-3 star hotel.  Denver asked us to be patient, while he figured it out. 

In the end, Denver was able to get us an ocean view room on the 3rd floor.  The room was perfect and it was clean.  We heard the ocean waves crashing at night with a cool, crisp breeze in our room.  Denver almost disappointed us, but in the end he made our get away perfect and he was patient and accommodating.  

The hotel had a cool beachy, but Spanish vibe. I totally digging that. 

*Parking- You can either valet for $25 a night or find street parking

Seriously, I shouldn't have given this place a chance even after reading their reviews.  I wanted to give them the benefit of the doubt.  I'm a fan of Shabu Shabu and it's the perfect when the weather is cooler. I happened to be there on a cooler night and I stumbled upon this place and this is apparently the ONLY Shabu Shabu you can get in the Santa Barbara area.  I think this place has potential, but it needs a lot of work.  

The Kobe beef didn't seem fresh at all and they barely give you any veggies.  They don't have flavored broth here, too, so my soup was plain.  My wife ordered California Roll and caterpillar roll which was $18. Overpriced much? 

Our bill ended up being about $50 for not even mediocre food and this place was overpriced and customer service was lacking, too.  I think we were only checked up on once and it wasn't even a busy night.  

*The parking here can be tough since it's on State street, but you can find street parking or park at the parking structure.*

Alright so ever since I told people I was heading out to STL for a few weeks everyone kept ranting about Pappy's Smokehouse and that it was ranked as the best smokehouse in STL 3 years running. So naturally on our first week out in STL we decided to stop by this joint during lunch time. As we head over to the joint, we notice that there is not much going on around the area and even at some intersections, it seemed pretty sketch. But determined by our desire for Pappy's we finally made it to the restaurant. We walked into the back of the restaurant and there was already a 30 minute line at 11:30 which made me realize that this place was going to be solid. 

The servers are all very friendly and they were talkative as we waited in line. I know this sounds nerdy and slightly off topic but this place has gotten their customer service waiting system down perfectly. They have literally figured out the perfect number of people to allow within the restaurant and how to space out the customers so that by the time they are done ordering, your food comes out to your table (in my case before I even got to my table). Perfect management of customer waits. Now back to the main point of the review. This joint is a casual smokehouse and they have pictures of all the menus on the walls that have been signed by "celebrities" It is in quotations because you will notice that some of them are not actual celebrities but have made appearances here and there on shows. They have all different types of BBQ sauces on the wall and as you get to the front of the line, you see the trophies for their award winning BBQ. They have a few options for sandwiches but I decided to go with the two meats option and ordered the brisket and pulled pork. I received the fries and slaw as my two sides.  I know that most of you are probably saying whoa this guy has no idea how to eat bbq because I did not order the coveted ribs but that was for two reasons. 1) It is an aggressive lunch item 2) if they could do these two meats well I knew the ribs would be an automatic win. Now this is coming from a person who has had tons of Texas BBQ so I feel like I know a thing or two about BBQ. 

They have a few different types of BBQ sauce but I would say that the Sweet and Original are the two sauces that you want to hit up. The hot is nothing special. Now the Brisket had full flavor and was pretty solid but after a few bites of the pulled pork and one rib from a friend I knew that it was my least favorite. But trust me no regrets here still. The pulled pork was seasoned to absolute perfection. The meat was super tender and extra flavorful. Although it went well without any bbq sauce I am a bbq sauce fanatic so I had to pour some of that on. The bite of the rib that I had was just awesome also. It was super sweet and tender with the meat just falling off. The right amount of crisp on the outside also. The slaw was actually totally awesome. I loved this oil and vinegar based coleslaw. Totally underrated and something you should consider. I honestly wanted a few more helpings of this cole slaw.

All in all, this place is a Class A establishment and with the impeccable and friendly service it is impossible to knock down the rating from anything but a 5. I am just sad that I cannot eat here every day because I would gain 80 pounds but I will definitely be back a few more times before I leave STL.

I do not give out 1 star reviews lightly. Trust me, this pathetic excuse for a high-end bar has earned it. 

Vango likes to present itself as a sophisticated urban lounge. If only the staff, management, and patrons acted like it was such a place. In reality, this place belongs on MTV's "The Shore". 

The first thing you'll encounter is a huge numb-skull bouncer who will check your ID and stare you down. If you're lucky, you'll get patted down and searched like you're entering some ghetto club - right off Rittenhouse Square! Then you can walk up to the main level, which will blare cheesy pop-hip hop till your ears bleed while you wait for a bartender to give you the time of day. Once this happens, you'll be overcharged for a drink. And you NEED that drink if you want to get up to the main attraction - the roof deck. The bartenders have different glasses for anything nonalcoholic, and another burly bouncer with no brain but a huge bright flashlight won't let you upstairs without an alcoholic drink - even if you're the designated driver for a large party! 

The city view on a nice night? Admittedly, a bright spot. But half the roof is roped-off with VIP couches for bottle service - and I don't think the surroundings justify the expense. I don't think bottle service is ever worth the expense - why? So some other saps may look longingly over at your couch and bottle on ice? Please. 

And that brings me to the crowd. Vango seems to attract guys that like to pump their chests out and strut around in shirts unbuttoned just a bit too far. And the girls? They're showing skin in a way that screams "I think I'm too sexy to talk to." A true wasteland of hangers on and wanna be achievers blowing money trying to impress each other. 

When thinking of this place I'm reminded of a Dave Chapelle skit, one where he's imitating Rick James. In character he says "I wish I had more hands, so I could give that 4 thumbs down."

This must be rated highly because choices are limited. We've ordered here a few times to see if they gave improved and they never have. The pizza and canzone as always overdone to the point the crust has been black each time. The dough is rubbery and disgusting. The sauce is flavorless. I can't see how anyone who enjoys pizza could give this a good eating. Disgusting.

The newest Japanese restaurant to hit the Reno scene, I was fortunate enough to visit Haru during their 'sneak peak weekend'. 

The outside of Haru depicts a beautiful glass painting of cherry blossom trees on their front doors. The interior is spacious, with numerous tables, a bar area, and a bar for drinks off to the left. The decor is simple and minimalist. 

Their limited menu for the special weekend consisted of ramen, and numerous, skewered options, perfect for sharing between two people. Unlike the other ramen places in Reno, I really liked how Haru offers you not only the options of which flavor of ramen you'd like (between miso, tonkatsu, and shio), but two broth options as well (house broth, and tonkatsu broth). The ramen at Haru is my favorite ramen in Reno thus far! The combination of the house broth paired with shio was clean and rich in flavor. The ramen also came with pork belly, bean sprouts, enoki mushrooms, green onion, soft boiled egg, and naruto (fish cake). The noodles had a good chewiness to them, and I loved the smaller, square cut of the pork belly slices. I could tell that the pork belly slices had been grilled, and were of higher quality. I usually don't eat the soft boiled egg as I prefer harder boiled eggs, but upon trying it I was pleasantly surprised to find that it was seasoned with garlic and other well paired flavors. I hope that in the future the option is available to get additional toppings on the ramen. 

My boyfriend and I also shared many of Haru's skewers. We tried their galbi short ribs, bacon wrapped enoki, ribeye with chimichurri, chicken wings, and chicken skin skewers. The chicken skin tasted very similar to chicharron, while I unfortunately found the ribeye with chimichurri too spicy for my tastebuds. For the galbi, the server had asked how I liked the meat cooked, which I really appreciated. 
 
Overall, all of the food we had that night was super delicious. They were very short-staffed, so service was not the fastest, but the owner and other servers present were still very courteous. Sadly there was no dessert on their limited menu for the special weekend, but the owner assured that something was definitely in the works. The prices weren't bad either; definitely cheaper than the izakaya in Midtown if you just came for the yakitori/kushiaki, and about the same prices for the ramen as the other places in town, but for better quality. You could tell the owner put a lot of thought and dedication into the Japanese dishes he offers at Haru.

I can't wait to go back! I'd definitely recommend trying Haru out!

We love to eat local when we travel, but this place failed in my eyes. 

The food was good, the service was beyond slow, and the prices were shady. We stopped in here during a busy time and were greeted with a 30-minute wait! It wasn't a problem, and we went for a walk while we waited. We probably only waited about 15-20 minutes before being seated. We ordered right away, but our food took about 30 minutes to come out.
