This is the only market where I trust the take away and enjoy it.  PS to my omnivore, vegan, vegetarian and paleo friends, there are an equal number of great options for all.

CHEESE:  A very good selection of domestic and imported and a super helpful woman, who also once lived in my former home city, works there who always has a wonderful tip or two. .

PRODUCE:  Leans almost all organic, has local vendors (like Purple Sage and Peaceful Belly) and carries things no one else does, like the fresh Emmett grown strawberries that went into October this year.  Their seasonal offerings can't be beat.  This week they had two kinds of fresh kumquats, most groceries carry none at all, and beautiful escarole.  

BAKERY:  Local breads, like Gaston's wonderful Pouichette and Acme's teriffic breads of all kinds are sold here.  Their in house bakery has the most mmmmmarvelous ginger cookies and lots of other good things.   They have Wildflower Bakery  treats, like baked apple cider donuts or blueberry pound cake on a display.  They also have Boise's  own Guru donuts.

PACKAGED FOODS:  In addition to staples, like canned tomatoes, in brands we use, the Co Op always seems to have what I'm looking for that is hard to  find elsewhere.  Pomegranate molasses, for example..  They also have a great selection of top end, Italian made, speciality shape pastas.  My husband is a very happy guy that they have Willamette Valley Fruit Growers frozen berries in the freezer section in 2 pound bags.  

DAIRY: The dairy section is a bit small, but they have yogurt and buttermilk which does it for me.

MEATS $ FISH: The meat section is also a bit small, but what they do have is organic and humanely raised and the butchers there know their stufff.  The fish selection is even smaller and we normally find ourselves at Reel to buy ours.

TUNES:  Music on the sound system is so great it makes me want to sing and dance as I shop.

INSIDE SEAT TO EAT: There is a nice area inside where you can sit to nosh.   Seating is both at high counters and  standard tables so accessible to everyone.  

THIS N THAT:

1) PARKING:  Can be bumper cars even though the lot is good sized.  Proceed with caution.

2) ACCESSIBILITY:  From accessible parking in the door and throughout ample aisles, all is good.

3) NEIGHBORS:  The Co Op Wine Shop is unarguably the finest in Boise.  It may even be the best wine seller we've ever had the fun of shopping at and it is just across the parking lot.  See those reviews too.  Richard's Cafe Vincino two doors down from the Wine Shop is a wonderful place for lunch or dinner.  

4) MERIDIAN ON THE HORIZON:  Co Op is opening a second location in Meridian.  Will be closer to home for me.  Wohoo!  Their goal is summer 2015.
CLOSED.  Although with a 2.5 star average on Yelp and owner who seemed to let this place slide from marginal at opening to worse as time went on, I imagine it isn't going to surprise or upset many.

Fast casual food eatery, a newly opened locally owned franchise of a 84-ish unit chain HQ'd in Alabama.  Delicious food; bright fresh Mediterranean flavors from a scratch kitchen, no freezers or fryers in the place. No kidding, y'all, this "food for the masses can be good and healthy too" concept originated in Alabama!  I loathe chains.  But I sure am a fan of this location for this one for good eats and friendly people.  We left eager after our first meal today eager to return.  I never thought I'd say that about a chain restaurant.

HOURS:  Lunch  only 11a - 3p for now.  Take out dinner packages to serve 4 people are available starting at 2p if you call ahead to order.  Dinner hours planned in the future.

LOCATION: This Eagle outpost is the first of three planned for the Treasure Valley and the first Taziki's to open west of Denver.   Across from Starbuck's parking lot off State Street and Edgewood.

THE DRILL:  Whether it is so on all days or only because today was their opening day, we were greeted on entry by a nice young woman who handed us a well organized foldup menu and said she'd be happy to answer questions if we had them.  We did and she did.  Every one and in the kind of "good answer" way that made us want to stay and eat, although that had not been the plan going in.

We proceeded to the counter to order and pay for our eats, were given a number for the table, they delivered to us and both the  young woman and the manager came by to thank us for coming in and wanted to know how we liked the food.  Easy answer - a delicious surprise!  They bus for you when you're done.  All good!

MENU:  Choices for omnivores and vegetarians...gluten free options too...a range including the following (prices rounded):
* soup - Greek Lemon Chicken ($4)
*veggie salads - grilled proteins can be added including chicken, turkey, beef, lamp, tilapia, salmon or shrimp ($4 - $14) 
*appetizers like hummus and pimento cheese ($5.50ish)
*gyros of fresh pitas filled with grilled meats or veg ($9 - $10)
*"Mediterranean Deli" sandwiches ($8 - $9)
*"Feast" plates with protein & salad & side ($10 - $15)
*Daily special listed on back of menu - ex: Tues = pork loin sandwich ($9)
*Desserts - chocolate cake, cookie, baklava ($2- $3)

A children's menu has four options each $5.

Take out dinners for 4 people, available starting at 2pm (call ahead order necessary) include 3 options for protein (chicken, pork, lamb) with 2 sides and salad ($27 - $40 so only @$7 - $10 / head).

EATS:  Their proteins do not come pre-portioned and shrink wrapped like other fast food places - they cut their own.  (For example, the lamb which was grilled to make our delicious gyro with skordalia sauce.)  Gryos and sandwiches come with chips and choice of side.  We selected pasta salad with fresh tomatoes, herbs and just kissed with a balsamic dressing. Other side choices were roasted potatoes (remember no fryer - yahoo!), fruit, tomato-cucumber salad or basmati rice. 

VIBE:  High ceilings, industrial look, cement floors, some high top seating, step up booths and standard height seating and chairs...my personal must have fav.  Outside tables with umbrellas on a sun drenched, south facing patio. High ceilings plus hard surfaces equal noisy setting, but music was set at a reasonable level to not compete with conversation.

ACCESSIBILITY:  Accessible (aka ADA) parking at side lot. Level in the door. All on one floor.  Standard height table seating.  As it should be 28 years into the ADA but you'd be appalled at how many new Boise area restaurants don't follow this law to allow all people equal access.   They do here.  (I have MS so pay attention.) 

A TIP:  Right next door work is going on for a new Italian restaurant, owned by the same guy who owns Rembrandt's in Eagle.  Scheduled to open August-ish time frame.  It will be called Cacci, an abbreviation of the owner's Italian surname, and will be open for dinner (maybe lunch too).  Hooray for that.  Taziki will have a good neighbor and vice versa.

tHe FuNky tAco.  Quirky charm in how they lay out their name suggests the personality of this food truck evolved to downtown located bricks and mortar eatery.  Yet, but for a Yelp reviewer's high praise of FuNky  I would have passed it by.  And that would have been my loss for good food, friendly service and fun vibe all at reasonable prices any time of day and a true bargain for Linner specials as that friend (who will remain nameless but whose initials are Joy W. :-)) was first to share in her review.

The FuNky folks say their goal is to have diners leave wanting more.  Goal achieved with us for sure!

Letting FuNky tAco owners speak from marketing materials describing their focus: "We have no boundaries, we have not put ourselves in the proverbial box, we are free to create. We are tHe FuNky tAco. We create food within a "farm to funky fare" framework. Our emphasis is on Asian, Indian, Mexican, and Americana ethnicities / styles of food.  We religiously support our LOCAL farmers and our menu selections will morph and change with the seasonal yields. We have options for everyone, the carnivore, the omnivore, the vegetarian, the vegan. We love and think about you all." 

My husband and I love them right back!  In our omnivore but leaning to plant based and persnickety way of ours about wanting to know what's in the food we eat and where it comes from.  Noting some who reviewed FuNky don't share the affection in full, I'll offer information that might be good to know before you go so you might love it too.
 
DRILL:  Order counter is up front as you enter with paper menus on the wall to your right to take and peruse.  Folks who shared that they felt confused or rushed in needing to order right away may not have known the paper menus were there.  Those menus are your friend, as will be the nice person at the counter who will happily explain anything.  Order, pay and seat yourself at a table, booth or at bar counter, you'll be given a number and they'll find you to deliver when food is ready and clear when you're finished.

MENU:  Short and easy to navigate - 

*10-ish tacos with options for all eaters from vegan through omnivore.  Tacos come in pairs (except at Linner of 3p-6p weekdays when some are offered 'onesie') at about $10.75 for pair (+ / - 50 cents).
*3 sides at $4 each.  On our visit they were cream corn (vegan), pinto beans or small power greens salad. 
*10-ish options for starters / sharers ranging $4 - $11 including larger sized salad ($7), kimchee quesadilla ($11) and not-to-be missed cauliflower ($11).  

EATS: We enjoyed were - 
 
*Piggy Stardust Taco - slow roasted pork butt, pickled red onion, cilantro, lime crema. 
*Chicken Roja Taco - grilled chicken thigh, salsa roja, peppers, onion, feta and radish.
*Fried Cauliflower (vegan) - panko breaded and light fry served with bomb sauce, habanero salt, cabbage and tortillas.   Along with "don't miss" I recommend "share" because this dish easily served 3 lighter eaters who were also enjoying a taco each.  (From first hand experience - the cauliflower is great as leftovers!)

House made flour tortillas (2 for $1) are cherrywood smoked which gives them nice 'je ne sais quoi'.  These flour tortillas were perfect size and 'flex' for the generous amount of filling in the tacos.  (Corn tortillas available on request but they are not house made.)  The chips made from the house tortillas are in unusual and large pieces so you'll need to break them up with your fingers to eat them.  Criticism of the chips turns up in some reviews so worth mentioning - but we like to "play with our food".

LINNER: We visited early during their Linner Time (3p-6p weekdays), not only for discounts on libations and some food as well as option for onesie (generously sized) taco (only $5) but also because this 'tween lunch and dinner time frame (aka early Happy Hour) fits my introvert (seriously) nature to avoid crowds and chaos.
  
THE LIBATIONS: Wine and beer.  For fellow winos...umm oenophiles...this is not a wine list you'll likely use.  Rotating taps for beer.  Also local Meriwether Cider.  (The Pineapple - Jalapeno cider was dee-lightful.)  Margarita-styled drink made with the hard cider. 
 
SERVICE:  Friendly, helpful, and attentive.

VIBE:   Unique art by local artist Bruce Maurey on walls.  An upper level stage where musicians perform on some nights. (Check Facebook for schedules.)   Sound system during our visit had nice music mix set at level that didn't compete with conversation.  Seating is at booths or standard height tables (hooray - the days of my boosting into a high stool are in my rear view mirror) and chairs, plus high seats at the bar.  Outdoor tables and chairs on front patio.

ACCESSIBILITY:  Level in the door and most on one floor.  Ample space for path of travel to tables and loo (two, gender neutral, both accessible).

PARKING:  On street. Good luck with that.

""Mezze mezze."  The term used by my Italian in laws meant "some good, some not so good".   They would say it accompanied by a shoulder shrug.  I'm doing the same for our two dining experiences at Fork.  Maybe our expectations were too high given the buzz about this place.  We'll return to give Fork another at bat to see what we missed the first two times.  If our third experience is like the first two, then three strikes and Fork is out.  

AMBIANCE:  Interesting but not the 'all that' we anticipated.  The light lined patio in the front is part of what makes one want to go in to this converted old bank building.  The main dining room has the benefit of being lined with big windows but seating is oddly arranged with some banquettes and too tight tables.  There are also sardine can tight tables in a secondary smaller room. (Tip:  Avoid that one.)   The bar has counter stools and a couple of high perch tables on the periphery with not a single spot of standard height seating.   High ceilings and lots of hard surfaces makes the acoustics poor.  

SERVICE:  Friendly on both visits.   

The first time we sat at the bar since all restaurant tables were full at 7:30 on a weeknight and we didn't want to wait 40 minutes for a table.  As evidence that not everyone has had  "mezze mezze" experiences at Fork, I offer up in fairness that these kinds of crowds typically come in due to good things.  

Applause for Jess, the bartender, who knew the menu well and could describe dishes to the people ordering from the dinner or dessert menus at the bar.  She was adept at mixing great cocktails while taking orders for and delivering food from the kitchen all with smiles for her customers.  She could teach a master class in how to get this right.  

Our second visit was at brunch on a Saturday late morning and the restaurant was nearly empty.  The server was very friendly but food coming out of the kitchen had long delays and one of our two dishes arrived lukewarm while the other was hot.  This suggests one dish waited on the other in the kitchen with coordination problems on the line or between the kitchen and server.  

FOOD:  This was the big disappointment; both flavors and presentation. Most dishes were just OK for flavors and some were off for temperature at service.  Food looked as if just plopped on the plate, presentation that suggests lack of attention in the kitchen.  Were this Denny's, we'd say that would be consistent with low expectations. But to have that happen at Fork was not what we expected.  On the plus side, the cinnamon donut holes with chocolate and peanut butter dipping sauces were as good as we heard.  We enjoyed them at the bar for dessert where they arrived piping hot out of the kitchen with interesting presentation.  (And at $9 in a size to easily serve 2 or 3, a good value too.) 

MENU / VALUE:  Broad number of options and across price points.  Choices range from $2 for a biscuit to $9 for a unique Caesar salad to $11 for a club sandwich to $14 for mushroom ravioli or trout to $25 for a flat iron steak.  Given the range of prices and options, seems that two could dine well at Fork without libations in the mix for as little as $40 before tax and tip.

LIBATIONS:  Full bar with great cocktails at on par prices.  Also have a decent number of wines by the glass and an extensive by bottle offering with an appropriate focus on NW wines.  Bottle prices seemed too high for lower end offerings, like King Estate Acrobat Pinot Gris for $40.  Higher end wines, like $127 for Leonetti Merlot, seemed on par.  Nearly four dozen bottled and canned beer options. 

THIS N THAT

1) GETTING IN THE DOOR:  Patio is on street level and entry to check in at the restaurant or dine inside is up a flight of stairs. For those who can't climb that many stairs, includes me as I have MS, Fork built a ramp along the side of the building with entry through a side room door. From the strollers parked in that side dining room during brunch, we'd say a number of folks use this access.  It is the law (ADA) to provide a ramp like this, of course, but not all places do it. 

2) COFFEE:  Worth singling out the coffee service as it is unusual.  Good dark roast, served in a huge mug is brewed as pour over.  At $3, you are allowed only one refill.  When we sat at the bar coffee was served piping hot.  At the brunch service, the first mug was served lukewarm.

3) ALAVITA NEXT DOOR:  Not big fans of Fork but we're smitten with  sibling, Alavita, located next door. Same owners. Italian themed.  http://www.yelp.com/biz/%C3%A0lavita-an-italian-joint-boise

Juniper was fallback choice for Happy Hour when first choice was closed. (There's a First World Problem. No complaints.)  Splendid serendipity to have been vectored here.  The list of things enjoyed was almost as many as the years of wedded...umm...bliss being celebrated.   Vibe, menu, foood, service, price point all get thumbs up.

VIBE
All people will feel welcome here from those in little black dress (as was our hostess) to the bartender's jeans and shirt. During our late afternoon into early evening (about 4:30 - 6:00) folks of all ages (from twenty to seventy somethings) and all attire (including shorts and tees) arrived to take tables in and out. 

Music mix was nicely eclectic to fit the space and tuned low enough in volume to be a thread in the tapestry of the vibe but not take over the experience or drown conversation.  Nice!

Two story interior was remodeled from a former restaurant for uber cool meets warmly inviting design. Exposed a wall of brick on one side as counter point are sleek black wood tables and chairs, unadorned for meal service but for white cloth napkins with black design. Look up to creative lighting options. 

Open only three weeks let's hope they keep this universal appeal going and don't devolve into "hipster central" because this is a location for people of all stripes who are lovers of great food and drink.  Nolo timere, fellow Boomers! ;-) 

SEATING
Some tables on front patio.  About 14 high stools at the bar. Maybe 35 seats at standard height tables with banquette seating and chairs line the wall on main floor.  More standard height seating up a flight of stairs.  Seats 120 overall I am told. 

Plenty of space in the aisle way for service staff or guests on their way to and from tables or the loo. That owners avoided the "sardine can" in traffic flow here is "yahoo" worthy. So is that the bulk of seating is standard height tables and not obnoxious (IMHO) high perch tables.

SERVICE
Top notch for warm welcome, good attention and follow through. We were greeted promptly, given menus and had "the drill" explained when we asked questions. Our server knew the menu, could answer questions and also make recommendations. We felt well tended but not hovered over.

LIBATIONS
Specialty menu leans to gin cocktails, one of my favs, and then it dawned on me...duh...Juniper...what is a key ingredient in gin? 

Both gin mojito ($7.50) and Juni and the Jets ($8.00) a perfect summer sipper of muddled grapefruit, gin, St.Germaine, and prosecco were expertly crafted. 

Thoughtfully assembled by bottle and glass  wine list and approachable prices. For big "woohoo" they had two sparklers by the glass and a third poured at brunch times. 

Coffee is Dawson Taylor ($2.50) served hot in white mugs.

MENU & PRICES
Food is  fresh twists on classics along with new creations that leverage seasonal and local ingredients. That there are so many options that encourage small plate or shared plate dining is right up our alley. Chef Aaron Wermerskirchen clearly knows his stuff for creativity and execution.  Prices ranging from $5 to $25 are a good value for this quality. 

FOOD
We ordered a couple of things and both were excellent so we are eager to return. Fried root vegetables were crisp and seasoned just right and came with warm blue cheese dipper (@$6). Mussels and clams with chorizo and sweet red pepper (@$14) came in a broth so delicious and perfectly seasoned we asked for spoons to be sure we got every drop along with the three generous baguette or batard slices sent out with the dish. The only suggestion we'd make is for the kitchen to put grill marks on that bread to have it be an even better partner for the broth.

The dessert menu is short, four or five options all presented in the same way in a mini mason jar.  We shared rhubarb and strawberry with pistachio crumble that came with a scoop of fantastic cardamom ice cream (@$5).

THIS N THAT

1) LOCATION: Downtown next to Matador. Parking can be a bear on street.

2) ACCESSIBILITY: Level in and throughout first floor. Many standard height tables. Ample floor space for path of travel. Upper level seating is by stairs only.

3) HOURS & HAPPY HOUR: Love that they are open straight through from about 11a to 2a, so if you like to dine for late afternoon "linner" you'll find them open. No Happy Hour here but since they are open straight through, there are lots of options on the lunch menu (until 5) or dinner menu (starting at 5) for that purpose.

CLOSING 12/23/20 FOR HIBERNATION UNTIL SPRING 2021.  Hibernation is the word used in the trade now to describe the action of a restaurant to close to wait out the pandemic until Spring.  A number of good local restaurants have done this. (Txiketeo and The Modern come to mind.)  The Stuffed Olive announced this week their plan to hibernate; see the notice below.

This isn't an eatery I would often choose simply for menu of what I might describe as white-bread-American-suburb take on Italian plus soup, salad, sandwich format.  We all have different eating lanes. But food is prepared with pride and welcomes are warm.  

I admire the local owner operators here who have done everything right every step of the way from the beginning of challenging pandemic times.  In the beginning days when eateries were closed they offered take out including 'family meal' style that really could feed a household for multiple days as one of the options at a time when many were being cautious about going out.  When restaurants were reopened for inside dining they followed all the spacing and mask protocols and when deciding they were too small an inside space to reopen inside service they did take out and made it easy to pick things up.  

Along with all of these challenges they were one of a couple businesses in the strip mall where they are located to have had building services problems (was it plumbing or electric...I can't recall now) to result in multiple day closure even for take out and then they were vandalized leading to another extended closure for repairs.

Through it all these owners operated with graciousness in communication to their customers and with respect for their staff.  I'm a fan of their behavior and tenacity in the face of these tough times.  

Here is their "gone hibernating" message:

"Friends, family, and community members.   Like many others in this industry, we have made the decision to shut our doors for the winter. This temporary hibernation will be difficult, but is critical to our longterm success. 

Restaurants are, at their core, a gathering place. As we face a winter where gathering is discouraged, and in many cases downright dangerous, we feel this is a necessary step to take. Therefore we will be closing our doors until we can once again invite you to sit at our table and commune with us free of restrictions. 

We truly appreciate the genuine outpouring of love and support we have received up until this point. This year has thrown many unexpected punches, and we are deeply grateful to the members of our community for helping us weather the storm. While we realize this decision may disappoint some, until we are truly able to gather again this was the only choice for us...

Thank you again to all of our cherished patrons, friends, and community members for your support!

Merry Christmas, happy New Year, and until next time,
The TSO team"

In the unexpected location of a strip mall in Boise's north end you will find this gem, a crown jewel really, pastry café.  From sparkling and warm ambiance to the same in welcoming service to the absolutely remarkable pastries, "c'est magnifique!"

Baking, they say, is about precision and chemistry.  I say pastries this remarkable also involve artistry, a bit of magic and passion for the process and outcome.  You can feel the love in the surroundings here and taste it in every bite.

Were I a Boise resident I'd manage my calorie and financial budgets to be a frequent customer at Janjou.   As a visitor to Boise, this is on my "do not miss it" list.  It recharges body and soul to go to Janjou.  Highly recommended.  We wish this was in our neighborhood. 

THE VIBE:  Urban cool and "ahhhh...some" warm all at the same time.  White walls, dark wood floors, chic white tables and chairs with chrome bases and legs, sparkling windows looking to let in lots of light, sparkling pastry cases displaying lots of artisan bakery delights. Gift bags with brown and orange tissue paper peeking out add a punch of color.  Just right café music mix set at the just right level to support conversation.  People coming and going seemed all ages and walks of life; truly a neighborhood "all people are welcome" place.

THE SEATING:  Seats for roughly a dozen people at six two-top tables  and maybe half a dozen more at high counters with stools at the front windows. On nice weather days there is additional seating at café tables and chairs on the front walkway outside. 

THE BACKSTORY:  Patissiere and Janjou owner Moshit Mizrachi-Gabbitas moved to Boise from Israel in 2007.  She graduated from the prestigious baking school Estella kitat Oman in Israel and completed worked at Patisseries there.  In 2008 she open Janjou Pâtisserie which she named after her mother.

THE DRILL:  Choose some delights, you won't be able to stop at just one, from the case displays of pastries or quiche.  There are also little cylinders filled with cookies or chocolates which make perfect take away for yourself or as gifts.  Espresso beverages are available too.  Order at the counter, they'll deliver to your table, bus your own.

THE DELIGHTS: I kid you not when I say in learning the Patissiere was introducing the Breton pastry kougin amann to the line up beginning yesterday morning, that my husband and I made it pilgrimage to the bakery (we live in Bend Oregon six hours away) to try some.  These orbs of tender dough folded with butter and sugar are hard to find in American bakeries and these were excellent!  Worth the trip or those alone, but we also enjoyed framboise choux (puff pastry filled with raspberry cream and topped with fresh raspberries) and a bostok (think brioche toast meets frangipane) to take away.

We thought prices were very fair too.  Is I recall our choices were @$5 - $6 each.  We have our eye on quiche ($6.95) on our next stop in.  Not to mention I have a doctor to whom I owe being well enough to travel to Janjou.  I think a gift bag of cookies from Janjou will be a nice thank you. 

The coffee service was also perfect.  Americanos we ordered (12 oz $3.20) were hot and bold.

THIS N THAT

1) LOCATION & NEIGHBORS:  Look for the Marketplace strip mall.  Mazzah Mediterranean is a neighbor.  So is Airbrush nail salon. 

 2) PARKING:  Ample parking in the mall lot, there's a location advantage!

 3) ACCESSIBILITY:  Accessible parking in the lot and curb ramp onto walkway.  Level in to the patisserie and throughout.  Saw a mom with a stroller inside and that means room for wheelchairs too.  Loo is accessible down a hallway.

4) FUN:  In the hallway at the back of the cafe you'll find a window that looks into the bright kitchen where the pastries are made and you can watch the Patissiere and her team creating the pastries.

During 2020 pandemic months and through the hot summer of 2021 we have shifted our patronage of Bodacious Pig from dine in to take out and in that use not so much for ourselves but as gifts for friends or neighbors who needed a meal as thank you or because they were injured and unable to feed themselves.  Just as from our first visit as inside diners here in May 2014, the first of dozens of meals, in this 'all people are welcome' inside space delivering consistently good service and delicious food, Bodacious owners have managed a business and team of people to deliver top notch experience for take away too.  Orders called in have always been right and ready on time when we go to get them.  (Yes, you can order delivery via 3rd party app like Grub Hub but small businesses pay big fees for that and it eats into their already narrow profit margins so picking up yourself supports the business better.)  And food to go is as delicious as food eaten there.  The pick up window is outside and so easy to park, pick up and go.  A tip:  If you're ordering cold sides like slaw or green salad to go with the hot meal ask them to put the cold things in a separate bag so they aren't wilted on the way from hot package.  Another tip:  The wedge salad and Cobb salad made here might be the best version  of those served anywhere in the Treasure Valley and they also 'travel well' as take out.

Size does matter.  Bigger is not necessarily better.  It is easier to scale down a successful big model than size up a small one to work.  These 'truisms' came to mind as we soldiered through our first - and likely last - meal at Joe Momma's new location in the old Famous Dave's BBQ building which Joe Momma's owners purchased, revamped slightly and opened for business last week.

They have painted inside accents of the eggs and chickens motif of their old location (it in leased space in aging strip mall in Eagle).  But  given they upsized seating by 300% (from just under 90 to almost 290) in this yuuuge building, it seemed as if the mascot-motif should be a cow for the "moovvvvee 'em in to the feed lot" feel of the place.  Nothing worked for us.

I like eateries to evolve so I'm not 'boo-hooing' about change of address.  I seldom went to JM's old location because the waits for a table could be long and other eatery options are plentiful.  I imagine waits will be less long to sit down here, given the tripled number of seats, but everything about this huge space is awkward.  And whether you wait 15 minutes now for a table vs 45 in the old space and then wait 45 minutes now for not-as-ordered food to reach the table since with cattle-call seating of 290-ish capacity neither servers nor kitchen can keep up,it is equally 'tilt' for us.

TIP: May be wisest not to plan for quick work day lunch hour here.

VIBE:  Similar to the Three Blind Men and The Elephant parable, you may have a different view of this space depending on where you sit.  The seating being used for dining in the dark bar is all high top tables too close together and step up booths at walls.  In spite of ADA going on 29 years old, if you have a disabled person in your party, you will not be welcome there.  If you sit in the cavernous main dining room with high timber ceilings and too-bright lighting and manage a table near the fireplace, you may be happier.  Or if you sit in a booth along the walls.  But tables down the center of that room are too tightly spaced for anyone's comfort.  And if your party includes a wheelchair user, passages are too tight for that person with only a table or two in the worst location coming into the space being available. (There's a "thanks for your service - NOT" to a vet in a wheelchair.)

Also 'thumbs down' to the cheap 'mess hall quality' awkward flatware.  And for the distant 'mono quality' sound system playing pop music mix.  And for the table clearing process involving a person carrying big plastic tub around to dump dishes into it...crash, clang...

SERVICE:  Very friendly folks trying hard to cover the too many tables in the too big space.  A long pause between seating and greeting and disconnected food service throughout.  See rest of review for details.

MENU:  On oversized, double sided laminated page and a tad confusing looking but actually not difficult to wade through. New items have been added and old favorites remain.

EATS:  Lackluster experience of not as ordered food and lukewarm dish for one of us.

Something we appreciate about JM's is Benedicts are offered in half portions.  For which we always order the eggs "poached hard as golf balls".  I the old location the kitchen always got this right.  So we each ordered half-Bennies here.  Alas, not so good for eggs outcome.  With no way to fix it.

Because after a long-ish wait a runner arrived at our booth to 'auction off' our dishes.  "Who gets Carnitas Bennie?"  Answer "He does".   With "OK" as response the plates - his warm, mine not - were plopped on the table.  Our very nice server was busy somewhere in the huge space but nowhere in sight so we went ahead to eat around the eggs.

In a medium-ish while she arrived to check on us but we were half-ish finished with the food.  The revelation the eggs were wrong was met with sincere "Oh sorry...".  A phrase we also heard the hostess say to folks walking out as well when she asked "How was everything..." with negative feedback offered by some.

This was in essence 'soft opening' week.  So hiccups are expected.   But my instinct is this place is just too big for them to get it right.

BOOZE IS A PLUS?:  Although JM remains a breakfast into lunch hour eatery with "Breakfast"  embedded in name and hours no later than 2:30, JM's owners acquired a full liquor license when they bought the Dave's building.  (Given how difficult it is to sell behemouth sized old chain restaurant spaces, Dave's building owners may have been eager to offer the license to sweeten a sale).  So for those who really must have alcohol with breakfast or lunch, you can get a bloody Mary or mimosa or beer or shot of Makers or anything else.  (They don't start pouring hard stuff until 10:00 per state liquor control rules.)  Given we'd heard "multiple flavors" of mimosas touted, we each ordered one - cranberry for him, raspberry for me - with lunch.  Marginal even at $4 price.

VALUE:  Two Half Bennies + 2 Mimosas = @$25.  Good value.

Indifferent service, salt lick meets greasy-soggy food, "WHAT DID YOU SAY?" levels for music and noise.  Two strikes visits.  We don't need a third to know "they're out" on our list.  If it isn't evident Matador in Boise is part of a restaurant chain, the chain roots sure show with Casa del Matador. (They are links in the same chain.)  I write few one star reviews.  This one is fitting. 

If it wasn't oddly amusing on its' own that the food is so bad in such an overwrought interior design space, the fact that they seem to mistake themselves for French Laundry for no menu modifications is really laughable. Here are examples. Comical in hindsight.  Irritating at the time.  

1. One dish came with a grilled flour tortilla.  We asked if we could substitute a corn tortilla.  The server hmmm...ed and hawwww...ed.   Probably not, she said, the kitchen does not like to substitute.  Give it a shot we asked.  Pretty simple thing.  Well, she said, I'll try.   Good thing she was successful because the corn tortilla (it was served with just one) was the only edible thing for a mushroom dish that was literally too salty to eat.  Yet our server did not ask why we left it uneaten when she returned at the end of the meal.  

2.  A taco sampler contained pork, chicken and beef tacos.  We don't eat beef so asked if we could substitute another pork taco in its' place.  Probably not, said our server.  The kitchen really didn't want to do things like that.  They had 'rules' from...and here she didn't say corporate but that's my memory translation of the message.  Give it a try, we said.  If not, just leave the beef one off.  I'll have to charge you the same price even if it is left off, she warned us.  Yes, we said, yes, that's no problem.  No sense bringing us something we won't eat just because it is included in the price.  OK, she said.  The kitchen apparently did have dispensation to substitute pork for that beef taco.  Not that it mattered much in the end given the tacos were so soggy sitting in greasy liquid when delivered that eating them was not so good a thing.

We don't eat at the Burger King chain but we do know the jingle and wondered if we should wander into Matador chain corporate offices singing a few bars.  "...special orders don't upset us...have it your way." 

Not that any of this is the problem of the folks serving the tables or manning the cooktops.  I imagine it has to do with policy.  But there you go.

There are places to get good Mexican - American themed food in the Boise area.  A couple for authentic Mexican food too.  Casa Del Matador is among neither group.

THIS N THAT:

ACCESSIBILITY:  Level in the door.  Some standard height seating in the perimeter areas of the restaurant and outside.  But the 'happenin' stuff' is in the bar area and that's where most will want to sit.  Yet if the Governor of the State of Texas, a man who uses a wheelchair due to being paralyzed in an accident, or actor Michael J. Fox whose walking is limited due to Parkinson's disease, or U.S. Congresswoman Tammy Duckworth whose legs were severed in Iraq, wanted to sit in the bar they would likely find not one single standard height seating table that they could use. The ADA requires they have seating available to them for equal access.  It is a Civil Rights law for inclusion passed in 1990.  Casa del Matador was built in 2015.  Beyond belief that they didn't know better.  The law has been in place for 25 years.

The front of the menu says WELCOME and they mean it. Owned by the same nice family as much loved Pueblo Lindo 'mothership' in McCall, this eatery is in remodeled space previously home to the defunct Souper Salad in a Meridian strip mall.  A little off the beaten path to see it from Eagle Road, you'll need to drive into the mall parking lot to find it.  (My husband and I have been driving by weekly since late September like raptors after prey waiting for it to open.) The same extensive menu as Pueblo Lindo McCall, good food and friendly service.  Setting expectations up front being important, I'll share they are in 'soft opening' mode now so expect some kinks in service and food timing and you'll be happier...or wait until they have the new place wrinkles ironed out. 

VIBE:  Bright interior colors, fun sculptural décor above and things like sombreros as wall decor.  Big windows at the front let in light but also lots of sun and they have thoughtfully provided sun shades to help with glare for those who choose a window table.  There are booths against walls and standard height tables with "woven barrel base" bottoms and chairs of similar design throughout.  The hitch-in-the-giddeup for this seating is one cannot put their feet under the table, feet are blocked by the barrel base, which means one is sitting a good way back from the table - even those of us with short legs like me (5'4") and hubby (5'7").  I imagine this might be even more awkward for taller people with longer legs. 

SERVICE:  Today (12/4/18) is the first full day of operation (they opened with dinner on 12/3) and there clearly are opportunities for service staff training for a couple of folks on diner care (as in following up after food is delivered and when there are long waits between order and food to table) and process delays to work out for food coming out of the kitchen.  No worries as this is expected in what is their 'soft opening' window.  That's what this period is for - to work things out.

And I say 'gracias' to whomever hired the skilled and adorable (those dimples!) Orlando, who worked at one of the nearby competitors before being hired to train at PL in McCall and come back to Meridian.  He has a natural instinct for diner care and he was also helping his teammates.  As diners we appreciated the work of all of them.

MENU & FOOD:  Another Yelper posted very good menu photos so you'll find options and price points there.  We ordered our favorites from the McCall location from Pueblo Lindo's lunch menu (fresh spinach enchiladas for him and pollo en mole for me) to compare apples to apples for the two kitchens.  We thought the food at this new location was equally as good and maybe even better than the McCall location as this kitchen seemed more expert in restraint for salt.  And the whole beans (as option to the also good refried) were particularly good here.

All is house made. (Except maybe the tortillas.)  And the salsa is delicious for our taste-buds for being spicy and chunky with white onion, scallions and tomatoes incorporated.  I regret I didn't ask for a spoon to eat it without the need for chips calories included!  (Although the chips are very good too.)

LIBATIONS: As with McCall, options are soft drinks, a small selection of wine or beer and pre-bottled Margaritas.  We chose water here, served in tall glasses with ice and a pitcher for refills set on the table.

VALUE:  Two diners well fed with just-big-enough-but-not-too-much sized lunch entrees + one flan = $23

ACCESSIBLITY:  ADA parking in associated lot.  Level in the door and all on one level.  Standard height seating but at barrel bottom tables that would not allow a wheelchair user to get up to them.  Didn't check Loo.

NEIGHBORS:  For location notes - Pho 779 is on the right and Hot Spot Café on the left.

Name change forced by threatened litigation, Pizzeria Sazio will soon have a new sign outside with their new name Red Bench Pizza.  Sazio fans should worry not that yet another pizza place has bit the dust at this location that has seen others meet their end.  Same owners but when served with legal action by a Florida restaurant that had the Sazio name trademarked, the owners felt it would be better to change the Sazio name than pay licensing fees.  New name has roots in "Red" for the pizza sauce and "Bench" for the neighborhood location in which they're located.  The owners also plan to make a few changes to the vibe and menu, making it less Italian-centric, they say, and more casual.

Sad news is Pizzalchik owner Brad Breakell died yesterday at the home he shared with his daughters.  The Statesman broke the news last night, Thursday night.  Pizzalchik has always been a family run business, with Brad's son behind the counter with him on the times we were in.  It seems to have been struggling in the last year or so and we recently learned that Brad had turned over day to day management and ownership to one of his daughters.  Maybe after he created a good amount of controversy for the restaurant by posting on line ads where he dressed up in character costumes perceived by some, well even by many, as to be racial or ethnic stereotypes.  You'd have to have met him and talked to him to know this always wearing tie-dye and knit beanie child of the 60's and still rock-n-roll band member and sometime actor was the furthest distance from racist.  But he made big 'oh no' mistakes with those ad postings.  There was even nationwide coverage of it.  the controversy took its' toll on the business.  And that wasn't a first for Brad, nationwide coverage, since Pizzalchik got Diners Drive Ins and Dives coverage on Food Network back in the day too that helped put Pizzalchik on the map.  The family is grieving and plans to keep the restaurant open.  I wish them all peace of spirit.

Tasso has moved to be 'in the house' in downtown Eagle - the little old house once home to Zen Bento - as of May 4 2021 after closing the original downtown Boise location in 2020.  Same delightful owners, the chef (Dan) and his wife (Hannah) who is a nurse, with similar menu to the original Tasso including unique, outstanding, handcrafted sandwiches, salads and sides.  Here as always the owners apply pride of ownership integrity to running of the business.  My husband and I celebrate Tasso opening in Eagle because we live here (so do Tasso owners we learned) and this is a much shorter commute for us than when we were driving to the Boise location and back.  But if you have to commute to get to Tasso your taste buds will tell you it is worth the trip!

First meal at this new location and the sentiment from first review in 2018 at the now closed Boise location still applies:  "Remember a first date ending with a kiss so delicious you were still thinking about it the next day?  First lunch at Tasso was like that date and the sandwich was like that kiss.  So delicious that my husband and I were still talking about it the day after.  We returned for another delicious meal and concluded we may have had sandwiches as good as Tasso's but we can't remember having any better  - anywhere or ever.  If you think sandwich is art form, try Tasso."

Go! 

THE MENU & EATS:  Divided into about 10 Sandwiches ($9 - $13), 4 Salads ($7 - $12.50), a couple of sides and a changing soup option.  Everything is scratch made with something for everyone in options to delight vegans, vegetarians and omnivores.  The owners' strategy is to do a few items and do them excellently with high quality ingredients.  The clever combinations have flavors play perfectly with the others.  Every sandwich has been mmm...marvelous as was our order today, a new to us Kimichi Club ($10.50), with tasso ham, sous vide turkey, kimchi, herb sauce, cilantro, mayo, pork cracklings and miso slaw.  Dan has changed bread and we like it this new just right crispy and chewy and tender baguette style even more!   Sandwiches are big enough to share and come with a really fresh green salad with oven roasted tomatoes, pepitas and lovely rice vinaigrette.  (How Dan coaxes all that flavor into rice vinegar is a mystery.)

THE DRILL:  Order at the counter from large hand painted menu on the wall https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/tasso-eagle-2?select=uXjKY-PvIjgfZm0dWHRHrQ&userid=3CwMwbY9UgP-qvTDxNs_0g or place your order via Tasso's website to pick up at scheduled time.  (To go menu photo here.  https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/tasso-eagle-2?select=-_MFR5kpAZnXv9aKidaS-A&userid=3CwMwbY9UgP-qvTDxNs_0g  ) Delivery available via UberEats.  (But, really, don't choose that option if you can help it.  Uber not only adds $ to what you pay for each item but they charge small restaurants commission / fees that really bleed already small profits.)

VIBE:  Tiny old house space is light and bright and sparkling clean inside.  The fun and eclectic assortment of art that was in the old Tasso in Boise is here too now displayed as 'gallery wall'.  Pride of ownership shines.  If you're eating on site you'll find a plethora of standard height tables and chairs (hooray for standard height everyone can use) on the patio outside the old house and about half a dozen high stools and small counter and one small table for eating inside.    

LIBATIONS:  In the Boise location Tasso sold wine and beer in addition to soft drinks.  Looks as if they may have only soft beverages here for now. 

ACCESSIBILITY:  Tasso's entry is level in from the sidewalk and all on one floor with ample space at the order counter. There is a loo on site but I didn't check it for ADA standards.  Accessible parking is extremely poor throughout Eagle and the nearest spots to Tasso are all the way down by the Senior Center.  That failure is City of Eagle's not Tasso's. 

PARKING:  On street or lot in back of building.

THEIR "FOOD LANE":  My husband and I hold Tasso in the same high regard for food quality and hospitality as we do local eateries which are also husband / wife / family owned with a chef driven kitchen creating excellent food and customer centered hospitality with integrity in business practices.  Those include restaurants like Madre Boutique Taqueria, Ansot's Basque, Alyonka Russian, Certified Kitchen & Bakery, Janjou Patisserie and Casanova Pizza all in Boise as well as Amano Mexican in Caldwell and Bacquet's French and Bodacious Pig BBQ  in Eagle.  All different cuisines and service formats and yet all the same in focusing on excellence by owners of the business.  Tasso drives in that lane too.  If that lane is one you appreciate as a consumer, Tasso is a sandwich place you'll love. 

IF I WERE QUEEN:  I'd wave my scepter and update online ordering site (they are using Square) to let the customer make requests, like "please hold tomato on albacore tuna sandwich...".

HOURS:  Tue - Sun / 11a - 7p

This is apology for how unattractive my review behavior was previously when I was hangry.  And I'm going to use this to mention a don't-miss-it seasonal pizza that will be off the menu in March because sometimes one regrets not having had the advance chance to know of fleeting delicious things.  Read on. Prego.

FIrst the apology.  Look at me stomping my review feet last Fall when I discovered for the first time that Grimaldi's re-stokes their coal fired pizza oven in afternoons daily and so no pizza can be ordered after 4:00 or served before 5:30.  Daily.  I was perturbed that the first world sort of problem was only learned by me after we went in the door at 4:00 hungry with pizza on our radar and unable to order it.

Now I know better the OOS oven hours to put this in perspective.  I mean I had it in perspective before.  The lesson is don't write reviews when hangry. 

So this is a 'do-over" review given we have been in Grimaldi's twice in the last two months to enjoy delightful mid-afternoon service (thank you Connor) before the ovens shut down.  And on this most recent visit was also the happy discovery that Tuesday is half off bottles of wine day so we could order a full bottle for less than the price of two glasses.  We got to sip wine (no, we didn't drink it all, we left some for our server to enjoy post shift) and enjoy the warm space on a cold winter day while we listened to the "old Italian neighborhood" classic songs from Sinatra, Dino, Sammy et al to which my old Brooklyn - Italian husband knows every word (and with which I would sing along had the wine bottle been finished).

But we came for the Seasonal Special pizza - Onions Braised in Red Wine, Italian Sausage, Fresh Basil and Mozzarella.  It was one of the tastiest pizzas enjoyed during  five years of Boise area living.  As high praise I suggest this was a pizza that could make Tony's Pizzeria Teatro (arguably the best in the Valley) proud if it came out of that oven.  Perfetto all around for just enough toppings and not too much and just right crust finish with just right coal oven char.

Is there a new manager in charge of the kitchen or was it just good fortune to have the seasonal pizza perfecly done on that day?  We may need to try it again before it departs the menu in March to find out.  It is one to put on your "to eat" list too, I think.  And as tip - leftover slices taken home hold and heat well but have no fewer calories as leftovers than if you ate it all there. 

A reason to leave room while there for 
dessert is the cannolli which is filled just before being delivered to the table and very good here - the best of any in the Boise area based on our 'research' - and is nicely shareable by two with a Illy Americano.  

But if I could change one thing, I would move this concept-chain eatery out of The Village so parking and getting to the door was easier.  Village Parking is a bear. The darned parking problems are the only reason besides the numbers on the bathroom scale that we don't go to Grimaldi's more often.  

PS - Grimaldi's now has a liquor license to expand beyond wine and beer and a full bar will likely be launched sometime in Spring.  See what you can learn if your all the way through a long review?

Once upon a time I thought Cuban food was the second most delicious thing to have roots in that beautiful and beleaguered country.  The most delicous thing?  Andy Garcia.

While I still so appreciate how yummy is Mr. Garcia, time passes and at my age priorities realign to put him in second place.  Now my vote for the most delicious thing with Cuban heritage is the food.

How lucky are we in the Boise area to have remarkable Cuban food in this independently owned restaurant where pride of ownership shines in every detail.  From the ambiance, to the service, to the food it is all fantabulous.

Gems like this are rare.  They can be fleeting given so much depends on the people who own it and cook the food wanting to continue to do that.  Enjoy it now.

VIBE
"Welcome to Cuba" says the little sign near the cash register as you enter.  But even if you didn't see that sign, you might know where you were.  The Cuban music playing at just the right level on the sound system, the aroma of garlic and braising pork, rice, toasting bread and simmering beans, the warm colors, the tile floors and wood tables, the photos and posters of Cuba on the walls; on each visit you'll likely notice some new detail.  Like the lyrical hum of some of the diners and staff speaking Spanish, a beautiful language that in this restaurant sounds especially so.  It sparkles in every sense of the word, from the greeting at the door, to the pristinely clean surroundings, to the stellar service to the flavors in the food.

SEATING
Comfortable chairs at standard height (hooray) tables throughout.  Some tucked into alcoves, some in the center of the room, some in a separate room (a great spot for a private party).   My husband and I particularly appreciate that even if full house the seating is arranged in a way that one feels they have 'elbow room'. 

SERVICE
Welcoming, friendly, gracious, efficient, delightful.  This has been a perfect experience for us on each visit from the beautiful young woman who was covering the entire restaurant.  Top notch.

MENU / FOOD / VALUE
The multi page menu is the same from opening at 11a through dinner service that ends at 9p.  You'll find appetizers, entrees, sandwiches and sides all of traditional Cuban food.

Don't miss the soup list on the back page.  In addition to the delicious black bean soup served daily there is a special soup for each day of the week.  If you go on Thursdays, do not miss the garbanzo bean soup that has a wonderful full flavored broth with pork and potatoes.  Remember that tip.  And note if you order a sandwich you can substitute a cup of soup for the fries that come as normal side for only a $1.99 extra.  Leave the fries.  Order the soup.  You'll thank me.

You can't miss with anything on the menu.  The tostones con mojo (fried plantains with garlicky mojo sauce for dipping) are wonderful. ($3.99)  So are the black beans.  And the sweet plantains.  My husband loved the bacalau, a cod dish simmered with tomato and bell pepper sauce with potatoes.  ($11.99)   Braised pork shoulder asado with onions is served with a side of black beans mixed with rice and also yucca with garlic that is scrumptious.  (And a bargain at $9.99.)  You'll find shrimp dishes and classic chicken dishes, like arroz con pollo, and sandwiches including the ever popular Cubano.  Sandwiches (around $8) are large easily shared by two, and stand out not just for the perfectly crafted fillings but for the Cuban styled bread on which they are served.

Portions are generous and we always eat very well here with leftovers to take away for just about $30 for two people and that includes a couple of beverages and always (always!) a dessert to share.  Look at the dessert card on the table (beverages on the flip side) and save room.  I recommend the Flan de Coco, a dense coconut flan drizzled with real caramel or the Cuban chocolate pudding. (Each about $4.00)

LIBATIONS
Soft drinks, bottled beers domestic and imported, a few wines by the glass and housemade Sangria ($4.50).  The Sangria is delicious.  So is the Cuban Espresso ($2.50) made with coffee brought in from Miami; the perfect counterpoint to any dessert.

THIS N THAT:

1) PARKING: Private lot.

2) ACCESSIBILITY: No marked accessible parking in the lot. There is a curb ramp accessing the sidewalk at the front door. Level iin and throughout. Single stall in loo likely too narrow for people who cannot stand and step in.

3) 7 DAYS A WEEK:  It must be exhausting and daunting to be open every day of the week in a small restaurant ilke this.  Hats off to them!

4) FOOD TRUCK TOO?:  Note a spiffy looking food trudk sometimes parked behind the restaurant.   Seems as if it is a mobile until for the Casa Blanca sandwhiches.

Wow! I've definitely been missing out. I've heard for awhile about the deliciousness that awaits at doormet and I finally got around to trying it. Their menu consists of gourmet sandwiches, salads, pizzas, pasta dishes and more. You order at the counter and they bring the food to your table. Kind of reminded me of Panera bread, except WAY better and made from scratch. I ordered a half size salad, the "house"- romaine, cucumbers, tomatoes, bacon, and gorgonzola dressing. The veggies were so fresh and tasty! I also ordered the marsala pasta: rigatoni, garlic, spinach, mushrooms, and a creamy garlic/mushroom sauce with parmesan sprinkled on top. So good! The only complaint I have is the price. I wish they had something like a pick 2 pairing option. The pasta was 15$, salad was 5$, and with drink and tip it was 25$. You are paying for better quality, though. They also have vegan/gluten free options. My girlfriend had a gluten free pizza that was amazing! I'll definitely come back.

First time here , really disappointed , when first came in said not seating for 30 minutes , kitchen it backed up
, that should have been a clear picture as to what this place is about 
Food not the best , service wasn't nothing to speak of.told at The beginning to separate  checks , didn't . Waited long time for food while others sat after us and they got their food before us . Water on floor , my friend told the table about it , they left , staff didn't care , 
People got seated , staff talking let them sit , , he told us his limit to wait is 10 mins , hit 10 mins no one showed up , they left , Person at front who sat them told them as they left hope food was good ,that was a joke they never got served .
This place needs help  badly

Wow! It has been a   l o n g   time since my last visit here!
I was greeted as soon as I walked in and told to have a seat anywhere that I liked. They had a Ruben pizza on the specials board , I would have ordered that because it sounded interesting. Sad face, it was last months special and they no longer had it. I ordered a medium build your own with wild garlic sauce , sausage, red onion and extra cheese, I also ordered a Coke to drink while I waited for my pizza to get made. They filled my Coke before I left!
It did not disappoint! Very tasty and cheesy! I love the crust, I actually eat it all! 
Yes, I do recommend that people try them!

I was with Amanda L. , we were celebrating my daughter's and her mother's birthday. Everyone got something different and it all looked very good. Most of us were happy with their meals. One of the sandwiches had so much cheese sauce on it that it was making the bottom bun soggy. That person ate their meal quickly! My Barbacoa Mac n Cheese was not very hot when it came out. When I asked for it to be heated he took it back with no problem. It was very hot when it came back out. It was good, very cheesy, I did wish there was more Barbacoa in it. The service was excellent! He brought out a pitcher of water so we would not run out of water and filled it at least once. He also made sure to fill the other drinks. I would like to go back and try some more of the dishes!

I was in on June 3rd with my family, to celebrate three birthdays.
My sister ordered the vegetable sample platter for us to share. I had told her that I was planning on ordering it for my lunch because I wanted what was on it more than anything else. This made it so I could order something else. I ordered the catfish basket with sweet potato fries and added some fried okra. I love fried okra! The breading on the catfish was light and did not over-power the catfish. Every thing that I ordered was cooked perfectly.
Everyone else really enjoyed their choices. The staff did a great job keeping everyone's drinks filled, and making sure that no one needed anything else. Everyone liked the bright colors that the walls are painted and the decorations.

Sorry , I did not take any pictures today! I was too eager to eat!
I ordered pot stickers and squid with spicy pepper salt. The pot stickers are the best that I have had. They are big and the meat they are filled with is tender and nicely seasoned. They do not count on the dipping sauce for flavor. The dipping sauce is very good it is just the right amount of spicy. They are easy to eat and do not fall apart like many others that I have had.  
The squid has a flavorful not to heavy breading. It is slightly chewy, as squid tends to be, but it is still fairly tender. They gave me a small container of chili sauce , in case I wanted it hotter. I dipped some in the pot sticker sauce and it was perfect! I am glad that I always ask for extra pot sticker dipping sauce! I enjoyed this meal very much!
If you have not tried the Chinese Duck House yet you should soon! I highly recommend this small, simply furnished place. The service is quick and friendly and the food is excellent.

This was my first time here and I look forward to coming back and trying more things on the menu! I ordered the pork belly tacos. The meat was tender and nicely seasoned, the cheese gave a nice tartness to the dish, it was also topped with pickled shaved carrot and pickled onion.  For me the carrot and onion overpowered the pork belly and liked it better when I took it off and ate it to the side. I tasted the onion rings and enjoyed the batter that was on them.
The service was very good, drink refills were offered in a timely manner. Prices even though they are a little high for my pocket book seem fair for what you get. With some planning I will go back and try more dishes.

I came here today because I really enjoyed the food and service during the recent Yelp event and wanted to try it on a regular business day. It did not disappoint! I was greeted as soon as I walked in the door and told to sit anywhere. As he was getting my water I looked at the buffet. Although it had a good selection of dishes I decided to order off the menu. 
I ordered the Papadum, a lightly spiced lentil wafer $1.50 and Tandoori Gosht Dalwala , Lamb pieces cooked tandoori style with black lentils $11.95. When he asked how I wanted it, mild or more spicy, I ordered it mild to get an idea of the dish. It was very good , however the next time I think that I will order the 1 spicy, and see how that is. The lamb was very tender, I could cut it with my fork! The lentils were tender and tasty and the rice that it came with was tender . 
I will be going back because everything that I had was enjoyable! Yes you should try them!

Our driver recommended breakfast at The Ruby Slipper as a local favorite. He was confident that we would be satisfied. With that said, he set the standards pretty high, and I'll tell you, he did not disappoint.

We arrived with a large party. It was quite busy around noon time but surprisingly, the hostess seated us in seconds. I will mention that the only seating available were the high chairs, which we did not mind at all. Once seated our waitress took our drink orders immediately. I was thrilled there was a drink menu. Mimosas everyday!! And inexpensive as well!  BTW, our waitress was fantastic! I have yet to encounter any negative experience  with service in NOLA.

On to the menu.. We all had difficulty choosing our brunch. Everything sounded so delightful! I contemplated between a eggs benedict and a specialty option. I settled for the Chicken  St. Charles benedict. The chicken breast was moist and crispy and tasted great with the poached eggs. The sauce that finished the dish was delicious as well, both creamy and savory. Members in our party opted for the Florentine Omelette, the Costa Rican dish, and a Catfish sandwich. (I can't recall the other meals that were ordered!) Overall, everyone was content with their choice. We were satiated, no complaints! Unfortunately, I could not finish my entire meal. I was sadden that I could not take the leftovers since I had no time to finish it. What a waste!!  =(

We came across this bubble tea shop after noticing other popular spots had an extensively long line. I want to say we waited about 10-15 mins, which was not bad at all. We decided to order food along with our drinks, because, why not? 

The drinks came out prompt, however the food did not. An order of chicken wings and sausages, how long could that be? While the employee stated 15 mins, we actually waited a painful 40 mins. We noticed several customers who ordered after us received their food orders first. When we went to address this to the employee, she gave us a short "2 mins" response. I found this strange as 40 mins had passed, (which they probably forgot our order), and now the food would be ready in 2 mins? Ooh and BTW the wings were extremely salty and the sausage was bland. Also, our milk teas had way too much milk! Gross!! I'm not sure if it was just a bad day for them but I will reconsider coming here in the future...

Oh Geno's  I really liked how fast I got my food, but I have to say where's the beef? I came here with our of town guest we shared a Geno's and a Pats cheese steak.... and the winner was Pats. 

While I have to say the glimmering light of Geno's is tempting I would most definitely go to Pat's. Not to say they don't make a tasty Cheese Steak, I will definitely give it another try.

Came to the Little Tuna for an intimate dinner and enjoy some BYOB.  When we came here on a Thursday night, there were only a few other couples here. We of course knowing this was a seafood joint, brought a bottle of chardonnay, which the waiter was super nice, opened for us and brought over a bucket of ice to chill the wine. 

We ordered the fried dumplings for and appetizer very tasty, around $8. For our entree I went with the flank steak and mashed potatoes around $22, they were fantastic. Yvette got the wasabi tuna, which was really amazing and actually had a sushi taste and came with a boat load of wasabi which was around $25.

Food was priced decently, food was great and BYOB, I will definitely be back.

Came here on a recommendation from a co-worker and they had a deal online. First of all, BYOB, brought 2 bottles of wine, that probably had something to do with such a great dinner. 

Anyways, very cute decor, definitely a nice place for date night. dishes are around 19-25 bucks, not too bad, we ordered 4 different dishes and 2 deserts and everything was amazing. I went with the sausage Bolgonese which was stupendous, would definitely do it again. Our deserts were a lemon tiramisu and a 2 layered cannoli, bought were amazing. 

I definitely plan on bringing any of my out of town guest to try this place out.

Came here with Yvette, they have AYCE for $25, great deal. I hate eating alone or else I would be on top of going again. 

Can you believe this place on having AYCE also offers BYOB? Well it does, these are 2 of my favorite things. BTW there is Canal Liquor Store across the street so make sure you pick up some Saporro and Sake.  Sadly I was unaware of the BYOB, so I had to see all the other table enjoy BYOB, while I drank water like a sucker. 

Sushi rolls were on the smaller side, but that was actually a good thing, gave me more of a chance to try different things. So on top of sushi you can also order appetizer items like chicken and beef sate, which I recommend and tempura, which for some strange reason they are stingy with the sauce, so ask for extra. This place was pretty busy so that night service was lacking.

Used to live near here 3-4 years ago and we were semi-regulars. Turning point is a "nice" chain for people who don't feel like "slumming it" at a diner for breakfast or brunch, and they charge accordingly. For example, a plain Belgian waffle with zero accouterments is $9...TWO measly links of chicken sausage will run you nearly $5. Etc. etc. I know, I know: product prices are up. Don't worry: turning point also has the now ubiquitous "we are short staffed" sign to greet you up front. 

They used to do call ahead seating, but not anymore. Wait time on an outdoor table for 4 on Sunday at 10:30 am was quoted as 30 minutes. We went to check inside at the 40 minute mark and the table was ready...I'm not sure why they didn't call us on the phone # that the hostess initially asked for in order to let us know? 

All that being said: the food and drink quality is pretty good. The avocados look green, the coffee and tea selection far exceeds what you'll find in a diner, the decor is "cute" and the cherry hill location has a decent amount of outdoor seating under a pergola.  The tables are set back a little bit from busy Haddonfield road so you won't have any problem holding a conversation. Ambiance was enjoyable on a cool autumn morning and being outside put our dining partners at ease. 

Service was mostly good except for a couple of fairly big things: they forgot my waffle!

Everyone else at the table had more complicated orders (egg stuff, I dislike eggs so I can't describe what they got, omelets probably)  that came out without issue. To avoid any awkwardness, I told them to go ahead and mangia while their food was hot. My waffle was eventually served and it was good, golden brown and I think real butter was served atop. Fortunately I don't like fake maple syrup because that's what they serve. Plus  I guess it isn't brought out unless you ask? 

Speaking of ask: I also had to ask for a refill on tap water. The two of us (we split the bill with another couple) paid $44 before tip for breakfast. Nikki had some sort of omelet and coffee, I had the aforementioned waffle with chicken sausage and a "meadow" herbal tea. I highly recommend the meadow tea if you don't want caffeine: the mix of chamomile, rose petals, linden flowers (makes me think of the Union county town), and other aromatics is simply delightful! Aside from my company, the tea was today's highlight. 

We'd go back again if we had visitors in the immediate vicinity who wanted to grab brunch someplace "nice." You could definitely do worse, but there's also better. Hence the 3 stars.

After a grueling two-night-long Yelp search for a nice place to have dinner, I decided the food scene in Santa Barbara is wack. I eventually came across Arch Rock Fish and decided their Happy Hour looked good enough. And that they were:

East Coast Lobster Tail, $13
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/arch-rock-fish-santa-barbara?select=2p3EWMe7YLtURnpEz7__9w#rDFGhJk2Tw7fgq1Ny0lZKQ
Not super fresh but decent quality considering the price. Size wasn't mentioned on the menu, but I'm guessing it's 6-7 oz.

Lobster Slider, $6
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/arch-rock-fish-santa-barbara?select=2p3EWMe7YLtURnpEz7__9w#lZ7C5DBpTKdbPRc8TMxuSQ
This was so good, I ordered two as each slider is tiiiiiiiny... I'd say two inches in diameter? I would think for $6, they'd make 'em bigger or at least include more lobster meat.

Smoked Salmon Deviled Eggs, $3
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/arch-rock-fish-santa-barbara?select=2p3EWMe7YLtURnpEz7__9w#yJYiJMC_qR6fqfdPfvZGvg
Not the best I've had but still very good. We also ordered 2 of these.

Crispy Calamari, $5
Didn't try.

Mahi Mahi Sandwich w/truffle tater tots, $12
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/arch-rock-fish-santa-barbara?select=2p3EWMe7YLtURnpEz7__9w#2p3EWMe7YLtURnpEz7__9w
Super forgettable and wouldn't order again. The tater tots however, were so tasty, I thought about ordering it by itself ($4).

Other dishes included on their Happy Hour menu were Guacamole & Chips, Spicy Tuna & Salmon Sushi Roll, Truffle Grilled Cheese, Grilled Fish Taco, Shucked Oyster, Oyster Shooter, Loaded Dog, Edamame, Grilled Corn, Crispy Fish Slider, Vegetable Fries, and Shrimp Cocktail, all varying from $3 to $13. Beer (Stella, Kirin, Firestone, etc.) was super cheap, many at $4/glass.

Even though they offer an extensive Happy Hour menu, "a-ok" is exactly how I feel about Arch Rock Fish. Most of the plates were mediocre and although the prices were great, the portions weren't. If I'm ever back in Santa Barbara, I might stop by for a few bites... but most likely not.

Whenever I try somewhere new, I usually go in without expectations, starting with 3 stars in mind. With that said:

+1 star for serving Thrifty's ice cream, yum!

-1 star for hiking up the prices to $5/scoop, wtf?!

-1 star for terrible service

I asked the girl helping us if she could split 1 scoop into two flavors and she replied flatly that I'd have to get two scoops for two flavors. After we paid, she flatly said, "Have a nice day," with absolute zero expression on her face and walked away. Ummmmm. How am I supposed to have a nice day after looking at your poopy face? It's not my fault if you hate your job.

-1 star for her poopy face

My wife just asked me if I was going to rate this place a 5 star.  I said I wish I could rate them a 6 star.  We ordered the shrimp and grits, gumbo, lamb tenderloin and mixed berry crumble.  We were seated in the indoor area where the windows were wide open.  So it was like being outside and not dealing with the wind.  As our server recommended what we ate, I would have hugged him - but you know, this covid thing...
My wife had gumbo and shrimp and grits for the first time.  Now any other gumbo or shrimp and grits she eats will probably disappoint.  The gumbo  was the right thickness and saltiness with a hearty, full flavor.  Their grits were soooo creamy and rich.  The shrimp was prepared perfectly and the combination was delicious.
Our lamb loin was served with chimichurri sauce, sour cream mashed potatoes and asparagus.  The lamb was cooked a perfect medium rare and the sauce enhanced the flavor of the lamb.  Their mashed potatoes were sooooo creamy and rich (do you see a theme here?)
Then we were given a mixed berry crumble upon the recommendation of the general manager, Michael.  Michael, here's an air hug from Patty and me.  This is possibly the best crumble we've ever had.  It was the perfect sweetness and the crumble was the perfect crispiness.  And with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top, it made the crumble sooooo creamy and rich.
The best boba in Tucson. Wonderful drinks and neat ambiance. Great place for study nights and game nights alike.

Aw, c'mon, Brian, how am I a shill for "a coffee shop down the street" by providing readers information that $1.91 for a cup of coffee in a toxic styrofoam cup and 75c refills are ridiculous; and, that all-you-can drink coffee, comfortable, safe seating and privacy from street bums and   dogs is available down the street. Down University Boulevard at the University of Arizona Main Gate  and down North Fourth Avenue toward the railroad underpass.

The pastries are to kill for...literally.  All the artery clogging ingredients your doctor warned you to avoid.

Readers would benefit knowing that the contaminated unsanitized key to the Epic's toilet (used by the filthy homeless and drugsters that wander through along with unleashed and unmuzzled dogs, and people who refuse to use soap and water to wash up), dangling off the grimy metal spoon or plastic chicken that serves as a key-ring, reeks of pathogens waiting to explode. The toilet is consistently dirty.

Would you eat, drink, in a restaurant with a dirty toilet? If the public toilet's dirty, how committed is the owner, reputed to be a thug in the Hell's Angels, to assuring that the less-public food-preparation area is clean and safe?

As for the employees currently wrecking havoc at the Epic, since long-time, customer-centric barista Chelsea and her excellent chick baristas quit or were fired by the new owners, the service at the Epic has simply gone to hell.

Best advice is, stay away.

Love this place!! To be honest I was kinda skeptical about a 5 star casual burger and salad joint, especially a make your own. But sure enough, it is indeed worthy of it's almost flawless rating. 

Choose from almost a dozen pre-designed burgers, simple classic salads, milkshakes, New Hope Natural sodas, typical burger sides such as onion rings and fries AND the option to create burgers (veggie or beef) made to order, hence the name, M2O. ((Took me a minute. You shush!!))

Kiddos and I decided to create our own using one the kiosks. (Kiddos loved this!). Veggie burger on a crisp pretzel bun with grilled kale, spinach, cheddar cheese and lettuce with the M2O sauce on the side and two create your own half order salads...

My salad was compromised of kale with arugula, avocado, pumpkin and sunflower seeds, red onion, cucumber, tomato, carrots and jalapeño with garlic vinaigrette with crumbled veggie burger on top. It was an excellent salad!!! The ingredients were super fresh and plentiful and the burger was packed full of veggies and grilled to absolute perfection!! It was very spicy however. I didn't mind, but the kiddos weren't taken by surprise. (I wish they stated this somewhere on the menu!) The half order plated in a beautiful wooden bowl was quite the portion!! It seemed as if the bowl was never ending and I didn't mind one bit!! 

We enjoyed the clean open space with complimentary cucumber lemon water and good tunes. We equally enjoyed the cute courtyard on a gorgeous day! 

This place has such a great concept. There's really nothing like it in the area! Awesome choice for carnivore and vegans, the health conscious too.

Can't wait to return with my meat eating hubs! I've been telling everyone about it!

If Ross, Rachel, Monica, Chandler, Joey and Phoebe smoked pot, played hacky sack, perhaps had dreads and were maybe bike messengers or glass blowers, this is definitely where they would hang out and satisfy their caffeine addiction. 

Higher Grounds is somewhat of a boho coffee shop in the middle of thriving Northern Liberties. It has a very chill, relaxed vibe. It's great for catching up with an old pal or flying solo getting work done or reading a book while curled up. The eclectic space is filled with vintage sofas and other vintage decorative items. Very mix and match, but it works. Lots of plants, and I think I even spotted some macramé. There's always local artists showing their work on the walls which I adore! They have a chess, checkers, and a bunch of old school board games making it not only a nice throw back for us adults, but also a welcoming place to bring the littles. 

Don't shy away if you're not into the hippie dippy trippy thang...it's totally legit. Great local coffee. Standard caffeinated drinks, creative ones too. Milkshakes, Thai coffee, a nice tea selection, and even seasonal drinks such as a delicious kale lemonade! Yum! Always something new on the menu! 

They have really great food and cater well to veg-heads and gluten free patrons alike. The majority of their drool worthy pastries are made in house by one of their main employees and they are quite delicious. My hubby always brings me home some! From brownies to blondies, cinnamon buns, cupcakes, muffins of all kinds, lemon squares and mini pies too! Yes, even some of these are vegan! Score! They offer homemade quiche, sammies, soups and bagels from local fave, and our pals over at South Street Philly Bagels. 

Stop by for a yummy bite and a cup of joe. I have a feeling you may just want to stay awhile...

We loved the food and hospitality here! 
Whether you're in the mood for hibachi, sushi, tempura and teriyaki meals, poke' bowls, including a make your own option (with tofu as a protein choice), hand rolls, or maybe something a tad unique with a bit of a fusion touch such as lobster bao, creamy edamame soup or lobster miso soup, this is your place!
