The fam has previously enjoyed treats like red velvet cones with taro, strawberries & strawberry drizzle, a salted blue corn cone with almond cookie ice cream topped with chocolate chips & caramel & coconuts filled with pandan ice cream, sticky rice, & topped with fresh fruit, mochi with condensed milk drizzle with Pocky! 

Enjoy your own special combo in a cup, house-made cone (hello, green tea & red velvet!!) or even in a Hong Kong street waffle, made fresh & hot to order ! So cool! 

They have milkshakes & delicious smoothies also! 

This isn't your typical ice cream shop, that's for sure!! It's really an adventure! 

Arctic Scoop is currently operating on a call when you're outside/they'll bring it to the door system. No entry at all! Cards requested. It's a super easy, virtually no contact system during COVID 

Arctic Scoop is without a doubt a shining star of East Passyunk! A MUST!!

Jules is a small chain which started locally in nearby in Doyelstown, PA by a couple looking for more organic, feel good, affordable eateries to take their daughters to. Jules serves up wide variety of delicious, gorgeous, crisp flatbread pizzas piled with the freshest, locally sourced ingredients and herbs.

They're gluten-free, vegetarian, even vegan friendly. They offer a gluten free crust (that does contain egg as of now) and a special meat and dairy-free pie they keep in the back to avoid "cross contamination". Their words, not mine. They will also gladly substitute Daiya "cheese" on any of their signatures pies to make them dairy free. Their buffalo sauce and pesto pies do contain dairy so those three are a no-go. Just an extra couple of minutes and your own customized pie is ready! You must buy at least two slices to customize a pie. 

I LOVED my Veggie #7 I ordered with Daiya sans sour cream. It was so flavorful and perfectly crisp! Absolutely delicious! Fresh, hot out of the oven, with fresh meaty veggies. Wow! So, so good!

Laura, smiling behind the counter was outstanding! She was so kind and extremely helpful. She was so full of information and knew every pie inside and out. Her knowledge and passion for her products was admirable. She should totally be commended! She's a rockstar!

The space is kid friendly and it's rare I leave a pizza joint feeling good about myself the way I did leaving here. These slices come in at around 200 calories or so each and are light, yet filling. 

A terrific stop! Happy to have it on my daily weekday journey but I do wish there was one in the city! (Hint Hint) closest locations to Center City Philly are Cherry Hill and Ardmore.

Yum! Been dying to try a poke' bowl and the taste did not disappoint! There's over a dozen pre designed bowls (including veggie) to choose from here, some with clever names of local neighborhoods. You can also grab a sheet at the front and completely create your own which is what I chose to do to keep it as healthy as possible. 

Since I'm vegan I decided to chose the organic tofu as my protein. It's served plain, not fried with no seasoning or breading in other words, perfect for those watching caloric intake. I must say I really appreciate tofu being offered as most poke' spots I've come across don't have a plan based protein. Other protein options include yellowtail, crabmeat (+$1), big eyed tuna, Scottish salmon, eel, shrimp and chicken, so definitely something for everyone. 

I went with seasonal mixed greens and nixed the rice in order to keep it light. On this initial visit I added cucumbers, red onion, edamame, carrot and pineapple from their list of over a dozen mix ins. 

I chose the spicy sesame shoyu which was the sauce option with the least amount of calories. After I asked the lovely girl behind the counter, she informed me it's mostly soy sauce based with a hint of sesame oil and a bit of Sriracha so no need to really worry about the oil too much. It was tasty and on the light side but still had nice flavor with just a hint of heat. 

I opted for the avocado which is $1 up-charge as a topping because well, avocado. Duh. The seaweed salad as a topping I felt was also a good choice to add some texture, wetness and flavor. 

For flare I chose the fried garlic bits. Holy yum! I highly recommend these! It added such a punch and crunch. Hey, I rhyme! 

The bowl I created was over $11, but I was just happy to keep it mostly healthful and fresh...and fast, which isn't always so simple to do. 

The only minor complaint I have would be my bowl wasn't as pretty as I would've liked. I say this not only because it wasn't as "Insta worthy" as I was anticipating, and how others seemed to be, but because a lot of the mix ins were at the bottom of the the bowl and the bowl was filled so much I couldn't properly blend. Not a huge deal. Next time I'll just ask for them to be placed side by side instead. 

This area definitely needed a "fast food" option beside Lorenzo's and Wawa and I'm happy it's a healthy one for a change!! Can't wait to return and keep creating my own unique combinations! I think the kiddos will enjoy it also because kids love anything 'make your own'. 

Kiosk meter parking. Lots of spots. There's also a lot under Abbots Square. (Entrance east of TD Bank).

We hit this place up before going to "Monsterville"  which is what the town is called around Halloween. For those who don't know, the whole town converts their old huge Victorian homes into spooky haunted houses. I mention this because it's a great place to eat beforehand, park and walk to many of the homes on the list. It's a very cute little section of the city, it's all lit up with lights and a gazebo. It's like you're on a movie set. Adorable! Great al fresco area during Covid also. 

They had some Halloween themed cocktails and some fall gems, too. The apple maple bourbon Old Fashion did not disappoint for warming me up on a chilly autumn evening! Yum! 

We split a bunch of plates for the table and not one wasn't loved. Salmon leek wontons, a huge Mediterranean plate with hummus, baba etc, Old Bay crab tots with cheese, fried avocado bits with aioli, and Thai mussels. The mussels were definitely the star of the show with all of us wanting to bring home tubs of that so I chili sauce they were floating in. We would recommend any of these starters!! 

Kiddos had big classic caesers to split. 

For dessert they had big brownie sundaes for the kiddos, classic cheesecake with raspberry drizzle and sweet potato maple cheesecake, which was unreal! Definitely a highlight of the fall additions to the menu. 

I would absolutely dine here again and look forward to seeing other seasonal treats!

Han Dynasty still takes the lead for my all time favorite Sichuan food! It's all so absolutely delish and perfectly spicy! 

If we're being honest, I much prefer their Old City, Philly counterpart for ambiance reasons alone, as it's located in a STUNNING old converted bank with insanely gorgeous details, but the food at this location is the same, and was really difficult to resist while trekking through Jersey! And well, if Anthony Bourdain gave it a big thumbs up, who am I to say any different :) 

The dan dan noodles which  come at a level 6 out of 10 spiciness are in my opinion, a MUST!! They are perfectly spicy and perfectly peanuty! They are a wonderful thick consistency and tossed with chili table-side, too! How fun! They do come with minced pork here, but they will happily eliminate it, no issue. These noodles are TO DIE FOR and the stuff my dreams are made of! I honestly crave them often!!! YUMMMMM! 

During a recent lunch date, my husband and I indulged in the seafood tofu soup for two. It was massive and quite delicious! Little seafood, but the taste was surely not lacking at all! Great starter on a colder day! 

We also had two lunch specials, at a mere $8 or so. They were given with copious amounts of white rice. (Lots of leftovers for two more meals the following day!) 
The garlic eggplant was a favorite with the mapo tofu a runner up. (The tofu also comes with minced pork that can be eliminated). Both dishes were outstanding and packed full of flavor and spice!! We would order both again! 

Service was wonderful and the food, which came out super quick, is without a doubt a 5 star!!! 

If this is anything like the one in Philly, it's BYO. 

A must try!! I can't wait for a return visit soon!  It's sooooo good! So, so, so flavorful and drool-worthy!!

Not only was I fairly underwhelmed by the brews I tried (Great Bells & Lucky Friend), I was bummed that a brewery wouldn't allow flights, the kitchen was closed in between lunch and dinner AND the place, while cute...is kinda disjointed and a bit confusing. 

I did thoroughly enjoy getting buzzed with my awesome friends out on the patio, the humorous descriptions of the brews and the Mexican din we had down the street, so there's that. 

Definitely not worth the drive up from the city in my opinion, especially with all of the new clutch breweries we have, but I was glad to finally try it as it's been "on the list" for years now. It's not a place for someone new to the brand and looking to sample. 

Just 'ehh' for me, and check the times if you're looking for food or snacks with your large glasses of beer.

What's not to like? Great brews on tap, a wide variety of food, weekend brunch, al fresco seating, vegan and GF options and a cool laid back, welcoming neighborhood vibe. 

We split a few plates included vegan wings, which essentially come a bit deconstructed in the sense that the tangy hot sauce is in ranch form and placed on the side for dipping rather than smothered in them. The wings are big chunks of breaded seitan. Bigger than ones you would expect. I'm admittedly somewhat of a vegan wings, and these honestly weren't my favorite, but the sauce was very delicious! My daughter however loved them so I'll be sure to give them another try with her. 

We also split fish and chips which were outrageous and rivaled those we've had in Iceland, where they're notoriously excellent. These were HUGE chunks with perfectly fried exterior served appropriately with tarter. The "chips" were actually purple fingerlings with vinegar. Different and tasty, and while I enjoyed the mix up, I think hubs missed actual traditional fries. 

Mac and cheese was fair. It's homemade with creamy shells. They come topped with fried onions and scallions which we loved and there's an option to add toppings. We added summer veggies, which were delish!

Orecchiette pasta with eggplant ragu was wonderful! Meaty and savory with chunks of zucchini too. Yum!! A winner

We also split a refreshing pomegranate and pear sour on draft although the cocktails, some named after South Philly spots were intriguing. The beer list was solid and we found ourselves wanting to come back just to keep up with what's rotating. 

The desserts sounded tempting as did the vegan BLT Sammy and their brunch menu, so a return visit is definitely in the cards. 

I love and appreciate their variety of offerings and the seasonal additions. It's a chill seat yourself type place so don't feel strange if you walk in and don't get addressed immediately. It's the kind of place that make me love South Philly, especially West Passyunk....it just has that cool vibe. 

Parking isn't the easier, so bring your patience and your parallel parking skills.

4.5 Stars. Pastarami, knishes and kasha, oy vey! Oh Hershel, go on with your bad self! This will be absolutely be the best smoked meat sammy you will have in Philly and certainly up there with your favorite NYC and Montreal delis. You can see by just watching folks making love to their stuffed sammies and well as just looking at how the super tender corned beef and pastrami meat just falls apart, also how it's dripping with juices. 

Hershel's offers all of your favorite Jewish deli staples...matzoh ball soup, knishes of all kinds, latkes, kasha and bow ties, smoked fish, salads such as tuna, chicken and whitefish, to name a few. Ruebens on rye, and don't forget the dill pickles that come complimentary with any purchase, amazing spicy brown mustard and a can of Dr Brown's of course! If you've never had one, HAVE ONE! Birch or cream rock! Diet available too. 

The knish was on the smaller size (as were the matzoh balls), but big in flavor and absolutely stuffed with filling. The kasha was the best I've ever tasted! Ever! Ever! EVER!

They offer 1/2 soup & 1/2 sammy special for just under $8, as well as breakfast sammies too! 

Prices were very fair especially for this type of cuisine and the amount of meat in the sammies. 

The boys behind the counter were all sweet and very helpful. 

10% off for jurors. Just ask. 

They are NOT certified Kosher as they do indeed mix meat and dairy.

First of all, this place is gorgeous! Very spacious with a full bar, neat sculpted trees, a ceiling made to look like a nighttime sky, banquet seating and a koi pond too! 

It served as a lovely spot for an inexpensive lunch after a spa day nearby. 

They have wonderful lunch specials available from 11:30am-2:30pm M-F...Hibachi, Kabuto and Maki bento and sushi which included 2 rolls, soup (miso or mushroom which is in a fish broth) AND salad for just $9! This is the option I went with. Unfortunately the house ginger salad could not be substituted for a seaweed salad, which is what I was craving so I paid the $4 for the addition. No biggie. Brought the ginger salad back to the city for the less fortunate. 

All the food was delicious and fresh. My veggie rolls (sweet potato and vegetarian which was avocado, asparagus and cucumber) were tasty and left me super curious about their other plates!

 I noticed they have meals for the kiddos, impressive specialty rolls and even filet and lobster hibachi! Desserts looked amazing too! 

My girlfriend enjoyed her shrimp hibachi which was plated so pretty in a 4 part special plate ;one for her veggies, one for noodles, one for rice and one for her shrimp. 

I would absolutely love to come back for dinner and enjoy one of their tempting cocktails. Not sure when I'll be in the area, but would certainly return! I actually found myself wishing it were closer to home. Kiddos would love the fish!

Totally dug the vibe, and service was really great and prompt. 

Be careful of hours! They do shut down between lunch and dinner. 

Check out their website for coupons!
Kids eat FREE on Mondays & Tuesday's. 
Half priced cocktails for Ladies Night on Thursday's. 
30% off signature rolls Mon-Thurs.

(5 Star Rating based strictly on food) Super legit. 
Perhaps the best croissant you'll have in the states. Bold statement? Try them! Perfectly buttery and flaky. Filled to perfection with a variety of goodies...cheese, cherry, mocha cream, chocolate, almond, etc. I hear they also make a pretty fantastic breakfast sammy such as bacon, egg and cheese on one of their famous croissants as well as a pretty solid bahn mi. Even tofu ones for us veg-heads! Add a delicious Iced Vietnamese coffee, or Thai when she makes it, and you're all set. The super kind owner suggested the sticky sweet sticks for the kiddos. Try them all....and then head directly to the gym! 

Our order of 3 croissants, one stick and one coffee was about $17. Extra couple bucks for tip jar. Cash only. Fair. 

There's was a line for this small corner, no frills shop just off of East Passyunk around 10am on a Saturday. I suggest getting there early. They open at 7am! It did move fast and you can tell there were "regulars" in line who know what's up. 

There's only a few seats inside as well as a few outside in nicer weather. Not much to the place but the baked treats is why you're coming, not  for ambiance. 

Typical South Philly parking. 

Oh, they also received:  

The James Beard Foundation Award for outstanding baking in 2015. 

Best of Philly bakery 2015 

Travel Magazine Best Bakery.

Driven past a zillion times and always kind of wondered about this place. Heard nothing but good things too. Finally, we stopped by for a quick, casual lunch after my girls begged for Bahn Mi. Umm..love them! 

We entered the tiny spot on the corner Washington Ave through their parking lot they share with a Vietnamese market. (That's also where you'll find restroom as Nam Son doesn't have their own). We appreciated the easy parking situation here. 

Our tofu Bahn Mi were ready in about 5 minutes although you can order ahead via Yelp. They were fantastic!! So good! I actually want to split another right now!! Perfectly crunchy carrots and cucumbers, fresh cilantro and almost de-seeded jalapeño for the right amount of kick. Perfectly toasted roll and the tofu has a bite to it. It was drenched in a tasty, zingy sauce and the sauce didn't take away from the "meatiness" of the tofu by making it soggy! 

Fried doughnuts were also purchased for a mere $1.15 and well liked by all. 

They have a few other offering besides Bahn Mi and pastries. I definitely want to try the tofu summer rolls sometime soon! The red bean goods looked tempting also. 

I absolutely seeing us order to-go here often. 

Staff were friendly. 
Prices were super fair. 
All around good stop. 

A few tables inside and a few chairs outside to enjoy your goods. We sat outside on a gorgeous day and didn't even mind the fact that we were indeed in parking lot on lawn chairs. 

$10 card minimum.

Oooooh! I must start off by saying that this is the first pho place that I had encountered at the time which catered to vegans. An entire city...no veggie (broth) pho at all! What's up with that?! Kinda bummed this spot is so far from the city, but definitely glad to have found it, and to add it to my growing list of options when I'm in this area.   

There was no online menu and no menus posted on Yelp when I visited. It was a chilly day and soup was all that would cut it for lunch that day. I saw this listing pop up while at the mall nearby and figured what the heck, I'll call and see if they can make me a bowl of animal friendly pho I've been so desperately seeking. The kind gentleman who answered the phone chuckled and said "of course". They actually have an entire veg-friendly side to their large menu! 

Located in a suburban strip mall is this clean space with fresh flowers on each table and  the friendliest, attentive staff. Both the waiter and manager on duty were exceptionally sweet! 

Your meal will start with complimentary rice cakes. I then ordered clean, light tofu summer rolls with hoisin. There were two to an order. They were the best summer rolls I've ever had! The tofu inside was slightly cooked giving it just a little bite to it. The crisp veggies and herbs were fresh, evenly distributed, and there was so much flavor in each bite!

I then chose the veggie pho in veggie broth. They also beef or chicken broth, and have gluten free noodles upon request. It was absolutely delicious, packed with veggies and that slightly cooked, not fried tofu with a meaty bite, and it was huge, easily enough for two-three sittings! Accompanied with the appropriate toppings pho traditionally comes with...bean sprouts, jalapeño, basil and lime wedge. I was so happy with my giant bowl of tasty pho! 

I can't wait to come back and would highly recommend a stop here if you're from, or in the area! All around great experience!!

Without a doubt, this family's, and I'm pretty sure all of Philly's favorite donuts! They're light, filled fresh, and the toppings and fillings are given very generously.

Hubs picks up a box whenever he's remotely in the Reading Terminal Market area....and I'm pretty sure even when he's not. And I'm not talking one or two, I'm talking like two dozen which he and our girls down rather quickly. They're $10.99 a dozen which is really a great bang for your buck, comparatively speaking. 

They have all types from classics such as glazed and apple fritters to fancies such as maple bacon, salted caramel and Nutella. My one daughter's favorites are Oreo and M&M. The other is the key lime and hubs is certainly banana cream. There's really a flavor for every taste, but sorry fellow veg-heads we're out of luck with this one. Whomp whomp. 

I do enjoy watching the staff roll and fill them fresh as you wait in line and bringing a box home to surprise the fam is the only upside to jury duty nearby. 

Coming early in the morning on a weekday is definitely the way to go to get your pick and to avoid lines. 
Oh, and both locations are closed on Sunday. 

Everyone loves these so much I'm considering getting them for my mom's birthday this weekend instead of a cake because I think the extended crew will be so impressed, and everyone has different tastes to satisfy.

Stina is without a doubt worthy all the hype!! This new(er) WEST Passyunk, heavily Greek inspired kitschy joint by the one and only Bob Saritsoglou, is such a freaking GEM! 

To be completely honest, I wasn't as thrilled as most when I heard a pizza joint was opening up, but Stina is SOOOOOO much more than that! Sure, they have insanely delicious, PERFECTLY cooked wood-fired pizza (the truffle pie with garlic and fresh thyme is a favorite and so INSANE!!), they also have classic Mediterranean dishes and amazing fusion ones as well! Even the simple seeming sides like roasted potatoes with turmeric aioli were not only outrageous, but beautifully presented. The fattoush, borek and pedi are also winners. I hear the octopus is to die for, if that's your thing. 

It's BYO AND they serve delectable desserts. The chocolate cake with tahini cream is NOT to be missed!! DROOL!!! 

The place is super adorable and filled with vintage pictures, collectibles and mirrors. It's so fun to just look around! 

The only negative will be finding a table, as the spot is small (but super cozy!) and in such high demand. On our first go, we stumbled in on a random weekday and the only seats available were at the high tops, which was fine but I would definitely recommend making reservations! 
The entire meal I dreamed about bringing my whole family back, and can't wait, to but 6 is the most they can accommodate so, sorry bro & sissy in law but we got you covered, Mom & Dad :)

Definitely strike up a conversation with Bob while you're there! You can't miss him and his mustache back there shoveling the pizzas into the gorgeous stove. He's so passionate about his place, his food, his culture and his neighborhood! Wonderful guy, place, food, location and service!! So happy to welcome Stina to the 'hood!!

Lentils, grape leaves, falafel platter, spanakopita, lentil soup, and kabobs...YUM! Apricotstone, the tiny BYOB in a Northern Liberties is worthy of all the hype. It's absolutely delicious, completely authentic, family-owned and run, priced fair, and your meal comes with excellent service.

Our first visit was on a chilly night and the cozy place was just perfect. The food was so tasty. Each dish I mentioned above was more flavorful than the next. The falafel was a perfect consistency and accompanied appropriately. Even simple lentils were great. The grape leaves and spanakopita were some of the best I've ever had. The owner's son who was our kind, informative and attentive waiter told me they would be the best I've had and he wasn't wrong! 

We were all thrilled with our meals and will be returning. If you're a fan of Middle Eastern cuisine, a visit here is a must!

They also hosts Sunday brunch and have tables outside in warmer weather. 

*Not suitable for large parties.
*Dont forget those bottles!

4.5 Stars This spot was "veg only" before it was trendy and I'm pretty sure this is the first place I've ever dined at that was actually. I have been enjoying lunch dates here with my mom since I was just a teen and it was located across the street at a much smaller, more intimate space. Good for them for the move and new addition of a bar and fireplace, but it loses a little something with the new big vaulted ceilings. They were always packed so I do get it, but I prefer the more cozy feel the other location had. 

Food wise, you will not be disappointed driving out of your way, even from the city, for a meal here. Honestly. Veg or not, the food is absolutely fantastic!! The menu is very creative, taking notes from many different types of cuisines from Asian to Cuban, etc. Menu highlights I feel show its uniqueness are: Pumpkin seed crusted tofu, maple mustard vinaigrette, pickled red onions and Tabasco Mayo, to name a few. Every dish is absolutely packed with flavor! You cannot go wrong with anything here.

They soups are to die for! They are not listed on the menu as the change daily. A bowl will cost just under $10 but can definitely be split or eaten as an entire meal. Their spicy Thai peanut was the stuff (my) dreams were made of. Very disappointed they removed it from the menu, but from what our waiter said, it's in high demand so maybe they will bring it back! I used to take a quart of it home every visit! Most recently we tried two.... a creamy, cinnamony butternut squash with maple crema and toasted seeds and a white miso packed with veggies. Both so fantastic we couldn't choose a favorite! You must try one! 

We usually stick to cubano sammies. They have over half a dozen varieties. They are rather large and made on the most perfectly crispy toasted baguette. They come plated with a side salad that is not to be overlooked. Mixed greens with house balsamic, currants and white marcona almonds! Yum! We usually get the portobello which we love. Most recently we opted for a chickpea fritter sammy and it was very tasty! 

The apps are also fantastic and definitely leave some room for the desserts or take one home! They have decadent vegan ones too! Oh wow! 

The menu is clearly marked vegan or "dairy free upon request". Again, you don't have to be strictly veg to thoroughly enjoy a meal here, but if you are, the plethora of delicious options is pure heaven. 

Although I'm mostly here during lunch hours and don't really see it, I do believe it's BYO too! So bring those bottles. 

A must try! A huge winner especially for the area!!

4.5 stars for food. Worth the almost 40 minute drive from the city! Side note: It absolutely boggles my mind (and actually pisses me off) that there are no strictly raw vegan restaurants in center city! WTF?! C'mon people! Ok, end rant. 

This place is so great! Eating raw foods just makes you feel good. Like really, really good! I think the creativity that goes into raw cooking is absolutely remarkable and quite evident here. 

This quaint shop with its clever name offers a variety of innovating, feel good foods boasting with flavor. Whether you're just looking to eat healthy with a kale salad or such, thinking about stepping out of your comfort zone a bit or are full blown, strictly raw, there's something for you here. 

We started with the orange creamsicle smoothie which was delish!! We split the pad Thai and the nachos complete with sun dried tomato and walnut "meat". In a world full of faux meats, all natural alternatives are definitely appreciated. We LOVED everything!! 

If I lived closer, I would be here a lot more often. Gotta get back here ASAP!

We have driven past here a zillion times and had no idea just what to expect. We were so pleasantly surprised! 

We came here for a late lunch and walked into the small corner shop which had totally laid back 50's diner vibe complete with a long counter, classic round bar stools, specials written on chalkboards and food served in those red plastic baskets. Diggin' it. 

Just coming back from Memphis & Nashville, this was a perfect stop to give me all of those southern, home-cooked, comfort food feels I was craving. With items on the menu such as Memphis dogs, chicken and waffles, hush puppies, biscuits and gravy and get this... The Elvis Melt!! Hello, South Philly meets southern! Awesome! 

Classic breakfast items as simple as eggs two ways with toast, to omelettes and veggie burritos are available as well as some "trendier" items such as breakfast egg rolls and salted caramel French toast too. 

TONS of vegan items as well! Vegan grilled cheese! Yeah baby! 

We split the sampler which included hush puppies, bacon wrapped jalapeño tots, and fried pickles served with BBQ sauce and some kind of sweet cream. The hush puppies were TO DIE FOR and the bacon wrapped jalapeño tots were the sole reason for my husband's visit. The pickles weren't my favorite pickles I've had. A tad dry. 

I ordered the Elvis Melt sans bacon and let me tell you, it was better than the one I had in the oldest diner in Memphis where Elvis used to eat his!!! It's was bananas! Yes, pun intended. A must try! I could barely finish a half it was so thick, dense and stuffed with deliciousness. 

Kids had the grilled cheese which was on nice thick bread and oozing with melty goodness. We ordered the free tots that came with the check in too. Very, very good! They have a seasoning that is perhaps a tad spicy for kiddos. 

Hubs got the breakfast egg rolls and liked them a lot. No skimping on meats and eggs there. 

They are BYOB so bring the champs and enjoy your mimosas. 

We were all every satisfied and would recommend this no frills, breakfast spot. But keep in mind that's what it is, no frills. If you're looking for "brunching" with girlfriends at a fancy place, this isn't it. It's very casual and a nice change from the other scene. 

We came on a Sunday around 1pm, parked right out front and  had no wait at all. Perfect.

A lively, casual place to nosh in between taking in some jazz on Frenchman! It's one of the only eateries mixed in with a bunch of bars so it can definitely get crowded when the drunkin' munchies hit. We came before closing at midnight and there was still a wait! 

We heard from some locals say this is the place to go for good times, brews and great dogs. The fact that they have not one, but three veg options had me sold! They also have crawfish sausage, a dog made with Guinness, gator, duck, bratwurst, kielbasa and a creole dog too. 

Torn between the three vegan dogs, Spicy Chipotle Dog ,Field Roast Italian Dog and Smoked Apple Sage, I wound up going for a chipotle dog. I decided to top my own with unlimited toppings for just under $8! You have the option to "chef choice" it, but I was too chicken with my dietary restrictions and we'll, I'm a bit of a control freak so that option is not for me. 

Since this was my splurge meal of the trip and decided to totally load it up and I ate Every. Single. Bite. Yum! Even the fluffy New England style bun which by the way is also vegan. It is toasted perfectly and super delicious! You can opt for "naked" dog but, these buns are amazing and worthy of the calories and carbs!!

I added pico, guacamole, pickles, fried onions and blackberry sauce. Perhaps a bit out of the ordinary and maybe a strange combination, but it worked. The dog itself was super spicy so the chill of the cool guac and the seeetness of the amazing, thick blackberry sauce balanced the heat quite well! Highly recommend the blackberry sauce! Super yum! 

I added a local Boot can although they do have Louisiana Abita on draft. 

They have some awesome sounding loaded fries which I held back from, but they looked amazing! FYI: WTF doesn't stand for What The F**k, rather White Trash Fries and they are one of the more popular choices. 

I will definitely be back for a casual meal or late night snack when I'm jammin in the neighborhood next time. They also have a few other locations further south.
So fun!

Our family had such a great time and awesome meal at Yaikatori Boy! I actually never knew what a solid  place to dine it was! I always thought it was strictly a karaoke bar! The downstairs restaurant is family friendly! Sorry I didn't know this all along! 

The menu is really extensive! There's definitely something for everyone, kids included!

We started with some "Japas" aka Japanese tapas!! We enjoyed agedaahi tofu and edamame, then moved on to "Yaikatori" aka skewers. We had they shrimp and shishito, and both were wonderful! The starter that really stole the show however, were the brussels! They were INSANE! Hands down, the bet I've ever had!! My husband and youngest who aren't fans normally, LOVED these!! 

The kiddos had simple avocado and green rolls, while hubs and I dove into some specialty rolls that were outrageous! The 'He Roll' has scorched scallops that gave it an unexpected smokey flavor. The 'Rocket Roll' featured cold lobster salad atop salmon with sweet apple that balanced the wasabi tobiko so well! It was wrapped with black sesame soy paper. So neat!  

We also split the whole grilled bronzini, which is actually a pike fish, and was a steal at just $18! 

We finished, or shall I say, the kids finished the meal with tempura ice cream. They devoured it before we could grab a bite! The mochi flight is what's up for us next time, oh, and the lobster two ways!! Yaaaassss! 

Service from Aaron was stellar and the cocktails and imported Japanese beer were the perfect accompaniment. Shirley Temples for the kids! 

I now know you can order any of this food upstairs for a night out with some singing! Yep, definitely coming back for that!

Love. The. Concept. Stopped in for a casual day date after wanting to try it out since they opened, but didn't think the kiddos would go for it. Finally made it, just the two of us, and we're so glad we did!! 

What a fantastic idea ...dogs offered in many varieties including all beef, pork, bratwursts, chorizo, lamb, duck, Cantonese sausage, chicken, even wild boar, alligator, kangaroo and python, topped with ingredients inspired by domestic and international travels! 

Each dog is so insanely clever, with names just the same. They also list the corresponding airport codes to each locale on the menu. Each dog represented their respective destination so perfectly and had me wanderlusting quite a bit! I bet it was a blast creating this menu...The Hebrew hammer which has latkes, the Louisiana Dog which has a combo gator and shrimp sausage and included jalapeño remoulade and so on....

I chose "The Veg Dog Millionaire", (the most popular vegetarian option...they informed me they're working on adding more vegan options) which gave me a chuckle and had me wanting to rewatch Slum Dog Millionaire ASAP! This dog was obviously Mumbai inspired and had a samosa filling topping! Oh yessssss!! Delicious!!! It contained all of those warming spices I love in Indian food! So, so good! I asked for the spicy aioli on the side which hubs gladly added to his dog, the "Salchica Vergara", inspired by the cuisine in Bogota. It was deep fried, topped with bacon, yellow mustard, mayo, ketchup, pineapple relish, coleslaw and crushed potato chips.

 While I had a difficult time finishing what was on my silver tray which included a small side of potato chips, he had no issue finishing his dog and chips, and wanted to chow down three more! Say what?! We did both agree the bread was a bit much however. The dogs are served on a bun shaped like a New England style lobster roll, but we think it was more of a Texas Toast type deal which was a tad too thick on the bottom for our personal taste. I can imagine some folks nix the bread towards the end of their meal as the dogs themselves are rather long and filling. 

The staff is uber friendly, knowledgeable of the menu and they're willing to substitute any protein to any dog combo. They are also open to replacements and/or additions to the toppings. Very laid back and they cater well to picky eater such as myself. Thank you! There's even an option to completely create your own dog, but with ones so carefully crafted it seemed silly for us first timers. 

Brews are pretty great and varied, with about 16 on tap. We decided to taste the Mardi Gras, a lighter lager for our first go in honor of Fat Tuesday. Delish! They also have some pretty rad cocktails. 

I loved the simple decor with nods to traveling found in the vintage inspired posters and on the flight arrival/departure board which I absolutely loved! Nice bar with flatscreens too. We enjoyed catching some of the Winter Olympics while we dined. There's also a few video games in the back! How fun! 

We will definitely be back and after seeing what it's all about. I think the kiddos would actually dig it too. I mean, kids love anything 'make your own' and the promise of crushed potato chips as a topping sounds right up their alley. Add games...sold. 

I really think it's a must try! It's all just so fun and such a novel idea! It allows your tastebuds to travel the world or revisit destinations you love in one restaurant. You can come a bunch times and still taste a different combo each visit.

How do I not have a review for one of my (all around) favorite pizza joints in the city? Let's change that, shall we? 5 star is for all around experience. 4.5 for slice. 

I'm not sure if it's...
-the awesome memorabilia (Pizza Party, Shari Lewis & Lamb-chop, Ninja Turtles, Mystic Pizza, etc) that takes me right back to my childhood? 
-the fact that it's BYO? 
-it being so conveniently located next to an ice cream shop making for one sinful delicious stop?
- has kick ass murals and Philly legend Izaiah Zager mosaics in a cute courtyard outback. 
-or that they have really great slices and make your own options including vegan cheese too! 
But..... I FREAKING LOVE IT HERE! 

Located deep in the ever evolving Fishtown section of the city is this crazy quirky little pizza shop which is actual a pizza museum!! They hold the Guinness Book World Record for pizza memorabilia and boy is it a hoot to look over it all! 

Pizza Brain serves up a daily rotating variety of oversized slices with funky fun names. There's always an option to make your own which I what I normally do. My signature self created pie is a "Tom" aka plain topped with blackened Brussels, meaty portobello, fresh basil, Daiya vegan cheese and pine nuts. Oh. So. Good! So, so good! I top it with their house made crushed red pepper but watch out, this stuff is seriously spicy. "A little dab will do ya", as they say. 

My husband and the extended fam is obsessed with their "Forbes Wagonese" which has baby smoked pepperoni they say is outrageous. 

Pizza Brain is attached to Little Baby's Ice-cream which is so genius. You can sit over there enjoying your pizza and visa versa. My favorite place to dine is outback however. Don't miss at least a peek back there! Way cool! 

Pizza Brain in BYO and also serves Virgil's old fashion sodas too. Try one! Cream is delish! 

Fab Philly Mom say: BRING THOSE KIDS!! It's THE perfect pizza and ice-cream night out spot! My kiddos love playing with the make your own pizza video game and looking at the toys hidden in clear boxes in the floor. Sit outback and forget worrying if they're loud or spill crap which you know they're going to do! Also, bribing them with ice-cream if they finish their dinner is oh so acceptable here. 

It's cash only! Unmetered street parking!

*Damn, I wish my old photos I posted of this place were connected to my review. Such a cool spot!

3.5 Stars. Sweet little 'top your own' fro-yo spot in Grad Hospital area. Kiddos just love it here. In fact, they host kids birthday parties! 

Positives: 
-The location is great. Very welcoming, safe neighborhood with an adorable polka dot painted outdoor space. So, so lovely to sit outside here in warmer weather! 

-Very friendly, helpful staff! 

- Pretty standard pay per weight fro-yo prices with sugar free options. 

-Tv, coloring books and little sitting area for the wee ones. 

-They hand make beautiful creamy popsicles and cater them to a theme with colors if you're having a party here! Nice touch! 

Negatives:
-Only one dairy free option and its water ice, not yogurt. Whaaah. 

-A lot less toppings than other places were used to. Less fruit and healthier options too. 

 
All and all, we'll be back, especially in summer. It's so fun to sit outside with the neighbors. Very cute little outdoor space.

I must admit while I was so excited to have a Lil Pop Shop closer to home, I feared this location would pale in comparison to its adorable sister shop we love in University City. Boy was I sorely mistaken! This space rocks!! It's super sweet. (Pun intended). 

I always say a business that specializes in one thing, offered in many different varieties has the ability to perfect the art of their one item. Lil Pop Shop has done that and continues to do so...

These creative pops for those who have never indulged, are THE perfect consistency! They're not too icy when you first sink your teeth into them. They're creamy yet not melty like ice-ceam. They're perfectly sized and available in many invented flavors including dairy free ones too!! 

I think by now this fam has tried almost every pop they have ever created. Chocolate salted caramel brownie however is a forever favorite in this house! I personally always find myself choosing a flavor with coconut, whether it be coconut hibiscus or lychee coconut! So darn refreshing!! It's really so hard to choose just one I mean, key lime pie, pumpkin s'mores, earl gray black pepper, blueberry maple. Yu-u-u-mmm! The kiddos new go-to is the buttercream, because well, it has colorful jimmies in it! Yes, they're called jimmies, NOT SPRINKLES! This is Philly! 

The kiddos love taking their pop up a notch with the newer option to dip your pop in chocolate and/or add toppings! How fun! 

Lil Pop Shop now also offers Rival Brothers coffee, various special lemonades, spritzers, coconut water and assorted baked goods including croissants, cookies and house made tart cherry granola. This location also offers quiche and other lunch bites on the weekends!

This space is bright and super cute like University City, but this location is much bigger. Greenery, adorable, Instagramable floral wallpaper, magazines and nooks perfect for conversations. What could be better than taking some time out for a cup of Joe and a delicious treat? Don't forget your 20% off coffee or tea with Yelp check-in! 

Kiosk meter parking. 

Fab Philly Mom says: This is an obvious must if you have children! (and really a must for the big kid in all of us!)

Booked on Open Table last minute, no issue. It was simple and much appreciated especially because it doesn't seem like it's a popular method of booking in this area and I like using it for convenience. 

The space is absolutely gorgeous! Black and white with modern art to match, fresh flowers at every turn and striking, drool worthy marble table tops! Ambiance and decor on point! Oh, and there's an open kitchen! Love that! 

We were a tad early for our reservation and the kind, smiling hostess sat us early no problem. Hospitality went downhill from there. Our waiter Kit was super unfriendly each encounter and once he dropped our drinks off, we barely saw him again! No water refills and it was at least an hour between the crew's apps (which came about 35 minutes after drinks) and when their entrees arrived. There was so much time in between I had forgotten completely that the girls in my party even ordered any mains! And the place was empty! I thought we were just chatting post nosh at that point. It was atrocious in my opinion. No apology. No concern. He was mixed up and even brought two of one of our dishes. We were in no rush honestly, and the girls I was with overall didn't care too much, but I think Kit should be a shamed. Seemed like a lovely place and we had great conversation over our fantastic cocktails, but he ruined any chance of a future visit for me. It was the only negative service experience of our whole jammed packed trip! What a shame. 

Limited veg options. 

Drag brunch looks like a hoot, but we won't be returning.

Stars for decor, ambiance, cocktails, easy booking and availability only.

First of all, the original concept is GENIUS. Pure genius! I must admit I too once had a similar business idea that came to me late night, way back then when I was up wishing something was open at that very moment to fulfill my munchie cravings. I was actually going to name my mobile late night sweets delivery business "Baked". Get it? Oh well, they kinda beat me to it. Such is life. Maybe if I had less late nights I would've had more motivation to jump on that idea? Hmmm.

We have been fans of Insomnia since they were just a modest food truck up in University City. Now they have over a dozen locations and ship nationwide! Congrats guys! 

When these cookies are hot, they are ridiculous!!! These novelty cookies are on the flatter side but their flavor definitely is not. Melty, gooey and oh so, so good! So good!! The whole thing is kitschy and cute... name, concept, packaging. The to-go pizza boxes are an adorable touch. 

This fam always gets s'mores, M&M, double chocolate mint and double chocolate chunk! You cannot go wrong with any of those! Yum! They will now also stuff ice cream Between two of these bad boys! Wow. 

Oh, and now they have ahh-mazing VEGAN cookies too!! Oh yea! I thank you Insomnia!! My waistline does not!

Always a home run with these cookies! 
Makes a great take home dessert after a meal or happy hour across the street at Double Knot! 

Oh, service at this particular location could be a tad friendlier, but this Cookie Monster will
put up with a little Oscar The Grouch for these delicious treats. Nom Nom Nom. 
4.5 Stars

I can't really think of anything to add to the  list of rave reviews for Sabrina's except for maybe the fact that they hands down have THEE best tofu scramble in the entire city...and I've eaten my fair share around this town. It's hearty and filled with sautéed spinach, peppers and meaty mushrooms. It's perfectly egg colored with some turmeric and is accompanied with the best Le Bus toasted multigrain and perfectly fried cubed fried potatoes. Pro tip: ask for a side of spicy marinara. Totally completes the taters!

If you live here you know Sabrina's is pretty solid and without a doubt one of the best brunch spots in the city. With that being said, you may be totally over the long lines you'll find here on a weekend. If you're not from the area I'm going to go ahead and say, it's worth the wait. Stuffed sweet challah French toast is a specialty and not to be missed. Go ahead and splurge. We usually do one savory, and one sweet dish to split. Get a side of their insane sweet potato fries for the table. They're  incredible and perhaps my favorite ever. 

Another go-to for this fam is the Greek salad for lunch dates which comes with perfectly toasted pita wedges and mounds of their delicious hummus. It's outrageous but vegans beware, it does contain diary even when ordered without the feta. 

This actually isn't my favorite location, I'm more of an original South Philly kind of gal, but the service is always good, the 70's vintage vibes are groovy, and this is where I actually tasted that scramble for the first time on a "morning after", walk of shame kind of date. Nostalgic. Oh, and this location is opened late. 

A must if you've never, and a good old classic if you have. Be prepare for leftovers. The portions are massive!

Scoop DeVille isn't your average ice cream place and it's definitely somewhere I think everyone should try at least once. The concept is very interesting. They create flavors as they are ordered by mixing various ingredients. It's really kinda neat!! 

They have a very extensive menu which you can find copies of at the beginning of the line. Shakes, sundaes and splits. You still may not know what you want by the time it's your turn to order as there are so many tempting options. 

In addition to the regular menu, they have dairy free, gluten free and calorie conscious options as well as a seasonal menu! I mean, there's really something here for everyone!! Everyone! No excuse not to visit. 

Our most recent visit was after date night when we both turned to each other at the same moment when we said we wanted dessert and exclaimed "Scoop DeVille". Done deal. He went for one of their signature blends with banana and loved his and I chose the pecan pie from the vegan/gluten free menu. It was dairy free soft serve blended with maple syrup, pecans and sea salt. Love the wholesome ingredients in this one! Also, since I was torn between two blends I asked for one scoop to be made with Oreos and they obliged without issue. It was outrageous!!! 

You could visit so many times and never taste the same thing. I love that there are both suggestions as well as the opportunity to completely create your very own signature ice cream! How cool!! 

The place is super cute with lots of cute photo ops!

There a 30 minute loading right across the street for an easy in/out. 

Prices I believe are fair and service is a wee bit on the slower side but since they're creating something especially for you, it's kind of to be expected. 

We all love it here and will continue to return! 

They currently offer a promo to go hand in hand with Center City SIPS on Wednesday's from 4-8pm which is half price shakes, floats and smoothies. 

*Currently offering free cookie with Yelp check in which I always forget so don't you!

Adorable little Mom & Pop ice-cream shop offering 38 mouthwatering flavors! THIRTY EIGHT!

While I can't personally speak about the taste, I can comment on the kindest, most gracious owners you could ever imagine. Just the signs around the shop say it all "we are not in the food business, we're in the people business" and "throw kindness around like confetti". They asked me where I was coming from and if it was my first time, which it was. I'm assuming this means they have a lot of regulars from the neighborhood. Love this! They even gave me treats for my dog which they allowed in the shop. So, so sweet!

Prices were very fair. We left with a kids portion of mint chocolate chip (with big hunks in it), on a jimmie and chocolate dipped cone and two little chocolate covered marshmallows made to look like a scoop of ice-cream in a mini cone. So cute!! 

I personally would've chosen the chocolate raspberry chip, Bullwinkle or banana pb chip but no vegan ice-cream here. They do however have sorbet, rainbow and lemon. Toppings were just .50 extra. 

It's cash only and there's a tip jar. 

There's a dog bowl filled with water outside on the front porch. Rocking chairs and lights strands for at night. Despite being right on Township Line, it had such a small, seaside town feel to it which I adore. 

I found a new ice cream shop to take my kiddos to when we're in the area! So happy to have finally stopped here. It was a pleasure! 

5 Stars for hospitality and variety alone, but since I didn't taste...4

I can't get enough of kitty cafes, and this one is the cutest I've been to! (So far). It's bright with pastels, lots of pink with pink faux fur accents. The perfect place to have a girls' day!

Reservations are simple and made online. $11 for one hour time and they're very firm with you staying for your allotted time only. 

The place is definitely on the smaller side. Only 10 guests are allowed at one time and slots fill up rather quickly so plan in advance. 

The names, ages and personality traits are listed for you on a chalkboard so you can get to know the feline friends better. There were about 6 mostly playful kitties when we visited. Ages ranged from 4 months to about 2/3 years. 

I would be lying if I said that another draw for me beside the obvious wasn't the unicorn treats! Hot cocoa, milkshakes and sundaes too! They will make all of them vegan too if you ask, which I LOVE and surely appreciate. Just a heads up, they're made with coconut milk. May be a deal breaker for some. My little isn't a fan of coconut. I should've thought to ask before I ordered. I had no problem finishing hers however :)

The cafe itself is separate from the visiting room so feel free to stop by for a caffeinated beverage and to peek in at the kitties even if you don't have an appointment. 

We had a great time! Such a fun way to spend sometime and help out the animals too! Even if you can't adopt for some reason, you can at least get your fill of kitty love here and take satisfaction in knowing you're helping to keep the place going, and the cats well take care of. 

We will all be back! 

Bring quarters. 4th Street is old school meters.

Awesome find!! I can safely say after my first experience here and tasting only two items so far, this place is legit! So happy to add it to my list of restaurants in this area and finally cross it off my bookmarks. Hidden gem for sure! 

Stoped by for a quick lunch while in the area.  They have a $9.99 small lunch buffet but the lovely waitress informed me there were only two veg items there so it wasn't really for me personally. Take a look for yourself. 
Perhaps there's more options for you! 

The menu in the photos on their listing is lacking a great deal. There's a TON of options including an entire page of vegetarian dishes! Yeah baby! (I took a pic. Didn't sync. Ugh!) 

I started with samosas. Two huge perfectly crispy, absolutely packed samosas to an order, served with a chutney and a spicy dipping sauce. Each bite was a of crisp exterior and soft warm veggies and potato. No bites of just wrapper. Absolutely delish! Not too chewy. Not too hard. Goldilocks style, just right. These have replaced my current front-runner for 'Best Samosas'!

I then had my eye set on my Indian go-to, Aloo Gobi. I asked if they could bulk up the protein by adding lentils, spinach and chickpeas. She obliged, no issue. Mild was the perfect amount of spice. Packed with flavor and served with a side of basmati. This simple yet flavorful dish was done so right. Another winner. Decent portions left me with dinner that night as well! 

The ambiance was lovely. Deep red walls, mirrors and ethnic touches. The music set the mood and mimicked the cuisine also. Very nice. 

Service was great!

I can't wait to head back when in the NE again. I'm bringing my fam in the area next time too! Already told them what they're missing!

*It's BYO! 
**They have a Halal Market attached to the restaurant. 
***Located in the shopping center behind Nifty Fifties. 

My food photos didn't sync with my phone. Ugh! (Just an excuse to head back soon! Lol)

3.5 Stars Located just past Pat & Geno's is this tiny little Italian sweet shop and cafe. I've probably walked past it a bunch of times and never really noticed until recently... 

Pros: 
-Pretty decent espresso and coffee 

-Free, unmetered street parking 

- Their hot chocolate is the big draw for us. Way cool! Kiddos love it! Choose from a variety of fun chocolates chunks and they will custom make your drink. Pumpkin, cotton candy, chili, orange creamsicle, pina colada, caramel, pb and more! Very cool! 

-Italian imported grab and go packaged items goods

-A wide and unique variety of cannoli options. Pistachio and get this, Parmesan crusted cannoli shells with fillings such as hazelnut Ana tiramisu. Fun! Mini available too. 

-classic gelato too!

-bags of chocolate chip ricotta filling for sale!

-If you're in the area for a cheesesteak and need to use the restroom since Pat & Genos don't have one, grab something in here to use their facilities. 

-enough space to relax and meet a friend for a cup of joe without feeling rushed. 

-staff was very nice! 

Cons-
-pricey. VERY pricey. 2 mini cannoli and 2 hot cocoa came to just under $25! 

-mini cannoli are must buy two. 

-While there's a huge variety of cannoli and they will satisfy a sweet craving, you may be left wondering if they were worth the calorie splurge. 

All and all, we'll probably come again for make your own hot cocoa for the kiddos, but only when we want to splurge, financially I mean-oddly enough.

We came to this location of Whole Foods for the first time in forever this past weekend to avoid the 'Made In America' chaos we would've encountered headed to the location we usually shop at across The Parkway. Instead we encountered chaos here....

I'm not one to feel claustrophobic, I mean I sleep in tents sometimes, but this place is the stuff panic attacks stem from. Ugh!! The aisle are so small, so tight and so packed. I never noticed it before! I kept saying to hubs "I can't. I just can't". 

If given the option, I would never shop at this location and don't recommend it unless you live very close by. If you can get to the other one easily, I would absolutely go there instead. In fact, I would personally go completely out of my way to go to the other location in Philly...period. 

Not only were some of the shelves empty, one elevator was broke while the other one took FOREVER. To boot, the employees were ALL miserable!! I asked someone for help and they didn't even turn around from stocking the fridge shelves to answer me. The cashier barely said "hello" and the guy pushing the carts almost ran us over and didn't flinch. I have definitely been spoiled with the customer service at the new location and have honestly come to expect certain high standards when shopping at WFM in general. This location was sorely lacking. 

The saving grace for us here was frolicking with the kiddos on the rooftop with 360 views of the city and the photo ops the Isaiah Zagar mosaics provided. 

I actually referred to this trip as the equivalent as shopping at Walmart on Del Ave on payday. Ugh!!! Never again. 

Generous stars because in the end, it is a WF.

Shopping in the area and in search of a quick, healthy lunch. Last time we opted for the make your own salad place I won't name in the mall. It was so bland and so boring. Service was horrendous and I felt as though I was being punished with that awful meal for trying to eat clean. Never again will I eat at one of those places. Ugh, Gross! That was the last go. Bleeech! What to do, what to do....Looking for somewhere guilt free and just as quick, but actually tasty...

"Let's try Zoe's again" I said. We weren't completely sold the first go around with our falafel. This time? A totally different story!! So glad we gave it a second try because we now have a go-to when we're in the area again! 

The menu is clearly marked with vegan, vegetarian and gluten free options as well as calories!! Hallelujah! Lots of great low cal options! Soups, salads, sammies, protein boxes, flavored hummus and sides too! Grab a menu from the box at the beginning of the line. You probably still won't know what to eat when you get to the front! 

Mom chose the 1/2 soup, 1/2 salad option which is only available with their house Greek. (I would've ordered the 1/2 lentil, 1/2 Live salad but they wouldn't do it) Side note: they sell their famous Greek dressing to go and have bottles to taste on each table. She was very pleased her her meal. 

I was torn between the quinoa or Live Mediterranean salads and the lentil soup. I asked the girl behind the counter and without hesitation she suggested the "Live" so that's what I went with (without the parm cheese). It was incredible! Packed with flavor and fresh herbs. It had great texture and protein too. Now THAT'S how you do a salad! (It's the same price as the crappy one in the mall too) Healthy eating should be a pleasure, not a punishment! Here it was a delight! My tasty salad had spinach and farro, ribbons of zucchini and squash underneath, crunchy veggies and Iupini beans!! I haven't seen lupini beans on a menu since Vedge! Woo hoo! Mmmm, so delish! The woman who brought our meals to the table handed me a cup of pepper dressing on the side, but it didn't need it. I think it was lightly tossed already. Taste before you pour. You too may not need the extra! Not sure if the 590 calorie count included this extra dressing or not. Hmmmm? 

We both added a flavored seltzer to our meals. She chose raspberry and I went with cucumber which was amazing and refreshing! If you're watching your intake, read the labels. Hers had sugar, mine had none. We assumed they were both cal & sugar free like a LaCroix. 

A fantastic grab and go spot with a variety of clean(er) eats! 

A few tables outside too! 

They also cater! 

We will be back soon!

I'm no expert on Indonesian food and I'm primarily a plant based gal, but I still really enjoy D'jakarta, a small friendly authentic corner spot deep in the heart of South Philly! 

So far we've tried the happy lychee and happy mango drinks and enjoyed them both, with the mango being a favorite. It's piled high with tons of fruit and had a waterice/smoothie consistency. Definitely go for one of their fruity drinks, even if just to split and taste! 

We're big fans of ketoprak, a traditional vegetarian dish from Jakarta, which consists of tofu, vegetables and rice cake, rice vermicelli served in peanut sauce! It's so flavorful! 
*They can and will sub the fried egg to make it vegan!

I love their tamarind soup! It's located on the back sheet of the menu and it's easy to miss. It comes in small or large with a sweet and sour base, cabbage, peanuts and potatoes! Most recently we added a side of their delicious coconut rice for just $2 to bulk it up! So good!!!

We've tried their spring rolls which are perfectly fried and crispy! They come with an insane tangy peanut dipping sauce I could eat an entire bowl of!! 

Hubs recently had the chicken wontons and said while they were tasty, they had too much dough. He prefers the satay. 

The menu can be a bit overwhelming to newbies and/or plant based folks, but it's definitely worth venturing out for! I have yet to be disappointed by anything! 

For those from Indonesia or who are experts in the cuisine, they all rave about it here! 

BYO! 
Street parking is typical South Philly and requires a bit of patience.

I kept trying to think of reasons not to give our first experience here less than 5 stars and I honestly can't. It wasn't that it's such a fancy 5 star restaurant, it's that our cocktails, all of my food, and our service were really outstanding. The vibes here in the former two story bank, now an Americana themed restaurant named for Alexander Hamilton was lovely and overall, a fabulous night out was had by all of my girlfriends. 

We made reservations easily via Open Table for Restaurant Week on a First Friday at 6:45pm. We were seated shortly after arrival and even before all in our party were there. Much appreciated. We walked past coat of arms decor, past the welcoming bar which had signs for 'buck and shuck' happy hour, past the open kitchen which had lovely trendy white subway tiles and Mason jars giving off a hint of southern feel. We were seated at a cozy candlelit window booth which we all said would be great during the day for people watching here in Olde City. 

We were greeted immediately by our kind and personable waitress Shannon who from beginning to end, was absolutely fantastic. On top of water refills, quick with menu suggestions (both food and drink), getting plates cleared, and she checked in on us often. She knew the menu very well and anything she didn't she asked the kitchen for me right away. I should also note that our two male busers were equally as friendly and efficient. 

While their beer selection was pretty clutch, most of us started with some of their strong creative cocktails which by the way, are different than the ones listed online. (I took a photo for you guys.) These are not to be overlooked! Lemon Fizz & Lavender Drop which the bartender made for me so kindly without the whey. Both the lavender and the lemon were perfectly noted and not overpowering. Next we had the Blood Orange Paloma and Cucumber Crush made with a fresh rosemary. That rosemary!! Yum! Highly recommend!

Three at our table decided to go with the Restaurant Week $35/3 course menu which including some menu additions only available for RW. They started with both east and west coast oysters trays. I on the other hand decided to choose from the everyday heavily Southern influenced menu... 

I started with the Butter Lettuce, Apple & Pear salad ($11) with Endive, Toasted Pecans, Stilton, Fig, Candied Bacon, Maple-Cranberry Vinaigrette. They made it without the cheese and bacon and it missed nothing. So juicy, sweet and refreshing! Very generous plate. 

Next, the table split the Sweet Potato Fries with
Sorghum Molasses, Powdered Sugar ($6). These were the best sweet pot fries I've ever had! And I have had my fair share of sweet potato fries. ((Covers eyes)). Whether it's dinner or brunch, if you're with a larger party, try an order of these to split! You neeeed a taste! Delicious!!! 

For my entree I chose the Kale Pesto Pasta with Cauliflower "Steak", Roasted Tomatoes, Orecchiette but sans Farmer's Cheese ($16). It was outstanding! The addition of crispy kale chips on top was perfection and so unique! Dreaming about a plate of this right now! Again, very generous portion leaving me with an entire meal for the following day! 

We all had a fab time and thoroughly enjoyed our meals here. We would all recommend! I definitely want to hit up brunch here soon and would do a happy hour no question.

Robert's Western World was everything I thought a Honky Tonk would be... a tad edgy, dark, filled with nostalgia and history, crowded and absolutely rockin'. It took a few minutes for us to find a seat which was made a little awkward as everyone was staring me down because I had the kiddos with me. Children are allowed to enter, stay and have a ball until 6pm, then it's strictly 21 and over. Honestly, this was THE best way for me to show them first hand what Music City is all about!! People wouldn't think Nashville would necessarily be a destination for children and I'm here to tell you that's absolutely false! We all equally LOVED honky talk hopping and Roberts was at the absolute top of our favorites list! A must stop! The girls LOVED Eileen Rose & Silver Threads who played while we were there. They were incredible! I highly recommend trying to stop by when they're there. They are regulars! Check the band schedule on Robert's site. They played it all....Janis, Patsy Cline, Cash (obviously) and some fab originals such as "Rose Garden" which is one of our favorites. They were so insanely talented!! That guitarist blew my mind!! He could've easily been Stevie Ray Vaughn, Kenny Wayne Shepherd or Satriani. Wowza!! 

Make sure you bring cash to drop in their artist's bucket. They live on these tip and it's the least you can do as there's no cover charge. The girls begged me to purchase the CDs the band was roaming around selling. I think I paid $5 each! It was the best souvenir we bought our entire trip! We still listen to them daily!!  

The bartender was a doll. You can place order at the bar and she will bring it to your table. I had some local drafts, Yazoo for about $6 each The girls split pickle spears and sweet potato fries they gobbled up in two seconds as well as moon pies for $1. Typical bar food. PBR & fried bologna sammys are the supposed "thing" here however. 

Definitely put Robert's on the very top of your Broadway stops list!! It was an absolute blast!!

We hadn't been to this casual Steven Starr in forever. I mean, probably since the first week they opened years ago. No real reason except we don't frequent this neighborhood as much as we used to. When we found ourselves at an event at "The Shambles" across the way with the kiddies on a weekday night, a chill pizza date at Stella seemed like a no brainer...

The place definitely has some interesting design details and an all around cool vibe. We loved walking in the front door to see the  guys flipping dough and placing pies into the gorgeous wood fire oven. I also love the idea of dining al fresco on Headhouse although this particular night we sat at the bar downstairs which had a flatscreen making it a good option if you want to catch a game. 

Although pizza is their main thing, their antipasti, flatbreads, pasta dishes, smaller plates and specials are not to be overlooked. They're authentic and strong accompaniments. 

Their pizzas range from traditional to more creative. The pie is all around somewhat thinner, just how we like it. The zucchini pie was so memorable and flavorful! Vegan friends, they can and will make it sans the lemon ricotta cheese. It has a bit of olive oil so it certain won't be dry. The crunch of the julienned zucchini with freshness of the mint and the zing of the black pepper...it was quite perfect! 

Our waiter was very knowledgeable of the menu and efficient. He suggested a red we really enjoyed also. Don't hesitate to ask for suggestions here! 

Glad to have put Stella back on our radar! It's a truly great place to share a pie, grab a fantastic glass of red wine or even one of their creative cocktails, and just hang. We'll be headed here the next time we have the fam in tow when we're in the area

Obsessed!! Not only with the insanely gorgeous space that showcases impeccable attention to detail and so many stunning ways to honor and highlight the culture... in the decor, market goods and dish-ware, but with the food too. And I haven't even tried half of the traditional Lebanese offerings! 

 I'm going to go bold here and say Suraya dishes up the best falafel I've ever had...and I've eaten falafel in the Middle East! It's pretty darn fantastic!! Unbelievable, actually. Crispy fried golden exterior, perfect warm interior. Perfect crunch to soft ratio. So incredibly delish! If you want to save the carbs or just eat a smidge lighter, go for the balls themselves, and not the platter. Not listed, just ask! 

To date, I've tried two of their hummus flavors... the mushroom and the crispy chickpea. They're both uber creamy, totally flavorful, loaded with toppings, and just excellent. Up there as my second favorite hummus in ALL of Philly! 

I've also tried their baba ganoush complete with pomegranate seeds! What a lovely, crunchy, colorful addition to the dish. This smoked eggplant dip has just the right amount of smokiness and garlic! Great texture too! 

Their rosewater lemonade is just beautiful and refreshing. I absolutely love it! Tart and sweet. A must! 

The clementine ginger beer with cardamom served in a copper mule mug is also fantastic! 

The beet salad, and Man'oushe (Lebanse flatbread) are up for me next! Oh, and the tehina hot chocolate! Yessss!! 

Make sure to leave some time to walk around the entire space. It's just gorgeous! The cafe is super sweet with fresh deep jewel tone blooms on each table and bright light shining through the big windows. The bar is gorgeous and inviting. The dining room is spacious and candle-lit, and the back porch will transport you to another country!! I can't wait until it's officially open back there! I'm in love with the patterned pillows, wrap around bench, wood-burning fireplace and tiled floor!! Oh, and definitely take a peek at the goods for sale. Most of them, if not all, are straight from Lebanon. Spices, oils, body goods, and textiles too! It's like perusing a shuk! 

The only things that bum me out are the fact that they're closed on Mondays. There have been several, several Mondays I've wanted to go. Also, the fact that they don't take ressies for brunch. I really wanted to bring my mom and our fam here for Mother's Day. Perhaps a dinner soon will be better? Those cocktails and even the Lebanese beer are calling my name. I hear Open Table is starting to accept reservations for that time frame!

I cannot say enough good things about Suraya!! It's such a pleasure for all the senses to dine here. I'm so in love! I heard 'Suraya' is the name of the owner's grandmother. They are certainly making her proud. 

I honestly can't see me ever tiring of this gem! It's really worthy of all of the hype it's receiving!

*There's street parking which is easy to find during the day, but also an entire lot across the street!

Super stoked to have Second District here to help put this side of South Philly on the map, so to speak. A terrific addition to this West Passyunk neighborhood that gets much less recognition than its east side counterpart. Perhaps with places like this popping up, that will change...

First of all, the space is awesome! It's a converted garage and they have left the doors there for opening open up in warmer weather! They also kept the original exposed brick and beams, and an old faded sign. They've added a variety of unique vintage mirrors and sconces to the bar area and it's completely candlelit at night. It was perfectly romantic for our first visit on a rainy night date! There's also a back room for spreading out a bit more room with vats and such. I totally loved the vibes!

While they don't offer tasting flights, they do offer three sizes of pours. We opted for 4oz of 5 of their brews... Friends & Family, AlterNative, SuberOwl, Bancroft and A Series Of Grand Gestures. All were delicious and unique! 
Bancroft, while we hear is a fan favorite, was our least favorite. If I had to choose one, it would definitely be the AlterNative, a lighter ale brewed with lemon and thyme while hubs enjoyed the SuberOwl which is fermented with foraged saison yeast best. 

I really admire the fact that they partner up with local breweries such as Foster & Main and Lost Abbey/Port Brewing. I love seeing that! 

SD offers a small variety of bar snacks and their veg friendly options were definitely a plus for me! We tried the vegan pork rinds and while I have no idea what they were made out of, they were tasty! Salty and light. We also shared the curly fries which were crispy and fried to perfection. The smoked ketchup which accompanies them was fantastic!! Do NOT miss a dip in this ketchup! We also had our eye on the sliders which come three to an order but you must get one of each variety or three of one kind. They do offer a black bean one as an animal friendly option. Next time for sure. 

If you find yourself here and in the mood for a sweet treat, they will serve you their HUY brew, a Vietnamese coffee stout served with with a donut and spoon. Neat! 

Our bartender Alex was attentive and friendly. Bites and brews were served in a very timely manor. 

We look forward to many more visits here. Welcome to the neighborhood! 

*Parking isn't the easiest, but not impossible. Uber, by foot, even bike may be best. They just installed bike racks. 

**As of this time there was was no contact information, but they do have social media accounts. Their Insta is interesting!

Wonderful little BYO Italian spot in the adorable, quaint town of Haddonfield. 

We hosted a truly lovely bridal shower here where we were able to bring our own centerpieces and decorations, including candles and balloons. We were able to invite our guests a fresh bread basket with house oil on each table, a refreshing, light, crunchy apple salad to start, and to select one of two entrees. We chose to offer their signature crab cakes with whipped mashed potatoes and veggies and thinly pounded chicken parm with pomodora. Both seemed to be very well liked by our guests! 

They even created a vegan meal just for me! It was the most delicious pasta primavera I've EVER had over my choice of pasta, capellini. It was filled with sautéed veggies and quite the hearty portion! Made with olive oil and no parm. Super tasty! Veg-heads, don't hesitate to ask for this! They were super helpful with dietary restrictions! Fountain beverages of our choosing as well as the wine we brought were our drinks. 

For dessert, the restaurant made a large layered cannoli cake we were able to personalize! Love that they took care of all of this leaving us, the hosts, to focus solely on other aspects of the party. A plate of mini chocolate chip cannoli were also given to each table in addition to the large slices of moist airy cake with thick creamy ricotta frosting. Coffee as well as single and double espressos were available for our party during dessert also. Espressos were on point. 

There are three separate rooms; a main dining room, and two back rooms. All decorated slightly different, but very well! The copper tin ceiling in the main room was just gorgeous! The middle room we used was bright and looked out onto the Main Street of town. It was super comfortable for our party of 25 with room for about 10-15 more! The entire place is all very cozy! 

There were two parties including ours going on at the same time, and one did not interfere with the other as there are separate entrances for each dining space! Super smart! 

Overall I was highly impressed with the precise attention to detail while planning and executing the party. The service given by our kind waiters was really fantastic! They should absolutely be commended. They checked in on the hosts often, my salad was brought without cheese without having to ask after ordering a main meal sans dairy, and they even knew to wait for the proper time after photos to cut and serve the cake, plus they packaged the leftovers as to-go slices for our guest! This was not their first rodeo! 

The food I tasted was really, really great and the $25/pp included everything I mentioned, and was well worth it in my opinion! It was such a wonderful place to host. We were left to worry about very little! What a joy! Throwing parties can be super stressful and the staff here made us feel so at ease. It was such an enjoyable, relaxing event as a host!

I would highly recommend checking this place out if you're hosting a special lunch or dinner if you live in Jersey. They did a remarkable job with everything! I would actually consider it for future dinners I host even driving the 20 minutes or so from Philly. 

I would like to come back and dine on a regular night and taste from the set or maybe even try the 3 course for $22 menu also!

We were able to park free, unmetered in PNC Bank lot just next door on a Sunday. You can do so after hours also. Other than that, bring quarters for the old school meters in town.

A true NE Philly staple. Located centrally on Roosevelt Boulevard is this 24 hour diner which has pretty much remained the same for decades. 

Breakfast served all day long making it a convenient stop for late risers or late-nighters looking for some sobering up nosh. 

The fam favors classic Jewish deli fare like matzoh ball soup, lox and whitefish salad platters which are plated with traditional and generous accompaniments. 

Daily lunch and dinner specials for a steal. 

Kids menu items are about $6 and under and include drink and dessert. Although my kiddos go for the chocolate chip pancakes which of course are NOT are on the kids' menu, they are two to an order, filled with chips and huge. Definitely shareable between two littles. 

Their salads are massive and also splittable. 

A few vegetarian options and literally one vegan option which is the grilled veggie wrap. It's completely stuffed and good. It's served with pretty tasty fries. I personally need a dipping sauce or mustard for the wrap however. 

People loved their desserts. Maybe grab one as you're leaving. 

Prices are overall very fair making it a decent option for larger parties. They also have a back room where tables can be pushed together. 

The place is rather large and we have never had to wait even with a group. 

Service is never something to write home about here however. 

It's definitely not on my list of places I would head to eat when in the area but it does serve a purpose.

We came to this bar with high expectations and we were really disappointed. The drinks were good but the food was overpriced and not great. All of the waitstaff was extremely rude and talked about us right in front of our table. Overall, we were really disappointed. Also, a 20% gratuity was automatically added when it was definitely not deserved.

I hate giving bad reviews so I'll just make this short. 
The BBQ didn't live up to the hype and the place was dirty. Sorry but I have to keep it real.
