A pretty bizzare experience if you ask me. 
Please help me understand why a server will serve  you a glass of white wine for 15$ and then turn around and sell it to your dinner date when he requests the bottle and the price is 12$ for the entire bottle? I was baffled! 
Where are these products made? The international space station? That must determine the ridiculously high prices like 16$ a pound for hummus. hummus. You read that right. 
Service is polite but slow and you have to go downstairs to pay for everything.  Get a grip people! I moved down to Florida to escape inflation

Finally decided to stop by for a real sit down dinner. Can't believe it's only been a year since they opened and it's still a very busy place. The interior is spacious and full of interesting architecture. My four starts goes mostly to our excellent server who we kept on his toes for the entire night. I had the grouper and even though I liked it I felt it was missing a bit of seasoning. I also tried the chocolate ice cream and the flourless tart both good but the tart is very very rich so I recommend you share. Some tried the dessert with bacon and they felt in love. It's a great space for events and will absolutely go back to to try other items on the menu. I got what I'm calling truffles as a Ulele gift and they were amazing why are these not on the dessert menu... Please add them ASAP

It's a beautiful place BUT that is it!!  Skip this place if you want great service. There was a group of us and we waited 20 minutes for the first round of drinks.  Water service came once during our 2 hour stay. Finally someone in our party went and got their own pitcher. The waiter was irritated when we asked for champagne glasses for champagne instead of wine glasses. Food- well lets just say everything came cold and took over an hour to get to us.  
Save the frustration and head to Flemings!

This is a nice spacious restaurant with outdoor seating right on Massachusetts Avenue. You can either be seated or place orders to - go. Use your camera to take a picture of the QR reader and it will send you to the menu. The only thing is you can't tell what's in the tacos. So, ask the hostess and she will hand you a paper menu to see what the different type of tacos are. The service was pretty quick since a lot of people were ordering or had already ordered to - go when I was there. 

The Plain Jane taco and the Blue Dream tacos were good. I preferred the Plain Jane over the other, but they have so many options trying different ones would be easy to find more favorites. The chips are thick enough that they can withstand queso! I loved that! The smoked Gouda queso was good. The only thing that wasn't great was the amount of grease I had to drain off the top. The chips and salsa were good and I ordered  a cup of guacamole which wasn't in the bag :-( 

I look forward to trying out more options they have and am glad that tacos are the star of this restaurant. Taco Tuesday everyday I say!

Made a reservation for a booth for two, celebrating a special occasion.  When we checked in with the hostess she showed us to a table for four.  The wine flights were tasty and appropriately priced.  Being this is a small plates dining experience and we started with white wine, we ordered cheese fondue and cream cheese wontons for our first course.  The cheese for the fondue tasted like a very floury béchamel sauce given no attention.

As for the cream cheese wontons...  Head to your local Walmart and steer towards the frozen appetizers and you've got Divvy version.
The wait time is ridiculous and is thrice the time they quote to you. The owner does not understand how to seat people in sequential order. She is confused. The one star is for food which is good

Would you throw away $16.00 worth of food over a $2.50 drink. No you say. I wouldn't  either. But they would. My fiancee were there from out of  town I ordered a beer $4.50. The waitress came back at least three times to ask him for his drink order while we waited for our food. There was no sign saying you MUST  GET IT BEFORE your food comws. He said no apparently a bit to strongly for the manager and the next thing I knew they were coming to either take our food and trash it or him order a drink immediately. 
The food staff and and everyone we're not very customer friendly stating they had  been burned many times. It was a minimum $2.50 and I had  already paid $4.50 for a beer. Geesh. Will never go back. Didn't even get to taste the food. It was at the table less than 2 minutes before the came to scoop it up...

First off, their bagels and cream cheese are amazing!

But...

 4 out of 5 times that we went there they got my order wrong. I always order a poppyseed bagel, toasted, with plain cream cheese (not too difficult).

The last time we went, I got an un-toasted pumpernickel bagel, and I realized while they make your bagel that they don't wear gloves. Also they go from handling money, to making bagels, and back to handling money without washing their hands.

So from here on out I will be going to Einstein Bagels (where they wear gloves).

Those elevators tho! 

This place has cool driveway like Vegas and is new and modern. I don't review hotels normally unless they are bad. This is a solid Marriott with all the requisite accoutrements. The staff I encountered is quintessential NOLA southern hospitality.  Great location to exactly what we wanted to access aka French qtr, river view, 
Those elevators tho!

Walking distance to literally everything and a line of cabbies at your beckon call in case you want to explore farther out. 
Those elevators tho!

Bae, working a convention  was starving and needed to eat prior to managing their company booth and ordered a PO boy via room service. It came piping hot in 15 min! 
Those elevators tho!

Maybe cause I only ate half of a over priced turkey Samich, at 9:45 am at airport hearing east, and one measly bag of stale pretzels on da plane...
But this was rockin BBQ combo! Brisket, pork shoulder, and hot links 
Really didn't need any of the three BBQ sauces. That was until a brother at next table took a whole jug of "XXX hot sauce". I cleared a spot on my plate and he poured it Then it was on! 
Well triple X was more like a single X but made those meats jump lively. 
Perfect low carb accompaniments were the slaw made with sweet vinegar vs mayo and the crunch and acid was on point.
Then the cucumber salad also added acid and crunch to brighten the boldness of the proteins.
My fav was the links,  then brisket. The pork was a lil chewy but had great smoky flavor. 
All washed down with Pennsylvania's finest and my favorite brewskie.

Chef Paul Prudhomme was a family inspiration growing up. Whether it was his spice selections at the grocery store, or catching him on PBS doing his cooking show.
After my first visit to NOLA which was post Katrina. I got inspired to make grilled oysters at home for a dinner party. I used some of his "stuff" to "hook dem oysters up". 
Apparently along with my jambalaya, dem boys were  dah hit. One of the dinner guest in the printing biz sent us a newly  published edition of Chef Paul Prudhomme's cook book. 
I've made plenty meals to the delight of family and friends using his recipes, spices and inspiration. So it was an honor to finally dine in this establishment. 

I realized long ago it's important for any foodie dedicated to great cuisine to not just by cookbooks or watch cooking shows... but to immerse yourself in the culture by visiting the places in person.  I also realized as solid as my recipe followed creations are, there is no way to duplicate it. You just can't do it justice. So here we are window seat about to throw down on what I consider the 
Richest culinary mashup of cultural iconoclasts in the world.

Dah bread-shut up! No buttah required.
Dah turtle soup- I felt my blood thickening and my veins hardening with each decadent spoonful. So rich, a thimble full would be enough along with an eye drop of brandy. But I'm glad for the small cup because I was able to share! 
Dah Caesar salad- relief!  some acid, saltiness and fiber to counteract the rich decadence of the soup and bread. 
Dah Drum- I've used the Chefs blackening seasons for decades but mine never tasted like this!!!! Beat that drum chef! It was so flaky and fork tender! 
Dat tuna- made rare and seared with "hot fanny sauce"
This dish would make any died in the wool steak lover forget red meat. 
Dah veg and taters- I think potatoes, zucchini, carrots, peppers and squash would all like to end up being prepared like this. They taste like the absolute best versions of themselves. 

Dah Brewskie-Oh crap I forgot to mention I was drinking Yuengling throughout this culinary cavalcade of palette popping perfection!   Lord you can take me now. 


This meal was so perfecto, that we literally debated for 15 minutes to get dessert or not. The dilemma 

Totally stuffed and packed for our first class shuttle to heaven with spicy, briny, bright, savory and naturally sweet umami nirvana happening.

Or

Our two favorite pies: sweet potato and pecan assembled into one slice of heaven with whipped cream......

Like a hot hand in Vegas we decided not to push our luck as things could start to go in a very decadent and devilish direction rather swiftly.  

Our rational... we can always come back ya know.  Guess where we went for dessert the next day

I've been here before... not sure which trip. (I remember the loo being in a courtyard out back.) 
I'm being quite generous with 4 stars. We sat upstairs on the balcony over looking the street. The wait staff all seemed to have to run up and down rickety stairs to deliver food and drinks which may have contributed to the lackluster service. 
We only saw our actual waiter initially taking our order then when the bill came. A couple of other folks were also taking orders and delivering food and drinks around us. 
We ordered a Yuengling and appetizer of fried gator along with ice tea. The gator was as tough as a marine drill Sargent with hemorrhoids.
But because it came decades after we ordered it, one of the waitresses (maybe manager?) comped the gator. So we never bothered to tell her it was like eating fried dinosaur ass. 

So why 4 stars? Because this place is set up to be one hella great venue for Mardi Gras. And you can tell by the set up that theirs bars and service facilities to take care of upstairs patrons. 

Bring plenty of beads or a easy access shirt or blouse to flash your junk to collect some. Because from the upstairs vantage point you will have a solid perch to let it all hang out!

Place is in a strip mall ubiquitous in So Cal. We're heading elsewhere initially but the poke special was calling our names! Great photo advertising a poke salad for 12.99
And the ones delivered to our al fresco dining table looked like the photo. 
Healthy portions of spicy tuna, crab, salmon, along with furikake crusted rice triangles, edamame, seaweed mango cubes etc. big portion and we ate it all. 
One of my work associates never had poke. He is local and said he's bringing his wife back for dinner it was that good he said.

I don't get to SB often but if I wanted a casual but fresh and light meal, this place was spot on!

Ok I'm a dumb ass! Or maybe an idiot savant? So I am a visual guy. I actually DID use Yelp...and typed shrimp and Grits into the Yelp search menu. I then browsed pics of which places grits looked the best. As Andrew Zimern would say, "if it looks good... eat it!"
Browsing images of this place, I saw the shrimp and grits in that sculpted do-hickie bowl along with buttermilk biscuit. But it actually looked too Foo foo-e for me.  

However having worked in the hotel til noon, I looked up at clock, Holy Guacamole! Famished I redid the "shrimp and grits" search and the Ruby Slipper showed up closest walking distance. Yep that's my lazy ass scientific search criteria. It wasn't til I was done eating that I bothered to read my fellow elites reviews; raving about the place. 

When I arrived walking down Magazine St,  I thought there was a street party as folks were hanging out with bloody Mary's in plastic cups and a strip of bacon as the swizzle stick. I Bogarted my way up to the front and a gorgeous young lady all 4'9" of her asked if I wanted to sit at the bar. I was ok doing that. Then she started talking and I couldn't understand so I leaned down and she got mock mad at me for implying she was short and I couldn't hear her way up in 6 foot land. Short Stuff lead me to the bar and literally in 2 minutes I was seated. In another minute I had hot coffee and water and my order of shrimp and grits on its way. 

I then proceeded to search for "Dubs" tickets on line since they are playing the Hornets 2-nite (sorry ya'll, I can't bring myself to call them the P-bird word).

The bar is a great place to hang, catch up, make new friends, and score some hella good seats for a fraction of Oracle prices to see the Dubs!!! The waiter delivering my plate saw the section I was purchasing and said "Score.. great seats".

The shrimp plump and well seasoned the grits were no big thang except I like the rosemary they used to  season them. I'm totally steeling that idea! It's not like the grits were bad, they were perfectly cooked but pa-leeze when do you ever rave about toast or mashed potatoes? Only when they suck! Well these grits did not suck. 
The biscuit was as big as an 8 month pregnant hockey puck but cutting into it was light, flakey and moist as a cloud. Great with some buttah and Honey. 

The coffee was awesome; had two there, and my waiter hooked me up with a fresh cup to go. 

The meal was uneventful except some dude in a Chiquita Banana outfit apparently delivered a banana-gram to someone in the restaurant. Also Short stuff stopped over to inform me two ladies wanted to speak to me. I told her to tell them I was her squeeze and to back off. That got a big hug from her. 

Feeling stuffed and accomplished that I scored Dubs tickets and likely saved $500-1000 smackers, I headed out coffee in hand and managed to get another big hug from short stuff on the way out as well. I assume that was the signal to whomever those ladies were to back off jack!

Chef Michael was our guide to the history of New Orleans  and the reason the cuisine is a mash up of what makes America so great... aka diversity, respect for various cultures, equality and freedom  for all regardless of national origin, religion, sex, race or age.  
We learned so much about the history and reasons things happened as they did, how food was instrumental in shaping the culture, the selections and the diets of the locals.
Chef Michael gave props to chef Paul Prudhomme' who while working at Commanders palace "burned the redfish" and a culinary cuisine was born. 

Beside the amazing "who knew" history lesson, we were able to sample some great food. And to make a rue! 
Artichoke and shrimp soup. My favorite of the dishes, primarily because i'd never had it before. Very rich and decadent. 
crawdad étouffée could have used more spice so the little mini shopping carts full of condiments  on the table was perfect to spice things up.
the praline being made was as awesome as tasting it. 
abita beer perfect cool refreshment along with ice tea and aqua.
Our class had 29 folks so there was actually enough Artichoke and shrimp soup for second and a couple of folks at our table got 3rds. Not so much for the pralines which were woofed down rapidly. Bae and I split one leaving a second for the overtly grateful lady next to us.

Of course we took advantage of the discount on spices and stuff for attending the class to have it all shipped home. So I can continue to be inspired by Chef Paul Prudhomme' having just ate at K-Paul's 2 days ago having a mind blowing foodie experience. 

As Michael would say, when someone asked the question where is the best gumbo or e'toffee? " your house! 

I highly recommend the class and Chef Michael to any foodie or history buff.

There are only two types of music I hate! Country and western! Fortunately for us, we had to squeeze and push through to the back in order to find a clear area to hang... far enough that the squealing whining drawl did-not puncture my eardrums. There we spied 4 ladies all happy to celebrate one of theirs 51 birthday. There were a couple of seats and I politely asked if we could borrow a couple. 
Oh no...you may hafta sit on Tina's lap...that's her chair. Said one. Yep you better not she may not be happy another warned. I'm thinking Tina must be 6'10 and 2 fiddy! 
But the Yuengling was talking. I saw they were all drinking what looked like pink lemonade and figured Tina had to be diminutive based on those girly ass dranx. I said nope I'm sitting and when she gets here she can sit on my lap! 

Tina all 5 foot nada and 100 lbs soaking wet shows up. I introduce myself and explain the status of the sitting arrangements. To which she says I can't sit on your lap cause of my enormous set of Balls! 

We all hollered laughing! They said they were from LBC and I'm like where exactly? They said they had to go over a bridge and I'm like ah you are San Pedro homies! (Not that I lived in SP)  that got Tina so excited she swore one of her other girls told me. But that bonded us Cali folks for a couple of sets. Even my client lived in Manhattan beach and we had a good ol time chatting about So cal. 

Of course they never heard of Yuengling so I educated the crew who unanimously agreed "best f-n beer evah! 
But Tina was insistent i try that girly drink. So we got a round and I asked the bar tender what's in it. Apparently ruby grapefruit flavored vodka and tonic... damn if it wasn't very refreshing and good! Like Fresca! Tina corrected me no this drink is called titanium balls!  More hollarin! 

We pushed off to the next bar saluting the bday girl who got a tribute song cause Tina spent a bit of coin to have them do one in her honor. Another climbs on the bar stool to permanently etch their names on a vacant strip of woodwork on the wall. 

Country western is much more palatable when you are in the back of the joint with 4 cool ladies from So Cali!

I'm depressed.  I'm sick, my ass hurts from falling on it, getting overly excited during Superbowl, I bit my tongue and now have an alien living in my mouth named canker sore, and most of all, I miss New Orleans.

I didn't expect to fall in love with this city, but I did.  Madly...  I haven't felt this way about any city in a long time.  Especially, in the US.  Maybe it was the music, the people, the beautiful streets.  Maybe it was because I got to experience it with someone I love.   Whatever it was, I know I'll be back.  As soon as I can.

The Man and I were strolling along in the French Quarter taking in all the sounds and smells of history.  The warm southern air makes time stand still.  We did a quick search for a casual place to rest our feet and feed on some local fare and found this gem called Three Muses.  The sounds of piano keys and voices led us in.  After being seated, we quickly ordered cocktails and a plethora of food.  It was amazing.  To have this kind of food at a gastropub, left me in awe.  Rosemary infused cashews, oysters, sliders, and everything you can imagine was all so incredibly delicious. 


Three Muses defined New Orleans for me.  Musicians playing with their hearts, great food prepared by people who care,strong, tasty cocktails in an unpretentious environment, relaxed people, smiling and enjoying the moment.  Friends laughing, sharing delicious food.  

This is what our lives should be.  Not just on vacation but everyday.

I've enjoyed dining at this place for years. The food, atmosphere and staff has always been wonderful. However, I will no longer spend my money at an establishment owned/managed by a horrible person. The woman in charge berates staff, is extremely rude to customers, and obviously hates people. Time after time I've tried to convince myself, and guests who dined with me, that she was having an "off" day. No, that is her personality, and it's not getting better, it's getting worse.

Goodbye Stone House. It was great until it wasn't.

I have eaten at this place a few times.... tonight will be my last! The food is really the best soul food philly has that being said the business,  customer service and the overall organization Is THEE WORSE! 
Almost every time I have come into this business my order has been wrong or they are out of something & the young person taking orders at the front doesn't even have the decency to let customers know! 
Today I saw on their IG account they were having a delivery service so I called in at 5:45 pm guess what time I got my food...8:30pm!!! Mind u i live 10mins away!  I called over a dozen times looking for my order the phone lines never worked,  I got hungup on or was met with this NASTYYYYYY attitude! And my food was Luke warm! I'm done with tasties! When you can handle the demand of your customers.... maybe I will be back. MAYBE.

I would have given this a slightly better review, as the food wasn't too bad. The issue I have, and the reason I won't eat here again is because of what I saw when I was paying...

The cook was cleaning off his spatula with a scraper. Then, to clean off that scraper, he simply ran it across the top of the open trashcan, using the lip of the trashcan to get the gunk off. Of course, he uses the same scraper whenever he cleans off his spatula. Gross, and completely unsanitary...

5 star! 
Finally I got to experience The Catbird Seat after many attempts. We've scheduled earlier in the year but due to conflicts we had to reschedule. They did update their reservation process where you need to pay in advance. The cost plus drink pairings can run you 235 per person so be ready to drop some cash..

It was a Saturday afternoon and our reservation was at 5:30 the door was still locked so we had to knock. Wasn't a long wait but they opened up and we were the first one I there. You will go up the elevator to a small room that Sears roughly 12-14. The cook, sou, host, floor manager are all knowledgable of the menu and provided top notch service. 

The food was full of taste, texture, perfectly cooked, and well balanced with their drinks. You will not need any salt or pepper.. It comes out perfect! We had roughly 7-8 dishes including dessert. The food came out fairly quick as they cooked/made each dish right in front of you. I felt like I was in an episode of the iron chef. 

Portion for me was a tad bit small but in the end it was enough. I wasn't full but wasn't hungry. The entire experience is well worth the try and perfect for a special occasion. We will be coming back. 

It was a perfect place to have a date night with my wife.

Only place I could find in the area that has ube soft serve!!!!

Conveniently located across the street from the Atlantis Tesla chargers, so we can park the car and walk over for some dessert :P

They rotate flavors, with only about 3 - 4 different ones per day.
It's not like your standard froyo place, so don't expect the typical flavors or a huge selection.

They have flavors like ube, horchata, matcha, and black sesame, and you have the option to have it over some cake!

I went with just the soft serve since we had AYCE KBBQ right before, and it was delicious! so we'll definitely be back for more!

Small parking lot in front, friendly employees, Instagrammable decor ;), treat your tastebuds and give it a try if you haven't already!

Weekday AYCE lunch ($17.95/pp +$7 if you want to order off the dinner menu)-- 
Easy parking (same plaza as Costco), short wait, COVID-compliant (for a small restaurant), friendly staff, fun ambiance, and great food.
On another AYCE sushi adventure.
We always see this place when going to Costco and finally gave it a shot because why not? 
Did not disappoint! 
We sat at the sushi bar and our chef was very friendly, speedy, and accommodating! 
It was like visiting a relative's house and you don't want to be rude by rejecting anything they offer, so they feed you until you go into a food coma. That's what happened. 
My partner loves anything fried so all the appetizers, tempura nigiri, and the Midtown Roll were his jammm. 
My favorite was the Salmon Skin + Octopus Hand Roll and Mickey Nigiri (great fish to rice ratio). 
Sooooo full, but we always love to finish off with sharing a chocolate mochi. Chef insisted we get a mango mochi too so we did because you don't say no to Chef. Loved that the mochi was the right consistency when served (vs. being rock hard and having to wait for it to thaw). Both delicious and satisfying. 
Overall, a very enjoyable experience and would definitely recommend this place. Makes it to the top of the list of AYCE sushi in Reno. 
We left fat and happy, so what else could you ask for?
We'll be back to try the rest of the menu :)

Warning!!!!! Valet damaged my Rolls Royce!!! 

I'm very upset with this hotel and the lack of action to resolve this matter!!! The valet damaged my Rolls Royce on July 22nd 2016 and the hotel still has not done anything about it. I've been going back and forth with the hotel management and yet nothing has been done!!! 

To make matters worse I recently learned (from my attorney) that the hotel has several other claims pending against them for damage to vehicles from their valet department.

I'm staying at the Normandy Farm for a month on business and so I frequent this place a lot during my stay in PA. I'm usually not a fan of hotel-restaurants, but this place is awesome. Complementary breakfast (egg strata, scrambled, sausage, bacon, potatoes, cranberry juice, orange juice, yogurt, bagels, coffee) every morning, which I always take advantage of if I'm not running late. I haven't had lunch or dinner here yet, but I have tried some of their late night bar food. When in doubt or don't want to shell out too many dolla bills on food, get their bacon cheeseburger with beer-battered fries. I've heard good things about their lobster roll as well.

So far, strong drinks (if you ask for it!), good service, and good food. Not to mention, the interior is gorgeous as well as the simple table settings - cute mason jars on each table that really add a nice touch.

Came here for my birthday lunch last week and had a great experience. We started off with the vegetable rolls (similar to spring rolls) and peanut sauce. The peanut sauce had a bit of a kick to it, but it was also somewhat sweet and super tasty. 5 stars for the vegetable rolls!

The interior is modern and clean. You have the feel of being at an upscale bistro without the hefty price tag. 

We also enjoyed the lunch special which is currently priced at $8.95. You can essentially pick any type of noodle dish and your meat or tofu preference. I chose the tofu pad Thai. The pad Thai was tasty for a mild version. The fried tofu had a nice texture on the outside the the creamy tofu flavor on the inside. It also comes with a small side salad. The portion is not dinner sized, but was also more than I could eat for lunch. Definitely value to the meal, in that regard. 

I should have taken more pictures of the meal, but I figured I'd be back soon to try more dishes!

Oh no! I was so excited to try this place and I'm sorry it was such a let down! We just left here and I have to review this now! 
Our waitress was Victoria and I don't know if she is new but she wasn't that great. She didn't have a sense of urgency to get food out to her customers or realize what is an appropriate pace of a meal. The other waiters were okay so its not a staff development issue. We ended up tipping poorly which is something we never do unless service is very poor. I promise you we usually make it rain. We are generous tippers.
The first problem was our drinks. I ordered a Hurricane and it was the equivalent of overly sweet koolaid and lacked any alcohol whatsoever. My brother ordered a cognac and coke which lacked alcohol as well. His drinks took a super long time to come out and the ice melted. They should have remade the drink! No bueno. I asked for an extra shot of rum to put in my drink and that was forgotten. Oh well.
We ordered appetizers of crab cakes and coconut shrimp which were good.
Next issue is it took an hour for us to get our main entrees after our appetizers were cleared. It was laughable but we just waited. I ordered the snapper Oscar and subbed corn mache choux for the rice, my brother ordered the Robert, and my mum got the lamb chops. Nothing complicated. My brother's ribeye came out cold as if they used a frozen steak. Cold, yuck! Well my brother decided to send the steak back and told our waitress to try the steak.........which she did ( where do they do that at???!!!!) and agreed it was cold. It came back out hot. It had a proper cook as well. 
We got the butterscotch bread pudding with ice cream for dessert and it was good.
Our bill came out and it wasn't even ours. Then we got our correct bill and we were charged for the free bread pudding that I received when I checked in. Third time was a charm.
Our waitress only had four tables and I'm sure the table in front of us left because of the service. We had to flag her down several times.
Aww, one of the places I was looking forward to while visiting Tampa. I will definitely be returning to Tampa but I definitely not be returning here!!!

So I tried their cupcakes again... because somebody on their staff or connected to the place had the audacity to contact me on yelp, question my credibility and asked to change my rating...

This time i didn't go in, I had a friend buy some of their diligently made cupcakes (because I was afraid someone would jump me for expressing my opinion) and I am sorry, I'm still not impressed, I had better cupcakes.  And on Yelp, 2 stars = "Meh, I've experienced better" in philly.  Don't believe the hype.

Man, this place is awesome. Having been to France over 10 times, I have to say that SIPS really does a great job of replicating that exact feel of a French bistro... And for good reason, the owner / operator is FRENCH. 

Anyway, I like how they serve all the classic dishes without the fusion flare that most modern restaurants throw in. This way, you get a real sense of what classic French cuisine is meant to be and why it has obtained its supreme culinary reputation.

I've been to SIPS three times now, and it's my place of choice in Phoenixville. I've had the Bouillabaisse twice... It's just too good. I've had the Confit Duck once and it was the best duck dish I ever had. I saw another review that stated it was salty, which it is, but in my opinion it was perfect (I like salt).

All in all, when it comes to fine dining, I'd rather spend my money at SIPS than any other fine dining establishment in Phoenixville!

I hate that I'm having to write a negative review of this place, but the unfounded pretension and appalling service has really upset me.

I dined here once last year and had the most spectacular time. Literally everything about this place was incredible! So, you can imagine my surprise when, after raving to a friend and dragging him here for Sunday brunch, we had an absolutely terrible experience. How embarrassing.

We arrived around 11am and it was fairly busy. We were told that our wait would be 30 minutes. That didn't bother me, because I assumed that it would be well worth the wait. To start, the host was incredibly rude (and dressed like a sailor). After he announced that we were next on the list, I had the nerve to ask if we could have a certain table that was being cleared because it seemed like a pretty awesome location. He looked at me as if I were a homeless person trying to gain access to a VIP room and responded with a long, drawn-out, condescending "No." I looked at him expecting to be told a reason, but after 5 seconds of silence, I had to ask, "Why not?"

"Indoor seating is for reservations only."

Are you KIDDING me? Because we didn't make a reservation, we have to sit outside in the heat and humidity? Are we to expect our seats to be out on the curb? In the gutter, perhaps? I had maintained a sunny disposition until this absurd moment, and as my blithe expression turned to hatred, he changed his tone slightly and found us another table inside.

Our server was worse than the host. I mean, the girl seemed to HATE us. She appeared horrified that we wanted some brunch and therefore refused to give us adequate service. For example, my dining companion had hoped that he could order the chocolate chip pancakes sans chocolate chips. We asked nicely with a smile, but her response was exactly the same as the host's: "No." Because flour and milk are so hard to whip together without chocolate chips. I understand that it's busy, but nowhere on the menu does it say "no substitutions". Believe me, I checked thoroughly. 

Mkay. So I ordered the spinach and goat cheese crepes. My companion, defeated, had fruit and a side of bacon. The crepes were nothing to write home about, and fruit and bacon are pretty difficult to do wrong. Our server didn't bother to ask how anything tasted. I'm really not exaggerating about her: she HATED us. Never made eye contact, never smiled. Acted rushed and annoyed.

You know, we tried really hard to be patient and pleasant during a busy Sunday brunch. How could we possibly deserve to be treated so badly? I felt like we were trying much harder to be nice than any of the staff, and we certainly weren't getting paid to do so. The last time I dined here, I was treated like a member of Margot's family. What happened? Could it have been an "off" day for our host and server? Possibly. Is that an excuse to treat nice, paying customers like absolute dirt? NEVER. 

And I will never return.

I'm a fan! Farmer & the Cow is a small, hole-in-the-wall burger joint on Market in downtown Wilmington. Easily near the top for restaurants on Yelp around this area and well-deserved. I've gone at least twice within the same month. 

Food/Drinks:
The gourmet burgers here are on point, and they have a great selection! For all their burgers, you can choose different proteins for your patty instead of traditional beef, including turkey, fish, and veggie. I highly recommend the Moo Caliente if you're into spicy, though be warned, it is really spicy! I also had the Badger Badger, which is an interesting mix of mushroom and goat cheese. As for appetizers, definitely consider the nachos and the mac & cheese; they were delicious and definitely filling (don't get both for a small party). The truffle tots also have a good essence of truffle and it's not too overwhelming. Decent drink selection with plenty of craft beer and mixed drinks. They also have a happy hour as well. Oh, I'm not into milkshakes, but they are look delicious and are huge (see pic)!!! 

Location/Environment:
Rather small place, and tends to get packed. Waits can definitely be avoided if you make a reservation, which I would recommend. Bar is also small, so there might not be much standing space. Being on Market, parking might be a bit difficult to find (unless you end up parking at a nearby lot). The inside is styled as a modern, casual, trendy tavern. Service is decent.

Rating: 9.5/10
Pros: Burgers are amazing. Moo Caliente. Creative names. Hippy environment.
Cons: Busy (though can be avoided by making reservations)
Best fried chicken in town! So delicious and crispy while the chicken is still moist. I love the fried pickles and whiskey selection. Becoming one of my favorite places in town. See you guys soon.

I had eaten here seven years prior and remembered it clear as day. For those of you that don't know (5% tops), this would be a vivid memory. Just trying to help out the 5%. 

Whether you're a 95%er or 5%er, you might find it interesting (100% know that word) that it was the same waiter as seven years prior. Good waiter, too. 

The food, atmosphere, pricing, and service are all very good! 

The End.

We waited 32 minutes for our food, ten of which we watched two of our meals sit under heat lamps. 

I have no interest in eating a meal when it has been 32 minutes, my food has been out for 10 minutes, and the bathrooms are nasty (no details provided because I'm a kind individual). 

The Daisy Mae mixed drink was tasty at ($9), and no problems with the sprite or water, but not recommended based on this experience. 

Clearwater Beach isn't recommended in general if you don't like touristy areas. It's similar to Myrtle Beach and Gatlinburg in that sense. Only went to see dolphins, which was successful.

The atmosphere, service, and food were all excellent. I requested some changes to the Filet Mignon Salad when ordering and they accommodated to perfection. It was one of the best meals I've ever had (Top 15). Even the presentation was on the money. 

You have to request bread and butter if you want it. The bread is pretty good. It's not like an Italian restaurant or anything, but solid. 

They are serious about service here. Several people asked about the meal and the experience. There were five people in the party. Four of five loved their meal (Pork Chops, Salmon Salad, Steak Kabob, Filet Mignon Salad). The fifth ordered Prime Rib. I tasted it and it was a little soft, but I'm not a Prime Rib expert. 

Other important notes: French fries are excellent, green beans are not. Go unhealthy with the sides.

The line was out the door, which is definitely a good sign. And the service was excellent. On the other hand, maybe those positives were just to butter me up.

Anyway ... the bagels were average, imo. I didn't taste anything that made me say to myself out loud: "These bagels are the jam!" Nope, that didn't happen. But I did floss many poppy seeds out of my teeth while driving back to hotel.

Update: 

Imo, this is the nicest poker room in Florida. I have played at 28 of 32 of the poker rooms on Florida and even wrote a book about it (my worst book), including all the ones that would potentially considered the nicest. 

I'm not alone on this opinion. Most people think this is the nicest poker room in Florida. I could describe it to you, but a picture is supposedly worth a thousand words and I posted nine pictures. You can do the math on that one. 

The cash games can be tough or gambly/soft. Just make sure you go up against the right people and at the right times. Patience is key. 

There are great deepstack poker tournaments every Saturday and Sunday. The buy-ins are moderate and they're a lot of fun because they move fast. They play like deepstack turbos. The only negative is that the payouts are top heavy. 

Overall, definitely recommended. 








This review is for the poker room. 

I kept telling myself: "Remember to take a picture." But when I'm playing poker, I'm not really in Yelp mode. So, my bad. I'll have to do my best with words. I did take a picture of a sandwich from the poker room deli, but that wouldn't help you much. 

This is a huge and beautiful poker room with great dealers and service. The waitresses are on-point and the massage girls come around regularly. I sometimes get a massage while playing poker but did not so on this trip. Therefore, I can't give you an evaluation. I do know it's $2/minute without a 15-minute special. This is high. 

As far as the poker goes, I played like a Donkey Doodle Dandy. Florida players view money differently, which makes it a different game, but I didn't adjust, so it's my fault. Needless to say, I lost. 

Losing is okay (in a while), but playing poorly sucks. I'm currently battling for the Top 50 players in the World Series of Poker, but I can't beat a low-stakes cash game at the Hard Rock. Then again, you only learn when you lose. If you apply what you learned, the wins get bigger. 

When I talk about poker, I go on a tangent. Sorry. 

Overall, I would recommend playing here, but only if you're capable of playing very tight (very patient). They're mostly a different breed of poker player. They probably won't pick up on the fact that you have only played 10% of your hands and call anyway. This is good news for you. 

Basically, the most patient player will win over the long haul in this game.

I don't get it. This place has high reviews so it's probably just me. The first sign of trouble when I walked in was no other customers. On the other hand, the waitress super polite and efficient. And the restaurant was clean. As far as the food goes, the meatballs were blah and the pizza was blah +1.5. I wish I could rate higher, but I just wasn't feeling it.

Excellent service, great music, plenty of space. The prices are high since it's inside a casino, but that's not the big problem. 

The big problem is that the pickles are just okay. As far as the burger goes, it's good, not great. Will fill you up, but that's all. 

This is the End.

I needed a good meal after a long drive and poker tourney. This is where things led me--with a wine. Yes ... a wine. 

I ordered a wine at poker room but busted tourney. The waitress in the poker room was walking by in the poker room with my wine so I took it, went to car, poured the wine into a water bottle, and put the water bottle in a bag of popcorn bags. You know when the big white bag with eight bags of popcorn in it? That! I wasn't drunk or drinking the wine, but I didn't want to waste it.

When I got to this restaurant, 10-12 cops walked in and I thought to myself: Do they know about the water bottle of wine in the popcorn bag on my passenger seat? 

I let it go and ordered a burger and fries. Good service, spotless restaurant, decent burger and fries (not amazing), and a clean getaway. 

Only recommended if you have no better options in the area.

What a weird night we had at Golf & Social.  There was a group of 12 of us with several visitors from out of town for a two hour reservation.  The team at G&S was very accommodating over the phone in helping us set up a reservation, and informed us that with a group of our size we would need two golf simulators so that everyone could play.  Because there was a mix of experienced golfers and beginners we specifically asked when making the appointment to set up a "best-ball scramble" between the two simulators, where everyone could tee off and then the entire team would play from the best hit ball, giving everyone a chance to take some shots and contribute to the team.  We were assured this would be no problem.  

When we arrived we were introduced to a concierge of sorts who, while very sweet, clearly wasn't well versed in how to use the simulator or set up what we had asked for.  We spent the next 45 minutes watching as our concierge tried to figure out getting the simulators working and doing troubleshooting.  One of the simulators wouldn't turn on and the concierge was hitting balls himself most of the time trying to get everything functioning.  After an hour of standing around with drinks and some mediocre nachos with no golf we informed the concierge that the group was getting antsy and we'd like to leave.  Because the simulator wasn't working we wouldn't pay the golf fee but we'd pay for our food and drinks and tips.
  
The concierge said that he could get one of the simulators running and that the problem was the game we had chosen.  He asked us to please stick around and he'd set up a standard round on the one working simulator.  We said ok, and he did so, but after 20 minutes or so of half the group playing and the other half standing around watching, our hearts weren't in it.  We told our concierge again that we'd like to leave and that we'd be happy to pay for food and drinks but not the golf, he said he'd get the manager and proceeded to disappear for another half hour.  We contemplated just leaving some cash and walking out, but wanted to be polite.  We honestly thought the manager would come out and comp us drinks or something for wasting most of our night.  Finally the manager came out to speak with us, but instead of even talking to us he threw a bill on the table and said "you used the simulator, you pay for the simulator, end of story".  We were taken aback by his approach to customer service there, especially with such a new (and otherwise totally empty) bar, but we all remained pretty even keeled and politely explained to him that they had agreed to provide us a certain service that they never even came close to delivering.  Over the course of the next few minutes the manager proceeded to get very upset and tell us that he didn't care if we were happy with the service, or if we decided to come back or not,  He also asked my friend if he wanted to step outside the back door and fight him(!).  I really thought for a moment that he might get punched by this manager for complaining about the service. 
 Annnyway, we left money for our food and drink and a tip for the service staff and walked out.

As a Chicago native, I miss good pizza in NOLA. Shockingly, I don't love deep dish and I don't love super thin/flatbread type pizzas either. I was so happy with my experience at Theo's! It's just the type of pizza I like. The crust is thick and fluffy and the dough is sturdy enough that the slice isn't floppy. It's not very greasy, either.

You order at the counter and the food is brought to you. There are so many flavor combos to choose from, in addition to the option to make your own! They also have sandwiches, salads, and some good-looking appetizers (my friend loved the wings). I chose to split a 14" West Bank special (tomato sauce, crumbled bacon, chicken, roasted red peppers, jalapeños, pineapple & mozzarella) with a friend. This particular flavor combination was amazing and they sure did not skimp on toppings! We each got 4 generous slices. 

My party of 6 enjoyed the variety of pizzas we got. The only complaint was that the food took a bit of time to come out, even though the restaurant wasn't very busy on that particular weeknight. It was probably due to the size of our party. Regardless, the food was great, the staff was friendly and I liked that the restaurant large enough to accommodate parties of all sizes, including my larger one. What a nice, family-friendly joint in Mid-City.

While I wouldn't go as far to say this is a dive bar, I'd go as far to say this is the most economically sound bar in the Indy Metro area. 

$2 wells. 24 hours a day. I can't. I almost cried from happiness. 

The menu is huge, and everything was delicious. I have some artichoke pasta that warmed my soul on a blustery winter morn, er, afternoon. It was definitely afternoon.

The service was great, and I was in good company.

Figured I would give the authentic stuff a try, I've had enough Americanized Sweet & Sour Chicken in my life for an army.

So I gave the Hainanese chicken a try.  Was told it was served cold...okie doke that's new to me!  The rice it came with was hot so there was that contrast going on.  I have to confess that this dish wasn't my favorite and didn't exactly blow me away, I enjoyed the rice most of all, it was very ginger-y.  The chicken I could care less if I ever tried again to be honest but that doesn't mean it was bad, it's just not to my taste.

I was brought some fish soup to try and that was decent enough, I'm just not a big fan of "egg drop consistency".

I can't stress enough how NICE the owners are.  We were given those soup noodle things at the end of the meal gratis as a parting gift, but these ones were sugared so it was like dessert!

I would gladly come back just for the hospitality aspect of things, and maybe next time I would try a hot meal which I prefer, but trying new things is always so much fun!

Let's get them off to a good start. Walked in 3 minutes after official opening and took a seat at the bar. They've done good with the old Mile 277 space, obviously the stage is gone and separation walls have gone up in places. You can tell there was quite an investment into the renovation, all looks clean and new. It's a nice space but doesn't have that classic steakhouse feel as the decor is modern. Wall signs and decor are bordering on garage sale finds/TGI Fridays but not overdone.  Plenty of beers on tap & bottle, wine & cocktail list looks ok too.

No bar menu which is kind of disappointing but maybe they could implement that. I don't think I want a full meal experience if I'm just watching the game (one TV) so maybe some lite bites and happy hour specials would be good.

Three bartenders on opening day for full coverage, all are pleasant!

Best of luck folks!
The food here is just ok but the service here is awful. It's like our waitress was completely unhappy that we were even there. I can get better service anywhere else so I definitely will not be back.

Great little Gelato and ice cream shop!!
They have a lavender and lemon flavored ice cream  and so many flavors to choose from that are to die for, very smooth and creamy. I love this little shopping area the shop is located in , it's very quaint! It can get very busy during nice weather, who doesn't love great ice cream!!
They did a beautiful job cleaning the roads after all the mud and debris after the rains,
You can't even tell, they really did do a great job....signs are everywhere thanking the police and fire department for the excellent job they did!!

Bleh.  Not really worth going out of your way.  The free "hand pumped" donut is about as bland as pastries get.  The store has some cool, hipster-type products that are locally made and such, but if you just want some coffee or a donut, go someplace else.

I work nearby and was pleasantly surprised to see this shop open up.  Fish options (especially eat-in/take out) are seriously lacking in and around this corridor.  Looks like they were pretty successful in taking over the previous tenants w/o much fuss.  Agree on the tartar sauce, quite memorable, as tartar sauce is typically such a lazy crutch in a fish sandwich.  I've done a couple take out fish sandwich lunches, and both were quite good, especially the catfish sandwich.  Perfect crunch breading, tasty meaty filet and good medley of pickles, onions, greens and tartar.   It is made to order, so this isn't fast food, and you should like that.  

The owners are quite knowledgable about their products, which were quite diverse and impressive.  I've picked up a few great selections, which have been well received at home.  I only hope these guys succeed in that spot, I hope some of their 'up-market' offerings don't scare off the locals.

Wow! This is the best Mediterranean food I've had since living in Tucson. The service was excellent, food came out quickly and with HUGE portions. We got the hummus appetizer and chicken shawarma plate. Everything we had was great. The appetizer came with really cold slices of cucumbers and tomatoes which made it extra refreshing. I loved the chicken plate. The shawarma was a little fattier than what I typically prefer, but next time I would just get the grilled chicken instead. I can't wait to go back. I love finding new places like this. As a random review from my kids: the bathrooms were VERY clean here too. Haha 

As a side note. Our server was so wonderful and kind. I felt badly for her because some older man was giving her the third degree about finding Turkey on a map and really just being rude regarding her knowledge of the country (not a pre requisite to be employed btw). She handled it well. I also enjoyed the owner or manager coming out the next time to deal with the customer himself. He defended his server and really did the right thing in protecting her! Honestly, the way she handled herself and how the management took care of it and really didn't give the guy any slack for his rude behavior was excellent and makes me want to support them even more. Tucson doesn't have time for that nonsense and she didn't deserve any ! 

Bottom line: Fresh and Delicious!

Yay For Casino Happy Hours!

I love the Roxy for being a nice, quiet place to retreat from the main Casino floors, listening to some soothing jazz, whilst sipping delicious cocktails.
https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/roxy-reno?select=cjuTw-NqyUl483HwuONpxA

THE SETUP

If you are cruising through the El Dorado Casino, it is definitely worth going up a level to catch the Happy Hour at the Roxy. 

Roxy is well known for it's libations and entertainment, which includes such accolades which includes being voted both "Best Martini" and "Best Lounge Act" in Reno!  Think about that high praises while sipping on one (or two or three) of its 102 listed martinis, AND a mind-boggling selection of 350 wines.  

COCKTAIL JOY!

Why put up with the swill that they serve you on the floor?  Take a moment to grab something delicious, like the hand-crafted Pomegranate Martini I got to enjoy while passing through.
https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/roxy-reno?select=ZS4PF3_yBXPFVU0nCv9PYg 

THE LOWDOWN

Come for Reno's best happy hour (from 4:30pm - 6:30pm) with $5-$7 Martinis!  Stay for the wonderful live piano and singing talents of many musical artists.

200-Year Old Building on Nashville Historic Registry Undergoes Modern Renovations to Develop Club, Restaurant & Music Venue!

SITREP

I had an awesome opportunity to tour this historic building in Downtown Nashville on the first & oldest block of Broadway.  

SOME HISTORICAL PERSPECTIVE

The Acme Feed & Seed building has (literally) "roots" going back about two centuries, that include some of the original pillars dating back to the time of Andrew Jackson. 

FEED & SEED

Back in the day, this warehouse was a stop for the buying and selling of agricultural and livestock.  Much of the important agricultural commerce of Nashville took place here during the 1800s and early 1900s.

BUILDING DEVELOPMENTS 

Owner Tom Morales and his working crew are in the middle of some major renovations to turn this old historic building into a vibrant part of the Nashville restaurant dining & music scene, and we saw them ripping, drilling, wiring and hammering all around us on this working-tour. 

Tom stated that when completed, this building will feature three different levels of activities - restaurant, bars, clubs & live music venue.  There will also be a penthouse  bar-patio overlooking Downtown Nashville.

THE LOWDOWN

A fantastic tour of an historic period building!

Worthy Stop In Reno, But "Small Plates" Indeed

SITREP

I was visiting great friends this recent particular weekend, and on Saturday evening we decided to stop in at Sierra Street Kitchen & Cocktails ("Sierra") and grab some bites (since we had no idea what to expect for our "Rat Pack Party" later that night @ Thirsty's).

THE SETUP

There is a lot to appreciate about Sierra as well as a few things I wish were different.  It is a "Small Plates" establishment by set-up.  It may not be my choice, but when you are invited by cherished friends, you take things "as is." 

* PARKING

Located right on North Sierra Street, Sierra is easily accessible on the Downtown Reno grid, and there seems to be plenty of nearby garages, as well as ample metered street parking on the adjacent streets about 1-4 blocks in every direction - after 6pm the bonus is no cost for the meters.

* THE SEATING

The seating is just a tad cramped - especially if, like me, you sitting in the chair that everyone has to walk by to the kitchen or the restrooms.  But even the spacing between tables was just a bit too modest as well:
https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sierra-st-kitchen-and-cocktails-reno-2?select=n4BUXDlIpd-hXaqY3MPXvw&userid=3mNz5nQFTIBQm0oU5mBR0w

Also, 2-4 patrons work great, but I would reticent to be bring a group of 6 or more, and would definitely make reservations.  We had reservations for the 3 of us. 

* WINE SELECTION

Props for the very respectable variety of wines of many vintages in their wine cellar, including some Italians (like the bottle of Vermintino).  Most bottles ran from $25 through $135.  But you could grab a single glass on average for $10. 
https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sierra-st-kitchen-and-cocktails-reno-2?select=UC00GyHlUl8kXh5b4jngrw&userid=3mNz5nQFTIBQm0oU5mBR0w

But if on a budget you may want to ask what is their house wine or what bottles may already be opened.

* MENU ITEMS, VARIETY, FOOD PORTIONS & PRICING

Wonderfully broad & diverse - there is most likely something here for everyone, and we already heard the servers share with patrons to explain what their dietary restriction is and the kitchen can work with it.  [But although interesting selections, I found most of items to be overpriced and unsubstantial.] 

My selections included....
== The crab cakes ($12) - indeed tasty, but small plate with two very small crab cakes (I did NOT share with my companions) :)
https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sierra-st-kitchen-and-cocktails-reno-2?select=y1jzs8GWPsmf6GzbDWJ9Xg&userid=3mNz5nQFTIBQm0oU5mBR0w

== I'd also squarely put Mac N' Cheese option ($8) under "tasty, yet very small."  Comes out in it's own cute porcelain dish, but there really wasn't much substance to it, and not enough to share.  And to be fair again, perhaps I'm used to Mac N' Cheese favorites where a side like this would be under $4.  [I think I will stick to these other places if I really want that Mac N' Cheese "fix" to be satisfied.]

And without sounding redundant, I'll also say that the Tomato Caprese ($8) and the Thai Chicken Wraps ($9) were tasty, yet pricey for what was received.

I get it.  "Small Plates".  But not my preference.

SERVICE

For the number of servers present (all clustered by the kitchen even when there was no food present to deliver), there longer waits on service items and details:  water replenishment, replacing dropped utensils, ordering, items coming out at crazy intervals and not at near together to enjoy together, waiting the check ...... still waiting for the check.  Now waiting for the credit card statement to come back.

What seemed to be missing here was a coordination aspect where another server - who may not happen to be busy at that moment - could step in and assist, to deliver an item, to replenish a glass, to retrieve a check, etc., when the other primary server is busy doing something else. 

OTHER METRICS

But of course, as in all things, there are other factors at work, and going out is not all about "Food" and "Drink" - sometimes its just about finding a beautiful little spot to have a quiet, possibly intimate, conversation with someone you enjoy spending time with, and on this front.

And so I will give a higher mark to Sierra for being a great sanctuary for imbibing in conversations, which is why this not a 3-Star review if left to just the "product" and "service" aspects of this business  

THE LOWDOWN

If you are in the area, Sierra is definitely a nice option to stop in at and have a bite, but it is a lighter meal option.  If you like big meals, with big steaks, large portions of other meats & fish, cheesy potatoes, lots of other substantial comfort sides, at reasonable prices, then "NO", this is definitely not your spot.  

But if you love to socialize and have quiet chats, this could be the new spot for you in Reno.  Bon apetit.

My Most Awesome Meal In Nashville!

SITREP

I'm not kidding.  Hands down, bar none, THE BEST dining experience I had in lovely Music City.  It was the perfect culinary cap to a great weekend.

And what a treat it was for my first-time visit to Nashville!  Loved everything I did, everything I ate, everything I drank, and most of all everyone I met!  I have fallen hard for Nashville.  When I come back (and I will!), I look forward to trying a bunch of new things and going to a bunch of new places I didn't have the chance to do the first time around.  But you can make dam sure that I WILL find time to come back to Monell's!

THE SETUP

My god, where do I start?  First, a shout out to my Nashville buddy, Chris G., for taking both the time & the interest to show me a more in depth experience in Nashville than I had the chance to capture before this meal, and that was by bringing me to Monell's.  

He told me to bring an appetite, and so I did!  I skipped breakfast - and I even ate a lighter dinner the night before (which wasn't too hard to do since I was out doing Karaoke all evening long!).  So "appetite present" - check!

PHYSICAL PLANT

The building is beautiful historic Southern charmer, with rich red tones and surrounded by very lovely landscaping. 

*PATIO

The outside patio area, wit all of the bushes, the koi pond & bridge, the lovers' swings, etc., created a gorgeous environment for outside relaxation and sipping on a mint julep.
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/monells-dining-and-catering-nashville?select=WCPKnDaBdLq_2wGJgrk_PA#eEqAc-jo0p7K40pt5jPK3Q

*DINING AREAS

Inside, each of the dining areas with large tables, high ceilings, comfortable seating placements at the table, the refinery & place-settings on the table, were elegant.  I felt like I was in a culinary sanctuary for where fine-dining would occur, and I wasn't not wrong.

*FESTIVE SPIRIT ALIVE!

And the seasonal festiveness had not been missed!  Mother's Day was just the day before my own Monday lunch experience at Monell's, and there was a beautiful tree up in the lobby - but this tree, instead of being covered in Christmas decorations, was festooned in the livery commensurate with Mother's Day, with elegant garments, knick-knacks, and décor paying respect to the traditions of motherhood.  
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/monells-dining-and-catering-nashville?select=WCPKnDaBdLq_2wGJgrk_PA#WaEal71ccFwUPks68SP05w

DINING METRICS

Monell's Dining & Catering is an exquisite culinary find in the Germantown area of Nashville, and one, quite frankly, you should not miss on your first trip to Nashville.

* FAMILY-STYLE / OR IS IT MORE "COMMUNITY-STYLE"?

Many call this family style.  But I take this one-step further and think the more correct moniker of this social tradition is "community-style".  I equate family style with the nuclear family, maybe with some grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins, etc., like you would find around the Thanksgiving or Christmas dining table.

However, THIS kind of "style" you would more likely find at an Amish-barn raising, or the Manhattan community-dining rooms of the 1910s and 1920s.  Because this is MORE than just family, it's neighbors, and complete strangers coming together - as I enjoyed on this dining-experience.  

* A STRANGER MAY JUST BE AN "UNMET" FRIEND

So I won't quibble too much on the definition of "what"-style it is.  But whatever metrics you use to ascertain the most correct definition, the facts are, that besides Chris G., the 10 other people sitting around this dining table at the beginning of this lunchtime meal, were complete strangers to us - but by the end of the meal, we all knew a fair amount about each other, their families, and the reasons why they were in Nashville.

THE MENU

The menu was filled with such Southern stables and prepared with in traditional fashion and you would never find a better bargain for $13.50..

*THE SIDES

Oh my goodness!  I could have just filled on the following:  fresh biscuits, fresh dinner rolls, cut steamed green beans, the corn pudding, the mashed potatoes, asparagus casserole, and cheese grits casserole.

*THE DISHES

But luckily after two servings of the cheesey grits, I still had room for the tomato meat loaf, the skillet-fried chicken, and the chicken & dumplings.

With some down home iced tea and banana crème pie, I was more than satiated with a meal to last me the next two days!

THE LOWDOWN

A must stop for any trip to experience the best of Nashville dining!

ACHTUNG!  *TASTEGASM ALERT!*

SITREP

If there was restaurant-establishment I could hide in my pocket, fly back home with me, and set it up on my street corner, it would be this one.

Jägerhaus is one of those Über-Fantastico Deutschland-traditional establishments that takes food, pastries and dessert making up an knotch.  [Since it closes at 10pm it doesn't quite make it onto my "Munchies For Night Owls" list (to make it on this list, a place must be open at least til Midnight) - and we got there at 9:30pm.  But still, they let us hang out til 10:20pm, so we never felt rushed.

THE SET-UP

My sweet friend and I had just finished a party at Indulge Grill Island and we were working our way back to Hotel Modern, but we decided to take a quick side-trip since we were looking for something to satiate our sweet-tooth.

Now she was from New York City, and how she found this place I don't quite know since this was her first time to New Orleans too, but I am so happy I decided to let her take charge of this night because she was firing on all pistons.

THE TASTE TREATS!

The food here looked amazing.  And I kept telling myself that I would come back earlier in the evening one of the days I was here, but, alas!, that was not to be. A Fantastic Trans-Altantic Tastegasmatic experience here in New Orleans!

Great Location & History, But Customer Service Metrics Are Lacking

SITREP

We came back here for a reunion a couple of Sundays ago, knowing this place from previous stops, and current  recommendations by Reno friends.

My Favorite Brewery Tour & Tasting In Nashville

Rum-A-Rama-Thon!

SITREP

Coming to this historic site made me feel a bit like an old Conquistador on a quest with the famous Spaniard, Ponce de Leon, searching for the "Fountain of Youth" in the New World.  

And in a way, we succeeded, for we found what we searched for:  an original well-spring for RUM @ The Old New Orleans Rum Distillery itself!

THE SETUP

If coming from the French Quarter, I would make sure to drive the distance, or at least take the bus, but it's a long walk other.  The Rum Distillery is in a hood surrounded by some dilapidated buildings that really took a pounding from Hurricane Katrina, and it shows.  

During the Rum Distillery tour, our guide pointed out on a few different occasions at different locations throughout the building where the watermarks were for where the flooding had completely immersed everything beyond eight (8) feet above ground-level here, which is pretty high ground as it were here in NOLA period.

THE RUM VARIETALS

I sampled all their rums, all delicious with their own character.  I went from the silver to the Cajun Spiced, to the super smooth aged blue label, all before the tour even started:

*  Their Silver Blend - knows as "Crystal" - she is the youngest & cleanest with no Oak Barrel aging - and interestingly enough, my favorite -  and the one I purchased at $17 for the bottle.

*  The 3 Year, which is a delicious blend and very very smooth, with a deeper taste.

*  The 10 Year, which had a delicious oaky and smokey taste to it and probably still worth it at $55, but a bit beyond what I was willing to spend for a bottle of rum - and to be honest, at this price I'd rather spend it on a bottle of Cognac Brandy.

THE TOUR ON RUM MAKING

The 70-80 minute tour was a lot of fun and it allowed me to get answers about the art of rum-making:

(1)  From it's fermentation process with the hops, 
(2)  The cleaning process and getting rid of acetone,
(3)  The very colorful bottles that package the rum for sale; and, 
(4)  The interesting history of this particular distillery's successes AND failures since they were all out for us to see.

It was interesting to note one prototype bottle that was sitting out there for all to see labeled "Jalapeno / Anaheim" - one could only wonder what kind of Frankenstein'esque concoction this was intended as!  All in all, it was a grand time and I got quite a few pictures to show along with the very interesting dialogue about this exciting history of rummery.  

THE LOWDOWN

This distillery is a fun stop for any trip to NOLA and it provides a delightful rum tour showing the process from beginning to end.

It's unfortunate that I'm having to give my review 1 star because of a customer service issue, because I actually like Kilroy's. 

Last night I came in with 3 of my friends. Two wanted Hennessy, or any type of cognac, which they did not have. The waitress made a drink recommendation of Crown Apple and cranberry as an alternative, so they ordered that. When their drinks came, it was not what they wanted. No big deal, it happens. They asked the waitress if they could swap it out for something else. She said she would go get a manager but that she's letting us know, they're not going to do an exchange. We thought it was strange that she would have such a negative outcome already in her mind, but then we learned why.

After waiting 30 minutes for the manager, Jordan White, to come over (when we were already done with our food), we had to ask a couple of the staff to remind her to make her way over. When she finally came and my friends explained the situation, she told us that we chose those drinks for ourselves and that they don't do exchanges because they didn't do anything wrong. Well - we didn't say you did anything wrong. We would just like to pay for a drink that we like. Happy customers buy more drinks and reimburse you right back. It's simple. 

After some going back and forth, she says, "Your server already told you what I was going to say. I've never ordered something that I didn't want." I couldn't believe that someone in the restaurant business, let alone a manager would say something like that to their guests. The conversation ended with her saying "this conversation is over and it's staying on your bill." And just walked away. 

Just to clarify - this has nothing to do with us being out $6 for the drinks. The way that the situation was handled was unprofessional.

I am not totally opposed to the "fancy Mexican" concept. I have a place in my hometown that would fall in that category. But it is not quite to this level of offering kobe beef and lobster in their dishes. That does sound like a bit of a stretch. But hey, I'm willing to try anything. Especially that involves high grade beef and lobster.

We were seated in a private room. Which was definitely nice with our large group. Our group of 13 definitely maxed out the occupancy of this space. We started with some margaritas and queso. A whole lot more queso was ordered later. But the kurts queso with ground beef was definitely the best. The margaritas and the queso were probably the best part of the experience. The service for our large group was a little slow and definitely not easy to flag down anyone from our private space.

My friend and I couldn't decide between the kobe beef fajitas or the lobster fajitas. So we went halfsies on both. It definitely took a lot longer on our food than a normal Mexican restaurant experience. But with good company around, no one seemed to mind. The steak was nothing spectacular and was like the $9 fajitas I could get just about anywhere. The lobster was really tasty. But barely had any lobster amongst the pile of peppers and onions. With two of us splitting it, we just had enough for each of us to have one tortilla.

I didn't see the final bill. But I'm sure it was pretty high. If I had been paying for this, I probably would have a lower star rating than this. But strictly judging the dining experience without the sting of the bill, this was just A-ok.

After a long trip from Birmingham, a welcomed dinner at Andy Bistro was in order. We did want to let our kiddos get a little energy out before sitting for a couple of hours. And Andy's parking lot was empty and large enough to do so since we were on the early side. Andy's Yelp Page says they aren't good for kids. But they are good for kids that aren't too crazy at a restaurant. They have a kids menu and high chairs. But the environment does not feel like a place for kids that like to run around.

We decided to go early enough that we can take advantage of their Prime Time Menu. I am not normally a dessert person and would shy away these type of three course meals. But the price, what I wanted and the addition of a salad made me really want to go down this path. The bread that came out was absolutely incredible. And that is before I even got the Prime Time meal that I ordered. Our kids also really liked it. Even though I personally know how hard it is as a server with two year olds, they were attentive and patient with us throughout the whole meal. Which again is why I would change their "good for kids" status on Yelp.

The salad was fantastic and the paneed Veal was absolutely incredible. The sauce with that and the pasta made an incredible dining experience. By the time the dessert came, I was pretty full. But despite my preference to not go the sweets direction, I couldn't resist the bread pudding. It wasn't big, which I was thankful for. But it was absolutely delicious. The entire experience was 5 stars from the service to the food. Great visit to Andy's Bistro.

We were looking for a convenient spot to grab something to eat before we headed out of town. The Stillery was one of the few places open for lunch on a holiday Monday morning. So we put our luggage in the car and walked down to it. There was no wait if we were willing to sit at the bar. So that is what we did.

We got a bloody mary to start. It was pretty good. Definitely not the best I've had. But definitely not the worst. It hit the spot for sure. I ordered the hot chicken with fries. I didn't want to get too bold with the heat, so I asked about it. Our waitress/bartender said it wasn't blow your head off spicy. But just a little kick for flavor. She was spot on. With the ranch, it was a perfect blend. My wife and I decided to split our sides and food in general. So she got the mac and cheese. It was really good.

Overall, it wasn't a blow my socks off meal. But it was solid. I would 100% recommend going here for convenience. Which is what we did. A solid 4 stars.

Although it has been close to 20 years since my last visit, I have been to College Inn numerous times in the past. But since that delay was so vast, so many things have changed. Although the location is (roughly) the same, the building is totally different. My childhood memories recollect a much smaller, darker, family environment. My most recent experience shows a much more modern, open, and quirky place. Both experiences deserve 5 stars.

I remember as a kid I would always get their spaghetti and meatballs. Not really sure why. But I always remember being excited about our trips to College Inn. Back then, I probably couldn't have fathomed crawfish mac n' cheese or even known what truffles were. Now I can't imagine going here and NOT getting that. The truffle wasn't overpowering, it was loaded with crawfish, and full of flavor. The noodles were not your regular elbow but was a Cellentani noodle. How do I know the name of it? I Googled long curly pasta to find out exactly what it was called. 

When we arrived (late) to join our fairly large group, they already ordered a few appetizers for us to have when we got there. The onion rings were absolutely outstanding. And the fried green tomatoes were near perfection with a delicious sauce and tons of shrimp. There was not a thing that I had in this meal that was less than stellar.

Since my wife and I split such a hefty appetizer and there were others already on the table, we decided to split a shrimp po-boy. The shrimp was fresh and plentiful, and the bread was soft and delicious. All the recipes needed for a great po-boy. The service was great and the beer was cold. If all that doesn't prove to be 5 stars, I'm not really sure what would.

Look at Metry stepping up its game!  Once again, I was lucky enough to be invited to Cafe b with a group from work.  I had heard a lot of raving about Cafe b and I was not at all disappointed. The lunch menu is not extensive, but I think that anymore than what they have would be overwhelming.  There is a very nice drink menu that is designed to accompany lunch, with choices between $4 and $5, including a "skinny" option that is perfect for the "ladies who lunch" clientele.
