I had the Wedge Salad that was as good as any I've ever had with big chunks of bleu cheese, thick and lean bacon crumbles, and a subtle dressing that was just right.  For my main dish, I had the Seared Steak Salad that was phenomenal.  The rare and tender steak was topped with caramelized onions, jack cheese, and  the most perfect sauteed wild onions imaginable.  The bread held up very nicely and I was over the moon happy about the whole thing.

A number of people in our party ordered the Shrimp & Lobster Ravioli, and they said it was good, but I wasn't particularly impressed with its anemic appearance.  One person got the Cafe b Burger that looked and which he said was) fantastic, with a killer presentation of fries served in a cup. The Chicken Pot Pie also looked amazing.

Bottom line: go here and go here often.  Let's revel, fellow Metry-ites, in our own chic brand of culinary coolness! Go us!!!

Ever since I went on my first cruise, I found the experience so delightful, so fulfilling, so, well, for lack of better descriptors, so experientially orgasmic, that I occasionally have a very vivid dream that I'm on a cruise.  I mean I live through the whole seven day experience. I dream up new friends, crazy foreign waiters, foreign outings, drunken karaoke, injuries, the whole bit.  Like after having dreams of lost loves or finally bagging Ryan Gosling, I tend to wake up sad as I face the cold reality of my workaday, hamster wheel life.  

Ever since I ate at Bayona, I have had new dreams... dreams of tangy, perfectly cooked sweetbreads, kinky rabbit three ways,  exploding fonts of delicious spicy Spanish wines, perfect service, and basically the best of everything epicurean... you get the picture. 

Just like I was "happy with my life" before I went on my first cruise, I thought I had tasted some of New Orleans' best cuisine before I ate at Bayona.  Not so!  If you have not been, get thee to Bayona.  You will not regret it.  In fact, you'll never be the same...

Martin Wine Cellar makes me feel fancy.  And thirsty.  

I must have tremendous resolve, though, because I have only ever had salads at Martin, but Sweet Baby Jesus they know what they're doing at that place.  My favorite is the Sena Salad, which is pulled (not chopped) warm oven roasted chicken, raisins, and field greens, bleu cheese, and pecans tossed in the most amazing Tabasco pepper jelly vinaigrette.  There is something about this salad that will make you dream about it all day and all night, too.  It's insane.  

The Martin Special is awesome too, but you have to be hungry to eat it.  It is a heavy, cobb-type salad with green leaf lettuce, bacon, avocado, tomatoes, boiled eggs, radish, and crumbled blue cheese.  It is over the top rich and so super yum.  The spinach and chicken salad is also wonderful - It is what you would expect: spinach, (cubed) grilled chicken breast, eggs, cucumbers, and tomatoes. But, what makes this salad special is the warm, freshly-grilled onions and peppers. KAZAM!

The last time I went (and the only time I have dined in), I was SO impressed by the appearance of all the food I saw on display and on other diners' tables.  I wanted to go into hoover mode in a big way, but I resolved instead to go back as often as possible and eventually try it all....YAY resolve!

Wine? Yes, please.

Delicious wine that is housed in a super fancy, high tech yet old world Willy Wonka-esque fantasy endless vending machine? Yes yes yes.

I love me some wino.  Here is the deal: you belly up to the little service counter that is located in the center of the store and you load up a pretty little pink credit card with some loot (don't worry about having too much or too little - you can never have too much and you can always add more loot to it.  Trust me on this one.).  Then, you spin around in a wonderful boozy haze and take 1, 2, or 3 oz shots of a gazillion different varieties of whites, reds, sweet wines, dry wines, dessert wines, b'fast wines, all the wines you can imagine from all over the world.  Some wines are a little spensy, but they have many wines that are very low price, so you can have the best of both worlds!  It's like a drunk Goldilocks story except there is no family of bears coming to get you when you wake up!  Oh, wait, actually that may sort of happen, depending on how many of the less spensy wines you have...sometimes they get you in the morning...

12 STEPS TO MASTERING YOUR OLD NEW ORLEANS RUM DISTILLERY EXPERIENCE:

1. Admit that you are powerless over the delicious nectar and/or its secret location, so google map it, use a navigation device, or ask a veteran how to get there.  Get there at least 25 minutes before your tour is to start, so as to partake in as many delicious samplings of the daily offering as possible before the tour.  

2. Breathe deeply of the magical sweet, alcoholic scent and come to realize (after the first or second sample) that a power greater than ourselves must have inspired this rum's creation. Maybe slow down to fully appreciate the awesomeness of your surroundings and a truly unique New Orleans experience.

3. Make a decision to listen to the tour guide and to be a respectful and conscientious tour guest. Do not scoff at the tourists. They are people who love rum and New Orleans, too. Don't forget to tip off your glass before the tour is to start and remember to ration for 30-45 minutes.

4.Take a searching and fearless tour of the place with your trusty tour guide, most likely an amazing hipster with a rad rat tail, who is an apprentice taster.  Marvel at his expertise and the complicated process that has brought you the delicious bevvy that you were smart enough to top off before the tour began. Ask questions.

5. Admit to God, your friends, and yourself, that there is no better rum in the world, as attested to by the fact that it has won the world's Best Tasting Rum Award for four years in a row (or something like that).

6. Notice how much of the distillation process is about removing nasty impurities and defects from the final product. Sip slowly and be happy that the distillers love you enough to take out the shit that gives you hangovers.

7. After the tour, humbly and applying all the charm you can muster, ask the bar wench for another drink, but don't let anybody get wind of this secret transaction.

8. Sample each of the distillery's offerings in tiny plastic shot glasses, and make a list of your favorites, to prioritize your purchases.

9. Make amends to the rums that aren't your favorites, and recognize that someone else loves them as much as you love your favorite.

10. Continue to take shot samples, as there will be far too many offered for the crowd to possibly finish.  Waste not, want not.

11. Seek, through prayer and meditation, another chance to come back.  Think of all your friends who will be coming to visit soon, and take comfort in the fact that you will return.

12. Having a warm belly full of the best rum in the world, purchase a bottle to take home or maybe some swag, so that you might carry the message outwards to those who have not yet come to know the glory of Old New Orleans Rum Distillery.

I was happy to call the troubadour my home away from home while visiting NOLA. Check in is normally at 4PM but I arrived at 7AM and the front desk assistant was able to check me in early as well as give me a room on a higher floor (13th to be exact). 

These rooms are smaller than standard hotel rooms but they used the space adequately. The mini bar and fridge was stocked well with alcohol and I had all of the amenities for a great stay. 

My favorite thing was the shower. I'm used to either hotel showers having too little pressure or too much pressure. This shower was just right. 

Everything was clean to my standards and trust me, I have big standards about where I lay my head. 

The rooftop bar, Monkey Board, offered a gorgeous view. I only went during the day, not at night since I was usually too sleepy to make my way up lol. I could hear the music a bit from my bedroom at night but it wasn't overbearing. 

The petit lion bar downstairs is also a great touch to the hotel.

I eat here too much. I know this because the staff behind the counter told me I'm in there a lot. Sweet. 

This is the only Thai place in South County and it happens to be very good! My favorite Thai place in St. Louis by far is King and I, but this place will certainly do. 

The first thing I ever ordered was the Drunken Pad Thai. Excellent, get it! I now only order the regular Pad Thai as I have determined I don't need the dish to be spicy. With the "Drunken" dishes you can choose a spiciness level of 1, 2, 3, or 4, with 4 being the hottest. Even level 1 is a little hotter than I'd like, but acceptable... so if it is your first time here, I recommend starting with level one, or a dish that is not labeled as "Drunken". Drunken just means it is spicy. 

I previous yelper said the Pad See Eiw had "slimy" noodles. I must firmly disagree! I've gotten this dish 4 times now and it is one of my favorites on the menu. It comes with wide noodles like I've never seen before, and the texture of them is great. Delicious sauce.... mmmm.... I want it right now. There is slightly more spinach (I think it's spinach, but vegetables are stupid so I'm no pro on them) than I'd like, but no big, I just scoop much of it off to the side. 

The Drunken Noodles dish is incredibly awesome as well whether you get it with chicken or beef. I've never gotten it with tofu because I'm not a hippy liberal idiot, but I'm sure that would taste bad. Be a real American and put some meat in that dish. I've ordered Drunken Noodles about 6 times over the course of the last year or so and it has never disappointed me.

I've tried all six of their "Drunken Best Dishes" (signature menu items). All of them are good, but they are not my very favorite menu items. Two are worth mentioning though. Twice I've ordered the Duck with noodles. The first time it blew my freaking mind, I thought I found a new favorite. The second time something just seemed off, like there just wasn't enough flavor and not enough duck. I'm planning to order it again to make a final verdict on this menu item. I've also gotten the ginger chicken a couple times. The sauce is very tasty, I just wish there were more of it! Don't use all the rice... it will soak up too much of the sauce making the entirety of the dish less flavorful that is desired. Take it from a pro!

Pad Kra Pao is really good! It's a different kind of beef that looks like it belongs on a taco. Don't make this the first thing you ever order from the restaurant, but do try it at some point.

I've also had the Drunken Chicken. It's okay, but doesn't overly excite me. There are so many great items on this menu that I don't know why I'd order that one again. 

Red Curry Pad Thai is awful. Do not order it! Bad taste and it doesn't even look appetizing. 

Pot stickers are on the appetizer menu. Get them. I'm not suggesting this, I'm ordering you to do so. I'm a veteran of this restaurant so you should listen to me. I don't even like pot stickers but these things are the bees knees. They are crispy, awesome, and the sauce that comes with them is also the bees knees. 

The thai spring rolls suck but I think that I just don't like this type of spring roll. It is a roll full of stupid vegetables wrapped in a clear noodle. How stupid. Moving on.

Stay away from the chinese portion of the menu. Low quality chicken and they generally overcook it rendering many pieces of chicken inedible. I tried the orange chicken and the general tso chicken. So disappointing. The crab rangoon and egg rolls are fine, about what you'd expect from any average chinese restaurant in St. Louis.

I highly recommend this restaurant!

I don't often give a review for a place unless I've loved it or I've had an agonizing experience. 

I have ordered from Pizza Brain in the past and their pizza is rather delicious. However, I will never order from Pizza Brain again due to a horrendous experience I had last Friday. 

I placed an order for a pizza around 4pm with a 45 minute timeframe for delivery, and I don't live too far away from Pizza Brain to begin with. Around 5:30 I give a call inquiring about my pizza, and am told that the delivery guy is out doing his rounds. I call again around 6pm to figure out that they never put my pizza delivery through the system. I am already frustrated at this point, but I really would like a pizza so ask them to put it back through the system. Around 7pm I call again wondering where the hell my pizza is, 3 hours after my original order. It seems they took down my number wrong, so my pizza again is not delivered on time. I never get pissed off but after three hours waiting for a single pizza, i'm fuming, but don't take it out on the employee. He informs me to email his manager about the situation so it can be rectified via complimentary pizza next time I order. Never received an email back. Never ordering from here again.

If Heaven were a restaurant, it'd be the Shaved Duck. I LOVE this place and I'm really tempted to call it my favorite restaurant in all of St. Louis. This place is THE BOMB DOT COM (sorry cheesy statement I know, but I want to get your attention with how much I'm in love with this place).

The Shaved Duck is located near the Tower Grove neighborhood in good ole STL. This area of Tower Grove is undeniably in a redevelopment phase...so I applaud Shaved Duck for helping with that effort by being located here. It's located on a quaint, unassuming corner, surrounded by a bunch of residences. There are no other businesses in this area for at least a couple blocks. The interior of the restaurant has a shabby chic / COZY / slightly country / STL proud atmosphere. I emphasize COZY because this is not a large restaurant. There are very few tables. A bar area is also located in the front of the restaurant, but that also gets crowded easily.

TIP: Because this is such a small restaurant AND such a popular restaurant, you're always going to have to wait for a table (at least for dinner). Just accept it. It's worth it. Bring your favorite friends and grab a couple beers at the bar and just enjoy yourself while you wait in great anticipation of the awesome meal you're about to have.

Let's discuss food now....I visited the Shaved Duck on a Saturday night with two girlfriends. Here's the breakdown of everything I tasted:

SMOTHERED FRIES: We ordered this as an appetizer based off all of the Yelp review recommendations. It was delicious, but not the best "french fry style" appetizer I've ever had. The dish was a pile of slightly crisp french fries smothered with pulled rib meat and their house made cheese sauce. The fry to meat to cheese sauce ratio was perfect. We scraped that dish clean. We also dipped the fries in their "smokey boubon" BBQ sauce...it was mouth-watering.

BEER MENU: They have a great, small selection of draft beers available...mostly local St. Louis brews. I ordered the Urban Chestnut Count Orlok...a dark pumpkin wheat ale. I give it two thumbs up!

THE B.O.S.S. SANDWICH: Two soft brioche buns with smoked tri tip meat, covered with bacon swiss sauce, and topped with a crispy battered onion ring. It was so tasty and I only ate half of it! The tri tip meat was the star of the show though. You could taste the seasonings/flavor/smoke in the meat and it wasn't the least bit dry. I also dipped my sandwich in the "smokey boubon" BBQ sauce.

RIBS: My friend ordered the ribs and generously let me try one of the ribs. I really enjoyed the house rub they used on the ribs and the fact that I could really decipher the taste of it. The ribs also had plenty of meat on them...few things suck more than ordering ribs that are 90% bone.

CARAMELIZED ONIONS MASHED POTATOES: I ordered this as a side with my meal. I love mashed potatoes and adding caramelized onions flavor to them only makes me love them more!

MAC & CHEESE: My friend ordered the Mac & Cheese as her side. They were prepared with the shell-type noodles and it absorbed the cheese sauce perfectly. The dish was also served with crispy bread crumbs on top. 

GOOEY BUTTER / BROWNIE DESSERT: After a huge meal, we thought dessert was out of the question...but when our waiter described this dessert to us, we couldn't say no. The brownie was a chewy brownie...my favorite. It also had a slightly dark chocolate taste...also my favorite. The gooey butter cake portion of the dessert was amazing as well! Because the gooey butter cake is...well gooey...it paired perfectly with the chewy brownie. OHHH and this dessert was served with a cup of milk. It was a dream!

The service at Shaved Duck was awesome too! Despite working in a busy/crowded/packed environment, all of the servers were in great moods and gave each table the proper amount of attention.

Ok review over...it's officially decided, the Shaved Duck is my favorite restaurant in all of St. Louis. I'll definitely be back.

Dear Half & Half,
I'm sorry for the things I said when I was hangry. I used the nowait app & waited much longer than my suggested time. But it's not your fault, I should've followed suit of Snickers commercials & just had one handy in my purse while I waited, and waited, and waited. 

45 minutes after arriving for our nowait "reservation", my husband & I finally got our seats sitting across from each other on the shared long skinny table next to the bar. I had a nice view of the baristas making fancy drinks. Our waitress sensed our urgency for food. Before she could ask what we wanted to drink, we had our order placed & hot coffee poured (blueprint coffee, baby). Not 5 minutes later our food arrived (again, I think our waitress has esp & could sense our hunger). 

We ordered:
-Donuts w/ chocolate sauce. Why don't all donuts come w/ a side of choc dipping sauce?!?

-biscuits & gravy. I loved that the entire plate was covered in gravy. They're not stingy like most places.

-sausage biscuit w/ potatoes. I always order this meal & it doesn't disappoint. Note, dip your potatoes in the gravy meal, cause why the heck not?

I dig this new location, it's clean, light & inviting. Aesthetically pleasing to the eye which is how Sunday brunch should start.

Mony's was on the drive back down from LA to San Diego and I've heard good things about it.  We saw the lines of tables outside the building before we saw the shop itself.  There are only 3 tables inside, and everything else is outdoor seating.  I also see that most people just take their orders to go.  We went around 11:30 am, and there was no line yet.  Towards the end of our visit though, the place was packed and the line was coming out the door.  

I ordered the Al Pastor Taco and the Carne Asada Taco ($1.95).  I liked them both, but between the two, I liked the carne asada one more.  The al pastor taco was super flavorful and really sweet because they also had pineapples in them.  The carne asada taco really accentuates the flavor of the meat itself, which is probably why I like it more.  What's cool here is that they also let you choose between a corn, flour, or hard shell.  

They have a really nice salsa bar in the corner.  One guy recommended mixing one part pistachio salsa, one part avocado salsa, and one part habanero salsa.  Let me tell you, that guy was a genius, so shout out to him for this wonderful creation.  

Service was great.  The guy at the counter was very patient with us since it was our first time, and luckily there wasn't a line.  The food came out decently fast, so we weren't sitting down for long with an empty table.  They also provide complimentary chips for you to snack on while you wait anyway.  It's best to come here when it's non peak times but it's definitely a must if you're in the area.

I dont even know where to begin.

First of all the food is incredible. 
The place and atmosphere is so welcoming and cheerful. the artwork in this place is just joyful and bright.

I had the Raw Vegan Course wich came with a salad, a cold soup, a main dish, 2 freshly squeezed juices and a dessert. ALL VEGAN, ALL RAW!

first I started off with a freshly squeezed watermelon-mint juice 

second came the delicious salad that was sweet and tangy and full of zest!

next I was presented with a fabulous cold cucumber soup that came in a beautiful martini glass.

for my main course, I had the best "sushi" I have ever had! it had a medley of veggies and "crab meat" (young coconut meat). it came with a side of asian slaw made with jicama and carrots. YUM!
they perfectly paired it with carrot-ginger juice.

by this time i was so satisfied and full that i couldn't eat my dessert and instead asked for a to go box!
I peeked in the box and to my surprise, a beautifully presented strawberry arrangement on a pastry which was made of raw nuts seeds dates and strawberries. 

I WILL BE BACK!

No Wheelchair Access!
- they just did a huge renovation, and somehow got by the requirement to install a ramp and wheelchair accessible washrooms?

If you want to try out the place, as long as you're not in a wheelchair you're welcome.

Dear Yelpers,
This place is wicked. It's in this little strip mall right near NAIT and I never would have ever gone there, except that a foodie friend of mine strongly recommended it to me... and it didn't let me down. When you enter it looks like a fast food place due to the large neon menu behind the cash, but it's totally a sit-down place too (liquor-licensed).
I don't know if Tom is the owner but he was working the tables and is an extremely engaging guy. Funny and chatty, super nice too - he even changed the TV channel so that we could watch some NFL action! 
Food is very reasonably-priced (about $7-$10 for mains), and they have a decent vegetarian selection too. It's mostly Thai-inspired but I did see a pho option listed. We started with appetizer-sized tom yum soups - a savoury fragrant broth with some onions, cilantro, and I think fish sauce in it as well. You can also order a full-sized one which I imagine would have the mushrooms and shrimp in it, and they also have a tom yum noodle soup bowl that I would definitely try.
My fiancé ordered the red chicken curry with potatoes, at the 2-pepper spice level (you can have up to 3), and it was perfect. You get a steaming bowl of jasmine rice, and a large bowl of tender dark chicken pieces and potatoes in a red curry coconut broth. So, so good.
I ordered a supersized ($13) shrimp pad thai, at the 1.5-pepper spice level (also perfect). It's served on a long narrow rectangular plate - very pretty but I kept worrying that I was going to get noodles everywhere. You get 5 large shrimp on the bed of noodles, green onions, bean sprouts, peanuts, egg bits, and something so deliciously crunchy - I think it might have been a pickled carrot julienne? Noodles were perfectly resilient, and all the flavours were perfectly balanced, especially with a squirt of lime. I would definitely order it again but I look forward to trying out their other dishes! Thanks to the cook Monica for a delicious meal!
The service was really exceptional. Even when we had to wait a little to pay, Tom kept conversing with us, asking if we minded waiting a minute, and making sure we knew that he hadn't forgotten about us. They do accept credit cards here and there is ample parking in the lot. 
Absolutely will be coming back here again and highly recommend this little gem to others!!

In response to Denise B., I have not "made every effort to discredit" what she does nor did I write a "nasty" review. I felt the food was just average and the portions quite small for the prices being charged for them. This was an honest reaction. I am fully aware of the restaurant's background and what they actually do, but that doesn't mean I'm required to rave about a mediocre meal. In a message she sent me five months ago, Denise chastised me for my negative comments because "restaurant owners really work hard and try hard and bad reviews directly effect their business." As a restaurant owner, Denise needs to understand not everyone is going to be impressed by what she does and learn to accept she's subject to both good and bad reviews. That she would attack someone who did not enjoy her experience at Leafy Greens Cafe more than a year after the review was posted says far more about her than it does me, and I stand my my original comments.

Like some other people commented I stopped here because of the long line at the other one. Actually I didn't taste a difference between the 2 places these were just as good and not tons of people and noise. I would probably stop here again

I can't believe I forgot to review I stop every time I'm in NO it's a southern staple. I could eat one everyday the only bad part is I get the sugar on myself each time. If your in New Orleans it's a must to get one.

My friends and I came here for a Father's day friend brunch. The food and the drinks here are amazing and I will continue to come here because I love the Ciccios group of restaurants.  For brunch my friend and I split a bottle of champagne ($20) and I got the Hot and Crunchy Tuna bowl (yum)! My biggest complaint is the service. We were at brunch for close to 2.5 hours (not by choice). I completely understand that holidays are tough on restaurants but our server verified out checks 2 separate times only to bring out incorrect checks. A manager came to check on us but didn't come back to follow up and the server sent a different waitress to our table after finding out she messed up our checks. Although this was not a good experience I highly recommend Ciccio's because the food and drinks are amazing and the atmosphere is really cool. I'm hoping this was a one off because the server was maybe new to her job and struggling on a holiday.

I went here on the advice of other yelpers who have raved about the food.I thought this place was a hole in the wall based on how the outside looked,but I was pleasantly surprised at the inside.It was small,but cozy and because I went on a Saturday morning,it was nearly empty,but for 2 regulars. The owner greeted me with a smile and gave me a menu with descriptions of all their goodies.I went there with the intent of getting breakfast,but once he said that the entire menu was available,I decided to try the item that made my mouth water the most.That broccoli chicken cheesesteak.ummm....chunks of fresh chicken breast,fresh broccoli,melted cheese,toasted hoagie roll and chili sauce on the side.It was truly delightful.The wait was a tad long but worth it.I will definitely call my order in next time. I can't wait to try some of the other yummy items on this menu.

If it's class, comfort and excellent service you're looking for, then W New Orleans - French Quarter will certainly deliver. 

I scrambled all over Yelp in search of a hotel that would not disappoint. I'm not too picky with my hotels, but when you're traveling with a little diva, one must plan accordingly. Amongst the sea of reviews on N.O. Yelp, a lot of the more aged hotels were said to have thin walls, A/C issues and no-pet policy. I was only left with a few boutique hotels in mind; but no complaints here. Once I came across W's page on ol' Yelp, I was pleased and booked my one-night stay via Hotels.com.

This W differs from the other locations; rooms are a bit smaller in size, though I never felt cramped, and though the interior design, decor and amenities are trendy, the exterior and pool area still keep with N.O.'s historic look. 

For check-in, pull up to the valet but don't take out your bags and bring them into the mini-lobby. Rooms are actually located to the left of the lobby and hotel restaurant, Bacco.

My standard room ($139/night) was in the corner, far from the elevator--just how I like-and equipped with a plush king-size bed, extra pillows, flat screen, iPod station, Bliss bath products, and a large restroom with stand-up shower ... and much more: http://www.starwoodhotels.com/whotels/property/rooms/amenities.html?propertyID=2030 And it was a lot larger than I anticipated. 

Don't forget your workout gear (ahem, eat a lot of beignets?) because they have a workout room, and also your swimsuit. I only checked out the pool located on theground level complete with small grassy areas, cabanas and lounge seats. It was a Sunday night, so not much of a scene, but I'm sure weekends make for better people-watching. 

As mentioned, W New Orleans - French Quarter is pet-friendly. Keep in mind, they require a $100 non-refundable cleaning fee and $25 for additional nights. I didn't know about this when booking my room, and it was too late to turn back once I caught it on their site. The P.A.W. - Pets Are Welcome amenity offers the following: dog walking, custom W Pet Bed, pet treat. Also--according to their site--you receive a welcome packet with a pet toy, W Hotels pet tag, clean-up bags, food/water bowl, pet-in-room door sign, special treat at turndown and, and a letter explaining the pet services, such as pet-walking and grooming. For that $100 fee, I was pleased to read this ... but ... we didn't get *any* of this. Thus, the one star deduction. They also have a 40lb limit for dogs, so keep that in mind. And as other reviews mentioned, there was a small dust issue. Not too big of a deal since I only spotted it below the nightstand on the glass and ice bowl tray (which I didn't end up using).

I'll still book my next stay here. It was a comfortable, accommodating with excellent service and so many amenities that I've yet to check out.

I can spend hours upon hours at this backyard wine bar. In fact, I did. 

Walk in to the front of house wine retail store to pick out your favorite bottle of red, wine, rose, champs or beer - along with any snacks - and pay. Then head on back to grab your wine glasses, buckets o' ice, water (you'll need to hydrate if you're gonna camp out for hours), and snag a table!

:: Live music is offered all day, every day. 
:: There is a menu of food - like a fantastic cheese plate and other light bites.
:: Above the wine retail shack is a second story bar with hard liquor.
:: Tip your musicians!  
:: Enjoy the laid-back backyard atmosphere, cool tunes, great vibe, fun people watching.

On the corner of State Street and Figuoroa is a cute little bistro named State & Fig. Well, it's actually tucked into the shops, but needless to say it's a good find and a great brunch spot. 

Three amigas and I met up for a post-travel meal and bottomless mimosas. They serve brunch seven days a week, according to their website. The $18 bottomless mimosas is a great deal in theory, but they're made with $3 J. Roget Brut Champagne - a slight letdown. I def rec just ordering a nicer glass of sparkling from the menu if you're only going to drink a few glasses. 

The food menu is what made us happy. I had the $12 pesto mushroom omelette (you can get your choice of an egg scramble or omelette) made with crimini mushrooms, baby arugula, fontina cheese, basil pesto, toast, and fruit. I tend to say no to bread (well, lately) but so glad I didn't. Their house made jam paired with whipped butter - yumm, the best way to end my meal.

After walking the streets of New Hope on a surprisingly beautiful day, we grabbed a spot on the patio overlooking the Main Street so we could get a glimpse of the Budweiser Clydesdale horses that were making a special trip and making deliveries to local pubs, restaurants, and bars. 
This review deals only in decor, service and drinks as we only had cocktails. Our server came immediately and offered to get us drinks and although the Logann Inn was packed, he repeatedly came by to check on us and refill my seemingly hole-y bottomed beer. 
Decor is great because you can sit under a canopy or have the open sky views on a pebble covered patio. Either way you are afforded a fantastic view of the street and if you are a people watcher, you won't do much better.

I ordered the salmon Félix and when it was sat in front of me... I thought "wtf, this looks like Mac and cheese" -___- 

Idk about y'all but if you order Salmon with crab lumps and it comes out looking like Mac and cheese, you would be disappointed too.

Anyways, I grab a chuck of the salmon and crab lump with my fork.... already knowing it was going to taste as subpar as it looked.

I'm so happy I was wrong. I could of licked my plate clean if I wasn't struggling to finish my entire plate (the portions are nice). 

The salmon Félix was really, really good and def didn't taste like Mac and cheese. The sauce was kinda buttery, paired with perfectly cooked salmon, sliced bell peppers, lumps of scrumptious crab and paired with rice and garlic broccoli. It was soooooo good, y'all. My boyfriend ordered the ultimate combo and that was delicious too! 

The appetizer was shrimp crab dip which was a hit too.

The food was really, really good and at a great price. Service was great as well.

The place is tucked in a corner of a plaza and def has a family owned, small biz feel to it. However, what it lacks in appearance it def makes up for on taste! 

Highly recommend.

If you're trying to do the right thing for your health this is the place to go. 

The hot bar and the consistent good selection of soups, salads and other foods keeps me coming back for more. 

Customer service is above and beyond here, my little toddler managed to knock my soup on me and they were very helpful in assisting me when he didn't have to. They are constantly cleaning the dining area which is a good thing. 

Many a times the lady in the supplements area has been helpful and I always see her assisting customers sharing her knowledge of the supplements.

There are also a lot of educational seminar events held here, I only wish they could duplicate this place so more people could benefit from its presence! 

I've been coming almost everyday and don't see myself stopping any time soon. If location is a deterrent for you to not come, then make arrangements when you can because it will be worth the commute. 

The crowd of people this place attracts are health conscious people but I've seen a lot of executives, Holk Hogan and his wife, students and a wide variety. I was a Whole Foods regular when I was in NY, and this is my local replacement.

If you're looking for a more eclectic breakfast place South City, Egg may be the place for you.

Upon arrival the only strange thing is the parking situation. EGG shares some parking spots in a lot next to Hodak chicken. Egg only has a few spots and Hodak's has the majority of the lot. There are signs all over the place saying you will be towed if you're there to eat at Eggs. Needless to say you don't want to start your meal off worried about being towed.

Once inside restaurant, the staff is very accommodating. The restaurant is a mix of industrial and antique American items from the 50s and 60s. It is a bustling restaurant serving up some tasty egg entrees.

The menu is somewhat confusing as you don't quite know what you will be getting. Their entrees are different than most restaurants. You can order off the ala carte menu for traditional items such as bacon and eggs.

I had two poached eggs over strips of grilled pork on hash. I did not know quite what I was going to receive, however it was excellent.

My son had two eggs over tortillas and several other items and they were also excellent. My wife ordered off the ala carte menu and her bacon and eggs came out exactly as it were ordered.

Egg is a great place to stop for breakfast. I think you will enjoy your meal, surroundings, and service staff.

Oh and back to the parking, the owner came out and confirmed which spots we could park in, as he saw us driving around reading all the signs. Our car was still there when we came out!

Located in the Streets of St. Charles, Prasino's has great ambiance and atmosphere.

They are very accommodating for groups - I had about 20 people here for a gathering and they do separate checks, etc. without a hassle.

Food is tasty!  I normally get Greek salad and flatbread - my go to food here.  Everything looks very good!

Stopped by for some drinks on the outside patio on Mainstreet. Despite serveral servers, we sat for 15 minutes with no attempt to serve our table of four. I went into use the restroom and see if I could order at the bar. Upon entering, two large dogs were chasing each other and jumping in front of the darkened bar area. I'm a dog lover, but this was just strange. They weren't under control and more like walking into a friend's  house... except your friend would normally control their dogs.

We left, disappointed as the setup here could be great with service and some basic hospitality training. 

Two stars for initial appeal of patio, 0 for the rest of the experience. Will try again sometime in case this just anomaly.

A quaint, packed, corner sandwich shop in the Hill section of St. Louis with jam packed tables and bright, homestyle feel inside. This place always seems crowded at lunch, but you can normally find a spot to sit. 

The salad is a bit too sweet tasting for me, but the generous portion sandwiches on fresh bread will have you coming back. Lots of Italian specialties and St. Louis style thin crust pizza.

The restroom could use some updating as it looks like 1950s home basement  facility.

Overall,  a great place for a quick lunch on the Hill.

Pat O'Brien's is quintessential Cajun NOLA experience! A must go to have a potent ice cold hurricane that packs a category 5 punch as the alcohol isn't immediately apparent, then hits hard like Katrina! The music and mood set's the stage for a memorable trip to the Big Easy!

We stopped in this side street venue hearing the live music and it is a great find. Reasonable prices for Nashville, cold beer and fried chicken and other favorites.

Walk the Line to Johnny Cash's!

I love the vibe of bar restraunts in the City, but Tin Roof did not cut the mustard with us.

That staff was slow, rude and not hospitable in our visit. Hopefully this was a fluke.

Voodoo shrimp smelled weird and somewhat rubbery. Overcooked frozen shrimp in curled cream sauce.

Dixie biscuits were made with tough brisket...uhg!  Disappointing as it sounded like a southern treat.

Lots of great places in the area, too bad as we hoped for a better experience on a big sports night in the Lou.

One of our favorite outside places on Mainstreet St. Charles!

We enjoy listening to Rod and Carl who play here frequently. This is also a great place to people watch on Mainstreet.

Picasso's is the quintessential coffee shop at a perfect location on historic Mainstreet  St. Charles. 

If you want a java and read the paper, do some homework  or listen to some great  music at night and people watch out the windows, Picasso's  is the place!

Chuck a Burger drive-in is a classic 1950s type hamburger and malt shop known for car shows and other fun times. We stopped by here for lunch this week and enjoyed tasty hamburgers and delicious and delicious onion rings! This is the last chuck a burger left so don't wait long and come to this retro classic! The dining room is still closed due to COVID-19, just park on the parking lot and an attendant I'll stop by your window take your order and deliver your cravings right in your car.

Fresh field greens with candied walnuts, red grapes, Gorgonzola and a citrus vinegarette is our favorite salad to kick start a phenomenal meal at Dewey's pizza.

The Streets of St. Charles is packed because of restaurants like Dewey's.

What can be better than stringy mozzarella cheese, mushrooms, onions, green peppers, fresh tomatoes all baked to perfection on a hand tossed crust?

Dewey's is a bomb! A great place for a cold draft, great pizza and good times.

Great little kosher delicatessen and restaurant on Olive Street road for many years.

We stopped in for a sandwich on a cold day.  I had the pastrami on rye with a bowl of chilli.  The chili was very flavorful and a spot hitter! Served up eight half a pastrami sandwich was just right.

They brought a plate of pickles while we waited a short time for our meal. Crisp and garlicky!

Amighetti's is a comfort food sandwich created on The Hill, a historic Italian restaurant in South St. Louis.  Created on a fresh Italian bread, it consists of roast beef, ham, salami, pepper-chinos, special sause and lettuce. It's the whole package that makes this a one of a kind sandwich.

For whatever reason, the original Amighetti's location closed on the Hill after generations.  Now it's returned on Manchester Road.  Apparently it is soon to return to it's roots in South City.

When you drive for 45 minutes to get to a new restaurant, you are normally expecting something special. I was hoping to like the Hofbrauhaus in Belleville, Illinois but our experience said it's not quite there yet.

Hofbrauhaus is a chain of large microbrewery / beer hall type establishments which can draw quite the crowd. They invest a fair amount in a beer haus style building with microbrewery, so it's a multi-million investment.  Upon arrival we were quickly seated using the Yelp reservation system. We avoided a 45-60 minute wait  Thanks Yelp! 

The waitress took us to a table near the bandstand and our original impression was this was a nice place to sit. Then cold air started blowing from the vents above, and literally blew the menus off the table. We asked the waitress about the unusual velocity of the air conditioning and she said there was nothing she could do. We then requested a manager and he had several reasons why none of the other 20+ open tables were available. After a long conversation he agreed to turn off the AC system. Then the table was fine, but we had to explain several times why being blasted by cold air was not acceptable. I'm not going to enjoy anything if I'm uncomfortable, here on a cool rainy day, everyone surrounding our table had outside coats still on, and were miserable. A teenager at the next table had earmuffs on! Turning the AC off solved the issue, but having to get the manager, hostess, waitress involved seemed extreme and took 15 minutes to resolve. We had agreed amoung ourselves to leave (after driving 45 minutes) unless we got moved, or changed the vent situation.


We sampled several items on the menu and found the food to be okay but prices high for what you get. We did order a schnitzel meal (that as quite tasty!) which on the menu showed as $14. When our bill came it was $18. When we inquired about this to the waitress she once again got the manager. Manager said we had the lunch menus, which is what the waitress gave us at 3pm. They did change the bill back to $14. The schnitzel was exactly what we hoped fot, it was great.

The Hofbrauhaus does a strange activity of "paddling" guests who do alcohol shots and then agree to be paddled. This just seems weird in today's world.  After a few beers and sampling a couple of menu items it was time to leave.

Overall Hofbrauhaus did not live up to the hype that we were expecting. We did not find the Hofbrau house staff very accommodating, nor some of the food to be anything that special. It's a great concept, but for us it was a let down. That's not what we hoped for so hopefully they improve.

The Hofbrauhaus appears to be the type of facility to attend once, then wait years until you forget why you didn't like it... before returning again.  We won't be back until we forget this experience.

Great little restaurant on historic South Mainstreet in St. Charles.

They have an attractive side patio for social distancing.

If you're looking for a fun meal while enjoying an afternoon or evening in St. Charles, this place is perfect.

Note to everyone NOT from St. Louis.... please read......

Yes, I'm a lover of all types of pizza depending on how hungry I am, where I'm at, and what else is being served.

For the East coast crowd, yes, the big round New York style pizza is tasty. In St. Louis my favorites for this style is East Coast Pizza in the Valley or Racannelli's. A long  triangular  cut, folded in the middle and served with a Tastykake...our old neighbor's were from New Jersey  and explained this ritual to us. 

For Chicago style....it has to be winter as it's a heavy deal...but Nancy's pizza on Highway K is the best in STL.  St. Louis and Chicago  are long term rivals,  but we admit Chicago has a few good things. 

Now ...my favorite pizza will confuse anyone not from the Lou. History will tell you that lots of Italians immigrated to St. Louis. They invented their own thin crust St. Louis style pizza. It is normally served in a rectangular pan. It may have a variety of cheeses. The sauce is tangy but uncomplicated. The crust...well it has to be thin and crispy. It's an art, not science here. Just like New York and Chicago...the crust has to be perfect.

Maybe these STL Italian immigrants were the first on a thin crust, low carb diet??? More topping taste, thin and perfectly crisp. Mama Mia!

I grew up on Ponticello's, Halls Ferry Inn, Angelo's, Pirrones pizza. I can't get enough of the smell, the crisp crust...or my other treat... leftover Sunday morning thin crust pizza!!!! Yum! I can still see the dented and bent up Ponticello's pans with years of black burn chars on then, I can smell the wonderful aroma of pizza drifting out the window sand vents of the Ponticello's kitchen. 

Serra's is the same style, abeit served in a round pan, but still sliced into square pieces.

Sausage and or pepperoni.  The pepperoni can be greasier.....tasty....but just sausage will keep me happy.

Serra's is a great St.Louis style pie. Family owned and best served after a house Italian salad with iceberg, onion, peppercini and basic garlic vinegar and oil dressing. Frankie Toccos and Faracci's are other great ones from the same cookbook!

If you're not from St. Louis, you are missing out on one of the best inventions of STL immigrants! The other being toasted ravioli! Don't forget the ice cream cone and hot dog were also served first in 1904 in STL at the World's Fair!

Have an ice cold Busch in a fish bowl and go figure!  Now I've really confused you! You're just missing out!

Let's go Blues!
You're in Nashville so grab a beer and have some food! Great town to kick back and enjoy some country music!

Manchester Road is a hub of microbreweries in the Lou, with Side Project in Maplewood being a real gem.

Somehow I missed finding this place in the past, until I saw reports on the news they were recently voted #2 microbrewery on the country.

I really liked their IPA. I forget the name...but it was the lower alcohol of the 2 they made. Very smooth!

The place was a little cold inside....until we found a table in the dart room....fun overlooking the brewing area. 

If you're into craft beers, this is a great find!

Think Bon Air and you know it's about Fast Eddie's!

Where else can the food for two people be less than $10 and tasty! 

Grab a table, order a Big Elwood on a stick and a cheeseburger then go enjoy the coldest beer in town!

Bring CASH as Fast Eddie's is CASH ONLY!

Amazing smoked chicken wings and ribs await you at Salt and Smoke.

Located on Main Street in St Charles with an ample supply of both indoor and outdoor dining spaces makes this an ideal venue for your barbecue cravings.

We had the appetizer portion of smoked wings and ribs, share them, and it was an excellent choice. 

We did not try the sides, but they also looked very appetizing.

It can get very busy here on a holiday or peak timing time, so check in on their app to reduce your table wait time.

I don't normally write Yelp reviews unless the establishment does something that pushes me to, whether that be all star awesome experiences or on the other end of the spectrum. 

This one is not filed under "awesome".

Now, I come from Austin where I am fully accustomed to bitchy, hipster service. Heck, I think it's great, as long as your pie tastes as good as you say, who cares how it gets in my mouth. But seriously, I came across the hive queen of hipster bitches tonight at Elsie's, and though I love the mellow vibe and comfy couches, I am seriously reconsidering coming back.

The chick behind the bar - the one that looked like she just came from some exhausting women's studies night class - had me waiting, sitting, staring at her as she chatted about some benign bullsh*t to her friends without giving me a glance for a good 10 min. Finally when I thought she might be taking a breath in between her run-on, stream-of-consciousness sentences, I asked if I could have a beer, even apologized for interrupting...

Apparently that was the wrong thing to say because she rudely snuffed "You DON'T mean to interrupt??" before proceeding to make THE most ANGRY and AWKWARD beer I have ever been served in my life. I'm serious, this woman wanted me gone - what the hell kind of service is that? Like I said, I am fully used to snotty, self entitled baristas, but the stink eye on this chick took it to a whole other level. 

Now you folks at Elsie's may be snickering reading this, perhaps even patting yourselves on the back for being so "edgy" in this white bread town. Who knows, I don't know who you are, I just know who is representing you, and if that's the way you want to run your business...more power to you. But seriously, alienating your locals like that is not going to line anybody's pockets with the dough, and as a business, I imagine that is fairly important to you. At least I'd hope so.

One of the bartenders stole $$ from my husband. If I could give zero stars I would. My husband frequented this restaurant often as he is a professor at Rowan university and often gets late night meals here or has meetings, etc. A few weeks ago he checked our bank account the day after he went to Landmark for a meal at the bar and noticed a discrepancy. He left a 4$ tip on his bar tab and the bartender added an extra 6$ to his tip!! He wrote to the company and told them, and had a conversation with a manager about it. She did refund our 6$ BUT there was no real apology--she made a lame excuse that the bartender hit the wrong number. Seriously?! How exactly do you mistakenly hit a 10, when you are supposed to put a 4 in? That is stealing plain and simple.

I've been to K & A a handful of times now and I gotta say they make a pretty Kick Ass bagel (see what I did there ;). Although, I can't say they make my favorite bagels, they deliver on several things. 

#1. Space - Almost every bagel shop I've been to has suffered from the same problem - not enough space which means disorganized lines, long wait times and general confusion (mixed with feelings of being hangry). 

Not here - it's spacious, nicely lit (yes this is also a problem I've found with some bagel shops) and very inviting as are the folks making your bagels and taking your order. 

#2. The menu - this includes all of your standard favorites - plain, wheat, salt, poppy, sesame, everything, cinnamon raisin ($8/baker's dozen). There's also classic breakfast sandwiches - BEC, PREG, SEG, plus they have some unique creations such as the Honeymoon (pepper jack, chorizo patty, salsa avocado) and the Triple Threat (pb, banana, and bacon) all averaging around $5 

#3. The bagels - the most important part, of course! These are pretty tasty when they're fresh. Fluffy, airy, and chewy - all things you look for in a great bagel. Now, longevity is true test of time and these bagels do not pass the mark in that category. Sadly, only a short day later (concealed within the brown paper bag they came in), these bagels quickly went stale. There's no arguing that bagels should be consumed fresh but any good bagel that I've ever had will usually last a day or even 2 (if they are really good). So, be sure to freeze these right away if you do not plan on eating them within a day. 

Come for breakfast or lunch, admire the artwork, and enjoy fresh.

This is one of the best Italian restaurants I've been to in South Jersey in recent memory. It's a bit off the beaten path, you need to make a reservation and you shouldn't come expecting the likes of spaghetti and meatballs and chicken Parmesean to be gracing the menu; but that doesn't mean it's not worth a visit. 

The first thing I was taken aback by was the noise in the restaurant. I was hoping for a more intimate, quiet setting; however, it felt like you had to talk loudly even to the person right next to you. Not the worst thing, just not as quiet as I had hoped. 

After placing our order, we were served a variety of freshly baked bread. We started off with the grilled octopus which was a special of the day. We both agreed that the flavor of the octopus was delicious but felt that it could have been a tad bit crispier. 

Next we shared the pesto Trapanese - fusilli pasta with almond-pistachio pesto which is one of the best pasta dishes I've had in a long time. We were also served complimentary gnocchi alla' Argentiera - spinach and ricotta topped with Sicilian caciocavallo which was very good. 

As for the entrees, I ordered the Coniglio Pizzaiola - stewed rabbit with tomato and fresh oregano with rosemary oven roasted potatoes. I really enjoyed the sauce which was full of flavor as well as the crispy potatoes. The rabbit was super tender but also a bit under-seasoned. My dining partner ordered the lamb and we both agreed that although it was cooked perfectly, it too was lacking in seasoning. 

We rounded out our experience with Zeppoli Siciliano which even came with a lit candle for my birthday thanks to my companion. We both agreed that the zeppolis were by far the best thing we had eaten off the menu - not dense at all, so light, airy and sweet. I still think about them sometimes....

I really enjoyed my experience here and love that Zeppoli is not just any other NJ Italian restaurant. Four stars which can easily be five stars. Perhaps invest in some nice napkins (the dish towel on my lap is better suited for the kitchen), work on the noise, and add just a tad more seasoning. I look forward to returning.

It's rare that I review after only one visit but I gotta give it up to Cafe Carmela. They know their way around the kitchen in a way that will heighten every one of your senses. 

We paid them a visit after hearing through the grapevine that they make a killer cheesesteak. Not only is this true but I can confirm that it's one of the best I've ever had. Gotta love that freshly baked seeded roll and Cooper sharp American cheese (the upper echelon of Am cheese). 

Also noteworthy are the truffle fries w/Pecorino Romano and chicken parm sandwich. I'd love to try their dry rub wings, pizza, and other sandwiches. In fact, I'd really love to work my way through the menu. Check it out for yourself. 

The vibe is casual. Service is friendly. It wouldn't be Philly without talking about your favorite cheesesteak with a local sitting nearby. I may have to make a return trip sooner than later...

Central Taco & Tequila is one of the newest hot spots to grace the Haddon Ave restaurant scene. It may not be the only place you can get a taco on the street, but it is certainly the best and only place to find a wide selection of both tacos and tequila. 

This is a go to spot for my friends and I. Our trips typically consist of ordering multiple tacos and pitchers of tequila (no surprise there). We came here recently to celebrate both my buddy's and my birthdays and had a great time - even sitting outside in the parking lot during these COVID times. Props to the burrito bowl which was a nice alternative to the tacos. 

Be forewarned that if you come with a group, each person's order may come out at different times (something they warn you about if you're a first timer). They tend to get packed and don't take reservations so get here early on peak nights!

Once upon a time, it was quite difficult to find really good pizza in South Jersey. It's mostly fine but after living in that far-away land known as North Jersey, I can confidently say NJ does pizza better and SJ does sandwiches better. Of course, this is a whole other debate, but I digress. 

I have ordered a number of times from Brooklyn Pizza over the past year. There's a reason why they are highly rated. This is some of the best pizza in the area and quite possibly some of the best you can find below I-195. 

First I tried the Boardwalk pizza w/pepperoni. The experience was good enough for me to try them again. Next came the Brooklyn style w/pepperoni and that's when I really fell in love. This would be my recommended pie if it's your first time trying them as it is their signature pizza. They totally nail the execution - crunchy, thin square crust, then mozzarella, then the sauce, topped w/oregano, basil, olive oil and parmesan. I ordered a pie recently and was eating slices like I was training for the olympics. 

A couple of things to note - Avoid ordering on a Friday or Saturday night as it is extremely difficult to get through on the phone and once you do, it can be an hour or more until your order is ready. Their Panzarotti is actually just a pizza turnover (not fried) but can feed a family of four.

Here's the thing. You're either going to love or hate Oscar's. There's really no in between. Just like you're either going to start or end your night here. In case you haven't picked up on it from the 300 + reviews, Oscar's is a Dive with a capital D. It's also cash only and if you sit in a booth, be careful not to pick the table where your rear end is given a colonoscopy that you didn't agree to by a rusty spring, but...the drinks are strong and cheap so that more than makes up for it right? 

It's a mixed crowd of trendy twenty somethings, couples, larger groups, and the solo visitor looking to grab a beer and bite to eat. It stands out like a sore thumb in these parts but all the great dives usually do. 

As many others have said, go for the LIT. It's served in what looks like a 16 oz glass and is not for the faint of heart. Don't come in looking for a wide craft beer selection or chic cocktail list. Do come in looking for a bar with character, no shame and a great time.

When you've reached your fill of diners and chain breakfast restaurants, you start to look for something new. The Bistro fits that criteria perfectly. It's nothing special. In fact, I'd go as far as saying it's like a nicer diner sans sassy waitresses, mediocre food and drunks at 2am. 

I live two towns over in what some may say is the unofficial restaurant hot spot in the area yet we are severely lacking when it comes to breakfast options unless you are willing to wait an hour at Sabrina's or want to go to the Pop Shop (although it's not a requirement to have kids when visiting, it might as well be). 

So I came here and I'm glad I did. The coffee and food is fresh, the menu is large with plenty of options and specials of the day and the prices are quite reasonable for what you get, which is a lot of food. I've also found the servers to be friendly and mostly attentive (my waitress kinda forgot about me on my first visit which got my eyes darting around the restaurant trying to see where she went and hoping to make eye contact). But will I be back? You betcha.

I have ordered from Aroma a few times over the last several months but am thinking that those are rookie numbers since I should be ordering here more like it's my job. 

Highly recommend the Chicken Vandaloo, Lamb Tikka Masala, Gobi Machurian (fried cauliflower) , and don't forget the garlic naan. The spice level, tenderness of the meat, and combination of flavors has been fantastic. I'm no expert but this food beats the pants off of some other Indian restaurants I've ordered from. 

Can't speak for the dining experience since I have not yet had the pleasure. Take out or dine in, I am happy to oblige.

Was craving Vietnamese food and recently ordered from Hên. We really enjoyed the Bánh mí and were super surprised at how crispy and flavorful the house wings were. The summer rolls w/shrimp were okay but were definitely filled w/more lettuce than shrimp. The beef pho w/eye round and flank was tasty especially after adding some hot sauce, basil and bean sprouts. 

One thing that threw us off was that half the steak came cooked and other came raw. It would have also helped for them to include some deeper bowls for take out. There is a ramen restaurant that I order from that does this and it is perfect sized disposable bowl for a take out soup noodle experience. 

Would I try them again? For sure, and those wings will absolutely be included in that next order.

Ever since I've found out about honeygrow, I've slowly started coming here almost on a weekly basis. 

It's quick and casual, the food is fresh and locally sourced, and I always leave satisfied. There is very little interaction with the staff as you order from a kiosk and your name is called out once your food is ready. 

I've tried the Sweet Soy Five Spice stir fry which is brown rice, ground turkey, green beans, red onions, and sesame seeds which has been very good. I've also created my own stir fry on at least one occasion as well as my own salad. 

My one minor complaint is the cost. As I mentioned before the food is fresh but it comes with a price. It's been rare that I have left here spending less than $13 which is typical for an entree (without any extras) and a drink. 

Nevertheless, I will still continue to re-visit when I do not wish to get the mid-day itis or when I am looking for a fulfilling tasty lunch or dinner.

No frills pizza joint currently taking walk-ups only. Ordered the plain pie, was told it would be 30 mins, and it was ready on time. Thin crust, tasty sauce, cheese, and EVOO with an upper crust that was a bit charred. A tad pricey for $4/slice and $22/pie but overall, it's a solid choice if you're in the neighborhood.

Perhaps, it was the food. Or the service. Or the excitement of being with my dining parter who is a Chinese food expert. All of these things made for a memorable, exciting and more than satisfying first experience at Joe's. 

We ordered several dishes so that we could sample as much as possible. This included the steamed pork dumplings, Shu Mei, Peking duck, and Spicy Szechuan beef udon noodles. All of this ended up being more than enough food for two people but also provided leftovers for at least a couple of more meals. 

The Szechuan beef was tender as were the udon noodles that came together in a marriage of their spicy sauce that had both a nice kick and came out piping hot (perfect for a cold winter day or night). The pork dumplings can be described exactly how I'd like to describe dumplings, full of delicious soup and juicy. The Shu Mei, packed with well seasoned ground pork, was both hearty and filling. 

The main star of the show comes straight from the title - the Peking duck. I've never had the pleasure of eating Peking duck but I can say that I really enjoyed it - crispy, glazed skin on the outside and juicy, dark meat on the inside - what's there not to love?

Our service was nothing less than outstanding. We even received a visit from Joe who was walking the restaurant, chatting with diners as they enjoyed their meal. Joe's is leaps and bounds above your average take-out Chinese restaurant. Between the traditional and Americanized Chinese food, everything is fresh and made with TLC. I consider this to be the perfect place to come if you want more traditional Chinese dishes but also if you're with someone who just can't not order their General's chicken. I already can't wait to come back and try something new!

I sat at the bar and the bartender was very helpful and attentive when providing recommendations. I treated myself to three courses:

1) Appetizer-Shrimp and Alligator sausage Gumbo. Coming to visit New Orleans, I had to try it. I would say it tasted great, but I was expecting it to be heartier with more pieces of shrimp and alligator sausage.

2) Main course- Herbsaint Flamed Catfish. The bartender informed me that the Herbsaint liquor gives the fish a licorice flavor. I don't like licorice but I decided to try it anyway. I'm glad I did because the licorice didn't overpower the fish at all, in fact it complemented the fish well.

3) Dessert- Double chocolate bread pudding- It was their signature dessert! Luckily I had enough time because it takes 20 minutes for them to prepare it. But it was well worth the wait! I'm not a dessert person but I enjoyed it.

Lastly, I've been trying to get into different types of bourbons. The bartender gave me a sampling of a couple different types and educated me on them.

Overall, the food was good but the service ultimately pushed it up to 5 stars!

That's it. It has been decided-I have found my new favorite neighborhood spot. It has long been a favorite gastropub of mine, still high up there in the rankings, for sure, but since moving into the Rittenhouse neighborhood, I have found a lot of places, just not a lot of places I wanted to return to multiple times a month. 

After a few visits I've found what I was looking for. A cozy bar, exceptional friendly servers and bartenders who will remember you and treat you like old friends, a CHEESE CART with one very, very knowledgeable cheesemonger, and a great selection of beverages ranging from some creative and well crafted cocktails, to classics, a nice wine selection, and yes-even "the champagne of beers," on tap. Not that I'm ordering that but... Gotta admit I liked seeing it on the chalk board. My fave bartender-shout out to Shane-is da bomb.

Bonus points for sitting down at the bar, my favorite spot to sit, and none other than Chef Perrier sits down next to me. Just all casual like, ordering his beverage and chatting up some lucky ladies sitting at the other end of the bar. Yep, apparently he's a regular. That is saying a lot for an establishment, me thinks. I admit, I got starstruck. 

This place is so good I'm bringing the future inlaws here for dinner for their first visit to Philly in the near future. This is in your hands, Crow and the Pitcher. In your cheese cart I trust.

Holy freaking moly. This place is kind of amazing. And by "kind of," I mean REALLY FUCKING AMAZING. 

I came here for a Sunday brunch with a few friends. We were in the mood for some simple breakfast food -- pancakes, bacon, eggs -- you know the deal. As much as I love a fancy schmancy brunch, sometimes you just want the basics, you know? 

We arrived around 11am, and the place was PACKED. Apparently, we weren't the only ones with the bright idea to hit this place up. 

After an hour-long wait, we were finally seated. I was pretty hangry at this point, and had high hopes that the food would make up for the absurdly long wait. 

Well...it did. It definitely did. I went with hash browns, bacon, and pancakes, and the freshly squeezed orange juice was highly recommended, so I went with that, too! Oh, and coffee. Because yes. 

Everything was fantastic! The pancakes were soft and fluffy, the hashbrowns were crispy and hot, the bacon knocked my socks off, and the orange juice? Whatever $500 juicer they probably used to make this stuff needs to be in my house, PRONTO. The juice tasted like I was drinking from an orange with a straw. Words can't even describe! It was sweet and just amazing. 

I highly recommend this place. Just writing about it now is making me super hungry, and I sort of wish The Pancake House had evening hours so I could do the whole breakfast for dinner thing. Breakfast for dinner? Yes...I'm 12 years old.

I am very excited to see a place like this in Tampa (especially in my neighborhood). I stopped in for their "sneak peek" on Sunday. They took advantage of the extra foot traffic from the Gasparilla Arts Festival to do a soft opening with a limited menu. 

The location is great. The spot has been a couple of different places that weren't able to survive like it's neighbor, Taps. Anise coins itself as "Global" and there is a wall mural behind the bar to prove it. They have a couple of different seating options; the bar, booths/tables and a lounge area with small tables and sofas. It's exactly what you expect it to be, modern and sleek, but with an eclectic feel since the chairs aren't all the same and they have influences to match their global theme. They struck a good balance of being modern and hip without making it feel cold. They paid extreme attention to detail, all the way down to glasses filled with rose petals on the tables. The service was great for a restaurant that has been open for 1 day. There was a steady stream of people coming in and out and the service and food barely showed it.

My roommate and I were looking for a little afternoon snack so the menu with small plates was perfect. The owners own the food truck Stinky Buns so we had to give those a try. They had pork belly, beer battered shrimp or beef. We got the beer battered shrimp and pork belly. If you've never had a stinky bun, get ready to be pleasantly surprised. The bun is like nothing I've had before. They are almost sticky to the touch but light, airy and soft when you chew them. The beer battered shrimp was great. They come with a sort of coleslaw on them that adds the moisture needed to keep it fresh and light tasting. The batter on the shrimp was good and not at all greasy. The pork belly was my favorite. They're tender and juicy with a great barbecue flavor. Stinky buns are like a mix between a taco and a pita in the best way possible. I'd like to go back and try the beef. We also ordered the Chicken Bulgogi and Kimichi Nachos. My roommate is a picky eater so she asked for the Kimichi on the side. Chicken Bulgogi is a Korean way of preparing chicken. All I know is that it's marinated and simmered. The chicken was good in it's own right. They could definitely serve it as a stinky bun too. My only complaint about the experience was that the cheese on the nachos wasn't super melted. I don't know if they set too long or they weren't cooked long enough but I like my cheese melty. The flavor of the nachos was on point! They have cheese, fresh jalapeños, kimichi and sour cream. The way the flavor meld you would think that Korea and Mexico were neighbors. 

I wasn't planning on drinking but we were at a gastroBAR and I knew I was going to be the first to review on Yelp so I had to do it! They are pricey. Signature cocktails are $10. I got the Bramble, my favorite drink at Ciros, as the waitress suggested. It was ridiculously good. The fruit muddled at the bottom was so fresh and flavorful (though I'm not sure what it was). When you have a fruity drink like this, you appreciate the meaning of the phrase. It's naturally sweet and not loaded with corn syrup and fruit flavorings. Cocktails like these stand out among the crowd.

I'm excited to see how Anise grows. I have no doubt that it will be successful. This is the kind of place that Downtown/Channelside needed. It will be a great place for girl's nights out, dates, and pre-Straz festivities. I also read that they plan on making picnics that you can bring across the street to Curtis Hixon- brilliant!

Cheer Anise! And welcome home!

O Cocina is everything that Besito is trying be. The decor of this place is amazing. It's another great bright spot on the Tampa scene. It's a place you can bring an out-of-towner and be proud to say it's in your city. I've been a few times now and I can say that it just keeps getting better. The craft cocktails may take longer than the vodka soda you typically order but it's worth the wait. As all good Mexican restaurants should, they have a killer margarita. However, my favorite drink on the menu is the Freshman. I'm not 100% what goes into it but I think they might add sunshine because this drink makes me want to sit outside and enjoy Florida in the spring! The appetizers are amazing. Tableside guac is an obvious choice but I'd suggest you dig deeper and try the elotes. Elotes is Mexican street corn. It's grilled and then they add a delicious sauce and cheese crumbles. I had this for the first time on the streets of Mexico and I can tell ya that this is as good and you'll save yourself the airfare. Another great app is the Queso Fundido. It's not your typical "queso." It's meant to be scooped up into the tortillas it comes with (not dipped in with tortilla chips). A quick tip though- go ahead and ask for some extra tortillas so you don't waste any of the cheesy-chorizo goodness. For entrees, I highly recommend getting anything with the mole sauce. Their mole is true, authentic, I-wonder-how-many-tries-it-took-to-get-it-right mole. There are a ton of ingredients that go into the complex flavor that ends up on your plate. As for tacos, my favorites are the short rib (de res) and and the pork (cochinita pibil). If you still have room, the skillet cookie with ice cream is delicious! 

O Cocina is still experiencing some growing pains as they settle in to their new spot, which is to be expected. But any hiccups we've experienced have been met with great customer service and a willingness to make anything right. Overall, I think this will fall in with Ulele, Ichicoro, the Refinery, and Oxford Exchange in the "Places You Have to See in Tampa" lineup.

Oh gosh. For real. I haven't been this impressed with a food place in a long time. Really, despite having high expectations because of the hype the place still blew my socks off. Don't let the hype or long lines make you think that this is just some tourist trap. It's not. It's completely legit. Also, don't be intimidated by the "hot chicken" spice if you aren't into heat - they have plenty of options including non-spicy. The flavor and preparation of the food was perfect - it's not just all about the heat.

I ended up placing an order online 30 minutes before I arrived at lunchtime on a super busy Saturday. I walked right in past the long line that stretched down the block. The employees at the counter were super nice and engaged in small talk with me despite them being in super busy mode. They were fantastic. It's like they legitimately enjoy their jobs and they like their customers. So awesome. My food was brought out and I ate elsewhere. The dining area is quite small but there is a decent sized patio but you're still going to have a wait during peak times.

Ok the food: I ordered a chicken breast quarter which was very big with the wing attached. Heat level "damn hot" which is second to the top of the heat range. The heat was noticable and it would be a kick to someone not a fanatic about spice. I would recommend maybe level 2 to the typical person. The chicken was so good. I ordered it "fried hard" which made it super crispy but it was still very moist. So impressed. The flavors were great. That flavor profile is quite unique and tasted so good.  I also ordered a few grilled chicken tenders to try and they were great too. The grilled tenders would be a great choice for someone wanting to avoid fried chicken.

I didn't get any sides but they have plenty of choices that all looked really good.

You have to try Hattie B's if you are in the area. It really is the real deal.

I love this local Taiwanese boba shop in West Philly! Lulu Cafe is named after the owners' adorable French bulldog, and the menu and flavors are authentic. The shop is small, and there are a couple of tables and window spots. I stop by here once in a while for a brown sugar milk tea and some popcorn chicken. On Sunday, they introduced a new grape refresher - a grape slush with jelly on the bottom, topped with sea salt cream and sliced frozen grapes. if you're into Welch's, you'll probably enjoy this refreshing cooler. The slush is sweet, but not overwhelmingly sweet, and you're able to adjust the sugar level. The sea salt cream helps to balance out the sweetness, and I love the jelly that sits at the bottom. 

Tip: There's only street parking in the area, so parking in this area might get a little bit tricky.

I just couldn't break through this terrible writer's block until I started staring at a photo of the luscious plate of boiled shrimp I had here at Desire. I just find it funny how predictable humans tend to be. 

For one, you put them all around cheap and abundant liquor without any real restrictions and man, the outcome gets pretty obvious. PLASTERED. A good amount of them...always get plastered. Not to mention, for once in my whole life, I watched people walk one instance, kiss the ground on the next, and stay still as EMS flashily arrived to escort them away.

For two, you put me around restaurants and I'm bound to enter another one, sit down, and start ordering all over again. So yeah, while the rest of Bourbon Street was drinking it up and living it up, I was hungry for more Louisiana raw oysters...as well as the famous Louisiana boiled shrimp, which I *desired* for oh-so-long. (NOTE: I developed an allergy *only* to shrimp and couldn't eat it for the last 4 years).

Predictable was the raw oysters - same supplier, same size, shucked just about the same. Predictable also was the shrimp - despite being overcooked, it was truly flavorful (and causing enough desire for me to begin planning my next trip to a NON-tourist part of Louisiana for a better culinary experience).

I was just stunned at how good this plate of boiled shrimp was. Come on...we're in tourist NOLA and it is still this good? Geez. Now I understand why even the air whispers how unique the spices are in this region that come together to breathe life into even the simplest and "unrefined" dishes. 

Now comes the *unpredictable* part of it all. I am no longer allergic to shrimp. FREAKING SMOKED CHICKENS. I am NO longer allergic to SHRIMP!!!

Now back to being predictable and catching up on the last 4 years of missing out...

Cured by Cajun spice and everything NICE.

#FreakingLoveNOLA

Time, oh seconds, minutes, and hours...you pass so fast that I'm already another decade older. Crap, I better do some catching up...so time to start 2014 right (albeit late) by writing a few reviews - beginning with the one spot in NOLA that was double, no triple freaking AWESOME.

The weather was weird when we were visiting New Orleans. It was supposed to be warm; however, greeting us as we left the plane was...cold weather that would freeze the typical Californian. But it didn't faze me at all; if anything, I was hungrier than usual and being around this area - THAT is a GOOD thing. So post-check-in, we rushed out to...conquer the French Quarter.

Beginning to form within the skies overhead as we stood like all the other tourist idiots in a never-ending line outside ACME Oyster House were raindrops that smiled as they slowly gained mass in readiness to drop like pigeon loads unto earth to scatter humanity away and out of the over[tourist]populated Bourbon Street. We were still several legions behind in the line and were very far from being able to wage war on the famed char-grilled oysters...and the incoming raindrops artillery made staying put significantly less desirable.

We decided to ditch this battle for another day and hopped across the street to give Felix's a shot instead, which had a significantly shorter line. I would say that this was definitely the BEST decision we made during our stay in NOLA.

Locals had told us that this was *the* local spot among the tourist traps. Here, one will find good food, competitive prices, straightforward service, and a relatively short line.

Post-NOLA-Binge-Summary:

1. Raw Oysters - same supply, same price, same size, shucked better - yeah, BETTER. (On the other hand, I don't think I'll ever enjoy Pacific-side oysters...raw Louisiana oysters don't have the "fishy" scent that most abhor).
