2. Char-grilled Oysters - because this is a direct comparison of the two...Felix is DEFINITELY better than ACME (and they are supposed to be the best???)

3. I thoroughly enjoyed their Jambalaya and Crawfish Etouffee.

#FreakingLoveNOLA

Spoiler alert, they have the BEST Lamb burger I have ever had in Tampa Bay. The hubs found this little gem as a hot new business on Yelp. A little vacation day brought us here before heading to Safety Harbor for some sightseeing. 

We came in at lunch time and the waitress directed us to seat ourselves. We choose a table at a booth hybrid.. half booth, half chairs at the table. The inside decor is warm, wood with copper pipe fixtures and intimate. Our waitress took our drink order and answered questions about the menu. 

After ordering the drinks we needed a few minutes to review the menu.. We decided to try the venison sausage corn dogs to start. For entrees I ordered the the Jucie Lucy, the lamb burger, my hubs ordered the regular  burger, our oldest daughter got the pulled BBQ pork and my vegetarian daughter got an order of fries and side of fruit opting to not try either of the salads they had for lunch.

The corn dogs arrived quickly, hot out of the fryer plated beautifully with pickled  cauliflower and a spicy stone ground mustard.  They were delicious. Not long after the entrées arrived. Hot and plated perfectly, they were served with a side of fries. The lamb burger was cooked with a beautiful warm pink medium center sandwiched inside a soft bun which was layered with taziki sauce, lettuce, tomato and red onion beneath. 

My hubs and I split our sandwiches so we could try each others but our oldest daughter got to his burger before me so I got to try her pulled BBQ pork instead. The pork was "wet" with the sauce already in the pork. It had a distinct flavor, a taste like cumin was one of the ingredients. Interesting and tasty whatever it was. 

Throughout the meal our waitress checked on us, filled drinks over and over and ensured our food and dining experience was going well. With great service, exceptional food, the Little Lamb is a little gem.

When in Rome, they say....
Nashville is the home of hot chicken and Hattie B's is mecca. It would be sacrilegious to give them anything but a 5 star, if not for reputation alone 

Not all reviews need to be 1000 words, and this one of them. Good sides, lots of beverage choices, and no joke, some of the best flavored and most well fried chicken out there.

The only negative about Hattie's is that the secret is out and the lines are insane. If you're an out of towner, do yourself the favor and don't come to this location, especially around lunch time. Go to one of the other locations about 5 miles away.

Until next time...

I am pretty sure I have visited all the South Coast Delis in the Santa Barbara area. This one seems to be on the smaller side, however, during this Covid-19 pandemic, they manage the high amounts of orders very well. They have two social distanced lines out front: One for Online Pre-Paid Orders and another for Phone/To Be Placed Orders. The staff is very friendly, even during busy lunch rushes from behind their warm masks.

I am truly thankful on this Thursday for their delicious salads and sandwiches. Often I crave the Foul Play salad, or their take on the (S.C.D.)BLT sandwich that I scarfed down today. Keep those huge portions coming SCD!

If it weren't for Thai food, I don't believe I would have survived college. I would have wasted away to simply dust in a corner of the library. When you're broke or on a budget, Thai food is one of those few affordable meals that every student turns to besides pizza or Top Ramen. Now that I am no longer a college student, yet still broke, I always find myself craving Thai cuisine on the regular. For me, Siam Elephant is one of the top Thai joints in Santa Barbara County and competes with Rice By Mama down south in Ventura.

I often visit Siam Elephant for their spectacular lunch special which is offered Tuesday thru Friday from 11am until they close until dinner at 2:30pm. For under $11 you receive a cup of soup (usually Chicken Tom Yum) or side salad (FYI: dressing is a runny mayo), steamed white rice, crispy fried wontons, a vegetable spring roll AND your main entree (costs $9.50 or $11 if your choice of meat is shrimp). They have an entire variety of entree choices ranging from noodles, to curries, to specialty Thai dishes. 

I cannot help myself and always order their Pad Thai because their tamarind sauce they use is perfection--tangy and sweet, yet a kick of sourness with some lime added. The peanuts add a pleasant crunch to the al dente noodles. The lunch special is a large portion so I usually request a box to take half home for the following day, and indulge in either sweet Mango Sticky Rice or savory Coconut Ice Cream for dessert. Siam is located right off Linden Street in Carpinteria's main street beach town. Simply look for the wooden elephants at the entrance as you head toward the beach. There is also a large outdoor patio to take advantage of on those 350 or so days of sunshine!

We are all well aware of how 'abnormal' 2020 has been. My family usually celebrates with a homemade Thanksgiving dinner on Black Friday. We didn't have much planned for the actual Thanksgiving evening. I had seen in the Santa Barbara Independent newspaper that Live Oak Cafe was among local restaurants offering Thanksgiving dinner this year. We wanted to support a local business while staying at home. Due to Covid precautions, instead of providing dine-in, Live Oak Cafe had individual Take-Home & Bake Pot Pie Dinners. Given that most folks are celebrating what they are thankful for in smaller groups and with less travel this year, we decided to give Live Oak Cafe a whirl (outside of their breakfast which I thoroughly enjoy). Let's just say we were extremely pleased!

At only $25 a person, they offered:
- Choice of Turkey or vegetarian Mushroom Pot Pie
- Shredded Mixed Salad with lemon vinaigrette
- Sweetened, cubed Yams
- Green Beans with crispy onions
- Choice of mini Apple, Pumpkin or Pecan Pie.

For this price, it was quite a deal! Simply for two pies of any sorts is spectacular. The entree and sides filled us up enough that we had to save our dessert pies for the following day. Thank you this Thanksgiving, Live Oak Cafe!

Finding decent barbecue outside of our local delicacy of Tri-Tip in Santa Barbara ain't an easy feat.  

Chicken in a Barrel is totally random because: 
1) It's in a generic strip mall
2) They barbecue whole chickens in a barrel (make me think of beer can chickens...)
3) It is a small Hawaiian-inspired chain with locations where?!  Four on the Hawaiian Islands...ok fair, but then Lake Tahoe and Goleta... Random.  But I'm pleased it is close by.  Fact: Goleta was their first franchise location.
4) You'll read about my last point in the last paragraph, so read on...

I have become a regular here since I often find myself with barbecue cravings.  Their Axxess card deal (no longer available) is what originally caught my eye and dragged me in.  I don't know what all their tricks are but the meat is almost always perfectly moist, tender and super tasty.  I always have to go for their slab of ribs or the chicken.  In the past I did stray from my normal order by trying the chicken tacos (meat was surprisingly dry) and the brisket (a bit chewy and overcooked), so I now only stick to my favorites.  They have two barbecue sauces: classic (my favorite due to finger-licking sweetness) and spicy; not to mention their secret spices and rubs!

To be honest, I am not a religious person but don't mind others having their own beliefs if they keep it to themselves and respect others.  The owners stamp every take-out box with "John 3:16."  At first, I thought it was a bit 'in my face' but after coming in regularly and the staff being super outgoing and friendly, this is the most discrete and pleasant method of spreading their beliefs.  I did some further research on their website to find that the owner Mike Pierce began Chicken In A Barrel to combine his two missions: "spread the love of God and this extraordinary culinary joy."  Now this I applaud this.

Often we forget what it is like to be a tourist in our own town. Sometimes work and the daily grind takes over while stripping us of our sanity. I have been fortunate to experience The Ritz-Carlton Bacara Resort from three different perspectives: as a local resident and Foley Wine Club Member, as a hotel guest, and as a mobile IV nurse--all of which are consistently extraordinary visits.

This secluded enclave of Goleta/Santa Barbara offers everything one could need within a five star resort. Stellar ocean and island views, exceptional customer service, modern yet Santa Barbara-inspired design and architecture, a span of endless services and amenities (including a wine tasting room-Foley Wine Society Tasting Room, coffee shop-First Drop, three bars-O Bar, Angel Oak and poolside, beachside Bistro Cafe and upscale restaurant Angel Oak, a full-service spa, gift shop, event venues, three saline pools-one adults only, natural beaches, four tennis courts, nature trails, and daily activities including guided nature bluff walks, workouts and exercise classes, bike rentals, kids clubs, happy hour, and more).

During COVID, the Ritz-Carlton Hotel Chain offered local healthcare providers a discount for nightly stays. I have to admit that it is even more spectacular--and my favorite way to visit--as a guest. From valet drivers upon arrival, to a personalized check-in with cocktails and bottled water, dinner at the restaurant, ending with the check-out process, my partner and I agreed that there wasn't enough time in the day to take advantage of everything offered and we never wanted to leave! Our room (well "suite") had ocean and garden views, colorful decor, free high speed wireless Internet, a fireplace, outdoor patio seating, two separate bathroom areas, shower and deep bath tub, a Nespresso coffee machine, a mini fridge, and everything else needed for a comfortable stay. It's was absolutely splendid! Thank you for a refreshing start!

My only small complaints are regarding high pricing for valet parking ($30/night), resort fee ($50/night), "Posh Pooch" pet fee ($250/night) and room service fees (delivery fee, high food menu prices and automatic gratuity). All of these add up, particularly when rooms begin at a very minimum weekday/low season rate of $500+ a night. Lastly, whoever decided to have paver walkways throughout a hillside resort that are loud and not luggage friendly requiring golf cart travel should have thought ahead. Of course all of these are somewhat avoidable.

In the end, I cannot recommend the Bacara enough!

After relocating to Santa Barbara years ago, I had always heard raving reviews of Ca' Dario downtown. Still 'til this day I  have not made it to that location, however, I HAVE been to the newer Goleta location countless times.
Each and every time I have received excellent:

-Customer service...
The two brothers who work here remember my partner's and my names, plus always smile while carrying on a friendly conversation.

-Food...
Their food is absolutely spectacular and is easily at the top of my list for Italian cuisine in Santa Barbara County. Deliciousness starts with the appetizers and continues through to dessert. Their seafood dishes are always fresh and pasta cooked perfectly al dente. Oh and their thin crust pizzas are not to be missed either!

-Ambiance...
Given the strip mall corner unit location, you wouldn't know the interior is as large as it is! They have minimal yet elegant decor, dim lighting, and a lovely outdoor patio with a fountain.

Most recently, my family took advantage of Ca' Dario's New Year's Eve pre-fixe meals for $85. It came with a small plate of choice, lasagna, main entree, and an included bottle of Dard wine. Deals like this, along with what I've always said keep us coming back.

I am all about supporting local, family-owned businesses. Sadly, when you give a place three attempts--each ending up to three strikes--they're out in my book. Usually my go to Thai spot is Meun Fun Thai on Calle Real. However, when they are closed, Pattaya is my next closest Thai option Goleta.

Pattaya is somewhat hidden within Old Town Goleta with more authentic Thai offerings than other places around. The interior is a bit dated and odd with almost half of its restaurant looking abandoned (to the right upon entering the main door)--seems as if they had plans to expand or renovate 'on day' which has never made any leeway, even  before Covid was a thing... The staff is often not the most helpful or friendly which doesn't help the lacking ambiance. I will say though that the lighting is pleasant with natural skylights.

This latest visit we ordered online through their website and the timing was quick (around 20-25 minutes). The appetizer, Puff Cheese with Shrimp (similar to crab rangoon), was fried to perfection, but had barely any cream cheese stuffing and a fourth of a shrimp sized piece inside. When we got to the three main entrees of all Pad Thai, they had an acidic/sour flavor; perhaps from too much tamarind sauce? If it hadn't been made with fried tofu I would have thought it had bad meat inside. Unfortunately, we were not impressed at all with the dishes this time or in the past.

Finding culture in Santa Barbara can be a tricky task given that the population is predominantly Caucasian and Spanish-American/Mexican (the one exception). I am always stoked when I do find a place owned by immigrants who pour their heart and soul into their business. From the minute you step up to the entrance of Brasil Arts Cafe, you can tell that it is Brazilian given the flags, bright colors, art on the walls, and difficult to pronounce food items in Portuguese. 

I have visited several times and unfortunately, the availability of all their food items is hit or miss. If they have Coxinha ("Brazilian Chicken Fritters;" shredded chicken meat, covered in dough, breaded and fried) and Pão de Queijo ("Brazilian Cheese Bread;" baked cheese bun) in their display case, you've hit the golden prize! Pão de Queijo is a great gluten-free alternative to those with dietary restrictions. Both have spectacular flavors and make perfect fried snacks. They also offer fresh fruit smoothies and acai bowls.

If you want to jump in and try an authentic, larger Brazilian meal, they offer fish, chicken, and steak accompanied by rice, beans, farofa (toasted cassava or cornflour mixture placed on top of other foods for texture), vinaigrette, chimichurri, and fried plantains. I enjoy that you get a little taste of everything with the entrees. You can never go wrong with a zesty chimichurri or sweet plantains!

Be sure to peek in the back of the cafe near the restrooms where there is a gym that offers classes of Capoeira, an Afro-Brazilian martial art combining elements of dance, acrobatics, and music. I absolutely appreciate how Brasil Arts Cafe has become the center for Brazilian awareness, culture, and community in Santa Barbara. Check out their website for other events that involve classes, dances, exercise, concerts, and other activities. Stay strong and represent, Brazil Arts Cafe!

Those of us who are fortunate to live in Santa Barbara know how blessed we are. With the ocean to the south, we have the ideal breezes, moisture, sunlight and other factors that allow for perfect produce and agriculture. The majority of items found here are not only local but also organic. Some of the vegetables and fruits are shockingly massive and potential Seymours ("Little Shop of Horrors" reference) that when you take them home they may insist you to feed them!

As you walk around you can find everything from honey, kombucha/juices/jun, jams, hummus, flowers/plants, nuts, cheeses, meats, produce and beyond. Once you bite into these items, you'll realize how altered everything we buy in the grocery stores are. The colors and flavors are so vibrant!

You will also see some of the most interesting granola, hipster, individuals; similar to the Buskers of Seattle's Pike Place--except they're friendly so I lean more toward comparing it to the Portland City Market.

A few tips:
- The market runs Saturdays 8:30 am - 1 pm. Go early for the best picks.
- There is not much seafood at this market; instead check out the Saturday Fishermen's Market at the Harbor running 6 - 11 am (http://www.cfsb.info/sat).
- Be sure to bring your reusable bags! Less plastic, the better. Otherwise you may feel guilty and find yourself signing 5+ county public petitions like I did.
- Bring cash! I was surprised by how many vendors do not take plastic using the Square app.
- Only service dogs are allowed; though many folks were cheating.

I am hoping that they will relocate the market to somewhere more appropriate besides a parking lot, but only time will tell.

I APPSolutely LOVE Finney's. And the reason for the capitalization is for emphasis of the word "Apps" since their appetizers are where it's at! Finney's specialize in upscale gastropub food. Blame it on Sweet Home Chicago for being my hometown leading me to appreciate unhealthy, sharable grub... I am one of those diners who enjoys when each person gets a plate or an entree and everyone shares. Sharing is caring, right?! I have tried pretty much every small plate on Finney's menu and keep coming back for more:

Crispy Coconut Shrimp-Check!
Bavarian Pretzel-Check!
Onion Ring Tower-Check!
Mini Lobster Rolls-Check!
Cheesesteak Egg Rolls-Check!
Brewster's Brats-Check!

Well those are just to name a few of my favorite regular items. Funniest part is that I'm not a beer drinker and they have a bunch of local beers on tap. I don't like loud spaces or sports bars. Nor do I care for copper counters or tables due to the linger metallic smell it leaves on your arms and elbows. Nonetheless, I LOVE Finney's simply because of their food.

Pizza Online Co. is a very ingenious creation given that everything is becoming so convenient with mobile and online ordering. You have three ordering options for food service here:
1) GrubHub (via Yelp) or DoorDash
2) Their own website (pick-up only!)
3) Stopping in and using their iPad device

Keep in mind, they have no business phone if you have any issues after placing an order, you need to go there in person or manage it via the ordering website. The staff was very friendly, welcoming and efficient.  I have no idea how they keep everything so organized.

I'm unsure what the connection is between Boba tea, calzones and pizza, yet it's fun nonetheless.  The interior decor is mainly a kitchen but with cool artwork and basil growing on the wall in planters.  The chef came and picked the basil for my margherita calzone right there on the spot.  The flavors were super fresh and the marinara sauce not very acidic.  When I was handed the box, the calzone was the size and weighed the same as my head!  If you're looking for a convenient, tasty food option, you've found it!

Personally, I like Convivo because their menu consistently offers something different than everyone else in town. Chef Peter McNee considers it a blend of "nomad" Italian with its Mediterranean influences and local California 'farm to table' ingredients. While I don't fully understand what all this means, everything is simply delicious. So delicious that it is always winning an award or being mentioned in the press (SB Independent Foodie Award, New York Times Places to Go, Zagat, to name a few). Don't get me wrong, the service, atmosphere, setting, and service are all spectacular. You're practically on East Beach for gosh sake!
Yet, they have one of the best Happy Hours in Santa Barbara daily 3:00-6:00 PM that features how it stands out from its competition. Between the Yellow Potatoes with Za'atar and Romesco sauce, tender Polpette lamb meatballs with tapenade and chickpeas, and Wood-fired za'atar flatbread with fresh accompaniments, I don't know which item tops the list. All of the Happy Hour items are tapas-style, or meant to be shared. Since Convivo is the restaurant for the Santa Barbara Inn, it's hours are extensive. 
P/S: Don't get tripped up by staring at the bar which has one side all windows and the other all mirrors. It becomes even more confusing with each glass of wine (worth mentioning, they have a great selection of wines available).

In celebration of Latinx Heritage Month, why not choose an Isla Vista institution like Freeb!rds World Burrito (Freeb!rds for short). Say what you like by comparing it to Chipotle or Qdoba, they just aren't on the same caliber. 
First, Freeb!rds began back in 1987.
Second, UCSB students wouldn't have a staple restaurant to call their own. It's like In N Out Burger to Californians, and an essential hangover or munchie food.
Third, the wall has pictures of customers taken during their travels around the world, along with signatures and notes stating how much they wished they were able to eat a Freebirds burrito from their current location (hence "World Burrito" being part of the name.
Bottom line, portions are large--particularly if you choose to go with the Monster Burrito. Choose a burrito, bowl, tacos or nachos, meat, cheese, bean type and toppings including lettuce, pico de gallo, guacamole (fresh but an additional charge), and salsas (available on the side too). I usually end up splitting the entrees of nachos or burrito.
So now go get in line and get your grub on!

Brophy Brother's is a well-known seafood staple for Santa Barbara locals. After moving here, I had a handful of people say, "Have you been to Brophy's yet?" Now living here for some time and exploring other eateries in the area, I have some things to say. You come to Brophy's for two things, and only two things:
1) The views: It's the quintessential postcard photo of Santa Barbara with boats in the marina, Stearn's wharf pointing at the Channel Islands and the Santa Ynez mountains in the foreground.
2) Fish & Chips: They're pretty darn stellar. Beer-battered, fried well without being greasy, and reasonably priced. The fish is better than the chips which are fairly basic but still hit the spot.

Instead of waiting in line at Brophy Brother's looking for ______...go to... _____ instead:
-Strong drinks...go to...Harry's Plaza Cafe, Joe's Cafe or Longboard's Grill
-Chowder or Lobster Bisque...go to...Enterprise Fish Company
-Oysters...go to...Lure Fish House or Broadstreet Oyster Company
-Flavorful/Spicy Seafood...go to...The Palace Grill
-Seafood Brunch (Brophy's opens at 11 AM daily)...go to...Hendry's Boathouse
-Same Fish & Chips without the wait?...go to...Brophy's On The Alley in Goleta.

Whether you decide to take my advice or not, the bar is always quicker (and steals the best views) and there's 90 minute free parking right after turning in off of Shoreline Drive and before entering the pay lots.

Oui Oui, mon ami!  
I absolutely love myself some Renaud's. Be sure to arrive before 10 AM to avoid an excessive wait and line--plus get first dibs on the freshly baked goodies. I haven't had anything here I didn't like. Their baguettes have a perfect crispy crust and soft interior. The croissants come in classic, chocolate and almond (my personal favorite) that all are perfectly buttery and ideal for any occasion. All of their pastries are stellar including the eclairs, fruit and lemon tarts, chocolate and fruit bombs, and macaroons.

Not only is it a bakery, but they also offer brunch. I enjoy the American Breakfast with their chicken sausage, two eggs and baguette. If you have a taste for more of a European continental yet carbalicious breakfast, go for the Baker's Basket that comes with a toasted baguette, croissant with butter and jam, fresh squeezed orange juice, and coffee or tea. You can also upgrade your croissant to almond or chocolate for an upcharge. If that's not what you have a taste for, they also have salads, sandwiches (the Croque Monsieur will blow your socks off) and quiche.

To visit Renaud's, the main location is off of Las Positas and State Street, however, there is a location within Gelson's (at the same intersection), mid-State Street at Arlington, and Montecito's Coast Village.

I'm extremely stoked that Handlebar Coffee Roaster's opened up a second location in Midtown/Upper State outside of downtown Santa Barbara.  For some time it has been known as the best coffee in town (sorry Santa Barbara Roasting Company).  The line out the door at it's original Cañon Perdido location does seem to prove this point.  After moving here from Seattle, I was happy to find a place with decent coffee that is made like an art.  The owners still roast their coffee biweekly on Mondays and Thursdays.  The new spot is humongous with a total of 4,000 square feet with plenty of spots to hop a squat and study (bring a charged laptop because there's next to no outlets--bummer!), meet up with a friend or listen to music while drinking a fabulous cup of coffee.  The owners are often present and super friendly and welcoming like their employees.  They take a moment to get to know you which keeps it local and intimate.  I'm so happy to have this location nearby to become my "go to caffeine fix."  Welcome to the neighborhood!

To start off the New Year of 2022, I figured I would write a review for a place I regularly visit and appreciate. Given the bags under my eyes and slight fatigue due to being up past my normal bedtime of 9 pm, I could go for a cup of their joe right about now!
While I do enjoy many coffee shops in town, Java Station often has a few perks that places it toward the top.
- Shorter line for friendly service
- Better food offerings
- Decent amount of parking and seating
- High speed Wi-Fi (not sure how this is possible in town)
- Welcoming to all (they celebrate Pride, Halloween and beyond)
- They have games available to play
- It brings a sense of community to an odd little neighborhood (What the heck is it considered?! Noleta? Or Hope Ranch Annex? ...Now we are just getting particular...)
I enjoy their Klatch Coffee Co. espresso which is bold without being acidic or underbearing. I often order the Oat Milk Vanilla Latte (yah, I'm basic), yet recently ordered a fall/winter special of Maple Bourbon Latte which I'm a big fan of. I will note that their "small" coffee is truly small, so order a medium if in doubt.
Now that I'm rambling due to a lack of sleep, I will adjourn...until a Review Update comes along!

I absolutely love and fully support mom 'n pop joints. Driving down Yanonali, it's easy to miss this "corner shop" within the Funk Zone. Weekdays are busy with workers from the surrounding businesses sitting on the outdoor patio making it a bit more noticeable. There is always the option to call in your order and beat the line. Otherwise, you order at the deli counter (menus available at register and counter), receive a table number, then pay at the register. Forewarning: Before standing in line, have your mind made because some staff members can be a bit impatient.

From the minute you step in the door, you'll easily be distracted by all the fun European products that stuff the grocery store. Breads, pastas, oils, sauces, and the list continues. Metropulos is the ideal place to create your own charcuterie board given the cuts of cheeses and meats at the deli.

If it is your first time, I recommend starting with a Gyro Sandwich. While I can't lie and say it's the best I've ever had--after all I am from Chicago, Home of  Greek Town--it is extremely well done with seasoned lamb sliced right off the spit. The pita is puffy and warm to the touch, with creamy tzatziki sauce and seasoned tomatoes, cucumbers, and onions. Opa!

They have a large selection of unique sandwiches, both hot and cold, to choose from. I am personally a fan of basic sandwiches like a BLT or the Pesto Chicken Sandwich. I love that I can add a side of deli salad to any sandwich; plus two soups a day are offered. They have a wonderful refrigerated case of freshly made salads. If there aren't already enough decisions to be made, don't miss out on the weekday specials:
Tuesdays - Annie's Banh Mi
Wednesday - Metro Tri-Tip
Thursdays - Metroburger
Fridays - Hawaiian Job

All of the above are to die for.
Metropulos is still open during the Covid-19 pandemic but with limited hours (Closed Sundays). Support local!

As many of us know, Habit Burger is truly a Central California institution.  It has put little Goleta on the map and continues to pump out delicious burgers out of its original location off Hollister Avenue. It takes me back to small towns across America where our generation would congregate at the local burger or ice cream joint. Whether it was Dairy Queen, Tasty Freeze, soda fountain, or Habit Burger, this occurrence is not to be forgotten.

When I get the craving for a burger, it's gotta be Habit. 
Sorry native Californians, In-n-Out ain't got nothing on The Habit!
The burgers come with multiple options of bun type (sourdough, lettuce or regular), toppings (avocado, onions-grilled or raw, tomato, lettuce, cheese, and the list goes on...). The meat patty is just the right thickness and full of flavor. It is one of the few places I don't feel obligated to get two patties to taste the meat. It was love at first bite!

The onion rings, WOAH! Perfectly breaded, crispy circles of Heaven.
Pair that with my other favorite, fried green beans, and you have a win-win. When I thought it doesn't get any better, it does. Dip those suckers into homemade Ranch dressing for a mouth-watering experience. After all, Santa Barbara is proudly the home of Hidden Valley Ranch...

Lastly, their shakes shake my world! The strawberry shake has legit real strawberries blended inside. Then they add on the thick and dreamy whipped cream as the cherry on top!

I sure love me some Habit Burger!

While looking at homes and planning my relocation to Santa Barbara, I happened upon this unassuming Mexican cocina in the city market.  A year and a half later, it was one of the deciding factors to relocate from Seattle (a Mexican food desert...) after 4 years of deprivation.  It was no surprise that a year later, it has grown by the addition of a dessert and helados stand next door.

One word describes Corazón Cocina: ¡Perfección! 
Corazón Cocina does EVERYTHING right.  From the first bite, you can tell that chef Ramón Velasquez, who started out his career with a Mexican food truck in in Tijuana, has poured his heart (perhaps a connection to the word 'corazón' in the name?) into his cuisine.  Freshness is key, and obvious, since everything is made at the time of ordering--note: well worth the wait.  Their menu has a diverse variety of food items (vegetarian and gluten-free friendly too) that are elevated from classic Mexican street food, yet all worth trying.  With each and every visit, I must start with the Guacamole of which has just the right amount of cilantro and is paired with freshly fried tortilla chips.  
My all time favorite item is La Chicana Quesadilla (wild shrimp, cheese, roasted corn, poblano pepper, crema, salsa and flour tortilla) that is far from your average quesadilla.  The goodies are placed on top of a homemade tortilla without sandwiching it between a second tortilla like you would expect.  Plus the shrimp, poblano and zesty salsa pair perfectly.
All the tacos are sold individually but stuffed to the max.  I salivate thinking of my two favorite tacos, Mole con Pollo (chicken, black almond mole, rice, onion mayo crema, cheese, tortilla) and Al Pastor (adobo pork, cilantro, salsa cruda, pickled habanero-pineapple salsa, tortilla).
Truly, you can't go wrong with anything on the menu.  As you can imagine, since moving to Santa Barbara, I have quickly become a regular.

A few tips:
-Come at odd hours to avoid a line since everything is made fresh.  Once you order, you'll be given a buzzer.
-Take advantage of the fresh salsa bar.  Keep in mind, that all the quesadillas and tacos come paired with the chef's choice of salsa on top.
-Two tacos and/or quesadillas per person is plenty of food, especially if you take my recommendation of ordering the quesadilla or another appetizer.
-If you have an Axxess card, take advantage of their discount.

Since moving to Santa Barbara, and later Goleta, I knew Old Town Goleta was on the move. I deem that Old Town Coffee (OTC) is the start to this transformation. I have been anxiously watching OTC prepare for opening day, which finally took place on 7/28/18. 

Besides Goleta Coffee Co. and The French Press, there are surprisingly few decent coffee options in this area. I'm so pleased with alllll OTC has to offer to make it the perfect coffee spot and make me a regular:
-Serving coffee from the "New Kid on the Block" Roaster called Rise Coffee Roasters. It's a perfectly bold and dark blend.
-Pastry selection with a random variety of breakfast sandwiches, empanadas (from Buena Onda!) and whatever else the owners get their hands on around town. They sell reasonably priced fruit and healthy snacks too!
-Rustic modern interior decor that is perfect for studying (a bar designated to laptop work with USB electric plugs) or just relaxing with your cup of joe and a newspaper.
-A large outdoor back patio with games including life-size Jenga, Bags/Corn Hole, and Table tennis.
-Extensive hours starting at 6 am on weekdays (even I can make it before starting work at 6:30 am) and going into the early evening; they also will pull all-nighter 24 hour shifts when UCSB has midterms and finals. 
-There's two stations with all the works including Simple Syrup, white and raw sugar and sugar alternatives. 
-They have a Community Bulletin Board listing current events in town to stay in the loop.

Welcome to the neighborhood OTC Tim & Rachael!

Awarded Review of the Day in Santa Barbara, California on 10/2/2018!

I have been told that my reviews are too wordy, yet quality and quantity are both important to me than poorly written, inconsistent, short reviews. So for the judgmental, here's some quick deets:
-They are open daily until 5 pm. (For coffee...see below for the after hours)
-They serve food and tapas that are created by Corazón Cocina and Sama Sama. 
-They are an eco-friendly and zero waste business resulting in no take-out disposable cups or boxes. You are encouraged to bring in your own mug or purchase a ceramic cup for $5 which you can trade in at a future visit or keep. Otherwise, stay for a bit.
-This location turns into a "speakeasy" called Social Lab starting at 5:30 pm. Entry is through The Mill back door with bands on some evenings.
-Parking isn't too tough on Haley Street, but keep in mind that it's usually limited to 90 minutes. Well behaved dogs are allow inside.

For those who appreciate a thorough review, read on:
After living several years in Seattle and Chicago, I consider myself a coffee snob. Sadly enough, Santa Barbara has settled for mediocre coffee beans, creations and foam art for far too long. Sorry locals but Handlebar isn't all that. Thankfully, Cajé has arrived to the forefront and has grown outside of Isla Vista for another round. I have stopped in several times and am already counting down to the next visit. 

The interior decor is fun with high speed WiFi and modern with a fair amount of seating. I absolutely love the succulent green wall! Staff is not always the most knowledgeable but very friendly nonetheless.

The coffee menu drinks tend to be a bit on the sweet side. My absolute favorite is the Burnout, but the Yemen is a close second. Each coffee creation takes so much time and care into making it with quite unique ingredients. They are always coming up with new concoctions though. Of course, you can order your average coffee beverage like a latte, americano, etc. with oat, coconut or almond milk. Plus, they make all their syrups in-house!

That's a wrap!

I suppose the third time is a charm! I have been here not one, not two, but three times and I'm finally giving it the 5-star review it deserves. The Lark embraces all things Santa Barbara with a beach town vibe, mock food truck (with a skeleton driver), string lights, gas lamps, plenty of foliage, and antique decor touches. While the majority of seating is outside on their patios shared with The Lucky Penny (due to Covid), there are several tables/booths inside which require a reservation. The bar unfortunately does not have stools, however, there is a communal social distanced seating option.

We were welcomed by the hostess and received a bowl of their homemade flavor-alternating popcorn (sweet lemon poppy). We were all ravenous and fighting over each and every kernel! The appetizers and salads came out quickly, even though there was a rush of people who arrived around 6 pm. I simply would come here JUST for small plates or "happy hour". If it is your first time here, don't miss out on their most popular items: Crispy Brussel Sprouts or The Garden Of Little Gems 'Wedge' Salad.

We wanted to try some new items this time around which could be shared communally (highly recommended approach!). Their salads are super fresh and tossed with local vegetables. We enjoyed the Ancient Grain Salad and Heirloom Tomato & Persian Cucumbers. Everything from the celery to the cucumbers was full of flavor! We continued with the Chilled Artichoke & Crab Dip and Steelhead Trout. Both were spectacular whether it was the homemade potato chips with dip piled on top, or the meaty, salmon-like trout with its tasty maitake mushrooms. We wrapped up with the Grilled Hanger Steak including blistered shishitos, oven-dried tomatoes, green chermoula, and bone marrow butter. EVERY single one of the dishes was sure to please.

All of our food items paired well with our creative mixologist cocktails and local bottle of Brave & Maiden Cabernet Sauvignon. If you're a wino, don't pass up their spectacular wine list that is overwhelmingly Californian wines. The manager Chris was extremely welcoming and checked on our table during our meal. He is super knowledgeable about wine pairings and helped us find the right bottle to choose for the table.
We spoiled ourselves with dessert which usually consists of a panna cotta, tres leches, or ice cream. I can tell why they have so few options since I was not previously a fan of either of the first two until I tried them out here!

If you're looking for a place to celebrate a special occassion or enjoy shared small plates, The Lake is a wonderful choice. You may get lucky enough to see a celebrity...

I'm bummed to have to leave a less than stellar rating, particularly with all the anticipation I had behind trying Secret Bao and the current COVID lockdowns hurting small businesses. As with most "pop-ups," I followed the steps of ordering ahead online, paying electronically, and picking it up in person at Handlebar Coffee off De La Vina. I had witnessed their weekly special of the Breakfast Bao on Instagram and was stoked. I also added on a second Bao, Salmon & Lox, to fill me up. 

Upon arrival, the gal who found and handed over my order by viewing my electronic receipt was friendly. I passed on plastic to-go silverware since I knew this is meant to be finger food. It was when I opened up the box to find two fairly small baos that cost $14.05 all soggy, wet, not super presentable and cold. I arrived at my requested time of 9:30 am and they may have prepared it a bit on the early side? Perhaps? I get that food cools with time, so I was more disappointed in them sitting in their own juices and over sauced causing them to be gooey. Santa Barbara lags behind on the food front--particularly given my past of residing in Chicago and Seattle where Asian food excels. Nonetheless, these baos were extremely underwhelming. Great concept, wonderful collaboration of local businesses, disappointing product.

I am sad to admit that Santa Barbara is quite limited on the front of cultural diversity. Thankfully, however, we have places like Lokum popping up like spring flowers! The folks that run this coffee shop and bakery also own Seven Hills Saratoga Turkish Imports & Bazaar (yelp.com/biz/seven-hills...) a few shops down State Street. You can't miss seeing Lokum since it stands out with extraordinary chandeliers and lamps, patterned tile floors, and canned Turkish coffee from floor to ceiling.

I met my fellow coworker and Santa Barbara Community Ambassador predecessor Dani N here for coffee and a chat. Lokum offers four various coffee flavors at $5 a cup including the original wood-fired, hazelnut, mastic (aromatic gum), and Ottoman (for a slightly higher price of $7). The coffee arrives at your table in a tiny cup with the option of sugar, a small cup of water and two cubed Turkish Delight samples. Of course, I had to choose an additional treat to enjoy with my coffee given their endless selection of Turkish Delights and Baklava. I went with the "crunchy, juicy pistachio" Baklava, as described by the employee. He did not steer me wrong! It was exactly just that.

I learned that Lokum is another word for Turkish Delight. If you're not familiar, it is "a family of confections based on a gel of starch and sugar. Premium varieties consist largely of chopped dates, pistachios, and hazelnuts or walnuts bound by the gel; traditional varieties are often flavored with rosewater, mastic, Bergamot orange, or lemon" (thanks Wikipedia!). I'm huge on texture but did give it a try, however, I prefer the Baklava.

I "cultured" Dani a bit by having us flip over our cups and follow a specific process of reading one's Turkish coffee grounds fortune. We really had no idea what we were doing truthfully but whether there is a complete vs. incomplete circle, or any letters, symbols or numbers remaining inside the cup's coffee grounds tells us something.

While nothing inside this store is inexpensive, it is an exciting new place to check out in downtown Santa Barbara. It is said that they import fresh all the coffee and treats, so it's no surprise the prices a bit high.

For all the Yelpers out there that are: Gluten-free, Lactose-free, Ketogenic, Vegetarian and/or simply fans of any and all Latin foods like myself, be sure to stop in to Cuernavaca. They offer dine-in (the inside is much larger than it appears) and take-out. Note: The parking lot is limited so you may have to park on the side streets.

Interestingly enough, the menu has an unfamiliar item that you can't find at a "traditional" Mexican spot. Of course you can indulge yourself in the classics like tacos, tortas and gorditas. However, as the name indicates, they serve a central Mexican delicacy called an "Alambre," reigning from the Morelos capital of Cuernavaca. I would compare the Alambre to a skillet where they chop ingredients and toss them into a pan to cook. Each Alambre is customizable withy our choice of meat (ham, steak, chicken, chorizo, and/or pork chop), in addition to multiple additions such as cheese, onion, bell pepper, pineapple, mushrooms and avocado. The alambre comes with homemade corn tortillas that are piping hot and ready for some taco making with chopped cilantro, onions, lime and/or salsa. Oh and did I say I truly live for their avocado salsa?! Bravo, Cuernavaca!

In true celebration of Latinx Heritage Month, I will continue to Yelp local Latinx businesses...

I couldn't agree more with my fellow Elite Eric G's statement: "Mexican fare with true flair."
Whenever I find myself craving Mexican cuisine, I simply need to listen to my intuition and go to Los Agaves off De La Vina. I've been to other competitors (and sadly other Los Agaves locations) throughout town, and nothing can compare. A few examples of what makes this particular Los Agaves stand out:
- Fresh and well-maintained salsa bar with a variety of not only chiles used but stellar flavors and complexity; these paired with their delicate, golden, warm tortillas chips = HEAVEN! Half the time I fill up on chips and salsa alone...
- Unlimited chopped cilantro (yes, you heard that right. I'm a cilantro addict!)
- Seafood does not taste like it came out of the sea and sat on a pier and then in a truck in the sun; Nor is the seafood over or undercooked.
- Hands down amazing margarita recipes with delicious flavors available (Jamaica, Mango Pineapple, Tamarindo con Chile, Blood Orange & House); not to mention they are $7 daily during Happy Hours 11 am - 5 pm.
- All of their enchilada sauces are spectacular! I will say that their chipotle one used on the seafood burrito and enchiladas is my ultimate favorite, however.
- They offer a molcajete for dine-in. Enough said!
- All of their entrees are not only delicious and perfected, but the portions are humungous to last me two to three meals. A few of my favorites are: Chiles Norteños, Agaves Enchiladas & Burrito, Enchiladas Suizas, and Burrito Mojado. Basically you can't go wrong with anything on the menu and there is something for everyone in the family.
- Their take-out service is impeccable with an employee solely dedicated to it and a separate area for payment and pick-up.
- Lastly, this is where the hard-working, super attentive manager Amador works. He somehow makes everything inside run smoothly and efficiently, no matter how busy they are.
I always--and will always--recommend Los Agaves (the De La Vina location, or their sister restaurant Santo Mezcal: https://bit.ly/3koZhc4)!

Cristino's is a like finding a diamond in the rough. Amidst industrial warehouses and the airport lies this bakery as part of a quiet strip mall. Yet, the parking lot is always mysteriously full as workmen pull up to purchase their morning coffee, Mexican pastry/"pan" or breakfast burrito. Stepping in here, I feel as if I have flown to a small Mexican panadería. It brings back memories of being a high school student when I was referred to as a "Watino" because although I'm White, I always sat and felt a sense of belonging with the Latinos. [Now the world knows why my nickname on my Yelp profile is "Watino"]. The gal at the cash register is super friendly, smiley and always prefers to speak English with me, even though I respond in her native language of Spanish. I don't mind a bit because we both get to practice our secondary language skills with one another. Now here's why I truthfully come here:

TAMALES:
Most people are unaware, but they make and sell tamales here. Often run out, but if you're lucky, grab one of each. They carry a green salsa with chicken, red salsa with pork and rajas with cheese. You can't go wrong with any of them--especially if you like a kick of spice and just the right amount of masa. This is crucial.

MEXICAN "PAN":
Yep, they make some legit Mexican bread and pastries. They make all the different varieties, many similar in texture and sugar coated, but offering different fillings. The texture is just right here with a crispy outside and soft/warm inside. Never stale, like I've experienced at other bakeries. I love the "conchas" with both chocolate and white sugar on top! Then of course the crispy "palmeras" that look like palm leaves or butterflies, similar to an American elephant ear without the cinnamon.

COCA MEXICANA:
Many folks don't know but the Mexican Coca Cola in the jade glass bottle is 100 times more delicious being made with natural sugar, versus the American version with corn syrup. I also prefer the smaller amount of carbonation. They carry it in the refrigerator with juices, flan, and Jarritos.

Believe it or not, I always come here first thing in the morning to get the first pick. However, I continue to tell myself to come here for lunch because they offer various sandwiches that sound delicious according to the other Yelpers!

Now listen closely Cristino's: I want you to succeed so I exposing you to the Yelposphere, but please succumb to any changes. I like you just the way you are!

My partner and I ordered take-out from Masala Spice for Yelp's Big Night In on April 11, 2020. I had previously received in the local newspaper that they were offering free delivery within 4 miles of the restaurant, however, when I called they said only pick-up is available. Bummer! Nonetheless, after I returned home with my food and dug in, I was loving all the flavors!

We ordered the following:
- Butter Chicken: It's that staple that I have to always order and judge an Indian place by. While I thought Tamira downtown was better (bless its heart given it has closed), there was plenty of chicken to sauce ratio, it was the right color without being oddly pink, and the creaminess was perfection.
- Samosas: Another must-have. Fried, crispy pastry stuffed with spiced potato and peas. Plenty of flavor and goodies inside with the delicious pairing of mint and tamarind chutneys.
- Cauliflower Bezul: This was something new I tried after seeing other Yelper's photos; and they did not lead me wrong! Crispy fried cauliflower florets with coconut milk sauce that was delectable and a new favorite.
- Fig Walnut Kofta: This was another new winner after reading the description on the menu. Fig and walnut stuffed paneer dumplings served in aromatic sauce that had a slight kick but was super flavorful. The little paneer dumplings were fluffy and a delight.
- Naan: They have a fun variety of naan available that are all eggless (butter, garlic, basil pesto and lemon pepper; $3.25). Not to mention, they also have stuffed naan of goat cheese, onion, paneer cheese, bacon, mushroom, potato, lamb keema or kashmiri; $4. All of the above sound amazing and are the same price. We stayed basic with garlic naan, but it was perfectly fluffy and still warm. They also have a long list of Dosas too to choose from if that's your thing.

This is one of the few places I would easily consider eating free of meat! For all the vegetarians and vegans out there, they have a large selection of delicious options. I hope to try the Avocado Bhel and Tandoori Artichoke Hearts next time. If you do go for meat, they use halal meats. Even better yet, they're open 7 days a week for when you get an Indian craving.

I came in from out of town to have dinner with local family members. We arrived at 6:30 and were promptly seated. Service started off well enough, but towards the end of the night went downhill quickly. Around 9:30 the restaurant was pretty empty and the waitstaff and bus boys gathered in a group in the dining group pretty much staring us down, waiting on us to leave I guess. The closing time is listed as 10pm, so we didn't think much about it and continued to enjoy our drinks and conversation. 

It was then when one of the guys turned on a bright spotlight and turned it on our table, startling and blinding us! Thinking it was an accident, we asked them to shut it off, which they refused. My uncle got up and shut it off. After seating himself again, the staff AGAIN turned the light on our table, blinding us. We left of course, which is what they wanted. The staff wanted to close and leave work early, so they harassed us 1/2 hr before closing until we did. 

Our table consisted of 6 polite adults, no children, and no rowdiness. Just a family catching up after a few years and enjoying a meal and drinks together. The unprecedented rudeness of the waitstaff was unbelievable to everyone at the table. My local family are regulars,  but said they would never eat there again. I don't blame them.

You asked for a brewery, Fishers, and you lucked out with Four Day Ray.  This spot pulled out all of the stops when building this brewery/gastropub.  You can tell from the moment you walk through the doors.  No small detail was overlooked here, that's for sure.

If I'm going to venture up to FDR, I'm coming first and foremost for the beer.  The Coffee Blonde has been one of my favorite sips this year, and the Track Jumper IPA is pretty stellar too.  I believe FDR has a firm grasp on their brew process, and I look forward to trying more of their beers.  The food hasn't blown my mind yet, but I do think there are several dishes worth a try, like the candied pork belly, stout my onion soup, and two-bacon BBQ cheeseburger. (S/O for using Fair Oaks cheddar cheese!)  I know these are safer options, which is why the next time I'm going to take a risk with the scallops.

As long as Four Day Ray continues to brew hoppiness, I'll keep coming back for more!

10 tips before dining at Mississippi Belle:

(01) Make sure your stomach is empty before coming, and make no plans to eat afterwards.  This meal will stuff you to the brim.  My pick: Sunday lunch.
(02) Wear stretchy pants and leave your belt at home.  Portion control does not exist here.
(03) Do not be dismayed by the decor and the vinyl table cloths and seats.  Do you come to a restaurant to gawk over the interior?  No, you come to eat the food!
(04) Bring friends.  Although you order your own meat, you share the sides, and all of the food comes with free refills.
(05) Do not bring any friends who are on a "health kick".  There is virtually nothing on the menu for them, and they will be horrified by the "unhealthy" options.
(06) Meatloaf is a fine choice.  The beef combined with the bits of veg. are super moist and saturated in a tangy red sauce.  It's just as good, if not better, than mom's.
(07) It is perfectly acceptable to order both the mashed potatoes and sweet potatoes during your visit.  Both contain butter and love and more butter.
(08) Do not be ashamed to ask for a refill of everything.  Delicious home-cooking deserves to be properly appreciated. 
(09) Try to save room for dessert, but know that there's no chance that will happen, because you will eat enough of it in sweet potatoes.
(10) Fit in a post-meal nap, because you're bound to go into a food coma, and remember that you can always go for a run tomorrow.

I've been monitoring Crispy Bird's Yelp reviews, thinking, "What the cluck is going on?"  The Hoosiers have been hatin' for sure.  I was intrigued to see what's cooking.

My friends and I shared:
-Buttermilk biscuits
-Mini pork tenderloin sandwiches
-Grits
-Twice baked potato
-Mac n' cheese
-Black eyed peas

Of these shareables, the black eyed peas were the overall favorite.  They've got a nice kick to them.  The buttermilk biscuits were the least favorite.  The mac n' cheese, while rich, is pretty awesome too.

I'm on a vegetarian kick, so I did not get the fried chicken.  Instead, I had the Nashville cauliflower.  WOWZA!  Crispy Bird puts an entire head on the plate.  Include the pickles and the meyer lemon aioli, and you've got a trifecta of flavors. 

All in all, I'm on Team Crispy Bird, and I hope that the 3-star average doesn't deter folks from coming.  Check it out.  Bring friends.  Try a little bit of everything.  Include the black eyed peas.

I like the concept, I like the hospitality, and--most importantly--I like the milkshakes.  Where I hesitate is the price.  I don't mind shelling out $8 for a milkshake, but when I can see the ingredients through the clear glass and the brands that are being used to create this sweet treat...it's more of a $5 milkshake.  It's easier for me to justify paying more money for a premium product, but that's not the case at Gordon's.  Then I'm reminded of a bigger issue here: the price of the milkshake is likely because of how much it costs to operate a business on Mass Ave.  While I want local businesses to dominate the landscape, I also want to get my money's worth.  Overall, I feel conflicted.  

I have a feeling this won't be the only time the price is brought up on this Yelp business page, and I hope that as this business figures out the ebbs and flows of being on Mass Ave, their products and prices will reflect that.  Until then, I know I'll return again with my favorite 11 year-old, and I'll let her order whatever she wants, even if that means I'll shell out a few extra dollars in the process. As for me though: I won't be ordering a milkshake.

There's no need to hunt Chef Dan down in his food truck anymore.  He's set up shop on the main drag in Irvington, and I am THRILLED!  

The number one reason you need to visit Chef Dan's is the authenticity.  Everything inside the restaurant screams Bayou, from the decor to--more importantly--the food.  When you're cooking your Southern grandmother's recipes in your restaurant, you're doing something right.  

Chef Dan divides his menu into two sections: "Mississippi" and "Louisiana".  I went the Louisiana route with a bowl of red beans and rice, Cajun squash and zucchini, and banana pudding.  I can sum up my meal in one word: WOWZA!  My main and side were both well-seasoned with Cajun spices without being overpowering.  The banana pudding was straightforward yet fantastic, especially because of the vanilla wafers and sliced bananas.  I licked my bowls clean!  

Walking out of Chef Dan's I made a mental list of dishes I need to try on my next visit.  It may have been my first time there but it was definitely not my last!

Ask me my thoughts on Open Society, and I'll start with, "it depends on the time of day".

You'll find me here in the morning for sure, sipping my coffee and nibbling on a thumbprint cookie.  As a spot to co-work or co-ffee date, Open Society is without a doubt a five-star spot.  I couldn't say nicer things about the space, well-trained baristas, and--most importantly--the beverages. (Try the shakerato)

You might just find me at Open Society in the afternoon as well.  The ambiance stays low key, and the ladies' plates at the table next to me may motivate me to order lunch.  I'll take a break from typing on my laptop to savor a Latin-inspired brisket sandwich topped with an over-easy egg.  Better yet, there's a bed of shoestring potatoes to nosh on between my sandwich.  I'll be thankful I stayed for a hearty lunch.

When won't you find me at Open Society then?  Ordering small plates at dinner.  I wouldn't say the food is bad - it's simply nothing to write home about.  My scallops were a tad on the rubbery side and my meatballs reminded me of something from GFS.  Luckily there was a goat-cheese/potato chip combination in the salad, giving me a nod to at least one dish.  To sum it up, I found my four selections pretty underwhelming in comparison to the scrumptious baked goods and outstanding drinks.  When you've got an outstanding spot by day, you come to expect the same at night.  For me, the beer and wine can't carry Open Society's dinner eats.

I'll be back soon enough, slinging my laptop on a table eager to work over a cup of Madcap and a scone.  There's a good thing going at Open Society, and I know just the right time to enjoy it.

This one is to all the haters out there...

Sorry to disappoint you if you think I'm about to ramble off some song lyrics.  I'm not THAT creative.  Actually, I'm updating my review because I've received a great deal of hate mail for loving Bent Rail so much. "Did they pay you to write that?" "Are you related to someone who works there?"

Psh, I wish, because I probably would have access to awesome food more often.

I get it.  Bent Rail is not brewing their own beer yet.  If you think you're frustrated by this fact, try being on the other side of the bar trying to explain that to customers 11 times a day.  There is no doubt that it's disappointing that we're not guzzling some exceptional ales yet, and no one feels that more than the staff.  However, I think what we're forgetting is that Bent Rail sells some quality beer from breweries at the local level and around the Midwest (i.e. Outliers, Sun King, Schafly, Dark Horse, Bloomington Brewing, Founder's).  In addition, they've hosted two tappings of some exclusive Founder's beer (KBS, Devil Dancer).  That effort to provide "the next best thing" and go the extra mile has to count for something.

Best of all, they're pairing the beer on tap and in cans with some terrific sandwiches.  Have you been lucky enough to gorge a Roast Beef Brisket with horseradish cream, caramelized onions, dijon aioli, and white cheddar?  How about going into a food coma after demolishing a Pork Belly Banh Mi with Smoking Goose kitchen sausage, pickled daikon, carrots, garlic aioli, and jalapeños?  Or perhaps you've sunk your teeth into the Tre Oche Panini, a pile of cured meats, house pickled vegetables, hot peppers, cambozola cheese, and garlic aioli pressed to perfection.  Not to mention the daily specials that Travis surprises us with, whether it be fried catfish, mussels, gyros, or noodle bowls.  I have yet to be disappointed with anything served to me, and I doubt that will change knowing who is behind the menu.

So the road to Bent Rail has not been a smooth one.  Welcome to the real world.  I say we ride it out just a little bit longer and enjoy what's coming off the taps and panini maker until then.  Besides, our patience will only bring great things aka superb craft beer.

Let's talk about the backstory of Love Handle:

This is not the first Love Handle to open.  In fact, the first Love Handle (under the same ownership of Chris and Allie) was established in Milwaukee.  Having friends up in MKE, I know for a fact that Love Handle was considered a beloved hipster sandwich shop because of their high-quality, creative combinations.  When Love Handle chose to close its doors in February 2015 because Chris and Allie were moving back to Indy, patrons were devastated.  Where were they going to immerse their mouths in layers of delicatessen greatness?

Sorry, Milwaukee.  Your loss is Indianapolis' gain.

What exactly have we gained?  A hip, progressive, breakfast and lunch menu.  Chioggia Beet & Hot Pepper Biscuits & Gravy.  Duck Fat Popcorn.  Beef Tendon Noodle.  Sandwiches of epic foodie proportions, like Yanni B's slices of smoked pork heart, sour turnips & a spicy creamy spread.  Miso Ovaltine Sweet Rolls.  This is the type of menu that belongs in the ranks of popular Indy hot spots like Milktooth and Bluebeard.  The food is UH-MAZING and the people are wonderful.

But here's the thing.  Love Handle hasn't become mainstream yet.  It doesn't require you to tailgate outside of your car while you wait over an hour to to get in.  With a spot that hasn't been "discovered" yet means I have access to the best shit on the Eastside without the fighting the foodie crowds.  I'll be taking full advantage of this, and I suggest you do too before the cool kids make it their new destination.

Just as I was about to drive past Paco's for the 900th time, I thought it was about time that I checked out this taqueria.  I was expecting more of a hole in the wall, but the interior is pretty neat with all of the vibrant artwork splashed on the walls.  My stomach was growling for tacos, and luckily there is a 3-taco meal for only $6.50, in which you can mix and match your meats.  Therefore, I chose the carnitas, chicken, and al pastor in addition to the beans.  

I can't believe I'm leading in with this, but I can't get over how much I love, love, LOVE Paco's refried beans.  Yes, you read that right: I'm obsessed with the BEANS.  That little styrofoam cup of brown mush has a kick of seasoned heat to them, and I'll be returning just to analyze what's all mashed inside that little magical masterpiece.  You can't forget to include them in your order!

The beans weren't the only thing I reveled in - Paco's seems to know their way inside a tortilla most of the time.  Of the three I ate, I most enjoyed the al pastor.  The meat's marinade was on point, and the addition of fresh (!) pineapple really sealed the deal for me.  Many people rave about the carnitas, and while I thought it was tender, my meat needed a touch of salt or a drizzle of salsa with it (I didn't see that there were bottles floating around until I had finished my meal).  The chicken...will not be ordered again.  It was on the dry side, and I was underwhelmed with the lack of seasoning too. (Note to self: stop ordering chicken tacos all together!)

I'm not going to complain too much because I'd rather you remember that the al pastor and refried beans are two tasty reasons not to bypass Paco's Tacqueria any longer.  I will be back again!
That hot fried chicken and corn cake gave me life and the fried pickles they are a must!!!! Great choice as we were looking for a good Tennessee eating spot.

Very attentive service... Bruschetta was overpowered with garlic . Jalapeños poppers were decent.... mac was bland and runny . Ordered the steak medium it was over cooked and tough..... Creme Brulee top was like plate glass....way to hard . Oh ...not to mention old red wine . But as I said .... Good service. Also when I placed my reservation they asked if it was a special occasion which i stated its was my wife's birthday. Did they even mention it while at dinner ....  BIG FAT ....HELL NO !!!! Save your money and time .

I wish I could give 2.5. The food gets 5 stars. Interacting with the owner gets 0 stars.

Authenticity Questioned at Locally Grown Gardens:

"Ron Harris has made Locally Grown Gardens into a collection of what's best in life, culled from a lifetime of caring deeply about ingredients, aesthetics and community. And pie."
-- Katherine Coplen, Nuvo

As a Locally Grown Garden's patron, I greatly question Ron Harris's deep caring for community. I am disappointed in my interpersonal experience with the owner of Locally Grown Gardens as I now see through the warm inviting façade of an open relaxed atmosphere plentied with open smiles & Reggae music and now I realize the true urbane condescension and inaccessibility that one sadly identifies with upper class food movements. I want to be a part of an authentic food scene that serves from the land, communicates from the heart, and invites people to communally enjoy in delectable meals. 

Today, as I waited an hour for the LGG kitchen to open for lunch (and my salmon filet with LGG coleslaw!), I alone in the sunroom, typing on my laptop, with a purchased LGG coffee and an apple, with everything else including my coat bundled into my bag was greeted by a rude comment from Ron. His opening remark to me was to put my laptop away and that, "LGG is neither Starbucks nor Paneras." 

I, Immediately, wanting to be respectful put the laptop away but felt suddenly unwelcomed and demeaned by the tone of voice and unsaid implications by Ron's comment. I expressed to him that I frequent his business often in my short time having very recently moved from Portland, OR, and wondered why he felt the right to chide me instead of speaking to me with mutual respect and integrity? He merely insisted that LGG is not a lounge and by me acting as such he was authorized to be unkind and rude to me because in his eyes I had disrespected his establishment - even though no earlier hints had been given by the kind cashier who sold me coffee had offered me water as I typed on my laptop.

I support the work of LGG but I would greatly encourage them to review their interest in sustaining relationships with those in the community. Respectful communication is a great way to begin that dialogue. Setting clear expectations with signs or a heads up from the cashier would be a great way for them to allow others to know how to operate within their space. Boundaries are important and should be clear to all parties. Local Sustainable Food should support Sustainable Community relationships which, disappointingly, is not my experience with Locally Grown Gardens. Just a week ago I returned to the states from Portugal and I am I reminded by the terseness in which people operate food establishments here where community is not first but business is.

It's worth the hype! It's worth the wait! 

Upon my visit to Hattie B's, I went to three other places for hot chicken. I thought all was good until I ate a piece of Hatties. I told my friend, now this is what HOT CHICKEN is suppose to taste like. WOW, it was juicy, flavorful, crispy and just amazing. The others places did not compare at all. 

I got the Nashville hot. Perfect for me. But my friend thought it was too spicy for her. She got mild. As for the sides, mac and cheese was so good and fries too. Everything was just great. Finished my whole meal. I wish I ordered the banana pudding or peach clobber. Now I need to make a visit back to Nashville just for HATTIE! 

I was here on a holiday Monday, President day around 11:15am. It was about a 50 min wait. Since they open at 11, I think its better to arrive after 12 or later. Because when we left around 1, there wasn't much of a line. I did hear on weekends it gets crazy long, therefore I recommend going on a weekday if possible.

The best fried chicken I ever had. Flavorful, moist, simply cooked to perfection. My favorite meal in my four day visit. I wish you open one in San Francisco! 

My friend and I arrived at the restaurant around 6:15pm and got seated right away. We didn't mind being outside, even in 89 degrees weather. The outdoor seating was not in the sun, which was perfect! From what I see, its communal tables, unless you go with a big party. Didn't mind it at all. 

Ordered: 
*Half Fried Chicken: Amazing! Comes with breast, thigh, drum and wing. It comes with their special honey (a little spicy) but the chicken had enough flavor that I didn't even use it.  
*Mac and Cheese: Delicious. Cheesy, tasty, plus I added bacon, for extra crunch and flavor. 
*Corn Bread: It was good because it was not dry, baked with real corn. 
*Kale Salad: Love that they added apples and the dressing was refreshing. 

Everything was delicious, service was quick and friendly. They kept the ice water coming. It was hot!

I have brought over 100 people into Muriel's this year alone and never meaningfully interacted with the owner--before now. I used to find the environment enjoyable, and their cocktails are actually quite good, so I'd take my friends from out of town there for drinks and snap a few pictures of them in the restaurant's upstairs lounge. Most of them would come back for dinner afterwards and go on to rave online about their positive experience.

However, today I had a friend visiting who has a service dog, since he can't see out of his left eye. The dog keeps him from knocking stuff over and tripping on unseen objects.

The owner saw me photographing him and his girlfriend upstairs and rudely confronted me about it, then asked us to leave while pointing her finger as if we were vagrants. She said she didn't allow photoshoots there--which was strange as she had literally seen me talking pictures of another friend not 4 days earlier--and told us we had to leave "now."

Being a reasonable person, I apologized and explained that I wasn't aware it would offend her to have people taking photographs in her restaurant, and I offered to compensate her for each photograph taken in her restaurant going forward or rent out the upstairs area. She proceeded to tell me that I "couldn't afford it" and that she didn't believe that my friends service dog was actually a service dog. Her attitude in the face of a genuine apology was reprehensible.

I won't be coming back ever again, and I won't be recommending Muriel's to anyone either. For the price, there are better restaurants in town--restaurants that respect customers with disabilities *and* money to spend.
The most racist establishment I've been to. Don't even waste your time. Unless you are white with money they will pay no mind to you. The food was underwhelming, and overpriced.

Walking into this place you think wow.  Cool decor. Very open and welcoming. Great place to dine. 
The menu is thought out and we saw many menu items we were interested in. Including Dutch style breakfast served all day. The food when we got it and all finally had our plates in front of us. I stared at mine awkwardly for a good five minutes before two other entries came and another good 5 mins waiting for our last friend to receive his entree. 
Two Cobb salads looked absolutely appealing and fresh. My Indonesians fried rice with fried egg on top accompanied by a peanut sauce, some kind of fried puff chip and cabbage -the entree was great. (If you like a big pile of rice with bits of ham and some spice ...which I do.)  the pork chop was done perfect. 
So ambiance is 5 stars
Food is 5 stars 

Here is why it gets 2 stars. 

They sat my group (4 in total) right before a large group totaling 12 to 14 people (not gonna be that detailed) same waiter as us.  
I asked waiter to explain menu items. Waiter was short and not informative about products in menu items that are not explained in English. 
2 of us decided on the house made spinach Alfredo to be told the restaurant was not serving that menu item at that moment. Waiter treated us like we were an inconvenience for not knowing Dutch or knowing what menu items were not being served for the day. 
We were bummed.  The Alfredo looked good  (Obviously must be since they're are out.)
That's when we started asking about other menu items and we got nothing. Luckily I chose an alternative that was good but it would've been nice to know what the sides were all about. 
I asked for a coffee last minute. Obviously that flew out the window. I never got it. 
What the biggest fault is: either the waiter didn't ask for help or the others working around him let him flounder. 
Once he left our table after ordering, we were given zero service and trying to wave down anyone else who walked by us (many times.) either blatantly looked away or are that spacey? Dunno. 

At the end of our meals is when we were paid attention to and finally started getting refills. Too late at that moment. We tipped the waiter 20% only because that is how we roll and once we got all our food.  The food itself is fantastic. 

Do I recommend this place? Will we be back? 
Sadly and disappointedly, no. 

The low rating at this place is a warning as to what to expect. It is sad because  service should be the easiest to get 5 stars on. 

If you need help to right your services issue. I'd be glad to help constructively and positively impact your business by sitting down with your staff. 

mic drop

2nd time updating my review and YAS! Korea House really stepped up!

I had bibimbab lunch special today and I cannot complain at all. Side dishes were amazing and something new I noticed is that now they give you a bowl of miso soup with your bibimbab. I like my egg fried hard and they did accommodate. They were pretty packed for lunch so I was glad to see that this restaurant is doing well during this unprecedented time. 

One thing I want to tell the management of the restaurant: PLEASE have more than just one server at a time! I felt so sorry for the server as he was the only one who was taking care of customers, checks, phone and pretty much everything. I was not mad that it took a while to get seated and order my food as I saw him flying down the hall taking care of other customers.

Such a great dining experience I had last night at La Carreta... The service was by far the best in town among all the restaurants I have been to lately AND they were packed! Our waiter, Leonardo, as well as other waiters and who seemed to be the manager, so nice and came over to the table multiple times to make sure everything was all good. 

We had skinny margaritas, ceviche and chicken fajita and everything was top notch. Their price point is very reasonable compared to other neighborhood Mexican joints. The bar is actually a converted truck and it was very eye-catching; brilliant idea! The atmosphere at this restaurant is something that I do look for when looking for a place to dine/drink on Friday night. According to their board on the wall, they have some sort of happy hour going on everyday so that is a plus always. 

I highly highly recommend this joint so stop by when you are on Magazine street folks!

I just had a lunch at Singha and as I was checking in on Yelp, I was like "Wait a minute... I left them 2 stars?" I totally forgot to update my review! I have come here multiple times after not-so-great experience and whole a lot has changed. 

First the service has improved significantly. Today it was just as packed and busy as the last time I came and left unpleasant. It is Thursday lunch time so definitely expected. But we were promptly seated and I saw that there were definitely more employees working on premises. Without surprise, they took our order fast, the orders came out in order and quick. Food all came out boiling hot, not cold! 

I also must add that portion seemed to change as well. Last time, I thought lunch was a deal according to their lunch menu price yet when the food came out, it was "you get what you paid for" lesson learned. But today, lunch special entree was pretty decent size. Left the premises happy plate and happy belly. 

I am so sorry that it took me so long to update my review on this restaurant. Now I might need to add this joint on my calendar as my weekly ritual...

After just returning from NYC, where I ended up having disappointing cupcakes from both Magnolia and Crumbs, I was skeptical to say the least when I happened upon Philly Cupcake. 

I happened upon the bakery while heading home from a trip to Macy's, as the cute decor lured me in. However,  I told the owner (i assume) and 2 other workers that since I'm a self-proclaimed cupcake aficionado, I  had to check this place out and determine it's worthiness.  I even offered to taste it out in front of them, and give them my honest opinion (i feel constructive criticism is imperative- esp. when dealing w/ a new bakery), and they eagerly accepted. 

I took my first bite and the cupcake (I kept with the basics and had vanilla w/ Choc) and was pleasantly  surprised. It was delightful, in fact! The cake actually had a caramelized, crunchy top and a moist, dense cake. Less dense than Brown Betty though. The icing was creamy and not overly sweet, and I thought the ratio of cupcake to icing was spot on. It was unlike any other cupcake I had ever tried, and that's nearly impossible to achieve since we're talking about cupcakes here.  

Though they are smaller  that the average cupcake, they are so delicious and filling, you only need a few bites. I felt the $3 price is a bit too steep for Philly, however, and would make more sense to charge no more than $2.75. The high price is probably a good thing though, as I will make less visits. 

I tried taking my nieces there, as  they were in town for the holidays, but we were greatly disappointed to find them closed on a Monday, with no hours of operation sign posted. All my nieces talked about all day was getting a "Philly Cupcake" :-(  Hoping they hire more staff soon so they can be open daily.  This place is a fantastic new addition to the city and I wish them well!

Found this spot on Yelp that was full of 5-star reviews and decided to give it a try. Oh man! What a perfect find! We were on a mission for tacos and margaritas and this place nailed it! 

The staff was super friendly as soon as we entered. The gentleman was flattered that we found them on Yelp. Even though we had a specific server, the staff really worked well together to make sure guests were tended to. We appreciated the complimentary hand sanitizer offered by the entry.

The margaritas were flavorful and strong so be prepared. I ordered a 12-oz raspberry on the rocks and my boyfriend ordered an 18-oz mango on the rocks. The prefect blend of flavor and tequila! We were definitely feeling these drinks!

We each tried a sampler of tacos after polishing off our complimentary chips and salsa. I ordered 2 chorizo and 1 shrimp taco. My boyfriend ordered 2 pastor and 2 arabe tacos. I love that they came on the little taco holders and not lying in the plate where the filling could fall everywhere. Hats off to the the chef because these were LEGIT!!
