They doubled up on the corn tortillas so there was mess-free enjoyment. Our tacos were so FULL to the brim of meat. The shrimps were large and the chorizo was plentiful. My boyfriend said that the pastor and arabe were on point, too.

Overall, it was clean, friendly, and worth the stop. We already plan to go back and make time for the margarita pitchers next time. Enjoy!

OK, so it was the second (actually third if you count take out) time at Han Dynasty and it gets better every time.  Han remembered us from the Yelp UYE so of course we got the VIP treatment.................. well, OK, I'm exaggerating a little because Han treats everyone like a VIP.   But he did remember the UYE and even remembered what we ate that night.  

Again I relied on Han to make his expert opinion on what we should order and again we hit a grand slam.  Han first recommended a cold chicken in hot sauce dish that I was tentative to order (because I'm not a huge fan of cold dishes).  But we went with his suggestion and it was perfect.  The chicken, although cold, was light and prepared to perfection (not chewy or dry) and melted in our mouths like butter.  The chicken was mildly hot (spicy) but was leveled out by the nutty sauce it was served in.  

Han also recommended the Meat Buns (based on our raving about Dim Sum Gardens "soup dumplings").  These tasty little (lol!.... not) dumplings were also filled with some soupy flavors but had a little more meat then the favorites we described.  The dipping sauce provided (like a soy sauce) was perfect because it added a sugary flavor to balance some of the bitter flavors present in most soy sauces.  

Our entree was not even on the menu.  As Han was digging our brains for a dish we could brag about he came up with a favorite of his which was ".... a special fish dish" as explained by Han.  He went to the kitchen and whipped up this fabulous fish dish that was lightly flowered and fried, but not a heavy frying.  It was the perfect, slightly crusty on the outside and flaky and light on the inside (it's amazing how food that is fried properly isn't greasy or heavy).  

Finally, I have to say that after thinking about what makes Han Dynasty so awesome is........................ well, Han himself.  He is so honest and outgoing that it permeates your fears of new foods and lets you experience the greatness of honest Chinese food.  It's amazing how the soul and heart of a chef is evident in their food and their service.  Han himself is a 5 star +,  and his restaurant is equally as impressive.  5 stars is doing him no justice.  Honestly.

This is one of my favorite destinations for sushi. Of course, I like to go all out with my fish, but this place doesn't disappoint. I always order their Love Boat, which has enough sushi/sashimi for two people. It's a nice variety of great quality fish. Another thing that's a *must have* is their wasabi fries. It is soooooo amazing!! I also love their Okonomiyaki... very tasty. This place is highly recommended whether you are a hardcore sushi eater, or if you're afraid of the raw stuff, they have a lot of cooked entrees as well.

I've always loved Lee's Deli!!!! My 1st time in 1999 I was amazed with the quality of food and Mr. Lee's kindness! Now that I'm back in the area I'll always order from Lee's deli!!!! Their menu has changed so much and I can't wait to try everything! This is thee best place in town!! The quality has never changed!!!!

I had dinner on Tuesday night here. There were plenty of people at the restaurant but very ample inside and outside seating was available. We sat outside and had the whole patio to ourselves. The service was a little slow BUT very very friendly and welcoming from the time you walk in. 

We ordered an array of rolls and all were fresh and delicious. The Spanish Roll was especially good and my second would be the Vegas Roll. There was this absolutely spectacular sauce we dipped our sushi in...I can't recall the name but it was Beets! And we added Sriracha and Wasabi. Most def ask for the sauce if you check this place out. 

The restaurant is located on the outer side of the Tucson Mall with soooo much parking available. The mall seems to be really slow...and not full with stores. It seemed as thought most the vehicles there were for the Sushi Restaurant or the Melting Pot which was next door.

I spent several days in St. Louis and my time at Slider House was one of the best nights there. I loved every single thing about this place. Parking was convenient with the restaurant located in a large shopping center. One of the first things I noticed that I thought was SO cool was that outside in front of the restaurant, they had sidewalk chalk for kids and so many of them were having the best time playing. I had never seen a restaurant so something like that and it was genius. They also had laid back patio type furniture that you would have in your own house...again genius because families with kids & dogs could enjoy dining out with everyone comfortable and entertained and not worrying about their kids running or screaming upsetting other patrons. I personally hate when I see kids on the loose and parents not controlling them while out in a busy atmosphere...but with the way Slider House had things set up, all I noticed was how beautiful it was that the families could enjoy their time out together and I loved watching the children run and play. It was really cool.
 
We had a really large group, so while we waited for a table we went to the bar. I always try to drink local beers, wherever I am so I really loved the beer selection since it hosted multiple options. I had an excellent IPA. We were all having such a great time at the bar that waiting for the table didn't feel like waiting at all.
The service was really great from start to finish too. Everyone worked hard and as a team. The same young lady who served us at the bar, was running food. The same gentleman that took our order was helping at the bar...I saw everyone doing everything - whatever and where ever they were needed. I don't think I have ever seen such a well-managed team of restaurant staff. It was really impressive.
I loved the menu, everything sounded so good, all kind of slider variations. Everything was delicious. Believe it or not, the big winner for many people was the Black Bean Slider! The Sweet Potato Waffle Fries were bomb too and I also tried Fried Green Tomatoes which were tasty too. There wasn't one complaint from our very large group - which I think says a lot. For the quality of food & level of service, I thought the menu was very well priced. Worth every penny. The servers were kind enough to give us all separate checks which was so helpful to us. There isn't a single thing that I would change about this place or my experience there and it will be one of my top picks the next time I am in town!!

Whoa! I can't believe I have never written a review for this place. Well here is my contribution!

I have been to this place plenty of times and just recent post covid. The quality, service, and loyal patrons that frequent this place has not changed. What has changed is the availability of items. When I dined here yesterday, they sadly did not have tri-trip or beef ribs due to inability to obtain said product through their vendor. Again, not something they can control and I don't believe their prices has changed from the last time I dined here. The flavor is still consistent and yummy, I can honestly say I have not had a bad meal here. From what I recall their bloody Marys are also bomb!

I finally tried their kick ass fries and man!! This is definitely some good post drinking food. The fries are thin and crispy, the toppings melded well together, and the side of sour cream and green onions definitely works. I can't believe it took me this long to order this item, but it for sure won't be my last.

I have always passed by this place, but I never saw any cars near the building. For the longest time I basically felt and thought that this place was like an abandoned building. UNTIL, one morning the BF suggested we come here for breakfast. Comes to find out they're only open to 2pm.. Yes! now it all makes sense!

I am crazy about the biscuits and gravy! This is probably one of the best biscuits and gravy I've ever had. Though, I've only ever ordered them only a handful of times. I've tried their corned beef hash, country fried steak, steak burrito, and their burger (I think it was called hell something). Everything was super yummers! I honestly feel, whatever you order from this place, it'll never be a disappointment. I don't know who the chef/cook is, but that person sure knows what their doing (really good flavor profile).

This is my second favorite breakfast place in town and again, another place where I am willing to wake up for. PLUS!!!! They serve alcohol, and living in NV, it's NEVER too early to be drinking, haha.

Yelp 2-star "Could've been better", but really terrible in my opinion.

I came here with my parents and we ordered a variety of items off the menu. I was thoroughly disappointed from beginning to end. I understand that opening up during covid is tricky, but this definitely does not excuse poor and basically forgotten service. There were other items that I ordered that I did not take pictures because, honestly, I have lost my appetite with this place solely based on the service we received.

I am very understanding and I can not take offense when another is complaining and you're busy caring for them, but when they leave and we're still being ignored and never been checked up on and water maybe refilled once, not ok. The first thing I noticed was when my father ordered the oysters, they brought it out and just dropped it down and walked away. They didn't tell us anything about it, it was just  "well here's your oysters. Yeah they look different, but you figure it out and just eat it" kind of scenario. I tried to catch our waiter's attention without success and at this point I had to point out which oysters I knew was what and the others were a mystery. Second spiral of neglect was when I didn't have what I wanted to order ready because I had questions, boy did we wait for almost 10 minutes until someone came back to take our order.

Once the food finally made it out, at this point in time I was pretty ticked and quite honestly when the food came out, I have lost all desire to be at Charlie Palmer. It was embarrassing to receive the type of service we received while I was with my parents and they rarely go out somewhere nice to eat. Yes the pork chop was moist, but everything else was underwhelming and now 1 month later the only impression or memory of this place that I have is pork chop was moist, service was beyond bad, food was average.

VERY FLAVORFUL PORK SCHNITZEL!!!

Everytime I go eat german food I'm always left with the thought "maybe I should've brought Sriracha", thought not here at Brauhaus. The breading was not super dense, gravy was flavorful and probably the star of the schnitzel itself, and still crispy even with the gravy. The mac and cheese wasn't bad either. I also am a fan of unfiltered wheat beer which they have.

I wasn't too much of a fan of the burger but the beer cheese was interesting none the less. Vibe was nice and chill, staff was super friendly, and the only complaint I have is probably the parking (which is out of their control because it's downtown). I'll be back for sure.

Before ordering the Caesar salad, I asked the server if they prepare it the genuine way, with anchovies, and the server said "Yes", so I ordered it as well as the lobster bisque, which had very little lobster in it.  I politely asked the server to please rectify the situation and she flipped her lid.  It was incredible.  Not only did she fail to rectify the problems, but she would not let me speak with any manager and to top it off, I had to pay the full bill even though I only ate two bites of each dish.

This place is HORRIBLE.

We were very underwhelmed by the atmosphere, food and level of service. The people were nice enough, but at $30+ for entrees, I expect to be impressed.

Service was slow, no suggestions or offer to explain the menu. The menu was not very creative.

We ordered one 8-wing appetizer, three entrees and a bottle of wine. The total was nearly $200. 

Save your time and money and try another spot.

Tony's makes me really sad.  We LOVE their authentic Neapolitan-style pizzas, but we have also received very poor attitudes and irritated comments when arriving too close to their closing time (9pm).  In my opinion, arriving at 8:40pm shouldn't be considered "late" for a downtown restaurant that isn't even kid-friendly.  But, that's just my opinion.  In any case, I don't object to their decision to close relatively early, but I DO object to the rude manner in which they treat their later-arriving customers.  

My husband and I are dinks with demanding jobs, so we don't  think about eating dinner before 8:30pm most nights.  Fortunately for us, both Community Flatbread and Protos Pizza in Downtown Boise serve equally delicious wood fired Neapolitan pizzas, and are open much later.  Fortunately for Tony, he must have more business than he can handle before 8:30pm, and certainly doesn't need our patronage.

As long as you don't attempt to darken Tony's doorway after 8:30pm, you'll enjoy their beautifully crafted pizzas, fresh salads, and generally good service.   Maybe we can go back after retirement.

Dear Edomasa owner,

Yesterday (May 24, 2014) was the first day in my Japanese-food-loving life that I have encountered a rude waitress at a Japanese restaurant anywhere in the world. It surprised me because it happened at Edomasa, a place where I had always had a positive experience when I ate their from time to time in the past 7 years. In fact, I have very rarely encountered a rude waiter/waitress anywhere in this friendliest-town-in-the-world Santa Barbara. That's why I was taken aback when the waitress who was taking order from me and my friends yesterday, around 7:04 PM, gave us an attitude,  raised her voice, and made us feel extremely unwelcome. 

What exactly happened? It was silly. When I tried to order by saying "Number 117 Assorted Sashimi, please." The waitress answered, "we do not order by number." So I said, "I'd like to have the assorted sashimi." The waitress said sternly: "we do not order by number." Baffled, I repeated myself, "it's the assorted sashimi." The waitress said again, just like a computer stuck in an infinite loop, with the volume increased and the tone stiffened, "we do not order by number, you point to the item on menu and tell me what you order." 

I was unable to determine whether she was intelligently challenged, or it was a language barrier, or she was going through a difficult phase in her emotional life, but I wasn't qualified to offer a medical diagnosis. I only know that I was a patron at a business and I deserved not to be treated that way. I stood up, closed the menu book, and said, "I'm sorry but I will go some place else." My friends and I then left. 

We went to another Japanese restaurant in Goleta and had a wonderful evening. 

I wasn't sure if this waitress was an employee or an owner/partner. If she's the owner, then that would be unfortunate because probably nothing can improve. But if she's an employee, I hope that my review and the details given here is helpful to the owner/manager to identify the problem and take a correct course of action. Whoever she is and whatever distress condition she was in at the time, I hope she recover and find a way to love people again. I wish her and Edomasa all the best. 

I am writing this review not because of hate or anger but out of my feeling of obligation to tell the community so nobody has as to be subjected to this rudeness again. 


Best Regards,
- the Chinese-looking guy in khakii shorts and a dark blue polo shirt

If you don't like macarons, cookies, fruit tarts, chocolate, or anything baked with sugar & butter, don't come here. In fact, if you don't like puppies, babies, or butterflies, you'd better stay away too. Because this place is ridiculously cute! You won't be able to handle it. 

This bakery is like something out of a storybook, filled with pretty delicious things, smiling children, and the smell of baked butter. Apparently, the founder of Duchess studied the art of macarons at Laduree in Paris, then brought the cookie sandwich magic to Edmonton (yes, Edmonton of all places!) 

Next door to the bakery is the Duchess Provisions shop, where you can buy all the materials needed to (attempt to) replicate their sweets at home. They sell adorable macaron-making kits in canvas bags, flavored syrups, sauces and jams, and lots of baking tools like cake pans, and cookie cutters. I bought the cutest Eiffle Tower and Fleur de Lys cookie cutters here! I'm going to throw a French party just so I can use them. 

Cuteness, sweetness, and happiness to the max! Can you handle it?

A desert dream come true! Such a beautiful property that feels classy, tranquil and historic. Tons of character & charm, while still having all the modern amenities you want (free wifi, room service). If you want a real slice of Tucson, Arizona Inn is the spot. 

The rooms have lots of privacy, they feel more like condos with little private patio areas and lots of landscaping around. The pool area is gorgeous. Room service was very gourmet & affordable. Parking is free in the lot across from the hotel, or you can park on the quiet residential street. 

Most notably, the staff were SO nice. Everyone we encountered were super hospitable and helpful. Good vibes! 

If you prefer more of a unique, boutique hotel experience to a grand, modern resort, you'll love Arizona Inn. I can't wait to go back!

Classy as heck! Agustin is a lovely place to experience Tucson hospitality and cuisine. The atmosphere is super sleek and comfy, with a splash of vintage glamour. Perfect for impressing a date, family, or business folks. 

Menu is dauntingly huge, and portions were very generous. We especially loved the wine-soaked orange & burrata appetizer, and the cioppino was the best I've had! Packed with seafood, and the broth was perfectly rich. The brussel sprouts were a bit overrated, too "al dente" for my taste. 

The cocktail list has 20+ options, and wines are abundant too. Plan on at least $50/per person if you're having drinks & dinner. 

Service, of course, is wonderfully attentive too (maybe a bit too eager to clear plates). They were very accommodating with my sleeping baby-in-a-carseat :)

If you were to mix a casual French bistro with a sleek business lunch spot, you'd get something like The Marc. The ambiance is upscale, primed for wooing clients or just simply feeling like a rockstar. My dining buddy, Jennie M, knew the owner so he promptly brought us glasses of a new white wine he thought was perfect for lunchtime, an Italian "Pecorino" (yes, like the cheese). Indeed, it was the perfect mid-day sipper. This little gesture seemed to sum up the vibe of The Marc: welcoming, indulgent, classy. 

The menu is pure French bistro goodness, so having wine with lunch is almost a necessity. The menu is short & simple, with just about 10 items each day. I had the smoked salmon with red potato salad with dill dressing. The salmon was a meaty filet, smoked to perfection (not a slimy layer of lox, like most places will serve). For Miss M, the braised lamb sandwich with carmelized zucchini and onion, dripping with jus. For $13-14 each, the quality of everything was incredible. You can fill in any empty stomach space with some of their famous frites & aioli. 

Even though the food, service and ambiance are all top-notch, you can actually have a casual, express lunch here.  We were in & out in about 30 mins. Though, the table next to us was having a massive multi-course lunch with bottles of Cote du Rhone and all. Something for everyone!

So now i've had lunch as well as dinner at Bricks and it's still one of my favorite resteraunts in town! They are open for lunch i believe wed-friday. Its a good alternate to their higher price dinner menu with food that is just as excellent. For an appetizer we had mushroom caps filled with escargot and blue cheese. Very rich but very tasty. For entrees i had a grilled portabello veggie sandwich, my boyfriend had a shrimp and avocado salad and my mom had an appetizer of grilled scallops and calamari steaks. Everyone's was awesome and they were very decent portions. 2 NA drinks, an appetizer and 3 lunches was $60- very reasonable i thought considering the quality of food and service. Thanks for taking care of us Mike!

I've been coming here since the very beginning and it's had it's highs and lows, the lows being the service. I hadn't been here in about 6 months and when I came again I was happy to see the place jam packed. I've been 3 times in the last month and once again it's back to being, in my opinion, the best sushi in Reno. My boyfriend is from the Bay Area and he thinks it's as good as any top rated sushi place there also. The guys behind the bar are very attentive and are happy to be creative and custom make you whatever you like. The very petite Asian hostess/waitress is also excellent. Lunch is only $14.95 and there is no difference between the lunch and dinner menu. Finally they seem to have it all worked out and our last several experiences have been awesome!

Excellent, excellent, excellent!

I had lunch here with the hubs yesterday and think I've found a new favorite Vietnamese spot.

It's located on Magazine St., which is my favorite street in the entire city.  I spent so much of my childhood on my memaw and pawpaw's porch, watching people walk by on the banquet on this very street.  What a great location.  But I digress.

We were greeted very warmly on a pretty chilly day. While we checked out the menu we sat at an adorable table - the seating is bench style and the benches are covered in cushioned velvety soft fabric.  So comfortable. 

I chose grilled pork over rice and my honey went with grilled pork vermicelli.  I asked if they offered a small pho, and although they don't, the sweet lady who waited on us was kind enough to give me little a bowl of their beef broth complete with fixings so that I could give it a try.   The pho was amazing. Seriously - best pho I've ever had.  My husband isn't a big pho fan and he loved it. 

Our entrees were much the same.  We were impressed to say the least.  The pork was perfectly cooked, and it was lean but still juicy.  The flavor of both dishes was spot on. 

I really can't say enough good things about this gem.  I'm so glad we gave it a try.

I stopped in for lunch yesterday with my hubby and have zero complaints.

They're located on Maple very near Carrollton and in addition to the squeaky clean interior, there's ample covered outdoor seating. We chose to sit inside as we we had to get back to work and it was in the 90's yesterday. 

Our waiter let us know that we could sit anywhere we liked and brought over menus. Our drink order was taken and delivered right away, and we placed our food order at that time. I went with a small pepperoni pizza and my husband chose their chicken and portobello lavish. 

After just a brief wait our food was delivered and at first bite I knew we both had made excellent choices.  I loved my pizza. Really, it was that good. I love a sauce that's on the sweeter side and theirs fits the bill.  I know that lots of people have a crust or cheese thing, while I'm definitely all about the sauce. This one's a definite winner. All of the other components were top notch as well, and it was big enough that I had a couple slices remaining to bring home and snack on later.  My husband's lavash was delicious as well, and it was a very generous size.

Other info - there's a full bar and there are TV's around for those who might want to tune in while they dine.

Nice spot.

This place is so cool.

I'm talking old school steak house with service that's out of this world.  I seriously felt like family.

 My hubs and I shared the chateaubriand for two and loved it.   It was cooked to a perfect medium rare and served with velvety smooth bearnaise and Marchand de vin sauces. When we first caught sight of the dish we swore that there was no way we could finish this more than generous portion for two.  Well, we almost did. 

The atmosphere was laid back and it was clear that everyone in the restaurant was enjoying themselves. There are a few private, curtained booths that I'd love to reserve at some point. 

And I've got to mention the service again. It was excellent.

What an excellent experience.  My husband and I had lunch at PB this week and are still talking about it.  

We started with 2 grilled pork bun/tacos, and we each had the vermicelli with grilled pork for our entrees.  We were not disappointed. The pork on all was flavorful and lean, and we gobbled everything up like it was our job. A+ for the food for sure.  And the service was every bit as good as the food.  Our waiter was friendly, helpful and so on top of his game.  He was the kind of person that you feel like you know from somewhere because they're so endearing. 

All around great experience.

My husband and I had dinner at Annunciation recently and our visit was a bit strange. 

The service was excellent.  The hostess and our waiter were wonderful. I literally only have the best things to say about them.

Here's the rub.  The food wasn't good.  I don't think we ordered anything that we enjoyed. I'm hoping they were just having an off night, but who knows. 

I don't know if we'll return, but I can say that if we don't, we'll miss the service.

This was my first trip to the new-ish location.  They've been here for a while now, so I'm kind of late to the party.

This is the old Wasabi location, and it looks very similar inside.  The decor is very dark, very basic, but the dining areas and bar are pretty spacious.

Today I had the same thing I've always ordered and it was still as tasty as ever.  I'm a sucker for their baked potato.  I know they serve a mean burger as well, but today it was just the spud for me.  I had it stuffed with cheese, sour cream, chives, and drumroll please.......marinated mushrooms.  

Their potatoes put any others I've had to shame. They're large, fluffy, they definitely don't skimp on the toppings, and those mushrooms - goodness gracious! - they're delicious.

My server today was a very attentive, warm, lady who was so on top of things.

This place has a laid back, very casual vibe.  Their drinks have always been good, as well, although I didn't imbibe today.  Maybe next time.

I had lunch at Hana with my family and it was ok.  It wasn't my first trip but it had been a while since my last visit and I thought I'd give them another shot.

We arrived when they were a bit slow, and I think we were one of three tables being served. We were greeted and seated, but then our wait was pretty substantial. Our drink and orders were eventually taken and our drinks came soon after.  My noodle salad arrived as did everyone's salads and soups.  The noodle salad was sweet and creamy, but the noodles were a little tough.

It took quite a while for us to receive the rest of our food. I had a snow crab roll and was underwhelmed. The crab salad was a little dry, and there wasn't much of it inside. The rest of my family was feeling the same about their choices. 

We all left just a little let down.

We enjoyed Christmas Eve dinner at Sofia this year. We usually get all gussied up and go all out on Christmas Eve, but these are different times, so we chose to go a different direction.  What a great idea it was.

I made a reservation for an early dinner. Reservations are a good idea here. They're very popular for good reason, and it's well worth the trip.

First impressions:  friendly staff, hip, chic decor, the homage paid to Sofia Loren is lovely, the pizza oven is definitely a piece of art.

For appetizers we ordered the meatballs and the olive assortment.  The meatballs were loved by all of us.  It's a small portion so the next time we're there we'll get a second order.  The olives were good too, and I appreciated the flavors of the different varieties.

Three of us ordered pizzas and one of us had the bolognese with pasta. Our entrees were scrumptious!!!! And the pizzas were big enough to split. We had so much food! I had the spicy pizza but asked to omit the hot peppers. It was perfect! A little sweet thanks to a drizzle of honey, a little earthy thanks to the kale, a little creamy thanks to the ricotta. 

I finished up with a cappuccino and two of us ordered dessert.  My coffee and one dessert came out, so we guessed my husband's dessert was on its way. The dessert at our table along with my cappuccino were eventually finished and we were ready to go, with no sign of the wayward dessert. We asked for the check and our server left to get it for us. She came back with the check and the long lost dessert. We just asked her to box it to go. It was a gelato dessert so it was melted and not good when we got home. Womp womp.

Otherwise a good meal.

I had a relaxing dinner with my husband at Barcelona Tapas and am hoping to get back there soon.  

We arrived at around 6:00 and I think we were the only customers there.  People did begin to arrive soon after, but I guess we were the early crew.  

Our waitress came by right away with menus and water. She was very personable and super helpful.  The menu is quite extensive and as it was our first visit, we needed some explanation. She was gracious and kind.

We were hoping to have paella, but as it takes a while to prepare, we decided to call ahead and place a paella order on our next visit. 

We had several dishes:  garlic mushrooms, Brussels sprouts with Havarti, calamari steak, grilled lamb chops with fries, and ceviche. I enjoyed all of our small plates, but my favorite dish and clear front runner was the lamb chops with fries. Delicious!! 

Last but not least was the 1/2 carafe if sangria. I finished it all by myself and am not sorry. 

This place is quaint, has a great location in the Riverbend, the service was wonderful and I enjoyed everything I had.  I must also throw this out there - lots of the dishes are full of sultry, pungent, decadent garlic. Yep, you can tell that I love the stuff. I just want to make sure that you vampires know to stand down and you first daters are forewarned.

This is my go to La Madeline.  It's near my office and I stop in every couple of weeks or so.  The food is consistently good, and there are lots of healthy options.  Don't get me wrong though, I don't always make healthy choices, and when I don't, there are so many less healthy, but super yummy options available. I guess what I'm trying to say is whether you're trying to exercise self control, or satisfy that craving for rich food, there are options.

I recently tried the lentil and kale soup and it's a winner.  The kale and quinoa salad's another healthy keeper.  I'm going to lump the pasta salad in with those good for you choices, because it's light and, come on, it's a salad. Forget that it's pasta. 

Their soups are all amazing, and I'm hooked on the tomato basil and the mushroom as well.  My favorite sandwich to pair with one of those is the chicken salad croissant. So good!

As far as customer service goes, the staff is always professional and friendly.  My biggest complaint is that sometimes service is a little slow.

I've seen the ads for Spudly's for decades and I can't believe this was my first visit.  

I was craving a baked potato - which has strangely happened a lot lately - and I thought this was a great time to finally get to a place that specializes in spuds. I knew they were located in Metairie, but I hadn't ever seen the building, so thanks to Yelp directions, I found my way there.  They are tucked away - I mean really tucked away - near Lakeside Hospital. I parked in front of their Alpine like building and ventured inside.  I first noticed that it's a very small place, but there was an available 2 top that I was shown to by the sweet server. I was given a menu and my water was brought over right away.  I went with one of their small potatoes after looking around and checking out what other patrons were enjoying. The large potatoes are gigantic and the small ones are normal sized.  

After about 6 or 7 minutes my mushroom mania potato was delivered to my table. It was delicious!!! Large, fluffy potato covered in cheddar cheese, chives and yummy sautéed mushrooms.  

So I had a very satisfying, tasty lunch for under $8. I'm sold and will definitely be back.

I had yet another fantastic experience at Ruth's tonight. We came in to celebrate my youngest daughter's swim season and the visit was a huge splash. Yes, I agree, that was uncalled for.

Seriously though, as always the staff was awesome, the food was perfectly prepared and absolutely delicious, the ambiance was tops, and we went home stuffed.

We each had petit filets - tender, juicy, flavorful, sizzling in butter

We shared:

Brussels sprouts - prepared with bacon - yeeeesssss!! 

Fries - skinny little tidbits of joy

Crispy lobster - sweet with a bit of crunchiness

Chocolate duo - Wow.  Just wow.

Creme brûlée - perfectly rich and decadent

Bottom line -

I love this place.

I had an early dinner at Fat Boy with a large group (13 of us) Saturday evening.  The staff was welcoming and more than understanding considering we had 4 little ones in the party. By little I mean 4 and under. 

We were able to reserve our table so that once we arrived we weren't charged with pushing tables together or waiting while our little peanuts became restless.  

We ordered at the counter, received our drinks immediately and our wait was very brief for our pizza.  Seriously, the staff was wonderful.

We ordered a slice per person after hearing that they'd be large.  Well, large is an understatement. They're huge!! I gave half of my slice of pepperoni to my son-in-law. I liked the pizza ok, but I'd prefer a sweeter sauce, which is just a personal preference. The crust was perfect, and they were very generous with all of the toppings.  They also offer a few frozen drinks in addition to beer and wine. I had a Frose' and loved it.

There are several arcade games and claw machines, which we had fun with.  They kept the kiddos plenty busy.

This is a cool spot.

I had a little date night with my sweet hubs Saturday night and we chose Fharmacy, based on Yelp reviews.

Fharmacy is super casual and laid back.  All employees were masked and tables were appropriately spaced.

We sat at a two top and were brought menus.

We decided on the Vietnamese wings, and I ordered a basic burger. It was served with lettuce, tomato, pickle, and instead of raw onions I requested grilled.  Not a problem.  

First the wings.  Wow.  They were absolutely fantastic!! So full of flavor! They were tangy with a hint of kick.  They were hot and crispy, and I could've eaten a bucket of those little nuggets of goodness. 

Now for my burger.  It was prepared just the way I requested and it was tasty. The fries were the thin kind. They were good too. 

Final thoughts:  

Portion sizes were generous
Wings were delicious
Burger was good
Very casual vibe
Prices were reasonable

I had lunch at Saba and I'm wowed. 

First things first - they have a parking lot. Yep, on Magazine. It's small and they share it with other businesses but you just might find yourself lucky enough to snag a spot. It's definitely worth a shot.

Upon entry I was welcomed and shown to a small two top in this brightly lit, impressively decorated space. I had expected a stuffy visit, but I couldn't have been more wrong. Every staff member I encountered was warm and friendly.

I ordered the blue crab and lemon hummus and hanger steak.

Goodness gracious!! The hummus was aaaaahhhhhmazing!!!! It was creamy, lemony and full of crab. And I'm talking large pieces of crab. And the pita was hot, fluffy and over the top delicious. I can't wait to  on go back for another helping.

The hanger steak was flavorful and tender. It was a very small portion, but was very good.

I can't wait to  go back.

My husband and I had a dinner with friends planned, and lucky for us they chose Luvi after having eaten there once before.  

We had a reservation, and thank goodness we did, because this super hip, adorable space is small and very popular.  We were seated as soon as we arrived and greeted by our amazing server, Noah. Our friends explained what turned out to be a great dining strategy and we went with it. We ordered one feed me per couple and then several small plates to share.

The feed me raw selections were all light and flavorful. I've never had flounder sashimi before and was blown away. 

Other dishes we ordered:

Dan Dan noodles - not to be missed
Curried dumplings - my favorite menu item
Crispy spring roll - delicious
Smashed cucumbers - loved them 
Chicken wings - get some
Tuna meatballs - my only regret of this meal

I can't neglect to mention the Shinobu sidecar. This luscious little cocktail was a tricky character. It fooled me with it's sweet, sugary rim. This little lady turned out to be a brawny imposter. Kicked my lightweight butt. Not that I'm complaining, though, because It was unctuous. 

That was my visit. I'll be back.

I really enjoyed my lunch at China Orchid yesterday.  They serve solid, traditional Chinese food at very reasonable prices.

I had a cup of egg drop soup and their broccoli chicken with a side of brown rice and an egg roll.  I was happy with both dishes.  The flavors were great and the ingredients seemed to be of very good quality.

The service was excellent too.

This is a beautiful Whole Foods located on Magazine Street, and there's ample parking in the rear of the building.

The store is clean and well stocked, but it feels a little cramped. All of the produce and meats appeared fresh, and there were lots of employees around in case you need any assistance.

I must note that I love the little mochi bin.  The strawberry is by far my favorite flavor, as it tastes like fresh berries. 

The checkout process on this visit was a breeze.

Wow.  

My husband and I were tooling around uptown and decided to turn to my yelp buddies to steer me to a new-to-me lunch spot.  Once again you all have come through.

We decided on Tito's and are so glad that we did.  We found a parking spot directly in front of the restaurant and were impressed with the curb appeal.  There are a several tables and chairs out front with colorful pillows that really set the tone for us.  It all felt so inviting.  We entered this bright, very pulled together, chic restaurant and were greeted warmly.  We were seated in front by the large windows that overlook the interesting, beautiful homes and foot traffic on Magazine Street.  Our drink order was taken and we were given menus to look over.  Our waitress made it clear that she would be more than happy to answer any questions we may have about the menu.  As this was the first time we had ever had Peruvian cuisine, we took her up on her offer.  We asked lots of questions and decided on the Ceviche Nikkei appetizer, I ordered the Causa de Cangrejo as my main, and my husband ordered the Arroz con Marislos.

The ceviche was delivered to our table soon after and it was DELICIOUS!!  The yellowfin tuna was super fresh.

The Causa de Cangrejo was sort of like a Napoleon of crabmeat, avocado and aji potatoes.  This dish, although small, had it all and filled me up.  The crabmeat was fresh, the avocado was cool and creamy, and the potatoes were perfectly spicy and rich.  Next time I visit, I may order this dish as an appetizer to share because my husband enjoyed it as much as I did.  

My husband's Arroz con Marislos was killer good.  It was like paella.  This dish had just the right amount of seafood and everything had flavor for days.  It was like a party in every bite.

We will absolutely return sooner rather than later, and I'll be trying some of their other dishes.  I'm looking forward to eating my way through their menu.  The service was excellent and the food was fantastic.  

Oh, and on my next visit I plan to  enjoy a Pisco cocktail or two from their interesting drink menu.

Maple Street Cafe is perfect spot for a business lunch or a get together with a few friends.  It's quaint, tastefully decorated and cozy. Everyone is greeted with a genuine hello when the arrive.

I've always had impeccable service and delicious food. On my last visit I went with a Caesar salad topped with smoked salmon. The Caesar dressing was rich and creamy, and the salmon was thinly sliced, fresh and chilled.  My husband went with a grilled chicken salad that was equally tasty.

I usually opt for a salad here, but have had some of the pastas in the past. They've all been good choices.

This is a nice quiet spot in such a cool part of town. Love it.

Sweet Handkraft has been on my radar for quite a while, and finally I made my way over with my daughter.  She shares my sweet tooth, and was happy to take on this adventure with me.

We were greeted by several sweet, helpful guys who pointed out the goodness they create each day.  Yes, their items are all freshly made in house, and they do a phenomenal job.

I had a waffle cone with almond brittle ice cream. Wow. It was huge, rich, yummy, scrumptiousness.  My daughter had a Cookie Monster macaroon ice cream sandwich. Another win.

I couldn't leave without macaroons to go and two of their giant cookies.  It was explained that they warm their cookies in the store, and to please do them the justice of warming them at home prior to devouring.  I did, and, what a great suggestion. These cookies are out of this world.  The chocolate, chocolate chip was delicious, but the chocolate, sea salt, caramel cookie was by far my favorite item. I can't even describe how good it was - that's how good it was. 

Yep, you guessed it. I'll be back.

Martin's has been a part of my life for years, for so many reasons.  

When I need a hostess gift, birthday gift, or am having friends over, they are a great resource for this wine ignoramous. When it comes to wine and spirits I have very little knowledge, but the staff here is always helpful.  They've never steered me wrong, and they carry good wines and cover all price points. And they have a great selection of gifts for wine drinkers, cute wine gift bags, party extras like crackers, candy, wine buckets, etc.

Now for the food......

Their deli is amaze-balls.  Awesome sandwiches, salads, soups, cheeses and ready made party food. Their burgers are top notch, but take a time to cook, so place your order and be prepared to wait few minutes.  I promise it will be worth it.

Their catering is great too.  I've ordered most of their menu and have always been impressed. 

I just love this place.

Lebanon's Café is worth every one of the 5 stars I'm giving it.  I have dined in and taken out in the past two weeks and am pleased with both services.

Service was excellent, COVID precautions were taken in abundance - social distancing table configurations, masked employees, no waiting inside for tables or to go orders.

Now for the food. 

Good gracious!!! I had a gyro plate and I can honestly say that this was the most tender and flavorful gyro meat I've ever had.  I'm so serious that you can't even imagine how serious I am right now.  I love good gyro meat, and theirs was over the top scrumptious.  Also, the plate comes with hummus, and their hummus is different.  It's served with some sort of vinegar and oil mixture.  Not sure what it was, but the flavor was bright and left me wanting more.

I went back within days and will do so again and again.

Love me some Blaze!!

I enjoy being able to see all of the available ingredients to customize my pizza while I'm making those ever important decisions.  Fresh mozzarella, ricotta, parm? Pepperoni, mushrooms, olives, Brussels sprouts? Yep, Brussels sprouts!! And they were delicious!

The concept isn't brand new when you're talking sandwiches, but it's new to me when it comes to pizza.  From the crust, to the sauce, to the toppings - you can see how fresh the ingredients are. When you're done putting your pie together it's fun to watch it go into the big oven.  The whole process is a quick one, and before you know it your pizza is done. 

The staff seems to be happy to be at work which always adds some sunshine to my meals. Several of the employees made sure we were all good during our visit. 

When I checked in on my yelp app there was a free dough garlic knots offer. They were delicious!! Make sure you check in and give these nuggets a try.

This City Greens didn't completely live up to my expectations, as I'm a customer of the Metairie Road location and absolutely love it.

I found the service here to feel rushed, and the place just didn't feel as sparkly clean as their other spot. It wasn't filthy, the tables were turning quickly and I think they were too busy to get to all of them before a new customer sat down. 

Over all, it was an ok visit, I just felt a little let down. Not saying I'll not return, because they offer such delicious, healthy options. The ingredients are always fresh and I feel like I'm doing my body a favor when I eat at City Greens.  For these reasons I'm giving them 4 stars.

As I love Dominica's original spot, I had to try this one too.

We arrived at a little past noon and there was an abundance of available seating.  The hostess led us to our table, and soon after our server brought menus and took our drink order. Our drinks arrived and we placed our food order.   We went with roasted cauliflower, the meatball appetizer, a pepperoni pizza and a calabrese pizza.

So our food was delivered to the table soon enough. The cauliflower was pretty good, and the meatball appetizer was fantastic. The meatballs reminded me so much of my grandmothers, and my grandmother was the quintessential Sicilian Memaw. This is indeed a compliment bestowed on few.  It's usually only  reserved for other Sicilian Memaws.

On to the pizzas.  The pepperoni was up to par, but the calabrese was topped with way too many olives.  It was like olive salad, and our pizza was covered in it.  I love olive salad, but this just cancelled out all of the other flavors that should've been allowed to at least peek through.

Next visit I'll skip the calabrese and go with something else.

Refuel is a breakfast/brunch/lunch spot, but there weren't many lunch options available.  Luckily today there was a Cuban sandwich on the menu - I think it was today's special.  The roasted pork was delicious, but I chose to remove the bacon as I'm a traditionalist with my Cubans.  I chose roasted potatoes as my side and they were well seasoned and perfectly cooked. 

I'll have to go back for breakfast because the options were many, and all sounded yummy.

The staff was friendly and all of the windows across the front of the restaurant really let the sun in.

5 stars for sure!

This was my second visit to Bittersweet Confections and definitely won't be my last.

I stopped in for their basil chicken salad and to pick up some sweets for my sweet, seeing that Valentine's day is tomorrow. 

The chicken salad was beyond good. It's made with chunks of tender white meat chicken, and the basil sends this dish it into orbit. The side crostini are such a winning complement. 

As I mentioned, I was there for sugary goodness too, so I picked up a bag of salted dark chocolate and an individual flourless chocolate cake. The desserts are not only delicious; they're also beautiful. 

Before closing, it's important to note that the atmosphere and service are excellent. The staff is friendly and so helpful. 

I'll be back to try their pimento cheese sandwich soon.

I had a nice little date night meal here at the bar last night with my partner in crime.

I've wanted to try A Tavola for a while now and am happy I finally came by.

It was dinner time and we had no reservation so it was either a 30 minute wait or eat at the bar. We chose the latter.  The ladies behind the bar were wonderfully sweet and fun.  They were attentive and took really good care of us.  My man had a very generous vodka tonic, and I had an Amalfi Collins, which was so refreshing.

We ordered the meatballs appetizer and loved them.  They were as authentic as a meatball gets, so we were very impressed.

We each had entree salads and they were ok.  I had the kale and beet salad, which was good, but the kale was a little too tough for my liking.  My husband had the grilled tuna salad.  He liked the tuna, but wasn't crazy about the dressing.  Neither salad was awful, but next time we'll make different choices.

Oh, and the complimentary  bread and oil are amazing!!! We requested a second basket.

I really wish I could give Mother's no stars.  If you've looked over my reviews you'd notice that I'm not into trashing an establishment for the sake of doing so, so this is an honest and real opinion.

I was born and raised in New Orleans, and although I've traveled to lots of other places, I've always come home ready for a New Orleans meal.  I've NEVER had the desire to make it a meal at Mother's.  If my mother ran mealtimes this way, I would've moved out at the age of 7. 

The line is ridiculously long, the food is mediocre at best, and the service is terrible.  I DON'T GET IT?!?!?  What am I missing folks?

I had Shake Shack for lunch today and am happy to have them in the area.

I arrived about 5 minutes before they opened, so parking and waiting were two things I didn't have to worry about. My daughter and I were hanging with friends, so we all ordered together at the kiosk then found a place to have a seat.  

It wasn't long before our order was ready. We picked it up
from the counter, found the extras we needed at the condiment/utensil station and brought our goodies to the table to check them out.

We each had burgers and shared 2 orders of fries between the 4 of us. We had 2 fountain drinks, 2 bottled waters and a small shake, and the total was $45. Not horrible, but these weren't large burgers. The fries were more than we needed, on the other hand.  I think we all liked the flavor of the burgers and the way they were prepared. I wasn't a huge fan of the fries. At all.  They were bland and tasted like frozen grocery store fries. My daughter thought the shake was just o.k.

As we left I encountered a parking issue. The front lot was full and several people were waiting to get into the one or two available spots. They seemed annoyed with each other and then I got blocked in for a few minutes.  

I'm sure I'll be back, but I'll wait for the hype to die down.

My husband and I stopped in for a late breakfast Sunday after mass, and the place was hopping. We snagged one of the last available tables and about 10 minutes after we arrived, there were about 10 customers standing around waiting for a seat. 

We were happy to be greeted and seated right away. Our waitress came by soon after to bring our menus and take our drink orders.  When she came back to bring our drinks she took our order. Our food came pretty quickly and it was delicious!  I had the debris Benedict and it was crazy good. Y'all, the fluffy biscuit, the sweet, tender debris, the rich buttery hollandaise - it was over the top. 

My only complaint was that it was a little tough to get the attention of our waitress. She didn't check on us after she brought our food, and I was hoping to add a coffee to my order.

Considering the crowd, she's forgiven. She was sweet and our orders were accurate. 

I will definitely be back.

This Blaze is spacious, clean, and located on Freret St.  The concept is like Subway's, but with pizza.  They offer great crust choices, like traditional thin, thick, gluten free, and cauliflower.  From there you just add what you like from a bunch of good stuff.  I really like the cheese selection - shredded mozzarella, fresh mozzarella and ricotta among others.

The staff was very friendly but a little on the slow side when it came to putting our pies together. Also, I was surprised there were no Brussels sprouts at this location. They have them at their location on O'Keefe, and I love them. Also, please Blaze, add sundried tomatoes to your list of ingredients. 

Our pizzas were delicious, but the crust was burnt on the edges.  

We had a couple of dough knots, and they were sheer perfection, and with my Yelp checkin they were free.  They were garlicky, fluffy, and piping hot.

Wow.

I was looking for something new-to-me in the area and am SO GLAD that I found Boucherie. 

This is a small quaint restaurant in an old New Orleans raised home.  It's decorated for a more elegant, but not frou-frou dining experience. It's classy but comfortable if that makes sense.

My honey and I arrived at around 11:15 for lunch and had no problem being seated. We perused the menu and had a very hard time deciding.  We decided to order a slow roasted wagu beef poboy and a pulled pork poboy, then we split them. OMG.  OMG. OMG.  They were AMAZING.  These sandwiches were over-the-top unctuous.  The beef was debris style, there was a horseradish cream sauce, and the bread was just perfect. The meat was rich and so tender, the sauce had just the right amount of bite, and the bread was lightly crispy on the outside but soaked and soft on the inside.  The pulled pork was also beyond tender, and was just sweet enough. Same deal with the bread.  We were so full that we weren't able to order desert, but I swear, on the next visit I'm going for it come hell or high water.  The choices were so up my alley - I saw Krispy Kreme bread pudding, and there was a chocolate ganache something or other.

Before I close out I can't neglect to mention that the service was outstanding. 

I'm hoping to bring family here when they come in Thanksgiving week. This place is exceptional.

If you're going to have a Snoball in NOLA, and let's face it - you HAVE to have a Snoball in NOLA at least once a summer because I think it's some sort of law here - then please do yourself a favor and make it a Plum Street Snoball. 

The prices are excellent, the ice is powdery, and I've loved every flavor I've ever tried.  My favorite is their chocolate with sweetened condensed milk.  It's rich, sweet, and perfectly chocolatey. And if nectar's your thing, go for it here. Theirs is delicious.

Other notable info.:

My sister in law swears by their vanilla, but being a total creature of habit, I can't leave without my chocolate. I believe her and am guessing that the vanilla is the bomb.

Keep in mind that it's street parking and cash only.

I had a fun family lunch here yesterday, and will definitely be back.

We were greeted warmly and asked to sit wherever we'd like.  Our waiter came by immediately to take our drink order and bring our menus.  I took a minute to check out my surroundings, and found LPK to be clean, brightly lit, and it has a laid back vibe.  

I split a pizza with my honey, my daughter ordered a Caesar salad wrap, and ditto for her friend.  

Our wait was brief, and then the goodness arrived. Our pizza was delicious! Every component of this pie impressed my husband and me. The girls' enjoyed their wraps but couldn't get close to finishing them. They were huge and tasty.

This was my first visit, and it certainly won't be my last.

Loved my lunch at Hoshun!

Upon arrival we were greeted warmly and were able to choose our table.  Our waiter brought menus and took our drink order right away.  I loved that there was a TV nearby with scrolling images of some of their most popular menu items,  as it definitely helped us make some food decisions.  

We ordered edamame, tuna tataki, a Metairie roll and a Haiku roll.  Everything was delicious!! The tuna tataki was so fresh and had a nice kick.  The rolls were equally fresh and the Haiku roll was bomb.  

The service was outstanding, the restaurant is lovely and is in a really great spot on Magazine.  I'm glad to have found another sushi place to add to my rotation.

So I stopped in here today with my almost 14 year old for a birthday eve cupcake, and am so glad I did.

The shop is nestled in a little courtyard area on Magazine Street. Upon entering this bright, cheery space we were welcomed warmly and offered assistance.  The cupcakes are beautiful and the shop smells like pure sweetness. 

My daughter went with 2 cupcakes - 1 chocolate and 1 yellow with chocolate frosting. She devoured the former and was kind enough to share a bite with me. It was delicious.  The frosting was creamy but also fluffy.  The flavor was reminiscent of old time rocky road fudge. That might be just me, though. We both loved it. We haven't tasted the yellow cake cupcake yet, but it's beautiful and I'm guessing just as yummy.

I was checking in on my Yelp app and noticed that there was a free mini cupcake upon checkin.  As there weren't any minis available at the moment, the gracious ladies helping us were kind enough to give us a free small cupcake. The mini flavor of the day had been sweet potato, so they went with that flavor. Y'all, it was yummy! My daughter who's usually not much of a sweet potato pastry fan, loved it. It had just the right amount of spice and the frosting was sweet and tangy.  

A hit for sure and we'll definitely be back.

After my experience here, I have to seriously ask: What are these reviewers smoking?! And...how did this place receive a "People Love Us on Yelp" sticker?! (That must have been stolen from another business)

My friends and I are desserts and boba ADDICTS (seriously), and there's rarely any leftovers when we start indulging in both. But, this place managed to make us stop after one bite, which is unheard of!

Upon walking into this small, lackluster bakery, we had to wait a couple of minutes before someone came from the back to help us (no greeting whatsoever). Given that this was an Asian bakery, and most Asian places are infamous for their (lack of) customer service, we let that go.

Here's where things get a bit awkward. In their display cases, they have a TON of bread, pastries, and other desserts just sitting there for you to indulge in...with your eyes. We tried ordering what we saw, but the cashier kept telling us that it wasn't available. How is it not available when the display case is filled with them? Couldn't he at least take one out of the display case? You don't need to display 10 of the same thing for others to see what it is.

It would have been so much easier if he just told us what was available in the back. Needless to say, their "available" selections were quite LIMITED. There were maybe only 4-5 things we could choose from.

Egg Tart: This place has one of the WORST egg tarts I've ever eaten. One bite out of this FLAVORLESS, STALE pastry, I could barely even force myself to finish the first bite. Egg tarts are supposed to be flaky on the outside and bursting with flavors in the middle. I experienced none of that magical combo. Only thorough disappointment. ): 

Chocolate Mousse-Like Dessert: I don't know what they think chocolate tastes likes, but this certainly isn't how it's supposed to taste like. A spoonful of this gelatin-like dessert is enough to make you vomit in your own mouth. Definitely steer clear if you don't want a vomit party happening in your mouth.

Coconut Custard: This was probably the best out of the three we tried. Though it's far from spectacular, it didn't make us want to spit it out right away. The custard didn't have much flavor, and the bun itself was pretty bland, but at least it didn't have a funny taste to it.

And here comes the icing to the cake...
Boba: We originally came here for boba. Although we weren't expecting the quality we'd find from The Bay Area, we weren't expecting it to be this bad. You could definitely tell that the milk tea was made from a powder packet (one that you can easily buy from an Asian grocery store). The boba was appallingly terrible! It was really hard and tasted like plastic. I LOVE boba, but even I couldn't finish something as terrible as this.

They should rename Honey Bakery to...HORRIBLE BAKERY! I don't remember ever being this disappointed by boba and desserts. After snowboarding all day, we just wanted to enjoy some good desserts and sip on some boba, is that too much to ask for?! ):

My wife and I live in Tower Grove and have been very excited to try Olio ever since they opened.  I drive past them every day on the way to work and it's refreshing to see that people are taking action to fix up what has historically been a blighted neighborhood.  

Unfortunately, my wife and I had a very disappointing experience there today.  We arrived early this afternoon and were seated on the back patio, which was great because it was a beautiful day!  We each ordered a drink from the first server who visited us.  While we waited for our drinks, two additional servers visited us but we politely informed them that we had already been helped.  After waiting for approximately 30 minutes and speaking with 3 servers, our drinks had not arrived so we left disappointed.

We both sincerely enjoy the fact that we can walk and ride our bikes to fantastic eateries, bars, and other businesses.  I had high hopes for Olio, but will not be back for a while (if ever).

Burger #146: Caviar & Sour Cream

I toiled for weeks trying to pick the right burger to eat in NOLA and I settled on Yo Mama's since it was the closest walk from my hotel. The place was your standard dive bar feel with a few tables for eating. I plopped up at the bar and stared down the menu. So many good sounding burgers, but one caught my eye, the Romanoff burger. A burger topped with sour cream and caviar! Curiosity took its grip and off I went. 

About 10-15 minutes later, this is what appear in front of me;
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/5CbJgHWgvjyDRw9Sl4BXhg?select=7yhuFDR1brMb59aFxS5Ufw

Not only was the burger patty huge, but they used about half a tub of sour cream and a good heaping tablespoon of caviar! I dove in, instantly the sour cream and perfectly medium-rare beef were swimming in a perfect harmony of creamy goodness. The caviar added a nice level of saltiness and the slightest fishy hint. I loved it! 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/5CbJgHWgvjyDRw9Sl4BXhg?select=R6Vx7j4jUyXy_WXs_cMWCg

All in all, it was a damn fine burger for a good price (under $10). I'd go back.

Located inside the Hyatt, I came here twice to eat during my stay. 

The first time I ordered the piled high corned beef reuben. Oh what a letdown that was! You can't say "piled high" and only have a few slices of meat! It was good, but I felt misled. 

The second time I came, I decided to order the pulled bbq pork. Now St Louis style bbq is known for their sauces and this one did not disappoint me at all! The sauce was probably a little on the sweet side for some people, but it was just right for me. That, mixed with a generous pile of perfectly, falling off the bone, tender as tender gets pork, was a slice of heaven on a soft roll. 

Too bad my first meal here was meh. 

***At night, this place is prime hotel cougar hunting grounds***

Probably my favorite cheese steak I've had in Philly. 

This was the first of three I tried during my two day stay and it was so good we had it twice. Located across the street from another cheese steak shop (my next review), Dalessandro's had some of the nicest staff I've encountered in Philly. I ordered my usual, cheese steak with onions, whiz, and provolone. 

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RQAF6a0akMiot5lZZnMNNw?select=Cxt1Op3aZkIberH02UclMw

When it came out I asked for hot peppers and the lady there was so proud that they make a few types of hot peppers all in house. Very cool! I tried them all and loved them all. The cheese steak was the perfect ratio of bread to meat to cheese and the peppers elevated it to the right spice. 

Another plus was their ridiculously long beer menu and since you can't find it in California, I had to get a Yuengling with my sandwich. 

As I said, we loved it so much that we went back the next day for another.

I couldn't have asked for a better finale to our tour de force of birthday weekend eating. 

Julienne was a random pick for our post wine tasting meal and it didn't fail to impress at all. Located off the main strip in Santa Barbara, Julienne reminded me of a small town French bistro; very simple and very good. After an intense debate as to whether we should all get a small tasting menu or a la carte, we chose the latter. Here's the breakdown:

Foie Gras Terrine: I always prefer whole lobe seared foie, but in a pinch I'll settle for the cool and creamy variety. The couple ounces served didn't go very far when split 5 ways, but the bites I had were as good as a foie terrine can get. 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=UuJCKxYQlzds9ZK2EMMCwA

Duck Tongue Salad: Tender pieces of duck tongue (yes they have tongues big enough to eat), topped with radish and some other veggies. Very mild dish, but you could definitely taste the duck.
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=ZBwVL-2P2j9NBjE764xkAg

Beef Carpaccio: A solid dish but not revolutionary. Props for the perfect proportion of meat to other stuff. 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=MzJfd0uous2KF8Ck_q9e9g

The Best Pork Chop In The World: I shit you not, this was hands down, without question or contest, the absolute BEST pork chop I have ever eaten! Perfectly cut, seared, seasoned, and cooked, it was a masterpiece. The huge glob of compound button on top helped a little too, but the crust on that thing was to die for. It's almost impossible to get such a perfectly crusty crust on a piece of meat while keeping it moist, tender, and delicious. The meat itself was cooked perfectly and I was literally gnawing at the bone to get every last meaty fiber. I would drive to Santa Barbara in an instant just to have that pork chop again. After that pork, nothing really mattered anymore. 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=0ohVTBOBGFtqQK1vDqE93Q

Lamb: The wife's lamb was damn good, but not as good as my pork chop.
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=w-X6D_g0uoPQX1AigGGmnA

Pork Belly: Jenni's pork belly was good but the skin was almost too caramelized and stuck to our teeth. Not as good as that pork chop.
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=h3tzPDJAfefY5E1TiMRkJw

Sausage and Noodles: FG's sausage was pretty tasty and the noodles were done right. But I just want pork chop!
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=1MErcqOhKAHSH_pRhBVdpw

Fired Chicken: Squirrel's chicken was nice and crisp but a little on the bland side. It didn't matter though because I had that pork chop.
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oktohqIGhMQxOP7h5ugHlg?select=y2tZKwmnAsbnmV8K5XqPOw

We skipped dessert since we had a craving for frozen yogurt, but I'm sure it wouldn't have been as good as that pork chop. Again I cannot say enough about that pork chop. Even while writing this, I'm trying to think of ways to con the wife into making another trip in that direction. I will be back for sure.

Let us all take a moment to thank the good foodie karma I have right now because a Thai place on my side of town?! With more than excellent food?! With the nicest owner ever?! 

WHAT DID I DO TO DESERVE THIS BLESSING?!

I found it by chance on Yelp so we moseyed over got ourselves a generous helping of Thai delight. The owners were crazy nice. They all apparently know how to cook and we felt like straight royalty because their service was IMPECCABLE. They even have wine to pair with your meal. I mean. Come on. 

So far we've tried:
- Thom Yum: Slightly spicy lemon grass soup. Perfect appetizer or entree depending on your mood. 
- Drunken Noodles: A fave. Plenty of veggies cooked, but not soggy. Has a great crisp! Excellent sauce. Wide/thick/hefty noodles. 
- Ro tee: A dessert. Kinda like an elephant ear had a baby with baklava. Drizzled is some kind of magic sauce that makes all the bad stuff go away. 
- Fried Banana: Another dessert. Perfect for anyone. I legit hate banana but I ate the crap out of these things. About the size of a quarter, one order comes with a good number of them. Drizzled on honey, topped with whipped cream, sprinkled with love.

If you're looking for some good vegan/vegetarian food this is an excellent spot to hit up. My only complaint and reason for 4 stars, is I often find this place fairly quiet when I go, but feel rushed by the staff to leave. Overall excellent food, but not a spot to savor a fresh squeezed juice and check emails.

There are lots of reviews, so I'm going to focus specifically on what I love... the fried chicken.  It's superbly fantastic... the best I've had anywhere. Frey's has absolutely perfected the batter and fries it up just right, a perfect amount of grease and served hot! Make sure to get a side of the sriracha aioli for dippin. 

Now... that's my fav... a lot of other good thing there too, like the ribs, smoked wings, biscuits, and the shakes. 


BOTTOM LINE: Instantly the #1 BBQ place in NOLA.

I got a suggestion to head to this corner store from one of my old coworkers, claiming it was an elite cheesesteak place, but not in the traditional sense, so I had to try it out. Given COVID restrictions, everything was done socially distanced, and I was not allowed into the store until my order was complete, which I was completely fine with.

For the two of us (me and my friend) we tried the revered Rule Breaker and the KBBQ Cheesesteaks along with their garlic parm fries. I will not lie, the Rule Breaker did not exactly hit the spot, but the KBBQ hit it out of the park. If I had to go back, I'd try their regular cheesesteak along with the KBBQ one again. The fries, albeit slightly soggy, were flavorful and packed with seasonings.

Definitely worth a trek if you're ever in the Baltimore Ave area.

Urban Grub's Shrimp and Grits with Andouille Sausage has just made my list of all time fav Nashville dishes. 

My husband and I decided to drive to 12 South to try Bartaco. We put our name on the list, and we were number 12,456 in line. During our wait, we decided to stroll down 12 South. We ended up at Urban Grub, where there was also a two-hour wait. However, the bar area at Urban Grub is open seating and we were able to snag a table after thirty minutes.

Every single thing we had was amazing. Every single thing we had is something I would order again. The Shrimp and Grits are stellar. I liked the weird little gluten-free roll things they provided. The House Salad = amazing. And we also had the 7oz Creekstone FarmsCertified Hereford Filet, which was melt in your mouth smooth and oniony and good.  Our server told us that they have their own butcher on staff as well as their own meat curing room. Meat is definitely their forte. 

Next time, we'll make a reservation. And there will be a next time. Urban Grub is now one of my favorite restaurants in Nashville.

Omg this place is so beautiful *heart eyes* The dusty rose furniture, lighting fixtures, and high ceiling make this a classy place to hang out and/or study. Always on the search for boba and this place was nearby so we stopped in after lunch. I went with a classic choice and got boba milk tea and my friend got a mango lemonade green tea with grass jelly and boba. I liked my drink, but the boba wasn't as chewy as I'd like. The cups are fun and can be used for hot and cold drinks. The young lady at the counter was friendly and answered our questions, also great to get 10% off by checking in so make sure to use that.

We hung out on the chairs for some time and it was a comfortable environment to be in. It was fairly quiet so we were able to have a conversation without feeling like we had to yell. I wanted to come back on Sunday since my receipt had an offer of buy one, get a second drink 50% off but they are closed Sundays. I'd def come back if I was around UA again.

Bad food. Horrible service. My family and I used to frequent this place when it was good, but that was over 10 years ago. Things have gone way down ever since. We went here on Mother's day for dinner. There were six of us, and we wanted to order the $138 set dinner. However, we were told that we have to order at least $150. Irritated, I wanted to stand up and walk out, but my mom begrudgingly changed our order to a $188 dinner. When the food came out, I totally wished that we had stood up and left. The food was terrible. The chicken dish was BLOODY raw. We sent it back for them to cook it more. The plate of chicken itself was gone for a good twenty minutes, yet it came back the same--cold and bloody raw.

Me thinks NOT/NEVER AGAIN is the perfect way to describe my experience at R2L last night. 
I was so proud to take my bf to my (FORMERLY) favorite restaurant restaurant for his retirement dinner (20+ years in the United States Airforce---stationed in ALASKA). We ran late for sunset, so we ate dinner somewhere else but STILL opted to come to R2L for drinks, light apz, and dessert after dinner. That was a MISTAKE. They ALMOST KILLED HIM AND GAVE US A CHECK FOR IT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

... Long story short, I was sitting next to him (at the bar) when he tapped me and motioned me to look at his mouth and the champagne glass he was drinking from. THE GLASS had BROKEN IN HIS MOUTH!!!! I was freaking out, but trying not to make a CRAZY scene. He spit out the glass and scurried off to the bathroom. I told the bartender, what happened and he started apologizing. A minute or so later (after consulting with some guy in the corner who looked important in a suit) the bartender asked me "did he (my bf) bite down on the glass and break it?" HUH? WTH? Who bites down on a glass and breaks it in their freaking MOUTH????? Have you ever drank out of a glass and broke it? What the hell  kind of question is that? At this point I'm  TOTALLY disgusted AND HUMILIATED. Was it being suggested by him or the "important corner guy" that bf PURPOSEFULLY broke a damn glass in his own mouth? Are you FREAKING kidding me???
About 5 mins later my bf returned and said he thought he was ok and got all of the glass and HOPED he hadn't swallowed any.  Finally, "Important corner guy" came over asked if he was okay. I had a funny feeling what was to follow. Yup...You guessed it...THE FREAKING CHECK!!!!!!!!!!!!

I was SOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO DISGUSTED by the fact that these people had the NERVE to #1 SUGGEST that the glass was broken on purpose (or even ask that stupid a$$ question) and #2 to give me a FREAKING CHECK for it? Granted they were "kind" enough to take off the "Broken GLASS" drink, but the other drink, dessert, and appetizer was STILL on the check. I was absolutely SEETHING MAD. I wanted to flip out, but I was ACTUALLY wayyyyy TOO HURT by the treatment of this seemingly classy establishment. It totally sucked. My bf was pissed and wanted to go, before he got upset by the check-gate incident.
 I was treating for the night because it was part of our celebration of his service and THIS was the way the night out ended? I am so ashamed that I have suggested this restaurant to sooo many people and was equally excited to share this "rare gem" with my bf. I could go on and on about what should have happened, BUT at the end of the day IT DOESN'T MATTER. WE DON'T MATTER. OUR PATRONAGE DOESN'T/DIDN'T MATTER. AND YOURS MAY NOT EITHER. 

If I can keep one person from going to this snooty, stuck up, MONEY HUNGRY establishment I will be fine with that. I am going to contact the owner (luckily I have some inside info) and certainly make a big fuss. If you are on the fence about going---DON'T. This place totally let me down, but MORE importantly they just don't give a d*amn about their customers. At least some of their customers. I guess there are those who count and those who don't. I won't say anymore because it's not even worth getting into. 

R2L you officially are THE WORST. I will make it my mission to let everyone know AND I GOT A BIGGGGGG MOUTH! Shame on you! SMH

Don't go people.

Well, I let three years pass and tried again. No better this time, food and service-wise than back then. The biggest mystery to me is how they are still in business. I've heard management has turned over twice, but apparently this hasn't fixed things. Still serving frozen food dipped in the deep fryer or other stuff warmed-up in the oven. Folks, unless you are getting drinks or checking out the car and bike shows, you might want to eat at Buddy's or Chuy's before venturing on to Hot Rods. The only thing they might be successful at is keeping the Sysco trucks rolling in regularly.

I am an Eastsider and Eastsiders, for one reason or another tend to stay Eastside-with living or eating, but this is well worth the 25 mile trip Northwest. When their Tanque Verde location disappeared off the map about 3 years ago, we were very sorry to see it go. Best steakhouse around, period. When we saw that it had "re-surfaced" out Thornydale/Cortaro Farms Road 'way, I said, "we gotta hit this place, if it's anything like their Northeast location used to be, it's gonna rock". We did, just the other day, and here's the rundown:

Steaks cooked exactly (and I mean EXACTLY) like you asked for - Check

Solid steakhouse beans, cole slaw, and steak fries - Check

Many other good sides for those who like more variety in theirs - Check

Good bread "appetizer". It's like this pumpernickel deal. Served warm - Check

More entree stuff on the menu than just steak to please just about anyone - Check

Signature 'giant brownie' and ice cream dessert (this thing feeds 3, not kidding and it is great). The brownie is awesome, not one of those dense, rock-like things you get at some places - Check

They also have many other desserts, including bread pudding in Bourbon Sauce. This is also to die for. 

This place has not changed at all, except for location, and that's a good thing. Outback, Texas Roadhouse, etc. can't hold a candle to this place.

Judging by the owners response, it's obvious he takes no responsibility and doesn't care about customers. What a tool. Keep talking like this to people trying to support your business and you won't have one anymore. But then you'll just blame covid right?

3.5 stars

Wow, overrated?  Zwahlen's is very unique and very good, but it's not the most amazing place ever as so many other reviewers make it sound.  The ice cream technically isn't even ice cream and is more of a frozen custard.  That's not bad, but I think calling it ice cream is misleading.  I came expecting hand dipped ice cream, not sloppy soft-served custard.  Compared to other frozen custards, the texture is fine but the flavor isn't very good.  The vanilla tastes more like marshmallow, and the other flavors tasted phoney to me.  At least the prices are very right.

I think the main draw to Zwahlen's should be the desserts, or the chocolates.  They have an extensive array of freshly made candies, truffles, and chocolates.  They also offer a whole slew of desserts, like apple crisp, all served a la mode.

The restaurant itself is made to look like an eastern european lodge, and it's pretty charming.  I like that everything is fresh made, and it's cool that they have a flavor of the day.  Still, when all is said and done I'd probably still rather have a DQ Blizzard than return to Zwahlen's, but I would probably be back if they featured a flavor of the day that I was particularly drawn to.
