This place is SO awesome. I'll tell you why.

1) The sushi is FRESH. Oh-so-fresh. Nothing worse than sushi that isn't fresh, and they are on point. And simple. They don't need a bunch of crazy ingredients to cover up poor quality fish, because it's not poor quality at all.
2) Everything is DELICIOUS. Try the tuna cheek. And Pesce Hamachi. YUM!!
3) Everything is made with love, and presented beautifully. You can tell they really put their heart and soul into what they're doing.
4) The staff is extremely friendly and thorough.
5) It's AFFORDABLE. Seriously, nothing is overpriced; especially for the high-quality ingredients which they very apparently use.

This is, hands down, the best sushi in the city. I have found nothing even remotely comparable. It keeps getting better every time I go, too.

The location is out of the way, but it keeps it from getting too busy (and keeps the price point low due to low overhead). It's worth the trip, though, and I really want this place to succeed so I can keep eating there. So, get your ass in your car, and go, for the sake of me and my sushi cravings!

Why was this place so dead on a Friday night? I don't understand. Someone please explain this to me.

Hubby and I had been craving Indian food for a while and have been previously disappointed  by most of the places in Philly, so we decided to check out Mood this past Friday. We arrived at around 7:30 and we were the only ones in the restaurant. And it stayed that way. For the entire time we were there. I don't understand.

OK, so the location is a little weird. Mood is located on the ground floor of a loft condo building, and it's BYOB. Personally, I think this location would do better with a liquor license, but I'm not complaining. 

The reason I'm so confused is the food is seriously the best Indian food I've had in this city. We ordered paneer pakora (basically Indian mozzarella sticks, served with mint chutney and a tamarind dipping sauce), samosa chaat (like a deconstructed samosa- think Indian nachos), lamb seekh kabob, tandoori chicken and some garlic naan. They also served us a healthy portion of jasmine rice on the side. The only thing I wasn't completely crazy about was the lamb. I don't know if it was as fresh as what I'm used to. But everything else was seriously spectacular. The naan was served super fresh and piping hot, the chicken was served perfectly tender, juicy and full of great flavor, and the paneer cooked to perfection. 

The samosa chaat was probably the most memorable for me just because I found it to be so well put together. I could seriously eat this every day and be happy. When I see a dish like that, it makes me sad to think there are so many Americans who don't eat Indian food because they don't think it's accessible. What is more accessible than mozzarella sticks, barbecued chicken and nachos?

Bottom line: grab a bottle of wine and some friends and go to Mood. You will not be sorry.

Simply stated: No self-respecting Philadelphia native would ever eat here. What you will find here are tourists, Rangers fans, "bros" from South Jersey, and people who just plain don't know any better. The meat and cheese are always cold, the rolls soggy, onions undercooked, and there is hardly any meat on the sandwich at all. It's not the impression you want to get of a cheesesteak.

Do yourself a favor and go to John's Roast Pork, Gooey Louie's, or pretty much anywhere else in South Philly that isn't on that tourist trap corner.

Found my new bagel spot! Quick, friendly service, and the line can be long at times but moves decently quick enough. There are different specialty flavors every day of the week and certain cream cheese flavors seem to change too. I love the honey whole wheat everything bagel (toasted of course) with the spicy red pepper cream cheese ($3.20). The bagel was a great texture and not too heavy/dense. They also put the perfect amount of cream cheese. There's a morning special from 7-8am where you can get a bagel + cream cheese + coffee for only a little over $4! Great spot on Freret and so many adorable pups around to swoon over as you devour your freshly made bagel.

Nope.  Never again.  You cannot make me do it.  I do not care how few places there are in this area, I am not coming back. 

Okay, to be fair I will start with the good.  The concept in theory is good.  They have a lot of great memorabilia.  They have a large parking lot.  They have lots of seating.
Now on with it.  I have been here twice.  First time we sat in the bar at a high top.  Very few people were here.  It was a Tuesday night, however there are few places to go in Vail/Rita, it should be busier.  It took awhile to get service.  When we did it was just okay.  The bar selection is good, but they were out of a number of things.  (my guess is they don't have the customers to support the large selection and are not keeping it up). The food was sad.  That is the best way to describe it.  Bar and grill food should not be hard.  This was just really, really not good.  Portions were not right.  The chicken sandwich had one piece of wilted lettuce and a sad bit of cheese that was half melted.   It was served on bread (not buns), and half falling off the sandwich.  The stuffed jalepenos... well.  We pulled the "melted cheese" right out of the pepper.  The only saving grace was the pepper.  Took forever to get our check, was just an extremely disappointing night.

Second time, just wanted a drink and decided to swing in here.  Stopped in at the bar.  About five people in the whole place.  This is at 5 on weekday.  Not a big happy hour crowd.  There are groups of employees standing around near the bathroom, talking on their cellphones joking around with each other.  You can tell they do not abide by the "you have time to lean you have time to clean" policy.  There were dirty tables. 

Bar was again out of the one beer on tap I wanted.  The second one they had to switch kegs.  Again, it just felt sad being there.  Did not even attempt to look at food.

At this rate I do not imagine they will be open much longer which is unfortunate.  But no way would I recommend this place to anyone.  Especially travelers headed through town and swinging in off of I-10.  I would hate for that to be their impression of the area.

Tiny little cafe that fills up pretty quick, so get here early to beat the lines! I was quoted a 40 min wait the first time I tried to go. Luckily if you do need to wait, they offer free coffee outside! 

I love going out for breakfast, but lately breakfast places have been a little disappointing, but not Sky Blue! The menu isn't massive but offers a pretty good selection, and of course you can pick either savory or sweet breakfast. After eyeing some of the plates around me, I quickly figured portions are decent and I wouldn't need a whole dish to myself (I have a small appetite though). So my boyfriend and I shared the Brie stuffed French toast and the Tuscan 2.0. 

I love French toast and I love Brie cheese so I was pretty much guaranteed to love this. Fruit toppings were fresh. Brie was warm enough to provide a gooey filling. The Tuscan 2.0 was a standout dish! We've never really had a breakfast dish like this anywhere. The pesto topped French bread was packed with flavor and made an amazing base for this dish. Factor in the garlic, olive oil, tomato, and parmasean and you basically have your favorite Italian dish in a breakfast entree. 

Overall, Sky Blue Cafe is serving up some pretty unique dishes that are also delicious in a cozy little environment. It's not a fancy breakfast, but you'll enjoy it!

Mango Mango is a hidden gem located on Cherry St. I didn't know it exists until I saw a advertisement inside Xun Yu Si Kao. After a family brunch at Xun Yu's, we wanted something cold, sweet, and fruity. So we decide to hit Mango Mango.

Any yelpers ever try Fruit Life in Chinatown? Well, Mango Mango now sits at the same location of Fruit Life(I've heard FL moved to another location). 

As we entered, there were no seats available. We waited nearly half an hour for a table to
 become available. After we seated, it took a while to order and it took another half an hour to get our food. We got Vanilla Waffle sandwich, Mango Snow white slush, Mango Sago, and Mango Strawberry Slush. I have to say everything were very delicious. It was so freaking tasty that we waited another hour for more take outs( I know we are crazy lol).

I absolutely love this place, my only issues is the speed. That's why I give them 4 stars rather than 5.

As of right now, Oyster House is my favorite spot for shuck a buck. I've been dying to try Oyster House since finding them on Yelp few weeks back. Finally got a chance to try them this Saturday during their HH. When I arrived around 10pm. Oyster House is "jammed pack". What I mean is you can't walk anywhere without "excuse me" and "sorry" over and over again. Me and hubby were seated around 10:30 at the raw bar. Raw bar is the only seatings you can get HH menu. 

We got Kelly's Punch, clam chowders, Lobster roll, Seared Scallops, Oysters of the night during HH (Chesapeake), and Kusshi Oysters. I once thought RL got the best clam chowder but not after OH. Oyster House Clam chowder is one of the BEST in philly. Kelly's punch tastes like sangria with ginger, not my favorite. Lobster roll and Seared Scallops are oooh soooo good. I can't even describe how delicious they were, but we did cleared both of the entrees. Especially the sauce in Seared Scallops, I wanna lick the bowl clean lol. I didn't forget about the oysters, they were so fresh and tasty. For $1 each, is definitely worth it. And the Kusshi Oyster got cucumber flavor to it, which is so good. But it came with a hefty price tag of $3.50 each, I got two at $7.00. Probably will treat myself in the future.

Really loved the food. But it is very crowded in there. But I will return for their clam chowders and oysters during HH.

I called ahead and placed my order, but my order wasn't ready by the time I get there. Maybe because is about to close, they want to make sure the crepe is not gonna be eaten by their trash can:) At least I know my crepe is fresh this time, so I don't mind the wait.

I got the Matcha Azuki Bean with extra side of green tea gelato. Just one bite, I'm hook. I couldn't wait until I get home, I ate it in the car, it was that good. The crepe is lukewarm and a little crispy. Definitely love the creamy tastes.

A Cup of Tea is a hidden gem in Chinatown. Why is hidden? It is located on 9th street, a couple doors down from Asia Bank. As many of us who frequent Chinatown often knows there is not much "going on(variety of stores)" on 9th street, especially comparing to 10th street. 

I decided to try their famous foam tea, it can be made hot or cold, base on your preference. I got the Sakura Foam Tea and Rose Foam Tea, both cold. Hubby got his all time favorite, the Avocado Milk(Milkshake). Hubby says A Cup of Tea is his new favorite spot for Avocado shake. 

As for me, I drank the Rose Foam Tea within 10 minutes. That's how tasty it is. And the Sakura Foam Tea is equally as good too. It really tastes like milk tea with a slight salty flavor in the foam. Unlike milk tea, these tea are real tea not powder.

Many of you probably wondering how did I end up going to Yokohama of Maple Shade instead of staying in Philly? Well, my usual spot is usually Kyoto's, and after driving 20 minutes and found out they are take-outs only. So I yelped again, and try the surrounding restaurants and no luck. But I knew there will be plenty of options across the bridge. I yelped and found Yokohama of Maple Shade.

We were seated immediately the moment we enter. Our waiter Hong came over and took our drinks and appetizers. I wanted some kind of sweet alcohol, so Hong suggested Sweetheart Martini. I have to alter a bit bc i want the drink on the sweeter side. And it tastes so good that I decided to try Pear-Tini, not my favorite. We started with Miso soup, BBQ Squid, Fried Tempura Shrimp and Veggies, and Fried Shrimp Shumai. The Shrimp Shumai were so good that we got a second order. Hubby got a taste for hibachi so he order the Seafood Combination. He says this lobster, shrimp, and scallops combo is hard to get in Philly, he will definitely come back for more.

As for me, I want sushi. I order Tuna Dumplings, Kobe Beef Sushi, Live Scallop Sushi, Uni Sushi, King Crab sushi, Komo Oyster, and King Crab roll. Everything were really good, two stands out the most. I had Hokkaido's uni from another restaurant and didn't like the texture and the taste. But Yokohama's Uni are ohhh-so-good, I'm drooling while thinking of it lol. It got a more creamy texture and tastes, ok I need to stop now..... If you don't like eating raw sushi, may I suggest Kobe Beef sushi, trust me, you will thank me later! I was really there for the Double Toro roll, but their toro were sold-out today, what a bummer, but it is always a next time! 

We finished our meal with Vanilla ice cream, Green Tea ice cream, Coconut ice cream, and Mango Mochi ice cream. Everything were so good, we will be back!

P.S. Yokohama have suspended the Hibachi performance due to Covid, but entrees are still available just not cooking in front of customers.

It 's really hard for me to write such a negative review but something should be said. Our family has been going to this location for some time now and the service has been disappointing lately. First of all, as a customer, I do not care if you are having a bad day- I don't deserve your attitude. Secondly, if the app is not functioning properly, it is not our fault that machines have glitches. Don't give me an attitude saying I came at the wrong time to pick up my food because your system failed you and not even apologize. Lastly, be consistent with the amount of food I receive. I'm paying for a large and my bowl if half-filled. As I mentioned before, I've been going there for a while now so I know what a large should look like. 

Hopefully, you will be able to treat other customers with some respect after reading this.

Went for the first time last Sunday for a special occasion and all my expectations were exceeded.

First of all, great service. Our server, Jesse, took care of us the whole time. Our champagne flutes were never empty and had orange juice and water (with lemon, always a nice touch) brought to us (almost) without even asking.

The food: seafood, including raw oysters, oysters rockefeller, snow crab legs, shrimp, etc. On the meat side, I had the lamb chops and some cold cuts. They also have breakfast, of course, and had to try a few pieces of bacon and scrambled eggs. It was nice to see eggs benedict as well, but as you can tell, at this point I was mixing quite a bit of food so I stayed clear of those. After a few glasses of champagne I stopped caring I guess! And dessert options were incredibly tasty as well (we had chocolate tart and cheesecake), but it was hard to find room for it.

Steakhouse atmosphere, because that's what Sterling is, which is pretty nice of a setting compared to your typical casino buffet.

When you think about it, what you get out of this brunch makes it an amazing deal.

Overall a great experience and, though this may sound corny, made me love Reno a bit more.

Pho is one of those foods with many facets. There's the broth, the rice noodles, the meat and the garnishes. So nailing all of these aspects is rarely seen and this place almost does it.

I had #24 (rare meat, tendon and well done flank) and as usual I tasted the broth first. I was happy. They did it right. 
The usual garnishes were served along with it and a basic array of sauces are on the table for your own use (don't ever dump sauce on the broth. Ever.) I usually mix my own sauce to dip the meats.  

The noodles were different from all the other pho places I've been to. They were more chewy than usual and that was something new to me. Not sure if it's a style, the type of noodle or a bit of overcooking, but I didn't mind that too much.

Now the meats. The tendon was by the far the most tender I've had, silky and almost melting in your mouth. But I was a bit disappointed by the rare meat, which was too thin and flavorless and the flank as well. Also, I definitely would have preferred more meat on the bowl. But that's something that they can hopefully improve later.

Service was perfect. Friendly staff and a clean atmosphere added to the whole experience. 
Will definitely be coming back to taste some of their other plates.

Glad to see more Vietnamese spots like these in Reno.

My husband saw The Awful-Awful on TV and when we were in Reno he insisted we go to The Nugget to have it before we go home. So, we headed over to have lunch at the diner.

The Nugget is old and really smoky inside. I told my kids to hold their breaths until we got to the diner. It was REALLY packed when we arrived but managed to snag a few seats at the counter after people left.

My husband ordered:

- Bowl of Clam Chowder
The kids killed it and LOVED it.

- Hot Dog
Was HUGE! The boys shared it.

- 2 Awful-Awfuls
The Awful-Awful lived up to the hype! It's HUGE, delicious and came with a basket of fries. My sister & I split the awful-awful between the two of us and we didn't finish the fries. 

- Fried Calamari Sandwich
Tasted pretty good. The kids enjoyed it and we all had a taste.

The food came out pretty quick. The servers and cashiers were really friendly. We left with doggie bags. We will definitely be back for the Awful-Awful :)

Before heading home after our weekend in Reno I wanted pho. Pho 777 had some good reviews so I had my husband take us. 

It was busy when we arrived so I took it as a sign that the food was good... but I was wrong. Lots of people does not necessarily mean great tasting pho. It just meant lots of hungry people that were met with SUPER slow service at Pho 777.

- Spring Rolls: was dry and not at all that tasty
- Pho Ga: was kinda bland. I had to dress it up a lot with lemon juice, hoison & sriracha sauce and even then I was not a happy camper.
- Tai Nam Sach: my sister said it was alright. She didn't finish so that should tell you something.
- Pho Rau Tofu: Husband was not satisfied
- Wonton Soup: the kids said it was good

Next time we are in Reno we will try a different place for pho. Hubby was not a happy camper and was more than irritated at how long it took for us to get our food. The service was friendly but we won't be back. 

NOTE: NO Pho Bo Vien on Sundays :|

Folks be hatin' on Harrah's pretty hard. I went with a group of friends who after a bachelor shindig. Most of them live nearby and frequent this place pretty often and a couple were diamond members. I'm not much of a gambler so I only played a little. We spent most of our time in the high rollers area which was too rich for my blood but the staff were all great and I had a good time even though I wasn't playing much. The place is pretty big so make sure to have game plan on where to find each other if you're with a group of drunken thirty-somethings. Some of our group lost and some won. If you count my drinks for the night, I definitely won... maybe too big.

Oh damnnn Miguel's... you fancy! You can typically get in and out of a Mexican cuisine dinner for $10-$15 a head, but this spot is a little more high end. They've got plenty of entrees in the $30 range and the atmosphere is classier than your average taco joint. We came in for a group dinner and were seated in a glass walled room with a big table in the middle. I liked that they had the curtains you could close so it didn't feel like we were on display as an exhibit to the rest of the diners.

Our server told us the two must have items were the Margaritas and the Kurts Queso Dip so we started there. With our big table we ended up with a handful of different quesos and the kurts was definitely the best. It's a white cheese with ground beef and spices... easily a must have item. I knew I wanted the fajitas but I was torn amongst all the choices. They've got more than just your beef or chicken options here. Mi amigo and I decided to go halfsies so that we could both try the Kobe Beef and the Lobster fajitas.

A handful of others also ordered the Kobe Beef and to be honest it was somewhat disappointing. I've had Kobe a handful of times and it wasn't as tender as it should be. On the other hand, the Lobster was excellent. We had it poblano style which added a ton of flavor. Unfortunately, there was a minimal amount of lobster in the dish for the money. We definitely enjoyed the private room and the excellent staff. The food was good but a little pricey for what you get in my opinion.

I came for the blackened Fresh Florida Grouper Sandwich and it didn't disappoint but it didn't wow me either. If you're here it's probably the item to get. I was also interested in the seafood chowder. It only comes in a bowl so I got my friend Will on board so we could split it. They actually brought it out split in two for us which was thoughtful. My interest was mostly based on how much seafood they've packed into this bowl. It's got clams, grouper fish, and even shrimp in here. I thought it was just okay and could have had more quantity of the seafood and less of the chowder.

The Depot is one of my go-to places for dinner with friends in Reno! I love the atmosphere here and the history behind the building, being an old train station definitely ups the cool factors. 

When you first arrive there is a small parking lot in the front to the left of the building, but there's another parking lot if you drive further back that usually has a spot or two open. There is outdoor seating which is really nice during the summer spring and fall, and first-come first-serve bar seating in the downstairs area. There's also more seating upstairs, which is usually where they will put you if you have a large group. 

The service here has always been really great! One time my grilled chicken burger wasn't all the way cooked, and they immediately apologized and brought out a new one. The cocktails and beer are all delicious, and the the grilled chicken sandwich and spring burrito are two of my favorites. Will definitely be back again soon!

I have loved coming to Poke King ever since it first opened two years ago! I can't believe how long they've been here. And during that time their wonderful service and pricing has stayed pretty much the same!

All the food they have here is very good, and if you are ever overwhelmed with all the options the staff is usually very kind and helpful in helping you pick out whatever you need. There is also a points system where you enter your phone number and earn points to get a deal once you order a certain number of times. I personally always get the salmon, tuna and yellowtail, and usually if I get a large at lunch time, and save it in my refrigerator, I have another large portion of that for dinner!

Will always come back here - especially now that it's almost summer!

Sakana Sushi in Somersett has been one of my favorite spots for sushi in town for a long time. The quality of the sushi here definitely stands out from many of the other AYCE sushi places in town, and the atmosphere is always pleasant. Throughout the COVID pandemic they were really taking customer health and safety into account by spacing out tables, taking reservation only, and having all staff wear masks. Now that restrictions have been lifted things are a little different, they are no longer taking reservations ahead of time, although I have found that they are still taking reservations the afternoon and night of, so I would just be aware of that if you are planning on heading there, especially on a weekend night! 

The nice thing about this place is the atmosphere, lots of walking around you can do before or after your meal to walk off all that sushi you just ate! They also have a great variety of fantastic fish, and I would definitely recommend seeing if the sushi chefs have a special for that night as well. My only qualm with Sakana in the past is that the service is a bit slow at times, but only because they are so busy! Expect things to take a  little time, and if you are patient, you will definitely be happy with the quality of food that you get.

Ordered Take-Out and was very pleased with the meal! We ordered Steak Pho, Vegetable Pho, Beef Drunken Noodles, and a Shrimp Summer roll. The Pho was a huge portion and tasted fantastic! The drunken noodles were delicious and the beef inside was super tender. The summer roll had a lot of rice in it which I wasn't used to but was still good with the peanut sauce. Overall would definitely order from here again and would recommend to others!

I have been here more times than I can count, and I've always loved it. Their fries were always on point, their dipping sauces magical, and the wraps at least decent, usually very good. 

Then I went there after taking a little Old City hiatus and I was appalled. The service was terrible, the woman at the counter was incredibly rude. The trash was overflowing, the tables were scuzzy, and I felt like I was inconveniencing them by patronising their restaurant. 

She was scolding me for not wanting a soda, it made no sense. I ordered the meal combo; wrap, fries, and a soda. Okay, but I don't want a soda, so just a water. She "informed me" in a raised voice that she will still charge me for the water in addition to the meal. I don't understand, you're going to charge me for 2 drinks? I just want a water. So she huffily says it's fine, then charges me for it anyway! ??! What? No, lady, I pay for the combo, I get a drink. That's kind of how that works. 

So now she's pissed, the guy from the back has to come up and I tell him the same thing, I just want the combo with water instead of soda, is this really the craziest thing that's ever happened here? The guy tries to offer me a soda, when I tell him I ONLY want the water, not a soda too, he says it's fine, just pay for the combo and get a water. Like, literally less than no big deal.

Oh Lord, I go to pay-- finally. And I only have a big bill. I just got paid, in cash, and I didn't have time to stop at the bank. I only have a $100 or a $50. She says she can't take it. At all. she can't take my money now. Well, it's a holiday, all the banks are closed and there's no MAC machines nearby. I can't give you anything else. This place is filled with customers, you're telling me that you don't have two $20s in your drawer? 

Fine, whatever, I'm not in the mood to argue with her.... again. I ask if they take cards, she snaps back, Of course they do! again, this is somehow also my fault. (?) Okay then, the card is all I have if you won't take my money. So without saying anything, she adds on a surcharge for the card and runs it, I notice when I go to sign... Hey, why is this more than what it's supposed to be? 

Again, she's mad that I had the audacity to ask why I'm being charged a different amount than what I ordered, I thought she was charging me for the soda + water. She starts in with how "I'm costing them money by holding up the line and now I'm not paying and OF COURSE there's a surcharge, why wouldn't there be and how dare you question me I wouldn't steal from you" and I was like are you kidding me? Now I'm definitely NOT paying a surcharge that I probably would have been fine with before you flipped out. Take my cash or comp my meal. I'm done. I'm so far beyond done.

Guy from the back comes back out, tells her to take the cash, she's glaring the entire time she's counting out my change. Tells me to wait, it'll be right up.

I've found a seat, with my back to the counter. I like to be able to see the door when I'm out and about. So they (dunno if her or him) put my food down on top of the bakery case, and don't say anything. Like, I'm supposed to divine when my meal is ready. After a few minutes, I get up to inquire if I'm actually going to get anything in return for my money and she points at my now cold food on the bakery case. AREYOUKIDDINGME. 

Whatever. I'm leaving, I'm furious and I just want to enjoy my food. What's on the tray? no water. no dipping sauce. The sauce is 90% of the reason to go here!!!! It's certainly not the service!!! So I go up to the counter.... AGAIN. 

Excuse me, I need the sauce and my water. she yells that I can get my own water, from the case. It's bottled water. ?? What? You have fountain sodas literally right next to you. Whatever. I'll take my bottle of water. the guy comes back out because the lady is yelling again. I tell him I need the dipping sauce. She's like, you really want free stuff? Really? No, crazy lady, I want what I paid for, this is crazy. 

Now the guy's pissed and he asks which one I wanted, I told him that I ordered the jalapeno one.... back when I placed this order. He slaps it down on the counter at me. 

I'm NEVER going back. I couldn't believe how INSANE that experience was. So if you don't mind getting secretly charged extra, getting screamed at, terrible service, and having a mediocre wrap with really good fries, check this place out!

We went there a few weeks ago, soon after it opened... perhaps too soon.  I'm a sucker for Asian buffets and sushi/sashimi in particular -- and not too hard to please.  Noburu? One of the worst eating experiences ever!  The fish quality was mediocre.  The sashimi was cut improperly (do not use the word "chef" for these poorly trained employees).  The Chinese dishes were uninspired, routine and badly prepared.  Steam table-itis all around.  

With all due respect to those that rated this place with five stars, you've never been to Minado's.  Try that Japanese seafood buffet.  If you do and still think Noburu rates, I'll eat my chop sticks.
Good food, OK wine list, horrid service; will give one more try...

When they were in their previous location, I had good experiences.  This time, was awful.

Our group took nearly 2.5 hours to be seated.  And when we were waiting on the patio to be seated inside, we were told we could not sit outside, despite a number of chairs on the patio.  One of the folks in our groups has MS and uses a walker with a seat on it.  When she sat on the walker outside, she was quickly chastised by the wait staff for sitting outside.  So, she had to sit inside with a few folks while the rest of us waited outside for a table.

Waitstaff told us for over an hour a table was being cleared for us, and it should be ready in 15 minutes.  This went one for approximately 1.5 hours.  This, along with overpriced drinks, was a sore disappointment.  No apologies, nor any mitigation appeared to have taken place by their staff.

The kicker about all of this, is that it was a going away party for a co-worker that beat a particularly aggressive form of cancer that she shouldn't have survived.  Many of us left early, myself included.  

I'm not willing to give any money to a business that treats their customers so poorly will not be  getting any of my money.  This was a disappointing experience.

i always thought this place was a little pretentious, but sometimes that's okay. the unspoken "no talking rule" enforced by the laptop kids was always obnoxious, but the drinks and staff made up for it.

until one afternoon, i saw a customer getting reamed by a person who seemed to be an owner or manager behind the counter.

the argument seemed to be about Chapterhouse's minimum for credit cards -- which is, by the way, illegal. the owner/manager guy even acknowledged this, but acted like the customer was deserving of punishment for even asking!

it seemed like the customer gave up and went to sit down when the owner guy mumbled something else, wouldn't let it go and in my opinion was looking for a fight.

the climax? at one point this owner guy actually said: "it's my business. i can do whatever the f i want." the customer left at this point and the owner guy kept mumbling and banging things.

no, actually, you can't do whatever you want. there are plenty of laws for businesses, intended to protect patrons and keep the peace. the dogs in Chapterhouse? also not cool and totally illegal and a health code violation. also some people are just plain uncomfortable with dogs; talk about tunnel vision.

not going there ever again. that was ugly to see.

Come for the view and that's about it. 

Drinks are watered down and food is bland. Plus the outdoors area is filthy.

Workers are nice though.

I just visited and I must say the food was good.  My problem came after I paid and was leaving.  The owner, older lady sitting outside, said you have to pay your bill and tried to keep me from leaving.  I had the receipt in my pocket, with a good tip on it, showing I paid.  The waitress came and said I didn't pay and when I showed her the receipt she suddenly remembered and then said I didn't give it back to her.  I handed it to her when she passed the table.  Then she remembered.  Talk about being totally embarrassed. I will never go there again and I don't recommend it with how they treat their customers.

By far the best Mexican food we've had in Tampa. We've been twice now and it's phenomenally flavorful. We've gotten tacos, sopes, and tamales. Our favorites have been the shrimp and the Chile relleno but we haven't been upset at anything we've rated there. Overall it's our go to Mexican food in Tampa and I can't wait to explore more on the menu

I could see how this place would seem kitchy to native Philadelphians.  I, however, was totally into the kitch!  I felt like each time you climbed the stairs you ended up in a place that was even more ridiculous than the next.  And I LOVED every moment of it!  

First floor is old time diner looking.  Looks of shiny retro accessories.  We came around 9p and there were still families (what?!) in the dining room.  We climbed the stars to the upstairs bar and the first thing that caught my eye was the swinging basket chairs.  I ran over to sit in one....I just had to!  Too bad five people couldn't have fit into one or I may have been swinging there all night!

The drinks are complete froo froo girly cocktails.  I love the candy garnishes they give with all of them.  I actually wanted to ask what candy was at the bottom of mine, but I drank too many...and forgot!  If you walk behind the upstairs bar there's these animal shaped chairs to sit on. It took everything I had to not put one under my arm (if I was a body builder and could lift them) and run away with it to.  I want one for my house!  

The FINAL level is the upstairs patio/bar.  That's were the vibe tends to shift to the nighttime "out on the prowl" club scene.  There's a huge lounge area with fireplaces and chairs to sit and sip.  The deck also serves dinner, so it's a great place to take advantage of the summer weather.  

But let's not get lost in the decor, because you totally can!  We also ate dinner there.  It's tapa style dining so since we had 5 people we each decided to pick a dish.  Our choices were the lamb flat bread, ahi tuna tarter, philly steak egg rolls, kofka, lobster mac n' cheese, hanger steak  and shoestring fries.  You can't NOT come here and get that massive mound of fries.  It felt like I was eating crispy air and it was delish.  

My fav tapa by far was the lamb flat bread.  It was almost like a lamb meatball that was Indian inspired.  Very tasty.  I also enjoyed the hanger steak which came with blue cheese mash taters.  I was pretty disappointed with the mac n' cheese.  It was made with very thin rice noodles and lacked any flavor.  

If I lived in Philly I would ABSOLUTELY take tourists here and since I was a tourist, I obviously had a great tour guide!  And if it's kitchy, I'm usually in!

I feel like it's few and far between now where I have a delicious meal from start to finish, and I totally did here! I started with the crispy veggies, which was just a preview of what was to come! It was seriously so good. They describe it as a chow chow, I was still a little curious as to what it would taste like, but definitely glad to order it!

I'm happy to report they carry gluten free pasta, so I was able to order the lamb ragu. It wasn't with the papperdelle noodles (those are so good, I remember pre-gluten free), but it didn't matter. The flavor is what mattered, and it was delicious, with an ample amount of lamb. 

Service was excellent and we topped it off with dessert, which for me was a excellent hazlenut ice cream. It just capped off a wonderful dining experience in a casual, yet approachable restaurant.

I was not happy with my Asian chicken salad ($11.50).  Never at any restaurant (ANY restaurant) has a Chinese (or "Asian") chicken salad been so disappointing, especially for that price.  There wasn't much iceberg lettuce, but worse, it wasn't fresh.  Lots of bell peppers and celery.  The cilantro ginger soy dressing was not chilled and didn't have great flavor.  But really, the worst part about the salad was the dry-ass, unseasoned chicken!  That makes me mad thinking that I wasted stomach space on this dish.  Thank God I ordered some potstickers ($6) for an appetizer that were really tasty, cooked perfectly, and served with a delicious sauce.  My friends said I should send my food back to the kitchen, but I didn't feel like waiting while everyone else was enjoying their food, and honestly I'm not real big on sending food back because you never really know what you'll be getting instead!  IJS.  I ate half of it since I was starving, then just picked food off of my boyfriend's club sandwich and fries ($10).

The only reason we ate here was because we had a $5 voucher to use at any Silver Legacy eatery, we just missed the end of the Flavors Buffet for lunch (served til 2pm), and not everyone wanted the oyster bar.  Service was alright since we had multiple people helping us throughout our meal and the restaurant was pretty busy at the time.   I'm not totally counting out Café Central since everyone else's food was average to good, but I won't be ordering their Asian chicken salad (or anything else that has chicken in it) again.

This is an excellent stop for happy hour and to grab a bite to eat. Parking isn't ideal, they have a super tiny lot (maybe 10 parking spots) in the back. There is also a parking lot next to WOB but you have to pay to park, which is not unusual for SOHO. There isn't really an inside area, everything is outdoors which is great when the weather is nice. It's a pretty small outdoor area but we didn't have a problem finding a seat.

They have happy hour from 4-7 on the weekdays which consists of beer, spirits, wine, and select appetizers. Get the $5 mac and cheese bites. If you're looking on the normal menu, get the German pretzel with beer cheese, you won't regret it!

We came on a Tuesday evening for trivia. Trivia is from 7-9 pm with prizes and there's adult trivia from 9-10 pm with prizes as well. Tuesday is also their Taco Tuesday night, so they have drink and taco specials. They also do Ladies' Night on Thursday. 

Our waitress was very attentive and checked on us the whole time we were there, no complaints there. We will definitely be back.

We decided to go to the historic Jimmy Kelly's for our 29th Anniversary dinner, as we had one year ago, and were excited to see the recently completed renovations they announced in their emails.  Unfortunately, as soon as we arrived, we were taken directly through the first dining room out the side door to a table situated on the inside porch, so we really didn't see any changes from the last time we were there.  The host showed us to the table located at the doorway to the patio, and walked away, not noticing the errant jumbo shrimp tail that awaited me at my place setting.  Gross.

Another couple was then seated at the table across from us.  As we sat at our empty table with that random crustacean remnant staring at us, I couldn't help but notice as a waiter promptly arrived at the other table, greeted them with menus and took their beverage order.

Minutes passed as we sat waiting to see who our server was.  The other table received their drinks and a sample of house corn cakes, and we fidgeted awkwardly, talking about the menu we had read online, wondering when we would see one in person. I actually watched that table receive their salads before we even met our waiter.

Finally a server came over, introduced himself, but before anything further, I asked him to please remove the shrimp shell.  He snatched it up, apologized and said he'd return with glasses of water.  It wasn't until he brought waters that he delivered the menus and we asked if there were any specials that night.  He stated there were not, though he did tell us about the fish of the day, which happened to be the same as one year ago, Chilean Sea Bass with Beurre Blanc, but I'd had that last visit and was looking to try something different.  We did request some bourbons and an order of the crab cakes appetizer, which were over-cooked on the bottom but otherwise satisfactory.

We then decided upon our entree. I've always wanted to try the Chateaubriand for Two so we ordered that and although all other entrees came with salad and baked potato, we were told it came with salad and broccoli. Knowing I don't particularly care for plain, steamed broccoli, my husband asked the waiter to "dress it up" for us. Salads arrived, but I remembered from last year that the house salad was and still is the definition of "meh." Just mixed greens, two little tomatoes and a tart balsamic. 

Aware that our entree took longer to prepare, it was probably about 30 minutes later that I smelled an aroma surround me and asked my husband if our food had arrived. Our server was busy somehow preparing the entree, but I have no idea how it looked upon arrival nor what the preparation process involved, since he had situated his tray behind me.  

The oval plates were presented before us, containing from left to right: broccoli, sliced mushrooms, three hearty slices of filet topped with burgundy sauce. Both the beef, perfectly cooked to requested medium-rare, and burgundy sauce were delicious, mushrooms were adequate, broccoli was completely uncooked, no seasoning whatsoever, definitely not worth the effort to chew. Temperature on all was tepid at best.

As the other waiter gave the table across from us their check, he asked if it was a special occasion, and accordingly wished them a happy anniversary as they were paying their bill.

We chose to share a dessert, the apple pie cobbler.  It arrived on a very hot, flat plate, making it difficult to chase around the melted ice cream.  I found the cobbler itself to be grainy, pasty and rather unappealing.  This was one of the very few times we left more than half of a dessert on the plate.

We waited too long to get the check, especially since our table was situated directly over the air conditioning vent, and it was definitely blowing cold air through the second half of our meal.  The bill finally arrived, along with a Customer Satisfaction Survey brochure, which I was going to fill out, but reaching for a pen in my purse as I opened the flyer, I discovered that it had already been completed, dated two days before. That customer actually left praises, perhaps a Saturday is a better night to dine there than our Monday.  

When we were first seated. there was a party on the patio, so it was pretty noisy, but it disbursed about halfway through our visit.  Still, it was awkward being in the doorway of the two. Nothing was as annoying as the constant creaking and banging as the door to the inside was continuously used by the wait staff throughout service.

The atmosphere itself in the room, which was a type of sunroom, perhaps, was uncomfortable, awkward. I didn't feel like a valued guest, instead felt like we were gratuitously being "fit in" at some extra space. Our waiter was not particularly attentive nor accommodating, though he certainly was cordial and personable.

As we were leaving we noted that our server never asked if it was any occasion.  In fact, there was nothing about the visit that felt even remotely special.

Okay... here is the scoop... i've been wanting to go to year since it opened. The chicken and rice in New York  is phenomenal.   here I noticed, they put a lot of rice and salad at the bottom and stack it up, then put a thin layer of beef and chicken. So what I got was a big layer of rice and salad , and a thin layer of chicken and beef.  

And they don't mention to tell you that the hot red sauce  is extremely hot.   They should warn customers that the red sauce is really hot.   More then three stripes and food is uneatable.  

But overall the food was great.  

Here's why I gave it low  stars.  CUSTOMER SERVICE.  

No one wants to walk into a store , and have people behind the counter making jokes or making fun at the customers.  That's what the cashier behind the register and another guy who had his hands folded , doing nothing was doing.  I looked up and he's staring at me laughing with the cashier. Maybe my face was funny looking to hiM... maybe I reminded him Donald trump I don't know.  

As soon as he saw me staring back at him and realized I understood him and the cashier were talking about me he walked away.  

For that reason, my first and last time at the Halal...

I don't Care how good the food is, you have to provide great customer service.  
Hopefully management reviews this and makes some necessary changes.  This happened on 10/13 around 5 pm.

Walking into Drama Burger and I couldn't shake the thought of the old Chinese restaurant with a paint job and some new decor. I just couldn't get my mind away from the gross and erie feeling of the failed restaurants of past.

After sitting down, taking in the atmosphere, my opinion quickly began to change...  

Lounge style seating on one side with black couches and unique chairs and lighting fixtures throughout the rest. A cozy bar with four seats an open look into the kitchen. Red, white, and blue colors cary throughout the walls making this Lithuanian owned restaurant a bit American feeling. Clean, sharp, and different. So far, visually, I like it.

We started with the black breadsticks. Weird, right? When she dropped them off I was surprised. Long pieces of thin black bread with sunflower seeds in them and a side of homemade thick blue cheese dressing to go with.  Crunchy on the outside and soft in the middle... Not exactly the breadstick most people will think of, but man are they great! Good size portion will fill you up quickly and the homemade blue cheese is a great compliment. It's not a runny, watery, ranch dressing with blue cheese crumbles. This is the real deal. Thick and viscous. Rich in flavor to compliment the bread.

Fridays- Sundays they have Pastrami, which is the house specialty. It takes 9 days to prepare so this is the reason for weekend only Pastrami. Two options here, Pastrami sandwich or pastrami burger($12). I opted for the later since I wanted a burger in the first place. However, when in Rome. Also, this is their most expensive burger on the menu. I believe another is priced the same but this is as expensive as the burgers get.

Served on a fluffy and buttery brioche bun, this burger was top notch. From the homemade mayo and mustard, to the fresh produce. The burger itself was great, cooked medium as per house preference. Still full of flavor and the hot pastrami was a real kicker. I loved it. I don't think specialty burgers can get better than this. 

Fries come separate, which is common and a lot places now. I split the sweet potato fries with the party I was with. Good choice after the appetizers. These sweet potato fries are top notch. Not from a frozen bag, not from anywhere. House made, cut straight from the potato. Different size pieces make for different texture on each one, which was great. They were also letting us try the different sauces for the fries that they offer free of charge because they want people to get accustomed to them. We opted for the truffle ketchup and chipotle mayo. The mayo with the fries was awesome, can't beat sweet and spicy. I don't like ketchup, it's a Chicago thing. However, the truffle ketchup is something I could eat on occasion. That's saying a lot, believe me. 

The beer list was good, seasonal and local selections along with a nice variety of bottles. They even have some milkshakes on the menu, which is great! I'm gonna have to get one next time!

Now, here's where I will say I was left shocked.

I came here expecting a good burger, I got it. I didn't come here expecting delicate, decadent, and amazing desserts. Mind blown.

The red velvet cake dessert was unreal. Rich RV cake with cream cheese on bottom, vanilla ice cream, topped with chocolate shavings, blueberries and diced strawberries. The presentation was unreal, the taste, equally as good. Visually, this dessert was as good as it gets. From a BURGER place?! Here's the kicker, it was $3.... That price won't last long, severely under priced, and I'm lucky to have been there when it was.

This dish was something I would expect to see at many other restaurants, yet here it was, at a revamped and remodeled Chinese shop that now slings specialty burgers and Pastrami. 

The Key Lime panna cotta was a perfect compliment to the RV dessert. It was tangy, creamy, and just the perfect hint of key lime. Very elegantly presented, made it look dainty but the food spoke for itself. Powerful punch of creamy tartness, which I loved. I can't believe these two came from a burger place. Unreal.

Kudos, Drama burger and kitchen staff alike. I will be back.

Sushi conveyor belts rolling delicious options to every table just like I remembered in Japan but with a modern american twist!

Having experienced conveyor belt sushi restaurants in Japan & NYC, I was so excited that a place like this finally exists in Tampa. Came here with the misses & wanted to try just about everything on the menu. kind of like Japanese tapas as the dishes are small enough to encourage you to grab a few to get full. Pretty simple concept, you sit & watch the food roll by ...  if you like it, you just pick it up off the conveyor belt, take the cover off the plate & eat away ! 

each dish is priced according to the color of the plate, and when your finished the waiter tallies the damage on your bill. with so many yummy things rolling by, it can be easy to rack up a hefty bill so just be careful because you pretty much want to eat everything that flashes across your eyes. 

I loved that everything on the menu had a picture on which made it easier to know what you were looking for. be sure to look out for the time stickers on the plate covers to check the freshness of the sushi on the conveyor belts! every dish we enjoyed alot as it came out fresh & hot since it was cooked straight from the kitchen! 

super friendly staff any awesome waiters! they actually took me & the misses 10 minutes before closing & didnt turn us super hungry folks away ... thank you ! i could see this place doing well as its smack in the middle of international plaza & a new concept with the conveyor belt gimick not seen in tampa as of yet!

Beautiful space, very enjoyable atmosphere, friendly and efficient service, and great coffee. I am not a big fan of Turkish delight or toffee. I am picky with textures and I find those treats a little chewy and sticky. 

I was hoping to find some pastries or chocolate. Sadly that will not happen as this business will be focused on confectionery. 

I will definitely go back with a friend to enjoy a cup of coffee. And will give the toffee a second chance.

Even though Corazon was our intended destination, we did a quick lap around the Santa Barbara Public Market to see what other options were around the eatery. Not only did Corazon have the longest line, they practically had the only line. We took it as a good sign and patiently stood in the queue.

The woman who took our order was super helpful letting me know what items are vegan or can be veganized. Here's what vegan items we got:

- Butternut Squash taco http://bit.ly/2J5HHFw
- Fried Plantains & Black Beans
- Guacamole http://bit.ly/2GT1042
- Horchata http://bit.ly/2GgHcuh

Aesthetically, I absolutely adored the colors and presentation of the tacos. There's something about watermelon radish that makes anything look so pretty!

Flavor-wise, I totally love the flavor combinations. The Cauliflower taco was not just a cauliflower taco but tempura-battered cauliflower with almonds, Medjool dates, sunflower sprouts, and salsa verde. The sweetness of the dates and crunch of the almonds were a nice texture.

Just thinking about the Butternut Squash taco has me drooling! The roasted squash had this beautiful caramelization. Avocado makes any dish awesome and I loved the pops of color, and tanginess, from the pomegranate seeds. And if this wasn't already enough color on the plate, this features gluten-free blue corn tortillas. Yum!

The Fried Plantains & Black Beans didn't really do it for me but the Guacamole and Horchata is legit good!

Totally worth another visit!

We were researching breakfast places in the area and decided to check out this place for two reasons:

1) The menu offers a vegan breakfast burrito
2) The Meateater BF loves biscuits and gravy

Upon arrival, parking was competitive. Tiny parking lot with no one leaving anytime soon. We ended up parking in the lot across the street but I cannot advise if they allow this or not.

Busy place for 11am on a Saturday but they sat us right away. Large dining area and more tables on the patio outside. The atmosphere is a basic/clean diner and I appreciate that they didn't choose kitchey New Orleans Cajun decor.

Breakfast Burrito No.3 is filled with soyrizo, black beans, potato, and avocado. The portion size was slightly more than enough to fill me up. All ingredients involved was delicious! One strange thing about it was I had one bite of burrito that had a red grape. You know, if there's going to be an accidental ingredient in my breakfast burrito, I'd rather it be a grape and not meat! :) http://bit.ly/2HVUEjD

The Meateater BF wasn't super impressed with his biscuit but liked the gravy. But he can write his own review ;P

The garlic heads are sprouting, the blueberries are molding, the greens are limp, and the tomatoes are flavorless.  The people who work at the deli are either cold and grunt at you or are unresponsive.  The aisles are poorly organized.  

And the cashiers? The first time I shopped here, I was shouted at for placing my basket on the conveyor belt.  One time a cashier gave me the stink eye for having the nerve to ask him if his line was open.  

Recently, I watched a cashier take out the garbage from beneath his register, and then reach for my strawberries to scan them.  I stopped him right there and asked him to wash his hands.  That was the last time I subjected myself to the "Fresh" Grocer.  I would rather trek a mile to Trader Joe's than pay for crappy produce and even worse customer service.  The employees act like working here is punishment.

They say you get what you pay for. When you pay $6.95 for an all you can eat brunch, you get powdered eggs, over oiled omelette's and deep fried bacon that curls up.

After a long night out the grease helped to soak up the alcohol but the food wasn't cry good. For being a Greek restaurant, I really expected more of a touch of Greek on the buffet. For example, there was no spinach to add to the omelette's making a Greek omelette.

This brunch left such a bad taste in my mouth, I don't think I will go back and try their Greek food for lunch or dinner.

A Mecca of SUPERB Mexican food. A must-go for authentic mexican-cuisine!! 

 I will be back again to bring friends and family. :)

Have had takeout twice in the past couple months.  Super friendly people answering the phone, quick service, beautiful presentation and awesome portion sizes!  All the soups are amazing and so are the salads.  I had every soup, my fav is the mushroom Thai soup!  Thanks guys for offering takeout during these times and making dining in a nice treat!

On my best friend's bucket list when traveling to St. Pete's was Hurricanes, her family's childhood haunt for grouper sandwiches.

Their Yelp reviews were less than stellar so I was not expecting much when walking in but surprisingly, I had a great meal! The three story restaurant is set in a quaint Victorian looking beach house that looks over beautiful Pass-a-grille Beach. We sat on the top level so we could enjoy the Gulf breeze and the sights.

I decided to go for the grouper sandwich since that is what they are known for and I'm so glad I did (my friend went with their shrimp po' boy and was grossly disappointing). Blackened was the way to go and my fish came out hot, flaky and meaty and on a hearty potato roll. You have a couple of options of sides but I went for the onion rings which was a yummy beach side treat. Honestly, it was really good -- even better than the grouper sandwich I had the night before at a four star rated restaurant down the street.

If you go here, stick with the house special and a frozen drink, don't expect great service and you should be good to go!

Finding a highly rated brunch spot with no wait on a Sunday afternoon is like walking out from Target and spending less than $50...pretty damn near impossible. Thanks to Yelp and the 726 other people who led us to Roux!

Located in a strip mall somewhere in Tampa, I was a little bit worried when we pulled in the parking lot. But that's the last time I judge a book by it's cover because this was the best meal I had during my entire trip.

Between us three girls we ate EVERYTHING:
+ Crawfish Beignets: Light as a feather, melts in your mouth and that saffron dipping sauce? Divine! 
+ Chargrilled Oysters: At $1 a pop, how could we say no? One slurp immediately brought me back to my last vacation in the Big Easy 
+ Monkey Bread: The reverand's wife who used to teach my Sunday school used to bring in her world famous monkey bread on special occassions and this was just as good!
+ Crawfish Hash: This was the only dish I wasn't crazy about, it just had too much flavor going for me. Or it could have been the fact that I had already eaten 80 other things as well. But the potatoes were cooked perfectly and there were plenty of crawdaddy meat all about.
+ Cajun Crab Cakes Benedict: Perfectly poached egg, 100% no filler crab cake and came with the most addicting cheesy hashbrown casserole side 
+ Bread Pudding: Free with Yelp check in and you know I was going to take advantage! It came hot in a cast iron skillet and was the perfect way to end our meal. It was super rich and if you don't order it with a side of ice cream you are doing it wrong.

Service was absolutely on point. We were a high maintenance table in just the sheer amount of food we ordered but our server Amanda did not bat an eye. Even when she was double sat, her teammates popped in and effortlessly covered for her. I was really impressed!

This would be a great place to host a private event or brunch party due to their many rooms and ability to host large tables. Happy eating!

I don't know what possessed me to walk down to the Garden District in heels but by the time I hit Magazine Street I was dying. I pulled up my trusty Yelp app to find a place to refresh my spirit. While I was sitting in a nearby ice cream parlor I saw a review for this crawfish shop and immediately made a change of plans.

Big Fisherman's is nothing fancy. It's your standard seafood shop and it's take out only. However, they sell crawfish on the cheap! $4.99 got us a pound of jumbo crawfish and we also added an order of corn, potatoes, and half pound of shrimp to round everything out for a total of $16.

The crawfish are precooked and did not have the spicy butter coating that is usually found at places like Hot N Juicy but that did not stop it from being lip smacking good.

As other Yelp reviewers have noted you can go to the pizzeria across the street and use one of their outside tables if you buy beer. Do this. Beer is EXTREMELY cheap, I got two Abitas for $7 and if you go on Monday - Thursday you can get a whole pitcher for $7.

You can NOT get prices like this in DC. This was my favorite impromptu meal in New Orleans. 

They also accept American Express, zing!

Pour some sugar on me and I will like it and ask you to do it again! 

Samples samples samples...they have tons and plenty for you to try! And they are FREE! Who can argue with free? 

Of course I found the one candy store in New Orleans that was on almost every few blocks in the French Quarter. My job is to find the best treats in every city that  I visit, so when I found this place it was like I hit the jackpot! They have so many samples it's like I came in for dessert, but I don't like to take advantage and eat all their treats. So I decided to up buy:

-A King Cake (specialty Mardi Gras) 
-Praline cookies (all different flavors) 
-Bar of Cajun White Chocolate Macadamia Nut (sweet and spicy but so good) 
-Chocolate covered Oreos 

The customer service was excellent and the prices were average. Laura's was super sweet just how I like my desserts!

These D-O-N-U-T-S...OMG... All I can say is good thing I don't live by this place or I'd be in big trouble! This place was voted one of the TOP 10 donuts shops in America and I definitely know why! 

Recently I made a trip to New Orleans for Mardi Gras and District Donuts was on my radar all the way from Los Angeles! Um yeah... I can sniff out good donuts from hundreds of miles away! 

 When I first walked in there was a line, but that didn't deter me. I was only worried they might run out of donuts and I was anxious to get my order in. The line looked pretty long but it only took me about 10 minutes to get through it. I was a overwhelmed because I wanted to try...um..all of them but I can only eat so much. When I finally got to the front of the line I found out my biggest nightmare had came true, they were sold out of the King cake donut, and that was the one I was really looking forward to trying! I asked them if I could pre-order it and wait to the side because they were cooking them, but they said they couldn't do that. I understood because there were so many people that wanted them that people pre-ordering could get confusing. 

If you're not familiar what king cake is, it is a cake during Mardi Gras in New Orleans that is covered with different colors like pink, purple, and yellow. Inside they hide a baby. The tradition is, whoever finds the baby in the king cake has to buy the next king cake. These cakes are very popular during Mardi Gras. 

I ended up buying a box of donut. It included the Wedding cake donut, the NOLA, Red velvet, and the Spicy Maple Praline donuts. I also got a buttermilk drop (it's like a buttermilk biscuit that taste like a donut), a buttermilk biscuit and chocolate chip cookies. Don't judge, I shared all my goodies with a group of friends, that way I could taste everything. For full enjoyment I advise you buy all the above or you will be cheating yourself! 

While I was sitting in the store eating my donuts the owner came up and asked me if I wanted a king cake donut. He had heard the commotion I made at the counter about wanting a King Cake donut and my disappointment. I thought that was really awesome, and I didn't have to wait in line. Thank you Aaron! 

Unfortunately I was so focused on their donuts I missed out on getting some of their breakfast sandwiches and the Croquenuts (griddled donut sandwiches). They look so good that I could kick myself for not trying at least 3 of them each! 

Most importantly donut lovers, District Donuts  changes their donuts daily, which is a good and a bad thing. The good thing is there is a bunch of different kind of donuts that seem endless. The bad news is I don't live in New Orleans so I won't be able to try them all. If you live out here take advantage of how lucky you are. Here's a list of just a few of the donuts they have....

Vietnamese iced coffee

I can't wait to come back and try them all!

Consuming a regular meal on a daily basis is an important task in every day life. It may be even harder to accomplish this task during Mardi Gras! 

I'm not sure if you're familiar with Mardi Gras but if you like to party I know you may not get a lot of real meals. I know we didn't! Second of all I really appreciate a place that serves breakfast all day because God knows we're not gonna make it out anytime close to breakfast time! 

Originally I found this place because I saw breakfast food but I wasn't sure if they served it all day. When I came up to the restaurant there was a huge line and my heart sunk because I was starving. I now realized there are two reasons why there's a huge line. One this place is pretty small and two the food is delicious! 

Let me give you the good and the bad news. The bad news was that the people in front of me had to wait an hour to be seated. The good news was that we didn't have to wait that long. We waited about 20 minutes. It's almost like five tables left at once and then they let five of our tables in. We waited another 15 minutes for our food and it was definitely worth it. I finished my entire plate and that's rare, I usually have leftovers. But I licked my plate clean. Actually everyone in our group joined the clean plate club!

I ate and loved the:
-Eggs Rancheros which had 2 fried eggs, cheddar cheese, crispy tortilla, black beans, salsa, and avocado creme. So good!
-Eggs Tuscan Style which has two poached eggs, creamy polenta, vegetable ratatouille, spicy greens and all of oil. Omg GET IT! Amazing! 

Jimmy J's has a huge menu and I wish I got to try more dishes! Too bad Jimmy doesn't live in LA because I definitely would like to date him!

We walked in and walked right back out! The front of the building is a mess, you walk in to signs telling you where to go to get help, and it stunk! This was our first and last time to try this place. We do NOT recommend it!

Another Thai gem! I use to think there was limited good Thai food in the city, but I've realized there's plenty hidden throughout the city. The latest and greatest find is Royal Thai located in Harahan.

Nothing failed to please! My friends and I LOVED the Royal Thai dip and ordered a second..maybe even a third??? (Along with maybe 5 rounds of sake...) Everything was great. We ordered the Pad Thai, Pad See Ew, Chicken Wings, Curry Puff, and Green Curry. I loved every single dish. The restaurant is not too far from the Elmwood Shopping Center, but it is hidden in a more warehouse-y commercial area. It's so worth it!

LOVE: Royal Thai Dip. Solid and delicious classic Thai dishes. Affordable drinks.

What NOT to LOVE: nothing?

If you're familiar with most of the boba spots/ shops around Tucson, I think you will find this one to be a pleasant surprise. 

First off, it has giant pictures of some of their drinks, labeled in both English and Chinese. To me, that's a good sign, and makes visualizing the more exotic flavors easier when ordering.

Secondly, their milk tea actually taste like tea, and is made with real brewed tea, rather than that weird powder everyone else uses. It actually taste the closest to what I've had in Asia, and is probably one of the better ones I've had in the US. I've only tried their regular milk tea with boba so I can't comment on the other flavors. Some of the flavors are definitely intriguing. 

Thirdly, you can customize how much sugar you want in your drink. That's a first for me. I had regular sugar with my drink, and it doesn't taste overly sweet like most places.

Lastly, It's a nice large space with plenty of seating, and SURPRISE, free wifi. The tables are large, and I see several university students holding study sessions here at night. Although I can see how the constant shaking drinks with ice, and blenders going off can be distracting for someone trying to focus. 

You may not find the shop the first time because the sign of the shops name is tiny, to the point that it's almost nonexistent. It's right next door to China Szechuan, if that helps.
The only good thing about this place is the location. The wait was stupid, the service slow, they seemed confused and the food was ekkkk. Done

The art of sushi, lives at Yoichi's. And no surprise, as apparently Yoichi's previous experience includes the all-mighty Nobu of Japan. 

We went on Sunday night, and were in awe, taste after taste. 

If you expect your sushi to come with rocking atmosphere and crazy sushi guys tossing sake shots, this is not your place. 

But, if you appreciate the minimalism necessary for a complete focus on the food, Yoichi's is a must try, incomparable to anywhere else in SB. 

The star of the show is their 7 course meal, called Kaiseki. Plate after plate arrived, and each was such a huge wow of taste. 

From an amazing oyster, to a really hard to describe never before tasted but impossibly delicious seaweed shot, to A+ perfect melt in your mouth sashimi, to an eel roll that was oh so so sooo good, to absolutely perfectly grilled black cod and on and on the dishes kept coming and the wow's just kept flowing.

Pricey? Yes. Worth it? Absolutely. If nothing else, it's a gorgeous reminder of how amazing food can be when you stop trying to outdo the next guy, and instead, simply focus on your passion. - AB in SB

Got to tag along on an amazing mini Tennessee trip.  Being the weirdo I am I instantly fell in love with the horse statues.  The atmosphere and decor gave me high hopes for this place.

The staff was friendly.  I always find with restaurant staff you get what you give.  My group was happy and we were treated with kindness.

I got to try 3 different things: the bbq ribs, a bite of Mac & cheese, and their fried pickles.  I love bbq and anytime I get the chance to try ribs I go for it.  They were good.  Coming from a northern state tjat has a lot of people who try to succeed at bbq I've tried a lot of good and bad ribs.  These weren't my favorite but I can see myself ordering then again if I lived in the area.  The fried pickles though?  Those were incomparable to any other friend pickles.  So good.  You have to get them.

Overall just a fun spot.

Great beer garden for the ambiance and space (the place is HUGE but still gets crowded)

Food and drinks are nothing to write home about but when you're enjoying great company under a vine grown patio near liberty bell, it's not all that bad
---wings: crispy but the meat was a bit hard to chew

NOTE: there are a couple random games you can get your hands on, we played checkers while we were here

3.5 stars!! food was okay but each dish had some flaws and was just short of execution THUS  the higher prices for dinner didn't reflect the quality

---vagabond: yummy tequila cocktail!
---basil collins: another refreshing cocktail
---baguette w/ mozzarella appetizer: crusty baguette with salted olive oil & fresh mozzarella, pretty nice & a cheap starter
---phyllo chicken: thin crispy phyllo wrapped around goat cheese & chicken. the chicken was a little dry but the RICH goat cheese compensated a bit. i only enjoyed the potatoes that had been halved & then fried
--stuffed pepper: the quinoa filling was tasty but the pepper really needed to be roasted longer

NOTE: outdoor seating area in back that would be cute for dining in nice weather!

JAMAICAN fast food! i hear D's used to be a truck but they're now a brick and mortar

my plate of oxtail to-GO was $12, a bit pricier than the jerk chicken that yelpers also seem to like, but i was happy with my choice
---oxtail plate: the meat=tender goodness! the plate comes with rice & beans, cabbage slaw, and a fried bread that had a subtle sweetness but good crisp

NOTE: it was hard to locate the restaurant via yelp directions but it's actually on the south side of the intersection in a plaza!

Re-visted Hershel's on memorial day weekend (a surprisingly not crazy busy weekend for Philly) and got to try their pastrami sandwich again PLUS the BRISKET sandwich

You definitely want to order your sandwich TOASTED! 
---pastrami sandwich: still good!!
---brisket sandwich: wouldnt have thought to order this, it was almost a mistake, but glad we did! They recommended it with a bit of bbq sauce which paired well with the meat which was very moist!

Meat was all cooked perfectly but could have used a tad bit more flavor

A very unique cafe experience, like a cocktail bar for coffee and tea drinks!

Yes the drinks are on the pricier side but you're paying for the complexity and aesthetics! 
---bella rose: I don't usually care for matcha but this drink was delicious and beautiful
---burnout: a great coffee based drink, perfect balance of sweetness that doesn't over power 

Will be making this a regular visit when I return to SB!

having just come Chicago...and loving Giordanos there I was really excited that they'd be nearly walking distance from my work.....

So On Feb 20th I ordered a pizza at 10 AM...got an email saying it'd be ready by 11:45.....the next day on Saturday morning I got my confirmation of my order. Now I'm 30 miles away...a day later....

I understand they are busy...overwhelmed...saturated....blown away...add whatever you like. However...it's feb 22....enough time to have resolved some things...like ...

After two days and countless phone calls I was unable to get through to cancel my order...so now I got debited for nearly $30 for a pizza I never got. 

So, you can't get through on phones...if you wnat you can drive over...stand in a long line with hopes of a chance of possibly getting help....

Myself...I think I'll stick to tony Greeks pizza in Carmel....meanwhile maybe I'll get a call next week sometime saying my pizza's ready...

If I could leave zero stars I would. 

Every time I come to New Orleans, I ALWAYS make a trip to Verti Marte. I've introduced so many friends & colleagues to this low key late night munchies "must go", but I will unfortunately never be taking my friends here again. I was in town for work & brought my 5 colleagues here for food as it was the only place I knew that was open at 4am. After we ordered & paid, my friend went to ask for the bathroom. She first asked the kitchen staff who were super nice & directed her to the cashiers for access but was met unprecedented rudeness. Not only did he tell her she wasn't allowed to use the bathroom, he accused her of trying to get away with not paying for her sandwich when our other colleague had already paid for them all & further kicked her out of the store. I am so embarrassed & disappointed thinking my friends would love this place when they ended up being treated so horribly. I will never recommend this place to anyone again.

Was in town for a tradeshow and stopped in for a cold beer. All the Row staff were so friendly and the place has a cool vibe and decor. Was in town only two days but came back here three times -  we loved the live music, beer, staff. It's a fun after dinner place too but you have to order the fried pickles NO MATTER WHAT and drink a Kentucky Bourbon Barrel Ale or two. Bartender let us try a few different beers. I will be back!

Wouldn't give me the code for bathroom until AFTER I had bought my espresso 

Otherwise nice space
Good seating area

But thumbs down for customer service

I'm all in on Destination Dogs. I was pretty surprised at the level of ambiance/swankiness when I visited for the first time- heard 'hotdog' and automatically assumed that meant 'divey'. I was wrong. This is a lesson in never making assumptions, kids.

Let us run through the positives, of which there are several:

1) Hot dogs. Who doesn't love a good hot dog?! (vegans, I hear you/I'm sorry). The selection of dogs alone is impressive, and when you add in the fact that they're actually really delicious in addition to being creative, we're off to a great start. 

So far I've tried the: 

-Cyclone 
-Oscar 
-Paul Bunyon
-Hebrew Hammer
-Swede Dreams

Do yourself a favor and read the descriptions of all the dogs on the menu. I cannot pick a favorite, I would willingly eat any of these again right now, and it's only 10am.

2) The bar. Solid beer and cocktail options! I am proud of you, Destination Dogs.

3) The pool table! How is it always unoccupied when I visit?! I mean... I'm not complaining at all, I just don't get it. Either way, another bar with games is a welcome addition to the city in my book. 

4) Staff is friendly and efficient. They have cut our dogs into 3 pieces before just to make it easier for us to share. That, my friends, is customer service. 

5) Quizzo! The quizzo at Destination Dogs is LIT. Just trust me. 

The only minor downside I can see here is the steep prices for ... hot dogs ... but these really are next-level hot dogs and I think it's well worth it.

YAS HONEY. Nevermind the fact that the upstairs is so cramped that you can awkwardly stroke your stranger-neighbor if you feel the urge, or the fact that you have to learn how to lip-read REAL quick cause you legit cannot hear a word that your dining mate(s) is/are saying. Butcher Bar was worth it. 

Every human we encountered, from the hostess to our waiter to the random dude who brought dessert out was nothing less than perfectly friendly and helpful. 

They have wine on tap, and I...I just really appreciated that. 

The sloppy joe poutine was really good once my mouth adjusted to the sweetness. The fries maintained their crisp even while buried underneath the mountain of sweet slop. Impressive.

The pretzel monkey bread (though more of a baby pretzel loaf than the traditional pull-apart monkey bread), when dunked in that divine horseradish mustard and cheese sauce, was sent straight from the heavens.

I dunno man, sometimes you're just craving a messy, greasy cheeseburger. Since we're adults now who go to places like Butcher Bar instead of McDonald's at 2am, it's not as easy to get your fix. The Royale was reminiscent of the Quarter Pounder, yes, but it was a well-executed rendition and it hit the spot so who cares. 

And finally, the skillet cookie. I was immensely glad that we kept our normal food order kinda tame, because if I hadn't had enough room to finish this cookie I would've been all kinds of pissed. Each bite was more delectable than the last.

Alllll of this goodness came to only ~70ish bucks + tip. I plan to return as soon as humanly possible to try roughly every other item on the menu.

First, the wings. Oooohhhh the wings. 

Second, the bar itself. So kitschy, so beer-y. So good.

Third, I attended an event on the 3rd floor here last week. The event was cash bar and buffet-style food, and the bar was tended to by the lovely and talented Josephine. Not gonna lie, I was unsure what to expect from a catered event here, but I was pleasantly surprised! Food options included antipasti, salad, penne vodka, tortellini, meatballs, and sausage. Everything was delish and hot, and the service was fantastic. Way to up the ante, Moriarty's.

A new brunch favorite that I found today after I have passed by many times during my afternoon runs-oh how I'd love to keep this place all to myself. It's like someone went into my brain and picked out all of my favorite things - imperfect brick wall, floral wallpaper, coffee everywhere, mason jars, flowers on the wall, paper scrolls, chalkboards... a basic girl's dream! ;) did I mention they apparently serve Franklin Fountain ice cream??? You already are a winner in my book.

The staff here are super friendly and professional. We were greeted with a smile and given the option to sit down at the counters or wait 25 minutes for a table for two.
