Of course since we were starving on a Saturday at noon, we opted to sit at the counter. My friend ordered an iced tea and I had the vietnamese coffee. I wish they had condensed milk but they just gave me regular milk. I enjoyed it nonetheless.
I got the shakshuka - I LOVE shakshuka so I was pretty excited to find that my dish had plenty of flavor. A+ with the bread too.
My friend got this amazing grilled cheese with different kinds of cheese and bacon and tomatoes...WOW that was delicious.
I'm in love!

What a fantastic find ! I've been trying to come here for over a month now. Unfortunately they only serve dinner so I had to strategically make plans to eat here.
That aside, it was totally worth the effort!
Came here on Thurs evening at 6:45pm and we were seated right away. Given that they don't allow reservations, they're very fast to greet and seat. As soon as I walked in I noted the bright but simple decor. The lights made everything classy and romantic. A great place for GNO, a date or hang out with coworkers! The customers were dressy and trendy so keep that in mind when you check this place out.
Our waiter and his trainee were very friendly and attentive. They continued to check up on us which was nice. They offered us in house stilled water or sparkling. Now, onto the food.
The winning dish was hands down the spinach gnocchi, which we ordered on a  whim. It was just right on texture and the sauce was delicious. You could actually taste the spinach! 
We also tried the bacon wrapped dates which were yummy - the sweet dates filled with cream cheese (?) Complimented the saltiness of the bacon. I didn't care too much for the dipping sauce, which was a yogurt like sauce, because I felt like it covered the flavor of the bacon and dates. The beets salad was so so good - they used golden beets which are my favorite because they're sweeter.  The salad that was paired with it was fresh. The squid ink tonarelli was good in flavor but a bit too chewy for my preference, but that's my biased opinion. In addition, I was pleasantly surprised by the roasted cauliflower. Most places throw some spice or salt and call it a day, but tredici's version actually has a kick! Since I love spicy food, I really enjoyed this dish.
Our bill came out to $60 for 3 people. Not breaking the bank and you get quality food! It's definitely a place I recommend going with 3-4 people so you can share because the portions are modest - more like tapas style.
Definitely a great place to check out considering they have vegetarian options !

Dim sum, win some. I think this new establishment in UC is a great addition to the west philly asian cuisine scene. I would note that this restaurant has a solid amount of the classic dishes of dim sum but they can be adventurous as well. For example, there was a durian pastry that my friend pressured us into trying, which turned out to be fairly tasty if you don't mind the durian flavor. It wasn't as powerful as I feared.
The service was average, some of the servers seemed to be inexperienced or didn't really know the menu items but we tried to be gracious. They also forgot about one of our dishes so we had to remind them to bring it our or remove it altogether.
I would give notice to the fact that because this is more upscale than the humble restaurants of chinatown the prices also reflect that. I don't prefer to pay more for this type of food considering it is "snack" food, but I do value their quality. The flavors were on par with good dim sum so if you do not want to travel past the Schuylkill river, Dim Sum House is the one.

Geno's has the big name, but after living in Philly and exploring the cheese-steak market in great detail...there are MUCH better places to go.

One plus is that this place is ALWAYS open. You want a cheesesteak at 5am? You got it! The ambiance is cool if you are a tourist. There is always a big crowd and the blinding neon lights are definitely a sight to see. Drive or walk by and then go somewhere else to eat!

The sandwich is just OK, with a good amount of fatty pieces left on the meat. Pretty expensive and nothing special compared to many other places I've been.

The worst part of this place is the service. When you get to the window and see a sticker that says, "This is America, when ordering SPEAK ENGLISH" above another sticker that says, "Management reserves the right to refuse service" --- That sort of sums it up. They pride themselves on being the tough, South Philly folk who will tell you off if you don't order the way they want you to. You will definitely get an eye roll if you ask for "Cheese Whiz and Fried Onions" instead of "Wiz Wit."

If you want a cheese-steak served by a bunch of people who think it's ok to be racist and offensive and serve crappy food...go to Geno's. If you're looking for a late-late night cheese-steak after a night of heavy drinking...I'd suggest Pat's across the street. If you actually want a good sandwich, go to Jim's on South Street or John's Roast Pork off of Columbus Blvd.

Casa Del Matador just opened up recently in the village. I was very excited to see this open and try it. There just arent any newer clean upscale Mexican places in or around Boise. If this place turned out to be good, I knew it would be a hit.

Like most of the other restaurants in the Village, this place is mostly a huge bar. The only restaurant I can think of that does not fit this mold is the Counter. I did notice that they seem to have an upstairs. It did not look like it was open, so I could not tell if this was really a diniing area, or just for show.

Casa Del Matador is basically a huge bar with a few booths and tables thrown in. Its noisy and busy!

We went here on a Thursday night around 7 and it was packed. There was mostly 20 somethings and 30 somethings when we went.

The menu is small and does not have the traditional Mexican items on it. They have the normal tacos, enchiladas and burritos, but they all have some sort of twist to them. Most items, according to our waitress and spicy. I saw a couple things that said they had habanero. 

It was so busy, that we were not able to get a table. We had to sit around an elevated fire pit, that thankfully was not going.

The 1st thing I noticed was the very interesting decorations. There are huge things hanging fro the ceiling that look like over sized Christmas decorations. It was very unusual, but I liked it.

Our waitress was very friendly and had a great personality. She took our order promptly and we got our food in good time, especially considering how busy it was.

I had the fajitas. I ordered half steak and half chicken. They dont have a price for half steak and half chicken, so they charged me the price of the steak fajitas, which is $18. Very expensive compared to other Mexican restaurants.

When it came out, the 1st thing that came to my mind was that old commercial; "Where's the beef?"

I got 2 pieces of steak and 4 pieces of chicken to make my fajitas with. The rest were veggies and there was not a lot of those either. The steak that I got was in chunks instead of cut up nicely like other places that serve fajitas. They were not bid chunks my any stretch of the imagination, but too big to be just a bite.

This made eating the steak hard. The steak had a good flavor, but was chewy and tough. Cutting it into smaller portions would have made it easier to eat.

One thing that I did like about the Fajartis was that they roasted their bell peppers. Most every Mexican place that I know just sautes them. This adds a nice texture and smokiness to the bell pepper, which I loved.

The chicken was just ok. It did not have much flavor to it. I was happy to see that I was not charged extra for guac, like some other places do.

I was very dissapointed in the fajitas and especially the lack of meat. Next I will tackle my wifes meal. She had a chicken burrito. The burrito was big, but we soon discovered why.

It was so large because it was filled with black beans and rice. We had to do a burittoectomy and like an exploratory surgeon, look for the chicken. I counted 4 or so pieces of chicken in the "Chickenless" Burrito.

If you like garlic, you will love the salsa. One word of cation on this is that if you are on a sodium restricted diet like me, be careful with the salsa. its loaded with salt as well.

I thought I was going to OD on salt right there in the restaurant!

We noticed a young man in black walking through the restaurant. He came to where we were, picked up my empty water glass and filled it. 

This young man had no expression on his face, and never said a word the entire time we were there. He was not taking orders, so I am guessing he was a manger, or something like this. Whatever he was, he needs customer service skills and a personality.

The bottom line here is that If you are younger, make good money, love the bar scene, want some ok Mexican food that is non-traditional, and like to socialize, this is the place for you.

If you are older, prefer a more quite atmosphere, like meat, are on a budget, and prefer more traditional Mexican food, you will NOT like it here.

My wife and I saw Pizzlachik on Diners Drive Ins and Dives some years back. Guy Fieri made this place look good, so I have wanted to go ever since.

Well, last night I finally got my chance to try it. I hate writing poor reviews. I really do. Especially when there are so many that really liked it here. Plus these days, I try really hard to find the good in places, even when I did not have a good experience.

The problem here is I just did not find a single thing that I liked. 

My first objection is cleanliness. This place is filthy! The floors looked like they had not been swept in a month, much less mopped. The ceiling and everything on it was dusty and just plain yuk.

Now these might seem like a small thing, but think on this. All that dust, dirt, and filth   has to go somewhere. Guess where it winds up? In your food. The old saying, that holds true, is a dirty kitchen puts out dirty food.

This is a HUGE pet peeve of mine, so its hard for me to move on, but I will. This place is very small, has no ambience at all, and is just plain uninviting.

I had a small pizza with Italian sausage, pepperoni, Mozzarella cheese, and Asiago cheese. They list 3 herbs on their menu, but beware of these. They are a $1 each as are the other ingredients on the menu. So this means your pizza can real expensive real quick. My small pizza with a couple drinks came to $20. 

After I placed my order the guy behind the counter said I had to go to the bar to get my drinks. I ordered tea and a sprite. Why I had to walk over to the bar to get these is beyond me. A small thing, but weird and inconvenient.

I looked at this places pizza oven. Its just a steel oven that is gas. So the cooking process is no better than what you would get from your oven at home. For me, when I have pizza, I want it cooked in a way that I cant do. Like wood fired, or coal or just something different. If its cooked the same way I can cook it at home, whats the point in my coming to your restaurant?

I had to use a ton of napkins to sop up all the grease from my pizza. The taste of it was....well, I am not sure what the flavor of it was. I was hungry, so I ate it, but I wish I had not. The meats were very salty, I could not taste the sauce at all, and it just lacked flavor.

My wife commented that she say the guy that was preparing my pizza dough walk around the kitchen area, and doing things with his hands to make them unclean. 

Even my 13 year old daughter said it was disgusting here. My wife refused to even eat. She had wanted a salad with chicken, but was told that the only way she could get chicken was to order a Full, Half, or quarter chicken. 

My daughter got chicken on her pizza, but the chicken was all dark meat. She does not like dark meat, so she did not eat it.

The bottom line here is I don't recommend this place. Now if you are a teen, in your 20's, or someone that just does not care about cleanness or grease, you might like it.

For me, there are far better pizza places in town that serve way better pizza for around the same price. I highly recommend Grimaldi's in the Village in Meridian. So far, it has the best pizza I have found anywhere in the Boise area. But I am always searching, so if there is a better one out there, I would love to hear about it.

After reading some good and some bad reviews about Sam's I have come to the conclusion that either their competition is writing the bad reviews or they are written by people with no taste.

For me to hand out five stars you have to earn it! While it is quite the drive from Tampa it's well worth it. This is my third time here and it just gets better and better. Don't expect gourmet food but some of the tastiest bar food I have ever had.

Today was some kind of special occasion and they had the parking lot closed off with a live band, as a result they had a special N'Oleans Cajun menu. I wasn't expecting much as I know this isn't a Cajun restaurant and to top it of I had just been disappointed by "The Bayou" restaurant. But I can't help it, if crawfish etoufee is on the menu I have to order it. This has been one of the biggest surprises I have had in years. The crawfish etoufee was downright fantastic! My wife had the chicken jambalaya and she thought it was some of the best she had ever had and we have been to the big easy.

Sam's Hudson Beach Bar has it all, great food, great service and a unbelievable view of the Gulf Of Mexico, it's the perfect trifecta.

If you love life you'll love this place, however if you're not that bright go ahead and skip it all together.

Enjoy!

For months, I've had Washoe Public House marked as a place to visit after reading reviews from my fellow Yelpers, Donna B and Mike B. My family and I were finally able to try them for lunch on a Friday afternoon.

Since it was nice day, we asked to be seated outside. Our waitress was friendly and efficient - and didn't forget about us as can sometimes happen when we're out of sight. 

We started with the pork belly egg rolls as an appetizer: two egg rolls cut in half with a side of hot & sweet mustard. The egg rolls were good and the sauce was amazing.

My daughter had the tri-tip bowl which came with asparagus, lettuce, tomato, avocado, and a chimichurri sauce. While she liked the tri-tip, the avocado was unripe and sauce a bit over-powering. 

My son tried the Washoe burger: a 1/2 lb. patty with lettuce, tomatoes, carmelized onions, bacon, white Cheddar, and beer mustard in a Challah bun. Cooked medium-rare, the burger was flavorful and huge! It also came with a side of fries - which were seasoned nicely and perfectly crispy.

Hubby had the pork belly bahn mi sandwich on a French roll. It had generous slices of pork belly, a delicious sauce, and wonderfully soft bread!  He too had the fries and enjoyed them as much as my son did.

I had a small order of warm beet salad: roasted beets with hazlenuts, a slice of brie, some greens, in a Champagne reduction. It was delicious!  Plus, I had the BLTA: crispy bacon, lettuce, juicy tomatoes, and ripe avocado with grilled bread. That, too, was delicious and fresh!

Overall, the food and experience was great and I'm glad we finally marked Washoe Public House off our foodie list!

BLT: $7
*Miracle Whip: be still, my little, barely now beating heart. I LOVE MW. 
*This rounds out to roughly $1/lb of bacon. For real. 
*Crunchy, toasty white, zero-nutrient bread. 
*side of potato chips and pickle
*L&T for good measure

Chocolate Malt: $4.75
*Easily enough for 2-3 people, made in a REAL malt-maker, brought out in the ice cold shaker, and presented with a fountain glass, straw and spoon. 
*Legit. 

Homemade Candy, too. I resisted. 

Vintage, in a real sense, around since 1913. 
Yes, I'm a tourist. Fine, get over it. IT's a huge f'in BLT and a malt, and anyone can get on board with that. It also arrived to our table within about 2 minutes flat, and the white paneled booths, Coca Cola signage from the old days (though they serve Pepsi now, which makes me sad), chocolate monkies, etc. It's a good stop. The service was sweet, too. 

Surefire family pleaser, on vacation or not. It's cute and has great food that won't break the bank and you can get your BLT fix for about the next 2 years. 

And chocolate malts. Really good ones. And, if you can chug down 5 of them (they are huge, remember) in 30 minutes. You get them all free. I don't really know what the bonus is for ANYONE there, but hey...one was good. I managed about half of one in 20 minutes.

Go frickin' figure...my ideal coffee shop lives in St. Louis. 

Components: 
1. Free wi-fi. 
2. Comfy furniture. 
3. Outlets
4. Square, stable tables. 
5. Breakfast ALL DAY LONG. (the french toast with apples and raisins, yum!)
6. Great, strong coffee. In real mugs. 
7. Friendly people. 
8. a CAT! (Captain kitty)
9. Full Menu with sandwiches, salads, soups, pastries, etc. 
10. Kitsch

If you like coffee shops, you'll love the Mud House. Clean and quirky, sweet and strong. Love, love, love. 

Take note, Chicago.

All up in here it says: "Ladies Welcome." I wonder...is that strange for women to be invited to dine? This is man food though, just sayin!

The best food I had on my trip, no lie!

Me: I'm pretty hungry. 
My mom: Ok, let's not get the whole po boys, we'll just get halfs. 
Me: Sounds reasonable. 

I order the shrimp, she orders the catfish variety. Both dressed (blasphemy to get it undressed, mine came with some sort of cocktail sauce/mayo=heaven). 

Mine comes out first. I think "oh, they must've not heard me...I only wanted the half size." Oh well, we'll take it home for later. 

My mom's arrives, same portion problem. 

Then we realize, THIS is the half. Which is more like a sandwich that is approximately a FOOT LONG and 6 inches high. Holy man. If I ate like this as a half portion, I'd easily weigh 500 lbs. Easily. 

Regardless, these were the best po boys I had in Louisiana! I tried them at many places, and this beat everyone else by a long shot. Crispy, fresh, French bread...fried shrimp, awesome sauce. Mmmmmm. So good. So very, very good. 

Someone rec'ed that we get the mac 'n cheese, so I ordered a small plate. Again, with the portion problems :) It fed 4 of us. A SMALL. Fed 4. It was DAMN good, too. 

This place is somewhat cafeteria style...you go up and order from the waitress, then pay...then sit down and they deliver. It's busy, but really fun...and the food is fantastic. The location is sort of out of the way, but it's basically just like the best diner I've ever been to, with the biggest food that's ever been called "half" or "small" in the world. Cheap, too. I think mine came out to about $10 (with drink, tax, tip) and I took some home for later...

Best Po Boy. YAY! If you are down in St. Bernard, New Orleans or Chalmette...def make it a destination, and bring your eatin' pants!

Ahem, I mean...I'm a lady. I don't have eatin' pants. Oh whatever, yes I do...

Daughter, 3 year old granddaughter and I visited on Thursday to try their Ramen as we are all 3 HUGE fans of Ramen and have heard good things about this spot. We also love sushi and would like to try their sushi sometime but this visit was all about the Ramen and Saki! 

WARNING: They have no children's menu at all and are not nice about trying to accommodate for a child. We asked if we could please just purchase a side of pork broth for her and were told no, I was like you have no children's menu and I can't even purchase her a bowl of broth and was told no, server did suggest white rice for her and I was like no she doesn't want to eat plain white rice and she just smiled,  shrugged her shoulders and said sorry. Weirdest thing I have ever seen.

Atmosphere: It's in a nice new very attractive plaza. Daughter and I found the interior very nice, clean and cute. 

Service: Sever was minimally friendly and seemed aggravated by any questions we asked and was very unfamiliar with the menu, specials and anything else we asked of her. Please read more about the customer service under my review of their Shoyu Ramen below.

Shoyu Ramen: We ordered this as it was the only Ramen available for lunch special price of $10, menu did not indicate that it was chicken broth. When we tasted it we were shocked as it tasted like a very salty, strong beef broth...unpleasant. I let our server know that we did not like it at all and pointed out the fact that the menu did not indicate it was chicken broth (although it did not taste like any chicken broth we have ever tasted and even my granddaughter wouldn't eat it) and that we did not like it so could we please trade it for Tonkotsu and that even though it was more we were happy to pay the difference. To our surprise we were rudely told no, when I informed the server that we would not eat this she indicated rudely that we still had to pay for it....at this point I was getting aggravated and said fine I'm a Yelp Elite so I hope you enjoy my review and then the servers attitude did a complete 360 and she was so sweet, friendly etc and was happy to exchange the Ramen. Although I'm glad I got to exchange so sad that when they didn't know I was a Yelper they were going to have such horrible customer service.

Tonkotsu Ramen: This is what we traded for, it was amazing! The broth had an amazing Umami flavor that we all just LOVED! The pork was good but we like it a little more seared but it was still smokey and yummy. Will go back for this alone. 

Saki flight: Daughter got a ski flight that had Pineapple, Apple and Peach! Apple was the best, would definitely get that! Would not get the Pineapple or Peach, it was ok but the Apple was fabulous.

Tried out Box of Cubans yesterday for the first time. First off locally owned husband and wife team making delicious Cuban sandwiches, the pork was so good next time I would probably just get a pork sandwich! Their signature cilantro sauce is fantastic and they are making a huge variety of homemade empanadas right in front of you behind the plexiglass so you know they are homemade. Perfect ratio of meat to bread and FABULOUS customer service! Also got a Cortadito which was fantastic and tried one Croquette which was super yummy as was the beef and cheese empanada....will return for sure! Don't let the fact that this gem is tucked inside a gas station deter you!

So as I said in my past review the jalapeño poppers were all hype well it's sad to say the same goes for their po boy and lobster pops. Everything is over priced and your po boy doesn't even come with fries. This place is strictly only for drinking and the views. This time we came for Valentines Day this year. We should have known how the night was going to be when we saw a waitress roaming the parking lot looking for her car screaming "where's my car!" Then we go to the hostess and it was a chilly night they didn't ask if we wanted to be by the water or stay in the blocked off area. We were seated by the water. We had jackets so it wasn't that big of a deal she then swats us at the only dirty table when there were plenty of clean tables around and then had then proceeded to ask would we like them to wipe down the table?! Of course we said yes and a young man came over and wiped the table down and then we waited 15 min for our waitress and low and behold it was the same lady looking for her car. She looked disheveled and we say "Did you find your car?" She says "what?!" And we explain we saw her she laughs and says "oh yeah! I did. Can you hold on a moment it looks like my last table took off" and walks off without getting our order. She eventually comes back and takes our order but her quality of service was awful and we constantly had to look around to find where she was. It deft put a damper on our Valentines Day! We had to even get another waitress to take our card so we could get out of there. I deft change my mind about this place and prob won't ever come back just not worth what you pay for and the service stinks!

I am no Picasso, but...

Let me paint you a picture of how I spent my Saturday afternoon in beautiful Carpinteria, California. 

It all started when my 2 year old said, "Daddy, I wanna go the beach!" 

So off we went to pack the car with all of the beach essentials...

Towels, sand buckets, hats, sunglasses, sunscreen, change of clothes, water, snacks...

Basically...

Everything, but the kitchen sink. 

-------------------------------------------------

I've come to Carpinteria several times over the years and I've always parked alongside the beach on Santa Claus Lane. Of course Padaro Beach Grill has been there for as long as I can remember, but to be honest I've only actually eaten here a couple of times and it has been many years since I had. 

As we hit the road and we encountered a bit of traffic going through Camarillo, I could tell my wife was getting a bit hangry and even asked "Is this place even that good?" And the classic, "How much longer until we get there?"

Knowing that it was a solid 50 minutes out with traffic, I told her "oh it's about 40 minutes" and just pressed a little harder on the accelerator once we started moving again.  ;) 

Upon our arrival, we lucked out and found a parking spot almost right away. The parking here is hit or miss and sometimes you just might not find a spot alongside Santa Claus Ln. and trust me it happens more often than not. 

As we walked up to PBG, the line was about 15 groups deep, but the line was moving and our stomachs were not about to cooperate if we decided to go elsewhere. 

As we inched closer and closer to the front of the line, we started smiling knowing that we were almost next to order. 

As it was busy, my wife took the kids and found a nice outdoor table with some good shade. 

Within about 10-15 minutes of ordering, I heard the Magic Words over the loudspeaker, "Number 06, your order is Ready!!" 

As I walked up to the pick-up counter, I couldn't help but let out a sigh of HELL YESSSSS (in my head of course).The food looked SOOOOOO AMAZING, I literally couldn't wait to get back to the table to share the feast we were about to devour. 

Here's what we had: 

Pretzel burger with bbq sauce, bourbon caramelized onion, chipotle Mayo and American cheese. (The pretzel bun glistened and is life changing good!)

Tuna melt on grilled sourdough (it was as delicious as it was beautiful) 

Kids cheeseburger with fries (closest burger to in n out I've ever had) 

Onions and tater tots were cooked perfectly! 

A sprite and a Margarita to share, it was just what we needed to quench our thirst before heading over to the beach after we ate. 

The great service, the friendly staff, the delicious food and the spacious outdoor seating area at Padaro Beach Grill is everything you would expect for a beautiful day in Santa Barbara County, and trust me, it was a beautiful day indeed. 

As more and more people get vaccinated, life seems to be slowly returning back to the normal we once knew. Everyone wore masks and were respectful of each other's space. As I looked around while we ate, I couldn't help but smile knowing that we as humans, are doing what we do best...

Persevering through difficult times, hopefully a little kinder this time around. 

Thank you Padaro Beach Grill for allowing me to have a memorable outing with my family, we will 100% be back to support your business.

CASH ONLY SPOT!!! CASH ONLY SPOT!!! CASH ONLY SPOT!!! CASH ONLY SPOT!!! CASH ONLY SPOT!!!

I think I fell victim to overhyping!  So many people...so many people...told me this is the best of the best snowball stand of New Orleans.  My mouth has waited for so long to try this place, because I am a West Bank New Orleanian, and this in the middle of the East Bank.  I decided that this time, I definitely was going to make the stop.

All in all, this place is just decent.  The ice isn't the softest ice I have ever had; it is just merely decent ice.  The strawberry flavor is really good, but the grape and Hawaiian punch flavor, just decent!  Are you sensing a theme here?

I do like the variation of sizes, and the pricing is not that bad overall.  I really like just the mere look of having a Chinese food container, what normally the rice comes in, used instead of the traditional cups, to serve you the snowball.  Just remember to ask for a plastic bag to put that concoction in because the juice will eventually leak out the bottom...and there is a lot of ice packed in that thing.  I believe the bag cost an extra nickel...go ahead and splurge on that eating accessory!  They even offer a pail size, which would be a cool family thing to dig into!  Remember not to be on your phone or you will be skipped in line.  Have an idea of what you want because they zoom through customers.  They have to because you are waiting outside to get these beauties!

All in all, definitely come here for the experience.  You will not be disappointed in that at all.  Just know that there are many other snowball stands in New Orleans that can rival and beat these folks.  Also remember, this is a CASH ONLY spot!

I finally had the chance to dine at Hyde Park Village's newest restaurant, Goody Goody Burgers. I invited my fellow Yelper, Steve E., to join me for lunch.

After reading multiple reviews that mentioned the long wait I downloaded the "No Wait" app and we decided to meet at 11:30 am to beat the lunch rush. I checked the app multiple times prior to our visit so that I could reserve a table and each time I checked the app it said "no wait, come on in". Unfortunately, this meant that there was no wait for a table OUTSIDE. There was a 30-40 minute wait for a table inside. Since my lunch break is only an hour we decided to eat outside, overlooking the construction on Swann Avenue. Luckily, the weather was nice, but I would have preferred a table inside since there is no atmosphere in the outdoor seating area.

Goody Goody's menu consists of your typical, all-American diner dishes including breakfast served all day, club sandwiches, meatloaf, and of course: pie! Steve and I decided to order the signature POX burgers with cheese. For our sides I ordered the coleslaw and he ordered the side salad. 

My first impression when our burgers arrived was that the burgers looked small and I should have ordered a second patty. I couldn't believe that this squashed, messy looking burger cost $5.50 and comes with no sides. The POX secret sauce wasn't my favorite and reminded me of a really sweet ketchup. I would probably order the Hyde Park cheeseburger next time because I couldn't taste anything on the burger other than the POX sauce. If you do not like sweet relish I would not recommend the coleslaw. Next time I'll order the french fries or onion rings.

Overall, my experience was good so I would visit again, but I think I will visit for breakfast on my next visit since it looks like you get more bang for your buck.

Parts of Paris is a charming French bistro in Safety Harbor. This isn't your typical stuffy, fancy pants restaurant. The waiters are dressed in cheerful polos and the decor is a mix of Florida casual with a Parisian flair.

My husband and I started off our date night with a nice bottle of Cabernet that was recommended by our waiter. We ordered the Foie Gras and the Steak Tartare Classique as appetizers, both excellent. The pan seared foie gras was paired with pearl onions, poached apples, port bordelaise, and marcona almonds. The steak tartare was served with a quail egg, capers, onions, pickles, anchovies and toasted baguette.

For our entrees I selected the Pork Belly with mustard maple butter, steamed radishes, and fingerling potatoes served over a pea purée. This dish was phenomenal!!! My husband ordered the Filet Mignon with Pommes Frites, His steak was cooked a perfect medium rare and cut like butter! We finished off our meal on a sweet note. My husband ordered the assorted cheese platter and I ordered the chocolate truffles and berries because I mistakenly thought this dessert would be small. Little did I know that I would be served nearly half a pound of assorted chocolates. My husband's decadent cheese platter included some wonderful aged Gouda and blue cheese as   

My husband and I enjoyed our meal so much that we returned the following weekend to enjoy cocktails and dessert with my sister. During our second visit my sister ordered the Le Poire cocktail with was a heavenly mix of pear vodka, fresh lemon juice, and agave nectar. My Bardot cocktail was the perfect summery blend of raspberry vodka, fresh raspberries, citrus and sparkling wine. For dessert my husband ordered the Chef's Choice Dessert sampler with mini crème brûlée and chocolate mousse cups, my sister ordered the Crème Brûlée, and I ordered the Crêpe Suzette with vanilla ice cream. 

Will be back soon!

I was so excited to finally try the Deviled Pig after drooling over their mouthwatering photos on Instagram for the last few months! It was worth the wait; everything was fantastic!

Yelp moms, Tina and Christina, and their adorable babies joined me and my son for a much needed afternoon out. We arrived prior to the lunch rush and greedily snagged both of the indoor tables. There was also seating outside and bar seating inside. The employees at The Deviled Pig could not have been any sweeter! They carried a high chair to our table for me and brought some animal crackers for our littles! 

I wanted to try the deviled pig appetizer, but I didn't want to completely blow my diet so I ordered the Porky Bowl instead. The Porky Bowl contains all of your barbecue favorites with BBQ pulled pork, corn, shredded carrots, pickled red onions, and fried jalapeños served over coleslaw. I appreciate that the ingredients were thoughtfully layered so that the coleslaw and pulled pork did not get the jalapeños soggy. My meal was delicious and my son loved his side of red skin mashed potatoes. Missed opportunity: Christina's seasoned fries were awesome! Perfectly crisp and salty! Will be back to order the fries and the ribs!

The parking lot was larger than expected and easy to enter and leave, despite being located on busy Dale Mabry. My only negative comment is that there were no changing tables in the bathroom. Since this restaurant is tiny and mostly a take-out spot I didn't dock them a star, but hook up the South Tampa parents with some changing tables!!!

Bar Louie is a fun urban bar/restaurant in International Plaza that offers a large menu selection of appetizers, bar food, burgers, sandwiches and more.  The drink menu includes many tasty martinis (my favorite martini is the "Fizz" with St. Germain and Prosecco) and features 48 beers on tap as well as other bottled selections, and wines by the glass or bottle.  

Why only three stars?  I like the atmosphere and the food slightly more at The Pub in International Plaza.  Bar Louie is fun a fun spot to hear a live band, but the bar can get too loud at times so it's not a great spot if you want to have a conversation.

Check out their daily happy hour specials. Many of the drinks and appetizers are half off. They also have $1 burger nights every Tuesday (doesn't inlcude cheese or other additional condiments, but still a great deal!) and $1 draft nights every Wednesday.

one of the best buffets to go to IF you have an iron clad stomach that nothing affects, dont care about cleanliness, want to feel like being in the cattle herd, can stand being surrounded by hogs and inconsiderate diners, eat tough steak, greasy chicken, sloppy side dishes, scroungy salad choices, AND rotten rude cashiers........I actually felt bad for our waitress-she was so much better than the place she was working for and deserves a better environment!  hope she moved on.NEVER EVER WILL REVISIT-and thats after 3 trys--all the same result...board of health anyone??

Backyard is a smaller, lesser-known, anti-douchebag bar within the South Tampa, South Howard inebriation scene. Upon walking into one of Backyard's two entrances, you'll find only two restrooms, one for each gender, but luckily there are usually more males than females (hence the reason for my visit). Using the facilities is typically not an issue - unless of course a certain member of my gender is treating the giant one-room bathroom like a personal down-time space.

The atmosphere in The Soho Backyard is perfect for those arriving in any mood. The lighting is dark & dim and the air is lively and fun. Indie Rock tunes by various bands including The Naked Famous, Cherub, Empire of the Sun and Two Door Cinema Club play in the immediate background. The music is never too loud and is nothing like what you'll experience at bars that turn into amateur nightclubs at 10 p.m. 

Backyard has something for everyone, including a shuffleboard, dart board, plenty of TV's and random bar games. There are a couple of different bars at which you may sit, or if you arrive at the right time, a variety of tables are situated directly in the center of the bar. 

The menu is pretty standard - one unique item being the Duck Wings (which I have not tried). However, I have ordered the Brussel Sprouts (pretty good) and more recently, the Margarita flatbread, at the recommendation of my bartender - and it was phenomenal! All of the entrees and snacks on their menu are reasonably priced but most people visit Backyard for the drinks. 

Our female bartender was willing to create any concoction that my buddies asked for. I spied an unopened Rodney Strong Cabernet sitting behind the bar and inquired about the price, as it was not listed on the menu. The gentleman returned and said that they just received the shipment and even though it was not yet on the menu, I could have it for $8.00 a glass. As you might guess, I didn't even hesitate (Rodney Strong for $8/glass at any establishment is a heck of a deal). 

In sum, if you can locate the Backyard, check it out. If not, just keep it that way, so as to not ruin this perfectly fine watering hole whose surrounding area is increasingly being overrun by a less intelligent crowd of 20 somethings.

I love their happy hour!

Jamonera is on a great strip with other restaurants and cute little boutiques. Be sure to stop by to grab some spanish plates and then walk around.

I went and got the tortilla espinosa, papa fritas, seared steak pinchos, cheese plate, bizet cocktail and white sangria.

I absolutely recommend the papa fritas, seared steak pinchos and the bizet cocktail. The fries had a great crispy taste with cheese drizzled all over. The steak was fresh over a baguette and the bizet cocktail was something new but refreshing after a walk over.

Overall, the atmosphere was great and the bartender and staff were great company. I'd recommend stopping here and they also offer happy hour at their outside seating. Be sure to grab a seat before it's too busy, it's first come first serve.

Generally in suburbs of Philadelphia, conservative Americana rules with an iron fist. But Assi atop a high hill in the 5-point pike area of Montco stands resolute against a world which would normally see another Giant or Acme rise. Owing its survival to the mass population of Asians which resides in the area due to Merck. 

Assi is a clean Asian Supermarket, and when I say clean I'm talking truly clean. Not clean for an Asian Supermarket. So it should not turn away anyone less acquainted with the "functionality over aesthetics" policy which dominates Asian culture. If you want to be truly immersed in the experience go during a Sunday/Saturday afternoon, and set lunch aside to eat at their food market, as well as try the various Korean samples found around the store.

As the old saying goes. "Eat the food, know the culture"

Love Love Love this cupcake shop. Having enjoyed both Billys and Magnolia's in NYC I have decided Philly Cupcake really has the best icing AND cake. 

I loved the guys in the shop, they are so funny and knowledgeable. Cupcakes are a real treat and I know I will be going back when my sweet tooth is calling!

Stellar hospitality!!!  My husband has booked dinner parties here every year for the last five (5) years when the PUMPER show comes to town.  It's now called the WWETT show, and this year, I had the luxury of coming with.  Which also meant, I get to wine & dine at this fabulous dining establishment - score!  This restaurant is truly a foodie's heaven!

Events Manager Laura is efficient and extraordinary!  She accommodated our large party upstairs, and everyone had a blast.  I think hubby earned some brownie points for planning this event (wink, wink).  The waitstaff were attentive and came around with endless libations.   We enjoyed the company and conversation.  I had the mouthwatering shrimp scampi, and they accommodated our son with tasty fried shrimp and fries, since they don't offer a kid's menu.  He loved every bite of it.  Many oooohhhh's and aaaahhhh's when the food came out, especially the baked Alaska.  

Everything was presented beautifully, from the appetizers to the main dishes...jaw-dropping!  I see why my husband comes back here every year.  The good news is the WWETT show will be held in Indianapolis for another seven (7) years under new ownership.  It's a win-win for everyone and cheers to thriving restaurants like Oceanaire Seafood Room!  

'Til we meet again, cheers! =)

During the WWETT convention, hubby made a dinner reservation for 15 people on a Wednesday night.  Morton's is always on point.  I can finally say I've tasted Midwest steaks, and they are humongous!  It was neat to go downstairs; I love the ambiance of any Morton's.  I know it's a chain, but it's safe to say they're always consistent.  

Morton's makes some mean azz drinks.  I thoroughly enjoyed my appletini, looked like some awesome green love potion.  Almost as good as House of Prime Rib.  The steaks were amazingly delicious.  I'd rate them beyond 5 stars if I could.  Events Manager Sherri did a stellar job with our dinner party.  Our long table sat right in front of all the action; they were bustling in the kitchen on a Wednesday night.  Our waitstaff ensured everything was flawless, pouring wines, refilling our glasses, topping off water, etc.  The evening was memorable, highly recommended for juicy steaks and a fabulously good time!  

'Til we meet again ~ cheers!!!

I came here for the first time today. I saw some dumplings and started craving them and I'm glad to report I wasn't disappointed. 

Between my fiance and I we got a pork bun (as huge as my hand), 15 piece celery and pork dumplings, braised pork belly in brown sauce and rice, and a bowl of beef noodle soup. 

I don't think I'm going to say anything different than the other reviews. Their portions were huge, their seating space was small. But it's totally worth it. All the food was hot and delicious. 

Their beef soup was really well balanced and wasn't too oily like other places. The noddles were firm and the beef slices were tender. 

The pork bun was huge and only $2. I could eat 2 for lunch alone and be happy! Make sure you order one. 

The pork belly was about half fat half meat and cooked just right. My fiance took two bites and wanted to take it home to enjoy. 

And the dumplings were our favorite! They are bite size and come in 15 or 30 piece. The sauce is great!

All the utensils are at the table and we were in and out pretty quickly. It was a little warm inside so I'll go next time at night. All in all I give them a 5+ star! I'm just sad I didn't come here sooner. It blows the Americanised Chinese restaurants out of the water! 

I ate too much! X.X
Terrible service, crap food and ignorant staff. I'd recommend burning your money before I'd suggest this place.

This has got to be my favorite breakfast place in tampa!! I found it by accident. I wanted to get some breakfast and this gem pooped up! I had their avocado Toast with pouches egg and omg it was sooooo good!! In addition I also had their cheese sandwich and it was so tasty. It was so good that I told a friend and came again the following week and had the avocado toast with egg and return again few days after. Their coffee I would say it's ok but my friend really enjoyed it! They have plenty or seating area and customer service is outstanding. Very affordable in comparison to other breakfast areas. Parking however is somewhat limited but they do have more parking in the next plaza!! It's a must try place I would say! Thanks for the delicious food and outstanding customer service

In a city where the predominant foods are hoagies, pizza and cheese steaks, it takes some stones to open another pizza joint. I read all the articles and feel like it was all hype. Did the menu have some interesting selections for pizza combos? Yes. Was the crust good? Sure. Just had a hard time getting excited about it all. 

It also didn't help that the staff take such a laissez faire attitude that they didn't bring silverwear (yes, I like to eat my pizza with a fork and knife). They also didn't bring me glasses for the BYOB wine I brought, (my date had to go search for plastic cups), and I practically had to beg for a wine opener. Once I got it, I was afraid I would break it because it was so cheap. 

If you go, bring your own wineglasses and your favorite corkscrew. Bring your own silverwear if you need that too. After all that, I questioned why I was paying $20 for a pie.

Oh, and the infamous museum to all things pizza? I passed by it without realizing that I missed the museum. Next time, I think I'll just stay at home, order pizza from any number of their competition and watch some vintage Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles from the comfort of my couch. I'd get a much better experience.

It's really difficult to find something original about 'Willie Mae's Scotch House' that hasn't already been said a thousand times over. This place is epic... like beyond epic! It's no coincidence that this place has become as much a part of the New Orleans landscape as the raging Mississippi or the intoxicating cacophony of jazz spilling out onto the streets in the French Quarter. 

Willie Mae's Scotch House was established in 1957, first as a scotch bar in the Historic Treme neighbourhood. After a year, the bar moved to it's current location & in the years following, the bar expanded into a barbershop & a beauty salon in the front. In the early 70's, the beauty salon closed, which brought demand for a restaurant from Willie Mae's bar customers. As a result fried chicken began leaving it's kitchen, soon becoming the stuff of pure legend. In recent years Willie Mae Seaton was honoured with a prestigious James Beard Award & only last year, President Obama dinned here while in town for the 10th anniversary of Hurricane Katrina.

Armed with all this information, a couple of friends & I walked to Willie Mae's from the French Quarter in pure anticipation & curiosity. After hearing that this place made the best fried chicken in the world we were in hook, line & sinker. For a Flight Attendant, the world is a small place & my palate was absolutely up for the challenge.

We pretty much rolled up close to opening, keen to avoid the reported line often down the street. Upon arriving, we were led to our table by a genuinely warm waiter & seated in the corner of the front room. 

Each of us ordered the fried chicken (obviously!) with a selection of different sides including the Cajun Seasoned Mac n' Cheese, Corn Bread & Collard Greens.

Still being the only people in the restaurant, the food hit our table quickly. At first sight the chicken looked marvellous. Majestic even. With a distinctive crust & a crunch that cannot be described in words, this chicken had my heart immediately. On first bite I'm convinced butterflies took off in my stomach & upon reflection, I'm sure time stopped, just for a moment. 

As a result, fried chicken anywhere else is ruined for me. Completely! I'm not sure whether to be grateful or horrified. I guess I'll let you be the judge if you're intending to visit.

Do yourself a favor & put this place on your bucket list.

Not too shabby but not too great either. 

The food presentation and flavor were nothing remarkable and the environment was pretty much the same. The bartender was friendly enough and the selection of beers was better than average.... however, I don't feel the any real draw to come on back to the Pour House. 

Perhaps to check out the patio?

Perhaps.

Just had yet another visit here at Suzy Wong's because I am addicted to the Curried Tofu & Potato Pockets ($6), Vegetable Gyoza Potstickers ($6), and Vegetable Spring Rolls ($5), 

The Vegan, Vegetarian, and Gluten Free options here are a little piece of heaven and the Lychee Cocktail is beyond refreshing.

Read my first review for the full scoop but even after all of these months...Suzy has come through and I visit her whenever I can!

P.S. The staff here has always been a lot of fun and offer fantastic service.
Cheers!

What a fabulous Sunday feast I enjoyed here! 

After the completion of a long (and sometimes grueling) project, I grabbed a couple of my dearest friends and we headed to Moto to celebrate. This was indeed a grand idea. 

I was instantly smitten with the ambiance and textures of the space. From the exposed brick wall with the clean fonts painted carefully on it to the rich dark wood and opulence of the bar. The open layout was refreshing yet still managed to feel cozy and easy at the same time. 
Oh, heck yeah. I can totally get used to this....

And, the service? Stellar although there was a bit of a wait and an error with our Brussels Sprouts ($11) that came out with pancetta when we requested that it be nixed. (I'm vegan) They still receive 5 stars from me because they brought out a couple of complimentary desserts and checked in with us throughout the dinner to let us know that the order was taking longer than expected. I'm all good with this because of the effort, communication, and thoughtfulness with the way they addressed it OR could it be because I was enjoying the delightful bottle of Zenato Valpolicella ($44) that we ordered? Either way, no biggie! The Stone Ground Polenta ($9) and Cannelini Beans ($9) were nice additions to our table and were easily shared. One of my friends opted for the Green Plate ($22) which is a beautiful vegetarian entree that features green and local produce and I couldn't help but take a bite - delish! 

However, it did not hold a candle to what may be my new favorite vegan dish in Nashville: 

Blueberry Lasagna - $19

You may be scratching your head? Blueberries and lasagna? Yes. Indeed. 
I have to admit that even I was a bit thrown off when I first noticed it on the menu but I am so thankful that I jumped in with both feet! This entree is savory, comforting, and oozes an elegant flavor of wild mushrooms paired with blueberry balsamic. I didn't miss the presence of cheese at all with this dish. Even if you are not a vegetarian or vegan, I would still highly recommend ordering this to give your taste buds a jolt of tasty goodness. I seriously can't say enough wonderful things about this scrumptious take on lasagna. 

Need to plan a romantic date? Close a deal during a business dinner? Just need an excuse to enjoy delicious food in a beautiful environment? 

Head to Moto. 
You just may run into me while you are there!

TIP: This restaurant is a new addition to M Street's fleet of dining/nightlife/venue spots. It is tucked in next to Virago and Saint Anejo and across the street from Whiskey Kitchen. Complimentary valet is conveniently located across the street!

Burger Up didn't disappoint again as the fantastically delish Marathon Burger ($10) satisfied my hunger! The blend of black bean and quinoa is a textural home-run (which isn't always the case with veggie based patties) with toppings that include the basics lettuce, tomato, and red onion. For non-vegans, the cilantro lime creme fraiche is a nice touch. 

TIP: You may request any toppings such as jalapenos or other sauces to customize your burger! 

I opted for the steamed spinach ($1 extra) due to my current health kick but was salivating over the french fries that the rest of the table ordered. 

Service was great as they accommodated our impromptu birthday party of nearly 12 and even moved seating to make it work for us. Food was efficiently served too.

Keep in mind that you are paying a bit of a premium for a quality experience made from quality ingredients. If you're seeking a quick and dirty burger, proceed to drive-thru a fast-food chain. 
Burger Up is for consumers who adore food!

So so so close to 5 stars. 
Like, ridiculously close to 5 stars.
We're talking 4.75 on the 'ol Yelp star scale.

The reservation confirmation was super efficient and professional. I booked our "Girls Night Out" dinner (reservations are only for parties of 6 parties or more) and our table was ready within moments of our arrival. 

Our server was super helpful and was very familiar with the menu - we opted to share some Small Plates that included the super savory Crispy Brussels ($8) and the Potato Fries ($6). 
I thoroughly enjoyed both very much but I simply can't stop thinking about those dang Potato Fries. They are the perfect blend of crispy, comforting, and spicy. I was literally getting edgy each and every time another friend from the table reached for another fry and wanted to smack their cute little hands away. 

We promptly ordered cocktails and I opted for the No. 1 and was dazzled by own drunken state after just one! The Broker's Gin, Cynar, Plum & Peppercorn Shrub, Lemon Cordial, and Peychaud's Bitters make up one of my favorite new cocktails in this town. Order it. You won't be disappointed. 

Speaking of my one and only disappointment, while our server happily suggested vegan options on the menu such as the satisfying Soba Noodles ($8) and tasty Ramen that I previously ordered at an Otaku South event last weekend ($12), I was very surprised that there was not a veg-friendly sushi option listed on the menu. They were kind enough to have the chef prepare a veggie roll for me on the fly but wouldn't it make sense to have at least one on the menu? Seems like something that they can easily do and I can attest that it does make a huge difference to us vegans and vegetarians who crave sushi without sea creatures in them. 

The overall layout and space is beautiful and I love the overall ambiance. The lighting is dark and moody but can get a bit loud (likely due to my table) so it may not be the best spot if you're seeking a quiet evening out or need to have a profound conversation with your dinner date. 

Overall, this is a fantastic spot to visit for dinner and/or drinks and I'd highly suggest that you at least give it a try, even if Japanese food isn't normally your thing. You may be surprised what entices you on the menu. 

TIP: Budget an extra 5 minutes into your arrival time to locate parking (especially on the weekends), I had to "get creative" and made my own spot at the end of the lot. There is also off-street parking but that can sometimes require a bit of luck or magic to score one.

I am usually an all or nothing kind of gal and feel pretty dang comfortable with issuing a solid 4 or 5 star review but in the case of Silo, I wish that there was a way to give them a loud and proud 4.5 because they are just so close to perfection. 

I chose Silo to host my birthday dinner party this year as I wanted to support a new local business but have to admit that I was taking a bit of a risk as it was site unseen and I wanted to make sure that everyone who attended would enjoy a tasty dinner too. 
No pressure, right? 

I felt comfortable enough about my selection based off of the impression that I received on their website along with the innovative "Farm to Fork" menu that was posted as well. My friend Hillary was nice enough to organize the reservations and evening on my behalf too. 

When I arrived for dinner, most of our party of 20ish were already seated and the dark and moody room was exactly what I was hoping for! The Silo team had set up 2 long tables separated from the rest of the restaurant so we enjoyed an intimate setting for the special celebration. 

Proprietor and Chef Clay Greenberg greeted me and treated me to a potent yet tasty shot of a 21 year old bourbon named Willet ($30) when I mentioned that I just left my duties as a judge for the Bartender's Bash. Well played. Very well played.

With my vegan diet, I had already communicated to Silo when we were in the reservation booking process so I was looking forward to seeing what they had concocted... I was not disappointed! 

I started off with the delicious Field Pea Salad which boasted red onion, Easter egg radishes saturated with a lemon vinaigrette. This was altered for my diet as the regular version includes Benton's ham. 

My Market Veg entree consisted of oyster mushrooms that were locally sourced from Goodlettsville, beets, butternut squash & Anson Mills piccolo farro (grain).
I can't boast enough... this dish was divine. The texture and burst of flavors were on point and I literally ate every last bit. How could I not? You haven't tasted comfort food until you have enjoyed this dish. If you like risotto, you'll appreciate this!

And just when I think it's all over... the grand finale:
A VEGAN carrot & walnut cupcake with vegan cream cheese icing

Jackpot! Yahtzee! Bingo!

I was so very impressed with this perfectly sweet and satisfying massive cupcake that yet again, I ate every morsel. (a few guests were brave enough to ask for a bite)
Wow. You did good Silo. Real good. 

My only tiny gripe was with the server assigned to my table. There were 2 that helped with our party (1 male/1 female). Forgive me as I normally recall names but after my stint at the Bartenders Bash earlier that evening.... 
The male server assigned to the other table was friendly and efficient and even came over to introduce himself. The female server was friendly but had a few notable slip-ups.

She wasn't going to bring out a first course for me at first as everyone at my table had received theirs and my friend Chris and I looked at each other like, "Why is the b-day girl getting dissed here?" When we inquired about it, she said that she didn't realize that I wanted one and ended up bringing out the Pea Salad shortly after.
(I should note that I reminded her when I arrived that I had prearranged a vegan menu with the chef and she said that it was all set.)

Next, my friend paid for his bill with cash and handed it to her. She came back a bit later and asked if he was ready to settle? He let her know that he already had and she just said, "Oh, Okay." 
(It should also be noted that although he was okay with leaving her the generous gratuity that he did, she did not ask if he wanted any change back.)

Look, I'm not trying to body-slam the server here (clearly still a 4.5 star review) but I really enjoyed Silo and want them to succeed in their Germantown neighborhood. They bring so many fantastic elements so I would hate for some dings in service to affect them adversely especially as they are ramping up their fresh business.
Besides the small issues with the server, the overall communication with the Silo team was overwhelmingly positive. 

I definitely plan to try brunch or another dinner and perhaps even pony up to the bar here very soon!

Prices are fair especially with the quality of ingredients that are used.

Trust me, I can completely understand how a coffee shop may feel if on a daily basis, a troop of people come in, buy a cup of coffee and
occupy their tables and spaces all day which can deter other potential customers from enjoying the business. 
Tables also must be turned over to ensure that servers can make an honest living too. Again, this all makes sense.

What I can't get a grip on is: I popped into Fido for a meeting this past Friday, and was unable to gain access to the Internet at 3pm in the afternoon. I moseyed up to an employee behind the counter to ask if there was a passcode or if she could offer some advice on how to access the WI-Fi. She was friendly enough, but let me know that during various times of the day, dependent on how the current traffic was, they turn off the Wi-Fi to motivate people to leave and to allow a fresh batch of customers to come in. Hmmmmm... doesn't sound like the best idea to me? 

Isn't it blasphemous to not offer complimentary WIFI at a coffee shop? Huh?!
There has to be a better way to create customer flow in your business. 
Instead, my meeting and I grabbed our laptops and drove to Edgehil Cafe where we enjoyed coffee, treats, and Internet access... of course!

Cliff Notes: Fido is a dandy spot to grab a leisurely meal, treat, or cup of coffee. If you plan to get any work done, you're better of going somewhere else.

Oh, yes. 
Oh, hell yes.
Oh, (beep) yes.
(sometimes even I need to be censored)

As someone who never had the luxury of enjoying a meal at brilliant chef Deb Paquette's previous venture, Zola... I had scraped together enough hear-say to know that Etch is a complete departure from the previous menu and aesthetic. I was finally able to enjoy a Paquette experience for lunch the other day and was very impressed. 

I should also start off by saying that parking WAS NOT an issue as I know that many locals get worked up about how/where/who to park but I pulled right up front and slipped a few quarters into the meter. You may also utilize the complimentary valet service too. Easy breezy, right? 

Next, I strutted my ravenous self into Etch's gorgeous modern space that boasts natural sunlight from the abundant windows throughout. Throw in lofty high ceilings, clean design, and a classic white tablecloth and you feel as if you've been whisked away to NYC. Many spots try to reenact the quiet sophistication that Etch so nicely pulls off. The space felt comfy and inviting yet chic' in the same breath. 

Rumblings of an "Etchy Hour" (happy hour) along with a Downtown Resident loyalty were program were in the air along with the capability for the space to be used as a venue for special events and dinner parties. A smaller private dining area (10-20ish guests) is nestled near the entrance too. 

Ready to get the scoop on the food? 
The extremely veg-friendly menu was much appreciated for this vegan and the doting and experienced server was great at suggesting some tweaks for my lifestyle. I opted to start off with an appetizer of Roasted Cauliflower ($8) to share and enjoyed the healthy yet filling dish. This normally comes paired with truffled pea pesto, salted almonds, and feta crema dipping sauces but he made some adjustments for me. For my main course, I chose the innovative Zucchini Slaw Roll ($9) that was a DELICIOUS concoction of arugula, fennel, red onion, roasted carrot, shiitake confit, avocado, and horseradish mayo (I altered to not include the mayo) paired with house-made potato chips. As a bit of a splurge, I tried the peach sorbet ($3 per scoop) and didn't feel the least bit guilty as i ate every last bite. 
Everything that I ordered was thoughtfully prepared, presented, and beyond tasty.

I normally refrain from giving 5 stars on a first visit but I just can't help myself... Etch will definitely become one of my regular spots. My next visit will be to try out the dinner menu and to pony up to the bar to try their cocktail menu. This would be a fabulous spot to take a date... hint hint.

Oh, the guilt. 

THE GUILT. 

How the heck did I literally inhale that veggie burger and truffle tots as "efficiently" as I did? Seriously. The shocked look on my friend's face clearly showed that I most certainly chowed on the "Taco Truck" version of a burger waaaaay quicker than what could be classified as humanly possible. And, although some may roll their eyes at the $11.50 price tag for a burger and a side (plus $2 upgrade for the "truffle" tots) but I can attest that this was one of the best veggie burgers (and tots) that I have had in quite some time. 

I appreciate that you have the option to choose a bun preference that included Brioche, Pretzel, Gluten-Free, and Wheat and that vegans like myself can opt for the House-made veggie patty and still enjoy any of the 12 styles that they have available ranging from the "Tennessee" or "Jalapeno Popper" to the "Hawaiian" and "Shroomin" with just minor tweaks. The burger was nothing short of hearty and full of robust flavor. This hungry lady was happy and stuffed!

My only issue came with the 2 glasses of wine ($9) that I ordered. My first glass tasted a bit "off" and had some discoloration that hinted that this vintage may have been sitting out uncorked for wee bit too long but when the bubbly waitress came back around to see if we were still feeling dehydrated, I went ahead and ordered a second glass to keep up with my appetite. I should have refrained as the second glass definitely hit all signs that the quality of the wine was an issue. Perhaps, it was my newfound sluggish state (due to the heavy load that I just ate) or the swell spirits that we were in but we didn't send the glass back. So my glass just sat there untouched. 

For my next visit, I'll try one of the brews instead as they have quite the extensive craft beer list here. 

Overall, this is a nice addition to the Gulch neighborhood and the food is solid. Just be sure to bring your appetite and Sommeliers beware!

Ya know... 

I really didn't know what to think when I first saw The Row from afar. Hmmm... what is that? After driving by on a pretty frequent basis, it did appear that patrons were having a good time basking on the large patio or I would hear the buzz of live music echoing out when I was nearing the stop sign. Is it a bar? Is it a restaurant? Are they only going to focus on bacon (seriously people, will that trend end?) and look at me like I'm a wilderbeast because I happen to want some veggies and am not fond of dousing everything with butter. I digress...

On my first visit, we popped into the bar for some drinks after the Old Crow show at Fontanel and rather enjoyed ourselves in the open-air seating and casual vibe. The bar and server staff were friendly and on point so we stayed for a bit and I do believe that all of us murmured something like, "Yea, we should come back here again soon..." 

My other visit was during a lunch meeting and perhaps it was the fact that I hadn't had any cocktails as of yet, but I felt as if it was more of a restaurant spot than a drinking hole. It was bright and sunshiney as were the staff, and instead of bottlenecks and bourbon, there were Housemade Pickle Flytes, a fresh perspective of Hot Chicken, and event a Quinoa and Kale Veggie Burger on the menu for me. I looked around and noticed all of the pieces of art and collectibles that resulted in a thoughtful homage to Music Row, songwriters, and local people and goods. And, not only do they feature a healthy selection of beers (28 or so, I believe), The Ros sources many locally and regionally while still finding time to pickle vegetables and make their own preserves in house. 

I do also want to point out that my friend warned me that she didn't think that The Row was going to be very vegan-friendly... and she's friends with the Executive Chef. She couldn't be any more inaccurate! I'd have to agree with their tag-line that The Row is distinctively Southern and especially with their charm, the Chef whipped me up some tasty tasty tasty veggie tacos that were full of flavor and filling! Along with veg-friendy items on the menu, they will certainly step up and with much ease, I might add.. and make sure that you're eating well and are happy. My dietary restriction didn't even make him blink.

And, lastly, throw in the fact that there is music performed there at least 4 times weekly and a diverse floor plan that could offer quieter nooks if you're feeling anti-social, closed off rooms for privacy, or open spaced areas if you want to meet new friends. I also appreciate the convenient location to my home and that parking is simple with the the connected lots. Prices are fair for brunch, lunch, dinner, happy hour, and nightcaps so The Row could truly fit many of your needs throughout the day. I'm curious to try brunch next... gotta get my hands on those homemade preserves... and make sure their Bloody Mary is worthy! If so, The Row has a good chance of being a stomping ground for man occasion.

I kind of feel like I just went on an awkward first date with Tavern and am still a tad unsure of how I feel about going on a 2nd...

First off, getting mixed signals about what image M Street Entertain Group wants to portray with this new venture? M Street chose to move Lime to the Gulch area to be near sibling establishments Whiskey Kitchen, Virago, and the soon-to-be opened Kayne Prime. I had heard rumblings that this location was slated for a pub (which made sense considering the area) but when our group walked in on Saturday, that surely wasn't the case. We were greeted by a doorman who advised us that on this evening, only members of the private club Citizen could enter. Wasn't expecting that! Coincidentally a member of our party was a member so we were able to enter. Not exactly pub-like. 

Once inside, the space is laid out very much like Whiskey Kitchen and the crowd is also a tidy little marriage of Virago and WK. Drinks are priced on the higher end and they wouldn't serve any food (including chips!) after 10pm. 
Overall, I wasn't particularly inspired by the vibe, service, or cocktails but really couldn't say anything terrible either. 

Thank goodness our large group was able to be seated at a large booth area so that we could create our own little party!

After doing a little research, I found out that Tavern's business tagline is "Inspired Pub Cuisine & Libations." Hmmmm.....

Would consider a 2nd date with Tavern but if someone else were to ask me out before them...

Prima is the equivalent of a "mic drop" when it comes to restaurant ratings...

From the impeccable decor and excellent service to the fantastic cocktail list and wine list, I was smitten even before the food made it's way out. 

My friend ordered the steak (from a sustainable farm in Leipers Fork) while I opted for some vegan options that ranged from a potato soup that was full of sustenance and flavor paired with an interesting Lobster Gnocchi (sans lobster) that energized my palate. I ended the evening with a delightful Cortado which was comprised of beans from local coffee haven - Crema. Along with all the other thoughtful details, I also appreciated the Thistle Farms soap and toiletries in the restrooms. The dedication to utilizing local purveyors was across the board. All around the experience was very enjoyable. I look forward to many more enchanting meals at this premier Nashville restaurant. 

This is a very solid option for special occasions or romantic dinners! Hint hint! 

TIP: Valet is available but there is also a self-serve parking lot across the street.

Oh, Treehouse...

Why aren't you just located in my backyard?

Perhaps, I'm sounding a bit spoiled since you're just located a few miles away, but I put all the blame on you. YES. Indeed. It is your fault that I now have this sense of entitlement that now has me actively campaigning for your 2nd location to be conveniently located behind my loft. 

If you wouldn't have knocked my socks off with your thoughtful and diverse menu which also includes an enticing assortment of dishes that are vegan, vegetarian, and gluten free. The fact that the menu clearly denotes which dishes are specific to the dietary needs is much-appreciated added bonus. And, while I can't make this statement about the mass majority of dining spots that I have frequented, I can cross my heart and swear by the statement that "I've NEVER had an experience that I haven't absolutely loved here." 

(LOUD THUD)

What was that? Oh, just the sound of the mic being dropped. 
I've enjoyed myself here since they opened their doors  7 months ago - so this 5 star review is quite delayed but well-deserved.

From the Cauliflower Steak, Fideo, and Kale + Quinoa ($10) dishes to their tasty concoction of Plantains ($6) or Beets + Radishes the menu stays innovative with unique flavor mashups. Plus, I haven't even touched on the fact that you're not acquiring debt to enjoy the "good life" here. There's no excuse to ingest toxic foods elsewhere when the menu is so affordable here. The 10 After 10 Menu proves my point as you can enjoy some of their signature items for $10 after 10pm. Goodbye, drive-thru. Hello there, Sunchokes and Empanadas.

Ready to chitty chat about libations? 
Yeah, me too. 

The bar program here is solid. If ciders, drafts, or bottles and cans make your world go round, you won't be disappointed. Perhaps, the grape variety is more your bag? I can attest that the the list isn't overbearingly extensive but the consolidated options that they do offer will please your palate. Give their Madeira and Port options a whirl. Wine snob? All good. Bring your own goodies and you'll only have a $15 corkage fee.

NOW, THE COCKTAILS. Oh, the cocktails. 
Vodka, lemon, Casoni 1814, and grapefruit bitters happen to be the ingredients to one of my favorite cocktails in town. Order the "Don't Mind If I Do"  ($10) and after a couple of these, you'll feel A-OK, my friends. Is Bourbon your BFF? The "Kentucky Hussy" ($10) is the way to go. Comprised of Old Forrester 100, lemon, ginger beer, and sugar, you'll feel a bit of the heat but the sugar softens the blow a tad. Admittedly, portion control can be an issue when you pony up to this bar.... better have that Uber app downloaded on your iPhone, yelpers. Bottoms up.

With the recent expansion of the treehouse in the back dining area, it opens up the space a bit more from the cozy 40 seat main dining area. The intimate yet well-designer layout of The Treehouse just adds to the overall charm especially since this property  has been in the Co-Founders family since the roaring 20's and before The Great Depression. The aforementioned treehouse in the back was actually built by the patriarch of the family when this location was used for residential purposes. I also just adore that they also utilized local and regional makers to craft the lighting, tables, seating, and bar areas. And, is it odd that the bathrooms are one of my favorite touches? I won't give it all away but you'll find some unexpected "Steampunk" and "Rock and Roll" influences in there... a little mischief, never hurt anybody, right?

So, I hope this helps explain why we all need a bit more of The Treehouse in our lives. We certainly aren't asking them to alter the beautiful space and dynamic energy that they already have in place... BUT if this this young restaurant were going to add a secondary location, I just wanted to throw my very own backyard in the hat.

TIP: There is currently a Yelp Deal where you can purchase a $20 certificate for only $10

It's my own dang fault for coming back. 
Sometimes the idea of cheap sushi seduces me but you get exactly what you pay for.

My friend and I wanted to do an early, casual, and frugal dinner so we decided to pop by here again. I usually come here for a cheap sushi fix but decided to venture out and try a fried tofu Yu Dofu dish ($4.95) and the Rice Ball ($1.95). The Rice Ball never disappoints as a cheap appetizer that consists of a Teriyaki flavored ball that is fried on the exterior but has a boiled rice center. Simple and satisfying. The Yu Dofu lacked flavor and consistency. Essentially, it was a dozen soggy cubed fried tofu pieces that sit in a basic Teriyaki sauce. No vegetables, spices, or anything else. I ate in haste and my stomach is still holding a grudge.

I don't expect exquisite food from here and have real expectations for the price but come on now!

Innovative and interesting.
This hidden gem in Edgehill Village offers up a fresh perspective in the Nashville bar scene. From the carefully crafted cocktails to the gorgeous nod to Art Deco decor, you will be finding every excuse in the book to plot your next visit here. Plus, I love the #grrrlpower of the Soler sisters who founded and executed this top notch establishment. Come now, come often. 
Order the Tangarang and All Gold Everything off the cocktail menu.

I DIG it. 
I DIG it a lot. 

I along with most others who drove by for months was very curious about this new large development in the 12 South neighborhood. What was this snazzy new building going to become? 
Aha!
Urban Grub. (love the name and branding BTW)

A few weeks back, my good friend and I had an impromptu brunch experience which ended up lasting way past the typical "brunch" hours thanks to the refreshing cocktails, tasty quinoa burrito, and lovely patio area. I am literally smitten with the layout of this place! There are so many interesting nooks and options to enjoy the space. 

Perhaps you want to enjoy the breeze? Two separate patio areas can ensure that you enjoy the weather.  

Prefer a bustling and energetic environment instead? The bar area is spacious and full of vibrant interaction. 

Want to celebrate a special occasion with some privacy? The over sized booths and cozy dining areas will ensure that you get to do just that!

Now onto the food... my brunch was smashing as I noshed on the hearty quinoa burrito that was full of flavor and coupled with their seasoned edamame, this broad was satisfied. 

Fast forward a few weeks later. I made reservations for a dear friend's birthday. We were all seated in a comfy booth while our server was expedient and excellent throughout the evening. He also made some solid food and beverage recommendations for our group which I am especially thankful for considering my veg diet. I was a tad disappointed that there wasn't a vegetarian/vegan option on the dinner menu but with our server's assistance, I was able to tweak one of their taco options into a very tasty meal. The wine selection was excellent as well... I sipped on an intoxicating glass of Malbec. Including tip, I was able to walk out for just $20. Urban Grub's prices are very fair!

You will definitely see me checking into Urban Grub on many more occasions. What a wonderful addition to the 12 South neighborhood.

Came in about a week ago and left unsatisfied. I choose this restaurant because of its high ratings with the assumption that it would live up to its expectations. 

Food: very small portion which is fine but extremely mediocre. I waited approximately half an hour for my food to come out & when it did it was cold. I got pad Thai but the shrimp was over cook and dry and even worst the noodles was extremely greasy.
NOTE: I also saw my waitress drop my spring roll and picked it up and served to me.

Bottom line: I would not recommend anyone coming here but maybe you'll have a different experience. Honestly, I could had better food from a Chinese take out and paid a fraction of the price.

Cool cafe for working or relaxing over sophisticated drinks and snacks. Located just a short drive from the French Quarter, it's a great spot to escape the 24/7 party vibe without having to travel too far. It also means Mojo is frequented by a mix of both locals and tourists. There's ample street parking, a few tables set up outside to enjoy the sun on a good day, and plenty of seating inside for customers. 

Mojo has a good set-up for those wishing to get work done, including Wi-Fi, outlets, and a variety of seating options. Unfortunately, the actual store lighting isn't too bright so if you're sitting where the natural light can't reach and without a computer screen, it feels a bit dim. Particularly on the dark wood counter space.
