My other qualm is that there's only one bathroom stall located in the back up a ramp, which means that if there's a tourist trying to purge their morning beignets, you can't empty your bladder and get back to work. Otherwise, the background noise and music level are kept at a good level for that cafe ambience without being forced to overhear a neighbor's conversations. 

There's actually two counters to order from, one for drinks located near the entrance, and the other on the opposite side in the larger sitting area for food, including their popular acai bowls and crispbreads. 

In addition to the customary caffeinated beverage selection, they have some unique offerings like an Elderflower Sparkling Lemonade, which was decent but not quite what I was expecting. I WAS impressed that it was made on the spot, lemon squeezer and all. I'm no coffee expert, but from an appearances standpoint the Mojo baristas seem to put effort into each drink and I enjoyed my Cortado.

Busy traditional Vietnamese bakery and restaurant off the beaten path from downtown New Orleans renowned for their baked goods. Unfortunately, I was largely underwhelmed by our experience with both aspects. 

Dong Phuong is a bit of a drive from most tourist attractions, or any other settled parts of New Orleans, but it's made it onto people's radars for their King Cake (unfortunately 'twas not the season when we went) and recently recognized with a 2018 James Beard America's Classics award. Bae and I made the trek for some pho and dessert, and found the gravel parking lot pretty full, but not yet packed. 

We were seated right away in the dining area and after ordering the Vietnamese Crepe (#3) and Pho w/ Eye-Round Steak (#44), ventured over to the bakery. We decided not to stuff ourselves to food coma oblivion by ordering a Banh Mi sandwich, but walked away with a large Egg Tart that was promptly devoured. Hearing about the buttery, flakiness of their other pastries, I was very, very disappointed with the tart's hard crust and the blandness of the custard. 

The crepe was good and different from what we anticipated, quite a filling appetizer with generous portions of meat! The pho was... well, your average pho, served with basil, cilantro, bean sprouts, etc. Even bae, who is not a snobby Californian, didn't find anything particularly noteworthy. 

Normally I am happy to be ignored after the waiter has taken my order so I may dine in peace, but we literally had to ask 3 times any time we wanted another bowl, a fork, a water refill, or the check. 

It's hard to imagine we missed out on the blissful happy-stomach feelings I had expected on 3/3 counts, but maybe we just didn't order the right things or came at an off time. The food is satisfying but easily outpaced by other restaurants in New Orleans. I would return for the elusive King Cake and sample a few more of their baked goods, but probably not to eat in.

Ate here after reading some reviews so I thought I'd give it a shot. Darkly lit place, not the most comfortable. I ordered the Lasagna, which was delicious. Can't say enough how good it was. It was 4-5 stars easily. 

The reason I knock the place a little is because when I ordered the Lasagna, the waiter asked me what I would like for my salad. I just said a side salad with whatever dressing would be fine.  I ASSUMED it came with my meal, I really didn't even want it. Well, when I got my bill, I had gotten a 9 dollar salad.  I didn't say anything about it, but be careful when ordering so you don't accidentally get tricked into getting something you really didn't want to pay for. It's an older crowd restaurant which is fine. I like my food, just wish I hadn't paid for the salad.

This is a great authentic Mexican restaurant! It is BYOB so don't forget to bring a bottle  to enjoy with your meal. 

The food is so delicious and very affordable! I had the Pastor Pork Tacos and I think they are my favorite pork tacos I have ever had. The order comes with 3 full sized tacos served on corn tortillas topped with cilantro and onions. They only cost $5.95! That is a steal!

Wow! Wow! Wow! I've been seeing this little place in Dunedin, FL on my way home from work, making a mental note that it might be a place I'd like to try.

A friend from work recommended it so my husband and I decided to try it out this weekend. He's always up for trying new places so it was easy to get him on board.

What a cute little restaurant that oozes with Florida charm! Inside decorations very appealing. We opted to eat out on the patio, however, since it was a nice afternoon.

I ordered the surf and turf (braised short ribs and scallops) with sweet potato purée and collard greens. I'm not a collard greens kind of girl so I substituted the fried corn. My meal was AMAZING!! I ordered the small portion ($15) and it was more than enough- a large meaty piece of beef and five scallops. My husband ordered the grilled hogfish (peach chutney) with green beans and garlic mashed potatoes. He might have been over there licking his plate but I was too busy polishing mine off to notice ;) . Even though we were full, we decided to try their chocolate peanut butter pie for a shared dessert.

In total, we laid down $53.78 (not counting tip) for this phenomenal meal, dessert, a beer and a soda. And trust me, we plan to tell every Yelper that this is a MUST TRY place you will be certain to enjoy!
I did like this place but now no because the noodles were dry and the person that send me to the seat were looking at me like some thing is wrong

I tried the freshly opened Tamarack Steakhouse and Lounge on Friday March 30, 2012 along with my wife and a girlfriend of hers.  In short, our experience was a pleasant one, and are happy to have this option in South Reno and look forward to returning.  I'll include a quick recap below for those seeking specific details.

One of the things I noticed immediately on arrival were a set of (closed) glass doors to enter the restaurant.  I'm not a big fan of hanging around inside the Tam as I don't play slots and it's generally dark and smells of stale cigarette smoke.  The closed doors told me they are making the effort to keep the restaurant environment separate from the casino.  Good thinking. (Plus)

We arrived on time for a 7pm reservation and were seated within a few minutes.  The room is nicely decorated, well-lit, and up to date, with both tables and booths.  Seated in a booth on the back wall, we didn't find a full dining room to be overly loud.  Fresh white linen, beautiful chargers and brand new flatware adorned a table devoid of things that shouldn't be there.

We were greeted promptly at our table, drink orders taken and served and then appropriately informed of specials.  My wife has an allergy (not an intolerance or preference, but a serious allergy) to all dairy, which in some places can be a real challenge.  The staff worked with us pleasantly and accommodated her with options from the menu both standard and what could be modified and how. (Plus)

Additionally, I had brought a bottle of wine to enjoy and it was opened with a smile and even a few questions about the winery. (Plus) Corkage was fair at $20.  The wine list was sufficient, if not a bit heavy handed with Ferrari-Carano, but certainly more than enough other quality options.  Pricing was average for the bottles offered.

The three of us started with the table-side prepared Caesar salad for $9 per person (one with no dairy).  It's a bit of a lighter preparation than the slightly heavier and more pungent one at Harrah's, which is a fav.  It was nonetheless very pleasing, complete with the fresh anchovies two of us requested. 

Entrees come with a choice of soup or house salad, and a chef's-choice side.  There are also a la carte classic steakhouse sides to choose from.  Since we had ordered the Caesar, we were told that we could still have the soup if we wished.  We declined and as it turned out the salad was more than ample.

Our chosen entrees were an experiment of sorts.  NY Strip, Filet, (each $39) and the table-side prepared Steak Diane.  We wondered if two different cuts and a table-side entree would be timed properly with the correct temps coming out of a newly opened kitchen?  They passed with flying colors.  Just as the Diane was being plated (after being treated to it's olfactory pleasing preparation) the other two steaks came out, not only at MR+, and rested properly, but they were also hot! (Plus)  The side was an au gratin potato which was cooked properly and nicely seasoned as were the steaks.  In the end a bit of the rich Steak Diane went home for a snack, the NY and Filet happily devoured. (I apologize for the marginal picture quality, suffice to say we thought what was in front of us was worthy to share)

For a restaurant that had barely opened it's doors there were a few very tiny bumps which should be expected, but nothing that would keep us from returning and a couple of work-flow adjustments won't solve.  The effort was there, and if you know anything about the business, it simply takes a little time to find the right rhythm between kitchen and front of house.  Additionally, no matter how many soft openings you have, all the peculiarities of real guests can't be duplicated.

Try it, bring a little patience, and if you have suggestions make them to management after the meal for the best chance to have them considered.

I am a donut fanatic so I knew I had to try five daughters ASAP. I came here on a sat morning around 12 ish and there was already a good chuck of people waiting in line. The line moved pretty quickly. I just wished I had more time to look at the various flavors and options. I felt really rushed and confused, like I was having a speed date with all them donuts. (can't complain about that though.. donuts are probably better than any tinder matches) 

It was super hard to narrow down my choices, but I ended up picking three 100 layer donuts. Can I live a hundred years so I can eat one everyday?!?! I ended up getting chocolate raspberry, maple cinnamon, and cherry. They were all DELISH!!! I just wish i had more monies so I could have tried more. but i be on that poor student budget :( My favorite was definitely the cherry, it had just the perfect balance of sweetness! 

So if you're ever out running or hanging out around 12 south, treat yo self to some 100 layer donuts! I promise you won't regret it!

Hello its me, the ice cream fanatic. 

Whenever I'm feeling that I need a little pick me up either during the day or at night, Jeni's is my go to place! Just a heads up though, if you are looking to binge eat ice cream, then this might not be the place for you... unless you don't mind dropping some $$$. Which I don't mind at all, because Jeni's is THAT good! I'm all for quality over quantity, but I do love my cheap buffets every now and then! 

The best part about visiting Jeni's is getting to sample ALL the flavors they have. I'm sorry to anyone who had to wait behind me because I was too busy stuffing my face in the unlimited samples. The workers are all super friendly and won't get annoyed that you keep asking for samples. They're also super helpful in explaining the flavors and their recommendations!! I always need their help cause I can never decide on what I want !!! 

Honestly, you can't go wrong with anything at Jeni's, but I'll list a few of my favorites! 
1. Brambleberry Crisp- This was the first flavor that I had at Jeni's and it was love at first site. I mean you don't really forget your first love, amirite. 
2. Wildberry Lavendar- Whenever I'm missing the bay area, i'll get this. I don't know why, but it just reminds me of eating bi rite while people watching at Dolores Park! 
3. Ndali Estate Vanilla Bean- This is your go to flavor if you don't know what to pair with your chocolate or fruity flavors. Theres something about Jeni's Vanilla bean that you just won't be able to find in other vanilla ice cream! 
4. Torrone- I don't know if this is a seasonal flavor or not, but if you see it then you HAVE to try it. Theres a surprise with each bite. It has toasted almonds, white chocolate, honey and sea salt. I don't think it can get better than that! 
5. Red Raspberry Sorbet- This is for when you're missing summer. Its super fruity and light! 

If you haven't been to Jeni's yet, you definitely have to add it to your list! How can you pass up on a cute place with good vibes and ice cream. You'll definitely leave Jeni's ice screaming for joy!

3 times out of the week, i'll usually crave Thai food thats why it was so important for me to find a cheap and delicious Thai restaurant! I've tried a bunch of restaurants in Nashville and Thai Esane took home the prize. If you're not in the Nashville area, don't fret! Thai Esane has another location in Antioch! Its part of an Asian supermarket! 

I alternate between getting Pad Thai and Pad See Ew. The pad thai is a solid 10, it had enough veggies and peanuts to complement the large portions of noodles! Fair warning: they don't joke around with their spiciness. I got the medium pad thai thinking I could handle it only to have tears rolling down my face and flames coming off my tongue with each bite. Still, I powered through and finished everything because it was THAT good! The pad see ew is also perfect. How can you go wrong with thick noodles, veggies, and that savory and rich sauce!!! 

The portion sizes are pretty big for dinner so you'll be able to have leftovers that you can take home and eat while you watch chick flicks the next day. Something i'm very guilty of doing on a constant basis! No shame!

This place deserves 5 stars for being the real MVP when I need to satisfy my midnight drunchies or muchines. Let's be real, we've all had those times when we're craving something fried and bad, but nothing is opened. 

Not only is this place opened late, it has all kinds of wonderful fried concoctions and tons of drink options that you can choose from. Best of all are the prices. You can get a whole box of food for only $5, it honestly doesn't get better than that. 

Cookout is honestly the place where I can let my inner fat girl come out, no shame at all.

Del Frisco's is all bark and no bite.  

The steaks are not remotely on par with other steakhouses in the city (outside of price) and the wine for the most part is on a 300+% premium, which is significantly more than most restaurants in the city.   

If you look forward to a poorly designed 24,000 sq ft space where your table is almost touching your neighbor, come here.  If you enjoy sending your steak back because it's OK for a new steakhouse to "work on their kitchen" even though you paid at minimum $36 a steak, DF is the best place to do so.  They will probably comp the whole check!

With so many steakhouses in the city, there is little point in spending your money here unless you're dead set on impressing your friends with the enormity of the space.

Fellow Yelpers, how often do you trust a restaurant where most good reviews were written by someone with 2 or fewer reviews who has not  written since their review of DF?   The picture posted by a "reviewer" here on Yelp isn't even from the same location!  Don't let the marketing machine here fool you.  (reference their TripAdvisor review as well) 

btw...their "signature" cocktail is a lesser (Smirnoff) version of the Stoli Doli at Capital Grille which has had the same cocktail (with less pineapple juice) longer than DF has even been in existence.

Food is amazing! Service a bit on the slow end but the food, ambience and hospitality overshadows the snail pace of its service. Meet my yelp friends for a Christmwas dinner. Located in a mini plaza in between a KFC and another southern restaurant, this hidden germ is truly tucked away from the main motorway. Seating is limited and self served. Options to pick up are available. The food was delicious. Not constipating either, especially with its high carbohydrate component. We ordered, the meat and chicken skewer platter. It came with two chicken skewers, 2 meat skewers, fried cassava of yuca, fermeted corn meal wrapped in corn leaf, sausages, salsa and lightly fried corn meal. The meat was nicely seasoned, taste was perfect. Went well with the sausage links, salsa and cassava. We also ordered, what tasted like a corn meal embedded with cheese fried in butter. Delicious!

Rooster's menu and attention to its customers far exceeds most restaurants I've been to. Located in a developing and changing part of town, I was surprised to see how soothing and welcoming it was upon entering. Bar stools please. I and a friend sat at a bar and got prepped by a supper friendly wait staff who went over the menu with us. The menu is not overwhelming but its uniqueness can be a bit much to absorb especially when your brain has not been fed yet. Luckily this was not my friends first rodeo with Rooster so that helped a lot. We ordered 4 out of the 6 items listed on the slightly larger menu. Gnocchi, middlins risotto, R&tT fish, and the black garlic braised beef shank. Based on these four items we tried, I can say the flavours of the menu are most definitely internationally inspired. You can taste a bit of every continent and what I wondered the most was how their menu comes about. Its definitely unique in a sense that Rooster cannot be placed in a box when it comes to the type of food served. By the way all dishes were good. As limited as the menu was, the bar was also miniscule. Wine and beer. No complaints there as the ambience, customer service and food made up for my crave for mixed drinks.
I know there is a lot of hype here but it just wasn't all it is made out to be.  It was nice to sit outside but didn't really enjoy the cigarette smoke blowing in my face.

Went for lunch and I will probably never go back again.

The problem wasn't the decor (call it stylized Modernist Northwoods Hunting Lodge) nor, really, the food.

The problem was my waiter.

Me and my companion sat down and were immediately caught up in the high energy prattle management forces their waitstaff to recite.  Mine got into it only too much.  But this I can understand.

Choose a high energy person, and have management put a boot up their butt to be even higher energy and that's what you get.

Nor did the informality really hurt (though, of course, my waiter was informal by even neighborhood diner standards).

No, my waiter violated a cardinal Goddamned rule of waiting.

She argued with me.

I was asking for a beer list.  So she went through the taps.  But I was looking for German Lager, so I asked about bottles.  She said, "We have just about everything."

I replied, "Anything German?"

She said (and I'm quoting) "What Yuengling isn't German enough for you."  

Maybe she thought she was being cute, but I don't tolerate dismissive and argumentitive comments from waitstaff.

I replied that Yuengling was not German at all and was in fact from Pottsville, PA and had been since 1808.  Now that was the wrong year (the real one was 1829), but you see my point.

If the answer was no to German beer, simply say no.  Don't plug a completely un-German, totally American product, in place of what I'm asking for.  Don't be flip and dismissive to my legitimate dining related question.

What did she do?

She corrected me on the date that the freakin' brewery opened and talked about their German brewing tradition and how her Grandfather was a brewer in Western Pennsylvania.  In other words, she kept arguing.

At which point I told her, as calmly as I could, "Stop arguing with me."

I wanted to walk out right there, but my companion was in for the long haul.

I ordered a Coke.

That, I think, is when she got that she'd screwed up.

She apologized for offending me and tried to explain that she'd just turned 21 and apparently started being interested in beer.  Or maybe she meant she was finally old enough to pick fights with diners.  Or that the years of meth abuse had been hard on her.  Frankly I don't know or care.

What she should have done was keep her mouth shut.

I was ready to talk to her manager if she didn't stop bothering me.  You know, in the kind of, "You should fire her" way.

After that she was grossly over attentive, hovering, as informal as ever and obviously trying to protect her tip.  She Got 10% and no drink orders.

The food, by the way was decent, but the Buffalo burger needed to rest longer.  It leaked juices as soon as I bit into it.

Visiting the Yelp Spring Break Nashville 2014, we went off the beaten path for this experience on a Saturday morning. Told that there would be a wait of over an hour, I had no qualms. Travelling all the way from Alexandria, VA, I had a hunch it would be worth it.

It has been a long time since my childhood, growing up in Florida, that I tasted truly authentic southern cooking. Ham steak, sausage patties with biscuits and gravy, grits...mmm.

The bonus is there are many things to keep you entertained while you wait. It's a village of family fun to entertain everyone. Antique and boutique shopping, complimentary sweet peach tea, quaint areas to bide your time while playing bean bag toss (AKA the "corn hole" game which made me blush). And Pumpkin Butter samples!

When we were finally seated, it was by the general manager, who enthusiastically made us feel welcome. The waitress was also a sweetie. Service is key here.

I can vouch for the:

Complimentary Biscuits and (3) Jelly Sampler
Ham Steak
Pimento Cheese
Biscuits and Gravy
Omelets
And Creamed Spinach

If I were to visit Nashville again, this would be a destination!

Id put this place up against ANY sandwich place in the country ..I shit you not , they're that good.

IF you come,  come hungry as  they do not skimp .

I have been going there for years, and they only seem to get better with age 

Now they have gone and opened a pizzeria connected to the damn deli.. and the Pizza is outstanding .  They have a trademark extra thin crust, with some of the most original combinations I have ever tasted. 

SO lets see what the hell you actually have here .. You have an Italian Bakery, which is also an italian market offering items, you cant get in regular supermarkets, which just also happens to be Italian deli (one that serves a roast pork sandwich that IMO is better than DiNics!!! ) , and now one of the most original pizzeria's you'll find on the east coast

The SOB's even serve Crepes filled with Nutella ....  

The staff is about as friendly as there is, they are family owned and operated, and are genuinely appreciative of all their customers 

If youre in the Collegeville area you owe it to yourself to give it a try

Tried and tried since day 1. Every time is a fail. SERVICE and MANAGEMENT are the worst. Gave it a 2 star, not 1, only cuz food doesn't suck. It's every other aspect. 

I blame mgmt, down, cuz they can't keep  great staff; instead, promote worst staff who have no clue. Managers "showboat" and never really serve.

TVs for sports? Great if you can hear them. Wait 20 mins for a drink, 1+ hrs for food. ??  Don't waste your time. Native is opening soon, closer to the road.

I love this place and Vincent is always a great host and funny too! This is a great place to get a delicious meal and always interact with an owner who appreciates his guests! The entire staff is very attentive and they really do work to get you in and seated quickly! The food is always prepared well and all dishes are great- hard to narrow down choices!

This was my first experience at Saint James. Unfortunately, it will very likely end up being my last. I was part of a relatively large group (10 to 12 people) that had made a reservation. This was a casual, after work get together -- drinks with the option of others staying for dinner if it suited them.

The place is somewhat difficult to find if you're not familiar with the area. It's not clustered with the other quality midtown restaurants and shops. There's a large parking lot shared with other businesses. This is problematic -- a member of my group that parked in a section designated for one of the other businesses was towed (the parking lot was very full all around). This is not the fault of Saint James or its staff, but seems like an indication that the climate between the businesses in the area isn't exactly positive.

As mentioned in several of the other negative reviews, we were pressured by the waitstaff to order food almost immediately despite the fact that a reservation had been made for our group with details about the type of gathering it would be. When it became apparent that no one was ordering food, we were encouraged to leave. The service overall was mediocre, and the attitude of the waitstaff wasn't helping anything.

The worst part of the experience was actually the aftermath. Two members of my group had holds placed on their credit cards for the entire bill. The bill was, in fact, paid across a combination of cash and multiple cards (again, large group -- and the waitress didn't offer to split the bill... though the 20% gratuity was automatically added, of course). When contacted about the holds placed on the cards from last night, the staff was unconcerned and suggested that the affected people just call back if they were actually charged.

Long story short, though this place has potential, I was disappointed by the way we were treated. I don't care how good the food is, if I can't bring colleagues or clients here without fear of being shuffled back out the door with very little common courtesy, I'll pass.

One of the most amazing bento box lunch deals you can get anywhere in the country.  You get soup, salad, asian veggies, dumplings, sushi, and lots of whatever protein you order plus more rice.  I ordered the sushi bento box and it could have easily been split with another person, but of course I ate it all by myself ... weight loss goals here I come... My mom also ordered some gyozas which were fried perfectly to a crisp that I also hoarded onto my plate.  Everything was fresh, cleanly presented, and absolutely delicious. 

The quality of the sushi was great and I can't wait to go back to get more sushi rolls.  They also have a killer happy hour with $4 rolls - umm yes.  I will be back again.

For the span of 2 months, I would pass this store going to and coming from work. All I saw was a new place baking and serving cupcakes was going to be in the store. And I was excited. 

Well, it finally opened and my fiance and I visited it Christmas Eve day. It smelled wonderful. I really liked the decor. I spoke with a gentleman behind the counter and he said that business was brisk, which is fantastic. 

We bought 4 cupcakes, vanilla bean w/ vanilla icing, lemon w/ lemon icing, cinnamon swirl coffee w/ crunch icing, and banana w/ cream cheese icing. We had one after dinner that night and saved the other two for breakfast the next morning. 

Instead of describing each cupcake, I will summarize in one short sentence - These were fantastic tasting cupcakes w/ icing that wasn't too sweet. 

We definitely will be back, but not too often. $3 for a cupcake is a bit too much for us to be making multi-weekly visits.

I was glad to see this location open again after Baxter's Black Sheep Grill closed. I was excited to give the new place a try. Unfortunately, 30 Main is way below par from Black Sheep or its competition along that stretch of Rt 30. Dinner was mediocre. My fish tacos were OK (a little bland, but passable), while my wife and daughter didn't like their meals at all. Service was disorganized and painfully slow. Among the problems was our waitress depositing someone else's credit card on our table after I paid cash. 30 Main was the worst dining experience I've had since moving to the area 3 years ago. With so many better choices within the same couple of blocks, I'm not going to waste my appetite or my money here. Neither should you.

If you don't know Jack, the owner of Latea Bubble Tea Lounge, please introduce yourself and become best friends. He's one of the nicest business owners in the entire state of Indiana (no joke). Not only does he bring his positive attitude to Latea Bubble Tea Lounge, his passion and education for bubble tea and tea products shine through their high quality ingredients and attention to detail.

I was beyond ecstatic to find out that Latea was finally making its way down south from West Lafayette to the vibrant Mass Ave. It was worth a drive up to Lafayette, but now that it's only a couple of blocks from work, I'll be a check-in regular. 

Reasons to love Latea: 
- great attention is put into the ingredients of the products. The boba is made in-house (there's even a window where you can watch their pastries and bobas being made). The products are all natural or organic, meaning no artificial flavors are added like many boba teas around the city. As Jack would say, if he wouldn't drink it, neither would his customers. 
- the staff is beyond incredibly helpful. They go above and beyond to make sure that every customer has a five-star experience from start to finish. 
- the interior was made for business meetings, casual hangouts with friends, and study sessions. I feel like literally every single seat in this place (both the main floor and the 2nd floor) have outlets near them for charging, and some even have USB plug-ins. 
- customization is here to make it fit your dietary needs/requests. They have light ice and/or sweetening options. They have dairy-free milk options. They have caffeine-free options. 
- the amount of product options is through-the-roof endless. Bubble teas, nitro-infused teas, iced/hot, espresso/coffee drinks, cheese-topped drinks (yes, they have tea drinks with cheese on top), super dessert-like drinks, pastries, and more. 

Yes, there are tons of boba/bubble tea options in Indy, but this one is truly one of the best, if not -the- best. Give it a shot, stay for awhile and hang out, fall in love. 

Tip: don't forget to sign up for their rewards program!

Prior to dinner, my dinner mate asked, "Where's your favorite veggie burger in town?" My response was a local, popular burger joint. Now, Baby's has taken the spot. 

First off, their designers did an amazing job at taking this place from dingy, dark, gross nightclub to dainty, pink, and Instagram-worthy restaurant. It's retro with modern touches - very fun. 

The staff are all very, very friendly as well. I hadn't been in before, and they were very informative (without being overwhelming) about suggestions, what their known for, their favorites, etc. 

I opted for the BYO veggie burger. The veggie burger is made from black beans and sweet potatoes. You get a nice touch of smokiness, which really ups the flavor, making it my new fave veggie patty in the city. (PS - chefs - if you're a local restaurant and you're still using Impossible Burgers or another frozen plant-based veggie patty - c'mon, you need to up your game.)

Along with the burger, we got a chocolate milkshake to split and an order of fries to split with a delicious dipping sauce. The food was all spectacular. 

That being said, my thrifty side will say that it's easy to spend $20+ a person at this joint as everything is a la carte and we didn't even order boozy shakes. The prices add up quite quickly here, which is a little frustrating as I won't frequent this place as often as I'd like to, but it's still one of my new favorite restaurants in the city. 

Great job, Baby's!

Well, it's hard to even force yourself to go to a place when you walk by the kitchen door (it was opened in the Marsh parking lot) and see one of the chefs drinking from the water bowl and spitting into one of the sinks where food was nearby. 

I'll definitely be back as the staff was nice and it seems like a good restaurant with nice interior, but the health department should probably inspect this place if they allow their staff to drink out of mixing bowls and spit out water into the sinks where they cook and clean dishes.

Eek.

Now that I've been to a few hundred breweries I get a sense about places before I even enter one. Cage has an amazing vibe - it looks like it is excised straight out of the South Slope landscape in Asheville. The octopus logo and mural have so much character and originality. The interior is a bit rough around the edges but gives it a totally laid back feel. The outdoor space is humungous. This place makes 4 and 5 star beer and every one I tried was a solid, well made product - kudos to the brewer(s). 

So why 3 stars Michael??

My bartender on April 15th (female, dark hair shoulder length, high-waisted shorts) was so rude and unfriendly, I can't not mention it in this review. It ruined my visit to their tap room. I began a short lived conversation with "I really like your logo, you guys seem really legit". I got a snarl and a snarky "Yeah, we are legit". That was all she wrote - not another look or word. You can't have people like that at the front of your house representing your beer. Just straight up not cool.

Now the beer - Mango Bob's - their Mango American IPA is one of the top three IPAs I've had this year (up there with Burial Scythe Rye IPA and Fonta Flora's Alpha vs Beta Carotene) - five freakin' stars.  Lucky Dragon is one heck of a good Pale Ale with honorable mentions to Galaxy Cat (American Pale Ale) and Sir Eric IPA.

I would have stayed and had many more Mango Bob's - I would have probably "bought the hat" - but beside the beer, all I had when I left was sour taste in my mouth - just wish I'd gotten one of the other two bartenders who were actually being nice to people and not a total a$$hat.

Places like these are why I Yelp!!! I would have never found this place, or found it so quickly on my own!!

Barracuda was literally the first place we went to after arriving at St. Pete and so glad we did!

AUTHENTIC - through and through - probably the best Cuban sandwich I've ever had. In a addition to the normal ingredients, which were all high quality, including the mustard, thin sliced pickles and fresh crusty bread, there was a healthy portion of their slow cooked Mojo pork on top. To Die For! It also comes with a side - we got some incredible red beans and rice. These ladies know how to cook! Both the red beans and the black beans were perfectly seasoned. The Mojo Pork bowl is as good as if not better than the Cuban. Check out my picture. Look at that massive amount of tender pork with grilled onions - I want some right now!! It even comes with a massive plateful of house salad.

Everyone here was so wonderful and attentive - fantastic customer service - they make you feel like you're family!!!

Ridiculously highly recommended!

Have you ever left a brewery and though, "Wow, just, Wow!" - come to Old Bakery Brewing Company in Illinois and I guarantee you will be impressed not only with their beer but also their food!

First a little background - the brewery is a bit over four years old now. It is located in Downtown Alton Illinois right across from St. Louis. The building they renovated and now occupy was once the Colonial Bakery Facility. The space is massive - the building contains 18,000 square feet. You will be drinking awesome beer very close to where Abraham Lincoln and Stephen Douglas debated for a Senate seat.  The owners Laura Patten and James Ragalsky came from Urban Chestnut Brewing in St. Louis to open the first Craft Brewery in Alton and it has been a catalyst for local growth with at least 25 new businesses opening their doors along with them.

The building itself from the parking lot is a bit unassuming, but once you enter, the massive scale/size of this operation is immediately apparent. There's even a historical section that pays tribute to the Colonial Bakery, has sculptures, additional seating and a life size painted stand-up of Robert Wadlow, the tallest man in history according to Guiness (and Alton, Ill. resident) for photo ops.

Then there's Matt, one hell of a Taproom manager and then there's Rory, one hell of a bartender - both of them just all around great guys - genuinely friendly and every Brewery Owners dream to have the front of their house represented in such a positive, professional manner.

The Food: Stunning - Fantastic - Well Thought Out - Literally Something for Everyone. Both my Asian Style Cauliflower Tacos and Pastor Pork Taco were just amazing. Flavor for days! You can taste the love! Just look at their Instagram page and you will see some examples of the kitchen's skill and creativity.

The Beer:  All Organic. Utilizes a Reverse Osmosis System. The first two things you will notice in general about their beer - the clarity and the crispness of flavors. That's the quality of the water, the freshness and difference of the organic ingredients and of course, the recipes. There was not a beer I didn't like - but I did have some favorites.

My Flight: Digital Orange IPA, Kind of Blueberry Kolsch, Cerveza Con Lima, and Session IPA. The Rosemary IPA here is the best I've ever had. I could go on and on and write a description about each beer like I normally might, but my words might not do them justice. Let me just say that I've almost never encounter a flight (and then some) at a brewery that has had such a strong, impressive lineup. 

Thanks for such great hospitality (and the cool history lessons) Matt and Rory!!!
 
You guys have built something amazing and I know you will just keep growing!

I've been able to experience the joy of getting to visit and the sadness that you guys are so far away... hey I've got an idea, open a location in Charlotte!!!

Bearded Iris is 100% rock n' roll - if the Ramones owned a Brewery it would look and feel like this.

Located in The East Germantown Neighborhood of Nashville, this place is busy and stays busy. Part of that is because Nashville is a big place with lots of locals and tourists and also because these guys make very good beer. 

Some quick things to know: The menu here is heavy on the IPAs. The parking lot fills up quickly but there's plenty of street parking. They will check your ID even if you're 90, so don't be offended. Real Estate at the bar is hard to come by, so if you want some and see some, grab it. No flights here.

My visit there was a single line to the right of the bar. Multiple Bartenders were checking  IDs and taking orders. If you're looking for variety here, do like I did and get a few half pours - they will also give you tastes.

The taproom is cavernous and faces the big beautiful shiny production tanks.  The music is loud, the people are cool and the artwork is badass. Love the big portrait of Louis Pasteur, who could easily be mistaken for Sigmund Freud. Outside there are several covered picnic tables if you can take the brutal heat!

I had three half pours - Homestyle, one of their flagship IPAs was my favorite - clean, fruity, delicious - followed by the DDH version of Chief of Chiefs - dry, smooth, grapefruit.

Would put this up there as one of the top three breweries in Nashville!

3 Daughters has a pretty large facility (including canning) and as expected this place was hopping on a Saturday. Even with the crowd it didn't take more than a few minutes to get a flight. Not sure what was up with the free Valet parking on the day I went but it was a nice treat!!

The selection of beers was pretty impressive - as a spoiler, I had already had a can of their IPA locally and knew it was good already. What really won me over was the Black IPA - so well balanced and full of flavor - smooth and hoppy - it was totally bad ass.  The Black Lager was also pretty killer. The Bimini Twist IPA has a nice hop profile and the Beach Blonde Ale goes down easy.

Outside were some food trucks, a live band, corn hole and those giant connect four games. It almost looked like there was some kind of festival going on, but maybe this is what every Saturday looks like at this place! It's good to drink beer in St. Pete!!! There's a little something here at 3 Daughters for everyone!!

I was really pumped for some good ice cream when I saw the sign for Larry's and read the Yelp reviews.

Then not so pumped when I saw the line was out the door. There were three or four employees working the counter so the line moved pretty quickly. With some shuffling of bodies we got to view some nice looking trays of gelato and some very interesting donuts with creative toppings. There were some crazy looking waffle cones as well that had fruit loops and fruity pebbles spackled to the outsides.

I was looking forward to locally made homemade ice cream but noticed the side of the containers they scooped from said The Ice Cream Store (or maybe Factory) 35th Anniversary. I asked if the banana was made with real or fresh bananas and he replied no. The Black Cherry was okay but the Peach had pieces of what had the texture of canned peaches. Maybe my expectations were too high. Maybe they make their own gelato and I should have ordered that instead.  Compared to true homemade places like the ones popping up in Charlotte, Udderly Delcious in Hickory or The Hop in Asheville, this might as well have been Bryer's.

Came here for a banquet tonight. The food is ok nothing special to talk about. The service well I ask 5 different waiters for a high chair before I actually got one. The place need some serious renovation. The carpets are all sticky n yucky. The chairs are all wobbly.

Bacon. Wrapped. Shrimp. 'Nuff said! 

Fajitas are my fave at a Mexican restaurant, and I've discovered some of the absolute BEST I've had anywhere: the Juarez Shrimp Fajitas. Perfectly done, 10 jumbo bacon wrapped shrimp arrived on a hot, but not typically sizzling, plate.

Their prices are a bit higher than similar Mexican restaurants in the area, though it was worth every bite.

The decor is absolutely gorgeous, friendly staff, huge place! As we're still in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, all staff was masked, and diners wore masks when walking to/from tables.

I demolished most of a basket of chips and very flavorful, mild salsa (just my speed), while awaiting my friend's arrival, washing them down with a Blue Moon draft.

We opted to sit at the bar, where we had plenty of space on a Monday evening. 

The negatives:

The bartender wasn't aware that the fajitas included red peppers, which I prefer. I asked if they could add red peppers, as on the menus, on both Yelp/website, mention only green peppers (and onions). She said they didn't have them.

She mentioned while I awaited my friend's arrival that she'd worked there for a while, so I thought she'd have known the menu more thoroughly.

My friend's large margarita on the rocks was pretty weak. Definitely not a lot of alcohol and it was...missing something. She let the bartender know and she offered my friend a shot glass of lime flavoring, saying they typically go lightly, as it's intense. Adding some of it didn't make it any better, unfortunately.

Once all of the outdoor diners were gone, we got blasted with music from a somewhat old school boom box that got turned our way. The volume was better suited for a busy weekend evening, rather than a handful of diners on a weeknight.

I'd love to sit out on the patio next time - I'll surely be back for those fajitas!

Ordered delivery, just a ceasar salad and some onion rings. Delivery driver called and had a problem with my gate, he was opening the wrong end. No problem. Got my food and he was nice. Opened the salad and there was a pubic hair right on top. Couldn't eat anything after seeing that. I tipped 1 dollar on the app and some cash so I thought maybe it was because of that. it only showed a dollar tip on his end and I tipped the rest when he came...I thought it was payback for that. Will not order again.

Holy moly my very first one star review ever and I didn't even eat...A. Evil hostess try and be nice. Smile and seat people happily instead of rudely greeting them, taking them to their seats and placing the wine menu just out of reach. I shouldn't have to lean across the table to get the wine menu. NEWS FLASH YOU'RE IN SALES TOO!!!! B. With totally insane prices which we were happily willing to pay I should have literally had a beckon call waiter in place of the several that walked by us without even so much as a greeting for ten minutes as we sat there thirsty. Have you heard of the 5ft rule people?! Come on! C. When we get up and walk out because you clearly have no clue how to give good service don't look at me like I did something wrong and laugh as we walk out the door. Bottom line I will never ever even consider this place again! Get a new hostess and learn some customer service!

We moved from New York City to Tampa this summer and left a slew of really wonderful restaurants that we frequented. One of those amazing restaurants was Pio Pio, an awesome Peruvian restaurant in Manhattan. Where to go for Peruvian food in Tampa? No idea, but Yelp will know. Yelp tells us it is Happy Fish, so we go there, along with my Aunt who has actually never had Peruvian food. We've found our Peruvian food home here now. Upon entering we were warmly welcomed my waitress Sheila. We quickly learned that this is a proud family business, dad Kevin, owner and manager came to every table TWICE to ask all patrons if they were happy with food and service. Two tables were celebrating birthdays- lots of regulars, a real comfortable family place. We had three heaping dishes which were delicious- ceviche, chaufa (chicken fried rice) and lomo saltado. Also the fried donuts for dessert. I'm so full I can barely breathe right now, but I'm still craving more of those delicious donuts. We're thrilled that we've found our Peruvian food home here in Tampa!

Best BBQ in the bay- hands down. You can find this small family owned business in the middle of carver city (neighborhood surrounding Jefferson high). For $10 you can get a meat and two sides. I personally get the chicken but the ribs are awesome as well. The MAC AND CHEESE! Cheese heaven. The pineapple tea is the perfect drink to wash it all down with. Don't bother getting dressed up, this is a down home bbq spot with picnic table sitting. Get there early or you will be in line and potentially miss out and some of these delicious sides because they do sell out. This is definitely somewhere you have to visit yourself because you will not believe the hype until you experience it yourself.

While visiting Nashville our friend said we had to check this place out for their weekend brunch. Unfortunately we were only in town until Friday and we could not make it to there brunch (Friday- Sunday) hours so we decided to visit during lunch. We were kinda of skeptical because all we heard of was their awesome brunch but we were pleasantly surprised. Located in the trendy Gulch neighborhood this place definitely has a great atmosphere equipped with contemporary decor and nice outdoor seating on the patio. Additionally the food did not disappoint. We had the jerk chicken. This was some of the juiciest chicken I've ever had! For a restaurant that was not a Jamaican restaurant, this jerk chicken was top notch! One of our other local friends just happened to be one of the restaurants beer distributors and we randomly bump into him there as well, we joked about the coincidence with the manager - he was such a great host during our visit. We will definitely be coming back when we are back in town and definitely check out their famous brunch !

Fogo KOP, please fix your restaurant. It's like the Applebees version of Fogo De Chao.  
Went to this location for the first time for my anniversary. When we arrived, they couldn't find my reservation. I had to pull my phone out and show the hostess my open table account. Opentable even sent me an email saying that I missed my reservation. 
We walk in and all the classiness of your other location is lost. The dining room has a large cafeteria like ambiance. I always thought you had to get dressed up to go to Fogo. There were large families made up t shirts and hoodies, not the "business casual" dress code that Fogo prides itself with. 
On top of that, there were unaccompanied children running around the aisles. When we were at the salad bar, there was a child who kept taking cheese with his hands and throwing it on the ground. No parents in sight!
Across the dining room there was a small child in a height chair continuously screaming on and off for the majority of our meal. Who takes a 1 year old out to Fogo?

I felt like we kept getting passed over with good cuts of meat because there were only two of us. We saw large parties get bottom cut (my favorite) and top cut (my girlfriend's favorite) and then when the gaucho was finished with them he would completely ignore us! It happened at least five times. At the Philadelphia location, you get bombarded with all different cuts of meat AND they bring you the fried bananas and fresh bread constantly. Your KOP location brought us one plate of bananas and one basket of bread for the entire meal. 
The bathrooms were awful too. The men's room had one urinal and one stall. For a huge restaurant of your size that is unacceptable. My gf says that the ladies room had only two stalls and she had to wait for over ten minutes to use the facilities. 
I think the manager felt some of our pain because he gave every table in our section a free desert. That was very nice, but fix your staff. 
I frequent the Philadelphia location a nice amount and have never had any problems.

TL;DR - Perfect place for a weekend lunch date and everything italian

Mazzaro's is basically one huge sensory overload.  You walk in and you're instantly hit with fresh aroma of deli meats. Decor covers the walls that makes you feel like you're in another country.  The big crowds resemble that of the hustle and bustle of a small foreign market place.  There are huge lines everywhere and for everything but If you plan your visit right, it truly is a remarkable experience.  Here's what to do.

1) Go straight to the deli in the back of the store and take a number and wait to be called.  Don't venture too far as they take orders quickly!  Getting your order is a different story as that takes a little bit longer

2) You'll have give or take 15 minutes until your food is ready so go browse their vast selection of imports of olive oils, spices, pastas, and other itialian goods.  Take note of what you want to buy but wait to pick it up AFTER lunch because you have to pay for your groceries and food separately if you want to eat there.  Save the long line for the END 

3) Head over to their wine and beer section.  If you're lucky, they'll have a free wine, cheese, and meat sampling.  Treat this as a light appetizer for your sammiches! 

4) Had your fill of vino? Now it's about time to go pick up your lunch. They have tons of unique bottled sodas and drinks to go along with your food.  These are located  in a row of coolers along the back wall, next to the patio area where you pay for your lunch and eat.  Remember, no groceries allowed in this line.  I saw some people enjoying a bottle of wine from the store with their lunch but I'm not 100% sure if you can pay for those here or at the front with the rest of your other stuff.

5) NOM NOM NOM!  I got the 8" Italian sandwich served on fresh italian bread.  The meats and flavors are anything like I've ever tasted and are definitely of a different quality than your typical chain sub shop.  My girlfriend got the herb crusted italian panini thats lightly sprinkled with sea salt.  Very similar fillings but completely different sandwich in a good way.  There's a patio area in the back where you can eat your lunch.  While you stand in line to pay, have your significant other scavenge for an empty table which can be hard to find on a busy afternoon.

6)  After you're done eating and before your brain can tell you no, run over to the bakery and choose from the dozens of pastries or creamy gelato to complete your meal.   Now is the time to pick up anything you were looking to buy.  That way,  at least you'll have some dessert to make the long line more enjoyable

7)  Repeat on a different weekend!!!

TL;DR - Carrollwood's first Vietnamese restaurant is a good one!

I'm highly critical when it comes to vietnamese food because nothing beats good ol' home cooking so you can believe me when I say this place passes the taste test.
I ordered the Pho Dac Biet (Pho Special) and everything about it was on point.  It was served in a good sized bowl with just the right amount of noodles and meats. The broth was rich, beefy but yet still light and fragrant.  Along with Pho, Com Tam Suon Nuong is also a staple of every Vietnamese restaurant which I also highly recommend getting here.  Very tender meat that is well marinated and grilled with just the right amount of char.  If you come in a group, the appetizer platter is great to share which comes with a variety of egg rolls, spring rolls, and other shrimp fried goods. 

Not too many complaints other than their Goi Cuon aka spring rolls.  Waaaaay too much noodles with waaaay too little meat.  It might as well be a vegetarian roll because you can barely taste anything but the noodles so I would avoid getting this.  I also don't like the idea of paying a lot for Viet food so I hesitated a little after seeing dishes priced 10+ bucks in the menu including the Pho and Com Tam.   These items should be and are usually 7-8 bucks at any other restaurant.  Luckily for me, my wallet, and my stomach, the portion sizes are good so you really are getting your money's worth.

I'll definitely be back on another night to see if the quality holds up.  Here's to hoping it does because my mom has been lazy on the cooking lately!

Outrageously expensive for what it is -- almost $30 after tip for one beer (Canebreak) and one burger with cheese and tots. It's more expensive than Company Burger and about the same price as Cowbell, but nowhere near the same quality. You can get the exact same style burger at Beachcorner for a fraction of the price, and it tastes better.

I got the spicy burger, which is a mix of beef and hot sausage. It was way over salted, on a very cheap bun. The burger was very large though, I will give them that. I would have preferred half the meat with a higher quality bun. Tater tots were a $2 upcharge, and the portion was fairly small. My stomach was not happy the next morning either.

They aren't gonna make it if they don't up the quality and/or drop the price.

Edit: also, I tried to eat here 2 times on thier opening week. Would you believe that a new restaurant would be closed with no notice? There were 2 other couples trying to get in when I arrived too. Ridiculous.

I must take time to review this place! A good friend of mine took me here and first thing it crossed my mind was this must be a joke because the place doesn't look like they actually sell sandwiches hahaha. Don't get this appearance fool you you must try their food I had roast beef sandwich and OMG was it delicious every bite I took I couldn't stop eating, sandwich is huge and I finished it all, the flavor you get it just reminds me of real food and I have to tell you before you get there go to ATM because they only take CASH during the time I was waiting for my food I saw a lot of locals coming in the store and getting their food it is more like a secret store with great food and they pretend to keep it secret. Thanks god Yelp does EXIST :)
We enjoyed the food but service was awful. Appetizer brought after entrees were finished. Very poor waiter.

This place is pretty inside and love the antique decor and gift shop with all the little trinkets, candy and souvenirs.  The place is big inside with lots of tables and a nice fireplace to keep you warm and give you that cozy warm feel.   

Unfortunately, that's where the love of this place ends for me.  I was greeted right away by the host and sat right away.   My server was nice and ordered right away which was nice.  I had ordered the double meat breakfast with three eggs, bacon and sausage with all the fixin's (sides) as they call it.   The bacon was way over cooked so bad that it crumbled when you bit into it.  The white gravy for the biscuits were about as bland and tasteless as you could possibly imagine and the biscuits tasted like dry flour.   Not moist or buttery or even a hint of salt.  I asked them to please send a new order of bacon out and they gave me half. After 45 minutes of sitting around I had to leave for work.  

When I went to the register in the gift shop area the cashier asked how my experience was.  I told him it was okay not great and they didn't even bring out my full order of bacon.   He replied "oh" and that's it.  Not even an apology or is there anything we can do to correct it.   The food is nothing memorable and the service started off great and ended poorly.   I definitely will not be coming back to this location.

This place used to be good. Clean,  with friendly service. 

I've been observing my server, as well as the others. They only smile at the people drinking. 

Watched the female bartender with purple highlights fix others drinks then wipe her hand on her jeans on the butt then proceed to make my water and drop a lemon in my water with the same hand she just wiped on her butt. 

Still fixing others drinks,  wiping her hands on her jeans. 

Worst service yet. 

She's going to get someone seriously sick. 

I'm not happy with the cleanliness or lack there of from the wait staff.

When your Mom's in town and you've got to chat wedding, the only way to get through the conversation (on a hot af day) is with a refreshing, mind-numbing (in the best way possible) frosé and a dozen chilled oysters, am I right? 

Since Superior Seafood rose from the ashes of my former childhood "fancy" restaurant request, aka Copeland's (RIP Mile High Pie on my burfday with grandma...where did I put those calories back then?), it really has done a great job reppin' this corner. The space is absolutely beautiful and they keep it up really well. I would totally suggest this as a go-to spot for a large group looking for a seafood restaurant Uptown or two women discussing one's upcoming nuptials and said bride's complete lack of having it together (thus the 2-hour lunch meeting). 

I heart oysters, and while their oysters don't seem as big as the one at my other favorite oyster bar, Cooter Brown's, they're colder and a touch cleaner. I can make a dozen from here disappear faster than the Walrus. Bye, bivalves. 

That being said, $15 for a dozen feels steep...But before you go breaking into your piggy bank, my ballers on a budget, they're happy hour is a solid deal! Daily 4 - 6:30PM 50-cent oysters! Solid, solid deal. AND 2-for-1 frozen mojitos, aka slushy goodness, y'all. From their frosés to their frozen French 75s, they know how to make a great fancy daq. They must've rung up the King of Slushyville or the High Priestess on the Island of Daiquiri (where the word actually comes from) and asked for some secret recipe...'cause they're so good. Dangerously good, so watch yo' self and designate a driver.

But with the help of two orders of a dozen oysters, a frosé for me and two French 75s for the mom, and an order of the tuna tartare (not something I would technically want to share in the future because it's so flavorful and not really of sharing proportions), I survived this meeting. Thank you to our waitress who was there when we needed her, and didn't push for us to order more than the above. I would suggest though sitting at the bar if enjoying drinks and a dozen oysters.

They do have a copious amount of other seafood dishes on their menu, so since you're saving so much during happy hour already, be sure to check it out!

I'm so glad this place has had staying power and I think it's because they keep it simple. They didn't take reservations on this Wednesday so not sure if they've changed to first come first served for the weekdays or all the time, but I'd still call when they open. 

I brought a bottle of wine, corkage fee is $10 and they'll keep it chilled and refilled. As mentioned this place keeps it real simple, I think there is only 8 things on the menu. 

I like that they explain their dishes in sweet, savory, and spicy since that's usually how I gauge what I'm going for. We got these suuper tasty squash dumplings seared perfectly with a pico de gallo and peppers/okra on top. SO good I could've eaten a dozen and the spicier wings that weren't really spicy but oh-so-delicious. 

I got the meow meow bowl and my hubs got the bou-jee bowl of ramen. I definitely had entree envy since his noodles were the fat kind, he had bok choy, and his broth was slightly cinnamon-y, but if you like a meaty bowl, the meow meow is where it's at! 

The staff is still incredible, and I need to come back to get their delicious Vietnamese iced coffee / jasmine tea hybrid. Mmmmm...Tomorrow.

Impastato's...never would I have been like, "let's go eat Italian in Metairie off of Causeway, it'll be great." Alas, when one has a friend that goes by the moniker "Meatball" and it's his birthday, you find yourself in Metairie off of Causeway going to eat Italian. 

I had no idea what to expect, and I hate spoiling it for anyone who likes to be just kind of...flabbergasted/in awe of what an uber duber authentic Italian restaurant in New Orleans with serious ties with the Saints, politicians, people of interest....well everyone in New Orleans, looks like, so maybe skip the next paragraph. 

Entering, the corridor between dining rooms is wall-to-wall who's who of who, and I don't believe any of the pictures are from this decade which is great. We were seated in the back dining room with a faux stained glass ceiling, booths, and pink table clothes. Yep. And wine glasses with the pink napkins skinny rolled sticking out of them; I assume a signature look though comical to me. See picture. 

The staff was familiar with our birthday boy so it was more casual than I assume it would usually be but still very polite and on point with bread, water, and wine, oh yes, if you're not looking to have bottomless wine, make sure to wave them off or they'll seamlessly fill your cup. 

Now onto the food. Again with the who's who, these people must know some people. Dishes are named Sonny & Dottie Hughes' Spidini, Joanne Caldcleugh's Crabmeat Canneloni, and Wendy Smith Moffett's Penne all'Arrabbiata. Full on first name last name dishes. Did Ricky Jackson come up with the recipe for Ricky Jackson's Crab Fingers? OR was he like, "damn, these Crab Fingers are uh-mazing!"? You tell me...The prix fixe meal definitely looked like a great deal, but because we were heading out later that night and not looking to go into food comas, I went with Oysters Norman* and the Fresh Fish Payton*. Norman, Payton (I'm assuming Mr. Manning here), your names are glorified in these two delicious dishes!

Oysters Norman 
Oysters sauteed in butter, imported cheeses, shallots & our own special seasonings

I've never had oysters like this before. The perfect portion for one person. Don't even try to share that deliciousness and make sure to have plenty of bread on hand to soak up the sauce. This dish is for someone who isn't afraid to enjoy raw oysters sans a saltine but bathed in a delicious rich sauce with light, crunchy shallots. 

Fresh Fist Payton
Fresh fish, breaded & pan-sautéed, then topped with a sauce of lemon, butter, Dry Sack sherry, fresh mushrooms, artichoke hearts, crabmeat & crawfish

Oh man. They're doing this right y'all. In terms of textures, there is not much in complexity there or levels of flavor, but that's not what is making this dish. The ingredients all meld together so well...each bite taste exactly the same which is fine by me since it was so good. They give you 3/4ths a giant lemon that I squeezed all over my dish. I would say enjoy a few bites and see if that's what you like, which I do. The crabmeat atop the fish was huge fresh chunks, and the portion of the dish was perfect for me to finish. There was quite a bit of lagniappe juices, butter, and what I assume was olive oil still on my plate; a testament to the richness. 

We were a loud, rowdy group towards the end, and the staff put up with us which was much appreciated. It was around $60 per person not counting the copious bottles of wine (probably closer to $80). I will say, not many dishes come with sides and don't necessarily expect the pasta dishes to be heaping bowls of noodles that you can make 3 more meals out of. Time has taught this restaurant how to make the perfect portions that are worth the price tag. 

I noticed the other room was chock-full of football memorabilia, so if you've got a sig. other that loves him/her some football, Italian, and rich dishes; this is your new spot, in Metairie, off of Causeway.

Legitimately have no idea how I haven't reviewed Lilly's before!

Of pho broths in this city, I do think that Lilly's has my favorite. It has a cinnamon-y fragrance that is rich enough but not overpowering. I also like the accoutrements you get with your to-go order. Whenever I am sick or it's cold outside, Lilly's is my go-to!

It can get pretty packed on the "pho weather" days as I like to call them so I tend to order pick-up then which is pretty fast and efficient. 

Their Vietnamese coffee is no joke. It's delicious and is a great option to power through a sleepy afternoon.

Of the phos, I usually get the Combo but have tried the Spicy Shrimp (does have a kick but not overpowering) as well. I also enjoy the Spring Rolls with strawberries and the nutty sauce that it comes with complements it well!

They are closed right now for a hot second ( maybe renovations?) 'til March so call before heading in to make sure they're open!

I wanted to try a new restaurant spot out, but didn't want to do an all out brunch. Wakin' Bakin' delivers...well yeah, they deliver, but we dined in! 

This is your no fuss breakfast place when you're too lazy to make your own breakfast at home...which is basically every morning for me. 

You order at the counter, and they bring the food to wherever you're sitting, even if you're outside enjoying a beautiful day. Make sure to grab your silverware, napkins, condiments, and bring them to where you're at. The water surprisingly had a fresh cucumber taste to it instead of the usual tap water taste you get when you just order a regular water. Love that!

The boyfriend and I both ordered the Queso Burrito with hashbrowns, bacon and avocado bringing a $5 burrito to about $8.75 with the add-ons; still affordable to me. It comes with a small side of sour cream and salsa (I could always do with more salsa), but when all is said and done, it was just the right amount of food to kick off my morning. 

I didn't see any dishes that necessarily scream New Orleans, or are super fancy, but if you want a breakfast done right, quick, and simple...this is your butter and jam.

Stepping into Brown Butter, you can't help but admire what they've done renovation-wise to this space. Like others have said, you can't even believe you're in this mini-strip of stores because BBSKB is so welcoming with a dark color schemes, lots of wood paneling, and great big wooden tables and booths; perfect for a lunch meeting so you can spread out!

We came for lunch with ample parking (until everyone finds out about this spot!) and ordered the fried pickles, my most favorite fried pickles I've ever had that came in a light buttermilk ranch sauce. SO good, ate them like Gap Girl Cindy. "LAY OFF ME, I'M STARVING!"

My dining buddy ordered the burger and I ordered the Chicken & Waffles with a side of braised greens (trying to be all healthy and what not). I like their take on Chicken and Waffles and the proportion was perfect, though how are we all so bad at reading that it was sourdough and not waffles? The drizzle on the sourdough had a nice sweetness that paired well with the savory, tender chicken. I would suggest a fork and knife if you're on a date 'cause things can get sticky! As for my braised greens, y'all know I'm a carnivore above all else, so I think a person that enjoys greens would enjoy these, consistency-wise they were perfect, not smooshy but not too drained, I just might stick to a second order of those friggin' pickles! YUM! 

The waitstaff was sweet as pie, and was great at checking up on us, and understood that we were meeting at the same time so she let us do our thing. I like that they have the square/iPad to check out on rather than needing to hold onto a paper receipt.

I will absolutely be back to Brown Butter. I think it's a phenomenal non-chain edition to this area of Carrollton!

I've had a solo excursion here at the bar as well as a 5 person nosh sesh, and both times were spot-on! 

Some die-hard tiki interior designer really had their way with this place because it is tiki from head to toe with very little recognizable aspects from when it was Iris. The bar and restaurant are separated by a wall that kinda cuts out some of my people watching ability but probably helps me focus more on the peeps I'm with. They also incorporated a plug and USB plugs in the booths on the restaurant side! Drink/food pics fa' days (but please no flash, thanks).

I was in between engagements one night, and decided to belly up to the bar here. I don't often go to bars by myself, and my phone battery was running on low so I couldn't just scroll through Instagram photos of cute puppies for the next hour. Instead of just staring into my delicious Hawaii 504, Hadi was incredibly kind, and talked with me about the bar's unique mural of different idols around the world and how their uniform is part of the owner's personal collection of Hawaiian shirts. What I like about their drinks is while they come out looking like they took 30 minutes to make, they're incredibly fast at concocting them and the staff will still chat away with you while they do their mixology magic. 

The two drinks I've had thus far are the Hawaii 504* with Chinese five-spice suspended in honey and shaken with Virgin Islands rum, ginger liqueur, lime and orange juices and the Paniolo with Kentucky bourbon and Hawaiian macadamia nut liqueur shaken with lime, our own cranberry syrup and a dash of molé bitters. While The Hawaii 504 may still be my favorite with a light ginger and spice kick, but refreshing like a Pimm's Cup; the Paniolo is a great option for someone who's not into rum but wants to hang with the cool kids. In my opinion it's a sweeter, more drinkable cocktail similar to Bourbon Old Fashioned, but not too sweet. 

The chow party happened the other week with only 45'ish minutes to eat. I usually don't put this kind of pressure on French Quarter restaurants but we were able to enjoy drinks, apps, dinner, more drinks and still make our show! We enjoyed the taro chips and steamed pork and chicken? dumplings for starters.  I don't usually get steamed dumplings, but they were fresh, full, handmade, and soaked up the sauce nicely. Loved the kimchi ketchup and sriracha mayo that came with the chips so much we got them with our steak frites. The steak was cooked perfectly medium rare, and was a good size for my mom and I to split. 

For 5 people, our bill with tip was around $230 with everyone enjoying multiple drinks. I think for the occasion, this was a really fun dinner in a great space with a very knowledgeable and friendly staff. I'd definitely come back with friends to grab drinks and enjoy some of the other dishes or an order of taro chips!

I remember when Dat Dog was just a pup taking cash on Freret in their little store with a few tables outside. The food was great then, and is still great with the expansion to a larger location on Freret and this fairly new one on Magazine. 

**BRAND NERD ALERT** Love it. Love the colors of their buildings and how they tie together. Also love the folksy Simon artwork and drawn chalk boards. 

K, so let's get this confession out of the way. Never was a hot dog person. The idea of processed meat icked me out, but I'd eat a sausage on a bun if I had to. Always was Team Burger, and still am for the most part.

Dat Dog didn't renew my faith in the Dawg, they turned me on to them. And it doesn't hurt that their fries are killer. 

I apologize for the prefacing of this location with so much back story, but I'll get into this location now. The patio, amazing. It' s huge with tons of seating and has access to an extensive outdoor bar that has an opening so bartenders can go back and forth from inside to outside. 

If you don't know how Dat Dog works ordering-wise you might be a little confused. Have no fear! Come to Yelp and we'll make you look like a pro. Go to the back of Dat Dog inside and order from the kitchen. The guys back their aren't peaches & cream but they'll get your order out to you in no time so you're not drooling too much on their tables.   There are specials and the usual menu. We asked what the spiciest dog was and they said their Spiced Sausage. Personally, it's not that spicy, but Tabasco gives you that extra kick. 

It's no Coney Island pricing. If you're loading on toppings you're adding on $ signs, but if you can grasp the concept of a gourmet hot dog and how delicious it truly is, than you'll simmer down. The White Trash fries though came super loaded for an extremely fair price, (I can't recall the exact $, but I was imagining they may have written it down wrong since there was so much going on) 

Apparently they have special nights including trivia. I wish I lived closer, but I think I may make the trek to enjoy some of their activities or the patio when the weather get's warmer. Viva la Dat Dog!

So...After being tortured by Yelpers John L. H. and Kim-Thao H. drool-inducing photos of donuts and sliders and having individuals react like I had just said Justin Timberlake had walked in the door when I mentioned DDSB, I had to make my way over to the District Donuts Sliders Brew, not to be confused with The District ( a bar in the CBD). If you end up at The District, you are going to be sorely disappointed if you're looking for the D,S or the B. 

The first time, I grabbed a sandwich from Stein's next door because it was looking pretty packed seating-wise, but decided I'd get two donuts to go from DDSB. The line goes pretty quickly and I was picked two donuts in Jeopardy Final Round time. What is the Banana Pudding and, I think, the Roselle. There is no proof of the pudding because I inhaled it in traffic driving back home. It was uh-mazing. I mean uh-mazing. I unfortunately thought I'd share the Roselle with my sig. other who didn't eat it and left it at work. Note to self: Never share donuts. Another great thing is, I felt no regret nor belly ache that sometimes follows a donut binge. Well done, District, well done. 

The second time was yesterday, and I got the Donuts, Sliders, AND Brew in! I am going to make it a habit to eat the donut first. Every time. I split a French Toast donut with ma Mere. I ordered the large Mocha, and with two packets of Splenda, it was perfect!  

Note to everyone: do not try to split sliders. We ordered the three specials: Pork Belly, Oyster and Duck 5 Spice. Again, no picture, because we murdered them. We cut them in half and demolished them, scooping up every little piece of slaw and cracklin'. So good. I might've put the tiniest Sriracha on my halves, but really they don't need anything. This was 3pm on a Tuesday and there was no wait or line, FYI. 

 If you're massively hungry, you could end up spending around $20/25 here, maybe. I think the prices are definitely reasonable for the quality and deliciousness that ensues. 

Besides all this, I love the concept. **Brand Nerd Alert** love the graphics and the set up. Tons of seating, bar stool style or booths; only the most favorite of all seating types for loners and groups alike. The booth swallowed me and my mom so you could fit a clown car in a booth. 

Lastly, their donuts seem to change daily. If you want a specific donut, DEFINITELY call ahead and see if it's in so you don't cry a little. IF you are feeling courageous, go in anyway! It's fun to try new things and delicious donuts!!!

This Rouses is delightful! I wish I lived down here, but my sig. other does and I love to make groceries here.

Like it's been indicated: no lines ever, fresher feel than other groceries and, of course, with any Rouses; it's local! This Rouses is unique because it's got a TON of parking, they have huge single beers of all types, an aero phonic herb garden on the roof, a Red Box machine, a mini food court area...

If you already go to Rouses, you'll really love this one. The CBD is a little too quiet of a neighborhood for me, so I really like how bright and lively this Rouses is and tries to bring the community together for events. The view from the roof is quite nice too.

Sometimes I'm feeling massively carnivorous, and I can't quell the meat eater in me until I eat a big juicy burger. If you put a bowl of romaine lettuce in front of me during one of these episodes, I can't be held accountable for the things I will say and do. 

There are a ton more places way closer to me, but Fharmacy is a really good fhix for this werewolf phenomenon that occurs within me. I can't eat in the building because it just wouldn't be pretty for anyone, so I order to-go. 

Everything is packaged neatly and travels well. Let me just start here. If you don't get the boudin balls, you must work at a car crash test facility 'cause you a dummy. They are the best boudin balls in town. Light crispy exterior with the perfect ratio of rice, meat, and seasoning AND it comes with a "can't-get-enough-of/would-likely-drown-in" side sauce that's pretty dang good. My husband asked that I order the balls and I wanted the balls too, and I pondered whether to order 2 orders (6 balls in each order), but these balls are so rich and delicious that 3 balls really is enough for me, or I'd never make it to Dr. Tan...

I don't know who Dr. Tan is or why a burger is named after him but his chart reads "damn delicious" in scribbly doctor handwriting that you can't actually read but be happy that I'm typing this out for you. 

Dr. Tan's buns... Going to be totally honest... I wish my buns looked this good. I almost feel guilty biting into this immaculate bread but I know what's hiding just underneath and that monster inside of me has a strong lack of manners. Grilled jalapenos, grilled onions, house slaw, pepper jack, chipotle aioli, bacon all vie for tastebud attention as bits fly like shrapnel through my fingers.

When they offer napkins, take the napkins. 

There are hints of bahn mi from the slaw, backyard barbecue vibes from from the bacon and grilled onions, and a kick from the jalapenos and pepper jack (but not as strong as you might think, if you're shying away from the massive jalapeno stack). The crispy-fried fries taste like a Rally's fry's distant cousin but bigger. 

Truly the only lone vegetable that won't make me hulk out is their pickle. These pickles are intentional and delicious. Not like the vinegary afterthought of a spear you get thrown in with your deli sandwiches at other places.

The folks are nice and quick to put together my order, and everyone stays safe when I get my burger (and boudin ball) "fhix".

This little Yelper went to market...

I love St Roch. The vendors and the staff are so sweet. The space is always clean. Parking is easy. The food is good! 

Auction House Market is St Roch's super chic sister in the CBD, and she's droppin' it like it is hot.
