If you don't know that Auction House is one sexy b, you're living under a ginormous rock with no wifi. It's beautiful. I want to live here. Just put a couch made of the same material as the bar stool behind the bar, and I'll be good. I promise to water the plants on holidays.

Parking is metered around here but I haven't had any issues with finding a spot. My buddies from Coast Roast are here so I know I'm gonna get a solid cup of Joe and I will slowly but surely work my way through all the vendors.

What I love about this location is how many families were there! Not to be the creeper without the kids, but I have never seen so many families in the CBD. There's hope for you folks with kids! You can go to cool places too! 

Looking forward to trying out more vendors in this lovely space!

I love oysters, and not the skrimpy mini ones that are "more sweet" and are "fuller flavor"...I like me some big ass oysters. You'd think a place like Luke, with its Parisian vibe would be trying to sell me on some babies, but they're not pushing the petites at all. 

You listen to mama Morgan and you go in during Happy Hour, 3-6, errday (last time I checked) and get you some big ass oysters. They don't call them that, cause that's how the businesses in the Quarter try to reel you in, but they are!...They're big and I love them AND they're 50 cents. Yes, 50 cents each, so splurge on a dozen or two. Of course, if you don't like oysters, just take me and I'll help you out. I have been to Luke a few times, and just recently discovered the humongoness of their oysters, only rivaled by Cooter Brown's, thought they may be a little cleaner here at Luke. Can you tell I like oysters?...

I love the vibe at Luke with a long bar that's great for dining at as a couple. If you are a people watcher, then request the front. If you enjoy your privacy, the back is perfect and intimate. I recently sat in the back here with my boyfriend's family. I must say I experienced some serious entree envy (which duh, don't order an appetizer then) when my boyfriend's dad ordered the HUGE burger and fries, and I went with the Crab Maison. I do have qualms with the price tag on this petite Crab Maison when comparing with similar restaurants, and it wasn't as flavorful as I had hoped though the temperature was perfect and the bread that it came with was a nice crunchy texture to go with the meat. Size-wise though this IS an appetizer so be forewarned this is not an entree substitute which of those who got entrees are rightfully sized.  To fill my belly, I ordered a side of their jalapeño grits though it wasn't specifically on the menu (thanks!), and they are damn good. Perfectly creamy with a spicy kick. I will definitely have to try their shrimp and grits some time that they cook with these grits. 

Our waitress was attentive without being overbearing, and handled a neighboring situation of ornery guests very well without missing a beat with us. 

I'll definitely be back for Happy Hour at the bar sometime very soon!

If you know me, you know that I'm a Bloody Mary junkie, a fiend for tomato, vodka, and a heavy hand of pickled veggies...so when I saw that they had a Build Your Own Bloody, I couldn't wait for this spot to open. 

The space is incredibly expansive for a new restaurant with lots of great natural light and various seating. The host station is oddly placed, and the hostess wasn't really corralling people over so take initiative when you get there to put your name down. There was a bit of a wait, but that is to be expected at most places for breakfast. 

We were seated towards the back of the restaurant along the wall. The seating seemed unfinished, like they might be putting down cushioning eventually back here. A plus to the seating back here is that they have plugs and charging outlets for your phone for great photos of your bodacious Bloody Mary. 

Bloody Mary verdict...So it's a gigantic Bloody with lots of eye candy, yes. Base price is $12.50, then any extraneous things (as noted on the sheet) is extra. IF you make a bad Bloody, that's on you. My Bloody was tasty, and gave me a nice little bloody buzz. I really enjoyed the addition of spices and a peppered rim. My gripe is that I think the base price should include more veggies. You max out at 5, and then .20 each after that. A lemon, lime, celery, olive, and green bean ARE a base, and then you're telling me an okra and my fave, the cocktail onion, are extra? Sad face. Most bars in New Orleans will do that, and a slice of bacon for max $9. My Bloody set me back $14 with the addition of okra, onion, bacon and pepper jack cheese though I did get a lagniappe cucumber slice that wasn't marked on my sheet... hmm k. You are getting a big ol' Bloody, but I didn't feel as jazzed about the Build Your Own after I saw the pricing structure. 

After watching a handful of dishes go by while we waited, we decided on going with the cool lookin' Breakfast Tacos and the Shrimp & Tarragon sandwich. Our waitress was very sweet but really not on her A game that day with servicing our table. Another waitress ended up bringing our food out to us. My Shrimp & Tarragon was good. The bread was lightly pressed with the shrimp and bacon well cooked and crisp spring mix. My friend's Breakfast Tacos were not on par, more like a triple bogie. They had definitely been chillaxin in a window for too long. The romaine had wilted and the toppings were sparse. The wonton shell is tasty to pull off and dip in the sour cream but didn't really work for taco-like consumption. The dish all together just wasn't really a winner for us. 

Though I was in good company, I don't think I've spent that much time in a restaurant in a while. Price-wise, I think for what you can get in the city and with a more well-rounded experience, I don't think they're currently very competitive. 

I say three stars because my sandwich was good, my Bloody was tasty, and there are other things on the menu I'd love to try and I think the space is pretty cool. I definitely think if they work on their service, they'll be able to up their game and the quality of what's coming out of the kitchen.

I was familiar with the hype but had never had a firsthand experience prior to the Trader Joe's in Metry. 

Upon arrival, this place was buzzin' like a beehive but with a lot less coordination that I would assume would be present in the production of honey.

Locals, remember your first time shopping in the Children's Museum at their grocery store and knowing what it looked like to grocery shop but really you just ran your buggy into fellow minion shoppers and grabbed willy nilly at things. That's the vibe I get at TJ's. Most these folks are new to TJ's and have no idea what's good since most everything is relabeled Trader Joe's! It's a bit of a mindf*** when you realize how much you're sold on branding and packaging. 

So if you can get passed the discombobulation nation, you can find some pretty great products in stock. But just an FYI, this is not a one stop shop for me, and if I come to terms with that then it's not worth lowering the star rating when that expectation is set off the bat. Some things I've really enjoyed that we've bought is literally any one of their hummus, toasted coconut pancake mix, popcorn, honey, and a few other items that did not last long in our house cause they were demolished by our highest hippo ways. 

Their bread was not my fave. At some of these more healthy spots, the bread tends to mold faster. I'm guessing it's because of less preservatives, but just a fair warning. 

They don't have a deli, so we got our meats at Rouses down the way and a few other things they don't carry. I didn't partake but the wine is uber cheap and there is an article floating around online that grades them all!

The culture is tres hippy meets our current decade with hand drawn advertisements, bells to ring for service needs and other intentional branding that harkens to a simpler time.

I will return. I'm not a fan of discord and folks that take too long to pull the trigger in front of the little hummus fridge area so it might be a while but I do think they have some items worth trekking out to Metry for to have a taste.

I was told when coming to Nashville to try out Nashville-Style Hot Chicken, and this was one of the spots that a lot of folks clucked about. I was forewarned about the line situation. I think to wait in long lines for a singular food item, like hot chicken or cronuts is such an interesting human behavior but as you can see from the majority of the reviews, folks don't have a problem with it. 

A friend and I had just eaten breakfast and decided to mosey over and be first in line before they opened up. As we waited the line grew and grew 'til it snaked around the side of the patio and down the block. While we had scoped out the menu and had an idea of what we wanted to eat, no one prepares you for the pressure of being first in line (of nearly 50 people by the time they opened their doors). Risa did it right. If you have any issues with "order fright" as I like to refer to it as, order to-go and two-step passed the line. 

Walking up to the counter once the doors swung open, I saw Chicken & Waffles, and was like, "oo, can I get that?!" Chicken & Waffles is only on Sunday, folks. After fumbling a bit, I ordered a Small Dark Hot! with potato salad and cole slaw. My friend who was equally flustered ordered Chicken Tenders Southern-style, and tripped up over ordering her sides, and asked the cashier to just pick the two best sides. The cashier wasn't really looking to help out my buddy, and yes there was a line behind us waiting for us to complete our order. We got her sides in, paid, and...we didn't get a ticket or anything, so we kind of felt like chickens in a coop just standing around. It definitely is an order, grab, go-type spot with little staff interaction from what I can tell. That being said, it's efficient and the folks were pleasant that put together our order. 

Maybe eating on their patio is the way to go (it gets a bit claustrophobic/packed and the cooking aromas are quite strong inside). This way your chicken is still hot, you can order a beer to drink with your chicken which I'm sure is delightful, and maybe really experience Hattie B's. We took ours to go. The chicken was well-cooked, the heat level was tolerable and good, but I wasn't blown away. The sides were also good, but not anything to shake my tail feathers at. 

I know a three-star review isn't the majority here, so take the suggestions of ordering to-go (but still eating on their patio) with a cold beer to enjoy your hot (hot) chicken and other suggestions brought on by five-star reviews, and you'll probably really enjoy your experience! I am no Nashville Hot Chicken connoisseur but if I do return I'd like to try them out again along with other NHC high standard spots.

Very happy to have had the opportunity to try out Compere Lapin with a group since I was able to try a handful of appetizers as well as their delicious entrees. 

The space is pretty large compared to new restaurants, but still feels intimate at your table. I can see that they've incorporated some sound proofing elements since their opening and it helps to be able to hear the folks at your table. I love that James Michalopoulos' work adorns the walls, and it's mostly some of his lesser known work including landscapes that he did while vacationing in France. It all fits very well in the space. 

We were seated at a wide table making it easier for us all to share/see one another's dishes and great lighting (how'd they know we were going to be those pic-snapping guests? ;) ). 

The menu is broken down by Small Bites, First, Second, and Extras. I love that this restaurant doesn't cater to the traveler's need for "authentic New Orleans cuisine". It genuinely feels like 100% what the Chef wants on the menu. I also love that it's pseudo-Caribbean without succumbing to the tiki theme. Everything I ordered or enjoyed a bite of was wonderful.  

Dishes - 
Cold Smoked Tuna Tartare/Avocado/Crispy Bananas $14

Great starter dish. Light and fresh with no fishy smells. You can appreciate the tuna's natural flavors without being overpowered by seasoning or lime juice. If you need texture, the banana chips add a great crunch. Be selfish and order this one for yourself if you really enjoy tuna. 

Brussels Sprouts/Buttermilk/Crispy Chicken Skin $13

I really have to stop saying I hate Brussels sprouts. I've managed to enjoy Brussels sprouts at a few places around town including 1000 Figs and Brown Butter. The sprouts at Compere Lapin may take the cake. I think the winning factor is the crispness. Nothing mushy or sour about these morsels of heavenly goodness, and again...maybe just order these for yourself if you're feeling exceptionally greedy. 

Caribbean Seafood Pepper Pot $21

I ordered this as my entree. This dish falls under the First section so it's not going to be as large as a dish in the Second section but I wouldn't have had my entree any other way. First off, the dish is beautiful. After a short photo shoot of bright greens from the fresh dill and basil, hues of pink from various seafood and the watermelon radish, and the orange of the broth that bathed all this deliciousness, I dove in. I really can't tell you what spices were mixed into the broth, nor can I identify every type of seafood in this pot of heaven. It wasn't overly spicy and the broth didn't cloak the flavors of the seafood.

My best way to describe this dish is that it transported me to an open air restaurant atop an island overlooking the ocean watching the sunset with a cool breeze passing through. 

Duo of Beef/Cauliflower/Foie Gras $32

While I was experiencing nirvana with the Pepper Pot, I did do a bite barter with my neighbor who was enjoying the duo of beef. He was kind enough to let me enjoy both meat options that were perfectly cooked, melt-in-your-mouth delicious. 

I will absolutely be back, and will venture into the Second menu section for a taste of this Curried Goat that is wildly popular in other reviews.

So excited about all the Gracious Bakeries popping up all over the city. While the love of my life has the sweetest of tooths, I love me some savory pastries and Gracious is packin' heat. The first time I visited this location they had some bacon carb-y deliciousness that had the bacon all sorts of baked in. It was like a bountiful easter egg hunt for bacon pieces hidden in the layers of flaky dough. The next time I enjoyed some other form of savory goodness since "Hidden Bacon Treasures" wasn't made that day. I like that they mix it up. I've also ordered lunch there, and sweet baby Jesus, the bread does make a difference. I had the Smoked Turkey, and I was awkwardly "mmm"ing over it...but what's great is this location doesn't get really packed so I didn't feel THAT awkward. 

If you're looking for a new spot to get some work done, check 'em out and don't mind me "mmmmm"ing over here.

Writing this review, I'm already dreaming of my return to Blue Oak BBQ...

This space needed a revamp, and I love how Blue Oak BBQ set up in this space and made it their own. Counter service with a line that doesn't get in the way of diners, plenty of seating inside and out, and a cute little bar. There are whole paper towel rolls on each table for messy eaters like myself and huge bottles of various barbecue sauces to try. Parking in their lot might be non-existent during busy hours but you can probably find a spot on the street. 

Their staff moves the line as quickly as possible which for me was enough time to pick the Pit Viper* and an order of Smoked Buffalo Inferno wings (8 for $9). One side comes with the Pit Viper and because it comes topped with Ginger Sesame Slaw, the cashier suggested I try another side so I ordered the Roasted Garlic Mac N' Cheese. My main man ordered the famed Brisket Plate ($13) with a side of the Mac N' Cheese and a special side of Watermelon Salad. Since there was a bar and it WAS a Saturday, I asked if they had a Bloody Mary. The bartender let me try their mix before making the drink, which I really appreciate, and promptly ordered one up for $6!

While it didn't take long for our food to come out, we're already PRETTY sure what we want next time after seeing the plate of nachos pass by. We jumped on our wings first, all meaty with a nice crisp to the skin. While these are their hottest wings, by no means are they painfully hot unless this was just a day they were a little bit more tame than usual. Don't worry, I'll definitely be trying them again. I want to say their ranch dressing is homemade and doesn't overly coat the meat like some ranch dressings do. 

My sandwich was a softball of moist jerk pulled pork with a smidge of the slaw and some big ol' chunks of fresh jalapeno buried in the meat sandwiched in a seedy bun. The Pit Viper lives up to its name, in fact, I feel like kind of a weenie because after the first bite, I had to pick off the jalapenos. This sandwich brings the heat, so faint of taste buds, beware. I greatly appreciated the self-serve water at this point. I do wish there had been more slaw to add more dimension to the meat and heat, but their slogan IS "Vegan-Free since 2012." The Mac N' Cheese is delightfully creamy with a tasty layer of crumbs on top. The side portion for the Pit Viper was a little bigger than my boyfriend's sides for the Brisket Plate so I shared after he demolished his cheesy goodness. I did get a juicy bite of his brisket, and you don't need teef to eat this beef. I'll definitely need to try more on my next visit. The only recommendation we had for the Brisket Plate was to change up the white slice of bread to more of a Texas Toast, but this piece of bread was my savior when trying to quell my jalapeno fire so maybe that's why it's plain. 

I know I'll be back this way to try other things on the menu, and I think the owners of Blue Oak did a great job setting up shop at this spot! 

*Pit Viper - Jerk Pulled Pork, Ginger Sesame Slaw, Jalapeno, on a Laurel St. Bakery Bun.

Highly recommend this warm and inviting breakfast spot. They utilize NoWait on the Yelp app! 

We decided to pop on over here for breakfast. The space is cute with a variety of seating options. We were seated in one of their nice sized booths.

The menu looks great with a lot of very homey dishes. I ordered the Avocado Toast and Breakfast Fried Rice. 

No skimping on fresh avocado and feta and a wedge of lime for a nice splash of acidity on the Toast. 

The bowl of Fried Breakfast Rice was way more than I was expecting and would be great to share with a table. I dabbed some Cholula for a kick but loved the variety of flavors from the chunks of sausage, light bits of egg, and fresh cilantro. It wasn't like Chinese fried rice that has an overpowering smell that sticks with you throughout the day which I really loved about it. I actually had to take it to go and finished it up later in the day. 

I also had the Bloody Mary that was good. I had to try the fried pickle which felt more novelty but liked the type of pickle they use! I wish it had been a little colder but still a tasty Bloody Mary! 

Our waitress was wonderful with a lovely smile. While the restaurant filled up around us, she seemed calm as a cucumber. She was attentive without hovering and accommodated our table's wants and needs with ease.

The din of the restaurant is perfect for bringing little ones since it's not too quiet and can handle a wee one's jubilations ;)

I would 100% come back to this great little spot when passing through town again!

I was able to visit this lovely space on a Saturday for brunch before the Irish Parade on Magazine Street. Brunch hours are Saturday and Sunday 10am to 3pm. 

It was a little wet that day or else we may have eaten on the patio, but the interior dining area is really lovely. I felt a tad underdressed in my green tank top and rain jacket, so maybe class it up a little if you make a reservation. I love the deep greens and blues, a beautiful bar that begs to bellied up to, and there is a ton of natural light for wonderfully-lit food pics. 

We easily made our reservation on the website, and were called the day before to confirm. They put us in one of their comfortable booths and our waiter was attentive and amicable during our meal. 

I am a Bloody Mary junkie, so of course I wanted to try the Bourbon Bloody Mary*. I like Bourbon and I like the components of a Bloody Mary, but I think in the case of this cocktail, I'd prefer it to be vodka but that's not saying it wasn't a good cocktail. I think I just would rather not taste the liquor when it comes to a Bloody Mary though I prefer to taste my bourbon and whiskey in any other type of cocktail and most times straight/on the rocks...If that makes sense. 

We ordered the shrimp toast* with celery and ginger aioli. The presentation was really nice though our toast was a little on the burnt side, which surprisingly complemented the creaminess of the slaw-like mixture on top. I think the dish could be even more delicious with less aioli with more of the flavors coming through, but I really enjoyed the texture of this brunch appetizer. 

The stand-out dish for me was the crispy grit cake* with pulled pork, Brussel sprout leaves and sauce mornay. The layered flavors and textures were on point from the incredibly flavorful crisp of the leaves, creamy richness of the sauce, perfectly seasoned pulled pork and the surprisingly light grit cake. I split this dish with my boyfriend along with a side of bacon. 

After this brunch I didn't feel overly stuffed, and was ready to take on the Irish Parade! If you're looking for a deal, they offer a $24 prix-fixe menu (that includes the tasty grit cake) with a cocktail! I'm looking forward to returning to take advantage of their patio space and whiskey menu!

*Crispy Grits Pulled Pork, Brussels Sprout Leaves, and Sauce Mornay 14
*Bourbon Bloody Mary Fresh Horseradish, Spicy Pickled Green Beans 9
*Shrimp Toast Celery and Ginger Aioli 14

I'm really glad this pizza joint has been able to grow into its own space across the street from Banks St. Bar where I first enjoyed it during Spaghetti Western night.  My first visit to the new location was on a slow Sunday night. We ordered a Caesar and a Margherita, and sat outside with friends when the weather was still pleasant. The Caesar came out immediately, and was a really great serving size for the $6.50 price tag. Definitely shareable for up to three people IMO, but I pretty much ate it all by myself...I also enjoyed a bit of my friend's caprese salad ($6.99) that was also a nice shareable size for the four of us at the table. 

By no means am I a pizza aficionado, but as you can tell from the pictures their pizza is New York-style. The toppings were evenly distributed with a good bit of shredded fresh basil, tomatoes and nicely melted chunks of buffalo mozzarella. The toppings held fast to the thin dough underneath, and the crust, while thin, is pleasantly crispy and will disappear from your plate as you finish what you started with each slice. A friend said they brush it with 7up or Sprite? Wives Tale? You tell me. 

I've noticed on social media, they have a pretty serious slice of the day game between Monday and Friday, so I'm thinking I need to get on that!

It's been almost two years since my initial review, and I definitely want to add a star! A group of gals pals and I recently went for my birthday giving me a great opportunity to revisit and enjoy some of the dishes again.

We started out with pineapple-cilantro margaritas and added jalapeno. It was the perfect level of heat and tang. No faux sour mix flavors here! 

The ceviche is still $12 but they've bumped it up a notch. I still think that there isn't really an Ecuadorian-style ceviche in New Orleans on par with what Robert's family makes, but I will just have to come to terms with that. 

The friends had a food porn perfect serving of the corn (see picture), and for my meal I had the Chori-Arepa*. Delicious green flavors, perfectly grilled sausage and just the right amount of cheese in a hearty cornmeal pita-type casing. The arepa are obviously where it's at and worth every penny. They're hearty and packed with great flavor. Throw a couple of the plantain chips in their for a little crunch. 

It was pretty busy, but the service was doing pretty well to keep up while we were there. I do want to go back and try some other dishes on the menu in lieu of the ceviche since an app and the arepa is really enough food for one person, IMO. 

Chor-Arepa - Grilled chorizo, avocado purée, Aji & melted mozzarella.

An extensive bar with a huge selection of liquors and wines as well as a great kitchen!

This was my first time sitting down to eat at Delachaise. It's usually so packed on the weekends, and so I've just grabbed a cocktail or glass of wine and some of their goose fat fries to enjoy, usually on the small patio and listen as the streetcars rattle by every once in a while. 

This day, the weather wasn't so great, and the crowd was lighter, though still a good bit of people in there. We were lucky enough to score an inside spot in the front curved area. This place resembles the shape of a streetcar in it's design, kinda cool right there on St. Charles. 

I love eating out with Joi because she sneaks veggies into my diet. This time she did it through the grilled eggplant cannolis and their cup of assorted olives. I don't even like olives, and I was going to town on these.  I think I ate all the caperberries (taste like giant capers). The eggplant was canoodling with chevre and ricotta. I was only going to have a bite, but somehow a whole cannoli made its way into the depths of my belly. I love that it was grilled and not fried. Go Joi!

We also had an assorted cheese plate that the waiter was extremely, and I'm talking EXTREMELY well educated on. I most enjoyed the cave-aged cheese. No idea what it was called so I failed Cheese 101 but not for lack of a good teacher. 

We also shared the mussels, which I ate 75 percent of between 4 people. I'm going to say it...Best in Town, and it kills me because there is another place that is a close second. But it's their unique use of ginger (I think) that gives it a floral "spicy" kick that is sometimes lacking in mussels. And they give you ample bread and fries to dip into the delicious goodness. Thank God I didn't have a straw. 

My only gripe is that there isn't any table service. You do have to order from the bar, and though the staff is very attentive, I still wish they were able to provide ordering from tables. Also, mini word of advice, there are a few people around the area that ask for money outside (totally unassociated with the restaurant) just to let you know. But, occasionally, there is a saxophone player (also unassociated with the restaurant) but not too shabby if you want to throw him a bone.

There is a difference between making plans and making reservations, and while I naively had my fingers crossed that Tito's had yet to be discovered...My fiance and I along with another couple walked into a packed house. No problem, they made us a reservation from an hour from the time we had arrived so we just went down the street and had a drink. Lesson learned, make reservations! 

We were seated promptly when we arrived, and our server was amazing! There when we needed him and knowledgeable about the menu. He dropped the amuse bouche of cancha and an aji limo (I think) that we could've drank it was so good. Most of us had never had Pisco, so he brought out a sampling for the table of which we ordered refreshing Pisco cocktails because "When in a Peruvian restaurant!..."

I'm just going to start by saying we all wanted to sample a lot of things, but I would say four folks sampling from the Ceviches, Tiraditos, Appetizers and Salad menu is a stretch if you really want to get your share of each dish. They're priced fairly for their portions, but they're better to be split between two people, in my opinion. 

So we ate a lot, but this isn't the type of meal that makes you feel like you need to be wheelbarrowed out and get a good belly-rub because you're 5 months pregnant with a food baby named Regret. We ordered one ceviche (maybe two but we were a bit ravenous), I think we had two tiradito though one isn't pictured (it was a tuna massacre y'all), two appetizers, a salad, and from the platos del mar menu.

All the food came out very quickly. Again, props to this amazing staff that have been open for less than a month. You all are killing it. The Ceviche Criollo was refreshing and light, without the acidity that is sometimes expected from ceviches. I think the leche de tigre helps to balance that out, and I've realized in the last couple of months I love sweet potatoes with literally everything. 

The tiradito (raw fish) dishes are the Peruvian versions of sashimi or crudo or carpaccio. Don't expect these to be filler dishes. They're light with very clean flavors. It's a type of dish that makes you feel like you should be on a beach deck and these ingredients just so happen to be ones you found after you went fishing that day. The Nikkei was clean with the complementing flavors bringing out the inherent tastes of good tuna without being overpowering. No fishiness at all. You can't go wrong with pairing flavors like mango or passion fruit with salmon, so the Maracuya was pleasant without being too sweet. The pricing is on par with other restaurants, but if you're looking for more filling appetizer, maybe pass over the Tiraditos and find your way into the stunners that were their Appetizers. 

Vegetarians if you're still reading, maybe even you Pescatarians, look away. I discovered while judging dishes with NOWFE, I really enjoyed the dish Anticuchos de Corazon, and they nail it here. This is the point when I came out of my "sharing is caring" coma, and remembered how much I hate sharing dishes that I really really like (Tom and Michelle if you're reading this, I love y'all, promise). I used to make that face you see on old horror comics that the woman makes when she sees a werewolf or a zombie whenever I saw octopus dishes. I still can't handle seeing the little suckers on the tentacles (can't, can't think about it) BUT their Pulpo Anticuchero is worth fighting my fears. Packed with flavor and so dang tasty. The potatoes were also cooked perfectly. And that chimichurri...*insert thumbs up emoji*

We also ordered the Ensalada Verde. Have you ever seen a play and there is that person in the play that does literally nothing but they're doing it really well, and it's hard to notice them because EVERYONE is freakin' killin' in this Broadway production?! That's the Ensalada Verde. 

Lastly, we ordered the Jalea Real de Mariscos. The two pseudo Latin Americans at our table were head over heels for this dish. I don't order fried seafood often, but (in The Most Interesting Man In The World Voice) when I do, it's Jalea Real de Mariscos. You could tell the seafood was fresh and still moist beneath the light batter. I lerv me some yucca fries, but of all the homemade sauces, I wasn't in love with the spicy aioli that came with this dish. A bit too mayonnaise-y and not enough kick for me. That being said, I'm sure they would've brought something else out if I had requested! 

All in all, I will 100% be back, but probably just the two of us, and will make reservations!!!

While I get to see the new restaurants pop up on here from my fellow Yelpers, it was lovely that a friend of mine chose this spot for our Friday din! 

The location is in a converted church so vampires, beware! All kidding aside, it's very inside is very lovely with a long bar, a handful of communal dining tables and even a little sitting area. Their menu resembles a church program, but other than that, they're not overly themed which I think is great. 

No reservation, no problem (though I bet things change when they really start getting the word out). We were sat at the communal table across from each other. If you're not a huuuuge fan of the communal table aspect, they do have other options. Surprisingly, it never got that loud in the space, even when they were filling up so you can still chat it up with your friend across the table. 

The staff was uber pleasant, but not overly so, from the host stand to the server to the manager touching tables. 

Now for the important part. New Orleans is really catching on to this whole small plate scene which I love, and Vessel does a wonderful job. Here are the dishes we had, and how I felt about them:

House Pickles - 5 choices for $9
Lerv pickles!! This is ALL the veggies you can get. I'm not even a big beets person, and the beets were one of my favorite, as was the kimchi! They don't give you crackers with your pickles but I'm okay with it. 

Smoked Gulf Fish Dip with Lavash Crackers - $7
Not overly smoky and a great flavor, and worth the $7, easy. Lots of crackers so you don't have to ask for more. 

Gulf Red Snapper Crudo, Watermelon Sorbet, Pickled Rind, Basil Pimm's Fizz -  $13
This dish was pretty, and well constructed but it wasn't my favorite. This crudo is definitely a sweeter version, more sashimi'ish (sorry if this doesn't make sense) than I'm used to enjoying. 

House Ricotta Stuffed Caramelle Pasta, Charred Corn, Summer Squash, Black Truffle - $15
Holy delicious, batman!!! The aromas coming off this plate were amazing. The pastas were adorably-wrapped with pockets of rich ricotta shiny with black truffle oil. Everything about this dish made me happy. The hardest one to share but totally shareable. 

Two Run Farms Ground Lamb, Bell Pepper, Crushed Tomato, Red Onion, Parsley - $11
No-skimp city! Their flatbread is piled with lamb. Turn away, vegans, turn away! Favorite part of this dish...the adorable parsley sprouts PACKED with herb-y awesomeness.

Lastly...promise, almost done. While I was blasphemous enough to try to order a Bloody Mary (which they don't have JUST yet), I did get a perfect Old Fashioned (or two). Bars like Vessel are spoiling me with their giant spheres of ice to keep my libation perfectly chilled. Apparently, they have 16 different glasses so that each drink has its own special vessel. See what they did there?!

With all those plates and two drinks each, we both paid around $60 (that includes tip) and well worth the experience! I'll definitely be back!

If you try to order to-go here, you're not going to make it home to eat it...

You'll place your order and shimmy onto a barstool to wait for your pulled pork on a bun topped with slaw and a side of potato salad... 

You'll see that there's a pretty tasty drink special, this time around it was the aptly-titled "Cat Whiskers" with Cathead's delectable honeysuckle vodka. You'll sip on your refreshing sweet/sour cocktail that tastes like the last rays of summer before Fall, then that's when it happens. Remember watching cartoons where the main character is napping and the scintillating smells of a forbidden dish waft under their unsuspecting nose, rustling them from their slumber and tantalizing them with a come hither movement only cartoon aromas can master?...That's what happens.

You're so overtaken by the smell of barbecue, that you yearn for the next meat-ladden styrofoam container to have your name on it. You distract yourself by reading all the funny pig-related signs that cover the walls, still using your peripherals to eye the kitchen. 

Your order comes out with not much of a wait, and you tell yourself, "I'm just going to eat my potato salad since I still have to finish my Cat Whiskers..."

This homemade potato salad uses red potatoes and Creole mustard to set it apart from other potato salads, and has no resemblance whatsoever to the yellow glob that tries to pass itself off as potato salad elsewheres. 

So I've licked my potato salad clean, but by now I've ordered an LA-31 Biere Pale, and they basically make this beer to go with the rich flavors of barbecue and Southern dishes. It's more bitter than usual pale ales, but if you're into malty light beers, I think this is a really good choice. 

They hook you up with two different types of barbecue sauces, and one is really vinegar heavy. I'm obsessed with heavy vinegar flavors so I liked this one best. There barbecue isn't already spicy so this is good to let you gauge how spicy you'd like it to get. 

While I did eat by my lonesome, the bartender was very attentive and the other to-go orderers were pretty entertaining. I love the design of the inside. I had gone to their former location a handful of times, and love the space of this new locale with a much bigger patio than before. I would definitely go back by myself or with a crew, but like I said, you'll have to really discipline yourself not to gobble up all your food on-site.

Great seafood, untouched by a fry batter,  in New Orleans usually isn't cheap. Enter Basin. I will preface my review by saying a friend is part owner, but he knows I don't like him much anyway, so I'll be honest here and not flatter them too too much. ;)

If a friend's in town with an expense account or no budget and want's to treat you to a New Orleans seafood dinner, this is your jam. Go all out with signature cocktails, apps, and entrees for the full experience. As an entree, I've had Kay Kay's BBQ Shrimp, not a first date meal since it's head-on, but the right amount of spice for this spicy lady. 

If you're looking to maximize your budget, do this (what I did this past Monday). Head in on a Monday for .50 cent oysters. They're small, but sweeter and so so clean for those OCD about big ole oysters that got a lil' lagniappe gook on 'em. I like bigger oysters, but I feel like the majority of the world would prefer the size we were served. BTdubs, I may have taken a shell home. Berto and I ordered a dozen each, and they gave us a few extra per the size, I'm guessing. 

I also ordered their Bloody Mary, 'cause that's what I do, right? At this time, it's the best Bloody Mary I've had in town. Why, you ask? The garnish. Y'all...Y'all...I don't know how they pickle, but they pickled baby corns, and they are soo damn good. I could've eaten a jar of JUST the pickled baby corns. I asked for the secret. Obvi, they wouldn't tell me. This is my thing: If it's a damn good Bloody Mary, one should be enough, and it was. It was soo soo good with a nice kick, amazing homemade base, and again, the garnish, woo. The bartender that made it has short blonde hair, and I only want her to make me drinks ever, unless her Bloody Mary masterpiece can be replicated...I'll let you know. 

There was a margarita on the menu, but Berto asked them to mix it up and make a Satsuma Marg. He had two, while also enjoying complimentary satsumas that had been by the door. I'm not big on tequila, but they were the right amount of sweetness with a nice salt rim to even it out. 

We followed up our oysters with small plates. Robert had the Duck Poppers, and I had the Tuna Tartare (Watermelon / Cucumber / Grapefruit vinaigrette / Avocado / Chips). I didn't have any of Berto's Poppers but they looked like little bacon-wrapped bits of deliciousness. Mine was very fresh tasting (sorry no pic cause I dug right in). I think the chips are homemade, very similar to Zapp's, adding a hint of saltiness to the very mild combo. I could've added salt, but I also still had my Bloody to sip on. 

I didn't need to loosen my belt for any extra LBs put on during the meal, but my wallet wasn't totally emptied either. We sat at the bar, and really enjoyed catching some Monday Night Football before hitting the town. One thing I hate is trying to go out on a full belly too. 

We sat at the bar, but there are high tables near the window and a couple 4 and 6 tops farther back from the window. I'd say if you're bringing in a big group, call ahead and if there is a wait, grab a drink down the street or enjoy a drink at the bar if there is room. 

Also, they've already had TWO CRAWFISH BOILS this year! Not sure of how good they are, but will update you as soon as I get my claws on them.

I haven't been to Cane & Table since my 2013 review, and we ended up popping in there post Easter festivities yesterday. We filled up half the bar with half of us already flailing two sheets to the wind. The dimly lit ambiance inside to escape the evening drizzle and fading beautiful weather was just what the afternoon ordered. 

My amigos had enjoyed mai tais in these incredibly amazing Killer Whale tiki cups (I may be buying them offline this week) with copious amounts of fresh mint. Happy Hour (on a Sunday, wahoo) had just kicked in (3-6, 7 days a week), and David, our bartender couldn't have been more patient with our krewe. 

I enjoyed a Manhattan cocktail off the Happy Hour menu, while my friend sipped an orange-y/ raspberry gin cocktail (very tasty, and I'm not a big gin gal). I decided to get off the hard liquor, and enjoy a Tecate Michelada-style with a lime and salt rim. (One of the few places in town that knows what a Michelada is, yay!). My gal pal turned her interest to the main menu with a Smoak & Plank made with Mezcal, Caribbean spices, and "Cherry Bounce."

This is where David comes into play. We're like, "what's Cherry Bounce?!" thinking maybe Big Freedia or Nicky Da B had some influence on this libation. We were dead wrong...Apparently Cherry Bounce is a "colonial-style" infusion of cherry, sugar, and spirit (in this case, rum) and the name dates back to ol' Martha Washington's day when she wrote down a recipe on the president's stationary. Who knew Martha kicked back somer serious cocktails! We thought David was pulling our leg, so we Googled, and he was telling the God's honest truth. Way to know your stuff, David. 

To quell the inevitable hangover, we dined on a pu pu platter that came in an uber-cool wooden Lazy Susan. They were plum out of fried avocado, and subbed in fritters, but I think the avocado was definitely missed. My favorite part of the platter was the cracklin' that you dipped in maple syrup! I'm not even a big fan of cracklin' but dipped in the syrup made it all worth while. 

Thank you David for putting up with us, and I will definitely be back sooner than later for what sounds like a great brunch! Hello, bottomless cocktails!

While parking will forever be a bitch for this bitchin' spot, I doth love The Rusty Nail. This is in my top 5 of places to go grab a drink with one friend or fifty. 

There isn't much change from my previous review, the extra star is just for the consistently stellar service and good times I've had since my former review. They've since expanded their patio space for popular games, and I've had some truly memorable and not so memorable ('cause I actually can't remember) times at Rusty Nail including petting a pot-bellied pig named  Lily Munster that likes beer; hanging out with Woody Harrelson and his fam (did he know he was hanging out with me? possibly not); and eating some amazing crawfish that happened to be free at the moment of said consumption. 

I can't guarantee an amazing time for everyone, but I've yet to have a bad night at Rusty Nail. Again, be careful where you park, grab yourself some food from the food truck, and enjoy a Moscow Mule on the patio. I'll probably be there, so don't be a stranger!

Whilst playing tourist with Katie D, we headed over to Cafe Beignet to do a "sweet" photo shoot with an order of beignets. The space looks to be the old stables of the police station building. I like the palm leaves on the ceiling and the cute brass rings on the tables. They also have a courtyard if you'd like to sit outside. 

There was no line for our sugary concoctions, and ordering was quick. Wait at the counter for your drinks but your food will come to you. The beignets were beignet-y; fluffy, airy and perfectly covered in powdered sugar. 

They sell a bunch of locally-made products and all the staff was pleasant. I know this is more of a tourist spot, but I would 100% grab an iced mocha from here again. I'd also suggest them over spots with lines for the same product ( per my no-waiting-in-lines-for-a-specific-food rule ).

"Babe, can we go get *insert chain ice cream store*"
"No...but we CAAAAANN go try Sweet Handkraft!"

My ice cream-obsessed husband wanted to satiate his sweet tooth and after seeing all the pretty pretty pictures on Yelp, I wanted to bring him here. 

Everything in here is so cute and picture perfect. I had to get the bubble cone since I've always secretly loved the cone more than the ice cream. I got a scoop of the Honey Lavender and two 6 packs of macarons for Mother's Day, one for my mother-in-law and one to send to my mom in Iowa. Unfortunately the macaron boxes are a touch too big for the half dozen and I should've put some padding in there 'cause they showed up in crumbles to my mom, though she says they still tasted good. Just a note that they're delicate! 

Shelby nails it in her review. The ice cream is delicately flavored and creamy. LOVE the bubble cone though know it's made-to-order so it's going to take a second. #worthit

They also had a handful of other very delectable looking bites that I'm sure to return for and I love a good flight of anything so I'll definitely try their ice cream flight!

Y'all, I've been lucky in this life and have yet to meet a crepe I didn't like. I've had some saltier ones in my life, but I love the marriage of sweet and savory that is the crepe (and I think I was a French dancer at Moulin Rouge in a past life so I had no time for anything but crepes in my life). 

Enter Merchant. I've been here many a time, and it has never let me down. The store is always really clean and bright. Sometimes there's a line but it moves very quickly. The staff is very pleasant and your fare comes out in no time. 

This time I bellied up to the bar to wait for my order. They have various seating options but if you're solo, get your tush on one of their red cushiony bar stools. They're so damn comfy, y'all. I ordered to go and my crepe came out in one of those plastic containers that keeps your food in pristine shape and doesn't smoosh everything together which makes me a very happy crepe escapist. 

I had ordered a mocha and the prosciutto, tomato, fontina, balsamic, onion, basil, and truffle butter crepe, and they don't play y'all. Tons of prosciutto is jam packed in this lovely crepe. The sweetness of the balsamic and basil balance out the saltiness of the prosciutto. They don't over cheese which I appreciate 'cause I love cheese but it can sometimes mask the flavor of everything else, and they keep the onions at bay so I'm not offending my breakfast buddies. 

I once had a meeting in their space right outside the restaurant that felt a bit awkward because it feels like it's in a hallway, but that's not enough at all to drop a star for me. I know when I'm in the area, I can get some fresh fare, a tasty mocha, and hang out for a tic if need be on their perfectly worn-in bar stools.

No, I don't work in the CBD, but somedays I yearn to clutch my briefcase and walk with a purpose down Poydras...Today, whilst wearing my tennis shoes and Dirty Coast "Do Watcha Wanna" shirt, I got to catch a glimpse into the #CBDlife with lunch down at City Greens. 

City Greens don't play...Eating salads shouldn't feel like eating rabbit food. City Greens does a good job at shaking up a bold flavored salad, my favorite being their Farm Fresh Greek with fresh crunchy cucumbers, light shaved onions, kalamata olives, tomatoes, roasted peppers, parsley, sheep's milk feta, bibb lettuce; tossed in a greek yogurt ranch dressing. I would say pack some gum before heading back to the board room since these robust flavors can cause some robust breath. 

The space is smaller than the Elmwood location, but there is also some seating outside. It was 12:45 but still a bit of a line around this time that took about 15 minutes (just an FYI).  The staff were a little rushed, but there was a really nice employee who seemed to know his regulars and greeted them, bringing that laid back love to lunch hour...and delicious bread...I figure since I went heavy on the dressing, some bread wouldn't hurt to soak up all the yum yum. 

They had ma' fave San Pellegrino Blood Orange soda, other bevs, and their array of fresh made juices. Next time maybe I'll rock the power suit, but I can definitely say this is a great healthier option for people in this area to get their lunch bunch on at.

Fast food joints, ya best hold onto ya greasy spatulas, 'cause fast and fresh AND local is gaining a foothold in your precious Elmwood, mwa ha ha. 

This trifecta has the added lagniappes of being damn tasty and ecofriendly, so maybe it's "pentagood"? 

I was on my way to a neighboring business for a salad but chose to pop into this newly minted City Greens locale. My first impression was Subway with salads, this lasted but mere seconds. Very clean with compost and recycle trash receptacles with explanations for people who don't know what goes where (I might've been there for a second...) Full bins of fresh greens and a ridiculous array of toppings that you can ooh and ahh at. 

I ordered the Farm Fresh Greek salad with medium dressing of which is Greek yogurt ranch. Cucumber, kalamata olives, tomato, roasted peppers, shaved onion, parsley, sheep's milk feta, and Bibb lettuce. A great mix of ingredients that I inhaled. The cheese didn't overpower the other ingredients and medium dressing was the perfect amount for me. They take the time to mix it before putting it in a bowl you can save for later if you don't finish. I could've gone lighter on the olives and heavier on the cucumber due to a later work meeting. FYI, no amount of Icebreakers mints will rid your breath of olives. Just sayin'.

I also scooped up a What-A-Melon juice with lemon, watermelon, pineapple and volcano salt. You had me at volcano salt and I don't even know why... It was the perfect amount of sweet with a hint of spice. I'm not a juicer by any means, so take my op for someone that thinks a tasty juice would be even better with vodka or rum. 

My total came out to nearly $20 which surprised me a little. The juice was the same price as my salad...but I'd totally do this combo again. Worth it to me. 

There are a tons of puns about lettuce everywhere and if you know me, you know I love puns so it's the healthy yogurt icing on a City Greens wrap...which I will try on the next go round.

When Breakfast and Brunch are two very, very, very different things. This review is for Breakfast, not Brunch. Breakfast on a Friday to be exact. 

It sounds like they kill it for Brunch. Music. Bloody Mary Bar. A Lively Brunch-y Scene. I picked this spot because it was within walking distance, the pictures on here looked drool-inducing, and I mistakenly thought the Bloody Mary Bar would be in existence (or at least the Bloody Marys from the bar would be good). 

We arrived to a gaggle of waiters. I saw a chalked sign that said, "Try Our Bloody Mary Bar." I get excited about Bloody Mary Bars like a kid does about going to Disney World. But this is where they set it up for Brunch...not Friday Breakfast. OK, I'll just order one from the bar...totally okay. But there seemed to be a bit of confusion with the waiters, and then finally one of them sat us in the bar area where it looked like folks were enjoying their early morning drinks...not necessarily brunch-style though. More just like...I'm in a bar drinking...Still okay...

Our waiter. He didn't want to be there. It was brutally obvious. As I'm all about that Yelp life, I asked if the Fried Pickle check-in offer was applicable. I got a, "um, no." *sad face* I love pickles, and it sounds like this place does it right, so now I'm starting to get that gut feeling like I made the wrong breakfast choice. 

I ordered The Row Bennie, and my buddies ordered their dish and the Biscuits & Jam. We also order three Bloody Marys. The Bloodys are comparable to what I'd make at home with the very little ingredients I might have to make a Bloody. Super average if not sub-par. Then our food came out... Per the professional shots online, the dishes looked amazing, whereas it really just looks like our food was thrown onto the plate cafeteria-style. The jam served with the biscuits are in black plastic to-go containers, and the dish itself is nothing special. One of our gal's orders was wrong so she sent it back, and our half-hearted waiter says, "yeah...I entered that in wrong." There is literally maybe only one other table here eating food other than the half-dozen regulars enjoying breakfast beers. 

I say two stars, 'cause my eggs were perfectly poached though I'm not sure what they're talking about "thick" sliced bacon. 

I was mildly embarrassed about my recommendation of this place. But again, Breakfast does not constitute Brunch, so maybe they kill it then. 

*THE ROW BENNIE* $10.99
thick sliced bacon, poached eggs & hollandaise

*BISCUITS & JAM $8.99
6 biscuits served with jam & butter
strawberry * blackberry * tomato * peach

It was the first time the cold spell hit New Orleans ( and then days later went back to 80 degrees) but I was starving and craving something warm so a friend suggested we go grab Red's. From what I've been told it's a homage/connected to Mission Chinese in San Fran, but don't quote me on that. 

It's the lower part of what looks like a house on St. Claude. I'd suggest parking on St. Claude or not far off it, especially if you're coming by yourself. The space is quaint and wasn't busy which was perfect for us. 

Together, to share, we ordered 4 sliders ( $12), yaka mein ( $10 size) and the ginger scallion noodles ($10) , so I guess you could say we really ordered oodles of noodles. This was more than enough plus leftovers for us two. 

The yaka mein was uh-mazing. As you can see from the lack thereof a picture, it's because we just dove right in like Olympic synchronized divers Kelci Bryant and Abby Johnston. The broth was perfect, not-too-salty, with little boiled eggs bobbing around chubby udon noodles with hearty pieces of beef short rib just lurking under the surface. The $10 bowl was easily shareable between the two of us, and we may or may not have sipped up the rest of the broth like a tasty beefy cocktail. I would say next time, I probably wouldn't get two noodle dishes again just because we ended up taking the ginger scallion dish home in two to-go containers to be enjoyed the next day. The flavors weren't as bold as the yaka mein which actually made it a great second dish with fresh scallions, a heaping bowl of silky noodles, a big yummy egg, and light flavors that can be kicked up with a couple shots of Sriracha. 

The sliders (I can't remember the meat) were OK. I liked that they're on steamed bao buns, but would've liked more texture and flavor, but I'm pretty sure their slider recipes change often, just an FYI. 

They were out of their warm toddy cocktail at the time, so I ordered La Diabla, with ginger, creme de cassis, arbol-chili infused Sombra mezcal. I'm not big on tequila, but the smoky cousin is muy delicioso especially when infused.  I would love for them to have hot sake on the menu. They didn't at the time, but maybe they'll bring it back! 

Will 100% be back to try other dishes, and will need that yaka mein in my life again; the ultimate cold weather comfort food and hangover cure!

We came to this spot because another neighborhood breakfast joint was pretty packed. It was a Monday around 10am'ish and it was pretty mellow. I just made a little edit to the hours, because it looks like they actually close at 11am, not 11pm on Mondays, so the fact that they were out of grits when we arrived makes more sense, but it still a bummer if you're not much for their other sides (beans, potatoes (note these are actually quite delicious), and fruit). 

I opted for the fruit with the California Burrito* ($10) sans black beans with a side of bacon and Robert ordered The Meat Burrito* ($12.50). They don't have espresso here, so I ordered an orange juice. 

The California Burrito is a hunk of burrito heavy on the eggs, though I wish there had been more toppings in this bad boy. I am a 50/50 type person when it comes to this, but if you love you some egg, this is where it's at! My side of bacon was cooked perfectly. I definitely had side envy with Robert's crispy potatoes and sauce. He also randomly got bacon (maybe it's part of the dish?) so I didn't have to share. 

The staff was nice and the space was clean, and they're open at 7am on Mondays if you're an early bird! 

*California Burrito - Eggs, mixed cheese, avocado, pico, black beans
*The Meat Burrito - Eggs, bacon, andouille, ham, mixed cheese, and potatoes

A friend of mine religiously goes here, so I thought I'd take her up on the offer of us both popping in here. We sat down in the window to the left, and were IMMEDIATELY served complimentary chips and two kinds of salsa, red and verde. We ordered their guacamole to give us time to look at the menu. I apologized to our waitress at least 3 times because she kept coming back and I still wasn't sure, so know that the staff is very attentive. 

The place has an authentic look about it, in terms of a Mexican restaurant where actual Mexicans and/or Central Americans living or visiting New Orleans would eat, if that makes sense. The menu has the names of the dishes in Spanish with half the explanations in English and half in Spanish and some explanations in both... It was only us and two other tables; one with a very unhappy baby, but it was nice to not be on top of other people eating dinner.  

The guacamole arrived, and we ordered the large Cocktail de Camarones and the pork Tostadas Mexicanas to split. Their guacamole is more of a soupier guacamole, not really chunky at all, but so so good. You can pick up flavors of cilantro and lime, and I really like this spin on a guacamole that's almost more of a guacamole salsa. 

The Cocktail de Camarones and Tostadas arrived not long after. They were both picture perfect as you can see; the tostadas matching their picture on the menu to a T. I should've seen that their were refried beans on the tostadas, aka frijoles, but I guess I thought I could pick around them. If you like beans, you'll like these since they make up the majority of the Tostadas with not a copious amount of pork on them. I didn't think the flavor was really there (again, I'm not a huge bean person, so take note). The Cocktail de Camarones reminded me more so of an Ecuadorian shrimp ceviche rather than your typical shrimp cocktail, and it's the closest I've come to tasting that flavor here in New Orleans. In Ecuador they use ketchup in their ceviche to tone down the acidity of the lime. The best way to describe it was, "tangy." Again if I hadn't been sharing, I probably would've added some heat, but it was a goblet of shrimp, and a ton of avocado, so I would definitely order this dish again. 

The split bill was equivalent to us both getting a footlong Subway, and we had an app and two dishes, so I'll probably stop in here again to try some other things, right after I knock out a few chapters of my Rosetta Stone.

If Southern-style dishes made a baby with Southeast Asian cuisine and they decided to raise their love child in their quirky grandma's house (but it's that grandma that always made great comfort food), that's Marjie's Grill. 

The building is a bright lil' ray of sunshine on a underwhelming stretch of Broad Street. You walk into a quaint dining room where intentional hodge-podgery exists in every nook and cranny, like the hand-embroidered sign of their Instagram handle hanging over their cutlery station. The sweet aroma of "I want that" wraps you up in an invisible blanket of hunger. Grab a chair upholstered in this fabulous retro cosmic vinyl to peruse the menu. 

The menu changes so drool over what they've got online or just be ready to enjoy whatever they've got going on. From my experience, I doubt you'll be disappointed.  Alas, I still felt the need to write a love letter about what I enjoyed!...

Fresh Cracklin' $7 
Dusted with tumeric-chili spice. 
Delicious, the perfect amount of chewy and crisp with a hint of spice. 

They had riblets (short ribs) as a special that day and they were perfect. You know how in other reviews I talk about my problem with sharing? If you like short ribs, do not, I repeat, do not share this dish. Perfectly sauced and easily came off the bones. 

Charred Pork Shoulder Steak $26
served sliced with tons of fresh herbs and a sweet chili sauce.
*Expletive Expletive Expletive* So gosh dang good. This hunk of meat was twice the size of my head and the four of us struggled to finish it. When they suggested we wrap the meat in the bounty of fresh herbs and dip it in the sauce, I hesitated...for maybe two seconds. The fresh herbs complemented the rich flavors of the meat and were only elevated by the light sauce provided. Hot damn, y'all. Hot damn. 

Did I mention we also ordered cornbread? Dios mio. 

With drinks and a copious amount of food, I couldn't believe how affordable it all was. I have an internal struggle telling Yelp about this because it really was one of the best meals I've had in New Orleans as of recent. 

Did we leave smelling like the sweet aroma of "I want that"? We sure did. Did we care? Not in the least bit.

The summer of last year during the "poke stop" craze I actually went to a place that was called Poké Stop in Portland, and lost my damn mind over the concept of fast, fresh poké bowls. I wished upon a star, kissed the clock at 11:11, fingers crossed, blew out some candles, lit some candles, rubbed a rabbit's foot (still connected to a rabbit), all in hopes that New Orleans would open a poké spot. 

My prayers (or strange superstitious wish bomb) were answered! Assembly line creations of delicious to-go bowls of fresh tuna and salmon, crunchy edamame, spicy roe, ginger, tempura flakes, all the things with a pleasant staff and my favorite flavors of Big Easy Bucha. What more could I ask for? 

Oh yeah, lightly-flavored water (yeyas), Tamari (new favorite thing, richer flavor and gluten-free), and a really lovely space to eat in. 

On the cost issue, yeah it definitely cost more than my usual lunch, but if you really consider it more of a deconstructed sushi roll, it's about 3 rolls worth, and think about how much that would've cost. AND usually this bowl could last two meals, but I can't stop at just satiating my hunger...I usually just end up eating the whole thing and have no regrets like I do when I eat an entire pizza. 

I'm so happy for the owners who are now opening two more locations (if you're looking for a third, Maple Street is just down from where I live, just sayin'). They really did their research and it shows, so I look forward to trying out their other locations.

First time coming to Willa Jean, my partner in crime and I had the bright idea of brunching before kick-off...as did everyone else in the city. 

Much like our Saints should've done that day, we reevaluated the situation and saw some window space with a counter. While the line situations for ordering to-go were a lil' unorganized with people oohing and ahhing at the baked good and also trying to figure out what to do, we were able to order fairly quickly. 

Willa Jean was prepared for the game day rush with plenty of aproned and gingham-wearing waiters in full gear. I mention the shirt because a patron at the bar was wearing the same EXACT shirt as the staff. 

We received our order of a chicken biscuit with Tabasco honey, a club sandwich with chips, a chocolate muffin, and two mochas for around $36. I thought the prices seemed high but for what we split (and could barely finish) it was totally worth it. The chocolate muffin was a funny cylindrical shape but tasted oh so good and packed a ton of chocolate, carb-laden flavor. The chicken biscuit was a sticky one, so maybe use a fork and knife to enjoy this dish or have some wet naps handy. The Tabasco honey was a great complement to the salty crunch of the chicken...sweetness on the front end with a little heat on the caboose. The mocha had a good flavor that wasn't too strong but definitely helped wake me up that morning.

Standing in the window was perfect for game day to watch the crowd pass by in their Saints gear. The space is expansive, clean, and bright. The bathrooms with a rooster for the guys and a feline for the girls (love the humor here) were pristine with fancy sinks and a dyson hand dryer.

I will definitely be returning, but if I'd like to sit, I'll be making a reservation for sure!

Shucks, I can't believe I haven't reviewed Cooter Brown's since 2013, hot damn. 

Late 2015, Cooter Brown's changed hands to the folks that own Rusty Nail (one of my other beloved watering holes) and what I love is they didn't really change much or nothing so significant that the folks that despise change in New Orleans would throw any sort of online hissy fits over. 

The same salty shucker that's been there for-ev-er is still there with his wonderful sarcasm and general grumpiness, but they've also brought on another nicer guy. Oysters are generally still big and fat, and shucked well off the shell. They still don't carry cocktail sauce, but you can make your own with their fresh horseradish, ketchup, hot sauce, and other accouterments. On Tuesdays, a dozen oysters are half off so they're $8 for a dozen, just make sure to remind the shucker when they ring you up. 

I've dabbled a lot more in their menu and my two favorites in the last couple of months were the Gator 'Mater* and the Irish Channel Special*. I'm a sucker for the slaw that comes on both, and I think the homemade sauces on both pair well with the meats. The kitchen is quick, and while the sandwiches don't come with fries, I tend to be struggling to find the belly space after my usual 1/2 dozen, sandwich, and a cold pint! 

Parking has still been pretty easy. I'm not really uber big into watching sports, but I'd imagine this would be a good spot to do so since they still have the projector screen and other TVs, but I find when there isn't a big game on, it's pretty mellow and a nice place to grab a bite with friends! 

*GATOR 'MATER $12.95
Grilled Link Alligator Sausage, Fried Green Tomatoes, Creole Mustard Spread, Buttermilk Slaw

*IRISH CHANNEL SPECIAL $11.99
Braised Corned Beef, Caramelized Onions, Swiss Cheese, Buttermilk Slaw, Crystal Remoulade, on sliced Semolina

You 2/3rds roast beef po'boy is really good, moist and just right, in terms of roast beef. And the staff that cleans up was courteous. Tons of indoor space. And somehow I made it on a day where there was only, maybe 15 people in line. 

But, it's hard for me, as a local, to justify being corralled into a line like herded cattle, and scolded when I stand in this line by staff carrying pans of food. There is a polite way to say things loudly even if you're carrying hot food. That might be a schtick, but it's off-putting when so many restaurants in the Quarter work on being congenial to both tourists and locals. 

$40 bucks for two Bloody Mary's and 2 2/3 dressed roast beef poboys is redonkulous. Their roast beef poboys are good, and 2/3rds is the perfect amount for me, but for the amount we paid, I'm usually leaving with half my overstuffed poboy, a pleasant service experience, and some change.

For some people, this is a cool experience, and that's great. If you enjoy the company of a line, okay with a little 'tude, AND solid po'boys at a higher price (and don't necessarily like leftovers), then Mother's may be perfect for you. I'm not a fan of waiting for a po'boy in New Orleans, when there are so many amazing places around town, that I'll get a hefty to-go box to take home and nosh on later.

A great place to bring visiting friends or grab a TO-GO po'boy that could fill you up twice if you eat like me. 

While I have more favorite po'boy shops closer to my apartment and a little less pricey, I think Crabby Jack's has a great vibe and seems like one of those fun, under-the-radar po'boy shops to bring friends from out of town. While it is owned by Jacque who owns Jacques-Imo's and you can catch him in there every now and then, it's a totally different feel than his Oak Street restaurant so it's fun to try out both locations. Dr. Bob artwork covers the walls, and there are some interesting catchphrases besides the "Be Nice Or Leave" that we all know and love so well. 

On our most recent visit, we ordered four Regular po'boys including Duck, Cochon-de-lait, Fried Green Tomatoes with Remoulade, and a Half/Half as well as a side of cole slaw and sweet teas. 

We'll work our way up to the po'boys. The cole slaw was very vinegar-y but I love that with great crunch. I'm not really big on fried po'boys so I didn't really munch too much into the Half/Half, but I did get a skrimp and I like the batter taste, not too thick and still maintaining the flavor of the shrimp. The Cochon-de-lait was a little too rich for me, but the meat was really thick, and everyone else absolutely loved it.  The duck is always amazing to me. The meat is cooked to perfection, was moist, and the flavor wasn't too overpowering. I will say it might be a tie between the Duck and the Fried Green Tomatoes. The Fried Green was the freshest tasting to me, and has good crunch. 

Their sweetened tea is always good, and you get a great big go-cup to take home! You better believe I have "set" of these! Definitely worth the visit!

The hunger overtook me the other night, and I had to find me some sustenance. I've always wanted to try Ba Chi, so I headed over there. The space isn't really anything to write home about so I'm glad I was ordering to-go.

I read through some of the current reviews and swiped through a handful of pictures before deciding on the Kimchi Fries, Spicy Lemongrass Chicken Wings, and two Bacos ie Vietnamese Tacos ( Pulled Pork and Beef Saté), and a Jasmine Tea. I thought for sure I had spent some mula but all that was $27 which I thought was really fair. 

I would definitely say order before you get there but they had had quite a few togo orders so the wait was a little longer than expected. Staff was as they are at most spots like this with a mission in mind, getting shiz done, and not overly friendly. 

The bacos were OK. The buns were fluffy and the flavor was good but the Wings and Kimchi Fries were the standouts! Damn...those Kimchi Fries. I could just order those and be a happy little clam. Not too spicy but rich in flavor. The wings also were not too spicy but had a good kick. They were also HUUGE! With two U's! Great value, and I can't wait to try the other flavors. Word to the wise, these wings are not a sexy dish to eat so enjoy with a friend or a life-long partner that is stuck with you. Not a first Tinder/Bumble date...

Looking forward to many more togo orders and trying their pho.

No idea why this star hasn't been added sooner. You can read my first review for tips on how to navigate this unique space that is often imitated by never duplicated. My advice is to visit with someone who has been before so they can pass on their knowledge of favorite cheeses, wines, and how to best sneak up on empty tables to waste away the evening at. 

There are so many places in New Orleans to be seen and to people watch, and maybe you come to Bacchanal for that but I feel like this corner venue that you'd pass up if you didn't know better, turns your attention to the folks at your table or to the band playing on the stage; not to trivial conversations on why Becky has such good hair or why white is so not fetch after Labor Day (someone still needs to explain this to me). 

I've had amazing conversations with local friends and travelers under cotton candy clouds and twinkling Christmas lights while enjoying delicious cheese plates and bottles upon bottles of sparkling wine. No judgement is passed if you show up in running clothes or a ball gown 'cause there is no dress code. And while you may bump into a former lover or loser, there's enough room at Bacchanal for everyone. 

The folks that work here have always been incredibly pleasant, a band is nearly always "slappin' the bass", and I think it is just one of those spots you shouldn't pass up while visiting our wonderful city.

I'm kind of in love. I've mentioned this in other coffee shop reviews but it rings true. All these new lil' espresso utopias are making it hard to ever go back to the chains. 

I've been to Cherry a handful of times. I kind of wish it wasn't on anyone's radar but here I am writing a review about it so at the end I'm going to Jedi mind trick / Men In Black erase your mind. 

The space is a renovated firehouse painted in happy colors. While there sadly is no firemen's pole, I love the expanse of the space and the artwork they have been filling it with. They have communal tables, outdoor seating, two tops and a lovely couch you can feel proper on. The guest volume is pleasantly between Rue de La Course and MOJO leaning toward RDLC. They play a variety of music from rap to indie but it's on a level that's not disturbing and you may catch yourself singing aloud ;). 

Love the staff. They make you feel very welcome, and I have yet to have a bad mocha. A large with an extra shot still has a great balance of chocolate, milk, and coffee and does the job. I ordered a pear salad off the menu for the first time the other day. No overpowering flavors, nice crunch, healthy and filling. If you're hanging out, their glassware is lovely too. 

Someone mentioned how fun it'd be if this spot did late night dance parties, just sayin'.

I will definitely be keeping Cherry Coffee in my work rotation for mochas and meetings! 

Now what were we talking about? ;)

I could give this place a one star, just to keep you all from ever knowing how amazingly awesome it is, alas, I will tell the tale of how I fell in love with Mid-City Yacht Club one fateful Thursday night...

Some friends invited me out for a ladies night to Mid-City Yacht Club. The last time I had been there was when they still allowed smoking and I was in and out in less time it took to take a breath. I wasn't expecting much even though I knew they were no longer smoking. I will eat crow someday for saying that...

Parking pro-tip...you'll see this fabulous spot right up the street next to the ball park that is kitty corner from the Club. There's a reason it's open. Fly balls are your enemy so go around the block. 

We waltz in, and the ratio of older men to girls is 5:1 with our two friends sitting at the bar. But it's not that creepy I-just-busted-into-your-territory feel. I sidled up to the bar and ordered my usual first drink of the night; a Bloody Mary hingeing the "I'm sorry" to it 'cause some bartenders roll their eyes at me ordering the meal in a glass. Not this guy! He made it literally in seconds flat, garnishes and all with their vegetable infused vodka that the bartender told me all about. Uh-freakin-mazing, y'all. Not too spicy or crazy with ingredients, but the infused vodka mixed so well with the tomato juice, I drank two. They have a number of other infused vodkas in cool little transparent honey pot looking jars. 

We enjoyed our delicious cocktails on the back patio that I wish was my own. Misters  kept the temperature at least 6 degrees cooler than right outside the gate. There are a ton of chairs and a couple of picnic tables you can push together. This is where all the girls were hanging out. Duh. 

My friend and I began a laid back game of cornhole that then turned into a blood thirsty team vs team triathlon including cornhole, giant jenga, and pool. We played the cornhole on the patio, giant jenga in a side room that'd be great for parties and pool in the back area of the bar. We did this all while enjoying the sweet sounds of the '90s brought to us by the other bartender who was equally as awesome as the first.

But wait...IT GETS BETTER! So after two Bloody Marys, a Moscow Mule, three losses, and one win...you work up a hunger. We split an order of Pulled Pork Poppers, like baseball sized boudin balls that were crispy on the outside and tender cooked pulled pork on the inside with a hint of spice, and a Lucky Burger with bacon and sauteed mushrooms that needed no condiment to mar the delicious crispy piggy strips and juicy 'shrooms. They said the Pulled Pork Poppers were being changed out for something else, so I'm glad I tried them when I did. I'm drool dreaming about the burger, and will definitely be back for that. 

Needless to say, I really liked this place. The bartenders are awesome, the vibe is great, the games keep you entertained, and there's no smoking...And they allow dogs. Mic drop.

While Uchi has been on my list for a while now, it was Bobert who introduced me first through take out and secondly by bringing me to the restaurant off of Causeway. I've been here a few times when it was other iterations, so I was interested to see how it was different.

A bit of a slower night, but the staff was on point with hot towels and drink orders. We ordered the poke salad, and a handful of rolls including the Cowboy Roll, Johnny Special Roll, Cucumber Sashimi Roll, and a Spicy Crunch Roll. Our eyes were DEFINITELY bigger than our bellies. 

Everything came out fairly quickly. The rolls we got were really medium to XXL. This might be weird to point out but I feel everything is rolled really well. Sometimes with large rolls, they just fall apart, but not here. I like that they also have a wide variety of seaweed, rice paper, and cucumber (my fave!) rolled rolls. Favorite was probably the Johnny Special, and the poke salad. I wasn't a HUGE fan of the Cowboy since there wasn't anything really crunchy about it and it was served warm. The Cucumber Sashimi had a great fresh crunch and was ridiculously huge. 

I love service that is attentive without being overbearing, and they joked with us when we realized we ordered waaaay too much. 

Only mini complaint is most of their rolls had snow crab, and I really try to avoid it though most our rolls that we ordered had it. I feel like it's a bit of a filler, and really doesn't add much to a roll for me. I'm going to try to ask if they can make it with no snowcrab next time, and I know the roll will be smaller, but I'm okay with that!

The more I think about Ancora, the more I really liked it. 

I am not a pizza snob, more of a pizza slob. We tend to order Papa's once a week and break out the Tabasco, homegrown banana peppers, and ranch, yes I defile my pizzas with a ton of ranch. 

Back to Ancora...We were going to get it to go so we could marathon watch American Horror Story's The Coven, but I begged that we stay in and eat. The space is expansive, with a great big window similar to other businesses on Freret.

We received our menus and the beer menu, were told specials were on the wall, and left to decide. We were kinda hangry, so after deciding, we're like, "yo where'd our buddy waiter go?" but I think it was the hunger pangs slowing down time between menu receiving and ordering. 

We scooped up an order of the Lardo Bruschetta, which the waiter was kind enough to let us know it wasn't cheese since some peeps think it is. It's strips of  fatback cured with herbs. It seemed to be very very thin on our Bruschetta, but I loved the taste (though unique and kind of hard to explain) and it was great to dip the rest of our bread in the special app, Arancini Balls; fried rice and cheese balls with a marinara sauce underneath.
