Open these up before biting into since the cheese is like molten delicious lava. 

Then on to our pizza, the Diavola. Wait till it cools just a little or your toppings may slide off. Coming out, it doesn't look like much since it's 12" and a thinner pizza without being New York size(#pizzarules) but the flavor is so much more rich than what you'd expect. The salumi packs a lot of flavor in the little slices, and is just enough on each piece. Robert joked about them having ranch, but we did request red pepper flakes. The waiter (who was on point and informative after the hangry wore off) said he would bring the pepper flakes, but also suggested a chili paste that he though might go better with the flavors. This attention to complementary condiments to their menu items is a huge plus to me. We ended up not using the flakes at all and putting the chili paste on our pieces (sparingly, because it is quite spicy). 

I thought this was the perfect amount of food, and well priced for what we ate. I think next time I will definitely have to complement my pizza with a glass of red wine. While I still love my Midway across the...way, these pizzas are night and day, and both equally delicious in their own right. 

 Diavola: Spicy Naples Salumi, Fior di Latte, Chili and Tomato

Back in 2008 when I worked around the corner, I would order from Cake Cafe for lunch all the time. Six years later, they're still consistently good, fairly priced and a great corner to enjoy a meal. 

I usually get the sandwiches. I recently had the *Chicken Salad Sandwich on Ciabatta. You can tell the chicken salad is freshly made because it's not a "scoop" of chicken salad. I kicked it up a notch with a little hot sauce, cause that's how I do, but it's crunchy, with a hint of sweetness from the grapes. The ciabatta is the perfect bread pairing, I think. 

I like all the original artwork in their dining area, but on a beautiful day, I enjoy sitting outside watching the neighborhood. Pro-Tip: if you order a soda or bottled water, the cooler is to the right with all the other drinks, so go grab it or else you may forget. 

I always stare longingly at their baked goods, but have yet to partake. I need to go back to hit that up. Stay tuned... 


*CHICKEN SALAD
Herb-roasted chicken with grapes, almonds, onion, celery, mayo,
a hint of curry, dressed with lettuce & tomato 8.75

Our group of gals headed over to Tavern for a brunch while visiting Nashville for a bachelorette party. We were a party of five, and while we waited for a table, we found a back bar that was quieter than the main dining room chock-full of brunchers and bach parties ( I literally had no idea that Nashville was such a bach party destination). At this little back bar was one of the most chill bartenders, Rebekah, who took care of us with delicious bloody marys and bellinis (and much needed waters). During brunch, there is a two-for-one on their Brunch Libations which includes bloody marys, mimosas, bellinis, and sangria. Definitely worth it. 

We opted to sit outside since the weather was pleasant. The prices are really fair especially since some of the dishes were massive. I split the Singapore Stir Fry with another gal, and my own dish seemed like one serving. I also got avocados to mash into it!  I do feel like this dish could've had more oomph of flavor, but maybe its toned down for the hoi polloi so ask for some hot sauce!  

The Maple Fondue is great to try a little bit of everything on their menu, and I love savory and sweet flavors together. Standout was the grilled spicy chicken sausage. Great for the whole table. 

Not sure if it was because we were outside, but our waitress (not Rebekah, but a different gal) was a bit MIA at times. Note to folks wanting to eat outside during the summer, at some point it will get warm, haha, so maybe bring a fan 'cause what's brunch without a cute fan. 

I'd definitely suggest this as a great spot to bring a group for brunch, and would be interested to check them out on a return visit for other eating hours and to peruse their beer selection! 

$11.50 SINGAPORE STIR FRY
#1 short-grain rice / sunny side up eggs / bacon / scallions / sweet & spicy soy / wok-flavored

$17 MAPLE FONDUE ( FOR THE TABLE)
warm maple syrup / fresh fruit / red velvet waffle / grilled sausages / pain perdu

I've been going to Dorignac's since I was a wee one and they've really done an amazing job keeping up with their competitors in town if not exceeding them at times. 

If you're buying wine and liquor for a party (or even a few bottles for yourself), go here. They've got a ton of options, great prices, and a handful of well-informed employees working this area to help you out. They also usually have wine tastings going on, hello!!!

Since this isn't my usual go-to grocery spot, it takes me a second to figure out where everything is, but they might have one of the best staffs of any grocery store in town from their stockers to their check-out peeps to their baggers to direct you to the correct aisle. 

From local-pickled products to Taco Bell's new chocolate tacos you can make your own Choco Taco's with, they really do "got dat" as John "Spud" McConnell keeps telling us in their commercials. They even have dry ice! Not sure who else in town carries that year-round! They also have some pretty sick deals from time to time, but you'll find them on little tags by the items so peruse the aisles. 

I'm a pretty quick shopper so I get a little crazy when I'm maneuvering aisles at break-neck speeds and have to wait for older clientele to pick out rice. Same goes for the parking lot, but by no means is that Dorignac's fault. In fact, it's a tribute to customer loyalty, and I just need to pump the breaks but know that you're going to need some time in there because check-writing is still a real thing, people!

The hubs hit it big at the casino so we headed to Fleming's for a fancy steak dinner on a Sunday night. White tablecloths, low romantic lighting, and wine cellars make this date destination in the parking lot of the Lakeside Mall in Metairie an island of fance. 

We enjoyed the Sweet Chile Calamari. The light sauce that came with the perfectly breaded and fried calamari had a nice sweet and spice to it. We both ordered salads. I got the modern Caesar made with hearts of romaine, parmesan, fried capers, crisp prosciutto chips. It was interesting. I wish their had been more capers and I think the prosciutto is more a texture thing than very flavorful. We also ordered the sautéed mushrooms. As a matter of preference, I like a more vinegary finish and these were heavy on the garlic, but still really good. The finalé ('cause there was no way I could put away a dessert after all that) was the steaks. The 8 oz filet mignon was cooked perfectly and a great cut of meat.

Kali was our server was incredible. Knowledgeable about the menu but it didn't feel rehearsed. Very sweet and just a lovely complement to a nice dinner date.

I believe I have finally found my coffee shop! Cue the heavenly light and angels...AWWWWWWWWE!

Off the bat, it smells amazing. Not that coffee shops don't smell okay, the slight hint of tea leaves in the air is so refreshing here.

They still have everything I love from the other Mojos including the nifty chalkboard, local art, but more of it, including the postcards and flyers lining a step right under the bar. I called for a Milky Way and forgot to request it cold. Nonetheless, it was DELICIOUS and beautiful to boot. 

Though there are no couches for that homey sort of feel, I love all the tables because 1. They're big enough for all my shenanigans I bring to the coffee shop. 
2. There is no lack of plugs. 
3. They're spread out enough that everyone's biz is their own.
4. This is a weird one. I love seeing people I know, but sometimes it can be distracting when trying to knock something out. There are enough tables that you don't have to be by the front door where you'd constantly be looking up when someone comes in and possibly seeing someone you know with the obligation to chat. And there is a back door that you can escape out of. 

My only problem is the chairs are a little tough on my boney butt, but I think that's a personal problem. Next time I'll just bring one of those blow up cushions, and be the cool kid. Will definitely be returning!!!

During this wonderful Lenten season there are so many options for fish on Fridays, so me and my bub spun the virtual Yelp globe, and stuck our finger on Trenasse (after some research and finding out they had live music)! 

If you come to New Orleans, never underestimate a restaurant in a hotel. This one is located in the Intercontinental but by no means "feels" like you're in the hotel. We easily found street parking around the block. We were led to an intimate little two-seater. 

I had stalked many a dish on the Internets, and we were two hungry hungry hippos. To start we ordered the Crispy Red Chili Shrimp, Alligator Hot Tamales, Ceviche, A Half Dozen Raw, and A Half Dozen Chargrilled...to start. 

Our service was top notch, and our table quickly filled up with our starting dishes. The raw oysters were clean and big. While I favor another local spot's chargrilled, these were pretty good as well! 

The alligator hot tamale with sauce piquant and maque choux was the perfect marriage of Cajun and Latin dishes. I appreciate the greens to balance out the dish! The crispy red chili skrimps were sooo good! They were perfectly crisped with a tasty dip we couldn't get enough of. And then there was the ceviche...the presentation is lovely and incredibly utilitarian since it holds ice to keep it deliciously chilled. While it was not an Ecuadorian ceviche, it was one of the best, well-proportioned ceviches I've had in the city and I'd order a thousand times over. In fact, you can get it on your oysters. I'll totally be doing this next time. 

What's amazing about Trenasse is that their entrees are hard to choose from because there are seemingly so many amazing options. That being said, I pooped out on starters, so I got a bowl of their soup special while 'berto go the seared tuna special. Ohmagersh...Good thing this man loves me 'cause he shared and it was probably the most amazing tuna I've had in a restaurant ever, ever, and we've had tuna right off the dock, so we a bit picky. Very clean and perfectly seared, letting the natural flavors shine through without any hint of fishiness. 

While the Stinky Stew had been on my mind for literally three months (I'm telling you picking Trenasse was totally a whim...but not really), don't pass on their specials, especially if they have the tuna. 

I look forward to trying out their brunch sometime, and this bloody mary you folks have been snappin'.

A little mix-up with which Surrey's location on Magazine to meet my pops at brought me back to the first Surrey's I ever experienced Bananas Foster French Toast at. Mmmm...It's helpful to say LGD or Uptown when getting a group together! 

It was drizzling, and it's a tiny bit of a pain since this place is so popular and there isn't really anywhere to go nearby during the inevitable wait, but it wasn't too shabby this time around. Though I must warn you...the neighbor's have a sprinkler system that senses people that don't like to get wet. just an FYI. 

This location is more tightly packed than the other locale but the servers are all pros at manuevering the labyrinth that is their setup. There's fun local architectural artwork on the walls, and the tables are all uniquely different. If you're looking for the condiments, they're hanging on the wall so as to leave more room on the tables for delicious food. 

I enjoyed my go-to Shrimp & Grits (that comes with bacon), with the grits being on the creamier side this time around and a side order of avocado mash, which was more guacamole textured and tasting to the usual chunkiness, but still gone in seconds. To wash it down I had an Apple Ginger juice. A small is perfect for me, and the ginger wasn't overpowering.  This is probably my favorite juice combo! 

Food came out in a timely manner, and we ordered the Bananas Foster to go for my main man at home. This location feels busier to me since it's smaller so just be aware that if for any reason you order something and they forget, they're more than happy to take it off your bill or make sure you get it post-haste.  

While I may still go to the Surrey's Uptown ( since you can get a Bloody Mary while you wait at the bar next door) for breakfast, I've been to this Surrey's for lunch without much of a wait at all a while back, and will have to go back to give you an updated review then!

I love this place, and I rarely drink wine. So if you want to know about the wine on tap, this isn't the review for you. If you have wino friends like myself, and are wondering whether you should accompany them to this establishment, that's a hell. yes. 

Since this spot has opened, I've been here four times. You're probably like, "Five stars, Morgan?!" Is that not a little premature?!...Judge me all you want, folks. I really really like this spot. 

"Ode To Bayou Wine Garden"
I've been on a Friday night, I've been on a Sunday. 
I've been with my gal pals, and I've been with my bae. 

I've ordered champagne by the bottle, I've ordered a beer next door. 
I've downed quality H2O and I've had The Fireman, a cocktail I adore. 

Half their menu, I've consumed, and I have only one request.
More dipping sauce for the bread sticks would be best. 

That being said, everything I've eaten has been delish. 
From the wontons to the Cubano to the Fried Smoked Shrimp, my favorite dish. 

The staff is amazing, and how they keep this place so tidy, I'm incredibly impressed. 
I'm sure these past few weeks have put them to the test. 

Yes it gets crowded, and a little smooshy at times.
Sorry guys, I'm running out of rhymes...

OK, okay, for reals though. I do see some things that they'll probably need to work out in some way in the future, i.e. where you order food at (it's really close to the kitchen door so there is a bit of maneuvering that goes on), but I think that they are killin' it. 

The Fried Smoked Shrimp* could be my second most favorite po'boy'ish sandwich in town behind Crabby Jack's shrimp remoulade and fried green tomato. The shrimp aren't heavily fried and the sauce drizzled atop and the accompanying dressings is the makings of a perfect sandwich IMO. 

The staff really is amazing. The kitchen is open so you can see them creating these delicious concoctions, and I don't think they all ever stop moving. From those behind the wine bar to those bussing tables, everyone is doing it with a smile, and they all just seem to work incredibly well with each other. 

The other night, I ordered the Fireman off their drink menu. Well priced, and damn delicious. I love a drink with some heat, and this has just the right amount. I easily consumed two and could've gone a third round. Probably my new favorite drink, and will soon be "the usual" for me here. 

Yes...This place gets crowded, like "chicks swarming near your table waiting for your butt to leave the chair to swoop in"-crowded. So don't complain 'cause I warned you. Have that awesome friend go hold down a table early so that you can get on up in there to people watch your night away. 

I've yet to have any issues with parking in the back, and appreciate this extra parking since the expansion. They also have a great bike rack right out front. 

Bayou Beer Garden, I won't forget you...but Bayou Wine Garden, I'll probably see you Friday night. ;) 

FRIED SMOKED SHRIMP ON LIEDENHEIMER PISTOLET 13.00
Sparkling Wine Tempura Battered Cold Smoked Shrimp with BBQ Shrimp Aioli and House-made Pickled Radish, Onion & Green Tomato... Served with Chips

FIREMAN 8.00
Bourbon, Elderflower, Lemon, Mint, Jalapeno

Yesterday we were passing through and decided to stop by this spot my mom recommended we try! After browsing through their extensive menu, I decided on the Mango Blackberry Chicken Salad and an Unsweetened Ice Tea with Lemon. Lemme tell you, this was not your average salad, the price point is decent and filled with fancy ingredients! One bite sends you, I had never tried mango on a salad so I was curious and with the blackberries and tangy balsamic vinaigrette and all the fancy Ingredients of this large salad, caramelized pecans, bleu cheese, my taste buds went on a flavor ride! The chicken was also grilled to perfection and I was left very satisfied with my meal! The Ice Tea by my surprise came in a nice large glass, with a fresh slice of lemon and the herbs were very flavorful on their own! No need to sweeten it! 

My toddler chose the Chicken Tenders and I asked for a side of fruit for her in place of fries, since it was a healthier option and otherwise she wouldn't eat her meal. She loved it and I couldn't help but  smile at the name of the kid's menu which came with a variety of unopened crayons she enjoyed coloring with, "Little Big Foot Menu" Cute right?! 

This was my first dine-in since quarantine and the staff were very welcoming, mentioned to check out the statue inside, which is life-sized, my toddler thought the Sasquatch was real until we assured her it was safe to approach! They followed the guidelines: seating was nicely spaced out, our server was masked up and our food came out in a timely manner in time for our drive! I would highly recommend paying a visit to this well-known spot! I know I'll definitely be visiting again to try more off their menu and take another pick with our Sasquatch friend! I know he isn't "big foot", but he reminds me of one of my favorite family movies Harry and the Hendersons with his big broad smile and significant size! Support small, especially when they need our business the most, Happy Memorial Day!

This is definitely a go-to BBQ! When I saw the long line I was hoping the supply could fulfill the demand. Blue Oak BBQ was on point with everything. 

The wait was very short thanks to the helpful staff and menus strategically placed at the beginning of the line. 

The aroma of pit smoke and BBQ sauce had my mouth watering and rereading temptations listed on their menu. 

I placed an order for four ribs and the garlic mac&cheese.  Every time I pick up a meaty rib it would slide off the bone. It really felt like it melted in my mouth. The garlic & Mac cheese was just right. I wanted MORE PLEASE! 

This was lunch but I was done eating the entire day. #Lethargic

The burgers are totally tasty! The beer, The beers are ice cold!  Patty choices: Angus, Zapp'd chicken, Turkey, Bison, Philet, veggie and alligator. The sauce and toppings are too many to name but include: Crystal wing sauce, grilled jalapeño aioLi, avocado ranch, sweet chili BBQ, Fried egg, pineapple rings, avocado-tomato relish.

The Happy Hour?Mon-Friday 3pm-6pm:

 1/2 off house wine and ALL BEER! $2 Kobe Sliders, $2 Meat pies, $1 Chick or duck wings!

But wait there's more! The Pecan Pie Shake(mix of vanilla ice cream and pecan pie) is sooo yummmy! 

Somebody roll me out the door, LoL.

I came here for a private group dinner.  The ambiance is really nice.  The restaurant itself is on the second floor. The downstairs is the bakery.  It has a very chic farm to table look.  Think this place is relatively new. It's in a newly developed area in King of Prussia.

The service was excellent.  The food I enjoyed the most was the crab spinach dip. The wings were juicy and well flavored but nothing to write home about.  I had the 10oz ribeye and it was cooked perfectly.  The steak sauce on the side was fantastic!  My friend had the risotto crab and shrimp which looked heavenly.  I had food envy.

I also had their cucumber vodka drink and it was so refreshing.  Overall I had a great time and will definitely bring my husband here.  Only knock was parking is kinda hard to find.

I have tried so many bubble tea places in Philadelphia and this has become my favorite place.

This place allows you to order drinks that actually aren't overly sugary and tastes like tea.  They have options of sea salt or cheese foams and it is really a neat experience.  It adds a lightness delicacy to the drink.

My favorite is the green tea with sea salt foam.  If you want a real treat add a scoop of green tea ice cream then it is amazing.  The cups and lids allow for straw but to really enjoy the layering of the foam it's best to sip it.

Only downside is cost.  It is slightly more $ than competitors but I rarely treat myself so it's worth it.

So this review is just for dimsum.  We've been here twice and it gets better each time.  First the restaurant is huge and can accommodate a lot of people.  This is an area in Busleton that some consider to be the next up and coming new Chinatown.

On a Sat brunch time it was busy which was reassuring so that food would be fresh.  They have all the essentials shumai, hakgow and roast pork buns.  My favorites are the fried almond bun with roast pork buns.  They also have lots of flat noodles with shrimp or beef.  The congee is just ok not great.  The service is better than most other dimsum places.  Prices are reasonable.  There is also free parking in the lot.

The only knock is that this place is so cold that in winter you may need to keep your coats on.  We mentioned it to staff and they couldn't do much about it.  However food is good, nice selections and prompt service so we will definitely be back!

um... When they ask you to pay $ 10.00 entrance fee to Gamble???? **

Slot Machines.... CHECK
Tables (Pai Gow, Black Jack, Roulette)..... CHECK
Drinks.... CHECK 
MUSIC..... CHECK.....

Place is pretty small, but if you're around the area.  I rather go to AC where there  is more options for you to play.

** Unless you are staying in the Hotel, then you don't have to pay to get in...

The food is amazing. Besides that, last time we went, the cashier gave my bf the wrong change - short a 20. After we left, he noticed and called to let them know. The lady said she would check her drawer and call back. Not only did she call back right away, but she verified that they were indeed 20 dollars over. She could have easily kept the difference, or waited until the end of the day to check, but she didn't. Very honest and considerate employees! Thank you!

I've been to Sampan numerous times. With friends, for my birthday, an intimate setting, etc. This restaurant is one of my favorite places to eat in Philly! The atmosphere is dimmed and chill on the inside and outdoor seating is on the sidewalk. All about preference!

I loveeee being able to choose flavorful foods from Sampan's different categories on their menu -- as well as sharing those items with others. Sampan has a great happy hour too! Also, you're able to easily make reservations on Resy.

This particular night, I did not go for the chef tasting menu (7 selections for $45 per person). I tried their edamame dumpling (one of my favs, broth so good and it has a smoky sort of flavor), crab wonton taco (first time trying and it was so good; wasn't expecting it to be cold but still delicious), scallops (another one of my favs; cooked to perfection), and shrimp pad Thai (requested no tofu; amazingly tasty and a big portion). Lastly, ordered their Thai Punch. You can definitely taste the alcohol and overall a good a** drink!

Staff was cool. The servers brought the food out FRESH and would describe what the dish was before walking off. Another thing, I LOVE that the staff brings the food right out after it's been cooked! 

I love this place! No complaints!

I hardly ever give a place 1 star but what else can you give a place when you weren't offered anything.  Not offered anything ... you think in dismay ... not a glass of water, a menu, a drink, or even an unwelcoming glance.  Maybe I wore my invisible cloak that night and didn't realize it.
I've been so excited to try this place every since I noticed the big billboard on I-24 back at the end of 2016 speaking of it's upcoming opening.  I decided to head to The Diner to pass the time while waiting to meet a friend at another spot.
There was not a crowd on this lovely evening.  The entirety of downtown Nashville was in the throes of "Pred's Fever" and most of the fans were elsewhere watching the game.  I went straight to the 2nd floor to the sports bar.  Deciding that watching a piece of the game and enjoying a drink would be cool.  I sat facing the Batman building.  The building itself really is in a lovely spot and has a unique look and feel.  The first floor does truly look like a diner with upscale accoutrements. I sat there and I sat there.  I looked around and yes there was staff there and other patrons.  I decided to give them a break and to give it a little more time.  So I sat some more and still nothing ... I kid you not ... I was ignored for over 20 minutes.  Finally, I got up and walked out.
In my hard heart, I would like to say that I'll only come back to this place if I'm already downtown and some friends/family have come in from out of town and it's 4am and we're starving and intoxicated with no place else to grab food and drink at that time of night and the closest is uber is 30 minutes away but every place deserves a second chance ... I guess.  Maybe a different floor will acknowledge my existence.

I love you Philly cupcake. The décor is beyond impressive. The cupcakes are displayed in pink armoire like the pieces of art they are. We settled on the pistachio and the sweet potato cupcakes. The pistachio was not my favorite, but not bad. It was a bit dense. The sweet potato cupcake was worth a trip from DC to Philly. The cake was moist and the frosting creamy and not overly sweet.  The staff was very friendly and informative. I will definitely be back.

A top notch spot in Rittenhouse that is sure to please, whether its with cocktails or through their food, or ambiance and service. Easily one of my favorite places in the area, and worth a trip across town. The best news is that they are open for more than just Friday, Saturday, and Sunday (haha there is my corny humor but something I still really think about since the first time I saw the name of the place). 

The cocktails are divine and if you are lucky enough to sit with Sasha, you will have a new best friend. She is a master mind with the tools of the bar at her fingertips. Allison is also quite talented too for what its worth. For food I can recommend the shrimp cocktail app (some of the best shrimp I have ever had, large and tasty) and my favorite, the octopus. Honestly could be the best I have ever had. The style of food dances the line between trendy and homey with bold flavors that are sure to please. 

Its often crowded so dont be surprised if you pop in and there is no room at the bar, and if you want a table for a meal, reservations are suggested. Put this place on your must visit list, especially if you are a foodie like myself.

The Screamery Handcrafted Ice Cream has me ready to shout from the rooftops in adoration. I'm John Cusack in "Say Anything" for this ice cream. ::Cue the Peter Gabriel:: Using natural ingredients and milk from grass-fed cows, this homemade ice cream is hands-down some of the best I have E-V-E-R had! I can't help but compare any honey flavor to the Sweet Cream Honeycomb. A sweet cream base with swirls honeycomb pieces. I will eat a whole pint in one sitting and I don't care. Sorry, thighs! Easily in my top 5 favorites ice creams EVER from ANYWHERE! Grab yourself a pint but be prepared for the overwhelming desire to serenade a dessert by holding a radio over your head by the time you get down to your last spoonful.

Lulu's is so delicious! Even for a non-vegan, they have great food! The menu changes seasonally. Some favorites have been the sushi bowl (made with watermelon!) and the tots. Their sauces are so good, especially the ranch and spicy aioli! Their buffalo cauliflower is also delicious. Service here is fast and friendly. When you're done eating, they have various bins for dishes, compost and recycling. It's very low (zero?) waste. I appreciate the work that Lulu's does for the environment and the veg community of STL!

Wow! Hidden gem, for sure! I brought International Supper Club here, and I am mad at myself that I haven't tried it sooner. 

First, let's start with the pita bread. THE BEST I've had in STL. So yummy!! I started with a Greek salad - also amazing. Ample amounts of feta, pita to soak up extras, flavorful dressing. Loved it. I also snagged a bite of saganaki (flaming cheese) and greatly enjoyed it!  

I got the spanakopita. It was delicious! Two large pieces with a side of tzaziki for dipping. Definitely tasted fresh - flaky pastry rather than chewy, lots of spinach and feta taste. I couldn't eat it all and took some home. 

The service was great - despite having a group of 12 and there being other diners (and one waitress). She was totally on our needs, got things out fast, flamed the cheese, processed checks.. it was awesome.

I WILL BE BACK.. SOON!!

This is a new place that's near my house, so when I heard that they had vegetarian sliders, I definitely wanted to try it. I got the opportunity twice in one weekend. It's a great place for kids - fast and friendly. It's large, but very popular right now and so there was a wait one of the two times (dinnertime). They used the No Wait app to put us in line, but at that time, it was not available for me to check in myself. Hopefully they will expand to this in the future. 

In one visit, I shared the appetizer plate that came with fries, sweet potato fries, house made chips and tater tots. The fries and sweet potato fries are awesome! The platter came with a couple sauces, including a cheese dip and ranch (our choice). Both great,especially the ranch. The chips were just ok. The tater tots are not like any I've ever had. They are more like huge balls of shredded potato - definitely house made. There were only a couple on the plate and I didn't eat much. 

In another visit, I got the platter, which comes with two sliders and a side. I got the fries and the veggie slider that is a black bean burger. I got both a little different, with different buns. I like the whole wheat bun the best (better than pretzel) - it was so fresh and delicious! The burger was just ok - the toppings made it better. I hope to try the quinoa one soon - they were out when I wanted it. 

Service was good both times, and food came out fast. I think I will become a regular customer. The other thing I'd love to see is a "build your own" slider option. There are so many varieties that are available - I would love to choose my patty, bun, sauces, and toppings. What can I say, I have discerning tastes.

This restaurant is going on my "Hidden Gems" list. I'd heard of it for years but had shunned it due to my perception of there not being much for me to eat there, as a vegetarian. My good friends Ben and Charleen S recently went and raved about it and encouraged me to go since they do have vegetarian options, so I scheduled our next International Supper Club get together here. 

We came before Christmas and WOW is the inside gorgeous! The room we were in had a huge brick fireplace, woodburning, very cozy and beautiful. This would be a great place for a family reunion, rehearsal dinner, etc. Especially in winter! Our table was so nicely set. Our waiter was on point the entire night. Service was FABULOUS! We wanted for nothing and they handled our part of 14 seamlessly. 

They started by serving us bread - it looked like fairly normal, white bread but it was delicious, along with the yummy butter. I couldn't stop eating it! I ordered the cauliflower schnitzel and the butternut squash soup (which was on their autumn menu, so is no longer being served as it was the last week of it). I also got a side of spaetzle, which I love. The cauliflower came out - YUM! So flavorful and delicious, with a red pepper sauce on the side. The soup was smooth but with potatoes and carrots in it. It was very good. The spaetzle also was super good. I ate almost everything, and I was stuffed! I didn't stick around for dessert since I was getting sick with a cold, but it looked delicious. Next time! And there will definitely be a next time soon.

I wanted to like it. I just didn't. 

It's cute - service was ok - my husband liked his sushi. The veggie spring rolls were pretty good. 

I ordered tempura udon, and selected veggie tempura (other choice: shrimp). It was described as udon noodles in a soy broth. Vegetarian, right?

WRONG. 

It came with something floating in it that looked like a japanese vegetable. I put it in my mouth. It was fish cake. It looked nothing like fish. Nothing in the description said fish.

Shame on me for not asking, but why didn't it say fish? 

They fixed it for me, but I didn't not enjoy what they brought back and ended up not eating it, and I felt ill all night. I haven't eaten meat in 30 years. 

I won't be back.

I was really debating betweeen 1 and 2 stars here. We used the living social Voucher. Even though I was on crutches from a recent knee surgery we were made to try to squeeze through a crowded bar area to a high top table in the back corner. This would be bad enough if there weren't normal open tables right in the front of the restaurant side. I get that they aren't expecting big business from living social customers, but if you are going to sell the voucher at least try to gain repeat business from it. Some people who buy vouchers can actually afford to pay full price for a nice meal, but after our experience I would never spend my money at Malios. Instead of trying to gain repeat business they just nickel and dime you on everything while you are there.

After struggling on one leg through the bar and into a high top table, we were given the pre fixed living social menu, which had very limited choices on it. In spite of the lmited options the restaurant made sure to print on the bottom that the meals actual value was $110 and we should be sure  to tip on that value. Really?? Very tacky. We ordered the fried mozzarella app, which tasted fine, but not much different from one I wold buy at any restaurant or in the frozen food section of the grocery store really. Then I got a very bland bowl of French onion soup, and my husband was given a tiny house salad. I ordered mahi for my entree, which I thought tasted good, and my husband ordered a steak that was overlooked. The entrees did not come with sides, so we ordered the homemade chips for $7, and they tasted like lays potato chips. I was expecting something like the awesome chips from datz.

After our entree was delivered, our server disappeared. We finally flagged her down after waiting about 15 minutes and asked for the dessert that was included in our meal, a slice of key lime pie, to go. We paid our bill and waited, and waited. My husband even stood up. The server came over after about 25 minutes to tell us It would just take a few more minutes to cut our slice of pie, put it in a box, and bring it out. I started maneuvering my crutches back out of the cramped bar area. My husband waited 5 more minutes and finally left without the pie. 30 minutes to cut a slice of pie? Am I missing something here?

After reading my own review I am downgrading this to 1 star. The only positive was the fish. For 2 drinks, some chips, and the tip on top of the full amount which our server also wrote in pen on top of the receipt (again, so tacky!) we paid $45 fo the meal plus $55 for the living social voucher. I would rather eat at outback for half that price. For an upscale restaurant this place really needs to get its act together.

Nowhere can you experience a more diverse bar-going crowd than at McGurks.  Except at an East St. Louis strip club.  That doesn't count, though.  That never counts...because we were never there...ever.

The vast patio at McGurks features a smorgasbord of boat shoes, hair gel, roofies, high heels, and short dresses.  These are the Kings and Queens of college.  Be careful with this group.  They get messy by about 12:30 AM.

The live band/booth area is where you'll find a bit of an older crowd.  A crowd that actually likes to listen to banjos and violins.  However, there is also a cluster of young-ins that are cutting a drunken rug on the dance floor.  This is where people pregame before going to Talaynas.  What's Talaynas?  If you don't know, consider yourself lucky, but also unlucky.

The other parts of the inside area are where you'll find young professionals adorned in business casual wear, a timid group that can't decide if they can handle the patio crowd, and those that just want to leave but their friends are having a good time.

I'm a master of disguise.  I fit in with all of these groups.  
I spiked my hair, said I was 19, and was asked to join a frat on the patio because of my ability to tell Budweiser apart from Bud Light(sidenote: it was a complete guess).  
I put on both a sweater vest and a corduroy jacket and discussed the Irish Potato Famine with a couple of scholars in a booth.
I business suited up and outlined the advantages and disadvantages of forward and trailing P.E. ratios with some of Clayton's finest at the upper bar.

McGurks, much like its Soulard counterpart Molly's, is also one of the largest bars in St. Louis.  It's reminiscent of Willy Wonka's Chocolate Factory.  You get to the tiny little door and you think there can't be much behind there.  Then inexplicably appears a forest of gummy bear trees, a chocolate river, and Gene Wilder signing "Pure Imagination."  
There are 6 different bar areas serving drinks at peak time.  It's as close to utopia as a Pub can get.

Bear with me on this review.  I ate here about 4 weeks ago.  I've been extremely busy sleeping and staring out a window since then.  I have finally set aside the time to write about The Shaved Duck but I'm gonna need a lot of recall here.  Perhaps, Total Recall??

If there is one thing that I remember vividly(besides the rotund stomach I sported on the way out) it is the Smothered Fries.  Holy potatoes, Aquaman!  It's like The Shaved Duck used Inception to figure out that rib meat and cheese sauce over crispy fries is something I dream of often.  

A buddy of mine and I also ordered the Big Jimmy Sampler.  One piece of advice to The Shaved Duck: give 4 ribs instead of 3.  You're just inviting a dog fight for that last rib unless the sampler is meant for three people instead of two.  In that case, my friend and I better get our fat arses inside a gym.

If I'm power ranking the contents of the Big James Sampler, here's how it'd look: 1) Brisket, 2) Pulled Pork, 3) Ribs, 4) Mac N'Cheese, 5) Pulled Chicken

The brisket makes you consider taking genetic science classes in order to understand the cloning process.  You will want to clone the last bite of brisket over and over so that you never run out.
You may be wondering: Mac N'Cheese over Pulled Chicken?  What is this?  The BCS?  The chicken wasn't bad.  The mac attack was just that good.  

The Shaved Duck puts an elegant spin on pigging out on swine.  It may not be the absolute best BBQ but as far as upscale BBQ goes, I can't imagine many places doing it better.

The chicken is a little bit of heaven dipped in batter & deep fried.  It comes out fresh and piping hot and is as juicy as any chicken I've ever had.  

I undersold it with 5 stars. We're talking the Milky Way galaxy here.  I love it so much that there are times I just want to get up and slow dance with this chicken.  On a few occasions I've recited poetry to it.  I took a wing to go and we went to the park and watched the sunset.  We are now "Facebook official".

Great lunch special too: $5.99 for 4 pieces, a side, and a drink.  This place is gonna make me fat(ter).  I'm cool with that.  

There have been many King Edwards throughout history.  I doubt any of them made a bird as good as this Edward does...maaaaybe Edward the Third but I doubt it.

King Edward vs. Popeye vs. Lee vs. the Colonel in a cage match.  Four men enter, one man leaves...Edward is walking out without breaking a sweat.

Ladies and gentlemen, this is how you restaurant.  To everyone else in the business: take notes. Corner Bistro should be a case study in business/restaurant school.  You should have to do a 10 page paper and presentation detailing what you've learned before opening your own place.  

Let's start with the menu.  It's perfect.  They limit the options while still offering a wide variety of popular items.  They don't go crazy like some places and put sushi, duck confit, egg rolls, and pop rocks under "Chef's Favorites". They have a plan. They stick to what they do well: pizza, apps, sandwiches, pasta, & dessert. And no weird "artisan" stuff either. No lamb and lobster pizzas or vegan burgers. Seriously vegans, just give up if you need a burger that bad.

Next, the brick and mortar.  The outside patio and inside are a bit small but they are clean and quaint. They don't pack in as many tables as possible and make you feel uncomfortable. I think we'd all prefer not to sit elbow to elbow with some hipster with a man bun and glasses without lenses talking about his favorite beard creams, whatever the hell that is.

Lastly, the food.  Everything lived up to my expectations.  I had a pizza from Pizzeria Tivoli the night before.  It was very good. I had a slice of my friend's Bistro buffalo chicken pizza. It blew Tivoli's pizza out of the water!! I felt great shame for not coming here the night before to get my pizza. 
I also had the 1/2 pound bistro bacon burger.  I bet by now you can guess I loved it.  I will add the wings were small but they were tasty.  Another friend got the bruschetta. I didn't have any because that is healthy. Gross. She liked it, though.

The best part? The waitress! Who may have been the owner. Such a wonderful woman!  I don't know why but she gave us a free slice of graham cracker cake at the end.  And you know what?  It was one of the best desserts I've ever eaten!!! I want the recipe but I'd be afraid that I'd bake and eat that cake every day and balloon up to 800 pounds.

Most people have deep regret about something from their past.  Maybe about not asking that cute girl or guy out.  Or not switching to a different career.  My deepest regret is not coming here sooner.  It has been in my sights for so long but I just never pulled the trigger. So many wasted meals elsewhere.
Tasty place but the platters were pricey.  The wildcat gyro sandwich was the best. There is decent sitting but will come back for a pita sandwich again.
Decent Indian food on University Drive.  Not super spacious but come over for your favorite Indian food picks.
Enjoyed this beautiful museum.  Take in the one hour collection your that is offered to get a quick glance if museum highlights.   The museum has lots to offer and will leave you inspired.

Very hip and casual restaurant.  Everything was tasty.  Great place to eat, talk, drink and spend out.  
The server wasn't as friendly tonight but maybe they were tired.  But I would recommend this place to all.  Bon appetit.

I've been to The Row several times and have always enjoyed the service, love music, and food! The Hot Chicken is so crispy and perfectly seasoned my boyfriend and I always get it! Try the fried pickles and bacon Mac & Cheese!

Decent food, a good atmosphere, and a great dessert!

I've eaten at Bourbon a few times and have always received friendly service regardless of how busy it may or may not have been.  The food is above the average bar food and everything has a hint of Ne Orleans spice.  The creme brulee earned this place a star by itself!

This place is good for brunch or dinner and also has an decent crowd for the evenings.  However, remember about the $5 cover after 10 PM (at least on Saturdays).

In need of another pho fix and wanting to continue my quest to try every pho place on Washington Ave, I ventured to Nam Phuong.  The beef salad was a great way to start things off, but arrived only a minute or two before our main courses.

Again I went Deluxe Pho, #152, this time only $6.25.  At first, I was disappointed in what I felt was a lack of meat in the pho... until I started to dig in.  I kept being pleasantly surprised by finding more.

Service started out weak but seemed to improve as the meal went on, probably the only negative experience I had at Nam Phuong.  It is highly recommended.

How Casino's like this one is putting Atlantic City out of business is beyond me.  It's relatively new, yet dated and ugly.  Its offering are sub-par, parking is a pain, and  even the Starbucks isn't legit (its just a machine that makes your coffee at prices higher than a typical Starbucks.  The only thing going for VF Casino is how heavily it advertises "Have a Gambling Problem?", probably because you need to have a serious problem if you are coming here...

A $5 cover (after 10PM) with no significant drink specials makes it impossible to get anything more than 3 stars in my book.

On the other hand, it does have an incredible deal on (good) wings on Mondays and seems to have something for everyone.  A decent dance floor with live band upstairs, a smaller dance area down below, and decend amount of sitting at and around the bar.  They also have a great selection of bottle beers.

Forget driving down to South Philly for the best cheesesteak in Philly!  And no need to stand outside Passyunk Ave in the cold either!

Since I'm lucky enough to work five minutes away, I make sure to visit frequently.  Things to remember:

* Limited Seating (especially at lunch)
* Order your steaks from one line, Drinks at the other
* Cash Only

I finally made it to TGKT for brunch and can say it is everything you've heard and more.  Get here early because even the cold and snow didn't stop the crowds.  And while it should go without saying, come hungry because you've gonna want one of everything.

We loved the regular menu, but too many of the specials jumped out on us to avoid.  We ordered the Bahn Mi and Short Rib Frites.  Portions on both were fair and flavors out of this world.  The Bahn Mi sandwich was absolutely the best one I've had outside of QT's in the city.  The pork melted in my mouth and the pickled veggies were mixed in with just the right proportion.  The Short Rib came with two fried eggs on top, a solid pile of meat, and fries that we couldn't stop picking at.  

Between the two of us, we cleaned out plates and decided not to press our luck with desserts.  Next time, I take my own advice and come hungrier.  Those desserts sounded great.  Also, judging from the posts, I think I'll need to grab a drink (or two) next time as well!

An amazing, four and a half-star experience.  I'm not kidding, a few small details landed Zama just below perfection, but high enough on my list that it will be getting another shot at glory soon enough.

JJ and I arrived Saturday evening for dinner.  Since it was snowing, we hoped the lack of reservation might not be a problem (hint: book a reservation).  Luckily, they were able to seat us at the sushi bar quickly.  Turns out, the sushi bar is a great place to sit since you get to see all the menu options come to life.

A little gun shy about a recent chef tasting experience, we decided to make our own tasting experience.  First up, the Kirin Ichiban Braised Short Ribs.  I wondered how I might eat such a dish with chopsticks, however, the meat was so tender that was not a problem.  It was probably my favorite.  Next, a simple Oshinko.  It helped clear our palate and prepare us for item three, the Sufer roll (yellowtail jalapeño roll topped with tuna sashimi, avocado salsa, and crispy rice cracker).  I lied, this roll had to be my favorite.  It was fresh and delicious with a variety of textures which really helped enhance the flavors .  Item four, a refreshing Tuna Usuzukuri, to no surprise, also made its case for my favorite.  It was sliced into 6 pieces for easier enjoyment which ensured eat bite delivered the chef's intentions.

Our last main of the night was the Jose Garces Chirashi.  It is a rice dish with various fish on top. It was good, but not the way to end our night. It just didn't seem well balanced (although the dish itself was setup nicely to split between two).  We also tried three small desserts, since they have a sampler 3x$10 dessert option.  While all enjoyable, none blew me away.  For the complete picture, we had the Yuzu Crème Brulee, Banana Springroll, and Apple Gyoza.  Make sure to ask about the desserts, as the menu is a bit nondescript.

To end where I began, Yay! I'm a fan nearly Woohoo'ing.  I'll be back and recommend you plan a visit as well.

I walked in and this place was packed!  While that is a great sign, it meant a long wait.  Turns out, they were also experiencing issues in the Kitchen, which added to the delay.  By the time my food arrived, I wasn't exactly happy with the situation.

So how did they end up with 4-stars? 

First, sincere and apologetic service.  They were slammed and I was ok with that.  They were not satisfied that our experience was delayed.  That certainly picked them up a notch!

Second, the food was solid.  My order was delicious and the kimchi might have been the best  I've had.  Considering you come to restaurants to eat, it has to be the focus of the review.

I'll be back, hopefully on a quieter night!

For late night food, Spice End gets 6-stars!  Seriously, their offerings are delicious no matter when you get them, but add to that being open until 3 AM!!

Food Quality:  I know I started this review with details about how late they are open.  No, that does not mean its just 'drunk food' that no one would ever enjoy sober.  In fact, I was introduced to Spice End complete sober and amazed by the rolls.  I recommend the Lamb Kabab, but was equally impressed with the Chicken Tikka.  

Food Quantity: A single roll might not fill you up if you've had nothing else to eat, but is certainly enough to put some food back in your system.  I haven't had a platter yet, but they seem to be more sizable.

Price:  Seriously, dirt cheap.  And they take credit.  Oh and check in w/Yelp for a nice discount.

Everything Else: I don't what else you need to know to check this place out.  The Mango Lassi is sweeet!  They have teas and other drinks.  The place is clean (even at 2-3AM) and the staff is friendly.  They have veggie options as well!

I cannot sing and typically dislike Karaoke yet still always manage to have a good time here.

The food is solid and their weekday specials rock.  When it comes to the weekend, check out upstairs and enjoy the show.

I visited Adobe once or twice pre-COVID, but became a regular after we went into lockdown.  

I really feel like their COVID precautions should be the standard.  They have shower curtains between every seat outside (and when indoor dining was allowed they had plastic walls between in table).  They clean and disinfect regularly and have a good system to ensure people know which tables have been treated and went.  The staff all were masks and follow social distancing.

With the track less than a quarter mile away, we usually stop in as a small group (2-4) following our track workout on Tuesday's.  They have a Tuesday night special which is awesome. I've had most of the menu by this point, and recommend the steak fajitas, shrimp tacos, and red & green chicken enchiladas.  A friend of mine lives off the veggie burrito - it is huge and can probably work as two meals.  The best part, free chips and salsa (amazingly good salsa).

The staff is friendly. Prices are reasonable and in the case of 2-for-$35 with a pitcher Tuesday nights more than reasonable. And as a I mentioned, the COVID standards are well implemented.

They have limited outdoor seating and as it is getting colder I'm not sure how much longer we'll go to eat there, but it is our standard post-track.  Hope to see you there.

Average age in this bar is less than 21 years old.  That should tell you something right off the bat.  It gets crowded, everyone seems to want to fight, and the beers are overpriced (plus no Miller Light)!

On the flip side, the DJ is really pretty good on Saturday nights, which makes me wish I could give it a higher rating.

The atmosphere made me feel like I made it to a classy restaurant downtown without the headache of getting downtown... 

Be warned, the food is slightly pricey for Manayunk. However, their "cheap wine" is actually pretty good (@ $12 for a half carafe, it is not a bad deal). The food was good, but the serve put it over the top. Our server Richard was very attentive without being pushy and checked in just enough to make us happy without driving us insane. Worth adding to your tour of Manayunk restaurants!

I wandered down main street Manayunk on a nice fall Friday afternoon in search of a good meal and pleasant atmosphere for a lunch date.  Once I decided on Chabaa, I was not disappointed.  

They began by hitting on the little things, such as a friendly greeting and clean environment, continued to elevate things by taking the time to explain and answer questions, and locked up a solid rating with a great meal.

While I cannot say it was the best Thai I've ever had, it was well prepared, fairly priced, and did not leave me wanting more.  The coconut ice cream, served in a coconut, was a nice dessert to share.

Amazing lunch specials.  Excellent and authentic food.  Just do it!

I'll start with where I started, lunch specials.  For like $8, you get a decent portion of an entree, soup, and an egg roll. Don't worry, the quality is the same as a non-special entree and top notch.  My go to for lunch is the Double Cooked Pork.  It's like slices of perfectly cooked bacon with just the right amount of greens.  To pair, I recommend the hot and sour soup.

Other dishes I've tried include all of their shredded pork options, the fish stew, and the beef and tripe in oil appetizer. They know how to cook pork it seems as those dishes were my favorite. The Fish Stew was also amazing, however, it is a bit spicy.  The best part on the stew is the portion as it overfills a large container and so they also fill another smaller container.  Certainly big enough to share.  I can't rave about the beef and tripe, but wouldn't stop you from ordering it to decide for yourself.

I've only ever gotten take out from Bamboo and look forward to post-COVID days to try them dine in as well.

A certain philly yelper is leaving us, heading south in less than a month.  Before she heads out, she hopes to maximize her time with the diverse food selection philly has to offer.  As such, Thai was on the menu for this evening.

JJ Thai was easily able to accommodate our party of 5. I started with a special app, the trio sampler, which included steak sate, mini crispy duck salad, and a crab and shrimp roll.  For $15, the portions were fair (2 sata, one roll split in half, and a cup size salad).  More importantly, they tasted awesome.  Others at the table got apps as well, but we really didn't share so I can't comment further.

We did, however, share mains enough to judge others. I had the red curry, two had the drunken noodle, one had pad see ew, and one had praram (crispy pork). The red curry was decent, but not a home run.  The noodle dishes certainly took center stage.  I was surprised at the flavor profile differences between the drunk noodle and pad see ew, given they are identical noodle types.  The dishes do indeed make a difference!  The praram was tasty as well.  I'm not saying I wouldn't recommend the curry, just that I'd probably recommend the noodles more.

Throw in great service and the fact that they are a BYO and bam, we have a winner!

The Spirit of Philadelphia earns one star for being able to make a drink strong enough to make me forget their attempts at food. While I'll admit to having a great time on my company cruise, it was in no part due to the SoP offerings. Great friends-coworkers and alcohol on land would have worked just as well at a much lower cost (to the company).

South Coast Deli is always a good go to for sandwiches and salads in the SB area! They have reasonable prices and their portions are huge. They have so many different options to choose from so there is something for everyone. They also have the option of being able to create your own sammie and or salad.

I've tried many different things on the menu and have loved everything that I have! Some of my favorite things on their menu are the mexican caesar salad, the cobb salad, the chipotle chicken club, the phatty sandwich and the caprese sandwich. Everytime I order from here everything's made to order and always is fresh. 

This most recent time I got the chipotle chicken sandwich which was incredible! This sandwich was HUGE, it was triple decker sandwich and way more food than I expected. The chipotle chicken club has turkey, bacon, jack cheese, with chipotle mayo, lettuce, tomato, red onion, and pepperoncinis! It's so delicious and the chipotle mayo gives the sandwich a real kick. 

They have a huge selection of chips and drinks here too! Also if you want to order ahead and pick it up you can online or over the phone. During the lunch rush I would recommend to order ahead so you don't have to wait because the lines here during that time can get super long. Overall this place is one my favorite places in town and I will be back soon to get amazing fresh food soon! :)

Came here last Saturday during their happy hour and had an amazing time with friends! They have happy hour on the weekend's so keep that in mind it's from 3-6pm which is awesome. We got a seat on their patio and they were able to accommodate our large party with no reservation. 
Their patio was so relaxing with an awesome atmosphere and I'm sure at night it would be beautiful too!

We came for the happy hour so all of us ordered our drinks and food off the happy hour menu. They have many different margaritas on their happy hour menu! I tried the house margarita, the cucumber margarita and the pineapple margarita. All of these were super delicious! None of them were too sweet and you couldn't taste the tequila which is good because I hate the taste of tequila in a margarita.

Their happy hour food menu had so many options! They had tacos, nachos, quesadillas, and much more! We ended up all ordering many different things and trying each other's food. I loved the chicken tacos and the veggie quesadilla the best! The chicken tacos were cooked perfectly and had an amazing salsa on it. The veggie quesadilla was packed full of veggies and was so fresh, I loved it! We also ordered some of their guacamole which was delish too.

We had a large party of 7 and our server was very accommodating! They kept checking on us and asking us if we needed anything. They were very helpful and even included the tip in the bill to make it easy to split the bill between all of us at the end. I'm so happy I finally discovered this hidden gem and can't wait to come back for happy hour again! :)

I love the Santa Barbara's Farmers Market! The best thing about this farmers market that there is one every single day of the week so you are able to find one no matter what day it is. I like the one on Tuesday's on State Street and the one on Saturday's on SB & Cota St. 

The market is always clean, not too crowded, and has so many different types of vendors to check out! There are many fruit and veggie vendors. Some of the vendors have the same things but sometimes they have different things from one another. I typically browse the whole market and then go back to get my food! Alot of the fruit vendors give out samples which is great so you have the chance to try the fruit out before you buy it. 

There are also many other vendors besides just fruit and veggie vendors. There is fresh cheese, eggs, bread, pasta, honey, beans, nuts and more! They even have a hummus vendor too! My favorite vendors are the flower vendors. They also have some of the most beautiful flowers in town and great prices too.

Lots of vendors take credit card these days but they also still take cash too! I would recommend bringing your own bag so you don't have to use plastic bags. Sometimes on the street there are people playing music too which is always a nice touch! Overall I recommend this farmers market to anyone in Santa Barbara looking for fresh delicious organic produce, flowers, bread, eggs or any other fresh groceries.

I have come to Finney's many different times and have enjoyed each of my experiences here. They have such a wide variety of things on the menu so everyone is bound to find something that they like here! They also have many different delicious cocktails and beers on tap here. They have local beers as well as other tasty beers for you to try!

Their happy hour is incredible and I highly recommend it! It's from 3-6pm Monday- Friday currently. There is $5 beers on happy hour, as well as some special wines, and cocktails too! The happy hour has chicken and waffle bites, poke tacos, chicken tacos, coconut shrimp and so many more! Everything that I have tried on their happy hour has been super delicious!

I have tried a few of their entrees as well! They have fresh salads such as the cobb salad and the chinese chicken salad! Their burgers are always cooked perfect and very tasty! My favorite is the impossible burger! Even though it's plant based it taste just like meat and I highly recommend it to anyone! The bbq chicken flatbread and the cauliflower tacos are both two of my favorite items on the menu as well! They have many meat, veggie, and even vegan options here making this place the perfect place to bring anyone! 

All of the food I have had here has been tasty and the service has been great too! Sometimes they have a long wait so I would recommend using the Yelp Waitlist feature. On Yelp you can sign up for the waitlist and then from there you can see how long your wait time will be! I usually do this before I leave my house so I don't have to wait as long. Overall I love coming to Finney's and can't wait to come back to grab happy hour soon!

Mesa Burger has some of the best burgers! They are all named after different places in Santa Barbara which I think is such a unique idea. They have some really creative burgers and over time I hope to try them all.

So far I've had the Funk Zone burger, the Montecito burger which were both so delicious! The Funk Zone burger with the bacon, tomatoes, mushrooms, and the egg were was so good! I've never had a fried egg on a burger until I had this one. Now that is my favorite thing to have on a burger! I loved the BBQ sauce on the burger was well. The Montecito burger was incredible too. With the onion ring, goat cheese, and truffle this burger is one of the best I've ever had. Both of the burgers were made fresh as you could tell with each bite how fresh they were. 

I've had the regular fries along with the parmesan & truffle fries and these are both delicious as well! The fries were crispy and cooked just the way I like them. Their milkshakes were delicious too! All of their salads look really good too especially the Southwestern arugula salad. I can't wait to try that soon! 

I love the openness at Mesa Burger. It's nice that the restaurant is open and there is alot of natural light that comes in. I love the patio as well.  They have local beer on tap and lots of sodas to choose from too. They also have free wifi here which is awesome! 

I'm looking forward to coming back to Mesa Burger soon to try one of their salads and get an order of the fries!

Brophy Bros is such a classic place to try in Santa Barbara! It's located on the harbor so the best place to park is in the Santa Barbara harbor parking lot.  With the amazing views, delicious food, fun cocktails and amazing service what else can make this place even better?!

This place can get very crowded so I would recommend to go here on a off day or night or just be prepared to have to wait! The restaurant itself is not that big which is why the wait time can be long but it's worth it!

They have some of the best clam chowder I have ever had here! It comes in a bowl or a cup and they even have an awesome soup/salad combo! They have delicious mussels and clams here! Even the crab cakes and fish and chips are so fresh! I love the crispness on the fish it's so good and not too overpowering. 

This past time we finally decided to the sea bass and wow it was probably the most delicious fish I've ever had! The butter sauce totally made it and I loved it! The fish was very fresh and not fishy at all. I can't wait to come back and to try it again! We also tried the cocktails of la paloma and the mai tai! Both were super delicious!

Overall I also have a great time here! With the freshest food, incredible views, and fancy cocktails this place is a great place to come any day of the week! I can't wait to come back here soon to grab another cup of that incredible creamy clam chowder!

I'm SOOOOO happy this place has opened up in Santa Barbara! I loved it!!!! This place was so delicious, great service, and overall just is a great addition to SB's food scene! 

My friend and I stopped in here last Friday for dinner. I had found this place on Yelp and since it was new thought we should try it! We were seated right away outside at a communal like table which I thought was neat. We got to sit facing state street which was fun. We had to wait a few minutes for our server to come over since it was busy. Once he came over he introduced himself to us and after that we had great service! He told us what he recommended and even brought us the specials list. 

We decided on getting bruschetta for an app and each of us got a pizza to try! I got the arugula prosciutto pizza and my friend got the basic margherita! Our app came out pretty quickly after we had ordered it. It was so fresh with lots of garlic which we both enjoyed!!! As soon as we had finish our app, our pizzas came out!!! They were both delicious!! Full of flavor, perfect amount of toppings, and the crust was cooked perfectly!! Overall 10/10! We even asked for extra olive oil and balsamic to put on our pizza so they brought us three kinds to try which was awesome!

I brought in a bottle of wine so instead of us trying their wine, we had the wine I brought. They charged us a $20 corkage fee which was fine by us since the bottle I bought was a $30 bottle!

Overall I had an amazing experience here and I can't wait to come back to try their pastas or meatballs which is what our server raved about! He also told us they are opening up a Wine Bar next door, which I think would make a great addition to this place. I'm excited to come back here again soon! Thanks for a delicious experience MIZZA!

I love this place!! This is one of my favorite delis because of all of the fresh delicious food I have had from here and the amazing service I get while I'm here! They have so many fresh salads, sandwiches, chips, desserts, wine, special drinks, and so many other things to choose from!

Some of my favorite sandwiches that they have include the pesto chicken, harissa bomb, basil turkey, club metro, and the salami turkey. They can even custom make you a sandwich and you can put whatever you want on it! They have so many veggies and meats to choose from making it a great place to customize a sandwich. The meats and cheeses are freshly cut making their sandwiches even better.

They also have many great salads to choose from too. The chicken salad, the cobb salad, and annie's salad is also super delicious! Everything is so fresh because they make it right when you order it.

My favorite chips are the truffle chips, they are so good! Some of the best desserts include their fresh cookies, and their cheesecake is to die for! They serve their cheesecake with fresh berries which makes it even more delicious. 

They even have a small market where you are able to walk around and shop while you are waiting for your food. In this market they have pasta, sauces, olivos, chips, desserts, wine, and more! I'm looking forward to coming here again soon and trying something new next time! :)

Corazon Cocina is so delicious and I wish I could eat it every day! I love Mexican food, and this place was just so good that I can't get enough. 
I just found out they have axxess card deals for the 2018 axxess and the 2019 axxess so make sure to use yours!

I tried the shrimp quesadilla, chicken taco, and the al pastor taco. Everything was amazing! There were large chunks of shrimp  with flavorful cheese in a perfectly crunchy tortilla for the shrimp quesadilla. The chicken taco was tender and perfect! The al pastor taco was my favorite! :) They also have an amazing salsa bar here which was awesome! They have spicy pineapple that you are able to put onto any of tacos which was my favorite addition!  

The flavors of this place were just so incredible and I loved everything! I can't wait to come back here to try all of the rest of their stuff! :)

I am so happy I finally tried this place and we will definitely be back ASAP. If you are ever in the SB public market try this place! They also have amazing Taco Tuesday deals too! :)

Right when I walked into this spot I fell in love with it!! The vibe of this place is welcoming and positive making me excited to come back already! There is no parking lot for this place but plenty of street parking around which is easy to find. The best thing about this place is there is tons of seating everywhere and LOTS of outlets!! Outlets are a key at a coffee shop and most don't have enough for everyone. Old Town Coffee really did well by putting tons of those in. 

I was greeted by the owners of this place right away with smiles and recommendations. It took me a few minutes to decide what I wanted but I finally made a decision. I decided to get a iced latte and a bagel with cream cheese. Both were really good!! The latte was made to perfection and of course with almond milk which is what I always get. The bagel was toasted perfectly served with cream cheese and was so delicious! 

They have tons of different coffee and tea drink options which is really nice. Old Town Coffee even has a cold case filled with Yerba Mate and other cold drinks. They also have food for purchase including fresh pastries, bagels, and empanadas from Buena Onda which is another awesome local spot. Their back patio area is huge have a huge back patio which has lots of seating spots and even a cornhole set up.

I'm excited to come back here again try some more of their amazing coffee, eat their delicious pastries, and take advantage of that awesome outdoor patio! :) Thanks for the incredible first experience Old Town Coffee, I will be back soon!

This is my new favorite coffee shop in town for many reasons! I used to visit the Caje in IV when I went to UCSB but haven't made my way back there, so I'm so happy they have opened up a location downtown. It's located right next to The Mill on Haley St. Parking is street parking and some of it is only 90 min parking so make sure to set an alarm so you remember to move your car if you plan to stay here for awhile!

Their menu is full of really unique drinks to choose from! I love matcha so I was excited to see that they have a matcha latte on the menu. I ended up ordering the Bella Rose which is a matcha rose latte. It was DELICIOUS! It was my favorite matcha I have ever had and I can't wait to come back to have it to again! It was the perfect amount of sweetness and not watery at all! They have some food on the menu and the avocado toast looks delicious.  

The vibe is very cool! I love the lighting and the rustic modern decor. They have some outlets but not too many so make sure to charge up before you go! The staff here were all very friendly and helpful. I had great service and I can't wait to come back to try another of their amazing drinks!

Yellow Belly is one of my favorite spots in town due to the good food, service, and the outdoor seating! I love this place! I have been here for happy hour, dinner, and breakfast. Each time I have come here I have had delicious food and have enjoyed myself. 

During dinner/happy hour I have had many different items on their menu. I have had their brussel sprouts, pizza, wings, burgers and fries! Everything I've had has been delicious! The brussel sprouts were cooked to the perfect crispness giving them alot of texture which I loved. I loved the sauce on the wings and they even gave us blue cheese dressing to go with them!

The burger was cooked at a medium temperature which was perfect and what I had ask for. The fries were so good! The put garlic and parmesan cheese on them making them just so delicious! The pizza was crispy and cooked perfectly with fresh veggies as the toppings!

The brunch here is always the best! Their mimosas are super fresh and not expensive at all! They even have beers during brunch too which is great! I've had the breakfast sandwich and changed it. I made my eggs scrambled with bacon. It was so good! The bacon was cooked perfectly crispy and had a nice crunch to it. 

Overall I love this place and I can't wait to check out the live music they have here! Thanks Yellow Belly for being great, I can't wait to come back again soon! :)

What I LOVE: watching my ice cream come to life, the flexibility and customization options, the friendly staff, and that this is a family-owned local business. 

What I LIKE: the location is great inside of Dorinda's, the Southcreek area is great for browsing, spending an afternoon, and satisfying my sweet tooth. 

What I DISLIKE: $8 for a cup of ice cream, no matter how generous, is a bit much. Yes, it's more than enough to share. But it isn't something I'd go buy frequently. 

What I HATE: they serve the rolled ice cream with chopsticks and wooden spoons. The chopsticks are silly and fun. The wooden spoons, however, remind me of tongue depressors and unhappy doctor visits. No matter how much ice cream you eat, the gross taste of the wooden spoon is the taste that is left in your mouth at the end of the day. Please change your spoon options, Rolled Mountain Creamery!

If you live in the Mt. Airy section of Philadelphia, Bacio's is an excellent place for a nice dinner out without having to travel far.  This small, unassuming BYOB has an inviting atmosphere, with bright crimson walls, candles on the tables, and an open kitchen.  

The night we went, there were 2 chefs preparing the food, and one person handling service.  

As far as the food, the winner of the evening was the antipasto appetizer.  This dish was very attractively arranged, and included marinated mushrooms, roasted red peppers, beets, asparagus, olives, and an assortment of meats and cheeses.  We ordered the medium sized choice , and it was more than enough for 3 people.  

In general, the portions are very generous at Bacio's.  The menu includes homemade pasta dishes, house specialties which are mostly chicken dishes, and grilled fish, rib-eye, or chicken breast.  Vegetarian items include ravioli (cheese or vegan), meatless meatballs, and eggplant parmigiana.  My pasta dish included silky fettucini, broccoli (somewhat overcooked), and a flavorful white wine sauce.  

Prices for entrees are in the $13-18 range.  

Tiramisu and canolis for dessert were solid, but not memorable.  The coffee reportedly was very good.  

I would not call Bacio's a "destination" restaurant, but if you are close by and would like to go out to eat, it is real asset to have in the neighborhood!

I was taken back to vintage dinning here in Nashville. I can remember as a kid coming to Tin Angel to meet my grandmother for brunches and/or dinners. Where has time gone?!? You wouldn't be able to tell inside Tin Angel. I LOVE their location, atmosphere, vintage Nashville feel! Truly comforting to my feel goods. With all the restaurants in town it was hard for me to decide on a date night "new" place for us to go. I haven't been to Tin Angel as an adult. 

Shock value: I called around 5pm on a Saturday and was able to get a reservation for 7:30...unheard of on a Saturday night in Nashville. (I shouldn't have waited this late to call, but wow, I was impressed with the quick accommodation! Verrrrry friendly hostesses!) 

Our waitress was great! She was attentive but also gave us our space, allowing for a proper date night. I feel as if many others would want to get rid of us as quick as possible. This right here alone will keep my husband and I returning for our date nights! 

What we chose: 
Dirty martinis 
She crab soup
Stuffed mushrooms 
Swordfish, rice pilaf, and brown butter shaved brussels
Filet with blue cheese chunk, potatoes, and mushrooms 
Almond Tarte with Lemon topping along with fresh fruit ( strawberries on top) 

My cons for our evening come with pro's to make up for the mistakes. We waited 15-30 mins for our apps (which were on the house due to the backup, thank you Tin Angel!) We didn't mind, like I said we were enjoying our date night. My brussels were extremely over salted, when I mentioned it to our waitress, freshly sautéed brussels appeared at our table! Great service! I'm not one to ever send something back but this time they were the perfect addition and crunch to go along with my perfectly cooked swordfish and  rice pilaf. 

Ending with our desert...I know, how could we after all the holiday sweets?!? Let's just say I did a bomb ass work out earlier and we were indulging...and I am beyond ecstatic that I decided this. The Almond Lemon tarte was AMAZING! We took one bite and just stared at each other before continuing to chew...the look of yummy! No regrets, if available on the menu for the night, get it!!!! 

Can't wait to have another night out at Tin Angel!

Nashville you better keep this guy around

I had no idea Pork Belly Café existed in Lenox Village. If you don't live there you could easily have no idea like myself. Thank goodness my bother-in-law recommended it to us. Tucked away on the corner, one drive by and you can't miss it. 
We went around lunch time on a Monday. When you walk in you are kindly greeted and welcomed. To your left there are giant chalk boards on the wall with the menu, under that you have their jarred signature sauces and pickles for sale.
From reviews I had read before my visit I found they are known for their Panini's...on a cold winter day, this was what I was going to order. 
I rarely eat pork so I went with the Turkey and Provolone with SUPER slaw and Pesto Aioli on Wheat. I typically don't like warm lettuce but this SUPER slaw was REALLY delicious. As my side I went with the Pesto and Tomato Pasta, which wasn't over powered with Pesto. jus the right amount. 
My husband got the special which is always written on a board behind the open set kitchen...he loved it! 
If you are in the area near Lenox Village please make a point to check out Pork Belly Café...I know we'll be returning customers, loved it!

I have nothing but wonderful things to say about The Row. My fiance and I are getting married in October and hope to have our rehearsal dinner there. They are fairly new and haven't had a rehearsal dinner yet. 

Myself, him, and his mother went during lunch on a wednesday and had a few items. We sat down at the bar. We loved the bar atmosphere to the right, as apposed to the restaurant, both are beautiful.   The friend green tomatoes. topped with homemade pimento cheese. The three pots, this had the pimento cheese spread, a white bean hummus, and some chicken spread (I'm vegetarian so I didn't eat this...but looked yummy) these three pots came with homemade cracker and their in house pickles and pickled red peppers.
