The crackers were somewhat like homemade cheez-its. YUMMY!  Then we had the bbq chicken sweet potato skins (I peeled the chicken off) it was amazing! Ohhh ohh and the biscuits with jam, we picked the red onion chutney and the blackberry. 

EVERYTHING was amazing!!!! 

I highly recommend The Row :) I can only hope they work with us for the rehearsal dinner.

Martin Wine Cellar Metairie is the most piss-poor caterer I have ever used.  We asked that our food be delivered at 9:30am and they didn't show until 11!!!  We had to completely reorganize our meeting agenda to accommodate the lateness.  When they arrived they had forgotten our two crab meat and brie cheesecakes which were supposed to be the centerpieces!  We also ordered the bruschetta and they forgot the crostini so all we had were toppings.  They tried to redeem themselves by bringing crostini and wild mushroom pinwheels (to make up for the cheesecake) about 30 minutes later.  

While the food at Martin Wine Cellar is absolutely delicious, they do not deserve to cater food for trusting patrons.  To put the icing on the cake, I just called to request a receipt for my records and they said they could TRY to get one for me.  You can TRY to get me a receipt for catering I ordered?  I also included that their chafing dishes and ice chest were still here and they told me that I would have to return the items because they were rented.  We have to return items that we had PAID to rent???  This was never stipulated as well as the fact that I have never ordered from a caterer that asked for the customer to return what was rented.  MWC Metairie should be absolutely ashamed to call themselves a caterer.  The food is top-notch but as for the catering aspect - NEVER AGAIN.  Imagine if they had done that to some poor bride and groom on their wedding day!!!

Our server was adept.  That wasn't the problem.  There were pieces of shell in every one of my 6 oysters. Over cooked and tough hamburger.  Salads good, and excellent cupcakes.  Cocktails okay.  My sidecar wasn't the best but at least it was served in a sugar-rimmed martini glass, as requested.  The absolute worst part of the experience was being put in a boring private dining room in back when half the restaurant was empty.   We came for the much touted renovations (and the raw bar). When we arrived at 6pm, the patio was also half empty. The weather was lovely, and I asked to sit there but was told it wasn't possible.  As we left, I asked the hostess about patio seating and she said it was first come, first served.  So why weren't we seated on a half empty patio??  We won't be returning.  The food isn't good enough to compensate for the poor treatment.  Even in the suburbs, there are better options than this for times when one doesn't feel like going to center city. Gee, I miss Ravenna though.  And when I want good, well shucked oysters, I'll go to Little Fish.

TERRIBLE MANAGEMENT.
Made a reservation for six on 3/5/14 over three weeks in advance of our dinner date.  I called day of to confirm our reservation and guess what?!?  I didn't have a reservation because the entire restaurant was rented out for a private party.  

When I make a reservation over the phone, I always repeat the day of the week, the day of the month, and the time back to the hostess since we all know that they aren't often the brightest crayons in the box.  I asked her to search for my name and came up with a reservation for the following day.  Then the manager I spoke to said, "Oh yeah, she's not supposed to be taking reservations" in reference to the hostess who took mind down three weeks previous.  Unfortunately, that doesn't resolve my situation.      

So here we are with no reservation on a Friday night for three couples.  Two of the couples had to get childcare in advance for this date night which is now in limbo.  

Thanks Five Palms - We won't be making another attempt to dine with you.

Met some people here for a Sunday brunch and immediately fell in love with the space. Such gorgeous decor.

Then the love stopped.

Service started slow, but still seemed promising. I forgave this as not all in our party had yet arrived. Unfortunately, it didn't improve.

When making reservations, I had noted a jazz band would be performing during part of our visit. I couldn't see them once I arrived, and couldn't hear them as one should acoustically either. So even though they ended their performance early, it didn't matter anyway from where we were seated.

Not in the mood for breakfast-y foods, I decided to order the Liberty Burger. When it arrived, I was a surprised at how small it was for what I thought was going to cost $13.00. (Think back to Table 3's $5.00 duck burger -- yeah, same size.)
One of my tablemates ordered the same and thought it was too small also.
It tasted wonderful though. When there's no need to add any condiment to a burger, that's a darn good burger. 
The frites weren't exciting at all, but not terrible.

I grew tired of our increasingly lackluster service when my beverage sat empty for a long time. Thankfully there was water available.

What sent me over the edge was the bill. They rang up the wrong beer that was $2.00 more expensive than what had been ordered AND charged $16.00 for the burger! 
Our server agreed to correct the beer mistake (and did), but told me I ordered the double Liberty Burger, not the single. When I challenged him on this, he then said if it's not specified at the time of ordering a "double is assumed, and a double is what you got."
Wow. So observant and classy of him. He didn't deliver any of the food to our table, or consume my burger for me. How the heck does he know what I actually received? 

Many of my fellow diners had issues with their invoices as well; some with additional taxes/fees that no one could account for.

Ah, to top it all off, the parking. Their reservation site indicates you can park next door in the 222 garage for 2.5 hours for only $5.00. Almost $17.00 later, we were driving away. False advertisement. Absolutely ridiculous.

No, the beautiful decor and delicious burger couldn't even save a star for this place.
Nashville has so many other wonderful places that will check all the boxes. 
Skip this one.

I've had a fair share of leftovers from Red's Chinese, but this go 'round I actually made it INTO the restaurant to order my own dishes! Ha.

Just as I don't like Americanized Mexican food, I also don't like Americanized Chinese food - ya know the kind of places I'm talking about...there's one on every street corner. The stuff is disgusting. 
But Red's is NOT that kind of Chinese place. Yes, Americanized, but refined (sorta) and delicious.

The red square will get you there.

The neighborhood isn't the greatest, but inside feels like a warm New Orleans basement that ran into China(town). It's typically stupid busy, but at one point we had the whole place to ourselves on a Wednesday mid-afternoon. I was highly entertained by the beautiful light streaming through the back seating area, just inside the back door leading to the patio.

I don't jump excitedly for pork-anything, but decided to try the Pork Buns [crispy pork belly, kimchi mayo, pickle, cilantro] which were $7 for a small order and $12 for a large. I have no recollection of what convinced me that day (maybe the bao bun?)...I just went for it.
Oh. My. Gosh. They're soooo good. Every element of this dish balances perfectly, and I just had to order another. Of course, with my main dish too, I couldn't eat it all...but I tried!

I opted for Veggie Fried Rice as my main entree [buku veggies, thai basil, chili oil, togarashi] -- $10 for small and $14 for large. Definitely not as good as the Pork Buns. I just didn't love it - I didn't hate it either though. I'm not sure I'd order this again unless I was just having a veg-only kind of day which happens.

That said, I think I want to try the cucumbers next.

So I did something a little crazy....

I steered my vehicle to the Deg Thai truck, and upon approach, thought that maybe I should try something different from my norm tofu basil dish.

I stared at the menu, and the owners made suggestions based off my dietary restrictions...but decided I would just stick with the usual...because it IS so damn good!

I went into Friedman's to shop while my food cooked, and when I arrived back to retrieve, the owners wanted to confirm I was a vegetarian. I smiled as I certainly understand why they would think such...I've only ever ordered vegetarian dishes from their truck.
I explained how I loved vegetarian food, but still a carnivore. They suggested I try the Massaman Beef Curry next time.

Instead, I decided to get both! One for the moment, and one for later!

Jay packaged up the Massaman Beef Curry in preparation to be cooked the following day, and gave instructions on how to prepare properly for the best meal. (Love this dude.)

It was so very good. While the tofu basil is still my favorite, I must proclaim this truck offers the best, and fresh, Thai food in town!

I've never had su h an incredible dining experience. Simply perfect: I cannot see any way that this place, its food, its staff could be any better! The restaurant is immaculatey clean, crisply neat, and very organized. The menu is diverse. There is food (and beer) for every taste, and each member of the staff was exactly the same: warmly hospitable, kind, and sincere as they were explaining the different dishes and foods. 

I ordered the dolsot bibimbap: IT WAS INCREDIBLE! Every bite was packed with delicious, fresh, authentic Korea flavor and the meal filled me up without leaving me feeling sick. The food is fresh, clean, and delicious!  

I could eat here everyday, and I know people who do. I always swore to mysef that I woud never eat Kimchee after smelling it years ago but I had it tonight and it was INCREDIBLE. If you love Korean food, go to this place and you will be blown away. If you DON'T like Korean food or have never tried it (like me before I came here) come here and be amazed by your new favorite restaurant. 

I am a serious foodie and usually don't leave comments, but I want the whole world to know about ths amazng place. Come here with your family, come with your date, come as a birthday party, by yourself, as a lunch appointment for work, all occasions are appropriate. Also, the staff truly treats you like you are family. What a wonderful place. 

Thank you Omoni, for finally giving me the only perfect dining experience I've ever had. You have truly achieved the impossible. I will be back, with lots of friends.

This is probably my favorite Thai restaurant in the city. And I say 'probably' because while I had a great dining experience, it was my first and only time to date. So I'll need to update this review after a few more visits, but if first impressions are lasting, I'll remove the 'probably.'

Food - authentic! And if you want spicy, ask then to crank it up! The appetizers weren't that big of a deal to me, but the noodle entrees.... Mm mm.. The evil jungle princess and Shrimp pad Thai really did it for me. The pad Thai was the perfect blend of spicy and sweet, and the noodles were just the right chewy consistency. The jungle princess was extremely flavorful - so much coconut flavor. My wife had the drunken noodles and it was great as well.  But I got a level 2 spice level, while she got a 3, so I really couldn't eat much of hers. But she loved it.

It is a BYOB, which is always fun, and the dessert options seem very authentic as well. My friend could not stop raving about her cup of coffee after, so I guess I'll be trying that next time!

Both times that I've been here, this place does not disappoint!  Great prices, decent portions, and good flavor. However, I can't review much - both times I got the same exact thing - started off with mussels in red sauce and the grilled calamari, and indulged in the linguini pescatore in red sauce entree. 

Complimentary bread is as expected, and the dip for it is made in-house. Grilled calamari was perfectly grilled, and comes on a bed of spring mix. Squeeze the lemon wedge over it and enjoy!  (If you prefer breaded calamari, look elsewhere; it's not offered here.) The mussels in red sauce are a huge portion, and trust me, you're going to want to dip the complimentary bread in this sauce. The fresh tomato sauce really shines here.

The linguini pescatore is the star of the show. Made with fresh pasta and more seafood than you can hope for, it's the perfect portion amount for you to finish and be satisfied. The presentation and taste are top notch, with fresh tomatoes stewed into the house made red sauce. The linguini has this light/chewy consistency which doesn't taste 'starchy' and just mixed well with the seafood. I've gotten this 2 out of 2 times that I've been here, and will probably continue to get it every time. 

While I never gotten dessert, the complimentary limoncello shot is a great finish to my overstuffed belly and speaks to the authentic Italian experience I remember from overseas. I've met the manager or owner of the restaurant and he is the real deal - from his Italian accent to his passion when describing the specials.

Top off the fact that it's a BYOB and this place rounds out to one of the best restaurants in the area, amongst a sea of chains and pubs.

It's time I update my review. It was already great for me before, but it feels like it's gotten better the more often I go. I frequent this place a lot more now than I did before (got the duke crown!) and it's consistently on point.

While I still do the 3 roll special with every order, I've come around to the Thai food too. The spiciness level can be requested, and it is a hot but addicting burn. I still strongly dislike onions, so I just order the Pad Thai without and it's  fine. Noodles are a good consistency and the squeeze of lime really brings out the flavor!

And the staff. Oh the staff. The service is 5-star here! I'm greeted with a warm smile when I arrive and a genuine farewell when I leave. EVERY TIME. Really good people.

Good food. Good price. Good service.  That's sums it up.

Oh, almost forgot -  BYOB!

Skeptical to write this review, because hidden gems become unhidden once it goes viral. But the food here is too good not to share! 

Yes, it appears to be a hole in the wall. Yes, it is within an apartment complex (lucky tenants!) But if those points don't bother you, you will be in for a decadent brunch your taste buds will go wild for.

We went as a group of 12 (if including babies) for brunch, and we made up probably half the entire restaurant. Yes, this place has a maximum capacity of 20-25 people (I'm no Fire Marshall - just guesstimating). Despite our large group, the staff was very accommodating, attentive, and fun/friendly.

As 12 patrons, we got to try a variety of the menu. The food that really stood out:

 Burgers - I got the breakfast burger which was a hit - made to order inside a brioche bun and let's be honest, anything inside a brioche is yum! Plus, it's fun to say! Brioche, Brioche, Brioche! Ok, not fun to type. Anyways... the burger was accompanied by fresh hand cut fries which also happen to be my favorite type of fries. Quality of this platter is upscale in taste and presentation!

French toasts - decadent is the word I'd use to describe it. Presentation is phenomenal. Fluffy thick slices, syrup oozing down it. We ordered both the plain and Nutella variety - both were excellent and again, top notch with the variety.

Aside from a Sunrise (staple eggs, potato, breakfast meat entree), most of the food had a Latin flare - empanadas, huevos rancheros. All tasted good, but I have no baseline to compare it to as a don't frequent that cuisine.

The burger and fries really shined for me, so I definitely would return for that alone. They seem to offer other burger varieties, which I have no doubt are just as good as the breakfast one.

Quick tips: they only have two high chairs, which was more than I was expecting. We carry our own portable one in the car which we ended up using.

There is no bathroom inside the restaurant itself (again, very small). It is located in the apartment complex - just get a key from Chef Vargas.




Brioche.

Back again since they now have a full selection of hoppy IPA beers.  Yes, Revision appears to be the IPA hop forward specialist in craft brews.  Jeremy has "Reviisioned" and perfected his art in Revision Brewery.  Thank you.  The "Revision IPA" won an award for best IPA locally recently.  I agree.  Good crisp clean tasty IPA.   Revision, you are doing everything right!   Keep up the Hoppy work.
Waiter trying to hard, bug on curtain, 4th dish came out late and too salty....should I say more?

Went with my partner and another couple to bowl and have some drinks last night, and the entire experience was great! Service was wonderful (quick, nice!) at the counter, bar, and on the lanes. Prices are totally reasonable for bowling (it was about $15/person for 2 games + shoes), and it's nice that they charge by the game and not the hour (although that also explains why they don't reserve lanes). We had NO problems getting a lane at 7 pm on a Friday night, and it looked as if there wasn't ever much of a wait - it was busy, but not overly so. 

Cocktails were weak but cheap ($6 for a martini?!?!). Wine list was short, but $26 for a bottle? YES PLEASE. 

And the FOOD! We have already talked about coming back just to eat. $5.50 for tots with cheese, bacon, scallions, sour cream - DELICIOUS. And the $7 pierogie skillet was a little weird but also yummy! Inexpensive and good! Saw the burger on our neighboring lane and will have to try that next time. 

After bowling we played a few games of pool and considered Buck Hunter - a few good arcade games, no waiting! 

An Uber ride from CC is only $10-15, there is plenty of street parking, and the crowd was great - not hipsters (North Bowl), not young professionals/suburbanites (Lucky Strike), but a good mix. We will be back soon!

Our dinner at Vernick Fish was extraordinary, from start to finish. Service, atmosphere, and food were all exceptional, and the night ended up being a very special experience for my partner's birthday. 

Service. From the moment we arrived and the hostess not only greeted us with a smile but wished my partner a happy birthday (those details are so important!), the service was (almost) impeccable. The pace was perfect, our water and wine glasses were never empty, and everyone we interacted with (including the server - not our own - who showed me where the restroom was located) was pleasant and accommodating. The only minor issue was that we could have used more information about some of the plates, especially the oysters. We ordered two different kinds, they came on the same plate, and we had to wait for someone to come over and tell us which was which - and no one told us what the two accompanying sauces were. 

Atmosphere. Beautiful space - more modern, darker, not as "home-y" as Vernick, perfect for a special dinner! There was a good distance between tables. Great music selection and not too loud. A gorgeous place to have a meal. 

Food (this is what you're here for, right?). Incredible. We kept talking about what we would re-order when we return (everything - except there also were 6+ other dishes that we would have loved to try!). Here's the breakdown: 

Bread & Butter. Always a lovely way to start a meal, and Vernick's bread never disappoints! (Complimentary bread is always appreciated nowadays, too.) 

Cape May Salt & Moondancer Oysters. Fresh & delicious. We like the salinity of east coast oysters, and these were excellent! The sauces were also wonderful - the green (cilantro?) I could have eaten with a spoon. 

Scallop Tartare. One of my favorite dishes of the night! Seasoned so well. The chips are wonderful. 

King Oyster Mushrooms. Why go to a seafood restaurant and order a vegetable side? Because they are UNBELIEVABLE. My partner is not a mushroom lover, and this was his favorite dish of the night! Get them! 

Oysters "Philadelphia Style." Oysters + broccoli rabe + provolone + parmesan = weird, you would think. They were outstanding. The brininess of the oysters was a nice surprise in an otherwise very Philly dish.

Swordfish. Now, we never order swordfish because of environmental issues. But we decided to go for it. I was disappointed when it first came out - the cut was thinner and smaller than I expected. But it was cooked perfectly, and the tomatoes and squid garnishes were great accompaniments. 

Tres Leches Cake. Somehow... we saved room for dessert, and having read all the rave reviews we had to try this - it was wonderful. Not too sweet and the perfect end to the meal. (Followed by salt water taffy with the bill - nice touch!) 

Wine list was reasonable, interesting choices, some local. We did not try cocktails, but will next time! 

Greg Vernick has hit the ball of of the park AGAIN. We will be back (for a special meal) as soon as we possibly can. Thanks to everyone for making our special occasion so memorable!

I love love loveeeee GreenHouse. First and foremost, it's right in the heart of New Hope. It's conveniently located in close proximity to all the good stuff. I like the decor and the outside atmosphere...super chill. I went inside to use the bathroom (which is gender neutral), but due to Covid there was no inside dining the day I went, so I obviously couldn't get a good feel. It still looked cute though. 

I love that they have a digital menu. You literally just use your phone camera to scan the code and it pops right up. We decided to have some drinks while here. These were HANDS-DOWN the best margaritas in New Hope. During our trip, we tried margaritas at 4 different places and this one easily took the medal. We tried both the strawberry and the blackberry...equally delish. 

Anyhoo, I wanted to also say how awesome our waiter James was. He was super friendly, attentive, and welcoming. He chatted with us about all the best places to visit in New Hope, which we truly appreciated. Glad we got him during our visit!

PokeMee is a fairly new, up and coming restaurant that resembles Miso Hungry and/or Panda Express/Chipotle for sushi. You start with a base (white rice, sushi rice, brown rice, or salad). I typically do the half and half of sushi rice (because who doesn't like vinegar/sugar based rice)? The next is protein- depending on if you get the 3 or 5 scoop option, you can mix it up with sashimi, such as salmon, tuna, spicy tuna, yellowtail, albacore, and many more delicious options. There are also vegetarian options like edamame, and tofu that you can add as your protein. Any extra protein is $1.50.

Then comes the rest of the symphony. The sauces and toppings. I typically like getting the cucumber, red onions, fish egg/roe, crab meat (for an extra $.50??), ginger, and fried garlic... ohhhhhh yeah. That's the good stuff. 

The 5 scoop portion is more than enough. I was pretty darn full. I also got a mango green tea boba. It wasn't overtly sweet, which is nice, considering I love tea.

The reason why I'd give this place 4/5 stars is the price. It is expensive, especially when you start adding extra toppings and protein. I paid $50+ for 3 meals plus toppings and boba. It adds up quick. Even with the 10% check in offer, we all know that's only tax!

Other than that, I would recommend this place to my friends and fellow yelpers if you're into poké!

I'm not sure I get the hype here. I went in when they weren't too busy and the person handing out cupcakes was very rude to the person in front of me, then tried to cut off my order before I was complete. With the attitude I almost didn't get the additional cupcakes I wanted but I was hosting guests and wanted to have something nice on hand.

The cupcakes themselves are alright. The cake was good and the frosting was very sweet, over the top in my opinion but I'm sure that's how some people like it. I ended up trying the brownie love specialty cupcake which was dry even with a filling inside. I ended up liking the plain chocolate cupcakes much more. The price point was seriously over the top for the quality though. 

There's plenty of other cupcake places in town to deal with overpriced with attitude. It's a shame because with so many combinations I wanted to find the right one for me but I just don't see it happening.

Tl;dr a trendy, Westernized ramen bar with solid food and overpriced drinks

Cheu Noodle Bar turns the traditional ramen bar on its head, opting for offbeat decor, Japanese fusion dishes, and an emphasis on booze to complement your meal. The cramped space has a handful of tables toward the entrance, while the bar and open-kitchen concept stretch all the way back. Opposite the bar, the wall is decorated with graffiti art and squares of uncooked ramen noodles. Bright red walls and colored Christmas lights play up the "dive bar" ambiance. Be warned how popular this Wash West joint gets during prime time -- they do not take reservations during weekend nights. But with every day happy hour, including $5 small bites and drink specials, even off-hours have their perks. Vegetarian, vegan or gluten-free? No problem -- a millennial spot like Cheu has you covered for these dietary restrictions.

I rolled through Cheu happy hour the other day with a friend, and we were seated immediately. While it was but moderately full when we grabbed our table, the space reliably began to fill up as afternoon turned to evening. Service was prompt and friendly, perhaps on the casual side.

I opted for the Miso Ramen, while he ordered the Sichuan Spicy Fat Noodles, and we both tried the mixed drink of the day, Spicy Whiskey. Our drinks were brought out within a few minutes, followed quickly by the food. My ramen was perfect for a rainy day -- the rich meaty-and-garlicky broth set the stage for the well-cooked noodles and the melt-in-your-mouth pork shoulder. I found myself slurping every last drop of broth, which I almost never do with soups. My only concern was with the arugula on the ramen, which I found blasphemously hipster-y, even for Cheu. While the food was remarkable, the drinks fell flat -- there were small, not particularly strong, and served in ice that further diluted the flavor. For $7 (which is the happy hour price, too!), I expected better. Next time I'll definitely aim for a draft over the cocktails.

For $25 each, my buddy and I left satisfied with our tasty soups, albeit a tad hungry. Cheu is definitely a place to try at least once, for the experience if nothing else.

tl;dr an eccentric dog-themed eatery with upscale farm-to-table offerings

As it prides itself on locally sourced and organic eats, White Dog has long been the restaurant within the University City bubble that college kids will pass over for some cheap fast food -- that is, until family comes to town. As was the case for my last visit, as my partner and I joined family for a nice meal in the University City district.

Located on the first floor of converted row homes, White Dog hosts a number of rooms. While the overarching theme is "dog," as evidenced by the offbeat doggie portraits and busts throughout, each room has own vibe like a British pub. In our room, the fireplace and moldings were dwarfed by the colorful abstract portrait painting of various dogs. 

My family ordered oysters for the table, then my partner and I split the two daily specials: a Branzino and a NY Strip Steak. The oysters were fresh and robustly flavored, and my Californian family enjoyed comparing the East Coast sampling to the West Coast ones. The branzino was served skin-on with a citrusy cucumber slaw, atop crispy polenta sticks. on the other side of the plate were dots of vibrant green pesto and golden aioli to dip the fish. This dish culminated into our favorite of the night, tasting uniquely fresh with an interesting texture. The steak, meanwhile, seemed larger than the advertised 8oz, and it was served with roasted potatoes, bell peppers, and onions, then sauced with a plum jus. The meat was cooked perfectly to our rare temperature, but the dish as a whole didn't particularly stand out. 

The food itself might be worth 4 stars, but the service and prices left plenty to be desired. Despite having made a reservation well in advance, we ended up waiting for nearly 20 minutes for our table to be prepared. On top of that, the hostess went out of her way to be snotty when we asked a second time if our table was prepared. And when we finally were escorted to our table, lo and behold, the entire room was empty besides our party. Moreover, Good Dog charges borderline-criminal prices for some of their dishes -- the $40 entrees are probably worth closer to high 20s, low-30s. As I emphasized before, this is a reasonable restaurant to hit up, as long as you're not the one paying.

tl;dr this brunch bistro offers an all-day breakfast menu, featuring Southern comfort food classics with an Israeli twist

Honey's Sit 'N Eat is commonly featured as a top brunch destination in Philly, and for a good reason: tasty dishes, reasonable prices, and BYOB options appeal to Grad Hospital students and families alike. Don't be surprised to wait for 30+ minutes during peak hours on weekends -- Honey's has a cult-like following from those in the neighborhood.

Inside, you are immediately greeted by the hosts at an antique spinning wheel to put down your name. The lime green walls are decorated with rustic knickknacks, and tastefully corroded signs hang from the semifinished plank ceiling. Crude hardwood tables are crammed into the space, and a diner-style bar is situated toward the back.

During this past visit, I arrived with two of my Honey's-naive friends. I decided to go with my tried and true favorite -- the Country Fried Steak and Gravy with Two Eggs, which comes with a potato and toast option. The latke is always an easy choice for potato, but to my dismay, Honey's no longer serves corn muffins. I settled for a biscuit as my bread instead. Service was spotty -- our waiter was friendly, albeit inattentive, and he forgot a handful of items as our food arrived, and my friends' coffee was only topped-off once during our visit. The chicken-friend steak dominated the large plate, and the breading was still crunchy and flavorful despite being doused in gravy. The gravy itself was a star, with a rich flavor to go with both the steak and the sides. The latke was had a crisp shell and cheesy potato within. The eggs were well cooked, and they went quite well with the gravy. The biscuit wasn't the most noteworthy, but the apricot jam at the table sure was -- be sure to douse your toast with the seasonal fruit spreads.

For under $15 a dish, Honey's is among the cheaper brunch options in the city. The dishes are always reliable, and don't sleep on the bottomless La Colombe coffee. Definitely give it a try, and it likely will become a mainstay in your brunch repertoire.

tl;dr a sophisticated take on Southern-comfort food specializing in all things carnivore, but the service was shockingly poor

My friends, fortunately, were able to book a last-minute brunch at Butcher Bar. The atmosphere was exciting, a chic bi-level eatery accented by Southern homeyness. Immediately walking in is a long bar, stocked with plenty of drink options. We were brought through dining areas, decorated with vintage posters and butchershop decor, taking the stairs down into a backyard patio. The patio had a hydraulic awning and heat lamps to make sure its comfortable even for the winter. 

We were surprised, however, when they brought us to a table for 6 when our reservation was for 8. The host sheepishly proceeded to place 2 extra chairs on either end of the table, but it felt too cramped. Afterward, no one greeted us at our table for nearly 15 minutes. When we finally managed to get our waitress's attention, she was unprofessional and rude toward us. Her attitude lasted throughout the remainder of the meal, and it seemed as though she made every effort to ignore us from then on. We even ended up having to ask the manager for water.

Although the service was abysmal, the food was actually quite good! One of my friends and I decided to split two dishes: the Fried Chicken & Waffle Benedict and the Royale with Cheese. The chicken was separate from the waffle benedict on the plate, which ensured that it stayed crispy. My only critique was that the waffle was soggy, but that's what happens when it's left to sit underneath the egg and hollandaise. Meanwhile, the burger was really good. The bun was firm and buttery, while the burger was juicy and flavorful (but perhaps a bit overcooked for my taste). The fries were well-seasoned and served with a delicious BBQ sauce, but I wish they were just a bit crispier. In all, I would recommend giving Butcher Bar a try for the food, but I do not think I will be going back myself.

tl;dr a hip ice creamery in Washington Square West that surprisingly hosts the best happy hour in the city

After having lived in Philly for 5 years, I frequently get asked for restaurant recommendations, so "What's your favorite happy hour spot?" is a common inquiry. While these individuals are almost certainly asking about a cheap spot for a drink at 5PM, my favorite happy hour doesn't serve any alcohol. Or even savory food for that matter. No -- my favorite happy hour is Scoop Deville. Monday through Friday 5PM-7PM, they ask a paltry $4 for any size of their unbeatable ice cream concoctions.

Located just a few blocks west of Washington Square Park, Scoop Deville can feel like trek if you're walking from Rittenhouse. But their cute spot is already a means for going out of your way. The walls are decorated with sugar-themed murals, and the tables sport a ripped-magazine art pattern. The space is long, with just a few spots for seating -- perfect for a rush hour. And if you are wondering whether an ice creamery could ever draw a crowd to make the design worthwhile, then come at 9PM in the summer to see the line straying out the front door (even on weeknights).

And I haven't even gotten to the food. Scoop Deville is known for churning out some adventurous ice cream flavors -- think a bright-green mint-brownie blend in celebration of the Eagles' Super Bowl appearance, and black charcoal vanilla for the Game of Thrones final season. With these in mind, the list of suggested blends is on the tamer side, opting for classic flavors and wide variety mix-ins. But if you ask, the staff are more than happy to customize a suggested blend toward your palate. The ice cream is always high quality, focusing on a light creaminess with rich notes. There's a reason I make a point of going all the way over to this establishment from Rittenhouse -- besides maybe Franklin Fountain (which costs twice as much and is a whole other experience entirely), Scoop Deville is the best dessert spot in the city.

tl;dr in a neighborhood defined to interesting and exciting desserts, this green tea haven remains a step above the competition

Like most of the other Chinatown restaurants, A La Mousse has a colorful neon sign, beckoning you into its brightly lit interior. The aesthetic aims for a cross between industrial and zen garden, accented with wooden walls and metal chairs. Several bar tops and tables for two line the walls of the restaurant, while a camp-like bench sits in the middle for a larger party. The glass display at the back gives you a live glimpse of the various desserts. Grab a table and a server will greet you shortly. Plan your visit to avoid the after-dinner crowd on the weekends. Service is friendly and efficient, but it takes plenty of time to peruse the thick menu containing everything from matcha cakes to bubble tea.

My partner and I decided to split the Green Tea-ra-misu and the Mango Mousse Cake. Within 10 minutes, our server brought out our dishes. Immediately, we were floored by the presentation. The tiramisu was a vibrant green, served within a sake masu. Meanwhile, the mousse cake had a smooth orange shell, crafted in the shape of a mongo and complete a faux leaf.

Too often, the desserts in Chinatown look gorgeous but end up tasting little more than straight sugar. On the other hand,  these desserts lived up to the visual hype. Unlike a traditional tiramisu, the tea-ra-misu had a creaminess more equivalent to a mousse. True to the Italian classic, the tea-ra-misu was not too sweet as to dilute the matcha flavor. The green tea whipped cream and cookie sticks topped off an already solid dessert. For our other dish, cracking open the mango shell revealed the mousse within. It too was light and creamy, not overpoweringly sugary but unmistakably mango. Both dishes were served with a scoop of Chocolate Salted Pretzel ice cream, atop a mound of crushed pretzel, which was as good as any ice creamery in Chinatown.

A La Mousse, while a little on the pricy side (almost cracking $10 per dessert), takes to effort to ensure that their dishes taste just as delicious as they look. The cafe has numerous other exciting items on its menu, so I can't wait until I'm in the area again to try some more.

tl;dr authentic Vietnamese food, big portions, and fresh ingredients, but the prices are higher than many other restaurants in the Chinatown neighborhood

Walking into Vietnam Restaurant, I immediately felt transported back to the air raid shelter I stayed at last time I visited Southeast Asia. Dark wood panels covered the walls, tables, and floors, while the wall light fixtures gave a warm, dim glow. We were greeted immediately by a host, who whisked us past an oak bar counter toward the restaurant seating. Vietnam Restaurant was only moderately busy for Tuesday dinner primetime -- no doubt because it seems like one of the "fancier" Chinatown restaurants. The tables, floor, plates, silverware, glasses, and bathrooms were all shining clean, a huge step up from many of the other surrounding restaurants. There was the hum of restaurant-goer chatter, but I had no trouble hearing my partner at a room-level voice. Service was attentive but not overbearing.

Now for the food. My partner and I split the Pork Claypot and the House Special Vermicelli. At about $15 a pop, these were reasonably priced, but still substantially higher than most Chinatown fare. As I bit into the pork, I immediately lost any regrets I harbored about the price. The buttery meat had a delicious sauce and melted in my mouth, and I had to control myself from eating more than half. As I switched over to the vermicelli, I was impressed by the crunchy freshness of the spring roll -- no microwave meals here. There were several Vietnamese slices of meat to sample in the bowl -- I was all over the grilled pork, while my partner hoarded the beef meatballs to herself. All in all, we left feeling full and satisfied, escaping at just about $30 for the night. This is the only Vietnamese Restaurant I would frequent in the city, besides Vietnam Cafe in West Philly (which has the same owners).

I've been wanting to try Cafe Minh for awhile so when a friend called to join him there, I was all in. Our waitress was warm and helpful. She rattled off a specials list almost as big as the menu. Which was terrible because everything sounded so good I wanted to order it all! 

We started with a sampling of appetizers. First was a special of clam chowder. A modest sized cup of New England style with more broth than cream, so a lighter version that was flavorful and good. The crab watermelon appetizer came next. Fresh herbs, lime, a hint of jalapeño with house made shrimp chips made this refreshing and ample offering our favorite of the night. Last in our appetizers round was the shrimp beggars purses - beautiful homemade dumplings with a rich dipping sauce that hit a perfect balance of sweet, spicy, savory. I need to take my dumpling loving daughter back for these.

For entrees I got the special of lobster tortellini (I couldn't resist) and my friend got a spicy catfish dish. The tortellini was homemade and large with an herbaceous tomato cream sauce. It was topped with fried lobster which I don't think did the lobster justice. Loved the ravioli though and would get again. My friends catfish had a balanced savory sauce that also went great with the ample steamed vegetables it was served with. 

As a surprise, the chef came out to say hi to us and then delivered us to desserts: mango cheesecake which was divine! 
I will definitely be back to bring  my daughter who will be over the moon fir those dumplings!

Went to dinner with a friend who wanted to try Sofia. Open table said there was no availability but we showed up and were able to get a table right away anyway. Our waiter, Josh, was a great guy and very friendly and helpful. I ordered a glass of wine and my friend had a mule to start. We chose to share all our dishes, starting with the kale beet salad. I loved this salad with the crisp frilly kale, a small amount of beets, a slightly sweet vinaigrette and covered in gran pardano snow. 

Our second course was homemade ricotta with sourdough toasts. There was a touch of honey, paprika and an earthy flavor on the toast I couldn't quite place. I asked Josh and he said it was fennel seasoning. Very good and different. 

I have a favorite pasta dish that is hard to get in this area so when I saw it on the menu, I campaigned that it needed to be our entree. It was a homemade pasta (which is a different food group from the dried variety) with pancetta, peas, pea tendrils, a touch of cream, lemon and Parmesan. I really like this slightly modern version and will have to return for it! Craveable! 

My friend wanted dessert and Josh recommended a dish of chocolate hazelnut pudding, marscapone, crushed oreos, and hazelnuts. Excellent! The adult and child in you will rejoice. 

Coming back again soon! Ok

Good bagels, slightly fluffier than I like but great flavors and well done. Humble has great cream cheese flavors and makes generous sandwiches from their bagels. My favorite is the lox with cream cheese, tomato, red onion, sans the capers. This sandwich feeds me for two meals. Fresh juices are a nice touch as well. Go early as they can run out or have long lines on weekends, especially during Mardi Gras.

I've been wanting to try Fharmacy for awhile because I've read the reviews and seen the pics which are all impressive. My son had a craving for good French fries and hamburgers (in that order) and it seemed like the right night for a visit. 

The location is humble but modern on the far side of broad where you don't think to wander often. But...this is a destination burger...and I'm not a even a big burger fan. 

We were greeted warmly when we arrived by a few guys behind the counter. Our waiter was awesome and clearly takes a lot of pride in the place. We asked a few question and he said that if it was our first time, we really needed to try the burgers. He was serious so my son ordered a plain burger medium and I, the Cali burger (Swiss, sautéed mushrooms, guacamole, lettuce, tomato and chipotle aioli) medium at the waiter's suggestion. It took a bit because these burgers are crafted. 

These are 8 ounce burgers made of a combination of house ground chuck, short rib and brisket, a unique choice. The patties are evenly seasoned on the outside with a spice blend that I can't quite identify, but is awesome. Burgers are seared well but not charred on the outside with a moist but not drippy interior. Very flavorful overall. The buns are clearly made for the restaurant, nothing out of a bag here. The texture is perfect, soft but with a slight chew that holds up well with the meat. 

Toppings are very high quality; these are not  everyday sautéed mushrooms, detecting a slight bit of spicy heat. Guacamole was on point, lettuce was a full leaf of red romaine(no iceberg here). 

Fries were perfectly crispy thin but not skinny style, well salted and so good that the boy ordered a second batch. 

House-made dill Spears and bread and butter pickles come on the side and my fries had cheese sauce, pico de gallo and house-made pickled jalapeños that were amazing. 

Fharmacy delivered on all points from service, atmosphere and most importantly,  a perfect burger. We will be back...repeatedly.

I've been to Tsunami several times but this last trip was my favorite. I've been doing keto so chose low carb options of the truffle salmon sashimi and roasted brussel sprouts. 

The salmon was fresh and good but the star of my lunch was the brussel sprouts. They were not Asian at all but perfect roasted and crispy with spicy sweet slivers of sausage and sprinkled with Parmesan. So good! Crazy good!

Stopped in for breakfast prior to heading to the airport. We had coffee and split the Cajun omelet with hot sausage, onions, peppers and cheese. It comes with hash browns or grits and toast. The grill was down so we had to swap out our hash browns for grits. Hard having a diner with a non working grill! 
Still, we had a good breakfast and I'm sure better and cheaper than the airport.

I've paused in writing a review of Lillette because my experience was wonderful yet terrible. Lillette is lovely and peaceful in its decor and elegance. The food is amazing with great care to let simple high quality ingredients sing - try the crab claws with mango butter, simple perfection. On my visit I had the cruddo of the day which was a beautiful Alaskan salmon - my favorite! A few slices in I bit down on something hard, thinking it was a bone. It ended up being a gnarled piece of steel wire which cut the end of my tongue a slight bit. We called over the waitress who was more mortified than apologetic. They brought me a new plate and I found another twisted piece of metal in the fish, feeling so fortunate I had not swallowed it. Can you imagine what that would have done?! We called over the waitress again rather uncomfortably and her horror was clear. This place is used to perfection and they did not handle well having something go wrong, quite frankly more worried about their lack of perfection than my well being. The manager came over and apologized. Our dinner, an anniversary celebration, was very good but a bit awkward from the experience. We were cool about it and they comped us dessert. They later came and told us the wires had come from a brush used to scale the fish, and that the fish had been discarded. In retrospect, I think the staff handled it poorly. It wasn't an issue of poor preparation but safety which could have had horrible consequences. It was a mistake and mistakes happen to good places. But, the staff under reacted. They should have comped our whole meal and even urged us to give them a second try. As a manager, I would have handled it differently. In fairness, the meal was exquisite otherwise but my experience was tarnished. I could have walked away impressed with their conscientiousness and care, but...I did not. I doubt this experience would happen again, but I haven't found myself wanting to revisit this restaurant. They had an opportunity to make a fan if handled with a touch more grace, but ended by letting us leave not feeling valued. A miss.

I'm fond of Outback's blue cheese chopped salad, a combination of chopped romaine, blue cheese, pecans, thin crunchy noodles and a slightly sweet vinegerette. This location has improved in the past year or so and I've been here a handful of times for lunch special or steak. The wedge salad and loaded baked potato are worthwhile sides, and we all love the pumpernickel bread they serve complimentary to the table. Service has been solid here too the past year. They were a little bit weak in past years but have upped their game and are much more consistent.

This is one of my favorite lunchtime sushi places because it's close to my work and they have fresh ingredients and interesting  sushi combinations. Their specialty rolls are very large, much bigger than most places and are filled with fish and proteins with very little rice. No skimping here! This isn't the prettiest place but the staff is efficient and the food is great. 

The New Zealand salmon is something special and worth a try. Also, the smoked salmon sushi is some of the best I've ever had, large, rich and lightly smoked. Really good! 

The chefs here have lots of unique rolls. This is a favorite place.

Updated review: visited tonight and waited for over ten minutes and was not at all acknowledged by either of the two men working. One was wholly focused on flirting with the girl he was waiting on. Her ice cream was started before we walked in and after over 10 minutes hers was still not done. This means our 4 orders would have taken over 40 minutes to make. The other man was cleaning up in back and never came out though he saw us waiting and looked at us several times. We left without ordering. 



My little one had an ice cream craving and Freezy Street turned out to be the closest place open. We are still figuring out our new neighborhood. It was a busy Saturday night and the line was long but the place and clean and bright with ample seating. It's $6.99 for a cup with toppings. You choose your inserts ( fresh strawberries for me, Oreo for the boy ).

I love how much you can customize your pizza with fresh ingredients, multiple cheeses, tasty sauce choices and toppings. You can have it anyway you want at blaze- add a double crust, have a salad, pile  either with anything you want. Be as creative as you want and they will indulge your whims. I'm not a fan of a chain, but I like Blaze's products that are simple, fresh and done your way.

I took a small team for a special celebration work lunch at Fleming's yesterday. There were 5 of us. The whole experience (with exception of the clumsy valet guy) was exceptional. Service was kind, abundant yet subtle. With the rainy day we started with soup, some had French opinion and others the lobster bisque. Both were very good but the French onion seemed the standout favorite. Four of us had the lunch special which comes with choice of salad, choice of steaks or salmon and half a side (still a large and shareable amount). The salads are large and very good. We had Caesar and wedge salads (not the only options). The wedge was so large that we each had half and took the rest to go. Both salads were covered in high end ingredients, very fresh with delectable dressings. The bread service of warm sourdough rolls with spreads (one and onion, red wine spread and the other a butter, ricotta spread) was refilled several times for us. 

Our steaks were high quality, cooked exactly as asked, tender and flavorful. The filets were served on a smattering of wonderful sautéed mushrooms and drizzled with a mild, thin blue cheese sauce. The strip steak had Brussels sprouts and a side of glaze. One of our party had the seafood Cobb salad with large shrimp and crab, and an abundance of other toppings like egg, blue cheese and glazed nuts.

Everything was excellent with the whole lunch exceeding expectations and my people feeling very pampered - which was the whole point. Service, again, was wonderful. I highly recommend. I read earlier reviews from when they first opened that seemed unimpressive but I experienced that they have worked out the kinks and are performing very well.

We ordered  Franklin Street Burger which is half pound black Angus burger, smoked brisket, pork belly, and applewood smoked bacon topped with Sweet Baby Ray's Barbecue Sauce and melted cheddar cheese, served on a Kaiser roll. Quite delicious! It's not a boring burger at all. The side of seasoned shoestring French fries was also good.  I loved their inside and outside sitting area, friendly services, good food. This is a very nice eatery and bar at Tampa downtown.

This place was new so we gave it a try. I signed up with their e -club so I received a coupon for a free pepperoni pizza. We had the ribeye steak, the salmon, chicken wing and pizza. They all tasted good. Some entrée came with two choice of side dishes. We had the chili - yum, yum. The side salad was my top favorite- big portion, fresh, crunchy vegetable and topping, the vinaigrette dressing was excellent. It was the best side salad I've ever had. Sweet potato fry was also very good, the seasoning was specially designed, tasty. The steak was  perfectly grilled and got good flavor. The pizza was good even the edge of crust got herb flavor. The raspberry chipotle chicken wings were fried to crunchy and the sauce was delicious. The service was as good as any professional chain restaurant. Food was served fast and fresh. The ambience was like sport bar and yet friendly to lady, children and seniors. Their pricing was reasonable. Monday and Tuesday got special discount price for  Burger & Pizza. I was impressed by their chef's skills and designed recipe -  even the ordinary Wing, Pizza & Salad stood out from their peers. This was my new top favorite restaurant in Wesley Chapel area.

Fudge yeah! Shout out to my current Yelp fave, Que N for recommending this place for brunch during my recent visit to NOLA! 

H & I decided that we would try all new places to eat & drink this go around so I contacted Que for some recs cuz you know, she's in NOLA every other week. ;) So I sent a message & got a quick reply w/lots of recs. While our dinners were already decided I wanted a brunch place because H & I usually just grab something on the go (bagel or beignet) for our starter meal of the day. I wanted something unique, something local & boy howdy did we hit the jackpot. 

Stanley was convenient to our hotel so we moseyed on over. It looked busy but what do you know, they had a table available for two! I had already perused the menu earlier so I knew what I wanted, Eggs Stanley which is eggs benedict with cornmeal crusted oysters fried to perfection. H opted for the Stanley Classis - scrambled eggs, smoked bacon, potatoes & toast. I ordered the Mega Mosa (cuz you know, I don't do anything half-assed). The Mega Mosa magically appeared & looked like my kinda mimosa, lots of champagne with a drop of orange juice. 

Our plates arrived & we immediately dug in. Hands down the best poached egg experience. I just love the oozy-goozy goodness of a runny yolk. The English muffin was crisp topped with Canadian bacon, poached eggs hollandaise, fried oysters & what really made this dish outstanding was the green onion. Funny how something so simple like a few chopped green onions can do. Mmmmm, mmmmm! H said he wasn't in the mood for fried oysters but I made him take a bite & he immediately changed his tune & got plate envy. I was nice enough to let him "clean" up my plate with his toast. (H did mention his plate was served barely warm but I still stand by my 5 stars).

Service was nice & quick, the place clean & hopping. Yep, definitely will be back for brunch the next time I'm in NOLA cuz I want to try the Eggs Stella which is similar to the Eggs Stanley but with fried soft shelled crab in lieu of the oysters.

Who is the owner here? Food is alright, but man... talk about bad customer service. We just had a business meeting here and we felt unwelcomed, it almost seemed like we were an annoyance to the employees. The server was nice, just a bit inexperienced. The rest of them seem to feel like they're too good for the job they are doing and are only there for looks. The hostess was nice too. It all reflects bad to the owner and the type of customer service training he provides for the employees,  or lack thereof.

Come during 3 PM to 6 PM!!!! Really. Come during that time frame. I don't care if it's too late for lunch and too early for dinner. Just come!!!!

It's happy hour time everyday during those time. Ever..y..dayyyyyy!!! And what you get for messing up your internal clock for eating? 50 cents oysters.  I had $1 oyster happy hours before but never 50 cents. And not just some cheap oysters, but NOLA's famous crazy meaty P&J oysters. Look at my photo of it. Just look. I have never seen one meatier than these at this size. If you like thinner style oysters, these might not be for you.

And if you want it cooked instead of raw, they have the same thing for $6 for half a dozen fried ones.  I didn't have any of those because I ordered 2 dozen raw oysters for just myself. As an afterthought, I should have ordered less raw just to at least try out the fried but I liked the raw one too much.

Oh yea. They also have half priced drinks during happy hours too but why would you care about that right?

Of course I couldn't just live on raw oysters alone so I started with a small cup of gumbo and because so many mentioned it, I fought internally between their famous burger and what some said was the best Shrimp and Grits around the area. The Shrimp and Grits won out just because it was more of a local food where a burger, no matter how good, is everywhere.

I would pass on the gumbo. 3 stars. Good but there are better around the French Quarters.

The Shrimp and Grits was amazing. The Shrimp was tender. The grits was buttery smooth. There is a nice slightly charred cheesy shell on top of the sauce which I didn't get at the other place. I would say this is my second favorite Shrimp and Grits so far. Just be aware this one is with a slight french twist as per the kind of higher end restaurant that it was so it's less traditional but not far off. 4.5 stars

The staff was amazingly attentive and friendly. The atmosphere as mentioned was slightly higher end but not to the point of feeling snobby. You could walk in with your casual clothes as long as you look decent.

This was probably my best deal during my whole trip. And a delicious one at that.

Mango is my favorite fruit and I have been dying to come here. To my surprise this is a sit down dessert place. So if you're not planning on paying for service/tip steer clear. My boyfriend and I came here around 7:30 PM on a Friday night, not too crowded and we were seated right away.
I ordered A1 which was mango ice cream with tapioca and pomelo. My boyfriend got the green tea Sunday with jelly. I would have given this place 5 stars but I'm knocking off a star because they ran out of mango ice cream. How can your name be mango mango and you don't have mango ice cream. I ended up substituting with vanilla ice cream.
I loved mine except for the fact that the pomelo was super sour, not ripe at all so I had to avoid eating it. My boyfriend liked his as well except that there was too much jelly that it was overpowering the green tea. 
Hopefully next time I come back here they will have mango ice cream.

I haven't been here and years and was not disappointed, the quality and service is still going steady. My boyfriend and I arrived at around 6 PM on a Friday and we did not have to wait for a table. We opted in for just all you can eat hot pot which was $24.99 pp.
Our waiter was super attentive with when to refill our water our our soup base. He also checked in to see if we wanted to order more food. 
However, when we were ready for our check which was around 7:00 PM and the place was more busy, the service was lacking. It took about 15 minutes for us to get the check and have them process and bring it back. Definitely coming back on off hours again.

Impressions can be slightly deceiving at Saints house, the quality, the atmosophere, the food and especially the rum all have a way of subtly sneaking up on you.

The atmosphere is nice and low key (nothing that will blow you away). The service is all friendly, laid back and very knowledgeable. The list of rum is extensive. Once we finally made our selections and ordered the drinks, then the saint started to shine.

The hurricane was the most impressive of the drinks with its tall curvy glass and bush of herbs sprouting out. The other drinks were modest in appearance but very good quality. I got the Banks 5 island rum and enjoyed that it wasn't overly sweet but a good, well balanced, stiff drink. 

Once drinks were in order, we made our food selections with the scallop & mahi with mango ceviche, stew del mar and tostones.

The ceviche was my favorite dish. Very well executed with tender and moist fish/scallops and a pop of mango and citrus. It was well balanced, not overly fishy or acidic. It was served with taro chips which were just plain addictive. It was one of those dishes that got better and better as I took more scoops. 

The tostones (batter fried plantians) had an almost meat like texture and were nothing like the plantian chips I had in mind. The were very hearty but still tender. It was served with "banana ketchup" (think mashed banana chutney) which was only so-so. Maybe next time I'll ask to substitute for the mango salsa which looked good at other tables. 

The stew del mar was a very simple curry dish. The fish was well cooked and it was a very fresh tasting, but a bit too bland for me. Maybe I am just to accustom to tangy Thai style curries, but we weren't all that thrilled with this dish. that is until we started to dip the tostones in the curry which gave both a boost of flavor. 

We ended by sharing a dark and stormy with an English rum. Best dark and stormy I've ever had.

I hate to sound like a snob, but I'm very disappointed in the high reviews this place has.  Either Indy doesn't know good Ramen, or people are just overly hype about a new place opening up.

This place does NOT have good ramen.  Please keep in mind that I consider the only true ramen to be Tonkatsu, and that is what this review is based on.  I did not try their Miso or Shoyu ramen so I cannot comment on them.

Tonkatsu is supposed to be a velvety broth, that almost feels like cream.   This broth was watery and felt like it was made in an hour or two, versus what is supposed to take 8+ hours to melt down from pork bones.  They took a cheap, flavorless, quick way out, and it shows.  Secondly, Chasu, or pork belly that goes into the soup, was hardly pork belly, it was the texture of roast beef, with spots of unchewable meat that I had to discard.  Lastly, the egg!  A staple of ramen is a softboiled egg.  You want this to break apart and spill out almost like a gel.  This was half hard boiled, half raw as it came out.  Like what the hell?  You can get a commercial sous vide for about $400 and throw in 20-30 eggs in there with the shell and cook them a perfect soft boil....there is no excuse to mess this up in a ramen place.

Last but not least, the price.  $15 for a bowl of ramen in Indy is beyond absurd.  The best ramen shops in the country cost that much (if you can't tell, I consider myself a ramen connoisseur).  This ramen is a $7 at BEST..and even then...I'd rather go somewhere else.

It seems Indianapolis will have to wait even longer for a ramen place to open up and actually do it right, because right now...everyone has failed.


Sorely disappointed by this place.

Yikes.

It isn't often I re-review a place and the rating goes down.  This place has been going lower and lower on my chart, and frankly...there isn't much more room on this chart for it to dip further.

This past visit, (which is my 3rd and I believe final) I was once again disappointed by their food menu selections which were marred by high prices and uncreative choices.  My friend ordered the Pimento Grilled Cheese which, although being 9 dollars, was exactly what you thought it would be.  Velveeta cheese with Pimentos spread on 2 Texas toast bread slices.  While that sandwich would be great during the great depression, we are a bit more advanced than that today.

The drink menu, did have some creative options, and I did enjoy a $10 cocktail I ordered there.  I can't complain to much about a $10 cocktail as I pay for them at Libertine (a much better version of this place) quite often.  When a cocktail is good, it is worth $10.  That being said, my girlfriend ordered one of the cocktails but did not like it.  The server, instead of asking what else she could get her, or how to fix it, simply didn't seem to care.  One of our other friends at the table said "maybe you could add a splash of soda to the drink" in which the server nodded and said it would be a good idea.  My girlfriend agreed and the server disappeared only to come back with an open soda bottle (6 ounces) and set it on the table.  When the bill finally came, we nearly choked.  Not only was the cocktail that she didn't like $10 as I mentioned above, but the server charged us $4 for the splash of soda my girlfriend used in her drink to make it bearable.

I couldn't believe it. I asked the server about it, and she said they do not have soda in the fountain gun at the bar so this is all she could do.  I asked her if it ever crossed her mind to let her customers, who already don't enjoy a drink and are trying to salvage it with soda, know that a tiny bottle of soda water was $4.  She simply said, "I thought you knew, my mistake" and walked off.  We waited to see if she would remove it from the bill but she did not. I truly was disgusted with the service here.  I feel the drinks alone could keep this place at a higher ranking, but the service and food bring it back down to 1 star.

3 times was not a charm, I've written this place off.  Goodbye Thunderbird.


**Update on this review**  I have been contacted by the owner of Thunderbird with an apology which I respect dearly.  It clarified some issues and alerted me that new training has been done with the staff to prevent this in the future.  I have agreed that we will come back again to give Thunderbird another chance.  I have not yet had a chance to go back, but I will definitely do that and re-re-review.

When I went to eat here, I didn't have very high expectations because I had heard it was very overpriced, and there wasn't great service.  My expectations were correct.

When we got there, the hostesses didn't even know the table numbers so they had to stand there for 15 minutes trying to figure out where they were taking my friend and I.  When we finally got seated, it took our server 15 minutes to come and greet us.  When she did, she took our order and we didn't see much of her for the rest of the night.

The manager brought us our food after giving it to the wrong table (He didn't know his own table numbers either).  The only good thing about it was that it came out in a timely manner.

There was one server in the entire restaurant that was hustling her butt off, and we pulled her aside, told her she was doing an amazing job with her tables, and wished she was out server.  We asked for her name (which was Holly), and I will be sure that I ask for her every time I go.

We gave good feedback for Holly to the manager on our way out, and he just nodded.  Didn't say anything, didn't say sorry for the bad experience, and didn't ask who our server was to give her the feedback.  He didn't seem like someone who could handle customer service issues, and didn't seem to know how to run a business.

I wouldn't recommend eating there, but if you want good crab nachos Joe's is the place to go!

Yes, it's located inside of a resort. Yes, the prices are going to be more than your average sports bar. There, now you know that ahead of time. I for one haven't been impressed by many bars and restaurants in Nashville, so this five-star review is somewhat of a rarity for the area. 

I've pretty much dined and drank at every single place in the Gaylord and I must say, Fuse is my favorite. It's located near the convention center area, in the Magnolia, so it's always easy for me to find, again a rarity in the Gaylord. It's in the same area as Jack Daniels and the Irish bar, so this entire area of the Gaylord reminds me of sports/pub bar, adult only area. Don't get me wrong, of course, there are kids at each place just not as many like in the Delta area. Side note: parking is validated.

Everything that I've ordered is huge. The burger is not only big but cooked to perfection. The chicken quesadilla seemed way overpriced, but it was the largest quesadilla I've ever had (and it comes with guacamole, sour cream, and salsa).

If you're a bourbon fan, try the Gaylord private selections. They have Makers Mark and Knob Creek... private selections!

Ok Brett, you win! This was place was a hit. Even though I'm not a sushi expert, or a sushi consumer in general, I'm always open to trying the local hotspot experiences.

Located in the Ybor area, you apparently have to park and pay in the garage. The area in general is kick ass and I wish I could've explored a bit longer.

I always get a bit nervous when I'm not in charge of staking out the menu or my order ahead of time, so I played it safe and ordered the lunch special, which consisted of two rolls and a choice of salad or soup. I went with the salad. This time I didn't even ask for my dressing on the side. It was excellent! My sushi rolls may not have been exotic, but they were within my comfort zone... California and Mexican rolls. They were safe and simple. The wasabi was perfect!

The other three rolls at the table were excellent too, although I couldn't quote what they were (I wasn't allowed to look at the ingredients listed on the menu). Thank God for those who make you step out of your comfort zone.

Very good!  

We might have been among the youngest people here, but we were not going to let that deter us from trying this place out.  I had heard for years that I needed to check into this place, so we finally got around to doing so yesterday.

We came on a Sunday.  Upon entering, we were asked if we had reservations, to which we stated we did not.  That wasn't a problem, and they seated us shortly after.  We did come kind of during odd hours though say 3:30ish.  The staff was all dressed up.  We were in sweatshirts and jeans.  It was a little intimidating.  Most of the patrons there were dressed nicely in addition to the well-dressed staff.  

Nevertheless, we prevailed.  We ordered the family-style chicken dinner.  We both got the creamy onion soup.  It was somewhat like French onion soup, but it didn't have cheese, and it was, well, creamy.  It was very good.  I prefer French onion, but this was still a tasty take on that.  Along with our meal came rolls, apple butter, butter, corn, mashed potatoes, chicken gravy, and green beans.  All were very good.  The chicken was simply divine.  Mmmmmm!  Nice, crispy, and just a touch salty.

We finished off our meals with sundaes (which were included with the dinner).  We had our choice of ice cream as well as our choice of sauces to put on the ice cream.

This restaurant is located in what looks like a big ol' historic house.  It is somewhat oddly laid out.  Also, they make the poor women who serve you wear what I consider to be silly-looking uniforms.  It would be nice if what they wore went along with the nice suits and ties that the men wore. 

The food and service were both great.  The place is just a wee bit quirky.

I really wanted to like this place. I'm vegan and I want to see vegan restaurants succeed. But I was pretty disappointed by the experience. 

My boyfriend and I were attending a play at the Walnut and gave ourselves two hours to eat. The service was so slow at this restaurant that we got to our seats at the theater just as the curtain rose -- literally! At Charlie's, we had a table all the way in the back, where servers were preparing checks and doing other things, and the restroom was immediately beyond that little area. We sat there with dirty dishes for so long, no check, the clock ticking away, and servers who were less that six feet from us just being idle. So that was pretty frustrating. When we did get someone's attention, we mentioned we had to go, and they check was brought promptly. Maybe slow service is part of the scene here?

The drinks. The cocktails are $12. Don't order the Five Year Plan because it's served in a short glass on the rocks and it's loaded with peaches and mint (I think?) so the actual liquid is like one or two sips. I felt truly ripped off! The draft and bottled beer is really not worth mentioning -- they offer a handful and none were interesting. 

The food. We ordered the Maryland crab cakes. They dish consists of two little patties on mini rolls and they were good, very oniony though, but fine. Then we ordered the mini hot dogs, and they were fine. Then the chickpea fries, which come with garlic aoili. That was probably my favorite dish. But to be honest, our bill was $125 (including tip) and we both left hungry.

I'm not saying I don't recommend this place -- you should go if you know what to expect, and that would be alarmingly overpriced food and drink and slow service. Also, it's a really small space, so the tables are very close together. It didn't bother me, but if you need a lot of privacy, you'd most likely feel uncomfortable.

Like others have mentioned, this restaurant is very dark. It has sort of a weird vibe because there are lights that sort of rotate around and light projected onto a dark curtain -- not sure what was up with that. But it would be "I can't see at all" dark, then a light would turn toward you for a few seconds, then go away. It seems like the owners are going for a specific feel here, maybe nightclub? It felt amateur, though, and annoying! 

Don't go here expecting something on the same level as Vedge. I think Charlie's needs to lay off the gimmicks, lighten the place up, make the service more efficient, and ease up on the cost of the cocktails in order to attract diners who would turn into repeat customers. It sounds like I just described Vedge here. Maybe just go to Vedge and skip this place. For now.
Annoyed I even wasted my time walking over there to find out its an hour and a half wait for an overpriced pizza. I'll stick to Rustica.... at least they take phone orders

During COVID-19 I had take out.  Way too expensive for take out pasta and really small portion sizes.  Great example is the garlic bread were two small slices.   I wasn't super impressed buy the dishes or recipes also.  Pretty disappointed overall.  I had heard great things but the entire experience was really underwhelming.

Had the portions or prices reflected a Covid take out situation and not a person going yoBYOB at there Restaurant dining I might give it another star.

Don't go here if you need a cup of coffee.  Go here if you WANT a cup of COFFEE.

Fanfreakingtastic.  I dont drink fancy stuff.  I like black coffee.  I hate flavored coffee.   I just want plain black coffee.  This place is a super tiny shop that you are only going to go to if you really like coffee.  They have about 6-7 different countries represented by 2-3 diff companies.  The coffee descriptions on the bags were intense and misleading. But after having had the Bolivian it was spot on.  The descriptions are all something like "apricote, black roasted cherry, chocolate.. ".  That is kinda the stuff I do not like but when my cup was awesome and very subtle.  You can tell it is not a standard cup but it is not overwhelming.  It is really good.

The place is small so the line can reach out the door. Be prepared to get it to go because there is no where really to sit.  It is poor over coffee and only one person working so be prepared to wait.  Good coffee takes time.  I normally enjoy sitting and people watching but it is so small you have to go back out into the qrtr and people watch while on the move.

After all this time, I can't believe I have not reviewed Ni Hao Tea! The reviews pretty much this place up. The teas are excellent, premium quality, fresh made boba and so many favor choices! It's literally the best of everything! Ni Hao opened just a couple month before the pandemic started and they've really made through these tough times with amazing service And constant communication with their customers. They are now open for walk in orders, you can still order online. Not sure when they plan to re-open their indoor seating area but surely they'll update us on Instagram. My favorite drinks are the Tiger milk boba tea and the taro root smoothie. The taro root is cooked fresh and it's so good! You can choose your level of sweetness for the drinks which I appreciate big time. I always got for the lowest amount. Ni hao is the perfect treat. Support women- owned, Asian- owned biz!

Fast casual in some pretty fancy digs. This location is extra chic! Grab a menu and order at the counter. The menu is the same as the Mercado San Agustin location. Much more seating indoors and out. My top picks are the carne asada salad, taquitos, and the tocino burro. Much more comfortable at this location.

Simplicity for the win! Anello- with its small menu delivers in every category. Three pizzas, a rotating veg and three desserts make the entire menu. Plus only two choices for toppings- prosciutto or fennel sausage. And there is usually a special pizza. In a world with so many choices and requests for substitutions- this is a concept that I highly welcome and hope other will enjoy. Simple ingredients that are fresh and speak for themselves. Chef Scotty knows what he's doing and he does it incredibly well. And he's humble and welcoming to all. Anello is cozy- seating only about 32 seats or so. Reservations only for large groups- so you can expect a wait most nights. My suggestion if there is a wait is to grab a beer at crooked tooth or a drink at Royal Room while you're waiting. They'll call or text you. If you love a traditional thin ItalIan pizza this is the best.

It's been almost two years since I wrote my first review and really, it should've been 5-stars then (but I was holding off for a full meal!) Renee and Steve are 5-stars alone. There couldn't possibly be a more dedicated and awesome couple running a business together. Love them! These cinco estrellas are also for the lovely staff and of course the  fresh and quality delicious food. It's like eating a homemade meal. The spinach dip is still the BEST in town. It's so delicious, ordering it to share is a little stressful for me. The tostadas- you simply can't go wrong with these- both the black bean tostada and the hummus tostada are equally good- topped with fresh and crisp ingredients. Lasagna in general isn't one of my favorites, but Renee's chicken and pesto lasagna is a game changer. Creamy layers of cheese, pesto and marinara with free-range chicken. Order it.
The pizza here is a no brainer- but I hadn't tried the Thai Curry pizza until recently and the vegan version of it is off the charts. Coconut red curry sauce in place of regular old tomato sauce makes this pie badass and the crunch form the cashews and sweetness from the pineapple make this the most unique pie in town. Vegan or not, this pizza is not to be missed. 
As others have noted, ROO is a small and intimate space, so make sure to make a reservation, as this place gets packed early! Go there for a fresh and thoughtful meal!

A solid neighborhood bar doing it up, craft cocktail style. It's intimate, cozy with a midcentury modern feel. A small and limited menu of super light bites comprised of mixed nuts and a cheese plate is available too. Service is friendly and fun, but can get a little slow when the place is busy. I don' think they intended to have table service, but I highly recommend they have servers available for that, as the bar can get tied up leaving folks sitting at tables inside and out, with a bit of a wait. Cocktails are high quality and highly creative. Sidecar is a welcome addition to the cocktail scene sans attitude.

Eating in is always a treat but takeout in a rainy day is great too! The Grill Sampler Plate really hit the spot and makes for a perfect item to share.
