It comes with lamb kifta, chicken shish tawook, chicken shawarma, yummy rice, green beans, mixed greens and that extra garlicky sauce. So super yummy!
All this goodness for $14 bucks. Add an order of hummus and extra pita to the order and you're all set. We also love the Zayna fries, but they tend to get soggy for takeout.

Best burros in town! I love Barista del barrio and I miss the days when you could call them and place an order for pick up. They don't answer their phone anymore, but that's because they are super busy making 5-star burritos! Other love their coffee drinks- which I haven't tried. I'm personally not into frappe style drinks, but if you are, consider trying theirs! 

Back to the burros: If you like Chorizo, I think theirs is among some of the best in town. It's perfectly spiced. My favorite it the breakfast burrito with bacon, eggs and potatoes. The potatoes are thinly sliced, gratin style, so good! The best part is that they grill the burritos and they use really good flour tortillas.

Do know: Parking can be tricky. This place gets busy but they try to serve fast. Get there early. Sometimes they run out of key ingredients like potatoes. I love this place so much and clearly so does everyone else!

I'm a fan all the way. Falora is small yet stylish. The ambiance is warm and a rad record player with super crisp sound sits on the window sill.  I loved it. The beautiful Italian wood burning oven sets the tone in many ways, but so do the community tables and the awesome back wall that serves as storage for the fire wood. I came in on a Monday night and sat at the bar. It was one of the funnest solo dining experiences yet. The staff (Sam, Kerry and Izzy) was extremely friendly and sweet as can be. I love to ask questions about the menu and this team had all the answers and recommendations too! Lately, I've felt like every where I go staff is poorly trained, they don't know the menu. I had the exact opposite experience here. Not only did they have the answers, they were enthusiastic about the food and have actually tried the food on the menu. I ordered the kale salad, the margherita pizza and finished with a very good macchiato. The kale salad is literally exploding with flavor....quite a bit of it. Kale, artichokes, sun dried tomato and olives. The portion is easily fit for two or as a entree salad. I ate less than half and took the rest home, as I also wanted to save room for my pie. The margherita was thin crust as it should be, the sauce was bright and tangy. A little on the salty side for my palate, but that could easily be me since I don't use very much salt in general. The pizza was super tasty. And they use an entire ball of fresh Mozzarella! Great quality ingredients. The entire meal was super fresh and clean just as you would expect given Ari's other establishments. They also try to support local producers and vendors as much as possible which is always wonderful to see and worth the price, in my opinion. For me, it's refreshing to have a bite to eat that's simple and straight forward, as the Italians do in Italy. I waited to come to allow Falora to settle in a newbie in town. And my experience was fantastic. I look forward to more pizza nights here, next time with a glass of vino!

Holy salsa and tortilla heaven! This review is long over due, but it a total must. These cinco estrellas are really for the salsa and tortillas, while the food is tasty, it's not quite as good as just the tortillas and salsa, but perhaps I don't order the right things. If you're on the search for the best handmade flour tortillas in town, come here. The best tacos I've had at other restaurants in town have always been served with an Anita Street Market tortilla. This is a MUST for any Tucsonan. I love waiting in line and watching all the fresh orders of tortillas come out for customers. Yes, there is usually a wait...because they will make you a fresh batch of tortillas to take home. It's a thing of beauty. And the salsa...damn it's spicy! The red salsa is entirely chiltepin based! Every spicy bite is oh so very worth it. So, do yourself a favor and visit Anita.

47 Scott is the quintessential cozy neighborhood spot and it's about time for an update!  After all my visits, I've officially concluded that my favorite meal is to order a bunch of appetizers and share with friends. The crusty bread with olive oil is a must. And for a dollar and order, it's the best dollar you'll ever spend. Your evening will be complete with an order of:  stack of grilled cheese, seared scallops, kale salad, eggplant caprese and the mac and cheese. We were a gluttonous bunch, so we had two orders of the grilled cheese. We were also a lucky bunch- as we were  given an extra order of the scallops on the house, since the dish is plated with three scallops (we were a foursome), how thoughtful! Did I mention we ordered two bottles of wine too? All of that and the bill was super reasonable. At 47 Scott, you're sure to be greeted by owner, Travis or one of their lovely hosts/hostesses. The service is always attentive and welcoming and that really just completes the entire experience.

Tumerico is one of my favorites for a fresh and healthy meal. I'm personally not a vegetarian but I'm always in the pursuit of finding places that serves of honest, simple and fresh food. Tumerico does this extremely well and with a Smile! The menu rotates so just go there with an open mind and know that your going to have a nourishing, delicious meal!

Covid take out seems to be a lot of misses. You can count on vivace for consistency, that's for sure! We called in for a 6pm. pick up.- three entrees- the eggplant, stuffed pork chop and shrimp. Everything was as good as it would have been for dine in. The staff brought out food out curbside which was highly appreciated.

I love this spot. I come here at least three times a month or more. Yamato stands out on numerous levels. Serving traditional fare, the sushi menu is small and simple, as it should be. Nigiri portions are appropriately small, rolls are bite size and the fish is fresh. I recommend sitting at the sushi bar and chatting it up with Chef Noboru. In fact, he welcomes us to place our orders verbally, one at a time; a rarity at sushi bars these days. As others have noted, he's always there and is the only person manning the bar, so don't expect fast food here. I'll agree with others that the sushi is pricey, but we Always enjoy everything We eat.  Some of our go to items are hamachi Nigiri, maguro (tuna), Toro ( tuna belly $20), a yellow tail roll, spicy tuna hand roll and a sea weed salad. Typically we share one large beer and sale our bill was close is around $70. I'm  a stickler for quality and stay away from any "all you can eat" sushi joints, as I find they compromise on quality. Yamato delivers on both quality and tradition. We're regular fixtures at Yamato and intend on keeping or tradition for many year to come. Yamato has been around for over twenty years. His wife teaches traditional Japanese dance in the sushi bar on Saturdays too. Go there for an un-Americanized    experience. Order nigiri and sashimi. The ramen is quite tasty too. And revel in the fact the the owner has hosted the sushi bar day in and day out all by himself for 20+ years. That's dedication! Chef Noburo is the sweetest soul.

If you're a Tucson local and have never been to the Arizona Inn, I strongly suggest you stop in, especially during this time of year, the gardens are in full bloom, it's gorgeous. AZ Inn is spread over fourteen acres in midtown Tucson and as I mentioned, the grounds are  covered in gardens, fountains, flowers and perfectly manicured lawns. Built in the 1930's, it still maintains its classic and elegant charm. I'm not sure if it is still operated by the Greenway family, but regardless it was or has been a family owned operation for over eighty years. Did you know it's listed on the National Register of Historic Places?

I also love stopping in during the holidays to admire their beautiful decorations. The library (where you can enjoy hight tea) is extra cozy with roaring fire place and the massive tree they decorate. Really, the Arizona Inn is worth a visit at any time of year. 

I can't really speak to the rooms, since it's been a number of years since I've stayed over night. But from what I recall, they are spacious and very classic in decor. 

The pool area is fabulous. It's not too large but definitely comfortable and probably one of my favorite pool settings in Tucson. Every step you take at the Arizona Inn offers a feeling of stepping back into a dazzling and gracious era. The best part? Their free ice cream sundae bar from 5pm-9pm! For your entertainment, there is also a ping-pong table, tennis court and croquet lawn on the property.

Although the Audubon Bar is typically frequented by elderly folk, I still love coming here one in a while for a glass of champagne. They have a live pianist nightly and the they're open until midnight. 

The Arizona Inn loses its fifth star for the food. They operate on such a high level of quality and service at this place, but the food could use some improvement. While the menu is very classic fine dining continental fare, for the price, there should be a wow factor. Perhaps they have difficulty maintaining a consistent chef on staff. I prefer to stop in for lunch out on the patio or the Audubon bar. Again, the food here is pricey, but I come here for the overall experience of enjoying a leisurely lunch in a gorgeous setting. On my last visit, my dad treated me to lunch and we both enjoyed the Shrimp Salad with Avocado. It was tossed with marinated tomatoes, bacon, corn, edamame with spinach and arugula in a lime-cilantro vinaigrette. It was super tasty and refreshing, but the $19.00 price tag reminds you at the you are definitely dining at a hotel restaurant.

Regardless, this little piece of history that we have in our backyards remains high on my list.

There's no question that this place is a little sketchy sketch on the outside...and while the interior is no gem either and little to no English is spoken here, and the kitchen is separated with a curtain, and both times I've been our server has been a minor and placing an order here is like picking a number out of a hat, and the most descriptive words on the menu are "three shredded stuff,"  I'm intrigued. This is not your typical Americanized joint. Is it fast? Yes, but that's as American as it gets. Portions are definitely generous and you won't find sweet and sour chicken on this menu...unless I read it wrong. Yelpers in the know of the legit Chinese food directed me CPH. I wouldn't have made it through my first experience without their guidance! 30 shrimp/pork dumplings, 1 pork bun, and 1 order or fried rice later, I got a good taste of MSG free Chinese Cuisine. While China Pasta House literally is a noodle house with most dishes resembling Pho or Udon dishes you can also enjoy Century Eggs, Gruel, rice dishes, Hot Pot and more. The noodle dishes are really soups and portions are huge and spicy here mean spicy, like a level ten spicy. While fellow yelpers broke a sweat over their noodle dishes I peacefully enjoyed my fried rice and Pork Bun. I'd never seen anything like it! So if you love spicy food then this place is for you. You're bound to run into Chinese students and families at this spot. For sure check out the the specials as they feature several soups that are on the regular menu and it's a good way to taste something new and not commit to full-sized entree.  
-If you're not super familiar with Chinese food, it's ok! I'm not either....read the Yelp reviews first!

Rollie's Patio is a-ok and a welcome addition to the scene in town. This cozy taqueria is family run-100%. I love seeing the owner, Wife and their young daughter all working together, greeting customers and just being welcoming all! We ordered the Rollie's with red sauce, the flat enchilada with shrimp and the special quesadilla, Bbq chicken. I found the enchiladas to be more like a flat gordita. The shrimp were served cold (which I don't think was the intent). Overall I didn't love this dish. The sauce was a little on the bland side and the enchiladas were hard to eat. My husband enjoyed his Rollie's. The bbq quesadilla was a little too sweet for our taste. We're glad we checked it out. We may be back to try out a cochito ice cream Sandwich.

Brand new and off to a good start over all! The space has been updated and is quite large with two seating areas- bar and a separate dining room with tons of tables. When I dined it was late afternoon and quiet so I can't speak to whether or not it will be loud when busy. The servers were very attentive and knowledgeable on the menu items which is great to see so early into an opening. We took their recommendation and started with the al pastor cheese crisp. It's quite large for two people- so definitely something that can ordered to share! I  ordered the fideo soup which is Mexican style noodle soup. The broth was zesty! I really enjoyed it. I supplemented my order with a rajas taco which was also good. Served on a corn tortilla. My friend and fellow yelp elite, James G ordered the eggless Chile relleno which was served with culichi sauce and stuffed with shrimp. The Chile had a nice crunch to it and the sauce was good but lacked the richness and texture I love about culichi sauce. Chinito Gordo offers a fairly standard Mexican menu so I was missing the "twist" part that others so enthusiastically have commented on. They have a full bar with wine, beer and cocktails. While they have fun names for their cocktails,  I'm missed the actual twist on the classics. Overall the meal was good. I look forward to exploring more of the menu!

It's been a Hot minute since my last visit and now that things are opening back up and more people are vaccinated I was ready to explore downtown eats hub is as good as ever and now under the new management of former Isabella's ice cream owner Kristel,  things are going smoothly. Their artisan ice creams and vegan sorbets are handcrafted in  Small Batches. They create 30+ flavors each week...and rotate them between the parlor and the HUB restaurant. The shop is super cute. Small. There was proper distancing in place and they also have a pick up window. Lola like the flavors are a mix of the original HUB and flavors brought in by Kristel- such as honey lavender! We enjoyed small cup which allot for two scoops and one ice cream sandwich. We devoured everything! The staff member was super nice and informative. I ordered the Java Bean and honey comb as my two scoops and they were divine! It wasn't too rich or overly sweet- it was just right!

Everytime I consider purchasing a birthday cake/pie elsewhere, I always come back to Village Bakehouse. Their pastries and baked goods are always a hit. You can pop in anytime during business hours and surely you will find something you will love. From cookies to muffins, danish, croissants, fruit tarts, lemon bars, and more. They bake fresh pies daily. You might even luck out with a whole cake on a whim. But with 24 hours notice, you should be able to secure a cake or pie that is on their menu. The cherry on top: they  serve breakfast all day!

Maru just spiced up the Westside! This place is not solely a ramen shop. Maru aims to share traditional Japanese culture through their menu. While they have a variety of ramen options ( tonkotsu, shoyu, tantan and miso) they also offer Udon noodles, curry and an array of appetizers. There are several kinks that need to be ironed out for Maru to be a four or five star experience due to factors such as the general confusion people experience in the ordering process. There definitely needs to be more signage around how to order. Perhaps placing a large sign up front with a"how-to" description.  From a food standpoint, Maru is a four, simply because the timing of your arrival will really dictate the quality of your experience. But the food is good! So keep on reading this review for tips on how to navigate Maru.

-Maru is order at that counter, but a server brings you your food.
-Head up the the front where the appetizer/hot bar is located. That's where the process begins.
-The appetizers bar offers a variety of items such as onigiri, tempura, egg rolls, gyoza, katsu, etc.  As mentioned, if you arrive during a busy time the bar may not be fully stocked. BUT, what they don't tell you is that if there is an item not currently on the bar, you can still order it. They will cook it for you. They are constantly replenishing the bar, so again, it's a timing thing. But all items can be ordered. 
-From the hot bar just grab the items you want. They are all labeled. The next step is the cash register where you can place your order for your noodles or non-appetizer items.
-Before you sit down, head to the toppings bar!
-Also not mentioned anywhere, they do have beer, we just didn't see a drink menu when we were there. They have soft drinks as well as other Japanese softs drinks and tea.

Highlights:
The tantan ramen was our favorite. Spicy, but not overwhelming. Rich broth and just super delicious. The katsu and gyoza were also very good.

The staff at Maru are super friendly and helpful. So, just ask questions if you're unsure on what to order!

Alright Tucson, there is some major magic going on on the corner of Wetmore and Flowing Wells. It's kind of a drive for most of us, but who wouldn't make the effort for a taste of some of the most succulent Sonoran food offerings in the OP? PLUS, the magicians cooking up all this deliciousness are doing it out of a food truck! These guys hail from Ciudad Obregon (which is where my mother is from) and not only are they serving all kinds of tasty treats in a timely fashion, at reasonable prices, but they also include one of the BEST complimentary condiment bars in T-Town. You can load up on fresh cucumber, shredded lettuce, pickled red onions, pico de gallo, cilantro, onion, guacamole, salsas....and the list goes on!

I've had the luxury of enjoying the Sonoran hot-dog, served on a fluffy toasted bun and loaded with beans, bacon, tomatoes and onion..YUM

If you haven't tried their Lorenzas do it! A Lorenza is a corn tortilla that is baked/fried so its kind of like a tostada, but its served with melted cheese and any meat of your choice. Then you can garnish it any which way you want!

Their carne asada torta was pretty darned tasty too.

There is plenty of seating if you want to show this place to a group of friends. 

I am definitely not surprised that Rachel Ray listed Aqui con el Nene on her Tasty Travels show.

Don't miss out on this place Yelper friends!

Covid update:

I've dined at za'atar before COVID19 and enjoyed a number of meals and plenty of if their fresh baked pastries and bread! Meals were always flavorful and fresh, service super friendly and and iced mint tea is glorious. 

During covid they have closed the dining room and are operating as takeout Only.  We called and placed our order over the phone. Our fold was ready to go upon arrival. We went in and paid and were out in less than 5 minutes. They've set I'm the entry way to be the pickup area. As the dining room is roped off and totally closed. They are also not baking any bread as far as we know. But call and ask to make sure! Gyro plate and chicken shawarma with a side of baba ghanoush is our favorite! #supportlocal

A great concept from the Charro Vida family. The perfect marriage between vegan eating and healthful menu items for us omnivores. The guacamole-hummus served with plantains and chips is tasty. Although on the small side for sharing. The vegan mini chimis well received at the dinner table. We also ordered the street tacos with carne asada. Taco salad, Chile relleno and a vida bowl. Overall, everything was good and healthful. Our server was very friendly. We'd return for lunch some time soon for for sure!

Villa Peru had long been on my list of places to try.  I know the space really well from the previous restaurant. So, I opted for take out, because it's a little too snug for indoor dining for my comfort level. 

I placed my order online on a Saturday evening for a 6:30pm pick up. When I arrived to pick up, the order had not been started. According to the hostess, they stop accepting online orders after 6pm. Two issues with this: 
1. I placed the order at 5:45ish pm
2. It is not stated anywhere on their website that they stop taking online orders at 6pm. In fact, they should not only state that somewhere but also turn online ordering off. That's honestly really bad for business.

Additionally, the hostess said it would be 15 minutes, which ended up being closer to 40 minutes. 

The place was packed. I'm torn about this rating. The food was simple and uniquely flavored. I ordered the half chicken, quinoa salad and the salpicon de pollo. The chicken was on the salty side for my taste. I'm sticking to a three because I know it's been rough for businesses to get back on their feet with the re-opening, but I will likely not return for now.
I really dig this place. I don't eat burgers too often, but when I'm craving something fast and fresh this is my top pick. And it's locally owned too!

Since the huge loss of the Bistro Zin.....I know, it's been a few years, but I still consider it a great loss, I would have to say that Wildflower is the runner up on my list of Sam Fox restaurants in Tucson. I don't dine here too often, but over the last year all my meals have been quite pleasant. Although I don't think Sam Fox food is anything life changing or revolutionary, I do greatly appreciate their consistency in good food and  customer service. On my most recent visit I enjoyed a delicious salad. It was loaded with all kinds of crisp veggies and beautiful colors; bright orange and yellow carrots, almonds, cranberries, and mixed greens. This salad  was the perfect reminder that a great salad does exist in Tucson. This time I was extra disciplined and didn't load up on their ciabatta bread and sundried tomato butter. That butter is dangerously tasty. I've devoured a loaf of bread on many occasions, it's so hard to turn down all that complimentary deliciousness!  Wildfolower seems to change their menu somewhat frequently, so at this point I don't have a regular item I tend to order. For dinner, I tend to order fish because they usually have good specials. In addition to consistently tasty fare and creative cocktails, the service remains the solid Sam Fox service we'v all grown accustomed to. Service tends to be more important on my list than delicious food, because, life changing moments of deliciousness are rare, but great service isn't that hard to provide, but so many people blow in that department. So good food with great service goes a long way, so in my book, this place has earned its 5 stars for nailing the basics: providing good food and service.

You'll find The Parish in an indistinct strip center off of Oracle Rd. It seems to be  our first and only Southern fusion gastropub that's pleasing palates all over Tucson. The atmosphere is funky and the interior is somewhat mixed, but somehow it works. The drinks are creative and bold and pretty much EVERYTHING on the menu has a major kick to it. I think the peeps at The Parish are doing things right for sure. They have fun with the menu and with the flavors. This style of food, however, is not my personal favorite and not really something I could eat on a regular basis. The bacon popcorn is second to none. Holy bacon bits. It's delicious. I couldn't stop eating it. I've never had southern cuisine, so I have nothing to compare it to, but diners at our table, who have traveled to New Orleans many times, were pleased.

Major major brownie points for the design. I love driving down Broadway and seeing the hustle and bustle through the large open windows. Penca got the aesthetics down for sure, thanks to FORS design. While we prefer to sit at the bar and watch the bartenders in action, any seat in the house is good. I'm not entirely sold on the food yet, but overall I enjoy coming here. The cocktails are solid, the wine list, although oddly mapped, is nice and the ambience is fantastic. Their tequila selection is worth a visit alone. I appreciate that the menu steers away from the heavy Sonoran cuisine that we're accustomed to, but there's a number of items that I think could use some extra attention. So here ya go: the red salsa, although made fresh, lacks spice and depth almost to the point that it tastes like tomato sauce. Every time I come here, I have the hopes that they've made the simple fix, but no. The guacamole. Please add some seasoning. I hate to point out basic things, but I'm only doing so because I care and I really think this place is rad. I'm Mexican and I think Tucsonans whether they are Mexican or not have eaten enough Mexican food to know what a legit salsa and guacamole tastes like and a place like this is no exception. So, I hope that with a little closer attention, they will make this fix. The tacos are good. The tortillas are freshly made per order. Of all the meat choices, the Guajolote is the best. I've decided it's their signature item. I'm not a fan of tilapia ever, so after trying them once, I decided that's not the taco for me. The carne asada was also good. Another pointer to the staff. For some reason, the rice and beans have arrived at room temperature on more than one visit. Either the food is sitting at the kitchen window for too long or the kitchen isn't heating properly. Portions for rice and beans are a little scant. For $14 dollars a plate I'm sure you can spare a few more spoonfuls on the plate. The farmers salad is my favorite dish here. The combination of jicama, avocado and pepitas is perfect. I'd like to see a little more than a pinch of the queso fresco, but I'd have to say that this is the best salad I've had in the downtown area. And now you can add a protein. Add some carne asada and you're good to go! 

While Penca hasn't won me over with what is meant to be Mexico City cuisine, I do appreciate the concept, the simple menu, the fresh tortillas and the stellar bar. I look forward to checking out their breakfast too.

I've eaten at the original Scottsdale location several years ago and enjoyed it very much. I finally  made it to the Tucson location, although this time for takeout, due to COVID. The dining room is open, but I have stuck with takeout during the pandemic. We place our order over the phone, although it looks like you can order from Yelp as well! For our group of four people we ordered the Yogurt & Cucumber Dip (Mast O khiar)-
Homemade yogurt with chopped cucumber and mint. Shirazi Salad-
Diced tomatoes, onions, cucumbers, and chopped parsley with fresh lime, lemon juice and olive oil dressing. And the Tour of Persia platter which is a 
combination of barg, cornish, koobideh and gheymeh bademjan served with Zereshk polo and Basmati rice. The menu states is serves three people but it more than enough food  for four people. We had leftovers for the following day. The food was packaged and sealed very well. Everything traveled well in the car and was still warm when we got home. The house-made flat bread is one of those items that is best enjoyed dining at Persian Room. The combination of the fresh herbs (cilantro, basil, mint), raw onion and butter is so unique and really good! I look forward to enjoying that in the near future. 

If you're comfortable with dining inside, it appeared that they had a lot of spacing between tables. For takeout, we only had to wait a few minutes for our food. Everyone we encountered was very pleasant and friendly.  5-stars for great customer service and food!

Looking back at my first review for EXO, they really are a five star coffee shop. What they are doing here in the Old Pueblo is comprable to any solid roaster in Portland or Seattle. EXO knows what's up. They are quality driven in every way as far as beans go. 

So I'll break it down for you with a few of my useful tips:

1. They roast their own beans in site and you can smell it down the street. Smells rich like caramel. No burnt beans here!

2.Best Cold Brew in town. Don't even need sugar. Order a Toddy.

3. Shop is beautiful. Plenty of work space. They play excellent music. 

4. Doug knows and cares about his product. He's humble and is always willing to answer any of your coffee questions. Thanks to Doug, we've worked in mastering the pour over and making our own Toddy at home!

5. EXCELLENT coffee sans attitude.

I welcome Diablo Burger to Tucson with open arms! I advise people to read their menu carefully. They are actually quite thorough and clear about their mission and the what to expect from their beef. Just read the menu! Their efforts to support local are no joke and they've got quite the history. So, I'm willing to pay the price for local product that's ecologically sound. Additionally, they donate 1% of their sales to local environmental organizations who are approved 1% for the planet partners.  

The hamburgers served on English Muffins are quite tasty and very satisfying. I did not find the portion size to be an issue. It was plenty of food including their delectable fries seasoned with herbs de provence. Those are probably some of the best hand cut fries I've had. Although, my boyfriend and I couldn't help but notice that his basket of fries was a bunch of small pieces. He called it "fry dust." So to the folks at Diablo Burger, might I suggest checking the fries before serving? Other than that, they tasted awesome!

As far as the burgers go. Yep, the meat is super lean and not the fatty, crazy juicy stuff that we're used to, but their still tasty. I went with the Marylyn which is basically a cheese burger (your choice of two cheeses). I went with sharp cheddar. The burger is served with lettuce, tomato and a pickle. I enjoyed my burger with some mustard and two sides: the DB sauce and the hatch chile mayo. Thank you to the server who brought out generous samples of the sauces for us! Both were delish and added fun flavor to my burger. We ordered our burgers as suggested on the menu, and they were definitely pink. But we're cool with it. The texture of the beef is wildly different than your typical feedlot cow. It's a little more dense and I can definitely see how ordering it medium or medium well would compromise the meat. It's so lean, that it would literally dry out. Leave your fears of pink beef at the door and order your burger as is. It's worth it. We also enjoyed the garden salad with balsamic vin, and it was a prefect starter. 

Service was timely and friendly, but I would have liked to see some management on the floor greeting people and engaging with customers considering they're newbies in town. I look forward to more DB visits!

Kingfisher is a Tucson classic and one of my personal faves. It's a place where more often than not, you will run into people you know, it's a place where the service is personalized because over the years I think all of us have gotten to know the great staff (more specifically the team that serves in the bar area), and it's definitely the best place in Tucson for delicious mussels, oysters, jazz and late night snacks. 

Although you can aways rely on the fact that your favorite dish will probably never be taken off the menu, you can also rely on the fact that Kingfisher keeps things fresh by offering special menus, like their Summer tour menu that highlights awesome dishes from across the United States, and it's not all seafood!

As long as they keep the chilled grilled shrimp, the fish and chips and the grilled cheese on the menu, I'm happy as clam.

It was certainly time for an update! I wrote my initial review in 2013 and since then....ownership has changed. I can't really speak to that aspect, but I can say that I am super grateful to have this little gem in the downtown area. They've got salad, wraps, soups, smoothies, juices and pastries galore! It's definitely a vegan/vegetarian haven in the city and really offers food for all. It's healthy, fresh and thoughtful food. The team there is incredibly friendly and on one of my recent visits I got to take a peek in the kitchen to see a food item I was curious about. Call me lazy, but if this place was located in my neighborhood at the Mercado San Agustin, I'd eat there everyday without a doubt. Next meal will definitely be breakfast. I encourage everyone to check this place out.

Either my taste buds have changed or the kitchen has changed, but Scordato's isn't quite what it used to be. Scordato's was on my regular rotation for a several years when they were located at St. Philip's Plaza. When they moved to this new location, while I missed the ambiance of the St. Philips, the food was the same for the time that Danny was there. Perhaps over time they have changed ingredients. The pizza dough is more crunchy and cracker like than the original. We ordered a margherita,  mushroom and the Zucchini pizza. The mushroom was the most notably difference .It was a giant pile of mushrooms on a flat crisp- it was missing the creaminess of the fontina. The only thing that resembles the original Scordato's was the herb oil for dipping bread and pizza crust. 

The pizza's are enormous- ordering 3 for a party of 4 was a lot of food. There were left overs. Ordering for pick-up was easy. You can pay inside or over the phone .

It's about time for an update! But this time it's for the frozen food items. If you're in a pinch or simply don't feel like cooking- Roma Imports is an excellent choice. From homemade pasta, lasagna, sauce and even dessert you can serve a full dinner that tastes super fresh. High quality ingredients and a whole lotta Italia love= five star meal.

A much needed addition to this part of town for for sure! Beer enthusiasts will enjoy a variety of top quality brews from all across the country and of course local Arizona beer. I think they've got a small wine menu too. Stop in for a couple brews or pick up a growler or six pack to take home. There's always something fun going on over there- from tap take overs to live music and food trucks, Tucson Hop Shop brings a lot of activity to the Metal Arts Village. Once a month on the full moon the entire metals arts village hosts a celebration with music, food trucks and the artist studios are open too. Definitely a unique spot to check out.

El Minuto has been around for a looong time, but quite frankly it feels like they've lost their pizazz and spark. The food is really your basic Mexican sonoran style cuisine- you'll the typical combo plates, tostadas, etc. Standouts are the green chile green crisp and their salsa is pretty tasty! The tortilla soup is also worth trying. It's served traditional style...clear broth, tortilla strips and cheese topped with some avocado. I'd return for this soup. Our servers were super friendly too. I'm just not sure the owners show they care about their customers all that much. No greetings at the door on arrival or departure- just not that friendly...and with so many choices in town, I'd rather support a local business that's excited about their business, their food and service.

So, I said I'd give HUB another shot if the menu was updated, and for several months  I've been following their updates on Face book, and alas, they've made menu changes. They've mostly kept my interest because they post pictures of their daily specials, which really do always appear delicious. Bravo camera! And I recently read a food related article on CNN, that stated "a picture never lies" but I'll have to disagree with that sentiment, and HUB is exactly why. Pictures that had me salivating dishes like Ahi Tuna, and Chicken Pasta and Crab Cakes led to my long awaited return.  Nervous and excited (mostly nervous) to give HUB another try, my boyfriend and I treated our moms to lunch over the weekend. We also chose this spot for the variety of items on the menu. And this may be the problem - too many selections without enough attention to each. 

Based on the rating it's obvious that again I was underwhelmed. Decor and ambiance still earn this place that extra star and service was improved, but indifferent, so no additional stars in that department. And for lunch, you'd think that out of four entrees ordered, that at least one or two people would be raving about their meal. Sadly, that did not happen for us. We started with an order of the fried calamari. It was an average dish that heavily resembles the calamari at Wildflower and North (both Sam Fox concepts) in both presentation and style. Fried (super mini) rings of calamari tossed with greens and served with a roasted tomato sauce.  I'm neutral on this one.  For my entree I ordered the Roasted Corn and Avocado salad with baby arugula, heirloom tomato, pistachios, cotija cheese and chili-lime vinaigrette. I added grilled chicken. All salads are supposed to be served with ciabatta. First, the wrong salad came out, I think it was the Cobb. There was nothing roasted about the corn on this salad, the chicken was sadly on the dry side and the promised ciabatta was stale and cold (refrigerated cold). Oh, and it wasn't ciabatta. It was the bottom half to a sandwich roll. Did they run out of ciabatta? I felt confident that I would enjoy this salad, given that the menu description caught my eye right away. Really, the salad was flat in flavor and the description was somewhat misleading. Instead I filled up on my boyfriends tater tots and my moms french fries that came with her burger. On to the burger. My meowther ordered the cheese burger, which she kindly shared with me. Cold bread...again! Her bun was cold all the way through. Never toasted or heated. Perhaps just defrosted? Already annoyed by the cold non-ciabatta bread on my salad, which came out noticeably earlier than the rest of the entrees, I spoke up to server about my moms bun and ordered her another bun on the side...toasted. By that point, we all had our entrees: my boyfriend ordered the Pastrami sandwich and his mother ordered the lobster roll. I can't speak to the lobster roll, which didn't receive much enthusiasm from my BFs mother, but I did taste the pastrami sandwich. I can appreciate that they smoke their pastrami in house. It has a deep flavor, but I found it very fatty. I don't eat pastrami often, so I am not sure if that is to be expected. It's served on white toasted bread with swiss cheese. The tots and fries were the super stars at lunch. Sadly, this has always been my experience at the HUB. The prime fries are probably the best thing I've had here, but that's hardly a meal and certainly not a good enough reason to come back again for a meal. Maybe we ordered the wrong items? I don't like to give a 2 star rating, but with all the comfort food restaurants in Tucson, I really have had better.

Before opening their brick and mortar eatery at the beginning of the pandemic, El Rustico posted up at the Tohono O'Odham Swap for over four years. I never made the drive to the swapmeet and regret not having done so, but I trust that the restaurant is just as good, especially if Dawn K (Rustico's original #1 fan) says so! 

You can smell the mesquite grill from the parking lot. Rustico is super casual, order at the counter. We ordered the Rojitos de camarón, tacos de chicharron, lorenza with grilled chicken and birria soup. Everything was truly delicious. 

The rojitos de camarón are one of their most popular items and were a highlight of the meal for sure. They are basically shrimp quesadillas served with a red chile dipping broth. They are crispy and delicious!

The birria soup was served nice and hot with all the right garnishes- shredded cabbage, lime, salsa. 

If you order a lorenza, which is a crispy tortilla with melted cheese on it, much like a tostada. You can choose the meat or topping. I chose grilled chicken. It was perfectly simple and I garnished it with some extra cabbage and lime from our birria order. 

The menu boasts a variety of  burros, sopes, quesadillas, gordita, tortas and there also vegetarian options

Yes, Cafe Poca Cosa is one of those Tucson classics, but quite frankly, this place doesn't really do it for me. I've eaten here countless times over the years and at this point, I have their "daily made from scratch menu" memorized. But before I get to that, anyone planning on dining here must understand that this is not a Sonoran style Mexican restaurant. Rather, the flavors represent various other regions of Mexico, relying heavily on Mole sauces; red or sometimes chocolate based. The menu rotates 3 proteins that are all cooked by the same method of marinating and stewing. Usually, you will see a chicken, beef, pork and fish item on the menu. The green tamale pie (which is basically an extra sweet an giant corn tamale without the husk) is ALWAYS on the menu, made daily from scratch of course. All entrees are served with a generous bowl of rice, beans and tortillas. There are no appetizers offered. Only entrees all starting at about $25.00. You do get chips and salsa. Let me remind you: There is no guacamole, sour cream or shredded monterey jack cheese anywhere on the menu. I'm Mexican, so I totally understand the flavors at Poca Cosa are not Sonoran, and I welcome it! But I don't welcome the heavy side of attitude served with a meal at Poca Cosa. It's quite unfortunate, really. I commend them for their amazing success, but perhaps it has gotten to their heads. Don't even think twice that they will let you make any requests about your food. It simply won't happen. They wouldn't even accommodate the dietary restrictions for a friend who is Hindu. Clearly customer needs are not valued too highly here. The food here is tasty, but it's not good enough for me to come here over and over again, to always leave with the same feeling; that the service is cold and rushed. I'm passed the hype of Cafe Poca Cosa, but it still wouldn't stop me from recommending it to a foodie visiting town. Like I said, the food and the flavors are good, it's chic enough to satisfy the big city out of town-er and its style is certainly unique. As a Tucsonan, I'd rather spend my time supporting a local restaurant that shows some love for its customers and offers a sense of community. Isn't that what it's all about?

Barrio Bread and si charro are shaking things up on the corner of Prince and campbell! What. Great way to honor family recipes, heritage and the culture of the region. With dons award winning bread and the Flores family recipes this place truly speaks to Tucson. I love the market vibes indoors with seating through out and addition tables out on the patio. It definitely falls under a fast casual type of eatery with ordering at the counter. A server will go d you and deliver the food to your table. Everything is served in disposable containers, which I found Kind of wasteful. Perhaps it's a covid thing? I hope that's not the case. 

We enjoyed the chicken salad, torta and a toast with beans and avocado. It was a lot of food for two people but we like to try different dishes. The chicken tinga torta was really good and messy to eat! The salad was very fresh and flavorful. The toast with beans was good but I found the beans were a little on the heavy side and I had also ordered it without the salsa on top and it came with the salsa. Everything was  tasty though. 

The Retail section is really lovely. You can find everything from house-made salsa by carlotta Flores to tortillas, empanadas, more barrio bread, cookies, books, home wares and more!

A great spot for locals to support and Also bring their out of town friends to enjoy a very Tucson meal.

Just when you think Tucson couldn't possibly fit another Mexican restaurant, Calle Tepa opens. Sure, I thought to myself, "another Mexican place, seriously?" Yet, I just had to check this place out and I'm so glad I did! It's definitely more than what you would expect from your average taco joint. Yes. It's casual, order at the counter type of service, BUT the menu is beautifully painted on the wall (There are printed menus too), and it's for super fairly priced. They make their corn tortillas fresh per order, they use great quality angus beef (which your average taco place does not use, guaranteed), they make their own version of al pastor and you can watch it all happen, as the restaurant boasts an open kitchen with glass windows to sneak a peek at all the action. Salsas are made fresh daily and the garnish bar is super generous. Salsas range from mild to spicy, including an habanero salsa for the brave. On the taco front, they offer up great variety, from al pastor, to carnitas, carne asada, pollo adovado and even fish, which by the way are super tasty and a must try. But beyond this tacotopia.....they do breakfast, and rice and bean bowls, Manchego quesadillas, tortilla soup and tortas. The menu here is legit. What amazes me  is the quality of their product. Fresh and handmade usually comes with a price point that's a little higher than normal, which is totally cool with me, but they keep the pricing real low here. 

They also have a full bar at the back of the restaurant. It's super nice and it almost feels like a separate restaurant. As mentioned, they have a full bar and they make their own Margarita infusions, have a solid selection of good tequila and for rum lovers, they've got the Rum-Chata (rum & horchata) and they have a daily happy hour. 

It's worthwhile to point out that although the bar area has high top tables, they do not have table service. So if you want to order food, you have to order it up at the bar before you sit down. However, if it's quiet enough, the bartender will gladly come to your table and take your order. Perhaps they'll incorporate table service on super busy days like Fridays and Saturdays, but keep this in mind if you pay them a visit. You can't say you weren't given a heads up!

The combo of tasty food, good quality, fresh ingredients, a super awesome interior with hand painted walls and unique wall furnishings and friendly service set Calle Tepa apart from the pack. 

For those who are fans of the Original Guadalajara Grill, pay Calle Tepa a visit. It's the same owners! A fabulous Mother and Son team. JorDAN is always onsite at Calle Tepa making sure things are running smoothly. He's a young one, so I'm sure most people don't realize he's the owner. He actually did the entire remodel himself (of course with contractors) and transformed the previous business into what it is now. 

Cinco estrellas for awesome owners who keep it real. 

Can't wait to try a torta. They use Alejandro's bread.

I'm clearly the odd woman out here, but I've been totally misled with this place. YES, I knew it was a burlesque bar, which I have yet to watch (and remain intrigued, but only happens on the weekends), but my foodie radar was highly triggered by several folks in town, claiming their bar fare is the "best" in Tucson and their vegetarian options are "not to be missed." After one dining experience I know that I do not intend on dining here again. Aside from the fact that their food is not very fresh (this I gathered from the clear view into the kitchen that one gets as they place their order at the kitchen) there is zero customer service. I walked in with a group of friends after deciding that being on a wait list at Lindys wasn't worth it and based on the recommendations I was excited to give it a shot. Epic fail. Walk into the bar and awesomely and nicely present myself to the bartender and told her how excited I was to try the food (her response was "yeah, it's super awesome!), grab a few menus and sit down at a booth with my friends....about five minutes later...no server, no water....the basics. I head back to the bar to ask about a server: "oh, yeah...we don't have servers." Given that I told her with excitement that it was my first time there and had heard great things, it would've been nice to have been told that you have to order food at the kitchen window and drinks, including water, at the bar. Ordering at the kitchen was even more painful. Again, trying to express interest the single person manning the kitchen, it was very clear our meal was going to be an adventure. Explaining a "bun less" burger was like a foreign language. Half an hour later I had to go back to the kitchen to ask about our food (two bunless burgers, one order of fried tacos and fries). Awkward much? Food came out and tasted of fryer oil that had not been filtered or changed recently. Ranch dressing 100% bottled. Not a single item was hand made. I'm hoping the lettuce and onions for the bun less burgers were at least hand washed. At a previous job, I trained customers on keeping their fryers clean, and this one tasted of old oil. Bummer. When a menu advertises that they have "Brew City" Onion rings, that essentially tells me that they're buying their goodies prepackaged. Yes, the patties, fries, veggie burgers, etc are prepackaged, frozen and hopefully defrosted. I can't speak to the "highly regarded" chili, since all I saw of it as I ordered from the  window at the kitchen was the frozen chili in a tupperware container as the cook held it in is hand and said "ugh.....I think it's still frozen."

Perhaps, I'll change my mind after a Burlesque show....but this foodie is less than impressed.

I've been going to Contigo since the day they opened 2 years ago and have experienced the growing pains a new restaurant goes through from the back of the house to the front of the house. I basically know the menu like the back of my hand!

So here are a few of my personal favs:

Since day 1 the Ahi Tuna Ceviche has never failed me. It's tangy and slightly spicy, served with house-made Peruvian Purple Potato Chips. And now, Chef Pen. Jones will serve it on a tostada and topped with sliced avocado (but this is an off menu request) Both ways are equally delicious.

Tacos Contigo: Holy Flavor Explosion! These are of Chef Pens best contributions to the menu. Short Rib Tacos served on soft corn tortillas topped with Pickled Onion and a smokey tomato salsa (kind of like a crema). I loooooove this. And this dish never goes unordered on a visit to Contigo. Served with Rice and Beans, that by the way are equally as flavorful as the Tacos. ( I just wish they would serve a tad bit more rice and beans, because I'm always left wanting more!)

Queso Plate: Since Chef Pen came on to the Contigo scene, the cheese plate was revamped, and truth be told, this cheese plate has my heart. Not only is this cheese plate gorgeous, but it's extremely generous. Chef rotates Manchego, Bleu Cheeses, and other Spanish Cheeses and serves them with Dates, Fresh Berries, Honey, Spiced Walnuts, Toasted Bread, and Spanish Chorizo. The plate is a little too big for 2 people, so now my Boyfriend and order a plate for 2 and leave it up to Chef to customize it.

The Rib eye: Can't go wrong with a good quality piece of juicy marbled rib eye! 

Ensalada de Jicama: Anything with Jicama, Avocado and Tamarind automatically makes my favorites.

Make sure to ask if there are any small plate specials, because sometimes they go unmentioned and you could potentially miss out on something really Delicious like the Chicken Drummies with Chef. Pens Chipotle BBQ sauce....just a TIP.

Don't miss out on their homemade ice cream! Corey, their dessert dude is truly a young talent. He makes the best Ice Cream Sundae in town. I can't believe it hasn't been featured in any publications! Save room for any of their desserts. They really are all 10 out of 10 delicious.

Chef Pendleton Jones has led the Contigo Kitchen for over a year now and has brought with him  fun new flavors and delicious specials. And best of all he's a humble dude who just wants to cook great food.

This review wouldn't be complete with out a shout-out to Carlos the bar manager. Whether you're eating alone or with a couple friends, Carlos makes sure to make your bar experience super personal. He's passionate about mixology and you can definitely taste it in all his creations! Since I'm so indecisive with cocktails, I usually leave it to him to create something that's "not to sweet" and he always delivers.

So, I give 4-Stars, because more often than not, when we walk in, there is no one to greet us at the door and we are left standing around and it gets a little awkward.

This is a real deal butcher indeed. Go there for the meat, for sure. Quality is definitely high and priced right. Some might call it "spendy", but you're paying for good quality and personalized service. I can't speak to the awesomeness of the so-called Ugly Steak, as I have yet to try those, but the choice filet is certainly delicious. This isn't just a meat market either, they've got fish and poultry in addition to the "exotic" meat section. Did I mention there's a deli too? This place gets busy, so you can order a sammie while you're waiting for your order to get prepped and packaged.

Oh Wild Garlic Grill.....with your beurre blanc, tropical salsa and rice/risotto making an appearance on almost every dish. Not sure what exactly it is that I'm missing here, but it could be the fair prices and huge portions that excite people the most- Bolognese that could feed 3 people for $14 really is a smokin' deal and a fish special enough for two people sounds nice too, but at the end of the day, I prefer quality over quantity. I waited to have a few meals here to make sure it was just a fluke that I didn't enjoy my first meal at Wild Garlic Grill. EVERYTHING here is served with beurre blanc sauce, tomato rice and a tropical salsa. Basic French cooking with a tropical flare? The menu certainly reads well, with descriptions that instantly spark interest, but for me that's as good as it gets. Perhaps I didn't order correctly, as many reviews point out the lamb shank. I've had the fondue, I found the garlic overwhelming and quite loose for a fondue. Although runny, it was tasty, but it was served with dry cubes of white bread. I've had the ahi tuna, served with rice or risotto, tropical salsa, sauteed kale and beurre blanc. The salmon, served ala Ahi Tuna, which I ordered without beurre blanc and it was delivered to my table covered in beurre blanc. I politely sent it back, and they essentially scooped out the sauce and re-plated, resulting in cold salmon with tomato rice, sauteed kale, and remnants of beurre blanc. I've also had the grilled shrimp appetizer with....wait for it....beurre blanc! And a chunk of cold brie on top....oh...and tropical salsa. Seeing a pattern yet? I ordered the mushroom soup on another occasion and for my taste, it was quite salty, but that could just me. The ribs could easily feed 2-3 people and we found them overpowering and only ate about a quarter of the dish.  

I commend Wild Garlic Grill for bringing a seemingly upscale eatery to First avenue and for that, they get a third star. The building doesn't bother me. In fact, I think it's quite smart and interesting of them to have moved into this neighborhood. The interior was totally redone and the patio is large and comfortable. The service is still a little rough around the edges. Their signage may be a little misleading on the outside, because they advertise it as a burger/grill joint, so a person coming in expecting a super casual burger experience may be caught off guard by the open kitchen, art on the walls and white paper covers on the tables. Overall, the dining experience was not really my cup of tea. I was hoping for more refined culinary execution. Perhaps, if I saw value in super sized meals I'd probably enjoy this place more, sans beurre blanc on everything.

Amy's delivers on so many areas- from variety of flavors, playful colores and designs including your favorite cereals as toppings. Too fun! The experience of selecting a donut can be daunted. Don't want to pick the wrong one! Start with four and then build on from there. Ultimately these donuts are just too much for me. Just a touch too sweet and heavy. I like them simple and classic. For donut adventurists this is a great spot

Came here for the first time yesterday! I had heard great things about Revolution Ice Cream and was mostly excited to try their bacon flavored ice cream

The staff was very friendly and had no problems letting me sample 3 different flavors before I decided what I wanted. I did end up trying the bacon and while it was delicious, it wasn't as bacon-y was I imagined so I ended up with the Brownie flavor instead. 

The ice cream was delicious and really unique. My boyfriend loved his milkshake as well.

I think Hubby was jealous of the boil I got in Destin, because upon my return he was like - let's go eat at Storming Crab! 

I'm here for it, I love food. So we headed over for lunch over the weekend. 

We ordered an app to start with - boudin balls. I enjoy these in general and their's were good but not great. A bit mushy on the inside for me. They also brought over complimentary seafood bread (you can also order more on the app menu) and WOW this was AMAZING delicious! I would eat this every day! 

Hubby got a boil with shrimp, crab legs and crawfish. He selected cajun medium spice and let me tell - it was kickin spicy! WHEW my mouth was flaming! I had just had a boil recently so I ordered a bowl of clam chowder and it was pretty good. Large bowl too.

This was A LOT of food! 

Overall good experience. Our server shared that he was new (2nd day on the job) and it was obvious he was working hard to keep up. That said this place was fairly empty and there only appeared to be 2 employees working. They were a bit behind and probably could use more help or even someone to at least help our new server learn the ropes.

I had a fantastic time at Little Spoon. The Monte Cristo I ordered was perfectly cooked, with a nice buttery crisp to the outside of the bread. The Death By Sunrise smoothie was the perfect blend of citrus and creaminess to pull me out of my mid morning haze. Hats off to the cook and smoothie maker (not that I wear hats due to finicky curls, but the sentiment still applies)!

I am so happy to know this place exists!  We currently live in the NY area and have access to places like Buon Italia in Chelsea Markets and Eataly - but with our upcoming move to the St Pete area, I am thrilled to death that this place is here! We got a variety of cheese and charcuterie at our last visit, as well as bread.  A quick scan of the grocery shelves confirmed that some harder to find items in a normal grocery store are available here.

I will echo another reviewers advice, get here early!  Parking is INSANE!

Running errands in the area and my husband found this place on Yelp!  Given we are from arguably the pizza capital of America (sorry Chicago, I'm talking NY here) we thought we'd give it a try for lunch.  Ordered a bunch of slices to try.  I sampled the white pizza with ricotta and spinach.  This was really good!  Not too doughy and just the right amount of cheese.  Then had the grandma slice.  I'm a sucker for grandma pie and this didn't disappoint.   Perfect ratio of cheese, sauce and crust.  We also tried the cheesesteak pizza.  Yea, I know, not real pizza but let me tell you it was really freaking good!  

It's not the super thin crispy crust that I love but it's not the doughy thick kind of crust that I hate.  Considering where I'm at, I was pleasantly surprised by this and would definitely go back!  Next time we'll come up with our own pizza and try the salads too!

We need half stars!!!!  While this place is a solid 4 for dinner, brunch is definitely 5 stars!!!  Outside patio is dog friendly.  They brought Out a bowl of water!  Saturday is the ala Carte brunch menu, which is a must!!!  The variety of eggs Benedict is just insane.  Since we usually get bacon for our four legged kiddo, I got the tomato and spinach Bennie.   Crispy home fries and a slice of watermelon.  Delicious.  But the best by far is the salmon Bennie.  Smoked salmon, capers, red onion.  Absolutely spectacular!   Note though, ala carte is Saturday and breakfast buffet is Sunday.

This outdoor park like place of funnery with several food stands and is so Florida! A modern waterfront with a biergarden in the middle overlooking a huge open space with various seating options. At night the lights come on and the music plays and the place is alive with a party spirit. If that's not enough go bowling and eat chicken at Splitsville also,  A hipster bowling alley with fun for singles or familys. 
This area is located downtown bayside by the aquarium and next to the cruise ports.  
I had some of the best chicken around and it came from Flock and Stock. Chicken sandwiches were so tasty and juicy with the best waffle fries I have ever had.
The Biergarden offers a vary of beer choices and the service was great. It was busy but they were on top of it. 
The event seating/ Park area was a bit crowded but there is also alot in the restaurant patio areas that is socially distanced. Great fun. Enjoyed alot...

Hidden gem or at least hidden from me. Decided to stop into Jacks London grill while I was in the area waiting for my dog to be beautified

It's a medium size restaurant with a small bar. It seemed like a lot of locals were the bar, which is nice. Sinve the bar was full, I decided to have a seat in tbe dinner room. 

The menu has various English fare, like savory pies, fish and chips and shepherds pie. Not food I  normally eat so I asked the server his thoughts about a few items.Keep in mind their are many items, sandwiches,  salad and various pub food but I wanted to try something different. 

I ended up getting the beer battered onion rings and the chicken brie leek pie. Omg the food was fresh, hot and delicious. First the onion rings came out piping hot and piled high. Definitely need to share these because they're a lot of them. Now on to the chicken leek pie,  the crust eas flaky, buttery and heavenly. Once it cooled off, I dug into the creamy white wine goodness. The pie was full of chicken chunks, pieces of leek and melted cheese. Soooo good. It even came with a side of fresh veggies, lightly sauted with a slightly sauce. Loved the veggies,  still had a bit of a bite and not mushy, would have a little more. 

Everything was great, server was nice ,  there wasn't much of a wait and delicious food . They also had a good selection of wine and beer. Great place!

Couldn't wait until St. Pete opened a Ramen shop. Within the past year, the Mango Tree opened up and it's the only Ramen shop in this area. I've been to the Mango Tree and couple of times and both times the food was full of flavor and visual pleasing, which is also a plus. 

This time I ordered the pork based broth Ramen, I don't remember the name of it. It was full of sliced of pork, an egg, of course noodles and a few other things. The broth was delicious and full of flavor, I will definitely get this Ramen again. I also ordered the edamame dumpling, I asked about it first because I don't like anything with seafood, the waitress said it was just edamame.  It looked really good but there was some type of seafood, maybe fish sauce. I ended up eating one of my friends veggie spring rolls and he ate the edamame dumplings and loved them. 

We also has a couple friends that joined use, one had the teriyaki chicken and the other had sushi. The chicken looked amazing and smelled good. There wasn't  any left overs, that's how good it was. Our other companion, had the sushi and said it was really good, I can't speak on that because of my aversion to seafood.

Mango tree is a great spot to get a solid meal. I'll be back for sure.

We've lived in the channelside area for about a year and a half now but just made it out to Cena for the first time in the last few weeks. And I'm sad that it took so long because Cena was awesome! The restaurant is very small and intimate with probably 20 or so tables but the decor was very cute. And the food? Delicious!

We started the meal off with a cheese plate that made me excited for everything to come. They had a nice selection of I think 6 cheeses and 6 or so meats to choose from. I had one of their risotto dishes, which was to die for. Mine included shrimp and scallops that were cooked to perfection and the risotto was cheesy and delicious too. It paired perfectly with a glass of wine from their list. We finished the meal with some dessert, and if you are a tiramisu fan you HAVE to try their version. It's one of the most unique takes on tiramisu I've ever seen, pretty to look at, and a pleasure to enjoy. 

Definitely a stop in Channelside worth visiting again!

After hearing all the buzz, I was very excited to visit Lark. 

We went on a Wednesday night, and the three of us sat outside on the patio. We brought a couple bottles of wine (corkage is $20/bottle). The food is reportedly served family style. We started with the fried, goat cheese-stuffed Castelvetrano olives, and moved on to Caramelized Cauliflower Gratin, Little Gems 'Wedge' salad, Pork Belly Sliders, and Whole Grilled Branzino. For dessert, we had the Chocolate Pot Du Creme and the Meyer Lemon Tart. 

The food was generally OK. The Cauliflower Gratin and Pork Belly Sliders were the best of the dishes we ordered. The portions were fairly small, especially for a family-style approach. I don't think it really is family-style, but that's what they're telling people.

There was something not right about the Lemon Tart. It tasted like liver pate. All three of us tasted this. We pointed it out to our waiter and he said something like "let me check that out" and basically never returned. We were charged for the tart nonetheless. 

I think The Lark has potential, but they're going to have to make some adjustments in order to truly succeed.

You know what the best sort of steak dinner is?  A free one, and I would advise you find your sugar daddy before venturing to B&S for dinner.  

The food and service for our meal were perfect. In fact, they were better than perfect. The salad sang, the oysters danced, and the server could read minds.  Lamb chops were so tender they practically melted.  A heap of creamed spinach beckoned suggestively, like a sexy green pin-up.  

As with other Stephen Starr joints, they really gouge you on the drink prices. $13 for a 4-ounce absolut martini is highway robbery, but the lighting is so flattering and the leather banquettes are purring to your backside, so you let it go. 

Recommended for those with money, who appreciate on-point service and dry-aged cow.

Once upon a time in Rome, a few of my more adventurous friends dragged me to an Ethiopian restaurant.  The heaps of undifferentiated glop and bony bits we received angered me greatly, because I was a student and could not afford to eat out and hate it. Feeling the loss of 15 euros, I vowed never to eat Ethiopian again. 

Now that I'm older and wiser, I realize the foods I've hated have just been terrible versions of those certain cuisines. Kaffa Crossing is the perfect restaurant to convert those new to Ethiopian, or those like myself who had a traumatizing experience. 

Tender collards diced in a mathematical brunoise, lightly spiced red lentils, chewy, flavorful lamb tibs and a kitfo touched with cinnamon (?) decorated the giant's plate of food we ordered.  Scooping it all up with the best-textured, fresh injera I've ever encountered was gloriously messy and rewarding.  

Plenty of options here for vegans and vegetarians, but carnivores should definitely check out the kitfo.  You order up to your preferred temp (I'd say rare or mid-rare) and it arrives looking for all the world like a bowl of raw hamburger.  Don't be put off -- it's delicious.

Walking into Charlotte's Restaurant produced in me a profound feeling of nostalgia.  The smell of mothballs and old people, the dense floral fabric wallpaper and the servers clad in black tuxedo vests and bow ties brought  me back to lunch after my 8th grade graduation, or a funeral banquet in the Crystal Room.

What Charlotte's has now that they never did before it All-You-Can-Eat Crab Night on Monday.  For $25 bucks, they throw down salad, your choice of starch, and as many Dungeness or Snow crabs as you can cram down your gullet. 

The service on Crab Night is so efficient and friendly it borders on fawning. The servers are used to pouring half-cups of decaf for old ladies who always say the coffee is not fresh, and are thrilled to wait on anyone with a pulse and sense of humor. 

Hit it up.  I haven't eaten here recently off the a la carte menu, but the piles of Dungeness crabs I ate on Monday were absolutely worth a return visit.

If I like Ladder 15, does that make me a yuppie scumbag?  Of course not. 

I don't understand this blind hatred for Ladder.  Yes, the food used to be crap and the drinks were sugary and uninspired. Despite this, Ladder is always crowded from happy hour through last call.  Now that they are firmly financially successful, the owners have called in a new chef, David Ansill, to rehab the menu of upscale bar food.  

Burger with truffle aioli and bone marrow, polenta fries, lamb empanadas -- this is not just gastropub, it's David Ansill!  He's a professional Francophile who is obsessed with food, dudes.  You are not going to have a bad meal here with David on duty.  

The beer and cocktail lists were also re-done as of April 2010.  There's about ten craft taps representing local, US and European beers and they are knocked down to $3 during happy hour.  Hello, beer geeks !

I personally think its fashionable to bash Ladder because people are so eager to have something easy to hate, like the yuppie-white-hat post-college crowd.  You are not the things you hate, you're not the things you love, either -- no matter how little identity you actually possess.

I have four words to whisper in your ear. They aren't in my native tongue, and before I visited Le Viet, meant nothing on their own. 

Once uttered, the brief quartet of syllables Hen Xuc Banh Da manifests as a plate not soon forgotten, the kind of thing that should be crowned "Appetizer of the Year" by a glossy local magazine, if that particular title were not on the auction block annually.

Sweet, tender baby clams sauteed in "house special" sauce with basil, onions and some magic seasoning completely mysterious are ensconced in a crispy sesame rice cracker bowl.  It's snapping-and-scooping glory.

The 'Vous manages to strike the ideal balance between dive-y appeal (cheap beer and shot specials, round-the-clock dimness) and a friendly, almost-family-like atmo.  

Case in point, our daytime bartender (whose name I did not ask, bad reviewer!) took the time to point out the "healthy" items on the 'Vous expansive menu when I lamented my pudgy state.  Drinking beer at 3pm has nothing to do with this, thank you. 

Advised that the turkey was roasted in-house every day and not some lunchmeat drivel, my girlfriend and I ordered a behemoth house salad topped with said bird, a cheese-lidded crock of onion soup and a huge plate of their criminally crisp Spanish waffle fries gilded with chopped jalapenos and onions, all very thoroughly coated in more cheese. 

Of the three items, only the onion soup disappointed -- it was like licking a beef bouillon cube.  Otherwise, the grub was tops -- and cheeeep. 

The $2 shot of the day was Pinnacle Whipped Cream vodka. I'll just let you imagine how good this tasted (and felt) after all those Spanish fries... yummm jalapeno whipped cream!

$3 pints of Victory Prima Pils were cold, at least a dozen flatscreen TVs kept us up-to-date on CNN freaking out about FourLoko (they just found about it, I guess) and the place is happening during local sporting events.  No matter where you sit, you'll find a screen in your eye-line.  The 'Vous has always made me feel cozily at home in Center City, and I'll stand behind my five-star rating forever.

Just in case you don't happen to have a Polish grandparent stashed away somewhere, you should know that pierogies are one of the most bitchingly annoying things to make, possibly ever. 

The dough must be handled just right; the rolling and stretching carried out with precision.  Fillings must be made ahead of time  and assembly executed with Japanese vehicle-line efficiently, in order to avoid running about higglety-pigglety from counter to stove and back again, expending more calories than you will eventually glean from eating the things.

This is why you should not attempt to make these treasured Eastern European dumplings yourself, but rather get to Czerw's (say it Shev's) Kielbasy and choose from their mind-boggling array of perfect pierogies. 

Traditional versions come stuffed with potato, sauerkraut, or my favorite, potato and soft farmer's cheese, among others.  If you prefer a new-school flavor, try their lusciously salty Philly cheesesteak, buffalo chicken or bacon-cheddar versions.  Unorthodox but assuredly addictive simply fried up in plenty of butter and onions -- all in less time than it takes to nuke a Hot Pocket.

Have the fangbangers discovered Catahoula yet? When word gets around of its down-home Louisiana bites, True Blood soundtrack and stiff drinks, this place could be overrun with wannabe Sookehs and Beehls.

It's only because the staff is so charming, and I dread the thought of them closing up and depriving me of my new hushpuppy addiction, that I am even yelping Catahoula.  Formerly the BYOB Sauté, the narrow room has been transformed with flatscreen TVs, a heavy wooden bar running along its length and just a few high-top tables.  A simple, even humble setting for some of the best Cajun food being plated north of  Morehouse Parish. 

Oysters fried to what only can be described as a fluffy texture were nestled in a nest of shredded lettuce and spicy remoulade; a soft-bite baguette finished off this po' boy worth a thousand shocked yummmmmms. A catfish version was just as nice, and the Phillies game-time special of a half-po' boy "slider" complete with fries for $5 is an amazing deal. 

The confited quacker leg topping the duck jambalaya ($18) recommended by the staff was absolutely luscious, its rice and sausage bed cooked to an ideal "al dente" bite. My virtuous chopped salad ($10) was generous with the goodies: soft goat cheese clouds, piquant pickled apples, halved cherry tomatoes, fresh corn and an herby viniagrette. Hushpuppies studded with more fresh corn kernels are a requirement of dining here; the truffled tartar sauce that accompanies them possibly the condiment of the Southern gods. 

A postprandial Sazerac cocktail screamed to be accompanied by something sweet from the dessert chalkboard menu.  We zeroed in on the "white chocolate bread pudding bananas foster"($7) after confirming with our server that it was indeed a single dessert.  

Served hot in a gratin dish, this custardy glory was topped with a heap of caramelized bananas in their signature sticky fosters syrup and fresh whipped cream.  Beneath was one of the best bread puddings I have encountered, and I've had my share and yours too.  Based on brioche, this was an almost ethereal texture, especially compared to the dense bready bricks that pass for pudding elsewhere.  White chocolate does not normally hold much appeal for me, but this sugar bomb transcended preference.  It was, like Catahoula, a shockingly singular pleasure.

There is no real reason to serve 23 ounce Long Island Iced Teas.   A L.I.T. in a pint glass is certainly adequate for all stripes of boozehounds, but Oscar's takes it right past the line of logic.

I saw our young, bruised waitress sweep up broken glass three times in our visit there.  Also sweeping up spilt pierogies (at least paper plates can't shatter), and policing the many underagers who attempted to get served. 

Oscar's is such a dive: a smoke-filled room, sticky vinyl booths, cash only. But surely the cheapest hangover you will every purchase.

I had a nice little run with my silly rhyming review below, but it was accurate about two chefs ago (the one before the lion scandal chef) and now the time has come for updating. 

The first time I went into the South Philly Tap Room it was with my mom, an ER nurse at St. Agnes at the time.  Her boozy nurse, cop and fire-fighter comrades would gather at the new SPTR to celebrate the end of another shift saving lives.  We ate crab and artichoke dip, among other, not-at-all-memorable items, and I favorably reviewed the meal and upstart beer selection for my Temple News column. 

In the intervening years, SPTR has gone from a beer oasis to one of the most consistently tasty and different gastropubs in town.  The fried chicken that is being served right this minute --an orgy of wing, thigh, breast and drummie-- is one of the best I've had north of the Mason-Dixon. 

"Mexican construction worker" headcheese tacos for $1 was our go-to cheap appetizer of summer 2009.  Aggressively gilded with jalapenos and superhot salsas, the tiny, rich tacos were weird, provocative and quite simply delicious.  Even the fries, which are more like a British chip-style, are extraordinarily enjoyable. 

The beer selection is still outstanding, and the service, while not perfecto, has certainly improved.  Many of the staff are extremely competent in addition to being friendly and unpretentious. 

I'd recommend SPTR to anyone looking for a memorable, upmarket pub dinner.  Ask the servers and bartenders for beer recommendations -- they know their stuff more often than not.

To the table of obnoxious, out-of-town d-bags sitting next to us and doing their worst "Yo, Joey!" imitations: Just because you saw The Sopranos once doesn't mean you know dick about South Philly.  We will cut your narrow white ass with a sword if you keep that garbage up.

Having got that off my chest, I can now expound on the wonder that is Stogie Joe's.  Where else is staffed by a mom-and-daughter server team who call you "hon" with zero irony and keep your table of 15 aswim in 15 different beverages?  Where else can you mingle with the many, many different types of folks who live on and around East Passyunk Ave?  Seriously, the patrons are gay, straight, young, old, Italian-American, transplant, local, hipster AND South Philly Willy and Millie. Where else can you lounge in a converted garage that is open to the breezes in fair weather and made snug by a roaring fireplace in foul?

Besides the lively Tuesday-night karaoke scene, Stogie's is stellar for thick-crust, square pizza, mussels in marinara and meatball parm sammies.  My personal go-to is the Stogie Joe stromboli, an epic fatty of thin-rolled dough, salami, prosciutto, provolone and some herbs.  No pesky vegetables here!  The monster is $10 and enough for two people to share. 

The whole place is cash only, but when you brandish your ATM receipt to the bartender, you get a FREE BEER!  That's right, a free beer in return for using the cash machine.  Is this South Philly, or... heaven?

When your chef friends want to meet at a restaurant, it's a sure sign it rocks hard.  I like to meet friends here for the $1 oyster happy hour and eat as many as we can before we die from iodine poisoning.  The beer is cold and local, the bartenders are super knowledgeable and friendly, and their shuckers are perfectionists -- each oyster is perfectly opened and slides out gracefully with no creepy slurping action necessary. 

Gorgeous lobster rolls on toasty buns and razor clams dipped in butter are my other two favorite dishes. Be sure to get here early for happy hour, Oyster House is hugely popular with the successful business sorts in Center City and fills up quickly!
