I'm on a boat, B***h!  

Though the food is most assuredly banquet hall slop, I found the employees friendly and efficient both herding people up the gangway and making sure they knew there was a big step up or down imminent.  The decor is ahoy-eighties cheesy, with mirrored pillars, linoleum-topped tables dotting the upper decks and the sort of carpet that you see in budget hotels. 

Though we laughed at the food, the booze was flowing and the boat cruised along briskly, giving us that fat-cigar, wind-in-the-hair feeling of elation you can only achieve on the water.  Philadelphia and Camden looked beautiful from the river, much more so than they do up close with their grit, garbage and omnipresent crackheads. 

To Sum Up:  Do not go expecting a culinary experience -- it's institutional, steam-table stuff.  If they offer a drinks cruise or event (like the excellent whiskey festival we attended), by all means, set sail!

Zee frites, zey are fantastique! Thick-cut, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside... I was in carb-lover's heaven.  

A friendly fellow-customer at the ordering counter advised me to check out the cheddar-jalapeno dip, and upon hearing I was ready and willing to pony up an extra fifty cents for a second dip, was right on cue with a lemon-dill recommendation.  

A sneaky spice percolated through the cheddar-jalapeno cup, but the cheese was undetectable -- it was much more like a zingy mayo.  Lemon-dill played a cool counterpoint to the hot fries; a fountain Diet Coke cut through the salt attack. One "regular" sized fry cone, an extra dip and a medium fountain drink set me back $5.40, and I'd definitely return when I'm craving some spuds bathed in bubbling oil.

Still currently sitting at the restaurant and I can't not write a glowing review! 

Upon my arrival (waiting on my party of 5) I was greeted by who I assume was an owner. He was extremely friendly and made me feel right at home by offering me a seat at their beautiful bar area to wait. They immediately started getting a table of five ready and soon after we were seated! 

Our fantastic waiter Austin suggested the guacamole, mentioning it was the best in the city. Having been to a many Mexican cuisine restaurants, I've had my fair share of guac. But Austin's tip did not disappoint. Fresh, flavorful, and topped with sweet pomegranate seeds! We asked for more chips so we couldn't waste a drop. 

Next we tried the tinga chicken and arabas taco platters. BE AWARE everything is to share and a la carte. Each platter came with 5 corn tacos shells and fixings, including 3 different sauces to dress with. The tinga was saucy, tender, and delicious! The arabas was tender, a little dry and could've used a pinch more salt but the underlying flavor was there. Nothing too spicy (not even their spiciest sauce, so go for it!) 

We finished our meal off with flan to share. It my first flan experience. And being a creme brûlée snob, I was in love! Do not miss this dessert when you visit. 

I also tried 2 margaritas. The house and another flavored with blood orange (I believe it is seasonal). Both delicious and give Bakersfield a run for its money! 

The bottomline? GET TO FESTIVA. Great atmosphere, kick ass staff, and awesome vibes. You won't regret it. It's gonna be a great summer spot.

I have been longing for good Asian food ever since I moved to New Orleans two years ago and FINALLY it's here! The ramen was INCREDIBLE and featured the best egg I've ever eaten in my life -- PERFECTLY soft boil and magically tempura-style fried?!?! Ugh. I'm gonna dream dreams about that egg. I also had the PERFECTLY seared scallops, the most flaky delicate kimchi empanadas, brussel sprout salad w/ lamb pancetta... I just... I... It was just all so incredible. The warehouse district is already a hub of some New Orleans' best restaurants and Rebellion is not only a fit, it's a front runner. Do your tummy a favor. Eat this food.

The meal we had here just kept getting better and better. First off, I'm not a fan of unsweetened green tea, but their's was quite the exception. It was fantastic!! They give you a complimentary Korean style tapas. We also ordered the Korean BBQ wings. THEY WERE THE BEST WINGS I'VE EVER HAD! I ordered the bulgogi box and was slightly disappointed to find out that I got goyza instead of noodles, but the goyza was good so I was ok with it. The bulgogi was fantastic- slightly sweet and slightly savory. My meal also came with a salad. The salad was good. My fiancée ordered a spicy pork bimbap that was great! We will be back! This place rocks!

Bacio is an Italian restaurant-wannabe. With televisions all over the restaurant with the sports channel on, there isn't an Italian theme feel to this place. The food was just okay. The pizzas were okay. The eggplant parmigiana was just ok. Nothing mind-blowing. The gelato tasted artificial. Slow service.  

Won't be back. I give this place a few months before it closes down.

Spicy shrimp pho. Add some chili oil. It's so fragrant. So delicious. Good bang for the buck. I may or may not even be slightly allergic to shrimp and I still get it.

I come back time and time again to get it. Also, tried the spicy tofu dish and it was also very good if you like spicy food.

Not super impressed with the pork spring rolls, it's hard for them to stand out. And it's almost $5 for 2 rolls.

Service is friendly and efficient. Lots of street parking nearby.
Too early to tell with this place as of yet. Time will tell. They need to rotate beef stock more ...

Super pleased with my first time at The Industry. Ambience is great for intimate tables or group setting. The bar has tvs. There's something for everyone! 

Came on a Friday night and we got a table easily. Their specials all looked incredible. The menu was diverse. 

Mussels: if you like them, get them. Nice flavors and they pair well with the great beer selection. 

I got the fish blt. They fish itself changes based on catch of the day. I had a whitefish (can't remember which) that was tasty. The bread holds up well and it's a huge serving. Fries are perfectly cooked. 

My boyfriend got the wings and he seemed very happy. I didn't taste them but he's picky and didn't complain.

You want cocktails at very classy bar this is a  must!  This review is strictly for cocktails only.  We came to town for a quick weekend trip.  Our very good friend Johnny T. lives here and we made plans to meet up before we headed over to a festival we had planned on going to.  We took an uber over since it is so hard to find parking downtown. Sea Salt is located in the heart of downtown that is obviously getting a huge make over.  Within a few blocks these great places are opening up and revamping this whole area.

My husband and I arrived early and when we walked in I could not get over how beautiful this restaurant was.  Very romantic, classy, amazing energy from the moment you walk in.  The bar is in the back of the restaurant. Behind the bar is all Himalayan salt blocks, super pretty.  The main dining area is all dark wood tones, very softly lit, such a peaceful setting.

Since we would be eating at the festival we were going to we did not order food.  My huge regret was not having enough time to go back for dinner.  I saw the menu and wanted to dine here so bad. The main thing that caught my eye was the Grouper, oh man it soun ded incredible. The bartenders were all excellent, made some really nice cocktails  and took good care of us. Like us even if you can't make dinner this is a perfect place if you want an elegant setting  where you can enjoy drinks and good company.

So thankful our friend picked this place.  It will be on my radar next time I visit for dinner.
Great spot for a date, this will impress!

We stumbled upon this place walking around in the afternoon.  This is not your typical Irish bar. As we walked through the walkway we saw two bars inside and then towards the back to this beautiful open area with fountains, flames, and plenty of staff in their very cute classy attire. 

We were not quite hungry yet as we did eat breakfast so we stopped in for cocktails. This place was happening. Plenty of patrons partying and having fun. Great for large groups. We saw a huge bachelorette party and guys celebrating a birthday. 

It looks like a nestled garden with beautiful purple flowers, clean, plenty of tables and great service. Their drinks are awesome here. They do upcharge  you $4 per glass in case you want to keep it as a souvenir or you can return to any of the bars for a cash refund. 

I can only imagine how much fun it is here at night. They have live entertainment and plenty of spaces to enjoy the venue. 

Classy fun place with e celebrating drinks in quite a lovely decor. This is a must to check out.

Our daughter moved across from this area so we have visited twice now. It's a perfect place to come with your family and fur babies. They have a very large fake grassy area with plenty of seating and a stage with live music. 

You get the breeze from the water. Tons of young kids playing and having so much fun. There's a large bar so plenty to drink. They have several food options although with such an attraction spot I feel they need more of a variety. 

The parking lot is large where you pay at the machine $2 an hour. We enjoy coming here with our dogs and daughter and fiancé. 

Very nice place to unwind, enjoy good music, eat and drink.

*******MUST CHECK OUT THIS BREWERY*********This brewery is by far the BEST!!!  After visiting quite a few other brewery's by the time we got here it was LOVE at first sight.  The area of Dunedin is a small town, with so much character and some of the most friendly people you will ever meet.  The outside has high tops and some picnic tables. There was a couple of bartenders who helped over a couple of hours of hanging out and enjoying the incredible beers.  They were very helpful and super friendly.

The vibe is very chill with various age groups so yeah not your typical hipster young crowd only.  As we sat outside drinking we met so many patrons that were so cool and friendly.  Everyone who comes here is just ready for a good time.  I can't remember all the beer that we tried but a few really stood out.  The first one was the Grafitti Orange Creamsicle, oh my so good.  I also enjoy a good Saison, after trying two different one's I fell so in love with the "La Fete" Table Saison. It was so good I got a growler to bring home.

Unlike some other brewery's in the Tampa area this place is so fun and friendly with very good beers.  We enjoyed the fact that this is a small brewery that makes it that much more special.  After quite a few hours of hanging out here we all decided this was by far our favorite brewery.  We purchased hats, t-shirts, growlers, stemware, LOL....... I enjoyed shopping all of their fun items. 

The name peaked my interest and after looking up what it meant I was quite intrigued with their decision on the awesome name.  The seventh son of a seventh son is a concept from folklore regarding special powers given to, or held by, such a son. The seventh son must come from an unbroken line with no female siblings born between, and be, in turn, born to such a seventh son.[1] The number seven has a long history of mystical and religious associations: seven virtues, seven deadly sins, seven Sleepers, seven days of creation, etc. In this case, it refers to a man who is the seventh son of a man who is himself a seventh son. Very cool.

I look so forward to visiting again for some fabulous beer and a great time!!

We used to frequent this place often when it was at its smaller location. Gave it a try in the new location - much bigger space and seems to be booked most weekends so props to them. We, however, will not be returning. 

Starting with the huge mural on the wall of the ex-con owner surrounded by fellow mob legends to the fedora pin striped servers, it is apparent that this place has been overcome with exploitation of the owner's criminal past than with continuation of great food. Another huge let down was the newly added sharing charge on the menu. Have a little faith in your food to bring us back and quit the nickel and diming - I can't stand when restaurants do this! 

The bread was sesame, cold, sliced, store bought -  no biggie but just don't bring it out encased in a napkin in a huge basket like it's fresh out of the oven. Our favorite appetizers from the old location were no longer on the menu and are only featured as specials from time to time. They could not make either of them for us last night. I ordered the eggplant parm which they've changed the recipe and is now just average  as opposed to the towering layered deliciousness it used to be. Husband got the sausage meatball which was very good - over Sevorino pasta which we were glad to see they still utilized. I also ordered a caprese salad - good, not great. 

Portion sizes were very large.

Total for 2 basic entrees and a salad with 20% tip - $72! 

Next time we will go to Nunzios or Sapori.

This ice cream shop is a gem! Lots of alcoholic and non-alcoholic options, but we were feeling more nice than naughty and went for the Gooey Butter Cake and Persimmon Cardamom. 

-Gooey Butter Cake 4.5/5 - soo good with the tiny (actually gooey) chunks of cake mixed in, almost made up for not getting a chance to try the real thing while I was in STL 

-Persimmon Cardamom 5/5 - my fave!! as one of their seasonal flavors, this harbinger of fall made from real persimmons & persimmon butter (didn't know this was a thing but now wanna get my hands on a jar) struck an ideal balance between the notes of fruit and spice, with neither overpowering the other and joining together in a delicate blend of creamy herbal deliciousness~ 

Usually tasting such drastically different flavors simultaneously can result in a loss of individual integrity, but these flavors were each so bold that they held their own as we went back and forth between the two. Pretty pricey at $5/scoop but so tasty that it's still definitely worth trying!

Warning to vegans! Don't buy their vegan pizza. It costs $10 more then their regular pizzas, but it's made lighter then the cardboard box that it comes in. Total rip-off. Their large size is not even enough for one person.

I saved pictures of it so that I could compare it to Gourmet Pizza Company's pesto vegan pizza. As you can see, GPC's pizza is about 3 or 4 times heavier at around the same price.
Worse burger place in Philly -- poor presentation, average food and lousy service. Better if they stick to the classics.

Right now anyway, all sushi is 50% on Monday and Tuesday from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m.! Great deal, and no strings attached like I've seen at other places (the 50% off applies to regular and specialty rolls alike). I had a spicy scallop roll and a specialty roll with spicy crab and tuna on it (can't find it on the menu online), as well as a small hot sake for $14.95! The rolls were both very tasty, although not mind-blowing. Nice atmosphere, dark decor, kind of urban. Service was fine.

Fortunately for me I work about 50 feet from their front door so I went to lunch with a coworker here and was very happy.

The interior is tastefully done, clean and modern - they transformed this restaurant completely from what the building was used for before and it looks great.

After walking in we were seated promptly which was nice and the restaurant at 11:45 on a Monday was already quite busy.

Our drink orders were taken right away and delivered quickly as well.  I do like that if you ask for water they will bring you a glass jug that you can pour with.

Not wanting to eat anything too heavy I decided on the salmon tacos with cottage cheese as my side (yeah I'm weird - whatever).    The tacos were large and served on soft corn tortillas.  The fish was grilled/blackened and had plenty of flavor and cooked well.  Served along with some napa cabbage, pico de gallo and some kind of dill sauce that was delicious - I was very satisfied.

I can't wait to go back and try more of their menu!

Eating at ZoZos recently was truly how a restaurant experience should be, from the service to the food it was how a restaurant experience should be.  I don't like handing out 5 star review unless a place truly deserves it and ZoZo's delivers.

I'll spare you with my usual 'Dear Diary' review where I chronologically describe everything and cut to the chase:

Ambiance:  It's a little hole in the wall (although it's bigger than you think) and with the way it's decorated it makes for a charming, intimate place to have dinner.  It's not ultra upscale modern looking and I wouldn't want it to be.  They way they've made it feel is absolutely perfect.

Service:  The star of our evening had to be Pepe.  The man should open a school where other hosts and waitstaff learn how customer service should be.  He is friendly, genuinely happy, personable and just a great person to talk to.  He is part of what made our meal so special that evening.  We talked with Sid at the bar who recommended a bottle of wine that we overlooked, and was cheaper than what we wanted but was delicious.  Judy was a great host and what really made our experience complete was when both Judy and Sid came over to talk to us about our meal, wines and other events we should come info for at their restaurant.   Everyone here made it feel like you're eating at home with family.

Food:  This is the other half of the experience that Zozo's totally nailed.  We started off with crab cakes which were melt-in-your-mouth delicious.  Served with a light lemon cream sauce that didn't try and take center stage.  The crab cakes were moist, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside.  Just enough celery to add that crunch in the middle but without taking away from the rest of the cake.   Once we had enjoyed the crab cakes we figured out you could take their delicious garlic bread and soak up the uber delicious sauce with it.

Next came our salads which came on a small plate, presentation was standard but there were two things that really stood out.  1.) the veggies were nice and crisp 2.) the dressing they use is not only delicious but acts as a great way to cleanse your palate before enjoying your main course.

Lastly we received our entrees. This is what sealed the deal.  My wife ordered the short rib special and I ordered the mushroom ravioli.   If you go to Zozo's and the short rib is available - ORDER IT.    It is this perfectly (and I mean perfectly) cooked, tender short rib served on top of a bed of mashed potatoes that is absolutely to die for.   Take the best sex you've ever had, think of it as food, and you have the short ribs at Zozos.  I could eat this all day, every day.

The mushroom ravioli was also extremely good.    Mushroom raviolis have become very common place at italian restaurants now but few execute it well and dare I say that many places in Reno do a poor job of making their filling.  Not at Zozos - I received a little less than a dozen LARGE raviolis served in a sauce that put the ravioli in center stage and complimented them excellently without overpowering.  The sauce literally exists as a best supporting actor while letting those delicious ravioli be center stage.  Nothing needed extra salt or seasoning.  Ravioli perfection.

If you don't make this place one of your go-to Italian restaurants in Reno, you're doing yourself a disservice!

If my review was tl;dr - We love Zozos!

We came here with some friends and were extremely pleased with our experience.

Once you walk in you're surrounded with a very mid-century modern vibe.  They had a projector playing a movie onto one of the walls (The Women, with Joan Crawford and it's set in Reno) and all the furniture and decor was done perfectly.   Our hostess, Taylor, was amazing.  Not only was she friendly but she also did an incredible job of keeping with the theme of the bar.  

The drink and bites menus are small but it works.  The cocktails are delicious. My first cocktail was "The smoking gun" which had whiskey, maple syrup and a slice of bacon in it.

I also had a "Wolfie" which was very tasty.

For food, we had some of their pork belly sliders (yum) and a Caprese flatbread (also delicious)

We will most definitely be here again, what a terrific first experience.

Forget the other big local names for breakfast in Reno/Sparks.   Now that I've discovered this place I don't know if I want to go anywhere else.

No matter what you order on the menu make sure to get the scones.  Put some butter and honey on them and... WOW.

Personally here I've had the corn beef hash and eggs as well as the biscuits and gravy and they were both excellent.  The portions are so large you'll find yourself taking it home or sharing it.  The fresh orange juice is delicious as well.

There is almost always a wait on the weekends but it is totally worth it. Try and get there early to avoid the rush!

WORST DINING EXPERIENCE EVER!!!!

My family and I came on Easter and the entire lunch was terrible! Did I mention that we were charged for mimosas AND orange juice that we never ordered or had?! That's a total of $36!! NOT COOL!

We were seated immediately, but waited for quite some time for someone to take our drink order. I get that on Sunday's people normally do brunch, but what about those that don't feel like eating eggs and sandwiches? Why have the menu so limited, and until 3pm? Sorry, I like my eggs BEFORE 12pm. Not after.

Lemme tell you about the staff... Our waitress, Jane, seemed overwhelmed from the beginning and kept using "I'm new" as her excuse for every single mistake -- big no-no! She wrote everything down yet managed to forget my salad, gave me fries with my burger when I didn't order them, under cooked my oldest son's burger (it was pink; I said "well done") and forgot to bring us our soda refills. 

Not only was my family VERY, VERY upset with the level of service we received but I was left utterly disappointed. This is an establishment in Montecito; it should be a fine dining experience! WHAT HAPPENED?!?!

I highly recommend you go elsewhere because Lucky's is a total waste.

Biggie's, Biggie's, Biggie's, can't you see sometimes your burgers just hypnotize me.

Oh man.
I don't even know what to say.

All the sounds that came out of my mouth while eating here weren't even words. The bf seriously asked me if I was going to have a foodgasm while I was chowing down.

I ordered a bbq burger($8.50) with soft cheddar and grilled onions. It came on a bakery bun but I was offered it on garlic bread if I had wanted. I also substituted waffle fries for and additional 75 cents.

The bf ordered the grilled chicken sandwich with pickles, lettuce, and tomato. It also came on a bakery bun but he was given the same choice of garlic bread. He played it healthy and ordered cottage cheese with his sandwich.

I didn't taste the chicken but the bf said it was good. My burger was freakin' fantastic. Seriously. The best burger I've had in St. Louis. Big, juicy, cooked well done as I had requested. The grilled onions complemented the char-grilled flavor and the bbq sauce. The soft cheddar oozed out of the sides. So tasty. Then to top it off the waffle fries were, again, the best I've had in St. Louis. Maybe anywhere. The were seasoned well but didn't taste too salty. They had a nice texture and an awesome flavor. 

Our waitress was awesome. Friendly with some flair. She was helpful, attentive, and knew the menu and options well.

We sat on the "patio" (tables outside of the building) so I can't speak of the ambiance but the weather was great.

We will mos def be back and I'll be recommending Biggie's to anyone looking for a good burger.

Walking in it wasn't quite what I expected. It was open and bright and for some reason it had a cafeteria feel to me.

The hostess and server were friendly and efficient. They immediately brought us Papadum, yum! At the point of ordering it got a tad confusing. They asked us if we wanted Garlic Naan or plain Naan. We said no thank you to both but I ordered more Papadum and the sever was like yeah, yeah I will bring you more Papadum. Do you want plain Naan or Garlic Naan? We were both like um, none. Then he said he will bring plain. We don't know if it came with our meal or what.

The Hubs ordered Chicken Tikka Masala @ $12.75 - Marinated boneless chicken breast roasted in the clay oven & sautéed in a creamy tomato sauce with spices. 

He reported the sauce to be flavorful, the chicken to be tender, and the veggies to be good.

I ordered Baingan Bharta @ $10.50 - Eggplant roasted in clay oven, mashed, lightly creamed & sautéed in fresh chopped tomatoes, onions, ginger & mild spices.

It was delightful. The sauce was flavorful and not overly creamy. The veggies were cooked to perfection.

They brought plenty of rice for us to share.

We will mos def be back at some point.

~Just a note, they have a parking lot and there is plenty of street parking.

Molto Buono!

Oh my double da**. After several somewhat recent let downs I was almost expecting to be disappointed but man. This was a brilliant experience. Our Moms were in town and the BF and I decided to take them to Charlie Gitto's. We made a 8:00p reservation on a Friday night and didn't have to wait at all. Much appreciated with the Mom's in tow.

From walking in the door to walking out the door we had a stellar experience.

We all had drinks instead of appetizers. I had a drink of the day watermelon martini that tasted like liquid Jolly Rancher. Although sweeter than I usually like it tasted fantastic. Everyone else had beer or wine.

For dinner we ordered:

The bf's Mom: Manicotti with ricotta cheese filling and baked in a tomato cream sauce. It was a huge portion with rich flavorful sauce.

The bf: Filet of Beef Tenderloin an 8 oz. center-cut steak finished with brandy peppercorn sauce or herb butter (he got herb butter on the side). This steak was so tasty pink/red (as ordered) and melted like butter. 

My Mom and I ordered the special which was Diver Scallops. I could envision myself on a deck at the beach. Seriously, I'm pretty sure I could smell the ocean. These were the best scallops I've had in STL.

Everything was fantastic. So fantastic that we had to try the tiramisu for desert. Which was an awesome ending to an epic dinner.

Part of the awesome was the customer service and atmosphere. It was dark and classy. Perfect for an old world feel. Everyone was polite and friendly. Doors were opened and chairs were pulled out. Not one time did I feel like I was a burden as the customer (which, unfortunately, seems to happen semi frequently in STL).

Seriously, Charlie Gitto's, you're doing it right.

Molte Grazie!

Well hello Bosnian food. Where have you been all my life? Oh yeah, not in Wichita, KS.

While STL is lacking in some good ethnic foods it sure makes up for it in other areas.

The bf and I decided to try Grbic kind of on a whim. He suggested it and I jumped all over it because he normally suggests the same ol.

We walked in and were greeted in a large open room. The hostess was very welcoming and we were seated quickly.

Our waiter was friendly, patient, and helpful. He offered explanations of food and suggestions of what we might try based on various things we might be looking for with our orders.

We both tried foreign beers and were pleased with the lighter one. I unfortunately can't remember the name of either. I suggest you be adventurous and just try a few.Next time I want to try the flavored brandy.

For our appetizer we ordered a half order of Cevapi which is traditional Balkan style grilled beef sausages served with Lepinja bread. O.M.G. Tasty and the sauce that comes with it is so good. I will ask for extra next time.

Our entrees came next. The bf ordered Chicken Rouladen. It is chicken breast filled with chopped spinach and feta cheese, breaded and lightly fried served with
buttered potatoes and vegetables. He enjoyed it. I thought it was too rich because of the cheese and the fact that it was fried. The veggies and potatoes were tasty and cooked just right. I ordered the Sarma. Which, I was told, is a more traditional Bosnian dish. Sarma is cabbage rolls stuffed with ground beef and rice topped with a paprika sauce and it came with with golden mashed potatoes. So good! The cabbage was cooked well, the stuffing wasn't too dry or soggy, the sauce was a freaking paprika explosion in your mouth, and the potatoes brought it back home to comfort food. 

Hvala lijepo, Grbic. Bilo je ukusno.

4.5 stars! I have eaten in the dining room 4x & ordered takeout twice. This restaurant is consistently above average in all regards. I love that its female owner is on the floor-- often @ the counter ringing up customers. The restaurant is clean & orderly, & conveniently located beside Panera Bread just off busy Bruce B. Downs in New Tampa. 

Sushi Cafe is open Sun - Thurs from 11 AM to 10 PM & 11 AM to 11 PM Friday & Saturday. Its menu is extensive-- 12 appetizers; 5 salads; 8 Sushi Platters Chef Choice; 70 Sushi or Sashimi Rolls; 25 Speciality Sushi Rolls; 26 Hibachi Dinners (including Tofu, White Fish, & Teppanyaki Vegetable); 2 Katsu, 3 Tempura; 5 Small Plates, 5 Japanese Style Fried Rice or Noodle; 10 Side Items; & 6 Desserts (including ice creams & Tempura Cheesecake).

Available are 3 Children's Dinners for age 12 & under & an entire page of Lunch Specials from $7.95 to $12.95. (Lunch specials include soup, salad, vegetables, & steamed or fried rice. All orders must be placed no later than 3 PM.)

Each time I've eaten here we've ordered the $14.95 Hawaii Speciality Roll, which is my favorite sushi ANYWHERE! With its esthetically pleasing pink flower-like pedals, the 10 pieces consist of tuna, salmon, shrimp tempura, crunch, & avocado mango wrapped in soy paper w/ spicy mayo & washabi sauce. On today's visit we also ordered the $7.25 Crunch Speciality Roll; it was very good w/ its tuna, avocado, cucumber, & tempura crunch w/ teriyaki sauce & sesame seeds. The Pacific Fushion Speciality Roll @ $9.35 is even better; it is made w/ spicy tuna, crunch, & cucumber w/ avocado, spicy mayo, spicy eel sauce, masago, & honey wasabi sauce on top. The Crab Rangoon @ $4.95 is very good, although no Rangoon can compete w/ Little Ninja of Zephyrhills (due to the curry butter). The Miso Soup that accompanies the rolls here is also very good-- more flavorful than many others I've tried. The Hibachi is on my radar, but I have yet to forsake the delicious sushi for it-- the Hawaii Roll is just TOO GOOD. 

Vida, Mastercard, Discover, & American Express are accepted. Curbside pickup is still available.

As of August 10, 2020, the dining room is still closed; however, takeout, curbside, & delivery options are available. This restaurant is open seven days a week from 11 AM - 8/9 PM. 

This establishment advertises "Authentic Neapolitan & Original NY Style Pizza & Pasta." Delivery is offered thru DoorDash, UBEREATS, & Mobilemeals .com

With a craving for pizza, I popped in to order a small extra sauce/extra cheese pie & Caprese. For approximately $22, I went home w/ a delicious meal(s). 

I ordered at the counter, paid, then was sent to my vehicle to wait. Manager Brian (the most personable & professional young man-- very impressive) brought my order to my driver's side window. 

I arrived home w/ hot, fresh, & delicious Italian food. A huge fan of NY pizza, the woodfired pizza I was provided was excellent. I finally found a restaurant manager who knows the meaning of "extra cheese."  

Will I return to try other items on the menu? Of course! Brian's enthusiasm & the quality of the food I received demand a second try!

4.5 stars for the delicious salad, excellent service by Amber, & the friendliness & warmth of general manager George. This Glory Days is the first in Florida. It has been open 8.5 years, & replaces the old Leroy Selmon restaurant. The building was erected in 2003. The interior has been updated on more than one occasion.

I try hard to avoid chains & I seldom sing their praises, but after stopping in @ 4 separate Glory Days locations, it's a shame that I REALLY like the brand! There! I said it! I like this chain! And I enjoyed this location! The food & the service here (& @ other locations) was fresh.

The more I visit Glory Days, the more impressed I am. And the decor ain't bad either. This one has a handsome bar bathed in red tones; multiple dining areas w/ a variety of seating styles; 54 TVs (Yes, 54! I asked George), along w/ a large outside front patio area for patrons & their canines alike. Can't beat that! 

I lingered here today to both relax & observe. Multiple staff members greeted me as I entered & a few checked on me after I was quickly seated. My server was attentive & efficient. As patrons entered, staff not only acknowledged their regulars, but spoke w/ them like family, reminiscent of the old neighborhood bars "where everybody knows your name." Cheers! 'cause I've found the same @ all Glory Days locations, which tells me corporate leadership is wise & worthy. 

This restaurant/bar is perfect for large gatherings-- retirements; sports teams; birthdays; graduations; girls night out, & more! It's also convenient-- off Bruce B. Downs & nestled up beside I-75. There's even a major intersection w/ a light, so entering & exiting the parking lot is easy. 

Glory Days boasts of "using the highest ingredients, including freshly baked Artisan breads, always-fresh bone-in chicken wings, fresh custom-ground steak burgers, and locally grown produce whenever possible." As the Monkees sang, "I'm a believer" after having excellent food at each & every location I've visited. Today was no different; my Burger & Blue Salad @ $12.29 was spot on! 799 YUMMY calories & lots of leftovers-- see pic.

The weekly Daily Specials menu is admirable. MONDAY is Burger day ($8.99), as well as Pulled Pork Sandwich & Buffalo Chicken Sandwich day-- each $6.99. On TUESDAY, the savings is on Nachos @ $6.99. Can't have a week without HUMP DAY, when you'll get Wannabe Shrimp for $6.99 plus Wine Bottles @ half price. If it's a THURSDAY you decide to drop in, try the 8 oz Filet Medallions for $12.99, & Fish Fry FRIDAY will cost you $9.99; the fish is battered in Stella Artois.

Happy Hour is "all day every day." Drinks are $5 & $6-- SEE DRINK MENU PICS. 

The large Drink menu is refreshingly eclectic: 6 Speciality Cocktails including Sangrias & Bloody Mary's; 6 Margaritas (Mmmm); 6 Mules & Mojitos; 5 Classics that include a Martini & a Cosmopolitan; 13 Red, White, & Sparkling Wines in glasses & bottles; & 3 tempting alcoholic dessert selections. 

Beer? Did someone say "beer"? There are 3 Beer Coolers @ $16, $22, & $29. And there are beers in cans, bottles, & drafts. I counted 12 Draft beers; 7 American beers; 7 Craft/Import/Premium beers; 2 Gluten-sensitive beers; & 1 Non-alcoholic beer. There's also 3 Hard Selzers. What more could a girl want?! Lol. 

Well, there's also 6 types of Spirits that include Cognac; 14 Cordials/Liqueurs; 4 Gins; 6 Rums; 5 Tequilas; & 14 drinks made w/ Vodka. Beyoncé would be "Drunk in Love" with the variety of booze available here! 

Will I return? The Daily Specials, Happy Hour; fresh ingredients (many local); quality beef; variety of foods; welcoming staff; excellent management; comfortable seating; & the large volume of TVs for easy sports enjoyment will definitely beckon me back. 

"Yeah, Glory Days, they'll pass you by...in the wink of a young girl's eye" if you let 'em. This grown up girl won't let them:) Thank you, George, Amber, additional staff, & the chefs/cooks who made my culinary experience so enjoyable!

4.5 STARS! This relatively new sushi bar & Japanese grill is a WONDERFUL addition to the Lutz area. Its interior is clean, fresh, & modern. The reclaimed natural redwood from the San Francisco Bay area is GORGEOUS! 

There's a beverage bar (yes, alcohol), a sushi bar, tables & chairs separated by plexiglass, three larger more secluded padded booths, & many tables taking center stage on the dining room floor. Service was fast & friendly; Adeline C. was especially good. The thick wooden menus are sanitized after each use & sealed. 

According to the menu, "Zukka-San represents an elevated experience & expanded menu from the first Zukku-San started from a humble 350 sq foot stall inside Tampa's Amateur Works Food Hall. The towering wood patterns of "Koi" fish swimming against a sea of waves were meticulously designed & carved by a local artist." L00K UP to see all the Koi! Truly an aestetically-pleasing restaurant!

Fourteen (14) "Signature Cocktails," nine (9) "Sake," eight (8) "White Wines," one (1) "Rose," seven (7) "Red Wines," three (3) "Bubbly," three (3) "Spiked Seltzers" ($5.50), "Draft Beer" ($6); and Domestic ($4.50) & Imported ($5.50) "Bottles" are available. Non-alcoholic Boba Milk Teas are also served. 

The menu offers 16 "Starters," including Crab Rangoon, three types of Yakitori, Ahi Tuna Tartar, Dumplings, & Baked Mussels. (Our Steak Yakitori was EXCELLENT. Our Shrimp Yakitori was EVEN BETTER-- see pic!)

There are 17 "Masterpiece Sushi Rolls" available. Our Sunset Roll @ $12.95 w/ real crab, Ahi tuna, cucumber, avocado, & cilantro (etc.) was EXCELLENT. The waitress stated that the Dancing Dragon @ $13.95 is a patron favorite. It includes Spicy Ahu tuna, tempura shrimp, tuna, scallions, spicy mayo, & eel sauce, etc. (We returned for it two days later; it was VERY GOOD!)

Seventeen (17) "Nigiri & Sashimi" offerings range from $4.50 to $6.95. Nigiri consists of two pieces-- Sashimi three. Twelve (12) "Classic Rolls" & ten (10) "Hand Rolls" are available; they range in price from $5.95 to $7.95.

If it's Tempura you want, fifteen (15) varities are offered. Five salads & two soups are prepared here. (Our Miso was very good, although a tad more salty than @ many other restaurants-- see pic.)

Eight (8) "From the Wok & Grill" menu items are accompanied by Miso Soup & a Ginger Salad. Prepared entrees include: Fried Rice, Hibachi Noodles, Udon Noodles, Soy Butter Glazed Baked Salmon, Grilled Short Ribs, Chicken Teriyaki, Miso Garlic Scallops, & Miso Garlic Tofu. 

Kids can enjoy a choice of five meals, including Fried Panko Chicken @ $9.95. 

The six desserts sound DELICIOUS: Triple Chocolate Cake, Triple Layer Carrot Cake, Matcha Green Tea Cheesecake, Fried New York Style Cheesecake, Vanilla Bean Shortbread Ice Cream, & Carrot Cake Fried Ice Cream.

Am looking forward to returning soon-- repeatedly returning-- lol! Definitely a very good sushi & grill restaurant. Lots of parking available, as well as Curbside (see pic), Delivery, & Take Out.

4.5 stars. Open 7 days weekly from 11 AM till 10 PM, this long-standing Asian restaurant has been open 16 years. It offers a separate & extensive catering menu. 

The "Keep It Fresh" guarantee: "We believe you should know what you're eating-- you should see it & feel good about it. That's why we use simple, natural, & (when at all possible) local ingredients." 

Select among dine in (in a comfortable setting), outside patio seating, or drive through. The large menu includes: 12 Appetizers ($5 - $10);  4 Kids's meals w/ soda @ $8 ea; 16 Signature dishes ($13.50 - $20); 11 Wok Classics ($13.50 - $15.50); 4 Balanced Options @ $11 - $17; 6 Noodle Dishes ($12 - $14.50); 6 Vegetables; 5 types of Fried Rice entreee ($11 - $13); 4 Salads; 6 Soups; & a page of Lunch Specials that range from $9 - $10. There's also two Lunch A La Cart menu items: Chinese Fried Rice & Lo Mein-- $8 to $9.

Spicy dishes (SP) & Gluten-free (GF) menu items are marked. Most entrees are accompanied by one of the following: white rice, brown rice, or fried rice. 

I ordered the Seared Ahi Tuna (over Seaweed Salad) @ $10. It is VERY GOOD. And I coupled it w/ the Liang's BBQ Ribs appetizer @ $10. The ribs are EXCELLENT. 

My order took approx 15 min to prepare. I could wait inside or step outside before driving to the window for pickup. The interior male greeter was very friendly, as was the male drive-through staffer (11/1/20). 

I am looking forward to returning. The menu appears quite varied & inviting.

Happy Fish. Happy me. Just INCREDIBLE! Everything that passed our lips was SERIOUSLY INCREDIBLE! And there's so much more than fish on the menu. If it's beef, chicken, or multiple types of seafood you want, it's here. There's also pasta, rice, potatoes, & fries. And beer, wine, & Sangria! Ya really need to stop in whether you're a Peruvian food connoisseur or a newbie. You will NOT be disappointed!

Nothing we ate was not PHENOMENAL. From the Beef Empanadas appetizer (traditionally-made w/ minced beef, as well as egg & olives, & nestled within a soft flavorful crust)... to our EXCELLENT entrees... & finally to an OUTSTANDING traditional dessert (to go), we could not have been served better Peruvian food! 

My Tallarin Saltado De Mariscos (Seafood Lo Mein) @ $13.99 was DELICIOUS; it was loaded w/ seafood, which included Calamari, Shrimp, Oysters & others-- see pic. My dining partner's entree (Lomo De Polo) included lots of chicken, as well as onion, tomato, etc. At $13.99, it was supplemented by well-cooked white rice-- see pic. Our To-Go Picarones Con Lucuma @ $9.99 was EXCELLENT & could easily have served 3 or more adults-- see pic. The five warm donuts are made from squash & sweet potato; they are not overly sweet, which was appreciated. The Chancaca drizzle had a hint of cinnamon, & the Lucuma ice-cream was very creamy; its lovely subtle flavor (either caramel or maple) complemented the donuts perfectly. We HIGHLY RECOMMEND this traditional Peruvian dessert....as well as everything else! Some seriously g00000d cooking goes on in this kitchen! 

Open daily, the medium-sized dining room consisted of booths, tables, & a bar. The almost florescent orange exterior & dark colored interior unfortunately detract from the dining experience, but not enough to lower the star count. The owners's niece was friendly & helpful. Her service was very good, & she was also knowledgeable of the full menu (which is large). 

The menu (contact less, if you prefer) is organized by genre (ex. Beef, Chicken, Seafood, etc.) & provides a helpful English explanation w/ every offering. Check out the menu online; a photo of each offering is visible. There's so much to choose from in every food genre that everyone in your party will be able to find an entree s/he likes.

This restaurant is not in an upscale part of Tampa, & some may feel uncomfortable stopping in during evening hours; however, it has over 523 reviews & its rating currently stands @ 4.5 stars. It has EARNED that honor. The recipes used; the immense variety of entrees; the quality of the food; the large servings; pricing; & the knowledgeable, friendly service make this an EXCEPTIONAL eatery!

Delivery is available thru multiple companies. You're forewarned: servers hand out Trip Advisor business cards requesting patrons write reviews:) Let's show these talented local owners some genuine Yelp love!

Hands down the BEST Indian food I've eaten from Tampa to Lake City. A good friend had told me I needed to patronize this restaurant. She said it was frequented by Indians & that she & her husband had never had a bad meal here. They both raved about the naan & all the varieties offered! 

Upon arrival, we decided to each order naan & share four different entrees. We ordered the Garlic, Cheese, Keema, & Kashmiri naan. (Keema is stuffed w/ mince & spiced lamb while Kashmiri is stuffed w/ nuts, raisin & coconut.) ALL were PHENOMENAL-- easily the BEST naan I've ever enjoyed. The latter two were my personal favorites; the Keema offered delicate flavors that melded perfectly while the Kashmari could be called a delicious sweet bread. As a fan of Garlic naan, the naan here BURST w/ flavor. With all the varieties, the texture & consistency of the naan coupled w/ the fabulous flavors make ordering different varieties to share paramount. (I've been told the Onion naan is excellent as well.)

Along w/ the naan, the CHILI SHRIMP appetizer @ $12 was a SHOWSTOPPER-- see pic! I will definitely order it upon our next venture here. And the Samosa was excellent; it had the most flakey outer shell of any Samosa I've eaten. (& I order the appetizer @ each & every Indian restaurant.) 

Our entrees (paired w/ white rice) were perfect-- see pic. The Goat Bhuna ($18), Lamb Saag ($18), Shrimp Vindlo ($20), & Chicken Xacuti ($16) were DELICIOUS! Soooooo good! Even though the more expensive Shrimp Vindlo was very good, the three of us each picked one of the others as a favorite.

This restaurant in Ybor (close to two large paid parking lots) offers a large, outside uncovered patio w/ a beautiful fountain & up close view of the trolley, the Ybor roosters, two sections of an esthetically pleasing dining area, a daily lunch buffet (pre Covid), one large wall TV, & EXCELLENT SERVICE. 

The MENU is extensive-- many dishes offered here that I've never seen on menus from other Indian restaurants. (These's a menu section of vegetarian offerings as well-- see pic.)

I am SO happy my three friends (who are regulars here) finally decided it was time again for Indian food. For me, Rasoi Indian Cuisine is hands down the BEST Indian restaurant in the area! I'm already excited to return!

NOTE: Unless yuu get lucky enough to locate a parallel parking spot on the street, you'll need to pay to park. AVOID the 717 PARKING lot close by. I learned too late that parking is $10-- the near-empty lot should have been my clue. Just one block further away is the City parking lot; it will cost you approximately $1.50 per hour. Don't be a schmuck as I was:)

I've eaten here over two dozen times & picked up food for takout on three ocassion while in town visiting my mum. 

This restaurant draws a large crowd due to its large menu, consistently above average food, its large wooden deck w/ live music nightly, & the fact that the town lacks a large quantity of quality restaurants. There is also a large back room that can be reserved for parties; in February, thirty of my mother's friends joined us for her birthday celebration. Bikers also gather here one night a week. 

I've had only one sub-par entree here, but was quickly contacted by the manager after my complaint; he had me return for a complimentary dinner. 

I come for the whole bellied clams @ market price, but the fried plaintains, sweet potato waffle fries, coleslaw, & hamburgers are very good. Friends have enjoyed the lobster rolls, French onion soup, & salmon. The servings are always large & the prices are decent. There are beer specials, & a bar on the patio. Staff has always been satisfactory to excellent. 

The large outside covered deck is wonderful. Tonight the soloist playing guitar (a regular on Friday nights) was outstanding! Emmet Stevens, Jr. played a medly of alernative songs. He's THAT GOOD, yet still in high school! I shall return on additional Friday evenings-- he's a very talented young man from nearby Dade City. 

I've learned that when a large gathering of bikers return regularly, the food & booze are good. They didn't steer me wrong!

Not the best seafood eatery I've frequented, but definitely an above average one that has such an extensive menu everyone can find something worthy to eat. Parking is limited in front of the restaurant, but after businesses close next door, there is ample parking.

Doin' Chef Irvine's happy dance:) Bern's didn't work out due to problems encountered w/ a reservation for our original party of 10. The six of us ended up here (w/ a reservation) & we voted on the overall rating: 5 voted for five stars w/ one dissenter favoring four stars. (Nobody listens to him anyway:) 

Once your party has arrived (& after you've hopefully made a reservation), you may wait for your table outside on the AstroTurf beside the river-- you'll share your experience w/ canines, a fountain, & wicker chairs & tables. Or you may wait @ the outside bar or on the elongated bench on the main floor. 

From drinks to appetizers to entrees to desserts to coffees to service & finally to ambiance, this was easily a 5 star experience! Six diners w/ not one single complaint is truly an amazing feat! 

The appetizers were all phenomenal: Alligator Hush Puppies, Sea Bass Crudo, & Sea Scallops. Our entrees were excellent: Scallops, Shrimp 'n Grits, Gouda Grouper, Crackling Pork Shank (2), Juan's Snapper, & Seafood Risotto (scallops, shrimp, & lobster claw). The Native Loaded Chili (alligator, venison, & duck) was also excellent. We all sampled the $7 Fortune Taylor's Guava Pie-- delicious! Even the chocolate ice cream was delicious! Our alcoholic beverages, coffee, & espresso were spot on. 

Service by Jamie was very good, & the restaurant's main floor was attractive & comfortable. The six person booth allowed for considerable arm & leg room. 

The vibe of Ulele was simply excellent. Five stars alone for the character of the physical building-- w/ its red brick, black trim, & long staircase to the top floor. Couple this w/ the bustling chatter of satisfied patrons & the  briskly moving eclectic staff balancing overhead serving trays, & you have one visually stimulating evening. There's a palatable industrial feel to the place kissed w/ a touch of class.

Bathrooms were clean, & the very old French stained glass windows were GORGEOUS-- see pic! (Photo courtesy of Katie's amazing Dom Ivenor & his Samsung 8:) There's even a horse in the middle of the floor. Yes, a horse! What more can a gurl ask for in a restaurant! Lol.

This is a no brainer-- I'll return. We all will. And hopefully soon!

4 stars. We received excellent service from Cameron T-- Thank You! 

Our food was very good; the interior of the restaurant was clean, aestetically spacious, & striking; the large bar was gorgeous; but the open front patio area was plagued by the extreme noise of many large cement trucks that regularly haul from a plant nearby. (I recommend you eat inside.)

Our two appetizers were very good-- SEE PICS. The Goat Cheese & Tomato Jam Bruschetta was tasty, but the Crab Stuffed Mushrooms were OUTSTANDING (although few in number).

The Southwest Roasted Wings were delicious, although their skins could have been more crispy, & the very popular Chuckawalla Chicken was moist & flavorful. The three sides were standouts-- SEE PICS of the Steamed Brocolli (in lieu of asparagus), Mexican Street Corn, & Roasted Brussels Sprouts.

My friend LOVED the chocolate flourless cake-- a very rich, decedent cake-- SEE PIC. The Bourbon Mule & two additional alcoholic beverages were prepared well. 

The menu displays 26 wine selections as well as 17 cocktails. Wine countries include Italy, New Zealand, Argentina, Chile, France, Spain, & of course the U.S. (California). 

I may return when in the area again, especially since there's a convenient $3 parking lot nearby & it costs less to dine @ this eatery than in many other Germantown restaurants.

3.5 STARS. This award-winning restaurant is open Sunday thru Thursday 5 PM to 10 PM; Friday & Saturday from 5 PM to 11 PM; & Sundays for brunch from 11 AM till 2:30 PM. Patrons can vie for street parking, use the Whole Foods parking garage @ $12 for 3 hrs, or find a Pay Lot. 

Online reservations are recommended. The last table reservation of the evening is @ 8:30 PM, although there's available bar seating. Co-owner & Executive Chef Menee Chauhan brings her "globally influenced Indian cuisine" to the table nightly. Also available is a "worldwide collection" of beers, cocktails, wines, & spirits. (I posted menu pics.)

After everything we had heard about this November 2014 India fusion restaurant, it was a tad disappointing. 

Although service could have been better (quite the long wait--- the manager finally took our order after we had been forgotten) & tables should have been fully bussed sooner, this review is mainly for the food. It was average at best. And $21 for an average Indian entree is simply too high. 

We were very hungry, so we ate half of the popular Artichoke Pakoras appetizer ($11-- see pic) before our server returned. When he finally appeared & asked us how we liked it, we expressed displeasure at how salty it was-- SO salty. (Without a request, it was removed from our bill, which was appreciated. However, it would have been more appreciated had we been given the choice to order a different appetizer or have the chef remake the one that we originally ordered.)

As for our entrees, the Chicken Tikka Masala & Chicken Korma were simply average-- tasted no differently than how they do at all the quality Indian restaurants I frequent. The only difference here is that the serving sizes (including that of the rice) were smaller yet more expensive, & diners are not asked what spice level they desire. So don't forget to request a side of hot peppers should you prefer some kick. The HIGHLIGHT of our late dinner was the Short Rib French Onion Naan @ $12. It was VERY GOOD. 

The restaurant's narrow interior is eclectic & quite beautiful. Gaze upward to see the white tin ceiling tiles. The decor combines dark brick & solid woods w/ a mixture of peaches, fuchsia, & purple. The low lighting & geometric hanging light fixtures add to the comfortable & interesting ambiance. Truly an aestetically fascinating dining space! 

I do realize that until Tennessee's extended unemployment benefits end July 31, restaurants are likely shortstaffed, so the following did NOT factor into the stars awarded: the one busser (who we saw) allowed the booth across from ours to remain uncleaned (complete w/ dirty dishes & cloth napkins) for much of our meal-- he'd remove a few items, leave, return, & repeat. He then never completely cleared the table on the other side of us-- he came close, but for some reason never finished removing all the dirty dishes. Management was walking the room; why he (or they) didn't step in to assist is beyond me. If I'm going to pay elevated food prices, I definitely want to eat in a comfortable & clean setting.

For parties of 12+; catering; or private dining, submit an online form; staff will reach out to you. 

Will I return the next time I'm up from Tampa? Doubtful. There are just too many highly rated restaurants on my list that I want to try. Nothing we experienced tonight (not the food & not the service) begs our return.

4 stars for the food. 5+ for service in the market & gift store; & more points for somehow making a tourist spot NOT feel tacky & cheap. 

In 1951, Mr. & Mrs. Loveless started serving Biscuits & Fried Chicken through a window. Due to the small business lying on the only route from Nashville to Memphis & due to the quality of the food, Loveless Cafe grew. In 1959, a motel was added. A market; smoke house; gift store; & corn hole games, along w/ a barn & event room were also added. The motel closed in 1985, but the original neon motel sign still greets visitors as they enter the property. This successful business changed hands in 2014 to owners #3-- Chuck & wife Trisha, a local couple unrelated to the Lawless family. (The Lawless children were not interested in taking the reigns.)

Closed every Tuesday, we stopped in the Cafe on a Friday to try the hickory smoked (on site) pulled pork dinner w/ delicious cornbread hoe cakes ($14.49); we chose the country green beans & caramel sweet potatoes for our included sides. With BREAKFAST OFFERED ALL DAY LONG, the Chicken & Waffle @ $10.99 was our second pick. We paid $2.59 each for the caramel sweet potatoes & turnip greens sides that we requested. Serving sizes were LARGE-- SEE PICS! The food was of very good quality & both entrees were VERY GOOD. (I especially liked the C & W, & my daughter loved the Hoe Cakes!)

However, our dinners could have been better had we known that the barbeque sauce would be heavily mixed throughout the pulled pork (not how either of us like it) & had we known the turnip greens are prepared with vinegar. (I detest vinegar.) Neither food item would have been disappointing had the ITEM DESCRIPTION on the menu been more thorough for us to order better. Our waitress also checked on us just once after we started eating; had she returned, I would have requested the Turnip Greens (which sat uneaten) be removed from my bill. She was; however, very friendly. 

I headed to the gift store next to buy a t-shirt, but unfortunately due to a state staffing shortage, the store closes early each day at 4 PM. However, once very friendly SAM in the market realized I was interested in a shirt, she ran across the road to grab a handful of shirts in my size. SAM was just an incredibly outgoing & personable employee-- such as asset to this business! EMMA, too, was great. The market was very clean & well-organized. Make sure you check out the Loveless biscuit mix that's available for purchase. (AND CHECK OUT ALL THE MARKET PICS to see what items are currently sold in the market.)

I returned the next morning to exchange the shirt for one that would hopefully look better on me; the gift shop was open & I had the pleasure of talking w/ sweet KATEY before & after using the available dressing room. I'm unsure where management finds such friendly, excellent young employees, but I truly was W0Wed by the market & gift store service I received over both days! Like the market, the gift store was spotless & beautifully organized. T-shirts were $20 to $30, while the most expensive hoodie was $52. (CHECK OUT THE GIFT STORE PICS to see all the currently available merchandise.)

There's three large corn hole games on the property; I enjoyed watching complete strangers team up to compete against each other. On the Loveless property, even the visitors are very hospitable! 

There's plenty of parking on site. In fact, I counted 3 lots; I took a pic of the largest lot, which resides behind the market. Dogs are welcome on the property. There are picnic tables w/ umbrellas directly in front of the cafe should an accompanying pet preclude you from eating inside. 

If you are planning a wedding or other big event, consider renting the Loveless event center (known as Harpeth Room).

Loveless Cafe & the other buildings on the property bring in the tourists for VERY GOOD REASON-- good food & large servings; quality merchandise (at not exceptionally high tourist prices); excellent & friendly service; clean grounds; & a family-friendly atmosphere. What's not to like?!

LOoOoOoK at the deconstructed pic of my pitiful sandwich! It speaks volumes! 

Due to the two very friendly female staffers, the gorgeous weather, the adorable outside seating, the chill hipster crowd eating & conversing in the sunshine, & the Hispanic music, this eatery of 1 year & 3 months almost earns 4 stars.

HOWEVER, if I am to rate Bodega on the reason it exists (for FOOD & DRINK), it earns two stars. It was a little DISAPPOINTING, to say the least. (Three stars is the compromise.) I did love the vibe, but a vibe w/o great cuisine is just a vibe. 

There's NO smoothie menu, & the varieties are not listed anywhere -- how strange. I listened to the sweet staffer as she spoke of the available smoothies, & I opted for the smoothie that had the word "berries" in it. For $7.05 (not cheap!), I got a smoothie made w/ almond milk. (I opted out of whole milk.) 

It looked absolutely GORGEOUS! But it tasted HORRIBLE -- I swear I tasted COFFEE GROUNDS! And I detest coffee! It was so bad that I tossed the entire drink the moment I arrived home. What the heck was in that smoothie?!!

I should have gone w/ the famed Cuban sandwich (especially after the staffer claimed it's Bodega's best seller), but the $9 coconut marinated chicken sandwich w/ avocado & fresh mango (POLLO ASADA) just sounded too good not to try. 

Unfortunately for me, the sandwich was w/o merit. It had almost NO avocado & NO mango flavor-- see pic! It was practically FLAVORLESS & the chicken was not consistent throughout the sandwich-- some bites had it, some didn't. Really NO FLAVOR to this sandwich! One of the worst I've ever been served.

And sadly there's no reason to return. I'll stick w/ Marino's on Broad St for a great Cuban (on better bread).

5 stars for me, at least w/ regard to Lunch. And, yes, the Roasted Cauliflower @ $10 was absolutely AMAZING. Just DELICIOUS! I NEVER eat cauliflower because I've never liked it, yet I would gladly return for this appetizer.

Closed Sundays, Etch is open Monday thru Thursday, 11 AM to 2 PM, & 4:30 PM to 10 PM. On Friday, it remains open until 10:30 PM. Saturday hours are strictly 4:30 PM till 10:30 PM. 

We made reservations for a weekday lunch, & were surprised @ how reasonable the appetizers, entrees, & desserts were priced. For the quality & quantity, prices were MORE THAN FAIR. Via our cordial & professional young server, Chef Deb Paquette presented us w/ excellent dishes. A graduate of the Culinary Institute of America in Hyde Park, NY, this award-winning chef is Tennessee's first female executive chef. She is also the owner of Etch, an upscale restaurant w/ a beautiful full bar; two private dining rooms; & even a chef's bar where patrons can speak w/ her as she works. According to the webpage, Chef Deb has an "eclectic menu that incorporates innovative dishes inspired by her favorite regions of the world..."

Along w/ the excellent cauliflower appetizer, the Fried Cornmeal Catfish @ $13 was BEYOND EXCELLENT. Definitely the BEST CATFISH either one of us has ever eaten! And the Argentinian Beef Tenderloin @ $15 was VERY GOOD. We were too full to opt for dessert, although we would have loved to try the Chocolate & Pretzel Mousse ($9); Peach & Raspberry Pavlova ($9); Olive Oil Almond Cake ($9); Ice Cream Sundae ($9) or the House Made Ice Cream or Sorbet @ $3.

HAPPY HOUR offers four specials that are priced $8 to $24, including the Roasted Cauliflower @ $8 instead of $10. Also available are four drinks ($8 to $10). Happy Hour is Monday thru Friday 4:30 PM to 6 PM, & Saturday from 4:30 PM to 5:30 PM. 

I posted menu pics downloaded from Etch's website. All the dishes are unique to this restaurant-- all are very creative. Along w/ the impressive eclectic menu, another reason to make a reservation here is the beautiful, clean dining area in downtown Nashville. I LOVED the long, gorgeous bar & the windows that line one entire side of the dining room, allowing for sunlight to filter in. I noticed many a business lunch occurring @ tables; w/ the fair prices for lunch, if I worked downtown I'd stop in weekly to eat w/ my coworkers. 

You're definitely on your own for parking. Etch does not have a lot. The public lots aren't inexpensive, so Ubering here may be best. Etch definitely lived up to its reputation as a top Nasville restaurant serving innovative New American fare. We walked out full & happy:)

3.5 stars for this restaurant that opened its doors on Nov 19, 2020. The following is printed on the menu: "Begun in friendship, nurtured by family and continued by community, our vision of Casa Santo Stefano offers a look back to Sunday suppers, simpler times and shared stories." 

With its dark wood walls; high ceiling; rich accent colors; & eclectic yet sophisticated 1st floor decor (coupled w/ higher than average pricing), Nana's family kitchen did not come to mind. And after a cursory look around, it was obvious that many of Casa Santo Stefano's diners are far more affluent. 

Prices for the nine appetizers ranged from $6 to $22. Offered were eight sides from $6 to $8. The four salads & one soup ranged in price from $5 to $14; and the twelve pastas were $12 (vegetarian) to $24. The thirteen "Traditional Plates" cost between $22 & $38. You'll shell out $6 to $10 for each of the seven desserts. 

If it's wine you want, you'll find 48 varities sold by the glass and/or bottle. The least expensive glass was $8, while the highest priced bottle was $140. 

I had hoped to leave 4.5 or 5 stars, but unfortunately there were too many little disappointments; they added up to more than what I find acceptable when I lay out approximately $90 for my dinner alone.

With a 7:30 PM first floor reservation, we were a party of six drinking & enjoying our round table on the second floor when we were notified to come downstairs for our table (15 min late). After heading downstairs, we learned there had been an error, but only after one in our party had to continually initiate inqueries. Three separate times he was told, "We're cleaning your table," as we stood uncomfortably lingering in the path of other patrons for 20+ minutes. Not cool. Even less cool is the fact that not only were we the ones reaching out to staff for answers, but management never approached us to offer an apology. It was great that the owner Richard walked the floor & spoke w/ different tables of patrons, even providing an earlier tour to three diners (SEE PIC), yet a tad insulting that we six did not earn his attention. (Richard proudly owns the successful Columbia as well.)

Once seated at our corner table, we did score a very good waiter who possessed a lovely accent: Mateo. And we enjoyed our appetizers & one side: Scacciata Siciliana ($6); Calamari Fritti ($16); Antipasti Salumi E Formaggi ($16); & Meatballs Della Nana ($8 Side). "Della Nana" represents a Tampa-Sicilian recipe; the meatballs were delicious. (They & the Calamari were the showstoppers.)

Brought to every table was individual warm bread w/ seasoned dipping oil; it received rave reviews-- excellent, as well as very filling. 

Our entrees; however, received mixed reviews. While the duo of "K & K" loved their $18 Spaghetti Con Polpette ($18) & Scaloppine Di Pollo Al Marsala ($22) w/ a substitution of potatoes-- SEE PICS, "D" was not thrilled w/ the bland sausage & dry noodles of his $22 Spaghetti Nana Maria; it was followed by a request for salt. And while "KT" felt her Spaghetti Al Nero Con Polpo @ $24 was good, it just not great. Our "P" enjoyed his $22 Bucatini Con Le Sarde, although it was just "good." I really liked my Linguine w/ Lobster. For $36, it was somewhat sweet, but w/ a hint of spice from red pepper. There was sufficient lobster woven throughout the perfectly-cooked pasta. It was also a generous serving. (I would order it again; on Day 2 it's still delicious.)

We ordered just two desserts-- the Panna Cotta ($8) & the Affogato Al Cafe ($10). Both were quite good. There were others from which to choose, as well as Liqueurs; Amari; Grappa; Spirits; Espressos; Doppio; Latte; & Macchiato. 

The 1st floor restaurant appeared very clean w/ its variety of tables & chairs; booths; & sectioned off dining areas. The restaurant was full to capacity w/ a 60+ minute wait for those w/o reservations (even at 9 PM.) The second floor differed greatly in style & had a separate menu, along w/ outside tables w/ umbrellas. I enjoyed the owner's artwork that lined the upstairs walls, as well as his family photos dating back at least two generations. Bathrooms on both levels were clean, as well as interesting-- of course I snapped a PIC-- the red was a draw. There's a second floor stand-alone wine room that can be viewed from the first floor dining area, as well as a bar to the right after you enter from the street. 

The receipt provided each of us w/ a "Suggested Gratuity" of 18%; 20%; & 22%-- definitely not reminiscent of my Nana's Sunday supper with family:)  

There was convenient parking across the small street; the lot is reserved for patrons of The Columbia & Cafe Santos Stefano. 

We'll return. The restaurant has been open just a little over five months. As w/ all restaurants, floor staff; chefs; cooks; & even management require time to acclimate. We'll give them time before returning to sample additional entrees & acquire second helpings of those very good appetizers.

3.5 stars. Definitely NOT a bad buffet. The quantity & quality of food is not @ issue. The good service & spacious, clean dining area w/ tables & booths are not @ issue, although the brown room decor is outdated. The extended hours & cleansing table @ the entrance are also not an issue. 

What IS @ issue is the $17.99 cost per person when almost all of the food offerings are low in cost. Yes, there are cold crab legs, cold shrimp, sushi, sashimi, & crawfish, but no combination is worth $17.99 unless the diner makes multiple trips to the food bars for those few specific items. For $17.99, I expected to see more higher priced/higher quality prepared foods. 

The beautiful food bar (w/ its pink lighting) consists of many sections-- appetizers, salads, cold entrees, hot entrees, a sushi bar, a Mongolian barbecue (which wasn't available upon our visit), desserts, & ice creams. The food bar was clean & well stocked. 

The cost of an adult meal jumped $1 to $17.99 due to Covid. Even @ $16.99, the cost would be too high. I wont return; I simply don't eat enough to justify spending the money. The two individuals I covered also didn't eat enough to sanction a subsequent visit. (At $9.99 per person, I'd return, but that ain't ever gonna happen:)

Check in to save $5 off a $25+ order. Miss MARY was phenomenal-- friendly, attentive, fast, & professional. She was so sweet; she brought me extra blue cheese because she was worried that my special order wings might be too dry. Whenever we needed her attention, she was at our table quickly. 

The wings were really good (not dry) & our catered entrees of pasta, Greek salad, chicken tenders, Shepherds Pie, & Cuban sandwiches was very good as well...or so I was told by six table mates who laughed @ me for taking pics for Yelp:) 

This Irish pub has an excellent staff (everyone was very friendly), there's a live band (unsure of the nights, but definitely Friday & Saturday), & the food is quite standard pub fare (& good). There are six TVs on the wall. If I lived in the area, I'd definitely stop in for booze & finger foods on a regular basis. Just a comfortable atmosphere. 

If you need a venue to hold a work or sports related (etc.) event, the staff here puts out a great spread & follows up w/ excellent, friendly service. Kudos to everyone! 

Go rainh maith agat!

4.25 stars rounded up for this pizzeria chain. The first & last time I was here was just shy of 4 yrs ago. I'm happy I stopped in today while visiting the area. My food was VERY GOOD. If I had wanted beer or wine, it was available-- 16 rotating taps & wine! W-h-o-a!

This is a clean, spacious, aestetically-pleasing eatery that makes an excellent place to gather for birthdays; retirement parties; sports celebrations; a large gatherings of friends; or just an easy, but tasty, family dinner. I stopped in & enjoyed my spot @ the small bar. Wall TVs are viewable from every seat in the restaurant. The dining room was clean & bright, as was the bathroom-- one for males & one for females. 

There's one four-person metal table outside complete w/ an umbrella-- perfect place to sit if your favorite furry companion accompanies you. 

Diners can see the open kitchen as they eat. If you insist that patrons & staff all be masked, this is not the pizzeria for you. (Pasco recently removed the mask mandate; this business allows individuals to choose to wear a mask or not.)

My NY Pizza was very good-- as I had remembered. The cheese definitely tasted fresh. I also loved the small Antipasto Salad that was well-stocked w/ meat, cheese, tomatoes, black olives, etc. Fresh & delicious! (My PICS are To Go pics; I ate a few bites on site before heading home.) 

My server was very young & he was pleasant; however, he had worked here no more than a handful of shifts, so he made a few understandable errors. I'm confident he will be excellent in no time. I do wish the white-haired gentleman working in the open kitchen while overseeing the dining room had bothered to smile or offer a greeting. Even though he made eye contact with me a few times, he offered nothing. I recall the same behavior four years ago. I believe he was in charge. 

Should you stop in interested in an appetizer, on the menu are 14 "Starters," including Johnny's Bruschetta; Fried Ravioli; Fried Calamari; & Mac & Cheese Bites. There are many wing varieties--  Firecracker, Leprechaun, Citrus Chipotle, Barbalo, & 9 more. I counted 6 Salads & 4 Flatbreads on the large menu. 

Offered are 3 Wraps, 7 Subs, & 4 Parmigiana Subs @ $9.75 each. Burgers anyone? There's an All-American Burger, as well as a Firecracker Burger-- each $9.99. (Toss in an additional .99 to add bacon.)

Baked here are 13 Speciality Pizzas. Slices are $3.99 & $4.99. Medium pizzas range from $13.99 to $19.99, & Large from $17.99 to $23.99.

There are SPECIALS Monday thru Friday from 11 AM till 4 PM. Soda or iced tea accompany each-- Pizza, Stromboli, Calzone, Sub, Wrap, & Spaghetti. There's also a $39.95 Family Meal dinner; a Buy 1 Get 1 Italian Dinner deal, as well as $2 off any large pizza. Daily Specials on Beer & Wine are also available. 

Three Stromboli varieties & three separate Calzones are on the menu, along w/ 15 Regular Toppings; 15 Speciality Toppings; & 5 Premium Toppings. 

Want fewer carbs? Order a 10" pizza w/ a Cauliflower Crust. There's also a 10" Gluten-free pizza for anyone w/ the allergy.  

Dine-in, take-out, delivery, order online and curbside pickup are available. 

Johnny Brusco's is a very good chain pizzeria that is clean & spacious. It offers quality foods; beer & wine; & lots of space to meet w/ groups. When I'm in the area again wanting fast & delicious Italian food, I won't hesitate to occupy a seat inside.

As you peer thru the large window on Broadway, your eyes will feast on dozens of freshly made Caramel Apples & warm Pralines.  It is difficult to walk by this large candy store w/o stopping!

This is a large chain location that originated in  Georgia. It's open 10 AM to 10 PM Sunday thru Thursday, & 10 AM till 11 PM on weekends. Other state locations include South Carolina, Maryland, and soon Florida (Miami). This truly is a large & very busy candy store on Broadway that also sells many flavors of Gelato. Do NOT stop in expecting to find great prices on candy! 

Most of the candy is not made at this franchise. It's shipped it from the parent company. (The popular pralines, as well as the chocolate and/or caramel dipped apples are made on site.) The assortment of candies is extremely large, which is a positive. However, oddly there are NO PRICES ON MUCH OF THE CANDY you'll find here, & that includes the prepackaged candy-- see pic! And there are few labels as well. Not posting prices is a mind blower (for me), but apparently tourists are not hesitating to buy. 

The two cases of Gelato to the rear of the store hold many varities-- SEE PIC. A single serving is $4.95 for a regular cone & $5.95 for a waffle cone. Doubles are $6.95 & $8.95. My daughter is a huge fan of the Banana Pudding flavor. Rootbeer Floats & Milkshakes are $6.95.

We purchased Chocolate Raspberry Truffles; Dark Chocolate Coconut Clusters; Pralines (EXCELLENT); Milk Chocolate Pecan Gophers; Salted Milk Chocolate Caramels; & prepackaged candy for kids. Unsure of how much we paid for the non packaged candies, we do know they were expensive-- our two combined bills totalled approx $110. (The prepackaged candy actually cost the most.)

There's pretty much every candy available here-- which patrons will line up to purchase at the large oval display case in the center of the store. (There were just two center area cashiers for much of the time we were in the store; however, a third finally joined in after the bulk of the customers had finished w/ their purchases.) 

This is definitely a candy shoppe any kid would love-- SEE PICS. This is not a candy shoppe to visit if you are on a budget or hate to stand in line...or want to know ahead of time how much the candy costs per pound PRIOR to standing in line.

There is a convenient ATM on the premises.

Should of, would of, could of been a 4+ star experience. The food was spot on! The service; however, was perhaps the worst I've ever experienced in decades of dining out. 
 
What occurred tonight might be described as a comedy of errors--  had it not been intentional & far shy of funny. We had 6:45 reservations for dinner on the porch (on Super Bowl Sunday). Take eight steps in our dining shoes:

1. Our waiter had to serve only us two patrons the ENTIRE time. Not knowing what a Yelp check-in offer was, after he took our appetizer order he (w/ my permission) took my phone somewhere to show someone the free glass of house wine offer. He was gone way too long.
2. He returned w/ our appetizer & to ask what kind of wine I would like. He then hurriedly ran off to get the wine... WITH my phone & WITHOUT leaving us any plates. Without my phone, I couldn't even take a pic of the appetizer. Without plates, I managed to spill food on the table...twice. 
3. He finally returned my phone before leaving to retrieve two plates. Only he never returned! We waited & waited. Unable to locate him, I finally walked inside to the bar (whose bartender was MIA as well). I decided to stand on my tippy toes & awkwardly stretch across the width of the bar to reach two small plates on the shelf behind the bar. (I'm sure the couple @ the bar thought I was nuts; I intentionally avoided eye contact:)
4. When our server returned to learn if we liked the appetizer, he didn't even recall that he had never brought us plates! (Thankfully, the Gorgonzola Garlic Bread was Very Good-- see pic.)
5. A friendly young woman, not our waiter, delivered our entrees. Our Basa Meuniere entrees were delicious-- see pic. 
6. We decided to share a dessert. I couldn't be sure if our waiter had heard my request for the Espresso Caramel Cream (see pic). WHY? Because once he heard a cheer emanate from the outside lower level, he BLURTED out, "I might have won again!", then quickly whipped his body around & RAN. Yes, RAN off while we were still speaking w/ him! (Surreal!)
7. However, he apparently had heard my request because we received the dessert (see pic), but unfortunately we received it w/ the two spoon bodies up against the dessert...& sticky. (For photo purposes, I moved the sticky spoons.) Is it possible he didn't see the spoons??? Who knows. Off he went...AGAIN! 
8. Just when we thought the saga of poor service had come to a dismal end, our distracted server returned w/ our checks & credit cards, & in record speed set them on the table in front of us. He turned then scurried off... leaving each of us w/ the OTHER'S credit card & check. LORD HAVE MERCY!

My friend (& her husband) are regulars here. They speak highly of the owner. They really like the food & have always had good service. I liked the food. I HATED the service. And unfortunately, service is a large part of the dining experience. Our experience was crappy. (I even omitted Step #9:) 

I do hope our waiter enjoyed the game & won some cash... because I tipped just 15% & wrote "Service was terrible" on my receipt (#9003). I'll definitely be back (just NEVER on a game day). I do want to give this area favorite (not our waiter) another try. The kitchen did not disappoint & the menu offers appealing entrees along w/ many drinks.

UPDATE: Within 24 hrs, a server saw my review & notified management...who immediately messaged me. I've been asked to return, request her, & I'll be compensated. Speaks volumes to the professionalism of management! I'm impressed--

4.5 stars rounded up! This North Austin-based Ramen eatery first opened in May 2012... as a food truck! It took just a few months for Michi's first Brick & Mortar eatery to open. And in 2015, it earned the honor of "Best Ramen" in Austin. At that time, Michi offered two basic broths. One was Miso-based while the other was soy-based. There are currently 3 Austin locations.
