This spot was surprisingly not packed around noon on a Saturday morning, and I plan to be back here for a quiet weekend morning with quality food and service that won't break the bank.

If you enjoy being on your back for the 48 hours post-dinner writhing in pain, burning up, and exploding out of all orifices then this is the restaurant for you.

Went here for a banquet that had over 200 attendees on Feb 27. A large number of people got a stomach virus and in some cases it was so bad that they had to go to the ER. Needless to say I will not be eating here anymore.

http://www.philly.com/philly/health/special_reports/clean-plates/20150327_Dozens_sickened_at_banquet.html

I have to give this place 5 stars for the service, if nothing else. My friend had just finished taking the bar exam, which unfortunately overlapped with our anniversary, so I thought it would be nice to treat her to a good dinner. Word on the street has been that Valanni has the best paella in the city. Having never had paella before (and my friend having studied in Spain), I thought this would be a good place to go. It really did not disappoint. 

As for the food, there are 3 different options for the paella--seafood, mixed seafood and other protein, and vegetarian. They also offer two different portion sizes: enough for one or two. As a meat lover, naturally I went for the combination. And as a tip, anyone who goes should double that portion size in their head, because even though the dish may look small, there is A LOT of good stuff in it (read: a lot of meat and seafood). I did not think my hunger would be satisfied by splitting a paella meant for one, but boy was I wrong. It was more than enough food for two people.

Additionally, we got the beef kabobs, which I personally liked but my friend thought was fairly underseasoned. They also used this sauce that tasted eerily like A1. Lastly, we ordered the lobster macaroni and cheese, which I had also heard was one of the best items on their menu. Again, while the dish itself looks small, it is filling (as well as delicious) and they do not skimp on the lobster meat. 

Now, with regards to the service, I was blown away. Everyone from the hostess to our waitress was so gracious and helpful. They also gave my friend and I complementary champagne to celebrate her finishing the bar. However, people should be aware that Valanni is not for those looking for a quiet night out. The atmosphere is very hip, the music is fun, and the decor is extremely modern. But that is exactly what we wanted, so I was perfectly fine with it. 

Overall, a great meal and a great way to celebrate the end of my friend's reign of bar-studying-induced terror.

The setting is interesting and unique. The food is okay, not great but good, with decent variety. But the service is so lackadaisical as to be almost non-existent. The only grown ups here seem to be the customers, with the staff comprised of unsupervised teenagers. They're not bad kids, but they haven't the faintest clue about customer service. And no one has taught them. And nobody is there to check on them. 

If this restaurant fails, they will have deserved it for not paying attention to the most important ingredients, the PEOPLE. And that includes both the customers they ignore, and the poor kids they inflict upon them.

Mmmmm I love this place!! Great vibe, great food, great prices!! It's right next to the harbor and you get to see sea lions swimming around. It's such a busy area, ppls taking kayak lessons, lots of eye candy around. 

My friend surprised me with all the dining we did in Santa Barbara and this place was a hit. Even though we were there during the day, it seems like a local hangout bar. Everybody was super nice, all the waiters/waitess were also super cool. 

Now the food, oh gosh great seafood at a affordable price. We started with spicy Bloody Mary's, they went perfectly with our meals. 
We also ordered the dozen raw oyster, they were nice and sweet no gritty taste.

Dungeness Crab Platter $13.25 (was my fave thing, so much crab meat for such little price. Sweet, juicy crab meat...Mmmmmm i want more)

I also had a cup of there yummy Clam Chowder w/ the soft sourdough bread.

Cioppino-Fish Stew, Topped w/ Parmesan (my friend ordered this, I didn't get to try it but heard it was delicious :)

I will definitely be back to enjoy the food and ppls here.

This place used to be known as 38th Pizza and Korean food, but ever since it changed owners and is now called "Koreana", it focuses solely on Korean food. I'm told the Korean food now tastes better (but I can't really judge, because I never visited it before the change).

I used to called it the $6 place, because all their dishes used to cost that much. Unfortunately, they've raised the prices slightly, but I enjoy their food. It's not stellar, but in way of close, cheap and fast Korean food around the UPenn area, you can't go wrong with Koreana.

Try their bulgogi or kalbi, traditional Korean dishes they don't ever mess up. Their noodle dishes are alright, but don't ever seem to fill me up. Lastly for dessert, there's always the Korean shaved ice - a cute fun way to end any date if you're nearby.

Update-May 6. I took off a star (so now it's 3 stars) because the quality of this joint has gone down. For example, their pork meat doesn't taste like meat anymore. Prices have also gone up (which is understandable with the crazy world food situation at the moment), but I'm disappointed in Koreana's lack of adherence to quality. The ONLY dish worth getting now is their kalbi.

I came here with the understanding that it was transgender friendly but I was rudely greeted with "hey dude" following continuous malicious male pronouns usages. . my friend bought a burger and when it was delivered the comment was made, "killer." I'm a vegetarian personally but why serve meat if youre so strongly against it? I didn't dare to use the restroom so we left and went to the gelato house down the street where we were warmly invited. I think its ironic that I went to the salvation army later that day and I was treated with more respect there. Fascists. Wolves in sheep's clothing. I will be telling all my trans friends not to go here.

As a COVID era meal, this spot did a great job of social distancing. We sat outside and the waitress was great, the tables were distant, food was good, and the ambiance was good. 

What was unacceptable was the treatment a man received from the manager/owner maybe? Not sure- a middle aged woman with brown hair. There was a homeless man wandering in the restaurant area, talking to tables. I understand the concern that this is ruining the ambiance and bothering the customers. I get It. BUT this man is a human being and this woman absolutely treated him as less than. 

He approached a table behind us, requesting something- not sure if It was food, money, or what. The table was about to give him whatever It was when you hear the woman BARRELING over SCREAMING at them not to- a loud "NO NO NO NO NO" (talk about ruining the ambiance). 

She ushered the man away and was loudly speaking that she was going to call the cops, she "isn't doing this today" etc. Drew so much attention to the situation, and this man was being totally silent back. 

I do not think the man should have been allowed to stay walking around the dining area. But causing a scene with the simple intention of embarrassing this man, just looking for his next meal? He's a person too, and this was disgusting and inhumane treatment for someone who was not causing a scene. 

You made a whole lot of customers feel uncomfortable today. 

This country's homeless problem is out of control- we all know that. But show some humanity this holiday season. Offer a glass of water and something warm to this man and maybe he won't have to ask tables.

st louis' go to bbq a lot like pappy's.  bogarts has better prices especially on large orders.

i didn't like their sides nearly as much but the ribs and the sandwiches were great.  line out the door but they had some shade and a menu so you were completely ready to order and had stuff to do.  bring a friend!

small place but again their staff was on it and letting you know which table to go to when you got your food.  good stop!

tl;dr as good as pappy's for less money.  but the sides are just okay when pappy's are great.

don't have any ZERO STAR to vote for them. Anw, it took us an hour just for appetite. The foods were cold and salt. also, their staff are so mean. I am not sure the know how to run a business. STRONGLY recommend DO NOT TRY. WORST TRIP EVER. 


母親他媽的

This restauration is located right in the heart of the shopping/eating area of KOP.   

Parking is tough and I parked a few blocks away but it was nice out so not a big deal.

We had a large party for Sunday brunch.   The service was great.  The food was amazing.  

The salad bar had a nice selection of items so my salad was very tasty.

The meat selection was good.

I left with a full stomach.

I'll definitely be back.

[659]

Visited this Harrah's location a few time and was not disappointed.  

The racetrack was closed the day I visited so not sure how popular or cool it is but I can say the seats were great as they are not on top of each other.

There are a few restaurants which  I did not try (yet).  They have a Starbucks.   

There are overpriced ATMs in the building ($6 fee).

Plenty of free offstreet parking.

The place is not huge but it's big enough that you won't have an issue grabbing a table or machine.

They have a self serve soda machine. 

There is a VIP section for Diamond members.

I'll definitely be back.

[946]

6/25/2019

This Olive Garden is located on busy Baltimore Pike.

Plenty of parking available.

The staff is very friendly and the restaurant is clean.

I love the breadsticks and minestrone soup.

The soda was flat so I switched to water.

The food came out while we were in the middle of our soup.  We had to take it (who sends food back).  We felt a bit rushed because of this.

I had the grilled chicken on pasta $14.  It was just ok as the one piece of chicken was really small.   I should have just ordered the soup and breadsticks

Hubby had chicken parm which he enjoyed.

Kid had the chicken tender kids meal.  He had a few small chicken pieces.  He doesn't like pasta so that was a waste as we could not substitute it for more chicken or grapes.   He was still hungry after his kids meal.

Hubby had potato soup which he loved.

We spend about $50 and felt like a waste :( 

Probably won't come back.

[828]

This Spasso Italian Grill location is located in the heart of Media.  

Plenty of metered parking (parking deck is 1/2 block away).  

We came here a few years ago and really enjoyed the food so we wanted to try it again.  I'm glad we did as we really enjoyed our experience.

Appetizers - 
Grilled Calamari - I never had it grilled but I am glad I tried it.  It was tasty and different from what I'm used to.
Arancini-  It was ok.  I didn't like it but hubby did enjoy it.

Dinner
Veal Parmigiana - Hubby had this and enjoyed it.  
Gnocci - Since it was homemade we wanted to try a plate.  Glad we did as you can taste the freshness in every bite.
Chicken Fontinella-  topped with asparagus, fontina & roasted peppers.  I saw a picture of this and it's as tasty as it looks (check out my pic)
Chicken fingers - The kid has this which he enjoyed.

Dessert
Chocolate mouse cake- We ordered one slice but we should have ordered two.  We ate every last piece.  

Our server Pete was very attentive and helpful.

We will definitely be back.

Updating to reflect the amazing service we received for our party of 30+.

We came at opening so we were able to reserve the back room for our private party.  We had about 30 people and the room holds about 50.  It was nice to give a range of guests expected and not be locked into an exact number.  

We originally expected 20-25 guests but ended up with a bunch more.  They quickly set up more tables which we used as a "kids table" (they loved it as they had their own space) and a "teen table".  Everything was perfect.

We were provided with 3 servers which were amazing.  They were very attentive and helpful.   

Our reservation was at 4 but they allowed us to come in earlier.  They put our beer and wine on ice (it's a BYOB) and served it to our guests throughout the night.  At the end they packed it up for us to take back home.

All our food was brought out at the same time which was  great.  I did not hear about a food mistake or error.  Everyone enjoyed their food.  The portions were huge so most of us had leftovers to take home.

We choose their dinner package (set price) which came with a salad, entree and desert.   You can add endless apps for $X but we decided to pick our own (I think we had about 12+ apps for the group) which were ready for us when our guests arrived.    Guests had the option from about 10+ items and then specials were added which included steak.    Dessert - everyone had tiramisu (I think I picked it in advance).   The kids wanted chocolate cake and the staff happily provided them with the amazing looking piece.    Dinner also included soda and coffee.

All in all. It was a perfect group dinner and if I need another place to entertain this will be my first option.

[1083]
2/2020

Plenty of parking at this Philadelphia location.  We used valet.

We had a table of 8 near the inside waterfall (?) which was nice as we can see outside.

We ordered a ton of stuff which we enjoyed most.  It was more a hit or miss.

The clam chowder was watery and boring.   The lobster bisque soup was tasty.   

Appetizers we ordered
The coconut crunchy shrimp was tasty
Shrimp cocktail was tasty.
Kim Chee Calamari was good
Oysters on the half shell was good
Crab cakes tasty
Charred Octopus - first time trying and I enjoyed it

Dinner - Shrimp and Scallops - $39.  WOW what a disappointment.  I can't believe I paid $39 for 3/4 shrimp and 3/4 UNDERCOOKED scallops.  I made my husband try the scallops ...  I'm so sad about this.  I WANTED to say something  but we were there for a birthday and I didn't want to spoil it.   The waiter saw I didn't eat much and wanted to wrap.  I wish he would have asked if it was ok because who doesn't wrap a $39 dish they don't eat.

Our servers (one was in training) were horrible.  Very nice young men but they were horrible.  They both needed to be trained.   Kept interrupting..  forgot soup spoon.. rolls were brought AFTER dessert.  ..water was forgotten..   twice coffee took forever and the standard line was "making a fresh pot" was code for I forgot.   

Anyway I won't be back.  I just don't see it unless we only come for appetizers.

[1095]

8/2020

Plenty of parking at this location.  The restaurant is located in a strip mall on Baltimore pike. Great location.

This PF Changs location knows how to properly seat people while adhering to local social distancing laws/norms.

We made a reservation for lunch and were promptly seated.

The staff was friendly and helpful.

I really like the decor in this chain restaurant (last time I was here was over 10 years ago).  

Hubby had the Mongolian beef which he loved.  I would definitely have this dish next time I visit.  

I had the chicken fried rice.  It was good!

Kid had chicken tenders which he loved.

We will definitely be back.

[602]

This is one of the local places which are loved by many.  I tried this place around 10 years ago and this is my first time returning since and I remember why.

Parking is horrible and tight and every second I was afraid someone would back into my car in the small lot.

There is a line by the front entrance to sit to eat.  No one comes by to see if smaller tables can be filled.  You just wait near a ton of quarter toy machines while your kids beg for nonsense toys.

The booths need to be refurbished.  When I sat I nearly sat on the floor .. no cushion left in that bad boy.

Ordered the double burger (waitress suggested I get two since they were small).   I also had lettuce, tomato and fried onions on it.  The little red baskets are like bowls and awkward to eat my food especially w/ onions.  My whole basket was greasy which made it visually unappealing.   

Had a small order of fresh fries which were very tasty.  It was big enough to feed all 4 of us so I can only imagine the large bowl.

Ordered a diet coke and it tasted very off/different.  Then I noticed the signs that said "Nifty Cola" so I guess they have their own soda.  I asked the waitress if it was diet coke.  She said YES! So it's either really off or she doesn't realize Diet coke is different from Diet Nifty cola.  Ended up drinking water.

Kids had a chicken tender kids meal which was great since the chicken was not frozen.  They enjoyed it.

We each had a milkshake.  Tons to pick from... mine was ok.  The kids enjoyed theirs.. well half.  The shakes are too big.  Too bad they don't make it half the size and price.  We tossed half of our 4 shakes.  

I know many locals like this place but it's not for me.

I will not be back.

Walked past this cool looking place so we decided to stop.  

The large store has plenty of room for seating and enjoying your treat.

They sell coffee, drinks, pastries and ice pops.  The ice pops seems to be the major item. Many different types with two sizes. 

Ordered the banana, pineapple and mango in a large $4.

It was very tasty and you can taste the food in each bite.

Can't wait to come here during the summer to sit and enjoy another fruit pop.

I'll definitely be back.

[887]
4.6.2019

This juice bar is located in Reading Terminal Market.  

Each time we stop here we have a smoothie.  

All the fruit is fresh and you can taste it in the drink.

Most of their drinks combos have carrots.    You can even get drinks with wheatgrass.

I'll definitely be back

[624]

This diner is located in Reading Terminal Market and confidently opens for breakfast before the terminal opens.  

Stopping in on a Saturday morning for breakfast before our road trip and was pleasantly greeted by the staff.  

Our food was brought out quickly and to order.   We ate all our food and had no complaints 

Kid had scrambled eggs which he loved.  I had scrambled eggs w home fries which I also enjoyed.  Loved the chunks of fresh potatoes.   Hubby had eggs and steel cut oatmeal which he enjoyed.

They have a counter where you can order and eat which is really cool.  

Not sure about the lunch menu but we definitely enjoyed our breakfast 

I'll definitely be back

3.5 stars. The bread was stuffed with steak and topped with big chunks of lightly fried onions. I tried a piece of the steak on its own and was extremely bland. Each ingredient needs to stand on its own and the sandwich could've benefited from just a little salt. All in all it was a decent cheesesteak. It's definitely a neighborhood (and city wide) favorite.

Estia is absolutely amazing. I have been coming to both this and the Philly location for years JUST for their incredible weekday lunch special. My husband and I like to come here for lunch dates when we can to split the greek salad & chicken souvlaki. Both of these dishes are SO delicious and fresh and do not compare to any other greek food we've had - EVEN in Greece! It is only $19 for the 2 course menu, and actually plenty to share between the 2 of us - especially after filling up on the complimentary bread and hummus they serve when you sit down.

We've recently started to come here for happy hour and dinner but we love the lunch menu the best. They have a different offering at dinner and do not have the chicken souvlaki (bummer!). Our new favorite dinner order is to split the trio of dips and the moussaka. The moussaka is a bit different than I've had elsewhere but still very tasty. The cream sauce has a strange texture (almost egg-y/jello-ish) and it is served in a round shaped stack.

I highly recommend this location for anytime but lunch especially. Outdoor seating is great and the decor inside is REALLY pretty and looks exactly like some of our favorite spots in Mykonos.

BEST CANNOLI EVER!

*Clouds in the sky parted, sun beams rays directly down on Termini, heavenly angels sing, and this cannoli appeared to bring joy and delight to all those on earth.*

Choice of fillings: Chocolate, Vanilla, Cheese & Chocolate Chips.  The later of which is what I had.  

$3.00 for one and worth every penny!  Perfectly crunchy pastry shell, smooth, sweet, cream with chocolate chips, powdered sugar sprinkled on top. Thank God for the local Philadelphian who send me here for one.  WOW!  I nearly fainted with delight.

(They have other items too... candy, sfogliatelle - baked ricotta cheese, orange peel. and cinnamon, fig bars, cookies, coconut macaroons, cakes of all kinds,)

This stuff is so good that you can order it and have it shipped anywhere in the US.  6 cannoli for $40, 12 for $60.  Order them for a party and you won't be sorry!  You can also call their 800 number - 800-882-7650.

Urban Saloon's one big room, but still a decent spot to enjoy a beer. There's room for friends and then some: when I was there, it was chock full of folks watching the Phils spar against the Yankees on several flatscreens. A projector was set up, too, but I'm unsure if that's normal. In any event, it got loud. Thankfully, there was no cover.

I've heard good things about brunch, and will have to return for that.

Find them near the Eastern State Penitentiary.

The Malvern Buttery is the best place to be stood up.

Why? Their unlimited bread bar will keep you busy. $4 (as of press time; credit accepted) scores you as much fresh baked bread as you want. Top your slices with organic butter, and the best dang peanut butter and blueberry jelly around. So good you should write to your mom about it once you've had it.

I LOVE THIS PLACE[2]. I'm still glad they've, er, STUCK around after all this time - my first visit being May last year.

Walk in, order your coffee[1], grab a pastry or savory item off their bar, nosh, then pay on your way out. Ordered a ton and can't keep it all straight in your head? There's pencils and paper for you. That's how much the Buttery trusts you.

[1] Shout-out to Heidi, who makes the best cortados.
[2] There's not enough capital letters to express my Buttery love.

Hungry? They have decent crabcakes and sliders. Duck confit chicken wings doused in a pomegranate molasses-bourbon-chili sauce fail to impress, so go for their zippy macaroni and cheese instead - they're popular for a reason.

Have a sweet tooth? Share an order of their cereal ice cream.

Refined booze-hounds will appreciate their beer selection.

At night, a DJ does his thing for the crowd. The crowd itself is interesting, but there were too many dudes last I was there (read: they're not Vagina Bar).

This BYOB serves Thai fare.

When I ask for my food to be made spicy, their staff does a great job bringing it out just right. On the menu, if there are 3 peppers by an entree to indicate its spiciness, I request at least 5 (usually 8 to see how high they can kick it up)!

Their green curry is genuinely spicy - you ought to sign a waiver before trying to eat it! I've ordered their Thai Bamboo ($7, stir-fried dish with beef - you can get it with chicken - with bamboo shoots, peppers, beans, and fresh basil), drunken noodles (with chicken), and pad thai, all delicious.

Servers are friendly - our servers (Nui, and another one I can't spell) are always good and efficient. I've ordered take-out here as well and the food comes out quick.

They get busy Fridays and Saturdays! Make reservations if you want to dine in on those days. This is one of my favorite regional Thai restaurants - highly recommended.

UPDATE: I came here on my birthday and someone mentioned it was - they brought out a cake with a candle, on the house, how nice is that?

Vintage continues to deliver. No, no, not literally - though that would be insanely awesome - but they still deliver in quick-yet-personable service (thanks Bryan, and others), mood, and in both their food and drink offerings. Relax with a glass of red (or opt for a wine flight), and munch on baked brie. Their bruschetta is always dependable, as is their calamari.

They're still not Tria, but I'm fine with that. There's a time and place for each, and what fun is having no choices?

Tasty coffee and live entertainment in a cozy space? What a wicked idea.

Obviously it's been done before, but this independent coffeehouse nails it. Besides their brews, they have a collection of eclectic artwork (much if not all is for sale), in-house baked goods, and offer Wi-Fi access. Under a table I spotted a wayward pile of newspapers. Not sure if they have board games, but a friendly game of Scrabble probably wouldn't bother anyone chatting or studying or relaxing nearby.

Friendly service brought our orders out: I savored a deliciously strong espresso while a friend had a hot chocolate. Try their chocolate chip cookies; cookies and coffee are a lovely coffee combo.

Apparently, the larger pizza chains close after a certain time, leaving you in the lurch if you have hunger pangs in the middle of the night. Who will come to the rescue? Tower Style Pizza, that's who: they continue to take orders and deliver pies until 4:30 AM[1].

We called in a request for a large pepperoni pizza that set us back about $18[2]. The deliveryman arrived about 20-minutes early (we were quoted a 30 to 45-minute wait, I think?), handing us piping-warm goodness.

Even under the influence, we could still tell the pizza was bad for human consumption - it's greasy[3] as all get-out - yet we still devoured it in no time flat. With the exception of a pleasantly crispy crust, Tower Style isn't quality pizza - not even close - but they provide a valuable service, pizza pies delivered to your door after a long night of partying.

[1] Maybe I misheard the deliveryman? Their web site states they will deliver all hours.
[2] Are my notes lying to me again? Doubt it was that pricey, as their menu shows a 14" single-topping pizza to be $8.25.
[3] Even as I type this, I still feel the grease slopping through my veins.

Prohibition Taproom has got personality. Their huge "BAR" sign calls to you, even visible from Spring Garden. This faux-speakeasy's interior fits their name, with a large wooden bar dominating the space, lit by beautiful hanging Victorian bulbs. There's room for a crowd, even in the bathrooms[1]. My only gripe is that the exterior is brighter than it ought to be.

Prohibition opened earlier this month, and as young as they are, the staff was anything but. Brendan, our bartender and a trained chef, kept us happy, making us shots and taking food orders (they have a full menu). We took down gin ($7/shot), Jameson, and pineapple rum shooters[2]. Would have drank more, but conceded, with great lugubriousness, that it was a Monday night.

Stop into Prohibition[3], and tell 'em I sent you[4]!

[1] Their non-unisex bathrooms can fit two comfortably, though most will prefer to go solo. Don't ask how I know.
[2] I asked for a light, random shot, and was pleasantly surprised with the shooters.
[3] Do this!
[4] Don't do that!

One of my favorite cafes in Philly.

A rockstar (he sure looked like one) suggested I get their caramel latte. Glad I listened: It wasn't cloyingly sweet, and went perfectly with my Flying Monkey oatmeal raisin sandwich cookies.

Plenty of seating meant less headaches for our group, and the chairs themselves had a bit of bounce (in a good way). The decor is up there, for sure. And there are board games.

Coffee and cookies probably weren't the wisest dinner choices ever, but who's keeping score?

On a flight my seat mate told me about Pub & Kitchen. The name stuck, so I grabbed a friend and gave it a go.

A "no reservations" policy meant a small wait before we were seated.

Even during the day, the Pub's darker than I'd like, but there's sidewalk seating for the nyctophobic. Besides a gigantic bar, this restaurant has comfortable stylings, subtle rabbit and pig imagery all about. Despite the crowd inside and out, server Laura managed to keep us buzzed.

We shared fresh kusshi oysters (at market price, which we all know is scary markup), before moving onto a bowl of Thai basil mussels. For an entree, I had a pan-fried pork cutlet, not bad, not too dry, with a decent amount of flavor. Table bread was so-so, but we spent more time on their other yeasty treats: a Yards "brawler" pub ale and a pint of Sly Fox served nicely.

Delicious Indian cuisine. Can't speak to their Thai (I only tasted the pad thai, which was okay).

Their goat special (get it with "spicy vindaloo") is excellent, tender meat, with a savory sauce. It's the right amount of spice, and not too crazy.

Pleasant interior, and easy shopping center parking.

Kildare's Manayunk is rank madness, a confusing maze of rooms, but even taking this into consideration, it is not a horrible venue. There's sometimes live music, and you can't go wrong with multiple bars. Staff are friendly.

I've only drank here, but I assume their food is just like their other locations: bland. (That works on so many levels; don't take me seriously. Not too seriously, anyway.)

I last partied at Kildare's for a birthday party, and our massive crowd crammed in fine. Heck, it even becomes a meat market. By the end of the evening, folks were meandering off to other places. Like them, give this spot a shot, and if you're unhappy, stumble to the next stop.

They're okay.

Hate happy specials? Then you'll hate Harp & Crown.

Don't come here if you don't like being confused. They have TWO bars, one on street level, and one downstairs. The downstairs one is tucked away down a long hallway and takes forever to walk to. Imagine you're on a cruise ship, minus the whole motion sickness deal.

Addicted to catching Pokemon or swiping on Tinder? Downstairs there's poor cellular service. And no Wi-Fi! The nerve!

Shout-out to bartender Ryan for keeping my glass full even when it probably should have stayed empty.

Dined with a friend who's pickier than God; she wasn't willing to eat anywhere else. Thankfully their (decent) hot and sour soup warmed her up.

Their main room is decorated beautifully, with sprawling Chinese characters along the walls. Real estate is tight (a bar takes up a lot of space), but small groups will do just fine. It was crowded, but we snagged seats at the sushi bar.

Due to the crowd, servers weren't ever-present, but that meant more privacy. Besides, sushi chef Ken met all of our sushi-loving needs. Thanks to Ken, we sampled a couple of outstanding rolls, including the substantial Crazy roll ($11.95), jam-packed with eel, shrimp, crab, smoked salmon, cucumber, avocado, and egg, plus caviar. Easily a meal by itself, several bites are needed to subdue it.

The highlight of the night? The Green Lady roll ($10.95). Cucumber, avocado, scallion, sprouts, striped bass, mint leaves, and LIME, it was wonderfully fresh, almost like eating a drink.

This South Philly bakery sells crack by the mouthful, in the form of ice cream doughnuts.

Go on, try one.

Imagine a doughnut, halved, with a block of vanilla ice cream - they'll dish out Neapolitan if you're feeling patriotic - jammed in-between the doughnut halves, all covered in powdered sugar. The ice cream's an unknown-brand, but who cares: one ice cream doughnut goes for the bargain price of $2.50. Plus, we're not talking any doughnuts, but Italian doughnuts.

If you don't like doughnuts, they've got other pastries, too.

Tavern on Camac is still one of the best bars I know of, and I'm not just talking gay bars. The DJs[1] draw a crowd, and always seem to be on point, playing a mix of classics and dance pop to keep everyone pumped til the wee hours. This is a dependable spot; I regularly entertain out-of-town friends here.

There's no cover, but you'll be spending money on booze. Beer seems to be a bit pricey here, but liquor remains reasonable. Remember, they're cash only, but there's an ATM downstairs if you need it.

[1] Not sure if there's one or more DJs that spin here.

Met friends at this Tampopo for a late lunch (to which I was late for).

Unsurprisingly, the place was empty save for two tables. Much like their state of affairs, the interior is simple, naturally-lit, with austere wooden stools. At the counter, I wished for (and paid $8.50 for) a bowl of Tampopo ramen and received a buzzer. When it lit up and made noise, I ran to the counter for my ramen.

Tampopo's ramen was a welcome afternoon snack. The noodles were okay, yielding, with a little heft. There was a good amount of meat, sweet and tangy, and an egg added flavor. Not sure if you can set the broth's heat level - I didn't specify - but it was slightly spicy. (Most normal people will cough after their first sip.)

When we were done, we cleared our table, placing plates and silverware in handily-labeled rubbish bins.

Those new to ramen will enjoy Tampopo's interpretation of ramen, but all others should leave high expectations at home. For sure, my meal didn't suppress my noodle-y ramen cravings, but their menu is intriguing enough to warrant future visits.

Trekking to Philadelphia looking for a good cheesesteak? Hit up D'Alessandro's in Roxborough. If you're without an automobile and don't want to venture that far, go to Jim's on South Street. Avoid this tourist trap. (Or stop by, take photos like the tourist you are, then leave.) Their steaks are good, but not worth fighting crowds for.

Geno's is one of the well-known spots in Philadelphia - find me an in-flight magazine that doesn't mention them. I've had their regular cheesesteak, without cheese, and roasted peppers (it's half decent, greasy as all get-out as they should be), and sat at on a bench outside - but ever since they posted those wonky, inflammatory "THIS IS AMERICA: WHEN ORDERING, SPEAK ENGLISH" signs, Geno's has been on my "no-go" list. The signs are a little tasteless and turn off English-speakers, regardless of origin. I'm as patriotic as the next American, but can we be more diplomatic? Maybe "Order in English please"?

As good as a standard Garden Inn gets.

Beds are comfy, with soft mattresses, and no sign of bed bugs. Decent shower pressure.

This Hilton is at one corner of Chinatown, and has ready access to the Gallery, Reading Terminal Market, SEPTA Regional Rail, and the Philadelphia Convention Center.

This neighborhood spot works for any kind of rendezvous, low-key or otherwise.

The Vous is somewhat of a dive, but well-lit, and rather clean. It's innocuous; when I passed it originally, I had thought it was a deli. No lie.

Accommodating staff. Server Mandy got us plenty of drinks, and even inquired about our friend who was taking a bit long in the bathroom - ruh-roh! Turns out she had had too many shots, which is easy to do when we're talking about a $2 cherry vodka shot special.

Their Reuben is pretty reasonable (reasonably-priced, too), and perfect for quelling those hunger pangs.

Spring Mill Cafe is a romantic BYOB tucked away in a Conshohocken nook. Their charming decor is peppered with vintage artifacts of a bygone era. Walking in is almost like visiting France. (In fact, the owner grew up there.)

A friend and I dined here one Friday. We managed to find the place without getting too lost, and their large parking lot was a welcome treat. Besides folks dining on their patio, it wasn't terribly crowded. Dinner was a pleasure. Our server (Nicolleta) was attentive, anticipating our needs, keeping us happy. Our appetizers (ah, escargot!) and entrees were savory, countrified French fare, on par with other Gallic places I've been, and worth the price. My rabbit was a little dry, but tasty, and seasoned just right. My friend enjoyed her dish too.

Good company, good cooking, and good service, what's better than that? Can't wait to try their brunch service! Recommended, and worth a trip to the suburbs - they're a short walk from the Spring Mill train stop.

P.S. I'm happy to see this review get Review of the Day (ROTD)!

UPDATE 2/17/2009: Changing my star rating to 5 - I realllllly had a good time. Also, check out their web site for the latest menu and other updates!

Coyote Crossing still turns out mean cuisine.

The duck (!) and mango quesadillas aren't bad, and come with a hearty sauce. The mangos in the dish seemed "off" to me, but I never did get any food poisoning. Not that it would've been possible, as any malignant germs would have been destroyed by the fresh habaneros I ate (special request) or that wicked-strong house margarita I downed.

Be sure to try their super fantabulous pico de gallo, that's a tasty mix.

Soy Cafe is like an old pair of jeans: familiar, comfortable, tasty.

Maybe not that last bit.

Mismatched chairs, potted plants on the sill, and window art make Soy a charming Northern Liberties destination, perfect for a low-key date or casual meetup. Seating up front and a cozy back room ensure there's plenty of space to relax.

Soy churns out special soy drinks ($2.75 at the time; cash only), so I tried a cocoa mint soy, served warm. This uncouth soy drink virgin found it surprisingly soothing.

Friends and I shared steamed dumplings and shrimp shumai (6 for 4.50). Not bad, but their sammiches are where it's at.

Try their mushroom omelette sandwich (7.25). Choose between shitake, oyster, or portabello mushrooms (I had portabello), then enjoy eggs (or eggwhites), garlic, sweet onion, and soy cheese. On the side is a refreshing spring mix salad dressed in a homemade garlic mustard. Their toast on whole wheat sandwich is a gourmet treat; the sauce in it made my taste buds backflip.

Stop in for lunch, dinner, or a soy drink, and don't forget to tip the friendly help.

Pho and More is a recent addition to the Vietnamese food scene (what scene there is) out in Montgomery County. It's pleasant and well-lit, with room for a good crowd.

Their menu's reasonably-priced - especially for the suburbs - and pretty tasty. Their Thai beef salad is made with tender, flavorful cuts of meat, and their fish is cooked to perfection. Their pho isn't bad - lots of noodles, meatballs, tripe, etc. - but last I was there, I found the meat to be noticeably tough.

Despite the number of staff, Pho and More seemed to be overwhelmed at times. They need to work on their stride, but once they've got that down - and if they keep the kitchen they've got - they'll do fine.

The Bards is surprisingly homey, and way more Irish than its neighbor, the airport bar of Irish pubs. Practice your aim with a game of darts, or burn your hand in their fireplace.

During busy times, it can take a bit to get noticed at the bar. Those in a hurry to drink will not be amused. (Our bartender was pleasant but overworked.) After sambuca shots and Irish car bombs, we retreated to a table - especially for the faster service - to munch on curry fries and nachos. Their curry fries were wicked tasty. The nachos, not so much.

The best part about the Bards is their reasonable prices, a boon for any place around Rittenhouse Square.

Feeling punkish? Go here. Even if you're not, still go; they welcome patrons of all types. (You'll leave with color in your hair.)

Their interior is eclectic, yet somehow manages to stay low-key. There's something about sharing a couch that lends a casual feel to a place, and Tattooed Mom's is no exception. If the spinning tops and lollipops lying around don't keep you busy, their delicious tater tots will.

Service was lukewarm, but friendly enough. Never found out if they had house drinks, but we knocked back shots with impunity: Swedish Fish shots fell, plus a random blend of pineapple and mango liquor ($5/each; credit cards accepted).

Oh, and they have music or something.

Besides a typical Whole Foods inventory[1] - and local vendors hawking product samples, of course - it's possible to grab a beer in their restaurant pub. Sample their buffet, purchasable by weight. Like oysters? Get them shucked in-house. (We asked if they had cocktail sauce and got a container free!)

Enjoy your meal in their lower sitting area, or head upstairs to their atrium and deck. While the lunch rush is intimidating, it's not unreasonable[2]. Even during nutty times, there's lots of parking.

Whole Foods's dining offerings make this one of my favorite supermarkets. It's healthy, reasonably tasty, and does in a pinch. Not bad for their flagship store in the region.

[1] This is a good thing.
[2] Those who came here during for their opening week know what I'm talking about.

Not sure how famous Famous 4th Street Cookie really is, but I can say for sure that their double chocolate chip cookies are quite the treat, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, especially fresh. They're a good size, easily sharable with a friend.

If you take them home, they'll keep for a few days; microwave them and don't forget to pour a tall glass of milk.

Find them in the Reading Terminal Market.

Ever heard of Yogurtland? If you love Yogurtland, you'll love Phileo.

Phileo's actually produced by Yogurtland, which explains their identical offerings, all the way down to their wall tile styling. While their pricing here is higher than their siblings on the west coast, Phileo frozen yogurt prices are on-par with their competition; if you go on a froyo binge and are short on cash, credit cards are accepted.

We tried several froyo samples, and I relished how they stock tons more varieties than Pinkberry. I shared a mix of strawberry and banana - mixing is encouraged - with my friend, sprinkled Captain Crunch cereal on, and added strawberries too. Service was friendly.

Phileo's froyo is to my liking, but don't take my word for it. Try them yourself.

Try a pastrami sandwich.

As soon as you're done with that, feel free to send me a Thank You card.

Unlike the pastrami, their bagel lox is just so-so. Theirs is one of the biggest I've had - they pile on the salmon and trimmings - but not exactly bursting with flavor. On the other hand, it's good enough to save you a trip to NYC.

Koreana[1] stocks a standard menu of Korean dishes, prepared above-standard, at decent prices.

Last I was here, I walked in 10 minutes past closing. Talking to the owner/chef/cashier (not sure which), I mentioned I just arrived from out-of-town, and he took pity on me and whipped up some delicious yukgaejang with chicken ($7.25), a piping hot, lightly spiced thick soup. A mildly-pungent side of kimchi kept me entertained, and I left happy.

[1] I miss their previous incarnation sometimes, but I'm glad this is still an option for Korean in University City.

I'm hopelessly addicted to Han's cooking. His Sichuan is always a dependable standby, and I'm glad this restaurant is an option in Manayunk.

Last I was here, I brought a large crew and we went for the tasting menu. It was an assault of the senses: the smells and tastes and textures of Dan Dan noodles, dumplings, soups, and a medley of other dishes blurred through my mind.

Be prepared for spiciness, or ask to tone it down a little. Their tasting menu is a boot camp of hot peppery goodness in your face. Dishes rated at "10" make even this tin man cry.

Unlike my previous visits, service was friendly. Felt a little out of place, but I had fun with friends. Not too many popped collars in the crowd, big plus. It was busy - both floors were happening - so we enjoyed a few drinks before moving on to the next place for dinner (and more drinks, of course). McGillin's has tons of alcohol, so it still was a decent spot to start the night (really).

If you're unlucky enough to need a car, McGillin's validates parking under the Holiday Inn Express on Market.

For those into sophomoric humor, it's difficult not to think "happy ending" when you see Sweet Ending.

They have a playfully futuristic interior, one of their strong points. I feel guilty loitering here occasionally since it's not the largest frozen yogurt place. Conveniently close to several restaurants, Sweet Ending is perfect as an after-dinner dessert. (There are bars nearby too - but they don't open super late - so it's not out of the question to "pregame" here.)

Sweet Ending has a healthy number of fruit, cereal, and cookie toppings, and several froyo flavors. Their froyo is wicked expensive ($3.10 for a small cup) but wicked delicious. Think tart froyo, though. Like pretty much any froyo place, pricing's determined by weight - I don't think I had much in mine - so be conservative when adding toppings.

This place is currently one of a kind (as far as I can tell, there are no other locations), and worth a visit.

Just your friendly neighborhood karaoke dealer.

Yakitori Boy's private karaoke rooms are among the best in Philadelphia, decked with flatscreens and cushy furniture. A lively upstairs lounge has a fog machine and laser lights which accent their dark woods.

Their Tuesday night drink specials are especially popular, but no matter the night, it's always a packed house, with a fun, supportive crowd, festive singers armed with liquid courage. Bartender Jose delivers, pouring us sake bombs and shots - even introducing me to Vincent Van Gogh's Double Espresso caffeine liquor.

Go to Yakitori Boy for happy hour, or a bite - try the pork sausage skewers!

Weekdays, this spot seems to host mostly a work crowd. But don't fret, there's still space to sit.

Haven't been to Pudge's old location, but this one is clean and pleasant. Walk in, seat yourself, and place your order when someone gets to you. Friendly service.

Tried their pepper cheesesteak (around $7, thanks to my friend for paying!): It was a hefty size (ended up taking half of it to go), with a colorful mishmash of peppers and tender meat. Cheesesteaks aren't usually my thing, but I left satisfied.

Good experience all-around; I'll be back for their hoagies.

Love Farmicia's location and Old World atmosphere. This is a good happy hour spot.

Thirsty folks converged upon Farmicia for an ICON happy hour I helped organize.

Early on, their bar was a bit understaffed: only a lone, brave bartender (Ed) was available to serve our party of fifty, which confounded all logic. Then again, I may have misinformed management on the expected number of guests.

We negotiated complimentary appetizers and Farmicia was quite generous with the food. Everything I tried was fresh, tasty, and locally sourced - I enjoyed seconds where possible - and I heard no complaints from my associates. We took advantage of the best drink specials that I had seen in recent memory: two shots set me back a mere $8. For the curious, I had a rather dashing shot with root beer and vanilla vodka, and a "Nuts and Berries" shot, which was a berry explosion of flavor.

Chef Michael Schulson's take on banh mi isn't awe-inspiring, but I can't besmirch a restaurant based on a single sandwich[1]. Their pork variety is only $7 (lunch price; credit cards accepted), and nets you a bag of Utz chips and a soda[2]. Inside the bread, find cucumber, carrots, and a Berkshire pork belly. The roll's decent, but overall the sandwich doesn't quite capture "asian street flavors" - it's a tad sweet. However, banh mi purists won't be disappointed; they simply won't be blown away. 

The rest of the menu fares better. Rock shrimp lettuce cups tickle the senses, while roasted scallops satisfy. I haven't had their crab wonton tacos yet, but throw cilantro on anything and I'm a fan.

Sampan continues to be a welcome addition to Philadelphia's restaurant scene: they score major style points, from a striking front to their bold graffiti bar. Hospitality is much appreciated, too. Thanks to the accommodating staff (bartender George, and others) for their service.

[1] Unless they're a sandwichery.
[2] Asked to be surprised and got a cherry Coke. Haven't had one in years!

Their gourmet pizza is off the hizzle.

Seriously, their Healthy Hawaiian makes me want to fly to the islands. Pineapple, turkey sausage, and mozzarella? Sign me up. The Viva Espana isn't shabby, all Spanish chorizo, red onion, and paprika. If you want pocket-sized party favorites, opt for their personal pies. No matter what size you get, save any leftovers.

Find Couch Tomato Cafe in Manayunk.

Azie on Main[1] is a hidden happy hour gem. Literally.

Azie's a bit tough to find from Lancaster Avenue, but if you can find the Staples off of 476, head to the rear of the parking lot.

They have solid daily standard sushi specials. For $4 each, we got a crunchy spicy tuna roll and a spicy salmon roll. Did I mention they're as tasty as they are value-packed?

Azie's large, trendy space, with the ubiquitous flatscreen TV, makes for a good happy hour venue. Our group sat in their front lounge area, and despite the proximity to the front door and outside cold, remained warm.

Good service. Ivy brought everyone drinks and dishes fast, and was friendly too.

[1] Formerly known as Maia, with new ownership.

I'm happy Yogorino is in the States.

My friend bought me a cup[1], adding chocolate frosting. The yogurt was rich sweetness, and still managed to be refreshing and somewhat filling. Eating it, I felt cleansed. Dodgy health benefits be damned, Yogorino's froyo is naturally delicious. Even during cold weather.

[1] Anyone else notice their signature blue serving cups? Say souvenir!

Look up apple pie in the dictionary[1] and you'll find Isgro's apple pie.

Their pies contain a near-perfect balance of sweetness, firmness in their crust, and savory apples. Even after a night in the fridge, you'll want more.

If you bring me a pie, I'll pay you. And even share some.


[1] I found out that "apple pie" is actually in the dictionary. Sadly Isgro's hasn't yet made it into Merriam-Webster.

Pleasant atmosphere, reasonable pricing, and high quality ingredients make Kabab Cafe a welcome addition to the area.

Friends and I walked in to bright colors and to the sounds of appropriately ethnic music. A decent crowd filled the restaurant. We got in line, placed our orders, and waited a bit. A staffer brought our food out, and even helped us rearrange tables so we could sit together. How's that for service?

Lunch was a treat. I enjoyed the joojeh with a shirazi side salad ($14), a delicious marriage of basmati rice and tasty meat. The shirazi was fresh - wish I had more - and I made full use of the included limes. My combo, while large, was a bit pricey, but you can take advantage of their dope lunch specials: $5 for various dishes, daily from 11 AM to 2 PM.

Check them out!

Remember Sansom Oyster House? Since their reboot, their dining room is more open, ample seating catering to groups. It can get noisy, but that comes with the territory; they're popular. Even so, it's typically not an issue snagging seats during the week.

Try the roasted oyster sampler ($15), which scores you a pair of: oysters Rockefeller, oysters Espanol (chorizo and cilantro lime butter), and Portuguese (anchovy butter, parsley, and lemon). Their lobster bisque isn't bad, and the clam chowder satisfies.

Looking for a creative way to down an oyster? Ask for a Chihuahua shot (especially during happy hour): this creative concoction is a mix of hot pepper, cilantro pepper-infused vodka, and tomato juice. It's surprisingly pleasant, but be wary, these dogs sneak up on you!

No matter how you shuck it, the Oyster House is the place to sklork oysters.

Teresa's Cafe (neighbor to the appropriately-named Teresa's Next Door) has been recommended for some time, for good reason: they cook up solid Italian fare with no fuss.

Our entrees came out wicked fast. My penne arrabiata had an agreeable sauce, but its spicy sausage wasn't as hot as I thought they'd be. Luckily, the penne still was "piccante" thanks to meaty jalapenos. If they still offer it, try their outstanding lobster ravioli special.

Skipping dessert, we had wine: my South African Sauvignon blanc ($7), Vrede en Lust (2006) was as fruity as advertised, with a touch of cut grass (!), and my associate enjoyed her Australian Riesling.

Their well-lit dining room hosts a healthy crowd, even Mondays, so make reservations to be safe. (It can get loud, so speak up!) Even with the crowd, server Luis provided good service, never rushing us.

Not bad for what it is, where it is. (3.5 stars)

Right near the Naval Air Station, the Iron Abbey is next door to Na'Brasa steakhouse. It isn't too expensive, and they've got their selection of beer, beer, beer (tons of beer on tap). (No idea how their food is but I enjoyed a dirty ho last I was here.) From their central bar, there's lots of seating plus  easy access to bartenders. If you're driving, they've got a huge parking lot. It's got a rustic feel to it, for sure.

The night I was there there was a good crowd. Interested in a happy hour? Iron Abbey offers that Mondays through Fridays 5-7 PM.

Brittingham's is a good place to drink. It's an Irish pub, for goodness sake!

Daily, from 5 PM to 7 PM it's happy hour. ($4 Guinness? Not too shabby.) There's live music (at times), and they've got a stage (all the time). They have plenty of seating plus a bar worth its weight in booze, so bring friends.

As for brunch, they're a decent spot. Besides the bar area, they have a homey dining room, naturally lit, with tablecloths to keep it real. You've got standard brunch offerings, plus regionally-flavored ones. If you're thirsty, they've got mimosas. If you're of a mind to grab lunch, try their corned beef special sandwich ($6.75), served cold with a side of oh-so-crunchy homemade potato chips. Not sure what makes it special exactly, but it's a sound meal with lots of meat; you won't leave hungry.

We've been buying cakes from here for years, back when they were the Swiss Pastry Shop.

While we usually stop in for special occasions, there's no reason to wait for a visit. Their bakery offers a full assortment of cookies and pastries besides cakes. Like traditional Chinese cakes, Swiss Haus's tend to not be uber sweet, a plus in my book. Need a cake for a wedding? They do those, too.

May I recommend their Black Forest cake?

I don't know much about the "cafe" part of this charming BYOB, but I do know that their kitchen turns out satisfying fare and that their friendly staff are happy to serve it to you.

Their brunch menu is a familiar mix of dishes and sides, including croissants, steak, and scrambled eggs. Their smoked salmon bagel sounded tasty, but feeling traditional - Sundays have a way of doing that - I chose a few items a la carte, mixing Canadian bacon and pancakes, and adding eggs sunnyside up. Bacon was tender, and a slathering of syrup helped the pancakes along. Servings weren't overwhelming, but considering the sweltering weather, no complaints. Especially once I started downing my virgin mimosa.

Next time I'll pass on the outdoor seating and head indoors; their cafe chairs sure looked comfy!

From the sidewalk, it's not much. But inside, this amber-tinted BYOB is old-school chic, perfect for a romantic interlude or catching up with friends.

Chef Sam Jacobson[1] delivers Nouveau American fare with a personal touch, from the marvelous mac and cheese (Italian sausage and roasted tomatoes) to a delightfully spicy jambalaya (classic New Orleans style, prepared with sea salt)[2]. Try the tender poussin (stuffed with mushrooms, beet greens, and Munster cheese - love at first bite!), or share an artisanal cheese or charcuterie plate. Solo? Splurge for the Malpeque oysters. Can't decide? Service is there every step of the way.

When it comes to desserts, I'm still standoffish, but their Kahlua mousse - and flourless chocolate cake - sometimes makes me reconsider that stance.

[1] We're friends, but I show up unannounced to keep things kosher.
[2] Their menu changes seasonally to ensure a fresh experience, so some dishes mentioned may not be available.

This lone Vietnamese place fills a culinary gap in Upper Darby.

They make tasty pho, comforting and inexpensive, with decent-sized meat chunks (if you're of a mind). The broth isn't the best I've had but you can't beat the convenience and speed of their kitchen.

Best of all, you can order their pho to go, noodles and fixings all neatly packed for your pleasure.

Try the cumin lamb[1], it's worth making the trip here[2]. Savory, and very Szechuan.

Their cooking is outstanding, authentic to a T. Everything is quite good and, in some cases, packs a decent amount of heat. Picky eaters can order Americanized Chinese; there's a section on the menu labeled as such. Fantastic service.

An upscale interior makes you forget you're in a suburban strip mall; comically, Han Dynasty's layout is damn near identical to Sang Kee Wynnewood. Coincidence?

Thanks to my friend for suggesting Han Dynasty!

[1] Sorry vegetarians. On the bright side, there are many non-meat menu selections.
[2] Don't feel like driving? Han Dynasty has a few other locations in the area.

This mainline French BYOB was a tad crowded when we arrived, so be sure to make reservations to be safe.

We shared three appetizers: the moules Provencale et frites ($11; mussels and fries) were easily the best of the trio, while the escargot ($10) and pate du jour ($10) were merely okay.

My main dish, a duck breast ($26) cooked medium rare, was pleasant, tender, and more than made up for the appetizers. A fresh fruit compote balanced the meat nicely, adding sweetness to every bite.

A la Maison's prices are steep enough to keep me from dining here weekly, but at least they're a BYOB! (I must say, the Riesling we picked up brought everything together.)

Helpful service (friendly Tatiana took a photo of us), a warm and casual ambiance, and tasty entrees - and excellent company, of course - all add up to an experience I'd like to repeat soon.

Like the Liberty Bell, cheesesteaks, and that pesky city wage tax, the Reading Terminal Market is one of those things that makes Philadelphia uniquely Philadelphia.

Yes, it's a historical site, but more importantly, it's full of vendors selling delicious food. There's something for everyone: Amish sellers are there part of the week, and you can pick up groceries or get your grub on if you're in the mood for a cheesesteak, Thai, Indian, ice cream, oysters - you name it.

If the Market was open past 5 PM, I'd be the happiest camper. And poorer, but who's watching my wallet?

PRONOUNCIATION: Remember, it's "Redding", rhymes with sledding. Don't ask me why.

The Mill is now in Tampa at corner of Azeele & Armenia.   Valet parking or parking on street if available.  

The menu is about 80% the same as St Pete location.  You can organize your meal the way you want with a combination of 1st, 2nd and 3rd plates.  The house original Old Fashioned was a good start.  Then salad (easily splittable) an Shrimp Orzo.   The cuisine, service and atmosphere are all 5+ rating.  

The entire interior has been transformed into a stunning mural which includes bar & dining rooms.  It can be noisy, however, a huge outdoor dining area under the trees and by the mill will give you tranquility.

A welcome addition to Kennedy Blvd.  This location previously was Cafe con Trey, Bin 37 and Flying Pan Creperie after that.  Miguelitos means little Miguel, thus named by the owners of Miguel's Mexican which is just 3 blocks away.   

Extensive renovations have been completed to deliver a new vibe. The bar area in front has black walls, floor and ceiling giving a dark atmosphere but the white illuminated bar provides a glowing radiance.  Next are booths in the middle section and then the huge outdoor seating area with a canopy overhead that is retracted each night.  These areas give the restaurant 3 separate personalities.

Menu includes tacos, soups & salads, Tortas (Mexican sandwich), burritos, tapas and bowls.  First visit was the Torta BLT (not recommended).  On second  visit, the carnita taco and especially the beef fillet tacos were good.   You can also order Lengua (tongue) and Barbacoa (beef cheek) tacos.

I have always loved attending carrabba's. I went tonight for my cousin's birthday and I just love a great family outing. We sat down and enjoyed the fresh bread slices with olive oil for dipping. Their stuffed mushrooms and shrimp scampi with sauce were great starters. We then visited the bar for an awesome drink called "prickley pear" I had two and I turned my family into prickly pear fans. We had an array of prickley pears along our table which seated 10. They are hooked now and everytime we go everyone order the same drink. I ordered the chicken carrabbas pasta with shrimp...it had flat fettuccini pasta with peas... I did ask for shrimp to be added on top. My greedy butt had to. I'm sorry....let's out a prickly pear burp. My honey ordered the steak, shrimp and scallops meal with a take home meal for $10. He got the salmon to take home. All our meals came up to 60.00 roughly, an amazing deal, for amazing food.

One of the most pleasurable modern Italian meals I've had in recent ages. Can you believe that we drove all the way from Los Angeles to eat here in Santa Barbara and plucked this chic restaurant -- miraculously -- out of a hat? How serendipitous!

Found inside the Santa Barbara Inn, this is off-boardwalk, just across the street from the ocean, and if you choose the outdoor patio you can see the beach clearly (on a summer day you can see the beach forever). Yet once your nose and mouth quicken to the LAMB MEATBALLS or BURRATA CHEESE starter plates, that nose and mouth might never glance out again until the rest of the meal is over. The artisan California-style pizzas are merely B+ (and worth it as a family share add-on), but there's no way you can finish out your life and call it complete until you've had their QUADRATI RIGATI seafood puttanesca (what a symphony of flavor!) and their BUCATINI chili pasta. I love alcohol to celebrate a great meal, it's so apropos, but I could have ordered three non-alcoholic GINGER BEERS just to keep things going effervescent as they were. Oh, cheers! #classiceats

Peachy and pitched down the middle when it comes to features and accommodations. Everybody that works here is very nice and peppy to extend a helping hand. A double-bed room can be spacious, even tidy, without it being exactly flush with color and vibrancy. It has an early 1983 pastel feeling to it, like it was given a rustic-vanilla paint job that would, supposedly, last for decades. It's nothing to sneer at, it's just that Hyatt is more conventionally classy than it is an enchanting romantic paradise. 

Truly, it's a strong recommendation from me to a lot of double-dating couples, or families, to be here off East Cabrillo Blvd. where you're across the street from a desirable part of the beach -- you can swim at this beach, you can catch an outdoor cafe, and let kids play on a sandy playground, and there are frisbees and footballs being thrown in every direction. So yes, I'm high up on the "Hyatt" when it comes to bachelor getaways or family vacation packaging. The in-hotel food, I'm speaking of the Marbella, just barely misses the first-rate ranks for me, but it's hard not to eat like crazy here, and hard not to eat the filet mignon at least once. The pool has a standard-issue shape, but at night, it has florescent lights that light it up splendidly. Alcohol at the pool bar. You won't get world-class libido indulgences at the Hyatt pool bar at night, but you get something of a tickle of it -- if you don't have kids weighing you down that is. #goodtimes

When I asked my lovely Stone House server today why their hostess wasn't wearing a mask--while every other employee was--I was told, "Oh. Um. Yeah. She's the owner."

I watched the owner close-talk everyone who came to check in. I noticed her leaning over a number of patrons' tables to place or pick up items, while talking the entire time. I  saw her absentmindedly put her fingers in her mouth before grabbing menus.

If you're being careful, please be aware that not everyone at Stone House feels they need to comply with the rules.

This has GOT TO BE the best fried chicken EVA!  I'm so glad I had a chance to see what Nashville Hot Chicken is all about.* The order took about 10 minutes mainly due to freshly frying a new batch.  This batch came out glistening with fresh oils on its surface which gives the skin a crispy, spicy and slightly sweet crunch. The inner white meat, as you break open and pull it apart, starts to ooze out its juices followed by the hot steam escaping into the air.  If you desire REAL fried chicken, be ready for a fattening experience that'll overwhelm your taste buds.

The sides equally played their part.  Collard greens is a side item that epitomizes the Southern  comfort food, perfectly done.  Pimento mac and cheese surprised me with the correct consistency of the cheese and I never would have thought of this match, just as a sandwich spread.

Finish yourself off with a happy ending, with dessert that is.  Dive into the melt-in-yo-mouth peach cobbler and do NOT forget the ice cream on top.  O M G, look at those fotos, Becky!

Five stars.  Head there during off peak times to avoid extremely long lines.
_____________
*And no, KFC's imitation of Nashville Hot Chicken is a FAIL so let's not go there.  ;)

I don't think the intimacy vibes could get any better here, because this place WHISPERS sexy from the moment you are seated. They do a good job making your visit feel like a secret. Depending on the occasion that could be a good or bad thing...LOL! It's fabulously alluring inside, especially if you reserve a booth. Fantastic place for a romantic date, small celebration or endearment gesture. I'd strongly suggest that you make reservations ahead of time to take advantage of the whole speakeasy experience. They have a small menu but unique array of cocktails and each drink is designed to encapsulate the senses. Valet parking is a requirement if you are parking near the restaurant and they do not offer validated parking. You can park for free if you decide and can find street parking. I'd recommend purchasing one of the punch bowls to share because the food takes a long time to arrive.They even have a little surprise inside as advised by our server, ours had a flower and Ninja inside. The long wait is okay because the atmosphere is very helpful in making you focus on the conversation or your party rather than the long wait time to get your food. The duck fries are a traditional fare but savory. The sauces provided really give it an extra special touch, they're sooo delicious you'll want to order more. The seared salmon was mouthwatering and perfectly cooked but I wish I had a little something more on the plate, maybe even more rice to make the dish more filling. The broken english was a suggestion made by our server and I'm so glad I decided to try it. I wanted something sweet but not malibu rum style and this was the perfect fix! The aroma of that drink is just TANTALIZING and provides a serene and aromatic experience that is just incredible! Its strangely a whole journey in a wine glass! We wanted to try the oven roasted duck breast but they were out due to the fact that they are in the process of changing their menu. I would suggest sitting at the bar or in the bar area if you are considering a more casual experience with less provocative feels. However, I love the fact that they offer both! It's interesting, appealing and will definitely make you glad that you tried it.

I can't review Buona Via on the quality of the food, the ambiance of the restaurant or even the attentiveness of the servers. I can't review on any those things because even though we fully intended on going to Buona Via for dinner, we didn't even get through the door, or successfully into the parking lot for that matter. 

My wife and I were going to Buona Via for Dinner because we had a Living Social deal we wanted to use and we're still hunting for a new "go to" Italian restaurant since our previous one drastically changed it's menu. 

We pulled into the parking lot, into a spot (there were more than a dozen open spots) and parked the car. Immediately we found ourselves being yelled at and told that we couldn't park there. It was the "Valet" who insisted that spot was valet only. So even though we were already successfully parked, we decided instead of dealing with it to pull around to the other side of the restaurant and into another open spot. We got out and started to walk in, when we were again confronted by the 'Valet" and told we couldn't park there because it was valet only. 

Growing tired of this stupidity I asked where we could park. The response I received was that I could give him my keys and he'd park my car... even though I had already successfully parked it twice, I needed him to park it for me. I had no intention of giving this guy my keys so I inquired where I could park without giving him my keys. His response was nowhere, apparently the only way to park at Buona Via is by handing your car over to a "Valet"

Now to further expand on this completely pretentious load of shit, Buona Via is a standard Italian restaurant in the suburbs, this isn't some high-end restaurant in Center City where a Valet is expected. On top of that the "Valet" at Buona Via wasn't exactly someone whose first impression screamed "trust me". Yeah he was wearing a red jacket and tie, however I am confident the last time this guy wore a tie he was being referred to as the defendant, as in 'Will the Defendant please rise".  

So back to the review, the defendant ... sorry, valet,  says to me "If you don't want to give me the keys I guess you don't want to eat here". If was the smartest thing he had said all night, and I told him so. 

Fuck Buona Via and fuck their stupid valet, there was no way I was eating there then or ever in the future. Which is really just that much more foolish when you consider the entire reason a business makes an offer through Living Social, Groupon, etc is to get customers exactly like me. A fat guy who loves to go out to dinner, has no problem grabbing several bottles of wine with dinner and when he finds a place he likes goes there over and over and over again. 

In conclusion just skip it and go somewhere else. There are plenty of other Italian places in the area that will make you feel like they actually appreciate you business. Not to mention ones that are damn good and less expensive for the same menu items. Search my Yelp history to find those places and please take this advice, GO SOMEWHERE ELSE. You'll be happy you did.

Changing my rating to 3 stars because the have recently updated the rooms and painted. The area outside the room, elevators, and open areas still need updating but the rooms overall look much better. Definitely a step in the right direction for some of the changes they have made. Pool is still a great place to be and is usually pretty busy. I look forward to seeing more renovations for this property.

What's not to love about this place. As soon As I saw that outside seating area I knew I would love this place. I kind of felt like I was on vacation being here. It was a beautiful day. We got a cozy table out back. Those picnic tables and umbrellas are nice. Then our food was ready. Perfect food to compliment our perfect atmosphere. 

I had the turkey burger. It was delicious. The bun was soft. Meat was tasty. Thousand island dressing on the burger was delicious. I was in burger heaven. I like the variety on the menu. Many burgers to choose from. Fries are not included in burger purchase. Veggie and vegan burger options also available. 

I even brought home a burger for my boys. I ordered all the toppings on the side. They loved it. The prices were right on. Beer also available. This will be a must stop place when ever I am passing through. 

Bring the kids. Very kid friend. Kids sand play area outside. There are tables available for reservations for special parties or events.

You know you're eating at a fancy shmancy restaurant when you notice three things:

1. Your waiter is dressed like a penguin
2. He comes over with a crumb scraper and scraps away your crumbs after ever course
3. They have a dessert cart and explain in great detail every dessert to get you to try one

With that said, you can tell this was a high caliber, classy spot. Ambiance was soft, candlelit. And for being in a recession and being a three dollar sign $$$ spot, I was quite surprised to see this place was packed with other parties of 5 or 6 and couples.

Service was what you would expect at a place like this. Chaz (yup..that's his name) was super nice and was super attentive to us during our meal. There wasn't anything he missed and even switched out my drink when it was barely half empty = very very attentive.

So why no perfect 5? The food.

It's too bad to say a place like this had a loss of a star because of the food. Even though I had a great starter house salad (with homemade croutons) and this wonderful cheesy bread to start, my underseasoned halibut entree fell to the ground. Even a dash of salt and pepper could've remedied this snafu. I begrudgingly reached for the shakers at this time. Thank goodness for the dessert cart and the creme brulee sampler. The classic vanilla, chocolate, and pistachio creme was a great ending to an almost perfect dinner. 

Sidenote: Happy Birthday Mommy!

3.5 stars. Centrally located and a popular place to grab breakfast or lunch. I particularly stopped by this place because it was one of the few good breakfast places nearby my hotel that was opened early enough for me to make it to my work event on time. In a way, I was glad I stopped by a little past 7am (right after they opened), as the place was super packed and there was a line out the door by the time I left the restaurant.

I had their peacemaker (e.g. choose your 2 eggs benedict) and went with the Cochin and shrimp bogaloo. Personally i thought the food was ok. It wasn't as hot as I would like it to be..tasted more like at a room temperature...so that was a little of a let down for me. Portion was a good size but taste was ok..a bit bland for me taste and not anything partocularly memorable. Perhaps if I ever had a chance to stop by this place again, I would probably try something else.

food was great, service was a little slow because of the restaurant week rush.

i had the house salad, which was delicately dressed in a ginger vinaigrette. it was served as a very generous portion - it could have been an entree in itself. the fried pork dumplings (my second course) were served piping hot and had a great crunch and juicy filling.

i selected their maki combo as my third course, which included a spicy tuna roll, yellowtail jalapeño mango roll and a salmon avocado roll. the fish was fresh and i loved the deep bowl that it was served in - felt like i was plucking sushi out of the sea.

the best part of the meal however was... dessert! you were given a choice of two selections off the menu and my friend and i decided to get one of each (chocolate cake, black sesame mochi, apple crisp, and pumpkin bread pudding).

the pumpkin bread pudding was amazing - i would come back just to pick up some dessert if they still have this on the menu next time. it had a chewier texture than most bread puddings - i think they might have snuck some mochiko flour in it to give it that japanese edge.
