For what its worth, the YELPER who complained about not getting FREE refills on the side dishes. I read your critique and I have read and re read it. I feel you are way off base and absurd. Did you read what you wrote? You have got to be kidding! YELP has become more and more of a 5 star love in or lets rip a guys business because I couldn't eat for free! I would have 86th him. Its these types of customers that bankrupt good business.  

If you don't agree with my reviews then please change the channel!

I stopped for dinner at Oh Yoko because of the shining reviews here on YELP. Of course sometimes I forget that most people shoot a load for the minimalist positive experience. As usual, the review on YELP is totally over-rating an eating establishment. It was good but NOT EXCELLENT.

Started with An appetizer of Sea Scallop Sushi. SUPERB. albeit expensive.

Miso Soup - Eh just like any other Japanese restaurant

Wasabi Fries - Totally over -rated and expensive considering we are talking about thinly cut potatoes. People on YELP droned on and on about this appetizer. I guess the reveiwers don't get out much so every time they eat something decent, they must give it 4 or 5 stars. The Drizzled Honey Wasabi Aoli on the fries is not difficult to reproduce in any home kitchen. For 8 bucks you have got to be kidding me!

Entree - I left it up to the server. She brought over a large cold Salad with plenty of greens, rice and some SMALL dices of Tuna and Salmon. A side of very spicy dressing. A few pearls of cheap Salmon Roe in Salad. I would never have ordered this for a dinner entree but I did leave it up to the server. It was good, but for 26 dollars,you have got to be kidding me! 

No dessert. Total including tip was 60 dollars!!! No way will I go back. Yoko Sushi serves good ingredients but is easily 30+% more than the worth of the dinner. 

Oh Yoko your prices are out of line with the end product and the over-all experience.

Ka-POW! No I don't work for Zeppoli, however I am offering you my opinion of a wonderful restaurant. Yes, its small and yes it gets a bit cramped, maybe also a bit noisy, but the food overwhelms all the preceding challenges.

We were celebrating and a small group of us decided to try something adventurous. We already had experienced the talents of Chef Baldino and tonight after getting into town I let this talented Chef  create and serve to us whatever he wanted. 

It was a memorable and delicious evening. So many plates that I am sure I will leave some out, however I want to emphasize, everything was top notch.

We started with a rich Homemade Ravioli stuffed with what tasted like the Chef's Gnocchi, served in a Brown Butter Sauce. Melt in our mouths goodness. 

Then we were served Cockle Clams with Sausage in an incredible broth. On another plate fresh prepared Artichoke Hearts under very well seasoned Bread Crumbs. Ka-Pow goodness.

Next Courses were three delectable Pasta Dishes. One with Oil, Garlic and Broccoli Rabe. A fantastic Plate of Pasta with a Rabbit Ragu. Wow, And the third plate of Pasta was the I believe was the Troffiette. Each of these dishes were wonderful.

Next Course was  a Fish, served whole almost like a Branzino. Our Server, Tommy did a wonderful job cleaning the fall off the bone tender fish. There was not a bone found. 

Meat Course was the Marinated rib-eye steak served with arugula and tomato salad. Magnificently Cooked and Fork Tender. Just the perfect amount of Garlic seasoning. The arugula and Tomato salad was tremendous. Some at the table mentioned how the Chef and its Kitchen's wonderful staff finds an out of season Tomato which tasted amazing. The Steak tasted as good if not better than any Steak House I have visited.

We were loosening our belts at this point.

Dessert was as good as good gets.

A Flourless Chocolate Cake, A Vanilla Homemade Gelato, and 3 out of this world after dinner aperitifs. One a Pistachio Flavored, One a Star Anise flavored, and the last a non flavored Cello. Simply delicious. 

Each and every one who joined me enjoyed the evening immensely, the service was terrific, and the center of everyone's attention was some of the finest Italian Food I have ever had the pleasure of eating. 

The cost was an absolute bargain. Less than 100 per person including Gratuity. 

As I have stated in previous reviews, this Man can cook!

Ka-POW

A decent choice for a local restaurant.

Lips and I decided to have a good steak dinner and was suggested we fly in to try this family owned and operated restaurant.

Appetizers:
Lump Meat Cocktail was a gorgeous serving of magnificent large pieces of Crab. One of the best versions we have had. 
The Thai Calamari was interesting. I stay away from the 1970's versions of heavily breaded Calamari and this was a pleasant surprise. NOT BREADED! Yippie. The sauce was meh. A bit too sweet and not spicy as described. I loved that it was just sauteed, the sauce was a bit of a let down. 

Lips had a cup of the Chicken Soup. Really good.
I had the salad which was small and the Home Made Dressing was very good. 

Entrees: Both of us had the Rib Eye and although the waitress encouraged us to order the Steaks Medium, the end result was they both were still Medium Rare which is what we preferred any ways. The cuts were tender and tasted very good. The Mashed potatoes were also Home Made and were very good.

The Portion of the Steak was on this side of small due to the price point. At 35 per entree, we both thought the size of the cut could have been more generous.

The service was friendly although the waitress made some boner errors such as;
we asked to take home the left overs. The Waitress proceeded to place the plates on top of the food. Not very sanitary. The waitress also never asked us if we wanted deserts or even a cup of coffee.
Because of her friendliness we still tipped 30%.

We would go back.

Authentic Chinese food.
You want Sweet and sour chicken go to the thousand of other restaurants in the area. Don't come here, you won't like it, and all you will do is jam up this small place with your ilk.

Excellent real food. You won't find dry noodles or duck sauce here.

I had the fabulous manager, who was so sweet and helpful order for me. She couldn't do enough for the customers and wanted to share her enthusiasm with all the customers.

I received a very spicey huge bowl of soup. Holy cow, this was spicy, but delicious.

The manager then brought over a HUGE plate of almost a roasted chicken, with Potatoes, Wide Noodles. This too was super spicy but very good.

Next time, I will go ALL IN and order some amazing very authentic food, like Pig Intestines...mmm good!

Fatty says... yes!

The resulting 1 star is not for the individual food although it was far far from anything memorable. To charge 10 dollars for a hot dog, a small fry, and one soda is absurd.

The Bathroom was filthy. The dining area looks like it's been ignored. The floor was so STICKY with dirt and not being cleaned properly that we probably should not have stayed but I was so looking forward to trying this place. When we walked, our shoes were sticking to the floor. ewww

I ordered the Chicago Dog. If you have it on the menu, you should serve the item as described on the menu. It came to the table missing 2 items. The Dog tasted fine, then again the Hot Dog tasted like I made it myself. Nothing, absolutely nothing distinguished paying over the top prices when I easily could have made it home. All this "Chicago Dog" ended up as was a Dog with unripe bad tomato, onion, a couple of sport peppers, (No Celery Salt and no Pickle Spear) 

The Fries were good.  

There is no value here. Nothing at all to want to come back to Cool Dog. The place needs a deep cleaning. The prices need to be evaluated. If the same item would have been 2 bucks I would have not felt as ripped off. The prices are easily DOUBLE than what is the worth of their items. Plus, not receiving what was ordered, along with the dirty feel, nah, won't be back.

Sigh as I really wanted to love this place.

There were 4 in my group

The head chef has changed in the last couple of months.

Lips wore an outfit of, Scrubs, a new Tag Watch, a simple 2 ct, 3 stone underwhelming diamond ring. Definitely dressed down as this restaurant is connected to the Mall, so one of the draw backs in my opinion is that some customers come in in shorts and sneakers. Takes away from the atmosphere. now to the food and why as you can see, I have dropped 52's rating.

We started with those over rated flat breads. Is it just me or do most reviewers on this type of food is too generous with their opinion? I wouldn't order Flat breads  but my guest wanted to...

Appetizers:
2 in the party ordered mushrooms stuffed with crab meat. According to Lips, these too were not extraordinary and he felt they were, "just ok."

I had the Buffalo Chili. Tasty and I enjoyed it.

The Arugula salad was the highlight of the evening. 

Entrees:

The waitress who provided the service raved on and on about the Salmon. "Its the best fish on the menu."

I just discussed with Lips last week how I wont order salmon anymore because there are so many other choices and I feel ordering salmon is too, "safe."

Well, how the waitress raved about the dish I along with another friend, received the Salmon. Very small portion, and totally and absolutely nothing, nothing to remember the dish. It was Blah. 

Lips had a Filet and although he stated the meat was prepared well, he also stated how disappointing he felt the portion was. Very small, he didn't care for the vegetables and the dollop of potatoes  was so small.

Another guest had the seared scallops. VERY SMALL to the ridicules.
Again, tasted ok but we were all still hungry at the end of our meal.

The Desserts are the now TIRED "Indulgences" which I skipped as with the flat breads the desserts are no long cutting edge but rather very tired and just a stale idea.

We will not be coming back to Season's 52. For 320 dollars for 4 people, including cocktails and tip, we can go anywhere. And we will.

Also, I have received messages from some of you who follow my reviews.  Most have been positive and some very upset that it is felt I am too critical in my reviews. I'll explain again..

I believe when you are spending X amount of money you should expect good food, reasonable portions and good service. I do not expect the same level of experience say from an Applebees verse lets say Season's 52. I think I offer a fair assessment.

I ENCOURAGE all restaurant customers to expect MORE than mediocrity. For those who enjoy reading my reviews, yea! For those who hate, please change the channel!

Come on Yelpers, review a restaurant with honest experience. For those who never get out of the suburbs, yea I guess this is gee wiz isn't it cool and wonderful place to have dinner. It's neato! 

There were some highlights, (Good Service) and real low lights, (The Food)

Decent enough atmosphere. Cheap prices. Very good service. 

The Salad Bar was hellacious. Every thing on the bar seems like it came right out of a can. Limited variety, and what should have had seasoning was bland, and very disappointing. Actually, I think for the price, this has got to be one of the worse Salad Bars seen. Chinese Buffets is almost its equal regarding salad bars. Ok, we were here for the meat. 

The meat was at times over cooked and dry. The cuts of meat like the Sirloin was tasty but was served so sparingly that it became a hassle to keep having the "Ganchos" interrupting the conversation. Even at such a reasonable price, we think we would have enjoyed the experience more if Rodizio would have charged us more for better quality.

Dessert was good. If we ever must stop in again for dinner, I would have been more assertive and just ask the server for what ever cut at whatever level of doneness and told them to put a decent slap of meat on the plate rather than play the stupid game of "look for wooden disk is showing green, we beg you for a thin cut of meat."

The whole Brazilian Steak house fad is stale and quite inconvenient.

Just give me a good steak and put it on the freaken plate.

All in all, at best it was ok, at worst it was ok. Went here with a gaggle of people.

Lets see, I'll just list what was had, what was good, ok meh. Nothing was great.

Mushroom soup was good
Seafood Bisque was good
Scallop Appetizer was good, but pricey for the plate.
Tuna Polke nothing extraordinary or even worth while to order again.

Entrees:
Beef Taco a complete fail. Small, dried out meat, terrible
Meatloaf - a horrid dried out saw dust like lump of coal
Sirloin - reportedly good although very pricey
Fig Salad - reportedly meh
One other entree had by a guest stated it was pretty good

Service was meh, seemed unprofessional and could have used more training. It wasn't due to a lack of effort, but so many common sense things were missed. Hmm come to think about it, no the service was not good or managed correctly. Of course we over tipped.

Total for 5 including tip and a round, 250 which was entirely too much for the over all experience. On the level of an Applebees, but priced way over.

Fatty says swing and miss...

No, sorry, Sometimes the YELP inflation seems to be more than just the daily ordinary and typical.
So, yes its new, yes its clean, but the PHO was very thin in the flavor department. The soup not really giving us the in-depth multi layered flavor that so many have learned to enjoy about PHO. The service was fine. The main ingredients of the PHO in this case, Flank, and soft tendon was inconsistent. Very little flank, a decent portion of Soft Tendon.

Ceilings are yellowed, booths have Duct tape holding them together.

Most importantly, the food is not being prepared well.

Hamburger was served RAW. Sent back, Hamburger was served RAW yet again.

Potatoe Salad tasted like it was sitting around for 8 hours too long.

Meatloaf was hard as a rock. Stale.

Marlton Diner used to be the Go TO Place in case. No Longer.

The current owner needs to invest some money to update and fix the place up. Plus, hire better employees.

BYE BYE Marlton Diner.

To update my first Han Dynasty review I have experienced the following;
The food is definitely more authentic, however after trying many dishes here, they kind of all begin to taste the same. Yes, I understand that most of the dishes are cooked with a tremendous amount of Chili Oil. Yes, I understand that most of the dishes are cooked with Red Hot Chili Peppers. The menu is very limited, NO a customer may not ask for something customized except for the heat index. So, I really don't know that next time I am in town, I will be a customer of Han Dynasty. 

Appetizers:
Rabbit which was a Cold Appetizer which was Ok, nothing to be wowed.
Dan Dan Noodles - Ok we get it. Spicy noodles. Ok, ok.
Spicy Beef.- This was off the charts heat wise. My tongue was numb and tingly. I actually enjoyed this the most.

Entrees were Dry Pot with Lamb. This is where I think Han Dynasty lost me. Although tender Lamb, the heat was a 10, it tasted like every other dish. Yes ok I get it, Szechuan is HOT, SPICY yes I get it. But, does all the dishes have to taste almost the same?

Meh after some thought and having direct experience with the Szechuan Province, NO NO NO, all dishes SHOULD NOT taste so similar, So gosh darn it, I don't think I'll be coming back. 

Thank you and for all a good day!

Service was as expected.

I can not believe I tried this place again.
Had no choice as total gridlock made it impossible to go anywhere else.

Same problems as before...

Terrible waitress service. Just didn't have a clue.

Food tasted all the same.

All in all, we would be back.
Still the default good restaurant in West St. Pete.  Great Viet/French atmosphere with good food to compliment.  Though it would be nice if they would freshen up that menu just a tad.

I'm a little surprised that this place is only 3 stars as it embodies everything you would want in an old fashioned steak house. Dim lights, original paintings, white tablecloths and strong martinis. 

We came here for my friends bachelor party "boys dinner" and we're given a private room upstairs so we be as rowdy as we wanted. There were 18 of us so good looking out management as I'm sure any other paying patron wouldn't want any part of our shenanigans. 

Anyway, I ordered the bone in filet as my entree which came with a baked potato and side salad. Solid move as most of these places are purely a la Carter for side options. We did tack on some of those sides and the potatoes as gratin were cheesy delicious. My steak was perfectly cooked to a mid rare and I found the quality of beef to be quite high! 

Our servers were more than attentive and made for an enjoyable 3+ hour evening filled with laughs, speeches and copious amounts of libations.

Man, so disappointing. I'd heard from so many people that Geno's was super legit (and maybe it is) but, the airport location was very lackluster and I wouldn't return if at PHL again. 

The main problem...no love! The employees looked miserable cooking these cheesesteaks and it came through in the end result. Extremely light handed on the meat, peppers and cheese for $12+ bucks...boo. Basically, it was like eating a big piece of white bread and you'd catch an occasional pepper (which provided the only flavor). 

I think Geno himself should tend to this location a bit to bring things back up to standard. 

Pat's King of Steaks it is from here on out...

Bomb tacos and batting cages? Yes, please!!!

I couldn't believe my eyes when I walked into east beach tacos and noticed the neighboring business was an awesome set up of cages. Talk about a blast from the past back to my childhood. I digress...

Let's talk about the tacos. I ordered a set of three and opted for the battered fish, carnitas and raw ahi. They were all super fresh and the ingredients worked well together. In fact, they were so great I went back and ordered one more, the bahn mi taco and it was delicious too! 

Check this place out if you're in the mood for casual tacos with a gringo twist.

On the day of our departure from Nashville, slightly hungover from the weekend, we were looking for some comfort food for lunch. After a brief yelp search, we found The Stillery. We were a large group (12) and they immediately found us a table upstairs near the music stage. Boo ya. 

We ordered a round of greyhounds and the drinks were tasty. Kinda tough to screw up a greyhound, but still. Our servers were attentive and had that friendly southern charm about them which made for a pleasant lunch. 

As far as the food goes...

We split a bunch of items on the menu and my favorite was definitely the hot chicken tenders. Nashville is know for this style of chicken and while these weren't as good as Prince's or Hattie B's, they totally hit the spot. I love how everything in that town comes with a slice of white bread too! 

Check his place out for a solid casual lunch as we were all satisfied when we left.

This one's for Tony and his excellent service! I haven't been to a Sharkeez since I was in my twenties, but fiancé wanted to catch UCSB play during March Madness as we were walking down State St, so we lucked out on a table here. Despite the limited capacity, the tables were all filled with excited patrons looking to celebrate an upset. 

When Tony first sat us, we weren't quite ready to order, so he returned with water as well as a bowl of water for my pup! I started with a glass of bubbly, and then went for their Skinny Margarita, both of which were perfect for my tastebuds. Tony scored more points for carding me! 

I wasn't super hungry so I snacked on the Shrimp & Spinach Queso Dip ($8.99) and the Cabo Mango Fish Taco ($5.49). There wasn't much spinach in the dip, but I did like the shrimp, corn, mushroom & pico de gallo mixed in it. The amount of Mahi in the taco was quite meager, but it was fresh, along with mango salsa and veggies. 

Although I didn't eat much, fiancé, his dad and I asked for drinks and such throughout the game and Tony was attentive and consistent till the very end. I found out later they were even understaffed and he was covering for a server who called in sick last minute. What a good sport. If all Sharkeez had this kind of service with decent food and drinks, I might actually consider going again sooner!

Tried something new to me tonight. Not just a new restaurant but a new style of food. I was quite impressed. We shared a cachapas. This is a cheese stuffed sweet corn meal pancake. Add a touch of sour cream and tomatillo salsa and you have happy taste buds. Since the restaurant is named Arapas I assumed this was their speciality so I ordered  the pabellon arapas. This is a stuffed tortilla filled with amazingly seasoned shredded beef, black beans, queso, and fried plantains. It was a good assumption. Yummy, yummy, yummy.

My wife, son and I went here yesterday. I got the chicken, shrimp, spinach steak with Alfredo sauce all I can say is it was "NOTHING BUT THE TRUTH". I'll be back here many more times. The owner was super friendly and very helpful. Lees Deli should be a good landmark in Philadelphia

The food here is fantastic. If that is literally all you care about you will have a very enjoyable time.

Some of the woes of this places is really unavoidable, the limited seating, the hustle and bustle, etc. I don't mind these at all when it comes to quality food at a great price.

For those who are not familiar with the establishment, you order at the counter and they give you a number you place on the self seating table and they bring your food out. Works pretty well for such a small place.

My biggest complaint was the cashier. Seemed pretty oblivious to customer service. Not only did he not acknowledge me when I came up to the counter waiting for him to greet me and notice me before I started talking to him (he didn't even make eye contact to let me know he was ready), he offered no thank you when I paid nor did he offer to give me a receipt.

Now, these all seem like small issues, but this is not how you present yourself to customers as an establishment. You greet your customers not just for politeness but to also let them know you're ready for them. You say thank you to your customers not just for gratitude but to let them know the transaction is done. Really seemed like the dude did not want to be there or that somehow he was doing me a favor for coming to the place.

This alone makes me reconsider visiting again. Such a shame since the food is delicious. I wish I could overlook this experience simply for the food but I don't think I can ever forget such an odd experience.
I concur with the other reviews.  My review is simply to acknowledge the carrot cupcakes and sweet potato pies at the counter.  I can't seem to leave this place without one or the other.

Must read. Very shady business practice. 

This review is not about the food or our server. It is about how they charge their gratitude!!!

I came to this restaurant with a party of FOUR. And without reading the bill closely, we continue to add on a tip as a reward for their service. However, if you look at the photo closely, what do you notice?

They charged a 15% gratitude which is written in fine prints under the total dollar amount. Without looking closely, one would think that it looks normal. Like any other restaurant bills, the tip option is under the total price. Which leads to our party double tipping them. I understanding that if it is a large party, then you can charge a mandatory gratitude, but for a party of FOUR??? Who does that?!!!!!

And they still have the audacity to put "tip suggestion" on the bottom left corner which is % off the total price AFTER they added on a 15% gratitude. I think they did this on purpose. Shady!

I only found out about this after I came home from my Reno trip and this has made me furious. Hope no one else falls for their shady business practice!

First time at Finch & Fork. 
Found them through Yelp of course! 
I liked what I read and saw. So I figured, why not let's have dinner! 

As soon as we walked in we were greeted and shown to a table. Restaurant was busy but not noisy. 
Our waiter was so kind and patient with us. We truly appreciated that! So many great things on the menu and it was hard deciding. He helped us pick a few things to try. He also explained to my daughter the difference in mac and cheese from the kids menu verses the appetizer. 
We enjoyed a delicious mai tai thanks to his recommendation as well. 

Honestly, I would've given them a 5 if the bread was not burnt. Not just the bread that I needed due to my allergy to flax seed but also the toast that came with one of our dishes. We didn't ask for fresh bread because it took so long to get it in the first place. 

Other than that. We enjoyed our appetizers and meals. Our waiter was attentive when it came to our drinks. 

I would definitely go again.

*** Right on, you rockin the jam sessions. ***

Mon nite was quite impressive.  It was a drizzly,
cool, and random evening.  The street sign here
caught my eye so I stepped in to see some talent.

Band ... 5
Beer ... 3  (I'm not a fan of the nitrous after taste.)
Liquor ... 5
Decor ... 5
Food ... 5

I was really impressed with the bar food.  The fries,
chorizo mussels and spanakopita were decadently 
prepared in a tasty signature way.  I enjoy them all.

*** I'll surely return again.  The band was great! ***

*** C'mon, these beignets are better than Café Monde! ***

And Café Beignet offers a pretty decent breakfast menu too.
Tried the Crawfish Omelet and Southern breakfasts ... 3-star.
The beignet of course is the best thang served here ... 5-star.

*** 5min line moves fast, beignets served up fairly quickly. ***

The only Whole Foods (currently) in all of Reno was minutes from our hotel.  We don't shop at Whole Foods very often when we're home in Vegas, but this location was convenient and had what we wanted as far as healthier options.  Our first visit was just for snacks, but we returned the next day to eat lunch because you can usually rely on Whole Foods to have a great selection at their salad and food bars.  This was a Saturday afternoon and the store was crowded, but I think it may always be busy since it's the ONLY WF in the city.  Still, we didn't really mind.  I ended up with some bbq chicken and rice and we ate outside where there is plenty of room for diners. Convenient and healthy alternative when you want to dine and dash.

Party of 16!!! WoooHoooo!!! We had a great time. With great service. Our Server Leticia was phenomenal. She was attentive and made sure that we were taken care of. So please ask for her when you go. You will be glad you did. 

Everyone had something different. Unfortunately I can't name them all. I'll only talk about what I had. My husband had the same as me. Lol. 

First they bring out Cuban Bread and butter. Y'all.... it's the Bomb. It's made at La Segunda Bakery. Another fabulous spot. We also ordered the Crab Croquettes. You get 2 and they come with their "special " hot sauce. Let's just say.... YUM!!! The crab is amazing. 

For my Entree I ordered the Combo... Cuban Sandwich with the 1905 Salad. You can see In the pics the portion is perfect. And the flavas are fantastic. Everything taste so good. I'm not a big fan of different things in my salad but theirs is sooooo good. I really loved it. I can go on and on about the Cuban Sandwich. I mean.... theirs has to be the best. It really is. 

Run.... don't walk to the Columbia Cafe!!

My sister and I took our husbands here for Father's day. We made reservations for 7:00. We were seated about 7:15. We sat at the table until 7:30 until we were first visited by our server. After we ordered things moved smoothly. While waiting for your dinner they bring you warm pita and white bean hummus. I ordered grilled grouper with dipping sauce and a dinner salad. It was absolutely delicious! Everyone thoroughly enjoyed their food. I would highly suggest this restaurant if you find yourself in Indian Rocks beach.

Let me start by saying I used to love and recommend this place...  Sadly, that has changed.  I noticed lately that the service has gone a bit down hill... Rushed, dirty plates sitting for a long time, etc.  the straw, or should I say straws, that broke the camels back happened within the last two weeks during two separate occasions.  First, I ordered a diet soda last week and when it came it had an oily looking substance at the top, seemingly looked to be soap from a cup that wasn't rinsed all the way.  No biggie, things happen...  I ordered another soda and it looked ok, started drinking it and at about a 1/4 of the way down there was a used fortune out of somebody's cookie that was stuck to the inside of the cup.  At this point, I was pretty thoroughly grossed out- mentioned it to the waiter and he didn't charge me for the soda.  Today was the last straw. My husband went for lunch with coworkers and was eating a bowl of hot and sour soup...  And low and behold...  Scooped up some soup with a big old bug in the middle.  He told the waiter and they did give him his meal for free... But this will be the last time we patronage this establishment- so sad because for a while they had a good thing going.

My boyfriend and I used to drive up to Scottsdale a couple of times a year in order to go to Fogo De Chao as he is a big lover of Brazilian steakhouses. I am only a chicken eater, but even I love the variety of options that Fogo offered. So when we found out a Brazilian steakhouse was opening here we were very excited. 
Churrasco de Brasil has been open since the 10th I believe and we've already gone twice. I really love that the prices are cheaper and the location is a lot closer than Fogo. The salad bar is pretty much identical to Fogo with offerings such as Caesar salad, cheese, salami, potato salad, green beans, lettuce, tomatoes, caprese salad, a garbanzo bean salad, Tabbouli, and a variety of other cold options. There's also rice, feijoada style beans, slices of a sourdough type bread, soup, bacon, and farofa. They also bring mashed potatoes, roasted bananas and my favorite: pao de queijo. 
If you're getting the full experience, I won't even attempt to list all the meats but meat eaters certainly won't be disappointed. I tried the chicken legs and they were amazing and filling. I also tried the molten lava cake which I definitely recommend if you can find any room in your stomach after trying all the tasty food.
I will definitely be back. The food is excellent and the customer service is as well. I am so glad that Tucson finally has a Brazilian steakhouse so I can finally try some new places on my visits to Phoenix.

If it hadn't been for the sweet waitress, the sangria and the deviled egg flight, I would have liked to give this place less than one star. 
In a nutshell, every dish was served cold. Most of it under-seasoned and simply bland. And dry... Sahara desert dry... There are heaps of the less expensive items on the plate (grits, potatoes, cornbread), in sharp contrast to the diminutive nature of the more expensive items (salmon, asparagus). 
I actually apologized to my foodie for bringing them here. Some assorted details:
The deviled egg flight was fabulous. Each egg filled and garnished in a different way. Pleasing to the eye and the palate. $10 a bit steep for  5 half eggs, but it's Carmel, so it's expected. 
The cornbread. Huge portion of it... 4 big squares... this at least had some flavor, but also on the dry end of things. A bit of butter and bit of Pimiento cheese accompanies this cornbread appetizer. 
The fried green tomato and black-eyed pea fritters. For $11 you get three slices of tomato and 4 little fritters. The dips are great, the fried green tomatoes also quite tasty. The black-eyed pea fritters not so much. After biting into one, you find the center has the consistency of re-fried beans, but cold and tasteless.  I wish they would just sell the tomatoes in a separate dish, because I will not ever eat those fritters again. 
So let's discuss the main dishes. Grits, cheesy grits... I was so looking forward to those... what I got was a mountain of some substance that clearly had corn in it, but was more the consistency of... darn I can't even think of anything that I would willingly eat with that consistency... It was a huge lump of cold, dry, hard tasteless something with bits of corn showing. There were some black beans on my plate also and they were cold but tasty, so I do recommend those. I also had two pieces of fried banana on my plate and they were delicious. Wish I had more of those. My friend who had also ordered the same dish did not receive any bananas. The salmon seemed tiny on the mountain of grits. Nice grill marks though... a little too much actually as those were seared halfway through the salmon and tasted simply burned. Welcome to cold hard unseasoned burned salmon. The chili lime butter did nothing to combat the situation as the grits soaked it up like a sponge in record time. My friend's salmon was in the same condition as mine. 
All my guest that had ordered dishes with asparagus received 4 extra skinny half stalks of it. That in itself would be ok, but it looks ridiculous when you lay that across 5 pounds of grits or mashed potatoes that are on the plate. 
Unfortunately the meatloaf didn't fare any better than the salmon, but there was a more generous portion of it on the plate... unfortunately... nobody really wanted more of it. It's a giant cube of meatloaf, which apparently has to have one or more sides that are completely burned. and of course it kept with the theme of cold, dry and bland. The slow roasted pork... per my guest... evoked memories of her childhood's school cafeteria... cold, dry, bland... 
The mashed potatoes were deemed to be ok by some of my guests. 

In my opinion this is great if you want to hang out on the patio on a nice night, sip some drinks and share some apps. Otherwise... NO

Of course I had to check out the new seafood spot on Mass Ave. I'm not a particular fan of seafood, but I am a foodie, so I just had to check it out. 
Let's start with the interior: Fabulous, I would have never thought they could get an airy ocean feel in Indianapolis, but they sure managed to do just that. Already I'm impressed.
Since I love craft cocktails, I had a Hummingbird, which is nice light and refreshing, yet packs a punch. Same goes for the Avenue Twist, but that one is a bit fruity, but not too sweet. I highly recommend both. 
I played it safe and ordered the burger. A great burger considering this place specializes in seafood. Flavorful with lots of bacon chunks, sautéed onions and cheese. Seasoned fries on the side. YUMMY.
Of course I had to sample most of the dishes my friends ordered. The crab cake turned out to be a single crab cake, however very delicious. You can taste the fresh crab. 
The conch fritters came in a huge portion, I passed based on previous conch experiences... conch is not for me. 
Some sort of crab pot turned out to be awesome. It came with a side of crusty bread and had the consistency of a regular dip. Very delicious the whole thing. And while it looked small, it was actually quite a portion. 
Most of my friends ordered the salmon over potatoes. I had a taste and it was savory, cooked to perfection, highly recommend it.
Also sampled the Grouper, which in effect is more like their version of fish and chips. Also very well prepared, not greasy as it is in so many restaurants. 
And of course the sweet corn brulee. A bit sweeter than expected, but oh so good. 
And while I didn't sample it personally, my guests raved about the Caesar salad. 
As far as the food goes, while it is a bit pricey, the food quality is well worth it. In addition to that, the food portions complement the Hoosier appetite. These are not chintzy portions here, you will not walk away hungry. 
Service was friendly, spot on without hovering. This place is great for anything from date night to a casual get-together with friends.

Even with the pandemic, this place remains friendly and so quick with the food too.  Of course they follow all the current health and safety regualtions.

I took full advantage of the Yelp check in offer of free curry fries, which btw were absolutely delicious and such a huge amount of fries that I shared with the entire table. 

I also enjoyed the fried shrimp appetizer. Delicious, nice, crisp, hot and worth it. I probably could have asked for a little more of the aioli though. 

For my entree I chose the fish and chips, full portion ... on hindsight I could have done with half a portion. Oh well, live and learn, right? The fish was perfect. Light and crispy on the outside without being greasy and tender flaky on the inside. Perfect.

I was talked into sharing an elephant ear, yeah it took a lot of convincing there... NOT... I love those and since there wasn't a state fair this year... anyway, the elephant ears alone are reason to pay this place a visit... huge and covered in cinnamon suger just like they are supposed to be... yumm

Yes, I realize I won't make any friends with this review, but I can't help but tell the truth. Let me say that I have worked many years in the food industry myself, was married many years to a chef, have run a successful foodie group over 5 years now... and by the way was born and raised in Germany. And I cringe when I think about this place being marketed as German. 

Getting some glass mugs and throwing some German words on the menu, does not make a German restaurant. I generally enjoy Sahm's restaurants, but this is a huge blunder I am sorry to say, because I really wanted to love this place and I don't leave bad reviews lightly. I do not understand how this place get's these good reviews.

Let's start with the good: The remodel of the old Bent Rail space is phenomenal, looks wonderful. Great job. It doesn't have the advertised beer hall feel though. 

The beer is great. A very nice selection of brews. Then again, if you are marketing it as a German spot you should be aware that Germans have different glassware for the different types of beer. While you can drink most out of you regular glass mug, you really should serve a Weizen in a Weizen glass... that would be the tall slender glass. Minor detail, but it keeps that type of beer from going flat so fast.

The food.. Oh my... the only god remarks I heard from my entire group was that the beet salad and the tomato salad were excellent. Not German, but quite tasty. And that is where it ends. 

I understand that this is supposed to be fancy German cuisine, but before you get fancy, you need to get the basics right. If you're just throwing stuff together to be different and to go with the trend it will catch up with you eventually. 

I ordered the brat... yeah, it came with doctored up kraut that had kale in it, not great but edible. The potato dumplings had zero taste, leaving you with a rather dry tasteless mass in your mouth while you are trying to figure out how on earth you're going to swallow that. The brat itself, first off not what a German would call a brat, but let's not be too particular, the casing was tough and the filling dry and very chewy. So horribly overdone I couldn't eat more than 2 pieces. The only redeeming quality was the mustard, that was delicious. 

Tried the frikadelle, another bone dry meat, yet at least it had some taste to it. The fries were however served cold. 

Blood sausage, also dry and extremely salty.

Krapfen, or donuts as you may, because those certainly have nothing in common with a Krapfen, other than the sugar they're covered in. How can something so greasy be so dry inside and dense? 

Maybe all this dry stuff increases beer sales?

And the advertised Gemuetlichkeit? Not so much. Clearly the waitress was efficient but had about as much warmth as a glacier. Clearly she wanted us out of there quickly. Can I finish ordering before you rip the menu out of my hand? I do know that tables need to be turned, but geesh. If you can't reach something, could you ask for help? Don't reach and lean all over me as I am trying to eat. 

Only about 1/4 of our group would come back for food. The majority would come back for a beer if in the neighborhood, but would not make a special trip here.

Delicious food, great for something different, BYO!!!

First off, I'm not vegetarian... but I guess you could say I'm veg-curious.  I haven't really been to many vegetarian restaurants, so I don't have anything to compare to... but Blue Sage was pretty amazing. I highly recommend you make a reservation. We had a reservation for 8 people on a Friday night - and the small dining space was pretty packed.

The menu can be a little intimidating at first glance... the descriptions are pretty elaborate and choosing your entree will probably take some time.  I suggest you check out their menu online in advance.   We started with a few appetizers - the nachos were like crack (i could probably drink a bowl of that cheese sauce), the spring rolls and plantains were awesome too.  For dinner I opted for the Poblano - a giant pepper stuffed with eggplant, zuccini, a ton of cheese... paired with some onion rings.  I have to say that the presentation of the large plates were something special - almost too pretty to eat.  Fortunately it tasted just as good as it looked.  I also got to sample the Wild Blue Foccacia, which was also awesome.  Oh, and if you have room for dessert try the Hazelnut Toffee Basket.  As you can probably tell, I left the place very satisfied.

I haven't encountered such a miserable person in a long time!

Saturday (4/29) morning around 11 am I dined at Rubicon with my partner, a friend and her daughter. My partner and I arrived first, and walked up to the counter to view the menu. The lady behind the counter looked at us but didn't bother greeting us. After we placed our order I went to pull up two additional chairs to a table to prepare for my friend's (and daughter) arrival. While my partner was waiting to pay, the lady questioned whether we had other people joining us. WTF?!?! First off, why would I set up a table for four if it was only two of us dining? Secondly, I have never ever been asked that question before at any restaurant. Those of you who know me know I eat out on a daily basis. Any way, that was our last interaction with the lady behind the counter until we went back to the counter to ask whether we got refills on our iced tea and lemonade. They lady said one refill and she proceeded to fill up our drinks. When she handed them back, the cups weren't even filled to the top. There was a good two inches of space before the lip of the cup. This lady acted as if we were inconveniencing her the entire time. I did for a second think, "well maybe she's having a bad day" but I saw her crack a smile with another customer. I don't know what her issue was. Maybe she's just constantly miserable. All I know is that this was the worst service I've received in a long time.

Update: After posting the review above, I started to read other reviews and it appears I'm not the only person who has encountered this woman's unpleasant demeanor.

Where to begin....

First impressions when walking into a very small, yet charming Florida like restaurant was extreme happiness....then we met the owner. 

We were unsure of who or what we were supposed to do when walking in. Seat ourselves? There was a sign on the floor that said "Wait for hostess to be seated"...but no hostess. We went and sat at the bar to ask two (2) simple and quick questions.

Question 1: "We parked in the big empty lot behind the restaurant that said "Pay attendant $10" but there was no attendant. Can we still park there?" She said yes because they do not have an attendant on Tuesday's and then walked away. Ahhhh...Ok. We will wait for you to come back around for question two.

Finally when she came back...Question 2: "How do we get a table? Do we seat ourselves or let you know?" Her answer.."If you are going to sit at the bar you need to order food because we are a small place." Ok...I'm fine with that but again...if we wanted a table what do we do? We are newbies here. Her answer was to repeat the "If you sit at the bar you eat at the bar". Whatever. Getting a straight answer was difficult and she disappeared again. She came back and said there was a table in the back....so we went and sat down. Honestly at this point I was just annoyed with her attitude and really just wanted to leave. 

I turned off my annoyance and looked at the chalkboard menu as she rattled off what was left on the menu, all while kicking a family out of the restaurant because their child was erasing part of the chalkboard menu with her hand....thumbs up for multi-tasking.

So the food. One order of crab cakes (2 very small crab cakes) and one lightly blackened fish, both over some greens, both excellent. Key Lime Pie. Excellent as well. An $80 bill for it??...nah. A little too much. 

The food is worth it but I wouldn't go back based on the owner and price point.

On my most recent visit, I got a Blueberry Cheese Croissant and Almond Croissant.  They were fresh out of the oven.  Upon my munching, tears of joy literally streamed down my face.  Angels also resounded seraphific hymns.  It was glorious.

Fun Facts:
-Tea leaves are from Taiwan's Nantou farms!
-Uses fresh fruits 
-No additives 
-Filled with vitamin C from the lime/lemons in the drink

This place has amazing fresh fruit tea and juice. You taste the strong fragrance of their tea and refreshing aroma of the fresh fruits inside the drinks. Don't know how they do it, but I love it! 

Recommend:
- Pearl Milk Tea (Best in Chinatown: my opinion, with only the finest ingredients from Taiwan)

If you notice and wonder in suspicion of some unidentifiable black dots swimming in your fruit drink.... well rest assured- those are called seeds, which exist in fruits and are absolutely safe and nutritious to eat in the drink :) My silly friend did not know those were seeds and ended up spitting each one out. *Face palm*.

Reviewer Feira T. and I had the same problem with this Rouses: bag check. 
I'm a cyclist, and I transport my purchases home in a backpack. I know it's annoying, wearing a backpack in a small urban store like this one because space is at a premium. My bag rides in the cart for that reason. 

When my roommate and I rolled up, it was easy to lock up our bikes...awesome! (The bike racks are not on Barrone Street but in the parking lot behind the store.) 

Then we walked into the store. The greeter--clearly not prepared for bikers who were confused--half-assed a scripted statement about having to check our bags with the security office. We asked to see a sign, explaining the bag check policy. No sign. The greeter told us we would have to leave the store or check our bags. Groceries are more important than no groceries so we went with it. 

The security guard was terrible. He was a total creep and an outright jerk. When we asked for tags, he half yelled, "I'LL BE HERE WHEN YOU'RE DONE SHOPPING, GOD. WHAT DO YOU WANT?" Sir, we wanted bag tags. Did he have a pen? No. Would he let us have a piece of paper to make our own bag tags? No. Did we have paper and a pen? Yes. Did he threaten to throw us out of the store for wanting bag tags? Yes. Urk! 

We were on a time budget, hoping to get my whole list in under 20 minutes...but Jesus, I had to complain about this guy. The GM of the store appeared quickly, heard my complaint, and was properly responsive. The man--name now forgotten--has some good training and a great manner. I felt heard and responded to instead of placated. I understand the need to check larger bags because of loss-prevention, and I'm okay with that...but I would really appreciate a sign and proper training for security staff. 

So that time budget I mentioned? We managed to get everything on my list in under 10 minutes. The layout of this store is clever and intuitive, with a good flow. Traffic is managed well everywhere except a weird bottle-neck at the end of the produce section. I blame the prepared food counter being super delicious. 

The depth of stock isn't perfect, because this location is a smaller urban market. However, it has 98% of what I'm looking for in a larger grocery store. Yay! And still, flow! Intuitive shopping! Good things! The check-out process was fast and wonderful. Just like the Rouses I know and love on Tchoup. 

But hey, going back to the security situation I opened with. You remember that guard promising that he would be in the security office when we were done shopping? He wasn't. Instead, he followed us around as we shopped. YES, THAT'S RIGHT, YELP, A CREEPY ANGRY SECURITY GUARD FOLLOWED TWO WOMEN AROUND A GROCERY STORE GLARING AND MUTTERING UNDER HIS BREATH. And by "followed" I mean "was 10 steps behind us." It wasn't even clever loss-prevention stuff...it was just damn creepy. As we left the store, the GM intercepted the security guard who was "stalking" us with an unhappy look on his face. I don't think the officer made a good decision there.

Were this review not tainted by the weird security situation, I would be happy to give a 4 star review. If I go back and the security situation has cleared up significantly, the ratings will go up. Until then, no. Bikers beware. 

To recap:
- lots of bike parking: check
- well-lit bike parking: check
- weird/bad policies about large bags: check
- stalker-like security guards: check
- helpful manager: check

Accessibility notes: Ramps and automatic doors at all entrances. Store is single level. Aisles can be crowded for mobility devices. Shelves and coolers are quite tall; seated shoppers may require reaching assistance. All food service counters (deli, butcher, cheese, prepared food) are high. No braille signage. Carts available for shoppers needing assistance. Can get loud at peak hours.

Years ago, my buddy Shercole K. posted about this spot on Facebook. She was bumping this dish and that side and this cocktail. It was all too much for me, and I was so sold. Gonna go get my munch on! But no, the  Munch Factory was way the heck up in Gentilly/Lakeview. I am not hiking out there on a weekday. 

A few years later, what moves into the empty restaurant across the street from where I cook? The Munch Factory! This has to be the hand of fate telling me that I cannot go another second without trying this fabulous spot. And fate was right. Shercole was right, too. 

The new "nearly Magazine St" address of the Munch Factory is everything I want in a restaurant. It's just sweet enough to take your date, but it's also open and spacious enough to bring the whole family. Every time I've been here, it's been packed with a mix of diners: families, parties, dates, kids, grandparents, young couples. It's wild. Everyone just bring your friends. 

The menu is full of tasty and tempting dishes, but I always order the pork chop. I can't pick anything else. I'm just so drawn to that fabulous and incredibly skillfully cooked piece of tasty meat. They do it right every time. Every single time. Every side dish is also excellent, but I'm partial to the tomato salad and the mashed potatoes. 

On Valentine's Day, I took home a trio of desserts to share with a friend. We had a great time and enjoyed all of our goodies. 

Yes, the service is often overwhelmed and slow. But the thing that I notice (as a line cook) is that the kitchen keeps up with their orders. Once things get back to the kitchen, the cooks are on top of their game. It's moving things from tableside to kitchen that could use some refinement. I'm not sure how to see a better balance of personable service and servers making good money while having a more efficient experience. (See, if they add more servers, everyone on the floor makes less money which is less ideal. That's not really a great balance, you know?)

On quiet afternoons, I've cozied up to the bar with a textbook and a tiki cocktail to knock out some studying. On bustling Friday nights, I've brought friends for a really fun time. On work nights, I've called across the street for a to-go order because I can't go a single second longer without some Elysian peels. The Munch Factory hits all of those needs, you know? 

One last story, if I may. This is a family-run joint, and the couple who runs it really does care about their city and their neighborhood and their people. One afternoon, I was walking home when I saw a kid who was maybe 14 trying car doors and poking at someone's scooter in a suspicious way. One of the owners also noticed, and she dipped into the kitchen for a second. A minute later, one of the cooks popped out of the kitchen casual as could be. He greeted the kid by name and chatted him up. Instead of chasing this kid off or calling the cops, they talked for a few minutes and intervened by just being present and being part of the neighborhood. The young teen wasn't treated like a menace. He was treated like part of the neighborhood, and that's what the Munch Factory is: part of the whole neighborhood. 

I'm so glad. 

Accessibility notes: step up into the shop. Doors open out (front) and in (side). Can get loud at most hours. No Braille menu or signage. Lights can be dim after dusk. Lots of space for mobility devices to move around and between tables. High bar at back and high hostess stand at front.

When I can't bring myself to go back and try a place again for the sake of the review, but I also didn't get sick the first time I ate there...well, that's a 2 star spot.

I make the mistake of dating people who basically can't eat food. (But gosh, they are cute!) My current +1 mostly exists on BBQ so off to BBQ joints we go! I actually save up all of my cravings for when she's in town so we can try new spots together and have some fun. 

We were here on a weeknight in December, and it was nearly empty. It was also totally frigid outside so that might explain the empty tables. You'd think empty restaurant = more attentive service, right? Nope. Our service was mildly lack-luster at best. The simple requests we made just...took...a...long...time. Like asking the bar what their seasonal beer was. Forever later, our server walked back and...had forgotten. The food was run promptly, which was a perk. 

Neither of us were dazzled by the food. I got brisket and asked for some burnt ends. The server had no idea what I was asking for and went to get her manager. (This confused me.) The manager was really condescending to both the server and to us as he explained that they didn't just "request" burnt ends like that, especially on the brisket because "no one wanted burnt ends." That, sir, is a tragedy against quality burnt ends and should be filed away as such. The server also couldn't tell us what was gluten-free. (Soy sauce is a common addition to BBQ/smokehouse sides.) We eventually figured out what was safe for both of us to eat, ordered, and got it all together. Finally. It took so much longer than I expected, though. 

The food didn't take long to arrive, but it wasn't anything special. I feel like I paid a MidCity premium for something that's just not that special in the first place. Everything felt very "we're about to franchise this m'fer so HURRY UP AND FLOCK HERE." 

I remember all of our sides being so, so salty. Just so salty. How are they so salty? What is happening here? Even the charred Brussels spouts--which were pretty novel and stuff--were just super salty and not great. 

But neither of us got food poisoning so that's a win, I suppose. 

Accessibility notes: ramp up to the building. Door opens out. No Braille menu or signage. Hostess stand and bar are both high. Can get loud at peak hours. Space is well-lit.

I am unabashed about asking for information. If I want something, I will put on a smile and go looking. In a restaurant, I will ask about where they source x, y, or z ingredient. I will ask about preparation. I will ask what something means. I will ask about wine, beer, or cocktails. I will leave no stone unturned. 

Ancora was ready for me, in that respect. We asked our server to define roughly half the menu; and he did so with panache. I asked about the nuances of some of the different cheese; he had a simple explanation ready for me. I wanted wine, but I didn't recognize any of the varietals on the menu so I asked the bartender (who wasn't slammed so I didn't feel a bit guilty). I asked and asked and asked, until I was happy with the answer. And Ancora's staff kept answering me. That pleases me. 

So why the emphasis on questions? Because Ancora has a learning curve. With a menu that relies heavily on Italian, it can get confusing. But see, Italian is a language with a number of very specialized food words so each nuance of cheese or meat has a name. This leaves us with a delicious precision in food preparation. I am happy with the precision because it means the flavors are carefully cultivated. 

We had two pizzas (the daily special and the Bianca), both delicious. Between three people, two pies and an app were enough to satisfy. Now, the trick with the pizzas we ordered was compromise. One member of our party doesn't like olives or capers, both fixtures on the Bianca pizza. She agreed to try it because she was out-voted...then she loved the pizza. I think that reflects strongly on the quality of the ingredients going into each pie. Another of our number doesn't love arugula on pizza, but she didn't mind picking it off if it was too much. There wasn't a leaf left on her plate, either. I was super impressed. 

There is no doubt that I would return to Ancora. I'd love to see the decor change a little bit and move away from using grey as the neutral. (Art historian moment: I feel like they need a warm neutral like taupe or soft yellow to really capture the creamy, soft, crisp vibe. Grey was too cold, too industrial, too "Chipotle-esque" for my eye.) 

And a note on the service: They seem to have ironed out the issues other, earlier reviews noted. I can see where the service would get thin, but everyone was where they should be doing what they should be doing tonight. It was like watching a beautiful bicycle being put through its paces. I really enjoyed the cohesive nature of the service, with management blending into table service blending into the bar blending into the kitchen blending into the pizza makers. It really worked. 

I want to give Ancora a 5 star review, but I also want to leave room for the place to grow. My fervent hope is that I will bump this place up to a 5 star joint with my next visit.

Accessibility notes: Door opens out. Fully accessible for mobility devices. Can get loud. No braille menu or signage.

This is a great place for a ice cold draft beer if you're in Dunedin.  This place is always busy.  Service is just okay.  Food a little pricey. So not a place to do lunch often.  I was working in the area.  For a couple weeks.  Not wanting to spend 12 to 15 dollars for lunch every day. But food was good

Birthday dinner at Cody's.  I had the blackened rib eye steak with loaded baked potato.  The server when she brought our food to the table asked if I wanted steak sauce! Absolutely not.    If I need steak sauce.   Something wrong.   The steak was cooked perfect.  Lots of Flavors.   It was delicious.  Loaded baked potato was great.   My wife ordered the salmon with sweet potato.   She liked it.  But to me the salmon was to small of a piece for dinner.  It was a 3oz piece.   That's lunch size portion.  The salad here is awesome.  It's been 5 years since we ate hear.
