I've been here a bunch of times and it's usually for the char siu fried rice or char siu pork bun (not pictured). Those items, in my opinion, are to die for. I can't get enough! The price point is what you'd expect for a ramen/Japanese restaurant and I'm overall satisfied. I do think I've had better ramen at other locations but it doesn't mean they're by any means lacking.

April 9, 2016, a day that I will forever remember. The Rittenhouse Hotel and the Lacroix Restaurant in The Rittenhouse Square area of downtown Philadelphia were an extraordinary backdrop for a special moment in my life ... My Wedding Day!

The Rittenhouse Hotel, situated directly across from Rittenhouse Square, and Lacroix Restaurant with Lily's Cafe and the La Serre private dining space provided us with the wonderfully ideal, intimate, elegant and organic setting for our wedding.

5+ Stars for Sylvain Briens, Food and Beverage Director for Lacroix. From Day One upon when Sylvain walked us through the hotel lobby, lounges, and the various areas within the restaurant, he was not only the consummate professional but also very charming, personable and witty. Sylvain's attention to detail was also second to none and certainly solidified our decision to make this the perfect setting for our special day. Aside from the obvious visual beauty of the hotel and restaurant, it was comforting knowing that everything, including all the little details, would be taken care of with ease and elegance. Equally as impressive was the way in which he and his staff accommodated our guests treating them with the same level of importance as we were given as the bride and groom.

So, who expects a snowflake-laden day to pop-up on the second weekend in April? Well at least not me, however the atmosphere of The Rittenhouse was so wonderful that the snow was an afterthought as it was sunny in my head and heart.

The pre-wedding cocktail hour was held in Lily's Cafe, the same space where the nuptuials were exchanged, was quite splendid with several hors d'oeuvres ... tuna tartare, short ribs rillette, heart of palm tempura with aioli and crab complimented by an open bar of wine, champagne and cocktails. The hors d' oeuvres received rave reviews from all the guests as they nibbled and mingled prior to the ceremony.

My vision for the decor played out perfectly as my wedding planner, Tonia Adleta of Aribella Events, brought all the decorative elements together in such an organic, intimate and luxurious way.

Our dinner reception was held in La Serre, an intimate private dining space with a long wooden table with seating up to 18, adorned with cream and green florals and accented by beaded candles. The chairs were upholstered in a forest green velour which enhanced the overall natural feel for this quaint environment. It was just the touch that we were looking for to complete the picturesque French country setting.

The servers were very precise, executing their skills masterfully like a choreographed performance, attending to each of the guests' requests and needs. Dinner was exquisite ... a true compliment to the setting with traditional starters of either Caesar Salad or Shrimp Cocktail followed by expertly prepared and plated selections of Butter Poached Lobster, Filet Mignon, Green Circle Chicken, or English Pea Risotto. Some of the main selections change seasonally depending on when you hold your event, just one of the finer details that Sylvain discussed with us as we built the menu for the evening. Dessert was artistic and yummy choices between a Chocolate, Salted Caramel, Hazelnut and Mango delicacy or Pavlova with Grapefruit, Pistachio and Honey. We told our guests that hopefully they saved room as last but not least was the wedding cake ... baked by Sweet T's Bakery in Haddonfield, NJ ... a gorgeous naked triple-layered cake champagne vanilla with salted caramel and blueberry velvet adorned with fresh florals and drenched with strawberries and blueberries. The wait staff also gracefully handled serving all of the slices of cake to our guests after we cut the cake and shared our first slice.

If you are planning a mid luxe wedding in Philadelphia and want exceptional customer service, attention to detail and a setting with a multitude of beauty, style and elegance, Lacroix restaurant in the The Rittenhouse hotel is the place.

So, I ended up at Vesper on a whim for a NYE dinner and it paid off. After arriving at another restaurant in which we had reservations, to find a sign on the door stating "Closed due to electrical problems", we Yelped to find another place within the near proximity. I have never even heard of Vesper but once I read a few reviews and saw the rating I decided why not give it a try.

Since it was not on one of the main streets in Philly, I was initially apprehensive. Upon entering the restaurant, there was a staff to greet you in a small vestibule area. They were pleasant and showed us to our seats right away. On this night they had a live local singer/songwriter, Travis McDaniel who was a perfect accompaniment to the evening. Great vocals which seemingly blends jazz, with slashes of pop and funk. And I also could hear a modicum of soul pouring through those vocal chords hand in hand with his side kick guitar. Awesome, original, and fresh talent.

For dinner we dined on a selection of seasonal oysters, jumbo shrimp and the crab cake w/ beurre blanc and kale slaw. The oysters and shrimp tasted like they were plucked straight from the ocean. Succulent and plump. The crab cake was satisfying and filling and gets a solid 7.5-8/10. It's hard not to compare crab cakes to my beloved Maryland crab cakes but these were not bad. Less filler is always the best way to go. Dinner was gratifying and few complaints.

Vesper is multidimensional as its downstairs houses a club. It was not or shall I say had not opened while we were there but after reading the reviews and seeing people talk about the password protected door, it intrigued me. Maybe another time, depending on the age group it caters to.

The decor could be a bit more updated as the decor seemed heavy but it was not distasteful just seems a smig dated with the heavy curtains and wood elements and tray ceilings.

I like Vesper, I really did. It was just a fun and spontaneous evening which turned out to be a god one.

So, out tonight with my guy and friends for our monthly Friday Foodie gathering. It was my 1st time at Parc and I was very pleased.

Piping through the sound system was melodic french music which sounded like a variety of contemporary jazz artists. Great tempo and volume for the overflowing crowd dining for the evening. Although there were many people filling the tables and bar area, the noise factor was surprisingly neither overpowering nor intrusive.

The restaurant was larger than I expected but tables were spaciously distributed so you did't feel so close to the neighboring table. Dim lighting set the early evening mood with hint of romance but enough light to make it appropriate amongst friends.

For my appetizer, I had escargot and my table-mates indulged in Macaroni au Gratin and ravioli stuffed shells with a delicate cheese. We all shared and each was an 8 out of 10 on the delicious scale. The escargot was tender in a broth containing mushrooms (& other ingredients I can't recall). They were out of their shell which was a departure from my previous escargot experiences. The Macaroni au gratin was piping hot with a white cheese. It was slightly rich and creamy with a mildly sweet taste that was so appetizing. The ravioli hors d' oeuvres of four was a appropriate size and were good. Light cheese filling and the pasta for the ravioli was simple without any fanfare.

For my entree, I had pan-seared scallops which in one word, Divine. A mild sweet flavor, tender and juicy. Although only 4 scallops were served with dinner,  they were generous in size and very filling. A top the scallops were black trumpet mushrooms, onion suboise &  peas. I am not a mushroom fan but found the assortment of all 3 to be tasty and savory.  

For dessert I had the coconut sorbet with rum... It was so lip and tongue swirling delicious, I decided on my next visit, I'm eating dessert 1st. Dessert & a cocktail all in one. What more needs to be written!?

Enjoyed, happy & full = return & I mean soon...

Stopped into this vegan restaurant on a whim. Was excited that a vegan option was available as Wilmington was a pit stop in route traveling back home.

At the Wilmington Riverfront next to a couple other notable restaurants it could be easily missed as it is unassuming and no external signage that pops for your attention.

The oddity was it's a vegan restaurant that also sells dairy ice cream. Perhaps they want to capture a wider customer base. At the front cashier station, is a glass display case that showcases books by African American (AA) authors and retro candies from the past. One wall is adorned with cultural art, a piano and a variety of AA relics from historical events and tchotchkes.

I came solely for the vegan hot dogs and they were tasty accompanied with a side of sweet potato chips. They filled the spot for a fast and quick energy boost. I also had a Mojito Green with limes, green tea leaves and fresh mint leaves which was a delightfully tasty.

First impressions are everything so my next comments are meant for constructive critique for forward improvements.

Aesthetically, this vegan spot has huge potential. The biggest concern for me is it needs a deep cleaning, dusting, streamline the clutter and a cleaner look. From the kitchen, floors and bathrooms. Bathrooms should always be stocked with hand paper and other essentials. If it is also used for storage it should be conspicuously hidden. 

The staff were pleasant especially the young teen @ the counter. Yet, the owner/staff on the phone during my entire visit was disappointing and showed a lack of professionalism as a representation of the restaurant. Maybe it was just this day only or @ least I hope so.

I want this place to work and do well. It is the only full service vegan restaurant I was able to find in Wilmington. Hope they know how valuable their BRAND is and can be... The food & drink I would rate 4 stars but the other elements lowered the scoring and 1st impression.

Would like to return and see a 360 because it has all the right bones.

Berry Berry multigrain pancakes w/ strawberries, blueberries, blackberries & raspberries........I should just stop "The Review" here but I digress. LOL

Amy's is one of NJ's many diners but to me it stands apart given a few qualities. 

1. The menu although has many many items, it is creative, well organized, descriptive and fun. The descriptions of the food items make you want to try different entree each time you visit.

2. The decor is simple yet it has some interesting photos, art and objects all over the place, distinct to NJ, from the inland to the shore.

3. It has great seating with a combo of booths and tables. The waiting area is just outside the hostess area with seating so there is not an overflow inside where peeps are eating.

4. Lastly, the food. I have only had breakfast here and each time it is hands down filling and tasty. The bacon is crisp and they bring it to you minus lots of oil/grease. And the Berry Berry pancakes are light, airy and scrupmtous. There is a one panckae option that is greatly appreciated for those of us with tiny tummies or just want to be conscious of intake. Candian ham is also a winner, with not an overbearing salty taste.

Hands down, thus far in my diner experience, Amy's is the best in overall ambiance, food, services and options. I give it a solid 5 stars and a promise to return.

Stopped in today as I was headed back to work from an appointment. Since it was early, thought I would get a breakfast bite to fill my ever so empty tummy. Saw this delicious looking crab and asparagus quiche in the prepared food showcase. Requested it be warmed, so by the time I returned to work, I could sit and enjoy what I knew was going to be a seafood fiesta in my mouth. Boy, was I disappointed. Just trying to cut the quiche was difficult, the crust and crab, asparagus and egg filling were all dry. Was the lack of moisture due to how it was prepared or was it overheated? Not really sure but this was a miss. I've had other food items at Di Bruno Bros and was pleasantly happy with my choices but today.... Not so much.

I live in NJ across the bridge just about 6 miles away from Philly, work a few blocks from Reading Terminal and have come to Iovine Brothers Produce (IBP) a few times for fruits never any other items but TODAY, was a lesson in "This is what it feels like when you don't pay toooo much!!

Had b/fast at RT and decided to pick up a few items at IBP, while there so we could avoid going to our favorite luxury organic market. Well, slap my butt and call me Silly...  Who knew the prices here were so low?  Clearly, all but me.

I purchased fruit & veggies to include sweet potatoes, Brussel sprouts, mixed greens, arugula, 3 types of apples, bag of Halos, sesame oat bran sticks, raspberries, blackberries, grapes, strawberries, bananas, a slice of watermelon, mango and broccoli all for under $40.?! What? I am so sold on this place.

Yes, it is small, aisles are narrow, and so it can be cramped but for the prices you get here, can't be beat. A few items I was able to snag for $1 and a couple others were under $3. The fact they use a local farm for their produce gets them even more appreciation.

I'm sold and this place will definitely be a part of the weekly errands, just need to come early to get a good parking spot.

I'm keeping this just above one star only because they are new, and the point of this review is to help identify areas for improvement as I think this place could have potential.

We were a big party, and they seated us in a nice private back room, things were looking good at the beginning.

The list of service ills is long, but I think reasonable for an establishment with $20+ entrees.

1) No water refills - we were constantly asking more.  Just put some pitchers on the table if you're not going to dedicate staff to this task.

2) No drink refills either - everyone had to specifically request another cocktail or glass of wine usually twice as the server was running out of the room.

3) Are you selling used cars or fine dining?  The high-pressure pitch about the menu works against you.  Highlighting the most expensive entrees and how your $260 bottle of wine is almost half the St. Elmo price doesn't make you look good, it cheapens the experience.

4) The line caught, amazing ahi tuna that you rave and rave about was charred on two sides - who takes a wonderful piece of fish and blackens the crap out of it?

5) No vegetarian entree - plus the server actually made fun of their beet starter saying "you should only get that if you're vegan or something".  The comment was fairly offensive to my vegetarian wife and also to vegans since the dish has a yogurt sauce.

6) Mistakes with the salad and entree courses were handled with minimal grace.  The salad order was wrong for one person.  The entrees were right, but they were set in front of the wrong people.

7) Trying to give us our check without offering dessert, coffee, port, etc. and then blaming us for your mistake saying "I thought I heard someone say no dessert".

8) Our server, the head of service, interrupted conversation to awkwardly ask for feedback about the food and service from the entire table.  Who gives meaningful feedback to you in front of 8 of their friends, especially when it's going on one check?

When the head of service doesn't know what good service looks like, you have a major problem.

Got to try this spot with a friend and was so excited to try the new Cunningham concept! 
Atmosphere is great and a little moody. Service was great and our waiter seemed highly knowledgeable and excited about the menu offerings. 
We wanted to try a few things so we got the bao buns, soft crab tempura, and the main lobster Rangoons. 
Bao Buns are so delicious and I'm demanding these as my last meal! Haha
Main lobster rangoons are fantastic as well! So flavorful. 
The soft crab tempura feel super flat for us and was surprisingly disappointing. Kind of tasted like just a piece of fried dough (funnel cake consistency almost). The slaw does nothing to complement the crab and the entire dish was flat. We told the server how disappointing this was when everything else was so amazing! 
It was my first time trying sake and they have a sparkling one that's a great intro to it. Cocktails were also tasty. Overall a great experience and would recommend! Just avoid the soft crab tempura haha.

New to the neighborhood and we're trying to land "our spots". We found our Thai Spot for sure in Baan Thai! We ordered takeout on a Saturday and it was a quick and painless process. Phone to table in 30 minutes. Staff is Covid ready and eager for your orders! 

What we snagged:
-Money Bags (SO Baan [damn] good!) 
-Pad Thai (Veggie and Tofu) 
-Pad Kee Mao (Veggie and Tofu) 

Everything was VERY flavorful and HUGE portions. All for sub $30. Got two meals out of it all. We'll be back to Baan for all their great dishes for sure! The ONLY constructive feedback is ensuring the tofu isn't as mushy next time around.

Great beer menu. Great affordable food. Listen the beer and food is more than a regular bar fare. But this is not a regular bar. Great selection of beers. About ten beers on tap from IPAs and local fare. The food is great   The chef takes time with every order to make it the best. This is not your everyday bar food.   The environment is also on point. As I was eating there a jazz band was playing. This place deserves more credit.  It's hard to get a tap and restaurant a stablished.  Check this place out. You won't regret it. It's a upper class place.  With casual dress code.

Really good Croquet Madame!  Tip - only difference between a Croquet Madame and a Croquet Monsieur is the Madame has an egg on it!  

The Crab Maison is basically lump crab with some sauces/spices.  If you don't like horseradish, don't get this.  

We also got the seafood tower.  EVERYTHING was so fresh.  Pricey but worth it.  Goes really well with a nice bottle of champagne.  Good wine list and a lot of the bottles are reasonably priced.  

Service was really friendly and helpful!  I'll definitely come back for the Croquet Madame!

Stopped here for dinner on the way back to LA.  

This Bouchon is a nice, quaint little restaurant, not affiliated with the infamous Bouchon in Napa and Beverly Hills.

However the food was just as fantastic but it wasn't as pricey.  Pretty PRICEY but not Napa/BH Bouchon pricey.    

Here's what we got:

Scallop Trio - simply AMAZING
Exotic Mushroom - pretty tasty, nice starter
Roasted Duck Breast - their flagship dish, most popular, and very delicious.  The duck was prepared really well and cooked perfectly.  If you're a duck lover, you MUST TRY THE DUCK HERE!  
Grilled Lamb Rack - if you don't like your meat squirming in your plate, order it medium well.  They tend to lean more in under-cooking the meat.  
French Onion soup - kinda salty for my taste and I tend to like salty things

Good price range of Champagnes and Sparkling Wines and good variety.  You can ball out if you want or just go with an average bottle.  

Service was top notch and free parking is available.  There's a city lot close to the restaurant, first 75 mins is free then it's $1.50 for every hour.

WARNING - This is a fine dining spot so try and dress up a bit.  No flip flops, ripped jeans, and tank tops!

The burgers here always give me massive diarrhea. I'm not the only one of my friends who complains about this. The servers are also always too hipstery and act too cool to be working there and waiting on you. Unlike most of these people just writing things based on the news, I live in Philadelphia and have been here many times, starting when they opened. 

Also, they seem to not respect the privacy of their customers, that's disturbing. I don't think I'll come back.

I don't know man...I expected a lot better based on the reviews.  The location is in a really run down building but YAY for a private parking lot!  The space is confused, like it hasn't been remodeled or given a proper face lift from whatever it had been before the Kitchen Sink moved in...and putting art on the wall does not fix that confused run down vibe, sorry.  

We arrived around 2pm on a week day and there were only 2 other tables seated.  The service was painfully slow for it not being busy.  I ordered the reggie, which is a basic burger, but I went with a turkey patty.  The hubs went with a breakfast burger.  We ordered a large sweet fries to split.  In my mind I kept thinking, sweet potato fries...nope, don't think that!  They are SWEET fries.  So while they are sweet potatoes that are cut like fries and fried like fries, they do not taste anything like fries because they are covered and swimming in syrup.  You need to eat that shit with a fork!  And they are SO sweet, sweet doesn't even begin to describe them accurately.  I have to say they aren't for me but I appreciate the creativity.  Total dining time was well over an hour, of which at least 30-40 minutes were spent waiting on our food....which doesn't equate when there are only three tables with patrons (all that came in at different times).

I used the restroom after eating and quickly found out that NONE of the toilets flush and that the sink had barely enough water pressure to wash the soap off my hands.  If I had used the bathrooms first, we probably wouldn't have eaten here.

THEY DON'T SERVE KIDS or anyone with them!

The owner came outside and let us know blatantly..  So it sort of sucked as I wanted to try it..  

I get it... but it still hurt...

I believe this place is as serious about pizza as I am!  All of the pizzas (yes, plural) I had here had the perfect combination/amount of toppings and THE perfectly light crust. Among them, my favorites were &pizza's versions of a mushroom pizza (which I would usually order) and a Hawaiian pizza (which I would actually usually avoid). Every bite of the mushroom pizza (Moonstruck) was full of mushrooms and truffle essence, grilled onion, and a goat cheese/fig balsamic finish. The Hawaiian pizza (Pineapple Jack) was also absolutely delectable, as it had fresh (not canned) pineapple, freshly pickled onion, and a punchy "cherry bomb barbecue" finish.

 ... Yeah, I would absolutely come back.

French 75. I could probably finish the review there, but I won't, but I probably should. You shouldn't visit Bourbon St. without drinking a French 75 at Arnaud's. They have a nice drink menu and their staff is super nice. 

A little quaint, but a pleasant ambiance and a wonderful place to meet up with a friend for drinks.  

Their French 75 is reason enough to pay them a visit.

Always consistently delicious food and really great, friendly service from this family-owned business. I love even more that their employees are family, too (many have been with them for a very long time). 

We went over the weekend (the first time during covid) and they were reassuring with masks on; a contactless Venmo option, and limiting the number of people in the store. Everyone else we saw who went in to pickup orders while we were there were also masked as well.

Thanks for being an institution in west Philly, Lee's Deli!

Corazon Cocina is located inside the Santa Barbara Public Market. Best to go family style to try a little of everything. I shared the Corazon Salad, Sal De Mar, Tia Juana, La Chicana, tres leches cake, and I feel I'm missing one more item. Of these, my favorite was the Sal De Mar because the poke was refreshingly fresh on a surprisingly hot day in Santa Barbara. The watermelon to that dish was a nice touch. 

My other favorite that concluded this delicious lunch was the tres leches cake. It wasn't too sweet and full of flavor. 

Prices are on the higher end for tapa-size portions, but trust me, it's worth to indulge!

Lines can get long as it was on a mid-August Sunday, but moved quickly enough. Everything is self-served, you get a buzzer and pick up your food when it's ready. Plenty of seating throughout the public market. Overall, a great first experience at Corazon Cocina.

#50/2018

State & Fig is a great place for lunch, tucked in a small walkway of different shops/restaurants. I came for a late lunch on a Monday around 3pm and pretty much had the whole place to myself. I had a portebello mushroom panini and couple bites of the fig burger. 

The portebello mushroom panini included a generous amount of red bell peppers. The bread had a touch of pesto sauce and it all melted nicely together with provolone cheese. This also came with a side of arugula salad. I loved how they put the vinaigrette dressing on the side.

I had a few bites of the burger and it was just ok. I did enjoy the fries that came with, lightly crunchy and not overly salty. 

Service was ok, can't complain, prices were fair. I'd come back to State & Fig in the future.

PREVIOUS REVIEW FOR VISIT ON 5/17:

I had never been here before and my friends brought me for the first time today.  It was a $15 cover charge which I thought was kind of high.  I ordered a Stoli bloody mary upon entry from the super friendly bartender at the inside bar.  It was good, not the best I've ever had, and had a nice level of spice to it.  

I was hanging out in the pool with friends, having a good time, when I decided I wanted another drink and went to the outside bar.  I waited patiently, making contact with the 2 bartenders, who never bothered to acknowledge my presence.  A girl in a bikini arrived at the bar after me, complaining that her drink was not up to par.  One of the bartenders working, chubby white dude in a black tank top, immediately attended to her even though I was there first (I've been standing there at this point waiting patiently, haven't said anything).  She said something to him along the lines of, "Go ahead and take care of him, I need a second to make up my mind."  The same chubby black tank top dude looks at me and asks what I want, and I order a Pina Colada.  He says, to me and the girl, "I'm not making that drink, you make that drink" (talking to the other bartender at this point).  He then says, "Why do you want that, man?  You trying to get diabetes?"  

The interaction was beyond unpleasant.  He was ridiculously rude and publicly ridiculed my drink choice.  Forget it.  I've been to tons of bars in NOLA and NEVER had that happen to me anywhere but here.  The drink was $10 and it was one of the shittiest pina coladas I've ever had.  

The bloody mary, pina colada with a side of douchiness, and entrance fee was $35 before tip.  F*&t that.  I'll go to my gym and go to the pool there.  It's cleaner, they have a bar, and the bartenders aren't judgmental pricks

I enjoyed this place. Fried pickles were great, not soggy and drenched in oil like others I've had. Fried green tomatoes were great as well. Nice thick cornmeal crust. Had the chicken fried steak, nothing too great, but not horrible either. My sister had the quinoa burger and she enjoyed it. The tomato jam was delish! I would come back next time I'm in Nashville.

Brittingham's is back and better than ever! After being sold last year and closed for massive renovations, the space opened again this week--and, oh man, is it spectacular. 

Everything in the space has been overhauled, and you wouldn't recognize it if you'd been here before. There is a huge patio with gas fire pits, a roof deck, three bars, and valet parking. 

The menu has been totally reimagined and is executed to perfection by by their head chef, who trained under Perrier. I've had housemade pickles (tasty) and the chicken sandwich, which was wonderfully smokey. Perhaps my favorite thing from here is the raw bar, though--yes, you heard that correctly: legit raw bar in Lafayette Hill (and that's not a euphemism). The east coast oysters, blue points at the time, were massive and super fresh, with a nicely prepared accompanying mignonette. They were seriously up there with Oyster House and Route 6, maybe even a touch better because of their huge size. 

I beer selection is not bad at all, and is priced well, with some big bottles, like the Rogue Double Chocolate, coming in as low as $6.50! I'm hoping that in time they work on the draft beer selection a little and make some more creative picks. They just opened, though, so I am sure they will work this out. The wine list is fantastic, though. Really nice selections, and I believe they even have a sommelier--yes, you heard that  correctly: a sommelier in Lafayette Hill!

Perhaps the most exciting thing, for me, about the new Britt's is that they are opening early on the weekends for English Premier League soccer! I cannot wait to roll in at 7am to watch my Chelsea or my wife's Tottenham throw down on their opponents, over some tasty breakfast. 

I seriously could not believe it when I heard about the new Britt's. How could they know all of my favorite things--beer, wine, food, soccer, oysters--and bring them together? Somehow they did, and I love them for it. Welcome back to the neighborhood, Britt's.

These guys are as excited to be here as I am to have them! Formerly associated with Frankie & Johnnies, Luca Eats owners have revitalized the old Roman Pizza location in the best way. The once corner filling station has a retro look and cafe style eats served on fresh baked breads. The breakfast and lunch panini can be ordered anytime with ingredients like eggs, avocado, Chorizo, fried green tomato and fresh veggies. 

They've also added the famous fried green bell peppers and an array of taster sounding salads. I'm excited to make this a regular stop for casual breakfast/lunch on the go. But there is a surprising amount of seating for such a small place. The future looks bright!
Best Gelato in the world! Also, there is an amazing atmosphere. This is something Philly has never seen before!!

I'm sorry, Brown Betty. You can slap me like a scorned woman if you want, but I have been been cheating on you. Yes, I know. It is a sordid state of affairs, indeed, as I have been a valued cupcake patron for the past two years. You know something is up because I haven't been coming in as regularly as I once did. I keep blaming the new "gym routine," when I've really been cupcake-sluttin' it up over at Philly Cupcake. Don't cry. I'll be back. I just needed variety in my cupcakes.

The owners of Philly Cupcake are courteous and helpful, and the atmosphere is a joy to experience. The cupcakes are kept in adorable cupboards and the shop has the feel of an old ice cream parlor. Philly Cupcake serves up light n' fluffy cakes that melt in your mouth. They are so yummy, that I can never wait to get home and eat them. There has been many a shameful afternoon and evening when I have bought a cupcake, walked right out of the store, and proceeded to practically rip the bag apart with my teeth in order to get to the cupcake goodness hiding inside. Yes, that was me on the corner of 12th and Chestnut with icing all over my face...

I hesitate to give this place a good review because I want it to remain a hidden gem. Bottom line: this place is awesome. If you live in the hood, go there. Get the lamb. I cannot pronounce much less spell most of the dishes but every single one I've had there makes me sad when it is finished. The staff is attentive and the chef is authentic. You will not be sorry you tried it.

Heard through the grapevine that today was the soft opening so I got in the car and sped here. First of all, the location is perfect since the area is lacking in Vietnamese cuisine. Located in the same plaza as Fresh Market so it wasn't hard to find. Yes, that Fresh Market that was on the news recently. 

The restaurant has several booths and probably 10-12 tables that sits 4 per table. The place is new so it's still nice and clean. The dividers are decorated with pleasant neon lights. 

The food:
We ordered several items so that we can get a feel for the place. We got goi cuon, appetizer sampler, pho dac biet, hu tieu heo, and com tam bo suong nuong bi trung. 

The goi cuon was meh for me. Too much noodles and not enough pork or shrimp. The peanut sauce that comes with it was standard. 

The appetizer sampler for $11.95 is a good deal. The eggrolls were tasty and the nuoc mam that accompanied it was seasoned well. 

The pho dac biet's broth was flavorful and light not heavy as some other places. There was a good balance of noodles and meat. 

The hu tieu for me was bland though. It needed a dash of fish sauce, but still lacked that hu tieu aroma and taste. 

The broken rice platter with pork chop, fried egg, and shredded pork (com tam bo suong nuong bi trung) was huge. The pork chop was tender and had a slight sweetness to it, but still very good. I would order this platter again. 

Service was good considering it was their soft opening, and food came out fairly quick. 

The prices are a little steep, but it's par for the area. I will have to come back to try the other dishes.

Love this place! Unassuming exterior, but don't let that fool you. The interior is cute and exudes that warm Ohana feeling. There was nothing on the menu that I didn't like so I just ordered several items. You could just tell the owners pay attention to detail and quality with each bite. All organic and fresh. 

FYI: If you do takeout they will bring out the food to you so you don't have to change out of your pj's:) 

I just wish they were closer to me!
Go to place for dimsum when I'm in this part of town. Great for family dinners. We always order the Canh Chua and tom rang muoi.

I figured I would write a quick review before I fall into a food-induced coma. 

Pizza Gregario is located on a side street in downtown Safety Harbor not too far from the pier. When I inquired as to why they weren't open for lunch, I was told that they did when they first opened, but lunch business was not cost effective. I can understand why because they are not located on Main Street. They have only been open for 14 months. 

I bookmarked this place awhile ago, but every time I had a pizza craving it was usually around lunchtime and they weren't open. Finally, my craving kicked in at the right time and I made the drive here. 

As I stepped in, I could tell right away this wasn't a typical pizza place. One of the owners greeted me right away and asked if it was my first time there. When I said yes he quickly pointed out the menu to me which was hard to miss since it was a huge blackboard. The board states their veggies, and meat are all sourced locally. Locally grown organics and grass fed meat. Quality you can really taste because of this. After looking over the menu, I decided on the caesar salad, beet salad, market salad, margherita pizza, and Eh Mate pizza.   

As I waited for my order, I got to talk with one of the owners. It's two brothers who own Pizza Gregario. They are from the New England area and came here about 2 years ago. Both owners were really nice and made you feel welcomed. The order was sent by a clothesline like string from the cashier counter to the counter where the order was to be made which was cool. 

The Caesar salad with romaine lettuce, manchego cheese, lemon anchovy dressing and soft pita was very good. I thought the pita added a different dimension and spin on the typical caesar salad. The salad wasn't drenched in dressing nor was it lacking dressing. It is perfectly balanced which is their motto. 

The warm beet salad was my favorite salad by far. The beets, onions, cheese and lemon garlic vinaigrette all combined in a harmonious balance. 

I added their housemade bacon and sausage to the margherita pizza because my motto is, "no meat, no eat". At Pizza Gregario, they don't load their pizzas with massive amounts of cheese or sauce so as to mask the true ingredients of their pizza pies. They offer 9 inch and 13 inch pizza pies. The pizza is light and airy, but loaded with substance. You can also build your own pizza. 

I loved the Eh Mate pizza, and can I say, Good job Mate?! The arugula, sausage, candied nuts, fig balsamic and gorgonzola cheese looked and tasted amazing. It was like a yummy salad on pizza crust. 

Pizza Gregario has given me a reason to make the jaunt to downtown Safety Harbor more often. I will definitely need to come back and try their other pizza pies. The only negative is that I have to drive so far to get home with the intoxicating smell of yumminess in the car!

So good that I had to come back again with my parents! My parents are Asian so they don't eat non-Asian food often, but they gave this place two thumbs up. 

Don't let the nondescript exterior scare you. The interior has been totally renovated from how it used to look when Pao Cafe was here with a clean and inviting ambience. 

The menu is concise so you aren't overwhelmed with fillers. My eggs were cooked perfectly. The Shelly pancakes were light and fluffy so it doesn't give you that gross feeling after eating all that carbs. 

The omelettes legit remind me of home cooking. Full of flavor and tasty! 

Service was attentive and the manager came around to greet us to check to see how we liked our food. 

Not many places draws me out of my five mile radius, but you can count me as a regular now!

So. freaking. classy.

I kinda regretted not arriving in pearls and heels, because I love all things girly and they wouldn't have been out of place at Butcher and Singer! You could probably sit there and pretend that you're at a Downton Abbey type dinner party without stretching your imagination too far.

I came for restaurant week, and the impeccable service and ambiance just put me in a great mood. Honestly, it's probably the best deal I've ever had for restaurant week as well. 

The steak is obviously the only reasonable option for the main meal on the restaurant week menu (why would anyone get chicken here?!). So much yums, not just the steak but also the bread and dessert and sides (although I have to say the creamed spinach was the only so-so part of the meal). 

Would love to come again!
Great fine dining restaurant with exceptional specials, wine selection, and service.  You must try this place!

I've been a long time customer here. I used to be a cook at a restaurant too, but anyways I know that the owner doesn't like criticism whatsoever but this place is kinda shit; honestly the food is overpriced and mediocre, it's hyped a lot, yet it's not good quality food for the price. I mean the cooks there are shit. For example: one time I got a hamburger and the bottom and top bun were burned - literally black. Their buffalo fries aren't the best and I used to order that a lot. Sometimes the cheese would be melted (which is a good thing) other times i would get it cold. I don't understand how they could send the food out when the quality of it is awful, it's a huge hit or miss with several food items. I ordered the fried rice and it was very salty; how could you possibly mess that up? The burgers aren't so good just go to In N Out if you want a burger. i've gotten their quesadilla and it was nasty, it was super greasy too. I just wish for the price of the food the quality would be better but it's so shit. I've tried to give this place a lot of chances but it's honestly not worth the price. I've been disappointed more often than satisfied with the food here, and if the owner reading this please get new cooks or train them better or make better quality food for the price it's at, seriously.

The bartenders and servers are great at James Joyce and so is the food. We visited this place at least four times a month and almost every time we come to Ybor. 

The negatives are the horrible management who has no problem being completely disrespectful and disgusting to people on their Facebook page. There was an incident where this happened in the past over a bicycle and we didn't pay much attention to it. After losing a local competition on Sunday, Ryan (the owner) was posting on the FB page was out of control as they proceeded to call children mongoloids, people rednecks, mother f**ckers, c*ck suckers, and hicks. He told a guy (the respective redneck) that he among other things he would "...headbutt your f'ing teeth out of the back your f'ing skull mother f'er and butt f*ck your mother..." 

After reading these things, I posted the following comment on their page: "We go to James Joyce often, but if we were to judge your place by the way you are representing your company on this post, we would never consider going there at all. So unprofessional. I hope this post doesn't turn people off as you have a great establishment and usually a welcoming atmosphere."  I thought that was a respectful comment. To which I was told: to go f$ck myself, piss off, eat sh*t, "hope you get ebola and your kids catch cat aids", that I was a self righteous tw*t, a f*cking c#nt, and that I was a self righteous f'ing c$nt burger.   

He also said to "Post this on yelp. Screen freeze it. and while you are at it, f*ck yelp those extortionist f#ckheads that extort small businesses."

All comments were saved and are posted here as of this posting. Whether yelp allows them to stay is yet to be seen as they are extremely vulgar.

On Monday they claimed that their page was hacked, they shut down their reviews on FB, and deleted and blocked anyone who disagreed with them. There's a pattern of bad owner behavior here and it's obvious the page wasn't hacked. If it was, why didn't the employees who were commenting on the post mention it?

Place sucks. Charged me for crap I didn't even order. Even had the audacity to tell me I did eat it, 5 mins later told me "you're right" after realizing who's at fault.
Never will I return. Wish I had left a 20 cent tip

Tonight was my first disappointment with Arizona Pizza Company. Tonight I ordered the Meatball Sub and was very disappointed. I ordered this last week and it was superb. a good blend of the meatballs, red sauce, onions, peppers and cheese. Tonight I basically got dry meatballs with cheese between two pieces of bread. Did you run out of sauce, onions and pepper????  Sandwich was very dry. It may  be awhile before I try again.

I've probably waited too long to write this review nevertheless...I attended McGillin's on a Sunday night in February. I was taking a girl out for the second time with a group of her friends and I had another gentleman with me. The bar itself was very fun, vibrant, great beers, fun people etc. We sang Karaoke and had a stellar time.

The bill came it was 29.00 and some change so I offered to pay the tab. I handed the money to a waitress with long dark hair. I gave her 40.00 and handed her the small tab itself. I waited, I waited , I waited never got my change back. (I didn't want to make a big deal about an extra few dollars on a second time meeting a girl out.) So I let it go. No big deal. My friend and I were going to leave earlier than the girls so we kindly said our goodbyes forgot about the change... NO BIG DEAL?

About fifteen minutes later the girls call me from the bar asking me who I paid? I clearly specified the waitress I paid. The waitress comes on the phone, tells me she never received a payment...Then I get the night-shift manager on the phone she also advises me "My waitress is one of our best, she'd remember an 11.00 tip on a 29.00 order" etc Funny I spoke to the day manager, much more professional advised me the waitress was only working for two weeks.... I paid cash, horrendous mistake on my behalf. So with three girls thinking I left them with the tab, they REPAID the tab out of sheer humiliation (Not to consider the humiliation this place put me through to this point now anyway).

I knew I was right, I insisted to speak with the owner who refused to show me the camera (which was the giveaway) showing the transaction where I gave the waitress the money.. He neglected to show me the footage. He advised me he'd personally refund the girls their money and he gave me $11.00 back (my tip)... Mind you the loop I had to go through just to get that. Clearly the film would've showed me handing the money to the waitress, that is unless the cameras are as old as the bar is, which may be possible.

The night shift management expressed poor customer service skills. Foremost , the customer is always right, even when they are wrong and in this case I knew I was right. The waitress who was working at night who double charged the girls and myself honestly deserved to be barbecued over this, sorry Courtney or whatever your name is.

The owner could've handled it better. He WAS kind but far from genuine. I really really had a nice time at McGillin's but I'll never return to this establishment due to pathetic customer service and poor management.

This  surprising little gem of a place tucked away in a tiny strip mall on Lancaster Ave. has some of the best bread, pastas and salads I have ever had. Inside it is very cute, the man who owns it or runs it (not sure, he is always there though) is a real sweetheart and all the staff is friendly and nice.

Their bread is the absolute best, very crispy outside and soft inside; I've actually stopped in there late afternoon and bought a loaf to take home for a special dinner (they charged $6).  

I work close by and have gone here for lunch a couple of times and always been delighted with the food - they have the best ravioli, amazing salads (looove the goat cheese one) and great gnocchi too.  But here I will review the dinner I had last night.

I wish I had a camera to take a picture of the grilled vegetable platter we ordered as an appetizer - so pretty and colorful and beautifully arranged  - sweet red peppers, asparagus, zucchini, eggplant and tomatoes grilled to perfection so they were soft yet still firm.  I ate so much of that with bread dipped in olive oil that I took most of my entree home!

Their menu is huge - I think almost any pasta dish incarnation you can dream up will be on it.  It's very hard to decide and just sitting there sipping wine for a bit and watching the food come out of the kitchen didn't help, absolutely everything looked scrumptious!

Last night I had the "Tagliatelle ai Funghi Porcini" which was pasta with porcini mushrooms, garlic, cream and onions.  Oh my, if you like a deep mushroom taste try this, so good and the sauce was not thick or too heavy either. My dining partner had the chicken cacciatore which I tasted and though I would not order it, it was still very good made with boneless chicken breast with some yummy salty olives in the sauce.  

We split a slice of chocolate mousse cake for dessert and it was completely delicious, deep dark chocolate cake that was not sweet with a luscious rich chocolate mousse in between the layers and a lighter chocolate butter cream icing outside.   I teasingly asked the owner if he baked it and he said it was from Sweet Jazmines (a local bakery, which I now need to check out!).

It's BYOB so take a nice wine, the food deserves it.  The only negative is how small this place is.  With the exception of a few tables in private alcoves, it's mostly European type seating with lots of tables squished very close together so you are practically sharing a table with those around you.  Lunch it's very quiet there but at night it is hard to get a table, so call for a reservation.  This place is no where near my house but I would go out of my way to go back.  Maybe I should give it a four because of the seating but that doesn't really bother me so it's a five, just really excellent food and service.

The Burg is the absolute worst restaurant experience I've had in the past year. My boyfriend and I came in for lunch on the weekend and left with food poisoning and a disgusting aftertaste, with little to no apology for why.

When we finally received our food, my boyfriend commented that his burger was pink after he bit into it. What he showed me was a burger patty that looked half raw inside. We brought it up to our server, and he explained that it's because they use ground chuck, and it's okay if it's medium rare. Once he walked away, my boyfriend took a couple more tentative bites before I stopped him again. Finally, the server took the burger, got his manager, and they disappeared into the back for about 10 minutes. Eventually he came back out and explained that yes, the burger did look pink, and they informed the chef and removed the cost from our bill. My boyfriend had food poisoning for two days afterward. 

FYI for people who think burgers can be pink inside - the meat is covered in bacteria from being ground up. This bacteria needs to be cooked off. Any kid above the age of 8 knows this to be true.

If you have a burger restaurant NAMED after a burger, and you don't even know how to cook it properly, there's a problem. If you're not equipped to please an unsatisfied and poisoned customer, there's an even bigger problem. What made matters worse was that my (cooked) burger tasted worse than burgers at most fast food restaurants, and yet I paid triple the price. I was incredibly disappointed with The Burg, and caution anyone who visits them to be careful what they're biting into, and take a look to make sure it's even cooked properly. There are many other burger places to go to in the 104th area (The Blue Plate Diner has amazing bison burgers that put The Burg to shame), and I suggest going to them instead.

Oh yea, and the onion rings were disgusting and dry.

I give this restaurant three stars because it's not quite where it is going to be in a month or two.  Very nice set up with family style seating and a bar area with a stage.  The bartender is on point with the cocktails. I had the strawberry field while my date had the blublack jack. BOTH WERE OUTSTANDING!!  For an appetizer, we had the pickle flight with the peppers, sting beans, crazy carrots and pickles.  All four were good but the sting beans (yes, it's "sting" and not "string") stood out to me.  Very tasty dill flavored appetizers.  For the main dish I ordered the meatloaf with snap beans and bacon mac and cheese. The meatloaf was not meat...or mainly meat for that matter. I think they used stuffing mix or something.  The mac and cheese was just ok. The snap beans were just ok as well.  My meal was just ok.  My date ordered the catfish with Brussels sprouts and the cheese grits. She kinda liked the catfish but she's not really a big seafood person. She said the Brussels sprouts were not that good at all.  The cheese grits, however, were tasty.  The biscuits were pretty big and pretty good.  The service was fast and courteous.  This place will BOOM within the next few months, mark my words.  It reminds me of a Whiskey Kitchen but they're brand new so I know they will improve and blow Whiskey Kitchen out of the water.  I can see this place growing into a consistent 4-4.5 star place....wait til summer gets here.

You gotta have the word "sucker" written across your forehead to show up at PYT. Remember the time Bush screwed up the "throw me once, shame on you, throw me twice, shame on me" line in a speech? Well, PYT managed to throw me twice. Shame on them. Or wait, is it shame on me? Thanks Dubya. 

Either way, PYT's service stinks like a dead skunk in the middle of a country road. It's shame-full. We ordered two burgers for take out last fall when they opened. They told me to come pick them up in 20 minutes. I arrived in 20 minutes and had to wait another 20. Then I returned home to enjoy an average-at-best burger which featured future indigestion and heartburn. 

The second time we walked in on a weekday evening. The place wasn't really crowded, but we stood in the doorway for a good ten minutes before being seated. Another five minutes went by and some staffer came over with glasses of water. He informed us that he had no menus to give us and would be back "soon." Ten minutes went by without seeing a server, a menu, or even the offer of a cocktail. We got up and walked out and were not even asked if anything was wrong when we went past a cadre of employees. 

The final result was dinner at El Camino on N. 2nd Street. They at least seem to give a damn about their customers! Perhaps they ought to change their name to PDT. Pretty Disappointing Time.

Bar Lucca is a three-dollar sign ($$$) experience with two-dollar signs ($$). Sweet ambiance, exceptional service, yummy food and drinks equals an overall delightful experience. What more could a girl ask for? The atmosphere is simply lovely - cozy, romantic and idealistic for a wine & pizza night with the gals or date night with the S.O. Our server was a sweetheart and made us feel welcome, didn't rush us (even though it was busy - I'd recommend making reservations!), answered all my random questions, and was exceptionally personable! 

3 things that made my tastebuds remarkably happy: 

* Affogato Doppio, the fresh brewed espresso poured over your choice of gelato, my-oh-my where have you been all my life!! This is a MUST HAVE - coffee and dessert - HEAVEN SENT. Yes, yes, I know the dessert menu has some pretty mouthwatering options and I too struggled between choosing this or a Nutella dessert, but this was perfect I tell you. The only gelato option that really stood out to me was the pistachio, which sounded weird with the gelato so our server said she won't pour the espresso on top so we can experiment first. AMAZING. Do not knock it until you try it. One of the simplest, yet best desserts I've had in my life. 

* The caramelized onions. We asked for onions on our Neapolitan Style Pizza and immediately upon the server placing the pie on the table, the aromas of the onions made us salivate. They were so flavorful and together with the buffalo mozzarella - bomb dot com! 

* Pizza comes with a side of FRESH OREGANO. I don't know why more restaurants don't do this. It added so much flavor and character to our already tasty margherita pie.

How did Pietro's wake up? Flawlesssss! 

Pietro's is a staple of Philadelphia. While living in Philadelphia, I frequented the Rittenhouse Square location, but this was my first time here. Everything (food, drinks, ambiance) was nothing short of extraordinary. 

The Margarita Pizza was delicious with luscious sauce tomato sauce - totally drinkable. I'm typically not a pasta person, but hands down, BEST. PASTA. EVER = Rigatoni ala Vodka. The pasta was cooked to perfection and the sauce was creamy and scrumptious. I took seconds. And thirds. Could've gone for fourths. Also, I hate tiramisu, but their homemade tiramisu was one of the best desserts I've had in my life. It was flawless. I took seconds of this too... 

Mind you, I came here for an engagement party (private dining upstairs!) and the food was made catering style for 40+ people. If the chef can perfect food for that many people, major kudos to them! 

Being that I'm not in Philly that often anymore, I always want to try new spots when I'm there, but I legit have been craving Pietro's since I stepped foot out of that restaurant. Looking forward to coming back here on my next visit!

To be honest, I was quite skeptical about going to a "chain" restaurant, but after seeing White Truffle Garlic Bread on the appetizer menu - I was sold. North Italia exceeded my expectations to say the least. Everything from the food to the service to the ambiance was exquisite. Believe the great reviews and the mouthwatering photos - the hype is real, Yelpers. One small piece of advice, get a side of red sauce. I'm so picky and judgey when it comes to sauce, but I'd have to say I was blown away by the highly flavorful marinara... I could've drank it. As reluctant as I am going to chains, I'd frequent here if I lived closers (corporate, if you're reading this, please open one in Central NJ!)
Food porn realist at its best! Take my advice and try the Seafood Paella or any martini to wash the spices down.

Hands down worst customer service I have ever received anywhere in the world. 

We arrived with our service dog, as we do in restaurants across the state. The 'manager-partner' was very argumentative and confrontational about our service dog. He then forced us to leave - begging us to 'sue him or take him to court.' It was very uncalled for, we were very patient and polite and he was absolutely livid. It is against the law to prohibit a registered service animal from an establishment - these guys will be hearing from us shortly.

It goes without saying that we will be taking our business elsewhere. There are plenty of deserving business owners with friendly establishments that we will happily dine with instead.

Good food, horrible service.

Management, you've got a problem. I've been here twice and both times I walked out frustrated with the service.

The first time I walked in, I was the only one in the restaurant and the three employees behind the counter were glued to the cell phones, no greeting. Finally, after asking if I could place an order, and only after they were done with Facebook, I received a "yeahh?"

I asked if she could recommend something for a first-timer and she responded, "Um, yeah, I don't really eat here." Silence. 

Really? Then lie to me, but don't make me feel like I'm eating at a place that the employees dare not touch.

While one person prepared my food, the other two continued on their phones. Finally, after the food was made, she looked for the fries, which still hadn't been dropped yet (apparently the fry cook was conducting important business on his phone and couldn't be bothered to pay attention).

As everyone behind the counter stood around, the line was building behind. One couple snickered, "let's go next door to Anthony's so that we can eat today."

I could go on and on.

I figured I might have been there on an off day with new employees. I went back today, to my absolute regret. 

I dare anyone to go in there and walk out without feeling like the employees are doing you a favor just by doing their jobs.

Management, you have decent food. However, you are doing a horrible job training your employees and setting standards. Read through your reviews, people are largely happy with your food but the service is dismal and the employees incompetent. For whatever reason, the three other restaurants in your building have been able to hire competent people, so the common denominator is you. 

My recommendation, until management gets its act together, is to go next door to the Jimmy Johns or Anthony's where the employees are happy to serve you. You're much more likely to get a simple, "thank you" over there than you are at Naf Naf.

Noble is super pretty. I love the bar that looks like a tree, the glass, the skylights, the painted brick, the half-finished frames. Thankfully, the food and drinks live up to the ambience.

I'm going to add Noble's bar into my regular rotation. They have an interesting, mostly local beer list, and the wine list was clearly put together by someone who cares. The short list of cocktails is creative and unique, and the ones I tried (something with lemon and birch beer, another with tequila and apple cider) were refreshing, delicious, and not too sweet. Also, the bartender is friendly, made great suggestions, and has an exceptional moustache.

Time to eat. I ordered the baby romaine to start, which is a very nice salad. The asparagus with herbs and a fried egg was fantastic, and breaking the egg and watching the yolk flow out over the asparagus...divine. Chickpea fries are strange and good, and my friend praised his foie gras app (I shake my fist). The cheese plate included something mild, a strong, tasty blue, and the sharpest cheese I have ever eaten.

There's a veggie burger on the bar menu. It comes on a big fluffy buttery roll, dressed up with a slice of beet, and crispy sea salty fries and tiny little pickles, and it is good. However, our waiter suggested the vegetarian specials. I got a sweet onion rice pudding with a green pea sauce and carrots, fava beans and perfectly cooked chanterelles - fantastic. Friends said the fish (we had halibut and striped bass at the table) was notably good. 

Finished up with sorbets (the cucumber, I wish I could eat that 3 times a day in the summer!), carrot cake (moist, fluffy and spiced just right) and the chocolate peanut butter thing. You know what's even more appealing than cracking a fried egg? Cracking a chocolate cake and watching peanut butter ooze out. Damn. The peanut butter marshmallow on the side is lovely and made with agar agar instead of gelatin.

I will be back, for a quick drink in a nice place, or for a noteworthy meal.

Happy Rooster is like a friend you don't see too often. You get together, and you're thinking "Man, this is great. Why don't we hang out more??" By the end of the night, though, you remember exactly why you never call this person first.

Cozy and dark, with roosters all over and big, comfy booths that encourage conversation, I like the space here. The bartender and wait staff are friendly and accommodating and just a pleasure to be around. This has the makings of a great bar, except that, unfortunately, there isn't a whole lot to drink.

Clearly the Happy Rooster isn't focusing on beer, but a list with Chimay Red and Boddington's as the best options just doesn't cut it in Philadelphia - it is not a good thing when the jacked up deli on the corner has a more interesting, less expensive beer selection than your bar. I usually opt for a glass of wine here, and that list, too, seems a little limited and a little pricey. 

That goes for the bar menu as well. An order of fries, at $7, could have used another minute or two in the fryer and some salt. We also tried the mozzarella with tomato and roasted pepper, which was a disaster of a snack. The mozzarella puck earned itself two comparisons to shoes (my friend said leather, but I was thinking more along the lines of a rubbery sole, myself), the tomato sauce was sadly lacking in verve, and the two shreds of pepper on top just made the whole thing a little more pitiable. This was difficult to eat and the opposite of delicious, but the kindly bartender told us they had just changed the dish, so hopefully it's only temporary.

Happy Rooster has a lot going for it, but in a city where you can't spit without hitting a top-notch drinking establishment (and believe me, I've tried), it's not quite up to par.

I see that it's been some time since I've raved about Tria. It's still perfect! I go here about twice as often as I go to every other bar in Philadelphia combined. Here are some things that make Tria the best: 

-There isn't a bad item on the menu. Every once in awhile I'll order something that isn't to my taste, but you could randomize the menu via computer, order whatever drinks, cheeses and snacks come up first, and be completely assured that you will have a high-quality, lovely meal.

-The staff is so great: knowledgeable and nice and willing to listen to your preferences and suggest just exactly the right thing. Sometimes they suggest just exactly the right thing with nary a clue from you at all; it's kind of uncanny.

-Deals! On weekdays at happy hour time, they offer a selection of menu items (usually a red wine, a white, a cheese and two different beers) for $5 each. All day on Sunday, there's a wine, a beer and a cheese for half price. I trust Tria a lot, so I usually just get whatever's on special without thinking twice - you can try all kinds of delicious, well-chosen stuff for a pittance.

-The rewards card. On the plus side, you get gift cards after you spend a certain amount, as well as prizes for trying x different wines, beers and cheeses. The minus is that every time you use the card, you can see a lifetime running total of how much you've spent at Tria, and the number can be downright staggering. Don't you think, though, that drinking and eating really well is easily as responsible a way to spend hard-earned cash as, say, paying down student loans? Yeah, me too.

Tria's top-shelf menu would be enough to bring me there frequently at full price, but when you factor in the top-shelf service and discounts, it's hard to justify going anyplace else.

Recently, a friend and I planned a brunch for another friend who was about to get married. Our requirements were pretty straightforward: an at-least-halfway-cute space for a group of about 20, a menu that could accommodate vegetarians as well as Atkins followers, and booze, preferably available in a variety of tasty cocktails. 

We called approximately 1.7 billion restaurants serving brunch in Center City, and got a lot of "Sure, but we'll have to...seat you in 4 different rooms/charge everyone a minimum/do it on this other random date/etc." I understand why restaurants place such restrictions, but we got none of that from Devil's Alley - they were super accommodating, friendly and easy to deal with. 

We hosted the brunch in the back of their upstairs area, which is nice and open and has a fire pit, and we had our own server who made sure everything ran relatively smoothly. The Bloody Marys and French toast flowed, and everyone was happy.

If Farmicia were a book and I judged it by the cover, this would be a 5-star review. With a delectable menu, tons of options for herbivores, a focus on fresh and local and a long list of herbed-up drinks, this place should knock my socks off. While Farmicia does a lot of things right, somehow I feel that it doesn't quite deliver.

During a recent brunch, I was impressed by the thoughtful, friendly service, even though the restaurant was packed to the gills. I also appreciated the fact that I could hear and converse with my friends amongst all the chatter, and they were playing some low-intensity female-singer indie music (Lykke Li, Feist, et al.), which seems exactly right for brunch. The "brunch happy hour" is a fantastic idea, and the brunch menu is wide-ranging and appetite-inducing. 

Unfortunately, things looked less bright when the food and drinks started arriving. My Bloody Mary was watery (although it had a healthy horseradish kick), and my overwhelming impression of the food was that I could've cooked it myself and it probably would've come out better. Breakfast potatoes were completely lacking in seasoning, a side of veggie sausage came out burnt on the outside and lukewarm on the inside, the vegan scramble with soyrizo was plain chunks of tofu mixed with the fake sausage you get at Trader Joe's, and while I admit to being particular about my grits, Farmicia's cheddar ones had zero cheesy flavor. 

I think this shows that fresh, local ingredients can only get you so far - they still need to be treated right to make for a good meal.

One of my coworkers has taken on the title of Happy Hour Coordinator (doesn't every office have one of these?), a position of little lucre but great utility for the rest of us. After many long hours researching in the field, his diligence lead us to crown Valanni our Office Happy Hour Spot. Valanni is dead, long live Valanni. 

With half priced drinks and apps, a big, square bar and cozy little tables in nooks nearby, this is an accommodating place for a gaggle of people. They make a mean mojito, with lots of mint and aesthetically pleasing rock candy. When it's cold, I often opt for the frequently-changing seasonal stout (Bell's Expedition and Dogfish Head Chicory, for representative examples). My favorite embarrassingly-named cocktail looks like a trainwreck with three ingredients too many on the menu page, but with a splash of balsamic vinegar to cut its sweetness, it's different and delightful.

The patatas bravas and other bar snacks are a cut above your typical happy hour fare, and the lobster mac n cheese makes my colleagues rave. At a catered party in the back room (which is a nice spot for a party), Valanni really showed its stuff, with an extensive Mediterranean-inflected selection of hors d'oeuvres, plated in single bites on spoons and presented alluringly on a tall rack. Everything I tasted - hummus, white beans with pesto, vegan flatbread, cucumber salad and especially this one feta dip - was well-executed, and I appreciated the balance of vegetarian and dead animal options.

Service here tends to be either exemplary or execrable, and occasionally, that can result in a truly abominable drink. I recommend having your Happy Hour Coordinator spend some time getting to know the bartenders, who now start muddling and mixing as soon as they see our guy walk through the door.

You can tell that whoever is behind Matyson really cares about finding, cooking and serving top-notch ingredients in a creative and delicious way. Everything I've eaten here speaks to the chef's deep passion for food and attention to detail - the cooking is flawless.

Vegetarians might be put off by the lack of options on the menu, but at Matyson, it's almost an advantage because they will cook something just for you and it will be awesome. On a slow night, they've asked me what I felt like eating, and the chef made something based on that - exceptional service. Also, if you're out with a few veggies, they make something different for each person, which is thoughtful and appreciated. 

I wish they weren't on the wrong side of the foie gras debate, but that is the only thing I'd change about Matyson. It's fantastic.

Super disappointed in this experience. I wanted to love it so much. It was a total fail.

Went there for brunch on my mother's birthday. We had reserved the smaller of the two private rooms, as we had about 20 people coming. Upon arrival, no record of our reservation existed. Apparently the banquet manager had left (for the day? for good? no idea) without putting it in the book. Reservation was made weeks in advance and re-confirmed by us days before. 

They were able to install us in the private room anyway since it was not double-booked, so that was ok, but they clearly were not prepared for us- not just in terms of set up but in terms of wait staff. We had a 'primary' server, but would not see her for lengthy stretches of time. Took ages to get drinks.

The biggest issue was that three of our party (including yours truly) are on gluten free diets. We reminded the host and wait staff of this multiple times during our visit, including when we ordered. Of the three of us, two of us were served regular old gluten filled versions of our order. My daughter noticed (prior to eating) that her french toast looked remarkably similar to her (non GF) brother's french toast, so we asked the server, who seemed irritated and said "I trust the chef". I pointed out the similarity in the dishes and explained that it is extremely unusual for gluten free bread to look so similar to gluten bread, and asked her to please CONFIRM with the chef. Meanwhile, my daughter and I shared my (assumed to be) gluten free breakfast. 

About five minutes later, server returns to inform us that neither of us had been served gluten free due to a 'communication error' between server and chef. Brief apology and ten minutes later we had the correct food. Unfortunately, I had already eaten about half of the non-GF food they had originally served. Within 20 minutes I was throwing up in their bathroom, and my entire day (week, really) was ruined. 

Apology from manager? Chef? Any response when I told server I was inevitably going to be very ill? NO. Any removal of charges from the bill? No. 

I did not pay for this meal- my dad did- but if I had not been puking at the time the bill came, I would have brought it up. As it was, I didn't want to ruin my mother's birthday, but COME ON. If you are going to perform a big song and dance about how GF friendly you are, then TAKE IT SERIOUSLY. It is not a fad diet for me or my family. It causes tremendous pain and illness. I will never go there again, and I would not recommend this place to anyone who needs to follow a gluten free diet. 

Prasino, if you are listening, just take it off your menu, and do the people with Celiac a favor.

I ordered, based on the online menu, a gluten-free asparagus pizza to go. Advertised asparagus pizza was 12" with asparagus, artichoke, pine nuts, fresh arugula, fontina, and balsamic reduction. What I received was an 8" pizza with asparagus, artichoke, pine nuts and what may or may not have been fontina. And I paid $5 for the gluten-free crust, which they don't make there, and is smaller than the regular pizza. 

While the 30% upcharge is noted on the menu, the 30% smaller pizza is not. When called out on the lack of toppings, I was told that the online menu must not be updated, as they now make the asparagus pizza differently. Was also informed, in a very perky voice, that yes, there is an upcharge for gluten-free and yes, it is smaller. "Sorry you were not informed of that when you called." Me too! 

The final straw was that the pizza was burnt. Burnt enough that over an inch of crust was not edible, making this effectively a $23, 6" pizza. Husband is returning it as I write this, in order to get our money back. They offered us a gift card, which we declined, as I never intend to return. Kind of offended to even have to return this dinky thing in the first place.

I really, really wanted to love Katie's. Too bad they feel that taking advantage of the gluten-free community is ok. With three GF people in my household, I sing the praises of places that accommodate us well. Unfortunately, I'll be telling a different story for Katie's.

When in Nashville I had one food mission.... get some Hot Chicken!  Party Foul was highly recommended by a lot of locals, so a bunch of us tried it out. It was busy but our group got a table right away. Our group had a lot of questions about the drinks (boozy slushies) and what the best food was. The server was awesome, she explained everything. From the different types of spice levels on the chicken...mild, medium, Nashville Hot and  Poultrgyeist. I went with the mild Hot chicken -1/2 bird with cole slaw, texas toast and pickles. I was so glad I choose mild, amazing flavor not a lot of heat! I did try some of the other flavors from my coworkers, med was really good but to hot for me. A few people got the hot and lets just say it brought tears to their eyes.

Lot's of drink choices but I wanted a nice cold beer to go with my hot chicken. I had a good people Ipa- very tasty and a pale ale- lighter but smooth. I did have a taste of the BOURBON BANANA BANSHEE- this is one of their boozy slushies...damn this was really good like a piña colada to the extreme!

Came here with a large group of people, we had reservations but this place was so empty we really didn't need them.   Since I haven't been to many Greek restaurants I leaned on my group to make decisions on what we should order.....   First of we went with their famous Estia Chips,  thinly sliced zucchini and eggplant that are lightly fried and served with tzatziki....these are so freaking good! We devoured these so fast we had to order a second set.  We also had the cheese saganaki,l pan fried Kefalograviera cheese, served with lemon.  Iv'e had this in other places where it is served and then they put the flames out and its amazing.... here it's served on fire but you decided when to put the flame out.... and our group was unsure when to put the flame out. It was still good but I have had better. Our group also enjoyed the calamari and mussels.

For dinner I ordered the Thursday Special GRILLED SCALLOPS ....Jumbo sea scallops grilled with lemon and olive oil with fresh citrus and roasted zucchini. But unfortunately after I ordered our server came back out to inform me they were all out...... I was disappointed because it was only 5:50pm and they were all ready sold out :(  So I  went with the Organic Chicken a roasted leg and breast served over caramelized onion .... the breast was good. but I wouldn't order it again. 

I would come back, hopefully they have more daily specials. Otherwise I'll just go with appetizers and drinks.

A trip to St.Louis would not be complete without a visit to the Budweiser Brewery... right? We walked in and joined the next available tour, the Day Fresh Tour. We sat down and waited the few minutes until the tour started.

The Day Fresh Tour is the the journey of a beer from seed to sip.We started out seeing the Budweiser Clydesdale Paddock and Stables.. great photo opportunity here! Just wish they had a Clydesdale out for us to pet. Next was the Beechwood Aging Cellar(love the smell here) the historic Brewhouse was very interesting and the BEVO Packaging Facility. So many different beers being packaged..very cool.  Had a few samples on tour and  also got to will take home a day-fresh(about 12 hours old) bottle of beer! Lot's of interesting information and history, loved seeing all the memorabilia on the walls and in cabinets. 

After the tour you get one pint of beer to enjoy on site. A few comfy chairs and couches inside or grab a spot outside. There is a gift shop onsite, lot's of different items. I got a shirt on sale for $12. 

Tour was about  75 minutes and tickets were $10. I'm glad we checked this place out and did a tour. I think you do it once and your good.

Everything has gone downhill at this casino. My husband and I visited Harrah's Philadelphia at 11PM last night. By the time we left (@ 4 hours later) I noticed:

-the slots are tighter than ever
-the only eating establishment that was open is terrible
-we couldn't get water or ice at the "free" beverage dispenser on the casino floor
-there needs to be security present in the ATM areas, I felt very unsafe when two strangers approached me as I withdrew cash
-the "C" bar/lounge isn't even open when you want to relax and get a drink (yes if I'm handing you $$$$ at 3AM I should be able to go to an open lounge!!)
-we got no free play/comps whatsoever even though we played (and lost) nearly  $1000 here on our last visit 3 weeks ago
-a casino experience cannot be this horrible if they want customers to return

My husband and I both agreed:
-The lack of quality food options, a bar that's open, security placed where needed, and low % payout on any slot machines we played are very real problems.
-This casino won't stay in business much longer if they don't improve conditions.
-We have no desire to come back here anymore.

Soy café makes me wish I were a "NoLibber" (I'm not quite sure if anyone actually uses that term but, whatever).

Anyway, Soy is everything you could ever want in a café venue:
(a) Delicious & unique specialty beverages (smoothies, teas, coffees - made to order with their homemade soy milk, of course. I particularly enjoyed their Soy Chai and Cocoaberry smoothie - cocoa, bananas, raspberries, oatmeal, soymilk & honey)
(b) Fresh, healthy dishes and snacks including a wide variety of vegan options (that grilled eggplant wrap, just...wow. PLUS it's surprisingly filling)
(c) Plentiful seating (including a cute little outdoor patio area in the back)
(d) Quiet, relaxing atmosphere aided in part by the lime green and bright purple color accents
(e) Various magazines & newspapers to peruse to your heart's content
(f) Service with a smile

Despite its admirability, I must share a few words of caution:
-They are cash only, but have an atm
-They are slow - definitely not a "grab and go" type place unless you are just getting a coffee or a counter-sitting baked good. Everything's made to order - aka you WILL in fact witness the peeling of the carrots on your wrap. This could be quite agonizing if you are in a rush. I warned you.
