The best stop in West Philly....especially if you live or are staying within walking distance of Mr. Lee's then this is your best bet for an interesting crowd and a no-nonsense breakfast to get your Philly day started right.

underwhelmed. 

right to it. 

walked in on a monday night. seated right away.

service was surprisingly good. i wouldnt say tfl good, but fine dining in reno... it was just fine...actually great. our waiters were great. 

the decor? pleasantly surprised again. as a tourist in reno, this a very welcomed change. as a contractor, well, not bad.

now the important part.

seared foie gras. a slimy pasty mess. bad.

salad. well salad, sides and asparagus were good... 

but the steak? well, my kansas city ribeye, aka cowboy aka bone in ribeye was cooked very well, but it just was lacking in flavor. i liked the different sauces accompanying the steak, but come on, steak at this level, you shouldnt need sauces to make your steak taste good. 

ive had my fair share of steaks from all sorts of places. i am not one to shy away from any type of steak houses from the most high end to the tuesday night random dinner. this steak at charlie palmer steak in reno nevada was a bit lacking. 

call it a bit gimmicky but i liked the french onion soup. though it was lacking a bit in body, the puff pastry cover was fun and a nice change for me. 

the complimentary small bite dessert was a very nice touch.

would i got back? probably. its a very nice venue. its inside what i would consider to be my new go to hotel in reno. maybe this is a very unfair first try review. maybe i had way too high expectations for my first charlie palmer experience.... but yeah. i will try it again probably, just no big rush.

This theater is located in the rundown, slowly decaying University Mall and it definitely lives up to the attributes of them mall.
Once inside you will notice that most things are old and not well kept. The place was pretty dirty; for example, I ordered a drink but did not use the cup holder because of all the gunk that was built up in there.
During my first visit, I ordered popcorn with no butter. When my order comes out it is quite obvious that there's butter on the popcorn. When I requested no butter, the waiter made it seem as if it was such an ordeal, so I just ate the popcorn because it seemed to me that they were unable to provide unbuttered popcorn. About 10 minutes later, another  server comes out with the unbuttered popcorn that I ordered.
My second visit was on Monday, which is when they have a $5 special on margaritas. Both my friends and I ordered the margaritas before the movie started. As soon as we put in our order the waiter charged us for the drinks. I also must note that the theater adds gratitude (tip) to every order regardless of the amount. After the drinks arrived one of my friends ordered a salad. About 30 minutes into the movie the salad had not arrived; she buzzed the waiter to question what was going on and all the waiter said is 'I'll go check on it.' Over an hour into the movie, she hadn't received her salad or an update. She buzzed the waiter again, they had no word on what had happened to the salad, so she just went ahead and canceled her order. When the movie was almost done, right at the climax of the film, we had a waiter come out and start explaining to me how the charge that they did at the beginning of the movie, for one of my friends and I, did not go through. Literally during the climax of the movie! If you make a mistake, please explain to me why I should be punished by having you rudely interrupt a movie that I paid to see? And the conversation was not just interrupting me it was disturbing the other viewers in the theater. Honestly I was livid and shocked. I politely asked him if we could address the issue after the movie. I don't know what he was talking about, we received a receipt saying that our cards were charged and there was a charge when I checked my bank account.

Needless to say, I do not recommend visiting this establishment. Maybe other chain locations have good service and etc but all I can say is that this one does not.

This place has just newly opened and I have already been twice. That is saying a lot for me but then again, I love buns! 
Sweet Buns is like your typical Chinese bakery; you have the buns, cakes in the cold case and other pre-packaged sweets (they also have warm food and drinks, but I never look in their direction).  One of the things I appreciate about this establishment is that they do no have the large amount of options that most Chinese bakery do; which makes it easier to choose. What makes a Chinese bun so great is the nice yeasty, perfectly sweet bread and the shiny of the bun that adds to the taste of the bread. And this bakery delivers good Chinese buns. I have had the Honey BBQ pork bun, Coconut Peanut cookie, Ham Cheese and Onion bun and Blueberry Cheese bun. The two savory options were by far my favorite, which is surprising because I am not a fan of ham. The cookie, which was not really a cookie but a flakey pastry shaped like a cookie, was a miss for me (not awful, just not good). The Blueberry Cheese bun had the makings of a good bun on the outside but the filling I didn't care for; it had a wierd texture and the favor wasn't great. 
As for the space itself, it was well lit, clean and roomie enough for people to sit down and eat.

I have yet to find my 'sweet bun' at this establishment, so I will definitely be back and highly recommend that anyone else head over as well.

Amazing crabs! These are the best tasting crabs that I have ever tasted. I got #1 combo with the Hot N Crazy Crab "mild" sauce. It was amazing and I couldn't even finish my meal. 

The restaurant was clean and the staff are friendly and welcoming. Ask for Harrell as a waiter. It has only been opened for three days. They just opened on 7/16/19 and are already getting great business. 

So now there are three major crab restaurants in Brandon- ( Crafty Crab, Mr. & Mrs. Crab and Hot N Crazy) and I can tell you that I have tried them all & this one is the best. Let me know what y'all think!

(Dined 02/25/15 W @ 1:00pm): Settle in, kick off your flip-flops, dip your toes into the soft sand, and enjoy the scenery because you won't want to leave!

Thank goodness one of my friends along on this overnight trip to the Chumash Casino recommended Padaro Beach Grill as our first stop on our way up California's Gold Coast. The vibe alone sold me, but how was the grub!?:

Chocolate Caramel Handmade Shakes ($4.75) - Nearly a "$5 shake", this truly hit the spot in Southern California's warm winter weather. Not as thick as Jack-In-The-Box so my lungs were intact, this was a wonderful mixture of really good chocolate ice cream dolloped with a cloud of whipped cream all poured-over by sticky sweet caramel. Honestly, this would've sufficed as a meal, but I was eager to explore the food menu. The only "negative" was that you didn't receive a little extra shake in a mixing cannister like some places. But this was damn good! http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=RX6qdpO3DOH4Z1USJMkTRg

[ONION RINGS/STRAWS/STRINGS ALERT - 4.0 of 5 STARS]
The Trio ($5.95) - A bountiful basket filled with French fries, onion rings, and sweet potato fries with a collection of BBQ, catsup, and ranch dipping sauces, this also could've been a meal in itself for one. The French fries were crispy, slightly seasoned and skiny; I liked them. The sweet potato fries were more crunchy on the outside but moist and sweet on the inside; I LOVED sweet potato fries and these didn't disappoint (no sauce needed). You only received a few lovely dark golden brown and extra crunchy medium-sized onion rings which had plenty of extra "nubs" to chew on. The onion stayed intact when you bit into it and didn't pull out from its batter casing. I loved these but only wished you got more in this sampler. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=elJv_ZWjaTt237mrmdIq6g

Baja Shrimp Po' Boy ($9.50) - A two-hander for sure, this was filled with large pieces of crispy Cajun shrimp throughout, house made coleslaw, lettuce, Thousand Island dressing and chipotle mayo served on a toasted French roll. Oh boy, this was no shrimpy sandwich with its burst of flavors and finger-licking goodness! Multiple napkins needed. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=biMo9-Sdib2u9k--JXyw3A

Service - An "order-at-the-counter-and-take-your-number" kind of place http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=rqWaapJwF687nwmawzgJUw, we placed our orders, received our order numbers and drink cups, paid, found a table outside, and our numbers were called about ten minutes later. Once we were done, we threw our trash away (didn't appear to have any wait service but plenty of trash cans). All was easy-peasy with no hiccups. 

Parking (Free) - They shared a small elongated strip of private parking with a number of other businesses along a stretch of beach, so parking could be rough. Otherwise, distant street parking might be avialable. 

Atmosphere, décor, ambience - A casual beach shack along the Amtrak railway line and the beach in Santa Barbara http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=PKMgHmcMa3qEg-L2FbK3Bw with Adirondack chairs on the porch http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=Lt1uyS_7nbvfdBabLupKzQ, inside dining was at a minimum with a couple tables for four. However, it was all about the outside patio picnic bench and table dining area as you gazed out to the ocean and watched the train as they went by. There was even a sandlot for the kiddies http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=pcoKQePJRQFshFbH04scrg. Minimal decorations and pictures hung from the walls all with a beach theme. A chalk-written colorful menu was placed directly above the order counter. Natural lighting was everywhere while some electric track lighting was used (but why!?). There were a couple TVs while music played in the background http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?userid=8jVT2inwc8GIQ6sH2UG9Vw&select=J8cjAfcPJNN4OiBS3cyU2A.

Attire - Totally casual, so I would normally be in a t-shirt, boardshorts, and flip-flops.

Overall, I completely enjoyed Padaro Beach Grill with its amazing food, wonderful prices, and outstanding view (location...location...location). Maybe the beach bum in me was swept away by the scenery (it kind of was!), but this place truly had the whole package. The menu was simple, healthy, and offered that casual SoCal vibe. Although I didn't order any alcohol, their beer and wine selection may've been limited but the prices were standard to below-standard. Yeah, I'd definitely return next time I was in the area. I found total value based on the prices, service, and experience noted above (total bill was around $22.00 before tip). And, they accepted my credit card of choice...AMEX! 5.0 STARS

What can I say Pappy's sets the tone for St Louis Barbecue. It can come off as a tourist attraction/stop but they have been able to maintain "the local's" expectation! It's because they do it right and they've nailed it every time I've visited. This visit I got the ribs and brisket combo and it was amazing. The ribs were tender and fell off the bone with just right amount of meat, charcoal/smoke, and heat. The brisket was s also very tender and I didn't need any sauce. The long line can be intimidating at first glance but the service was quick and efficient. They've really mapped out and applied all of what the Covid pandemic requires to keep customers as safe as possible. The restaurant was very clean and the service was  extremely friendly. I can't tell you how many employees walked over to our table to ensure the food and service was meeting our expectations!

Best BBQ in StL HANDS DOWN! You can't go wrong with absolutely NOTHING HERE! I go to are their brisket, burnt ends, and smoked turkey. It's very rare you find a BBQ place where both meat and sides are equally good. This place nails both! Enjoy!

My initial expectation of Polite Society was extremely high. I can honestly say not only did this restaurant meet all my expectations but after many visits it continues to surpass them. I swear this place gets better and better which each visit. I'm telling you the food that the kitchen is pushing out is pure GENIUS! The depths of flavor in all the dishes I had has been sooo creative with every bite offering something completely different. The cocktail drinks to are some kind of special. The bartenders I found to be very personal and know their craft. Don't over look their craft beer selection, you'll be surprise what they carry. With each of my visits, I've been fortunate to have great service both at the bar and out on the dining floor. 

OK so what would I recommend you might ask? Currently I'm addicted to the Pork Osso Bucco, deviled eggs, and the sweet potato cornbread with jalapeño honey butter! Honestly you can't go wrong with anything on the menu.

I typically keep my reviews local, so normally I wouldn't review chains unless I experience something extraordinary. This fast food restaurant was impressive! This particular franchise really demonstrated not only are they committed to quality ingredients but also delivering outstanding customer service! I went during lunch rush hours and boy was this place jammed packed. BUT here's the thing, as crowed as it was my order still arrived under five minutes. I was so impressed of how efficient the staff was operating. They handled the crowd masterfully. I wonder if the management and staff went under some kind of 5S lean training? My order arrived correct, hot, and fresh. This particular visit I dined in and found the dining room to be well kept. I liked seeing management out on the floor cleaning and refreshing customers beverages as well as outside in the Drive-thru line handing out orders. I honestly believe other fast food restaurants should take a page out of Chick-fil-A's book...

No I'm good ! Your fronting on Philly dog ! Tomato on a Cheese steak is a Sin ! No Amorosa Rolls even if you have to ship them in ! Forget Bout It ! Real South Philly here Bro ! Jim's, Johns, Max's, Chinks,etc... I could go on forever ! Its Pork Roll man ! Taylor Ham is pure garbage ! Case's, Trenton Pork Roll, even Thumans and or Loefflers before Taylor dude ! Seven bucks for a Pork Roll sandwich ! Crazy as hell ! Nine bucks for some wings ! Lol ! Avoid this joint at all cost ! Your better of eating nasty ass Subway ! Fugazi Fuckery at this joint !

I wouldn't have stumbled upon this restaurant if I hadn't been hit with extreme hunger during a trip to Value Village. I'm so glad I found Lan's. The lemongrass chicken vermicelli bowl is one of my go-to dishes, and it's always flavorful and delicious. Tom, one of the owners, is always super friendly and helpful which makes the experience even more enjoyable (if the food wasn't enough).

Lan's is a clean, inviting, friendly, cheap, and delicious place to go when you've got a craving for Asian. What more could you possibly want?

Truly a gem among a sea of mediocre Asian eateries in Edmonton.

This review is over my two experiences here. My first was a few weeks ago. I had a party of 5 and I was the first to arrive. Naturally, I walk up to put our name in for a table. I tell the hostess that I had 5 people and she says, "The rest of your party obviously isn't here so we will deal with it when they show up." and she walks away.
Ok.... In the meantime, several other groups arrive and she is still no where to be found. Several of them leave without being seated. My party arrives a few minutes later and we walk up to be seated. She looks around and says, "It will be about 20 minutes." 
Ok.... I had already waited 15 minutes in the sun sitting on a rock with no shade or water. So I was a bit annoyed. We eventually get seated. The food was great and so was our server. That part I would rate at 4 stars.

A few weeks later my girlfriend and I decided to go have breakfast there. We hop in the car and since it was a Sunday morning and I assumed they might be busy, we decide to call to either put our name in or  see how long the wait will be. Here is how our conversation went...

"Stonehouse Cafe."
"Hi, there will be two of us and we would like to sit outside with our dog. How long do you..."
She interrupts, "Hold on"
She puts us on hold for a minute or two...
"Stonehouse Cafe."
"Hi, there's going to be two of us and we want to sit outside, how long of a wait do you think it will be?"
In a not so friendly tone, "How am I supposed to know where you are and how long it will take you to get here?"
My girlfriend looks at me a bit shocked and we have to take a second to compose ourselves.
"ummmm okay.... We just wanted to know if you were busy and how long of a wait...."
We get cut off again, "We are a walk in restaurant and we don't do that."
*Click* 
I hung up so neither I nor my girlfriend could have the chance to lay into her for being so rude. We went somewhere else and had a great experience.
I'm not sure if she is the owner or just a hostess but she has single handily stopped us from coming back. Its too bad because I like the food and there aren't too many dog friendly places out there. After talking to friends, we found out that some of them had similar issues with the hostess. I have had some bad days in the service industry but there is no excuse for treating customers this way. We only wanted a simple question answered. I won't spend my money somewhere that treats its customers this way. If this issue gets addressed I would be happy to try again. If the food was as good as last time, it would likely be a 4-5 star review.

Im Rating them with one star not based on the food...I would give them 5 stars for the food. 

I am giving them one star based on the owners stealing the waiters/waitresses tips!

Make sure you tip your server on the side as the owners keep the tips! Your server won't get the tip you left them! I really encourage customers to do so because they work really hard as servers and they bus the tables as well! They deserve every tip they get!

It was a better world before a lot of things. The baseball cap on backwards, Rap, the Bowl Alliance. Your whole grain police hadn't passed a law against any food that tastes good. Sausage and eggs weren't a felony. A cheeseburger didn't get you shot at. Hell, you can get arrested for food in your own home if you don't register your low-fat mayonnaise. You ever had that? Why can't we get some scientist on a government grant or something to get to the bottom of this? That stuff just don't ruin good tuna fish, that crap will poison a whole city!

Anyway, this is long overdue and I know I'm driving my friends crazy with all the 4:00AM checkins at this place, but it has honestly become my favorite spot in town for great and what might even be described as upscale diner food. 

I have made a full lap around the menu and everything, well almost, has been superb. The only thing that didn't exceed my expectations we're the cheese grits. I chuckle whenever I pull into the parking lot imagining the staff whispering to themselves..."On no, here comes the Cheese Grits Man!" LOL

There is always a good crowd here, no matter what time of day. Its popular with both students and retirees, and that's rare. The first time I came here I took one look at their expansive menu and thought "Well this can't be any good." I was wrong, its better than good, its incredible.... and I don't impress that easy. And BTW, save room for some of their homemade coconut cream pie, and remember me in your Will.

Blessings from the heavens. 

I had gotten hooked on 4 Rivers in Jacksonville, so when I moved down here I was happy to find a 4 Rivers operation in Tampa, and semi frustrated at the long trek up Dale Mabry to get there. Well problem solved, this new store has exceeded all my expectations, and even manages pulled pork that IMO is better than the other 2 stores I've dined before.

OK so the pork here is outstanding, now if they can just do something about that damn cole slaw. However, thats where my complaints end. I've been to this location several times now and the rest of the menu gets a full 5*. This is the best brisket I've ever had, and the prime rib and horseradish sauce is  not to be believed. Had my first Texas Destroyer today, that was like a whole meal by itself, I thought I was hungry but when you finish a meal here and don't have room for dessert, you know you've been properly fed. 

All their sides are great. The collards, beans, mac n' cheese, fried okra, baked cheese grits, all top shelf. Oh and don't forget a couple of smoked jalapenos, they will set you free my friends. The bread pudding is the best I've had this side of New Orleans, and the banana pudding sends me right back to my childhood. Now, that Sweet Shop.... I wish they didn't have it, because its irresistible. Maybe the best part is that you can wash it all down with a Sun Drop in a real bottle. 

Lots of good options for BBQ in Tampa, sorry Jazzy, this is my new favorite. I'm beyond impressed. 5 Stars

For a chain operation, it doesn't get much better than Moe's.  I've eaten at their original store in Birmingham dozens of times, my first bite of the Bama style pulled pork sandwich and I was hooked. Its served with slaw, pickles, and both white and red sauce and it is just out of this world. Whats that...you never heard of White Sauce? Its a mayo, horseradish, vinegar concoction that was designed for BBQ chicken, but its great on turkey, catfish, wings, and pretty much everything else. 

The sides are fantastic too, especially the collards. They have daily specials on the sides and they are all terrific, the smoked sausage is first rate too.   But the real draw here is the pork, its moist and tender and just beyond belief. The ribs were among some of the best I've ever tasted, and the marinated and smoked wings are also in a league of their own. So happy to have two Moe's locations in the neighborhood now, this will save me a lot of money driving to Alabama for barbecue. 5 Bones

I don't normally write reviews for chains but I've never seen anyplace more unfairly maligned than Steak and Shake's internet presence. I've been a regular customer for oh about 15 years covering 5-6 states, and the food is consistently good. The shortcomings here are the same companywide, service and cleanliness. But I'm not one to complain about a random napkin on the floor or unbussed tables, and any issues I have over service usually vanish as soon as they drop a chocolate malt and a triple steakburger in front of me.

The food here is simply fantastic. I've circled the menu 3-4 times and never been served anything that was below standards. I especially love the steakburgers, chili, and seasoned fries. And this place is the ultimate in late night binge-a-thons. When the vampire in you takes over, this is the place too be. And the selection of shakes and malts cant be beaten, the only thing they're missing is a pineapple shake and when I see that on the menu I'll put up that 5th star. Oh oh, and that red velvet cake milkshake? I would be violating terms of service if I tried to describe that thing, so I'll just say its the best thing I've ever had.... in a glass. Case closed. 

BTW, I recently tried the 7x7... no I didn't finish it but I gave it the old college try. My server just laughed when I asked for a box to bring home the unrecognizable remnants of that beautiful tower of fried meat and cheese that I had rightfully massacred trying to fit that thing in my mouth. I'm a regular at this location, it never disappoints. 4.5 stars

The Grande Dame of all Southern hotels. 

I remember the first time I walked into the hotel lobby, the building had just been purchased by Park Hotels I think it was, and they were planning a $40M refurb. And this property was in great need, you could see the detail, you knew it was special, but the years had not been kind. Much to the amazement of the new owners when they began to dismantle the stained glass ceiling, they found this beautiful artwork underneath a layer of brown cigar smoke that had accumulated over 70 years +. Well here we are after the latest facelift, and I'm still their biggest fan. Just something special about this hotel, I guess 105 years of history will do that for you.

The rooms are beautiful and tastefully appointed. Got a great rate on a Junior Suite, very reasonable, made for a fantastic last night in town after the best Christmas ever. The hotel was busy last evening, no executive suites available but thats not unusual because the ballrooms are in constant demand. They look like something you would find at the White House. 

I'll never forget my parents dragging me here when I was a kid, and over dinner my dad instructing me to "go see the bathroom." I told him I didn't need to go and he insisted..."Go to the bathroom young man." OK, so I went .... 15 minutes later he had to come find me, I was having my shoes shined. LOL I'll bet more ladies have visited this men's bathroom than any other facility on the planet. I know I've toured 5-6 through there, the other guys don't mind, its a right of passage that everybody must experience. 

The rooms and beds are designed for extreme comfort, we had a direct view of the State Capitol which always makes this a unique experience. Downtown Nashville is pretty compact so you can walk anywhere you want to go from here without breaking a sweat, just valet your car and forget about it until departure. 

Make sure to check out the Oak Bar and if you make a reservation at the Capitol Grille and go in with no expectations, you'll enjoy yourself. Just wished the Veranda had been open, thats my favorite spot to have a drink just off the lobby, may be a seasonal thing. Anyway, this place is just spectacular, if you're in Nashville for a visit do yourself a favor and come check it out and have a few in the Oak Bar. It should be on everybody's Bucket List.
This place is too hip to function. No waiters, so prepare for a huge line on weekends. Water is served in a box. Food's alright.

This is an impressive looking resort but it doesn't live up to it's looks.  We stayed here last year while visiting relatives in the area.   The suite was nice... fireplace...small kitchen...nice all around.. but everything else was a pain in the ass right from the get go.  

When we arrived, it was late.. and we wanted a snack.  Turns out room service offers a VERY limited late night menu.   As in like..  A turkey sandwich or a salad.   Two items.  That's it.  And they can't bring any wine to your room, even though it was well before 2am... cause they lock it up after a certain time.   

The mani/pedi I had at the resort salon was also totally overpriced for what it was.  Over $100 for a VERY basic mani/pedi.  No special scented goodies, no hot stone massage, no nothing.   Lame.

The service at the bar was also sucky due to understaffing issues.  The floor to ceiling windows looking out at the amazing Arizona landscape is spectacular but *don't* advertise all day table service throughout the lounge if you can't follow through.   Only one bartender is not able to work the bar AND the table service.

To add insult to injury they fucked up our bill at the end of it all.  

On the upside, the concierge was helpful in making reservations for us at Janos, at another resort, which was lovely.  But, Jesus Christ...   Bellagio, where are you when I need you?  For the prices they're charging here, the service should be MUCH better.  It's supposed to be a "Resort" for crying out loud. 

One star for the helpful concierge, one star for the pretty view.. but we won't be staying here again.   Next time I'll stay at The Westin La Paloma where Janos is located.

I was super excited about Penca ever since reading about it in Zocalo magazine. A restaurant with the potential to give Poca Cosa a run for their money?? GASP! I feel like those trash magazines that try to make up feuds between celebrities. Was Hathaway peeved at Seyfried for her choice of Oscar wear or not?! Well, this doesn't matter much I suppose since I don't think Poca Cosa needs to worry. 

This brings me to my review: I did not like the food at Penca. I LOVE how much downtown Tucson is growing and I fully want to support everything new that pops us (which seems to happen at an almost alarming rate). However, I cannot get behind this place. My pozole was hands down bad. Probably the worst pozole or soup I have had, actually. My godmother in San Luis Potosi makes this pozole that is magical. Yeah, snicker all you want but you haven't tried it. It's that good. Mainly, it has taught me that pozole is a complex soup that is not easy to make. Long story short- Penca's pozole was flat and too heavy on the hominy. If Penca wants to do a turkey based pozole, I would recommend using heavier spices (as the broth is not depending on fatty meat like beef or pork for flavor).

The tacos were good, albeit a bit on the pricy side.I cannot help but think that the taco plate, with the fresh tortillas and vegetables sides, strongly resembles the taco plates at Taqueria Pico de Gallo. However, Penca's rendition is pricier and nowhere near as tasty.

My last gripes: the horchata and chicharrones. The horchata comes served in A LOT of ice (i.e.  you get very little of it). Come on, horchata is basically rice water. How can you get away with charging so much for so little? And the chicharrones are exactly like the bagged Baken-ets pork rinds you can find in 7-11. Why would I pay for this stuff at a restaurant? In Mexico, the chicharrones that are served at restaurants and eateries have meat. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicharr%C3%B3n.

Style over substance is the major theme here. The interiors are gorgeous. I'm digging the Mexican movie poster with Maria Felix. And similar to my review of The Hub, I don't feel like my bad review will hurt this hoppin' spot in downtown Tucson-it always looks busy and patronage doesn't seem to be a problem. With that, I try to erase the guilt of my harsh review of Penca.

Disclaimer: I am not some snarky online nerd who writes negative reviews all of the time, hiding behind my computer.  I used to review restaurants for AAA and I currently work as a trainer in the service industry.  So please note that when I give something 1 star? I mean it.

Several of my friends have been raving about the burgers and shakes here for awhile. Philly Mag gave their burger props with the likes of Rouge and Village Whiskey. Although I'd been inside before, I hadn't eaten here yet because I was frankly annoyed by the disingenuous feel I got from the staff and decor. But I got a living social voucher so I figured "what the hell?"

We were seated by a REALLY excited hostess and waited about 10 minutes before we were asked by our waitress about drinks. Not the best start, but fine. We ordered our burgers (we both asked for medium) and didn't make any kind of special requests. I'm figuring this will be a simple task. But no.

When our food finally arrives, my burger is overcooked (and I mean 90% brown, 10% pink overcooked) and both of us have a plate of almost cold fries.  At this point, I'm ready to just throw in the towel and head home.  But I decided to tell the waitress.  When I shared this with her (politely), she silently took my plate to bring it back to the kitchen.  She shortly returned with a smaller plate with those same cold fries on them.  Umm, huh?  Ok.  A good 20 minutes later, she finally returns with another small plate that has my new burger on it.   It is cooked medium, but has zero flavor. None.  But I'm so hungry after having waited 40 minutes for the order I made that I scarf it down so that I can finally leave.

The thing is, no one here seems to give a crap. The waitress didn't care that my food sucked.  The hostess seemed more interested in the music than she was interested in providing good service.  I guess that's the "charm" for some folks and if you like that, then this is the place for you.  If you want to eat at a place that seems to care more about it's "rep" than it does about food quality or service? PYT is it!  If you just want an AWESOME burger?  Go to the Abbaye or N. 3rd.

Frugal MacDoogal. The adult liquor store that is similar to Liquor Barn(for those of us in KY).

This place could easily be 5 stars but unfortunately, I can't give it more than 3. 

The selection here is awesome. Their prices are somehow cheap which is surprising. I even saw some bottles local to Louisville that are cheaper here than in Louisville!

So after that last paragraph... what could be the issue? The issue is they have very few beer singles to choose from. At least 85% of their craft beer selection forces you to buy 4 and 6 packs. I'm so spoiled with being able to buy singles that liquor stores that make you buy beer by the pack aren't worth my time. There are way too many beers out there to be potentially stuck with a 6 pack of beer that I might not like. 

If Frugal changes the way they sell beer sometime in the future to where you can buy singles of all that they have, this will be the place to go in Nashville.

Two friends and I went here on a Friday night. This place is exactly how the name is, half Chinese and half Thai food mixed with one or two Vietnamese appetizers. So you can definitely get a decent amount of Asian variety here. Everything was pretty good, we got the lettuce wraps, different noodles, and curry and everything was good. Definitely a place to check out if you're too far from Chinatown but in the city. Prices were normal for center city. Service was decent and place is nice and clean.

I'll start with the positives:  Ample and convenient parking, acceptable decor, generally clean atmosphere.

Now for the laundry list of negative.  This casino has no cocktail waitresses and no free alcoholic drinks.  There is a chuck-e-cheese style free soda machine, but that is as far as the complimentary service goes.  At least at chuck-e-cheese you get prizes for all the money you dump into the machines. At Harrah's Chester you get second hand smoke.

The machines seem tighter than AC or Vegas.  I'm not sure what payback percentage the machines are set at, but it seems like they are all set at state minimum.

The casino is located in a slum next to a state prison.  You can't fault Harrah's for that, but it is certainly a negative.

The Temptations  Buffet is the worst buffet I have ever been to in my entire life.  What better way to celebrate losing $50 in 20 minutes than a chafing dish of what looks like lukewarm excrement?  See photos.  Thankfully, this buffet is not indicative of all Harrah's buffets.  Harrah's Waterfront Buffet in AC is excellent.

Fresh lemonade of the day, fresh made ciabatta, calamari, crudo - repeat!
Perfect little 'Mediterranean Italy' nearby, you can never go wrong with their lunch menu on a beautiful sunny day. They have an outdoor (garden and sidewalk seating). Beautiful indoor seating as well. Service and music accompanying the good is always excellent. I've only been here once for dinner, it was very good as well.  Remember, this isn't fried calamari, this is sauteed, different but very good.

If only I could drive there often.  I absolutely loved what I tried there and there are plenty of menu items that I want to try.   From presentation to packaging, service everything was good.   It has a cute cozy atmosphere and definitely put your phone away while enjoying the meal.  

Smoked salmon Blinchiki is my favorite,  I do love smoked salmon...so... yes. I can eat them cold and as leftovers!

Next,  Draniki with meat mushroom and cheese.  They are more than enough to fill me up really.  I like them when they are warm and fresh,  better than reheated.

I had Golubtzy, cabbage roll with beef rice and pepper filling, presented in creamy tomato sauce. It was like comfort food.  

Finally Lamb plov.  It's something very familiar but a different version of what I've had before,  from a totally different part of the world and I really enjoyed it. The mild flavor of the spices, cooked perfectly and presented on Jasmine rice.  Delicious, comfort food and it doesn't make me feel heavy after finishing it. 

I'll definitely try other menu items next time,  if I can resist these ones :)

Another place that disappointed with not only the food but also with service. Yes they were busy on a memorial day weekend but the servers were in rush to get you through the experience quickly. 
You can join the waiting list on Yelp, but you'll have to check in within a given period of time. It also tells you how many parties are ahead of you. 
Food wise, coffee was just okay, chicken was dry in fried chicken sandwich and we couldn't finish it, omelette was plain, very plain and I've had better. The avocado toast was okay, but the bread itself was tough and we didn't finish it.

I'll try to keep it short, love at first sight - redefined.  
Such a welcoming face of the restaurant right on Howard, with a beauty of it's own. 

It's probably one of my favorites,  if not three favorite restaurant in Tampa. It's just not the food,  which everything is simply delicious,  it's the presentation, service,  flavour, aesthetics. You can see everyone pouring their heart at everything they are doing  including the family.  After already quite a few visits now,  I love how they pay attention to every little detail.  

When the butter was delayed by a few minutes,  they brought fresh biscuit without extra charge.  When they ran out of one item and we were okay with the replacement, they did not charge for the replacement. 

Hey everything so far has been delicious,  even double shot Espresso has been one my favorite in Tampa. 

Nothing so far has been heavy, yet it maintains the layers of flavor and taste.  

I still have to try their weekday breakfast and more of the specials and lunch menu.

If you can avoid waiting in line outside, which we could, it's a good stop for the thin crusted fried chicken. If you like your lemonade sweet, definitely try their lemonade, or there's always unsweetened tea.

My 3 piece dark meat fried chicken came with a side and I decided to get a red/kidney beans. The chicken was moist and the crust was so thin and blended with the chicken as if it was the extension of the fried skin. 

The side was generous and it came with a scoop of white rice. It definitely had mild but good flavor and consistency. 

Nothing fancy but overall it was filling, delicious and quick visit before the flight.  Yes it's a short Uber/Lyft ride away.

I definitely recommend it if you like fried chicken.

Probably my final review for this place. I called for a pickup right when they opened, and for specific reasons they asked me to call back as the kitchen wasn't open, understandable.. so I called them after a while.
During the second call they informed me that the kitchen won't open until 6pm,  so I wanted to call back later, especially when they could give me an estimate about how long it'll take to pick my food up. They insisted that if I place at order right then, they will make sure that the order is ready within 20-25 minutes.

I reach there in about 25 minutes and they said it'll take 15 more minutes. I wait outside in the car and when I walk in after 15 more minutes of wait, everyone on the table already have their food ready. They didn't acknowledge anyone waiting to pickup food. 
About 20 minutes or waiting inside, I had to finally ask them about the order again. They just smiled and said it'll be ready shortly. It was ready 5 minutes after that but there wasn't any apology, no one offered water, it was completely unprofessional from them. I've probably ordered a delivery from the over a dozen times and been there for dinner about the same amount of time, but this will be my last time at Deccan spice. They have missed a few items before during delivery but this experience was a bit extreme.

No I won't start another review with Billie Jean song even though it's stuck in my head right now. 
To keep it short, it's located around the business district area which has seen a good change in the last few years with a step towards increased number of restaurants and attractions. 

Willa Jean, another Yelp recommendation that didn't disappoint. There was an hour's wait for the brunch but we got seated in about half an hour.  The service was good and they were really quick and efficient. We didn't get to try their baked items but that's what attracted me to this restaurant. 

It had a modern and welcoming feeling to it. The food had a perfect fusion and a good twist as well. That's all on the menu, what about the actual food? 

Starting with coffee, it tells you a lot about a restaurant and it definitely didn't disappoint. 
Add the BBQ shrimp on sourdough toast and the hangover bowl, so comforting, full of flavour and delicious. The perfect amount of fat on the short rib and poached egg can cure hangovers for sure.... Just add that delicious grits to it! 
BBQ shrimp toast was unique and full of flavour. Definitely had a good touch of New Orleans with a nice comfort food blend. 
Fried chicken sandwich, yes it's too much food but how can one resist? It was good, the crust was really good but the biscuit was different and delicious! 

Definitely a must try place!

This was my first time trying Jamaican food and I am a fan :)   I got it delivered and the delivery was pretty quick, food arrived in about 30 minutes,  given that the restaurant is about 10-12 minutes drive away.  

I ordered Jerk Chicken (large with two sides), Roti with goat curry.  Loved both of those items,  as the chicken was moist and the sides of steamed cabbage,  rice and peas was good and filling.   Roti with goat curry is one of my favorites now and I'm sure that I'll crave it again pretty soon. 

 It's priced reasonably and I've ordered it again last week with different sides.  I'll try different items on the menu next week and update this review accordingly.

Just Wow! Even if it's a little local place, it has a big character and it left a huge impression on me. Don't get me wrong, there's still quite a bit of place to sit inside and  with outdoor seating, but you can always take out and your order will be ready in no time. 
Back to food again, with their special grouper sandwich, I got it blackened. It was magical, creamy and it defined simplicity with perfection. Did I say comforting as well? 
The side of garlic parmesan fries were as good. 
Do try their blackened shrimp if you like shrimp and you won't regret. I'll probably return many many many times to try  other menu items.  Yes the can of beer can cost a bit more than other places, but it's local and the food itself deserves the price.

Such a cute local coffee place that has been on my bookmark list for a while. It was definitely busy around 11am on Sunday, although they have shaded 'indoor' and outdoor seating ( perfect for cooler months and if you have a dog). This place reminded me a lot of Cuban coffee queen from key West so I wanted to try their Cafe con leche. It's brewed with whole milk, a little bit of sugar and cinnamon. It was pretty good paired with their Mediterranean frittata.

I know y'all just opened so I sincerely hope that I can write a better review in the future. My wife and I had lunch there earlier today. The tacos are extremely small making the price not so cheap after all. The meat had no taste. We had the beef fajita and pork steak. It was super plain tasting. We have been looking forward to this place for weeks and were shocked and disappointed. If your main draw is going to be tacos, they have to be way better than what we had. Another thing.... Your green and red sauces are also plain. I know we are just two people so you can take our opinions with a grain of salt. However, we had a conversation with the couple sitting next to us and they felt the exact same way. The chips and queso were good but that's just not that hard... You have a place down the street that sells tacos too... Their tacos are not plain. We have Cherokee Street with a variety of places to get tacos.... Those tacos are not plain either... You see where I am going with this? There is a lot of taco competition on the southside. I have no reason to return if the tacos are plain, the salsas are plain, I have to stand shoulder to shoulder in line next to an old decommissioned deep fryer, all while hoping that I might actually be able to get a seat at one of the few tables.... I believe that you did a very good job marketing your restaurant because the entire community was waiting anxiously for y'all to open. However, your tacos didn't have any 'wow factor.' If this continues, you will see very few returning customers. There are too many taco places for me to return to your place with less than mediocre food. Sorry for the harsh review but I was really, really looking forward to your food. I left your restaurant disappointed.

I went here for their $10 open bar on the weekend of my 21st.  
It was way too crowded and no one could get a drink.

I started to pull the "It's my 21st" card to get some drinks and about 20 minutes later I finally got 1 drink.  

Well, that was 1 drink too many because I was ROOFIED.  That's right, someone slipped something in my drink.  I'm not one to exaggerate or claim things for attention.  I thought this kind of thing never happened, but I was so wrong. Anyways, that sums up the crowd that was there that night. 

You can assume I'm never going back.  Even if I weren't drugged that night, my opinion of Copa would be just as low.

Worst bagels.  Worst service.

There were so many things wrong with this place that I won't even go into.  

However, my biggest issue was that I got a bagel that was stale.  I couldn't bite through it and it was pretty much like baked bread gone wrong.  I would have preferred frozen bagels from the grocery store.

It was so bad I asked for another bagel, which is something I never do.  The cashier tried looking for another bagel while another employee (whom I'm guessing was the manager) thought it necessary to tell me that "they're all like that" and was apparently annoyed by my dissatisfaction.  Hm.. Smart.  Let the customer know that ALL of your bagels suck, not just the one I received.  Defeated, I went back to my seat.

Then, I realized how absurd that was, as someone who works in customer service, and went back to ask for another bagel.  The same cashier was trying to be helpful while the same manager, again, thought it necessary to make a passive-aggressive remark in my general direction.  "Just give her whatever the hell she wants."  As a result, I got another stale bagel.  

Pissed off, I took the other damn stale bagel and decided to leave it at my seat, uneaten.  I've never directly experienced such terrible service.  If I lived in the area I would have reported that one manager... or else asked what in her 20 or so years of life could have caused such a miserable existence to have her feel the need to share her unfortunate state of being with innocent bystanders such as myself.

The Tavern and other nearby restaurants were on a 1.5 hour wait. A colleague and I were too hungry to wait which led us around the block into the heavenly smell of smoked pork emanating from The Row Kitchen & Pub. The exterior looks a little worn down but don't let this discourage you. Yelp's overall rating of this place is 3.5 stars which was enough for us to try it besides the smell of that BBQ pork was intoxicating. 

Thankfully we stumbled upon this place; it was rustic with wood finishes and country décor. The hostess kindly greeted us then sat us in a cozy booth. Our waitress warmly greeted us before giving us her food and drink recommendations. We ordered the smoked chicken, pulled pork platter with a side of macaroni & cheese and snap peas. 

The food was amazing without condiments but The Row has a unique "white barbeque sauce" made with a small amount of cayenne pepper. It is SoOoOo good and addictive, we used  1/2 the bottle. It was like no other BBQ sauce I've ever tasted. The macaroni & cheese was out of this world topped with a sprinkle of smoked bacon. Umm umm umm it hit the spot. 

After a long day at work we were in the mood for this place. Everything from the friendly employees to the warm atmosphere and delicious comfort food infused with a touch of gourmet. 

I HIGHLY recommend The Row Kitchen & Pub and would love to see it on "Unique Eats". 

I'll be back

OMGOSH.. words cannot describe how good the food is at Restaurant Rebirth. Everything was delicious and the service was great.
To start our server brought us some cornbread. I don't know what word can do justice to how good it was. It was a slice of heaven. 

I decided to try the gumbo which was chicken with andouille sausage. It was very tasty and had a kick to it. I also ordered Just Picked garden salad and I was surprised how well balanced the Creole sugar vinaigrette was. I also liked the candied pecans that were tossed in the salad. 
I have to say the dish that I thought was a home run for me was the BBQ pork belly that I was able to taste. It was phenomenal and I honestly think that it could be an entree.

Dessert came out last and I have to say everything was delicious from the chocolate tarte to the café au lait crème brûlée. My personal favorite was the bread pudding. It was amazing!
All in all I had a very great if not excellent dining experience at Rebirth. 

If you're ever in New Orleans and are looking for a great place to eat, a place close enough to French Quarters but away from the tourist area, Rebirth is your place. Not only will you have amazing tasty foods but you will have great service as well.
I will definitely be back!

Good bang for your buck.

Wanting to have buffet in Reno that is not located in a Casino and something different from the usual fare, I searched Yelp for buffets and this placed popped up. I just wanted to escape having to smell another cigarette smoke that is extremely suffocating. I called and discovered lunch was only $7.99. Why so cheap, I wondered. I read the other reviews and in Yelpers I trusted. 

Located just a mile or so from the strip and parking is located in their back lot. Area looked clean and safe so we proceeded inside. Interior and furniture looked nice and they had a bar in the back and the buffet table on the other side. One thing I noticed was there was not one Indian soul working in the restaurant so I had a slight hesitation but quickly vanished once I glanced on the buffet table and saw something familiar. The server asked us if we were there for the buffet and told us to grab a plate. 

The server started us with some Garlic Naan bread that was very good. They have the usual Chicken Tandoori, Tikki Masala, Lamb Curry, Potatoes, Rice, Veggies, Chutneys etc...that are a staple in a typical AYCE Indian cuisine. We were not disappointed one bit. All the familiar flavors, spices and texture were present and very comforting. Service was also exceptional as they kept refilling our glasses without even asking. 

I probably had one plate too many (I had three) since I had to drop a deuce in their very clean toilet. Yes it was nice and clean, and I know it's T.M.I. 

But it is what it is!

My only negative comment would be that I was looking forward to some Bollywood movies as mentioned in other reviews, but it was a Sunday and all their monitors had on the Steelers vs. Redskins on TV. All is forgiven, except I couldn't stop comparing the throwback jerseys the Steelers were wearing looked similar in color to what I left in the......never mind.

Oh yeah....I'd come here again. But next time I'll keep it to two plates.

This casino sucks; save your money and go elsewhere!

The parking garage is a nightmare; when you get up to the level that all the 'regular people/ base players' park; they block the whole aisle to wait 20 minutes for someone to come out so they can park.

Once inside, my friend needed a casino card and she didn't have one, but they refused to print it out for her since apparently her id didn't look like her(she used to be blond and is now brunette) and was going to expire soon. Even though she had her renewal paperwork on her (and note, the ID was not expired yet!), they refused to print her out a card.

Then within the first 5 minutes of being on the floor, I was harassed twice for my ID, and not nicely either. 

By the time the second guy came over, I was pretty annoyed already. Then he told me I had to wear a wristband; this would help with the ID issue because it is apparently their policy to harass people who look under 30 if they don't have a wristband on. Apparently the first guy who grabbed me should have given me one. 

He then told me if I refused to wear a wristband, I would have to leave (which for the record is absolutely insane. If I've already proven to you that I am over 21, what the hell is the problem?)

At that point, I decided it was no longer worth it to spend any more of my time and any of my money at that casino; I didn't play a single game, since I was so annoyed. I went to Parx instead and had a great time.

After my horrible experience in Harrah's, I was not happy with my PA Casino Experience. However, Parx was a godsend. Not only is the outside much more exciting from the road, the parking was much easier as well. 

The employees were pretty nice for the most part; although I was made to wear a wristband here in this casino as well. The difference was the employee was not a jerk on a power trip and he was overly helpful in explaining why I had to do so. Plus since I had my AC casino card on me, I got $25 free slot play so I got to have fun and not worry about losing all my money!

The overall appearance of the place is like comparing the Taj Mahal (Parx) to a McDonald's(Harrah's). Location probably plays it's part, but this whole place was exquisite. They even had a live band at their 360 club doing covers of old favorites. Even the crowd who hangs out there is not bad looking. (Guy wise anyway. I didn't see too many overly attractive girls, but there were lots of decent looking men which I was not expecting!)

The only complaint I have it that its hard to get a drink and yes, they are free here as long as you are playing! I tried to catch one of those drink girls so many times, and finally by the end of the night, one took my order. However, even though I went up to the bar twice, I was still not able to get service from the bartender. So between the bartender and most of the drink girls I came in contact with, I think they could do with a little retraining.

From the outside, it looks like a fantastic idea. However, for the price, it is not fancy enough.

My family was celebrating my sister's birthday as well as Mother's day for my mom and grandmom, but to cut costs we decided to go Friday night for their 3-hour dinner cruise. We ended up spending $340ish for this dinner cruise.

We had our photo taken before getting on the ship where we were greeted half-heartedly by a few of the ship's employees. Then we were shown to our table.

Our waitress introduced herself, but then went MIA for the rest of the night, even though the table next to us received constant service. Her trainee was slightly more attentive to our needs, but we still ended up making a trip to the bar ourselves after waiting a while for drinks.

The buffet food was not that great.The salad looked okay, but offered a very watery vinegarette or cream style dressing. The salmon was okay, until we realized the skin was still on the bottom! Gross. And then when my grandmother ordered roast beef, they gave her a tough end piece that she had issues cutting. Even the rolls were hard and tasteless. We ate very little.

Then we had the cake brought out, and we were unable to sing Happy Birthday due to the DJ deciding to turn on loud music.

We participated in a little bit of the dancing, but ended up staying on the upper decks for the remainder of the evening.

All in all, it wasn't a great trip and we were sorely disappointed.

This is the type of restaurant that downtown Carmel was waiting for. Although Ruth's Chris is located on 86th, there is no need to travel downtown for an upscale steakhouse. In the newly and continually growing downtown Carmel scene, Anthony's is a well executed contemporary steakhouse design. A large bar welcomes you on entering. The dining space is two floors with the upstairs equipped with the bar from the Glass Chimney. 

Cocktails were the black walnut old fashioned (I wonder if they use Cardinal Spirits' Nocino) and a limoncello/vodka/prosecco cocktail that were both enjoyable. 
 
I started with a 1/2 dozen East Coast oysters with the chili magnonette. The sweet house ketchup that also comes is a bit too sweet for my liking. The tempura cauliflower is fantastic with a delicious roasted red pepper bisque with just the slightest bit of spice. 

The petite filet and 8 oz filet were cooked perfectly with a delicious salt and pepper crust. There are many personalizations that are available for the steaks - we went with the black truffle butter and the port cherry demi. Solid picks. 

Two sides of the broccolini with shaved almonds and cherry and the gnocchi were both filling. I recommend the gnocchi and the broccolini is a hefty order as well.

For dessert we split the Kentucky bourbon bread pudding that was very tasty and recommended by our waitress. 

A nice white tablecloth dining experience. We were seated promptly and the staff was attentive to detail - I even saw them re-make the same table three times as the tablecloth was not suitable enough for them. We plan to return.

possibly NO ONE can fathom how much i've complained about the lack of good Vietnamese food in the eastcoast (NYC, for example). i bitch about it constantly in all of my reviews, for starters. =)

i decided to give it a chance and try out Nam Phuong. as per Dave H.'s suggestion... i had a feeling i could trust his advice. i will admit, i had an inkling of doubt on my conscience, though. 

upon entering this establishment... you realize this place is HUGE! they have a nice banquet area and on the other side... a casual dining area. this is a great place for big family/number parties. the servers are swift and the food comes out in heaps of humongous portions. i haven't seen this in years! sh*t you not.... for the same price of the dishes served at Nam Phuong- you would be getting 1/3 of the portion in New York. lame sauce. 

the food looked fresh, smelled magnificent and i just knew i was going to be in pure ecstasy during my meal. 

what is the usual deal maker for me at ANY Vietnamese restaurant? well- the Pho and Goi Cuon (summer rolls with shrimp, vermicelli, basil, bean sprouts)... they HAVE to be on point. the Pho cannot be too greasy, the broth has to look like it's been cooked for hours and reduced (then skimmed of fat), a slight smell of Anise and onion and of course... have that "kind of ghetto" feel to it. that vibe... i tell you, is very hard to explain. however, if you're a regular Pho connoisseur like i am... you TOTALLY know what i'm talkin' abouts.  this is the kind of Pho you'd find in the urban/ghetto areas of Seattle, Vancouver, LA, SF and Houston. the westcoasters know their Pho, yo. now, being that you're in SOUTH PHILLY... oh yeah, they know their ghetto Pho quite well- and i LOVE IT. 

the Goi Cuon (summer roll) was fresh and stuffed full of shrimp and pork. the peanut/hoisin dipping sauce is a perfect addition to the rolls. then, came the Cha Gio (fried spring rolls) and those suckers were addicting! perfection. another staple i always order at Vietnamese places is the Bun aka Vermicelli (thin rice noodles) bowls. we chose the Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork) and added the Cha Gio to the dish. the bowl was literally bigger than the size of my head. the amount of meat compared to the actual portion of the vermicelli was uncanny. 

overall... this is the reason why i think there is hope for my existence in the east coast. if i really have an aching feeling of good quality Vietnamese food- i could always go to Philly for a weekend and chow down. unfortunately- that means i have to settle with mediocre stuff in NYC. *le sigh*

Dave H.- thank you. =)

I'm Going to HELL for this review,  but at least I'm Honest!  I heard a lot about this favorite Italian Restaurant outside of Eddystone, PA.  Locals Love it.  It's been around forever, and the interior shows it.  Inside, an outdated interior reveals, Italian paintings, and colors from the 60's & 70's.  Walls are dirty and in need of fresh paint.  The floors need to be updated.  The tables are covered with table clothes (OK),  but the early 70's style chairs are filthy and need either recovering, or updating.  
    We made sure we stopped by 4:30 on Good Friday at the first seating.  One other couple was there.  The Owner ushered us to a table.  We were Hovered over to the point where it was uncomfortable.  We were there to relax,  not to rush.  The Owner ran through the specials, not disclosing the prices, (It Happens).  I ordered the Calamari, as a first.  These were low quality, Calamari Rings, Previously frozen, and served with a Marinara ( Seemed to be Canned Gravy ).  The portion was small for the price.  I also ordered the Portabella Soup.  The Soup presentation was that of muddy water.  OK Flavor,  however no discernible pieces of Mushroom.  The Garlic Bread that was served was a Hoagie Roll,  Sliced in half with Oil, and a little parsley.  I didn't taste any garlic,  and I believe the oil used was vegetable,  but I'm not sure.  Not Olive Oil.  There was also another roll served with diner style butter packets.  Can't serve butter in a dish?  When asked what I would like,  I first ordered the Chops,  then quickly asked the Owner if It were too late to change to the Eggplant Parm.  He said No Problem,  then walked away mumbling nastily in Italian.  My Date ordered the Portabella stuffed Ravioli's in which she said was good.  My Eggplant was Chewy, Soggy, and was served over spaghetti with too much water on my plate.  Another young lady,  I'm assuming the Owners Daughter,  was very accommodating and attentive.  The whole meal seemed like it was being served at your Aunts House.  Nothing amazing or Special.  It could have been intimate,  however the eavesdropping of the owner, made it uncomfortable.  I'm Sure the Locals are going to berate me,  However, This is my opinion!  Disappointed!  Could really be a Special Place!  Needs a Restaurant Make Over!

HOOOO MY GOD. I HAVE DIED AND GONE TO BAR-BE-QUE HEAVEN!

I recently visited St. Louis to see a friend and almost everyone I met that weekend asked if I had been to Pappy's yet! Sign that I should go? Oh, most definitely.

Hands down one of the best BBQ ribs I've ever had. So juicey and tender just by itself. Some rib joints I've been to pride themselves on ribs, but are smothered in sauce. The thing I loved about Pappy's was the fact that the ribs were amahhhhzing with and without the sauce. I couldn't decide which one I enjoyed more! 

But what really set the ribs apart was the glaze/crust! The smokey flavor and crust really gave the ribs an extra something that *dies* I just can't..

The place opens up at 11am everyday and I would suggest going at 11am everyday, if not a little earlier. I arrived at 11am per my friend's suggestion and there was already a good amount of people waiting in line and even more people already sitting down and eating! The line only grew longer, so I would come early and avoid the lines.

I got one of the rib combos and you get to choose two sides to go with your delicious ribs. I opted for the green beans and sweet potato fries. Both were excellent choices. The fries tasted great as most sweet potato fries do and the green beans were a good balance to the meal so I didn't feel like a complete fatty :P

Striped each of those babies straight down to the bone and would do it again in a heartbeat!

Tampa's first izakaya!! I was so excited to come here w/ my husband & another couple. We ordered all of the skewers, and most of them were good. I forgot to take pictures of the 3 plates of skewers! *FAIL* I wasn't a fan of the chicken gizzard (no flavor) & chicken thigh (too fatty). The takoyaki was really good, and it had big chunks of octopus in it. The gyoza was supposed to be pan fried but it looked deep fried... it was ok. Lotus root chips with guac was AWESOME!! My husband had the mi-so-hot ramen (which was not spicy), and the rest of us had tonkotsu ramen. We were all not impressed with the ramen. I heard so many great things about their ramen, but it was just ok. My husband lived in Osaka for 2 years so he KNOWS good ramen. Our 2 friends recently moved here from NYC so they've also had a lot of really good ramen. I'm a fat kid for life so I've also eaten a lot of good ramen. The ramen just wasn't savory enough & it didn't have a lot of deep flavors. The one saving grace was that it had a generous amount of pork belly in it, which was DELICIOUS! I also had 2 of their japanese beers (Ginga Kogen & Far East Tokyo White)... both were good beers. One of our friends had the ponzu cocktail, which she really liked. My husband had Hitachino Nest Red Yeast Ale, which is one of his favorite beers. The service was excellent, and the ambience is wonderful. I definitely want to come back to try more food, sushi & sake. Each couple got a thank you card w/ a surprise discount on our next visit... hubby said this was a popular thing that they do in Japan. So we need to use that surprise discount, right?? Winner winner, izakaya dinner!

So far, my favorite Italian restaurant in the Tampa area. I absolutely love their gnocchi with meatball (add-on). I've ordered take out once & dined in once. I ordered the penne a la vodka when we dined in (which was good), but I was wishing I had ordered the gnocchi again instead. I usually like to order different items if I haven't been there more than 3 times. I'll update my review when we revisit this restaurant.

We have friends who spent two weeks in Nola with a promise not to dine in any spot more than once. They broke that promise when the found Superior. And now I understand why.

It's very pretty, and very full which is always a good sign. Felt more local than touristy as well, so bonus points for that. Service was exceptional, food was excellent, and the biggest surprise of all was the check. It was the most reasonable meal we had on our trip!

I had gumbo and a shrimp poboy.  The shrimp poboy was stuffed with shrimp! We also shared bread pudding for dessert.  We have been on a bread pudding kick our last few visits to Nola. This one was excellent... seeping in whiskey sauce. I would do that again. In a heartbeat.

So even is you're like us and don't drive while in town (cause we drink way too much to drive while on vacay) the streetcar stop is right on the corner making this easy and cheap to get here. Enjoy!

The first time we visited NOLA (so many years ago) we stayed at the Marriott. The last time we visited NOLA we stayed at the Marriott. That speaks volumes.

The very first time was shortly after we married and we were so young and so inexperienced (don't snicker). The first night we were there we wanted to go to the French Quarter and couldn't figure out from a map how to get there. So we had dinner at the hotel, and a room service breakfast in bed which I judge all room service breakfast's by to this day...an entire basket of baked goods, coffee and juice. I can't even tell you how generous and how good this was. The next morning we hit the desk to ask how to get to the FQ. They didn't even roll their eyes when they said "go out the door and turn right and you'll be there." Duh.

We'll older and wiser now, and tried so many of the hotels here. And even when we were staying elsewhere, we would always end up in the bar here, which is lovely and has great happy hour specials. And it's all about the location...not in the Quarter (loud) and not miles from everything else. While it's "corporate" it does have a NOLA feel and it's one of the main reasons we've become loyal Marriott customers (Hint: it helps to be an Elite cause they upgrade you) Unlike other hotels, when we say we want a river view, they don't jerk us around. They give us the view!!! A big shout out here to Justin Tye at the Elite desk who takes such good care of us - he takes care of everyone. I've watched.

Everything here is top notch. Have a problem...don't worry, they'll take care of it ASAP. I even left a favorite pair of shoes in a room and had them returned to me. Rooms come equipped with coffee pots and refrigs. And there's a Starbucks in the lobby, a restaurant and a 24 hour M Club, so when you have that 0 dark thirty flight you can get coffee to go!! We've made the rounds, and we're here for the duration. So keep the light on...we'll be back! You know we will.

Just need a bite of something? Walk in have a taste of Mississippi Mud. It's gooood. So was some of the other candies like the marshmallow bar and their version of a turtle. Their version of pralines are good, but my favorite is still Southern Candy Kitchen. The truffles were plentiful, and I had a good sampling but I just didn't like most of them. Too heavy for a truffle...in my opinion (which is free here). But the cost was very reasonable. Again...in my opinion. I've paid much more than this for chocolates. And they do have a NOLA sampler box if just want a good feel for NOLA sweets. I'd go back....just not for truffles.

STELLA! That's what I wanted to yell when I walked in the door. I love this place so much. We've never had to wait (even on Easter Sunday) and the food is so damn good.  Bananas Foster French Toast? Why yes, I think I will. When was the last time you had ice cream for breakfast? Soft Shell Crab Eggs Benedict....oh yes.  So many wonderful things to eat and so little time. And Bloody Mary's full of healthy veggies. I can't imagine coming to the Big Easy and not eating here.

After hearing all the hype, we had to brunch here. So we followed the Yellow Brick Road, and even though they say it's on Canal it isn't really...more like an alley behind Canal. We were told to look for the line, and promised it would move quickly. I was told a 20 minute wait...just like Cracker Barrel I think to myself. Unlike CB, I belly up to the bar and order 2 Bacon Bloody Marys and we enjoy then in the sun before being seated.

Make no mistake...this food isn't heart healthy. Or low calorie. But it is the bomb. I had the Trifecta...more food than I needed for the entire day. Think shrimp, sausage, pork debris, fried chicken. All on English muffins with poached eggs and sauce. Each one better than the last. The Pork Debris was my favorite, but I enjoyed them all. Bob was more sensible and had pancakes and bacon. 

If you go, and you SHOULD go, be sure to have the Bacon Bloody Mary. BEST bloody mary . And I know my BM's.....you know I do.

Mother's isn't what it used to be. Or maybe I've grown? I do think it changed hands sometime after Kartrina and employees are ruder and food doesn't seem as authentic. Either way, I'm not interested in eating here again. But if you're new to NOLA tourism, maybe you want to say you've eaten here. It's not awful...it's just not eye rolling good. And it sure isn't cheap like it used to be. You can do better. Just my free advice. And you know what that's worth.

Is there anything more iconic NOLA than sipping a late afternoon adult beverage on a front porch with Columns on St. Charles Avenue? Not for me.

It's beautiful here. Check out the side garden and fountain. Then go inside. How beautiful it is. And rooms are reasonable. Made us think about actually staying here ( but only saw public areas...not guest rooms.) Drinks were good and there is a happy hour. 

We'll be back. You know we will.

Early in our trip we walked by and I remarked this place had great reviews and we should try it sometime. Later that day while making plans with friends they suggested we meet here. Don't you love it when a plan comes together!! And what is more Nola than dining in an open courtyard? Nothing I can think of.

Honestly, the setting was enough I probably would have been happy with a ho-hum meal, but thankfully that didn't happen. The food is amazing. I had a Pumpkin Curry soup to start, and while I don't think of Pumpkin this time of year, it really hit the spot. I followed up with Shrimp and Grits, and while I had this several times this week, this was the hands down winner. We all loved our food. Wine prices were very reasonable and really added to the experience.

And as a finale the waiter heard it was my husband's birthday (none of us told him) and brought out a Lemon Doberge Cake that was one of the best things I ever put in my mouth! I will be dreaming of that cake. But who wouldn't love a place that does that little extra to set them above other dining experiences? We'll be back...you know we will. 

If you looking for this place...don't blink. There's a small sign and doorway into the large space. Just walk on thru!

We love going to museums, but this one is extra special. 

I find this place packed with amazing collection of Mr. Cash memorabilia, instruments, costumes, awards, handwritten lyrics and other items in the best designed museum I've seen.  Heck, it even has his original Amex card!  

Self-guided museum with numerous videos playing and iPads throughout provided details on his life and his career.  The tour shows information that most people were not aware, like Mr. Cash was in the Air Force stationed in Germany in his early twenties. Although we learn about this adventure, we don't know what influence this may have had on his career. This kind of ambiguity occurs throughout the museum, so you get an informative but superficial understanding of who he was.  Maybe it was designed that way as we all know Mr. Cash was a man of mystery.  

Plan on spending some time as there is so much to see. It can get crowded especially if weather is uncooperative.  One part of the museum that caught my eye and really enjoyed was a small area where Mr. Cash is projected on a flag while he says "Ragged Ol' Flag." 

This museum sets a standard for others to live up to. Whether you're a fan of the Man in Black, or even casually interested in this American icon, this museum is a must see. 

Cafe and gift shoppe on site.  Located just off the honky tonk of Broadway Street.

"People call me wild.  Not really though, I'm not.  I guess I've never been normal, not what you call Establishment.  I'm country."  - Johnny Cash.

Finally, a Brazilian steakhouse in Tucson! But "steakhouse" is a misnomer. This is a traditional Brazilian "rodizio"... and as a frequent traveler to Brazil, I can assure you that they got this right. The owners are long-time veterans of the Fogo de Chão chain, and they know how to bring this concept off beautifully. 

If you're not familiar with it: massive salad bar -- but don't fill up on salad; that's not why you are here. Gauchos bring skewers of meat to your table until you beg for mercy. Twelve different kinds of beef, pork, lamb, chicken, and sausages. (You can also order salmon separately, if you are the pescatarian in the group. Or just the salad bar, for vegetarians. But this place is all about red meat.)

Unlike some Brazilian rodizios, this one doesn't try to fill you up on cheaper chicken and sausage before getting to the sirloin and picanha (a cut of meat you can't get at your U.S. butcher, but amazingly flavorful). No limits on side dishes: fried banana, mashed potatoes, and delightfully fluffy cheese bread. (Gluten free, made with yucca flour.)

The owners have made training the waitstaff a priority, and it shows. We received impeccable and attentive service. Pleasant modern interior, with ceilings high enough that noise isn't a problem. This is a great destination for date night, or a family celebration, or the business dinner commemorating a successful deal. 

We guessed that it would cost $60/plate, and were pleasantly surprised to find it was $40 (plus drinks, desserts, etc). Not cheap, but you should arrive hungry and will probably skip your next meal... so the price is actually reasonable. Go! You won't regret it.

The Clearwater area has been in dire need for a sushi spot like this!

This restaurant offers an excellent all you can eat sushi and hibachi menu along with plenty of appetizers and soups to choose from. For dinner the price is very reasonable at $17.95 per person and kids 4-8 are only $4.99! Can you even get a happy meal for that price? Our daughter loves sushi and Chicken Teriyaki so she was in heaven. If you aren't into sushi that's ok as you can choose from a wide array of dinner items.

Please note this is not a buffet style place like many other places in the area. You place your order from the menu they give you and then they make the items for you and bring them out. This is better as you know they are making it fresh for you and it hasn't been sitting on some warmer exposed to the public with a chance of people breathing all over it.

We went on a Monday night around 6:30 and it was nice and quiet as we were the only ones in the restaurant. The inside is very nicely decorated and doesn't quite feel like a Japanese restaurant with the tasteful decor they have.

We had a few of the rolls on the menu including Spicy Tuna and Salmon rolls along with a Mexican roll off of the standard rolls menu. Each one was amazing and you could tell everything was fresh as it melted in your mouth and the fish had no smell whatsoever. The spicy rolls are not really spicy so if you like it hot ask for it Extra Spicy to kick it up a notch.

Where the good rolls are at is in the Signature Rolls section which is included in the menu. I know some other places in Pinellas County where they charge you extra for these. We had a large variety including The Hawaii, Rainbow, Dancing Krab, Green Sarabay, Saki, Volcano and the Crunchy 2 in 1. Wow that sounds like a lot! Our favorite by far was the Volcano which was baked and topped with Krab and spicy mayo. I'm not usually a fan of cooked rolls but this was amazing. Another to recommend is the Crunchy 2 in 1. Our goal is to try every roll they have as the menu is quite extensive.

Make sure to only order what you know you will eat as they will charge you for any pieces you leave up to .75 per piece I believe.

The server was always smiling and very courteous and made us feel welcomed. By the time we left, the restaurant was starting to fill up.

This is definitely a place to try if you are into sushi and looking for an all you can eat option. The sushi is actually better than other places in the area that don't off the AYCE option.

LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION~~~ earns their stars in my eyes. Also just a few minutes before State Street. Staff is attentive and friendly, too. We were able to check in at 9AM, thankfully.  Although compared to my other Hyatt stays, this location has been the least comfortable unfortunately. Loved its location with the beach just across the street with a lifeguard post/station directly in front.
