We dined at their Bistro restaurant and food was tasty from their breakfasts to their creme brûlée dessert; even their room service late night snack (before 10pm) was enjoyable (tried their crab and artichoke dip and a cinnamon pancake for our son which he loved as well) A room fridge helped keep some snacks and drinks cool for us to enjoy later when room service wasn't available. Their literature from concierge also provided restaurants nearby and a few even delivered.  

So, why the discomfort in my stay here? I don't know if it was the air conditioner or just the beachside climate but I truly never felt dry, everything felt clammy and damp, including the bedding. When I washed my 2-piece bathing suit (not much material to dry)  it never fully dried the next day, I noticed, to give you an idea.  Second, our faucet water kept releasing this horrible smell, like raw sewage each time I went to wash my hands so at one point I just used bottled water to brush my teeth and wash my hands.  Our son kept complaining about this stench, too even when he sat 15 feet away. Just strange as our shower did not have this stench. The downside to the shower is the lack of water pressure so returning from the beach, and covered in sand, be prepared to shower for an hour or so to get rid of all the sand. Our rm was on the ground level and I could not even lock our window. Even though we have Hyatt membership levels and accommodations I don't think I would stay here again.

I don't like giving 1 star reviews, but in this case, it's warranted.  Not going to rehash the whole evening but here's why it bombed out for me.

1) The service.  While everyone was very friendly, service was slllllooooooow.  The mango lassi never came and it took an hour to get our appetizer.  When it finally did come, it was very disappointing.  

The vegetable pakora here is just chunks of deep fried veggies, mostly sliced potato and onion rings.  I wanted the dumplings, but this would have been OK if the veggies had been cooked all the way through.  The potato was still frozen\raw in the center.  

2) When dinner arrived, about 20 mins or so after the app, it was good until the second helping when a very long hair was found in the food.  And by found in the food, I mean my boyfriend actually had to spit it out.  At that point, we both lost our appetite and wanted to leave.

After discussing what happened with several people, none of whom would say whether they were a manager, and being offered free ice cream and free buffet coupons, we were given our bill with both entrees taken off (drinks and apps were still included).

This kind of thing happens sometimes, and it's unpleasant for all when it does.  It may just be a one time thing... but sometimes it only takes one bad experience to ruin a place for you.

Spent this warm MLK Holiday Sunday walking and shopping Coast Village Road Shopping District in Montecito, CA.. We were fortunate enough to come across "Here's the Scoop" Gelato Sorbet Gourmet Cafe ( x-street was Middle Rd). FABULOUS! Walking in we were greeted by Ellie Patterson (Proprietor) who thanked us for walking in and was very personable and kind. Several samples later we ordered a scoop of "Cafe Expresso" and a scoop of "Italian Chocolate Chip" gelato.
The establishment was clean and bright and located in a very modernish Sidewalk Mall. The Gelato had real "flavor"...in fact, both flavors were down-right-yummy and really refreshing. Some past Yelp Reviews mentioned the "cost" seemed expensive. Hmmm...this is Montecito right? Just walked out of a store...right down the street, looking at a Cardigan for my Spouse ($678.00) and a Sweater for my Daughter ($350.00)
THAT my fellow YELPERS was expensive! But I gladly footed the $10 dollar tag for our treat and with a smile, bid Ellie a respectful "adieu". So on this occasion, in this humble Yelper's opinion "Here's the Scoop" Gelato Sorbet Gourmet Cafe" truly earned this "right back at ya" 5 Star "highly recommend" review.

In the short amount of time we spent in Tampa, I was very selective with the places I wanted to try for lunch, dinner, dessert, etc. Revolution Ice Cream stuck out to me with their whacky ice cream names, large and in charge looking scoops, and so much personality in their interior decor. They also had great Yelp reviews to boot. But something fell short... 

The flavor just didn't match the description of the ice cream, so much that when they brought our scoops to our table, they swapped orders and we couldn't even tell until probably halfway into it - very disappointing. Ultimately the overall vibe of the place was cool, but wasn't fond of the actual ice cream. 

Other things to note: there are vegan options and cbd infused (interesting!), parking is minimal, but we had no issue finding a spot.

Before coming to Tampa, I made sure to do some research. I reached out to Tampa natives to see what they'd recommend in the area, I looked on Yelp to for the most popular spots, and I decided to go to the places that got the same votes across the board. La Teresita was one of those places that had great reviews, plus praise in word of mouth! Authentic cuban cuisine - as advertised. I ordered Ribeye Bistec with black beans and yellow rice. The flavor in the ribeye bistec made my taste buds happy dance. The yellow rice and black beans were awesome sides. However, the meat to rice ratio was incredibly off. I had plenty of rice and beans leftover, but no source of protein to eat it with. And for me, I wasn't interested in eating them by themselves. I also ordered the papaya milkshake...didn't really like it. 

Otherwise, my experience was fantastic and it was a great meal to start off the day. The meal was inexpensive as well, making it that much better. Just wish I had more meat.

The only sushi I tried in Florida! Per another Yelper's rec, I made sure to add Samurai Blue to the rotation. It's in an awesome, historical shopping strip called Centro Ybor. Some pluses: 

1. Fish was very fresh
2. Pressed sushi was amazing
3. Relatively inexpensive for 3 people (we ordered a total of 7 rolls)

Some questionable things: 
1. I think the space was being renovated, but bar seating experiences a leaky ceiling. The entire time we were eating, we were getting showered on. 
2. There was no regulation for folks who sat themselves at the bar instead of waiting for the hostess...so even though our party got to the restaurant first, this couple who came in after us sat themselves, got all their food first, and left before us...
3. Service was partially friendly

Regardless, the food was still pretty good. It gets pretty busy during dinner time if you don't make a reservation!

Arrogant manager, cerviche seafood very old and fishy. Nice surroundings, new restaurant, prices
unreasonable high for what you get but won't return as the manger was insulting and said that" cerviche isn't for everyone ". In this case it wasn't for anyone who has tastebuds. The tortilla soup tastes like barbecue and has no salt, would never order again if I was returning which I'm not.

Wow the tamales here are probably the best I've ever had in the U.S. We came here on Christmas day, looking for a delicious Mexican restaurant that was open during the holidays. When we walked in, we were immediately seated and served tortilla chips with green and red salsa. We ordered four tamales first, which were made of pork and red sauce. They were so delicious and appetizing! I'm from LA and they have a ton of Mexican restaurants there but the tamales here are just so much better. 

We also ordered a bunch of other food since we were hungry. First, the steak quesadilla was great and it had a ton of cheese and steak inside. It was topped with lettuce, sour cream, and pico de gallo. The cubano sandwich was awesome and super flavorful. It had breaded fried chicken, eggs with sausage, ham, lettuce, tomatoes, sour cream, and avocados. It's a gigantic sandwich that can easily feed two people. Last but not least, I got the sopes (two pork and one beef), which were topped with lettuce, cheese, sour cream and more. All the dishes here are very traditional and authentic, and it totally satisfied my love of Mexican food!

Vegan Gumbo? Yes, please!

I was seated at a table with fresh cut flowers right next to a window that looked onto Chartres street; I could also see parts of Saint Louis Cathedral and Jackson square. A lovely rose scent traveled through the air in slow motion and I got a whiff, from time to time, from the flowers that were on my table (a centerpiece for all the tables), which was nice. I took a peek at their menu ahead of time so I knew that they served vegan gumbo and that was top on my list of things to try. I came here for a spot of lunch.

Louisianians seem to love their gumbo; gumbo is a strongly-flavored stock, hearty, warming, and rich. In this instance it was vegetable stock and also meat-free. It usually comes in a bowl as it is quite similar to soup and typically always served over rice. From what I gathered it is a tradition staple in regards to traditional food and It fits right in with the melting-pot nature of Louisiana cooking. I have tried gumbo many years ago. This is merely a prelude to my take on vegan gumbo. 

My food arrived shortly after ordering and I had to let it cool for a moment as it was piping hot. Water was my beverage of choice. Once the gumbo cooled down a bit I took a spoonful and it was delicious. The flavors were impeccable and I appreciated their spin with vegan gumbo; keep in mind it is a little thicker than regular soups. It had fresh seasonal veggies, scallions and all on a bed of traditional steamed rice. It warmed me up so nicely on a chilly day and a perfect dish for gumbo adventures.

Friendly vibes and good service. 

PreCOVID

TIPS
It is in close proximity to Jackson square,  
The Original Cafe Du Monde, and Washington artillery park.

Open Thursday to Sunday 8am to 4pm
(Always a good idea to double check, especially during COVID)

No reservations 

FUN FACTS:

A quaintessential New Orleans restaurant experience.

Buena Onda is located in Santa Barbara and it is famed for their traditional Argentinian empanadas. You know...empanadas... a fried turnover pastry with sweet or savory filling. Well I got wind that they had a few vegan options, which gave me all the more reason to swing by. I arrived during the evening and when you walk in you can almost taste them in the air. There were two people ahead of me and a few behind me. I had already placed an order over the phone so once it was my turn I simply said the magic words and paid my bill. 

The options were vegana quinoa (peppers, spinach, quinoa, and vegan cream cheese) and Hakuna Batata (shallot, sweet potato yam, and spinach)--I ordered both. They also have meat empanadas and they are all oven baked to order. Both were quite delicious but of the two the Hakuna Batata stole the show--it means no worries, am I right or am I right? My order came with a herb/grassy olive oil dressing for the empanadas which was nice and I was quite full once I finished my meal. They have outdoor seating and twinkle lights for an elegant look. 

What I love about them is that they are authentic and organic. Their dough and fillings are housemade. You can purchase in bulk or family meals for a better deal. They also have frozen empanadas that you can take home and cook at your leisure. They even serve soups, salads, and desserts. After a few years the secret is out fresh and bake to order empanadas right here in sunny Santa Barbara. Thank you for making the world a little more wonderful. 


Covid compliant

Uh-oh.  Um.  Wow.  Okay, let's start here: I've been waiting two years to write this review.  Why?  Every single time I go to Loquita my experience is moving and I haven't been able to put my finger on why...until now.

To tell of this transcendence requires delicacy and time, something few have these days.  If you are in a hurry I encourage read another review.  If you want to join me on an all-encompassing journey through the truly unimaginable, nearly indescribable, experience that is a dinner at Loquita...then let's jump in.

It's a Wednesday night and you want to make Friday night plans with friends.  Great idea!  You start thinking about where you could go, what vibe you are looking for: Bar scene?  Sit-down?  Street food?  Pizza?  Then it hits you, "Oh...or we could go to Loquita."  You start thinking about the cocktails, the shared plates, the Paella... Three minutes later you find yourself sitting in the same spot, staring at the same place on the wall, feeling warm, content, like everything is right in the world.  The decision is made.  You call and make a reservation.  Because you've put your name in a few days early, there is an open table for four.

You wake up Thursday morning and can't shake Loquita; the thought of it enhances  your day.

7pm on Friday comes around.  The host walks you inside and you teleport to a different country: Spain.  The design and attention to detail is phenomenal.  The countertops were custom built and installed by local craftsman.  The tile-work, timeless.  The lighting, perfect ambiance.

Because of COVID you can't sit inside, which you are fine with because every table outside is either next to a fireplace or a heater, and the vibe is just as perfect.

You are seated and the staff explains the menu, the hand-crafted cocktails inspired by the bar manager's travels through Europe, the tapas (shared plates), the paella...the paella, the harmony of everything good in the world (we'll get there).

The cocktail menu isn't overwhelming and is well balanced.  Some smokey, some sweet, some fruity.  You find something just right for you but you need clarification on an ingredient.  Turns out the Vermut has been mixed with something beautiful to create a foam that is applied to the drink as it is served (see photos of the Maravilloso in the following images).  Your eyes grow large and the words, "I'll take it," barely escape your mouth.

Your friends order different and equally wonderful sounding drinks which the waiter, at your request, has meticulously described and recommended as pairing well with your tapas.

Oh...the tapas.  The shared plates.  The flavors.  Spices. Meats. Veggies. Texture. Color. Beauty.  You decide on 3 or 4 tapas (food is always served with a utensil for sanitary distribution but sometimes we can't help ourselves and dive head first onto the plate of mushrooms (see the photo of the champiñones).

Speaking of mushrooms, I actually teared up at the taste of one of Loquita's mushroom dishes a year ago and not because of a memory/nolstalgia/spice/onions being cut nearby.  No, I was truly moved by the experience of tasting such a delicious, well balanced, thoughtful, piece of food.  I will never forget it.

The tapas are brought out and served.  The ingredients and cooking processes are explained to you in a way that brings you into each dish, highlighting each bite you take, making you conscious of each flavor and the time put into the experience happening to your taste buds and nostrils.

After three tapas with varying degrees of adventurous flavor, shared amoungst you and your friends, it comes time for the Paella.  The Paella, whether veggie, chicken, prawn and short rib, or marine inspired, doesn't matter.  They are all mind-bending, and for their own unique reasons.  The smell of the paella, the presentation, the temperature, the texture, the taste, all combined, create a unique and immersive experience into a traditional culture that is unparalleled by any other restaurant in Santa Barbara.  Your heart skips a beat with every bite...you know your life will be different from here on out.  You have just experienced one of the best dinner dishes of your life.

Dessert?  You and friends know there is some room to spare.  You look at the menu.  You ask the waiter their recommendation.  After trying 4 or 5 different dishes (tapas and paella) you know you can't go wrong...so you order one of each plate.  Your taste buds know the end is coming, when the last bite of grainless chocolate cake (see photos) disappears from the plate.

You all sit there, speechless.  3 hours have gone by that felt like 30 minutes.  You've laughed, you've teared up, you've had good conversations, hard conversations, you've gotten to know the people around you in a new way.  Loquita has given you more than good food, it's given you connection.  Connection the people around you, to a cuisine seldom experienced, to the present moment.  It will move you.  Receive it with open hands.

I've always considered myself to be better than homeless people.  

The list of my superiorities is so extensive that I almost don't even know where to start.  My style is more sophisticated, my palate is more refined, my book collection is more impressive, my hygiene is far superior, and, most obviously, I have an actual home.  

Last Friday, as I was leap-frogging over a bum who had the gall to lay lengthwise across the sidewalk, I found myself marveling at the extreme disparity between my fabulousness and his patheticness.  How could two of God's children, cut from the same cloth, be so damn different?  

I'm generally not one for comparative analysis, but let's call a spade a spade.  It's fairly evident that I'm far more advanced than my shoeless brethren and, as a result, I've never found us to have much in common.  

Well, that's all changed with the arrival of this lovely Spring weather.  

Turns out, we share a deep-seated passion for one of the greatest hobbies ever invented.  

Drinking in the park.  

I love it.  For my life, it doesn't get any better than to gather with friends in Rittenhouse to drink beers out of paper cups, catch some rays, and have some laughs.  This has gradually become something of a Sunday tradition.  There's literally no greater way to reclaim the weekend and ensure maximum utilization of your meager 48 hours of freedom.

When we're hankering for cold, crisp brews in the park on a warm, sunny day, we always go to Food and Friends to select from their spectacular collection of beers.  While the options tend to run on the pricey side, it's all well worth it.  As the gray-heads are wont to say, you get what you pay for.  

While I don't mind spending nearly $4 for a Flying Dog Double Dog Double Pale Ale (11.4% ABV), it does render the price of a six pack exorbitant and I understand that most people don't want to lace it out in this fashion.  Given the downtrodden state of our economy, I know that everyone's looking for a deal and, in my opinion, the best buy currently running at Food and Friends is Old Dominion's Spring Buck Blonde Ale.  With 7.8% ABV, tremendous taste, and a price tag of a mere $2.19 per bottle, you can't beat it.

So despite my initial speculation, it would appear that I do share something with the shiftless lay-abouts running rampant in Rittenhouse.  And while I may opt for the North Coast Brewing Company's Pranqster Belgian Style Golden Ale (7.6% ABV) instead of a plastic pint of Bankers' Club, our intent is clearly the same...to enjoy the weather, take the edge off, and bask in the heart-warming glow of our fellow man.

Lolita is one of the top BYO's in the city and arguably the best sit-down, date-night, high-class, restaurant-style Mexican around.

The quality of the food sets Lolita well above the rest of its competitors.  It exposes Tequila's canned refried beans and bland dishes as the dog food that it truly is.  I had never had great Mexican in a formal setting until I had Lolita.  

The carne asada a la Lolita is king of the castle.  The beef was cooked to perfection and the diverse array of flavors were combined in such a manner as to render subtle otherwise dominant ingredients.  It was a pleasure to eat...almost orgasmic at times.  Unparalleled in Philadelphia.  I nearly fell out of my seat when I took my first bite.

Regrettably, a black cloud hangs heavy over Lolita - the $18 per person minimum.  Aside from being tacky, it's not properly enforced.  Such an archaic requirement should not be implemented in a dialectic nature.   It's not black or white.  They need to provide for some situational gray-area.  

Allow me to expand.  A new friend of mine had originally planned to meet up with our crew after dinner for a party, but he happened to be in the neighborhood, so we told him swing on by to have a drink.  There were three of us at a four person table.  A seat sat empty, waiting to be filled.  I knew of the $18 rule as I had already bored my dining mates with a lengthy rant regarding the outmoded nature of minimum requirements.  We had eaten our appetizers and our entrees had been served.  We still had plenty of tequila left that we were determined to finish and his services were required if we were to ever complete the task at hand.  I figured I'd invite him in, what's the big deal?  He may not order food but we are certainly going to have to get some more mixers to accommodate his arrival.  Would the waitress rather the chair sat empty and we didn't order more Margarita mix?  Sadly, the answer turned out to be yes...

It was a cold evening, so our aforementioned friend was bundled to the gills.  Looking like Ralphie's little brother, he trundled in and began the laborious disrobing process.  He's a terrific guy, but not the most fashion forward and certainly not the most coordinated.  Needless to say, it was a bit of a scene as he bumbled around, grunted, and cursed his inability to unzip his jacket (I kindly suggested he remove his gloves first) ala Ignatius J. Reilly.  The entire time, the waitress watched him like a hawk watches an injured rabbit...menu in hand, ready to pounce the instant he got settled.  Literally, one second after he sat, closed his eyes to collect himself, and exhaled a sigh of relief, the waitress shoved a menu in his face.  

"What'll you have?" she squawked in an openly confrontational tone.  

"Ah, I'm actually just going to have some drinks.  We're on our way to a festive bonanza momentarily, but first, there are Margaritas to be crushed and I'm just the guy to do it," he replied in a jocular manner.  Being the friendly, unassuming gentleman that he is, he had failed to detect the venom dripping from her fangs...she was daring him to defy the $18 minimum.  She was reveling in her knowledge of what was about to go down.

"Well, I'm really sorry, but you're going to have to leave.  We have an $18 minimum per guest," she hissed through clenched teeth...fake smile threatening to tear her cheeks asunder.  

We were floored.  Really?  You can't be serious, Flo.  The seat is empty, unused, wasted.  Furthermore, we're almost done eating and we're going to order more mixers for him!  What gives?  I briefly considered protesting, but her wrinkled brow and hands-on-hips stance told me it would be nothing but an exercise in futility.

Embarrassed and chagrined, I apologized to my friend as he rose to his feet to begin reassembling his wintry armor.  As you can imagine, this was another task of monumental proportions, the entire time all eyes in the restaurant were on him as he dressed in shame.  He slunk out, head hung low...rejected, dejected, humiliated. 

It was absurd and I was infuriated.  What a dope she was.  We paid our bill and high-tailed it out of there.  The negative vibes were threatening to kill the evening.  We gathered our friend from some sad, lonely street corner, wiped the tear from his eye, and moved on to greener, more welcoming pastures.  

I love Lolita's food so much that I will give them four stars for their domination in this arena, but I've yet to return.  I will one day, I just don't know when.  

You can't rationalize the irrational.

I was running a little late for brunch a few weeks ago.  The previous evening had been exceedingly brutal and I had the headache to prove it.  Pulling my torn and tattered corpse from the comfort of my bed had been a monumental exercise in pain.

I had no memories; all that remained was an empty wallet, a complimentary admission pass to the Gold Club, and a receipt from the Pen and Pencil.  Nothing but ragged reminders of a terrible, horrible, no-good, booze fueled night of debauchery.  My sense of regret was palpable.  I'm definitely too old for this nonsense, but here I am again, proclaiming this to be the final straw.  They say that repetition of abnormal or destructive behaviors is a sign of mental illness.  If this is the case, then I need a serious evaluation.

As my inner dialogue spiraled down into the depths of a Jungian nightmare, my only glimmer of hope was the feeling that perhaps a light-hearted brunch with some decent, manner-born friends could wipe the stale taste of shame from my palette.  Noble American Cookery had been proposed and I'm mildly invigorated at the prospect of adding a new breakfast spot to the repertoire as I was beginning to tire of the usual haunts.

A wave of anxiety washes over me when I pass John's Books causing flashbacks of late night whippet runs and threatening to quell my slowly improving disposition.  However, once I turn the corner onto Sansom, all is forgotten and I remember how much I like this block.  Quaint, but harboring some serious fire power beneath the surface of its unassuming façade - Vic, Porcini, Village Whiskey, Tinto.  

Noble looks impressive from the outside.  Hip, clean, simple.  Just what I need.  Several of my friends are huddled around a table towards the front engaged in a heated debate regarding topics that I'm certain have little merit.  All are well-dressed.  Mr. Fox, apparently in a sporting mood, even went so far as to wear a tie.  A little over the top in my opinion, especially considering he's also wearing loafers with bare feet, but I feel good about my decision to wear the houndstooth blazer and even better about my argyle socks.  

A loud grumble from my gut announces my presence and I realize that I'm absolutely famished as I take my seat. 

Opening the menu, I'm taken aback by what I find.  It reads like a listing at Dorsia, circa 1988.  Decadent culinary concoctions abound.  Fruits mixed with meats mixed with grains mixed with vegetables.  SNAFU.  Apple punishing omelet, beet suffocating burger, tangerine brutalizing char, grapefruit defiling duck, parsnip molesting skate - the bizarre musings of a Danceteria cowboy.  Where am I and how did I get here?  This is not my beautiful house.  This is not my beautiful wife.
 
I order the burger, hoping the grease can wrestle my flip-flopping stomach into submission.  I'm careful to politely insist that my burger be served beet free.  The beet invasion of 2k9 is in full force and I want no part of this central European plague.  Doesn't seem to be an issue and the burger arrives promptly.  

Frankly, it's amazing.  The bun is lightly toasted to perfection, the burger is well cooked, the special sauce is incredible and it's managed to erase all vestiges of last night's insanity from my memory banks.  Consider me a huge fan.  

My appetite satisfied, I can't help but feel infuriated.  Why do they ruin their delicious food with absurd flavor pairings?  Who needs uniqueness when you have quality?  Let the food speak for itself.  Do your thing and keep it simple.  I'll be back, but I'll definitely be special ordering despite the fact that this social transgression is one of my most intense pet peeves.  Hate to be that guy but there's no way I'm eating beets on my burger.  It's treasonous at the very least.  A man's got to take a stand every once in a while.

The bill comes and it's time to pay.  As my friend reaches for his money clip, I spot a Gold Club complimentary admission card...at least I wasn't the only one.

With a staunch, well-documented history of heterosexuality behind me, I feel proud to say that I am a huge fan of Tavern on Camac.  

I'll never forget my first foray into this intense world of mirrored dance floors, Britney remixes, unisex bathrooms, pint glasses of Red Bull Vodka, and dudes.  It was an eye-opening experience.

Most straight guys are missing the point when it comes to gay bars.  They tend to fixate on the superficial, while totally missing out on some real opportunities to rock.  Get over yourself.  You have got to get up to get down.  It's a simple mathematic equation.  

There are TWO fundamental rules that all straight men must abide whilst visiting the Tavern in order to fully maximize their experience:

1)  Don't be afraid.  You will get hit on, that much is guaranteed.  The quarters are tight and there's nowhere to hide.  In fact, although it may seem counterintuitive, the straighter you act, the more suitors you will attract.  I suppose you're viewed as a challenge, a latent ball of homosexuality just begging for a special boy to bring it to the surface.  While we all know this isn't true, you should take advantage of this false belief.  

Instead of being offended when a tiny little man in a tight v-neck tee, True Religion jeans, an out of season tan, and an impeccable complexion approaches you to talk about football, embrace the opportunity.  Live in the moment.  Accept the drink that he has offered to buy you.  If you can simply maintain conversation, that one drink may turn into two drinks which may turn into three drinks...all for free.  Think straight dudes.  How many dollars have you spent in your life buying drinks for girls at bars?  How significant of a return on investment have you seen from those dollars?  Generally speaking, I'd be willing to bet it's pretty low.  So why not recoup some of those sunk costs?  Why not get yours?  Shed your antiquated inhibitions.  It's your turn to feel pretty.  It's your turn to feel special.  It's your turn to feel wanted...sigh!  At Tavern on Camac, for once in my life, I could keep my wallet in my pocket, sit back, and enjoy an evening of lively chatter and free booze.  Take...Ad...Vantage.

2)  Keep your head on a swivel.  While it's fun to get free drinks, it gets a little old as the night draws closer to last call.  At some point, you will have had your fill of dudes night out.  And herein lies the magic of the gay club - a secret fact of life that most of my straight friends are hesitant to believe, but are quick to embrace once they bear witness to this amazing phenomenon.  In Philadelphia, gay bars are the best place to pick up chicks.  

Now wait wait wait.  Take it easy over there.  Allow me to explain.  Every weekend, girls get together with their pack and head out looking for fun.  Invariably, they end up at the same old bars getting hit on by same old guys.  It's gets tiresome.  They need a change of pace.  So what do they do?  They call their gay friend and they set up the classic - GIRLS NIGHT OUT!  "Whoooo...it's going to be great.  We'll hit the gay bar and dance the night away without having to fear the shady, straight guy, back-end, sneak attack on the dance floor!"

They get all dolled up, they meet up with their gay friend, and do just as they planned.  No straight guys, just girls and gays having fun.  They are easy to spot, dancing in a herd in a circle around their one gay buddy.  That is until midnight hits.  They've had some drinks, they're starting to feel good, and all of a sudden, they realize, they might actually want to meet a nice guy.  You can literally see this switch flip in their brain as they start to frantically scan the dance floor for anything even slightly resembling a straight man.

Well, when that happens, if you're the only straight guy in the gay bar, you start to look pretty damn good.  You have no competition at all.  You could be the biggest loser on the face of the planet, but if you're in the right place at the right time, you could be getting your swerve on.   It's a good thing to be a big fish in a small pond.  Furthermore, it's such a liberating feeling to be able to meet the young ladies without any interference from spiky haired dorks in their t-shirt and blazer combo ala Ryan Seacrest circa 2K5.  The fact is, you can't compete with these tools because they have no sense of shame, so why even try?  Go gay bar and avoid the competition all together!

Most guys don't realize this aspect of the Tavern.  They shy away for no good reason at all.  As a result, they are seriously missing out.  To all my straight men out there, get on over to Tavern, drink for free, and meet some chicks.  Doesn't get any more hetero than that.  

My only word of warning would be to avoid feeding the bears on the first floor.  They're an aggressive bunch and often known for their frugality.  No free drinks here.  Just lots of burly man hugs.

My lady friend loves me.  How do I know?  She treated me to Mercato for my birthday last month. 

Mercato is the best overall BYO in Philadelphia.  Now that I've written it, feel free to state it as fact.  I will accept no arguments to the contrary because they are inherently flawed.  It's literally impossible to disagree with my assessment.

I ordered the Grilled Petit Tender Filet.  $25.  Beef Consommé, red bliss potatoes, brussel sprouts, smoked bacon.  Cooked to perfection.  Incredible price point.  Large portions.  Comfort food doesn't get any better than this. 

A debate between archaeologists, historians, and anthropologists has raged for years regarding the catalyst behind the shockingly accurate premonitions of the Pythia at the Oracle of Delphi.  How could they know the future?  What could possibly trigger their vivid hallucinations?  Nerds say it's ethylene gas emanating from the earth beneath the Oracle.  Dreamers claim that it's pure, unadulterated divine inspiration.  I think they're both wrong and my hypothesis has the potential to shake the conventional wisdom to its core.  

The Oracular Statements of Delphi are clearly the result of the mind-altering aromas that wafted up from my Filet masterpiece.  I didn't see Mackenzie Hilton, but I'm almost certain that she is the reincarnation of Aeschylus, brought back to spread the ancient joys of Gaia throughout the modern world.  Upon reaching my olfactory receptors, the vapors drove me into a trance-like state, not unlike a coma.  My girlfriend said I looked like a junkie on Intervention after a nice, fat shot of heroin.  I slumped over in my chair...inert...dead to the world.

However, while my body languished, my mind exploded with glorious visions of the divine and the improbable.  There I sat for a thousand years, a bucket of water resting precariously atop the Great Wall of China until a nomadic Giant came along and poured me out.  As I splashed across the stone and mortar, the droplets of water constituting my essence shattered into an infinite number of stars that laughed and sang their way into the nether regions of the universe...It was a spirit quest of the highest order.  If only I could find Don Juan, I could piece together the puzzle that is my being.  Alas, he is dead.  Oh well.

When I came to there was a pool of drool collecting on my sweater and my lady friend was frantically digging through her purse in pursuit of a cell phone with which to call 9-1-1.

Thank God she didn't or I wouldn't have had a chance to eat.  And oh boy did I eat...voraciously!  Like my yokel South Carolina cousins after a long day on the farm, I tore into my dish is if it were my last meal on earth.  Every successive bite was better than the last.  

By the time I finished I was fully satiated and depressed.  Like the end of a great book or an engrossing movie, I couldn't believe it was over already.  I will be back...if I can ever get a seat again!

Best Tomato Bisque in the city.  Best Tomato Bisque anywhere.  I challenge you to try it and disagree with my assessment.  One sip and you'll be hooked...guaranteed.  If it wasn't so cliché, I'd insinuate that the Bisque was spiked with crack cocaine and formed the lynchpin of some CIA driven plot to bring down the Fitler Square Yuppie community.  People turning tricks for Bisque?  Try it and tell me it couldn't happen.  I dare you!

If you don't fall head over heels in love with this Bisque, then there's something wrong with you and I'd encourage you to consult your primary care physician as soon as possible.  

In fact, the only plausible explanation for an unenthusiastic response to the Bisque has to be some sort of deep-seated hatred of the French.  I mean, I get it.  They're ungrateful for all we've done for them, they get 6 months of vacation a year, they don't work then complain about not working, Sarkozy's wife is way too hot for a first lady, and Proust is a god-awful bore, but you really shouldn't hold any of this against the Bisque, so get over it.

The intense cravings brought on by the Bisque can best be described by a short story.  

It was pleasant fall Sunday, circa 2K8.  A dear friend of mine invited me to lunch at Café Lutecia.  I had never been, it was close to my house, and he'd been raving non-stop about a Tomato Bisque for the past four months, so I was understandably curious.  By all means, I said.  Let us go.  

We made the short walk to Lutecia and were fortunate to sneak into an outside table moments before a crowd of 20 bumbling Penn students arrived (as a side note, this species has since disappeared from the neighborhood thanks to the bridge construction so they are no longer a concern).  

I was comfortable, menu looked strong...life was good by all accounts.  That is, until the waitress came out and boldly announced that there was but one Bisque remaining.

The music stopped.  My friend turned his head so quickly to gauge my reaction that I could literally hear his neck muscles creak and his brain slosh against his skull.  His eyes blazed with a feverish insanity of an intensity that I had only seen one time prior in the eyes of a crazed Czech drunk on murky wormwood and anti-American rhetoric.  

His look said quite clearly so as to leave no room for confusion - "I found this place, I allowed you to come here, you would have never heard of the Tomato Bisque were it not for me, so stand down, back off, and be grateful for your Lentil Soup.  If your mouth even so much as begins to form the O necessary to pronounce TO-mato, I will flip this table, tear you limb from limb, and be forced to enjoy my Bisque amidst the ruins of your mangled corpse."

Needless to say, I ate Lentils, he ate Bisque and all was well in the universe.  It wasn't until a full month later when I was finally fortunate enough to savor the nectar of the Gods that is, Café Lutecia's Tomato Bisque.  

Go to Lutecia, order the Bisque, become the heart of D'Artagnan, and swim in delirium.

I never had friends before I found Fish.  I used to slob around in my one-piece, footie style pajamas on Friday nights watching Full House re-runs while shoveling Ben & Jerry's into my face with my bare hands pining for the days when TGIF was king.  

It was a sad scene.  Sometimes, I wouldn't even turn the television on.  I'd just sit there in the dark, desperately trying to imagine what all the other people my age were doing at 11 pm on a Friday night.  What did they have that I didn't?  How were they able to mingle so effortlessly?  

This answer proved to be perpetually elusive.  For years, I spent weekends wallowing in a pool of my own self-pity.  My brother would often advise me to turn to drugs or alcohol.  "You're a loser," he'd say.  "Just accept it and forget it."  Sadly, I wasn't nearly cool enough to buy drugs and the guy at the liquor store didn't believe my ID was real.  I was trapped.  Alone, sober, and pathetic, I was destined to live and die in ambiguity.

 But the gods took pity on my forsaken soul and saw fit to open Fish less than a block from my den of depression.  Like the bronze plaque at the Statue of Liberty, the clap board sign advertising their late night, weekend happy hour (11 pm - 1 am), beckoned to me.  "Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free..."  Yes, yes, finally...respite!  And like a moth to a flame, I couldn't resist.  

From the moment, I crossed the threshold into the stylish bar complimented by the clean, open kitchen, I knew that I had found the rock that would give me the strength I needed to branch out.  To make friends.  To live!

The Fish Happy Hour is unparalleled.  Forget about $2 PBR.  That doesn't happen here.  This is a happy hour for adults, complete with a custom menu.  $3 dollar, top line beer (UFO, Yards, etc); $5 cocktails (pisco sours, margaritas); $3 oyster/vodka shooters (spicy & cool); $5 food menu.  It literally doesn't get better than this.  They've managed to find the perfect blend of value and quality in a sophisticated environment.  Of all the places I've been in Philadelphia, this is my favorite spot to lounge with a great group of friends. 

Now I have more friends than I know what to do with.  I've signed up for The Facebook and I'm doing just fine.  No more nights with Carl Winslow for this boy.  

If you ever want to hang out on weekend evenings, you know where to find me.  In the back lounge at Fish, laughing with friends, drinking delicious cocktails, enjoying the impeccable service, and reveling in the classic ambiance.

I have heard about this spot for a long while. Even backed their Kickstarter. Today was the first day I had the chance to actually go in and try it. Visiting Reno after moving to Washington, it was in my list of places to go. 
This place is awesome. Walking in everyone is super friendly and welcoming. We got the cardamom latte, Turkish tea, and four Turkish delights. We tried the sour lemon and the rose and pistachio ones. Also with a drink they bring you a piece. I got the macadamia nut one and he got the rose. Both were excellent. The tea was steeped perfectly. No too bitter and there was a lot of it. The latte had great flavors and it was just a nice relaxing morning. 
The delights were so good. Chewy, flavorful and awesome. I am torn to choose a favorite. I loved the sour lemon one because it had the sour bites and sweet notes but not too sweet and the pistachio rose one. They were just so good, hard to choose. 
The atmosphere is welcoming and everyone there kept checking to make sure everything was good and to see if we needed something. I will definitely be back. I also bought a Turkish loose leaf tea to bring home and share. They are awesome and I am so glad it seems like they are doing well with all the covid restrictions.

It took me a really long time to work up the desire to write this review because I enjoyed Bibou so much it felt terrible to speak badly about this restaurant...

Anyway, boyfriend and I were invited here by our other couple friend for our regular double date nights. This is the same couple that introduced us to Bibou and a few other fantastic eateries in Philadelphia. We went sometime during the grand opening month, so perhaps they've improved since. 

Le Chéri is roomier and has very beautiful ambiance as compared to Bibou's cramped yet intimate setting. 
In short, the food was decent. Not the greatest I ever had for the price that I paid. I believe boyfriend got lamb and I got the special for the night - dry aged steak. Our dinner mates got scallops and dry aged steak as well. 

The two dishes came and were served to the appropriate guest and our two dry aged steaks were brought out and cut table side. My friend received his steak first and as it was being served to him I noticed it looked more medium as opposed to rare, as he enjoys his steaks rare. I comment and say perhaps our steaks got mixed up. They switch and give me his steak which was still too over cooked for my liking but I didn't want to cause problems. They then cut open the second steak and it looked even more well done than the first steak. Since we aren't high maintenance, we would've just sucked it up and ate it anyway but the waiter removes my plate from on front of me, takes the second steak away as well and holds it right up to his face into the light and exclaims that "no, the second steak is more red... SEE?!?!" And pushes the plates into my friend's face, pointing at the two overcooked steaks (for our likings) with the knife. We nod, smile and say "ok just place them back down I'm sure they will taste amazing." 

Dinner continues and little things start to bother me..... The servers are a little confused and I'm watching them as they move throughout the space and it didn't look like there was a proper flow to the service. Granted, I'm not that high maintenance but if I'm told to expect greatness in a Rittenhouse restaurant (since Bibou received four bells in the Inquire) with these prices, I have higher expectations. The servers were slow on refills on water/drinks and then as I continue eating I notice too much juice running from my steak - from my knowledge, dry aged steaks aren't supposed to have that much run off especially since it was cut prior to being placed onto my plate. Regardless, my friend finished his steak off by himself and I eat most of it myself as well. 
Fast forward to the end and the bill arrives. We notice $45 each for four steaks, totaling $180 just for steaks. I mention to the server that we ordered two steaks, not four, and they proceeded to tell us that it is $45 per person, as each order of the steak is meant to be shared for two people. So, my friend who finished a whole steak by himself that THE RESTAURANT deemed MEANT to serve two people, that didn't actually do so and pricing that wasn't mentioned during the "specials speech," cost $90. For like.. A 32oz steak. Ridiculous. "Meant to serve" isn't the same as "plate sharing" so this place must be out of their mind, especially with a place literally right across the street (that has received 5 stars from me...Which is a feat in itself) that has real dry aged steaks ranging from $40-$60 each steak, not this ridiculousness.

The steak tartare was fantastic, though. Probably the best in the city, so they've got that going for them.

Atmosphere: The ambience of this restaurant is enjoyable, the interior designing is creative and different. The restaurant has a vintage country cabin feel with modern upgrades. You don't see a lot of that in Florida and especially in Tampa. I have to say this is the biggest restaurant I've been to in Tampa and I have been to many restaurants all over the Bay Area. It's connected to the convention center which I thought was going to be annoying and a problem to get to but there's a parking area directly in front of it and they offer valet for a small charge. 

Food: The food items that I had on the menu were very delicious, prices are a little expensive very similar to fine dining prices. I really enjoyed their roasted gulf oysters and oysters aren't a food item I typically order. I'm very picky with where I eat them due to the lack of freshness but the bartender Linda recommended them, and they were some of the best oysters I've ever had, and I've aten oysters fresh out of the ocean. 

Service: I sat at the bar one because the set up of the bar is comfy and casual and two because all the tables were giving me anxiety, when I tell you this place is big, it's BIG. There has to be hundreds of tables (lol). The downstairs bar is really awesome because there's a vintage truck that sits directly in the middle and holds all of the liquor, gave me Nashville feels but I decided to sit upstairs because I wanted an elevated view and I was not disappointed! I had the pleasure of having Bartender Linda take care of me and she was so full of energy and wanted to make my dining experience great which I feel has been a problem lately which a lot of good restaurants so it was really refreshing to have someone give me their full attention. Overall I had a great experience and if you ever decide to go sit at the Bar ask for Linda, she was great!

Cactus Creek Prime Steakhouse Pros

Management needs to address the lack of consistency in good Customer Service and cleanliness.  Mostly Customer Service and cleanliness are adequate, sometimes not-so-adequate.

If it wasn't for the second-hand cigarette smoke, I'd give it 4 stars for, Yeah, I'm a fan.

I found Juicy's Giant Hamburgers to have taken the pledge To Leave No Veteran Behind.   They are above-average with product and customer service.  They are a Veteran-Friendly business with a Veterans / Military Discount.  They are accommodating to we disabled Veterans for our Special-Needs due to our military service connected disabled disabilities, especially in their adhering to the ADA laws about us bringing our service dog into the business.  The place was clean, including the bathroom.  We saw that the staff there did wash their hands after handling money.   We ordered to-go.  The Cheeseburger and BLT with no fries for each of us, and the strawberry shake only our toddler granddaughter wanted, were pronounced satisfactory by all.  At 16 oz, the shake was more than she could consume all at once, so half was eaten later as she gets a big kick out of putting half into the freezer at home, then being reminded a week or so later it's there, pulling it out, watching it defrost and then eating it with a spoon.  It's the simple pleasures.

In 1986, Al "Bags" Norman opened a little hole-in-the-wall barbecue spot in the Silver State Shopping Center at Prater and McCarran in Sparks. It sat about 35 people comfortably (most customers took their food to go), and quickly developed a loyal following for the delicious barbecue.

BJ's Nevada Barbecue Company won Best Sauce at the "Best in the West" Rib Cook-Off in 1991.  In 1995, it moved to a former burger shop on the other end of the plaza that had double the seating and a bigger kitchen.  

In 2011, BJ's purchased the building at 80 E Victorian Ave (previously an IHOP, and before that, a Bob's Big Boy).  They remodeled the entire building and it opened in Spring of 2012, under the name Hog Wild Cafe, serving breakfast and lunch.  A year later, the two restaurants merged and you can now enjoy their breakfast, lunch, and dinner.  And, boy, did we enjoy it.  So do many others.  It has won awards 7 times at the "Best in the West" Rib Cookoff.

BJ's lovingly grinds its own burgers by hand, lovingly grinds and stuffs its own sausage, and lovingly makes their own gravy, sauces and biscuits.  The really good taste of the food here reflects it.  We went with to-go as the place was full, had a waiting line, and we had a young grandchild with us who is always hungry.  I and a daughter shared the Skillet Scramble; four farm-fresh eggs scrambled together with beef brisket, onions and tomatoes.  Yummy.   Husband and a son shared the Rib Eye Steak and Eggs which is a 10 oz. USDA choice rare steak with two farm-fresh eggs cooked to sunny-side up with toast.  The grandson with us had the One-One-One; 1 egg fried break the yolk, 1 piece of bacon and a cup of their homemade applesauce.

The wait staff was courteous, efficient and accommodating to our military service disabilities.  The place was clean.

I found BJ's Nevada Barbecue to be above-average with product, average with customer service, and to be a Veteran-Friendly business with a Veterans / Military Discount and accommodating to we disabled Veterans for our Special-Needs due to our military service connected disabled disabilities.

We hadn't been to the Nugget since 2013, when The Ascuaga Family, another victim of The Great Recession, announced bitter-sweetly that it had sold the family business then being run by John Ascuaga's daughter Michonne. Today, all that glitters is not gold. After our recent visit, we won't be back. We found it to be now corporate owned and run, impersonal, not-welcoming, cold, and not locally owned and operated.  We found no charm, no warmth, no decent customer service, and no adequate food let alone exemplary food. They're so damn corporate greed now, it's only Tuesdays and Sundays for local advantage rewards club members getting the 2-for-1 buffet, not valid on holidays. We found today's Nugget was not Veteran Friendly to us. They were not Disabled Friendly to us.  They were not Family Friendly to us. They were not Gaming Friendly to us. They were not Senior Friendly to us. From the behaviors we routinely witnessed of its employees, no pride in their work, they are not Employee Friendly. Overall, the place was not clean. We were left saddened at the changes in our old beloved friend. The nine scariest words are, I'm from a corporation and I'm here to help, as they mean help the corporate executives not the customers, employees or community. Our recent trip to the Rotisserie Buffet reminded us that the army from Asia introduced a foreign luxury to Rome; it was then the meals began to require more dishes and more expenditure . . . the cook, who had up to that time been employed as a slave of low price, become dear: what had been nothing but a métier was elevated to an art.  Restaurants that know and practice the difference between a cook and a Chef are a satisfying delight.  We found no satisfying delights here.

A member of The Greatest Generation, after an Honorable Discharge from the United States Army, John Ascuaga, also a twin, used his G.I. Bill at the University of Idaho for his Bachelor's Degree in Accounting and then Washington State University for an additional Bachelor's Degree in Hotel and Restaurant Management. He and Dick Graves together built up from a modest coffee shop in Sparks, Nevada and within its first two years it had a bigger employee base than the railroad, which was a welcome economic diversification for the City of Sparks government. Then its general manager, Ascuaga bought the Nugget in 1960, on a handshake, five years after it had been established as Graves retired. For 29 years Ascuaga drove 1200-1500 head of cattle along the back roads from Bridgeport to Smith Valley providing his own high-quality beef to his Nugget. For 53 years, John Ascuaga was regularly seen walking his namesake hotel-casino-restaurants. John Ascuaga's Nugget became an powerful anchor of pride for and brightest beacon of prosperity of Sparks, and the Ascuagas one of Sparks' most fervent and loyal supporters. Tiki culture -- a kitschy decorative and dining take on Polynesian art and food -- had become hugely popular in the United States, fueled by military personnel returning home from the WWII Pacific Theater, James Michener's "Tales of the South Pacific," movies like "South Pacific" and easier air travel to Hawaii. Trader Dick's at John Ascuaga's Nugget wonderfully harnessed this popularity. It was in the Nugget's Steak House that Ascuaga met Rose Ardans, his future wife. Together, they built John Ascuaga's Nugget into a popular resort destination for out-of-towners and routinely-visited favorite destination of locals' in Northern Nevada. For the citizens of Sparks, the Nugget was The Place to go for fun, headliner entertainment, special-times dinners, the place to put friends and family up for the night, their first job, their first promotion. It was a mark of pride to work at the Nugget and a sign of your integrity to work there for a long time. John Ascuaga's Nugget was the primary driving force of the Sparks economy as its rooms, entertainment, restaurants and special events yearly brought hundreds of thousands of people to Sparks. For more than a half-century, the Ascuagas and the Nugget awarded college scholarships to support their commitment to higher education, making it one of the longest-running programs of its kind in the state. The Ascuagas and the Nugget were also the sponsor of Military Appreciation Day for years at the National Championship Air Races held every year at Reno-Stead Airport. Continuing the honorable American tradition, the Ascuagas truly made their way from the bottom up; John Ascuaga's daughter Michonne started working weekends and after school at age 13 as a front-desk clerk at the family business.

Nevada Magazine quoted John Ascuaga about his way of doing business, "A handshake really means something. You've just got to have a conscience, and you know what's fair. I never had a goal to be rich; I just knew that I had to make it for the employees to make it." I miss The Ascuaga Family, and what they so generously and with dignity shared with Northern Nevada for 53 years.

Holy Tucson! So I've lived in Tucson my whole life, but my father and his family are from the south, and after visiting down there, I just couldn't eat any of the crap BBQ in Tucson. 

Well friends, that has all changed. After finding this place, we eat here almost every week. The brisket is amazing, smoked to perfection. I came here for take out during the COVID-19 pandemic. So don't have direct review of atmosphere/ambience. However I do want to comment on their service. Food:

This place is delish - but OMG, you need to really REALLY want it for the summer wait times. 

I jumped in the drive through (that was wrapped out into the street) and a super friendly employee took my order just like in and out does here in Cali. (Walked up to my car window with an ordering system). The bummer was... I'd never been here before! Looking for a Sunday night dinner spot, and Vivian K suggests Wild Garlic Grill.  Upon checking the Yelp reviews I was intrigued if slightly skeptical.  After all, what kind of place gets numerous 4 and 5 star reviews within 30 days of opening?  Seriously? Are these reviews the real deal?  Reservations were made, and we headed across town at the appointed time.  As we pulled into the parking lot, the hubby turns to me and says "oh boy, what kind of place is this?". While I had read the review noting it looked like a burger joint I wasn't prepared for the exterior which still resembles the 70s fast food drive thru it once was.  However, this is a classic case of Don't Judge a Book By its Cover.  The interior is simple and casual.  Not a lot of fluff or atmosphere, but the food, oh the food. 

We started off with the fondue.  I thought it may have been put together a little quickly.  It lacked the thick, cohesive quality I expect in a fondue; however, the taste was good. The accompanying bread was great.   A bottle of Zinfandel for $30 that we all agreed was a good buy.  A decent quality wine for the price. 

At our table were 2 Lamb Shanks, Linguine Bolognese and a Cabrilla Sea Bass from the specials board along with a Caldo of Braised Pork from the regular menu.  I suspect the specials run for a considerable time as they are mentioned in most every review thus far.  Everything was absolutely fantastic.  Presentation was great. Portions were great. Taste was off the charts good.  The flavors are complex and perfectly paired within each dish.  Our entrees were served with a side of veggies that include sauteed kale, red chard, snow peas and purple cabbage.  I do believe this is the best side dish of veggies that I've had in this town. Serious kudos for original thinking on this one. 

As with most start ups service is a little rough around the edges.  I'm not going into details as I don't think it's fair.  It takes a while to work out the kinks, and I always believe some understanding and patience is necessary for the first few months. Other than being a little slow and awkward there were no glaring issues.   

We will definitely be back, and I've already picked out my next menu choice!

I had this spot on my hit list while visiting the area.  I arrived late on a Friday with one thing on my mind the catfish and shrimp étouffée.  The restaurant is spacious and was busy but not crowded.  I placed my order at the bar as I decided not to eat in.  The bar staff was very friendly and my order was out in no time. Friendly staff, great boba! Good free wifi, always willing to help UofA clubs with their percentage nights. Offers lots of games for your group activities.

I must say, I was very skeptical upon entering this BBQ joint...it didn't have that strong BBQ smell that hits you before you bend the block.  You know that BBQ smell that grabs your nose right as you turn on the block and won't let go until you're back home lol. 

However, to my amazement, the food was absolutely delish.  We had a little fam fun day on Sunday and I ordered the smoked wings platter which comes with your choice of 3 sides. I got baked beans, potato salad and sweet potato soufflé.  Oh and that thick grilled jalapeño cornbread is da bomb. The other two got smoked chicken and ribs.  Again, the ribs were indeed plenteous as was the 1/2 smoked chicken. I see why the reviews are great here, the food is good but the service could be better.  No greeting upon entering or at all for that matter but the food was great!

Stalls are electronically operated by push of an obscure button, toilet stalls have toilet seat covers, hand washing soap is manual, faucets are automatic, air hand dryers are available, entrance/exit to restrooms have that convenient square entrance so no need for doors

The first time was with the group from work there were 19 of us the kept the drink coming and the food came out fresh and hot and the Plummer,s wings are off the hook (they are named after my boss) we had seared sashimi too I had a Cameron's Rib Eye $15.95 14oz. one of my co workers had Maddy's Filet $18.95

it was great to be in a big group and still get great service.

Visit number 2 lunch with the wife we started with around of tap beers and a plate of 
Plummers wings ohhh spicy! 
 I had Dr Randy Shuck's Hangover Burger $10.95 It's Guarantee to cure any hangover an 8oz burger topped with a fried egg, apple wood smoked bacon, double cheddar, crisp lettuce, fresh tomato and onion. it was delicious and on point!

Elizabeth had The Weiser Hammer $10.95 a  1/2 lb. flame grilled beef with shaved London port roast beef, cooked onions, white American cheese, horseradish and au jus. we took half the wings and half her burger back to the room for later evaluation ;)

I had the BBQ Western Burger one perfect med rare Beef patty, onion straws, cheddar cheese, bacon, and BBQ sauce all melty and sauce dripping glad for the stack of napkins Sofie brought over. third time still doesn't disappoint.

THEY ONLY TAKE CASH $$$$$$$!  I had to leave and go up the street to the Wells Fargo!

I came here with my girlfriend about a month or 2 ago.  I had anxiety about writing my review.  Could it be that Blue Oak is on par with my baby The Joint.  The Joint and I have been together for so long.  We have been together at multiple locations.  We were together back when they were the only real BBQ in town.  Could there be a younger, sexier slinger of smoked meats to make me stray?  I fought the temptation for a while but today I decided to go back and just drive by to see if I could resist.  

Upon arrival Blue Oak's perfume of smoky goodness made me realize I was going to commit BBQ adultery.  I could no longer hide my hunger for their delicious brisket and perfectly cooked pulled pork.  I had to have her!

I order a 2 meat combo with the brisket and pulled pork with bbq beans and baked macaroni for sides.  The friendly fella behind the counter asked if I wanted the brisket sliced or chopped ( sliced of course). Then he asked if I wanted it fatty or lean.  I chose lean because I remembered it still having that slightly crunchy thin layer of fat that gives the brisket it's flavor.  The brisket is perfect.  Tasting of smoky mesquite....or probably smoky oak since oak is in their name.  Do not ruin the brisket by adding sauce.  It does not need it!  The pulled pork is very flavorful without any sauce which I was pleasantly surprised by.  I've been to "World Famous" BBQ establishments in other parts of the country and the pulled pork is usually bland requiring sauce.  Blue Oak's pulled pork is slightly salty, smoky and leaves a peppery flavor at the end that lingers.  If you want add a little of their vinegar based sauce to enhance the flavor. The sides were equally as good.  The beans were mildly sweet and smoky. I think I've used the word smoky too much. The Mac and cheese came with bread crumbs on top and tasted peppery and quite gawlicky.  Delicious!  

So after proclaiming my new found love to this younger vixen it begs the question, Am I leaving the Joint for Blue Oak?  The answer is Yes and No.  I decided to convert my bbq love to a polygamous lifestyle.  I am now a Mormon of BBQ....it's ok to love more than 1.

What an ice cream shop!!!  Never been to an ice cream shop as unique as this.  This place is decorated in the 50's and 60's theme.  Lots of flavors to choose from including my favorite, Salted Caramel...yummy!  The staff was very friendly and the place was super clean.  I will definitely be back!  (Elvis Sundae looked really good to.......next trip!)

I just thought about it, they do have valet parking but clearly I always forget about it so I haven't ever used it. If I ever get a dish that isn't rave worthy I will update this review but don't wait around for it. Oh yeah, happy hour!

Immediately sold on this place upon walking in the door and being hit in the face with all the smells. To my right I see one of the guys hand pulling noodles and to my left all the other customers face down in their bowls. 

The setup is very cool because I feel like I'm at the kitchen table being able to see everything be cooked. We only waited about 10 min for seats. 

Guy sitting next to me gifted me a beer which made me realize its BYOB. They will put ur drink in their fridge if you'd like. 

For appetizers we had wings and dumplings. They were really good but my ramen was even better. The noodles were perfect and the broth I could've had alone and been perfectly satisfied. My beef was surprisingly tender even though I would've preferred it more rare. It was very filling so I only made it halfway thru my bowl. 

I'll definitely be back!

Disclaimer: I went here solely for the drinks.

I didn't eat anything here. As a personal rule I try not to eat in the quarter much. Too touristy, over priced and just not good (in most places, not all). How did I end up here then you ask. Post Carribean vacation  I had a longing for another alcoholic beverage inside a pineapple. I was too lazy to do it myself so i typed "tiki bar" in the search bar. This place popped up along with one a few blocks down. The decor sold me. It is so over the top lol. I got the signature drink, Latitude 29, and it didn't disappoint. I don't think I will ever get used to a cocktail over $10 but can't knock it 'til you try it, right? It wasn't too sweet. I did also choose this one for that same reason after seeing lots of creme and syrups in the others. I was also worried about the amount of liquor in it but it did the trick.

This is a tough review for me.

I love donuts. Growing up, a lit "HOT NOW" sign followed by a warm Krispy Kreme donut was a favorite scenario of mine. Rightfully so yeast donuts have always been my favorite until I grew older and couldn't deal with the excessive sweetness and converted to an occasional cake donut  

I heard all the rave about this place when I moved here and I just knew I found the perfect way to satisfy my donut crave without being too sweet like Krispy Kreme or too dense like Dunkin. I think hearing everyone else talk so much about it clouded my judgement and I just thought they were the best hands down. After that excitement wore off I returned and I was able to think on my own how I felt about them. 

As for the donut itself I could go without. It's dry and not usually what I think of as a real donut (in my opinion) when it comes to taste. Not yeast-y but also not cake-y. It's definitely it's own breed. 

What keeps me coming back however, are the toppings. These guys are always making up the best flavor combos using just about anything u can think of as inspiration. They post the donut lineup of the day on their Instagram every morning so you know which they are offering on that day. Between the varieties of the flavors along with their levels of sweetness everyone is sure to find something they like. 

They have an entire menu outside of the donuts though. Usually 3 slider options for the day. Your usual coffee drinks and teas plus soda and juiced veggies. 

They do have wifi and indoor as well as 2 outdoor seating locations. I love the open kitchen and hearing the buzz of all the customers in and out. Definitely a place to at least try once.

I cannot think of a better burger place in the city.

First and foremost I can order my burger medium-rare and actually get it that way. The family that runs the place clearly loves what they do. Their menu has creativity written all over it. Each time I try something new and I have yet to be disappointed. That's coming from someone who rarely orders things just as they are described on the menu. I trust them enough not to ask for things to be taken away or added. 

Bring your appetite because the portions are huge!

**Imagine me twirling like Julie Andrews on that hill in The Sound of Music as you read this.**

This place has all the things! Full disclosure I waited a good while after it's opening before I finally visited because the menu never grabbed my attention. Yes, there are times I actually don't go to places just because it's the cool thing to do. I have been known to also let the wait time on NoWait and the availability on Open Table to deter me as well. Moving on,  I knew when I finally came I had to make it during brunch for the bottomless. One morning I was like let's just go for it. Nobody loses when there is bottomless anything. Turns out the food is great! The real star of the show was their vodka. I was too busy enjoying the scene (aka watching college football) to actually get up and tour the distillery BUT I could tell they knew what they were doing. Their fresh juices were awesome also. If your aren't in to them don't be ashamed to ask the bar back for something else to use as your mixer. Put this place on your to do list if you haven't already checked them out.

One of the few places in the city that have been on Food Network that I actually go to for the food not just because of the name. Of course our first visit we got wings. They were so bomb. We thought ok, maybe we are just over hyping them. We decided we should revisit them to see if we still feel the same. We did. They are just that good! On an alternate visit we ended up here after an extended search for burgers. We weren't let down. They were equally as rave worthy. Also super large so I could only eat half in one sitting. I think it goes without saying french fries at this place are served hot and fresh.

I will admit I'm not fully committed to the 3 stars I'm giving this place and here's why. The fried chicken was good. I hear plenty of talk surrounding this place and how their chicken is one of the best, and to some, the best chicken in New Orleans. So I went in with high expectations. The truth is. This chicken was good but I wouldn't tell all my friends and family that come to town to visit me that it's somewhere they can't leave town without having. I definitely don't think the chicken is worth $15 (technically $17 for me because I asked for only dark meat and that came with an extra $2). We all know chicken is super inexpensive which is why it has been a staple forever in just about everyone's culture across the globe. So unless they are connected to a poultry farmer whom they directly get their meats, and not Cisco, it can't be justified. Again, like I said there is always a lot of talk surrounding the place so people are going to pay regardless just to say they've had it. 

Service was fine. Our waiter did his job and regularly made sure we didn't need anything. I will admit I was confused upon walking in because it says to wait to be seated however there wasn't anyone near the door. I had to walk in the hall where the kitchen window is and ask employees where I should sit. Also, the food came out fast. Like within 10 minutes of ordering. 

So yea I couldn't give 5 stars mainly due to price. I had to give at least 2 because they took our order and had our food at the table super quick. Which almost never happens in the city especially not in super touristy places such as this. Also gave another because I felt it was my own fault for having such high expectations for chicken.

I can not tell you all how many times I have been driving down Felicity and tried to figure out what this building is. Today was the day i found out. My partner just bought a house one street over and we were looking for something we hadn't had before. These guys popped up on Groupon and without any hesitation we went. The food was cooked to order so don't expect to walk in and walk out. I knew by it not being pre-made that we were in for a treat. Chef Jeff is on it. I'm not sure how I haven't heard about him yet but this has to change. I had the Superdome and I'm sure you've already read plenty of reviews about it. It's everything they described and more. I also had the crawfish fries. Yum-o! I am a stickler about taking pictures but this time I dove right in without a second thought. The only bad thing about this place is it being literally steps from her house. Be careful what you ask for. You want to learn self control and then BOOM you find yourself having to exercise it everyday. #ThoughtsAndPrayers

My favorite location!

So glad this one opened. I will admit at first I was like oh goodness magazine does not need anymore restaurants. More so because the previous restaurant in this space, Brick and Spoon, didn't make it. However Ruby Slipper has proved that it is possible to be successful in this location. This is my favorite of the chain. The menu is still the same. I think it might be because of the family style high top seating. I always go straight for that. Call me weird, I don't care. The whole feel of this location is just different.

This location is not my favorite.

They are way over crowded. The servers are being pulled in a million different directions so they don't have the time to do more than grab your drink and deliver your food. The food is thrown on the plate without any attempts to make it look nice. Make sure it's your food though before you dig in because I've had other people's order brought to me before. I think this place just needs to decrease the amount of seating so that they can slow down the traffic in the place. I was seated at the bar but still hesitant to move for fear of bumping a server that was balancing an entire table's worth of food at once. Direct people to the one around the corner if you're that pressed for business.

I know, I know. It's a chain restaurant so I shouldn't expect too much. The place was just as everyone else here has described. I don't doubt that they clean I just don't think it's as frequent as it should be. My booth was very messy. I just decided not to look under my table. 

As for the food, it was the standard black bean patty. I do appreciate that they didn't burn it too much. You'd be surprised how often places will try to cook bean patties like it begins as rare beef. My fries were hot and for the most part my waiter was attentive enough to keep my water refilled. 

The atmosphere of the place wasn't bad. Very sports bar like but also family friendly. They have a large variety of seating too. High tops, bar, regular tables and booths; whichever you'd like. They also have outside seating plus a second level with both inside and outside seating. 

I'm not a frequent visitor so I can't speak of consistency but overall if I were to be hungry late at night AND in Metairie I would get a to go order, maybe.

The one thing the other reviews left out was the bread pudding!

I'm not one for soggy bread things so I usually pass when it comes to bread pudding. Besides people asking for the menu of the day and commenting on their Mac n Cheese, their bread pudding is the next most popular discussion on their Facebook page. I decided I should at least give it a shot. 

Once I finally got to the front of the line there wasn't much left so I was thinking it wasn't going to happen this visit. It did. Mind blown. I'm not going to try to figure it out because I know I won't ever get it right but I would love to see how they do it. It wasn't too sweet and it wasn't too soggy. 

Also! That stuffed bell pepper .....man. Another food mystery that I'm perfectly ok with not knowing how the magic happens. 

Forgot to mention they already sold out of ALL their food earlier in the day and closed up shop for two hours to cook more.

Great ambiance and lighting. Perfect for everything from lunch with a friend to special occasion celebrations and even date night with your Lovey.

I ordered the lamb sirloin on a baguette but unfortunately, I was so full from my roasted pear, gruyere, with sweet potato hay salad, and truffle butter potatoes that I couldn't eat one bite of it. I took it to-go and it was still tasty the next day though I'm certain it would have been better the night before.

The sweet potato hay salad was way better than I had expected. The thought of eating "hay" was so unappealing that I was thoroughly delighted to actually taste how delicious it was. Definitely a must-try.

What I love the most about Prasino, however, is the quality antibiotic- and hormone-free meats, and organic produce. They have an eco-friendly focus and strive to buy local whenever possible. 

Kudos, Prasino!

Chili for breakfast? If it's in an Olive Street Slinger, then yes! It's St Louis, remember, and chili is one of those perfect cold weather meals...so why not?

The Olive Street Slinger includes a layer of crispy hash browns for a base, then an over-easy egg with a perfectly runny yolk, candied bacon, and chili topped with a layer of cheddar and a sprinkling of scallions. The crispy, crunchy layer of hash browns was the perfect base for this filling, chili breakfast.

The slingers include your choice of toast (biscuit for the Country Slinger) and over easy eggs. 

Another notable item is the house made strawberry marmalade. It's delicious and has just a hint of vanilla. Spread some over a toasted and buttered marble rye...mmm, party for your mouth.

Overall, a great little breakfast spot!

Homemade soup, Gingham style.

The beef and vegetable soup was loaded with both beef and vegetables. It could have used a bit of salt and pepper but as a homemade soup from a diner it was decent and I would probably order it again. 

What am I saying? I actually ordered 2 more bowls. Why? Because a couple extra bucks gives you an unlimited bowl which you can mix or match with a different soup or even chili.

Probably 3.5 stars but I'll round it up to 4.

Rock on, Gingham style.

Complimentary chips and salsa: 5 stars. Loved that the chips were hot and fresh. You also get 3 different salsas brought to your table.

Guacamole: 5 stars. Fresh, flavorful, fantastic. It was near closing and we were the only customers so I'm certain that this guac was made fresh, just for moi. It looked beautiful and tasted fresh and delicious.

Tacos: 4.5 stars. Soft duo of corn tortillas with your choice of protein or veggie, with onion and chopped fresh cilantro. Served with fresh lime slices.

Service: 4 stars. We arrived 25 minutes before closing and asked if we could just get something quick and easy. They weren't thrilled about it and said they were closing soon but didn't turn us down.

Setting: 3 stars. It's a tiny taco shop in a small strip mall and it has a liquor store inside. Fluorescent lighting. Two televisions, one on either end of the dining area.
