We were served with flimsy plastic utensils and paper plates but that may have been due to us being the last customers of the night. We actually ordered, ate, paid and left by closing time of 9pm.

After seeing Anthonino's on a DDD episode, we decided to check it out when we were in STL.

For starters, the house salad with Greek dressing was crisp, fresh and delicious. It included feta cheese and a few red bell pepper and cucumber slices.

Next, the toasted ravioli appetizer was delicious. It included 6 perfectly toasted raviolis and a cup of sauce with Parmesan crumbles on top. It seemed a little pricey at $9 but I suppose that's the price you pay for watching Guy Fieri ooh and ahh over this little dish on national television.

The shrimp scampi with lemon butter sauce and fresh herbs was delicious. The shrimp was perfectly cooked and although I am not a huge fan of breading it worked well and was tastier than it looked.

The Palermo style chicken with white wine butter sauce was very good although, again, I'm not a huge fan of breading. The sauce with capers was very tasty.

We also had a pasta side with pink sauce (combination of marinara and Alfredo) which was positively okay. It wasn't anything earth shattering but was tasty nonetheless.

The service was excellent. Our server had tasted every dish on the menu and was able to make some good recommendations. 

Overall, I would probably check it out again if in the area.

Nice little cafe connected to a French bakery which, incidentally, smells delightful.

The rolls for a late breakfast were light and flaky. Think: croissant-like and tasty when loaded with real whipped butter. 

The spinach with lemon and asiago quiche du jour was perfectly golden-brown, with just the right amount of lemon. Cheesy and delicious. 

I would have preferred a crispier roasted rosemary potato. Not a fan of soft roasted potatoes. I want them nicely browned and crispy on the outside with an almost creamy inside. Instead, I had potatoes that were soft, not crispy. Not a fan.

Hubby ordered a waffle and it was loaded with fresh berries: blueberries, blackberries, and strawberries.

Service was excellent and a post-breakfast tour of the bakery while your belly is full is a must even if you're just checking out the beautiful cakes.

If you are in the USF/University area, this is an option if you are in the mood for BBQ. They are avid supporters for veterans as seen in the decor of the restaurant as well as the opportunity to donate money the veterans by buying a drinking cup. 

It is conjoined with Keke's Breakfast cafe, so don't be confused. 

It is on the pricey side for casual bbq (considering I went for lunch and spent $30 for two people on combo meals), but I have been twice and the food and the service has not disappointed me. The portion size is average but satisfactory for me personally. You have two options for the brisket (choose the non-lean option, it tastes way better). You can ask to sample them if you don't trust me. They have 6 BBQ sauces to choose from and a mayo-based/cream sauce (which i liked). The pulled pork sandwich NC style is good stuff. 

Overall, a place I would eat again. Gave it 4 instead of 5 stars because of the price.

Bakery and bakery service: 4 stars
Restaurant: 3.5 stars for yummy food
Restaurant/cafe service: 1.5 stars

I've been here many times and love, love, love the pastries and sweets they offer! While I want to love this place, I can't. And after last night, here's why:

While my spouse and I were NOT on the receiving end of this (our service was lovely and so was our server Susan), I want to be clear that I observed this behaviour "loud and clear" b/c it happened right in front of us. A young couple walked to their seats and as they passed the servers station, the servers began making comments about this young person's looks--giggling, and then talking about how pretty his date was...in Spanish. They weren't even subtle. Eventually, they crowded together and gawked at them for a few minutes.

As the night went on, one of the other servers walked into the kitchen and started singing loudly, and we could even here  what sounded like sarcastic musings about what other patrons from other tables were requesting. Again, while it did NOT ruin our Valentine's dinner, it was distracting and rude. In the end, I was embarrassed for wait staff. And I was sad for this establishment. 

My plea to La Bonne Bouchee management: PLEASE TRAIN YOUR SERVERS, HOSTS, AND HOSTESSES! Organization, courtesy and professionalism go a long way!

*SPIKEMAN WHARF ALL DAY PARKING $15*

Really friendly service by everyone!

Ashlee was wonderful, she recommended the salad and sandwich combo. GET THAT!

Random but the water is really good, the ice is made with filtered clean water. I love that!

The white sangría was refreshing 

Rice and beans and fried plantains PERFECT

Azucar!!!

**FRESH, HOT BEIGNET'S MADE HERE**

*Located in a shopping center*

EXCELLENT customer service!! Cameron is a Rockstar!! Wow, super great at anticipating what you'd like and then exceeding expectations.

Flavored creamers available yay!! (for people like me who like a little coffee with their creamer)

Everything looks delicious,  I will go ahead and say that everything will be delicious because they will make sure you get a perfect meal!

THE ORDER:

-2 coffee's

-Veggie omelet with potatoes and raisin toast ( nicely buttered) side of crispy bacon

- 2 egg combo with bacon, rye toast, and tomato slices 

- Cameron suggested the beignet's (nice and hot!)

If this restaurant was close to my house we'd eat here all the time!

Bon Appétit

Rest assured, if you're looking for a good cupcake, THIS is the place! 
For two weeks I was craving a moist, delicious red velvet cupcake. I bought a sorry excuse for a cupcake at Starbucks - too dry, threw it out. I found one at the grocery store - an embarrassment to red velvet, so it was thrown out. Then, after a morning trip to Reading Terminal Market this past Saturday, my friend said "Look! It's Philly Cupcake!" Suddenly, there I was, standing in the street, staring at this amazing site - feeling pretty confident that THIS was the place to get the red velvet cupcake I had been searching for - and WAS IT EVER!!!!! 
The cupcake was fresh, moist, and the most delicious thing I have ever eaten! It's been three days since I've eaten that cupcake and I find myself tossing and turning at night, wondering when I can have another. I do believe that Philly Cupcake is my new favorite Center City place to visit! (and my dog LOVED the pupcake that I brought home for her) 
I am going with 4 stars instead of 5 simply because the store is small and cramped. It was a busy time of day so we were in and out quickly due to the crowds, but I would have liked to spend a bit more time looking around! The store is beautiful, the cupcakes all looked delicious, and the employees were so helpful and pleasant.

Don't let the previously unassuming entrance fool you, Boat House stands out as one of the best bars in the Philadelphia suburbs. They have done an amazing job of getting creative in light of COVID restrictions and the new outdoor setup is incredible. The booths have individual TVs and the larger tables are situated with a great view of big screen TVs. Once you make your way inside things are as great as they've ever been as the bar gives off a welcoming vibe for anything from a post-work happy hour to a kickball pregame. 

No matter where you sit you will be treated to great service, good beer, and better food. The staff are always attentive. The beer is constantly rotating to highlight local breweries and classic favorites. They do a great job of offering a menu for any taste without trying to stretch themselves too thin. Their wings are what keep people coming back but their specials are also worth stopping in for. Whether it is the tried and true favorites or the excitement of trying something new, Boat House is the definition of a one stop shop.

If you haven't been here yet...go :)  wants some reasons why? 

1. At noon every day, they stop and sing the national anthem. 

2. They honor all those who serve, police, fire, army, navy, airforce, coast guard and more. They hang badges throughout the restaurant. 

3. Buy the American heroes cup. $2 from ever cup goes to the USO, who help service members connect to family, home and their country. 

4. 6 different bbq sauces from Texas to Georgia to Tennessee to Kentucky to Mississippi to Maryland.  Choices!

5.  The food is just plain good!

2 meat sampler.  Jalapeño and cheddar sausage, pulled pork, mac n cheese, smashed potatoes and cornbread.  Yum!!  Now I need a nap!

PS....staff is super nice and helpful!

Glad this chain has made it to Nashville!

I did the tourist thing and tried Pat's and Geno's and compared. Sadly, Geno's came in second place. If I could, I would have put them at the very bottom of every list. The staff members were rude, the food was not up to par, and the decor/branding was a little over the top. 

The cheese-steak was sub-par. The meat was not seasoned and was really oily. The oil caused the whiz to be thin and runny. No one likes runny cheese! Honestly, my fiance and I were more obsessed with their onions than anything else. 

Aside from that, there is a sign on the door that reads "This is America, when ordering please speak English". Not cool.

I was so excited for so long knowing that the same owners of Time Market bought this. I finally came to check it out. Nothing like Time Market. 

Had a BLT with avocado. They offered a choice of either cole slaw, rice or fries as a side. I asked for a side salad and they wanted another dollar. I passed. The BLT came. Greasy thing. Hard to eat. Not good. Greasy. A bad taste in my mouth.

After striking out at two different downtown Reno restaurants (hour long wait to get seated!), we headed out of town to Chop 40. What a great decision. An old west style building greeted us as we pulled into the parking lot. As I got out of the car, I was struck by the wonderful aromas coming from the building.

We were sat right away in a comfortable, rustic dining room. I ordered a Revision IPA from a pretty good list of craft beers. There was a wine list and full bar also. The menu items looked really good and the prices were reasonable. 

I ordered one of several nightly specials, a 22oz rib eye. The steak came with garlic bread and a salad. Both the salad and garlic bread were delicious. The steak was the star of the show. Perfectly cooked medium rare, and seasoned just right. This is one of the best steaks i'd eaten in a very long time.

I will definitely be back!

I recently received a menu from Thai Terrace in my door, decided to try it out the other night. I will never order from there again. First off, the guy who waited on me was rude and abrupt, not only to me but to a coworker who dared to question him while I was there. 

Second, their menus are wrong. I only just received the menu in my door. It says they offer delivery and they don't. According to rude guy, 'Just so you know, we won't EVER deliver'. Also, I was charged $2 over the menu price for my entree. When I questioned it, I was told they raised their prices over a year ago.  Then why are they actively sending out wrong menus??

Third, my meal wasn't that great. The crispy calamari with sweet chili and ground peanuts was no better than something I would find in a freezer section at the grocery store. It was rubbery, not crispy and the sauce was served on the side. The salmon in the Pad Thai was dry. The Pad Thai itself was otherwise tasty. 

It's a shame, it seems like a nice atmosphere but I'm really big on customer service. They lost my repeat business because of rude guy and outdated menus...

UPDATE: Just received nasty reply from owner. I WAS there to eat and not complain. But the whole bait and switch with the menu pricing was what made me write the review. I can deal with no delivery and dry salmon. Save the customer service training for yourself, Mr owner.

There's very few Sushi places I haven't tried yet in the area, so, I thought I'd check this one out because I was going to see a movie next door.

Done...check...not again...

The interior decor does not match the exterior. I was expecting something better. It looks like a casual dining restaurant on the inside...nothing to write home about.

The staff was friendly. I sat down at the sushi bar around 5pm. There was exactly 1 other group of diners sitting at a table.

The first thing I noticed was the food debris on the top of the glass refrigeration case and on the top counter space next to it. Old rice, cilantro and pieces of other food stuff abounded. The next thing I noticed (and that stayed constant throughout my meal) was that the sushi chefs left the sliding doors to the refrigeration cases open all the time. Then I noticed that the fish itself was not wrapped tightly in plastic wrap as is done in every other sushi place in the area. Fish is supposed to be re-sealed every time it's opened. Nothing was ever re-wrapped. I also noticed that all the fish had been pre-sliced! That's a no-no in anybody's book, as fish quality deteriorates immediate after being sliced. I've NEVER seen any other sushi place do this. The fish did not look as fresh as it could've been and I could tell by the taste that the quality and freshness were sub-par due to these practices. The Miso Soup? Salt bomb! I could barely do a few sips.

A couple of good points...the chicken skewers appetizer was good...juicy meat with a spicy sauce on it. Unfortunately, when asked, the sushi chef had no idea what the sauce was. The specialty Nigiri called Picachu, Moana and Speedy Gonzalez were tasty, even considering the quality of the fish. Especially the Moana, with Mango sauce and Macadamia nuts.

I have no other positives to speak about and I'm positive that I won't be returning unless they step up their game and the quality of their product, especially considering the $24.95 price point for the AYCE dinner...

So yummy! There are a million flavor combos- both simple and decadent. The workers were amazing and you can even taste flavors! All of the flavor were spot on and the ice is very fine. I will definitely be back.

My family and I had an amazing meal here. The service was fantastic and every bite of food was delicious. No one ate anything that they didn't rave about! My husband and cousin got the fried chicken that comes with awesome Mac and cheese, greens and gravy. My aunt got salmon with black eyes peas. And I got the shrimp and grits- one of the best versions I've ever had! We shared the creme brûlée trio for dessert- sooo good! We also started with the turtle soup and the beet salad. They were great!
The only negative thing that happened was when the manager stopped by our table. My aunt asked him a question about Emeril and was was really rude and dismissive....he told her to look at Emeril's picture on the wall because that was as close to him as she was going to get! Yikes :(
I'm from New Orleans and not used to such poor customer service. However the waiters were outstanding so I didn't want to deduct any stars for the actions of one rude person. Maybe the manager should take a cue from his fantastic staff! We will definitely dine in again :)

Delicious food and super friendly people made our lunch experience here wonderful. My husband got the daily special/ white beans with choice of meat/ he got fried chicken. My mom got gumbo and a 2-piece fried chicken meal with greens as the side. And I got the shrimp plate with dirty rice and candied yams as the sides. The fried food was excellent! Hot and crisp, not overly greasy, and the batters were light. The gumbo had a good flavor and lots of stuff in it. The greens were very well seasoned. The yams were very good but very sweet. My husband liked the dirty rice, but there was some flavor in it that I didn't care for. It was a really good meal and I would absolutely return!

I am surprised I have not reviewed Muriel's sooner- I have been here several times. Each visit has been as close to "impeccable" as you can get. The restaurant is beautiful, with so much interesting art and decor. They will give you a tour if you ask- the upstairs has some super cool rooms and stories as well. The service is top notch. I've been there for regular dinners as well as (most recently) for a private party event. Throughout the evening everyone continuously remarked about the service. No drink was left low, the dishes were cleared quickly, each time someone got up their napkin was folded. And this was all done with polite smiles and chat. It was beyond impressive. The food is outstanding. We have had the pork chop- cooked perfectly every time, the shrimp and grits, the soup, and (our favorite) the goat cheese crepes. I could eat those every day. Whether you are visiting NOLA or live here (we are from here), this is a place to try out- more than once!

The wings were good. And then the good times stopped when my black friend Ray went out to have a smoke. Then they would not let him back in. For who knows why? I was let in even though I was more drunk than Ray. They are a bullshit bar with no good drink deals, and to top it all off they are racists! Do not go here

I can't even begin to put into words how much I love it here - but I will try my best anyway! My sister had told me about this gem and how I needed to try it - particularly the salted caramel! I went 4 or 5 times in my trip down to visit family, and everytime I went I had salted caramel mixed with one of their other flavors - a win with everything! 
My first adventure was salted caramel with praline cream - the salted caramel was the star, soooo amazing, but the praline cream was a little lost in it. So I tried again the next day with Salted Caramel and Butter Pecan - that's the winner! These perfectly compliment. The NY Cheesecake flavor is also lovely.
Servers here are friendly, and Sunday is Karaoke - always a fun and delicious stop!
Owner is a whiner who thinks character assassination against a fine private school is the best way to drum up business. His beer sucks, too.

I'm a big fan of Zoe's Kitchen for a quick, reasonably priced, healthy Mediterranean meal. I booked mark this place after seeing one of my yelp friend's check-ins who lives in that area; I am so happy I had the opportunity to stop by for dinner on my latest trip to the area. You place your order at the front counter; your meal will be delivered quickly from the kitchen by one of the servers. I ordered the Salmon Kebob dinner plate which comes with hummus, raita, Greek salad, and pita. Everything was delicious and I marveled at how tasty everything was especially  the salmon. My meal was very well prepared using all fresh ingredients; the Greek salad dressing was outstanding and available at each table to use as you please...nice! When in that area again I wouldn't hesitate to stop in for lunch or a quick dinner as Zoes delivers a quality affordable dining expereince!

Most impressive to me was opening the beer menu and seeing certain items I hadn't seen since my last visit to Germany; ie, Augustiner Bräu Edelstoff. The beer menu is extensive with some 15 German beers on tap and countless bottled beers from around Germany. The food is authentic and solid, this restaurant does it extremely well from service, to beer, wine, appetizers, main courses and desserts, Brauhaus Schmitz comes as close to a visit in Germany as you will get stateside!

If you want high quality Italian cheeses, deli meats and imported pasta's and tomatos this is where you come to in Philadelphia's Little Italy Market District. When I say top quality I mean exceptionally high quality, you will almost be force fed samples of cheeses and deli items and for good reason, you try you buy! The cheeses are simply out of this world but worth every penny, the home made sausages are exquisite especially the cheese broccoli-rabe sausage, oh my goodness bought a ton. Don't miss the market with it's coffee shops and restaurauts when visiting Philadephia.

The Pour house is a Gastro-Pub with a very large selection of mixed drinks, shots and beers on tap backed up by a sizable selection of bottled beers. Beers on tap rotate as new introductions are frequent and rising market trenders. It can be insanely busy but that's the fun of going to the TPH as you will always have a great time in the frenetically paced pub atmosphere. Good burgers, wings and all your pub grub favorites are to be found on the menu but they do specialize in a wide assortment of oysters which is one of the reasons I am so fond of this place. They have a "Buck a Shuck" evening every Wednesday I believe, if you are an oyster lover looking for a value this place is a must stop.The service is good and the atmosphere is just what you would expect and want in a good Gastro Pub.

What an eclectic crowd this place draws most unusual as I looked around, no matter I was there for a late lunch. I was quite satisfied with the burger I ordered, it was slightly overcooked but tasted alright. Others in our party remarked that while their food was just okay it wasn't quite what it use to be and felt the place had slipped a bit. Still another wasn't satisfied at all with the avocado, tomato grilled cheese sandwich and I had to agree. The bread was barely warm, cheese wasn't melted, the center was stone cold, it never should have left the kitchen like that. The apps on the other hand were good, fried calamari with an Asian dipping sauce and the loaded fries were a hit. 
There is nothing memorable about our dining experience that would beckon a return visit.

I attended my cousin's wedding here a couple of weekends ago. Arizona Inn has long been raved about and described as "old elegance". I must say the grounds are exquisite but when we arrived for the wedding, there was no one in the lobby or anywhere who could help direct us and we all found that a bit odd. 

I did not see any guest rooms but the walk through the bar, restaurant dining room and finally the ballroom  were all lovely. The ballroom is pretty small and with the dance floor and live band made the room feel even smaller. Otherwise the drinks were prepared well, the few passed hors doeuvres were tasty and it was a lovely event (with a few snafus). 

One caveat-this place is not wheelchair or very walker friendly, so if you are traveling with the geriatric or disabled set, beware.

Please don't waste your time.  We ate there for the first time (12/16/14) for dinner.  Upon arrival, we were seated immediately which means they weren't busy at all. The waitress took more than 10 minutes to  come to our table to get our drink order.  My husband ordered a full hot pastrami sandwich.  I ordered the half braised brisket sandwich. When our food arrived the side French fries that came with our food was hotter than our sandwiches. The hot pastrami should be called the cold pastrami because it wasn't even warm to say the least. My sandwich was less than subpar. It wasn't flavorful at all and the meat was very dry. Based on our experience I don't think we'll be coming back.

Extra Cheesesteak Wit Whiz

Tips for Ordering at Pat's

The line at Pat's King of Steaks moves quickly, so it's best to be prepared -- know what you want, and how to order it by the time you get to the front of the line!

Step 1
Specify if you want your steak with (wit) or without (wit-out) onions

Step 2
Specify Plain, Cheez Whiz, Provolone, American or Pizza Steak

Step 3
Have your money ready. We are cash only.

Step 4
Order just your steak at the first window. The second window is for fries and drinks.

Step 5
Eat up while it's hot! Honestly, when it comes to Pat's, I figured it would be best to "borrow" their Tips for Ordering (pasted above). That's really all you need to know.... Whether you want a Steak, a Hot Dog, a Pork or a Fish Cake, the most important aspect of Pat's is knowing how to order. The food? Well, it's in the title..."King of Steaks" No, seriously, every bite is complete Cheesesteak Bliss and you SHOULD believe the hype!

For those who can read Chinese, the cover of their menu says that when you order takeout over the phone and pay with cash, you get 10% off. (Notice that's not printed anywhere in English... Racist much?) So I do what it says and when I get there the woman at the counter says "sorry, that's only for orders over $25."  If that's your policy, say so in advance!

Very disappointed. 

UPDATE: As I'm eating my chicken, I literally find a piece of metal IN the chicken. Not to mention disgusting, this place's food isn't safe. See the pics on Yelp for the weird triangle-shaped piece of metal.

Great balance of authentic Chinese and Taiwanese dishes and what we Americans would refer to as "Chinese Food." The store owners (Cathy and Andy) are often on site and very friendly and welcoming. Their regular customers are all greeted by name and the wait staff can usually remember their favorite orders.

Have been coming here for years and every time its a feast! With high quality Chinese food and really long hours, this restaurant has become a staple in Philly's Chinatown.

This place is amazing! Tried this place for someone's birthday. We ordered drinks (a little pricy but delicious!) like Blonde Ambition, Aviation and Last Word. Three tapas - Beggars Purse, Vaca Frita with Chimichurri, and Bacon Wrapped Dates. I have never had dates before so this was a great way to try them, wrapped in bacon! So delicious! The Vaca Frita was on top of whipped potatoes were amazing! Crispy yet tender! The Beggars purse was good, but heavy. The phylo dough was crisp, but the pork combination inside was just too much. Tasty, yet heavy. I will definitely go back!

I have been to lunch and brunch. I have yet to try dinner. 

Both times I have been here I have been extremely pleased with the food and the service from the workers. Their take on French as most know it, seems pretty safe. I love that they serve bread with everything and the flavors are on point. 

Lunch I had the French onion soup and roasted turkey break sandwich. For a steal for both at $12.95 for a delicious lunch! The soup was creamier than I thought it would be, as their soup doesn't seem to be beef broth based. Nonetheless, still fantastic! The sandwich was so tasty I should've gotten just that!! 

Brunch was a braised brisket on toast, which sautéed onions and fontina cheese. And a crap load of fries. I wish I had more of an appetite when I had brunch but I wasn't feeling very well. Reheated it the next day and was almost as good!

I've been dying to try this place out, but alas, two of the three chicks I hang with are vegetarian... in the Midwest. Weird. Anyway - I made my own burger. I got a single with pepper jack cheese, bacon and bbq sauce. Simple and delicious. I was not expecting the sauce to be spicy, but it was perfect between the sweet and heat. The burger was not as thick as I thought it would be quarter pound to 6-8oz. I'm good with that though. I didn't get anything else to eat but the burger filled me up without making me feel like I had just ate a giant meal.

This was such a bad let down. I have lived in this area for 35 years and say I need to try this place every time I pass it. Even brought the wife with me on this trip. We wanted to have a really good hamburger. Still looking. I don't know how this place stays so busy. We walk in and no one greeted us. Had to ask if we just sat ourselves, we did. First thing I noticed is they very plainly spell out on their menu "NO FREE REFILLS ON DRINKS" AND they even charge for just a class of water with lemon. (WHAT!!!!) This has to be the only restaurant to actually charge for water (and it was TAP water, city tap water) and charges for refills from a soda tap. Anyway, we order the broccoli cheese bites as an appitizer. Nothing special there, I could have gotten the same from the frozen foods section at the grocery store. 

Next the wife and I both get a hamburger with mushrooms and provolone. After looking at the pictures on Yelp of the same hamburgers, I just want to say DO NOT TRUST or EXPECT YOUR FOOD TO LOOK AT ALL ANYTHING LIKE THAT IN A PICTURE FROM HERE! I don't know what restaurant those pictures were taken from, but not here. Also, since the menu is ala carte, we decided to order a side of fries to split. From the description on the menu of being a "large basket of fresh french fries" they were anything but. 

The hamburgers came out and were small. The bun was nothing more than a bun from the grocery store down the road, TINY. The mushrooms were canned. not fresh. The hamburger was over cooked. Menu specifically states they cook to med-rare unless otherwise specified. We did not specify. Our burgers were med-well and greasy. I suspect they used an 80/20 meat blend. The fries were not fresh, rather frozen fries similar to McDonald's. 

This was my first and last time going here. For what we paid for, $23 plus a tip, we could have gone to McDonald's and gotten more food for the same price and we could have gotten refills if we ate there. I make better hamburgers on my grill than this place. We were still hungry after leaving here and ended up going out for a real dinner somewhere else for less the price. 

If you are looking for a good place to pay for overpriced food, small portions, and pay for each refill or even pay for a glass of tap water, this is you place. It is a shame too. For as long as I have lived here, this place is constantly being the rave of friends who have been here. Not sure if we missed something here or what. But this is NOT the best hamburger joint in the Tampa Bay area.

Well I'll get down to it, the food is bland and there is nothing special about the menu. Granted it's and American based selection but the burger I chose had absolutely no flavor at all. I also tried the sample platter and although all the items were fried they tasted better than my entree. 

I would like to say that the lemonade was delicious and the overall design and theme of the facility were intriguing. 

Sadly I would not recommend eating here based on the over priced menu and the boring flavorless food.

Stumbled upon this unique bar & cafe while in Tucson when my sales rep & I were looking for a place to sit, grab coffee and discuss business.  When we entered, there was a girl working there who was not the friendliest person, but we gave the place a chance as we couldn't help but notice the pretty cool hipster interior and the most unique "bottle" chandeliers hanging from the ceiling.  We both ordered regular coffees that were lukewarm and bitter but powered through it.  I then saw pretty pink iced doughnuts at the counter which I ordered but when bitting into it, it was dry, hard and tasted old.  Perhaps this place is better during lunch time when having a hot sandwich that's made to order or coming for after work drinks?  In the meantime, they'll need to up their game when it comes to their cafe and service.

My friends and I were excited to visit Le Cheri and, upon arriving were impressed by the building and the surprisingly spacious interior (definitely large when compared to Bibou). Armed with three bottles of wine, we got seated. 

We order food, waiter opens (with some difficulty) the wine and pours it (again, surprisingly, with some difficulty). 

We order and then a bread basket is dropped off. Cold, hard bread. Almost frozen butter. Not really what I expected. 

Before we got our appetizers, our Chablis was done so the waiter asked if we should open the next bottle (a Chateauneuf Du Pape). We said yes and asked if he could decant. He decants the bottle and we say "can you open the other bottle as it doesn't need decanting?" He opens it and then says "you know we have a corkage fee, right?" 

No, we did not as when we called in late November they told us we would need to bring wine as they didn't have a license. We told this to the waiter and he said he couldn't do anything, then said he could waive the 3rd bottle. Okay, whatever - it's not a ton of money for corkage ($20/bottle). 

Appetizers were okay: fennel soup was flavorful, goat cheese ravioli were well-prepared and the steak tartare was good but unevenly chopped. 

Entrees followed after a pretty long wait (we finished another bottle in the interim, to give a sense). Rabbit ballotine was the best of the dishes, moist and well-seasoned. The cassoulet was unbearably dry. The duck confit on top was literally like jerky and the beans were very overcooked and dry. The short rib dish was well-prepared and flavorful.  

Desserts were all well-made and creative. Whoever is prepping the desserts has a deft hand with odd flavor combinations and most of them worked out well. 

So, to sum, the appetizers were mostly average, the entrees were good and bad, and the desserts were good. I'd say the food was a 3-out-of-5 since most of the dishes were just good and nothing was great (or approaching mind blowing). 

Service was a 4-out-of-5 (wine service gaffes aside).

So, why 2 stars?

Upon getting our check, we see they only charged us for one corkage. We think "oh, cool, they are giving us even more of a break. Classy." We give our credit card. They charge it. We sign the slips. 

...then the owner, Charlotte, comes out. She literally dresses us down in the middle of the restaurant, loudly, saying it doesn't matter that we were told before that they didn't have a license and now they do. That we should have called before to make sure they were still BYOB (who does that in Philly?). And that we received an Open Table email confirming the night before saying it is no longer BYOB (not true and we forwarded the email subsequently to the owner to show she was wrong on that).

Then she says she's going back and charging us another corkage fee and brings out a new, higher credit card receipt. Seriously, what kind of shit is that? 

We brought 3 wines, the total of which dwarfed our meal in cost, so the corkage issue (which wasn't really an issue until she made it one) wasn't about cost on our end. We simply didn't know and felt it was odd to be reminded after our 3rd bottle was opened. There are far too many other good restaurants for us to visit the few times we make it back to my hometown every year. I won't be going back to Le Cheri (or Bibou for that matter).

So, 3 for food. 4 for service. 1 for ownership. 2 stars overall. And I read they just fired their head chef. Maybe that cassoulet won't taste like it came out of the food dehydrator anymore.

With so many farm to table establishments in Nashville, Sinema fell very short.  

The Good:  The greatest  attribute to this restaurant is it's interior, which is spectacular.  They've done a great job of making this a hip/swank place with old movies streaming on the walls, comfy couches upstairs and very cool lighting.  The drinks were very well done but took a while to make it to the tables.  When they arrived, they kept coming in different style of glasses - for the same drink.  Tall and skinny tube like glasses to short rocks glasses for the exact same drink.  Just think that's kind of odd.

The Bad:  How high brow are you to charge $3 for valet parking?  This is the only place in Nashville that I've ever seen that done.  $12 bucks for a bread basket?   How good is the bread?  Isn't bread one of the cheapest things in a restaurant?   The rest of the meal  (fish and chicken for the table) was over salted and underwhelming.  

The tables themselves felt cheap and more like something you'd find at Ashely Home Furnishings.  I'd expect more if dropping well over $200 on a meal for 4.

I say all of this with baited breath but I don't think I'd go back or recommend it to others.  There are much better places with better and well cooked choices than here.  

I'll take my $3 valet charge and apply it to an Uber ride to a different place next time.

If it weren't for the New Orleans Wildsam guide on the counter I might not have guessed this coffee shop was in the Big Easy.  Everything--the colors, countertops and concrete--looked so IKEA kitchen modern.  It fits the Warehouse District aesthetic but I prefer cozy coffee shops and it was a bit sterile for my tastes.

We popped in for drinks and then went back to watch the Running of the Bulls down the block.  I ordered a chocolate iced coffee and a chocolate chip cookie wrapped in plastic for later.  My guy commented that his coffee was a serious jolt.

Judging from the crowd that flooded in during our visit, they don't have trouble attracting customers.  However, I didn't get a sit and stay vibe from Revelator Coffee.  I would return if I was already in the area but I doubt I would make a special trip across town.

We came to Restaurant R'evolution to celebrate after our wedding and had an amazing experience!

Out of all the restaurants in this fabulous food city, this was our first pick because:
a) They're on countless best of the best lists in New Orleans.
b) They boast an impressive 4.5 stars with 773 Yelp reviews.
c) They serve up Louisiana cuisine with special occasion ambiance.
d) They're within walking distance of the Canal Streetcar.
e) I'm obsessed with Chef John Folse.

So if I'm being honest E was the main reason.  His cooking shows are entertaining, his cookbooks fly off shelves, I've enjoyed his other restaurants and I'm a fan of his flavors.  Stamp Folse on something and I expect it to be delicious; his partnership with Chef Tramonto did not disappoint.

We reserved the Wine Room, a private dining room that seats up to 12.  It was an inviting space with warm colors, exposed wood beams & brick and mood lighting.  The back wall was a shared glass with their wine room...literally an entire wall of wine.

For a couple of hours, we were treated to efficient service from a team that included Luke, Kevin and others.  They were attentive when we needed something and they made themselves scarce when we didn't.  We never felt rushed and were allowed to savor the experience.

We all enjoyed the courses from start to end.  The plates were cute but hearty if that makes sense.  In other words, the presentations were creative (in keeping with the high-end concept) but there wasn't a tweezer food in sight.  It was stick to your ribs Cajun/Creole fare.  My personal favorites were Crab Beignets, Death By Gumbo, Creole Cream Cheese Bread Pudding Crème Brulee and Chocolate Doberge Cake.

In Restaurant R'evolution, Chefs Folse and Tramonto have dreamed up an admirable trio of flavors, ambiance and service.  In a city renowned for southern decadence, our meal was truly memorable.

I bought into the hype about Willie Mae's legendary fried chicken.  As we sat there waiting for our food to come out, I was literally remixing that Az Yet song to make the lyrics chicken appropriate:

Last night
Chicken was in my belly
Last night
While chomping down on skin
I saw the sun, the moon
The mountain and the rivers
I saw heaven eating Willie Mae's chicken

Corny and embarrassing?  Yes, but the point is that my expectations were way too high.  It's just chicken.  It's darn good chicken but don't come here expecting it to change your life like I did.

We both ordered Fried Chicken Mixed, three pieces of chicken served with one side dish.  (There was a $2 upcharge for all dark meat.)  Our picks were Red Beans, White Beans and an extra side dish of Mac and Cheese to share.  To wash it all down--root beer and fresh squeezed lemonade.

The lemonade was some of the best I've ever tasted--refreshingly cold, lip-puckeringly tart and sweet!  I didn't try the red beans but the white beans were the tastiest I've had outside the late Silver Moon Café in Baton Rouge.  Herbs flavored every bite of butter soft bean and an impressive level of flavor infused the dish even though they didn't use seasoning meat.

Of course, the chicken was outstanding.  The skin was Zapp's Potato Chip level crisp but flakier.  It was perfectly salted and the meat was super juicy too.  The only thing I didn't love were the globs of undercooked batter hiding between the skin and meat.  I assume they hurried our batch of chicken out of the fryer.

The mac and cheese was moist and creamy but couldn't outshine the white beans for best side dish.  Thanks to our server, Candy, for recommending those delicious beans!  She did a fabulous job working the entire room during the lunch rush.  There was no line at the door but every table was occupied.

I should note that we got here on a Monday around 12:15PM and only waited two minutes for a table.  But wait or no wait...eating at Willie Mae's is one of those things you have to do when you're in New Orleans.  Don't expect it to change your life but get here.

I've been to several coffee shops in the city but Treme Coffeehouse is my favorite so far.  As you can guess from the name, it's located in the historic neighborhood spotlighted in the HBO drama.  I'll quickly rundown the reasons to check them out when you're in the area:

PROS
--They sell coffee and snoballs!  They're the only place I know of that has both.  We didn't try the snoballs this time but our coffees were solid.  They also had a tempting assortment of pastries in the display case.  

--The décor was very NOLA.  Cheerful, eye-popping color greets you at the door.  Inside, the walls are a mix of bright orange and exposed brick.  Black and white photos line the walls along with Jazz Fest works from a local artist.

--The staff was super friendly and welcoming.  No hint of barista-tude, just service with a smile.

--On the day we visited, it was busy but seating was available at café tables and sofas.  They have a stack of board games and a really cool chess set.  We definitely got a sit and stay vibe here.  It's a place to relax, hang out with friends or get work done.

--Parking is free and easy to find on the street a few yards from the entrance.

CONS
--I'm reaching here but the coffeehouse is on the French Quarter Segway tour route.  While we were there a group of tourists made a pit stop at the café instantly doubling the capacity.  Not a big deal unless you're easily distracted.

Treme Coffeehouse is on my short list of best coffee shops I've visited so far in the city.

Willa Jean was swarming with people when we got there for three simple reasons:

Cute restaurant
Instagram worthy food
Delicious flavors

Put those three elements under one roof and crowds will come.  Also factor in that Willa Jean is the brainchild of celebrity Chef John Besh, Chef Kelly Fields and Chef Lisa White so people know she's from a good southern family.

When we got there all the tables were occupied but we slipped in at the countertop in the front window.  Our picks from the brunch menu were fresh juice, Griddled Banana Bread, Crawfish & Grits and BBQ Shrimp Toast.

GRIDDLED BANANA BREAD
I was not ready for this banana bread!  They paired two hunks of nut-free bread with a silky butter and every mouthful was so satisfying.  The bread was perfectly baked with a moist crumb and almost caramelized edges.  I always say you can tell how good a movie is going to be by watching the previews and you can usually tell how good the entrée will be on the strength of the starter.  The second I tasted the banana bread, I knew good things were in store for our entrées.

WILLA JEAN CRAWFISH & GRITS
For the first few enjoyable bites, this dish was essentially crawfish etouffee (crawfish tails smothered in gravy) over grits with mini cheddar biscuits.  Then I dug in for another bite and my fork hit the slow cooked egg hidden inside.  It popped, oozing yolk everywhere and since undercooked eggs gross me out I couldn't deal.  (My guy was happy to take it off my hands.)  I know like 99.9% of Earth's population loves runny eggs but for the rest of us...know that "slow cooked egg" is code for a bursting, oozing egg.

BBQ SHRIMP TOAST
Their version of NOLA BBQ shrimp was profoundly delicious.  The unmistakable fresh-from-the-sea flavor of Gulf shrimp...the crisp sourdough topped with bubbling burrata...a savory sauce for sopping.  I've never had cheese in a BBQ shrimp dish before but now that I've tasted it how can I enjoy other versions again?!?  Just thinking about the flavors again is making my mouth water.

Our perch in the window was good for people watching and the service was brisk.  I didn't enjoy the egg surprise in the Crawfish & Grits but I really loved everything else.  So glad we found our way here and I can't wait to come back.

Damnnnnnnnnn Gina! 
The Mofongo was so good. She gave me a special green sauce to go on it. OMG it was so delicious! 
So I'm going to start a little bit negative... Please don't come to this restaurant asking for vegan and gluten-free mofongo! If you don't know anything about ethnic food, please know that most of our food is meat-based! That's like asking for meatless collard greens! Yeah you can make it but it won't taste like anything... Well it'll taste like paper trash! 
But the food looks good as well as smell good. 
Dessert time!!!
I got this pineapple and coconut type pudding. The smell was that of a warm winter candle. The Taste made me want to sing Christmas carols! Now a restaurant can lose an entire star if their dessert aren't worthy of my palate. I'm big on desserts! Your dessert should make me want to marry you! And for the lady who made that dessert... I'm Yours lady! It was so good! I had to eat it slowly and carefully indulge in every bite! By the way... I was told the desserts change time to time. So whatever the name of this, it had pineapple and coconut in it! I know that's not helpful but do know it was incredibly delicious! I'm sorry but a dessert should make me want to be friendly to my man when he's f---ing up! And that's exactly what this dessert did! 
I will be back... And probably soon! Hats off to the chef! Some ethnic foods are incredibly hard to make. It's too easy to use a bunch of artificial flavorings to enhance the flavor. But this was perfect! It wasn't over season or under season! 
***Also, this restaurant is in Berry Hill*** and it actually has seasonings! And don't act like I'm being funny... You all know that area is known for seasonLESS food! I'm certain over half the restaurants there don't even know what salt it is! 
In short.... five stars in worth it! Every single bite!
One more thing... They have this fruit juice there. Now I'm not saying take a small little thing of rum to put in your fruit juice.... buttttttttt! Well.... wink wink!

Was super excited to try this place for the first time but was disappointed. I just went in for lunch and the employees who had a mask were wearing it under their chin. The kitchen staff did not have mask. Bar staff had no mask at all. We were seated and the server removed his mask to speak, we ended up walking out.

What a wonderful dinner my friends and I had
On the eve of Christmas, the service was grand
We were greeted with warmth and a cozy table for three
Ordered entrees and apps and waited with glee

 7 fishes, gnocchi, and chicken soon came
To our gastronomic delight we savored the same
Desserts were amazing and the check rather low
To this BYOB we recommend that you go! :)

I'm so happy this restaurant finally opened! First things first, Gangchu takes their Covid precautions seriously. Tables were spaced out, masks were worn, and you could see them sanitizing often. 

Another highlight is they're dedicated to paying staff a living wage so a 10% charge is added on to all checks and split between workers. This doesn't bother me at all and actually made me happier to eat there knowing the staff was making a livable wage, but I know some people who complain about a small charge for extra condiments probably think this is outrageous. 

The negative reviews from opening few days aren't an accurate representation as no restaurant ever opens at their best, especially during a pandemic with covid restrictions and precautions in place. 

Honestly, the food was so good. We got 12 boneless wings tossed in the sweet chili garlic sauce. The wings were so fresh, hot, and crispy and the flavors were delicious. The perilla ranch that is served with it was so good and we didn't leave a drop. In fact I paid the 75 cents to take a container home for the leftover wings. Did I mind the charge? No, because these condiments are made in house and not just dumped out of a Heinz bottle. Freshness and quality is always worth a little more. We had the gangchu cheesesteak which was exactly as it was described, a delicious Korean inspired take on the classic Philly cheesesteak. It came out piping hot and the fried that came with it were nice and crispy. We also had the tteokbokki-spicy rice cakes and they were not not what we were expecting but they were delicious. They were more like a pasta than we anticipated but worth the try to venture out of your comfort zone. 

We left with a great experience of the food, drinks, and service. Another gem located in Seminole Heights. I'm excited to go back and try the other sauces for the wings and the other sandwiches and entrees.

Ordering delivery is a rare indulgence for me. During this recent Santa Barbara getaway the foggy weather had us feeling like home bodies so I scoured grubhub for a spot that would suit my tastes/dietary restrictions. 

In fits pizza mizza! They had me at cauliflower pizza- although I did not order that, knowing they served it indicated to me it was my kinda restaurant: emphasis on the healthier/lighter vs. more traditional Italian. 

They had a good selection of salads so I opted for the Greek Goddess. The feta, lettuce, olives and onion were all fresh and the salad was a substantial enough serving I could share with my hubs. I also ordered a side of meatballs and they left me pleasantly surprised. I'm a stickler for meatballs and these were definitely cooked in their marinara sauce which left them flavorful and moist. $3.99 for 3. That feels like a bargain. 

The delivery arrived faster than predicted. The meatballs were warm upon arrival and I was pleasantly surprised to find the cookies  sweet touch that my husband thoroughly enjoyed. 

My pizza mizza order left me feeling mighty satisfied (my weak attempt at Goddess humor- fail?). Next time, we're trying that cauliflower pizza because there will certainly be a next time. Thanks Pizza Mizza!

Casual breakfast restaurant that delivers a reliably tasty breakfast!

We were driving through S.B. trying desperately to find a new breakfast place to try that didn't have a line out the door. We spotted this one from the road and circled back when it looked fairly open. 

It's in a quasi strip mall but is surprisingly bright inside with a homey feel, given the cutesy hanging artwork and large windows. I liked the vibe!

Our server was attentive and friendly. We were seated at a large table for 2 but that was just fine with us. 

Our food arrived and although it was very good, there were a few mistakes with our order. Honestly I'm chalking it up to "newly opened" restaurant jitters. For alI I know we walked into their friends and family soft open but I think as this place evolves and catches their stride, it's going to be a fantastic new breakfast restaurant. Watch out! 

Great eggs & toast, for the record. I loved them & my husband raved about the pancakes.

My favorite Mexican restaurant, probably ever but definitely In Santa Barbara. 
To note: also Julia Child's favorite Santa Barbara Mexican restaurant. 

The flavors here are strong, bold and authentic. The ambiance is non existent, but in some way it's part of the charm? I do like the turquoise trim so that's a plus. Occasionally I feel frustrated with the lines out the door, other tables immediately abutted against you while dining- but then I consider the fact of how good their food is. The fact that I never wait in lines generally. That it is insanely reasonable! And then, when I receive my food, I realize how all worth it it has been because their flavors and the quality of their dishes is outstanding. 

Walk up, check the chalk board menu and order accordingly. You can see the girl making corn tortillas by hand, one by one. 

This place is Cash only & my favorite Mexican restaurant

The flavors here were a surprise to my palette with each bite. 
My friend selected this place & the minute I walked in, I was captivated by the petite bar and cool, modern chic look. Lots of exposed concrete with moments of warm wood. 
Now, I'd been told Nashville had excellent food but I wasn't expecting quite the sparkling flavors I experienced from my salad. With the first bite, the crisp and sweetness hit my tongue. The sweetened orange rind perhaps? Not sure but that vinaigrette too was light, crisp, and tangy. It had the perfect portion of dressing, nuts, and a small bit of blue cheese. 
I splurged & ordered the Turkish sweet potato appetizer and wow, it was divine. Sweet, creamy, spicy, try it. 
We sat at the bar, enjoyed a delicious happy hour wine. Etch is located directly across from the Nashville symphony & perfect for a preshow dinner.

A delicious, Gulch local. It's located in the ever hip Thompson hotel. 
We stopped in for our farewell brunch with all of our dietary restrictions. As with everywhere in Nashville they were super accommodating. 

The meal was outstanding. Everything was fresh as can be and our mimosas divine. The ambiance is lovely but cozy and comfortable. Our waiter very attentive. 

I think it may have been the best omelette I've had with the crab? Superb!

Worth the line? Hmm, can't say yes to that. It's lengthy. 
We were lucky and grabbed a high top outside. 

Oddly, they don't have heating elements above the self seating location but they do around the other outdoor areas that require you to see the hostess to be sat. Um, that's bizarre. Are the managers/owners against keeping the patrons who elected to sit in the first come first serve area warm? Seems very biased to those who "wait" in line. Had to drop a star for that. Just makes zero sense when you're sitting in the alfresco area! We're all paying customers right? Different menus are not circulated. 

Anyway, the lattes were epic, albeit slow for delivering. Ours took about 10-12 minutes respectively. They weren't delivered together. I get it, the place is insanely busy but it's worth noting. 

My omelette was excellent. Plain in appearance but made to my requests. Loved it & fueled me up for my day. 

My friend loved her brûlée grapefruit but we were puzzled as to why they didn't provide a grapefruit spoon? Made digging a bit more challenging. 

Great name, good place, good food. I'd be back, but would bring another jacket if waiting to grab a self seating spot outside. Also I'd hit it on a weekday.

So yes, the rooms are tight. You are snug as a bug in a rug here but boy that location ! We're beach people so close proximity to sandy paradise always attracts our attention. 
We used to visit Santa Barbara quite regularly and when Covid struck, there was a tug pulling us to return. 
SB is just so relaxing.

The room is small but comfy. The pool was shut on our visit but the new renovations feel great. 

We had a sliver of a beach view but it was lovely. 

I can imagine this beach haven will be a blast in summer. Give them a try!

For the quality of the food, flavors, ingredients and the price for the lunch buffet, I just can't give them less than 5 stars. Best value for lunch in Santa Barbara!

We popped in shortly after opening. The buffet was fully loaded & ready. 

They had the typical fare with my favorites tikka masala & tandoori chicken. They were missing my favorite saag paneer- I love that stuff but the chicken curry dish they had was an excellent substitution with strong curry flavor in the sauce. The tandoori chicken was perfectly cooked & not too dry. They had a good selection of wings & breast which was nice. 
I enjoyed the tikka masala but will admit the flavors were a little less rich than I'd like. I love the typical strong Indian seasoning but it may not work for their typical crowd or maybe I went on an off day. 

At the buffet they also had a small Israeli type salad- the chopped cucumber with mint & tomatoes. I love that & was thrilled to see it since I missed my greens in the form of spinach. 
Their additional sauces/seasonings/dishes of condiments were fantastic. Intense, spicy flavor. They were really really great. 

My husband gave their flat bread his stamp of approval too. 

I purchased a to go box for my in law & it was all so reasonable. If I can make my husband crave Indian like I do, we'll be back in no time.

I'm a sucker for tasty, flavored, drip coffee. I just love a flavored cup that isn't bitter & doesn't require coffee mate or some other sugar laden faux creamer to sweeten it. 
Daily Grind helps me through my daily grind by providing a great flavored drip coffee; no unnatural sweetener necessary.

Good place to go and get shot. No really, PYT draws the 'thugs' from the hood. After a few milkshakes spiked with Jim Beam, the egos come out and so do the guns. Last night the inevitable occurred and someone wound up dead. Nice bar.

Wonderful location. Too bad the poorly trained staff and crummy service craps all over that. 

My grievances:
-Room not ready at 3pm
-Bell boys rummaged through my car (after I unpacked it myself for them) and they brought additional items into the room I didn't want. 
-staff at beach bar fighting amongst themselves yelling at eachother to "chill out". (Shut up surfer bro)
-saw beach bar staff shaft people who were waiting for tables
-was repeatedly told by the concierge to "make dinner reservations at carusos once we were settled" and low and behold the restaurant was fully reserved for Friday and Saturday once our room was ready 
-couldn't get ahold of staff via phone without repeated tries
-asked to be transferred to a manager several times and they couldn't figure out the phone system apparently 
-"adult" pool only open till 7pm. 

In summary, most obnoxious guest wins. Be a new-money loud mouth and I'm sure you'll enjoy it.

Mesquite and chiltepin coffee drinks! Say what?! Local! Local! Local! That is what I say. 

Utilizing mesquite and chiltepin in their drinks makes Exo innovative, but it also shows how much they believe in utilizing local resources. Win! Win! Best of both worlds. 

This little mom and pop shop is tops when it comes to crafting your brew for you. They roast their own beans. They believe in excellent products, Strauss milk..only the best mixed into the best. 

I can't recommend them highly enough. We absolutely fell in love with this place on a lazy Sunday afternoon. The actual owners were there manning the shop along with their 5month old baby girl on their hips. So flippin' cute! 

We chatted about harvesting mesquite and chiltepin...they harvest their own from the mountains and surrounding environs. They are enthusiasts about every aspect of the coffee and coffee making process as well as local resources and high quality products. I can't imagine a  better cup of coffee being had in Tucson. Exo is the place to go. 

Oh and I love the record player. Looks like they have amassed quite a selection of records that sing about the town of Tucson. Way cool!

In house Pasteurization is what sets this ice cream apart.  Less than 5 ice cream shops in the entire United States Pasteurize their diary products in house. It's an expensive process, but the owner of the Screamery is ice cream obsessed, and he wanted to produce the best ice cream possible. 

Ice cream aficionados will appreciate the subtleties of flavor that this process imparts upon the ice cream. The flavors will be more imbedded into the ice cream, especially alcoholic flavors. The bourbon ice cream will taste like the best bourbon ice cream in the world thanks to the pasteurization. The booze will taste like it's part of the ice cream DNA instead of feeling like it's just being worn like a winter coat. Can you say creamy? This is ridiculously rich and creamy stuff!

The owner came from the construction business. Check out his beefy forearms! He is an all around American Dude. The shop will have country music playing and the polo shirt that the owner wears is bright construction orange reminiscent of his previous career. He isn't a chef or hipster foodie but he does know to use quality organic ingredients. His flavors are good old-fashioned American inspired. Thinks Hans homemade for those in California. 

Whole Foods has already approached him to carry his ice cream in their shops, which is awesome. The Screamery could use the business, being located on the edge of Tucson, far away from the University Crowd, schools, and the main touristy part of town. The investment into the pasteurization process was steep and it is nice to see that he is on his way to getting a return for it. 

All around nice guy, who is learning the ice cream business as he does it. He didn't do market research to select a location. He just jumped right in and opened a shop close to home. 

There is so much to love about this place. The naiveté of the owner, the amazingness of the product and the charm of special construction touches  to appeal to children. Love the little astroturff covered footstool that allows kiddos to step and and press their noses up against the ice cream case to select a flavor. Also love the large open repurposed wood counter(made from a nearby defunct bowling alley-notice the markings for where you'd line up your ball) which allows kids to plop up and watch the pasteurization process. Also loved that he didn't know much about Yelp, or how it worked, and was surprised to find that he was the first place that popped up when you searched for ice cream in Tucson. 

I'm glad we went out of our way to patronize the Screamery. It was a very memorable ice cream experience. It was a luxurious treat to taste ice cream that was produced in this manner. Good luck guys! We'll be back to visit next time we are in town.

I'm giving this restaurant one star (frankly it deserves no stars)- not because of the mediocre food or the dingy atmosphere, but because of the despicable service I received both while at the restaurant and afterward when I confronted them about overcharging my debit card. 

A group of 7 of us girls went to this restaurant. I only authorized $30 to be charged to my debit card and was not offered a copy of my receipt and to my regret I did not ask for one. I came home and checked my bank account and they charged me the entire bill. I called right away and asked for the owner. The hostess told me to call back at 4pm to speak with the accountant, Kathy. I promptly did. She promised to call back after she dug into the previous weeks checks. She called me back and apologized for their mistake and that they would send me a money order for the difference. I waited 2 weeks and no resolve. I called again and this time she backtracked and made me speak to the waiter we had, Gio, who tried to give me the runaround and spewed out lies. Promised to call me back the next day and he would make it right. NEVER got a call and at this point I was furious and still am. 

I am thoroughly disgusted by the people that are employed at the restaurant. You would think any restaurant that wants business and to keep a good standing would do anything to keep their customers happy. I have put a complaint into the Better Business Bureau. I don't recommend anyone to dine here. Beware.

Tried this place based on a colleague who lives in Philly.  Said it was a really good Asian restaurant and to my surprise had Ramen options  on the menu.

Spoke with the waitress about the Ramen options and opt for pots belly Ramen.  Presentation was terrific, full body flavor, delicate noodles, perfectly cook egg and of course the main ingredient, the tender pork.  

I did start the dumpling appetizer which was explained as being like a soup dumpling, was more nice egg roll with soupy taste.  One of the two was over cooked and crunchy while the other seemed spot on per waitress description.

Was quite surprised and pleased overall.

So me, my husband and my 5 month old baby went here about a week ago and let me tell you why it was one of the worst experiences I've ever had.

While we were heading there, we called and spoke to a younger guy and was told they were out of some other dishes but still have lechon kawali and chicken sisig. He mentioned that they were busy but didn't mention they were gonna close early. When we arrived there 10 minutes later, the doors were already locked and it was only about 7PM (sign on the door says they close at 8PM). After a minute, an older gentleman came out and told us that they were closed and that they are running out food saying that the kitchen was closing. We told him that we just spoke to someone over the phone just a little while ago and was told that they still had food, but all he told us was that he was sorry and that he cant let us in.

My point is how can they operate when they dont have enough food? If you close at 8PM, you close at 8PM. If you ran out of food, then cook!

And i later found out my aunt came here for the buffet and were baffled to see that they only had 6 items on their buffet. And 2 of those 6 items are rice and soup!

Went there last night to check it out, and was underwhelmed. Granted, they've only been open for 6 days, but I expected a little more for the price. I met up with a friend at 4:30 and we basically had the place to ourselves - yet it took almost 30 minutes for our food to arrive (including our pork bun appetizers). 

The pork buns were cold - not sure if they were supposed to be that way or just got cold because they were waiting for the ramen to be done.

I ordered the traditional Ramen, and it was just ok. The pork belly seemed fattier than usual, and the broth was pretty bland. I've had ramen in Los Angeles and New York that had more flavor and cost less. This place wasn't even table service (walk up to order and pay) and I still paid $18 for 1 pork bun, ramen and a glass of ice water.

The decor was nice, the staff was friendly, but I don't see myself going back. Between the meter parking, the cramped community tables, the overall tininess of the restaurant, the price, and the lackluster flavor, I'm not in love. There are a few other ramen spots popping up, and I'll likely be checking those out.

First of all, if I had the opportunity, I would rate this place a zero (no stars) but not able so they get 1 star. Honestly, we ate there a week ago and I am still disgusted at the experience. When we were seated, we were told that we could not order wine by the glass. Ok, so we ordered a bottle of wine (party of 4.) We were then presented with a menu featuring 4 courses for $55 per person. My first course was scallops with a cilantro sauce. Please note, the references to portion sizes are NOT embellished but actual. The plate came out with 4 scallops the size of dimes with droplets of green sauce. I could have EASILY piled all four scallops on one fork. My husband ordered the tartare. This came out in the portion of MAYBE a tablespoon and 1/2 over ONE cracker. The next course was a sweat bread ravioli. Yep, you got it. ONE ravioli and barely enough stuffing to even taste it. Third course was lamb. 4 Slices of thinly sliced lamb with absolutely NO flavor over approx. 3 tablespoons of some lentil mush. Not to bore you with what everyone ate, but the final straw was dessert. Chocolate layer cake with espresso mousse. What a joke. I wish I could draw a picture. The cake came out on a 12 x 12 plate and the wedge was the size of a medium size strawberry. The express mousse was no more than a tablespoon. The waitress then proceeds to ask us if we would like more wine and then informs us that we can order the wine we are having by the glass now... Really?? Why now and not at the beginning of the meal? The tables are very close together, and we spent the better part of the evening shouting because the table of six next to us were right on top of us. The lighting is dreary at best. And here is the best part: with tip, our bill was over $400. We ate on our way home. My husband and I are not big eaters and appreciate smaller portions when dining out, however this was an insult--really. What a disappointment.  I will be surprised if this restaurant makes it a year. Certainly the neighborhood where this is situated cannot afford these prices. Shame.

1.  The food here is outstanding.  The roast chicken is, without exaggeration, the best roast chicken I've had anywhere in the world.  The flavor is intensely bird-like, the white meat is juicy, and the lacquered skin is as addictive as crack.  Their pastas are perhaps the best deal in the city. But do not skip the appetizers (elevated but completely unpretentious) and definitely stay for the desserts.  The Labneh panna cotta is to die for.

2.  The downstairs bar is the coolest bar in all of Philly, with a long marble countertop, and black and white checker floor. It's understated, elegant, and pure class - I want my living room to look like this.  Again, with zero pretense.  The friendliest bartenders in town.  Sasha is 100% sweetheart & can make me smile even after I've had the shittiest 12 hour travel day.  And while Paul's "Assassin's Handbood" was named best cocktail by Philadelphia Magazine, I'm pretty I've had at least 3 other cocktails from him that were better, like the one with some essence of smoked eggplant that was from another planet.

3. Husband and wife team Chad and Hannah are amazing, generous people.  Kudos to them for creating this amazing restaurant.  It's people like them doing things like this that make me love this city and proud to call it home.

What a pleasant surprise!  This restaurant just opened 6 days ago and what a great meal we had tonight!  It's located in the former Tri-City Plaza corner at East Bay and US19.  It's in the strip center just north of Chili's.  The interior is shiny and new with an upscale feel.  There are lots of cozy booths to choose from.  We were quickly greeted and seated. 

For appetizers, we started with the Tom Kha with chicken and the Tom Yum with shrimp. (see pics)  They were both great with bold flavors.  We also ordered their Sampler Platter.  The pot stickers were outstanding.

For entrèes,  we ordered the Panang Duck and the Nam Sod. (see pics)  They were beautifully presented and tasted fresh and delicious.  As you can see, they were huge portions.  I would order both of the dishes again.  

Overall, we had a great dining experience!  It has a new and shiny dining room and had very nice bathrooms.  The service was quick and friendly.  Our iced tea glasses never got below half full.  Despite the fact that they had just opened, I'm was quite surprised that they were so organized.

With an ownership change at Thai Town, a new awesome sushi and Asian fusion restaurant has been born.  Due to the great Yelp reviews, we decided to give it a try. We were pleasantly surprised to discover folks we knew from and the prior owner of Thai Town. The same wonderful recipes that we are very familiar with followed them across the street. YAY! The overall atmosphere is airy and the wait staff is exceeding friendly.  Emma was our waitress.  We felt immediately relaxed.

As always, we were starving.  We first ordered soup.  I ordered the Tom Kha with chicken(Thai hot) and my partner ordered the Tom Yum with shrimp(med.).  OMG, both soups were exceptional and had a depth of flavor we could not remember eating elsewhere in the Tampa Bay area.  At this point, we realized that we were in for an amazing meal.

For appetizers, we opted for their steamed dumping special that was shrimp based and the chicken satay.  The dumplings were large, hot and very tasty.  We will order them again.  The chicken satay was a little chewy and could have used more of a char on them but the dipping sauce made up for any missteps.

As a courtesy, we were given small ginger salads for an intermezzo before our entrees. The dressing, on this simple salad, was bright and flavorful.

For entrees, we ordered the Panang duck and the sweet and sour shrimp.  The duck was extra meaty and the Panang had a depth of flavor that had hints of a variety of spices that were not in the canned paste bases that seem to be the norm, elsewhere.  The sweet and sour sauce was another wonderful surprise.  It was not the standard thin sauce but it had a substantial consistency with lots of pineapple pieces and other veggies.  It would be wonderful just by itself over some rice.   

The sushi menu will be explored in depth on our next visit.  We left with smiles on our faces. SCORE!  We have a new favorite Thai restaurant!

I've driven by Our Place many times over the years and this morning I decided to stop in for breakfast.  I was quickly greeted and seated in a nice booth.  Both coffee and water promptly arrived.

From a very large breakfast menu, I ordered a Ham and Cheese Omelette with hash browns and whole wheat toast. (see pic)  The food came out very quickly and it was awesome!  The ham in the omelette had been seared on the grill first and then diced...delicious!  The omelette was packed with ham.  Most importantly, the omelette was NOT overcooked.  A lot of diners seem to brown their omelettes and I don't like it!  The hash brown were crispy and plentiful.

Overall, I had a great breakfast!  It is a wonderful feeling when you stop by an new restaurant on a whim and end up getting a delicious meal.  I will most definitely return and I can recommend the breakfast!

Oh Applebee's, what happened to your Mojo?

Back in the day, it looked like you had Chili's lined up in your sites and "Bam!"; you over expanded, forgot about quality control and now UR closing places as fast as you use to open them. 

Today's lunch experience is a good example. We arrived at noon and were welcomed by a very competent greeter who showed us very quickly to our table. Nice beginning.

But no matter how courteous our server Naomi was, she could not make up for the m'eh food here. Btw, she was great. 

We orders the Ultimate Trio which didn't look anything like the menu picture (see photos) for $14.99 and the American BLT for 8.99 (again see photo). It had nothing but crunchy bacon bits. Both were wilted and looked and tasted as if they had been sitting in the window for a while. 

Our tab for two came to $31.24. Sorry, we'll pass in the future.

Bisbee Breakfast is a fun place to stop, if only for the coffee and energetic service. 

We came here this past week around 9:30.  They weren't too busy and thankfully we didn't wait long. A group of Tucson's Finest was just finishing up and we timed it just right. Always a good sign, when you see it's popular with our first responders in blue!

What impressed us most, was the energy of our server Dylan. He was like a whirling dervish (https://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=Whirling%20Dervish) and fun to watch in action.  LOL 

Their barista on the other hand, was so slow with our expresso drinks arrived after our food. As for the food, it was pretty good. The French Toast however was cut way too thick(photo) and was more like bread with a eggy outer shell. Sorry

Our bill, including taxes but before gratuities, came to $33.44. So expect to pay $15.00+ each.  Overall, the coffee is as good as anything found at the green siren.  It was worth the wait and certainly a reason to stop at Bisbee Breakfast. 

Three Stars, "A-Okay"

Life is about taking the good with the bad.  Or, if life hands you lemons, then go make some lemonade. LOL

We had a negative experience in Bisbee today, which was more of a distraction, than an annoyance. After resting up, we decided to come to Shlomo & Vito's for some comfort food and we're glad we did. 

S & V likes to market themselves as a genuine Brooklyn New York Deli. We agree. The service is first rate and our server Josh was outstanding!  The deli meats are all Boars Head, and they even have Dr Brown cream soda. Nice. 

We started off with some kosher dill pickle chips, shared a Pastrami on marble rye bread, a knish and finished with a huge slice of Carrot Cake. Remember, I said we were sharing,. But we just couldn't finish it all. There was just too much food. In the end, we took two fork fills of the cake and asked for a box. LOL

The bill came to $26.08 including taxes but not gratuities. One word about the knish.  It was made fresh with pieces of potato and had a flaky exterior. It might not be like the one on a Sabrett's cart in Manhattan, but we liked it just the same.   A shout out to Tammara W for her review, now we love Shlomo & Vito's too. 

Enjoy!

Scordatos is a Neapolitan style pizza restaurant. There's no wood fired brick oven that we could observe, but the pizza was very good. 

After reading my friend Susan P's review, we knew we had to come here. I guess her BF knows his pizza. 

We started off with two glasses of wine ($7.50 each), one Cartidge & Brown Pinot, the other Montepulciano de Abruzzo Capestrano.  Both were tasty and had no alcohol residue or bite 

Next we decided to split a Caesar for $5.50. Our server Nate was on top of his game all night and offered to serve it on two plates. Nice!  Btw, he never let the water glasses stay empty for long and politely checked in from time to time. 

We ordered a 1/2 Margherita and 1/2 Sausage & Roasted Cipollini Onion pizza. It was great. The crust was perfect and the tomato sauce tasted very fresh.  Thank you Susan (and Susan's BF) for a great review and Tip!

Our bill came to $39.26 including taxes, but before gratuities. We'll be back. 

Enjoy!

This family-owned Bagel Shop is just what South Jersey needed. My husband and I are always on the hunt for the best bagels in town. Well, we found it!

The bagels are made fresh daily with a huge variety of flavors to choose from including the cream cheese selection!

You can order your bagel any style you want: fresh, lightly toasted, sandwich style, topped with an egg and Pork Roll, etc. 

This place is quite popular and can definitely see why. Don't be disappointed if you don't see the flavors you want because most likely everyone else gobbled them up earlier!

This is a very very very small boutique pastry/pie shop. The pies and scones are delicious. The scones are probably the best I've had in a long time. My favorite is the lemon blueberry scone; highly recommend.

Street parking only and it is usually not difficult to get a parking spot.

There are a few picnic tables outside for you to enjoy a scone or piece of pie with a cup of coffee on a nice sunny day. Take out is easy.

Note: Cash Only

Very impressed with Kunkel's with both my husband and I agreeing 'why we haven't been here before?'

Steaks were cooked to order and cooked perfectly the way we like our steaks - medium rare leaning towards rare. 

Plenty of food and can't beat the prices given that it's the ONLY steakhouse in the area that is BYOB. Where can you go locally and get great food, bring your own wine to pair with your meal, receive great service and delicious food? (waiting for your answer.....) LOL.

We will certainly be back and bring friends and family. When we want a steak, we're heading to Kunkel's. They accept reservations on OpenTable.

Best cheesesteak outside of Philly. Haven't been to the Camden location but highly recommend stopping by Donkey's in Medford.
