The pizza came out great! I couldn't finish the whole thing so I had left overs. The crust is nice and crispy but still chewy. I just didn't like the little black crumbs at the bottom but I dealt with it.

Overall it's nice to see Pieology finally arrive and I look forward to going back when I'm in the area.

This might be an unpopular rating but I assure you that Vivace earned it.

We started with a plate of asparagus, prosciutto, grilled zucchini, olives, marinated red peppers, spinach and toast with a creamy spread.  This plate was absolutely delightful in every way - all fresh ingredients and a clever way to present an antipasto.  They must have run out of their usual rectangular plates as this time they presented it on a round plate, but it was still exquisite.

Salmon and linguine and the seafood soup:  seafood soup was very tasty, though scant on the shrimp/scallops but heavy on the salmon.  The linguine was nicely flavored with capers and olives to lend a saltiness, and overall was a success, despite a small puddle of oil on the plate after everything was consumed.

The disappointment began with the hostess who suffers from CHS (see my review of Sakura for "Crappy Hostess Syndrome").  We were meeting the person who made the reservation, who was already seated.  While another hostess walked a party to their table, this hostess said "oh yeah, she's at a table down this hall and near the window."  Thanks, we'll go looking for her while you sit there.

Then the service was spotty at best.  Refills were rare.  I think you can safely tell that you won't be seeing your server often when a table is pre-set with a water pitcher on it - you will be serving yourself.  Acceptable at a place like The Heist, where it's more casual.  However, Vivace in the Foothills with lush interiors, gorgeous views, and expensive menu should fix this.

Our server asked if we were ready to order - we asked for 5 more minutes.  Those 5 minutes turned in to her taking 2 other tables orders who were seated well after us, and then disappearing for a while - equals about 20 minutes.  After taking our order, she disappeared again for about 25 minutes until we got the appetizer, and then again, making our lunch last almost 2 hours.

Final noteworthy comment - when the reservation was made, Vivace was reluctant to even accept the reservation until they asked the name on it (tacky) and changed their tune.  At the time of service, the server told the head of the party that she could not offer the dinner menu that day as they were too busy to offer it (even though they had in the past on other busy days).  This sets a terrible precedent - either ALWAYS or NEVER offer menus at different times, period.

While we're at it, either take a reservation or don't if you're too busy - lest you overcrowd the kitchen and make service suffer, as was evident.

I feel that we will give them another chance, but they must prove that their service level has risen above the pool of oil under the linguine, at the very least.

I'm being sympathetic with 2 stars.  I know, dear reader, that I can be a bit of a snot in some of my lower rating reviews so I'm going to leave out the fancy boogers and blow my nose clean of why I don't like this place.

The concept is great, just as Mark S. stated in his review.  Reclining chairs, servers bringing you food while you sit comfortably.  And that's what it has going for it.

I find eating in the dark isn't fun, and it actually takes away from the quality of the food.  I don't know that I've had any food here that I actually enjoy or desire, and I've tried the gyro, the pizzas, the "gourmet" popcorn.  All of it is just so-so.  I also think that it's a nuisance to pre-order your seats, since these are smaller auditoriums it is almost necessary - and rare that you ever get in as a "walk-in".

Minor issue #1 is that the prices really don't quite justify what you get.  The $13.50 I paid per ticket online last night was to recline while watching a new movie, since I don't really like the food.  And if I did like the food, I would be paying a rough average of $9 per item anyway plus tax / tip, so the inflated initial buy-in price only compensates the theater for the reclining chairs limiting their capacity.

Minor issue #2 is the bothersome lights located near your seats that, while necessary to see the menu or bill, are distracting when you're trying to watch the movie since they are at eye level.

MAJOR ISSUE:  My son got sick eating here.  We absolutely narrowed it down to this food.  I gave my number and name to the manager upon leaving, and he had absolutely NO follow up.  No phone call, no real apology, no offer to refund the food that made him sick, just absolutely nothing.  This was back when Mad Max came out, months ago.

Follow-up to MAJOR ISSUE:  Last night, leaving the bathroom, there was an employee wearing his Roadhouse shirt who used the bathroom and left without washing his hands.  Unacceptable.

So, I don't see value in returning, and will definitely never order any food or drink here if we do.

It's not very often that I find myself on the low-end of a Yelp rating spectrum, but at least for now this appears to be the case for The Missing Brick, a new and locally owned pizza joint on the northeast side of Indy that opens at 5pm from Thursday-Sunday. 

I had high hopes for this visit based upon initial reviews, though I couldn't help but notice that six of the first few reviews were folks having only 1-2 reviews total. 

Friends, perhaps?

I dunno. Regardless, I'm glad they're happy. "The Missing Brick" is located in a small strip center alongside Morellis Cleaners and Uptown Cafe. I believe it took the spot vacated by a BBQ joint. 

There's a couple accessible parking spots right about the mid-point of the short building. It has an appropriate curb cut. There's a single glass door into The Missing Brick. As you enter, there's a row of high-top, bench seats along the window on the right, three high-top tables directly to the right, and 3-4 benches that are lower to the left. You go straight forward to the ordering counter. 

It seemed like a majority of their business was take out, though I did see one couple dining in. They are definitely set up for dining in, though all beverages are cans/bottles including soft drinks, water, and they do have some beer options. There's no iced tea option - a definite bummer for me. 

They basically offer some salad options along with a handful of pizza options plus a BYO option. Pizzas are all one size - starting around $12 with most either $14 or $16. 

I ordered the OG - essentially their meat lovers option - along with a bottled water. It's a 12" pizza made Detroit Style (square).  While it's listed as "individual," I'm guessing it would suffice for 2 people and I certainly didn't finish it. 

As has been noted, The Missing Brick is 21+ only. 

You definitely have an adult vibe - I mean, you have a pizza joint calling itself a "dope" pizza joint and the name is "The Missing Brick." Um, figure it out. (FYI - I actually find this quite clever if maybe a bit weird for marketing). 

So, the rating? Why not a 5 like the majority?

First off, accessibility is a concern. We know that matters to me. We also know the lack of an iced tea option bugs me. Minor issues, but easily 1/2 - 1 star off issues. 

The pizza was solid. I see why folks love it. I will admit I found the crust a tad chewier than expected, but the flavor was awesome. I'm guessing I'd put the pizza at a 4-star. It's a bit much for one person, but it would be great for two. 

The crew? As has been universally noted, super friendly and very helpful. 

Atmosphere? Hated it. Seriously. I love hip-hop music but this was excessively loud to the point I couldn't hear anyone. While I'm far from a prude, I also found the selections a bit questionable for a public venue. I will admit that I tend to prefer quiet dining, though even a place like Kuma's has some appeal. This music was FAR louder than Kuma's. I guess maybe I'm a bit old-fashioned, but I don't think a public restaurant should be playing music with obscenities or sexualized language. 

I had planned to eat in, but by the time I received my pizza I was so over it that I decided to take it home. The design/decor is generally pleasing, but overall I'd go with a 2-star for atmosphere. I am aware that atmosphere would be pleasing, or at least fine, to some folks but it's worth noting. It also appears from some other reviews that the musical selections may change. So, perhaps on another occasion I'd be fine. 

Overall, I appreciated the people, enjoyed the pizza, spent more than I wanted, couldn't stand the thought of actually eating there, and generally thought this was a decent but not great experience. I can't picture myself rushing back, but for those who want to support a locally owned pizza joint with a unique vibe then I wholeheartedly support giving it a chance and finding out if it is for you. 

Open limited hours, The Missing Brick is one of the more unique experiences with a vibe all its own. Just remember - no kids!

I've wanted to visit New Bethel Ordinary for quite some time. I've always managed to convince myself it's too far of a drive. Located in the heart of downtown Wanamaker, New Bethel Ordinary is only a few minutes outside the Indy city limits heading Southeast. It's an easy drive and worth it. 

"The Ordinary," as it is most often called, has a wonderfully retro vibe and feels as if it belongs in the heart of a small downtown area (That's a compliment). While you can easily feel like an outsider with some small-town diners, there's a quick sense of welcome here in The Ordinary. Wanamaker is part of Indy and the school district is Franklin Township. It was annexed in 1970. 

The Ordinary is most known for its pizzas. I seriously contemplated pizza but having had a large meal yesterday I decided ordering an entire pizza while dining alone was out of the question. So, I took the opportunity to check out the hand-breaded tenderloin. You get two sides with it - I choose fries and cole slaw. 

Of course, I ordered my usual unsweetened iced tea. I resisted the urge to get a beer. 

The Ordinary is right on Southeastern. This is the downtown Main Street for Wanamaker. Downtown is a bit of a stretch, but it's the business area for this unincorporated town first settled Reuben and Mary Adams in 1825. A year later, Reuben died and left Mary as a single mother of 11 in what was then Indiana wilderness. In 1834, it was Mary who arranged for the laying out of the town. Originally, Wanamaker was known as New Bethel and you'll see Bethel on quite a few things within the town's boundaries. It is now named after John Wanamaker, the U.S. Postmaster General when New Bethel got its first post office. 

Okay, back to The Ordinary. This is a free-standing building. It's a decent size and they also have a nice patio off to the side. There's also a deck in the back that has 2-3 tables. Today, everyone was inside but I'm sure that would change by day's end. 

If you're in a wheelchair like me, you'll want to use the front entrance. The back entrance has a step going into it. The front is level to the ground. There's a couple parking spots directly in front and a parking lot in the back. However, the parking lot isn't the greatest for wheelchairs as it's semi-crushed gravel. I was able to maneuver it fine, but it was a bit of a hassle. Going in, a customer helped me with the door. Going out, a server grabbed the door. 

As you enter, you're immediately in the dining room. It's a combo of wood booths, tables, and 1/2 booths. There are widescreen televisions. The place just feels relaxing. It seemed very family friendly and it seemed like most of the servers were high school students and/or younger servers. 

The vibe is very friendly, and the servers seemed to enjoy working there. It was relaxed but professional. 

My server, Jaida, was spot-on. She was friendly, attentive, helpful, and personable. I got an iced tea to go which I always appreciate. She also knew to pull the chair out for the wheelchair. 

The food was wonderful and generous in serving size. I thought I was cutting back by not getting pizza, but I was wrong. The tenderloin was wonderful with a nice thickness and moist meat. The fries were generous and nicely seasoned. I had low expectations looking at the cole slaw, but I really enjoyed it. 

I was honestly stuffed after my meal. The meal came in at just over $13 without a tip. 

The menu is soups/salads, appetizers, sandwiches, pizzas, wings, bar drinks, craft beer, and they do have a kids' menu. They also cater. 

Ordinarily, I'd take off a one-half to 1 star because of the parking lot and minor accessibility issues. However, I really enjoyed this experience and will go back. The service was wonderful. The food was great. The prices were fair. This was exactly what I needed on this Sunday afternoon!

I am not a hipster. 

I am not a wannabe hipster. 

Heck, I'm not really even a nerd. I'm just me. I'm an average joe, an elite Yelper, and manic lover of just about everything Indy. I've always had a hit-and-miss relationship with Patachou establishments precisely because I tend to become irritated as heck with the vibe that says "You're lucky we're serving you" rather than "We're lucky to have you as our customer." 

I admire the Patachou enterprise. I respect Martha Hoover. I adore the Patachou foundation. It just seems like I always have less than stellar experiences when it comes to the actual dining. 

I'd been wanting to try out Crispy Bird, the Patachou establishment at 49th & Penn devoted to all things chicken. Crispy Bird was named by Eater and Tasting Table as one of the hottest restaurant openings in the nation in 2017. So, take my review with a grain of salt - there are apparently people who've had better experiences. 

Straight from the Crispy Bird website, which reports that they serve  American Freedom Ranger, a breed raised specifically for Crispy Bird by Gunthorp Farms, are plant-based sides, locally sourced vegetables and greens, homemade cultured butter and from-scratch biscuits and breads-- all skillfully crafted and beautifully presented, seasonally inspired soft serve and homemade desserts, a full cocktail bar and an edited wine list consisting of old and new world wines."

If you know this area of town, you know that parking is almost exclusively street parking. This can be a pain for those with mobility issues, but it's a modestly traveled street and people in this area tend to be considerate. There's a ramp heading into Crispy Bird and the floor plan is generally roomy enough - if it got packed, there may be limited options for someone in a wheelchair as the tables are pretty tightly packed in. 

I arrived in the late afternoon. I'd ended a work meeting early and hadn't had time for lunch. So, I figured a good late lunch/early dinner would be a nice way to spoil myself. Crispy Bird was empty, though within a few moments a second diner did arrive. I had my choice of tables. 

Things started off promisingly. I was greeted in a friendly manner and the menu with still, bottled water arrived promptly. I did acknowledge it was my first visit - I got a warm welcome, though no real explanation of anything (which will eventually become a factor). 

The menu is fairly basic. They have snacks, think modestly priced appetizers, along with sides/small plates and fried chicken/mains. All of the mains except for one are chicken - the one being a Nashville hot cauliflower. 

I ordered the "Fried chicken sandwich, spicy aioli, pickles,
coleslaw," though I'll confess that I assumed the coleslaw was a side and was surprised, not pleasantly, to find it on the sandwich. In hindsight, I could've asked; they also could have clarified, though it's probably obvious to them. I've just never heard of it before and, in fact, never seen it before. The sandwich comes in at $10 with no side (sides are a la carte). I did order my usual unsweetened iced tea. The entire bill came in at just over $14 without a tip. Generally speaking, you should plan on $15-20 unless you choose to order craft brews or wine - that will obviously take your bill higher. 

I really wrestled with how to rate my experience. 

As I noted, I was surprised by the coleslaw on the sandwich. I certainly can't completely fault them and I would certainly know now if I should return (I won't). While I've had coleslaw on pulled pork, and at times even enjoyed it, it's just not a selection I'd have made if I'd realized it. 

Rather than eat it as a sandwich, I ended up simply eating the chicken. The serving size was certainly huge and the seasoning was definitely favorable. It wasn't the best chicken I've had, but it was unique and I could see where some would view it more favorably. 

I considered a 3-star rating because this was a mid-range experience for me. The service was functional, though certainly never made me want to return. For a $3 iced tea, I'd expect at least one refill (and if you've been reading my reviews for a while, you know I take my iced tea seriously). I just got this overall vibe after it became apparent I wasn't eating the "sandwich" that felt negative. Was it negative? I don't know. It "felt" negative. There was never any inquiry into it - even after I at one point said "It's better not as a sandwich." If I were a server, I'd have inquired. I'd have at least acted like I cared. 

So, I paid over $14 for a meal I didn't expect, that wasn't particularly filling and was fairly middle-of-the-road in terms of taste. The service was also fairly middle-of-the road, but here's the kicker - the difference for me between a 2 and a 3 star is "Will I go back?" Honestly? I won't return. 

I don't mind paying a premium price, but I expect a premium product and experience in return. I didn't get it.

I had high hopes that today would be the long awaited day that I would finally make my visit to Ale Emporium happen. A staple of the Castleton area since the early 80's, Ale Emporium is one of those places I've always wanted to visit but for a variety of reasons simply haven't with the exception of one previous visit prior to my Yelping days when I dropped in for a fundraiser that was going on. 

I've long heard terrific things about Ale Emporium's food and I've long appreciated their support of a variety of local causes. As a locally owned business, I'm aware they do support their community. 

One of the reasons I've struggled to visit Ale Emporium is that their parking situation is fairly dreadful. They're in an older strip center that has accessible parking, yet it's limited and only truly ADA compliant at the other end of the strip in front of a furniture store. There's nothing directly by Ale Emporium with the exception of one weirdly situated spot across the parking lot that isn't close to ADA compliant. Seriously, it's not. 

It seems like every time I've driven by, I've been unable to find a spot where I was convinced I'd be safe to go in, enjoy a meal, and trust that when I returned to my car I could actually get in it. So, I haven't visited. 

Today, however, I was able to find a non-accessible spot in the front of an aisle. It allowed me to get out of my wheelchair on the side facing the street - thus, I had no risk of being blocked in. That worked for me. There's a ramp in front of a rug store that works pretty well. 

I entered and was immediately aware that they had, in fact, renovated. They'd placed the stage toward the front and created a variety of seating options - essentially dividing the place into a bar area and a more traditional dining/stage area. I entered through the glass doors and was immediately struck by the significant number of high-top tables in the main dining area. It seemed like a weird, very busy design but it wasn't really a deterrent. 

I looked around and couldn't find a single low-top table in the main dining area. I even wheeled toward the back. I've faced this once before in another local bar and grill type setting, so I really tried to make sure I was correct. It's weird to me that in 2019 a restaurant could literally provide zero options for those with disabilities, mobility issues, or simply who don't want to sit in a high-top setting. 

Do they have low-top tables? I couldn't find any. I passed three employees, none of whom offered any help (Admittedly, I also did not ask mostly because I thought I'd eventually find a place). 

By the time I wheeled around the dining area, I lost hope and started to leave. I saw a couple more employees near the bar area, however, and detoured that direction. While bars are notoriously less accessible, I figured at least I might get some help. 

Nope. And nope. 

I still couldn't find a table option and there was no help to be found. For the record, it was late afternoon and business was brisk but definitely not busy. 

While I generally don't write reviews without a full experience, my rule is that if I visit your business and it's the business's fault that I couldn't fully patronize them that they're fair game for a review. I was here. I was fully in the business. I tried to find an accessible table and/or service. I couldn't find either one despite literally wheeling through the entire business. 

So, I left. 

I truly hope that there's something I missed here. I'm most certainly open to being wrong, but if I go out of my way to patronize your business and your business isn't just as welcoming to me then not only will you not get my business but my review is going to reflect my disappoint in your poor accessibility and business practices. 

I will also note that they do have an outside patio area that has some lower tables, though it was off and on rainy today. 

So for now, I'd wholeheartedly caution customers with disabilities that this appears to be a business that will not welcome you. If I'm proven incorrect, I will happily rewrite my review based upon a future experience. 

NOTE: As of 7/6/19, a member of Ale Emporium Management reached out to me and shared that there is a backroom section that offers low tables. While I'm not necessarily satisfied with that as an optimal solution, it could well impact my review. I have promised a return visit in the near future and will update my review as appropriate!

I was not one of the legions of fans eagerly anticipating the arrival of Indy's first Giordano's, a Chicago pizza institution since its arrival in 1974 and most famous for its stuffed crust pizza. However, after a long week at work and in anticipation of an expected weekend snowstorm, I decided to spoil myself on this Friday evening and pay a visit to the restaurant during its first few days of opening and, in fact, before its official opening on February 3rd. 

You could tell that they were still working out the kinks in their systems. As much as they'd been expecting a warm reception from Indianapolis, it seemed like the reception they are getting has overwhelmed them a bit. For those who know Giordano's, you know that their stuffed crust pizza isn't a quick fix with a typical waiting time of 45 minutes to an hour. Tonight, I arrived in the early evening hours and was told to possibly expect 90 minutes and, truth be told, it was more like two hours until my pizza arrived. 

The waiting area out front is also not a large area and, at times, it seemed like a controlled yet chaotic mess. 

Let's just say that if you went expecting to have your usual quick meal at Pizza Hut, you'd likely end up stressed out and frustrated. I personally hope that doesn't happen, because even with some kinks left to work out this is an exceptional experience. 

Giordano's is not only the kind of place where you can actually chill out and enjoy your friends and a meal, it's the kind of place where you really need to chill out and enjoy your friends and a meal. If you order the stuffed crust pizza, you're going to be there a minimum of one hour - you know it, they know it. It's awesome and relaxing and maybe a little bit strange to not feel immense pressure to hurry up, eat your meal, get your one refill, then leave. 

Enjoy your meal.

The restaurant is quite wheelchair friendly and, in what I've never seen before, even has a wheelchair friendly bar with one side of the bar that has a couple spots that are lowered to allow for someone in a wheelchair to easily sit at the bar. I was assured by staff that this decision was quite intentional. While the decision has a couple flaws, for example being a tad too close to the kitchen and being in an easy location for those who want to walk up to the bar and order a drink and disturb your meal, it's still a rare design perk and I really enjoyed myself there. The one time I was bumped by a server, they apologized PROFUSELY. 

It's rare for me, but knowing I'd be waiting for my pizza I did decide to order an appetizer - their cheesy garlic bread at $6.95. While that may sound a bit high, I can assure you it's a quite healthy serving and easily shared amongst 2-3 people. While I'm usually a fan of good old-fashioned garlic bread, this was simply outstanding with marinara. I also ordered my usual iced tea, in this case a Rishi Organic Tea that offers the expected free refills. It was also quite good and refills were given freely throughout my visit. 

For my main course, I ordered their stuffed crust pizza - a small that is said to serve 1-2 people. They also offer a thin crust and an extra-thin crust pizza and these are typically served faster (about 25 minutes). All of the pizzas start in the $11-12 price range and go up according to toppings. My 1-topping (sausage) pizza was right around $15. While I've never fancied myself a stuffed crust fan, this pizza was outstanding with fresh and plentiful toppings, a perfect crust, and sauces that hit the spot. I should mention that they do also offer a gluten free option. While many pizzas will say "serves 1-2," this one could easily say "serves 2 and maybe 3." After two slices, I was stuffed and brought the other 4 slices home. 

The service? It was even better than the meal itself. Sitting at the bar, I was primarily served by the constantly friendly and attentive Rachel along with another bartender. Additionally, there were a couple other servers, one in particular, who stopped by often and checked in (especially while I was waiting on my pizza). While I didn't sense much tension in the restaurant even with the long wait times, I think my naturally calm and friendly demeanor was helping them a bit on a night that was proving busier than they'd expected with strong dine-in and carry-out orders. The servers were conversational, friendly, helpful, and frequent with the iced tea. The bar proved to be a tad high for actually serving out the pizza, but the servers were incredibly helpful with this issue. I also appreciated that on more than one occasion, especially after the 90-minute wait mark, the servers would go check on my order yet they were doing so in a friendly way that was helpful to me without being negative toward each other. 

The pizza? Incredible. The service? Stellar. The atmosphere? Busy yet warm and inviting. With locations on the way to downtown and Greenwood, I expect Giordano's to quickly become Indy favorites.

After listening to friend after friend sing the praises of Papa Roux, the clincher for tonight's visit was Yelp's listing of the establishment in their Top 50 Restaurants in Indiana list. 

Um, what? 

I beg to differ. What I experienced tonight was one of the more disappointing restaurant experiences I've had in Central Indiana. It was along the lines of my visit to Some Guys Pizza, a visit that went so badly that I doubt I'll ever return to the place. While Papa Roux's wasn't nearly that bad, the entire experience went south quickly and never bounced back. 

Don't get me wrong. I admire Papa Roux's, an establishment that has gotten a reputation for customer service, treating its employees well, and doing the "right thing." Like I said, my friends swear by the place and these are friends whose opinions I deeply respect. 

The restaurant is located in a divey building, and I mean seriously divey, on East 10th Street. It's a free-standing building, but a surprisingly small portion of it is actually devoted to dining. The interior is decorated with an exceptionally urban feel - think graffiti on the walls, etc. It's a unique approach. If you've followed my reviews, then you know I appreciate divey and that certainly was not part of the problem. 

Papa Roux's has one wheelchair accessible parking spot, clearly marked but not ADA compliant. They also have a nice concrete ramp that is ADA compliant. The front door is pretty workable. You go inside and to your left is an ordering counter. To the right is a dining area that is a pretty tight fit. I have a friend whose daughter visits in a power wheelchair, so I know that it can work but it's definitely not wheelchair friendly. On this busy Friday night, I was pretty much limited to one larger table toward the front that also accommodated another 4-person family. If you have mobility issues, you also want to note that there's a drop in their floor (that is clearly marked). 

You order at the counter. Their menu is fairly limited and, as you should expect, it's all of a cajun/creole style. You've got sandwiches and stews. The sandwiches included chicken, pork, beef, catfish, alligator, fried meatballs, etc. The stews include red beans, mushroom etouffee, crawfish jambalaya, spicy garlick stew, cajun bean chili and spicy tomato creole. They serve locally made colas and have quite a few sides (about 10). 

Now then, according to quite a few other Yelp reviews a couple of things should have happened. The iced tea should have been free for dine-in (It says $1.00 on the menu, so maybe that changed). I also should have been offered sides once the drink came out and the sides are free and unlimited. 

None of that happened. The iced tea definitely wasn't free - the sandwich with iced tea ran a bit over $11.00. No sides were ever mentioned or offered. As a newbie to Papa Roux, it took me a while to quite grasp how everything worked but it sure would have been hospitable if someone had acted even a little bit helpful. 

So, I spent my entire meal with no sides, no utensils, and never got another refill on iced tea despite sitting there eating a wrapped, decently sized sandwich that was fairly messy (and had no napkins). I finally caught on to the whole "card" in the cardholder thing that's supposed to get someone's attention so they'll bring you more stuff or refills - I thought I did it, but apparently it's in the taller cardholder. I suppose having an empty glass isn't enough of a sign. 

The meal itself? Chicken served on soft bread in sort of a wrap style. It's an abundant sandwich and definitely made quite well. However, it wasn't nearly good enough to compensate for an otherwise negative experience. 

I didn't expect for this to be relaxing - I'd heard enough about the place to know it could be packed and tends to be rather "busy" in terms of atmosphere. I was alone and sure didn't need to chat with someone. However, I did expect to be treated well and for folks to act like my business mattered. The only true customer service expression was a busser who saw me starting to clear my table and said "Don't worry about that. I'll take care of it." I give him kudos. 

In short, if this is one of Indiana's Top 50 Restaurants then I must be one of Indiana's Top 50 models. 

In case you're wondering, I'm not.

I stopped on the way home to quench my thirst with an iced tea, a rather abysmal statement considering I'd just left a restaurant where said thirst should have been satisfied. 

I really wanted to love Papa Roux, but I left dinner incredibly disappointed with just about every aspect of the experience with the lowest points being for the complete absence of customer service and hospitality. I will give 2 stars - the sandwich itself was pretty decent and abundant, while the busser deserves kudos for being aware and reaching out to be helpful. 

Po' Boy? I think that's meant to describe anyone who pays $9-13 for a sandwich and still leaves the place hungry and thirsty.

Having read an article about Taziki's Mediterranean Cafe, I was already planning a visit when I discovered their support of Best Buddies and their commitment to employing persons with disabilities. 

That's good enough to get me in the door but, of course, you have to deliver on the service and the quality to keep me coming back. 

Fortunately, that shouldn't be any problem for Taziki's. 

A growing national chain started in 1998 by Keith Richards (No, not that one!) and his wife, Amy, Taziki's has just entered the Indiana market with this location on East 82nd Street. In looking at their location map, they seem to have a strong southeast presence with locations also now in Indiana, Idaho, and Colorado as they begin their move west. 

Taziki's is located in a relatively new strip center right next door to Grand Appliance. There's ample accessible parking and sublime curb cuts. There's a double, glass door entryway. The doors were surprisingly light. As you enter, the ordering counter is to the left with clear signage. The dining area is mostly to the right, though there's also some directly in front of the window to the left. There's some tables that are more high-tops, though there's plenty of accessible dining options and aisles are pretty wheelchair friendly. 

The menu obviously emphasizes the Mediterranean theme with daily lunch specials, appetizers, soups/salads, gyros, Mediterranean deli (wraps/sandwiches), feasts/entrees, a kids' menu, healthy sides, desserts, and drinks. They serve Coke products for drinks, though their iced tea (sweet/unsweet) option is actually a brand called Royal Cup.

I ordered a grilled chicken sandwich with feta cheese and grilled onions on a kaiser bun. It comes with chips and a healthy side. I really, really like the healthy side options - roasted potatoes, fresh-cut fruit, tomato-cucumber salad, pasta salad, basmati rice, or in some areas grilled veggies. I ordered the roasted potatoes and they were amazing. 

The meal came in at about $12. You can eat for less or you can eat for more here, though prices are on par with this neighborhood. The drinks are self-serve, refills are free. 

I loved the sandwich. It was different, satisfying, and tasty. I wasn't sure the kaiser bun would work, but it does. The chips are a bit of an odd touch, definitely an Americanized touch, but they were good and I loved the potatoes. While I wasn't sure how I'd feel about the menu here, there are several things I see myself trying here. 

The atmosphere was light, breezy and calm. I don't recall being influenced by the music one way or another. The staff was friendly and made sure to explain the rewards club to me. They didn't quite explain the menu, which might be a nice touch, but there was a menu on the counter and I figured it out pretty easily. The manager checked on folks once during the meal, while staff also cleared the table without being intrusive. 

In addition to supporting Best Buddies, Taziki's has a charitable effort called HOPE (Herbs Offering Personal Enrichment), and it's lovely to see on their website "Imagine if every restaurant in America hired just one individual with a disability." 

Indeed. As an adult with a disability in the workforce, that kind of commitment excites me. 

The overall experience is probably somewhere in the 4-5 star range. I'm pushing it up to a 5 star on the basis of a quality meal, strong service, and because I love their corporate ethics and community commitment. 

The question is not "Will I be back," but "When will I be back?" I promise. It'll be soon!

The Iron Skillet is one of those restaurants that I've often heard about, however, I've simply never made my way to it. So, when a friend invited me to a gathering of "already vaccinated" friends I couldn't resist the chance to see some friends and check out a restaurant I'd always wanted to check out. 

The Iron Skillet has been serving "family style" since 1953. Initially the home of August Wacker in the late 19th century, the home was acquired by Mr. and Mrs. Charles Kelso and became The Iron Skillet in 1956. The Kelso's maintained the restaurant until their retirement in 1996. At that time, present owner Ronald Torr acquired the restaurant and has run it ever since. 

The home was unquestionably a mansion and it has long maintained many of its original charms, though there's also no question the home's interior has been maintained much more successfully than its exterior. My comment to a friend was that The Iron Skillet seems to want to be fine dining but can't quite commit. 

The Iron Skillet has a definite retro-vibe. It overlooks Coffin Golf Course and sits atop a hill that offers incredible views. It's very close to Marian University and right across the street from the Soap Box Derby. During May, it's not uncommon to see race fans as the restaurant is fairly close and is known for its fine food, comfortable atmosphere, and service.

We had a large party of either 12 or 13 and we did have a reservation. The Iron Skillet has limited hours and it was definitely pretty darn full on this Saturday night. 

"Family style" essentially means that you share a common meal (think Buca di Beppo as a common example). The meal starts off with a homemade soup or chilled juice. You get your choice of entrees followed with a selection of vegetables. For us, we chose fried chicken as our protein and were also served mashed potatoes, rolls, apple butter, beets, chicken gravy, and sort of a wedge salad side. Oh yeah, we also had green beans and corn and ice cream for dessert. Rather than individual meals, plates of each item are served up and you share. I'm not one who does "family style" often because, well, I'm single and don't really hang with groups often. 

The evening started off rather weirdly as we arrived and they seemed thrown off that I was in a wheelchair. They said "you didn't tell us there was someone in a wheelchair." Um, your website says very clearly you are "handicap accessible." Why would we tell you? Besides, customer blaming is poor customer service. 

To their credit, they did adjust and move our table to the first room you enter which is accessible. 

For the record, The Iron Skillet is NOT "handicap accessible." It is partly accessible. They do have a ramp to enter and the bathrooms are surprisingly solid. However, a person in a wheelchair can really only use the front room. and even that gets crowded. I would advise some sort of statement on the website indicating that it's recommended to mention accommodation needs when making reservations to ensure the appropriate location is reserved. 

See? It's that simple. 

After the initial weirdness, things went much better. The food was good. The service was solid. My iced tea was refilled and water refills were regular. I don't think the front room is really meant for large parties - the aisle became fairly narrow and by the end of the night I was feeling somewhat claustrophobic. However, it worked and I enjoyed the meal. 

My meal came in at just under $27 with my meal and iced tea. Ultimately, you're paying for the finer dining experience - the interior is very nice and staff dressed fairly well. It almost reminded me of Elkhart County's Das Essenhaus. 

One other reviewer has mentioned it and I feel compelled to also mention it - if you're going to wear pandemic-related masks, then wear them. Quite literally, every single employee I saw wearing a mask initially was wearing them incorrectly. I realize we're at the tail-end of the mask mandate, but you honestly look stupid going halfway. I'm vaccinated and didn't necessarily mind a lot, but the customers were overwhelmingly elderly and it just felt disrespectful to go halfway. There were points during the latter half of the evening when I noticed masks starting to be worn correctly. But seriously - wear them or don't wear them. Halfway is silly. 

I'm really torn on my rating here. I've bounced between 3 and 4-stars even as I'm writing. 5 stars? Not a chance. On a Covid curve, I contemplated going 4 stars because times are hard. However, I was genuinely bothered by the comment about telling them about the wheelchair and I was also bothered about the haphazard approach to masks. I know many who absolutely love this place, but based on tonight's experience I simply won't be rushing back. So, 3 stars it is.

My husband and I stumbled into this place around 7:30pm on a Tuesday evening. We spent a few nights in the area and were excited to learn about all the outdoor dinning options during the winter months that New Hope had to offer. Given the pandemic, we haven't ventured into indoor dinning mode yet. Anywho, After checking several places online to ensure it would be safe and warm, we got lucky getting one of the outdoor fire pits. Even with cold weather these pits keep you super cozy as you're also surrounded by standing heat lamps. We had our baby with us so it was important that it stayed warm and it was more comfortable than we could have imagined. The cocktails were super, the food was tasty and best of all, our waiter Molly was pretty on point. She checked up on us enough without over doing it but she also made sure we had what we needed. She was super friendly and even changed out the gas tank so that our fire was roaring. She got a peak at us sneakily changing our baby's diaper and was a great sport about it as we shared some laughs! 5 out of 5 and can't wait to come back.

A food craving can sometimes belie rationale. You can't be too smart to crave for seafood in a non-coastal town like Reno where the nearest ocean is at least 200 miles away. My buddy was exactly that...not being too smart and rational! He had this craving set while we were in Reno and we resorted to Yelp for help.  The name "Sky Terrace" popped out as one of the premier seafood restaurants in the area. The other negative is its location inside a casino, the Atlantis, and we are both sensitive to cigarette smoke. Bingo! Sky Terrace is a non-smoking restaurant!  It is a seafood restaurant complete with a sushi bar and an oyster bar in a sea of blue colored décor.... from the counters, tabletops and comfy padded chairs to the soothing blue lightings behind the sushi bar and oyster bar. It projected a nautical theme although it did appear a little too gaudy for my liking. The huge glass panes provided stunning views of Reno with its bright city lights, Virginia Street that it spanned over like an overhead bridge and the Sierra Nevada in the background.
 
We sat at a table, as we weren't planning on sushi. The sushi bar smelled a little off putting (not obnoxious) like a fish market and besides we were more into the other seafood offerings.  A basket of fresh bread started us off as we perused the extensive menu that featured Alaskan king crab, lobsters, clams, shrimp cocktails and a unique array of pan roasts in a tempting mix of oysters and seafood. All-You-Can-Eat sushi was not in my book and I never had any good sushi experiences in Reno. I was talked into trying a jiveass roll by my bud, ridiculously named "Tsunami" Roll ($6.95). I wouldn't even attempt to guess how the name came about but I was pleasantly surprised that its taste exceeded my expectation! It had good flavors....spicy fresh snow crabmeat with very little mayo, cilantro, avocado and jalapenos. The taste was more akin to a burrito sans tortillas but wrapped in nori (seaweed). Sushi rice was not too well seasoned but adequate as a burrito! (4/5)

The New England Lobster Roll sounded like a steal priced at $14.99. It was a traditional Maine lobster roll with mayo, chopped parsley and celery on a warm brioche bun. After the first bite, I hate to let the cat out of the bag. It wasn't meat from a live lobster but a frozen lobster. Other than that, the recipe followed closely to the real stuff from Maine (3/5). The roll came with a cup of clam chowder and we opted for the Lobster Bisque.  I wasn't impressed with the bisque as it was too creamy, salty and lacked the crustacean flavor be it lobster, crab or shrimp. (2/5)

The Cioppino Mediterranean ($19.99) was a generous portion simmered in a zesty wine and tomato sauce with chockfull of the usual stuffs like mussels, scallops, shrimps and tilapia fish. Shoot! No calamari and tentacles in a cioppino like in the North Beach or SF's Fisherman's Wharf? I was a little disappointed but the broth was tasty enough although not the best. I'm just being picky with my cioppino coming from the Bay Area but would still like to give props to the chef! (4/5)

It was a nice respite for us for a couple of hours from the outside world with the bright and sexy lightings that were almost Disneylandish. It seemed like we were waiting for our next ride in Disneyland eating in a big restaurant that was packed, noisy and not conducive to quiet conversation. The dining experience was unique to say the least!

I was a frequent visitor of Reno until I moved out of the area 2 years ago. I was excited to learn that Sakana Sushi Bar is the latest hot shit to hit Reno. I am all for trying a new sushi place. Much as I tried to keep an open mind, set aside any prejudices and preconceived notions on how one can define sushi, I couldn't in all honesty pat Sakana on the back for a job well done. Judging from the rave reviews, sushi diehards applaud Sakana for their laudable and innovative creations that have thrilled many sushi lovers in Reno. I hate to go against the flow as I was less than gratified with the meal. Sakana's sushi is just not my style.

Unsurprisingly, maki sushi (sushi roll) was the star attraction in Sakana. Some yelpers fondly refer to them as jive ass while others have called them 'yada yada whatever' rolls. I for one can't handle the overpowering sauces. While aesthetically pleasing to the eyes, the sauces weren't as pleasing to my palate. The first bite was dynamite. It was like an explosion of flavors but that quickly reached saturation point. The taste rapidly turned 180 degrees when the sauces took charge and overwhelmed everything else. If your idea of maki sushi is akin to Chinese Chop Suey or Mexican burrito where anything goes, then Sakana is for you.

Their special creation off the menu came highly recommended. Known as the 'Hulk', it was in honor of the big green creature from an old TV series. A whole avocado was cut into small slices and patted into the size of a tennis ball. There was no doubt that the presentation received top marks. The sauces were splattered in the center of the dish for a dramatic shooting star effect with the Hulk as the centerpiece. It looked more like a masterful piece of art than a sushi creation. You have to really love avocado more than the fish to enjoy this. Don't get me wrong, I love avocado in my burritos, salads and sandwiches but not as much in my sushi. The avocado in the Hulk had the soft and mushy texture of guacamole. I couldn't even positively identify the kind of fish that were inside the Hulk due to the avocado/sauce slush.

The other roll I had was the Sommersett that I believe was their signature roll. This was one of those 'anything goes' kind of roll w/ spicy scallops, spicy tuna and cucumber slathered with spicy mayo and unagi sauce. As though the ingredients were not outlandish enough, they dumped a hefty pile of tempura onions on top. Whoa! Tempura onions? I love tempura onions with my burgers. But with sushi? I felt it was a little over the edge. I have to say though tempura onions are pretty tasty eaten separately as an appetizer. Again, the ubiquitous sauce overwhelmed everything else.

There was really nothing much to write home about on the nigiri sushi. The fish displayed in the sushi refrigerator were dull looking instead of being vibrant. Maybe it was the lighting, I dunno. I just had one order of tai and it confirmed my hunch that the fish was just edible. Didn't see any uni though. Shari (sushi rice) needed some work. The rice was too grainy, under seasoned and had insufficient water content for nigiris but with maki sushi...why bother? It was hard to taste the rice anyway as the sauces completely buried them too.

Ambiance was trendy, modern and chic. The decor still smells new, as this is a new construction. The sushi chefs are young Korean boys, amiable and helpful and provided great customer service. Although I am not real familiar w/ Reno, I can tell Sakana is in a tough location business-wise being inside a residential neighborhood . I wish them well.

Ambiance: 4 stars
Service: 4 stars
Food: 2 stars

I hardly ever go out to eat due to it being rather difficult ordering vegan food..Since Lovin' Spoonfuls is vegan I was super excited to stop in and get a yummy Vegan meal. After looking over the menu, I had a couple reasons as to why I chose what I did (Southwest Breakfast Burrito). One reason was because I make this dish at home quite often and after asking the cashier if the chorizo was made in the restaurant and hearing yes, I was excited to try it out. Another reason was due to time. I didn't think this dish could take very long to make and I was on a break from work. So I order it and wait literally 32 min for it to be brought out to me. So I figure it is what it is and I should just be happy to get to dig into this scrumptious $10 burrito.... So I drive back super anxious to work and open the box to only find an oversized potato filled burrito. The description on the menu lists: 

Southwest Breakfast Burrito -- $8.75
Chorizo, green chilies, organic tofu and crispy home fries wrapped in a locally baked tortilla.

They should update it to: Potatoe Burrito, because that's the reality of what this burrito consists of.

I've been here several times. The space is incredible. 2 floors, so much stained glass, and that trolley. 

They were super short staffed last Sunday--grand total of 4 employees. Told us it would be a 45 minute wait. We were seated in 20 or under. Great service. Was my aunt's favorite meal of her week in the Midwest. She and I had pasta with browned butter and mizithra cheese, which neither of us and tried before. We both liked it. Our other 2 companions much enjoyed their meaty dishes.
Before that, I had a salad. I forget which one. After the pasta, I had a scoop of spumoni. 
Great service and they had us socially distanced. 
It is so worth a stop, the wait, and even the prices. You get a full meal with that order!

If it wasn't for yelp reviews, I would've never discovered this little gem of a restaurant. Now that I did, I'll keep coming back again and again.

The location of Lan's is less than desirable. However, don't let it deter you from coming here next time you are craving delicious authentic Asian food because Lan's is that - out of this world, top-notch, taste-buds-are-crying-happy-tears food. All menu items are reasonably priced and portions are generous.

My co-diner and I ordered salad rolls, chicken, potatoes and rice curry bowl and chicken pad thai. To say that everything was delicious is to say nothing! Spicy, savory, flavorful...completely and utterly satisfying... I'll say no more.

Actually, I'll say one more thing: Tom, who appears to be the greeter, the order-taker and the waiter will make your stay at Lan's pleasant and memorable. This gentleman is friendly, funny, chatty and courteous. He's the gem himself:)

Due to my arrival time in Boise I made it to Moe Joe's more for lunch than for breakfast and yet I was still really happy with my meal. While I wished I had the interest in a cinnamon roll because they legit sounded delicious I was more in the mood for something savory so I ordered a Prime Rib Philly. Made with prime rib, topped with mushrooms, caramelized onions, bell peppers and Havarti cheese, this thing was dang delicious. It could have been the thinly sliced prime rib, it could have been the fact that it had Havarti cheese, but truthfully I think it was all about the bread they used as a bun. It was the perfect combo of soft yet crisp and it 100% made this sandwich.

The service was friendly and fast and the prices were definitely reasonable for me. I would not hesitate to head back here again if I find myself in Boise at any point in the future. I will hopefully, be there for breakfast cinnamon rolls that time though!

Wine + Cheese + Outdoors + Live Music = one of my favorite New Orleans experiences. This place is fantastic.

You walk in through a little corner door and see what looks kind of like an old, slightly run-down corner store and walk in to see loads and loads of delicious wines. You pick the wines and then if you want (but, seriously who wouldn't want?!) you also pick out some cheeses to have them put together a lovely cheese plate for you then you head outside to drink said wine and wait for the cheese plate creation to be delivered.While you wait you get to enjoy the open air, the great company (you did bring someone that you enjoy hanging out with, right?) and live music on an old wooden stage. It's seriously the bees knees of places to spend an afternoon.

Beyond the cheese there is also a little window outside where you can order other types of food, from the snack-y bread and butter to a full on meal like seared beef tongue or steak frites. (I think they have a seasonal menu though so some of those may change throughout the year.)

I 100% wish Denver had a place like this, but it would be hard to get through the winters here I imagine. Oh well, I'll just add it to the endless list of reasons to return to New Orleans again in the fairly near future!

This place had a lot going on for it when we first arrived.  But I'm glad that I was here for a stretch of days so I could feel it all out before making a decision on this place.  First things first, if you show up early here make sure that you are prepared to wait.  When I say that I mean that you are going to have to wait because your room may not be ready yet.  I ended up getting here a few hours early because of my flight and I had to wait until the late afternoon before I got into my room.  

Let me tell you about the fiasco it was to do that.  When I went to check in they said that I didn't have a room reserved.  After a bit of the back and forth found out that they had my last name spelled wrong and that was the hold up there.  Thinking it was about to go smoothly, I was unaware of the next roadblock that I was about to approach.  The room was set up and paid for ahead of time.  Then they tried to charge me for the room.  Nope.  On top of that, they want to put a hold on one of my cards for incidentals.  Nope.  The hold, just so you know, is $50 a day.  Once that was all figured out, I finally had my key in hand.

Make it up to my room and I can say that I was happy with the way it was setup and the size of the room.  Tip, immediately go and set the thermostat lower, I walked into an 80 degree room, just about fainted.  All the amenities were great.  Fridge in room, WiFi worked amazingly (after that was figured out), iron and ironing board, ample drawers and hangers, comfortable beds/pillows.  I was happy with my room, there was no doubt about that.

Conference center was huge.  Huge enough to accommodate multiple conventions/events happening at once.  Easily navigable as well.  Multiple access points from multiple floors.

Restaurant and bar in house was fairly decent, pricing needs a look at.  Front desk was helpful when needed.  Staff were all super pleasant to deal with.

The hotel complex is rather large.  The main tower is rather tall, at least 29 floors.  Depending on the floor you are going to will determine the elevators you will use.  Then there is also another tower across the tracks that has rooms.  Over this way you will run into a Marketplace.  The nicest thing about this place is that it is connected to the Riverwalk, no need to go outside to get here.

Now let's dive into the not so great adventures had here.  After getting settled in my room I attempted to connect to the WiFi, no matter what I did it didn't work.  Made a call, no one answered.  Decide to walk down to the front desk, no one there.  I felt like I was striking out.  Remember how they spelled my name wrong?  Yeah, that was the problem, I needed to know the way they had my name in their system so I could access the WiFi.  Instead of correcting in during check in, they left it wrong.  Did not make me feel heard.

The noise is constant here.  Especially from the elevators, constantly running.  A couple of days I was awakened by noise of some type of construction (?).  When I mentioned that at the front desk during check out their answer was, "We didn't have any construction going on."  Well somebody was doing some Bob Villa stuff in their room.  How about we talk about the hot night that the air conditioning went out?  Or when the fire alarm went off?  It was a whirlwind of a stay when some ups and many downs.

I was a bit worried when I came here.  I mean when you come to a restaurant that is over 160 years old and you worry that you might not like anything on the menu.  Especially when you still serve food on your menu that is original to the establishment.  I pulled up my britches up and headed in, glad I did.

Tujague's is steeped in history here, but seems to also be a well kept secret.  When we showed up there weren't many in house, maybe it was early?  We were greeted by the bartender and headed back to the seating area.  Seated immediately and had menus in hand.  A quick look over the drink menu, place a drink order, given some suggestions by our server, and we are off to the races.

Our server was amazing.  He was very knowledgeable about everything on the menu.  Any question my party had, he knew the answer.  He knew the history of the place and that the brisket recipe that was originally used is still in use to this day.  Even though I kept looking over the menu, I kept coming back to the brisket.  Knowing that the recipe is original made me keep telling myself, "You have to try it."  And I did.

Several people in my party decided to get an appetizer, I however decided to save room for the meal I had my mind set on.  I stuck with the fresh bread brought to the table.  One of my friends in the party got the oysters.  These things were charbroiled.  I am not one for oysters but they looked amazing and my friend, who was trying oysters for the first time, said they were delicious.  Others in the party went with the Duck and Goat Cheese Crepes and Fried Green Tomato Ravigote.  Both looked amazing and there were no complaints from any of them.

Then out came the main courses.  I can't tell you much about other people's food because I was focused on my meal.  Tujague's Famous Brisket did not disappoint from a visual standpoint.  The brisket it prepared boiled.  This meant to me that it was going to be falling apart and flavorful.  And it was.  I felt like I needed to suck on the meat rather than chew.  I was in heaven.

The brisket was served over a bed of smashed Yukon golden potatoes.  My god, those potatoes were dynamite.  Loved the consistency, some clumps with the right amount of mashed, it was great.  Then the Brussels sprouts, yum yum yum.  They are cooked in bacon and onion, those things just sopped up the flavor.  If you are brave enough, eat the brisket with some of the creole horseradish sauce.  Just the right amount of kick to it to not overpower the bite.

Price was a little up there, but for the meal I had I wasn't worried.  I would gladly pay that price again.  It hit the spot and we were taken care of like rock stars.
My new favorite spot! Can not wait to explore the menu. Their service and quality of food are both top notch. You will not be disappointed!!

Wow, never expected Peruvian like this!

We walked in around 8:30 p.m. on a Saturday night without reservations and luckily seated within a couple minutes. It's fairly cozy with cute outside seating. This would be my first time having Peruvian food so I honestly did not know what to order. To start, our server brought us a small dish of dried corn kernels (hominy) with a herb sauce that was pretty tasty. 

*Pulpo Anticuchero - $9 - Grilled octopus, potatoes, Aji panca, chimichurri
Mind blowing, no seriously. This was my favorite dish out everything I tasted. The char from the grill really carries throughout each bite, pairing perfectly with the chimichurri drizzled on top. Okay, so those potatoes aren't your ordinary potatoes.. With each bite, I was trying to figure out what I was eating.. Aioli? Bingo, red roasted aioli! It's like a play on american potato salad, but with warm potatoes. Addictive! 

Ceviche Limeño - $15 - Mixed seafood, rocoto, choclo
This fits the description just right, refreshing lemon ceviche. 

Arroz con Pato - $19 - Duck confit, beer glaze, cilantro rice, salsa criolla
First off, the duck was pull apart tender, melty goodness. I loved that it didn't feel heavy and how each element balanced each other. As a preferrance, I do like my duck skin crispy... this was a different take on how I normally like it sooooooo that's the only comment. 

Tallarines Verdes Con Bistec - $24 - Linguine, basil sauce, hanger steak, queso fresco, pecans
This dish was good. The hanger steak was a little blue so a couple more minutes on the grill would have helped. It didn't bother me too much since I like it med-rare. The noodles were authente tossed in delicious basil sauce. 

Our service was exceptional and couldn't have ask for a more knowledgable server. No complaints here plus the chef came and talked to us about some of his dishes. It's nice to put a name to the face of the food. I would recommend this place to anyone who wants delicious food and great service.

Finallyyyyyy, I made it and in loveeee!

We made reservations a day in advance for three on a Saturday night. It's a bit of a crowd so much sure you call for reservations. This place was very welcoming and cute.

Beef Short Rib with Potato Rösti - $15 - Salsa verde, horseradish cream
Mmm, I really enjoyed the flavors in this one. The short rib was very tender and the potato rosti was the perfect amount of crispiness! I can't tell you how much I LOVED the horseradish cream. It was mild yet still enough heat to get me excited. 

Jumbo Lump Crab Salad - $15 - Watermelon gazpacho, olive oil fried bread
I did not expect to like this as much as I did. I saw "fried bread" and thought.. oh that's different? Yessss, you must try this one. This dish had very light and refreshing flavors. My favorite part was probably the crunchy fried dough, of course! 

Housemade Spaghetti with Guanciale and Fried-Poached Farm Egg - $14
Forever a winner in my book. I seriously still dream about this dish. The bed of spaghetti had richness and creaminess while the egg and bacon had crispy textures. Ah! How can you taste sooo goood!

Gnocchi with Pancetta- $14 - Preserved Lemon, Parmesan Yassss, pillows of yumminess. It just melts in your mouth then you get bites of salty pancetta. Overall, excellent dish! 

Banana Brown Butter Tart with Fleur de Sel Caramel - $8
Ah, I normally do not order dessert but I am soooo glad we did this time! The filling sweet level was just right for me, not too sweet - nice crust and hints of banana. 

Fried Blueberry Pie with Cream Cheese Ice Cream $10
Give it a few minutes to cool off. The filling in ours was smokin' hot, and fresh as they come! A nice balance of velvety ice cream to help cool it off. I actually loved how flakey and light the pastry dough was. I didn't feel so bad eating it. 

So the only thing is that we DID NOT try any entrees so that could be game changer. But, I literally loved everything I had here and couldn't be anymore pleased. One compliant and it's not food related was the lighting. There was a light bulb that was constantly flickering and you could see them in my food recordings. Also, we sat near the door so it was a bit warmer than I'd like, but that didn't break my experience. Service wise, our server was very attentive and friendly. I would definitely come back to try their other menu dishes!

Thrilled to have a coffee shop up this way! Apparently this isn't necessarily a new business, just moved from a location off McGavock. 
Today is the first day the inside has been open. You'll feel like you're in a diner (think Pied Piper) but you'll quickly notice the elements of what the building used to be: a bank. There's a working drive thru, bank teller windows inside, a safe, and the deposit slips table that holds the cream and sugar.
The coffee menu offers your traditional offerings, including chai lattes, iced options, and even an espresso milkshake...which is created with their made in-house ice cream. Yeup. Made. In. House. They make the ice cream for Mike's Ice Cream downtown...yeah that place on Broadway that always has a line. Be a local and stop by here instead if you have that craving for something cold and creamy.
Their coffee beans come from local roaster Drew's Brews, and their pastries from Provençe Bakery. All local, all delicious.
Stop by soon, enjoy a sip from the pew, and chat with their friendly staff. There are outlets here and free wifi so you can plug in and crank out some work too.

I have a thing for really really spicy food, and this restaurant was literally across the street from my hotel. After reading the reviews online, and not wanting to wait in line I placed an order around 10am in the morning, and they had my order ready by 11:15am, 15 min. earlier than scheduled.  

I ordered the 3 wing meal with Mac & cheese, and coleslaw as my sides, the peach cobbler, and the large dark meal with no sides.  I ordered both meals super clucking spicy, after having howling rays secret menu nothing scares me anymore.  The super clucking spicy wings were delicious, soo spicy, and a little salty, I wish I had ordered some fries to balance out all the saltiness.  I wasn't a fan of the coleslaw, it wasn't vinegary enough for me.  The pimiento Mac & cheese was delicious though, next time I will be ordering a large size of it.  The peach cobbler was warm, and had a weird after taste, I'm not sure what it was but it wasn't strong enough that it overpowered the deliciousness of the cobbler. 

Hattie B's is a must go if you are in Nashville, but I would definitely order online!!

Upon landing in philly, my friend and I were starving and looking for some food to eat. We hadn't had very much asian food the whole week, so we chose this restaurant. 

They had a stir fried dry pot that looked delicious so we ordered it. Prices very depending on which items you choose. We chose lamb, intestines, mushrooms, and seaweed.

The pot came out quickly, it was huge and enough food for 6 people !!  I loved all the different flavors,  and I especially love the Sichuan oil.  The combination of meat and veggies make for a delicious meal. 
 Great place to come for Sichuan food !

Since my wife and I are on the keto diet, we love all of the options here at Jasons deli. The salad options are beyond top-notch. They have regular prepared salads that hit the spot and they also have an outstanding salad bar. You can also get your sandwiches protein style, wrapped in lettuce as an option if you're on the keto diet. I know this doesn't appeal to all but just the fact that you can select what you want makes this a great place to dine. The customer service is always good and they do offer military discount which is another bonus. The establishment is always clean with plenty of seating and really fast service.

Would've loved to write a review about this place, but when I went there for lunch with my fiance on a Saturday, we were not able to get in. Not because the place was crowded, but because we stood around in the garden area waiting to be seated for nearly 10 minutes before we gave up and went somewhere else. 

There was a "please wait to be seated" sign but nobody even approached us. At least 5 different staff members walked past us but nobody seemed to be interested in greeting and seating people. Not a great first impression.

I have not been to this location but I did have lunch delivered to my office. The sandwich I ordered had good flavor but the bread fell apart before I got half way through my sandwich. I also ordered a side of fried eggplant that comes with marinara sauce. The sauce was good but the eggplant was HORRIBLE! It was thinly sliced and then fried and because it was thinly sliced and not in larger pieces it could not stand up to the oil. Each piece was limp, floppy and drenched in oil. The 2 pieces that were not drenched in oil were burnt. Even with trying to pat down the eggplant with a napkin I could not eat more than 1 piece. I was very disappointed and can't believe I paid $16 for this lunch!! Will not order from here again

Dear owner, here are the 3 reasons your business will fail:

1. Crepes are overpriced.
2. Crepes are overpriced.
3. Crepes are overpriced.

No one in the right mind will pay an arm and an leg for a thin sheet of corn starch. The crepes should cost no more than $5. Stop taking advantage of consumers.

Vegetarians in want of flavorful options without going to an all veggie joint, this is your place.  An impressive beer selection and servers who can confidently make solid recommendations is a plus.  Resurrection is great for brunch, late lunch and dinner -- you really can't go wrong.  There are always new seasonal additions to the menu, and several savory vegetarian options.

For brunch last weekend I ordered the pumpkin and pear sandwich -- served open-faced with seasoned almonds and garlicky cooked greens over a slice of toasted fresh bread.  I should also mention the mammoth pile of shoestring fries & addictive curry dipping sauce that accompanied my sandwich.  My friend ordered the off-menu croque madame... describing it wouldn't do justice, but if you eat meat & want a rich brunch I'd recommend asking if it's available.

For drinks she had a wheat beer mimosa & I tried their homemade bloody mary.  Didn't love the drink (too much juice, too little vodka), but that didn't stop me from finishing.  

Go early & grab a seat at the window.  Service is laid back & friendly, but can get easily distracted if a crowd starts to form.  If you're uber needy go during off-peak hours to get the attention you seek.

Truffle oil and pistachio mousse and wine, oh my!

I love visiting places where the staff is equally excited and enthusiastic about being there as I am.  I could smell the black truffle oil calling me!  It was potent and sinfully indulgent.  I thought of my budget... then the $31 truffle oil... budget... truffle oil.  I rationalized that I'd rather come back and spend the $30+ on dinner.  

Saturday night I revisited the Graces Trading Co.  The atmosphere was really laid back.  We were able to secure a table, walk around to select a wine, sample some oils & return to have the bottle uncorked by our friendly waiter.  The chef's special cheese pairing ($16) was the perfect amount to split between three people.  

The funghi pizza ($13) was insanely rich - I brought half home.  My two girlfriends ordered the butternut agnolotti lobster dish and were satisfied with the small portion because of all the large lobster pieces and heavy sauce. My boyfriend finished his margherita w/ boquerones ($18) *gross* and I'm happy to say that his pizza didn't stink to high heavens.  

Chef Jose Garces was there each time I visited.  Sources - our waiter - tell me that he's been in the kitchen each and every night.

In the last couple weeks I've been to Alma several times for their happy hour specials for the cheap food & atmosphere.  

I prefer the white sangria (papaya w/ pisco - $6) to the red (mango w/ brandy - $6) because it's more tart.  The drinks aren't killer strong and the fruit isn't fresh, but they're not terrible.  The $6 truffled guacamole with plaintain chips keeps drawing me back in!  It's a great value for the price and easily feeds 2-3.  

The soft lounge seating is 10x more comfortable than sitting at the bar or a high top table.  I recommend arriving before 6 to snag these seats.

Yes - the texture & temperature of the froyo is inconsistent.  Yes - Yogorino is much creamier.

BUT - Sweet Ending has tons of toppings (added cereals & syrups), friendly service & new flavors.  

AND - on my last trip they had **BLACK SESAME** frozen yogurt.  I mixed that in with some green tea & topped with mochi & mango.  The cup in the picture cost $3.50.  AMAZING... the black sesame is less tart, more earthy and reminds me of Japan.

My bf mixed up a messy concoction of strawberry, vanilla, green tea yogurt with strawberries, mangoes, mochi, sprinkles & raspberries - he called it the beauty of diy yogurt.  His overflowing disaster in a cup ran $5.50.

For location, price & the joy of experimentation, we'll definitely be back.

They also added frequent buyer cards - 11th yogurt is free.

Delicious takeout!  What a surprise for delivery in Rittenhouse!

We ordered our standard - saag paneer (spinach w/ cheese) and tandoori chicken with garlic and aloo naan.

Our food was still piping hot when it arrived and the price was just right (approx. $30).  The portions were so large, we had enough for dinner the next night.

I can't wait to visit the restaurant in person.

Two Saturdays ago (1/10/15) I went to a wonderful cooking class at the Tasteful Kitchen. It was actually a dehydration class. There are many tricks with vegan and raw food that use a dehydrator. This class shared some of the good tricks and techniques. The chef said "dehydration, slow food at its slowest", how funny. I am not a vegetarian and I don't have a dehydrator but I am so glad my friend invited me to take this class with her.  

This was my first experience at the Tasteful Kitchen. We met at the restaurant and walked through the tiny but cute dining room. We were introduced to the two sisters who own the restaurant. We also met Chef Laura, she was great. 

The room along the front of the building was setup for the class. Everyone had a table in front of them as the class involved a four course lunch. The tables were set with plates, glassware, and stylish brown tablecloths, really nice. Everyone had a front row seat. There is also a clever mirror hung from the ceiling, so the top of the demonstration table and the inside of bowls can easily be seen. 

We had a glass of water and a wonderful coconut drink to start with. The recipes were printed with room to add notes in the margins. Almost everything we ate we were given the printed recipes for. We even got to try a few impromptu extras like fire cider, a horseradish, hot pepper, vinegar shot that aids digestion and circulation. It was intense. We made "facon" eggplant marinated, dehydrated and used like bacon, that was my favorite. 

The food was good and creative. We were served beautiful plates of food not samples. We were served coconut pumpkins "crepes" for desert. 

The class ran way over the scheduled time but I could have stayed all day. The class was pretty well organized and well presented. There were a few breaks where the atmosphere was more casual. The price included the class and the four course lunch. All of this for just $40, cash or check only. The next class was already completely booked and I can see why. There seems to be a group of regulars who take these classes but there were other first time people too. Everyone was nice and friendly. We even got some gardening tips from the couple sitting next to us. 

The Tasteful Kitchen is a great place to take a cooking class. I learned a lot and I had fun. The food they make here is quite complicated and time consuming. These women who own the restaurant are dedicated. Now I have a greater appreciation for what they do; I will be back to try dinner in the future.

This is one of those businesses that is successful because they stick to doing one thing and they do it very well. In the case of Cafe Marcel that one thing is making crepes. 

I am still missing the Fourth Avenue location, with the cute interior and the chance to watch the crepes being made right in front of you. However, I must say the crepes taste the same, delicious. 

The new location requires a bit of a leap-of-faith as it really doesn't look promising from the street. The lack of curb appeal aside, the food is delicious. If you are hungry go for the full-size but on a regular day the half-size is perfect. 

This is a basic coffee shop environment so you can get a hot or cold drink to have with your crepe. 

As for the crepes, I recommended anything with brie cheese. Everything is good and you can't go wrong with any of the flavors. 

I would also recommend eating your crepe at Cafe Marcel. I have never tried a take-out crepe. They are just one of those foods that are so much better when you can eat them immediately. 

If you have the option, go on a weekday. It does get busy on the weekends. Even with a bit of a crowd Cafe Marcel is worth trying. Lookup the hours before you go because they do the breakfast-lunch thing and you don't want to miss these crepes.

Just south of Alvernon and 22nd, Alvernon Donut is my favorite donut shop in Tucson. 

First, I love the donuts-- they are great. They do all of the styles equally well, fried and fluffy, cake, chocolate cake, filled, glazed, with icing, old fashion ... I am sure I am leaving some out. Second, I love the price--still less than $10 a dozen. 

The storefront looks a bit worn-out from the road. Don't judge the place by the vintage, sun-faded exterior. Go inside and you will be greeted by delicious smells and friendly people. They have a drive-through but I always park and go in. I like to see the donuts in the glass case. 

Their donuts are consistent, always fresh and yummy. 

Currently, there is construction in front of the store but I still made a u-turn to get these donuts. Leaving, I took the side street out. There is a way around the construction. 

I love Alvernon Donuts.

For Valentine's Day, my best friend and I went on a Girl Date to The Vegetarian Supper Club at The Tasteful Kitchen.  I was blown away.

The Vegetarian Supper Club is a fixed menu, four course gourmet vegetarian meal (which can be made vegan easily) event.  For $25/person you get a soup, salad, entree, and dessert.  Included throughout are fresh, well-balanced vegetable fruit juices and herbal tea.  The food is fantastic.  The portions are perfect.  Normally a four course meal would make me feel overstuffed, but here it was perfect.  They do not serve alcohol, but we brought a bottle of wine to share.    

The walls at The Tasteful Kitchen are used as gallery space and we were entertained by lovely, non-intrusive live music.  The space is small, warmly lit, and near several art/sculpture galleries.  I am telling everyone about this place and look forward to taking friends there.  There is also a tasty-looking ala carte menu that I'm excited to try.  

Oh!  One last thing. There are no meat substitutes or tofu used.  The food is made from fresh, whole ingredients, very nourishing!

Just visiting... Not okay that the staff can be exceptionally rude to its patrons. Your food does not make up for that, ok?!  

Sat down with my friends. Because there was plenty of seating... After about two minutes, a man comes up to us and says "I'm gonna need y'all to get up.".... Dufuq?! Ok so we did.
