We understood that we needed to order and then sit. But still, be polite... Lady at the counter was twice as rude. Smacking her gum, rolling her eyes. "What do you want"... 

So ok, my Gumbo was booooomb! But this service is trash. Wtf.

There is a certain feeling that the customer service at Tinker Street and Festiva creates. It's a sense of authentic warmth and hospitality that the "hipster crew of tasty food" around town could learn a thing or two from. Every time I leave these businesses, I think to myself, I should come here more often. I like these people. 

In the case of both Festiva and Tinker Street, they have played a strong role in shaping the future trajectory of the 16th Street corridor. I appreciate a business that is willing to take a chance for the sake of the neighborhood's future.

But "what about the food?", you ask? Fret not, it's wonderful too. We kicked our drinking and dining frenzy off with the horchata-based cocktail (Cowboy Horchata), a margarita and the star of the show: bartender Jason Foust's creative "Urban Sombrero" (Mezcal, cucumber, corn, lime and serrano) ---two of my favorite cocktail flavors: smoke and spice rolled into one.

Our crew ordered the guacamole (topped with pomagranate seeds), Indiana goat/cabra tacos (stop kicking your feet around and order these - trust us!) and the rice pudding dessert. Of these items, the goat stood out by far. I appreciated the adobo flavors paired with the build-your-own style tray of fresh accoutrements that the tacos are served with (picked carrots/jalapeños, cilantro, pico, onion, salsas, etc.). Thrilled to see a lady chef's name on the menu. More specifically, Rachel Hoover. Apparently, "Rachel Hoover" is synonymous with kick ass goat tacos ;) 

On my next visit, I hope to find a spot at the wrap around bar. Stop reading, dear Yelpers, and head on over to Festiva.

Indy!

This is your bloody Mary bar and bottomless mimosa spot! (I am asked this question ALL the time!) Here it is, in the heart of downtown on Ohio Street. This is a cozy and happening spot on quiet Sunday mornings in Indy. What to expect? Live music and a packed house. Our group opted for reservations to play it safe. 

The bloody Mary garnish options were delicious - ranging from pickled onions and bacon to cheese and jalapeños. I would definitely return for the bottomless bloody Marys ($15 with the purchase of an entree- on Sundays). You can also choose your type of vodka - for example, bacon vodka or cilantro vodka. 

Unfortunately, the brunch food could use a little love - there is so much potential here! I can only imagine what would happen if they kicked up the menu a notch or two. 

Highly recommend if you're looking for a boozy brunch in the Circle City.

Ohhhh yeahhhh, I may have just found my new favorite Thai eatery in Indy. 

$7.95 for red tofu curry, a hefty portion of rice, roll, Tom Yum soup, and made in house rum cake. I like to think of it as a $4 meal because technically it is plenty for two sittings. If you want to get technical/nerdy about it...

The service and charm of Thai Taste is hard not to fall in love with- cozy interior, bustling lunch crowd, fast and friendly service..,could a tofu loving, Thai-craving girl ask for more? I think not. 

But more is what I found...
-generous portions
-yummy tea
-a simplified and easy to navigate menu
-fun ice cream flavors like rum and raisin, mango, etc.
-larger than average Tom Yum soup side servings

We just had the sweetest experience at the new LaTea Bubble Tea Lounge location on Mass Ave and had to hurry home to write some of their first reviews... we literally chatted the whole way home about all the ways we think this spot stands out from the pack. For starters, they make their own boba in house - its beautifully chewy with hints of a honey flavor. Second, the staff is incredibly passionate and friendly. Their enthusiasm quickly had me ordering something new and going outside my comfort zone. Did I mention that they have a super cool second story loft with tables (and built-in outlets!?). I've literally already made plans to go back and work there tomorrow.

The location is smack dab in the middle of the Mass Ave action and only a block from the Cultural Trail. They're located in the new Penrose On Mass development along with Old National, Eat the Frog, Condado, LouVino and many more. 

The menu features a selection of milk teas, homemade Taiwanese desserts, espresso drinks, hot/cold teas and more. Per the owner's recommendation, I ordered the chocolate milk drink with boba and 1/4 sugar - oh man, so good, you guys. Here's wishing this new biz the best of luck! So excited to have you walking distance from our house...dangerous!

This is my boyfriend's favorite restaurant in all of Indy. Even before he moved back to town he would often mention Brugge with a dreamy smile on his face. His go-to order is the Hanger steak with eggs and pommes frites (pick from 8 - 12 different dipping sauces like vinegar and sea salt, homemade mayo, garlic aioli and curry). 

Knowing Brugge's frequent use of duck (from Maple Leaf Farms in northern Indiana), I opted for the duck confit sandwich with onions and tart cherries. Delicious! Although, I think this sammie would make a great open face option (Step aside bread, I like to keep my duck center stage). 

If you're looking to have the authentic Brugge experience, your order must include two things: beer and frites (beer is their own). Unfortunately, I wasn't feeling in a beer mood last night, so I opted for the budget-friendly glass of wine. Note: they have bottles available for as low as $24.  

One more reason to love Brugge: outdoor seating is available both downstairs and up (fun view of the Monon and fellow Broad Ripple Village businesses). 

Love crepes? They offer both sweet and savory options.

$50 later. Be warned- it sneaks up on you here when a glass of wine is $15. My friends and I split two appetizers, each had our own flights and one glass of wine. In the end, it totaled up to around $140 with tip for the three of us. I'm not one to often note or complain about price but it really didn't seem like $140 goes very far at this business.

I do feel that this is a great addition to the Fishers fabric offering something different from chains (in also happy to see that the Fishers biz scene as a whole has really blossomed in the last one to two years. Note that LouVino comes from Louisville, our neighbor to the south (hence the name). We ordered the cornbread and Brussels sprouts as an appetizer along with our flights (I enjoyed that there are several pre-set options for flights ranging from dry reds to bubbly/sweets). With each of the flights you can choose to also pair it up with suggested cheeses. 

The space itself reminds me of Cunningham Restaurant Group restaurants -nice and clean but not overly full of a distinct character. Note that it is located next door to a few other new-ish businesses like Four Day Ray Brewing and Well Pourhouse coffee. I will say that my $15 glass of wine was mighty tasty but after looking it up online I'm still feeling the sting.

The pasta. It's all about the pasta.

Made in-house pasta is hard to come by in Indy....until now, that is. Spaetzle with mustard seed mixed in? Yes, please. The kale, squash and chicken jus took this seasonal dish to the next level. No matter what you order, make certain the spaetzle makes the cut.

I spent six months living in Lugano, Switzerland so when I heard there was a Swiss/Austrian/Italian eatery coming to Fountain Square, I couldn't have been giddier. This specific region is often overlooked as a culinary region but if you pull out a map, you'll understand how easily the the cuisine of these countries cross paths and make for delicious flavor combinations. 

Pioneer is the combination of a spacious and sexy cocktail bar with a menu that leaves you plotting your next visit and begging your dining partners to share. Per usual, we opted for family style: gnocchi, spaetzle, and  broccoli rabe.  As for the drinks, I was really impressed with the beer menu - they boast several European imports that will leave beer geeks taking notes. 

Next time: I'm going to tango with the Hungarian Farmers cheese. Oh, and the Vienna Style Kasekrainer. (heavy, I know)

You know what- I like this place. There's something low-key and simple about it that reminds me of a small town diner with an elevated menu out of New Orleans. Think: crawfish, shrimp and grits on the menu. Oh, and how could I forget the biscuit beignets topped with powdered sugar and honey marmalade? 

A few of my favorites include the granola, fruit and quinoa convo with coconut milk w d fresh bananas. Pretty much anything you order will be tasty and at a reasonable price. 

Outdoor patio seating is available and the menu offers several options for those who are gluten free and veggie friendly.

Prepare to unbotton your pants... yessss, this is one of those place where you keep eating until you Champion the food that lies before you. And Champion we did. 

I love the way Mississippi Belle's ordering process works. Each diner picks their own meat - options range from some of the best pan-fried chicken known to mankind to falling off the bone ribs. Catfish fan? Don't miss the all you can eat catfish Sundays. Family style sides are included in the core entree price - pick 4 for the group. We opted for green beans, mac n' cheese, boiled cabbage and mashed potatoes and gravy. The  buttery cabbage stood out as my favorite. Don't forget the suprise hot water corn cakes. Best part: everything is all-you-can-eat.THIS is what soul food tastes and looks like. Our table looked like a bloody battleground at the end of the feast. Food: 0. Diners: 1. 

Next time I will plan ahead to make it to the chess pie for dessert.

We had a delicious carry out experience at The Missing Brick a few weeks ago after having it bookmarked to visit for months. One of the things that really stood out to me about this business is how they weave other great Black-owned businesses into the menu. For example, the brisket on the the brisket BBQ pizza is from Hank's Smoked Brisket and Chef Oya's Trap Buttah is used on some of the pizzas and as an option with the knots. We ended up ordering the bbq pizza and knits with a side of the trap Buttah. The pizza was packed with flavor and shaped similar to a flatbread. The knots were a little too buttery and heavy for my liking but we're glad we tried them. 

The setup at The Missing Brick is ideal for social distancing with a large patio for outdoor dining and call ahead orders being easy peasy to execute. Next time, I'll mix it up and order the buffalo chicken pizza.

I loved this place already but I needed to update my previous review to highlight their new brunch offerings: 

A group of ten friends and myself treated ourselves to brunch last weekend and sampled as much of the Delicia brunch menu as possible. Our orders ranged from Cuban Toast and coffee to Thyme biscuits and gravy with spicy (and very popular) Fire n' Ice Cocktail. All were delicious - I would know because my friends and I eat quite communally. As noted in my previous review, the service was spot-on. Lastly, I would like to note that I thought brunch menu prices were very reasonable. All meals ranged from $9 - $12 and were beautifully plated.

Some of Indy's best businesses have found a new home in Foundry Provisions and Brittany S can't stop smiling about it. Long's Donuts? Circle City Sweets? Smoking Goose? Traders Point Creamery? Teas Me Cafe? Stop it, you're too cute! (and smart)

As I sit here on the patio (which, I must note, is quite spacious with 8 four-seat tables) with a Circle City Sweets croissant and budget-friendly $3 skinny chai, I can't help but I've found a new meeting spot to add to the roster - requires only a ten minute easy bike ride from Mass Ave to boot! Aside from the great sandwich list, soup of the day, sweets and drinks, my favorite thing about Foundry is the staff's attention to names. I'm a sucker for businesses who go out of their way to use customer's names and make them feel at home. "Thank you, Brittany." "Here's your receipt, Brittany" "It'll be just a minute, Brittany." (okay, so they didn't say it with every sentence)

The space is very raw both on the exterior and interior: think grey concrete, black fixtures and abstract art. Very simple, nothing to write home about. I was told the $7.50 sandwiches are delicious - thus far, I've stuck to the sweets, so it looks like I'll be having a savory lunch meeting on the near horizon. This is a great addition to the Old Northside/Talbott Street area neighborhood (located directly across the street from Greg's). 

Note that parking can be challenging, but their is ample bike parking space available in the front.

Yelper Jon C said I had to check it out- so, check it out I did. Interestingly located on the main party drag in Broad Ripple, Taste of Havana brings a breath of fresh air and culture to an otherwise 10p-3a atmosphere. 

The highlights: 

-if you're a fan of Cuban Sammies this is supposedly the place to get them. They are served in three sizes. (A vegetarian option is also available). I personally haven't tried them yet but...next time.

-my order recommendations: delicious black bean soup (offered in cup and bowl options), plantains and last, but definitely not least- the pork wings. You heard me, pork wings. Juice tender meat served with a mole-type of sauce. 

-the sweet stuff: if you saved room for dessert, there is plenty to go around- tres leches, guava-based croissants and if you're lucky, the co-owner, George, will bring around tasty complimentary Cuban coffee to your table. 

All in all, a tremendous business and excellent addition to Broad Ripple. This is the kind of eatery where the owners will get to know you by name and smother you with feel good vibes.

What's that you say? Made in house butterscotch syrup paired with walnut syrup? They call it " The Yorkshire", you say? Yeah, I'll have that.

I don't often order coffee drinks with all sorts of added syrups and sugar, but this one was TOTALLY worth it. The coffee itself was delicious and the added flavors were not so sweet that it destroys/camouflages the coffee/espresso flavors. 

There are many reasons to love this new-ish coffee joint:
1.) they have an awesome cause (check out their website for more information) I had the pleasure of meeting the owners and they are just as sweet as their mission.
2.) beautiful space with two side meeting rooms 
3.) Fishers totally needed a spot like this -tasty coffee and somewhere to hold meetings that wasn't a chain
4.) beyond the coffee/drinks, they have several made in house naked treats 
5.) no "too cool for school" barista vibes here- I appreciated their laid back and friendly ways

The wind is on your back. The earth between your toes. You are the music and the music is inside of you. Your house is filled with trinkets like shells, wood and sea glass. Mama Nature is your friend - and you like it that way. Your sunny afternoons are best spent AIS at SoBro Cafe with a smile on your face and not a care in the world.  

Are you there? Do you feel me? Maybe take a little yoga break and come back to this review to fully experience what I'm talking about. 

If ever a restaurant was a reflection of an artist, SoBro Cafe would be Alanis Morsette - only a little less pissed off. She would order a vegan-friendly meal like sweet and sour cabbage with apples over a bed of mashed potatoes with ease and a pint of local beer. Alanis would pull pull up a chair at the window counter because it's the best spot for people watching in the Cafe and she knows that.

In my Alanis-less SoBro Cafe experience, I ordered the Thai Coconut Soup. Coconut milk is brilliant - I just have to come out and say it. The soup had a great flavor and not a lot going on inside of it as far as chunks/texture goes. I could have done without the mushrooms, but that is a personal preference. Hell, you might adore mushrooms. If Alanis had been there, I bet she would have ate my shrooms... I topped my bowl of goodness off with a side order of the Moroccan carrot salad =shredded carrots, gold raisins and a "special" dressing. mmm...I could almost make a meal out of this side. My partner in crime ordered the vegetarian burger with avocado and loved it. Being the generous soul that she is, she allowed me to take a bite - so there, 2 veggie burger fans' thumbs ups = 4 thumbs up. 

The service was excellent. I wish I would have paid more attention to the Dutch pancakes section of the menu (chocolate+bacon=yes!). Oh well, it gives me a good reason to return soon.

This place is bustling around lunchtime on weekdays so make certain to give yourself plenty of time. However, service is friendly and bustling to make up for it. 

I've been dying to check out Ruth's Keystone Cafe for quite some time. Now I can see why my fellow Yelpers are big fans. 

Holy eggs benedict. Not just any eggs benedict. We're talking beautiful eggs piles on thick slices of bacon piled on Norwegian herb-filled potato pancakes. If only all eggs benedict were piled on these tasty little potato clouds. We kicked the meal off with a "pancake appetizer", if you will. You know that moment when you're thinking to yourself, "should I go sweet or salty with this meal?" Well, that's the moment when I say...."both." We ordered the cheesecake pancake with strawberry butter on top to kick the meal off. HUGE! Perfect appetizer or dessert for three to four diners. 

Overall, I recommend checking out this bright local spot in a chain-filled part of town. Fun and quirky decor paired with tasty eats make for a five star experience.

I was eager to check this place out after all of the rave reviews. Funny enough, I even watched a Netflix documentary on hand pulled noodles last night... it must be a sign. I just so happened to be near the Castleton Mall (near Meet Noodles) so this visit worked out beautifully. We ordered carry out and purchased the teriyaki ramen and Tonkatsu (pork broth) ramen. The staff was very friendly and hospitable during my fifteen minute wait for the order to be prepared. 

I want preface this review with the fact that I have a very serious seafood/fish allergy yet it seems that Asian/fish-forward cuisines seem to be my favorite. I worked with the waiter to place a fish-free/fish/bonito-free order in-person and made it clear how serious my allergy is. Unfortunately, my delicious Tonkatsu ramen was topped with a cutesy fish slice (pink swirl- looks somewhat like a radish). It was a very close call and honestly scary to see this little slip. Moving forward, I hope they're extra careful with relaying allergies from the front of house to those preparing dishes in the back. Again, the noodles and broth were delicious and this would have been a five star experience if not for this scary slip up. 

If you're able to eat fish, please go nuts on the menu for me bs try everything!! 

PS: this strip mall is full of fun treasures like an Indian and Vietnamese grocery!

This is my first review of sushi - ever. 

Let me be clear, I am allergic to shellfish and saltwater seafood so sushi isn't always the most ideal option for playing it safe. After trying their sushi at the Yelp elite party, I had to order some carry out - - literally the same night. I've never had vegan sushi that was this flavorful. Typically, these non-fish options are more of an after thought and not the most interesting and flavorful. This is not the case with Blue Sushi Sake Grill's Eden sushi roll ($8) The roll consists of sweet potato vegan tempura, grilled asparagus, edamame hummus, sun-dried tomato, brown rice, soy paper and olive oil. Eight pieces. In addition to several shellfish free options, their menu gives serious love to gluten free diners 

Sunday is where it's at for their Happy Hour specials - I'll certainly be back for this - discounted rolls, drinks, etc. Dine-in only. Great way to feast affordably - sake and all. A little more info on their happy hour menu: https://bluesushisakegrill.com/locations/indiana/indianapolis/ironworks-hotel/menu/happy-hour 

As for the space, I should note that Blue Sushi Sake Grill is located inside the Ironworks Hotel on the first floor. The space is stunning with warm lighting and a full wall of Japanese paper lanterns as a backdrop to the bar. I can't speak for customer service until I dine in. Last night's order was carry out.

I really enjoyed this speedy and healthy lunch. Here's why: 

1.) Moar renovated the space to make it feel much more cozy. There were around 4-5 tables, a couch and coffee table as well as a mini bar along the front windows looking out into Mass Ave. 

2.) plenty of healthy ingredients to choose from to build your poke bowl or wrap. I opted for the bowl and filled it up with everything from pickled ginger and edamame to greens and wasabi. The tofu and spicy mayo brought it all together beautifully.

3.) they feature a fun and extensive boba tea menu that includes multiple add in fillings and fun lightbulb shaped containers (take a look at the overhead lights that match!)

4.) friendly staff and speedy service 

5.) I appreciate that this businesses mixes up the Mass Ave vibe and brings a fast casual option for downtown employees.

If Pinterest and Instagram had a baby, it'd be Locally Grown Gardens. With this visual in mind, I think it's high time we all stop pissing around with a mere slice of pie and go big and get the whole thing. And for those days when we're feeling painfully cute, lets grab some fellow Ron Harris pie groupies and take said pie into the front room for what I like to (cleverly) call a Pie Party. LGG will provide the forks and plates, whittled candelabra and reggae music - we provide the warm bodies and $16/17, of course.

There is a reason this unsuspecting deli located only a few blocks from the ocean has made Yelp's top list of restaurants found in the Tampa Bay area. The first time I saw the date a list, I booked March the spot and finally made my way here two years later. I followed the recommendation of the reviews and quickly ordered the classic Cuban sandwich. Which, I should add, is a very large sandwich and could easily feed two people. And because I can't leave a Cuban restaurant without ordering plantains, we squeezed those into the order as well. Had a more time in the area, I probably would've returned for a second time. 

This was an exceptional Cuban sandwich. I typically enjoy Cuban sandwiches but this one in particular boasted the most juicy pork I've ever had on a Cuban sandwich. On top of that, the pickle mustard combo was just the right amount. It's been a few weeks since I had the sandwich and I can still taste the deliciousness in my memory. 

The restaurant offers a handful of tables and it is ideal for a grab and go. They are located in a strip mall location makes it easy to pull in, find a parking spot and take your food for the road.

I'm loving it. 

The only thing better than their first location? Having spot #2 one mile from mi casa. And that cactus wallpaper. That bar. The daily soup offerings. The natural light that flows in as if you're sitting outside. Gah, all of it. 

Yes, it's on the saltier side but the price matches the product. Check out all of the local ingredients they're featuring on the menu like Tinker Coffee, local meats and fresh veggies. A few standout reasons I enjoy The Garden Table - their juice flights (PS: they now offer juice samplings for $3!!!), toast selections and most of all, their soups. Two recent stand outs include the chicken pot pie (mind blowing) and the broccoli soup - much lighter than your average broccoli and cheese soup. Back to the space, it's stunningly located on Mass Ave next door to Bakersfield (an easy walk from the Wholesale District). From the tile to the beautiful bathroom to the wrap around bar, they nailed it with this space. Note that if you're just wanting to nab a container of juice you can stop in and check it out in the front fridge. 

Once it warms up the new patio will be put to use. I'm thinking this will be prime real estate for breakfast cocktails and some of their fun Tinker coffee creations.

Oh, holy chicken fingers. Yes, you heard me. Chicken fingers. Hold this in your memory because I probably won't be raving about chicken fingers for another 5 years. I swear I'm not a snob but this isn't typically a dish I'd run to on the menu- especially at a burger joint. (Note, surprisingly enough, Bru also makes some of the best salads in town).

What made the chicken fingers so delicious? The fine balance between crispy corneal based exterior meets juicy and tender interior. All paired with homemade ketchup and honey mustard. I now have a new go-to at Bru. Paired with a salad and you have a meal. 

As for the Carmel location, it is quite spacious and located a stone's throw from the Carmel arts district. Parking is easy in the lot adjacent to the restaurant. Most importantly, the customer service was incredible. The manager stopped by to check on us and our server was both attentive and friendly.

Hitting the spot, La Parada! We were hungry and desperately wanting to avoid making dinner...I was also hankering something not so healthy... The original plan was a breaded tenderloin but an enchilada would suffice as a stand in. 

La Parada is our go to for budget-friendly, no-frills Mexican eats - for me, it's all about the salsa, refried beans and rice. This spot reminds me a lot of the Mexican eateries I grew up on in rural Indiana. Fast and delicious. 

For this round, we called in our order and the food was ready in 20 minutes. I opted for the #4 (like I said, I was craving unhealthy) which consists of an enchilada, taco, tamale and rice and beans. My dining companion ordered the guacaflauta (fried little tortillas wrapped around chicken and all topped with a generous serving of guac). We never leave La Parada without an order of the chips and salsa. I could drink that stuff...

Overall, a lovely experience that hit the spot. Their carryout system is working really well given the situation.

One of the most amazing eating experiences I've ever had. We had no idea what we were getting into - all we knew is Yelpers think it's pretty fantastic (and rightly so).

I'm going to walk you through our experience chronologically (forgive me for t-totally making up the times):

7:46 p.m.: arrive in Germantown, Nashville at Monell's Dining. Jaw-dropping beauty of the historical house lit up in the evening with a beautiful garden alongside the building. From the outside you can see families feasting.

7:50 p.m.: we realize this is a family-style eatery. The tables that we once thought were ginormous and tremendously diverse families are actually big groups of strangers. (ding, ding! extra cool points) Our diverse family (the table in which we are seated) consists of locals, Bostonians, and a few other folks who I couldn't really hear because the table is so big. 

7:51 p.m.: thought to self: where is the menu? seconds later: realization that you don't order here. As my dad said growing up, "what you see is what you get." or "what you don't see, don't ask for." In the case of Monell's, everything you could ever wish for is already in front of you (friendly strangers who love good food and mounds of southern comfort food). 

7:55 p.m.: let the face stuffing begin: potato salad, pulled pork (one of my favorites), chicken, fried catfish, greens, breads, so on and so forth. 

8:28 p.m.: I feel like I could puke but I totally got my money's worth. But, heyo, wait a minute, those awesome tablemates from Boston insisted on buying my sister and I's dinner. After a few minutes of the check tango, they won. (could this experience get any sweeter? why, yes, yes it could....read on)

3:45 a.m.: remember those locals at the table? Well, they just so happen to work at a recording studio and have all sorts of producer friends. Let's just say we partied hardy with this crew of cool folk. Hell, they even sang us some songs at the studio.

This place is my new obsession. Seriously, that clotted cream and ginger fig jam ... me.oh.my.

For starters, they offer a nifty buy $10 get $20 Yelp deal (super easy to purchase via the app). From there, it only gets better. $12 for two scones, a pot of tea for two, clotted cream and jams? What a steal! Not to mention the creativity behind the made in house jams like Vanilla Chai, lavender, ginger fig and so on (both times I've visited there have been at least 5 jams to choose from). I've also noticed that these jams are sold elsewhere like Porter Books and Bread. 

This charming home turned business oozes with lady charm. Floral imported tea cups? Check! Fresh scones? Check! Long tables that are perfect for bridal and baby showers? Check! Sand tea timers for herbal and black teas? Check! (see photo) Wifi? Check!

I hope Tina doesn't mind if I curl up in a corner with a pot of tea for days...

My mama is a doughnut mama. So, when she was in town this past weekend for a visit and said "oooo! the Donut Shop!", I whipped her minivan in their and bought her all the doughnuts her out-of-town heart desired. Having my mind recently blown by the bourbon maple blueberry donuts found at Blue Star Donuts in Portland, OR, I've been craving clever and fluffy morning dough more than ever. Much to my surprise, the moms and pops shop that is "The Donut Shop" houses a few unique options to mix up the ordinary chocolate cake and yeast you'll find elsewhere. The oreo, German Chocolate (topped with coconut) and maple bacon stood out during this particular visit.

I had already eaten breakfast (no judgment), but I HAD to get my hands on that maple bacon (yeast donut, topped with generous amounts of maple icing and three to four mini slices of crunchy bacon). Pure perfection. My mother, whose palette is often on a different page from mine agreed. The fluffiness of this dandy was as if they pulled it out of the frier and plopped it directly into my white to go bag.  Also of note, this place is cheap! Perfect place to play Mr./Mrs. cool and buy breakfast for all of your friends ;)

If donuts aren't your thing, The Donut Shop is quite popular amongst the greasy spoon/hangover crowd. Breakfast on the cheap with no frills (est. price $4- $6). 

Heads up: parking on weekend mornings can be fairly difficult.

It's no secret that finding local gems in the Castleton area can be a bit like finding a needle in the haystack. But thanks to my dear friend Yelp and northside pals, spots like Ale Emporium can be found. Ale Emporium is a sausage fest, maybe it's the dozens of tvs on the wall screening sports games or the amped up bar food menu? 

Okay, so now you're at the restaurant - what to eat?
Iconic Ale Emporium:

-The Hermanaki Wings: breaded with a teriyaki-like sauce. Orders are in large proportions, so bring your friends if only for this reason ;) 

-Honest Pizza: literally the heaviest (as in dense) pizza I've ever encountered. You could almost make a meal of one slice. Primarily traditional toppings and starting out at $11 for a cheese pizza.

-Beer list: true to its name, Ale Emporium has an extensive list of brews (local, regional, seasonals)

-Tuesday night filet deal: no joke, get ready for it....$6.99 for a filet, side and salad. Seriously? You'll be taking home leftovers and despite my expectations, the filet wasn't too shabby!

This was a much needed addition to the Carmel coffee shop scene and has beautifully became a hustling and bustling spot for meetings, remote workers and families. I've visited multiple time and this past weekend enjoyed a spot on their shaded patio to crank out some work for a couple of hours. I typically opt for their seasonal creations and they never seem to disappoint. This round I tried the peanut butter jelly latte which surprisingly was not too sweet. 

A few notes:
-great natural light in the space
-walking distance from the main downtown street of Carmel and the Monon Trail
-plenty of outlets for remote work
-a few baked good treats are available
-they roast their own beans
-rumor has it their cold brew is quite delightful (next time, next time...)

It had been awhile since my last Tastings visit, but this past Friday night a friend and I decided to grab a glass of wine and some light appetizers after seeing a show at the IRT. 

Given that it was pretty late in the evening, I wasn't up for the whole tasting card scene (you load up a card with a certain number of dollars and taste to your heart's desire at dozens of computerized wine stations). In fact, I wasn't really craving a drink but I felt slightly obligated (hence my decision to go with the cheapest red on the menu $7.50 - it tasted slightly cheap but you get what you pay for, right?).

As for the apps, we had the prosciutto wrapped figs with cheese and bruschetta.  I enjoyed my figs but wished they were a little larger to match the price. I would order them again. *Typically I go for the cheese board ;) You rarely lose with a cheese board. 

Why four stars and not five? We found ourself with a dud waitress - she was slightly aggressive and seemed miffed when we weren't ready to order. We appreciated the friendly and proactive gentleman working behind the horseshoe-shaped bar.

I love this neighborhood spot. After two recent visits this past week, I wanted to reiterate my love for West Fork Whiskey. Their new summer menu knocked my socks off with a spicy watermelon creation and coconut milk paired with pineapple juice and lime to name a few.  A few key reasons to add this Kennedy King business to your hit list include:

-dog friendly!

-eats can be ordered through their next door neighbor and they also offer budget friendly snacks

-all cocktails are $8 and made using their in-house spirits 

-love the long bar and garage doors facing out on to the street 

-super friendly staff (you could easily show up solo and have a great time here)

Synonymous with "Tick Tock Lounge" = "Bloody Marys with the most beautifully obnoxious garnishes ya ever did see" What do I mean by obnoxious? How about tater tots, pepperoni, cheddar cheese cubes, green olives, a massive celery stick and slab of crispy bacon. What about the juice? Bacon and jalapeño-infused vodka. Talk about a kick!

I expected this place to be much more divey than it was. In fact, both the fascade and interior were clean and well kept. It appears that they are really into liquor infusions. I'm mighty curious about the banana-infused whiskey. 

Kitchen closes at 10pm.
If only I could have ordered one big bowl of those tater tots - they taste like the tater wedges you find at McDonald's.

So I had a vision of what I thought Poccadio would look like inside - I was pretty off. Not in a bad way, but in a "this is a Moroccan Subway more than a Saffron plated experience." I like the way Chef Sentessi's restaurants compliment eachother. I wish I would have ran into a sandwich shop of this nature when I was in Marrakesh. 

Let's talk about the food: When it comes to salad bars and topping options - I'm the gal who fills her plate till it's overflowing on the sides. I want it all. As was the case with Poccadio's sandwich fillings. Feta, red pepper paste, kalamata olives, hummus, spinach spread, tasty this, tasty that, mystery this, mystery that. All tucked away in a caraway seed loaf (as recommended by the very friendly and helpful sandwich artist). My sandwich started out as the vegetarian Atlas - but I seem to have a way of making vegetarian/healthy meals unhealthy with blobs of cheese and such. Please note, this sandwich is enormous - could easily be split between two people with dessert ;)

And, because I lack any form of self control, I had to go for the Moroccan baklava - so, what made it different from other types like baklava? This particular version had a dynamic combination pistachios, sesame seeds, and walnuts. The sesame seeds are what sets it apart the most. I dare say, I may fancy the Moroccan version over the Greek. 

Lastly, make sure you check in on the Yelp app to claim your free hot/cold mint tea!

Mi dispiache Iozzo's! What a fun surprise! Not that the front of the building gives off any bad vibes, but there is so much more to this place than I expected. We walked in with the plan of sitting on the front patio, but when the host mentioned the terrace, we jumped on it (never knew Iozzo's had a magical secret garden tucked away in the back!).

"Magical secret garden" doesn't begin to explain how cute their patio is! Curly stairway filled with terra cotta pots and pansies. A large mesh screen filled with an old black and white family picture. Water fountain with the perfect trickle. The smooth sounds of Dean Martin and twinkling light strands overhead. After a day at the pool, I was ready to crash on this patio. Set up camp and make it my home.

I was hoping for some gnocchi on the menu, but didn't mind going with the spaghetti for plan B. I topped it off with two meatballs. I'm usually more of an angel hair kind of girl, but the tasty sauce made up for the thicker noodles big time. And the meatballs - oh! the meatballs! I should have asked if there was turkey or something else mixed in. They were very lean and had a really nice texture. The meal also came with a salad and nice hunk of fresh bread. Thank you Iozzo's for not using iceburg lettuce. The fresh mixed greens and shaved Parmesan hit the spot! My friend had the chicken sandwich with pesto on brioche and enjoyed every bit of it (even came with a side of sketti).

Service. Service. Service.

I've said it once and I'll say it again, I don't care how beautiful your sea salt browned butter cookies are, if you don't offer a strong customer service experience, I'll most likely leave with a bad taste in my mouth.

I left The Eagle with a good taste in my mouth. Both in flavor and experience. 
From our friendly server, Beth, to the great atmosphere and energy, we were smiling for two hours straight.

I kicked my feast off with the Bloody Mary (their version features Guinness beer and a thick slab of maple bacon, olives and celery). I was surprised by how much I enjoyed the Guinness with the vodka. 

Next up:
-pickled veggies (tasty light start $4 - not mindblowing but a great lighter start)
-horseradish mashed potatoes (yes! Horseradish should be used more in general, in my opinion)
-fried chicken dark meat (2 legs and a thigh for $6) -- that fried, crispy goodness...the meat comes from an Ohio farm
-mac and cheese (follow your fellow Yelpers' recommendation on this one: "get it!")
-thrown biscuits with jam and butter
-cheesy grits (one of my favorites from our five sides)

Last piece of advice: order family style! Who says you can't try it all?

Yes, yes, I've reviewed this place before but I haven't told you about their incredible new summer salad option - worthy of its own follow up review: 

Think of your mom's old tomato cucumber salad recipe and kick it up a notch (tenfold) with endive, goat cheese and asparagus. The small option is enough for a filling lunch ($9). Don't dilly dally friends, this salad is on their rotating summer menu. 

Lastly, how can I not mention the friendly face and service delivered by Jared? I whispered across the table to my boyfriend that Jared is one of those cool looking guys that you want to stand near so you can claim association. From head to toe he's fun inside and out.

Let me kick this review off by saying that I LOVE touching my food. Any hands-on restaurant experience I can find...I'm all about it. In the case of Sakana if Tokyo, I've been geeking out about their recent addition of Mongolian Hot Pot to the menu. Fun fact: the owner/head chef, Bart, is from Mongolia. 

A brief rundown on Mongolian hot pot at Sakana: 1.) select two of the four broths to be shared table side (all ingredients you select are cooked in the boiling broth). I highly recommended the herbed broth. Note that some options have fish contents (for those of us with shellfish allergies;) 2.) each topping has a value assigned to it - diners can pick and choose from more than 30 offerings ranging from sweet potatoes, eggs, mushrooms, and bok choy to chicken, meatballs, prime rib and fish. The ingredients arrive in generous amounts ready to be dropped into the broth. 3.) note that one pot (which contains two types of broths) can feed as many as four people. This is a super fun and interactive date night option and also works well for picky eaters (choose their own ingredients and comfort levels). 

As for the atmosphere and location, Sakana is a stone's throw away from Castleton Mall and judging from the outside and sushi vibe of the business, you wouldn't expect it to feature authentic Mongolian hot pot. Craving those sweet potatoes and broth as I type!

The setting is perfect - especially on a fall day with the autumn leaves reflecting on the water. Opt for outdoor seating if the weather is right.

So, why two stars? (please note that I rarely give two stars and it pains me to write this)

Our brunch was a-okay: I opted for a real face stuffing via the eggs, fresh fruit, biscuits and gravy and bacon paired with a $6 Bloody Mary. All were decent and to be honest we were there for the views and not a mind-blowing epicurean experience.

Shit hit the fan when we pulled out a gift card. 1.) you must use the entire gift card in one shebang and Rick's will not leave the remainder on your card for a future visit (needless to say, our brunch was only $60 and the gift card was $100 meaning we wasted $40). We thought of ordering more food to use up the remainder but at that point we didn't want to stick around for another half hour.  2.) tax is not included on gift cards? Tacky. I've never seen this before. They recommended that we pay cash and visit again to use the gift card....

Dagnabbit, all was rosey until the gift card made an appearance.

A seafood market has my heart and I can't even eat seafood. That's the magic of it. Caplinger's has a way of catering to all needs, questions and types of customers as they roll in the door of the Shadeland Avenue establishment. In my case, I've had the pleasure of enjoying their grilled chicken (truly delicious and not an afterthought as it most often is at seafood joints), collard greens and mac n'cheese. I'm all about southern sides and Caplinger's has them down to a 't'. 

For those who can enjoy seafood - I do know a few of their most popular offerings are the smoked seafood salads and dips in the front case (you can sample before you commit!), the chunkiest clam chowder you ever did see and the vibrantly red lobsta rolls. 

Lastly, I would be remiss if I didn't highlight Caplinger's knowledgeable and educational approach to the fish of the sea. In fact, they now offer Seafood 101 cooking classes where guests can eat and learn at the same time in the side room. Caplinger's is a place you can go with zero fish knowledge and stroll out with beautiful and rare-to-the-Midwest types of fish and all the fixins to prepare it at home. 

I love you Caplinger's. But you knew that already.... :)

Let me start off by saying how much I love that this addition to Mass Ave (and Bottleworks) is walking distance from our home. Second, it's hard to go wrong with a Cunningham Restaurant - they kill it in the customer service department (along with design, menus, etc.). The thing that I loved most about Modita is that despite being an Asian-centric menu, they offered up several vegan and vegetarian options clearly noted on the menu which is key for someone with a severe fish/shellfish allergy. It certainly makes the experience 10 times more relaxing. 

I'm pretty sure we ordered everything on the menu but a few standouts included my mocktail version of the Suburban Birdcage (ya know, because I wanted to pretend I was on an island vacation), the sweet and sour beets on the appetizer menu (vegan), and heirloom tomato salad (vegan). I wasn't able to try it but my dinner companions loved the bao buns with grilled pork, miso aioli and Asian slaw. The mapo tofu I had was quite tasty and I appreciated how they shaped the rice nuggets into cubes similar to the tofu. 

Our server was very helpful and hospitable and the space was beautifully decorated with low mood lighting and a gorgeous tile selections throughout. 

Next time, we'll save room for dessert ;)

Overdue to update my Brics review. 5 stars. Hands down. Some of the best customer service and biggest smiles you'll find in all of Indy. My new shout out also goes to the cherry ice cream. Next time, I'm having my way with the double dark chocolate ice cream.

Side note: Brics carries an impressive number of local products like XXX root beer from West Lafayette, cookies from 4 Birds Bakery, pies from Upper Crust and ice cream from Hubbard & Cravens.

An enthusiastic second review for this new downtown bakery conveniently located on the edge of the Chatham Arch, Old Northside and Mass Ave neighborhoods. 

What a wild time to open a business but we're so glad you did, Leviathan Bakehouse. We can't complain about having an artisan bakery walking distance from our front door. 

As of July 26, Leviathan is offering curbside services as well as carry out.  In their front case you'll find a mixture of sweet and savory options like saag paneer croissants, carrot cake, full buttercream frosted cakes, traditional croissants and so on. Their menu also features around five made fresh-to-order sandwiches, soups and side salad options. You'll find a line up of coffee drinks made using Tinker Coffee alongside Circle Kombucha and local treats from the likes of Frittle and Home Ec.

Service was very friendly and our saag paneer croissant was delicious. I look forward to sampling my way through their menu on the road ahead. Congrats!

Where are we? No, seriously. Where the hell is this place? The neighborhood surrounding Danny Boy is straight out of the Stepford Wives. I've never seen anything like it. My jaw dropped a foot in response to the perfectly manicured lawns, over-the-top neighborhood planning and general silence of the 'hood. The tatted bartenders and brewers in Danny Boy are a far cry from its navy-khaki surroundings. I suppose it adds an interesting and slightly humorous contrast. Date night idea: have a few drinks at Danny Boy and go for a "tour de casas" walk.

Okay, to the beer and our boy, Danny. This place is much more crisp and clean than I imagined (not in a bad way). The modern lighting fixtures and abundance of stainless steel give it a masculine feel. The bartender (whose name I wish I could remember) was super playful and fun to chat with - he handled our large group with ease. The food that was rolling out from the kitchen looked above your standard bar/brewery options. I'll be certain to give it a try next time. As for the beer, I thoroughly enjoyed the stout and look forward to sampling more of their offerings next time.

My love for Natural Born Juicers started on a sunny winter morning in 2010 at the Indy Winter Farmers Market. This sunny morning was also my first tango with wheatgrass...

Fast forward to 2011 at Indianapolis City Market - three little letters take this small town girl's love for NBJ to a new level: I. O. U.

Yes, oh yes. If you want to win over a small town hillbilly in the City - show them that you recognize their customer loyalty with an IOU when they foolishly forget you only accept cash. Needless to say, it is not only their expert juice and smoothie making abilities that make this place top notch, but their ability to love on regulars. 

My current smoothie/juice favorites:
1. Juice: The Glow - carrots, parsley, apple, lemon, dash of smiles
2. Smoothie: Chocolate Raspberry - the name says it (note that this is a tasty 
cocoa-y approach to chocolate mmm..)
3.  Smoothie: Spice Cake: cinnamon, carrot, banana, apple, vanilla (I would take this over a real cake any day)

**Please don't take advantage of the fact that I shared this information - you can bet your bottom I was back in there the next day with my five dollars and forty-five cents.

I treasure my trips to Trader Joe's- now, more than ever. We're currently limiting our grocery trips to only once every two weeks and in the meantime, I look forward to the adventure. The staff has always been incredible at Trader Joe's and they're truly rising to the occasion with this challenging situation. From the staff wiping down carts to those restocking the shelves, the pour positivity and warmth into every customer experience. It's hard not to have your spirits lifted here. 

During the time of COVID, they're limiting store entrance to 25 customers at a time and limiting their store hours. You'll be happy to find that the alcohol shelves, seasonal offerings and budget-friendly flowers are all still accounted for. Here's to pouring some love and gratitude onto our hardworking grocery employees!

You can have the best food in the world, but it gets to be a little frustrating when service is crappy time and time again. If it weren't for your historic charm and knock-your-socks-off good tenderloins, I wouldn't be back.

I'm still thinking about those tamales...and rice...and Mexican zucchini soup. All were delicious and thoughtful in execution. For example, the seasonal turkey tamale was paired with a made in house cranberry jalapeño salsa. The worst part? Eating every last drop and wishing there was more (to be clear, I wasn't hungry but there's always more room for good food). 

The owner was very friendly and passionate. I appreciate that he takes popular Mexican dishes and kicks them up a notch with unique flavors and more vegetables. Note: the tamales are made with olive oil not lard. The space only offers seating for four but you're not there for the space, you're there for the food. Big props to the owners' daughter for creating such a fun and festive illustrated logo (personified tamale). 

You'll find Tlaolli's tamales in a few spots around town for purchase (frozen, take home tamales). Check out the $9 lunch special (you pick three: tamales and tacos and one side). This offers an affordable platform for sampling the menu.

Officially one of my new favorite coffee spots in the city. If you receive a meeting request from me in the next few weeks, I'd say there is an 80% chance I'll set the location to Open Society. (You can thank me later)

The feel:
Exposed bricks, sleek decor, beautiful backdrop to the bar in the rear of the building and the long communal wooden table is great for group meetings and those of us who require some extra elbow room.

The service:
This is what will make Open Society stand apart from many of the new trendy spots in Indy. They've remembered that good customer service is key to the experience. As you know, you can make the coolest, organic, local, heirloom whatever but if you're serving it with a "don't-give-a-shit" attitude that's most likely what your customers will remember at the end of the day.  for seeing the big picture!

Food and drink: 
Where do I begin? The baked goods are both creative and delicious. Expect everything from a spicy pepper scone to mini lemon poppyseed cakes. As for the coffee portion of the biz, I cannot recommend the shakerado enough (maple syrup espresso magic in a glass). Note that they also have Hidden Pond Kombucha on tap (rotating flavors) and nitro coffee also on tap. 

The best part? Businesses like this are key to adding vibrancy to a neighborhood. I'm confident that Open Society's presence is a game changer for this intersection on College (SoBro/Meridian Kessler neighborhood).

Fresh, fast, budget-friendly.

Upon entering this Main Street business in downtown Carmel, you will see that it is set up in an assembly line similar to Qdoba and other fast casual establishments. The thing I love about this business is how you can build your own bowl with vegetables, tofu, proteins, brown or white rice, and a variety of flavorful sauces. In the and, you will have a $12 meal full of nutrients. Vegetable and topping selections include cucumbers, red cabbage, seaweed, fresh greens, and dozens more. Ingredients are prepared daily so you know that you are receiving fresh, quality eats. 

The space offers at least a dozen tables and is ideal for a casual lunch or dinner. During both of my visits the staff has been extremely friendly and willing to explain the process and all of the ingredients. They are also very conscious of allergies which is sometimes hard to find. This business is a great addition to Main St., Carmel.

Well this was a delightful last minute lunch decision. I have to admit, it was the charming facade, neon signs and location that drew me in. I was so excited to see another addition to the 22nd St. corridor. I most often find myself biking to the area for meetings at Teas Me Cafe. 

For starters, the vibe of Baby's is retro, quirky and one-of-a-kind in the downtown area. From the pink neon signs to the fun wallpaper in the bathrooms, you can't help but smile from the overall look of this eatery.

Second, they have boozy milkshakes. Not just any ole' milkshakes though... you guys, I am going to be blabbering about their vegan key lime milkshake for weeks. I honestly left and thought to myself, hmm..would I be overdoing it if I went back tonight and ordered another?

A few more reasons I'll be back in a hurry: the patio is dog-friendly and the fried chicken is mighty delicious. Our server was very friendly and sweet and the lunch turnaround time was impressive - especially for a new business. Need I say more?

"Black bean corn fritters." I repeat, "Black bean corn fritters." And if you're seeking specifics, "black bean corn fritters topped with shoestring beets and a generous serving of an herb-based cream that hit the spot." 

For starters, way to go Shoefly for being one of the businesses to pave the way for development in the neighborhood - excellent location selection. 

Other noteworthy highlights from our cozy Friday night visit:
-go for the mulled wine served by the mug (Guhlwein is hard to come by in the Circle City) And for $4/$5, why not have a second?

-Herbed polenta - this thrown with another lighter side would be suitable for a satisfying meal

-salad: the $4 small options are a great route if you're looking to sample as much as possible from the menu. I opted for the Escarole salad and would probably consider making it my meal along with the shared black bean corn fritters on my next visit. Although...the beet hash might be calling my name...

-friendly service and overall laid back environment which makes the innovative and progressive menu all the more fun

-while I'm at it, if you're really hungry or hankering for a heavy option, I recommend giving the cheese cornmeal waffle sandwich filled with pulled pork a shot. The meat is extremely juicy and tender.

Finally popped in here after years and years of saying, "I'd love to check that place out." We were popping between grocery stores and had the time, so voila, I finally experienced Georgetown Market and it was delightful. 

A few key takeaways from my visit:
 -extensive natural beauty care products sections

-abundance of locally made products like Hidden Pond kombucha and oat cookies from Four Birds Bakery; I also noticed a few regional items like kraut and pickles from Detroit 

-the produce section is on the smaller side 


-small parking lot but it wasn't hard for us to find a spot

-the in-house cafe offers a daily hot bar with prepared foods as well as juices and smoothies along with a handful of seats and large windows that make this an ideal spot for remote work

-the space is just a wee bit smaller than a Trader Joe's snd equally easy to navigate 

-the beauty of it is, if they don't have what you're looking for, one of the dozens of neighboring international markets probably does

It's local. No, really. It is. Despite it's uber sleek branding and almost Swedish-ly clean interior, Punch Burger is an Indy-only business. My dinner companion and I had to requirements for our restaurant selection last night: affordable and fast. In walks Punch Burger (which, unbeknownst to me, my friend is a regular - like the kind where they remembered the last special sandwich they made for him). 

First note: I love the clean interior of Punch. Reds, whites and greys with Ikea-like furniture. If you're wanting to get in on the action and see the burger action up close, you can sit at the bar. 

Second note: I opted to fail my 25 days (thus far) of vegetarianism for this experience. Please note, they do have a vegan burger - but I, however, insisted on trying the Thai Burger (which was worth the splurge). Asian slaw, whole wheat bun, peanut butter, red onion and sweet chili sauce. This is one of their seven signature specialty burger. My friend ordered the burnt cheese on Texas Toast. Both were very good - between the two, I choose the Thai. $6.75 for the burger. I had read so many reviews noting their sweet potato tots, so we opted for the half and half mix of waffle fries and sweet. Of the two, I fancied the waffle fries much more as the tots hit me as little balls of grease. Good flavor, but just a bit too much grease for my fancy. As for local beers on tap: I was happy to see 4 of the 6 were local: Triton, Flat 12, Fountain Square and Sun King, I believe.

Third note: Service. Extremely friendly and interactive. I'm sure that it helped that Jonathan (friend) goes there as often as 2 to 3 times a week but either way, a very fun and lively crew.

Holy rice balls. 

Holy potstickers.

Holy coconut green boba tea.

One more - - - holy edamame that seems to have been soaked in magic juice. 

I met a friend here for lunch with the following criteria in mind "86th street area" and "somewhere I've never been." I should have added "kickass Taiwanese eats" to the list because it would have knocked all three out of the ballpark.

When entering this strip mall business I was surprised at how "cozy" it was in the small sense - there were a handful of tables that suited the vibe very well. Simple Taiwanese done well. 

I claim to make a killer edamame (lemon juice, garlic, sea salt, and whatever other ingredients I'm feeling at moment) but this restaurant gives me a real run for my money. The flavors were completely soaked through the beans and they shelled oh.so.beautifully. 

Rice ball description: bean paste wrapped in sticky rice then lightly fried? and rolled in sesame seeds - - soooo good. I can't describe the texture but I was definitely digging it. 

This would be a really fun spot for those who enjoy eating family style and sampling the menu. The sizes were perfect for dabbling in this and that. To top it off, our server was extremely friendly and the food came out in a jiffy which was perfect for our lunchtime schedule.

Smoked elk with blueberries soaked in New Day Mead - stop it! You're killing me with your pure gastronomic brilliance!

Hidden gem: h2o Sushi just so happens to make brilliant oatmeal cookies and sells them at Goose. Getchya some. If it has oatmeal in it - I considered it to be consuming my dose of grains for the afternoon.

Womp womp - today's service (or lackthereof) paired with the fact that a small will run you $12 after tax (more than I paid in San Francisco for an acai bowl a few weeks ago), left me feeling that a 4 star review was more adequate. Don't get me wrong, the bowls are delicious, I appreciate the free park and cleanliness of the space but I didn't enjoy standing in the store for 5-8 minutes before being acknowledged/seeing a staff member.

This is an Indy classic. I used Yelp's Big Night In as an excuse to revisit their original location on Rockville Rd. The beauty of their tamales is they freeze beautifully! I decided this would guarantee us a midweek culinary pick me up ;) 

We opted for the chicken verde, sweet corn, black beans and cheese and pork and red sauce tamales. It was a fast and simple carryout experience. I'm not certain how they're currently operating at their other locations. If your new to Tamale Place, I suggest also ordering the chips and salsa and tacos. They have my favorite chips and salsa in Indy. Go snag yourself a freezer stash!

Alright Yelpers - I finally made the voyage to Egg Roll Number 1 based on your trusty reviews!

I went in with two items on my radar: Pho Tai and Vietnamese spring rolls (veggie)
I left with every single bite of my Pho Tai and spring rolls in my tummy (this meal was probably worth of two portions, but damn, why stop now?).

The menu is enormous - a mixture of Vietnamese and Chinese options. And the budget-friendly prices allow diners to dabble in a little bit of this and a little bit of that. I'd venture to say Egg Roll Number 1 is one of the tidiest Chinese restaurants I've been in - not that this factor has ever stopped me from stuffing my face. 

I highly recommend the pho tai piled high with bean sprouts, jalapeno slices and basil. It's a bit greasier than Saigon's version, but equally delicious. The spring rolls were a-okay, I'm thinking it might have been an extra-spicy batch of basil that through it off a bit for me. 

Now, I'm a bit pissed at myself for hogging down the whole pho tai last night and not saving enough for today's lunch....

Yes! Indy's food diversity surprises and delights me daily. Yes, we're in the heart of the midwest and yes, we have Ethiopian, Cuban, Nigerian, Laotian, Mongolian, etc. Phan's brings fresh Laotian cuisine to the table with friendly and enthusiastic service. The team is eager to share their story and the scoop on dishes found on the menu. First and foremost, you'll be surprised by the Washington Square Mall location on the East Side but the food is worth the mall adventure. And, it goes without saying, the eastside is always full of surprises. 

I'm still thinking about the Laotian jerky and delicious rolls we experienced during our visit. The pork spring roll and jerky were my favorites. Kicking myself for not purchasing a stash of the jerky to take home. The food was vibrant in flavor and color. Bring on the food photos! You'll find light and healthy options like the chicken larb gai salad as well as heavier fried dishes like the Laotian rolls filled with meat, veggies and rice noodles. If you're familiar with Vietnamese cuisine, you'll notice that several of the ingredients are similar given their geographical proximity. Fun note: Phan's Kitchen hosts fun events throughout the week to bring people together - pho and football on Sundays ;)

With it being located only a few blocks from my apartment, I was really hoping this place and I would hit it off. 3.5 stars might be a better representation of my experience. Service was great - no complaints. I give the extra .5 stars for the great beer selection, specifically the Kentucky bourbon barrel. Mmm...I can just taste it now.

So, why the downgrade in stars? A quick glance at the menu and I was chomping at the bit for a little of this and a little of that - because what's better than food with a glass of bourbon beer? Creative, well thought out food with a glass of bourbon beer. Unfortunately, you can call anything great, but that doesn't actually mean it's great. We ordered the fried pumpkin ravioli with honey, fig and date reduction, sweet potato fries with whipped cream cheese and cinnamon dip and fried green tomatoes with a flight of sauces. It seemed that all were fried in the same breading/frier leaving them all tasting the same. I can't figure out why, but the ravioli tasted like the french toast sticks I was served growing up in school. The sweet potato fries weirdly had almost no flavor at all. I wish I could put my finger on it. 

Regardless of the food, I'll be back for the beer and laid back atmosphere. It also helps that it has a great location on Mass Ave.

Note: nice looking website!

I get around. And when I say "around" - I mean I have eaten my fair share of authentic Mexican food. Chips and salsa till my teeth were ground to the gums. Ew gross, not really. But it would be worth it...If we were to play the scenario of being deserted on an island with one ethnic food of my choosing: it would be la comida de Mexico. Es la verdad. 

Top 5 reason Te Amo Los Chilaquiles:
1. Amazing margaritas - not too sweet and prissy, yet not so strong that the tequila takes over
2. chips and salsa that comes with regular and green salsas as well as a mild runny sour cream concoction
3. unique menu - they have your basic Mexican dishes like burritos and tacos, but you'll also find unique items like hominy soup and beet juice (yyyyeeahhh!)
4. beautiful new space - check out that sleek lighting ayayaya
5. Amazing service! 

Can't wait to give the hominy soup a whirl on my next visit!

Ayayaya! Elotes!

SO pumped to see this bright new spot in the "Mississippi Belle Strip Mall" - now there are two dining powerhouses in this strip wedged between College and Keystone Ave on 54th.

Yelper Sara C deserves the credit on this one. The combo of her personal message nudging me to check it out and tasty photos of chunky guac had me chowing on street tacos in no time. 

Why you shouldn't dilly dally to check out Indy Tacos:
-no frills, budget-friendly prices
-some of the best fresh guac around - key word: chunky
-friendly staff (how can you not love a business with enthusiastic owners?)
-elotes! (corn on the cob smothered in a mayo/cheese combo with chili powder (popular street food in Mexico - also found at Carniceria Guan.)
-delicious street-style tacos with a simple menu (in their words "it's all good!")

See pictures...'nuff said.

I've never left a restaurant craving cocktails for days. Not that I don't love a good cocktail but it's not typically something I crave and daydream about. Not until now, that is. Repeal and 12.05 Distillery have blown it out of the water with a creative cocktail menu prepared by King Bartender, Eli. Not only are his cocktails delicious but his charm leaves you wanting to stick around for hours. The food is delicious as well but I want to keep talking about the bebidas...

My two order recommendations (apologies if I've butchered the ingredients):
"Oh Your Funkiness" - cucumber lemon shrub, Allspice Dram (gives it a molasses-y warmth), gin and jalapeno infused syrup

"Sour Punch" - strawberry rhubarb shrub with vodka - I know there are other ingredients but for me, it's all about the shrubs (drinking vinegar) - it's the ingredient that sets this cocktail apart from the pack

Last, but definitely not least, Repeal did a kickbottom job on the exterior and interior of this historical building (located in the Fletcher Place neighborhood). My favorite elements were the lighting (ranging from loose hanging bulbs to chandeliers) and the solid brick hallway that leads to the bathrooms (pee or not, you need to check this hallway out). 

See you at the bar with two cocktails in hand, Indy.

How have I not reviewed this place? 

I'm on a bibimbap kick and this is probably the best place in Indy to find it. What is bibimbap, you ask? It literally translates to "mixed rice" and is topped with pickled veggies like daikon and carrots, along with protein - beef, chicken, tofu and iconically, an egg on top. Koreans were throwing eggs on top of dishes before it was trendy. 

I specifically like Cafe Korea because the staff is enthusiastic about their product and you quickly can feel the family owned biz vibes here. The space is both clean and cozy with a wall displaying their local accolades. I have yet to sit at the spiffy counter bar - front row access!

Cafe Korea offers affordable lunch specials and their dinner entrees come with a Korean pancake and fruit after the meal. The staff handled my seafood allergy well and took the time to explain which dishes were on or off limits. According to the other reviews, I need to give the dumplings a try next time.

Fun fact: the recipes are all from the grandma/owner. This is a three generation business. They used to have a location in Indianapolis City Market downtown at one time.

This saddens me to write...the carnitas tacos=amazing, the beans= delicious, and the same goes for the chips and salsa. 

Unfortunately, during my last visit the girl working the counter was so unbelievably rude I thought I was going to blow a top. Between messing around on her phone and speaking to her coworkers she kept ignoring that we were standing directly in front of her and then, when she was "ready" to take our order she was pissy as all get out. I'm a firm believer that bad customer service can ruin even the best food. I know they have better staff on their team but this unhappy character needs better training or the boot. 
-------------------

CAT'S OUT OF THE BAG. I'M TELLING EVERYBODY. 

After meeting the marketing gals of Paco's at a Yelp event on Monday night, I quickly bookmarked this easy-to-miss business on 44th and Keystone. I had seen it (and the carwash tucked behind it) a million times, but not this time. We had our eyes on the Paco Prize.

The space is very clean with an open kitchen and friendly cooks behind the counter. You'll find a handful of tables and easy to navigate menu on the wall (order at the counter). 

Our order for two:
-four carnitas tacos (quite possibly the best I've had in Indy - very large chunks of  tender meat)
-side of rice
-side of beans
-chips and salsa
-strawberries and creama (their signature dessert)
Total: $17 (note: we had leftovers) 

All were extremely delicious. I'm drooling just thinking about it. I can't wait for our next visit. Fun fact: they have a new location opening up on the northside (different name- same folks).

What a tasty and delightful carryout experience! I've had this place bookmarked for eons and finally had the chance to enjoy it this past weekend for a carryout car date. I specifically bookmarked this business after seeing pictures of their pork carnitas mole. Great news, it's as good as it looks! 

We ordered the pork carnitas mole and the guacamole with chips for carryout. The food was all packaged beautifully and the carnitas were served with fresh tortillas. I am not one to often order mole but this one will certainly have me coming back for more. The customer service over the phone was friendly and efficient. Next time I'll have to take advantage of their yelp check in offer. 

Easy to see why this Castleton eatery is rocking five stars. #thankyouthursday

Whatttt???!!! Every dish here is worth adding a photo to Yelp. Good news is, its as delicious as it is beautiful. Fun note: this business is one of Yelp's Top 50 Places to Eat Indiana in 2017. 

Where to start? 
The fast casual vibe allows newbies to Korean food to ask questions and build their own bowls as they work their way down the made-to-order counter that boasts more than a dozen vegetables and fillings ranging from pickled daikon to zucchini. I personally enjoyed the sweet potato
Noodles with tofu and bi bim bap with Bulgogi beef. I love filling my bowl to the max with fresh and healthy vegetables - minus the work it typically takes to create something like this at home. There are at least a dozen tables inside but it's also a super convenient option for carry out. 

So happy to see this business adding diversity and a pack of flavor to the Carmel dining scene.

If this 575th review doesn't make you pull the car over to order the sweet daddy (5 meat sampler with two sides), I don't know what will.

Let me make ordering easy for you:
Meat daddy ($22.95): brisket, ribs, pulled pork, smoked turkey and cheese and jalapeño stuffed sausages with two sides of your choice (scalloped potatoes and baked beans for us). This meal can EASILY be split between 3 hearty eaters. We took home nearly half the meat after sharing it between two. Some of the tastiest BBQ I've ever encountered. The cherry on top? Unique and rotating side options. 

For dessert? They're known for their pies and milkshakes so you can't go wrong there.

Note: the line moves quickly but on the first night we visited they sold out before 8pm. I recommend going somewhere between 2-5pm.

We're going to start this review off with a little language tutorial. "Crep" Say it. "Crep" - just as it is being spelled here (Yes, I know, I know the correct spelling is "crepe"). It's like "crap" with an 'e'. My French friend from Lyon quickly corrected my "crape" pronunciation before we walked up to a vendor on the streets of Lyon. To this day, I have this constant internal battle between whether I should say it crep-like and be deemed a snob Immediately or go with the flow and say 'crape' even though you know it's conforming at its finest - and wrong. 

I couldn't even tell you how I said it the last time I visited Three Days in Paris, but I can tell you I want 5 days in Paris. I want it savory. Sweet. Fruity. Meaty. Cheesy. Ooey. Gooey. Preferably with havarti and a red pepper sauce. What's that you say? I can do it half and half? Oh, stop it! You're killing me with all of your délicieux options! 

When making the life and death decision between which crepe could be my final in this beautiful world - I tend to opt for the special of the day (most often loaded with seasonal veggies) or the Red Eggs with Bacon  - - egg, bacon, havarti, spinach and red pepper sauce!  For sweets, you'll find me gushing over the Twist - butter, cinnamon sugar and lemon zest.  #1 step in making Brittany S. a loyal customer: Hand me a Customer Loyalty card and watch me light up every time you punch a whole in it.

Would it be okay with you if I just copy and pasted Kinsey E's review because she pretty much covered everything I was going to say... 

I'm really feeling 3.5ish on this one but here it goes:

Food:
Great bang for your buck - quite possibly one of the cheapest brunch spots in the city yet with a little more pizzazz on the menu than your typical moms and pops diner (for ex. cheesy grits, mimosas and made in house jam. I was happy to find that you could substitute for healthier options like egg whites and turkey bacon. I opted for the spinach Florentine omelette minus the bacon- fret not, there was PLENTY of cheese to get my dose of saturated fat in for the day. But, I'm not complaining...

Environment: I've said it before and I'll say it again, I'm a sucker for big windows and gobs of natural light. Check and check in Good Morning Mama's case. It's a rehabbed auto body shop with windows galore. 

Service: not so much. It almost felt as if I was sitting in an Ed Debevik's only the harshness was unintentional or shall I say natural? I'm not asking for cupcakes and rainbows, a slight smile will suffice.

While I do enjoy the food, the service is lacking. It's obvious management isn't concerned with customer service. I've witnessed employees (management) yelling at other employees while on the floor. While I wish I could say I love this place because the food tastes good, I probably will not return because I have been in this business before and if you cannot display external customer service, it is due to a lack of internal customer service.

Trying to plan a birthday party at a distance can be a challenge, to say the least.  But I thought I had it made when I found Sophisticakes' website.  The photos told me they could make beautiful cakes, and I felt it safe to assume they would taste as good as they look.  The decorated cake photos showed a passionate attention to detail, but as it turns out this was totally misleading.  

I called and made an appointment, since I would be traveling into the area for two days only and had all my other appointments lined up.  Kathy, the owner, was very personable on the phone and assured me she would have her designers come up with sketches prior to my appointment.  I left my cell phone number in case anything came up and she needed to move the appointment.  I did not hear from her and assumed we were still on.  However, on the appointed day she was totally unprepared.  This after my driving 250 miles!  And Kathy KNEW I was driving 250 miles to meet with her.  Okay, you are busy.  I understand.  But the look of utter annoyance on the owner's face when I showed up was not okay.  And did I mention I can read lips?  I know what she was saying to the counter girl back there, and it wasn't at all nice.  In fact, it is the last thing you would say if you ever wanted to keep a customer.  At that point I decided to cancel the cake order.  The last thing I need is to worry about whether the cake will get lost again, leaving me with nothing to serve to my guests, and I certainly don't need a bunch of attitude along with it.  

My advice to Sophisticakes is to try to be grateful for the customers you have and not treat them as an annoyance.  Companies who don't care about their business soon go OUT of business.  And try to manage your paperwork a little better.  Watching Kathy rummage around in stacks of paper all over the store looking for my order didn't do anything to inspire confidence in her business ability.  It just looked inept and inefficient.  And her excuses were totally lame.

Okayyyyyy, this place is awesome. 

The perk to being extremely late to your brunch double date is that the first couple to get there gets to let you know if the initial place you planned on meeting is lame, and also they get ample time to find a new place for the group. Lucky for me, we were so late, that the other couple was able to try TWO places and then finally end up in El Vez. (I know I sound TERRIBLE. And it's because I truly am terrible when it comes to showing up on time). 

Anyway. I love this place. It was around 1:00 when we finally ate and I was ravenous. I got the El Vez Burger and added chihuahua cheese and bacon which was actually only a dollar extra. It came with smoked poblano aioli (a lovely touch), lettuce, tomato, avocado. I added my own dab of ketchup and bam. It was so good. And I am not just saying that because I was crazy hungry. It came with an arugula salad on the side. (All of the dishes did). And I loved that too instead of fries. Actually ended up eating everyone else's salad. (More people need to jump on board with arugula). 

The coffee was delicious and much needed. The space is crazy cool - we all sat in this big comfortable booth. The waitress was really friendly and the food came out quickly. If I lived in Philly this would 100% become a regular brunch spot for me. Be aware though: this place is a lot. There is music, a lot of people, and many colorful decorations. I was a big fan.

The Mockingbird was there when no other brunch place was and for that (and my gigantic plate of scrambled eggs) I am eternally grateful and full... well maybe not eternally full. 
 
We sat outside because they didn't have any indoor tables available, but even with the heat it wasn't so bad! We had the shade from an umbrella and endless ice water to keep us cool. When I say endless, I am not kidding. We asked the waiter to keep 'em coming (think SJP ordering Cosmos a la Sex and the City). 

We were there a for a late brunch because our intended spot (Biscuit Love Gulch) had an unreasonable line. We were so late in fact that they were no longer serving brunch and were on to lunch. No problem because the lunch menu looked fantastic and had a small breakfast-y section. 

I got the 'Merica - scrambled eggs, bacon, toast, potatoes, orange slices. Yum. I asked if they could add cheese and spinach to my eggs and it was no problem at all. Bacon was crispy, toast was soft and came with butter and jam on the side, and eggs were fluffy and delicious. It was a lot of food. A LOT.
