But it all tasted great and that is the most important part. 

The only thing that could have made the meal perfect would have been an iced coffee, but they didn't have it. Like I said, we were there for breakfast basically, so coffee was needed. But I pushed through and just chugged more water. Our waiter was super friendly and helpful and didn't seem to mind the multitude of tiny alterations to orders nearly everyone had. 

I'd recommend! But get a table inside if possible... Not only just to beat the heat but because it's actually super cute in there.

I experienced racism at this establishment. I was getting fresh air via a bike ride, for the sake of my sanity, during this pandemic. Being thoughtful of others & following Phase 1 orders from our city had on a mask. After I ordered a juice a staff member (unmasked) on the other side of the shop told me that he did not like my mask b/c it looked like I was going to "rob them" & told me to take it off. I thought he was joking but quickly learned he was not when he repeated his statement in a stern manner. I am a 125 pound African American woman. This was not only hurtful but delusional. I left in disbelief and I am leaving this review publicly so that anyone who is African American or stands in support of our right to not be discriminated against, in 2020, chooses somewhere else to patronize. I am still in disbelief that this even happened and this staff member should be held accountable.

So after I had given this place 5 stars a month ago, I must come on and write a review updating the HORRID experience my friends and I had on Saturday night. Basically, don't come when its busy. Early on Saturday (between 4-6) is when it is busy and you will literally be forgotten and ignored, or maybe it was just us. Our waitress didn't check in on us for 45 minutes, resulting in us not getting to order another round of happy hour drinks.That was annoying, but not the end of the world, so we decided to get the check and move on for one more drink elsewhere before we headed to the basketball game. However, we never saw our waitress again. No really, she never came back. We had to flag down another random waitress after another 45 minutes and she finally brought us our check. She was very sweet and also confused. Our original waitress never came over to apologize. The manager did come over to apologize and he comped a few of our drinks which is why this is a 2 star review instead of 1. I appreciated the gesture but it was so horrible and awkward seeing your waitress just ignore the situation, especially when we saw her tending so nicely to all her other tables. "We are really busy" is not an excuse for horrible, bad customer service. I can't say I need to go back again anytime soon.

Cupcakes for days, matter of fact, put a week on it. A super friendly and extremely helpful staff. The inside is clean and organized. Allow me to get to the cupcakes, delicious. I got the red velvet with chocolate icing-awesome. We also tried the carrot cake, moist and tasty with great cream cheese icing which is not too sweet. Tried the reese's peanut butter cup which was my favorite by far. Also tried the coffee cake kind. They were good but a touch on the dry side, just make sure to pair it with a coffee, it's from La Colombe.

Nice! This was a sweet gem to have found next to our place as we were tired of the same old same from Longhorn's, Chick-Fil-A, and other major chain restaurants. This is the place to go if you're craving for burgers, meat, and drinks! 

The interiors doesn't match the exterior so we were in for a big surprise! The interiors kick ass!! I like it! Very different like an classy and contemporary spin to the western theme that is so boring like Longhorn's or Texas Roadhouse. Blah. I was in the mood for something fun and somewhat eclectic and this is the spot!

My husband was hankering for a burger and he was craving to go to Stein and Vine, another great location to grab a burger, but I was also in the mood for something different as we hadn't explored much of Brandon. He was happy that we came in because his burger was cooked to perfection as he WILL pick on the fact if it's toooo pink or too overcooked. So, they knew what he was talking about. I'm glad. I ordered the South of the Border but requested to substitute the angus with chicken instead and also instead of the bun, I wanted it on a bed of greens. It was delicious! I would totally order this again. So, if you're ever in the mood for something western, burgers, and not dine at Longhorn or Outback- try Square 1. You won't be disappointed!

From the first visit till now (I lost count) me and my family of 4  (including two toddlers) have thoroughly enjoyed this ice cream... from how it's made to how it tastes and looks. 

I'm a mom that wants my kids to enjoy the finer things in life, but without compromising too much health and rolled mountain makes this task easy and guilt free. 

The ice cream is made fresh right in front of you and made with the best cream (high quality), fresh ingredients and no artificial colors and ingredients.  

First you pick from their menu. They pretty much got all of America's favorites covered and last visit, I noticed they even added a few more flavors. 

Then they ask weather you want cow's or coconut milk for your base. One time I tried coconut milk but it was much too over powering in taste and masked the other flavors. I would love it if they actually had a different menu with flavors that really work well with their coconut milk base (almond joy anyone?). Or maybe ask for their suggestions first.  It is great that it is available and I would thoroughly enjoy it if I were vegan.  Instead of coconut milk, I always get cow's milk and it always makes a mean cup of rolled ice cream. 

Based on the flavor you pick, they'll add the ingredients along with the cream on a freezing metal plate. Then they take their scrapers, chop away, spread the mixture into a thin sheet, cut into strips, then roll into several rolls.  

They'll ask you if you want toppings. I like to say yes to their toppings from their original recipe as I find that they compliment the ice cream well. For my husband, he's not the biggest dessert fan so he does what he can to keep the sugar to a minimum. He enjoys the ice cream all on its own. 

This time around my family got green tea boba, mud pie and peaches and cream. For my husband's green tea, I asked for extra green tea as the first time we had it, the green tea flavor wasn't strong enough for us. It was a bit too much, but better than the first time. Next time I'll ask for just a little extra and I think that will be perfect. I love the fresh red been paste and the matcha powder has great flavor. My daughter's mud pie was so good with great chocolate and Supreme Oreo flavor. It was one of the sweeter options I've had. The peaches n' cream was out of this world. I was making my way through their flavors (I've tried 7 so far) and I finally got to peaches n' cream. Every bite, I just couldn't stop saying wow!!!! The whipped cream, caramel and teddy grahams on top along with the ice cream were just so perfect. It was light, flavorful and refreshing. It's my favorite flavor for sure and usually I'm an Oreo girl.  

The ice cream shop shares it's space with Dorinda's chocolates. These chocolates look so fancy and yummy. One day I'll be sure to give them a try. I believe Dorinda's actually works hand in hand in flavoring the ice cream but I'll have to double check. (Update: Dorinda's  makes the chocolate and caramel toppings. On a side note, you MUST try Dorinda's delicious ice cream sandwiches fit for the gods).

If you like super fresh ice cream with nice clean favors, I highly recommend rolled mountain creamery. They have your nice fresh lighter flavors and they have your richer, slightly sweeter options. I think they have something for everyone. 

I don't mind paying $7.50/cup because I only visit on special occasions and holidays and plus I'll gladly pay top dollar for high quality ingredients and the experience. The workers are also nice and knowledgeable. 

P.s. Check out the restaurants in the same south creek plaza. South Creek Pizza is so good. And Yosh's Unique deli is great for lunch.

Not sure if it's the "new restaurant" hype, the chain's reputation, or the great food, but I would highly recommend making a reservation, because this place gets packed.  I made a reservation request through their website online and they called back to confirm the reservation within the day.  We added a 5th person to the reservation 2 hrs before, and they accommodated despite being fully booked at 12:30pm on a Friday, but most of their tables are 4-tops, and it took us about 15-18 mins after our reservation time to be seated.  This place has a high-end bistro feel from the menu to the decor to the service.

Some notes on the 5-star service:
1) So even though we had a wait, the hostess came back to us every 5 mins to give us an update on our table, which was quite professional of them.
2) When ordering a burger, the server was thoughtful enough to mention that their version of "medium" was quite red in the middle.
3) The server brought new drinks promptly and, noticing I was using my knife with my salad, she brought me a new knife before my entree arrived.

Food was 4.5/5.0.   Our group had the Cheeseburger (see pic) ($11), Half Rack of Ribs ($14), Steak Frites (see pic) ($18), Fish Tacos ($14), and Vermont Cheddar Bacon Cheeseburger ($14).  Everyone really liked their food.  My cheeseburger was especially good and quite filling!  Since I was told "medium" was very red in the middle, I ordered "Well" which still left quite a bit of pink/red in the middle but was cooked well and tasted perfect.  I was able to substitute the usual side choices of fries or slaw with an option from the Sides menu at no extra charge.  I ordered the Three Cheese Macaroni, which I probably won't order again.  It was nicely done, but one of the flavors (one of the cheeses) had a particularly sharp taste and did not blend with the creamy/smooth texture you expect for a Mac-n-Cheese.  Their fries are the skinny type and looked good with the Steak Frites.

The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is because we found their Lunch Menu to be pricey.  Meals cost an average of $20pp for lunch - Burger $11, Soda $2.25, Side Salad $5 plus tax n tip.  A French Dip sandwich was $17, for example.

10 of us dined here. First of all in the middle of my meal the owner took my chair because he wanted a higher chair to help HIM (not another customer) so he can smoke hookah. Now at this very moment the owner is not letting us leave because he thinks we did not pay for a meal when in fact one of our members had to leave (he's a doctor and was paged) now he is leaving his patient and driving all the way back with his receipt to prove that he paid his five dollar meal! HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!!! 

Update the owner just threatened one of our diners when he said he is going to post on yelp about his customer service. He said he is going to track us down. Really? Really? Come on now.

Let me preface this review with the ONLY reason I gave them one star is because I can't give anything less.   My place of business orders  take out from here often and most of the time the food quality is decent but there have been many forgotten items such as sides of french onion soup and side salads.  We just write it off as a mistake but we don't even order from here anymore because it has gotten so bad.   So therefore this place deserves one star.  This really bums me out because I live out here in Sparks.  I WANT places to succeed out here and stay open.  I have seen one too many establishments close down in Spanish Springs and it truly bums me out.  But somehow this place stays strong even with the many times I have had messed up to-go orders and this following in-house dining experience has pushed me away from Red Robin for good. 

I am not sure what the problem is but my gosh...unreal.  Get your act together.  For one, their gluten free menu is online only.  Seriously!  My son has celiac and in order to eat dinner here with him I have to download the app and look at your GF menu online?  After being told by a snarky teen that I could only view this menu online my daughter spent about 10 minutes trying to download and navigate the GF menu.  Once we had it downloaded it was still unclear as to what entrees were completely GF.   Waiting for items to download on an iPhone so you can order is just downright ridiculous.  

We came here on a Saturday afternoon around 3 pm.  It was not busy by any means.  We were seated and it took about 5-10 minutes to be acknowledged.  The server  took our drink order and left.  She did not write anything down during our entire  visit and she REALLY needs to.  A list of things she forgot:

1. a kids apple juice
2. a side of jalapeño peppers
3. my mom's entire lunch
4. drinks were completely messed up.
5. My son has celiac so I ordered a side of apples, those were forgotten
6. My daughters side of fruit
7. asked for no sour cream or cheese in the soup and there was a large dollop and cheese floating around in the soup. 
8. we were given 3 place settings and there were six of us. It took a while to get someone flagged down.  Once we did get the attention of wait staff it was as if we asked them to donate a kidney to get more napkins and place settings.
9.  The worst part was that we went to THIS ESTABLISHMENT because my son has autism and is quite tough to take to a restaurant.  It is a rare occasion that we do so.  I thought Red Robin would be a great choice being that they are supposed to cater to kids and families.  

 When we placed our order, we told the server it was my son's birthday.  She said ok no problem.  She COMPLETELY forgot his birthday.  All around us people were getting sung to and "happy birthday'ed".  Nope.  Forgot his.  I would've reminded her but by the time we got our bill and food along with everything that was forgotten we (and my son) were just ready to go.  On the way out my son-in-law said to the server "You forgot his birthday"...to this she said "Oh I am sorry".  Nice.  Class act.  

We will NEVER go to this Red Robin again.  The service is just downright awful.  It is a shame because I know there are other RR establishments that are deserving of more stars but I will avoid the Sparks establishment.  No more take out for my workplace and definitely no more in-house visits.

ZoZo's is one of my favorite places to eat in Reno.  I have been coming here for about 15 years and the service, food quality and taste is so consistently awesome.  The garlic bread is some of the best ever.  Plus they keep the basket full for you and I love how they cut the pieces into small rectangles so I don't eat too many.  

Every special I have tried here has always been top notch.  The seafood is always cooked to perfection and the sauces are devine.  My absolute favorite though is the Zozo's chicken.  This dish is one of those that you would ask for as your last meal on Earth.  It has the perfect amount of pasta, sausage, garlic and chicken.  Totally amazing.  

The caesar salad is nice as well and their wine pours are always very generous.  They have a nice selection of wines to choose from.  There was a server here a long time ago and I can't remember his name but he was awesome.  He would consistently get "server of the year" back in the early 2000's.  

I love their creme brulee but I know some people do not like it since it doesn't have that hard sugary crust on the top.  I still like it regardless.  I love the raspbetter sauce drizzled over the top.  

If you haven't tried Zozo's yet you need to do so.

I wasn't sure what to expect when I pulled in here.  I think this place used to be an old Arctic Circle or something like that right?

The place is decorated very old school but it is cute and charming.  The parking lot was packed on a Sunday morning so I was stoked when we were seated right away.  The booth was cozy and private which I enjoyed but I think we were forgotten a little.  The service was a little slow but I LIKED this a lot.  We got to relax and not feel like we were part of the breakfast rush. 

I love how the tables come fully stacked with flavored creamers and lots of sugar and faux sugar selections.  Most places have like one creamer left of my favorite flavor.  Not Sparks Coffee Shop...they were fully stocked.  It was awesome.

I ordered the California omelet but this one came with bacon.  When it comes to bacon I forget that I am 41 and start acting like I am 80 (extra crispy please).  I asked that they make the bacon extra crispy in the omelet because fatty bacon in an omelet is just NAAAAAASTY!  My omelet came out with perfectly cooked bacon and it was very meaty and hardly any fat on it.  I LOVE bacon like that.  It truly was the perfect omelet.

My friend ordered the classic meat omelet and he was in heaven.  The meat was cooked perfectly.  Ham, bacon and sausage were in abundance.  The hash browns were awesome and I loved the little chives on top.  Everything was top notch.  The scones that are an optional item with the omelets are to die for!!!  They are the old school small town Nevada scones, not the Starbucks kind.  So so so good!  

Overall, this place blew my mind.  I can't wait to go back again!!

Updated 07-01-16.  Didn't think the place could get any better.  Met with Able last night about arranging a dinner conference for local teachers.  He is such a nice man and a hard worker.  Oh yeah the food and service was great too. 

Another five star review for this new place.  I am always happy to see another great place pop up in Sparks.  I have been here twice but the first time was appetizers so I wanted to wait to write my review after I had an actual meal here.  

The service is AWESOME!  The owner  is so friendly.  When we walked in he greeted us and talked to us for a few minutes and it felt like I was chatting with an old friend.  The server and busgirl were  friendly and always around to make sure everything was taken care of. 

I had the huevos rancheros.  The crispy shell with the refried beans was excellent.  The entire dish was yummy!!! The hash browns were crispy and nice and hot.  My friend had the chicken fried steak and it was crunchy and salty (just the right amount of salt).  Loved it!  We were both very pleased with our meals.  

The night we stopped in for appetizers was no different.  Awesome service and the apps were yummy.  We had the coconut shrimp and the beer battered clams.  The marmalade sauce was deelish.  Can't wait to come back.  

I read they have karaoke nights here and there is also a Valentines night concert.

They gave my credit card to a different customer, and I had to report my card as lost. 

They also require a minimum five dollar purchase, and make it difficult to use the WIFI. Nice place, but my experience was poor.

This place is a welcomed addition in a neighborhood that has been waiting for a place like this!  Sleek, no frills interior with a patio that would make you want to sit there all day.

We have dined here twice and this is our new go to weekly dining place.  The fried broccoli was lightly breaded, still had that crunch in every bite and the side of remoulade was the perfect accompaniment.  Jambalaya cheese fries are a thing and surprisingly they aren't carb overload.  Speaking of fries the debris fries are done right with well seasoned meat and no gravy to make them soggy.  The flavors work in harmony on both types of fries and they give new meaning to the word comfort food.  Boudin was authentic and the pickled "salad" in the middle added a nice bitter flavor to the spice of the boudin.

The shrimp???  Well pardon me while I order and devour pound after pound and you should too!  They are hands down the best shrimp in town.  On first bite they were buttery and then the flavor develops into spicy and finishes off with buttery again.  I have no idea how they accomplish this but it's downright magical for your taste buds.  

You can definitely taste the quality and the love that goes into every dish.  Impressive food at great prices served by friendly staff is a win win!  

I struggle to find reasons not to eat here every day and I can't wait for crawfish season!

I've been here about 2 times a year for about 6 years or so, and always enjoyed it.  It always was a great post-work happy hour.  But tonight, I went in with a friends, and couldn't be more offended.

I had 3 drinks, and I was not driving, really thinking I wasn't "drunk" or anything, but I was starting to be bothered by the service.  There was no waitress that defined herself to our table, and when I tried to go inside, I couldn't even get the same bartender twice.  It was far below what I'd been use to there.

I ordered at the bar, and then one from the table, as did my friend.  And then my friend was bothered by no service, so I had to walk in myself and order the next 2 rounds at the bar and take them back to our table.  

The service was so bad, I walked into the bar and I asked for one last drink and my tab to close out, they refused to give me my tab!!  Yes, not only did they say no to the drink, the refused to give me my tab WHAT? Fine, cut me off, whatever, but, let me pay so I can leave.  They made a HUGE scene at the bar for at least 10 minutes, and insisted I prove I was with a friend. They got another customer involved for some reason, sending her outside to confirm I wasn't alone.

And yes, I have the bar receipt, it was 3 drinks before they chose to embarrass me in front of my friends....

I'd been quite polite, talking to friends, not bothering anyone, and trying to be polite to the very chatty bar patron who started up a conversation sitting next to me.  Sadly, the woman next to me started arguing with the bartender and next thing I knew, there was staff loud and rude all around me, arguing.  I repeatedly asked, "I don't need a 4th drink, please stop the lecture (which she repeated and repeated and repeated "we have a policy, we have been sued, we can't serve more" and I BEGGED  PLEASE just let me pay my check so I can leave" and the embarrassment continued for another 5 minutes or so.  They just got louder and ruder in front of my friends, and more obnoxious.  It had been at least 10 minutes since I asked for my check, and they were STILL just sending one person after another to the counter to give me the same rude lecture after another.  I really wanted to explain to each person I'd only had 3 drinks, but it just became so obnoxious I was actually BEGGING to pay them so I could leave.

Wow, I did not drive there, I was not drunk, I quietly and peacefully asked for my check after 3 drinks, and because someone sitting next to me accused the bar staff of being belligerent (which they honestly were) they took it out on me, were excessively rude, and embarrassed me in front of friends.

All the way home, in my friend car, I just heard over and over, "wow, I can't believe I saw that" and I have no excuse for suggesting we go there anymore.  The band was ok, the staff outside was cool, but the bar staff was INSANE NASTY.  I had to apologize all the way home to my friends for suggesting we go there, because one of my friends apparently had their own run-in with a bartender also.

A friend took us there to have lunch. Obviously with everything that is going on (COVID) the place is not crazy packed, but if it wasn't for that I guarantee it would've been a big line of waiting for a seat there (so worth it).

We were greeted by Danny Boy (owner) and right away had our drinks  thought to us along with the menu.

Plenty of tables there. Menu with photos, the environment is great, you feel like you are in Mexico. Very tradicional.

We ordered some nachos as an appetizer. We asked to have onions and jalapeños on the side. Score! Best nachos I had in a long time. Make sure to order Asada for your choice of meat. It was so worth it. Every bite was so flavorful that there was nothing left in the plates.

They also serve with some fresh made chips and salsa. I don't eat spicy food, so Danny improvised and gave us some of the red enchilada sauce  (not spicy) and that was delicious! 

Our orders came in, big plates, every bite was delicious. We all ordered enchiladas but different flavors. My friend even asked to get one with chicken and the other one with shrimp (customized) since you usually get 2 enchiladas in your plate. 

Great service, awesome Food. Macho Tequilas it is definitely a great find! Check it out!

There's more in the future for these guys than just being a truck on a college campus. They cater to college kids: a lot of food, you can hold it while you walk to class, and it is cheap. I love the BBQ Crepe. And it's fun to watch these guys work to, they have crepe-ing(!) down to a science. 

The sweet crepes are probably the crowd favorite though. The cookies 'n creme crepe is perfection, and I've had my eye on many others on the menu. The wait can sometimes be a bit, but that comes with the success of any good food truck.

In a world where everywhere is a FroYo shop, this is my favorite in Philly. They always have really unique FroYo flavors, and their toppings are always fresh.

I'm usually against Skittles in FroYo because they freeze up and break your teeth. That's more of a general FroYo rule, nothing specifically about this place.

Prices are fair, and there's seating inside. It's a great stop if you're on South Street looking for some sweets in the summer!

What a great Italian spot! I've been here a number of times and have always been pleased.

I've been on weekdays during lunchtime, and Saturday nights...there's never a wait! I don't understand why, the place is always satisfying! There are TVs for sports and great bread to accompany your meal.

I'm a big fan of the Lasagna Bolognese, but the pizza is terrific too! It's quiet here for dining on a date with a nice little bar area if you'd like to go that route.

Coffee is a life necessity for me, and I'll drink it from just about anywhere I can. But what's fun is to try these different independent coffee shops that Indy has to offer.
Won't lie, I keyed in coffee shops on the yelp app and rabble came up so I decided I had to try it.
Located on 10th street you will find this coffee shop. 
Very interesting set up, but I love how unique it is, so many different kick knacks.
Staff is so friendly! I even got an extra shot in my latte free of charge because they had left overs from a previous order.
Not only to they have that liquid gold that is caffeinated coffee goodness, but they also have tasty snacks as well. I can never resist a good cheese danish so I had one of theirs and it was delicious! 
Not only is it a coffee shop, but barter school indy meets there as well. I'm also excited for pumpkin season to get here because they have a pumpkin spice latte that is awesome and not super sugary

Coffeebar is a good option for a coffee or a quick breakfast or lunch. I honestly don't care much for regular coffee but I'm a sucker for mocha. 

Their mocha is awesome, I'd say its in the top three that I've ever had. I tried their Giuseppe bar and their chocolate bread pudding on different occasions. Both were big enough to share and tasted great. Well worth the almost four bucks they charged for them. 

The service is superb. The employees are super nice and quick too. They do some pretty cool latte art that never seizes to amaze me. 

With exposed ceilings, modern paint colors, exposed brick, cool wall decor and a really cool looking chandelier, the place is inviting and fun to hang out in.

The only thing I regret was not ordering the Shrimp Po Boy!!! From the looks of precious commentators, the Shrimp Po Boy looked crisp, thick and had jumbo sized shrimp to enjoy. But Gumbo is something I wanted to taste around while touring the streets. Very petite portion so it sort of was disappointing because I wanted a dozen more to consume. This small place has very dim lights and the specials for the place gave off an authenticity view for us tourists at the time. It is incredibly hidden and we only found it by chance. The Seafood Platter is very appetizing-- will have to see it to order it when I'm back in the states. They have one of those thickest and by far the FATTEST sausages I've seen. My friend has been a fan of Jambalaya since she could crawl. Thought it was very meaty, way more filling than the Gumbo. 

To be fair, this place averages 3.5 but it's very nice to find myself enjoying small restaurants with a family charm shine on. The food was indeed fair so the wonderful service can lead me to say this was a positive experience for my friend and I.

Nachos. Nachos. Nachos. Good lord the nachos.

I can't say enough great things about this place (and the nachos). 
Both times I've been have been during restaurant week in Center City so the place was pretty empty. Apparently it gets pretty busy during the week and it's not rare that the place will be filled with merriment and cheer when 90% of it is reserved for a big party. The waiter was attentive and twice has suggested some spot on delicious meals. He even let us choose the Pandora station to listen to!

The food is incredible and it is very inexpensive. Second time I went everyone raved about their meal and their drinks (we brought tequila and they had the margarita mix ready for us). I had a the seafood soup and went for the optional pasta instead of the soup. The plate was bigger than my head and was brimming with deliciousness. I took it home and it fed me for 2 more meals! 
For 6 people the bill was just over $100 and this was after the nachos (remember me raving about that?), guac, and meals that could feed twice as many of us. 

Be warned it's a BYOB but they are more than happy to pour it for you. Believe me...*more* than happy. 

This is definitely a date night restaurant. Don't worry if neither of you speak Spanish -- the waiter is Italian and speaks English (ask him to tell you the story of how he got the job!) so that's not a problem. He does speak some Spanish from working there for a while so that isn't lost.

All around a really great place to have a delicious meal and a laugh.

The staff here is terrible. The food is decent but not good enough that I would subject myself to that experience again!

I was 9 months pregnant, with a 1.5 year old waiting for a friend to meet us there for lunch. I sat down to wait for her and was told by a staff member that I could not sit until we ordered. I explained I was waiting for someone and was told I could stand and wait. Seriously? Also, they don't have high chairs, definitely not kid friendly...

Aaah Pinky's! I frequented this place a lot when i was younger, now every calorie counts lol. Located in the heart of South Tampa, across from Cappy's pizza. There aren't any parking for Pinky's in the plaza they're situated in but you can park at Cappy's. Most of the seating is inside the restaurant, few chairs are available outside.  They don't take any reservations or call aheads. 

I had the ultimate BLT which is what i usually get but it was lacking something, i didn't like the bread they used, not as buttery toasted like i had in the past. My friends loved the Italian frittata, i had a bite and it was very very good. The rosemary potatoes were good too.

I usually don't care for the service if the foods good but our server seemed little pissed off, maybe it was because the restaurant was busy or she was having a bad day but it got awkward.. fast. 

Overall, come for the food.

Yeap 5 stars! 

Located on Kennedy Blvd, across the street from Barnes and Noble bookstore. Lots of parking available in the side and back of the restaurant. It was quite busy when I was there. Lots of seating available inside the restaurant. They offer different kinds of pastries like guava and cheese, croissants, slices of cakes, bread and so much more. 

I usually come for their Cuban sandwiches, which are very good. They are stacked high with shredded chicken or pork, cheese, veggies and condiments. They don't stop there, the sandwiches are then wrapped in foil and pressed until the cheese melts, everything is warmed thru and bread becomes crispy on the outside. 
They also have amazing desserts, I usually get the slices of cakes, varies from $2 - $2.30 a slice. My favorites are the Tiramisu and Tres Leches. Opera and Flan were among the favorites with my friends. It's the best deal for a cheat day celebration. 

I'll definitely be back for more of their yummy desserts!

Where: Rocco's Tacos on Bay Street
When: Tuesday nites starting at 7pm
What: endless tacos and tequila for $16.99. 

Little young me had 14 tacos tonite. Beat that!! ;)

This local joint is located in International plaza, it's my first time being here and maybe not my last. This place is singing on Tuesday nites because of their endless taco promo. My favorites were carne asada, chorizo and shrimp but disliked the blackened mahi (over cooked and salty). 

Since we were celebrating, i had original mojitos with the addition of jalapeños and no simple syrup, O-M-G, so good. I loved it so much, I ordered another but to my amazement, it was quite watered down. $10 for a watered-down mojito, heck no!

For dessert, my friend opted for the Mexican chocolate Sundae. I only had one bite and it was fantastic. Best sundae I had in a while! 

So why 3 stars? They added 50 cents for each lettuce "shell" we got. We end up spending over $10 on lettuce.  Not cool!

WOW! Such a great establishment. It's very easy to skip this place, located in the plaza with Yoko's sushi. Ms Muna, owner of this quaint restaurant and main cook was present when we dined on Saturday. 

Pros: 
* parking spots galore
* unlimited sampling to help you make the right choice 
* amazing prices 
* BIG portions 
* very flavorful Lebanese/Syrian food.

Cons: 
* not many seating available 
* high carb intake ( i was bloated for the rest of the day lol)

Overall, fantastic flavors. My friend and I got the 5 item platter and falafel sandwich + 2 water for $27. Not too shabby for South Tampa. I'll surely be back for more.

The age-old Philadelphia debate: who has the best cheesesteak? In my opinion Dalessandro's is a sure-fire contender. For me, Roxborough is about a 25 minute drive without traffic, and if you're wondering why I would drive that long and presumably pass countless other cheesesteak places (which I do), it's because of their fried onions. 

Even without the onions, they have the most amazingly flavorful beef in their steaks, but I'm telling you, whatever they do to their onions is addictive. 

I'm very happy to see they have a super organized system set up for window pickup during the time of Covid-19. Not only did I feel safe, it was well-organized and smooth. They have separate windows for ordering paying/picking up. And they call your name out on the loudspeaker so nobody needs to crowd the window. 

All in all, I got my fix yesterday and I was happy. It was nice supporting a long-standing Philadelphia staple during this time when it's needed the most.
Best prices around the area for breakfast along with good taste. I had two other spots I went to also but they don't compare to lee's. This is the only one now .

OMG amazing food but THE MOST UNUSUAL CONVERSATIONS are surrounding me. A grown man at the table next to us is describing, in detail, the wart on his hand. The gal next to us spent an hour proudly talking about some girl who had sex so hard that she went to the emergency room. 
Service: solid.
Food: yum.
Bloody Mary:perfect.
Come For the soup, Stay for the exhilarating conversation.

DD Mau is a Vietnamese Eatery that serves tasty Vietnamese entrees. I personally can't get enough of the freshly made Spring Rolls which comes in a variety of proteins that will satisfy any diet. The menu selection consist of Soup ( Pho) to Banh Mi Sandwiches and everything in between. This Hot Spot is located in a Strip Mall with plenty of parking. They offer great service and reasonable prices.

What a great experience here at The Blue Owl Restaurant & Bakery. Home Cooking at its best. Every dish I received was spectacular in flavor and quality. Customer service was very helpful, prices were reasonable and there is a huge private parking lot for the restaurant. This is a Must Try restaurant. Great place to chowdown .

AW

Jilly's Cupcake Bar & Cafe makes delicious and uniquely made Cupcakes. A  2x winner of Cupcake Wars they have proven that they can hold their own and can take on anyone at anytime. Put to the test  already Jilly's Cupcake Bar  ranks high because the judges said so. Jilly's Cupcake Bar is definitely on the fast track with no intentions of slowing down.  Displaying their skills already to the world they have shown their creativity and commitment to making cupcakes. By trying them you will not be disappointed .The cupcakes are superb and you'll be coming back for more.
Great Cupcakes! Highly Recommended.
AW

Italian Deli's are a must in every town. Fresh Bread, Sandwiches, Pastas and Italian desserts ( my  personal weakness). Literally heaven on a plate. This Deli/ Market has a huge menu of Italian classics or shop for all your Italian favorites in house. Either way you are getting want you desire. Everything I ordered from the deli counter  was fantastic, from the Spaghetti Carbonara to Meatball Sub then I topped it off with a Tiramisu ,delicious to the very last drop. 
This Italian Deli/Market is located in a Strip Mall with plenty of parking. Friendly service and reasonable prices. Aw

Family Night at its best. Burgers, Fries, Big Screen T.V's, Cocktails for the adults and a creative selection of Ranch dipping sauce. Twisted Ranch has taking family night to a different level. This place is very kick back and super live. Arrive early because they know how to party and pack them in. Street Parking is available. Superb customer service and delicious food. 

Enjoy !

This is a Hidden Gem, located in a strip mall next to an Asian market.  Wudon is a Korean BBQ Restaurant with a uniquely styled menu to serve your Korean BBQ needs. My menu items consist of a Seafood Pancake, Bulgogi, Seafood and Green Onion Pancake made to order and it was very delicious. The service here is friendly and  hospitable . Prices are affordable and  there's plenty of parking. Great dining experience.

You can't go wrong with a Brazilian Steakhouse. You are offered  all types of Brazilian flavored meat , a buffet with a variety of side dishes and a blocker of some sort to let the staff know to keep the meat coming or end it altogether. Then finally you are handed a   bill  after your meal. It's a busy task but a very delicious adventure.  Tucanos Brazilian Grill is very tasty and reasonable. Great customer service.

I'm not normally a big fan of chain restaurants, but Outback Steakhouse has won me over with this brand-new "open concept"-style restaurant in Carrollwood, along Dale Mabry.

Outback built this place from scratch with a new look, new drink selections, and a new menu. This ain't your Daddy's Outback Steakhouse anymore. Nope, this is the only Outback Steakhouse in the country with this "open-concept" dinning room and bar area. The walls are decorated with barnwood-style planks, and the interior is very bright with lots of windows and lighting. That is quite a bit different from the old "dark as a dungeon" look of Outback Steakhouse. The artwork on the walls is big and bold, and themed to the Outback brand.

The bar area is behind the hostess stand, and the centerpiece of the room is the large bar with bar stools and high-top seating in that area. Around the periphery of the room are the traditional tables and chairs, which can easily be pushed around to accommodate large groups. The open-air kitchen is to the back of the dining room, so you'll have a good view of all the action while you enjoy your meal.

The restaurant has been open for less than a week, and many of the servers are still sorting out all of the options on the new menu. I was very lucky that Ashley S was my server, and she was on top of her game tonight. There are several different Ashley's working at this new restaurant, so be sure that you ask for "The fun Ashley", and you'll be in good hands. She started by telling me about many of the new drink specials, and really knew the details of these craft cocktails, house-made sangria, and beers on tap.

Next we talked about the new menu for this restaurant. Again, this is the only Outback Steakhouse in the country where you can sample some of these items. The folks at OSI are using this location as their test kitchen, so expect to see some interesting twists on the menu. Ashley told me that I'd find many of the familiar stand-by's such as the Bloomin' Onion, Aussie Cheese Fries, and Shrimp on the Barbie for appetizers. But you'll also now see calamari and several different shrimp dishes, along with some small plate options for starters.

The menu is still predominantly steak, with a nice variety of cuts which can be prepared seasoned and seared, or wood-fire grilled. You can also order steak combos with shrimp and lobster tail. You'll also see a lot of your Aussie favorites like Alice Springs wood-fire grilled chicken, ribs, pork porterhouse, parmesan pasta, salmon, crab cakes, and swordfish as new items. You can select from soup, salad, potatoes, and classic side dishes for your sides, or select from their menu of premium sides for a slight upcharge.

For my dinner I started with a house salad, and that came with a basket of warm rolls and compound butter. For my entrée, I selected the 14-ounce New York Strip steak drizzled with roasted garlic butter cooked perfectly at Medium. For my second side, I paid the dollar upcharge and ordered the creamed spinach topped with melted parmesan cheese. Half of that steak is sitting in my fridge for lunch tomorrow. YUMMMM!!!

While I was enjoying my meal, Mindy, the manager, stopped by to introduce herself and tell me a bit about the restaurant's design and new menu. The place looks spectacular, and the new menu items will be a big hit. Best of all there is a huge parking lot around this restaurant, so the old parking woes are now long gone. Yes, you'll probably have to wait in line if you arrive during peak times, but that happens at every Outback.

If you happened to save room for dessert, they offer the Chocolate Thunder from Down Under brownie, cheesecakes. cookie skillets, apple pie, and some new mini parfait desserts to enjoy after your meal.

This restaurant is open for lunch and dinner, and they have lunch combos featuring soups, salads, burgers, and sandwiches from which to choose. 

If you're a fan of Outback then I encourage you to come visit and see all of the new changes. I know that I'll be back.

My Yelp buddy Michelle M and I are always on the lookout for fun places to enjoy a nice lunch near her office in South Tampa. We had been following all the stories of the arrival of the well-loved Goody Goody Burgers in Hyde Park, and we were very anxious to try the place after some of the initial hype had died down.

For those who don't know, Goody Goody was a famed Tampa hamburger restaurant that opened in 1925 and eventually closed in 2005. Legendary restauranteur Richard Gonzmart and his team from Columbia Restaurant Group stepped in to resurrect this Tampa icon. Gonzmart was able to acquire the rights to the brand, as well as the original recipes, signage, furniture, and even the magical POX secret sauce.

You'll find Goody Goody on Swann Avenue right next door to Cinebistro. You can park behind the restaurant, or across the street in the Hyde Park parking garage. Goody Goody opens by 7 in the morning to start serving breakfast, and stays open until 10pm or later on weekends.

The interior of the restaurant has a classic upscale diner feel, and there is a huge case filled with desserts and pies, but more about that later.

Breakfast is served from open till close, and you'll find breakfast sandwiches, four-egg omelets, and a personal favorite called "The Slinger" which is two beef patties, layered with home fries, two over-easy eggs, chili, cheddar cheese and jalapeños. I can attest to its legendary restorative powers after a long night of pub crawls.

Most people come a bit later in the day to enjoy the legendary Goody Goody burgers, but you can also order hot dogs, sandwich baskets, entrée salads, and Blue Plate specials like meatloaf, open-faced roast turkey sandwiches, Southern fried chicken, grilled grouper and more.

If you have a sweet tooth, then you'll enjoy the legendary Goody Goody desserts and pies including Butterscotch, Coconut Cream, Banana Cream, Chocolate Cream, and Apple pies. These are available by the slice, or boxed up and ready for you to take home.

Michelle and I were being well-behaved for lunch, and so we just ordered the Goody Goody Cheeseburgers with a side. Even though I'm not a big fan of ketchup on my burgers, I decided to try the POX-style which included pickle slices, onions, and the tomato-based secret sauce. The burger was delicious, and we learned that it was locally-sourced Florida beef. I found the secret sauce to be too sweet and drippy for my liking, and so next time I'll order the burger plain and add mustard at the table, or else try the Hyde Park burger.

There are lots of choices on the menu, and I'm sure that you'll find something that you enjoy. Use the "No Wait" app to cut down on the time you have to stand around and wait for a table.

Goody Goody is back, and it is a real delicious option in Hyde Park.

Al's Finger Licking Good Bar-B-Que is that combination of a classic Southern barbeque shack, with some down-home Ybor City friendliness. You'll find Al's in a little shotgun-style house, just south of 7th Avenue in Ybor City. Al's sits on Angel Oliva Sr. Street (also known as 18th Street), and it's just below the railroad tracks. You can park in the small lot behind Al's, or in any of the nearby City lots and just walk over.

Follow your nose for the scent of smoked meats, and listen carefully for the crowing roosters. That's when you know that you've found your way to Al's. The big smoker sits right out front, and the rest of their catering vehicles are parked behind the house. The roosters are hiding under the front porch, or else walking along the streets. Yup, roosters in Ybor City. That's how they roll.

Enter Al's up the front steps onto the porch, or come in through the side door, and make your way to the counter. That's where you'll see the guys swinging the big knives, and chopping up the meats. You'll find the menu on the wall, or there are smaller versions to be found on each table. Place your order at the counter, and then take a seat. Your food will be brought to you as soon as it is prepared.

On the menu, there are sandwiches made with smoked meats with sauce (no sides), full dinners served with your choices of two sides, meats only, sides only, and desserts. The meats include pork ribs, pulled pork, smoked sausage, chopped beef, dark chicken, white chicken, turkey breast, and turkey legs (Thursdays only). There are all sorts of combos so that you can mix and match to your heart's content. The dinner meats are served without sauce, so that you can taste the meat and the smoky flavor. They have bottles of sweet, mild, and hot sauces available, and sauces to go as well.

The sides are all very classic Southern and homemade from scratch. They include black-eyed peas, spicy collard greens, homemade Cole slaw, Southern-style potato salad, baked beans, yellow rice & chicken, Mac 'n Cheese (Fridays only), okra and tomatoes, and some outstanding homemade cornbread.

For the dessert fans, Al's features homemade pecan pie, sweet potato pie, and an ever-changing selection of OMG cakes.

The food is fantastic, and the staff is a lot of fun to chat with while you're enjoying some excellent barbeque. They know their regulars by name, and even know their favorite orders. On the day that I was there, Trey would say Hi as people walked in the side door, and then pull out the smoked meat to be ready to chop up their food and serve their meal. He made up a lot of To-Go orders.

Al's is only open Weds - Thurs from 11:30 to 4:30pm, and Friday - Saturday from 11:30 to 9pm. The restaurant is available for meetings and private parties, and they do a brisk 'on-site with the smoker' catering business. I liked Al's a lot, and will be back the next time that I'm in Ybor City and looking for lunch.

Ding, ding, ding, ding, ding........We have a winner, sports fans!

Cappy's Pizzeria has been a Seminole Heights institution for years, and they serve up some mighty fine pizza inside of a fun, kitschy, throw-back-to-the-50s funky Florida roadhouse kinda place. You'll find Cappy's on Florida Avenue, south of Hillsborough Avenue and right before the Florida Avenue "split". This local pizzeria chain also has locations on Bay-to-Bay in South Tampa, St. Petersburg, Brandon / Riverview, and most recently up into Tampa Palms. Most of the locations don't open until 5pm, except for those folks in Tampa Palms who wanted Cappy's open for lunch as well.

My business partner and his wife invited me to join them for dinner at Cappy's tonight, and we were also joined by their daughter and her husband -- all of them are Cappy's regulars and they knew the drill about signing your name onto the clipboard as you walked in the front door. We got there about 6:30 on a Friday night, and I had just enough time to click a couple of interior photos before we were being shown to our table back near the open-air kitchen.

As other have described, the décor is very fun with advertising pennants from old Florida roadside attractions, old license plates, and crazy antiques hanging on the walls. Additionally the tables are built like shadow boxes with glass-covered tops displaying board game playing pieces, and nostalgic memoirs of days gone by within Florida. Oh, and let's not forget the train that circles the ceiling of the dining room while you're eating your dinner. The menus are printed on the backs of old cardboard covers for vinyl record albums, and that just adds to the charm of the place. 

Speaking of the menu, Cappy's offers a Greek salad, Caesar salad, or regular tossed salad, along with breadsticks or cheesebread for you to inhale (I mean, daintily nibble upon) while waiting for your pizza to bake. You can order either NY-style thin crust pizza, Chicago deep dish pizza, or a calzone. The list of toppings includes anchovies, bacon, chicken, ham, meatball, sausage, pepperoni, artichoke hearts, banana peppers, basil, black olives, broccoli, feta cheese, garlic, green olives, green peppers, mushrooms, onion, pepperoncini, pineapple, spinach, sun-dried tomato & fresh tomato. Whew!

You can "build your own" pizza from the list above, or select one of their two special pizzas, "The Cappy" which is made with sausage, ham, pepperoni, green pepper, onion, and mushroom, or "The Veggie" which is green pepper, onion, mushroom, black olive, and tomato.

Now let me be perfectly honest......I'm not a huge fan of Chicago-style deep dish pizza, as I prefer to enjoy the tomato sauce and toppings atop a thin crust rather than munching on slices of pepperoni perched atop a wad of Parker House dinner rolls, but hey......it's your choice, and Cappy's offers both styles of pizza.

Since there were five of us we started with a large Greek salad and two orders of cheesebread, followed by a large "Cappy" NY-style pizza, and just to be sure that no one went home hungry we also ordered a second large Pepperoni pizza (also NY-style). Let the oinking begin now!

I won't bore you with the ooohs and the ahhs that followed each bite of food, so I'll just say that everything was delicious, and we did walk out with a box of leftovers for them to enjoy tomorrow while I'm busy working the Gasparilla parade.

Remember to bring CASH for your dinner at Cappy's as they do not accept any plastic, checks, or IOUs. CASH only, and there is an ATM on-site. Remember to also bring a hearty appetite as the portions are huge, and the food is amazingly tasty.

Miguelitos Taqueria Y Tequilas is muy bueno indeed!

Miguelitos is a sister restaurant to the insanely popular Miguel's Mexican Seafood & Grill located along Kennedy Boulevard. In fact, Miguelitos can be found about 5 blocks to the east of the original Miguel's. Where Miguel's is known for large plates of authentic Mexican dishes served with your favorite cocktails, the new Miguelitos is a very sleek and sophisticated tequila cocktail lounge which serves great Mexican small bites and lighter fare.

The interior of the restaurant is painted black and silver, and filled with booths as well as seating at the bar. The bar is a light show in itself with gently waving color changes throughout your meal. Outside, there is a surprisingly large patio with space heaters and large umbrellas to shade the Florida sunshine. There's also a second bar outside with a huge wall display of various types of tequila. (According to the bartender, they will be adding misters on the patio when the summer heat kicks in, and there is a possibility of tequila flights to allow you to enjoy many of the different styles and flavors of the fermented cactus juice.)

I started my lunch with a kicked-up spicy Bloody Mary, made from scratch, and garnished with olives and celery. It had the perfect amount of seasoning for my palate. Next I ordered a basket of chips with guacamole, which turned out to be a platter with the mashed up avocado, and then finely diced peppers, onions, cilantro, and lime off to the side. I was able to blend together the ingredients to adjust the guac to my personal taste.

The lunch menu is filled with traditional Mexican street-style tacos, tortas, enchiladas, rice bowls, and tapas. The tacos looked good, and so I ordered three different ones: smoked sausage, pork belly, and blackened fish. All very tasty.

Miguelitos will draw more of a young, single crowd versus the families that pack Miguel's. The bar area is very popular before heading out for a night on the town. Regardless, the Rodriguez family has a pair of very successful Mexican restaurants which are jewels along Tampa's Kennedy Boulevard.

My new Asian foodie obsession is a steaming-hot bowl of ramen noodles served in a rich, savory broth. Now let's be clear... this is not the instant ramen noodles in the cellophane wrapper that you ate in your college dorm room when you confined yourself to a $5 a week food budget (because you were saving money for beer). No, this is something very grown-up, and very delicious which has quickly become a food trend that is sweeping the country.

Japanese Kitchen Dosunco is an authentic Japanese-style, ramen-ya restaurant, located along Kennedy Boulevard, in a small strip mall, opposite the Fox Channel 13 TV studios. There is no blaring rap music, pretentious attitude, or an abundance of tattooed and aloof servers here -- this is a quiet, relaxed place to enjoy your meal and socialize with your friends. Dosunco offers stools to sit at the bar overlooking the kitchen, or tables of 4 scattered around the restaurant. The place can get busy, but the wait is seldom unreasonable.

The menu is very basic, with a variety of Japanese beers, sakes, sodas, and teas to start. For appetizers, they offer gyoza (dumplings) either fried or steamed, a green salad with miso dressing, and karage (Japanese-style fried chicken) with a spicy mayo dipping sauce. The karage is made with small pieces of chicken breast that are breaded and deep-fried. YUM!!!

Then you have the choice of either ramen noodle soup or udon, which is a thicker wheat flour noodle. Ramen is a thinner wheat noodle which is served in a meat-based broth, often flavored with soy sauce or miso, and uses toppings such as sliced pork, ground beef, dried seaweed, fermented bamboo shoots, fermented eggs, and green onions. The soup base takes hours to make, and it starts with roasted beef, chicken, or pork bones, mixed with a variety of ingredients and seasoned according to region and taste.

Dosunco offers a traditional miso ramen, a spicy miso ramen, a shoyu ramen (seasoned with soy sauce), and a broth-less abura soba bowl. They also offer some vegetarian-style ramen made with a soy bean paste broth. Each has it's own flavor profile, and all are very delicious. For the first time ramen eater, you should know that it takes time for the chef to individually prepare your bowl, so please be patient.

If you're seated at the bar overlooking the kitchen, you'll see Ramen Chef Alihiro ladling the broth into a bowl followed by a portion of freshly-cooked ramen noodles. To that he adds the various toppings and seasonings, and finally hands the bowl off to a server who whisks it to your table. The bowls come out one-by-one as they are prepared. Your bowl holds a traditional wooden ladle (larger than a spoon), and you scoop up the broth and drink it down using this tool. You'll also be handed chopsticks for eating the noodles, the pork, the egg, and generally slurping everything else down. (Slurping is acceptable!)

If your chopstick skills are a bit shaky, then ask them for the "Gringo Tool" (better known as a spork - spoon / fork combination). No one will snicker at you as everyone else is busy slurping and making yummy sounds.

A bowl of this deliciousness is about $13, and you can add the karage appetizer for $5 more. You're out the door for about $20 (before tip).

Dosunco is my preferred ramen noodle shop in the Tampa Bay area, though there are other choices. See what appeals to you, and happy slurping!

Alessi Bakery is a real Tampa gem that was founded over 100 years ago by Italian immigrant, Nicolo Alessi. The business of baking and cake decorating has been passed down through the generations, and Mr. Phil Alessi is still operating the business today.

You'll find Alessi's retail store on Cypress Street in between Armenia and MacDill. Watch for the big green roof, and the exterior signage in this busy area of town. This is where the beautiful wedding cakes and pastries are produced, and you can watch through the windows as the decorators do their jobs early in the morning. Alessi also has 100,000 square feet of manufacturing space in NW Tampa where they create many of their specialty items and custom orders.

Inside the doors to the retail store, and you'll see the baked good cases lining the walls to your right and along the back of the store. On your left is the deli area where you'll find soups, salads, delicious deli sandwiches, scachatta (Sicillian cold pizza), and various hot entrées such as Cuban roast pork, arroz con pollo, and chicken marsala. There is a dining area behind the deli, and you can enjoy your breakfast, lunch, or baked goods treats while watching the cake decorators through the windows.

Most folks are here for the pastries and baked goods, and you'll see that the cases are stocked with breads, cookies, exotic Italian and Cuban pastries, cakes, pies, and all sorts of diet busters. Fabulous treats just waiting to be boxed up and go home with you. (Sorry Blakely! I got you a Halloween pumpkin cookie, but I had to eat it, because it was calling out to me.)

I've used Alessi's for a number of catered events, and they've always done a superb job with pastries and coffee in the mornings; or salads, sandwiches, and cupcakes at lunchtime; or full catered dinners in the evenings. If you like traditional brown bag lunch meetings at the office, then you should really consider their combo lunch specials which provide deli sandwiches or salads with a bag of chips or pretzels, and a cupcake. Yes, Hello.....your own cupcake!

Alessi's is a great little spot that's open 7 days a week for your baked goods and catering needs.

The Tampa Bay Brew Bus is a fantastic idea, and a great way to experience many of the craft breweries in the Tampa Bay area while leaving the driving to someone else!

A group of Yelpers (led by the lovely and talented Kelly K.) chartered one of the Brew Buses for this past Saturday afternoon to tour several of the breweries and pour houses in Pinellas County. The bus (roughly the size of an airport parking shuttle bus) picked us up in front of Cigar City Brewery in Tampa and took us on a tour of three different microbreweries "across the bridge".

Dave was our driver, and Trey was our Master of Suds-ology / Tour Guide for the afternoon. They stocked the bus with a cooler full of three of their Brew Bus beers (Rollin Dirty Irish Red Ale, Are Wheat There Yet? Hoppy Wheat, and You're My Boy, Blue blueberry ale). It turns out that Cigar City produces these craft beers for the Brew Bus folks, so there is a natural relationship between CCB and BBTB.

Kelly brought along trays of ham biscuits, deli wraps, cookies, and a mountain of snacks to be sure that no one went hungry in between our stops. Our bus held 22 people (there is a larger bus for larger groups) in air conditioned comfort. Dave turned up the tunes while Trey handed out free beers and told us a little about the different stops.

We drove across the Howard Franklin Bridge while enjoying a frosty cold brew and happily checked in on Yelp (in the middle of the bridge), and then stopped at the Brewer's Tasting Room in the Feather Sound area of Clearwater to pick up some additional passengers. From there we headed to the Barley Mow Brewing Company in Largo, which was a very elegant pour house with a solid wood bar, an outdoor seating area, and a very cozy feel to the place. 

After about an hour, we piled back onto the bus for our second stop, Rapp Brewing Company, which sits in an industrial park in Seminole off of Bryan Dairy Road. Rapp had the widest selection of beers on tap, so several of us decided to pool our money and split a sampler of each type of beer.

You guessed it, after about an hour we were back on the bus for our third stop, 3 Daughters Brewing, in midtown St. Petersburg, south of Central Avenue on 22nd Street. This was the largest of the three craft breweries, and surprise, surprise, there was a huge indoor area filled with ping pong tables, electronic darts, giant games of Jenga, chess, checkers, basketball, corn hole tosses, foosball, bar shuffleboard, and even a miniature golf course across the parking lot. What a fabulous place to sip some tasty brews and then hang out with your friends and play some games.

After that it was back on the bus, and Dave brought us all safely back to Cigar City where we had left our cars.

The folks from the Brew Bus will help you to plan an itinerary which includes either stops in Pinellas or Hillsborough. They have an extensive list of the craft breweries and pubs in the region, and will work with you to pick the stops that will keep your group happy. You can either rent the entire bus and fill the seats yourself, or buy individual tickets on the bus and go with a group of strangers. Trey told me that you can also rent the Brew Bus as a shuttle to sporting events, concerts, and bachelor parties as well. Check their website for more details.

A couple of closing comments need to be made here.... The Brew Bus is open only to those 21 and older. You are expected to drink responsibly and party safely. If that is too difficult for you then please stay home. No one wants to spend the afternoon with people who are grossly out of control -- you'll just ruin the fun for everyone else.

Osaka Sushi & Grill is a new sushi, sashimi, hibachi, teriyaki, and Asian Fusion restaurant which opened about a month ago (as of this writing). Osaka is located in Carrollwood, along N. Dale Mabry Highway, tucked into a nondescript shopping plaza a few doors down from Ledo Pizza.

The spectacular interior of this place belies the ho-hum exterior of restaurant. Outside is a drab store-front with generic signage and a brown awning, but inside is a sleek, modern, and hip interior with brightly-colored water tube features, low-level lighting, a tiled floor, and dark wood furniture. There is seating at the large sushi bar, and a nice mix of tables and chairs around the room.

Osaka's menu is surprisingly diverse with a big selection of sushi, sashimi, rolls, and hand rolls, along with appetizers, soups, salads, noodle bowls, teriyaki and hibachi dinners, bento boxes, and a section of the menu filled with "Premium Fusion Entrées" including grilled salmon, curried chicken, Chilean sea bass, and grilled New Zealand lamb chops (to name a few).

I sat at the sushi bar and started my meal with their wakame (seaweed) salad, which was a generous portion of the sesame oil-flavored strips of greenery. After that I selected a mixture of nigiri sushi including tuna, seared tuna, salmon, red snapper, octopus, and King Crab (real crab -- not that fake krab junk).

At the recommendation of my server, I tried the Chef's Special roll of the day, called the Lovely Angel roll which was made with peppered tuna, then tuna, salmon, eel, yellowtail, and 3 different types of fish roe with crunchies & special sauces. I'm not normally a fan of sushi rolls covered in sauces, since that masks the taste of the fish, but this particular roll was quite tasty.

All in all this was a very nice experience in a lovely, new restaurant. Even though Carrollwood has the reputation for being hard on new eateries, I would like to see these folks succeed. They've put a lot of work into the interior design of their restaurant, the crafting of their menu, and the quality of their food. By the way, in order to stay competitive in the area, Osaka offers $1 sushi, $2 sashimi, and $3 rolls during Happy Hour.

Give them a try and see what you think.

Tucked away in an unassuming strip mall at the corner of Dale Mabry and Fletcher Avenue, in the heart of Carrollwood, you'll find the charming little Simply Pho & Grill. The restaurant occupies the same shopping plaza as Fresh Market and Bed, Bath & Beyond, but it's sitting around the corner so that it faces out onto Fletcher Avenue.

This is very good Vietnamese food served in a surprisingly classy environment. It's not the best pho in town, but it is certainly quite good, and it fills the need for lunch or dinner if you're in that section of northern Hillsborough county and looking for something different to eat.

The restaurant is sleek and modern, with a colorful light display around the room. Seating is primarily in booths designed for groups of four people. The wait staff is extremely friendly, and very helpful, making this the perfect place to visit if you are new to Vietnamese food.

The menu has a lot of the traditional Vietnamese appetizers - Spring rolls, pork sausage rolls, steamed or fried dumplings (Gyozas), shrimp wraps, crab Rangoon, and even chicken wings. By all means try something different, and share with your tablemates.

There are stir-fried noodle bowls with egg or rice noodles and a variety of different proteins (shrimp, seafood, squid, chicken, beef, or pork) sitting atop. They also serve soft vermicelli or Vietnamese Angel hair noodle bowls topped with grilled meats and seafood, and served with lettuce, bean sprouts, sliced cucumber, and crushed peanuts. Very tasty and surprisingly healthy.

If you prefer rice dishes, they have fried rice in a vegetarian style, or loaded up with a variety of proteins and veggies. Broken Jasmine rice platters are another favorite with grilled pork, chicken, beef, sausage wrap, and shrimp as toppings.

One of the main reasons that people visit Simply Pho is for their noodle soups (Pho) which is a northern Vietnamese dish with a rich and hearty beef broth that has simmered for hours and hours. Again, you select your protein which is added to a bowl of broth, rice noodles, yellow onions, scallions, cilantro, and a combination of spices and herbs; serve that with a side of cilantro, basil, bean sprouts, jalapeno peppers, and lime wedges. Grab your little Asian spoon and your favorite pair of chopsticks, and start slurping!

Simply Pho is a terrific little spot to enjoy a bowl of noodle soup, or any of these other Vietnamese delicacies. They're open till 9:30 on weeknights, and 10pm on the weekends.

Portillo's is a well-known Chicago-based chain restaurant serving Chicago-style hot dogs, Italian beef sandwiches, and other Midwestern favorites surrounded by kitschy nostalgia-ridden décor. This newest location can be found along Fowler Avenue near USF.

From the outside, the building is a standard brick façade with a series of murals depicting life in Chicago in the Roaring 20's. The inside of Portillo's is a large open space with ordering stations located around the walls. Decorations on the walls include photos of Chicago, sports teams, and famous Chicagoans. Hanging over your head is a replica of the beer wagon driven by Dick Portillo, and on the walls you'll find photos of the original 6x12 Hot Dog Stand trailer.

Now here's where it starts to get confusing.... there are three separate ordering areas: one for salads; one for hot dogs, burgers, and other sandwiches; and a third ordering station for shakes, malts, smoothies, and desserts. God forbid that you want to order a sandwich with a side salad, and a shake, because you'll have to stand in three different lines and pay at three different registers. This is either a poor restaurant design, or else there needs to be some major restaurant staff training, because as a customer this is very confusing and frustrating.

The food itself is ok, but nothing stellar. As a former Chicago resident, I have fond memories of eating Italian beef sandwiches at Wrigley Field, and so I ordered a combo char-grilled Italian beef and sausage sandwich. As expected, it was a pile of thinly-sliced roast beef with a sausage, split length-wise and char-grilled, a heaping of giardiniera Italian salad, all served on a sandwich roll and then dipped in the beef gravy. It is great in concept, but the bun did not hold together after being dipped in the beef gravy, and the whole thing split apart / dissolved into a mess on my plate. I'm not sure if it's the fault of the bun, or the dipping process, but this sandwich was a hot mess that needed to be eaten with a knife and fork.

My recommendation is that you skip the "dipped" sandwiches, and stick to basic Chicago-style hotdogs, burgers, or chicken sammies. The little side salad was OK, but seemed overly expensive for what we got in return. It's petty hard to screw up a milkshake or a malt, but again, I didn't think that it was anything special. I did not try the legendary chocolate cake as I've heard a lot of mixed reactions to this dessert.

I suppose that if you're from Chicago, then you'd be a frothing-at-the-mouth maniacal fanatic of the restaurant, since it serves your hometown favorites. But honestly, I've had a lot better food for more reasonable prices, and with significantly less hassles. 

*YAWNS*

Arirang is, in my opinion, the best of the Korean restaurants in the Tampa Bay area.

I've eaten multiple times at all of the major Korean restaurants in town, and really enjoy the cuisine. Arirang was one of those places that had been on my bucket list for quite a while since it is a ways south on MacDill Avenue, and a good hike from Carrollwood. You'll find Arirang about midway between Gandy and Interbay on S. MacDill in the Ballast Point area of town.

My frequent dining companion and very dear friend, Anna M, and I were in the mood to try something different for dinner, and after a quick look through our Yelp bookmarks we both decided on Arirang. The restaurant is small, but very cozy, beautifully decorated, and supported by a fantastic staff.

Our server for the evening was named Young, and she spent some time welcoming us to the restaurant and telling us a bit about its name and its cuisine. This very delightful lady was quite helpful, and willing to answer all sorts of questions about their menu and their specials. "Arirang", pronounced AH-Re-Ang is the name of a Korean folk song, and is considered the unofficial national anthem of Korea. The food of the Korean peninsula is an interesting blend of Chinese, Japanese, and Portuguese flavors.

After we looked over the menu, I decided to order something different from my usual Galbi short ribs, and so I placed an order for spicy pork Bulgogi. But first.... how about some appetizers? We ordered the fried Yaki Mandu dumplings which were filled with chopped pork, beef, chives, white onions, and green onions, and served with a spicy dipping sauce. We also ordered a small tasting of bacon-wrapped scallops topped with chopped green onions and sesame seeds. Normally this is the point during your meal where you rub your tummy and wait for the main course, but at Arirang they have more surprises for you.

Young was back with a trio of Korean tastes to put in front of each of us. We started with a small tossed salad topped with a miso dressing, a second bowl with some grilled pork floating in an herbaceous broth that's great over white rice, and finally a third bowl with their savory pumpkin soup. While we were busy nibbling away, Young brought out the traditional Korean banchan side dishes, and in this case we had nine different little bowls of greens, bean sprouts, radishes, pickles, kimchi, grilled onions and more. She also brought some Bibb lettuce wraps, a spicy paste, and a bowl of white rice.

Next came our actual main dishes, and in my case the Bulgogi was a sizzling skillet filled with grilled strips of marinated pork. The Bulgogi was topped with sesame seeds and had a healthy kick of spicy heat which I really enjoyed. Young showed me the traditional way to eat Bulgogi which was to put a few pieces inside a lettuce wrap, add some of the savory paste, grilled onions, and then roll it up and enjoy. You would then take bites of banchan in between nibbles on the lettuce wrap.

Thankfully I decided to stop after eating half of my main course, as Young was back again with a bowl of diced, fresh fruit that had been marinated in lemon juice and Sprite -- and it was fantastic! She also gave each of us a mug of their spiced cinnamon tea as a digestive aid after such a heavy meal. She very kindly refilled the banchan before wrapping up all of the leftovers, and she sent me home with plenty of Korean food for the next two days!

All throughout our meal Young was checking with us, and answering lots of questions about Korean cuisine and cooking techniques. At the conclusion of our dinner we also met Misook, the owner, and had a great visit with both of these delightful ladies.

After I reviewed all of the food, and the customer service, and the genuine hospitality that I received for the cost of my meal, I am convinced that these folks are the best in town! I really like Korean food, and so I'll gladly go back to see them again. My dinner was $25 for everything listed above, which included two Diet Cokes.

If you're in that area for lunch, many of their lunch-sized portions are priced under $12.

Westchase coffee drinkers rejoice! You've got a great new independently-owned coffee bar and café sitting in the little "Restaurant Row" section of the community, next door to the World of Beer, and across the street from Westchase Elementary School.

That's right Moms and Dads, right after you drop off the little munchkins at school you can race across the street for a cup of finely-crafted, premium roasted coffee - the kind that Juan and his fuzzy little burro hauled down from the mountain tops in Jamaica. This is not a big Fortune 500 enterprise pumping out gallons of over-priced Seattle swill, but rather a local Westchase couple providing a high-end coffee experience without the corporate attitude. 

I should confess that I don't drink coffee, but that doesn't stop me from appreciating a fine little coffee shop and café. The Grind is a real alternative to chains with their handcrafted espresso drinks, a full tea bar, and real food options. 

There is a breakfast menu and a standard café menu to help fill your tummy as you ponder the many delicious caffeinated drink options. For breakfast they serve frittatas, egg dishes, pancakes, bagels, breakfast sandwiches, and pastries. The rest of the day they offer soups, salads, flatbread pizzas, and sandwiches. I was there for a client lunch, and I ordered the muffaletta which was made with salami, mortadella, ham, and provolone with homemade relish of kalamata. pepperoncini, sun dried tomato and diced onion. That came with a side of fresh fruit. Very fresh and delicious!

Since I wasn't partaking of the coffee I ordered an iced tea instead, made with freshly-brewed green tea. I like the fact that they offer some higher-end types of teas rather than depending on what comes out of the little colorful tea bags.

Their motto is "We grind for you" and promote the fact that their local baristas know that great espresso takes more than pushing a button. A delicious meal, and a wonderful experience -- even for us non-coffee drinkers.

Sushi Alive used to be a favorite stop for Happy Hour sushi prices when their restaurant was located in Carrollwood along N. Dale Mabry. Late last year they closed the original smaller restaurant, and moved into a massive restaurant site on the edge of Westchase along Race Track Road.

I was there on opening night in late December of 2015, and very underwhelmed by the service which our group received. It honestly felt as though Sushi Alive had bitten off more than they could chew (Sorry, couldn't resist!). The place was slam-packed on opening night, and the servers were totally clueless. The food, when it eventually was delivered to our table, was good, but we waited forever for our server to take the initial order and we had to beg other servers to refill our glasses of water.

Last night I decided to give them a second chance, and drove down through the heart of Westchase along Countryway Boulevard till it intersected Race Track Road. Sushi Alive occupies the space formerly held by the Courtside Grill, and it's massive inside. Directly behind the hostess station is a large sushi bar, staffed by about ten chefs, and with room for about 20 diners. Behind the sushi bar is the kitchen. Looking towards the right of the sushi bar is the full bar area and outdoor seating patio. Towards the left is the main indoor dining room. There are still big-screen TVs on all of the walls tuned to your favorite sporting events. That seems a bit odd for a sushi bar, but whatever....

The main draw at Sushi Alive is their Happy Hour prices. Individual pieces of sushi are $1, sashimi is priced at $2 for 2 pieces, and assorted rolls are $3. That pricing is in effect from 5 - 7pm Monday - Friday, and as expected the restaurant is packed during that time. 

No matter how many chefs are standing behind the sushi bar, you'll be waiting for your food during Happy Hour. Unfortunately the Westchase soccer Moms and golfing Dads have very little tolerance for waiting, and a couple of extremely rude people walked up to the sushi bar and started bitching out the chefs because they were having to wait "too long" for their food. Geez people, there's a McDonald's down the road that might be more your style.....

I ordered the seaweed salad to start which was the traditional thin strips of wakame, seasoned with sesame oil, and served with diced mango, and ribbons of carrot and daikon radish.
