That was followed by a nice selection of sashimi which the chefs had artfully prepared to look like rose buds on the plate. And then finally to top it all off I ordered the spicy tuna roll.

To be fair, my food was delivered quickly since I was seated at the sushi bar, and able to watch the chefs prepare everything. This isn't the best sushi that I've ever tasted, but it's inexpensive and tasty. If you're there during Happy Hour you fill up for less than $30, but during the non-Happy Hour times you'll pay about twice as much. If you're there for Happy Hour then be prepared to wait. If that's not in your snobby Westchase DNA, then go find a McDonald's.

Trader Joe's has finally come to Tampa, and after all of the waiting I can assure you that the store is worth the hype. Yeah, it's gonna be crazy crowded for the next several weeks, but once the initial frothing-at-the-mouth-must-have-cookie-butter mania subsides we still have a pretty phenomenal marketplace located a few blocks south of Kennedy off of Dale Mabry. 

The store can be found about half a block off of Dale Mabry on Swann Avenue, in a refurbished space that used to house a health club. There is a small parking lot adjacent to the store that holds about 70 vehicles, and once that's full you're on your own to find a space. Many of the enterprising neighbors are renting parking space on their front lawns for $5, or you can park in the lot at the Christ the King Catholic Church about a block away and say a few "Hail Mary's" as you walk back towards Trader Joe's. I would imagine that the parking issue will settle down in a few weeks, and it'll be just like any other business in south Tampa.

You'll feel the vibe as soon as you walk through the front doors at Trader Joe's. There are a lot of staff members roaming the aisles, restocking the shelves, answering questions, and helping people find various items -- and they are all laughing, joking, and having a great time. In addition to everything else, this is a FUN place to shop!

Down the right side of the store is the produce section with lots of all-natural and organic fruits and vegetables. I picked up a bag of kale greens for $1.99, along with an assortment of mushrooms, leeks, and peppers before moving down to the back right corner. Today they were demo'ing how they manufacture Speculoos cookie butter which is an insanely delicious spread made from crushed cookie biscuits that tastes just like gingerbread. I forced myself to have a sample so I could report on the creamy texture to my good friend, Chris W. After one small spoonful I was saying "OMFG!!!!!" (which means "Goodness but that is mighty tasty, I think I shall have another sample just to be sure")

Around the corner and along the back wall are the deli meats, cheeses, dairy, seafood and butcher cases, and after that you start weaving up and down the aisles -- just like a trip to IKEA. You'll find cereals, grains, nuts, breads, pastas, tomato sauces, salsas, chips, cleaning and health & beauty items, pet foods, a big assortment of wines, and their legendary collection of canned, boxed, and frozen entrees. Here are a few examples from today's shopping trip:

TJ's brand organic marinara sauce @ $2.29
Frozen entrée - Indian Paneer Tikka Masala @ $2.99
Frozen entrée - Lamb Vindaloo @ $3.99
Frozen fried Japanese-style vegetarian rice with tofu @ $2.99
Frozen box of wild salmon burgers (4-count) @ $5.99
Frozen Thai Shrimp & Vegetable Gyoza @ $4.79

Add to that their legendary Charles Shaw Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc wines (better known as Two Buck Chuck) @ $2.99 each, some natural cleaning supplies, and a few cartons of their TJ-labeled soup, and I was out the door for under $70.

Insanely good prices on lots of healthy food options. Most everything carries their private Trader Joe's label, so don't expect to find the big name brands. You're not paying for brand-name advertising, and so you'll find items that are a lot less expensive. Based on a quick reading of the food labels, they have minimal hidden sugars, salts, preservatives, and other experiments-gone-wrong from your sophomore Organic Chemistry class.

The folks working the registers knew that the place was mobbed today, and they helped make the best out of an agonizing situation. One of the cashiers climbed up on a ladder and hollered out "Hey look everyone I can see the end of the line! Wave to me if you're paying attention!!!" and other sorts of silliness. Everyone was so gosh darned friendly that it was tough to feel frustrated even when you stood in line for so long.

One word of caution, if you're not fond of screaming children then I would suggest going in the middle of the weekday when the little bambinos are locked away in school and the aisles are cleared of double-wide strollers. Oh, and watch out for roaming food bloggers who feel the need to artfully arrange the products so they can get a better photo while rudely holding up everyone else. Grrrrrrr!!!

Bring lots of patience and have fun at Trader Joe's.

Almost two years to the day from my original review of Happy Fish Peruvian Fusion Restaurant, and it is time for an update. Happy Fish will be one of the sites of our first "Latin Crawl" event for 2015, and so I needed to go back and coordinate details with the owner / chef.

You'll find Happy Fish along Armenia Avenue in the Winn-Dixie shopping center, just north of Tampa Bay Boulevard. If you're coming from the south it's best to take Howard Avenue north until it rejoins with Armenia. Once through the traffic light at Tampa Bay Blvd. you'll see a McDonald's on your right, and the shopping center on your left. Happy Fish is located right in the middle of this L-shaped shopping center, next to the grocery store.

Happy Fish has a new owner named Kevin, and he has improved the appearance of the restaurant by replacing the tables and chairs, adding new colorful murals to the walls, as well as adding some new items to the menu. He has also taught his staff how to interact with customers who are not familiar with Peruvian food, and they really go out of their way to explain the ingredients and preparation of the various dishes. All very positive changes.

The food is just as glorious as before with a number of delicious seafood, beef, chicken, pork, and native dishes which will keep your taste buds very happy! Many of us are familiar with ceviche which is made with a variety of fish and seafood that has been marinated in citrus juice, but very few of us have experience this dish in the Peruvian style with sweet potato, yucca, and two different styles of dried and puffed corn, and then served on a platter for sharing.

Seafood is the centerpiece of this restaurant with delicious platters of fish and seafood that has been sautéed, fried, and served up Lo Mein style. You'll be quite surprised to try Peruvian-style fried rice, known as Chaufa, and find yourself comparing that to something you'd find in an Asian restaurant -- only better. 

For the meat lovers, you can't go wrong with platters of Lomo Saltado or one of the Palomilla steak options served with sides like sautéed tomatoes, onions and herbaceous spices over rice. If chicken is your thing, then try it as Peruvian-style chicken fried rice, or Lo Mein style. Of course, you can always get the popular Latin standby of grilled chicken breast with rice and beans.

There is a new dessert item known as Picarones which are very light, beignet-style, Peruvian donuts drizzled with cane sugar syrup that has been infused with orange zest. Very filling and very delicious. You'll never go back to Krispy Kremes after trying these!

Happy Fish has all of your favorite Coke products, along with Inka Kola, Chicha Morada, fruit juices, beer, wine, and pitchers of sangria.

Chef Kevin and his team will be ready for the Tampa Yelpers on February 21st, and he has promised to speak with us about the history & culture of Peru, as well as the interesting mix of cultures which form the basis for Peruvian cuisine. If you can join us on that date then we look forward to seeing you (Details are here:  http://www.yelp.com/events/tampa-uye-2015-latin-crawl-1). If you're not able to join us on the 21st, then please give this restaurant a try the next time that you're in the Armenia Avenue area.

With my cooler of fresh seafood tucked safely away in my SUV, I walked back down Dodecanese Boulevard, along the Sponge Docks, to have dinner at Mykonos Restaurant. In my opinion, this is the best Greek food in Tarpon Springs, and that is saying a lot given all of the competition in the area.

Mykonos is a small, no-frills restaurant, and they easily get stacked up with customers during peak times. This feels much more like an authentic Greek taverna, and a bit less touristy than some of the other places at the Sponge Docks. Your placemat is your menu, and your server will be by to drop off a basket of freshly-baked village bread and take the drink orders while you decide what to eat.

If you're with a group of friends, then it is best to share some of their small plate opektikas (or appetizers). You'll find choices like the famous Saganaki flaming cheese, eggplant spread, chargrilled octopus, squid, shrimp, and other authentic delicacies.   They have a very excellent Greek salad, but also Horiatiki, Kalymnian, and Mykonos salads for something different.

At lunchtime the pita sandwiches like gyros, souvlaki, and loukaniko (Greek sausage) are popular, but the dinner entrées are just spectacular. You'll find a lot of grilled chicken, lamb, pork, and beef dishes on the menu. The names of the dishes might not be familiar, but the ingredients and preparation will be something that you'll enjoy. If you're in the mood to be adventurous, then I recommend Chef Andreas' special Greek creations, with dishes like papoutsaki (stuffed eggplant), briam (a Greek vegetarian specialty), and all sorts of charbroiled or pan-fried fish and seafood.

I started my meal with a regular Greek salad served over top of a scoop of their house-made potato salad. The salad was made from shredded lettuce, chopped tomatoes, cucumbers, green peppers, onions, pepperoncinis, Kalamata olives, and a chunk of fresh Feta cheese, all topped by a light vinaigrette dressing. I snarfed that bad boy down in no time, and happily consumed several slices of fresh bread to go with it.

Since I was in a "shrimp" mood after a long day in Tarpon Springs, I ordered the Garides Mykonos, which was locally-sourced Gulf shrimp, sautéed with fresh diced tomatoes, onions, fresh herbs, and crumbled feta cheese. This came with the salad, and a side of oven-roasted Greek potatoes. Lord have mercy......this was an incredible meal!

Mykonos does not have the expansive glass cases filled with decadent Greek desserts, and that is a good thing, because it allowed me to focus on this fabulous meal. I highly recommend that you add Mykonos restaurant to your Tarpon Springs restaurant bucket list! This place is #elfreakinyummo

A small group of my favorite Yelpers joined me at Sea Salt restaurant, located up on the second level of Sundial St. Pete (formerly known as BayWalk). The restaurant is quite elegant, and a real classy date-night type of place. Since the weather cooperated, our group decided to sit outside under their covered patio, and that was just perfect.

When you walk into the main restaurant you'll immediately see an open-air display of whole fish and shellfish sitting on ice off to your right, and a large bar area off to your left. We gave our name to the hostess, and they sent a server outside to seat us and hand out the menus. After taking our drink order, our server was back to present us with a little amuse bouche tasting while we contemplated all of the choices. (Where was Jeremy Stoppelman when we needed him?)

Along with our drinks we were treated to a bread basket, and a community plate of different types of exotic salt to mix with the olive oil and bread. Yeah baby, we be fancy now! We ordered a few appetizers to sample, and then placed the orders for our main entrées and shared side dishes.

My favorite appetizer was the warm, marinated octopus, sliced thinly and served with smoked paprika, beluga lentils, chorizo sausage, and a tomato marmalade. We also tried a sampling of fresh oysters while laughing about the evening's antics. For my entrée, I ordered the grilled black grouper over a bed of fava beans, smoked fingerling potatoes, edamame and oyster mushrooms. That was superb! Since our group is not shy about eating, we also ordered a couple of different side dishes to share, including their broccoli ricotta cheese gratin, and brussels sprouts, grilled with pancetta bacon, and drizzled with a bit of maple syrup. Seriously good eats!

I know that the four of us stuffed ourselves silly, but it was a very delicious meal, shared with really excellent company under the starlit Tampa Bay skies. 

If you're in the downtown St. Pete area and looking for a very fresh and unique seafood meal for lunch or dinner, then I highly recommend you give Sea Salt a try!

Besito describes themselves as a little kiss from Mexico, and that's definitely the ambiance you'll feel as you walk up to the front courtyard of this new restaurant in the Westshore Plaza area. Besito occupies the space that was vacated by The Palm steakhouse, though the entire restaurant has now been transformed into a high-class Mexican cantina.

Unlike most chain Mexican restaurants, Besito does not smother you with cheesy pictures of a cat wearing a sombrero, or the piped-in music stylings of 101 Strings playing your Mariachi favorites. Instead, the restaurant is classy and elegant, with a warm, romantic vibe. The wait staff was quick to our table with some very tasty salsa and chips to enjoy while we spent a moment studying the drinks menu.

I started my dinner with the Besito Patron Margarita, made with Patron reposado tequila, cointreau, pomegranate-tangerine juice, fresh, and freshly-squeezed lime. Happy Happy Happy! We decided to pair our drinks with the tableside-prepared guacamole, which was a fabulous show to watch, and even more delicious to eat.

I ordered the Iron Skillet Mixtos Tacos for my dinner, which was grilled skirt steak, chorizo, chicken, melted queso Chihuahua, nopales salad, avocado salsa verde, and chile de arbol salsa. This was a very delicious entrée, and there were oodles of leftovers to take home. They brought us some complimentary churros at the end of our meal, but I was honestly too stuffed to eat another mouthful.

After this delicious meal, I was most intrigued by the little "prayer doll / worry doll" that they gave to each of us. This tiny little figure was supposed to adsorb all of your cares and worries, and leave you free to enjoy the rest of your day. I have no idea if this actually works, but it was a unique end to a terrific meal.

I have been to the mountain and eaten the brisket. WOW!

That's all you would need to say to a die-hard 4Rivers fanatic, and that would earn you a fist bump and nod of respect.  However since most of us have not yet sampled Brett's favorite culinary mecca of smoked meat yumminess, let me elaborate for the uninitiated. 

4Rivers is a chain of BBQ smokehouse restaurants which started in Winter Park, FL under the control of Pitmaster extraordinaire John Rivers. John spent 20 years in the healthcare industry before retiring as president of a billion-dollar company. During that time, he had the opportunity to travel the country, honing his taste and talent for brisket perfection. 

4 Rivers Smokehouse began with the launch of the "Barbecue Ministry" in 2004, when John hosted a cookout fundraiser to support a local family whose young daughter was battling cancer. This one event resulted in a passion for supporting local schools, churches, and charitable organizations. He opened his first smokehouse restaurant in 2009 and has been slowly expanding his empire since then. This newest 4Rivers location in Tampa opened today at 11am, and I was one of the first people through the doors for the Saturday lunch rush.

According to a story in yesterday's Tampa Bay Business Journal, the 4Rivers crew started prepping and smoking 960 pounds of brisket last night. (Yup, that is nearly half a ton of moo cow!) They were also smoking nearly 500 pounds of pork, and major amounts of chicken, sausage, turkey, ribs and more for the grand opening celebration. Justin Clermont is the General Manager of the new Carrollwood location, and he was walking through the dining room and shaking hands with everyone as we were happily munching away on the smoked meat goodness.

You walk through the front doors and snake your way up to the front counter where the guys will take your "meat" order. Beef brisket is the king, along with pulled pork, burnt ends, sliced pork, smokehouse turkey, Texas sausage, smoked chicken, ribs, and wings. Your food is placed on a metal tray covered with a piece of butcher's paper. You can also order sandwiches and salads.

Your tray is slid over to the ladies scooping up the sides, and you have your choice of cornbread salad, fried pickles, mac n cheese, baked cheese grits, BBQ beans, potato salad, Smokehouse corn, Southern-style green beans, French fries, coleslaw, fried okra, collard greens, bread pudding, sweet potato casserole, smoked jalapenos, and your choice of cornbread or a biscuit.

From there your tray is slid to the cashier where you can add on drinks, bottles of sauce, homemade seasonings, and gift cards. You gather up your metal tray and then walk past the Sweet Shop  where you'll be taunted by cupcakes, "cake bombs", wedge o' cake, fried Oreos, pudding cups, and Kolache which is a type of pastry that holds a dollop of fruit rimmed by a puffy pillow of dough. 

Assuming that you make it past the Sweet Spot without dropping into a frothing diabetic coma, you then wander towards the back of the dining room to collect your plasticware and fill your fountain drink cups. Then it's out to the main dining area where the long tables are set out to encourage Texas-style family dining. Don't plan on an intimate little 4-top dinner. You'll have neighbors to your right and to your left, whether you like it or not.

The 4Rivers staff was constantly circling the dining area to say hi to everyone, refill drinks, bring over to-go containers, and answer questions. They stopped to tell us about the Pitmaster loyalty program where you can earn points and free treats for being a frequent diner at 4Rivers.

For lunch I ordered a plate of their legendary brisket, and the guys gave me a generous taste of burnt ends on the same platter. That came with three sides, and I selected fried okra, mac n cheese, and baked cheese grits. And the whole meal came with either a biscuit or cornbread. I highly recommend the cornbread!

The brisket was juicy and tender, and the homemade sauce was a perfect complement. 4Rivers has other homemade BBQ sauces, pepper sauces, and pepper vinegar out on the table. Very yummy meal, and well-worth a visit!

Sorry Brett but I cannot endorse your gushing enthusiasm for Mission Barbecue. In fact I am truly challenged to even give this place three stars, but here goes....

Mission Barbecue is a Baltimore-based barbecue restaurant chain that has outlets in 5 different states, with only a Ft. Myers and a Tampa location here in Florida. The Tampa location is at the site of a former Perkins restaurant at the intersection of Waters Avenue and Anderson Road in NW Hillsborough County.

According to the founders, "We believe there is nothing more American than BBQ. And nobody more American than the brave men and women who have sworn to protect and serve our communities and our country. We do what we do for the love of our soldiers, firefighters, police officers, first responders--all our loved ones in service."

They go on to say that they strive to serve authentic BBQ made from the freshest, most delectable ingredients, and serve it in a patriotic dining room filled with tributes to those who've made our country great, given to us by the people who earned them. Stop by at lunchtime, and you might catch them during their daily salute to the Stars and Stripes.

I totally support their mission, and believe very strongly in giving back to the members of our military and first responders in our community. I applaud their passion for this cause, and whole-heartedly cheer for their involvement with the Wounded Warrior Project. But at the end of the day this is a barbecue restaurant, and they need to be judged primarily for the quality of their food. I've been to this restaurant twice, and both times I've had disappointing results.

I ordered their beef brisket both times -- the first time with sausage in a two-meat sampler, and the second time just the brisket. Now I don't profess to be a barbecue pitmaster, but I'm certainly very familiar with what makes a good piece of brisket.

You should be able to hold the brisket slice from two ends and pull gently. The meat should easily separate and still be very juicy. There should be an outer crust (known as the  'bark') which is mahogany-colored, and there should be a pink smoke ring just underneath the bark which is formed as a result of the low heat and slow smoking process.

Unfortunately both times I ordered the brisket I found it to be dry, over-cooked, lacking in juices, and highly over-salted. Normally you can eat a bite of the brisket without any sauce and be able to taste the meat and a hint of the smokiness of the wood. In the case of Mission Barbecue's brisket I was immediately reaching for the sauce to try and drown out the extreme dryness. No bueno!

Mission Barbecue has a "sauce caddy" on each table which holds six different types of barbecue sauces, and there is also vinegar and hot pepper sauces. The people sitting around me today were squirting out their own homemade mixtures of the various sauces, and then dunking the meats into the sauce before eating everything. Everyone was commenting on the sauces -- no one said anything about the quality of the smoked meats.

Their sides are ok -- nothing especially unique: Mac-N-Cheese, baked beans, green beans, cole slaw, and fries. The only thing that I really liked was the peach cobbler that was available for dessert.

So after trying this place twice, I'll have to give it a thumbs down. I think their mission is fabulous, but their barbecue is lackluster and just mediocre. There are definitely better places in town!

Three stars for their mission, 0 stars for the food.

10 years ago today the very first Yelp review was posted to the site by a guy in San Francisco, and so it seems appropriate that I picked today to post my 1000th Yelp review.

I can think of no finer place to spotlight with this milestone review than a restaurant which exemplifies the very best of Tampa's food, drink, architecture, history, and customer service -- and so, Review #1000 goes to... Ulele.

For those who don't know, Ulele Restaurant is named after Princess Ulele, the young daughter of the chief of the west Florida Tocobaga Indian tribe. In a story that seems eerily familiar, Princess Ulele threw herself over the Spanish explorer, Juan Ortiz, moments before he was about to be roasted alive. The Pocahontas - John Smith legend happened 80 years later. Hmmmmmm...

A group of local Yelpers gathered at Ulele about a week ago to enjoy a spectacular meal, and to say Bon Voyage to one of our favorite friends. Eric C has taken a two-year internship in Providence, Rhode Island and so we wanted to send him out in style. With a bit of cunning and deception, we all gathered at the bar at Ulele ahead of time before Eric & Robbie's arrival. The plan was to surprise them, and then all enjoy a wonderful dinner.

The restaurant is located in a refurbished two-story warehouse along the Hillsborough River just north of the Performing Arts Center and Waterworks Park. The weathered brick exterior combined with the modern metal works sculptures is the perfect juxtaposition for this fine dining establishment. Something old - something new - and something WOW! Through the front doors and to your right is the open-air grill and a beautiful bar area displaying colorful bottles and Ulele's house-brewed beers on tap. Keep an eye on the walls for some gorgeous modern artwork and stained glass windows.

While we were waiting for Robbie & Eric to arrive, Head Brewmaster Tim Shackton gave us a tour of the on-site microbrewery, and shared some secrets with us about the delicious Adult beverages that are produced back in his brew palace. Order the Wedding Beer!!!

The hostess snuck our group through the back patio and in through the open doors that face the Hillsborough River. Our group hid our faces behind our menus until Eric rounded the corner, and then it was time to yell "SURPRISE!" and have some fun.

Amid all of the laughter we ordered some very fabulous dishes off their unique menu. The food is an interesting mix of locally-sourced ingredients with Gulf Coast seafood, fresh-from-Florida Beef, fowl, pork, and vegetarian options. I started with a dozen charbroiled oysters and a dash of their homemade hot sauce, and shared my oysters with several people. Others ordered crab mac & cheese, pulpo carpaccio (shaved octopus in a spicy piri piri sauce), okra fries, Florida native chili (alligator, wild boar, vension, and duck), and a wide variety of house special salads.

I added the half-sized Ulele salad, which was mixed greens, arugula, and watercress with baby Swiss, cranberry beans, fire-roasted peppers, onions, and a warm balsamic vinaigrette. Excellent choice as a light precursor to a delicious dinner!

For my entrée I selected one of the specials for the evening which was a dry-aged, 14-ounce NY strip steak topped with sautéed shrimp, and served over Ulele's white cheddar mashed potatoes topped with popcorn & roasted garlic. That came with a side of perfectly cooked string beans. (I confess that half of my dinner came home with me for the next night).

I should pause here to give credit to our servers Sydney and Rodney. Both were extremely knowledgeable about the menu and the food preparation, and they did a fabulous job keeping up with everyone's drink orders and special requests. They remembered what each of us had ordered and helped make some very useful suggestions about pairing entrees with appetizers and so on. Two thumbs up for you guys! 

By now we had bestowed our gag gifts upon Eric including a palm tree tiara, palm tree table centerpiece, woolen hat and scarf, and a tastefully tacky Hawaiian shirt. (Be sure to check out the photos.)

It was finally time for dessert, and wow the choices were fantastic. I ordered a basic dish of their homemade very berry ice cream which arrived at the table as two scoops served inside of a hollowed-out coconut shell. Very whimsical and extremely tasty.

Our surprise dinner for Eric was a huge success, and the folks at Ulele treated us to some incredibly delicious food and home-brewed beers, and then dazzled us with their creative architecture and spot-on customer service. Thank you to Ulele for an amazing evening, and thank you for giving me the perfect spot to honor with my 1000th Yelp review!

In a town known for small-batch craft beers, and trendy, hipster neighborhoods, it wasn't long before someone decided to open a trendy small-batch ice cream shop in Seminole Heights.

Revolution Ice Cream can be found along Florida Avenue, between Sligh and Lambright, in the Graham Building which is also home to a small beer & wine shop. The parking lot out front in miniscule, and it fills quickly with people running in to Chop Chop Shop in the next block. Patience is the key, my friends.

Revolution Ice Cream has about 15 rotating flavors, made in small batches, and sold in cups or scooped onto cones. Our group stopped there one night after dinner at a popular Asian restaurant, and since the place was busy, we opted to sit outside at a circular table.

The flavors are located on a board behind the counter, and each has a quirky, fun name. You'll need to read the fine print on the bottom of each display card to find out what's in that particular flavor of ice cream. The servers will give you small samples if you can't make up your minds, but be forewarned that this slows down the ordering process, and you might be waiting a while to get your ice cream.

The five of us each ordered a different flavor of ice cream, and then compared our notes. The ice creams were all pronounced to be tasty, though expensive. This is a fun place to try, but I'll likely not make the drive over from Carrollwood just to have some ice cream.

I'm a big fan (some would say obsessed) with 4Rivers Smokehouse up in Carrollwood, and so I decided to try their other location in South Tampa on MacDill Avenue at Swann. The food is consistently good, but there are some challenges with this restaurant.

Parking in this area is terrible, and so when the little lot behind the restaurant is full you'll need to circle and circle in order to find a space. Don't be like the snotty lady in the minvan who sat in the middle of the parking lot and blew her horn hoping that someone would hurry up and finish their meal so that she would have a place to park.

The restaurant is smaller than the Carrollwood location, but they still have the communal tables in the center of the room. There is also a large outdoor, covered patio which is cooled by misting fans. Lots of folks were standing in line outside by the "to go" window with plans to take their meals home. Inside the restaurant, the line of people was moving slowly past the counter while they waited for their meals to be prepared, and the food to be totaled up for payment.

I'm not sure how to best describe this experience, except to say that the 4Rivers staff lacked the rhythm and efficiencies of their counterparts in Carrollwood. There was a lot of hesitation and head-scratching as the staff members looked at each other in confusion. "Two sides or three with a full dinner?" "Wait, can he substitute cornbread for a biscuit?" Clearly there are some training issues still to be resolved at this store. The service was slow and cumbersome, so thank goodness that the food was excellent.

Those who are hoping to find a full dessert bakery like in Carrollwood, will be in for a surprise. The Sweets Shop has been downgraded to a glass display case near the cash register. You'll need to stand in line with everyone else if you only want to buy dessert, or else the South Tampa soccer Moms will hiss and boo at you with cries of "Line jumper!"

Thankfully the food was of the same quality as the Carrollwood location, and my standard meal of the brisket dinner with three sides and cornbread was very flavorful. My issue is not at all with the food, but just the service and the parking.

Brett mentions in his review that he is one of 4Rivers biggest fans, but I should like to point out that *I* am the one with the brick in the Pitmaster's Hall of Fame. So with that I'll give Brett and Chris W. a pat on the head, and a little Grasshopper cupcake and say, "Thanks for playing......maybe next year?"

I had the pleasure of visiting Roux last year during a special preview event which was offered to the Tampa Bay Yelp community. At that time the restaurant was still under construction, and the chefs were still tweaking the menu options. I walked away from that event enthusiastically cheering for Suzanne and Roger Perry's latest venture into the South Tampa restaurant scene. For those who don't know, the Perry's are the creators and owners of Datz and Dough restaurants as well.

Roux is listed as a Creole Nouvelle restaurant, in the style of the big-name eateries from New Orleans. They offer muffulettas, gumbo, Po' Boys, and etouffee on the lunch menu. In the evenings diners can expect white-linen service while they enjoy elegant New Orleans dishes such as turtle soup kicked up with a splash of Madeira wine and quail eggs, BBQ shrimp in a spicy butter sauce, shrimp Creole, blackened redfish, and smoky chargrilled oysters.

You'll find Roux on the southern end of MacDill Avenue, south of El Prado and Euclid. Parking can be treacherous in this part of South Tampa, so just plan on handing your keys over to the valet, or taking your chances parking on one of the side streets.

I've been back to Roux a few times for lunch while on business in South Tampa, but this past week a group of us went there for a late dinner after a nearby wine and cheese tasting party. We were all haaangry, and a fast-food cheeseburger on the way home just wasn't gonna cut it. Thankfully they were able to accommodate our group of five without too much begging and pleading.

The interior of Roux will definitely remind you of the genteel Southern homes and elegant dining rooms of many N'awlins French Quarter eateries. They've decorated the ceiling with tin roof tiles, and outfitted the walls with exposed brickwork, along with wrought iron details. Both the restaurant and bar area are lit with wall sconces featuring soft gas lighting with dark wood accents and themed artwork throughout.

The bar area (known as Toula's) features a bar made from reclaimed Southern bricks with a white Carrera marble bar top. The bartenders will be pouring traditional Crescent City cocktails including Sazeracs made with bourbon or Herbsaint, absinthe, Peychaud's Bitters, and sugar; Pimm's Cups made with dry gin, liqueur, fruit juices, spices, and a splash of ginger ale; French 75 cocktail made with gin, champagne, lemon juice and sugar; Bloody Mary's, Abita beer, and so on.

There are so many signature items at the restaurant, that you'll need several trips to find your favorites. My first choice for appetizers are their delicious char-grilled oysters made with Romano and parmesan cheese and an herbaceous compound butter. I also like their skillet cornbread, Boudin balls, and the Mumbo Jumbo Seafood Gumbo. For the entrées I like the voodoo swordfish, N'awlins-style barbeque shrimp, and trout menuiere. They also do some amazing wood-fired steaks, pork chops, and lamb.

Assuming that you left room for dessert, Roux is featuring tasty French biegnets to go with your Café au Lait, bite-sized Baked Alaskas served over a variety of fruit ice creams, and several other treats for your sweet tooth.

As the Cajuns will say, "Laissez les bons temps rouler", and let the good times roll with your visit to Roux!

Hank (the owner) and his team were incredibly gracious hosts to our little unofficial Yelp gathering on Tuesday night. We sat inside at one of the picnic tables and happily munched away on plates of pulled pork, ribs, fried catfish, sliced brisket, and smoked sausage -- along with collard greens, cheesey grits, baked beans, black-eyed pea salad, and a whole lotta other yummies. 

Hank brought over baskets of their onion rings, fried okra, fried pickles, fried green beans, hush puppies and fried sweet potato fries for everyone to try. We convinced him to hang out with the Yelpers for a little while and tell us all about building this restaurant - which is a mix between a Carolina BBQ house and a Florida fish camp. He said that his biggest seller is the all-you-can-eat catfish which is available three nights a week for just under $10, and it includes 2 sides. Hank's is one of the very few BBQ places that offers fried catfish, and it is very tender and moist.

He's especially fond of the ribs they churn out through their smoker, and I'm a big fan of the sliced brisket. It has a nice crunchy bark with a perfect smoke ring, and just the right amount of "pull" before it breaks apart into yummy goodness. I've never found it to be dry, and I generally don't add any sauce to the meat as it's already perfectly seasoned and moist.

We learned a little secret about Hank's that is worth going back to explore .... His Mom makes all of the desserts from scratch, and he promises that they are dynamite!!! 

The restaurant has only been open since the beginning of 2012, and he has already found some new fans to enjoy the food.

Give it a try, and let him know what you think.

Hong Kong House is a spectacular new Chinese dim sum restaurant and tea house located directly in front of MD Oriental Market on Fowler Avenue in the USF area of Tampa.

The restaurant is co-owned with MD Oriental Market, and they have gone to great lengths to offer delicious Chinese cuisine accentuated with the diversity of food found in their market. Hong Kong House is quite large, and they advertise themselves as an Asian banquet hall, tea house, dim sum and seafood restaurant. Inside the front door is a stunning water wall which sends the water underneath glass blocks under your feet, and then back up to the top of the enclosed fountain. Yes, they have fresh whole fish swimming in tanks just like in the market.

You are presented with two different menus when you're seated. The first is a dim sum menu with a large variety of dumplings, rice balls, steamed buns, and so on -- roughly 50 different choices. The second menu is the more familiar Chinese menu with a wide mix of appetizers, soups. pork, chicken. beef, seafood, tofu & veggie, and clay pot offerings. You'll also see noodle dishes, fried rice, and whole fish, lobsters, and Dungeness crab entrees. 

The ladies will wheel the traditional stainless steel dim sum carts to your table to bring you your order as well as to tempt you with many other delicious types of dim sum. I had a bit of a language challenge with my original server, but another lady quickly rushed over and explained what was on the cart and then helped me to make a selection.

I ordered the Steamed Shrimp Dumplings and Fried Chive Dumplings off the dim sum cart, and matched that with the lunch-sized Salt & Pepper Calamari and Honey BBQ Pork (small plates). The food was outstanding and went perfectly with a pot of freshly-steeped green tea. The whole meal was under $20.

If you're a fan of Ho Ho Choy or Yummy House then I highly recommend a visit to Hong Kong House. Very impressive food in an elegant new setting.

I will be the first to admit that Ted Peter's Smoked Fish restaurant is not for everyone. Some people are turned off by the roadside-dive appearance, or the fact that it "smells funny", or that you have to sit on picnic tables, or that you have to pay cash for your meal, or that the servers are too laid-back. Thankfully most of these finicky food snobs are not my friends.

Ted Peters is a Florida-style roadside shack located on the southern end of Pinellas County as you drive over the Gulf Boulevard causeway back into the area of South Pasadena and Gulfport. It is located directly across the road from the South Pasadena Hospital. You'll see the restaurant's sign as you drive over the bridge, and you'll smell the fish smoking as you draw closer.

This place has been around since 1951 which tells me that they are doing something right, and it has become one of my favorite destination stops after a day in Pinellas County. There is one building that serves as the main smoker, a second building with a covered deck that serves as the restaurant, and a series of outer buildings for the business. You park in the gravel lot, walk over to the covered deck, score a picnic table and wait for your server. The menu can be found on your placemat and it is very simple, and very basic.

You can order a smoked fish dip appetizer to start which is served with a handful of crackers and some hot sauce, or you can order a cup of Manhattan clam chowder. The main course is a plated smoked fish dinner made with your choice of salmon, mahi-mahi, Spanish mackerel, or mullet. (I prefer mackerel or mullet.) That's served with a scoop of German potato salad, cole slaw, a slice of tomato, a slice of onion, lettuce, lemon wedges and some homemade tartar sauce. They also serve surprisingly good hamburgers, cheeseburgers, and hotdogs in case you don't like fish. All of these items can be consumed on-site, or you can order them to go.

The flavor of the seafood comes from the smoking process, much like meats which are smoked in a barbeque pit. The raw fish are laid out onto racks, and placed over a smoldering fire of Florida red oak. The fish cook between 4 and 6 hours depending upon size and thickness of the filets. The smoked fish are then moved over into the kitchen where they're plated and brought to your table.

This place is not at all fancy, but it is a delicious treat for those who enjoy traditional smoked Florida seafood. Ted Peters is open 6 days a week from 11:30 am - 7:30 pm, and closed on Tuesdays. Make sure that you bring cash, as they do not accept plastic!

After our delicious dinner at Council Oak Steak House, my lovely date and I decided to try our luck at the casino, and so we ventured out onto the main floor at the Seminole Hard Rock Casino. For those who've never been here, the property is located off I-4 at North Orient Road and Hillsborough Avenue, about 10 minutes east of downtown Tampa.

According to their promotional information, SRH is the world's sixth largest casino with 190,000 square feet of non-stop gaming action, including over 5,000 slot machines, 110 table games, and about 50 live-action poker games. As with most casinos this place is lively, energized......and very very smoky. As non-smokers, my date and I were both struck by the heavy smell of cigarette and cigar smoke throughout the casino, and the eventual burning sensation in our eyes and throats really turned us off as the evening wore on.

I am a frequent business traveler to Las Vegas, and have spent many evenings exploring the various casinos, restaurants, and clubs throughout The Strip, but certainly do not recall the same feeling of "walking through an ashtray" as I do at SRH in Tampa. Frankly it is overwhelming, unnecessary, and a real turn-off to non-smokers like me.

Brittany took a stab at the casino's slot machines, and had a lot of fun playing the newer electronic games for a bit. I went looking for a craps table, and sadly learned that they don't offer live-action table craps. Instead I found a friendly blackjack table with a reasonable minimum, and sat down to try my luck.

After about an hour we were both feeling the effects of the smoke and decided to call it a night. We won back the cost of our dinner, plus a couple of tanks of gas, so it was a successful trip to the casino. Had the air been "fresher" I am sure that we would have stayed longer since we were both having a good time. Instead, the first thing I wanted to do when I got home was take a long hot shower, and throw my clothes in the washer.

The casino is very nice, and I'm sure that a lot of people enjoy this place. However, in my personal opinion, I have to say thanks, but no.......I prefer not to inhale second-hand smoke all night.

I've had The Front Porch Grill on my bucket list for quite some time, and since today was a gorgeous sunny Florida day, I decided to mosey on over to Seminole Heights for an enjoyable lunch.

The Front Porch Grill is located along Florida Avenue, just south of Hillsborough, and at the intersection of Idlewild. The Front Porch restaurant resides in a refurbished 1898 Victorian house that once was home to Tiffany's Tea Room. The formerly bright pink Seminole Heights landmark is long gone, and in it's place is this quaint two-story home with a great wrap-around covered porch. The Front Porch are neighbors to several well-known trendy restaurants, bars, and Cuban bakeries in this section of Seminole Heights. 

The restaurant is trying to create a dining atmosphere that reflects Southern comfort. Diners can enjoy soups, gumbo, both side and entrée salads, a wide variety of appetizers, burgers, sandwiches, and flatbreads. Entrées include Southern-style meatloaf, pot roast, eggplant parmesan, char-grilled mahi mahi, Porch Bouillabaisse, hot pepper vodka ravioli, steaks, and chops, to name a few. The Front Porch also has an extensive craft beer, wine, and cocktails menu.

Food is served on the spacious, covered front porch or in one of three rooms inside the restaurant. Since the weather was so spectacular, I opted to sit outside and enjoy my meal during a warm afternoon. I started my lunch with a side salad, and that came with a complimentary serving of homemade warm cornbread that had been drizzled with local honey.

For my entrée, I selected their Southern-style meatloaf, which sat on top of homemade mashed potatoes served with a port wine sauce, and a side of sautéed squash. To that I added the gorgonzola garlic bread which was a char-grilled French baguette, topped with caramelized onions, minced garlic, and served with a compound butter containing gorgonzola cream.

This was a real nice meal of basic comfort food, and setting on the front porch was delightful. I recommend a visit when you're in Seminole Heights.

Quite possibly the very best Italian meal that I have ever enjoyed.......Osteria Natalina is a small family-owned and operated restaurant, located in a little strip mall off MacDill and just under the Selmon Expressway.

Osteria is an Italian word describing an eatery which is a bit less fancy and more of a casual feel, but still with great homemade food. Natalina is the name of owner's (Spartaco) mother who still resides in Rimini, Italy, a northern coastal village. She makes many visits to Tampa each year to see her son. His Mother was born on Christmas Eve, hence the name Natalina.

Now this delightful Italian eatery is small, but with amazing personal service, and out of this world food and wine selections. Our meal started with Spartaco greeting us by the front door and welcoming us to our table towards the back of the restaurant, where he introduced our waiter. They told us that while there is a fixed menu, and that the chef prepares several special dishes each evening, and that if we didn't see anything that we liked that they would be honored to cook us anything from scratch.

Candace and I started with glasses of Sangiovese, an Italian red varietal, while our waiter described the Chef's specials for the evening. We settled on a special seafood dish in a light cream sauce, served over linguini; and Bucatini (sausage) with freshly-sliced cheese over spaghetti pasta for our entrées, and split a Mozzarella and Caprese salad which was drizzled with good balsamic vinegar. Oh my gosh, the meal was superb, and our waiter spent some time describing the dish and how it was prepared before allowing us the opportunity to pounce on our plates like rabid wolves. Everything was made from scratch, and simply outstanding!

Even though we were stuffed to the gills, we managed to squeeze in a few bites of a very light and delicious cake, layered with cream, and drizzled with a Key Lime reduction. Oh my goodness!

Truly an outstanding meal, enhanced by very warm and personable service. We felt like members of the family by the time our meal was over, and Spartaco once again shook our hands and thanked us sincerely for dining with them as he held the door for Candace and me.

Grazie Mille, Spartaco!  We will definitely be back.

Crab Shack has been one of my favorite little hole-in-the-wall seafood dives located on the Pinellas County side of the Gandy Bridge in a well-weathered wooden shack by the side of the road.

This place is packed with a variety of locals, including boaters, fishermen, gamblers from the Derby Lane dog track down the road, bikers, and people just wanting a no-frills seafood meal in an extremely casual atmosphere. You squeeze your way into the cramped main bar area, and either grab a seat at the wooden bar, or one of the small booths surrounding the room. If the place is packed, then walk past the bar to the hostess stand and leave your name. They'll do their best to seat you at a picnic table in the covered dining area, or at one of the outdoor tables so you can soak up some sunshine.

While you're looking over the menu, be sure to order a round of Oyster Shooters for everyone at the table. It's a plastic shot glass filled with a raw oyster, a dash of hot sauce, and topped off with vodka. You'll be tempted to order several, and you should!

The menu has a whole host of seafood appetizers including chowders, gumbo, crab cakes, oysters (fresh or fried), clams, mussels, smoked fish spread, calamari, and more. Most folks are here for the crabs, including Maryland hard-shell blues, Alaskan snow crab clusters, King crab, Dungeness crab, soft-shelled crabs, stone crab claws (in season), and a variety of crab sampler platters.

You can also order char-grilled, fried, blackened, sautéed, and broiled seafood platters with specialties like frogs legs, stuffed snapper filets, wild salmon, scallops, and catfish. The land lubbers in your group can feast on pastas, steaks, and chicken, as well as platters of wings, and a number of different sandwiches. Everything is cooked fresh to order, which means that you'll need to be patient while they prepare your meal.

My friend and I started off with a half dozen oyster shooters, followed by a dozen raw oysters and a round of beers. We put in an order for a dozen hard-shell Maryland blue crabs ("Blues") that were steamed and coated with Old Bay seasoning. To that we ordered some potato salad and celery sticks for sides, and sat back to enjoy a very messy, but incredibly tasty meal.

The Crab Shack gives you a pair of metal lobster crackers to break open the outer shells, and also a pair of kitchen sheers to cut through the legs. A little knowledge of crab biology plus these implements, and we were soon digging out big sections of delicious crab meat. This is a meal that requires a lot of time and patience, but you'll be well-rewarded with a full tummy and some happy smiles.

The prices are inexpensive and the divey, super-casual atmosphere is perfect if you want to spend a couple of hours chatting with friends and enjoying an outstanding dining experience.

Saki Endless Sushi & Hibachi Eatery is a great spot to fill up on "All You Can Eat" sushi, teriyaki, and hibachi-style meals for one low price. I didn't know what to expect, but a business associate assured me that the sushi was made fresh to order, and the $11 price tag for lunch is hard to beat.

Saki is located along US 19, right at the intersection of Gulf to Bay Boulevard (Route 60). This corner is known as the Clearwater Mall, and Saki can be found facing US 19, behind Michaels, and in between Lowe's and Costco. It's a bit tricky to find, but well worth the effort.

At lunchtime the restaurant fills up quickly, so plan to get there before the lunch rush. Once seated they hand you the menu and explain that you can order ANYTHING on the menu for the one flat price. Yes, anything.....and as much as you want. The only kicker is that if you leave food, or rice balls on your plate that you'll be charged a "piggy fee" and made to wash dishes for the rest of the afternoon.

So let's say that you check out the menu and decide to order a cup of Hot 'n Sour soup, or maybe some gyoza dumplings, and then a couple of pieces of traditional sushi, and maybe a maki roll or two -- and it's all one flat rate. Your dining companion might choose eggrolls, chicken wings, hibachi steak and some teriyaki shrimp -- and it's also one flat rate.

You can order sushi and sashimi either a la carte or on a platter, along with a surprisingly good variety of basic rolls and signature rolls. If you prefer the more traditional Americanized-Asian entrées you'll see sweet & sour pork, General Tso's chicken, beef with broccoli, etc. From the hibachi grill they have steak, shrimp, chicken, salmon, veggies and more. Then finally they have teriyaki steak, chicken, shrimp, and salmon. That's right -- everything for one flat price, so mix 'n match to your heart's content.

I saw at least five different chefs behind the sushi counter slicing up the fish and making rolls as fast as their fingers could fly. I'm sure there were equal numbers of folks back in the kitchen preparing soups, salads, appetizers, entrées, and desserts. Plus there was a large staff of servers checking in on each table to see if you wanted to order more food, refilling drinks, and whisking away empty plates. It was all operating very fast and efficient.

The lunch price is $11, and the dinner price is $18 for all you can eat. There's also a $16 Endless Sunday price. According to the menu you can order individual rolls and entrée items priced per item. I can only conclude that these are to-go orders since everyone else seems to be oinking their way through the AYCE deal.

Heads up little porkers, if you like Asian food, and you're willing to strap on the feedbag and eat like there is no tomorrow, then you need to make a beeline to Saki Endless Sushi and Hibachi in Clearwater.

Today for lunch, I was in the USF area and decided to stop and check out a new chicken salad restaurant that my friend Chris W. has been raving about. Chicken Salad Chick is located in the shopping center at the intersection of Bruce B. Downs and Fowler Avenue. It's tucked behind Chili's (which can be seen from the road), and next door to Ichiban Sushi. There's plenty of outdoor seating which will be nice in the warmer months, and a large dining area with a private dining room for groups.

Chicken Salad Chick is actually a lady -- Stacy Brown, to be exact. She went in search of the perfect chicken salad, and started tinkering around with various recipes until she developed THE BEST. She and her husband started a chain of Southern-style tea houses which serve chicken salad, deli sandwiches, homemade soups, and typical Southern sides (broccoli salad, grape salad, pasta salad, and fresh fruit).

You start by selecting your flavor of chicken salad. There are at least 15 styles to choose from, including pimento cheese, apples & grapes, curry, sweet pickles & hard-boiled egg, diced jalapenos, etc. Then you decide if you just want a simple scoop of the chicken salad, or if you want a chicken salad sandwich. Then you select one of their sides, and get all of that on a platter along with a pickle spear, wheat crackers, *AND* a warm white chocolate chip fresh-out-of-the-oven cookie. *insert choir of singing angels here*

I tried the Dixie Chick version of the chicken salad which added a dose of diced onions to the mix of diced chicken, mayonnaise, seasonings, and love. I opted for a bowl of fresh fruit for my side which was strawberries, blueberries, and seedless grapes. Their platters allow you to mix and match different styles of chicken salad, or a cup of soup and a half sandwich. You can even buy chicken salad by the pound to take home (or back to the office).

The decorations are very quaint and genteel, and remind me of my Mom's very Southern kitchen with pale green and cream colors throughout. You almost expect a lady in an apron to bring you your food, and then whisk away the empty dishes at the end of your meal. Ordering is done in a cafeteria-style line, and then they'll bring you your trays of food as they pop out of the kitchen.

If you have trouble deciding which type of chicken salad you'd like to try, they will offer you free samples. Nom Nom Nom!

We recently celebrated a friend's birthday at Haven, and were delighted with the entire experience. Haven is located at the intersection of Howard Avenue and Morrison Avenue -- at the former location of SideBern's. Just in case you're not familiar with the pedigree, Haven is part of the famed Laxer family restaurant chain, best known as the owners and operators of Bern's Steak House.

Haven is their newest venture, and as the motto states, Haven is Crafted, Cultured, and Cellared. In other words, they're known for crafted cocktails, cultured artisanal cheese, and  cellared wine selections. I would add to that they're also known for their house-made charcuterie, and some phenomenal small plate dishes. In addition to an incredible wine cellar, Haven also has their own cheese cave. Totally amazing!

Our group of three started with a nice glass of wine, while considering our dining options. We ordered the Cheese Monger's plate which was a chef's selection of 18 different tastes of cheeses. To that we added the Butcher's Plate which was a massive amount of Chef-selected cured meat and pork fat. Had we been smart, we would have stopped there, as we were all quite full from the delicious meats and cheeses.

But no.......as professional Yelpers, we knew that we must press on and try more of Haven's incredible small plates menu. Once past the many selections of cheese and charcuterie, the menu is then divided into three different sections. "Roots & Leaves" are the salads and organic vegetarian offerings. "Hooves & Feathers" is where you'll find fresh game, veal, pork, duck, chicken, squab, goat, steak, and marrow bones. And finally, "Fins, Scales & Shells" is where you'll find the fresh fish and seafood selections.

Our group ordered several different small plates to share, including:

* Thinly-sliced octopus with feta cheese, dill, candied olive, ink & pepperoncini aioli

* Whole roasted cauliflower with shallots, ginger, ham, and a goat's milk beurre noisette

* Hamachi Sashimi with jalapeno, mint, egg yolk, and cider Ponzu

* Snapper Escabeche with piquillo pepper, avocado, tomato, and celery

* Cobia Carbonara with speck (ham), egg yolk, and peppercorn spaghettini

* Grilled Foie Gras with dan dan noodles, cashews, and pickled mushrooms

* Stuffed Marrow Bone which is red wine-braised short ribs with a horseradish and mustard sauce

Thankfully we rested a bit before ordering one dessert to share between the three of us. At the recommendation of Cory, our server, we split the Dirt Pie which was Valrhona chocolate mousse, coffee soil, and a Scotch gummy worm. YUM!!!

Haven is a spectacular high-end foodies treat, and I encourage you to break out the credit card, and soak in the lovely ambience of the restaurant. Executive Chef Chad Johnson is really showing off his culinary chops, and you deserve to treat yourself to a fabulous meal.

Jack's London Grill is an authentic British pub sitting in the middle of St. Petersburg, along 62nd Avenue, just to the east of Dr. MLK Street. The pub sits on the south side of 62nd Avenue, and you'll have to watch for their signage if you're zipping along, otherwise you might miss the place.

Inside, you'll find a charming British pub atmosphere with TVs on the walls showing the latest soccer matches, and a steady stream of great British 80s hits pumping through their sound system. Spend a moment looking at all of the pictures, signage and artifacts which give this place it's character.

If you're in the mood for a proper British pint, or a craft beer, glass of wine, or mixed drink, you've got plenty of options, so take your time and try something which might be new to you. The menu is classic British pub food with a great assortment of savory pies, including steak & ale; chicken, brie & leek; Fisherman's pie; and the classic shepherd's pie. They have a chicken curry, classic fish & chips, and my personal favorite British pub fare - Bangers & Mash. Jack's also serves soups, salads, sandwiches, and a whole slew of pub appetizers and side dishes.

Since I was between business meetings, I had to pass on enjoying a pint of Boddingtons, and opted for an iced tea. For my lunch, I ordered the bangers & mash platter which was a perfectly seasoned and grilled sausage that had been stuffed with garlic, herbs, and a pork / beef mix. The lunch-portion banger came atop a dish of mashed potatoes, and was smothered with brown gravy. Grilled veggies and a roll completed the meal. In true UK style, I asked for a small dish of strong English mustard to enjoy with my sausage, and a short while later Chef / Owner Peter popped out of the kitchen with my mustard.

If you're not familiar with Coleman's or any other type of dry English mustard, the secret is to go lightly with this potent stuff. Much like a big ole hunk of wasabi, it will hurt you if you're not careful.

The sausage was delicious, as was the serving of mashed potatoes and gravy. I am anxious to go back and try their legendary fish & chips, as other Yelpers have raved about the dish.

This is definitely a fun place that serves authentic pub food. If you're in this section of St. Petersburg you should give them a try.

Umami Sushi is located wayyyyyyyyy up there on N. Dale Mabry, at the intersection of Van Dyke Road, and not far from St. Joseph's North Hospital in Lutz. The restaurant opened earlier this summer to rave reviews from my fellow Yelpers, and so after the wonderful folks at St. Joe's looked down my throat and up my birth certificate, I had built up a powerful hangry, and was in need of a late lunch.

You'll find Umami in a large shopping plaza just south of Van Dyke, which also houses HomeGoods, LA Fitness, and a bunch of other restaurants. The restaurant sits in the middle of the strip, and it's easy to drive right past it unless you're paying close attention. There is no dancing clown out on the sidewalk to advertise the restaurant.....just some simple signage.

Inside, the place is gorgeous -- very sleek and modern, with attractive lighting and furniture. I chose to sit at the sushi bar so that I could look over the selection of fresh fish, and visit with the sushi chefs. The menu is very expansive with a nice mix of Asian soups and salads to start your meal. They also have hot and cold appetizer specials that further highlight their talents with different styles of Asian cuisine.

Umami has a lot of sushi rolls -- with raw, cooked, and vegetarian options. They also offer the traditional sushi and sashimi a la carte menu, as well as sushi and sashimi platters.  If the idea of raw fish doesn't float your boat, then flip the menu over and you'll see cooked tempuras, teriyakis, and curries, along with noodle and Pad Thai dishes. Everything seemed very affordable, and certainly in line with other high-quality sushi restaurants in the Tampa Bay area.

Since the fish and seafood looked very fresh I ordered the luncheon-sized sashimi platter which came with my choice of miso soup or a ginger-dressing salad. I watched as the chef sliced the different types of fish for my platter, and then sat there with a curious look on my face as he started decorating the plate with a very intricate Japanese flower arrangement and hidden LED light. When the sashimi platter was placed in front of me I was in total awe of this beautiful piece of artwork which was now surrounding my lunch. BRAVO to the Chef!!!

The sashimi was perfectly proportioned and very delicious. It seemed a shame to tear into that beautiful artistic display, but I was seriously hungry. I saw they were featuring fresh uni on their specials menu, and so I ordered a couple of pieces of uni sushi to cap off my meal. Uni is not a taste which is popular with a lot of people, but I love it, and it was a nice way to end this delicious lunch.

Great little sushi place located wayyyy up there near all of the parks and cow pastures. If your travels take you to the northern end of Dale Mabry, then I recommend that you stop in and see the folks at Umami Sushi.

BJ's Alabama BBQ is served out of a refurbished drive-through fast-food place, located on South Dale Mabry in between El Prado and Bay to Bay. The restaurant is small with a large counter area, open-air kitchen & smoker, and a few tables - both inside and out. 

The intoxicating scent of wood smoke hits you as soon as you get out of your car, and when you step inside you'll see their open-air smoker and grill with all of that delicious BBQ goodness just waiting for you.

You'll find the menu posted on the wall advertising ribs, chicken, beef, pork, sausage and combo meals, along with plenty of sides. You can either eat everything there, or take it home for later.

For my lunch I ordered a two-meat combo with ribs and smoked sausage, and added potato salad and collard greens for my two sides. I'm not a huge fan of the overly-sweet Alabama-style BBQ sauce (lots of molasses and honey), but the food was excellent. The ribs were fall-off-the-bone tasty, and the collard greens had been stewing in their pot liquor all afternoon. The smoked sausage had a very nice mix of seasonings, and the flavor was enhanced by its time spent inside the smoker.

Don't show up in a shirt & tie, or you'll be wearing BBQ sauce for the rest of the day. BJ's is the kind of very casual place where you roll up your sleeves and get elbow-deep into the sauce. They do have a unisex bathroom so you can wash your grubby paws when you're all done eating. May I suggest a bib and a lot of paper towels if you eat ribs they way that I do!

This is a real basic, locally-owned and operated BBQ joint in South Tampa, and the ladies working there have every right to feel proud about their food. Very tasty, and not very expensive. Give them a try!

Surprisingly good diner / restaurant located in the heart of Temple Terrace, along 56th Street, just north of the Hillsborough River. From the outside, Sefano's looks like a pizza restaurant that never got updated, but don't let that stop you from going inside.

Stefano's is a blending of a Greek / Italian restaurant combined with an American-style diner. There's a wide mix of choices on the menu as well as daily specials on the white board. The portions are massive, and the prices are very reasonable. During the week they're open from 11am - 9pm, but open by 7am on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday for breakfast.

This is a seat-yourself kinda place, and you can choose from 4-top tables or 4-person booths around the restaurant. Your server will be there in a jiffy with the menu, to take your drink order, and to tell you about the daily specials. Stefano's is known for their Greek salads, and Greek specialties such as Mousaka, Dolmades, and Gyro Platters. They also feature homemade Italian favorites including Lasagna, Chicken Parmagiana and Chicken Alfredo.

The lunch menu has all of the traditional, authentic Greek specialties, along with soups, salads, sandwiches, wraps, paninis, burgers and sandwiches. At dinnertime you have all of the above plus traditional Italian meals, seafood, steaks, pork, chicken, and vegetarian dishes. Truly something for everyone.

I ordered my lunch off of the Specials board and had two massive crab cakes (each was easily three times the size of any other crab cake that I've ever seen!). Those came with a house salad, side of pasta and sauce, garlic bread, and a Diet Coke for $15. I took home half of my dinner, so it was 2 full meals for $15!

As I looked around, everyone was receiving HUGE portions of food, and most all of us were leaving with to-go boxes. I thought that the food tasted quite good, and was certainly pleased with the value of my meal. The next time that I'm on this side of town I'll gladly stop back at Stefano's for another meal.

My Yelp friends Coty and Paul asked me to join them one evening at Mei's World Pizza and Salads along Bearss Avenue, near Bruce B Downs, in the USF area. I wasn't quite sure what to expect, as the name of this place seems to imply a pizza shop, and yet Coty told me that they serve very good Taiwanese food. Hmmmm, well, she has never failed me with her selection of restaurants, and so I was game to give this place a try.

Sure enough, this little restaurant on the north side of Bearss Avenue looks like a pizza / sandwich shop from the outside, but inside, the place was packed with college students in the know, as well as folks looking for good Thai food. 

The first thing you should know is that nothing on the regular Thai menu is priced over $10. That includes rice bowls, noodle bowls and platters, traditional Thai appetizers, and a great mix of entrées. Secondly, they DO serve pizza......and apparently you can have them put Thai or Chinese / American food on top of your pizza. Finally, if you are so inclined, they do serve pig's feet, chicken feet, chicken lips, chicken butt, and a whole lot of things that will never go into my mouth. Sorry, but I just can't picture a chicken walking around on a pair of crutches because someone wanted to eat chicken feet! Nope, it's not gonna happen.

Coty ordered a number of very tasty dishes for the three of us to share, and so we enjoyed Mei's pan-fried pork buns, pepper-seasoned fried chicken (no feet, please!), hand-cut Zha Jiang noodles in a black bean sauce, and a sliced, boneless pork chop served with a tea egg. The egg was awesome, so we ordered some more of them. Mei, is of course the owner, and she & Coty got in to a very fun discussion about Coty's upcoming trip to Taiwan as well as her experiences with enjoying Taiwanese food in New York City.

I really enjoyed my meal, but was glad that I went there with people who were more experienced in ordering this cuisine. The wait staff at Mei's was super-friendly, and very helpful about making recommendations about the menu.

I liked this place a lot, and will gladly go back when I'm in the neighborhood.

After a couple of very long weeks at work, our team decided to treat ourselves to a superb dinner at Roy's Restaurant along Boy Scout Boulevard, across from International Plaza.

Roy's is the brainchild of culinary pioneer, Roy Yamaguchi. After graduating from the Culinary Institute of America in Hyde Park, NY, and earning his executive chef credentials in Los Angeles, he moved to Hawaii in 1988 and opened the first Roy's restaurant in Honolulu. Roy's is best known as a Hawaiian-fusion restaurant, serving the best of the distinct flavors of the Pacific Rim. This is a really wonderful place to enjoy an exotic dinner of very fresh seafood (flown in from around the world), which is not drowning in heavy sauces.

We began our evening with a celebratory toast, and I ordered one of the specialty drinks called the 1988, which was listed as a tribute to their opening year in Honolulu. This light and refreshing cocktail was made with Finlandia Grapefruit vodka, SOHO Lychee, and Patron Citronge. It was damn good, and surprisingly strong. One was enough for me!

Instead of bread, Roy's serves bowls of edamame which are warmed and salted just right. I highly encourage you to spend some time splitting open the bean pods and enjoying the soy beans instead of carbo-loading on bread.

We ordered some sushi rolls to share, along with our salads. As you might expect with a group of non-Yelpers who don't understand the etiquette of "take pictures first before snarfing down the food", any thought of getting a picture of the tempura-crusted Ahi roll and the Ebi roll kinda went out the window when the food hit the table. Oh well, they were good......you'll just have to go and order your own. Oh, and the shared bowl of poke was outstanding!

I did have a great salad called the Maui Wowie Salad which was made with butter leaf lettuce, and topped with shrimp, feta cheese, and avocado, with a caper lime vinaigrette dressing. It was very unique, and not at all heavy.

For my main course I tried one of the House specialties called Misoyaki "Butterfish", which was Alaskan Black cod, served with baby bok choy over Furikake rice, and drizzled with a light miso dressing. Wow, this was spectacular! Again, very light and very tasty.

Several of the guys ordered Roy's Pineapple Upside Down Cake for dessert, but I was too stuffed to have more than just a bite. This was caramelized pineapple baked with a brown sugar pound cake and topped with a heaping mound of vanilla ice cream. It was very tasty, and I know there was some serious oinking that would be happening later in the evening.

By the way, if you are following a specific diet, then speak with your server. Roy's has a complete Gluten-Free menu, and they will also prepare most dishes to meet your needs (no sauce, no oil, etc.).

This is a really elegant, yet affordable restaurant, which is perfect for a business dinner or date night. The ambiance is wonderful for quiet conversations, and the service was top-notch. Roy's has 20 restaurants in the continental United States, six in Hawaii, one in Japan and one in Guam. Go find one, and enjoy a great dinner.

I confess that I knew nothing about this restaurant until I read Katy S. and Kelleigh M.'s reviews, but have since been to Gino's several times for some delicious and classic Italian comfort food dinners.

Gino's Bar & Restaurant is located on the northern end of Armenia Avenue in Carrollwood. To get there you drive north on Armenia, cross over Busch Boulevard, and follow the road as it winds around to your right. Make a left at the first traffic light (which actually puts you back onto Armenia Avenue), and you'll see Gino's on your left, under the cluster of trees, and behind the gas station.

As you face the building the entrance to the bar is the door on your left, and the entrance to the dining room is the door to your right. Apparently they also have a banquet hall, but I believe that must be in a separate building. The place is very casual and comfortable with tables and built-in booths in the dining area, and high-tops, booths, and bar-top seating in the bar.

The wait staff is superbly-trained and extremely-friendly. Each time I've been there my server has talked with passion about the evening's specials and how the food will be prepared, and given lots of great suggestions about pairing appetizers with entrées and wine. I've never had to ask for a drink refill or search for my server when I was ready for my check.

The dinner menu is very classic Italian with a nice mix of appetizers including bruschetta, fried ravioli, calamari, Caprese salad, mussels, gnocchi, and flat bread pizzas. The entrées all come with Caesar salad, a house Italian salad, homemade soup, and some incredible garlic bread.

Dinner entrées include Italian samplers with lasagna, eggplant or chicken parmagiana, capellini or  linguini pastas. You'll find traditional spaghetti, baked ziti, raviolis, fettuccini alfredo pasta dishes. If you like seafood specials you'll find shrimp, grouper, salmon, mussels, scallops, and clams on the menu. Chicken or Veal lovers will see parmagiana, picata, marsala, and sorrentino choices.

During my last visit I had Veal Scapariello which was veal medallions sautéed with sage, homemade Italian sausage, mushrooms, pepperoncini, garlic, olives, and white wine served over linguini. (Please pardon me while I start drooling on the keyboard.) The portion was HUGE and there was plenty to take home for a second meal. Not too shabby for a $16 entrée!

The lunch menu has soups, salads, burgers, sandwiches, and wraps.

This place is well worth a visit if you're looking for something different from the standard chain Italian restaurants so prevalent in Carrollwood. 4 thumbs up earns this place a super el-yummo rating from me!

I really wanted to like this Midwestern burger restaurant based upon all of their hype when they started opening locations in the Tampa Bay area, but after my visit I drove away thinking "mehhh".

Culver's started as a fast-casual food chain in Wisconsin in the mid-80's, and has quickly spread to over 500 franchised restaurants nationwide. They advertise "Welcome to Delicious", and promote their Butterburgers and frozen custard, among other menu items.

This particular location of Culver's can be found on Nebraska Avenue, just north of Bearss. I visited there on a weeknight, and stood in line with lots of families. The menu is quite large, and it takes a while to read through everything before finally making your selection.

I ordered a Mushroom Swiss Butterburger with a side of onion rings, and took my numbered placard over to a vacant table while they prepared my meal. According to the information I read, Culver's uses a freshly-ground mix of three cuts of beef: sirloin, chuck and plate. The patties are mashed down on the flat-top in order to cook more quickly, but that also means there is a loss of some of the juices. The buns are lightly-buttered on the crowns, and toasted, and then the whole thing is assembled and placed into your basket along with your sides. (I don't get the concept of buttering the top of the bun, but I wasn't a fan.)

What I ended up with was a bun that was greasy to the touch, and meat that was dry and lacking in flavor. Thankfully they had added the Swiss cheese and grilled mushrooms, but I had to get up and get some mustard and black pepper to put on the burger. Maybe I was supposed to ask them to add condiments and seasonings, but that certainly was not made clear during the ordering process.

The onion rings were OK, but they'd sat in the fry oil a bit too long and were bordering on being burned. Again, back to the condiments bar for more ketchup and mustard as a dipping sauce.

In the end I paid $10 for a meal which left me disappointed. I've certainly had much better burgers at other places, and so I'll have to plan a return trip to see if I just happened to catch them on a bad day.

Bring on the street tacos, and step away from my basket please!

Acapulco Mexican Grocery is a fabulous little bodega / neighborhood grocery store with a small taqueria in the back. You'll find Acapulco at the corner of MacDill and Cypress in a small little strip center. It happens to be right next door to Rollin' Oats health food store, which makes a great landmark.

The very front of this store is a small ethnic grocery with dry goods, spices, homemade chorizo sausage, masa flour, and all sorts of salsas and sauces. If you walk past the register, the store opens up into a small taqueria / lunch counter and butcher case. On the right are the coolers for drinks, where you'll find your traditional Coke products as well as a nice selection of Latin sodas to choose from.

There are six-to-eight small tables in the taqueria, and about half a dozen seats at the counter, so this is clearly a locals place. The menu is short & sweet -- various types of proteins and tacos on the left, and sopes, huaraches, and taco platters on the right. The tacos are priced around $2 each, and the platters run a bit more. 

The soft tacos are served with diced onion and cilantro, and if you're a messy eater, they'll double up the homemade tortilla to make it easier to lift up out of the basket (for an additional charge). They serve your food with their homemade green salsa and a bowl of sliced limes, but don't go looking for fancy napkins and silverware. Nope, this is a place for paper towels and using your fingers.

The food is cooked to order, and it is fantastic! I happily gobbled up two chorizo tacos, and one of the sesina (beef steak) tacos. No need for any side dishes or extra food. Truly delicious, and this place needs to be on your bucket list!

Big Ray's Fish Camp is a classic Florida seafood shack located inside of a small building that looks like a concrete bunker in Ballast Point, down in South Tampa. You'll find Big Ray's along Interbay Boulevard, in between MacDill and Dale Mabry, and next to the Interbay Meat Market. If you're familiar with the area, this building used to be home to the Chubasco Seafood Market. 

Chef Raymond "Nick" Cruz took over the property last summer, and transformed the place into a great little seafood shack that serves an abundance of very fresh (right from the Bay and the Gulf) seafood. The interior of the restaurant has space for just a handful of tables, and a little lunch bar along the window. Otherwise they have seating outside along the railing and on the patio area off to the right of the restaurant. Big Ray's is decorated with a traditional kitschy nautical theme which fits in perfectly with the classic seafood menu.
