I've heard stories of their legendary grouper sandwich served grilled, blackened, or fried -- supposedly this rivals the grouper sandwich at Frenchy's, and so I'll have to go back and give it a try. They also have a grouper reuben if you prefer to slather the fish with 1000 Island dressing, cole slaw, and Swiss cheese. They have a variety of fish and seafood specials along with traditional burgers, Cubans, pulled pork, fried chicken sandwiches, corn dogs, and salads for the landlubbers in your group. Most all of the seafood is fried -- which is not a bad thing, as the batter is very light, and the food is not at all greasy.

I spotted the oyster Po' Boy on the 'Specials' board, and ordered that for my lunch, along with a classic devil crab to take home for later. The Po' Boy was served on a toasted baguette, and dressed with tartar sauce, lettuce and tomato, and then topped with big juicy oysters that were lightly battered and fried. You get your choice of sides with the sandwich, and I'm really glad that I went with the onion rings, as these are some of the best in Tampa. YOWSER!!!

I thought that the food was excellent, and was really glad to find this place. I'll be back there soon to enjoy the grouper sandwich.

FYI, Nick is building a new Mexican restaurant right next door, and plans to have that open in time for Cinco de Mayo. Ole'

YO! Sushi is a fun, gimmicky Asian restaurant sitting in the center court area of the International Plaza mall. The concept of conveyor belt "kaiten" sushi has been popular around the world since the late 90's, but has only recently been introduced in the US.

YO! offers seating at their small sushi bar, or in booths along the conveyor belt path through the center of the restaurant. The chefs will prepare small plates of over 80 Japanese-inspired dishes including hot classics, sashimi, tempura, salads, hand rolls and desserts. Each order of food is placed on a color-coded plate, and covered with a clear plastic dome. As the food zips by on the conveyor, you grab whatever you like, and then stack up the empty color-coded plates for your server. Each color of plate is associated with a different price - anywhere from $3 - $7 per plate, and the server will tally up your bill after counting up your various empty plates of food.

All of this is explained on the plastic-covered menu which serves as your placemat. At first I just grabbed some dishes that were familiar to me, but then I would look down at the menu, and look back up to try and grab something as it was zipping by. Very much like "I Love Lucy" in the pie factory!

The concept was fun, and certainly gimmicky, but I quickly grew tired of waiting for something that I wanted, and just grabbed whatever looked good as it came by. In the end I spent a lot more money than I planned, and thought that the whole experience was so-so.

YO! Sushi is a fun, novelty place for people that are new to sushi and don't have a lot of experience and expectations. In my case, once was enough.

My good Yelp fried, Anna M, tipped me off to a great little Peruvian steakhouse located on north 56th Street in Temple Terrace. Cazador Grill can be found in a commercial center located a few blocks north of Busch Boulevard.

Cazador is a "Parrilla Peruana" which translates to a "Peruvian Grill" or "Peruvian Steakhouse Restaurant". They feature high quality, marinated and grilled meats, and seafood accented by those delicious Peruvian sauces, all cooked on a parrilla grill by Chef Richard Diaz. The very first Cazador Grill was located in Arequipa, Peru (southern Peru). But then Richard and his wife moved to Tampa, and decided to open another Cazador Grill to showcase the food that they both love so much.

As with most Peruvian restaurants, the menu includes marinated and grilled meats (beef, ribs, pork chops, chicken breasts, and sausages), along with seafood (including ceviche), traditional Peruvian fried rice (chaufa), and other South American favorites. They have quite the variety, and some very affordable prices.

I was in the area for some business meetings, and stopped at Cazador for lunch. From the luncheon specials menu I ordered the Picanha platter (which is actually Brazilian Top Sirloin steak, but it's one of my favorite grilled steak options). My steak came with a side salad, and a mound of white rice. The food was excellent, and it's easy to see why Anna raves about this place. They've been open about two years, and they've earned "Best Restaurant in Temple Terrace" awards.

If you enjoy Peruvian, Argentinian, or Brazilian steakhouses, they I encourage you to try Cazador on your next trip out towards Temple Terrace.

SoFresh is a great little healthy food eatery located along South Howard in between Platt and Swann in the SoHo section of South Tampa. The restaurant is small, and so the place fills up quickly at lunch. They have a couple of larger tables inside, which are stacked up with communal diners, and a few smaller tables to the back. Most folks were taking their orders to go, as this place seems quite popular with nearby residents and business workers.

Parking is atrocious in this section of South Howard, so be prepared to circle the block while looking for a space in their tiny shared parking lot, or else bring a designated driver while you dash inside to pick up your to-go order.

So Fresh has a lot of customizable bowls, salads, and wraps, along with their homemade soups and smoothies. This style of healthy eating has become popular lately, and though it can be pricey, it's certainly a tasty and filling lunch.

The menu is displayed on big flat-screen TVs over the front counter, with constantly-scrolling pictures of the bowls, add-ons, and a list of ingredients. They also have printed menus for those who don't with to stand there and go "uhhhhhhhhhhh" while holding up the line.

The basic bowls and salads start at $10, but you can add-on various protein toppers, or egg and avocado for an upcharge. Wraps start at $8. I ordered the Greek bowl, which was made with brown rice, onions, diced tomatoes, spinach, feta cheese, cucumbers, and house-made tzatziki sauce. I topped that off with seared Ahi tuna for a $3 up-charge. If you want to eat super healthy, they you can top your bowl with tofu or Zoodles (zucchini noodles).

While waiting for them to prepare my Greek bowl, I also ordered their homemade chicken veggie soup ($4), which was a fantastic blend of veggies and slices of chicken breast simmering in a very tasty broth. Unlike a lot of soups, this one was not overcooked, and the vegetables still had a lot of 'bite'.

I thought that my meal was delicious, though it's a bit pricey to eat here every day. Eating healthy is a good thing, and SoFresh gives you a delicious way to enjoy a healthy meal.

'Live life to the coolest' is the motto at Jeremiah's Italian Ice, and what an awesome way to enjoy a refreshing treat after a big meal. No big surprise that Jeremiah's ended up building their Carrollwood location right next door to the wildly-popular 4Rivers Smokehouse so that the patrons with their well-stuffed bellies full of brisket could enjoy a little dish of icy goodness before waddling off to their cars.

Jeremiah's is an Orlando-based chain with about 15 locations in central Florida along the I-4 Corridor. Their concept is very simple. You walk up to the window and look over the list of choices of made-fresh-daily Italian ice flavors, and then decide if you want to have just the Italian ice, just soft-serve ice cream, or the wickedly-decadent combination of layers of Italian ice and soft-serve ice cream (called a Gelati).

The Italian ice is made from fresh fruit, fruit puree, filtered water, and sugar which has been churned in an ice cream machine. The board by the ordering window details the various flavor options (25 or so each day), and the staff will gladly let you sample a few of the flavors till you find the one that pleases your palette. Next comes the tough decision of whether you want just the Italian ice, or just the soft-serve, or whether you'll throw caution to the wind and go for the gealti layered-flavor extravaganza. 

The servers will encourage you to go wild and select more than one flavor of Italian ice to be layered between the soft-serve ice cream, and as a result you'll end up with some pretty crazy concoctions. A word of warning to concerned parents.... if you let your child eat a lot of the black raspberry or blueberry Italian ice, they will end up with a multi-colored mouth. Do not despair, just make them eat some soft-serve ice cream and all will be well.

I've been to Jeremiah's several times, and always enjoy ordering at the outdoor window and visiting with the staff as they help me select a unique flavor profile for the evening. They're kind of like Italian ice sommeliers, so use their expertise when building your gelati. Once you have your cup of frozen fruit puree and sugar, you'll walk around the corner to their covered eating area which is filled with picnic tables and happy little children. Who knew that the little munchkins would be so busy eating ice cream that they'd forget to scream and run around?

I'm not normally a fan of desserts, but I'll make an exception for Jeremiah's Italian Ice.  YUM!!!

This is a perfect example of "looks can be very deceiving." This store had a remodel within the last year and it's fucking fantastic. Wide gleaming aisles, outdoor dining, they are really trying to go the Whole Foods/Fresh Market route. The place is a "natural" food & toiletry palace.

But they fail. Miserably.

My Greek salad from the deli, when I got to work and opened the box, contained brown lettuce. This means that the lettuce in this salad came from a bag that was likely VERY old.

Next up: The Classic Chicken Salad I got, also from the deli, contained a piece of bone connected to RAW chicken/cartilage. 

Let me tell you that in my 20+ years of shopping at Whole Foods, Fresh Market and even Publix, this has never happened to me. Not even Trader Joe's prepared foods have been this bad. This has certainly never happened to me with Mazarros salads either. I am just mentioning the normal places I go to get lunch salads for work.

Prices here are in line with Whole Foods, etc. Trader Joe's/Publix are cheaper. Service was good. 

But the minute you put brown lettuce in a 7-dollar salad and raw chicken in a 5 dollar salad, you lost me. Forever.

Bye bye.

+++++++++++++++Before you drive to the store READ THIS+++++++++++++++++

YES IT WILL BE MOBBED.
YES THEY MAY BE OUT OF ITEMS YOU WANT (CALL AHEAD TO CHECK):
YES THERE MAY BE A LACK OF PARKING.
NO YOU SHOULDN'T CARE, AND HERE IS WHY:

Trader Joe's likes to invest in its products and in its employees, not in parking lots. Lack of parking at Trader Joe's is COMMON all across America. Don't believe me? Just Google "Trader Joe's parking problems" and pick a city. They bitch about it Denver. They bitch about it in Burbank, Calif. They bitch about it in Miami. You can bitch about it in Tampa, but instead of bitching, why don't you be smart and shop there at OFF-PEAK HOURS?

This is just how it is; there is never enough parking for the mobs and mobs of people who love to shop at a grocery store that is essentially the size of a CVS with a CVS-size parking lot. If you REALLY hate parking hassles and crowds, then I guess skip it. But you'd be doing yourself a huge disservice. Because the stuff they sell is unique, cheap and besides, you are not the only person in Tampa, in Florida, or in the United States frantically looking for a parking space at a Trader Joe's store. You are one of hundreds of thousands. Get over it, move on and go get your Two Buck Chuck!

Now, the review:

Congrats to Tampa Bay for finally, after many years of cruel and inhumane deprivation, landing a Trader Joe's store. Finally we get to savor a little taste of California in Florida; people in California have been eating multi-ethnic, gourmet, healthy food like this for decades (OK, some of the stuff they sell, like salted caramel sauce, is NOT healthy, but I digress)! This store, No 766 in South Tampa, seems a little smaller than the other TJ's I've been to. But it may just have been all the boxes everywhere and employees (pre-opening day) and crowds making it feel cramped. Anyway:

Fantabulous, orgasmic, euphoric, to-die-for and astonishing. That's how I describe almost any Trader Joe's, and the Tampa location is no exception. How do I love Trader Joe's? Let us count the ways:

fresh Cubano wrap w/ cumin mustard sauce, frozen chicken tikka samosas, TO-DIE-FOR salted caramel dessert sauce, fresh individually packaged organic chicken breasts for a few bucks a pound, frozen chocolate croissants (when u bake these things u will feel like u are in Paris), frozen scones ready to bake, Chinese chicken salad cold and ready to eat, frozen sliced leeks, Spanish Serrano ham, the best chocolate chip cookie ice cream sandwich you will ever put in your mouth, peanut satay sauce, cilantro salad dressing, huge bottle of Italian EVOO for 7 bucks, fresh herbs cheaper than Publix or Fresh Market, chocolate covered potato chips, squash gnocchi, a bottle of wine for 3 bucks (Two Buck Chuck is an excellent cooking wine), fresh (not dried) rice noodles, 52,000 flavors of hummus, frozen seafood of every kind, vegan pad thai, cream scones fresh-baked, whole wheat water crackers, organic mango lemonade, high fiber trail mix granola bars, fresh pineapple juice, frozen pizza made in Italy that will make you never want to buy a frozen pizza at Publix ever again, frozen pie crust of superb quality, curried turkey burgers, double fire roasted salsa, organic + fresh butternut squash ravioli, caramelized onion and ham pizza, spinach and kale greek yogurt dip, freshly churned coconut juice, asparagus risotto and every kind of deliciously inventive salty snack, cookie or chocolate confection you can think of.

######Do you like Thai curry? If so, RUN to the refrigerated entree case and look for something called Chicken Medallions in Coconut Red Curry. That right there is basically the BEST red chicken curry you will ever eat from a grocery store and likely many restaurants. ****In fact, it is better than ANY red curry I have ever had in a Thai restaurant in Tampa Bay. Same goes for Mexican and other cuisines. You will find yourself going to a lot fewer restaurants. Craving Mexican? Much better to go to TJs and get their frozen chile relleno entree for a couple bucks than go spend 30 bucks in a mediocre Mexican restaurant.

Oh yeah, and their seasonal produce and foodstuffs are outrageous: pumpkin goodies in autumn, chocolatey goodies at Xmas, oh my!

Please tell me where else you can buy this kind of delectable stuff for a delectable price? Oh yeah, that's right: 

NOWHERE EXCEPT HERE.

Don't marinate on the idea of going to TJ's after it opens: JUST GO. 

The hype is true. Trader Joe's is freaking awesome. And it's not expensive (unless you are buying saffron or some crazy item like that). And the customer service rocks (hate their peanut butter pretzels? return them anytime, even if you ate half the bag, no questions asked). Also their employees are genuinely happy to work there and help you. And they even play The Smiths over the store speakers. 

I honestly don't know why anyone would NOT shop here.

DO NOT EAT HERE.

The calamari had a fishy taste = old.

The grouper sandwich was more like a fish cake, with pieces of grouper stuck together with some sort of oily glue = gross.

The restaurant smelled of old wood, mildew, feet, seafood and is extremely dirty. The air conditioning is weak and clammy.

The employees also looked dirty. This is one of those old Florida seafood restaurants that is in need of a renovation, a new menu, a refresher course on food prep, etc.

DO NOT EAT HERE.

ALERT: Lots of fake 4/5 star reviews posted. Take their advice with caution.

The first thing you need to know about Besito is that this is a restaurant that was founded in New York state in 2006 by non-Hispanics.

The second thing you need to know about Besito is that I went to this place over the weekend, spent nearly $200, ordered nearly 10 items off the menu (just to cover all the bases), and only one item was great.

The third thing you need to know about Besito is that it is not Mexican, Tex-Mex, Cal-Mex, or any other type of Mexican you are used to. Besito is a New Yorker's version of "upscale Mexican." And it's not very good.

I would encourage anyone who is really looking forward to eating here to study the menu and read the Yelp reviews from the Besito restaurants in NY and CT and MASS before eating here. That way you are well-educated ahead of time and prepared for what's to come.

Before I say anything about Besito in Tampa I am not going to review the service or the prices b/c the service with time I'm sure will improve. The prices, well, if you don't like the prices, that's your own damn fault for eating here to begin with. Study the menu, study the prices, avoid if you think paying 20 bucks for enchiladas is outrageous, etc. Remember these are New Yorkers who think dropping $100 on a meal is nothing.

But I digress.

Here's my take: I would not return. Yes, the restaurant is beautifully designed and decorated. So fucking what.  The salsa is terrible. The corn tortillas are too small and mediocre. The flour tortillas are better but served folded and stuck together. The tableside guacamole is spectacular (b/c of the freshness not necessarily the flavor) and really the only thing worth returning for, but that's not enough for me. I can't speak about the cocktails b/c I don't drink. The entrées ranged from poor to mediocre. Enchiladas had a nasty dark orange sauce unlike anything I've ever seen on an enchilada (this will happen a lot, Mexican staples are done very differently here), skillet taco meats were served soaked in burned cheese WTF???? Here, when they serve you fajitas, you don't get pico, sour cream and guac. You get small portions of bizarre salsas and some shredded lettuce. The beans and rice were different but at least decent (the rice comes with delicious pumpkin seeds). The desserts (flan, choc pudding, tres leches, etc.) were atrocious. 

I am not exactly sure what kind of Mexican cuisine Besito is going for; I certainly do not get it. Maybe you will get it? Maybe they get it in NY state and Connecticut. This is not the kind of food I have had in Cali, Texas or Mexico for that matter. I would have NO PROBLEM loving this kind of Mexican food (NY Mex???) if it were actually good. But it's not. Perhaps they will improve the cooking in Tampa and make great food out of this bizarre menu? One can only hope. But for that to happen they would have to change the recipes for nearly everything I ordered, and I ordered A LOT of food. I would be extremely curious to read the thoughts of a Mexican reviewer on this restaurant. Or someone who is from Arizona or Texas or Mexico and is an expert on Mexican food.

Thus, I am devastated that after waiting months and years for a good Mexican chain restaurant in Tampa, we got this place instead of a Chuy's, Uncle Julio's, Pappasito's etc. Those places would have been much more successful, IMHO.

A travesty for Tampa.

This place is going to have a very hard time being successful in St. Pete. 
 
Reason No. 1 they will have a hard time being successful is because the people who think paying 43 dollars for a steak or 20 dollars for a pound of "deli meats," as some Yelpers have already complained about, will not shop here. When I was here last week I saw a lot of people looking around, gawking, but not a lot of people buying. That's a big problem. This place takes a lot of capital to run and I'm just not sure that there are enough people in Pinellas County who have no problem paying 6 dollars for a bell pepper. 

Reason No. 2 they will have a hard time being successful is because people like me, people who have NO PROBLEM paying 30 dollars for a pound of prosciutto or 50 dollars for a pound of artisanal butter, people like that, think this place is lame. There is NOTHING at Locale that would entice me to go back. It's not a "foodie's dream," as some Yelpers have said. It's a very poor, poor knockoff of a Dean and Deluca, or some other fancy market/food court. I am not even going to mention Eataly because Locale doesn't even deserve being mentioned in the same sentence as Eataly. But I did it anyway. Locale is poorly stocked, poorly designed, poorly run. It's all show and no substance, with a big A/C problem. 

At the bakery, which is hidden upstairs (mistake), selections were few and the stuff I bought (croissants, baguette) was just OK, not so good that I would make a special trip to Locale to go get again. The prepared foods looked good (portions were small, tho), I did not try them, but that's not my thing. The dry aged meats looked good, but again, not my thing. The seafood selection was a JOKE in terms of variety. The grocery sections, with the produce and the pantry items, were again nothing that you can't find at Rollin Oats or Whole Foods or even Trader Joe's. That was really disappointing. I was expecting to find unique produce or high-end, artisanal cookies, spreads, condiments. Instead they stock what you can already get at Mazzaro's or Fresh Market. The deli selection was ridiculous; you can find more selection of meats at your local Publix! 

I cannot imagine that anyone would prefer this place over Mazzaro's, by the way. I think that when it comes to high-end markets/food courts in Tampa Bay, Mazzaro's is the place to beat, and Locale loses big-time.

Oh yeah and the staff here all have that "deer in the headlights" look, cashiers are incompetent and slow. You have been warned.

Maybe they will make enough money off all the people who hit the wine bar and buy craft beer?

Prasino, he said ...

Best in St. Charles, he said ...

He just might be right ... 

So, I'm rounding up from 4 stars to 5 ... because he said so.

The best drink to warm up to Prasino is no longer on the menu. So, ask for it by name because the spicy jalapeno-infused "Little Heat from Mexico" cocktail is a hot way to start. If spicy alcohol isn't your thing, then you can't go wrong with a classic Negroni or a Vodka Smash (ask for light ice); however, my other recommendation is a smoky "Fire at Rickhouse" Cocktail with Buffalo Trace Bourbon served at the table in a smoked glass.

For appetizers, I have three recommendations and, in this order:

 * Shrimp Tacos
Thinking about tacos or shrimp in Missouri makes my head hurt, so, don't and get a trio of these crazy-addictive soft shrimp tacos that are meant to be shared, but won't be because they're that good.

 * Wood Fire Grilled Wings
These wings taste healthier because Prasino isn't joking about using a wood-fired grill with extra charcoal tips for flavor.

 * Cheese Farm Flatbread
The cheese blend isn't special, but a dash of chives and truffle honey ... yep, it's really all about the truffle honey, honey ... make this a cool twist on your kid's favorite.

And onto the main entrees of which I've only tried a couple. My family likes the Prasino Burger or Turkey Burger or just more of the Shrimp Tacos. For me, these were worth trying:

 * St. Louis Pork Steak
How could I pass up ordering this local legend that features a THICK cut of pork topped with Fitz Root Beer BBQ Sauce plus a Jalapeño Corn Biscuit and Crisp Apple Slaw? I couldn't.

 * Short Ribs with Sweet Wine Risotto 
Even better was a meaty serving of tender rib meat floating on Swiss Chard, Cauliflower Gratin, and Truffle-Mushroom Cabernet Sauce.

The food was good and the drinks better; however, the service was the best. I don't know the name of our server, but he's cool and had spot-on recommendations. Prasino was packed, yet, he helped us feel special.

He said Prasino. He said best in St. Charles. He just might be right.

If you are used to great brisket, ribs, and pulled pork from a local hole-in-the-wall joint, then Jack's Bar-B-Que may disappoint you. It's large with 2 floors full of tables and paper towel dispensers, but the meat, sides, and corn bread weren't tender or terrific. Thank God for a relaxed atmosphere, an ok XXX sauce, and some bottles of beer.

Prior to a night of drinking, a small group of us hit Jack's Bar-B-Que for some BBQ. I tried the 3-Meat Combo Plate with Tennessee Braised Pork, Texas Beef Brisket, and St. Louis Style Pork Ribs with sides of Mac & Cheese and Corn with a piece of Corn Bread. There were 6 sauces and after trying 4 pretty much stuck to the XXX spicy one. It was only available downstairs in plastic bottles, so, search for it. The 3 meats were so-so with the brisket being the softest and most memorable. The dry corn bread was notably bad as half our table didn't even try to finish even a slice.

Service was patient while we ordered & later while cleaning upstairs waiting for us to leave. Jack's BBQ was barely a-ok.

Wise men say only fools rush in, but I couldn't help falling in love with El Vez.

My affair with El Vez began, as so many romances do, with alcohol and a cheesy opening. An appropriately christened Perfecto Margarita ($11) on the Rocks with El Jimador Blanco, Cointreau, Grand Marnier, and Lime Juice awoke my senses while a bawdy Melted Manchego Cheese Dip ($9) with Sweet Onions proved to be liquid lust. My heart was captured, my soul surrendered.

Seeking a little less fight and a little more spark, I ordered the rich "Indian Red" Lopez Guacamole ($18) with Spicy Crab and Salsa Roja because you've got to follow that dream, wherever that dream may lead. All hail the King of Guac.

At this point, I didn't need any more food, but El Vez makes you want to live each day, as if it were your last. It's written in the stars, my destiny was cast with Crispy Mahi-Mahi Tacos ($14) with Red Cabbage, Avocado, and Chipotle Pepper Remoulade.

Our server was tender and sweet. She made the experience complete and I love her so. Take my cash, take my whole life too, for I can't help falling in love with you.

Lord have mercy, I got a hunka hunka burnin' love for El Vez!

Truth? Oh, I CAN handle the truth ... when it is Frozen Rolled Ice Cream ... because that's honestly what this place makes and sells.

Ice Cream.
Rolled.
Frozen.

Hooray for truth in advertising. This dessert is unique because the cream is mixed right before your eyes, flash frozen into a flat sheet, and rolled into cute edible coils. Voila, Frozen Rolled Ice Cream. Add 3 toppings (included) to match your mood ... and you'll find yourself able to handle the truth.

The flavors are Asian-inspired, but choose whatever suits your mood. Olivia got a Green Tea & Strawberry Rolled Ice Cream with Nutella, Mochi, and Condensed Milk while I opted for Vanilla Rolled Ice Cream with Blueberries, Condensed Milk, and Mochi. The ice cream definitely isn't the "creamiest" around, but it is "rolled" ... so, it's fun ... and still ice cream with sweet toppings.

Sometimes we all hate to swallow the truth, but I'll eagerly gobble it down if the revelation is Frozen Rolled Ice Cream.

Bar Hopping is THE thing for tourists to do in downtown Nashville. So, 2 nights in a row, we did. Bailey's Pub & Grille was the worst bar. It was nearly dead at 1:30 a.m. with only a small band playing some lazy tunes for a few minutes. It's a big place that could seat a lot more than the handful of customers, so it felt very empty.

A small gang of new friends were starving after a few hours of drinking at other spots and Bailey's was one of the few places still serving food with pizza on the menu. A few of us were really, really craving pizza. We got a Cheese Pizza to split and an order of Hot Honey Wings (flavor recommended by the bartender) plus another round of brews. The beers were  fine, the wings were almost ok, but the pizza was like a frozen Tostinos that wasn't even really edible.

With soooo many options within 4-5 blocks, I can't recommend Bailey's as a pit stop along your path of drunken music appreciation.

One meal with fabulous food, stellar service, and a couple magical Moscow Mules elevated Arch Rock to rock star status. I totally whiffed on making it there for Happy Hour (as planned), but it turns out the Arch Rock bar area is too tiny anyways. A kind host seated me in the dining area and asked what I wanted to drink. I said "Moscow Mule" and he replied, "Good choice." He was right.

Moscow Mules ($10) are one of Arch Rock's signature cocktails. The tart 'n tasty thrill ride comes with Beluga Russian Vodka (add a splash of gin if you prefer), fresh Lime, and Goslling's Ginger Beer served in a classic Copper Mug (when available). I ordered a 2nd before even finishing the first. Hey, I'm drinkin' ovah here!

A pair of starters, were both memorable. Arch Rock's Stilton Blue & Truffle Honey Grilled Cheese ($6) is not your mother's grilled cheese (sorry Mom). Wheat Bread with melted Stilton Blue Cheese, Truffle Oil, and Honey created one fragrant flavor explosion that almost overpowers the senses ... in a good way.

If you like meaty chowdah, then get the Arch Rock Clam Chowder ($5 cup) loaded with tons (technically, not a ton ... just A LOT) of Clam, smoked Bacon, chunky Potatoes, and creamy Cream. It's even better with the free Sourdough Bread served with Butter in Olive Oil.

As the Moscow Mules messed with my memory, a bowl of Arch Rock's award-winning Cioppino ($16) with Pasta (recommended by the server) arrived. I asked what award it won and she said "Best Cioppino" at the Santa Barbara Bouillabaisse Festival ... which has got to be one of the top bouillabaisse festivals between Goleta and Carpenteria. 

The red Italian seafood soup has Shellfish, Fin Fish, Tomatoes, Sopressata, Basil, and extra-virgin Olive Oil. The addition of thick Spaghetti really made this a fantastic pasta dish more than a fantastic soup. Either way, I recommend it as the Best Cioppino in Santa Barbara (that I've had ... ya, and the only one).

Since I lucked into street parking about a block away and enjoyed such superb service while fawning over the food and drinks, there weren't any negatives to my meal. I didn't expect a 5-star experience, but for casual and comfortable dining in downtown SB, that's what Arch Rock was.

Sure, the "Rocky Steps" and "Rocky Statue" are inspirational (and famous photo ops), but, honestly, take your pic and run up those 72 steps as quickly as possible because inside is where you'll find the real inspiration of the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

 * Admission prices cover 2 consecutive days
 * So, try to come back-to-back days to see it all
 * Admission also includes the nearby Rodin Museum
 * Adults: $20; Seniors: $18; Students: $14
 * Children (12 & under) are FREE
 * Pay What You Wish 1st Sundays and every Wednesday night
 * Closed Mondays
 * Open other days 10:00a - 5:00p
 * Open late until 8:45 every Wed. & Fri.
 * Parking is $12 for 4 hrs then $2/hr
 * Instead, take SEPTA or PHLASH
 * No food or drink in galleries
 * Onsite cafes have sandwiches, salads, & soups
 * Permanent collection photography is allowed (no flash)
 * Coat check is on the ground floor near the store
 * All-gender bathrooms are available
 
Some of my favorite pieces of inspiration at the Philadelphia Museum of Art include: 

 * Lute Player (c. 1620) by Theodor Rombouts (Flemish) 
 * Portrait of Harriett West (c. 1824-1825) by Sir Thomas Lawrence (English)
 * Christ and the Virgin (1430-1435) by Robert Campin (Netherlandish)
 * Portrait of a Lady (1577-1580) attributed to El Greco (Domenikos Theotokopoulos) (Spanish, born Crete) 
 * Little Dancer, Aged Fourteen (Cast 1922) by Edgar Degas (French)
 * Avenue de l'Opera: Morning Sunshine (1898) by Camille Pissaro (French)
 * Portrait of a Roman Lady (La Nanna) (1859) by Sir Frederic Leighton (English)
 * Under the Pines, Evening (1888) by Claude Monet (French)
 * Carnival Evening (1886) by Henri Rousseau (French)
 * The Japanese Footbridge and the Water Lily Pool, Giverny (1899) by Claude Monet (French)
 * The Large Bathers (1884-1887) by Pierre-Auguste Renoir (French) 
 * L'Ornière (The Rut) (1918) by Joan Miró (Spanish)
 * Sunflowers (1888 or 1889) by Vincent van Gogh (Dutch)
 * Diana (1892-1893) by Augustus Saint-Gaudens (American)
 * The Counterfeit Note (1858) by Daniel Huntington (American)
 * Portrait of Marianne Holbech (1781-1782) by George Romney (English)  
 * The Goat Girl (c. 1868) by Jean-Francois Millet (French)
 * Bicycle Race (1938) by Antonio Ruiz (Mexican)
 * Man in a Cafe (1912) by Juan Gris (Spanish)
 * Man with a Guitar (1912) by Pablo Picasso (Spanish) 
 * Departing for the Promenade (Will You Go Out with Me, Fido?) (1859) by Alfred-Emile-Leopold Stevens (Belgian)
 * Liverpool from Wapping (c. 1885) by John Atkinson Grimshaw (English)
 * Spanish Woman (1855) by Gustave Courbet (French)
 * Portrait of Mademoiselle Legrand (1875) by Pierre-Auguste Renoir (French)
 * At the Moulin Rouge: The Dance (1890) by Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec (French)

The Philadelphia Museum of Art's inspirational collection of paintings, sculptures, and history rivals any motivation the Rocky movies can provide.

After a couple visits during a conference at Gaylord Opryland Hotel, it's easy to say this is one of the better restaurant/bar options on-site. It's a sports bar with a full bar and a menu full of burgers, salads, wings, and appetizers. For lunch, it was a place to chill out for a conversation or watch sports on one of the many TVs. After dinner, it was a bar to crowd around and let the company pay for drinks.

I tried the Three Alarm Fire Burger for lunch. The 1/3 lb. beef burger comes with Pepper Jack Cheese, Jalapenos, and Green Chili Sauce, but it was made even better by upgrading to the Dante's Inferno version which comes with Dante's Inferno sauce. The waitress was helpful and brought extra on the side for dipping. 4 stars for the burger, but only 2 stars for the "Wrinkle" Fries which were simply old fries.

During a late night drinking binge I ordered sliders. The bartender asked if I wanted them Coney or Chicago. I said Coney which apparently means they are Hot Dog Sliders covered in Chili, Cheese, and Onions. Good thing I was drunk because those "sliders" sucked.

So, why four stars? Because I went twice and had a good time both visits. Compared to some of the other options at Gaylord then Fuse will do just fine if you aren't willing to leave the reservation and head downtown.

Unlike crack, Beiler's Donuts are legally addictive.

It might of been the sweet cream filling or the even sweeter frosting, but I had the sugar shakes after getting my first hit of an Elvis Delight Donut with Peanut Butter Creme, Banana, and Bacon. El diet has left the building.

Jonesing for more, how could I not obsess over a Maple Bacon Donut, Salty Caramel Donut, Boston Creme Donut, or a PB & Jelly Donut? And, don't ask about calories or carbs for these sugary stimulants. Also, don't ask about sharing the half dozen I got to get me through the night.

Pop quiz time ... 

I have 6 Beiler's donuts. Someone asks me for one. How many Beiler's donuts do I have? That's right. 6.

"Philadelphia is a wonderful place; I spent a week there one night." - W.C. Fields

That night might of been right here at McGillin's Olde Ale House which literally puts the "old" in Olde! This Pennsylvania pub legend opened its doors in 1860 ... making McGillin's the oldest continuously operating tavern in Philadelphia. It's busy with tourists and locals mingling for cheap food, cold beer, and loud energy. 

Don't know what to drink? Get the Beer Sampler? Don't know what food to eat? Get some $0.35 Chicken Wings and a Cheesesteak while you decide. Then spend the rest of your wonderful night/week growing olde one beer and daily special at a time.

As "King of the King Cakes," this New Orleans legend has been baking, selling, and shipping classic Mardi Gras King Cakes during the Carnival season ... and all 365 days a year for 60 years. Getting a Gambino's King Cake delivered to your home or office means you can celebrate Mardi Gras any time you want. 

An office at work got a colorful Gambino's King Cake to share and the game was quickly on to see who would discover the hidden baby Jesus inside. At Joe's Gambino Bakery, King Cakes are baked daily with Danish Dough full of Cinnamon Swirls and topped with Purple, Green, and Gold Sugar-coated Fondant Icing. The cake's as colorful as it is yummy and fun.

Of course, New Orleans has been celebrating Mardis Gras for hundreds of years and the French Cinnamon Bread tradition of King's Cakes is now available year round no matter where you live. Just remember that whoever finds little baby Jesus inside buys the next one from Joe Gambino's Bakery.

Everyone's breakfast could use a touch of magic like Sabrina's. Charming staff and an enchanted menu of Philly sorcery left me spellbound ... and about 5 lbs heavier.

Stuffed Challah French Toast ($11.29)
It's supernaturally overstuffed with Bananas, Cream Cheese, and Honey then topped with more Bananas and a Vanilla Bean Syrup. The stuffing was too overpowering for me so I'll probably just get regular Challah French Toast for $8.69 next time.

Mel's Chicken Cutlet Sandwich ($11.79)
It's advertised as a Philly favorite and bewitched fanatics with cornmeal-encrusted Chicken cloaked by Spinach, Marinated Long Hots (peppers), and Provolone Cheese on a Sarcones Roll. I might order it again.

Scrapple ($2.99)
Philadelphia has many different kinds of scrapple (aka Pannhaas). I wasn't a fan of this fried loaf of meal & meat scraps. It was filling and more weird than wizardly. 

It was a LOT of calories, but Sabrina's cast a spell on me (and my diet) for one magical Philadelphia breakfast.

Shabu shabu is usually so nice, it's named twice; however, Hippot serves Chinese-style hot pot using the Japanese name to fairly timid results. It's okay ... and, like a flat state in the bible belt, that's OK.

We went with the split pot (about $20) of Hot & Spicy in half and Herbal Pork Soup in the other half. Neither broth met expectations. The spicy wasn't spicy and the herbal wasn't herby. Both were like Giuliana Rancic: thin and comical.

Of course, high quality meats, veggies, noodles, and balls can rescue any hot pot from mediocrity. Or not. We selected an assortment of beef, lamb, fish balls, tripe, tofu, tong ho, mushrooms, and more. Most were priced in the $3-$4 range with the meat being about $7. My favorites were the winter melon, frozen tofu, and whatever was next because the meat was like Ben Affleck: sometimes tolerable.

Since sauces are self-serve creations of your own blend at Hippot Shabu Shabu, I had no one to blame, but myself if the dipping sauces were weak or lacked spice, but I'm gonna blame Anne Hathaway.

Our server had to be flagged down to get another beer, more broth, and more food, but once we asked, she was on it. Service was fine ... just fine ... like Chadwick Boseman.

Hippot Shabu Shabu is no celebrity when it comes to Chinese-style huoguo (hot pot). It's ok. Since the prices aren't bad, consider it an okay choice in Philadelphia.

Wildhorse Saloon is for tourists. It's big. It's comfortable. It takes all the fun and liveliness of downtown Nashville and puts it into a safe and clean environment. I was one of many tourists who took the shuttle ride to this Nashville icon. It wasn't the worst experience of all-time, but we've all probably experienced better.

The dance floor is large and the line dancing pretty much non-stop. If you've never line danced then don't worry because most people there are just like you. Get out there and have fun because honestly no one is watching. 

The drinks (Gin & Tonic) were fine and the noise level is lower than some other nearby bars so you can probably have a conversation. As with most things geared towards tourists, the prices are high and food average.

Wildhorse served as a lure to go downtown, but was more of a starting spot for a night of convention-goers bar hopping their way to a night of beers and bands.

Bank & Bourbon is an above-average hotel bar in the downtown Philadelphia Loews Hotel in the historic Philadelphia Savings Fund Society (PSFS) building. The building and setting may be iconic, but it was some late-night drinks and American fare which make me a fan.

The Taste of Ham board was a triple taste of yum featuring Hamery, Benton's Ham, and Creminelli Prosciutto. The meats may change with the season, but this trio was hamtastic. Other yummy bar menu discoveries were a Grilled Octopus with Fingerling Potatoes and Cherry Pepper Relish plus a sizzling plate of Chive-roasted Local Mushrooms.

An even more bankable discovery was a Fist Full of Dollars cocktail laced with Maker's Mark. If you like bourbon, this is the bar for you in Philadelphia. If you like sweet bourbon cocktails, then this is the cocktail to order.

Even if you aren't staying at the Loews Hotel, Bank & Bourbon gives plenty of reasons to visit and see the historic 1920's building with some above-average food and drinks.

Robert's Western World is famous for a reason: it IS Nashville. Everything that Nashville is famous for can be found here.

 - Great live country music? Check.
 - Cheap well drinks and beer? Check
 - A crowd actually having a good time? Check
 - Food that will stick with ya? Check (like a Fried Bologna Sandwich)
 - Tourist gear like a PBR Hat to take home? Check
 - Cowboy boots? Check

Even if a can of Pabst Blue Ribbon isn't your drink of choice, Roberts Western World should be a part of any night out on the town in downtown Nashville. It's got everything you want in bar in Tennessee: great music, sketchy food, cheap drinks, and a honky tonk vibe.

I love A La Mousse so Matcha!

For green tea lovers, A La Mousse is a cute cafe with a bounty of decadent Matcha drinks and desserts. I'm sorry that I love Matcha more than the average 14-year old anime fan ... then again, I'm not sorry at all ... because there's never been a case of too much Matcha.

 * Matcha Latte
I don't always drink tea, but when I do, I prefer Matcha Lattes.

 * Matcha Mille Crepes Cake
Game. Set. Matcha!

 * Green Tea-r-amisu and Homemade Ice Cream
I see what you did there ... it's a Matcha made in Heaven (aka Philly).

My Matcha love for A La Mousse had me singing and spinning like Julie Andrews in a mountain field. Ya, Matcha brings all the boys to the yard ... and will bring me back to A La Mousse.

Reading Terminal Market is like a massive Pennsylvania food court with something local for any Yelper to try ... and 2-3 things for me. 

Coming here has been a Philadelphia tradition since 1893 and it still ranks as an obligatory tourist attraction for city visitors. We came a couple times (over a week) to try different foods and shop a little in the other stalls. 

Recommendations include:
 * Beiler's Doughnuts (underrated donuts)
 * Miller's Twist (Warm Amish pretzels!)
 * Sang Kee Peking Duck (Beijing-style duck)
 * DiNic's Sandwiches (ok, yet overrated)
 * Spataro's Cheesesteaks (average, but historic)
 * Downtown Cheese (say Cheese!!)
 * Valley Shepherd Creamery (Grilled cheese please)
 * Bee Natural (Local honey)
 * Fox & Son ("If" you like corndogs)
 * Dutch Eating Place (Apple dumplings)
 * Flying Monkey Bakery (Red velvet whoopie pies)

Note that the Reading Terminal Market is open 7 days a week from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm (except major holidays), so, plan accordingly with your meal schedule.

I adore this generically-named little place. My husband and I made a trek to Indy to get sushi since there's no decent places within 50 miles of our little town. We went to our regular spot, Asaka in Castleton, only to be shunned by the staff (see my scathing review). We drove to Broad Ripple to find something... anything. The neon sign spelling out "Sushi Bar" grabbed our attention and we both said "Good enough."

The warm welcome and immediate seating we got upon arriving was enough to give this place 5 stars after the Asaka ridiculousness, but the sushi was fantastic and very reasonably priced, and OMG, the huge glass of Moscato they brought me made the entire night worth it. 

We will most definitely be back.

I'm not into race cars, or get excited about cars period.  But being here, knowing mister, my son and pretty much all the men in my family would be super stoked if they were here, I had to get excited for them.

There weren't any racing happening, but I did see a bunch of beautiful race cars circling the tracks, which I was able to record.

There is a souvenir shop which I spent a bunch of money at purchasing shirts, hats, and collectable cars for those back home.

We didn't have any trouble with parking.

There was a concession stand which is probably opened only when there are races going on.

If i could give this place less than one star I would. Went last week for a birthday dinner and had possibly one of the worst experiences Ive ever had. The owner is insanely rude and conceited. Ive never met and owner that was more disrespectful than he was. 

Called Tuesday morning to make a reservation for that night since they were closed the day before, they told me they dont take reservations under 24 hrs notice. However, the waitress i spoke to said she would "absolutely still accommodate" the party on the patio as requested. she takes my name and info and puts us down.

When we get to the restaurant the owner says "unless we took your credit card number, you dont have a reservation, i dont care what she told you." I politely tried explaining to him what the situation was and he says "IT says our reservation policy on our website. the problem with young people is that they dont take the time to read instructions on the internet." SIR! If i call your establishment and speak to the people YOU employ, they should know YOUR policies and not give their word to accommodate us!

he wouldn't let me speak to the waitress i spoke to in the morning, EVEN THOUGH SHE HAD OUR RESERVATION READY! She had it under the wrong name but had my correct phone number and party information and the patio was ready for us. HE refused to acknowledge that the waitress was trying to rectify the problem and work with me. He started raising his voice at us and said "I cant help you anymore, you need to leave." Opened the door and kicked us our.

TL:DR the owner is a pompous, rude jerk and I will never support his business again.

The Service: When we first arrived, no one was at the front to greet us. It took five minutes for someone to appeared randomly out of a back room and ask if we had reservations. We did, so we were then seated and met our friends. Luckily, they were seated quickly due to our reservation. 

A nice gentlemen came over to fill our water glasses, then, we had to wait  five more minutes for our waiter to come over.  He was very loud and went on about how the menu changes every day and about what was being served that night (even though the menu was exactly the same as when my husband looked it up weeks ago). It just seemed like a pretentious speech that went on forever.  We emailed ahead, as we do with many restaurants to see if the chef is up for the challenge of making us a vegan dish. Many chefs we've asked to do this actually are really excited and up for the challenge. Late Harvest's chef said that when we come in to ask the server what can be made vegan, and that he would make us up something special. We told the server this, and he pretty much ignored our request saying since there is one vegetarian dish on the menu, the chef would not make something special. 

When we asked what could be made vegan, the waiter didn't seem to know much about the menu in terms of animal ingredients. We went back and forth for a few minutes trying to figure out what we could and could not eat. First he'd say something could be made vegan, and the a minute later, he would correct himself. He had to ask the chef several times and literally a few minutes before our food arrived, he said, "Oh, sorry, The Potatoes Minneapolis are made with a clarified butter. We can just fry up some potatoes in canola oil." We were starving at this point and agreed. 

The Worst Part of the Night's Service: The main thing that stuck out to my husband and I was when our waiter refilled my husband's water glass. He reached over the table with his arm literally a centimeter away from my face. I had to back up, and he never said "Excuse me" or apologized.  For a restaurant that has "daily" specials and where the waitstaff take the effort to remove your salad forks, we were flabbergasted when this happened.

The waiter came by and asked us if we wanted dessert and my husband said, "I'm sure there's probably nothing for us to eat." The waiter laughed and said, "Yeah, we should have a sorbet as it's summer, but we don't. We replaced it with a sundae, sorry limited menu space." Then, he gives us one check. He never even asked us if we all wanted to split it, so we have to wait more to get his attention. He rudely and loudly look our cards and said, "Which one goes on what card." We explained it to him, and we finally got separate checks. 

The Food: We ordered three things: Potatoes Minneapolis (which were switched last minute for French Fries), a side of vegetables, and the North African Vegetable.  Overall, it had little flavor.  With how much the waiter seemed to brag about how fancy the food was, it seemed like the food should've at least had some seasoning in it besides salt.

Let's break it down by dish:

-French Fries: Now, we don't expect french fries to be spectacular. They're simply fried potatoes, but at least don't over cook them. It seemed like the grease that they were fried in was burnt. Sadly, they just threw a couple slices of raw jalapenos on top with a ton of salt. No other seasoning.  At least it was a large portion? Sigh. 

-North African Vegetable Tagine Couscous with golden raisins, feta cheese, apricot chutney, charmoulas: We got this without feta and and butter. We were so excited to try this. Ugh, what a disappointment. While the portion size was large, they barely gave us any couscous or apricot chutney. The vegetables were fresh and cooked well, and we while enjoyed the sweetness from the apricot sauce, the dish was so flavorless. This type of dish calls for mix of African spices, and it didn't have any of that. What a let down... Not worth $18 dollars at all. 

-Roasted Vegetables: These are the same vegetables that come in the North African Vegetable Tagine, seasoned the same, so if you bought that, don't waste your money here. The vegetables include, carrots, mushrooms, cauliflower, broccoli,  and green beans. We didn't expect the vegetables to have a strong flavor, but these were just so greasy and bland. The carrots and the cauliflower were the best part of it. 

Overall, if it wasn't for our nice friends, it would've been a terrible night. The rude waiter was loud and made a huge deal that we were vegan. He lacked the manners and skills to be a good waiter. We never felt welcome. The service was slow, and the food was bland and overpriced. One dish and two sides with tip for $45 is not what we want to spend our hard earned money one, especially considering we both felt sick afterwards from everything swimming in oil. 

Needless to say, we won't ever be returning.

Not the greatest casino in the area that's for sure.. Just not impressed maybe because I come from Miami and Fort Lauderdale where the casinos are on a whole other level. The cocktail servers majority are not friendly and act like they are bothered serving you and this place will leave you selling smokey ,I couldn't  wait to leave here ...the drinks I've had were less than average to much on the sweet side..and the staff can be lacking in customer service. Nothing at all against older people but this place is filled with the elderly. I would say it's not a young fun hip place to want to be in.

I've been a fan of this restaurant in the past, and I have a personal commitment to support restaurants that pursue Mexican cuisine. But a return visit to Plaza Azteca Exton this past weekend was an utter disaster.

The food was good enough, and our party of 7 much enjoyed a good meal in celebration of the pending return of a family member to his native South America. But near the conclusion of our visit, matters went badly awry. We discovered that the floor between the dining area and restrooms was quite slick with some oily substance. I managed to avoid a fall, but my long suffering wife was not so fortunate. She took a rather bad spill.

But it got worse. During a visit to the restroom I watched in shock as one of the liveried staff flushed the toilet, exited the stall and left the bathroom -- without stopping to wash his hands. Such things shatter confidence. I really doubt we'll return. But they're such simple problems to avoid.

I posted this message privately to the restaurant's Facebook page, but received no reply. And so I must post it to this more public forum.

Your restaurant has promise. Please don't continue to betray it with poor attention to safety and hygiene. Train your staff properly and be vigilant. Be respectful of your clientele and you may yet prosper.

A Lambertville Miss

My wife and I really try to support local businesses, and eat out very often, so we were excited when we read about D'Floret. From the description, they seemed to be doing things right - create a small menu using fresh, local ingredients, prepared by an experienced chef. Sadly, D'Floret does not live up to the promise.

The place has potential. Unfortunately, with the other fine options in the regions, potential isn't good enough. You have to be exceptional in some way in order to survive.

Why didn't we like it? Let's start with the ridiculous curved silverware. There's a reason knives and forks aren't curved - when you use them, they spin in your hand. And when you set them on the table, they roll around like a Weeble. But I could deal with weird forks and knives if the food was excellent.

We tried the pea soup, anchovy appetizer, salad, salmon, fettuccine and the profiteroles. Most of the food was ok, maybe a 6 or 7, but not worth having again.

The pea soup was flavorful, but it was pea with ginger, so the ginger overwhelmed the subtle sweetness of the peas. The anchovies were tasty enough but they came with tomatoes that were hard - definitely not farm fresh. The salmon was attractive but overcooked - a mortal sin in a fine restaurant as far as I'm concerned (we asked for it medium-rare and were assured that was how it was done normally). The pasta was "tasty" albeit boring and swimming in cream sauce.

I was hoping that the dessert might make up for a mediocre dinner. Unfortunately the profiteroles were almost inedible and tasted like refrigerator - absolutely unforgivable. How bad were they? The pastry was so tough that my wife had to use her knife to cut through it. When I used my fork to cut through the pastry, I literally had to push down with so much force that the fork hurt my hand. It was so stale that the fork tines could hardly penetrate the surface. Really, really bad.

One last thing - during dinner, there was a man sitting with his laptop and paperwork spread out  on a table next to us. All dinner, he was working away on his paperwork. Very odd, we though. He's acting like the owner, but no owner, especially a "celebrity chef" would do paperwork in the dining room, ignoring the kitchen. We just figured he was a very rude patron. When we arrived home, we looked up the restaurant and sure enough, that was the chef-owner. WTF? Really? We're paying to eat at an establishment that portrays itself and it's chef as world class but the chef can't bother himself to actually cook or taste the food?

It's really a shame. Like I said, we love to support our fine local restaurants, but we predict a short life for D'Floret. It's simply not worth it.

P.s. - So with all these complaints, why did I give it 3-stars? Because the food was generally decent or at least average. I finished my meal and I'm sure some people would enjoy their meals. I reserve 1 and 2-star reviews for places that are so bad that I wouldn't even eat the food.

Stopped by this place on our way to Mixto restaurant. Tried the cookies in the paper bag, brownie, and cupcakes. Let's start with the cookies. Where was the butter and golden brown color?These chocolate chip cookies were white. White. And tasted like nothing. I strongly believe it was a mistake batch meaning they forgot to add butter. The brownie was HUGE and once we ate it, it looked undercooked and did not taste good. The cupcakes were good. $4 each good? No way. My suggestion is to stick to just selling  cupcakes and come down on price AT LEAST .50 cent. $3.50 per cupcakes sounds better then $4. The size and taste is NOT worth $4, sorry.

We had heard about Willie Mae'e on Food Network and made it a priority to go while 
in NOLA.   So we headed out early and we were the first ones in line.  I'm a big fan of fried chicken and this is considered the Mecca of
fried chicken in New Orleans.  So I was  really looking forward to this.  Well I was sadly disappointed .  

We ordered fried chicken of course, a fried pork chop, butter beans and red beans and rice.  The butter beans were delicious (I'm personally not a fan of butter beans) and the red beans and rice were seasoned to perfection.  

I was very turned off by the fried chicken.  It tasted like it was chicken left over from the day before and it was refried just to heat it up.  My partner in crime also agreed.  Also the pork chop was nothing to write home about. 

We left there pretty disgusted and very disappointed. So we decided to get some fried chicken from Popeye's on Canal street, so we could compare.  We could really taste the difference.  Maybe we went on an off day, but we're not in a hurry to go back anytime soon.

Forget about all the other burger places you were thinking about going to - BurgerFuel is the best darn little burger place I've run across in quite a spell!

When we walked in we were greet by a really nice guy named Cory who was standing behind the counter.  Given that he knew their menu inside and out, he had no trouble at all helping us figure out exactly what to order.

When our burgers came, they were seasoned and cooked to perfection; juicy and amazingly flavorful. All the condiments were allocated exactly right - nothing drowned out the flavor of the meat, or fell short in any way :-)

It gets even better - not only was the food wonderful, but the restaurant was ship-shape, clean, and obviously well taken care of.  It was easy to see that all the employees care about their jobs and the experience of all their customers.

My compliments to the employees and their management for a job well done!

If you don't read any more of this review, here's a short summary:  literally the worst service I've ever experienced in a hotel.  Don't waste your money and stay elsewhere.

We came here from LA for a weekend, and this place should be embarrassed that they're charging $500+ per night and giving you the service of a $29/night Motel 6.

======================
PROS:
======================
- comfortable beds
- friendly staff (though they don't really care about doing a good job)
- nice pools
- the drive to the property from LA was nice
-  the hotel arranged a nice wine tour of Santa Barbara for us (party of 4, total cost: $700 not including tip)
-  The bar in the hotel lobby has good music and friendly staff.  That level of service unfortunately ends in the lobby and is the only reason this hotel gets more than one star.
- ???
(yep, that's the extent of this hotel's most redeeming qualities)

======================
CONS:
======================
NICKEL AND DIMING:
- This place really nickel and dimes you with a mandatory $25 per night resort fee and $30 per day valet fee ON TOP OF a minimum $500/night room.  If you want room service, they charge you a $6 delivery fee.  Seriously absurd.

THE BISTRO:
- We at at the Bistro for breakfast.  For four people it was $180.   Reasonable given the prices of everything else at the hotel.  Not reasonable given the incredibly horrible service.  For instance:
1) We were told at the Bistro that they were "extremely busy" and that it would be a "10 minute wait."  90% of the tables were completely empty.  
2) We were invited to enjoy some complimentary coffee while we waited.  They were out of cups, and I notified the hostess.  10 minutes late I grew impatient and went to an empty table to grab my own ceramic mug.
3)  After I got my cup of coffee, people were complaining that there was no coffee.  Yep, they replaced the cups but not the coffee.
4) We were missing a set of flatware.  We asked for an extra set, went to the buffet and came back, and no flatware.  So again, one of us got up from our table after waiting for 10 minutes and got our own flatware from a neighboring table.
5)  When we went back to the buffet for another plate, none of the staff cleared the dirty plates from our table.
6) Our salt and pepper shakers were both out.  I notified waitstaff, and they brought another two empty salt and pepper shakers.  It took me another 10 minutes until they fixed this issue.
7)  25 minutes to deliver three mimosas. (!!!)
8)  There's one lady making omelets for everyone at the bistro, so it takes forever to place an order.
9)  The buffet was out of bagels, and I notified staff. It took them 8 minutes to refill the bagel basket with freezing cold bagels.

THE POOL:
- We hit the pool and hung by the pool awning for about 10 minutes.  No staff showed up, so I just went behind the counter and got my own towels.
-  The pool is FILLED with kids.  This is definitely a kid-friendly resort.  If you don't like kids, this isn't a resort for you.
-  The pool staff doesn't pick up the towels from the chairs when people leave.  So, you have no idea which beach chairs are vacant and which are in use.  If you get to the pool past 3pm, you'll find there are more chairs with towels than people in the area.  The staff should really be sweeping the area for vacant chairs.

THE ROOM SERVICE:
- We hung out in a friend's room Saturday night and were planning on enjoying a  complimentary bottle of wine, except that housekeeping never made sure that there was a corkscrew opener.  So, two calls to the front desk and 45 minutes later, we were FINALLY able to open that bottle of wine.
-  We ordered room service which arrived pretty promptly, but we were surprised that they added a $6 "delivery fee" to an already outrageously priced burger and turkey club.

THE BEACH:
-  The beach is overrun with sand fleas and has a picturesque view of an oil rig.
-  The beach has "naturally occurring tar," so you'll likely end up with tar on your shoes and clothes.

THE ROOMS:
- Our room in villa #3 smelled like an old musty beach house.  This would be find if I were in MD or NJ paying $200 a night, but I'm in SoCal paying $500+ a night.
-  Housekeeping cleaned our room, but failed to top off the shampoo, conditioner, and body wash.

======================
BOTTOM LINE:
======================
-  If you want a nice beach hotel, go to Santa Monica and stay at the Casa Del Mar instead.
-  If you want to go on a vacation that's centered around wine tasting, either go to Napa or stay at a hotel in Los Olivos (44 tasting rooms, cute dusty town, easy drive into Santa Barbara).
- If you love to burn cash, enjoy being fleeced,  and long to rub elbows with the mega rich and their loud, pre-pubesent privileged children while you enjoy non-existent service you typically find at a sub-thirty-dollar roach motel, then this is the place for you!

I stumbled upon the Conshohocken Cafe a few weeks back when traveling between the bank and the CVS. I've been working in Conshy for over a year now and I have no idea how this place evaded me.

I was thoroughly pleased with the service and the quality of the food. We sat outside and perused the menu (which is much larger than the online one). The cashier/waiter was super friendly and didn't rush us at all. I got a cup of chili and a full chicken salad sandwich. First of all, the cup was more like a bowl (a GREAT value) and the chili was a little watery, but it was chock-full of meat and beans. You can get cheddar cheese on the side for no extra cost. The chicken salad was a solid choice (came with cheddar as well) and also arrived with a little side of mixed greens. I definitely should have gone for the half-sandwich + salad/soup combo like my friend, because there was way too much food to eat (not that I'm complaining).

My advice: If you want chicken salad that tastes just like the kind your momma used to make, go here.

My stomach is getting rumbly just sitting here thinking about the last time I went to Tria Taproom. The vibe in TT was "sophisticated hipster" and the place was packed and buzzing loudly with conversation when we arrived around seven. We managed to squeeze in at the bar, thanks to the advice of a friendly host. I went with a fellow beer nerd and we were in fits about the sheer amount of taps available. We eagerly poured over the iPad with the draft list (hah, see what I did there?) and made our first choices. 

I went with a draft of Saison di Pipaix, which was a farmhouse ale that was very heavy on the barnyard/funky aroma side. I felt that this and my second draft (a Left Hand Nitro Milk Stout) were both served far too cold for me to enjoy. I had to let both sit out for a few minutes before really being able to taste them. 

I don't know how much Tria can do about serving temperatures (as I expect all of the kegs are lined up next to each other behind the taps), but a warmer pour would have been much appreciated.

Finally, the food. In a word: delicious. I had an heirloom tomato and cucumber salad that was fantastic in its simplicity. Also ordered their beer burger, which I excitedly gobbled down as well (beer pickles, beer-naise sauce, and Chimay cheese? Holy moley). You could tell the patty was hand-packed only a few moments before and it was perfectly cooked to order. The crispy fried onions on the side were a perfect addition. I thought I was over gourmet/artisanal burgers, but boy was I wrong.

Oh how disappointed I was in you today. I did like my cupcake, I just didn't want to eat it and I will tell you why. I came in after getting a fab haircut from upstairs and there was a lady with a boxer in the restaurant. 
(Even an in and out dogs inside a restaurant where you have food is kinda gross and I LOVE pets!) The dog jumped its front paws on your counter. The server even petted the dog and proceeded to wait on me, touch my cupcake, and box it to go. Maybe I am just being super picky but I don't think I will come here again. 
I have a theory about restaurants. If you don't know where the server's hands have been, how do you know where your food has been?

K-Paul's is magic. Pure, unadulterated, ridonkulous magic.

We went here to celebrate my son-in-laws B/D. Since it was his first ever visit to NOLA, from a culinary standpoint, we had to do it right. Had a 9:00pm dinner reservation and were seated immediately upon arrival. This was the first visit here for all of us and we were not the least bit disappointed. Our server, (whose name I unfortunately cannot remember due to the massive amounts of libations we had ingested prior to our arrival), was professional, helpful and extremely accommodating. He walked us through any menu item questions we had and made a suggestion or two to make it even more difficult to decide on what we wanted from K-Paul's expansive menu of delectable delights. Between the seven of us, we must have tried nearly every cocktail option available!!! I had a pair of jalapeño margaritas and the wife had the Decatur Mule. My margarita was one of the best I've ever had. Perfectly mixed with a hint of spice that I couldn't stop with at just one.

We started with a couple orders of the onion rings and frog legs, mostly so the youngsters could, pardon the pun, hop on the frog leg bandwagon. (The wife and I have had them before so we let the youngin's try). Onion rings came with a dipping sauce that was simply out of this world!!! Three types of bread are brought out early on and you must try them all, though our fave seemed to be the jalapeño bread. We were warned not to eat it all because we wouldn't finish our entrees. Sound, sound advice because we could have ate that $hit all day, every day and twice on Sunday!!! Incredible to say the least...

On the entree side, we pretty much ran the table!!! (Not really, but you get my drift). And we all shared just to savor the entire experience. I had the Cheese Stuffed Pork Chop, the wifey wanted to go light so she had the Shrimp Enchilada app, then there was the Blackened Louisiana Drum, the Blackened Rib Eye, the Duck / Shrimp / Andouille, some Blackened Beef Tenders, a few cups of the Turtle Soup and the Daily Special, with each item just as good as the next.

Serving sizes are very generous, so when it came time for dessert, we all had to pass. That even included the birthday boy, (whose dessert choice would have been complimentary), had to pass. It's not inexpensive, but for the quality, portion size, ambiance and service, double the price would still have been a huge bargain. A must visit next time I'm here.

This place is FUC'n awesome!!! Conveniently located across the street from our hotel, I went late one morning to check it out and it was freakin' packed!!! Too packed to go in for sure, especially for a to go order, so I bided my time for another opportunity, which just so happened to manifest itself the next morning. The place is hustlin' and bustlin', every single day.

Tried to book a time via the NoWait app, but they apparently won't reserve for groups that size so patrons beware. We had a fairly large group (7), so I figured the wait would be extensive but surprisingly, it was only about 10 min.

Epic selection of delectable breakfast goodies and one of the most bad ass Bacon Bloody Mary's you'll find anywhere!!!

We pretty much ran the gamut on the breakfast food order, from an Eggs Benedict combo, (I had the Shrimp and Eggs Chocon and the pork is unreal), to the Bananas Foster French Toast to the Blueberry Creme Cheese Stuffed French Toast to a couple BYO omelette variations. Every item was better than the next and miraculously filled the cataclysmic voids in our bellys!!! The hash served with each is incredible to boot. Throw in some Mimosas with those Bloody Mary's and we needed wheelbarrows to get our fat a$$es back up to our rooms. Nappy time was inevitable. So was dropping a horrendous freaking deuce!!!

Excellent service and a great value given the price and food quality. A must the next opportunity I have!!! (Hopefully during my next visit in July).

My most recent business trip to NOLA brought a buddy and I here, a first for the both of us. It's located smack dab on the corner of Iberville and Bourbon, it's hard to miss. Now I have been to New Orleans probably about 15+ times, for both business and pleasure, yet somehow I'd never stopped in... I've walked by it, I've looked in at it, yet I had never stopped in. My bad for that...

So the both of us were so hungry we would have eaten just about anything, but Bourbon House called us in with her charm and warm lighting. I suppose it doesn't hurt that the both of us are seafood lovers as well and it is of course, a seafood house...

We started off with a couple of adult libations, (geez... who'd have thunk), and ordered up some Cajun Sushi, (not really sure what it was but it was delish!!!), and a couple orders of Raw Oysters in the half-shell, while we perused the menu and decided on what to select for our entrée's.

Now... Here's the disclaimer. As much as I love seafood, I'm not, nor have I ever been, an "oyster guy". About the only way I would ever have eaten them thangs was if they were fried. (I'm typically not a fan of food that has the consistency of boogers in flu season). But I decided what the heck, I can wash 'em down with a couple Abita's, right?

Now I'm not sure if I was already buzzed, my old, drunk ass, aged taste buds had finally failed me, or if they, (the oysters, that is), were THAT good, but I thoroughly enjoyed them!!! I downed 4 of them just myself, and each order came with a half dozen... A "oyster" record for me, cuz I could never get past the first prior, lol.

For dinner, I got a pescado plate, (I requested a "special order" of whole gulf fish, blackened instead of fried), that was pretty much a "standalone" entrée. But it was good. Really good. Perfectly infused with Cajun seasonings that awakened my taste buds in a fashion not unlike any they had been in for quite some time. Truly spectacular!!!

Service was exceptional, even given the hectic atmosphere that we so unabashedly had infiltrated. Prices, while not cheap, are reasonable and well worth the price. As Arnold would say... "I'll be back"!!!

Blah... Me thinks not.

WARNING: DO NOT GO HERE FOR THE FOOD!!! This is, (or should be), a beverage only establishment.

This just so happened to be my second time here... (Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me). Food is crappy and barely edible, the service sux, BUT the beers are cold. Problem is, dining options are limited in the Southwest Terminal at MSY.

On this visit, the place was packed like it was Commander's freakin' Palace!!! Barely got a seat and when I did, it took forever to get service. Ordered a cerveza, which took 10 minutes and then a sausage po' boy. 

I was pissed for two reasons:

1) because what I got was not my idea of a po' boy, (at least not like any of the dozens of others I've had in Louisiana), and;

2) I didn't take a picture of it. (Or more like what there wasn't of it). Bread, sausage and nothing else. No dressing, no lettuce, no tomato, pickle, dog hair, not a mutha effin' thing!!! Plus... The MoFo tasted like the sausage in it had been aged outdoors at Lafayette cemetery. Nasty. Chewy. Tough. And as hungry as I was, I couldn't even eat the damn thing.

So I spoke my peace, bailed out, walked across the way to the "Lucky Dog" hot dog cart and got myself an edible wiener. A big, bad a$$ quarter pound weiner for ~$6.00. And it was gnarly good too.

As for Zatarain's... Blah, me thinks not.

I came with a group of six on a Friday around 3pm, purely for the means of wanting to get their happy hour oysters. The hostess told us that there were no tables available because of reservations. After debating, we told her that we were willing to split up into small groups for tables and she directed us to a table of 6 chairs.. then proceeded to ask if we would be done by 6pm. I don't know if I've ever had a meal at a restaurant that lasted 3 hours. I think I understand where she was coming from but it was still a little off-putting that she wasn't going to offer us an empty table for a reservation 3 hours away.

That aside, this place is pretty nice and our server was friendly and on-top of his game. We ordered 6 dozen gulf oysters (one for each of us) and I got a cup of the seafood gumbo. The rest of the table also ordered drinks. The gumbo was alright. I think I would prefer a small mom&pop's gumbo. On to the main attraction of the meal.. the oysters. They took a while to come out (understandable, busy happy hour) so my group was able to drink a couple drinks each. The oysters, when they finally came out? Totally worth it. They were some of the best oysters I've ever had, fresh and good sized.

If you're looking for good happy hour oysters, this place should be on your list.

We came on a Saturday brunch/lunch and there was a small line that reached out the door. But once inside, it was pretty quick. One worker reserved us a table. Then we stood in line debating what to eat before ordering at the counter and sitting down in their small house-shop. The walls are filled with decor, mainly paintings to be sold.

The food was brought out to us at more or less the same time. I got the french toast, a side of fried potato salad, and a cinnamon roll. The french toast was unfortunately a little burnt. The fried potato salad was pretty good though: three deep fried potato balls, crisp on the outside. I actually didn't get my cinnamon roll, but they were extremely nice and apologetic when I asked for it to go.

As a last minute, found-a-Groupon decision, my friend and I came here for dinner. It was late and the place was kind of hard to find. It seemed a little sketchy because there weren't many people, even on a Friday night.

The place has an inside and an outside-type patio. We opted to sit inside because it was kind of windy. Our service was very casual (almost too casual) but extremely friendly and helpful. We were under the impression that the placed closed at 2am (Yelp), but they were closed up at 10pm (it was 10:25pm by the time we realized, sorry!). The website doesn't list a closing time either. So that was confusing. Thankfully our server was extremely patient and told us to take our time, but we packed everything to go as soon as we realized.

The menu was pretty large. The prices were definitely higher than what I expected but with the Groupon, I didn't mind so much though I'm not sure if I'd come back without the Groupon. For appetizers, we got gator bites (not bad) and fried crab claws (so good). I ordered the Jambalaya which was okay (kinda seemed like mush and was really spicy) and my friend got the crawfish etouffee which was tastier.

Overall, service was great. Food was pretty good for Groupon price, but maybe not full price.

I road tripped with a group of 6 people to New Orleans, driving from 10 pm and arriving at 6 am. We were beyond exhausted and hungry. After checking into our hotel and Yelp-ing/debating for about half an hour, we settled on Majoria's.

Walking in, it's a pretty small place and kind of reminded me a little of Waffle House. The staff is so friendly and accommodating. One of my friends was cold and without anyone mentioning anything to the staff, the owner graciously turned up the heat a little.

I got the cajun eggs benedict and it was SO GOOD. Eggs and a meat-jalapeno cheese hollandaise on a biscuit.. mm. I think it's a temporary special though. If I'm back in the area, I'll be back for this cheap, cash only breakfast place!

Tyson Bees could use some improvements if they want to survive on Penn's campus but they have a good concept going so far. 

The Grilled BBQ Lemongrass Pork Bahn Mi sandwich is very flavorful (slightly spicy) and very colorful. The portion is reasonable for $5 but definitely not as big as other sandwiches from other food trucks nearby on Spruce. 

The Korean BBQ Short Rib Beef & Kimchi Burrito for $5 is slightly disappointing. Most of the burrito's size is comprised of white rice, the meat was very hidden if there was any.

I like trying new things so I might return in hopes of another surprise like the Bahn Mi sandwich but I would strongly suggest TB lowers their prices!

I got The Fixx flatbread in hopes that their eponymous flatbread would not disappoint and I rejoiced when I did not have order remorse! Yummy yummy gruyere and caramelized onions, so delish!

Prices seem reasonable for such quality ingredients. However, the service and atmosphere is what pushed it up to 5 stars for me. Love the big round tables at the front of the restaurant with the wide windows open out to the street. Perfect meet up spot with a girlfriend on a sunny spring day! I was surprised they would have such nice servingware and even give us a bottle of tap water to share.
