The girl who took our order even came by a few times to check on how our food tasted and to take our plates away. Over-the-top friendliness for a delivery place, love it!

A friend and I came here with a girlfriend visiting from nyc. We were impressed by the decor and had fun taking pictures outside the restaurant with the sparkly lights. I enjoy eating family style (you get to try more things!) and this place was perfect for that. 

They mean small when they say "Small" appetizers. The Edamame Dumplings came in a tiny bowl with four bite sized dumplings. They were good but left more to be desired for sure. 

The "Sides" are more worth their money for the bigger portions. Kim Chee Fried Rice was fairly bland, and wasn't spicy like we assumed it would be. Crispy Brussel Sprout was the winner for the night. LOVE the charred-ness and crispy rice puffs. However, they were soaked in soy sauce, so tasted best when mixed with some rice to soak out the sourness. 

We also ordered a "Meat" dish - Grilled Vietnamese Pork Chop. The pork was was nicely cooked but the pineapple fried rice served with it was underwhelming. I wish the pineapple chunks had been larger rather than diced into rice-sized pieces.

I gave two stars instead of one star because I thing they try hard, but the execution isn't there. I ordered the double-wide platter to sample three meats and two sides, and hog balls. The meat was mushy and over-cooked. The brisket, pork and chicken all tasted the same. The hog balls were over-fried and/or the grease had not been changed. For nearly $30, this was not good BBQ, not even close. Finally, they need to do something about the flies, they eat more of my meat than I did.

You must get the ribs. You must get the ribs. This place is a modern BBQ joint with first-class service. I ordered the three meat plate with ribs, brisket, and pork. The pork and brisket were good with a nice smoked flavor, but the ribs were amazing. The dinner comes with a popover. I have always been fascinated with popovers and have tried to make them at home. This popover was dry and stuck to the paper wrapped. I chose mac & cheese and BBQ beans. The beans were good but the mac & cheese was fabulous. Look up the word creamy in the dictionary and you will see a picture of the Salt + Smoke mac & cheese. I ate inside and didn't know about the beautiful outside terrace seating. Next time I will opt to sit outside...and get the ribs.

Drove up from the Bay on a Monday morning and decided to have a quick lunch before checking into our hotel.  Exited off Virginia Street on highway 80 and headed through Downtown, pass the Truckee River and into the revamped "Midtown" area.  We liked how the streets have been repaved, streetlights upgraded, roundabout and center islands installed.  This area will be hopping in the next few years.

Arario is a Korean Asian Fusion restaurant located on the second floor with a nice wood deck for outside socializing.  Extensive bar area equivalent to the side of the dining area.  Modern decor with plenty of glass and a roll-up garage door to increase the size of the bar area.

Waitress was top-notch as she basically covered the whole restaurant with ease.  Think she handled around 8 filled tables without sweating!  She handled orders, water, food delivery, payments and table clearance with ease.  Management would be smart to make clones of her.

We ordered:
- Shrimp Tempura
- Korean Soy and Garlic Chicken Wings 
- Kalbi Burger with Fries
- Bulgogi Bibimbop in Hot Stone Bowl (Rice was nicely crisped)
- Miso Cod (table really liked this)

Complimentary Banchan (you can ask for refills) of Kimchee, Mac Salad, Cooked Shitake Mushrooms, and Spicy Shredded Veggies.

All of the appetizers and entrees that we ordered were tasty, although when I think of Kalbi, I think of Short Ribs and expected slices of Short Ribs in a sandwich.  Arario's version is a grounded up burger.  Still good....

Overall, very good Asian food, Korean based flavors, modern hip decor, excellent service with indoor and outdoor dining, well-stocked bar and a parking lot!  Restrooms are located on the first floor of the office building and are coded for entry.

Located right on Stearns Wharf, you'll find Longboards Grill which is located on top of another restaurant.  Longboards is a nice chill restaurant that is first come seating throughout.  If it's not too hot sit on the patio for a beautiful view of the ocean.  

We sat alongside the window by the bar (it was hot on the lanai) and we still got a beautiful view.  

So, when you seat yourself, a server will bring the menu to you.  I think the servers are a little slower and not as attentive as I would've liked them to be.  The reason why I say that is when we first sat outside on the patio, we got our menus then no one else approached us to take our order after 10 minutes so we made our way inside (also cause it's cooler).  
Seems that this is a popular place since it's the 1st restaurant on the pier.  

Food: 
New England Clam Chowder
Specialty Burger (I forgot the name-but it had bacon and it wasn't on the menu) with fries
Garlic Bread

The food is mediocre and nothing really stood out.  The fries were just alright too.  :(  

I would return for drinks in the future but would prefer to venture out to the other restaurants on Stearns Wharf for food.

Bouchon would've received a 5 Star from me but I needed to deduct a point for a couple of things.  

We had reservations for 8:30pm.  We arrived and waited for about 20-30 minutes before we were sat.  Unfortunately, some tables took longer to turn. The next negative is the restroom that is located next door in their private dining room area.  The restrooms are dirty looking.  :( If there's a wait for the downstairs restroom go upstairs but beware because there's a shower up there too that is not in use because there was dirt all over and wide open.  
There was a private party going on and while we stood on the patio for that long period of time we watched the servers walked out into the street to turn right next door to serve the dishes to the patrons.  
Now the last negative is there no waiting area. That's fine that there's no bar but nowhere to sit or stand other than on the patio seating where others are also eating.  Brr it was cold so a lot of people who were waiting for their table began to congregate on the patio as the patrons on the patio began to look at us. 

Now the positive.  We sat at our table and the service was absolutely impeccable.  We were given complimentary champagne due to our wait.  
My HANGRY moment started to calm down when I looked at the menu and drank my drink.  :)  

Food: 
Tutti Frutti Farms  Heirloom Tomato Salad- This was just alright.  I wish we ordered the Pork Belly after seeing our neighbors dish.  But the salad was refreshing.  
Grilled Snake River American Wagyu Center Cut Ribeye.  I ordered it medium.  It was cut in half like a burger and the top half was perfect but the bottom half was RARE.  I had to return it back to cook a bit more and they ended up making it medium well.  :(  I still ate it cause I was not about to wait again for another one.  It was seasoned well and nice and tender.  
Lastly, my friend ordered the Salmon that was dressed and cooked well.  I had a bite of it and it was delicious.  

It was our birthday so they put a candle on our dessert.  We had the lava cake.  The lava was not hot but very luke warm. It didn't not ooze out when we tried to break it apart. 

Overall, it was a nice dinner.  It is not a huge restaurant but more intimate setting.  I would return back because the food is good and would recommend it to all.

******WARNING!! As of November 2016, the VAST MAJORITY of the 267 reviews found on this page are NOT for this Rouses Market (i.e., the one on Royal St. in the French Quarter), but for the Rouses Market on Baronne St. in the Central Business District/Warehouse District.******

This review is for the Rouses Market located at 701 Royal St. in the French Quarter. It ranks a solid 3 stars in my book because of the following factors;
1) It is essentially the only real grocery store located in the French Quarter.
2) Its product line leans toward natural products. In many ways, the Rouses chain tries to compete not only with supermarkets, but with Whole Foods as well.
3) It is open for long hours each day, and in fact, is open until 1 AM.

Having said that, I will admit, as others have noted, that the store is incredibly small, and that it has only one small set of doors, located at a front corner of the store, through which all customers, and also all deliveries and tradespeople, must all somehow manage to pass.

Because of the small size of the store, the selection and range of items offered is rather limited. For example, I recently spent five minutes trying to locate the section that stocks nutritional supplements, and, having failed at that task, I asked a grocery clerk for the location of the nutritional supplements section. When he confessed that he had never heard of nutritional supplements, I gave him  some examples, citing products such as "vitamin C, or calcium tablets". He searched in vain for five minutes, and then gave up  He and I then went to the front desk, where I asked  a woman (who identified herself as a manager) the same question. Much as happened with the clerk earlier, she confessed that she had never heard of such a product, and, thus I shared with her the examples (cited above) that I had shared with the clerk. Looking  at me blankly, she vaguely pointed me toward a spot in a specific aisle that, of course  bore no  trace of  nutritional supplements. A conversation with another manager later confirmed that they do not carry nutritional supplements.

I had much the same experience days earlier in trying to locate Dr. Bronner's liquid soaps, a line of natural and organic soaps which are, and have been, a staple of natural foods stores for over 60 years. The manager had never heard of such a product line, and admitted that he did not carry it. In contrast, even the tiniest and shabbiest Whole Foods store, even a one-star rated one, always offers a wide selection of this staple product line. 

Now it is time to get back to the header paragraph of my review: The sad reality is that as of Nov. 2016, the VAST MAJORITY of the 267 reviews found on this page are NOT for this Rouses Market, but rather for the Rouses Market on Baronne St. in the Central Business District/Warehouse District. In fact, a quick survey that I conducted yesterday of all 267 reviews indicates that at least 85% of them, particularly the 5 star reviews, are for the vastly larger Rouses Market located in the warehouse district. 

So, if you should see on this page a review (and there are many of them) that claims that this store sports any of the following features:
-- tons of free parking
-- an outdoor open-air dining area with garden
-- a rooftop herb garden (some reviewers have called it "aerophonic", whatever that is...) where you can prance happily through the aisles of herbs
-- a burrito bar
-- a coffee bar
-- rooftop overflow parking
-- a fresh pizza bar/counter
-- a huge selection of single-bottle beers
-- a sushi bar/counter
-- never a line at the "many checkout registers"
-- wide aisles
-- an amazing and wide selection of foods and other natural products
-- a fresh seafood counter
-- a fresh meat counter

....well, those reviews are TOTALLY WRONG!!! None of those things listed above are true for this store, but they are true for the Baronne St. store, which is about ten thousand times larger than the French Quarter (FQ) store.

However, the FQ store does have a deli counter, albeit a very small one, and the staffers there are very friendly.

Some pluses about the admittedly very tiny FQ store: 
-- It does carry a good selection of yogurt and kefir products.
-- The refrigerated products section offers a limited array of  pre-packaged sushi products made at its larger sister store. 
-- It often carries bottles of  egg nog in the dairy section.
-- Most of the staffers try very hard to be helpful.

Lastly, let us address the question that has been burning in my mind for the past week: How could it possibly be that over 80% of the reviews found on this page are really for the much larger store on Baronne Street in the Warehouse district? How could so many reviewers possibly make the same mistake? After hard deliberation, I feel  that these gross errors must be chalked up to the fact that there is a very high rate of consumption, and abuse, of alcohol and drugs in the FQ, and in all of New Orleans, and thus...!

Social distancing ans outdoor seating during COVID-19. #YELPLOVE #COVID19 # SOCIAL DISTANCING

For me, this is one of my favorite 'go-to' place for chargrilled oysters.  

Love the ambience... Love the great customer service... Love the excellent taste of the product...

Kudos to Drago's for shifting and hosting parties of customers outside as a result of #COVID19. Nothing more excellent than still being able to get good food during this #COVIDquarantine2020.

Although, I was doing take out, the oysters were packaged well enough so that the temperature of the food was as it was when I left the restaurant.  Happy Happy Joy Joy!!!!

Pricing was fair.
Ample parking. 
Excellent service.
