This is my go-to-hide-away place to get my knowledge on.  I love the feel of the area & this coffee shop takes on the same vibe.  The flow of people in and out is just as 'easy breezy'.  

Sit indoors for ac air or journey outside for a killer incognito view & natural air; either way it's all good.  

The food here, especially the Caprese sandwich is the bomb!!! And it's just what the doctor ordered when you're in study-mode & fear stopping for a bite to eat will break your mojo.

The dirty chai is killer here.  I mean, no you won't die, but it's truly one of the best I've had.  They get it right each & every time.  

Other offerings of coffee based libations are good too, but the dirty chai hails as my favorite.  Flavored teas, hot or cold.  Water juices, whatever your pleasure of the non-alcoholic sort, they can accommodate you.

Eco-friendly, pet friendly & baby friendly... It's just all around friendly. 

In the heart of mid-city, this place is a truly gem!!!!

A must go when in the Downtown Bourbon Street Area. Pat O'Briens is a treasure in and of itself. Offering food, great music and fantastic drinks; there's always a party here. 

Enter from Bourbon Street and you're in the front bar area. Food & drinks can be ordered here to your specifications. 

Once inside, follow the pathway to the middle of the facility, where you'll see more dining area & a beautiful water fountain that lights up the area at night. 

Just adjacent to the fountain, and with an entrance of its own, you'll find the infamous dueling piano bar. What a treat this is. The musicians entertain the crowds with songs and melodies. They also take request. Dimly lit lights provide just the right atmosphere for all things serene & relaxing. 

Pat Ohs (as be natives call it) is a must-go-to when in he area. Try it & see for yourself.

I found this restaurant to be nice in decor, the general feel, the host/hostesses/staff, the food & the drinks. 

I found the base pricing to be fair on most items, but had the potential to get pricey. For instance pasta (alone) is one $18 for this one dish, then add in $8 more for shrimp; ehhhhhh, $26 for shrimp pasta, I'll pass. 

I did find the drink, Singapor Sling, to be tasty & I had a warm fuzzy feeling after just the one, WINNING!!!! A member of my dining party tried the Pimm's Cup & said it too was delightful. 

And the ambiance is great, lots of open space, which can get noisy, but makes for a more lively dining experience. 

Service with a smile is what we got. 

She separated the checks for us, although she was a little reluctant. 

Reservations can be made & I would guess during a holiday or something of that nature, that might be recommended; but we were able to walk in, be seated & get to eating!!!!  

Love that a portion of the proceeds go to the Roots Music Foundation; Saint Cecilia is the patron saint of music, makes sense.

Ahhhhh well I could say WALMART IS WALMART IS WALMART, but that's totally not true in this case.  This WalMart is FAMOUS... this is where Mr Ghetto shot the Wally-World, #ijs; don't judge me, check it out for yourself.  But anyway...

I must admit I USUALLY steer clear of this WalMart like the plague, because of the unprofessional, lacking customer service, unhelpful store associates BUT there has been a considerable change in the attitudes & work ethics of most of the employees.  With that being said, I am now open to visit & patronage this Walmart.  New & improved employee attitudes, clean aisles, bathroom are USABLE, quick check out lines, items in place & in stock.  This is GREAT news for the uptown community as I know they frequent this location.  So happy for the new-old environment.

My visit was uneventful, I was able to do my normal "stick & move" caper; get it & go... I love the fluidness.  I was able to walk into the store, grab my items & proceed to the checkout area without hassle.  This is how shopping is supposed to be... YEAH!!!!!!! 

I find this location to be great in its placement.  One of 3 WalMarts in New Orleans; I'm happy about the changes & I look forward to returning to be a FREQUENT FLYER of this location.  Happy Happy Joy Joy!!!!

Great location. Great pizza. Great customer service. Great pricing. Great timing. 

Picture it: WORK MEETING, 35 people and counting... Theo's to the rescue. 

The food was timely, the taste was GRRRRRREEEEEAAAATTTTT & the temperature was PERFECT. 

Again, be reminded, it was a WORK LUNCH MEETING, so timing was critical and they NAILED it. As it hit the door I smelled the pizza, despite being upstairs, some 20 feet away; trust me, the NOSE KNOWS pizza!!! 

Boxes upon boxes upon boxes of pizza and none went to waste; everyone clearly enjoyed it, as was evident due to the number of empty boxes. 

I've passed this location on Canal St several times and always promised to stop in. But TODAY, since it was delivered FRESH & PIPING HOT right to the front door, there was no excuse; and I was glad about it. 

We also had a caprese salad with perfectly slice FRESH mozzarella and plump tomatoes. All parts of this salad were ON POINT!!!!! So winnnnnnnning!!!!!!

I hear the folks at work have future plans to make this place a GO-TO for pizza and caprese salad; I second that notion.

Convenient and right there when you need that 'must have' snack while you're out and about. I love that fact that this store is a Rouses, a name you can trust and you know what to expect, branding; but obviously, it's smaller than most Rouses and as a result, it lacks the appearance that you expect at Rouses Stores. 

Seems that it might have been a convenience store that they slapped the ROUSES name on, upped the prices a bit, added some "standard" Rouses items and called it a day. 

The cashiers were friendly and although there was a line 5 people deep, it was reduced quickly, they work fast. 

4-5 aisles are stocked full of goodies to feed your high if that be the case or for light weight grocery shopping. 

It was just what I needed, when I needed it.

Needed to grab a late night bite and I specifically wanted a breakfast sandwich (bacon eggs cheese dressed on French Bread). I chose this place because as the menu stated, it fit the bill for what I was seeking. Additionally, there was a BLOODY MARY that I spotted on the menu, so I said '2 for 1', #leggo. 

Arriving, of course parking wasn't the greatest, but I made due. 

Getting there an hour before closing, probably wasn't the best thing, but hey, when you're HANGRY, you just are. 

I got the Bloody Mary, chatted it up w a member of the kitchen staff, as he was at the bar when I arrived; ordered my food and I was gone lickety-split. 

I will say the food was good, a tad bit dry, but I may have needed to dress the po-boy, next time I know. 

The potatoes were seasoned properly & they were eaten THE NEXT DAY for dinner. 

Good experience across the board, I'll be back after visiting another spot just down the way. 

Great decor on the walls, lots of great local & national musicians... Way cool!!!!! 

Open til 11p; but get there before 10p as by this time they're prepping to close.

Dining during COVID - DDC the acronym I created. 

To be noted: Visited this dining establishment post workout on a Sunday, in the midst of COVID. 

This is a GREAT idea, multiple different eateries in one location. Makes me think of a FOOD COURT in a shopping mall, but much nicer decor, oh and with a fully stocked bar... hello #winning!!! 

On this particular day, we tried visiting a few of the eateries, buttttttttttt they were closed. So we settled on ELYSIAN SEAFOOD & ASIAN LICIOUS; both good choices. 

I will admit, the young lady working at ELYSIAN gave a little 'tude, but I over looked it. It was a Sunday, it was nice outside & they seemed pretty slow, so maybe, just maybe she didn't want to be bothered or wanted to be elsewhere; can't say I blame her, but anyway... Anywho, 'tude ignored, I ordered my food & went on my way to the next stop... SUSHI!!! 

The gentleman at ASIAN LICIOUS was welcoming, made suggestions & was very patient. I make sure to mention the bad AND THE GOOD; I'm not biased, ok? OK!!!! I'm sharing the experience... 

Anywho, the BBQ Shrimp po-boy from ELYSIAN was delightful, not enough for sharing, but definitely enough for satiation. 

The sushi roll from ASIAN LICIOUS was mooorreee than enough & very cost efficient. 

It was fairly empty in the place, so we unmasked & chowed down on the vittles. When I tell you there wasn't a crumb left in sight... those plates could have been reused as we left them... we were HONgry and the foot fit the bill. Lite enough for a post workout meal & heavy enough for that GOODY GOODY GUM DROP, I'm full kinda feeling. 

Love that the cleaning guy was readily available to remove our used utensils & plates. He was ON HIS JOB... this was commendable & much appreciated; next time I'll have cash to tip him out, we were CARD CARRYING MEMBERS on this day #freshoutofpapermoney. 

COVID precautions were being taken & this was quite refreshing, all things considered.  

Also to be noted, the other side of all the eateries is like a sort of quiet, meet up & chill area; it was quite pleasing to the eye & seemed to be a place of "overflow". Were it to be too crowded in the dining area of the building, one could just mosey on over to the non-eatery side of the building. This area is quite relaxing, if I must say so myself. 

As I stated, I will return, hopefully more eateries will be open & ready for business. 

Street parking is the call for the day and unless you go in a Sunday, watch out for meter maids.

Delicious oh so Delicious. Love the play on words regarding the naming of this restaurant; Crescent City Works & the background image is the ever loved water meter cover... Way cool. 

Located on Busy Bustling Bourbon Street; this place is ah-mazing when it comes to pizza. You'll love all the combinations ie spinach & green tomatoes; hello winning.  There are a few bar stools & a bar for your dining in pleasure; which should be a short stint. Because really, how long does it take to eat a slice of pizza? Well for me, NOT LONG AT ALL!!!!! I fold mine in half like a sandwich, yesss, yesss, yesss... a couple bites in succession, chew, chew, chew & what was once in-front me is NOW inside my belly... #happyhappyjoyjoy. 

The slices vary in price starting at $4.50 & increasing upwards... But not too much more. I mean a meal for $5; you can't beat that. And might I add the size of the slice is ample, you'll be happy.  

Beverage choices range from water to beer to soda... Pick your poison. 

I found the staff to be quite helpful & patient while you're making selections. This is great because with such a WIDE VARIETY of choices, selection can be hard. 

In the couple times I've been there; there were a few links that needed working out that managed to delay me a bit; namey one visit, the beer on tap was too foamy & the cash register went down on another visit. Both times, staff and management came to the rescue & the day was saved. 

Most recently, I have managed to find a quickie parking spot & dash in & out to grab a slice or two... Hope that quickie spot is always available.

Jess the owner is simply magnificent. Totally a gracious, kind hearted 100% customer service orientated owner. And for that this place gets an automatic pass for me. I watched home work the room and visit table by table by table to greet his guests. Almost like he was home hosting a party. At first I didn't know who he was, but as I watched, I made the correct assumption. 

Brittany was our server and she was also just as pleasant and accommodating. She advised of specials on the menu. She gave restaurant history. She was VERY patient as we decided on drink choices as there was an LSU Drink Special going on & then there were regular specials; we had choices & important decisions to make. We decided on the one-price all you can drink vodka bar, while I know that's not the name, you get the point. The vodka bar had all the fixings for whatever stimulated your palette. From blood Mary's to screw drivers... Garnishment overload was the name of the game. And while I might be biased, I think the bloody Mary mix ranks up there with some of the local award winning mixes. 

The decor indoor was very modern and trendy; totally my kind of place. Open and free for people watching, a favorite sport of mine; and just being a general lookey-lou. High bar chairs at the dining friendly bar or there is seating in the bar area that is kinda first come first serve or you can wait for a table in the main dining room... Any option is a good one. 

And the food was delicioussssssss. Perfectly prepared. Temperature was accurate and Brittany did advised me of the hot-to-touch mini skillet with my mac-n-cheese on it and I heeded the warning.  The burger was seasoned absolutely perfect and despite being well done as requested it was not dry; totally a perfect combination. 

This is a great place for a dining experience; I hear there's a brunch special that I need to return to take part in.

Great place for all things BUBBLE TEA. I can honestly say, the menu is a tad bit overwhelming. I mean there are slushies, tea-based drinks, non-dairy drinks and the list goes on and on. Where's the cheat sheet? Then let's not even talk about the toppings (wide eyed stare). I can honestly say, "I wasn't ready..." 

Thankfully, the friendly cashier took the time to assist me with narrowing my selection; this was great because I didn't want to delayed other customers. 

My wait was very short & I was glad because I was ready to taste my concoction. 

I found the cup sizes to be drastically different, which is a good marketing scheme. $4.75 for 8oz or just a quarter more for a 12oz; .25¢ for four more ounces... Which do you choose? No worries, we all know the answer. But keep in mind, most drinks are filled with ice... So there goes your .4oz & 25¢ more. Also they charge for the tapioca... I guess this made the norm as it's my 2nd time encountering such. 

I also noticed, this seems like a hangout place; as I waited for my drink, I noticed some of people just chilling and watching movies etc on the iPad, as well as families dining/drinking in. This is a rare novelty to see, the families "dining/drinking in" as most folks are always 'on-the-go'. 

Shared parking lot with ample space. A few spots are dedicated to other businesses, but that's just a few. Most spaces are open for all to park.   

I will return to this location, after I've studied the menu that is.

7 3 Distilling... I like it. Nice place. Nice people. Smaller than most distilleries, but hey you gotta start somewhere huh?

The tour is informational & enlightening. I might've should've taken the tour BEFORE I started tasting the product & then I'd be able to remember if the 73 was significant for the number of neighborhoods/areas in New Orleans or the number of cities in Louisiana orrrrrrrrrrrr what the 73 was for, ehhhhhh. 

The decor is nice and I even saw a t-shirt I have plans to purchase when they got more sizes, SCHmedium please... 

The resident dog is a people friendly mixed breed, looks like some sort of Alaskan shepherd collie breed, heck idk, Suki was very friendly & open to hugs & rubs. 

I found the pricing to be fair; $6 happy hour cocktails, I'm with it. 

I love that connection with all things New Orleans; the drinks all have names of local areas i.e. Gentilly, St Roch, yeah they had me there. I love to see pride in the area. 

For now there's Gin & Vodka; but soon there will be MOONSHINE, yesssssssssssss!!!!! 

Demetrius, our tour guide was friendly, very knowledgeable & very accommodating. He set us us with "THE FLIGHT", which was a generous shot of ALL 3 products... very nice!!!!!! 

While there are food trucks that may show up from time to time; I'd like to see them have a few things to nosh on while you're getting your drink on; the food truck thingy is cool, but I'd prefer to keep the PARTYING @ THE PARTY.

Well I believed "the hype" & this place DID NOT live up to it; I found the food to be just a bit above average. 

Love the Marigny/Bywater Area & its feng shui, the people at the restaurant are very friendly & accommodating, but the food was lackluster. I know, I know my review is different from the norm, but I could've passed on this place. 

I found the meat, although tender & easily chewed; to be just was ok. (Humps shoulders). I expected more flavor in the meat, I guess what it lacked in flavor, it made up for in tenderness. 

There were an array of sides, I chose Mac-n-Cheese, because I'm a cheese loving girl, I found it to be not good. It was quite cheesy, but lacked Mac-n-Cheese flavor, crazy right.

Just not good to me. 

Ehhhhh, I won't be back.

Stopped in for FRIED CATFISH for my granny; because it's FRIED FISH FRIDAY, ya know. 

I stopped in Fiorella's because the neighboring restaurant that I was initially headed to was closed at 2p, everyday, hmmmm... AnyWHO, I made my way in & as I opened the door, I could smell FRIED FOODS cooking; BINGO, I was back in the FRIED FISH FRIDAY game. 

The young lady took my order & I was NOW in line to play the 'waiting game'. After paying for my food & having a seat, I noticed patrons that entered to dine in came in AFTER me, placed ordered AFTER me & received their food BEFORE me; ehhhhhhh not cool, but I patiently waited, after all, I was winning in the FriedFishFriday game, despite losing in the 'waiting game'. 

Once my name was called & was presented with food, I exited & took note of the ability to call in an order; maybe I'll try that next time go ro

Post Bubble Run eating, 11am-ish, we landed here. Okie Dokie Chokie... let's get it in.

Picture it:
-5 of us, 4 post bubble run, rainbow colored folks
-20 minutes to decide on food & drinks (I think the bubbles had our brains BUBBLED...lol)
-Bridget, our server with an elephant-memory was able to get drink & beverage orders without writing anything down... Hello, I'd never want to owe her money or anything else
-food took a little longer than expected & she, elephant memory Bridget, apologized immensely & provide chips to satisfy our hunger; way cool
-food and drinks appeared & we're munching... Bridget returned several times, despite be assigned ANOTHER TABLE ACROSS THE RESTAURANT of Post BUBBLE RUNNERS; she still managed to assist us and check to ensure we had no wants
-checking out was a breeze; a few separate checks here & there... and bing bod-da boom, we're outta there

Kudos to Friday for Bridget with the elephant memory
Kudos to Friday for EVERYDAY 2 for 1... Hello hence the motto "here it's Friday EVERYDAY"; I'm loving it!!!!
Kudos to Friday the good food (or maybe we we're just super duper hungry after the run which we walked... lol); temperature was good... taste was better...  pricing was great
Kudos to Friday for swift checking out methods

Shared parking is limited, but as I stated we were there riiiiiiiiiiiight after they opened, soon it didn't matter.

Nice place to grab a quick bite to eat. 

Open and spacious seating area; indoors and outdoors. Indoors seating areas available are: bar seating, raised floor area, street level seating, island seating.  Outdoor seating available area: street level meeting, stage/platform area. Pick your pleasure, indoor or outdoor; you won't be disappointed. 

Cool happening little place. I remember it used to be a sandwich shop & what a major overhaul. I love the environment, it just screams HAPPY HOUR, LETS MEET AFTER WORK. Love the laissez faire attitude; very relaxed environment. 

I found the staff to be very friendly and inviting. The hostess can sometimes been seen right outside the front door greeting passerbys; how cool is that. 

This place is a nifty little spot for chilling & linking up!!!!

I loveeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee EVERY bit of this place!!! 

From the ambiance, love the minimalist decor, hello is that a window in the ceiling doubling as decoration... to the handsomely eye catching, ever helpful server... to the succulent, melting in your mouth, made to perfection food... to the affordable, you can eat here everyday and not break your budget price points... to the Naturally N'awlins off Camp St location... to the plentiful, I'll have one of everything on the menu choices... You get what I'm saying. 

About a year into this "No-Meat" life change, I'm glad to see more vegan/vegani-ish restaurant & choices being made available.  Part of the struggle of being a non-meat eater is the availability... But SEED has come to my personal rescue on this effort. 

Lots of choices and what I like most is it's ALL VEGAN... So you can't go wrong. 

On this day I opted for the coconut burger with quinoa, with buffalo dressing on the side, NO CHEESE & an adult beverage, well I guess it wasn't all VEGAN; lol, lol. My dining partner had the same with a little variation, less the adult beverage. 

The atmosphere is so chic and free flowing, until I didn't realize the time that happen elasped, hello 2 hours and counting. 

The food was presented in a swift manner. Long enough to know it was freshly made but not too long as to make me start chewing on my knuckles to pacify my hunger. Surprisingly, I ATE ALL MY FOOD in this one setting. This is a rarity for me... But I did it. Talk about feeling accomplished. I diddddddddddddddd notice a dessert section, but I passed on it as I was comfortably stuffed. 

I plan to return as this was truly a pleasurable dining experience.

Open 24 hours and it's all good!!!! 

Full bar. Full menu. Breakfast at dinner time. Dinner at breakfast time... Have your way. 

I guess this is when IH*P met a dive bar = DeJaVu!!!! 

Seat yourself; and then wait for a server to bring menus & water. 

Window seats or middle of the restaurant, the view is pretty much the same. 

Myself & friends took the larger table in the middle of the restaurant, we needed the space for eating & sharing. 

Wings, mini crab cakes, fried catfish poboy, nachos & a Bloody Mary to wash it down; we shared the food, but not the drink.  (#sharingiscaringBUTnotwhenabloodymaryisinvolved)

Service was ok & pricing was good. Glad to know this 24 hour place is open for business.

I am pizza... Pizza is me!!!! That being said, this place gets it all the way right. $7.95 plus tax gets you a whole pizza pie, all to yourself. The menu calls for the standard for $5 & some change; or $7.95 to build your own. 

I crafted my own with Garlic Basil as the base, ALLLLLLLLLL the cheeses in the building, add in a few jalapenos & HAPPY HAPPY AM I!!!! Then to top it off, literally and figuratively, at the end, I added oil and balsamic vinaigrette drizzle to my pizza once it edited the oven... OMG!!!! Sheesh!!! My only disappointment was that I couldn't eat it all in one setting.  

For my beverage of choice, I opted against the water, soda, coconut water, juices options... Bring on the NOLA Beer on tap. It was my first time trying it annnnnnnnnnd I was pleased. 

Start to finish, this process took about 12 minutes. That's novel for pizza making. What's the secret? Is it the massive fire oven? Or the thin, flaky, buttery crust? Or the super efficient restaurant workers? Idk, whatever the reason, it happened and that made the difference. 

The only draw back for THIS location, is the lack of parking. Truly this location caters to the CBD/downtown crowd and that's super cool. And since I know parking is the challenge I will face, I'll be prepared for it HEAD FIRST. And speaking about head first... Did I mention there's an option to call ahead??? I saw it, it happens and then so now BLAZE has been added to my list of places for one of my infamous #stickandmovecapers!!!! Great, Great, Great!!!!

Nothing do I love more than a good, hearty, filling salad... and then enter CITY GREENS!!!!! 

Where have you been all my SALAD EATING LIFE???  Salad & salad things as far as the eye can see.  Fix it up or fix it down, this salad heaven is great for all, not just the heart healthy.  

Hop in line, decide on the salad of your choice, tailor it to your liking, pay & have at it.  

Watching them prepare the salad is interesting as well.  A bowl for measuring the lettuce, flipping it up & then down... put it in the bowl & there you have it.

Love the GREEN-feel of the restaurant as well.  Clean floors, bright lights, windows that border the restaurant... all make for an open-green-clean feeling.  The recycling receptacles add to the GREEN-feel as well; nothing I like more than recycling.

Pricing is fair.  Parking is great.  Employees are friendly.

Out for a night of dining and pleasant conversation, we settled on this restaurant.  Been here before and so I was aware of what to expect; sooooo Outback Down Under was it for the night.  

Not a long wait, which was great as this place is normally packed to capacity.  Maybe because it was the middle of the week, Yes HUMP DAY.  

Glad we came on this day, as there was a Wednesday special that gave options for different entrees, sides and dessert for a nominal fee; a glorified combo, less the drink, but definitely way better than McDonalds or BK.  

So, once we were seated, Joe was our server and try as he may, the food was just off on this particular night.  He confessed to us that he was a former kitchen employee and was compassionate about our complaints and satisfaction, or lack thereof.  Here were our issues: My sirloin was sent back because it was too tough and over cooked... Mahi Mahi was sent back because of a rancid odor...  Chicken tortilla soup was returned because it was cold... Sheesh, idk what the heck was going on in the kitchen on this night, but we weren't happy campers.  And as I was ear hustling, apparently it just wasn't my table, as the gentleman behind us had a similar compliant.

We were told the manager would come by, buuuuuuuuttt he didn't.  No matter because, having been here before, as I stated, we opted to leave and come back on another day... I'm told Saturday is a good day #Joereturnstokitchenduty

Finally made it to this restaurant; timing is everything. 

From the first time I heard of this restaurant, it was on my "places to go" list. The popularity was astounding. I heard people say their wait times were 1.5-2 hours long. As a result, I waited for the hype to die down & I'm soooooooo glad I did. 

The menu is quite extensive, but I came for 1 thing and 1 thing ONLY... THE SEAFOOD BAG!!! 

(1st visit) Looking at the menu, there are lots of choices to be made. And it never hurts to peruse the menu, but I knew I came for SEAFOOD BAG & that's all I could see on the menu. That being said, when our server came, we ordered & I was asked of the level of spiciness that I preferred for my "bag" (bag of seafood). I'm that girl, so I asked for the "hottest/spiciest" level. 

My anticipation was super high... I just knew the spicy seafood was gonna "tear my MOUF out"... I WAS DISAPPOINTED. Not only was it "not super duper spicy" as the server explained, it also LACKED flavor... It was bland. Although, there was LOTS of buttery-sauce coating the seafood, the seafood flavor & spiciness were BOTH lacking.  I was majorly disappointed. 

(2nd visit) It is to be noted, that I returned, because I thought maybe the 1st visit was a fluke; but sadly it wasn't. Once again, the seafood was NEITHER spicy nor properly flavored. 

This is LOUISIANA... Bland seafood SHOULD be illegal, lol. I won't be returning. I'll take my hopes and anticipation of spiciness & seafood flavor ELSEWHERE. 

Off street parking is available, but never seems like it's enough because someone is always waiting for a parking spot. 

Not a long wait, the time I went, and once again, I'm glad I waited for the popularity to die down.

Finally made it. Love the ambiance. Great staff. Location is cool, less the parking situation (arghhhhhhhhhh they don't validate). A little price, but I guess being in the CBD it goes with the territory. The food was good, not a large selection, so you're relegated to a few choices; I will admit I was full though. Glad to see this place is more than just breakfast foods; although breakfast is my FAVORITE meal. 

Love the window seating, especially since I'm a self-certified Lookie-Lou; I can see all I can See-See-See. 

I get a So-Cal vibe from this place due to the set up, the outdoor tables, the table settings & the all around general vibe; I can dig it!!!! 

The pastries counter looked all too delectable, but I was super-duper full after my meal. My Bloody Mary was good but lacked said "buzz" I was expecting. 

I'm going to have to stop in for breakfast and partake of one of the fine assortments in the pastry case.

I came, I saw, I conquered...

Looking for a place the serves BEIGNETS & then some... Well you've found it!!!!  On the corner of Decatur & Toulouse, you'll find the place.

Open bar & food other than BEIGNETS.  Order you food & take the number, some one will bring your food to your table or the are where you're seated.  Despite being here during the 2017 French Quarter Fest, my items were delivered quickly.  But not before I had an opportunity to take part in some libations at the FULL BAR just steps away.

I will admit the beignets taste different than the other famous place, but they are as tasty. An order consists of 3 doughnuts & all the powdery goodness that comes along with it.  

Love the open cafe feel & the tables & bar seating. Lots of activity can be seen here & it makes the place more lovely,  This place gets it right.

Finally made it & the coast was clear. 75 degrees and balmy; and the Freezy 'My Thai' ice cream for the bill for ice cream goodness. It was hard to decide, but hat just means, I'll be back.

Love the nature/disposition of the employees. Friendly, patient & accommodating. The creators take time to take your order & carry it out to your specifications... So be patient. 

Love the selection of pre made creations available. All kinds of cute creations with Quirky names... And the toppings, oh my. 

Cost is a little above the norm, but consider the process & the creation... So Worth it.

I love this Rouses. In the heart of the CBD & open late, SIMPLY FANTASTIC!!!! 

Going here is an experience. Parking is a bit of a chore, especially on a busy day. Don't get me wrong, there's plenty of GARAGE parking. But if folks are like me, you're going right in & right out; who wants to park in the garage, when you can most assuredly park in the 30 car rear parking lot OR grab a spot on the street... Ehhhhhhhhhhhhh not me. Lol. 

Once parked though, the experience begins; walking into the store, either from the front door or from the rear parking lot. Lots of shopping items to choose from. Great exercise for the wandering eyes. Aisles & aisles of food items, hard to find items & general run of the mill items. 
Sushi is always fresh. Freshly baked pizza. Fresh looking fruit. Myriad of beverage choices. LSU & Tulane items, Other gifts, Friendly employees, "paper or plastic", fresh bakery delectables, various food & beverage items; just don't enter THIS store hOngry (yes I said hOngry). Lots of foot traffic here. And did I mention the "mini cafe-like" eating area oh and the sidewalk tables in front the store; channelling my inner Los Angeles feel. 

I find pricing to be a bit more than the regular neighborhood Rouses, but given the location, I understand.

Love this place. It's like ASIAN FUSION or something like that. Iea what can't you get here???? 

They've recently extended their hours and they have bubble tea and parking and it's near my job and it's just GREAT!!!

Lots of noodles, pho, banh mi, wraps and so many more choices. I've been here several times & never been disappointed.

The staff is always pleasant and accommodating. 

Sitting outdoors is a plus. Nice patio area. 

Private parking lot, but getting in early is best as the lot fills up quickly.

Great restaurant in one of my FAVORITE parts of town. Locally owned and operated, near my neighborhood and helping to fuel the economy, I'm all in. 

From the outside, one wouldn't think all this quaintness is bottled up inside, but it is. 

Great decor. Friendly, patient staff. Good gooooooood food; no complaints here. The food selections we decide on were: the salmon with asparagus and parmasean grits, chicken and waffles & shrimp-n-grits (which I will be trying upon my next visit). The food was delivered in a timely manner and the temperature was right as well. 

Pricing was fair; separate checks are available, but with parties 5 or more, gratuity is added & I think that's fair. 

My BLOODY MARY was great, great, great; it came with cucumbers and olives. This was new to me, but hey I tried it and I liked it. 

Love the logo, simple yet memorable. Oh and the slogan on the wall in the bar area "Morrow of the story..." Love it!!! 

This place gets packed on Sundays, so come early. And there's valet parking for a small fee should you desire curb side service. Security looms outside, so dine with ease. There's a set brunch menu on Sunday, but seemingly other days there's a full menu to select from. 

We said it would be nice if they added a dining area on the sidewalk... Maybe that's coming in the near future.

Hello!!!! Winning!!!! Only a month old!!!!  

If you build it, THEY WILL COME. 

SORRY St*rbucks, y'all missed out. I'm happy to see more businesses come to the area and this one is no exception. 

The spot of the former ICE HOUSE on Gentilly across from the Baptist Seminary; between 'God is good car wash' &  Church's Chicken is this god-send of a coffee shop. 

Not only that, but this is a FAITH BASED coffeeshop... LOVING IT!!!!

Proceeds from sales go to the program to help other program participants; way cool!!!! 

Annnnnnnnnnnnd to top it off, there's a loyalty program that is super duper awesome. 

Pros:
Close to my house
The loyalty program
Great hours 
Great pricing
Giving back to the community
Coffee, tea, lattes, snacks & lite bites 

Cons:
More parking

I'm so ecstatic!!!!

I am FULL AS A TICK... All I need is to pitch a hammock in City Park on this breezy, beautiful April the 13th... Hello!!!!!!

Oh my God!!!!! What a god-send in mylife. I think this place was personally created for me. 

When I got wind of the opening, I knew with haste I must make my way & today was the day; and there was NOOOOOOOOOO disappointment. 

Broad & St Phillip is where you'll find this treasure; located beneath a babershop the "pièce de résistance" lives!!!! 

Walking in, to the right are 3-4 tables & chairs for dining; to the left is a table for two that sits flush with the wall... then straight to the back is all the veganie-goodiness... The FOOD!!!!!

Two sides, one is for hot food & the other is a salad bar of sorts.  All the food is served by the staff, this is GREAT; I don't care for buffets, things happen at buffets, ewwwww.  

The food is served a la carte or you can get a combo-of sorts, 2 entrees and 2 sides.  I choose the Pasta, Okra Gumbo, Sweet Potatoes & Mac-n-Cheese (I'm a cheese lover, despite being lactose intolerant).  Then to top it off, I got some VEGAN ICE CREAM & a drink of Green-Goddess; all for under $20 bucks; winning with a CAPITAL W!!!!!!

ALL THE FOOD AMAZINGLY great & flavorful.  Lots of times, removing ingredients from foods you've been eating all your life, you anticipate am unfamiliar, 'gotta get used to it' taste; but that wasn't the case this time go round.  

The okra was robust & tasted of all things creole, thankfully it lacked that acidic tomato taste; this was fantastic, made my tummy happy.  

The sweet potatoes tasted like my granny's; enough said!!! 

The pasta was a new taste for me, just because it lacked seafood, but the replacements were right on time & made me glad I had made the selection.  

And the MAC N CHEESE; since this is an ALL TIME FAVORITE of mine... This was the seller for me.  It PASSED THE TGB-MAC-N-CHEESE test!!!!! I love it!!!!!!!!   

With some many other choices to select, I'll definitely be back to get more of this VEGAN SOULFOOD.  

Oh and the Ice Cream, you can taste the flavors should that be your desire; but it's VEGAN too... I'm over-joyed this little piece of heaven is open & in the direction of my house... HELLO, dinner as I head to the house.  

Ooooooh and the Green Goddess, to rinse it all down... I'm a happy, happy, dairy free, vegan food eating camper.

What a disappointment. Average to good food & God-awful service. 

This is the first time I have ever intentionally left $0 as a tip; believe me she earned it. 

Out with friends to celebrate a birthday, we decided upon the Cheesecake Factory for two reasons: it's newness in the area & proximity. 

The wait was 35 minutes; we provided a cellphone number, as requested, for notification when our table was ready. We asked for 1st available with a preference for outdoor seating. 

*****Reasons for less than 5 stars*****

More than 5 items we attempted to order were unavailable or the kitchen was unable to prepare (for 1 reason or another)

A bread basket was promised before the meal, however, it arrived AFTER our food was served. 

Drinks were not refilled even after the server visited our area on more than 6 occasions, yes I counted, she managed to steer clear of our table - maybe she was embarrassed, idk. 

Three in our party & one person received her meal 20 minutes prior to the other two of us 

We had to request silverware, which arrived 5-7 minutes after the 1st person in our party received her food. 

Appetizers were NEVER delivered or even spoken of until we had to remind her NOT to place them on the bill. 

The manager brought our food out & apologized for the error; as he stated he was just made privy to the disastrous issues & he comped our desserts; however even though she was aware of the freebie, because she reiterated the plans of free dessert as stated by the manager; little miss sunshine STILL charged us for the cheesecake (crickets); we felt like this should've been an episode of Punk'd!!! 

*****Reasons for AT LEAST 2 Stars*****

Extensive menu, lots to choose from. Great selection of cheesecake. New to the area. 

I'll be back, but I pray the experience isn't as such; this is a great restaurant as I've been to other locations throughout the US. And I know this location has the same potential.

I'd be lying if I said I hadn't been looking forward to this place opening for the past year. I moved to Fishers last December literally counting down the days to when a brewery was down the street from my apartment. So true. And now I'm able to live the dream and am pleased to say that FDR did not disappoint. 

I was fortunate to attend one of their soft openings and was immediately impressed with the layout of the brewery. You can tell they put a lot of heart, soul and sweat into this place. I've met with a few of the owners and now several of the staff and it means a lot to know how passionate they are about making FDR successful and well loved by the community. It's something that Fishers was missing and I think it coming to town was the beginning of something great for the city. Fishers didn't have anything like this, so I truly believe it will be a perk for those moving here. (It's a major perk for me, anyway!)

The beer - obviously the most important thing. I love it and already have a favorite. As of today, it's their Half Cocked Pale Ale. (Take a minute to check out their website as they've done a great job of explaining each of their beer's unique names. Also highlights the reason for FDR having ITS name.) Anyhow, the half Cocked Pale Ale is delightful. I've also been a fan of their Track Jumper IPA. Mmm. So FDR has an awesome layout for their tasting room. They also have a huge area for dining (all ages welcome in this area) and an upstairs bar for those that are 21+. The rowdier crowd, if you will. ;) (Fun fact: There's one table on the second floor that overlooks the tasting room. Neat spot and you'll feel like you're a cool kid.) 

The food is quite tasty and they utilize a lot of local ingredients. I'm a huge fan of this as who doesn't enjoy local flavors? So far I've had their Classic Caesar and American Classic Cheeseburger Single. And for me, it's always going to be w/o the cheese ... but perhaps you don't care about that fact. Anyhow, it was good! The next thing I'm dying to try are the Blackened Bayou Gator Legs. Maybe it's just because I want to say I've eaten gator legs, but to be fair, I've heard they're quite scrumptious. 

Parking is a plenty. There's street parking as well as a parking garage literally on Lantern. You can't miss it. And it's free, so take advantage of that because we all know what a treat it is to have free parking. 

One amazing addition to FDR that I can't wait to check out: the outdoor patio. I've heard amazing things about it and know it'll be a treat. Love me some outdoor seating! 

So - if you haven't been here yet, I strongly encourage you to check it out. It's lovely and has quickly become one of my favorite places in Fishers. The fact that I was on cloud nine when I won a waffle tee FDR shirt really says it all.

This place is the biggest joke in Tucson.  If I could give it negative five stars, I would.  This review is based off of four years worth of experiences coming to this place (why I chose to keep coming back when my friends wanted to go here is beyond me).

The sushi is nauseatingly bad, and the beer tastes like the draught lines haven't been cleaned since the Reagan Administration. The management is terrible, a sad reality reflected in the abysmal level of service provided.  It must be a requirement to have serious attitude issues in order to work at this place.  You basically have to kidnap a waiter to get them to take your order, let lone bring you what you ordered.  

What is most annoying about this place is that they refuse to do separate checks, despite being a college bar only a few steps away from campus.  This is probably so they can add extra unlabeled items on to the bill in an attempt to rip them off, something I've caught them doing repeatedly.  

Do yourself a favor and avoid Fuku like the bubonic plague.  The faster this establishment goes out of business the better Tucson, and indeed the world, will be.

I adore Mexican food and never cease to crave things like pinto beans, flour or corn tortillas, salsas of all kinds, etc. My parents are huge fans of this place and I was so excited to head back for a return visit after a year or so. I've had a few different items over the years, but there are a few things anew to me that I think make this place shine far brighter than I had ever thought before --

First of all, what Carmelita's calls "Pico" is not what you'd expect. This stuff is pure magic. A compilation of chiles, of which the majority is poblano, onion, and cilantro. It packs a bit of a spicy whollop, but its a pain worth enduring for the flavor. It goes well on anything -- mix it into your salsa, alone on chips, tacos, you name it. It's the kind of flavor that will work with anything that hits the table. I wish they would sell this stuff by the barrelful. I'd be a happy patron. 

The other thing I must note is the Tacos al Carbon. I'm not typically one to go for steak of any kind, but they came after many recommendations from my folks. I can't say I've ever had steak more flavorful than this. The marinade and spice mixture they use on this skirt steak is heavenly in flavor. Though well done, it doesn't matter. They could serve this steak in tacos or upon a plate with rice and beans and I'd be just as happy. It hits all of the right notes on your palate and only beckons for more of the same. I absolutely love this and see why my folks order it time after time. 

Those two things alone make me a fan of Carmelita's. I seriously can't wait for another visit next time we're in town.

It was as if Homer Simpson was guest starring on Mad Men, but here I was, enjoying lunch at Butcher and Singer. 

I think, if I hadn't been with a regular B&S pro, Id have been turned aside quicker than a Giants fan at the Linc.- I kid, i kid,- they were an extremely friendly and accommodating group, from busboy to manager. Our server was as efficient and competent as she was adorable. It was a treat to be regarded so warmly. 

The decor was like being on a movie set for some fabulous movie directed by Orson Welles. Lots of marble and wood, with a charming mural of dogs, that would have been at home on both Al Bundy or Don Drapers wall. 

Im something of a burger connoisseur, and I can say with inflated authority, that B&S serves up one of the best burgers in Philly. I had heard that there was a burger special, and at under $10 , I thought it was a good deal...until I was told that the special is over and it used to be $5. That is as unreal as I can imagine for a place of its stature, who could easily charge $20 for that gem. 

The fries were just OK. I prefer them larger, but with a burger so intense, I consider them an above average garnish. 

We needed a little sweet to offset the large smack of savory, so we settled on a slice of chocolate cake. Its hard to impress a baker, even a bad one, but this was a pretty decadent slab of dessert. It only took a few bites to satisfy and it was equally as good leftover ( *cough* 45min after I got home) 

I wonder if Ill ever get the chance to go back. Based on the quality, and the relatively cheap prices, I think its a given. I think my usual lunches of the drive-thru variety just got their walking papers. This place is Homer Simpson approved!

3.5 but rounding down due to the onion.

 My sister and I both voiced our opinions at the same time (although I dont remember who stated it first). After numerous excursions that have gone by the Charcoal Pit, we both agreed that we wanted to try it.  Since its not really a convienent location to just go for us, it would take a birthday wish to see this happen.

My father takes us out for our birthday, to the restraunt of our choosing. He lives in Deleware, so a central location is usually necessary. While Charcoal Pit would geographically fit the bill, neither of us was willing to waste a birthday meal on an unknown commodity. This dance went on for years.

Enter both Yelp and the fact that I now work in DE and pass The Pit every day. Recently, I saw a few reviews on Yelp and combined with my late thursday shift at work, I decided to take the plunge alone.

The Pit was gloriously retro, from the neon sign out front, to the 50s decor. It was a little cramped and busy for Thursday at 9pm, but I was seated immediately. The menu was retro as well, and pretty sparse for what is essentially a diner. It didnt matter because I was there for a burger, so anything else on the menu was moot.

The service was good and efficient, however it was the standard diner attitude. Very robotic, no warmth or sincerity. I dont take much off for such things, im there to eat, not make a new friend, and being in the business I know the ins and outs of serving.

Ordering was simple business. You can order a Burger or Cheeseburger, 60z 0r 8oz. I was surprised that a Charcoal place, didnt offer more burger choices such as bacon or mushroom. I suppose one could order that extra but I wasnt there to buck the trend.

My burger came quickly, but not too quick. It looked divine, served with fries (after a day at the shore where all is ala carte, it was welcome to get potatoes, served in the french style). It was juicy, cooked to perfection with fresh sides.  Here is my complaint. I love onions, both fried and raw, however, when raw, a thin slice will suffice( restraunteurs, keep that mnenomic in mind). I basically got half of an onion on my burger. 

The meat and bun were tasty, yet I only remember it in the background. The onion was front and center, for hours after as well. It was really unnecessary. Hopefully, the chef was daydreaming when he sliced my onion and I recieved the anomaly as opposed to the norm. That aside, I left stuffed and satiated.

Im not big on icecream or milkshakes but apparently, its something CP does well. I left satisfied, with breath that smelled like an italian cutting board. I had beat my sister to the punch and tried the Charcoal Pit. The build-up in my mind, may have something to do with my disappointment. Things rarely live up to the mythical proportions that ones mind creates. But at least I can say to my sister, ' FIRST!"

Yelpers Note:  I dont think anyone has mentioned this but the Charcoal Pit has many locations in Deleware and is founded by the Capano family...of the deleware Capanos....which produced the scion Thomas Capano...who murdered Anne Marie Fahey...and disposed of the body with the help of his family.....yep that Capano family.

Now I dont let the political and social problems of a few bad seeds get between a good burger and my mouth, but aparently it is responsible for the decline in business over the last few years , as explained to me by a Delewarian co-worker.

Funny Story.................

 Because of Yelp, I had seen and heard much about Zwahlens, and was eager to try it. As it turned out, I had business today, up in the KOP area. It was a beautiful sunny summer day and I thought it would be a good opportunity to check out Zwahlens, which I knew was nearby.

While I knew it was nearby, I didnt know exactly where, so I consulted my trusty GPS companion, Chewie, as to its exact location. Maybe its the funny name, maybe I was spelling it wrong, but nothing was coming up. I then searched icecream and still no dice. I knew it was in the Trooper/Audubon area so I decided to go into the heart of the area, and see if things changed. 

I parked in a shopping center in Audubon and tried again...still no dice. I was getting angry at Chewie ( he also wouldnt tell me if there was a Sonic nearby). It was our first fight. I had my Ipod touch with me, with its internet access, I could get the address and go from there. I only needed  a WI-FI connection. I found out that both Starbucks and McDonalds, which crow about Wi-Fi on their doors, charge for their Wi-Fi hookups...Bastards! As if they dont rake in enough money.

So here I am, driving around the shopping center, holding my Ipod to see if it picks up any Wi-Fi. I parked somewhere to beat the crap out of my stubborn GPS, when I looked up and saw I was parked directly in front of Zwahlens!!!

 Chewie looked at me as if to say, " Shut Up! I got you here didnt I?" I dont know how initially, I was able to miss what looked like an Alpine lodge in the middle of a suburban strip mall. Seeing it brought back memories of living in Germany. Once inside, I was hit by the super sweet aroma, that filled the place.  I cant imagine how anyone who works there escapes Diabetes.

 Much like the outside, the inside decor is spot on in its depiction of an Alpine restraunt. From the Family Tree on the wall, to the chairs and benches, I was having flashbacks to when I lived in Germany and had to psyche myself up and practice what I would say in German to order.

I was mainly interested to try their hand made icecream. Im a Vanilla man, but was interested to see what special flavor they had (It was Blackberry crunch). Didnt intrigue me enough to try it and I got a Vanilla cone. It was $3, plus I tipped, because when in the Alps....

I have to say, I wasnt blown away by it (thus falling short of 5 star status). Maybe I expected too much. It was definitely as good an icecream as id had, and it hit the spot on the warm day. I probably wouldnt recommend a special trip out here, but if you are in the area, its definitely worth checking out.

Id love to try their other wares, and even tackle some of the special sundaes they offered.  Now that I know where it is, Ill be back. No thanks to Chewie.

My 2 word review:  Der Hooters (please imagine umlauts over the "oo" as my smart phone cant perform that function)


And now my multi word review.

I've spent a good deal of time in Deutschland. There was my time actually living in Germany, and my time married to a German Frau. I like to think I know my German food, but the fact is, I probably wouldn't know popular authentic German cuisine if it was wearing a black turtleneck and mocking my genitals.

The reason for this is simple. I was sheltered in my German experiences. I spent all of my time with my inlaws at home and rarely ventured out to restraunts. We also didn't live in Bavaria, which is what people imagine when thinking about all things German. It would be like a foreigner, basing America as a whole, based on a trip to NYC.

All this being said, much of what Brauhaus Schmitz has to offer, conjured up pleasant memories of my time in the Mutterland.

In the middle of the quirk parade, that is South Street, there is the wooden arched doorway that is Brauhaus Schmitz. It's German sensibility almost seems out of place in the wild South Street vibe, yet it works. Set up as a kind of biergarten, Schmitz captures the Bavarian spirit, of which I am only a distant acquaintance. 

As European beers go, this place is a paradise of Teutonic proportions. You want to try them all, but the alcoholic contents of these quaffs, force you to hit the breaks. After 3 good sized brews, I was feeling loopy, the inner Griswald  rising to the surface.

I can say with some authority, that the food choices at Brauhaus, represent the majority of German foods, I have come to love. When dating my wife back in the early 90s, I had always been looking for a place like this, to stave off her homesickness ( and to stop the complaining about there being no good German food in Philly.)

Each thing I sampled at Brauhaus, transported me back to Oma's Sunday dinner, in a way that memories and photographs can't.

I'll only give short schrift to the extra bonus of BS, that is the outfits that the waitresses wore. It was certainly a sight(s) to behold.

While the Brauhaus Schmitz virtual Bavaria experience can certainly do a number on your bank account, I feel it is worth it.  They do a fantastic job of bringing Germany to you, and in my case, bringing me back to Germany. Prost indeed.

Federal Donuts, where the donuts and chicken are hot and the staff is hotter.

All of the forces of chaos combined, have kept me from trying out the best new eatery in Philly but recently, they became confused on the way to my house and I was able to slip through, like just about any Running Back through the Eagles soft defense.

I had heard the horror stories, of how the clamoring masses have stacked body upon body, in their attempts at getting themselves a shiny donut or chicken part. I'm not good in crowds so I tried to time my arrival accordingly(around 10:30am). SUBURBAN COMMUTER NOTE: I parked on the far side of Washington, thinking there would be no space available, but upon my trek over, noticed ample spots, just a block away.

Upon my arrival, there was already a small group present. Those last vestiges of the morning rush combined with the early chicken go getters and I , in my arrogance, considered myself an equal member of both camps. I immediately took in the familiar and inviting faces of Blake and Felicia. They were busy but I couldn't help but think that they considered this their " down time". 

Here's the part of every one of my reviews, where I make an ass of myself. I was invited to take a seat at the counter. When I got there, there was counter space but no seat. I stood (happily) and watched the goings on. After a few minutes, Felicia came out to gently explain to me that the stools pull out and she" pulled out my stool " (sorry). You'd think someone who grew up with transformers would have figured it out, but ill blame the fact that I had been up since 4am.

Once properly seated, I was able to enjoy the best coffee and donuts the city (world) has to offer. I advise anyone to skip their usual cream and sugar and experience the flavor of that coffee raw. really good stuff. Granted, I was a little late to get the donuts fresh from the fryer, but damn, were they still the best I'd had and as a baker, Ive eaten cake donuts right out of the fryer before.

I may have missed the hot donuts but my arrival meant I was one of the first to get a golden ticket for chicken. I was also lucky enough to have an eating companion there, who offered a mix and match scenario with the chicken so I was able to try both the Chili Garlic and the other (whose name I forget but it was the dry rub one). Both rocked my world and were just as good leftover later that night.

In my time at FD, I witnessed a staff that was  amazing. Blake was a fountain of donutcoffeechicken information, Felicia was the perfect "face" of the Front of the house and the BOH staff were a grim lesson in startling efficiency and ingenuity. The magic that they work in that small space was impressive. Unfortunately, there was a computer malfunction, that threatened to bring down the store's mojo. Skynet is truly taking over. Yet I watched these heroes, power through the hurdle like pros as the patient masses accepted the situation with quiet reverence, knowing that they have a good thing going here and to complain would kill it.

I will cop to being a personal friend to a few of the staff here, but that should take nothing away from my great experience. There's a simplicity to Federal Donuts that will keep this endeavor afloat for as long as it wants to be. I propose to all national sports coverage, that henceforth, you can quit the cloying shots of louts making cheesesteaks in your cutaway shots and get a camera in FD, to show the real working class spirit of Philadelphia and foods that are actually appetizing. If only they could fit a camera in there....

This is one of the few times in my life when I was comfortable being in the doghouse.

Located on the busy business area of the Concord area, I had seen Johnnies often on my morning commute. I took the opportunity of  a half-day to check it out. It reminded me of 5 Guys in a lot of ways, from the decor, to the ordering style and the many articles about the place plastered to the walls.

It was through these articles, that I recognized the owner, who was manning the register. He was friendly and informative, able to talk about all things, from hotdogs to real estate. He treated his patrons as friends and was sincere in his approach. Johnnies offers a special called the Deleware Destroyer which is 2 hotdogs on a hoagie roll topped with mac and cheese, saurkraut and anything else you can think of. If you order it, you can get your picture on the wall (you dont even have to finish it!) and the owner, took the time to point out the wall and tell some related anecdotes.

There were some great options of Dog, different styles from different areas. I got the Texas Tommy (bacon wrapped with wiz) and the NYer ( kraut with brown mustard) . Those 2 along with fries and a drink cost about $11 (also reminiscant of 5 guys, its almost exactly what their burger fries combo costs). Its more than I want to spend on hotdogs, but Ill say 2 things in Johnnies defense. 
                   1. My eyes were bigger than my stomach. I was hungry so I got 2 dogs and fries. 1 dog or no fries would have sufficed. I couldnt even finish the 2nd dog.
                   2. The product is worth it. It was as good a dog as Id had outside of home grilling.

 Note that I didnt get the Deleware Destroyer. It seemed too much, even in my hungered state. I was however entertained watching 2 aged hippies (who I dubbed Ben and Jerry) get smacked down by it. They started out all excited, high fiving , ready for their close up. By the time the camera came out to chronicle their trip to the wall of fame, they looked like a couple of prison newbies, owned by another kind of hotdog.

So im putting Johnnies in 5 guys status. Above average fast food, meant for the occasional treat. I feel welcome to come back. There were so many topping options and areas i havent visited ( boston, chicago) as well as onion rings, mac and cheese and milkshakes. It will be awhile till Johnnies is boring to me. Maybe someday Ill see just how bad to the bone I am and try that Destroyer. I havent been owned in awhile.

Now that Aaron is gone, I feel it's safe to finally do my Ikea review, without getting a swastika carved into my forehead ala Inglorius Basterds. 

I think its notable, that there are a limited amount of Ikeas in the country and the world, and we here in the Philly area have 2! I recently went to the Philly location with a friend , but I usually go to the Conshy location...a fact that I must have brought up a number of times during my visit, to which my companion appropriately mocked me for. Really though, once you are in the Land of Ikea, the outside surroundings bear no effect on your experience. 

I needed some things for my new home, and my friend needed some things for her apartment so once I made sure she had her passport and the appropriate papers, we ventured to the store for college kids and divorced dads. 

She was a newbie here, so I helped guide her through the twisted maze that is Ikea.This was the first time Id been back in awhile. Early on when my marriage first imploded, I wanted to meet with a friend to vent and get advice. He suggested meeting at the cafeteria at Ikea, as it was a central location for both of us, and quite frankly, he was a fan of Swedish meatballs. This turned out to be a mistake. Anyone going through a separation or divorce, should stay clear of furniture stores. I full of happy couples, optimistically starting their lives, picking out furniture, happy in love....and I wanted to shoot them all. 

Time , however, heals most wounds, so here I was back at Ikea. The murderous feelings had passed and I felt more pity, for these clueless couples , picking out furniture that they may one day have to chop in half with an axe. (woah! bitter much?) 

Ikea is actually a fun place to come, even if you don't really need anything. The maze, the little room displays, the toys, even the food is decent. I have absolutely no taste when is comes to these things. I like their simplistic wares. And the fact that they have funny names is a plus. Who wouldn't want a bookcase named Billy? 

We filled our night wandering, speculating, eating meatballs, and even found a few items to buy. Upon exiting, we were met with a torrential, biblical downpour, and I wondered if Aaron wasn't right and we were being punished by God for our support of the false God Thor. The rains, however, died down and we were spared being smited with a watery death. 

But enough of my yakkin, Ill let Jonathan Coulton give the essential Ikea Review. There need be no other review after this http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d0oo9SitPWk

I have my reasons, for never having tried Indian food. The 2 words that would best describe it , are " Stubborness" and " Curry". My pickiness is legendary, and I credit Yelp with breaking alot of my culinary prejudices. Era, Han Dynasty, Zot and now New Delhi, have broadened my edible horizons. 

Of course in this case, I credit Blake, for forcing me to break my Indian food cherry. It was her Indian food UYE, where she called me out specifically, that introduced me to the world of Naan bread and Tandoori chicken. 

Vishnu must have really wanted me to eat Indian food. As it turned out, I had my kids on the night of the UYE and would have to miss the event. I had settled in, to a night of Funniest home videos and board games, disappointing both myself and others, who had wanted to see me get smacked down by ND's buffet. However, Karma was on my side and the class my wife takes on Wed was cut short. She showed up a little before 7,and I rushed to make it to ND on time for the event. 

Luckily, it was in a part of the city I knew well, as my therapist's office is across the street. This was ideal, in the possible scenario that the scary foreign food would make me need to get some mental help in a hurry, I would just need to crawl across the street. 

As it turned out, there was no need. Between the great company and tasty food, I was mentally set, for at least a week. New Delhi is a cozy little restraunt, with a delicious looking spread of Indian food. After communing with some Yelpers, old and new, Blake was kind enough to be my guide at the Buffet and thank Shiva for that! She explained what each thing was and made great suggestions. 

I tried a little of everything and deemed the Naan bread and Tandoori chicken my favorites. I would need another visit to get a better idea of some of the other entrees, and I'm sure it will happen in the near future. There was even a bar there, although I didn't partake...this time. 

We also had a blast with the desserts. Its amazing how much mileage a good "balls" joke will get, with a bunch of supposed adults. However I did not get the Balls dessert, no matter how much Aaron begged me. I tried the Pistachio ice cream, which had a name that sounded like coffee. As a matter of fact, I thought I was ordering coffee until they placed the dish of tan ice cream in front of me. My embarrassment turned to joy, as the frozen treat was awesome. 

Upon leaving, I felt like I had such a good experience, that I thought I would walk across the street and cancel all future therapy sessions. It was only when Aaron forced me to ride him piggyback across 41st street that I realized I actually needed to double the appointments...and I'm sure the homeless guy, and everyone else who witnessed it felt the same way.

Drum Roll Please........

And the winner of Jim H's best cheesesteak goes to ...Docs Deli!

Actually forget about the drum roll and make it a Liscios  roll. 

I was first introduced to Docs about 6 years ago when I worked in the area. Not sure why I didn't get around to writing a review but I felt pretty strongly about it back then as well. I have since been transferred out of the area and an now back and one of my first questions was, "Is Docs still good?"

It is. It's as good as I remembered. It is without a doubt the best proportioned (meat/onions/cheese to bread ratio) best seasoned (they salt the meat but don't over sodium) best bread ( Liscios is up among the Giants for me) of any cheesesteak I've tried in a 100 mile radius. 

Another plus is the price. For $10 you can get a 24" cheesesteak the size of your extended arm. There's no way you could eat a cheesesteak that size in one sitting so find a friend to share. 

I can't say enough good things about this place. The service is always stellar. It's just a pickup shop so no parking or seating. You can usually just street park out front on this moderately busy side street. 

Do yourself a favor and get yourself to this hidden Delco Gem and see what I'm talking about.

Maybe I was bored. Maybe it was the fact that its been so hot lately. 
Maybe it was because it was 7pm and my kids were still in their pajamas. Either way, I insisted that we all go out to get some ice cream at Handels. 
Ive also been dying to take someone , anyone! , here since I came earlier in the summer. Anytime you have a fantastic culinary experience, its always great to go back, and see if it was a fluke. 

I'm happy to report that the ice cream was actually better than I remembered it. Handels has ruined me to any other ice cream. Its so refreshing and delicious. You don't get that sticky, thirsty feeling afterwards, that you get from most other ice cream. 

Yes, lines are long but you need that time to figure out which flavor and style you want...and then change your mind...multiple times...before making a game time decision at the window.
