Were it not for some word of mouth from trusted friends, I'd have never tried this South Philly gem. They are only open for breakfast and lunch, which is fine by me as they are my 2 favorite meals of the day. 

It's a small, clean and welcoming establishment. The host/server is friendly, helpful and engaging. The menu is split up into Breakfast and Lunch and I assure you, you will find a number of items that are unique, that you will want to come back again to try. I almost wished I was more into sweet breakfast fare because some of the options looked fantastic. 

I was somewhat overwhelmed by the choices until someone pointed out that the special was a meatloaf sandwich with egg. Amazing. It rivals Paesanos in its decadence. The meatloaf was about as flavorful as it gets. Add to that, cheese, a fried egg and a latke-like hash brown and you have an idea how good it was. There was a seasoning in the sandwich that I can't pinpoint, but it lingers with me ( in a good way) even as I write this a few hours removed. 

Overall, this was as good a breakfast experience as you could ask for. Delco people, who are fans of the famous Hungry A will love it. It was also a nice touch watching History of the World Part 1 as I ate and chatting with one of the owners.

I never thought Id say this but Im burgered out!

I was instructed to come here by my GPS Navigator, Chewy. We had spent the day in the Main Line woods and were hungry like a wolf. When my kids are involved, I always look for diners because the menu usually suits all involved. I have been aware of Rubys for quite some time but never really wanted to go. The whole retro burger joint concept doesnt do anything for me. I hate paying for the decor as well as the food.

 But again, my pal Chewy told me this was the best choice in the area and I always listen to my electronic devices. (like once, when my camera told me to take the picture of the MILF bending over). As many others have alluded to in reviews of this area, I dislike the Main Line, Suburban Square, Porche driving socialites. I make it a point to avoid this area at all costs. Luckily, this was a holiday weekend and most of them can afford to go away, so the crowd was sparse.

 We were one of only a few patrons on this humid Sunday evening. As stated earlier, the decor is retro 50s, all employees are dressed in the style of the day (even the cooks, whose kitchen was open to the viewing public). Service was fast and somewhat friendly. I guess I would be a little jaded too , if forced to wear such ridiculous outfits. I liked the Train set rounding the store, and giggled when imagining it falling on a 3 yr old Ben B (see his review).

 I know they are known for their burgers, but id had so many lately, I was looking for something different. This changed when I saw the menu insert for their new, Bleu Sliders. It was 3 mini sliders, with a bleu cheese topping (actual bleu cheese, not the dressing) and an onion ring. I had to have this in my life! My kids were boring and each got chicken fingers. Luckily, my picky son raved about how good his was. I dont care what they get, as long as they eat it and are happy doing it.
 My burgers were as good as they looked. Tasty toppings and the burger itself was a treat as well. The fries were just ok. Hard shoestring fries that had no particular flair.

 The bill total for the 4 of us was $40 (no apps no dessert) This is a little more than I expect to pay at a diner, and cant help but feel like I was paying for all the staff to be dressed like Back to the Future extras.

 Just some notes about Rubys.

  - We absolutely loved their kids menus. It is a sheet of cardboard that (with instructions) they can fold into an airplane and are given stickers to decorate it. I have never seen anything like it, and wonder how much extra this costs to them. Matts and crayons are getting sooooo old.  All places should look into this.

- They are known for their milkshakes, but we arent a milkshake family, so we didnt partake. SPOILER ALERT!!!!!!  We were seated near the milkshake station and I noticed they didnt use real icecream, but instead used icecream in a carton, like ive used at bars to make mudslides and such. Not necessarily a dig but Im just sayin......

  To sum up. Im putting this in the win column for Chewy. It was definitely a positive experience for all involved. While I paid a little more than I would have liked, there was plenty involved that I feel was worth the money. I need a trial separation from burgers though. Thank God tomorrow is Memorial day, where I can have a nice home cooked meal of.....uh...burgers and dogs. Jeez I should have thought this through a little better.

I'm almost ashamed to admit, as a proud Philadelphian, that the Italian Market is one of the Philly Institutions, that I hadn't ever stepped foot in. This, despite the many praises it has received across the board , from personal friends to professional critics ( and Rocky).  No single spot in the IM had caught my eye more than Paesanos has. The very name pops up on Yelp frequently as a sandwich Mecca and I had taken more than a passing interest in seeking it out.

Yet often, procrastination gets the better if me and I wind up putting things off indefinitely ( a box full of old pictures just nodded in stern agreement as I wrote that). This most likely would have been my fate in meeting The Arista( roast pork & broccoli rabe) if it weren't for a drunken stumble to my car on a Saturday night.

It was a night of particularly bacchanalian revelry and a friend and I took advantage of the crisp fall air to sober up. Even in his inebriated state, as we passed 9th and Christian, he had a moment of clarity where he stopped, and told me I had to try a sandwich here and it had to be the Arista. The fact that this topped the list of  places I had already wanted to go, cemented the fact that I would go the next chance I was able.

This chance occurred today. I found brilliant parking around 8th and Washington in one of the few free municipal lots in the city.  When I arrived around noon on a Wednesday, there wasn't another soul in the place. Good for me, bad for others. I ordered my Arista ( despite being swayed by some other great choices) and it was weighing down a plastic bag within minutes. They have seating there but I opted for the solitary experience of eating it at home ( or in this case, in my car because I couldn't wait).

I took the scenic route back to my car and it dawned on me that I would be making many more trips to the Italian Market, not only to go back and try the other awesome sandwiches at Paesanos, but a number of other spots along 9th Street. This is going to be a weekly excursion.

So as I alluded to earlier, I got in my car and the smell of the roast pork, broccoli, and sharp provolone immediately filled the car. I had to take a bite. It was a monster sandwich  and definitely called for a bib or full body condom. I think the Arista is dipped in pork fat before it's wrapped up. This may have been the best sandwich I've ever tasted ( with apologies to my beloved A Cut Above). I ate half of it in the front seat to the sweet sounds of sports radio.

As I made my way home, my senses were all tingling. The smell in the car, the taste still in my face, the constant glances at the half that still lived, the sounds of my body trying to process this masterpiece. Needless to say, the poor arista didn't live much longer once I arrived home. Anyone who has ever had one knows that trying to consume the whole thing in one day, is a bad idea. One could easily get 2 days of lunch out of one of those bad boys. However, I plead insanity. I just couldn't stop myself.

So thank you to Yelp and everyone else, who pointed me towards Paesanos. As far as my relationship with The Italian Market, better late than never. If they can forgive me for waiting so long , I can forgive them for.... Well, nothing yet but the more I go I'm sure I'll figure something out.

When contemplating a pregame spot for the Yelp 10th bash, I was glad when some good friends invited me to meet at black sheep for a number of reasons.

First it was spending time with good friends instead of drinking alone like an asshole. Second, in order to keep my elite status, I need to review things and in order to review things, I actually have to go somewhere, otherwise I'm reviewing another damn McDonalds. 

Lastly, since I never go out, eating out is a treat I relish and Black Sheep didn't disappoint. I had a happy hour Guinness and 2 of their $5 apps ( wings and cheesesteak spring rolls). Both were out of this world. I'd go so far as to say that the wings rivaled the best I've ever had. 

So mark Black Sheep as a new go to pub in Philly. They had me at $5.

This isn't the first time I've tried something based on a popular rap song. I once ordered a Brass Monkey at a bar and was disappointed at how ungangster it was. It was just a screwdriver with rum! Gin and juice didn't fare much better so I entered Pizza Beddia with a touch of trepidation. 

PB doesn't open til 530 and it doesn't have a phone so get there early. I arrived at 5:31 and was told my pizza would be ready at 6:15. Far from being annoyed by this, I was thinking that this was bound to be great. 

My last experience with out of this world Pizza was at Difaras in Brooklyn. Just 2 guys painstakingly crafting the perfect pie that will not be rushed. If Difaras redefined pizza for me, Beddia has reinforced it. 

I ordered a regular pie and an angry pie. We ate there, standing at one of the 2 tables they have. The pizza was perfect . Thin, almost burned crispy crust, wonderful cheese sauce and spices. It could be very easy to eat a $20 pie in one sitting by yourself . As it was, 3 of us were able to demolish 2 pies with ease. However the angry pie, which is deceptively spicy, was a bit more slow going due to its increasing heat. 

So on the gangsta rap scale, this one hits Tupac level. It's so inspiring that I feel the need to start a little East Coast/ West Coast rap battle with Brad P. * Cue Sanford and Son Theme*

Pizza Beddia
It'll knock you on your ass
We all see ya
Other pizza has no class

Ok I'm done.

in some of my more spiritual moments, I imagine Heaven to make even your best day on Earth pale in comparison. Something akin to running underwater, laden by weights and suddenly the weights come off and you can run free on land. Until Sycamore, the closest I had come to this, was when I finally decided to see an eye doctor to get glasses. I couldnt believe the clarity that came with getting new glasses. movies and TV were so sharp. Driving was no longer fearful .


Sycamore did for food, what the correct glasses did for me for my eyesight. I was perfectly content at places like Olive Garden and Ruby Tuesday (hell, im content at Wendys). I looked forward to the special treats, provided by the chain restraunts, on special occasions. 38th birthday? Its Chicken and Gnocci soup and all I can eat breaaaaaaaad stiiiiicks mother f***ers!

Yelps own Sam L runs Sycamore. He is a friend and an all around good egg. This fact does not make him a good chef or restraunteur. No. Its insane culinary talent and skills, that make him one of the best chefs in Philly and puts Sycamore as one of the best dining spots west of the Deleware River (maybe east as well).  What credentials do I have, to make such a claim? How bout over 40 hours watching Food Network a week? Hows that grab you? How bout cause Im fat. Do anything for you?

All kidding aside, I came here with a small group of friends, after realizing that its been too long since Sam took over, that I tried the place. Its a charming little spot, in a part of Delco with alot of character. 

I was prepared to put all (most) of my pickiness and preferences aside to get the full culinary experience. We started with a spoonful of a potato soup like liquid topped with a crispy peice of bacon. It could have been dishwater and the bacon would have made it taste good, the fact that the liquid was delicious was goosebump inducing.

 We ordered the 7 cheese plate for an appetizer. It was just chock full of tastiness and hit the spot exactly like an appetizer should.

For my meal, I debated between the small plate of Italian Sausage mac and cheese or the entree of short ribs over mash. This was a special occasion for me, so I went for the short ribs. Luckily, my tablemate ordered the mac, and I was able to try it. I say luckily, even though as I tasted the deliciousness of it, I thought I had made a mistake in passing it over, but at least I had something to pine for until my next visit. Hey Mac and cheese debate thread! The search ends at Sycamore.

The entree came, and I hoped it tasted half as good as the presentation. Actually, words cant describe, how good it actually was. It melted in your mouth. There were things garnishing the meat and potato, which the lout and me said were french fries, however I was told they were parsnips. Im not sure ive ever eaten a parsnip in my life, but I now count myself as a fan. i believe i was in another world, for those few moments  that the entree was in front of me. It seemed like my tablemates were in the same boat, we all had a few minutes that we cant remember after our plates were put in front of us.

After the meal, when the deserts were read to us, we simply said yes. Thats right, we tried them all. Trying to say which one is the best, is like trying to say which of your kids is your favorite, so I wont dare try.

This was truly the most perfect combination of food company and atmosphere ive ever experienced. Of course, Sam came out to chat with us, ask us how our meal and experience was. He is our friend after all. It would be no surprise at all, to know that The experience and food we had, was no different than what patrons, who werent his friend had. We witnessed Sam chatting with all the tables in the restraunt. I got the feeling that this is what it was like in the old days, good place, good ingredients, ...community. Its  crazy how a good food experience can enhance  your overall existence.  Will I even be able to go back to Olive Garden? Will it now be considered slumming. I will definitely return to Sycamore, friend of Sam or not. And if someone asks the question, " Is this Heaven?" The answer is, " No, its Sycamore."

This review is as much for the UYE ARSE event as it is for the establishment. Honestly, I'm comfortable with my boring eating habits. Lately however, Ive been forced out of my culinary comfort zone. I often feel like the grumpy guy from "Green Eggs and Ham" (did he have a name? Was it Jim?) 
I will not eat Tripe and Pig Intestines 
I will not eat them in a car 
I will not eat them on a bar. 
I will not eat them piled high with amazingly hot chile peppers. 

I came to Han Dynasty with some great people, with the intention of trying some new things and burning my face off at the same time. Han's is in an unassuming strip mall. Its often been said about UYE's, that the quality of the company is so great, that the location is inconsequential. I would usually agree but in this case, Han Dynasty (and more specifically, Han himself) was like the 10th guest and intergal to the fun of the evening. 

Hans has a very cool and inviting decor and we were set up right in the middle of the action. We had a very funny and entertaining server, who I later found out was the owner, Han, himself. His level of humor and honesty is unmatched. When jokingly asked by one of us, how the General Tso Chicken is, he replied, " Its Shit!" He definitely encouraged us and( by the segmented Authentic/ Americanized menu) others to steer clear of the normal Chinese food staples and try authentic Chinese cuisine. 

Our group, was full of knowledgeable, worldly people and it enhanced the whole experience. Between the conversation, and the food I was overwhelmed. They made it easy for me to try things and my God! there was alot to try. Steaming plates of spicy goodness, fantastic wine, sweat inducing pallate spankers. Everyone left stuffed. 

I love how there was a menu insert, which told you the specials, as well as the Top Ten most popular entrees of the month. I could almost hear Casey Kasem reading them off to me. ..... 

" And now, at #5 dedicating this to his one legged cat, Tea smoked Duck!" 

It was through this list that I made my choice of entree, Double fried Beef strips (3 chile rating out of 4!) It was awesome and widely considered a good choice. Owwwww! I just injured my arm patting myself on the back. It was just as good the next day, while I sat in my car on my lunch break at work. It was also somehow hotter the next day as I also sat in my car contemplating guzzling antifreeze to offset the heat. 

As stated earlier, we left Hans, entertained, stuffed and ready for round 2 at a date to be named later.I had been debating going but once again, I was glad that I overcame my initial fears of trying new things. Ill leave you with some observations of the event. 

- The women who showed up, (including Aaron) were stunning in both appearance and charm. 

- I haven't had such good wine in ages. Between Caroline's husband's homemade white and the Francis Ford Coppola Red (better than Godfather 3 -not as good as The Outsiders) there couldn't have been a better accompaniment to the meal. 

- Han was amazing and we were honored to get the VIP treatment from him. He was like the Asian Chris Rock, cracking us up with his "blue" material. My favorite , was his idea of "different" fortune cookies. The only one that is printable was " That wasn't Chicken, you just ate" 

- Its funny to watch beads of sweat, form on bald guys heads. 

- I feel truly sorry for those that didn't attend. Dont make the same mistake in the future.

We've been going to 3 Daughters for over a year now and it just gets better and better! It's a great place to hangout with friends or family (definitely a low-key and relaxed environment) and grab a couple drinks. It's not smoky or too loud, just perfect!

I'm not really a beer drinker but I LOVE going, which I think is saying a lot! What really sets them apart is their indoor/outdoor environment that's chock full of great games. Plus, I've noticed recently they've added a lot more beers for the beer-intolerant like myself. For instance some of their darker varieties are almost like a fine wine or have notes of whiskey so it feels like a mixed drink. Not to mention their light and dry key lime cider I just tried. It was so gulp-able! 

Looking for foosball, shuffleboard, darts, board games? I could go on and on because they have everything. They even bring in some great bands for live music and some food trucks. Go check it out!

My boyfriend is dairy free and I'm always down for dessert, so we stopped in late at night for a scoop. Turns out they were out of pretty much everything except for one flavor: Golden Hippie Juice. Seems like there's a huge demand in DTSP for this sort of thing. 

Although the flavor was a little crazy (mostly turmeric and other spices) we couldn't leave without trying out this new business. 

The scoop was so rich and flavorful that we split it and were both satisfied. I'm also quite sure it had CBD oil (a few of their flavors do) which I think is a great benefit! It was like getting dessert and vitamins in one fell scoop. 

While we're not sure we'd try the SAME flavor again, we're looking forward to going back when they've made some more. Who could fault them for being so cool that they can't keep the freezer stocked?

Just came here for the grand opening on Thursday, and it was amazing! Nashville has been in long need of a jazz club, and Rudy's exceeded my expectations as its first. This new venue in SoBro is super swanky and intimate with a early 20th century speakeasy vibe. Although there's no official dress code, you'll probably feel underdressed if you wear a t-shirt and jeans. The drinks are also pricey, but well worth it. All the house cocktails are $12, but the one I got had two generous pours of liquor in it, so I may as well have bought 2 1/2 drinks for $12, which isn't that bad when you think about it. I haven't tried the food yet, but I saw the menu, and it looks delicious and well suited for the venue. It's all creole and Cajun, perfect for a jazz club.

Which brings me to my favorite part--the music! When you first walk in, it's unmistakable that this is a jazz club. There are photos and posters of vintage jazz musicians all over the stone walls, and when there isn't live music playing, there's always jazz playing over the speakers. I've only been once so far, but last Thursday, there were two awesome swing bands, perfect for dancing--The Anna Arata Vintet and the Moonshine Rhythm Club. Bring your dance shoes because the dance floor is lovely! At least it is now that it's new, and nobody has spilled their sticky drinks all over it. That said, the dance floor isn't huge, so make sure you practice floorcraft, and don't get too tipsy if you plan on swinging out!

Thursday nights are $10 live swing nights with live swing music, hosted by Shindig Mafia, so I'm sure this is the best night to come, but I hope to go other nights too, to hear what other kinds of jazz is played there.

While there's no official parking lot for Rudy's, there's plenty of street parking, and there are a few offices next door that are free to park at at night. You can even pay $2 for valet parking if you prefer.

Definitely five stars from me. This has quickly and easily become my favorite bar/club/music venue in Nashville.

Honestly I was disgusted by food and service

First off a little back story, I live in the neighborhood and always love to try new local places. Pizza is one of my favorite foods and so I was eager to try out Falora. 

When we arrived, there were five people In the restaurant. We were seated by a very nice waitress. Everything was going well until my salad came. The waitress informed me that I could not get it with dressing on the side because it was pre mixed(YUCK). The croutons tasted like gummy bears, they were so stale. 

Next came the pizza. I ordered a pizza that said it had mozzarella on it. When the pizza came, it had no cheese on it, no oil, no salt, no nothing. Just crust and vegetables. I am nota big salt person but it really could have helped. When I asked the surly waiter/manager about the cheese, he responded by saying, oh we put very light cheese and proceeded to dissect my pizza. He then pointed to a piece of wet dough and said "there is it." I was really disappointed and upset that I had to pay 14 dollars for this pizza that wasn't completed. 

Hope that they can improve for others sake.

Wow! I can't believe I waited so long to come here- this place is off the chain! The decor was great, with license plates all around, Merle Haggard playing, and it all made you feel right at home. The workers were all very friendly and helpful, and we got some great recommendations from them and some of the other customers. We got 2 double-wides (you get 3 meats, 2 sides, and oversized hush puppies) and it was more than enough to feed our crew! Everything tasted phenomenal. Be sure to get a bunch of their sweet and smoky sauce!

I have no idea what's going on with all the negative ratings here but Gray's is way better than all these reviews let on. 

I don't have a lot of experience with the food here but I can tell you that the drink program alone is worth 4 stars easily. This place is a serious craft cocktail establishment. Maybe the people in Franklin aren't ready for that yet but Gray's is doing things with cocktails that you will have a hard time finding in even larger markets like NYC or Chicago. 

Two of the highlights are French press cocktails and an extensive list of Brandy based drinks. The French press cocktails are brought out to the customer's table in a French press, allowed to steep, and then preparation is finished off at the table. I've traveled through a lot of the best cocktails bars in the nation and I think I have seen it maybe once if at all so it's a rather rare concept. 

As for the Brandy drinks... I'm a whiskey forward guy through and through but even I can get on board with the cocktails here. I recognized a few of them to be very similar to classic cocktails but with a Brandy slant so if you have some favorite classics there is probably a drink here that you will like. The Brandy theme is a nod to the age of the building back in a time in the mid 1800's when Brandy based drinks were much more predominant than whiskey or rye. In a city that prides itself on history and old stuff as much as Franklin does, it's a fitting throwback. 

So as you can see, what this place is doing with drinks is very different and well thought out. It should be applauded since it's not just another clone craft cocktail house serving old fashioneds by guys in 20's style hats and suspenders. It's really pushing boundaries and the quality is every bit up to par with what you'll find at even the best cocktail bars around.

Bacio is my favorite restaurant in the Mt. Airy/ Germantown/ Chestnut Hill area. It is the perfect little neighborhood BYOB. Everything I have ever ordered off the menu has been wonderful but recently I have been almost exclusively ordering their specials- there's usually a bunch of them and they are always fantastic. My favorite recent order has been the Pumpkin soup, and my boyfriend swears by a mushroom/ gorgonzola/ teriyaki appetizer. 

If it is not too crowded the service is fantastic, but if it is crowded you have to be a little patient, which is why you should always bring a bottle or 2 of wine. It really is the kind of place you want to go to when you don't have anywhere to be afterward because the meals can sometimes take a little bit longer to come out... but the wait between the appetizers and entrees is really what makes the meal a special experience, you never feel rushed and you have time to savor the appetizer and build up anticipation for the main course.

Once you try it once, you will keep coming back. It has become my go-to place for special occasions like birthdays, but it is also a very special treat on any ordinary day. I love going there with a bottle of wine after a long day at work. Enjoy!

Lured by the idea of limitless steak fries, I asked for the burger with mushrooms and wanted provolone with it. The server said most burgers were cooked as medium, with a bit of pink on it, unless requested otherwise. Sounded perfect.  Burger arrived with a small serving of the steak fries, lightly done (also my personal request).  Fries were quite good, not overly salty and done the way I requested. The burger was another story. Hard as a hockey puck on the outside with one side clearly blackened.  I waited for awhile to get the server's attention regarding the burger. When I pointed how overcooked the burger was, she just shrugged and said, "I'll let the kitchen know." No offer to get another one made - silly me - I just assumed she was going to do it.

Another few minutes pass but I'M HUNGRY, so I ate half of the burger in front of me, but no other burger ever made its way to my table. I finally asked for the manager, who clearly agreed that the burger was overdone and apologetic. It was just too late to take her up on her offer to have another burger made for me, so she very nicely comped the meal - that's the only reason I'm giving this place anything other than one star.

This is a review for the spa only. I was curious how it differed from the Peppermill's spa. Both were very good and each offered something the other didn't. Highlights here:

Very luxe feeling.

Lovely, gentle staff (Jordan did my salt scrub and she was delightful)

Tea room inside ladies area was small - only seats for 5

Bit convoluted to get to the different areas; i.e. from the dressing room you have to go through reception to get to the pools

Ask for a local's discount - worth 15%. Total cost for the salt scrub with a generous tip and with the locals discount was about $100.

You can order food for delivery at the inside pool (wait can be long - an hour, in our case)

Kids were in the inside pool - a bit noisy and splashy

Only got to try to the herb room which I wish I spent more time in

I still can't decide which I like more, so this means I have to go back to both and research more.  Boo hoo.

Growing up in NJ where $12 large plain cheese pies at Mafia-run pizza joints litter every corner, I can't help but be thrilled that we've got a really good, NY-style pizza right here in the middle of Reno. Even better, it's run by the nicest folks in the world who employ workers who love what they do. We ordered the 18 inch pizza with mushrooms to go and it was absolutely top-notch. Nothing fancy, but the crust was superb, the sauce tasty and it had a just-right combination of cheese and mushrooms. If I have a very minor complaint, it's that the center of the crust was not quite as crispy as the rest of pizza, but I am guessing that is just due to the sheer size of the pizza.

Compared to NuYalk Pizza in South Reno, this is far better. Their sauce is much too salty for my taste buds and service there is hit or miss.

I was introduced to Rapscallion via a special Yelp Elite-only event where I was quite happy with the high quality of different dishes and drinks offered to guests.  Impressed, I decided to return to see what "normal" people would experience.  I had a friend fly in from Tucson and after picking her up at the airport, we came here for dinner.  Our final tab was $79 + $16 tip = $95.

For appetizers, we chose the Diablo bacon-wrapped scallops and the fresh oysters.  I never got to touch the scallops since my friend devoured hers before asking me if I wanted a taste (harrumpf) but my fresh oysters, though quite small meat wise, were tasty.  A complimentary slab of sourdough bread with butter was given to us.

Our mains:  shrimp scampi (buttery, garlicky, generous with medium sized shrimp) and grilled salmon on a plank, which came with sautéed veggies and a wild rice pilaf.  The salmon was small in size, but delicious and fresh.  I don't think there was a sliver of salmon left. The rice was excellent, but the veggies were a bit bland and too soft.

The crowd was a mix of dressed up couples on date nights, to girlfriends night out get-togethers, to good ole boys drinking shots of whiskeys and doing lots of toasts.  People came in heels and dresses, in shorts and polo shirts, you name it.

Lovely way to splurge on a dinner.

I want to start out by saying we actually had a good time at this bar, right up until the end.  At the recommendation of one of the locals in our group, roughly a dozen of us went here after enjoying the Broadway Street scene in Nashville.  We got a table and some drinks and were enjoying ourselves when were told we had to try the Jedi shot (a mix of six or seven liquors that come in a complimentary shot glass).  Cool drink AND a souvenir?  Sold!  I went up to one of the bars, found them on their cocktail menu, and bought three of them.  I was surprised when they came in regular, plain shotglasses, but hey, free glasses are free glasses.  About an hour later we noticed a commercial for the Jedi shot and complimentary glass on one of their giant TV screens, and the glass was totally different.  At this point the server came by to clear the table and wanted to take away the glasses we had been given.  I explained those were supposed to be included, and he said "not those glasses, they must have been out of the free ones.  Tell you what, go ahead and take those anyway."  When we left I walked out the front door with the three glasses stacked in my hands, at which time a bouncer said I had to give them back.  I explained the situation, and he went and got the manager, who said "those glasses aren't free, you can't have them, who told you you could take them?"  Rather than get the server in trouble I explained "I bought them at the back bar, and your drink menu says the drink comes with free shot glasses".  He brought the bartender out who said accusingly "you're saying I told you they were free?  I told you that? I never said those were free."  I said "no, your MENU says the shot comes with a complimentary glass.  You may not have said they were free, but you certainly never corrected the menu by mentioning they weren't.  I would not have ordered them then."  To which the manager replied "either give them back or I am calling the cops."  I offered to give them back in exchange for the correct glasses, or something else in return, and he reiterated he'd call the police if I didn't hand them over.  At that point I was pretty disgusted by the whole situation and gave them back to the manager, who disappeared back inside without a word.  The bouncer then apologized for the manager being an jerk, and we left.

It's actually a cool place, and the locals with us said it had great food, too (which was why we went in the first place, but unfortunately the kitchen was closed).  And it very well may be a fantastic place.  But there are about a hundred other fantastic places on Broadway Street, and if this is how they treat their patrons, I don't ever see a need to go back to this one.  Thanks, but no thanks.

So the Truckee Meadows now have another Korean BBQ option. This one is located in Sparks and just like the other one, a burden for us living in the south part of town. But just like the other one, the unique dining experience is worth the trip. As the other place opened first, and to not go on with an extremely long review. I'll keep this one short and simple. Comparing to the Reno Korean BBQ place, in my opinion this place has better meats and side dishes (my sister in law disagrees). The selection is slightly fewer but the quality difference is noticeable, to me anyways. One thing this restaurant pales in comparison to the other place is the ventilation system. This one has a hood over the table and depending on the airflow, it may be in your face. Management can adjust it but it can be a nuance. Service is attentive but staff needs some time to get acquainted with the different culinary experience. Overall, none of the little things were worth deducting a star especially because it's a new place and I'll give them the benefit of the doubt.

Should Reno stop it with the AYCE sushi bars? I don't think so. More competition, the better. What Hinoki does here is opposite of a lot of sushi bars in town. You will not find a menu with a hundred rolls, at which point you can't remember what's good and what's not. You won't find a list of "specials" of exotic fish that are just that, exotic. No one ever said exotic had to actually taste good and while having rare type of sushi is fun, none the less, I don't come here to play. I came for great sushi and Hinoki delivers. Menu is simple and not over crowded and the best part is the chef's get to know you. Your likes and dislikes. Then once you've gotten your usual or even in between, the chef's whip up different delicious creations to serve you. They are fast and friendly. Before we knew it, we were pretty full. This is how sushi restaurants should be run. The most important thing besides the sushi is having a chef that caters to your personal preferences. No more generic sushi chefs pumping out generic rolls for me. Oh and even their nigiri can be had with subtle touches too instead of the plain fish and rice. My only gripe is that the waitress can probably take away the plates a bit faster but hey they've only been open 3 days so I don't deduct any stars for that.

POKE! POKE! POKE! OMG! YES! Sorry for the caps but I'm excited. It's about time Reno caught on to this new craze. In a world of AYCE sushi, this is a nice break especially if you don't got time to sit down and spend an hour to eat. In and out, this fast, casual and healthy lunch alternative is heaven sent. They technically aren't open yet. This is their soft opening run and still working out the knick knacks. Pricing is fair, especially when all the toppings are included and the fish tastes fresh. The friendly customer service is still getting used to their Point of Sale system but it's not worth deducting a star. I went with the gentlemen's recommendation of mixing of spicy mayo and truffle shoyu with salmon, yellowtail, and scallops. Then I proceeded to add all the toppings like seaweed, krab mix, tobiko, cucumbers, etc. Now they just need to open one in South Reno even before they technically open this one.

On the way to Hudson Beach is a little spot called Hudson Beach Ice Cream Parlor. The place is clean and bright and decorated in a 50s diner style with oldies blaring. They have a nice selection of ice cream and (for my father) a smaller selection of sugar free. They also a few hot items- think hot dogs, basic sandwiches. 

My three year old LOVES their Superman ice cream. Basically it is vanilla ice cream dyed an outrageous array of colors- bright blue, yellow and red. Making a mess is probably half of the fun!

They are open year round, because it rarely really gets cold in Florida. This little shop is now a required stop when we are in Hudson. 

*As a side note- I added this business to Yelp.com in summer 2010 and it magically disappeared from the site. I am adding it again, we'll see what happens!

Extremely disappointed with my New Years Eve dining experience. We selected the 3 course meal for $59 per person. After just now looking at the menu online, it looks like we paid $59 for a $31-$34 meal off the regular menu. Irritating because it was the same sized portions that you're served any other day of the year. Not to mention it was the exact same menu as last year on NYE with the exception of one dish.

After making my reservation, I asked for the menu and was excited to try the short rib dish. Upon ordering, I find out that they have run out of short rib. Ok, fine, I'll have the filet and was told they cook all filets to medium rare. Not my first choice, but ok it will work. When it came out, it didn't look like a filet. Didn't taste like a filet, tasted like my mom's pot roast. And on top of that, it was well done. Since the menu was the same last year, we know the plating and presentation of the filet. This was two triangles of meat that are over cooked and clearly not filet. Pot roast is great, but I ordered and paid for filet. So at this point, I'm thinking, you didn't have my short ribs and now I feel like you just tried to pull a fast one us. Ok, lets move on. My veggies were cold. Not like "oh the top pieces are cold but the middle/bottom ones are warm" like all of them were cold. My potato fries and filet were luke warm. The plate is ice cold. This means that the plate wasn't heated, the food was put on it and then it sat on a counter without a warmer long enough to cool off.

Chocolate cake- it was 3.5 stars at best. Not moist. The frosting was sweet and that was the saving grace.

This is a roughly 50 seat restaurant. It's a pre-set menu and they are controlling the flow of the seating with what appeared like 3 servers and 1 manager. The menu was simple enough-- caesar salad, caprese salad or beat salad -- filet, short rib, cod or scallops (oh hey, heads up- you only get 4 and they are tiny and yes, you're still paying $59 for 4) -- chocolate cake or creme brulee. This is not a rocket science menu especially since this restaurant did the same menu last year and these items are on their normal menu. You'd think they would be experts at this.

Overall this experience was disappointing. Someone with experience needs to get in there and help this place on the "big nights". Thanks for the crummy dinner experience on what was supposed to be a fun and exciting night.

Bottom Line: Exceptional service - Expensive and Mediocre food

We ordered burgers blah blah blah, thats below.  The shake is ultimately my issue for downgrading my rating to three stars.

Wife is preggo and wants a shake - so we get a shake and it comes out tiny.

Now this was in one of those small cups that they give a child water in - FIVE DOLLARS for a tiny shake that's not that good.

Its a scoop of ice cream, splash of milk and some malt.  IMHO this is the one you sell for $2 to keep people coming in and THEN you can sell burgers for $12.

My wife and I have been here a few times and I have to say the service is very, very good.  Above any burger joint that comes to mind.  Everyone is extremely friendly and their knowledge of the menu is significant.  This is all awesome.

The burgers are good - dont get me wrong.  I have really enjoyed their burgers each time I have visited, but they are not $14 good.
I really appreciate the diverse burgers on the menu.  There many strange and yummy combinations I never would have thought of.
The last time I Was there I got the one with the egg on it and I liked it.  The patty was a little dry but there was lots of flavor, but man it wasnt worth $12.

Wife and I both had burgers, I added a salad and we also had the milkshake and the total was $38.  $38 for two people to get hamburgers - no beer or booze.

Probably not goin back

Bottom Line:  Average food and threatened to charge us for not finishing our plate

I was VERY excited to try this place out as I desperately miss living in Koreatown down in LA where I was for 13 years.
  The biggest problem is that most of the things that are brought to the table are not marinated in anything.  The bulgogi - which has always been my favorite - was super yummy, pre marinated and grilled up very well.  
   However things like the unmarinated pork belly, was just cooked meat at the end and not a lot of flavor despite my efforts to add things to it and even my attempt to kind of marinade it in my bowl of spicy sauce.
   Service was mediocre at best - somewhat attentive.
There are no vegetables - at all - except a bowl of salad that was periodically refilled for us.  Toward the end I was definitely starting to get the "meat sweats".

We hadnt quite finished what was left on the Bulgogi plate when the server came back and told us we would be charged $10 for not finishing all of the meat - that after we spend more than $50 for our dinner and received mediocre service.
  Not only that - this whole chargeback thing was the first that we had heard of this.  It's not on the menu and our server never mentioned it.

Having never heard about this, IMHO it was quite rude to charge us what they did for dinner, then threaten to charge us more for something we know nothing about.

This place was good but has some work to do in the customer service department

I am from San Diego where Roberto's was invented in 1964. I loved Roberto's back in my college years. 

The one here in Reno is a sad example of what happens when a company franchises out restaurants and does not uphold any standards. 

The service is lack luster to horrible depending on when you go in. The food is just okay at best and lacks any familiar flavor. (no Mexican food place should serve guacamole out of a can)  The place was not clean prior to CV19, and still is not. The trash can is typically over flowing and smells bad if you sit anywhere near it. The prices are nearly restaurant grade with less than cafeteria service and quality.

I was shocked to walk up on Superbowl Weekend at noon and find no line. In fact there was a sign out front assuring people they were actually open even though the Buffet was virtually empty. 

WHY? Might start with the piss poor attitude of the staff. I presented my basic players club card for the $3.00 discount.The cashier said it was outdated.  I left my party there and went on my way to find the players club. Got a new card. Upon returning to the buffet the new cashier informed us that there is only discounts offered to "higher" guests. I guess that means more important that us. I asked why the other cashier didn't bother to tell me it would be a waste to bother getting a useless card since we are NOBODY,  she said she did not know. There are no senior's discounts for my parents,  no first responders discounts, no locals discounts and nothing but attitude for having the audacity to ask. The manager happened to be at the desk and only showed her own disgust for us asking about a local discount. 

How did they get a second star? Some of the food is still good. We did find several choices old and sitting around in the warmers too long since it is not busy. 
Most of the waitresses and cooks have been around for the last 10 to 20 years that we have been coming here and bad management is not their fault.  

What did the Eldorado teach me today? 

They don't want your business unless you engage in losing your butt in the casino. No problems,  there are local businesses dying to serve us in exchange for our hard earned money. Message received clearly Carano family and Eldorado  management we won't bother coming back. 

Harrah's is one who embraces locals because we live and work in the area 365, 24/7.

Because of the prompt and polite reply from Noble Pie, I decided to bring my fam and try the food. 
The salad was impressive in both size and content. The calzone was pretty decent but not really meal sized. Maybe if they had the regular size and a larger option. 
The service was good. We were greeted, offered information on the menus, and our order came quickly.

It is hard to think of any criticisms. This is a family operated deli. The food is always fresh. The menu is extensive and has unique items. The art work is awesome and the restraint is kept pretty clean. If you are in the mod for a panini, salad, sandwich or wrap come here and there will be something that looks good and tastes better. 

This place was midtown before midtown was cool. 10/10 all categories.

The Western Village has figured out how to make a smaller local neighborhood casino work well. You can walk through the casino without getting a lung disease or smelling like a heavy smoker. (this was a huge problem in the past) The place is now immaculate. The service is good, most employees report being employed there for more than 15 years. 

The Steak House is better than most in Reno/Sparks. Cafe Bellini has amazing food and specials. There are senior discounts available for our seasoned friends. 

Parking can be challenging during busy times. Free valet parking is right next to the doors though. 

I don't gamble here so I cannot say too much. It looks like lots of local people do. They have the latest slots and the table games seem upbeat and crowded.

We called in advance of going to the buffet to make sure the recent maintenance was done and that we knew what to do to get the locals discount.  
What we were told apparently not how to do it. The snotty "manager" was so rude in telling us that we were wrong. We had to leave and go get a coupon. When we came back we just stood there without anyone acknowledging us. I guess they wanted us to wait in the SLOW line again. 
Bottom line, NOT going back. 
Service 0/10
Food.    7/10
Cashier Manager should be fired /10!!!

Glad to see two Chicks making it in a 2nd location. This is not quite as cozy as midtown, the feel is different for sure. The menu and comfort food is right on point though.  You are doing yourself a flavor favor if you clear your mind and open it to some of the unique menu items here. 

My favorite part of Two Chicks is their commitment to locally source as much product as possible. Coffee, bread, dressings... Way to go.  

The wait time estimates need to be worked out a bit. We were told 45 minutes or more so we went to look at a few things across the street only to be rushed back when our table was ready 10 minutes later.

Still good food and a great atmosphere after all the years. Had a bit of a wait but it was expected on a weekend night. Prompt service at a reasonable price. I saw that there are Happy Hour specials Mon-Thur 2-5 that looked reasonable too.

Upon a second visit I am now sure that the full 5 Star is earned. I didn't want to be drawn in by the DDD hype. The truth is that they have a great product, fun atmosphere, and good service.

The prices appear to be a bit high, however you are getting plenty of high quality food for your money. The employees are upbeat. The place is clean and comfortable. They feature Blind Dog Coffee that is another great local company. 

I did not know this but there is a midtown location now too.

The friendly competent staff is attentive and welcoming. Like most Flowing Tide Pubs the lighting is dim, which I find enhances the looks of your date. 

The variety of food is good. The food is prepared consistent with the other locations. 

The TVs are actually on sports and the staff will happily change a channel without a bunch of attitude.

The WiFi works well too.

This is what I love about Yelp! 

Southern food IS comfort food, and this IS the real deal. 

10/10 Food. Every plate was just right. The greens were crispy not soggy, the chicken is crisper than any in town. The chicken & waffles are great too. Have patience with the fried chicken it takes a good minute to cook properly. 

10/10 Service. Felt like regulars on our first visit. 

8/10 Atmosphere. It is as authentic as you can get for a strip mall. Think Next Friday 2.

Excellent menu with lots of unique choices. The atmosphere was kind of flat compared to visits to other Hash House A Go Go locations. The prices are a bit high compared to most of the local competition for similar eats. 
Bottom line for me is that there is good food, great choices, that cost a bit too much.

Staying in Reno NV for a snowboarding trip and stopped here for dinner. We were so pleasantly surprised at the high quality and excellent value of this buffet. A wide variety of salad, entree and dessert choices awaited us.  I had 2 slices of the prime rib and some rice to start out.  The prime rib is delicious, and so juicy!  All my friends that came with me said everything they had was excellent.  I don't eat seafood but there was all you can eat crab legs, and a decent size seafood section.  The gelllato was so good OMG....My only complaint is the waitress wasn't really around at all in the beginning.  She dropped off water in the beginning while we walked off to get our food but after that she wasn't around often.  We had to order drinks from one of the porters.  Excellent quality of food and it was decently priced.  I will list the prices below;

This place was a pleasant surprise. Was visiting a brewery in the area and this place popped up on Yelp as a decent choice for a sandwich. It looks like any of a number of dumpy looking bodega style store you would see in the area, but damned if they don't have a spot on deli for making some fantastic sandwiches. I was fortunate enough to be there when there wasn't much of a line (although a line formed pretty quick after I ordered). Placed an order for a shrimp po'boy and it was pretty freakin good. After I ordered, one of the guys from the back came out and asked me HOW I wanted my sandwich done. I told him to fix it like he thought it should be done. He smiled a bit and after he walked back to the prep area I could hear him tell his co-workers he wished everyone would order like that. Shrimp was perfect, had the perfect amount of condiments and it was a fairly hefty size. Like others have said it is a divey looking place but the peeps are solid and the food is to kill for.

Opening days can be a challenge for any business, but this one seems to be off to a steady start. Through the front double doors, that look more like the opening of a Roman eatery than a new restaurant in New Orleans, I found myself in a bright and semi-opulent room. Three steps up brings you right to the hostess stand and into the open room with the bar immediately in front of you. I was greeted by an entourage of hostesses with smiling faces that have not yet been jaded by the drudgery of working the job, and was seated in a comfortable booth table that I had requested.

The tables are dressed in the bare necessities of cloth napkins, utensils, sugar tray, and salt/pepper. Other than the booths, the tables and bar are complemented by relaxed wood chair seating. Wait staff are comfortably dressed in jeans and button down gray, green, or faded red shirts. Everyone, is bright eyed and fresh due to it being opening day, but the staff are off to a great start, until they got busy and started to forget about our table. We ended up sitting for about 10 minutes after a wrong item was left at our table without anyone stopping by. We ended up eating it because we didn't know when anyone would return to take it back to the kitchen. 

Everything is new and smells of clean fresh paint, wood, and textiles that have yet to be blemished by the overwhelming scents from the kitchen and customers. Opening day is more of a mixture of tourists and locals, with it being heavy on the locals side. This restaurant is the latest from the acclaimed chef and owners of Herbsaint, so it's interesting to see them expand into an Italian inspired theme abutted next to the French quarter. 

I dined here for an afternoon soirée with my partner. We enjoyed the Rossini spritzer and Menta Fresca cocktails while snacking on the marinated olives. The drinks were light, effervescent and refreshing. The olives were good, but nothing to bother ordering again since Whole Foods sells practically the same thing for far less money. 

On to the nibblings. We ordered the baked spicy sausage provola. Interesting and served in a escargot platter, the ciabatta bread came in handy to soak up the remaining oil from the sausage nooks. On to the next course of grilled radicchio. Personally, I found it to be very bitter and off-putting, but my partner thoroughly enjoyed it, so order this side dish only if bitter dishes are enjoyable to you. We next moved on to snacking on the house made mozzarella. Smooth, soft, and a little on the firm side. It's garnished with salt, olive oil and a little parsley. Last up, we ordered the tuna stuffed peepers to complete our 3 for $11 anitpasti. It was ok. The tuna tasted more like canned tuna than fresh tuna. I would probably skip on this dish as well. 

Overall, I think the restaurant is off to a great start, but they obviously have some growing pains to go through. Some of the dishes really need to be re-thought as to remaining on the menu, but the "Feed Me" portion of the menu is worth a try. Happy dining!

Great pizzas, meatball sandwiches (when they have them) and friendly employees make Pitruco my favorite stand at Franklin Food Hall. The pizzas are thin crust and cooked to order and feature fresh bufala mozzarella and other high quality ingredients.

In case you haven't seen the other reviews, Stina is a great addition to Philly's pizza scene. But how many pizza places serve succulent, juicy octopus with dollops of olive and tapenade and roasted red peppers served up in artistic manner that just raised the bar for the best in Philly? I could eat seven more of these delectable tentacles in one sitting and be perfectly happy but I'd have to miss ever present chef Bobby Saritsoglou's perfectly crafted margherita pizza hot from the wood fired oven with lightly charred crust ample sprigs of aromatic basil, and Parmesan sprinkled under the pie when it is served. I downed that one with no problem either. Too bad I was too full to try one of Bobby's pides, mantis, or boreks, but that's what return visits are for. It's truly a labor of love and it shows in everything Bobby creates. My only nitpick is that they have these eight ounce Diet Coke bottles like other fine places in town that I am downing two or three at a meal, but when I am eating food this good I could be drinking green juice from Jim Jones and wouldn't complain. But then I'd miss those boreks so maybe not.

A recent trip to Vernick Fish really caught me off guard. As I entered the lovely space on the north side of the ground floor of the new Comcast Building I felt as if I had been transported somewhere else. Glancing at the long, spacious interior I wondered if I was in New York? London? Architectural Digest? Fortunately after we were seated at the chef's counter by a friendly hostess a glance upwards brought me back to reality. Hidden on the beautiful tile wall evoking the sea was a small clock with an Eagles football helmet on it. I was still in Philly! 

Seriously though, Vernick Fish was a spectacular experience from start to finish. Our server, Jade, was truly a gem and saved me from ordering something that would definitely not agree with my food allergy. And I do recommend that you sit at the chef's counter. You can see the food being prepared in front of your eyes and even talk with some of the prep staff and runners. You also get too see all of the dishes being made and plated so you know what to get on your next visit here since you will be back (but why does that pork Milanese look so good?) 

We started with salmon tartare with gaufrettes. I eat a lot of good salmon but never have I had any salmon like this. It was so silky smooth and tasty that I can't see not ordering every time we go here. We also had the sardines on sourdough which were good and flavorful, but given our vantage point we saw that the sardines came from a jar and were de-boned and placed on the toast without any other intervention from the staff. For the mains, my wife had delicious grilled harissa shrimp while I enjoyed a spectacular grilled black sea bass with broccoli and tomato sauce. The fish was juicy and perfecto cooked and my wife's shrimp were yummy and had yogurt, melon cubes, and cucumber. For dessert I had an excellent slice of key lime pie with whipped cream on top mimicking fish scales. 

Our bill was presented with two pieces of saltwater taffy from Joisey (we're in Philly) and my credit card transaction was done with one of those handheld wireless devices that are all over Europe (but maybe we're not). 

So if you're looking for an excellent seafood meal (or maybe not seeing that pork) in Philly, London, or wherever you may be, just head to Vernick Fish.

We really enjoyed our food at this restaurant . I had the usual veggie roll and soup and Hubby had his salmon shrimp roll  and he said if was off the chart great. Service was good and the portions were perfect. This restaurant is a busy place. Parking is difficult  we were lucky to get a spot right up front but to leave was hard with so many cars coming in and out of lot.
I would love to come back and eat here again.

Really beautiful restaurant . Food and service was great . We had a very nice server . She came right away with the water And then these hot towels to clean our hands a very nice touch .
I ordered the miso soup and it was delicious. Also had the veggie avocado roll . I am learning to like the spicy  wasabi. Hubby had the shrimp roll and he said it was really good 
I now know why wasabi is served with sushi . The reason is some like  it hot but also for the raw fish to kill off parasites.
Would I come back here and eat most definitely yes. Parking is ample . Everyone following COVID plan .

If you took an autistic 14 year-old, forced him to sniff glue and then asked him to design a "real fancy big city restaurant" from 1978 the output would probably look a lot like 5 Palms- the latest in double ghastly overpriced Catalina Foothills eateries.

As you enter the vast multi-layered 5 Palms compound a liveried doorwoman anticipates your entrance and opens the portal into a foyer with black and white tile, wood-paneled walls, blue carpet, and fluted columns that seems like an off-brand cruise ship steakhouse crossed with a striving brothel. The host is in a suit and the wait staff are formally attired; this contrasts really painfully with the elderly guests in their Tommy Bahama shirts tucked into pleated shorts.

The menu consists of both surf and turf. Our order took over an hour to leave the kitchen. The steak was adequate but at $70 for a ribeye it turned to ash in my mouth. The sauteed spinach looked like a child with pertussis blew some snot into a bowl. My guests seemed to enjoy their Chilean Sea Bass and Halibut but it looked like fish night at the nursing home to my jaundiced eye.

There is a bar upstairs with great views of hard-eyed middle aged divorcees and their natural prey: well-to-do Foothills geezers. There were a few youngsters that appeared to be rich kid Sonorans trying to look cosmopolitan.

So, to sum it up pithily: this place should be called 1 Palm! Hey-oh!

I was just in here today to grab a quick hoagie for lunch. 
The schmuck taking orders called me "sweetie" THREE times while I was placing my order. Excessive and unnecessary. Normally I wouldn't say anything but this was getting patronizing and condescending. As I continued placing my order I paused and said "....and don't call me sweetie". Well, in a very loud and dramatic voice he says "OOOOH sorry, ma'am m, is that ok ma'am, if I call you ma'am??" Everyone stared at me. I continued with my order ignoring his douche tantrum. He started staring at my boobs, I crossed my arms. 

Finally, I went and stood on the side waiting for my order and thinking about what kind of misogynistic A-hole treats people this way, especially paying customers!!!!!! I noticed immediately that EVERY single person (all men) who came after me were not called anything!!! Not sir, etc. nothing!!! WHY call me anything???! Why not just treat me like a normal freaking person like everyone else??! Just take my freaking order without being a condescending, womanizing jerk!!!!

My family and I wanted to order simple take out and have a drink while we waited. We ordered our food, paid, and then went over to order a drink from the bar. We were blatantly ignored as we were seated at the bar for more than 10 minutes, and 3 staff members/bartenders walked right by us without any acknowledgement. We were finally able to place our drink order after flagging down someone who appeared to be a manager. For what they charge there was very little alcohol. Presentation wise the drink was lovely! Taste and value... not worth it. We finished our drinks and continued to wait for our food. We ordered salads. To go. Only to be told they thought we left?!? The place is not that big. If we weren't directly next to the order here sign/window we were at the bar directly across from the order here sign/window. We ended up waiting over 45 minutes- for simple salads..they weren't that busy at all.. which is what we couldn't get over .. or what the issue was.. and the dismissal of our presence at the bar. Once we finally received our order- it was made incorrectly and the guy didn't even apologize or offer to fix it. At this point we just wanted to go home as to who knows how long we would have been there waiting on the correct order. Overall that could have been overlooked if it customer service had been welcoming and well just more customer oriented. Sadly, the trophy fish doesn't not earn a trophy from me. Our first visit was not a lovely experience, which is disappointing as it could have easily been a weekly favorite with the live music, ambiance, and seafood!

This place doesn't look like much, tucked into the side of an alley and sandwiched in between some very popular midtown eateries. But just look for the bright pink doors, and I promise you won't be disappointed. 

The al pastor tacos are some of the best I've ever had, perfectly seasoned, with chunks of grilled onions and pineapple. Delicious tortillas that stand up to the massive amount of meat they put into them. The fish tacos are crispy and light with a beautiful radicchio slaw and creamy avocado. And the green salsa is tangy and fresh and just the right amount of spicy. 

When I say you need to go here, I mean it!
I finished 4 tacos and immediately wanted to try everything else on the menu. 

Tacos are 2/$6 or 3/$8 so bring a friend and share so you can try all their delicious meat selections.

And as if the food alone wasn't enough, the staff are super kind and warm and I really enjoyed my entire experience here,

Haven't been here yet but I have been calling f this place for 2DAYS and no answer. I want to confirm the Valentine's Day menu for my reservation tonight and no one picks up the phone and their Instagram page is useless. Not a great first impression so far.

Kiryuu-chaaan !


In Japanese, the word "kiwami" apparently means "extreme" or "ultimate". My first exposures to the word were the Yakuza Kiwami video games on PS4(These were all new remakes of the original Yakuza games on PS2 in the mid 2000's) Anyway, despite liking many Asian foods, Ramen is not something I've really eaten much. I've had it once at Ichicoro a few years ago but it didn't strike enough of a chord because I never went back.  

I decided to go to Kiwami because of the name and to see if I could get excited for ramen. KRS is located on Causeway Blvd, about 0.6 miles from 301. It's a little hard to maneuver because the back of the restaurant is facing Causeway. You have to turn into the adjacent Racetrack gas near Falkenburg road and drive  past a construction site to get to the strip mall and the front of KRS. The plaza looks mismatched and most of the spaces are empty save for a PT place and a coffee joint. Parking is very easy to find.

When you enter, you are treated to an intimate place with a cozy contemporary look. I invited my yelp buddy Lisa C. to experience KRS. We both decided on the Kiwami Ramen, which had a pork broth, boiled egg, sweet corn, noodles, scallion,mushroom, and pieces of pork meat. The food took about 10 minutes to come out and and was served hot and in cute red bowls. While Lisa used chopsticks, I went full gaijin and used a fork for the solid parts. The broth was really tasty. They also put a lot of noodles so the balance of liquid to solid shifts to solid unlike pho which is generally equal.   It was the second best soup like dish IVe had in a while, second only to Saigon deli pho.    4/5

Our server , Emily was very nice and was efficient at refilling our drinks. One thing to note is that as of this review, they do NOT have a liquor license and no drink menu. They are working on getting that updated. I think sake or some Asian beers would be a nice complement. They have sushi rolls there too which look great but we were too full to partake.

The ramen was $13 which was fair. I think ichicoro is roughly the same, but Kiwami is more intimate than cramped like ichicoro. Ichicoro seems to feel like a ramen nightclub while Kiwami feels like a casual or date night spot. There were a mixture of couples and young families there.

Overall: A very nice and promising ramen place in Brandon. Worthy of Kazuma Kiryu and Goro Majima.

After seeing a movie and having a little extra in my coffers than usual, I decided to get some sushi since its been nearly 2 years since I've stepped into a sushi restaurant. With my discovery of poke bowls, I've latched onto those bc I Can customize and its 2.5 less expensive.

Anyhoo, I've been a sushi nomad for the last few years. I decided to try Sushi Cafe since its pretty close to the AMC Highwoods 20.

Pros: 

Customer Service. The waitress refreshed my soda and brought my food relatively quickly.

The prices were fair. Few of the rolls were above $12.

Cons:

I ordered 4 rolls (I usually get 3).
Spicy Tuna, Yellowtail and Jalapeno, Lobster, and Ocean Blue.

Spicy tuna - The fish was mushy and not spicy.
YT/JP - The jalapeno was fresh but I could barely taste any fish.
Lobster - Nothing really stood out.
OB - This had sweet potato in the ingredients which was different, but I felt like the outside and top of the roll was tastier than the inner part.

I feel overall the food is 2.5/5 somewhat average.  Even the placemat was paper which made the experience seem a little flat. I'm a blue collar guy, but I'm a little surprised by the rave reviews. 
I think that since this is purely in the suburbs, people are more generous. 
Another thing that irks me is the use of cream cheese in way too many rolls and I feel that the types of fish included could be more varied.

Maybe I built my expectations too high since Its been a while, but this was disappointing.

After seeing Shazam today, I felt like eating some Mexican food. I have heard this place and Miguel's in South Tampa are the best.  Interesting...

When you go in, you'll notice that there are legions of people waiting outside. Thankfully, I only had to wait 10 minutes. The interior is filled with faux palm trees, and orange/cream tiled floor. The restaurant isn't small but with so many customers entering and leaving and servers dashing between , you have to tread carefully. 

I was given chips, salsa, and I asked for creamy jalapeno sauce. The chips were crisp and tasty. The salsa was thin but had fresh vegetables and was slightly spicy which was nice. The jalapeno sauce was awesome. It tastes similar to Pollo Tropical Cilantro sauce-spicy but not overpowering. Put in your entree too!  -  
Chips/salsa/jalapeno sauce  5/5

My main entree was the beef fajitas for one ($17) and a soda ($3). The beef and bell peppers come sizzling in a cast iron skillet with a small pan for refried beans and rice, a flat brown circular container for the tortillas , and a dish with lettuce, shredded cheese, pico de gallo, sour cream, and guacamole.  Everything was fresh. While the beef was seasoned nicely and the pico/cheese were very good and the tortillas were soft , the refried beans and rice were plain and had little zing. They were the weakest part of the meal. It is strange that such a staple of Mexican food is done so poorly in Tampa restaurants. Other than Caribbean Crown, no place in Tampa does it well. I also wish they would give you 4-5 tortillas total.     
Fajitas - 4/5    
Beans/Rice  3/5

The service was decent. My server was quick and kind, however the one time I wanted drink refills I didnt get any. It's not really the servers fault , more like there so many customers and few servers that the time per customer can be different depending on work load.

You do get a lot of food for the money.  
Overall: Id say this place gets 4/5
They need to improve on beans/rice.

Pho is one of those great dishes I've discovered in recent years that hits the spot when it's cold.  Simply Pho and Grill is located in a plaza on the corner of Fletcher and Dale Mabry. It is between Core Life and the Hibachi place.

I went at night and while the restaurant is a bit small, it has a sleek look. The coolest thing is the colored rectangular panels  on the walls/aisles. It makes it look like a nightclub or a Riddler deathtrap from the Arkham video games. 

My server was nice. I decided to get seafood pho since that's something Ive never had before.  I got my food in a few minutes with the usual accoutrements of sliced fresh jalapeno, mint, and sprouts.
The only nitpick is that they don't have regular forks at the table. They have a soup spoon and chopsticks. When I use chopsticks, it's like I have the proficiency of a stroke patient. I simply use the soup spoon for broth and fork for the solid matter. 

My pho was served hot with lots of big shrimp, scallops, and imitation krab along with the usual vermicelli noodles in broth. I thought the broth was good and the serving was roughly the same as places like Saigon Deli or Pho Quyen. Since it was seafood, the cost was $11 for a regular. Regular beef was around around $9. The broth isn't quite as good as Saigon deli, but better than Quyen. I'd give it a 8/10.

The only negative was that my server pretty much left once I got my food and I couldn't get a refill of my soda or my fork until I batted my eyes at another server. Thankfully I got those and another brought my bill with due haste.

Overall: A solid place to get pho and it's nicely designed so you can bring a date too!

Pros:
Nice decor.  There is black furniture with a red dragon mural on the wall. An intimate spot.You wouldn't think this is in a dingy plaza on Fletcher. 

Quick service. I went to the counter to order and got my food in 10 minutes. I ordered a Dan -Dan noodle and a can of coke. There is no true table service FYI.

Cons:
While the menu has pictures,I wish there was also written descriptions. I dont know exactly what meat I  got (I believe it was ground pork)

For all the talk I've heard about Szechaun food being spicy, I was supremely disappointed. I ordered medium, out of three possible levels. The medium at Thai Sweet Basil has a lot more kick. I normally don't order the max level of spice because I don't want my bootyhole to look like Chernobyl but this was impotent.  The flavor was lacking. There was a good amount of noodles and meat with some veggies. It came with a small serving of egg drop soup but it tasted bland and straight out of a can. 
I dont care for standard Americanized Chinese food so I was hoping this would be something on the level of Saigon Deli pho, a poke bowl, or mongolian barbecue, but it seems that the food isn't for me.

Bodega is on Florida avenue almost across the street from the Refinery. It is behind a grey facade hat is one story. While there was adequate parking today, I can see it being crowded in evenings.

When you enter ,it is multiple small tables with two bar areas, one for drinks and one for ordering. While I was tempted to order the Cuban, I ordered the lechon plate and cafe con leche. My total was $13.

The lechon plate came with roast pork, black beans, white rice, onions, and sweet plantains . It was very filling and the beans were seasoned adequately. One thing I like was that they didn't skimp on the pork. The rice/beans were solid but not as awe inspiring as Hemingway's.
The cafe con leche was good, but La Segunda tops it easily. Sweet plantains were good, but it's hard to screw that up imo.

Service was quick  and polite. Since it is open air, Im less lkely to go during June-Sept.
One interesting note is that it is conjoined with Mandarin Heights, a new bar. From the road, you cant really tell unless you park and go through a a small ramp near the bar.

Overall: A good place to get Spanish food, but not a game changer.

I ordered the Shaken Beef and Garlic Noodles and a coconut Chocolate churro by delivery app.

Shaken Beef ($15): The Beef was very tender and the portion size was great.  Parmesan Cheese was a different but clever touch to give more life to the dish. The only negatives were that I would prefer more house sauce and more vegetables    4/5

Coconut Chocolate churro: I've only had a churro once a long time ago. Since this was a delivery order, I couldn't try it hot , but it tasted crunchy and chewy. The coconut flakes were a nice texture and flavor. The chocolate seems understated, but that could be due to not eating it newly made. I would like to try the other versions in the future.     4/5

One thing to note for people wanting to use Delivery for them is that the fees  are higher. Most delivery apps are about $8-9 plus the food cost/tax. Hiccups was about $12 more.

Pros:

LOTS of toppings!. This is really a customizer's dream!Three toppings are included with the base price.

-Inventive flavor combinations with cute names.I go tthe dark Knight (in honor of the Bat's 80th :) and it was indeed a mix of Brownie and Kit Kat!

The base price is $6 plus tax - on par with Cold Stone. Fair price imo

Cons

The rolled ice cream looks cool, but I'm not sure what other benefits it has compared to standard ice cream.

The texture of the ice cream is more towards the icy water side of the  equilibrium than the milk/cream side.  Not horrible but not as good as Cold Stone or Ice Dreammm. 

The AC is weak. I went at night and there were only a 2-3 people but I was still sweating.

This is purely subjective; the sticky notes covering the whole walls looks more like the work of a schizophrenic investigating a conspiracy theory than young folks having fun. They should emphasize the cute koala character more in their marketing. 

Overall: Nothing overly special. Young kids may like it more, but to me this gimmick era of ice cream (Liquid Nitrogen, Rolled) is a fad like hologram or die cut glow in the dark covers were for comic books in the 1990's.Mostly flash, little substance.


--

Pros:

The Tennessee Stud cocktail was strong, cool , and a bit fruity. I'm not a whiskey connoisseur but it was a very good drink   4/5

The Whiskey cake . I've never had a toffee based cake and it does taste like a Heath bar in cake form. The vanilla ice cream and the spiced pecans were the best part. The bourbon cream (?) was yummy too. The cake was very tall making it hard to finish. If I wasn't super hungry , I probably would have taken it home. 2 women could probably share one piece.    4/5

My server was cordial and prompt in bringing my items. Granted it was Memorial Day in the evening and the restaurant was practically empty.

Cons:

When I entered, there was no one at the hostess station to greet me for 5-6 minutes. I was wandering around until a bald guy came to assist me.

The restaurant is SUPER dark and its hard to read the menu. There is a difference between dim lighting and  dank David Fincher cave. I'd like to at least make out what I'm eating too.

For my main entree, I ordered the pork brisket and cheese grits.  The pork itself was soft as butter and there was a good amount of meat. However, it didn't taste properly seasoned and was insipid. The "grits" tasted like shredded potatoes and I could discern no cheese taste. 2/5

Overall:   I think this is a good place for drinks and dessert (maybe appetizers) but my entree was lacking and using sonar to eat isn't my idea of fun.       3/5

I wanted to try breakfast outside for a change(read: My breakfast items ran out at home). I usually go to First Watch,but wanted to try another place. With yelp, I found Shelly's.

Shelly's is located in an overly large and inactive plaza on Florida. It is close to the Florida/Bearss intersection. Upon entering , you see that is it is a very small cafe that can seat 35 folks MAX.

I was greeted by Cameron, a very affable and efficient guy. I decided to get coffee but wanted something different so I got the beignet bites. Reviews heaped accolades on the pancakes so I didn't need an excuse to also order the Banana walnut pancakes lol.

Impressions:

Coffee:    Solid coffee, but not my favorite ever.   3.5/5

Beignet bites: ($4) I've never had beignets but I really liked this . Imagine a sweet hot chewy pastry but in the form of spheres. There were approx. fifteen of them covered in mounds of powdered sugar. They are similar in size to "donut holes". This could have been breakfast enough with the coffee ! Since it was listed under "sides", I though the amount would be miniscule.    4/5

Banana walnut pancakes:  ($8) .  There were three of these pancakes and they were 4 inches in diameter similar to ihop. One cool thing is that they had a a lot of banana topping and walnuts. I assumed since they had those things on the inside that they wouldnt give them as toppings also. Great to be proven wrong!  They tasted great. They really taste home made, like if your mom made them for scratch. While I love first watch's pancakes, they feel super heavy but Shelly's felt very light. I cant say which is better. FW has 2 big cakes for $7; shelly's has three smaller ones for $8. Draw    Shelly's has buttermilk, chocolate chip, banana, and banana walnut varieties IIRC     4.5/5
