Service  Cameron was very quick in refilling my coffee and creamers. He asked how I found out about the place. I asked him how long Shelly's was and he said 1.5 years. Until recently, I havent gone to this plaza  for anything but now I have a reason to!

Overall: a great place to get breakfast in North Tampa.

While I normally go to Thai Sweet Basil in Carrollwood, I was coming from New Tampa and didn't feel like going that far.

The outside of this strip mall looks like a Transformer toy from 1988. Bright pink and teal. When you go inside, it is somewhat small, but very nicely decorated. There is jazz music playing on the stereo which is different for an Asian restaurant.

I ordered a Thai Tea and one order of Drunken Noodles. Interestingly, the dish is called "Thai Sweet Basil" noodles. Strange that they would name a dish after a competing restaurant, but oh well.

The Thai Tea was sweet with the usual "spices/flavoring" . 4/5.

The DN was 15-20 % larger than most noodle dishes I've gotten from Thai restaurants in Tampa. I love Thai Food, but usually am hungry a few hours later. After eating this, I was quite full for hours (Part of me wonders if there is extra sugar , MSG , or other ingredients in Bangkok's preparation or was it something that was in my recent diet?) 
The dish had broccoli, bell peppers, wide egg noodles, chicken, and sauce.  I ordered medium spice and I thought it was accurate. It was pretty good, but not the best I've ever had.  4/5

There were only 4-5 people in the restaurant dining in, but there were 1-2 few people and Food delivery drivers coming in and out repeatedly so they must be making profit from that. The service was pretty good with my water being refilled quickly and the bill handled smoothly by the two young men who were wearing masks. :) No complaints.

This is located in a very non descript light grey plaza on 56th street about 1/2 a mile south of the Fowler intersection.  It is adjacent to a 5 star pizza. Parking is adequate since its in a strip mall.

When you go inside, you will notice the reddish orange hue with many Peruvian objet d'art and  the Peruvian flag in the window. You can sit anywhere you want. Due to Covid, they have put the menus under a glass layer so you can see what you want without manhandling menus. clever idea.

There were 2 young ladies serving and they both wore masks. There were only three parties that day, but I was attended to very well and was brought out all the items in the correct  order w/o having to wait.

I have heard that many South American restaurants have a "mixed grill" for 3-5 people. I decided to try the 2-3 person combo of meats that comes with rice, 2 sides, salad and of course CARNE!

Since I was dining alone, I figured I could try a little bit of everything and take the rest home (and my stomach couldn't contain all that CARNE that was served)

The food was served with 2 different sauces, chimichurri, and an orange tangy sauce that was mid spicy but still flavorful. I believe this is called Hauncaina sauce. It went well with meat, rice, and fries. 

The salad that comes with it is mostly lettuce, sliced carrots, a bit of cheese, and a really nice oil based dressing. It looked simple, but it was light and very tasty. Normally, salad is either bland or has a lot of big coarse pieces, but this was easier to eat.       

I had chicha morada which is a purple corn derived drink that has cinnamon and pineapple. This was solid. It feels like a mix of juice and a cider. It is a cold drink and has no alcohol.  

The meats included various cuts of beef, sausage, pork ribs. there were approx 14 distinct pieces, with 2 of each type. The cuts of meat were pretty flavorful, but thin. This is the main difference from most American chain steakhouse that usually have thicker cuts, but sometimes not as flavorful. 

The steak cuts were the best and second place would be the ribs. They were super soft, and they seemed to marinated in a type of orange juice type of sauce.

The meat seemed to get cold a bit faster than I liked. The place is somewhat casual; it feels like a neighborhood place than  something on South Howard place.

I haven't head South American steakhouse fare often, but this is pretty good. Not the best I've had in my life, but good.   4/5.

BEST Spring Rolls in Reno 

Anytime I have spring rolls I always compare them to Golden Flowers spring rolls. Every time I have them I am not disappointed.  They are always made with fresh ingredients and rolled tightly.  Each bite is satisfying especially when you dip the spring rolls into the house made peanut sauce. The peanut sauce is a perfect chunky consistency mixed with sweet chili. When the peanut sauce is paired with the spring rolls - wow!! The combination of peanutbuttery spiciness with the fresh mint, basil and shrimp send my taste buds to heaven.

They also carry a Vietnamese beer I've been wanting to try called 33 Export.  It is a nice refreshing beer. 

This restaurant is always clean and has wonderful service. When I lived in the area I would often call in my order and they would always have it ready.

BEST CBH in Reno!!!

Great breakfast.  
Every time I'm in the area I make it a point to stop by for the best corn beef hash in Reno, Nevada. The portions are huge. The meal is served with big pieces of corn beef, onions and peppers with two eggs of your choice on top. The season of the corn beef hash makes this dish unlike any other. 

The Hawaiian breakfast is also fantastic. It comes with fried spam, Portuguese sausages, eggs and rice. All very tasty.

Coffee is AWESOME here.

Service is fantastic. 
Home style vibe.

Unfortunately this was our third time here, each time the service was awful, made a reservation but was not seated for over an hour.  Thought the food would compensate but for the third time the service and food was less than mediocre especially for the price .

BOTTOM LINE :   Way over priced and piss poor  service 
After three times it STRIKES OUT!!!!

Having dined at Krazy Kat's a number of times in the past few years (and loved it), I was very intrigued to hear that Mr. Merrill had decided to start his own venture. My girlfriend and I both enjoyed the crab soup, with generous chunks of lumb crab, as well as the Blue Point oysters - cold, fresh, and well paired with a glass of Sauvignon Blanc. For the entree course I had the Seafood Pasta - house-made pasta, a plethora of fresh shellfish, and a sauce that married everything perfectly. I recommended my lady try the crab cakes, knowing that if they are Chef Donny's recipe, they'll be phenomenal. Her plate was empty before mine!

In short, you have to give this place a try. Seafood is the name of the game, but I would bet two crab cakes that the other fare is just as tasty. 

As for the reviewer that gave one star because a worker was hosting and not serving that night... did you eat?

I heard this place was a good restaurant. I really was annoyed about this place once I arrived with my wife. we arrived at the door a 6pm saturday and was told that were no longer serving because they were now closed! I seen this place on late on weekends, and their doors was still open when we left. Ive drove past this place many times since that day and they are always open late past 6pm. I really felt that we were turned away due to our skin color. I would not recommend this restaurant to any of my friends nor family.

This place is great. We don't get it often but when we do its always 2 or more pies. This time we got one pepperoni. Sauce is nice and sweet crust is light and crispy. You don't get that dripping grease when folded. Just mouth watering goodness.

Here's the deal - this is an in&out kind of place. Do not expect an experience or some kind of customer service. The people that work here are literally here to provide you with fried wings (which are OK at best). We walked into this dingy place with music thumping so loud you can barely hear yourself speak. The menu is on a wall and it's pretty straight forward. We ordered about 25 wings in total, with regular fries, seasoned fries, and watermelon punch. Close to 8 people with orders of 10+ wings walked in after us - they were charged and served long before we were (hmmm side eye). The wings are okay, the fries suck, and the service is nonexistent - will not return.

While I've been to Philly a few times before and had cheesesteaks, this is the first time I've tried one from the two biggest names in the city.  I chose Pat's to try first as they're the older of the two.  Geno's, you're next. 
 
ATMOSPHERE:
We must've stepped on dog poop because we luckily found parking right across the street from the restaurant.  As we pulled in, I saw the line that spilled out onto the street.  I was thinking hell no, forget it.  But you know what?  The line moves pretty darn quick, so just do it!  Hordes of cars kept coming and coming with the line at Pat's and Geno's taking turns ebbing and flowing.  Everyone entertained themselves while waiting to get to the ordering window, especially in selfies with the neon biz sign.  Once you near the ordering window is when you'll see the menu and "how to order" signs.  The first window handles strictly sandwich orders.  If you want sides or drinks, you order and pay again at the second window.  Picnic table-style seating wraps around the fluorescent-lit covered lanai.  There are no restrooms or place to wash your hands.  Napkin dispensers are readily available to mop up the messy job at hand.
 
MENU:
Steak sandwiches in 13 varieties, roast pork, hot dog, fish cake, fries in 4 varieties.  Water, soda, coffee, tea, cocoa.
 
3-STEP ORDERING:
It's beneficial to know what you want by the time you get to the window as things move swiftly.  Step 1: Choose your sandwich.  Step 2: Say "wit" AKA "with" if you want grilled onions in your sandwich.  Step 3: Order your cheese type (cheese whiz is the liquid stuff, provolone or American).
 
FOOD:
Mushroom Cheese Steak - $11.04
I got mine wit (onions) and cheese whiz.  The odd price is so that the total rounds up to an even amount with tax.  No time to deal with change here.  Does it live up to the hype?  I say, sure.  I'm not a cheesesteak aficionado but I thought it was good.  The bread was soft, the rough-chopped steak tender and flavorful with the liquid cheese adding more savory notes and the fresh mushrooms a nice earthy flavor.  It's quite a large sandwich, probably close to a footlong but I finished it!  Had I taken time to read the menu better, I would've ordered the sandwich with peppers too. 
 
SERVICE:
It was a chaotic, comical mess but in an organized way LOL.  I've never paid for and received food so quick in my life, literally within 20 seconds.  The guy taking orders was cool, even double checking that I really wanted onions and mushrooms on my sandwich.  I added on sodas but was told it's ordered at the next window.  Wham, bam, thank you ma'am!
 
TIPS:
Cash only.
 
Open 24/7.
 
OVERALL:
It's something you should experience when visiting Philadelphia.  It may not be the best cheese steak around but these guys are legends in their own way.  We'll see how Geno's compares next time.  Follow/friend me and you'll know soon!

Soft pretzels do not impress me, but my spouse is a big fan.  

ATMOSPHERE:
The simple shop has no tables or chairs, just a stand up counter used mostly as a condiment bar. 

MENU:
They sell a variety of pretzels in different shapes, sizes and flavors, including pretzel dogs, melts and even a cheesesteak version.  Dips include several types mustards, "liquid" cheese, cinnamon, cream cheese, chocolate, buttercream and marinara.  Party trays are also available. 

FOOD:
Salted Pretzel - $1.50 for two
What a deal!  I was wanting the liquid cheese dip but my spouse chose the spicy brown mustard which ended up being very tasty and not too spicy.  The pretzel was soft and chewy as expected. 

SERVICE:
The gal at the counter was friendly and provided quick service. 

TIP:
Yelp states their hours as 24/7 but their website states otherwise. 

OVERALL:
Cheap and tasty, exactly how life should be!

The food was ok. The portions were rather small considering the price. The service was slow and not very friendly. The drinks were weak. They told us in the beginning that we were able to have separate checks and when it was time
To pay they said it was too much of a headache to do it. They gave us the entire everyone paid their portion and the manager came out and proceeded to tell us we were short 55$ when in all actuality we have overpaid by 17$. The manager was really rude and unprofessional. I will never step foot in this establishment again!

Terrible service, extremely long waits for food after you get your order in, mediocre food at best when you get it, and absolutely the worst service EVER.  Save yourself some grief and time.... Don't stop here

Color me completely unimpressed. I dined this evening at Adele's with a group of 9 people tonight and I did not enjoy my meal. Not only was the food mediocre, the service was borderline abysmal. 

The limited menu was small yet the kitchen seemed backed up and s-l-o-w. We arrived at our table at 7 pm and walked out of the restaurant at 10:03 pm. Our server was kind but not the best, and the main problem with this restaurant is the service. We ordered two identical bottles of wine for the table. Our server poured me a sample to try and when I nodded my approval, she moved on to everyone else at the table and filled their glasses but forgot me. Then she opened the second bottle and started topping off the other glasses without letting me try the second bottle! She also still neglected to fill up my glass.

Other spotty service issues included bringing dessert without utensils and my cappuccino (no decaf available, bummer) was served in a cup with no saucer, no spoon, and no sugar. 

The menu items all featured weird combos, were overpriced, and the portions were ridiculously small. The side dishes in particular were rip-offs, as was my pre-dinner cocktail. I ordered a glass of prosecco for $10 and it was outrageous the tiny little glass I was served. I also didn't like that the restaurant didn't have proper wine glasses (the wine list was less than stellar too). 

For dinner I ordered the specials, including a Freekeh salad that consisted of a plate of raw cauliflower with a tiny bit of freekeh. I saw no tomatoes as listed on the menu. The burrata on top was good, however. It was an ugly and unappetizing plate, and the flavors did not work. Salty olives made this a disaster of a dish. 

The appetizers didn't fare much better. There was a so/so steak tartare and a good focaccia with olive plate. The olives at least made sense with this one!

Next up was dinner, salmon with rice, peach chutney and papadums for $32. The fish was delicious and cooked perfectly, with an interesting, salty crust on one side. The other components of the dish were awful and was wholly unsuccessful. The Indian spices made zero sense and the flavor was very unpleasant. This plate was also ugly to look at. 

The best thing on the table were the fried potatoes, but the side dish was extremely small considering the ridiculous $8 cost. 

For dessert I had the coconut cake ($8) and a cappuccino ($4) and I didn't like either one. The cake was completely dried out. No way it was freshly baked and it wasn't worth the calories. It was topped with lime shavings which ruined the buttercream flavor. The coffee was bitter and again wasn't served with a proper saucer or accoutrements. 

The chef coming up with these odd combos needs to stick to tried and true flavors. This stuff would've been ok if the recipes had been simpler. It felt like the kitchen was just throwing a bunch of ingredients on a plate with no regard if they were a good pairing or not. 

I do not recommend this restaurant. It's overpriced and not great. I left hungry because the portions were too small. There are too many good places to eat in Nashville than to waste your time and money here.

This place isn't good. As first-time visitors to the area, we didn't know any better. I'm here to warn you so you don't make the same expensive mistake we did. 

We were in downtown Tampa for a hockey game and since this place was close to the arena, we went here for pre-game drinks and dinner. There was a good crowd, so we figured it would be a decent place to eat. It isn't. 

We arrived around 4:30 pm and were seated immediately. There's a large bar area and then a large dining area with booths and a view of the street. We were given a large booth which was very comfortable. We were delighted at the menu at first glance, because EVERYTHING sounded so appealing. I couldn't decide what I wanted to eat because I wanted to order it all. 

Our server soon came over, and boy was she a weird one. She started talking about her ex-boyfriend and how she hated working restaurant jobs...just really strange. I asked her drink recommendations and she suggested the Key Lime Margarita ($8.50). I ordered that. Hubby had a classic Manhattan ($10). My drink was excellent, if very small. It was also super sweet, so watch out if you aren't a fan of sugary drinks. The amount of liquor was appropriate too. 

For starters, we chose the spinach and crab dip. It sounded so good on the menu, but it was one of many of the over promise / under deliver food items. At a $15 price point, this should've been much better. We were served a small dish of frozen spinach thrown in a bowl topped with basic melted cheddar cheese and a scoop of crabmeat on top. The presentation and the ingredients were exceptionally disappointing. I could've made this at home, and it tasted freezer burned. 

I wanted fresh seafood, so I got the grilled salmon. This was a really weird dish. The salmon was fresh and well prepared, but it sat atop some sad roasted potatoes, a couple of raw artichoke hearts, and some pitiful wilted spinach. At the base was a thick coating of tomato paste. Yes, paste. It was gross and tasted really nasty. Nothing about these ingredients worked together. What in the world was the kitchen thinking?

Hubby fared better with his order of classic fried shrimp with fries. He added grilled asparagus ($1.50 upcharge for 3 spears). His food was good, but we both got tired of nibbling on it about halfway through. Grease goes a loooong way! 

During our meal, we asked our server for a side of Ranch dressing for thr fries, and this started up a long discussion about how she has to charge for extra sauces because the kitchen can't make money, they used to offer it for free but then they were losing money left and right. Um, okay lady, that's way too much information. The service was decent aside from the tall drink of strange that was our waitress. 

I was shocked when our check came and the total was $99.83! That is just an outrageous amount of money for how bad the food was. Granted, that included 3 drinks, but still! The bar food was decent, but avoid anything that sounds even slightly creative or chef-driven. And please, please don't order that nasty crab dip appetizer. It makes me gag just thinking about it now.

I was looking for a divey, cafeteria style place to grab a hearty lunch and P&G fit the bill. I was disappointed that there wasn't a selection of green vegetables on the day I visited since that was what I was looking for. I ended up getting the daily crab cake lunch special, which was nothing more than carbohydrate central. 

The extraordinarily salty crab cakes were mostly cornmeal and were very dry and bland. I had to chug three huge bottles of water after I ate them. The side of French bread was mediocre too, but at least it had been buttered and toasted. The standout of the plate was the truly delicious macaroni and cheese. It was loaded with gooey goodness and black pepper, giving it an authentic Southern spicy kick. 

This place has all the charm of a sterile hospital cafeteria so I chose to get my lunch to go. The employees were friendly and my lunch was less than $10. I would've loved this place if they had offered some Southern style greens -- maybe they do on other days since the menu changes daily.

I grew up in the rural South, a place where we gathered at my Grandmama's house every Sunday to eat her famous fried chicken. Is Willie Mae's chicken as good as Grandmama's? Nah, it's not. But it sure is close! This place is legit and needs to be added to every foodie's must-eat list. 

I arrived early (at 10 am) and while there were only a couple of folks already seated in the inside dining room, the takeout area already had a pretty large crowd. I watched as a steady stream of local construction workers would roll in and get their usual and then roll back out. We were seated at a small table in the dining room, which has an authentic Southern flair. It really did make me feel like I was back home. The hospitality felt very family oriented too; as a tourist I didn't feel that I was an annoyance to anyone (we were the only tourists in there by the way). Now did we get some stares from folks? Yeah, but that was most likely because of our "Yankee" accents. It was obvious that "ya'll ain't from 'round here."  

We both opted for the fried chicken plate (white meat costs extra). The chicken was moist on the inside and crispy on the outside. It was a wonderfully juicy, delicious and traditional plate of fried chicken. The rice and gravy was killer good but wasn't what I was used to as a kid (it was spicy brown gravy instead of white gravy, which confused me at first but it tasted great)! Of course I had to order the green beans since that's one of my favorite foods ever, and they were tasty as expected. 

The restaurant is very unassuming and it's just a little house in the middle of a regular neighborhood. Parking is on the street. If you're up for it, come early when they open at 10 am to avoid the wait. Remember that it's never too early for some lip smackin' good fried chicken.

I loved this restaurant! I initially stopped by to get a coffee and cookie but I was so intrigued by the menu (and over the moon about my cookie) that I dragged my husband back the next day for lunch. I'm so glad I did! 

Willa Jean has a modern Southern menu. The sleek, industrial dining room is comfortable yet cozy with a stunning interior design that compliments the surrounding area of the city. Service was efficient and cordial. Get your cameras ready because the kitchen puts out some beautiful plates of food. We shared a few items including the fried chicken sliders, crab toast, cheesy broccoli casserole, and honey bathed chicken thighs. All were pricey but worth it. The local Zapp's potato chips disappeared quickly, and eventually so did every last crumb on my plate.

This was a very memorable meal. If you don't have time to dine, at least stop by the takeout bakery and get a chocolate chip cookie and biscuit. Both are among the best of the best treats I've had anywhere in the world.

First thing id like to say about this place is that the decor is amazing. The whole place is decked out in old farm tools and loads of art pieces. Just the inside could be on exhibit. Then they have two oldschool cars outback that you have to check out! But i dont even know where to start with the food, everthing you place in your mouth explodes with flavor. My favorites are the lettuce wraps & the debris fries. Your must get there BBQ plates & their specials of the day!

I'm sorry, but I am just not on the "Rooster and the Till" bandwagon.  I understand Tampa's obsession with trying to create a trendy, hipster type persona, but this place is trendied into obscurity. First, when I go to a restaurant, I want to eat, not snack.  This Tapas style menu is just not my thing, so a bunch of $17 4 oz appetizers is going to get old really fast.  Even that I could stand, but the obscure and bizarre combinations of flavors was way over the top, all in the name of "trendy".  Grouper paste on Ribeye, really?  By the way, that was the most palatable of these little appetizers, the rest were just strange.  

I'm from LA and seen my share of these trendsetting ubercool eateries, but R&T fails where it counts.  If you want to spend $100 a person and feel like you are cool because you ate something you wouldn't even consider tasting anywhere else, then Rooster and the Till is your spot.

One of my MOST favorite Santa Barbara finds! I can't remember what I was searching for at the time but as soon as I came across this turkish delight spot, only 5-10 minutes from our hotel the family and I HAD to explore! Needless to say, good ole Yelp never steers us wrong!

The best baklava, halva and turkish delights one can find! Innovative flavors, great combinations, high quality too! 

I feel bad for a friend of ours, I had her try Turkish coffee for the first time when she was craving a "regular cup of joe" she was not feeling it! However, Turkish kava is a different coffee drinking experience all together!

This place is very aesthetically pleasing, clean and CAN GET busy!  I encourage you to explore the various sweet treats Lokum has to offer, grab a shot of Turkish coffee just for bragging rights! ;) And enjoy the well thought out and designed atmosphere!

The best place in Reno for KBBQ! There are so many things to choose from and the service is always quick and friendly. Also, kind of random but their playlist is *insert multiple fire emojis*, it's also the chefs playlist! My friends and I are pretty much regulars here and they definitely provide the best service compared to the other KBBQ place in town, and even when ordering wayyyy too much food, they always get it right. You're also able to order boba from the Asian express side, and they have a pretty impressive wine list. The Hawaiian steak, chardol, any of the pork bellies, and kimchi tofu soup are my go to staples.

If you're looking for a warm bowl of hearty ramen this winter, Haru has got you covered. There aren't many ramen places in Reno, but out of all of them recently Haru has become my personal best. The broth is very flavorful no matter which ramen base you choose and like other places you are able to customize the spice level to your desired preference. 

Their appetizers are also very tasty and I highly recommend trying the chicken karaage, gyoza or takoyaki. If you're not feeling noodles they also have a variety of Japanese rice dishes and curry to choose from. When I last visited, the restaurant was very COVID-19 compliant, everything was extremely clean and the entire restaurant followed social distancing guidelines.

Oh My! Came here for birthday brunch, it was a pleasant surprise.  The atmosphere was pleasant on a Sunday it was poppin.  The food was plentiful and so good.  Lots of options.. breakfast meats, made to order omlettes, waffles, soul food, fish, collards, chicken, pasta, fruits, desserts... so much food and it was all seasoned well, nice and hot.. I'm really not a fan of buffets but I'm a super fan of good food.  Relish showed me not all buffets should be lumped into one, I couldn't stop raving about how delicious everything was and everyone was nice welcoming, it was a great experience, everyone looked like they were in the stat of food pleasure, lol.  They have indoor and then somewhat of a sunroom dining area as well.  The layout is pretty interesting.  I would definitely come back for a great meal.

Roti, doubles, plantain, pure deliciousness... I went back n forth between 4 n 5 stars because man it takes a lot for me to give a 5... But there was no reason found to deprive them of the final star.... Ok so I love coming in here, they are sooooo nice, love the song song Trini accent, smells great and best of all I know I'm in for a great meal. I started off here with my go to... Curry goat Roti... I have this spot in Bklyn that I compare all Roti too, this is meets the mark, and best of all no Ny lines! Lol. So their Roti is always full, meat and potatoes busting through... I have never eaten a whole one in one sitting... But then again I never have anywhere, but I legit only have about 1/3 of it and save the rest for dinner.... Well that's also because I never walk out without doubles... They have shrimp doubles that is to die for... Someone like me who loves curry shrimp but can't commit to a whole shrimp Roti when goat is available this is a perfect compromise... The best part is they mango sauces... For someone like me who loves spice, grew up on it, but now my delicate stomach can no longer take it, instead of hot sauce I get mango sauce, the flavors are amazing with a slight kick.. Love it! Seriously I can not come to this strip without stopping here... I'll come for something else and end up leaving with both... It'll be the weekend, and I'll be like hmmm should I drive the hour for some Roti?! I haven't yet, but I have made it out twice in a week, yup, it's worth it!

The fact that I have only had takeout from here and am blown away every single time is amazing! This place was recommended to me years ago, and it's been on my list for a while, why I took so long to come here is beyond me and I will be mad at myself for that until I eat my weight in their Risotto Crema di Pesce... Trust me since our first visit I have been on a mission to do just that... it's soooooo good, like extremely good, like you have to try it for your life to be complete good.. Let me not take away from anything else on their menu, because everything I have had is top notch.. from the longhots, to the filet bruschetta for apps, the mustard seed salmon and Jumbalaya.. It's all so good.  So much so that since it was just my fiance and I for Easter dinner, we decided it order rather than cook a big meal, we were not at all disappointed.. We ordered from the special menus which thankfully included the seafood risotto and we had their leg of lamb and honey ham... Every order is packaged well, including bread & salad. The ordering process is simple, the staff is friendly.  I have nothing but praises.  They have indoor and outdoor seating, both look lovely, I look forward to dining with them as well.  No hesitation with my 5 stars at all!

I've been here a few times now and I have mixed feelings about it.  It's one of those places that everyone raves about so you feel like you should love it, but I don't.  I mean I think they are okay.  Their wings are good, but nothing spectacular.  I personally could do without the nickel and diming that adds up in this place. I had wings here, sauced and un-sauced, I don't really like their sauce, or maybe I just haven't found the right mix, but considering when I got dry wings with sauce on the side I was charged for the initial sauce as well as the extra, as if they didn't give me less than if I had gotten the wings sauced, I don't see me trying multiple sauces, and they dry wings really aren't that good.  Oh and also not a fan of them asking if you want celery and bleu cheese but not telling you that for the 4 1/2 stalks of celery and teeny drop of bleu cheese that they are going to charge you $1.20.  Yea for some reason I'm not a fan of excess charges.  My last visit I tried the mac & cheese balls, I asked and the waitress said they were awesome.. unfortunately I disagree, I wasn't a fan.. I do like their fries though, they are pretty good. When their check in offer was 50% off wings, I think it was worth it.. now with the $5 off, it doesn't entice much since all it does is cover the extra charges.  Will I be back.. eh it's a possibility, but I'm not in a rush.

We were in the Phoenixville, PA area this past weekend for my son's wedding.  On his wedding day, I picked him up so we could have some quality time while his mother and his bride to be had their hair and makeup done.  He suggested we stop by the Nook and Kranny Kafe.  I am very glad he did!  This is a very small place, but they sure moved the food and the tables.  My son ordered the two eggs, bacon, toast and hash browns.  He is a classic trained Chef and he said his food was excellent.  He and his now bride eat here often, so I certainly trust their selections.  I ordered the Ultimate Breakfast sandwich that featured sausage, fried egg, avocado and pepper jack cheese.  I ordered a cup of fruit for my side.  My sandwich was very good!  Excellent service and a nice atmosphere.

After being a loyal customer for almost two years now to the Plumb location, this is pretty much our favorite sushi restaurant in town. We love the staff, we love the sushi, and the to-go specials they have been offering during COVID can't be beat. We still order here at least once a week, and they recognize me by name on the phone at this point lol. It is our absolute favorite to sit at the bar for all you can eat sushi, but since we haven't been comfortable sitting indoors yet the take out here has been helping us survive quarantine. They did set up some outdoor tables with umbrellas which look super cute, so we will likely venture there soon :)

The food was tasty but the service was SO bad. I'm talking we-waited-two-hours-and-our-food-still-didnt-come-bad. It's a shame because I had read so many good Yelp reviews about this place and my co-workers wouldn't shut up about how good it was. And yes when the food came two hours after we were seated, it WAS good. But it was a day late and a dollar short. 

Would I eat from this place again? Maybe, but I'll be getting it to-go. I don't think I've ever experienced such bad service in a restaurant before. They literally brought us random food that we didn't order and took hours bringing out the food we did. Maybe we just came at a bad time but it was 12pm on a Friday, they should've been prepared for an increase in the demand.

[And to the waitress with the short pixie cut (yeah I'm calling you out) who complained about having to serve such a large crowd and who wasn't the least bit apathetic about having us wait hours for our food, I hope you got an even bigger crowd after we left. ]

The reviews got this one right. We decided to have a Geno's/Pat's showdown and Geno's lost and lost badly.

We went at an off hour so we wouldn't have to wait on a long line. We had the cheesesteak with onions and whiz. When we opened the wrapper, we were greeted with more bread than anything else. The sandwich didn't have a lot of meat and what meat it had was very overcooked. There was also a tremendous amount of grease.  

If it is a choice between Geno's and Pat's, I would go with Pat's.

Absolutely LOVED everything about Jason Aldeans! Their staff is wonderful, their bands were fantastic, and their rooftop view is perfection!! To top it off, our favorite cidery in Asheville has beers at Jason Aldeans! We were very happy and pleasantly surprised!! If you like cider, get the Bold Rock! It's only 12g sugar and tastes like pure heaven!

This is an awesome atmosphere for live music and multiple floors to enjoy the talent!  The rooftop is a beautiful view of the entire Broadway strip! Luke's and Jason Aldeans share a roof, so you can easily pass from one to the other. The bands at Luke's were fantastic! We found the rooftop to be very spacious and not nearly as crowded, with plenty of seating options from bar stools to couches. The rooftop was also very clean and well kept.

Probably one of the best places to get an actually awesome Philly Cheesesteak!  They are always crowded with a long line, but they have a full on system, and it works.

I LOVE their cheesesteak and I always add their hot peppers.  Service is great and friendly, but keep in mind that they are almost always packed (I am talking 99.9% of the time, there is a line out the door) so they are trying to keep things moving and help everyone.  

Everything about the cheesesteaks here is awesome.  The bread is great, as is the meat and cheese.  It doesn't fall apart the minute you start eating it...its just perfect.  They are also HUGE, so you can take half home, or eat the whole thing!

Street parking in a mostly residential area, so be prepared to look for a spot for a little while, especially if you are here on a weekend.

I highly suggest coming here if you are looking for a GREAT Philly Cheesesteak!  I also suggest adding the hot peppers (you can either order them or they are on the counter where you eat in a jar) if you don't mind a nice spice!

This rating is not for their expensive product. They do produce great donuts and some other items. I do not mind paying extra for a good product. I do, however, have an issue with poor customer service. I have been a customer on many occasions and each time have never experienced great customer service. It always seems like it is an inconvenience for the staff to assist a customer. Today proved to be no different. Today, the unprofessionally dressed, indifferent staff barely acknowledged me and definitely offered no closure to the encounter.  The one individual is always there in the morning but clearly is miserable regardless of time or day. I have decided that I will no longer go to Lochels. Their recent fame is based on their quality of the product. I am certain they will never win a customer service award.

While visiting good ole St. Petersburg, my cousin invited us for dinner since he was making some ribs. I let him know I would like to bring something because I hate showing up empty handed. Well the weather was not being kind so we just went straight there and I asked my cousin to come with me to the store so we could get something everybody would like and spend some quality time together. We headed up to Publix to get something from the deli but when I saw that their deli no longer makes it fresh, he made a call to his mom and she recommended Cesarina. 

When we arrived, there was a line but OMG did this place smell good. I looked around while my cousin waited in line. The cases were loaded up with some sides, meats, sausages, desserts and olives. I thought I died and went to heaven. I even found some dried pasta that was hand made that I have not been able to find locally. 

I bought some of the potato salad, tortellini salad, two varieties of olives and some marinated artichoke hearts along with 2 bags of pasta to take home to Orlando with me. The ribs my cousin made were lip smackin good but those sides and olives were ALL incredible. The next time I am in Largo, you can bet I will be stopping by this place to grab a few things to take back home to Orlando. 

If you live in the area, you really need to check this place out!!!

While in town visiting my dad, I chose to take him some place special since I was not able to make it for his birthday earlier in the week. Wildflower had an impressive brunch menu so I decided to bring him here. 

Just a heads up...  The main entrance to the restaurant is around back. You put your name on the list and wait. If you want coffee while waiting, ask for it since they do not have coffee at the entrance. They also have an outside patio and are pet friendly. I made friends with two dogs name Charlie and Freckles on the patio this morning. My father learned the hard way that smoking is a big no no on the patio. Being a former smoker I was grateful the hostess informed him the patio is NOT a  designated smoking area and he put it out. 

We looked over the menu and and our server told us about the chef's specials. They sounded delicious but it was the Scrambled Eggs and Applewood Bacon for my wife. Dad selected the Eggs Arnold with roasted potatoes. I was in an Omelet mood so it was The Sunday Omelet "All The Way" and roasted potatoes and a side of grits.

Here is a breakdown of our meal...

Coffee - 3.5 
A high quality pour over would have been a great compliment with my meal.

Dad's plate - 5
Presentation was great and the texture of the croissant was perfect for that dish. The seasoning was great and that Hollandaise sauce was fabulous. 

Wife's plate - 4
The eggs were cooked perfectly and the bacon was nicely crisped. She requested some salsa to top her eggs but it was a mango salsa and not a traditional salsa. It was good but the server should have given her a heads up. It was good but a bit sweet for scrambled eggs.

My plate - 3.5
The flavor of the omelet was stellar but the egg was a wee bit overcooked. I also ordered some salsa and it was a bit sweet for a savory omelet. A traditional salsa or a Pico de Gallo would have been a better match.

Side of Grits - 5
These were hands down some of the best tasting grits I have had. I told my server to let the chef know and he came to the table to thank me personally. 

Service - 4
It was quite busy and it did take a bit longer for our food than expected BUT it did give me time to catch up with dad so it was not too bad given the circumstances. I also noticed they have a help wanted sign so I suspect they were just short staffed. 

After breakfast I went to the market and grabbed some of the Kale Pesto, Honey Butter, a Key Lime Cooler cookie, Oatmeal Cranberry Pecan cookie and 2 raspberry scones. I have tasted everything and all of my choices were wonderful. The Key Lime Cooler was my personal favorite. 

Would I return?  IN A HEART BEAT!!! There were a few minor misses but overall the food and service was on point but I would recommend offering coffee to the waiting guests instead of making them request it. Aside from that I can't think of anything else that can really be improved. If you are in Clearwater on a Sunday...  Go check out their brunch...  Just be aware that you can't get a mimosa until after 11 am. Blame that on Pinellas County though!!!

A Florida Foodie

After checking in we went shopping in downtown St Petersburg. I found the hat and shirt I was looking for. We saw Sea Salt and decided to make a reservation for the patio since I'd heard so many great things about them. 

When we arrived for dinner, we chose to sit inside and were escorted to a table but baby wanted a booth instead. The place is stunning and so Kudos to their designer! I made it clear we'd never been to Sea Salt before but when our server came to the table, she came as us just like an order taker and never really explained anything about what sets them apart. I had a dirty knife in my setting and my server seemed a bit annoyed I pointed it out and asked for a new knife. Not a good first impression to be blunt...

Baby wanted water and I had my usual iced tea with lime. The server seemed to know the menu but was not trying to the sell menu. She was merely going through the motions and kept rushing us for an answer. At one point I was getting annoyed.  We chose to start with 6 oysters and followed up with the Tomato Basil and Zucchini soup. She selected the Ahi Tuna and I opted for the Red Snapper with some Broccoli Ricotta Au Gratin as a side.

We were brought some bread and hummus while waiting for the oysters. It would have been nice if we were offered more of it. Sigh... The black sea salt gave it a "boiled egg" taste which I really enjoyed. Next up were the oysters. We were brought 2 of the Riptide, Sunset Beach and Standish Shore oysters to get us started. They were all good BUT I was not blown away by any means. Given what I heard about their AMAZING oysters, I was just not that impressed. It might have helped if our server pointed us towards which oysters were exceptional that day.

Our soups were brought to us and I tried a bit with each of the three salts. The server poured the soup into the bowl from a metal holding vessel at the table. He exercised great care to ensure the presentation was perfect. I preferred the Himalayan salt with both of the soups but my wife preferred the Hawaiian sea salt. BOTH soups of them had a nice flavor and texture. That goat cheese was a nice touch in both soups. We both preferred the zucchini.

Finally the Ahi Tuna and Red snapper arrive. The Ahi was nicely seared and the presentation was great but I was far from blown away with the taste. The Red Snapper stole the show. The flavor and texture when eaten with the mushrooms was a work of art. A touch of the Hawaiian salt finished it nicely. And I would just like to forget the Broccoli. It was overcooked and overdone. A simple dish of steamed broccoli topped with one of the salts would have been much better.

Bread - 4
Oysters - 3
Tomato Basil Soup - 4
Zucchini Soup - 4
Ahi - 3
Snapper - 5
Broccoli - 1

Atmosphere - 5
Service - 3

I am guessing that we'd have had a much better experience if the server was more helpful navigating the best part of the menu instead of "Figuring it out" without much guidance. When a guest says "We have never dined at Sea Salt before" it is up to the server to guide you through the experience and not to just take your order and seem annoyed for asking questions. If you didn't want to work on the Fourth of July, I get that but don't take it out on MY dining experience. I will come back again in the event their holiday service was just off.

Locale Market did not exist when I lived in St Petersburg BUT after taking a stroll through the market, I can see it would have been a favorite stop of mine if I ever decided to move back there.  I could write a very lengthy review and it would all be good but instead...  

Just look at the photos I am uploading because I took a few of them. 

Locale Market is welcome to open a location here in Orlando!

After tossing around a few places to go for dinner, we finally decided to check out The Burg. I  heard from several of my friends how good the food was and since mama waned to go to first Friday so we could meet up with a friend later, The Burg it was...

To say this place is small is an understatement but it is quite charming. You have an L shaped bar and a few tables inside and some patio tables out front which is nice. It reminded me of a little bar in Pittsburgh that I had been to about 25 years ago only smaller. 

We sat at the bar and the server the two young ladies helping us were very nice. They let my wife sample a couple of the beers so she could make up her mind and were very good as selling the menu. After a bit of indecision on MY part, we decided on the Jerk Chicken and chips for mama and the Gyro and chips with a bowl of the Lemon Chicken soup.

About 20 minutes later the burger and Gyro showed up but they forgot my soup. The Gyro was very good and the Tzatziki was made OLD SCHOOL with yogurt and NOT sour cream. FINALLY a place that stands by tradition. My wife's jerk chicken sandwich was excellent. The jerk blend was not too sweet and not too much kick. It had a nice balance of sweet and hot. The chips were homemade and nice and crunchy but best of all they were not over salted.

One of the servers came to check on us and I let her know about the soup. She apologized for the error and said she would bring me a bowl on the house to make up for it. A few minutes later my soup arrives and OMG was it good. The last time I had Avgolemeno this good was when I was in High School. A good friend was from Greece and his mom did not speak any English but she could cook some incredible food! This soup was on par with hers and I really savored every spoonful.

I wanted to try the homemade Baklava but mama was not well and they had run out so that was a bit of a let down because I was already told how good it was by several others. After finishing up, we requested the bill and to my surprise, she did not remove the soup as she said she would. I never said a word and just paid the bill but when you tell a customer you are going to do something, you should follow through on your word.

Atmosphere - 4
Presentation - 3
Service - 3
Jerk Chicken - 4
Gyro - 4
Avgolemeno - 5
Chips - 4

I can see why this place is popular with the locals and I will definitely be back to try the Baklava. Some of the other items from the menu being served passed by us and everything looked and smelled wonderful so I look forward to future trips here when I am in town...

Review #143 - 2019

After our not so good drinks from Bubble Tea Station, I decided to search for another place to grab my drink & we ended up here.

We showed up around 6:30 PM & the place was empty.

The kids weren't actually in the mood for anything so my nephew, the only one who was actually smart enough not to get a drink at Bubble Tea, decided to get a taro smoothie with boba and he said it was good.

I got the only fresh fruit smoothie that's offered here, which is the avocado smoothie, and it was pretty good.  It was pretty bland, but I didn't mind that they don't add any extra sugar to my drink.  I don't need the extra fat any ways.

My son was actually hungry so he ordered a combination fried rice, which they all decided to share & said it was actually really good.  

Unfortunately, the portion is quite small here so I guess we should've ordered another one; but we were planning to have AYCE KBBQ for dinner, I didn't want them to over eat before dinner.

The place is actually cute & clean.  I guess they were in the process of getting ready to clean up for the evening when we showed up since the lady was mopping the front.

We stayed for a good 45 minutes playing Uno & the lady didn't mind us being there that whole time.

Friendly and accommodating service!

Review #203 - 2020

After our 3.5-hour long drive into Reno on Thanksgiving night, I wasn't in the mood to hunt for food so I let my husband & the kids decide on what they wanted to eat.

Unfortunately, most places are closed on Thanksgiving Day so it was already going to be hard to find a place that's open, let alone at 10 PM.

Luckily, they found a place that was still open until 1 AM & had some pretty good reviews to back it up.  They do offer delivery, but just not to our hotel.  Darn it!

So, they placed an order for a large half pepperoni and cheese (for the girls) and half spicy Hawaiian pizza with alfredo sauce, per my request.

I went with the chicken alfredo since I'm not a big fan of pizza; but I'm willing to eat it, if it's made without marinara sauce.

We arrived about 25 minutes later and picked up our order.

We were all starving so we decided to just sit and eat in the car, which was a very good thing, because we then realized it was not enough food for the 5 of us.

The girls attacked the pepperoni and cheese half while I took a slice of the spicy Hawaiian and it was very tasty.  Sadly, the pizza was a lot smaller than we anticipated so I felt like I was stealing their food.  Their large is more of a medium compared to most places.

Unfortunately, since everyone was starving, I didn't get a picture of the pizza.

My chicken alfredo was pretty good, but it was a little dry so it could've used a little more alfredo sauce.

My husband then picks up his phone and places an order of spicy chicken alfredo for our son, since he liked mine, but his was actually much tastier because it had the perfect amount of sauce and a kick of spice.

He also ordered a Bolls calzones, which he seemed to enjoy.  I took a small bite of the breading and it was actually very moist and buttery.  He ate less than half of it since he over ordered the second time around.

The food is actually good, but portion is pretty small for the price.

Next time we're back in Reno and craving pizza or can't find a late night food option, we know where to turn to!

Review #240 - 2018

My brother and his family are big sushi fans so when I told him I'd take him to my favorite AYCE sushi spot, he was super excited...until I told him that all the rolls come with rice.

Sadly, he and his wife are on a strict diet, they avoid eating rice--so going to AYCE sushi didn't make any sense so I suggested that we come to Bluefin for poke instead.  However, they've never had poke before so they didn't know what to expect.

While we were driving here, we had a really hard time finding the place and the stupid GPS kept sending us around the block until I decided to call the place at 7:55 PM and ask where exactly they were located.  Let me remind you that they close at 8 PM.  Yes, we had 5 minutes to find the place and place our orders for six people.

The young man who answered the phone was super sweet and told us that we were still welcome to come in and I was overjoyed because we were stressed out from all that driving.  When we got to the front door, it was 7:58 PM and I told the young that I was the one who called.  He smiled and said, "you made it!"

It took me about a minute to get my order because I'm already a pro at this ordering thing.  I went back to order everyone's bowl for them because none of them knew what they wanted.

The three young people who were serving us were super friendly, patient and accommodating.  I wish I'd asked to take a picture of them, but I'm sure that management can figure out who they are from the date and time.  We were there on Tuesday, August 7th.

Kuddos to the wonderful team!

All of us enjoyed our poke bowls.  My brother and his wife, who've never had poke before, said it was super good!  Ingredients were super fresh!

We'll definitely be back...

**Sadly, since we went to eat at the park and it was getting dark, my picture was kind of blurry.**

Review #141 - 2019

About a year ago, I came here & left disappointed because they were closed for 5 days while I was here around Thanksgiving time--which was understandable & forgivable.

Luckily, this time we showed up during summer since the kids had just finished school & I wanted to take them out to enjoy a few days of good eating.

We showed up around 6 PM on Monday, June 10th, and the place was actually pretty quiet.  I expected it to be a lot busier considering it was 93-degrees out, but I was fine with not having to fight the crowd.

The 3 kids got almost exactly the same thing, the matcha/vanilla, while my other nephew got the ube & I went with the ube/black sesame.

I really wanted to give this place a 5-star review since the people here are very friendly & accommodating.

The place is small, but clean and still felt comfortable with the table arrangements.  I love the cute set up, especially their Instagram wall.

The kids really enjoyed their dessert & I liked mine too, but I wish it was a little less sweet & a little creamier.  It didn't really taste like soft serve ice cream, more of a sorbet texture, which I wouldn't mind if it was more of a fruity flavor.

Portion seemed much bigger than I expected so I couldn't finish the whole thing, even with my daughter's help.

The kids had a nice time hanging out there playing Uno for about an hour.

We'll definitely be back in the future.

Review #368 - 2018

After my disappointment at KRĒM being closed, I decided to give Icecycle a call just to make sure that they were open.

The eight of us showed up around 1:30 PM on Saturday, November 24th.  The outside looked dark so my brother commented that they might be closed, but I told him that I'd called and made sure they were open.

The young girl who was working that day was very friendly and patient.  She took her time to help us sample whatever we wanted.

I tried some kind of wine flavor, which I forget the name, but it was pretty good.  I also tried another flavor which I can't remember, but it was too sweet for my liking.  I decided to go with the "just ginger" on a sugar cone out of the three flavors that I tried.  It was actually really good!

My younger sister got the curry banana, which she said she really liked so she insisted that I tried hers to see if I'd like it.  I thought it was pretty good and definitely a very interesting flavor.

The place is very cute and even offers a 10% discount if you ride your bike.

Review #030 - 2018

I've been a fan of Raising Cane's since we first gave them a try back in 2014.  We always look forward to enjoying the moist tasty chicken fingers every time we visit Reno or Las Vegas.

This trip was no different.  I decided to visit this location because it was closer to downtown Reno and it stays open until midnight on weekends.

When we showed up around 8:30 PM on Saturday night, the place wasn't too busy; but as we sat & waited for our orders, we noticed the place was packed with college kids.  Of course, it's right next to the college so it made total sense to stay open later.

This location does not have a drive-thru and it is smaller than the other location; however, the employees here are super friendly and helpful.  They definitely stand out from all other fast food establishments in that arena.

Review #111 - 2016

You'll notice that I rarely write reviews for fast food restaurants since there's really low to no expectation on the quality of food being served on my part.  In all honesty, my motto in life is "if you expect quality then don't expect it to be quick".

I have no idea why people expect a fast food restaurant to serve 5-star food and service.  But that's just my personal thought...

Now, on to my review as to why I felt the need to write a review about this Popeye's.  I didn't feel that the food was any better than any other Popeye's that I've visited.  But on the Sunday of May 29th, around 1:30'ish, I brought my sister and nieces in to order some snacks before we started walking around the outlet in that awful heat.

My 7-year old niece is actually really hard to please when it comes to food, she won't try anything new.  She won't eat meat except for chicken nuggets & pepperoni so it makes it really hard to take her anywhere.  

However, while we were placing our orders, the young man who was helping us was really sweet and patient.  He didn't rush us even though we kept trying to convince our niece to pick something.  He even gave her a piece of the Cajun fries to taste before we decided to buy her an order.  He definitely went above and beyond his duty to ensure that our niece was happy.  

I'm giving 5-stars just for his service...

Review #156 - 2017

I'm surprised that I haven't written a review for this place yet since I've been back three times already.

The first time we came here was for Memorial Day weekend and they just so happened to be opened later than most other AYCE sushi bar & their reviews looked pretty good so I decided to give them a try.

We came in around 30 minutes before closing with group of 8 and they were still friendly even though we stayed a past closing.

Today, we came in for lunch and had plenty of time to stuff our faces with as many rolls as possible.

Their food is good and service has always been consistently excellent.

The biggest deal breaker for me is that their restaurant is bigger than most places so we never had to wait to be seated.

I guess we won't need to look for another AYCE sushi place in Reno for awhile...

Review #369 - 2018

I honestly do not care for buffets because I'm not a big eater and I'm always afraid of catching some food borne illness or food poisoning because there's so much cross contamination in these types of environment where everyone's touching the same serving utensils.

I've been here twice for their Sunday brunch, which includes complimentary wine, champagne or beer.  However, since none of us drinks, we didn't take advantage of the alcohol.

The first time we came to try it just because I had a free coupon for all three of us to dine in, and the second time was a buy one get one free offer.

Even though this place has plenty of selections, I enjoyed the fruits and salads the most so I tried to stick to just those.  Although, I did have a few pieces of bacon and some scrabbled eggs for my protein intake.

The most important thing is that the boys really enjoyed themselves and got our money's worth.  

Sadly, they complained about not feeling so good afterwards so I'm not sure if it's because of the food.

Review #102 - 2020

I had this spot bookmarked prior to our mini getaway because it was new and had a few good reviews, some of which were a little too good to be true so I should've seen the sign that it was probably written by friends or family of the owners.

The 7 of us showed up at around 6:20 PM on Saturday, June 13th.

The place is very cute, but that's probably about all there is.

We each ordered our drinks and I specifically asked if any of their drinks are made with fresh fruits and the guy told me that all their fruit drinks are made with fresh fruit, which was awesome! 

Much to my surprise, my avocado smoothie and my daughter's mango smoothie had a very strong powder taste so I told them that neither drinks tasted like fresh fruits & the lady, whom must have been the owner, told me that only their drinks on the smoothie list were made with fresh fruits.  Thanks for the clarification!

She told me if I wanted, I can tell her what I wanted the next time I come back, which will be a never-- since I only took two sips of my drink and tossed it at a gas station.  

My daughter hated her mango smoothie & refused to take a second sip of it so hers went in the trash as well!

My son got the house milk tea, which is basically a Thai iced tea, and it was ok.  You really can't mess up something that simple.

My 11-year old niece got an Okinawa milk tea, which she also said tasted like Thai iced tea, which was very odd.

My 15-year old niece got the cheese foam green tea & she said it was ok, but she wouldn't order it again.

My two nephews got two different types of lemonade drinks, and they were the only two who said their drinks tasted like what they ordered.

So, just as a mean joke, the next day before we left Reno, I asked the kids if anybody wanted a drink from Num Num for our drive back home and they all yelled, "Please no!  We're good with bottled water!"

Never coming back to this place!

Review #029 - 2018

When I saw the reviews and photos, I expected this place to be a small boba type setting rather than a full service restaurant.

We showed up around 1:30 PM on Saturday and the place wasn't too busy so we were seated right away.

I wanted to try a little bit of everything since they had a pretty big menu selection.

Our salty pork belly fried rice showed up first and I have to say that it was very flavorful.  You can definitely tell that they use MSG here, but it wasn't overwhelming to the point where you'll get sick.

The pancake wrapped pork was actually our favorite out of everything we ordered.  The boys really enjoyed it.

The fried pork intestine was pretty good as well, although it had a little too much fat so it gave us a slight head ache.

The pork stomach with pickled mustard was just ok.  I actually had high expectations because I like pickled mustard and was hoping that it would be bursting with flavor, but it came out pretty bland.

Our least favorite, was the Taiwanese noodle with chicken, which the waitress recommended.  The noodles were dry so it didn't absorb any flavors.

We each ordered a drink and I enjoyed my pina colada slushie.

Service was decent for a Chinese place.

We also received a 10% discount for checking into Yelp!  Yay!

We'll definitely be back for the items that we enjoyed and try something else next time.

Sometimes you find the perfect place and Tennessee Brewing was and is the prefect place. The beer was good the staff was amazing the food was delightful.  The atmosphere was perfect.  The upper deck allowed for a picturesque view of the city. The lower decks and patios gave the feel of your own back yard with family and friends. The staff was so helpful with explaining about their beers.  They took the time to describe their beers and how their flights should be drank to get the most enjoyment from flavors.  Once we settled into a spot and began to soak in the view and tease our taste buds with some down home great beers our food showed up. We were just knocked of our feet with the flavors and visual presentation of meal.  It was our last night in town and the experience at Tennessee Brewing was spectacular.

My expectations were admittedly high - I wanted some serious Italian cuisine in Philadelphia.  Is that too much to ask?  Here, yes.  It was amateur hour from the very beginning, and I sincerely hope it's because this restaurant just opened or something.  Let's first start with the most obvious - La fourno is incorrect Italian.  It should be Il forno.  And that pretty much sums up the experience at La fourno.  The lighting upstairs is all off - way too bright - and the rest of the atmospherics just seemed a bit thrown together.  I was served a lemon wedge in my gin martini (really?), it had ice cubes in it, they didn't have Hendricks or Tanqueray (only Sapphire), and it tasted all wrong.  I sent it back asking for some vermouth.  The manager asked me a couple of times if try #2 was better, and I guess it was better but still off.  Sure, it's fine.  They struck it from the bill, but c'mon people, gin martinis are not complicated.  Their success with the drink foreshadowed the meal.  I ordered the "star" menu item, a $28 veal parmaggiano that tasted like they dumped a whole jar of Prego and then melted a block of Kraft parmesan on top of it.  The accompanying pasta met similar success, probably store bought.  I should have known better but I ordered an espresso after the meal and it tasted like just really strong bitter coffee with just a hint of crema atop it.  When you shell out $55 for a meal like I did here, I'm sorry Philly, I just expected more.

Get their coupons online before coming here! You can get a free coffee drink with any purchase. 3 beignets and an iced cafe au lait after the coupon cost $4.92 as of 4/18/2015. The beignets are soooo good. However, do NOT get them if you are wearing black, and it's best if you eat them there just because they are so messy to eat. Wipe your seat off just in case, the powdered sugar tends to get everywhere.

Only disappoint was the cafe au lait is pre-mixed. If you get it iced they just pour it out of a gallon jug. You can get better coffee from Cafe Du Monde.

Oh and there's a charge if you want to use your credit card for a purchase under $5, just FYI.

We decided to go to LongHorn for lunch before we went downtown. The waitress came and got our drink orders and then waited to take our orders. Everything seemed to be going well as she brought the bread out pretty fast. 

Things took a weird turn when she brought the food out. She set the food down and walked away. I tried the mac and cheese and it was really gross in my opinion. It tasted like onion or chives. I put my fork down inside further and got a noodle covered in cheese and tried it again. Again it just tasted like onion and I hate onion. My husband tried it too and said the same thing. I felt grossed out so I didnt want to eat it. When the waitress finally came, my mother in law told her about the mac and cheese. The waitress responded really rudely. She said "thats funny because theres no onion so how are you tasting onion... and we never had this problem before." Instead of simply apologizing and attempting to fix it she was rude and cold. When she grabbed it to throw it away I saw her roll her eyes. The funny part is there was green things inside that looked like chives and she told me they never added onion. I politely asked for mashed potatoes instead and she brought it out... rudely. She seemed pretty annoyed from that point on. It made me feel really crappy and guilty moving forward because I wasnt trying to make a big deal out of it. 


At the end of the meal, my mother in law asked to check the balance on a gift card. The waitress was irritated that she had to check the balance. She was trying to be nice about it but I can tell she was irritated. I got back to the table and saw her over the table discussing the bill and trying to fix it. I saw the bill and mentioned that she left the mac and cheese on there which was an additional charge. She rudely grabbed the receipts and said "yah I didnt take it off so I will fix it I guess". She huffed away angrily. The best part is she sent someone else out to give us the receipts and the money they owed us from charging us for the mac and cheese. We saw her walk to another table and she looked really mad. We were absolutely shocked that she had such a negative reaction over a tiny mistake mentioned. 

This really ruined the experience for me. The food was pretty good. I did enjoy the mashed potatoes once they came out. The ribs were really good as well. To me though, when the service is hostile it really dampers the mood. I dont want to be treated rudely because I didnt like the way something tasted. Hopefully my in laws will try to give this place another try but with a different waitress.

| Woohoo Noodle Shop |

A trendy and modern take on a traditional dish like ramen. Ordering is simple via touch screens at the entrance. The choices range from poke to ramen to rice bowls, so there is a bit of something for every pallet. 

I ordered the spicy chicken ramen and it was easy to customize the order with my spice on the side (or s.o.s as it's labeled). I did notice that the fee for swapping or adding ingredients averaged $2 - $3 per item, which seemed steep and could inflate the total price quickly.

My order arrived quickly and was tasty (hoisin and spicy sauce are magical toppings). I was confused about how to properly use the namesake wooden ladle, but I just did what felt right. I also ordered fried dough for dessert, and even though I had to remind the server that I ordered it, the dish was tasty and came with dipping options. 

Service was great and very attentive. The decor is cool with the ramen themed anime on the walls. I will definitely return to try different dishes.

| BurgerTown Burgers |

I'll start off by saying I had great service. I see in previous reviews service has been an issue so maybe they've heard those complaints and improved. I also went early in the day and it was busy. 

I really enjoyed my meal which didn't take too long to be served after ordering. I got a Brewtown Burger which is an ale infused burger with multiple fixings. It was a very nice size and I was stuffed by the end of my meal. I will say there wasn't really a different taste with the burger being "infused" but I appreciate the creativity. They did unfortunately change the waffle fries to a premium side so it costs extra. Also my server was very nice and helpful. I will definitely return to try some of there other items on the menu.

If you're looking for the perfect pizza in a relaxed yet trendy atmosphere then you can't go wrong with Pizzeria Vetri. There is something about their dough that just cannot be matched by any other pizza place. I'd recommend getting pizza, calzone and the fried dough dessert just to experience how amazing and versatile their dough is. This place is consistently amazing, has a great bar and fun atmosphere. Can't go wrong!

I had been to Kinme a number of times prior to COVID and always loved their food, quaint atmosphere and service. However, I came to write this review as they have been a stand out restaurant during the pandemic. I order sushi from them nearly once per week and it is always extremely fresh, fast for delivery, and delicious. Even under extreme times, their quality has maintained its excellence. I've never had any issues with any order ever. This place is great for classic rolls or special rolls (the one with the cilantro and yellow tail is my favorite!) I'd recommend this place to anyone looking for delicious sushi! 

PS I actually ate here for my first sushi after 9 months while I was staying around the corner at Pennsylvania hospital after having a baby. As a sushi lover, I looked forward to sushi dinner for months and this was my first choice!

Clean, bright and (relatively) new and spacious. This rest stop is well maintained and the bathroom is always well stocked with tissue paper. The only issue is that most of the fast food restaurants tends to close quite early, we stopped by here twice a little after 10 and most of the shops are cleaning up and closing. Only Starbucks was open and you could see that they were cashing in on this from all the food people where buying from their front cooler fridge.

Oh, and no tax always helps a bit.

We came here a little after 11am on Memorial Day. It was pretty busy but we were seated right away. We have been here before as well as the Sparks location. They both seem very consistent.

Our drink orders were taken and we looked at the menu. My wife said she already knew she wanted "The Works" Belgium waffle and bacon. I decided on the pastrami sandwich. 

Our food was delivered in a timely manner and looked really tasty. I'm a big fan of pastrami sandwiches. Both of us were extremely satisfied and I even had half a sandwich left. I don't think their pastrami is as tender as some other places I've tried but it's still really good. Also, the pastrami sandwich had mustard on it which was not stated in the menu.

The food and service are good, prices are decent and there's a nice selection. We will be back to Jack's.

My wife had to check this place out and since we had a soup in the crock pot at home this was a great day to stop in. 

The interior is simple and highlights the exposed brick and general industrial feel. There was a short line which allowed us to look at the various options. This morning they had various croissants, banana bread, pumpkin bread, cookies and several types of whole loaves. We explained that we were looking for a bread to compliment the soup we had at home and the lady behind the counter explained the breads and made a recommendation. 

We chose a loaf and my wife got a piece of pumpkin bread for the road. Both were very good!  

We do have to admit though that taking the loaf home and having to slice it up and make a total mess is less desirable than buying a loaf at Whole Foods where you have the option of having it sliced to your desired thickness. Now maybe some people prefer to slice it themselves but it would be nice to have the option. 

Great addition to midtown!

My wife and I were looking for someplace new to try and started heading west on I-80. On the way she remembered reading about a newer place that had opened in Verdi. I searched Yelp really quick and we hopped off at exit 5. We arrived a few minutes after 11, which is when they open 7 days a week. 

In addition to the rustic exterior, we walked in and immediately loved the feel of the place. We were greeted by Michael who we later learned was the owner. We could see they had a full bar and about 20 tops with some great beer options. Michael was also mixing some drinks in clay pots which looked really interesting and smelled delicious.

We decided to try our luck so we chose to sit at the bar. Michael provided us menus and we were impressed by the options available. We were curious about the Elote balls appetizer and also wanted to try the mac and cheese. We asked Michael about both of them and ended up placing an order for each!  Both the elote balls and the mac and cheese were delicious.

My wife ordered the Tangent salmon burger (which Michael told us is named after the fisherman's boat which he gets the salmon from) and a side salad.  I chose to try the house smoked pulled pork with fries. When they arrived they both looked delicious and the portions are quite large. My wife loved the salmon burger the pulled pork was delicious!

We chatted with Michael about the place, the food, the area and how it has been going. He told us they opened in the fall of 17 and they they are currently experimenting with potential breakfast items.

This was an amazing experience and we would recommend taking the short drive out to Verdi to experience it for yourself.  This is also a great local spot before heading over the mountain.

We stopped here on a Saturday afternoon about 12:30pm. I was craving a good sandwich and we thought we would try this place since we have never been here. 

They have a few tables outside that we noticed as we walked inside. The menu is on the wall directly above the order counter. We appreciated that the sandwich options were clearly explained and it was hard to chose just one!  

I chose the #12 - The Odinson which came with Hot Pastrami, Roast Beef, Salami and Swiss Cheese and my wife chose the #3 - The Lennox Lewis which came with Turkey, Ham, Roast Beef and Jack Cheese. We were given options of wheat, white or sourdough bread.  Adding "Everything" to your sandwich includes: Mayo, Mustard, Secret Sauce, Lettuce, Tomato, Pickles, Onions and Peppers. I am so glad they explain what "everything" means.  I get really frustrated when someone asks me if I want "everything" and they don't explain what it means. Every place is different and my wife and I are not dressing people. 

We took a seat at one of the outdoor tables while our sandwiches were being made and enjoyed the sunshine. When our sandwiches arrived they looked delicious. There was a substantial amount of meat and the veggies were fresh!

We began eating and they tasted as good as they looked and were prepared exactly how we ordered them. 

Overall it was a great experience, the prices were very fair and we will definitely be back!!!

We had a coupon in our email for $10 off $40 for BJ's which expired on 11/3, so we figured we would go and take advantage of the offer. 

We arrived about 3pm and had a seat at a booth in the bar area which is open seating and were brought menus shortly after. 

The restaurant and bar area was fairly busy when we first arrived and there were several football games playing.  Someone came by and took our drink orders and provided us menus but then it was quite a while before anyone came to actually take our order.  I intended on ordering a small deep dish pizza but was told they only had the mini/personal size and large size available. How do they not have the other sizes available? I was caught off guard and proceeded to order the large as I figured I could always use leftovers but WHAT in the world, no pizza crust for small and medium sizes!?  

Throughout the time we waited for our meals to arrive we noticed that they did not seem to be understaffed, there were quite a few employees gathered around the take-out counter area and we even noticed one lady cleaning the glass on the entrance doors but we definitely did not feel taken care of by our server and noticed the other folks around us who were seated were not attended to any better.

My wife used the restroom and stated it was in need of attention - one of the three stalls was out of toilet paper and there were paper towels on the floor and counters that should have been taken care of.

Our food FINALLY arrived at 3:47 (approximately 40+ minutes after we were seated).  The food itself looked and tasted good but overall the experience was impacted by the overall service.  

This was our second negative experience at BJ's in recent months.  The Reno location had fabulous service but my wife's salad was sent back and comped and now this experience.

We've always been a fan of BJ's in the past so we aren't sure what is going on.  We will likely think twice before coming back to either location.

We come here every so often when looking for something special.

We came last weekend for something which I cannot remember at this point. But, we discovered they sell a refrigerated pizza dough near the entrance where they sell ready to eat slices of pizza. Since we love pizza, we thought we would give it a try. It is Terranova pizza dough from Bronyx, NY. 

I would consider us pizza connoisseurs and have made our own pizzas before. We have even smoked pizza on the grill. I feel that we have not reached the level of some of the best pizza places that we have been to. This dough has taken us a few steps closer. In fact, at this point, I think we would prefer to make our pizza at home.
