I have added a few pics to show what we made. I really wish they carried the sauce which is from Del Grosso, but we had to go to another grocery store to pick up that, as well as, our other ingredients at a lower cost. 

The Del Grosso pizza sauce is awesome, but it is from the East coast an only a few places carry it out here. I remember using it when I lived on the East coast. We would recommend that Whole Foods sell it and if you are making pizza, that you use it as well.

We had a reservation and met here as a group of 10 to celebrate a birthday at 6pm on a Saturday evening. It is tucked away amongst office buildings off South Mccarran near Lakeridge golf course. 

When we walked in it felt a little dark but we saw part of our group right away and joined them. There were plenty of tables, some were open and there was no wait for others. 

They have a bar area with high top tables as well with TVs showing various sporting events. The bathrooms are downstairs where there are also some other rooms that were unused this evening. The restrooms were very clean and well-kept.  They offer an elevator for those who are unable to access the lower level via the stairs. 

A cake and balloons were dropped off earlier in the day for the birthday boy. When we arrived the balloons were tied to one of the chairs to represent his location to sit.

After we all had arrived we placed our drink and appetizer orders. We would highly recommend the stuffed risotto balls and shrimp ceviche.

Shortly after the appetizers arrived we placed our entree orders. With 10 people we ended up getting a wide variety of options.  Everything arrived in a timely fashion and looked amazing. Everyone was very pleased with what they had.

Overall this was a great experience, the food was excellent and we felt well taken care of. Highly recommend!

Adding to my wife's weekly dose of Mexican food, we came here a little before 4:30pm on a Saturday. We decided to try this place because we were in the area and had a coupon for buy one entree, get the second entree half off.  It was not very busy, there were about 3 other tables occupied. We were seated right away and offered a booth which we took.

It looks like they have a full bar just off the dining room as well an outside patio area. The bar has several TV's which looked like they were playing college football.

We were brought chips and salsa. One salsa is similar to pico de gallo. The other salsa was similar to a chili colorado sauce.

After what felt like a long time, someone came to take our orders. My wife ordered the chicken chimichanga and I ordered the chili verde with flour tortillas.

We continued to munch on the chips and salsa until our food arrived.  Both meals looked great and tasted delicious - we both enjoyed them a lot. The chili verde pork was very tender and did not seem fatty like we have experienced elsewhere. The chicken chimichanga was absolutely stuffed with shredded chicken. 

The place was starting to fill up as we were leaving. 

Other than the long wait time when we were originally seated we were happy with our experience. We will have to try their south Reno location as well!

We had a reservation for a group of 9 at 5:30 PM on a Thursday. Our table was set and ready to go when we arrived and we were seated right away. It was not too busy but filling up fast.

We ordered drinks and the bruschetta and fried calamari appetizers which were delivered in a timely fashion. The appetizers were very tasty.

The group of us ordered a wide variety of entrees which were delivered in a timely fashion. Everything looked and tasted very good.

Overall this was a good experience and we were well taken care of.

Since we have lived in the area, my wife and I have tried many of the buffets and restaurants in the casinos, however, we had never been to the Buffet at the Eldorado. We noticed on a billboard this week that Silver Legacy, Eldorado and Circus Circus are now offering a 20% discount on restaurants to locals. We decided to check out The Buffet at the Eldorado. 

It was Sunday a little after 4pm and they had just opened for their Sunday Mexican dinner buffet when we arrived. There was a short line that moved pretty quickly. As we waited, we could see the menu which appeared to include a wide variety of options beyond what we would consider a Mexican diner buffet. In addition to the Latin specialty area, there were many salad options, hot soups an Italian pasta station, pizza, fried chicken, corn on the cob, a carving station with brisket, turkey, keilbasa and prime rib. They also had an Asian specialty area. There is also full dessert area. 

We were seated very quickly after paying and it did not appear to be very busy. We seldom go to a buffet on a Sunday night but were very pleased that it was no comparison to a Friday or Saturday night experience. 

My wife and both went to check out the options and grab a plate. We filled our plates with various options and returned to our seats. We each sampled two plates worth and went back to check out the desserts. 

Both my wife and commented how different an experience this was from the other buffets. We were very impressed. 

We would recommend checking out The Buffet at the Eldorado.

This is not your average gas station and convenience store! You need to check this out and get a sandwich!

My wife and I have wanted to try this place on several occasions but every time we stopped in there was a line almost to the door and we did not have the time. Today, Sunday, when we arrived about 10:30am there were only a few people in line. By the time we sat down, the line was to the door.

My wife decided to make her own sandwich and chose roast beef, pepper jack cheese, lettuce, pepperoncini on jalapeño cheddar bread. 

I like meatballs and marinara so I chose the medium meatball sandwich thinking I could save some of it for leftovers.

The employees were friendly and efficient in creating our sandwiches and they looked very good.  They provide you with a paper to take to the register and there are plenty of seats available both inside and outside if you are eating there.  We also saw several people taking sandwiches to go.

As we were sitting there talking and eating our delicious sandwiches we commented to each other on how CLEAN the entire place is.  This has got to be one of the very cleanest convenience stores EVER.  My wife also went in to wash her hands and had to take her phone with her to snap a couple of pics - it's that CLEAN!

Overall, our sandwiches were delicious and we enjoyed them.  Great experience - glad we finally got to check it out!

My wife and were looking for a place to get breakfast or brunch on Easter Sunday and really just wanted something simple and weren't exactly sure who was open and did not require a reservation. We decided to head downtown to the casinos because we figured they always have something open.

We wandered through "The Row" and tried our luck at a couple of machines and noticed the small line of folks that were previously in line waiting had all been seated. We were seated right away and provided menus. I would have preferred to order something from their lunch menu but it wasn't an option prior to 11am so I decided on the breakfast burrito while my wife chose the California omelet. Our server Marie was friendly and efficient and our breakfast arrived quickly and tasted good.

We were checked on regularly and when we asked for to go containers Marie was quick to bring an extra ranchera sauce to go which I appreciated. Overall it was a good experience!

My wife and I came here for our Friday lunch date. I have been here before and thought I did a review but apparently I did not. 

I really like Canter's for their freshly sliced meats in a tasty sandwich. We arrived about 12:30pm and were surprised when we parked in the garage how easy it was. We aren't used to coming to Silver Legacy during the weekday. Therefore, the parking garage nor the casino were busy. We both commented that we should come here during the day and not in the evening when they have events going on.

We took the elevator and walked to Canter's on the main casino floor. My wife and I stopped at the menu board to see what they had. There were a lot of sandwich options, burgers, melts and paninis. They also have soups and salads. It really neat to see the open kitchen area where they slice the meats and cook on the grill, it also appeared very clean. 

You order at the counter, have a seat and they bring it out to you. My wife decided to get a patty melt which we both love. I really had a craving for a hot ham and Swiss sandwich which I did not see exactly on the menu. I asked and was told it was no problem. I got it on grilled rye bread. 

We had a seat with our number and a short while later our meals arrived. They looked really good. 

We both enjoyed our sandwiches. My wife said the pattty melt was a good solid patty melt but not mind blowing knock your socks off. I thought my ham and Swiss sandwich was very good but not as good as the pastrami sandwich that I had the last time. I just remember it being so awesome, hence the reason for our visit this time. 

Next time, I will get the pastrami again.

We came here about 5pm on a Saturday. It was not too busy, about 5 of the roughly 15 tables were occupied. They also have some outside seating in the front.

We were immediately greeted and taken to a table and provided menus. We were impressed with the menu - there were lots of delicious options and a nice cocktail menu. They also have a good selection of beer, which I appreciate!

My wife ordered the strawberry blond cocktail while I ordered a Ballast Point IPA. As we perused the menu it really started to fill up!  My wife chose the caprese salad and the steamed clams and I choose the mac and cheese and kobe beef sliders. The menu states that items are delivered to the table as they are prepared in the kitchen. We had never been to a tapa restaurant before but it was kind of fun to anticipate which item would arrive first. 

We sipped our drinks and the caprese salad arrived first which my wife said was simple and delicious. Next, the beef sliders arrived and looked very tasty as well. The steamed clams arrived and included a good amount of bread to dip in the broth. Last, was the mac and cheese which was baked in small dish and looked equally incredible. All of the food tasted fabulous!

We really enjoyed the food and the service was very good. Danny was an awesome server and took really good care of us. Great experience and we highly recommend!

My wife and I came here about 12:30pm for lunch on a Friday. You enter into the bar area and there is a sign stating, please wait to be seated. The dining area is to the right. It was not very busy and there were about 11 tables open when we arrived. We were seated right away.

We checked out the menu and were brought waters and had our drink orders taken. My wife decided to order a cup of the minestrone soup.

The soup was delivered along with a small basket of bread and butter. My wife really enjoyed the soup and said it was very tasty.

For our meals my wife ordered the lasagna and I ordered the meatball sandwich. They were delivered in a timely fashion and looked delicious. We both really enjoyed them. Everything tasted great!

Throughout the lunch hour it continued to get busy and there were quite a few people there when we left.

Pepe was an awesome server and took really good care of us. The lunch prices seemed very reasonable  and we commented that we need to come back here for dinner. Overall it was a great experience!

My wife and I came here for lunch about 1:30pm on a Friday afternoon. 

Burrito Bandit is located at the legends mall in between Burlington Coat Factory and Olive Garden near the roundabout. 

The interior is decorated nicely and is very clean and comfortable. We were immediately greeted by several employees and walked up towards the counter. They make your item to order and walk you through the selections of meat, beans, rice, veggies, hot sauce etc. I was also pleasantly surprised to find out you can add avocado for no additional charge.

We each decided to order a Carne Asada burrito and The employees were quick efficient and friendly.  We paid and had a seat at a table, you can then take your cup up to the soda fountain and grab napkins and things like that.   They have a large selection of assorted hot sauces and sauces for sale by the bottle but we noticed they had an assortment of samples for people to try next to the small salsa bar. 

As other people have said the burritos are huge!  Everything tasted very fresh and delicious. My only suggestion would be to offer a whole wheat tortilla option. 

Overall was a great experience and would highly recommend!

My wife and I came here a little before 1pm on a Friday. It is located in a small strip mall. After finding a place to park in this busy complex we walked in. The majority of the tables were already occupied and we made our way to the counter to order. We were about fourth in line. It looks inside to be very authentic.

The menu boards are easy to read while you are standing in line and there are descriptions including ingredients which makes it easy to determine what you want by the time you get to the front of the line.

The employee taking orders was friendly and helpful and we thought the prices were very reasonable. He provided us our sodas and a number for our order. We found an available booth and patiently waited as we saw other orders being delivered to the various tables. 

Our number was called a short time later and our food was delivered and looked yummy. I chose a carnitas wet burrito and my wife chose the chicken nachos. We were also given a small dish of salsa. The salsa was really good.

Everything was very tasty and we enjoyed it. Definitely a hidden gem and we would recommend. 

They are open 7 days a week from 9am-9pm which makes it nice too. This is a really good place for authentic mexican food. Not fancy, but good food at a good price in a relaxed atmosphere.

My wife and I came here about 5:30pm on a Saturday. She has been craving Asian food for a while now and today was the day. Happy wife, happy life!

We were seated promptly after they cleared a booth. It appeared they were just using the booths which had a high separation for social distancing. We both commented that it appeared they had a lot of people working and it was not very busy. 

Before we perused the menu, we were offered water to which we replied, yes and my wife asked for an appetizer of the potstickers. 

A short while later our orders were taken. My wife chose the cashew chicken and I chose the pepper beef. 

Our appetizer of the potstickers arrived soon after our order was taken. They looked really good and were very large. 

Within 5 to 10 minutes our entree's arrived with one big bowl of sticky rice to share. Everything looked really tasty with fresh and crispy vegetables. 

We both were satisfied and had leftovers to take home. 

I am sure we will be back one of the next times my wife is craving Asian food.

It has been a while since we were here last, primarily because there are so many options in Reno. We decided to check it out again about 10am on a Sunday. Roughly half the tables were open when we arrived and we were seated right away at a small table by a window. The tables all appear to have fresh cut flowers on them.

We were given menus and our drink orders were taken. After perusing the menu, my wife chose the chili verde omelet and I chose the ham and Swiss sandwich. We also decided to share a side of bacon.

Our meals were delivered in a timely fashion and looked really good however, there were a few issues: The ham and Swiss sandwich was really a ham, Swiss and cheddar sandwich, not a big deal but their menu describes it as only having Swiss cheese. But, hey it is their menu not mine. The side of bacon and my wife's toast were not there. We had to ask again for both of them.

My wife thought the chili verde omelet was amazing and my sandwich was really good as well. I did not like the ketchup that came with the fries, it lacked flavor and had a taste like cinnamon. Bacon is always good but we prefer a thicker cut. The strawberry jam that came with the toast my wife really enjoyed.

Overall, it was a good experience but there are some details that have been lost since our first visit.

My wife and I stopped here while running errands in the neighborhood at about 4:30pm on a Thursday.  We were immediately greeted by the owner who was helpful explaining the options available and offering us samples of the different flavors. 

Once we made our choices he went to work on creating our treats. The ice cream is light and flavorful and it was fun to get to the bottom and finish with cake and sauce. 

Great experience and we will be back!!  Prices were very reasonable as well.

We came here about noon on a Saturday. It is a small place, about 10 tables inside, a bar with about 8 seats and some counter seating and a table outside in the front. 

The decor inside is very eclectic with a copper colored ceiling and ductwork. The bar has copper colored corrugated metal underneath with railroad spikes that allow for purse and/or backpacks to be hung under the counter. The footrest under the counter is a piece of railroad track.

They have a full bar and about 18 beers on tap.  We were immediately greeted and directed to a table and provided menus and water. We were told they were serving both breakfast and lunch. 

The menu selections looked really yummy and we both decided on sandwiches. My wife chose the BLTA and side salad with lemon vinaigrette dressing and I chose the pulled pork sandwich and fries without the purple slaw. My wife said the BLTA was very fresh and tasted amazing. The pulled pork had a sweet flavor up front and a kick in the back.

Our server, Justin, was very friendly and thorough. He forgot his pen when taking our order but repeated it back a couple of times for clarification.  Great experience we will be back!

We have been wanting to try the steakhouse for a while now. We even had some giftcards we purchased at Costco at a discount. But those were stolen when our home was broken into. 

Lately we have seen signs for a happy hour from 4 to 6pm and thought we would check it out tonight. We did not have a reservation for the restaurant which does not open until 5pm but the bar opens at 4pm and is open seating. We discovered that at the bar you can have anything from the full restaurant menu after 5pm but they also serve drinks and some appetizers at a discount from 4 to 6pm.

Technically, we did not have the full experience of the restaurant because we were at the bar and did not go for the full meal deal. But our entire experience was awesome and we will be back. 

We arrived shortly after 4pm, ordered drinks and asked a lot of questions of Jessica, the bartender. We decided to wait until the restaurant opened for a wider selection of food, so, we took our drinks and went to gamble a little. After I was up about $50, we returned to the steakhouse bar as it was just about 5pm. 

I chose the prime rib and Italian vegetable soup and macaroni and cheese which is a side dish.  My wife chose the clam chowder and a house salad. Jessica brought our soups and a basket of bread and butter.  She then brought the Mac and cheese and salad, everything was delicious!

Jessica is a rock star!  We feel that we typically get good service when we are out but Jessica takes it to the next level. She was extremely friendly and welcoming and as we enjoyed our drinks and meals we heard her interaction with others as well.  She knows many of her customers, many by name and knew their drink orders. 

It's nice to have an option on the north side of town as well. If the smoky casino bothers you enter through the entrance on the south side of the building - that takes you right into the restaurant area between the cafe and the steakhouse.

It has been a while since we have been here. For our Friday lunch date, my wife and I decided to try it again. We stopped in about 12:30pm and were immediately greeted by a friendly face at the counter. We asked for a few minutes as it had been a while. There was no one behind us so we did not feel rushed. It did not feel too busy but appeared that about a third of the tables were occupied. 

We looked over the menu and my wife chose the Fish Sando (Atlantic cod, blackened, coleslaw & tartar sauce) while I choose the Big Dippa (Roast beef, onion strings, Swiss cheese with au jus & horseradish creme). I do not like horseradish, so asked for it without. We decided to also get a small order of fries and a small order of onion rings so we had the best of both worlds. We each ordered a medium drink which you fill on your own at the beverage counter. In addition to the usually sodas, they had three types of tea and house made lemonade. 

We were told they would bring our orders to us so we got our drinks and had a seat.  The decor is simple but comfortable and clean. 

Our orders arrived in a timely manner and looked and tasted delicious. Total cost was about $25. We need to try their other locations as well - we highly recommend!

I have been here once before with a group from work and enjoyed it. My wife and I have had it on our list for a while. We came here about 4:45pm on a Saturday. We did not have reservations and there were already about 4 tables occupied and they were able to seat us at a booth. 

There are roughly 15 or so tables in each of 2 rooms and they also have about six seats at a counter. The decor is what you might expect from an Italian restaurant with the fake brick paneling and dim lighting. 

We were provided menu's and our drink orders were taken. My wife and I perused the menu and made our choices. When our drinks arrived our orders were taken. My wife chose the Linguine with clam sauce and I chose the Lasagna with a side of mild Italian sausage. We both chose the minestrone soup over a dinner salad. 

Our soup and a basket of garlic bread arrived shortly after and the minestrone and the garlic bread were delicious. 

As the restaurant started to fill up, our meals arrived a short time later and looked amazing. Everything tasted delicious. 

About 5:30pm we heard them turning people away who did not have reservations because of the wait.

My wife and I both used their restroom and we both commented how worn and discolored the white doors were around the handles. After that we discussed the upkeep of the interior, such as a hole in a wall and well worn carpet. 

We both thought the food and service were amazing and would give Zozo's 5 stars but we thought the interior could really use some upkeep and refreshing. For that reason we are giving it 4 stars.

We have been meaning to come here for quite some time and finally got the opportunity.

We initially came in because we knew the 775Eats food truck was there on Saturday afternoon and early evening but we thought it was also a great opportunity to sit and relax with a cold beer!

We entered through the retail space which allows you to purchase canned beer to go or you can buy a flight or pint to enjoy.

There was a wide selection of beers and even some seltzer's which my wife enjoyed. I choose a pint of "Reno as F&@k" and we walked into the warehouse area of the building. There are tables and chairs setup and also a bar area.

It was clean and comfortable and we were able to enjoy our food and drinks while listening to music.

We were a little surprised to see how many people brought their dogs but they all seemed to be well behaved.

From the tables you can see the various tanks used for making their delicious beer.

Overall it was a great experience and we will be back!

My wife has been wanting try this place for a while, but every time we come by the line is out the door. Well, today the line was inside the door so, we stopped in.

We waited in line and noticed all the seats were full. Most of the tables are for two or four, however, they have two that are for larger groups. It appeared they were managing the order process based on the available seats so that no one would need to stand and wait for their food. We might have waited about 10 minutes although it always feels like longer. As we waited, we reviewed the menu and made our choices. We both decided on the Reggie (fried chicken, bacon, cheese, sausage gravy on a biscuit).

After we placed our order, we were given a small stainless steel number tent to place on the table, but, we had to wait a few minutes until a table came available and had a seat. We could see that they bring the food out to your table. 

At this point, we patiently waited and in a timely fashion, our orders arrived and were set on the table in front of us. Wow, they looked absolutely amazing!

The chicken had a little red around the outside under the breading which we think may have been some kind of hot sauce. We say that because we both thought they tasted a little spicy. We were guessing they marinate the chicken in a hot sauce, bread it, then fry it. They tasted delicious!

Overall, it was a great food experience and the interior is cozy and comfortable however, we both believe they could use more seating.

We saw something that said the Carvings Buffet offers a 50% discount to locals. Then we looked on Yelp and sure enough there were comments about the locals only 50% discount. We have been to the Hash House a Go Go next door and really enjoyed it but we had never been to Carvings, so we thought what better opportunity to try it out.

We went to the players club to sign up for their rewards program. They also told us about the locals discounts and placed a round silver sticker on my card which says, "Reno Local".

We then went up to Carvings. We were given a 50% discount for the entire check for both my wife and I. I only had to show my players card with the locals sticker. 

We were taken to a table and began the adventure to see what they had. They were having their champagne brunch. We thought there was a pretty wide variety including prime rib, Mexican, Asian, Italian, breakfast items (eggs, bacon, sausage, waffles) and a large dessert area. My wife and I each sampled several things and returned to our table. Shortly after sitting down, our drink orders were taken. We were also offered mimosas. 

My wife really enjoyed the prime rib but as we anticipated most of everything else was just allright. None of the food really stood out to us. It did fill us up and was adequate with many options and the price was awesome for locals.

We came here about 3:30pm on a Sunday. We have been here several times before and always enjoyed it. 

Upon entering, we were surprised to see Tonya working. We know her from another local Reno restaurant which we go to on some frequency. We talked a bit and learned that she left the other place and now bartends and manages here. 

During our conversation she suggested the mac and cheese. She is a ROCK STAR and amazing at customer service!

We perused the menu and both commented that prices have definitely increased. We agreed this was not surprising considering what we all have been through the past year and the inflation we are starting to see.

We pretty much knew the menu from prior visits but never had the mac and cheese. We decided to order the mac and cheese skillet appetizer first and ordered our meals a short while later. My wife chose the club sandwich and I again ordered the ham and cheese sandwich but with Swiss cheese.

The mac and cheese arrived first and looked huge. We ate about half of it before our entrees arrived. It was delicious!

Our entrees also looked and tasted amazing as we had expected.  This is always a great place to have a meal - check them out!

We tried the rock candy short ribs the night before at Yelpstronomy and had wanted to check this out for a while, so my wife and I came here for lunch on a Friday about 12:30pm.  

The inside was very trendy, clean and simple. The outside seating was very tempting but we decided to eat inside and chose two seats at the bar.  It was not very busy, there were a few other tables occupied both inside and out. They have about 20 or so tables inside and 15 or so outside. 

We were given menus and water right away. They have a Friday special which is 3 tacos and a beer for $10. We checked out the menu and my wife decided to try the BLTA and I chose the rock candy short rib grilled cheese. We both chose waffle fries with our sandwiches. 

Our meals were delivered in a timely fashion and looked awesome. Everything tasted delicious as well.

This was a great experience and we would like to go back and try their dinner menu as well.

For national pizza day my wife and I decided to try a new place. We had heard about Nik & Willies but had never been before.  

We arrived about 3pm on a Sunday afternoon and were immediately greeted and decided to take one of the menus to a table and decide what we wanted. Many of the pizza options sounded delicious and we decided to order the combination pizza but had them hold the olives, tomato and mushrooms on half of it. We also couldn't resist to order the cheesy garlic bread with marina sauce. 

The dining area is kind of small but they also have outside seating which is probably great in the summer.

We got our drinks and took a seat. There was one other family enjoying their pizza but many people came in to pick up their orders while we were there. It sounded like many people were getting their pizza to bake at home which they also prepare for a discount.

Our cheesy garlic bread and marinara arrived in a short amount of time and looked delicious. We quickly devoured it and our pizza arrived shortly afterwards and also looked yummy!

We really enjoyed the pizza but I was disappointed the olives, mushrooms and tomatoes were over on "my side" of the pizza since I really don't like any them. They also chop them rather fine which makes it much harder to remove. Next time I think we will order separate pizzas. 

We also like the fact that they don't skip on the extra marinara which we ordered on the pizza or the marinara that is served with the garlic bread.

Overall a cool experience and we will stop again.

We decided to try the lunch buffet here because we had not been here before and they were offering a free lunch buffet to veterans.

The normal weekday lunch price is $19.99. With 20% off for locals, that brings it to about $16 before tax and tip for two people with the free veteran lunch. Pretty sweet deal!

We arrived just a bit before 11am and there was a nice line, so we waited. The wait was not bad and we got the counter a little after 11am. 

We were seated in a booth, had our drink orders taken and told we could help ourselves to the buffet.

There is a lot to choose from at the various stations and the folks at the carving station were generous with their portions.  Overall we enjoyed it and will likely be back.  We often forget that Peppermill offers 20% off to locals and we've always had good food when dining at the various spots throughout the casino.

The staff was also very attentive in refilling our sodas and stopping in to check on us and remove dirty dishes. The service felt better and the restaurant is more well kept than some other local buffets. We would consider this to be at least in the top three local buffets.

We came here a little after 3pm. We initially could not find the entrance and decided to go into The Jesse which is also a place we wanted to check out. We discovered the only direct entrance to this place from The Jesse or the shared parking lot on 4th street to the shared outdoor seating area. We came from The Jesse after having a drink there.   

We walked in and saw the menu right away with the kitchen area right in front of us. It was not busy and we were the only customers. They have about 10 to 12 indoor seats. It is a very small area with what appears to be just counter seating and no tables. 

We reviewed the menu, placed our orders and had a seat. My wife grabbed two small bowls of each of their salsas for our tortilla chips that we ordered. 

My wife ordered two of the shrimp tacos and I ordered two of the short rib tacos. 

The tortilla chips arrived first and we were both very impressed with the salsas. The green is a little hotter but the red was my favorite. It was a little smokey and tasted amazing. We enjoyed both of them.

We watched as the chef's quickly prepared our tacos with all the yummy ingredients.  They presented them to us on a shared platter and they looked beautiful and delicious.  We both enjoyed them - each bite was incredible.

We learned from talking with the staff that you can order and eat in The Jesse or vice versa.  They do have a bar area but the offerings are different than at The Jesse.  We will come back when the weather is nice and sit outside on the patio - check it out!

We were craving pizza and decided to try this place out. It was about 4:30pm on a Sunday. 

Upon arriving, we read their message board above the entrance. It was a commanding statement overlooking the parking lot which said, "Absolutely the worst pizza I ever had." - One guy on Yelp. It just intrigued us even more based on the reviews we read on Yelp

We walked in and it looked really busy. The main room has what appears to be a bunch of picnic tables with some others thrown in. There is a back room with a few more tables, booths, and counter seating with some slot machines at a bar. This is the kind of place where you review the menu on the wall and place your order at the window. You also pick up your order from the window when your order number is called. 

We decided to order the extra large meat lover and a small order of rojo's. We always like taking home the leftovers for work lunches. $25 and change is a decent price for a good extra-large pizza. They told us it would be about 50 minutes. We knew it could be a while based on Yelp reviews so we had a seat at the bar had a few drinks and played some slots. 

1 hour and 20 minutes later our number was called. We each already had 2 drinks. We went up to the counter which still had a lot of people waiting to order. We picked up our pizza and rojo's and took it to the bar area where we were sitting. The pizza looked amazing and tasted very good as well. They make a thin crust and it was crunchy on the bottom.  The rojo's were also very good. 

Normally, we would not feel good about waiting over an hour for our order BUT they were upfront about the length of the wait when we ordered and we read the comments on Yelp about long wait times. They have slot machines, a full bar and TV's which entertained us while we waited. The cost of the drinks were very reasonable and we had fun. We will plan accordingly for our next visit and would recommend that others try this place out, the pizza and rojo's were delicious and reasonably priced.

We have had this place on our radar for a while now. We came once before and they were closed for the holiday's. We decided to check it out again. We arrived a little before 4pm on a Sunday and were greeted by the owner, Cony. It was not very busy and we were seated right away. I know this is our second Mexican experience for the weekend but what can I say, happy wife, happy life. 

We asked how long they have been open and were told about a year and a half. She expressed pleasure that she had made it more than a year since many start up restaurants are closed within a year. Throughout the course of our meal, we were fortunate enough to be able to talk with Cony about the location, the restaurant and her love of the Mexican arts. 

We each ordered drinks and chips and salsa and continued to peruse the menu. The place looks and feels very clean and comfortable. My wife decided to try the Arrachera and I chose the chicken enchiladas. 

We placed our orders a short time later and they arrived rather quickly. 

Throughout our conversation with Cony, we learned about her love for the Mexican arts, her experience decorating other Mexican establishments in town and her experiences with the property, as well as, what her plans are for the property.

We were both very impressed with the presentation of the plates when they arrived and my wife absolutely loved the Arrachera. The meat was cooked with a little bit of char on the outside adding a tasty flavor. The chicken enchiladas were delicious. We talked a bit with Cony about the enchiladas not including rice and beans, to which I responded that every other Mexican restaurant includes them. I felt that some people may feel they are getting less for their money. But, in my opinion, the chicken enchiladas were perfect on their own. And, I don't even like the beans anyway. 

We would recommend visiting, checking out the place and having some really good food and drink. In addition, Cony has a beautiful outdoor area that is perfect for enjoying the sunny weather and a small event space for larger groups.

Since we were in the area and I have pasta pass, we decided to stop here.  We arrived about 4:15 pm on a Saturday afternoon and it was busy but we were seated right away. 

We were provided menus and someone took our drink orders and brought us breadsticks almost immediately. 

We both commented that the feeling inside is much different than the Reno Olive Garden. The restaurant is nice and seems well kept but the dining area seems crowded and loud. 

It must have been shift change because our initial server brought over Morgan who would be taking care of us and we placed our orders. My wife ordered the chicken scampi because she really liked it the last time. And of course I got another variation of the pasta bowl because I have the pasta pass. We both ordered the Zuppa Toscanna because we really like it. 

Our meals arrived in a timely manner but we noticed the portions of our meals seemed considerably smaller than our other recent experiences in Reno. Regardless of the smaller size, we still took home leftovers. 

Overall the experience was good but we will likely make our way back to the Reno location.

My wife and I stopped here once before but only to check it out since we didn't realize it existed when visiting Brewer's Cabinet a few months ago. So today, we decided to come and grab some food and enjoy a beer. 

It was about 3pm on a Sunday.  It is not a large place and many of the seats were taken. There are about 3 tables as well as bar seating for about 10. 

In addition to at least 20 taps they also fill 32 oz. crowlers and 64 oz. growlers.  We had never seen the 32 oz. crowlers before, they are large aluminum cans which they fill with the beer of your choice and then crimp on the lid.

Maggie took our drink orders and provided us menus.  She explained that the tap room offers the same menu as Brewers Cabinet except they do not serve the entrees in the tap room because of the proximity to the kitchen. All of the food is prepared in same Brewers Cabinet kitchen in main building.

We decided to start with the homemade tater tots which are described as Winnemucca potatoes, sea salt, creamy cheese sauce, crispy bacon, green onion, fried egg and ketchup.  We decided to order it without the fried egg.  We also each ordered a sandwich, my wife ordered the patty melt with side salad and I ordered the ham and cheese on marble rye with fries.

Our tater tots were delivered and looked interesting and delicious.  The manager explained that they put a tempura on the potatoes and deep dry them before putting them in the bowl of cheese sauce and topping them with the bacon, onions and ketchup.  They were delicious - the potatoes were soft and creamy - we would highly recommend!

Our sandwiches came out shortly afterwards and looked and tasted equally delicious!  We have always enjoyed Brewers Cabinet but really like the feeling in tap room, they have a real fireplace and lots of rustic wood - it's cozy and comfortable.  

We have to give a special shout out to Maggie who took excellent care of us and answered all our questions.  She even dated and labeled our to go containers.  Fabulous experience - I even chose a crowler of the double IPA to enjoy at home!

We decided to stop in for breakfast recently, it's been too long.

We were seated right away and provided menus and our drink orders were taken. We looked over the menu and my wife decided on the sausage and eggs breakfast which comes with potatoes and toast. I chose the chicken friend steak and eggs which also comes with potatoes and toast. We both commented on how reasonable the prices were as well.

Our server was friendly and our food arrived shortly afterwards and looked delicious!  Everything tasted just as good as it looked and we agreed we would be stopping in more frequently in the future.

The only downside is that it is a small place and can get busy at times. So, there may be a wait. We have seen tables reserved for larger parties. 

Great local spot and we highly recommend!!

My wife and I randomly came here just after noon on Sunday. We did not check Yelp or anything else until after we had ordered. We seldom do that but we were hungry. We were seated right away as it was not very busy. A lot of tables were open.

We ordered the queso dip and tortilla chips as an appetizer.

My wife kept commenting that it was cold in the the restaurant.  The temperature either needs to be turned up earlier or a higher temperature to be comfortable. 

We both ordered the Whisky Bacon Burger but my orederd onion rings as a side and I chose fries. Our appetizer arrived shortly afterwards. The flavor of the queso was good but the temperature was only warm, not hot as expected. 

About 45 minutes later our entrees arrived and looked good but both had fries. Our server said he would bring out an order of onion rings which he promptly did. 

The burgers were tasty, the temperature was good and they were cooked as ordered 

The place appeared very clean and the restroom was as well.

For the experience we had we both thought it would have been just as good at Steak and Shake or In-N-Out and a whole lot less expensive.

We wondered what was happening with this place the last time we stopped and they were closed.

After stopping today, we found out they are under new ownership.  The current owner, Abel told us that he has owned it for the past 6 months.  The interior and exterior looked almost identical to the last time we were in. We had a seat at the bar and were greeted and we noticed the happy hour menu. My wife inquired if a blended strawberry margarita was included in the happy hour house margaritas for $5 and was told yes. I inquired about IPA's and Abel not only told me the names of the four to five IPA's he had on tap but also told me the location of the breweries which I thought was a nice touch. I decided on one from Fort Collins, Colorado and was pleased to see that all draft beer is $4.25 during happy hour. 

We began looking at the menu and noticed right away it is different than before. There are several appetizer options, burgers, salads, Mexican options and the prices are very reasonable. 

I decided on a patty melt while my wife chose a BLT. Several customers came in while we were there and they appeared to be regulars because they all began chatting and knew each other by name. One of the other couples at the bar who we learned had never been in before were chatting with Abel and they were from the Verdi area and spoke about a former restaurant in which Abel owned in the past. 

Our meals arrived in a timeline fashion and looked delicious. They tasted delicious too!  Each came with fries and everything was cooked nicely and temperatures etc were perfect. 

Overall it was a great experience and we will be back!!!

We recommend trying out the new ownership!

We came here at 6:30pm on a Thursday as a group of 6. We had called earlier in the week and made a reservation requesting a table outside.  We were seated right away and taken to a table in the rear of the garden area which was very nice and private. 

We were told they were short handed that evening but that Kelsey would be our server and would take great care of us and we were provided menus. 

Kelsey stopped in shortly after and asked us if we were ready to order some drinks and she was helpful and knowledgeable when we had questions and asked for recommendations. 

Our drinks were delicious and we ordered two appetizers for the table and placed our dinner orders. 

We enjoyed relaxing on a beautiful night in early June - the outdoor area is unlike anything else in Reno that we have experienced. It's quaint and charming being surrounded by plants and flowers, while catching up with colleagues. 

The appetizers were delicious and just right for the six of us. Our entrees arrived and looked amazing as well. Overall we were very pleased with our meals however the two people in our group who ordered the steak special felt as though the steaks were not cooked to their liking. They had both ordered medium and felt they were much closer to medium well. They both enjoyed the flavor and were overall satisfied so they didn't mention it to Kelsey. 

Even though we were all full we decided to order desserts and were impressed by the number of dessert options and when they arrived they looked and tasted yummy. 

Overall this was a great experience and we would highly recommend for a nice meal or special occasion!

My wife and I came here about 11:30 am on a Sunday. According to their hours they had opened at 11am. 

Our experience started a little strange. The place was empty and we got the attention of someone in the back who told us they were supposed be open but had no server or bartender and apologized. As we were walking out someone was walking in wearing  a Brauhaus shirt. So, we went back in, it was the bartender/server. 

We had a seat at the bar. The interior appears freshly remodeled with a lot of wood and brick accents. We could see they have 20 taps and what appears to be a full bar.

We were brought menus and ordered drinks. We also ordered a pretzel appetizer. For entrees, my wife decided to get the Wurst sandwich and chose the polish sausage. I decided on the bacon cheese burger.

Our meals felt like they took a long time to arrive and the pretzel appetizer was delivered after the entrees. Everything looked delicious and tasted great.

The place has only been open a couple of weeks and you could tell they are still working out some kinks based on our experience. The food was great, we will come back and try it again.

My wife and I came here for lunch on Friday about 12:30pm. She had seen a review and photos from fellow Yelper Emily A. and just had to try the nachos. 

The place was probably a little over half full when we walked in the door. The order counter and menu board are right in front of you as you walk in. We were surprised to see such an extensive menu as well. 

We perused the menu and made our choices. My wife chose the chicken nachos and I chose to get a wet green burrito with chili verde inside. They gave us our drinks and a bowl of tortilla chips with salsa. The salsa is a very chunky type of salsa which is not what I prefer. We then went and found a seat. 

A short wile later our order was brought to our table and we were very impressed. They looked really good. The burrito was huge. The nachos were large loaded with toppings. As we dug into them, we were even more pleased. Everything was delicious. 

The food was delicious and the price very reasonable!

My wife and I decided to check this place out. We have been in Peppermill many times before but had never been to Biscotti's - we actually didn't know it existed mostly because it is on the west side near the conference room areas and located away from the casino.  

Since we were there on a Sunday they have a Sunday Brunch option but it was a little pricey for us - $54.95/per person.  We asked the hostess if we were able to order off the regular menu instead of the brunch and she stated yes.  Therefore, we decided to have a seat at the bar where we were greeted by William.

He was quick to take our drink orders and provide us menus.  We decided we really liked the feel of the place - it was nice to be away from the casino area while still having the option to play after we ate.

We perused the menu and my wife decided on the Fish and Chips while I ordered the North Beach Burger with no thousand island.  We enjoyed chatting with William and he was able to easily manage the drink orders coming in while being friendly and efficient.

Our food arrived in a timely manner and looked delicious.  We both enjoyed our meals. My burger was excellent with the crispy parmesan crusted sourdough. My wife didn't feel like the batter on the fish was fully cooked - it felt a little soft for her liking.  

Overall it was a great experience - we will definitely be back!

We came here about 11 a.m. to meet some friends for brunch. We had a reservation but we could have done without it, it was not very busy. 

They have a bloody mary bar with different hot sauces and offer unlimited bloody mary's or mimosas which is pretty cool!  

Our server, Angel was very attentive and checked on us while we chatted until we were ready to order. We each ordered something different including eggs benedict, huevos rancheros, an angus burger and a salad. 

The interior space is very trendy and cool and there was live music  

Our food arrived in a timely manner and looked fabulous. Everything tasted very good and we were impressed. 

Steven, one of the chefs came out and chatted with us a bit. He told us a bit about the restaurant and catering business and spoke highly of another young chef named Colin. It was a cool experience speaking to him and learning more about their endeavors. 

Overall it was a fantastic experience and we would highly recommend to others!!!

This is hands down the best fried chicken I have ever eaten. I've dined in, ordered from the store via Grubhub for both delivery and pick up, and the quality of the fried chicken is consistently phenomenal and customer service is polite and cordial. I am a hardcore wings fan (the meat falls off the bone!), but their boneless chicken bites are also delectable in soy garlic and honey garlic. The shop provides plastic gloves to contain the messiness and a well-stocked supply of ketchup packets for the crinkle cut fries. Boba tea is coming soon to this location in late February as well so look out for a one-stop shop!

[Visitor from California review]

5 stars just for the $10 Happy Hour Cheese plate alone. This was a fantastic deal for 3 generously portioned cheeses, a basket of bread, 4 jams/spreads and a handful of nuts/berries. 

While you don't get to pick the cheese, I found that I liked 2 of the 3 cheeses offered. (I'm not much of a bleu cheese fan) 

You can get this deal everyday from 3-6 PM!

Would definitely stop by again if I'm in the area. Wish we had this in CA!

I already knew I'd be bypassing Acme for this place before I even arrived to NOLA. There was no way I'm standing in line for an unnecessary amount of time just for oysters no matter now much I love them. 

So I came at what I thought was an off-peak time (2:30 PM) but there was still some people in line. Although it was only about a 7 min wait at Felix's, the line across the street at Acme looked at least 40 mins. Suckers!

Because this was a pre-dinner, I only ordered a half dozen raw oysters and a half dozen chargrilled ones. The raw ones were super plump and fresh! It didn't even need any mignonette. And when I was considering thinking about getting more raw ones, the chargrilled ones arrived and BOOM, I was thinking about getting more chargrilled. They were SO delicious that I was almost bummed that I didn't stuff my face more with oysters. 

However, I still had the rest of NOLA to feast off of, so I enjoyed my brief time at Felix's and look forward to the next visit!

A friend & I stopped in after the Carpinteria Beer Festival and were looking forward to some fresh food for an early dinner. We waited outside sipping water for about 30 minutes while they prepped for dinner service. That was great considering we had been in the sun for hours, so shade & fluids worked perfectly for both of us.

While the service was very nice, what didn't work so well for us was the quality of the food, including the fish & chicken. The fish just wasn't very good caliber, including bloodlines in the Yellowtail, plus the chicken was undercooked so much that my friend wouldn't eat it. I worked my way around the reddest parts, but we shouldn't have had to deal with undercooked poultry. She declined to order something else, so we settled the bill and figured it was a lesson learned.

What draws me most to this Kaldi's is the atmosphere and how genuine the workers are. It's a very welcoming environment that ensures you have a good start to your day. Every time I come in it's nothing but smiles and pleasantries, which says a lot about the people who work here. I used to live in Portland and developed an appreciation for places that possess that chill hipster vibe, so this place is perfect for me. I like to come in, order a 16oz Mocha, find a cozy spot to sit, and get work done for hours. Great spot to be productive and grind some work out some. Additionally, a nice spot to have an intimate conversation while enjoying a delicious beverage. Incase you build up an appetite, they have a full menu, which features quite a few delectable items. They also serve breakfast all day, which is a major key. Highly recommend this place and suggest you come check it out if you haven't already.

The food was surprisingly good considering the fair ratings. We came with a large group and each person's food looked great and was said to have been good. I ordered cheesesteak egg rolls and truffle fries. Both were tasty and flavorful. The truffle fries are basically lightly seasoned fries and dip on the side. The prices are reasonable and we had an attentive and friendly waitress. I'd definitely want to return to try some of the great looking items others had ordered from our table.

So lemme give you the Artic Scoop: the almond cookie ice cream inside the lavender cone and fresh strawberries atop was refreshingly delicious! The creamy, light and sweet almond flavored ice cream is so good! You can taste the soft, tiny cookies throughout! The strawberries were sweet and fresh--it paired well with almond cookie ice cream. What was most intriguing was the lavender cone. It had a subtle lavender flavor and left a beautiful aroma in my mouth. The waffle cone had the best texture! That's not all the Artic Scoop has. I have to go back and try their amazing-looking coconut bowl!

I really enjoyed this Italian restaurant. I was pleased with the fettuccine carbonara which provides a large portion to share between 2 people. It was flavorful and filling, with pork, mushrooms and peas. We were given warm complimentary rolls which were tasty. Our food came out pretty fast.

What I liked most was the architectural design of the restaurant and the quintessential Christmas music playing in the background adding to a nice December night.

The service was prompt, friendly and attentive.

I'm sad to say I was quite disappointed with my cheesesteak at Dalessandro's.  It did not live up to the hype.

First the good:
- The roll.  It was fresh, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
- The cheese.  Sharp provolone.  Do I need to say more?

The bad:
- The meat.  While I am a fan of chopped meat, Dalessando's meat was so overchopped it was essentially dry meat crumbs.  In fact it was so dry, I was looking for add-ons to moisten the sandwich.

Unfortunately, I am not a fan.

This review is based strictly on their customer service.  I'll never be able to review their Inn, as they'll never get my business.

I called to inquire about blocking 20 rooms for two nights.  Over the course of a week I left two messages for the general manager, who never returned my call.  So I left a message for the assistant general manager.  They both finally returned my calls within moments of each other, asked for my email to send me more information, and I never heard from either again.  That was two weeks ago.  They clearly don't need my business, so I took it elsewhere.

Me and my wife stopped here on a whim while having a free day for lunch and I'm so glad we did. We ordered from the lunch special menu both times. The ceviche and whiskey flights definitely stood out the most. My tacos were good and flavorful. but were a bit watery for my taste. The second time I ordered a burger which was pretty solid and the fries were supposed to have adobo seasoning, but tasted pretty normal imo

Overall, the flavor and serving size was on point and the whiskey flights ranging from 5-15 years aged paired well.
I actually really digged the decor of the space. The displays with the combo with bottles of bourbon and books really worked. 

OMG I wish I could remember the name of the dessert we had! I think was some type of banana bread pudding with butterscotch bourbon ice cream. Whatever it was, it was outstanding. Will definitely check out the happy hour next time. It's supposed to be really good with pretty nice deals.

Hey, my fellow yelp fam!
Honestly I come to Max's for the experience on top of the good cheese steak. Although the service and food takes literally what feels like an hour, it's still worth going way up olney to have. 
My personal advice about Max's is going early as possible, getting takeout, or ordering and leaving to run a quick errand nearby. Don't wait in line unless you just don't mind the long wait. Oh and don't dare ask for toppings last minute once it's time to wrap your sandwich unless you want trouble. 
And if you happen to need some random headphones, socks, laundry detergent, or sixers tickets, there's always someone walking through selling those items. Where they store it all no one knows, but back to the review.
Max's doesn't skimp on the amount of steak. The prices went up a little bit since my last visit over 8 months ago, but the quantity / quality for your buck is still there. I used to be able to eat a whole cheese steak to myself, but now-a-days, I just split one with ppl I make go up there with me lol. 4 stars only because the wait time is terrible, but overall I still love Max's once in a blue moon.

So if anyone ever wants to go to Max's to split a cheesesteak, let me know! :-) 

#cheesesteaksandheadphones

Renata's is the perfect example of how social environment plays a big part in your food experience. Renata's fits right into Baltimore Avenue's hipster home grown foodie vibe with a seasonal menu to compliment it.
It took me a good year after this place was open to try it because its pretty full on the weekends and they aren't really open after 5 pm during the weekday. So you catch it while you can. 

During my first dining experience here I challenged myself not to be basic and not order something with pumpkin in it. 
I ordered the empanadas with chorizo and fried egg (which was on the seasonal menu). The empandas were stuff with some really flavorful vegetable medley with some type of  warm hollandiase sauce with a taste I can't describe.  

The portions were fair, but what makes this place really magical to me are the random folks just dining, doing work on their laptops, or having small business meetings over ice coffee. The outside seating is lovely in the summer with little foot traffic of pedestrians between tables. I'll for sure be back to try the pumpkin pancakes soon. I can't escape my basic tendencies forever.

Me and my wife went here on a random kid-free day just to realize that our daughter would have a ball watching the chef in action. This hibachi wasn't the most upscale of them all, but it got the job done. Plus the chef threw me some extra shrimp and veggies and we're best foodie friends now if doesn't already know. 

We we're almost sat next to a family of six with 4 lovely, but very excitable children and I hinted to the host that we were kid free today and they immediately redirected us to the kid free section lol. We sat next to some really cool ppl who hadn't experienced a hibachi style dinner before, so it was cool to chat a bit about it. 

I ordered some chicken fried rice with spicy dragon sushi and some type of volcano inspired drink. No LITERALLY the drink was on fire lol. I really enjoy my chicken fried rice! The mix veggies were cooked well, but the sushi was just okay. My volcano drink started off tasty, but they put way too much ice in it, so the watered down taste wasn't as appealing. 

Prices were right up there with any other hibachi, but I did notice they have lunch specials so I will be looking into that soon!

I mean what else is there to say about the one and only capital grille!?! I came late to the party but ordered my food right on time because no menu was needed lol I order the chicken with shitake mushrooms and risotto layered with asparagus and paired it with a glass of Joseph Phelps chardonnay. 

The lighting was a bit dim since the sun was on full beastmode, but the clouds brought the same energy which changed the lighting mood in a good way. My chicken was slayed to perfection. I still have leftovers. Not that I couldn't finish it. I just wanted to taste more the next day lol The risotto was great, but needed a little spice for my liking. Our server was dope. She brought me out a tiny bowl of red pepper flake which really gave me the taste i was looking for in the risotto. I did nibble from a friends lobster mac n' cheese which was REALLY GOOD. 

Did I mention our server was dope?!? We asked if we could take a pic in the wine room that's displayed in the middle of the restaurant which isn't normally open to customers, but she asked the manager to grant the b-day gals wish we came out to celebrate and they did. :-)

I had doctors appointment and was really hungry afterwards and of all the food trucks nearby, this one had the most interesting food. The line wasn't too bad and there weren't a load of options to choose from which I prefer at a food truck so I'm not take time up in line with HANGRY people behind me. lol

I ordered the korean rib burrito which I expected to come out sort of small but to my surprise was pretty big considering the good price! My burrito definitely was falling part which was not fun while trying to keep a car clean, but the flavors were amazing. The rib wasn't overcooked and the sauce..was VERY good. The blend of sweet and spicy was perfect and the added crunch of the ginger coleslaw added great texture. 

I'll definitely being ordering that little (big really big) burrito again If I'm in the area.

This was my third time eating here and I generally enjoyed it every time.
For Tampopo to be located in a very competitive foodie area, it seems to be doing very well. This spot is a nice eat-in / take out hybrid and has a chill environment. I've only order the rice bowl with spicy chicken. I honestly assumed the chicken would be THAT spicy but it was! And In a very good way. The chicken was a bit dry, but overall pretty good seasoned well. 
I tried some type of unsweetened tea drink that I absolutely hated, but that's what I get for ordering something I knew I wouldn't like since I'm not the biggest unsweetened tea fan.
It's also a little pricey, but overall its good quick group hangout / meet up spot to chow at.

Not gonna lie, I didn't know what to expect reading some recent reviews hat were really mixed, but WHOA was I pleased! This was a last minute option, but a great stumble upon. The waitress let us know that their pizza was made by Pizza Gutt and I knew we were gonna eat good. 

We ate outside and it was a bit cold, but I was too distracted by how good the pumpkin spice beer paired with the pepperoni pizza I ordered. The pizza was one of the best pies I've had in YEARS. The crust was charred perfection and very fluffy and light, yet crispy. The sauce was seasoned so well and jus enough cheese, but not overbearing. I only ate half and had the rest the next day. 

This $17 price point for a pizza pie was well worth it.

** This review is based on the new Falafel Burrito**

When attempting to create a Falafel Burrito, there are a few important things:
1. gotta know how to make actual Falafel. Honest Tom's? Check.
2. Ya gotta know how to make a solid burrito base. Honest Tom's? Check.
3. A tough one. How does one fuse the classic burrito taste with the strong flavor of Falafel? I. Don't. Know.

Honest tom's made a brave attempt at this feat. It was a very tasty burrito, but I was wish there was more of a corn salsa / guac like flavor to it. That's really it! 
The falafel itself wasn't over cooked nor did the ingredients present lack any flavor. Overall it mostly tasted like falafel in a burrito wrap. Like if you were making falafel at home and you were like "Dang it, I ran out of pita! Oh well, I guess I'll use these burrito wraps." It kind felt like that. 
Not that it wasn't tasty! 
Trust me I will be eating this again!

ME and my wife have been eating at Vietnam Cafe for a few years now and decided to order takeout tonight. I was happily surprised that the wait time was  only 15 minutes! In the past, dining in would have a 25 min wait time.

My favorite by far were the spring rolls. I forgot to take a pic of them, but they were so light, flavorful, and crispy as it gets. I even ate the random lettuce used for decoration and dipped that in the eggroll sauce.
 
My pad thai was pretty solid, too. The texture of the noodles was good, but I did expect more spice, more peanuts, and there were no shallots at all which made me a little sad. They aren't known for their pad thai, so I wished I tried something else. (Does anyone have any suggestions? Hint. Hint.)

Overall, the quick turnaround time for ordering is well worth putting vietnam cafe in the take-out rotation

I hadn't even had hibiscus in over a year and mostly because there are so many other options in the area now and hibiscus has love a little bit of a history of being slow. Luckily all that changed! 
The food is just as good as I remembered. I ordered the vegan cheesesteak and my wife got the jerk tofu  platter. The food is as good as I remembered it with the texture being just right and the portion size. My wife enjoyed her tofu jerk situation. We also ordered a piece of carrot cake to go. The carrot cake texture just wasn't for me. Overall I still love the food here

As ya'll know, I had a bad chicken casear salad from here last week, which I have to say in retrospect was an isolated incident because I went yesterday for Happy Hour and the food and drinks were AMAZING as usual! I normally only get cheesecake while i;m here but the adventurous side of me said "bruh, lets get some carrotcake". 
And lemme tell ya...the Carrotcake was arguably the best I've had. I've had some good carrotcake in my short life, but the cheescake factory carrot cake was HUGE and very moist! Well worth the $8 value! 

The Nachos are really...really..really good, too. It's usually all I can handle unless i'm sharing some with my greedy friends, i mean hungry friends. I'm actually going to attempt to try the chicken casear salad again because I'm confident it was a one-time thang. 

Thangs happen, yanno??

Not a bad burger joint at all. The fries were really solid. My only gripe with the burger was it overall felt flat. It's hard o describe, but usually burgers are a bit plump and juicy, but this was almost as if someone in the back flattened the burger as much as possible. Still pretty tasty tho.

My daughter didn't like her chicken fingers at all, but I ate them for her. lol I do wish there were more options for kids, but all is good.

Oh, how I missed the donuts here! Grabbed some donuts before the holidays to take to the fam. Grabbed some basics, but wanted to try the bacon donut. It was ok. I'm such a traditional donuter (Yes, I said donuter) and good ole chocolate or vanilla donuts are my preference. The line was CRAZY, but well worth it.

I'm JUST learning there is a location in west philly and that I trucked it all the way downtown for nothing lol I'll be heading to the west philly one next time.

I'm not gonna wait on this one and just start by saying this was one of the best breakfast platter I've had in quite a while. Just the right amount of food, just the right amount of portions, and the right amount of seasoning. 

I ordered the pancakes loaded with bananas and chocolate chips cooked in the pancakes, with seasoned potatoes, eggs, and turkey sausage for $14 which wasn't a bad price compared to another fave place I went to recently that charged $13 just for baked french toast with a small fruit salad. Both were tasty, but bang for buck matters sometimes.

Honey's flavor on the potatoes and crispy edges were such a good balance to the soft eggs and maple syrup-ish sausage, but the real highlight were the pancakes....So soft due to the bananas melting all in the batter yet at the same time creating a crispy edge. Just perfect.

I'm giving 5 stars but, it's more like 4.5 because it was soooooooooo drafty in there, and we were sat next to a super drafty window and it was tough to really enjoy the food. Def will be here in the summer tho lol

I've been to Jones a dozen times over the years and this was my first time hanging at their bar for happy hour. It wasn't bad at all! The bar has limited seating, but the overall decor is beautiful. 
The bartender was pretty chill and made some good drink pairings with food. I decided to have dessert for dinner and ordered a butter pecan spiked milkshake.
Usually I either taste the sweetness of a spiked milkshake or it's overly spiked and there's no flavor. 
]Lemme tell you how THIS ONE was perfectly balanced. And it actually tasted as advertised! The best part was the flavor. The butterscotch liqueur, the whip cream, and candied pecans were just fantastic. The only thing I wish was that it was bigger for the price point ($12), but it was served it in mason jar so they get a pass. Drinks taste better in mason jars. Clearly that's sarcasm or is it?

I really wanted a chicken crepe from here, but the online menu said they "may can fulfill" the order depend on the moment. I didn't understand that so I just ordered the lamb manakeesh type flatbread. My wife ordered a potato and cauliflower wrap. 

The taste of my lamb mana was all there, but i was really surprised at how small it was compared to before. All good, I get that's becoming the norm at some places. I pretty much folded it into a wrap lol

My wife's wrap was HUGE and she really enjoyed the flavor. I asked for a bite, but she wasn't in the sharing mood because her wrap was so tasty. Maybe next time she will share. OR maybe I'll just order a wrap.

MMM I love me some Ed's. I hadn't eaten at Eds since lock down and I've missed their signature general tso pizza! (Yes, you read that right) 
Finally got me a slice and the foodie nostalgia just overwhelmed me while I shed foodie tears, enjoying every bite. Ordering fries took way longer than I expected and they were as good and crispy as I remember. Overall, I'm glad one of my fave college style eats is around and kicking.

So I came here for restaurant week hoping to be but dazzled off my toes  Because of all the awesome things I've heard about in this restaurants and the beautiful decor has.  
And don't get me wrong, food with good but not as flavorful as i thought it would be. 

I ordered a solid for an appetizer. Nothing to talk about. Basic salad.  Basic lettuce. Basic vinaigrette. Basic fork. Basic plate.
Then I order the aged Burger with brioche bun cause I love a basic burger.  The poblano peppers on the Burger though? WELL PLAYED.
I'm basically basic.

 The highlight of this whole ordeal was the dessert.  The blueberry pie with that wonderful  raspberry compote was tear jerking good. The dessert was bitter sweet because from what I heard it wasn't going to be available after resturant week because the pastry chef changes out desserts often. 

I'm thinking a good idea would be to go there just for wine and dessert because at least the pastry chef is full of surprises.

I knoowwww i knooowww Trader Joes is known in the community sometimes as the high end hipsters market, but I always feel great when i walk in here! I can't explain it other than it always smells like spring time and they have the most unique food items and even people lol. 
I love that the shopping cart is big enough to get everything i need, but small enough so i don't overspend. Cause Trader Joes prices can sneak up on you. Maybe you shouldn't buy that small pack of 3 cheese artisan mushroom and cilantro ravioli for $8 bucks. Or that apple cinnamon goat cheese..mmm on second thought keep the goat cheese, its freaking delicious when they have it. 
The lines are never long either. I always bring my own bags cause those paper bags lowkey rip pretty easy if you aren't going straight home. 
If you ever go to the center city location, park on the street and save yourself 20 min just waiting in the car line for a parking lot spot to open.

I stumbled upon t-swirl on a random walk thru Chinatown after spending half my life in Penndot. I badly needed a bubbletea fix and couldn't help but notice the beautiful dark wood design of t-swirl. Displays of their crepes were in the window inside of glass cases like fine works of art. 
Plus I saw their $9 crepe and bubbletea combo deal between 11am and 6pm which is hard to pass up because the crepes average between $7-$7.50 and bubbletea at $3.75. Simple math to me.

I purchased the "Matcha" crepe which featured  strawberries, pistachios, chocolate truffle drizzle and yogurt cream. And a mango bubbletea cause I'm basic like that.
The mango tea was...mango tea. Let's get to the crepe, mkay?

The crepe was prepared in a waffle cone like shape and stuffed in a giant French fries container pretty much. Not a bad idea if u want your crepe on the go. I expected the crepe to be soft but surprisingly it was nice and crispy around the edges. It wasn't as dense as I would prefer for the price point but very tasty overall. The yogurt cream was a nice equalizer between the sweet strawberries and the salty pistachios. The chocolate truffle drizzle gave the crepe a nice soft texture in the middle. I wasn't full from the crepe but combined with the bubbletea it was just right. 
I'll totally eat here and and try a savory crepe next time. I heard the thai chicken crepe is LIT.

The one thing I will say about Suraya is the layout is absolutely beautiful and well thought out. The front is more like a chill cafe for casuals which blends into the main dining area for both casuals and some fine dining without seeming like their trying to hard. 
The decor of Suraya reminds me of the one friend with the one Aunt /Uncle with old money that no one in the family actually knows what they do for a living, but damn can they throw a chill gathering with good food and good vibes. 
The food itself is pretty solid and more portions than I expected. 
The only thing I did expect was a lot more flavor, but it just wasn't all the way there. Not that the food wasn't amazing, but I didn't day dream about it as much as I daydreamed about the decor.
We ordered the mushroom hummus which was the best item of the bunch. Full of flavor and nice big portion of it. The falafel wrap was what you would expect. A wrap. 
I will surely be back to Suraya to try the cafe side next time out of pure curiosity, especially since they have a kid menu.

I've been eating at green eggs for years  And they never disappoint.  There was a point in time where the line green eggs was out the door and you'd be lucky to get a seat on the weekend.  Now that they have more locations it's a bit easier to pop in and get a good bite to eat.  The price point has increased a bit but the quality of the food is still the same.  All The Times I've call in there I'm surprised I've never tried their coffee or tea but I make a note to do that 1 day.  I've noticed the portions are that smaller regarding the pancake and french toast selection,  But I'm not complaining because I can barely get through half of the meal when I used to get it. 
I tried the pecan stuffed French toast which was filled with cooked down pecans with a cream cheese like drizzle over the french toast.  I expected it to be sweet as a grandmothers forehead kiss, but a surprisingly was not. 
 And I actually made it through an entire serving! Yay me!

*&Pizza and CerealMilk Collab Review*

Soooo the other day i tried the soda created by &pizza and CerealMilk. Boi....this had to be the most interesting flavor I've had in a long time in a GREAT way. I had only tried the fig soda at &pizza and swore i would never find another fave....til now. 

The strong taste of vanilla cream  in the soda paired so nicely with the farmers daughter pizza i had since it has a little spicy kick to it. 

All i could wish was i had some vanilla bourbon to slip into my soda but we don't encourage drinking in our yelp reviews. 
Stay in school, kids.

Anyway I enjoyed the soda collab!

I can't believe I'm just eating here! As much as I spend time at HMart which is right next door. The food looked and sounded very good and I couldn't wait to dive into my food. After ordering, it only took 15 minutes for the food to be ready. 

We ordered the Tofu and chicken vermicelli, some chicken and steamed rice for my daughter, and two pork and veggie spring rolls. The vermicelli was pretty solid and hefty. I barely finished mine but it was really good. There was more protein in both dishes than we expected which is never a bad thing. I do with the food came in tougher styrofoam because once you pour the sauce on, it feels like its gonna leak on ya. Otherwise it was darn good. 

The spring rolls were by far my favorite thing. I don't think I've ever had crispier rolls in my life. The roll was very thick and well done, just how I personally prefer them. The sauce which is the same as what comes with the vermicelli was good, but kinda thin so it didn't hold well until you took that first bite when the roll is open which lets the sauce roll on through. 

Everything was around $40 bucks which was a darn good deal for the quality and portions. Definitely trying other rolls and pork buns next time.

Business lunch surprise.  Came to this beautiful location for an informal business lunch and it really was outstanding.  One of the people I was with ordered the guacamole as an appetizer.  They came out with a tray full of ingredients for you to choose and make the guacamole tableside.  I don't think you can get guacamole dip any fresher.

For a starter I had their soup and it was in the upper half of all soup I have had since I turned 60 and the government made me eat soup.

The Carne Asada was very flavorful and seasoned to perfection.  I do believe this is the first time I have ever eaten Carne Asada.  I am a total fan.

For the location, Clayton, the prices were well within line of an upper tier Mexican place.

Café Telegraph is very hard to put in a category.  They have normal bar food, burgers, fries, onion rings, hot pretzels, BREADED BACON.  They also have an Italian menu, pasta, pizza, toasted raviolis, meatball sandwich.  Am I finished no.  They have a smoke house featuring, pork steak, chicken, meatloaf, and ribs.
