I had the pork steak and it served with a dry rub with BBQ sauce on the side.  I like my pork steaks old school no rub and sauced cooked into the meat.  What is astounding is how big the pork steak is.  Gargantuan. Godzilla, Big Foot huge.  This can easily feed two people or if you are wimps 3 people. For $16.00 you get the pork steak, and two sides.  

Mrs K. had the pulled pork sandwich.  She ate only 1/3 of the sandwich before calling it quits.  She is not a fan of dry rub and was not happy with her sandwich.  This is in no way a slam at the food.  It was preference.

All the food is named after St. Louis High Schools.  I could not find my dear Chaminade but St. John Vianney was on the menu..  There was a tilt toward the Catholic schools. 

 So I had to ask our server where did you go to school?  St. Elizabeth's and Soldan.  Wow now that is interesting. (for those reading this not from St. Louis this question is very normal to ask.  It also tells you many things about the person, IE religion, affluence, status.)

I would not hesitate to recommend this place.  Service was very good and friendly.  You should have no problem finding  something here that will suit your taste profile.

This area of Creve Coeur in fact all of Creve Coeur needed a café.  Olive Street comes to the rescue.  

They know the area they are in and serve slightly upscale food.  At an upscale price.  

I ordered the "Country Slinger".  Which in any other world would have been called ham and eggs on two biscuits smothered in gravy. I was a clean platter I ate the whole thing and washed down with cups of coffee. Not bad at all.  

For people who are not from the slinger capitol of the world a true slinger is as follows.

 butter
 shredded hash brown potatoes 
 hamburger patty, cooked to desired doneness
2 eggs
 yellow or white onions
chilie  with beans (such as Edmond's Chile), heated through 
 mild cheddar cheese
2 slices buttered toast

As you can see a true diner slinger is something much more cholesterol friendly.  A slinger a day will make sure you will not on this earth stay.  

Good luck to Olive Street café I hope they knock it out of the ball park.  And if I ever want a buffalo burger this is were I could come.

This is a great cross section of St. Louis.  A good place with good food and good service.  Hard working people serving you and hard working people being served.

I ordered the chicken livers in linguine(not on the menu) and they made it up for me.  They were good not the best ever but darn good.  I was finishing my serving when I bit down on something that was not chicken livers, nor linguine.  It looked to be a small twig.  I did not want to make a big deal out of it so I didn't.  The twig did not influence my review.

I would not hesitate to come back and try other items on the menu.

This is now my official 400th review.

Wife and I come here on 2/20/2014 at 12:15pm.  Walk in and stop at the entrance table and wait for the person who is running the seating to get to her station.   At 12:20 a server says someone will be right with us.  At about 12:23 the person shows up looks at her table chart and asks how many?  I say two.  She then stares at the table chart some more.  Now this is where it really fell apart.  I am looking at a 4 top right in front of me empty.  She then asks the people behind me how many are in their party?  Who just walked in by the way.  They say 2.  Now as if by magic there are three people staring at a plastic seating chart and I am staring at an empty table.  It is now 12:27 and I walk out.   Folks at Katie's it is a service business and you failed.  Now I know you have all the big 5 stars going for you but not from me.

The owner of Milagro is a big fan of Rick Bayless. I want to say thank you!!  This is Mexican food that is not stereotyped like every other Mexican place in St. Louis. The food is good, different, and filling.  

Being Father's Day my son wanted to pick up the bill and I got to choose.  Happy I did choose Milagro.

I ordered a cup of chili for a starter.  This chili is not like any version I have had.  It had prime cuts of beef mixed with the chilies and the sauce. Best I have ever had.

 For my main I ordered the chile relleno.  A wonderful relleno pepper stuffed with cheese and beef and then fried with a batter.  The dish came with Mexican rice and sweet corn which complimented the relleno.  

Funny story I asked it I could have refried beans.  Dead silence from server and my son.  I mean crickets could be heard.  Uh sir we don't serve that here.  Dang!  I forgot I was not at the norm of Mexican in St. Louis, I was at the best.

I have not written anything in about 2 weeks and thought hey why not update Pappy's.  It does not have any reviews so I thought I would throw them a bone.

Mrs K and I went for lunch on Thursday at 11:20 am the line was not out the door but close.  As been said many times it does move fast.  I ordered the BBQ brisket plate with coleslaw and just to be friendly I also ordered a hot link.  Filled the soda found a chair and out comes the order.  god they are fast.  I slathered the bbq brisket with Pappy's original sauce.  Tangy with a bit of heat fantastic.  I proceeded to eat the hot link not too hot but good.  Mrs K refused a taste of the link so I had to eat it all by myself.  Bless her heart.  We finished eating at about 12:15.  So you can do the math at how long it took.  I don't do math.  After lunch it was off to the Fox for Jersey Boys afternoon show.  Pretty good day off huh?

I came to CJ Muggs because I was on jury duty and it was the closest place to have a nice lunch.  I would say with all the money I made being a jurist for one day would not pay for this lunch.  In fact the money paid would not cover McDonalds.  I am sorry I digressed.

I came alone as I was the lonely jurist.  Oops digressed.  

I was seated upon arrival at the establishment.  I could have eaten at the bar but a table with a TV just above me was a great choice.  My server introduced herself and promptly served me my drink.  I ordered the muffuletta ( olive salad, including oil. Layer with  salami, ham, mortadella, mozzarella and Provolone).  It was served with French fries which I did not eat as the sandwich is huge.

I have had muffuletta in different places and I am going to say this was the best muffuletta I have ever eaten.  It was like every bite you were sad because there was less of the sandwich and you knew the end was going to come.  Dang that sandwich was wonderful.  And I am sure my fellow people on jury duty loved my breath after eating that sandwich.  LOL!!

I was fortunate enough to come here with our Yelp International Supper Club.  As usual Sarah did all the work and the rest of us just walk in and sit down and have a great meal.

Thai food can be very complex and I think this is what makes it so different than any other Asian cuisine.

I ordered their roast duck with white rice and cucumbers.  Never in my experience would I have thought cucumbers would add to the flavor of any dish much less duck. It was very good with the duck and very refreshing to the palate.

I tend to like mild duck or I would supposed farm raised duck as opposed to wild duck.  As the duck of my youth never tasted as good as the duck of my latter years.

I came here for our monthly International Supper Club.  Taking care of 12 foodies and getting almost everything right is one hard job.  Oh just to make it more complicated we also need 12 separate checks and you must somehow get the food to us at the same time.  Whew!  That is a tall order.  I do believe one person food came out late but understandable.

I had two items their house salad and the Beef Spiedini.  This dish also came with a side dish of pasta your choice of white or red.  I have challenged myself to find a better meal at the price I paid.  The bill was $18.00.  The food was just awesome with good flavor and texture.

As with everyone of these meetings Yelper Sarah put it all together for the group.  We just walk in and she has made sure we are taken care of.  Great job Sarah!!  And it was a wonderful group of people who attended.

I have come to the second most popular smokehouse barbeque place in the Metropolitan area.
While dinning I was treated to the inside scoop as why Bogart's split from Pappy's.  It was not a friendly split it was rather acrimonious.  Lawyers and legal battles.  Not what we were led to believe the owner of Bogart's wanted to spread his wings and fly.  I also have been told it was now ancient history and the two smokehouses get along and play nice together.  It is just the right ending.  As the belief that all the these places are somehow connected to the magic name of Pappy's.

Went on a Wednesday and the line was of course out the door.  With a gentleman outside handling the line with true professionalism.  The line moved fast and we were able to order sit and the food came to the table very fast. 

I ordered the burnt ends sandwich.  Burnt ends are the overcooked part of the beef brisket thus the name burnt ends.  They were tender and of course slightly burnt.  I used the voodoo sauce which has just the right amount of heat.  Not so much that you are in pain when you eat just enough to let you know the sauce is there.  Great sandwich but no need for the bread as the meat was piled so high the bread would have been too much to eat.

The meal came with two sides of your choice mine was slaw and potato salad.  The potato salad was closer to a German style than an Irish style.  I really enjoyed it.  The coleslaw was the typical creamy coleslaw you get anywhere.  Solid but really what can you do with a creamy coleslaw?

It is worth the hype and drive.  They do close early and of course run out of food fast.

I like a good Gyro and St. Louis Gyro is an ok gyro.  It is in the style of made fresh while you wait.  You also pick out what you want on the gyro. I am not fond of this concept as I feel like I am at a Subway place instead of a gyro place.  The taste was fine because I think I guessed correctly on the ingredients.

This is a small establishment with limited tables.  With drink I was at $12.00 which I thought was on the high side of what I wanted to spend.

I have wanted to try this place since I first read about it.  We had a UYE with a group of ten.  The place was very crowded and it was Tuesday night.  Good for them bad for us.  I think we received about what I would expect as far as service. 10 people, 10 different orders, and 10 different checks.  That is hard my friends.

I ordered their Bestie Special.  The special consisted of the following, beef brisket, bologna, and pork ribs.  This dish also comes with two sides which were pepper potato salad and smoked beans. I took a taste of each side and did not need to go on.  Was not my type of food. Nor my taste palate.  In fact it was almost inedible.

 The rub they use at this BBQ place is very heavy.  In fact it is so heavy you cannot see the meat on the ribs just the rub.  I took one bite of the ribs and that was enough for me.  No more.  I took a taste of the smoked bologna and it was as dry as shoe leather, which leaves the brisket.  Way to much rub so you could not taste the meat.  I do not think this is typical of Salt and Smoke I caught them on an off night.  But I can say in all honesty I don't see a reason to come back. I can say I have been there and tried that.

While the service was top notch and attentive I was very disappointed in the main dish rack of lamb I was served. Their name for this dish is "Agnello" and the dish is described as "GRILLED RACK OF LAMB WITH GRAIN MUSTARD, HERB GLAZE AND ESCALLOPED POTATOES "
 While the rack of lamb was served as chops and not rack did not really disappoint me but the grain mustard was very off putting to the lamb.  I thought when I was eating the lamb it was vinegar based sauce.  I never picked up the grain mustard flavor.  I asked for medium and was served medium well done lamb.  Again not a deal breaker but not what I wanted.  

The positive to this meal was my starter dish. They called it "Cozze al Brodo"  and the description is as follows "STEAMED MUSSELS IN SPICY TOMATO BROTH WITH BRUSCHETTA"  The spicy tomato broth was also heavy on the garlic I loved it.  The broth was the best thing I ate that night.  

Mrs. K. ordered their beef filet and requested it cooked medium well it was served well done.  I don't fault because anything ordered above medium on a steak is asking for it to be overcooked.  The steak was very dry and was not finished nor taken home.

Not a three star or two star review because in final analysis I believe their are dishes that would have been 5 stars on the menu I just did not order them.

I came here for an unofficial Yelp Event.  International Supper Club.  One of my favorite events put on by Sarah.  She does wonderful work making sure everything is in place for the supper club.

Taze is an interesting concept.  Street food served in a café setting.  You go through the line like a cafeteria.  And they will customize your order the way you want it.

I ordered a gyro and had it my way.  Feta, cucumber, onions, olives, with beef and lamb.  I really like the gyro as it was made to my specifications. 

Taze is one of places I would never would have gone unless the supper club had it.  I also know my wife would not have enjoyed it.  The beef and pork kabobs would have been a little to dry for her tastes as she likes the meat to be tender moist.

International Supper Club.  Really I should just leave with those three words.  Sarah once again hits a home run.  The service for 14 people with individual checks and of course different selections.  Our server place every order to the correct person without asking.  Great Job!!

Being a Greek place I was very happy to order a Greek salad and the lamb shank.  While the picture of the shank looks huge and there was ample meat on the bone it was by no means able to feed a family of four.  It fed just me and I left wanting to come back and get some different dishes.

Most importantly this is a value place with value pricing and outstanding service and outstanding food.

This restaurant has been around forever.  I have been around forever.  Two forevers came together for a wonderful evening of celebration of awesome food.

We have an area of the city that is a neighborhood dominated by fine Italian dining.  This has been one of the crown jewels of the area.  The list of celebrities that have eaten here is long but Frank Sinatra should sum up the caliber of food they serve.

I had two items their salad and their Pasta Seafood Suzanne.  The salad came in Charlie Gitto's own dressing, hand selected cheese, and for $1.50 I added anchovies.  This is a high quality salad and the cheeses did not dominate the salad they complimented it in a very unobtrusive manner.  

The Pasta Seafood Suzanne had homemade noodles, shrimp, mussels, clams, and bits of seafood in a light garlic cream sauce.  To kick this up a notch they added a pepper spice that did not overpower but complimented the seafood and pasta perfectly.

Food impeccable, Service impeccable.  Location impeccable.   Amazing older building with free valet parking.

I have read reviews of this place and the first thing I thought of what is naughty about ice cream?  I found out last night.  There are regular ice creams then there are ice creams made with bourbon or just about any other alcohol available.  So that was the naughty.  

I had the nice ice cream.  I saw on the board gooey butter ice cream.  Oh my!  For those who don't know what gooey butter is here is a link https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gooey_butter_cake

Now you are informed on the origins of gooey butter you will be pleased to know it tasted fantastic.  I don't like to say it was the best I ever had, (saying that means I have nothing to look forward too),  but it was great.  

Locally owned and operated.

There is a new steakhouse in town and it is worth every penny you spend.  

We started with their onions rings which I was told had a 17 step preparation before they cook them.  My expectations were high and after my first taste I was a bit let down.  The second onion ring gave me the taste I was looking for.  I believe it took my taste buds a bit to adjust.

While the prices are steep I want to remind you that every meal comes with a salad and one side.  So the price you see on the menu will be your complete meal.

Their salad is served family style with the addition of cold plates set so place your salad on.  They serve it with their house dressing or if you choose they will bring you blue cheese dressing.  I opted for the blue cheese and you could tell it was scratch made.  What a delectable dressing.  Out standing job.

The beef here is supplied by a single supplier which will give them a consistency in their product.  All beef is then aged on site from 77 days to over 100!!  I mention this because the beef will lose about 30% of the weight because of aging.  So this makes the prices more reasonable in that they are losing value while gaining quality.

I ordered their super large cut of prime rib.  I knew I was not going to finish it and I was planning to have another meal.  In all my years I have had many pieces of prime rib.  I will state here and now this was one of the best I ever ate.  The aging took the prime rib to a tender level that I have never ever eaten in my life.  I was amazing.

The table shared a turtle pie.  While wedding cake is their signature dessert this dessert is well worth trying.  And one piece was more than enough for four people.

I came here the day after Thanksgiving.  The high points was the toasted ravioli and the service.

I ordered the Osso Bucco  and was disappointed.  It is a pork shank which is fine with me.  The Osso Bucco was served with polenta and asparagus.  The shank while tender was very dry and had no flavor. If  it came with potatoes and a decent sauce it would have helped the dish.   But the sauce was almost dried on the plate.  Not making my list of places I really want to do over.  Way too many other places to try.

I have been seeing reviews on Roberto's on Yelp.  I never really gave it much thought.  Everything about Roberto's screams wrong don't go.  Location being the biggest.  But as one Yelper stated if it wasn't for Yelp I would have never gone.  Very true statement.  

Now what did I and Mrs. K enjoy?  I had the caesar salad for a starter.  It was a true caesar with the raw egg mixed into the dressing.  I was very surprised that it was made this way.  Health laws have made it almost illegal to make it with the raw egg.  This was one of the best caesar salad I have had in a long time.  Mrs. K. just had the house salad with the house dressing and she loved it.  

For my entree I ordered spaghetti Americano.  It was a spicy red sauce with onions mixed in.  It was not really spicy but it sure was good.  Mrs. K. ordered the chicken spiedini.  This was also a top notch dish.  

The menu is not large but has a variety to make you want to come back and try many other options on the menu.  My next visit with be a veal chop.  I saw it on someones plate and I sure like what I saw.

This is a two person operation.  One partner works in the back doing the cooking and the other owner works the front of the house.  Both are from Bosnia.  What is interesting is they do not serve Bosnian food. They serve Paninis, hamburgers, and pizza.  I ordered the  Bistro burger.  This burger was served on a super fresh bun with all the toppings.  It was fried on a grill and tasted perfect.  The burger came with an order of French fries.

Mrs. K. (my Mrs. K.) ordered a pepperoni pizza.  This pizza was served neopolitan style.  What makes this pizza special is the dough is made from scratch, cooked in a wood fired oven, and served hot.  The other Mrs. K.(Chip K's) ordered a buffalo chicken pizza.  Made the same way as the pepperoni pizza.  There was a light drizzle of ranch dressing on top.  Never tasted a buffalo pizza before and it was mighty fine pizza.

What makes this 5 stars is the food is solid, the service was somewhat slow but remember only one person working and the price was amazing.  All the food we ordered including an appetizer was $59.00 before tip.  This included soft drinks.  Crazy great pricing.  I would so come back again and try some other items on the menu that caught my attention such as the meatball sandwich.

Parking can be a bit of a problem as only street parking is available.

This establishment could not be more hidden.  I was familiar with this area in my youth and my truck driving days.  But 40 plus years things change and I was about as lost as one can get with a GPS.  Gribic is located at the confluence of three streets and the signage is not obvious.  I stopped my car in the middle of three streets and looked around and thought this must be the place.  Eureka!!  I was or rather the GPS was spot on.

Now knowing it is somewhat hard to find I walk in and what I expected to  see and what I saw was stunning.  Beautiful wood, table cloths, fireplace, ambiance of the first order.  The thought comes to my mind of a expecting a sow's ear and seeing a silk purse.

Gribic is one of those places that should not be visited once and say been there done that.  I saw at least 4 items I really want to try.  Their goulash and Swiss specialty being first to try followed by the veal schnitzel.

For starters I ordered the Tarhana which is a traditional soup of the Balkans; homemade sourdough noodles with ground beef and vegetables.  More simply it was a lintel soup. Darn fine soup.

I ordered the Mixed Gribic plate which consists of A mix of their finest cuts of meat grilled to perfection: Babo's chicken, Cevapi, Pljeskavica, Chicken Shish Kabob, cutlet of veal served with vegetables.  I cleaned my plate and felt like I had a wonderful Bosnian feast.  Yes Bosnian.  

St. Louis has had the great privilege to be an immigration point for the people of Bosnia.  And they have given so much to the area in culture and customs.  Gribic is just a small part of a great story of immigration and energizing a city.

Born and lived in Webster Groves for 28 years.  When I left, this location was a pharmacy.  What makes CJ noteworthy is they are the first to serve alcohol in Webster Groves.  Webster Groves was a dry city (dry meaning no bars or open servings of alcohol.)  If you wanted a drink you had to go to Cousin Hugo's (Maplewood) or the long gone Chatter Box (Brentwood).

Ok this is a normal bar food style place.  I had cup of their beef stew soup wish I had a bowl.  It really was first class.  For my main I ordered their cheeseburger (locally sourced from Herman Mo.)  I ordered it medium but it came out done no biggie.  The burger was $10 and came with French fries onion, pickle, and lettuce.  I thought the burger was good not great.  I wish they had sourced the burger from Arcadia Mo.  It would have been better. (joke)

Mrs K. had a cup of chicken soup and potato skins.  They looked good I did not sample either dish.  We had to drink a diet coke and ice tea.  The bill came to $36 before tip.  This is not an inexpensive bar food place.  Food was very good not awesome.

I got a haircut today.  What does this have to do with Sugarfire?  Well it is next to Earl's International where I get my 5 hairs cut every month.  I finished with the cut and was walking by Sugarfire.  OK it kind of pulled me in.  I had no idea what I wanted so looking over the menu board I saw "The Big Muddy".  Smoked sausage, smoked brisket, slaw, pickles and a nice Kaiser.  This sandwich is original to me.  I never heard of the combo before.  It was outstanding.  I really want everyone in the world to try this sandwich and reinforce my love.  And I think it will bring world peace.

Every time I go to a sushi or Japanese style restaurant I keep hoping to find dishes I have seen my friends in Japan post.  

I ordered crab Rangoon, and shrimp tempura for the table of four.  We had one of each.  Both the shrimp and crab Rangoon was good.

For my main meal I ordered Gyudon (add Egg)  slow cooked beef with caramelized onions, served with  steamed white rice.  I was not expecting the Gyudon to be mixed in with the salad.  There was nothing on the menu that I found that explained this option.  So I just ate around the lettuce and tried to eat what I wanted.  What was somewhat bad is the beef and rice was on the cold side of my preference for a served meal.  The fruit flies hovering around the table was also not to my standard.

I took a picture of my meal and a good friend from Japan made note it was nothing she has seen before.  Oh well I tried.

With the fruit flies, cold food, and an improper explanation of the food. I feel I am being generous.  Oh and the smell of dead fish was very unpleasant.  Place really smelled bad.

We take our staff out to eat once a year and this year I chose Tucano's.  I chose this place because of a Yelp Elite event I attended.  I needed something that would take care of 14 people who all have different food needs.  One Vegan, a few picky eaters and of course me.  I am a meat eater and this place seemed to be the only choice.  We all ordered the lunch special and added appetizers of calamari, nachos and fried onions.  Then we moved on to the salad bar.  Everyone loved the salad bar.  I myself had a bowl of soup as I knew what a tidal wave of food was on its way.  Beef in the form of  tenderloin, sirloin, brisket, and round.  Chicken in a sweet sauce, turkey wrapped in bacon.  Mixed vegetables were also served on the skewer.  Every piece of meat was very well seasoned and had that wonderful grilled flavor.  My favorite was the house sirloin.  It is just fantastic.  After having all sorts of special non alcoholic drinks and soda's I was finished.  The crew?  Nah.  These champs had almost every dessert on the menu.  Huge chocolate cake, fudge brownies with ice cream, creme brulee, apple crisp with ice cream and on and on.  I cannot believe how much food was consumed.  The funny part was how quite the table was getting as the meal progressed.  I guess eating that much food puts everyone in a food coma. 

On the ride back to work I was pretty sure we were not going to get much more work done for the day which is fine by me.  They all work so hard they deserve a goof off day.

The hotel staff directed us to Mr Ed's.. (in walking distance to the Bienville Hotel)

We started with the hurricane & Dixie beer (local beer recommended by our server) .. the bf really enjoyed the beer..

I had the creole platter .. creole shrimp, crawfish etoufee & jambalaya  ($20).. very delicious, lots of flavors on this plate .. really good sauces showed off the seafood and local flavors 

The bf had the 1/2 fried oysters & 1/2 fried catfish with jambalaya on the side ($22) .. good size order.. fresh seafood, great fry not greasy at all

Inside, upstairs and front side walk seating areas.. lots of locals, families and tourists enjoying the music, vibe, drinks and food at this place.. great service by Tamarra.. great recommendations. I would definitely return on my next visit to this location in the French Quarter

I've had this place bookmarked for some time now and on my most recent trip to Tucson I stopped by at lunchtime.

You place your order at the window & a table is assigned to you. They have lunch specials during the week.

I had the al pastor tacos .. nice chunks of pork, cooked perfectly, served with queso fresco & lime. The side salad was mixed greens with cucumber, tomatoes & red onion with a cilantro ranch dressing (yum!). 

Check the board for the agua frescas menu.. i had the cucumber pineapple it was delicious. They also had churros as the dessert of the day, not sure how often it changes. 

The patio seating under a shady tree in the courtyard was nice.. you didn't feel like you were in the middle of the city. 

All the plates i saw coming out of the kitchen were colorful and beautifully presented.

I am looking forward to my next visit.

Stopped in for a margarita on a hot Saturday afternoon with a girlfriend.. after a bit of shopping we were looking for a cool place to hang out.

We sat at the bar and were greeted right away, we decided on the house margaritas .. served in giant glasses with either salt or sugar rim.. 

We said yes to chips and salsa and a small basket of chips showed up with a lady asking if we wanted everything in the salsa and what spice level did we like. We went with medium hot .. she chopped and mixed ingredients and we ended up with this delicious salsa served in a molcajete 

Friendly people at the bar also drinking margaritas and chips & salsa .. is recommend this place for good Mexican food.. don't forget to have a margarita

I love when my customers let me pick a lunch spot! 

We started with the bacon popcorn because who doesn't love bacon and popcorn! It was yummy! You should get this to share!

I ordered the shrimp & grits paired with collard greens. Visually I thought the plate was to big .. but the plating was nice .. shrimp stacked nicely on top of grits and a huge pile of collard greens with pork. So many yummy flavors and that sauce was creamy goodness!

My lunch dates had the gumbo with hush puppies and the other had the drunken angel pasta dish. None of us was able to finish our plates, we all agreed this hit the spot.

The hush puppies were delicious too, I wish I had room for dessert! Service was fast & friendly. Will definitely be back! The bar area looks really cool, I'd love to come back for happy hour!

Stopped in for dimsum on a late Saturday morning and was surprised at how empty it was. The parking lot was full of weeds and the entryway looked shabby like they were going out of business 

We were greeted right away and seated in a big pink banquet room with bright yellow seat covers .. they seemed really out of place (the seat covers were new)

The steam carts headed over and we had shumai, sweet potatoes footballs, ribs, duck, pork buns.. shrimp.. all the favorites .. everything was good but not great. There wasn't a lot of variety 

This place has definitely seen better days. Service was prompt.. overall it was good

We grabbed some seats at the bar where two guys were shucking oysters in front of you .. we ordered drinks and raw oysters.. wow were they delicious.. fresh, raw, delicious.. 

So good we ended up sharing two dozen oysters and crab cakes ... the people at the bar were regulars to Mardi Gras and said it was their must visit every year!! 

Beautiful restaurant... would definitely recommend

After our swamp tour we were starving and the place I wanted to try had a huge line so we decided to eat here after having enjoyed dinner at the Bienville location .. 

This place is nicer then the other location, had the same menu & prices .. that's about it though 

We started with the crawfish hand pies .. mini empanadas with aioli drizzle on top .. these were good.. really hot (temp wise)

The oyster po-boy the bf ordered didn't look anything like the huge ones at their other location.. this was all bread and not enough filling (see pics) huge letdown and he paid $4 for fries .. there were about 25 pale looking cold crinkle fries on a plate .. the second plate of fries were hot but still pale .. not a golden fry on the plate (even combining the two plates this was not worth $4)

The crawfish etoufee was good .. I'd recommend this dish .. 

From my seat I could see fried shrimp on the carpet under the tables next to us .. it was super busy and some of the tables were tucked in corners and staff had to squeeze between chairs to deliver food and take orders .. we ate and got out of there fast

Ordered my burger medium but it was far from it. As you can see from the picture that my burger was basically raw.  I went back to get another and as a courtesy they gave me a loaded back potato.  Well the baked potato had a hair in it.  Do your self a favor and just avoid this place

Three years have gone by since my original review and the impression Mony's left on me has not faltered. Now, I have been to many taco locales in Santa Barbara and I have to say, Mony's delivers the best authentic tacos in the city of Santa Barbara. 

The quality and taste of the meats are simply unmatched. Sure there are other locations in Santa Barbara which choose to overdress their tacos, of which I too am a fan of from time to time. However, a taco true to its roots that provides you with the sustenance and memory of authenticity is one not soon to forget. 

Mony's has been and surely will continue to be my favorite Taco place in Santa Barbara.

I agree this was worth the detour. My Cuban sandwich  was fresh and tender. I see why people rave about La Segunda.
Oops, the carrot  cake  was tasty  too.

Very cool Southern vibe. The food was all fresh and steaming hot. The wings were nice and the chicken sandwich  big and delicious. The peach  cobbler was the bomb.
Janisa the server was on point and very professional.

The atmosphere is relaxed. The service (Yvonne) friendly. The steak was tender and done just right. I enjoyed the tingly sliced yuma.
Oh, and the desert was delicious  
You should try when you are in the area or make a trip for it.

The fact that this is the ONLY Viet restaurant in Port Richy automatically earns this place a high rating in my book!  Kudos to the owners for taking a chance on an area that is devoid of Asians & people who understand that not all Asian food is the same. 

The questions I overheard swirling around me made me GOL (groan out loud..is that a thing yet?...like LOL?...No?!  Why not???...anywhoo...). 

"Do you have General Tsao's chicken?  I can't find sweet & sour pork either."  "How about papaya salad?  Or sticky rice?" "Can you make hibachi?"  On & on.... P.S., folks, those are NOT Viet dishes.  

The VIETNAMESE dishes that they do serve here though are pretty decent.  Best I ever had?  Not really.  As Josh T. mentioned in his review, the Vietnamese food in Eden Center in VA is much better.  Been there many times when I used to live in Virginia.  But that's not a fair comparison.  The Viet population there is much greater there = better ingredients = more competition = better food.  So while not the best I've ever had, the food here is legit and satisfies my Viet food craving whenever I'm in the area.  Will definitely be back.

We wanted to try Jacques-Imo's, but were out of dinner spots on our culinary calendar.  On their website was the suggestion to try their sister restaurant "Crabby Jack's" for lunch.  Sure enough we had one lunch left in us on this New Orleans trip and the Yelp reviews sure looked good for Crabby Jack's.  We hopped a cab over from the French Quarter and 15 minutes later showed up at this local hole in the wall just as they opened.  It's a pretty simple order at the counter, take a number kind of place.  I got to try several items here and it was pretty good.

Shrimp Po-Boy - I dare you to find a place that puts more shrimp on their Po-Boy than Crabby Jacks.  It was impossible to keep them all on there, as they kept tumbling off.  If you order this your shrimp will runneth over.  Fried up golden brown and piping hot, I felt this Po-Boy still needed a little Louisiana Hot Sauce for some flavoring, which they have for you to add.  I also strongly recommend getting some remoulade to slather on.  Toppings were shredded lettuce, tomatoes, and pickles.  I have to say I was a little disappointed in the bread and wish it was slightly crispier.  4 stars  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/crabby-jacks-jefferson?select=jghxgt5ZNe8TibwkJ5haHA

Fluer de Bree Po-Boy - Baked Ham, Roast Beef Debris, and gravy.  Another sandwich served piping hot.  This is one soggy tasty mess.  Topped with shredded lettuce, tomato, pickles, and mayo.  No way did the bread hold up against the gravy and this sandwich fell apart instantly, so bring your knife and fork with you if you are going to attempt it.  4 stars  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/crabby-jacks-jefferson?select=SeX3S316ox5xV320Erq56Q

Jacques Imo's Famous Half Fried Chicken.  Ok your love for this chicken depends if you are an extra crispy person or an original recipe kind of person.  If you are in the extra crispy camp, this is your fried chicken.  We had to wait for about 25 minutes, since this is fried up to order.  This was fine, since we had those Po-Boys to keep us company.  I didn't find the batter that flavorful, but it was fried perfectly and had great crunch to it. The breast was incredibly juicy, there was nothing dry about it whatsoever.  That said, I'm an original recipe guy, so I've had better and was expecting more.  3.5 stars  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/crabby-jacks-jefferson?select=6QiSxsHRpKOQ9bumSqzxQA

Jambalaya - this was the best thing I ate here, with big chunks of sausage and tomatoes, I would have been happy with just a whole bowl of this.  5 stars.

Mac 'n Cheese - while not bad, it sure tasted exactly like Kraft Mac 'n Cheese.  I'm not saying it was, but I'm not sure why if you are making your own, you would want that same flavor profile.  2.5 stars  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/crabby-jacks-jefferson?select=guibPr5hUNOMYWbmU8Ie8Q

I guess my assessment is that you don't need to leave the French Quarter for Crabby Jack's.  It's more of a local place, with large portions and very fair prices, but it doesn't need to be on the Foodie Traveler's radar.  If you are in the neighborhood though, most definitely stop on in.  Everyone working there was very friendly.  I can tell this is a popular local lunch spot for many, and rightly so.

I made reservations here for 10 and they said ok no problem.  When I got there the table could only sat like 7 and then gave another table that sits 2 on the other side.  I told the host, if you guys couldn't sat 10 why didn't you tell me that over the phone, instead of making us drive here and finding this uncomfortable situation.  Do you know how odd it was to split people from out of town who didn't know what to order.  

As for food goes,  it was a mess.  The sprig roll sauce was all oily and the lettuce and all looks like it's just been run thru water once without really cleaning it.  

The ambience in there was hot and smoky.  And the bathroom was a mess.  

Save your money coming here. Go elsewhere .

I used to live in Tampa and this was one of the regular places that I would go to regularly, so on a recent visit, I went back craving those same flavors. This place was so amazing years ago. Something happened when Tara moved from the Nebraska Ave location to this one. This used to be one of the friendliest places in town and now it just seems that she's pissed off at everything and could care less about the customers. It was disappointing. I'm sure the food is still the same, but her attitude leaves me thinking it tasted better before.

We stumbled across a brand new restaurant in Lambertville, D'Floret.  Turns out is was just opened recently by celebrity Chef Dennis Foy. Its a small restaurant with an open kitchen, so its almost like going to someone's house for a home cooked meal. However the the type of meal is not the type you are going to have in most people's home. I love trout in general, and this Golden  trout, was not only delicious, but about the prettiest fish I've seen. The chef came over and fileted it for me personally. My wife had Marlin, cooked rare, just perfect, something she has never had before, and again delicious. I would suspect anything you had here would have to be perfect because the chef is practically within listening range if you were dissatisfied. The service was great also. I look forward to trying other things on the menu when we pass through town.

I like this Whole Foods a lot more than my local store. The employees here are super friendly and awesome. There are explicit no smoking signs on the patio and one of the employees actually went out to politely ask a lady to not smoke so close to the building. I feel like most of the times the employees kind of let it slide but I was really appreciative that he went out of his way to do that. 

There are some Reno touches to this store that include offerings from local businesses in Reno like the Lead Dog beer that they carried. There's also some cute signage that lets you know this is Reno's Whole Foods. 

They had some really great deals going on at the time including 2 for $6 bottles of Health-Ade kombucha and soups that were also a few bucks off. I had resist getting in on the good deal since I was on vacation. 

I think the store might be a little bit smaller than other Whole Foods that I've been to but they still had all the different sections, just on a smaller scale.

I made a point to come here on my trip to Reno. It was easy to find parking in the lot attached to the building. It's more than just a coffee bar as it offers some sandwiches, bowls, and pastries. There was a seasonal menu of drinks one of which was the maple cinnamon latte which I ordered iced and thoroughly enjoyed. It was probably not conventional lunch time but they were able to make a breakfast panini for me even at this time.

While I was waiting for my food, there was a man that was being belligerent and harassing some of the other customers that were there. I was in awe when one of the smaller baristas promptly marched over and told him that he had to leave and that his behavior was not acceptable. She was so calm and assertive and not taking any crap from people who were bothering their patrons! I'm pretty sure it's not in their job description to have to deal with that stuff and I can't help but give massive props for diffusing the situation and making everyone feel a lot more comfortable.

There is a lot of seating inside and outside on the patio which is really nice on a sunny day. There's a lot to look at inside the shop from the floor to ceiling wine rack and art from local artists on the wall. A really cool coffee joint that has a hip vibe.

I like Chuy's!  I like the fun atmosphere, the food and the servers.  The staff does a great job serving quickly (once you are seated) and they truly seem to care. 
The chips are placed on your table as soon as you are seated.  We loved the salsa and the creamy jalapeno ranch dip.  For meals, we've had quesadillas, fajitas, enchiladas, salads, and more.  My personal favorite is the Deluxe Chicken Enchilada meal... roasted, hand pulled chicken breast and cheese.  I opt for the sauce on the side and choose a few from the choices on the menu.

I almost don't want to review this, as this is my favorite location and a great find!  I always love dining here before a concert or game at Amalie arena.  It's located in/outside the Tampa History Center.   We always start with drinks and order a Cuban sandwich, 1905 salad and black beans.  YUM!  The food is consistent and the service is great.

I think the sushi at Osaka is good, although it isn't my favorite in the area.  My favorite roll was the Sexy Lady.  We went after happy hour, so didn't get any of the special discounts.  Would I come back?  Yes.

We had another fantastic lunch today. Great food. Great service. A truly wonderful and tasty meal. I had the grilled pork over angel hair and it was fantastic. I would definitely get this again. We are lucky to have Simply Pho in North Tampa.

I love sushi and can't believe I haven't reviewed their Westchase location before.  This newer location is a lot larger than their old location in Northdale, but truthfully, I miss their old location.  I recently dined here for happy hour.  The sushi rolls are definitely smaller than they used to be, but the pricing is so good, I  can't really complain.  
Our server was helpful and friendly.  She gave suggestions of her favorite items and our group of 6 were all happy.  
Happy hour pricing is not allowed for to go orders:(

We loved Babushka's!  We loved feeling like we were in a small Russian village dining among family and friends.  We started with the Borscht soup, which was surprisingly delicious.... a beef, veggie and beet soup.  Adults and kids at the table loved it.  We thought the meat Blinchikis filled with beef and mozzarella cheese were unique and tasty.  The Olivier potato salad was unlike anything we've ever tried and very good.  For our entree, we had the stuffed cabbage and loved it!  The cherry pierogis were good, too, but next time, we'd try a different kind.  
We loved that everything in the restaurant is fresh and homemade.  They even tell you that the food will be delivered to your table at different times, as it is all made fresh and brought to you when ready.  This allowed all of us to try everything.
We can't wait to go back and try new things!  If you make it out to Babushka's, enjoy your meal!  You won't be disappointed.

We went to Etch our first night in Nashville and everyone loved their meal.  We started off with a few appetizers, as recommended by our server.  We got the mussels, the octopus bruschetta and the cauliflower.  The cauliflower app was my favorite, then the octopus, followed by the mussels.  The filet entrée was cooked perfectly and was tender and delicious.  For dessert, I got the ice cream sundae and loved it.  All in all, from the food presentation to the server's knowledge and expertise, Etch stood out as a trendy and gourmet restaurant.  We loved our experience here and would dine there again.

I have dined here for lunch twice and the service has been great.  The lunch specials are well-priced and the sushi is fresh.  While I haven't had any of their more creative meals, I do look forward to trying them out.  The only thing I wasn't a huge fan of was their complimentary clear soup.  It was just ok.  I would definitely dine here again.

We dined in for lunch on a weekday... During lunch, you order from the counter and they bring your meal to you.  I ordered the Tuna bowl and the presentation looked great.  The ingredients were fresh, but it was so spicy that I would not order this again.  I truly couldn't eat it.  I was offered rice when I went up to the counter.  I would recommend that they ask how spicy the guest wants it, or if it is premade, they mention that it is spicy.  

Hubby ordered the Build your own and this one had blackened chicken, spaghetti squash and fajita style.  This was delicious.  I would definitely order this again.  

Although my meal was spicy, I still like the concept of a healthy and fresh meal.  The staff were friendly. If in the area, I would look forward to dining here again.

I have been here a few times and pizzas are definitely the star of the show!  I like the concept of creating your perfect pie and them having it cook for a short time while you wait.  You start by selecting a crust:  regular, wheat or gluten free.  Then, it's time to add on the toppings.  There is a large variety of fresh ingredients, so be creative and enjoy.  Uncle Maddio's is definitely a family friendly restaurant, so bring the whole gang!  
On a side note, I also like to see they support various local schools and other charities.

I have been to CSC three time now.  The first time, I had an individual lunch.  The second time I purchased 4 lbs for a group.  The third, 2 lbs.  Our favorite is the classic, hands down.  However, the kickin' one is fantastic, also.  We have also tried the Sassy Scotty and the Fruity Fran.  Everyone is nice here.   There are approximately 15 kinds of chicken salads and they are happy to give you a sample to try.  
Make sure you get the app, as they have a reward program.

I like Taps.  We had a great dinner (we made reservations) for 8 adults with drinks.  Nice and casual, with great staff.  We did stick with server recommendations and were pleased by food and beverages.  My favorite were the tacos.

I love Umami Sushi!  The staff is super friendly and proud of the food they serve.  The presentation is great and the sushi is fresh.  My favorite roll is probably the Umami roll, followed by the Tiger roll.  For appetizers, I love the sashimi app and the Dragon balls (no rice).  
We have never ordered any of their hot meals, but a table near us did and were raving about it.  We will definitely be back and hope to try it all.

We were so excited to find this spot as a friend recommended it.  It was great for going out with friends before seeing a show at Ruth Eckerd on Friday, April 14, 2017.  

From the décor, to the drinks, food and service, this place was top notch!  

We tried the beef tartare, the chili prawns, crab salad, the lamb shank and the Arctic Char.  We all enjoyed everything we tried.  For desserts, we shared the aerated cheesecake and the S'mores.

We decided to check out Yo! Sushi on opening day. We were seated by Alex at a booth and we was helpful to find out information on a peanut/tree nut allergy for us. Our server, Young, was attentive and friendly. He checked on us multiple times and showed us the help button that you can push if you need a server. 
Items on the conveyor belt appeared fresh and ours were tasty. We tried edamame, philly roll, California roll, tuna tataki, seaweed salad, salmon sashimi and yuzu salsa. All were tasty.  The seaweed salad was different from others that I've had before. This one seemed to have a kick of wasabi and added in edamame. 
My one complaint is that for lunch, this was a very pricey meal, as portions are small. I mentioned this and they are going to have specials, etc, but as of opening day there were none. (Instead of a roll having 8 pieces, these had 4, which allows you to sample a variety, but helps the price creep up quickly.)
Our bill included these items and we drank waters. It came to $36 before tax and tip. We enjoyed our meal and my child loved it, so I know we will be back.

I had the Pain Killer which is their take on a Pina Colada. It features rum pineapple coconut orange and nutmeg. I also tried the Scorpion Reef which contained Mezcal rum, orgeat, pineapple, and lemon. I would highly recommend both of these drinks as they offered loads of flavor but weren't too heavy. 

In the world of Covid, they have the perfect setup! They have Pods out in their parking lot that each seat 4 people and has a nice warm heater to help with the cold weather, you could bring your own throw blanket and get really snuggly if needed. The staff wear mask and there is hand sanitizer on the table and disposable glasses and silverware.

We went for Valentines Day and loved it! Kim and Jamie were very short-staffed but STILL attentive.  We are the only black people there and we did not feel any type of way - they sat us right in the front - this was a huge plus for us! 

The wines were delicious, we tried the classic flight, cheese box, and chocolate bouquet. We also loved that it was walking distance from State street so we were able to walk on the promenade after. We highly recommend Jamie Slone Wines!

Follow us on Instagram @woodley_wanderers and Youtube Woodley Wanderers for more travel tips and tricks from around the world!

After a whole day of driving, I just wanted to get a quick meal close to our hotel and rest. I had heard about this chain of personal hot pot shops and was glad to find it on Yelp. Located in Goleta just a few miles from the UCSB campus. The restaurant shares a space with a boba shop in a run down strip mall. 7:30 pm last night it was crowded and full of students. We ordered individual hot pots and a mango smoothie from the boba shop ( Do not order the Mango Smoothie its awful. But that is a separate review. ) I got their signature pork trotter was really good, but lots of work eating it. Taste wise 5 stars. However between the temperature ( hot ), spicy ness, the bones of the pork trotters and tiny table and plates it was challenging. Our server noticed and put out the flame on my hot pot sterno so the trotters in the soup could cool down. 

*** note the pork trotter is hot pot is not a dish one should order when eating with a date or unfamiliar people. Because you'll be chewing and knaughing on some pigs feet and spitting out the bones. 

Service was good. Lots of parking in the strip mall parking lot.

After a Holiday traffic nightmare on the road, we decided to just get off the 101 rest and wait out the craziness. Brophy Bros. is a Santa Barbara landmark and usually stop in when we are in the area. They open at 11 am and is constantly packed with locals and tourists. The main dinning room / bar is not large and they do have outside seating on the terrace with a bar downstairs too. Brophy Bros. is a seafood raw bar restaurant and IMO has the best clam chowder in Santa Barbara. Its chunky with tons of chopped clams. On our recent visit we ordered the following:

Seafood combo comes with ceviche, shrimp, oysters and clams
Little Neck clams on the half shell
Fried Calamari
A big bowl of the clam chowder.

The raw clams and oysters were very fresh and the hot fried calamari was excellent. The ceviche was however hard to eat spread out on the iced seafood combo plate. 

The restaurant is loud and high energy. There is parking spaces around the restaurant but they are hard to come by. So there is a large City parking lot right next to the center.

During our recent trip to NOLA we had brunch at Trinity restaurant.  During brunch at 12 noon and 2 pm the have a Drag show. Trinity is located right across the street from the French Market and a couple of blocks from Jackson Square. We ordered the following along with our bottomless mimosas: 

Asparagus soup excellent served with drops of Chili oil

Oysters on the half shell, very fresh

Brussels Sprouts salad , best dish of the brunch

Wagyu burger was ok but the beef patty was well done and over cooked. 

Shrimp linguine was so salty we told our server and manager before we took the third bit and the promptly took it of the bill. 

You need to make reservations for the drag brunch it was a full house with a large bachelorette party taking up the rear counter. The show was fun. Service was good they even give you change to tip the Drag Queens before the show starts.

Ruby Slipper Café is a very popular lunch spot in New Orleans near Harrahs Casino. Our lunch was ok but we waited a long time for the food to come out. Luckily, the best part of the lunch wait was the bacon bloody Mary's.  We ordered several of them and to give you an idea how long the wait was we were on the second one by the time the food came out. A lunch salad and sandwich menu.

Pros
Online wait list
Bacon Bloody Mary's excellent 
Our server 

Cons
Long wait to get in
Long wait to get your food
Mediocre food 
( eggs benadict, corned beef Reuben,  fried fish , biscuit and gravy )
The fried fish awful, the corned beef was stringy 

The consensus of our group was go for the bacon bloody Mary's and definitely sit inside because to odors from the street is not pleasant.

Trenasse is located in the Intercontinental Hotel New Orleans.  We made reservations a couple of days in advance for our party of 8. Arrived at 5.30 pm and seated promptly. It was just the tail end of Happy Hour so we ordered some appetizers and drinks. A couple dozen raw oysters, a dozen grilled oysters, boudin balls and a round of Hurricanes.  The oysters were smaller then ones we had earlier that day but were excellent especially the grilled ones. 

For dinner we ordered the following item some multiple orders.

Escargots decadent rich in butter garlic and herbs
Duck with romaine lettuce as taco shells
Several Fish of the Day
Scallops
Drum
Mahi Mahi 
All were outstanding especially the scallops tender and sauteed just right.
Oyster salad 
The gumbo made with a dark rue, was the best I have ever had. 

Desserts were a cheesecake and a huge creme brulee.  Service was excellent . $340 before tip. Southern food at its best.

Worst meal I've had in years. The calamari steak was so thin with thick bland crust, no dressing on the cabbage. Mussels were all mushy, broth was flavorless. Brussels sprouts a bit greasy and not quite cooked enough. Will not be returning.  Sorry I rarely give a bad review but this should never have been served.

If I could give this restaurant 100 stars I would! Da Sesto is a hidden gem on the corner of a strip mall in Pinellas Park. I first went to the restaurant after winning a $100 gift certificate. I took my hubby and we had an incredible meal with a bottle of wine and Richard as our server. Last night we took another with us for a pre Valentine's dinner and Richard was assigned to us again. He is amazing and really knows his wines and dishes! I recommend making a reservation as this is a cozy place with limited seating. The food is out of this world and reasonably priced. You must try the olive balls and I'm a huge meatball fan and they are so good! During our first meal I had the lobster ravioli which was to die for. Last night I had the lasagna with meat. You can tell the pasta is freshly made. For dessert we were treated to free canoli's for checking in on Yelp. We also received a free bruschetta and meatballs for waiting patiently for our table at a large table set up outside. Richard recommended a bottle of wine which we enjoyed with bread before going to our table.  It was a 3.5 hour experience and wonderful night out!

This is our neighborhood go to place for good, reasonably priced Italian food. Tonight we split a bottle of wine between 3 of us and it was $19 for
The bottle! I had the sampler platter and there was a ton of food! I have leftovers for lunch tomorrow .  mine had Eggplant parmigiana, cheese ravioli and pesto pasta. And I added a side of meatballs (there were 3) because I LOVE meatballs! Everything was so good! My hubby had the veal parmigiana and ate all but one small piece and our friend Dave had the chicken Marsala and ate all of it. All our meals came with a salad. The ambience was great as we were put at a table off to the side in front of a wine rack. It was a very enjoyable meal. Even our waiter was pleasant and attentive. I highly recommend Gino's for a wonderful Italian meal that isn't crazy expensive!!

I found this restaurant while searching for good places to have dinner while staying in Nashville. It was our first night here and we wanted to go out to a nice place and have dinner that provided a casual upscale service and this place was a perfect match for that. I called and tried to make reservations but the hostess informed me that they did not take reservations however they would be able to accommodate if we came in.

We were greeted immediately as soon as we walked in by the manager Shawn who sat us right next to the window. We had Joseph as our server who was very polite, courteous, and professional through our entire evening. Since it was our first time here, he went through the whole menu and gave great recommendations on apps, entrees, and cocktails. 

I started off with the red rock martini and the bf got the Sedona martini. Both drinks were absolutely delicious! Not too sweet or too strong, just perfect. For appetizers we decided to get a Cesar salad and the crab cake sliders that came with 2 sliders and a side! I chose grilled asparagus but asked for it to come out with my entree since I was already going to order that anyways hehe. The crabcakes were delicious and had a house made roulade with coleslaw. I thought the sliders were delicious and I don't even like coleslaw! It also had all real crab meat and none of that breading fillers like most crab cakes that are served in restaurants. 

After we finished our martinis we ended up getting a bottle of pinot Grigio since it was half off wine Wednesday's..SCORE! Even if you don't finish it they will pack it up for you to take home. 

For dinner I ordered the jumbo shrimp stuffed with crab and the bf got the Italian Flat bread since he wasn't too hungry after eating all the apps and salad. I thought the shrimp was soooo good! It had 5 huge shrimps stuffed with lots of crab with sautéed spinach and whipped mash potatoes. The shrimp was perfectly cooked and the crab was superb. The spinach was perfectly seasoned and was packed with lots of flavor and chunks of garlic. YUM!! I let my bf try one and he kept eating more from my plate..I thought you said you weren't hungry hmmmm? The mash potatoes were good too but I could've done without it since I was already so full from the other dishes. I tried some of the bf's FB and thought it was ok however he did seem to like it.

Although the dinner was absolutely wonderful, what I enjoyed most about the whole experience was the service we received from our server Joseph.  Joseph was very down to earth and honest, and never rushed us during our time there. He was very attentive and made sure we were always taken care of. I also saw the manager Shawn helping out the whole staff with bussing tables, seating, cleaning, and doing anything that needed to be done which I totally respected. 

The meal came out to 80$ which I thought was reasonable! This would've easily been over $100.00 if I were to have this same experience back in San Diego. I wish we had this restaurant back in SD so that I could come back and try other things on the menu. Thank you again for the awesome experience Joseph and to the whole team at The Sedona! Will definitely come back here if I'm ever in Nashville again.

Drago's absolutely lives up to the hype. The chargrilled oysters platter may be my favorite preparation of _seafood_ that I've ever had. Unbelievably good. The drum with crab is an enormous serving of extremely fresh fish charred on the bottom. Seafood pasta was super creamy with piles of crab and fresh shrimp. Gumbo tasted like minestrone soup; weird, and the only item to avoid. Overall, we loved it here. Nice restaurant interior too, not too fancy but still comfortable and classy. It got pretty busy around 7:00.

Best restaurant in the _country_. Everything about our food was great. We got the meal deal with ribs, brisket, pulled pork, chicken, beans, sweet potato fries, and coleslaw. We ate everything. This is the first time that I've enjoyed sweet potato fries ever; not only that, I loved them. 

Each table has three sauces. The St. Louis style one with molasses was just out of site good. Expect to wait over an hour to make your order. But then food comes out almost immediately. If you compare to a restaurant with a 15-20 minute wait for a table and then 20-30 minutes for food it comes out to nearly equal time.

3.5 stars. This is basically just expensive junk food. Kind of like doritos in steak form. It's good, I enjoyed it. But this isn't exactly a food destination in terms of quality or pricing. In my measure Geno's willingness to go the extra inch toward junky-ness put it a notch above Pat's, which was equally as junk-foody but with pretension to being better quality.

A top notch eatery by any standard. Spectacular barbecue, a plethora of sauces, make sure to come during off-hours. 

The ribs were mildly flavored, not too smoky, slightly sweet, very soft but still stuck to the bone. Excellent. The unusual and creatively imagined BBQ prime rib made for a good prime rib sandwich, though the natural fattiness of the ribeye held up perhaps a little too strongly against the sauce and smoke. Interesting and nicely prepared but not exactly a barbecue revelation as much as a new preparation of a standard sandwich.

Baked beans were literally the best baked beans I've ever had. I'd go back and order a large beans and some pulled pork and eat that for lunch...every day. 

Tiny great-smelling room, surprisingly fair prices, great bar down the street for post-barbecue craft beers. To answer the redundant question, "Bogart's or Pappy's?", the answer is Pappy's by a notch, but both are so amazing that this is a false choice. Eat at both often. 

St. Louis is one lucky city.

3.5 stars. This is basically just expensive junk food. Kind of like doritos in steak form. It's good, I enjoyed it. But this isn't exactly a food destination in terms of quality or pricing. In my measure Geno's willingness to go the extra inch toward junky-ness put it a notch above Pat's, which was equally as junk-foody but with pretension to being better quality.

I literally just had a bunch of Kansas City BBQ the day before, and Salt and Smoke blew it away. The ribs were good. Smoky, unctuous, but a little too fatty. The brisket was literally the best I've ever had in any form. Char, smoke, fat, sweet, ample portion. It was an inspired serving of top shelf food, executed perfectly. The pit beans were also probably the best bbq beans that I've ever had and tasted like brisket drippings. The mac and cheese was on the good side of very good. This is your spot. Highest recommendation.

This place helped me to understand the diversity of cheesesteaks a little better. It's a giant, great sandwich. There's a line out the door, and you really get a sense of Philadelphia from standing in the storefront for about a half hour.

Basically Dalessandro's provides a lean, mild steak that makes most sense with their "American" cheese, which is more of a mild white cheese that adds moisture, than any resemblance to Kraft. With lettuce, tomato, and some mayo, you pretty straight-forwardly have a good steak sandwich on a roll. 

I tried the onions wit wiz version too (which is my favorite). It was too generous with the sauce, but honestly the wiz didn't quite mesh with the flavor of the steak like it does at the other shops. 

Dalessandro's presents simple, humble steak sandwiches, without over-excess of grease, meat, seasoning, etc. I can see why so many people are in to this. It'll depend what you want - big, tasty, junk food flavors one regularly finds around town (which I love), or the sandwich that probably resembles what one would have bought 50 years ago. If it's the latter, this is your place.

This little restaurant was a wonderful surprise. First of all, it's beautifully decorated and quaint and we noticed right away that it was full of happy locals. We shared a crab and spinach crepe and crawfish crepe. Both were outa-site delicious as well as fairly priced. The chocolate dessert crepe was clearly made in advance and put in a fridge (probably so it wouldn't melt the ice cream on top), so it was a little tough when it was served. Overall I'd give Nanou my highest recommendation. Basically they do staple New Orleans food preparations in crepe form. It's a respectful and simple twist on classic cuisine and a wonderful little place to eat.

I got take out from here a few days ago . I got wonton soup, 2 egg rolls, and sesame chicken. The egg rolls were really greasy and i did not care for them. The wonton soup was just average.  And my sesame chicken tasted weird. the chicken didn't taste fresh.

After doing more research i found out this place is being sued by the city over numerous health violations and earlier this year, many people in banquet got food poisoning.

After reading all the violations about unsanitary conditions in the kitchen, It's not surprising why the food does not taste good. How this place is still in business is beyond me. shouldn't they be shut down by now?  i would caution anyone about eating here.

I have ordered from there  about half dozen times, toppings are ok, but that base? It's like eating my grandfathers WW2 boot soles

Worst Place EVER!

I went to the Worker Bee Cafe a few weeks ago and I will NOT be returning. 
The old man, I'm guessing that owner, is the rudest man I have ever countered. I ordered home fries and asked if they could add tomatoes and the waitress took my order to the kitchen. A few moments later a grouchy old man came over to my table and asked which one of us ordered the potatoes with the tomatoes. I said it was me and he asked where I saw that on the menu. I was going to say I didn't see it on the menu with the tomatoes but I thought it would be easy to add them in. He interrupted me and said "THAT ISN'T ON THE MENU" He then barked at me asking if I wanted the tomatoes cooked or placed on top. he brought me my meal and to mess with him I ate all the potatoes but left the tomatoes on my plate. 

DO NOT GO HERE.

Tavolo V is an AWESOME trendy Italian restaurant in The Loop. They have great food all around and it's an awesome space. It's a very open "raw" space. It has a pretty cool bar, too. I would love to come here and eat at the bar sometime! Anyways, onto the food.

I've been to Tavolo V twice so far and each time I got a pizza? What's wrong with me??

I think Tavolo V has helped me figure out that I really dig fancy pizza. 

I'M NOT BORING. I PROMISE. 

The first time I got the "Pazzo's" and it comes with "Olive oil, shrimp, pancetta, mozzarella and goat cheese." I am huge fan of pancetta and shrimp so I had to try it. While it was delicious, it was a little too salty for me. But yes, I did eat the whole thing.

Pizza round 2 was the "Babbo's" and it comes with "Tomato sauce, sausage, caramelized onions, fresh oregano, and mozzarella cheese," This pie was super good. While the sausage and caramelized onions were delicious, what really made this was the unlisted balsamic vinegar they put on top. This pizza was the perfect combination of flavors and I highly recommend it. 

I also tried some of their appetizers. They are a little pricey for how much you get but are still packed with flavor. The ravioli and zucchini were great but their best was the calamari. Oh myyyy laawwwwwdd. The spicy tomato sauce they put on top of these puppies has so much flavor.  I used to think tomato sauce was boring and predictable but this stuff was magic.

I hope to be back and explore some other dishes....or more pizzas.

Kitchen House coffee has been on my radar for a while now. It's very highly rated on Yelp, obvs, and I just found out it's right next to me in Tower Grove East. Sooooo of course I had to make a trip over. 

First up, the atmosphere is amazing. Kitchen House is easily in my top 2 when it comes to a coffee shop to sit down, get some work done, and relax. They have a low key patio you can hang out on in the front. Inside they have a huge bar with seating, a giant community table, and a handful of smaller tables. I'd tell you my favorite nook but I'm afraid you'll take it. The tables and bar are all clearly handmade with unique pieces of wood. Oh yeah, did I mention they have chickens out back? You can walk back there to hang with them but I warn you, it smells. They use their eggs for their breakfast sandwiches! 

Their food selection is pretty limited. They have a good selection of baked goods and a really small sandwich menu. The sandwich thing is brand new and they're still figuring it out. Most of the items are veggie only. I've tried their cold brew coffee which was pretty good and had an iced soy latte that was amazing. 

I'll be back soon for more delicious coffee and to hang with some chicken-bros.

Scarlett's Wine Bar is probably my favorite out of the Sasha's family. It has similar ambiance's and menus than the rest but definitely a step up on the culinary side of things. 

Yes, it's a wine bar but I'm a sucker for a good cocktail.  You already know they have great wine but I'll let you know their cocktails are on point...and I'm a snob when it comes to good drinks (I don't want to be this way I just am, don't hate me!). They have a couple watermelon cocktails on the menu right now that are as sip-able as they are chug-able. Seriously tasty and to top it off, one is named after Queen Bey. 

The food is bomb. Yes, they're hopping on the wood-fire pizza craze and I'm all about that life. After eating here, you'll be glad they did. I got the breakfast pizza and I felt #blessed after each savory bite. I love breakfast for dinner and I love pizza so you can imagine how much this bad boy hit the spot. 

My summer fling opted for the chicken sandwich that came with a side of mashed potato-tater tots. Normally I don't harp on my other people's food but those tots were the best I've ever had. Drake would be all over these. They are essentially fried mashed potato balls. The texture and flavor is perfect. Gettttt themmmmmmm.

I was told by Sasha's on Demun that Scarlett's takes their gift cards as well. Unfortunately this wasn't true for our visit. They even 2x checked with their manager which was nice but win for us. Oh well, guess we HAVE to go back to Sasha's.

The Tavern offers one of the best dining experiences you can find in St. Louis...especially west of 270. 

Food: Their food is phenomenal. They have an extensive menu of choices with the majority being seafood. I get something different every time I go here and I'm always happy with it. 

Service: The clearly only hire the best of the best with their wait staff. All of them are extremely friendly and helpful. They make a real effort to be personable and are very attentive. 

Special notes: 

1) YOU HAVE TO GET THEIR DESSERT! The Tavern easily has the est dessert that you can find at any restaurant in St. Louis. I'm not kidding. Their cookie comes out in a cast iron dish with ice cream and peanut butter mouse on top. You have not tasted heaven until you've tried a bite of this. 

2) They have the best bread I have had at any restaurant EVER. It also comes out in a cast iron dish and is very heavenly seasoned. It's so flavorful you will want to eat it for your entire meal. 

If you haven't gone to the Tavern and are looking for a great dining experience, than you know where your next stop is!

No, it's not IHOP. Think nicer facilities, better food and way more expensive. 

I went here, not by choice, with a large group of friends. We had 11 or 12 of us on a Saturday around 10:30 and had about a 30-45 minute wait. The staff is friendly and the place is fine, but there are so many better breakfast options in the area. I mean, they have great staff and standard food but it's pretty expensive for what you eat. My girlfriend and my meal combined was around $30? That's just coffee, pancakes, & a tip. 

It's a little overpriced but still has fine food. I'd rather just spend less if I'm getting pancakes/diner food.

The Preston is brand new to St. Louis and easily one of the top ten new places I've eaten in STL the past year. Located just inside The Chase, this tapas style bar is exactly what you'd expect from an upscale hotel. The space is freshly renovated; they did an amazing job. The massive open kitchen is a great backdrop to the upscale ambiance. Anyways, let's cut to "the chase"...see what I did there?

The food and drink is boss. 

It's New American cuisine served on small plates to share. My girlfriend and I split the Charred Octopus, Bread Plate and Scallop Chowder. They have the best damn bread plate I have ever had. Don't think of the bread plate as, "oh it's just a filling dish" because it isn't. It came with three different flavor-packed spreads, two pretzel croissants, one wheat roll and one jalepeno cheddar biscuit. All of the bread was fresh and warm but I basically could have eaten those spreads alone. As for the Charred Octopus and Scallop Chowder, get them. They're extremely decadent and filling. 

Their cocktail list is nothing short of unique. I got the Nancy's Night Out that comes Bulleit bourbon, Big 'O', grapefruit and crystallized ginger. The ginger is basically candy and who doesn't like candy with their booze? They definitely don't skimp out on presentation here. 
All of their cocktails are pretty enough to take out on a second date...or third. 

I can already tell The Preston is easily one of my favorite spots in The CWE.

Wild Flower is the perfect lunch spot in the CWE. With most things in the area being pretty high priced, it's nice to find something relatively less pricey but still have a classy atmosphere and delicious food. 

I came here with Aimee K and we got seated right away. It was mid-week and mid-day so this was pretty much expected. I'll say it outright, our service was fantastic. I didn't see the bottom of my coffee cup once. Not that I'm picky like that, but they were on top of it. 

Now to the bottom line, the food. Their menu has a fantastic balance of traditional, unique, light and heavy options. I was tempted to go with the 1/2 sandwich salad AND soup (not or) but followed my true spirit and went for the grass fed burger. I denied myself a bit and got a side salad over fries. The burger was juicy and clearly made with high-quality ingredients. The salad wasn't anything special but got the job done. 

I hear Wild Flower has a baller brunch. I'd be interested in trying it out but if you're looking for an easy lunch then this is a solid choice!

Okay, so I have to update this review. Yes, I am a fan of Sasha's and the Shaw one is my favorite location. But let's be real, you should only go for the atmosphere and drinks. The vibes are one-of-a-kind. They have an unbeatable patio and I'm equally excited to enjoy sitting inside as I'm outside. It's a great place even in the winter. +1 for the fireplace. 

However, their service is consistently below average. In fact, it's pretty bad. After my most recent visit my waiter was actually great, but the past ~5 times I've visited this year they've been below average. They're generally unattentive and not the friendliest. 

The food is alright, but a little pricey for the quality. If you're wanting wine bar vibes with great food, go to their sister restaurant Scarlett's. Everything from their pizza to sandwiches is pound for pound better. 

Even though I felt the need to downgrade Sasha's, I'm still a loyal fan. Just wanted to keep things real.

Alright, I need to do an update. 

I had dinner here on Friday and was blown away by how delicious everything was. Seriously, I must have had some sort of ordering clairvoyance because I don't know if it could have ordered any better than I did...or maybe you can't go wrong at Hiro?

We started with the Asian Greens, Lobster Rangoon, Lotus Leaf Wrapped Sticky Rice, and split the San-Pei Chicken Claypot. The Asian Greens had the perfect texture and just the right amount of flavor. The Lobster Rangoon fulfilled all my hopes and dreams. It's everything you want from fancy "crab rangoon." The Wrapped Sticky rice had a Chinese sausage in it that had an unforgettable savory flavor.  Our Chicken Claypot was very satisfying. It came out fresh, piping hot, and boiling in a highly addictive sauce. 

I'm going to go ahead and be a bigot. You need to order what I did...you won't regret it.

I don't really know why Das Bevo isn't getting more love. It's a one of a kind beautifully restored historical landmark and you can drink beer in it. I mean, what more could you want?
You probably want amazing pretzels. Which I want, too. And they have them so everyone is happy. 

I sat outside but I didn't hesitate to take a gander at the interior before I settled down. There isn't a bad spot in the whole place. I've been inside Das Bevo before it changed hands. The new owners did a great job at renovating it. It has a modern appeal but still maintains the integrity of the original architecture. I love the inside but the outside might be better. STL has great patios but our overall patio game is weak. Das Bevo adds to that with a huge and beautiful biergarten. Dare I say, the best in STL? I suppose that's a matter of opinion but it's top 5 no question. 

They have a great beer selection at amazing prices. There are steins and ubersteins which are just giant servings. Always go for the uberstein... it's more cost effective so you gotta. I've had their pretzels which I approve of but I need to come back for a proper meal. 

If you like beer and are looking for somewhere new and unique then you should visit Das Bevo.
