I've finally been to a Toast Bar. I know I'm a year or two late but that's a win in my book...it's getting so hard to keep up with those darn kids and their weird trends. This time around is everything comes on toast...ez enough. 

As for the space goes, it's your typical hipster building with eclectic furniture and little to no space inside. Most of the available seating is on the patio. I wish they had more indoor options but the toast is good enough to keep me coming back. 

They've got a ton of different toasts. Your classic avocado toast and a bunch of other amazing ones including...s'mores, mushroom, chorizo and a few others. I split the sampler which came with 2 sides. Deff the way to go if you're eating with a partner. It's around $15 and you get to try 5 different toasts and 2 sides. 

My favorite was their apple brie but I seriously LOVED them all. They were amazing. The sides were okay but nothing spectacular. They also have some great Japanese style cold brew coffee. All in all a great experience. Go here and enjoy some of the best toast you'll ever have!

Mission Taco is one of the few spots in the loop where you can sit outside and enjoy some great food. Don't get me wrong, it's totally worth sitting inside but sometimes you just need to enjoy that good ole sun! 

Something I really like about Mission Taco is that even though it's Mexican the food isn't super greasy!  I love Mexican food but sometimes I don't want to eat a bunch of grease--delicious or not. 

During my Saturday lunch visit I had the chips and salsa, grilled fish taco, fried fish taco, and the carne asada. My favorite by far are the fish tacos! They are sooo good. You can tell they use quality fish because it's super light and fluffy. They put the perfect amount of their "baja sauce" and other toppings on it. I could eat these every day! The carne asada was also very good, but I'm a huge fish fan so it got overshadowed. These fish tacos are the bees knees. 

The chips and salsa isn't anything too special but it gets the job done! It comes with a salsa verde and a red salsa. Normally I'm not a big salsa verde fan but this one was decent. There wasn't too much cilantro which is usually what deters me.  

Mission Taco has a great craft beer selection and a great cocktail list. I highly recommend checking it out!

I don't go to a ton of sports bars but The Post is one I enjoy. They have plenty of TVs if you're there to watch a a game, a lot of seating and a great menu. They have a great selection of beers and other drinks. They don't have fancy cocktails but it has everything you need to get your happy hour fix. 

What really makes a sports bar great in my eyes is the food. And The Post has some great food. They have a huge menu of traditional options (burgers, wings etc) in addition to pizza, wraps and cheesesteaks. They also have tons of specials and more than enough staff for those busy nights. 

If you haven't been to The Post and love sports bars then you need to get in here ASAP!

Antonino's is one of those places I've known about forever but never found the time to visit. They have great Instagram game and the old school credit that comes with being on The Hill. ICYMI, Anthonino's was on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives a while ago but they were popular well before that. 

Here's what you need to know before you go...they have a diverse menu, plenty of greek AND Italian options with an emphasis on Italian, the atmosphere is diverse for any occasions, and the food+drink is very reasonable priced. 

Now let's dig in. A lot of people say they have the best T-Ravs in town! I think I've had better but they are up there and classically made. I went with the pizza. Why? Because I'm basic but also love the classics. I went with cheese and pancetta topping. The pizza was great and mine was around $14. It would feed two hungry people easily. Especially if you get an app. Most of their Pizzas were priced around $20. Normally I'd think this is a bit pricey but for the size it's worth. The crust is hearty and the toppings are plenty. 

Their cocktails aren't the greatest in the area but for $7-$8 at pop it's hard to complain. Stick to the classics and you won't have any issues. 

I already want to go back to try their Greek/Italian/Fusion burger. It's between two pieces of garlic cheese bread and topped with gyro meat. How amazing does that sound? I'll be sure to report back with a photo after I do.

I'm happy to Three Kings right off of Manchester. Considering the area and options, this place is easily 4-5 stars. Anything within 5 minutes of the West County Mall is seriously a culinary desert. 

I cam here on a Saturday night during the holidays and it was PACKED. Like, 45 minute wait. I was pretty hangry by the time I got seated but that's my fault. Should have made a reservation that close to the holidays! I decided to go with one of their burgers and it was amazing. Seriously, one of the better burgers STL has an it was only like $12. 

3 Kings also has a pretty large selection of local beers on tap, plenty of bar and dining seating areas, and a trendy outdoor patio. I will for sure be back. It's a great go-to if you're ever in the area.

Holy monster burger. If you didn't know, Half & Half is "the brunch/breakfast spot" of St. Louis. It's pretty much everyone's favorite spot. 

First off, it's adorable. It's a small spot in Clayton with a homie whimsical vibe. That being said, it's always packed. There aren't a lot of seats so if you go on the weekend, you can expect a wait. 

For my most recent visit, I went with the burger (recommended by the amazing waitress) and a chai tea latte. The chai tea latte was classic and delicious. They brought it out in a giant mug with plenty of foam on top. The burger was also a great choice. It was monstrous and it came with egg and bacon. My dining partner and intern, went with the blueberry pancakes. I didn't get to try them but they looked perfect. 

I can't wait to come back and skip the burger for something more breakfast-y. I highly recommend Half & Half but beware of the wait!

Sauce On The Side upgraded with their new location. It's still the same fast-casual calzones you love but with much more room. They now have a ton more seating both inside and out. If you can sit on the patio you should. There aren't many patios downtown but this is one of the few. 

I went in for a to-go order a decided on the "Carmen." It's prosciutto, capicola, spinach, parmesan, fontina, ricotta, garlic oil, & garlic butter sauce. It is really good but I've had other ones I like more. I don't think there is a calzone I wouldn't like on the menu...

PS they also have ice cream and it's delicious. You won't regret trying it!

I know some people don't care for Salt+Smoke BBQ, but I say bring it on! 

Okay, so I didn't try their BBQ technically speaking...except 1 burnt end a kind dining partner shared with me that was amazing! But I did try their 2x bacon cheeseburger and was very pleased. It was super bacon-y and red-meaty with relatively thin patties for a 2x burger. I highly recommend it. They also have BOMB green bean salad. Craving that slim waistline? It's a great alternative to their southern alternatives that maybe be a little more...buttery. 

On top of great food, they have AMAZING bourbon drinks. I got a barrel aged Manhattan and it was super strong and made just right. I highly recommend Salt+Smoke for craft cocktails, they do it right. 

Also, don't be afraid to leave room for dessert. 5$ for some VERY chocolatey pie? Sounds like a deal to me! 

I'll be back and maybe try a plate of their traditional BBQ.

I've been to Pi in Kirkwood, I've been to Pi in The Loop, and now I can say I've been to Pi in the Central West End! Aesthetically speaking, this location might be my favorite. It's eclectic and fun plus it has a great patio with a great view of the CWE. 

If you know me at all, I'm a glutton for Pi Pizza...some might say, "he's a glutten."  I always eat too much and never regret it. I always get the deep dish. The cornmeal crust will change your life. While I was here I tried vegan pizza for the first time. Wasn't my thing but the vegan in the group loved it!  

They have a signature appetizer called Pi Squares that are little baked balls of veggies. I recommend avoiding them. They're flavorless and are just a worse version of pizza. My only other complaint is the cocktail and beer game is a little weak.  They don't really carry many local brews and their cocktails sway to the too sweet side. 

If you're wanting pizza and thinking of Pi, the answer is "DO IT!

There's a new coffee shop town and it's awesome. I found my new favorite coffee shop and it's in my neighborhood! Seriously, I can walk here. While I'm bias to places I can walk to, Fiddlehead is a destination regardless of it's prime location in Shaw. 

Fiddlehead has some strong west coast vibes. The whole place is white, minimalist, beaming with natural light and has a small selection of wooden tables all with mellow music playing. There's a patio that's perfect for this fall weather and they have a great menu from drinks to food. 

For drinks they've got all of your typical coffee shop needs plus wine and cocktails. I wish they were open in the evening because I'd seriously hang out here at night. Guess I'll have to settle for alcohol in the morning or lunch...oh darn ;)

Their food menu is limited but more than most coffee shops. Tons of different toasts (chickapee, avacado), soups, breakfast scrambles and baked goods. I had the chickapee toast which was delightful but I want to try their avacado toast. The coldbrew coffee I had was solid as well. 

If you haven't figured it out yet, I'll be back...a lot!

Hands down one of the best places St. Louis has to offer. Juniper specializes in popular souther cuisine, but does it better and tastier than you've ever had it before. Not only is it less greasy, but it's also way more flavorful. 

I came here on a double date and advise you make a reservation like we did. It's pretty popular and you should know they do use community tables. It wasn't that big of a deal having others at your table considering they're pretty big. 

There are so many amazing things. We ordered everything as if they were small plates which I highly recommend. 

+Breadbasket: So good. Seriously amazing bread. Great to share. 
+Chicken and Waffles: First time having it, and I'm spoiled for life. It's gourmet and some of the best fried chicken I've ever had. Sweet and tender. Seriously amazing. 
+Frog legs: I was feeling adventurous. They were pretty good but I wouldn't order them again. The dish was pretty soupy. 

I also tried some other things that come to mind and it was all fantastic. If I come back, I'm going straight for that Fried Chicken. Also, you may be wondering about their amazing booze selection! I highly recommend checking out some of their bottled cocktails or anything else on their menu. They make some mean craft cocktails. Overall, Juniper is an amazing experience with exquisite food.

I've been to Olive + Oak a couple times now and I'm shocked I've never written a review! I went around when they opened and then recently came back for a date night with my wife. 

O+O is pretty much always booked up with reservations. WIth that said, I think they fake it a bit. I've walked in here no problem before when they've said they're booked and at sat at a table toe at. If you're feeling bold, you can probably come as a walk-in. When we came they had the bar and communal area packed in. 

Their cocktail are amazing. Really worth the $10-$12 each price point unlike a lot of guilty businesses in STL. 

For food, we go the chili, cheese curds to share and I go the O+O burger. I thought the burger didn't come with fries so I got the curds, but it does! With that said, I would not get the cheese curds again...not my thing. The chili was amazing. I think it had venison in it. The perfect gamey flavor. As for the burger, OH MY! It's your typical diner-ish burger but with perfect ingredients. It reminds me of a burger I had at a famous spot in Chicago called Au Cheval. 

On top of all that, the service was great. O+O is worth the splurge. If you want to eat cheaper, their are plenty of items on the menu under $15. I can't wait to come back!

I dined at P.F. Chang's on a Gift Card...so I thought (we'll get to that later). I was at the mall shopping with my SO and had two $25 gift cardf or over a year now so I thought "what the hell!" So real talk, I'd probably go to P.F. Chang's over most of your other chains  (Cheesecake Factory, Chili's, uhhh Olive Garden?) but would rather just get it to go. However we were tired and thought it would be nice to just chill here for a bit. 

We were seated immediately but were ignored for a good 10 minutes before a waiter came. We got the Lettuce Wraps, Crispy Honey Chicken and the Lo Mein to share. First off, when in doubt just get the Lettuce Wraps for your meal. They're addictive and the lettuce makes it taste fresher/lighter than it actually is. Also, crispy honey chicken ain't so bad. The Lo mein literally just takes like garlic. It wasn't very good but I was hungry so I ate it. 

The waiter, who didn't handle people very well, took my gift card and didn't come back for ten minutes. He then said it didn't work. I asked him to try it again and he just replied "it won't take."After a bit of back and forth I just gave him my credit card so we could get out of there. I hate making a big deal out of things but think they should have given a better excuse to why the gift cards that never expire can't even be ready by their machines. 

If you're looking for asian food in this area, just go to Mai Lee http://www.yelp.com/biz/mai-lee-saint-louis. The food is much better and it's like a mile away.

Soooo I'm pretty torn on how to review this place. I came here expecting more Pho food but that's not what I got....and I'm okay with that. This place is basically a take-out spot and they have everything from Chinese, and Thai, to Pho. 

The Pho was deff lacking on the menu considering the name...

Anyways, the food was great and dirt cheap. It was literally what I was wanting - Cheap asian cuisine. 

The major set back was the service. It was AWFUL. I mean really really really really really bad. There were maybe 10 people eating in and it took over 2 hours for us to get and eat our food. A different patron had to tell the waitress that we were waiting to be served. Our food took forever but on top of that it took me about 2-3 tries to get our check. I was about to leave money on the table and walk out. 

I got the hot braised chicken and white rice. For $8 it's a ton of food and you could tell it was freshly made and relatively high quality. My friend got the fried rice which was amazing. They basically give you a trough of it and it's super tasty for how cheap it is. 

This place is going to be my new go-to carry out but I will never eat in again. Moral of this review...if you eat here you must call an hour ahead.

Oh my, this is easily the best BBQ dinner I have ever had. Normally I stray away from BBQ which is a sin in STL but if I'm being honest it's not my first choice. Shaved Duck has completely changed my perception of the culinary heights BBQ can reach. 

My table had a bunch of different tasting options including shaved pork, spare ribs,  pork flatbread pizza, veggie flat bread pizza, salad, creamed corn, Duck Confit, chicken wings, smothered fries, walnut bacon, sirloin, mac n' cheese, and Brussels sprouts. I could have not have been more full and happy with everything I ate. 

If I came back I'd prioritizing getting the smothered fires, duck, chicken wings, and creamed corn but it was all life changing. The smothered fries were everything you could dream of and more with cheese and delicious meat toppings. The duck confit was seriously the bets duck I've ever had and I'm generally not a duck fan. The dry rub chicken wings were to die for and the creamed corn had a unique spicy kick to them adding a great flavor to a general bland dish. 

If you're looking for amazing service and want to experience some of the best BBQ STL has to offer then you must visit Shaved Duck.

The Shack is probably my new favorite brunch spot in St. Louis. It has literally everything you need.

1) Tons of tables
2) Multiple locations
3) Amazing food

I wish they had more locations in the city but for now you'll have to venture out quite a way. However, the county tends to be a culinary wasteland so I'm glad there is somewhere to go now. 

We called ahead and only had about 15 minute wait on a Sunday at 1:00 (an hour before they close). his location is massive. It has a huge waiting area, too. They do close at two which makes sense but I reallllly like sleeping in. I secretly wish they were open for dinner so I could get breakfast any time of the day from The Shack. 

Now to the point: the food. The menu is massive. They have every breakfast item you could ever want. From boozy cereal shakes to the most expansive and exquisite list of savory breakfast items I've ever seen. I went with the chicken and waffles. The fried chicken was cooked fresh and tasted fantastic. It came with eggs, too. I also tried a myriad of other dishes at the table and everything was perfect. For the price you really can't beat Shack. I'll for sure be back.

How has Lafayette Square gone this long without having an adorable place to get ice cream? 

Seriously, Clementine's is a genius for opening here. Lafayette is easily one of the cutest neighborhoods in St. Louis and Clementine's is the perfect edition. Now I can get ice cream, walk around the park, and stroll by historic homes all while enjoying some delicious ice cream. If that's not your speed, which you're crazy if it's not, you can also enjoy it on the patio. 

They have boozy flavors but I went with the traditional ones--dark chocolate and salted caramel. It was amazing. Paired it with a waffle cone and I was SET. I wish they wrapped that little piece of paper at the bottom so it doesn't drip on you but luckily I was prepared and didn't get any on me. 

Their smallest options are a bit pricy, with a cone the smallest scoop is a little over $5. You know how when you get a small and it really looks like a medium? Well this time it's actually small. It's literally two normal size scoops so you aren't going to want to share. 

Enough of my words. You must go here, get your favorite flavor, and walk around the Lafayette area on a warm summer night.

I know Cherokee has the best Mexican in STL and I shamefully do not go enough. El Bronco is one of the highest rated on Yelp. It's cheap, casual, and authentic. Most places that carry cow tongue on the menu do it as a gimmick but here it's a staple. 

The menu has a ton of misspellings but that somehow makes it feel more legit. They bring you chips and salsa for free. Their salsa was fresh and delicious. After scrolling through photos on Yelp, I couldn't get anything but a bunch of tacos. I went with 2 Carne Asada beef, 1 pork, and 1 chicken. They were all good but of course the beef is the best. 

I also tried some of the Fajitas my wife ordered. I think if I come back I'd order fajitas purely because of the delicious meat fiesta that comes with it. 

Their Margaritas ($6) and beer ($3) are cheap which is what matters here. The Margaritas use a mix that isn't bad but at the end of the day it doesn't compete with fresh juice.

I had a great experience and look forward to coming back.

You are now entering the Twilight Zone.

The cash register looks like they bought it in the 1930's. And no, they weren't going for that vintage look. It's actually old and dated. With that said, bring cash. No electronic payment is taken whatsoever. Yes, it sucks because who has cash but you'll understand once you see the owners/employees. 

Don't worry though, cause errrrything here be cheap. We made out with 3 donuts for $1.99. Most of the donuts are around 60 cents with the specialty ones being a bit more. That's a whole lot cheaper than Strange! 

The donuts themselves were delicious. One of the cake donuts we got was overly sweet but hey, it's a donut? Next time I'll come back prepared with more cash in hand to rob this place blind of a cool dozen.

I recently picked up some sugary creations from Whisk because I needed something unique to put in a few giftbags. While I was there, I picked up a treat for myself and sampled a few of the leftovers I bought. 

First off, Whisk's bakeshop is adorable. It's feels very homey and has a really cute set up. Most bakeries don't give you the vibe that you could get a cupcake and talk with a friend there for an hour.

Bonus: The owner is awesome. Kayeln Wissinger, owner and baker, helped me herself! She was super personable and very down to earth. 

Onto the treats.

The first thing I tried was a chocolate chip pumpkin cupcake. I was in the mood for a seasonal pumpkin treat so this seemed like a logical decision. It ended up being the best decision I could have made. It made it into the car for about 5 minutes....It was everything you want in a pumpkin cupcake: moist, sweet, and delectable. I really liked that it wasn't too sweet/sugary. Plenty of cupcakes out there are way too sweet. That's what makes these so much more dangerous, you can eat multiple and be fine. 

I also got to try the chai cookie and the homemade Pop Tart. The chai cookie was good, it tasted more like a sugar cookie. I wish there was a stronger chai flavor but I imagine that is hard to get ANNNNND it's a cookie...so it's always good. 

The homemade pop tarts are adorable and delicious. They are most similar to what I think of when I hear the word pastry out of everything I tried. They look just like plump cinnamon pop tarts except a bazillion times better (obviously). They are extremely soft and melt in your mouth. The innards are filled with apple-pie like filling and the exterior crust is super soft and tasty. 

If you are in the area or want to see a super cute bakery, head over to Whisk. You will NOT regret it!

Walking around town with the boys and we worked up a sweat. What better way to cool off with a Frozen Pimms Cup? Damien was craving it and I was down. 

We decided to sit down for a bit and drink it hear. The bar staff were really nice and even gave us a free beer on our way out from an accidental pour. I know that doesn't count as service it's just smart not to waste. It felt like a clean laid back place that you could for a beer anytime. 

The Frozen Pimms Cup is delicious. Obviously it's sweet but not so sweet you can't finish it. It went with the small which was a decent size. The larger size was like 32oz and only around $8 if I remember correct. Pretty good deal if you ask me.

Yes, we can all agree that the name Uncle Bill's is a little weird. But if you're from STL, then you know this is a safe place for good ole fashion diner food 24/7. 

I made my girlfriend come here for the first time just a few days ago. After a long day of moving and travel, 10:00PM rolled around and we needed some noms. I rarely ever want fast food so I thought we should skip that and go to this late-night sanctuary. 

Yes, it's unbelievably dated but it's got a late night crowd! Plus, the decor adds to the charm. But that's not why you go here... it's for the eggs, bacon and pancakes of course. We both go the same thing except my eggs were scrambled and here meat was turkey sausage. Their hickory smoked bacon was superb. We were both happy with the taste and proportions. Each meal was about $8 plus three pancakes. Way too much food for me. Of course, I ate until it hurt. 

The service was great as well. Little pro tip, after 10 they put an auto-gratuity on your bill. Be aware!

I finally made it out to Corner Bistro. Which, if you didn't know, is one of the top 25 most highly rated restaurants on Yelp for 2015. So of course I need to try it out and see what all the love is about! 

It's a small mom and pop joint in an underrated area of town. They have a small handful of tables and probably seat about 20-30. We stopped by on a Friday night and put in a take out order that probably took about 15 minutes to fulfill for two people. 

While waiting for our order we were oogling over how delicious their homemade cake looked and the owner cut us a slice for free while we were waiting. Who does that? Seriously, we need more people like her in this world If you want to make people happy you give them free chocolate cake. I tipped on my carry out order for that gesture. 

Back to the food, for our meal we split a Margherita Pizza and their meatball sandwich. Both were fantastic. The pizza's crust was perfectly cooked and was seasoned with delicious garlic and spices. The star of our meal was the meatball sandwich. The meat and the sauce was seriously fantastic. I haven't had a meatball sandwich that tasty in quite some time. I'll for sure be back to explore more of their tasty menu.

I've finally made it! Retreat has been on my list to try for months now. I stopped in yesterday for lunch and was sooo glad I did. 

Whenever I hear pub, I immediately think dinner. Retreat is as friendly for lunch as it is for dinner and cocktails. In fact, I think I'm going to add to my arsenal of go-to lunch spots. It's reasonably priced, has a fresh and diverse menu, and they encourage you to have a drink at lunch with their lunch cocktail menu. Sounds like my kind of fam. 

I went with the grilled chicken sandwich that comes with fries. It was bomb. You could taste that the chicken was fresh off the grill and was robust with flavor. The bread was moist and the chicken garnish was delicious. I think it's really important that restaurants do something unique with their fries because if not they can be way too basic. Retreat hit it home with their seasoning and house made ketchup. 

I'll be back for lunch and hopefully check out their dinner menu. I hear they have a pretty killer brunch as well. If you're wondering, the atmosphere is casual. Come as you are!

Another International Supper Club means another 5 star restaurant! 

I literally knew nothing about Eastern European cuisine until my visit this past holidays and I was blown away by this place. This isn't a "hole in the wall" international hot spot, it's a fine dining experience with streamlined service and it's own private parking lot. 

The space itself is huge and I imagine it's a fantastic event space. It has a modern-industrial appeal with quaint decorations. They have a huge picture-perfect roaring fire place in one of their bigger rooms when I visited that I hope is there all the time. 

They have a huge wine and beer list with cheap house options for you diners on a budget. Their menu selection is large but I was told to try the Jager Schnitzel so I did! It was to die for. The dish offered a hearty portion with tons of flavor. The creamy mushroom sauce on top is addictive to say the least. 

I look forward to coming back to Grbic and showing my friends this hidden gem!

This was my first time at Heavy Riff Brewing. We have so many breweries in STL it's pretty hard to make it to all of them unless you make it a point. This visit wasn't to make a point, just a happy hour. 

Like most breweries, most of what they had on-tap leaned towards a selection of heavier brews and IPAs. Life is hard out here for a wheat beer love (and IPA h8er). 

I got their citrus wheat and tried one of their sour ales. The wheat was fine but nothing super special. Light and easy to drink which is what I expected. I know nothing about making beer but it didn't have a ton of flavor. The sour was good and not super sour which was nice. 

The staff were helpful and friendly. Heavy Riff is a great neighborhood brewery!

Olio is easily a "must visit" for foodies in St. Louis.  I came by for the first time and was blown away. 

The space is super trendy with awesome outdoor patio seating available. From start to finish, Olio has amazing service. I would put them at top 3 service experiences I've had in town. They were super professional, friendly, and helpful. On top of that, they have an amazing menu. 

It's basically intended to be small plates/shared but you can order however you want. My dining partner and I shared the baby octopus salad, hummus and bread, as well as a marinated zucchini dish. The baby octopus salad was delicious and not seafood-y at all. The hummus was fantastic as well as the fresh bread. My favorite was the marinated zucchini. The flavor was unlike anything I've had before...especially on a vegetable dish. I highly recommend it. 

For dessert we had chocolate and sea-salt carmel pie from Choquette. It was sooo good and well worth it. 

The other nice thing about Olio is they have a huge drink selection of wine, cocktails, and beer. I can't wait to come back and explore their large and unique menu.

Confused, cold and lost a hungry boy named Aaron B stumbled into India Rasoi after he couldn't get his favorite Bento Box next door because Kampai closes at 2:00. I walked here with the legendary Aimee K and was dazzled by the wonderful lunch buffet. 

I scarfed down two whole plates. I literally wasn't hungry the entire day. In fact, I kept thinking to myself "I wish I ate less" with every step I took. The rice, fried veggie item, and tikka masala were all amazing. I tried a couple other items that I don't know the name of and was seriously blown away by all the wonderful flavors. 

I'm not super knowledgeable of Indian food, but I loved what I got here and would come back in a second. The buffet was fantastic. I think it was around 11 a person? I can't remember but a fantastic deal. 5/5 would make the same mistake again.

Yay! I convinced my dinner party to go here the other weekend and was so happy they agreed. We came out on a Friday or Saturday night (can't remember) and it was crowded but we got seated after about 7-8 minutes at the bar. First up, amazing bar. They had the Boulevard "Tell-Tale Tart" beer on discount for $2 a pop. They were dropping it from their list so I made out nice on their fire sale. Their cocktails were delicious as well. 

As far as the menu goes, it's all pretty heavy. It's a mix of elevated comfort food and classic Asian fusion. For starters, we tried a couple things but the one that stood out were the brussel sprouts. They were seasoned in an asian glaze and simply delicsious.  Seriously amazing. For my meal I got the Bi Bim Bap Bowl. It was fantastic. Hearty, fresh, and flavorful. 

I can't wait for another reason to take a stroll down SoHa and eat at Copper Pig. Check it out!

I officially have a new favorite thing...and it's Korean BBQ. I seriously want to go here every chance I can get. I've gone my entire life without eating like a king and need I to makeup for lost time. 

My wife and I came here for our friend's birthday. It was just four of us and the friends are both from Korea and self-proclaimed experts on K-BBQ. This made the whole experience a lot more enjoyable since the less-cultured of the group didn't have to figure everything out for ourselves. Granted, it's a pretty low barrier to entry. Don't be afraid to visit if you've never ate at a DIY grill-at-your-table experience. It' worth every last bite. 

You don't have to do the grill-at-your-table options but it's oh so worth it. Depending on the day and time they have all you can eat options for ~$22-25. We went for the "Beef and Pork" platter that feeds "4-6" and costs around $85 (Yes, they'll split up checks for you at the register where you pay). Your meal comes with the meats and veggies you grill yourself, these appetizer-type plates that are meant to be paired with the meats, dipping sauces and a couple soups/other dishes. All of the soups and apps are fantastic but I want to spend the rest of the review talking about the meats...

They are stellar cuts with beautiful marbling. Your server will start the grill and you can use the tongs  they give you to grill everything. I recommend throwing the cuts on the grill to get started and then using the scissors to cut them up in bite size pieces and fully cook them. That way once they're cooked, you can put them on the sides of the grill so they stay warm. From there, you can pick them directly off and dip them in your sauces and straight to your mouth. You can imagine how delicious it is when you have top quality meat this fresh off the grill. 

Don't forget to order some Soju and maybe some Korean beer as well. You can throw a shot of Soju in the beer to add a kick. Soju tastes like a stronger Sake. If you can't handle vodka or Sake then try a flavored one.

If you can't tell already I'm in love with Wudon and I can't wait to come back.

Park Avenue did it again! This is their 3rd location and it's another home run. 

It is literally the PERFECT neighborhood coffee shop. The interior is practically 100% made from recycled material and the whole place runs on solar power. The bright orange and blue really lightens up the environment and makes you feel like sunshine! That's right SUNSHINE. 

This one has less space to sit down than the other locations but I totally dig the communal table. It's large and great for getting work done/co-working. 

And if the shop is full? You can always grab your coffee and head right down the street to Tower Grove Park if the weather is nice (keyword if). 

The coffee and treats are top notch as always. I can't wait to come back!

There's a very fine balancing act when it comes to Chinese food, cost, convenience and health safety. Bo Fung is so popular because it hit the nail on the head. This is probably some of the best take out Chinese I've had in STL especially considering that it's also the cheapest. 

We are talking Panda Express prices, if not cheaper, without the mystery meat. Bo Fung is deeper in South City but worth the trip. The restaurant itself is small and the customer service was fantastic. The cashier was extremely friendly. 

As for the food, we each got their "meals" which are around $5 each. It comes with rice, your choice of meat and an egg roll. It was the perfect amount of food so that you over eat but don't want to completely die after. Unfortunately, I finished my wife's and entered that territory. 

We got the hot braised chicken and sesame chicken. Both solid all around and dirt cheap. Bo Fung is my new go-to for Chinese takeout.

Now let me preface this review by saying, I LIKE Thai food.  I don't LOVE it and I don't DISLIKE it, (nor do I ever crave it)..... I just LIKE it.  
For the main reason that whenever and wherever I eat Thai food, I know what to expect as far as presentation and flavors.  Nothing really blows my mind.

That being said, Xiandu Thai is slightly an exception to the above and mostly because their service excels.  Our server never neglected us, made sure we had everything we needed, chatted with us (sometimes a bit over the top at times with the jokes) and all the dishes were perfectly timed when served.

Came here with a group of 7 and did a family-style dinner.  The space easily accommodates large groups and the decor is clean and modern.  Would also recommend this as a date spot and love that it's BYOB! 

Most of the dishes we had were overall standard and solid.  You can't go wrong starting off your meal with orders of Vietnamese Summer Rolls and Roti Canai.

Entrees:
As for their Thai Fried Rice with Chicken, I like that they topped the fried rice with a fried egg and had some sauce to go with the dish.  Wouldn't have minded if the egg was poached either, which they probably would accommodate if we asked them too.  Their Vegetable Pad Thai was average and just what you would expect as far as flavors.  We also got the Seafood Lover which I wasn't a big fan of.  The mussels were super overcooked. 

My FAVE dish of the night is their Green Curry which we got with beef.  This is a MUST if you love Thai green curry.  The spice level was on point and the coconut was evident.  And I love that they served it to us in a stoneware pot, keeping it nice and hot upon arrival to our table. 

Overall, I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for some really good Thai food.  Although slightly overpriced, being a BYOB spot will save ya dough on booze.  And having outstanding service and exceptional green curry, would make this my first choice for Thai food in this hood.

BOTTOM LINE: F* THIS PLACE GO TO OLD PEKING, better food better service.
 

                 Seriously I hope someone got fired at the end of the night!
                 It was that bad!


Me and the special decided to try this place. Got there about 7:45 on a friday night, had to wait for a table. They seat you first come first served, no list just a I was here next type of thing. So No big deal took about 15 min to get a table. takes another 10 min to get drinks (8:15) and another 10 to take our order. Then another 10 for some one to take our order again. 8-10 min our order of crab puffs comes out, they are average. Then another 10 min go by and the chicken in foil comes out, the ones at neo malaka are 10 times better, heres 2 suggestions if anybody at this places reads yelp. Thigh meat and cut the meat into smaller chunks before putting them in the foil.

Now here is where the wheels fall off:

15 min after the second appetizer comes out they come by and say your food will be up shortly.
15 min after that they bring some rice to the table and tell us it will be right up.
15 min after that they re assure us again that our food will be there shortly. at this point we realize that several groups who were seated after us have eaten and left.
I tell special lady friend at 9:05 I WANT TO LEAVE NOW!
she says give them until 9:15, a full hour fine...
I go to the bathroom and come back to the table, Finally the spinach in garlic sauce comes to the table. (9:10).
IT TAKES A NOTHER 10 MIN to get the twice cooked pork. So by the time we get our full order it is about 9:30 the rice is cold the spinach is hard to eat seriously trim the f*ing stems and the twice cooked pork needs more leeks.

AND WHEN YOU REFILL MY DIET COKE, REFILL IT WITH DIET AND NOT F*ING REGULAR!

Ok now I can under stand that you already screwed up someone's meal and you probably are not getting a tip so yo might as well not try anymore. but this was totally unacceptable.

I also believe that when doing business with some one tell them the truth, say hey we sent your order out to another table or we lost your order agin. Dont keep telling me it is coming right up and leaving me hanging.
Also dont take my politeness and patience for acceptance.

 IF THEY ARE SCREWING WITH YOU AND NOT SERVING YOU MAKE A SCENE AS FROM WHAT THE OTHER REVIEWS AND NOW MY OWN EXPIERENCE HAS TAUGHT ME IS THAT THEY WILL CONTINUE TO SCREW THINGS UP AND NOTHING WILL GET BETTER.

On another note if you have ruined someone's dinner so throughly comp them their appetizers or one soda or ANYTHING. To have the audacity to hand someone the check for full price after all that is mind boggling. I told special lady friend we should have left a $20 and a note telling them to go F* themselves(the bill was $28 and truth be told I didnt want to pay them anything, I was willing to stiff them for the full price only the second time in my life that has crossed my mind) , she said no as she might want to come back. I told her well I highly doubt they will remember us in 3 months. Now I can say there have only been 3 times in my life that I have shafted/ partially shafted a bill, always when no part of the meal I felt deserved any compensation. The only place I have had a worse experience was in Russia where they handed us tourist menus with special (inflated) tourist prices (I can read Russian) and had service ALMOST AS BAD AS THIS PLACE. 

Look I will give them the benefit of the doubt and say that they have never had a friday night this busy, as they haven't been open that long, they just got a good review in the paper, and this was the first weekend since U of A has been back in session. I may even go back IN SEVERAL MONTHS once they have sorted their shit out. I will not come here on a friday night ever again. They are clown shoes when the pressure is on. I also heard "Im sorry" told to several other tables so I dont think we were the only ones having a poor dinner. 

BOTTOM LINE: F* this place go to Old Peking better food better service.
Hey good news to the helper monkey who was worried about getting a bad review you just got one.

I really enjoyed this place until today.  I've eaten here many many times over the last 9 years, and now, I don't know if I can ever go back.  I got the General Tso's  chicken like I always do, but this time I got a little something extra.  I started to eat, then noticed something strange, and what I thought at first was a frayed chili pepper stem...Nope, a huge roach, cooked into the sauce.  I couldn't believe my eyes.  I'm so disgusted and doubtful that I will ever be back.

New Canadian! Well Edmonton's been old hat for me, since I've been working in the West Edmonton Mall as both a comedian and a zip line instructor for just under a decade. Now I know what you're thinking - T.J.! There is no better food than in the mall! How is this woodwork joint going to chalk up even one dish to being half of 1/4 as delicious as any of the entrées at the spaghetti factory!? Are you going to tell me that the West Edmonton Mall Sherlock Holmes chain restaurant could have its ass kicked and then handed to it post being kicked by this woodwork business!?

Yes. Yes I am.

Oh I get it, I ordered the fennel sausage for two and it only took one person to eat it? Yes and that person was me. I'm not sharing the fennel sausage with you. I may not even share my brussels sprouts or cold smoked shrimp with you. Sure I'll share a laugh, a crisp hi five and a shot of Canadian club whiskey chilled... But stay the fuck away from my fennel sausage plate. 

I'm not gonna tell you again this is new Canadian motherfucker you take your old maple syrup ass back to the mall if you think you can get a better meal at a fairer price. I mean you might be able to at least have a really good meal for a fair price, but why would you do that when you can come out of the woodwork feeling full, satiated, and just drunk enough to make it across the street to the bar at the Westin Hotel. I can't think of even one reason. Oh Canada! You've done it again!

Love,
Canadian at heart tee jay miller

Having lived in Chesterfield from when I was 2 to the time I went to college and then on and off afterwards, I was back in my hometown for a few weeks this past spring.  Me and a friend and his girlfriend at the time we're going to go out for brunch on a Sunday at Original Pancake House, but the wait was very long so he suggested we go to the Shack.  This sounded like a divey miles away from Chesterfield, but surprisingly it is only a few miles from my parents house.  This is apparently a new chain with a few other locations, Clayton and Frontenac I believe with a decor and menu that is contrary to the upscale nature of the locations.  In just a few months since opening, the walls were already full of writing on them which they give you markers based on request to use.  Then I got a boozie milk shake (I think Captain Crunch) and the Shack's Big Crunch which is a delicious brioche French toast encrusted with Frosted Flakes and sugar.  While I love Original Pancake House and their Apple pancakes as well as Dutch Baby, the Shack's Big Crunch is equally one of the best breakfast dishes I've had.  

I was back in town earlier this October, and told my parents about this place they never heard of.  We went for brunch on Columbus Day before I flew back to DC/Maryland.   They were also extremely impressed with the food as we all had the Shacks Big Crunch, House Smoked Salmon (with a sunny side egg on toast), and Downstream to Mainstream Omelette (with smoked salmon, avocado, and feta).  I also had a Drinkable S'more milkshake to enjoy our delicious food with.  My parents will certainly return and will recommend to their friends.  I certainly hope to come back again when I am back in town.

Fast and reasonably priced Korean food. Great lunch spot if you're in a hurry! The owner is very nice. A modern, clean vibe. Good menu options. Very happy to have this as a new option so close to work.

Having lived in Mexico and considering myself a connoisseur of authentic Mexican food, it takes a lot to get me excited about Mexican restaurants.  Since around 2006, they all started to lose their originality.  Adobo Grill, however, stands above the competition.  We arrived just a few minutes before 4pm and waited outside to get in, but it was definitely worth the wait.  The interior decor stands out, and the bar area is nicely arranged.  Regarding the food:

Chips & Salsa:  The house salsa is a roasted chipotle flavor, and was fantastic.  Chips appeared to be made in-house (more on that in a minute...)

House Margarita:  Shaken and poured table side, the house margarita was fantastic.  It was smaller than lots of other restaurants serve, but that's ok.  There's nothing less elegant than a jumbo margarita served in a glass the size of a bird bath.

Tortilla soup:  Poured table side, it was also phenomenal.  The soup has a darker, "mole sauce" type of appearance.  It was also served hot, which is a big plus.

Fresh Guacamole:  Fresh guac prepared on a cart at your table is nothing new, of course.  However, at Adobo they tend to use more salt, and that brings out the flavor.  This was probably the best fresh guacamole that I've had in a long time, although I wish the portion size was a tad larger.

Tacos de asada:  Served with a Mexican rice pilaf, the three tacos come with noticeably house-made corn tortillas, and they were outstanding.  Real Mexican street tacos are less marinated and are much more basic than these, but the tacos were very flavorful.

So why did I withhold the 5th star?  It was the chips.  Disclaimer:  There are people starving in the world today, so let's all keep this Yelp thing in the proper perspective.  This holiday season, let's all help feed a needy family, or plant a tree (sincerely).  Having said that, the chips (although very tasty) were being rationed by our server.  At a Mexican restaurant of this caliber, I should have to slap my server to get him/her to stop bringing so many baskets of chips.  However, after the fresh guac was presented to us, we waited for another five minutes for chips to go with it.  Just a small blemish on an otherwise great experience though.  

Adobo - if you're listening, please tweak that one semi-trivial (but nevertheless, very disappointing) aspect of your operation, and you'll truly be knocking it out of the park.

So I must say when we walked into the Crafthouse on a gorgeous February Day we were taken aback on how spacious this place was, and sat at one of the bars in the upper area. We were just looking to sample and then have a pint or two.  The were very under staffed I'm sure the weather had something to do with it.  A lady with a lot of tattoos was manning the bar but as she kept saying to us I am not the bartender.  We sat for a good 15 minutes before she took our order, she did give us a head nod as to say I'll be over as soon as I can but I'm extremely busy.  

She finally took our order. We went with 2 flights of beer (5 4 oz. pours) This lady needs to learn how to fill a draft beer half the glasses were not full and if I was her I would have been embarrassed to send them out to patrons. Their boards had no labels to tell you which beer was which and she definitely did not pour them in the order we asked for.  As we were sampling you could hear the expeditor shouting at the kitchen and wait staff, which could be heard through out the establishment. Now I work in the food industry So i was watching in disbelief as the short staff was running in chaos.  Managers were pitching in but they were not very helpful. Why not call in more staff?  They also had a birthday party going on in the lower area which was also backing up the kitchen. 

While we were sipping our beers we asked for an order of soft pretzels with beer cheese.  By this time a real bartender came in for her shift, She walked into a complete nightmare.  Tattoo lady was still all over the place and came back to the bar and I heard her whisper to the bartender these 2 ordered the pretzels,  40 minutes had gone by and still no pretzels. We asked 2 people if our pretzels were coming they said let me go check. Never getting a definitive answer.  Finally after the kitchen brought us out some wings for the bar to share I asked the bartender, are we getting our pretzels or what? She responded not likely, which was fine with us at this point because I was not going to order any more beer if this was the case.

The bartender said Tattoo lady never took our order, I wanted to talk to her but I refrained and figured I'd use yelp as my forum.  Later to find out Tattoo lady was a a manager. Now I really wanted to chat with her about her lack of hospitality and communication, but I refrained because I have been on the other side of angry customers.   

We asked for our bill and to our liking there was no charge. I quickly handed the bartender some cash because of her excellent service as she apologized for the nightmarish day.

I get it Flying Fish, you probably had call-outs on your 70 degree February day, but as managers you have to have plans in place for crisis.  There should have been more staff on when you knew you had a private party going on downstairs. If you are short a bartender keep the one bar closed until some one comes in. This place has a lot of potential. It's conveniently located in Brewerytown, by the Zoo.  Its in what seems to be an apartment building.  The beers are good as Flying Fish has been in the market for years.  But for being open since only November this was their first nice weekend. Guess what many more nice weekends are coming, start hiring and training. I will be sure to give this place another shot but it is going to be a while until i get the foul taste out of my mouth.

Several friends and neighbors now boycott this shop on my behalf after a bad accident I had here shortly after they opened. I really hope this issue is resolved for the safety of the neighborhood. PLEASE be careful walking inside here, especially with little children.

While going to the end of the open bar style counter trying to get to a roll of paper towels to clean up some coffee I spilled, I fell straight down six feet into an open basement stair with no railing or protection of any kind. It was just gaping  hole in the floor for the basement steps. The manager was horrified and kind to me at first, but while laying in shock on the cold basement stair, I overheard the owner telling a concerned customer "Well she shouldn't have been behind the COUNTER!"  

After my hospital visit later that day, weeks on a cane and months with a sprained knee, I saw the owner in the area and she again seemed very nice and concerned.  Note I was never angry, never asked for any damages or took any legal action.

I did gently suggest that if a business  did not want anyone falling into a hole next to an open ended counter (not behind it)  then perhaps a STAFF ONLY, BIG HOLE sign, pullman step cover, rail or simple chain to rope it off may be in order. I got more snark back about how I had invaded staff space. I suppose staff should have to dodge a gaping hole in the floor in a coffee shop that may have wet conditions? How about small children that run around loose in the family friendly neighborhood? I was told that hey 'watch out' for people about to fall into the floor hole. Yeah, that worked. 

If I almost kill myself in your floor-less coffee shop and am nice enough to not not get angry or sue your small local business, perhaps some graciousness, a $5 chain at Home Depot to rope off the hole,  and maybe a free cuppa would be in order. Even if I was doing a dance next to your register (which I was not) I fell in a HOLE in your FLOOR. I don't think I should get guff.

When reading real reviews by real people, you have to understand that you might not be getting a opinion of someone with a trained palate or culinary studies experience. I am no exception, but I do eat out more than frequently, OK a shit load. I believe you start gaining a more valid opinion based on the trial and error. I like to think of it as the culinary school of hard knocks. I also think if you have a favorite dish and order it frequently, you do know exactly how it should be prepared. 
For me, that dish is duck...I jones for it like quack...sorry i mean crack. I have a tough time passing it up when I see it on menu. The duck at Farmicia was the best I ever had, in fact only the late Copper(RIP) came close. What was special about it? Absolutely nothing except that it was a great piece of fowl, seasoned and cooked without discernible flaws. everything else I have had was also pleasing. My advice for the frequent diner, is have a meal at Farmicia and use it as a baseline for judging other meals. Good cooking is obvious to even the inexperienced palate.

I can not get over how good this place is. 
Seriously, I am looking for any excuse to come back and I've already messaged about 6 of my friends saying we need to come here.

Never have I ever had Korean BBQ until I came to Dolsot House and I am so disappointed in myself for never trying it earlier. My girlfriend and I came here because we wanted to try something different. Not having any idea what to order or expect we asked our awesome server for advice. 

Here is the break down of what we got:

10 piece wings- 2 flavors, honey sesame and Diablo. Both so incredibly delicious and flavorful. 
wings were crispy yet juicy- it seemed as though it had a breading to them that was fried perfectly.

Chicken Bulgogi Dolsot (chicken rice bowl)- we ordered the spicy chicken but you can order BBQ. Interestingly, it comes out in a clay bowl?! (no idea if its clay but its a cool looking bowl) and its super hot and it continues to cook once it comes out so be careful you don't burn the rice- burnt rice is something I love so I let it get crispy. Loaded with veggies and flavor this was amazing!!! So good in so many ways. Full of flavor, meat, and veggies. Spice level 3 but I would go higher next time, maybe a 4 or even a 5.

L.A Kalbi (beef short ribs) SOOOOOO good! Perfectly grilled, juicy, and flavorful but not dry or anything. Thin pieces and lots of them. I loved this dish.

Over all- this was a great experience and exceeded any expectations I had for this place. 
I am beyond happy that we tried DH; I cant wait to come back. 
ENJOY!! OH its BYOB too!

Coming from an Egyptian person (me, obvi) I can tell you this spot is LEGIT! So many fast food spots and food carts have falafel yet none of them actually taste like real falafels. Sorry to break to you people Philadelphia and south jersey- these spots don't have really falafels!!

Then comes another Mediterranean grill, Naf Naf Grill. Okay, I see you with the camels and pyramids being represented! It's def a bowl/create your own type of place. I ordered a hummus bowl with chicken and some of their add-ons and I also added some falafel cause I was so desperate for a little taste home. To my pleasant surprise these meal would be one my best in Philadelphia. I mean, everything was so flavorful, so filling, and so authentically delicious! The falafel tasted as they should and I can bet that they make them with (chick peas) as they should be done!

Thank you for not letting me down Naf Naf! I appreciate you and your beautiful falafels.

I didn't make it to Creme when I was previous living in Reno for work, and I'm sad I missed out before! My friend and I went on a Saturday morning before heading to Tahoe and had a great experience. I loved the atmosphere. We sat at the bar and I ordered a cappuccino. The server warned me he was not yet good at pouring the milk in and wouldn't be able to give me a nice design but I didn't care. He was funny and friendly and though this doesn't have much to do with the restaurant, we had a great discussion about music. While we sat there a couple of other people came in and I got the feeling that they were regulars. They chatted with us which I thought was really cool and added to the overall good vibe in the place.

I ordered a glass of water too and I can't remember if this is a Reno/western/whatever thing or what, but it wasn't served with any ice. To be fair, I didn't say "ice" water but I'm used to always receiving ice in my water. This didn't effect my rating or anything, I just thought I'd mention it in case it's A Thing here. Maybe someone can let me know.

Anyhow I ordered the Farmhouse savory crepes and they were AWESOME. Bacon, spinach, caramelized onion and cheddar cheese. It was the perfect light breakfast. The flavor was perfect. It was $10.95 and came with a choice of either potatoes, salad or fruit and I chose fruit. My friend got the German sweet crepes for which I will definitely return. They have lemon butter and powdered sugar. There was a fresh lemon slice on top and man, you could tell fresh lemon juice was used because it had that perfect acid tang to the sweetness and buttery flavor. I was jealous even though mine were so good. 

The dude did fine pouring the milk in my espresso for my cappuccino and my friend ordered a coffee which was served in a French press, which I love. Both our coffee drinks were good. They serve Blind Dog coffee which I thought was cool; I had enjoyed it when I was here before.

I also got an order of beignets but was not that impressed. They were a little over-cooked, too dark and crunch on the edges/outside. They still went well with my coffee and I'd be willing to get them again with a coffee to see how they turn out. 

I'll definitely be back here!

Holy crap where to start? Honestly I think we just had a really, really bad experience at this place but for the price, that is inexcusable to me. I had high hopes because the place looked awesome and there was a decent beer selection and our friends said it was amazing.

The night started off okay, the waitress was really friendly and had a great memory to be able to tell us all the specials. But come the freak on, when you have SIX dishes with 6-mile descriptions each, your waitstaff should not be rambling them off. We had to ask for the whole list 3 times (there were 7 of us and each were interested in something different). Then people were having to ask "Okay, what was the one with the crab and salmon?" I didn't know what half of the items were which was fine because I just wanted a burger, but my friends were interested in getting the specials and had to keep asking. 

Everyone got a special but me, I ordered the lamb burger. She took each persons order, asking them which salad or soup they would like and which side. She asked me too and I was surprised and said I didn't know my meal came with a soup or salad. She nodded encouragingly and I chose the French Onion.

So we get our soups and salads. Most people are satisfied with theirs. I don't eat a lot of French Onion so I wasn't sure what to think but it just seemed awfully salty and strong. I couldn't finish it. Another girl at the table enjoyed hers and one of the guys had a bout 3 bites then ate his cheese and quit because he couldn't stand it. No one had any complaints with their salads.

Next came the food. I couldn't even tell you what they all got other than someone had steak with prawns and a couple of people had salmon with dungeness crab. Everything looked absolutely amazing, but we were soon to find out otherwise.

My burger sucked. That's about all I can say. It had lettuce, feta and homemade tzaziki sauce. A LOT OF IT. All I could taste was feta, really, and some tzaziki. I had to scrape a ton of it off and even then it was still too much. Yeah, I could have complained and asked for something else or a new burger, but I was freaking starving and everyone was tearing into their food, so I made due but couldn't finish it.

The guy who hated the French Onion and ordered his steak med-rare, and it was definitely well done. Once again, he couldn't finish his food. He said flat out that it was terrible and that he was really disappointed. My friend who got the steak and prawns said that his dish was absolutely delicious and he loved it. Pretty much everyone else said their food was decent, okay or mediocre, and definitely wouldn't come back, not for the price. Then we got our bills.

HOLY. CRAP. Every salad or soup was another $7 on the bill, and the specials were all over $45 for the plate that DID NOT include a soup/salad. We. Were. Livid. When our waitress was handing out the tickets several of us exclaimed over this and she said "I'm sorry" in a really offended tone, and walked off.

Now, I was a waitress at a fancy bar in a resort. I know how to up-sell appropriately and deal with rich @$$holes who think you're worthless. I also know how to NOT piss people off. You say, "would you like to ADD a soup or salad?" Not, "which salad would you like?" as if it is included. And don't get me wrong, maybe the menu did not say that the specials came with these items. But how were we to know? They're not listed on the menu!!!! I with my burger even said skeptically that I didn't know it CAME with that option, looked at her, and she nodded and smiled. I get that she didn't directly affirm this, but it was SUPER shady and everyone at the table was SO SO SO MAD. We weren't rich @$$holes, we were a bunch of nurses. And the fact that she took that disgusting, offended tone with us really just put me over the edge. THEN she had the audacity to come out and nervously make small-talk as she took our cards back, sucking up by saying how amazing nurses were. It was the singularly most awkward experience in a restaurant of my life, because we were all so angry and staring daggers, and obviously being short and steamed with her while she chattered on about how amazing we all were and how nursing was such a noble profession. (She didn't even put it as eloquently as that.)

I couldn't complain too much about my cost because with my beer, soup and burger my bill came to around $27... The burger and fries was only $13 which normally I would not bulk at in the least, but it SUCKED. I was more mad for my friends who payed $45+ for their "specials" which didn't even include a measly salad or crappy bowl of soup. That waitress was just so sly. I mean.. Good for her for pulling one over on ALL of us, but she did NOT get a good tip. I think between the 7 of us she got maybe $25 for a nearly $400 table. I didn't tip and I left her a note to tell her exactly why. I initially I thought I'd go back and give it another try, but writing this review has made me angry again so no.

I hope this review serves as a cautionary tale for anyone who might even briefly consider patronizing this business. I was visiting the city for a friend's wedding, and up untill this point had enjoyed all the city, its graciosu residents and amazing culinary/arts scene.

The night before my flight home, I ordered a routine meal with little or no incident and about average service. However, 2 days later, I received a mysterious debit card charge in the amount of over $2k, all presumably for my jalepeno swiss burger with fries!!! While I was easily able to set in motion the process to dispute the fradulent charge with my bank, restaurant management has been evasive, incompetent and totally unable to assist me or even simply void the charge. Staff members at the restaurant gave me the number to a supposed manager, a number that continually rings a busy signal. I've called the main office and recieved no call backs, messages or any assistance whatsoever. As of writing this review, I'm still awaiting a resolution. 

I'd like to give Clover Grill the benefit of the doubt,  but this level of ineptitude has been expensive, ridiculous, and honestly frightening. Use cash if you can, or better yet, don't come at all.

This was our very first meal upon arrival in New Orleans and the French Quarter. We decided we wanted to check something off the list right away and have some Po Boys. Fried shrimp Po Boys ($9.95) to be more specific. 

We went this past Friday afternoon around 4 pm. We were seated quickly and ordered the Po Boys. The service certainly left much to be desired. The young lady who was our server couldn't have been much more disinterested in being there if she tried. She very much "mailed it in".

Lackluster service aside, the food actually quite good and the portions very generous! Even the fries were pretty damn good!

The food was very enjoyable, but service does count. Based on my experience here, I would Mahony's  3 stars. I would definitely go back and hope I had a more engaging and friendly server next time.

3 stars.

Meh.

Wildly unimpressed with Reverend Zombie's to be honest. We basically ran into this place while leaving Jackson Square. We saw an obscenely long line at Pat O Briens across the street and decided not to wait. Instead we wandered into here to look around and see what they had.

They are a bit overbearing with the no pic thing. Honestly, what I saw in there really wasn't all that impressive or interesting anyways. lol It came across as very kitschy and certainly not authentic.

$50 readings if that is your thing.

Meh.

2 stars.

Made reservations - drove across town, dropped off in front just to find out they were CLOSED.  (In response to owner below -  it says you dont close until 10:30 pm - wasted our time driving there - thanks for the apology). Have never written a bad review or posted anything bad about a restaurant.  But the way this owner doesn't take responsibly for closing early and apologizing sincerely - he calls me stupid in PMs.  Wow just wow!

Tony's will always have a very special place in my heart.  I have the world's greatest dad, and when I was a little girl, we used to go on fancy "dates" together.  Often times, we would go out to dinner at Tony's (my mom would blow dry my hair, make me wear a "party dress", and put a little bit of blush on my cheeks), and then we would go to Stars On Ice- it was a figure skating show featuring Olympic skaters.  In other words, my father made it impossible for any future man in my life to show me a great time.  

I will never forget the first time I saw fish being deboned table-side.  It was fascinating! As a little girl, I vividly remember ordering the Dover Sole and watching a server filet the fish and remove all of the bones.  It was so freaking cool to me.  I also remember the taste of the spinach tortellini, which was perfect.  

Fast forward about 15 years, and my whole family was back at Tony's.  It was just as I remembered and the food tasted just as great as it did when I was a child.  

I had the pleasure of ordering a Tony's salad and the Lobster Albanello.  Holy. Crap.  This lobster dish is one of the greatest things I've ever eaten... ever.  It was easily one full pound of perfectly cook and de-shelled lobster meat covered in the most decadent cream sauce I've ever tasted.  This dish was wonderfully simple; it didn't have any garnish or frills that distracted from the pure "good-ness" of the food.  If you even kind of like lobster, you NEED to go to Tony's to try this dish.  

One more great thing about Tony's: (drum roll please...) their prices have gone down! Yes, it is still expensive, but it will no longer cost you an arm and a leg (and another leg, your face, and your first born) to eat there.

This is my new favorite lunch place.  I'm a big fan of the "box" lunch - you get a choice of sandwich, choice of side, a deviled egg and choice of upcake - which is basically an upside down cupcake.  

I have had both the Thanksgiving and Veggie sandwiches.  They are both wonderful.  The T-sand is on this incredible bread called a "Sally Lunn roll."  This roll has the taste and texture of unsweetened cake.  If I didn't make that sound good here, it is.  

Like several reviewers noted previously, the potato salad is wonderful.  This is one of the only places in this area you will find good home-style potato salad.

The upcakes are good.  I have tried Pistachio, Toasted Almond and Chocolate with chocolate icing.  The Pistachio and Toasted Almond were a bit dry - dare I say - stale.  The Chocolate on chocolate was TO DIE FOR - moist and great chocolate flavor.  

The one area I would comment as "room for improvement" is the deviled egg.  They are bland.  They seem like they just need some zip, perhaps fresh parsley, curry powder, or something...

The box lunch concept is great.  Even if time permits only a dashboard picnic, it feels very gourmet and nutritious.  With my drink, the order has been $11 and change.  

They also have a full breakfast menu - weekdays until 10:30 and weekends until 2 PM.  I have yet to try it, but the eggs Benedict are next on my list.

This is a follow up even though it is a bit late.   We called or stopped in after each issue that was listed in the original review.  If the employees don't inform you when someone complains then it is not our problem.   You hired them and they represent you.  By the time you reached out, there was no reason for us to continue the dialogue.  We hope that at this point you have resolved the issues you were having with your employees and they keep you better informed when customers are unhappy.

The Chef's Hut is undoubtedly one of Boise's most reliable restaurants. It's a favorite among locals. I constantly see it being recommended along with raving reviews on Facebook food pages. After three years of drooling over other's pictures I decided it was my turn to witness the deliciousness of this special, local establishment.

My husband and I started our meal with a classic cup o' joe. He chowed down on the Veggie Spanish Omelet. Talk about LOADED. This beat came stuffed with green chilies, tomato, onion, bell pepper, pepper Jack cheese, salsa and sour cream, served with hash downs and toast ($10.49). I stole a couple bites and enjoyed how fresh the vegetables were. The eggs were very buttery-flavored and fluffy. The hash browns were also very buttery and cooked to crispiness perfection. 20/10 amazing freaking omelet. I pigged out with the brilliantly-named Eye Opener ($9.49). This dish had all my favorite breakfast essentials. One biscuit topped with hot, homemade sausage gravy, two eggs any style and choice of ham, bacon or sausage. You can add hash browns for an extra $3.49 but you might wanna think twice because the dish was so big itself. For real, those were some big ass biscuits. And seriously, such a generous amount of gravy smothered over them. Also generous was the 4 pieces of high-quality, juicy bacon! I don't think either of us said a word our entire meal. We were both lost in the tastiness. Man, my mouth still waters thinking about that creamy gravy and buttery eggs. NOM NOM NOM!!!

The location is rather different. The Chef's Hut is tucked away in an old business complex. It's hard to know it's there. The interior is decorated classic farmhouse kitchen style, providing a very comforting, homey ambiance. 

I'm so happy I get to add into the Chef's Hut never-ending collection of 5 star experiences. I will definitely be returning for more, I regret not getting down and dirty with a homemade cinnamon roll when I had the chance...

If I'd had known I'd be eating the best burger in Boise if I came here long ago I would have thrown up dueces to all the other burger joints way back then. I don't believe another burger will ever satisfy me the way that this burger did. 

It was Wednesday and I was super hungover from a night of drinking (I know, I know. This bitch drinks on Tuesdays? Why yes, yes I do.). All I wanted a big fat juicy burger to consume. My go-to had always been Bad Boy, or, if I really wanted to get down and dirty with a chain, Freddy's. My head was pounding and stomach rolling so I headed to the latter when I remembered reading an article about some special burgers being sold out of a tiny hut off Overland. Apparently they used Scottish Highland beef and the burgers were like no other. That sounded good. I thought, "You know what, girl? You're a bad bitch and you deserve real GOOD food." So I hopped into the freeway and waddled my hungover ass to the Ranch. 

Thankfully there was a small line of cars so I had time to pull up the menu. After scouring for what sounded the best I ordered the Amy Bitner Yum Yum (1/4 lb Highland burger, smoked gouda, mayo, jalapeños, grilled onions, and sautéed mushrooms, $11) with a side of fresh cut Idaho potato fries and a 24 oz drink. 

The service was awesome! The man who took my order was super ecstatic. The food was cooked quick. They'll ask if you want homemade ketchup (a must-try) or fry sauce. I recommend getting both in case you're not a fan of the ketchup. It's a litter sweeter than your regular Heinz. 

The burger was the best freaking thing ever. No I am not exaggerating!!! It definitely has a higher quality taste. No grease oozed out of the burger however it still tasted very moist! All the ingredients meshed together well. Each bite was mesmerizing. The saddest part was when I finished it! Almost wished I had ordered a second burger - I didn't know I could eat that fast. But I guess the burger was just that freaking good. 

Head down to The Ranch today for lunch, or for dinner, for whenever really, to treat yourself to what I do consider the best burger in Boise. And you can trust me, because I eat a hell of a lot of burgers compared to the average Joe. I think I'll head back down here today for the Barnyard. YUMMMMM!!!

I first heard about Bobo's whilst researching essential food stops in Tucson. For 40 years this little restaurant located midtown has been whipping up amazing breakfasts and lunches. Seriously, it popped up on every single Arizona food recommendation list. I totally understand why.

Bobo's signature dish is their Blueberry Banana Pancake (1 for $5.99 or 2 for $8.59) and that's what I went for. Being almost too big for its place, this gargantuan cake is a sugar-lover's dream. Juicy blueberries generously placed throughout the entire along with fresh, caramelized bananas in a sweet cream mixture, every bite is bursting with flavor. I say with 100% confidence this is the best fucking pancake I've ever had in my entire life. I wanted each bite to last longer. My heart died a little very time I noticed the pancake getting smaller and smaller. I wish I got another. I'm now on a mission to conjure this otherworldly dish in my own house but I know I will fail. I think I would fly to Tucson just for a morning to eat this one more time. That's how freaking good it is. 

Not in the mood for something sweet enough to send you to another dimension? Alright. Bobo's also has an extensive list of delicious, stuffed omelette ready for your belly. My husband ordered Bobo's Veggie ($7.29). This extraordinary dish was packed with fresh onion, tomato, bell pepper, spinach, Swiss mushrooms and sour cream. Talk about loaded! It was so good. Like SUPER good, my tummy rumbles just thinking about it. 

The service was spot on! Our waitress was super attentive and friendly. She was so nice from the start. Please leave a large tip for these awesome servers, they really put their back into what they do and deserve it!

I ate at many places turning my couple days in the Sonoran region but Bobo's tops all of them. I cannot wait to return!!!

I visited El Chinito Gordo on 09/05/2021 after coming across several articles presented by Tucson Foodie. They weren't kidding. This place is definitely worth a visit, especially if you're fiending for a tasty, cold margarita!

My husband and I arrived during happy hour on a 105°F day. We began with a house ($5.00) and a strawberry hibiscus margarita (blanco tequila, strawberries, hibiscus juice, agave purée, Tajin coated rim, $6.50), respectively. My drink was so pretty! It boasted a deep, red/pink color and had such a kick to it. Husband's house marg was much stronger, he really got the most out of dollar with the two he practically inhaled. 

I wasn't very hungry and wanted to enjoy drink so all I ordered were the Esquites (fire-grilled corn with crema, queso Cotija, chile guajillo, onions, cilantro and garlic, $8.95). This little bowl is the perfect appetizer. It's small but comes packed with so much flavor, you can taste very ingredient listed blend into a melody of flavor. I gobbled the entire bowl quick and almost asked for another one! My husband chose Enchiladas (red sauce, served with two sides, choice of chicken, cheese, ground beef or spinach, $12.95), going with the spinach option with a side of rice and calabacitas (Mexican style zucchini). So much food! And delicous combo of flavor. It didn't matter what your bite consisted of, it all blended together perfectly. The zucchini practically melted in your mouth, the rice had bits of corn mixed and with a creamy poblano sauce lightly mixed in. It was heavenly! 

I wish I had more room in my tummy but alas, I was still coming down from a food baby I got during lunch. I would have gotten at least two entrees plus an appetizer, desert and more drinks. Also, the service is soooo nice! We loved our waiter, he was really sweet and attentive. 

If you're looking for delicious, authentic Mexican food from a locally owned restaurant I would recommend El Chinito Gordo a hundred times over. It's super casual, perfect for large groups or date night! I hope I get the chance to revisit one day!

I've been venturing to Lemon Tree for some time now and I'm always impressed with how delicious they can make a vegan sandwich taste. As Boise's premier spot for artisan sandwiches, I have high expectations which they continuously exceed, more so with every visit! The sandwiches are definitely one-of-a-kind. You won't find anything else like it in BOI! 

During my most recent trip I enjoyed the wonderful Massaman Curry Banh Mi (roasted yams, spicy house made peanut butter sauce, cucumber, jalapeños, pickled carrot, daikon radish, spicy curry aioli and cilantro, $12.99). I will shamefully admit that I am one of those individuals whose taste buds turn away from most menu items that presents as  *vegan.* Not sure why, it just doesn't appeal to me! However, I wasn't in the mood for meat, and I had a gift card so I thought, "Okay, let's give it a try." 

If you're a meat lover, this may not be the 'wich for you. But I would recommend it to anyone looking for a great sandwich. First off, the bread is absolutely amazing. Each bite delivered a satisfying crunch it was like music to my ears. The yams, wow, were delicious! Soft and tender, it paired so well with the crunchy bread. The house made PB sauce provided a sweet kick, and the curry aioli plus jalapeños sent my tastebuds straight to heaven. What an awesome freaking combo. 

I'm so excited to try some of their other sandwiches. I think I have my eyes on the Toasted Fluffernutter next. If anyone's given that a try I'd love to know what you thought. Can't seem to find many reviews on it here.

Bacquet's is indisputably one of the Treasure Valley's finer restaurants. Our area falls so short on high-end eateries. The lengths Bacquet's goes to deliver exquisite cuisine in an upscale fashion is not only appreciated but respected.
