Let's get down to business: My husband and I began our luxurious evening with a bottle of 2016 Chateau Blaignan Médoc ($48.00 a bottle, 55% Cabernet Sauvignon & 45% Merlot). I've only recently jumped on the Red Blend bandwagon (YES that's a thing), so my judgement is soft for now. But I can say I did enjoy each sip and the extra bite of flavor it provided. 

For appetizers, my husband ordered the French Onion Soup ($15.00). The menu accurately describes it as the "best you have never had in your life." The soup itself came covered by a thick layer of cheese that delivered an oh-so-freaking-satisfying cheese pulls. The taste was fantastic! A lot of flavor but not too onion-y. By far, best version of this soup I have ever had in my life. My adventurous self ordered the Escargot de ma Grand-Mere ($15.00), a Bacquet family recipe. Who knew snails could be so delectable! These were every bit as good as Escargot I've eaten in France and Germany. Truly authentic and a treat you can find this here in Boise. 

Moving along, we were getting full so agreed to share the Jambalaya (large black tiger prawns, andouille sausage, chicken, fresh vegetables sautéed in a deep, rich sauce with a piece of creole spices. Served with a blend of basmati and wild rice, $34.50). This dish fell a little short of my liking. I really haven't eaten much Creole food so I don't feel qualified to criticize it, but this just wasn't for me. There wasn't a lot of flavor, a couple drops of hot sauce could have amplified it. I personally would not order this dish again, however I wouldn't NOT recommend it because to the more experienced tongue this might be it! 

Their menu is full of other delicious European dishes. Also, someone remind me to go easy with the appetizers because I really wanted to try some dessert but was way to stuffed. Our total before tipping came too $115.00. If you know fine dining, then you agree is a hell of a deal for a high-end experience. Not to mention the white-glove service is on point! Neither of us had to refill our own glasses of wine. Wonderful servers with fantastic training. 

Thank you Bacquet's for bringing fine-dining to the Treasure Valley! I will repeat that you have my full appreciation and respect for the outstanding food, service and atmosphere. Can't wait to be back!

I enjoyed my short lunch experience at Eight Thirty Common on 07/15/2021! Located right smack in the middle of downtown Meridian, it's fairly easy to find a parking spot despite the heavy traffic. It wasn't very busy for a Thursday afternoon so we were seated quickly, choosing to sit indoors to escape this God-awful heat. 

They have an awesome menu. Seriously, every single thing listed sounded tasty. I ordered the Crispy Chicken Sandwich (24-hour buttermilk brined & fried, Boar's Head baby Swiss, sweet spicy slaw, tomato, mayo, baby swiss, Bigwood Bread challah bun, $14.75) and requested it Nashville Hot (+$1.00).  It was tasty! The chicken was fresh and the bread is grilled adding a very satisfying extra crunch. Sadly, it was anything but spicy. Like, zero. Save your $1.00 or request they make it extra hot because obviously their meaning of Nashville hot is poorly defined. The fries were fantastic. They are sprinkled with large salt crystals. Also the fry sauce was a huge plus! I'm sure it's house made, it didn't taste like the cheap stuff found at Walmart. 

All in all, I liked my lunch. It was honestly delicious, even without it being all I'd hoped for. I would definitely recommend stopping in. I'll be back to try more menu items and for that 5 star experience!

DUDE this place has it all! One bite of their signature Charburger will have you dreaming of the next visit. I've had plenty of delicious burgers from chains but the Habit outshines most! I probably visit at least once a month so allow me to highlight my favorite menu pieces: 

Right off the bat I can tell you my all-time favorite is the Santa Barbara Char. This masterpiece includes two hot, fresh, chargrilled beef patties with cheese and avocado on grilled sourdough. Talk about a world wonder. Whenever I think of the yummiest burgers I've had, this one lands near to top of my list. That's saying a lot considering I've eaten more burgers than you (I'm totally willing to bet on that.). 

Another item I can't leave with raving about is the new(ish, by now) Chicken Caprese on Garlic Ciabatta. This seasonal sandwich features a fat, juicy piece of chargrilled chicken breast on toasted garlic ciabatta with tomatoes and lettuce, topped with melted mozzarella cheese and basil pesto aïoli. This sandwich is a burst of flavor, a neat twist to bring a little Italian to this burger joint. If it's still offered, you best get yourself one before it's gone. 

Lastly, it would be downright disrespectful to leave out the OG. If you didn't have a Charburger at least once have you ever really been to the Habit. This signature can come with one or two juicy chargrilled patties, but I only recommend the latter if you're feeling up for a challenge or sharing the meal. I got one today and ended up having to save half it was so darn big. It will make a fantastic lunch tomorrow! 

Before I leap off my soapbox, I would like to name a few honorable mentions, all sides. French fries, onion rings, sweet potato fries and tempura green beans are all fabulous choices, can't go wrong with any of them. I mean, the salad is good too, but if you're going to get a burger for crying out loud give yourself a break just get the damn fries.

This review may be a little over the top for a chain, but it's well deserved. Hit up the Habit if you're looking for a quality burger. Just like me, you just might make a habit out of it.

Due to my extensive travel history, I have built a very strong and picky tongue for authenticity. That being said, I can tell you Casablanca is the real damn deal. I'm about to tell you why. 

The entire menu at Casablanca is filled with what you'd find at a typical restaurant in Havana. I recognized many dishes that I've dined on and they were all delicious, so it was hard for me to make a decision. During my first visit I bellied up to the world-famous Sandwich Cubano (roasted pork, ham, pickles, Swiss cheese and mustard on a Cuban style bread). Man, I tell you, it was SPOT ON. Reminded me of my trip years ago when I had my first one. The meat was roasted to perfection, delivered a dynamite of flavor and was too damn good to stop eating! If you try one thing here, this is it!

On another occasion I was served the Ropa Vieja (shredded beef in Cuban Creole sauce with onions and peppers. Served with white rice, black beans and sweet ripe plantains (maduros)). This also happens to be Cuba's national dish! Again, each bite took me back to Havana. Sweet, delicate and tender beef paired with fresh cooked rice and beans. The taste was outstanding. Boise lacks so many authentic cuisine but Casablanca reminds me that true food is there if you seek it. 

On another note, I absolutely loved our waiter both times. He was very kindhearted and humorous, took time to inform us of what each dish consisted of, which was super helpful for my very Americanized husband (nothing wrong with that - he just doesn't have the palate for authentic food like I do!). 

In a heartbeat, I recommend this to anyone who is tired of over-sweetened, sodium packed eateries that boast but fail to deliver genuine cuisine. Also, if you've never had Cuban food you are missing out on so much!!! And it's here, in little Boise so HEAD OVER AND SUPPORT THIS LOCAL BUSINESS that I love so dearly!

Very unassuming bar with a sufficient menu for a nice dinner. Plenty of creative menu options which makes it easy to please the entire table. Full bar made for a good night out with the family. 

We started with fried green tomatoes which were served with pimento cheese. The tomatoes were well executed but I personally didn't enjoy them with the pimento cheese as much as the rest of the table. #BringMeSomeRanch. We also enjoyed the duck wing appetizer which were quite flavorful. 

My fried fish and tots was very good and was a very large serving. Also pictured is my daughter's veal special which she liked a lot. Large portions all around. They're doing something right as patrons were lined up outside as we were leaving.

We wanted to go to Campo's for a cheesesteak but it was raining and we didn't want to wait in line nor try to find a picnic table after waiting in line so we decided to walk into Mac's for a nice seat. 

We got lucky in getting the last booth available for a late lunch on a Friday with no wait. I ordered their steak sandwich and it was ok but nothing to write home about. The steak was a little thicker cut than a typical cheesesteak but it had decent flavor. Hand cut fries and friendly service made for a good experience.

This wasn't my choice but they were able to accommodate 10 of us at one table so that's a positive. 

We ordered the Tomahawk ribeye for 2 and the $95 dollar price tag left us feeling like we would have been better off with 2 16 oz. ribeyes for about the same price. These chains need to find their strengths and stick to them. It's a cute concept overall but in the end, people just want their money's worth. 

It was ok but left I unimpressed if I'm being honest. Waitstaff was friendly but kitchen was slow and we were here on a Thursday. Maybe the A team is for weekends only? This "steakhouse" fills the gap between Outback (which we all know has gone downhill) and your higher end establishments. It's a little better atmosphere than Longhorn but I've had a lot of good meals at Longhorn my last few visits. I wouldn't drive out of my way but if I did find myself back in here, I'd probably just grab a burger.

Went in the winter time on a Friday night. Called in our order so our food would be ready when we walked in and wouldn't have to wait in line because we heard it gets busy. Our order was sitting on the counter waiting to be picked up. We didn't need to confirm our order with anyone. In any other city this would have been a place where takeout orders get stolen by other people. 

I had a kid's meal: southern chicken tender with fries. I didn't get any type of spice because I didn't want to deal with all of that going on in my mouth. My friend got mild and my other friend got medium. They both like spicy food but the friend who got medium was dying from the heat and the friend who got mild was glad she got mild. Our food was kind of cold probably because it had been out waiting on the cold counter.

It was basic. If I had to come back I'd try their mild. I'd still call in my order because i don't think it's worth waiting in line for. 
They should think about improving their takeout/online/call in order system so that food waiting to be picked up is kept warm and not able to be taken by just anyone and turn the heaters on inside because it was cold dining in during the winter.

I went for drunchies around 2:30am on a Friday night and we were seated right away. It's open 24 hour so everyone at that hour were from the bars.

I had the grits with cheese, eggs over medium, and bacon. Bacon was crispy, eggs were seasoned, and grits were cheesy. It was a lot of food and it's way better than diner chains. 

I'd come back for breakfast food if I was in the neighborhood.

The cantina has one of my favorite patio bars and outside seating areas! It's so pretty and decorated and gives a great vibe. I came in early evening with a friend and had a couple apps and drinks. They have an awesome ceviche selection and it's all delicious! The drink menu is creative as well, there were a few that caught my eye.

We started with the guacamole and chips, and followed that up with octopus ceviche. It was so good and such a generous portion we could not even finish it. For drinks we had the passion fruit Margarita which my friend really enjoyed. We tried the hibiscus margarita as well, but it was way too sweet and sugary for me. I also had the cucumber margarita. It was so good and refreshing and had a delicious cumin salt rim. I was talking to the bartender thinking about trying a different drink, something spicy, but told him how much I liked the cucumber one, so he muddled fresh jalepenos into the cucumber margarita for me and it was amazing!! 

Can't wait til the next time I'm back, I hope it's a nice day so we can sit outside again!

Ok so I lived here for just under 20 years now.  Naturally Pats and Ginos were first, and naturally being a discriminating Yelper they were found ok, but surely there was more to this cheesesteak thing...soon Tony Lukes is discovered and why go anywhere else?  Jims was good, better then the tourist traps but hey Tonyyyyy...

On the way to Jersey what do we see?  Talk of the town - good but still no Tonyyyy...well we move to Cheltenham and find Steves.  Different then Tony - both are great, but hey we live in Cheltenham now not close to Oregon Ave, ya know?

Bout a year or so ago I come upon Chinks and hey 3 just wonderful steak places...So a few weeks ago a friend who is a computer tech calls and says pick a place and meet me I am going to Trenton from Delaware county.  There is that Delessandro's I have heard of for years now.

Just magnificent - the least greasy steak ever, nice counter service (puttin on airs in our old age) and Beer!  Not just beer, but good local beer too - yeah if light beer byproduct colored carbonated water is what ya want they got that too...

I am sure that as I continue to travel the city of brotherly love I will find more outstanding cheesesteaks, but this place is magnificent, and if you don't like cheesesteaks because of the grease this is your go to!

Unfortunately, I haven't even walked through the door, which would not usually warrant a review, but in this case, the last time we tried to go there, well, keep reading.

We arrived shortly before closing time. I will admit that we cut it a bit close, but we were looking at eating a few rolls and leaving; this was not an all you can eat trip. The Open light was on when we arrived, but we realized that we parked in the wrong spot so my boyfriend jumped out to have a smoke while my mom and I re-parked the car, this time moving it right in front of the building. Open light, still on. Boyfriend was right in front of the sign waiting for us. 

As we got out of the car, we watched one of the workers turn the light to closed and... this is the part that caused me to want to write a bad review...

do a little happy dance that he managed to close the restaurant before we walked through the door. 

If they closed late, I would get it. But it was only 8:30ish. I get closing time, I really do. I also get wanting to go home at the end of the day. It's the little dance that got me. It was the "HA HA, we see you but we are closing anyway" feeling I got as I watched that server jump around, knowing we would have to find somewhere else to go.

And we did. I don't think we will be making an attempt with this restaurant again. It's way easier to drive a couple of miles (even though Rickshaw is walking distance) to the place that is open later and has always behaved as though our business is important to them.

All the hype surrounding this restaurant initially sparked my interest. And when Tommy Up sent around that email begging people to write some positive Yelp reviews about the place because it was getting brutally slammed by the reviewing public, I felt like I had to put in my two cents, and actually experience the place for myself.

I wish I hadn't wasted my time.

All the reviewers that commented on this place's horrendous service and disturbing atmosphere where right! In the middle of the day on Saturday, when the place wasn't too packed, our orders took about 30 minutes to arrive. And you're talking cheesburgers, not leg of lamb or a filet mignon. The food was ok. Nothing spectacular. Local 44 on 44th and Spruce would put this place to shame on any day. And the place itself? Ummm... I guess some people may find it appealing, just like some people find it appealing to intentionally wear dirty, ripped clothig that is three sizes too small, put one inch holes in their ears and dye their hair all colors of the rainbow. However, this is not my cup of tea, and neither is this place.

In any case, it is no wonder why Tommy Up is having to send desperate emails begging the non-existent fans of this place to give it some positive reviews. The place is overhyped, overpriced for what you get, and simply isn't good news.

Not to be confused with Tired Hands Brewery (right around the corner) the Fermentaria has a great selection of beers for all levels of beer lovers to enjoy along with a pretty diverse list of snacks and larger portioned food options. Most beers can be served in either a 4oz, 8oz or 10oz (?) pours and 4oz can be ordered two at a time. 

We tried a bunch of appetizers which were good to share but also good for lunch: 

Hummus: served with grilled flatbread, pickled veggies and tabbouleh--hummus was creamy and you could tell it was homage, but not the best hummus I've had in my life. Okay but nothing to write home about. 

Pretzel Balls: served with beer queso and grainy mustard-- the balls were warm and we found ourselves breaking them apart into little pieces to soak up every ounce of the mustard and queso that we could. 

Hush Puppies: made with poblano, cheddar and sweet corn and served with a spicy roasted tomato mustard to dip-- we actually ordered two orders of these babies and probably could've eaten a third between the four of us. They were so good! I'm not necessarily sure what makes a hush puppy a hush puppy, but these bad boys were a sure upgrade from the hard balls I've had in my life from Arthur Treatures. They were warm and easy to pull apart the batter was mixed with corn, and the sauce just made the already tasty base just that much better. 12/10 would go again and just get 4 ordered of these things for myself. 
Fish Tacos: beer battered with citrus slaw and chipotle mayo--the beer batter was a cool take on the classic, but they could've used a little chopping up prior to serving. One large piece was kind of cumbersome. 
Tacos Al Pastor: served with grilled pork, pineapple, chilis onion, salsa verde and topped with cilantro--the flavor profile of the pork was out of this world, but the heat caught up to you when you moved onto your second taco. We had to take a break and drink some water in between, even though they were so good that we didn't want to wait. 

The dining space featured wall art and exposed brewery equipment and had me saying "YAS" before we even sat down to eat. If you're ever on the main line this place is worth a visit for both beer and food!

My friends and I finally got a reservation for Lazer Wolf, and 8:45pm on a Wednesday. Not super crowded, a little later yes, but we'll worth the wait. 

HOT TAKE: Lazer Wolf is better than Zahav, THERE I SAID IT (I've now been to both over the last two or so months, so I can actively say IMO that Lazer Wolf is the better of the two esteemed Philly restaurants). Lazer Wolf is a little more casual of a decor, whereas Zahav I feel like had an unofficial dress code even though nothing was said. 

Okay now let's get to the good stuff :) 

The menu was pretty self exclamatory, actually pretty simple--only one page front and back, which is nice because honestly reading a ton of options is cool, but sometimes exhausting and makes it harder to make a good decision. When we presented with the option to do the chef's tasting for $65 per person, we were instantly sold for 1. Not have to read the menu and decide on a couple of things and 2. To really be able to try the best of the best. 

The Salatim(s?) come out in a round tray with with about 10 or so Israeli salads to be eaten with pita. All we excellent and refills were strongly encouraged, but totally save room if you're doing the chef's tasting menu. 

All of the meats were cooked to perfection, and there was more than enough for 4 people to thoroughly enjoy themselves and still take some home for later. 

Also, the French Fries with the Tahani ketchup were the random star of the bunch. It's so funny when something so simple is executed so well. 

We really really enjoyed ourselves tonight. The staff was excellent and made sure to explain each and every dish, and were overall just pleasant.
Great selection. We eat there about once per month and have a five year old who always finds things he likes. It is cheaper to go to the lunch buffet. Can't beat the price.

I am continually pleased with Mellow Mushroom and surprised that a chain has such good pizza.  This is partly due to the fact that each Mellow Mushroom has some pizzas that are unique to that location.  Also, I have been to other Mellow Mushroom locations that were not as good.  So this isn't a cookie-cutter chain where all the food comes pre-prepared. 

I love that they offer interesting pizzas with lots of veggies.  I have had the Kosmic Karma and the White Rabbit and they were both delicious.  The crust on the pizza is really great.  The salads are delicious too--mind you, the regular is enough for two to split.  The beer selection is also great, a lot of locals and microbrews.  It is a great place for kids and loud enough to keep an infant asleep or mask any fussing.

This is a pretty brand new place, with brand new staff so I understand there should be some wiggle room with the review.

With that being said, I would say this place is overpriced and has an extremely shallow menu. It has a really nice exterior and an appealing sign, plus I loved the drum-stool style adjustable bar stools, but other than that i got kind of a bad taste from the service and pricing. 

That and the 2 guys working behind the bar just seemed like some "Bro's being Bro's" the whole time instead of really helping the customers. This place might end up OK over time, but there are just too many other great places around Midtown to recommend The Row as a good bar to go to. Probably won't go back.

I have not been this satisfied with a pizza place in a really long time. Upon driving into the parking lot for Cafe SiTALY, it became immediately clear that this is a local hole-in-the-wall pizza joint. It was in a strip mall on a road I guarantee tourists without Yelp are gonna find. On the inside it gives off all the smells and sights of great Italian food. After a glance at the menu I discerned that it was much more authentic Italian food than most Italian or pizza places in the US serve. Some of the items were definitely Sicilian-style. 

We ordered some garlic knots without knowing that each table also receives a basket of fresh-baked bread. Both were good. The homemade marinara sauce that came with the garlic knots was out of this world. The pizza itself was even better...we had the grandmom's pizza, which was a margherita-style pie. It was awesome. The sauce made from fresh plum tomatoes, the real mozzarella cheese, the fresh basil, the crust...it was delicious. One of the best pizzas I have ever had. Simple, fresh, and delicious. It put most pizza places in Indiana to complete shame. 

Also I would love to give a shoutout to our waitress...wish I had caught her name. She was so great! She actually wanted my mom to try the "chocolate bomb," a large chocolate dessert, so badly that she explained to us how to try and transport it in our cooler and even gave us extra ice for the cooler. My parents said the chocolate bomb was out of this world. 

All around I would definitely be a regular if I lived in Wilmington. Delicious food and great service at a tiny authentic Italian hole in the wall! I want to try the pasta so bad!

Kevin and Shawn have done a brilliant job of marrying the rich history of Nevada with the needs of the 21st century cocktail business. Their concept is unique to Reno and well done. The cocktails are either classic or made to order unique, Brilliant!

This place has such high reviews and we were so very disappointed. The food was cold and mediocre at best. The pancakes were ok but the nachos, biscuit and omelet were old cold and not great tasting. The hostess doesn't wear a mask and she  greats all the guests and yells out tables. She also walks from table to table filling coffee and was in our faces with no protection.

OUTSTANDING!

Now that I've gotten that little outburst out of the way, let's actually talk about this place. This restaurant came HIGHLY, almost stalker-ly recommended by a co-worker. Like, every other day he'd ask if my husband and I had been to 317 Burger yet. Well, when he gets back to work tomorrow, I'll be able to tell him an enthusiastic 'yes'!

We went as a part of our anniversary weekend celebrations and might make it an annual tradition. It's a little place hidden right in the heart of Broad Ripple, so my one and only gripe would be about the parking. They do have a parking area across from Brugge Brasserie, but that was only advertised inside so it didn't really help much while we were looking for parking.

Let's move on to the good stuff. It's a family-friendly restaurant with a full bar which is awesome. If you're really not feeling the kids that might be around, there is bar seating as well. We opted for the dining room since little ones don't bother us at all. There were many families out enjoying dinner and the 8 or so kids that were around us were really well behaved likely because of the delicious food. The service was great. We surveyed the other servers as they worked and they were all just as polite and attentive as ours was.

Food: AMAZING. We started off with country fried bacon with country gravy (WHAT?! Who does that??!!) it was soooo good. Along with the bacon app, we got the deliciously gooey fried mac and cheese balls that came with a marinara (?) dipping sauce. YUM. For my entree, I ordered the Strawberry Hill after reading all of the great reviews about it. I fell right in with all of the other ravers because that burger was the TRUTH! Sweet, mildly spicy, tangy, and the burger itself, which I ordered medium, was cooked perfectly. We also upgraded our fries to poutine which was an excellent choice because that gravy -- I could drink it with a straw.

Drinks: They had a $7 mule menu (base of vodka, lime and ginger beer) which we were super stoked about. I ordered the Lady Beauregarde (sp) which was a mule add blueberry liqeur and fresh blueberries. They also have beer flights for $6 and the three that we chose were tasty as well, especially the Ace Pineapple.

This place quickly became tied for my favorite burger joint. Now we just need to round up everyone we love and show them how much we care by introducing them to 317 Burger!

Sup bro!

After we get out of our banking jobs, you wanna unbutton the first two buttons on our striped shirts, slam on some backwards baseball hats and pretend we're still in college?  

Yeah?  Alright!  I know the best place dude.  They have waitresses that are totally hot and music that is banging.  It's the best, dude.

AFFORDABLE WHARF

Typically when you eat at a restaurant that's on the water the prices can get crazy. Luckily this location isn't one of those places. It was a little tricky to find because it's down a walkway. We opened up our Yelp map in order to start walking in the correct location. My wife was ready to throw in the towel because the map was a little confusing but with my persistence we found ourselves standing right in front of this place. 

This location is small with plenty of outdoor tables. We placed our order at the front counter. The staff then delivers your food to your table. I just want to warn you that the girl said our food would come out quickly but that wasn't the case. I was only concerned because we had a boat to catch across the harbor. I really can't knock the food taking a while because that is what you get with fresh homemade food. 

They also have a great local beer price. We were able to get draft beers for $5 which again is a great price on the water. Now you will have to turn your neck North down the walkway from the outdoor picnic table in order to see the water but it's totally worth it. 

My wife ordered a fish taco and it was really good. She shared a bite with me and I was impressed with the freshness and moistness of the fish. I was getting a little jealous and secretly wished I had ordered one for myself. 

My little one ordered the kids meal and it was huge. The large battered chicken pieces were incredibly tasty. I'm not sure if they hand batter them here but after one bite I would surprised if they didn't. It was probably one of the best pieces of chicken I've ever had on a kids meal plate. The order also came with French fries which had the best seasoning on them. This place gets food. 

Now you must be wondering..."What did Anthony order to eat?" Nothing! I wasn't totally hungry and I had this feeling that I would also be eating what the girls left. So I literally acted like a seagull hovering around their food getting scraps. I wanted to start shouting, "Mine! Mine! Mine!" That's how seagulls sound according to Disney/Pixar and I love it. The best part was that I was able to taste a little of everything. 

We did have to get a bag to pack up the food because we were very close to missing our boat. So we finished our beers and started to head across the harbor to find out boat. The Yelp map didn't work because the address for the boat is their office which happens to be next to this restaurant. So we totally had to Amazing Race it and as irony would have it my little one spotted a boat in the harbor that was used to pick up a clue by the teams in the final episode last season. We totally had to stop for a selfie. We then continued on our journey eating chips, fries and chicken from a paper bag.  

Eating here was truly an amazing adventure and we would totally do it again. If you're looking for affordable fresh food and beer then this is the place. It's a hidden gem surrounded by over priced restaurants with direct water views. I would chose this restaurant any day over those others located here.

Xtreme Tacos serves up the best tacos in Tampa!  And yes...its better than Loli's!  I'm just happy that Tampa finally has a legit authentic taco place.

I judge tacos based on the following criteria:
- Meat (quality and flavor)
- Tortilla
- Sauces

We tried the chicken tacos Tijuana style, tostada with chicken barbacoa, street corn (traditional style), and street corn (xtreme style).  Everything was super tasty and fresh.  The meat was nicely seasoned and the tortillas were homemade.  The homemade sauces were good.  I like the spicy red sauce the best.

All of the staff were very friendly and helpful. 

The restaurant has a ton of indoor seating and some limited outdoor seating. 

Definitely check it out!

7th + Grove is a great addition to the Tampa food and lounge scene.  The space is beautifully decorated and divided into two sections:  a restaurant on one side and a bar/lounge on the other side.  

The restaurant serves up hip, modern, inspired, southern cuisine.  The menu (designed by Executive Chef James) offers something for every palate and dietary restriction.  Each dish is named after a song, which is cool.  Note:  they also have a separate brunch menu and lounge/late night menu.

The food is really, really good.  We tried Get Your Roll On (Spring Roll filled with Collard greens) and Awaken My Love (Chicken Lollies) for the appetizers and Can We Talk (Blackened Turkey breast entree) and Let's Stay Together (Fried Chicken entree) for the main course.  

The service in the restaurant and lounge could both be better.  The server, Dee, was very good and stood out, but generally speaking the staff lacked knowledge of the menus.  While there were a lot of people working, they didn't seem to have clear direction.  It's a new business and hopefully the issues will be worked out over time. 

In terms of the lounge, they seem to have special events all the time so be sure to check out their Facebook page.

All in all, I really like 7th + Grove.  

It's absolutely worth the venture to Ybor no matter where you live.

Definitely check it out!

Best damn grouper I've tasted.  

Big Ray's is located in the middle of virtually nowhere but what it lacks in location, it makes up for it in the quality and taste of the food.  It's truly a Tampa gem.

We tried the Grouper and shrimp blackened.  Both were amazing!

They offer beret and wine.  Seating is mostly outdoor but covered and there are a few indoor seats.  

Definitely check it out!

Paesano ($8): Beef Brisket, Horseradish Mayo, Roasted Tomatoes, Pepperincino, Sharp Provolone & Fried Egg 

If it's your first time at Paesano, I'd recommend getting the Paesano!! It's probably the BEST freakin' sandwich I've had in my life! Never had a fried egg oozing with yolk in my sandwich either! The combination of a soft runny egg and brisket and the kick of the pepperincino and horseradish mayo is to die for! I travel a lot and have had a lot of really good sandwiches (Ike's Place in SF, The Sentinel in SF, Earl of Sandwich in Vegas, etc.) and I have to say this one was simply amazing and DELICIOUS!!! :D

The store was a bit hidden and hard to find while walking on 9th Street. It is super small inside and there are only few stools at the front area. I would recommend eating your sandwich in here and having lots of napkins and wet wipes at hand. It can get kinda messy. Their store hours are a bit short, so come early to beat the foodie crowd! (Sunday - Thursday 11am - 3pm, Friday & Saturday 11am - 5pm)

THIS IS A MUST TRY FOODIE STOP IF YOU'RE EVER IN PHILLY!!!! :D

The highlights of the meal were the mussels and the octopus. Each was in a unique savory sauce. The octopus texture was perfect and had an excellent charred flavor. The mussels red savory sauce had my father trying to eat it by the spoonful. Portions were very large. My only dissapointmen was my tuna steak which was overlooked and dry. My rabble loved everything that they had. I would definitely go back. 
We showed up with a party of 8 on a Saturday night, and were seated immediately. Service was pretty average.

La Fourno is a lot better looking inside than I assumed it would be based on the grimy outside... but the food was not. My clam and mussel pasta with white sauce was over salted in a way that makes me suspect that the clams were canned. My friend also had a dry pasta dish. However the dessert was extraordinary so I've bumped the star rating up to a 2. The service was fast, and personable but a little unorganized with only one person knowing the details of the living social deal that I used.

This is one of those magical vegan places that doesn't taste like a vegan place. At the suggestion of a regular though not on the menu, the bartender made me an artful and delicious bee sting that came in a honeycomb patterned glass, with one big round ice cube, garnished with crystalized ginger. Everything was very tasty, my personal highlights were the Peppernotta, outlandishly creamy potato croquettes, and the spiced cauliflower. 

Decor is seductive and interesting with an artistic projection on one fabric wall. It would be the perfect place to impress a vegetarian or vegan

Service was top notch, fast and patient with my group of 6 women who spent more time with chatting than looking at the menu.

The worst Ramen we have ever had. We have had some bad ramen, so that is saying a lot. 

First of all, we tried to order a rice bowl and they were "out of rice" and said it would be a 30 min + wait. We didn't want to wait at a place with literally hundreds of options (meaning Armature Works), so we went with Ramen. 

We had the Shio and Shoyu Ramen which sounded very similar on the menu. My ramen was so overly fishy that I could only eat a few bites. On top of that, the pork belly was like a slab of hard rubber. It was inedible. My Husband said that his wasn't as fishy, but the ramen noodles were low quality and were undercooked (also an issue in my bowl). We both decided to scrap our $30 worth of ramen after a few bites and go get empanadas at a nearby stand. 

I love Ichicoro Ane and their ramen which is why we even tried Ichicoro Imoto. Don't let the Ichicoro name drag you in, this location is not equal to the others. We will never eat anything from Imoto again.

We loved absolutely every aspect of our lunch here at Tasty Pho. 

-Great service - check
-Clean and comfortable environment - check 
-Great food -check
-Decently priced - check 

We are by no means Pho experts. As a matter of fact, this was only our third time having it. However, this was the best tasting Pho we have tried by a landslide. I ordered the Tasty Pho (minus the tripe and tendon) and my Husband ordered the Rare Beef Noodle. We both ordered the regular size and it was a good thing that we did because we were stuffed afterwards. 

I want to make a quick note about the service. It was amazing. We actually had three separate waiters check on us in the beginning to see if we were ready to order. I asked the young gentleman that ended up being our server for recommendations. He asked questions about what I like and made a great suggestion that I was already considering. When he learned I liked spicy food, he brought out extra jalapenos for me. He also kept checking back with us. Great service! 

The broth itself had a great flavor, but the chili oil that they make in house and serve along side it is amazing. We loved it so much that they brought out a second set of it. They also serve lime, sage, jalapenos and bean sprouts on the side. You can add Sriracha or Hoisin to taste. I prefer mine spicier with Sriracha, Jalapenos and the Chili oil. So, so good. I didn't love the meatballs in my Pho. I have a hard time with the rubbery texture of the Vietnamese style meatballs. However, the rest of the meat was very good. I thought there was an appropriate amount of meat and noodles. My Husband wished he had a little more meat. The flavors were spot on. 

I also ordered a Blueberry Boba tea smoothie which was delicious. I typically order Taro, but changed it up hoping my Husband would drink half. He didn't, but I was really happy with the flavor. 

At the end of our meal, I had tears in my eyes (if you are a spice fiend like me, you know this is a good sign) and we were both full and very, very happy. Our total was only $20. We will definitely be returning soon.

I really wanted to love this place...I am a huge beer fan and I always cheer when I hear a new brewery is open. 

However.....
1) Only 6 beers on tap with no description and a bartender that can't tell you a thing about them. From what she said they are mostly IPA's (which we are not really fans of) with a coffee tasting porter and "something that is more amber and less hoppy". I ordered this last beer and it was an IPA. 
2) This place is completely unfinished looking. No decor. Most the walls are cement. I felt like we broke into a warehouse for a pop-up bar. I'm not a snob though, decor can be forgiven. The next points...not so much. 
3) HOT. They are trying to do the "Ale and the Witch" thing and allow dogs. However, they are lacking the courtyard to do so. Instead they leave the garage door (yup, garage door on the front of the building) open. If there is air on, you can't feel it. 
4) Cash Only. It is a bit ridiculous to accept cash only in this day and age. It is even worse to tell customers AFTER you hand them their beer. It is UNFORGIVEABLE to make derogatory comments in front of a customer about how "people can just deal with it, the atm's aren't that far" (the owner said this to the bartender when she told him that she didn't tell us before we ordered...right in front of me). Did I mention it was storming outside? Also, the atm they referred us to (Regions right next to Cycle Brewing) only has an atm inside the locked doors. My poor Husband had to venture a bit to find a Bank of America in the pouring rain. It's okay though...according to the owner it isn't a problem. 

We quickly tried and dismissed our mediocre hoppy beers. We then headed our favorite local bar for some good craft beer. I don't wish failure on a new brewery; but I will predict it with this one.

Wow. 

Kao Thai Kitchen is not your typical Thai restaurant. Kao is more of an upscale Thai restaurant. The atmosphere is romantic, clean and extremely nice. They are in the former Da Sesto location. However, they definitely changed it and made it their own. 

When you receive the menu, it looks like your typical thai food. Prices are slightly higher than a lot of similar restaurants. However, when the food arrives you forget about all of that. We ordered an appetizer and two entrees. 

-Fried dumplings - 5/5 - Wow. These are unlike any fried dumplings that I have ever had. Make sure you view my pictures. These little fried pockets of deliciousness were perfect with the savory soy dipping sauce. It will be hard not to order these again. Definitely worth the $8.
 
-Rama (with beef) - 5/5 - This was my entree. I wasn't sure what I wanted when I walked in, but this peanut butter dish jumped out at me from the menu. I ordered it medium (which is semi spicy). This is the best peanut butter sauce I have ever had. I will come back again and again just for this sauce. A-M-A-Z-I-N-G. It comes with broccoli and baby corn and a meat of your choice. I tried beef this time. I may have dreams about this dish. 

-Pork Ribs Panang Curry - 5/5 - My Husband's dish. He loved it! I had a bite of the ribs and they were really flavorful and well cooked. He did mention that the meat was slightly fatty, but he doesn't mind that. The vegetables were a little al dente for his tastes, but he liked the ribs and curry enough to still give it 5 stars. 

-Coconut ice cream - 5/5 - They surprised us with a special treat of coconut ice cream with jellies and beans. The beans...meh. They are mostly for texture. You can't really taste beans. I would prefer it without. The jellies were really good and gave your palate a break from the coconut ice cream. The coconut ice cream was SO good. It definitely has a nice coconut flavor. It is creamy and smooth. The perfect dessert after a spicy thai dinner. 

We will definitely be back to Kao. I am hoping that they do really well. We had a discussion after dinner and decided that this was a different type of Thai food. It doesn't compare to other Thai restaurants in the way that a burger fast food place does not compare to a gourmet burger spot. We will add this in to our rotation for sure. Until then, I will dream of that peanut butter sauce.

I have to admit that I had a hard time looking beyond fu-wah when I got hungry for a hoagie, but I wandered in here and innocently asked who I assume to be the owner what I should get. The result was an absolutely amazing chicken cheese steak with spinach. A tad too much mayo for my liking but my god was it good. Fu-wah is still next door but I think I may stick with Lee for a bit and work my way through their menu.

For the pros...

First off, BEAUTIFUL area. They maintain the grounds nicely. Everywhere you walk to has something beautiful. The pools were nice (but super noisy). The grounds themselves and rooms were very clean.

Now for the cons....

Don't stay on a bottom floor. All night long I had to listen to kids running in the room above us. Sounded like elephants had moved in. Speaking of kids, they're everywhere. I would think a resort would be a nice place to relax and have a romantic getaway. There were so many screaming kids I felt at some times like it was a public pool. Definitely spa looking, but nothing spa-like in relaxation.

Be sure to check your card you were billed to few days after checking out. We had people in 4 different rooms, 3 of us were charged for things that weren't our charges! I had the people who stayed in the room the night AFTER me $130 dinner charged to my account! Other people had food they didn't even eat charged to theirs. Odds are in favor the same will happen to you considering 75% of our party had it happen to them.  They also said they refunded it, and I am having to call AMEX and file a dispute because no refund was ever sent in according to them.

They also charged one of our guests for the wine they said was free when we checked in. Obviously need to train the front desk people a little more because they're not doing too hot on being efficient.

Bottom line...

Ok experience. Just a few things to consider when spending the $$$ to stay here to see if the headaches are going to be worth it.

Aside from the hostess taking off her mask to say something to me and the amount of foot traffic on the patio (where we sat) during COVID times, our dinner at Arario was fantastic. Service was so friendly, food was delicious, and I love the selection of Korean fusion items on the menu. 

We had the kimchi fries, which were soooo delicious. Great amount of bulgogi and everything tied together so perfectly. Was a wonderful, comforting dish. I had the full squid salad, which was really yummy as well. But honestly the highlight of the meal was my husband's bulgogi pasta. I had total food envy! I had one bite and immediately wished I'd ordered that instead. It was so incredibly well flavored and comforting. 

Note that we tried to make a reservation on OpenTable and it said only 4:30pm and 5:15pm were available. I gave them a call and they were able to get us in at 6pm (for two). 

Parking is tricky, but they actually offer comped parking at the parking lot of the restaurant across the street. Just ask 'em!

What a great dining experience we shared together!!  Firebirds delivered excellence from the beginning to the end. 

It was surprisingly crowded on Thursday evening perhaps due to many graduations in the area drawing people to gather together for a meal. With it the noise level was pretty high when we first got there.  It died down about half way through our meal. 

Our dinner started a little slow. There was a little dead time between when the drinks were brought out and complimentary breads came out.  My sense of hunger probably got hightened this feeling, but by the time salad was served, things picked up. In spite of our large party of 22, our servers were very attentive, pleasant and accommodating.  That's what makes an eatery into a restaurant IMHO...

Food was totally excellent!!  Very fresh salad with cilantro vinegarette was excellent, and julienned jicama added great texture and freshness.  My prime rib was cooked to perfection with very good flavor.  My wife liked her wood-fired grilled salmon very much.  I was told cilantro chicken was very good, too.  Then, it came the time for dessert.  I was already pretty full from salad and about a half of my prime rib, I could only have a little taste of 1700-calorie chocolate cake with a cup of excellent vanilla ice cream--Big Daddy Chocolate Cake!! I believe all of us took it home at least partially.  

It was an excellent wedding rehearsal dinner.  I was very grateful to the groom's parents.

It's a very nice dairy farm open to the public with some extra attractions for the visitors.  In the early spring, young calves are kept in the separate area under dome-shaped igloo-looking crates.  You can visit them in a nearby barn other times of the year.  It's fun to see them especially during feeding time.

There's a small farm animal zoo very popular with kids including large pig cage housing Franklin when we visited.  I think it depends on who's turn to be sleeping there--I have seen Orville and Wilbur in the past.  I have never seen them being active (awake) during our past visits.  Bunnies are in their cages.  A large aviary houses a pair of peacocks.  He may startle you with his very loud cries that can be heard throughout the property during entire time of your visit.  There's a corral with goats and donkey.  It seemed number of animals decreased compared to our past visits--perhaps due to the COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns.

There's a small gift shop with a rack of t-shirts, some produce, local honey and such.  It also offers large selections of seasonal flowers (potted or cut) and vegetable seedlings & plants in the spring and summer outside.  In the fall around Halloween time, there will be a huge pumpkin patch for you to pick your favorite or two.... 

The last but not least, it's a local favorite ice cream spot--a part of an operating dairy farm.  Ice cream here is so fresh, smooth and sweet. 

It's a really fun place to visit and enjoy walking around this dairy farm and enjoy some great ice cream.

We opted for a delivery from this Philadelphia local chain favorite instead of braving the weather to go out on an unseasonably cold and wet evening.  We we're not disappointed.  

There's no delivery charge, and they'll text you with a delivery photo at the door...we didn't even notice anyone approaching the front porch.  We just saw a vehicle speeding away after receiving a text message. 

As for our food--Crab fries were somewhat soggy/wilted by the time they got delivered as some might well-expect it. They still tasted very good especially with the special white cheese sauce.  Roast beef sandwich was on point--very tasty and substantial--half was big enough for me to fill my appetite.  Crab bruschetta was good with fresh ingredients, and the balsamic vinaigrette glaze added a great flavor. 

Overall very good dining--delivery experience. Yes!!

Lee's Deli has some delicious fries and what I imagine is excellent hangover food, but it's also the main supplier of the ever-elusive Philadelphia cupcake man's carrot cake cupcake. Rumor has it, if you're on the trolley at the right day and hour, a mystical figure will walk through the car, selling these flawless treats to the SEPTA-weary. If you're not able to encounter this Ariel of cakery, though, go to Lee's and grab one...or four. They only charge a buck fifty and these are hands down the best cupcakes available in Philadelphia, far superior to all the bobo-targeted cupcake stores and trucks saturating the city. For some down-home decadence, get a sweet potato pie as well. It's like being at a family reunion with a whole picnic table of homemade desserts, and you can have it all!

Wow, I went to school in Philly for four years and never once set foot in this place. I think I had this notion that it was an older crowd, and what college undergraduate wants to get mixed up with that? I was mostly mistaken. There is definitely a mixed crowd here, with the upstairs pounding out popular dance songs for the more energetic crowd and the downstairs keeping it more mellow for those just looking to relax and have some good conversation. I could see myself enjoying both equally. 

Drink prices were reasonable, and the drinks themselves were generously poured (though not quite so much as at Woody's). Bathrooms were clean, and the whole place just seemed so..legit. Like there were nothing sleazy about the place at all, which is an amazing find these days. 

Consider me a fan!

This was the worst experience I have had at a restaurant in a long while. From top to bottom this was a disaster. To start off with the owner was rude and as we sat down he made it clear he is not a waiter and he doesn't pass out menus nor does he take orders. Then he went on to say no separate checks. Any other place and I would have walked out right there but this place had a great decor and reputation so I stayed to try the food. Then the food, the guacamole was nothing but smashed avocado and you get two tablespoons for $7 then I ordered what was supposed to be some special dish with a funny name that turned out to be nothing but fajitas and bad fajitas at that. I would have had a better experience at Juan's than this place. Not to mention our waiter ignored our calls from the table many times and slammed our drinks down in disgust for having to ruin his night by coming here to eat and be with friends. A group of my friends left after ordering one drink, I should have left with them. I will never come here again.

I don't often venture out to JP much but this was a special trip. Unbelievably for $20 I had all the sashimi and sushi I could eat served handmade and fresh when you order. The sushi is nice size pieces and very filling. The miso soup gets you started and you then could eat to your hearts content. If your looking for octopus you are out of luck but everything else is here. A great deal that is hard to beat.

WARNING!!!!! THIS PLACE IS $$$ LOOK AT REVIEW DATES BEFORE MAKING A DECISION BASED ON YELP REVIEWS.!!!!

So based upon Yelp reviews one of my best friends and I went to an early birthday dinner and I decided to go to Jamila because we both like Mediterranean food and when I saw the rating and reviews I said this was a great new place for me to try. The first warning was that it was a Saturday night on a holiday weekend and there was hardly anyone in the place. I was shocked and disappointed by this place. The food was massively overpriced and lackluster. We ordered the appetizer of mussels and I thought at $10 that it would be a big bowl enough for two like most places that are supposed to be on this level. It was a little dish that I could have devoured in less that five minutes. The entrees were nothing more that a lamb stew that was not worth the $23 price tag by any means. It was my birthday meal and it was mentioned to the owner and no customary free dessert like you would get at most restaurants at this level. I can see this joint not being around that long.

Blaze pizza has opened from California bringing the Subway concept to New Orleans. You walk in pick what crust you want and then proceed to choose what toppings you want from an abundant selection of meat and vegetable toppings. Its almost the Kramer concept from Seinfeld where you build your own pie. Once you've created your 12" masterpiece it bakes for 7 minutes and boom you have a pizza. At $7.95 you can't beat the price and they are big enough for two people. The drinks are great too as they have a blood orange lemonade that is excellent. I highly recommend this place especially if your on a budget. Only drawback is that because the ingredients are so fresh your pizza will be a little wet as 7 minutes is not enough time to burn off the condensation so the pizza is a little sloppy depending on how many ingredients you put on it.

Where do I begin with this place. We ordered almost the whole menu for a table of 6 people and it was just $20 a head with tip. 

Cucumber appetizer: excellent
Rice Dishes: excellent
Ribs: unbelievable 
General's Chicken: unbelievable 

Everything had a different spice and it was so nice, with great service to boot. This is Chinese food in name only, it should have its own category. Excellent choice and the more people you bring the better because the dishes are family style.

John Besh has done it again. Willa Jean is a welcomed addition to the Girod and Barrone street shopping area with a great atmosphere. Stopped in with a few friends to try a few dishes and it was excellent. The menu is not expensive, its great for breakfast and lunch but few options for dinner. Mostly the menu is filled with great sandwiches featuring the star of the show here which is the breads. I ordered the swordfish sandwich and it was excellent. The fish was cooked perfectly and a good size served with house made chips. The slaw and tarter were excellent with the highlight being the great Hawaiian roll. We ordered a few different desserts: hot chocolate chip cookies and milk, chocolate pudding and a peach and blackberry cobbler. All three were great, the cookies had a coating of kosher salt which went perfectly with the rich chocolate and sweetness of the cookies it included an egg beater with the cookie dough left in it that was a great touch. The pudding was rich with with a cookie crumble on top. The cobbler was huge and enough to share with whole blackberries and sliced peaches served warm with a rich vanilla ice cream. Overall Willa Jean is best for breakfast, lunch or when you need that sugar fixed dessert you can even use it as a coffee shop with your computer with great spots along the big windows to setup with your pc and get some work done.

Stopped into Gendusa's to try their huge meatballs with my dad, a true meatball and spaghetti lover. As they bring out this huge platter of meatballs my father questions "how are we going to eat all this" it already met his approval. What makes Gendusa different is their red gravy is made special to take out most of the stomach souring acid, this was a big plus for my dad, its darker in color and different in flavor than most red gravies around town. The bread was delicious and so was the salad. We were here on steak night and I cant recommend that enough. They serve a huge steak that two people can eat with sides for a great price. Its grilled outdoors on an open pit flame cooked to order. Its way out in Kenner but its worth the trip.

Some of the best crawfish boiled piping hot right in front of you as you sit in benches outside on Banks Street. Banks Street Bar is located next door for easy access for that I cold beer. Clesi also has the best fried catfish I have had in a while with a seasoning that is a special recipes. The owner is very friendly and is excited to serve. He also makes some great wings on the grill. A great experience.

Service....... horrible!!! I very much disliked this place. They were very inattentive from the get go. They came around for our initial drink order and then to get our food order and then went missing till we had to chase them down for our check. 
So first things first. I hate establishments that give you canned drinks. It just kills me. So of course the place is called State and Fig and I couldn't go here and not try the Fig Burger. So we ordered the Fig Burger with bacon on the side and the chicken panini. After about a 25 minute wait our food finally came. 
Well so we thought. He was halfway to the table and turns around. I can see the waiter being all frantic. So what had happened was that they forgot to put the bacon to the side. Because now he comes out with 3 plates with the bacon on the side. Burnt. And with bleu cheese. Ya they forgot about that. 
The food looked so good. Ummmm no!! First bite into it and all you could taste was burn. The burger was past well done and burned to a crisp. And then the bleu cheese in it just totally overpowered the whole burger. Honestly I always eat all my food. Even if it's bad and I don't like it I'll eat. I couldn't finish all my food unfortunately. It took them so long to bring out the order I wasn't ready to sit there and wait another 20 minutes. The side of greens I got with it were great. 
So my boyfriend had the chicken panini and his panini was bland and the chicken was dry. He got it with a side of Rosemary garlic fries. Those fries were soooooooo garlicky. Way over seasoned and so not made to eat. 
So after our miserable lunch we had to chase the waiter down to bring our check. We paid and left on our dandy way to never return again.
Rude rude owner as you can see from previous reviews, doesn't have any common sense or ettiquete.

What happened? We was just good a minute ago..

I went for Sunday brunch (9/16/18) and it appears the staff was brunching too. Wasn't even sitting close to kitchen and she could hear a lot of playing around and even cursing.

At one point a server came out wearing one of  those blue gloves you clean your house with and delivered a customer his food; his companion looked as shocked as I felt. What handling was done with that single blue glove? I'm going to assume they just ran out out food safety gloves that day. 

Food took a while to come out, omelet was hot and delicious, potatoes were salty, and pancakes were a tad warm. About time I was able to wave down the waitress for syrup, they were cold and so was I about Lebus.

I enjoyed the Flourtown location. I went for an 11:30am movie with 4 little gals. They actually were seated 3 rows in front of me and it was no issue with ordering. God Bless Dave because when those gals tried to order sundaes after having milkshakes, food and popcorn he came up to my row to check if they could have the sundaes and of course that was a big fat NOOOOO! He delivered the bad news hahaha

Overall my food was decent, it's not fine dining so be easy people. I ordered nachos and they were really enough for two. The girls had no complaints with their food and really enjoyed the experience.

Definitely get your tickets early so you can reserve seats WAYYYYYY back. That screen is humongous and will cross your eyes if you are too close. You have been warned!

Ohhh sooo I only have one loyal Yelp friend who told me to stop shopping around and go to Sophisticakes.

I've been wasting my time and my waistline trying all these other places... hunnny these cupcakes are THE BOMB!!!!!!

I ordered carrot (does have raisins), triple chocolate, and red velvet cupcakes!!! All three were delicious!!! Icing, straight buttercream; all quality ingredients. The cupcakes are a nice hefty size and decorated beautifully.

I would strongly suggest them if you are looking to order cakes, cookies, or cupcakes. My daughter got the cake pops and really liked them. 

Sophisticakes is located in a shopping center and I was able to find a parking spot easily; service was friendly.

If this place couldn't get any better, guess what? THEY ARE OPEN ON SUNDAYS!!! (Drops mic)

Yelp keeps telling me I need to review.... okkkkk here it is. Short and sweet.

* Its crowed except after 4
* Locals are irked by tourist who just stop in the middle of the isle when we are trying to get our lunch and you are on vacation.
* You will get lost (Local and Tourist)
* Have cash, many places don't take cards, there are numerous ATM located around. 
* Its delicious you can get a cake, smoothie, ham hocks, chitterlings, flowers, fish, cannolis, oils, Thai, spaghetti, ice cream , Shea butter, preservatives, donuts and a book under one roof.

Enjoy!

I love my Marriotts! Let's start with my seamless check-in. Rhia was so sweet. She was able to quickly find my mobile check-in. She even walked around the corner to give me my keys. 

Our room was on the 28th floor. Loved the view of the Mississippi view. Our room was giant, but the bathroom was pretty small. The light in the bathroom was bright! I called the lighting "the hangover fixer". It's soooo bright.

For you platinum elite and higher Marriott rewards peeps, the M lounge is great! Breakfast includes made-to-order omelettes and fresh made beignets. There was a huge spread, including exotic fruit. Loved the papaya and dragonfruit.

The location of the hotel was great. We were literally 2 blocks from Bourbon Street. I have stayed at the Ritz Carlton and the Saint in NOLA, by far this Marriott is the best location for easy access to the French Quarters. 

NOLA was a success and would definitely stay at this Marriott again!

The oysters. Absolutely amazing. I had the charboiled oysters, which were covered in butter and parmesan. I was so full, but I wanted more! The fresh bread that comes with the oysters has a parmesan crust on top. It makes me drool just thinking of my dinner. 

We started off with the calamari and the crawfish pies. The sauce that comes with the calamari has so much flavor. Fried food is typically fried food, but man that sauce. The crawfish pies were pretty good as well. 

If you like oysters, the wait isn't too bad. We came here during the high of Mardi Gras weekend and were able to get a table. We were too stuffed to get dessert, but not drinks. I loved the rum punch. Doesn't taste like kool-aid. Check this place out!

Views for days! What a gorgeous restaurant with stunning views. Our team dinner was at Teak. We made reservations in advance for 12 individuals. We had a lovely table in the corner of the restaurant. Loved the floor to ceiling windows! 

We started off with a handful of appetizers including the fried oysters, popcorn coconut shrimp, calamari, and a charcuterie board. I absolutely loved the fried oysters and popcorn shrimp. The presentation of everything was great! 

For dinner, I had the hardest time deciding between the grouper and the short ribs. I went with the guava bbq short ribs over cauliflower mash with kale. That was fabulous! A few of my coworkers ordered the grouper and looked pretty amazing too. 

Dessert. Where to start?! When in FL, you must get the key lime pie! So we did! A few others or their the whoopie pie. That was pretty great too. I enjoyed the German chocolate cake in the middle of the whoopie pie. Great twist on traditional whoopie pies.

Garden located in the middle of the French Quarters. I absolutely loved the ambiance. There are two options for dining, inside and outside. We stayed in the garden although it was freezing so we could skip the wait. There are heaters, so there definitely helped.

We started off with the oyster spinach dip. So yummy. The oysters aren't cut up, so there are huge chucks. No complaints especially when you're an oyster lover. I ordered the starter size shrimp and grits. It was a good size since the oyster spinach dip is pretty rich. Amazing! I love shrimp and grits. I've never had it with corn, but the infusion was great. 

My boyfriend ordered the gumbo and the shrimp pasta and my friend ordered the poutine. Of course I tried everything and it was yummy. The only downside were the drinks. They were ok. All of us were on the same page that the drinks didn't really standout to us. 

Super pretty restaurant. I recommend reservations if you want to sit inside.

As much as I love this delightful little cafe and everyone who works in it, I cannot give them a fourth star. The coffee is amazing, they do a great sandwich, an amazing quiche, a perfect soy milk hot cocoa with a tiny hint of hazelnut.... They just don't do any of it quickly.

There are way too many people standing around behind the counter to be getting that little done. I have somewhere to be. There is absolutely no sense of urgency here. 

On many occasions, I've been promised that my order would only take a minute & then witnessed that 1. Noone had begun making anything and 2. My quiche had yet to be put into the warmer. A coworker of mine once spent 10 minutes waiting for her order before I arrived to find her in a very similar situation. 

In order to overcome this, I now call in my order when I leave home so it's definitely ready by the time I make it uptown. This seems to work. So far. 

Good luck & Godspeed of you were on your way to work.

My group has recently switched to Latitude 29 for all of our tiki bar needs. They're so close to the office and the foods are amazing and the drinks are exciting!

It's comfortably dark and close, the atmosphere is really like a (nice) hole in the wall beach bar. If you're not paying attention you'd never knew you were at the Bienville. I've never sat on the dining area side.... Always at the bar or bar adjacent. Preferably at the bar because the bartenders are awesome. They make magic and witty banter look easy. Also,  there are several Steven's.... I think. Or a really confusing running joke. 

I mentioned that the drinks are exciting.... All the ice is special ice, like fun shapes and themes and edible flowers. My friend ordered something really cute and then found that her ice was actually an awesome snoball-ish volcano straw thing. We may have been more excited about that that we were about the drink (which was delicious, btw). 

Several things on the menu list extremely similar components, we thought that meant they'd taste similarly too. They do not. Completely different amazingness from the dumplings and the dumpling burger. There's an earthy something in those dumplings.... the sauce.... Dip the burger in the sauce. Just do it. It makes it even better. 

Presentation is here is great, I took pictures. I never take pictures, but everything was so cute!

I am slowly but surely eating my way through this menu. I'm about 1/3 done (i'd have more accomplished if it weren't for the wings & the emergency room spice)... 

Everything I've tried has been delicious. The wings, the burgers, the mussels, the sandwiches, the drinks (lol).

My favorite is the garlic parmesan wings with the emergency room spice & my second favorite is the garlic parmesan wins with ICU. 
So hot & SO GOOD. 

Atmosphere is really casual and friendly, it's great for date night (especially if you aren't sure it's a date).

The crowd here is cool ppl and the chefs (& bartender) are awesome. They bring so much personality and you can tell they really love bringing such a quality experience to the neighborhood.

We only went because of the groupon.
If you're only going because of the groupon, I vote skip it.

The menu was extensive, yes. There's every rendition of wings and fries that you can think of. Everything looks good and it smells good, but the rest of this visit was just... meh.

Service is ok. The wings were mediocre.

They got my order wrong twice.
Forgot to put hot sauce on my "crunchy hot" wings.
Left my broccoli bites out altogether.

By the time we got all this straightened out my Cajun ranch fries were cold.

I'm not likely to return, like I said... I was only there because of the groupon.

Top Five happy hours hands down, no lie. 

Movie on 3, Morton's on 2... That's a good night! 
I recommend the 3 way filet, the tiny wedge salads, and the fries! Oh the fries! Hot, crispy, subtly parm & truffle seasoned. 

The bomb dot com. 

When I'm dining in, I always have the filet and sauce au poivre. I love the way the Bourbon and cracked pepper compliment the steak. That and a salad and I'm happy. No take out box necessary, lol. 


My group tried the shrimp cocktail last visit. Good stuff, large gulf shrimp and cocktail sauce garnished with smoking dry ice. Very cute... nothing remarkable, tho. 

Anytime I go, there's a Manhattan involved. The bar here is lovely, everything they make is made well & there's atmosphere to boot. The low lighting & back-lit bar really give an impression. And the service is amazing!

This is probably the only occasion I will ever write that I preferred a place before the smoking ban.... but... umm.... I miss the cigar smoke.

French 75 is my quiet not actually quiet, alone in a room full of people place. It's just lovely being in a crowd of people that are all enjoying themselves and having a nice time. The laid-back atmosphere and the exceptional first-class service combine to make a truly unique and relaxing evening out. Once I saw a Jonas brother here (don't ask me which one)... I played it real cool.

The music is nice and jazzy and the chairs are comfortable. My favorite table is either of the front ones near the door. From one, you can see the whole bar and from the other, you can't see anything. Either way, your waiter is coming and they're going to take good care of you.

I Highly recommend their namesake cocktail, the French '75. Champagne and Courvoisier.... It's pretty like a butterfly and stings like a bee. So much stronger than it looks. A couple of these and I'm ready to go twirlin' on my haters. 

On nights when I can't stay and chill a while I like to have an Irish coffee. I kid you not, Arnaud's has ruined me on Irish Coffee. They lace theirs with caramel in the coffee and in the cream that's floating on top. I'm spoiled.

Foodwise, they took one of my favorite foods, oysters..... and wrapped it in another of my favorites, bacon.... deep fried them and serve this deliciousness with a Marchand de Vin sauce... just the right earthiness to complement the richness from the oysters and bacon.

I'm knee-deep in love with this bar. Can you tell?

Was on a family trip to Reno, and once again found this place on Yelp.  We were craving Mexican, it had great reviews, and was close to downtown where we were staying, so decided to try it.

The chips, salsas, and bean dip were unlimited and beyond delicious.  We ordered a starter of guacamole, which was incredibly fresh, served in a giant ramekin, and delicious as well.  Given that is place is called "The Fisherman" I decided seafood was the way to go.  I ordered "Pescado a la Veracruzana", this was a light white fish simmered in a red creamy tomato sauce with green, red, and yellow peppers, peas, onions, olives, and capers.  The fish was just flakey enough and wonderfully spiced with a thick and rich sauce.  Other members of my party ordered chicken fajitas, steak fajitas, and a specialty order fish burrito.  Everyone was more than satisfied.

The service was great, portions were huge, hot sauce selection more than ample, and food was great.  Wonderful place for Mexican food if you are in Reno.

I have been ordering from The Galley through UberEats for several weeks now, but today is the first time I had the pleasure of dining inside- and I could not have been happier with my choice.  My buddy and I went for a late lunch, he ordered the Florida Cracker Chicken Sandwich and fries- he tells me that it was great, very tasty fresh fried chicken, homemade quick pickles, on a cuban bun. I ordered the vegan buffalo sandwich.  

I am heavy set vegetarian, big boned some might say, so I often view vegan food suspiciously (cheese is part of what makes a sandwich good). But, today this buffalo sandwich was delicious- lightly friend tofu in a tasty homemade buffalo sauce.  A good mix of greens and sauces, with a side order salad. It was messy- but delicious.  I was really happy with this choice. 

I have also ordered the 7-grain grilled cheese several times, and the aubergine (eggplant) sandwich recently. I love a good grilled cheese and this one does not disappoint.  I highly recommend the Aubergine Veggie Sandwich- it is one of the best sandwiches I have had in a long time. 

The atmosphere inside the Galley is hipster/trendy/nautical, right at home in downtown St. Pete half a mile from the beach. The staff was amazing and made me feel welcome.  It may have been my first time being there today- but I plan to go back!
Everything was great chicken cheesesteak real chicken breast spinach shrimp on a garlic roll. They've got a new loyal customer. A lot of options

After walking past Gran Caffe L'Aquila many times (its right behind my office!) I finally stopped to have dinner here! My friend highly recommended this place as one of her new favorites in Philly, and I agree! 

Walk past the outside tables on the sidewalk, and inside is a nice gelato bar, showcased desserts, pastries, and paninis.  The downstairs restaurant is long and narrow, with a raw bar at the very back.  There's high top tables, and low dining tables, nice!  There's also a more formal dining room upstairs, with the homemade coffee making equipment up there showcased like breweries do!  Pretty cool!  Ask to take a tour of the upstairs! 

Now to the food. AMAZING!  Everything we tried was so delicious, and all at pretty good prices. There are tons of options in this large menu, and everything is authentic Italian style. They recommend tapas style sharing, but honestly, the plates were pretty large, so you don't need to over-order!  We had: 
 - ARANCINI appetizer, Sicilian rice balls stuffed with peas, cheese, some kind of meat, and a delicious creamy sauce. So good! 
- OCTOPUS appetizer was really good, very soft and tender, full of flavor.  I love the presentation of all the tentacles!
- BRUSCHETTE with added mozzarella, the slices were large and very filling! Something gave it a sweet flavor, very unique and not your traditional bruschetta!
- GNOCCHI in a ricotta cream sauce with mushrooms, amazing! This was probably the best gnocchi I've ever had. Melts in your mouth, freshly hand-made, you can tell!  Its rich, so I was pretty full from just eating half of this! 
- SALMON on a cedar plank was very good, perfectly cooked. Odd presentation, they put the cedar plank on a regular plate, but oh well, the food was still delicious. 

Dessert: Save room!  The gelato chef is award-winning from Italy, and makes 20+ types of fresh gelato daily.  There's quite an overwhelming amount of choices!  I loved the ones we tried, but they change every day so good luck repeating your order!   We were too full to try any pastries, but I wish I saved room for the creme brulee or the cheesecake.  I'll be back for that! 

Coffee selections are top notch!  So many fancy ways to make different coffee drinks, try some!  And, holy wine!  There are pages after pages dedicated to all the wine they have.  Impressive! 

Service was top notch.  We were greeted immediately by several different servers.  Service throughout the meal was fantastic. Everyone was on top of their game, and so very friendly.  Even the manager was amazing, he helped show me around the restaurant.  

Sorry for the long review, but I can't say enough great things about this place. I can't wait to come back again soon!

I FINALLY visited pizza Vetri on New Years Day. I live nearby, and have been wanting to try it for a while. I was very happy, and so were my tastebuds!  

Its small, so you walk in and there's likely a wait, but the servers are soooo friendly and everyone kept us informed where we'd be sitting, and how long the wait would be. Great communication! We only waited maybe 5-10 minutes, awesome! 

I had the beet & goat cheese slice special, which was sooo damn good I didn't want to share it with my friends! It was on a special square-type bread, not normal pizza crust, which was even better! I also had the Rotolo, which is only $4.50 for a delicious taste of dough, cheese, and pistacchio pesto all rolled up together in a ball. Delicious! 

My friends ordered a large pepporoni pizza, which isn't my pizza of choice, but they seemed to scarf it down. Also a small Marinara pizza which looked and smelled amazing. 

I'll come back! The food and service was excellent. The prices for single-serve items were good, but I thought the pizza prices were a bit steep. But overall, I reeeeeaaaaally like this place!

I love Roy Pitz! First of all, the atmosphere is amazing. Huge bar, tons of long tables good for large groups, and I love the octopus painting on the wall! 

The beer is amazing! So many flavors for all types of beer lovers; ales, IPAs, sours, stouts, triples, and an gose. My favorite beer is the Mr. Pitz, its a very sour ale, with peach, apricot, and kiwi. It is amazing! My only complaint is you can't get it in the flight, but you can still buy a small glass on its own, so I was happy. My other favorites were the dark sour, and the pretzel gose. 

Get a flight! And if you don't want to stop at 4, you can also buy the beers in a smaller half size, so you can try everything and not get too drunk (or spend too much money!)

FOOD is also amazing. The biggest Bavarian pretzel I ever had, with such delicious brown mustard sauce, and a cheese dip sauce! Best of both pretzel worlds. I also had the smoked brisket Mac n Cheese which was really good. The brisket panini was amazing, and so was the pork panini. My frinds cheese plate looked really good too.

Overall amazing place. Great beer, great food, good for groups. I came once for beer only, and loved it so much I came back again to eat the food. I'll keep coming back many more times! Can't wait to try more, different beer! Horray Roy Pitz!

Omg this is the best breakfast I've had in a long time. My husband and I waited over an hour for a table here, which we never ever do, and it was totally worth the wait! (Not in his opinion, but mine :)
