I am absolutely obsessed with the blue yogurt berry and granola bowl. This is by far the BEST yogurt bowl I've ever eaten!! See photos.. you'll be amazed. I have since dreamed about this yogurt multiple mornings for breakfast and sometimes am tempted just order it for delivery halfway across the city. 

We also had chicken and waffles which was pretty good, but not nearly as good as the short rib huevos rancheros, which to me looks more like quesadillas (see photos). This was also some of the best huevos rancheros I have ever had and the serving size was huge enough to feed two people! 

The cappuccino was delicious and the service was speedy fast because they were trying to turn tables over very quickly since the wait got up to over two hours long. 

I have worked in the food industry so I knew to eat quick and get out but others who were lingering around and drinking their coffee slowly could be annoyed at how they were being rushed to eat and leave. But because of Covid restaurants have restrictions on how many tables they can have outside so it's critical that people be aware that every minute equals money, and they should not sit and linger when done eating if there is a wait for tables. 

The owner was funny, A little rough around the edges, but I enjoyed watching him keep track of a two hour long wait on nothing but yellow Post-it notes. Maybe an upgraded computer system would do them good! 

But the food was so delicious it outweighs everything else to a 5-star rating. Bravo chef!

Wait? I haven't reviewed South yet? I came here 2 months ago and absolutely loved it!! I even told my friends throughout the dining experience that I couldn't wait to give 5 stars to this place! 

Well, congrats South. Well deserved. 
I've been to several southern-style dining restaurants, and this is one of my favorites. The food is unique to please the southerner, but it also hasn't lost the Philly-foodie flavor and style that us locals have grown to love. 

Start with the CORNBREAD- its the BEST cornbread I've ever had. Huge portion, in its own baking pan, topped with Honey Cream Cheese Butter!  What?! Yes, Honey Cream cheese butter. This needs an award itself. 

My next salivating dish was the SCALLOPS Special: perfectly cooked scallops, with lump crab meat, corn kernels, cherry tomatoes, zucchini, and the most amazing sweet sauce drizzled on top. I was making "Mmmmm" and "Yummm" sounds the entire time eating it, which probably annoyed my friends! 

SHRIMP & GRITS, a classic dish, was also mind blowing. Again, every southern-style restaurant has this, but there's something different about South's Shrimp & Grits that makes the grits extra delicious. I kept stealing bites off my friends' plate! 

Fried Potato Dumplings were amazing.. they are round balls with this amazing oozy cheese sauce drizzled on top.  Sooo good. 

These other items were good, but not my favorite:  Rock shrimp (didn't stand out like the other dishes), and Pork Pate toast (kind of boring, but its much better if you dip it in the beet spread).

FOOD: 5 stars.  DRINKS: 5 starts for taste, but 4 stars for price (the cocktails were pricey, $12-$14 each, beer is cheaper).  SERVICE: 5 stars.  Overall, great place. Just be ready to break your budget a little!  The 3 of us spent around $180 total, not including tip!

Pats vs. Geno's?  Its like a Philidelphian's religion, you pick one and stick to it!  Never cross over to the other side!  My side.... PATS.

PATS... don't eat a mis-steak!   I love Pats.  Nothing beats 3am oozy "Whiz Wit" after an Eagles or Flyers game.  Better yet, get the "Heat Attack Wit" if you want all 3 cheeses w/ onions.   The line wraps around the building, but you still get your steak quick because the line moves so fast!  Why does the line move that fast?  1) Have your cash ready in hand.  2)  Cash Only  3) steaks are already cooking awaiting your order, they just slap it in the roll, add cheese, and you're done!  4) Get your soda & cheese fries in a different line.

Pats vs. Genos:  Its like a religion.  If you go to Pats, park near Pats.  If you go to Genos, park near Genos.  Once, I was in line at Pats, late night, and someone (alcohol involved I'm sure) love-tapped the car in front of them trying to parallel park.  The customers in line at Pats in front of me says to the driver "Its OK, the guy in that car went to Genos!"  So the driver, still in the car, says "Oh he did!?? In that case...."  SMASH!  He literally hit the gas pedal and rear-ended the car parallel parked in front of him on purpose!  It was the most entertaining line-wait I've ever experienced.  The entire line was cheering and clapping!

I once did a "Cheesesteak Challenge" with my friends.  We went to several cheesesteak shops around philly in one day, and ranked our favorites:
1.  Pats  -- Fast service, down home Philly attitude, lots and lots and lots of cheese whiz
1.  Tony Luke's  (tied 1st place) -- better steak quality, less gritty fat in the meat, but much longer wait time 
3.  Jims -- Good quality meat, fine shaven, but I asked for xtra cheese whiz, and still got less cheese than a normal steak at Pats.  Size of Jims steaks are smaller too.
X.  Genos -  N/A.  Never eaten here, never will!!

Eating at Cheddar's is like that one song that you always skip but one day you finally decide to listen to it, and you find out how good it is. My Cheddar's virginity was taken a few weeks back when a good friend of mine decided we should go out for drinks since we had heard about how good their infamous "Pain Killer" is.

I had no intentions on purchasing any food since the menu did not appeal to me, the awesome waiter ( who's name I can't remember ), suggested we try the crescent rolls with honey butter. Let me start by telling you this, you will NOT want to share these so do not feel bad for ordering your own personal appetizer. By the time the drinks and rolls arrived I had worked up an appetite and settled on ordering a petite steak, with a potato, and broccoli cheddar casserole. My food was average but the drinks were very well worth mentioning.

Since my first visit I have been back to Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen numerous times, but I only have eyes for the honey butter crescents and any alcoholic drink on the menu!

Not one of the best seafood places I've been to but it's definitely a 4/5!

I split combo #2 with a friend, which includes 2lbs of snow crab, shrimp, sausage, potatoes and two ears of corn. We chose the fever signature mix mild which is just a combination of their lemon pepper and Cajun rub submerged in garlic butter oil.

Our food came out hot, fresh, and  extremely tasty. The portion size of combo two could definitely feed at least 3 people, judging by how much seafood we had leftover.

Great Dj, good wings, and decent drinks!

Came to No Vacancy last Friday and the place was pretty packed. Couldn't really get a seat at the bar but one of the servers walking past saw ya girl struggling and helped us put a order in. My friend and I each started out by ordering a Mai Tai, which came in a cute little tiki cup with a purple flower on top and a basket of buffalo wings to share. The wings were good as hell but our drinks were honestly just cute and we finished out the night by drinking claws.

I'm giving this place 5 stars because the Dj that night definitely put in work by playing a good mix of trendy rap and old R&B songs that kept us on our feet!

I dined here with my husband & his family (8 of us total) and had a pretty good experience! I will say that we did call a couple of other restaurants in the area but they weren't able to get a group of us in on Saturday night. Ending up at The Parish though was definitely a good thing! It's a cute little restaurant, I'd say more of a date night dinner place than a family restaurant as it had a more relaxed, intimate atmosphere.

We started off with drinks & then ordered dinner. The choices at the table included Guedry's Gumbo, Drunken Angel, The Tchoup, & The Tomahawk Special. I personally went a simple salad, The Garden District with Smoked Salmon. My husband liked his choice of The Tchoup which was a bone-in pork chop with BBQ sauce, apple kraut, and a sweet potato puree. His mom really enjoyed the Tomahawk Special, it looked too pretty to eat! The others liked their orders as well, minus the Gumbo as it wasn't found to be a hearty dish, lacking chicken and sausage. They did accommodate by bringing out some sausage on the side but the 3 who got it were still a bit disappointed. I enjoyed my salad and found the Smoked Salmon to be tasty; I was told they smoke the salmon in-house.

Overall, we thought this was a good choice and a restaurant we would come back to. The Shrimp & Grits have been calling my name ever since! Can't wait to try that dish ... and maybe some Bread Pudding too next time.

This is our new favorite place for date night. I can see why it won the award for Best Place to take Out of Town Guests. When they're understandably tired of Mexican food, we'll be sure to bring them here. 

From their cocktails made with their in-house fusions to their Cajun-inspired dishes, this place is a winner in our book. 

For drinks I had their Moscow mule and my husband had their Cinnamon Apple. The Parish offers seasonal cocktails. I'd recommend taking a look at their Instagram (@theparishtucson) for drool-worthy pictures. 

We had their hush puppies, salmon verlasso, and shrimp and grits. Next time we'll have to try the bacon popcorn - I've heard it's a must!

When leaving, I noticed they do weekly live music. We can't wait to go back!

This place is kind of dumb.

Okay, before I get ripped apart to shreds.. I haven't eaten here yet (maybe that's more of a reason to get ripped apart to shreds). But like most people, I not only judge a place on food but on service/atmosphere as well. And in the mist of raving reviews (which are probably well deserved food-wise), I think this might save someone a walk down girard ave in the blistering summer heat which might very well end in disappointment and sweat. 

So they have no phones!!!!! Awesome. I was looking for a nice pizza byob night. I am always the first one of my friends to be ready, so I decided to walk down and grab a table- because they only have two!!!!!! 

There are two high tops with no chairs. I mean, maybe I'm not sophisticated but I like to sit at a byob. I like to sit.. and talk.. and drink.. and talk. But I wasn't angry at the place, I just kind of laughed and said: No chairs? 
The guy looked at me in disgust: Uh no we don't have chairs.
His attitude kind of set me back, so I just laughed again and said: Oh you don't have a phone so I just figured I'd walk down. I don't really know how this works. 
Again with disgust: Well I have to take your name down, and you have to pay for the pizza, and there is a 30 minute wait.  
NOOOOOO friendliness in his voice at all. Like I was a giant idiot, didn't I fucking know how it worked?!?! P.S: What if you're far away and you want to take out pizza? Then what do you do? Come over physically, order it, pay for it,  then wait 30 minutes in a tiny ass shop with no AC? (You'd probably feel so awkward in shame standing there so you'd definitely have to wait outside)

Okay, its your thing. It probably makes a lot of sense. Whatever. 
But maybe it won't hurt to be a little fucking nicer next time :) 
So if you're looking for a place to sit down with friends and eat good pizza and drink some wine and you're confused because there's no phone to ask such questions?
1. It's Hot.
2. There are no chairs.
3. The service is rude. 

It's PIZZA and its PHILADELPHIA. There are so many places.

My wife and I were very excited to have The Bisbee Breakfast Club come to our neighborhood. We were very very disappointed. 
We arrived on a Saturday around 10:30am. We were able to be seated immediately at the counter. The restaurant was busy, but the server took our order immediately and placed it. I ordered the corned beef hash with 2 eggs over medium well and hash browns. And a side of biscuits with gravy. My wife had the California omelette. We waited 45 minutes for our order. I've been a chef for over 30 years and I understand that the restaurant was busy. But 45 minutes for eggs is unexceptable.
Ok. I can kinda get past that, but the food was well below average. My eggs were cooked over easy not over med well. If I wanted a runny yolk I would have asked for it. The hash browns came out of a box/slash carton that I saw sitting out on the back line. The corned beef hash came out of a can, which I also saw. My wife's guacamole came from a bag. The gravy had zero taste at all. I assume that wasn't homemade but I don't know that for sure. Look, I understand that there may just not be the space or storage, or prep area to make everything from scratch, I get it. But maybe try to season it, don't just pull it from the box, bag or can and just serve it.  Maybe the lead cook/chef could add something to the food in the way of seasoning to make it more palatable. Somebody is not tasting their own food they prepare. It could be so much much better. 
So much for having a nice breakfast/lunch place right here in our own back yard. I suggest you drive a couple/few extra miles and look for a good breakfast joint.

Delachaise is as unique as it can get. Amazing ambiance, amazing food, and superb service. I'm going to keep it simple because I'm sure the other reviews will tell you the same. This place is the bomb.com! Great for a simple girls night out and even date night. Cheese plates here are always perfect; I usually get the chef's selection (5) different types of cheese with sliced green apples & spiced walnuts, I believe. The steak & frites are to die for as well. You won't regret coming here whether it's for a drink or a bite, heck both!

There's not many negative things that can be said about John's donuts except one: their hours are super funky, (closed saturday night / sunday morning), and sometimes the guy working is just "not in the mood" but I guess when you have to work 11pm to 12pm everyday I would also want to just get my donuts sold.

This place is bomb. Every donut I had was amazing, but the ones that stood out for me were Blueberry!!, apple friters, double chocolate, and glazed. 

The second best part on top of their donuts being extremely soft, yummy tasting, not too sweet, and just perfect, is that this place is CHEAP! A dozen donuts cost like 10.50 or something ridiculous. You compare this to some of the "nice" donut places in other areas, who charge "$2-3" per just a glazed donut... It's unbelievable how good their donuts are, on top of how cheap it is.

I got a dozen just for me and my girlfriend and they lasted and were still good after 3-4 days.

Unfortunately Saffron, when I first came here 3-4 years ago, you were awesome. You guys had a variety of curry meats (goat beef and chicken if I remember correctly) and a bunch of other awesome stuff. 

I've been here 2 times now twice in the past 3 months and you guys have done nothing but disappoint. First of all your variety for the lunch buffet has diminished severely, there is only chicken curry and chicken tandoori for the meat dishes. There was no beef or goat or lamb or whatever else you used to serve. Second your waiter was extremely rude to me and my guests, there was some dried up chicken in the curry and tandoori and it was not good, yet you questioned whether or not I liked chicken... and why I didn't eat the small remaining pieces on my plate. Well obviously, because it was dry and terrible.

The second time I came, same thing, very limited amount of choices, yet you still charge 10 dollars per visit. On top of that, on your own website you guys say you close lunch buffet at 2:30 yet you denied customers entrance at 2 PM. I was absolutely shocked when I saw that.

Sorry, this is really unacceptable

Wow absolutely no complaints about this place.

Paul Manno's is a hole in the wall placed between a Goodwill and a Firehouse Subs. You wouldn't expect a gem to be in that plaza.

My girlfriend has been here before, but it was my first time. I heard great things so I was pretty excited.

Paul Manno's lived up to every expectation.

Very dark, date night place, white table cloths, small menu, great wine. We ordered Italian reds and they were awesome. They will let you sample the wine so just try a couple and see what you like the best!

Started off with the freshly baked bread, extremely good with a oil / vinaigrette dip. Followed by their clam / muscle appetizer special.

Extremely tasty sauce, pretty solid portions, and you dip the freshly baked bread into the sauce of the appetizer, wow, extremely good.

2 main courses of the special, the Chilean Sea bass, and the rack of lamb.

Wow both main courses and their pasta was awesome, delicious, cooked to perfection. That was probably the best cooked fish I've ever had before. 

Rack of lamb was also seasoned exceptionally well, cooked to a great soft pink (barely visible), extremely tender and soft.

Love this place, will be back for sure.

This place is located in the same plaza as Pink Galleon, and it is next to the korean grocery store. 

It literally has changed names and management and chefs (or so I've heard) probably up to 5 times in the past couple years.However, someone told me the new chef here (or management?) is from New York and it definitely is a lot better. 

They have an AYCE here for 21.95 and you can get Galbi (extra 3 dollars ) rib steak, and all the other normal KBBQ meats part of the AYCE. And it's good. How can you say no? This is the new go-to place for KBBQ in St Louis. Definitely will be back

Their banchan included a pretty big sea food pancake so I don't know what's the normal but It would be incredible if they keep it up. I'm impressed

Went here for happy hour,  the place had a nice atmosphere , really like the decored wall at the bar and service was good.  The drinks were good with happy hour $5 specials.   I give this place 2 stars because I did not care at all for the food which is the most important thing to rate.   Went with a group of friends and we ordered a bunch of appetizers.   We shared the plantain empanadas,  chicken flautas,  pork belly,  shrimp with tomato sauce,  queso (with soft tortilla which was an interesting combo).  Not one dish i liked.. I felt like the food was bland and just not really authentic.  For the price it was very disappointing in my opinion.   Out of all the Mexican food in Tampa Bay that I've tried, I'm afraid to say this is my least fave.

This is the kind of place where after I've carefully perused the menu, I want to simply hand it back to the server and say in wonderment, "Yes. I will take it all." 

The spot has a great vibe. Trendy enough for a first date, sophisticated enough to take an important client, and fun enough to make it one of your many stops on a bar crawl through the city. All while somehow remaining unpretentious. #sorcery

While visiting on business, came in TWO nights in a row (which is saying something in a food city such as New Orleans!). Smart, attentive service, killer cocktails and a menu that features items you cannot find anywhere else will bring me back. The Aburi Hokkaido (seared scallops), "Ghetto Sous Vide" short ribs, and Phat Rice were so good I almost needed a cigarette after. Had the Rebellion Ramen and the Wagyu Burger on visit numero dos and I would punch a stranger in the face to have them magically transported to me tonight. Seriously. I was so happy to hear that the place is a locally-owned small business and not run by some McCorporation or conglomerate. Can't wait to visit again!

First impression: such a large space! 

I honestly didn't think the interior would be this spacious. There are two large conference like tables along with plenty of two seater options and a couch style lounge at the front of the shop.

I have to be honest, I'm not a doughnut eater. I backed rocket 88 on kickstarter. I brought the doughnuts to work though and everyone enjoyed them. The chai and sprinkled seemed to be a favorite. 

I did have a coffee and it was so rich and delicious. The coffee sold here is from a local roaster, Miles Square and it's worth every penny. 

I would definitely hang out in this space and work during the day. Just the spacious nature and the coffee alone are two good reasons. 

Cheers to a new local business in ft square!

Wake Up Tucson! This is where your lunch and probably your dinner come to die. Bring the kids, the grand-kids, the friends from out of town -- just don't bring your belt. This place may get a warning from the county health board from all of the expanding waistlines. 

I found it difficult to decide on my order when my wife and I sat down for a Sunday brunch recently. Not in the same way you approach the Cheesecake Factory menu's bafflement of endless varieties, but instead with a hopeless dithering "Ooh! That sounds good too". Our waiter who may have been the owner was very helpful in narrowing us down between the sweet and savory options. I finally chose the weekend special: the Wildcat Benedict as long as my wife ordered the Snicker-doodle pancakes so we could share. The Wildcat was a genuine burst of flavor: like biting into a chuck-wagon of creamy southwestern heat with their chipotle hollandaise sauce, chorizo and fresh tomato and onions on top of a buttery-sweet corn cake. Flanked as well by crispy fresh hash browns that I'm not kidding looked and tasted like fried-gold snowflakes.

And the Snicker-doodle pancakes were a revelation: a heavenly indulgence that is more guilt-on-a-plate than a breakfast dish but luckily in this place no one is lifting their head to gaze at what others are devouring. I will say it's not easy to stop scarfing. 

I've yet to try their lunch and dinner menus but at this rate their breakfast will stave me off from trying anything else for the time being. Bravo Baja!

It doesn't look open yet, but it issss...

I love, love, love the new space. It's a bit smaller which I actually don't mind because they have booths and a larger bar area, a major plus for me! It's brighter and the ceilings are vaulted, so it's not as noisy in this location. Since the space has just opened its impeccably clean. There is plenty of waiting space out front for busier days. 

Most places have "watery" coffee not BBC, they consistently serve AMAZING COFFEE. They even roast it in-house and sell it, so you can enjoy it at home too or give it as a gift! You can order specialty coffees...like mochas, espressos, lattes, etc. I had a caramel latte and a regular coffee today..I'm greedy and wanted to try everything! They even have an after hours coffee window.

I ordered my typical favorite from the other location, Huevos Rancheros and it's still just as amazing as usual! They allow me to keep a special creamer and grape jelly here (since I'm extremely picky), I tip well because of this! I was checked on numerous times by several people to make sure everything was perfect! Customer service here is a priority with this crew as it was at the Ina location.

Both locations are about 15 min away from my house which is awesome. I like the newness of this location &&& my favorite waitress from the Ina location transferred over here, so needless to say I will be visiting THIS location the most.

I THINKKKK mimosas are on the way to the menu..YAYYY, so keep a look out for that in the near future.

This place really impressed me! The food and service was great!  Located inside the Intercontinental Hotel. Our server name was Kevin. 
You order your menu by courses. They had four courses. Now you don't have to order all four courses. You can pick and choose and also share. The five stars is for the taste and Quality of the food. Just keep in mind it is a little on the pricey side but the menu is very impressive and the food and service speaks for itself. I enjoyed everything and would not hesitate to return.

Fantastic museum to visit when you're in the area, a top Philadelphia attraction. Some of the great artist favorites:  Picasso, Monet, Rembrandt. Fantastic temporary exhibits: the Fashion Exhibit was a favorite of ours. And always amusing watching people make the "Rocky run" up the steps and line up to take photographs by the Rocky statue.

Incredible Italian food, and equally incredible experience having the talented opera singers as servers.  Fantastic place outside Philadelphia for a date, group outing and special event. What's more memorable than being serenaded by a group of opera singers while having wonderful food and well crafted cocktails?

Upstairs, there is a dimly lit lounge with sofas, comfortable chairs, candles and artwork.   

My favorite restaurant experience in Philly.

Chow mein heaven, or Sushi  is great too! I enjoy this place so much I have even held my birthday party here. 

Tonight we all had the Jazmine Chow Mein, that's 3 orders and what a great value at $13.00. 

The potstickers were a group favorite too.

The quintessential (and literal) hole in a wall. Found in the back of the the bar, with the proprietor "Mac" taking orders from it's opening, you'll be presented with several different varieties of their smashed griddle burgers (think Steak N Shake sized patties). 

You'll think a single is good, but Mac himself will tell you that you'll need a double (my girlfriend can attest). It's not a sales pitch, but a heartfelt heads up from an owner proud of the locally sourced food he serves, and to give his diners the best taste(s) possible - in quality AND quantity.

I had the pleasure of ingesting the Double Pimento ($10): a 2 patty burger with house made pimento cheese + house aoli & a pickle/tomato hybrid (I had mine without that). I chose the "rip fries" - fries tossed in Old Vienna Red Hot Riplet (chip) seasoning.

The burger was a boss. I'd definitely try three patties on my next visit. The Rip Fries were the highlight for the fry connoisseur that I think I am. Definitely an original idea, with a solid cut and yield to justify the $4.50 price.

There is seating at the bar or (weather permitting) in the courtyard out back that had seating and ample room for backyard games (ex. bags) if you were so inclined.

Dogs are allowed out back if on a leash, with bowls for water provided for your pup(s). Be aware that smoking is allowed and present outside, so you can't say you didn't hear it here, jack.

I'm already looking forward to our return visit. This establishment is a great addition to the Dogtown neighborhood. Here's hoping Mac will be there to recommend other tasty offerings on his menu. Bravo sir!

I ordered a small greek salad and the portion was huge as you can see in the picture, I even asked the waiter if that was the correct size because it was so much food, I also tried the eggplant spread appetizer, it had chunks of onions and also spices, my friend had a gyro and said it was good. What I liked the most about this place was being able to seat near the water and the awesome waiter.

If you are reading this review is because you are all about that taco life. I am too. There are so many places to choose from but I always go back to casita because they are consistent. They already have a good reputation  but they are still serving amazing food as when they first opened here in the 4th street location. Their food is not greasy or salty, they have hand made tortillas and their tacos are filled to the top :) So, while you can find cheaper tacos somewhere else, in my experience the portions are not even close to this one. I get full with 2 tacos and I have a healthy appetite so that tells you something.

9pm reservation. Got there and asked for an outdoor seat and was told there was no space. We saw several outside seating areas. We asked for it again and was told someone coming in was going outside. When we said we asked as soon as we got to the door Ella the manager said she didn't know why we were arguing with her. We got up and left. Super rude! It's a rooftop on a 70 degree day. Who would not want an outdoor seat?

RACIST!! UNPROFESSIONAL!! RUDE !! IGNORANT!! To say the least ! Horrible dining experience on the roof top with new servers with no appropriate guidance or overseer. Inadequate management and customer service !! Do not waste your time or money patronizing this establishment !! When expressing concerns to management he was not apologetic at all! He was extremely defensive and didn't acknowledge myself or the rest of my party's concerns. Served me raw chicken wings, I sent back and requested they cook a little longer for the waitress to return immediately with them stating the person who prepared them said they were well done! UNBELIEVABLE!  The staff didn't seem to treat the other guest of other nationalities this way...it was disgusting ! Would not recommend, do not dine here !

This is my go to deli. The food and service is always good. They have a one-page menu which is good because sometimes a person can get lost with too many choices. They have a ton of deli favorites like Corn Beef Cabbage, mile-high sandwiches. Their desserts at amazing, the cheesecake is HUGE, as are the brownies. One of my favorite is the chicken noodle soup, may be the best I've had and I have had a lot.

I've past by this resturant several times and never had the nerve to go in because I always got confused on what door to enter in. I finally found the right door and decided to grab some eats.

The environment upon walking in was the average bar scene which confused me on if the actually place sold food but right around the corner was the counter I was looking for.

I got the Louie which was flavorful and filling for the size of the burger. Based on recommendation I got the RipFries which were fries tossed in red hot riplets seasoning. The fries were on point,crisp and good portion of deliciousness.

It has a seperate dining area away from the bar if you decide to dine in

I thought the meal was a little pricey with a burger and fries being $15 (but it was good) and it was annoying after getting off work teaching middle school to just have kids running around in circles while I eat. 

Besides those little critiques above, it was a good food experience. I don't know if I could call it the "best" burger in STL but it is certainly good

We rsvp'd to eat a celebratory graduation dinner here but last minute had a change of plans when we were informed we would be charged $350 if we didn't eat there so we ended up still eating here. The food was good and we tried a lot of it, the skewers and Asian wraps were probably the best. The owner did allow us to bring in our own cake which was nice. The downfall was that the owner and staff were very rude after we attempted to cancel and continued to make us feel uncomfortable throughout the entire meal (except for our waiter who was amazing and the chef who went out of her way to cut a cake for us, thank you both!). Following this we of course told friends and family about our experience because that is what anyone would do. Other people posted reviews and the owner began harassing me and my girlfriend telling us to remove someone else's comments. He has continued even despite the fact that we don't know the people making them. Even going so far as to vaguely threaten us saying "it can get worse so have your friends go on and remove the comments." If you want good food then by all means, come eat here. But keep in mind they will harass you if someone leaves a bad review.

I doubt this review would ever be a candidate for a Review of the Day, but who knows, there's always a first time for anything, right?

In any case, while visiting my former college roommate in the Irish Channel last month, I was comforted to see this Starbucks a couple of blocks away on Washington and Magazine Street.

Surprisingly, I found locating Starbuckses, in general, to be difficult in New Orleans, especially considering that there are tons of really nice cafes and independently owned joints in the French Quarter and along Magazine Street. This particular Starbucks, however, served as a convenient road marker to know that I was on track to finding the St. Charles trolley a couple more blocks down on Washington Street.

I ended up taking a small detour here while walking to the trolley in the late morning on a weekday, only to find that the place was full of people. Lots of people who work immediately around the area, as well as students (your typical workday crowd) patronized the place.

Coming from Los Angeles for vacation, I did notice that I was the only one without a stack of papers, laptops or a backpack that morning. In a way, I was happy I was the only one without worry about work or studying and sat around observing the New Orleans/Southern style architecture here at this Starbucks. And, as is the beauty of franchises: you get a consistent product no matter where you are, and the hazelnut macchiato here was no exception and tasted as fine as anywhere else.

The baristas here provided a high level of customer service, as I noticed that they were keeping busy sweeping the floors in the main dining room area when there was finally a lull in the queue. In a separate incident, one of them didn't flinch or give a weird look at a patron who returned a partially drunk coffee. In fact, they were really happy about replacing the drink. The patron may or may not have realized that it was not to her liking until about halfway through, and most people, if they were in the barista's shoes would probably have made a look, gossip later or show a hint of attitude. None here...and I was impressed at the restraint and professionalism.

The setup of this particular Starbucks is elongated. The front desk is parallel to Washington Street (the long side of the rectangle shape of the coffee house's layout). There's a bit of an issue with seating arrangements inside because it gets pretty narrow as you walk towards the rear of the store (as if you're walking down the store with Washington Street to your right). If it gets a bit too claustrophobic for you, you can always do what many others did that day and take a seat outside. Thankfully, I like to think I brought the California weather with me that week, so it was totally enjoyable to actually sit outside in a typically hot and humid time of year.

I shared 5 small plates with a friend this evening and really enjoyed each of them.  
We did have to sit outside because we decided to drop in last minute (make reservations!), but our server was fairly attentive and our food was served quickly.  
We chose with prosciutto wrapped asparagus, Brussels sprouts, Thai chicken wraps, mini meatballs, and stuffed crimini mushrooms.   The "sierra selection" option allowed us to choose 4 of the small plates (under $10 each) for $28, and we added the 5th because we just couldn't choose! 
All of the ingredients were fresh, bright, and beautifully plated. Unfortunately our food wasn't very hot, and there were a lot of smudges of sauce and dressing on the dishes, like perhaps our dishes were rushed to us. I am not sure if that was because the outside temperature was chili or if that's the usual, but I think I'll hold off on the 5th star until I see what it's really like to dine inside.   
Stay tuned for an update...

I've been here twice and loved it both times.
We started with yakiton and a cucumber salad. We added a selection of nigiri and long rolls and were not disappointed with any of it. 
The fish to rice ratio on the nigiri was perfect. The long rolls we ordered were pleasing to the eye, rolled tightly so they did not crumble when we picked them up (a peeve of mine) and were all very tasty.  Our favorite was the 300...which was on the specials board not on the menu, but should be.  
I struggle to remember what was in it (mental note...write this stuff down!) but it was yummy! It had just the right amount of saltiness and spice to accompany the melt in your mouth fish that they serve here. 
Add in the clean and friendly atmosphere and it makes Hinoki one of my top 3 favorites for sushi in the Reno area.

I really like this brewery. It's got almost something for everyone. When you walk in the front door to the left is another door that leads to the brewery with all of the typical cylinder equipment you see in a brewery but you can also eat over on this side and get a beer from over here. Only Four Day Ray beers are served on this side and is 21 and up only on this side.

To the right of the front door is a typical brew pub with table service outside of the bar area where you can sit with your family. The bar area is 21 and up only.

There's also an outside patio that is covered and has an attractive outside wall area that provides privacy from the street and parking lot to folks sitting outside eating or drinking. There is a small uncovered area still protected by that outside wall but with Adirondack chairs surrounding a fire pit in a gravel area. I've seen folks with their pups on a leash in this gravel area, so dog friendly as well!

Unexpected. I was in this shopping center visiting another business and saw a brewery in the corner, so I had to check it out.

It's a rather small space inside with maybe about 10 or so beers on tap. 

The place was actually packed with a standing room only crowd of people enjoying craft beer. Some folks were outside. There is a larger patio area with tables chairs and a fire pit out there.

The brewery backs up to the Monon trail so easy access for walkers, joggers, and bikers to the brewery.

If you are looking for sushi and sake, this is the place! I've been here with work colleague and also by myself and both times were very good.

There are options for cooked sushi, which includes many tempura and veggie selections.

I don't have a favorite yet but I've gotten a few great suggestions from wait staff and also from some enthusiastic customers.

They do have some craft beers on tap which I appreciate. So give them a try!

Tale of two BRUs.

It was the best of times (lunch with a group), it was the worst of times (dinner by myself). 

I've eaten here three times so far. All three times I've eaten the exact same burger, their bleu cheese burger with fries. Ok, I'm a creature of habit.

The both times I've come here for lunch it was with a group and the burger came out exactly as ordered. Medium well, and the fries were hot with just the right amount of salt.

When I came for dinner by myself, I ordered the same burger but it came out well done and the fries were basically stale and cold. I couldn't have been more disappointed.

So I only come here for lunch only if someone else suggests it. I won't suggest it. But I'll come if someone else does and only for lunch. Too many burger places around to get mixed results.

From the outside it looks like a cool brew pub with a nice covered section outside on the ground level and also an uncovered outside patio on the second level. However, Sun King actually distills their spirits at this location. 

When you walk inside, it's very open and there is plenty of seating and places where you can get food like in a food court. In fact, you have to pay for your food at each food station. So it's basically like they have food trucks but they're inside of the building! The four food places have pizza, sliders, tacos, and sandwiches.

There is a fireplace on the second floor with cozy seating in that area to make it nice and comfy in the winter time or whenever it's cold out. 

The location is on the Monon trail in downtown Carmel. It's an up and coming area with lots of apartments and new construction. There's some street parking and a parking garage nearby.

Oyster House was recommended by a work colleague. I decided to check it out and I was not disappointed.

The service was excellent. When I entered the restaurant I was immediately greeted and seated. After a few minutes a server showed up, took my drink order, brought me the drink and asked if I was ready to order. I asked a few questions and ordered. The food came out piping hot and was delicious. 

Highly recommend!

Thanks to fellow yelper Nicole S. for her great review of this place. I bookmarked it immediately.

If you are looking for a unique Asian experience, try this Korean restaurant. What's unique about it? Try the dolsot bibimbap served in a stone bowl served to you at about 500 degrees! 

But wait! You can't eat it yet. You have to let it sizzle in front of you for about a minute. Then with the long spoon they give you, break the egg and carefully stir the contents of the bowl, combining everything together as evenly as you can, getting the hot rice off of the sides and into the mixture.

And this is the difficult part. Still can't eat it yet!  Waiting another minute for the mixture to continue cooking in front of you in this stone bowl while you enjoy the wonderful aroma of this dish is almost torture!

After 2 minutes, now you can eat. And what a wonderful dish this is. OMG! Highly recommend!

How cute is this place!! An adorable Italian cafe and restaurant for coffee, pastry, gelato, and food lovers, in general. We stopped here for lunch today and had a great experience. The service was so personable, although a little bit on the slow side - pretty authentic European if you ask me. 

I ordered their special Roman Egg Drop soup and soaked it up with the delicious house bread. Both were complimented with great olive oil, parmesan cheese, and fresh cracked black pepper. We split a lavender panna cotta for dessert and it was just delicious.

I have to also mention that this cafe is BEAUTIFUL and really clean and appealing.

I can't wait to come back here all of the time for the affordable coffee, beautiful pastries, and mouth-watering Italian gelato (some of which is infused with alcohol yay!).

I don't know if this place recently went under new management or something, but my recent experience here was vastly different than past visits. I used to really enjoy both the food and service, but I am sad to report that I will not be returning.

Our visit was during South Jersey's Farm to Fork week, which offers a $25 four-course pre-fixe menu. We came on a Saturday and dined outside. There weren't many other diners, except for a couple of tables inside. First, I ordered an unsweetened iced tea. When it came, I noticed that it looked a little cloudy. When I tasted it, it tasted like it had been sitting for a very long time because it was very bitter and just tasted "off." I didn't say anything because I'm not the type to complain about petty things and was confident that the rest of the food would be better.

We sat outside for over twenty minutes before the appetizers were finally brought to us. When my appetizer finally arrived, I noticed that it was cold. I was disappointed, because the menu didn't say it was a cold dish. It also tasted like it had no seasoning whatsoever on it, and I just plain didn't want to eat it - which is very unusual for me as I enjoy almost any type of food. This, like the iced tea, tasted like it had sat for a long time. 

When the waitress came to get our dishes, she asked how the food was. My mom had enjoyed her dish, but we did mention that I didn't care much for mine. She didn't say anything. We had an appointment later that day, so we politely asked if we could have the entree with the next salad course, as we were in a bit of a rush. The waitress said 'okay,' and then went back inside.

It was over a half an hour before our salads came, and when they did, the waitress explained that she asked them to rush our food but that they were "working as fast as possible" and the entrees weren't ready yet. We said okay and ate our salads. The salads were not bad, but definitely nothing to brag about either. It was a watermelon and feta salad, and I had expected at least some kind of green to go with it - if for no other reason than visual appeal, but it was literally just watermelon and feta. It contained more feta than we could eat in one sitting, so we asked for a box to take it home. 

It was at least another fifteen minutes before our entrees finally came. We enjoyed our entrees, and if the whole meal had tasted like that, we might have forgotten about the sub-par service. However, the portions were small, and although I'm a small girl, I left feeling hungry. 

But it was after we finished our entrees that things really went downhill. Our $25 meal was supposed to come with dessert. A male server - who seemed to have been a manager - came over to our table. We were already a bit turned off by him because he had been smoking outside - something I don't think an employee should do while diners are eating outside.

 He then informed us that because they had been "really busy last night," the cook had just begun making the desserts and they would take over an hour. He had known we were ordering off the farm-to-fork menu from the beginning, but only just then decided to inform us of this. He then said, "We do have pound cake, but it's not that good or fresh to be honest." 

Therefore, since there was really no alternative offered to us for the dessert, I politely asked if we could have some money taken off the bill. He seemed annoyed by this, which I really didn't understand because to me, it only made sense that we should get some kind of refund when were only getting 3 out of the 4 courses we were paying for with no alternative offered other than pound cake that was apparently stale and old. He then said he would take 10% off, which I initially agreed to.

After he walked away, my mom picked up a menu and noticed that almost all of the desserts were at least $5 a piece. If we were getting a 10% discount, that would only be $5 total off our bill, not the $10 minimum cost of dessert. Therefore, my mom went back inside and asked if we could get a bit more taken off the bill. The manager had a bit of an attitude about it, and then took more off our bill with a tone of voice that seemed to indicate he was doing us a big favor. 

So, after over an hour and a half lunch with below average food and service without a smile, I won't be back to this restaurant. It's unfortunate because I go out to eat a lot and have in the past recommended Kuzina's to several friends. In fact, when I taught a course at Rutgers centered around food, I also offered my students extra credit to dine here and write about it - which a few of them did. 

I love to eat out and rarely complain except in extreme circumstances, but this situation seemed to warrant my complaints. The staff was unapologetic and borderline rude. The food was not fresh, and honestly most of it was tasteless. I'll be taking my business elsewhere from now on, especially when Norma's and Cous Cous across the street offer great food/service

I came strictly because of the rating and this was definitely a time where the ratings was wrong! To begin, the service was horrible! I order oxtail, peas and rice, calaloo and a punch. I asked the man for a receipt or number and he said he'd call my name- it was printed from my credit card. I waited 30 minutes and realized everyone new was getting their purchases so I went and asked for my food. Lady asks what I ordered,  I tell her, she goes back and starts preparing the plate. I ask about the drink and she then pulls back the plate and was like I don't see your order. Now the whole time I'm sitting directly in front of the restaurant with my daughters while they're eating. I'm thinking like why would I make this up with kids in tow eating right in front of you, that would be a bold lie smh. But instead I told her that I had ordered from a guy and he's wasn't there. I pull up my credit card and try to show her on my phone where I paid and received a point from their store. She says well when that guy comes you should talk to him. She turns around and starts making other plates. Finally the guy comes back, I tell him the problem and he knew my whole order- partly because I asked him what he recommended. He fiddles around in the computer and pulls my order up. He shrugs, says oh sorry hands me the plate that had been sitting there and leaves. The lady never says anything at all. Now, almost 45 min later, I dig into my food and I'm instantly pissed! EVERY last piece of my oxtail is mostly fat and bone and in all my years of eating jamaican food- Never have I EVER had rice and peas made with instant rice! Plus the sauce was this weird brown gravy with carrots or sweet potatoes or something. I don't know but the whole thing was quite unpleasant tasting. All that drama and the food wasn't even good! This was very much one of the worst dining experiences that I've had in a very long time. I've had bad food before and come back to try other things, I've had folks forget my order and come back, but the fact that all of this happened in front of my children was slightly humiliating and for that, I'd never come back!

Ordered the catfish platter and it wasn't very good. At almost $30 with tax, it was probably the most expensive fish platter that I've had and not even the fries were memorable. Ended up giving it away to a homeless guy. I wouldn't recommend.

My Cheesesteak was absolutely delicious! I ordered it with mushrooms, sharp provolone, wiz and light mayo. I also added some of the fresh house made peppers. I see why they have such high ratings because they truly do have the best Cheesesteak that I've ever had. Next time I'm in Philly, I will definitely be paying them another visit!

I loved this cozy little wine bar! The service was excellent! The wine tenders knew their stuff and was great at recommending wines that suited your tastes.  I also enjoyed the little tapas that they had. We chose the dates and brie (see pics, I forgot the names). I highly recommend Tria whenever you're visiting Philly!

Sinfully delicious. You don't want to spend so much on desserts but they're worth every dime. I really don't even know what else to say other than to make sure you put them in the microwave like the bag/box tells you to so you can have an out-of-body experience. 

The sleazy brownie alone is so good that you want to kick yourself for not buying more. So glad they opened another location at Armature Works!

A clear case of an excellent, idyllic location overwhelming everything else so that service and menu never really have to break a sweat. Spectacular views of the Delaware and South Philly lull diners into a romantic hypnosis making the pricey, pedestrian menu almost an afterthought.

Service is glacial and your food may or may not be north of room temperature when it finally reaches your table making consistency an issue. If you're a foodie of any stripe prepare to be disappointed. However, if you love staring at skylines, nothing I can say will ever avert your gaze. Two stars for the view.

Unfortunately, the area surrounding the Liacouris Center in Philadelphia is a culinary dead zone. A few chains and the Draught Horse comprise some very thin options. Ahh yes, the Draught Horse - which for my money is simply TGI Fridays without the franchise fee. 

This flame broiled brew pub features meat of every description charred to whatever level of blackness you prefer. Unfortunately, if you are going to blacken meat in large quantities you better have the ventilation to back it up... ...unless of course, you're a forest fire Smokejumper from Nevada who enjoys a hearty meal with a layer of burning coal lingering inches above your head. This is the reality here that renders any discussion of the menu largely irrelevant. However, I remain particularly intrigued by the black lung happy hour.

I'm all for atmosphere, just not the one on Venus.

Perhaps they should have named the place Scorched Earth. I've been there twice and have returned home looking and smelling like a refugee from a house fire. C'mon guys, get it together - buy a better fan or at the very least, open a window.

I hate fussy anything but somehow I love it here. Could it be that the Turning Point always transforms breakfast into the best meal of the day. Yeah, they've gone full bore trendoid, offering an infinite variety of breakfast smoothies promising a thorough morning detox when all I really want is caffeine and a jolt of mood elevation but in the grand scheme of things, that's really small ball.

I came for breakfast and they've got that down cold (and hot.) Wonderful pancakes that I could never replicate at home and a parade of fluffy omelettes bursting with the freshest of ingredients. My tomato and mushroom was sheer bliss. Did I mention service? No need. it's always on point and never over or underwhelms. In fact, it's almost perfect and in these days of routine failure, and constant surrender to mediocrity that's high praise. Five stars.

There's a special burden for famous tourist destinations to live up to their hype or forever be consigned to the scrapheap of culinary fiction. In the hyperbolic world of New Orleans eateries, Café Du Monde has the proverbial target on its back. 

Its a shame because it shouldn't. Any trip to New Orleans and the Quarter would be sadly diminished without it. Beignets that allow you to float on a cartoon ribbon of powdered sugar bliss with a chicory coffee chaser that should and will be the highlight of your day. Café Du Monde is a treasure, next time you're in NOLA don't miss it.

At first glance you won't think much of this rough around the edges seafood shanty somewhere in the hinterlands of southern Jersey but Cap'n Cats has more than a talking parrot on his shoulder, he has some of the best seafood around. I'm partial to the broiled flounder and scallops but he can do fresh or fried done to perfection.

Don't be put off by the stuffed shark on the wall and nautical bric a brac straight from your uncle's basement. If you're looking for some great seafood in the least pretentious surroundings you can find, Cap'n Cats is waiting for you in West Deptford. Maybe if you're lucky you'll run into his cousin Cap'n Crunch drowning his sorrows at the bar. 

Most places try too hard, here's five stars for a place that doesn't try at all ... except where it counts, in the kitchen.

Not your typical Pullman Car diner or really anything "dinerish" at all. More like a small café with breakfast all day and a very nice BLT on toasted rye, crispy fries and freshly brewed iced tea. Service was fast and friendly so any complaints were few and quickly forgotten. Five stars for being in the right place at the right time.

Normally the presence of grease, cheez-wiz, provolone and surly service in the same sentence dooms the offending establishment to the Yelpian oblivion of zero stars. However, when you're navigating Philadelphia's famous quadrangle of Passyunk Avenue where Pat's and Geno's cheesesteaks ladle their magic out by the ton, they easily become your favorite meal of the month. 

Normally, you wouldn't get me near canned mushrooms much less the science experiment they call cheez-wiz but together they conspire to delight my pleasure center even though they bring more greasy ooze to Philly than a convention of Elvis impersonators.

I prefer Pat's but just barely. Truth is I love them both. I'm just waiting for McDonald's or Wendy's to discover the Cheesesteak and turn it into a test kitchen abomination wolfed down with gusto in flyover country. Am I the only one who thinks the McRib sucks. Besides, I still haven't forgiven Sarah Lee for ripping the soul out of the humble bagel. An easy five stars when only the original will do.

Alma de Cuba walks the line between elegance and fustiness with aplomb. Both beautiful and welcoming this five star treat hits you right in the pleasure center delivering on all fronts -  effortless service, inventive cocktails and a menu that restores your faith in anything that doesn't have to coast on their reputation.

I could go on for days about their Royal Date appetizer and Seafood Rice entree but why bother, go discover them for yourself as you indulge in a dining experience that is both rare and worth every shekel.

"We start with free roaming chickens who live a life of leisure and contentment." I'm always amazed at the eulogy some places will extend to their pampered, pre-homicidal poultry. They're usually dead when I meet them so the real question is... how does the unfortunate cluck taste in the afterlife?  At The Eagle in Indianapolis, it's downright amazing and when paired with their Mac & Cheese you'll have a comfort food feast.

The place is crowded and loud with service that is swift and professional. Who cares if they crank it out by the metric ton, they have the formula down and that's all that counts. I'm not big on "institutions" but The Eagle is more than deserving of their outsized reputation and rapturous reviews. Let me add another five stars to the pile. A great meal well served.

They almost lost me with the mash-up massacre that is Canadian import Poutine and reeled me back in again with a perfectly prepared and plated breast of duck. 

Roberts Block is a terrific addition to this leafy burb floating between the ying and yang of always popular comfort food and more adventurous upscale fare. Well appointed with a strong service spine, they really don't have to worry. 

So what if you want a burger and your companion wants sweet potato bisque and the pan seared scallops. If both are done well, that's a formula for five stars. A return visit is guaranteed next time we're in town.

No lookie-loos, no bikers and no undulating swarm of eager charm seekers left New Hope to the natives and a few lucky visitors on a random mid-week visit. Where has this place been the dozen or so times I've been forced to endure the invasion of the Ralph Lauren Khaki Klownshow that usually makes this on the Delaware hamlet a living nightmare.

Luck was with us that day and was also smiling as we popped into the Triumph (micro) Brewery for lunch. A few regulars held court at the bar and the dining room was wide open as we surveilled what I assumed was a more limited pandemic menu. 

We left 70 minutes later having been treated to a marvelous coconut curry soup and a delicious combo of fish and chips and a pulled pork sandwich that we shared and devoured. All was superb.

If memory serves, there was also a very tasty blonde pale ale involved. Aren't blondes always at the center of the action. For one brief shining moment New Hope was ours, khakis be damned. An easy five stars.

In my experience most Jersey Diners remain stubbornly enigmatic places - unapologetically trotting out massive menus and international cuisine palates with often questionable results. 

So here I am at the Red Lion ordering a fried crab sandwich already knowing that a cheeseburger and fries would have been a much better choice. The lump of grease-laden sog staring back at me confirmed all my suspicions. On a brighter note, the french onion soup was terrific.

Most Diners have a lane (breakfast, burgers, sandwiches and comfort food dinners) so when you ask them to draw outside the lines, the results are charitably "mixed." 

So five stars for that burger or chicken salad sandwich that would have been amazing, if only I could restrain myself from drawing outside the lines. My bad.

No surprises, Cheesecake Factory is Applebee's in a tuxedo. Sure you can order steak, salmon or a salad but the star of the show here are the waistline busters - mac & cheese, sliders, egg rolls and a complete menu of "glamburgers." Of course you'll want to stick around for a Hummeresque slice of cheesecake to make your gastric-bypass trifecta complete. 

Heck, they do what they do with a smile and the food is uniformly well prepared. Frankly, they're a little too rich for my blood but if you're out to put yourself in a Thanksgiving food coma you could do far worse. Four stars.

A sure sign of life, one of Philadelphia's great restaurants (and a personal favorite) is opening this week for take-out. While I'll miss the sublime atmosphere and service, the menu alone is going to make me grab my mask, jump-start my car and make a beeline to Philly. A good day.

If you agree with the proposition that if a restaurant can feed you one mouthful of exquisiteness then it's worth whatever the market will bear. On that basis alone, Barclay Prime should be considered the best dining value in the plutocracy.

The food here is outstanding but in portions so obscenely small that Barclay Prime is the literal incarnation of steakhouse porn - so keen to be chic and unpretentious that they are literally drowning in both.

The design of the space is impeccable as is the service with presentation as crisp and understated as I have ever experienced. You'll soon discover that you're no longer dining but participating in a ridiculous performance art ritual as you indulge in whispers of steak and rumors of side dishes. It was so amazing, that I couldn't wait for it to end regardless of the cost to purchase my freedom. In fact, that may just be their genius.

Honestly, I'm very aware that this place is swimming in accolades and awards but for me the entire experience was stilted in the extreme. First and foremost my expectation for a night out is to relax with a great meal and to enjoy the company that I'm with.

Barclay Prime is a gilded fishbowl that left me cold. By rights the service and the food were exquisite and demand five stars but I am leaving one off for personal preference. Nothing personal.

My beloved Chatime. Situated in the middle of nowhere of all places. Sorry if you're offended if I call Tucson middle of nowhere...but it is! 

Brown Rice Milk tea w/ grass jelly like always. Tasted like what I'm use to. WIN. 

Great big tables for people to study in here. Plenty of parking. 

Lots of fobby mandarin speakers if you want to spruce up your mandarin.

What a poor experience, and I didn't even try anything. 

Came here the other day for happy hour, which is advertised on the website as going until 7.  When we were arrived, we were told that it recently changed and is now only until 6. This didn't work for our group as several people had not arrived yet.  We pointed out that the website didn't state that, and that if that was the case, we would likely not be staying.  The manager offered to extend happy hour until 6:05- how unhelpful is that!   We decided to take our group elsewhere.

I don't understand a restaurant that would rather lose a group of 8 than give specials currently advertised on their website.  I will not be coming here again.

I really can't say enough amazing things about Time Market.  They recently had a remodel to both the store and the menu.  The bar is now much more inviting, and they upped the amount of beers on draft. For all you local lovers, they carry several Dragoon beers!  And the patio that used to be covered in vines has been opened up and feels much more like a part of the place.  The menu boasts several fine pizza options, and an awesome greek salad to accompany them.  My current favorite pizza is the Phig.  Figs, caramelized onions, prosciutto, and arugula combine to make one delicious pizza.  

I only wish I still lived across the street!

Finally!  Street food at street prices in a charmingly converted row home on W Girard Ave.  It seems like a family-run business serving traditional Vietnamese items with a modern, tapas style flair.  The menu ranges in price from $2.50 to $7 for everything except the wrap-your-own summer roll platter at $15 (for 2).  The portions are on the smaller side, but it's to be expected given the price point.  This is most definitely the kind of place to share a meal with a friend & some tequila while still being kind to your wallet.  

The vermicelli bowl was my favorite.  I had the chicken version that was marinated pieces of chicken thigh (I think) over rice noodles with veggies,  spring roll, cilantro and fish sauce.  Fresh, delicious and filling, yet not heavy.  The dumpling app was served steamed with a tasty dipping sauce.  Spring rolls in the vermicelli bowl were traditional but the "net roll" version was more like crispy tempura-ish bites.  Flan was amazing.  I'm a sucker for flan though.  Full stars for the selection versus price point for quality eats.

The seating is somewhat limited with a few tables & a counter by the window downstairs.  They have a second floor too, although I'm not sure if that's open yet.  It's byob with mixers and juice for purchase.  Delivery will be up soon on Grubhub, yay.

What a delicious sandwich spot!! Love how you can turn all sandwiches into salads.  A huge selection and variety of sandwiches for any mood you could possible be in. Beer, wine, champagne also available. 

They also had some s'more kits for purchase, including a gluten free one, which was great because I picked one up for a friend who has celiac, who I happened to be having dinner with later.  

Local 6 packs of beers also available for purchase to go.

Note there are only 4 or 5 tables inside, so if you want to dine in, you may have to wait.  But on a nice day, get some carry out and go sit in one of the nearby parks to enjoy :)

Guru undoubtedly has the best butter chicken in Edmonton.

I enjoyed lunch at Guru as part of the Yelp Staycation, where we got to try butter chicken, along with the beef vindaloo, cauliflower 65 and naan. Everything was good! That butter chicken though was good x 100: the creamiest, smoothest and best tasting butter chicken ever!

The appetizer, the cauliflower 65, was incredible. Deep fried and saucy, it reminded me of chicken wings (random, I know) and I could have eaten an entire plate of this all to myself!

I loved the drinks too - chai is always a great drink, especially when eating Indian food, and the chai at Guru was tasty. I also had the opportunity to try mango lassi (smoothie) and I would definitely have that again! It wasn't too sweet and it was colourful, cold and smoooooth.

The entire experience was great. The place is clean and classy looking. I loved the art everywhere and there was a cozy vibe about Guru that was very comfortable. 

Service was good and we loved that Chef came out to chat with all of the tables there at that time as well.

The Melting Pot is a great experience when you're looking for something different. You're in for a fun dinner with your two hour seating.

We went as a foursome on a Monday night. Even on Monday, the place was packed! You'll definitely want to make reservations a week or so ahead of your ideal time to make sure you can get in. 

The four of us all went for the dinner that includes the cheese, salad, main and chocolate for around $51, the 4-course experience. 

With four of us we got to choose two different cheeses, two different broths for the mains and two chocolate fondues.

We went for the four cheese and the baked potato for the cheese round. Holy amazing. the Quatro was my fav and we almost powered through all of the bread, veggies and apples that came with it.

With this dinner plan, everyone gets their individual salad. Four choices were available but I'm almost always a Caesar salad girl. This one was great and a nice fresh break after the cheese. 

The Hubba Hubby and I chose two different entres with the idea that we would share them. We went with the classic, which came with five different meats (steak, chicken, shrimp and pork) and the French Quarter, which has shrimp, sausage and more. Everything was fantastic. The angus steak was amazing, as well all of the chicken. We were really rooting for the steak all round but the chicken really surprised us with how amazing it was!

You can't go wrong with chocolate and we went with the original (chocolate and peanut butter) and the flaming turtle - a flambé style with chocolate, caramel and candied pecans.

The food was five star all around. Service was a solid 3.5/4. It took a long time for plates to be cleared off and even though the gentleman with the water would visit all the tables around us, we had to flag him down several times to stop at ours. And why is the Manager combing his hair where I can see him?

Overall I would definitely be back as it would be fun to go for a romantic evening, for a dinner with the girls or with your parents. It's a nice dinner to relax and connect over while enjoying incredible food!

Reggie was awesome & friendly, served me a nice bubbly Rosè.  Two days ago, also had excellent service & food!  Sometimes tho, I've noticed the bartender slow & gone for a long time w/ no one in the restaurant, won't name him.  The hostess is a sweetheart also.  

The Rotisserie Chicken Salad Slider was delish!!  Very nice roasted chunks of chicken, fresh lettuce, tomato & the perfect amount of Dijon Truffle Dressing on a soft Brioche roll.  Nice olive, cocktail onion & cherry tomato garnish.

Patatas Bravas w/ Pickled Jalapeño were absolutely beautiful.  Firm colorful little tomatoes & jalapeños w/ a nice dressing.  A must side dish! 

Lamb Stew Au Gratin was very hearty & a perfect Irish Signature Dish.  Loved it & soak up the bread mmm!

Tasso Hushpuppies comes in four.  Sweet & savory w/ sweet corn, pimento, cheddah fried w/ honey cane syrup. 

My driver told me that Public Service was where you'd pay your electric bills a long time ago.  Every where here has history & I love that you can walk to so many places.  The sidewalks suck & need help like the potholes in the roads, but the food has been delicious so worth it.

Next time will try the Crab Cake Rex which looks like a Scotch Egg wrapped in crab on top of Avocado, Roasted red pepper & corn w/ aged balsamic & hollandaise.  

BEST IN NOLA FOR: 
All three & possibly the Crab Cake Rex since about four orders go out.

Excellent service, although at first it was slow.  We weren't in a rush, but once our waitress got to us she was great.  

Pecan Crusted Trout was absolutely delicious!  I highly recommend it over the bison which there well-known for.  I've had the Bison Meatloaf & this time Roast.  It was good, but not compared to the trout.  Our waitress said her fav was the Turkey dinner & that it was like Thanksgiving so may have to give that a shot next time! 

If I'm ever in this area again, I will surely stop by to dine.  Excellent location too!

Excellent quick service, right in front of our gate & next to the outdoor smoking area.  Ordered two eggs over easy, bacon, hashbrowns & toast.  Bland & totally overcooked brittle bacon & hashbrowns.  The toast was buttered well, but that was all that was good besides the coffee.

Po'boy, salads, soups & breakfast, lunch & dinner.   Delicious & quick.  Very friendly & excellent food.  It's like that Alice show really, when the chefs yell at each other lol, but all is great!  

Regulars dine here all of the time ordering Spaghetti & Meatballs, Hot Sandwiches, Green Beans you name it.  There's a chalk board w/ specials also.  You can sit & order or head to the cashier & Order.  Slot machines are in a corner also.  Breakfast was excellent so don't judge the spot. Enjoy it.  

Ordered the Hot cakes which are pancakes not Johnny cakes, delish & fluffy!  And the breakfast sandwiches.  Also a Corona lol!  The table next to us ordered po'boys that were huge shareable!  Looked delish for next time!

Arielle was fabulous!  Thirty minute wait as it rained outside, and well worth the wait.  

iighly recommend the Corned Beef Hash Benedict.  Beautiful rich flavors we nearly licked the plate clean.  

The Croquet Madame was good not great like I've have before smothered in Bechamel, it was like the two French Toast w/ Brioche, ham & cheese topped w/ an over medium egg.  It needed that Bechamel oozing off of the top w/ the egg.  Served w/ fries of course.  

Washed it down w/ the spicy delish Bloody Mary & tried the Ruby Slippers mimosa which has pulp so not a big fan.  

They also sell souvenirs & text you when your table or bar seat is ready.  Looking forward to next time! 

1.18.18 Brought my parents in for breakfast.  Delish Spicy Bloody Mary & Irish Coffee to drink.  Ordered the Peacemaker which means you mix & match two of their Signature Benedict's.  We both did the Corned Beef Hash, one w/ the Fried Chicken St. Charles (it was ok) & the other was the Shrimp Boogaloo Benedict (it was also ok).  They also serve 'The Trifecta' which is the three Benny's I chose.  Next, I'd like to try the Migas.  

Mom & I bought two black red studded Ruby Slippers t-shirts that sparkle which were $35/piece.  Our server was totally awesome, our table wasn't totally clean & I put my name on the wait list through Yelp. (cause there is almost always a line) Easy!

Excellent family restaurant.  Everyone's food looked delish, fresh bright fruit, crispy potatoes & a bag of where they order their grits so it's not boxed Cracker Barrel type.  Very cute artsy decor & friendly servers.  The older gentleman seating customers was very accommodating & while people waited outside he brought them coffee.  Awesome!  

Ordered the Steak & Eggs, 2 Eggs Combo w/ Bacon, Crispy Chicken & Pancakes, Turkey Bacon Pancake Sandwich!  Absolutely delicious home cooking!  I highly recommend all four.

I went to the Row this weekend and was very happy to see that a new restaurant occupied the old Pie in the Sky location.

This is a great place to go if you are in search of a late night bite.  The decor and atmosphere is fitting of the current trend of Southern food in Nashville.

My friends and I sat at the bar.  Service was great.  I had the Grapefruit Fizz.  Grapefruit vodka, soda water and some lime was all I needed to hit the spot.  Priced at $7.50, I found the drink to be priced fine and very refreshing.  Wine by the glass can go as low as $6.00 and there is a great selection of local beer on draft.

We split two appetizers.  The Stuffed Sweet potatoes with Pulled Pork were so good.  Great flavor profile and very easy to split.  The fried green tomato app was very good too.  The cornmeal was spiced just right and the pimento cheese side was really good.

The live music is another draw for me.  I have to say the music, good service, ample parking and patio is going to bring me back.

I. Love. Lee's deli! 

I stopped here originally while visiting my boyfriend  in town about 4 years ago. Since then, we've gotten married and Lee's Deli is one of our favorites! I always always order the Rule Breaker with salmon and shrimp. It's such a filling, but not heavy, sandwich. Salmon, shrimp,broccoli, carrot, green pepper and cheese on a classic French hoagie bread - you can't go wrong! I order it with the fries and it always comes with a sweet/spicy sauce. It's a lot of food for the price too; I always split it between two meals. Yum!

My husband usually orders the same, but this time he ordered a spicy buffalo chicken cheesesteak. He gives it 8/10 - not perfect - But still very good! He says it was missing something, but he isn't sure what LOL. 

I also got a piece of carrot cake for my husband. The place is cash only, but since we used their ATM, they gave us another piece of carrot cake for free! (He loved the cake!) They are always so nice when we visit and for that they went from 4 to 5 stars! We will continue to go back!

My husband and I (who live downtown) were craving the Amighetti's special, so we were so excited to see that the location on Manchester Rd. was open on Sunday! We also didn't realize that this location is their test kitchen, so while we were both able to order the traditional "special" sandwiches, we also got to sample some other items, like the kale salad and vegetable soup. Both great, and to be honest, it was great to see some updated, fresher, more healthy items. I'd love to go back and try some of the other items on the menu!

The staff was great, checked on us frequently, and seemed to genuinely want feedback on some of the new items.

What a great little taqueria on Magazine Street. Came here on Cinco de Mayo and had a really great experience heightened by 1/2 price margaritas and tacos!

Tacos you basically can create your own way with choices of a plethora of ingredients on the menu. Maragritas come in every kind of conceivable combination. My favorite is the pineapple habenero for a nice kick!

Place is festively decorated and their selection of tequilas is very impressive! They had an awesome live flamenco  guitarist when I was there which added to the lively scene. 

Highly recommend Ãrana Taqueria Y Cantina for deliciously authentic mexican food and creative margaritas. 

Tip: go for happy hour when tacos and margaritas are 1/2 price. Well worth it!

THIS PLACE IS INCREDIBLE!!!! So much so I had to start by shouting about it. It's the best new (to us) restaurant we've tried in at least a year. Seriously. 

Because of corona, we decided to order takeout (they have a toasttab account so you can easily order ahead for pickup at whatever time you like, as long as they're open). They called us when the food was ready, brought it masked up to our car, and even told us a little about our dishes. In addition to the friendly super awesome service, which is pretty impressive considering we didn't even step foot inside, we were truly blown away by the beautiful attention they put into their food. 

We ordered:
- guac (& also got chips, salsa, & a red & a green hot sauce)
- taco carnitas (fried pork tips w/onion & cilantro)
- taco arabe (grilled pork w/herbs, lime juice, onions & salsa)
- taco chorizo con papas (Mexican sauage & potatoes with Oaxaca cheese) 
- chicken mixiote with charro beans, creamy Mexican spaghetti, & homemade flour tortillas; and
- enchiladas poblanas sauced in pipan verde with refried beans and arroz (rice). 

Everything was better than the next, but I have to say the chicken mixiote was among the best dishes I've had in my life. The chicken was so tender it was shocking. Even the cartilage was tender! We've been dreaming of making the one hour 49 minute drive back for that alone. Seriously. If you live in Indy, appreciate home cooked food, and haven't tried this place yet, you are hurting yourself. Please fix this problem immediately. You won't regret it.

Please note I went here SOBER..Wow, it's been almost 3 years since I didn't eat here. 

Since I work close by, I decided to break my boycott, and get an old familiar.

Bad news is I think it's frozen hamburgers (didn't ask, but could see them on the grill) from Smart and Final (thanks Drew for the picture!) now whereas if used to be fresh ground meat from Blue Ribbon Meat in Sparks and was cooked to order. 

It used to be 1/2LB burger, way back was 2 burgers, then it went to 1 giant 1/2 burger, and now appears to be a frozen 1/3LB from Smart and Final (thanks Drew - see his review and picture). I asked for it cooked medium, and was told it would be medium to medium well, and I said I prefer medium. 

It came out well done and hardly any juiciness to it. It's okay not tasty by any means. However the fries were familiar being abundant although not much seasoning and were actually crispy. 

The last part is it used to be $5.50 when I was last there, it's now $9 plus tax. So my review is really based on the fact it used to be anywhere from 2 stars to 5 stars and now it's, "Eeh Me Thinks Not" since it used to be a different price, ingredient quality, and taste. 

I would eat there again (no rush), but probably peruse the menu vs. getting a burger I could make on my grill direct from my freezer.

I have been wanting to try Smiling With Hope Pizza (SWHP) for some time, but the hours are different, so you have to strictly plan a visit. 

I arrived and expected to see some people with disabilities working, which I was excited to see, but there were none today.
