I ordered to go at the window, $20 for an 18-inch pie which is the basics (nothing organic), no toppings. I already studied the menu before coming in, so I knew this. I got 3 toppings, Sausage (made in house) Pepperoni and Mushroom ($2 ea.). I asked for the cook to be well done. The nice lady said it would be 10 minutes. 

When I arrived the cashier inquired about how I found them, I said Yelp. She mentioned they had an award on the wall. I didn't think much of it because I thought it was local, but it's actually national, so I definitely give them props for achieving this feat! 

My pie arrived I would say 10 minutes, and I was off. I got home and dug in, and it has a good flavor. The two standouts were the sausage and crust, both were excellent in taste. The slices were so you have New York style slices (Huge). It was very floppy in the middle, so next time I will have them cook it even longer. 

I enjoyed the flavors, but price point is a bit high for me. Out the door with a tip was over $30. I think this is a high price point for a few reasons, the place is not convenient unless you live on this side of town, it's open restricted hours, and it was a good pizza, but it's not super cheesy, or a ton of toppings, so much of your experience is the crust. 

Lakeridge is affluent, so they might be pricing for the area, but this pricing would be a treat for many people. The fix is setting up some deals, specials, happy hour, frequent visitor club, etc. as I am sure the owner wants to share his home with everyone, not just the affluent! 

Last, I like the fact they are helping people with disabilities, but I expect to see them working if that's the theme! Also, I would like to know more about the reason for this theme, the connection to the owner, etc.

1st experience today, I parked downtown, the minimum meter is $1.50 for 1 hour, 1st time paying for parking to eat, that didn't really set me back, to me it's all about good food! 

I arrived wasn't sure if I sit and order, so I asked a passing employee, she told me to order at the counter. No biggie, I am an aficionado of Chicken Fried Steak, Biscuits and Gravy, today wasn't super hungry, was recommended, "The Reggie" which is first posting on the menu. 

I sat down, then I saw a card that says, "Please bus your table". I was already instructed I get water by myself, and for me I really don't enjoy this. I'm old school reno, and I have been a busser. 

With that being said, I usually pre-bus and or bus my table at places such as Deux Gros Nez, because of what DGN created, it's like giving back respect, and knowing the place was small, service was FANTASTIC. 

You would see people working their a$$es off, usually, 1 person taking orders - making drinks and the other was preparing food, we would do whatever we could to support people, who had to frequently go downstairs to get ingredients, etc. 

I am happy to support people working their asses off, to make their job a bit easier and happy to tip 20%, 30%, 40%, again this is due to great food, EXTRAORDINARY service, and a place we stayed at for hours. It was a Reno Social Network - Pre Internet! I say all this because when I ordered my food, it asked me for a Tip, and the lowest, "Pre Selected Amount was 15%". I did 15% as it was my 1st time here, not knowing what I was about to find out. 

The only service you get is food delivered to your table, not even silver wear is given. I find this kind of dining quite shocking. The food was okay, not mind-blowing, but 100% tasty! I would eat here again! 

I just want to show that 2 Stars is for a Reno food veteran and I don't think to ask for a tip is even reasonable, considering the lack of service, I feel insulted actually. How awkward for myself and the employees. I really feel they should just call your name and keep it classy with everything else, and have a tip jar for those feeling especially generous.

Lastly, if it wasn't for this whole tipping thing, and some actual service I would have been 3 stars. In case you are wondering, I did bus my table, like a good employee! 

To me you EARN the RIGHT to have people SERVE THEMSELVES, you DON'T ASK! Also, they better be paying $15 an hour to all the workers, since they are not really earning tips, nor should they! Really Pine Street Biscuits, should just have an app or a screen like McDonald's and call your name, it would be more justified.

Lastly, the water tasted soapy, they don't rinse the glasses properly.

I really like Juicy's, but I watched a young blonde lady handle money and then immediately proceed to prepare and handle food. I cannot support nor eat a place that doesn't care about sanitation! It's sad because I was really digging Juicy's again. 

If you are going to ask, yes I witnessed personally, no hand wash, no hand sanitizer, nor any gloves, just straight from cash register to grill and food prep area (bun, lettuce, tomato, cheese to the cooking burger, etc.) Fortunately and unfortunately Juicy's allows full view of the people cooking too bad they don't ask that people follow Health Code, or I would be a regular!

If you haven't checked out this Reno Gem, you are surely missing out! Since my last reviews (Jan '14) I have eaten here at least 100 times, and mostly like many more. I can say this place is CONSISTENTLY AWESOME and DELICIOUS! . 

$8.99 AYCE buffet in which EVERY DISH DELIVERS, EVERY TIME! If you want the BEST EXPERIENCE get there at opening 11 AM, when everything is SUPER FRESH! 

If you are lucky enough to try the FISH PAKORA'S when they first come out, SAY HELLO TO A LITTLE PIECE OF HEAVENLY DELIGHT! 

There is always ample seating and parking, warm friendly service, and food that is simply FANTASTIC....ALL=WAYZ! 

TIP: This might sound strange, but if you like Ranch, try a bit on some salad after your meal, it's cooling and has an incredible flavor!

So glad to have found yet another great, authentic, Southeast Asian restaurant today. 

Great food and good service with a smile.

The lamb and chicken satay were both excellent. Great sauce on the chicken and the lamb was tender, fresh and perfectly grilled. 

Shrimp rollade was yummy. 

Grilled pompano was the standout...spectacular. Moist, perfectly marinated. Great accompanying sauces, and crisp delicious skin. I couldn't leave a crumb and even ate the fins . So good. 

Soto Betawl was also awesome. Tripe melted in my mouth and the broth was light yet interesting with depth. 

Tamarind soup side was just like we make it at home.

Left very satisfied for a fair price. 

We'll be back!

Terrible terrible SERVICE. Food is acceptable but this restaurant is not ran well at all. Maybe the owner will read this and get things turned around.  I know on this Sunday afternoon I was not the only customer unhappy.

From California, I was visiting my family and we went to Slate Bleu for dinner. It was Mardi Gras, Fat Tuesday, and we expected a full restaurant but were surprised to see it empty. We were first told that they could not accommodate us without a reservation and then told we could eat upstairs... We were seated and waited at least 15 minutes before anyone acknowledged us. Finally we were brought 2 tiny bowls with 10 peanuts each. More time passes and we ask for some bread from another server. For 5 people they brought a small basket of cold bread. Our oyster appetizer consisted of shells with a tiny puddle of slime in the middle.. I have never seen a worse presentation (although the sauce they served with it was unique and good). Two of us ordered Jumbalaya... came out looking good but was extremely bland... seemed like maybe they forgot to season it. My nephew ordered a steak medium well and it came out literally raw in the middle.... that was sent back and he sat eating 10 peanuts and french fries. Finally yet another server arrives and we informed her that the Jumbalaya was not up to par. Her reply was "yes it was". When I attempted to explain our discontent, the server's reply was "SHUT UP". We asked to speak to the manager and she stated that she was the owner. The next response was "Get the f*** out!" I had my 2 nephews there and could not believe her language in front of them. These harsh responses were uncalled for. My sister told her that the food was simply not up to par and asked why her response was so disproportionate and inappropriate... again we were told to "GET OUT". The whole experience was completely bizarre. We wanted to pay for the food that we did eat but the owner was completely unresponsive to any reasonable conversation. 

Needless to say we will never return there. Horrible, horrible service.... bland, poorly prepared entrees, and  unstable staff.

One of the better sushi restaurants in the city!

My friend has been raving about Fuji to me for over a year now and so we finally went a few months back. I have seen this place many times before since I frequent the vietnamese restaurant that shares the same parking lot. Needless to say Fuji had a lot to live up to because of the consistent endorsement that I kept hearing from my friend.

I ordered the Cajun Poboy Roll (crab, crawfish, and tempura shrimp) and the seafood fried rice (my friend said I HAD to order that rice). The sushi was exceptional. The rice was delicious (I could of ate an entire pot of that rice). We then ordered bubble teas. 

Great service from the staff. They were all friendly and most seemed to recognize the regulars. Small cozy restaurant that serves amazing food. Looking forward to my next visit!

Wonderful bagel shop! Came here the other day after not being here for probably a year or so. The quality of their bagels is the best around. Freshly made bagels that are just perfect. Easy to bite through and then it is chewy and dense in the middle. There was a bit of a wait when I went this past Thursday as the shop was busy. Ordered a poppy bagel with jalapeno cream cheese. If you like things a little spicy you won't be disappointed with the jalapeno cream cheese. Just enough kick to be noticeable. 

Overall love this place. Wish I lived closer to it as I would be a regular. All of the local and federal mandates during this time were being enforced (social distancing, masks required, etc) so that was much appreciated.

Fantastic service. Donuts that just don't quit.

Believe the hype! 
Donuts, sliders, and brew!
The name says it all.

My favorite seafood restaurant in the city!

Service is quick and the staff is very knowledgeable (Erica is really great). The food is always wonderfully flavored and the seafood is some of the freshest in the city. This not your typical seafood restaurant. Atmosphere is great as well. GW Fins is also one of the better places to go for special occasions as they really go out of their way to make you feel special.

Menu Highlights:
- Biscuits (try them and you'll love them too)
- Sizzling Oysters (juicy, plump, and delicious raw oysters)
- Bedford Sea Scallops (large succulent scallops served atop a mushroom risotto)
- Scallibut (scallop crusted halibut)
- Parmesan Crusted Flounder (my personal favorite)
- Pompano (perfectly cooked fish!)
- Lobster Dumplings (amazing starter dish)
- Creme Brulee (about as good as creme brulee gets)
- Chocolate and Caramel Bread Pudding (fantastic)
- Mashed Sweet Potatoes (an excellent side dish)

Great wine list! 
Perfectly cooked food!
Excellent service!
GW Fins rocks!!!

Chris Lynch is the new chef here and he has raised the standard. This is a place that serves pretty much just breakfast food all day. They do have sandwiches as well if you don't want breakfast food. 

John is always a pleasure to deal with. He is knowledgeable, helpful, and friendly. Some of the other staff are not so patient and helpful. Service is very inconsistent between the staff.

I eat here a couple times a month and have not had anything bad. The Tuscan Style eggs are my favorite though. That dish comes with two poached eggs over a vegetable ratatouille with a creamy polenta at the bottom of the dish. This is one of my favorite breakfast dishes anywhere in the city! Their steak n eggs are served with sauteed mushroom and these crazy good fries (oh and the steak is cooked medium-rare unless requested otherwise).

Probably one of the smaller restaurants/cafes you will ever run across. Seating for about 25ppl max inside this little cafe. So definitely don't come with a large group.

Still the best steakhouse around!

Ruth's has many locations around the country but Ruth's feels like a local restaurant to me. Maybe because it all started right here in New Orleans. The menu has some options if you don't like red meat but the reason you come here is for their delicious steaks. Cuts include filet, ribeye, t-bone, porterhouse, and New York strip.

Wonderful service almost all the time I come here. Mark really knows how to treat his customers and has been there for over 20 years. Ruth's also has a wonderful happy hour from 4pm-6:30pm every day except Saturdays. Happy hour choices include tuna, steak sandwich, burger, chicken sandwich, crab beignets, and spicy shrimp. I've had all of their happy hour choices and all are great. Each is only $9. Of course happy hour wouldn't be complete without some tasty cocktails. Happy hour drinks are also all $9. 

Come here for amazing steaks, a great happy hour, and outstanding service. There are more expensive steakhouses around but for me Ruth's is quite perfect!

Verti Marte is a French Quarter institution. No make that a New Orleans institution. If you haven't been to Verti Marte you haven't experienced a wonderful food emporium. Their menu is exhaustive and the food is excellent.

What are you in the mood for? Craving fish, chicken, or bbq? You want breakfast instead? Chicken Parmesan more to your liking? Come to the Verti Marte. They have it all. Literally! And all this awesomeness is located in the back of a convenience store.

If you want a sandwich I recommend the "All that Jazz" or "Royal Feast" poboy. The Philly Cheesesteak sandwich is top-notch too. An All that Jazz is loaded with ham, turkey, shrimp, grilled mushrooms and tomatoes, wow sauce, and cheese!! The Royal Feast comes with turkey, roast beef, ham, pepper cheese, olives, grilled onions, and wow sauce. DA BOMB!! I eat here way too much but the food is so good I can't wean myself away from this place.

Service is usually quick and pleasant at the deli counter. Sam Hartfield is always working the register and he is very diligent and patient. The store is uber small. Like two aisles small. The deli is located in the back of the store. Open 24 hrs and delivery is available to limited areas.

Everyone that lives in this area comes here because the food is unbeatable and the prices are just right!

I was a little disappointed with Cafe Adelaide. We were so excited to try this restaurant out for the first time after being told by Commander's Palace that they couldn't accomodate our entire party for brunch. I made a reservation here during Christmas week for 11 people and from the beginning it wasn't meeting our expectations. Once we were seated it took more than 10 minutes for our server to come by and take our drink orders. Our server did not seem to be in any big rush to take our order. Once we were able to finally order our food we waited for the great equalizer....FOOD! A great meal will make almost any service deficiency seem like a distant memory.

Most of my family ordered either the shrimp and grits or the boucherie biscuit. None of us thought either was a hit. The shrimp and grits were lacking in flavor and the boucherie biscuit wasn't the best combination of ingredients (pork, poached eggs, creole mustard slaw, and country gravy all served over a biscuit). The soup du jour was a blue crab and cauliflower soup that was excellent! And their bloody marys are top-notch too! I'm sure I will be back at some point but as far as first impressions go it sure was lacking.

The W hotel is intimate and very well appointed. The lobby is small and  beautiful. The rooms are beautifully decorated and their courtyard is one of my favorites in the whole Quarter (I adore many of the numerous courtyards that the Quarter has to offer). The staff here is wonderful! From the valets to the desk staff to the housekeeping staff...all of them pleasant, helpful, and professional. 

My friends and I rented a room during Memorial Day weekend for three nights and we were sooo glad we picked the W! Brian and Staci were amazing during our time there! The nicest employees in the Quarter are the W staff!! This may very well be my new favorite French Quarter hotel.

Seriously kickin' wings right here!!!!

Some of the best wings come out of this diminutive shop next to the Blockbuster and Shell on Claiborne.

Become a BEAST at Bayou Hot Wings! If you dare.

Recommendations: If you like spicy sauces try their ultimate Bayou Beast sauce. Or their Bayou Sweet Heat if the Beast is too hot for ya. If you don't like hot sauces try their tame Bayou Sweet sauce. Not a wings kinda guy/girl....get the Bayou Burger. It's big, flavorful, and delicious!

Love it here. Great people. Great wings. Inexpensive food (10-pc wings or the bayou burger are both under $7).

I love The Harbor! It's my new go to spot for me and the crew from the hotel. We love it here for many reasons. Krista, Lacie, Vito, and Makala are all so friendly and awesome! Love everything about this bar. Great drinks, reasonable prices, and wonderful service. Love this bar!! Get the Harbor burger.

This place totally suprised me. I thought the decor would be bland (it was quite intriguing) and the food uninspiring (food was delicious). Was I wrong!

I ordered the Redfish because our server, Andrew, gave it a glowing recommendation. The fish was tender and yummy. The crabmeat added on top was just an unexpected bonus. My friend ordered the Shrimp and Grits. I had to try those grits and boy was it amazing! I have never been one that craves grits but damn those grits were divine. I could eat grits every day if they tasted like those grits. The shrimp were plump and full of flavor. Our dessert was the chocolate bread pudding and it was a great dessert even though it didn't taste like bread pudding to me. 

Overall, I was really impressed with not only our food but the service as well. Andrew was such a wonderful server. He was very descriptive when describing menu items (which I like). Even though this is a high-volume restaurnat Andrew was very attentive to us and we were never in wanting. 

I will definitely go back here again and try the Shrimp and Grits and more.

This place is NOLA's well-kept secret in the restaurant world. This place is what is best about our city. Small, charming, yet innovative in their food preparation. My friends had the Roasted Chicken and the Seared Tuna. They thoroughly enjoyed both and said they were cooked to perfection. I had the Filet which was served with polenta, rapini, and this balsamic sauce......mouth-watering!! Creme Brulee and Banana Split for dessert. We were in heaven :D

Gautreau's is quiet, charming, and has a wonderful atmosphere. Service was great! What's not to love in a place hidden in a residential area!

If you want to be on Bourbon in the middle of it all there are only four hotels that face Bourbon St. The Inn on Bourbon Ramada, the Chateau Bourbon, the Bourbon Orleans, and the Royal Sonesta. The Royal Sonesta is the grande dame of Bourbon St. and the clear choice if you want to stay in the heart of the madness.

The Royal Sonesta has it all. A welcoming and helpful staff, a beautiful lobby, a restaurant, coffee shop, bar, and a business center. The best pool deck in the city is also found here. It even has Irvin Mayfield's Jazz Playhouse located in the lobby. Come out on Wednesdays to hear Irvin. 

I stayed here again this past weekend with some friends. Normally it is expensive to stay in the Quarter. Rooms are usually $359+ for rooms facing Bourbon. We paid $249. 

Our room was nice but a little small. We had a room facing the pool (as requested) and although the rooms are a little dated it serves its purpose. As long as it was clean we are cool with the room. The beds make the room though. They are great!

Kudos to Denise for having such a great staff and a wonderful hotel in the middle of one of the most popular streets in the world.

Yes I'm in love with Crabby Jack's!!! I used to come here often when I worked at Ochsner down the street so I'm definitely missing my frequent trips there. This is my FAVORITE casual joint in the whole city! 

Best bets: 
- shrimp poboy (best in the city)
- duck poboy
- roast beef poboy (2nd best in city IMO)
- fried green tomato w/shrimp remoulade poboy 
- couchon de lait poboy

They also have fried chicken, seafood platters, and other favorite foods. Most of their portions are huge!! GO SOON!!!

This is one of the best vietnamese restaurants in the city! They have the absolute best service of any vietnamese restaurant. David does a wonderful job of keeping and training his staff to be quick, polite, and helpful. I come here often because everything is so fresh here and the Pho is just about perfect. I usually get Pho but some of the other items I've tried have all been really great too: Chicken wings w/ butter, Orchid fried rice (combination fried rice), Vermicelli w/ egg rolls, and this sliced beef w/ nuoc mam sauce (aka DB4).

It gets really loud and is very busy during lunch so come for dinner if noise and crowds bother you.

Pho Orchid is definitely worth a trip out to Metairie if you're wanting excellent vietnamese cuisine.

Decent food and service. They serve breakfast and dinner only but they also have a cafe that is open all day and a bar that sells small plates. The cafe serves sandwiches and salads. 

I have had the sausage sliders a few times here already. It is served with pickled onions and green onions. One of the better sliders I have had recently. The steak sandwich is a great sandwich but kind of expensive ($15). My favorite dish, though, has to be the braised pork belly. Pretty moist and delicious. 

I have only had breakfast once here and had the boudin benedict which came with two sausage patties topped with poached eggs, collard greens, and a hollandaise sauce. Got it with some potatoes on the side. Really good dish presentation and the taste and texture of this dish were both good.

Vacherie is a nice new addition to the area!

Given the shortage of Burmese restaurants in New York, we had to try this place for their mohinga. Their mohinga was so good, we came twice just to have it again. During dinner on a Saturday, the restaurant was busy but not crowded. We were easily able to get a seat for two. The next day for lunch, we were the only ones dining in the restaurant, but I saw many take-out orders.

For dinner, we ordered the mohinga of course, which is listed on the menu as Festival Fish Noodle Soup. It was chock full of flavor with added substance from the noodles. I've only been to three Burmese restaurants, but this place has my second favorite rendition of this dish.

In addition to the mohinga, we ordered the Thousand Layer Bread w/ BBQ Beef skewers, the Banana Leaf Fish, and the Ahnyh Tamin (shrimp paste fried rice). I enjoyed the skewers and thousand layer bread which tasted similar to roti canai. The Banana Leaf Fish consisted of a whole fried fish covered in a sweet curry sauce. I didn't enjoy the fish as much since it was too sweet and tasted too much like Thai food. I wouldn't order the fish in the future. Out of the three, my favorite was the shrimp paste fried rice. I am a little biased though, since I adore shrimp paste fried rice in general. If you like briny-tasting foods, order this fried rice.

The next day we came for lunch just to order the mohinga. There was a little mix up because we asked to order two bowls of it. But the waiter misheard and gave us one bowl and two small bowls to share the dish. In the end, we also ordered the tea leaf salad to fill our stomachs. The tea leaf salad was tasty with all the different textures, but I would have preferred another bowl of the mohinga instead.

Good brand of quick sit down eating. A great place for happy hour with their $5 appetizers and drinks. The portions for the appetizers are perfectly portioned for small tapas style eating. Sat in the outdoor bar service area. Not five stars because they seemed too busy and only half the tables were full in the bar area. On a scale of ok (red lobster/Olive Garden/ Cheesecake Factory) good (, great (Ruth's Chris/ Lauriol Plaza DC) and gotta eat here (The palm/Roy's Hawaii) The food remains good. Do yourself a favor and do happy hour here. See photos. We got two sangrias, burger, shrimp, kids broccoli and fries, and two salads for $35. Great for the price.

I needed Pho in my body ASAP. I'm feeling a little under the weather with a headache and sinus problems so I decided to see if there was anything close to me on here and Sriracha popped up. They have such great reviews I was already there in my mind.

This place is great. There is no where to get  Pho or Vietnamese close in south Nashville so I'm beyond excited that this opened up. They also offer a Japanese menu as well, so that's a plus! 

The BF and I shared the tempura shrimp and egg rolls. They came out hot and crunchy with great dipping sauces. 

I got the Pho with rare beef, beef tendon, flank, and beef balls. Do you know why? Because it was only $8.00. They gave me some extra chili  because I love mine spicy and it cleared my head. I have so much left over as well. I also got the Thai tea which you can't go wrong with that deliciousness. 

The boyfriend got the bento box with the Bulgogi (marinated beef), gyoza, and a crunchy shrimp roll. It also came with soup, salad, fried rice for an extra $1.00 and veggies. He even had left overs too.
The Bulgogi was succulent and tender. GET IT. You won't be disappointed. 

All of this came to a whopping $33.00!  
At this price, we decided this will be a staple in our rotation every week. Thank you for having something in the neighborhood that's delicious, easy on the wallet, and not to mention great service!

What a wonderful discovery!!!! I'm on a personal journey of searching and sampling vegan cheesesteaks because isn't that what you do in your spare time?!

Goat was wonderful. I went for an early solo dinner and met a group of welcoming staff, especially my waitress Emily.  So cozy inside, the decor was pinterest worthy and the staff walking by would make small talk. I appreciated their warmness.

My meal consisted of the Seitan cheesesteak, the house made pickles and a side salad.  The cheesesteak was delicious, full of flavor, requiring zero ketchup, a rarity for me.  The roll was fresh and the onions were on point!  The salad...yum!! The raw sunflower seeds with green goddess dressing was a great side to my cheesesteak!  Oh and those pickles...Goat has their pickle game on lock!!! Curry, kimchi and garlic carrots were all delicious and fairly priced at $5. 

If not for Yelp, I would have never come across this hidden gem.  Situated in a small shopping center I couldn't predict Goat being so damn adorable inside.  Perfectly quaint, I hope to see this place thrive.  I'm not sure about the area, as I've never even been to this area of Wilmington, but when you have such wonderful service/great product...how can you not succeed?

I adore restaurants that cater to both meat eaters and vegetarians alike! While I look forward to trying more of that scrumptious looking menu I'd like to request a menu addition....Seitan Buffalo Wings.  Please!? 

5 stars deserved, see you soon Goat!

I'm a real Korean (as in someone who grew up there and still speak business-fluent Korean), and my opinion is that this is the best Korean restaurant in Tucson. In fact, this is a rare gem that actually has a Korean chef, which is difficult to find even in Koreatown in L.A.

The downside is that the two ladies are very overworked, and tend to be irritable. They cook and take orders all day... so I caution people from judging too quickly until they have had the chance to try out the food. Yes, the main lady was also rude to me on my first visit, but she turned out to be a very nice, caring person.

The upside is obvious-- you're treated with genuine Korean food here, cooked by a real Korean foodmaker, on a shoestring budget. I love the fact that they have high quality side dishes and sometimes "bonus sides". If you're craving Korean food in Tucson, then this is a must-try.

One word: phenomenal. I had the most incredible dining experience at Texas de Brazil - which was particularly exceptional because I had no idea what I was getting myself into.

Having purchased a Groupon for this restaurant, my husband and I stopped in while we were in the area. We had assumed we would go in and use our gift certificate on some appetizers and maybe a few drinks and be on our way. Not so much.

**For those of you who may find yourselves unexpectedly sitting at a table unsure of how the process works and reading this review on your phone, here's the run-down:

1) Light Dinner - $24.99 per person: Includes the salad bar, but no meat. Drinks (both alcoholic and non-alcoholic), dessert, tax, and gratuity are not included.

2) Dinner - $42.99 per person: Includes the salad bar and endless meat. Drinks (both alcoholic and non-alcoholic), dessert, tax, and gratuity are not included. 

*Prices for kids: 2 and younger - free; 3 to 5 - $5.00; and 6 to 12 - half off the regular dinner price.

*Discounts: They offer a military (active member and veteran) discount of 15%. This can be used for up to 6 people.

*This location is not currently serving lunch, but I was advised to check back in the future as they plan to offer it eventually.

Once you're seated and your server has explained the process to you (which is a lot to take in and, if you're anything like me, you'll probably miss most of it anyway), you can go to the salad bar. You're given a card; one side is green and the other is red. When you're ready for the meat, flip your card to green. 

You will quickly be bombarded by skewered meat-toting gauchos vying to empty their succulent meat onto your plate. Let them. 

Fillet mignon. Flank steak. Bacon-wrapped chicken. Bacon-wrapped fillet. Parmesan chicken. Sirloin. Lamb. Pork. Sausage.  All of it is unbelievable. They also bring out fried bananas dipped in cinnamon (it doesn't even make sense how amazing they are).

When you're done piling your plate for the moment, flip your card to red and they'll leave you to eat in peace.

Even though we were caught completely off guard (and found ourselves feeling more than a little awkward at first), the friendliness and level of professionalism of the staff (not to mention the exceptional quality of the food) quickly put us at ease. This was definitely the most exceptional meal I've ever had.

"Worst experience ever"
Being from New Orleans I've frequented this restaurant since I was a little boy. Today changed my experience forever. I had several family members in town so I had to suggest Deanie's. Big mistake, The service was horrible, Food was unseasoned and serval dishes was cold, French bread was hard, 4 days old hard. When we mentioned it to our server she immediately dismissed all of our concerns and said there was absolutely nothing that she could do. "it is what it is". So when we asked to speak with the Manager to address our concerns the manager came over with an extreme attitude and also defended the poor quality food and service. There are several great quality seafood restaurants in New Orleans and unfortunately Deanie's in my book is no longer one of those places. I would not recommend it. Disappointed is an understatement. Save yourself the dissatisfaction.

What do you get when you combine a good beer, good pizza, your fiance and you Dad? One heck of a good time.

This is what we had when we went to the WILD GARLIC! 
If you don't care for garlic, they can accommodate you, but if you love garlic, welcome home baby!

This location on Mt. Rose St. has limited parking. If you pull into the lot and it's packed, don't go away! There may be parking on the street. 
Be careful when crossing, some of those cars think it's interstate 80!

We were greeted with a nice smiling gentleman by the name of Billy. He welcomed us and requested our drink order. My fiance had the Citrus Mistress IPA by Hop Valley Brewing and I had the Tangerine Wheat by Lost Coast Brewery. My Dad had a diet soda. The drinks came and he took our order. 
1. House Salad with Italia
2. 1 Large pizza with red sauce, garlic, sun dried tomatoes and sausage.

While we wait for the salad to get here, if you haven't been to the Wild Garlic before, you will be perplexed by the large bottles of real honey on the table. Why is there honey? Well, it's for the pizza crust! You don't have to have it, but it's like having a little dessert after each slice of pizza!

The salad was fresh, crisp and cool. The plates were warm but the salad was good. We ordered it with Italian dressing.

Very shortly, after the salad the pizza was delivered! Wow, did that look good! It tasted great and a good crust too! Garlic on a pizza is good, but when it's baked into that same pizza, it's awesome! Served with small cups of ranch for dipping, there's not much better you can get!

---------------
Bottom Line

Yes, I will be coming back. Not the cheapest but it's worth it! You get good service, good quality food and a great comfortable environment!
Come in an order a good pizza pie!

It's been a long time since I've been WOWed at a sushi restaurant. 
Reno tends to have a lot of good sushi places. Some better than others.
Who'd think that a great place for "all you can eat" sushi would be in the desert of northern Nevada!
One of the better places is Hiroba Sushi.
When you first walk into this store front shop, it is non assuming. The environment is standard Reno sushi fare. 
You walk through the door and the employees greet you. My wife and I were asked if we would like a table or the sushi bar. 
We chose the sushi bar.

Our first order was spicy tuna hand roll. As we were looking at the menu for other tasty items, the hand rolls were delivered to us. 
It wasn't even a minute! This must have been a fluke. But, we ate the hand rolls and surprise #2. The tuna was Spicy! The first restaurant in Reno to serve something spicy and it actually was spicy!
YUM!!!
We ordered another roll and another. Finally, the test, we ordered two salmon skin hand rolls. Normally, an item like this takes 5 to 10 minutes to prepare. In less than 5 minutes, it was on a serving dish and we were munching into it. 
The wrapper was crispy and fresh. Not gummy at all!
The same can be said for the salmon skin too!
I like this place. 

Finally, after we had our fill, we ordered something that caught my attention. The Challenge roll. What is this roll? I'm not sure, but it did have 2 peppers next to the name.
Jalapenos, Habaneros and other things that bring a tear to my eyes.
The roll was good and tasted like the peppers it was made with. It didn't have a lot of other flavors and honestly, I wasn't looking for those other flavors. I wanted spicy and that's what I got!
The first piece was good but the second and third piece was, well this is the best way I and describe it. I could see tomorrow. 

Bottom Line
----------------
Oh yes, this sushi place is one that is on my list. Come hungry and prepare to be wowed. 
Great service
We were not waiting for any sushi!
Fresh fish!
We will be coming back to this one! Great job Hiroba Sushi!
You will be seeing us again!

I like a good Chicago dog.
I want the strange looking relish, those delicious peppers and about 3 points up on my blood pressure!
My wife, dad and I have been waiting for a Taste of Chicago to open its location by the river. Once it opened, we figured we should give it a week or two for the crowds to dissipate. 
Finally, my wife and I drove by their location. It wasn't busy. There were only three people inside. Hmm...

The following week, we went there. 
Parking can be a pain. 
If you can't find parking on the street or bridge, you can always try your luck at the Cal-Neva parking garage. Though, it's a decent walk, think of it as burning off some hot dog calories. 

We were given a few menus after we entered and told to place our order at the front counter. 
It was a nice menu. They had dogs, pizza and other Italian types of food.
My wife wanted the eggplant Parmesan sandwich and my dad and I got Chicago dogs. 

I went to the front counter, as I was told. I was greeted by the "owner?" She was nice enough but abruptly told me to go to the bar to order. The front counter was closed and she would have to re-open the register again. 
Hmm (that's twice I hmm). I stared at her for a moment and she took that as I didn't understand, so she proceeded to tell me again! Obviously, I went to the bar and ordered. 
The man behind the bar, took my order and got most of it correct after telling him twice. Then when we got the order, it was missing one dog. My G*d! Do I speak so poorly when I said "three" that it sounded like "two?"
Hmm (uh oh, three times! Or, was that two?)
I didn't say anything. I was friendly and was looking forward to the dog(s).

The meal came out in a reasonable time frame. A bit long, but reasonable.
A big no no happened in the kitchen. The dogs were wrinkled when they came out. A sure tell tale sign that they've been sitting off the heat.

The eggplant Parmesan sandwich was pretty good. The dogs were pretty good, aside from the fact they were wrinkled. That did not look presentable at all.
Hmm (too many times!) 

I know that a food truck business is a lot different than a brick and mortar store, but if they don't get their act together soon, that store will be vacant again. 

Bottom Line
---------------

-sigh-
It has promise and I may try it again.
Going for them, a full bar.
Against them, they don't know how to run a restaurant. Not yet.
Dogs are cheap, if they are wrinkled, toss them. 
I'm paying for a good experience.
What I got was not quite the experience I was looking for.

Finally a Boba place in Tucson that is done right.  Coming from Taiwan, it's hard to find a Boba place that offers the authentic taste in the area.  Most places, you can taste the powder in the drink and sometimes when not mixed right, the dry power gets sucked up, giving you a nasty experience.

Selection is good.  A nice mix of options including the amount of sugar to put into your drink.

The place offers Free Wifi, allowing you to enjoy the tea and work at the same time.  Staff is nice and very courteous.  The drinks can sometimes take a while to come out, but it looks like the staff is still in training.

They don't have a sign up on the store front yet, making it a bit difficult to locate for the first timers.  Hopefully that will change soon.  They are located next to the Szechuan Restaurant on Campbell and Ft. Lowell.

I had been to Karlton Cafe once before with friends and it was a very good experience. Food was great, service was fast. I was hoping it would become a favorite go-to since it's right in town and within walking distance. I was also very excited to take my husband for his birthday, raving to him for weeks about the place. But after today's experience, I don't think I can ever bring myself to go back. We walked and arrived around 10:05 am on a Sunday. It was far from being packed. We got right in right away and seated. Our order was taken approximately 15 minutes later and that's when things started to go awry. The couple who was seated at the same time ordered, ate and left and we still hadn't been served. A couple who came in 15 minutes after we did, ordered, and was served and we were still waiting. We finally asked our waitress if she could check on our order and was met with a "I put the order in immediately after taking it ma'am". I didn't imply that she hadn't. I was just asking for her to check on it since we were still waiting and sometimes things get mixed up. We ended up waiting approx 50 minutes before we were served. Two of the orders were wrong. We had ordered two omelettes with prosciutto, red peppers and manchego cheese. We were served something with asparagus and ham. Our other two orders were ok, but the pancakes were a bit burned. Finally our omelettes came out but the home fries were not cooked all the way through, to the point of still being raw/crunchy. We let the hostess know as nicely as we could that we were severely disappointed with our experience. That was met with nothing but a sorry. So we paid (full price, no comp or percentage off offered) and on the way out, my husband asked for the owner who happens to be the chef. He relayed his experience and that was met with a "then go find some place better". Needless to say, I don't think that is very customer friendly and I am severely disappointed by his attitude and unwillingness to keep us as paying customers. And overall, I'm really disappointed because I had a good experience before and hoped to make it a regular stop for us.

Went with a group of seven to La Fourno on Dec 17, 2011.

My son ordered the Gnocchi with Marinara. It came with grated cheese on it, which he cannot eat. We told the waitress, who sent over the manager. He said, "This is an Italian restaurant. Everything comes with cheese on it. What would you like to do?" We asked for gnocchi, this time without the cheese. We weren't warned, but we were charged for both dishes.

My wife ordered the Penne Pomodori - described on the menu as "chopped plum tomatoes, white wine, basil and fresh garlic." My wife asked that it be prepared without the garlic. What arrived was penne in what looked and tasted like the house marinara sauce. Not a single bit of chopped tomato was visible. When asked, the manager insisted that pomidori means tomato in Italian and that's what we had been served. The manager again asked what we'd like to do. We asked for the Cappelini Olio & Aglio (without garlic) instead. When the bill arrived, we were charged for both the Penne and the Cappelini.

Why didn't we raise a stink? Because we were out with friends for a celebration and didn't want to embarrass the other guests.

The place is a ripoff. Don't go there.

Went again. Casino itself was awesome. Games were fun. My beef with the casino is 15% of the games were out of order... That can't be good for business. 

My 2 stars is for the F&B service and food... We ate at Ryse ( or however it's spelt)

1- the food was unacceptable. If I'm buying a 12 dollar sandwich, I will have high expectations. Those expectations were not even close to being met.

2- service was atrocious. Our server was too busy doing side work to wait on us. Waited for sides, plates, refills, and everything else you can think of.

3- the "chef" was too busy leaning over the expo counter and joking with the cooks to read the tickets... And it showed when my sandwich came out wrong. But no server checked on us, so I ate it anyways

4- the FOH manager ( at least I assume she was seeing how there were 6 servers crowded around her like she was giving away money and everyone was joking around) was completely worthless. No tables touched, not one. Not even the elderly couple that we listened to complain for 5 minutes. We watched the server tell the "manager" who chuckled and watched as the elderly couple stormed out. It was a sight!

5- the hostess stand is pointless when you are not welcomed. It was more like "you want to eat? Fine, how many...". 

All in all, IF we come back, it certainly won't be for F&B. As a seasoned F&B operations manager, I'll tell you this... Someone needs to be fired.

Gray's is like the guy you want to date, but he isn't into you. 

I really want to like Gray's, but it's so incredibly expensive. 
Some of their sides are out of this world, but the entire experience is overpriced.
It's kinda like an upscale college campus bar, honestly.

Literally my husband and I each got a drink, and we shared the Buttermilk Fried Heritage Chicken meal, which wasn't filling and ended up leaving with a $60 bill (which didn't include tip). WOW..... 

DO NOT MISS OUT ON:
* Fried Pimento Cheeseballs, like dear God these are incredible.
* Charred Brussels, honestly I don't even like brussel sprouts but these. mmmmmmm.

The music and vibe is great. If you have unlimited funds, this could totally be your place!

This is for a to go first time order of pad Cee ew. SMALL dinner portion! Flavor was bland and not what I expected when I paid $14. 
Lose another star for no napkins or forks for a to go order.

I've only been here once, but it won't be my last. I would come back here simply to eat the grits. Wow. 

Everything we ate was delicious.  The grits were hands down the best grits I've ever eaten. We got them with sausage, roasted red peppers, avacado, and cheese. We ordered 2 other dishes but couldn't stop eating the grits long enough to dig into the rest.  The waffle was amazing and the breakfast burrito was awesome too. 

But those grits though....

If you are craving coffee Crave Coffee Bar would be a great place to get your caffeine fix. The interior is sleek, modern, and spacious. 

I came here for one reason. They had a drink called a marocchino which I had never tried before. It's a lovely layered concoction of espresso, frothy milk, with your choice of caramel or chocolate. I went with the traditional chocolate. The drink is served hot, in a small glass. It was a beautiful presentation and the frothy milk helped balance out the strong espresso. The chocolate added some depth and sweetness to round out the drink.

The pastry selections looked too good to pass up so I also had a plum crosta. The pastry was light, flaky, and I liked the balance of tart with sweet flavor in the plum filling.

Service was friendly enough, and the drink was made in just a few short minutes.

Neo Brooklyn style pizza! I love the idea. While on vacation it's a bit of a trip ritual to get some local late night pizza to go and eat it back at our hotel room. We had an 18" Margherita pizza.

The pizza was a hefty portion! It was indeed like a hybrid of Neapolitan and Brooklyn style pizza. The slices were large and the crust thin like a Brooklyn style pizza, but was a bit more pliable with more of a tender chew to it like a Neapolitan pizza. The pizza was so good that the toddler picked up a slice (The largest one of course) and licked it to claim it as hers. She is learning early on in life about pizza property rights!

I appreciated that the fresh basil was in a bunch off to the side of the pizza so you can add it right when you eat it. Some of the basil was a bit tired, brown and wilted looking though but overall it still tasted good. 

If we're in the area we'd definitely stop by again.

P.S. Check on YouTube for owner Scott Volpe's extraordinary acrobatic pizza spinning skills!

Got an order here to go. We had to call twice to get someone on the phone. We placed an order for chile en nogada, and a green chile chimichanga enchilada style. It was ready in about 20 minutes and was well packaged.

I was excited to try the chile en nogada. I had heard about this dish from the novel Like Water for Chocolate and it is typically a dish served at special occasions. The poblano pepper was roasted, peeled, and stuffed with picadillo, covered with a cream sauce with pomegranate seeds on top. The picadillo for this dish had ground beef, apple, walnuts, and spices. The combination of lightly sweet flavor with the pepper and cream sauce was interesting, but the filling needed a bit more salt to balance out the sweet flavor. 

The green chile chimichanga was a massive size, coated with green chile sauce. It was fried lightly crisp and filled with a lot of green chile and pork.

The order came with some freshly fried chips and salsa which were a good accompaniment to our meal. 

If I'm in the area again I'll come back to eat in and try more dishes.

Perish the thought of not going to The Parish while we are in Tucson! I had this restaurant bookmarked forever and I figured now was a good time as any to try them out. We placed an order to go. I had the shrimp and grits and shared some pork rinds. Everything was securely packaged for the trip back to our hotel room.

There was nothing shrimpy about this meal. It was a hefty block of fried grits, with plentiful shrimp, collard greens and coated in sauce. It did require true grit to try to finish everything in one go (I failed at this challenge). Overall, my meal was decent. I liked the greens and the idea of a fried grit cake is unique and was a nice balance of textures from the creamy soft interior and the crispy outer crust. I'm not sure if it was due to transport time but the shrimp was way overcooked by the time I dug into my meal though. 

The pork rinds were light and crispy. I enjoyed the seasoning on it. Next time I get food from here I'm going to try their gumbo!

Where else in Tucson can you dine at a restaurant visited by Madeleine Albright, Jake the Snake, Goldie Hawn, Adam Richman from Man vs. Food, and even one of our Presidents? (No not our current one)

I had heard so much about Mi Nidito from TV shows and had wanted to eat here for a long time. After reading reviews I knew I'd be in for a wait no matter what time I came. We got here around 8:30 on a Friday and the wait was about 35-40 minutes for a party of 2. 

The whole restaurant has a cozy but festive feel. There's a lot of dim yellow lighting and brightly colored decor. Waiting close to 40 minutes gives you a lot of time to look at the menu so I knew  that I wanted the famed President's Platter, the very meal that Bill Clinton had feasted on when he visited Tucson in 1999. It comes with a beef tamale, birria taco, chile relleno, bean tostada, and chicken enchilada. After eating it I can see why he needed to have a quadruple bypass surgery! It was a hefty amount of food for sure. My favorites were the taco and tostada, but unfortunately the giant bed of lettuce plated underneath them caused them to have (In a Mary Berry, Great British Baking Show voice)... A Soggy Bottom. No one wants a soggy bottom. 

Despite it being so busy, service was pretty good. We were checked up on as needed and drinks were refilled frequently. 

I felt quite presidential afterwards from our budget surplus due to the reasonably priced food. My saxophone skills are yet TBD though but I certainly felt like someone who could be nicknamed Bubba after eating all that food. 

I'm glad I ate here and tried their famous platter but for me this will probably be a one time visit due to the wait times and the plentiful supply of other great Mexican restaurants in the Tucson area.

We were looking for a good breakfast spot near our hotel and saw the good reviews for this restaurant. Plus, I got a kick out of the fact that it was called Jerry Bob's. It doesn't get any more diner-like than that.

The restaurant offers comfort food with some Southwestern elements. There were quite a few people waiting for a table when we got here around brunch time but the wait was only 15-20 minutes for our party of 6. I had the chilaquiles. I knew I was at the right place for this dish when the server asked me if I wanted them crispy or soft. I've never actually been asked this when I've ordered them so I appreciate that I have options. I went with crispy because I don't like soggy chips.

It did take a while for our meals to arrive since it was so busy. When they did arrive one of our orders had the sides switched but our server was good in notifying us shortly after we received all our plates. The chilaquiles looked delicious, with the crispy fried chips smothered in smoky red chile sauce, with a moat of refried beans, some sliced avocado, and over easy eggs. I liked all the components together and the dish was just the right amount of crispiness for me.

Service was friendly and splitting checks was no problem.

So I'll be honest. We got takeout from here primarily because it was one of the few places that were open on Thanksgiving. We actually tried to order from 2 other restaurants before hitting Thanksgiving jackpot with Sher-e! Much like any Thanksgiving meal we were quite stuffed by the time we were done and I definitely needed to nap off all those good eats. 

We shared the mushroom chicken, chicken biriyani, mixed vegetables and some naan. It was all very securely packaged for takeout in a mix of white paper box (Plain basmati rice) and round plastic containers for the curries and biriyani. The naan was wrapped in paper and foil. 

I loved the seasonings and spices in each dish. We requested it mild spice and I felt they delivered just the right amount. It was still a little spicy but just a subtle little hint of it in each entree. The white rice was soft and fluffy and while the biriyani was good flavor wise, I thought the rice was just a tad overcooked. The naan itself was a little unevenly cooked as one piece was still a little doughy in the center but had black charred bits in the thinner parts of the bread. Seems like the oven it was cooked in was too hot perhaps? 

Portions were plentiful and it was enough to satisfy 2 adults and one toddler with leftovers to spare. If I were craving Indian food, whether on a holiday or not, I feel like Shere-e is a solid choice.

This was definitely a very nice restaurant from the excellent service to the nicely appointed decor throughout.  We made reservations and were seated immediately upon arriving.  We started out with the seafood gumbo and oysters on the half shell R'Evolution Style. For our entrees we had Shrimp & Tasso Risotto, River Oak Redfish and the 8 oz filet.  Everything was so good and can't wait to return in the future.

This is a good place to go especially late when you just want some comfort food.  When we went in there were seats which I was surprised since it was kind of late.  We had the bisquits and gravy, very good and a waffle.  The waffle was pretty good.  It's off Dumaine and it's close to everything.  Service was good and our food was cooked to order.

We went to Louie yesterday at 5:15 to have a few appetizers and drinks and we were not allowed to sit at the bar unless we were ordering dinner and the restaurant was not full at all at that time.  It looked really nice and were told by others they had the same experience.  So sorry we could not stay.


One star is cause we were not permitted to place my order.


Sb
Great food. Decent amount of vegetarian options. Space is small so seating is limited. Cash only so come prepared. I'll definitely be back.
Chicken broccoli cheesesteak is very good.  Salmon cheesesteak. Come w shrimp and veggies. Carrots, broccoli fried onions green peppers!  Great eggs and bacon.

I'm surprised I never left a review for Sampan, seeing how I've dined here on several occasions.

The food itself is amazing and always on point. I've never walked out of Sampan disappointed in how little the food portions are or what horrible service I've had -- the alcohol and happy hour are very generous, especially for those who work 9 to 5; however, being in the medical field, I'll sadly was never able to attend but when dining at dinner, the alcohol that is poured is very, very generous aka I'm somewhat drunk walking out. Classy, I know.

I'm a huge fan of the kimchi fried rice and pot stickers! The adorable mini ice cream is also my favorite. I've also made a reservation this Thursday to bring a girlfriend that's never been before so I know she's in for a treat.

Sampan's architecture and interior is also to die for and a great addition on 13th street.

My little sister dragged me here for Korean BBQ, hearing over reviews from her friends and my experience there was nothing but horrible, as well as irritating. 

We asked for a table for three, only to be taken to a room shared by another party we didn't know, so staring at complete strangers in a room is awkward. Very, very awkward. The staff could've asked us if we were okay with this, rather than assuming we'd be okay with it (we weren't, but I didn't want to make it a big deal so we sucked it up and stayed) -- when we ordered, our server who didn't make any sense whatsoever kept pointing at different photos and nodding, basically pushing us and deciding what we should eat, rather than allowing us to make a choice and scoffing at what we wanted to eat, by then I wanted to go home but because my little sister wanted to eat and was hungry, I didn't want to be a party pooper.

It wasn't until our server yelled at me for using too much butter to cook the meat in. EXCUSE ME, SIR. THIS IS AMERICA, I CAN USE AS MUCH BUTTER AS I WANT. THANK YOU. He snatched, yes, snatched the tongs I was using to flip the food in and thought he was doing me a favor by basically cooking things for me and shoving it onto a plate. He did this throughout the entire dinner that my appetite was no longer there and I wanted to leave.

Food wise, we had the fillet beef, beef short rib, onions, some vegetables which was okay. Not meh, not amazing but eh. I could've made it at home.

I've always passed Philly Cupcake and thought it was a jewelry store due to all it's lights! I was curious but shy to enter it and you bet I was surprised when they sold my second gluttonous sin: Cupcakes! 

When I first went in the store for the first time, I was greeted by this adorable woman who asked me if I need help and if I didn't, just call her. Oh boy, was I tempted to buy everything in there but had to stop myself. It would kill me on my track team, besides my members. Anyway!

I bought this delicious rice krispie treat and a doggie cupcake for my dog Max (which you can see in my photo) 

I love Philly Cupcakes!

This is the latest iteration of a restaurant in this location (formerly it was The Vine) and it is a great addition to the scene on Main St. and St. Charles. It is a tapas and wine bar and both foci are done very well. The wine list is one of the better ones in the area, up there with Prasino. It is weighted heavily in CA, with a smattering of French and South America choices. Prices are anywhere from $26 to $90 so you should be able to find a selection that will match your budget. Highlights (in our opinion) are Siduri, Duckhorn, Rombauer, & Domaine de Cristia.

The array of tapas choices is impressive. There are flatbreads, dips, risotto, and others. Our favorites are the mac-n-cheese and the spinach & artichoke dip. Prices are fair and portions are generous. We did not try one of the desserts but we will next time.

This is a step up from the bars on Main St. and is a great choice for a date night or a nice bottle of wine on the patio watching the world go by. We will be back and we hope you will support this great place!

Tower of Pizza provides a great, Mom & Pop Italian restaurant atmosphere, and some truly exceptional pizzas!

Their pies are made fresh to order, so sometimes there's a short wait - you'll find the wait worth it though, because of their exceptional quality :-)

Everything necessary to a great pizza pie will be found in the pizzas here - the crust is just right, the sauce is Devine, and the cheese & toppings are 1st shelf - you simply can't go wrong!

I suggest you be sure to order extra, because the leftovers will make a wonderful breakfast :-)

Like most people who live in and visit this area, I've walked by Cane and Table many times, without having a clue about exactly how good their drinks are.  For starters, they have hands-down the best Hurricane to be found in the Quarter; it's made in-house with fresh ingredidents and no mixes.

In point of fact, the reason all the drinks here are exceptional is the that everything is house-made - even the Coconut Cream (their Pina Colada is to die for!).

Their drinks are STRONG, and generously sized with a kick like a Mule, and if you're going to have more than one it's best not to driving ;-)

Tip: In particular, their rum-drinks are sublime - their daiquiris are among the best I've had in recent memory.  

While I've been here a handful of times, I've never tried any of their food other than a couple of their small plates.  Of those, my hands-down favorite is the Tostones (Twice Fried Plantains, Pikliz, Habanero, Salsa Verde), but you can't go wrong with anything on their small plates menu.

Went here on a cold Friday at 8pm.  We were walking so parking was no issue for us.  Got one of the last tables, we didn't have a reservation.  It is a very small place and the service was good and the prices were reasonable.  I ordered the ravioli with meatballs and my husband ordered pasta with pancetta.  Both dishes were very good and the portions were perfect.  I got chocolate mousse for desert.  It was just ok.  It seemed like it was not made in-house. I would recommend this place but not on a cold night.  The only reason for my 4 star rating instead of 5 is that the dining room is small and every time someone arrives, the door opens and a gust of cold air flows through the dining area.  They keep the temperature warm in there, but it is not enough to offset the cold when the door opens.  If you are dining with more than 2 people you probably need a reservation.  I will go back again but definitely not during the winter months.

Skip this place and go to one of the other choices in town like The Keg, Acacia, Flemings, Vivace, The Abbey, The Hub, Janos Downtown Kitchen, you get the idea....even Taco Bell would be better at least you will get what you payed for.

We had New York Steak ( it comes served with green beans and potato purée) and Halibut steamed in parchment on rice and started out the meal with the tomato soup and a wedge salad.  The soup really was watered down pizza sauce - tomato-y but not great soup and the 'wedge' was really four small pieces of iceberg lettuce (they don't appear to understand the concept of wedge) with lots of bacon and blue cheese - would have been okay but the lettuce was brown both from age and from being cut definitely not worth $10 save your money.

The food was okay - not worth the price as the serving sizes were small and the prices large when compared to other restaurants.  The steak was cooked perfectly for doneness but was slathered with butter prior to serving obscuring the taste of the meat.  (If you want a baked potato be prepared to shell out $6 as it is not an option with your meal.). The parchment cooked halibut was so loaded with lemon it tasted like dish soap.  (The rice had peas and carrots mixed in - okay but not special with and no added vegetable - some asparagus or beans or spinach would have been nice.). The kitchen should learn more is not always better....

All in all, add one $12 glass of wine and you are $125 in the hole and really not satisfied.  That said, the waiter did what he could with what he had, the violinist was a nice touch, and they work hard to make it look like a nice restaurant.  The service was good.

One tip for the owner - clean up the patio where everything is stored and covered with tarps? Tablecloths? it is a mess and when you are not the one looking at the mountains you get to look at the umbrella with no canvas, and the other crap stacked along the wall on what could be a beautiful patio with nice landscaping.  It probably wouldn't hurt hot o realign the tables so both diners have that nice mountain view.

Jim's Steak was conveniently located close by to the Liberty Bell so we opted to stop by for some cheesesteaks. Only two people ahead of us in line on a Monday afternoon. 

I ordered the Cheese Steak with whiz and grilled peppers/onions for $9 (cash only). The meat was bland and did not have enough flavor. While they were cooking fresh meat on the grill, it appeared they only added water for cooking - no seasonings. The jalapenos available definitely helped the flavor profile of the cheese steak. Bottom of the bread got soggy really quick and made the sandwich messy to eat. Overall, unimpressed with Jim's.

On top of the mediocre food, the customer service wasn't too hot either. None of the staff were friendly nor welcoming.

This was the first stop we visited on our trip to New Orleans and quite honestly, maybe the best restaurant we ate at during our trip. It's definitely a hole in the wall, but where they lack aesthetically they make up majorly in flavor.

We were greeted promptly by the owner's daughter Tia who also served as our waitress. She was so friendly and welcoming! They only have two tables on the inside, so we opted to sit at one of the few tables on the outside. Our entrees included the superdome (blackened fish with lobster potatoes, corn, lobster sauce and onion rings), superdome with shrimp and the bourbon street love ( fried chicken over macaroni and cheese topped with "crawdat" sauce). We also tried their drink "dat shyt" which is a delicious fruit punch concoction. My entree was the superdome and when I tell you, I fell in love with each bite!!!! I swear! The flavors were orgasmic and I ate every bite. The lobster chunks were a nice size, the potatoes were creamy and the fish was cooked perfectly. I also sampled the bourbon street love and it was fantastic as well. Chef Jeff came out to greet us and was even gracious enough to take a few pics. You can tell he's really passionate about what he does and is grateful for his customers. 

Please don't be fooled by the outside appearances. RUN to this restaurant while in New Orleans and your tastebuds will thank me later.

As a former patron of the Pine Street Dmitris, I had certain expectations. 

First off, I had no idea that this (and the northern Liberties locations) were BYO. I really wished I knew that ahead of time. It's always nice to have a glass of wine with a nice meal right? I was bummed. 

Secondly- the menu at his location was missing the saganaki (fried cheese) that the other now closed location had.

Perhaps my overall disappointment clouds my review but the only thing that stood out was the shrimp pilpil. Outstanding! Everything else was good. But I didn't leave as satisfied as I did at the other Dmitris. 

We ordered the grilled veggies which were good. 
The meatballs were eh. I had to ask what kind of meat they were and please be aware there is veal in them. I don't eat veal. I am
bummed once again. 
Fried calamari platter: needed salt. What the deuce guys? 

Overall the experience was unimpressive. 

While the ambiance is lovely, the waitstaff is banal, and I wish I had gone there prior to the other location because I would most likely have an entirely different take on the experience. 

I miss my Pine Street Dmitri's location. I hear they're putting in a Tria. Eh. Whatever.

The service initially was excellent, and there may have been some confusion towards the end of the night when we had to flag people down for our check - but nothing that would mar the experience.

I had the Malbec. It was perfect.

My friend and I ordered a few plates to share and they were amazing.

The mac and cheese was über creamy but not overwhelmingly so. The cauliflower added a nice texture to it too.

Next we had ordered the Cobb salad which was really lovely; the wings which had a unique and truly wonderful flavor profile bordering on exotic and the crab cake. Everything was perfectly cooked, seasoned and in portions that are ideal for two people to share. 

The evening came to a close with the brownie. I wasn't a fan of the ice cream that came atop- but the brittle spiked caramel made my day. 

I will be back for certain.

Good choice for intimate dining with great service.  The outside and location are a bit rough, so I wasn't sure what to expect.  Our Ball State graduate chose Iozzo's for her celebratory dinner.    She made a good decision.

The inside is small and has a great atmosphere.  The tables are adorned with white linen and fresh flowers.  The overall design and architectural details set the stage for a memorable experience beautifully.  There are fabulous glass light fixtures, exposed brick... They also have an outside terrace that looks like it would be awesome in nice (summer) weather.

Service was flawless.  Our water glasses were filled consistently.  Brian was friendly and personable.

The food was very good.  The fresh warm bread and dipping sauce were tasty and appreciated.  Our party ordered Baked Penne, Orzo Portabella and Seared Scallops.  The scallops were cooked perfectly and nicely seasoned.  They came with Yukon Gold Potatoes with Pesto.  In my opinion, the potatoes could have used a pinch of salt.

This is a small, POPULAR, venue.  I highly recommend making a reservation to avoid an extended wait.

The name of this establishment may be the only thing that could be considered simple and basic.  At the same time, it's perfect.  Our Ball State graduate chose Cake Bake Shop for the finale of our time together celebrating her accomplishment.  We were enthusiastically pleased with her choice.

Everything from the décor to staff uniforms have been carefully choreographed to transport visitors to the perfect venue for tea parties, bridal showers or a bright spot in an otherwise ordinary random afternoon.  You'll find pretty glass and tableware, dreamy floral arrangements, twinkling lights, glitter and plenty of pink.  We were enchanted.

Even better, the cake served here stands up to the hype.  Yes, celebrities love the cake.  Yes, the Earls Court Chocolate won "Best Chocolate Cake" at the London Cake and Bake Show.  However, taste is KING.  And here, the King is in Court.  Hm, maybe that should be Queen.

Our party of four each choose a different cake (although three were chocolate versions) and we shared bites.  Every single one was a winner.  I do not believe you can go wrong.  Just choose with your eyes.  For this first visit we tried:  

Millionaire Cake (chocolate cake filled with caramel, vanilla buttercream, shortbread cookies and topped with chocolate fudge), 

Red Velvet Cake (frosted with a beautiful rosette pattern and sprinkled with edible glitter), 

Earls Court Chocolate Cake (chocolate, chocolate, chocolate - this is the FAMOUS award-winning cake) and

Cookie Dough Cake (had a surprisingly authentic cookie-dough taste).

Recommendation:  Make a reservation.  We were resigned to taking our cake to-go but were delighted when we were offered space at their bar.  We got lucky.  Enjoying the cake in their carefully crafted venue makes for a memorable experience.  It's worth taking the time to plan in advance.

Final Assessment:  We loved everything about Cake Bake Shop.  The cake was phenomenal.  Every member of the staff we encountered was friendly and professional.  Special mention goes to Danielle, who provided very good service and Martha, who made a point to stop by and speak with each of us individually and as a group.  We felt very welcome.  5 Stars all day long.

Great for breakfast and brunch.  One of the best meals we had during our vacation. 

Street parking might be a challenge.  We found a spot a bit down the street and considered ourselves lucky.  Put your name in with the hostess and don't be surprised to wait during the busiest times.  Absolutely worth the wait though.

Everything is super-fresh and high-quality but my biggest recommendation is the french toast.  It comes as traditional french toast (not listed) and a Bananas Foster version they feature on the menu.   Either way, you can't go wrong.  I will say that the Bananas Foster version was super-rich and I'd probably go for the traditional next time but that's only because I felt the best part of the dish was the actual french toast, rather than the added sauce and filling (which were both decadently delicious).  The french toast is phenomenal.

I had fruit to round-out my meal and my husband had two breakfast sandwiches and oatmeal.  His meal looked perfectly prepared and he said, "yes, it was," with a smile on his face when I asked.  His sandwiches included heavenly biscuits, crispy bacon and tasty eggs with melted cheese.  I would have been jealous...but I was sitting there with the phenomenal french toast (winning).

The décor was cute and quirky.  Tables are a bit close sometimes but not horrible.  The space had windows and doors open during our visit.  It was very comfortable for me but my guy had sweat beading on his brow by the time we left.

FINAL ASSESSMENT:  Excellent food, including my all-time favorite french toast.  Friendly staff providing very good service.  Solid 5 Stars.

Incredible! We got fresh Fusilli and Rigatoni pasta with bolognese sauce and tomato sauce, all to go. The cooking instructions were super easy to follow. I was able to whip everything up in ten min while keeping my kitchen spotless. It was the perfect meal for four, and our guests were super impressed. 

The service from just our quick interaction at the counter was very pleasant and put a smile on our faces. I am so grateful to have a business like this in our city. No more need for quarantine pasta making-- now we will be picking up hand made pasta from Pasta Fresca!

Nauseating smoking odor while waiting for seating at the 360 Theater. Smoking area is adjacent to theater. Parx should sue its HVAC contractor and the construction code inspectors should have failed this place! Bad enough to lose money - don't need a migraine on top of it all.

This place was about to be good until they sucked. We were leaving and I was curious about the espresso when the waiter told us to "get the fuck out"

Ok dude. Truth is, your espresso is not only shitty, it's horrible. Worse than your overlooked veal piccata or your shitty execute for Italian food.

There are a variety of meat and veggie options and portions were comparable to what you would get at chipotle. You'll find authentic meat options here like tongue and tripe.

Covid precautions- you can call in for pickup or have food delivered. I picked up to-go and staff were all wearing masks appropriately. Customers were keeping good distance from each other at the time.

They have a wide variety of things you can order as well as their secret menu on Instagram at lees_deli where the food is a product of the chefs creative power and culinary knowledge.  The layout is homey and atmosphere is relaxing.  Not to mention they have The Carrot Cake Man's carrot cakes!  Five time best in Philly you can't pass that up!  I've seen tourists from all over come to eat here just because it was the best rated place and every time they leave I only see good things from them!  This restaurant surpasses all other so don't pass up your opportunity to stay here and eat!

Let me start by saying,  I am a sucker for pain. 

I take pleasure in the hotter things in life. I feel that eating should at times be challenging.

Pleasure followed by immense pain
Death sweats
Lip quivering 
Ghost sightings (seriously, I think this chicken helped me reconnect with my dead grandma) 
A deep feeling that every fluid is going to leave your body at the same time forming a new you that will bitch slap the old you for doing such a foolish thing. 
Double visions 
7 stages of grief wrapped up into one big fucking stage.

To anyone who feels like trying the "Damn Hot" or if you want to go full fucking Roadhouse and try "Shut the Cluck Up" I would say tread lightly and bring a friend cause you will not be able to drive home on your own.

This chicken is diabolical. Like if you put Darth Vader, every Bond villain, Imelda Marcos, that crazy bitch from the Cocaine Cowboys documentary in a blender and then sprinkled it with the Goblin King from Labyrinth, this chicken would kick the shit out of that shake. 

I just left for 20 minutes so that the food that I ate before this chicken could exit my body before shit got real. It must be like John Wayne Gacy's basement in my belly right now. 

That's how serious it is. 

I've had the super hot at Princes. I've had the hot at Pepperfire. Those are fucking New Edition and the Damn Hot at Hattie B's is GWAR. Get out of the front 5 rows if you don't wanna get shit on you.

With all that said, I liked it, but you couldn't pay me to try it again. Hell is a place on earth and it lives inside the Damn Hot  chicken at Hattie B's

I never thought I'd find a market to rival Pike's Place in Seattle, but this came pretty close. I entered the market from the southeast corner, so I was greeted with the whiff of chocolate chip cookies when I walked in. I wove my way through the aisles and saw such an impressive array of fresh fruits and vegetables, an amazing variety of meats and fish (dare I say, better fish than Pike's Place?!), a huge variety of eateries (sandwiches, crepes, mediterranean, gourmet, vegetarian, Mexican, Chinese, etc.etc.), cheese, flowers.... I could go on and on. Luckily I came on a day when the Pennsylvania Dutch and Amish were here, with loads of fresh dairy products and baked goods. I came first for breakfast, but couldn't really decide, what with so many choices, and ended up with fresh oatmeal from one place, fresh squeezed fruit juice from another place, and coffee from yet another place. I came back in the afternoon wanting a sandwich, but unfortunately both Rick's and DiNic's were so crowded, I just ended up getting a hot apple dumpling from the Dutch Eating Place (http://www.yelp.com/biz/dutch-eating-place-philadelphia). Yum. I also went around and got some gifts for my family, including a bottle of PA wine and a nice big filet of bacalau. If I had had access to some cold storage, I would have loved to get some Amish butter, more baked goods, and more meats. This place is a real treasure; I wish I had a market like this in my city!

This place is pretty much too dope to be believed. My boyfriend and I stumbled upon Cafe Fulya when we were looking for a spot to drink some pre-TLA concert beers and we definitely found a winner. It has EVERYTHING you'd want, pretty much. It's a basically a Turkish-themed coffee shop that's open absurdly late (til 10pm Sunday-Wednesday and 3am Thursday-Saturday)... yeah, you read that right, 3AM. It's the perfect place for an artist, writer, or student to go on a late night work/study bender. When coffee isn't enough to fuel your creative juices, there's also cheap and delicious food to keep your stomach happy. The menu is surprisingly large for such a small space, and breakfast is served ALL DAY. The food options are diverse- ranging from the decadent and buttery (like the sinfully delicious 4 cheese mac and cheese) to the reasonably healthy (like the tabule salad). Everything is under 10$ and the portions are large. My boyfriend *literally* got an entire loaf of fresh bread with his salad. They get us here! The vibe is laid-back and the decor is homey and cute. Best of all, Cafe Fulya is BYOB, so you can change gears completely and get your drink on at the same time you're eating and late-night caffeineating. I mean, if that isn't perfection, I don't know what is.

The staff is friendly and knowledgable and their suggestions have always been helpful. Ask for a taste if you aren't sure what you want! There is always something new and interesting on draft.
