A week in Florida without a fix for my pizza Jones!?  Inconceivable!!

My coaster-crazed compadres and I were in Orlando running Amok at the amusement parks, but we took a two day side-trip to Clearwater for a little R&R on Florida's more pristine West Coast to recharge our batteries before finishing our coaster-fest with a bang!  Right after we hit the beach, we agreed we were due for pizza that night, so I consulted the Yelp app and found Cristino's.  I called and was told they don't take reservations, so I called back at 9pm to ask about the wait; it was only ten minutes.  We headed over.

Cristino's venue is downtown Clearwater; not unlike 1st Street in downtown San Jose, it's not the kind of place you'd want your Mother wandering around by herself at night - a surprising spot to find an awesome eatery like this.  You can smell the delicious pizzas from the parking lot, and the place has a cheerful, warm and friendly vibe.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/cristinos-coal-oven-pizza-clearwater?select=qCWU3ldAAWX0STL2UTSGig#qCWU3ldAAWX0STL2UTSGig This is a family-run establishment; the owner came up to welcome us while we were waiting for our table, and asked where we were from.  When I told him we were from California, he said that all his waitresses were from the West Coast too - Seattle!

Given how warm and humid it was that night, we were happy to be seated on the festively beautiful patio.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/cristinos-coal-oven-pizza-clearwater?select=bFFSlaxO-dlKiK-dqCyTnA#bFFSlaxO-dlKiK-dqCyTnA There's no bar; beer and wine only, with no draft beer - I order a bottle of Peroni.   http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/cristinos-coal-oven-pizza-clearwater?select=TyPQMSuySy6UV-_QXLeceg#TyPQMSuySy6UV-_QXLeceg  

Glancing at the menu, my compadres and I looked at one another and silently agreed that we wanted our usual pizza: extra cheese, mushrooms, pepperoni, sausage, and garlic - I placed the order.  Cristino's web site says that their "unique Coal-Fired Brick Oven can cook a pie in less than 5 minutes to a crispy finish!"  It took a bit longer than that before our pizza was done, but not much; we shared some of the complimentary Baguette Bread http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/cristinos-coal-oven-pizza-clearwater?select=e7vlHUKDA-kwxtTc5uDssw#e7vlHUKDA-kwxtTc5uDssw, enjoyed our drinks, and the star of the evening arrived! http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/cristinos-coal-oven-pizza-clearwater?select=67VdlfCNWTYIu1M6DiV3DQ#67VdlfCNWTYIu1M6DiV3DQ 

I'm not sure whether Cristino's claims to serve any particular style of pizza, but using my newly revised and renumbered personal four-category system:

1) New York
2) Chicago deep-dish
3) Neapolitan
4) Regional (formerly California)

It ends up in #4.  My system is pretty simple - it's all about the shape and thickness of the crust.  Cristino's falls into category four because the crust doesn't have the right shape or proportions to qualify as New York style, it ain't thick enough to be deep dish, and it's not thin enough to be Neapolitan.  That's all well and good, but I'm revising the system because it I don't think it's Kosher to label a pizza made in Florida as California style simply because it doesn't easily fit one of my other categories.  I know!  We'll change the name of category four - Cristino's serves Regional-style pizza.  As Robert A. Heinlein used to say: "If it doesn't fit, use a bigger hammer"

Enough pontification - time to dig in!  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/cristinos-coal-oven-pizza-clearwater?select=uIJYGf_kw8M6yE1oblC07Q#uIJYGf_kw8M6yE1oblC07Q 

The sauce here is very different; quite subtle and understated for pizza.  The crust is just a touch too soft, but still quite chewy and very flavorful.  It has above average saltiness (I like that!), and gets 4 out of 5 points on the "independent suspension scale".  The toppings were tasty and clearly premium quality; the cheese was just the kind of tangy, gooey goodness my pizza Jones was pining for.

The staff is obviously all very happy working here, which always enhances any restaurant experience.   When our meal was winding down, our waitress told us at great length about the desserts, and brought over little tasting spoons to tempt us - not hard to do with a dab of bacio (chocolatey-hazelnut with crunchy wafer cookies in it), or vanilla stracciatella swirled with a chocolate ribbon...

If you find yourself in Clearwater, and you've got a yen for some good, solid Regional pizza or some truly spectacular gelato, seek no further - Cristino's is just the ticket!

When this place first opened I was ecstatic!  I thought I had found my new bar in Maplewood!  As I had just moved back to St. Louis after 7 years in the mystical realm of Portlandia, it gave me a homesick vibe of PDX, but with just enough touch of STL that I felt I had found my niche!

The films that were shown, the records that were played, the ambiance and the really varied food selection was amazing!  Oh, and the beer!  A large tap selection, but still had my Busch in bottles for my whisky beerback!

Alas, something changed.  It almost became too self-referential and anti-STL vibe, instead of embracing the Keep St. Louis Weird it became a farcical version of the Hipster Hideout.  The bartenders and waitresses became snarly to the point of pissing me off and the outright lack of connection has turned me off of what was to be a gem of a place.

A case in point-  Now, I don't consider myself to be too much of a hipster, I mean I have Ray Bans but I wear overalls and I have friends who are not at the least "hipster".  I took a good friend of mine, a nice Christian woman who is over 45 and still likes her Michelob Ultra, to The Crows Nest.  Yes, she isn't the stereotypical customer for them, but she is a paying one, so you would hope her experience wouldn't be so different.  We didn't have table service and their kitchen had closed (even though it was only 8pm) so my friend saddled to the bar and waited... and waited... she flagged the bartender who nodded and returned to his phone (it wasn't busy- which is why I assumed they closed food so early) finally she got to order and he literally said "Really?  Michelob Ultra?"  My kind friend laughed it off as if it was a joke but I was SEETHING-  and I vowed to never come back.  

I walk by occasionally and look inside with longing... I want it to be the place I first went into- but I guess I will just have to settle for somewhere else.

UPDATE (down to ONE star):

I didn't want to go.  My husband and I sighed and sucked it up and went anyway.  When your brother-in-law comes in town and wants to meet at The Crows Nest, you go...

From the start, there were the usual looks of disdain... "who were these people in their special bar?  These people taking up the seats of their bar.  Do we have to serve them?"  Begrudgingly, and usually taking 10 minutes, we received our beer and shots and cocktails... and I know they were many because truthfully we spent a heck of a lot of money. 

So much money, that when I waited 15 minutes (watching the bartenders help 4 other people who arrived to the bar after me) and received my short version tab I asked for a breakdown of my bill... I was so surprised how expensive it was.  I soon realized that my friends and my husband did, in fact, drink a lot- but as I stood there  waiting to have them run my card, and waiting... and waiting... while the bartenders talked to each other, I knew that the tip wasn't going to be large.  Leaving a smaller tip is my right to decide as a customer... what is NOT RIGHT is how I was treated after making that decision.

Upon leaving, the bartender and two of his friends proceeded to follow me and my friends out the back door championing us that we had the largest bill of the night.  

Not only did he congratulate us on the largest bill, but he proceeded to yell just how big that bill was.  

Not only did he announce how much we paid in alcohol that night, he then said I only tipped 10% and said "I must be from St. Louis, because I didn't know 20% was industry standard".   

I know not every place is for everyone... but Crows Nest sets a new standard in assholery that I cannot condone.  And obviously other people are noticing... the bar wasn't as busy as I've seen it before (our large group of friends were practically the only customers) and their enormous tap selection has dwindled to half the amount... 

The only thing I can say is their food is excellent and the cook was extremely polite and kind to me and my drunken husband.  Huzzah to him... PBBBBBT to the rest.

A friend of mine who lives in Tampa recommended this spot when I was in Tampa on a surprise trip for my birthday.  It's located at the bottom of a highrise, near the water (but not with a view of it).

We were here on a Sunday, so brunch was going on.  You can have unlimited mimosas for $20.00, which I did not partake in.  However, my friend did and her mimosa was more of a glass of champagne with a splash of OJ.  The cost of the unlimited mimosas was a bit more than I'm used to, being an Orlandoan (usually $10.00 to $15.00 at most).  I opted for one of their local craft beers that was on tap.  They had a good selection to choose from, which is always a plus in my book.

The brunch menu was a little lacking to me.  Nothing stood out and made me say "oohhh, that sounds awesome!"  Same goes for the lunch menu.  However, I did enjoy my meal and thought it was very tasty.  I ended up ordering a flatbread off of the lunch menu that had alfredo, bacon, and spinach on it.  I also added grilled chicken to it, which I thought made the flatbread much better and more filling. 

We sat at the bar and I thought the service was great.  Our bartender was attentive, offered suggestions when we asked for them, and always made sure our drinks were full.  My only suggestion would be for the bartenders to be more up-to-date on the beers offered on tap.  I asked what a few of them were and he was unable to provide me with any answers.

A high speed, low drag, pizza experience unlike any other (or is it a low speed, no drag, pizza on a path to enlightenment)? Who cares? Call it whatever you want this is definitely some really good pizza, without a doubt! 

Literally, I made the high speed reference for a reason. The crust is all the way around light and full of flavor and as pizza should be the prefect vehicle for delivery of toppings. These pizzas are fired very fast and ready to go in a hurry. Baked on a thin crust and recipes that are kept on the simple, not overly laden side, and fired in a high temp oven, you'll be in and out fast. The steak bomb is delicious, it's simplicity in part lending heavily to its flavorful success. The BBQ chicken is equally successful in a short list of high quality ingredients and well balanced in sweet, salty, and a happy flavor punch in the mouth. 

Seating here is limited and I wouldn't say it's well suited for dine in, but it's certainly an option, with that said, not a great option for a large group. Recently open right next door, Under the Rose shares a wall and a door joining the two, so you can always grab a pint of suds while you briefly wait. They deliver and I've already heard chatter of another location (we can certainly hope). Staff is very friendly and always smiling (serving pies and making others happy, breeds happiness?) and definitely want to see their patrons equally so. Another welcome addition to mid-town, complimenting the revitalization extremely well and an overall excellent pizza destination, Pizzava is already on my list of regular locations (and walking distance to other equally cool mid-town hot spots).

We had an absolutely wonderful time during our first visit. It was our 35th anniversary get-away, staying at a nearby B&B, and we left happy and full. 

Our server, Colleen, was amazing and made our visit fulfilling and entertaining! What a gem! 

The restaurant is located just off the river- with a view from the prime porch tables. The setting is charming, rustic and relaxing. 

The BYO aspect is also appealing - don't forget to tip on the value of your wines - and really keeps costs down. 

Meals - esp. the "signature" dishes - are on the family style volume side, easily shareable. We took a different path with our appetizers and our entrees. 

Me - Pork chop with mushroom & Gorgonzola, mashed and veggies. Superb!

My wife - Squid ink ravioli with a pink lobster cream sauce. Delicious! 

Colleen surprised us with a slice of cake & a candle! A special evening! 

Highly recommended.

An ice cream with a twist. Made to order ice cream in rolls. Choose your milk. I got coconut milk. Your ice cream starts off as a liquid than freezes when it hits the surface. The rolls are formed when the ice cream is scrapped off the flat surface. Pretty cool to watch. $8 for the cup. 

Milk isn't my best friend so I usually pick something else if there is another choice. They have coconut which is great. But it was more coconut taste than I had anticipated. I taste more coconut than cherry. Still good. 

I will have to go back to try it with regular milk.       $8 is pricey for an ice cream of that size. Great option for people who have an intolerance or allergy to dairy. Will update to 5 stars if regular milk makes a difference. 

Great location. Easy parking.

2.5 stars. I want to give it 3 but it's not quite there. It's a bummer because the food is generally good. Every time we go here we have to wait quite a while. We waited an hour once. Last time was about 35 minutes. If you go in there with a super big appetite you're going to be waiting a while, to the point where the food's arrival is anticlimactic. I had the heavy Irish sub and it wasn't what I would call heavy. I got a similar amount of meat on my last JJ's sandwich. But tasty. There is potential here, they need to manage it better and I think it could be a gold mine. Until then, I won't be going too often. There are plenty of good sandwich shops nearby.

My experience with Vango was bad. They act like they are the most upscale place around the area just because they have a rooftop bar. They even select who can enter the "sacred" rooftop. What a way to hurt a girl's feeling if you don't get pick. To make it worse, you're only permitted to go to the roof only if you buy a drink from the level floor. After waiting for half an hour, a group us did get selected and man was I disappointed. It was not even that crowded, why the heck did they make all those people wait downstairs?! With the combination of painful feet and foul mood I left with my bf after 10 mins of being there.

I waited longer to get in than stayed in.

Hands down the best drive through taco joint I've been too. My only thing is I wish they had queso. Either way. The portions are HUGE. The taste is is top notch compared to any of the other fast food tacos I've had. They have tacos al pastor and the chimichangas are filled with with actual chicken breast rather than processed chicken.

This hotel is located in the Oro Valley just outside northern Tucson AZ.

The grounds are small and beautiful. Strictly a four-star. If you decide to stay, ask for an east-facing room with a view of the Catalina Mtns. 

The problem with hotels such as the El Conquistador and Loew's Ventana Canyon Resort is that you are going to run into the "wannabes" such as we have had the misfortune of doing. This will also happen in places such as Scottsdale like the Scottsdale Resort. You're going to have to either stay at a "road warrier" hotel or at a resort in Paradise Valley.

Recent example at the El Conquistador: we stayed there over the Thanksgiving 2009 weekend and although many of the guests are polite and considerate, the wannabes (aka "$30k millionaires") are also out in force acting loudly arrogant, inconsiderate, and resorting to bully tactics on very short notice. I'm not sure how they can afford to stay at a four-star, but apparently they do.

In our case, we had to use the Business Center computers (2) there because we had to conduct several transactions online using a secure server. This included banking transactions and other transactions involving use of our cc number. To use our laptop (we bring it with us) would not have been advisable since wireless keystrokes can be picked up by anyone in the vicinity, thus risking hackers. Note: there is a $10.00 fee for wireless connection in  your room - not a problem unless you need to use passcodes or cc numbers.

Anyway, 2 very rude and inconsiderate women looking like Dollar Store shoppers showed up about 4 minutes after we entered the Business Center, and stood directly behind me - which to a reasonable person, would put them in plain view of my screen since the screens there do not have a privacy shield.

I turned around in my seat and politely let them know we had just arrived and would need time to be able to finish up. 

The younger of the two rudely commented that "we're going to stay here" or words to that effect, as though she was concerned about keeping her place in line where no one else was waiting. 

I got the distinct impression that she was angry that they found us there first.

Her behavior was out of place and digitally ignorant of a user's need for cyber privacy. 

An older couple entered in about 10 mins later, and were rudely told by one woman (late-twenties) that they were "still waiting since these people were supposed to be gone by now." The older couple did the upper-class thing and left, stating they would return later.

Which if these two females had done, we would have been out of there by then since we would not have had to delay performing our necessary tasks having to wait for them to leave, since politely informing them of our situation did no good.

This situation is the 2nd & last bad experience I have had at this hotel. 

The first was earlier in Spring 2009 where a couple in the room next to us began fighting verbally which devolved into a series of physical attacks upon each other.

I guess other guests called the front desk since I received a call from staff inquiring about noise or other disturbance I may be hearing. (Are you shocked? There's more....)

I let the staffperson know that I was hearing sounds of a physical fight going on in the room next door and I was embarrassed to state this since I have never encountered anything like this in a hotel or anywhere else.

Anyway, she notified hotel security and two officers came up to the room in question, and conducted a room search. I could even hear them opening the drapes all the way and going out on the balcony to search for additional participants.

The fighting couple left a couple of hours later or were asked to leave, not sure which, but they left.

So, I have had two bad experiences at this place and will not be returning.

Loew's Ventana Canyon (not to be confused with the Ventana Inn in Big Sur) is worse since they feature "Girls Night Out" events which encourages the wannabes to stay there.

This is what the wannabes do: gang together in small groups and split the cost of a room four ways in order to afford it. They then party loudly all night long and goof off in the pool area. Their low-rent conduct is derived from the TV shows "Sex and the City,"  "Dallas Divas & Daughters" and "Real Housewives of Wherever" which are the Mother Ships of behavior standards for the wannabes.

The five stars such as the Arizona Biltmore do not participate in this sort of thing. Neither does Canyon Ranch in Tucson. These resorts/spas are fully aware of the wannabes and know what to do to keep them out.

I'm sorry, but I cannot rec this place to anyone seeking a pleasant resort experience.
Okay, the atmosphere isn't all spiffy-designer, but Lee serves up solid good food and even really good vegetarian food. It's cheap, fast, and friendly. How many delis are that awesome?

I don't know about the rest of you, but I like Groupons. Not only do I enjoy buying them to places I frequent, but I also love to buy them to try out local places that I wouldn't otherwise visit regularly. Fox's Donut Den falls in the latter category -- it's a bit of a drive for me, but I've had their donuts many times and know they're good, so I quickly snatched up a Groupon when they had one available. 

Flash forward to yesterday when I finally got a chance to use it. My parents were in for the weekend and I wanted them to have a only-in-Nashville breakfast experience, so we eagerly made the trek to Green Hills. After navigating the mess of a parking lot, we hopped in line, excited by the smell of fresh donuts that greeted us when we walked in. When I made it to the counter, I said good morning and informed the man before ordering that I would like to use my Groupon.... and that's where the fun began. 

The man rolled his eyes at my Groupon and then became visibly irritated by having to "help" me. He reminded me at least twice while ordering that what I was getting would cost more than my $10 Groupon would cover, as if I was incapable of reading and doing the math for myself. Then, while ringing us up, he made a point to tell us that they were being put out financially by people using Groupons and that they couldn't wait for the whole "mess" to be over.

In hindsight, at that moment I wish I would've told him to take his donuts and shove them and then taken my business elsewhere, but I think I was still in a state of shock that I was being spoken to this way when I was just standing there, politely trying to buy a freaking fritter. I'm especially irritated that I went out of my way to take my parents here and then this is how we were treated. The real icing on the donut (pun fully intended) was that I ordered a dozen mixed (which I was told on a previous visit cost around $10) and then a half dozen of mixed. (two fritters, two cream filled and two glazed donuts) and somehow I still paid $10.91 in addition to my $10 Groupon. That's $21 for 18 donuts and to be treated like I was somehow the one doing the ripping off in this situation.

I love supporting local businesses and yes, Fox's donuts are pretty good, but I won't be returning. I can drive a much shorter distance to Krispy Kreme for a donut fix and not be treated like a burden in the process.

fantastic southern barbecue and biscuits that could shame the hat off of the pillsbury doughboy, do not skip the loveless!  we found it on the drive back from memphis and hit it at a non-busy time, famished and in need of southern hospitality.

the waitstaff were really nice considering we were both yankees who had no idea what sorgum was.  i wish we had gone for breakfast though - from everyone's descriptions the breakfast sounds amazing.  this is not a place where you go for health food.  it'd be torture sitting across from people eating piles of biscuits dripping with jam and trying to eat healthy.

the homemade jams are great - especially the strawberry.  i wanted to bring some back on the plane but i thought TSA officials at the airport might jump me for it.  i had the pulled pork sandwich with a side of okra.  at first i felt like a glutton asking for more, but that went away after my second helping of biscuits.

flipping around on the tv the other day i saw them talking about the loveless on the food network and nearly cried.  how i long for a biscuit from the loveless.

At home, my wife and I subscribe to the notion that PETA actually stands for People Eating Tasty Animals. Despite knowing that CWAS was vegan joint beforehand, we still maintained an unexplainable glimmer of hope that the "Maryland Crab Cakes" might have a mote of meat. Turns out it was unnecessary. This food was delicious and pretty filling even for meat eaters like us. 

The goods:
Open restaurant floorplan kept my elbows happy

Cloth backing to one wall seemed to hold down the noise level enough so talking wasn't a chore (unlike, say, Mercato)

Incredibly rich flavors abounded. Our favorite was the Pappillotte of Sunchokes, which imbued the hearty veggies with a coat-your-mouth umami flavor

Great cocktail list also mentioned by other reviewers. Uniquely, CWAS doesn't appear to add much syrup/sugar to their creations, simultaneously making them less cloying to drink and more impressive that they are drinkable

One suggestion:
The beer list is good but not great. It focuses largely on less-rich lagers and un-beers. I'd love to see a rich Belgian-style (Raison d'Etre?) on tap in addition to the Kostritzer they have

Turkey Pesto 10

Steak salad 10

Steak baguette 10

Tomato Bisque 10

Beer ... Paulander Hefe-Weizen / Yummo

Artichoke dip - out of this world great! 10+++

Soooooo Good.  We gobbled everything up so fast we didn't stop to take pics. Sorry! This is a must go to place!

We checked in with the hostess & she was nice and encouraged us to try Pearl if we enjoyed seafood... If not she told us the cafe would be good. 

We were seated at a table & we waited & waited & waited. No sign of a server after almost 15 minutes.  No water... Nothing.  The server had passed our table delivering drinks to her other table.  We asked her if we could at least get a beverage. She said she would be right back... We said fine & continued waiting with our menus in hand.  Nothing happened. 

The bar tender Neal noticed we were distraught and welcomed us warmly as we got up from our table and moved to the bar directly across from our table... We had been waiting in an almost empty restaurant... Our assigned waitress was a girl with her hair pulled back in a ponytail, she seemed to have her hands full with one table??? 

Anyway, with Neal taking care of us at the bar seating area, things quickly looked up.  Water and lemonade arrived and we were off to a great re-start;~D

Neal told us that Silver Legacy was the newest casino & absolutely had the best owner. He invited us to use our comps for food... But to not over order to use them all, as they are valid for 14 months.  He told us he hoped we would return and stay at their location versus the casino we had stayed at. He said that he felt we would love the accommodations and staying at their property. 

Interesting how an employee like Neal who is interested in being an ambassador for his owners turned our bad experience into a great & memorable experience. He even managed to interest us in returning & staying at their property. 

Oh... The food was very good... Served hot & he was very cool about checking to make sure that everything was great... His recommendations of course were excellent.

Being huge fans of Ichicoro and living local, we were so excited for this place to open up. Unfortunately it was an overpriced let down. The staff was kind, cool place, and great location but horrible parking. The presentation of everything reflects the price but the quality and taste does not which was ultimately the biggest let down. Very disappointed.

It's a no from me dawg. 

Okay, i just want to preface by saying that i have been to condado in bripp three times... all which have been terrible.... I wanted to give mass ave a fair chance but it let me down. 

The only good thing i will say about this place is: great location, sick decorating and thats about it.

Now onto the bad...
1. KOOL-AID MARGARITAS: don't even get me started on these koolaid margs... if you want to know what they taste like, buy koolaid and add half a shot of tequila. So so bad... I'm still in shock that a restaurant would ACTUALLY serve these?! 
2. The chips.... greasy and paper thin. Imagine cutting a piece of paper into chip sizes and frying them. That's what they taste like.
3. Quality of ingredients is horrible. Again, I'm still in shock how a restaurant on mass ave (condado) thinks they can compete with top notch food like Bakersfield, eagle, Louie's, Mimi's, garden table, you name it... 

I hate rating restaurants 1 star which is why i never rated the bripp location... but I'm finally putting my foot down. This place sucks. Go down to Bakersfield or Nada... and if you're in bripp, go to la mulita or sangrita. 

Thanks for coming to my tedTalk

After starting with a red wine flight, when I got to my second sample it smelled so bad and the bartender smelled the bottle and deemed my assumptions were correct and I noticed the bottle was a little bit more than half gone.  I can only imagine what the people who are not as knowledgeable about wine as I am thought.

You can never go wrong with meat from Salume Beddu, as its made in the heavens so you are safe with a meat plate no doubt.  I also had the Cornish game hen, it was excellent even though on the menu its described as another type of bird,the breed escapes me now.


During dinner I switched to another wine and my glass was empty.  After waiting 5 minutes I get the bartenders attentions and ask for another.  He says hes on it, but then he got discombobulated and made 5 drinks right in front of me.  Drinks that needed to be measured and poured and loved and weighed and all the nine yards, while at this time I am already sipping off my hubbys wine. 10 minutes of waiting.  Then he remembers why the F I am sitting there and lets me have some wine, that's how I felt.


So about five minutes later I get the glass, we just wanted to go, so we inform him we want the check.  Ok, he says, and makes a few drinks (5 minute process), then grabs us our check and the credit card is put down right away.  He then actually, knowing the card is on the bar, and yes, in this 5 minutes waiting for the check I drank all my wine, we both did, we thought we could just pay and leave, he starts polishing a wine glass.  Long strokes, like he is making love to this thing.  I felt like a perv glaring at him during this process, but was he fucking serious?   He knew we didn't have wine and he knew the card was on the counter and here he is masturbating a wine glass.  And it went on for at least two minutes, right in front of us, then he puts it on a shelf, actually thinks about doing another one, but then decides to cash us out.   I was seriously not amused by this at all.   I was actually pretty livid.  

I love the concept and what they have done to the place, renovation wise, and am very excited to try Elaia, eventually.

Mr. Ed's Oyster Bar is a great place to get chargrilled oysters! 
It was great to get out of the hot sun, sit in the cool air-conditioned air and eat hot savory oysters with friends!  

Mr. Ed's has 4 locations in LA, the one we went to was in the French Quarter. This was the third location on our oyster crawl. 

We shared the Southwest (jalapeno), Bienville (Shrimp, Green Onions & Mushrooms) and Rockefeller(Crawfish, Bacon, Spinach) oysters.

We all had different favorites for this restaurant/bar. My favorites were juicy crawfish tails with the crunchy bacon on the juicy plump oysters (Rockefeller). The Bienville was also delicious- who knew that plump succulent chunks of shrimp goes well with cheese and oysters?

My least favorite was the jalapeno oyster. Who wants this when you can have crawfish or shrimp on top of a juicy oyster?

I hope NY gets an import of juicy chargrilled oysters.

Felix's Restaurant and Oyster Bar has some excellent charbroiled oysters. The restaurant had a 40s diner feel. The waitress was very informative and friendly. 

We came to Felix's as the first stop on our oyster tour. We had half a dozen of raw oysters, and a dozen of the chargrilled oysters. These were the best chargrilled that I've had in NOLA!

The raw oysters were ok- they were plump and succulent but didn't have much flavor (no brininess or complexity). 

The Chargrilled were so amazing! The combination of roasted parmesan, butter, garlic, thyme, rosemary just infused the plump oyster with so much flavor. After grilling the oyster, the oyster was still juicy and plump and it tasted great! I wanted a dozen of these for my self.

We had Acme's oysters the night before but these were better! 

The waitress was very sweet. She took the time to show us how to make a cocktail sauce for our raw oysters. 

I wish we came back for more chargrilled oysters!

Mother's Restaurant is a New Orleans restaurant since 1938. They are famous for their Po-boys amongst the locals. Their menu also boasts of the World's Best baked ham and the original Debris sandwich (roast beef with au jus gravy).

We arrived here as a recommendation from our Uber driver. He really appeared excited about Mother's. His eyes lit up and you could almost see him salivate. I was like, yes! I want to try this.

We ordered roast beef po boy with aus jus (beef juice with flour- a gravy) and side of baked ham. The roast beef was good. The beef was thinly sliced, the au jus offered all the juiciness and flavors. 

The problem was the gravy soaked into the crispy bread so by the time the sandwich hits your table, your sandwich is a soggy mess. You can try to eat it with your hands but it will definitely sag and you will resort to fork and knife.

The baked ham looked dry in pictures. We ordered it and it was really really really dry. All the gravy from the po boy couldn't save it. It tasted like chewing a stack of napkins. K was a trooper and ate it all with an soup of hot sauce. 

Pro tip: line up with the menu. Order, pay. Then pick a table. The waitress will bring you your order. 

Pro Tip: stick with the Po Boys if you come here. Avoid the baked ham.

Clesi's Crawfish offers crawfish and seafood dishes, a live band in the outdoor patio area and a small art gallery upstairs. The service is friendly, the food varied greatly and the music was great!

We arrived for dinner to try some of Clesi's crawfish. They had great reviews and we were looking forward to trying locally cooked crawfish. Unfortunately they ran out.

We ordered half and half (fried catfish and fried shrimps), shrimp and grits and chicken and sausage gumbo. The fried catfish was crunchy and simply fried. It was good. 

The fried shrimps were great! The shrimps had the head left on, they were battered and so crispy, you could eat the whole shrimp if you wanted (head to tail). The shrimp was fresh and not frozen, and you could taste the springiness in the body. This was the best bite.

The shrimp and grits were ok. The shrimp was good (well flavored, not overcooked) But the grits cooked down to a gummy-cake and cut into wedges and deep fried. 

The chicken and sausage gumbo was so over salted it was inedible. Four of us had a bite and could not finish it. It was terrible. When a waiter came by to bus our dishes and asked us if the everything was ok, I told him the gumbo was over salted. He nodded and said he would let the chef know.

Tip: Don't order the gumbo.

Protip: Sit outside and listen to the band. The girls that were playing there that night were from the Jazz Fest. They came from Cali and had a mellow sound, like Lucius. They were sweet, charming and a beautiful sound. 

Protip: Bring bug spray. If you sit outside, you don't want to feed the mosquitoes.

New Orleans School of Cooking was really fun!
K and I signed up for a demo class. The demo class is great because you get a mini food history, you get to eat breakfast and lunch and you don't do any cooking!

I really enjoyed learning about Cajun/Creole food from our chef. He told us about okra's word origins, its role in gumbo, how to make real gumbo. Did you know that most people from New Orleans don't eat gumbo in restaurants? Those that can make it, make a better version at home.

We got to eat buttery biscuits (hot from the oven), red buttered beans with Andouille sausage, sweetened cornbread, gumbo and pecan pies!

The Gumbo was the best gumbo that I've ever had! It was rich, savory, so complex and layered with flavors. It was unlike any gumbo that we've had in any restaurant (NOLA and NY). 
K and I got 3 servings of gumbo!
 
I enjoyed the sweetened cornbread. The Chef kept talking about adding sugar to the cornbread and putting sugar on top. "If you don't add sugar, your cornbread is cardboard!" 
I thought he meant he would make it like a dessert but it was still savory with some sweetness to the cornbread. 

The Pecan pie was delicious! The pie filling had crushed pralines and it had a great texture and crunch! The filling was a little sweet for me but I loved the buttery crunchy pie crust. 

My favorites were the gumbo and the pecan pie! 
If you are in NOLA, definitely join a cooking demo. It will be well worth your time and money.

Gallier Restaurant and Oyster Bar is a low key restaurant that seems like a diner. Service is good, food is ok compared to other oyster bars.

We came here as a 2nd stop in our oyster crawl. Gallier was highly recommended via food websites. We ordered a dozen of the charbroiled oysters and a dozen of the Rockefeller oysters. The oysters were plump, satisfying and filling. 

The toppings were ok. The toppings tasted like something you could have made at home. There was plenty of cheese on top of the oysters but less flavor (maybe less herbs and less butter). The cheese was mainly shredded and not Parmesan. For the Rockefeller oysters, there was frozen spinach. It tasted ok but not much flavor in the spinach. 

I liked the taste of the chargrilled oysters at Felix much better.

The waitress was very nice and efficient. 

Atmosphere: very casual, some locals were eating here. 

Thank you for the hearty snack!

You can find Sotto underneath the walnut street bridge on 24th street. (Hence the name Sotto which means "under" in italian!) #Funfact

I am a huge fan of Sotto for many reasons. 
1. It's BYO.
2. It's so stinkin' cute (I.e., Bring your first date here)
3. The food is delicious 

The pasta dishes are incredible. And while I think that their pasta portions are a great size for a meal, I also think you'll want to split one of their delicious apps or salads with your date/friend/random person to round out the experience. 

Prices are good and service is so polite. Bonus points because they are happy to let you enjoy your meal slowly.  

There is only seating for about 20 so make a reservation and be prepared.

The Short Version: Come here, get the breakfast sandwich, don't skip out on the potatoes.

The Food: So delicious....Res Ipsa has nailed breakfast with a just a few awesome menu items. The breakfast sandwich is delicious, paired with beautifully cooked spinach and delicious potatoes, I don't think there is a better breakfast sandwich in the city. 

The drink: Fantastic Coffee. No mention of what coffee they are brewing but worth getting a (large) cup.

The service: Order at the counter; brought to your table. Quick and efficient. 

Also...Did I mention the potatoes?

The food wasn't great, the service was terrible but the crazy rude owner made me inspired to write this review when she decided to begin a personal feud on my tip. It is she and her husband who run service on this restaurant and they are terrible at it. I left a 20% tip even after poor service because I know what it is to work for tips and she messaged me that I was a poor tipper. This lady is AWFUL and should treat the people that pay her bills with a little respect and hospitality.  That is hospitality 101. PLEASE STAY AWAY FROM THIS PLACE!!! If for nothing more than a terrible owner with no manners or decorum!

Cute cafe with amazing food, great service, wonderful atmosphere.

I came here on a Thursday afternoon with a friend, and we were seated right away. The waitress was very patient even though my friend had the hardest time making her decision on what kind of dish to get (because everything sounded so amazing)! 

She ultimately decided on the Parisian Za, and I got the Ananas Salad. I had a bite of her Parisian Za, which came out with a special smiley face from the kitchen - all the components of the plate came together deliciously, and the presentation was a nice plus.

My Ananas Salad was delicious as well - topped with sweet potato fries and filled with lots of different flavors and textures, this salad hit the spot for a filling yet still light-ish meal. The Ananans Salad comes with pineapples and shrimp with a spicy zesty sauce. I love salads, but I don't normally like paying $14 for something that I feel like I could put together at home. The Ananas Salad was worth $14 and felt like something much more special than something I could casually make.

I can't wait for my next visit to Cafe La Maude to try some of the other dishes out!

Philadelphia is such a City of Assholes.  AssholeFest.   Paradise O'Assholes.  I've never seen such a concentration of loud, rude, angry, foul-smelling, poorly-dressed shit-eaters in my entire life.  

When you've lived here long enough, you actually stop noticing it  - even BECOMING it - until you visit another city, and everyone there seems as if they're 3/5ths into a serious narcotic high: friendly, happy, talkative, relaxed.  When you visit that other city, people might say "HI!" to you on the street or at a bar, and it makes you feel suspicious - but then you realize: you've become a Philadelphia asshole.

I was recently browsing WIKIPEDIA.COM and learned that the French invented the term "déclassé" when they first visited the original settlement of Philadelphia in 1524.  I learned that we put the "phil" in "philistine".  Worse yet, I learned that many years ago corruption was almost eradicated from the collective human consciousness, but we Philadelphians kept it alive during this time much like the Arabs kept the Greek classics alive during the Middle Ages.  

This shittyness all seems to fade away when you visit Federal Donuts.  It's like walking into an alternate reality where Good Things actually happen in Philadelphia, and everyone is super elated about it.  For that brief moment when you first bite into a hot Indian cinnamon donut, we actually live in a first-rate city, with first-rate sports teams, first-rate city planning, and first-rate career opportunities.  For a split second, everyone is suddenly very attractive and has an interesting and articulate worldview.   You even think that, at long last, you might not run the risk of getting your ass kicked or your throat slashed if you walk home alone in the middle of the night. 

Every customer of Federal Donuts is happy beyond reason.   Adorable, rosy-cheeked citizens cup steaming envelopes of hot donuts in their hands and hold them to their noses, smiling like they just won the lottery.   At lunchtime as the line winds out the door for fried chicken, truck drivers hold hands with be-mohawked feminists who hold hands with Mummers who hold hands with hipsters who hold hands with the guys who used to beat them up in highschool - and they sing.

Everyone knows that the donuts and fried chicken are fucking delicious, but I give Federal Donuts five stars and tons of credit purely for the fact that they've created an oasis of joy and civility in this otherwise bleak tundra of disappointment, violence, and despair.

Check my record.  I almost never write bad reviews.  However, after my meal last night, I woke up this morning pissed off and wanting my $110 back - so I felt compelled to chime in here.

I was so excited to try this place!  The menu looked great.  The aesthetic was cool and clever.  Unfortunately, the food itself fails PROFOUNDLY to deliver on the promise of the menu.  

The space inside is narrow but attractive - vaguely loungey.  Everyone from the hostess to the servers to the owner was beyond lovely.  Sadly, that is where the good ends.

I ordered a drink, the "Escape Velocity".  The #1 listed ingredient was "tobacco-infused Johnnie Walker", which sounded fucking heavenly.  I expected this drink to be a strong, earthy, peaty kick in the nuts. Instead I received a completely flabby and flaccid fruit bomb.  Ugh!

To their credit, the other drinks ordered at my table were good: Purity of Essence, Battle New Orleans, and the Singapore Sling.

On to the food:

- Korean style fried tofu - Good texture, but as someone who eats actual Korean fried chicken quite often, there was nothing even slightly Korean about this dish.  One of my dining partners astutely pointed out that these tasted like "Bugles", the cone-shaped snack from our youth.  He was spot on - these taste like they were coated in "Bugles dust" before being fried.

- Confit potato cup & mushroom - When I see the word "confit", my heart goes aflutter, reminiscing on some of the more exhilerating dishes of my dining lifetime - which is why this dish was all the more painful for me to endure.   Moderately tasty diced mushrooms were absolutely BLUDGEONED by the thick, starchy potato cup.  The potato itself tasted like the oldest, most stale and horrid french fry you've ever eaten.  Frustratingly bad.

- Wild Mushrooms & Barley - The wild mushrooms were really good, but oddly these were served on little toasts and each toast was different.  One had some mushrooms, one had an aggressively giant piece of baked garlic,  one had barley and a few mushrooms etc.  Weirdly uneven.  Lazy.

- Saffron Artichokes - Awful. Artichokes are one of my all-time favorite foods.  Unfortunately, they somehow managed to fuck this up by cooking them into oblivion...resulting in chunks of generic vegetable matter smothered in some not-very-interesting sauce.  We ordered two plates of these and only one of the plates contained dill.  Again, lazy as hell.

- Potato croquettes - Slightly overcooked but an OK approximation of potato pancakes.  Whatever.

- Marinated asparagus - Fine, but something I could make in my sleep in about 5 minutes.  Nothing special about it.

- Little stuffed peppers - Again, fine-ish, but reminiscent of something I would wearily whip up with leftover ingredients on a Wednesday night after a long day of work.

- Tofu & bean sausage - These were pretty cool.  Very tasty but small tofu sausages paired with a wonderful mustard accompanyment.

2.5 stars, rounded down to balance out all the stupidly exhuberant 4 and 5 star reviews.

As a general rule of thumb, products of any category decrease in value when they are broken. A broken smart phone is about as "smart" as that one person who's still hoping to make his fortune on beanie babies. A broken engine turns your car into just another expensive place to store things like old magazines and sweaters you aren't going to wear. A broken spirit loses wars, and a broken heart results in the overproduction of cringe-worthy "emo" music.

...but broken rice? Broken rice is an entirely different story.

With each segment that the individual grains are broken into, the light flavors are able to seep in more delicately, providing a palatable texture, almost like a sexy, Vietnamese take on cous cous. Broken rice is so much more than "just rice," and Nam Phuong has the best in the entire city. I think about it often. Almost as often as "Call Me Maybe" gets stuck in my head. Broken rice dishes are accompanied by expertly grilled meats, with a salad of pickled veggies and a splash of fish sauce to top it off. This spacious establishment is located in the centroid of Philly's Viet hub, so really all of the standard options on their extensive menu (including many for vegetarians!) are authentically solid. Whatever you order, from pho to summer rolls to beef carpaccio, your tummy and taste buds will leave happy.

[But if you ever have any trouble deciding...just go with the broken rice.]

You can just call me Natalie Imbruglia, 'cause I am torn.

Cheu Noodle Bar is a cool place. Service is friendly and the ambiance is chill. The hanging lamps were created by one of the owner's glass-blowing brothers. Canned craft beers and other libations will soon be available to knock back with. The hand-torn collage on the back wall adds a touch of funk. They serve up raw Shin Ramyun as a complimentary appetizer (awesome idea).

One must keep in mind that this is not meant to be an Asian restaurant. Rather, it is two American men identifying aspects of various Asian cuisines and recreating it according to what tastes good to them. Taking this into account, Cheu successfully accomplishes what it set out to accomplish - providing a cool atmosphere for people to enjoy what the owners personally like about Asian food. 

But Asian food it is not. The noodles are a bit too chewy (though props for being made in-house), and the flavor combinations are heavy on the "sweet and sour" aspect so characteristic of Asian fusion. The ramen broth is better than some other ramen joints in Philly, but it could stand to be more complex. The pork belly is fatty and delicious, but the flimsy poached egg is a bit of a travesty ramenly-speaking. I preferred the cumin-seasoned lamb neck (served with hand-torn noodles), even if the noodles were a bit too large and stuck together. The black garlic wings were the highlight of the meal. Crispy and juicy, similar to Korean fried chicken, but a little greasier (in a good way).

So yes, Cheu is a really cool place. And the owners did a great job of creating dishes they liked. That just isn't quite in line with what I personally like. It happens.

I'd come here again to hang out and have a drink, maybe order some wings.
For other food, I'd probably just walk to Hand Drawn.

FedNuts is the anti-New Year's resolution.
It is pure gluttonous indulgence. 
The stuff diabetes-affiliated bliss and fat kid dreams are made of.

Fried chicken and donuts are the new peas and carrots (if peas and carrots were outrageously delicious and lower in fiber content). The donuts they serve here have delightfully exotic flavors like Indian cinnamon and pomegranate poppyseed. They are aromatic, tender, and make Krispy Kreme look like a soggy sack of afterbirth. The chicken, served starting at 11:45am, is divine and completely unique in this city. It is twice fried Korean style (see: Café Soho), but seasoned with a whole 'nother register of crazy spices. This place is pure genius. Come early. (and tip Blake and Felicia handsomely!)

Word to the wise: Before you scurry out the door, with your frontside doused in drool, pop in a breath mint and swipe on some deodorant. It gets crowded in here, and you *will* exchange a grope or two with some friendly strangers/soulmates.

This place is literally a hole in a wall. Walk downstairs to the underground Asia Supermarket, past the display of pig heads on ice, past the freshly gutted fish, past the mountains of Asian snack foods, and you will find a delicious smell. Follow it. As soon as you sit down, order the salt baked chicken wings (they can take a while, and they burst at the seams with MSG, but it is so freakin' worth it). You can order the rest later. You're probably safe ordering just about anything else off the menu. The rice dishes and noodle soups are all solid, and it's hard to find food of this caliber for dirt cheap.

I typically have a rule of thumb for Chinese restaurants like these. The quality and authenticity of the food is directly proportional to how dirty the bathroom is. In this case, that property still holds.

When I first told my parents I wanted to go vegetarian (okay, with some rare seafood exceptions), they nearly disowned me. "Chinese people and meat cannot be separated," they told me. "Like yin and yang, both are necessary to achieve a harmonious balance."

And for a while, I almost believed them. I began to wither, finding sustenance in Mediterranean, Indian, and Italian cuisines, but nothing palatable from my own native culture.  Even our tofu dishes contain meat, and when you remove it from the equation, it's hardly passable. I could feel myself and my body reacting. Eventually, I began buying items when they were NOT on sale, and I was only marginally taken over by Linsanity. Could my decision to stray from meat really be killing my inner Chinese??

By the grace of God, I found Veggie Lovers, a 100% vegetarian Chinese restaurant that does not sacrifice taste or authenticity. There are so many tasty options available here, including a killer sesame "chicken" dish that would probably fool even an actual chicken. The food actually tastes like Chinese food and not some bland, paltry imitation. Prices are low (but bring cash), the staff is sweet, and they offer some pretty fantastic green tea (though dishes, unfortunately, can be quite slow to come out). 

Thank you Veggie Lovers, for saving me, for making Chinese food a real option for me, and all of Philadelphia's vegetarians (plus those friends we drag to eat with us).

As much as I hate to do it, this review will basically just be a verbal Venn diagram comparing Yummy Lan Zhou to Nan Zhou Hand Drawn a few steps away. It won't be super colorful or even that interesting, but since I know many people are just wondering "Is it better or worse than Nan Zhou??", hopefully it will at least be useful. Broken down into categories:

- Decor: Yummy blows Nan Zhou out of the water on this one. Shiny new table tops AND a chandelier??
- Space: It's weird not having to wait to be seated whilst cramped in a door frame and half your party spilling out on the front steps. Another one to Yummy.
- Menu: While they are very similar (even in their choice of font and layout), Yummy's is a bit more extensive. They include an entire section for "chow hand drawn noodle" (served dry). It lacks the peanut butter noodle of Nan Zhou though, which saddens me slightly.
- Price: More or less the same.
- Service: Both restaurants deliver the food at lightning speed, though without a hint of a friendly smile or a "how is everything going here?" There is no real winner. But then again, this is Chinatown.
- Broth: Hand it over to Nan Zhou. Yummy's broth is good, but not quite as aromatic.
- Meat: Varies from bowl to bowl. I would say Nan Zhou's is generally more tender and less fatty, but the next person might say the opposite.
- Vegetables: Yummy adds a LOT of the sour vegetable and in much larger pieces. This is something I personally like, but I can see why it might be a negative for others.
- Noodles: Gotta admit, they both are damn good at making noodles. I would agree with a previous reviewer that the ones at Yummy are a little less consistent. Slight win for Nan Zhou.
- Chili oil: I personally believe Nan Zhou has the best chili oil in all of Philly Chinatown, so I was pretty disappointed with the bright red, less flavorful, overly oily sauce at Yummy. That's a pretty crucial loss for them. 

I haven't yet had the zha jiang mian at Yummy Lan Zhou, which is one of my most favorite things at Nan Zhou, so until then, the verdict is still out. I wonder if having these two competing hand drawn noodle houses will work to their favor (like when there are two Starbucks on the same corner), or to their ultimate demise (like when there are two mediocre looking men fighting to the death over the affections of a woman neither can have). Only time will tell.

WHAT DO WE WANT?
A bakery that's vegan, gluten-free, and low in refined sugar!!

WHEN DO WE WANT IT?
After every other option for anything remotely dessert-like has been demolished for some reason!! That bakery sounds like it would be awful!!

This was my mindset for the longest time. For someone who does not have eating restrictions or any semblance of health consciousness, any other bakery option seemed preferable. Then Sweet Freedom changed my life. The cookie sandwiches here are so, so good. Like boy band of five Justin Timberlakes good. Sweet, creamy, moist, and firm all at once - qualities I once only thought possible of creations containing animal product. And since they are presumably healthier, you can gladly have two for the guilt of one!! (but the price of three...they come at $4.50 a piece, yikes.)

Local at its Best!

This pizza place is brilliant!! Worth the price, you not only get amazing food, but you get the best customer service ever AND a fun experience.  You cannot go wrong coming here.

This was my first time here. The host greated us with a beautiful smile, our waitress Nicole was very attentive, and the refill guy Vincent kept our glasses full the entire time and also cleared all the plates. I couldn't have asked for better service. 

And now the food.....

We went all yelp on it... taking lots of photos and ordering several items to try and split....

The breadsticks are big, soft, and chewy. Yummy

The kale salad was tangy, oily, and bursts with flavor in your mouth. Lots of fun

The pizzas.... by order of kudos...and by a landslide the number one pizza we all liked was the baby cheesus. 

1. Baby Cheesus is for anyone that loves cheese. It was so succulent, they could serve it as a dessert with a glass of wine. Mmmmm I wanted to cuddle up to it.

2. Homeade Sausage was super moist and soft. Perfect traditional type of pizza.

3. The Green Pie has pesto sauce and Smoked Goose Ham. Yummo!!! Pretty and green!!

4. The White Devil is great for anyone who loves mushrooms. 

All of them were cooked to perfection!  I recommend anything on the menu!  


Tips.....

Pet friendly, handicapped accessible, perfect views of mass ave, bar AND stove seating.... yes a seating area in front of the pizza making area/stove area OH YES

Every meal here is big enough for two. Overly attentive staff who are friendly and hard working team players provide an exciting experience!  As soon as you walk in, you're family.

I know what you're thinking... This is a yelpers dream!! A fantasy place where we can by one plate each of something different and split it all up. Then review review review!!! Yas, it is true!!

Don't hestite and take a friend, an enemy, family, your boss, yelp club and enjoy your breakfast or lunch or dinner, it doesn't matter, just bring them in and share a good meal!

For a first timer hearing about this place, I wasn't expecting to walk into a classy upscale burger place. Very nice decor and a wall for their menu. 

I wanted something sweet and tangy so I got their aloha burger and added pepper jack cheese. What I got was a sweet tangy hot mess of gooeyness covered in cheese. Waffle fries are Indiana state fair quality. Sweet potato tots are fun and yummy. 

Loved the local art on the wall for sale. My favorite thing to see in Indy. The local flair! 

This place is a must to enjoy by far the best burger around.... ;)

Croissants that are created from tissue thin flaky layers. 

Absolutely yes !! Please !!
Finally I was in the Midtown when Perenn was open. I seem to always arrive after 2 pm. On a Saturday morning be prepared to see the line to the door and maybe out. There are a few seats at the window, a large community table inside and a couple of picnic tables out front. 

The counter is to the back to order and scope out the baked goodness. As you arrive at the counter there's a tartine menu. Almond toast, lox, Caesar, nicoise, ricotta, and Brie & fig. And / or try to choose a delicious baked good from the case as it whispers- "pick me, I'm delicious and totally not fattening."  Yes I picked more than one. There was four different types of croissants, danishes and sliced breads. The croque monsieur croissant, don't expect to cut it in half and save some for later. It won't work. The tissue thin layers of flaky pastry and butter wrapped around thin ham and gruyere cheese was more than I could take. Just eat it. And buy and extra for later. 

Street parking can be tight. I suggest you park a block away and spend more time in the Midtown area. Just start here for breakfast.

We had such a fabulous time at the recent Elite event.........

That when Sacramento Yelper Darci came to town, Debbie suggested we all go to dinner at Anthony's. So reservations were made for a private room, eight Yelpers having a great time can get kinda loud. The room was perfect. 

What a fabulous surprise, Sean was again our waiter. Mr. M checked on us throughout the evening. And it was a long evening. We were truly European. Our party took our time starting with wine, adding appetizers, then onto mains and finishing with dessert. Three hours of talking, laughing, eating and toasting. This is how dinner should be. We were never rushed and the room was superb- quiet. 

The Rocca vineyard creates some incredible wines. We ended up having 6 bottles of the Vespera. The crab cakes are still chunked full of crab and delicious. Calamari was huge, plenty to share. Scallops, buttery and for met, perfectly cooked. Sean checked with the chef, and the risotto dish was prepared with a change to accommodate and allergy. Bison is not easy to find. My steak was a nice medium rare. I believe I enjoyed the flavor more than the recent New York, and I still had enough for two meals. The rack of lamb tonight looked wonderful, and Debbie really enjoyed it. Sides included gratin potatoes, Brussel sprouts, and creamed corn. So much food. 

We wrapped up our night by sharing a wedge of the 24 layer chocolate cake. Just enough. 

We had a slight glitch in the bill, but it was quickly taken care of.  Eight people, 6 wines and a ton of food, it 

Thanks Yelp and Anthony's for the recent event I was lucky enough to attend. It showed me a great new dining spot with fantastic service. Anthony's layout is just right for small and large groups. 

Sean and Mr M you guys are splendid.

Shaun is the man to see for a fabulous Roxy's martini. 

Makes no difference if you're ordering martinis from their massive menu or having one created just for you, Shaun nails it every time. 

Make sure you come early for happy hour, roxy's fills up fast and for a good reason- fabulous drinks and staff. The prices have changed recently, unfortunately. Now there is a range $5-9. 
Enjoy the live piano music until 10, then it changes to DJ. There's always a dance floor available. 

Check them out for the best martinis in town. And say hi to Shaun for me.

It's been a while since I've been in.

Armed with a Groupon,  a friend and I go in after work midweek to enjoy a wine and olive oil tasting.  What a great deal. We started with a glass of champagne, then a Chardonnay and finished with a nice red Blend. Our deal came with a cheese flatbread and a four sample of olive oils. We added a delicious asiago and goat cheese dip plate for $12.  

It was a great kick back evening. We had the bar and a table of four other gals had a table behind us. More relaxing and quieter than a bar.  And delicious food to nibble on while sipping thru their wine selection. 

I'm sorry that I can't remember the girl that helped us because she was fabulous. Juggling the two different tables with wine, food service and answering various questions we had. 

Don't overlook this great spot for a light bite, sips of wine or some quality product shopping.

Another spot I haven't been to in a year, but on the Reno Bites Week list. 

I'm glad it was because I felt it hadn't been as wonderful as it was when it first opened. On a Friday night it was very crowded and had a 45 minute wait for a table. I do agree with other reviews- the host staff can be a little snobby and not very social.

Wait staff was good. And the food that night was fantastic. Dinner was the RBW  Argentine flank steak, sliced and laid on a bed of creamy mashed potatoes, and drizzled with a chimichurri sauce. Add a draught beer and the total bill was $20.  It was just the right amount of food to share that late in the evening.

I would like to come back again soon and check out some other changes to the menu. It's has a great pub atmosphere and the place is very clean.

I'm posting 4 stars but maybe it's more 3.5. 

The restaurant was very clean and we were the first at shortly after 5 for the dinner service. I did catch the Tom, our waiter having his dinner, I felt odd that he got up in the middle of a bite to seat us. But the rest of the service for dinner was great. 

Fresh naan and dip was delicious. The saffron cream pasta with chicken had nice flavor and lots of fresh crunchy vegetables. And plenty to share and still had left overs. The lamb kabob was a prefect medium rare and incredibly tender, but on the gamey side with bit a of seasoning coming thru. The grilled veggies on the side still had nice firm texture. And the dessert- always awesome- saffron pistachio ice cream topped with chunks of crispy sweet baklava. 

I'll return, as I live almost across the street, but I'll try a couple other dishes next time.

This is where the group wanted to grab a bite. And the visit reminds me why I don't care for large chain restaurants. 

Three of us walked in around 5:30 pm on a Friday for happy hour after an escape room visit. The restaurant was at least a third empty and we were asked to wait 5 minutes or do to be seated. HH is only served at the bar, I discovered after being seated in the main restaurant. I ordered sliders from the small plate appetizer pages because I wasn't in the mood to look thru the entire menu. BJ has a book of a menu that I don't care for- how can all that food be fresh? 

The sliders had an up-charge for cheese and another for fries.  The sliders were tasteless and were missing the grilled onions.  I did ask for the fries to be extra crispy and came swimming in a small pool of grease, but were crispy. 

Our server was fabulous, checking on us often and separating the checks.

Greatly under advertised. 

It has been opened for several months, but I just discovered this spot a couple of weeks ago. 
It's located in the southwest corner of a strip mall on Lakeside and Ridgeview in the former Taste of  Thai location. Plenty of parking. 

Pasta isn't fine dining, nor it is fast food. Fresh pasta made daily. Spaghetti, rigatoni, ravioli and lasagna were in the menu the night I went. There were also five sauce choices. The table tried spaghetti with Bolognese, rigatoni with pink vodka sauce and spinach ravioli with ricotta cheese topped with white wine cream sauce. All the dishes were tasty and decent portion sizes. We were going to try a different pasta, but the owner removed it from the menu because he wasn't happy with it. 

We also tried a few starters- caprese, burrata on tomato halves, and lentil cream soup.  I recommend the burrata over the caprese. Cheese and meat plates were were also available for starters. Also three items for dessert. 

Currently with covid, the city is slow in issuing Pasta's liquor license. So you are welcome to bring your own bottle of wine. They are happy to provide wine glasses and opener without corkage fee at this time. Also due to covid there is very limited inside seating- 6 tables if I remember correctly. So call for a reservation if you want to dine inside. While there, there was a huge to go business. 

Give them a try for authentic fresh pasta, I hear the chef is from southern Italy.

I believe this spot has been open for about a week now without advertising. And at 5 pm was filling up pretty good. 

Note the entrance is on the Lakeside of the building so you don't have to walk around the entire building to find the right door- like me. The interior is very nice- rustic painted cement floor and walls that look like various reclaimed boards. I like the over all appearance. 

Being the first time there, the only server I can comment on was Charlotte. Damn that girl is a perfect server. Subtle  suggestions - a drink from the bar, "we have a great bartender."  Or an appetizer or two while looking the menu over. She saw my indecision and said take your time, I'll bring the drinks. For a new restaurant she seemed to know the menu pretty good and made a couple of suggestions. One two sided menu has sandwich, burger $10-14, salad $9-15 and small plate choices $9-14. The second menu had more of a dinner selection - ribeye $20, pasta $13, and lamb chop $18. The food arrived on, my personal favorite, HOT plates. My three tacos were so stuffed you couldn't fold them in half and tender beef, fresh crisp cabbage and a creamy cool cilantro sauce. Hubby enjoyed the rigatoni with mushrooms and chicken in a cream sauce.  

A nice variety of wines from $5 to $11 a glass and also available by the bottle. Also a reasonable beer list. 

Of coarse Charlotte returns with a final suggestion and tease of some decadent sounding desserts. Next time, we were just too full. 

Will  absolutely be returning there were several other items we really wanted to try.

The best ravioli Monday's in Reno. 

Ok it's the only deal like this in town. 

Fresh house made raviolis, choice of salad or dessert, bread and a glass of wine house $20. My usual go to are the mushroom ravioli in a rich cream sauce. But on my recent experience, the waiter offered an added special for the night, duck confit ravioli in a truffle butter and cream sauce. I'm not used to such decisions. But he said- duck. Those pillows of yumminess were filled with tender rich shreds of duck meat, mmmm. Then covered in a cream sauce, that bonus - included mushrooms and a hint of earthy truffle. And the salad is no tiny side, this Caesar salad is plenty to share, but I don't. And the dressing is made in house with anchovies then tossed with plenty of Parmesan snowflakes. Don't let "house wine" fool you. It is a great wine and paired wonderfully with that duck. 

Some day I will venture beyond the ravioli and check out other menu options. 

Ask for a seat towards to front. The view overlooking Reno is fabulous.  At night as the lights twinkle or even during the day the mountains rise out of the city. Better yet in warmer weather reserve a table on the patio.  Perfect ravioli seating. 

Parking tip- pull in to the right of the building. It may not look it, but there is parking there and not as tight as the main lot that is shared.

You may think owner and chef Christian Christensen is all about soup, sandwiches and salads- and you would be so wrong. 

Sunday night at Pignic, Christian showed off his culinary skills at a pop up based on smoke and citrus. I seriously enjoy it when Christian steps out of the SUP kitchen and shows us some of his many other culinary talents. 

We came in around 4 pm and his staffed passed some small bites - smoked trout bruschetta, pork belly and scallop ceviche. All wonderfully devine. 

First course was a peach smoked grilled watermelon with feta and micro arugula. Pignic staffed paired it with Atlas Cider Company apple cider.  Interesting dish and fabulous cider.  Next to arrive was the "coolest" presentation- an applewood grilled chilled scallop with a ruby red grapefruit miso glaze. Check out the video, it came to the table with a smoke filled glass, it was just fun to see the smoke roll out as you lifted it to eat. It was paired with a smokey Paloma cocktail.  The main course was a bistro grilled filet with pecan smoked cremini mushrooms, yuzu ginger reduction and charred asparagus. Can you say Delicious!!  How does one even come up with this ??  It was paired with a Yuzu ginger sour cocktail. A cocktail that I wasn't sure I liked.......until I drank it with the steak and it took on a completely different composition that became heavenly. Finally dessert- Meyer lemon budino, green tea smoked raspberries, candied orange peels and whipped cream. This wonderfully tart delight was paired with a Prosecco  Bellini. 

Now I see how Chef Christian has won the Reno Bites Week Chef Showdown two years in a row.  I highly recommend checking out Pignic's pop up series- they are all fantastic, but if Christian is cooking I strongly urge you to go and check his creative side, you will not be disappointed.

Tickets were just $40

Don't  judge this buffet on my review, I'm not a buffet fan by any means.  

But this was were the other half wanted to go for thanksgiving. I'm not a fan of buffets because if I really wanted to go track down my own food,  I'd  go out hunting with my brother and shoot it myself. Eating out should be table service.  Sure there are a ton, litterly a ton of options.  But I don't need that many choices. And I can't eat enough to justify the price. I settled on just a few- a stack of crabs leg ( a little too watery), shrimp ( peel them yourself and little mushy) and the mushroom ravioli. The hubby was certainly delighted in his full turkey dinner. Along with lamb, ham and prime rib.  Other choices were Asian foods, pizza and Mexican fare.

All the stations were constantly kept clean and well stocked. Drinks were always full. Dirty plates picked up immediately. Bless the staff- it was a holiday and everyone of them I saw had smiles on and were so gracious.

Weekend evenings are packed due to live bands and plenty of good food. 

I remember doing a burger brigade here a couple of years ago. Those were some huge juicy burgers with lots of flavors. But recently I joined some friends here to listen to the band Apothic. Hellfire has a nice stage area and several different seating arrangements. It was pretty full of dinner diners as we walked in around 8pm. But after about an hour and a half the diners leave and there's room for the drinkers and dancers. Acoustics were good, and there's a small dance floor in front of the band for you'd and others entertainment. 

Our table tried several dishes- roasted Brussels sprouts with bacon were delicious and plenty to share four ways. The Mac and cheese, creamy cheesy goodness. The burger cooked to a nice med  rare was more burger than the girl could handle, and tapped out. Pulled pork sandwich had plenty of tender pork lathered in bbq sauce. The fish and chips..............where huge. Almost too big for cod, more like shark. 

And ladies we have a fabulous bathroom at our disposal.  Chandeliers and a mirror the Joan Crawford would die for. Well maintained. 

Parking is easy, as Hellfire is at the north end of the strip mall and there are three long rows available to use. 

Breakfast menu looked fascinating- I need to check out their weekend brunch soon.

I really like the new second location. 

I spend a fair amount of time in the Midtown area and the location is so much bigger than the original location downtown.  It also offers a fantastic area of outside seating. Parking here is also way easier than the downtown spot, at the corner of S Virginia and Cheney there is a large parking lot specifically for the 777 Center shops. 

This place offers the same great menu that everyone is used to- unique pizza variations, wings and calzones. Don't forget they offer a gluten free crust too. As well as a much larger bar area. 

Overall great place, give it a try.

Treated myself. 

5 stars to Carrie C esthetician
3 stars to check in staff. 
5 stars spa facilities 

As I checked in 30 minutes prior to my scheduled appointment time, the check in staff wasn't exceptional welcoming. My tour of the facility was quick and not complete. I felt rushed in the locker room. 

Lockers were great. Enough space for your personal items and you key in your own code. Slippers and soft comfy robe were provided. I kicked back in the lounge and enjoyed a snack and flavored water as I waited for my appointment. 

Carrie took me back to a quiet treatment room where we discussed facial options. I went all in and spent 90 minutes with Carrie. She started with steam as she described the treatments to follow. In the dim relaxing room I enjoyed two facial masks, scrubs and other moisturizer treats, as she attempted to take a few years away for me. Reflexology?!? Yes, Carrie spent some of the time toes and even the over worked hands. 

Afterwards, Carrie gave me a better tour. I chose to relax and finish my evening in the salt room. Fabulously serene as I was the only one there the entire time. 

Next visit I will arrive an hour or more earlier to enjoy a steam room or the crystal room before my appointment. They aren't recommended after the treatment I had. 

Checking out the same staff still wasn't very friendly. It felt like I was a chore making a purchase and settling my bill. 

They accept Spa Finder gift cards that you can purchase at Costco- two $50 for $80. They give locals 15% off Monday thru Thursday, but will not combine the two discounts.

Awesome place.  THE only place I'm buying spices from now on

They had everything I asked for. And it was great to buy by the ounce, so you don't have an over abundance of spices going bad in you cupboard any more. 

The store is well organized and labeled. And in case you're staring right at it, the  staff is great at helping you what you looking for. Testers are available to check the aroma and taste. I'm thrilled that they carry some of the hard to find and unique spices and herbs that I used to have to special mail order.  

The owners were manning the shop the day I was in. I was impressed with their knowledge of their inventory- where it comes from, the best places that supply it and the regulations that govern the growth and harvesting of the products around the world. 

Great addition to the California area of town.

It was free food and still three star ok. 

We had a $40 off food at Cafe Central from playing DJ Trivia last year and it expired in threes days.  On a Saturday late afternoon around 4:30 there is no wait to be seated. Menus and water came quickly, we needed a few more minutes to decide. But we were given several minutes. Food arrived quickly. But there is really nothing special about the food- thank heavens it was basically free. The kitchen did actually prepare my fried extra crispy and very piping hot- they were perfect after being well salted. Half way thru the meal I really would have enjoyed more water. I even moved the glass around the table and tried to catch the waiter's attention, but literally didn't get my water until we were leaving. Our table still tipped 20% on a $37 tab. 

The meal has a full page of breakfast items served 24 hours, and salads, sandwiches, burgers, and oddly enough a page of Chinese food. Average meal price $10. 

Would certainly return if I ate free again, but only then.

A great late night snack spot. 

Many say the location is cursed, all previous restaurants have never seen their first year anniversary there. I hope this one makes it. It is truly unique- not a chain, not fast food and not a casino 24 hour cafe. Sierra is a small quaint, nicely decorated restaurant just off the Truckee River downtown. So far they are serving tapas, small plates, until midnight. The server said if they are too slow they would close early. But in our three visits I have yet to see them be slow. 

Each time we have had Melissa and she has been wonderful about menu and drink questions, and separate checks for us. A few craft cocktails, as well as the usual bar fare are available. A nice wine list that even has splits- smaller bottles for the single person. We have been wowed by the freshness of the ingredients as well as the variety of menu items. Salads have been larger than expected with plenty of snowy soft Parmesan cheese.  Sliders with tender juicy meat and soft toasted buns. 

Hungry after 9 pm give them a try. Just need regular dinner, they're great for that too.

Thank heaven for events. 

I have had a few lunches here with a friend over the last year. But on a Sunday afternoon the Whiskey Hunt brought me in. I highly recommend mid afternoon. The perfect time between lunch and dinner rushes, and we had TJ all to ourselves. He was fabulous explaining the pairing to us. For the Hunt Arario served up a dram of Crown Royal Noble Collection - Blender's Mash 13 Year with a side of 
Korean Fried Chicken. The boneless chicken bites were lightly coated, crispy fried, and tossed in a sweet and spicy Korean sauce. Simply amazing how it changed the flavors of the whiskey. A perfect pairing.  

It was shortly after 3pm and this wasn't our first Hunt stop. TJ showed us the happy hour specials, and after the delicious chicken bites we were in. I order the steak tartare salad- wow.
