Small plate ?  This HH $12 special was a meal. A pile of tender julienne beef tossed in soy sauce, ginger and sesame on a nest of arugula, topped with micro greens and a raw egg. TJ explained how to toss all the ingredients for a heavenly afternoon meal. The dumplings and kimchi fries were also plenty big. 

With 2018 fall construction there is parking available on nearby Virginia Street or a lot at the corner of Virginia and Cheney. 

Great addition to the Whiskey Hunt. I highly recommend to try the rest of the year.

Now I've been here three or four times so an update is due. 

Chef Jolly came in a couple of months ago and has changed the menu some and changed the recipes up. I seriously want to try the fried chicken. 

But I have tried the massive grilled cheese, it is delicious- thick wheat bread with three kinds of gooey cheesy goodness. Still not a fan of the French fries yet, but I hear they may change soon. I highly recommend the black bean aioli to dip the fries in, it rather addictive. 

Tonight I checked out the  Dueling Beer Dinner - Brewer's Cabinet vs New Belgium. 
Only 24 seats were available at $35 each. 
I'm seriously glad you could buy the ticket there and not online for an additional fee.  There were 5 courses of food with 2 beers paired with each, one from each brewery. We got to vote on the best paired beer after each course. In the end New Belgium took four of the five courses. Me not being a big beer lover I thought this was a great way to learn and sample some unique beers for our area. 

We started with the most creamy smooth buttery popcorn grits topped with queso fresco and radish microgreens. Wow. Paired with a sour or gose, I liked the NB Tartastic for this. Next was a Tlayuda- Oaxacan style tostada topped with a Mediterranean spiced refried bean and egg poached in a tomato sauce and paired with lager. An Escabeche Trio- snapper ceviche, fried branzino, and  "canned" musselswere next. The ceviche had a nice firm texture and great flavor. I was surprised to learn that this dish is a staple in any ocean side village in Latin America.  The three preparations were  the ceviche Snapper, a crispy fatty piece of Branzino and Mussels that were prepared by Sous vide. All three were absolutely delicious and perfect in their own texture. Tamale Colados was the main course. Another unbelievably creamy corn preparation that just made your eyes roll, served with a very intense smoked pork. This was paired with an IPA.  And don't forget about dessert. Churro S'mores - crispy fried sugary churros nestled in
sinful marshmallow fluff, warm chocolate ganache, and an incredible bit of heaven- caramelized dolce de leche.  This was the one pairing my table was at odds with- both beers were good, but once you ate the churro they became bitter.  The beers were good with the toppings, but there was just something about the frying and the reaction with the beer. The best choice presented was BC's Barrel aged Wookiee. 


Again I admit I'm no beer connoisseur. And if you aren't either I strongly recommend you go in to Mellow Fellow and ask for Ryan. He'll take 10 minutes and ask you a bunch of questions, then for me he brought out 5 beer samples. I was shocked! I enjoyed the very first pick- a sour gose from Brewer's Cabinet. The rest got darker and hoppier. But after some time with him I have a better idea of why I don't like certain beers.  
I shall be back to learn more and eat more.

Wow !!!

We were next door earlier in the evening for one of Paul's Beer UYEs.  And now down to just four of us we went next door to Pizzava. 

I'm sure I have mentioned it before, but I'm not really a traditional pizza fan. I don't care for red sauce. Pizzava offers three sizes- 12" $14, 14" $16 and 16" $18. Sixteen specialty pizzas that have choices from red, Alfredo, BBQ or none. There are also five breakfast pizzas, seven calzones, three pastas, and other sides. 

Katie created her own pepperoni that looked fully loaded with meat and cheese. I went with the XL Alfredo Spinach- so cheesy with plenty of mozzarella, creamy Alfredo sauce, spinach, roasted red peppers and minced garlic. Plenty for four fabulous meals all week. And it was ready and very hot in under 15 minutes.  

There are a few tables inside, and some on the front sidewalk. Open from 11a to 2a, they have a big delivery area !!

Would I order again ? ABSOLUTELY!!  Tough decision to get the delicious Alfredo Spinach again or try a different mouth watering creation.

It's so tucked out of the way, I always forget about this spot. 

So far I have only ate breakfast/ brunch here. Pancakes are plenty big. My last eggs benny was ok, not as fabulous as I had remembered. But served with potatoes and fresh fruit. Next time I go for the chicken fried steak with eggs and potatoes. Enough for two meals. And an interesting gravy that tastes like it has bacon and sausage in it. Truly looked like grandma's gravy. Or maybe the huevos rancheros, another very full plate of flavor. Mimosas are not bottomless here, but served with the OJ on the side to create to mixture that suits you best. 

They offer a great prime rib deal on the weekends, as well as other changing specials. 

Timing can be a trick. Too early and you could wait for a table. We were 11 am on a Sunday and got a table as the previous rush was clearing out.  

A patio is available out front during better weather. It's not covered. 

Parking can be confusing. During the week there are surrounding businesses that you can't park in front of. Oxbow has a small limited lot and very little street parking.  On Sundays the parking is better since you can park in front of the closed shops. 

Yes, I need to return for lunch or that prime rib dinner.

Want a mountain of smooth soft served ice cream, sitting in a nest of moist cake drizzled with sauce ?

You want KRĒM!!  They just opened September 1st in the front side of the Asian Market on Moana. It's going to be a fabulous addition to the space. 

I was greeted with smiling faces as soon as I walked in. The concise menu screen is behind the counter. There are four recommendations- the Chocolate Wasted, I Love You So Matcha, Ube Baby, and the Sunday. (Check out picture of menu for details). Or create your own: 
Pick a soft serve ice cream from - vanilla, chocolate, ube, or matcha. 
Then decide on vanilla or chocolate cake. 
Finally add a sauce - ganache, strawberry, red bean or condensed milk. 

I went with the Chocolate Wasted, of course. The chocolate lover in me couldn't pass that up. The soft serve was smooth and chocolaty. The cake was moist and airy. The ganache was thick and rich.  Next time I will have just a tad more ganache added. But the entire combo was Devine chocolate goodness. 

**suggestion- to reach the bottom of the dish for every last bite, flip the long handle spoon upside down, it grabs and scrapes all the yumminess you won't want to leave behind**

The parfait dish is $6.80 and is just the right amount to subdue the sweet tooth, and not make you feel like a little piggy. 

I licked it, so it's mine - AND I'm not sharing.

Nice addition to the ever growing restaurant and bar scene in the Midtown area.  

Serving breakfast starting at 7 am to lunch, then dinner and late night plates till 2am. Homegrown has a mix of vegan and meaty dishes to please many palates. 

Mid May I met a friend for a long leisure lunch. My friend's burger looked juicy and was plenty big. My club sandwich had lots of roasted turkey chunks with fresh lettuce and tomato jam. I did ask for extra jam, I wanted a little more of its flavor. 
This weekend Angie B and I stopped in for dinner. Her salmon filet was big and nestled in a plate of veggies and quinoa. I'm not vegan, but when a restaurant does it right- you don't miss the meat. I tried the Portabella Stack- a juicy grilled portabella mushroom with a layer of tangy warm goat cheese topped with grilled veggies that were are all also nestled on a bed of quinoa. 

There's an outdoor patio available, but I also recommend sitting at the bar, especially if Spencer, the owner, is there. He was fun to watch bartend and great to talk to about his menu choices.  

Can't wait to return and continue eating my way thru their menu.

The Kintop sisters- Caitlin and Krista, for the last two years have been known for their fabulous lunches and catering. 

April 13, 2019, they kicked the Cheeseboard up a notch. Creating an inaugural Supper Club, a five course dinner with wine pairings for $80 a person. Chef Kaimi Coonrad didn't disappoint with a menu that hit several points in his life.  

Reservations were easy, I called the bistro and asked for two seats. We walked in at 6 pm and were greeted with a chilled glass of asti, how could you go wrong?  Staff took my name and showed us to the table. The place was sold out plus a large table had been set of the west side of the bistro. The owners welcomed everyone and introduced the Chef. Chef went over each course he had chosen. Crab cake because as a child he accompanied his mother to the beach to get fresh seafood. Artichoke soup from his days in the Pescadero area. Arugula salad is his wife's favorite. Short ribs reminded him of his mother's pot roast. And he personally loves strawberry rhubarb. The wine distributor then discussed each wine he chose.  From beginning to end every plate was delicious. Fresh slaw with delicate crab cake. Incredible buttery toast with artichoke soup. Salad with creamy goat cheese and crunchy pistachios. Perfectly tender and savory short ribs- yes, just like mom's pot roast. And moist cake with bright fruit. 

Sara was our area server for the evening. She did a fantastic job. This dinner was classy- each pour had a new glass, previous glass was picked up after each course, and the entire night's timing was perfect. Leisure three hour dinner to enjoy the food, wine, and company. The space does get a little noisy.  

The backside of the menu showed the wines and special purchase price, so you could place any orders while there. 

I hope this evening was exactly what the owners and chef expected, and make this a monthly event. 
I will return.

Wow I can't believe I haven't done this review. 

This little ice cream shop shares space with Peddlers Deli in a strip mall a little off the beaten path and near Smiling with Hope Pizza. But if your in the mood for some unique ice cream flavors that kicks Baskin Robbins butt - head here. 

Thanks to Yelp's month of coffee events last August, I headed in here to try Reno 911, coffee ice cream with pieces of cake donuts crumbled in it. Absolutely delicious as I fell in love with this place. Last week on St Pats day they served Bailey's and Jameson ice cream. Equally a heavenly treat for the day. Way better than green beer. 

They are forever trying unique combinations, so you need to stop in often. There are usually 12-14 different ice creams to choose from. How about Grandpa's Carrot Cake -Spiced Carrot ice cream with whiskey soaked raisins. Tomorrow I need to try maple bacon cheesecake. 

Don't wait too late in the evening, they close at 8 pm.

Wow !!

I was leery about trying this spot in Sparks, but still drawn by Rawger and Katie's reviews. So recently after a UYE at the Food Bank, I met a friend here for lunch. Still not totally sure what to expect, but wanting the Vampiro. 

We walk in and head towards the back. The girl welcomes us and reads the slight confusion on our faces. I wished I knew her name. She was one fabulous employee!!  She asked if this was our first time in. We said yes, then she smiles and fully explains that we order with her and pay, pick up a tray to our right, watch our food being freshly prepared, pick it and head to the condiment bar to top. So easy. She also answered all our questions about the menu. Again fabulous employee.  

Al pastor vampiro and a chicken taco was my choice. I heard tales of cheese melted on the griddle, topped with a crisp house made shell and meat. This IS what I wanted. The outer crunch followed by the cheesy goodness was heaven. The al pastor with pineapple was an explosion of spice and sweet. So much meat, pieces tried to sneak out. The chicken taco was also piled with plenty of tender chicken and delicious. I liked the four sauce choices, fresh cilantro, salsa and even lime slices offered at the condiment bar. 

Two tacos, two vampiro - the bill was $17. 

They offer a drive thru, but I would go in so I could top my order my way. Plenty of parking. 

Totally not in my usual neighborhood, but the vampiro is a new craving. And I heard I need to try the mula.

If you're the jealous type this may not be the review for you. 

This is a review of a very special dinner held at the restaurant. Chef Adam Ornellas, a CIA trained chef is the house chef. But for this one evening of culinary adventure he invited his mentor Master Chef Almir Da Fonseca to prepare a special menu. Keep in mind there are 191 Master French chefs and 140 Master American chefs. This gentleman is one of six in the world that has both titles. A chef beyond what this town has seen, and we have some phenomenal chefs in Reno. 

The evening starts with a reception meeting the Chef and a glass of Lampo Prosecco and music. This glass was a nice prosecco, not as dry as some can be. We are then seated in the Cactus Creek dinning room at tables with more silverware and wine glasses than even I own. 

Amuse- fresh raw oyster and a baked oyster with ( get this) bacon soufflé paired with more prosecco. 

Soup & Salad- the most incredible pea and asparagus soup with a watercress, pickled carrot and pea shoot salad. Paired with Chappellet Chenin Blanc 2013

Fish- scallops, mussels and shrimp with fennel saffron espuma, caviar and red pepper rouille. Paired with Blackbird Vineyard Arrivistes Rose 2012. Not my favorite wine of the evening, not a rose fan. 

Poultry- a rich wonderful duck terrine nestled on confit young potatoes, petite pan squash, with a berry infused natural reduction. Paired with my fav of the night- Bouchaine Vineyards Pinot Noir 2010. It's light spice and not dry finish was a fabulous selection with the rich fatty duck. Mmmm 

Meat- for the men in the group.  Generous portion of dry aged grass fed local beef stop loin. So tender, cut like a hot knife cutting room temp butter. Dreamy. Prepared with fennel, forest mushrooms, and a killer delightful Gorgonzola fondue. Paired with Hartwell Estate Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon 2013. It was a wonderful match with its hint of blackberry, dry peppery finish enhanced the steak. 

Cheese- Carmody, black pepper poached pear and crispy pain perdu with another unbelievable concoction- blue cheese ice cream. Wow.  It worked and was paired with Darioush Signature Cab Franc 2011. I have just died and gone to heaven. I'm completely happy, satisfied. But wait......

Dessert- right another one? Berry and lemon tart with a macaroon and ruby grapefruit sorbet. Paired with Sandeman Port. I enjoyed two bites of this dish and actually had it boxed to take home for breakfast. It was quite tart and sweet. The port was also a little on the sweet side for me and lacked the warm caramel tone.

This chef was Chef Adam's mentor, so you know his food will be of the same high standards, I really recommend you give Cactus Creek a try any time. But just a heads up- Chef Almir will be returning next year for another dinner. 

Bon appetite!!

Met a friend here for a Friday lunch on a March day. 

Cloudy and cool out ?  I don't recommend sitting anywhere near the back door. Every time someone came in and out a very cold draft came in. I had to wear my coat thru the entire meal. Another table went back to their car to get their coats. I'm thinking this may be a nice spot to enjoy the fabulous looking back patio in the summer. 

Art was a fabulous server. Water always filled, checked on us just the right amount and offered to split the check. 

My lobster roll was just eh. A good amount of lobster on the roll without drowning in sauce. But there was this underlying taste, like a chemical- could it have been the paprika?  It just wasn't rich and fresh tasting. I added onion rings for $4 to my roll because it's served with potato chips. Which would be ok if they were house made and dusted with old bay, but they are just plain ok chips from a bag. The lobster Mac n cheese looked delicious and quite cheesy. I need to move on and try some different menu items. I'm thinking I'll return this summer and try the happy hour menu and enjoy the patio.

Another 5 star spot everyone has been bragging about, and should be. 

And as all the previous reviews have stated- this is no ordinary pizza joint. For starters this restaurant has a social cause -  to create hope and meaning in the lives of people with disabilities. And every one I saw tonight were working their hardest. 

This small place was really hopping for a Wednesday night. We came in right at 5pm and was there for an hour. We watched the place fill up before we left and 8 separate to go orders being picked up. 

The pizza was, in my opinion, my the perfect crispy thin crust pizza. We only needed sausage, mushrooms, and black olives to create our delicious pie. You won't find any shakers of fake cheese on the table. They was their fresh ingredients to shine through. Our large classic New York style pizza was $26. There is also a New York ricotta pizza, and a New York Sicilian.  They also have calzones and salad. 

Enough choices for me to return and try more.

When you're greeted at the door and the staff knows you're name and remembers the last time you were in. Good or bad ?

At Zozo's, it's always good. 

Over the years I have enjoyed countless wine dinners, which are an incredible delicious value in this town. Check out previous reviews on those meals.  I finish work usually before five pm and Zozo's is on the way home. I like their Sunset menu. Lots of items at a discounted price if you order before 6pm. 

During RBW on a Wednesday, Erica and I went to try the $30 four course pre fixe special. Every year that Zozo's has participated they seem to outdo the other restaurants with sheer choices and value. This year yet again. Appetizer choice was either calamari or burrata.  The calamari was delicate. But I must say the huge mound of burrata looked SO creamy with the walnut pesto drizzled around. Totally my choice next time. Soup or salad, I took the Italian vinaigrette salad. Oh yes, the always addictive basket of garlic bread. I still think it may have crack sprinkled on it. It's not to stop at one basket. Main course, I went with the mushroom ravioli, five palm sized pillows filled with large pieces of earthy mushrooms smothered in a white wine cream sauce. Yes baby!!! Large enough to enjoy half for lunch the next day. Erica had the chicken pomodorro, spaghetti pasta with roma tomatoes, shaved garlic, olive oil, basil, capers, scallions and plenty of blackened chicken. Sprinkled on topped with pine nuts. Dessert was a choice salted caramel ice cream or spumoni. Duh, we did the salt caramel. 

I highly recommend reservations any time. We had 6:30 on a Wednesday and the place was packed. I have never been rushed thru a meal here either. I brought in a special bottle of wine for that night. Two glasses quickly arrived at the table, bottle was opened and poured for us. Reasonable corkage $15. On Tuesdays there is no corkage. 

Plenty of easy parking. Give this family restaurant a try. If you're not in the mood for Italian that's ok. Ask about ever changing steak and fish specials. Phenomenal quail too.

Tried place during a fund raiser. 

It's not located anywhere near my neighborhood, but since it was for a school fund raiser I made the trek. It's divided into a restaurant side on the left and a smaller bar side on the right. It easily accommodates large groups with three long rows of tables skirted by booths along the wall. 

They serve the usual pizza, sandwich and salad fare. Check the daily special board for great discounts. Wednesday nights a single topping large pizza was $16.99. Quite the bargain and was a fantastic lunch at work for the rest of the week. Large was quite generous in size. The crust isn't paper thin or exceptional thick, a perfect medium. Plenty of ingredients and a nice layer of gooey cheese. 

Staff was great at the ordering counter to explain their menu to newbies, and to make sure DA received their money.

Not technically open until tomorrow- September 29, 2018. 

The last few days they have been having their soft opening. So on a Friday morning at 8am Debbie P and I meet up for to check it out. Before 9am the street parking is free, then you need to feed the meters. Parking wasn't a problem. 

Walking up, the front door was open and the sweet smell of cinnamon rolls is lofting out the door. Mmmm.  We were greeted with big welcoming smiles. You order at the counter, get a number and take a seat. Coffee, water and silverware are self serve near the register. 

I went with the biscuits and gravy, with a piece buttermilk fried chicken on the side. The crispy chicken was moist and tender, there was bit of a spicy kick to it. Just right. The biscuit was fluffy, soft and buttery- grandma would so approve.  The sausage gravy was also delish. But.......after the second bite the manager stopped by the table to check on our food. It was delicious but my gravy was luke warm at best, he immediately took the plate and brought back a new pipping hot plate. No excuses- fabulous customer service. Debbie ordered the Reggie- a huge biscuit supporting a piece of fried chicken, bacon, fried egg and gravy (sans cheese). That was a meal.  You can watch the biscuits being made - there's a window at the end of the counter to see the Lovin' going into the buttery flaky pillows of goodness. I also took this week's pop tart special home. It was a smore, chocolate filled graham cracker crust tart with a toasted marshmallow on top. 

Final approval is finishing on their liquor license, so Bloody Marys and mimosas will be served soon. 

Great new addition to this downtown neighborhood.

Wow, so close and overlooked so often. 

Seriously almost across the street from my house and I haven't ate here in quite a while. Years ago twenty of us enjoyed an inaugural Yelp Supper Club here. The family style dishes bordered some exotic tastes and were beautiful plated. 

Intentions of walking up the street to get pizza, I realized the pizza wasn't opened. Then turned around heading to Wok. Greeted as soon as we walked in, we had our choice of seats. Menu still has many great creations. The duck needs three day notice. Small plates are also available. We both went with the Walnut Shrimp. Plenty of plump juicy shrimp lightly breaded and bathed in a light creamy sauce served over fresh cabbage. It was difficult not to eat it all, but I want some for lunch the next day. 

Service was also on top of keeping ice water filled on this toasty day. Clean restaurant with a half dozen tables and bar seating. They have their own parking lot out front. They are towards the back of the Orchard Plaza to the left.

I'm no beer expert.

But this is one hell of a packed place even on a Tuesday night. The layout is long and skinny. Short tables and chairs up front and high top tables and chairs along the left. A decent bar area- it has to be to display all those beers on tap. Watch the large screen TV's over taps to see what beers are being drawn from which breweries. They do offer a small selection of wine and a few craft cocktails for those of us not into the beer scene. But serious beer consumers need to check the spot out. 

They don't serve food but allow food from nearby Los Compadres and South Creek Pizza to be brought in or delivered.

Wow.  Again what took me so long.  

I have been wanting to try this well established restaurant for years. Today after a disappointing morning at the lawyer, I said to myself- you deserve a great lunch. I drove down McCarran to the Grill. 

A mid size restaurant that circles an open kitchen. Since I was alone I chose the bar with a great view of watching the chef at work. The service was on top. The lunch menu just perfect in size with a burger, some sandwiches, salads and a few larger dishes.  I went with the New York steak sandwich- fabulously tender and perfectly flavored steak on a soft buttery well toasted bun, with arugula and blue cheese.  I opted to leave off the raw red onions.  And served with some of the best French fries I have had in town.  I'm very picky about them. I want nice and crispy fries - they were perfect with salt and light pepper.   The meal was finished with check presented with a warm chocolate chip cookie.  

Absolutely I need to return soon and check out the rest of the menu. Now I want to see the dinner service.  

Note - they are closed on Sundays.

White pizzas are hard to find.  

On a Friday night make sure you eat early. Walked in at 5pm and was seated right away, in 30 minutes the place was full.

Menu has a salad section that the server said was shareable size.  Pizza crusts are available in gluten free. There's a small selection of set price combos, but it seems this pizza place is more about designing your own, each item being additional. There's traditional, white and pesto sauces. 
We went with the White Pizza that was quite creamy from the mozzarella, a little heavy on the garlic, and topped with an olive oil drizzle. Delicious, but next time I think I will add some artichoke hearts. The crust was thin but I've crispy. The pizzas are prepared in a coal fired oven. 

Service was great. The restaurant clean. The high ceiling do make it a bit hard to carry on a conversation when the place fills up.

I like to go with others who have the "in" or have been there a few times already. 

Robert S fits the criteria since in the first month Hinoki has been open he has been there at least six times. I have to totally agree with Robert's philosophy and sit at the bar and get to know the chef creating your sushi masterpieces. We sat at Gerson's station (he is one of the partner/owners). Robert said to just let him send out dishes. So Gerson asked if there were any allergies or preferences not to have- mine were no raw onions and not excessively spicy. And the adventure was on.......  So many great pieces of fresh nigiri on small pieces of flavorful rice began appearing. Intermixed with smaller version long rolls so we could check out all the various combinations and flavors.  There were a few rolls very unique to Hinoki and a couple of new fabulous sauces I fell in love with. Check out the pictures- I decided not to post everything we had because so tried so much, but you can see how wonderful the bites are. 

I had told Robert earlier that I felt like I needed a wow dinner. And Hinoki supplied it. Several dishes lit up the palate with fresh, bright and unique flavors. A couple of dishes were so exciting they made my skin tingle. 

No question about it- I'll be returning, sitting at the bar and hanging out with any of their great friendly chefs.

This place seems to be a little hidden.  It's the first floor, southeast corner of an office building. 

Search for it. It has a fabulous patio that is pup friendly, and a large inside dining area. Nice simple decor.  But it's really about the food and the service. 

The lunch and dinner menus are simple two sided menus. I love that. I dislike restaurants that hand you a bible sized menu. How fresh can the ingredients be in menus that size?  WPH still has plenty of delicious options.  

They were part of the 2018 RBW. I enjoyed the three course for $30. The Artisan salad was perfectly dressed with a light lemon vinaigrette, crisp pear slices and delicate shavings of goat Gouda.  The wild boar schnitzel with rye spätzle, pickled mushrooms and apple cider gravy reminded me exactly of a couple of meals I had in Germany. To finish was a huge chunk of hot bread pudding with an equally big scoop of caramel ice cream.  Delish!

I set up an Esteban Happy Hour there in September. We enjoyed the patio. Separate checks for ten wasn't a problem. At the time the HH food menu was rather small, and wine and beer were the only beverage specials available. Last week they released a much bigger food and drink menu. Very interested in returning to check out this new menu. 

Last fall for the Whiskey Hunt, WPH served a fabulous soft centered Scotch egg and a dram of whiskey.  Nice Saturday morning breakfast. 

Service whether for large HH group or for solo group has always been great. 

Parking before 6 pm is metered street parking.  After that the office lot behind the building is available.

It's a small shop, almost tiny, but holds BIG flavors. 

After an Elite event here at the start of the year, this is my only spot for buying my chocolate. I AM a chocolate snob. At least once a month I go in and select my fix for the month. Usually a cocoa nib dark chocolate bar for $10 and some Hub truffles. Mmmm.  We learned at the event Dorinda and Dustin use the best ingredients and NO preservatives. That's important if your not into the icky waxy feel a kiss or other cheap chocolate gives you. Just that smooth rich chocolate feel and taste- drooling yet?  You should be. 

Keep an eye out because Dorinda's has been having some great wine and chocolate pairing classes at Fine Vines. They have also recently started having chocolate making classes once a month. And rumor has it there is more to come. 

J'adore le chocolat !!!

Wow.   I always eat here early evening and midweek.  8:30 Friday nights this place is packed.

We were hungry and the line to be seated seemed long. But in less than 10 minutes we were seated, and a few minutes later put our order in. As busy as the place was our food arrived in good time. The portion size and flavors that I remember. #51 flamed pork cold noodle bowl always hits the spot and a healthy dish for a great price.  

The remodel is really pleasing. I like the new dark woods, tiles and colors. It's still one large dinning room but looks better that it did 10 years ago when I first started to eat there. 

Staff is quiet but boy do they hustle. 

Open until 3am on weekends- especially great if you've been across the street enjoying too many martinis

I'm not getting all the hype yet. 

It's kinda fast food and yet not. Meals are served in paper bowls and wing in brown boxes. You eat with wooden sporks- not fond of wooden utensils but that's just me. I think they leave an odd flavor. 
I tried the #1. Was it supposed to be just like warm? There were a lot of different veggies and the meat was tender. I tried the teriyaki sauce on half and the spicy mayo on the other half. You have to use a sauce because there wasn't much flavor without. Even with the sauces I wasn't really wowed. 
I did like the miso soup- very hot and nice flavor.  
I would try it again an order a different item. But I won't rushed back right away yet.

This spot has been bookmarked since it opened. 

I came in at the tail end of lunch rush, and the place was packed. Make your way to the back counter to check out the easy to read menu boards and order. My sandwich was ready in about 5 minutes and by then several tables had became available. 

For $8 the BLT on my choice of my many breads was a great buy. Quite the large sandwich piled with plenty of fresh ingredients and lots of bacon. 

If in the neighborhood again I would definitely try another delicious sandwich here.

A great spot to hang out with friends for a quiet drink. 

Set up in the old style of the late 1800's with no tv's. Clusters of furniture make it easy for groups to hang out and talk without loud tv distractions. Or enjoy a seat at the bar.  Several local beers are on tap and a nice selection of craft cocktails are also offered. All prices are pretty average with the area. They allow nearby food to be delivered if you get hungry. 

On Wednesdays at7 pm they play DJ Trivia for bar tabs. Great fun. 

Check out this unique neighborhood bar just south of downtown. 
Street parking available. Be careful not to park in the lot across the street, that is for the Cheese Board and you can get towed.

Of all the places I hit downtown to eat, this isn't high on my list.

In the last couple of months I have stopped in four times- once for a Burger Brigade night and three others when dinning alone. I would also like to note that I used a $5 off food purchase each time I ate alone. I got these a year or so ago over a bad previous experience. 

The BB night the food was fabulous, but the service a bit slow. I get that, we had over 20 in the group. They could have added another waitress.  But the time after that I sat a the bar for several minutes before being acknowledged. I ordered the BLTA, which being on Texas toast was mostly bread, with just a couple strips of bacon, and over ripe tomato slice and some shredded lettuce- disappointing. So next visit I went back to the burger. I ordered an Imperial. Now this is my own fault- I was so hungry I ate more than half and never told the waiter it had burnt crunchy pieces on it. It was no where as good as the first one at BB.

Usually has quite the college crowd in the evenings and weekends. At least for a downtown business they have their own parking lot.

I don't know 3-4 stars ?  I don't frequent chain restaurants all that much. And this occasion was because a coworker had given me $50 in gift cards. I really only truly like the Godiva dark chocolate cheesecake, but 5-6 slices of it seemed a little much. So we had a light bite after golf. 

After7 pm seems like a better time, just at the tail end of the rush. We waited only 5 minutes for a table. Service was prompt. Food took just a bit longer than expected, probably because we were so hungry. Then menu, as everyone knows is abut lengthy. Hubby tried the chicken Alfredo, which was enough for two meals at $16. It was a bit garlicky. I tried a couple of small plates for $7 each- stuffed tater tots and crab balls. Both ok but just nothing wow about them, lacked seasoning. 

The restaurant seemed very clean. The patio in the afternoon sun would be quite warm. 

The slices of Godiva cake I took home did not disappoint. But as soon as I figure out that recipe I have no need to return b

Stopped in a Friday lunch date. 

Located on the east side of the Wells roundabout. You'll have to park on the next side street. It's a short walk. Then through the large patio area to the front door. It was a gorgeous day so we patio dined. The inside seating is plenty spacious too.  

Not your usual Mexican restaurant menu, nice. A limited menu, serving breakfast at 10 am, lunch and dinner until 9 pm.  Sundays until 5pm. Several seafood items, pork chops, and soups. 
They keep an updated menu online, check it out. 


We went with a platter of 6 mixed street tacos. There was so much delicious, well seasoned meat on all of them. And very filling. The chips and salsa here are not complimentary. But we'll worth the $8. Fresh house made chips that weren't greasy and had plenty of crunch and flavor. The red and green sauces equally flavorful.  

Service was fantastic. 

Try this quiet beautiful spot on Wells. I don't think you'll be disappointed.  Perfect for a date night or night out with friends.

This isn't one of my go to Mexican restaurants in town. 

My hubby and I have been a few times, and the other night a group of Yelp girls headed here after drinks nearby. It always seems convenient when I end up here. 

The service has always been wonderful. The food is ok. They have all the usual dishes you would expect. For me there is no big wow dish, nor is there anything poorly executed. The portion sizes are big, if you go away hungry that would be your own fault. The prices seem average with other places in town. 

They have a great outdoor dining area in the front of the restaurant. And plenty of easy parking.

Its probably been a few months since my last visit here. 

Then the hubby and I dined from the small plate happy hour menu. We weren't knocked out by anything, in fact a could of plates were disappointing. 

This time I was out with friends who chose it because a couple of times a month they offer a $30 special. A prix fix menu of appetizer, main course and a glass of wine. Not a bad deal. 

I wasn't all that hungry so I just tried the rack of boar, just two double cut chops, that were quite over done. I requested it med rare, and it needed seasoning. The rest of the plate looks good and was delicious. 

Not my go to spot but ok when that's where the rest of the group wants to go it works. Service is usually good. And restaurant has always been clean.

It's like a Port of Sub for pizza. 

Early this summer I purchased a Groupon for two visits to My Pie.  I was in the area for other business and stopped for lunch. 

If you haven't been yet, it truly reminds me of a sandwich shop. You are warmly greeted went you walk in. Staff asks if you have been in before.  If not they walk thru the order. You start with three crust choices- white, wheat and gluten free. Only one size available. Then choose from their list of ideas or create your own.  It gets popped in the oven while you pay and get your dink. It's at your table in less than fives after you sit. 

I really enjoyed the flavor and concept. But I'm not usually in that area, so it will be a treat once in a while when in the area. 

Do sign up for the rewards program. They won't flood you mailbox daily, but once a month you get a free treat or a pizza for $5.

I used to go to Walmart weekly and really didn't mind them. It's a one stop shopping trip for the most part. 

But over the last couple of years......I tend to space my visits out about three months a part. Basic household items and groceries is my main purchase there. Prices and selections are usually good. I like their savings catcher program- after shopping scan your receipt with the phone app and in 24 hours you get a store credit if they find other stores had your purchases cheaper. The big hassle over the years is coupons. They never used to be an issue, I usually walk in with $30-50 in coupons. Sometimes they don't like the ones you print yourself from manufacturers or online. Recent problem was no being able to use two identical coupons for two purchases, seriously I bought the right product, coupon wasn't expired.  Lesson learned for now.  

For the most part this store is usually clean and stocked well.

A very different review for me, a collection of three visits. 

Friends and I met here three Thursday nights in a two month period to check out the secret menu. None of the experiences were  the same. 

First night was a 4 star night. Albert's service was fabulous. The three course pre fixe menu was just as we had seen with a slight variation in the wines poured. But that was to our bonus, neither of us are fond of Chardonnay and enjoyed the Pinot Grigio more. The steaks were perfect medium rare, the Mac and cheese deliciously creamy and cheesy, and the sautéed mushrooms devine. The Oreo cheesecake was rich and fluffy. It made a great breakfast the next morning. Again, service was wonderful.  Fabulous overall experience. 

The second time was more three star. Julian our waiter was so nice, but had been given a table of 12 at the last minute besides serving us.  The secret menu had changed from the posting two days ago. Some disappointment there. The surf and turf special, we had to ask about. So the table tried everything. Two of us did the surf and turf.  Plenty of food for two, even without sides. The others ordered the pork chop pre fixe with wine. This is actually a better overall deal - salad, main with sides, dessert and bottomless wine for $58. The surf and turf was $105, the bottle wine we picked $48. Julian was so pleasant with us.  Parents, please watch your children, allowing them to run around a nice restaurant can ruin the other diners' evening.  Also management could have asked them to stay seated in their area. 

The last experience, brought two of us to the back left smaller dining room, a nice quiet area. Hannah was our server. This time the secret menu was spot on. The halibut was a large piece, the ribeye well seasoned and perfect medium rare. The sides- sautéed mushrooms and Mac n cheese were smaller portions than the first visit. As was the small square of bread pudding for dessert. The beet salad was just a few beets and frisée, a very plain salad from the first visit. The wines and pours were nice. Service was fair. I wonder if it was because restaurants are now up to 50% capacity and maybe not fully staffed yet. 

Consistency is my issue.  Service varied. The food portions varied. 

The local's secret menu is a great three course value with wine and i still highly recommended giving it a try.

No matter what time of day you go in, this place is dark.

It is the coolest looking bar and very unique. The floor is black. The walls are black. The furniture is black. You get it. It looks like the can of black paint exploded inside the building. It's odd but I like it in a Wednesday Adams kind of way. 

The drinks are a precision. They take a little more time to make here so don't ever be in a rush for a quality cocktail here. There are many different variations on as many drinks as you can think of. The latest time I was in was during Negroni Week and they had created a special list of six variation of the Negroni. 

I do find the prices here a little higher than other spots around town. Our drinks that night were $12 each. 

Worth a stop just to check the place out.

My five stars are based on the fabulous job during Reno Bites Week and the 1977 dinner presented by Rapscallion's Chef Richie LaCounte. 

It had easily been three years since my last dinning experience at Rapscallion, and that last time was kind of a let down.  That's one reason I love RBW, it gives you reasons to try places.  

Rap and Chef Richie really served up a fantastic event based on their 1977 opening menu.  $50 dinner and half price bottles of wine made for quite the evening. Manager Patrick and chef came to the private sold out room to explain the menu. First up was a crab and spam quiche- in the 70's spam was all the rage. Next the most absolutely delicious rich earthy cream of mushroom soup- because in the 70's Campbell's was pushing it.  Remember Green Goddess salad dressing? The chef did and added bacon deviled eggs to the salad too. I was seeing all the 70's hot items except one. Where's the molded jello ? Then it appears- champagne flutes with cherry jello and prosecco granita for a palate cleanser. Chef kicks traditional beef Wellington up a couple of notches- serving a rather large lobster and Beef Wellington with a perfect blue cheese fondue. Watergate received a bad rap in the 70's, but chef's watergate pie was creamy deliciousness accompanied by a fabulous grasshopper martini. I grew up on grasshoppers, pink squirrels and Brandy Alexanders; and that martini was full of wonderful memories.  

Beautiful job and huge kudos to Rapscallion, Chef Richie, and his staff, and to Reno Bites Week for a killer event.

Who doesn't love ice cream??

For years I've been a fan of Dorinda's chocolates and Rolled Ice Cream on Riverside. Now she has a location in the new Rancharrah Village. This new location puts me equal distance from both, darn. :)
Both have great outdoor seating and the ability to buy Dorinda's fabulous chocolates while getting your ice cream.

Each dish of ice cream is made fresh to order while you wait, and watch. Choose from milk or soy for vegans.  Then a flavor. It's Dorinda's, so I always choose chocolate. There are fruit flavors and mint available. Next pick a mix, again, duh, I add chocolate. The mix ins are available on the counter to check out and pick from. If you really can't decide on a combination, the staff lists their favorite creations on the menu board.  The ingredients are mixed together on a frozen griddle, smoothed into a sheet, then cut into strips and rolled. 

Spoons and napkins are by the door as you head outside to enjoy it. There's no inside seating available at the current time. The Village offers a great seating area. 

Plenty of easy, free parking right behind Dorinda's.

I haven't been here in many years. 

The office staff wanted to go to dinner here as a group. 

First, your entire group needs to be present before they will seat you. Also Tuesday nights are a madhouse- due to AYCE Taco Tuesday for $8.95.  99 cent margaritas are now $3.  The smooth salsa was yummy with the complimentary chips. My shrimp and crab enchiladas were no so hot- odd garlic and mushroom sauce and very little seafood in them. Two were $16. Disappointing.  The fajitas were sizzling and smelled delicious and my friend said they were.  Another friend ordered the blackened chicken salad, she said it was dry and actually lacked flavor.  

Service was good. There was 9 of us and to split the bill we had to go the register to pay individually. 

Next time I would suggest a different spot for our large group.

Nine of us on a Friday night reserved the Chef's table. 

What a night !!!

This group has done many many wine dinners in many places over the last several years, and this was at the top of our list. 

We were seated at our own large table at the east side of Roundabout. Rather secluded, our laughter must have preceded us. Full night menu with each wine was placed at each setting. Rose started by describing how the evening would go as she helped serve the plates and poured the wines. She took the time to present each of the eight bottles and describe them before she generously poured each course. Chef Christian came out at each plate and walked us through each of his creations. Eight courses, not bites, full courses. Each plate topping the previous. Fluffy cheesy gougere stuffed with more cheese, wild rice and chicken. Tomato bisque topped with flaky pastry. Beautiful beet salad. So much seared ahi with fun puffed rice. Mushroom ravioli, look out ElDorado these pasta pillows are serious competition. The pomegranate granita, nothing like making champagne love to this devine dish. A perfect medium rare hanger steak with compound butter and house steak sauce. Oh my god, we're we supposed to save room for dessert? Peanut butter  pie topped with vanilla bean gelato and peanut brittle.  And the evening's wines- wow. French, Spanish, German, and west coast vineyards. 

Rose and Chef were so fantastic taking so much time with us. It felt like we were the only ones dining.  If you tried Pips Pass, here's another fantastic food and wine experience. Food and wine together were under $100. 

Can't recommend it enough to try.

Before I begin the review, its worth noting that I've lived in Okinawa, Japan for 6 years, and I was born and raised in SoCal(most recently there from 2010-2013). I've had tons of ramen from a lot of really good places, so some may say that I am picky, where others would say I'm well versed. My wife is also Japanese(Okinawan, for those that know the difference). So no one was more excited to learn that Ramen was finally coming to Tampa than we were(even though Anna M. seemed to imagine otherwise), especially right down the street. Not only did I keep my eyes peeled on Facebook, but I also pass by here twice daily. Yesterday, our day finally came.

We were pleased to learn that this place is a Japanese restaurant serving ramen, udon, curry, and a few other Japanese favorites. We were NOT looking for another sushi spot. It is new, they are hiring more staff, refining their dishes(as evidenced by the surveys at the end as well as the request to tell them if something is wrong when they bring your food out), and English is not the first language(the mark of a truly authentic restaurant). With those things in mind, you will need to be patient when you come here. Things will likely speed up and improve as they work out the kinks. We ordered the gyoza appetizer which wasn't bad. I wish I would have slowed down and read the menu, as I would have gotten the appetizer sampler. There are 2 ramen choices. Shoyu(soy sauce) and Miso based. My wife got the shoyu and I got the miso. Both were quite flavorful. The noodles were good, the seasoned egg(which will look questionable to ramen rookies) and pork were excellent, and the soup base was full of flavor. I really can't compare it to most places I've had ramen at because I usually eat a tonkotsu/chashu soup base, which isn't an option here. I can say that those of you who liked Nakaya should LOVE it here. The portion sizes were good too, as we all left full and happy. I noticed that the karage chicken looked really good, and I am interested in trying their curry rice.

As others stated, the restaurant is small, which I personally think is good for now. The service was good and they were very courteous as Japanese people always are, but as I said earlier patience is needed. Everything is handcrafted by the gentlemen in the kitchen(which you can see by the way. I thought that was cool), and there is currently one waitress. The place was also immaculate in terms of cleanliness. Dosunco is definitely a welcomed addition to the area, and we look forward to coming back again!

I will begin by saying that I'm no authority on Cuban sandwiches, Italian vs Tampa vs Philly vs NY bakeries, or any of that stuff. What I do know is that this place has an AMAZING tasting Cuban sandwich. I've had a few since I've been here, and this was by far the best. They've all had the same(or variations of) standard meats, cheese, and some type of sauce/spread, but the bread is what set this one apart for me. It was soft, but somewhat sweet and flaky like a croissant, and all the flavors from the aforementioned ingredients went really well together. They make a number of other sandwiches as well, plus there was breakfast served all day. They had samples of the Sicilian pizza to try, which led to me buying a small box of it as well. We also bought some cannolis, a mini cheesecake, meat pie(also amazing), and sausage rolls. There were tons more baked goods to choose from, to include custom cakes for any occasion. The damage came to around $27, and all of us agree it was money well spent. As for the facility, it was clean and well kept, and the staff were friendly and helpful. There isn't a thing I disliked about this place, so maybe I'll be ready to give it 5 stars after finishing the sweets and my next visit. Definitely go here!

We have now been here twice and tried a lot of the menu, and can say that this place is good! The prime rib and brisket are probably our faves for the meats, with the coleslaw and fries our favorite sides. The pulled pork is really good too. The desserts are phenomenal! I've had both the regular and lemon bayou bars, and there is no way I'm resisting these things anytime I come here. We've also had several of the cupcakes, which are big, delicious, and filling. I love how the fried sides are prepared to order so they are fresh. The old school soda bottles were good to see as well, as I enjoyed a Dad's root beer. We've come late afternoon in between lunch and dinner on both occasions, and have never had a wait. Good food and decent service make this an excellent spot for BBQ in (north)Tampa.

My wife had eaten here previously with friends and came home raving about it, so I figured why not stop in before shopping at MD on an empty stomach(which is dangerous). From the outside it doesn't look like much, but once you step inside it's different. The place is very clean, neat, and dare I say nice. They have a nice selection of beer, as I am a fan of most Asian brews. The menu is pretty large, but I chose the pho with rare beef. I thought about the large bowl, but once it arrived I was glad that I did not go through with it. The regular was big enough and very tasty. They bring out the usual cilantro, bean sprouts, lime, etc, which I like adding to the second half of the soup to get a different taste. The wife and child had bowls of noodles as well and loved it. These plus 2 sodas, and an ice coffee came to just over $30, which I consider money well spent. The food came out pretty quickly, and the staff is very courteous and not overbearing. We will more than likely be stopping here every time we come to MD, as there are several items I want to try from their menu, and everything here(so far) seems to be delicious..

I didn't read the Menu close enough and Ordered a burrito not realizing there was a choice between Chicken or Steak (I thought the one I ordered only came with Chicken).   My Waiter helpfully did not ask me which meat I wanted which lead to a delightful surprise when my Burrito came with Steak anyway.

When I asked if I could have it with Chicken instead, my Amigo/Waiter informed me that they already made my Burrito!  When I asked if that meant that I couldn't have the chicken my Amigo explained that of course I could, but I would be CHARGED AGAIN for a SECOND Burrito.

Stunned, as I did not expect such a response from a waiter let a lone a long time Amigo, we began a Mexican Standoff.  Luckily since I was going to be charged $10 for a burrito whether I ate it or not, I decided to let him live and eat my unwanted yet somehow already paid for Burrito.  OR I could make a scene and have an even more uncomfortable lunch.

When we inquired about the policy of "No Take Backs" at Plaza Azteca the Hilarious manager explained that they are trying to work on Waiter mistakes by having a wonderfully progressive and totally legal policy of  MAKING THE WAITERS PAY out of their own pocket for any food that is sent back. But for all our troubles he did offer us....well nothing.  

Actually he did offer us something, he offered us the advice that next time it happens we should just call the manager so HE could explain to us why we are totally, totally wrong.  Next time....

I feel bad for the number of birds that will have to die as a result of Crispy Bird.

I ordered the Chicken Breast meal and it was a large breast - just the way I like it. The breast was juicy, tons of meat and satiating. Ok, now back to my review of the meal. When you eat the chicken breast with the accoutrements (pickles, slaw), it's quite tasty. On its own, I wouldn't rank it in my fried chicken Top 10. The slaw was the best part of the meal.

As a side, we ordered the Mac and cheese and it's not creamy and dreamy. It has a Parmesan topping that some may love, but wasn't my thing. Clearly the three people who gave Crispy Bird 5 stars loved it.

A real turn off was when we sat down, I asked to order the chicken skins and was told "we prefer to have your whole order at once so we can time the meal." Listen, if I want my chicken skins, bring me my damn chicken skins. Hindsight he was probably trying to do me a favor because I didn't love them although the aioli was a nice touch.

Cool vibe, neat decor, average food. I love me some fried chicken so was a bit disappointed. I'd prefer Joellas on 96th.

OMG! I was on vacation with my family, was really craving mexican food. I tried Vallartas wasnt impressed. I couldnt believe they call themselves a mexican restaurant. I wanted Carne Asada and it was Rib Eye. I asked around a few places for a great Mexican restaurant and Casa Ramos was recommended. I was really impressed with the facility. It was nice and clean. Staff was really friendly and food was to the table promptly.

I had the carne asada here, it took me back to my roots growing up in Southern California. It was like home cooking. Real Mexican food in my opinion. It was great.

We had Gino as our server he gave us great service, the host and wait staff were friendly. 

Overall experiece 10 stars, I love it love it love it. I wish there was a place like this closer to where I live currently

Want a very unique dining experience with an awesome series of bites, look no further. BUT
If you have made the choice in your life to be a vegan, or not eat red meat, or not like fish or raw stuff, or not arrive at a reservation a bit early, or grill the waitperson about items on the menu even at Waffle House, or just not able to go with the flow in a dining situation, go elsewhere. If you have the very unfortunate affliction of food allergy, shellfish in particular, you should also pass. I pray God will deal you a better hand in your next incarnation.

It's dinner around a bar with no menu or choices. Many small courses, all super-duper. I won't describe the food, that's above my skill level. 

Hot tips - If you like to drink, go sober and order the wine accompaniment. There are several wines served with the meal that are very interesting and exciting. They also serve a cocktail of some sort to begin with. You will get your money's worth and will probably need to take Uber home.

Don't go to meet up with long lost old friends. This is like going to a show and you are part of the performance. Take your Honey, partner or old rugby mate so you can really dig in and eat. 

Be on time, this ain't like the movies where you can dawdle because you know there will be 30 minutes of previews. If you are like me and approaching senior status, get the first seating. This is a 2.5 hour feast and you don't want your face in the plate. That sounds long but the hits just keep rolling off the cook-top. 

There is discussion about the chef leaving and having a new one. I have been there just once and it was with the new chef. It was a damn fine dinner and he, like the others on the groovy staff, was very attentive. 

Lastly, it is expensive. With the wine accompaniment and gratis included, a shade above $400.00. For that you could get the best seats in the house for the Barry Manilow concert at Bridgestone, burgers,  beer and parking. I'm glad my girlfriend chose Catbird for her birthday instead.

If you are desperate for a casino, I guess this place will do.

My biggest problem with this place -- it reeks of stale smoke throughout the casino.  I've been in lots of casinos all around the country, and this is one is bad.  I couldn't take it after a while.  Then they spray some kind of deodorant product that makes it even worse.  Ugh.

There are lots of games that they don't have here -- craps, roulette, etc.  Unless you count the electronic versions... (I don't).

There are lots of slot machines, but not enought of the cutting edge new and fresh machines.  I don't personally think they pay all that well, but that is just my experience and I may have had a bad day.

We were there on a Wednesday night after dinner, and the table miniumums were pretty high.  I saw a few $15 min, but most were $25.

Oh -- and no free drinks on the gambling floor.

After an evening, I pretty much had my fill of this place for the foreseeable future.

Though i have long been mourning the loss of Jojo's and their fried wontons, I was giddy with excitement when I heard an Indian street food joint decided to take over  ... 

Kati rolls have long been a street food staple of urban populous in bustling cities like Kolkata and Mumbai and have recently garnered some attention stateside, mostly in NYC. Though I admit it did take a bit long for philly to catch up on the trend, I am glad Spice End is doing it right.

One has a variety of options for the fillings , but the concept is simple, a plethora of flavors from spices, marinated meats and dash of seasonings all bundled into one thin crispy paratha, to pack a punch all the way  to the last bite.

We sampled the Achari chicken and paneer .. Which was well marinated and tangy cos of the Indian pickles (more of a lime or a mango base in contrast to a vinegar base). Also got a Frankie ( the egg and chicken ) or as I call it the Mumbai burrito where the Paratha is doubled up with an egg base on the griddle. The aloo (potato) paneer had a nice kick to it too.

They all went well with the red and the white sauces provided on the side, so i guess you can't go much wrong from blindly picking one from the menu. Though if you do feel lost, the staff is nice and friendly enough to help you pick something. I will prolly try and go back and try the platters sometime soon ... 

So If a ravenous hunger pang beckons 2 of these rolls should do the trick ,  though one roll will easily satiate those late night munchies given that they are also open till late on most nights.

P.S : They also stack ThumsUp and Limca in the fridge, some potent Indian soda if you feel inundated with spices.

Ever since I heard about a Chutney company opening near my neighborhood, I had to revisit stalking 101, as I scouted the area each day waiting in eager anticipation for the opening of this place. Well finally yesterday was the fateful day when they opened the doors to the public. 

A bunch of us might be accustomed to a different variety of the indian fare with the likes of curries and naans, this time around the adventure is headed to the  peninsular regions of south india. Albeit south indian cuisine hasn't achieved mainstream aura in Philadelphia , this certainly marks a step in the right direction. 

A chutney can be refered to as any sweet, tangy or sour accompaniment to the main dishes. The traditional ways to make chutneys is to crush into a paste a bunch of ingredients using a contraption similar to a mortar and pestle, and diluted using either water, lime vinegar , tamarind or coconut paste. There is no limitation to what can be transformed into a chutney and with imagination running amok there are endless possibilities. And that's what I expect from the phila chutney company to surprise me each and every visit.

I tried all the wet chutneys, and other than the traditional coconut that is a staple south indian chutney, I highly recommend the mango and the tomato chutneys. The coconut chutney needed a little more kick as I felt it was a bit mellow for my palate. Nonetheless the ingredients were very fresh and flavorful.

Coming to my next favourite item on the menu - the Dosas. A distant cousin to the french crepes and Ethiopian injera, are primarily made of a mixture of rice and lentils and the batter is left to ferment overnight, and spread thinly over a hot pan glazed with either butter or traditional ghee. With a different permutations to the ingredients and the way of spreading across the pan, a few varieties like Rava ( semolina ) and Uttapams  can be made.  They can be just had as is or even stuffed with things that you like to savor. 

Though back home I'd devour a whole army of plain dosas, doing the same at a restaurant is not a financially sound proposition so go with some filling inside the dosas to satiate the stomach. The common fillings are the spiced mashed potatoes masala, cheese, chillies, Spinach, onions etc. We ordered the paneer dosa, a masala dosa and a deluxe masala. The latter ones stole the show as the masala was evenly spiced and with no clunky pieces of uncooked potatoes made it a stellar choice. The deluxe had the cheese and spinach in it as was certainly my favourite, though the fried paneer and the caramelized onions were a close second. The batter is perfectly portioned, which helps the dosa to be nice and crispy  to bring out a plethora of flavors to the forefront.

Albeit they are still fairing in uncharted waters, they were welcoming of any suggestions to make improvements and make the experience better. There are still a bunch of kinks that need to be ironed out, but there is great promise about this place. They go to great distances to cater to ur specific tastes if u asked.

In conclusion, My cousin said my face was glowing when I ordered my dosa and the pretty much sums up my visit here, and am certainly looking forward to more such outings.

Well I have to confess that I was not that big of a cupcake fan, as there have been many a evil cupcakes that have marred my dessert experience. But going to Philly cupcake has changed all that. 

The place is right on the way between my house and my train station, and i have to admit i have exchanged many a fleeting glances with this place, and yesterday I gave into my urge to please my sweet tooth and pay them a visit. 

This place is like willy wonka meets a chic LA boutique. the backroom houses the machinery that churns out these deliciously looking treats, and the front has swanky closets that house their latest batches of cupcakes. As soon as u enter u r greeted by one of staff who hands out a flier of the days offerings. Other than the cupcakes there are Hot and cold drinks to choose from, but i was too distracted by the fresh baked smell of cupcakes to even bother with drinks. 

U can choose ur poison from a matching of different cakes with different icings combo. I had the tough dilemma to choose between the red velvet and the Carrot Cake with the CheeseCake icing, though I went with the latter. What i was surprised by was the innovative idea to use a plastic glass as a To-Go container, it looks so good that u have second thoughts of biting into it. 

The good news is that it  it tastes as good as it looks, the cake was fluffed to perfection, the carrot gives it a dense texture and the Nuts and Resins enhance the flavor. the Cheesecake was also smooth and pretty much melts into the cake with each bite, making for a dynamic duo. The ratios of icing to cake was spot on too.

They do have a website, http://www.phillycupcake.com/, though I wish they added some more info on that. They only accept cash and offer takeouts.

In summary, i am happy to see a cupcake shop in my hood that along with great cupcakes have a charming staff, a great setup that one would like to visit often. So to keep in sync with my new year resolutions i have decided to "Run"  to the Philly cupcake shop as much as possible.

We made reservations for four and were not seated until over an hour following the reservation time. It was over an hour after we were seated that we received our meals. We were informed by our server and management that "we were next" and that there was a large party that tied up the kitchen. 

Prior to ordering I verified that the kitchen could accommodate food allergies and specified what I could not consume. I was concerned and did not touch the plate - lucky for me because the manager ran to our table minutes later to inform me the food contained ingredients I was allergic to. 

Our waiter, even with these circumstances, was great and doing the best he could in this environment. The managements inability to successfully handle reservations and deliver meals in a respectable amount of time is astounding. The kitchen potentially killing patrons due to their inability to meet the request they guaranteed - that is even more concerning.

After speaking with management regarding our experience a round of drinks was taken off our our bill, which apparently was a big deal for them.

I HAVE A BRAND NEW JEEP...
And it is in a super sexy shiny black that shows dirt.
And Kin is blocks from the awesome Rich's Wash Dat.
So after the "sit in your car" experience I stop at Kin.
But only because it's on the way home, not because it is all that.

SOGGY DUMPLINGS, BLAND RAMEN, DECENT WINGS
I predict that once the sheen of myriad fawning reviews has worn off, Kin will be as relevant as one-time wunderkind Rebellion in the Warehouse District. 

Oh wow, I just checked and Rebellion has closed.

just sayin...

MORE A LOCAL BELLWETHER THAN A GOOD SANDWICH: I was lunching here in 2001 on the day Governor Edwin Edwards was found guilty on 17 of 26 counts. Of all the places that #1 ranked local WWL TV could choose to gaige the quintessential natives' reaction they chose Serio's.  Coincidentally, today I dodged another WWL interview when they again selected Serio's to capture the true locals' opinion on the conviction of Mayor Ray Nagin, guilty on 20 of 21 counts.  NOLA may seem to be changing, but thankfully, Serio's continues to be a bastion of old school authenticity & opinion.

THE "GREENIE" WAS DRY, PRICEY, UNFLAVORFUL & didn't seem dressed.  But then Leidenheimer tends to suck up the maynez, so ask for extra. A single 7" with a side of potato salad & tap water totaled a whopping $12.

BETTER NEARBY MUFFALETTAS: Reuben's (900 block Gravier) but ask for extra olive salad; Welty's Deli (300 block Camp); Cajun Mike's awesome Muff panini (100 block Baronne); & Butcher makes a good Bronze Medal version.

.

DIM THE LIGHTS...
What a horrible pun, but the sentiment is correct. I'd seen reviews from respected locals that dinner was subpar so I went for breakfast. The fact that I was one of only two seated tables at 10:30AM was not that surprising, but I was not prepared that it would take 15 minutes to get my food. Especially given that it was one of just two house specialties: Porcheta Hash and Eggs. The pork belly was indiscernible, the hollandaise had no taste at all and the eggs had to be two of the smallest specimens of ovi I've ever cut into: $14 (see teenie pic).

NEARBY BETTER AND CHEAPER BREAKFASTS:
P&G, Ruby Slipper, Café Conti, Majoria's Commerce, Merchant, Jimmy J's, Daisy Dukes, McDonald's (but not the one at Canal & Royal where that guy stabbed two people in August).

MENU PRICES ARE 20% HIGHER THAN WEB
I totally agree with Marielle on this place. It's way over priced. I spent $18 on 2 shrimp bao and a very underwhelming chicken salad. If it were an upscale atmosphere with adequate air conditioining (of which it has neither) then it might earn a bit of that price point. They were also very irritated when, after sweating through several napkins at the claustrophobic bar, I changed my order to take-out rather than dine-in.

WHERE I'D RATHER SPEND LESS THAN THAT $18:
1. Nearby: "Breads on Oak's" amazing $4 almond croissant, "Refuel" (the best loaded grits in town with coffee $12), "Milk Bar's" $10 'Shrimpley the Best' sammy, "Moe's BBQ" (meat + 2 sides & drink; $11), "Camelia Grill's" classic cheeseburger, fries & chocolate freeze $14.
2. Asian: "Thai Mint" (awesome 3-course $10 lunch), "Lilly's" (our best vietnamese, imho), "Moon Wok" (best prices and an outstanding $6 Goi Ga Chicken salad), #1 "Red's" seems pricier but most entrées feed two.

A GREAT BURGER!!!
I have found only *three old school char-burger places left in the city. They all serve 1/2 pounds of quality beef, topped with shredded cheddar, on undersized buns with a baked potato side. Lakeview Harbor is one of the three.

THE PICTURE IS A CLASSIC
You should be able to tell by my photo that this thick medium rare juicy burger is a satisfying rare delicacy.

BUT OTHERWISE THIS IS A SHODDY RESTAURANT 
It's reminiscent of a college town bar that happens to have a restaurant buried between the video arcade and foosball table.

* Trolley Stop, D'Mac's.

COZY WAKIN' BAKIN' is suitably located on perhaps one of our quaintest commercial streets: gracefully tree-lined Banks.  To me this part of Mid City is the most old-school neighborhood in town.  Sort of the folksy Midwest of New Orleans.  The vibe at the café reflects this charm.  The morning I was there a family of five was celebrating a birthday.  One of the gifts was a handmade quilt patched from scraps of clothing significant to their past: a panel from a bridesmaid's dress, an uncle's favorite khaki workshirt, a younger brother's first communion suit.  It's a special place that can carry off an occasion like that.  But then it fit-in seamlessly amidst the other diners: a solitary priest, an older couple with a walker, burly construction workers, and a runner taking a break on his 10 mile jog.

AFFORDABLE: platter of pancrepes, 2 eggs, housemade sausage, iced coffee: $12!

THIS REALLY SHOULD BE A HOOTERS
or a Walk Ons or Dave & Busters. The old Phil's Gril is steeped in history but it's totally awkward as an intimate dining room. The long narrow space is windowless, cheerless, high ceilinged and dark. It's like being on a contrived restaurant set inside a sound stage.

EVER EAT CHILI WITH A HEAD COLD?
You keep expecting to taste those rich flavors but all you experience is the heat? The curry udon at Rebellion is like that. It's a beautifully golden bowl that is oddly lacking in any taste whatsoever. Given that it was a whopping $14 for a smallish scoop (see pic), I salvaged my investment with salt and several lemons from the service bar.

WAY BETTER NEARBY LUNCHES LESS THAN $14
Carmo (the Brazillian Salad is both filling and healthy and just $9), Cochon Butcher (the best counter cafe in the city), Pêche (believe it or not, all soup, salads, snacks and small plates are $12 or less, but the $11 fish sticks are amazing), Welty's Deli (the CBD's hidden gem family-run sandwich shop).

MINIMALISM RIDICULISM 
Yet another bit of bourgie fluff vending low margin wares (how in the heck do these new places cover their overhead?). The build-out is impersonal and consequently hackneyed: colorless hues of grey-white and steel-gray, slick low profile cabinets, back-lit shelving and bleached wood. If you throw some scarlet red pillows on the benches it would resemble most guppies' apartments in 1984. 

REVELATOR TAKE-OUT TAKEAWAYS:
1. They only serve whole milk, no cream or skim
2. They only allow simple syrup, no sweeteners
3. They don't have large-sized drinks
4. My iced coffee was bitter.

MUCH BETTER NEARBY COFFEE SHOPS:
French Truck (their New Orleans Iced is my favorite in the city); Merchant (illy Coffee and crepes in a functionally upscale space); New Orleans Coffee & Beignets (a local chain but they have half-and-half as well as pink/blue/yellow packets); the Keurig machine at Sherwin Williams on Decatur...

A PROMISING NEW CEMETERY-SIDE EATERY
But sandwiches are $9-$12 which is pricey for what you don't get. Even at nearby "Milk Bar" which has arguably the best sandwiches in town, all are under $10 including the generously stuffed Shrimply.

THAT PRICEY ONION RING MOCKED ME 
plumply crisping in its fry basket. But oddly substitutions aren't allowed and as a $5 add-on the cost of my lunch would've ballooned to $17 pre-tax. And that's without a drink! At local gold-standard "St James Cheese Co." most sandwiches are $10 and include a fresh side salad. Luca's unremarkable house kettle chips seem more like a garnish. I wish some of their interesting sides were options: the hummus, fried bell peppers, corn grits, etc.

WHA...? NO FOUNTAIN DRINKS?
Many counter spots in the neighborhood include soft drinks like "Moe's" where all huge bbq plates are less than $12 and come with 2 sides and free refills. At "Bud's" a burger platter with rings and a 32oz is just $9. Fountain service also keeps you from having to get back in queue.

THE BEST VIBE OF THE THEO'S
There is something about this space that lends itself to casual dining. Maybe it is the spaciousness of the dining room. Perhaps it's the $10 (after-tax) individual pizza & a beverage lunch deal with counter gratuity. Or those big windows over looking a tree lined section of Canal, picturesquely framing the occasional streetcar.

A REAL THIN CRUST PIZZA
Is Theo's one of the only parlors that offers extra-thin as its default crust? A true local neighborhood mainstay.

OH NO SHE BETTER DON'T!

Me:
(wide eyed with excitement over a new menu)
 "Oooh tell me about the 'drawn-butter remoulade' on your lobster po'boy."

Owner: 
(with deadpan snarkiness)
 "Remoulade is remoulade. It's the same everywhere. I don't know what more to tell you."

OH HELL-TO-THE-NO!
Hold my earrings girl, that b!t@h just threw me shade!
...no smile
...no "hello"
...no "you're welcome".

BUSINESS (OR LACK OF IT) BEFORE CUSTOMERS
Once this harridan was rid of me, she unprofessionally scurried to her bookkeeping splayed-out in the dining room, taking calls and texts (see pics). And although I was her only patron she was too busy running her culinary empire to be polite: 
...never asked how my lobster was (darn tasty actually)
...whether I liked the controversial remoulade (which I did)
...and unforgivably, didn't even thank me as I left!

NEWLY OPENED WITH LOTS OF POTENTIAL
- same group that opened DeVille in the Quarter last year
- most savories are about $9, sweet are $6 (some splitable)
- Orleans Coffee Exchange sources the brews
- counter service with seating inside for 20, outside 6
- generous hours 8AM to 9PM daily.

BUT THERE ARE KINKS...
- my sweet crêpe was tepid, the nutella sloppily dolloped
- there's no water or take-out station so you have to re-queue
- the ambience is off-putting, like stalls in a horse barn;

AND THE VIBE: DETACHED? SMUG? OHIO-AN?
- when I asked the transplant barista where the coffee was sourced I was met with a snarl. "Why do you want to know?" 
- not one of the four behind the counter told me when my go-box was ready nor did they thank me: "yeah that's yours".

...it's the genteel niceties that separate us from the carpetbaggers, no?

It was therapeutic to see old friends: a mix of ages, races, incomes, and sexes. All of us craving normalcy, a spa-like retreat from sallow water lines, decadent cabana service on a weekday afternoon; none of us working much, many living off of insurance payouts.

6/2/15: BUT I HAVEN'T BEEN BACK!
There are now way too many more affordable restaurants in the area that get my dollars!

QUIEN DAT! 
A fun balance of the New Orleans and Mexican cultures. And, everything is house made from the freshly fried chips, tomatillo salsa, flautas, etc.

OCH PIONEER! 
I moved to the Lower Garden in 1986 into one of those cool balconied spaces in the 1800 block.  However, living in the Irish Channel back then carried a lot of risk. The adjacent St. Thomas Housing Project was a virtual war zone and by 1988 Angela Hill reported on New Orleans' "murder a day" crime rate.  At that time, aside from a scuzzy Church's Chicken there was only one restaurant between Felicity and Jackson: Pizza Roma.  This tiny take-out was owned by a burly Greek named Haluk who saw potential in that blighted neighborhood. The man was a unique character and many's the night I would help him split a bottle of Ouzo at a street side table, his loaded shotgun resting atop. Eventually he expanded to Sophie Wright as Café Roma and the area boomed. Casa Borrega is a similar pioneer on OCH. It's owned by Hugo, an ebullient Mexican-born New Orlenian that has lived here over half his life. Yes, the food and drinks are outstanding but it's his vision and dedication that truly set this magical place apart.

I'M CAUTIOUSLY OPTIMISTIC
Two reviewers that I highly respect (Shannon S. and Elaine M.) had bad experiences here so I wasn't expecting much. Hopefully management read their reviews and made changes, or maybe I just ordered the right thing, because I had a really good lunch here today and at an affordable price.

BEST $10.90** (SEE PICS) I'VE SPENT IN MONTHS 
- I had the huge, 2-mealer, pastrami on lightly toasted rye with swiss*
- with a flavorful cup of dark-rouxed roasted tomato spinach soup
- one of the best housemade 1000 Island's I've had locally;
- I hear the chicken is good but it's only served at dinner.

THE STAFF WERE ENGAGING, SPACE CHEERY
Unlike pricey glum Red Dog diner down the road, the bar staff here were friendly, efficient and good conversationalists! It's cleaner than nearby Bulldog, Slim Goody's  or Fat Harry's. Martin's still ranks as my favorite among similar restaurants uptown, but I'll definitely be back.

*their Reuben without sauerkraut
**after-tax

WORST SERVICE I'VE HAD IN OVER 2 YEARS:
I selected Dickie's to host a visiting restauranteur today.

1. I'd made a reservation with my local 504 area code.
2. I requested a center table indicating that it was a special occasion. 
3. I was the only patron in a suit & tie amidst the unwashed tourists.
