4. The restaurant was 1/2 empty after 1PM, and yet despite all that
THEY SAT US IN FRONT OF THE SWINGING KITCHEN DOORS!

"we're trying to spread people out among the servers"

5. Our absent waiter was closing-out so lunch crept to over 2 hours.
6. There was no butter with the bread nor water on the table.
7. We weren't offered a Coolinary menu nor was there a printed copy.
8. They don't set separate butter knives nor proper soup spoons.
AND THE ROUX WAS THE HUE OF INGESTED METAMUCIL!

9. Our bill was overcharged twice for wine.
10. One Coolinary was tallied a la carte and thus $7 over.
11. Our unapologetic waiter wadded up the incorrect bill before us: nice
12. I eat out a lot, you can't make this sh__ up.
TWO $19.98 COOLINARIES, 1 GLASS OF WINE: $82 !?!?!!?!

WAY BETTER CBD/FQ LUNCH SERVICE:
Mr. B's, Salon, Trenasse, R'evolution, Criollo, Tableau, August, Domenica, a $2 greasy weener tepidly sliding upon the rollers at Kwiky Mart...

BEST BURGER IN NEW ORLEANS!
Finally a consistently superior sandwich. The "Fharmacy" starts with a hefty patty of locally sourced freshly-ground beef. Unlike thinner versions, the only way to get a medium-rare burger with a nice seer is to form it thick. The clean flavors of their house giardiniera aren't oily like jarred versions. The pickles, aioli and bacon jam are also made on site. Melted provolone holds it all together with the thin bun rightfully relegated to it's utilitarian purpose. (See my cross-section pic). With fries the whole platter is just $12.

PREDICTION
French Toast will become so popular that it will quickly outgrow this postage stamp footprint and move into one of the nearby closed storefronts. It's food is mid-priced, unique and well prepared.

STANLEY POST KATRINA
That restaurant was one of a handful that opened before Thanksgiving in 2005. It's reuben became so wildly popular with the $300 per/diem FEMA officers that they quickly moved to their current Jackson Square site. French Toast will too.

PRO-TIP
Abelskivers are your most economically filling choice.
Go for,the jams and the fresh lemon curd sauces.

A HEALTH FOOD "TAQUERIA" all items prepared in front of you to order;
ABOUT THE BEST VEGETARIANISH café in the Quarter/CBD.
AFFORDABLE: all non-seasonal  wraps & salads less than $10; Cup of soup $3!

I've been on a search for fresh ingredient, healthy lunch options in the French Quarter/CBD.  As you can imagine, most New Orleans restaurants serve foods either fried, slathered in cheese or cream sauces, wrapped in white bread or atop pasta, or laden with preservatives and sugar.  Here are my findings for the 5 most notable:

#1.  The Best:  "CARMO".  There is really no way to go wrong at this open kitchen café.  Unhealthy ingredients are replaced with interesting combinations of tropical spices, nuts, raisins, & fruit.  And none of the large, filling salads are more than $9! 

#2.  Close Second:  "CITY GREENS".  Sort of a high end, healthy gourmet "Subway" but not that much more expensive.  All wraps & salads are less than $10, & items are made to order.

#3.  Faux-getarian:  "BACK TO THE GARDEN". Although it claims to be vegetarian, 90% of all items include cheese, starches or dairy based condiments.  But it's cheap, fast and items are customizable.

#4.  Price Gougers:  "MEALS FROM THE HEART".  Not really vegetarian, in fact besides the smoothies everything has cheese, eggs, and bread. The menu is inventive however, but pricey: $9 pancakes?  $11 omelets?

#1,000,000.  Dead Last!  "GREEN GODDESS".  Probably the most true vegetarian options but it's also outrageously expensive: a $10 Wedge Salad??  And what's with the unhealthy cheese selection that's over half the menu?  Note To Vegetarians: cheese is not healthy and much worse for you than lean meat!

OVER-FRIED, OVER-BAKED, UNDER-BRÛLÉED
My photos speak for themselves. Also view Yelper pics of the singed fried chicken. Then compare that to my photo of the golden crispy tenders from Keys Fuel Mart (some of the best in town - if you don't get whacked by a machete wielding crazy***). The pigs in blankets were so torched that their brittle carapaces' unimpressive weeners were shriveled to the point of embarrassment.

RETRO VIBE (c. 1997 ABERCROMBIE & FITCH)
From the boxy blond wood cubbies to the waifish servers in gingham checked button-downs, the face of Willa Jean is both progressively anti-hipster but also stiltedly retail. At one point I believe I actually saw a server skein prepping napkins a la Gap-folding-board.  

PRO-TIP: instead of six dry single pigs for $9 at Willa Jean, walk two blocks to "Haro" and get three of their perfect Central Texas kolaches stuffed with several juicy sausages in bubbly jalapeño cheese for the same price!

***true incident reported 16 July 2015.

1 OF 7 RESTAURANTS I HAD TO REVISIT BEFORE MOVING OUT OF THE QUARTER. Yep, after almost 20 years I'm happily headed back Uptown! So this final week I've decided to follow my cravings and Mona Lisa is a "must do" for the:

MONA LISA'S SPECIAL PO'BOY is one of those sinfully delicious treats that I occasionally get the envies for. Decadent layers of pepperoni, ham, Canadian bacon, Mozarella, mushrooms and black olives toasted bubbly on a large butter roll.  Even better, it comes with a generous portion of pasta salad and costs just $9.50! It would be splittable if it wasn't so addicting.

TIP: order it without lettuce, it wilts into a tart goo when the sandwich is toasted.

BEST SANDWICH I HAD OUT OF THE 150 EATERIES THAT I TRIED IN 2013! The $8.50 sautéed "SHRIMPLY THE BEST" is light with a perfect pairing of red onion, pesto, mozzarella and lemon aioli. It's larger & has over twice the shrimp than Killer PoBoys' similar coriander seared $12 version & is 30% cheaper!!!

THAT BREAD IS AMAZING! soft with a buttery chewy crust, not thick and doughy.  Skip the tomatoes!  These sandwiches have such deliciously unique and clear toned flavors that a lowly Roma just gets in the way.

JEEZ THEY'RE FRIENDLY HERE!  From the chef in the goofy Christmas antlers to the bubbly counter waiter, this is a happy place.

2013 FAVORITES:
- Sandwich: MILK BAR, "Shrimply the Best"
- Appetizer: M BISTRO, "Jambalaya Tempura Fritters"
- Best Restaurant:  COQUETTE
- Breakfast: JIMMY J'S, "Monte Cristo & Home Fries"
- Burger: COWBELL, "Cheeseburger with Agogo"
- New Cafe: MISTER GREGORY'S,"Traditional Croque"
- Prix Fixe Lunch: CRIOLLO, "Osso Buco"
- Price Value: MOJO LOUNGE, "Thai Wrap, $7.50"
- Salad: CARMO, "The Brazilian"

THE BEST LUNCH I'VE HAD IN OVER A YEAR
and it was their $20, 3-course Coolinary. After a month of disappointing meals at some of our "all-the-rage" trendy new restaurants ("Cane & Table", "Johnny Sanchez", "Rebellion", etc.), I wasn't prepared to like this café in a hotel. However, the handsome yet unpretentious Trenasse impressed me course after course.

JUST LOOK AT MY PHOTOS!
The House Salad: locally farm-sourced, today it included field peas, sautéed parsnips and cucumbers. I was wisely directed to pair it with their corn cilantro "bisque-ish" creamy dressing. I wanted another, but then came...
The Crawfish Pie: (Wednesday's Special) is hand's down the best I've ever had. It's a cocotte with pie crust as delicate as my mother's. A thick spicy filling of heavy cream and cheese bouys its huge chunks of berled bugs.**
The Crème Brûlée: is a long slab of carmelized sugar adhering atop a thin layer of custard cream. Why is it served so oddly? More surface area for that crunchy crust baby!

**Not only does Trenasse smoke it's own meats on their Perdido banquette, they even catch a lot of their own fish!

OF COURSE IT'S THE BEST FRENCH 75 IN TOWN
albeit pricey and never on happy hour. It'll set you back $13.00. Even today on Bastille Day it was full retail.

SOUFFLÉ POTATOES: HOW WE ATE THEM AS KIDS
Okay so this requires ordering an extra side of hollandaise and double dunking. First dip then bite off just the very end of the puff. Then scoop up the sauce and let it ooze and puddle at the bottom. This gives you a sort of gourmet Cheeto (see pic).

A CLASSIC FRIDAY BAR CRAWL ITINERARY:
Start with Old Fashioneds at breezy 21st Amendment about 3 PM-ish, then a Sazerac at the renown Carousel Bar, followed by Happy Hour (4-6 PM) and $4 small-plates at the Bombay Club with a Pimm's Cup, then a French 75 here with soufflé potatoes, grab some apps and a Ramos Gin Fizz at Broussard's Bar and end up at the Davenport Lounge for jazz (9 PM) and Brandy Milk Punch.

N.B.
Both the bar and kitchen open at 5 PM...an important fact absent from the website.
I ordered the Bulgogi cheesesteak and it was good but I would only give it a 4 out of 5. The fries are seasoned and delicious.

I have to give Seminole Hard Rock a five star rating because every time I stay here, they confuse me with Primo the famous rockstar and upgrade me to a jacuzzi suite. 

I can't explain the treatment any other way. I've never played a dollar at any of the slots or table games, other than some poker. I don't have a players card, and I don't have any connections at the hotel. Yet every time I'm there I get the upgrade, and that makes Primo so happy. 

The jacuzzi room is awesome. Mini hallway leads to a huge bathroom with rain-shower and giant jacuzzi with sliding windows that open to the bedroom. Plush robe, bath salts, loofah and green-tea soap products... I'm in heaven! Did I mention the two guitar-shaped chocolates on the king size bed? 

Although I'm a big Starwood and Hilton points collector, I easily forego that for the awesomeness that is Seminole Hard Rock's treatment of Primo. I'd gladly be their spokesman, I like it that much. 

Primo has but one suggestion: Add an iPod adapter to the awesome stereo A/V system, and this room would be complete.

Boo, once again. I've dined here many times, in both the old and new locations. I've now officially grown weary of worrying going there will result in great experience (which it has on many occasions) or a bad experience to which I walk out thinking that I'll never go back despite the wonderful food. Last night's experience tells me I'm done - it's just too risky to potentially have a pleasant evening out ruined by/rude service and now inept hostesses. Boo, Susanna, Boo!

This place is as beautiful as it looks on Instagram. With endless options, diverse selections and a lovely setting, Auction House is a welcome addition to my rotation of lunch options.

Auction House is a food hall with a number of different outposts that range in cuisine from Mexican to Indian to coffee to rolled ice cream. I purchased a number of different things, including empanadas (Empanola), breakfast tacos (Sola Deli), and chargrilled oysters (Elysian Seafood). Each outpost has a different price range, but you can expect to spend about $15-$20 for lunch. In the center of the space is a bar that has standard drinks as well as an impressive list of cute cocktails.

I visited early on a Sunday morning and was pleased to find little to no crowd. The place itself is very open and spacious, but there aren't a whole lot of seats. I imagine at lunchtime or happy hour things can get crowded, but with the decor and styling, I doubt it ever looks cramped.

Each outpost is different, but all of the vendors were kind and friendly, explaining menu options and specials. Staff walks around, clearing tables and delivering water (there is also a water and cup station nearby). For the most part, you walk up to a counter and wait to pick up your food, so there is no table service.

Auction House provides endless food options and a perfect Instagram backdrop, making it worth the visit.

I'm a firm believer in waiting to visit new restaurants - I like to give them a chance to work out the kinks, and in the case of Morrow's, wait for the crowds to die down.

I waited until late June to visit Morrow's and overall I was not disappointed, but I was not impressed either. It was a good, but not great, experience. 

The space itself is SMALL. I can imagine during dinner or even lunch you might have to wait for a table. While waiting for a table is not an issue, Morrow's offers little to no waiting space. If the bar is full and you have to wait, you'll be standing. 

I visited for an early dinner, around 4 PM, and was seated at the bar right away. Here, I was disappointed to learn that the happy hour special is strictly well drinks, despite the website advertising "cocktails." Not quite the case - it's well cocktails only, no specials on appetizers or anything else. Definitely not the place to go for happy hour.

The menu had a solid variety of options for dinner, including New Orleans classics. I opted for the charbroiled oysters and Cajun crawfish pasta. I was pleasantly surprised at the generous portion size - the oysters were HUGE, the pasta included large pieces of catfish (more than I could eat) and an appropriate sauce to crawfish ratio. The food did take a while to come out - something I'll chalk up to the restaurant's newness - but it was hot and what I expected when I ordered. The food was tasty, but nothing exceptional in terms of taste, standard New Orleans fare.

The customer service, however, is exceptional. Everyone was warm and friendly and our bartender, Corey, is a superstar! Not only were the drinks served consistently and strong, Corey is truly a passionate bartender, sharing the history of Hennesey with us and making drink suggestions based on our food.

Overall, Morrow's is a place to see and be seen (and take pictures for Instagram), but I wasn't blown away - in a city of exceptional dining experiences, Morrow's certainly meets expecations, but doesn't quite exceed them.

You know, I've worked in high pressure jobs, and I know working in a restaurant is right up there.  You have to deal with rude customers with a sense of entitlement, breakneck speed, kitchen mishaps and long, long hours.

So I can even understand when your house is mostly full and you see a party of four come in 30 minutes before close. You might have dreaded the idea of perhaps having to work longer and harder.  And it might have been a bad day.

But what you don't do is go up to them, ask their party size, then tell them "there's no room for you" and hand-flip them in a manner that can only be described as "Up Yours."  There was no mistaking your message, and I'm a forgiving guy.  You pissed off all of us for no good reason, and if you just didn't want us there, you could have simply politely said the kitchen couldn't take more orders, or even "there's no room", but with a modicum of courtesy.   We would have found a place open later, which we did.  

We were excited to come to your restaurant, but instead it became a problem.  With as many great places to eat in New Orleans, there's never a reason to darken your door ever again, and I'll gladly share this with anyone who listens.  I've had incredibly slow service, gotten sick at and have had drinks dumped on my head before in places that I got over and went back to because they were polite, had good food and gave a simple apology.

Louisiana Bistro sinks below the floorboards of any of these places.

The most unique experience I have ever had as a Californian local coming to Tennessee. This is a must if you want to understand part of the local food culture.

We sat down in communal tables and were placed with people we didn't know. It was very interesting and they have a rule that you're not allowed to use phones at the table. It is essentially a all-you-can-eat except they choose which dishes they want for you. On the table was preset with apple juice, lemonade, sweet tea, and water. It was great.

There was so much food it was crazy, biscuits with gravy, cornbread with gravy, pea, turnip leaves, grilled catfish, barbeque, fried chicken, more gravy, and more bread and gravy.

Overall, I really enjoyed being able to talk to strangers and get to know people from the nearby area. It felt very homey and is an excellent example of was southern comfort feels like.

We had the pleasure of attending a wedding at this venue. Beautiful for sure! The lily pond and wisteria courtyard was dreamy in the sunset and the setup was very nice between the ceremony and reception. There's also a nice view from the hillside that includes the ocean, but it's not far from downtown at all.

I hear rooms go for $2000 a night here, but there's a great discount in limited quantity if a block is reserved by the wedding party. The rooms are separated into distinct buildings like a quaint little village and it really is cute. 

If you're in the market for a wedding venue, I have no idea how much this costs, but it's definitely worth looking into if it's in your budget.

This was a last minute breakfast decision today.  This place was unbelievably good!!  They had covered outside seating, so of course we brought our dog.  My husband ordered the burger with bacon and blue cheese, arugula and caramelized onions.  It had a potato bun.  He asked for well-done as usual, and he actually got it!  He was thrilled and said it was one of the burgers he's had!  I had the cortado coffee - I wasn't sure if I should get it - I had never had one - so glad I did! It was so thick, I ate some of it with a spoon!  It's expresso and milk and came with real chunks of sugar on the side - I savored every drop!  I had the breakfast board - WOW!!  Lot's of both sweet and savory items on it!  The board had fresh fruit, a breakfast flatbread with salmon, cheese, herbs, and avocado - yumm, a mini parfait with yogurt, granola, berries, and agave nectar - so sweet, an egg benedict- great sauce, and the best French toast I've ever had - I don't think they soaked it, but dipped it - it was perfectly crunchy on the outside with a caramelization on it that was so sweet and lightly crunchy.  There was powdered sugar and strawberries on it.  Just awesome!  The service was incredible as well - we were not forgotten about, even though we were outside.  The waiter paid special attention to our dog, bringing her water, asking her name etc... and he kept our drinks refilled, asking how we liked our food etc... we all enjoyed a perfect morning here!  We can't wait to come back because there are so many amazing sounding drinks and deserts on the menu too!

Great new wine bar in Safety Harbor. Right next to Ed's Fine Wines. In addition to an extensive wine list (from $6 to $30 per glass and over 100 selections by the bottle), they have a full menu. I tried the sausage stuffed pork tenderloin and it was fantastic. My wife had the corn soup and steak, which was was also wonderful. John and Dana, the co-owners, are very friendly and the staff is very attentive. They plan to have live jazz starting in early February, which should really liven the place up on weekends!

We're about to watch the movie and need to  eat before so Burger me is next door. The employees are friendly and helpful explaining its build your own burger. We're new it's our first time.  We order the basic meal. The cheeseburgers were okay and fries not bad. The price was $22 for two definitely to expensive. To much lettuce plus the burger had a plain taste. I don't recommend this place even though the service was polite .

I hear about this place cause many people gave it nice reviews, and that the pizza was huge.
We ordered a large pepperoni but the lady manager said were out of pepperoni so we chose ham right away a bad start. Next the waiter comes to take our order and says the pizza is huge and takes an hour to cook. 
The pizza arrives an hour later and it's huge but to much cheese and sauce the crust is not thick. As I pick up a piece everything falls off but the taste is okay.
The place is old and dirty, and the parmesan cheese shaker is not clean. We leave take the rest home let it 
sit over night, and the next day the pizza was fine.

The KBBQ cheesesteak is one of the best things I have tasted in a LONG time. We went in a little before closing but we still got great service. I wish I lived in the area so I could frequent this place because it's absolutely superb.

I feel bad to give this place only two stars because it seems like a lot of people like this place, but I really didn't think it warranted more than two stars since I've definitely experienced better. 

FOOD: I ordered the broccoli cheddar soup based on reviews and tips that it's great. Like one review also mentioned, it wasn't that great and the taste seemed off. The half turkey pesto sandwich I got was dry and couldn't taste any pesto in it. 
My fiancé ordered the steak sandwich and had asked for wheat bread because the hard roll it normally comes with is too hard for his teeth. Lo and behold, they bring it out with the hard roll. The server brought it out with the disclaimer that they forgot about putting it on the wheat bread, and they can re-make it, but it will take more time. We had been waiting much longer than expected for just soup and salad and were starving at this pointe so he opted just to take it. Bread indeed was too hard for him so he couldn't even eat the bread and ended up picking out the meat, which wasn't that tender or good anyway. 
Small cookies that come with it weren't anything special. Kind of hard. 

CUSTOMER SERVICE: The girl who took our order seemed nice. The server who brought the food at least apologized for the mistake in the bread, but I feel like they should've just re-made it so they brought out the correct order instead of bringing it out wrong. Or maybe at least bring out the wheat bread on a side dish so my fiancé could move the meat himself onto the softer bread. 

INSIDE: Inside feels like a small house restaurant like one I'd eat at in Berkeley. We sat by the front door, which didn't shut all the way unless you closed it all the way. It was cold so it sucked when people coming in and out didn't close the door all the way. I liked how they put the to go containers where people can grab them as needed instead of having to ask the staff. Neat they give you street signs instead of numbers to bring your order to the table. 

OVERALL: Unfortunately I will not be coming back. We thought this place would have gumbo and more options, but they didn't. I don't know if they sold out of gumbo or just don't sell that anymore. Also sad they didn't have a pastrami sandwich, which is pretty standard for most sandwich joints.

To go experience. 
CALL IN: guy was nice on the phone and made sure I was calling the right location because he said many people make that mistake. Nice day of him to prevent a common mistake, that's good customer service right there. Yes it was the location across Costco I was wanting. 

FOOD: I liked the Titan roll with cooked salmon and raw salmon on top with lemon slices. The lemon slices cook the tops of the raw salmon slightly and is a great citrus flavor that merges well with the salmon. 
I liked the Buckley roll even more with cooked scallops. Sweet taste. 
Gyoza was crispy but had more extra edging than what I'm used to. Dipping sauce was good too. To go sauce container is hard to dip into since the gyoza has wide edging it doesn't quite fit. 
Salad was good with the dressing. Like a Japanese coleslaw. 
Fruit strawberries didn't seem that fresh but maybe because it's not strawberry season. Orange slices were sweet. 
Gave us an extra albacore which was super nice of them. 

SPEED: said it'd be ready 10-15 minutes and indeed we were there in fifteen minutes and the food was ready!

OVERALL: I will be coming back to try their all you can eat! I'll do an updated review when I do.

We were staying at the hotel nearby and needed some stuff, so we came here to get a few things and noticed that they had a large amount of King's cakes available and since my family never had any before, I had to get a decent size one for us, and also use it as my husband's birthday cake. 

We didn't get the usual flavor for King's Cake, but we went with the strawberry one, which was just right and my kids loved the flavor. They also loved the babies on the cake and kept it as a souvenir. 

The cashier was really sweet and talked and interacted with my kids while she rang us up. Love the convenience and the friendly service!

I loved sucre, it's adorable and the shop from the outside as well as the inside is really pretty! It's like you stepped out in France all of a sudden because most of their dessert shops are like this. 

My kids went straight for the gelato and I got myself a box of macarons, they even had king cake inspired macaons for us to taste, so I had to get one. The flavors for the macarons are unique and NOLA flavors, at that. My husband got the white chocolate raspberry bar and it was really pretty and delicious at the same time! I got that with some coffee and sat in the shop, eating desserts with my family. 

If you have a sweet tooth or want to go to a dessert place after dinner, make sure to stop in here, it's really pretty!

I'll preface by saying I'm from MD and kind of a crab/seafood snob.

That being said I went here for a lunch meeting and had probably one of the most disappointing meals.

First the service. No one came to take our order for 20 minutes. We were 1 of 2 tables in the small place so it wasn't hard to see us. We had to do the waving of the arms to get the waitress' attention. The waitress was nice to talk to, she told us some good history, but she could not hear a word we said. I think I repeated myself without exaggeration 20-25 times. Kind of frustrating when ordering food or asking for a refill.

Now the food. I wanted to get a flounder sandwich, but noticed the lunch menu had a fried flounder sandwich, while the dinner menu had a broiled flounder option. I asked if I could have broiled flounder and was told no. So this either tells me a) they were just trying to get rid of the fried flounder or b) it was prepackaged portions. You'll find out the answer later. I also ordered soup, they were out of the soup I wanted so she suggested I try the lobster bisque. I love lobster bisque, but this was disgusting. It tasted like liquid bread, all starch.

I wound up getting the broiled seafood platter since I didn't want a fried fish sandwich. The soup came quick and then 45 minutes after I was done with the soup I got my food. I got shrimp, scallops, flounder and a crab cake. Shrimp, scallops and flounder we fine, just tasted like old bay. The crab cake tasted EXACTLY like thanksgiving stuffing. WTF?! Why is their sage and thyme in a crab cake?

Once our plates were cleared it was another 20 minutes before the check came. At this point I felt like we were there the entire day.

On the way out I noticed all the prepackaged food being loaded onto a dolly and taken down into the cellar. The lobster bisque, the fish, EVERYTHING. They are 7 blocks away from the italian market and fresh seafood, why order all prepackaged crap? Just disgusting. I would expect a place with so much history would present itself better.

Went here for the second time tonight. It's our new favorite pizza place. 

Love everything about their pizza. The crust is thin. Thin and crispy. Not cracker thin but thin and not overly doughy. The sauce is a little sweet and just a touch of chunkiness. Both of these make a great combination. My guys like bacon pizza and they have it at Dino's. They use a good quality bacon, probably an applewood smoked bacon. And they put a generous amount on each pie. I ordered half pepperoni the other half onion-mushroom. I was asked if I wanted button or portobello, nice touch!! 

I have seen quite a few cheese steaks being ordered here. They look amazing. Lots of meat on a good looking roll with sesame seeds. I really like the creativity on the menu. It will really set them apart from the other pizza joints!  

I like the staff that works here. They are friendly and helpful. I was a little worried after reading the one negative review about the staff. But then I thought, one out of 24...you can't make everyone happy. We like to dine in rather then carry out. So the staff always brings us our pizza, passes out the plates, brings us napkins and seasonings (garlic powder, oregano). They have the cutest shakers for the spices...little baby mason jars with the caps on and punched out G, S, and P for garlic, salt, and pepper. The big hole shakers are for oregano, and red pepper flakes. They also have antique silverware for those needing utensils for salads and entrées, etc.

The interior is nice, big wooden tables with rod iron bases (3 tables in the front & 1 in the back) we were able to fit 5 ppl around one table tonight. Marble counter top with red brick walls. 

They have quite a large menu and it's a little upscale. Which is a nice change! Pork Pie (slow roasted pork, broccoli rabe, extra sharp aged provolone, mozz, and roasted garlic. Steak and fries pie (season steak and french fries, mozz, and caramelized onions. Buffalo chicken pizza, chicken ranch, and many more. 10 salads to choose from, lots of hot sandwiches and cold ones too! Can't wait to try something else!!  

FYI Sodas are by the bottle, Pepsi products.

The prices and portions here just can't be beat. A 10 oz filet wrapped in bacon runs you $27 here and it's always a perfectly cooked and seasoned buttery piece of prime filet resting on a sizzling plate of garlic butter sauce. Anywhere else that 10 oz filet would run you much higher and I've done the meticulous menu research to prove it. 

If you can get it, ask for one of their intimate booths where thick carpet curtains close you into an old world dining environment. There is something mildly erotic to me about the whole idea of sipping on martinis inside a carpet cloaked, virtually sound proof booth while catering to your primal meat cravings. The servers were super nice and curteous without being overly attentive. As our server told us, "If there is nothing else I can get you, enjoy your meal and just open the curtain when you are ready." I thought that was marvelous. I like good service but I hate feeling suffocated while I'm trying to relax over good food so I appreciated their laid back curtain policy. It makes you feel like there is no rush in the world and your allowed to stay for as long as you like.

We tried their wilted spinach and mushroom sides, which were good but nothing memorable. Next time I'll definitely try the Au Gratin instead but I was avoiding any heavy sides so I could focus all my energy on my filet and saving room for dessert. 

Speaking of dessert, we got their Z Pie, which was exceptionally better than I thought it would be. The menu description certainly does not do it justice! I was completely full by dessert but vowed I would struggle to split a bite with my friend and ended up fighting with them over it down to the last bite. That is a pretty rare occurrence for me since I'm never much of a huge dessert person. 

I had been to this restaurant once before but wanted to take a new friend there who I knew would appreciate a good steak dinner and has the same picky taste for a rare "pittsburgh style" prepared steak as I. They were also very impressed with the quality of the steak for the price and loved that the place was a "casual steakhouse" atmosphere. You don't need to feel underdressed or out of place if your not in the mood to fuss over getting too dressy, but still want a quality dinner. I'm not sure if this area gets a little dicey at night or not but I did appreciate the nice security guard who mostly just hangs out outside and opens the doors for guests. 

I would suggest anyone who is on the fence about trying this place to definitely give it a go! I would be completely shocked if anyone who went here ever had a disappointing experience. I love a prime quality steak, but hate over priced and pretentious chain steakhouse restaurants so this place hits the mark 100% for me.

For lunch "beyond" Downtown Santa Barbara, quite possibly, Max's!

Easily overlooked--it's exterior, simple and unpretentious--Max's is embedded, humbly, amidst commercial strip developments along State Street's northern end, just off Highway 101 (compared to Downtown, an unbeaten, Santa Barbarian path, to be sure.)  We stumbled upon it.  In fact, as all stumblings invariably conclude, our coming across Max's was a mistake.  However, we Yelped (4-stars and a free dessert check-in!), shrugged, and agreed to give it a try.  I'm glad we did!

Inside, the restaurant is...I don't know...  Charming, maybe?  Not in the storybook sense of the word, but rather in a simple, Italian-esque cafe meaning: contemporary art adorning the walls, fresh flowers poised upon the tables, a well-stocked wine bar nestled in the corner...  You get the idea.

Anyway, we'd come for lunch, something light, something easy.  The staff was courteous, attentive, personable.  The menu, at least for lunch, showcased sandwiches, so we chose Tuna Salad and a Club.  Fresh fruit sides, refreshing iced teas, and a delectably delicious Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta finish made for a quick and relaxing break before heading south, back to Orange County.

Outstanding Poboys! Yes, Simple and Fabulous, Amazing and HUGE! 

The long line speaks....yells! It's off the beaten path of most visitors to NOLA, but my cousin lives and dies by all things fabulous in Metairie Louisiana. He brags that folks just flock to NOLA BUT OH what joyous eateries abound in the secret city of Metairie. I must admit his recommendations are a hit. Such as this gem. All I can say is get to know your neighbors while standing in line to place your poboy order. Eat in or take it to go. 

We enjoyed the hour wait in line by chatting with folks from South Carolina, Oklahoma, Mississippi, Tennessee and TEXAS! But most often hometown Louisianans! Their secret is no moreeee! Ha! There were 100s of poboy shops in and around NOLA but the half-half shrimp and oyster was worth the wait.

I have no clue where all the 5 stars are coming from on this place. 

It's so hard for me to believe that in a fish town like Santa Barbara, there is such a lack of good, reasonably priced sushi restaurants. 

No, Arigato doesn't count...it's not that great and it's horribly over priced. 

Ichiban is good because there's nothing else to really compare it to here. It's definitely not great and the prices for nigiri sushi are expensive. An order of tuna nigiri is over $6.00! If I want an order of tuna, yellowtail and salmon -- that's 6 pieces of sushi -- I'm already over $20.00! C'mon now! 

The other thing that bothers me is the older sushi chef -- he's rude. I've been here twice now and both times he's acted almost offended when I place another order for sushi and he has felt that I've already eaten a lot. I'm sorry, do you not want my cash? Is the point of your business not to make money?

This trip, I ordered: 1 tuna sushi, 1 yellowtail sushi, 1 spicy scallop hand roll and 1 spider roll. When I placed an order for a Cliff Roll the chef responded with: "oh you're sure hungry tonight...this will be your last roll." Excuse me?! I'm not some obese dude shoveling food into my mouth. I'll keep ordering until I'm done eating! Maybe if you actually filled my scallop hand roll and sliced the nigiri a little thicker, I wouldn't have the need to order another roll. 

This was the second time he was this rude to me and it sure isn't making me want to come back for a third visit. 

The other servers were attentive and pleasant. The older sushi chef is rude and should just learn to keep to the task of assembling mediocre rolls and keep his mouth shut. 

2-stars: "Meh. I've experienced better."

Kids needed lunch after a long morning / afternoon in the French Quarter. Concierge told me this place was a few blocks away and had the items my kids wanted to eat. I'm glad I ran over solo this a a 24 hr 21 and up only bar that serves food near Bourbon St. Not where I would go with kids but this place was close to my hotel and it had grilled cheese so I ran over for take out for the kiddos.
Daughter wanted grilled cheese. Son wanted a Poboy.
The lady behind the bar was friendly.
The order was delivered promptly.
The food was ok. 
It served its purpose.
Don't think I'll return on this trip.

The mock meats on the extensive vegan menu are delicious.  My favorite is the vegan lemongrass chicken, though central Vietnamese noodles with an assortment of mock meats are also high on my list, as are all of their rolls (spring, summer, autumn and winter).  Oh, why was I born with only one stomach?

I'll share their secret with you: the family who own Trang Viet Cuisine grow many of their own herbs at home, since that's the only way to find consistently high-quality herbs not ordinarily grown near Tampa.  The More You Know...

Been here twice now, and Roberto's certainly is A-OK, but I can't go so far to say I'm a fan.

My first visit was a little after 8 am for a breakfast burrito. The food was good, but it was not worth the long wait. The staff was really confused and I think they lost a few orders, but thankfully not mine. I left unimpressed but willing to come back and try lunch sometime. 

Second visit was about 10:30 am on a Saturday so I gave lunch a try. I ordered #1, beef taco and cheese enchilada. The staff seem better prepared, the wait was acceptable, and the food was good but certainly not great. 

Not sure why this place has so much hype. Not many parking spots so you have to your visit, which is not convenient. Seating inside is very limited. 

The menu is pretty extensive and as I've said, the food I've tried was good. Prices are reasonable. Best Mexican in town? Good for sure, but not the best. Tacos El Rey has better food, better parking and seating, and comparable prices just to mention one option. 

I won't be a regular, but if I'm hungry for Mexican, driving by, and see an open parking spot I'd stop; otherwise, I'll just keep driving.

Walked out 40 minutes after ordering. Service as bad as it gets. Avoid this place!

We came in at 4:25 on a Saturday. One waitress for over 25 customers. People seated after us had their order taken first. Our appetizer took 30 minutes to deliver. At 40 minutes, they delivered the pizza for a party that came in almost 10 minutes after we did, then another party that came in after us. When they brought a pizza to our table, it was the wrong order! We were asked to wait another 15 minutes, but after already waiting 40, we just left. One of the very few times in my life I've left a restaurant without eating. 

Epic fail. Will never return for any reason.

This place gets rave reviews on Yelp! so had to give it a try. Dinner on a Friday night and I expected it to be busy so we made reservations at 4:30. Didn't need them as it was pretty wide open when we arrived and still pretty open when we left around 5:15. They had the table ready for us when we arrived and we were promptly seated. 

Most impressive thing about this place was the service. Best I've had at a restaurant in Reno in a long time. Fast, friendly, attentive. 

Four small side dishes were delivered first per standard Korean style. The kimchi was very good, and I know the difference as I've lived in Korea for a few years earlier in my lifeServer recommended Kimchi fries so we tried those and pork ribs. Both were good and the Kimchi fries lived up to the reputation of being amazing. 

Main dishes were Udon, Bibimpap, Bulgolgi Hot Pot, and Bulgolgi fusion. All were good, but the best was the fusion. I think if I return I'll try a dish off the fusion menu instead of the classic Korean menu. We are hard to please when it comes to Korean food in Reno, as my wife is Korean so the standard is high. 

Delightful change of pace for Reno. Highly recommend you give it a try!

New place in town, just opened this week with lots of buzz. Decided to come very early to avoid the crowds. Arrived at 7:45 am so street parking was easy to find. Only one other customer in the place when we arrived. The place seats about 50 and it was wide open when we arrived. 

They were still training front register folks so ordering was a little slow and confusing. The food delivery was also surprisingly slower than I expected. I made a mental note to think twice about coming here when they are busy because if service is slow when they are not busy it's likely not good at all when they are busy. 

The food did not disappoint. I had the Reggie Deluxe - biscuit, fried chicken, bacon, egg, cheese and covered with gravy. The chicken portion was large and thick. I tried to eat it by hand but quickly gave that up. It hard to get all the ingredients in every bite, and it was more than I could eat. My son had Moneyball - biscuit, gravy, and over easy egg. If I return, I'll try shrimp and grits or get another breakfast sandwich without the gravy so I can pick it up to eat. 

There are many very good breakfast options in Reno. I don't see myself becoming a regular here, but I do think I'd return occasionally. The food and prices are very good, but the parking and service will be an issue during peak business hours.

First visit to the new location next door to the movie theater at Summit Mall. My son and I went to see a matinee at 4:30 so this location was a perfect stop before the show. 

We found ample seating, friendly service, and pretty fast delivery of our food order. I ordered a bison burger wrap. The bison was a properly prepared medium rare. I was very pleased with the lettuce wrap - sturdy. One of the better burger wraps I've had. My son and I shared an order of sweet potato fries which of course were delicious. 

Burger Me is a solid brand. It's not our favorite burger in town, but it's reliably good. Next time you are down south for a movie, grab a burger and fries too!

My first visit to the new Walden's on Wells. I arrived at 10:30 am and the place was totally empty. I had the place to myself the entire time - shame because it's a large space with good food, coffee, and excellent wifi. 

I ordered the carne and eggs, selected bacon for the meat, sourdough toast and fruit instead of potatoes. Cost was $12.99 - a little higher than I expected. The food was indeed good, especially the toast. They told me the sourdough comes from local supplier Franko and it is excellent. Service was friendly and my food delivered quickly. 

Another solid choice for breakfast in Reno. Not sure I'd drive all the way over to Wells often for breakfast, but if you are in the area and need a solid spot I recommend this one. The Walden's coffee is also good but just up the street is Magpie coffee and their lattes are hard to beat.

So many things to like about Rounds, but the service consistently sucks. 

I recently started meeting people for coffee here. Central location, LOTS of parking, very ample seating. I've never had a problem finding a seat. The baked goods are of course great, while the coffee is acceptable. 

Most of my visits have been between the hours of 10:30 am and 1 pm - off their peak morning hours. I've always observed many employees in the place, but usually only one working the front counter. If there is even one person in line in front of you, the wait can be long. If you happen to walk in with 2-3 people in line in front of you, be prepared for a frustrating wait. Management is non-existent, and the employees are not trained to back each other up to help serve customers. The employees are all friendly and courteous, but they are failed by a system that does not make customer service a priority. 

I'm going to stop meeting people for coffee at Rounds, and I can't recommend it.

Probably the worst customer service, was told by Matt ( dealer ) that he is tired of me 'cuz I changed my chip colors 3 times, and to my shock his manager Amanda stood by him and saying it is very frustrating. If u hate ur job so much find something else to do.

Darling little rustic restaurant and bar located in Verdi right off 80. It's very warm and welcoming the minute you walk through the door and service was great! The menu is full of comfort food selections plus salads, pizza, burgers and sandwiches. We started with the elote balls (deep fried cheese blend with corn and seasonings) which paired perfectly with my ice cold Sierra Nevada draft beer and were really good. They have a full bar and large draft beer and wine selection. The restaurant smokes their own meats and we selected a tri tip bbq sandwich with some crispy shoe string fries (you can also  add garlic or choose a side salad instead). The meat was really flavorful and next time I'm going to try the pulled pork, We added sides of baked beans with bacon and macaroni and cheese-both were delicious. Overall a great experience and we'll be back!

I had high hopes in ordering from this restaurant due to the great reviews, but did not have that great of an experience with my to go order. The standouts for the meal were the spaghetti Vincenzo-which was really good- and the cannoli. Everything was packaged well-which I appreciate-and the pasta noodles all had a fresh flavor. The caprese was bland, tomatoes were a little mushy and there was just a dot of pesto on top so not much flavor to this dish. I ended up only eating a bite and discarded the rest. The rigatoni did not have enough Bolognese sauce on it so although the sauce had a good flavor the dish was somewhat dry. I would probably go back to this restaurant to  buy their noodles to cook at home (because they are really good) but would not order food from here again as there are so many other great Italian restaurants in Reno that I'd rather visit.

So Walmart has stepped up their clothing selection. Really cute items but still reasonably priced. I also love their curbside pickup-very fast and customer service has bee great. Love the Dunkin inside the store too!

First time here-such a cute restaurant! Perfect addition for Midtown. The interior is decorated with brick and leather and has Aztec touches. They have a full bar with a good tequila selection and some tasty sounding cocktails.The tequila cosmopolitan (made with tequila, blackberry juice and fresh lime and orange juice)piqued my interest-it was delicious!
We started with the guacamole-so fresh and flavorful. Next I had the chicken enchilada and birria crispy taco. Both were bursting with flavor and tons of meat. A word of caution-food here is spicy-which I love but my husband was a little more challenged. Great service and food and a wonderful, fun addition to the Reno restaurant scene.

We visited this restaurant because of the 5 star review given by Spencer T. Sometimes when you walk into a restaurant it's a little confusing because you're not really sure what that restaurant is about and they don't really have a clear brand. This restaurant has its brand down and sets the mood with it's funky western theme from the minute that you walk in the door! Love the boot and electric guitar collections that are everywhere you look! It feels like you've stepped into a decorated barn and sets the casual, western steakhouse theme perfectly!
We got a friendly greeting from the hostess and were seated promptly by the hostess. Our food server Tanner quickly came over and gave us some of the best service for the entire meal. I had the top sirloin and shrimp and chose French onion soup and baked potato as my 2 sides. The soup was delicious and the baked potato had this delicious baked crust that I've never seen before. Steak and shrimp were both flavorful and cooked perfectly. Loved the half lemon they served with the shrimp! Hubby had coconut shrimp and top sirloin with sides of mashed potatoes and gravy and blue cheese wedge salad-loved everything! 
This will be our go to steakhouse from now on-only regret I have is that it took me 6 years of living in Reno to try it!

I'd give them 0 stars if I could. Anyone who thinks it's okay to have a sign by their register that says, "This is America, please speak English" on it, does not deserve to have a restaurant. If I had seen this before paying, I would've just left and walked across the street to Pat's. What about customers from across the world who cannot speak English? It baffles me that this place still exists and has a long line around the building.

It's a joke cause their cheese steaks aren't even good. Meat is dry and they give you a lot less meat in general. If you ask for onions, they'll probably forget since they forgot for me. Maybe my English wasn't good enough, not sure. All I know is that this place has garbage cheesesteaks and a garbage attitude. 

Pat's all day, everyday (way better meat and a lot of it!! All without racism too!)

I love BBQ.  Im originally from St Louis and visit my favorite BBQ city in the world, Kansas City, quite often.  Ive lived in Nashville awhile now and have ate most of places that serve BBQ in town and most have let me down. Martin's in Mt Juliet just opened up and I had been eagerly awaiting its opening.  I went there last night (7/1) and they opened their doors on the 27th of June- so I was expecting some rough spots in service.  

Overall my experience with the staff was pretty good. The servers did their best to get the plates out quickly although they forgot our cake 3 separate times.  They do not have a number system in place (perhaps it is coming later) so there was a bit of confusion on the servers part to get the food out. They would just walk through the room yelling out the numbers to find the appropriate person- while this worked fine, it definitely slowed down service.

But... I didnt go there for service.  Lets talk about the food.

I love BBQ in all of its forms but my weak spot is actually turkey.  I ordered the turkey plate with fries and baked beans (my favorite side), my girlfriend ordered the redneck taco.   Both of the meats were exceptional.  The baked beans were not my favorite ( I prefer brown sugar beans with bacon rather than onions/peppers).  We also ordered the coconut cake and pecan pie , both of which were pretty awesome.

Sauces-  Generally I dont love thinner, vinegar based sauces.  The sauces here were pretty good, their spiciest sauce had a nice kick to it. That said, most of the sauces had a very similar taste and did not provide enough of a difference for me to differentiate between them (all of them were a bit sweet, spicy, and tangy). 

While the food was fine, this restaurant is not without its downsides.  There needs to be some sort of change when it comes to portion size to the cost of the meal.  The food we ordered was about $36 for two people (including soda and dessert), which is fine price point but the portions were very small for that price.  Id like to see either larger portions including or lower prices on some of the items.

I can honestly say I've never witnessed such horrible FOH or service in my life. We were told a half hour wait..... Which turned into 45-50 minutes, which was fine, as they were very busy (even though they set at least 3 parties before us and we were told they didn't do reservations.... I'm still not sure how that seating system works.) However, the service after this was appalling.... Our water ran out and I had to actually ask the food runner for more water, then we ordered the Hot Chicken Buns (which I was excited to try because they had rave reviews) only for them to bring Duck Buns and to the wrong group.... I had high hopes (even after they told us they were out of the chicken and brought us duck) because they were quite good. Next I had the dumplings, which were disappointing and didn't taste like much of anything, the only flavor I got was the citrus in the sauce. Lastly I ordered the Tennessee Tonkotsu, to which I added an extra egg and a spice bomb at the suggestion of the server. When I received my ramen I was very disappointed at sip one.... It tasted like sesame and warm pork fat, the kind that my grandmother tosses because she's fried something in it and it's broken and gross. I added the spice bomb. Now I had sesame flavored spicy pork fat. I waited until I was able to grab our server (who was again very busy) and asked politely for some soy sauce. He stumbled on his words and gave me a story on how they may have a small bottle in the back. He asked me if I still wanted the soy and I said yes, then he continued by asking why I wanted it..... Um, what? Why does a server feel the need to ask why a customer would ask for a condiment? They had the option of add ins, which he had earlier recommended to us (a party of 4) so someone asking for soy sauce in an Asian place doesn't seem that absurd. I told him simply "because it's not very flavorful" he asked again and I added "it just isn't very good". He said he would see about the soy for me. This lead to a very long and awkward altercation over the soy... Which I never got because he told me they don't even make the ramen there and didn't have the soy to give me. Which is fine, whatever. Not my restaurant. However, he actually seemed offended that myself and my party weren't satisfied with our food and kept asking how to fix it, when I had told him a moment earlier how to fix it and he wasn't able. I sent my ramen back, because I wasn't going to finish it... Why waste the calories on something that isn't good? I still don't understand why he took it the way he did... I wasn't rude or upset with him at all. It wasn't anything to do with him personally, however his unwillingness to either 1. Fix the issue 2. Get a manager (which he did later) or 3. Drop the issue altogether makes me think he isn't a seasoned server. His skin is far too thin. After a long and drawn out discussion with my guest (which got a bit out of hand and heated, though I tried to end it several times, the server kept talking and asking questions) the manager came over (angry) and made the situation 100X worse. I wanted to crawl under the table. I've never been so disrespected or embarrassed in a food establishment in my life! I tried to end the argument between her, my guest, and toward the end (???) the guy seated next to our group but we basically were kicked out. It was horrible. All in all, the duck was the only positive thing I can say about this place, because they were good. Maybe they have buns to-go.

My husband picked me up at the airport tonite after I had traveled all day from a trip out of state and decided to surprise me with a meal at the Stone House as he discovered it was owned by the legendary restaurant name Abowd. We had eaten many times over the years at Adele's  in Carson City, (and have not been disappointed with the service ever),while Paul and Adele owned it and have continued to frequent it under Charlie and Karen's leadership. 
Unfortunately Cyrina Abowd never learned the meaning of hospitality from her mother, father, brother and sister in-law. As mentioned in many reviews she was exceptionally rude to us upon arrival as was the bartender inside...if you own a busy  restaurant you should be happy and welcoming  or soon you'll be not so busy and even more miserable ...biting the hands that literally feed you is just bad business. Pun intentional and we're not laughing or ever going back!

I loved everything about Boucherie. It feels like you're eating in someone's home. It's cute, cozy and romantic. Definitely a perfect date spot. They also had some tables out front.

I came across this on Yelp and I'm honestly not sure why I didn't find it sooner. It's considered barbecue, but it's more refined barbecue if that makes sense. I got the blackened shrimp and grit cakes and the elote (this was a special so probably not something you can get all of the time). My husband got the brisket with garlic Parmesan fries. The shrimp and grit cakes were so amazing. It was topped with a bacon vinaigrette and I actually don't like bacon but this vinaigrette was bomb. The shrimp was cooked perfectly and the grit cakes were a delicious take on traditional grits. As far as the elote, I got it without the Alabama white bbq sauce because I don't like that sauce, but it didn't need the sauce because of how good it was without it. It was topped with crispy shallots and that was such a game changer. My husband loved the brisket and kept saying how tender it was. 

Oh! And they also gave us these spoons of this coconut sweet potato soup as a starter and it was honestly the best soup I've had in my entire life. Seriously so good.

It's rare for my husband and I to agree on restaurants because he is such a picky eater and I tend to like more adventurous food, so for us to both love a restaurant is a big deal. And we both loved Boucherie. With that said, we'll be back soon!

Finally. 

If you don't understand the appeal of Trader Joe's, let me tell you... being able to buy myself breakfast AND lunch for 5 work days for $18 and some change including tax? Sweet.

If you aren't a brand loyal person and don't feel the need to have 8 different brands of Greek Yogurt to choose from, welcome to TJ's! Take your pick of any of their many amazing flavors (or, plain) for $0.99 and up. Don't need to worry about sales, and because it's TJ's policy that their food isn't stuffed full of artificial crap, slightly less time spent reading labels. It's wonderful.

It's a small store, as all Trader Joe's locations are, but it has just about everything a normal person needs.... with some awesome extras, like cookie butter, pre-made whole wheat pizza dough, pumpkin everything, etc.

Basically, it's good, it's cheap, and the customer service is always spectacular. I'm so glad this is on my way home from work!

WOW. I am in awe of Zeppoli right now. I honestly cannot say I have been more emotionally attached to any meal in a long long while. Is 6 stars possible? You know how some places do get that 5 star rating in your mind, but it's like a "you-barely-made-it-to-five-stars" kind of thing? Well from the moment I stepped into the door, I already KNEW it was going to be a 100% 5 star kind of evening. Everything they said, did, and served just blew me out of the water.

It all began when I read Michelle C's review. She had me at Sicilian fisherman's stew, and tagliatelle al limone with prosciutto. I called the restaurant the same day and made a reservation for a few weeks later. They only have 12 tables and that was the earliest weekend they had available. I live roughly 45 mins away, and more with traffic. Since I'm pretty noob at navigating in NJ, I naturally got lost on the way to the restaurant, and was 20 mins late for my reservation. I wanted to call to warn them and apologize as I normally do when I am late, but did not have the number and the combination of being lost and not being able to call just made me feel annoyed at myself. By the time I got the restaurant, I was frazzled and also extremely pissed that the bottle of wine (this is a BYOB) I had gotten for the occasion was sitting on the kitchen table...at my house. The server was all smiles when I walked in, and the restaurant was already in full swing with almost every table full except one. Each table had a bottle of wine, which only made me sadder. When I profusely apologized to the waiter about not being prompt and then jokingly mentioned something about being the only one without wine in the whole place due to my idiot self, he just smiled and said, " Sounds like quite a mess coming here! I want you to relax while I get you some nice wine pairings for your meal from my private stash, and also please take your time and enjoy the meal, dont worry about rushing because you were late". It was as if an angel with a Golden Harp was playing music in my ears! I instantly relaxed and the wine parings were amazing! A white for the apps I got, and a light red for the main course. All on the house! I didn't know service existed like that anymore. That one comment and 2 glasses of wine earned them a big. fat. tip. which more than covered what 2 glasses of wine would even cost if it were on the menu. Money knows no bounds with kindness.

On to the food. Amazing. I think you will drool when looking at the pictures. I would try to describe the things I ordered but I know I could not do it justice. Homemade pasta. Luxurious olive oil drizzled on our bread. Rosemary. Perfectly ripe and flavorful red tomatoes. Anchovies, Lemon! A tastful and rich balsamic. Tender chunks of fish, melts in your mouth lamb. Perfectly salted prosciutto. Tangy dried orange on creamy cannoli. Lightly whipped pineapple sorbet. Let's just say for me this meal was pure heaven sent. My bf and I both enjoyed all the things we ordered so so much. I would love to come back SOON!!!!!!  Just know that this experience is so much more than just eating. It is the pure enjoyment of flavors, essence, company, homecooking, traditional Italian fare, and a wait staff that you'd like to take home with you...or party with. Absolutely Outstanding. Bravo, Zeppoli, Bravo! Mi Amour!

Sexist Double Standard! 

I wish I writing about how fun this place is, instead I have to expose the gross sexist double standard in their dress requirement.   

I was in Nashville for the first time on a business trip.  My team and I were excited to try House if Cards. I came straight from a work meeting and was wearing a blazer, blouse nice, dark jeans and heels.  I had read the dress code page prior to coming and wasn't wearing any of the prohibited items: baseball cap, T-shirt, sweats, etc.   

I was stopped before going in because I was wearing denim.  Unfortunately, I had missed the dress code specific to women: cocktail dress preferred, pant suit, no denim. 

Respectfully, I let my coworkers go ahead while I caught an Uber back to the hotel and changed into slacks.  

Well, to my surprise there were lots of men dressed exactly how I had been before changing: denim jeans, nice shirt and a blazer.  Oh!  So it's not no denim, just no denim for women. 

I'm not usually one to wave the feminist flag, but the fact they turned me away when I was dressed professionally but wearing jeans, while granting my male counterpart access is disgusting.  Sorry I didn't fit into the mold of what you want your female patrons  to look like.  

I would have expected a little more acceptance in 2019.  Shame on you, House of Cards.

I may have just eaten my last meal.  I anticipate having a massive MI at any moment.  But it may have been worth it.  

I had the Commerce Special.  Basically biscuits and gravy but the gravy had cheese, sausage and jalapeños in it served with two lightly fried eggs on top.  I expected something like pump cheese but the gravy was actually a well made mornay but with sausage and jalapeños.   I orders hot sausage as well.  When it all came I thought of this is not bad I'll eat a third of it.  I scrapped the plates and am writing this in my car almost catatonic. 

The place is NOLA old school cool.  What I had was superb and something special.  I am going to buy aspirin.

My first visit here on Friday.  They have indoor, bar, and outdoor seating.  It was a nice evening to sit outside. The service was excellent.  Glass was never empty. Always coming by and clearing empty plates. 

Had the opportunity to try many things.  The highlights:

1.  Crispy Veggie Spring Rolls.  Wow!  Must get.  The wrap was amazing. Light. Crispy. Not greasy.  While the serving size was plenty, I could easily eat a few orders!  So tasty and the skin!!!

2.  Shaking beef. Cooked to your preference.  Extremely flavorful. This is definitely something you want to get. Amazing. 

3. Stir fried curry vermicelli rice noodles.  It comes with chicken and shrimp.  The chicken was tender and tasty.  You know how many times the protein is just there to get the flavors of the dish?  The protein here can stand on it's own.  I could've eaten the chicken without the noodles.  The dish in itself had good flavor and had some slight heat.  Definitely enough for leftovers too!

4. Coconut ice cream.  Homemade.  Plenty of pieces of coconut.  Definitely a light, flavorful, delicious end to the meal.  

Definitely a great meal with awesome service.  Just have to deal with the typical CWE parking.  Reserve some time to look for street or lot...

Been here a few times now. Service is fast and accurate.  I enjoy both the chicken ramen and the pho. The curry ramen is a good choice, lots of flavor, but caution if you get the tempura chicken with it, it's slightly oily. The bahn mi dip is also amazing, fresh, flavorful, and the dip is a good complement to the French bread.  Lately I've enjoyed the YOLO mein, standard lo mein but tons of delicious flavor. 

The crab Rangoon are a must get. They are known for it!  

Curbside is available. Just call in your order and ask about the specials.

My wonderful husband booked a surprise Birthday-Baby Moon weekend for us last week. Oh how I was ready to be charmed by this resort that I had dreamt about. Dreams do come true, but as they say, the devil is in the details. 
We had beautiful weather the whole weekend and the drive all the way up the winding road to the resort presented beautiful views of Santa Barbara and the ocean. The location is set amongst a residential area, high up on the hill. 

Room 2801- It has a cute private patio in the back where you can have breakfast every morning, but be prepared to share your morning with the overly energetic babies/kids in the private residence next door separated only by a hedge. You will hear their every word and they will hear yours. There goes your peaceful morning.
The bathtub was long, deep and very slippery. Not good for a pregnant woman. The toiletries were supplied by Etro which I used in Italy and did not like. I understand this is a sister property, but Molton Brown would have been more appropriate. 
The hair dryer is crap. Come on!
The mini bar does not come stocked. You have to request what you want and then get charged for it.

Room Service- They forgot to bring extra cream and sugar, they drop the tray and leave, the coffee pots were never distinguished as regular or decaf, food was cold and portions were pretty skimpy. Also, I request the WSJ throughout my stay and I never received it once. When I called to ask for it, they said they were out of it.
The Spa- One word: Tiny! There is literally one bathroom and two showers for the entire women's spa. There isn't any face wash or make-up remover supplied. The 80 minute maternity massage was delightful however. 

Pool- A beautiful pool with limitless edges, but not a true infinity pool in my opinion. Also there isn't a Jacuzzi which I overheard guests complaining about. The food was good, but they were going to heat up some food for me in addition and totally forgot about it. They ran out of bloody mary mix by 12pm on a Sunday. Really? Many guests complained that the salt water was too hot and not refreshing at all. It did feel like a big Jacuzzi. There were super annoying and very inebriated guests at the pool on a Sunday. This is Santa Barbara, not Vegas. They were extremely loud and bothered those trying to relax around them. The staff kept feeding them drinks instead of asking them to curb their behavior. 

The Valet- They lost our car when we were trying to get to our dinner reservation. First, they brought up the wrong car and then they couldn't find it at all which made us pretty late. 

The shuttle service- We were given a ride to dinner at San Ysidro Ranch by a very well-mannered and courteous driver named Cody. However, they did fail to inform us that the shuttle stops running at at 9:45pm and we ended up getting stranded and having to call a taxi service which was not fun after you are standing outside waiting cold and tired and heavily pregnant.  Had we known, we probably would have just driven our own car. Baby bump compliments from John Locke of "Lost" were an added bonus however.

Weddings- We almost walked right into the middle of a wedding going on because there was no staff to block off the entrance or redirect hotel guests. After seeing two weddings take place here, I would not recommend it as a wedding venue no matter how beautiful it is. 

Dogs- It's dog friendly which is great, but they need to have garbage cans somewhere, even hidden, where guests can dispose of the dog waste. I saw rooms with piles of dog poop bags outside the door because no one knows what to do with it. Also if you are not down with the furry species, know that there will be dogs at the pool and inside the lounge. Technically, not allowed I guess, but they do get away with it. 

Bellman- We requested help with our luggage checking out and no one ever showed so I walked down to reception and had to get them to send one again. Again it just seemed that this young and inexperienced staff was overwhelmed. I looked to see who was managing them and apparently no one was around. There was only one person working at the desk during a busy time when people are trying to check out and get home. 

Bike Rentals- The free electric bike rentals are really fun to take down to State street and the beach. Then when you are too tired to bike the hill back to the resort, just turn on the battery and zip back. However, if you aren't good with directions, don't listen to the staff's convoluted suggestions. They would do much better by offering a map to guests. 

I'm truly on the fence as to whether I would return. It is so beautiful, but all together the lack of attention to details just dulls the experience. If I went back to Santa Barbara I would probably be more tempted to stay at Bacara which is much more professionally run or San Ysidro Ranch in Montecito. El Encanto, the charm is wearing off...

My friends' parents honeymooned here in the 1940s. They had their 40th anniversary here. Their daughter was married here. The family celebrates here multiple times a year. Last week was an anniversary dinner. This week, they requested to have a picture taken while the family is having an a huge family celebration. They were denied by the AZ Inn as they do not have a room booked. Here's the family reaction:

"Deeply disappointed that the Arizona Inn will not give permission for us to have a family photo taken on their grounds after our large group had planned to lunch there Friday. We have held dozens of large and small family events there for almost 40 years but they won't budge from policy that you must book a room or schedule an event before any photo can be taken on premises. We will be looking for a new venue for future gatherings...."

I will never visit our recommend this venue again.

Shoestring Truffle fries were crisp and subtly flavored.

Bruschetta was very fresh with notes of balanced basil and garlic.

My main course was the papardelle in veal/chicken/beef ragu. The meats were decently executed. Not perfect but good.

The pasta was fresh made had a nice chewy bite and floury flavor. The red sauce was unmemorable.

Absolutely phenomenal french pastries. The croissant was extremely puffed out and light while still being buttery on the inside and flaky and crisp inside. The croissant sandwich had super savory sausage, fresh eggs, and oozy cheese.

I'm not exaggerating to say this is one of the best french bakeries in the USA.

Came here for a restaurant week meal. Unlike many places, Abe Fisher simply offered their menu for a reduced rate. So I can say we did get a chance to sample their real offerings. 

This place is small and has a very interesting vibe. Imagine a standard Jewish deli/dinner (like Bagel Cove in Miami or Snowden Deli in Montreal) but in a slightly more trendy/upscale setting. The is definitely a blend of art deco and industrial feel that you might expect this type of concept to display. The place was packed, yet all the servers were on top of their game and very well composed.

On the advice of a fellow Yelper, we decided to split up our 4 course meals family style, effectively getting 8 courses split between the two of us. This was an excellent idea that I highly recommend. All the items were easy to split. 

First round: Shaved Brussel Sprout Salad.

This was awesome. Extremely fresh bitter greens accented with the earthiness of Brussel Sprouts and a robust cheese (parmesan reggiano maybe?) The pine nuts added a nice touch of solid mouthfeel and light complexity to round out the flavor profile, which was earthy, fresh, and savory.

The Potato Latkes were equally incredible. Splendidly smoky and creamy salmon to topped a perfect latke with a crisp exterior and delicate inside. They expertly balance the dish with hints of classic sharp aromatics (red onion) for a well-rounded plate. 

The Reuben we loved, but was probably the least inventive dish on the menu. It had perfectly cooked pork belly topping a buttery rye toasty morsel. The pickled green onion was a nice sour crisp to counterbalance the fatty pork belly. This dish was a really good reuben slider. Great and well-executed, but not particularly inventive. Just nit-picking here. 

The Spinach Kugel was firm, full-bodied, and full of special flavor. The buttery crust, accents of egginess, and cheddary goodness came together for a symphony of unerring delight. I was shocked at how much I enjoyed a spinach dish. Spinach almost always comes of as too gritty and bitter for my palette.

The Halibut was insane. This fish was so incredibly savory, buttery, fresh, and full of the flavor of the sea. It almost tasted like one supremely large scallop with a more chunky, meaty texture. The Challah crust was delightful and not overpowering as I had feared it would be. This was likely out favorite dish. The flavors on the plate all payed homage to the venerable halibut, which could and should not be outshined.

The Beef Cheeks were also unreal. Such incredible tender fattiness. Not since had I tasted such decadent beef since the Tacos de Cabeza Tacos el Gordo in Las Vegas. Beef Cheeks are vastly underrated and disappointingly overlooked in most east coast Mexican eateries. Fortunately, Abe Fisher has done us all the favor of being a beef cheek bastion, and they do it well. This dish I feel is the meat dish that the reubens could have been. It's unique. Its texture is perfect, and its a well balanced assault on the palate.

For dessert, we split both the Flourless Cake and the Bacon & Egg Cream

The flourless cake I was skeptical of. I don't generally buy into the gluten-free hype and I love flour. However, this cake had me wishing I didn't have flour in more cakes. The chocolate flavor was extremely intense. The mouthfeel was so gooey and fudgy and hot. It was a truly explicit experience. To break the palette from such obscenity, the chef allotted a dollop of the most incredible hand-whipped cream. Such a treat.

To cap off the meal a dessert I was afraid of. The bacon & egg cream. I feared this exercise in culinary joy would be left with a savoury bacon oiliness. I was pleasantly surprised to be wrong. This dish is sweet, and the bacon somehow is like a cereal crunchy variety. It's not oily and it's barely savory. Yet it maintains its smokiness. The lightness of the chocolate foam (which I admittedly had hoped would be a bit more substantial in density and consequently mouthfeel) was expertly juxtaposed to the dense pudding beneath. 

Abe Fisher was an incredible experience. The service, food, and ambience were well worth the $50 spent. This is a place to come challenge you tastes and raise your expectations from cuisine.

The food is exceptional but the service is awful (with the exception of the one waiter who is always running around keeping the place afloat). The hostesses constantly act like you're inconveniencing them by asking for a table or wait time and that's if you can even find one. The owners daughter who supposedly runs the place is the absolute worse. She is lazy and has an attitude with everyone. 

To top the bad service off, when we were leaving today the head chef not only almost hit us in the parking lot because he was driving like a lunatic but also almost hit a couple and their dogs. 

It's really frustrating that the best food in town means having to deal with the employees at stone house.

I walked in all excited because I'm like so many, I've been dying for a new Korean place to open, finding Korea House too expensive and lacking.

Now I have two Korean places that I find too expensive and lacking.

I was a little confused when I saw that they do Vietnamese soup as well as Korean. I didn't really see a need for it since we do have several good pho places already. 
But looking at the menu, I noted they do not offer any of my favorite ones anyway (Tripe, sinew).

When I asked if they were going to be offering them later, some punk kid (10 or 11 years old) chimed in, "Well we're trying to show the Korean side!"

Um...Ok. But it has always been my experience that if you offer a food in a restaurant (And advertise it on your sign), it should be done the best that it can be, not ignored to focus on OTHER stuff.

Just my personal opinion, I guess...

I think back to California and Florida and Nashville Korean places I've eaten and  how much I appreciated the good value I received, it is just disheartening to see how over-priced and how low quality the ones we have here are. 

I can only hope some more competition pops up. Fingers crossed for it happening soon. Good Korean bibimbap is a wonderful lunch.

I do not like Eastbank Vietnamese pho. Nope. I like the real stuff.

So when I was starving today I decided to give Lilly's a try.
But no pho.
So I called and ordered pickup. The avocado and shrimp salad, the pork bahn mi, and the crab rangoons (because I heard they have bacon in them).

20 minutes later, I walked in and they had no idea who I was. After some scrambling, they found my stuff. Seems they wrote my name down as Abby and was totally confused by my actual name and me being a dude.
They gave me extra hot sauce and fish sauce for no charge. And the owner even joked about messing up my name and made fun of herself. What a sweetie.


Took the stuff back to work and with much trepidation, opened it all up and tried it all.

The bahn mi: Fresh veggies. Really well done pork and nice soft Viet-French bread. 
Also, almost 1/3 larger than most other places on the East Bank. Filled too.
A total win.
Seriously. Good stuff.

The crab rangoons did NOT have bacon (you lying bastages) but they were really good anyway. Very well filled. A little greasy but still good.

The avocado and shrimp salad was good. I didn't like the strawberries but that's just because I don't like them in general. The fried onions/garlic on top was, sadly, stale...the avocado was chopped into tiny little bits that were almost too small to pick up with the chopsticks. And not a large amount of them. But having said that, it was still quite good. Not too heavy and not too light. Just a great blend for lunch.
It came with a fish sauce based dressing that was perfectly balanced. The shrimp were large and had the tail shells still attached...I ate them too. Really good. 

SO all in all, I am very pleased with the effort and since it's summer, I think I can be comfortable ordering lunch from there.

P.S. It's about a block and a half from another Magazine street Viet-place that seemed like a ghost town compared to the busy and lively lunchtime crowd at Lilly's.
Sort of says something, doesn't it?

It's been 5 visits since my first review. Our last outing was on Tuesday and to say it was enjoyable would be a huge understatement.
I tried to get the daily special but by 2pm, they were sold out.

I was upset for less than 20 seconds because our waitress informed us they had an oyster special that day.
