After ordering, we had our choice of three types of bread, followed by the amuse bouche: smoked salmon pate on crunchy crostini. I really enjoyed this despite not usually caring much for salmon. 

Two of us started with the soup: butternut squash with minced chestnuts. It was rich, buttery and perfect for a chilly night. Our other friend had one of the house-made pastas with pancetta, which was also extremely flavorful. While ordering, I had asked about the mackeral with olives and squid, but I ultimately ended up ordering the scallops. Needless to say, it was a very nice surprise when our server brought each of us a tasting of the mackeral between courses. It was delicious. The briny olives went perfectly with the flaky but meaty fish. I instantly regretted not ordering it as my main, but now I have a really great reason to return!

The scallops were no disappointment. They were perfectly seared and resting over sort of a hearty bean stew, with a crisp hash of apples and fennel bulb (hate the seeds, dig the bulb) between. My partner in soup had ordered the same dish, and our contrarian friend chose the pork chop, which was a great plate of chop, potato pancake, apple sauce and sauerkraut. Apparently, my friend is not a kraut lover, so I gladly relieved her plate of the slightly sour, bacon-flecked cabbage, which was just as good as my Gram's. 

Stuffed, we accepted our check without soldiering on to the dessert course. This was easily one of my favorite girls' nights to date, and I'm so happy I was able to try Fork after many years of foolishly putting it off. I won't make that mistake again.

I eye up Moustaki every time I drive past but rarely find myself in the area. I've always been curious because I absolutely love Mediterranean food! Last week, I finally made Moustaki my dining destination before heading to an event at the Franklin Institute. 

The menu has a lot on it and there's definitely something for everyone. I'm trying to get into a more pescetarian diet so I gravitated towards the salmon platter. In an attempt to keep it healthy-ish, I went with rice and lemon potatoes, though I was definitely eyeing up the fries. 

We started with the feta dip appetizer which I wasn't crazy about. The cucumbers that came with were past their prime; they had that soft, translucent look around the edges. 

Fortunately, the main dish was really solid. The salmon portion was generous and I liked the potatoes a lot (the rice was fine, nothing extraordinary). 

I'd give Moustaki another shot if I happened to be in the neighborhood again.

I finally made it to Giuseppe & Sons after trying once before on a weeknight and striking out because they were already booked. This time, we made a reservation and were seated in a cushy booth in the center of the dining room. 

Our server, Nancy, was awesome! Great with recommendations and descriptions that helped us make the best choices. We started with the tableside mozzarella, compliments of the kitchen, and it was an incredible start to the meal. The cheese was so delicious, and the roasted peppers and tomatoes that came alongside were a great addition. We also started with the meatballs, shrimp scampi, and antipasti salad. All great dishes that, along with the irresistible tomato focaccia, ended up filling us up before the main event. 

When our mains arrived, we all took a few bites before having them boxed up. My rigatoni with vodka sauce was nice, but my husband's lasagna and his mother's chicken milanese were fantastic! I especially liked the chicken, which was served cutlet-style and topped with a gorgeous salad of tomatoes and red onion. 

I had saved some room for dessert, so we shared the tiramisu, which came in a giant bowl and provided more than enough for our party of three. This was absolutely delicious and I will order again next time. 

Giuseppe & Sons has shot to the top of my list for a great, albeit heavy, meal in Philadelphia. Perfect for the cold winter months ahead!

Melissa P and I decided to check out Cafe Chismosa for a casual lunch/brunch on Saturday afternoon. With an outdoor table available in the sun, we were sold right away. The inside of the cafe is also super cute - bright and airy. 

The menu is focused on Latin-inspired lunch and brunch items. I opted to keep my choices on the healthy side and was greatly rewarded with fresh, clean, flavorful food. To start, we shared the shrimp ceviche which was absolutely gorgeous and had loads of bright, tasty ingredients. 

Next, I tried a smoked scallop salad with avocado and quinoa. Wow. I haven't stopped thinking about this salad since I had it, and I can't wait to go back and get it again ASAP. I'd never had smoked scallops before but they were perfect on this salad and the perfect match for creamy avocado. 

I will happily go out of my way to patronize this wonderful business again.

The last minute decision to try Tre Famiglia was reached because of the restaurant's close proximity to my apartment, along with the added bonus that it was a BYO that I had yet to try.  With no reservations, I was nervous about how my party of two would be received upon entering the restaurant, but the hostess greeted us warmly and quickly seated us at an open table.  It was located in the center of the first dining room, which was slightly claustrophobic and very noisy.  Alas, beggars cannot be choosers much like people with no reservations should be damn happy to even get a table at 7:30 on a Saturday night.

We started with the calamari, a perfectly sized portion of tender rings with a large cup of red sauce.  I almost always ask for additional sides of sauce as I am a lover of condiments in excessive quantities, but there was no need in this case which was great.  I would be remiss if I did not also mention the delicious olive oil that came along with the bread basket.  

For dinner, I tried the tilapia livornese.  The large fillets were bathed in a tomato sauce with capers and salty halved olives, and were served alongside buttery julienned vegetables and a pile of creamy risotto.  Give me that fillet of fish, indeed!  This was easily one of the best entrees I've had all year.  

I almost felt a little sorry for my dining companion, who ordered ziti with grilled chicken, tomatoes and broccoli rabe in a white wine sauce.  I tried a bite from his plate and we both agreed that while the components were good, the ziti did not taste like it was homemade (I checked the website and sure enough, the pasta is "imported").  I'd imagine this is rough for an Italian who claims to make his own from scratch.

Full from dinner, we skipped dessert and opted for coffee, which was strong and very tasty.

I'll probably return but will make reservations for the other dining room, which was slightly nicer.  I'd also stick to non-pasta options in favor of the many other seafood or protein selections.

Everyone always told me how much better Vietnam is than Vietnam Palace but, to be honest, I wasn't really blown away. The options all sounded fantastic, and maybe I just ordered the wrong thing, but my chicken curry with veggies and white rice was pretty run of the mill. The sauce was thick, almost like gravy. Onions overwhelmed on the veggie end and there were a few green peppers thrown in, but I would have liked to see some more color.

My girlfriends seemed happy with their selections; some type of seafood stew and an order of salt and pepper shrimp which looked really awesome. Service was excellent and I was surprised how crowded the place got during lunch time, in a section of town I don't find myself in too often. 

I'll definitely be back to check out the full scope of the menu, but for my first visit, I adorn three full stars.

I'm going with three stars for my first visit, though I could easily see Dim Sum House earning another star with some small tweaks. Two friends and I stopped in for an early dinner on a Sunday, and we were seated right away at a table near the bar. It was only when I made a trip to the restroom later on that I noticed the much larger dining room - this is a nicer area though the more informal bar area was fine for our visit. 

I was in the mood for a cocktail, so I went with the What's in the Flask? Magic Potion?, which is a bourbon base with grilled peach syrup, oolong, mint and lemon. It was excellent. One of the best cocktails I've had in recent memory. The second one I ordered was just as good. That drink alone is enough to get me back in the door. 

We ordered a ton of plates to share; perhaps this is why servers kept bringing dishes to our table that we actually didn't order? We repeatedly had to tell servers, no, that order of... isn't ours, but we are still waiting on the... 

Another note about service: our server, while friendly, was also seen chomping away on food at the bar in between taking orders and serving drinks. Not exactly polished. 

As for the food itself, I thought it was really solid. Soup dumplings, scallion pancakes, honey walnut shrimp, noodles, veggies and more were all tasty and perfect for sharing. 

I'd like to return, and I'd love to see some improvements on the service since they are clearly going for a more refined vibe than some of the dim sum restaurants in Chinatown.

Philly Pretzel Factory can't have five stars, because my favorite soft pretzels of all time come from a small mom and pop in NJ. However, Philly Pretzel does serve up a tasty twist, with consistency across their locations. The fact that they were open on Thanksgiving morning until 1pm to provide my homemade beer cheese dip with a vessel (in the form of delicious, salty rivets) was a total lifesaver.

I've been loving Bakeshop on 20th for quick and healthy breakfast delivery every now and then. I love the egg white wrap with feta, tomatoes and spinach. So tasty! I also tried the avocado toast recently, which was absolutely delish as well. 

I'm not as big of a fan of going in to the shop. It's so tiny and gets super crowded. I also find them rather expensive. An avocado toast, salmon avocado toast special, and four largish pastries somehow set me back to the tune of fifty dollars last weekend (plus tip, for the super sweet gentleman working that Sunday). I'm still scratching my head over that one, and I'm clearly not over it. 

I'll be sticking with the breakfast bites, but will be purchasing bulk pastries elsewhere in the future!

SPLENDID! sums up our Ritz-Carlton Bacara stay. From the Bacara team's warm and welcoming hospitality to an unexpected avalanche of surprise-and-delight moments, every minute of our stay was enchanting. 

A heart-happy thank you to Serenity, Beth, Stan, Luis, and Francesca for making our trip so special! 

PROPERTY (5/5)
Sprawling across 78 acres overlooking the Pacific Ocean, the Mediterranean-style resort offers:

-358 rooms and suites
-five restaurants and cafes: modern steakhouse Angel Oak; elegant round O Bar for cocktails and Latin cuisine; The Bistro for breakfast/lunch/dinner; pop-in Lavazza caffe for coffee plus grab-and-go; Haskell's poolside. 
-three infinity-edge heated pools 
-direct au natural beach access. We spotted dolphins frolicking close to shore in the morning! 
-can't help but call out the gorgeous Holiday Rose Tree - created with 1800+ real red roses - and Ritz blue-and-silver Christmas tree avenue in the lobby 
-42,000-sq-ft holistic spa
-clay tennis courts
-ballroom and lecture hall
-versatile ballroom and meeting rooms

ROOM (5/5)
Upon arrival, Stan smilingly checked us in, congratulating us on our special occasions. The resort upgraded us to a 850 square-foot suite suite featuring:

-master bedroom with a heavenly four-poster Frette-linened bed, desk, TV, and sitting area
-separate living room with wet bar and coffee + tea + bottled water station, gas fireplace (so cozy!), TV, and comfy sleeper sofa and armchairs
-two full bathrooms, including a soaking tub complete with fragrant bath salts
-huge wraparound double balcony
-easy elevator access to pools and cabanas

Next, a bevy of in-suite surprises awaited us..

SERVICE (5/5)
Three words: ABOVE AND BEYOND! Starting with a helpful pre-check-in call with Serenity to concierge team members Beth and Luisa's thoughtful gestures to the cheerful friendliness at both check-in and check-out, we felt continually amazed by the Bacara's hospitality. 

Highlights included:

-Beth and Stan's enthusiastic welcome and personal greetings of our party's youngest little member
-generous room to suite upgrade (wow!)
-quick golf cart ride to our villa and bag drop off by Tony
-surprise gifts for occasion 1: Moët champagne; gift box containing a poetically-inscribed crystal and romantic blank message and a bottle; and a lovely handwritten card
-surprise gifts for occasion 2: Martinelli sparkling cider; balloons galore with stuffed Ritz lion; fruit gummies; gift box with a stone moon-and-stars mobile, inspirational crystal, gummy bears, and butterfly ornament; and TWO kind handwritten cards. Incredibly, the gifts were even individually themed! 
-adorable surprise rubber ducky for the smallest guest
-eco-hike guide Francesca's knowledge of the many benefits of local plants, including cowboy's cologne (ie California sagebrush, used by cowboys to attract the ladies!) and purple sage

AMENITIES & EXPERIENCES (5/5)
In addition to beach trails, complimentary bicycles for adults and kids, and heated pools, Bacara offered a wide array of regular fitness, spa, and outdoor and indoor experiences as well as special holiday activities! 

We especially enjoyed:
-guided morning eco-hike with Francesca who illuminated our understanding of local flora and fauna, Chumash culture and traditions, and area history
-Easels and Eggnog painting. Everyone had a blast! 

Other experiences including Aqua Fit, Core & Booty Blast, Zen Den Yoga, Yoga Meditation, a guided daily afternoon beach walk, CSI: Coastal Scene Investigation, Paint and Pinot, and Build-a-Succulent also sounded fantastic. 

Thank you, Ritz Bacara team, for a truly memorable celebration stay! 

PRO TIP 1: Book your desired experiences online well in advance of check-in. Some experiences fill up quickly. 

PRO TIP 2: Bacara is the place to be for the holidays - and any other time of year! Build a Snow Globe, Cookie Decorating, Homemade Hot Cocoa, Wreath Decorating, etc - we wanted to try all the holiday experiences!

Went for lunch empty and they walked us, a group of ten people good for a $500 bill at least and they walked us!!! Twice in fact sent upstairs from down and walked there basically told kick rocks, glad economy so robust that Sculleys can walk a group of ten while empty!!! Bubba Gump happy to seat ten, and when Sculleys is gone blame covid, blame economy, don't blame teens walking your guests!!!

I thoroughly enjoyed this place. We sat outside and when I went inside to use the facilities, I was charmed by the inside decor. It was a new place for us and I'm glad we didn't go to Noshville again because I'm worn out on that place. 

Love Local Beers!  Get more!  

Hot chicken was really good. Wife had the wedge salad w/out bacon (vegetarian). She said it was good, probably shouldn't cost $9.00. But we had fun nonetheless.

Nice spot for take and bake. First time here and it feels like an old school local joint.
Service was great. Price was normal.
Food quality was way better than their take n bake competition and tasted fresh.
The salad was good too.
The wings are baked. Which means they arent as good as fried. But that does make them healthier.
Will definitely pick this place over papa's any time.

I really don't understand the hype.  

Going to this restaurant I was expecting something a la Frontera Grill or Topolobampo -- gourmet, authentic regional Mexican food.  What I got was, as usual for St. Louis, a bland, unauthentic representation along with snotty, rushed service.  As usual, a focus on somewhat improved margaritas, which if you've had the real deal in Mexico (and no, your whitebread all-inclusive in Cancun doesn't count - that's not real Mexico).  

The pricing is outrageous for the quality of food.  Two of us ordered margaritas, queso fundido, pollo con mole poblano and camarones al mojo de ajo.

Margaritas were way too sweet.  A real, authentic Mexican margaritas should be fresh, strong, slightly sweet with fresh juices.  They're served in small martini-style glasses and pack a punch.  These were, as usual, served to please the St. Louisan palate:  too sweet and too large a portion to be of top quality.

The queso fundido wasn't terrible, but the flour tortillas were close to inedible.  If you're ordering anything that requires them, ask for corn tortillas.

The pollo con mole poblano was extremely dry.  The mole sauce wasn't that spectacular, either -- way too bland and came out cold.  The sides were pedestrian at best.  Where's the refried black beans with queso fresco?  Not on this menu!  

The camarones were overcooked and the sauce lacked any flavor other than burnt garlic.  Again, a painful representation of a dish that can be eaten perfectly cooked for less than $10 at any top-quality taqueria.  

Here's the deal:  you want real, authentic Mexican?  Go to Cherokee Street, pick any of the multitude of restaurants, and have a meal for two for the cost of a single entree at Milagro.  You'll find much more authentic flavors and, frankly, better quality.

Just like almost everything else in St. Louis, Milagro represents the problem with our food scene perfectly:  the average St. Louisan wants a place to get loaded on cheap "margs" with their friends with eating "guac" and nachos.  These people are so bland and conditioned to like terrible imitations of the real thing that when something just slightly better than Taco Bell comes along, they go nuts for it.  That's the case here.  Anybody who's dined at any real "modern Mexican" restaurant knows at one taste where this one fails.   Somebody's asleep at the wheel.   

Again:  bypass the hype, save the money, and go to one of the real Mexican joints in the city.  You'll be glad you did, while the Alive Magazine see-and-be-seen set keeps drooling over this place.

Darn good Jersey Fist Pumping Strip Mall food does exist! 

I have to admit this has been by far the best wiener outside of Chicago that I have ever had in my mouth! Get your mind out of the gutter and enjoy the explosive flavor of this long, massively tasty dog.

Not only do these bad boys pop & explode with flavor with every bite but they come in many styles with toppings GALORE!

Hot Dog Fanatics.. COOL DOG CAFE IS THE PLACE TO GO!

The fact that this place knows EXACTLY how to make a Chicago Style Hot Dog (not on the menu, but ask for one they'll make it) is a HUGE bonus. Besides not having the right bun ( when really one can only get a true Chicago bun IN CHICAGO), this place by far has served me the best Chicago Style Hot Dog I have ever had outside of The Windy City! Majorly impressed and satisfied!

They don't stop at dogs though, they have Mac & Cheese, Sliders, BBQ and FRITES with your choice of house-made dipping sauces. Honestly, you don't even need the dipping sauce because they also provide a bottle of my salty heaven on every table... MALT VINEGAR BABY! Drown those potatoes in a pool of vinegar!! 

In the end, when it comes to wieners I have to be honest..size, texture, and taste ALWAYS MATTERS. Cool Dog Cafe's wieners are worth the drive, just remember to load up on napkins because when it's this good it is bound to get MESSY! :)

I am a bad, naughty, dirty, weekday vegan....

Yes I just started my "summer weather diet" but I couldn't help myself. It was 87 degrees out and I live 3 blocks from Franklin Square Park. I took my dogs for a "walk" and decided to sneak myself the famous SqaureBurger *CAKE SHAKE*!

Was it Vegan? No
Was it under 300 calories? Most likely not
Was it amazing?! It's a milkshake made of vanilla ice cream blended with TastyKake Butterscotch Krimpets, sponge cakes covered with butterscotch icing.... YES IT WAS FREAKIN' AMAZING!
Do I have regrets?! Of course I do and no I did not tell my husband or post it on Facebook.

Ashamed, I took a long cold shower after to scrub off the guilt & sickness I felt from the sugar overload.

But yes ladies it is worth all the shame! Treat yourself this summer and let it remain your dirty little secret. ;-)

All I need is some vintage clothes, and I feel like I've teleported back to the 1930s... and as if, a small part of Paris is tucked inside NOLA.

The house sauce was INCREDIBLE! My boyfriend and I didn't know what to get and we felt like we were kind of in a rut, but then he suggested burgers and this place fit the bill. It was easy to order online and pick up from here.

I heart Philly Cupcake. 

I could end my review there because that's what I really want to say. However, in the interest of urging others to visit Philly Cupcake, I will expand. 

I am sort of cupcake crazed--this is something everyone should know about me. I have been to the store an embarrassing number of times already. I have tried many of their cupcakes as a result of my obsession. So here we go down the review path... 
Vanilla cake with vanilla frosting - An old classic. The cake itself was very interesting because the top had a bite to it while the inside of the cake was moist and fluffy. I really liked that aspect. Vanilla buttercream was great but could have used a tiny bit more vanilla. Second time I had the vanilla buttercream (on a chocolate cupcake), it was spot on. 
Chocolate cake with vanilla frosting - Even better. Their chocolate cake is fantastic. My only complaint is that, when ripping off the stump end, a few crumbles fell on the floor so I did not get to eat them. They died a tragically sad death that day. 
Lemon cake with lemon buttercream - One of my favorites! You have to like SWEET and LEMON to like this cupcake. Don't be surprised if you don't like it if you don't meet both of those requirements. I've had lemon cupcakes in other shops and, believe me, this one is much better. Who wants a bitter lemon cupcake? Not me. Philly Cupcake gets it right. The cake part is deliriously moist. I don't know what they have done with it but I pray they do that with another type of cake--maybe lime or blueberry. 
The Chocolate Coma - Flourless chocolate cake with chocolate buttercream covered in chocolate gnache. Ummm... wow. I thought I had died and gone to chocolate heaven. The cake itself, which is generally at the bottom of the cupcake love totem pole for me, was actually my favorite part. Philly Cupcake should make flourless chocolate cake more often with other toppings. 
Jewish apple streusel - I won't get this one again simply because it's not a cupcake if you ask me. My boyfriend loved this one because he's more of a simple cake fan than a cupcake with sugary frosting fan. Something for everyone at Philly Cupcake!
Banana cake with peanut butter frosting - Looks cute, tastes great. Brings me back to the days of peanut butter and banana sandwiches. The only way to make this better would be with a drizzle of honey or a strawberry jam surprise on the inside. 
Chocolate Peanut Butter Massacre - chocolate cake with peanut butter buttercream and Reese crumbles - WOW. Far, far better than the banana cake with PB frosting above. The combination of peanut butter and chocolate is always a winner. This cupcake does not disappoint. Plus their chocolate cake is much more moist than the flaky banana cake. 
Gingerbread cupcake - This little gem even had a tiny gingerbread man on top! So cute. I got it right around Christmas time. The gingerbread cake could have had a touch more spice. 
Cookies and Cream - this cupcake is made with devil's food cake and Oreo vanilla buttercream. This was my boyfriend's favorite of all the cupcakes we've tried. I liked it because the cake was moist but light--not as dense as their other chocolate cake--which is generally never achieved with devil's food cake. The Oreo buttercream was just so-so for me. 
Strawberry cake with strawberry frosting - definite winner! The strawberry cake has the same consistency as the vanilla bean cake with that slightly crispy top. I love that for some reason. It makes it even easier to rip off the stump end of the cupcake, eat that alone and then enjoy the top with a mountain of frosting.
Twix cupcake - chocolate cupcake with caramel buttercream and Twix pieces - my new favorite. Hands down, this cupcake was spot on. The caramel buttercream is sweet, light, fluffy, creamy... everything you could want in a buttercream. AND they drizzle this cupcake with caramel. Winner, winner, cupcakes for dinner. 

I think the only thing Philly Cupcake could do better would be to take credit/debit card purchases. Perhaps once they grow a bit more, they will. The folks who work there are so fun and friendly and, clearly, they love cupcakes. 

My suggestions to Philly Cupcake:
Blueberry cake with blueberry buttercream
Your fantastic lemon cake with blueberry buttercream frosting garnished with fresh blueberries (not fondant blueberries)
Flourless chocolate cake with vanilla bean buttercream frosting with salted caramel stuffed inside the cake
Key lime cupcake
Chocolate cake with mint buttercream

Disclaimer. This is a great 5 star sushi restaurant for Tucson Arizona. 
I've had my fair share of great sushi. Living in LA and Hawaii, I know my stuff. This is definitely some good American sushi. Not too rice heavy and the service was great! 
Came here on a Saturday night and there was no wait but definitely people were flowing in. The tempura was a little heavy for my taste but it was fresh and the edamame was nice. I definitely appreciate the free taste of sushi that came with our meal, but it was a super American fried salmon roll. 
Nigiri was really nice. The tamago and the tofu skin was flavorful and fresh. The rice was seasoned perfectly. The rolls we got were also very good and not to rice heavy which I really appreciated. 
All in all, best sushi place I've found in Tucson.

Bar none, the best Chinese food I've had, anywhere, ever.

I'm not even kidding. If I wanted to start this review with a joke, It'd go something like this:

Me: Knock knock.
You: Who's there?
Me: Gimme.
You: Gimme, who?
Me: Gimme all your money because this is a robbery and I needs it for my dry fried beef!
You: Ow, my liver!
Me: *flees the scene a la Cops*

You see that? This grub is almost good enough to induce murderous food lust. I say almost, because I took out the poison from my jacket (I always carry a little with me) and strongly considered applying it to each of my dinner companions to maximize the amount of food I was getting. I didn't... THIS time...

We did a whole ton of courses as a tasting menu organized by Dave H. Here's what I remember:

1) Cucumbers in chili oil - the name does not do these little guys justice. You have to have these. They're an odd mix of cold and hot, but it works.

2) Tripe in chili oil - I hate tripe. I LOVE Han's take on it. I was actually able to bite through it.

3) Cold sesame soy noodles - Semi sweet and vaguely nutty thanks to the sesame seed oil. A good contrast for the spicier things that we had.

4) Dumplings in chili oil - This was the hottest thing I remember that night. Not the spiciest thing I've ever tasted anywhere, but it packed a punch.

5) Dan dan noodles - With such a ridiculous name, it's easy to see how I was initially skeptical of them. I mean, I could practically hear the little oriental flute from Carl Douglas' "Kung Fu Fighting" going on in the background as I ate it. Still, this was probably one of the best things I had all night. Believe the hype, because these guys straddle that line between junky comfort food and quality cuisine that won't require you to spend the next 24 hours on a toilet seat.

6) Dry fried beef - Da bomb. Get this. NOW!

7) Cumin pork - my least favorite, but still pretty good.

8) Fish soup - standard hot/slightly sour soup with some kinda light-meat fish in it. I'm not so good at identifying fish meat. It was tasty.

9) Mapo tofu - I hate tofu. I liked mapo tofu. Spicy and pungent.

10) Salt-battered shrimp - very very salty. Not my taste, but maybe it was because I'd been eating a bunch of really hot things before that. You might like it, if you like salt battered squid.

11) Shredded chicken with crispy rice - This was surprisingly sweet and light. Very good as a contrast to the spicier dishes.

12) Some other stuff I'm sure I'm forgetting. Try it all!

This is the kind of food they write songs about. One of these days, Chef Han will not be remembered as he should - for saving us all from the combined robot/zombie apocalypse (Robozompocalypse 2020!) - but rather for his spicy dan dan noodles.

The Manayunk space is very well laid out - the dining room is more square than rectangle, so that means no fumbling your way around other diners trying to get to the rest room. Also, it's great for big groups, and is, at least since I last visited, still a BYO. 

On a final note, I met Han, and he was a really cool guy. I told him I'd be back with Dave sometime to sample his face-meltingest, sperm-killingist, spicy dish. I'm excited.

Pro-tip:
Bring friends to share with - everyone order a different thing, and have them all split family style. TOTALLY worth it.

What a disappointing experience at the very much hyped-up Prairie Noodle Shop. 

I came here today (a Tuesday) around 12:30pm with a friend. The place is pretty small but luckily there was a table free or room at the eating bar. We chose to sit at a table.

Our server showed up shortly afterwards to see if we were ready to order. No introduction, no pleasantries. But we needed a few minutes still to review the menu.

I decided on the chicken ramen while my fried ordered the pork ramen. Plus she wanted to try the pork buns (we chose the pork belly vs. pulled pork) which we told were about the size of your palm. Yup, no lies there... the "buns" were literally the size of your palm and filled with three measly pieces of pork belly each. For $10 I thought the portion sizes were ridiculously small and the flavor of their combinations nothing to write home about. 

Shortly after we finished the two-bite buns, our noodles arrived. My friend and I both agreed that our respective orders were also disappointing in terms of broth flavour and depth... plus I found mine too salty. The noodles (which are not made house) were just okay and although had the right texture and consistency, didn't really add much to the ramen surprisingly. I didn't even finish eating my whole bowl of chicken ramen which is how disappointed I was. Not to mention each bowl of ramen is a set price of $15 - pretty steep for what you get in my opinion. My chicken bowl came with a marinated chicken wing (mostly for garnish I think as there was barely any meat on mine), pieces of chicken, half an umeboshi egg, kale, green onions (way too many by the way that I had to scoop most of them out), and pickled pearl onions. 

Our server never once checked up on us to see how we were enjoying our meal. And when we were finished our bowls, she dropped off our bill without us asking (Grrrrr! Such a pet peeve of mine when servers don't inquire if there's anything else we want - i.e., dessert? a drink? etc). It wasn't overly busy in the place so I don't see why the lack of customer service and rush to kick us out.  Plus, literally right after we paid our bill, our waters were cleared from our table even though we weren't ready to leave.... Seriously?! We were so annoyed that my friend made it a point to tell the person who cleared our water glasses that we weren't done with them. The girl, although apologizing, didn't seem like she meant it, looked annoyed and said she'd bring us new glasses. That she did, but they were hastily filled only half way full. Really? 

Anyways, needless to say, based on the terrible customer service and disappointing food, I'm pretty sure my friend and I won't be back to this establishment. Edmonton's ramen scene, although improving overall with it's choices... is still not up to par with larger cities like Los Angeles and Vancouver. I'd rather save my hard-earned money and have a real bowl of ramen when I travel.

This restaurant has the worst customer service I've ever experienced.  Skip this location! Pick another place for your sports, wings, etc.

By request, here at the gruesome details:

I called the restaurant at 4:00 to place a to go order for pickup at 5:00.  Recognizing that Super Bowl Sunday is a very busy day for these guys I expected some delay in getting my food and getting back out the door to the Super Bowl Party.  In fact, when the hostess said they could have it ready by 5, I said "make it 5:15, I know you guys are busy".  I arrived early and began waiting with about 15 other patrons who looked equally irritated. 

At 5:30 a manager approached and told me that my order would be "right up".  At 5:45 the same manager told me that my wings were being "sauced up" and I'd be on my shortly.  At 6:00 I approached the take out counter to request a soft drink...the staff balked and it took significant prodding to get more than a "kid sized" cup while I waited. Looking back I should've asked for a bucket of beer.  Fast forward to 6:20pm, my wings arrive, the first quarter of the Super Bowl is over and I receive little more than a "our bad" from the manager(s) on duty.  There were no less than 10 other customers whose orders were presumably lost by the incompetent staff at this location.  I won't be surprised to see many more negative reviews of this particular location. 

In the interest of full disclosure, I like BW3's and have been a customer of theirs for a long time.  The food is generally good and other locations seem to have it "right" in terms of staff and customer service.

West side wins!  The west side of Tucson has amazing Mexican food but limited other options, in comes Maru to finally add a delicious option. 

It is very busy as is expected for an underserved area so plan to wait a bit to order, but the food comes out fast.

The set up is interesting with small side dishes and "appetizers" in a buffet like line that you select prior to ordering.  We selected the takoyaki, pork katsu, edamame, and salmon onigiri.  They have vegetarian options as well like tempura yams and plum onigiri.  All of the small dishes were delicious,  the sauces that were paired with them were balanced and matched the food perfectly.  

They have Japanese drinks (we got the green tea and mango drinks), soda, beer, wine and sake as well as deserts like mochi, daifuku, and cheese mushi pan.

The highlight was the udon and ramen.  Both were very flavorful and we'll balanced. We had a curry Udon Wich had a perfect curry flavor that went well with the udon and chicken.  The tantan ramen was spicy as advertised but not so hot as to be unpleasant.  The flavor was very deep and full of umami making you wanting more.

The staff were friendly, helpful and attentive even as busy as they were.  The price point was under $10 for a bowl and under $5 for the smaller items, very reasonable particularly considering the quality of the food. We are excited to add this place to our regular dining options on the west side and encourage people from all over Tucson to come to this hidden gem.

Yes!  Great Mexican food!  I've been underwhelmed by most of the other "best Mexican" places people have recommended and now, finally, the gleaming ray of sunshine that is Izatccihuatl has entered my life.  

The green & red salsas that came with the chips were spicy and flavorful; the whole table took turns tasting each one trying to decide which one was spicier, still a draw.  Choriqueso was incredible, not too greasy and quite tasty.  I got the chalupas and covered them in salsas... satisfaction attained.

This Mel's Diner happened to be inside Sands Regency Hotel where we stayed for the nice and we did a late check in and almost every every restaurant was about closed. This diner was open 24/7 which was convenient for us. 

The place was not really crowded but many had to-go orders. Also, on a Thursday, they only had one server so they limited seating inside. We had to put our name on the list and they texted us after 30 minutes. 

The staff was friendly and place was pretty clean. Mel's food are decent but not anything extraordinary about this American food. Portions are pretty decent. I still like that their shakes, they give extra for sharing but my cookies and cream shake lacked Oreos! :-(.   Not my first choice to eat at but glad it's open all day! [30th/100]

okay guys, I am so glad I found this place because we haven't had any decent sushi in months since we got here and I was starting to think boise just wasn't ready to give us the real stuff yet....

this place may not be in rolls but it makes up for all of that by being fresh, having tons of ingredients to choose for your bowl, and giving you lots of options.

I chose the "medium"
half rice and half salad 
tuna and salmon
chili shoyu/spicy mayo for sauces
seaweed salad, crab stick, cucumber, scallions, and avocado for my toppings (you get 5)
sesame seeds on top and wasabi on the side 

oh thank heaven for fresh fish and a really good sushi roll in bowl form! I was so happy. my hubby was as well. 

two bowls stuffed us and it was $30. we have spent so much money on sushi here and it wasn't half the quality that we got from poke bowl!

despite my 5 star review, I have a couple friendly suggestions- spicy tuna as an option! I looove spicy tuna all chopped up. another suggestion is instead of crab stick they have crab mix! it's the best thing ever. the stick was good but not the same. that's all I got. 

thanks poke bowl- you scored a couple regulars!

The Old Spaghetti Factory is our go to restaurant for a good meal. Our most recent visit was for my son's second birthday. I called the morning of and made reservations for seven people. The lady on the phone said they do not always take reservations, it depends on the day the time and the number of people in the party.  I am not sure about that. We arrived at our reservation time and we were seated immediately.
I love that all entrées come with bread soup or salad your entrée and ice cream for dessert. I always order the chicken marsala. It is my favorite thing on the menu. It is a chicken breast with a wine and mushroom sauce. I also ordered the salad with the house ranch dressing. 
My son is allergic to dairy so they put a candle in applesauce and sang happy birthday to him. It was super cute!! 
If everyone in your group is over 21 the bar is upstairs and it's open seating.

Went on opening night and we were greeted at the front door by Dan who introduced himself and showed us a nice table for two in the center of the restaurant so we had a great view of the whole restaurant. Texture seems to be important here as the walls, menus, business cards and lighting offers a nice touch to the whole classy but fun atmosphere at KO.  From the wooden wall with backlighting and the opposing wall had a white textured, and crisp clean line to it. Very cool! The lighting was well placed and appropriate, comfy seating and seating arrangements looked pretty decent.The staff were pleasant, engaging and checked on us frequently but not interfering at all. Clearly they wanted to make a good impression and that's always appreciated.  
Our orders of spicy Korean chicken and bao buns which are like little pillows that cradle your pork belly were Delish. So not only did the chef make our food look tasty, it was well presented and delicious. Not too spicy as far as the heat goes but I like fairly hot spices. There were other choices for the Korean chicken so feel free to try the others. That's my goal. The portion sizes were perfect and priced right. I don't like having to leave with extra to justify the price. That isn't the case here. Portion size and price match up nicely. Liquor license becomes effective next month or so and I'll have to go back when they can serve but for now I'm fine with a BYO.
When we were finished, our plates were cleared quickly and while a touch of dessert would have been nice, maybe it was a sign to not overeat. Lol
As an aside I love the color scheme too. By the time we left after 9 pm, people were still streaming in on opening night so bravo to the whole staff for working to give us a great experience at KO.
I'm telling everyone about this place and took a bunch of the cards with me. Can't wait to try so much more of the menu creations. 
Wishing KO much success! See you all there.

A great place knows what it does well and does it consistently. Stock's pound cake (or many pound cake) is a delicious treat. I haven't had it in years, and honestly it just slipped my mind as "a thing" even until I heard the name come up in conversation recently. And then...I had to go back. So on a trip last weekend to Port Richmond to buy kielbasa I had to make a swing down to Lehigh Avenue and got some "many pounds pound cake." The look on my kids eyes when they bit into it the first time was priceless. My 8 year old, who claims she doesn't like cake, had a sparkle in here eyes and asked "why didn't you tell me about this before".

Well....that says it all.

I'm such a creature of habit and really only decided to try Blue Moose because I was too frigging tired to walk down to Bitter Bob's where I have literally eaten breakfast 11,000 times, perhaps more. And with all due respect to Bob, this place is the shit. Great little restaurant with an absolutely charming (sorry but I couldn't think of a better word) outdoor deck. Food was awesome, service friendly and attentive and honestly, I couldn't think of a single thing wrong with it. Okay, maybe the bathroom's a bit cramped. 1/10th star deduction. 

But seriously, if you're looking for a truly excellent casual place to have a great little meal in New Hope, you'll be hard pressed to find a better choice. And to anyone who give them less than 4 enthusiastic stars, WTF? Really? This place is great.
Very nice! Good food, and very helpful staff. They always attend to your needs as a customer, and generally have a nice welcoming attitude.

My restaurant policy:   If I leave your restaurant hungry, I will never return.  It doesn't matter if your food is great (it was mediocre at best), or if your service is spectacular (which it wasn't).  If I have to go home and eat chips after paying $100, I will not be a happy camper, period.

I certainly feel like I'm going against the grain here as my star rating is not reflective of my fellow Yelpstas.  But, I'm writing this one certainly with disappointment.  My work team ventured to Palomino's for our Christmas lunch to toss around fun white elephant gifts over drinks and food.  

The dining room was packed which got me excited because I deduce lively guests as a hint to what I'm going to experience-- a great time.  I did have a great time, but that was due to my co-workers.  It took a long time before our server made it to the table.  She seemed rushed and understandably so as it looked like she had too many tables to turn.  We started with the calamari and bruschetta.  The apps arrived after some time, but the calamari was replaced with something else; thus, causing us to wait for the calamari again.  What peeved me is that instead of just leaving the wrong app on the table the server took it back to the kitchen.  Why wouldn't you just leave the app?  Extend an olive branch to a large group that was hungry.

My party ordered a variety of entrees from salads, sandwiches, salmon,etc..  I chose the scallops.  My scallops came out and all the anticipation I had for a great meal was exhausted.  Take a look at my pic and ask yourself if you would pay $17 for them.  Disc golf anyone? Then take a look at my pic of my wife's scallops at Joe's in Carmel. Palominos are underwhelming, tiny and far from quality especially when they were smothered in a putrid colored sauce.  If I wasn't with my co-workers I would have sent it back-- and I don't send stuff back.  They lacked flavor.  Total let down and I left hungry.  Who leaves a restaurant hungry?

Service was very slow and the menu needs re-evaluated.  Bring down the price point, too.  The quality of the food doesn't correlate with the price they demand.

I'm really struggling on what to rate Giordano's.  I grew up with them in Chicago.  They have always been my ultimate favorite stuffed pizza maker on the planet.  One time I literally walked miles to get one and take it home.  It's worth it, but the newest addition to the chain in Indianapolis has certainly disappointed me on multiple occasions.  

Before opening "officially," we carried out the all famous cheesy pie without problems.  For those that love Chicago style stuffed pizza you'll probably agree with me that this stuff would be a solid bartering item pre-dating currency.  I felt like I was going to get jumped by the waiting crowd when trying to make it through the crowd to the door.  If only they knew I was packing a stun gun.  LOL.  Just kidding but in reality these people had it in their eyes.  

So the first time carrying out went without a hitch.  A week later I called and received a busy signal and was hung up several times.  Finally, reached someone and they said they weren't taking carry-out orders that day.  Grrrrrrrrr.... Seriously?  Total let down.  Forget running the dining room.  Focus on carry out.  Get as many pies out there.  Then again they're proving the supply and demand concept works.

Last week I jumped online and placed an order to be picked up at 4PM.  Totally stoked that I even got a spot in the queue, I drove to the restaurant and was faced with a line of fellow pizza lovers already assembled.  The sign on the door said "Closed until 4PM due to an adjustment to the oven."  Not a big deal since my pick-up time was 4PM.  They promptly opened at 4PM and I made it fairly quickly to the carry-out counter.  Then it happened.  The online order system crashed and no orders placed online made it to the restaurant.  WHAT!  No!  This can't be happening.  I thought I was going into shock.

Long story short, the manager offered me a free pizza if I was willing to wait at least 45 minutes for it.  I ended up sitting at the bar and enjoyed a glass of pinot grigio until my pizza came out an hour and 15 minutes later.  By then there was a huge line, 3 1/2 hour wait, and a ton of people packed into a very small waiting area.  I ran like fire to my car with all eyes on the box.  

I know that the bugs will be eventually fixed, but I don't see the hype dying down anytime soon.  I look forward to revising the review and increasing my star rating in the future.  But for now, I'm going to wait, give my pizza fix a break, and give it another shot months down the road.  Better yet, I may just drive to Chicago and get one from the mother ship.  I could probably go to and back in the same amount of time.

Despite the rainy weather, we waited 45 minutes outside to dine at Willie Mae's Scotch House. The dining room was spacious and comfy. There was upbeat R&B music in the background. This establishment does not serve alcohol nor split checks, but the food is worth the wait. Parties of 5 or more must pay 20% in gratuity. 

Our server Candy was busy but attentive to our needs. We shared a House Salad, which consisted of mixed greens, grape tomatoes, bell peppers, croutons, and cheddar cheese and was served with Thousand Island dressing. 

Due to a $4 plate charge if we share plates, we were forced to order four plates of Fried Chicken. Each plate consisted of three pieces of fried chicken - either white or dark meat with your choice of side. White meat came in the form of chicken breast while dark meat came in the form of drumsticks, wings, and thighs.

I felt like chicken was double fried and marinated with hot sauce. It was crispy, airy, flaky, and hot (both in temperature and flavor). The dark meat was tender and juicy. 

Some of our favorite sides included the Rice with Gravy, Stewed Green Beans, Mac & Cheese, Fried Okra, Brown Sugar Glazed Brussels Sprouts, and Corn Bread Muffins.

By the end of the meal, we were stuffed and sadly, did not save room for dessert but heard great things about their cheesecakes.

Due to a late start, we missed the Old New Orleans Rum Distillery Tour, which costs $15 per person, includes tastings, and occurs every two hours between 12pm and 4pm. 

Since we didn't want to wait 1.5 hours for the next tour, we decided to have tastings, which costs $7.50 per person and consisted of a shot of five liqueurs - Crystal, Gingeroo, Amber, Cajun, Gris Gris.

Their Award Winning Crystal Rum is made from molasses that was fermented and distilled twice. It goes well in rail and mixed cocktails. 

Their Gingeroo Cocktail is made of their Crystal Rum, spicy orange ginger, and pure Louisiana sugar cane. It was light, bubbly, and refreshing. 

Their Amber Rum is aged in bourbon and whiskey barrels for 3-7 years. It goes great in classic cocktails such as Rum and Coke, Old Fashion, Mint Julep, Bramble, and Hurricane.

Their Cajun Spice Rum is made with Crystal rum and a blend of baking spices including Cinnamon, Nutmeg, Allspice, Cloves, Ginger, Vanilla, Chicory, and Cayenne. It goes great in holiday cocktails such as spiked apple cider or hot toddy.

Their Gris Gris Cayenne Liqueur is made from Crystal Rum, cayenne pepper, and organic ginger. 

I enjoyed the first three as they were lighter in flavor and body and did not have a spicy kick to it.

Kind of an absolute gem overlooking the Santa Barbara harbor- your lucky if you get the bar still spots facing the ocean  they allow dogs on the patio. They make pins coladas that are so tasty-you will want 2  chips and salsa  is a great combination and they provide an adequate amount of sauce for their price. It's a great environment to bring your friends to or even just to enjoy yourself on a beautiful  fun day

Nice space inside with a bunch of tables, friendly (enough) staff, and a truly delightful patio to enjoy the beautiful weather. My bagel with lox also came with red onions and capers and tomatoes and it was so tasty! I got the side of fresh fruit which was strawberries and they were a perfect sweet treat to balance out the tart and salty bagel and lox. The fruit side is seasonal. Potato chip side is a bag of Zapp's, solid but nothing to write home about. My cafe au lait was also very good--take this with a pillar of salt though because I usually drink the cheap stuff so any step above that is a fancy treat. 

The prices were very reasonable as all of the ingredients were fresh and tasty, and the lox portion on my bagel was also very generous! 

If I'm in the neighborhood, I would definitely come back, especially if the weather is nice outside because the patio...for real, beautiful. But I'm a little too much of a homebody to drive across town for this. So it's good and solid, but not out-of-this-world.

I've only been twice, and I got the same thing both times, yet I am still eagerly giving 5 stars. The Dr. Tan burger itself is worth about 48 stars so it wouldn't even matter what else I had tried, honestly. It's a thing of beauty; perfectly cooked burger, jalapeno slices, slaw, bacon, a delicious sauce...also, it's freaking massive! And comes with super delicious an addicting fries on the side. I was so enormously stuffed after finishing this burger and still nibbled away at the fries because they were so good.

It's a touch pricey (my burger & fries came to $14.30 before tax) but the size and quality of this meal make it extremely worth every penny. The service is great in a very chill way--last time I sat at the bar and one of the owners helped me, hung around just long enough for me to tell him how amazing the food was and not long enough to make it weird. Ya know? 

They do a brisk take-out business for lunch on the weekdays so eating in took a little longer than expected, but once that burger was put in front of me, all cares and worries were gone. I can't wait to come back and have it again...and again...and again...

My beloved TJ's is finally here in the New Orleans area! This branch is a touch on the small side, though I've certainly seen smaller. They've packed a big punch in here, though! All of the usual favorites are here. I love the double roasted salsa, the chili pepper hot sauce, the huge and affordable selection of delicious cheeses, the honey Greek yogurt, the spinach salad...the list could go on, but those are my staples. There are so many items here that you can't find anywhere else, and all at great prices!

Their seasonal selections are really fantastic. It's September 23 and they are chock full of pumpkin EVERYTHING! Even pumpkin vinaigrette! 

Plus, they treat their employees really well. You can tell when you interact with them. They're friendly, helpful, funny, just so pleasant! I love it! 

If you've never been before, definitely take your time to peruse the aisles and check out all the funky stuff they have to offer. And if you find something you love--stock up! Because they use a lot of small producers, sometimes things get discontinued unexpectedly. (My aforementioned salsa was discontinued for a while and my family was very distraught; luckily it came back though). 

They also have excellent canvas totes and 2 sizes of super cute and durable cooler bags. I've got every make and model and they are super useful. 

See y'all at TJ's!

I have never been to the original Willie Mae's location, which is probably one of the worst things I have ever done to myself. This fried chicken almost made me cry. I'm thinking about it right now, almost 24 hours later, and I'm about to cry. Every bite more delicious than the last. By far, the best fried chicken I have ever had, probably in the top 5 best foods I have ever had the privilege of eating. 

That's right, food so delicious it's a privilege to eat it.

The store set-up is pretty self-explanatory; order at the counter, get a number, wait for your food to arrive (whether take-out or eat-in). I got to try the chicken fried pork (unbelievable) and the red beans (delicious) in addition to my fried chicken and mac and cheese.

Honestly, this fried chicken is so good the cook could have come over and slapped me in the face and I still would have loved it. And him. And everything. And this chicken. I can't handle it! My whole life is falling apart and all I want is Willie Mae's fried chicken! Sentences are so hard! 

Luckily the cook did not slap me in the face (at least not literally!) and the service was very friendly. The chicken takes a while to cook so they came over and refilled my water and asked if I needed anything. Very thoughtful. It was a little bit of an early dinner so maybe they just didn't have much to do as it wasn't crowded, but I appreciated the gesture.

In summary: I'm going to marry this chicken, just like Pee-Wee married that...jello? Cake? I can't remember. I love this chicken, and it loves me. We are perfect for each other, and I look forward to spending many an evening wrapped in its warm and delicious love.

I brought the bf here for his birthday dinner because he loves wings. LOVES THEM. So I thought I'd treat him to some specialty versions of his favorite things, because my gift-giving abilities are just that original. 

The service is friendly, the menu is pretty compact so you shouldn't have difficulty choosing what you want. We got 3 types of wings--kim chi, jerk, and buffalo--and the boy wanted meat pies but luckily asked at the last minute and found out they had cheese in them, so we switched to hot boudin instead (for the record, I love cheese more than life itself, it's the boy who can't eat it). Some might complain about the price, and it is a little steep considering there's 50-cent wing places somewhere I'm sure, but obviously you're getting something a little more "craft" than "Budweiser" here so I get it.

The boudin was really good and comes with mustard. The wings were pretty good...they were bigger than I had seen before, which was good, so we were both full after the meal. The supposedly "jerk" wings were very much not jerk. They had this think, chunky sauce on them, which I really liked and would LOVE to cook some chicken or shrimp in and serve over rice, but it would too cumbersome for wings. The buffalo sauce was a little...sweeter I think, than I was expecting. I like buffalo sauce that's nice and tangy and vinegar-y and this didn't hit the spot. The kim chi really just tasted like teriyaki sauce, which wasn't bad, but I was expecting something a little more. Finally, the dipping sauce they gave us (both homemade) were seriously underwhelming. 

I have to tell you, fully recalling this experience as I've described it above, I just lowered the rating from 3 to 2 stars. I wanted to give the benefit of the doubt, but the more I thought about it, the more I wish I had just gotten some regular spicy buffalo wings at any bar, as those would have hit the spot better. Oh well, Bouree. I don't regret trying you, but I certainly won't return.

Man, does this place ever suck. My cousin, who was in town for just a short amount of time, went ahead and made this reservation for a group of six of us on somewhat short notice. I had never eaten here, so I checked Yelp and saw all of the terrible reviews and immediately asked her if we could go somewhere else, like nearby Fuji Mountain. It was to no avail, and we all ended up at Serafina.

Everything about this place is The Worst. They gave us a hard time about seating us a few minutes early, even though they literally told is that our table was ready, and tried to get us to wait in the overcrowded bar area. When they finally took us to our table, the table itself could have easily accommodated four patrons. But as I mentioned, there were six of us. The table was also jammed against the wall and two other tables, so we were all sandwiched in, to the extent that taking a deep breath would have been an endeavor. Being that I am claustrophobic, I especially did not appreciate this.

The food was as middling and underachieving as everyone else has pointed out. I paid $20 for lobster ravioli that contained no actual lobster, but a vague seafood-ish flavor, in a "lobster bisque sauce" that was basically just some sparse orangey-ish cream sauce with hunks of celery sitting in it. I tried some of my cousin's pizza and it was flavorless crust with uncooked mixed greens sitting on top. The hell? Special requests from others at the table were ignored, being that the service was even worse than the food. It took over an hour for us to actually get our food, and not once did our server come over to apologize about the wait or let us know what was going on. Someone from our table had to actually get up and go find him when we had all been sitting around with empty glasses for ten minutes and he was apparently just standing around.

They did end up giving us $15 off the bill due to the insane wait, but I would have rather had my two hours back. Yeah, I understand it was busy, but if your kitchen and wait staff can't accommodate that many patrons, than maybe, say, don't cram as many tables into your tacky-ass restaurant as humanly possible. Because customers like breathing as much as not waiting over an hour for their food.

I just can't say enough bad about this place. I hate it and I'll never, ever, ever, ever, ever go back in my life. You shouldn't go either.

Decorated in western style with country music, friendly waiters, the buffalo wings were crispy with ample tangy buffalo sauce.  It set our expectations high!

The black and blue 1/2 lb burger was made of good, slightly coarsely minced beef which gives it a nice bite but it was not seasoned.  The "good" fries were on their way to cook to a nice outside crunch, but they were prematurely served :/ so they didn't have the bite and were slightly greasy.

The French dip Tri tip came in 2 large thin triangular sandwiches slapped with mayo with three small strips of meat, nothing else.  The fried onions were over fried (slightly burnt) and dripping with oil.

You can definitely feel that the ingredient is good but the cook is sloppy!  Owner take notice.

It also made me realize that Yelp ratings are all relative! This place won't get more than 3 stars in LA or the Bay Area in California.

location easily passed it twice while driving, so decided to walk and found # 724, as there is no sign outside.  It's set for a pick up of orders but with a nice table outside, a true dive.  The gentleman that took the order was very pleasant, looks like his wife is making the empanadas fresh to order and his/her mum manning the oven.  A true little family operation.

Organic beef, chicken and prechutto  are fabulous!! Crispy from outside, great tasting meat, and the chimichurri sauce is fresh and tangy.

Delicious food, yet Unsettled Stomach
Interesting Contemporary Italian concept:  wood-fired pizza oven, Italian-cured meats, Southern dishes, colossal wine glasses, sparse décor, chef's table/bar, hardwood floors, mediocre lighting, with high ceilings in a charming rehabbed brick sculptor studio.

Dear Chef/Owner, 
Your failure to return my phone calls and email were a catalyst for my joining the exciting community of Yelp.  One Saturday evening in January 2010 a group of friends and I dined in your charming city eatery.  We dined in the upstairs dining room and were greeted by a male server whose name rhymes with 'Granule.'  He seemed a bit unprepared to discuss specifics about the short menu, but we were excited to take a few risks based on some previous online reviews.

I have to say the Crispy Octopus . . . . Yum-O!
Housemade Salami  . . . . .  tasty!
Olives with Tarrali . . . . . .   Mediocre at best.
Crispy Potatoes with Gorgonzola  . . . .   So Stellar we ordered two servings!

I indulged in the Springer Mountain Half Chicken, which was quite delicious, but I did not take a liking to the Creamed Collards, or the less than eventful cheese grits.

Other members of my dinner table ordered the House Made Belly Ham pizza, which they enjoyed, but if you don't like a lot of spices the chilies have quite a kick to them. The catfish was bland, the pasta bolognese was delectable, and the pumpkin pasta tasteless.

We highly recommend the Olive & Sinclair Chocolate Caramel Cake, it was a nice finish to our meal.

Here are the facts, and where my unsettled stomach comes in.
One week after dining at City House I reconcile my bank account and notice a large $400 debit to my account.  Whah?  I have my receipt right here and my agreement states that $50.12 was what I agreed to pay.  My 7 friends, had a similar receipt, and we all were charged equally.  I call the restaurant on three different days, and left voicemail messages since no one answered the phone.  My friend also sends the owner an email, no response.  I file a claim with my bank, and it quickly gets rushed to the 'Fraud' department.  ELEVEN days after my meal at CityHouse my $350 is finally deposited back into my account.  My friends' accounts were not charged.  Now hear this Tandy, my family owns a small business, and if we made an error on a customer's account we would take full responsibility right away, I would credit the account ASAP, and make a phone call to sincerely apologize for the mishap.  I would probably go as far as to comp the entire party's meals.  I certainly wouldn't charge her friends accounts 13 days later.
 
If I went back I would probably sit at Chef Tandy's bar anticipating a sincere apology, I would order the Bandit mixed cocktail, eat some starters, finish with a decadent dessert, and then pay my bill in CASH.  Sadly, however I have yet to get a phone call or apology, I will not return, and I will gladly use my debit card at your competitor's establishment. Questionable business transactions, coupled with poor service leave a very sour taste in my mouth, eek.

After my hike today, I helped the closest Chinese restaurant with good reviews and a dine-in option; that's how I stumbled upon this fancy Chinese restaurant. 

Not really knowing it was fancy, we walked in with hiking shoes and pants coated with dirt. I didn't feel too embarrassed because of the low lighting atmosphere. Phew! 

My bf and I ordered two beef noodle soups and veggie spring roll appetizers. The spring rolls are basically egg rolls, which come with two kinds dip. 

The waitress was nice enough to allow me to sub for thick rice noodles instead of thin rice noodles. Since I am Chinese and from the Bay Area, I've had my fair share of good a Chinese food, the best ones usually from hole-in- the- wall type places. Since this was a fancier Chinese place, I guess I expected more. 

It was kind of strange because none of the waitresses spoke Chinese and this was a Chinese restaurant! I ordered in Chinglish, which is what I normally do in the Bay Area, but the girl Asian girl didn't understand me. Man, I felt like I was at Panda Express-- a Chinese restaurant staffed by people who don't speak Chinese. 

Service: 5/5- waitresses friendly, professional, and attentive
Ambiance: 5/5- clean, upscale, romantic atmosphere 
Food: 4/5- good but not great. I've had better

They have about 2-3 boba places in Reno, all somewhat mediocre. A few hours before departing Reno last week, I made my bf drive to this location, which is the only location I haven't visited yet. 

Saw canisters of powder near the front window, meaning the drinks are made from powder. I saw a container with purple powder--taro powder. I'm not a big fan of powdered milk teas, but with a limited of boba places in Reno, I had no choice. T4 was nowhere to be found, so this taro drink would have to suffice. 

I ordered a Taro Milk Tea with tapioca (+0.50) and soy milk substitute (+0.50). Total came out to be $5.00+. 

They also provide milk subs for those who are lactose intolerant.
Almond, Soy, and Coconut: +0.50 cents. All barista blend. 

Plenty of outdoor seating. 

No bathrooms. They should make an exception for customers because I really had to go!

Service: 5/5
Black balls: 1/5. Not sweet enough and has a strange texture compared to Bay Area balls. 
Drinks: 4/5. Although made from powder, it was quite delicious!

My bf and I were pleasantly surprised with Taiwanese Cuisine during our trip to Reno. We stopped by for their lunch specials instead of shelling out $40+ for three plates of food during regular hours. 

Lunch deals:
2 entrees + 1 side:~ $ 8.00
1 entree + 1 side: ~$7.00

Entrees: meat dishes or veggies.
Sides: rice or noodles 

My bf ordered cashew chicken + beef broccoli + side of white rice. The beef broccoli came out perfect. Too much soy sauce in the the cashew chicken made it too salty. 

I ordered sweet and sour chicken + chow mein. The chicken came out crispy even though it was drenched in sauce. Totally hit the spot. Chow mein was hidden underneath the sweet and sour chicken, so the noodles tasted more like sweet and sour chow mein. 1 entree + 1 side is served in a bowl.  Next time I will ask them to put this on a plate instead of a bowl. 

Taro milk tea ($4.00) - tasty but way too sweet. 
Boba- bland. Will skip the add-on next visit. 

Overheard a group of business men raving about the beef noodle soup. Will try this next visit. 

Not crowded at all during lunchtime in the middle of the week. 

Food: 5/5
Ambiance- 5/5. Somewhat dark and has a soft, romantic feel to it. 
Service: 5/5. Attentive and friendly. 

Highly recommended.

What a hidden little gem in South Reno! My hairstylist turned friend suggested we check We Olive & Wine Bar after I got my hair done a couple weeks ago. I'd seen the location several times since it's in a popular shopping center, but never thought to check it out and always assumed they just sold olive oil. Such a huge mistake! 

My friend Kim and I were welcomed by a sweet lady who gave us the opportunity to sit wherever we'd like. There's both a bar and small table seating at the back of the shop. There was only one other person there so we kind of had the place to ourselves--which is both nice and sort of quiet. We decided to each try the sparkling white wine with balsamic. At first I wasn't sure about it, but I figured it wouldn't be a popular item if it wasn't delicious so had to give it a go. It was so yum! I'm definitely looking forward to going back for this specific drink. 

They have a decent selection of finger foods and larger snacks available. We opted for a artisanal cheese platter and a hummus platter. Both were really good and had yummy options. The cheese plater came with 3 types of cheese, 1 serving of walnuts, and 1 serving of pickled bell peppers, along with a couple jams/sauces. I would be lying if I said I wasn't disappointed by the price point and volume of cheese on the cheese platter. At $18 I would have expected a lot more cheese. Three little portions with some accoutrements was rather disappointing; there was barely enough for even one person let alone to serve as a share plate. To me this was worth maybe $10. The hummus platter was much more robust, but also on the pricey end at $13. In the future I'll probably just plan to grab 1 glass of sparkling wine and skip the food but enjoy the free bread and crackers they serve with olive oil. 

We did not try any of the olive oils, though now I have another reason to go back. My friend bought some other products--they sell cute little home goods, some spices, soaps, and such.

All in all it was a great little place. The location isn't ideal, but great if you're out and about doing some shopping. I'd avoid the snacks based on price point to quantity (note: quality was great!).

It took us way too long to try this place, but I'm so glad we finally did because it's such a little gem. The atmosphere is like a lodge and European pub combined. Very cozy. It reminds me a lot of the restaurants back east, particularly ones in Buffalo, NY, especially when they have a fire going in the main dining room. 

Since it was our first time in, and we weren't familiar with the beers, we ordered a sampler to taste a variety of beers before deciding on what we wanted to drink. I was a huge fan of their Mexican style lager, and my husband liked the red-headed ale so much that he actually bought a 4-pack to take home. 

For food we ordered the pretzel to share (definitely recommend), the mussels (technically an appetizer, but large enough for a meal, and highly recommend), and the pork and kraut (highly highly recommend). We have since been back and ordered all of the above, plus a chicken sandwich... which I would not recommend. The chicken had "dirty oil" flavor, was way over cooked, and actually burned from being over fried, plus the bread was really dry. That said, as disappointing as the sandwich was, we were not displeased with our experience and are more than eager to return. 

I also want to add that the Saint James feels like our replacement for The Depot. We've had a couple great experiences at the Depot and some really really bad experiences too; I want to love them, but the bad experiences have been really bad and I've been so disappointed with how The Depot handled multiple situations. That's cool though, because the Saint James is less pretentious, isn't trying as hard, and has yummy food and will now be one of our go-tos!

My husband and I decided to give this place a try after driving past it over the years. It's one of those places that you see regularly but you never think to go to so when we were both craving Mediterranean food we decided to give it a go. The atmosphere is dated but it kind of adds to the experience. It feels like they're aiming for a fine dining experience but instead it's kind of cheesy and dated. I think they could really increase business by updating things.

The food is delicious. We ordered a Mediterranean sampler so we could get a feel for their offerings and flavors. The house hummus is most likely the best hummus I've ever had. The Tzatiki is made with so much flavor. The dolmades are fresh, and the flavor is so unique you can tell they aren't a pre-packaged item. The Baba Ganoush was very Smokey and I could taste the fresh lemon and pine nuts. I prefer my Baba Ganoush to be a little creamier so the texture was a little different and wasn't what I'm used to but was still delicious. 

For dinner we shared the gyro platter and the dunar plate. Both come with choice of salad or saffron rice, and grilled veggies. We both ordered the salad. The meat was cubed which seemed weird, but it tasted delicious. For dessert I had an Awesome Dude. The saffron flavored ice cream was insane and the baklava complimented it perfectly. My husband ordered the Awesome Dudette which comes with a chocolate cake instead of baklava, and he equally raved about how good it was. 

Overall we had a great dining experience and I would recommend. That said, I think the atmosphere could be updated and the prices lowered. I'd love to be able to eat here regularly, but the more expensive price point coupled with the growing food options in Reno, makes that challenging.

This is my go-to place in Reno for chicken shawarma because it's so yummy. The rice is cooked perfectly and has so much flavor. I love love love the potatoes and wish the meal options included a few more of them. The mini salad is refreshing with just the right amount of light and flavorful dressing. 

The meal option only comes with two small slices of pita, so if you really like to eat pita with each bite then plan to order an extra full piece of pita bread for $1. I also ask for extra garlic sauce so I can really dunk each piece of chicken in there... it's so so tasty! 

This place also deserves a special call out for the very best baklava I have ever had. It's absolutely incredible. I would give it 10 stars if I could. It's so soft and simply melts in your mouth. The texture is perfection. The flavors are equally distributed. I always order several extra pieces to enjoy over a few days after my meal!

I love this Peg's location! Everyone here is sweet as pie and they each greet you with a warm smile regardless of how busy they are. This location's food is consistent with the other area Peg's. My favorite item is most definitely the Huevos Rancheros. In the fall I enjoy the pumpkin pancakes. I'm not a huge fan of the Benedict's (and yes, I've had them all). The coffee is always hot and fresh. The service is always good. And the price point is great.

My husband was craving pizza and neither one of us we're up for the options really close to our house so we decided to give Eclipse another go. It's really good pizza. Fresh ingredients. Lots of topping options. Fun concoctions. The gluten free and cauliflower crust options are still too pricey imo.

We ordered two small pizzas: the JAM and the total eclipse. Both were delicious and full of flavor. For us, the small is just enough to share or can be split into two meals. It's great because you're not spending a ton of money and eating pizza for days and days. We also ordered a dozen buffalo wings. They were yummy but I do wish they offered blue cheese instead of ranch.

Pizzas and wings were ready in 30 minutes. The staff was incredibly friendly when I arrived and even signed me up for the loyalty program, which gets you $5 off your purchase after 5 visits.

I think this is officially my favorite taco shop in Reno. Every type of meat we've had here is always good. Carne asada, lengua, chicken, carnitas, and el pastor... it's all consistently delicious. My husband and I typically order a mixture of different tacos and then share them between the two of us; this is a great way to try a little bit of everything and not fill up on one thing. We've had other things here too, but the tacos are just so dang delicious that I go back to ordering them time and time again. 

This restaurant is always packed and it's not uncommon for the line to be almost out the door around lunch hour or when downtown Reno has street activities going on. If you're not planning to sit down and eat in the restaurant they typically have a takeout line to the side that you can order from. Regardless, it's worth the wait if you have the time. I only wish they had additional locations.

This isn't going to be the best burger you ever had but for NW Reno, and the limited quick food options available, this is a pretty good burger. My husband typically gets the BBQ Bison Burger and is always happy. I typically get the French Dip and really enjoy it--recognizing of course that it's not really a burger. I've also ordered a few of their specials and haven't been disappointed.

The best thing about this place is the variety of proteins (beef, chicken, elk, bison, fish), variety of buns (white, wheat, rye, brioche, gluten free, and lettuce wraps), and the ability to customize your burger to your liking with toppings like fried eggs, avocado, grilled onions, onion rings, etc. I'm all about a custom burger. I do wish they offered more suggestions on burgers to show some creativity with what can be done. Sometimes I need a little inspiration before I can figure out my burger concoction. 

They can take a bit long to cook and the line can be lengthy (more so in wait time than anything else) but it's because everything is cooked fresh to order and I'm sure they give priority to the drive thru.

If you're on your way into Reno, out of Reno, or live in Northwest, then I totally recommend it for a cute little local place with good burgers.

This review is based on an experience that occurred in January 2020, before the covid era. Overall, I am disappointed to give this place two stars because I wanted so badly to love it. I have previously had the opportunity to enjoy Pine State Biscuits at various yelp Reno events over the last year or so and have enjoyed their food in those settings. However, I found my entire experience at the actual restaurant to be disappointing, and was embarrassed to have taken out of town guests here for breakfast.

Two of us ordered the Reggie. Overall the gravy was bland and lacked flavor, and the chicken on my biscuit was so incredibly dry. I tried washing it all down with a mediocre bloody mary that was just lacking... not sure how to describe what it was lacking, but it was just meh. The biscuit itself was on point, which is encouraging given it's an establishment that bases its menu around biscuits. Another person in our group ordered the pancakes, which were undeniably delicious. I wish I had ordered these instead, but given the basis of the menu is biscuit sandwiches, I found it odd that their pancakes were their most redeeming item. 

The prices were high, but the portions were large so that seemed fair... other than the fact that I had zero interest in finishing my food or taking anything home.

I am truly confused as to what went wrong and feel bummed to have to leave a negative review. I keep asking myself if it was the particular items I ordered, or maybe the particular day we visited? It's hard to say, but I don't anticipate returning.

Cute little bakery hidden in the Mayberry Landing shopping center. They have a limited menu of sandwiches and salads, plus the most delicious European pastries and bread baked fresh daily. Be sure to try the ham and cheese croissant (get there early before they sell out!) and the chocolate croissant. Both are heavenly! They also serve coffee and espresso drinks, and take custom orders for specialty items and special occasion cakes. The inside is small with a few tables.
