Nothing good to day except it was our fault for going there. Don't make the same mistake.

DO NOT get the Travelzoo deal unless you're absolutely desperate for a cheap one-night getaway. After spending an hour in this place, my husband and I were tempted to eat the $99 and drive an hour home to sleep in our own (clean) bed -- but in the end, sheer laziness prevailed.

Something about this hotel just seemed dirty. The bed looked and felt really old and the furniture looked like it was from the 80s. The whole room had a lovely BO smell that seemed to be ingrained in the carpeting and furniture, and the dimly-lit bathroom could've easily doubled as a movie set for a grisly murder scene. And there's no way we would've considered using the jacuzzi tub. 

As for the casino, yikes. Laughably tiny and insanely crowded -- there were lines to get on the video poker machines. If you get the Travelzoo deal, the promotional credits have to be used in full -- you can't cash any of them out. Don't make the mistake of transferring all of your credits to one machine, or you're stuck on that machine until you've used ALL of your credits.

The one bright spot of our stay was our dinner at the Tavern and our drinks later at Prime's bar. But other than that, not a fun time. I can't imagine paying the $10 cover to get into this casino.

I came here on a first date with someone. My date suggested we share the, " seafood voyage for two."  Well the name was the most romantic part of this dish. Imagine trying to be the best version of yourself while you are hunched over a bunch of crab legs like a Neanderthal with crab juice and butter running down your forearms. Not very sexy.  Although my date must not have minded too much because a year and a half later he proposed to me at this restaurant right after sharing this dish. 
Over a decade later, and we are still eating this dish here. Although the price has gone up slightly I have to say that you get a lot of seafood and we think it is a great value. The seafood tastes fresh.  
There are not many children's options but the staff will bring you a menu from the restaurant downstairs to order from.  
Ok so maybe I'm a bit sentimentally attached to this place, but I have to say I would highly recommend!

Dear Starbucks,
After many years and many fond coffee memories I'm afraid I have to break up with you, for I have fallen for another by the name of Lighthouse coffee. 
Lighthouse coffee is a local coffee shop that actually roasts their own beans so they are much fresher. Plus the customer service is excellent. For example, one evening my husband and I showed up there after they had closed. They were having a private party and despite being closed they let us in anyway and served us with a smile on their faces. Plus they gave my children fresh baked cookies! The owner Todd was extremely generous and did not mind that we were crashing his party. I have ordered their Caramillo both hot and cold and found it to be delicious. 
In conclusion Starbucks, it's not you, it's me.  I am looking for a local, unique, and friendly place to take my coffee business and I believe that Lighthouse coffee is "the one."

I was throughly impressed with this place and I am so glad we wondered in here. I like sushi at it's simplest and I don't really care for extravagant rolls and this place really delivered. This place really captured what sushi truly is...fish and rice! It reminded me of the rolls at the places I used to frequent in Hawaii.

I've been looking for a place that does hosomaki (small 6 pc. Roll with only one type of raw fish) and gunkan style nigiri (rice ball wrapped in nori making a boat with fish/filling placed on top of the rice) and we finally have a place in Reno/Sparks area. It is so conveniently located at the legends mall. I also love that they serve the nigiri one piece at a time. It gives you a chance to eat more of a variety of nigiri.

I ordered a couple of rolls and some apps and nigiri. Everything tasted great and the service was superb. Our orders came quickly and the servers were so friendly and attentive.

I'm definitely bringing some friends here and I will be back!

I would recommend Vango if:

1. You love waiting in lines! You'll wait in lines to enter the bar, go up to the roof deck, for drinks, in the bathroom, complain to the owner, etc. 
2. You enjoy crappy godawful lounge music and equally crappy Top-40 mashups! No one downstairs dances because lounge music is being blasted - but there's a dance floor. And no one upstairs dances because while Top-40 hits are recognizable, there is no real dancefloor. Refer to #1, as there will be lines both downstairs and upstairs anyway. 
3. You like shitty mixed drinks and paying way too much for them!
4. You hate yourself, want everyone to know it, and want to be treated as such! The owner is a pathetic and pretentious douchebag who clearly gets off on treating ALL of his PAYING customers like dirt. Is it your birthday? So what. Are you the designated driver? Fuck off. Don't want bottle service? Goodbye! 

The owner is a self-righteous prick in need of a serious reality check. 

Yelpers, do yourselves a favor and do not patronize this awful, awful place. Ever.

I was invited to sample some of Tango's specialty cocktails the week before the soft opening. I enjoyed my time at Tango so much I decided to return for the soft opening, and am happy to say I was not disappointed. 

I sat in the upstairs karaoke area both days. There are huge TV screens everywhere - last night two were showing ESPN and the rest were dedicated to karaoke. The karaoke screen is also projected on one floor-to-ceiling window, to lure in curious passersby no doubt!

Songs were free all night so after some liquid courage from Victor, the awesome bartender, it was time to sing. I belted out my favorite Ace of Base ditty and got some help from the night's emcee, Nate. (He's a great singer by the way; if you're shy about singing alone I'm sure he'd be happy to sing along!)

My favorite drink from the sampling was the Hello Kitty, but if tangy "girl" drinks aren't your thing, there's also a tasty Jameson Mojito or the equally dangerous Pineapple Express (you thought your 151 days were behind you - HA). 

Food-wise, I can only speak to the gyoza; my wallet cringed when I saw that it was $6 for six pieces, but I felt a little better after I received the order. The gyoza at Tango are not the typical light dumpling I'm used to (I don't think gyoza wrappers were used, I has a sad) but they were filling. 

My recommendation would be to try one of Tango's many noodle offerings, have a couple of drinks, and end the night singing Rihanna's "Birthday Cake" and imbibing the deliciously sweet It's Not Even My Birthday martini.

Here's what you do.  Save up some money (somewhere between $90 and $150 for two people).  And decide that you're going to treat yourself.  Take that money to Paul Manno's and go freaking nuts.  They'll roll you out when you're done, and you won't even care that your nice clothes are rolling on the parking lot.  It's that good.

Top notch service, top notch food, bottom notch location.  Go here and give your money to Paul to help him relocate to a proper area and building, and have one of the better meals of your life while you're at it.  Nuff said.
Got the bacon sand which and it was amazing also the service was up to standard. I tried the bulgogi cheesesteak sandwich and it was one of the best I've ever had.

The food is terrible.  Such a great looking place, but without good food and great hosts/wait staff...is a no go.  I have tried 3 different times over the past years hoping that things get better...but nope.

I work near RTM and go here way too much. Here's my quick guide on the highlights of where to eat: 

Breakfast
Beiler's donuts - Ranked by Fodor's as America's 20 best desserts spots. They do donuts well. Apple fritter and Dutch crumb are my favs. 
Beiler's bakery - You'll need to share the blueberry loaf of bread. Honorable mention for the sticky bun, but it's not served warm.
Metropolitan bakery - They do typical baked goods well. I love the almond croissant and various muffins. 
Dutch Eating Place - Breakfast done well. Love the pancakes.

Lunch
Little Thai Market - Their grilled salmon dish (comes with rice and broccoli) is good and affordable ($7 and some change). You can get extra curry sauce and/or shrimp if you pay a little extra. This dish is popular with the locals and you can see a line at lunch time. If there's a long line, I would skip unless you really want to eat seafood.

Sandwiches
Hatville Deli - Corned beef special
Dinic's - Featured on Man vs. Food. Get the roast pork, get it with provolone.
Herschel's Deli - Pastrami sandwich preferably reuben. The corned beef is also good. 
The Original Turkey - thick slices of turkey, cooked perfectly.

Snack -
Miller's Twist - The pretzels are way better than Auntie Annie's. 
Iovine Brothers Produce - eat healthy and get some fruits or nuts for the road.

Dessert
4th Street Cookie Company - My favorite is the chocolate chip with walnut
Basset's Ice Cream
Termini Brothers - Get the cannoli 
Beck's Cajun Cafe - The beignets are amazing, but only served on certain days.
Beiler's Bakery - The shoofly pie and whoopie pie are good and very unique to this culture.
Dutch Eating Place - Hot apple dumpling, the PA Dutch version of an apple pie.
Flying monkey - Get your dessert fix here if you're vegan.

Beverages
Old City Coffee - This hits the spot after all the food you've eaten. Goes great with dessert.

What is there not to love about a Cracker Barrel!? I mean who doesn't love down-home, good ol' country style eats...just like grandmother used to make it.  

The food is always finger-lickin' good and fresh at the Cracker Barrel. The menu is vast and there is a large selection (5 pages worth) of items and plates to choose from. This location is just like all the others I've been to and what I enjoy most is the consistency of the service and the quality of the eats.  There is also a country store section in the waiting area where you can shop around for typical country store novelty items, homemade jellies, sauces, spices, cooking utensils, toys, clothing, etc.

I stumbled on this location during our return trip from New York City during the Easter weekend.  We were all starving while driving back and as soon I saw the exit sign for Cracker Barrel, I couldn't help but to bust a right across three lanes of traffic to make sure we made the exit.  The food is just that good and we were starving!  On this particular Easter Sunday, I had one of the best plates of rib-eye steak, scrambled eggs with cheese, hash-browns, fried shrimp, hush puppies, any large garden salad!  Yes!  You heard me right! Don't judge!...I was a honorary member of "Team Greedy" that day!  All of that food plus the free starter biscuits was just for me. I think I occupied about one-third of our entire table with all my food. Everything with fresh, hot and cooked to perfection. Great serving portions and everything, even down to the scrambled eggs was super seasoned.  There's not much more to say about the meal except for it was damn good.  You can't go wrong with Cracker Barrel in my opinion. Not to mention, the prices of the food items, at this location, were more than fair.  This was a huge relief in comparison to breakfast food fare in NYC!...Where the parking alone can run to $60 a day!  There were a total of eight family members and friends at our table and our entire meal, including my smorgasbord, came to only roughly $100 or so. So do the math. Where Else can you go and feed an small army of hungry folk for just a little over $100 bucks. 

Every type of meal that I've had from traditional biscuits and sausage gravy, grits, omelets ....... to what you would call the more elaborate dishes for this type of place ....such as blackened salmon, shrimp linguini and lobster it is ...... ALL A-OK!  So if you ever see one of these places on a highway food-exit marker, you better make that right turn off the road immediately and try for yourself.

Cracker Barbell always gets a "Thumb up!"  in my book!  Haven't had a bad meal yet!!

Now, this is where the party and true Philly Cheesesteak is at!! 

Don't waste your time going all over the city, unless you want to just waste your gas and money.  Max's Steaks serves up a proper Philly Cheesesteak and is one of the best I've had during the many times visiting Philly.  And, they have the lines of Philly locals and tourists stretching out the door to prove it.  

As a general guide, whenever you are looking for good food native to a city or area....always follow the locals!!  You will never be misguided...trust. The locals pack this place more than the tourist or out-of-towners visiting.

What makes this place special is the nostalgic throwback, neighborhood feel and vibe to it; especially the bar.  Yes!...There is a bar  (Bonus..Yelp Star!) in the establishment that is just as alive with Neighborhood folks hanging out and people enjoying their food and drinks. It's nothing fancy, by any means, but there is a lot of love in the place, great music and the food is "Oh!, So damn good!"  This, I will kid you not. 

My friend and I stopped in here, after learning about Max's Steaks from our Uber driver. At first we had reservations, but the minute you walk in and see the juicy mounds of round-eye steak being grilled and seasoned to perfection and the stock piles of sub sandwich bread being toasted..you know its about to go down!

We ordered cheesesteaks only, as everyone in line said..."that's all you would need!"  And, they were right. We placed our orders and in a few short minutes...the goods were given to us. Let me be the first to tell you, I was shocked at the size of these things!!

Picture this, we ordered two "half" cheesesteaks, but when the cashier was bringing the sandwiches to us....I swear she was carrying two newborn babies...wrapped and swaddled in blanket!  These things were huge!! lol

We were planning to take them back the the Airbnb to enjoy them, but couldn't resist!  We ate them bad boys on prem!  We found an open booth in the bar area of the establishment... and began to feast.  And, the verdict?!....It was everything a man could ask for!  The sandwiches were full of juicy, seasoned meat, loaded with toppings....oooozing with cheese..,.and oh so good!   My mouth is watering, just think about it....as I write this review. 

My friend and I were completely satisfied. She and I were high-fiving and moaning in the booth where we were sitting the entire time...with each bite.  I am sure everyone was wonder what was going down in booth #4....if you catch my drift. lol

In all, this place is more than an experience.  It's an institution.  Great food, service, down-home appeal and the people working their make it unique...to quintessential Philly. The neighborhood is a little sketch, but by all means safe. If your looking for the real Philly Cheesesteak experience...no frills...just good food and even strong libation from the bar attached...look no further!!  You have found the right place!

I absolutely adore this place.  Nice variety of muffins, pastries, croissants, sandwiches and more edibles.  Way to many decisions for this girl.  The coffee is a great flavor,  strong but not bitter, I like that. I dont know why people think strong=bitter. this place gets it right.  The staff is great and so friendly and helpful.  I love the designs they make on the top of my latte in the foam.  if you havent tried this place you must. Indoor and outdoor seating.  Bring a friend or 2.

This brewery is awesome! My beer preference is the darker type, and after leaving a brewery that didn't have any porters, stouts, or brown ales, I walked right into heaven at this brewery! Cycle brewery can easily be missed if you're just walking by it, but once you get in, the staff will take care of you! There were three lists to order from, their regular drafts, their bomber bottle list, and a menu dedicated to barrel aged stouts, YES A LIST FOR BARREL AGED STOUTS ONLY! All of them were at least 10%, so I definitely got a glass off of that list! The only flaw with this brewery is that they don't have flights, but you can get a half pour, or a sample of any on the list except the barrel aged stout. Oh and you can have Uber Eats delivered to you while you're here! 
The two beers that I ordered were; The Please Hazelnut Cream and Sugar Porter, and the Cookie Butter barrel aged stout. The Cookie Butter was very rich but delicious, but I favored the porter better. I'd definitely return when I come back to downtown St. Pete!

This place just sucks. Let's see, one time the waitress spilled soda on one of the people in our group. Just a sorry. Every time service took forever. Pricing is just too high for the quality of food you get. Only been back a couple times just to have a beer with the guys. So, 1 star for getting a beer order right,and 1 star because they might have a hot rod in work.

I was so excited for this place to open - I live close by.  But I was thoroughly disappointed.  Highlights of why I was disappointed:

- When our appetizers came out, we still had yet to get water, let alone the drink order we put in as soon as we sat down.  We had to ask for water and bread.  And then the bread was put down but with no butter or oil.  

- This may sound stupid, but if you order calamari at an italian restaurant it's a good litmus test as to how authentic they are and how fresh their food is.  We were thoroughly disappointed with the fact that it was clearly flash fried frozen calamari.  No tentacles - just rubbery rounds.  

- We ordered a pizza after our appetizers and it came out a max 2 mins later.  Fast service would normally be something I'd praise, but in this case it was very apparent that their so-called artisan pizza's are simply a plain pizza that they throw the toppings on and heat really quickly.  While the prosciutto, arugula, and parmesan pizza sounded great, it was a pretty big disappointment in reality.

- Caesar salad was pretty flavorless and seemed to just be store bought dressing over some romaine.  The croutons were clearly the same ones you buy in the grocery store.

I talked to 2 other people who had recently eaten there and had the same experience.  The only reason I'm not giving it 1 star is because it's new and I'm really really crossing my fingers hoping it gets better.   For $120 it was no better than your average chain italian restaurant.    

The wait staff, hostess, manager, etc - were all very nice.  So this bad review is in no way reflective of them.  Just felt pretty sub par all the way around in terms of the food.

It pains me to write this review, because my veggie heart always gets so excited when something like this opens.  I am a fan sister restaurants Charlie was a Sinner and Hip City Vedge (chicken sandwich to die for.)  So, when I heard there was an entirely latin themed vegan restaurant coming to Rittenhouse, I couldn't wait. 

We got to Bar Bombon at around 7:30.  We were able to swing getting 4 seats at the bar.  I'm surprised that so close to opening the service was so unfriendly.  There were three girls behind the bar at all times, and I can honestly say not one of them smiled then entire 2 hours we were there.  They also were not very friendly or engaging at all.  I asked a couple of questions about how their opening was going and they were less than thrilled.  There's no passion from the staff at this spot, but no biggie.  As long as the food and drinks are good thats something that I can easily get over!

Now to the drinks...They are notably expensive.  I ordered a Mezcal drink (that honestly filled half a martini glass) for $15.  To give you an idea their non alcoholic (plain juices run $9-11.)  All 4 of us ordered a couple cocktails and no one was impressed.  I was surprised because Charlies makes EXCELLENT cocktails.  One of us got a spanish drink made with rum ($12) that tasted super artificial and I watched the bar tender literally fill an entire spoon 3 times with sugar before making it (enjoy that hangover!)

Next to food.  Chorizo Tacos were just blah.  I've had MUCH better chorizo tacos at places that DON'T specialize in vegan food (Shout out to StrangeLoves!)  They were under seasoned, lacked any presentation, and came with this side plate that honestly look like a child had thrown it together.  On it was onions, tomatoes, and lettuce.  Presentation is at a 0 here.  

One of the people in our group ordered the fish tacos.  She didn't like them.  I thought a fish taco might be a risk at at vegan spot, but when she offered me one yikes!  Stick with the meat options if you do go here.  I also ordered something (cannot remember the name) that comes out literally on some sort of corn bred and is filled with tofu.  There was very little tofu, and it was actually BAD.  

At the end of this day, this place will make it because its in a great area, but I will not return and would never suggest this to anyone in the city.  V Street is the closest thing I can think of to this place and the food BLOWS this spot away.  Not to mention, the service (and servers) are top notch.  Big disappointment.  

Oh, and someone once told me, ever trust a spanish/mexican/latin place that doesn't make it own hot sauce.  

Needless to say....they handed me a bottle of Cholula.

I'm from Chicago, which is basically infested with Mexican food.  When I moved here I was a nonbeliever in the "Mexican Philadelphia Restaurant."  That is, until I found this beautiful place.  I can't tell you one thing wrong with this place, except maybe that they have too many delicious sauces.

Oh do you think they are a little on the expensive side?  

Well let me tell you, my friend, you get what you pay for, and if you aren't going to pay for a little more tasty, you've got yourself a terrible problem.

Here's the thing with PYT:  in internet talk one would say they are just n00bs.  We came there, and sat down right away outside in the lovely Piazza, or pizza as I like to call it, and were served nice and fast, but I think the kitchen messed up almost everything in our burger order.  Like I said, they are new so I'll cut them some slack, I did have probably the most amazing onion rings I've ever had.

What makes me NOT want to come back is not the kitchen messing up our order (and the food is GREAT, so it's definitely not that). It's the obnoxious crowd that surrounds this place.  Never have I been so annoyed with the people around me (and you are talking to Queen Barbary).

2 stars for the view which I didn't get a chance to see during my dinner.

I made reservations and was seated in front of a window which was covered by a large pillar. Wonderful, right? No.

As far as the food - not even mediocre. I got a salmon and it was $32 and very small and bland. Not worth it. Overall bad experience. Nothing to rave about. I left the restaurant down $200 and rather disappointed. 

I will not be back.

Amazing experience! This is a wonderful addition to not only East Nashville but the city in general. 

The menu has just the right selection so everyone is satisfied. Ramen, skewers, appetizers, and salads. There are even a few sushi rolls if you're not feeling like noodles. My friend and I sat at the bar while waiting for the rest of our group to arrive and had a couple of cocktails: ginger/pineapple tonic and Dutch on the Run. The tonic was as good as you'd expect, but Dutch was spectacular. The bartenders were very knowledgable and also gave us and other people at the bar samples! I'm okay with that.

Most of us ordered the ramen bowls, which will definitely fill up anyone. My friend ordered the crispy Brussels sprouts, and let me just say: our drinks were great, so was dinner, even the dessert we sampled, but the BRUSSELS SPROUTS, GET OUT OF TOWN. They were that good.

I will definitely be coming back here. The space is so cozy and the Japanese tavern style is unique for Nashville. It's been a while where I've been so wowed over a new restaurant.

Disclaimer: they have a policy that does not allow you to take leftover ramen home.

It's really sad because 2 days ago this place would have gotten 4 stars from me. While the service is often disappointing the food is usually delicious and, as a local, I was quickly becoming a regular. I would have come to this restaurant without any deals but they are always on groupon or something similar so, we of course use those when we can. My mom, knowing I was a fan, purchased one for my fiancé and I as well as one for herself.

Last night she decided to come in for dinner and was excited to try it here. As we both had the groupon and it was expiring soon she called ahead, TWICE, to ask if we could both use it. The girl who answered claimed she spoke to the owner and as long as we got separate checks it was fine. She drove in from NJ. Upon arrival our waiter told us he couldn't take the groupons, despite my mom's calls. We were disappointed and after discussing with him, he agreed that as long as we did separate checks it would be fine. We even made an effort to separate our tables to make the waiter more comfortable. We had a good meal, the food took a long time to come out and didn't come out at once but otherwise everything was good. My step dad was ready to tip our waiter very generously for being so accommodating.

The waiter returned to drop our two SEPARATE checks and informed us that he was sorry but could in fact only take one groupon. Really? So we were lied to not once, but twice. For the sake of $13 this restaurant lost 4 patrons, 2 of which were quickly becoming regulars and recommending it to everyone. Now we will tell everyone to avoid it because of this terrible customer service. I hope it was worth it.

Tonight started out fantastic, we (my mom, my best friend and I) we to look at Christmas lights and were driving around when Nikki pointed out the new 24hr diner. I said great let's go! I made a u-turn and we were off.

We were greeted with a smiling face and seated quickly. The restaurant has indoor and outdoor seating, all of which is very clean and cute.

It took a few minutes for the waiter to come by, but it was ok since we were chatting:

Here's what we ordered
(My order) 2 eggs over medium, hash browns with rye toast and a single pancake - water to drink

(Nikki's order) 2 eggs over medium, home fries with wheat toast and a single pancake - froze to drink

(Mom's order) French fries and a glass of cab


Here's what we received (20+minutes later):
(My order) 2 eggs over HARD, grits and wheat toast (as the waitress who brought our food could not differentiate the toast)

(Nikki's order) 2 eggs over HARD, grits and rye toast

The separate pancakes we ordered came on the same plate so we asked the waitress to separate them for us, and she did.

At this time our waiter came over and I asked what the white stuff on my plate was and he informed me it was grits. I said bluntly I thought it came with home fries/hash browns. He said yes, but we are out of home fries so they said they would substitute with grits and I told them that wa ok! Politely we stated neither one of us like grits and we would like hashbrowns...

Now everything on my plate has grits on it including my eggs (gross!)

We had been done eating for at least 20 minutes and still no waiter, so i politely asked a nearby waitress if she could help up get our check as our waiter never came back. She apologized and 6 more minutes passed and our waiter arrived with our check and said "I was not hiding I was trying to get your hashbrowns". Strange as it seems that it what he said.. now 45+ mins and still no hash browns.

From this point on we never saw our sever again, and did not receive hash browns until we paid and were getting up to leave. We declined the hash browns and left disappointed.

All in all, very disappointing for a new restaurant in our hipster/foodie downtown. 

Tips for the establishment:
1. If you are out of something, ASK the customer what they would like to eat, after all they are the PAYING CUSTOMER.
2. Check on the customers, my mom and Nikki were never offered a 2nd drink
3. Diners are known to have fast service and turn around time, this is seriously lacking
4. If you are going to serve mainly breakfast, ensure the cooks know how to properly prepare eggs
5. Serving staff needs training on food items, not knowing what different breads are is unacceptable in a breakfast joint

Tips for my fellow foodies, do not go yet. They may need time to wire out some more kinks and training issues. Maybe in a few months they will be better #fingerscrossed

I usually find myself dining here for lunch a few times a month. 

Pastificio is one of, or the best sandwich shop in Philadelphia and I didn't think they could have impressed me any more than what they've done thus far. However there are two instances when I feel this place earned a few more notches on their belt. 

One thing that refreshed my love for Pastificio is their chicken cutlet sandwiches. On numerous occasions Pastificio would be ordered for team meetings, or other events at my office. Unfortunately, most of the time we don't always get to eat right away because a question would extend the meeting pass the lunch break. I am not the saying the chicken cutlet sandwiches were bad, as they still contained a enormous amount of flavor, but it was nothing like what I experienced the day I decided to switch up from my usual pepper turkey sandwich, and put my choppers into a fresh cutlet sandwich. Holy Heck! Why have I put this off for so long? The cutlets sandwiches have that nice delicate crust with a delicious moist interior. I am not a fan of mozzarella, so I prefer the OMG with sharp provolone, with the tomatoes, and pesto but, my favorite, is the cutlet with sharp provolone, and roasted peppers. You can tell the difference between eating a fresh sandwich right away or after a short ride back to the office; not over 45 minutes later. I am guilty of this too. (Read on) 

The second time I placed Pastificio on my deli pedestal, alone it was due to the catering order I placed with them just a little over a week ago at the end of July. After spending a tremendous amount of $$$ on my twins 1st birthday party, my wife and I wanted to significantly  cut the budget in half for their 2nd birthday. We were trying to cut cost, but not quality. I mentioned Pastificio and my wife put her trust in me. For sandwiches I ordered a five loft sandwich tray consisting of  turkey, Italian, and cold roast pork 3,2,1 respectively,  and  added a chicken & roasted peppers cutlet loft. Now I was the one guilty of picking up my order at 11:30 and not serving my guest till 2:30. The hypocrisy!! We had leftover sandwiches but the cutlets were gone before the party was even over. In addition to the sandwiches we ordered a full tray of chicken parm, and a half tray of baked pasta. I could certainly vouch for the sandwiches, but in regards to the other food items, I was confident we were not going to be disappointed; and I was right. Everyone loved the food. Our guest were pleased, so pleased that I had to place a little chicken parm to the side for myself or it would have all be gone. The chicken was so delicate but not soggy with an ample amount of cheese that didn't over power the chicken.

 I was happy that I was able to satisfy my guest while satisfying my wallet. Price was equivalent to the quantity and quality.

First time patron to this place. I read and people have raved about this place, what seems like forever. I came here for a work dinner. They have ample parking in the back of the restaurant. The restaurant itself is very visible on the busy street of south Virginia. The exterior is traditional and even though it is on a busy street, the energy of the place is calm and relaxed.  As soon as you walk through the door you see the bar with rock faced liquor shelving. It looks amazing, I regret not taking a photo of it.  The servers are fast, friendly and freaking awesome. She brought my tea and came back several times to check if I needed a new tea bag or hot water. 

The food was fantastic, we had a set menu but choices of dinner entrees and desserts. I picked the diver sea scallops. 

I can not tell you how wonderful these were. They were huge! Very well prepared with perfect seared marks. They were served with risotto, with that pairing it was like heaven. Buttery soft and firm scallops with the delicious risotto.  

I had to leave before dessert but passed them on my way out. Sigh....wished I had time to stay and enjoy. 

Overall my experience here was wonderful and I can't wait to be back. Maybe I'll even take my SO this time.

After snowboarding at Lake Tahoe, we stayed at the Grand Sierra Resort and decided to have dinner here our first night. Overall, the service was utterly atrocious, and the food just wasn't that great.

I have been to really "nice" restaurants with horrible service in the past, but this place really takes the cake BY FAR. This server (Asian guy with spikey hair and a cocky attitude) was the most horrible, rudest server I have ever encountered. He consistently placed all of the dishes onto my IPHONE. The first time he did it, I politely said, "Excuse me, that's my phone," but that did not stop him from placing the bucket of white rice onto my phone. By the end of the dinner, my phone had 5 different dishes placed on top of it. 

Moreover, since we had a table of about 16 people, each side ordered different things. When the food came, we simply shared the dishes family style. We ate all of the food on the dishes that came for us. Near the end of the dinner, the same server (Asian guy with spikey hair) came to us and said, "Why didn't you guys tell us we brought you extra food? You should've told us instead of eating it." WHAT KIND OF PERSON WORKING IN THE CUSTOMER SERVICE BUSINESS IN THEIR RIGHT MIND BLAMES THE CUSTOMER FOR THEIR MISTAKES? The reason we didn't question the food was that our table is large; we don't know who ordered what. We agreed to share it anyways. Why question it? But this particular server has the AUDACITY to blame US for his own incompetence? How pathetic. 

As for the food, it had its ups and downs, but mostly downs. The sushi wasn't that fresh. The rice was basically uncooked; in fact, I felt like I was trying to bite into pebbles. The fried rice and soup were bland. The curry was okay. The only thing was DECENT was the Korean BBQ style short ribs.

Overall, I do not recommend this restaurant to anyone. Their servers need to really get off their high horses and the food was just not good. If I could give them ZERO stars, I definitely would.

UPDATE: As of 1/13/13 at 1:48PM PST, I received an anonymous message on my personal blog (which is specified in my Yelp! info) with the following: "Lol you're a little b****. Thanks for the yelp review about me b****." Clearly, the server was unable to own up to his mistakes and felt the need to insult me after giving such horrible service. His way of adding insult to injury in an immature way, I suppose.

This was my first time in Manayunk.  So walking around here was a new experience for me.  It was around 10pm and we ended up stopping by at Bourbon Blue to have some drinks and some food.  Well, it was actually me that wanted some food since I wasn't going to have drinks alone, especially when their late night food menu sounded interesting.

I ordered their Andouille Poutine and got a taste of the Cheesesteak Eggrolls that were shared with the table.

Andouille Poutine -- http://bit.ly/2vldg7C
"loaded fries" topped with cheese curd, crumbled andouille sausage & our country gravy
OMGYUM!  The Andouille Poutine was delicious!  I'm always a sucker for some good poutine and Bourbon Blue's take on it was tasty with a Southern comfort twist.  I've had a similar poutine like this before from a food truck and it's actually one of my favorites with sausage and country gravy.  The gravy was thick and the curds was melted and gooey underneath (even though you can't notice them in the pic, there's a good amount of curds).  This definitely hit the spot and paired well with the drinks I ordered.

Cheesesteak Eggrolls -- http://bit.ly/2vlxTka
shaved sirloin, caramelized onions & american cheese rolled together & deep fried, served with spicy ketchup and garlic aioli
Sure why not have a fusion take on the Philly classic?  These were actually pretty good and were loaded with steak and cheese.  Although I think it would've been better when a cheese sauce for dipping rather than the aioli and ketchup.

The two drinks I had that night were pretty refreshing and went well with the poutine and egg rolls.  They weren't strong, but I didn't mind that too much.  

Bourbon Mule -- http://bit.ly/2vlyaDI
Four Roses bourbon, ginger beer, fresh apple cider, and lemon

Pomegranate Old Fashioned -- http://bit.ly/2vl8XJv
Makers Mark, cointreau, simple syrup, muddled pomegranate, orange, cherries, cinnamon

Overall, Bourbon Blue was a great spot to finish off the night.  I definitely wouldn't mind coming back here to try their dinner menu when I come back to visit Philly again.

The last place I stopped by at Reading Terminal Market during my last trip to Philly was Beck's Cajun Cafe.  What can I say?  They had their signature sandwich, The Train Wreck Po' Boy, on display and after walking by it several times, I couldn't resist ordering it.

The Train Wreck Po' Boy -- http://bit.ly/2vnDKbf
andouille, salami, steak, cheese, onions
The Train Wreck is a great Nawlin's take on the classic cheesesteak.  It had a bit of everything inside and had that spicy kick from the andouille.  In a way, it was almost like a jambalaya in a roll with a meaty surprise in every bite.  It definitely worth the try if you're craving a cheesesteak but with a little more kick.

I'm glad I got to stop by Beck's Cajun Cafe before leaving Reading Terminal Market and ending on a high note with the Train Wreck Po' Boy.  I hope I get another chance to come back again and try their other menu items such as their famous Jambalaya, Fried Mac & Cheese, Gumbo-topped Cajun Fries, and their Muffaletta.  They all sound so good!

If it wasn't for my cousins buying a box of Bieler's doughnuts, I probably would've totally passed them by at Reading Terminal Market.  

Oh my Lord, these doughnuts are crazy good!  Their texture is so unique.  It almost reminds me of like chewing into a soft crumpet but in doughnut form.  I can't remember what flavors we had, but I do remember that I enjoyed all the random ones that I picked out from the assortment in the box.  

The saddest part of my last trip to Philadelphia was going to Reading Terminal Market one last time before flying home only to find that Beiler's was closed for the day.  Nooooo!!!  Oh well, their doughnuts will definitely be something I will be looking forward to when I come back to visit Philadelphia again!

After a mediocre first visit last year, I decided to give this HHAGG another shot for breakfast.  I wasn't going for anything huge like their Farm Benedicts or Chicken and Waffles, but I was more interested trying one of their Famous Hashes.

I went with the Meatloaf Hash.  While it was a very hearty entree, it didn't really do it for me.  Everything was bland and dry from the scrambled eggs to the chopped meatloaf.  The melted cheese on top couldn't really save it either.
http://bit.ly/1aD2N4J

Despite the Meatloaf Hash, I still can't get enough of their Kiwi Watermelon Lemonade.  It's always a must order and definitely rescued my throat from the dryness of the Hash.
http://bit.ly/18a0DIB

HHAGG has come to point for me where you definitely go once or twice for shock value with a group of friends, but after going a few times, the novelty wears off after a while.  You definitely get a lot of value in terms of quantity, but the quality is lacking.  I would still go back for their drinks though.

There's no question that I love Reading Terminal Market.  So much that I actually went twice during my last visit to Philadelphia even though it wasn't planned.  In reality though, if you're visiting from out-of-town, you'll definitely need more than one day to try a good amount of the many food vendors it has to offer.

I covered a lot during those two days:  Beiler's Bakery, Dutch Eating Place, Tommy DiNic's, Keven Parker Soul Food Cafe, and Beck's Cajun Cafe.  All good eats and I highly recommend trying them all if you have a chance.  And even though that may seem a lot, there's still a multitude of over vendors I still have yet to try.  Maybe next time I'll try more of them, but it might be hard to sway from my favorites above, especially Dutch Eating Place and Tommy DiNic's, both which I already tried from my last Philly visit 4 years ago.

Like I stated in my previous review, Reading Terminal Market is truly a great sampling of what Philadelphia has to offer in terms of food.  And I don't think I can ever get tired of the place!

So my husband and I went to check out this restaurant because of all the rave reviews it was getting, 4.5 stars on Yelp no less, must be pretty fantastic. We drove up to visit Santa Barbara for the weekend to celebrate our 4th Anniversary. I really wanted to enjoy the experience at Black Sheep, but have to say it was a let down and frankly, a waste of time and money. 
I booked a table for 2 at 7.30pm, we showed up on time and were led to a table right in front of the door where people were walking in and out. 

I get that the restaurant is busy, but why didn't the person who reserved the table for me let me know that the table was going to be in such a awkward position where you'd be right up against customers and servers who were walking in and out? This is definitely not a table I would expect to get when I'm booking my table ahead of time. The person reserving our table should have asked if I would be okay with sitting there. 

Well, when I saw the table, I asked the waitress if we could get another table, she said there was a table where the customers were wrapping up and that it would take 15 minutes, 30 minutes later we were still waiting at the bar for the table. We finally got seated at 8.10pm. 

My husband ordered the ramen and asked for extra noodles and pork, the waitress mentioned that it would cost extra, but didn't specify how much. I wish she had told us it would cost $4 for some extra noodles and $4 dollars for the pork, making the bowl of ramen $21 before tax. The Ramen itself was rather sour, after the initial shock, you sort of get used to the strange taste. It is somewhat tolerable if you're hungry, but this Ramen is nowhere in the ballpark of a solid good bowl of ramen that you'd get at Tatsu Ramen, or Ippudu, or plenty of other Ramen places I've been to. In fact it was probably the worst ramen we've ever had. Definitely the most expensive and least worth it bowl of "Ramen" we've ever had. 

I ordered a two sides for my meal, I made that clear to the waitress that instead of ordering a main meal, I would order two sides, but my husband's Ramen came out WELL after the sides had come out. I tried waiting for his ramen to come out so we could eat at the same time, but it was taking too long: well after I had finished eating the scallop appetizer and the sautéed sugar snap peas, he was still waiting for his bowl of Ramen. 

The sugar snap peas were a joke, $8 for a tiny bowl of under seasoned and overcooked sugar snap peas? What a scam!

The scallop was strange, had a weird mushy texture and it didn't taste fresh. It was also under seasoned. I should have sent it back, but I was still trying to convince myself at that point that The Black Sheep couldn't be all that bad, it had 4.5 stars on yelp after all. In retrospect, we should have sent everything back and left. Eating at hamburger habit or even at Mac Donald's would have been much better at that point, if I had been honest with myself. 

I asked the restaurant manager for salt and pepper and he seemed offended. He said "sure" then took off and came back with the condiments, plunked them down on the table and left immediately, quite rude I must say. 

About the service of the staff, overall very unprofessional. They try to be chatty and helpful, but miss the most basic things. Firstly, the waitress set a pair of chopsticks for me down on the table itself, not on a chopstick rest or a plate or bowl or napkin, but the table. It's not a super big deal, I think I can survive a few germs, but for an establishment like that, I'm quite underwhelmed by the lack of thought and professionalism.

When another server came with the scallops, she plunked it down on the table directly over the menus! WTF? seriously? You can't even be bothered to move the menus away before setting down this fancy scallop dish. Am I at a food court or a nice restaurant??? I'm confused. 

We ordered a Lavender Beer, I asked about it cos' I thought it was interesting, it was highly recommended by our waitress, but it didn't taste good either. 

For me this place seemed really pretentious and hyped up, with a mish-mash of poorly conceived food concoctions and unprofessional staff. Won't be coming back again. Hopefully the management will take the negative feedback seriously and do something constructive about it.

Seems like there is not a lot of consistency with the food. Looking at the photos, the ramen and the scallop that other people had looks different from what we had. The sautéed snap peas look the same though, overcooked and miserly portions. 

I would have liked to be more honest with the management and give them my feedback right then and there, but I was not sure that the manager would be receptive to me, given how he responded to my request for salt.

There are a good number of 1 star reviews and now I can totally see why.

I've been coming here for literally 12 years, with plenty of memories (both clear and fuzzy).  But I will absolutely never return with the new $10 and $20 parking fees.  

Paying $9 for mixed drinks - even with the admittedly good people watching and pai gow poker - after dropping a Hamilton just to walk through the door?  Bye Felicia.

One of the good things when visiting Clearwater, Florida was having Puerto Rican food for the first time. 

Since we're not too familiar with the names on the menu, it wasn't hard to choose the entrees. The descriptions provided on the items were simple and the ingredients are similar to other latin flavors we've had before, but the style and combinations is what's new to us, which was really exciting. 

For appetizers we went for the "Fried Cheese with Guava" ($5.25). Once served you'll notice its golden brown color of the small cubes. And once you bite into them, you can taste the creamy and soft textures of white cheeses. The strong flavor from the guava sauce adds sweetness and I thought it paired well. For starters I highly recommend, it was good. 

"Skirt Steak Mofongo" ($15.95). Right down the core of the plate, what you see is garlic flavored mashed plantains. The mushiness of it tasted firm and starchy. The cut steaks were beefy, and I did like the taste of herbs from the chimichurri sauces on top. Having this was interesting because we've never anything like it and we were impressed. 

"Special Chicken Roulade" ($19.95). Its cut rolled chicken breast pieces, wrapped in bacon and stuffed with plantains and chorizo. The sweet flavors comes from the cream cheese and passion fruit glaze. All I can say it was loaded with deliciousness. 

Our server was friendly, he welcomed us as soon as we walked in and touched bases with us during the experience. 

Nice presentation of their meals to along with excellent taste that made the experience memorable.

This spot is so contemporary, so chic, so...Instagram-worthy! And their food is beyond delicious, diverse, and healthy! I ordered the chips and cashew queso, eggplant shawarma, and this thai noodle salad (can't find the name anymore on their current menu). 

I always think that appetizers are the best part of every restaurant. It's a little teaser of what is to come next and if it's superb, that only means the best is yet to come! The chips and queso really did it for me! The Cashew queso didn't taste at all different from your usual cheese queso! The waffle fries were delectable and fresh out the fryer! 

Eggplant shawarma was very unique! Loved the crunchiness of the battered eggplant and the bread itself was oh-so fluffy! The presentation also was BEAUTIFUL! The Thai Noodle Salad was very fresh and mellow! The oyster mushroom really made the dish stand out, it was so juicy! 

Would definitely recommend to all my friends about this cute place!

Very nice hotel- but not as nice as a Ritz Should be. I gave an extra star for how pet friendly they are- in fact they brought us a dog bed (made for a small dog and I had a large one) and two metal bowls to our room. 

The grounds are large and well kept. They need to put many more trash containers around. And a place as pet friendly as this, should have more stations with poop bags. 

The rooms are Spanish style. Ours had a very large balcony and a fireplace- but our friend's did not. 

There is a very nice path that goes parallel to the ocean. Beautiful to walk your dog. 

Lovely pool area with good service. 

There are too many staff that do not know the property at all, and cannot give directions to rooms and buildings. This property is far too large to have guests wandering around lost because, their staff cannot properly direct them to their destination. 

They have drivers in golf carts that are always cruising around the property and will pick you up and bring you places on the property site- a nice touch. 

They have a very odd way of setting tables- with extremely oversized table clothes that hang bunched up by your feet. Very dangerous. Last night when trying to switch between two seats my feet got caught up in them and I completely wiped out- full on toppled and cracked my head. Probably should have gone to the ER - I have a golf ball sized bump!  

Food is ok. Not great- nothing memorable.

The server was great the actual owner sucks and has a real  crappy attitude when I informed her that my hashbrowns had to be sent back 3 times because they were under cooked and not crispy. The owner didn't even apologize for the error. She asked what she can do to fix it and I asked if she can just take the hashbrowns off and she refused.  I also told her that my partners poached eggs weren't well done as requested and that they also had to go back.  Then her excuse was she has 450 people in the restaurant.  She then went to the back of the restaurant and IMMEDIATELY started to talk to the wait staff about us complaint about hashbrowns. She was vocal enough that I could hear it.  I gave my payment to our server who was again great, and the owner came back with it and THREW it on the table to where it actually fell on the floor and kept waking. I really hope this is not the everyday attitude of the owner Kathleen.

If your looking for a good restaurant in Eagle/Boise it's Biscuits N Hogs.  I recommend going there!
Excellent  The people are very kind caring and generous,you can't go wrong with lunch or dinner here.

We've been here a few times with friends, it always awesome. The food is always fresh and very tastie. The grilled calimari and bruschetta is the best. A great BYOB to enjoy a great night out. 
They recently remodeled the dining area, it's a very nice atmosphere to enjoy a great meal anytime.

Went to Blue Oak for a birthday celebration. It was easy to find and we got (what looked like) the very last parking space and it was right in front! Atmosphere-probably the best atmosphere of any bbq joint I've ever been in. Slightly woodsmoke smell (not over powering). Not too loud, though half the tables were full. It was casual and reminded me of a back yard bbq..but that bar tho! It was beautifully set up, well lit, and there were two bartenders. One of them greeted us promptly and took our order. We didn't get too crazy (just hard cider) but it looks like the kind of bar where anything you ordered would be simple, well made, and delicious. We then went over to the kitchen to order our food. Bae had the lean brisket (you have a choice of moist -a little fattier, or lean) with potato salad and the garlic mac and cheese. I had the pork sandwich with baked beans. His brisket was definitely more enjoyable than my pork sandwich. I don't know if it was the ginger slaw or the bbq sauce but it was very salty. I ate about half. The baked beans were good. Just baked beans.  The brisket really was the star. Moist, tender, perfectly seasoned! I really enjoyed his serving of potato salad too. The garlic mac was a bit too much for me. I like my mac plain and simple, I just sprinkle some salt & pepper on it. Since this was just a side dish I don't think it was necessary for it to compete with the entree. We didn't have room for dessert, but we will definitely come back for the brisket. I'm hoping they don't have to use mass quantities of liquid smoke but a late night belch hinted that liquid smoke may have indeed played a part in the flavoring.

WARNING: this is my most petty, saltiest review ever. 

ATTENTION FUTURE DINERS: If you plan to eat at Willie Mae's, please arrive to eat no later than 1.5 hours prior to the posted closing time. Or else you will not eat there. Basically closing time is the time they turn the lights off. The kitchen begins to shut down well before then. The attitude of the staff gets $/-7! about 30 minutes before posted closing time. 

Having spent 15 years of my life in hospitality, I GET it. Restaurant closing time is NOT run in the door time. Even though technically it is. 

Willie Mae's keeps banker's hours. Because they can. The Treme location has and always will. 

The new St. Charles location promises 9-5ers the chance to have delicious fried chicken without having to take a half vacation day from work.
So they close at 9. We arrived at 8:15. Definitely the last arrivals. Our waiter was prompt and courteous. Who wasn't??? The server behind the bar that apparently had something to do at 9pm sharp. Which she yelled louder than was necessary, considering no one else was there. 

DH ordered the baked chicken breast with mac n cheese side. Actually he tried to order that but was told they were out. Of both components. So he ordered the chicken fingers. I ordered the 3 piece mixed and had to pay an extra $2.00 to make sure I got a 2 wings and a drumstick because no substitutions or something like that. Fried chicken thighs are gross. Chicken breasts are too lean to fry  I had the red beans and rice and DH had the green beans. We didn't think to order cornbread muffins until we realized the meal did not come with any bread, but decided we had inconvenienced the staff enough by showing up after 8pm on a Friday night. 

Now. The fried chicken Is. DELICIOUS. Deee. Lish. Shush.  The red beans I think are better at Neyow's. The green beans just tasted like canned green beans. 

Considering everything is a la carte they are kind of like a Ruth's Chris of chicken. 

I'd like to say I'd never go back but at some point someone I know is going to want to go and dadgummit that chicken was good. 

For all other frequent chicken cravings, 
There's too many other great chicken joints in this town to feel that way after a dining experience. 

And I am the only black woman I know that can't make fried chicken to save my life so I will forever be at the mercy of a commercial deep fryer.

For me, pho is comfort food. The broth is the foundation, the soul of a bowl. The analog of the roux in a hearty gumbo. My ideal broth is salty, savory. You can taste the oxtails and bones that have been simmering for hours on end. The pungent steam soaks the aroma of star anise and beef stubbornly into the fibers of your shirt. The watery, one-dimensional rendition served here is nothing less than a deathkiss, regardless of the quality of the other ingredients. Add on meager portion size (one-size-only that's smaller than a usual "small"), miserly garnishes, and a viscous undercooked puck of noodles and the whole thing's a disaster. The entire table ended up drowning their bowls in Sriracha.

Pre-made cafe sua da. *facepalm*

2 different people tried to clear our dishes 3 times in the course of 5 minutes. Yes, you want to turn over the table, message received loud and clear. Service was polite and friendly overall though.

I bought the hype. I thought my West Bank drives were over. It was not to be.

Having lived in the NYC area for many years, I have eaten is some great restaurants including Le Bernardin, Union Square Cafe, and several of David Bouley's and Jean-Georges Vongerichten's restaurants.

The Catbird Seat was really an experience.

Of the 16 or so dishes, not all were to my taste, but the range, preparation, presentation, and pairing with drinks was truly impressive.

However, when all was said and done, I spent over $500 for two people, and I am not sure it delivered the value for the experience.

Don't get me wrong. This was an impressive meal, for Nashville.  But, for the price, there are many better fine dining choices in other cities.

I do not regret my visit to The Catbird Seat, but I probably will not be a repeat customer.

This place is great! I stopped by for dinner with my boyfriend. It was our first time there, and the owner came over and showed us pictures of some of their dishes. They have a pretty wide array of choices considering their small size: breakfast specials, sandwiches, meal platters with sides, burgers, and more, all pretty inexpensive.

There are four booths and four or five counter seats. They're a little worn and had a few crumbs, but they weren't dirty. There was also an ATM and a few refrigerators of drinks. 

We ordered a salmon burger and a whitefish club sandwich with Cajun fries. The owner checked that each topping and condiment was okay with us when we placed the order. Also, my boyfriend didn't realize that the whitefish sandwich was a hoagie and ordered it as a club, but the owner barely blinked and immediately agreed to make it.

The food took a few minutes, which makes me think it was freshly prepared. Everything was piping hot, too! My salmon burger came on a kaiser roll and I got it with cheese, lettuce, tomato, and their DJ sauce. The burger was really delicious and rich in salmon flavor. I wouldn't have minded some more lettuce. I only wish that they had put less sauce on the burger. They also handed us a jar of the DJ sauce with the recommendation to put it on the fries. The sauce is a little sweet and a little spicy, but I can't say what exactly it is.

The club sandwich was a double-layered BLT. The fish was delicious, and the sandwich was really good, too. I loved the toasted bread. The thick-cut fries were also great, but I couldn't really taste the Cajun seasoning that I could see.

Sitting there, I felt like the entire staff knew everyone that was there. The owners are so friendly, welcoming, and passionate about their food, and that passion really shines in their food!

3.5 stars
When ur hungry after a long drive, getting immediate chips & salsa is perfect.  They refill both + water on the regular.  Ordering is quick although the menu is big with many combos to choose from.  Food arrives fairly rapidly.  I saw them clearing & seating new folks with no delay.  The turnover is excellent here.  If anything the noise level is more than energetic so it being cool at 85-90 degrees, an opportune time to sit outside on the shaded corridor tables.  Kids & groups are welcomes with tables of varying sizes.  

The get;  - Queso fundido comes in a terra cotta plate all melty, gooey, & even with a tasty cheese crust 5*
- Albondigas soup with giant meaty balls was really good but I did add cholula 4*
- 3 item combo with choice of pork tamale or taco or chicken enchilada with beans & rice 3*  I think I expected to be blown away so maybe I'm too harsh.
- Flan 4* a little too sweet for me
- Tres leche cake 4* good but I haven't had too many of these so minimal comparison so maybe I ranked it too high....

When we left, tons of people waiting but restaurant isn't big, maybe 20-ish tables.  I'd return but with so many mom & pop places to try here....

I can't forgive a place that will give me a reservation but when I later in the conversation mention it's for a Groupon rescinds that reservation.  That is a horrible business practice and put me in a horrible mood before I even set foot in the place.  There is enough great Italian in this city that one can and should avoid La Fourno.

Let me just say that even though I grew up on Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and had birthday pizza parties as a kid, at some point in my adulthood, I turned my back on pizza.  Looking back, I realize that this is indicative of a system: pizza is just not what it used to be and every year, it's harder and harder to find a good slice.  Some people blamed it on Philly's hard water; others pointed to the inability of processed cheese to melt right; frankly, I didn't know what to believe...

And then, I tried NYPD's pizza and the first bite of that cheesy slice brought me back to my childhood.  Thinking of Michelangelo (the turtle), I almost mumbled, "Cowabunga" in between rushed bites of pizza.  So, so good.

NYPD Pizza has made pizza a weekly thing for me.  As Hayley Sara B says, it definitely holds up during delivery; plus, their delivery guys are so friendly and polite.  I also like the added touch of NYPD's pizza box: "In Pizza We Trust" (seriously, it says that)!  I guess my point is that NYPD has brought pizza back to my life.

Stumbled across this place as I was traveling through town and looking for a place to grab a bite to eat.  Warm, friendly service and fresh, tasty food.  What more could you ask for?  Would definitely stop by again, if I pass through St. Pete again.

I'm eternally grateful to spots like this that transformed the game of bowling from the stodgy past time of lebowski types to the fun and grandeur it is today. It's not your typical bowling alley, as the lights are lower, music is louder, and the crowd is cooler. 
The vibe is so much fun, and I always end up making new pals before the night's end. The fabulous sangria and other choice beverages probably help as well. 
I've never eaten here, but it looks interesting! I remember seeing the tater tots which were huge and looked quite tasty. 
The staff is super cool and hard working. The young brunette chick is so cool and on point with everything! I want to be her friend. 
Oh, and did you know, if you bowl a turkey you get a free shot of bottom shelf whiskey? Pretty exciting shit! 
This is a regular haunt of mine and is really firing on all cylinders. I recommend South Bowl to everyone who likes fun!

What is this cheesy wonderland I find myself perusing?! What a delightful spot. From the tempting cheese, all sorts of gourmet little jars of things, authentic Italian meats, and phenomenal staff, everything at Di Bruno is perfection. While it can be a tad overwhelming for the average cheese enthusiast, there's always an employee close by to make a recommendation. I had a wine and cheese party to attend and had the good fortune of meeting Benny the cheese man who let me try a few tastes and made perfect recommendations for my party. He even helped me pair some delicious cheese with a cranberry chutney that was nothing short of a culinary delight. This is the kind of spot where myself, or really any other foodie, can spend hours and an entire paycheck. But I regret nothing! And plan go back quite regularly.

Sometimes even native Philadelphians enjoy the touristy stuff, like waiters in colonial garb.  I know this Philly girl loved the ambiance and experience that was City Tavern.
As soon as you walk in, you get the feeling you are walking in the famous footsteps of hungry patriots of yesteryear.  The building looked very period-appropriate, which I find fascinating.  Our waiter was adorable in his colonial get-up, too.
Most places like this would rest on their gimmick and forgo great food, but not City Tavern. The food here was nothing short of phenomenal.  If you're like me and venison and rabbit meat don't necessarily do it for you, thankfully there are a few specials nightly that appeal to a larger audience.  I ordered the lobster pot pie, which was a culinary masterpiece.  The lobster pieces were quite large and delicious, as were the accompanying shrimp and scallops. The sauce was a delicious buttery concoction, as was the pastry crust.  Simply amazing.  I washed it all down with a Tavern Porter (brewed by Yards) for the closest thing to an authentic 18th century dining experience as I was willing to try.
City Tavern is the kind of place to visit if you are a tourist or just rediscovering your own city.  The food is delicious, service impeccable, and ambiance can't be beat.

I love a good BYOB and this did not disappoint! It is very unassuming and super easy to miss but definitely worth it. 
While all the dishes on the menu were very inexpensive, the specials were a bit pricey, but worth it. We started with a scallop appetizer special that tasted fresh and delicious. For dinner, I got a special which was squid ink pasta with shrimp in a rose sauce. It was delicious and again, all the ingredients were very fresh. My dining companion got a steak which he really liked. 
For dessert we shared tiramisu. The piece we got was ridiculously small, but the waitress only charged us half after she saw what was brought out. I found that to be a nice gesture! 
Highly recommended!

This is absolutely some of the best Italian food I've ever had. And I promise I am not saying that under duress! 
We started with arancini, which were every bit as delicious as those I recently had in Rome. Their gravy is wonderful and therefore anything smothered in it is wonderful as well. 
I had the eggplant parm which (besides my dad's!) was the best ever. Huge portion so I had dinner the next day too. It wasn't bitter at all like some eggplant can be. It was lightly fried so you could still taste the eggplant. Absolutely perfect!
Our waiter was a delight too. By the end of the meal I felt like we were buddies! I can't wait to get back and try everything else the consigliere has to offer.

I have a feeling I'm going to run out of synonyms for "awesome" while I write this review. Fair warning. 
My sister and I came here during Restaurant Week, and had a marvelous experience, which is not always the case for Restaurant Week.
We started out with the salad, which was fine.  A nice prelude to a phenomenal meal. 
I ventured off the price fixe a bit and ordered the pan seared scallops as an appetizer.  Best.things.ever.  Seriously, they were some of the most delicious bites of food I've ever tasted. The same could be said for the pork dumplings as well.  
For dinner I had the maki combination which was perfection. The sushi was hands down the best I've ever had. I can't wait to go back and try more. Also, it was matched perfectly with a nice glass of Malbec...delightful. 
After all this my sister and I shared the four mini desserts which were perfect. Little rice crispy treat sushi rolls? Hell yes. My favorite was the chocolate bread pudding though.
All of this fabulousness was matched by our awesome waiter Jonas. This was a perfect experience and I shall be back!

Parx is my go-to place for a night on the town when I don't want to contend with center city.  I love it here...they have everything you could want.  Plenty of table and video games, lots of bars, decent eating options, and a fun club.  The drinks aren't grossly overpriced like most casinos...$5 for a blue moon draft isn't terrible.  
Club 360 is my favorite place in the greater Philadelphia area to shake my ass.  I love it in here! They usually have great cover bands and an all around great vibe.  The cover can be a little steep but it's always worth it.
Allow me to map out a perfect night at Parx for you.  Dinner at Chickie's and Pete's, play a few table games, sit at the bar and play video poker whilst copping some free booze, party it up in 360, sober up with some Starbucks coffee at Foodies.  You're welcome!

I have been excited about Pizza Brain for MONTHS!!! And alarmingly, the experience and the quality of the pizza FAR exceeded my expectations. 

Brian gave us two slices to try before we even ordered to keep the slices in rotation. He made awesome recommendations and was super friendly. We tried the Jane pizza, which had a delicious selection of flavorful cheeses, fresh basil and tangy tomato sauce. The crust was AMAZING??  BEST CRUST EVER?? Charred and crispy and had a fermenty dough-y taste. 

We also tried the seasonal pie with sweet potato, honey goat cheese, and pumpkin pie spice. I was afraid it would be too sweet but it was delicious and savory and complex and had pools of butter or something on top??? I have no idea. But it was alarmingly delicious. we sat on the floor and crammed pizza slices into our mouths like gluttons. 

Also the pizzas were very hot, and the wait didn't even seem excruciating because we could eat ice cream appetizers and look at pizza trinkets while our pizza was cooking. 

I was initially more excited about the quirky museum part than the pizza restaurant part of Pizza Brain... But now I can say the actual pizza is WAY worth the trip.

I have resisted writing a review of Pizzalchik because I have such a complicated relationship to the place. In the end, I find that it is my duty to report the truth about how this place makes me feel awkward. If you can tolerate the oddness, then you will certainly enjoy their excellent home made creations.

When I first went there maybe 5 years ago, they had just opened and my mind was blown by their tongue expanding vegetative mixtures known as "salads". With that first bucket of zal... I knew the '90's era of smoothies and wraps was over. New food empires would be built on the backs of rotisserie chicken and raw veggies. 

But wait! This ain't no rotating bird apparatus joint. I believe the chicken is cooked in a hotter than hell brick oven made for pizzas. This is strange. Why doesn't the chicken dry out? There must be a mega-brining process, and maybe they cook the chickens when the ovens are just heating up. Still, just the thought of that hot oven sucks the juices out of my mouth and the chicken I am chewing becomes sawdust. It's psychological, I know. And honestly, the regular flavor chicken is nothing special. The garlic flavors are better. But I still wonder if it is worth the $ compared to what you can get at a grocery store, precooked. Or heck, just do this yourself. Brining is the key.

And then there is the Pizza... the first part of the name. Odd that the priority of the brand is on the pizza when it is not really that great. I know, you can't put emphasis on the salad since our species is geared to crave simple carbs in refined starches, salt and fatty cheese. So Pizza... it is.  The dough is not that great. The crust is thin which I like, but I feel like I am eating a saltine. The bubble bread is pretty good. Loots of cheesy grease on those little strips of focaccia. I have nothing good to say about the sauce. I know my pizza and this is high end blandness.

There are nice brews and vintages as well as killer desserts. There are specials that go beyond the brand, but I have never had them. Why? Well now the plot turns into the twilight zone side of Pizzalchik. When I was there the other day they weren't ready to start serving their specials until 6:30 at the earliest. Say what? On a Friday night? What kind of slacker operation is this? Everyone seems to be working hard. Hmmm... 

This is where I start to feel like I am from the normal rational version of reality and the people who own and work at this restaurant are from an alternate universe where the normal laws of vendor/customer interactions do not apply. There have been other occasions where the bill was really high and when we asked to see a receipt, none could be produced. We have had discussions about what their advertised prices are and we have been told emphatically that their prices were never $X. And then we would pull out a printed menu that we had ordered with over the phone where sure enough the price was $X, any acknowledgment? nothing. Not even a, "Sorry about that, yeah I guess the $4/gal cost of diesel is really sticking it to all of us, eh? Hey let me throw in an extra side because we really appreciate your business." No nothing like that at all. In any case, it looks like they have an upgraded POS system, so I always get a receipt now and check it.

Service? This is a self-serve deal. But sill, I have to say, a little help would be nice. I do tip and expect something in return as part of the experience. When I am eating your delicious salad and you bring out the chicken and I ask you for a knife to cut the chicken, don't say "oh yeah the knives are over by the counter where you ordered." and then walk away. This would never happen at the Brick Oven Bistro. The "Beanery" staff would be tripping over themselves to bring you the finest cutlery in the house. Not so at P-chick. 

The whole flow of the place is anti-customer. A tiny counter to pick up your drinks in between people sitting at the bar. The waters we ordered are not there. Mayhem getting your drink. The restaurant is designed for the people cooking the food not for your experience as a dining enthusiast. 

I can't believe I am finally writing this review. It makes me crazy to even think about this place there is so much wrong about the vibe. I never wanted to go off on a local guy trying to dish up some righteous roots and leaves. This is such a shame, because I like the food and I crave good salad. I just can't tolerate the wacko interactions with people operating this restaurant.

I hate to give local businesses bad ratings because I so desperately want them to succeed. However, this place just wasn't for me. 

The customer service is lacking and rude. The coffee was absolutely terrible and pricey. I tossed mine after two sips and after trying to rescue it with more cream and sugar. I came here to study but couldn't find any outlets. After ten minutes I had enough and went to find a better place to get some studying done and enjoy good coffee. 
 
Sorry guys but there are much better places to spend your money.

My fiancé and I came here for Valentine's Day (they accept reservations) and again the week after when my parents were visiting. Valentine's Day was busy and they only had one server for the entire restaurant. Everything took a long time to come out (45 minutes) but the server was working so hard, so we didn't mind. 

I ordered a salad, which was huge and extremely fresh. The mushrooms on it were delicious. We also ordered garlic knots to share and these were the best things of the night! They are like Garlic knot doughnuts because they are fried and super fluffy on the inside! They aren't sweet obviously and are tossed in garlic, ghee and Parmesan! We ordered these again with my parents and they loved them too! On our second visit we ordered the MASSIVE Stromboli. Unfortunately, it came out raw the first time. Only the outside dough was cooked. They took it back and remade another one even though we said they can just reheat it as we didn't want to waste food. Well the second one didn't have raw dough but the cheese inside wasn't melted at all. The waitress explained they had a huge catering order and the oven temperature was a little off. 

We were understanding however we still had to pay for a Stromboli we never got to eat. We ended up just having them pack it to go but we were over it by that point. The raw dough taste and the cold ingredients were enough for us. We really want to come back because everything else was so delicious and we're hoping it was just an off night.

We visited Hedge Row tonight for dinner and WOW

The patio has amazing close views of the city and Mass Ave. perfect for a summer night and they even allow pups!!

The service was AMAZING. Seriously, all staff members were friendly, detail oriented, & knowledgeable about the menu. 

Shoutout to the manager, Lauren. She was very welcoming on our first time in.

Highly recommend this place for date night or group of friends or family. You can get so many dishes to share.

Hi. I heard amazing reviews about this establishment and their cuisine and was excited to try it. Sad to say bu never got the chance to. My family decided to patronize this place after a funeral we attended. We walked through the entrance and a member of the staff exclaimed "here comes the zoo!"  While I do understand that Metairie isn't New Orleans, I still wouldn't expect these people to be racist! Who am I kidding? I actually should've known they were racist. It's Metairie for God's sake. 


Don't spend your money here fellow Blacks!!

Overpriced and average. $20 for a 16 inch and pepperoni??? Cmon! We've come to the conclusion that the reviewers here have never had a real pizza from up north or they are related to the owners. How could you possibly say that this place is better than brooklyn pizza? Unbelievable!! It's a shame Broadway Pizza is not near Vail. You can get a 18 inch pie with pepperoni that's a 100x more delicious and tastes like the stuff from the east coast for around $13.50.

Although in a slightly out-of-the-way location in Clearwater Mall, we were lucky enough to see the grand opening sign, and boy am I glad we did!

They have a standard take-out menu, if you go online.  But if you have a sit down meal in the restaurant, you'll be greeted with a standard menu with a single exception - no prices other than the $17.95 at the top of the page (for adults). 

You'll then be asked for your order, you can order a thing or two at a time, as you like.  Since there were 4 of us, we each ordered something different.  Each item was perfect to share with 3-4 people.  We got multiple appetizers, soups, hibachi items, rolls and even desert. 

We are all sushi snobs, and we were beyond pleased with the rolls.  

Some other things we loved:

*The General Tso's chicken was LIGHTLY battered and fried to crispy perfection, we would definitely order this to go. 
 
*The hibachi items kept us coming back for more, we tried both the shrimp and the beef.   All of us at the table fought over the vegetables as they were all seared to absolute perfection. 

There was nothing that we didn't enjoy on the trip, but what we LOVED the most about our trip is that we got mini meals over the course of a period of time rather than ALL the food at once.  So when someone ordered rolls, we shared the 6-8 pieces between us all and then got another item.  It was an entirely fun experience and we are already planning our return trip.  It allowed us to try items we wouldn't normally have, without sacrificing the quality of a sit-down restaurant for mediocre buffet fare.

The Boise CoOp provides the most disgraceful customer service I have ever seen at any food market anywhere. 

After searching the dairy area for cottage cheese I was unable to locate it. I asked an employee standing 10 feet away. Rather than step down from his ladder and walk me to the product--as is done in every grocery store in the country--I was directed to the deli area.
