When I couldn't find it there the deli employees directed me back to the dairy area. I then approached the original employee who did in fact step down and walk me to the item in the dairy area. 

On five separate occasions I have  requested information about a roasted turkey product sold behind the deli counter. I've asked three deli employees and two customer service counter folks where it comes from, is it organic, and why they don't slice it for sandwiches. Answers have varied from, "The turkey arrives roasted and chopped," to "We are only allowed to slice Boar's Head products on our slicer," to "You have to ask the deli manager." Oh really, who is that? None of these employees was interested in attaining the information for themselves so that they might better assist the next customer. Letters to management go unanswered. 

Looking for local organic products? Better go to the Saturday Capital Market rather than the CoOp. Although the packaging may be pretty very few items come from local farms. Expect to find produce from around the world. Looking for healthy packaged food? Products on these shelves may contain GMOs, BHT, BPE, and BGH. Read labels carefully. 

The local Winco has identical products for roughly 60% of the price, and employees who actually know the store and are willing to help. 

Boise CoOp, shape up! Although the latest Whole Foods plan was denied by city council, they will be here soon. Their employees are well trained and their products are guaranteed to be free of many of the carcinogens you sell in fancy packaging.

**12/28/10 edit**
I bought medicinal herbs here the other day. Without getting into specifics let me warn you that the herbs were mislabeled. When I got home I realized the mistake and threw away the mislabeled herb. This could have been a very dangerous situation. Medicinal herbs--used improperly--can cause a multitude of problems on their own, or in combination with other medicines.

I brought the problem to the attention of employees, who corrected it but did not seem concerned.

When I go to a place I've never been before, I always start out with a 5-star mentality. Then with each mistake, I deduct a star. I also have to consider the location. With that in mind, I was in Nashville, not NYC, or San Francisco, or Boston. 

We were here this past Saturday. My husband & I were visiting my family, and my brother had always wanted to come here. We had a large party with us, 9 to be exact. We got here at 11:50 and there was already a line. The restaurant opens at 12 sharp on Saturdays. We got seated right away, and by 12:30 this place was packed to the max. 

As you can see from the pictures below, we ordered different items from the menu. Except for one person who did not order ramen, the rest of us gorged on our food. There were a lot of slurping going on, which is acceptable when dining at a ramen joint. Myself, I got #1 Tennessee Tonkotsu. It was amazing! Absolutely enjoyed slurping on the pork bone broth and loved the pork confit that went with it. My husband relished his #4 Szechuan Miso. It had just the right amount of kick to it, the noodles tasted home-made, and the broth was flavorful, he said. The one person who did not order ramen, ordered Shiitake Maz & Cheese. She said it was just a bit salty for her taste, and regretted not ordering a bowl of ramen. 

My parents were with us. My mom is easy to please, but my dad is kinda finicky when it comes to food. With that said, I really trust his opinion. So when I saw him gorged and slurped on his Tennessee Tonkotsu, with a little smile on his face knowing that I was watching him, he gave me 2 thumbs up, daddy approves :-)

So in the end, there wasn't a single mistake I could find. It's a ramen joint, so order a ramen when coming here. Service was most excellent from beginning to end. I am surprised at some of the low stars given to this place, but for me, I genuinely think this is a 5-star establishment. It's nice to see a ramen restaurant in Nashville. Will go back on my next visit.

This is one of my favorite AYCE (All You Can Eat) sushi places in town. Definitely better than the other competitors because their sushi quality is consistent and they are not greedy with their ingredients. Also the rolls are not just stuffed with 95% rice and 5% fish. 

This place can get pretty busy on the weekdays, especially at rush time around 17:00-18:00. So if you are planning to visit, be sure to arrive earlier. However the servers still perform to their best and make sure they keep their customers happy when they are busy. 

The nigiri fish are pretty fresh and good portion, the rice taste fresh and are not falling apart. The same applies for the rolls. There calamari and shrimp tempura are nice and crisp, not over battered or over fried and burnt. 

If you are looking for a good AYCE sushi, this is the place to go. You won't get disappointed!

Now this is an amazing pizzeria place I definitely recommend. Definitely a classy place. At first I was always wondering why one of my best friends kept coming here until I realize how amazing it was. 

It definitely has a nice romantic and classy feel and is a little hidden inside the St. Philip plaza but hey, great places are always hard to find right? The servers and bartenders here are super friendly and won't hesitate to socialize with you. 

I two dishes I do recommend are the Antipasto and the Shrimp, Mozzarella and Pecorino Romano Cheese pizza. The Antipasto is definitely a great pairing dish with your wine. It includes mozzarella cheese balls, cheese, asparagus, and Italian meat. It's a pretty big dish let me warn you. Sometimes I literally get full just of that. The shrimp pizza is definitely something to try. The shrimps are pretty big and I wouldn't have guess it would go so well in pizza. The pizza has a pesto base sauce which always makes a good pairing with your wine. 

Also they have happy hour from 20:00-21:00 where every drink at the bar is half off. Yes even top shelf! So feel free to grab a bottle of wine, or an nice aged scotch for half the price! That's a deal! 

I'd definitely return and would love to hear about your experience as well!

"Taste it, Love it, Yelp it!"

My wife decided to try out The Row for late lunch on a Saturday. I ordered their Hot Chicken and I'm going to make some people mad but I think it's better than Prince's. the chicken is boneless drizzled with honey and placed on a sweet pancake! I also got the bacon Mac and cheese and it was probably the best I've had in Nashville. The decor had a little too much faux look but I don't go to restaurants because they look cool. I go to restaurants because the food is good. After trying many restaurants in Nashville that had a lot of hype but just ok food, The Row is on my short list of great restaurants here.

I visited Nashville in early June for the CMA festival.  No plans were made as my bff was trip captain with 14 years of CMA festival under her belt and as of last year, she became a Nashvillian.  

On a whim, I decided branch off from the group and take myself on a fancy date.  There were only a handful of "fancy" restaurants to choose from.  How I landed on The Catbird Seat, I don't know.  And how I was able to snag the ONE seat available at the perfect time (right before the evening concerts) is beyond me.  It was meant to be I guess.  

The Catbird Seat is small and intimate, seating only 22 people at one time.  I'm not sure if it's meant to feel like you're sitting at a friend's kitchen counter but if it is, TCS executed this idea marvelously.   I was seated at the corner of the U shaped seating area and was greeted by the executive chef himself.  Everyone was so kind, friendly, and personable.  There was definitely an air of casualness to this dining experience, which I absolutely loved.

When it comes to tasting menus, I always opt to wine/drink pair.  I also like to swirl my drink in my cup and pretend like I know what I'm doing/drinking, all while nodding my head in agreement.  Just kidding.  Not really.  But yes, I always opt to wine/drink pair because why not leave the boozing up to the professionals?  That and I've opted not to wine/drink pair before and the BS they feed you about particular drinks pairing well with particular foods, well, isn't BS after all.  At least in my opinion it isn't.  Drink pairing is an additional $60 ~ $85 with tax and tip.  

Dinner is prepaid via the website.  It is approximately $150 per person including tax and tip.  There was a total of 7 courses.  

Verbatim from the menu:

1) Ky Farm Cured Hen Yolk with Bloomsbury Farm Wilted Greens, Sweet Onion Puree, Catbird Cured Bresaola

2) Sunflower Seed Risotto with Porcini Mushrooms and Italian Summer Truffles

3) Wakame Seaweed Pasta with (I chose UNI over SCALLOP but don't recall getting any Uni) 

4) Bearcreek Farm Beef in Umami Crust with Smoked Tofu Puree and Morel Mushroom

5) North Carolina Softshell Crab "Bouchon" with Kimchi and Tobiko Aioli

6) Hatcher Dairy Buttermilk Panna Cotta with Lemony Olive Oil

7) Butterscotch Custard and Burnt Caramel Ice Cream with Vanilla Luxardo Cherry Choco

My 2 least favorite courses were 1) the Bearcreek Farm beef and 2) North Carolina Softshell Crab.  The beef was reminiscent of beef jerky and the Softshell crab (although extremely delicious) just didn't possess anything special.

All in all a wonderful and casual yet upscale dining experience.  I won't go as far as to say that this was best meal I've had but I will say that it was quite a phenomenal meal.  I would highly recommend anyone take themselves or someone special on a fancy dinner date here.

What a great concept/idea for a fresh, summertime, waterfront hangout. A great job was done on the decor and layout. Lots of buzz in every direction about this place and for good reason - I can see this becoming a regular warm weather hangout over the next few months for myself and many friends. As a seasoned patron of many of our great city's drinking and dining establishments, a rule to live by is to avoid avoid avoid anywhere until they've been open for at least a few weeks to give them time to iron out the kinks. Even the best establishments need training wheels at first, and that's OK. We expect it. 

We made the mistake of thinking it might be low-key and not-so-crowded on Memorial Day Monday after a full-on 'grand opening' weekend. I wouldn't say it was packed, but it was very crowded when we arrived. We had hoped to saddle up to the bar and enjoy a drink and maybe some food, but sadly my fiance and I were only able to find one stool and sorta share it while we had a few drinks and scoped out a table. The beer list is extensive and varied, and I love that they have a decent amount of canned (cheaper) beers. The 3-4 members of the bar staff we dealt with were slammed, yet were all pleasant, seemed experienced and were on point. No complaints there. I just wished we'd stayed at the bar. 

After a while our bellies were rumbling and we had given up on hopes of eating at the bar and pounced on a high top table near the stage/DJ (who needs a lesson on volume control/EQ'ing, but that's another story!). As mentioned, we know and expect any establishment will have hiccups on opening weekend. Table service, however, was sorely lacking. The table we grabbed hadn't been cleared and we waited for a good 15 minutes before a busboy or server even glanced in our direction (there was no hostess - the bartender directed us to sit at any table that was open). 

Eventually a busboy swooped by and grabbed the empty cans and trash left from the previous customers. Not once did anyone wipe down our table or provide clean napkins/silverware. Eventually a waitress stopped and asked if we "were OK" (as if she/someone already greeted us and taken an order). We explained we wanted to order food and drinks - my fiance and I each ordered canned beer assuming it wouldn't be a long wait. It was then we were informed half of the beers on our menus were no longer available because, in the servers words "the management did not plan this out very well". For food, I ordered the popcorn shrimp, and a burger and fries and my fiance asked for the chopped salad w/ buttermilk dressing. We were never offered water. No biggie, but the high in Philadelphia yesterday was 90 degrees. Also, table still never wiped down, no silverware/napkins.

After a healthy 20-25 minute wait, our food arrived. But not our canned beers. My burger was tiny but tasty and the fries reminded me of Mickey Dee's, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. The popcorn shrimp was also average - not bad, not great. The salad my fiance received was not only NOT chopped (ripped, maybe?) but was completely missing dressing. Also, still no silverware. Was she expected to eat this thing with her hands? At this point our server was nowhere to be found. Neither were our canned beers we had now ordered a half hour ago. Hmmmmmmm. 

Finally our flustered server resurfaced with the silverware, when we inquired about our canned beers she took on the look of a deer in headlights, and rushed away after promising that the beers were on the house. Another 10 minutes pass (you can't make this stuff up), the beers arrive with a second promise from our waitress that they are on the house. We thank her, she walks away, and... what a surprise! One of the beers is wrong! *Facepalm* 

At this point, we're simply trying to quickly finish up our food (the salad was average according to my other half) and either get out while we're still relatively calm, or settle our tab and head back to the now less crowded bar. We ask for our check, and comically, she has it to us instantly. And what happens to be on the check!?!? The beers that she promised were on the house (on multiple occasions!!!I) Ugh. I couldn't help but laugh. 

At this point it was either leave a shitty tip, make a scene with the waitress, or ask for the manager. The easiest and most gratifying thing to do was to take a deep breath, and... leave a shitty tip. So that's what we did. And, as someone who has worked in the service industry and has many friends and family who have and still do - I feel appropriately guilty about leaving such a shitty tip - but that's the trade off for such shitty, shitty, service. 

In closing, this place has TONS of potential and will probably do very well. As I've mentioned above we expected to have less than perfect service, and they'll no doubt iron out these kinks in time. We can only hope they quickly filter out the inexperienced/clueless employees & focus on a better overall customer experience.

Last month, my family went to Alma De Cuba for a dinner. The food was excellent. I had a special that night that involved duck and another meat. Our server, Craig, made excellent suggestions and we got to try a few things to share as a table. Additionally, the drinks were top notch. 

However, regardless of how good our meal was, I'm writing for another reason. When we called to make a reservation,  I heard my mom responding to a question from the person on the other end of the phone. My guess was that the person was asking if we were celebrating a special occasion. In usual fashion, my mom probably spilled too many beans.

We were not really celebrating at all. You see, my father had just passed a couple weeks earlier and it was the last night that my brother and his family would be in town. We wanted to all go out together as a family. We didn't know where to go but someone mentioned that Cuba was the last place my parents had traveled to together, directly before he got sick. It seemed like a logical idea and so we made a reservation. 

Halfway through the meal, the general manager came over to greet us and said that he had been the one to take the reservation. He wanted to send his condolences, but also tell us that he truly appreciated that our family had chose to spend our evening with them. They even brought over a free appetizer. We really appreciated the gesture. 

At the end of a really amazing dinner and experience (my 18 month old niece even behaved so well!), we asked for the check. We all took turns guessing how much it would be. Yet none of us would ever actually find out. The manager and our server came over again, and before dropping the check, they thanked us again for choosing them. Then they told us that they were picking up the check as a token of appreciation. We were literally blown away. My mom bursted into tears. She had just lost her partner of 35 years and their last great memory was being in Cuba and eating much of the same food. It was an extremely thoughtful and considerate gesture. They even seemed to feel bad when they asked us to only pay for the alcohol (state law). 

To the servers, staff and management of Alma De Cuba. Thank you so much for truly brightening our outlook during a time that was so dark.

So I've been waiting for this restaurant to open.  I was really looking forward to some authentic Mexican food instead of just well made tex mex.   My boss and I went today with a former co-worker who is Mexican and who was initially very excited when he saw the sample menus on Huma's Facebook page.

We arrived just shortly after noon and I was impressed with the cleanliness of the place and the fact that it seemed fairly busy for a place that just opened.

That's where me being impressed ended.

The waitress was fairly slow.  And not very conversational.  Other tables that came in after us (one of which seemed to be friends of the waitress) got their orders taken before us, and received their food before us.

I and my former co-worker ordered the chilaquiles with fried egg instead of chicken.  My boss ordered the enchiladas.  (I should mention I didn't know there was a separate menu for lunch.  This was not the menu I expected based on their rotation daily menus from their Facebook page.)

We waited.  And waited.  And waited.

One order of the chilaquiles came out and the enchiladas.  Then my order of chilaquiles came out.

All three orders were ice cold.  My eggs were under cooked as well.

We sent them back.  They microwaved everything.  Chilaquiles have deep fried tortillas in a sauce.  Guess how that worked out microwaving them?  And my bosses enchiladas were still cold in the middle.

I ate my food, because I was starving.  It was fairly bland.  My friend from Mexico said it didn't taste right or very good.  My boss barely touched his.

The lady who I assume was the owner came and cleared our table asked my boss if he was done, to which he replied "Well, I don't want it.".

No questions as to why or any offer to try and salvage this meal.  It was awful.  We never saw our waitress again after she took our initial order either.  The lady (owner?) was the one who delivered our food and cleared our plates.   She didn't ask how the meal was or make any attempt at conversation when I went up to the till to pay.  I paid because I was the one who suggested this place to my friends.

Disappointed doesn't even begin to cover how I feel about the meal and experience.

Will never be going back.  Will not be recommending to friends.

This business has not paid their creative staff in 2.5 years.  

"Dear Steadfast community,

We are the freelance creative professionals who created all of Steadfast Coffee's branding, including its logo and website. Unfortunately it's been more than 2.5 years since we finished our work, and Steadfast's owner still has not paid us a high 4-figure amount of money for the work we did - all while running a business on the fruits of our labor.

At this point, since this website is technically part of a work package that has not been paid for, we believe it's within our rights to share our story here in the hopes of garnering enough attention to finally be paid, once and for all."

Is it only in Reno you will find a dive bar whose parking lot is semi packed with Mercedes, Lexus, and BMW's? It kind of took me by surprise as I approached this venue that was established in 1956 and had been suggested to me by an acquaintance who serves as a bartender here. 

The place is quaint, a little dark as it does not have any windows. The floors were clean, standard square pattern. There was a completely filled long bar (about 20 seats) and several high top tables, one of which had just emptied, leaving us to wait only for the server to clean the surface before we were seated. We looked at the sandwich board specials and the breakfast menu. The kitchen was one of the smallest I've ever seen, no wider than the cook's arm span. Simple is the kitchen, simple is the menu. We were there for breakfast, which is served 8am-12pm. 

My daughter was less than enthused with the selection, as she has very picky tastebuds, but opted for the biscuits and gravy with soft scramble eggs and crispy, crispy x 3 bacon. I inquired about the huevos rancheros, which sounded delicious but not quite what my tastebuds were after, so I requested the 3 eggs over easy with homefries and sausage patties. My man ordered the house made corned beef hash. We were served a plate full of buttered sourdough toast, which came two of our meals, and told we could request more if we desired. 

The presentation was exactly what you would expect for a diner. There was a bit of grease and the portions were plenty. The only condiments on the table were salt and pepper, so be sure to ask for the ketchup and hot sauce if you desire them. My breakfast satiated me and the sausage patties were thick and juicy. My daughter was pleasantly surprised at how the cook satisfied her bacon desires...it really has to crisp, not bend, and most attempt it and burn it...not this cook, he completed the difficult task masterfully. She was a happy camper. May man seemed please with his hash. 

I also had a cup of joe ($2) while I was there and it was better than most diners I regularly visit. Now that I'm a coffee snob, it's really hard to find a decent poured cup that is bold and has good flavor. This was good enough that I would recommend it to others. Overall, the food was ok, and I would be willing to come back and check out their lunch menu, especially since I heard they make a really good burger. The price point seemed right on for the portions and equal to other diners in Reno ($7.50-$9.50). 

Service was a-ok; she was friendly and charming and helpful with questions, but she also forgot the creamer for my coffee, and the hot sauce for our plates...it's those little things that make a difference for me. 

I was surprised that the place nearly emptied out before the AFC Championship started. I was expecting the opposite to happen. The bar has two decent size flat screens and a third tv that were all easy to view from our high top.  They turn up the volume for the main event. The tavern also has some gaming at the bar. 

I didn't pay attention to the alcohol situation, just enough to know they have a full bar. Just might look into their Happy Hour situation and maybe suggest them to another Yelper for her event. 

So, if you want to check out one of Reno's longest established businesses that still rocks, head to Brickies.

I don't think it will take as much faith as its namesake for this southern comfort food venue to succeed! Master Chef Robert and the entire crew know what it takes to please this Louisiana-born and Carolina-raised gal, and I bet he'll satisfy your soul food craving for okra, collard green, and fried green tomatoes! 

This restaurant has New Orleans colors and the glass tops reveal Mardi Gras characters as center pieces. The tables are mostly four tops, but can be combined for group seating. Dividers will be available for private party areas in the near future. The menu is simple with effective descriptions and reasonable prices. They offer separate lunch and dinner menus. The servers are welcoming and check on you often to make sure everything is going well. 

So many of the items seemed appealing, but I opted to try the fried green tomatoes as a starter before the Blackened Bayou Burger with housemade potato salad, garnished by a pickle slice and peperoncino on a piece of green. My man ordered the cod fish & chips; he requested the sweet potato fries as his chips, and added a side order of collard greens. The fried green tomatoes were lightly breaded, plated on a small bed of spring greens, and drizzled with a ranch dressing. I am not a ranch dressing fan by any means, but this made for a nice content of flavor to the starter. My burger was cooked medium rare as requested, juicy from the first to last bite, perfectly charred and covered in melted cheddar cheese, and topped with iceberg lettuce leaves and a slice of fried green tomato. I was disappointed that it did not have any cajun flavor that I could detect, and I let the chef know when he asked for our feedback. He let me know that he will pay more attention to that and that I can always request for a greater level of spiciness if I desire. I stole a bite of the cod, lightly beer battered, flaky and delicious. The fries had no outstanding notes, but hit the spot for me. The collard greens were tasty, though not my favorite vegetable to partake. All in all, it was a fresh and fantastic lunch. 

I am looking forward to coming back to try the Gumbo, the crab cakes, the shrimp po' boy sandwiches, and much more. This is a great add to the Midtown offers! Get in The Sticks and try them out!!

Mama Mia, this has to be one of the best Italian lunches I have ever had! 

Came here for a little date time with my man because he had an interesting interaction with Kevin over Facebook.  I know that one of my fellow Yelpers is enthusiastic about this place, so my curiosity was piqued, and I was open to giving them a try.  I'm often wary about going to Italian restaurants because I get concerned over the salt content when I am not a fan of salt.

To enter the venue, you walk through double doors with a mini entry way that has a cafe table with two chairs.  I found that to be interesting because who would sit there while customers walk in and out?  Granted, it appears it's there more for decoration than dining, and perhaps it's to give the first impression of the cafe feel they present once you're fully inside.  

We were given a table in a corner where we could enjoy some intimate conversation.  Kevin came over and met us personally, and thanked us for coming in.  We each asked for a cappuccino, taking stock that this is an Italian restaurant, so they must have good coffee.  It was light and smooth.  I might prefer dark and strong, but this was a wonderful compliment to the meal, served in a glass mug.  And I was quite impressed that I sipped and savored my coffee, and it stayed warm throughout the entire meal, nearly 30-40 minutes.  I initially thought the $5.50 price was a bit much, but that quality and warmth over that amount of time, makes it totally worth it. 

The menu selection had so many options I wanted to venture, and I went with the garlic prawns with spinach, baby artichokes, and peppers tossed with risotto.  The presentation was wonderful, and the flavors were so fantastic, I nearly wanted to lick my plate clean, but then I would have ruined the atmosphere of this quaint little joint.  I appreciated that my prawns were fully cleaned, even the tails.  The garlic hit the taste buds just right.  The parsley added color and another dash of flavor.  And some bites had a hint of lemon that added a delicate surprise and made the dish complete.  I did not add any freshly grated parmesan, firstly, because I did not want to mess with the original taste, and secondly, because as forementioned, I am not a fan of salt. 

Backing up momentarily, I did have a first course cup of soup of the day, which was included with the meal.  The chicken and ginger soup seemed perfect.  It was light and yet had so many textures with the chicken bites and the vegetables, and the ginger in the broth was so savory.  I hope this is a regular soup of the day option, because I could and would come back just for a bowl of it!

Moving forward again, we come to the third course, as we could not pass up dessert, even if I am supposed to be on a six week diet.  The New York style cheesecake with raspberry sauce looked pretty and tasted even more beautiful.  For my preference of cheesecake, it seemed like most everything else I had for lunch, quite perfectly made.  The texture was smooth and each bite was delicate and creamy, and then the graham cracker crust was delightful. The sauce added just the right amount of sweetness.  And we ate the whole thing, a generous slice that satiated the both of us. 

I can't believe we hadn't heard of Zozo's until a few months ago.  Talk about your hidden gems!  This is a true jewel, and if you haven't check it out yet, I urge you to go!

I came here with my daughter for dinner after a soccer game because this is where some of her other team members chose to do dinner.  I haven't been in since they made all the changes.  And by change, I mean they no longer do bottomless bowls as a general service.  Sure, you can pay extra, but their prices are already rather high.  Why pay more?  They offer three sizes; small, regular, and large.  Instead of a plastic placard, they give you a piece of paper with your table number on it, you write your name, and mark which side you want with your entree.  The food came out rather quickly, which was nice.  And it tasted really yummy...oh wait, I did that since I put my preference of ingredients together.  Our server was friendly and seemed to do a good job of keeping the drinks refilled.

I'm not a fan of the changes.  Since I signed up for their Khan Klub a while back, I had a free bowl.  Thank goodness for that, because then my final tab looked reasonable.  My daughter is a fan of this place because she likes to make her own unique creation, I'll spare you the details.  As for me, I prefer to not return...just not enough value.

I lived a block away for over 4 years and Mr. Lee's takeout breakfast became a Saturday morning ritual. Cheap, just greasy enough, and completely filling. Plus he's the nicest man in the world. Try the omelet with provolone and a side of home fries.

I have no idea what makes "California Mexican" food. I'm not a connoisseur and I've lived in Idaho my whole life. But this place tasted like every other drive-through Mexican place we have in the valley. 

Ok, firstly some positives:

Drive through. Lol. If you've read any other reviews I've posted, you know I love me a drive through. For obvious reasons. 

The portions were super generous! Look at that kid's bean and cheese burrito. That thing was MASSIVE. It fed both my kids (I mean, they're 4 and 1, but still!) and their dad polished it off. The rice and beans were adult size portions too. 

The price is very affordable. We ordered the kid's burrito combo and the chimichanga combo and it all amounted to $12.50. Not bad at all. 

The rice was nice. Fluffy, well seasoned, and not crunchy. 

The negatives: 

My chimichanga was supposed to be shredded beef, but it was more like 5/6 beans and 1/6 shredded beef. I had to dig the beans out. It was also very lightly fried, so the bottom was really gooey by the time we got home. I guess I've learned something new about myself. If I get something fried, I want some serious commitment to that fry! :)

The beans were gluey and bland. Again, I AM NOT AN EXPERT, but these tasted straight from a can with melted cheese on top. I like beans to be a bit runnier and even a bit...creamy? 

They gave us two types of hot sauce, but didn't ask for requests, so I''m not sure if this is all they offer. I did not care for either. The red one was very hot and overwhelmed each bite. The tomatillo one was so mild and bland. There was no happy medium. Bummer.

If I'm driving past and want a quick taco, I might swing back through. But I won't make a special trip.

This is a very unique little joint. It has most of the traditional Mexican foods that you would expect to see in Idaho. But it also has fried chicken, homemade macaroni and cheese and the best broccoli salad. It's kind of a mix with Southern cuisine, I guess? Either way, it works! And it means that more people can enjoy the cuisine together. 

I've never actually been inside, because drive throughs. With little human beasts, drive throughs just get me. I have been extremely impressed with the service in the drive through! Fast, courteous and always with a smile. They also maintain their picture worthy presentation in the drive through. My burrito to go still had the same giant beauty of one served in house. 

We've had the chipotle chicken tacos, carne asada street tacos, green chicken burrito, beef burrito, all the sides, and the fried chicken. I have nothing negative to say about any of them. I love the chicken that they use inside the burrito. It must be pulled from the fried chicken, because it is on the drier side, which I love! It is packed with flavor. I will say, everything we have ordered has a kick of spice, so if your tongue is on the wimpier side of the Scoville scale, you might want to check with staff first.

Wow. I have no real expertise in French food, but I like eating all things pastry. We had a super hard time picking something to try because every last one looked incredible. I don't usually buy "Hungry" her own treat, but I couldn't pass up the chance to sample two things. 

We had a chocolate croissant and a bostock. I have no idea what bostock actually is, but I'm still dreaming about it. I was expecting a cakey texture but it was flakey and super light. It had almond paste and crispy thin almonds shingled on top. The croissant had a mind boggling amount of layers. It was so flakey. "Hungry" declared it "easier to eat in pieces" and licked her plate clean. 

I also had an Americano and it was smooth and creamy. They have beautifully packaged treats to go: crackers, cookies, pralines. We seriously had a hard time not buying more. 

The ladies working had lovely French accents and were so sweet and helpful. I can't wait to go back and try a chocolate dessert. I will say... it is not cheap. The pastries range from $5-10 but they are worth every penny. You are paying for high quality treats!

Review for my GRUBHUB order.. which is AWESOME! 

So based on other GrubHub reviews, I waiting until my 2nd order to write this. Each order was FAST and still WARM and being a rather experienced Grubber....Warm is GREAT (keep in mind they have to cook it and deliver it).

I always get the steak taco's and you get 3 GIGANTIC and totally filled with steak taco's. They are so amazing. We also get the chips and guac which comes with a couple yummp hot sauces, and they give you a REALLY LARGE portion of guac too! 

My husband gets the steak platter with shrimp, jalapenos, and cactus and he devours it! His words are, EXCELLENT to describe it. 

So if you are looking for mexican, this is the only place that I will order from...good grubbing!! And I can't wait to go in person and try this place out...YUMMY!

Does not honor the check in beer - ouch! And the bartender - well she pretty much ignored all of us from the time we walked in. 

I hear they may have some relatively good food, but we wouldn't know because we couldn't get her attention to give us menu's...not that I really wanted to stay after we found out they wouldn't honor their check in offer....bad call PYT - BAD FORM!

Let me break this down....

- $2 PER song for Karaoke!!
- Minimum spend to sit at a table - Not enough seating otherwise
- AUTO 18% GRATUITY ADDED IF YOU SIT AT A TABLE - so make sure you check your receipt...cause they list a tip line so you won't see the auto gratuity if you don't look and you will end up double tipping.
- $5 for a Lager!!
- $10 for 3oz of a so/so beef


...there are SO many other places that don't charge you to sing and don't charge $5 for a freaking Yuengling Lager....DANG! Seriously, Yakitori Boy upstairs isn't that nice to be charging like this...meh - going elsewhere to get my singing, eating and drinking on.

David was an excellent guide! He gave us so much information and we left with a much deeper knowledge of New Orleans rich history and an extensive restaurant list of places to try. Torrential rain and flash flood warnings caused us to miss the last place, but our group was perfectly happy staying at the 2nd to last place and trying alligator! Turns out, it was delicious and tasted similar to chicken. Yes, please be advised this is a sampling tour so don't come expecting a full meal. The best taste we had was definitely the gumbo at Oceana. I'd highly recommend Taste of Nawlins for anyone visiting the Crescent City.

I have always wanted to come here, and although there was a long line and jam-packed inside, I absolutely loved it!!!

The line moves rather quickly. Once you're inside, you look for a vacant table, cleaned or not cleaned, you just need to find one! Once at your table, your server will eventually arrive and take your order. It is a CASH ONLY cafe, so come prepared. There is a bit of a wait, but we didn't feel like it was ridiculously long.

We ordered a serving of beignets (3 doughnuts), cafe au lait, and a black coffee. Our bill was around $11. Totally worth every penny!

We really enjoyed our time here and would highly recommend!

This is one of the rare moments where I actually wish I had a 6th star to give. I went here tonight for dinner and since it's Saint Louis, and I'm from the West coast, my expectations were pretty low. I was amazed to find such fresh tasting fish, not laden with tons of sauces.
I've since been back several times, and each time not only is every dish (love the seared edimame) yummy, but service has been on point.
So happy I finally have a regular spot thanks to Yelp!! Tell em I sent ya.

Woa, why's it take me so long to come here?! My experience was for a large to-go order, mostly focusing on the food of course.
I was excited about the burger reviews, so I ordered two burgers, some spicy smoked wings, and goat cheese stuffed fallafal balls.
The wings were really good, even if slightly too hot for me. You can pick from a few sauces to coat the wings, and I got the sambal sauce. It was robust in flavor and added a nice layer of flavor over the smokey wings.
I wish I were as crazy for the stuffed falafel as I was for the wings. I found it to be very dry, without a ton of flavor (which was why it's paired with bacon jam), nor a lot of goat cheese.
My burger was damn good, the truffle aoli paired with the onions! The patty was undercooked but it was well seasoned and hefty in size. I got my burger without a bun and they were happy to oblige. Looking forward to trying more stuff here!

I came here because this place has some highly rated Cuban sandwiches. Now, I have been munching on those for quite a while, they are one of my favorite things to eat and almost a comfort food. I would say that KU BA's sandwiches are not exactly traditional, but an elevated version with a little twist, and that means herbs and spices that give the sandwich a bit of French cuisine flair but that are absolutely not necessary to elevate this sandwich. Yet, even if the added flavors are a welcomed addition, this sandwich cannot compete with a traditional Cubano. Yes, there is a number one on my list and it is not KU BA. The five stars account for the side of yuca and the sauce to dip them, this side dish alone is a five stars.

The space is pretty cool. They offer drinks, which I did not try because Tampa equals beer for me. I can't remember the other offerings on the menu, but I bet they are good if I take into account the sandwich. Service is OK.

One of the best smaller breweries out in the middle of nowhere (no offense), but extremely worth the time and miles, specially if you come here at one of their events. On a regular night, you still get solid beers but a limited tap list, while on special events, the taps will be rotating and this place is beer heaven. As someone who has experienced both situations, I cannot discourage you from coming on a regular night, and I obviously encourage to check out their events.

With so many breweries popping up around Florida, 7venth Sun is still one of the best and one of the older ones. They gradually stepped up their game bringing in the barreled beers, and there really is no competition. This brewery goes head to head with the big boys in the state, and it's easily one of the top ten Florida breweries.

Come, get some glassware and some t-shirts, fill a growler or two (check with them if they take outside growlers), and be friendly. Dunedin will thank you.

So supposedly, the Chinese letters and their logo is recognized as "Little Sheep" which is a popular hot pot chain up in New Jersey, New York and etc. But why is it also called Hippot Shabu Shabu? If it were the actual place, you could of saved yourself some trouble and named it Little Sheep. Obviously, this is NOT the real thing so don't let them fool you into thinking they are legit! This restaurant isn't even owned by the actual Little Sheep company so you're better off traveling the distance and trying the real thing. Went here on a Friday night, and the service was really slow. When we first sat down, no one even greeted us or gave us our menus or water until we had to waved down a waitress. They even forgot some of our items and drinks which took forever to come out. The broths were not appealing at all due to the amount of ingredients they put inside for flavor, pretty annoying having to take everything out that came along with it. It was just way too much than what was needed. Also, a little bit on the bland side, the spicy broth was not spicy at all. Had a really bad stomachache after eating here, won't be coming back again! Doesn't even deserve a star but that's the lowest I can give.. :(

No way will I ever return to this restaurant.  The restaurant is small which is ok but the noise level was so bad that I could not hear the waitress talking or have a conversation with the other people in my party.  Added to that was the lighting issue.  It was so dark I could not even see what I was eating. I understand trying to create an ambiance but this was ridiculous.  I was not the only one complaining as other diners were taking out their phone's flashlight to shine on their plates to see what they were eating.  It actually hurt my eyes.  Added to that was the issue with the seats that feel like you are sitting on a block of wood made.  To say the least, this is not a comfortable restaurant where you want to hang around the table to enjoy a date night out or an evening with friends.  

The food....I'm not even sure what to say.  I cannot undertand the other reviews on here as my experience was horrible.  Portions are small.  Like really really small.  Don't come hungry.  The linguine and clam sauce was like drinking a glass of salt water.  It was horrible.  So bad that we complained to the waitress and she just walked away.  Nothing.  No I'm sorry, can I get you something else.  Nope.  Just left.  

So we finished eating, paid the bill and could not wait to get out of there!

I come for HH here once or twice a month and never can get enough of this place. One of the best spots in town for HH. The menu is well priced and very extensive. HH portions are big enough. 
I am a vegan and can always find few items for myself. They usually are willing to customize some of their items for my needs, as well. The staff here is very polite and well-trained! Very nice and professional floor management, as well. 
For some reason every time my friends and I try to pick a place for a HH, we always land here. 
FYI Reservation is made through resy and HH is outside, but the place has covered booths and heaters.

Had a great experience at Saba this weekend. They were very busy, so we sat at the bar and received excellent service the entire meal. We tried all of the salatim and the blue crab hummus. I highly recommend sampling the entire salatim menu, it was a lot of fun and we got to try a lot of items we normally would not have ordered. It was plenty for two people. The blue crab hummus is divine and I dream of the pita bread. Honestly. Absolutely delicious. Their drinks were also super creative and delicious. I hope to be back soon!

I've been coming to this restaurant since I was a toddler, mostly for receptions and dim sum. Joy Tsin Lau is like that corner store that you go to just cuz' it's there and you've been going there for so long. 

Their food is decent, and their dim sum is on par with those around them. I'll share with everyone a recent experience I had at dim sum. Me and a colleague went in for dim sum a few weeks ago on a Friday, late morning. They seated us to the right, with that tiny aisle. I asked to be reseated in the center, where the carts frequent. I was shot down, even though there was capacity. Ok, fine, let's eat. The carts came by maybe once? We ended up trying to flag them down and trying to get the attention of the servers. In the end, we waited 45 minutes and were only able to get two dim sum plates. We paid our tab ($5) and left a dollar on the table for tip. We left the restaurant and got about 20 feet away when a server magically appeared and demanded more money for tip. Apparently chasing down patrons on Race street for tips for mediocre service is acceptable. I handed him another dollar and shook my head. It just wasn't worth trying to explain.

WOW, so impressed with the renovations! In my book, this Remedy location, has gone up at least 3 stars since my last visit.

I first stopped into Remedy a few years back and just hated it! It was old, run down and smelt terrible and the customer service was not good. And I know some people liked that "starving student" hang-out vibe... I did not. It was gross. I never came back. (I actually thought I had written a 2 star review - guess not). Then I was asked to meet there for a meeting, so begrudgingly I went. To my surprise the place has completely been re-done. 

Remedy is now airy, clean and fresh. The gross moldy-pachouli hybrid smell has been replaced with the heavenly smell of delicious foods. And the customer service - well, lets just say I was quite impresses! The young man working the counter went out of his was to be helpful. Even making taster size versions of a chai for us to try out. Remedy Garneau, I will be back. (But not the downtown location, that one's crap wifi irks me to no end!)

Alberta has its first Izakaya!! Hooray (and take that Calgary!) For those of you who may not be familiar with what an Izakaya is, well, basically it is the equivalent to a Hudsons/Pint/Brewhouse in Japan. It is the Japanese version of a pub that serves Japanese style pub food: The kind of food that one would want to consume during or after drinking copious amounts of beer an/or sake. It is a wood paneled, brew consuming, deep-fried fun house and I love it! I hope a ton more open up in our fair River City - ya, because that's what we need, more excuses for drinking beer; well, we are Canadian, so yes we always need more! Especially if they are going to serve the excellent and tasty food that an Izakaya has to offer.  From the deep-fried oysters to the beef tatki, I loved everything that was put in front of me. Oh, a mad shout out to Mr Arc P for doing the ordering! The chicken was good, the tuna was even better, the mackerel amazing. I loved the pickled veg; it nicely refreshed the pallet between the fried food and the sashimi. Oh, and it is probably because of the beer, but I just love and get the biggest kick out of fish flakes when presented on a hot dish: The way they seem to breath, with hot breath moving them from the heat of the dish and the air around them - so fun!

I came out to the Melting Pot for a big family celebration, a 30th Anniversary and a Birthday! We arrived and the table wasn't ready yet - which never bothers me as long as there is a bar to sit at. Often, I prefer to sit and have a drink at the bar before heading to my table. And I have to say, the two bartenders were great! The TV's were had the big game of the day on, and the bar stools are really nice. Points scored for a great lounge! 

We were seated at a long booth with 4 tables with dividers between some of them, so, it didn't really feel like we were really sitting together. The service was a bit slow, the menu a bit confusing. All I can say is thank goodness I got wine from the bar, because after we finished that bottle our server never once asked if I would like another drink... And I sure would have! I even tried to get her attention, twice, then just gave up. The cheese is tasty, as is the meat course, although the timing seemed a bit off. They tell you certain times to have the meats in the hot oil to cook, more then once I cut into meat and it was still raw and then had to back in (which makes me nervous that raw meat was then just cut open on my plate. And we were even using our cell phones as timers!) We also had a salad course, mine was just terrible and my cousin who made it quite clear when we sat down that she has a severe nut allergy, sever enough to be deadly, yup nuts came on her salad. 

I really, really, REALLY wanted to just love the Melting Pot. Alas, this was not a great experience. It was tasty and fun for a while. Then all in all it was just too long, too many snafus, and too many calories consumed. But, I would consider going to try again. I did come here when it first opened 5 or 6 years ago and I remembered really liking it. Be on the look-out for a re-review!

I came to your place for a World Cup match last month and the service was horrible, crappy attitude by our server, and mediocre food.  I make it a point to try not to write a bad review unless things were really awful - I believe in second chances and I will usually go back to the place and see if things changed.  But crying about a 20 cent tip and posting it online is completely unprofessional, thank goodness you have to be famous for that to happen. I would have left you guys zero for a tip but my girlfriend made me leave you $1.

The last time I ate here was good.  Service was also good.  Today, I ordered delivery today and got marinara and hot and sweet peppers on my cheesesteak. I was charged $1 extra. I was NOT told it was extra.  I also, which will make me NEVER go back to this establishment again, was CHARGED $1 to use my debit card. WTF???? Wasn't told about that either and i feel that is sneaky and unethical.  It's my money, I'm paying already to buy food and I'm going to get charged an extra $1 just to buy food from your place.  I'm livid.  Plus, since I'm in a roll, the cheese fries were so dry.  If your going to call them cheese fries, them put ample cheese on them.  The Philly pretzel must have been old,  it was super dry and brittle. I'm disgusted by the greed in today's eateries.  
I lived in Philly for over a year and there were pretzel vendors on almost every street corner.  And they were fab!!! The pretzel today was gross.  The side of cheese tastes watered down.  (indeed, it was watered down) The best cheesesteak ever is in Cherry Hill, New Jersey, course, Philly has awesome ones too. ....No matter how hard Tucson trys, not gonna get a Philly ( east coast) CS in Tucson Arizona. And back east,  they don't charge extra for sauce and pepps. So, all told, for $19.11. For a sandwhich, fries and a freakin gross ass pretzel.... i Will never ever ever order again from NOT east coast subs.  Such a bummer..........Blaaahhhhh.....

I rarely give out 5 stars but had a prefect dining experience at Butcher and Singer.  The service, ambiance, drinks, and food were all top notch.  I tried the Delmonico with truffle butter on top and it was to die for.  If you are in the area, looking for an awesome dining experience, craving steak, and have some $$ to spend then look no further.

I want to like this place but there's just too many things off about our brunch experience today.  The atmosphere was hectic inside, service was not all that great (didn't give me my coffee mug or let me know that coffee was self service), one bathroom and the sink was clogged, and then the food was not all that great. My Lobster Benedict had both poached eggs close to being well done, no runny yolk.  Coupled all that to the $$$ for brunch.  I'm going to give it 3-stars for our experience today.

Picture a bar that bills itself as the "Best Bar In The Entire World" but falls short by about, oh, everything, and you're just getting to what goes down at Big Daddy's on any busy night. 

In fairness, the bar as a space has some promise, with both an large indoor bar and outside patio for those warm cool evenings. I'd even say some of the bartenders are pretty cool, all things considered.

But wow, when the midnight hour rolls around, you'd think the Douche Olympics were in town. Popper collars, backward lids, jorts, striped shirts and Abercrombie seem to be the name of the game, almost like prerequisites for entry (strangely, a sign outside doesn't allow you to wear sunglasses at night there, and any place that doesn't support Corey Hart (http://search.creativecommons.org/?q=corey+hart&sourceid=Mozilla-search) is kind of lost proposition anyway). 

The bar, or rather dance floor is an awful mess of country hip hop sizzlin' singles guaranteed to cause spastic bumping and grinding. Granted, the Midwest Farmer's Daughter cum Drunk Sorority Sister look is popular here amongst the gals, but without any irony (guess that is good)...

Could this place be good? I suppose at happy hour it's another story and I hear their food is passable, but if you're looking for a modern bar with a somewhat sophisticated level of social interaction, you're not going to find it here.

Strange bonus: It's next to a wax museum, which is somehow wrong and right at the same time.

I had the opportunity to attend a networking event here the other day. I was able to experience the entire restaurant: from the outdoor back patio to the intimate and spacious dining hall. Overall, I enjoyed the experience. The service was fast and friendly, and always attentive.

I had a few beers, as well as a waygu coulotte entree and cheese cake dessert. I was full before the cheesecake hit my plate BUT it was soo good I couldn't stop eating it! Everything was simply delicious - from the preparation to the presentation, it was clear that thought and care was put into each dish. 

I really enjoyed this spot and will definitely be adding it to my regular STL rotations!
I don't eat at buffets. They are always medicore. Except this one. It's really good. Potstickers and cashew chicken. Yum!

Fabulous mom&pop restaurant: love it. Met Francesca and her husband: nice couple. Food is delicious and the atmosphere is pleasant. Dinner is lovely and you get or personal attention.
I would also add that 'Cami' paid attention to my needs and she was there when I needed something: 'Brava'!
Great place: try it and you will not get disappointed.

I was almost positive the old happy hour at Domenica couldn't get any better. Then Pizza Domenica came along. I'm so glad these folks saw what a great thing they had and ran with it! Here's a rundown of what's different:

-Order at the register, seat yourself with a bottle of that spicy olive oil that's so addicting. This is a much more casual vibe and service style that I thought was really fun.

-Happy hour times have changed, check the site! 2-5 daily.

-Daily drink specials, unlike the Domenica happy hour that had half priced drinks every day. Still a great deal though! Tuesday is $15 specialty cocktail PITCHERS. That sounds pretty great to me.

Here's what's the same:

-Same great, creative, delicious pizzas and some other much loved menu stand-bys like the whole-roasted cauliflower. Slightly abbreviated pizza menu.

-Great bar! Just like downtown, Pizza Domenica has a fantastic list of liquors and a really fun draft selection, along with some hard to find beer by the bottle. This really stood out to me as job well done. 

Tip: Sit at the bar or the pizza bar in the back to see the magic happen!

Great for the price!  I come here almost once a week for lunch since it's so close to my office.  It gets kind of busy during the week around 12, but if you don't mind an early lunch you can beat the rush and come before. Service is good and Lisa is great!  Lisa hooks me up every time unsweet tea, crab salad, miso soup, crunch roll and snow crab roll...it's sad when the waitress knows you by your order.  I wouldn't come here for a romantic dinner, but as far as quick, reasonable priced and tasty sushi this is the place.

So I was looking for a vegan place to get something sweet and found this local spot. It was hard to find the place when we arrived so when we parked I called and the man told us where to go. When we walked up there were a few people standing around in the restaurant, not really social distancing. It was uniquely decorated. I wanted the milkshake and wasn't sure if it was vegan becauseof the sign. I had to wait quite a while to even ask the server.  While waiting a man came in with a pitbull like it was nothing. I freaked out because I don't do dogs and why was a dog allowed in a restaurant where people eat? The owner of the dog had the nerve to catch an attitude because I freaked out.

When I finally got to the counter after waiting a while I asked about the milkshake and asked if it was 100% vegan like it was listed and yet again I got a a smart response from the man with the short dreads behind the counter.  I was not pleased with the service so I left.

I've been eying this place up for some time now, we always pass it while wandering around New Hope, but typically are en-route to other places.  On a cold Saturday we wandered in for an afternoon drink, but because we were running late (naturally), we arrived around 5pm.  Our afternoon drinks quickly turned into a leisurely early dinner once we took a peek at the menu! 

For drinks, I had the Savory Red Flight (3 reds for $24 - not bad!)  Nektar prides itself on finding unique and different wines that you can't just find around town - this was definitely a representation of that!  The wines are below:
1. Domain Les Fines Graves, (Moulin-A-Vent, France) - super yummy, had a raspberry/red currant/plum flavor and smooth finish. 
2.  Chateau De Saint Cosme Gigondas (Rhone, France) - this was described as "gingerbread, blackberry, white pepper, fully body" which was really interesting - by smell it was strong and a bit gruff, but had a very smooth taste and wasn't as sharp as I thought.
3. Weingut Paul Achs, (Burgenland, Austria) - This was super interesting, my favorite one of the bunch, plum-my and delish!

My husband had Barrel Aged Scotch tasting, and they smelled...like Scotch.  Sorry, I couldn't bring myself to even tasting these, but he enjoyed!

For food, we started with the Beef filet tip flatbread, this was the showstopper.  Beautiful roasted red pepper, cremini, red onion, and Boursin cheese.  Un.Be.Leive.Able. Definitely order this, so simple but packed with flavor - yum!

We also ordered the Truffle Ravioli, which was a ricotta ravioli, truffle, Madalo Calcagno cheese; I was expecting in-your-face-truffle, which this is not, but was good.  A bit on the heavy, bordering on gluttonous side, but was good!  My husband loved the Shrimp Santorini, which was a cast-iron pan with tomatoes, feta, jalapeño, and ouzo.  I was kinda full at this point, but he couldn't get enough. 

I can't wait to take friends or family here and taste much more of the menu.  The vibe is super chill, comfortable, slightly intimate, and relaxed.  The view at night is awesome, especially with all the Christmas lights in the wintertime.  It overlooks the Bucks County Playhouse - which is probably also super fun to look at in the Spring with all the flowers/outdoor seating.

Not a spot for the lighter fare, but a damn good breakfast joint if you don't mind indulging in delicious no-frills comfort food.

We came here at the start of a long day with the fam, and needed to have a solid base layer in our bellies, as we had plans to go on a Distillery Tour complete with multiple Whiskey tastings - Dog & Bull did the job right!

There were 7 of us dining, and knowing that Dog & Bull doesn't accept reservations, I called about an hour in advance to give them a heads up our party was coming in - the staff was super friendly on the phone and even thanked me for giving them a heads up!  Turns out they're not too busy on Saturdays at 11:30 (not sure how that's possible?!) so we were seated outside at the table right away.

The menu isn't too large, but has plenty of choices! Almost everyone ordered something different at the table - although there was a repeat chicken and waffles (which got rave reviews)!  EVERYONE's breakfast looked amazing to boot!

DWB, or drinking while brunching, is definitely something we're a fan of in this fam.  Our crew ordered a variety of drinks, ranging from a Beer Mosa (Troegs Dreamweaver & OJ), a Man-Mosa (La Marca, Absolut Citron, Troegs Dreamweaver, & OJ), and many more things I've never heard of - I opted for a Bellini *obviously the best choice*.  My Bellini was really good, a little bit heavy on the nectar but delicious regardless - everyone else seem beyond satisfied with their drink choices.

My husband and I (can you guess it?) decided to split our plates, he ordered the Biscuit Sliders and I ordered the Breakfast Burrito.  At first I was confused about the Biscuit Sliders, but eventually figured it out - 3 different sliders served on the plate.  The trio was:
:: buttermilk biscuits filled with cheddar-ale burger - OMG this was good, the cheddar-ale sauce was really savory and delectable, but glad it was a slider because it was really rich.  
:: buttermilk biscuits filled with tripel spiced BBQ pork - my hubby ate this one all on his own, I don't care much for bbq, but he said it was great.
:: buttermilk biscuits filled with fried egg with bacon - a classic, simple and timeless.  It was definitely the star of the plate. 
*The biscuits were amazing, so buttery and flaky - someone knows what they're doing in the kitchen.  
**I was so confused because the menu doesn't use an Oxford Comma.  #grammarslammer #AlwaysOxfordComma

The breakfast burrito was a home run - normally I stray away from breakfast burritos due to continual disappointment about texture - it tends to all end up being.... a mushy mess.  This Ribeye Breakfast Burrito was anything but!  Ribeye, scrambled eggs, home fries, cheddar cheese, in a tortilla, topped with green chili & pico de gallo.  The textures complimented each other and each component was jam-packed with flavor.  This was fantastic - plus it re-instated my love and belief in the Breakfast Burrito arena.

The perfect neighborhood casual restaurant spot.  This is right up the street from my parents house, and we decided to head in one night while we were down visiting.  I've been here plenty of times in the past, and ordered a variety of things off the menu, always pleasantly surprised by the meal.  We've also ordered take-out and this food translates really well to eating-at-home too!

Most recently, I ordered the Lamb Kebab entree, which was tender marinated char-grilled cubes of lamb with their house spice blend, and a side of grilled veggies with a starch - you have a choice of couscous or rice; I opted for the couscous.  It's also served with 3 dipping sauces, a tahini, a fresh tomato sauce, and tzatziki.  It was fantastic - not too salty, as I often find a lot of restaurant foods.  The veggies were super delicious and fresh, everything came on skewers, and the flavors mixed super nicely while cooking - they know what they're doing!  The couscous was simple and went perfectly with the dish by supplementing the already delicious flavors.  

My husband ordered the Tajen Shrimp entree which looked really cool when it came out!  It was shrimp with potato, onion, bell pepper, carrots and tomato sauce, and he opted for the rice.  The flavor was warm and bright - the vegetables really stood out. The sauce was somewhat of a tomato sauce, it almost had a spanish feel to it, despite it being Greek.  It was definitely good, but mine was better!

In the past I've ordered gyro, schwarma, and most of their falafel/kaftas.  NEVER disappoints.   We also had their Greek salad which is a pretty decent staple in my opinion.  The vegetables were super fresh and flavorful with whatever seasonings they add in addition to the olive oil.  I've had their lentil soup before, which is divine, but ungodly salty.  I am usually satisfied by just having a bite of my sisters order, rather than ordering my own.  

We had baklava here (we actually took it home) - it was great! They have many different flavors, (walnuts & cinnamon, pistachios & honey, cashews with caramel, and hazelnuts & nutella) we opted for the pistachio & honey which is my favorite!  Not the BEST I've ever had, but a really decent option!  

I've been back here so many times, and I know I will continue to do so.  Solid restaurant with many options for lunch or dinner!

The only drawback, is that this most recent time, there were an abundance of flies all around our table and the restaurant.  It was pretty invasive, and had to keep swatting our table area to ensure they didn't land on our food or drinks - I know that it is difficult to control for this, but it felt excessive.  Hope they do something about that soon!  Service is friendly, if a bit slow.  We had asked for extra tzatziki sauce midway through the meal and it was never delivered; totally not a deal breaker, but I would have liked some more.

The Philadelphia Museum of Art is definitely one of my favorite Museums.  First of all, the location is beautiful.  The grounds are immaculate and well maintained.  Truth be told, I actually ended up taking my Engagement AND wedding photos here (not why you necessarily visit, but whatevs).

The space itself is beautiful.  The construction for the building started in 1919 and it finally opened in 1928, that's just a fun fact!  It's really beautiful sitting atop Fairmont Hill overlooking the water and the Fairmont area.  The building is massive, and I always love walking up those steps (past the people posing as Rocky....) towards those giant doors.

Hours are pretty great, the museum is open 10 AM - 5 PM Tuesday through Sunday, and they're closed on Monday - pretty standard.  Wednesday and Friday the main building (the best building) is open late until 8:45 PM!  

Admission is what I expect, but the First Sunday of the month is "Pay What You Wish" admission - pretty nice!  This is also true for every Wednesday from 5 PM - 8:45 PM as well!  Otherwise, prices are below:
Adults $25
Seniors $23
Students/Youth (ages 13-18) $20
Children (ages 5-12) $12
Children 4 and under Free

There Philadelphia Museum is actually made of up a couple buildings: the main building, perelman building, rodin Museum, and Historic Houses Cedar Grove @ Mount Pleasant (never been to this last one).

According to the website, the highlights of their art collection include, the world's largest & most important works by Marcel Duchamp, the greatest collection of sculpture by Constantin Brancusi (outside Europe), the finest  collection of Auguste Rodin's sculpture in the US, Superb Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings, including Paul Cézanne's The Large Bathers, Vincent van Gogh's Sunflowers, and important paintings by Édouard Manet, Claude Monet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Camille Pissarro, and Edgar Degas.  Exceptional American painting, sculpture, furniture, silver, and ceramics - that reflect Philadelphia's central role in American history.

Great food - CHECK.
Outside seating complete with twinkling lights - CHECK.
Fantastic location - CHECK.
byob - CHECK.
This place literally checks all the boxes! 

First off, the chef is from Aleppo, and grew up learning to cook from her mother - you can taste the attention to details, spices, and tradition in these dishes.  After working in farmers markets for years, Apricotstone is Chef Fimy's newest project, only opening in 2016.  The food is technically Mediterranean, Armenian, and Middle eastern, which is why we get beautiful dishes full of flavor, with special offerings that aren't usually found on a strictly Greek or Mediterranean restaurant.  

I came here with the family on Saturday night (a large party - 9 people), having made reservations well in advance.  We were seated promptly at 7:30, but we were upgraded to sitting outside (always an upgrade in my book!) since the weather was perfect, sky was clear, and the twinkling lights outside really added to the ambiance.  We were pleasantly surprised by this! 

Service was a bit slow, unfortunately. They seemed very busy, which is a wonderful thing for the restaurant, but it was about 15 minutes before our waitress came over to provide water glasses (and water), wine glasses, and ask if we wanted to place an order.  Thankfully at this point, we had all decided what we wanted and put in our orders.  The food came out slowly, but when it came it, it was delicious!

To start, we wanted some spreads for the table - our server helped us figure out what to order, and suggested doing the dip trio for $12, so we ordered two.  We chose the 
:: hummus - chickpeas, tahini, olive oil
:: babaganoush - grilled eggplant, tahini, olive oil 
:: muhamara - roasted red peppers and walnuts 
All three dips were really good, but especially the muhamara, this was amazing - crunchy from the walnuts, but zingy from peppers - YUM!  The dips were served with pita chips, which were crunchy and good, but we would have preferred warm pita for dipping.

For dinner, my husband and I shared two dishes (surprise, surprise) the filet kebab and the luleh kebab.  Each plate came with rice pilaf, a side salad - greek for him, and israeli for me - and a choice of dip - babaganoush for him and the jajukh (an Armenian yogurt dip, similar to tzatziki).  The plates were phenomenal, the Luleh was amazing, it's similar to Kafka, ground beef/lamb with onions and spices - really good!  The filet was bomb.com, super tender, flavorful, cooked perfectly - YUM! The vegetables from the Israeli salad were very fresh and expertly seasoned - you bet I gobbled all of it up.

It was a family affair so we decided to share a couple desserts.  My husband wanted the gatnabur (armenian rice pudding), but I had my eye on the baklava.  Being a big fan of making my own (pretty damn good) baklava, I always feel a bit underwhelmed when I order baklava from restaurants - but I decided to give it a go.  Oh man - this is good stuff!  This baklava is made with walnuts, and is completely delicious!  Layers of filo dough, sweet honey baked into each layer, not too much nutmeg.... slam dunk.  I must admit, this is one of the best baklava I've ordered - I wish I had some right now!

Additionally, did I mention that the prices here are SUPER awesome - dinner entrees range from $17-$19 for the plates my husband and I ordered (there's a $21 mixed plate offering too, if you're feeling lucky).  There's also a 'dinner for 2' offering for $55 consisting of:
- a Dip trio 
- Stuffed grape leaves
- Spanakopita & Cheese boreg
- Falafel
- Lamb or Filet Kebab Skewer
- Chicken, Luleh Kebab, or Shawarma
- Choice of dessert
That's a TON of food for $55 - I think there's a date night here calling our name soon!  Can't wait to check out that special!

*If we could award 1/2 stars, this would be a 4.5 rating due to some of the service related issues - however, I can't bump it down to 4.0 stars - it was too good.  Resolving this would definitely improve this experience, but nothing can stop me from coming back.  A phenomenal dinner in a great part of town - my new favorite mediterranean spot!

RUN, don't walk, to Blue Sage!  It was hands down one of my new favorite finds - so delicious!  This places boasts catering to vegans, vegetarians, and other food-restrictive diets, but this food can stand up on its own - vegetarian friendly or not!

I came here midweek with 2 coworkers for a fun evening out, and we ordered a variety of plates to share.  One of our tablemates is a gluten free, vegetarian, who doesn't eat sugar or soy.  Everything we had on the table was within those parameters (excluding ONE dish which had edamame in it, which she ate around).  Below is what we ordered:

My least-favorite of this night would have to be the Taquerias we ordered.  The tacos are served on three warm, soft artisanal yellow corn tacos or there's the option for gluten-free blue corn johnnycakes - we opted for the second ones.  The johnnycakes were super soft and fluffy, like - well, a johnnycake; not exactly a tortilla but still good.  We ordered two different ones, both which were piled HIGH with toppings and potatoes.  Although I appreciate the potato aspect of the taco, it ultimately ended up being too much of the same texture. There was no crunch, or sharpness, or zing - which is probably why these were our least favorite.  They were still really good - but paled when juxtaposed with the remaining dishes.  We ordered the two below:
- Buddha: sweet potato hash, chile creme fraiche, peanut, avocado, heirloom pico, cucumber.  Good, the chile creme fraiche had a bit of spice, but very subtle.  
- Bravas: Spanish potatoes, heirloom pico, irish cheddar, creme fraiche.  Familiar with patatas bravas, I was expecting this one to have a bit of heat to it - but the flavor all melded together, nothing flavorful really stuck out.  

The talented chef makes Empanadas from potato masa (so they're gluten free!) and were absolutely amazing.  We ordered the Empanada Rizada con Queso (beluga lentils, black kale, quesa fresco with toybox tomato avocado relish, gazpacho, sweet pepper escabeche).  I wasn't expecting much from these, but omg yum!  The potato masa made for a hard exterior shell that immediately gave way to the potato-ness you expect.  Thin wrapper, filled with goodness inside - slightly bitter from the kale, perfectly balanced with the queso and the sweet pepper escabeche.  Definitely a must order! These bad boys come 2 or 3 to an order, you can choose!

My absolute favorite of the night was the Med Plate appetizer.  This was falafel, baba ghanoush, feta, grilled asparagus, and baby beets.  The falafel was perfection - super crunchy, highly flavorful, and perfectly soft in the center! Sometimes falafel can be too dry, but this had the perfect balance of texture and moisture!  These, dipped in the baba ghanoush was heaven.  The baba was super creamy, slightly garlicky, and 100% delish - it's hard to find baba I DON'T like, but this one definitely hit the nail on the head.  The pita it was served with was warm, and salty -  a perfect pairing.  (Pita is not GF.)

We also ordered the Roasted Fingerling Potato Salad, which I normally would never order - I mean, a salad with potatoes on it, that's kinda funky. 
 But I'm so glad we did - it was sublime!  Roaster fingerlings with char-grilled onions on spring mix, topped with maple pecans, buttermilk blue, maple mustard vinaigrette.  We subbed the blue cheese for feta, and feasted on this bad-boy of a salad.  The beets were out of this world, and the potatoes actually went really well with everything!  The real star of this dish, though - the salad dressing, that was AMAZING.

Can't skip dessert, of course - we shared the Hazelnut toffee basket.  Although it was vegan (no dairy!) it tasted like a very rich chocolate ganache - almost sinful, and thankfully we shared it 3 ways.  We didn't even finish it, but it was really good! Very curious about how it's made, from a culinary standpoint - it was beautiful!

** My friend went back here for dinner recently and ordered the Falafel Wrap - which is roughly the size of an adult forearm (read: MASSIVE).  She brought in leftovers for lunch the next day, and that wrap was awesome!  Definitely ordering this (and everything else on the menu) next time I come here - it was THAT good, even a day later!  For the record, it was falafel fritters, tomato relish, grilled red onions and peppers, cucumber yogurt, red pepper hummus.  Served with baby greens and chile lime vinaigrette

I seriously cannot wait until I can get my butt back here!  Check it out, you won't be sorry!  BYOB which is always a plus, and plenty of seating for large parties, or small.  Prices are super reasonable, especially considering the quality of ingredients!

This review is for Karaoke only - I didn't dine in the restaurant.  

We came here Saturday night for a birthday party, there were 15 of us and we had reserved a larger private room!  I don't know all the details, but there seemed to be a mix up in the booking process and despite making reservation for the larger room, we were informed they only had one 12 person room available.  After what seemed like forever, we finally took the elevator up to the karaoke bar area.  There's a larger area with a bar and some seats with Karaoke out in the open.  I have to say the general song choices were killing it, but I was glad to be in a private room for the sole reason of less people having the opportunity to hear me sing.

The room was tight with 15 of us, but we made do.  We were given 2 microphones (were informed, this is what everyone gets, nobody gets extras mics), and a less-than-friendly staffer explained to us how to use the song selection machine and how to call for assistance if we want to order more drinks.

The room was ours from 9 PM - 12 PM which at first seemed like it would be a LONG time to be singing Karaoke, but in hindsight - went SUPER FAST!  Mind you, my singing voice is probably equivalent to poor cats trapped in a burlap bag - that beautiful sound that I typically don't let anyone hear, however - I didn't CARE #alcohol! My husband was definitely cringing at times, but everyone else seemed to be loving whatever was happening regardless if I had the mic or someone else did!  Song selection was a bit complicated at times, however their song library seemed endless which was great!  Music videos to music were the strangest things I've ever seen - sometimes they were completely unrelated videos which was almost as much fun as the karaoke itself. 

Overall this was such an amazing fun night!  It wasn't as pricey as I would expect - there were 15 of us, and we spent about $500 for the room, tip, and all the drinks we had during the night.  I would absolutely come back! 
 I will mention, the staff were pretty unfriendly.  A friend of mine had medication in her purse (stomach medication for IBS, mind you - nothing of the "party pill" variety...) which were confiscated before she was allowed to get on the elevator.  Even the waitresses/waiters bringing us drinks were not the friendliest.  

Also - the whole paying-the-check situation was kinda clunky; our waitress brought out the bill VERY close to us having to be out of the room, and therefore we hadn't had it paid before the clock struck 12.  Waiting for her to come back and run the credit card, the staffers started coming in with mops and spraying cleaning supplies aggressively to get us out of the room.  Just kinda annoying...

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place yet! I've been here so many times, and each time is better than the last!!

Most recently, I came here on a Monday afternoon to kill about 4 hours while catching up with a friend before dinner (#teacherlife).  It was a sunny Monday - but there was a storm coming in, so there was an awesome breeze.
