Anyways, we show up around 3:55 and the gates are closed (they open at 4pm!)  We snagged a big booth on the dock side and chilled out with some wine and waters #roseallday . The waitress was super sweet about leaving us alone, and came by once in a while to check on us and refill drinks if we needed.  We also ordered food - the 7 layer dip on Happy Hour - I would almost suggest this as a single-person dip, it's TINY - but we were headed to dinner eventually so it might've been for the best.   It was the perfect way to relax in the city, while feeling like you're at the beach!

In the past, I've been here late-night and after dinner, they light up the twinkling lights, play music (or sports on the TVs), and it's such a fun atomsphere.  Lots of different sections to differentiate seating - the bar is a social and louder place, the seats by the trees for a more casual hang (and have pillow cushions to sit on!), or even upstairs!  A definite must-go on my Philly list. 

I'll definitely be back!

Strawberry Festival, Apple festival, Christmas Festival, .... What's not to love?  

I've been coming to Peddlers village for many years and love it, especially around the holidays!  Sure, the shops are a bit overpriced, and the restaurant scene has nothing to write home about, but the atmosphere is unrivaled.  We usually come here to stroll, sightsee, and shop around the holidays.  I think I've purchased candles, ornaments, and silly knick-knacks in the past - no major purchases.  The layout is super cute, and usually plenty of parking (Festival Days excluded - parking is always going to be rough these days!)

Bonus points:  Since the entire property of Peddler's Village is privately owned, you're legally allowed to walk around with alcohol (open container law only applies to public spaces).  Pop over to Hewn Spirits for an Old Fashioned or Spiked Apple Cider, to make your afternoon winter stroll that much more magical. #YoureWelcome

I can't believe I haven't written a review for this place yet!!

This is one of my favorite favorite restaurants in the area.  I've been here upwards of 6 times in the past 3 years, which for me - is a LOT!  Today, I finally finally had Blue Moose for brunch *confetti*.  

Brunch at Cafe Blue Moose is elusive, since they don't take reservations for Brunch.  On a gamble, we ambled into New Hope on a snowy Sunday morning with a couple of back-up options already picked out, in anticipation of a 2+ hour wait.  Guess what?! THERE WAS NO LINE - we were seated in 5 minutes!  initially, our plan was to run over and grab a bottle of champagne from the liquor store during our wait (#brunchgoals), but we happily plunked down with plans for a drink afterwards!

We got seats downstairs right by the window - there's cushioned booths and it's super cozy!  We all ordered coffee and started looking over the menu.  We all were slightly overwhelmed by the surplus of good options, and somehow managed to make a decision.  It goes without saying at this point, that the husband and I shared... He ordered the LGBT Burger - that came with lettuce, guacamole, bacon, and tomato.  It was Super yummy, and I love the play on the name.  I had the Zippity Omelette - which is a take on my favorite dinner salad - the omelette was made with bacon, avocado, baby spinach, tomato, goat cheese.  The goat cheese was ooey-gooey and super delicious!  I LOVED this omelette.   (For the record, my mom ordered the same omelette and loved it, and my dad went with the Bourbon Street Omelette: andouille sausage, onion, smoked gruyere).

They had a "scone of the day" which was gingerbread, I was so disappointed since I'm not a gingerbread fan, but I bet it was delicious.

In the past, we've only had dinner - and everything I've tasted has ALWAYS been perfection.  I remember a braised short rib on the menu that knocked my socks off - as well as everything I've ever tasted.  It's a typical European prix-fix menu (2 for $27 | 3 for $35) - don't skimp on the 3 courses, YES it's too much food, but it's worth it.  One of my favorite (read: only) salad is their Zippity Caesar salad, which is romaine hearts, caesar dressing, goat cheese, crumbled bacon, cherry tomatoes, croutons, avocado, sprinkled parmesan.  Also, their Crème brûlée is un.bel.ive.able.

Blue Moose is not only an amazing restaurant, but has a fantastic story behind it - founded in 2006 init was the first youth-run restaurant in the area. Skylar Bird, (only 14!!), and several friends began serving on a small scale out of his converted mill home.  As these things do, word spread and locals started showing up!   After refining of the menu, apprenticeships, and a degree from the French Culinary Institute in Manhattan Skyler opened the doors to Blue Moose officially on West Mechanic Street in 2011.   Today, Blue Moose operates with a staff of all ages!  Plus, it looks like they just opened up a grab-and-go location at Ferry Market, just up the street - called "Moose on the Loose".  I can't with that name, it's sheer perfection.

*Always make reservations. You'll be sorry if you don't - and don't expect to get one the day-of.  Reservations here are a hot ticket!

This is a review for Brunch only - my suggestion would be to come back for dinner, based on what the other reviews say!  

Since Suraya opened its doors, my hubby and I have been dying to check it out - the buzz and word of mouth about the place have been nothing short of spectacular.  Needless to say, I was expecting GREAT things from Suraya when we came on a cold rainy Saturday for brunch with our friends (having made reservations about a month prior)!

Walking in, the decor is absolute perfection - the floor tiles are beautiful and ornate, the walls are adorned with tiles and artwork, and the light fixtures and furniture complete the ambiance for an intimate minimalist design with middle eastern accents and a very welcoming vibe.  There's a long gorgeous bar in the restaurant, where it seems you can order drinks and food, if you're lucky enough to snag a stool.  There's a coffee shop of sorts when you first walk through the doors - it has takeaway service, and assortments of pastries and small plates you can order to go, or to casually nosh at the few tables in the sun filled atrium.  The walls in this space are lined with shelves, proudly displaying cookbooks, spices (zaatar!), and various specialty items including jams, chocolates, teas, and more.  The prices seemed honest for the product and we almost purchased a couple things!

We had reservations (a must), but there was still about a 10 minute wait while they readied our table.  The waiting area is large and comfortable, so thankfully we weren't hovering over someone else' table while they ate. 

Finally seated, we checked out the menu, and we all promptly ordered the mimosa.  This is no ordinary mimosa - which I usually find too sweet.  This is apricot, cardamom, and brut champagne - closer to a bellini if I'm being honest.  The addition of the cardamom transformed my favorite breakfast drink (the bellini) to new heights - the sweetness was cut, and the bite from the champagne was tempered down -  this is my new favorite drink!  I'm not even ashamed to say I had two! #brunching

Our friends had been here before, and suggested a lot of our menu choices.  If we ever come back, I probably would order slightly different, but it was fun to try new things! 

We ordered a few things and shared many of the plates -
:: Hummus with slow roasted lamb (served with mint, baharat) - delicious. The hummus was creamy and delicious, the addition of the lamb added a savory, almost crunchy kick to the dish - yum!  A solid starter.
:: Beet Salad: (dandelion greens, herbs, tarator, grapefruit, cashew dukkah).  We saw this on someone else's table, and it looked delicious so we decided to give it a try.  It was refreshing, zesty, and tart.  The first couple bites were delicious, but glad we shared this 4 ways, because after a while it was a bit too overpowering on the palate.
:: Man'oushe with Za'atar, tomato, onion, and an egg - i ordered this at the urging our our friends, they were thrilled with it the last time we ordered.  A Man'oushe is a Lebanese flatbread.  It was very simple, and slightly underwhelming in my opinion, pretty bland and unexciting - this was one dish I could have done without.
:: Kafta Kebab: (Lebanese ground beef, hummus, French fries, onion, sumac, parsley).  My other half ordered this, and I ended up eating some of it.  The Kafta was really beautifully seasoned and prepared, however the wrap was very heavy and stick-to-the-roof-of-your-mouth.  I put some of the dandelion greens inside the wrap, which helped.  I think this could use some brightening up with fresh tomatoes, pickled onions, or some greens.  The meat was great though!

Overall, the restaurant is beautiful, the service is awesome, and I LOVE that the Philly food scene is main streaming middle eastern/mediterranean/Lebanese food.  I think the brunch menu is slightly underwhelming, and found myself thinking about some of our other favorite spots in the city.  I'll definitely be back for dinner to check out more of the menu (and maybe order that mimosa again!?), but wouldn't suggest brunch as the best way to check out Suraya.

What a wonderful market that you don't expect (as most hidden gems are). 
There is a cheese & wine room, a front and back "grocery" store, as well as a bar you can sit and order from, that serves food as well. 
It was busy for 1pm on a Tuesday. 
They have some items that are in a typical grocery store, but others I haven't seen before. 
I bought $10 marinara and $10 pasta. While I know that isn't a lot, if you look at these in other places, it does. But you get what you pay for, so I'm excited to try!
I'll be back.

I am smitten with Lüke.

During our whirlwind weekend in New Orleans, we tried to experience the whole gamut of N'awlins food. Everything was amazing, but Lüke was definitely my fave. A John Besh restaurant, Lüke pays homage to the grand old French and German brasseries that were once hugely popular in New Orleans. A mix of casual yet classy, modern yet vintage, with Southern hospitality ever present and food and drinks that delight the senses. I was floored.

While everything on the menu looked tantalizing, three out of four of us decided to get their daily changing 3-course Express Menu for $23. Best decision ever. I had crawfish bisque as my soup selection, and it was fantastic - a yummy little crawfish with its tiny head poking out of a delicious pool of flavorful bisque. The Friday dinner special was a Redfish "Court-Bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters and rice served in a skillet. The generous portions of seafood tasted so fresh, and the cajun sauce was so delicious that I polished off my entire plate with my bread. For dessert, we had Brendan's bread pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce which was heaven in a bowl. Bread pudding is my favorite dessert, and Lüke surely blew away my tastebuds with it. And all this for ONLY $23!!

Lüke's classic New Orleans cocktails were also made to perfection. The French 75, St. Charles Streetcar and Sazerac were all wonderful.

Lüke really set the bar high for our dining experiences in New Orleans, but fortunately, we had many more wonderful ones to follow. A MUST VISIT. Your tastebuds will thank you for it.

It's places like this that make me feel super wasteful. Portions are so big one dish can easily feed a family of four.

This is Peppermill's version of The Cheesecake Factory. They even have similar Italian blown glass decor and a booklet menu. You'll find everything from burgers, pastas, pizzas, salads... just like Cheesecake.

We almost didn't get in - the restaurants have super early hours here (what's up with that?!); nothing like Vegas. The chef saw us and waved us in though. Thank goodness because only the coffee shop downstairs is open past 9:30p on Thursdays. Trevor took great care of us, and catered to our every whim.

We ordered the Hollywood pizza with basil pesto, chicken and sun-dried tomatoes, the prime rib dip and the garlic noodles with chicken. Everything was tasty, except the noodles were way too wet - it was drenched in a thick soy based sauce - and not a good dish to keep for snacking on later.

None of us were able to finish even half of our portions. So, I'd highly suggest sharing unless you are super ravenous.

Established in 1938 and it hasn't been cleaned since.

I remember this used to be a very popular place for the locals. It has since become a tourist attraction. So? Long lines and high prices. And you have to ask yourself for what?

Mediocre food and then you get to seat yourself. How pleasant. 

And by the way- if you want to sit down  you have a good chance of sitting with other people in group seating.

On the plus side: The staff all seems happy and they do have good attitudes.

Creepy. Creepy. Creepy.

Just the whole vibe is off kilter.

The room was filled w/ stale air. Patrons to this place just looked exhausted. The service looked as though it was moving a glacial pace. You enter off the street and BAM you're right in the middle of the dining room and there's no one there to greet you. So everybody eating just sorta stares at you. I'm not the shy type but this is very awkward. So they tell us that we are "welcome to sit down but it will be 45 minutes to an hour before they take our order." I reconfirmed that we had a 8:30 reservation. "Correct." But you not will be even taking our order until 9:30? "Correct." At that point we left. Just bad. 

(Also, the toaster oven sitting in the dining room was odd to me too. But that's a small quibble.)

This place came highly recommended. So I did my research as to what could possibly have gone wrong. It turns out that the masterful artistic Chef from Chicago that once upon a time enchanted foodies has since moved on and the place has now lost what sparkle it once had.

Pass on this place.

There's too many great restaurants in this city of great restaurants to put up with Louisiana Bistro.

They will be shuddered soon and I've never been wrong on this type of prediction yet.

I'm puzzled by the good reviews.

1. No shrimp Po' Boys. Really?!? You've got to be kidding.
2. Po' Boys are made with Baguettes, not sub buns, sorry. Way too much bread and no crust?
3. Bread pudding was the consistency of warm snot. Worst I've ever had.
4. Cramped seating.
5. Took way too long to get my Po' Boy, very sad.
6. Red Beans and Rice was absolutely nothing special. My 13 year old can probably make better. What's the hype about?

Obviously, this place has a lot of friends and scores high here on  Yelp but, I am not impressed at all.

I was visiting my friend in Philly and she took me here for dinner. We are both Southern California natives, so we were no strangers to Mexican food. I wouldn't say that this tasted like authentic Mexican food. But it was all still pretty good. I got the nachos. It was delicious but I wish they gave me more chips. It was very pricey for the portion I got. I would come back for the margaritas.

The last time we went there with a small group and were seated quickly. The place can get crowded and reservations are usually a good idea. The atmosphere is good and the place is kind of formal with a touch of a family ambiance. 

I usually get the corn and crab bisque that everyone raves about and it really is very good. They have a good selection of wine as well. You can usually see the chef going around from table to table greeting the guests. I have tried their pasta dishes and the stuffed shrimp pastry and always enjoyed them.

Vincent's has a lot of good Italian food and the service is always is great.

This is a fairly new location in what used to be a Borders bookstore. They seem to have done a good job with the unique NOLA style decor. The place has an outdoor balcony seating. The location is very convenient right on Veterans and has good parking.

I had been to other Mellow Mushroom locations out of state. So, I was looking forward to going to this one.

I have tried several of their pizzas and they were all good. But my favorite pizzas are Holy Shiitake, Kosmic Karma and Philosopher's Pie. Their calzones are also good and I usually get the Chicken & Cheese or house calzones. I have also tried the Spinach and Greek salads and they are very good.

Dorignac's is a very good place to shop for groceries. It has a good selection of produce, meat and seafood. They have a full bakery with a lot of baked goodies. They also have an excellent wine selection. A lot of times you can even get hard to find items at Dorignac's.

Friends...
This is, hands down, a new favorite. Boyfriend and I ventured out in the pouring rain yesterday to come in for an impromptu dinner. 

Best decision ever. 

Where do I start? 

Atmosphere: it felt so... idk, cool? To be in there. The whole ambience was just laid back, finer dining. A lot like Zahav, great place to just eat in. 

Service: our server was so amazing. The whole waitstaff really. From check in to check out. The communication between servers is great, and they know the food and LOVE it. When you talk to them, it's not a waiter, but someone who loves where they are and what they serve. 

Food: short rib tasting menu. Just, you can't go wrong. Just go. 

In all seriousness, the in-house baked breads and pastry/desserts were amazing. The rye bread had the nice chew, subtle flavors that didn't overpower the accompanying tastes. That Russian dressing is on another level. 

We let the kitchen choose our tasting menu items. Spreads were great, honey butter was sinfully good. Chicken liver mousse, so smooth. Salmon cream cheese was my favorite with the pickled radishes. 

Avocado salad was ok. The pumpernickel croutons it sat on was perfectly crunchy on the outside but so soft and fluffy on the inside. 

Gin cured fluke was so interesting. Boyfriend enjoyed it a lot. The whipped butter with the salty, almost gelatinous fish was something else. 

Also, angels sung when our waiter brought out the uncut Short rib. It looked that amazing. And then when you eat a piece of that gloriously marbled meat.. you go to that all in, happy meat place where meat sweats don't happen and carbs don't matter to your waistline. 

Then the dessert. The blueberry tart was good, but NOTHING compares to that bacon egg cream. It's my new favorite dessert. It was rich, but light. He crunchy bits gave it a unique texture, but didn't take away from the lightness of the chocolate foam on top. 

Sorry, I just really loved our meal. Def going back to try the duck.

Went for a pizza fix tonight. There is just something about a wood fired oven. My favorite is the Italian sausage version. Lots of flavor packed tomato sauce. Way too much for one person but I could not allow the sausages to have died in vain. 

Did you know they make their limoncello? They do! Oh baby, baby. Smooth and flavorful but with a kick. Be careful if driving. 

Dessert was a large slice of lemon tart. Great presentation with a raspberry sauce. Very, very rich and packed with lemon flavor. But I repeat myself. 

Lastly, Mondo has the best beer fridge in town. Always very cold as nature would have it.

I've lived a block from Lee's for just over a year and I can't believe I missed out on it until now. The man who's always behind the counter (the owner?) is consistently so, so nice and is never gruff or short-tempered. 

The food is okay; better than most corner delis but not amazing. Still, at what deli can you get steamed broccoli as a side?! Thanks, Lee's for giving me options that don't make me feel sad and greasy after I eat them. The prices are good and they have nutella!

Here's a tip though: If you get coffee and say you want sugar, prepare to drink a concoction that would knock those with the sweetest teeth on their buns.

Hearty and inspired menu with prompt and courteous service. The thing that I liked about the menu was the fact that, while willing to take chances with unconventional items, it remained true to its original mission which was obviously to knock out a good hangover. Unfortunately, the only drawback  to be seen is the relatively diminutive space, which when coupled with counter service, can make for rather cramped ordering and dining. Hopefully, though, this place will get the success that it deserves so it can move into a much larger space.
   Also, this spot is frequented by the youngish, hip nouveau-orleanian elite. WORD OF WARNING: do not eaves-drop on their conversations. They will make you want to set yourself on fire in the middle of an American Apparel.
   Across from Banks St. Bar, no signage and off-street parking.

Kind of hard to get to and thus under-crowded, Sahara Cafe has proven to me to be the hands-down best Mediterranean cuisine on the west bank and a strong contender for top ten in New Orleans. The service is excellent and the felafel is the best i've had since mahmoun's in NYC. I find the hummus and babaganoush to be a cut above average as well. Definitely a spot worth finding if you live on the west bank.

Brown Butter was a pleasant surprise that is pretty unsuspecting from its outside strip mall appearance. It's relatively cute and cozy inside, but the star of the show is their food menu. Our group of 10+ enjoyed their Valentine's Day menu here and was wildy impressed. For starters, we sampled an array of unique items: fried pickles & ranch, mussels & fries, black bean hummus, baked cheese & bread, and coconut shrimp bisque. Talk about indulgence-- this is what NOLA eating is all about! From the starters alone, it was easy to see why this Southern American restaurant is nothing close to predictable. Two bold glasses of Tempranillo later, I finished the evening with a sweet, savory duck confit topped with sweet cabbage. Great, attentive service and amazing food. Only disappointing aspect is that the chef seems to change the menu way too often. Some of the dishes that I had been looking forward to (i.e. fried goat cheese), are no longer offered.

They say NOLA is known for its food, and I'm sure this establishment is one of the many reasons why that is so. Until today I had never had Polynesian food, which is a sad, sad fact. Fortunately, tonight Latitude 29 WOWed me from start to finish. From service to ambiance to impeccable food, everything was on point. We split the dumpling appetizers which were nothing short of incredible. Stuffed with mushrooms and other deliciousness, paired with a sweet dipping sauce were so amazing that I forgot that they were vegan (pork and meat options also available). 

Steven was our waiter, and not only was he attentive, he was funny, friendly and added an already overall very enjoyable experience. The tiki cocktail drinks are STIFF, exotic, and flavorful.

For an entree, I indulged on the Green Curry Bowl. Surprisingly, it was completely guilt free and vegan (tons of vegan options, but not a vegan/ vegetarian restaurant). Charred Cauliflower dusted with sumac, chick peas, carrots, mushrooms,sweet potato'd rice... perfection.

Lastly, don't miss out on their addictive Sriracha mayo and fries, which are so ridiculously tasty!

Walk-Ons is your standard chain sports bar & restaurant. Solid, yet unsurprising. Average menu with a Cajun flair but in a prime location and pretty solid service.  My husband and I, along with two friends, wanted to catch the Cowboys game and this was a solid selection within walking distance.  A shrimp pasta, a couple of sandwich wraps, mixed cocktails, and beer pitchers ran us about $120. Not bad, but steeper than anticipated. The food was good and did the job, but the real draw of this place are the ample tv screens and of course: location, location, location.

Food is excellent. And the menu is incredible. 5 stars start to finish.

However, I didn't love our waitress. She a bit curt at times (telling me to "hold on" when I politely requested a drink refill) and not bringing us the basics like napkins after dessert. However, the overall experience, based solely on food, was very memorable. 

We started with a spread of tuna tartare, brussel sprouts covered in buttermilk dressing and chicken skin. They were plentiful, generously portioned and packed with intense bold flavors. Curried goat & sweet potato gnocchi was nothing short of sensational. Fragrant bowl loaded with tender meat, crunchy peanuts and sweet potato, and refreshing cilantro... it was such a complex dish that had all the texture and tons of flavor!

Four stars if you're drunk, three if you aren't. And chances are if you're in NOLA, most likely you aren't the latter. 

Clover is a 24-7 local staple and came recommended to us after a night of drag shows, live music and fun on Frenchmen. The joke here is that you can't go anywhere after Clover Grill because you will wreak of the greasy food. And that, unfortunately, held true for our group. So much so that we were even shamed by our uber driver! Hahaha!  

Still, it was worth it for the fresh-off-the-grill breakfast food: omelets, waffles, tater tots, etc. Cheap prices and tasty... not bad.

I really wanted to like this place and have a nice time, but alas, that did not happen.

It started on Tuesday when I called Two Stones to make a reservation for Saturday night, for six people, for my husband's birthday. I was told by the girl on the phone that they do not take reservations, and when I asked what to expect at 6pm on a Saturday, she told me that they are not busy in the summer and that there usually isn't any sort of wait.

Fast forward to us arriving on Saturday night and being asked, as soon as we walked in, if we had called ahead. No, of course we didn't call ahead, because when I called on Tuesday I was explicitly told that it wouldn't be busy and that they don't take reservations. At no time did anyone tell me I could call on Saturday to put my name in (AKA make a damn reservation).

We were told by the hostess that it would be a 30-45 minute wait for a regular table but if we didn't want to wait that we could sit at a high-top table with bar stools. This is a problem as my stepfather has Alzheimer's and really can't get around or sit on a bar stool. When we asked if we could grab a bar stool (from the actual bar) that had a back, we were told that we could only substitute ONE BAR STOOL!! Apparently the rules are VERY STRICT! Only ONE person can have a back to their chair! Not to mention the fact that the hostess didn't sub the chair out for us - we had to do it. Needless to say, my stepfather did not feel comfortable and my mother, who has severe back problems, was in a good deal of pain by the time we left. 

To add insult to injury - right after we were seated my husband went to use the restroom. There was a 4-seat and a 2-seat table, right next to each other, that could easily have been pushed together. Why we weren't offered that table, I am not sure. Perhaps someone else had RESERVED THEM?? You know, the thing we were told we couldn't do?...

Anyway, we took the damn table and the poor customer service continued. Our waiter was EXTREMELY slow. He forgot several drinks and we had to ask for them again. He didn't bring us small appetizer plates so we were sitting there with crab dip and pretzels and nothing to eat off of. 

When it came time for our entrees, I was disappointed again. The food was ... ok. Just ok. Plus the portion sizes were huge (and wasteful), which is always a negative in my book.

I will not be returning, and my suggestion to management is to get your damn policy straight. Do you take reservations, or not? Why was I not presented with the option to "call ahead" when I rang on Tuesday? Thanks for putting a real damper on my husband's birthday celebration.

I had the chance to try Harvest last week, and I was super duper excited about it going into the night. Ultimately, though, I was not impressed and probably won't make any effort to return. Here's the gist of what I thought of the various aspects of the restaurant:

Ambiance - 5 stars
Service - 4 stars
Food - 3 stars
Price/value - 3 stars

I really loved the decor and atmosphere of the restaurant. The bar is beautiful, and the restaurant as a whole is way more spacious than I thought it'd be.

Here are the items I tried:
- Blackberry acai margarita
- Jamaican jerk flatbread
- Rib eye with cornbread and slaw
- Macaroni and cheese
- Fish tacos

While I was thrilled to see a specialty margarita on the menu, it simply tasted like water. It wasn't flavorful, and for the ingredients that are listed, I expected more. It didn't taste fruity or have any kick, and I didn't order any other cocktails after that one for fear that they'd be the same. (Though the strawberry mojito was calling my name...)

The jerk flatbread we got as an appetizer was good. I mean, that's where it ends. It was good. It was nothing spectacular or that I'd order again, and really most of the flavor came from the spicy sauce that was on it. There was hardly any chicken!

My rib eye itself was tasty, but the jalapeno cornbread was awful. First of all, it wasn't jalapeno cornbread. It was plain old cornbread with some jalapeno butter on top. It wasn't spicy in the least, and the cornbread itself was dry and crumbly. I didn't finish it, and my husband was equally unimpressed. Cornbread should be moist, and if you're calling it "jalapeno cornbread," it should probably have at least a LITTLE spice to it.

The macaroni and cheese was also very boring. It was literally just elbow macaroni with some cheese. There was no seasoning or flare to it. I think even my little nephews were underwhelmed with it.

That was a trend throughout the entire night, though, and my main gripe with this place. NOTHING WAS SEASONED!! I get that they're trying to keep things healthy - under 500 calories and perhaps low sodium - but it just didn't do anything for me. My husband, who had the fish tacos, was also equally underwhelmed.

Frankly, when I go out to a restaurant I want the food to be better than what I could cook at home. This is not the case here. I know I could go to my local farmer's market, procure the same items, and make copycat dishes with waaaaaaaaaaaaaay more flavor. Even if they're trying to stay away from salt, there are tons of seasonings that could be used to lend more flavor to these dishes. 

I am bummed that Harvest wasn't the party in my mouth that I hoped it would be.

I came to Blue Corn after asking a friend where to go to eat before going to a show at Boot and Saddle. He said that the food was on-point, and after reading the Yelp reviews, I thought it was definitely worth at shot.

My favorite thing that I ordered here was actually a special - short rib tostadas. They. Were. BANGIN!!!

The main thing I have to say about this joint, besides the food being pretty authentic, is that the service was impeccable. My water glass was always full, the dirty plates were promptly removed, and the bathroom was spotless.

My husband and I ordered four dishes here and three drinks, and our bill was only $62.00. This spot is definitely worth a try :)

Wow-eeee. This place is GOOD!

The folks at my office got a large take-out order to celebrate our co-worker's birthday. We got a wide range of things - from soups, to salads, to appetizers, to entrees. Everyone loved everything they got! I didn't hear one complaint from anyone.

Their thousand layer bread with potato dipping sauce is to die for. It's so spicy and delicious, I just couldn't believe how yummy it was. Definitely don't skip it!

The crab rangoons were amazing. I thought "oh, these will be good" but then when I bit into the filling I realized that they were really, really, really, REALLY good. I didn't even need any of the dipping sauce that came with them.

I was sad that their online menu didn't have the Northern Burmese Noodles as an option to order - because that's what I really wanted - but I got the rice stick noodles instead. They were spicy and delicious, so it all worked out.

I'm down with Rangoon. I'll definitely return.

An outstanding greasy-spoon diner. Their breakfast sandwiches can't be beat. Their cheesesteaks are greasy, filling, and delicious (including the vegan cheesesteak!). And they've got Carrot Cake Man Carrot Cake on the counter! A hidden gem on Baltimore Ave.

A more than decent selection of vegetarian friendly food to go along with the bevy of beverages makes this a wonderful addition to the neighborhood.  There isn't really anything like it in this part of St. Pete and the hours make it extremely convenient to stop by before or after hitting up one of the nearby breweries. 

Unfortunately I didn't get to try the coffee since I already had some with me, but they use Java Planet's beans so they have to be pretty decent.  The atmosphere is very welcoming and the staff is extremely friendly.  Take a look at their menu online and stop by for brunch, lunch or maybe just to hang out for a bit and enjoy some coffee.

Only OK. Got home delivery, so maybe that was part of it.  Salad only average. Greens were cut, with hard cores left in. Pasta was average. There are better options, including on South Street. Core de Roma is better.

I heard a good recommendation for this place as far as breakfast, and boy oh boy, they were right! We started off with a chai latte and the fresh orange juice. You can never go wrong with fresh orange juice! And the chai latte was the perfect amount of richness and chai topped with cinnamon on the foam. 

We ordered chicken fried steak with a biscuits and gravy and the seafood Benedict! My husband generally compliments food in two phrases. "It's good for Reno" or "it's really good." Both entrees were really good, and not just "good for reno" lol.

My husband was browsing on yelp looking for a place to enjoy breakfast, but to be honest, my husband only really looks at pictures & we both know he was hunting down for a Chicken Fried Steak w/ biscuits and gravy picture... and he came to this pic. We were a bit confused what kind of food they serve, but it's pretty obvious when you get there (plenty of parking btw). You'll see sombreros on the wall & Spanish employees & Spanish decor BUT you can tell that they wanted to cater to the American folk & that's why there's corn dogs, steak and eggs, fries, soups, & salads etc lol. There's no specialty thing they're known for, they just pretty much have a lil bit of errrything. Enjoy :)

Service was much bien y me gusta mucho. I wouldn't mind coming again!

Hehe + an evil laugh. This place is my guilty pleasure.. mainly because I order the fattiest plates here. For starters, I get the bulaklak (fried intestine), Lechon (fried pork, Kare kare (peanut butter beef stew), lumpia (frie egg rolls), pancit (Filipino pan fried noodles), etc... see what I mean! Fried everything! Mwuahaha! And it all tastes amazing! 

Tip #1: Get taro milk tea with boba to flush the grease down your throat.... get 2 taro milk teas actually. It's delicious, you won't regret it. 

Tip #2: Service is a hit or miss & the drinks/bar isn't always available

I took my sister to The Catbird Seat for her birthday celebration.  This restaurant is situated right next to The Patterson House (a bar).  To get to the restaurant, you go through the lower level door and wait until a hostess pops out from the elevator.  Then, you go up the elevator and then are seated around a U-shaped kitchen.  Chef Trevor Moran is the jefe and you watch him and his team prepare your meal while you watch the whole thing.  You reserve only through their online booking system, 3 days in advance (you better get your finger clickers ready as they open 12 midnight, central time).  You can't find the menu online as the Chef dictates what is being offered for that dinner.  Our server was Adam (repping IL!), who was a little MIA, but our water and plates were always cleared away from the hostess/chefs themselves (kind of like a team effort).  We started off with a radish/daikon-wrapped prawn; nettles and a quail egg yolk in a black 'tea soup,' which came with a nice crispy bacon flavor; a pork (tail) sandwich on a grilled bread that was done on a traditional Japanese grill (for yakitori); a bundle of salad tied with twine with pecan and butter (and, yes, one lady at another party actually ate the twine!); baby potato soup that was cooked 'al dente' which was quite delicious; skate wing that was light and delicate; fresh beef carpaccio that melted in your mouth; 'Old Meat, Young Nuts' - roasted duck breast, asparagus, which was delicious and cooked well; Beer and Cheese with bar nuts (one of my favorites of the night as the cheese 'mousse' was very airy and savory with the sweet crunchy cracker); Strawberries and Cream; goat's milk ice cream with black locust flower; a potato 'cake' in a potato-stamped brown bag (potato mash with marzipan and chocolate 'dirt'; this was actually dense and it really looked like a big potato in there - so freaking hilarious, I almost died laughing); and, ending the night with macarons.  We each even received a hand-written menu of the items for the night.  I love the chefs there, as they were organized, systematic, kept their stations clean, meticulous, and had a great sense of humor, and were all so friendly and awesome.  Heart heart heart Chef Moran and his team (I had a mini crush on all of them); it was a great and cool dining experience in Nashville! Plus, they have a cute saying - 'Sittin' pretty in the Catbird seat' :D

+seated at the U-shaped kitchen
+love the chefs :D

This has been one of my favorite places in Reno since I moved out here for my freshmen year of college. It's close enough from the campus to walk to and cheap enough for the broke college students who can't stand campus food! 

I have tried a lot of pho broths in my young life (all over Las Vegas and homemade) and G-Flower's broth has this distinct, yet authentic, flavor that has me denying pho at any other Vietnamese restaurant I go to. They got me hooked.

I have never had a bad customer service experience here, probably because they know my face by now, but I have never seen them treat anybody differently. Sometimes I wish they would come by and refill my water more often, BUT I think it's a good thing, so I can have more room in my stomach to finish my food. 

G-flower reminds me of a fast casual restaurant. People tend to forget that the quick service, no small talk, and "just eat and go" mentality comes with the Vietnamese culture! 

Lastly, I'm pretty sure the employees are professionals at handling drunk and hungover people, because this is the hot spot for majority of college students after a night of drinking!
This is one of my favorite Mexican restaurants and really the only good one that I know about in the Brandon area. Its fast service great food with fair prices. Don't miss the cheese dip!

Edited review:  
I stopped in for lunch and found a nice environment, friendly service, and had a great "Carolina BBQ" sandwich.  I'd originally rated it 5 stars based on that.

I then went  for dinner with a friend; we both agreed that the food was good, but the portion size slid it over into a "not a good value" category.  A medium pile of pulled pork, and a small (1/2 cup?) sized dish of cole slaw, and a 1/3 cup of collard greens for $12 is pretty expensive.  My friend had ribs, and got served 4 (for $14, I believe).  Add a couple of iced teas, and we were at a $36 meal, with tip.  That was just too much for what we got, and where we had it.

Let me break it down for you... here lies the best review I can offer for Casa Ramos:

Our story begins the way many of my stories begin... I was being a cheapskate.  I bought the Groupon with the intention of dashing in there, getting my cheap on, filling my belly, and never coming back... no lie... we've all been that jerk so stop judging me... let's move on...

There might be a place down the road that I had flag-shipped as my favorite Mexican restaurant in Tampa for SIXTEEN YEARS.  Today = paradigm shift... Casa Ramos was so amazing that I've forgotten all about that other place... they win.  Period.

Enter the Gino factor... Gino took ownership of my night, a maitre'D of sorts.  He seemed to be born and bred for the purpose of creating incredible dining experiences.  He led me down a most adventurous culinary path, whilst offering me valuable suggestions in order to narrow down his favorites amongst a HUGE selection of dishes.  The most spectacular advice Gino offered me, however, was not to fill up on the chips and salsa... he was correct.  The portion of the entrées were beyond huge, but not as big a the flavor the dishes offered.

Imagine a slow-cooked pork burrito that melts in your mouth.  My mom is a chef, so I've been eating amazing foods for a long time, but I have no other way to explain this burrito other than the damn thing melts in your mouth.  Pork that falls apart on your tongue and is so jam-packed with flavor you will start crying... and not the fake "let's be funny in front of friends" crying... I'm talking honest to God "I wept because there had to be an end to this meal" crying. 

Did you read the part about Gino?  I really want you to understand that part... He honestly cared about the customer's overall food experience.  Remember when I eluded to him leading me down the path of Mexicano righteousness?  Yeah, good... because that's important.  Everyone else was awesome too, lots of warm, family vibe, but Gino - listen to him... he knows what you want even if you don't know what you want...  I'm serious... his name is Gino... okay, moving on...

So then the carne asada and shrimp ajo come out.  People, you know how you just usually skip the rice portion of the Mexican dishes?  Not this time... even the rice by itself was amazing.  Additionally, most Mexican places over-season their carne asada to cover up the fact that the meat is under-par.  Not the case at Casa Ramos.  The carne asada was simply cooked to perfection using minimal spices, bringing out the true taste of a perfect steak.  Paired with the shrimp ajo... more crying commenced... I was an emotional wreck... In fact, I'm crying right now as I type this.  The shrimp ajo was served with a perfect sauce of mushrooms, spices, and (from what I can make of it) something that causes erections. 

Simply put, if you are looking for the BEST Mexican food in Tampa Bay... welcome to Casa Ramos.  I am still cheap and will never miss an opportunity to purchase a Casa Ramos Groupon, however, I'm going back as much as I can - even if this cheapskate has to pay full price... it's WORTH EVERY PENNY!

(When using a Groupon - don't be one of those cheap SOB's that tips on the discounted price... tip on the full amount it WOULD'VE been, you punks!) 
:-)

Global makes me realize how lucky I am to be living in St. Louis. People from bigger cities lament the fact that oh, we don't really have a Ktown here or even a respectable Chinatown...or that we have a handful of Mexican eateries instead of 9 blocks, blah, blah, blah. But the truth is...if you really wanted to find some edible standout in some culture, you probably could make it with some help from Global.

Their produce section is very reasonably priced; the Asian vegetables and the herbs much more so. Sometimes, the "regular" produce is not as fresh as it is at Schnucks or Dierbergs, but there is plenty of thai mint or gai lan or yu choy. 

I love how there is a little bit of everything, and how it is all labeled by cuisines. Except for the cookies and candies: that has its own location right before you hit the produce --the manager is someone after my own heart.

Labne? Turkish cotton candy? Mango chutney? Sauerbraten mix? Kimchi? Puri? Rabbit sausage?? IT'S ALL HERE! And it's so fun to go up and down the aisles and just dump in your cart random things to try and cook. 

This Indian guy who was stocking the Indian snacks saw me poring over the puri and the ready-to-eat samosas. He indicated to me with a raised eyebrow, "The samosas are hot." I chuckled, was like, okay, but how are they? Should I get them or should I get the freezer kind? (BTW, thanks for not telling me to make my own, lol, especially because you saw I had paneer in my cart.). He was like, They're ok. Pause. Then he goes, But you should try the kachori; they are better. LIke how many times have you stood in front of the shelves and wondered, which mandu do those Asian people buy? Or which brand lumpia is the best? Or which samosas would an Indian auntie hope to pass off as her own? What is that orange stuff in the Russian aisle? Those are the questions I always have...and those are the questions that the staff here will answer...or try to find someone who knows. 

Having spent most of the past year in rural areas, it nearly made me cry to see beef tongue. And cut gyro meat. And pelmeni. And headcheese. A whole entire two shelves just devoted to feta. And for what they have, prices are reasonable. 

I just wish they offered threading. I should ask them next time.

Upon further consideration, and after a second visit, I've decided that Crescent Pie and Sausage Co. absolutely deserves the (oh-so-hard-to-get-nowadays-at least) fifth star. Not only because they have THE BEST MAC AND CHEESE ON THE PLANET, but because they're a cute, hip, trendy-ish, new restaurant, they're in Mid-City (on Banks St., in an up-and-coming, already cool location across from Banks St. Bar and Lazaro's), and they actually have vegetarian items on the menu. Unlike some other new, hip, trendy-ish restaurants I know. *cough* Sylvain *cough* Ste. Marie *cough*  But we won't name names. 

That's all. I had another wonderful business "meeting" here today, and it was so good I felt compelled to update my review. 

Five Stars FTW! Way to go, CPSC. You rock, and I heart you.

Oh Verti Marte, I shall always adore you, but it's definitely time to update my overly excited five star rating from right after you re-opened after the fire. 

Thank you for the delicious egg and cheese and tomato po-boy you just made me (best 2am dinner on the planet, IMO). However, next time, please hold the bacon. I definitely didn't order it, and although the sandwich was still edible, nay, rather tasty, I was also starving so even if you'd put a severed finger in my food I probably still would've eaten, even enjoyed it. 

The two other things we really need to talk about are: 

1) The cash-only thing. That's got to stop. Cash is barbaric, archaic, and extremely inconvenient. Having to find an ATM delayed my blissful union with this giant, chewy log of cheese/bread/grease by at least 15 minutes. Not cool. 

2) WHY OH WHY WON'T YOU DELIVER TO ME? You deliver EVERYWHERE ELSE on the freaking planet, but not to my house. Seriously! I'm not that far away! Someone needs to bring me breakfast in the morning! If not to my bed, at least to my front door. 

Please address these concerns, and I will happily consider restoring your previous five star rating. Oh, how I wish you cared.

I've never reviewed Delachaise? Really? Totally thought I did. Well then, let's fix that...

Okay, so I'm going to sound like a hypocrite/asshole/douchebag for saying this, and apologies to the many people who I'm about to offend, but Delachaise is one of those places that I really really like, except for the crowd. Not crowd as in it's always packed, but as in, I like the space, I like to go, but I'm not a huge fan of the people who go there. Ridiculous? Perhaps. Still true, though. 

My favorite thing about Delachaise is their round the world wine special, or whatever it's called. Every day they feature a different wine -- one red and one white -- and for $5 you can get a little decanter thingy (which is the same thing as ordering a glass of wine, but more fancypants to get it in a tiny decanter, like you would in Europe). It's always, always good when I order it, to the point that I never even bother to look at their (extensive to the point it's mind boggling) menu of wines, beers, and booze.

I'm surprised I haven't reviewed Little Tokyo before, because I used to come here a lot. It's been a while, though, and last week was the first time I've ever been here for lunch. And the first time I've done hibachi instead of a normal table. 

Overall, the lunch experience we had the other day was pretty underwhelming. The hibachi chef kept dropping stuff, which is totally fine (everybody screws up sometimes), but was a little bit awkward and embarrassing. Fortunately, no one caught fire. At least, not while we were there. 

We sat at a table with a bunch of random strangers, so you don't have to have a certain number of people to do hibachi, as long as you don't mind sharing a table. It's also possible to order sushi off the regular menu if you don't want hibachi, which is what I did. They have a great cucumber salad (though this time there weren't enough sesame seeds), and the salmon sashimi I ordered was wayyyy more than I could manage. An order of 2-4 pieces would've been enough, but this was close to triple that amount. 

The service wasn't horrible, but it took a while to get our check, and they never picked up the dirty dishes, so we had to stare at the post-meal carnage the whole time we waited for our server to re-appear, and waited some more for her to bring us the check. 

Next time I come here, I think I'll go back to my usual dinner in the not-hibachi room plan, and see if it's what I remember. If it's not, I probably wouldn't bother to come back.

Adore this little Vietnamese bakery, and am very glad to have been introduced to it, since it's hidden not only in a strip mall but is also located on the westbank. 

My knowledge of their baked goods is somewhat limited, due to the fact that I always get the same few things when I'm there -- specifically, croissants, the cream cheese ones are unfreakingbelieveable -- and thus can't speak to how good their bread is, for example. However, my native New Orleanian ex-boyfriend swears they have THE best King Cakes in the city. I've had them, they're great, but since I've only lived here 10 years (And didn't even try king cake for the first 6. No, I do not know WTF was wrong with me.) I hesitate to weigh in on the best king cake debate.

However, they DO have king cakes shaped like crawfish and lobsters and stuff, which I've always wanted to get, but they're kind of expensive. Around $30 maybe? 

Ordinarily, I would give a place 4 stars for being cash only (and on the Westbank, no less!) but once when I happened to be across the river and remembered to stop by Hi-Do, I bought a bunch of stuff and forgot they were cash only. The total was $12 something and I only had about $10. The lady behind the counter totally gave me the whole box anyway, which I thought was a particularly kind gesture. 

Seriously, this place is worth a trip to the Westbank in and of itself. Go find it. I'll be waiting patiently for your "Thank you for changing my life!" compliment/message. (And I'm waiting eagerly for the few of you who are SO grateful you'll bring me a cream cheese croissant. Hint hint. ;)

Go!

OMG I love this place. So much so that I cannot believe I haven't written a review for it yet. What a slacker I've been! For shame. Merchant is totally the venue of my dreams when it comes to a place I can go if I need to get out of the house and work. It has EVERYTHING.

All the other coffee shops and bars I frequent for quality time with my laptop have one or more failings - small tables, too few outlets, inconvenient hours, inconvenient location, no caffeine, no booze, crappy wifi. However, Merchant has everything I could want from a coffee shop. And then some. First of all, the space is gorgeous. I feel like I'm in another city, somewhere in Europe, because the design is very, well, designed. In a good way. You'll see what I mean when you step inside. 

The coffee they serve, Illy, is a fantastic brand. High octane and delicious. And perfectly prepared by extremely friendly, helpful and customer-oriented staff. Everyone I've encountered at Merchant has been a delight, which is certainly not always the case at most places.

In addition to great coffee, they serve food (I've had breakfast, lunch AND dinner there by now, since they're open all day until 8pm), and although I haven't tried it yet, I know they serve booze (because what else could "grapes" stand for in the "Coffee, Crepes, Grapes" that serves as their tagline). Speaking of crepes, I'm so glad to have somewhere other than the places Uptown to get a nutella filled crepe when I have a craving. All places should sell nutella crepes, but that's another story.

So. Merchant has coffee, food, booze, and ambiance. The attention to detail is apparent in the way the tables are set up in the corridor area (just off the main bar where you place your order), because each table has power outlets next to it on the floor, and there are potted plants that serve as dividers between the tables, which afford some privacy if you're there for a meeting (or just don't like people staring at you when you're hunched over the computer, posting status updates to Facebook about how you should really be working). The wifi connection is good, in my experience. On top of all that, the tables themselves are large, so you've got plenty of room even if you've got coffee, plates of food, and two laptops spread out in front of you. Which I know because I've tried this. 

Cannot tell you how happy I am to have found THE perfect coffee shop for the freelancer who sometimes wants to be around people (instead of cats) and wear real clothes (instead of pajamas). This is definitely a place I can spend hours and hours being productive, without having to leave for food/coffee/functioning internet, etc. Hooray for Merchant! You'll be seeing me there again soon.

Stopped by Three Muses last night and had probably the best time I've ever had on Frenchmen Street, at least in recent memory. I've been here several times since they opened, and it's always been great, but last night was truly magical. The music was FREAKING AWESOME (check out Sarah Quintata, she's incredible. Buying her CD was $10 well spent. The album is called Tail of a Whale.)

There are so many reasons I love Three Muses, it's hard to know where to begin. First of all, it's on Frenchmen Street, and therefore convenient, because I already spend a lot of time there. Secondly, the decor is upscale, classy, elegant. Makes you feel like you've wandered through some kind of portal and ended up on another planet. This is only reinforced when you leave the cool, quiet, laid-back-and-winding-down Three Muses toward the end of a set, only to emerge on the relative chaos of Friday night Frenchmen Street festivities. It's hard to go home when there are battling brass bands up the street. 

Great drinks! I had the Blueberry Bellini (okay, several) and everyone who saw it wanted one, for good reason. The food is equally fantastic, though I've not had a chance to try most of it so far. Guess I'll have to keep going back... ;)

For some reason, I always assumed this place was a tourist trap, and more or less avoided it. However, I ended up here for a drink after a wedding in the French Quarter recently, and was surprised to find that it's a really interesting place. Someone told me it's the second oldest bar in the French Quarter. No idea if that's actually true (I tend to believe anything anyone tells me these days, so when it comes to relaying facts I'm probably not the most reliable source), but it definitely seems like it could be. 

If you've never been, it's worth stopping in here for a drink or two, to check out the bar. And the very large, very old collection of dusty bottles of...some kind of booze. They have them in a display case in the bar area.

It is one block from my apartment and I couldn't be happier. One price coffee - $2 La Colombe Corsica, which sits well in my book. The space is small, as Carmen's was, so if you want brunch there'll be a wait. But their menu is awesome and inventive, with everything titled in a crusades/holy grail theme. 
I'll be frequenting this place as much as I can - IF I can score a table, of course. Cash only for now, be forewarned. The open kitchen is a plus, as you can see and talk to the lady chef and owner personally. Not one bad thing to say here.

We headed to Vinnie's for lunch and I could not be more impressed.  The menu is chock full of options but I had been looking forward to the Italian beef sandwich, so my decision was made.  I also got a side of the fried potatoes.

The sandwich was amazing.  The beef and juice was so flavorful.  The peppers added just the right amount of heat but there was additional hot sauce available  if you enjoy more heat.  I was really impressed.with the roll as well.  It had a great crusty outside and a soft mushy inside.  

The potatoes were amazing as well.  Golden brown and topped with parmesian cheese.  You could use ketchup on these but they don't need them.  They are better left alone.  I definitely need to come back and try the gyro and the dogs.  Everything looked amazing.

Well, it is a shame that I no longer live in the neighborhood because I am positive that I would live at Vinnie's.  I am excited for the folks living in the old stomping grounds.

Even if you don't live nearby, do yourself a favor and get to Vinnie's.

So far, so excellent. Everything I've tasted here is incredible! Where else can you go to have nachos as an appetizer and Pho as an entree? Seriously. And their nachos are DELICIOUS. EVERY chip is doused in gooey, tasty cheese with the meat and salsa of your choice. We've had both the pork and steak options! 

Being an indecisive (yet creative) group of friends, we each ordered different tacos and pulled the old switcharoo so we could try each one. I must say, I gravitated more toward the pork tacos and the fish tacos. Each selection was prepared differently, with varying toppings and sauces. The steak was VERY tasty, however, it was almost too high quality and flavorful for tacos? I liked it so much, I could've just ditched the tortilla and had the steak. That being said, I'm sure the steak frites are incredible!

Their beer and specialty cocktail selections are seasonal and quite delightful. They rotate their draughts frequently, but the flavors have always been consistent. 

I'll end on this note: I had the Pho here twice (wait for it...) in one day. Breakfast AND dinner...and had no shame in doing so. 

Please keep the deliciousness of my favorite hangover cure here Pho-ever.

This was my second visit about a year after my first. My only regret is not coming back sooner. Made a reservation so being seated was seamless and I didn't have to wait. We sat in the bar area where the street-level windows were open, which was lovely aside from the shirtless drunk tourist wandering around next to us. 

I used the Yelp check-in coupon to get free fried pickles...they were amazing. I'd gladly pay for them. We also ordered the bacon queso and chips, which was alright, but nothing to write home about.

Both of my friends ordered burgers and LOVED them. I ordered the hot chicken...GOODNESS GRACIOUS. It was FAR superior to anything from the other hot chicken joints around Nashville that I've patronized. I ordered the mid-level spice ("Hot") and it was just right. Hot enough that I consumed a lot of water, but not so hot that I couldn't eat and enjoy it. It was a huge boneless breast with a honey drizzle, and was served atop a bit of slaw and a delicious, perfectly textured corn cake. I could only finish half, so I took the rest home and put it in the fridge. When I took it out to have for lunch today, it was still perfectly crunchy, which I consider to be some sort of fried chicken magic. They do something magical to their chicken...I think maybe they brine it in pickle juice, along with some sort of ritual. The breading is perfect and held the hot sauce/honey mixture perfectly without getting soggy. At $11.99 for the chicken, slaw, corn cake, and amazing bourbon mashed sweet potatoes, it is a great value for the money. As an aside, our server was very nice, kept our drinks full, and everything was well-timed. I love this joint and cannot wait to try their rave-inducing brunch. Thanks for being awesome, Row folks.

I always eat at chicken and watermelon until today. Me and my sister ordered a 15 piece combo and wanted Cajun creole and hit with Cajun ranch fries and a extra Cajun ranch fries. Our fries had no ranch on it whatsoever and our wings were all wrong instead of getting the 2 flavors we ordered we received one flavor. When we called to inform them our order was incorrect the young lady over the phone said no that's what you ordered and she didn't hear the other flavor or the fact we wanted Cajun ranch fries with extra ranch. She didn't even offer for us to bring the order back since it was obvious I was order was incorrect. We don't even know the flavor we have because it's nothing that we've had before. I now know why I haven't been eating there often due to the lack of orders being correct and the poor customer service and to say I live less than 5 minutes I would rather drive to other places after today. So disappointed at this current moment it's just ridiculous.

My friends and I decided to have dinner at Superior Seafood last week. 

At this point, I cannot recommend it. If you'd like a quiet meal, do know the place is filled with a gazillion big screen television all blaring sports. No table is immune or far away; this is not fine dining or a place to have a meeting, date or an important meal.

We ordered several dishes but finished none.

This restaurant seems intent to garner the Cheesecake Bistro/Copeland's set. 
All butter and salt, all the time. MEGA salt- and I don't mind a bit of salt, but I also won't touch Copeland's.

The Pimm's cup was made with simple syrup, lots of it. It was insanely sweet.
Sugar is not an ingredient in a Pimm's cup. It's a refreshing drink made with ginger ale, apples, and cucumber. After diluting it with half a glass of water, it was quite good. 

As an appetizer, we ordered the Le Grande Maison Platter, dubbed the Maisonnaise platter by our table, a sampler of Shrimp Remoulade, and one each of Shrimp and Crawfish Maison? It arrived, beautifully presented and garnished. Heaping portions of plump fresh shrimp (just slightly undercooked) and crawfish, all in mayonnaise based sauces surrounding a center pile of greens. 

It was far too salty to eat. We tried. However, although all of us were starving, we left it. It was also served with thin French bread croutons, greasy, so doused in butter and salt, they also remained on the plate. The sauces themselves are too close to each other to review separately. I also have to question the wisdom of an appetizer sampler where everything tastes the same, looks the same, and is covered in a similar pale pink mayonnaise sauce. 

The bowls of Gumbo were a rich brown, smelled delicious, and were obviously made with a dark roux and a strong stock; they seemed a quality dish (albeit, the only seafood seems to be crabmeat in the thick broth, this is not a seafood filled gumbo, but more a thick soup).
However, we couldn't eat it at all - MEGA SALT. 

The spinach dip, SALT, we left it and moved on. Better at a dozen other restaurants.

The small Sensation salads were a perfect side salad, simple greens, cherry tomatoes, goat cheese, and a lemony vinaigrette, which as we were now really starving we devoured with the plain french bread on the table.

I can't speak for the other dishes as I didn't want to try them. However, no one ate more than a 1/3 and refused a take home box- SALT

I ordered the Bourbon Marinaded Shrimp and vegetable kabobs over grits and corn. The entire dish looked beautiful. The first bite of the shrimp was delicious; the marinade was a deep brown, rich glaze with many notes, the shrimp were cooked perfectly, the grits were creamy, some of the best in town, the corn was also delicious, HOWEVER, before the 2nd bite, the SALT hit me again. I tried to eat this dish, but could not. 

We fled to Houston and their perfect spinach dip afterward, we were starving.

The bill was $120 for three with no dessert. A bit high for casual dining.
We dub thee Superior Salt Palace.

Service:

The hostesses seemed clueless, over five stared at us for a few moments with no greeting (we were the only people there). However, it's the first week, and they were all young and sweet. 

The waiter and bus person were beyond excellent.

The decor misses in odd ways. Advice - don't look up and sit by a window.

They created a perfect turn of the century room, very much a men's club, all dark wood, and mirrors, it all works together nicely, until you notice the lighting and ceiling. The lighting is fluorescent! We were bathed in white office light???
The room is hung with long fluorescent lights straight out of Touro Infirmary's Operating Room. Beautiful art deco pieces that don't match anything else in the room. An odd choice of lighting and fixture.

The worst is the old tin ceiling. Someone thought it a good idea to ruin a beautiful tin ceiling with a Tuscan orange faux paint finish, more hideous lit with fluorescent lighting and inexplicable over a New Orleans old world Galatoire's/Cafe du Monde decor.

Avoid until they run out of salt.

Avoid until they replace the management.

Hostess vague, half asleep, uninformative, inattentive staff.

Arrived, given 20 minute wait time. Half the tables were empty, most dirty. Every table was eating except for two small tables. The wait area was covered in dirty cups, crumpled napkins. The lavatory was semi-flooded, obviously not attended to all day. Filthy. 

The busboy walked as though a zombie, ignoring the dirty tables as did the entire staff, the waitresses were slow, seemed hungover, carrying one cup at at time, etc.. no concept of combining steps, staring about the room, chatting, not really waiting tables. No teamwork at all. 

The hostess stared at the dirty tables in front of her for half an hour. The girl behind the counter made a half-hearted attempt to wipe down a long, dirty and empty counter, but gave up half way leaving the condiments askew for the next hour and half the crumbs waiting for the next customers. She also was doing NOTHING. The staff was over 7, plus a manager and none were working.

After 15 minutes of this and watching several families and couples walk-out vocally annoyed, rather than continuing to be ignored, I asked why no one was being seated. The hostess, vague, replied that the kitchen was backed up.
Only 50% full and only two tables without entrees. Hmmm....

Asked to speak to the manager. He was about as charming as a JFK taxi driver, rude, indifferent and walked away after he replied that he refused to seat people with a kitchen 45 minutes in the weeds. Hmmm...... not even close to true. He was also never in the kitchen helping, just walking about chatting casually, joking, ignoring the incensed customers and the dirty tables.

Eventually seated. 

Very nice but bizarre waitress, forgot half the order.
I ordered Eggs Benedict, the whites were uncooked and inedible on one, overcooked on the others. Very salty, small portion.

My friend ordered a simple eggs, grits, bacon breakfast. Waitress forgot the grits. Never checked back once after delivering food, which took forever.  Finally flagged her down halfway through meal. She was unconcerned that she forgot part of the order, then returned to inform us the grits out, but were being cooked, 10 minutes later she brought them as she cleared the table. No refills, no water. Very thirsty  breakfast considering how salty everything was prepared. All in all, horrid manager, staff untrained and asleep at the wheel, high prices, long wait, small portions. Food average.

Skip

My wife and I enjoyed a nice evening at Lucky's.  It's certainly one of the more popular fine dining restaurants in the Montecito area.  On this particular Friday evening the crowd was predominantly older, and seemed to be regulars.

There are various options on where to sit, the bar area, the main dining room, or the outside patio.  On the night that we visited it was raining, so we opted for the dining room, near the fireplace which has a classic 'rat pack' picture hanging above it - see my picture.
 
Our server was 'Brenda T' who was a joyous lady, she could not have been more pleasant.  She was patient with our numerous questions and had a good handle on the menu.  My wife started with a Lemon Drop martini which was divine, and it should have been considering the $17 price tag, I enjoyed a much less refined, Stella Artois draft.       
My wife and I both enjoyed their bread basket and also got an artichoke to start.  The artichoke had an excellent wood grilled taste and was prepared to perfection, 'A' grade. We also got the potato skins which was a large offering, 'B+'

We LOVED the entrée options, my blackened salmon was excellent and my wife equally enjoyed her NY strip.  Overall, the place felt special and delivered on charm and service.
We had big law school event here Friday February 27, 2015 and many people who went to the event had food poisoning over the weekend. Our event was in the upstairs dining room.

Best ice cream in Philly and completely deserving of its 5 star rating! This place has the unique Asian flavors I'm always craving, with my personal favorites being the pandan, taro, and lychee rose. It has a rotating array of flavors on display, but pandan and taro seem to be staples. The scoops are incredibly generous, and my preferred order is one scoop of ice cream in a flavored cone (highly recommend birthday cake or lavender). I regret going so long without ordering the flavored cone. With one scoop you get one free topping and drizzle, so I always go for the mochi and condensed milk. I only wish this place were more accessible to my apartment but I'm even willing to make the 1 hour walk for quality ice cream!

I'm writing the most basic 1-star review for The Mud House, because it literally was that - basic.

The backstory: What drew me to stop here were previous Yelp reviews and mentions of house-made marshmallows. I had a game plan and was ready to go in, order my hot cocoa with the marshmallow!

After waiting maybe 15-20 minutes in line, I was finally up and about to order. I asked about the marshmallow, but the cashier said, "Oh we stopped making those," then looked at me to order. No explanation or "sorry about that." Luckily, I had a second order in mind. I ordered a flavored latte, and my bf ordered a cold-brew plus we had two Topo Chicos. No big deal. The bill came out to about $14. Okay. So we take our little sign, so my latte could be delivered to my table and walk away.

I was upset, but this is not why I'm giving this place 1-star.

The place was nice and Jam-Packed, but I still tried looking for a seat. No seats were available. At this point I was frustrated and opted to sit outside. Whatever. 
We sat outside for maybe 5 minutes and then checked inside again for seats where it was warmer. Luckily we found a couple of of those high-chair seats against a tall wall table. By that point I think 10 minutes had passed and still no latte. Another 10 minutes. STILL. NO. LATTE. 

I finally went to the counter 5 feet away from us and asked the barista what was going on. She looked at me, shrugged, and said, "I didn't get that ticket," then continued to make someone else's coffee. I, at the least, expect her to ask me for my receipt, and let me know she'd have it out. Instead, the lady who took our order asked me what was up and I explained to her that I had not received my coffee. It took way to long to get a coffee out. I ended up taking it to go.

Lack of good customer service is the greatest pet peeve of mine when taking my business to anyone.

It's not hard. 

Never going back here.

As my boyfriend who works across the street from Le Tejana Taqueria put it,l "I never even thought about coming here because the outside looks questionable, but this food is amazing."

After searching for restaurants near the Funny Bone, Le Tajana won.  This place is in the middle of a sketchy looking strip mall that is filled with Latino stores.  Must be good food if it's surrounded by similar stores.  The food was cheap and fantastic.  Margaritas were amazing and not overwhelmingly tequila flavored. The chips are crispy and the salsa tastes like it was made in house.  I ordered an El Pastor Taco which is pork and pineapple with a side of rice.

I could only give 4 stars because the decor was minimal and nothing special.  Of course food is the most important part of the meal and was delicious.  I will most definitely be coming back.

One of my favorite cocktail bars in America. 

The menu is hand crafted and has the biggest variety of surprises I have ever seen. They make everything they possibly can in house including house made sodas, syrups etc. 

See full cocktail menu here: http://bluebeardindy.com/libations/cocktails/

We've had quite a few cocktails here over the years, but most recently:

Bee's Knees: bone dry gin, lemon, honey, lavender bitters 10
Galapagos: alipus mezcal, cabeza tequila, chili arbol syrup, bluebeard orgeat, cucumber, lime 11 (helllllllo Mezcal! If you are a mezcal fan this will flip your world upside down. Highly recommend!) 

And an off menu cocktail made with arugula. We came here maybe four years ago and this cocktail knocked my socks off. This time, I cozied up to the bar and asked, "Hiii I know this is really crazy but I came here and ordered an arugula cocktail once, and it was the best I've ever..." Interupts - "arugula yeah, the Zabrowski - let me see if the kitchen has any and I will make it for you." Me: OMG. DEAD. 

I believe his name was Mark? He is the one who curates the bar menu. He made it for me, and no joke I almost started crying. It was such a special memory for me. We came here when we were so young and this cocktail seriously made me fall in love with cocktails. It changed the way I think about them, and what they should / shouldn't be. I will never forget it, down to the booth we were sitting in. 

Thanks for the incredible hospitality Bluebeard, I will never forget you and I will scream from the rooftops how f*cking awesome you are.

From the beginning our experience was awkward. There is not really a host so we thought we needed to seat ourselves along with 3-4 other groups behind us, turns out after we are almost seated a person comes over and tells us we need to wait to be seated and apologizes for not being at the door. Ok so about 6-8 people go all the way back to the door, squeeze in and block everyone trying to get out of their booths to leave. 

We are then seated. I ordered a bee's knees, hubs ordered a whiskey flight. It took no joke, around 20 minutes for us to get our drinks. When we did my bees knees was warm and unappetizing. Also it was a little unbalanced for my taste. A simple cocktail like this needs to be properly executed, and it was too sweet, and not tart enough. 

We ordered a chicken biscuit and fries. The chicken biscuit came out at lightning speed. No fries. We assumed they were coming, and then we didn't see out server until my food and drink was finished. She brought the check and there were no fries on it, so instead of even correcting her, we just left. 

The chicken was good, the biscuit was good, but like my favorite chef always says, "you come for the food, you stay for the service." After being almost completely forgotten about, I don't think I will be coming back here to spend my money.

Came here because this place seemed promising for some good coffee and empanadas! Unfortunately, they only had quiche and no empanadas on the day I came but still a very cute coffee shop nonetheless!! 

The coffee shop is way bigger than it looks from the outside. They even have a back patio that offers cornhole, jenga, and ping pong. I would totally come here to study or hang out with friends. Love everything about the vibe here!!

SERVICE: The baristas themselves looked like a family owned business (not sure, wish I asked). Mom and pop coffee shop vibes for sure either way, which are my favorite! They were very timely with making our drinks and friendly as well!

ICED LATTE: This was good as well and came out exactly as I expected.

MATCHA LATTE: Loved this and appreciated how this wasn't sweet at all! You can really enjoy the matcha flavor the way it is. I can see it being a little bitter for those who enjoy sweet things, but they also offer sugar/syrup to add on the side if you prefer to. 

Next time I come, I want to try the chai latte since that was the barista's favorite order!

I've been to Mokabe's approximately a dozen times in the past seven years-- always with a friend / date / small group, just to get coffee or small plate.
My review is based on consistent experiences at this coffee house, and although it's subjective, I feel like having consistently experienced the same negativity each and every time, it was worth finally writing a review.
The good:.... maybe the hours? It seems to be open every time I drive by.
The bad: Where do I start? The staff is a hodge podge mix of characters with appearances ranging from " surely-must-be-homeless"  to "got lost looking for Starbucks". The attitudes are not as diverse, and likewise the service is somehow even worse. Everyone has a bad attitude, everyone acts like they're too cool to do their jobs or they're so overwhelmed by their simple tasks that they couldn't possibly function if they weren't about to get paid. The service is nonexistent. I really mean that, nonexistent. On two separate occasions a guest in my small group asked if there were nuts or soy or some other allergen in a treat they were buying-- each time a server droned out a monotone negatory response-- and EACH TIME someone in my party had to take benadryl or use a freaking epi-pen because they had an allergic reaction to the ingredient the staff claimed wasn't in there. What this says to me is that either: A) your kitchen is so disorganized and dirty that you don't clean up between making things and ingredients get into everything.... or B) your staff is so braindead that they can't even remember important things like that or don't have the conscience to ASK a cook. Either way, it's irresponsible and dangerous, and you're lucky no one sues you or dies from something like that.
The last time I was in there, I came by myself because I wanted a quiet place to read before I went to a meeting. I was surprised when, after a few minutes, staff started arguing with a (legitimate) homeless person-- staff were yelling at the person to leave and even called the police. It blew my mind because they kept advertising themselves as this haven safe from judgment and cruelties of the world-- but I guess that only applies to LGBT customers? 
You couldn't pay me to come back here. The staff is absolutely miserable, the food is always dried out/hard or soggy, drinks are never mixed right, and if you have any food allergies-- bring an epi-pen or tell your hipster friends you want to go to a real restaurant. South Grand is full of incredible small businesses-- the hypocrisy and bad service make Mokabe's a terrible waste.
The last thought I'd like to leave you with: I'm personally not interested in getting biased, unethical, questionable politics shoved down my throat every time an election rolls around.
