That's great that you want to support something-- it's great that you offer a place for LGBT people (like the rest of South Grand and STL?)-- but everyone seems so wrapped up in their own lunacy that they forget for a second that THEY'RE A COFFEE HOUSE.... and a horrible one, at that.

Walking in to the delightful smells of fresh baked pastries andd then seeing these AMAZING creations in the display case...you can't help but want to pick one of each.

Fresh, delicious and tasty baked goods are ahhmazing!! From their everyday menu to Today's Specialty Pastries choosing savory or sweet is the next question you'll be asking yourself when you step up to the counter.

On our latest pop-in we grabbed a Croissant Cinnamon Roll and the Chocolate Bouchon ~ absolutely deLISH!! with herbal mint tea and a latte sitting along the bar/front window enjoy && watch the day unfold outside.

Fantastic pastries, service, located in the heart of Midtown. Limited parking and inside dining but added bonus walking accessible from anywhere in Midtown && outside dining that is dog friendly too.

Be sure to grab a fresh baked pastry or even order online for grab & go. Enjoy!!

Stanley's was the PERFECT place to start our morning, offering a beautiful backdrop of St. Louis Cathedral and downtown New Orleans located on historic Jackson Square close to our next adventure/tour of the day.

Upon entering we were warmly greeted by the hostess offering either indoor or on the Square outside dining options. We chose indoor with a window overlooking everything, handed the yummy menu and our drinks were promptly brought over.

After reviewing the breakfast menu and our server offering up some tasty suggestions we made our decision with, I ordering the:
Eggs Benedict Poor Boy Deluxe w/Poached Eggs, Smoked Acadian Bacon, Poor Boy Bread, Creole Hollandaise, tomato & arugula ~ that was absolutely daBOMB!!
My hubby went with the:
Corned Beef Hash Sunny Side Up w/House Smoked Corn Beef Pastrami, Creole Breakfast Potatoes, Hollandaise, Eggs Sunny Side Up ~ that was OMTASTY GOODNESS!!

Quaint, airy building with lovely views of Jackson Square either inside or out, friendly staff, andd a menu that we could not pass up. This is definitely a good place to enjoy a delicious breakfast (BTW eggs cooked to perfection), sipping your tea or coffee while taking in the day.

Arario Midtown is THE place to go to share flavorful eats!!  Located on Center Street across from Death & Taxes upstairs in a shared building with Noble Pie you walk in greeted warmly by staff or the owner that is always quick to seat you for the best experience.  Service is on point, making GREAT suggestions and allows the experience to shine all around. 

They have signature libations to wet your whistle like the Cherry Bomb that's daBOMB or my hubby gravitates to the Angry Roger that he says is similar to a Manhattan....I lean to my standard a veryyyy Dirty Martini that is always made to absolute PERFECTION.  

Sharing a few or ALL of the Small Plates is a MUST as these are TO DIE FOR!!  Crab Tofu is incredibly delicate, rich and absolutely deLISH!!; The Porky Pops with sweet & spicy K sauce and garlic soy sauce - must I choose because these are TO DIE FOR!! andddd I NEED them errday!!;  Arancini: Breaded kimchee fried rice, cheese, bacon jam, roasted pepper sauce ~ this is just yummilicious goodness!!  All of these small plates are OUT OF THIS WORLD and they have mastered them!!  Definitely enjoy them with everyone in your party as that is the idea but be careful to leave room for an entrée either a Fusion or Classic options - those are OFF THE HOOK!  

My hands down fave is the Hot Pot BibimBop with sizzling rice, veggies, mushrooms, fried egg on top, gochujang sauce on side to add-in for flavorful tasty yumminess and beef or seafood whichever you prefer.  When this yummilicious sizzling bowl comes out you stir all of the ingredients up for deliciously FUN, Bomb.com, dish that will satisfy everyone at the table!!  Added bonus I enjoy watching my dinner guest stirring up the hot pot ingredients quickly as they smell all the yummyyyy goodness - FUN, FUN, FUN!!

Nothing better than to finish a wonderful meal with the sweetness of a wonderful dessert and why not take the suggestion of our trusted server of either Chocolate Lava Bundt Cake - choc - o - lat that runeth over or Hotteok: Korean Sweet Pancake with green tea ice cream that is just cinnamon-y yummilicious goodness!!  

Yep this gal will be back again and again just for those Porky Pops - those are just sinful and I told my hubby that they need to bottle up that sauce...please do NOT interrupt me if you see me eating them...I am in pure rib blissfulness LOL  I digress and say GO here!! Enjoy and look forward to hear what you find to be your fave dish to share or have as your pure blissfulness to yourself - LOL!

Running errands up in Reno, we wanted to grab a good breakfast nearby so we opened up our trusty Yelp app, I spied pictures, reviews and decided on The Cup Café.  Upon arrival although they have their own parking lot we immediately noticed on a Saturday morning they quite busy, but not dissuaded we continued on our course of grabbing our yummilicious breakfast.  We popped in and were warmly greeted by the hostess put us on the 30 minute wait list so we ran across the street to check off one of our errands and when we returned it was our turn on the list.

We were seated, asked what our morning beverage choices would be and we both opted for a mimosa.  I selected the peach and my husband ordered the grapefruit mimosa with waters as we perused the breakfast menu.  After carefully mulling over whether to have one of 'The Classics', 'Benedicts & Scrambles' or 'South of the Border' and boy was the Chili Relleno breakfast calling my name, we made our decision.

My breakfast choice for this Saturday was the Feta Scramble that had spinach, tomato, onion, topped with OMCheesy feta cheese and came with a side of fruit.  I'm not a big fan of melon so our fabulous server made a special side of fruit without for me - thank you The Cup Café!!   My hubby had house made patty sausage & over medium three eggs
home potatoes - perfectly cooked - deLISH!!  Anddd added bonus we both got the house made biscuit and gravy - that was OMTASTY!! 

Our server was friendly, food was yummilicious and came out fast! Wait wasn't too bad considering it was breakfast time but there was no where to sit hence why we ran an errand and opted to come back.  We noticed people outside waiting and we were grateful it was summer/fall and not winter time.  Parking lot people were a little aggressive but if you are patient the turnover was quick and then a spot opened up in both parking lot and waiting area.  

Overall worth the wait if you have the time and not in a hurry.  We would definitely come back (and will again) and I would recommend The Cup Café.  Be patient your tummy and taste buds will thank you!

DINNER served until 2AM ummmmm this place ROCKS!!  Not only can we have AMAZING food and libations here but during the wee hours  for a nightcap or after a concert or the ballet - I am a veryyy happy girl!!  Homegrown Gastropub is where it is at with mastering delicious organic food to nosh on whether for breakfast, lunch, dinner or late night eats.  Not to mention their signature cocktails that you will be imbibing while you enjoy your next meal here.

Homegrown Gastropub is located in the heart of Midtown one of our favorite places to go these days...yes you read that correctly...plenty of places to park as we venture inside this cozy establishment.  With many options on the menu to please everyone in our party from the vegan to the meat-eater all are sure to be happy.  Some of my favorite dishes are: Pan-seared Crab cakes with grapefruit aioli on arugula ~ yummilicious goodness!; Shrimp & Grits ~ absolutely TO DIE FOR!!; After-School Special that is the Grilled Cheese Sandwich with white cheddar & gouda on sourdough, served with a cup of tomato basil soup ~ OMCheesy goodness;  Sticky Toffee Pudding with espresso, candied pralines and vanilla ice cream ~ devilishly divine!  One must try a few of the signature drinks on a cold wintery night to snuggle up with a friend like the North Bourbon Cider, the French Berrymore or my tried and true the Dirty Martini.  

Quality food, top notch service and prime location in the heart of Midtown...Homegrown Gastropub will have us coming back again and again.  Perfect for brunch, lunch, date night or late night noshing - Homegrown is Where it's at!!

Driving by here over the years this has been on our radar and even more so the hubby as he LOVES his BBQ sooo the wifey finally caved driving him up from Carson City anddd Redwood Rotisserie + Grill exceeded our expectations!

We called ahead as we wanted to make sure they would be able to accomodate us with the current climate of indoor dining andd luck would have it that we scored a table.  Upon our arrival we were taken to our table with menus, H20 with our friendly server arriving, letting us know about an easy to use drink/libation menu by our cellphones.  We opted for the non-alcohol choice on this evening with hot tea for me and fountain variety for the hubby.

Our server recommended a few items giving us the opportunity to review the menu before he returned shortly for us to order the following:  I went with the Tri-Tip salad w/arugula, parmesan cheese, onions, potatoes (under the tri-tip) & a tasty balsamic vinaigrette dressing ~ yummyy!!  ~ hubby ordered (&& shared) Full Rack BBQ Pork Ribs - Ranch Hand is 2lbs.  slow-cooked St. Louis-style + Mac & Cheese and Tater Tots ~ OMTasty goodness with the ribs falling right off the bone...did I happen to mention how deLISH these are!!

Our server was friendly and attentive throughout our meal with checkins and refills on our drinks which we completely appreciated added bonus we saved room for dessert boxing up a few of those tasty ribs to-go home with us.  Our server suggested a few yummilicious options as we perused the dessert menu with us choosing the French Kiss Bread Pudding ala mode ~ to say it was delightfully sinful....well you'll have to pop over to Redwood Rotisserie to sink your spoon into this to try it for yourself!!  

Next visit...I have my eye on a Black + Blue Ribeye ~ yummm!!

What to do on the 2nd Thursday of the month...go to the Emerson for Drag Bingo uhhh duh?!  Grab your bingo crew and get ready for the BEST night ever!!  The Emerson NEVER disappoints with the bartendresses mixing up speciality cocktails that will be sure to quench your thirst andd their new snack menu is PERFECT for light bites to nosh on while catching up with friends, playing a round of bingo or date night.

AMAZING staff, owner, libations & food - yep color me a groupie because this gal and her crew are smitten with The Emerson!!   Easy to find, located directly across from Junkies in the heart of Midtown with chic decor and outside patio too - yep this where you need to be.  

Look forward to our next gals night out to contribute to a local charity, support The Emerson and the wonderful staff along with beautiful Drag Queens.  See you soon anddd B-4 you go to B-I-N....G...Oooo be sure to grab plenty of money to tip the staff and queens (insert wink emjoi)

I have to say I LOVE, LOVE me some yummilicious sushi and could it eat it for every meal, every day if my hubby would let me LOL 

So while running around Reno doing errands I convinced him that a Poke Bowl would be an ideal snack to tide us over before we headed back to Carson City - win, win for me - yahoooo!!  Then why the 3 star review (I will get to that soon), well first I would like to say that Midtown Reno is an eclectic, fabulous area that if you are looking to walk about this time of year to shop, peruse and find something rare and unique for family and friends this is the best area to do just that while hitting up local places, so get your booty to Midtown.  Yep, I said it andddd did I mention there are plenty of places to grab something to eat while people watching just like here at Finbomb Sushi Burrito & Poke Bar with friendly staff too.

Okay, okay back to my review...upon walking in the friendly staff immediately asked if we had been here before to which we said we had not.  They went over the options/choices by talking us thru it - again friendly and helpful.  As previous reviewers have mentioned the layout of the bar is much like a fast food sandwich place where the staff puts everything together for you, so you get to watch your 'build your own' or one of their 'signature items' created right before your eyes - works for me.  Basically just like the name of the place says you have the option of burrito or bowl with mixed greens or two different types of rice.  We opted to share a bowl choosing purple rice which in my humble opinion is healthier, we also had the option to put mixed greens in there too, win-win!!  

Now to why the 3 stars...the protein scoops were extremely small, reminding me of a cookie scoop or melon baller, rather a head scratcher on that one since the cubes of protein are chopped in some cases bigger than the actual scooper.  This made me wonder at 5 Scoops of Protein for $13.95 using a cookie scoop or melon baller scooper was it really a deal??!!  Not to say they should be using a ice cream scooper and I was definitely full after sharing the Poke Bowl with my husband.  I guess my question is, what is the measurement of the scoop equal to?  A teaspoon of protein or a tablespoon?  Just something to ponder... and are you paying mostly for the bases and toppings or are we going there to eat Poke??  Again something to ponder...Okay back to what I actually ate...LOL  

We went with 5 scoops of protein since we were sharing and piled on the toppings of our choice since we totally went rogue by creating our own poke bowl.  For our toppings we went with: cilantro, kale, red onion, seaweed salad, tempura crunch, surimi crab, cabbage, cucumber (strictly for the hubby - not my thang), masago ($1 extra charge), for our sauce choice - BOMB Sauce of course and the UCC Green Tea Unsweetened ($2).  Well, I will finish with our creation satisfied our Poke craving plus added bonus we sat in the window while people watching in Midtown.  Maybe the way to go is a Signature Bowl or Burrito and again the staff was definitely helpful.  Happy Yelping Everyone!

I'm pretty sure that Vieux Carre Pizza is really Dominos in disguise.  It looks like a Domino's pizza and it tastes like a Domino's pizza.  It's a good enough pie and it hits the spot when you need a self indulgent late night cheesy carb fest.  I've ordered pizza from them twice now and I've been happy with them both times.  The fact that they deliver late just adds some  awesomeness.  

The hotel I stay in is 1 block down and 6 blocks over and when I called at 9:55pm they quoted a delivery time of about an hour.  55 minutes later my medium double cheese pizza arrived.  Freshly made and still plenty hot, it was obvious that I'd gotten one that was hot out of the oven.  You also need to know that for security reasons, they will deliver to your hotel lobby but not directly to your room. 

No complaints.

4 Stars

Fortunately it was a perfectly warm afternoon and their doors were wide open, so I chose a seat by the sidewalk.  In just a few moments, a cordial young lady by the name Clevona came by to greet me.  The short conversation was:  "I'd recommend trying our Crawfish Etouffee, Muffaletta, Cajun Jambalaya or maybe you might want to try one of our Po Boys."  So decision made, food ordered, my Shrimp Po Boy was in front of me before I knew it.

Crispy, lightly breaded shrimp were piled on that deliciously toasted French bread that had just the right amount of crisp and crunch.  It came "fully dressed" with fresh tomatoes, crisp lettuce, crisp dill pickles and some garlic mayonnaise.  It also came with more tasty fries than any 3 people should eat at one sitting.  Now while I relished my Po Boy, that Hurricane just kinda fell flat for me.  It was Kool Aid sweet and had very little oompf to it but I manned up and drank it down anyways.  My search for the perfect Hurricane would continue at my next stop...

Chartres House provided me with a very pleasing gastronomic but not alcoholic afternoon.  In any case, I'd go back again tomorrow if I could.

4 Stars

So why would I back to Bennachin Restaurant?  It's easy.  I got a warm greeting as I walked into this small cozy restaurant on a Monday morning just after they opened their doors.  Taking a seat, I explained to my server that it was my my first time trying this cuisine.  I really appreciated that he took a couple minutes to walk me through the moderately priced menu, placing some emphasis on the $10.95 Daily Lunch Specials.

I choose the Cope Ni Cone which is a simple West African dish of boneless white chicken chunks with broccoli florets sautéed with a mild ginger sauce.  It's served over white rice with a sprinkle of cayenne pepper to bring the heat up to the level of your choosing.  It comes with a fist sized roll which was very fresh and soft.  Now the first few bites of my Cope Ni Cone were almost bland tasting but the heat and flavor built up as I worked my way through it.  In any case, it was a healthy, delicious and filling meal.  I also got a hot cup of Barajambo tea ($2.50), which was a flavorful compliment.  I passed on dessert as there as only one waiter on the floor and he was really getting popped by about 11:30.  Maybe I'll save that for a future visit.

My first African food adventure was a good one so I'm giving them 4 Stars.

A
Few
Things
You
Need
To
Know:

It's a small restaurant seating about 20 people.  Go early if you can.

The menu is very vegetarian friendly.

They don't serve pork but beef, chicken, lamb and seafood options are all available.

...An Awful-Awful review of the Nugget Diner...

Reno is known as "The Biggest Little City In The World."  So my favorite joke about Reno is "we flew to Reno and it was frickin' closed..." because it's so tiny.  So how appropriate to go to the "Biggest Little Casino in the World" - The Nugget (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/LbhraX3qY94g3Xn2Havbpg?select=0SoYEjC9IpsY6oBYyTDrPw).  And it is TRUE, it's like a 20'x80' opening in the side of a building that has a bunch of slots and a bar.  We were in search for Reno's best burger:  The Awful Awful (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/LbhraX3qY94g3Xn2Havbpg?select=jtI4ijN6snDw1PhU-fIpSw) found in the hole-in-the-casino Nugget Diner.

I have to say, this Diner was pretty much the pits of all Diners (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/LbhraX3qY94g3Xn2Havbpg?select=zmVAR3Rrw_52HZpKETnrGg), and the "character actors" all had their superbly acted roles:  The two waitresses that were stern-looking at first, but began to lighten up when talked to, whose discussions ranged from personal problems to which customer left the better tips.  The down-and-out locals that talked about how much money they made the day before bicycling visitors around downtown.  The other characters talking about how this is the best food in all of Reno; and the cook that never turned around from the griddle.  Spending all day in this place could really give you insight into Renonians:  Down-and-out, the life-of-hard-Knox, tough-skinned people who have nothing but kindness to give out.  The Diner had an "A" rating, but the grease and dirt surfacing the entire area made me really wonder... "How?"  We sat at the bar and was immediately told that we couldn't order from there, but had to walk about 10 feet to the right and order right under the "Please place order here" sign.  No credit cards accepted, cash only!

- We ordered "The Original Awful-Awful" (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/LbhraX3qY94g3Xn2Havbpg?select=Bo6Nl2-Ai0xHXmRuwMRE7A) at $6.50.  Made from a half-pound of ground chuck and grilled to order.  The Onion bun looked like nothing really special; and served with fresh lettuce, a raw red onion slice, tomato, cheese slice, and their "special" creamy sauce (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/LbhraX3qY94g3Xn2Havbpg?select=7I8J_hPJG7oHWzQ3EIeorQ).  An extra patty can be added for an extra $2.95, or bacon for $1.75 more.  I must say that the burger was "Awfully Awfully" tasty!  A 4-star experience that made the trip worthwhile... kinda...

- The burger was served on a huge basket of fries.  The fries were semi-crisp browned and soggy-soft in the middle... Just the way I like it.

- Coleslaw was also ordered, but nothing too special and a slight hint of horseradish. 

The Little Nugget got its Awful-Awful notoriety by winning Camille Ford's Food Wars with The Bigger Nugget that serves its version of the Awful-Awful.  It was funny because they kept showing the Food War's episode over and over and over...  I guess a place like this needs all the recognition it can muster.  To me this place will be known for a 4-star burger in a 2-star tiny little dirty diver in the World's tiniest city.  *flips the sign to CLOSED, and turns and walks away*

After two good lunches, decided to take some good friends to dinner.  HORRIBLE!  For a brewery - out if IPA and out of my second choice.  Rude and slow service.  Asked to substitute vegetables for mash potatoes on one dish and told no way.  Out of chardonnay my wife chose.  When we asked to take some food home the comment was, well how many boxes do you want and then they were just tossed on the table.  When I asked for decaf coffee, told we only serve regular.  

Two good experiences at lunch do not make up for the embarrassment of this evening.  Neither out guests, or my wife - who had not been to the restaurant, would ever return.  I might for a beer with an good friend at lunch and some mussels (which are excellent).  

It's too bad.  It's the in place for now, but this kind of experience will turn it back into an ice house.

I had been to Renee's a few times over the past few years but I went there twice in a row, last Saturday and this Saturday, much to my disappointment!.
Both times, the waiter came to us after 1.5 hours and let us know that "the table was reserved"! This is unheard of! I do not know of any other restaurant that would kick people out. Last weekend I came in wth my friend and it was the two of us, same thing.... I told me 3 other friends that this happened and they told me that it was bizarre until it happened again tonight. There were four of us and they came to tell us that the table was reserved.
This restaurant is overpriced to say the least! They bring bread without the butter and the portions are very small.
Very disappointing. This would be my last time at Renee's.

Nice little spot that is often overshadowed by its awesome neighbors. I got the chicken and broccoli sandwich and that shit was killer. Its got your variety of hug juices, rap snacks, and what not, but its also got some of the best hoagies on this side of the river. Pop in. Enjoy it.

We heard about this place through Yelp, and recognized that its related to Curry Leaves on Westshore. 

If you like Curry Leaves, then you'll like this place.  Menu, style, and the staff are the same.  The stag is mostly from south India, and the cuisine is mostly north. 

They had a dahl soup that was amazing. Defiantly the best item in the buffet.  

Lots of seating, which is great when the crowed arrives!

Certain friends have been obsessed with Skygarten since it opened, and I knew I had to make it up before the end of summer.

All I can say is I hope to be back again at least once more before leaving the area soon. I loved my first visit!

You get carded before entering and they'll check your bag. No outside beverages are allowed in, which for me meant chugging most of a water bottle (filled with water, not straight booze in disguise) in seconds.

You have a few options once inside. Go to the left for views of the art museum area and the eternal backup on 76, turn to the right and make another right for indoor communal seating and $7ish drinks, or go all the way to the right for the City Hall/Camden views.

It's so close to the Comcast Center that if you creep hard enough, you can see desktop screensavers and people walking around. From the left balcony, there's an awesome view of the new Comcast construction in progress too.

I came here for the sunset and loved seeing all the glimmering lights around the city from its central location. I also spotted my old apartment building in Francisville, which was so fun to see from afar.

Keep in mind it will likely be WINDY. I'm so glad to have been wearing a tank and shorts instead of a dress. Bring a hair-tie for sure.

I didn't buy anything this go around, so the whole experience was free. It was so nice and a bit shocking to not have a cover charge.

It was moderately busy on a hot August Thursday, but a good and safe number of people for the space. 

So far so good here!

I loved my experience here last summer so much that I had to duplicate it over the weekend.

Okay, I didn't actually do that on purpose, but after uploading photos of my meal, I was greeted with photos of...the exact same meal posted months earlier. Whoops. I'm also pretty sure we had the same server both times.

Shane walked over, noted that I was looking at the beer list, and asked if I was ready or needed a rec. I asked if the Brunilde by Birrificio Bresciano Montenetto (actual words were "the oatmeal stout") was any good, and he said it was excellent, so I went with that. While it was a good choice, I wouldn't call it excellent. Solid 3.75 stars due to lacking a robust stout flavor, but I'm always happy to try new Italian brews.

After the complimentary bread basket, we ordered the arancini rice balls. They were tasty and a great app, but I won't personally order them again. I didn't read the description before they were ordered, but I've since learned they contain mixed-in veal, which I don't eat.

My meal (both times) was the Carbonara pasta. It's a spaghetti tossed with cheese, eggs, and black pepper with a cute topping of bacon gelato. Gah, so good! I usually hate the taste of pepper (black, green or any other color!), but this was melded so well that it complemented the pasta perfectly.

I wish I could've finished my plate, but they offer up hearty servings even though the plates aren't massive. Dessert wasn't even an option!

I'd absolutely return...and should probably branch out on the menu. Too many great-sounding options still to try!

Oasis made a great first impression! Now, keep in mind it's located in the former home of Stella Pizza (now across the street in the former home of that barbecue place). That means it's a very bare-bones establishment with only a splattering of tables available for eat-in. You can also order pickup or delivery.

For my first visit, I ordered the chicken tinga quesadilla. This was not your typical quesadilla! The deep fried tortilla took over the whole plate and was topped with lettuce, cheese and sour cream. The chipotle-sauce laden chicken was so tender and tasty without any extreme heat. Absolutely delicious! I couldn't even finish the thing, but guess how much it set me back? Yeah. Six bucks plus tax/tip. Unbelievable.

In addition to the hearty portions, they also provide complimentary chips (donned with refried beans and cheese) and three sauces of varying spice levels.

Service was friendly and fast, and most other tables did BYO. With the new brewery open just a few blocks away, I'll have to come back again this summer with a growler! Looking forward to exploring their menu more!

Holy fantastic meal.

Similar to Brauhaus: Love everything.
Dissimilar to Brauhaus: Basically everything else.

Beer list was respectable. Decor was modern, airy, warm and welcoming.

There was a peep window into the kitchen area. And by "peep window," I mostly mean I just avoided looking through the large glass in the back of the dining room because I'm weird and would've felt uncomfortable watching people work. I don't want people watching me sit in my cube. But...I realize I'm missing the point of the peep window here so let's move on.

Food! Yep. Get the food. Go to Bainbridge if you just want drinks. The half chicken was pretty darn spectacular, and I even ate my peas. I do not generally eat peas.

Tried a bite of my friend's crab cake sandwich and that was also pretty good! And this is coming from a non-sea-eater.

Dessert was also phenomenal, but if you get the blueberry cobbler, you are now warned that you will walk out with a bright blue mouth. You're welcome.

Also, get the cobbler.

Talk about a great first impression.

While I never made it to the food truck, I knew I had to stop by when SpOt opened a location 1) conveniently on my way home from work and 2) a fairly short walk away. Our group of four headed in last night and had a great time.

Since it was my inaugural visit, I went traditional and chose the SpOt sirloin burger (cheddar, bacon, pickles, cole slaw, spot sauce). I was so excited that I didn't have to add "no tomatoes" to my order. I hate tomatoes like you wouldn't believe. My friend and I also split cheese fries.

We sat down at a high-top, waited a bit and, before we knew it, our orders were delivered by name, one by one. My burger was prepared to a perfect medium with juice dripping throughout the meal. Cheese fries were super cheesy in the best of ways and cut to an ideal size. My friends all enjoyed their burgers as well, although none of us were able to finish our plates.

All staff members were super friendly and suggested coming back with booze the next time. They're BYO and Rybrew is right across the street.

Will return soon! Such a great addition to Brewerytown!

Our goal at the beginning of Philly Cooks -- one of the greatest local foodie events -- was to seek out a booth that wasn't insanely crowded. We decided to start in the back corner.

I didn't realize that I'd be falling madly for a beautiful, wonderful, meaty heaven of a restaurant just seconds later. It all started with the cured pork loin. It came with a little potato chip too. It was glorious. Good god.

Kensington Quarters shot to the top of my to-visit list.

A couple weeks later, a reservation for six was made. I arrived first (because I was super eager, obviously) and I sat at the bar to order a drink. With some help from the bartender, I chose the Brooklyn Black Double Chocolate Stout. One and done! Awesome stout too.

Once my friends arrived, we walked past the butchering area and were seated in the dining room at a wooden plank table.

We tried a TON of the plates. I can't remember them all because it's been a good month now and also since I just checked their menu and it's mostly different. A return trip is IN ORDER! Who's in, Yelp friends???

Anyway. So at the time, I couldn't remember the name of the Philly Cooks sample that I had. With some help from our FANTASTIC server (in caps -- seriously, she was so peppy and helpful with answering our 100,000 questions), it was determined to be the cured loin. I put in an order for that (so much love! our server even laughed at how happy I was when I ordered it!) and also for the pork cutlet from the small plates section -- which is no longer on their menu but was so thin and juicy and siiiiigh.

I also tried bites from my friends' plates, including the pig foot lasagna (also not on the menu anymore, but it was delicious despite having foot parts in it) and the pork shoulder (emoji hearts here please). There was also some pasta in the mix at some point. I remember that much. And ummm... some other meats? Yes? I lost track of all the plates, frankly.

We tried all of the desserts too. The chocolate, chocolate, chocolate was my least favorite -- alas, it's not on the menu anymore either -- because it was too spicy. The best was the pear and lavender tort. From the latest version of the menu, I see a brown butter cake and I need it. Need.

So really. Who wants to visit?

Blue Monkey Tavern is a gem in Merchantville, but it also can get overlooked compared to newer, shinier locales. I feel like it's one place I tend to forget about unless I'm in the area, which is sad but true. Their food and beer options are both generally stellar, and I've yet to have a poor experience.

I was most recently at BMT last weekend for dinner with my mom. We sat in one of the booths near the front, and our server was really sweet and accommodating. We ordered the crab and cheese dip to start, which was okay. If you like crab, it'll be a great app. Loads of crab chunks. For me, I was hoping for more cheese.

After that, my mom had a caesar salad to start, and I stole half of it. SO good, wow. A seriously excellent salad, and I'll have to remember that for my next visit. [This is me reminding myself.]

I had the cheesesteak sandwich for dinner. It came with three kinds of cheese, and it was awesome. I was stuffed, so I had to box up half of it. Fortunately, it was still just as tasty the next day. Oh, and they had Cascade sours available on draft. Nice!

Blue Monkey has a lot going for it -- history, longevity, quality food, great beer, and a central location near the newish brewery in town.

I'm trying to think of an appropriate way to describe my feelings about Bottle Bar without sounding nutty. But, well...It's like this: I LOVE Bottle Bar. 

Like, a lot. Like, if I'm in Fishtown, I stop in without fail. But also, I'm not in Fishtown that often so that's overall a general positive for my liver, wallet and refrigerator space.

Their selection is immense and overwhelming. I always feel like I'm in a hoppy library when I visit. And let's not forget their bar section in the back. You're sure to find something fantastic pouring at any given time.

That's basically all I have to say. Will be back.

[OH HEY, REVIEW 700!]

"Fine" is probably the best word to describe Bottos. I always anticipate a higher quality meal than is actually delivered. I feel like they could and should be better, but, in general, it's a popular spot in Swedesboro.

I've eaten in the dining room for dinner and the front bar area for lunch. The front is chilly in the winter, especially if the door keeps opening, so bring an extra layer.

Service was okay...not overly pleasant or prompt, but not abysmal either. Right down the middle.

I found the chicken milanese platter to be bland, the cheesesteak to be average with too much wiz, and the meatballs a bit below satisfactory. I couldn't eat them in bulk, so I'm glad I just tried one.

I'd say this is a generous three stars, because chances are I'd prefer my grandmother's Italian cooking to a platter from Botto's any day of the week. I'm no longer a Jersey resident, and I don't anticipate giving the restaurant another try any time soon.

It's pretty nice to have Mugshots right down the block. Since I moved to the neighborhood at the beginning of this past summer, I've had three distinct experiences with this coffee shop:

Experience 1:
It was the middle of the day. It was hot outside. I had been gallivanting around Fairmount and I wanted something small to eat and also to try one of Mugshots' drinks for the first time. Since it was in the afternoon, I wasn't in the market for coffee. I walked in as a very-perplexed customer and spent a super-long time analyzing their menu.

The sweet person working answered several of my questions about their drinks and probably thought I was stupid for being so dumb re: basic coffeehouse offerings. Eventually, I decided on a Black Beauty smoothie, which tasted both sweet and healthy (blackberry, boysenberry, blueberry, and yogurt), and also a baconator bagel, whiiiich was.. not healthy. Mm.

Experience 2:
Mugshots was one of the stops on the Great Philadelphia Craft Beer Crawl last month. I did not have coffee during this visit. I had a Yards Pale Ale. It's nice that they participate in community events! They were packed that day. Aaaand that's the extent of Experience 2. Apologies that it wasn't more exciting.

Experience 3:
Tonight! They hosted a free menu tasting and fall celebration event, which equated to a generous spread of cheeses, spreads, hummus, pita, salad, flatbreads (apple butter + mushroom), and french toast. What a great way to bring people in! Standout: the apple butter flatbread. Unique, and I likely never would've thought to order that on my own!

After getting a taste of some of their delicious fall offerings, I purchased a blood orange mocha and a cranberry kale salad with organic chicken (~$15 together). The kale salad had a nice lemon-honey dressing on it and it was mixed with shaved parmesan and almonds. I'd definitely get it again. As for the blood orange mocha? Thumbs up x2. It had more of a chocolate taste than blood orange, but it was quality stuff.

I would probably frequent Mugshots more since it's super-super close to me, but I own a Keurig and I love my Keurig. Still, they do host some pretty fun events, their staff has always been very nice, and it also looks like a nice place to stay for awhile with a laptop. So far, so good.

PLEASE READ **DO NOT USE THE ATM MACHINE HERE** If I could rate this dining experience a ZERO I would. We went into the restaurant not noticing that it was CASH ONLY. So we went to the ATM machine inside and got money out. We notice one of the $20 bill was a little worn but payed it no mind because it looked authentic. So we after we paid, Eric came to us and said it's fake! We informed him that we got it out of the ATM there and instead of talking diplomatically with us his got loud and belligerent. I had to literally act as the manager he should have been to get him to calm down. I ask him to bring out a counterfeit detector pen and he says he doesn't have one. I ask him if there is a camera so we can see a playback of when my wife took the bill out of the ATM, he said there is no camera! He then demanded that we pay him another $20 or he will call the police! 
We told him that we will not be paying any additional money and he can call them and we will wait! He ran to the back and his brother came out to apologize and said the bill was real and offered to pay. We declined the offer because all we wanted to do enjoy our food, PAY and be on our way. I told the brother now all we wanted was an apology from Eric but the COWARD refused to come out from the back of the kitchen to admit he was wrong and apologized. As a man and as a manager that should have been the immediate result to this terrible ordeal! I should have called the police because now I believe Eric is running an ATM scam. If any of you experience this, REPORT HIM!!!!
DO NOT USE THE ATM MACHINE HERE! You have been warned!

Not bad. 

When in Reno, you can do one of two things: eat or gamble. We did both. 

Cafe Milano was honestly one of the more affordable options in Peppermill Casino.
When seeing a place that tries to do too much at once, you start getting concerned. Thankfully, Cafe Milano actually does Asian food well. Surprisingly, it was their pasta that I felt wasn't that great.

First off, the meats were all tender. Also, the plates and soups were all seasoned just right. The fried rice was surprisingly better than I had imagined. 

The fettuccini pasta was super creamy, but there was no other distinct taste. The noodles were also overcooked. Besides that, the garlic bread was just right: buttery, perfectly toasted, and not super salty. 

The service was okay. The atmosphere was alright: I liked how bright it was and the cushioned booths.

My review is for the event planning staff rather than dining in the restaurant.  We needed a classy place to host a high end client appreciation event.  My bosses wanted to have a wine tasting and the Union Trust came up with some food pairings.  I gave them a price point to work with and they did their best to get close to that number.

The event itself took place upstairs in a room.  We had a good amount of people, so the room was a bit cramped.  It definitely was not easy to mingle.  The staff was amazing and the food came quickly.  We had 5 courses planned (Oysters, Striped Bass, Scallop, Steak, Cheese Plate), my favorite was the scallops and bacon.  By the way, all bacon is delicious, we know this...but the bacon at UT was the best bacon I ever had.  I still think about it.  The next course was steak and it was perfectly cooked and seasoned, but that was no surprise.

At the end of the night, there was a bit of a delay with the check and that was more of a nuisance to my bosses rather than me.

This would be a better review if there weren't some snafu's.  When I had planned the event with the staff, I had requested that the sommelier do a little presentation about the wines, but when we showed up, there was no sommelier.  After the event, I left over 5 messages with the event coordinator to get a list of the wines so that we could send it out as a follow up to thank people for attending.  5 messages!  I never got the list.

The food is good, yes.  The wait staff is amazing.  The event was quite pricey, as you would imagine.  I am not sure if I would ever return to dine as the lack of follow up left me with a bad feeling.

Damn you restaurant week!  Did you learn your tricks from a drug dealer...you let people sample your products cheap, get them hooked and then turn them out on the street craving more....at a higher price...

I loved Del Frisco's!  We ordered off the restaurant week menu.  I went with the salad with apples and pecans...my date went with the asparagus bisque...both delish, though I loved the salad a tad more...We both ordered the filet (when in Rome...and all) and both were cooked to perfection....they came with a side of fancypants mashed potatoes....We also ordered a side of lobster mac & cheese....it was a tad over indulgent...we almost preferred it to not have lobster in it...

For dessert, my date ordered the chocolate mousse, while I had the warmed bread pudding....the mousse was spot on...the warmed bread pudding was great, but after the mac and cheese, potatoes and warmed bread, I was a bit over-carbed...so while it was tasty, it was too heavy to finish.

Bestest of all (I am making that a word) was the staff.  We were constantly swarmed by a flurry of helpful hands...and while there were many of them, they never ran the risk of being overbearing or intrusive.  Our main waiter, Jake, was perfect...everything was perfect and I can see why this place has a higher price tag in normal circumstances....

Alas, Del Frisco's you have me hooked, but I don't know how quickly I can return to your warm caress.  While I am off in the world eating less worthy morsels, I will be thinking of you...

This is the strangest review of all time. I had simply the worst breakfast this morning. I'll describe: soft boiled eggs (raw) totally runny couldn't have been more then 3 minutes. One half spilled out, served cold. The other scrambled eggs, ham, grits. All crusted over from sitting but yet oddly not hot. Asked for the eggs soft , they were served hard and browned. Sent the soft boiled eggs back. Shared the old eggs. Ham was cold and grits had a crust literally! The coffee was good. Ok, by every respect this was a horrible meal. I'm not sure why they would want to do breakfast down stairs when they obviously can't on the weekend. Third time on a Saturday or Sunday downstairs that was subpar. They only do a buffet on the weekends upstairs. I can't eat enough for the buffet. Kitchen doesn't care when the buffet is up?  Plus took forever to come out. 

This is the good. The service was great. I could see the pain of our server. I wasn't mad . How could I be? She had the manager come over. I could tell it wasn't the first issue that day. The manager comped the check. She didn't need to, but it was nice of her. She was totally professional. Sometimes managers will be defensive she listened and was responsible. I eat here often. I can't understand why it's so inconsistent. The service is always good. I wish I could say the same for the kitchen.

Only went for happy hour but it was great and I can't wait to go back. Bartender Sarah was great. Killer happy hour cocktail for $5 and many good options for like $5. Had empanadas and ricotta with grilled bread. The space is stunning. I hear they have two bowling alleys. How cool is that. Headed back next week for a full meal , but the menu looks wonderful. Lots of good choices at decent prices.

Down a tiny alley, you travel back in time to when butchers made real sausages and smoked meats. All kind of hand made smoked and fresh kielbasa. Real hotdogs, bacon, sausages. Homemade sauerkraut and pirogies. Serving this Polish neighborhood forever. Go, go soon and buy everything!

Totally unexpected excellence. It's in a strip mall. I know it came highly recommend but still it's in a strip mall! First the restaurant is very pretty. It's BYOB. The service was outstanding and very professional. If you are intimidated by the menu then ask. They can guide you through. The food was good to great. We had the cold marinated vegetables and the cold cucumber salad. Both were great. Got the pan fried and steamed dumplings. Good but I'm more fond of a thin dough wrapper. Dan dan noodles were very good! Dry pepper chicken was great, Clams in black bean sauce were as good as I have ever had, General Tao's Tofu was great, the Chengdu Prawns were good but not great. It's in King of Prussia , so it's easy to get to off of 202 and Henderson road. Definitely worth the trip! Much easier then driving into the city and free parking!

Located in the foothills of the magnificent Santa Catalina Mountains in Oro Valley, a desert community just north of Tucson, really great place to visit for relaxing.

Mountain is gorgeous. Mount Lemmon summit to this resort hotel is only 10 miles away but due to elevation change, temperature difference is significant. Driving distance to mount Lemmon is 60 miles.

Pool is heated and as long as the Sun is out, enjoy the warm weather and pool. Jacuzzi is available if you get cold.

Junior suite I had was spacious. Balcony was nice to enjoy the view of the pool.  Compared to other resort hotels within 5-6 miles radius, amenities and decor is not that luxurious. Breakfast buffet was $26/adult and I thought it was a bit too high for what they serve.

Came here for a quick lunch while in town based on the reviews.

They were busy with mostly customers with laptops. They have free WiFi here and most seemed to be staying there for a long time. Some even had their own snack from home....

Seating availability was limited and found rather uncomfortable stool by the window. 

Service was great, friendly and fast. I really enjoyed their coffee and crepes. It just they had too few many flys around my food while I was trying to eat.  Needless to say I left as soon as I was done eating. I wanted to stay longer and relax but situation didn't let me when I visited

Located within Hilton Hotel, I made a reservation via opentable app. They were busy and people were having a great time. They were a bit too loud after too few many drinks.

I asked for a quite table I saw in the back but they didn't want one person to sit there.

Server was friendly and fairly prompt.

I tried gumbo and oysters for a small dinner. Gumbo wasn't what I remembered as a traditional gumbo. I am not a gumbo expert but it wasn't what I remembered from 10 years ago.

I arrived after a happy hour but I heard they have a good happy hour menu here.

Gotta have Philly cheese in Philadelphia right?

I googled (not sure why I didn't search on Yelp) Philly cheese near me and this place came up on my search as most reviewed place in the area.

They currently offer take out only.

I asked them to give me whoever everyone orders the most. They asked me if I wanted onions or mushrooms, I asked them add if that's how most people eat. 

Staff there was friendly with great smile.

Since I didn't know where I can go to eat, I ended up walking back to the independence national park area where I knew they had plenty of benches to sit down.

It was a bit of walk, by the time I got to the park and ready to eat, bread was very soggy and I didn't have enough napkins to keep my hands clean. 

Sandwich itself was a full of flavor. A half was enough was it was very filling.  I needed to walk around more to help me settle my stomach.

I would like to come back when indoor dining opens and enjoy their food right after they prepare it.

Pleasantly surprised how good their food was! 

Coming back from Benson, as soon as I arrived back to Tucson, I pulled over and searched for a quick dinner nearby.  When I arrived here at 8pm, one hour before close time, she happily welcomed me to dine in.  I was willing to take to go if I was coming here late for them.

I started my dinner with seafood soup. Very good flavor, ending up finishing a large bowl of soup.  Mapo tofu had a very good flavor as well.  I throughly enjoyed my dinner and got to talk to the owner. They are first generation immigrant, southern China to be exact (I was trying to guess and I was right). While they do serve American Chinese dishes, food I ordered tasted so authentic.

A little gem located just outside the Tucson city. Not too far from the freeway, I would come back here when traveling on I-10.

Loved their pizza and tap water (she said it is filtered tap water).

We got lucky to dine in here without any reservation. They only have three tables inside due to COVID and reservation is recommended for indoor dine in.

Tap water tasted so soft, why am I commenting about their water but it really was tasty. 

They have a happy hour (ended 15 minutes before we arrived) and price on drinks and appetizers looked very reasonable.

We shared 28" braised pork (seasonal) and the pizza was very good. I liked that texture and flavor of the dough.

Sometimes pizza sits in my tummy for a while and I tend to avoid eating pizza but this place is exception. I would eat their pizza often if I live nearby.

I enjoyed watching the chef cooking from the dining area. They all ware mask and face shield. I know why but I wondered if they get really hot near that oven.

Staff was friendly and overall it was very pleasant experience dining in here.

Foodies heaven. Must visit for all Yelpers.

This place was recommended by so many people including Uber drivers. It is unfortunate they close early. I wish they stay open for dinner.

Don't make the same mistake as I did and be sure to come hungry.

Amish soft pretzels looked really good. I know they are good as I had one in Lancaster earlier. I walked around, up and down and everywhere to check out each one of them.

This market alone is a destination and must visit in Philadelphia.

Where to start with this place... 

I love the idea of world of beer. Great beer selection, awesome outdoors section with games. 

I wanted to like this place I really did but what I found when visiting on a few occasions is that it is way too crowded to sit and you have to hover over tables and or chairs to sit down. On top of that every beer that I wanted to drink on tap, pale ales, IPAs, lagers, are always kicked. If they kick the keg it should be erased or crossed off the board. Countless times I waited around for 10 or more minutes for a bartender just to have them tell me that my selection was kicked and they walk off and help another customer.

I'm saving the worst for last here. Do not eat in this establishment. Last time I visited two people who I was with ordered food and shared the plate. Both got violently ill a few hours later. They were sick for 48 hours and one almost had to go to the hospital from the food poisoning. 

The problem with this place is that it is new and popular. as time goes on the novelty will wear off and management will start to realize how they have been treating their customers. There are plenty of other places in the area who serve good beer, and you don't have to worry about bad service or getting sick when you eat there.

I'll take my business elsewhere

We recently ate at Fleming's in Metairie.  We were so disappointed.

Our steaks came out raw two times. The third time it was over cooked. 
We didn't want to wait for a 4th time receiving our steaks- so just ate it but it was not good!

By that time the sides were cold-so they just reheated them instead of giving us new sides. They also did the same thing for the steaks- just recooking them.  A fine restaurant shouldn't do that.

It took almost 2 hours to get the final meal- and by then we were disgusted with the whole experience.

We thought the salads were just fair- nothing special.

The prices are very expensive. The restaurant is lovely inside - but the food was terrible!

If you want a great steakhouse in Metairie-go to Ruth Chris's Steakhouse in Metairie- the food there is delicious and far superior than Fleming's.

Yesterday we waited in a long line outside the door of @hattiebs in Nashville with the sun beating down on us, was it worth the wait? YES! I'd do it all over again for this delicious chicken! $9.50 for this loaded chicken sandwich, with a side of your choice. The chicken is deliciously juicy chicken breast perfectly seasoned, read: ~SPICY~ !!!  
Just an FYI the mild is HOT, so Medium is HOT AF, Hot is  and so on. Choose your spice level wisely! 


The customer service was great, everyone was wearing masks, sanitizing very often, and very mindful of the fact that we're still in a pandemic. Order ahead and take out is available if you would prefer that!

Food was a joke, I ordered the Salmon Platter with Mashed Potatoes and Green Beans. 

Mashed potatoes looked like apple sauce (how is that even possible right?)

Green Beans were literally swimming in grease (why not drain it??)

Salmon was soggy and also......swimming in grease. 

Food was cold, customer service was cold. Honestly if I could give this negative 5 stars I promise you I would.

Hands down best pho in New Orleans. Argue with me as much as you want, you'll never change my mind. This is also the best locations of all of the Pho Bangs. Each one is owned by a different family member and I feel like this location gives the biggest portions. I usually order to go and budget out the amazing broth into two different meals. The pho is super reasonably priced (about $9 for XL). My two go to meals here are: 

1. XL Pho with tendon, brisket and raw beef. Broth is amazing. Some people might think its a bit salty but I think it's perfect. They also give a crap ton of meat. It's so worth it for $9. You can taste all of the herbs and seasoning and can tell it's been cooked for a long time. 

2. Lemon grass chicken: SOOO GOOD. They grill the chicken perfectly so it's crunchy. Also love the way they cook their rice and the amazing sauce. Huge portions and again generous with the meat. 

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Overall, love this place. Nothing beats it. Pho is the best, rice dishes are the best and service has been great. I wish it wasn't so far from new orleans but I guess thats also good or else I'd be eating here multiple times per day. It does get buy on weekends but otherwise, usually no wait. Must try.

Al and Stella's food rivals Quartino's in Chicago. I never thought I could find something that could possibly taste better than Quartino, but am I ever glad I am wrong! It is incredibly worth the drive from even Orlando, just to eat here. 

After my husband and I explored Honeymoon Island and the antique shops in Dunedin on Friday, Jan 13, we were incredibly hungry and craving something delicious. I remembered stumbling across this place on Yelp, so my husband, Jeff, called to get a reservation. Their phone message said that they opened at 5pm, same for most other places in Clearwater Beach. I don't know if it was because it was off-season, but I found the late start rather odd. 

Parking was incredibly easy to find when we arrived in Clearwater Beach at 4:30pm. All the spaces I saw were metered--but they stop enforcing the meters at 6pm, which made for cheap parking. One quarter for every 15 minutes is a bargain compared to parking in Chicago. 

When we arrived at the restaurant a few minutes later, the place was dark. There were no signs of anyone preparing in the kitchen or the dining room, so I was afraid that perhaps it was closed for the off-season. Yet, all the good Yelp reviews raved about their delicious food, so we decided to wait by going to the beach and watching the sun setting. Just before 5pm, we headed back to the restaurant to find the employees and I think the owner opening up shop. It was very cold out, so they let us come in and warm up even as they were still opening up the place. 

Some people complained about the decor, but it wasn't actually that bad. It's not Olive Garden level, but they have some beautiful paintings and pictures on the wall of scenes from Italy, and white lights were strung across the ceiling. The ambiance was quite nice--not cheesy like tourist trap restaurants, nor is it over the top like some faux-Italian places like the Olive Garden. There is beauty in simplicity, and it let us focus on the food and conversation. 

The waitresses were very friendly. They seemed slightly confused that we didn't order wine or sangria (I was tempted by the latter), but I wanted to have full facility of my senses while driving back to Orlando in the dark, and my husband wanted to be able to help me navigate. They do sell Coke products, and we each ordered a can of Coke. 

We ordered the bruschetta with fresh tomatoes and basil. It was delicious--the best bruschetta I've ever had.The seasoning was perfect--not too garlicky and not too plain. We then ordered the gnocchi, little potato dumplings in a marinara sauce. Again, the seasoning was perfect, not too strong and not too weak. They even gave us two plates to help us split the meal. 1/2  serving each of the gnocchi more than filled us up because it was so rich and flavorful. The meal came with additional bread and olive oil, which we also devoured. 

When dessert time came, my husband ordered a tiramisu and I had a lemon torte. The lemon torte was also amazing. Perfect texture, perfect flavor, perfect sweetness. I wish I had the recipe, because I'm craving it right now! I'm not a fan of tiramisu so I didn't sample my husband's dish. He said it was absolutely divine, though. 

Altogether, the meal for the two of us added up to about $42.59, not including tip. Incredibly delicious food, and it is definitely worth the drive from and to Orlando, where we were staying at a Disney hotel. Skip the faux-italian Disney restaurants, and come eat the real stuff. Yes, Al and Stella are real Italians, from southern and northern Italy, respectively.

Bacara is a waterfront resort on the Gaviota coast near the town of Goleta, which is north of Santa Barbara. The Mediterranean-style villas have a Spanish Colonial architectural influence, very typical in Southern California.

The parking is by valet only. The valet staff are pleasant & very welcoming.
While waiting in line to check-in, we were given a glass of champagne to sip. There are golf cart drivers to shuttle the guests around the very spread-out property. We choose the healthier option of walking the winding pathways to the suite, and looking at the property's architecture & landscaping.

The resort offers accommodations with ocean, garden or courtyard views. We were lucky to upgrade to an ocean view suite, as some rooms had a terrace facing other buildings. We highly recommend Building 19 if you can secure a suite/room in this villa. It is central to the two main swimming pools, restaurants, and has beautiful ocean views.

Every room has a complimentary bottle of wine on arrival. The selection in our suite was by Tortoise Creek, Pinot Noir "Mission Grove". If one prefers a white or another selection, the front desk will accommodate. 

The suite was appointed, in our opinion, in ten-year old furnishings of style and condition (worn/chipped). The linens were of good quality, but the bed itself was not comfortable for either of us. There was a sitting area next to a fireplace where one could watch TV or read. We also had a small living room for comfort.

The main bathroom was of good size, and had a jetted bathtub that overlooks the bedroom area. It also had a shower area & toilet in a separate room (water closet).

The room was well insulated as we barely heard any noise from the pools. The only noise complaint was the double-door entry into the suite. We could clearly hear people in the hallway.

We would rate this resort a 3.75 / 5.0 property, and the staff, a solid 4.5 / 5. A bit of a disappointment for a Ritz-Carlton, however a very pleasant location.

As one enters the nondescript building of the Meet Up Chinese Cuisine, masks are required for entry. Once inside, one's temperature is taken to ensure the safety of customers and staff. 

When dining late mid day, we were immediately seated in a nicely appointed, well-lit environment near a lovely cascading wall fountain. Our "human" server was very friendly & congenial. The menu is available by scanning a QR code on the table, or a paper copy is available. The printed menu is written in English and Chinese. 

Upon being seated, an individual bottle of water was placed on our table for each of us. After giving us adequate time to study the menu, our order was taken promptly.

In short order, our meal began to arrive from the kitchen via a talking robot server. Upon arriving at our table, the robot asked us to remove our dishes and tap her hand, so she could "get back to work". How cool is that?! The robot is a nice & fun addition to this family run establishment. 

We were quite pleased with the dishes we ordered. The selections of each dish were beautifully presented, and were generous in portion size. Everything was delicious.

Meet Up Chinese Cuisine is good for groups, and offers live music on Fridays & Saturdays evenings according to the male greeter. 

Come and enjoy!

Secret Bao is a relatively recently opened restaurant that one should not miss. Upon entering the restaurant, signs direct dine-in & pickup/delivery customers to the appropriate station, thus moving the customer flow efficiently. After placing one's order, a number is given to display on the table. Staff bring plates, utensils and napkins prior to receiving the order.

The indoor spacious dining area is well-lit with lots of natural light. The area was immaculate and tables were being serviced and sanitized as customers departed. There is patio dining for enjoying the beautiful Santa Barbara climate, as well as being located across the street from the Santa Barbara County Courthouse Sunken Garden, which is another great place to enjoy their fare.

Staff circulates around the dining areas to handle customer's needs, and to deliver orders. I would like to give a shout-out to "Celine", as she was very attentive and seemed to motivate her fellow workers.

Their signature offerings are a mind-blowing selection of modern Asian cuisine with fusion selections of baos, as well as "Not Baos". Currently, their specialty baos include Smoked Salmon, Fried Shrimp, Maitake Mushroom, Korean Fried Chicken, Pork Belly, among others.

A sampling of "Not Baos" include, but not limited to, Local Halibut Ceviche, Oyakodon, Tuna Poke, Bibimbap, Japchae, and more. The menu is still evolving, but one can't miss with the soft & fluffy bao buns and their delicious fillings, as well as their rice & noodle dishes.

They have an interesting beer, wine & specialty drink selections, such as Miso Michelada, Miso Bloody Mary, Sparkling Sake Mimosa. On tap, they currently offer Draughtsman Rice Lager, 3rd Window Nelson Saison & Boochcraft Kombucha. There are wine selections as well available by the glass, half-bottle and bottle.

There will be repeat visits, as we thoroughly enjoyed our dining experience at Secret Bao.

Absolutely beautiful experience. As others have mentioned, DSK is tucked--almost hidden--within Molly's Ice Cream Shoppe. If I had not done a search for vegan Wilmington restaurants, I might not have ever known this place exists.

Being our first time, we split a burger and a wrap; two smoothies wrapped up our order. Everything is made fresh. Everyone is warm, friendly, and sincere in hoping to tailor each item to a person's preferences and dietary needs.

Our food was delivered in about 15 minutes. Sweet potato chips and a huge pickle spear accompanied our lunches. The Amexem burger was delicious, thick, and held together perfectly under a slightly crispy exterior. The Caesar "chickun" wrap was quite nice as well but was overshadowed by the awesomeness of the burger, a blend of black beans, wild rice, and black rice. We'd get both again.

The absolute shining star of the meal, though, was the sour apple smoothie. Words cannot describe how magical the first sip was for me. I've never been a fan of non-yogurt based smoothies...until now. It is described on the menu as "apple, seasonal greens, ginger, and lemon," and maybe I am more easily impressed than others, but there was something extraordinary going on with that thing. Get one if you go.

I can't imagine anyone trying this place out and leaving without feeling satisfied and warm. If you are on the fence about trying it--especially if you aren't vegan and don't know if you'll like anything offered--go for it anyway. These guys know what they are doing and you'll be impressed.

Wow the 1st yelp review for the 1st location in STL 

I would give it 4/5 if the sides were larger and it wasn't so expensive. I made it for the soft opening. 

Chicken 2 piece white : 3.5/5  Kind of reminds me of old Charlie's Chicken  that was on West Florissant ( for my North side and North County ppl) juicy good and fresh  not overly spicy like Poeyes

Mac and cheese: 2.5/5 ok not overly cheesey it looked like it would have  that ole grandmother feel to it ...but it just didn't

Coleslaw: 4/5 some of the best tasting coleslaw ever tasted not too sweet just right 

Overall it's not a place I would just have to go because it's expensive and the size of the sides. However it is a place I would take people from out of town who want good chicken

Mr. Curry's is great for anyone who is new to Indian food and is trying to learn Indian flavors. When going to this lunch buffet you're able to experience a variety of Curry's and Indian dishes. And everyday they try to keep the menu just a little bit different in order to keep it exciting. 

It is set up buffet style, of course with a cook constantly refilling or exchanging the curries that are out. They had vegetable rice and basmati rice. Along with some Indian style noodles you can pair with your food. The tandoori chicken has a nice flavor and is juicy. Tikka masala is a great way to go because it has a kick and has inviting flavors and spices. Moving towards the end of the curry line is where you'll have the vegetarian options all great. 

After going through the line of curries and naan you are near sweets, Mango Lassi and Chai tea. Mango Lassi, Chai tea, and water go with your meal. You are able to sit down wherever you'd like and will pay after devouring at least two plates of Indian food. For the price mr Curry's is more than worth it. 

It is currently 9/28/17 and the price is $10 with cash and $11 with debit/credit. A fountain drink is a $1 more onto that price. But I do encourage getting the Mango Lassi and or Chai. :)

There is so much to love about the Loop's foodie scene. It's diverse and and as vibrant as all the neon lights that illuminate the neighborhood. One of the brightest stars on Delmar, though, is Corner 17! St. Louis has SO many amazing restaurants and really nails a lot of different cuisines, but I have yet to find any Chinese restaurants that can hold a candle to the quality of Corner 17. 

Let's first just talk about my favorite aspect of Corner 17, which is the window into the kitchen. This is such a FUN feature of their restaurant. For folx like myself who are self acclaimed home chefs, it is fun to watch the staff of Corner 17 hand pull the noodles that will be cooked for my meal. They are skilled and nimble! Whipping dough around the kitchen and creating gooey, yummy chunks of carbs. It's the kind of theater I am most interested in. Along with the bright green of every surface inside Corner 17, the window into the kitchen really amps up the atmosphere and creates a fun vibe as you dine. 

I love the drinks from Corner 17. Bubble tea and boba have long since been a favorite of mine (I swear I liked it before it was cool!) Their handcrafted bubble tea menu is massive. There are so many flavor options along with several ways for your drink to be prepared. I personally love getting boba AND the fruit jewels. I'm wild. I know. 

As far as the food, you really cannot go wrong with any item on the menu at Corner 17. However you MUST get dumplings. They are so perfectly doughy and fresh. I can easily house an entire order myself (speaking from experience obviously.) The spinach dumplings with mushrooms inside are my favorite. Being a creature of habit, I'm always drawn to one of two dishes when I visit Corner 17. The handsaved or handpulled noodles. I literally just wrote an entire paragraph about enjoying watching the chefs make the noodles so obviously I'm going to eat them. (Also... what an amazing marketing tool. You might walk in wanting General Tso's or some other non-noodle dish, but through the power of suggestion you're probably going to be like... shoooould I get the noodles?!) I personally prefer the handshaved noodles. They're thicker and have a much more enjoyable texture as you're gobbling them down. The protein I select usually bounces around from chicken, beef and pork. I've had them all and can confirm that they're all mindblowingly delicious. 

Corner 17 is an experience. Be in the mindset to set aside time to dine in. While service is superb, you definitely spend a fairly good amount of time when you eat at Corner 17. It's worth every second.

Seriously cannot recommend Carnivore with the amount of gusto it deserves! This chill steakhouse on the Hill has it all. You get the highest quality at a reasonable price and without the usual uppityness of some steakhouses. 

We have been to Carnivore for both brunch and dinner in the past. There's never been an experience that did not exceed our expectations. Brunch items are always delish and go down even smoother with their craft cocktails. Hello mimosas! 

We recently went to Carnivore to celebrate the 40th birthday of my best friend, Johnny. Making a reservation was as simple as stopping by their Yelp page. Upon arrival, our table was waiting and our bellies were grumbling thanks to the magical scents wafting through the air. Everyone at the table ordered something different so that we could try a little bit of all the items offered by Carnivore. My boyfriend ordered a steak flatbread that was covered in a savory gravy and mushrooms. The crust was crisp and the flavors worked perfectly together. The birthday boy ordered a filet and it was so well cooked that we could barely snap a photo before he dove in. I ordered chicken parm that was served with a plate of delicious pasta featuring paparadelle noodles (MY FAV!!) The meal was topped off with a lovely molten lava chocolate cake to celebrate 40 years of excellence! 

Overall I think the biggest selling feature of Carnivore is the laid back ambiance. They do an amazing job of creating an atmosphere of familiarity. There is absolutely no pretentiousness. They didn't even make fun of Johnny's wife when she ordered her steak well done!

Uncle Julio's has arrived in St. Louis, and folx are super excited. This higher-end Mexican restaurant that recently opened in the parking lot of the Frontenac Lifetime Fitness has been packed seemingly every night since opening their doors. 

I recently had the opportunity to grab dinner with some gal pals at Uncle Julio's and we were all underwhelmed by the experience. We had a reservation made for us, which was a solid check in the plus column as there was a nearly two hour wait to get a table when we were being seated. Our table was situated by a busy servers' stand which kind of sucked. Would assume a reservation would warrant a slightly less high traffic area. It was complete chaos as servers whipped around the corner to get to other guests.

We started off with a round of margaritas, and the server let us know (several times) that the bar was very short staffed which meant there would be quite a wait for drinks. So as soon as our drinks came we ordered another round. That was definitely a good idea because we finished our drinks well before they brought us our next round of margaritas. 

There was a snafu with our queso order. It never came. We waited and waited but never got it. When I finally brought it up, our server said the manager wanted to personally bring it out to us as soon as possible. Ok so this was a bit of a weird experience. Typically in my mind when a manager is going to be bringing out a missed or messed up item, they are most likely going to give some sort of feigned apology, offer to take it of the check, some sort of acknowledgement that there was an error on their part. But, that wasn't the case. A woman whom I assumed was the manager brought us a bowl of queso, set it on the table without saying a word and left. My friends and I all thought it was such odd customer service to make a note that a manager would be coming over, and there was no sort of interaction with said manager. Not that we needed/wanted an excuse for the lack of queso. Just thought there would be something said!

The food from Uncle Julio's is what you'd expect. Wannabe fancy fare. I ordered a fajita that came with steak, chicken and bacon wrapped shrimp. The plate was sizzling and my mouth was watering at the Instagram worthy plate. However, the taste did not live up to the hype. The shrimp was good, but throw bacon on something and you don't have to do much else. The steak was fine. Steak is steak. But the chicken. What a miss. There was zero flavor. And what's worse was the texture of the chicken. It tasted like it was super processed chicken that had been frozen and boiled before being put on my plate. I ate one piece of it and my stomach was so turned by the texture that I didn't eat any more.

Had the decision of where to eat been up to me, I probably wouldn't have picked Uncle Julio's. And to be honest, I probably won't go back. If there's a wait, it's not worth it.

I had such a great time in New Orleans it's a shame I must come back and write a less than stellar review of my temporary housing arrangements at this Hilton property.  

*Before my disgruntled review begins, I must say, the lone bright spot about this hotel is the location to Bourbon Street, French Quarter, Super dome, and other attractions downtown. 

Next time I come to N'awlins I will be staying at a different hotel but in the same proximity. While on vacation/business nobody wants added stress of navigating a terribly designed hotel with elevators that go to specific floors along with staff who all obviously posses no manners/common sense. 

I stayed at this hotel during a business trip, ohhh yeahhh...business trip to the Big Easy! Although my excitement was quickly stalled upon arriving at the hotel entrance. The film crew I was with had a some extra luggage and as the bellman greeted us at the entrance I told him we would not need any assistance. My job on the crew is to assist the camera operator and crew, which means handling the luggage. Apparently, this hotel charges $1 per item!!! to move from your car to anywhere on the property...and you are not allowed to use their luggage carts hahahaha I thought this was a joke until we were charged $20 to move a few things of camera gear to the second floor of the hotel, 1 floor up!. After arguing for several minutes and receiving a nasty attitude from several employees, we decided to not let this ridiculousness anger us anymore and moved on. 

Another disappointment. I stayed at this hotel for 4 nights. My very first night 2 separate rooms in my hallway ordered room service and then put their tray outside their door to be picked up. On my fourth night both of those trays were still in the hallway!!!!!! 4 days later half eaten food, milk and other things were laying in our hallway while housekeeping staff/employees walked past it for 4 STRAIGHT DAYS. I ordered room service on my last night and I thought for sure both trays would be picked up after dropping mine off, but sure enough, the trays remained! Not to mention the service fee, automatic gratuity, and outrageously priced $11.50 for microwavable boneless chicken wings, was the cherry on top for this dinning experience. I was shocked. 

The hotel's location is probably the only good thing about it. All hotels are the same: bed, bathroom, amenities, shelter. The hotels that stand out provide for their customers. *I don't give a flying farfegnugen who runs this place but at least make sure you are reminding employees to use common sense. I don't care what type of policies you have either, customer service should be a priority not a nuisance, its your job.

What a cool concept! I haven't seen anything like this - think Chipotle or Subway but for sushi. 

We had three rolls: 
*California Roll (inside-out seaweed wrap, crabstick, avocado, cucumber & sesame seed) - Classic California roll! No complaints here! 

*Wicked Spicy Tuna (seaweed wrap, spicy tuna, cucumber, avocado, green onion, BOSS sauce & sesame seed) - Classic spicy tuna but with spicy mayo on top! That's what the boss sauce is. The spicy tuna itself isn't too spicy - for those who don't prefer that! 

*Custom roll with double the protein (soy wrap, tempura shrimp + spicy tuna with cucumber, pickled radish and kamikaze sauce on the side) - this one was my favorite & not because I "made it." It all just tasted really fresh especially the tempura - I've had some soggy, cold tempura in my day and Sushi Boss' is NOT so. I LOVED the kamikaze sauce. It's so spicy & made fresh every day with habaneros. You can get any sauces on the side! 

These are HUGE rolls by the way - about 12 pieces each! So, the value is great. We were overstuffed with 3 rolls for 2 people. 

Sushi Boss also carries the best mochi ice cream! So, save room for dessert! 

91/365

I've been to Bouchon twice now - 1x on my 25th birthday & again almost 4 years later. I'm happy to see that Bouchon is consistently busy & tasty! NOTE NOTE NOTE: There is no association with Thomas Keller's Bouchon empire. 

My first time dining with them, we ordered a fantastic bottle of wine. We didn't order any wine during our 2nd visit. Order wine. Anyways, I had the: 
*PAN-SEARED FRESH LOCAL SEA BASS (Yukon Gold potatoes, Spanish chorizo, Littleneck clams, hazelnut Romesco, yuzu crema) - Really nicely seared sea bass. I loved the pop of salty fattiness from the chorizo & the clams were tasty. Wish there were more but it was a good portion as-is! 
*STRAWBERRY BAKED ALASKA (strawberry chiffon, Italian meringue, strawberry flambe) - We ordered this to share & it was a damn fine baked alaska by my standards.

Service was top-notch!

Walls filled with whiskey
Small, but good beer selection
Dope place, check it out

Last night at Public Brewhouse a senior Wildcat and his father told me about this place. Said it was the best whiskey selection around town. I'm not a huge whiskey drinker, but told em I would give it a rip. So here I am.
