Would have to say the whiskey list has over 100 choices, but I am not going to try to count right now. Got a beer and a bump. Mexican IPA (SahuarIPA) and two ounces neat of a Japanese Whiskey called Iwai Mars for ten bones. Tastes good, but I'm no connoisseur. Prolly have one more of something before I call it a night.

I kind of fall in love with every place I travel, but I have to say Tucson is a fun town. Struck up a conversation with some townies earlier tonight and told them that I was vacationing but down here from Phoenix where I flew into. They were like why would you bother to come to Tucson? I guess the Eiffel Tower is passé to the residents of Paris and the Red Rocks of Sedona rather mundane to those who live there. Tucson is alright. More than alright. Give it a shot and make sure to swing by Batch for a beer and a bump!

We have a winner!
Quantity and Quality
This place is the best

I guess I saved the best for last. This was my fourth and final cheesesteak in Philadelphia. For my tastes, far and away, hands down, no competition, the greatest. Went with provolone, fried onions and mayo. The meat is chopped rather than sliced which is my preference. The thing is just gargantuan and melt in your mouth delicious. As tasty as it was, I could not finish it. Left probably about a quarter of it uneaten. Think it was even busier than Pat's when I went there yesterday at noon, but I got out with a sandwich in less than fifteen minutes. The word must be out. Dalessandro's is where it's at when it comes to Philly Cheesesteaks. Next time I'm in town, I think I will make it my first stop rather than the last.

It has a nice press
Could use some more meat perhaps
Not bad, not super

Yelp led me to this place. Pretty, pretty good as Larry David would say. The Cubans in Tampa are pretty light on the meat. Not complaining if you can do it really well. They do it pretty well here. Right proportion of meat to bread. The MN versions I have had are so much meatier. Will keep exploring in the couple days that I have left. No seating inside. Small amount of outdoor seating. Green Bench is right across the street. Untappd board. Get your name up there in lights. Grab a sandwich and walk on over. Thank me later. Have to imagine it would be a perfect combo. Did I mention St. Pete is amazing? Get here, get here now in a hurry. If you don't love it, I guess you can blame me.

Bread is way too thick
Or pretty light on the meat
Had better up north

So I was at Rock Brothers Brewing in Ybor City. Asked the bartender where the best Cuban sandwich in town was. She said she did not eat Cubans but shouted out to the table behind me where I presume her manager was. They all said Carmine's has the best Cubans in Ybor. Had my heart set on Columbia, but decided to take the recommendation from the locals. Kinda disappointed. The bread overwhelmed the meat. Didn't seem like they put much of a press on it. Staff was friendly and service was somewhat prompt, but have to believe Tampa can do a better Cuban this. Maybe MN just does it better. The Cuban that I had at Buffalo Tap in Big Lake was loaded with meat and cheese and melted in my mouth. Gonna keep looking here in Tampa!

THE GOAT. I've been back and forth to Lee's for years

First. The place is great and you can sit and eat is a plus and the staff are very friend

BUT THIS IS ABOUT THE FOOD FAM

Burgers are amazing, cheesesteaks are amazing (and it you're vegan they have vegan cheesesteaks and black bean burgers)

But what really sets them off is there street food/chinese food mixup dishes that they do. They're really remarkable. 

The location is great as well because its right near downtown so once you eat go take your lady on a nice walk afterwards.

Nice stop on the pier for coffee

This is a no frills, no fuss, coffee shop (but also serves  food?!) right on the edge of the pier.  It looks like they are not getting extremely high marks for food, but if you go into the place it doesn't feel like a spot for a gourmet meal. What it is great for, and why I'm giving it four stars, is because of the beautiful view over the pier.  It has some awesome seating on the rail, right outside. I suggest going there early in the morning, maybe even for sunrise, and getting a coffee. I also grabbed a bagel, toasted with cream cheese. It felt like a Bagel experience you would have at Starbucks or coffee bean. 

Stop in for the coffee and the views!

Awesome pub & restaurant on state street

On our vacation in Santa Barbara we wanted some simple American food from a well reviewed restaurant. With 4 1/2 stars we thought this was the perfect place to go. When we showed up on Thursday the restaurant was packed! Which is great for them, awesome that they are doing such good business on a Thursday. They have sports on TV, so people were watching the Thursday night football game. Long story short we decided to take our food to go as we were tired from our first night. 

You can't order over the phone, so we ordered with the hostess who was super polite and knowledgeable about the menu. When I asked about their beer selection, she got somebody who is more knowledgeable about the alcohol they had, and the to-go Crowlers. We decided to go with the honey avocado wheat, which was so good, I highly recommend if you're into wheat beer.  We then decided to get a handful of appetizers and entrées just to split and try a bunch of the cuisine. Check below for my ratings!

Nachos
Pretzel 
Bison burger
Flatbread 

Take a look at the pictures, they were all great so I would definitely re-order all of them again. They also traveled well. I would definitely go back to watch a sporting event at the bar, seems like a great scene. I didn't see many American restaurants like this one on State Street, I could've missed them but this was a great choice.

Chill spot for wine tasting

 My wife and I were looking for a low key, fun and cool looking place to have a winetasting at.  The interior and exterior of this place was super artistic, modern and minimalist.  But when you walk inside it has so much character and the selection of wine looks so fun. There's also a furry friend to greet you when you grab your next wine to taste.

I am not very knowledgeable about wine, and haven't met many that I don't like, but each selection comes with a nice description card which really helped while trying to taste the flavors of each of the wines.  The ambience outside was awesome on a warm day, so we sat out there for a little bit. I could even go back and read a book on the patio while drinking wine.  After a few other wine experiences in Santa Barbara, I was glad we made it here. We also bought some wine that we enjoyed. I'm sure we will return once we are back in SB.

Fun brewery off the beaten path of state street

My wife and I were visiting the Funk zone in Santa Barbara for the weekend. We were able to walk around and try several different wine tastings as well as breweries. We had a few on the list, and this didn't happen to be one of them, but while walking around the funk zone we saw the big opening to the brewery that felt very inviting so we decided to sit down for a drink.

The beer here is great. They could get five stars alone for that.  I highly suggest trying a flight, with different selections to see which one you like the best, and then grab a Crowler to take home! We decided on the Kolsh, which was one of my favorite beers I had all weekend.

I would give zero stars if I could. Tragic experience. Well over an hour for our appetizers, at two hours of waiting for our meals (2 of which were also apps and one a medium burger) we started asking for our check to just leave. No one would help us and our waitress hid. After repeatedly asking to speak to a manager some guy showed up and started off by getting rude with US! He said our food took forever because it was raining (????) and their system was messed up. EVERYONE who was there when we arrived had eaten and left. A table that had just arrived had their food. Stay away, their staff is horrible, the food is horrible, and the management is a joke.

I have been to this restaurant often as my employer has us take recruits there for working lunches.  There are many good things, but to be honest I would never go there unless it was on someone else's dime.

The good:
Nice ambiance, convenient location with nearby ample parking in the downtown area.  I enjoy the ever changing menu and appreciate the uniqueness of their system and approach to food.  The waiters are knowledgeable and consistently help guide you in choosing an option that you are likely to be happy with.

The bad:
Overpriced.  The food is good, but the portions and food itself do not warrant the hefty price. (the plate is heaped with lovely inedible garnishes)

I have observed on multiple occasions that staff members routinely behave in a snobbish manner, it has occurred often enough that I've concluded it is not a fluke but rather an attitude the management at best tolerates and at worst actively cultivates.

My advice: If someone gives you a gift certificate to this restaurant go and enjoy yourself, otherwise, spend your hard earned money on an establishment that does not behave as though they are doing you a favor by serving you and offers a better value.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place before! Although I swear I've got more reviews on here that somehow have disappeared. *cues Unsolved Mysteries theme song*

Anyway, when I lived in Metairie, I used to eat here at least once every couple of weeks. Whenever the BF (now ex) and I would go to dinner or do date night, we knew it would be Fuji. Same with going on with friends. We all love this place. Why?

Because across the board, they've got everything you're looking for. Will categorize by chronological order (in order of when you'll get to experience the awesomeness of Fuji.) 

Parking- in a crowded Metairie/Kenner parking strip, normally I would be screaming with frustration trying to find a spot there. Luckily Fuji has two reserved spots that are rarely taken. So they usually have nice patrons that go here too! (Case in point, myself and all my loved ones! And even not so loved ones! lol.)

Atmosphere- they pull off the word cozy without feeling claustrophobic like Hana. Except for the Fox News blaring, (yeah, don't really understand how people can enjoy eating while watching the news. Chaos and Destruction does not make me hungry.) you would think you were transported into a Japanese sushi bar in Tokyo. Bamboo, cherry blossoms, and samauris artwork. All check!

Service- AMAZING! A place that definitely prides itself on its repeat customer. For over two years, I was one of those repeat customers. And I still go there whenever I'm in the neighborhood.

Food- I could go on and on, but I won't. Appetizers aren't really the bargain the sushi rolls definitely are. Their Hawaiian is one of my favorite things in the world. And I dream about their Rock and Roll II.

Dessert- three words: fried ice cream. The best in the city. Lots of perfectly fried banana pieces and huge scoop of vanilla ice cream. Whenever I remember to save room for it, I am always happy. 

Bathroom- Clean, two stalls. Always stocked whenever I go. No complaints.

So Fuji is definitely a class act. And in this rapidly over saturated sushi market, it's nice to see a place doing quality AND quantity. I heart you Fuji.

STOP! 

You now officially know about The BEST sushi in New Orleans. Pretty sure, the BEST sushi in the US. I'm not going to say the BEST in the world- but Japan, look out! New Orleans has been on a sushi kick for a while now, and Asuka is the proud child of our love affair with this edible art form.

Their speciality rolls are the stuff to write home about. The stuff of legends. I'm sure if Picasso or Degas were still alive today, they'd be eating at Asuka. And these are no exaggerations. In fact, I have yet to find a comparison appropriate enough for their food. 

The Louisiana Roll is definitely up for nomination for "THE Last Meal You'll Ever Eat" category. As soon as you say "crawfish, snow crab, fried shrimps, avocado, cream cheese and smelt roe wrapped in soy paper then dipped in tempura batter to be fried, drizzled with eel and spicy mayo sauce," your mouth just starts watering. This is the roll I give to people who don't like sushi. Raw fish? There's nothing in this roll that's remotely raw. Everything is cooked when it's then DEEP FRIED then drenched in sauce. Quintessential New Orleans, right?

Then they got others to satisfy your need for heat. The El Diablo is perfect for those that like a little kick in their sushi. Spicy assorted raw fish, jalapeños and Sriracha chili, this roll is guaranteed to clear up any sinus problems you have. 

I love to balance the heat from that roll with the sweetness of the Aloha roll. HUGE chunks of fresh salmon, snow crab and avocado wrapped in seaweed, with ripe mango slices on top. Then they serve it with this homemade kiwi-mango sauce. I would love to just bathe in that sauce. 

In fact, ALL their sauces are homemade. Their eel, teriyaki, tempura. I've worked AND eaten at a lot of Japanese restaurants but I've never seen one take the time and care this place does.  Owners Mia and Louis truly care about their food and patrons. And it shows.

They remember all their regular's orders, and I'm rapidly becoming one of them. In fact, I love this place so much, I've been holding onto this review because I know that my little gem will blow up and get busy. Then I take a bite of their food and realize how selfish I'm being. Everyone needs to know. 

Seriously what's not to love? EVERYTHING on their menu is amazing. Get the avocado popper and stuffed jalapeños, then thank me after!

Place is small, and it's not in the best of neighborhoods. But they did their best to make the interior seem like an oasis. Clean unisex bathroom. Comfy booths. Outstanding service. And they deliver! Be still my beating heart!

You forget about the weird parking lot and craziness of Earhart and allow all your troubles to melt away as soon as you have your first bite of that divine goodness. 

I normally don't consider myself a religious person, but places like Asuka make you realize that God created a mouth and tastebuds, so we can taste food like their LA roll. The creaminess of that melted cream cheese is the perfect compliment to all that seafood and fried batter. I never thought you could top the yumminess of fried shrimp, but Asuka does with style and flair. And a touch of grace. 

Sometimes, I'm eating my roll, and I'm transported to another dimension. I have a transcendental moment when I realize the sheer perfection of each mouthful of food. Nothing else matters but each bite. Bills, arguments, worries melt away as my entire being focuses on the next morsels. 

How could each ingredient compliment each other so well? How could you literally taste LOVE in each bite? How can something taste as beautiful as it looks?

Those are my koans as I seek joy and peace through these rolls and this tiny restaurant in that easy-to-miss intersection.

And moments like that make me realize I'm the ultimate foodie. 

Asuka and their LA roll is my Heaven. 

Hallelujah!

Yelp, once again, you don't steer me wrong. When it comes to food, fellow Yelpers definitely can show you the wonderful hole-in-the-walls with the best food. 

Pagoda Cafe is one of those places. Outdoor seating only, by the time I got there, I grabbed the last table they had- right in front of the guy playing his guitar. I loved his version of "Do You Know What It Means to Miss New Orleans?" It's a great place to people watch and enjoy a cup of caffeinated drink. I went with a hot turmeric tea. No upcharge for coconut or almond milk! 

Breakfast tacos had great flavor. Like everyone said, it's missing crunch. Wonder if the bacon would have provided that since it was definitely missing something. I was also wishing for some creamy avocado. Did love the fiery green sauce that came with it. Gave the tacos some needed dimension. 

Sausage roll had a wonderful flaky pastry crust and a delicious sweet tomato dipping sauce. Best pig in a blanket I've ever had. Very gourmet-tasty. It's obviously they make these fresh. 

Scone was flaky and had a yummy lemon curd. It was the perfect amount of curd to the scone. Also homemade, they did not skimp on the raisins. I normally pick out raisins but somehow they managed to cook their raisins enough that they weren't a soggy mess or leave that nasty cooked raisin bitter residue around everything it touches. 

Favorite thing on the menu was their Indian Banh Mi. I added the lemongrass tofu, and I honestly think it's the perfect sandwich. I want to put that chutney on everything- where has it been my entire life?? And then the beets! Seriously, I will defend this sandwich against many of the mediocre roast beef and shrimp po-boys around town. This Bahn Mi should be the sandwich to impersonate since no one else can attempt to replicate. 

Already made a mental note to try EVERYTHING ELSE on the menu.

This place is definitely a hidden gem within Mid City. Hidden in a corner store, I used to pass by the place all the time. Until one day I was perusing Yelp for some good pho in Mid-City.  

And I've never looked back. They're never busy (maybe because it can be seen as a seedy convenience store, you don't really want to linger) and you have to go to the back of the store to order. But I don't mind the sketch when you taste the quality of their food. 

Now, I have been slightly obsessed lately with their pho. Chockful of ingredients, I was wonderfully surprised by how similar it was to my mom's delicious concoction the first time I tasted it. Rich and brothy, it was obvious it had been simmering overnight so the ingredients and flavors had plenty of time to marinate. They also gave me traditional Vietnamese herbs and plenty of bean sprouts. I also like the fact that they use the same hoisin sauce as we do at home. Best of all, you feel satisfied afterward and don't feel the need to drink lots of water since it's not laced with MSG.

Their fried shrimp po-boy done Vietnamese style is also really really good. You don't get tons of shrimp, but the shrimp is perfectly fried. Plus it's a different flavor from the traditional po-boys so I'll get this when I want something different. Wasn't a fan of their bun bo hue. The meat was a little grisly and there wasn't enough noodles. Broth was deep and flavorful though. 

One star off because sometimes they're brisk and seem to be sick more often than not. And sometimes they will overcharge you for things. So check the register to see what they're ringing up.

Kicked off a girls night here with espresso martinis. The first round was okay, but the second round was much better! We ordered deviled eggs as an appetizer, which came with 5 different styles of deviled egg.

For dinner, I ordered the kale salad with grilled chicken. It was good! This place seems dependable. Not necessarily the most exciting culinary experience of my life, but it was pretty good!

Heaven, I'm in Heaven, / And my heart beats so that I can hardly speak; / And I seem to find the happiness I seek /

The happiness you seek is at Hinoki Sushi.  When you step inside, a cool interior with just the right touches of live bonsai trees ,angular lights, and attractive seating greets you as well as an attentive hostess and a team of smiling sushi chefs.  I had heard whispers of a new sushi place on the scene and I had to check them out.  Especially since one of my friends and trusted sushi advisers has already put his stamp of approval on it.  Each piece was cut to perfection and buttery, and the rolls were innovative and thoughtful, my favorite being the place's special, the Hinoki.  Try this place if you are out and about!

Came here based on the reviews of my Yelp friends -- they didn't fail us!  Small establishment, and a rather limited menu, but don't be deterred, this place is worth the stop. A basket of chips is provided after you order, and a salsa bar w/ an array of salsas is available to enjoy while you wait for table delivery.  The salsas were superb! They even offer a ghost pepper version, which I steered clear of . . . I had an asada burrito w/ the works: flour tortilla was light and fresh, and the onions and cilantro were so good. Only drawback for me was the asada, which appeared to be ground up, rather than chopped in small pieces. Still, excellent flavors all around!  Throw in a comfortable outdoor seating area, and we have a place that is worthy of regular visits.

Cheers!
RL

During the winter months, parking is a dream. It takes all of 2 minutes. Unfortunately, during those dreary, cold months, the vendors are not as abundant as the warmer months. Regardless, I will come here when I can for my new juicing addiction. When I started, I went to the commissary, Walmart & Target and never saw the true appeal of juicing. It was expensive and frankly, the fruit/veggies weren't that tasty. My co-worker mentioned going to the Farmer's Market and I figured it was worth a shot. After the first venture out there, I was hooked. Everything was so cheap, fresh, delicious and LOCAL! 

I have my personal favorite vendors, but really, they're all amazing. They're more than willing to tell you all about their produce or just chit chat for a few minutes. I've yet to meet an unfriendly vendor.

What sets this apart from normal grocery shopping? You can make a stop at their drink stand, order your beverage of choice (I do love a good bloody mary on Saturday morning) and make your rounds. Getting your groceries is so much more enjoyable with a delicious, cheap drink in your hand. 

I could go on and on about how phenomenal the Soulard Farmer's Market is, but you really have to experience it firsthand. They have meats, spices, chocolate and produce galore. You'll find things you never knew you needed here. Just go.

i took mushrooms before coming here and that was a very bad idea.

the french toast was insane and looked like fried chicken but was very very very sweet and the disconnect between sight and taste made my head spin.

the decor was bananas. dogs everywhere. looked like a movie set country club. but it was dark and air conditioned so it didn't make me feel too weirdsies.

the clientele was mostly very terrible. the man behind me was huge and had a voice like james coburn. he and his mom, whose voice sounded exactly like george costanza's mom, were having a terrible conversation and it was making me anxious and sad.  "why do people who flip burgers need health insurance?" were the first words i heard him say.

the waiter was nice but i kept having the thought that he was working there to get credit for a class.

it was expensive and i just wanted to be outside.


look, all i'm saying is: don't go here while you're out of your mind on mushrooms.

FIN

I've had a lot of positive experiences at OTP and I'm finally taking the time to write a review. I love the overall vibe of this restaurant and every time I return they keep adding in cooler menu items. 

The Mac and cheese is phenomenal if you are a gruyere person. It just melts in your mouth! Ahi tuna nachos are also delicious, ive also had a similar ahi tuna item off their farns and rail (speakeasy) menu. Now for the fall they have fun seasonal cocktails and a great draught beer list! I went for the Apple cider Marg my last visit, perfect fall drink! 

I also have to say they were very accommodating with their outdoor seating even when we came with two strollers (one for a baby and one for a dog). We were seated right away and received great service! The outdoor seating area and chairs have also been upgraded and expanded and make for a great outdoor, Covid friendly experience. 5 stars!

This is a pretty nice place for lunch if you have time for a leisurely meal.  Not a place I'd recommend for a quick lunch.  Also, this is not a vegan friendly place, unless you'd like to order a salad and ask them to add beans?  The black bean burger contains egg, unfortunately.  Would love to see even one vegan dish called out on this very large menu! 

We arrived at noon on a Monday, and we didn't get our food served till about 1:05 PM. Everyone agreed the food was pretty good, and the price point is very reasonable.  We had good service while we waited, getting checked on very well for drink refills.  

Parking may be easier for dinner hours, but our party had to hunt for parking spots in this shared lot.  This restaurant was quite busy and it shares the lot with several other businesses.

Delicious 100% vegan lunch including dessert downtown for $6.99?  Yes please! So very happy with my first meal here!  I tried the Poori and Potato Masala and loved every bite! I also ordered the Medhu Vada, thinking there was no way a $6.99 meal would fill me up. I was wrong, but loved trying this too!  I went with my team from work and every one of us loved our meals. Will definitely be coming back! Great price point, quantity, flavor, and location in West Street Market! 

This business is sharing the Thali restaurant space but serving lunch. All vegetarian or vegan and *mostly* gluten free. The owners were so nice and came out to ask us if we liked our meals and if we had any feedback for them.  Such a nice touch!

Make your reservations now, because this place is going to be PACKED shortly!   This little gem has only been open a couple weeks, and it's already, in my opinion, a stellar addition to Reno dining. I predict this is going to be a very hard place to get a table at in the next month or two.

What I absolutely loved:
- Food was beautifully prepared, fresh, and creative
- Delicious locally sourced produce and lots of it on the plates!
- Classy, intimate vibe with great music playing and comfy seating
- Delightfully unexpected beverage options
- Super quick to take our drink orders and bring them to the table
- Clearly marked vegan options, lots of veggie options, even more than one vegan dessert option (hallelujah)
- Service was warm and friendly.  
- Server easily told us if any of the daily specials/desserts were vegan or could be customized.
- Convenient location in Midtown with easy parking on Cheney 
- Cute outdoor seating
- They are now serving breakfast and lunch. Yes!

What could have been better this time, but they redeemed themselves: 
Out of five of us at our table tonight, one of us had an entree arrive late. The server explained the owner didn't like the way the sauce came out on her entree and decided to remake it rather than serve it up not up to their standards.  However, our server let us know and gave us status updates.  At the end of the meal, she took that entree off the bill too.  Bravo!  Excellent service.  

We will definitely be making reservations here again.  Lovely experience dining here this evening!  Cannot wait to check out the new breakfast and lunch menus!

When Taste of Chicago's food truck just decided to bail on their commitment, or even let Friends of Black Rock know ahead of time that they were not going to show up at the Bartley Ranch Amphitheater this evening for our non profit fundraiser, we stopped by here and they were so understanding and helped us out in a hurry! Excellent customer service!  We had heard so many great things about this business, and these guys totally saved our event this evening! Applause!! Seriously, they got a ton of pizzas ready soooo fast to save us!

Do you hear that?  It's my happy cheers for this new kick ass **VEGAN** local brewery.  Not only are they keeping it kind, but Revision is showing it's local love by sourcing ALL of its malt barley from Fallon, Nevada!  Nice work guys! 

From the outside this place looks a bit industrial, but you walk in and it's got a nice long simple bar and lots of picnic benches.  There was relaxing reggae playing in the background and a totally chill atmosphere with people playing a cornhole game in the back area.  The back area gives you a nice view of the beautiful array of brewing equipment and a bonus blast of a fun bright graffiti mural on their ginormous walk in cooler.  

There is lots of parking on the street and a smaller private lot in front.  The bartenders are super nice and quick here. 

I tried five of their brews today, and I have to say my favorite was the HOP ANATOMY.  I have a feeling this is going to be a star for Revision Brewing Company.  It's crisp and dry with a slightly sweet finish. Very light and refreshing. The first scent that hits you is like a mix of grapefruit zest and maybe a thin slice of ripe peach.  LOVE IT!!!   

While they don't serve food, Revision Brewing Company is cool with you bringing outside food and is down for some live bands and food trucks coming up.  On a normal day, though, you happen to be right across the street from #96 on Yelp's Top 100 Restaurant's of 2016 here:  Carlillos Cocina.  How could you ask for more people?

I was super lucky and spoke with the very nice owner and brewmaster, Jeremy Warren, who showed me the products they use himself, and he confirmed they do not use isinglass or gelatin in their fining process. THANK YOU!!  Instead, Revision Brewing Company uses Biofine Clear, which I have verified is NOT derived from animal products or animal by-products.   

Giving you a big Yelp hug Revision Brewing Company!  You can find their beer at Whole Foods right now, if you can't make it down to the brewery yourself.  They also will be at Ben's and Raley's too.

Umm, so Friends of Black Rock (an awesome local non profit) had a verbal commitment from Steve with Taste of Chicago a week ago that the Taste of Chicago food truck would be here tonight at the Bartley Ranch Amphitheater for their annual Wild Scenic Film Festival fundraiser. Twenty minutes before it started at 5:00 today, they were not here yet.  When they were called, they just answered nonchalantly that they wouldn't be coming. WTF??? 

When asked why, they said it was "too cold".  It would have been just SUPER if Taste of Chicago had been professional and kind enough to let Friends of Black Rock know maybe this morning? Maybe this afternoon? Or at all? that they just decided not to come, don't you think?? They stranded 70-80 people without food at the last minute. 

Would I, or anyone here recommend Taste of Chicago to anyone?  No way in hell!

Absolutely horrible experience here for many reasons, and BEWARE FOOD POISING

First of all, the service.. We had about three waiters.. and although the place was about half full when we arrived we were seated right in the middle of a crowded area and right next to the waiter station.  We asked if we could move and our host literally said "hmm I'm not sure its my first day" and just walked away! So we were stuck in the middle in the spotlight listening to our three waiters conversations about 3 feet away.  NOT a romantic environment in the slightest.   

Next, the food.  My girlfriend ordered oysters for the appetizer.  You would think at such a fancy and expensive restaurant they would know how to properly open the oysters, but they did not.  My girlfriend was disgusted to find numerous bits of shell cracked into her oysters.  Additionally I ordered the goat cheese mac-n-cheese and a potato cheese meal.  They were actually pretty good though all it was was oil butter and cheese, I suppose I expected something a little bit more even if it is just mac-n-cheese.

and finally.. the food poising and GSR's awful customer service

About 30 hours after our meal, my girlfriend became violently ill (it was her birthday weekend mind you).  I will spare you the details but suffice to say as the time progressed she was unable to get out of bed except to crawl over to the bathroom.  Additionally, she developed a strong fever reaching over 103.  The fever points to the fact that this was most likely a bacterial infection from something she ate.  Any guesses what??? Judging by the 24-48 hour window, and the fact that we ate the same food until the steakhouse leaves only... THE OYSTERS.  This lasted two days and I was about to take her to the emergency room when her fever started going away.

So naturally, I emailed the GSR about our terrible experience here and warned them about their oysters. I received no reply at all.  Next, I posted on their Facebook asking them if they had alerted the kitchen about the potential food poisoning there; they responded and asked me to contact a special email address.  Contacted them the next morning.  It has been 3 days and still no reply at all. Completely unacceptable.  How is this place even remotely respectable?

Great burger place, In the Gultch part of Nashville. Popular destination. Very clean and well run. All staff is friendly and accommodating. They have lots of specialty toppings and ways to fix your sandwich. You pick the bread, protein and  side. 
We had a few drinks... a spiked milkshake (not sure when this became popular, daughter likes them) I got a cold one, son had coke. All came out quickly along with our fried pickle appetizer. It was a cup of thinly sliced, tart pickles, lightly floured and season cooked nicely, I little greasy but we gobbled them up quickly. 
We each got a burger, the fineness was not right on the kids burgers so they did a biology, dissection of their hamburgers to trade patties? Which I said we can just send them back, they seemed okay with it, we mentioned to the server because you hope they will look at their process and be better next time. The server promptly got the manager and she was very nice and said she will look into it. Which was fine, again just wanted them to know. 
All good we finish and the bill comes back with no drinks on it, not our intention to get free things, this manage wanted us to have a better experience. Thanks again to the staff and yes we did tip to the full bill ! 
I will be back!

Holler and Dash Biscuit House - 
Mission: Our mission is to make the world better one biscuit at a time.
Food Philosophy: We believe comfort food should sizzle with excitement. And while our menu is rooted in traditions from the South, it's far from standard fare--with big bold flavors, premium ingredients and heirloom recipes reinvented for the way you want to eat right now.
Once you taste our biscuit sandwiches, we think you'll agree.
This is something special.

Very nice late breakfast. The parking in back in ample and available. 
We entered through the convenient back door and it is open and roomy; fresh decor. It is a walk up and order (WAO).  Very reasonable prices, so we tried a few items, pictures included. 
We got an order of the Fried Green tomatoes (3 to an order), light, well seasoned cornmeal batter - fresh with a hint of tart.  Next the Tatar Bowl, a mound of Tatar tots covered with bacon, cheddar and green onion, and Hollerback sauce on the side.

I had the Bacon, egg and cheese biscuit and my dining partner had the biscuit and jam. Both excellent, the biscuit is a dense, soft middle with a crunchy exterior, held up to all my ingredients.  

The Hollerback sauce is tangy and tasty, and went well with the tomatoes and the tots (need to know what is in this sauce...). 
Have to say Biscuit Love will be hurting with H&D on the rise. 
Many more items to try. 
I will be back!

Great place in Nashville. Quality cider and fun place to go, they have to live around the product and set up their seating in the afternoon. Met the owner who was very friendly and informative about their business and process. They have a nice menu to complement their outstanding ciders. 
I will be back!

My co-workers and I decided that we wanted lunch and this is where they had planned to go. I'm not going to lie, I was a hella skeptical at first because I'm like - "what can you really do with a bagel, especially at lunch?" Plus, I'm on a new diet, so I'm not really into bread. 

However when I got here, I found there were so many options on what I could try. There are so many varieties of sandwiches that they make, with assortment of bagels. The possibilities are just endless!

I was very happy with my sandwich and it was awesome. My diet call for fish, so I was happy their were a few options I could go to. I think I had the Tuna Meltdown. I really want to try Loxy Lady on my next visit.

I will definitely plan to come back here to try some more varieties of sandwiches. It's just so funny because I always walk by this place and never even gave it the time. Nor had I looked up to see what kind of establishment it was.  But I'm glad that I explored a new place in Indy which was outside of my comfort zone. I am happy I gave this place a chance;  I would highly recommend everybody do the same!

The food is great and the wait staff are excellent. 
I have a food allergy to oats and had fuzzy brain. I ordered the steak and eggs not realizing bread came with it. After seeing my food I asked if oat was in the bread, which it did have. I apologized to my server and he happily went to have it remade. Then the hostess swooped in and snidely remarked to me that the menu SAYS to inform them of all food allergies. 
I am sorry? I forgot? I am human? I apologized to my server and as it was my mistake, was happy to wait. 
The hostess needs to go. She is rude, smart mouthed and awful.

Update: Hostess saw me writing this review at my table. Demanded to know my name, which I would not give her, and informed me the restuarant will be responding to this post. As such, I took this review down to one star. How unprofessional.

Literally the WORST experience I've ever had a restaurant.
We went for my boyfriends birthday and had an 8pm rez.
Got there literally at 8 and the very rude hostess directed us to wait outside for our table to be ready. Well we waited..and waited...and waited...and after the hostess passed us back and forth about 40 times I finally asked what was going on with our table... 30 minutes later. I dont mind waiting if there really is a back up, but when I see empty tables and I'm being ignored it is really frustrating. It is BYOB so we sit down and no one comes to open our wine or pour water. I ask the bus person to open our wine and she looks annoyed. She takes the bottle and doesnt return with it for about 15 minutes. Still no water. We order food and I am told that I am not allowed to swap fingerling potatoes for the mashed potatoes that my steak comes with. Dont really understand that because I told her I was more than happy to pay the upcharge if necessary-still wouldnt swap them. Still no water. We waited about 30 minutes for our soups and after our apps we waited about another 45 min for our entrees. THIS is the kicker-there is only ONE person in the kitchen doing EVERYTHING for the whole restaurant, hence the wait times. OH and how do I know this? Because it is an open kitchen. So on top of the terrible service, rude employees and our meals taking forever...we have to listen to the chef scream and curse at the bus people/hostess/and server. Literally cursing the entire meal for the whole dinning room to hear. REAL professional. I was so upset. It was a terrible birthday dinner and I felt so horrible for my sweet boyfriend. As we were paying the check the server asks if they had ruined the birthday meal....ugh yea, i would say that you most definitely did. 
I will never eat here again and i tell everyone i know how horrible the evening was.

An ISC stop and overall a very good place!  First of all they have great parking which is huge for U City.  The building has a garage door/wall that can be opened when the weather is nice for outdoor seating.  
On this evening they were able to accommodate 13 of us.  When I first came across this restaurant I wasn't sure what to make of it.  I initially thought it was just a pizza place but it is actually a rustic style Italian themed restaurant with a loft like feel.  There is a bar with flat screen TVs to satisfy the sports fan.  

The specials this evening were a Lobster Risotto, Short Ribs, and a Trout dish.  We started with the Beet Salad and the Cauliflower soup.  Both were wonderful.  There was actually more beets than salad but the catcher was the fried goat cheese on top that added the perfect savory touch.  The cauliflower soup was very smooth and hit the spot on this rainy cold night.  
I ordered the short ribs because I couldn't resist.  The short ribs were overall tender but parts were a little tough.  Not bad though and with a good red wine taste.  They were served on a bed of garlic mashed potatoes and a handful of asparagus. 

Overall a nice restaurant with a good variety of food not just pasta or pizza.  My only regret is that I didn't have enough room for dessert!  

Great choice for ISC Sarah!

I have to admit I haven't had much Lebanese food before but had the opportunity to try Layla thanks to ISC!  

It is a little different than I expected but then also somewhat what I expected.  I wasn't really expecting thick juicy burgers made with different meats and with explosive colorful toppings along with milk shakes with rose water at a Lebanese restaurant... but I was glad they had them.  

We started our meal with the grape leaves appetizer which is similar to the dolmades in a greek restaurant.  These were stuffed with couscous, raisins, and goat cheese.  These had a wonderful taste but the grape leaves may have been a little under cooked.  I sure didn't mind.  

I also ordered the Beirut burger which included a slice of lamb on top of beef topped with apricot ketchup, sumac onions, flash fried kale and lemon garlic mayo.  I almost had to unhinge my jaw to take a bite but of course I managed.  The burger was extremely juicy and flavorful.  The flash fried kale trumped standard lettuce easily.  Definitely a winner.  You have to try the Beirut burger if you come here.  

The only hiccup of the night was the internet went down for a period of time delaying our ability to pay with a credit card.  

Did I mention they have private parking!!!  Always a plus in the Grove.  

Overall, thank you Sarah and the ISC for bringing me to a place it would have taken me months to years to try out on my own.  
Layla is definitely on my short list to return!

I've wanted to try this place for a long time, and what's kept me from coming has been some Yelp reviews.  Many of them claim that the wait to get your food can be lengthy and I wasn't about that life.  However this past weekend I had eaten a filling breakfast before I went to church so I wasn't dying once the service ended, so the possible wait time didn't bother me as much.

Once our entire party arrived we were seated right away.  Not soon after came 3 tall glasses of Philly's delicious tap water.  We ordered pretty quickly and our food came out in a reasonable amount of time.  

Overall PYT is a great place to have lunch.  The food was good.  Now, I had the Firebird Srirachi chicken sandwich which claims to be hella spicy.  Umm, try again PYT.  Perhaps a mere 1 on a 10-point scale.  Regardless, the food was delicious.  And the waffle fries, the best waffle fries I've ever had.  The service was also great.  Our server accommodated every one of our requests.  Definitely a great spot for good laughs with friends.

We took my mother in law for mothers day, the service there was no service. We ordered food 45 minutes later we asked the waitress if our food was ready,she said yes. Found out she had lied yo us,our food order never made it to the kitchen. We will never eat there again.

OK, I'm going on record saying this is the best place in Nashville to get your traditional Banh Mi Vietnamese sandwich.  Though i've only tried Kien Giang, Far East Nashville, and Dai Viet here in Nashville. I did grew up in an area known for its Vietnamese fare.  For those that are unfamiliar, its served on a baguette with either butter, mayo or pate as a condiment.  It also has pickled veg, cucumber, chilies, and a grilled meat (pork is the best)  Seems relatively simple but man oh man it's good.   When you come in, you've got to put your order at the register and they give a quick call to the back of the store to be made.  It's a great deal at under $3.

The grocery is a great place to find more of your exotic Asian ingredients.  And personally i like the feel of this smaller market as opposed to a Wal-Mart esque grocery like the K&S Market.  Also, remember to bring cash, because they don't accept credit cards. 

On weekends, they have another gem that is difficult to find in Nashville. Roast Duck and Roast Pork.  Get there early cause it sells out quickly, and you don't want to miss out on there succulent meats.  Yum.

I'm on vacation in Philly and seems like all I've done is eat!

And by far, one of the best restaurants that I've been to is Lolita's.  Granted, I did not order a complete meal.  I simply had an appetizer and dessert.  But the food and the service was phenomenal.  Great service was provided by Lewis, he was kind enough to give his opinion and try to steer me in the right direction.  I settled on carnitas con naranja y canela.  Yeah, like we all know exactly what that is!  It's orange-ginger glazed pork with a hint of mexican cinnamon and was served with pickled red onions, guacamole and salsa.  I loved it, the favors were amazing and it was deliriously spicy hot.

For dessert, I had tres leches de coco.  And while it was not the best version of this dessert that I have ever had, it was still delicious.

I highly recommend this restaurant.  I went in on a Friday night and the place was packed.  And rightfully so.

The food I really really enjoyed. We got the bacon popcorn, mac and cheese, bean dip, and Brussels sprouts, all of which I would highly recommend. On our way to a 5 star rating... until things took a turn. 

My friend and I were eating dinner upstairs in a room alone, it was a cute room, we were enjoying our time, when all of a sudden we see a huge MOUSE scurry across the floor. Mouse ran back into the wall and minutes later comes out again. At this point we had just ordered full beers so we immediately leave the room and tell the servers about the situation and head downstairs to finish the rest of our beers. My disappointment comes from the way the staff handled this situation. We got a half hearted sorry from the server and absolutely nothing else. I am never one to go looking for free things but honestly, if you're in a food establishment and your guests see a mouse, I think something else should have been done. It also scares me that this mouse was just running around in the middle of a dining room. I tried not to even think about what could be happening in the kitchen..

SO super excited this place opened up! This place has it all! Many vegan options and local craft beer, which is a added bonus for me. 

The pesto is absolutely amazing. I always get it in some form when I order food. I've enjoyed the seasonal soups along with the veggie panini and the stick it to the manwich. 

The environment is awesome, too. I brought my laptop on a friday night to a soup and work on some projects. A good amount of sockets located around the set up to make it easy to access an outlet for my laptop. 

Love it here and will be back again and again!

Hot chicken or Nashville hot chicken is a type of fried chicken that is a local specialty of Nashville. Typically a breast, thigh, or wing that has been marinated in a blend of seasonings, floured, fried, and finally sauced using a paste that has been spiced with cayenne pepper.   There are many restaurants in Nashville that serve a variant of the dish, but I recommend you try it here.  I honestly didn't see any sauce.  Please note.... this is not your typical "Buffalo wing"...... so do not expect that. 

Upon entry I asked the hostess what style she generally orders.... here response, "gurrllll I order the mild!"  I was honestly shocked by this.  She said its pretty hot.  She had me a little nervous, but I was ready to dive in.  I reviewed my options: mild, medium, Nashville Hot, and Poultrgyeist.  I ordered the medium "Nashville Hot" chicken.  Let me say... medium was soooo freaking hot!!!!!  I could not finish my meal and I needed to take a Zantac.  EEK!   But I honestly enjoyed meal.  I would certainly go back again....and would definitely order mild.

I sat at the bar at Nektar in new hope, PA watching people walk by while experiencing one of the nicest weather days this year. The glass, floor to ceiling windows were fan folded out of the way to allow an unobstructed view of the outdoors. More outdoor and indoor seating are available just past the bar. Unfortunately the yellow jackets joined us, otherwise the atmosphere is very nice. 

I savored a refreshing glass of Honig Sauvignon Blanc and nibbled on delicious procuitto and aged Dutch goat gouda. The server was young and knowledgeable about the premium spirits on hand and had no arrogance about her. 

In addition to wine, they have draught, craft & bottled beer as well as infused vodka. They also feature an extensive whiskey selection. Their menu is mostly small plates. Prices are a bit high but freshness and quality seem to justify it. If you are looking for a place to relax and wet your appetite, try Nektar Wine Bar.

Greenhouse is a trendy new bar and restaurant on South Main Street in New Hope, PA.  The historic building houses an upstairs loft where bands perform, a pool table and tables while downstairs is a much cozier lounge and dining area.  They have a sidewalk patio for fair weather outside dining while you people watch.

We tried Greenhouse for a change of pace from our regular favorites.  We were given a choice of tables between the one under the intense heater and the one adjacent the door.  We choice the one nearer to the door and it wasn't too drafty at all.  Our young server was very good and never once stopped smiling.  The menu was not overwhelming but had great unusual pairings of flavors such as the blood orange glazed chicken, which I had.  Normally, a vegan dish that the chef had no trouble preparing for me with real boneless chicken breast. The vegetables and rice noodles made this a truly enjoyable dish.

Vegan and gluten free offerings are easily identified on the menu and they are plentiful making this a great choice for your special diet.  If you are not looking for a large plate like I had, you can enjoy small plates, burgers, tacos, and sandwiches.  A great selection of beer, wine and mixed drinks.  

I was impressed on many levels with Greenhouse.  The owner and hostess were working at a feverous pace to make certain everywhere was clean and spotless.  The delicious food made from the freshest ingredients and the creativity that went into constructing their menu make me want to return to Greenhouse.  I recommend that you give them a try.

I could come here, pay close to $10 for a smoothie, and feel like I'm inconveniencing the unfriendly staff...

OR

I could go somewhere else.

See what I did there?

Southtown Pub's BBQ is better than Pappy's. It just is. And I don't have to wait in a line wrapped around a building with a bunch of crabby, anxious freaks that will just melt the F down if they run out of ribs. Jesus. You Pappy's people...

Anyway. I'd never been here until last week, despite living around the corner from it for two years. From the older reviews, it sounds like my decision to wait was a good one. For once.

I wouldn't call this place a dive bar. I'd call it a neighborhood bar, maybe. TVs with games on. Friendly patrons.I found it cozy. It smells of amazing barbecue and promises of good things to come as soon as you walk in. 

On this particular night, they were closing the kitchen at 8 pm for an employee holiday party. They awesomely went ahead and made us food anyway though. The turkey is the best anywhere. The wings were ridiculous. They were giving employee prices on drinks that night, so that was a bonus. 

Also, to settle the great mac n' cheese debate in this town: this place has the best. Shaved Duck is too inconsistent to be considered the best. Sweetie Pie's is good until it actually hits your stomach and you're just down for the night. But this was like Kraft on crack. I'm a fan. 

So for those of you reading this on your phone while you wait in the Pappy's line, stop staring down that family of four hoping they'll get up soon and you can shark their table. You can have all the spoils of amazing BBQ without the stress at STP. 

And you can watch SPORTS.

Cha-ching.

Gather round, Yelpers. It's time for another rousing edition of Angela's NSFW Restaurant Nightmares. 

Two friends and I went to Courtesy at around 2 am last night. We'd been out all night, had sobered up, and wanted some food. We have a long history with Courtesy Diner being our favorite place to go after a night out. It's been our standby for nearly a decade. One friend who went with me even got her engagement pictures taken there, because she and her now-husband used to love going there after a night out, too. 

We walk in last night and all of the tables are full. We're the only ones waiting. A table gets up, pays, leaves. Naturally, we go have a seat at the open table and wait for someone to clear it.

That's when shit got real.

As the three of us are sitting there, this female cook comes storming over and immediately starts yelling at us. "You don't listen do you?? I said NOT TO SIT THERE UNTIL SOMEONE CLEARED IT OFF."

What in the actual FUCK. 

We try to tell her that, no, she didn't say that to us. We didn't even see her when we walked in, nor did any of us speak with her. We just did what we ALWAYS do -- find an open table, sit down, and wait.

When we very politely (and frightfully) tell her she's mistaken, she starts to yell more and informs us that she will NOT be cooking for us and we can get the hell out.

Yes, folks. The long-standing question of "what does one have to do to get kicked out of a shithole like Courtesy Diner?" has finally been answered. You have to do nothing. You have to walk in, sit down, and a methed-out cook on bath salts will come over out of fucking nowhere, physically slam her fist down on your table, cuss you out, and demand you get out.

She walks away. We sit there baffled for a good five minutes, wondering if we're on an episode of Punk'd or if it was just a misunderstanding. We still want our god damned hash browns, so we sit for a few more minutes thinking it will blow over. 

Every waitress cold shouldered us. They wouldn't even LOOK at our table. Finally, I get one's attention and very politely ask what the hell just happened. 

The waitress informs us that the cook told the staff not to wait on us because we called her a bitch.

WHAT IN THE ACTUAL FUCK PART 2.

No one. NO ONE at our table even uttered the word "bitch". Had we actually believed what was happening, maybe we would have. But we were in such total shock by her initial outburst that we didn't say much of ANYTHING.

So to recap: 3 fairly sober adults walk into a diner they've been going to for years, sit down, get terrorized by Captain Bath Salts, sit there for a few more minutes, then say "fuck it" and go to Steak n Shake. Where the service was shitty. But after fearing for your life at the Courtesy Diner, Steak n Shake's the god damned Ritz.

Fuck this place. Avoid at all costs.

Ok, this place is awesome. I used to live in the South and was spoiled with great BBQ places. I always complain there are no good places to get BBQ around here. I am so happy Mission BBQ opened. This is a fast casual place. First, I love the nod to military and first responders. There is different memorabilia all over the restaurant. They also play country music. After researching Mission BBQ, I learned they donate to a lot of organizations that support veterans and other good charities. They also donated lunch to my husband's work. I think all of this is awesome. 

Now, for the food. We have visited three times so far and everything I've had has been great! I've tried the pulled pork and pulled chicken sandwich. For sides, we love the mac and cheese and cheesy mashed potatoes. They also have a bunch of different great barbecue sauces to try. We got the giant brownies they have at the register once and they were delicious. I also love their lemonade. Customer service is great, the people that work here are overly nice including the managers. So happy to have this place in the area even if it isn't super close to me. Now go get some BBQ, you won't be disappointed.

ROAD TRIP
Summer 2016

"Pleaaaassse no more junk food,"' I said to my fambam. "Let's go to this highly rated restaurant on Yelp!" I probably sounded like a snob but I didn't want to get a stroke during this trip. 

We went to Fork and the hostess said,"Unfortunately, we can't seat eleven people today, we're all reserved for Father's Day." 

Oh crap. I forgot. Well, we are in downtown, we'll find something! Across the street was this pho place and they were able to seat us! HALLELUJAH PRAISE THE LORD! Oh, and an old Vietnamese guy cooking in the kitchen was a good sign!

We started with the crunchy egg rolls. The server suggested to put it in the lettuce wrap and I liked it even better! I had the beef shank pho with beef meatballs. All the meat were cooked perfectly and the broth was so good I wanted to sip it with a straw. My toddler, who refused to eat, slurped the broth from her bowl and ate a lot of meat. Where does one go for breakfast after a pleasant (dinner, show, and after drinks) overnight at the Grand Sierra Nevada Casino?  McDonald's on the way home!  That's our pattern folks.  When the stay is over, there's no use lingering over breakfast at the Hotel.

A work colleague and I were sitting at Pat O'Briens, enjoying our Hurricanes, relaxing after a long work week, being amused by the Bourbon Street people traffic, and wondering where we should go for Dinner. Jeff launched his Yelp App and I proceeded to look over the many options. I picked Café Amelie and with no disrespect towards my friend, wished that it was Gayle that I was going here for a nice evening out.

Café Amelie is located away from the hustle and bustle of Bourbon Street and features comfortable, quiet, and romantic seating either inside the historic (and air conditioned) Carriage House or outside within the lush 150-year-old Princess of Monaco Courtyard. We sat outside as the setting is gorgeous, but the oppressive Gulf Coast heat and humidity did result in some second thoughts. 

The food was fabulous and was only a little bit ahead of the excellent service. Jeff enjoyed a jerked pork tenderloin w/ mango pepper jelly, along with mashed potatoes and green beans. I couldn't finish a generously delicious sausage and pasta dish (in a bowl) which left no room for dessert and plenty of desire for a good long walk afterwards.

Our timing was also fortuitous, as Café Amelie was participating that night in the "Pause 4 Dinner" fund raiser. 20 percent of their proceeds (and an extra Jackson on our part) were donated to the Louisiana SPCA.

During a return trip to Philadelphia for business, one of my associates suggested this sports bar for an after work watering hole.  This time, instead of having the luxury of staying in Downtown Philadelphia near the Reading Terminal Market, I was "holed up" in a long-term stay hotel up in the Northeast area of Philadelphia and was assigned a vehicle.  I noticed that this sports bar was located relatively close to my hotel so I felt "safe" to drive the short distance at night by myself.

I had never heard of Chickie & Pete's before but my dear Philly work counterpart, Linda, mentioned that C & P is a "Crab House".  Man, that sealed the deal for me!  This location is huge as it has 2 large bar areas, lots of flat screen televisions with different sports playing to accommodate all sports lovers and an exterior covered patio and deck.  When we walked in, this place was rocking with folks cheering a football game.  The place was packed and very energetic.

Our waitress was attentive and amazed me with her ability to balance all the large dishes while weaving her way from kitchen to table.  She gave us a few minutes to peruse the menus while she went to get our "Crabby Mary" cocktails.  Woo!  The seasoning that rimmed the glass was their signature crab seasoning and it sure kicked up this drink and prepared our taste buds for what was to come.

I let Linda do the ordering and the feast began!  

-Mussels in Red Sauce:  That bowl was huge and overflow with perfectly cooked and tender mussels.  The red sauce was thick, garlicky and clung onto the mussels.  There was a generous sprinkle of grated cheese.  It came with fresh bread that we used to sop up the sauce until the bowl was emptied and dry.  I was full but the rest of the order showed up.

-Crab Fries:  crinkle-cut fries seasoned with C&P Signature seasoning.  Very addicting and paired well with a delicious dipping sauce.

-Crab, crab and more crab.... I THINK we had King crab legs, a whole Dungeness and Snow crab legs. Each crab dish came with bread for dipping, er, sopping up the delicious sauce. 

Darn, I was so full I felt like I was seeing crab from behind my eyes.  Plus, talk about getting down and dirty... There is NO WAY to eat shellfish daintily.  Lucky me, I had laundry service included with my hotel stay and made sure that I wore a dark colored outfit just in case of any spills or squirts.  I should have taken a picture of our emptied dishes and the shells as Linda and the server remarked that the shells were stacked so neatly and sucked clean!  

For a local chain restaurant, I was happy with their quality, quantity and flavors.  I don't remember the cost as Linda picked up the tab but she did say that it was a good value.

Being from Hawaii, I had only heard of the Reading Terminal from playing the Parker Brothers game, Monopoly.  Hey, little did I know or realize that these railways (Reading, Pennsylvania, Short Line and B & O (Baltimore & Ohio)) actually existed!  Not only did they exist, the Parker Brothers strategically chose these railroads for their board game because of their routes and destinations.  Well, I've gotten over my ignorance as my business travels have taken me to the great city of Philadelphia many times.

During my first visit, which I think was the most memorable, my taxi driver was kind enough to point out the Reading Terminal Market just as he drove into the porte cochère of the Marriott hotel that I would stay at for a week.  The history and touristy draw of this market didn't dawn on me until I got into my room, began to read about it (and other Philadelphia "hot spots") and found that my room overlooked the market.  I was really excited about going to check it out right away but, having just come off an eleven plus hour flight, I, instead, opted for a short nap.

When I awoke, I quickly jogged my way into the market.  This historic landmark is divided into 3 structures:  1- Reading Terminal Headhouse, 2-Reading Terminal Train shed and 3- Reading Terminal Market.  I found out that the Reading Terminal Market is located BENEATH the Train shed.  The architecture of the terminal is beautiful and was designed in the Italian Renaissance-style.  In parts of the market, you can see the engineering and construction details it took to build these immense structures.  Back in the day, it was an open-air Farmer's market.  This is a huge Farmer's Market that has been in operation since 1892.

It was dazzling to see so many vendors from various ethnicities or cultures ranging from bakeries, flower markets, fresh produce, ice cream and restaurants--All Under ONE Roof!  This market is a melting pot of The aromas, colors and sounds started to drive me wild.  I immediately started eating my way through market starting from the famed Bassett's Ice Cream (America's OLDEST ice cream company) to Termini Bros (Italian bakery - got my FIRST cannoli) and onto DiNic's (for an Italian roast pork, Provolone and broccoli rabe sandwich).   

This was a day of FIRSTS for me... I got to see and experience a bit of Americana, hear the local cultural excitement within this huge market and  smell and taste culturally diverse Pennsylvanian cuisine. Geez, I thought to myself that since I'd be in Philadelphia for a week and hadn't really scheduled any other dining plans, THIS was going to be my life-saver!  I had to try the Pennsylvania Dutch specialty, scrapple.  Ah, if you have to ask what it is, I'm not telling...it was just tasty!  Alas, I ended up dining at other noted Philly restaurants and only got to return to the RTM 3 more times to get myself to more cannoli, amaretti, biscotti, and those Italian roast pork sandwiches.

Granted, the RTM may be more tourist-oriented but it sure was conveniently located to the Pennsylvania Convention Center which is in the Market East section.  I did return to shop and dine here on subsequent trips to Philadelphia.

Oh, just in case you're wondering... The reason why the Parker Brothers chose the Pennsylvania, Reading and Short Line (Shore Fast Line) railroads for the ORIGINAL U.S. Edition of Monopoly board game was because of their routes led directly to Atlantic City.  A side note:  B & O Railroad also operated on the East Coast but did NOT serve Atlantic City.

I'd likely have given the cake 3.5 stars (primarily for presentation, not taste), however, due to the piss poor customer service I was given I honestly wouldn't recommend this place. Bad customer service is bad business, and I don't care what you're selling. 

I called in on Monday informing the person I spoke to I was interested in a cake for a party Saturday evening and was wondering if any full size vanilla cakes would be available. This person told me there's no way for them to know which cakes are being made until 2 nights before so to call in on Wednesday. I asked if I could just place an order for pick up and the person told me they weren't accepting any regular order requests because it was wedding season. So you halt regular customers orders during wedding season? Umm, ok. 

Moving on, I call in on Wednesday and the worker tells me which full size cakes are on the schedule for baking  Friday/ available Saturday - of which is the vanilla I'm looking for. Great, now that you know you're making it, how can I reserve it? You can't (or so I'm told). Ok, well I understand not wanting to hold a cake that can potentially sell so can I purchase the cake over the phone? You can't (or so I'm told). So, miss how does one get a cake here short of stopping in? How will I know the cake is still available and I'm not wasting a whole trip? HOW?!?! I'm informed to in Friday before closing and make sure of stock for Saturday just in case. Umm, ok. 

I call in Friday and speak to yet another customer service (Ill fitting title) agent who informs me oh yeah we have a BUNCH of full size Vanilla cakes. Great! So once again can I reserve/pay? You can't (or so I'm told). Ok, I'll be in first thing in the AM (they open at 7AM). Oh, there's plenty I'm told - don't get up that early there's 4 or 5 vanillas they won't sell by early morning but I would come before noon. Umm, ok. 

So I wake up and head over to the shop. A little later than I expected (damn Uber pool) but I make it to the store around 9:10AM. The agent is helping another customer so I just check out the cakes/treats on display. Hmm, there aren't any full size vanilla cakes on display. In fact, there are only TWO full size cakes left. An earl grey looking cake and a cappuccino one. Well, the display isn't that large perhaps they keep some in the back. After helping the previous customer I'm approached and I tell the young woman that I called in the previous night and regarding a full size vanilla cake. She looks extremely confused and the first thing out of her mouth (no lie) is DID YOU RESERVE OR PAY BY PHONE? I'm asking because I sold all of them this morning. The other vanilla left is the small/mini cake size. I am stunned. So you DO take reservations? YES (or so I'm told). I explain to her my consistent inquiries throughout the week and requests to reserve/pay via phone and I felt bad because she honestly looked confused as to who would be giving me that information.  She was polite, but limited in helpfulness because there were only two cakes left. I'm limited as the party is that night, I assumed I would have a cake so I'm basically assed out. I call a few bakeries who tell me they need 24 hours notice for cake I'm asking for and otherwise subject to what's on hand (which is pretty much what I'm looking at here). I decide to save my many frustrations for a review and deal with deciding which two cakes are lesser evil. Because the flavors are unusual I ask if theres any tasters to which I'm told I'd have to pay for slices of both. Umm, ok. No. So I opt for the cappuccino because I mean, earl grey. Who wants to deal with explaining that choice? The espresso cake was the highest priced I believe around $55 (vs $35 or so for vanilla). The worker took pity on me and gave me discount for around 15% I believe. Probably the only positive thing out of this whole experience. 

All that to say, although the cake was beautiful and seemed to have ingredients that boast of a more gourmet tasting experience it honestly was not that better taste wise than a cake from Giant. The biggest issue was that although I was told the cakes were baked the night before, the cake part was a bit sponge-y and stale tasting. I'd imagine that cake sat for at least two days before being sold to me. I encouraged the guests who didn't like it to leave a bad review out of sheer bitterness of all the effort I had to put into acquiring such an average cake (petty queen? yes!). I'm unsure as to why an issue like this even occurred. I question how you can offer such terrible service to regular patrons in lieu of it being "busy wedding season" but expect the same patrons to frequent your establishment in the off season. Overall, my experience here was enough that I would not return or recommend anyone doing any "on call" cakes unless you prefer to be bullshitted and have your time wasted.

I took my nephew to Studio Movie Grill for his birthday and initially everything ran very smoothly. The ticket process was a self serve kiosk that prints out the tickets on little receipts. I immediately noticed the lounge/bar area is very modern and generally appealing to the eye.

I'm glad something told me to sit closer towards the front because in my opinion the seats toward the back were not as great of a view.

We rang for menus through the service button. The prices are what you'd expect. The problem was the actual service. The waiters were a generally clumsy/dysfunctional unit. Wrong food here, wrong customer there. They very noisily took orders throughout the entire film and did a terrible job of scooting in/out of aisles without disturbing the film or other patrons. The regular fries I ordered with my chicken fingers tasted like they had been in the same pan as the sweet potato fries which made the flavoring very awkward. Sauces that should come with the meal such as barbecue/honey mustard were extra costs and the hot wings I ordered came out completely cold! At this point I was so frustrated I decided just to take them home rather attempt to explain (over the movie nonetheless) and have another order brought out. 

Most of all what I didn't like was receiving the bill to see that a mandatory 17.5% gratuity was added to the bill for in theater dining. I didn't so much mind that there was an added gratuity but rather the fact that it was not mentioned anywhere (could've easily been listed on menu) was extremely off putting to me. They also interrupted the film SEVERAL times by coming around asking for the signed receipt. I don't get it - you already charged my card this can't wait until the lights come on?! To add icing to the cake when I asked for a to go container for my cold wings and leftover food I was ignored. I had to ask 2 more workers before one finally told me they don't actually have containers, bags or anything to transport food. After spending $50+ on food alone I told her she was going to have to find a solution. She ended up bringing my food out in tin pans with plastic wrap. How ghetto. I'm not sure if it's just me but travel containers are just one thing I'd have as a priority in any establishment that serves food - overpriced at that!

The theaters are small and the only positive was that I found the seating to be extremely comfortable. They were plush with lots of leg room. I was not impressed with the crowd - one guy in my row text and played Tetris on his phone the entire time while another girl on the end was balled up in the chair and sleep before the movie even started. Very odd. 

All in all, I do not see how SMG competes with movie theaters that have a restaurant on site or several options in the near vicinity. I would much rather enjoy my film quiet and uninterrupted and dine prior to or after the viewing. In my opinion, SMG  is one of those new age "modern" concepts that fails completely. Do I need constant distractions/interruptions that will disrupt my viewing experience? Do I really want to come here or am I just curious to see how they rehabbed the shabby old theater? Like, why do I have to eat and watch a movie at the same time? Am I hungry enough to eat all my food in one sitting since I can't take it home? If I don't want to eat and watch a movie at the same time what's the point of coming to this theater? These are all questions that have haunted me since coming here. The answers are no, yes, you don't-it's a stupid gimmick, probably not and NONE AT ALL. If you want to duplicate this experience for the better do like the general respectable population has been doing for years and sneak in your quiet/odorless food, snacks, liquor minis or "water bottles" into regular theaters. Yeah, "water".  *WINK WINK* Theater problem solved. 

So umm. Yeah. Thanks but no thanks, SMG.
