Excellent new neighborhood  hangout in the CWE. My drink was beautiful & light. For a main I went with salmon & it was cooked & seasoned perfectly.

Great new addition to the Cortex area - I'll be back & would certainly recommend it!

Fort taco is a new restaurant in the former Rally's location in Brentwood.  I was looking forward to this opening so I was gun ho even though I ventured out on a rainy Sunday afternoon with a completely empty belly and ready to break a tooth off on some good food.

I was caught off guard because the menu consists of only two items: traditional soft shell taco (hamburger) and traditional enchilada (potatoes, cheese, & peas) and combos of the two items. 

Immediately, I am already concerned about the longevity of Fort Taco because they only have two freaking items on their menu.  When you go this simple that means you have to be spot on.  The taco only comes in beef (i.e. no chicken, turkey...) and the enchilada comes in just veggie.  They say their taco is like the burger and the enchilada the fries.   I don't eat beef, so I ordered the two-enchilada combo with a Dr. Pepper  ($7.27) and my Mother had a combo of with one of each of the above noted items ($8.13).  I was taken aback when I saw there was a charge for salsa ($0.40) when that is a normal accompaniment (never paid for napkins or ketchup before but who can really tell what the future holds).

Yet when I pulled up to the window, I meet one of the owners, Tyson, he took the time to explain to me about his grandparent's vision and why they do have a limited menu. Also he said that they are planning on expanding the menu but they really want to focus on first time quality and being the best at the items that they have. This is their test location so if this does well then they will also be expanding two to three more locations in the St. Louis metropolitan area.  From our chat, I felt that they weren't just slanging tacos here; there is a real passion and a love for the family food they serve and that chat took away some of my concern.  Then, I tasted the food ...

All that build up and then the let down.  I haven't been this disappointment since they cancelled House. You could certainly tell everything was fresh to order but there was no flavor.  The mild salsa that I paid for was devoid of any flavor.  Then the food does not come individually wrapped; it comes in an open face box (meaning the box must remain flat/horizontal). The young lady that served me at the window must've forgotten and turn the bag up vertically so my food went Cirque du Soleil in the bag with the sauce smeared not on the food but on the bag.
 

Unless there are drastic changes, I will not be back and though it pains me (I so wanted to love this place) I cannot in good conscience recommend this location at present date. *** Review on food, the ppl were amiable.

This place is a tourist trap that was once a great diner. The food has seriously gone downhill since I last visited about five years ago. Most of the breakfast foods were already prepared in buffet trays behind the counter. We ordered Ferdi special, breakfast special and fries. 

The fries were a bit cold and not crunchy at all. The Ferdi sandwich (roast beef, ham and pot roast topped with cole slaw) was floating in pot roast juice which made the bread super soggy.  You couldn't lift it up to eat it. We rebuilt the sandwich with the tops of the baguette which were still dry. 

The breakfast special was awful. I asked for fried ham and got baked ham instead, which flooded my plate with the water the ham was soaking in. The ham itself was super fatty. The grits were rubbery from sitting out too long and no amount of butter, salt and pepper could save them. The eggs over easy were undercooked with the whites looking like clear snot. The white toast was the highlight of the meal. I also had OJ but it was too pulpy, which I'm not a fan of.

The line that for the bleubird cafe should be your first indication of how amazing this place is. This cafe definitely tries to keep it local and they do a damn good job. The food is the best ive had in boise and appeals to my foodie side. The prices made my wallet sigh with happiness and the wait times were short. We ordered:
Turkey and brie sammy: An amazing blend of brie, apples, turkey, Dijon and fig on a thick cut hard bread. Along side this artfully crafted sandwich was a steamy flavorful tomato soup. I was very impressed with both.
Grilled cheese and simple salad: lets start with the fact that I am a grilled cheese connoisseur. A few different cheeses, fig marmalade and carmelized onions melt together to envelope your senses and hold your taste buds hostage. Crispy on the outside and gooey goodness inside. The simple salad is a light refreshing break in between the bites of this rich grilled cheese. 
Rosemary lemonade: At first sip you expect an overly sweet sugery lemonade.....what you get is a nice balance between bitter, sweet and herby. Perfect pairing for any sandwich.

I don't believe you can go wrong with anything you order here. This is proof that simple and fresh ingredients make the best food. "The proof is in the pudding".......or in this case "the proof is in the lemonade"
5 stars

Atlast!!! I have been looking for a killer Mexican spot since I moved from VA in 2011. None have come close to what I was used too. First of all, the guacamole is super fresh! You can taste every ingredient and it's so creamy! Their salsa is The Holy Grail for me! I am so friggen happy I found this spot! Just waiting to since my teeth into my Carne Asada & Pollo Verde tacos! 

Excuse me whilst I stuff my mouth.......

And I'm a satisfied customer! My carne Asada taco hit the spot perfect for my hangover! Wow, juicy tender meat, the fresh made corn tortilla made me feel like I was a guest in a Mexican home. You can't get a more authentic flavor than here. This is a must get taco! My pollo verde was spot on! Fresh chicken and just well put together! Never a soggy tortilla or even soaked to the point of the taco falling apart! Best Taco Joint!!!

I've worked for small mom and pop local Italian spots in RVA. This establishment reminded me of them. Small, romantic dim lighting, the service and the amazing food made with love.  We've heard other Yelpers rave about Da Sesto and we've lived around the corner for a year and just now getting here! My husband is Italian and I'm Greek so we loved coming here.

We came on a Saturday night and it was a busy late dinner. The chatter of people, a live acoustic guitarist playing and singing and the bustle of servers. The lighting is just perfect, dim and sultry. Our server for the evening was Eric. He greeted us right away and began to tell us the history of the restaurant. Something that is very rare! He was polite and even laid a cloth napkin across our laps. He noticed I had on black and went right away to get a black napkin to lay across my lap. I felt like Belle in Beauty and the Beast, because I've only seen a napkin be laid on a lap that way! 

We weren't rushed to order and e answered all of our questions on the menu. We ordered the create your own Antipasto which is $4.50/per person and we split. We chose salami, prosciutto, fontina, Asiago, eggplant and artichokes. It also came with olives. We ordered a bottle of red and sipped on that while enjoying the antipasto. 

I ordered the Penne a la Sesto with Chicken. My mouth was in heaven! The menu has endless options of amazing Italian cuisine. I saw someone on Yelp had ordered this dish and when I read the description on the menu I knew it was what my tastebuds were craving.  You have to add chicken to this if you want and of course their is a small up charge. Totally worth it! A creamy sauce, mushrooms, I think it had roasted red peppers too. This is my new fav meal! Who doesn't love a creamy sauce!? It's just a comfort food for me! I can't believe we haven't been here sooner! I'm looking forward to coming back again!

I've read a lot about PYT, and it's been all over the place. A few things keep coming up: the location brings out the bros, and the onion rings are fantastic. I went with my friend Quinn and we worked through the full treatment of the menu: burger, rings and shakes.

The alcoholic shakes are a gimmick. That being said, I'm sure a lot of people love these. These shakes are $10 a pop and come mixed with different ice creams and liquors; there are quite a few different ones for different tastes. Mine was a simple mix of vanilla and Maker's Mark, while Quinn ordered one with vodka and kalua. She seemed to like her's more than I enjoyed mine. We both came to the same conclusion: these are made with a heavy hand and aren't really akin milkshakes at all. They're more like mixed drinks that happen to use ice cream as an ingredient. I'm sure that was the goal for PYT, but next time, I'll just go with the regular shake.

The onion rings are different than any you've ever had. The breading is lighter and sweeter than anything else I've ever had. It evokes memories of funnel cake batter. These were good, but I am in the same boat as the shake; I'd rather have a good version of what I'm expecting.

Finally, the burger. It was cooked to order and overall, well made. It wasn't the "fist of meat" that far too many pubs serve up. Still, Sketch burger has become the gold standard to which I compare all other burgers. PYT just doesn't hold up. I ate my burger quickly, and enjoyed it, but there wasn't anything memorable about it. There were a few vegetarian options that looked appetizing; I'd go for one of these if I found myself here again.

Bottom Line: PYT will thrive on location alone. It has a few cool tricks up its sleeve, but in the end, none of them "wow" me. There are people who will hate this place, other who will rave over it. I fall squarely in the middle. It's definitely worth checking out to find out which person you are. Of if you absolutely need a good burger, head a few blocks over to Sketch. PYT also has a full bar if you're trying to avoid Swift Half.

Victoria's Kitchen is a fairly new take out restaurant on West Oak Lane's ever growing Ogontz Ave. I'd been wanting to try this place out since it opened and when opportunity presented itself to do so today, gave it a try. I ordered the Fried Fish Platter which came with 2 sides, I went with the Smashed Potato Salad and Collard Greens.  Also picked up a second platter for someone else and they had the Fried Chicken with Mac & Cheese and Collards. 

Everything in my platter was very good, the fish was seasoned nicely, not too much not too little. Potato salad and Collards are both something I've only come to like in adulthood go figure so needless to say for me to like either, it has to be done a certain way and Victoria did them both well. 

I tasted a little of the Mac and Cheese and it was pretty good, not the best I'd ever had but I'd order it for myself. 

Finished my platter up with a slice of 7-up cake. MMMMM so moist and all around good. I remember my mom use to make this cake so that brought back memories.

I want to try a few other things before going for a full 5:) Other things offered are Crab Cakes, Fish or Chicken Fried Rice, Turkey Burgers among other things. 

They also deliver which I'm not so sure I needed to know, having soul food I like at my fingertips! Nevertheless rather I walk in or have it delivered I'll go again. 

Oh and customer service was very good, both the young lady who took my order and Victoria the chef, very personable.

Oh boy what a complete mess this place is. Starts off bad by walking in and being ignored! Ten minutes later hi what can I get you well I'll take a bud light sorry we're out. Okay how about just a regular Budweiser? Sorry we're out umm.. Okay how about a corona? Sorry yet again were out.. Okay how's this what do you have?? How about a pabst blue ribbon? Okay gross but sure why not. Hands me a already gross beer in a can classy. I ordered their wings witch were just okay and hope your ready for blue cheese cause that's all they have. 

As I sit there wondering how the doors stay open on this place things get worse. The bartender starts to make a martini she reaches for the olives and wait for it sticks her bare hand that she just touched money with in the olives and drops it in the mans drink GROSS! After that decides to stick her hand back in the olives and eats one!! it's almost mind blowing like am I really watching this? 

It may just be the time of day I went not sure but still not like that matters. The inside of the place is really nice I give them that but I'm sorry the management needs to seriously sit down and just watch how the staff work. To me it's just a big free for all and no one cares. Oh and FYI brass tap management if your out of three very important beers there's a publix in your plaza how about you go buy some since you can't seem to place your order correctly. 

I live less then a half mile from this place and will never return. There was one employee at the time of my visit who seemed to have his stuff together so for him I apologize for such a bad review. It only takes one person to ruin a place.

I sincerely wish that I could give this cafe the 5 stars it deserves but this review is strictly for the service that we had. A little back story, my friends and I are New Yorkers so we're definitely no strangers to snootiness and people that are rude. I would never expect that sort of thing from a place as friendly as New Orleans, which is why I was so taken aback at just how snippy our waitress was (an older Caucasian woman) 

A few examples:

1. One of our friends didn't have cash on her and wanted to pay with a card, so we asked if it was at all possible to have two separate checks and were met with a "Really?" and an annoyed expression. 

2. She gave us the check while we were halfway through the meal and was basically hovering over us the whole time while we figured out the bill as if we were some juvenile delinquents about to dine and dash. 

But perhaps the worst part was the fact that she'd chased after us even after we were already down the block to let us know that we didn't tip enough (which, spoiler, usually is the case when the only impression you have of the place you just ate at is the awful service instead of the wonderful food.) She even threatened to call the police on us for not tipping her the additional $5 on top of the 15% that she didn't deserve and when we advised that she could at least be a bit nicer of a waitress. She didn't even respond and stormed away with a huff. 

Again, I wish I could give this place all the stars it deserves because the food and the other staff was extremely pleasant and friendly. But this cannot go unaddressed. 

Love you, L'il Dizzy's - but as the locals say: Be Nice Or Leave!

The cutest coffee shop around. It's small but cozy. You're greeted by a sweet gentleman behind the counter. I explained it was my first time in and I was meeting my bfs mom and her friend. He was delighted to walk me through the menu of coffee, tea and Turkish delights. 
Each drink order is paired with a complimentary savory gel cube called Turkish delight. I learned that Traditional Turkish delight flavors are pistachio, rose water and lemon but pangolin likes to develop unique flavors like pomegranate, tart raspberry and Hawaiian. I ordered a vanilla latte with a vanilla rose delight. Side Note(Turkish delights are available for purchase on its own!) 

I placed my belongings down at the center table and wandered the coffee shop. I found some coloring pages and color pencils on the left hand side table. The coloring pages were adorable as they had the anteater(pangolin) on it. I began to color as I waited for coffee and company. 

Coffee arrived first, company arrived shortly after. I have to say the presentation of the vanilla latte was exquisite and the Turkish delight gave it a very European touch! We enjoyed our drinks and spending time with one another. 

I look forward to making more memories here with family and friends :)

Nick introduced me to Michael's Deli. 
I was blown away by the amazing service. Parking is a little bit difficult however they have a parking lot around back. Lunch time is pretty busy, so plan accordingly. My favorite sandwich to order here is the Spicy Chicken Club ! Spicy Chicken club comes with Roasted Chicken Breast, Pepper Jack Cheese, Applewood Bacon, Avocado, Chipotle Aioli, Lettuce, Tomato,
& Onions, on a Sourdough Roll.  Food is always fresh and delicious.  Highly recommend !

First found out about El Original Tacos Tijuana through a coworker. It became one of my favorite places to eat during pregnancy. My go to tacos were al pastor and chicken. The tacos are a bit pricey however they give you a huge amount of meat on each taco. The al pastor tacos have chunks of pineapple in them. The chicken tacos are seasoned to perfection. Each kind of taco is paired with a different salsa. The best part of these tacos are the hand made tortillas. I really appreciated hand made tortillas because to me it is a dying art. My mother and grandmother made handmade tortillas. Handmade tortillas taste very different than store bought tortillas. I definitely recommend supporting this taco shop, do not forget it is Hispanic heritage month!

Bj's was ordered for employee appreciation day. For high volume of food you will be directed to catering versus take out. Their customer service was very good. The food overall was average. We ordered mac and cheese, beans, brisket, ribs and corn bread. The ribs were a bit  overcooked and dry. The brisket was really good. They provide sufficient mild BBQ sauce to smother on.The corn bread and baked beans were really good as well !! Unfortunately the mac and cheese fell short. I am not sure but it seemed like the mac and cheese looked yellow because it had mustard in it rather than actual cheese. It tasted bland to me. Portion sizes were big enough for all staff. Overall would return but would order different things on the menu.

If I owned one bar in Reno, Emerson would be it ! The aesthetics at this bar are jaw dropping ! of this place. I originally heard about Emerson through Michael I who was attending the grand opening. I was not able to attend however I scheduled a time and date to go with Nick to check it out ! We stopped by on a rainy day. There was very little parking due to construction however that did not deter us. We were determined to drop in. 

We were greeted upon arrival. Inside was warm and cozy. Lots of gold accents, greenery and a projector playing black and white filmed movies ! Our server who was dressed up in a pin up outfit was very polite and gave us food menus and drink menus. We ordered a margarita, the rub a dub dub and tacos!

The drinks were strong ! The tacos were delicious very filling. All for a great price. This is my newest favorite bar it has everything you can ask for. It is beautiful and cozy, staff is polite and the drinks and food are delicious!

Taco shop is in alley! But before you dismiss it let me tell you these are the best tacos I have had. You can't miss taco shop the exterior is bright with bubble gum pink paint. The taco shop is family owned and operated. 
We ordered pastor, chicken and asada. The only catch is you can't mix and match. You get 2 of a kind for $6 or 3 of the same kind for $8. My husband and I have a rather big appetite so we end up sharing our tacos and mixing them after our food has been served. Be aware Taco shop has limited seating area and it maybe best to take tacos to go. My favorite tacos are al pastor with some salsa and a nice tamarind jarritos drink! If tacos are right up your alley then check out taco shop !

I've travelled to the city of Reno quite frequently. But I didn't know there was a taqueria located across the street (on Virginia St. Side) from the Circus Circus Hotel and Casino. I wish I would've known prior.

Whenever I stay at the Silver Legacy and if I'm lazy and/or hungry, at least I don't have to travel far to get my "silver-bullet" craving. This taqueria has a spacious dining area with locals and tourists enjoying the "South of the Border" treat in Reno.

From the menu posted on the wall, there are ten different kind of meats for your burrito or any meal. I've chose the Al Pastor for my super burrito. Not a bad price for $5.75 and that burrito had the usual condiments with fresh cheese and marinated pork. My burrito had plenty of marinated lean meat and fresh rice. I also got a $1.50 bottle of Fruit-punch Jarrito and a complimentary bag of Tortilla chips. 

And with my hotel room located across the street, you bet I took my burrito to go and enjoy my burrito in the privacy of my hotel room.

I paid my meal in cash and credit cards are also accepted. 
http://static.px.yelp.com/photo/MJfA0b1PsghBjPbVIdJFXA/l

You get the taste of Portland, Oregon in the city of Reno. The "Biggest Little City in the World"  can use anything in Reno. Show some love to both cities.

The restaurant in Portland is also one of my favorites. The "Reggie Deluxe" is the top seller and one of my favorites. The mid priced dish has fried chicken, thick bacon, melted cheddar sandwiched in a huge homemade biscuit and gravy. This dish may not win a beauty pageant. But you will eat like a BOSS. Your mouth is salivating, right?

Also had a glass of Arnold Palmer with free refills. This Reno location also brew Stumptown coffee. Keep those in mind.

To make your visit and meal enjoyable, dining-in is temporarily back (hopefully for good). Cashless pay first. And just minutes away from downtown. 

I will make another trip to Reno trip to try other dishes and maybe have a local brew. Check the medias for updated specials.

I arrived into Reno late Wednesday night. Mel's, which is located inside the Sand's Hotel & Casino, is one of the few restaurants that was still open until midnight. 24-hour dining in Reno won't happen anytime soon. I know, the pandemic ruined it for everyone.

Just like the other Mel's locations, you get the ambience of how drive-in diner was. If you like the musical movie, "American Graffiti", Mel's is the diner that makes you feel from that era.

Late-night eating is one thing I don't do often. But I was hungry. As I was looking at the menu, I saw the San Francisco Mel Burger has branded my name on it. For $12.00, the burger is really a patty melt, with thick strips of bacon, melted cheddar cheese on a toasted Texas toast. The burger also comes with thick cut fries. I also had a bottle of Budweiser with my meal. But the workers did not charge me for the brew, which was a nice gesture from them.

The jukebox was cranking with oldies. But I was cranking Pooh Shiesty on my phone.

Mel's treated Joe Cool very well. Free beer with my burger; I won't complain.

The Row has just opened, and I was really glad to be one of the first of my friends to visit.  This place is very Nashville - maybe even a little too Nashville.

First, let's talk decor.  We sat in the bar area (opened for the first time just hours before our visit) and it was very open and nicely laid out.  There was a full bar that's not totally functional at the moment, and a patio that will be amazing when they get it finished.  The only complaint I had was the cackling women sitting next to us - they had to be the most annoying group in the history of groups. 

The inside, however, seemed very Country-esqe.  They pipe in twangy music, and have pictures of old timey Country musicians on the walls.  It's almost as if the place belongs over on Brodway or by Opryland Hotel, and not in Midtown.

You'd expect a kitschy place like this to just have overrated bar food and lousy service, but food and service at The Row are fantastic.  I had the fried catfish for $14 and it was simply amazing, albeit a little pricey.  The bourbon smashed sweet potatoes are simply delicious.  

All in all, I was pleasantly surprised with The Row, and I wil definitely be returning soon.  I seriously hate the crummy bars in Midtown, and this place might change my mind about that.

I can't believe what transpired at Morton's Steakhouse tonight.  I just came there from a company Christmas party, and I've never been treated so poorly.

One person in our party is a cancer patient - and he needs to wear a wool cap in order to keep warm. His recent treatment makes him feel cold, and his measly wool cap helps him regain some warmth in these cold winter days.  
 
Our party of 16 went  to Morton's and had dinner.  Near the end of the evening, the person dons his wool cap, and was immediately told by the assistant manager, Catrina, that hats are not allowed inside the restaurant.  After being told that the person was going through cancer treatment, the assistant manger told him THAT HE NEEDED A DOCTOR'S NOTE.   You read that right - he was supposed to have a doctor's permission to wear a wool cap in Morton's.  He and his family soon got up and left.

After the rest of us complained - get this - MORTON'S CALLED THE POLICE ON US.  We were not unruly, and quite civil given the absolute rudeness of the management.  I was told by a manager that the police officer was just casually patrolling the area and came in, but I was told later that was a total lie.

It would be one thing if we were just a couple of guys, splitting an appetizer and causing a commotion.  However, we were a table of 16 with a $2,000+ tab and being treated like criminals.

I will never step foot in this establishment again, and I will tell everyone that listens to take their business elsewhere.  I will also make sure their corporate management hears about how awfully we were treated.

I wonder if this place will last after the novelty wears off. We got there fairly early on a Saturday night before it was too crowded, and I was able to play a few games. First, to play any of the video games or pinball, you need tokens, not quarters. These can be purchased at a machine in the corner with a credit card or cash (no coins). $5.00 gets you twenty tokens, and most games require one token, some two. I had no intention of playing that much before we left, so I just borrowed a few tokens from a friend (and our original plan was to stay till 10:00).

For alcohol, I prefer craft beer, and I prefer it on tap. There were three handles with the rest of the beer being cans with a heavy emphasis on citrusy beers. A pint-sized can of 4 Hands City Wide cost me $7.00, and the draft Urban Chestnut cost the same. The 12-inch meat pizza, a pizza topped with pepperoni and honey, cost $10 and tasted all right with the honey being an interesting twist.

Oddly, there seemed to be "VIP" couches. Since all the standing tables were taken, a few of us took our food and drinks over to a couch in the corner with a Nintendo 64 only to be shooed off by a waitress who first asked us for drinks and then informed us there was a $50 minimum to sit there, so we plopped our pizzas on an empty corner of the bar and hung out there for a few minutes. There were three more for-pay tables upstairs.

For the games themselves, there were about six pinball machines, which I didn't care about, and various video game cabinets for things like Centipede/Millipede, Ms. Pac-Man, Galaga, Crusin' World, Gauntlet, etc. Most of the cabinets did not have a flat surface parallel to the ground, so having a place to set drinks near the games would be a nice touch. There was skeeball, too.

Overall, I'd say the place tries hard to be trendy, and is really only halfway a bar experience and halfway an arcade experience. My friends and I all agreed, if we wanted to sit around a couch and play Mario Kart and drink beer, we'd rather do it at someone's house.

My 100th review...

I never thought I would see the day. I spent days wondering if I would ever make it to ROTD rather than even think I would make it to #100. 100 reviews!!!...whew... I finally made it. Seems like such a long time ago that I was nervously writing my first review...now I feel even more nervous...okay hold on to your hats, here it is.

I thought that for my 100th time that it should be extra special, you know maybe review one of the best steakhouses in and across the country.  I wanted to make it the best it could be by spotlighting a place that claims to be the best of the best... 

Well you won't be hearing about the best of the best in my review of Morton's. I visited Morton's about 10 years in the city on a client visit.  Since I wasn't technically paying for my dinner (thank you corporate card), it was a pretty spectacular experience at the time.  Now that I was going to visit this place again and going to be paying my way with my own hard earned money, I was not in a position to compromise any of the important factors in a restaurant: décor, food, price and most importantly, service.

I was invited to Morton's in K of P last Thursday with my friend and her husband to celebrate their wedding anniversary. Yeah I know what you are all thinking - I have no life.  But it was Morton's and I thought my last experience was pretty good, so why not?  So being the good little third wheel that I was, I made my way to the restaurant to partake in the anniversary celebration.  The first thought I had as I pulled into the crowded K-of P parking lot around 5pm was "Why would you put a Morton's Steakhouse right smack in the middle of an enormous mall; especially next to a discount shoe store?"  I continued, "You are Morton's you should be standing alone --separated from the rest...!!!!" The location seemed quite odd to me. Don't you all think so? 

Once inside, the restaurant seemed quiet and unassuming.  We walked into a dark narrow corridor and entered into the main dining room which was barely lit.  The décor seemed stale and not very welcoming or warm at all. As I nestled between the 2 lovebirds in a corner booth, I perused the menu that had been eloquently engraved with a "Happy Anniversary".  Awww.  I felt out of place.  I needed a drink.  Where's the waiter?

After about 10 minutes, the waiter appeared and right off the bat, I thought he was trying way too hard to earn extra moolah on his tip. Too happy and too pushy- a deadly combination for anyone in the food service business. I ordered a Thyme Lemon Drop Martini but failed to realize that it actually had pieces of really thyme sprinkled on the top of the drink as a garnish.  What??!!! Who in their right mind thought to mix thyme with lemons in a martini?  yukkk, bleck, ewwwww!!! 

I asked the waiter what was in the drink.  He said it was a "Thyme" Lemon Drop Martini.  Okay, thanks Einstein.  I get it.  I thought he could tell by my tone and the look of terror on my face that I did not like it.  Did he offer to take it back?  No. Did he offer to get me something different?  No.  Did he offer to have the bartender make me another one without Beelzebub's spice in it?  No... My night was immediately ruined (sigh).

The entrees were okay; the meat cooked the way that everyone had ordered; I proactively ordered a raspberry martini to try to wash away the taste of thyme from my mouth about halfway through my meal. 

So let's summarize, shall we? 

Décor - 1 star
Food - 3 stars
Price - 1 star
Service - 1 star

What started as a pretty crappy experience for a hoity toity restaurant, ended up slightly over mediocre in the end.  That is after the wait staff and fellow patrons sung happy anniversary to all three of us as we ogled the candle in the middle of the crème brulee and I made it smack dab in between the happy couple in the souvenir anniversary photo... courtesy of Morton's....

Ah memories.

I wish I could give "0" stars. I have been meeting a group of friends for dinner once a month for thirty years, that is 360 dinners.  We have tried many, many resturants and never have we left an establishment without eating UNTIL TONIGHT.  
We had hear that Teca had open under new (old) management and decided to give it a try. 
We had a reservation and was promptly seated. The Resturant was about one quarter fill. So not very busy. We received water in out glasses and menus. And that is where the service stopped. 
The wine list is extensive but not a lot of medium priced bottles. If one wanted to spend several hundred dollars for a bottle of wine, I doubt one would be in this establishment. 
It didn't matter, because no one came to ask us what we wanted. After 30 minutes, We stopped a well dressed gentleman passing by and asked if we might place an order for wine. He looked down his nose at us and his response was,"what color would you like?"  
We placed orders for four glasses of wine and 16 minutes later, we just gave up and left. 
Our evening was ruined. My only consolation  is the knowledge that this place will not be in business for another 6-9 months. With the reviews I've read, and the distinction of being the worst dining experience I've had in 30 years, they can not last long. 
Pity. The ambience is beautiful. But a Resturant has to actually serve people to make it in the business.

Just ordered from IV deli mart for the first time and it does not make me want to do it again.
A friend and I were hungry around 10 PM so we decided to order something small and have it delivered. It got here relatively quickly, but everything else went wrong.

They mixed up our receipt with someone else so we ended up with the wrong order. Finally, the other customer came back to swap orders. I'm not sure how they got mixed up considering our order was considerably smaller than theirs. 

After that, we realized there was no receipt in the bag. Since we were paying with cash, we needed the receipt to check the price. The delivery guy had to call the restaurant to check how much our order was. At this point, our order really should have been comped. It was freezing outside and our food was already cold. 

To top things off, we finally sit down to eat and notice that one of our chicken tenders had a bite taken out of it. Nice...
Needless to say, service is awful here. They really need to step it up.

Nothing is good about this casino. Slots are tighter then a than spandex on a 350-pound person. You cannot get a drink to save your life. You can order your drink on your slot machine and you will not see anyone come around for over 30 minutes. They want you to send your money, or should I say take your money since their slots sure don't payback anything, and lose everything before even getting a drink. You would think playing their Higher Limits area, we could get a drink and see someone hit something. We did not see one payout on a Saturday night, which really make you think about playing there. 

Playing tables is pretty much the same, you will wait and wait to get a drink. The tables are hard to get a seat at to play, while their are other tables that are not used and could be open. They don't rate you well at the tables. At least slots you get rated, tables are as good as lighting a match to your money. Little to no comps being based on your play.

Being a Diamond TR member, this is the worse Caesars property out of the 14 that I played at. Their diamond lounge is the worse one out of all of the other Caesars locations I have played at. Plus you need to pay for your drinks there, unlike any other Diamond Lounge. 

I am really surprised the Caesars Entertainment don't look into how bad this location makes them look. This casino is a total write off. Seriously, either go to AC or drive a few miles down the road to Delaware Park, instead on going to this casino. Don't waste your time and hard earned money here.

This past weekend I had dinner at Varga Bar with my husband. Shortly after I finished the watermelon arugula salad I started to feel ill. Flash forward to 5 days later of severe food poisoning, numerous doctors visits and tests concluding that I ingested bacteria found on types of lettuce. 

You can imagine my surprise as to when I informed the management of the situation and he laughed at me saying he sells out of "those salads". You would think that a patron who dined there and got so sick would get some apology or the fact I'm pregnant would raise some type of concern but no. Nothing. With a complete disregard to the fact my baby could have been seriously hurt. 


I don't know of any other establishment that would act this way when something on their end caused harm to one of their customers. Living around the corner I walk by this place daily. The kitchen is vile, unsanitary, and smells as it opens to the street and I can look in. Shame on me for even thinking about eating here, it certainly was my last as I have learned my lesson. Consider yourself warned.

This is my favorite sushi go-to place. I have been a customer for years for both dine in and carry out. I really like that everyone gets a miso soup or ginger salad to begin with while the rolls are being prepared. The rolls are always very fresh and delicious. I do like to come here also due to the location since it's across the street from Flatwoods bike trail. So, I can bike for 20 miles and come here afterwards-- it's my super healthy treat.
Best Devil crabs in Ybor City. I arrived early and had a cafe con leche instead of a mojito. Great casual fine dinning.

I visited Nashville for the day with family and we chose to try The Stillery. Our visit was a weekend earlier this month when businesses and people were ready and excited to bust out of the COVID way of living. Streets and businesses were extremely busy with people smiling and laughing - it was so exciting and refreshing to see life happening again. Unfortunately, my experience at The Stillery was disappointing which I was surprised given the great number of positive reviews. I ordered the Hot Chicken Salad. It took over 30 minutes for us to get our food, but that was understandable given how packed the restaurant was. The drinks were pretty watered down - tasteless - so I didn't ordered a second one. The salad was very dry from the chicken being dry and without flavor or heat. The salad also had hardly any salad dressing - it looked bare. The salad simply lacked taste. Although the chicken wasn't really hot, as in being spicy, I concentrated on eating it and then pushed away what was left behind. I'd be willing to give The Stillery another try if I'm ever back in the area, but I definitely won't order this salad again.

Much better than MTO, which is when you have an orgasm, but it leaves you feeling lonely and empty.

I prefer H20, but watermi talking about anyway.

My notes said - very fresh but can't believe how tiny, 1/10th. lovely service. most expensive i ever had

Compared to the large salads at the Salata near my house in Houston and the massive ones at Pie O Mine in Buffalo and Cleveland, honestly these are pitiful. Fresh, but tiny, and wayyyy expensive. They're more like New York salads, but shockingly even smaller.

This is probably the most expensive salad I've ever had, considering the size, and while service from the girl was really nice, in the two minutes that I was in here I managed to get a parking ticket outside. The situation is a nightmare for the PKNG.

So altogether it was one of the most disappointing salads at one of the most disappointing prices with definitely the most disappointingly small portion that I probably had anywhere. Philadelphia has issues. Tastes good, is fresh, is tiny, is super expensive.

Which area do you go if you want the best Salvadoran food? To the Pupus Area! Obviously.

This is a really friendly place with good pupusas and good tamales. Excellent Central American food from El Salvador and Honduras and Nicaragua. Definitely delicious and well worth a stop if you love this kind of food as I do and extremely cheap as well.

It's a lovely little central american place representing all the countries but especially El Salvador, in fact it's decorated like the Salvadoran flag and stuff. Very friendly, very cute, decor is second to none, and the wet chicken tamale is much better than Mexican equivalents. Try it and see.

When I want to feel like a fattie
I don't eat fried chicken or a patty
I come straight down to Nashville
Card won't work, but my cashwill
And I get the best sandwich from Hattie!

If Starlight comes here, it's Catty B's. If the sandwiches suck, it's Crappy B's. If they have parent issues, maybe it's Daddy B's. And of course, after too many trips here, I become Fattie B's.

I'll be the first one to hold up my hands and say that I'm wrong when I'm wrong. So the reason I waited this long to try Hattie B is partly because the lines were way too long at their original Midtown location when I tried to go before on several occasions - but partly because I thought it was hipster crap and that it would suck. The fact that they only sold fried chicken tenders and wings just kind of affirmed for me that it was some kind of gentrified crappy version of the legend that is Nashville Hot Chicken which I have had excellent versions of from other more low-key places.

But guess what? I was wrong. I was f***ing wrong. I was the most wrong I've been, or thereabouts.

I stayed here so long that my hair got all Nappy B's.

I don't know how the franchise locations taste and are doing in places like Atlanta and over in Memphis, but this is one of the several new locations around Nashville and I can't imagine that the original location could possibly be any better.

I came wearing my army uniform - Khaki B's.

I got the chicken sandwich and I have to honestly say it was the best chicken sandwich I've ever had in my life. I got a medium instead of hot and I'd like to try it hot next time but oh my god.

This thing was soaked in grease and so juicy and it was some kind of lightly spiced buffalo wing grease. One of the best things I've ever tasted. I've been trying to give up meat and this is the kind of thing that makes me want to eat chicken sandwiches everyday.

The chicken is crazy good. Should call it Wacky B's.

Chicken is kind of my thing I've had a lot of chicken from a lot of places so for me to say this is one of the five best chicken sandwiches I've ever had in my life and quite possibly the number one is one of the most grand statements I'll make. For me to say that about a chain which is already insanely popular with everybody else actually makes me kind of sad. Sad that I didn't trust everybody in this case because they let me down on other occasions. Sad that I didn't try it sooner. And sad that I love a place so much that is already very successful, that already everybody knows about, that is a corporate chain, because me telling you how great it is is not really going to make much of a difference to anything or anyone, and because they don't need my money or recs - or yours.

But for what it's worth, I have to be honest and I have to throw my hands up in the air and say I was so wrong. It's so good.

If it were in College Station TX it'd definitely be Aggie B's.

Another surprising thing about this place is how incredibly friendly everybody is. Nashville is not the friendliest city and I've had a lot of iffy experiences in Nashville with different types of attitude problems. It's a little bit like Los Angeles in that regard. But I'll tell you what. They pick some really great workers here. Everybody was ridiculously nice and so helpful and the girl who is serving me who is also flirting with me was a total angel. And she took my pictures and I'm a big fan of her and an even bigger fan of the chicken sandwich was she insisted that I get.

If you don't brush your teeth after, you'll end up with Plaquey B's.

The only thing that I have to say I didn't like was the mac and cheese. It was so bland and homogenized and anglicized. The Deep South is full of amazing soul food and that kind of mac and cheese and blows me away and I'm not even really into it. This is definitely the kind that tastes like it's straight out of a can and basically like plastic. I'm surprised it's such a popular side dish but then again I'm not. I'll definitely be trying one of the other sides next time I get a sandwich here and trust me there is going to be a next time because it is a sandwich that I will eat every single time I ever set foot in a city that has one, except for Atlanta where they don't do phone orders and are insanely rude and convoluted.

And if you get drunk in Japan after eating this, it's probably on Saki B's. And this f***ing internet is slow (Laggy B's). Looks like my review is too long again (Chatty B's).

It's just so good. $10 is a f***ing bargain, and the amount of meat that you get on here is massive as well.

By far the best thing I've ever eaten in Tennessee and by far the best version of hot chicken I've ever had. One of the best chicken sandwiches imaginable.

You'll need to do Jumping Jack's after eating at Jack's, but despite being on the most touristy strip for hundreds of miles in any direction, this place has excellent BBQ.

I'm not sure that it's the best in town (cough Peg Leg cough) but it's right up there. It will make you "Nash" your teeth with appreciation. I've only ever had the BBQ sandwiches, which are decently priced considering the location. I've always been satisfied.

Plus this place has nice memories for me. I first came here when I was super young. And, well, I'm still super young so I'm not sure what I'm talking about. But back then they had great sandwiches. And they still do. So I have no qualms about giving it 5 stars.

Besides, it's owned by Jack Nicholson, Jack Black and Jack The Ripper. Oh wait that's not necessarily a good thing.

I know a few Dan's, but none of them are fat. So that's a definitive case of false advertising. 

I hate to give this place a 5 star rating because of the attitude and the silly price, but hey, it's in a bar, so I suppose bar stuff is often marked up. I remember the days when bar stuff was marked down to get people to come in and drink but whatever. 

Still, the dog was delicious so I'll reluctantly give it a 5. They know how to make Chicago dogs in Indy. Well made and on a proper poppy seed bun. The girl couldn't have liked me any less, probably because since I was getting a dog to go, that meant no tip for her. But hey, when the dog tastes this good, I don't care.

Someone asked me where a dealer can be found. I pretended not to understand. They repeated: Dealer - where? I ran away. Next thing you know I'm writing a Yelp review of a welcome center.

Not a fan of highway rest stops. This is why. Gas is more expensive than most places in Delaware. Service here is appalling, some of the servers (cough cough Starbucks) are very rude indeed. Not that I even like Starbucks. Choices are awful (Burger King - yay... not), and the prices of all the places in here are higher than they should be. For example you can pay more for a Starbucks here than at a regular non-highway Starbucks.

Lots of bus traffic comes through here, much like your momma's bedroom.

Wifi didn't work properly, my lemonade tasted watered down, and the only reason it doesn't get one star is that it's safe to sleep in the parking lot (I would know), and it's kept very clean (like her motor).

Owned by Marlon Bando, and the food here is the reason he was a little rotund in his later career.

Bando, next time I come in and order $20 of food, please bring me more than 1 napkin pls and tysm. It's really a somewhat bizarre little hipsteresque ice cream shop with very high prices. I appreciate that they let you try lots of flavours, and some of them are really good. They are fairly expensive and very posh though. It's located in a nice historical area and I'd come back again to try more flavours.

So when Topanga dumped Cori (it was only partly my fault... if it wasn't me, it would have been a different guy believe me, and anyway could you blame me. You've seen her right? And he was a Savage. But in reality, I was the savage and that's really why she wandered, isn't it), I always wondered what happened to the poor guy.

Well, I found him. He opened an amazing hot dog shop in Nashville with one of the most extensive hot dog menus I've ever seen. And there are much worse things you can do when Topanga cheats on you with a hairy annoying English bloke who writes/talks too much just to hear himself write/talk, who thinks he is hot sh**, keeps making jokes that are so bad they can't even be described as humour, still insists on using an "ou" in words like "humour" even though he hasn't lived in the UK in decades, and to make things worse, has started wearing sleeveless shirts, flexing in gym mirrors, taking pictures of said debacle, and occasionally posting them on tired social media platforms designed for food reviews.

But I digress.

What to get: Chicago dog
What else: Explore the amazing menu

Ohhhhhh.

I tried 3 Chicago dogs when I was in Nashville this most recent time. Hot Diggity, and the one by McDougal's Chicken Fingers next to Vanderbilt Campus, whose name I forgot. Starlight, Mochi and Son shared all 3 hot dogs with me. They're all pretty good, but of the three, this place has by far the coolest and most extensive menu, and is the most spacious and comfortable to sit in. The other two are tiny little stuffy shacks, which is better in terms of cool points. But at Cori's, the cool points are out the window and I'm all twisted up in the bun.

So about that bun.

I was considering giving it less than a 5 because the bun isn't authentic poppy seed, but it was actually really tasty and well put together with lovely service. And the cats loved it. And their menu is so impressive and imaginative that I find it hard not to give them a 5. But most importantly, the Chicago Dog is a 5 star dog despite not having the right kind of bun.

That menu though... I posted a picture so you can see for yourself. They've assigned a hot dog to almost every city in the US! For most of them, I think they've taken some liberties (read: made it up), but it's very imaginative and innovative, and as someone who is obsessed with Geography and Traveling, and who has actually been to every... city... on that very long list... I very much appreciated it.

And now that Cori Haim, Cori Feldman, Cori Ander (the herb) and Cori Nation Street (another Brit, apparently big on TV back home) are all part ownes, I think these hot dogs will make you pretty satisfied. Just like my hot dog infamously made Topanga pretty satisfied.

If lambs could drive, I think some of them would be truckers. I'd love to meet one of these Truc Lams. Wouldn't you?

This place is old and sweet and part of the furniture in S STL. It has extremely cheap Banh Mi, and mine took about 10 mins. It was pretty good, although didn't love it, mainly because the meat was a bit old and stale, but considering it is so cheap and with great service, it scores 4.

I always get sad when I have to give a comparatively low rating to a place with a really lovely and cool and progressive employees. This is one of those cases. The servers and service would score 5 Stars every time. The prices aren't even bad. But the products just don't do anything for me at all. Not even close.

Probably because I get my Chicago Dogs in Chicago and my Bagels in NYC, and it's hard to compare to those two places. But I have found really good ones elsewhere, so it's not like I'm just being snooty about it. But I'm not saying I'm not snooty. But anyway.

Really funny and cool hipster employees, but the prices are high, the bagels aren't too fresh or even really particularly good (and brought in from a chain I think, the cream cheese is boring, they're shocked at the concept of untoasted (and I can see why, because toasting bagels masks the bland taste - you don't toast bagels in NYC), and their Chicago dog is really not very well made, the least enjoyable one I had in town. When I saw Elise, I was like "do me Elise!" And this is how I ended up being Elise's baby Daddy. This is off the record right.

Of course we wanted to love this place and I was ready to love this place and excited to love this place, but then they decided to randomly close 5 hours early on the day that we drove all the way across New Orleans to get here.

I'm a massive fan of Gelato, but nothing (OK, almost nothing) compares to the stuff I've had in Italy... and, er, Belgium. Yes, I'm serious.

There are a select few Gelato shops in the US that I would say are on the same level as the real thing in Italy. In fact I can only think of one: Morano Gelato in Boston & Hanover, NH. However, there are plenty of excellent Gelato shops around, and then some pretty good ones too.

This place falls into the pretty good category. It's not cheap, but it does have absolutely lovely service, if the young brunette girl is working and you're me, that is. (Flips hair). The prices may not be dirt cheap, but this is Nashville, so not much is dirt cheap. If you have to rush off to your car to share with Starlight, make sure there aren't too many people in front of you, because it can take awhile for people to sample everything and pick their favourites. So don't be embarrassed or feel bad if you hold up the line samplng 8 different things.

Because trust me, you need to pick the right Gelato, because the portions here - even for the smallest order - are absolutely enormous. Quite un-gelato like, un-Italian for that matter. Much more American. Quite Tennessee. 

I wonder if the server is from Tennessee? Because she's the only ten I see.

My perfect threesome on our first date: You-mi-bubbletea.
