WHAT.

If you only go to one place in Philly, go here, and get these items:

What to get: Hot Pretzel, Lemonade, Shake from Miller's Twist.
What else: Pot Roast Sandwich from Smucker's.
And what else: Roast Pork Sandwich w/ Broccoli Rabe from Tommy DiNic's.
Any more: Beiler's Donuts and anything from Dutch Eating Place.
What not to get: Caught at Reading reading Penthouse by an Amish security guard.

But: While you're in Philly, you must also try John's Roast Pork, Nick's Roast Beef, and a bubble tea at Mr. Wish.

This is the quintessential Market for the East Coast. Every other City along the Eastern Seaboard wishes it had a market as lavish and spectacular. Basically it is food Paradise with all kinds of deliciousness inside. A lot of it is overpriced and touristy, but there are also some amazing hidden gems lurking within the walls, particularly those which are owned and operated by the Amish, who have a very large presence within this Market.

Speaking of very large presents... (pulls down pants)... happy Amishmas.

The number one highlight is Miller's Twist which is where you will get the best hot gooey pretzel you've ever had , which will make you never want to eat a pretzel from anywhere else, and will make you speak in very long sentences, and I mean very very long sentences. 

Also try their lemonade and chocolate milkshakes which are amazing. Make sure you get the plain pretzel. Or if it's a flying pretzel, the plane pretzel. The only other pretzel that I've had which compares is down at Sadie Anne's at the Dutch Village Market in Upper Marlboro Maryland. 

Next on the agenda you have to go to Smuckers Grill and get a Pot Roast Sandwich. The breakfast there is ok but the pot roast is otherworldly and sensational. Truly one of the best sandwiches in the world. You do not come to Philadelphia for cheesesteak sandwiches. You come here for other sandwiches such as John's Roast Pork and Nick's Roast Beef and this gem here in the Market at Smuckers.

The Dutch eating place is also very good as are many of the other stands in here like Beiler's donuts. But the next top highlight belongs to Tommy Dinic's. Roast pork is the sandwich that Philly should be famous for, and the only place that makes it better than Tommy is John's which is the ultimate pork destination. Tommy does a wonderful if overpriced roast pork with broccoli rabe. And I highly recommend asking for extra broccoli rabe. Once again skip the cheesesteak. If you must get one, try one when you go to John's, or grab one at Joe's Steaks & Soda Shop, along with some shakes.

Parking here is an absolute nightmare and they give tickets out the way molesters give candy out to children while hanging out of dark unmarked vans. I highly recommend using the parking deck and just paying the lofty prices to avoid the drama. Alternatively, park somewhere cheap far away, and walk into the center so that you aren't paying for every minute you're here. The parking meters and garages here are almost as much of a rip off as your Aunt was last night.

And if your friend Adel is hungry, I'll take him to the market, and will duly Fill Adel For Ya.

Came here to buy some cows. Should have gone to the Bovine Brothers.

They sell a lot of different types of produce and it's a really nice fruit n veg market right in the heart of the greatest Market in the region - the Reading Terminal Market.

While you're here, wander over to Miller's Twist and get a hot pretzel and a lemonade. Also try the Pot Roast sandwich from Smuckers. Trust me.

Anyway, the produce prices are shockingly low, and the quality is sky high, but then so was my mom last night.

OYSTER FAN HERE

Came in about 2pm today, just to have a simple dozen raw. This is exactly what I want in my neighborhood. Darnell the shucker does an excellent job. Told us he worked under Mike at Casamentos, my favorite place for oysters. No reason to even go there now. Absolutely no rocks/grit on the plump oysters. Prices are exactly where they should be. He gave us some lagniappe and I made sure to remember to come back again and again. Five Stars and a great addition to mid-city!

Careful, you may just walk passed this restaurant since it's sandwiched in between two other establishments but once you find it you will want to come back. 

The cocktail list has a decent selection, as does the wine and beer list with happy hour specials as well. I was slightly confused by their Thursday $8 cocktails stated on the menu since we were still charged full price the Thursday evening that we went but our cocktails were great either way. I ordered the Secret Garden with gin, creme de Violette, rosemary syrup, and club soda. It was a beautiful and refreshing cocktail. 

As our appetizer we ordered the buffalo cauliflower and the bistro steak as my entree. Both were delicious! We tend to order cauliflower if it's offered as an appetizer and we have yet to be disappointed and 47 Scott's was no exceptions. The batter was crispy and the buffalo sauce was light yet flavorful. The bistro steak was cooked precisely as I ordered it and was seasoned perfectly as were the truffle fries. The broccolini was slightly over done for my liking but not a deal breaker. 

The service was swift and our server was polite and inviting. The only recommendation I would make is to tidy up the back patio. Where we sat it, there were stacks of chairs, heating lamps, and a fan that just isn't eye appealing. Even leaving the heating lamps as is by the tables would be more appealing so that they could tidy up that space and add more greenery because the patio area is, for the most part, very nice.

I have been wanting to try Baja Cafe for quite sometime and just hadn't gotten the opportunity to until the last time we visited home. I went with a few other family members during breakfast on a Tuesday and I was quite surprised with how busy it was so early on a weekday. 

Despite the high volume of diners, they had an area set up for us quickly since we had five in our party. They also had menus and waters to us quickly. I only got a small glimpse of the entire restaurant since we sat in a smaller dining area to the right of the entrance but the restaurant was definitely buzzing with a lot of customers and overall seemed to be able to accommodate a lot of hungry people. 

They have a lot to offer on their menu from breakfast sandwiches to full breakfast plates like biscuits and gravy served with two eggs, choice of meat, and hashbrowns! For under $10!! Two of my family members ordered that while I decided on the Construction Burro. Basically a breakfast burrito in which they give you the "tools" and "supplies" to build it to your liking. I simply got mine with egg whites, sausage, potatoes, peppers, and cheese on top only, served with a side of salsa.

The burro was made exactly how I ordered and to my liking. I was very appreciative that they made mine with egg whites only and at no additional charge. The sausage and potatoes were cooked perfectly and were not greasy at all and the peppers added a nice bit of heat. The size is perfect also, you will not leave feeling hungry after eating this breakfast burro. 

The service throughout was good. They were attentive and helpful and we did not have to wait long before she took our order and brought us our check. The food came out fairly promptly as well. 

Overall it was nice breakfast experience and I am happy that I finally got to try Baja Cafe. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a great local restaurant.

I found Brewd to be the perfect place to stop after a morning hike at Sabino Canyon Park. It is easy to find and it isn't too far from the park either. Perfect for us since we were famished. 

Upon entering this quaint coffee shop, your first thoughts will be that it is simple yet inviting. There is ample seating inside, with outdoor seating as well, an area with some local and commercial goods for sale, a bookshelf next to a cozy seating area with a couch, a cooler with cold drinks, and a counter with baked goods calling your name. 

After looking over the menus for both coffee and lunch I ordered an almond milk cappuccino, the Saddleback Ranch Panino on multigrain bread with a side of quinoa, and an apple turnover. 

The coffee was made quickly and while we waited a bit of time for our lunch, we simply sat at one of the tables and enjoyed dessert first. Once our lunch did arrive, I found my sandwich to be good. The roasted turkey, brie cheese, and roasted pepper jam made for an appealing combination on the palate. The teensy side of quinoa left much to be desired on the other hand. It was slightly dry and rather bland overall. Also being served in what appeared to be a small sauce dish didn't make me feel like it was worthy of the title of a "side" in the first place. But the sandwich and turnover were more than enough to fill me. 

Overall, I quite enjoyed Brewd and will happily return again after hiking Sabino Canyon.

If you want a difference coffee experience with many different options of beans come here. The owner is an expert in coffee and can really educate you on the various brews. The coffee is slightly pricey but it is quality for sure. I had an orange vanilla latte with homemade orange syrup. Function Coffee Labs is different than your average coffee shop!

Lunch: Silver Legacy [Reno]

Dined here two weeks ago when we decided to take my mom to Reno on a day trip. Café Central is located in the Silver Legacy at THE ROW. It was our first time dining here. It wasn't our first choice of place to eat but there was no wait in line so we went for it and we were seated immediately. Spacing between tables were good and complied with social distancing during Covid times. Staff wore masks.

We were actually seated in a booth and we were immediately tended to for our drink orders. Our waitress shortly came after to get our food orders. Mom and I decided to share a Chicken Alfredo meal. Husband ordered the Joe's Special (breakfast meal). Our food came in good time and the presentation was nice. 

Not the best Alfredo pasta I've tasted. The Chicken Alfredo was bland and the sauce was too runny. The two slices of garlic bread were placed on top of the sauce so half of the breads were soggy. Mom and I didn't finish it... it took the three of us to finish the plate. My hubby did not eat the hash brown that came with his meal... it was too oily. We enjoyed our glasses of Coke and refreshing lemonade, though.

We had a good waitress. She was attentive and friendly. It was unfortunate that the food was just mediocre. Maybe will try something else from the menu next time. 

Review #1964

This cruise is pure New Orleans!

We used our City Pass to ride aboard the historical Paddlewheeler Creole Queen Jazz Cruise and experienced the lively sounds of the amazing jazz band as they entertained us on board. Loved it, truly pure NOLA!

Our cruise was a nighttime experience that started at 7:00p. This cruise did NOT include dinner but there are lite fare available to purchase including shrimp cocktail, cheese board accoutrements and some snacks. We started boarding at 6:30p.

After lots of walking around the city we welcomed some time for relaxation as we rested our sore feet and enjoyed the sweet Mississippi River breezes on the promenade deck. We soaked in panoramic views of the landmark Crescent City Connection Bridge as the city skyline slowly disappeared from our views under the stars. The cruise ran for about 2-1/2 hours and reservations are required. I called the morning of the day before our cruise and had no problems with making the reservation for a party of 3. On the day of our cruise we claimed our City Pass QR code at the kiosk nearby and were given tickets to present before boarding. 

Normal Entry Price - Adult: $52.00  Child: $26.00 

Review #1713

Great food but, oh, the long wait!!

3.5 Stars. I was looking for a local spot for breakfast and found this through Yelp. Read reviews from six Yelp Reno friends who gave this place good ratings. So here we were. 

We found the restaurant outside from the busy N Sierra and N Virginia Streets and yet just 1.4 miles (about 4 mins drive) from the Sands Regency on W 2nd St. The drive on Dickerson Rd seemed out in the countryside of Reno and yet so close from the city. 

We got to the restaurant around 10:30a and had it not been a blustery day we would've sat outside in their patio area, the weather was a beautiful 80° temps that day. The flapping canopies were a hint on how windy it was outside. Inside we were seated almost immediately. We were given a menu and we placed our orders. The restaurant was full and there were still more patrons coming in, some couldn't wait and had left. For us, our food came about 45 mins later (almost an hour)! I thought they forgot about us. Not sure if they were still trying to catch the cow for my country fried steak. Mom just had a Denver Omelet and hubby ordered  an Oxbow Skillet... nothing complicated or fancy. I've seen a busy restaurant today at Peg's Glorified Ham & Eggs in Roseville and we sat at the bar. I've watched the kitchen staff cook, prepare, and hustle to get the food orders out and it did not take 45 mins to get our food (although we waited 20 mins to be seated). Anyway, I digress... I would've been okay with the wait except there were some that sat later than we did and they got their food first :(

Finally, our food came. Hubby enjoyed his Skillet and the Denver Omelet was too much for Mom, it was a big portion and had the rest boxed to go. I enjoyed my meal but couldn't finish. Hubby ate the rest of my country fried steak.

Maybe Sunday was just a busy day for the restaurant but I don't mind coming back to try this place out again. I will then reevaluate my star ratings.

Review #0548

It's the waiting game...

We came here for an early dinner while walking along Bourbon Street. Seating was scarce but the hostess asked if we didn't mind sitting at a high top table there was one available so we took it. We were given menus by the hostess and we were brought a couple of glasses of water but it took a while for our waiter to come by our table. I had to flag the hostess to ask if someone will be taking our orders soon. We had a haunted tour to catch at 5:00p.

After awhile our waiter finally came very apologetic. He took our orders down... that took awhile too. My Cookies & Cream Milkshake came first. It was cool, it came in a mini milk bottle. It's supposed to have booze in it. It was all this w/o the alcohol: Absolut Vanilla Vodka, vanilla bean ice cream, white chocolate and Oreo® cookies, with whipped cream and a chocolate Oreo® churro. I know, I'm no fun #enjoyresponsibly

Hubby had the Whiskey Bacon Jam Sliders. Yass! he scarfed those mini burgers down. He said it was good! Must've been that added homemade Jack Daniels Whiskey bacon jam!

It took another while just to get our bill. Our waiter checked on us once as we were done with our food and he didn't have our bill ready. I told him we were ready to pay, he took my credit card. Shortly after, the manager came to our table and said that he took care of our bill. He probably realized that service was not their standard?  I actually didn't mind since I was distracted from posting pics on my phone. Also, our waiter may be new but It was a nice gesture that we appreciated from the manager and we thanked him. Our waiter returned with my card and we were on our merry way. 

Poor wait service but good customer service.

Review #1497

Late night eats - Reno

After attending a concert at the Reno Events Center that finished a little after 10:00p hubby and I found ourselves starving. Unfortunately, at this late a time there were no restaurants open other than the ones inside the casinos. And just like we suspected everyone from the concert stormed these nearby casino restaurants for late dinner. There was no way we can get seated quickly. We also didn't have a car available since we missed the last shuttle to take us back to our timeshare. 

Original Mel's wasn't too far a walk from the Events Center and also close to our timeshare. It is located inside the Sands Casino. These restaurants are open 24/7. We were seated quickly. Our server was very nice. He was busy with other tables but he didn't lack efficiency waiting on ours. I ordered the Mushroom Swiss Melburger. It was a tried and true meal for me. Hubby had a build-your-own breakfast. Although we yearned for some Asian food that evening our dinner satisfied us for the time being. Mel's Diner can be accessed from the outside and we didn't have to walk inside and through the smoky casino to get to the restaurant.

Review #1153

Good food, good company

We were here for an event and I like that this place is also historic. This gastropub is housed in an old railway headquarters. This used to be a railroad depot that served the traveling public until 1937 and was vacant for 25 years.  This was the Nevada-California-Oregon Railway [N-C-O] and the restaurant boasts a state historical marker right outside the front entrance. There are lots of outdoor seating in the front and back. Only outdoor seating in the FRONT had umbrellas. It would've been nice to have some large umbrellas that shaded the backside as well. We were burning up. The back was interesting, though, as it had mural paintings on the back wall by Joe C. Rock. 

I had the Classic Burger while hubby ordered the Grilled Cheese (white cheddar, Swiss, provolone, bacon and sourdough bread) except they forgot to include the best part... the bacon! Not to worry, though, after we brought it to the server's attention the chef corrected the error and hubby got a second helping with all the yummy ingredients. My burger was yummy, even though I wasn't sure what was special about it. Carl's Jr.'s "Six Dollar Burger" was just as good. Our grilled cheese and burger cost $18... EACH! Not sure if this was normal lunch prices but I'd hate to see how much that burger is on the dinner menu. Then an additional 20% service fee on top of the already expensive meals was tacked on. Anyway, maybe we paid for the view of the mural in the back. 

Dining inside? I wouldn't know... it seemed nice (and cool, as in temperature). Overall not a nice first time experience at this restaurant. I did have a great time with friends here, that was it. Our server was nice but got a bit frazzled from singlehandedley catering to our large group. The place is gated and plenty of parking can be found adjacent to the restaurant but not sure if I'll be coming back here again.

Review #1029

Acme Oyster House inside Harrah's New Orleans

Hubby and I were desperate for something to eat the night we arrived in NOLA, late, after a long flight schedule that included a layover in Las Vegas. It was finally around 2:30a when we got to our room. We weren't up for a long wait or a walk to the French Quarter although that weekend was very much happening with the long Labor Day weekend and Southern Decadence celebration. 

We were happy to stumble upon the Acme Oyster House inside Harrah's. From our hotel we just crossed St Peters St. and we were there. Very convenient. We placed our order at the counter and food was served to our table. Seating was shared inside the Hoodoo Lounge. The lounge had a charming décor and a friendly atmosphere. Music played loud.

Hubby enjoyed the Fried Shrimp Platter which also came with fries and coleslaw. I had a cup of Chicken Gumbo and their New Orleans Bread Pudding w/ whiskey sauce for dessert (only because they ran out of Bananas Foster Cheesecake)... it was okay. I did like the chicken gumbo. It quelled our hunger. Glad we made it there before they closed at 3:00a. The staff was friendly. No wait service except when they bring your order to your table. 

Review #1494

Finally made it here!

After seeing Donna B's Yelp check-ins here [Yelp Reno] and drooling over her photos we made it a point to visit this charming chocolate shoppe when we were in town. This is one of Reno's most favorite sweet spots located near the Truckee River in Downtown Reno offering unique handcrafted chocolates that will for sure ruin you for all other chocolate. 

While captivated by the variety of sweets including truffles, bars, turtles, barks and baked goods on display it was the ice cream that called my name. The weather was warm and somewhere in the 80's that day. Hubby and I admired, oooh'd and aaaah'd over the beautifully made chocolates as we headed over to the rolled ice cream section . It had a different name but was exclusively part of Dorinda's Chocolates. I think the friendly gal at the chocolates counter mentioned that it was owned by the Professional Chocolatier's son, Dillon.

Along with the handcrafted chocolates offered were other specialty items including chocolate fondue kits and s'more kits. The chocolates can also be packaged into fun boxes for gifts and they ship nationwide!

Review #1077

Authentic Taiwanese dishes...

Up until today I've only stopped by here for boba drinks. On my 4th check-in we decided to dine here before heading back to California. We walked in and we were told we could sit wherever we wanted so we sat by the window. We were given menus and after deciding what to get we placed our order with the server. Service was pretty quick here. Got served our wonton soup first then the main dishes came shortly thereafter. 

We ordered the following:

Taiwanese Style Wonton Soup - didn't really like this soup. It had different taste and had bean sprouts and other veggies. I could handle the loads of veggies but not the bean sprouts.

Crispy Pork Roll - appetizer that came in six big pieces and sweet sauce. Unfortunately, I didn't get a chance to taste it to comment but Mom enjoyed it.

Pork Fried Rice - delicious and tasty! Right amount of ingredients mixed in with the rice. Was debating whether to try their Spam fried rice or Hawaiian fried rice. Next time :)

Salt & Pepper Pork Chop, a traditional Chinese dish and one of my favorites! The portions were big and it wasn't too spicy for me. I liked how they prepared this dish.

Of course, as we wrapped up our dinner I had to order boba drinks to go. Love their smoothies w/ boba. The service was fast and the food was great. The only thing I didn't like was they don't put ice on their drinks. I had cold water but not ice-cold water served to me. Parking is limited. There are some private parking spaces that is shared with a Starbucks and other businesses but there is also street parking available.

Review #0961

Dining in Nashville...

We had the most pleasant dining experience here today. Dine-in was available. Hubby and I walked in around 6:00p, we were greeted by the host and was seated immediately. The restaurant is huge! We were led towards the back where there was a huge pond with a waterfall. Very cool! 

We were given complimentary corn fritters. It was similar to a beignet but with corn in it. I wasn't too hungry at the time so I ordered something I thought was light... a cheeseburger from the kids menu. Simple yet filling and delicious with the fixins. I chose deep fried corn on the cob as my side dish. Hubby had the Pulled Pork BBQ Sandwich. I didn't have to ask how he liked... he almost inhaled his sammy. 

Megan was our server and she was awesome! Very attentive, friendly and fast. Also, there was Alicia (I think she is the manager), she came to our table and checked to see if everything was good and to our satisfaction. Also handed us a couple of coupons for one free scoop of ice cream at Mimi's Ice Cream Shoppe next door. The ice cream parlor was accessible from the restaurant. 

It looks like my fellow Yelp friend from Sacramento, Dennette and her hubby, enjoyed their experience here as well... five stars! Staff wore masks and guests were seated complying with social distancing. Big thanks to Megan and Alicia for a pleasant dining experience.

Review #1826

Nothing special...

I did not find anything special about this place. I've often wanted to dine at a HHAGG since I've seen them around Las Vegas, it seemed to be a popular place to eat. My first time dining in a HH and my experience happened to be in Reno. The restaurant is located on the second floor inside Harrah's.

Friday evenings they closed at 2:00a. Hubby and I came here after watching a show at Sammy's Showroom. We were told that the wait time would be 45-mins. The restaurant was only 1/3 full so we didn't understand why we had to wait at all. We were handed a restaurant pager. It turned out we only waited 25 mins and we already knew what we wanted since we were able to take a look at their menu while waiting. 

I ordered the BBBLT while the husband chose to have the Country Fried Steak (his favorite). It seemed longer than normal to get our food. The restaurant wasn't full. When we got our food the presentation was impressive... HUGE servings but at first bite the bacon strips were cold and hard. The BBB in my BBBLT was supposed to be the best part of my meal and there was a generous pile in my sandwich but I was disappointed, plus the food was bland, no taste at all. I only ate half of the sammy. The fries were good, though, tasty and crispy and the only part I enjoyed in my meal.

Although our server was really sweet it took a long time for her to initially come to our table, to bring our food and to give us our check. We had to ask for silverware and napkins. Did I mention that the restaurant wasn't full. Turns out she was also tending the bar. Had to flag the hostess down to give us our bill. Not happy with the food and service at this place. Spent too much time in here overall including the 25-min wait to get seated and the restaurant wasn't even at full capacity.

Review #1142

I was visiting Goleta from out of town for a wedding. We were looking for a place to eat and we all decided on coming to Nikka Fish Market and Grill since it was close to the hotel and the reviews were fantastic here on Yelp. 

I had previously had this bookmarked but I don't remember so I was glad that we ended up coming here anyways. The restaurant is a pretty decent size and were a party of seven and we were all able to fit inside of one of the tables fairly well. They have a really big menu here and everything looks so good that it was hard to narrow down what I wanted to eat. I ended up getting the seared ahi tuna burger. The veggies, the tuna, and the buns were all a really good size it was very satisfying.  The textural contrast all worked really well and it was delicious.  It came with a side of fries. I was given a choice of either fries or salad. I decided to get the fries in case any body wanted to share some.

My other friends went with a lot of different items as well. One friend got tacos, another one with paella, another got a clam chowder. So it was a big variety and nobody overlapped with their dishes. The staff here is very nice and they were very much on top of things.

There is tons of parking here and very easy to find. And it was a delicious choice and I'm definitely going to come back and try more food the next time I'm back in town.

Friday Night; 6p-8pm (Busy)
I was in the mood to feast, so I decided to come here for the All You Can Eat boneless wings special. It cost $16.99, and includes fries and a drink, the fries are also AYCE. It's not a bad deal at all. So for my first round, my flavor choices were Red Hot Riplets and Ridiculous  Ranch. I can see why the red-hot riblet  flavor is a go to, it is definitely a one of a kind and has an addicting taste to it, it is a dry rub type  and actually sweeter than spicy. The Ridiculous Ranch is more of a wet type of sauce, it is described to have  habanero & Ghost Pepper in it, which I didn't taste, it just tasted like ranch dressing with parsley sprinkled on top, but they were good. For round two my flavors were Traditional Hot, and Caribbean Jerk. Now the traditional hot had more of that kick, that I was looking for. But the way my taste buds are set up I definitely was craving something spicier. I like for my nose to be running and mouth panting type of hot sauce. And that was a wet sauce too. Now the Caribbean Jerk is kind of a mix between a wet sauce and a dry rub personally they just weren't for me, it was a little too earthy tasting and I guess I was expecting something fruitier, if that makes sense. Now for my final round, I chose Lemon Pepper and Honey Barbecue, they were both a wet type of sauce and tasted very good. So I'd have to say my favorite of all the sauces I tasted, was the traditional hot. And I would also like to note that I have been here on a previous occasion and I had the bone-in Wings which I would just like to point out are a lot better than the Boneless Wings. Not that the boneless wings were bad, I've just had better. 9 times out of 10 I'm going to choose boneless wings but their bone-in wings are just a hundred times better. I've also read mixed reviews about the fries I personally loved the fries, I thought they tasted great. I do hate that this place is so far from me, I had to drive 30 minutes just to get there. So it's kind of one of those places where I have to be craving it to go there. Overall I had a great dining experience and I'm sure I would return.

Very sad how downhill this place has gone.  After visiting recently I am lead to believe that the "secret recipe" only comes out for celebrities and people who come in with TV cameras, oh and James Beard award food critics.

Let me give you the order of events when we went:
No wait, which was a nice thing..
sat down 10 minutes later
menus 10 minutes later
meal 10 minutes later
silverware and napkins  10 minutes later
beverages
cornbread??!?!?( yeah that never happened)

I wish I was making that up, but unfortunately I am not and we weren't the only ones this happened to while we were there.  Their menu is pretty straightforward... chicken, pork chops, stuffed pork chaps and the sides are either a salad, red beans and rice or simmered green beans and rice with gravy. 

I got the green beans and they were nothing short of bland, the gravy was ridiculously salty.  The chicken was lukewarm and completely over-covered in a greasy SUPER salty batter the likes of a tempura. To pay $10 for 3 pieces of chicken and a side ($13 for all white meat), well let's just say I have had better at Popeyes.

The people who give this place RAVE reviews have clearly never had fresh Popeyes chicken or Lil Dizzy's.  I am being quite serious.  The funny thing is no one sends the food back or complains about it.  It's the craziest thing I have ever seen. The people just lap it up like there is a golden ticket hiding inside or something.

I politely (in an event to not upset the zombie like masses) asked for a to go box.. which in my case meant to go right into the trash as soon as I walked out of there.

Won't be back (even if someone else is paying!)

is it possible to give negative stars???? no really..

All the warning signs were there to include the 18 wheeler off loading boxes of frozen french fries and meat when we pulled up...  but oh how I ignored those flags.  If you want to kill 2 hours with bad food and even worse service, this is your spot!

I hang my head in shame because honestly I should have known better than to brave TGI Friday's but we couldn't decide what to eat and were starving and thought since it is fairly new, we would give it a whirl.  After a 20 minute wait... yes we had to wait to endure the abuse we finally were seated.

Our less than attentive waiter who honestly seemed put out that we even existed took our order, that was a quick relationship as we didn't see him again until it was time for us to wave him down like a person stranded on a desert island to get our check.  We had a little one in our party so the kids food was ordered right away.  Let's talk about the Friday's menu for a minute shall we, it is AWFUL bougie for a family restaurant.  $10 hamburgers, $14 pasta dishes... really??? I mean I could go to Port of Call or Yo Mammas and get an amazing burger for that price and a pasta dish at many 4 star places in the city that would blow the socks off of their offerings.  Apparently Friday's thinks they are pretty darn special! and by special I mean, expensive.

So let's talk about the food.  I got the burger because, amidst the myriad of crazy food combination meal choices (chicken, mango, and avocado salad I am talking to you), it seemed the safest bet.  So how do you ask did my $10 hamburger come out??? I asked for medium well and it came out very well done with absolutely no juice.. and the size?  equivalent to a regular hamburger at any fast food place.  I honestly wanted to ask a manager if they mistook it for a child's burger.. but I will get to that later.  There are truly no real healthy options, in addition to the crazy combinations of ingredients, everything has a thick sauce or is deep fried and don't fall for the "multi grain pasta" trick it's basically your traditional pasta.  

Service??  service???  no really.. can I can some SERVICE!  Our waiter (the one who we saw like a flash in the night when he took our order, yeah that guy) was non existent.  The child's food came out quick, the rest of our food didn't arrive for another 40 minutes, I wish I was joking.  When it came, it was cold and burnt (they like to defy the laws of physics at Fridays apparently) and completely underwhelming.  The flashy menu and descriptions of their bougie overpriced family restaurant food are a worse bait and switch than the average used car lot.  On top of that, when it did come the lady that brought it did the coolest waiter move I have ever seen.  Have you ever seen someone literally keep walking and drop/slide a plate at your table all at the same time?  Well this chick had that move down!  As she did it she said a quick "here ya go babe" ahh the joys of dining in Metry.  Now that's talent!  We never got condiments for the burger and never got a drink refills until... wait for it... after we paid our bill, because that's really when you need a refill.  The best part was not even our waiter dropped the refills off.  It was someone else who seemed rather confused and even said to us "I was told you needed refills,"  umm yeah about an hour ago that would've been greeeeeeaaaat (in my best Bill Lumbergh voice)

There was one female manager present that we could see and she was so busy comping other tables' meals that even though we asked to speak to her, after waiting 30 minutes she still never made it to the table.  We gave up since the stomach cramps started kicking in after this multi hour abuse session.  We tried to call after to ask for a manager but guess what?  No one ever picked up our phone call.. imagine that!

Who I am most upset with about this experience you might ask?  MYSELF!  I knew better than to go to a place like this and I paid for it... boy did I pay for it.  Throw in an upset stomach for several hours after, to add insult to injury.

After all of this I need to give myself a big hug and a dozen roses to apologize..  Seriously, save yourselves and go elsewhere!  The only joy I got from this experience was writing this review, so to Yelp 5 stars for allowing me to vent my frustrations, I heart you!

This is a very difficult review to write.  I always say that a good server can rescue a bad meal but the best meal can be ruined by the server.  Sadly in Ashley's case she was the latter of the two.

Writing a review after a bad experience can be frustrating as one wants to alert the issues while still giving credit where it's due.  Trashing a place based on a bad experience is usually not fair to the establishment when so many others enjoy it and so many other things are going right.  

Our group is visiting New Orleans from New Jersey, and myself from Massachusetts.  We also had one friend native to here.  The County Club was hosting their Halloween Drag Queen show which was fun and attracted lots of guests.  We were excited to come in as there a cancellation and got a table in Ashley's section.  

The show was entertaining.  Two drag queens came out at various times doing a fair number of songs.  Myself I found their performance dull, done to death, and they basically walked through the dining room with an occasional pose and mostly out of sync with the words.  I'm not really big on drag shows but I think I have been spoiled with the expertise of the ones in Massachusetts.

The food was magnificent!  Between the six of us there was boudine, fried chicken in green tea marinade, lemon curd pancakes, crab cakes, grits, home fries, and of course bottomless ten dollar mimosas!  Then food was beyond reproach and I think had service been better this could have been a five star review.

Now for service.  We waited about an hour and a half for food to get to us.  We even watched a few tables that came in after us get served.  Now I can understand a backed up kitchen but this was extra special.  Our server Ashley was quite often nowhere to be found.  I am not lying when I say that W had to go up to the bar to get herself the two Bloody Mary's sitting waiting both times.  Ashley made no apologies for anything, including not serving.  M  had to wait until the end of her meal to get her grits [of all things] at which point was boxed up to take home.  Again no apologies and simply not caring.  When it came time for the check to be paid she hovered over our table FOUR times.  It was just the worst service to be had.  Finding a host to complain to wasn't going to happen.  The place was busy plain and simple.  

So to sum up
Food - 5
Service - 1
Show - 3

If I could give this place no stars I would.

I have been wanting to try this place for a while, since I love a great cheeseburger (South Philly Tap Room has the best). We went after the Night Market in N. Liberties (another mistake). 
Seated right away which was good, but that was the last good thing that happened. The beer list is mediocre so I tried an adult milkshake. It was ok, but not worth the price tag. The service is super slow and by the time we got our burgers, my bun was completely soaked with grease. Disgusting. The burgers themselves are not great, average at best. They just put a lot of toppings on a basic burger. Not impressed. 
Do yourself a favor and avoid this hipster hotspot and get a burger at SPTR.

I was here last night with my groomsmen celebrating my bachelor party.  The food was excellent but it was honestly the service that prompted me to write this post.  When we first sat down from going to the salad bar we hadn't even turned our cards when the chefs started coming.  While this was nice, it kind of defeated the purpose of the cards, the really troubling part though was when they stopped coming around.  My best man was still eating when the chefs stopped making their rounds.  It become painfully obvious that our table was being passed over for new guests that had been seated regardless that his card was flipped to the yellow side and even repeated requests for service were made.  Only once did a chef come by when we asked our waiter to send someone and the chef did not have his former cheerful demeanor about him.  This was my first time dining at Na'brasa and for the price and the hype I have heard about your restaurant, I expected a higher level of professionalism from your staff.  My hope is that this does not come off as rude or trying to score a free meal because that is not the case, you have excellent food but when paired with poor service the end result is a bad taste in your guest's mouth, with little desire to return.

I sent this same post as an email to the GM, I'm hoping that this was a fluke experience because I've only heard good things about it.

Sometimes you try just one thing somewhere and you're sold!I wish I tried more of their foods but there's always a next time.

I'm such a craver of fried foods and cheese curds and fries top that list-maybe good wings also can be amongst them.

I have had the best cheese curds in Minneapolis in their State Fair.Ever since then I haven't really had any that came close to them.This place is located in the heart of Reading Market and caught my attention obviously by reading the mind blowing reviews it holds.

I ordered their cheese curds and lemonade.The cheese curds were freshly made-piping hot.With crisp thin batter and gooey cheese inside it was absolutely divine I could eat them all day.It came with a ranch kinda sauce which went perfectly with it.The lemonade was too sour for my liking and I did let the lady at the cashier know-she was kind enough to exchange that for a Coke for me.Great service.

I enjoyed the curds so much that I actually went for a second.Lol!!

Next time if I'm there or if YOU guys end up going there please try this place for its cheese curds and you won't be disappointed.

Omgeeeeee.....words can't describe how wonderful this place is.Without a doubt this is one of the best sandwich I have ever eaten.I may just go to Philly to eat this sandwich.

So this deli is located in their famous Reading Terminal Market.Everything here is so fresh and service is quick.

I wanted to try them after reading such amazing reviews on yelp and their photos were absolutely drool worthy.

I ordered a pastrami sandwich with slaw on the side.The sandwich was oozing of soft, wonderfully cooked delicious meat.The meat had such an amazing taste to it-it actually was melting away in my mouth.The bread used was fresh and delicious as well. It was so packed with meat that I actually took some out of the sandwich to eat with a fork.The slaw was crunchy and fresh.

Like I said in the beginning of my review I would just go to Philly for their sandwich.The market is always busy and thus it's hard but not impossible to find a seating.

Anyone going to Philly please try thus place and bless me with good wishes :-)

Ok. I am seriously biased, I know. But when an amazing Philly restaurant goes out of its way to celebrate your rich culture, food, at VERY reasonable prices..how can I not give this a five star?

I am Burmese. I also live in New York..which means the best Burmese food (apart from my mother's cooking down in NJ) happens inside of a local's home somewhere in Queens (which, you CAN order..by the way). This is the the best Burmese (yes Burmese! Not Thai, not Chinese, not Indian..though as many of those who know Burmese food know that the cuisine borrows from all these..and if you're new to Burmese food, yes you can have your chicken satay and jungle chicken but then this review is not for you) resto on the East Coast. I've come here a handful of times before with my family (they sort of know my mom's family) but last I was here- a few years ago- it wasn't nearly as popular. 

I came to Philly for the weekend with my bf and we easily got a seat for 2 around 7:30 on a Sat night. It was pretty busy but the space has grown, and can definitely support a lot of people. It's also very rich with Burmese decor- lacquer wear tea seats and Buddha statues are rampant. The menu is adorned with info on the Burmese heritage. The owners, which are 3 Burmese ladies, are so sweet and serve you themselves. We had Christine- and she spoke to me in Burmese (well she spoke, I listened and nodded)

The food: 

Thousand layer bread with curried chicken- This is our take on Roti Canai (for the Malaysians in the house) and if you like Southeast Asian cuisine, this is nothing you haven't seen before. It's still delicious though- a thin layer of crispy fried paratha (kind of like a scallion pancake if you know Chinese/Korean food), with a side of chicken curry. The chicken was so tender (dark meat) and rich in a non spicy curry sauce. 

The Asian Tea Leaf Salad- YOU MUST GET THIS. You will not experience anything else like this in terms of Asian food- imported, dried tea leaves retain their strong flavor in this salad that's mixed with cabbage (a Rangoon twist as my Mom doesn't use cabbage), peanuts, some other kind of nuts (not sure which- something imported), and shrimp paste which gives it its kick.  A very unique and tea-esque/salty delight. 

The Spicy Chicken Curry with the most fluffy, and bad-for-you white rice.  Note: this has bones. They ask you beforehand if this is ok but that's quite traditional for Burmese curry because we believe the dark thigh meat is the juiciest (beware there is also like chicken neck in this, thankfully my bf is adventurous). The meat is pretty spicy and falls right on the bone. Con: It's also very oily (as all Burmese curries). The rice is really simple, but fragrant and yummy. 

Ono Ca-Swah- a chicken coconut milk broth noodle soup- I'm calling it the Burmese name because I don't remember how this was written in English. It's very good but I prefer my Mom's, which has more lemongrass, but that's just my Mom. You can expect grounded chicken atop a rich coconut milk broth (that's not so thick it makes you sick), with thick spaghetti noodles.  You can top this with coriander, lime wedges, and dry hot chili flakes. Yum. 

Finally, dessert: FARLUDA!  Here, this is made it into a milkshake-esque thing. It's hard to experience.. but, it's ice cream combined with rose syrup, jello-type of thin strips, tapioca, fruits (not in this one though), infused with coconut milk (this was regular milk I think though).  We shared one tall glass. 

If I could order the entire menu, I would. I love Burmese food and am so proud Rangoon goes out of its warm to show others how warm and  wonderful our heritage is. Service is very polite and FAST- we got our dishes out in less than 15 minutes and we ate in less an than hour. 

Dinner came to $40. Don't miss it!

Great Boba tea for a place in Tucson. (Meets  SoCal standards.) Tried the pearl milk tea. They were running awesome promos for their grand opening. Nice open space to sit and study or relax with groups.

CURRENTLY, sitting in the bar.. 
- ordered barbecued shrimp, oysters and fish, and broiled stuffed shrimp with carrot soufflé and 3 drinks. 

The carrot soufflé was terribly burned. I took a baby bite and asked for a different side of equal or lessor value. CHRIS, the current manager on duty.. told me.. it was their policy and pointed to the board.. that no substitutions are made. I said, even if the customer isn't satisfied? His response, yea, no subs if it's cooked to our specifications; meaning the restaurants specifications. He leaves. 

I turn around to the policy board to read.. and no where does it say substitutions can't be made if the customers taste buds disagree with badly burned or torched food.  

I call him back out.. let him know the policy doesn't read that.. he reads something about not paying in full.. that has NOTHING to do with you replacing a side that tastes like crap. & SURELY, he isn't implying that I wouldn't pay for the ticket. 

He says that is policy and basically I don't have to come back.

He is TERRIBLE for this business, and if that's policy, this Deanie's will not do well. He needs to GO!

Namese did NOT disappoint! I was here twice in one week. Great service, swift, friendly. Definitely will be a regular. 

Our table had the vermicelli bun bowl with shrimp, and beef pho. Super tasty & great flavor. Herbs super fresh.

They also have a super sexy outside seating area with a fire pit in the middle and booths and tables surrounding.

This place is a amazing from start to finish. I see why they received a perfect 10/10 rating!!! The flavors are outstanding here, it reminded me of Italy.

Make sure you make a reservation because you cannot get a table without one :-) wear your mask too!

Our server told us they are known for their table side mozzarella and pasta so that is what we ordered! To start we got one of their signature drinks. The children of the corn drink which has tequila in it, so you know that is for me. Here is a rundown of our food. 

Bread: Delicious and complemented our table side mozzarella.

Table side mozzarella: Amazing. My friend was apprehensive to order it because she had it other places and didn't like it but I'm glad we pushed through and ordered. Others I have tried the mozzarella was rubbery but this was smooth and creamy. I love it freshly made because it is warm and melts in your mouth. 

Calamari: It's hard to find the words to describe how good it was. It was light and fluffy with Asian inspired flavors after. It's just really good. 

Taglioni- the sauce was so good with the right amount of beef and basil. 

Dessert the chocolate gelato. I had a taste of my friends and it had Olive oil with it. I was confused if that would taste good. It definitely did! 

We ended up sharing all the dishes, and they give you serving forks to do so. 

I am going to say it. This is the best restaurant I have been to so far!!!

I have been waiting for this place to open since I heard about it earlier this year because honestly, who doesn't like breakfast food. I wanted to be there for the grand opening to see if it would live up to the hype. When we got there there was a line out the door already. Once we got in and ordered things went very well. 

We ordered the big dippers (pancakes) and a billy the kid. The pancakes were medium sided disks good for just dipping into the syrup. The billy the kid was a egg sandwich with a thick sausage patty covered in cheese and chili all on a ciabatta bun. We also ordered a side of chorizo patties and a made to order fresh squeezed orange juice. Everything was amazing. The yolklore sign gives a definition of it as "legendary breakfast" and it totally lived up to it. 

The staff was also amazing. The owner was bouncing around from table to table to check in on how things were going and if any one needed anything thing. All ages were there and it just was a great atmosphere. The only down side was the size of the place. It was a little cramped but then again it was opening day. I would imagine in a few years they will need to upgrade the size! But I highly recommend this place if you are looking for a wonderful and quick breakfast!

Another Dogtown winner! Even though Pats has been around forever, I just visited there a few months ago. It was worth the hype for sure. I went in knowing only one thing to order, their famous fried chicken. What a good amount of food for under $12. You get a leg, wing and breast along with two sides. The chicken is crunch and super juicy. It will probably be the only thing I order there. 

The feel is just like an old style pub which is cozy and very inviting. The staff is amazing, we have had the same waitress the few times we have been in and she is always joking and having a good time.

It's a good place for Sunday dinner or any night of the week for that matter. Don't be like me and wait to go there, do it sooner!

We were in town for 4 days. New Orleans has limitless awesome food. We came here 2 of 4 mornings. Nothing and I mean nothing means more than great service with a smile.

Great strong brunch drinks $10 which is a deal in this tourist town. Do the online get in line thing. Never waited. The French toast is the winner. Hands down the best I ever had. Doesn't even need syrup n I never say that. My baby has an omelet he scraped the remnants off the plate. The grillades(?spelling). Grits were seasoned just right. Can never get great grits up north. 

Service impeccable. Checks your vaccine card before entry or you sit outside. Every server has a smile on their face. First time I didn't have leftovers. I don't care that its touristy. Its damn good

This place really overestimated my expectations and my mans.  So its on bourbon street. We woke after a 5 hour unplanned nap. It's 1 am. It's New Orleans so something is always open. I do a yelp search. Now it took 39 minutes to convince my babe this is it. Most stuff on Bourbon is overpriced madness but I saw the chicken bacon crunch pizza..

All pizza by the slice. $5.50. Big thin crust slices. So we wander in at 2am. Ordered the chicken bacon crunch (must have). Its chicken bacon n chips I believe. The buffalo chicken slice and the pepperoni slice. We were in and out in 5 minutes. Told the man. Check the box. No way they got it all in there accurate in 5 minutes. 

Yes they did. Those chicken slices had big hunks of grilled chicken on them. We were supposed to share but time we had got back to our hotel I had ate all the chicken bacon crunch. Every slice was delicious and we bought a few slices later to bring home. A+ service. Damn good pie

I just noticed today that we got billed for April payment even though the gym is closed. We were told we should be glad to pay the staff salary even though we can't use the gym, I thought that was the owner's job. She is probably already applied for stimulus money to pay the staff and is going to pocket our dues, what a terrible person. She is making herself money while I struggle to feed my family, I'm out of work because of the coronavirus.

This has been may different things, but Chinese buffets have seemed to rule.  The last one was good and after it closed I was sad, but...
Loving this place!!
They have remodeled the inside of it and it is now very open and well set up.  The price seems a little much for dinner but if you see their offerings it is worth it!  They have oysters, clams, sushi, and many buffet classics like beef and broccoli and chow mien.  On Fridays and Saturday nights they also serve crab legs and lobster.  Everything I have tried I have loved.  
This is a pretty amazing little buffet.

Ok people, many of the complaints I've read in the reviews are a good example of how entitled yelpers have gotten and how lazy people have gotten in general. I came for lunch on a Tuesday, got a half chicken salad and half Caesar salad. Yes, the guy talking my order wasn't overly welcoming or enthusiastic when taking my order, but that does NOT mean he's rude. It's not an if/than situation (if he's not overly welcoming than he's rude). To be honest I find overly cheesy and overly enthusiastic people to be fake and annoying.

The second biggest gripe people had was the cupcakes weren't labeled. People, there's a GIANT sign on the wall behind it telling you what each cup cake is. Just match the cupcake top with the photo on the wall. Jeeezus, you're going to dock 1 to 2 stars because you can't be bothered to do some matching? My 2 yr old cousin can match things.

Anyways. The food was above average but nothing to write home about. Prices were on the higher end across the board but still within the range I've come to expect from a fast casual type establishment.

Now that I'm a Jersey girl, I thought I'd give this place a try. Seemed like a place a suburban family would go to. 

There was ample parking, so already a good start to my dining experience. I get so amped about parking eventhough I know it's a thing in the burbs. I'm a Brooklyn girl and used to stressing over parking. Many occasions I've had to park a half mile from my destination. One would say that defeats the purpose of driving but I would counter back with it beats the effing subways. But that's not what this review is about.

It was the start of the dinner hour so not a lot of people and zero wait time. Got our seat, waiter came, placed our order. Easy as pie. 

My kid got crayons and something to color. Hooray for distractions. 

The food was what you would expect at a chain. It did not blow you away but it was still enjoyable. The portions were big, service was great, and the final bill was reasonable. Overall a good night. Will I return? Of course.

First impression:

Tucano's is friendly, boisterous, and loud. Or at least it was on the eve of its launch party, which I was lucky to attend (disclaimer: I ate for free). The expertly run, expertly marketed opening night demonstrated that Tucano's will be a space to watch for those in the St. Charles area, casino-goers, or those in the larger St. Louis metro area who really dig red meat.

As with many Brazilian steakhouses, its most overwhelming characteristic is its size -- this place is big. Lots of tables, huge bar, and a triple salad bar (excuse me, "salad festival") off to the side. I imagine you'll find a seat here without too much trouble, although without knowing the area all too well I can't say for sure. Once you get past the obvious, though, the smaller components also impress: the friendly and rehearsed wait staff, the comfortable ambiance, the great value. But we'll get to that later.

Let's talk first about the food: Tucano's is very solid in this department. The aforementioned salad festival suggests one could make a pleasant dinner out of this alone. Various kinds of salads, pasta salads, side dishes, fried plantains, and soups are guaranteed (and most likely expected) to fill you up. The Brazilian lemonade is a must-try, even if I hate to know about the sugar content. The main draw, of course, is the meat, brought along by friendly fellows in matador-like outfits (all overseen by an ever-watching mob boss). These guys are good -- rumor has it they spent a long training session upstairs with oranges instead of meat.

Favorites at the table here were delicious, kielbasa-like sausage; chicken in what tasted like a honey glaze; and the prime rib (or a similar meat -- it's all blurring together at this point). But everything was good, warm, and filling at first glance.

The last reason I might recommend an early visit to Tucano's is an important one -- the price. $21 gets you access to most everything in the restaurant (i.e., the salad and the meat cowboys). If you've been to a Brazilian steakhouse before, you're wise to the fact that these meals often sit above $40 a head. Add-ons exist, like a $20 lobster tail, but this reviewer thinks you're good with just the basic package before getting fancy.

Bottom line: Feel free to try out Tucano's if you happen to be in the area or are in the mood for an all-you-can-eat. My first impression, as choreographed as it was, suggests it is definitely worth a visit.

(Author's note: I write "first impression" articles when a location has recently opened or I feel not enough information is available to write a true review. They aim to capture the feel and vibe of a place without much more.)

ok, i'm a believer. 

i usually swear off food trucks, but this one is actually GOOD. 

i never bought into the whole kogi tacos when it first took off in LA. so my go-to item on the menu here is usually the jungle stew curry or the curry of the week. 

portions are large, easily doubling the amount of meat offered by the other asian food trucks within a two block radius. it can be a little pricier than other food trucks (ie. $5-7), but it doesn't taste like a bunch of msg poured over rice. and when they say something is spicy, it really IS spicy! how refreshing. tyson bees does a better job than most restaurants that claim they serve spicy food.

now THIS is what i'm talkin about. you haven't lived til you've had really good soondubu (soft tofu soup). and this ish is the real deal.

if jong ka jib sits at 5 stars in my book, then i'd literally have to go back to every center city korean restaurant review i've ever written and downgrade them by one star (at least). that's how much better this place is. it just completely blows all those so-called korean places in center city out of the water.

the interior decoration is about as traditional as korean restaurants get. and the flavors stay true to the korean taste buds.. no diluting spices to placate the westernized palate. of course, you can always ask for your food to be less spicy. ahem *weaksauce* ahem. they also give every customer a huge stone bowl of rice to accompany their meal. L-O-V-E.

the banchan is decent. more fresh than anything i've tasted in the city, but not a very wide selection - only about 5 dishes. however i'll take quality over quantity any day.

e mei is an amazing reminder of home. not home like my mom's cooking (cuz that's unparalleled), but home like southern california, a glorious region with many great traditional chinese restaurants.

e mei is a traditional chinese restaurant in every sense of the word. from the fish tank and cashier's desk/bar that greets you when you first enter.. to the 4-seater booths lining both walls and the large round tables with lazy susan's down the middle of the restaurant.. to the chinese paintings on the wall and the signature red and gold back wall.

the menu is a bit eclectic.. mostly a fusion of dishes from all over southern china, including, but not limited to, sichuan dishes. i wouldn't necessarily classify this as a sichuan restaurant, as their spicy dishes are not THAT spicy and their cooking lacks the signature peppercorns indicative of sichuan food.

however, there is ample use of hot chili oil, but not so much that the food is greasy. i love that the food isn't drenched in sauce so that you can actually taste the quality and flavor of the meats. and yes, their best dishes here are meat-based. vegetarians beware.

the standout of the night was cumin lamb (something like that.. i don't remember the exact english translation). the complimentary peanuts and spicy broccoli stems at the beginning and the watermelon slices at the end were a nice touch. another reminder of home.

service is also exceptional here by a chinese restaurant's standards. i was kind of amazed.

I liked this Bourbon Street pizza shop's focus on doing two things, and doing them well - serving both delicious pizza slices and relatively low priced beer.

My spin 'n shroom slice ($7) was one of the seven slice options. It measured 9" long x 10" across and tasted great, with a thin, crunchy and chewy crust. There was also no shortage of the spinach, mushroom and onion toppings, and the slice wasn't greasy - nice!

I found the service to be accommodative and fast. They also offered beer on tap or in tall cans for $5, which they claimed was the lowest price on Bourbon Street. Excellent!

I met a group of people here for a dinner buffet and I was so happy I made the trek to Camden for this. While the entire menu wasn't on the small buffet everything was damn good.
   The highlights were the baked mac & cheese and fried chicken. To me these are good barometers of the rest of the menu at any soul food/BBQ place. I haven't had mustard greens and yams since I lived in the south (over 10 years ago) but being at a new place I tried them both and was very happy with them both. The cornbread was ok but I admit to being really picky with that. Fellow diners say the ribs are fantastic so that will be on my plate next time.
   This was a small small in the middle
of Camden which probably contributes to or not being more well known outside of locals like it should be. Corrine was around and talking to us while the rest of the staff helping feed us were incredibly nice. I plan on bringing my gf as soon as possible.

We sat outside. It was a beautiful night. Once our food was served the flies and gnats came which was VERY annoying. By the time we were nearly done with our meal the staff lit citronella burners that are all along the perimeter of the outdoor seating area. It definitely helped but I wish they would've done that sooner. 

Oysters 3 ways, tasty! Lobster mac n cheese, lots of lobster and so cheesy, yum! 

The seafood pasta, amazing!!!! They did not skimp on the seafood in this dish! See pics! Seafood platter was also very good. 

The service was friendly but our server disappeared a few times. She forgot to bring bread and then when she asked us a second time if we wanted it, we waited a while for it again which was annoying. 

Overall it was an excellent dinner and I'd go back!

I've had Anthonino's bookmarked since they opened, I think.  We finally decided to try it a week or so back and we weren't disappointed.  The ambience is not classic "Hill" - more nice Italian.  It's pretty darn loud in here, at least in the front room.  

We had the old stand-by clamari as an appetizer, then shared steak mudiga.  Our daughter had a provel and mozzarella pizza.  All of these dishes were very good, if not amazing.   The pizza was pretty special - the crust was light and delicious.   If/when we come back, I wouldn't mind trying a more "loaded" option.  Based on the piece I had and what I saw coming out of the kitchen, I'd say you can't go wrong with the pizza. 

We are regulars at a couple of the Gianino's restaurants, and Anthonino's is very comparable.  If it were more convenient, we'd probably be regulars.

They have some awesome recipes here. Also a nice beer selection and drink menu.   It's been around so long now, it's way past being considered trendy.  The good news is there were several open tables on a Saturday night.  

It;s a fun place to try some new things with friends.  For three of us, we ordered 4 tapas plates and an entree, then share it all.  The tenderloin was cooked perfectly.   One of the best filet's I've had recently and at $26 is a pretty good deal. We also had BBQ shrimp, which had a sauce kind of like BBQ sauce, which is not a traditional preparation despite the name.   Still, it was really good and came with a big piece of cornbread.   We also had the crab empanada, brazil nut encrusted cheese and cigarro cubano (sp?), which was sliced flank steak in a fried wonton.  All of these items were excellent.  I would get any one of them again.

This is a really good, fun spot for some delicious and interesting food.  If you haven't been, check it out.

The atmosphere here is vibrant.  That's the euphemistic word.  My wife would say noisy.  It's good to know, though - If you want to have a conversation with the person you're with, this isn't the best place. The bare-brick walls are cool to look at, but they also bounce sound around a LOT.  We couldn't really have a conversation while we were eating, and that made the wife quite unhappy and ruined her night pretty much.    If you want to be seen, or just hang with the in crowd, or it you're used to being in crowded bars, you'll be fine.  

We came for the food, though.  Most of the reviews have been excellent.  

Of the six items we got, two were in fact excellent, three were just okay, one was bad.  The highlights for me were the chorizo and brisket tacos.  I thought they were amazing, but my wife didn't like the brisket because she said it tasted like it was cooked in beer.  That might be why I liked it.  We also had a fish taco (fried), which for me was just okay, but my wife loved it.  The other "okay" items were the South Beach burrito, which was mostly beans and rice, and the chips and salsa, which were good but so what?   Finally, we both hated the carne asada taco.  It had a kind of grilled taste, but it wasn't right somehow - I didn't want to finish it my first bite, which is very rare and surprising.   Maybe liquid smoke was used?  I don't know, I just know I didn't like it and we normally love carne asada.  

We would probably come back mid-afternoon sometime.  I'd come back for the brisket anytime, even if I couldn't hear anybody I was with.

Hype is kind of scary for me because I don't like crowds and I don't like waiting in line.   Add to that the one and only thing I don't like about Nudo - they don't have much room for a line without going out the door.  All of this stuff is two strikes for me, but the third strike never came.  Whew.

My wife and I met for lunch on a Thursday.  It was busy, but I'm pretty sure there was available table seating the whole time,  Also, the people taking orders were efficient, so there were never more than a couple of people in line.   The look and feel is modern, clean and well designed.  I was just a bit confused after leaving the registers when I saw some bowls of dipping sauce on the counter - should I take one?  The answer is no - they were for servers to bring out with the spring rolls.  By the way, they tried to upsell us on a spring roll when we ordered, but we resisted, although I love them.  Turns out they aren't necessary - our bowl of soup left us stuffed.  They did look good, though, so maybe next time.

We ordered two bowls of ramen - the Classic Nudo and the Hebrew Hammer.  As far as I could tell, the difference was one had sliced pork and the other had chicken.   I thought they were both great although we both preferred the Hammer.  My wife didn't care much for the pork, but I attribute that to personal taste.  I will add, though, a large slice of pork is kind of hard to eat with chopsticks or a spoon.  

The taste is the thing, though, and it was amazing.  It came out fast and hot and it was enough that we left feeling stuffed.   A couple of people stopped by to make sure everything was okay.  The staff all seemed friendly and happy to be there.  

Overall, a big five stars.  We'll be back a lot.

2.5 stars, rounded up to 3 because it reminds me of home. Coming from a 100% chinese background I'm struggling to give Seven Cups the five stars that many people think this place deserves, simply due to the "unfreshness" of the food and the high unwarranted prices. The tea house itself is beautiful, many of the tea pots, furniture and decor remind me of my grandparent's tea room back in Shanghai. The teas are great and are of high quality, but I really have to ding this place on their "snack" menu. $2.25 for one tea egg? China Pasta House 2 mins away sells those bad boys for .50 each. The japanese mochis? $3.75 or was it $2.75? each? Those (the same brand) sell at Lee Lees or Grant and Stone market at pack of 6 for $4.00. The steamed pork buns? $4.00 for 2 little buns? $1.00 at china pasta house! The "Zhong zi" bamboo wrapped sticky rice at $5.75 is an outrage especially if they have been previously frozen. I also refuse to pay for 3 har gows aka shrimp dumplings that are frozen and then steamed in house for more than a dollar each. Going through the kitchen to the bathroom confirmed my suspicions, this place does not have a stove at all! Only 2 huge freezers side to side or 1 freeze+1 fridge and one microwave and 2 steamers side to side on the counter, what a disappointment. Unsure how this place can dare charge so much money for their snacks when they are not fresh. 

Their tea is also expensive.. they can go upwards to $10.00 for one person for one pot of tea, but it may be worth the price due to the high quality, but I refuse to pay for their food, I absolutely refuse. The mooncake I got today because I was feeling nostalgic and wanted to celebrate the Mid Autumn festival by myself was $3.00+, it was small and average, and definitely cold because it came straight out of the fridge. The one exception on their snack menu that I will be willing to try next time is perhaps their chai and ginger ice-cream, but thats it.

A perfect 5 star yelp rating? Yes! and this place totally deserves it.. If I could give more stars I definitely would. Great food each time, and even better service. Rainy day? no problem! Owner walks out of his food truck goes to your car window with an umbrella and takes your order. Order too savory/sweet/whatever? Owner will fix it. Still hungry? They won't judge if you order round two. Trust me, I've been there and definitely done that. Overall I can't stress enough that this is the best place to get a fast, cheap, delicious, healthy lunch. You can't beat the quality and the service you get here.. and the warm fuzzy feeling I get from supporting such a great local business in town is uncomparable to any other place in town. This business truly cares, so come get some great food and support a great business while you are at it!

Finally a place that serves good drinks in town.. I came here to get a toasted milk green tea w/ boba the other day, and I was very shocked at the quality of the drink itself. I love all the wide variety of tea options, and how they customize each drink by the order. I was a little hesitant on the flavour of the toasted tea.. and they said that I could sample the base of the tea so just the toasted tea itself minus the milk+sugar to see how it pleased my palette. I liked it very much! The boba here was a little on the hard side the other day, so I wish next time I come in they will be a little bit more softer and chewier, other than that I most certainly will be coming here for all my boba cravings and perhaps to study as well.

I love trying new places in Manayunk that I have not experienced. I met up with some friends and we were seated upstairs. As far as first impression the look of the restaurant is great but it is loud. Possibly because we were seated upstairs but where we sat was not a problem. 

We started off by sharing the traditional guacamole for the four of us. Plenty of guacamole for four people especially because we also got salsa. I can't remember if the salsa was free or a la carte, but I don't see it as an option on the menu. The chips were nice a crispy and the guacamole was on point. 

For dinner my husband got the dolce cerdo tacos (basically al pastor tacos). They were very good and very tasty. It was also a very nice portion for tacos. I went with the mariposa (veggie) burrito. Unfortunately I was not very blown away by the veggie option. The produce tasted fresh and the burrito was a great size, but overall it was very dry and lacking in flavor. 

We shared a pitcher of the house margarita. It was delicious! And our server was very attentive in making sure our glasses were full. And I thought the prices were reasonable compared to the amount of food you received.

I am in love with Bam Bam Kitchen and I cannot wait to have an excuse to go back!  I needed a lunch place pronto because I was getting hangry and I was in the area of Bam Bam Kitchen.  I had this place bookmarked for a while so I was excited I finally had the opportunity to give it a whirl.  I went during the lunch hour so plenty of seating, but I could see how this place could get packed during the dinner hour.  Although I was not super hungry, my husband and I decided to get something extra to try knowing we could pack it to go.  Here are some fab foods we tried: 
-Jeon - Korean savory pancake
-Stone Bowl Bibimbop (one with mushroom and one with pork)
For the savory pancake we asked our server what we should order.  He was very knowledgeable and was able to give a description on how each were different.  We went with the one he described as "crispy" compared to the other savory pancakes.  For the stone bowl I would recommend the pork over the mushroom.  The mushrooms were lacking a little bit of flavor but the pork was wonderful!  The rest of the bowl was great so I was not overly disappointed about the mushrooms.  This was the first meal I ever had where it continued to get hot and crispy as the meal went on, instead of getting colder.

Excellent portions and excellent staff.  You also get a bowl of miso soup with an order of an entree.

I am in physical distress writing this 4 star review. My brain and my heart are in s fierce debate and I'm not sure a simple glass of cab sav will dull my pain. Every fiber of my being wants to give Roadhouse a 5 star review as it is BY FAR THE MIST GLORIOUS MOVIE GOING EXPERIENCE IN THE WORLD!!!!!!! The prices are reasonable. The leather recliners are luxurious. The sights and sounds are breath taking, the bar fare is top notch, popcorn gets free refills, the service is divine, AND THERE'S BOOZE. If we've spent time together then you know that movies, popcorn, and adult beverages are really all I need to sustain me so at this point you're asking, "But Rebecca, you're clearly describing Nirvana...why oh why just the four stars?" Okay...here it is but before I tell you, please understand you need to go and experience this theater from heaven...okay, deep breath...the only way to guarantee seating is by booking tickets online which should be great but their website is a nightmare. If it works for me half the time it's a win. I've tried calling but have gotten no help. They say, " well it's working here. Try refreshing." Then I say, "Weird, I've been refreshing on multiple devices for 30 minutes." Believe it or not, I've missed going to two movies there now because of this issue. I've tried a computer, phone, and tablet. It appears the best way to get tickets is to show up to the theater several days before your show and buy tickets from the box office. Is it possible this is an intentional ploy to get you in the door to go to the restaurant? Perhaps. If everything else about this paradise wasn't sheer perfection my review would be less. I'm hoping that by writing this they look into the issue...but seriously, go to Roadhouse. Invest in this wonderful gem of a small business and hopefully this hiccup gets ironed out soon...BTW Roadhouse peeps, message me when this gets fixed and I'll be thrilled to write an update.

Discover new memories and happiness. Seek out what the heart desires and give in, just a little. 

As our adventure begins with locating a parking spot. Truly, parking is a mess here, this little shop is located in the downtown area of Tucson. It's a hop away from the university. It's worth the extra time that you will spend to gain access here. Parking in most areas is always free, but this could change. When I have visited, parking is still free. 
 
Now all parked and out of the truck, let's go! Shall we explore what Woops has to offer. Aside from macaroons they serve "real food," here too. If your looking for a sandwich, cafe style with deli meats and cheeses on a fresh croissant let's do lunch. Besides macaroons, for us caffeine nuts they got ya! How about a matcha latte along side that box of macaroons. Prefer coffee it's all here brewed fresh whenever or whatever. Find your happy, then get ready to order. 

When ordering it can be done over the phone, in person, or from your social media app; Yelp. Their pricing is about average. What's average? A box of twelve macaroons will set you back around $24. This is a whole box. The macaroons are sold individually, but everything is cheaper by the dozen. Besides, who can eat just one or two macaroons? It seems I'm a creature of habit for when I find something that I like, theirs no chance of changing it. My drinks of choice are the cafe au lait and the matcha latte. Both are delicious with no added sweetener than what nature gives us . Their espressos shots are that smooth. The matcha latte has no after taste nor bitterness. In fact, they ask every time if you want sweetener in your matcha or coffee beverage. 

Prior to COVID, I cannot report how the business was handled. After COVID, the store is always clean, friendly, and merry. The lobby of this little cafe holds around two to three tables inside and a few outside seating areas. They are always clean and sanitized. The staff makes it their mission to immediately greet every guest with a genuine smile and warmth. Every time I visit here the merriment of the employees makes any unhappiness melt away. What's not to love? The ambiance of the store cries out to all. It's a call if you listen, deep in your soul. Good individuals gather and are employed here. Come and celebrate with coffee lattes and macaroons always. 

The owner of Woops is always kind. Her employees feel like family. The store is so inviting, it's worth a pop in just to see. If you ever have a few moments, come on by! The macaroons are delicious and oh so excellent. The coffee is in demand and always fresh. Find happiness wherever your heart takes you! For great eats and some fun make new memories. Come and explore the down town Tucson area. Stop in for that cup of joy to keep the days events rolling along smoothly. Make new memories and stops along the way.
