Explore new paths along the journey.

Espresso mint julep!  Lovely and very suitable for New Orleans!

They have other refreshing coffee brews! 

Get your mojo on here!

Creamy Cajun crawfish omelette for the homely win!  They had their signature hot sauce that complimented well when one drizzles it all over! 

Shrimp 'n' grits was nicely done as well!

It's surrounded by French esthetic homes! I adore the styles! 

Stupendous on their brunch dishes.

Brunchin' 'n' munchin'!

What a fabulous rice bowl as a late night munchie! 

They don't have lamb meat here, but the beef is good.  Spicy, packaged hot sauce, surely - too fuego (I did one and a half package size). Yogurt reminded me more like ranch dressing rather than the yogurt from a typical Halal stall.  It was the same for the hot sauce too - a bit thick on paste and not the flow of fluid hot sauce one usually gets from the stall.

I enjoyed the rice and beef bowl entirely.

Baklava, to my sweet surprise was flaky and nicely maple taste to the whole desert.  It was delightful.

One can't go wrong on this rice bowls here! Comfort food to my classic liking and yum!

I literally drove 404 miles non-stop for this meal.  Literally!

We were heading home after an extended weekend in PA.  We stopped in Columbus, OH for lunch and somehow nobody felt the need for a pit-stop before we made it to the restaurant for dinner.  Not quite sure how that happened but it makes a good story.

Late dinner on a Tuesday night.  It took a little while for someone to be designated as our server and the guy who sat us felt bad about the delay so he comped us an order of their corn fritter things as an appetizer.  Those were some really hot (temperature) little bundles of fried goodness.  Slightly sweet, crunchy and gooey all at the same time.

I decided on their shrimp po boy for my dinner.  I was anxious to see how it stacked up to the version I had tried at Gulf Shores the previous week.  I would like to say different but both were good...but that would be an understatement.  The shrimp on this version smoked the ones on the version from Gulf Shores but the remolade at the other place was a lot better.  Maybe its a tie - maybe not.

Kid 1 claimed she wasn't hungry but then decided on an order of fries.  They were pretty tasty and both looked and tasted as though they had been cut freshly in house.  Normally I would not let her call that dinner but after being cooped up in the car with the kids for almost 12 hours I really didn't care.  There goes my nomination for father of the year.   

Kid 2 ordered a humungous burger.  I thought about trying a bite but just didn't have room.  The wife nicked a corner and reported that it was very good.

The wife went after their SBR - sausage, beans & rice.  I managed a bite as well and it was delicious.  The sausage pieces were pretty small but that just meant that every bite had a piece or two and the flavors were uniform throughout the dish.  The beans were in a slightly spicy sauce.  Not spicy like hot, spicy like flavorful.  Delicious!

The kids each had a piece of their snicker's cake for dessert.  There was an invocation of the daddy tax and I thought it was a pretty good dessert choice although it is doubtful that it was house made.

Great place!  Can't wait to get back to dive a bit deeper into their menu...

Keeping this short because everyone and their brother has already reviewed this place.  A few thoughts:

* Pulled pork is better than Pappy's...by a lot
* Baked beans are nothing short of spectacular
* I should have had a different side instead of the fire & Ice pickles

I can't wait to find myself there around lunchtime again soon!

I ate what may be the most interesting dish I've had a restaurant in years at this place!

The wife and I came in for dinner on a Friday night and the place was pretty much packed.  Fortunately, they accepted our reservation when I called before leaving the house and had a table for us within about 3 minutes of arrival.

This is a family-run business.  They are Kurdish people and there are only as many of them as there are.  When the restaurant gets really busy they get stretched a bit thin.  These ladies sure do hustle and the amount of food coming out of the kitchen is a bit staggering if you get to peek back there and see the operation.  We were seated close to the kitchen so we had front-row seats to watch them busting their butts to get everyone taken care of as efficiently as they could manage.  The only male employee in view was the bus boy.  He turns out to be a friend of the family.  The restaurant appears to be an enterprise run by the women of the family with mom in the kitchen and the sisters/cousins waiting tables.

We started with the baba ganoj because we have a hard time not ordering the stuff when it's available.  Made in house and more mild in flavor than I generally prefer.  Still quite good but next time we will try something else.

I asked our waitress (one of the younger sisters) for a recommendation between a couple of entrees.  She asked if it was my first visit and then proceeded to tell me that the Sultan Pilau was what I needed to order.  The wife went in a different direction.  Our mains arrived as we were just finishing up the app.

"Wow factor" really doesn't do justice to the Sultan Pilau.  I believe this may well be the most interesting restaurant dish I've been served in years.  Please take a look at the picture attached to my review as I don't know that I can do it justice with an explanation.  When you break into the dish you're greeted by a puff of steam because it is served that hot from the kitchen.  The phyllo dough is flaky and buttery while the rice is flavorful, tender and incredibly interesting based on the depth of flavors which I cannot possibly put into words and do justice to the dish.  The lamb inside is likewise nicely seasoned and cooked to the point of fork-tenderness such that it almost falls apart.  There are a bunch of other ingredients in there as well and every bite contains some combination of a few different varieties of nuts, rice, lamb, phyllo and who knows what else but it's dang delicious!  

For dessert I had their kanafa.  In our family, this one is known as the hairy dessert because of the appearance of the shredded phyllo dough and their interpretation did not disappoint!  I was blown away by the depth of flavor in what is a relatively simple dessert: phyllo, cheese, honey and that's about it.  The dish was served at the perfect temperature such that the cheese was slightly melted and had a nice pull to it.  The phyllo was slightly browned on top and everything came together beautifully in each bite.  

Out the door for less than $60 after a generous tip because I was so enamored with the family running the place.  Great food, friendly if rushed service and a very reasonable price!

Confession time...

I'm really bad at remembering what I eat when I go to Indian restaurants.  This may be due to the fact that I have only been eating Indian food for a short while.  Possibly the fact that I have a hard time with the complex names.  Maybe it is what was termed CRS when I was in the military...can't remember shit.  Not sure but this is an area where I could improve as a food fanatic.

We went there based on the positive reviews on Yelp.  They had the buffet set up so we were able to try numerous things,  My favorites were the tandoori chicken and something I'm pretty sure was called korma.  

A few observations...

Some of their stuff was a little past mild.  This was a really good thing as the heat added considerably to the experience.  It was not a burning heat; rather, just enough to make you notice without being painful or detracting from the flavors of the food.

There were layers of flavor in everything we tried.  If you take a bite and then think about what you're tasting you can discern some interesting complexities.  

Tandoori chicken (not sure why that name resonates but others do not) was perfectly cooked.  Juicy, tender and flavorful with a hint of smokiness.  Simply delicious and the best version of this dish I've every tried.   

Their sauces are very flavorful and everything was really fresh tasting.  They had a great variety of dishes available for us to try.  Some were vegetarian, others were lamb and chicken.  Some were in sauces, others were deep fried.  There were about a half-dozen different sauces and chutneys to try.    

Service was amazing!  The staff explained the numerous dishes to us and answered questions about what is traditionally served with what else.  Our glasses were never empty and the recommendations they made were all spot-on.

If you hadn't yet guessed...we really liked this place!

Absolutely a 5-star experience!

We dined with a group of friends and between the food and the fellowship it turned out to be one of our better evenings out in a long time.

Here are some high points:

Bread and butter - both were delicious.  Two varieties of local bakery bread with a sweet butter that was served at the right temperature to really pull forward the creaminess.  Yum!

Charred octopus - I pretty much don't care what kind of restaurant I'm at...if they have something that sounds like this on the menu I will order it 10 times out of 10.  Glad I did!  The octopus was tender, flavorful and well-matched with the other ingredients. 

Cauliflower & cheese curds - also both delicious and worth trying.  I truly could have dined on the appetizers but for the fact I was really in the mood for a burger.

Burger - cooked exactly as I requested.  Slightly messy but that's alright sometimes.  I usually ask for something to be added or left off a burger but for some strange reason I decided to try theirs exactly as it was described on the menu.  I loved it.  The tartness and crunch of the dill pickles, sweetness of the onion, creaminess of the American cheese and sheer beauty of the beef all combined to make one damn fine burger.

The pot de creme for dessert was nothing short of a display of first-world decadence after the meal I had just enjoyed and it was absolutely delicious.  

There were no low points.

Brand new place out in our neck of the woods; aka, West County.  Owned by the same family who runs Classic Red Hots.  The main appeal there is how much of their food is prepared in-house.  That appeal carried over to this new offering as well.

The tea reminded me of being in Iraq and visiting with the locals in the markets...especially once I added the requisite amount of sugar.  The kefta also brought me back but the bread was different - probably because this is not an Iraqi restaurant and they are not selling street food.  About the kefta - loved the spice!  Lots of parsley, cinnamon, cardamom and others really brought the flavor to a level rarely seen in the US.  The wife is on a felafel tear right now so that was her choice for dinner.  We split our sandwiches so I got to try hers as well - also very good.

Almost forgot - their baba ganoj - one of the best I've had.  I really liked the fact that they kept it at a coarse chop instead of blending it smooth.  Big, smoky flavor with just the right amount of garlic.  That appetizer alone will bring us back to this place.

Disclaimer: This is a Middle Eastern restaurant run by Middle Easterners.  You will not get fast or very attentive service because that is not how they roll.  You will hear a fair amount of Arabic being spoken because it is their native language.  You will see things on the menu that you have seen elsewhere but they may not look the same when served because this place does not overly Americanize their food.  It was slightly painful to watch the only other American couple in the place struggling with these aspects of the restaurant.

What a fabulous experience!  Amazing food, great atmosphere, nearly flawless service all combined to make a perfect dining experience after walking through the garden glow at the Missouri Botanical Garden on a balmy night before Thanksgiving.

We arrived a but earlier than our reservation but it was no big deal as the place was only about 1/4 full.  The wife is picky about tables and seating so our experience was off to a great start when the host told us we could pick where we would like to sit.

Our first bite of the night was bread & butter.  Average bread but great butter.  Served just a little cooler than room temperature and so creamy with a slight saltiness.  Delicious!

Next up was the appetizer I ordered for the table and the soup that the wife commandeered.  I did manage exactly 2 bites of the squash soup and it was fantastic!  It was their seasonal offering and it will apparently be gone in another couple of weeks.  The appetizer was on the menu as cevapi - small beef sausages served with a savory sauce and lepinja, an amazing grilled bread.  They had tomatoes, onions and feta cheese as a garnish.  Cut a piece of sausage, add a small amount of the sauce, a chunk of feta and a piece of bread and you've got an amazing bite - savory, buttery, smoky and meaty...all in one bite.     

I ordered their mixed Grbic plate to be able to taste more of their menu on one plate.  It included a grilled veal steak, a chopped steak topped with butter, more of the cevapi, a skewer of grilled chicken breast with peppers & onions and a dark meat chicken dish that was topped with peppers and onions.  Everything was delicious but my favorite bite was the chopped steak with butter - so yummy!  I really enjoy a mixed grill and this one was no exception.

Kid 1 ordered the jager schnitzel and I tried a couple of bites.  As much as I enjoyed my food, I will order a schnitzel next time.  I loved the crunch from the pan-fry and the meat was perfectly seasoned and tender, probably because the family also owns the butcher shop that supplies the restaurant.  Most of their schnitzel offerings also come with spaetzle.  I've been to a good number of European restaurants on this side of the ocean looking for spaetzle like I have when I'm in Germany.  I can't say that theirs is the same but it's certainly one of the better ones I've had on this continent.

Dessert...wow!  We ordered a baklava and an order of palacinke.  The baklava was certainly one if the best available in St Louis although a little different than available in Greek restaurants in that it did not include any appreciable amount of rose water.  Flaky, sweet and nutty all at once.  Great dessert!  As much as we all enjoyed the baklava, the palacinke was even better!  There is just a certain something about how the Europeans make a dessert crepe and that certain something was present in this dessert crepe offering.  I love the combination of Nutella and crepes but these guys added some chopped walnuts and that somehow took it to another level.

What a surprising find in a veritable wasteland!

The wife and I stopped on the way to Parent's Weekend in Ohio.  I wanted something quick (but DEFINITELY not fast food) that we could enjoy.  I remembered that fellow Yelper Brian M had good things to say about the place and decided to give them a shot.   

The woman who was working the counter answered all of my questions about the restaurant and their food.  She also recommended the two-meat combo since we were looking for something to split.  She told us their two most popular meats are burnt ends and pulled pork so those were our selections.  We also picked their sweet potato casserole and baked beans.  

The food was so amazing that I really need to give some details on each item:

Pulled pork - Very good pulled pork.  Tender, juicy, smoky and with a really flavorful bark.  That said, it was completely overshadowed by the burnt ends.  More on them later.

Sweet potato casserole - this sucker should have been called a dessert instead of a side dish.  Nicely chopped pieces of sweet potato mixed with brown sugar and butter, spooned into a small pie tin and baked until tender.  Sounds great, right?  The dish certainly could have been done at that point and it would have been a success.  Not so fast...they covered it with marshmallows and cooked it a little more so that the topping was that beautiful brown that we all try to achieve when making s'mores.  Each bite was out of this world!

Baked beans - pretty good but there are better available at a couple of places in the STL metro area.  Certainly good but overshadowed by other things we ate.

Honorable mention to their house-made bread and whipped garlic butter.  The bread had a firmness not usually found in white bread that stood up really well to the rest of the meal.  As hard as it is for me to write...the garlic butter actually had too much garlic in it for my taste.  I am a pretty big fan of garlic, garlic butter, garlic bread, etc. so it was a huge surprise when I tried progressively less and less of their whipped butter on each bite as I searched for the right flavor.  Strange, huh?

The star of the show?  Most definitely it was the burnt ends.  I may well have had equally good burnt ends elsewhere but I'm pretty sure I've never had better.  I loved the amount of flavor imparted by the rub.  The meat itself was fork tender and unbelievably moist.  Wrap that in a bark that keeps each bite together and gives each piece all of the attributes one expects when eating barbeque.  Yummy x 10 !!! 

PS: There is a Taco Hell right next door that was slammed but this place was nearly deserted.  Made no sense whatsoever.

I'm impressed!

I'm really impressed!

I'm so impressed that I set this review aside while working on a couple of others just so this could be my 500th review here on Yelp.

This place is a total throw-back to the heyday of the greasy spoon diner.  Small, cheap and delicious.  This is most certainly not a place for fancy stuff, fusion or chef's creations.  This is not a place for anyone on a diet.  This is also not a place for special orders.  This is most certainly a place that was making comfort food looooong before that ridiculous label was ever contrived.  

Order off the menu.  Order something you know.  Prepare to be amazed.  

I went with a pecan waffle.  It was loaded with large pieces of pecans and cooked perfectly.  Slightly crunchy on the outside.  Fluffy and moist on the inside such that it let off a little puff of steam when I first cut into a section.  The waffle melts the butter perfectly and then you douse it with syrup.  No need to ask for a second little cup of syrup - it comes with it and it is warm.  Take a bite and be amazed.  This is exactly how a waffle should taste.

Kid 2 ordered biscuits & gravy.  I am not a huge fan of this dish but love to have a bite or two.  I managed one bite and was amazed.  I would have liked another bite but wouldn't risk getting stabbed with her fork so I left it alone.  I was really impressed with how many chunks of sausage there were in the gravy.  Also, the biscuit was light and fluffy.

The wife had fried eggs and hashbrowns and loved her food.  Kid 1 had scrambled eggs, hashbrowns and bacon.  She loved her food and I got to love a piece of her bacon.  It was flat-top griddled to perfection.

It is worth pointing out that the service really sucked.  I didn't deduct a star for that because the food was THAT good and everyone loved their meal.

I thought I was buying a cupcake for the wife but she only wanted a bite so I scored the rest myself.  Her little treat was a salted caramel cupcake and it was divine!  I tend to prefer chocolate for almost everything except breakfast (wait a minute...I love a chocolate croissant or churros con chocolat whenever I'm in Spain).  Regardless, she isn't as big of a chocolate fan so we chose something not-chocolate for her.

What a great not-chocolate we chose!  The frosting was very smooth and creamy with a saltiness that you could both taste and feel when you took a bite - it was not grainy, but the salt crystals almost popped in my mouth.  The cake portion was a bit more dense than I expected but certainly moist enough that it was not an issue.  They baked this cupcake exactly right.

They are a small shop and their variety is limited but the cupcake I ate was one of the very best in town.

I just donated $60 to whatever corporation owns this "farm". 

We drove in from NYC, paying $30 in bridge tolls plus whatever the NJ Turnpike charged. 3 hours of total travel time. On top of that, we gave away 3 tickets to the hockey game to come here. So we are NOT happy.

For $15 your wristband gets you into certain attractions. The "AMAZING" corn maze. Jumping pillows. Pedal cars. A peek at some animals. A "spider web" jungle gym. And a playground. You can also go through a less scary version of the two haunted attractions. And they have bonfires with s'mores! Heck yes!

The first thing you're greeted with is a guy screaming in your ear that you can't bring in any outside food or drinks. NONE. Not even water. Well this is just amazing. But I'll cover that a bit later. VERY welcoming. And greedy. 

This place looks nothing like a farm. It's basically a carnival without rides. They have booths set up with corn cannons ($3), pony rides ($?), monster truck rides ($7), hammer test- ($3), face painting and tattoos ($?) and t-shirts. OHHH! Kettle corn! I'll take 1! $7! What? That's pricey!  Okay, whatever- here's my debit card. Sorry! $10 minimum for cards, but you can buy 2. Absolutely not. Greedy! There's a $3 charge to use the ATM if we would like. Please. 

So we head over to the corn maze. It's just a corn maze. No bridges or towers to see over. No puzzles or riddles. No special number to text if you need help. There are five stations where you can dip your fingers in to color them, and find all the colors. So we decided to split up and whoever found all the colors and left the maze first was the winner. I finished it in 11 minutes. My husband about 12. The boys were maybe another 5 minutes. Hokey. And people had trampled through creating shortcuts.  

The line to the hay ride was ridiculous. You know why the hay ride is included in your admission price?? Because it takes you out to the overpriced (69 cents a pound!!!) pumpkins. It's not a hay ride through anything interesting. It's just a flat field you can see from the parking lot. And they are crowding  way too many people on to it. In the field, waiting to go back, are more hoards of people. No way.

So we next venture over to the jumping pillows. The boys are excited. First issue? You take your shoes off and then walk through dirt to get to the pillows. Not hardpacked dirt for a couple of feet. But tons of soft DIRT through the path to get there. So once shoes were off the youngest (the oldest refused to get his socks dirty and have to wear them all day), we discover that BOTH pillows have a height restriction! Are you serious? Pretty sure this was supposed to be "all ages". So now I have two grumpy kids who can't jump and one with dirty socks.

The two haunted house attractions that are included? I knew there would be no actors inside. I didn't realize there would be no effects. So basically your wristband allows you to walk through a closed attraction with black walls. Thankfully there was a kid standing at the entrance of the alien attraction handing out 3D glasses so at least the painting on the walls of the empty house were a little neat. Also- one member of my family has epilepsy and can't be around strobe lights. So I asked the kid at the front if there were any and he said he didn't know. Really? How do you not know this? He didn't even bother to find out. So three of us walked through. Upon discovering that there wasn't any strobe lights, it wasn't even worth it for the other person to go in.

We never found the pedal cars and couldn't find anyone that worked there (that wasn't at the end of a long line) to ask. 

My kids wanted water. So we get at the end of another very long line. I can't tell if they take credit cards, but surely the $5 I have in my pocket is enough for two bottles of water?? Hahaha! Nope. $3 a piece. So the husband goes to the ATM and spends $3 pulling out $20 so we can get an extra $1 to buy the kids water. The lady in front of me was upset because they were out of pizza after she waited so long in line. No signs. And $6 for a funnel cake?? I ask the girl in the s'mores section when that starts. Not for awhile. AND I discover that each kit costs $10! Wait. What? I've been to TWO pumpkin farms in the past and s'mores were always included. 

You know what else I've experienced at other pumpkin farms? A farm feel. Picnic tables where if you want, you can bring along a picnic basket. Homemade baked treats. Cider mills. Pleasant employees. This was nothing but a carnival rip-off. I am shocked they don't try to charge for parking!

Live entertainment was a young girl singing the same karaoke song over and over.

Smoking everywhere. Ew.

Now what about people with food allergies? I absolutely cannot eat anything they have there. But I am not allowed to bring in my own food. Nor are there picnic tables outside the gate. My entire family went without lunch because it wasn't fair to me. This place is run by greedy people.

Princess Iztaccihuatl, that's who. In the Nahuatl language the name means, "White Woman," in reference to the white-capped volcanic mountain. Didja know, didja know? We've ordered delivery from this place so frequently over the last few months that I took the time to learn how to actually pronounce, "Iztaccihuatl," instead of continuing what I had been doing, which was to say, "Izz..." and just trail off. This had been my lazy habit when suggesting the spot for some late night delivery nachos.

Certainly it was high time to brush up on my knowledge of the geography, topography and folklore of Mexico anyway, but I also enjoy acting as the insufferable know-it-all, after all as well: "Hey, didja know Iztaccihuatl is a dormant volcanic mountain?! It means White Woman." I mean. I started off the damn review with that fact, just pleased as punch that I learned something from these here internets. Snacks and facts, baby. That's the ole gal in a taco shell. Uh yeah, so the realization that this place is likely gonna stay heavy in the delivery rotation that got me curious- how bout I know what the heck I'm talkin about? 

I'm talkin about fast, easy, and reliable delivery through grubhub. I'm talkin bout the fact that they're generous wit the little containers of tasty red and green salsa, if you ask for extra- and I always do.

The nachos vegetarianos are my favorite order. Now, if you are in the habit of selecting vegetarian items from offa Mexican menus about town, you probably have had odd instances of being served up either a straight up refried beans and cheese type o' combo, or some senseless melange of frozen, or worse- canned vegetables, folded into whatever concoction. Maybe you've been left puzzled, "What the hell is with this carrot? What's this random string bean about?" I know. I've been there.

This is not the case if you order the vegetarian nachos from Iztaccihuatl. A mound of chips will meet you, covered in beans and cheese, yes, but also piled with sauteed peppers and onions, corn, zucchini, yellow squash, mushrooms, and crema. Lovely.

Be advised, if you also order anything entitled, "vegetariano," this is likely the mix that will be up in your enchiladas or what have you. Not a complaint, but you may wanna mix up the flavor profiles by gettin ya a mushroom quesadilla, or maybe those tacos de jalapenos rellenos de queso, if you're in the market for some more meatless items. The latter are tacos of cotija cheese-stuffed jalapenos. And I like em. Muy mucho.

Iztaccihuatl: Good prices, good portions, good for delivery. Keep up the good work, white woman!

Korean Fried Chicken.

I almost feel like that's my entire review. The stuff is amazingly addictive. At Umami, Korean Fried Chicken means huge, crispy, saucy, flavorful chicken wings that taste sweet and savory all at once. I think I could eat them for breakfast, lunch, and dinner and still want more.

We arrived one Sunday evening after having bookmarked the place for months. There was a huge party in the corner, but otherwise the place was pretty quiet (although it was a Sunday). The staff took a bit to get around to us at first (there was only one waitress - I presume the large party did not call ahead), but service was surprisingly quick after the initial delay. I ordered a beef miso ramen, and my girlfriend ordered the chicken bento. We decided to get Korean Fried Chicken just to try it. I figured a small order would be the size of an appetizer, not a meal (spoiler alert: I was wrong). All of our portions were HUGE. The ramen came out in a stainless steel mixing bowl it was so large. It was good, and there was a lot of variety of ingredients, but I always seem to forget how much I don't really like ramen. My girlfriend's bento was also surprisingly big. She had generous servings of savory-sweet teriyaki chicken, crispy tempura (vegetables and shrimp), and what looked like an entire California roll, all served with a delicious dipping sauce.

It was an expensive meal on paper, but the portions are so large that the one meal bought lunch for most of the week. If you aren't big leftover eaters, plan to split some of the portions, but try the fried chicken!

I only gave them one star because you have to put something but they don't even deserve that so I've been hot  rods around 20 to 30 times The menu is tired and the food quite frankly is disgusting the only thing that hot rods  had  going for it was karaoke on Friday or Saturday night and a very talented bartender/magician in the upstairs bar while I just heard that they fired Mark I can safely say that I have visited hot rods for the last time and I don't see them being open by the end of the summer if they don't get rid of the current management and turn the place around

Just when I thought life couldn't get any better, Mazzaro's Italian Market entered into my world. 

For the record, I'd give 10 stars if Yelp would let me. Mazzaro's is the mecca for all-things-Italian. I've never felt more like a kid in a candy store than I did while exploring the ins and out of this place. 

Here are a few of the specs: Butcher, deli, dessert bakery, gelato, cheese/wine shop, grocery store, coffee shop, fresh breads, prepared pastas and assorted dishes. Did I ascend into heaven without even knowing?

Guys, I was in Italy three and half months ago and being totally honest with myself, the food you'll discover here is on par. If not better... Let me introduce to my top three favorite sandwiches of all time (from the deli):

#7 - Prosciutto D' Parma, Sweet Soppressata, Hot Capicola, Marinated Sundried Tomato & Fresh Mozzarella on Ciabatta Bread. The $8.50 price tag should be marked up to 4x that number. 

I believe this beauty was fearful for its life when it saw the look in my eyes. I attacked this sandwich like a lion pouncing on its prey. It was sheer decadence, over indulgence, oily, meaty, cheesy, savoriness. I feel naughty just talking about it. 

Based off a conversation with one of the deli employees, Mazzaro's has been offered to branch out with other locations in various parts of the country, which they have refused time and time again. This place is still locally owned and operated for 15+ years, give or take. 

I could write a dissertation about this place. We visited three times in two days! It's a front running contender for my favorite establishment I've ever been to. Period. Mangia!

It seems like every time I'm in Nashville I discover yet another Barista Parlor. This one, located in Germantown, is yet another gargantuan space with their infamous rectangular-shaped counter. 

One thing I get really excited about before entering Barista Parlor is seeing who they have playing on vinyl. Yep, they have a dope set up with lots of records on the shelves. This time, I got even luckier than I anticipated. Dinosaur Jr. and one of my personal favorites, Master of Reality by Black Sabbath. #PraiseIommi

You're doing yourself a disservice if you don't order a biscuit sandwich. I'm not normally one to seek out biscuits. But hot damn, BP makes one of the finer ones I've had the pleasure of scarfing down. 

For my money, it's always a coffee shop I must visit when in Nashville. No wonder more locations are popping up by the minute!

Wow, serious flavor alert here at Maya's South Indian Cuisine in Reno! When visiting cities for the first time I always seek out a space/market housing multiple local businesses under one roof. West Street Market has got it going on!

This place is locally owned and operated. They are extremely accommodating to vegetarians and vegans, while serving organic and gluten free items as well. Have no fear carnivores, the flavors executed from this tiny kitchen will set your taste buds to new heights.

I went with the three combo platter. If I remember correctly, my meal consisted of Dosa Corner, Poori and Potato Masala, and Kuzhi Paniyaram. They are served with a trio of sauce, chutney and soup. Not only do you get your money's worth for $12.99, but OH MY GOD, you will be in heaven. The texture and consistency of each item was unique and made for some of the best Indian food I've had in a hot minute!

Service here was above and beyond. Our waitress, Sam I believe, was extremely accommodating to us first timers. She thoroughly explained the menu to us and checked on us constantly without being over bearing. Thanks for the rec, Michael T. and pleasure dining with you Patrick T. all the way from Des Moines!

Honored to be penning the first review for The Galley. On NYE (and apparently their first or second day in business) the bartenders were undeniably killing it! I'm used to experiencing hiccups during pre-openings, soft openings, etc. but this place was the most refreshing change of pace.

The Galley, a nautically-themed tavern, specializes in craft cocktails and gastropub style fare. Although I can't comment on the cuisine, the drinks were properly made and marked at a fair price. Plus, the bar was well-staffed. Servers/bartenders were walking around checking up on every table to assure a great experience.

It's not a large space, but they have plenty of televisions to watch a game. Peculiarly awesome are the stools at each table, which are extremely generous on the behind if I do say so myself. Seriously, check this bar out!

Who am I to say these are the best ribs in America? Right, I am a nobody.

Food Network, on the other hand, I'd like to think they know a thing or two about food. Years ago, they deemed Pappy's Smokehouse home of the country's best ribs. Talk about the ultimate endorsement!

While little old me was in St. Louis, this was the pit stop I was looking forward to the most. Pappy's has the most Yelp reviews of any biz in STL. I expected a long line and righteous 'que. And that's exactly what I received.

Knowing I was in for a BBQ-related food coma, I walked here from my Airbnb Downtown. About two miles, hey you need to earn your food sometimes! Surprisingly, the line wasn't as lengthy as I anticipated. I showed up right when the doors opened, and my order was right in front of me in less than 30 minutes. Thank you, BBQ gods!

Again, it's almost a disservice to have "best ribs in America" implanted in the back of your head while eating. Nothing can possibly live up to a hype of such crazy heights. However, this is what I know. These ribs were really f**king delicious! No sauce necessary! I catered my inner animal and tore apart every nook and cranny of them bones. Phenomenal ribs!

Sides were legit, too. The baked beans and green beans were mighty tasty. The former filled with unctuous flavor, the latter crisp and light. The one weird thing was the side of burnt ends I ordered. I felt like they weren't, well, burnt enough. Don't get me wrong, they tasted great, it just didn't taste like a burnt end to me.

Pappy's is an iconic smokehouse in the BBQ sphere. I'm so glad I had the opportunity to finally try out this institution. Amazing 'que worth the wait!

The scenario: Post Mumford & Sons show. Went on Yelp to find a 24-hour diner in close vicinity from the venue. City Diner wasn't too far away. 

We walked in to a full house. There was Prom at a local high school. And many others were there for some post-show refuel. Two customers were ahead of us waiting by the counter. They, in fact, informed us to write our name on the list. They also warned us that, "there's no pen to write your name on the list."

Bad start.

Now, let me prelude by expressing my love for diners. If Tallahassee had a locally owned 24-hour diner, I would be there more than you can imagine. Sometimes, you don't want to go to a sports bar late at night. Every now and again, I actually enjoy a late night coffee and breakfast fare. End tangent.

Continuing on, there were three employees working front-of-house. One woman was heading the hostess stand, one guy was rolling silverware and the other girl was serving tables. 

After 10-15 minutes we were seated at a booth, which had be vacant during our entire wait. Approximately 10 minutes later the hostess (who happened to be working at her own pace) asked for our drink order. She was outright rude and looked at us with dead eyes, as if we had no business being there. 

Two things were wrong with my order. No lettuce and tomato on the sandwich, and I received the Jalepeno and Cheddar loaf as opposed to Sourdough bread. The bread was literally stuck to the plate. The consistency was extremely off-putting.

The worst part was watching this poor girl attempt to pay her bill at the register. For over 10 minutes, she couldn't receive any attention. It was almost laughable, but realistically, it was excruciatingly frustrating. If that were me, I'm not sure if I'd have the mental capacity to keep my cool.

They ended up overcharging us for an extra drink. And that took even longer to edit the bill. We just wanted to get the hell out of there. Our experience was a downright disaster. Due to the poor service, tens of potential customers walked out. It's just bad business. 

Save yourselves.

**On the bright side** if you're seeking the largest pancake of your life you will find it here. The to-go boxes for pancakes are the size of a pizza box.

One of my good friends is currently in Nashville and I saw he checked in here the other night. I proceeded to click through to read my review, because it was my favorite brewery when I visited Nashville back in October. Then I came to the quick realization that I never screamed my praises from the mountaintops. 

THAT'S ABOUT TO CHANGE ON THIS FIVE-STAR FRIDAY.

Bearded Iris makes damn good beer. You know when the flagship beer (Homestyle IPA) keeps you going back for more that the remainder of the beers on hand are going to be fantastic. And that's the thing, it's not a tap list with fifty beers. It's tiny, probably seven on tap when I was there, and a cooler with 16 oz. cans for the road. Quality, not quantity.

It's an IPA heavy menu, containing hazy IPAs, Double IPAs, and fruited IPAs. Back in October, they had an incredible milk stout on tap, and I could not get enough of it. 

The microbrewery itself is one of the more unique ones you'll come across. Most of the time, you think of breweries as a bit of a macho boys club. Here, I was impressed with the decor, almost avant garde and vintage. They even had one of my favorite Radiohead albums (In Rainbows) playing on vinyl behind the bar. 

Although it's off-the-beaten-path, the experience was stellar. My girlfriend did not mind hanging out here while I geeked out indefinitely. And with that, my praises for Bearded Iris have been sung.

"I shot a man in Reno / just to watch him die."

When in Nashville, the Johnny Cash Museum is a stiff requirement. Fans of country music, rock music, or modern American history are guaranteed a trip to down memory lane. Learn something.

As someone who's not a mere bandwagoner of Johnny Cash, there's a lot more to him than "I Walk The Line," I was often emotional while intricately reliving his life story. Handwritten set lists, stage outfits, military paraphernalia, rare recordings, etc. There is a TON packed into a very small space.

One of the things I found cool was the recording studio-style exhibit where you can put on headphones and mix Johnny's signs. "(Ghost) Riders in the Sky" with amped up vocals, bass and horns? Oh, hell yeah.

The downfall of this place is the opening exhibit. The content they've displayed requires a ton of reading. It takes a lot of time to go through it all piece by piece. The problem is the insane influx of people they let in at once. It's slow, and people are well, annoying. It's hard to see and move around.

Once you break on thru to the other side, there's ample room to roam around and explore. Mini theaters with old television performances, a hall of records and memorabilia from his entire life.

Johnny Cash is one of the most fascinating humans of the 20th century. The museum does him justice, a true slice of Americana. Pay tribute to the Man in Black.

Hands down, the best foodie experience in St. Pete. Holy freakin' cow - our group of nine spared no expense on this meal. In turn, I think we're all in agreement that this set the bar incredibly high for all future team dinners. 

Nowadays, people throw around the term "best burger" like it's running out of style. And my boss definitely didn't shy away from repeating it. However, the B&M Burger is luscious, decadent and in my opinion, the way Jesus eats his burgers. One of the best burgers I've ever had!

Every dish we ordered for the table was excellent. The menu contains no fluff, all filler. Tuna Tartare with shrimp cake wontons were to die for. Carpaccio was top of the line. The Octopus was charred, seared and cooked to absolute perfection. The Meatballs with polenta were tender and creamy. Even their spin on poutine was phenomenal. 

The private dining room we sat in was rather odd, as it sits separate from the actual restaurant. But the privacy of wining and dining in reclining office chairs fit for an extremely comfortable meal. Job well done, B&M. Hopefully, we'll meet again soon!

Red Mesa in DTSP offers tons of available seating space, a luchador vibe and an appealing menu. For me, the flavors didn't live up to the expectations I had, especially after glancing over photos and reviews prior.

Our table of seven ordered two Ceviche Samplers for the table. These were really solid all around! Fresh flavor profiles and the spicy ones really packed a punch. However, the fish components were hard to single out from one to the other. The octopus was my personal favorite.

The Crab and Shrimp Quesadilla fell completely flat on the wow factor. The spicy, open-faced quesadilla had my mouth-watering in theory, but the only component I tasted was the jack cheese. To be honest, I felt really sad that it didn't live up to the hype.

This seems like an opportune restaurant to meet up with a large group of friends and order a few margaritas. The focus, especially the outdoor area, is all about the atmosphere. As for the food, I wish I liked it more.

Hot licks and honky tonk in Nashville's premier rocks off joint, Robert's Western World. Hell, tourists will flock here, don't let that discourage you. Locals are engrained into their bar stools here. Seriously, they don't budge even for a dollar!

One of the coolest live music venues I experienced in 2018, hands down. The music was firing on all cylinders. Upright bass, a child prodigy riffing on the electric guitar, and the crowd energetic as can be. 

Things of note that may sell or not sell you on Robert's:

1. Doesn't matter what time or which night you visit, the room will be packed like sardines. Expecting a seat? Yeah, fat chance.

2. Bands in Nashville are notorious for making their living on tips. Confrontational encounters with band members storming through the crowd looking for a quick buck are imminent. 

3. Going to the bathroom will take every bone in your body to power through the audience. Maybe just hold it?

You know I'm a cocktail and craft beer enthusiast. When you come to Robert's, order a High Life or PBR, and maybe a shot of Wild Turkey. You're here for the music and the music only, not pizzazz.

I'm itching to return!!

PB&J flavored Nitro Cold Brew? Freakin' sold. 

Coffee shops around Florida take note. Ginger Beard Coffee has not one, not two, not three, BUT FOUR varieties of Nitro Cold Brew on tap! It's a win for local coffee shops to have one on tap, let alone four with niche flavors and tasting notes. 

I don't make proclamations like this often, however this was the best nitro cold brew I've had in recent memory. Hell, maybe all year!

From the moment we walked in, the lovely ginger-bearded man behind the counter treated us like royalty, in his own charismatic way. There were some hidden gems behind the counter that I can't necessarily comment on in a review. You'll have to find out for yourself. 

Next up, they have a wall of beers on tap. If it weren't for our post lunch coffee fuel up, I would have loved to really explored the beer they served in house. All in all, a wide open shop with tons of space for the coffee or beer aficionado. Must stop in Tampa!

2 weekends ago, my husband said he wanted Breakfast, not Brunch, Breakfast. He didn't want to wait for an hour, he didn't want a menu to be so big and pretentious that you can't even process the items before blurting out "just bacon and eggs!", and he didn't want to spend a fortune. He just wanted breakfast. I remembered seeing Jim H's review on Grubhouse and told him I didn't know anything about it, but if Jim liked it, it had to hold some clout. We got in the car and took the 5 minute drive from our house to Grubhouse and were relieved when we walked in and were greeted with a friendly "hello" and a "you can sit anywhere". Not only do they have a vast menu with breakfast and lunch options, but there is a special board, and all the specialty soda's and coffee flavors are listed on the walls as well. I will get to what we ate in a second, but before I do, we were so happy with the first experience, that we came back the following weekend and had an equally good experience. Dining here is easy. You come in, you order, you eat, you go home. 

What we ate: The 1st trip I had the grande burrito, which came in a perfect burrito that you could actually pick up and eat. I am cutting back on breads so I just cut it open and ate the eggs, sausage and veggies that were inside. My husband had the biscuits and gravy which he had no complaints about. On the second trip, I had the omelette with onions and peppers, a side of bacon and tater tots (free thanks to Yelp!). My husband had the cuban. He was not crazy about the banana mayo, and thought more pickles would have helped, but that's just him. I did not try it so I cannot give an alternate review. My omelette was damn perfect. The hash browns are probably the best I have had in the city. What do you have to do to get crispy hashbrowns in this city?! Go to Grubhouse! All the potatoes here are excellent, whether they are fries, tots or hashbrowns, you are in for a delicous side dish.

So you know how I said I cut back on bread? Well I may need to break that rule only for Grub House. I am dying to try the pancakes and french toast. My husband really wants to try the burger, so we will obviously be back. Probably next weekend.

Hilton Riverside Hotel is usually our first choice when visiting New Orleans. Why? 

-Staff is very welcoming, valet is simple.
-Huge automatic revolving entrance door to main lobby
-Rooms are always very clean and bathrooms are nice. 
-Views from the higher floors are spectacular. I recommend the river view rooms. 
-Dragos restaurant located on first floor
-Hotel attached to Riverwalk Outlet stores
-Close proximity to Aquarium, Entergy Big Screen, Carnival Cruise terminal, Harrahs casino, Canal Street, Convention Center, River Boats and tons of restaurants.
-Quick access to the trolley cars that have several stops to/from the French Market
-Very nice fitness center equipped with racquetball courts

This hotel is huge, walking through the common areas is instant exercise. It's loaded with bars, cafes, meeting rooms. There is a lot of space to sit and just people watch if you want to. 

On 8/9/18 we had stay/self park reservations. When booking, I asked about parking specifically about what is the vehicle height restrictions for self parking and no one knew the answer but they said they had overflow parking that could accommodate any sized vehicle. What they failed to say was that it was a good 1/4 walk to/from the hotel from this spot. Just wanted y'all to be aware. The height restriction is 6'6" for self parking.

Upon checkin we surprisingly were told we were "customers of the day" so our Premium King sized bed with river view was upgraded to a suite for NO charge. This was awesome, it made our wedding anniversary that much more memorable. The suite rooms 2705/2706 had both city and river views.

I fully recommend a stay at Hilton, just be aware of the self parking restrictions other than that there were no issues. Maybe use valet instead?

I was in for my very first time yesterday to pick up a cake and some pastry's.  I live out-of-town.  I am in Tucson because my mom is gravely ill and she loves desserts and I wanted to bring her something sweet. I read the Yelp reviews and decided to go out of my way to Nadine's Bakery.
Let me share that I was never been made to feel so embarrassed at a bakery no less in my whole life!
I can say with 100% honesty that I did not see the sign in the upper right hand side of the glass doors. I was innocently unaware that I was to ask for assistance so someone from behind the counter can open the cooler doors and get the cake of my choosing and bring it back to the counter for it to be boxed. As I am standing in line with the undamaged cake in my hands, a young lady behind the counter was the first to bring my innocent mistake to my attention and that is when I actually noticed the clearly defined signs.
Maybe my focus was on the yummy looking cakes but as I said I didn't see the sign. I apologized to her and laughed off my silly mistake. Then a dark haired, middle aged lady, perhaps Nadine herself, I really don't know but anyway she comes from behind the counter with a scowl on her face and takes the cake from me and scolds me in the presence of other customers about taking the cake out of the cooler. Now I was insulted and embarrassed!
Horrible! Positively HORRIBLE customer service!
I can understand sharing your cake retrieving policy once but TWICE??!!  Flipping Unbelievable!!! Maybe put a pad lock on your coolers or maybe a flashing neon sign to alert your customers or maybe an alarm should go off of an unauthorized person opens the cooler doors. As I previously mentioned maybe I was distracted by the cakes or maybe I was distressed and distracted by my mom's dire medical situation or both.  No one ever deserves to be publicly chastised and embarrassed!!!!
Let's talk about the cake. I purchased a vanilla cake, filled with raspberry and topped with buttercream icing. The cake was moist. The raspberry jam compote flavorful. The buttercream icing was middle of the road.
The pastry's were very good. The only thing that needs to be substantially improved upon is the customer service. I gave 2 stars because customer service is HUGE with me. Always remember this truth. The employer doesn't pay your salary, the customer's do.  If I was confronted by Nadine herself, then shame on you! If it wasn't Nadine, then additional customer service training is warranted. Either way, whomever did go out of their way to publicly embarrass me then all I have to say is, You are better than that!

It's cliche, but true. "First time, long time." I'm a long time Yelp user, but this is my first review, and with good reason.

I've been to PYT 3 times now, and all 3 times I have received sub-par service and average food. But it wasn't until tonight when the owner, Tommy Up banned me from his restaurant via Twitter for voicing an opinion, was I finally pushed over the edge to write this review.

The adult milkshakes are hit or miss. When they're made correctly, they're definitely delicious, but since they don't always come out correctly, you're taking a gamble every time you order one. My boyfriend and I ordered two adult milkshakes and received one with zero alcohol and one with way more alcohol than it should have had - and were told by the staff that we were wrong when we pointed out the mistake.

The burgers are good, and Tommy Up does get very creative with his burger of the week. Having a weekly burger is impressive, and I do hope to see him keep up with that pace and the level of creativity that has been going into them. I haven't tasted them all, but the few that I have tasted so far have been worth the trip out to NoLibs. 

Unfortunately, no burger is worth a 25 minute wait, especially when I can get an equally good burger pretty much anywhere else in the city in half the time. Every time I've gone to PYT I've waited over 20 minutes for my food. Whether I ordered a burger of the week or a regular menu item, this excessive wait time held true.

I'm typically a very positive person and I don't really like knock things, and until tonight, I was very happy to continue going to PYT, despite its few flaws. However, after voicing an opinion of mine on Twitter and being told by Tommy Up that I was banned from his restaurant, I felt that something needed to be said. I was already unsatisfied, but now I'm very much so.

Even if you disagree with your customers opinions, it is not in your best interest to treat your customers the way I was treated tonight. Especially not in times where the opinions of your customers can be shared with the entire internet in a matter of minutes. 

Will my unfortunate situation with this establishment stop people from going there? Probably not, but that's not the point. The point is just to get the word out there. That is what Yelp is for, right?

This visit was in Sept, I've been meaning to write this for awhile.

Easily the most horrible experience I've ever had in a restaurant. I arrived alone at 830pm on a Thursday, sat at the bar ordered glass of wine and a crabcake. Bartender immediately started closing out the other checks at bar telling everywhere "We are closing early tonight". I had not even taken a sip of wine so pushed it back in and told the bartender if they were closing early to cancel my order, no big deal Ill come back another time. She resisted and said I was fine, they just close early about once a week. Strange for 830 on a Thur but whatever. A sat with my wine awaiting the crabcake I started wondering why they closed early so I asked. Are you ready for this one? She replied that the restaurant had poor plumbing and when they renovated it from Pie in the Sky they neglected to fix or upgrade the floor drain issues so now the bar floods about once a week. I leaned over the bar and saw 2-3 inches of standing water the entire length of the bar, with the bartenders feet sloshing about.

Crabcake arrives, was so so. Check for 1 glass of wine and crabcake was $33. Based on a previous bad experience (This was my 5th or 6th time in since Honeysuckle had opened and new restaurants sometimes need a bit to iron out the kinks as to be expected) a manager had given me his business card on which he hand wrote Free Drink & App with his signature.  20% tip on $33 is $7 and since what I ordered was comped with the certificate, I put down a $15 tip to be a good guy even though the food and service did not warrant a 40% tip. 

I stand up to zip my coat and head out when the bartender says very crudely, "Where do you think you're going?". Turned around to see who she was being so rude too and realized it was me! She then continues, "Where is the rest of the money?" like someone selling counterfeit jeans on the street. I point out the card she is holding from the manager and signed by him is good for a drink and app. She says, "I've never seen this before" and literally frisbee tosses the card towards me. At that point I said get the manager, incredulous that anyone would be so rude and unprofessional, let alone at the most expensive restaurant in Williamson County. I said to the other woman bartending, "Is this really happening?" to which she replied, "please say something to the manager about her attitude you are not the first one to complain".

Manager Steven Hudson comes out. I'm ready for "Good evening sir I understand there has been a miss communication, how can I help" or maybe "Hey man whats going on how is everything?" No, he comes out with his arms folded in a hostile manner and said "Whats up?". I reply, "Whats up? Really? Are you serious? Well I guess whats up is that your employee is accusing me of counterfeiting a gift certificate and forging a managers signature on his own business card, that is whats up. Bro."  Manager Steven looks at the managers signed card with note and says, "Where did you get this?". Where did I get? Are you kidding me? From the guy whose name is on the card. Manager Steven says, "What did he look like?" As if I'm in an interrogation. I said he was the bald guy who used to be manager at PF Changs. At this point he lets back, as if just now realizing it is legit and I am not trying to con them. Mind blown. Most expensive restaurant in the area and the customer service is well below what you would expect at a dive bar. He fumbles through the excuse of "Well I can see how she didnt recognize this, we use honeybucks for gift certificates. And her attitude, well, we hired her from a bar on 2nd Ave in Nashville so what can you expect?". My closing statement to the manager, "I want to see every restaurant in the area do well. Especially the good ones, because selfishly I want more nice places to go nearby. I don't want anything from you and I will never be back.  After this experience I cannot tell enough people to avoid this place and I look forward to the restaurant that opens here after you close.

I want to discuss the performance of Gambino's Bakery during our wedding. We first met with Capdebosq Catering on Nov 3rd 2017 for a tasting at their office in Marrero. While there, we were informed that we are to meet with either Gambino's Bakery, Swiss Confectionary or Haydel's. We met with Adrienne Rousse at Gambino's Bakery on March 24th 2018. We were there for a little over an hour, selecting and designing our wedding and groom cakes. We went over several specific details in designing our wedding and groom's cakes. Upon leaving that day we asked Adrienne if there was anything else we need to do. She implied that it was all taken care of. We left assuming, as any reasonable person would, that the cake order was complete. On August 13, 2018, Capdebosq sent us an E-Mail to make final wedding preparations. In this E-mail they asked us with which bakery we had placed our order. On August 21st, 2018, we responded via E-mail that our order was placed at Gambino's Bakery. It was at this point I wrote Capedebosq a $7,734.45 check.
On our wedding night, I receive a phone call from the Federal Ballroom to inform me that there had been a problem with the cake order. ABSOLUTLY NOTHING HAD BEEN PREPARED! In speaking with Gambino's just two hours before our vows, we were informed that our order status was listed as "pending", it had never been finalized.  The best they could do at that point was provide a fake cake and premade sheet cake that would not match our colors or theme. At no point prior to the wedding did Gambino's inform us or Capdebosq that there was a problem with our order. As Gambino's said in their own words "We had a pending wedding order for a 6-8-10 wedding cake and a crawfish pot cake...After more then sixty days, we did not hear back from you or your fiance.  We figured you had opted to go with Swiss or Haydels" A competent bakery in a similar situation would have reached out to the couple and/or the caterer to see if they still wanted the wedding cake they meticulously selected.
Furthermore, Capdebosq never contacted Gambino's prior to the night of the wedding to arrange for delivery of our cakes. By the time our caterer realized there was a problem with the wedding and groom's cakes, it was too late. Days later, as we tried to piece together what had happened, Gambino's claimed that there had been a small charge we didn't pay, approximately $200. Yet, they never felt it was necessary to inform anyone of this issue prior to the wedding. Obviously, after having spent nearly $30,000 on a wedding, we would have paid the two hundred bucks to avoid such a calamity had we only known.  

One would imagine that if a bakery and a caterer had failed to provide the correct wedding and groom's cake, they would be HORRIFIED by such an error. Perhaps they would reevaluate their process, retrain employees (or fire incompetent ones) to ensure that such a mistake never happens again. However, Gambino's and Capdebosq never seemed to appreciate the severity of their mistake. They were quick to pass blame and downplay the error. It was quite obvious that despite having spent top dollar and planning for over a year, our wedding was really never a priority for either of them. Eventually, after multiple heated phone calls, Capdebosq did offer a very small refund for their part in the error. Gambino's provided no compensation and neither Gambino's Bakery or Capdebosq Catering ever provided any form of apology.

Iron Hill is right in the heart of downtown, with both a cute little outdoor dining area available and indoor seating that's distanced far apart (during COVID times). 

My boyfriend and I arrived around 4:30pm on a Sunday and we waited only a short time before being seated outside, per our request. 

Our waitress Tiara was polite and efficient. 

I had the Figgy Piggy Grilled Cheese, which by all accounts is similar to ordering pancakes for breakfast -- you have to be in the mood for something sweet! The bread was super crisp and I think next time if I ordered the same I'd ask for extra bacon. 

My boyfriend had the Buffalo wings and they were soooo good. Just the right amount of spicy and that's coming from someone with a mild tolerance for spice. 

We also were a big fan of the fries which we had two extra sides of. 

For my drink, I had the Little Red Wagon and holy wow that might be my new favorite ale. It tasted exactly like strawberry rhubarb. Obsessed. 

Would be happy to return again!

The woman I spoke to on the phone at Bocconcini was exceedingly helpful and polite when I called to ask if my boyfriend's severe peanut allergy would be an issue. She assured me there are no nuts used at all in the restaurant and we would be good to go. Loved that confident reassurance!

We ordered through DoorDash, everything arrived on time, and it was so well-packaged. None of the sauce leaked at all, as they took the extra precaution of wrapping the takeout boxes in tinfoil. Our meals each came with a box of bread knots. 

However, we were a bit let down by the food itself. The sauce for my Penne Vodka (large portion) was very creamy and tasty enough but it stated on the website that it came with seasonal vegetables but the closest in there were long strips of basil. I also ordered the Meatballs and I really thought the main flavor was plain old beef, with little seasoning. I had one bite and couldn't eat the rest. As for my boyfriend's Chicken Parmesan, I wasn't crazy impressed with the marinara and it really is a thick chicken cutlet so it completely overpowers the breading and the mozzarella. 

One other note I'll make is that you should ask for a side of Parmesan with your pasta, as I neglected to do that and would've wanted some. 

Overall, I think this is a good place for protein lovers but not so much for those that are craving really well-seasoned Italian based on my experience.

Philly Bagels had some incredibly delish breakfast sandwiches, albeit a bit pricey by my standard. 

You can walk in and order (3 people allowed in at a time right now) or call to pick up, and either way there's a little window on the outside of the building where they yell out your name when your order is ready. 

My boyfriend and I went around 9am on Saturday and there was a small line accrued. It was a short wait. For our two breakfast sandwiches and an iced coffee it was a bit over $16. 

I HIGHLY recommend going for the pork roll. It's thick cut and totally worthwhile. 

Oh, and they told us that my boyfriend's severe peanut and nut allergies wouldn't be an issue and made note of it on our order (as they do have peanut and nut products here).

After 2 visits, I can honestly say, "DON'T BOTHER!" Prices are too high for the product they're offering, food is horrible, and the staff is unfriendly & rude.

We were excited about Gunner's Run opening. We love the location and had high hopes for it becoming a new hang out spot. We were sadly disappointed.

Our first visit was Saturday, March 19 - we stopped in a little after 3PM and were greeted by a frowning, no personality, hostess. The double hostess station combination is cumbersome and awkwardly blocking the door. The hostess asked if we were there for drinks or food - when we reported both, she announced that they were only serving appetizers between 3-5PM. We told her we were OK with that, cause we were excited about their opening (she did not share our enthusiasm).

She sat us in a booth and gave us two lame menus. One had a limited beer list, and the other the drab food menu. There were only 5 appetizers listed, and all lacked appeal. I selected the Vegetarian Tomato Basil soup ($5), and the rest of my party selected beers. Out of the 5 beers on tap listed on the board, they were out of two of them (which were the two we wanted). Pretty sad for the 1st weekend of being open.

We had two waitresses (who resembled roller derby gals), both sporting frowns, stop by our table to ask if anyone had taken our order. Each time  we said no, they walked away, with no offer to help us out. When a waitress finally came to take our order, she acted like she was doing us a favor. 

While waiting for our order, we looked around at the changes - still resembled Swift Half, but they added additional booths and tables, really cramming people in. Except, no one was really there - tables were empty, and bar area was packed (people literally sitting on top of each other and standing compressed). We found it rather odd that the venue is large, and people were compressed into one area.

Our order arrived - someone from the kitchen brought my soup to the table and just placed it on the edge, never asked who it belonged to and never offered any silverware, bread or crackers. We had to flag down the waitress to get silverware and napkins. The soup was slightly warm and looked like a thick, creamy vodka pasta sauce with 4 large chunks in it. The oversized chunks were tomatoes (I'm thinking a plum tomato quartered).  After a few bites I pushed it away, it was lacking in taste and left me thinking it should be served over pasta as a sauce, not as a bowl of soup. My friends all took a bite and agreed. 

We were so disappointed that we had to ask for the check and left before finishing our beers (which were served warm).

Our 2nd visit was Sunday, March 20th - we brought new friends and wanted their opinion. We stopped by around 5:30PM. Again, greeted by an unhappy hostess, and crammed up against the cumbersome hostess station combo (hostess stand & antique desk). BTW - this place really does not need a hostess at all. The unfriendly hostess was joined by 2 waitresses who asked if we were having drinks or food. We said drinks and they directed us to the bar, despite 3/4 of the tables being empty. There were 4 of us and we asked for a table, one waitress was very bitchy and the hostess backed her up - they stuck to their guns and directed us to the bar. 

Once at the bar, I wanted my friends to view the menu. We requested it several times, and finally received it as we finished our drinks and were paying the check. Service, again, was lame, slow and very unfriendly. There were two bartenders, and after taking our initial drink order, never paid any attention to us again, despite our attempts. Glad we didn't want a 2nd round of drinks, we would have had to beg for service to receive them. The bartenders seemed more concerned with their hipster friends at the end of the bar, then gaining new paying customers.

We won't be going back, and look forward to the next business that will take over the location when this place goes under.

We went to Hotrods after the NASCAR race.  We arrived at 10pm.  We were seated and given menus.  A few minutes later a waiter told us the kitchen was closed.  Why would the closest restaurant to the raceway be closed at 10pm? I guess all the 5 star reviews had made them flush with cash and they don't need to service the NASCAR crowd on a Saturday night.

First visit to Bacio last night to celebrate 70th birthday of three 'kids' who go all the way back to fifth grade.  We will surely go back.  

The owner and staff were attentive, the owner and chef were pleased to prepare anything we asked for, even off-menu (I had calamari and pasta), the food was tasty and properly prepared, and the price was reasonable.  You're paying for the what counts and not ambience.

Perhaps one-eighth star reduction because it was a bit warm inside - although it was 91°F outside.
--

South has earned the coveted five stars from me for its impeccable service, amazingly flavorful food and charming southern atmosphere.  

SERVICE
When we walked in, we were quickly and professionally greeted by our hostesses, one of whom led us to a two-top table.  And that's where Lydia, our server, entered our lives.  She was the sweetest and most attentive server ever!  She was able to answer our questions easily, gave recommendations and had an amazing attitude.  Lydia treated us as if she wanted us to have the most amazing time.  In addition to Lydia, a couple of managers popped by to check on our experience.  And the gentlemen who brought our plates were fun.  I felt that they, too, wanted us to have an amazing time.

FOOD
Ok. Warning: The words will fail me in this section because I don't know how to describe the incredible food! 

For my appetizer, I ordered fried oysters on a bed of creamy spinach. Separately, each item was amazing on its own, but together...POW! BANG! An explosion of flavors in my mouth!  

Then they have two types of grits: 
- one that comes as a side dish with cheesy and bacon-y deliciousness. It stands on its own and needs no accompaniment  
- the other is an entree made with lobster stock.  It comes with a few lobster chunks and about six pieces of medium-sized shrimp.  Full of flavor! I ordered this as my entree.
You can't go wrong with either of these dishes.

My partner in crime ordered the crispy fish entree.  She didn't offer me any, so I guess it was fantastic! LOL!!!

For dessert, I ordered the chocolate cake.  IT WAS CHRISTMAS ON A PLATE!  The dish included two brownie-type cakes, crispy on the outside and almost molten on the inside, and two dollops of pumpkin spice gelato on top of melted chocolate and chocolate crumbles.  O...M...G!!!! All I needed was some milk.  So, I asked Lydia.  And she obliged.  She brought my milk in a black mug, just like one I own.  It was as if I was having dessert in the comfort of my own home.

ATMOSPHERE
The decor is beautiful.  The entrance, which is off Broad St., is like a garden.  Once inside, and after sitting there a while, I began to feel as if I was in someone's beautifully designed, open-concept kitchen...wrapped in the seductive charms of a small southern town, like Savannah, GA.  In addition to the dining area, South offers a Jazz Parlor, which is a large, spacious design with a stage and booths, as well as tables.  There is a cover charge to enter the Jazz Parlor, which is added to your bill.  Check the web site for amounts, because the costs differ from night to night.  However, when the band is playing, you can hear them when you're in the dining space.  

The servers wore jeans, along with a white top and white apron, I believe.  So, while the atmosphere is hipster and upscale, it's ok to wear jeans there.

The next day, we told everyone about our incredible experience at South.  Soooo...in case you can't guess from the five star rating and long, complimentary review, you should go.

Culinary angels live in this kitchen wearing chef's hats and yelling for more truffle oil. I swear.

The service was great---patient, knowledgeable and warm. The atmosphere is amazing too---dim, bold colors, dark wood, crystal chandeliers, wrought iron and this vintage-modern-gothic feel. 

And the food. AAAH. Starters of foie gras, shrimp and grits, cheesy gnocchi. I ordered the filet for my entree, which was one of the best steaks I've ever had (and I used to live in Argentina, land of grass-fed beef). It came with au jus, potatoes and some other stuff I just scarfed happily without taking notes. They change the accouterments seasonally, so you can expect some variety. I also nabbed a bite of chocolate bread pudding (OMG) and Rachel F's short ribs and truffled cauliflower. Short ribs were a winner, but the cauliflower had me wishing there were some biscuits lying around because it tasted like gravy. Do with that what you will. 

The sour Clover Club was my drink of choice. It's a craft cocktail made with gin, lemon juice, housemade raspberry puree and egg white. Get this and be happy.

There are separate menus for upstairs and down. Down is more casual (but still pretty chic) and upstairs is fancy-town. I mean that in the best way because it isn't pretentious in the least.

I wish I could have eaten at Merchants every night I was in Nashville. As much as I might like, I wouldn't be able to afford eating here daily unless I was growing money in my backyard (which I am not, for the record---so stay out of my garden). It's probably best to come for a celebration with your friends and loved ones or an impressive date with your number one guy/gal.

Never have I been so irritated by someone at a restaurant who's not even serving me. I've been to Brio more times than I can count and sad to say I won't be back. 

Swung in to have a quick lunch and drinks at the bar. There was only one other couple farther down the bar, so we were quickly greeted by a super sweet bartender (I'll leave her name out to save her the embarrassment). While she was taking our drink order, a loud man (appearing to be a GM), came running into to the bar area to proclaim "ABOUT TIME!"... To insinuate that we had been waiting way too long for our bartender to wait on us. Which wasn't the least bit true. 

After she drop our food off and checking in on us a few times, we watched her head down to the other end of the bar to tend to the other couple. After their exchange, we overheard her ask the GM if she could take a few minutes break. That's when shit hit the fan. He immediately got loud and combative with her over the fact that she doesn't work enough hours and being that she's over 18, she's not entitled to one. The level of nonsense got to the point of the other couple butting in to saying something about state laws and breaks. He then turned around to debate the hours and laws with them. 

I really could not believe I was watching this go down... Our bartender naturally got flustered and upset to the point of walking away from him. As she passed us, I openly said to her that what just happen was not ok. She hurried quickly from the bar, GM 10 steps behind her, still shouting his point. Now no employees at the bar, myself and the other couple all looked at each other in disbelief. When the GM returned 5 minutes later, he stood in the area between the bar and the dinning room. Casually gossiping about what just happened to any employee who walked by him.

After watching all this go down, I was livid to the point I couldn't stand being there any longer. The couple next to us wrapped up their tab, asked the GM if he could give her (addressing him with her name) their tip money when she came back. He assured them he would (wouldn't put it passed him if he didn't). Another shake of their heads at us and they were gone. 

Our bartender returned about a minute later. We quickly finished our one drink and small appetizer when she asked if we would like another round. I declined and said we had planned on it; however I could not be in the same space as that GM. I was sure to ask her if they split tips there (which they don't) because I didn't want my few bucks going to that disgusting noob. 

Before leaving I got his name, Jonathan. And told the bartender how that was handled completely unprofessional and definitely undeserved, not to put up with that mess. No one needs that kind of abuse.

Last Sunday, four friends and I came here for brunch after some outdoor activities. We were ready to relax with lovely vegan food. Unfortunately, Green Table was a bit of a mess in terms of service. 

The staff were overwhelmed, there were only two people working the register and prep area (not sure how many were working in the kitchen), one of the folx working the register seemed new and swore to me the pesto was nut-free only to check with a colleague and be corrected--and that's a dire mistake. Also, they forgot one of our orders. 

On the bright side, after realizing their mistake, they hustled to get the missing food out to us just 10 minutes later. They brought over two free vegan cookies as a 'sorry' to boot, which was much appreciated. The food that my amigxs got was totally solid, according to them. 

I have a cashew allergy, and the dishes were cashew-rich, so whereas normally I'd taste everyone's dish to verify, I just stuck to my own veggie pesto sando. In that I subbed sunflower almond spread for pesto to avoid cashews, at the suggestion of the more knowledgable cashier. My food was super duper, so judging from that and the satisfied smiles and empty boxes all around, it seems like the grub hit the spot.

With very reasonable prices and a nice atmosphere, I would brave the service to return.

A friend and I ordered empanadas for pickup from Buena Onda a few weeks ago. The ordering process was smooth via their foodbooking.com ordering website. We called on the phone to ask about daily specials (Pro tip: always call and ask, as these often rotate!) I also asked about dietary needs, and the person we spoke with was helpful and friendly. As a vegan who is allergic to cashews, I wanted to make sure the restaurant's vegan cheese wasn't cashew-based. Our friendly employee was kind enough to get the package and read out the ingredients (it's soy+coconut-based, so I was in luck.)

That kind of customer service already had me thinking 5* and then we tasted the food. I ordered one each of the Vegana (organic red quinoa, peppers, onions, vegan cheese and spinach, wrapped in vegan dough made with Earth Balance) and the Hakuna Batata (sweet potatoes, spinach and shallots in vegan dough), $3.5 each. My friend had the Suiza (filled with Swiss chard, leeks, brie, and sage, and the Quinoa (basically the Vegana but with goat cheese instead of vegan cheese), also $3.5 each. In addition she ordered a sweet empanada made with quince.
