One little hiccup was that the sweet empanada said it came filled with emmental but instead featured goat cheese--no biggie there though, as she enjoyed it anyway. The side of chimichurri was totally delicious, if far more oily than either of us would have made it. 

If you're looking for something that tastes traditionally Argentine, this isn't it, at least not based on what we ordered. We realized that as a vegetarian and a vegan, we likely wouldn't get classic flavors, since this empanadería is trying to innovate rather than replicate (say, using veggie pork, onions, and potato.) We thoroughly enjoyed our empanadas and their novel flavor combinations, and would definitely order from Buena Onda again!

This was located off the beaten path. About 30min away from downtown. It is a drive but well worth it. If you're looking to feel like home and really get that warm feel, then this is the spot. Upon entering in the late afternoon, we were quickly seated. The server Owen was the best. Super attentive and helpful. He brought out warm fresh biscuits. It came with 3 different jelly spreads. Blackberry, strawberry, and peach. It was so good. The biscuits were hot and fluffy. with the homemade spread was a match made in heaven. Then we ordered the sweet tea as drinks. For our main dish I went with the half order of the loveless country ham, scrambled eggs, grits, and bacon. The country ham had a nice smokey taste to it. A thick cut and it was delicious. Better than any ham I've had before. Finished this off with the made from scratch banana puddin'. It was served cold and was a great way to end the meal. I'm so full yet so happy. The service here was also amazing. 

Recommendation: Country ham, biscuits, and banana puddin'

I love milk and honey! Big sign right in front. Walking inside to see some great designing. The store build out is very clean and great attention to detail. The menu ranges from brunch items to cold pressed juices. We got the fried chicken biscuit and the mean & green juice. It was really good the biscuit nice and fluffy. Chicken juicy and crispy. The juice was lightly sweet. I would definitely recommend this spot for brunch. 

Recommendation: fried chicken biscuit / mean & green cold press juice

terrible now since the renovation/ new owners. i used to love it before they made changes. food was very good and reasonable prices. now quality of food went down and prices are higher.

i was looking forward for them to reopen. and when they did i went. its just chaotic in there. they don't know what you ordered, bunch of people keep asking what did you order. then they can't find bill when you try to pay. they asked again. I went twice since they reopen and both times, same thing. also ordered to go recently. they said 25 minutes, drove out there, they don't even have it written down. then they said it will be ready soon. asked again 20 minutes later, they said they will go check in the kitchen, then they came back and said it will be ready soon. now i know they forgot and are going to rush cook it and they did. I am not going back there. 

such a waste, it was a great hot spot before the changes.

Average

I only came here because my hotel is right there and it was the only thing open at 10PM besides McDonald's.

It's really just bar food, not really all that great.  If you are staying at a local hotel, I would say just eat at McDonald's.

I'm the type of person who refuses to eat at McDonald's, but tonight I ate at McDonald's after eating at Gatsby's last night.  In the future I'll just get McDonald's.

As soon as I bit into the PYT burger there was white sauce dripping out the side of my mouth and all over my cleavage and I didn't even care to wipe it away cause the meat was so damn good. I just ate and ate until I had an orgasm!

Sike. The burger didn't jiz on me. It was actually pretty small and hardly juicy at all. I just really hate the ads for this place.

So yeah, in real life, the burger was fine but unremarkable. I liked that it was on a potato roll and the bacon was thick and super crisp. I couldn't taste the cheese. The patty was supposedly rare, but it was really well done and salty and dry. 

But the rest of my experience at PYT was pretty nice. We did shots of whiskey with pickle juice chasers which I loved. I had a fantastic spiked shake and basically my dream onion rings, thick cut and heavily battered. The service was good and the atmosphere wasn't as douchey as I'd feared.

The bottom line: 
Definitely not a burger destination, but a pretty fun time.

Update to my previous review: After receiving a threatening and nasty reply from a Kitchen Bar employee, disguised as a 'compliment,' riddled with assumptions about me, I've changed my rating of this business. I wish it was possible to give it zero stars.

I will never go back to this place, and I will have no problem sharing this experience with anyone I can. I'm wondering if other people who gave this place a less-than-stellar review (which is the majority of the reviews) have received similar messages from Carl W., or anyone else? 

I didn't love Kitchen Bar the one time I was there, but I didn't loathe it. Apparently Carl W. thought it necessary to tell me, "when you shit on a place you are essentially putting jobs of other human beings at risk." I don't think reviews are meant to be death sentences - they should simply be viewed as opportunities for business owners to look at for possible areas of improvement.  

Yelp reviews reflect a personal experience with a business, which is why it works. I hope harassment like this doesn't discourage people from sharing their honest opinions.

Update on 6/15-Carl W. is now going by the name Tychus F.

Still a 2 star sadly, maybe even 1 star...but I'll be somewhat generous, since I still ate it. 

I normally go to the L&L location on Mae Anne (sometimes on S. Virginia) and never really ran into issues. Their customer service, timing, and quality of food are always on point. I am not exaggerating when I say I can eat L&L everyday, I used to eat it at least once or twice a week. When I got my wisdom teeth out, my first solid food was their loco moco and spam musubi. I'm just such an avid L&L fan, I love it. 

However, I came to this location as it's closer to my work and it was my lunch break. I did have issues with this location a long time ago and decided to give it another try. Called, ordered ahead, and picked up my usual 1/2 order of BBQ Beef w/ all rice. 

Location is perfect, right next to other chain restaurants as Panda Express, Baked Bear, Peg's, Starbucks, and such. It's just a little ways down Legends Shopping Center. Super convenient. 

CUSTOMER SERVICE: 3/5. 
The young lady at the register did not greet me coming in, I was the one who started the conversation with a smile on my face. She wasn't smiling back or anything, so I just assumed she was not having a good day. I asked for a tiny thing of brown gravy on the side, and I wasn't informed that I got charged $1 something for it until I saw the receipt. No biggie, but communication is key. 

FOOD: 1/5...Awful. 
It did not taste anywhere close to the ones I get from the other locations. The rice was mushy like undercooked. The beef was very under seasoned; it practically tasted like nothing, so I had to dip it in soy sauce, something for my taste buds. The brown gravy, that I paid for, was watery and actually tasted like water with a hint of gravy. I wasn't satisfied with it, but I did eat it as I was starving.  

OVERALL: 2/5. 
I was just plain disappointed. I was on Keto diet, and this was my first craving after getting off it. I was extremely excited and talked highly of it to my coworkers. My coworkers have never tried L&L, so I had them take a bite of my food, and they said it was bland. I did agree, but it was just sad. 

Regardless, I still love L&L's Hawaiian food. I understand this is just one bad experience from a specific location but it won't change my loyalty to the restaurant.

Fresh, quality, unique, and varied menu items, outdoor seating, top-notch customer service, and live music; my Twisted Tail experience was 5+ stars. Situated in the South Street Headhouse District, there's no shortage of eats, shopping, and people watching. I can't imagine a better mid-week wind-down than a beautiful, warm evening sitting outside, eating my weight in small plates and chatting with friends - and The Twisted Tail provided just that. Keep in mind, this is not your typical greasy pub-grub menu, but if you're willing to step outside of your comfort taste buds for the sake of freshness and flavor - this place is a good bet.

This place is an ideal spot for a date or small group of friends. There were so many different, unique flavors presented on their short but encompassing menu, and with incredible suggestions from our server we ordered a feast - Spanish Octopus, Lamb Meatballs, Roasted Carrots & Burrata, Big Eye Tuna, and Swordfish. This was the absolute best culinary decision I've made in a while. Instead of coming out all at once, the plates were perfectly timed so we were able to take our time to enjoy flavors and conversation in between. Everything was spectacular. I'd never had octopus, and I was keen to try it. It was very tasty and a better texture than I anticipated. It is daunting to see a giant charred tentacle plated in front of you, but I was able to look past it after my first bite. 
Everything was excellent, but my two favorite dishes (I can't pick just one!!!) were the burrata and the swordfish. The burrata and carrots was rich but light, flavorful in all the right ways. The swordfish was juicy, buttery, and cooked to absolute perfection served with snap peas that looked and tasted like they were freshly picked. 

The live music, the warm breeze and outdoor seating, and the incredible service of the wait staff made for an incredible evening. To top the cherry, I got 15% off of our food bill thanks to simply checking-in on yelp! My friends and I polished five incredible plates of quality food for $60 - split three ways for $20 apiece. Honestly, it feels like robbery. 

I cannot WAIT until my next visit to The Twisted Tail. I've been told they rotate their menus with the seasons, so I'll be sure to try new things next time I visit (along with the burrata).

As a NON-vegan, I can say that their mac 'n cheese is delicious (and VEGAN!?!) In fact, most things I've tasted at Soy Café are delicious. You have to take in consideration that everything here is homemade and NEARLY everything is vegan. If you're a hearty carnivorous beast like me, I can highly recommend Soy as a chance to expand your taste buds for some earth-friendly, tasty dining. Prices are little on the higher side, as expected a super trendy, vegan-friendly destination. Their menu is very vast, so there are lots of options. I'm personally a huge fan of their smoothies - they are refreshing, freshly made, and insanely satiating. I can make a meal out of one of their heartier smoothies with peanut butter or bananas - om nom nom. 

I did give their vegan chocolate chip cookie a try, and I'd stray away. It was pretty crumbly and dry, so I'll probably just stick to my Tollhouse. The straws are paper, and are virtually unusable for the smoothies so BYO or go sans straw. I appreciate the thought though. Save those turtles, baby.

Soy's space is very big! It's a great place to grab a seat for a chat or to read a good book. Everything is freshly made, so it's good for a quick bite, but not if you're in a rush.

Overall - 5 stahs. I've had lots of not-good vegan food, and their food is delicious, vegan or not.

I loved this pub! Some friends and I stumbled in by chance, looking for brunch on a Sunday afternoon. 

The first pro: Brunch 'til 4pm. 

The second: Great selection of beer, delicious food, and generous portions all served quickly by delightful staff. 

The value is amazing: super affordable for a delicious meal. Very quaint and chill - a great place to kick back with a few drinks. I ordered a bowl of the thick, creamy sweet potato bisque and a pint of beer for $10. My friends ordered pancakes and french toast - the portions were very generous. There's a nice variety of savory and sweet brunch options on the menu. This friendly neighborhood pub would be my go-to hangout if I lived close by; it kind of reminds me of MacLaren's from HIMYM. Khyber Pass is definitely on my radar for the future.

Steel City has a lot going for it. Good coffee (and in-house Coffee Stout), a decent selection of bites, including gluten-free options, savory pastries, and egg-y breakfasts, and prime location in the heart of Phoenixville's bustling business district. 

Pre-pandemic, Steel City was the perfect place to study, enjoy live music, or grab a quick, satiating breakfast. Post-pandemic, Steel City has minimized their indoor seating, extended their outdoor options, and tried to implore social distancing when ordering in-store. There was a little bit of discombobulation during my most recent visit. The ordering counter is short, and tends to draw swarms of people waiting to hear their names called. There was a bit of confusion of who had ordered vs. who hadn't, and there were a few stragglers walking around un-masked. Honestly, they seemed a little understaffed, but I give them kudos for trying their best with what they have in a time of vague governmental mandates and adjustments to serving hungry customers. 

We ordered two breakfast burritos, which come vegetarian - egg, potatoes, and cheese. I added sausage to mine, and I tacked on my drink of the moment, an iced dirty chai tea latte.

We waited about 12 minutes for our burritos- which came out accidentally mislabeled. This was not an issue for carnivorous boyfriend and I, but if you're someone with a strict allergy or food restriction, this could have ended badly. I was reminded of my last visit, when I ordered an breakfast sandwich with sausage, and it came without sausage. That being said, the sausage is banging. Not like normal breakfast patties or weird overcooked links. This is good stuff. I dream of their burritos - topped with a side of sour cream and salsa - it's truly the breakfast of champions, keeping me satiated for the rest of the day.

The staff is eager and friendly, I was happy to see them trying to enforce social distancing and mask wearing on a super hot, busy Sunday morning. There appears to be room for improvement with speed and efficiency, but only if it doesn't effect their yummy burritos and great drinks. Order the coffee stout! Breakfast beer for the win.

YUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM.

I ordered take-out from apricotstone, and the portions and flavors were insane. I ordered the Chicken Shawarma platter, and it was easily two meals! The baba ghanoush was among the best I've ever had, and the greek salad was the perfect ratio of lettuce, feta, olives (with pits!! be careful!), and house dressing. The chicken was juicy and perfectly marinated. There was so much meat, my to-go box must have weighed a pound or more! I could only eat about half of the chicken before I was stuffed, which meant I got to eat more the next day (winner, winner chicken dinner!) The whole thing cost about $18. A little pricey, but worth it for a different take on take-out than pizza or cheesesteaks. 

While I didn't dine-in, I'd be keen to go back. The ambiance was cozy and dim, and while small inside, there was the option for candle lit outdoor dining on the front pathway. It's perfectly quaint, laid-back and delicious. This is the type of spot I'd feel comfortable popping a bottle of wine and chatting all night. 

If nothing else, I'll be back for the baklava....I'll be bak-lava. (I'm so funny to me)

I have a special place in my heart for quirky, mismatching coffee mugs, who were likely doomed to a long shelf life in a dusty thrift store, being brought back to fulfill their purpose of sheltering the sweet nectar of life: coffee. Little Spoon is more than the Dish's side chick to run a way with (Hey Diddle Diddle, anyone?)

Enough of my witty banter - Little Spoon is a gem. Nestled on a block of numerous brunch options, Little Spoon stands out with their specialty coffee drinks and unique flair on old school favorites. Savory French Toast, Cheddar and Chive pancakes, and Lemon Ricotta Pancakes are just a few of the standout dishes on the menu (which might be why we ordered them!) Be sure to peep the specials board, and BYO bubbly to enjoy a mimosa.

You will likely have a wait, and there is not a lot of space to hang around. Fortunately, you're right on South Street, so take a stroll or pop into one of the neighboring bars for a mimosa while you wait. You don't want to miss the food at Little Spoon!

The staff here was warm and welcoming, to the extent I almost want to quit my job and work here instead. They do NOT mess around when it comes to their wait times. You cannot make reservations, and you cannot call ahead. You must add your name in person, and they will text you when it's your time. They quoted me 35-40 minutes, and it was exactly 35 minutes.

All I can say is WOW. While searching for a place to eat on our last night in New Orleans we settled on this new gem on Bourbon St. There was a line outside but we were only in it for about 5 mins and we were quickly seated upstairs. The decor was nice and cozy, well lit and very clean. Our server Samuel walked us through the menu. I settled on the Oyster Po By  and fries, The Lady had the Catfish Platter and my cousin had the Ribeye and greens and we all shared a most wonderful piece of cheesecake. Everything was basically perfect ... food, service and the overall presentation of the restaurant. After dinner we hung out on the balcony and watched the sea of humanity walk up and down Bourbon St.

A 5 Star BANGER !!!! This lovely establishment checks all of the boxes. Drinks, Food, Service, Service beyond duty, decor, staff, seat comfort I can go on and I think I will. On Saturday night we arrived hungry and ready for drinks the wait for a table was 30 mins so we went to the bar to burn off some time. I ordered a Bourbon Flight, it was excellent and it had me where I wanted to be. After a few minutes we actually cancelled our table because we were thinking about waiting somewhere else.. but after more drinking we decided to stay,order food and eat at the bar. I ordered the OMG 2.0 Burger that just moved into the top 5 of the best burgers I've ever had in my entire life. It came with homemade kettle chips and fries. When the food came out the fries were cold, I informed our bartender Dani who informed her runner minutes later the manager came out and delivered hot and fresh fries and because of the error he offered to buy us dessert. Everything was great Dani even broke down the menu, answered every question and fixed every problem with a smile and a great attitude. Later the manager asked would we like the best dessert on the menu... The Whiskey Cake the answer was Hell Yes! This cake was gorgeous and delicious at the same time. Covered with fresh pecans floating on whiskey sauce with house made whipped cream on the side.... it made me tingle inside. This place is awesome and I pray that they expand to Jacksonville. Once again thanks to our bartender/ craft drink specialist Dani for being a pro and to management for correcting an error quickly and with a smile.

Welp had to see what all the hype was about. A few friends told us about this place and that we had to have breakfast here when in New Orleans. We opted to come to this location rather than a more crowded one, good move! We found a parking spot tight in front walked in and was seated immediately. I went for the gusto Catfish and grits, fried green tomatoes , breakfast potatoes and a big ole biscuit. The catfish was hot and with the creamy grits it was a tasty treat. The tomatoes were seasoned very well and the sauce that came with them had a tiny kick to it. The disappointment of the potatoes cost this place a five star rating along with the BBQ shrimp and grits that Tesha ordered only having 4 pieces of shrimp. All in all the decor was groovy our waitress nice and informative. Wouldn't rule out coming here again.

Wanted to buy some liquor and wine for the Hotel room....... ended up getting beer, wine, liquor a few cigars and some hand made Paganini's and a few other items. This place is the bomb.. A highly effective market with everything that you'll need while in town. They have a hot bar with chicken, fish and other. The staff was helpful and friendly. An added bonus was that I didn't have to worry about dogs or other pets all in my way as I'm trying to shop for FOOD.

Another African food place has popped up and they specialize in Eritrean which has the same concept as Ethiopian food. The place is a hole in the wall for sure and has some of the best tasting food I have tried. The service is a little lacking but it is owned by a family who often has their two kids sitting There. They definitely take the time to slave over the stove and make the food right.

 There are plenty of vegan options for those who avoid meat and dairy. Their shero (spicy chickpeas) is one of my favorite dishes due to the smokey and flavorful nature. I also really enjoy their potato dish. It might be a tad salty but I love the texture of how the potato is cooked--perfectly. When you order one thing it is like ordering everything since they give you a little of everything to try. The textures and flavors of each dish are unique and each are delicious. They have the option of getting a small or large of most dishes with the small being $7 and the large being $10. Small is enough! I haven't had the large but my small has always fed me and another person.

It's so good I've come like 3 times within the past few weeks. Everything is so affordable so it's a great spot for lunch or dinner. You can't beat a meal for 2 at $10-$15. I love the food so much and I am happy it's so close to where I work. However, the injera needs a little work. It has been a bit inconsistent the times I have been, and sometimes it will be a little dry or just not as spongy as I expect it to be. Nonetheless I would highly recommend the food. Definitely try the lentils or split peas as well.

If you're in or travelling through St. Louis, this is a MUST go if you want some St. Louis style ribs along with some of the BEST sides that I've had ever. 

Located in the Loop of St. Louis, Salt and Smoke is a dine in southern casual restaurant with all the southern comfort foods, meats and a surprisingly decent number of vegetarian dishes available. I have to say, I cannot think of a single bad thing about any of the food here, so it's definitely worth a stop. 

I ordered the half rack of baby back ribs with chili and Mac n cheese. It also comes with a small load of bread that was great. 

Ribs: 5/5 Super smokey, loved the texture and the meat falling off the bone, cooked perfectly. The sauces they had on the side were great, you had 4 to choose fr and all were delicious options to compliment the ribs. 

Mac n Cheese: 5/5 the crunchy parts in the cheese is icing on the cake. Absolutely immaculate with the cream inside. It's kinda unfair I live on the West Coast when food like this exists. 

Chili: 5/5 Honestly this one is pretty good too. Tastes homemade and normally restaurants don't focus on their side dishes but this one is great. 

Bread: 5/5 crunchy outside, soft inside. Nice and thick. My California brain enjoyed it. 

Overall, I really enjoyed this spot. I'm kinda jealous that we don't have this well rounded of a restaurant in California, so props to Salt and Smoke for some good food.

The service and the food was very good. Their prices are too high even for Santa Barbara. It's not Montecito. I left hungry after spending way too much money. 
The kicker was being served tap water which tasted like chlorine. When I asked why it wasn't filtered they told me they do have a reverse osmosis system but that would cost an additional $6.00. Really??? Your days are numbered!

It started out bad. At the bar, the lady who appeared to be in charge since she was the only one behind the bar, directed a male employee to make a drink. He stated he had never made a drink before. So, why when it's the customer's drink does she think is a good time to teach him? If she knew how, why not just make the drink herself?

From there things only got worse. We had a large group and were seated at two tables. One table got their food and were given to go containers well before the other table even got their food even though we all arrived together. One person ordered a steak medium but it was cooked wrong. Instead of taking it back, the staff decided to argue about it. I think it was actually the manager or the owner. It was a lady that came out once before when there was a concern about the drink. I ordered a daiquiri. I wasn't asked and didn't know there were flavors, the menu just says daiquiri. Another person in my group ordered a strawberry margarita. They were identical but this lady said they were different. Who knows. 

I ordered the Pardo Shrimp and it was horrible. The sauce on the pasta looked dry and had no flavor other than a little spice but I couldn't figure out what flavor it was trying for because it had none. The shrimp were small. I just left it there. A salad came with my meal but it came 20 minutes after everyone else got theirs. 

The service was bad. No consideration. No accommodation. No one was pleased with the service. No return visits from any of us. No word of mouth advertising either. That was my first and last time. There is more to say but I won't even bother. Just go elsewhere.

We walked down after Wednesdays at the Square, and had been here a couple of years ago when it was a different restaurant.
It's a nice room. Decent decor, clean space. Got seated right away, and our server came by quickly. Very friendly, and helpful with suggestions. 
We ordered apps of guacamole classico, and churros. 
At the same time, I ordered a Cochinita Torta, which is "Yucatan style Pork, cashew habanero aioli, pickled onion" as stated on the menu. Babycakes ordered a couple of al pastor tacos. 
In a few minutes, the churros came to the table, with a chocolate dipping sauce. 
The churros were great. Sugary, cinnamon dusting on a nice tasting fried dough. With the sauce it took it to another level. 
We were sitting after that for quite awhile. Enough so a manager came over and apologized for the wait. 
Our entrees came out, and it was underwhelming.  My torta had a lot of bread. Or maybe it was a lack of pork...or pickled onion... Or flavor.. Or (please fill in your own adjective here). The fries were good. 
Babycakes said the tacos had no flavor. She asked for some hot sauce or salsa to get some kind of taste to it, and it kind of worked. 
Two entrees, two misses. 
As we were eating, the manager again came over to apologize for our guacamole not coming to the table (we hadn't seen our server for a bit), and said he could see the guac in the window, and, not seeing anyone around to bring it, went over and got it and brought it to the table. He did comp the guacamole since we were almost done with our entree. 
The guac..... 
Had tomato in it, with lime juice. 
Again. 
Kind of bland and tasteless.  
No garlic?? No onion??? Salt? Pepper? Jalapeno? 
Come on. 
Service, not great. Food, not great. 
Dissapointed.

I rarely give 5 stars reviews.....
That being said.... WOW!!
This is the real deal. You smell the meat smoking as you park. The aroma only draws you in. 
Inside the door, a nice, casual atmosphere.  No fancy chef'fing going on. It's just homey and inviting. You order at the register, and the guy was super friendly and nice as we changed our order a couple of times while standing in front of him. It was 5pm, so they weren't busy yet. Went in back where there are picnic benches and other tables. Clean washrooms, big. 
THE FOOD: WOW. I mean WOW. Had brisket, chicken, pulled pork, and Sides of Mac and cheese, potato salad, and Smokey corn grits. 
The meats were ALL tender, juicy, moist, delicious, smokey, scrumptious, and perfect. I could individually break them down but it would all be great. 3 kinds of sauces. I liked the sweet and the hot one. There was a vinegary one, but I didn't care for it. 
Potato salad: red potatoes WITH skin, and light mayo, white pepper. Just right. Not SOAKED in mayo, but just FLAVORED with it. 
Smokey corn grits: this was a sides special on the board, and I gotta say, hope it becomes a regular item. Flavorful, savory and again, perfect. 
Mac and cheese: usually not my thing, but they were great. 
Also had key lime pie for dessert. Tart/sweet flavor was delicious,, graham cracker crust was superb, whip cream on it. A great way to end a great meal!
This is the real. 
BBQ
LOVE!!

I've lived in northwest Reno for a few years now and have never steeped foot in this restaurant until recently. Not sure why I never tried it sooner. From the moment we walked in they greeted us and sat us down right away. I tried the special which was French toast, with eggs and ham. The portions are good in size and the prices on the menu and reasonably priced. I'm glad we were able to try it, now that we know we have more tasty breakfast options closer to home we will have to come back soon.

A foodie's dream! So many different vendors, a melting pot of different cuisines. My favorites are DiNic's for sandwiches and Beiler's doughnuts. I will be back! 

Prices are very reasonable. They have a good amount of seating. Very casual. Make sure to get your parking validated.

Oh just wow. Amazing. I was skeptical of the reviews because I fear some restaurants are just too "hyped" up. But Osteria Natalina delivered. My husband and I arrived just after 7pm on a Friday night. They don't take reservations, but we were able to get a seat right away.

The owner greeted us and led us to our table. He has a passionate, big personality who genuinely cares about the cuisine his restaurant serves. A few other Yelpers have complained about him being too overbearing, but we appreciated it. He recited the specials from the heart and offered suggestions. I couldn't decide between two of the specials (the braised osso bucco and the braised beef & veal Agnolotti). The owner told me that he would have the chef prepare a smaller version of the osso bucco and also include a few agnolotti on there as well. I thought that was very thoughtful and much appreciated his generosity. 

For an appetizer we ordered the calamari. Phenomenal and very impressive. It wasn't your average breaded and deep fried calamari. It was grilled with just the right amount of olive oil and fresh squeezed lemon juice to harmonize the calamari steak without overdoing the simplicity of the dish. 

My husband ordered the lobster ravioli. I was skeptical because I feel like most Italian restaurants skimp on the lobster and it's overpriced. But at $18.50 for 9-10 jumbo stuffed ravioli with LUMPS of lobster in it with lumps of lobster on top of it as well, you can't go wrong. Osteria Natalina has restored my faith!

I ordered the osso bucco and braised beef/veal agnolotti. The osso bucco had fabulous flavor, and it was apparent that this had been thoughtfully prepared, as it was extremely tender. The agnolotti were outstanding. I would have eaten a whole bowl of that with that incredible sauce on top of it. Heavenly. The side of vegetables that it came with were great too. They were cooked without being overcooked. 

We did have to wait longer than usual to get our check, but the owners brother/nephew (some relative) came to our table with complimentary peanut butter gelato to cleanse our palates and that was the nail in the coffin for this fabulous meal. Hands down best meal that we have had in a long time in Tampa. 

I definitely don't dole out 5 stars very often, but when I do, take notice! I have already told all my friends that this is THE place to come for authentic, Italian food that doesn't skimp on flavor or quality. 

Stop reading this already and go check it out! :) You're welcome xo

We came to Moby Dick on our recent trip to Santa Barbara after unsuccessfully trying to dine at the nearby SB Shellfish Company (where the line was too long). The food was decent, but the service was way too inattentive and slow. It was a waiting game for most of our meal.

For starters, It took a long time to order because when we would ask a question, our waiter would say "let me find out" and then disappear and come back with the answer. We wished he would just hear us out and then make one trip to the kitchen to figure things out instead of going back and forth.

In addition, even though it was only 1PM, they were out of their dungeness crab. I ended up getting the local rock crab (great price at $25) instead. When this order came up, it arrived with just the crab and no sides and no melted butter. We had to flag down the waiter for these things. Also, when the crab was given to me, the staff member said he would return with a nutcracker, and that took more time.

Also, we were not given silverware until after we requested it AFTER we already received our food. Super frustrating sitting there with freshly delivered food and not being able to eat it.

We never were offered refills on our water or lemonade, and when it was time to pay the bill, it took forever again. My partner had to walk the credit card and bill up after it had been sitting on our table for over 15 minutes. 

The best part of our meal was the incredible view as you're sitting on the pier in an enclosed space. Also, that you can add a $2 cup of clam chowder to virtually every entree. A great deal considering the regular price is $6. We also ordered the fish and chips, and the fish was kind of bland but the fries were battered and INCREDIBLE.

I feel like we "lost" over half an hour in wasted time just from having to wait a lot during our visit. That's a real bummer when you're in town for a limited amount of time and want to make the most of your time.
Horrible place don't even eat here the pasta was totally overlooked and it is an Asian place in disguise of an Italian eatery don't wast your money u wouldn't even have given it a one star

Tough to pick stars.  As far as decor and ambience goes, I'd give it 4 stars, (and perhaps 5 for decor) but for food and service I'd give it a 3.
The hosts were very nice. As was our waiter.  All were "Santa Barbara good" which is to say that if you were in a big city you would expect more, but this is SB.  And, as I said, they were lovely folk.
I was stunned that they took my wine out of view to open it.  I brought my own bottle (special occasion). Corkage was $40 - highest I am aware of in SB. I have never had a bottle taken out of view for opening before. I would have taken this up with the manager but wanted to enjoy dinner with friends.
My hanger steak got the best review amongst the four of us. Other food was, frankly, just OK. Nothing great; nothing terrible.   Certainly not the standard that the restaurant would seem to promise by looks or prices.
Some interesting drinks on the menu. The duck fat washed bourbon was a big hit. The collins were not. Can't remember our other drink, but it was polished-off with gusto and relish.
If you're looking for "the scene", this may be your place.  If you're looking for Bouchon service and quality: go to Bouchon - a world apart in both areas.
I would not go back to eat, but may go for drinks.

Chocolate dipped cupcakes! Sprinkle cookies! Strawberry turnovers! They have every sweet treat you could possibly imagine. Everything looks so wonderful in their display cases, and I had to use all of my willpower not to come home with a box full of sweets in addition to the cake I ordered. The red velvet cake I got was heavenly. It was a triple layer cake with frosting that is to die for. Additionally, they did a great job decorating it with a Happy Birthday greeting and pretty flowers. The staff were very friendly on the phone when I called in my order, and they were just as nice when I came to pick up the cake. The small 7" cake I ordered cost $25. They say that size feeds 7, but when we cut it...because of the triple layers...we had half the cake left over after we cut 7 pieces. So, it's a great value for the price. I will be back to Nadie's for the next cake I need. Or for one of their chocolate dipped cupcakes!

Fantastic service!  $11.95 for a large pizza pie my coworker and I couldn't even eat the whole pizza.  The pizza was pretty good.  Crust, then cheese, sauce on top the cheese, then whatever toppings you order go on last.  I ate the rest of my pizza for dinner and it still tasted fresh.   Great experience.

DO NOT.
Worst experience EVER.
We were traveling through town staying in a nearby hotel... and were craving pizza.   Checked out the locals online.... papa johns, dominos... and came accross Penos, which looked upscale and edgy.   We went for it...
When I called... the ordering process took about 15 minutes.   Long pauses... I swear... I thought the person was on valium.   Finally.. when the order was placed... he said... "OK.. 15 mins.... but probably much longer"   Um... what does that mean?   Anyhow... the food came rather fast to the hotel.  The delivery guy was a bit clumsy, but super sweet.   And then it all comes tumbling down.   We ordered 3 things.... House Italian salad (7.00) .. "crispy chicken wings Vesuvius" (9.00) and a "make your own" 12 inch , thin crust pizza.(18.50)

DO NOT.

In a nutshell...
The "house" salad was a handful of chopped romaine, with ONE olive, and grated, processed mozzarella ... and a plastic container of olive oil.

The "crispy chicken wings" were 4 pieces of what looked like boiled chicken quarters (see photo) with an empty plastic container of "dipping sauce"

And then there was the "12" pizza" which was actually about 8 inches accross.. STONE cold..   and the most bland sauce... but what was really awful was the shoe leather crust.   My son couldn't even bite through it.   Awful....

So... OK.... we have to be open to "a bad night... Or.. an off night" with any establishment.   But this is were is gets really good....

We called the restaurant to give our feed back on the "Crispy" chicken which was delivered without dipping sauce... and the house salad, which consisted of a handful of lettuce and ONE olive... and the horrible, tiny pizza.... and when we called... we were immediately passed to the owner.   Before we could even finish a sentence , this guy JUMPED down our throats.... Saying... "DUDE... I have a restaurant full of people right now... Go ahead and write a review on YELP like all the other losers"    

wait.

what?

Did I just hear that correctly??

DO NOT support this pompous, arrogant restaurant owner who delivers bad, overpriced food.
The curious thing... is we were not asking for anything in return, but just wanted to give our feedback... and the owners violent reaction just proves that he must get many of these calls many times a night.

AWFUL food... Super awful experience, and 40.00 down the drain.

We ended up ordering 2 Dominos pizzas which arrived promptly, and were piping hot.

What a joke.

Trust me on this one.... DO NOT.

(Just a simple guy writing a review on Yelp with all the other "losers")

I used to love the country club. Once the novelty wears off and you experience how terrible the service is, it's not even worth it. I was almost in tears today after I made the mistake of leaving my credit card after paying in one of the books. I went back immediately, within the same minute, and it was gone. I waited a while trying to flag down one of the bartenders (after waiting 20 minutes just to close out) and finally got one, and he was so unbelievably pissed off that I had the nerve to ask him for my card back. He literally started yelling at me, stretching across the bar to get in my face, and was telling me that it was "my fault" that I left it and he didn't "have time" to deal with me or look for it, but apparently he had the time to stand there and yell at me for 10 minutes while I said not one word. He walked away and kind of poked around and then even came back to yell at me some more. At one point my girlfriend intervened and told him that I wasn't saying anything, trying to just make it stop. I was in such shock my jaw must have been on the floor. I was almost on the phone with the bank about to cancel my card and tell them that the country club stole it until a manager came up and surprise surprise, located the card that I was "lying" about behind the bar. I have never seen someone with such an anger problem in all my life working as a bartender like that. Even before I was able to close out, during my long wait I saw him yelling at another staff member telling him to "make the g*d damn burger" and patrons were even noticing it. All the while he was doing shots and mingling with other staff, but was SO busy. I wish I could say that this was the first time that I got bad service at the Country Club, but this was certainly the most upsetting. It almost felt like if there weren't anyone else around that he would have hit me or something, and I'm a small girl. I never ever want to go there again after being yelled at like that, and I cannot believe after reading some of these other reviews that these bartenders are able to keep their jobs. They definitely lost a customer who was this close to buying a membership if not for these repeated incidents. Here is another review my friend wrote a while ago for another bad experience we had there, which was forgiven, but after this I don't think I will be going there or recommending the CC to anyone again. - http://www.yelp.com/biz/the-country-club-new-orleans?hrid=lPBZyG2-Dday90F32S3eMg

Pros: delicious drinks and interesting theme. 

Cons: customer service. 

I brought friends from out of town last night for a reservation made a week prior. My reservation was not taken properly and we were not able to sit at a table. After dealing with the very rude doorman, who must have thought that we were trying to weasel our way into getting a table, the GM said we should go to the bar, have a drink and he would come get us with the first available table. 2 hours later the GM hadn't even checked on us. Having come from a customer service and bar service background, I could not believe their level of apathy over a mistake on their end. 

In a town where almost any restraunt can provide you with a great drink and dish combination, we decided to head down the road to Ceviche, where we were met with only the kindest host, server, and bar staff. 

Ciro's may have been great once, but since an obvious wait and bar staff change within the last year, it's ability to warmly welcome customers through its doors is incredibly poor. I have never been so embarrassed in front of my friends, and was made to look like a sneaky jerk on top of that. I cannot say that I would recommend Ciro's to anyone unless real changes are made there.

It's a pity, because the food and drinks are not bad at all. Just don't plan on quick, or polite service when you get there.

I am pleasantly surprised to report that I thoroughly enjoyed my time here at Superior Seafood. A few things I like:

Good char-grilled oysters that don't require a trip downtown and the wait at Acme.
A solid bloody mary. If you're gonna use a mix, it's Zing Zang FTW.
The Blackened Catfish Napoleon. Delicious.
Watching the Saints win with the rest of the fine folks in this establishment.
The shrimp salad. I stole some of my wife's and it made me feel healthy.
Excellent service from a hilarious waiter. He was happy to chat with us as opposed to the unbearably loud Sweet 16 going on across the restaurant.

Us: What is that crazy centerpiece they have on the table?
Him: Too. Fucking. Much.

I am a Bloody Mary snob, and I blame New Orleans. 

I don't know if it's the spicy bean, if I'm just more hungover and thus more grateful for the hair of the dog, if my opinion is skewed by the fact that you can walk around on the street with it, or if New Orleans just breeds bartenders who are born knowing how to make a better Bloody, but I'm convinced that the average New Orleans Bloody Mary would be the best Bloody Mary in any other city.

I don't know why, exactly. 

What I do know is that Johnny White's makes one of the best Bloody Marys in New Orleans, which means they make one of the best Bloody Marys anywhere. Any day you start with one of these is bound to be a good day.

It turned out we weren't the only people in Philly that wanted to drink on a Saturday afternoon, and Vintage Wine was essentially the only place in the area that eight of us could sit* at the same table. Lucky for us too, because Vintage Wine is a very nice little spot we might not have stumbled upon otherwise. 

While I usually prefer to order wine in a wine bar, I couldn't resist starting with the White & Wild cocktail. Not just because it describes at least a few of the friends I was with, but because it was composed of Vodka, St. Germain, white wine, and more. I like when people mix alcohol with other alcohol and then pour in some more alcohol...and then give it to me. And damn, that shit is refreshing. As was all the wine I sampled afterward.

They have food here, as well, if you didn't know. I know that people have been known to say that we eat first with our eyes, but I tend to disagree. I eat with my mouth, and presentation usually takes a back seat to taste in my mind. But here at Vintage, the meat and cheese plates are actually stunning. I don't know who is artfully arranging fruit and nuts and compotes around a nice array of charcuterie back there, but I really, really appreciate you. Not every place takes such pride in their pear spirals, and you sir or madam, are truly talented.

Now that I'm thinking about it, I like the whole aesthetic in this spot...from the enormous wine bottle chandelier to the glowing cork wall in the back to the tasteful bathroom decor. 

Plus, they have a lot of wine. I'd come back. 
______________
*There were plenty of bars where we could stand and drink, but I'm a crotchety old man these days, and I like hearing what my friends have to say.

The Good.

-The Bloody Marys are solid. 
-It's always fun. I can honestly say I've never had a bad time at Pat O's.
-The place is enormous. There's always a bar that's easy to get to. 
-There's a flaming fountain for gods' sakes.
-Piano Bar. There is nothing better than being lose-your-wallet-demolished and singing (OK, maybe screaming) along to your favorite songs about the Southland with 15 of your closest friends.

The Bad.

-Yes, it's touristy.
-The Hurricanes are tooth-hurtingly sweet, and your girlfriend is probably going to want one. And then she'll agree it's too sweet. 

The Ugly.

-Don't take this the wrong way, because I love and respect the elderly. I enjoy watching them dance and laugh and have a blast...but once they start grinding and hooking up, I feel the Hurricane coming back up.

The French Quarter is a touristy place. And when I say touristy, I mean that people will rip you off every chance they get. If you are looking for any sort of groceries, at somewhat decent prices, this is your spot. 

For example: I wanted some Tony Chachere's Creole Seasoning because I can't seem find it in NYC, and Rouse's sells it for $2, as opposed to the $6 they want at the tourist shops.

And if you don't have anywhere to cook, and you're just in town to drink yourself into a blind stupor, the liquor prices here are as good as you'll find in the area.

I'm not a big fan of anything Bam!-related.* Especially Bam Margera, that guy is the worst. But my girlfriend insisted we eat at one of Emeril's restaurants while we were in New Orleans, and of the three, I definitely prefer NOLA.

The food is solidly above average. As far as entrees are concerned, I've devoured the duck, the pork chop, and the shrimp and grits on separate occasions, and although none have quite dazzled me, they certainly haven't disappointed either. The only true standout is the garlic crusted drum, which is DOPE.

Portions are large though, and barring unreasonable expectations, you should be happy with your meal. In addition, I've always enjoyed the service, which is the right mix of familiarity (I got called "dude" several times) and consideration.

Despite the fact that I'm not exactly captivated by Emeril's shtick or by his food, one item on the menu truly impresses me. The stuffed chicken wings on the appetizer menu are wonderfully tasty, but more than that, I am fascinated by their construction. 

It's as though they've taken apart the wings, removed most of the bones, stuffed them with (I think) pork, shrimp, and the chicken, and wrapped the still-intact skin back around it. Served with a nice dipping sauce, it baffles me with its ingenuity and delights me with its flavor. 

After several visits, it is the one item that I continue to order, and I don't think you should miss.
________

*But I do love B.A.M. (Brooklyn Academy of Music).

I have two rules:

If there is ever scrapple on the menu, I order it. 
If there is ever andouille gravy on the menu, I order it.

These are weird rules to have, because until I ended up at the Market Street Grill:

I didn't know what scrapple was.*
I'd never seen andouille gravy on the menu.

But a man has to have a code. And mine forced me to order The Telly, which is three eggs, hash browns, peppers, onions, and cheddar all scrambled and topped with andouille gravy and scrapple. 

This literal mountain of deliciousness only costs $10, because Market Street Grill is the best. I couldn't even finish it, and I don't know if I've ever said that about a breakfast plate. 

Everything else about Market Street Grill is awesome as well. The service is friendly and helpful, the mugs have bacon sayings, the place is clean, bright, and comfortable, and they are FAST. Don't worry about the wait, they turn tables over more efficiently than anyone I've seen.

Also to the little kid I walked in on in the bathroom, I'm sorry. I didn't see anything. You should start locking the door though. 
_____________

*I thought I did, but I was wrong. I thought scrapple was like pork scraps...like some sort of hot dog shavings. Scrapple actually a loaf made of pork scraps mixed with cornmeal and wheat flour, and godknowswhatelse. Sounds quite unappetizing, but tastes delicious.

Honestly, we just stumbled on this place because it's right by Bogart's, and I needed some ribs. And while ribs are more important than everything else, the everything else that you can find here at the Farmers Market makes me reconsider [but not retract] that statement.

Before we get into all that, you should know that there's a definite New Orleans vibe happening here (and all over St. Louis); maybe it migrated up the Mississippi...all I know is that you can get a legit bloody mary from Julia's for only $4 (and beignets if you'd like). It's got pickled asparagus and a spicy bean, and sipping on that thing as you peruse the rest of the market is the move.

What else can you peruse? 

Pimped out pickles. Pecan pie in a jar. Any kind of meat you'd ever want, including pig ears. Fruit Loops kettlecorn. NFL jerseys, mugs, t-shirts, hats, etc. Goose Poop. Seafood. Every kind of fresh produce you can think of. Pork rinds. Mini-doughnuts. Spices. Flowers. Roasted nuts. SO MUCH SOAP. Pastries, oils, salsas...I can't even remember it all.

And that's just the tip of the iceberg. Get over here already.

Claustrophobics need not apply.

Beware, this deli is LITTLE. If you go at prime lunchtime, you're going to be crammed into their tiny little aisles with everyone else who just wants to get their sandwich and get out. There's nowhere to sit and eat (unless you call the USA Today stand in front al fresco dining), there's no atmosphere to speak of, and the ordering system is not exactly ordered...but there's plenty of friendly* to go around. 

More importantly, after your first bite you won't even care about any of that, because the All That Jazz really is all that. It's #1 on the specialty sandwich list for a reason: 

With sauteed shrimp, mushrooms, turkey, ham, cheese and a completely unhealthy dose of Wow Sauce (think halfway between Russian dressing and chipotle mayo), this thing is messy and delicious. I grabbed a two-inch stack of napkins on the way out, and pretty much destroyed them all. 

Their website claims them to be the best kept secret in the Quarter, and I can't even argue (because I'm not sure there are any other secrets). You're just a few blocks away one of the most touristy spots in the nation, and this is actually just a quality deli populated by locals. 

Great sandwiches, great prepared food, nothing but love.
_______________

*Perhaps it's because I no longer live in New Orleans, but this was the first time another man has called me "baby" in quite some time.

I'll say it: I'd switch teams for John Besh. 

Restaurant August was already among my favorite restaurants in the nation, and Luke is a casual alternative that offers up an entirely different but equally tasty view into New Orleans food. 

For one thing -- and let's be serious: probably the most important thing -- they make an EXCELLENT burger. It is massive (and shareable according to some), covered in caramelized onions, Allan Benton's bacon, caramelized and Emmenthaler Swiss cheese. And although the brioche bun stands up well, it's unavoidably messy when cooked to a juicy medium rare. Our bartender friend informed us that this particular burger was chosen as 8th in the nation; I'm not sure by whom, but I'm not mad I got it, just mad I'm not on the committee. 

The shrimp and grits are also apparently a specialty of the house. We were told that they do them a bit differently than most places; as far as I can tell, they just cook the shrimp perfectly, and make the sauce good enough to drink. 

I was a bit disappointed that the fries were cooked past crispy into crunchy territory, but the lady on my left loved them all the same. For me though, the only downsides were said fries and the fact that their bloody mary is merely a mix (although I do like the Gator Blood), and they don't provide a spicy bean. Sacrilegious, I know, but give them a chance to make it up to you with the food.

If I was only given one sentence, I'd say that the menu is entirely too long, the service is confused and disjointed, but the food is worth a try.

Luckily, Yelp allows me to elaborate, so I'm going to get long-winded with it.

If and when I return to R'evolution, I plan to eat at the bar. Our friend behind the stick not only made an excellent martini, he also introduced us to the term "dusty," to refer to a slightly dirty preference (as opposed to filthy). That alone was worth stepping through the door. (He was also the only staff member who didn't make me feel the least bit uncomfortable.)

Other items worth the price of admission are the Death By Gumbo and the beer-battered crab beignets. The former is spectacularly rich and complex, with the accompanying quail perfectly crispy (to be honest, I did die just a little bit as I waded through). The latter are light and impossibly airy, with the four different remoulades a nice touch but one that isn't conducive to sharing.

The entrees were less impressive. Although it wasn't fantastic by any means, I did enjoy my choice of Red Snapper and Pork Belly A La Plancha. However, it certainly seemed to be two separate dishes rather than one composed plate. Her tortelli was also well-made, but unremarkable to the point that I can't recall the components.

I'm not exactly sure how long R'evolution has been open but the staff, unfortunately, does not seem to have hit its stride yet. I always give new places the benefit of the doubt and I would never downgrade them because of it, but the inordinate amount of hiccups is worth mentioning. 

Other than the aforementioned bartender, everyone seemed to be visibly stressed and/or incompetent. We waited over a half hour past our reservation time, for starters. In addition, there was entirely too much fussing; silverware in use was taken away and dropped on laps, plates were stacked and dropped immediately, forks were removed and replaced for no reason...and somehow amid all the hovering, dirty appetizer plates were left on the table until after the entrees were cleared. I'd never even have noticed, but it was so distracting I couldn't help it.

There was also oddly pushy upselling at more than one point in the meal. One of our servers fell just shy of insisting we order a cheese course. I'm sure the cheese is excellent, but the gift box of petits fours (a cute but unnecessary touch) was more than I needed by the end of the meal. I mean, I had a quail inside my soup. 

All in all though, we had a lovely meal in a gorgeous dining room. I think with a bit more of a focus on execution in both front of the house and back, R'evolution could one day be among the best of the city. Until then, I think I'll stick to martinis and Death By Gumbo at the bar.

I have never in my life experienced hospitality so genuine, so heartfelt, and so absolutely amazing, as I did at Monell's. Michael, the owner, redefined going above and beyond the call of duty; my friends and I were absolutely astonished by his kindness and remain thoroughly grateful. 

Well, I'm getting ahead of myself. 

I suppose I should tell you first that the food is fantastic. If you're looking for some downhome, legit Southern cooking, this is where you want to be. Forget Olive Garden, you're actually family at Monell's. Everyone here will greet you with a smile, and after a short wait (they are quite popular, but the line moves quickly and the garden you wait in is beautiful), you'll be ushered into what looks like your grandmother's dining room. 

Unless you have 14 people or so, you're going to be sharing a table with some other folks for a family-style feast. The table was already set with sweet tea, tea punch and other beverages, as well as several types of hot sauce and other condiments you may or may not need. Don't worry about ordering right either, because they are just going to bring you everything. And I mean EVERYTHING:

Corn pudding, cheese grits, green beans, vinegar pork, coleslaw, cornbread, biscuits and gravy, mashed potatoes, fried chicken, BBQ chicken, mac & cheese, pecan pie...it's all there, and it's all good. You take however much you want, and you pass it to your left. And there will be enough for everyone, I guarantee it. I went back to my favorite items at least twice, and there was definitely still leftovers.

Once you've eaten yourself to the point of delicious, perfectly satiated pain, you get up and pay only $20, which is perhaps the best deal I've ever encountered. It is so worth it, I would easily have paid twice that for the privilege of sitting down in their dining room. I was sad I had to leave, but I will be back each and every time I'm in Nashville.

This brings me to the only downside of Monell's, as well as the reason they've earned a customer and advocate for life: 

It's not in the most heavily trafficked area of Nashville. If you don't have a car, it's nearly impossible to get back downtown because there is no public transportation to speak of. However, we had let the owner Michael know that we had a plane to catch, and he was nice enough to call us a cab. The cab company quoted us a wait of about twenty minutes. After half an hour though, there was still no sign of a cab. We were standing on the street out front, starting to get a bit worried, and Michael came outside suddenly and told us to come with him. 

We followed him to the back, assuming there was a cab waiting on the other side. He unlocked a silver sedan, and told us to pile in. This man was worried that we were going to miss our flight, and he insisted on driving us back to our hotel. 

Let me repeat that so there's no confusion: the owner of Monell's walked out of his own restaurant during service, and insisted on driving us -- four complete strangers from another city -- back to our hotel in HIS OWN CAR.

This selfless gesture of hospitality actually blew my mind. It's not like this man wasn't busy. Michael owns the place. From the time we walked in, he was busy keeping the extensive waitlist, running the cash register, leading folks to their tables...all while cracking jokes and welcoming everyone into the restaurant all on his own. And he just dropped everything and drove us, in his own car, back downtown. Unbelievable. 

Thank you Michael, for being the absolute definition of Southern hospitality. The sign above the door says that we arrive strangers and leave as friends, and you better believe you've got one in Brooklyn from here on out.

This. This is why St. Louis is known for barbecue.

For starters, Bogart's makes some of the best ribs I've ever had. They are properly cooked, porky as hell (in the best way), and if I had been smart enough to order a full slab, I would've eaten until I was very, very ill. 

As it is, a half slab of ribs is a solid meal, and Bogart's offers the generous and astonishingly sweet deal of adding a 1/4 lb. of any meat on for just a few bucks. Forgive my saying so, but if you don't add on at least some burnt ends, you're a goddamned fool. 

The burnt ends are the most delicious meat candy you've ever been lucky enough to put in your mouth, and walking out of here without any is the worst mistake you've made since the 90s.*

I'm of the opinion that neither the burnt ends nor the ribs need anything else, but Bogart's offers up several sauces for your use. Of the four, the Sweet Maegan Ann is my favorite, with its sweet molassesy goodness mixing in very well with pulled pork (which does need something else). My wife is a very saucy lass, and she threw the Voodoo and the Vinegar in there as well. 

As always, sides are an afterthought to meat, and Bogart's could honestly serve slaps to my face along with those ribs and I'd still come back for more. Thankfully for my already misshapen face, they've got a delicious deviled egg potato salad, some nice pickles, beans, and slaw instead. 

To sum up: 

Come here. Get ribs, burnt ends and some sides (more than you think you need of everything). Eat all of this food on the picnic tables outside. Listen to the blues covers coming out of the speakers. Enjoy the beautiful day and our place atop the food chain, because at one point in human history we were just gnawing on berries and sticks. And barbecue is better than that. 
_____________

*Don't think we don't remember that summer.

Forget cowboying up. Personally, I prefer to burger up before I do anything at all, and that certainly includes before consuming prodigious amounts of bourbon. 

I'm not sure there's a better choice for a gigantic group of dudes to have dinner. We were seated in the outdoor patio under a few heat lamps, and the staff here handled us like pros: offering advice when it was needed (which included when to urinate outdoors), kept the alcohol flowing,* and brought us plate after plate of excellent eats. 

We started with the habanero wings (not as hot as you'd think, but fantastic), fried pickles, fried mushrooms and more. They've got some great sauces, which I always appreciate: the blue cheese dressing was legit, the honey mustard fantastic, and the homemade Jack Daniels ketchup good on everything, especially the motherfucking TRUFFLE FRIES. With sliced parmesan on top, those things rocked, and the sweet potato and the house fries were nothing to sneeze at either. 

And of course, we ate burgers. Grassfed, juicy burgers. Cooked correctly, well-proportioned to the bun, and flavorful. Not the best I've ever had by any means, but damn good nonetheless. Our waiter made no bones about the fact that the Woodstock was the move, but I must say the pimento cheese option was no slouch. Having tasted both, I'd be hard-pressed to pick between the two. 

Basically, Burger Up held up their end of the bargain: If you put a dish in the name of your restaurant, it has to be good. And it was. 
_________

*Be warned. If you ask for a double bourbon on the rocks, you are basically going to get a pint glass of bourbon. Two in, I was a mess.

This was the best cheesesteak I've eaten in Philly. And admittedly, my experience with Philly cheesesteaks is somewhat limited, but I assure you that my meat and cheese sandwich résumé is quite impressive. And this was a damn good sandwich. Onions, mushrooms, provolone...perfect. 

We only got a few weird looks when my buddy jokingly mentioned he would beat his girlfriend for one of these. I think he was joking. I wouldn't beat his girlfriend for one of these. Well, maybe I would if I could take her, but she's a big woman.

Look, I'm going to level with you. I don't remember everything that happened at Cane & Table.* Here's what I do remember:

1. Crispy. Rum. Ribs. Even if ribs aren't your favorite food (like they are mine), you can't argue with this dish. Eat them and rejoice.

2. We ordered everything on the left side of the menu. Nothing was bad, but there was some sort of curry dish that was OUTSTANDING. Just order all the curry things, and you're bound to find it.

3. I drank a lot of mezcal.** They make nice mezcal cocktails.

4. Somewhere along the line, I realized this joint used to be Pravda. Well, I'm glad it's Cane & Table now.
_____________

*Not because I drank too much. Just because I have a terrible memory. 
**Wait, maybe it was because I drank too much.

At least once in their life, everyone should partake in the pleasure that is a jazz brunch.

While Muriel's might not serve the best food in the French Quarter, their brunch is an experience anyone with a soul will enjoy. After all, this might be the only time in your life that it's acceptable to eat veal, or a pork chop, or pecan-crusted drum first thing in the morning. 

My alligator hash and her andouille omelette were solid, if a bit overpriced. (Don't be frightened by the gator; it's in tasty sausage form, and you wouldn't know what it was if they didn't tell you.) The flavors were good, but the eggs (poached and scrambled) were overcooked. 

But although I might not revisit either of our entrees, I would GLADLY start any day with Muriel's Bloody Mary and the ridiculously rich crawfish and goat cheese crepes. That's the move here. 

The band starts the party and keeps it going, and in between songs you'll see that they are not only talented performers, but genuinely good guys as well. Not realizing my absolute ineptitude with all instruments, the leader asked if I wanted to sit in on bass. I declined, but offered him some of my Bloody Mary. Now we are best friends forever and ever. 

And ever.

If you're in need of some real food in Fishtown around midnight, the late night menu at Interstate is as good as many regular menus.

We drove in late and got down with a legitimately fantastic burger that was more rare than medium rare (juicy as fuck), chicken fingers, guacamole, and various draft beers (anything from sours to stouts to bocks to IPAs to hefeweisens). They call this a drafthouse for a reason. 

You can turn any of those beers you order into a beer and a shot too. I don't think they actually have beer/shot combos, but you just order a shot and there you go. Stay for too many rounds with your friends and you may hear a story you didn't want to about using Nair inappropriately. 

The only thing I don't like about Interstate is that they have Hunt's ketchup. What is that nonsense? Heinz, people. It's the only real ketchup. Don't mess with a good thing.

Crispy, fatty chunks of salty bacon (strewn about so liberally that many morsels littered the surrounding plate), buttery eggs and melted cheese laid upon a flaky, freshly baked croissant...this is breakfast sandwich perfection. 

I wouldn't change a thing.

Get there early though, because I can certainly see how the wait might become excessive as they get busier. However, if this one menu item is any indication, Merchant is worth waiting for. After an evening of excess, that pancetta croissant will be the best $5 you've ever spent. 

And even though she may have declined food, bring your lady friend a macchiato. She deserves it considering she basically carried your fat ass home last night.

When I was young(er) and dumb(er), I made an older, wiser friend. He watched me consume a wretched bodega "po' boy" with disgust, and insisted we go get a real sandwich. He took me to Domilise's.

It's been a couple of years, so I was worried that nostalgia and high expectations were going to lead to disappointment, but Domilise's still makes the best shrimp po' boy in New Orleans. This makes it the best worldwide. If you are keeping track, that puts it up with the best sandwiches in existence.

Dressed, with plenty of Cristal, it's untouchable. The French bread is impeccable, the shrimp crisp yet tender, the pickles, hot sauce and everything else culminating in bite after bite of sublime tastiness that will make you hate yourself for ever eating anything else.

The prices have creeped up over the years, but good seafood is worth paying for. If you don't think so, then you've never exploded from both ends from eating the wrong mussels. And I hope you never will.

It isn't fancy. It isn't formal. It isn't particularly well-decorated. The plates are not elegantly garnished. And your meal will not be the flawless experience you might be expecting from one of the more upscale establishments. However, the staff is warm and genuine, and most importantly, the food is hearty and satisfying. 

The Louisiana Bistro is a magnificent specimen of that rare, elusive beast, the local joint hidden in plain sight...smack in the middle of a touristy part of the city. You can tell because they have actual, serious regulars. A diner might receive a hug from his waiter as he leaves, a passing mention that they will be closed on his regular night next week, or even simply a yelled, "Bye Gary!" as he walks out the door. 

I must admit that it isn't a perfect meal; some asparagus might arrive mushy and overcooked, and the bread might be a bit stale. But these things can be overlooked as overall, the food is excellent. For instance, the BBQ Shrimp off the bp Menu (covered in a mysterious black goo)* are an intensely flavorful riff on, as well as the best I've had of the New Orleans staple. The Drum Meunière is absolutely perfect. 

And yes, the Feed Me Menu is a must-try, if you're hungry enough. The chef personally comes over to your table and discusses your tastes with you, and then designs the meal specifically for your palate based on what fresh ingredients he has in the back. This tasting option is the reason why the staff is bluntly up-front about whether or not they will be able to accommodate you when you walk in. Because such attention to detail takes time. 

Admittedly, it might seem like rudeness when they tell you they simply can't seat your table right now, or will seat you, but won't be able to take your order for a few minutes. However, I like to think that they are really just looking out for the customers they are already serving, and making sure they don't put too much strain on the kitchen. 

So maybe the Louisiana Bistro isn't particularly polished. But the food is really, really good. That's what matters to me; if it's what matters to you, I'd recommend you stop by.
___________

*A cutesy, tongue-in-cheek reference to the oil spill. bp = Bitch, Please.

As soon as I walked in, I said it reminded me of Essex St. Market in NYC...but as I kept walking, I realized it was just bigger and better (and I love the Essex market). This place blew me away. If you can't find something to eat here, you are going to have to turn in your digestive system. You don't deserve it. 

The smells, the colors, it's completely overwhelming. I saw amazing prices on everything from fish to fruit to beautiful NY strips ($10.99/lb). If I wasn't hopping on a train for an hour back to NYC, I would've stocked up for sure. 

Somehow I got talked into eating an enormous roast pork hero from Dinic's with delicious spicy peppers all over it. For breakfast. And it was phenomenal.

Since watching the Beer Wars documentary I've been a strong supporter of the smaller breweries. Although I'm pretty against The Big Three (Bud, Miller, Coors) which make up about 85 percent of the market share, I took a "when in Rome" type attitude in St. Louis...plus the tour was on my buddy Abby's bucket list.

 I've been on a few of these tours before and have concluded that they're generally not as cool as they sound. It's usually about an hour of boring science talk when half way through I realize that I don't really care how it's made...I just like to drink it. 

Well the Bud tour actually kept me pretty intrigued throughout the entire thing. Between the Clydesdale horses, the Dalmatians, facts about the bottling and packaging process, and free samples at the end, this tour was excellent for guys like me with a short attention span. Best part of all...the whole thing is completely free! 

If in the STL. I think if there's one thing to check out the Bud tour would have to be it. 

Oh yeah...minus one star for the World Series pokes. As a Cubs fan I was not amused.

The "Streetcar Roll".....my guilty pleasure. Always great service and even better food when I visit. I only come a couple times a year, but I'm always satisfied. They're open late so that's always a plus when you're looking for a good meal late night. I'd definitely recommend you give them a try if you haven't already have!!

Had some time to kill before a movie so popped in for some sustenance. Was seated promptly and then waited for 8 mins for a server. No apologies. Ordered te cue bacon burger and he asked me what temp i wanted it and i answered med rare. While i waited i glanced around. This would be a great place to watch sports as there are lots of tvs. Burger came and i couldnt believe that the fries were piping hot right out of the fryer. I didnt have to send them back. I was impressed. However with that said, the burger was overcooked to well done and lacking any cue sauce as advertised.  The tobacco onions tasted like they had been prepped and fried hours ago. But it still tasted pretty good over all and they got high points for the smokin hot fries. The arnold palmer was adequate but needed more tea in the mix. The peppered bacon was outstanding.

It was such a great spot for brunch. I gave them a 4.5 stars instead. The .5 deduction was for one of the servers' clumsiness who accidentally spilled some water on my friend's shirt. When we got to the restaurant, the hostess informed us that there would be an hr wait for a table. The hostess told us to give them one of our phone numbers so they can notify us through text when the table is ready. Afterward, we walked around the area and checked out Vanderbilt University's campus.We didn't have much luck this time that we really waited for an hr. I think we got out table around 1:30ish. We ordered 2 sangria since they do 2 drinks for 1 price for sunday brunch...sweet We started off ordering red velvet waffles and buffalo cauliflower to share. 5 min later after our server took the order, another server came to us with a plate of pretzel pancakes. He goes, we made a mistake and we're gonna give this to you guys for free. We're like..wow cool..why not haha We felt so lucky on that day even though we waited for a long time. It was a very charming restaurant with couch seating inside and a full bar. I noticed the floor was a bit slippery when I was walking to the bathroom. I think they should put some carpet around that area. Our server was a good listener. She seemed very friendly and got what we needed very quickly.

Sangria: refreshing & fruity; big glass size; I barely finished the whole drink

Red Velvet Waffle: a big flat waffle that can sliced into 4 triangles; topped with cream cheese glaze; maple syrup on the side; the most instagrammable dish;)

Buffalo Cauliflower: fried cauliflower covered with buffalo sauce; served with blue cheese dressing on the side; very filling; big size cauliflowers; great portion for sharing; spicy- I requested to make it more mild spicy but unfortunately they couldn't.

Pretzel Pancakes: served with 3 big pieces of pancakes and topped with pretzels & sugar powder; white chocolate mousse on the side; filling; sweet & salty; interesting pancake idea.

Have been here a few times and it is ok, not the best in the city but consistent. Today I tried multiple times calling to make a simple reservation, was put on hold TWO different times and also hung up on after holding for over 12 minutes. The second time I was on hold for over 10 minutes as well even though they said it would be quick and "walked" the phone to the hostess person. Horrible, no tunes on hold. Nobody checking in, nobody caring. Go somewhere else.
Amazing food. Stellar atmosphere. Excellent live entertainment. I can't say enough nice things about this place.

The happy hour here is fantastic. Half price all spreads and breads, flatbreads, and $5 craft cocktails. There's also some beer specials, but I can't recall those. We started with a beer and I got the LA cocktail with mescal, jalapeno, honey, and SoCo. If drinks with a little spice are up your alley the way they are mine, get that drink! It was so good. A little on the sweet side, but the spice cut through it perfectly. 
We also had the BBQ pork flat bread and the spinach and artichoke spread. I loved the flatbread; perfectly done naan covered with pork and grilled pineapples. The spread had a great taste, but was a little difficult to eat as a dip. Regardless, I absolutely love artichoke hearts and the large chunks of them in the dip made me really happy. 
As usual, we ate too many appetizers so we didn't even get a chance to try any of the sandwiches or tandoori meats, but we will certainly be back to try both.

So, this has definitely be on one of my favorite places to go to for happy hour. The food and drinks are always wonderful. I decided to have my birthday get-together here and we all had such a great time. The service was phenomenal and they were really accommodating to a larger group of people. I would recommend this place to anyone; I've never been disappointed and always can't wait to come back!

Mmmmm!  Raining today and needed some comfort food. I love the Moneyball, it simple, but so delicious. Sausage gravy on biscuits with egg over easy. The key---great ingredients and made with love. Reminds me of my dad's biscuits and gravy and I think that is why I love this place so much. Of course when I let the family I was coming over here. I got a lot of to go orders by text from them. I ate in with a friend and took home two orders of sausage biscuits and gravy with fried chicken, 2 cinnamon bourbon rolls and a lemon rhubarb pop tart.  Came home with the goodies and got hugs from the family. So good to see these restaurants still open.

The China Pasta House cooks up the most authentic Chinese food I have had yet in town.  If you go, you can expect to run into many Chinese students from the U of A, and that just totally proves that the food here is reasonably priced, tasty, and authentic enough to keep these discerning customers coming back again and again.
