There is no fancy décor and no real formal service to speak of in this family owned restaurant (there's only three of them running the whole thing), but then again, you aren't paying for that either.  The owner is very nice, and she works hard to give you the best of what they are good at, which is authentic Chinese home styled cuisine that is very close to what I could get at a restaurant in China or Taiwan. 

The restaurant specializes in a variety of steamed buns, dumplings, and noodles. The price is very inexpensive, considering the quantity of food you get; it's such a great deal for the money!  I have not had the chance to try all the items on the menu yet, but I keep coming back to order new items every time.  During the past few months, they've added more rice dishes to the menu, but the menu on their website has not been updated to reflect this yet. There are a few dishes I personally love.  This includes the Scallion Pei, Braised Rice, Spicy Fried Rice Cake with Shrimp, and Spicy Hot Pot. When they mark a dish as "Spicy," it is.  Personally, I love the spicy items especially the dishes with Szechuan Peppercorn or "Ma" flavor. Love it. So, for the folks who like spicy food and are open to new experiences, I would recommend you give these spicy dishes a try! 

I keep coming back for the food. The authentic Chinese home-styled dishes, reasonable prices, and generous portion sizes fills a unique niche and I cannot get food like this anywhere else in Tucson!!

This is a definitely hidden gem in the Rittenhouse area.  You would just walk by if you didn't know about it.

TL;DR: Fresh sushi at a cozy and clean place you wouldn't even notice.

Miso soup: Very tasty with a lot of tofu chunks.  Definitely not watery like some other places

Yakitori: The chicken is very juicy, not dry or burned.  Perfect with the teriyaki sauce.

Kei Sashimi: Good variety and very fresh.  Not sure why they have a cooked shrimp in, but I don't mind.  I would absolutely order that again once I've tried other items.

Forget about all of the noise of opening night; forget about the special sauces and toppings; let's talk about the burger itself: happy, grass-fed, hormone-free beef (cool, I'm into this), over-worked and tightly-packed into a super dense, meatball-esque patty (hmm...), over-cooked to a uniform grey (yuck!), but without that crispy char that can make you almost forgive a well-done burger. Two burgers and a side of fries: $26. Shoulda got that PYT Groupon...

My wife and I attended the first weekend after opening...it was busy and clearly they're were many wrinkles to iron out. 

Servers were polite, but it seemed like our main server had a training server with him, which was awkward because our main server didn't seem to have it perfected yet. 

The hostess was also polite, but I felt her outfit was a bit to provacative for a younger lady (maybe I'm old school??). The managers were swarming all over the place looking disheveled, and frustrated...which I can understand being a new place, but if you're opening a higher priced restaurant, you should be hiring higher priced managers for fluency. And, I'm into style...so all managers should be wearing the same thing. Not one with a sweater, and the other with a baggy loose fitting suit. Dress the role for success. 

Scenery looked great. Decor looked great. Setup was great. 

Food...overall, was good (not great). Tuna Tartar was good. Salmon entree was good. I had the lasagna...not so good. Arrived in a pan, loaded with cream sauce and soggy noodles. Not what I expected. 

Lastly, I do not like the branding. The name TECA was on every plate and on the wine glasses...really?? 

Overall, it was pricey for mediocre food and service. I'll go back once more hoping for a better experience that all wrinkles are ironed out. I'll update a new review as well.

I absolutely love this place!!! Rick Lewis has the midas touch and is the nicest guy!!!

I finally made it here for the 1st time yesterday afternoon, a little after 3pm. I wish I returned today for the duck meatloaf. I'll definitely be returning very soon. 

The setup is charming and welcoming. It's an all wood finish with a great music mix in the background. As soon as you walk in the door, you're greeted, you order at the bar counter. The young lady with the spunky blonde & blue hair is amazzzzzzing!!! She is extremely welcoming and knowledgeable regarding  both the food and drink menus. She represents the front of the house well.

We tried the catfish (regular), available in spicy, which I'm trying in the future. We ordered the turkey leg, collard greens, cornbread, sweet potatoes, butter beans, roasted cauliflower, a chicken wing and a cocktail. Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious!!! Everything was well  seasoned and beyond flavorful!! It all came to the table piping hot. The turkey leg was fall off the bone tender. My catfish nuggets were incredibly tender and flakey. I have to say every side we ordered was magnificently prepared and delicious!!!

This restaurant represents southern style comfort food at it's finest. I'm returning for the ribs, duck meatloaf and fried bologna. I've been spreading the word about this hot spot.

Originally went here when it was Seafood Exchange. We went a few times, and each time the quality went down. When Crabby Bill's went in, we were not going to go, assuming is would be similar quality to Seafood Exchange. Anyhow .. our son requested to go to Crabby Bills (he loves the corn hole and the patio seating) so we obliged.

Exceeded expectations. The food and presentation of the food was much better, than we had experienced during the end of Seafood Exchange. 

Had:
Grilled Octopus Salad -- YUM, large portion of octopus on a bed of lettuce with some potato salad.
Chicken Cesar Salad -- husband rates it as, MEH, 3 stars. (but the Chicken Alfredo came out at another table and looked fantastic)
Simply Calamari -- little guy ordered this, looked good, fried and calamari, he was happy.
Fried Oysters -- Yes, this was fantastic. 

Yes, will go back, probably will not be on the weekly rotation, but we will not ignore it like we previously did.

When I think of Korean BBQ, I look no further than Bando restaurant. For ~$30 you get unlimited chicken, kalbi , bulgogi, pork belly, brisket, AND dozens of banchan side dishes. Did I mention the banchan is also unlimited? To my knowledge, no other Korean bbq restaurant in Indy offers unlimited both meat and banchan 

Don't underestimate the banchan because it isn't meat either! They adds such an interesting layer of flavor to the whole bbq! You get sweet, sour, crunchy, spicy, savory, soft, a truly endless combination of flavors to an otherwise savory BBQ.

I don't consider myself an expert in Korean food, but I hope my perspective may help those who are more foreign to kbbq

My husband and I had a nice time at Finch & Fork.

As vegetarians, the mains on the menu are exclusively meat but we did small plates and still ate well. We started with the cheese plate, which is my only negative because it wasn't very varied in flavors (I'm guessing it was white chedder, asiago and manchego maybe?) but it was still delicious and a nice presentation. 

We also had:
- Deviled eggs minus the trout
- Fries
- Mushroom flatbread
- Macaroni and cheese minus the bacon

They are happy to remove meat items from dishes to make them vegetarian. My husband also had a fig-infused bourbon drink which he liked, and the pickled vegetables at the start of the meal are a nice touch. The service was relatively slow for a Tuesday in my opinion, but maybe this is just a laid-back pace type of place. If you're looking for a nice dinner spot in Santa Barbara I would definitely check out Finch & Fork.

I'm definitely a fan. 

I was tasked with choosing a restaurant in Santa Barbara for myself, my boyfriend and another couple. Finding a place you think might please everyone is a bit tough, and in the end Seven seemed to ride a fine line--not too expensive or too casual with food that could please everyone.

When we got there around 7:30pm on a Saturday it was full, but instead of having us put in our name the guy who I'm assuming was the manager made it his goal to find us a table (i.e. great, friendly service right off the bat). He pulled up bar seats from the outdoor patio bar and sat us a at a teeny square table outside. Our table had zero lighting, but we used our smart phone flashlights and made the most out of it. The fact that this small, dimly lit table wasn't ideal yet my experience still easily gets a four-star rating attests to the food, service and ambiance of this place. 

Overall the patio is cute and has several built-in booths with cushioned seats, pillows and built-in lighting. They have a nice draft list (Allagash White for the win!) at $6 each. The menu consists of gastro pub-y sandwiches, burgers, appetizers, etc. The seven deadly sins-themed sandwiches are each $12 (I think?) and they all come with fries. I got Lust (chicken breast, fresh pesto, carmelized onions on nice sliced wheat bread put on a panini press) and it was huge and delicious with a heaping helping of thin, yummy fries. My boyfriend got the Anger (basically a Cuban) and dayum did I wish I had ordered that. It was fantastic. Our dining partners were happy with the chicken and waffles half order ($9) and the Gluttony sandwich, but I would caution a hungry eater to order the full chicken and waffles order. Overall this is a really neat place and I'll be back.

Note: They checked our IDs at the door, so since this place is bar-centered it's possible it's only for 21+ on weekends? Around 9pm a band started and at that point it got a bit loud for a date/casual dinner, but the plus is they don't charge cover.

So I had to come to St. Petersburg for a business trip and stopped by my fave restaurant for a quick bite to eat with the girls and the service was good as usual but the food was ahhhhhhhh not so good this time. First of all they stopped serving the shrimp cocktail in a martini glass. They don't de-vain them anymore either. Yuck!! They serve them on a black plastic plate which is shaped like a fish on a bed of lettuce with no cocktail sauce. The cocktail sauce is now located on the table in a ketchup bottle?? It is warm which is not so good it makes the shrimp warm when you dip them into it. The chowder is always amazing is was definitely up to par yesterday. It is some of the best chowder I've ever put my sweet lips on. I had the usual mild blackened flounder. It was a nice piece of fish it is usually served with 2 sides i always get a double rice pilaf the girls always eat it all. The place is slipping just a little. It did not seam to be busy at all. That is very untypical for this place its always packed and you cant get in for all the people. It was good not great like it usually is.

All in all I was impressed by Superior Seafood! Superior Seafood originally caught my eye because they have a large gluten free menu and one of my dining companions can't eat gluten. We made a reservation on Opentable for 6:00 and when we arrived at 6:05, the place was packed (I was very happy that I made a reservation!). We had to wait 5-10 minutes for our table but we got to sit right before the end of happy hour. I ordered a frozen pomegranate mojito (you get a large for the price of a small during happy hour - $7) and my boyfriend had a Port Orleans beer ($3 drafts during happy hour).

For our entrees, I ordered the pecan crusted drum, my boyfriend ordered the blackened fresh catch with grits and potatoes, and our other 2 dining companions ordered the blackened catch and the salmon. I really appreciated that the waitress made sure we knew that you can sub the sides for any of the fish dishes (since sides are a deciding factor for me). After dinner we split a flourless chocolate cake for dessert, that came with vanilla ice cream and raspberry sauce. It was very yummy as well!

All of us really enjoyed our meal! While it isn't the cheapest restaurant (fish entrees are around $20-22), I felt like we got enough food for the price. Just keep in mind that it gets very busy during happy hour (3-6:30 everyday) so make a reservation ahead of time and be prepared for it to be pretty loud.

Food - 4 stars 
Price - 3.5 stars
Service - 4 stars
Atmosphere - 4 stars

I was so excited that District Donuts was coming to Lakeview so I had to check them out on the first day they opened (don't judge me I was in the area and needed donuts!!!!!)

The first thing that I noticed is that the space is very airy and comfortable! I also love the big windows so it gets lots of natural light! The donuts/ sliders/ breakfast items seemed to be the same as their Magazine street location, which I was very happy about.

I got the nutella donut, a fried chicken slider, and shared an order of fries with my boyfriend. My boyfriend also got the maple bacon donut and the cheeseburger slider. While they had some problems with the orders, these are absolutely kinks that they were still working out (it was their first day open after all) and the staff was super friendly and helpful with fixing everything! The waffle fries were so so so good and they gave you a decent sized portion! I also loved my nutella donut (stuffed with nutella with bananas on top) and my boyfriend was crazy about his maple bacon donut! He didn't particularly like the cheeseburger slider because he said that the roll it was served on didn't taste right with it but he's also super picky so I'm probably blaming him on this one! Once again, my major issue with District is that the slider prices are too expensive (around $4 for a tiny bite of food!!!!). However, I will probably be happy getting their fries and donuts next time instead! I also love their buttermilk drops so I recommend those as well!

Update: the cheese fries with jalapenos (they are a little sweet) are crazy good and the salad is a light refreshing option that is a good sized portion! Both great alternatives to the sliders and yummy additions to your donut choice for the day!

Food -- 4.5 stars
Price -- 3.5 stars
Service -- 5 stars
Atmosphere -- 5 stars

Flamingo A-Go-Go is a good spot in the warehouse district for getting together with a group of friends for drinks and to sit outside. I personally wouldn't classify Flamingo A-Go-Go as a necessary go to restaurant but I enjoyed my experience there.

I visited with 3 friends (and a dog) on a Friday night for a late happy hour. Our reason for picking this spot was because it was the dogs birthday (DON'T JUDGE) and they have puppy plates! The puppy plates are $3 and are little dog sized portions of human foods, it really was so adorable. The dog LOVED her meal so that's a plus!

Anyway onto the people experiences. They have a nice selection of cocktails, beers, and wines that are priced well. I ordered the froze, which I was a little nervous about trying, but I enjoyed it. My friends all decided to order wine and beer because we've heard the flock tails are over the top sweet. The menu is a little all over the place, which may work if your group is interested in different things. My friends ordered sandwiches, which they liked, but the real winner was the garlic Parmesan fries that I stole all of! Those were delicious! 

Overall I like Flamingo A-Go-Go for a great patio, affordable drinks, and a good vibe. If that's what you're looking for then I recommend giving it a try!

Food - 4 stars
Drinks - 4 stars
Price - 4 stars
Atmosphere - 4.5 stars

Totally different movie experience.
Wow all I can say is wow!!!!!!

It's about time Tucson gets with the act. Roadhouse Cinemas it's been a long time coming. The staff is friendly from the ticket box to the Theater servers. Has to be one of the cleanses venues in Tucson. The remodel looks fresh and clean stylish and welcoming. 

So what's the big deal you ask. 
A food menu with everything from mozzarella sticks, pizza, burgers, ice cream and even a hummus platter. They serve soda in glassware and popcorn in a stainless steel mixing bowl classy. The seats are set in pairs and are numbered. They are set up with food trays lite with a very discrete LED light. Set up with salt, pepper, napkins and everything else you'll find at any restaurant table. The seats themselves are leather recliner's but the best part was the call button that summons your personal server.

It gets better!!!!!!!
Beer Wine Spirits Cocktails 
Yes a full blown liquor license. 
Beers are all microbrew from the local area. Fourpeaks on tap.
My wife had her first real gimlet in this city with Rose's lime cordial.
 Honestly hand to God it was better than the one served to her by JW Marriott (trust me I'm a bartender). 

Here are some tips Tucson 
1. Respect this place. 
2. Don't complain about the high prices. 
You get what you pay for and it's a steel 
3. Don't vandalize this place was graffiti or "artwork"
4. Don't miss treat or be rude to any of its employees or servers.

Please can we have something nice in the city for once.

As for you Roadhouses Cinemas 
I love you and, thank you for bringing some middle-class class to this city.

I can understand the lukewarm reviews, despite the Hilton El Conquistador being a beautiful resort with excellent rooms and amenities that will make for a relaxing trip. 

Maybe it's paying $3.80 for ONE Diet Coke in the Lobby shop. Maybe it's the confusing layout that has one lugging their bag from the parking lot (full most of the time) to their room. Maybe it's the underwhelming quality of the internal conference catering. It just doesn't give customer service that matches the price. 

However, there are many excellent elements, from the pool and jacuzzi, the outdoor area (perfect for receptions or company parties), large rooms ample for large conferences, excellent on-property restaurant options, nice trails (Oro Valley and Linda Vista), a great golf course, relaxing spa, comfortable beds, and a helluva view. 

I went there for a conference ... me and the 500-or-so attendees had excellent facilities to listen to symposium guests and do interviews. 

I recommend stocking up on groceries before arriving, unless you're rich, then go ahead and pay through the nose for room service.

In the end, it's a nice place to stay in Tucson...

I always equated "gelato" with "nutritious" ... or, at least, more nutritious than ice cream. I can't imagine, however, this tasty, decadent, flavorful, smooth, cool treat is anything less than the fattiest, creamiest, best pile of frozen goodness this side of a Baskin-Robbins. Well, I'm wrong, it's gelato ... yummy, yummy, gelato. 

First recommendation: Go early in the day, like, really, 11 a.m. if you want to see these three-dimensional, blooming works of art, flowering with fruits and with mountain ranges sculpted from the gelato.  It is a sight to see.  

And the flavors! Along with their flavors of the month, there's somewhere in the neighborhood of 60 (!) gelato flavors and a couple dozen sorbets. I had their Peanut Butter Crunch, which was smooth with natural peanut-buttery flavor and, unshockingly, plenty of crunch. 

You'll find several one-of-a-kind (or at least pretty dang rare!) flavors like Bailey's Irish Creme, Bourbon Butter Pecan, Alpencaramel, Pear Riesling, Cioccolato al Perperoncino (yeah, that's chocolate with a chili pepper), Guinness (!), Panna Cotta, Honey Lavender, Halwa, and about 20 more things you'll have to look up on your phone. 

And, of course, they have all the classics: Chocolate, Bubble Gum, Vanilla, Strawberry, Rum Raisin, Peppermint, Mint Chocolate Chip, etc.  

Even with all this decadence, I still found the price for a small gelato to be a bit high ... but the taste was fantastic!

Just phenomenal!! My bf and I both had our own appetizer and entree here, which never happens, because there were so many delicious meals we had to try! I can't recall exactly what the name of the appetizer was ( the menu changes frequently), but it had kimchi in it and it was so delicious. For my entree, I had the game hen with rice, which was out of this world. For dessert we ordered the white chocolate carrot cake-oh. Boy. This. Was. Fantastic. Needless to say, we left happy and full. 

We got to chat with the chef for a minute; when asked how he would describe the food, he said,"Whatever we feel like making"...so I don't know that I could give a better description of its ever-adapting menu. 

The restaurant is on the smaller side, I would definitely recommend a reservation prior to going-even on week nights. Huge plus: they're BYOB!! Not only did our server pop,pour, AND keep chilled our bottle of wine, it was all done without a corking fee!

The reputation & Yelp reviews led me to choose Bouchon for my birthday dinner. Wow, what a disappointment!

We (party of 2) arrived at our reservation time of 8:30pm. The hostess initially sat us at a beautiful 4-top on the patio, close to the entrance, and with plenty of space to relax. About 2 minutes later she came back and said she'd made a mistake, and that she needed the table for a party of four. In reality, a 2-top had just opened up (the table still need to be cleaned). We politely agreed to be moved, but ended up being squeezed into a very tight corner of the patio.  No apology. No offer of a round of drinks on-the-house for freeing up the larger table for them. Nothing. 

Our waiter was nice, but paid much more attention to the four local women at the table next to us.  When we ordered, he didn't bother to give us much detail on the dishes. The four women got detailed descriptions. 

We also asked for the wine steward, so he could recommend good pairings. What we got was another waiter who served wine. The four women got the Sommelier, even though they brought their own bottle of wine. 

The appetizers were OK at best. Heirloom tomato salad, and pork belly (although the waiter that served literally called it BACON!).

For the main course, I had the chicken over risotto. I was shocked when I took my first bite -- the chicken tasted like salted cardboard. That's how dry it was. It must have been forgotten in the oven, or left under a heat lamp.  It was not edible, though I will give them credit that the risotto was good (but not great). 

When I told the waiter, he was nice enough to offer to replace the dish with a fresh one, or exchange for a new dish.  I opted to switch to the white fish. When that finally arrived (and by that time my partner was done with his dish), it too was overcooked. 

My partner had ordered the duck, which is a signature dish for the restaurant. He said that the breast was quite rare, but the rest was overlooked. Even one of the women at the table next to us had to send her duck back, because she "preferred to eat it cooked."

Moving onto to desert, we decided to share the Molten Lava cake. This was actually the best tasting dish we had all night, so hats-off the the desert chef! To accompany desert, I ordered a coffee, which was really mediocre for a 5-star restaurant. It tasted like standard drip coffee without much boldness or flavor. 

But worse than that, when my partner ordered chamomile tea, the waiter brought a little teapot of hot water and an empty cup with a Tazo tea bag (still in the wrapper) sitting in it! Really?? This is the best they could do??? 

All during the meal, we had an assortment of empty glasses stacking up on the table. Even though the waiter, busboy, and wine-waiter had all been by our table several times throughout the night, not one bothered to clear an empty glass. We literally had to ask them to do it.  

To cap off a really below-average birthday dinner, they didn't even put a candle on the desert, when the reservation clearly listed it was a birthday. And to make matters even worse, when the waiter presented the check, he apologized for the overcooked chicken, and said that he had asked the manager to remove it from the check. However, when my partner looked at the check, we were still being charged for both the chicken & the fish entrees.  We had to point this out to the waiter on the check, because he clearly had not reviewed it himself.  And when we did, he removed it from the check himself, no manager involved. 

Overall, a huge disappointment. And based on my experience, I would certainly not recommend this restaurant to anyone.

This restaurant is in an odd location in upper darby and looked like an old renovated diner but you can't miss the bright sign that stood out front 
Dining area was nice they had two rooms, one being a little larger. The buffet was to the right of the entrance with fresh meats, seafood, sides and etc
Soda machines and large rice cookers was at the end. 
I was a little skeptical about all the meat being displayed on a buffet line but it was all chilled. 
We were seated promptly and served a pitcher of cold water and our grill started. Our server gave us the basic run down on menu and price 
I immediately went for the bulgogi (brisket instead of ribeye as is traditional) and the kalbi with the kimchi, lettuce, and rice to make my Korean Wraps
The grill was nice and hot and switched out often when we were finished grilling each "round"
The kalbi/galbi was amazing!! Full size ribs grilled then cut into bite size pieces, perfectly marinated!
The bulgogi was good but the spicy pork was alot more tender and I liked the flavor more in a wrap
We ate and ate and ate, it was delicious!! And I loved that the Kimchi was authentic and spicy red so many places dilute it and I hate that
I will definitely be back again and soon even though it takes me an hour in traffic!!

I cant believe that I didn't write this review sooner! I went here in August 2020, 5 months ago and can't wait until I can come again!
We took Lyft from the French Quarter and everything was a Covid19 Guideline Set Up with very limited tables. They took orders at the counter, then we waited in the back until our order was ready. Once our name was called, we picked up our food then sat at one of the tables.
We ordered the large fried shrimp po' boy sandwich which was overflowing with shrimp!! it can definitely be shared by 2-3 people! we also got the medium shrimp remoulade with fried green tomato po boy and it was so tasty! I loved that one! The onion rings were great and of course finishing it up with the locally made Barq's root beer was perfect
It's worth the drive (15-25min depending on traffic) its a little outside the city, but its worth it. Its a small restaurant, very casual and serving great generous portion food.
Going back again in a few months...

Very short drive from NJ, about 10-15min on a Sunday morning and easy to locate. Parking wasn't too bad either but we also came at 8:30am
Normally we would sit inside but it looked crowded so we sat outside under an umbrella. There was a nice breeze so it felt great and relaxing!
The tables are a little tight and you can hear everyone's conversations but I wasn't here to talk I just wanted to try the amazing food that I have been hearing about lol
The Lady at the front desk was pleasant along with all the wait staff, everyone was attentive and accommodating! We didn't have to ask for anything before it was delivered
The menu looked great! My husband got the Steak n Eggs with Potatoes and Cheese Grits and I ordered the Creme Brulee French Toast! and Peach Tea (not too sweet with hint of peach)
It didn't take long for the food to be served, and I was so impressed! The food is so pretty with great presentation and it tasted amazing!!
The Creme Brulee Fr Toast was perfectly paired with the Fruit and the French Vanilla Glaze! Nice Brulee Crunch on Some Pieces of the Toast
The Steak was perfect medium and tender and the Cheese Grits???? The creamiest cheesiest grits they were amazing!
I was so happy we finally came it was a delicious beginning to our Sunday

To sum up my new favorite restaurant:

-steak (and other meaty goodness)
-great local beer
-good wine
-great concept
-excellent service
-reasonable prices for all the above

The Block is a great asset to Webster Groves, and it's my new favorite. Sit in the bar and get a dozen other specials they only serve in the bar. Closer to the beer and a bigger menu? Sold.

The Block, I love you.

This review is purely directed at management -- service, beer, food apps were all great.

We used the $13 Groupon for two flights and an app ($28 value) -- in no where on the Groupon did it mention we would be forced to pay a 20% gratuity for a party of 2.  Plus, the 20% was $6 -- do I need to get out a calculator for anyone?  Very shady, very disappointed, and will not be coming back to give my business to a company like this.

Why not mention it at the beginning of the service?  Or, better yet, on the Groupon itself?  Disappointed indeed.

Service is horrible, but best Cuban sandwich ($7.50) I've ever had (including Cubanos from Miami and Puerto Rico) make it worth the wait.  Large portions on everything and great prices.  Not very many tables either so maybe don't go at peak time.  Great whole in the wall dive, I will definitely be back.

PS. As there are no signs explaining anything in the restaurant, what you need to do is (1) order from the open counter, (2) keep your ticket, sit, and wait for your food, (3) pay at the cashier counter.

Awww, man. I had high hopes for this place as it has many high marks and is in the neighborhood of my childhood.  The menu had me salivating, but then came the HUGE cockroach crawling on the wall above the cooktop and moved toward us...and then back to the cooktop.  We alerted the waitress who then alerted the owner.  She showed absolutely no concern about the roach and did nothing about it, including offering an apology.  That came from the waitress.  The owner did walk by our table to go back to her conversation with 2 gents at the bar.  

The food took 30-40 min to arrive.  Mind you, there were only 6 people in this place split b/w 2 tables.  Food came and 2 orders were incorrect.  Red beans w/o rice was ordered, but of course, there was rice.  I'll excuse that.  My wife's shrimp order, along with our guest's order, only came with 6 shrimp - for a $15 shrimp plate. We asked how much for another order of just shrimp. Almost $7 dollars.  More than Two bucks a shrimp!!!  C'mon, man.  The Owner came over...FINALLY, but by request.  With a very aloof demeanor, she made sure to emphasize how much she pays for shrimp, by the pound, and that we were getting the "creme de la creme" and that there have NEVER been any complaints.  Yeah, ok.

We were all a bit surprise to her approach, really.  She should take notes of the interpersonal skills displayed by her waitress.  This young lady was on her "A" game and almost seemed to be trying to make up for her less than stellar employer.  

In closing, I'm glad a place like this exists in my old neighborhood, but there's a reason why so few people were there.  Besides the roach, the door by the bar with the black garbage bags and duck tape holding it on (bullet holes?) and the disappointing owner/manager, my fish was tasty.  I won't be visiting this place again, though.   Not even if it's free.  One of my guests was a childhood friend that still lives there.  She won't be there again, either.

Two great things happened when I visited Attico last weekend.

1. My party of 5 and I were at an outdoor dining spot before heading to Attico. As we were heading to a new spot, I decided to make a very very last minute reservation for Attico at 6:00 pm. Thank god, all the times were available, and I was able to get a confirmation. Once we got there, our 7th friend decided to join...but wait I only made a reservation for 6! Once we got upstairs, I kindly asked our hostess if there was any way possible, we would be able to get a chair for our 7th person. They said that they normally don't allow a 7th chair to be added on the outside, but they brought a chair over for us anyways. Score! I was so happy since this 7th person was my fiance's friend who I was meeting for the first time...didn't want to leave a bad impression. 

2. As soon as we got upstairs and were seated, literally within 10 minutes, it was POURING. But... wait til you hear the best part... the rooftop patio is covered!! They turned their rooftop patio into a tented patio! It was the most perfect thing ever considering it rained for like the 1.5 hours that we were there for. 

All in all, the drinks are good and they have taken all measures for covid-19 times. I would definitely recommend!

Until I ate at BrushFire, I was convinced I had eaten at the worst BBQ joint I would ever experience. BrushFire reminded me that you can still search for the bottom if you look hard enough (see BBQ baseline below). What surprised me was how highly regarded this place has been in the past. Makes me wonder if that is old news or this place dropped off the cliff fast. I will not go back...now, to the details:

To start on a positive note, the service was decent, not great. I would call it slightly below average. Not real welcoming, but not rude. The space is OK, not great. It was clean. It is in a strip mall; which, so is Smoky Mo's in Cedar Park, TX and I would eat there every week if I had the chance.

The food...

Smoked "Brisket" -- not sure this is smoked, nor brisket. But, it was the best thing we had and was eatable. But, they covered it with so much sauce, it was drowned and would never be able to come up for air. I order the hot sauce and it was so sweet it tasted like syrup. It was sort of like a molasses sauce but even sweeter like it has some artificial sugar flavor or a LOT of brown sugar and had a consistency of hot glue. The brisket was served on a garlic role kind of was like the bread you would get a SubWeighChainShop, but garlicky. Kind of doughy. Not great. Definitely not what I want to eat BBQ on...

Homemade BBQ Baked Beans -- READ: Bush's BBQ Beans with onions added. I almost looked for the can. Sweet and nasty. Wow, bad. Two bites and toss it.

Mac n Cheese -- Sour Mac? Pretty gross. Tasted like Kraft that had sat out all day. Uck.

Now, we reach the bottom....the BBQ Pulled Pork. Seriously, really bad. It tasted like a sloppy joe you got in the lunch room in grade school. Sweet and terrible. It was really bad. Once again, the "hot" sauce was so sweet it was sweet it was unreal. The meat quality on the BBQ pork was really bad. Lots of fat and gristle. And it was luke warm.  Food safety hazard?

The serve RED onions with the BBQ. Yes...RED! 

After we left, the person I was with said it was the first meal they remember in a long time that they wish they could throw up in the parking lot. If that is not grounds for 1 star, I am not sure what is...

I hope I never have to eat worse "BBQ" and I hope any BBQ enthusiast out there heeds this warning and steers clear because this shack needs a serious reboot.

It really calls into question Tucson BBQ in general now that Rod has moved on as this place has been voted best of several times....
---------------------

For the BBQ enthusiast looking for a baseline, here is my baseline in the BBQ landscape:

5 stars : Ruby's in Austin, TX; The Salt Lick in Driftwood, TX

4.5 stars: Smoky Mo's in Cedar Park, TX (the one on FM1431 & HW 183); Podnah's in PDX

4 Stars: Smoque in Chicago; GT's South in Indy; FoJay's in Omaha back in the day (closed); Hartland BBQ in Omaha currently; Po-Kee-Jo's in Austin (the old location with the barn)

3.75 Stars: Up in Smoke in Buffalo, WY; Smokehouse 21 in PDX

3.5 Stars: Rod's KC BBQ in Tucson; Honey Bear's in PHX (the Original on E. Van Bueren)

3 Stars: Smoke Daddy in Chicago; Best of the Famous Dave's BBQ locations; Ribs n' Bibs in Hyde Park; Brew BQ in Corvallis; Russel Street BBQ in PDX

2.5 Stars (would not go back): The County Line in Austin; Rudy's BBQ in Round Rock, TX on I-35; Average Famous Dave's BBQ

1 Star (Bottom of the Barrel): BrushFire BBQ in Tucson

"When in Rome......", so upon arrival in Philly, we headed straight to Geno's for a Philly Cheesesteak sandwich.   I took the advice of one Yelper and ordered the cheesesteak with peppers.  It was delicious!  Their fries were great, too, and served piping hot!  With almost 3,200 reviews this is certainly a Philly restaurant icon. 

Additionally, Geno's has been featured on the Food Network along with across the street rival Pat's. 
Who has the better Philly cheesesteak sandwich - Geno's or rival, Pat's?

Hubs wanted to introduce me to the Philly Cheesesteak sandwich so this was our first stop.  Pat's, as well as their across the street rival, have been showcased on the Food Network. On this late evening, there were plenty of patrons getting their cheesesteak fix.  With almost 4,000 reviews, much has been said!
Pat's sandwich has a gracious amount of chopped beef and drippy cheesey goodness, served on a fresh sub roll, served hot!  Delicious!  There piping hot fries are good, too!

Red Fish Grill is a casual, colorful restaurant with interesting artwork that give it a bit of a Jamaican vibe.  With 20 years of serving diners in NOLA, they seem to be good at what they're doing.  

We started with one of their signature appetizers, BBQ Oysters. These oysters are flash fried, and served with a drizzle of Crystal BBQ sauce and their homemade blue cheese. The oysters had a nice crunchy texture, but the sauces created more of a buffalo style flavor than BBQ.  

I ordered their signature Wood Fired Grilled Redfish with Lump Crab served atop a bed of Tasso ham, roasted diced potatoes, mushrooms with a lemon butter sauce. The fish was cooked perfectly delicious. The bed of mixed Tasso and vegetables was good not great. Also, they tout Lump Crab topping, however, Lump Crab is exactly that - lumps and chunks of crab.  Perhaps they shred the lump crab?  It made me question whether it was really Lump Crab.  

We all enjoyed a cocktail prior to dinner, but unfortunately no pics to show. Their cocktails were expertly crafted classics. Plenty of imported and local craft and domestic beer to choose from, ample wine list, as well as your desire of liquor drinks.  Cheers!

Mother's, founded in 1938 by a mother and son team, is a cafeteria type restaurant. It's not fancy, probably hasn't changed too much over the years, and serves breakfast all day long as well as Louisiana style comfort food.  If you expect a recently renovated, upscale modern restaurant you'll be disappointed. The line is long but moves fairly quickly. They handle crowds like pros, and will hand out their menus for you to peruse while waiting in line. They tout "world famous ham" along with being known for their Po Boy sandwiches. Their Po Boy sandwich history is interesting and you can read about it while you wait in line. There are a lot of menu options to read and choose from, as well as, restaurant history that intertwines with New Orleans history.  
We ordered plenty for sharing and here are the highlights:
*Their Shrimp Étouffée was delicious!  I'd definitely order again. 
*Best skin-on fried chicken I've had in a very long time and quite possibly the best I've ever had - sorry mom. Crunchy on the outside and tender moist on the inside. Consider an order or two for sharing if you have a large group. 
*Their ham they say is famous just didn't reach the delicious hype they advertise.  It was good, however, and a gracious portion. 
*Their red beans and rice side needed some salt, but it was delicious and authentic New Orleans. Additionally, it was plentiful with ham and sausage.  
*Yummy warm biscuits are made in house.  You can watch them at their biscuit making craft as they have a sidewalk window that lets you see them in action.
*They don't want their employees tipped, and there are signs posted as such.  
I'd certainly return to try their Shrimp Po Boy or have fried chicken and crawfish étouffée.
Cheers!

100% LEGIT!!!! i cant say enough about this place.....the food was amazing. All made from scratch  and its so obvious in the taste and quality. I had the juicy pork dumplings, mongolian lamb, Singapore noodles and the banana spring roll for dessert. Every single dish was outstanding...and fresh, not greasy at all. The owner Peter was so nice ..very attentive and welcoming. He made us feel at home. The restaurant and bathroom are very clean. The dishes are big enough for 2 people to share. I will definitely be returning i am so happy I stumbled upon this place. Oh i also had the tea flight i loved it. Next time I'm going to try the tea ceremony.
Note: this is NOT like chinese take out...its authentic quality food so the prices are higher with very good reason. I know good food so ignore the bad reviews

Great great wings ! Not too big not too small, crispy, juicy and the hot garlic sauce is so good and so is the Asian chili. I got the spinach salad with shrimp everything was fresh and there was tons of shrimp on it which I love and it's unusual because I usually only get like 6 shrimps on my salads. My wife got the roast beef sandwich it was pretty good but nothing special. It was crazy busy in there and so our waitress took a while to check on us or take orders but for as busy as it was she handled it very well. Very loud in there and def nothing fancy but I will definitely return for some wings.

I love coming here for Happy Hour - the pizzas are only $5 each, and you can add as many different sauces, cheeses, veggies, and meats as you'd like! I come here almost every week, and I've never been disappointed. The location is clean, the staff is friendly, and the food is delicious. Happy Hour is Monday through Friday from 2PM-5PM, and you really can't beat the amazing price for the quality food.

The restaurant is clean with a pub-like style to it. My fiance and I were excited to try some New York pizza, but as soon as we entered and saw the prices ($5 per slice!) we were a bit hesitant, but decided to at least try it out. We ordered a 10-inch pepperoni pizza and a medium drink that totaled out to be about $16. The pizza itself was delicious but the service was extremely dull and the workers did not seem at all pleasant. We were the only two people in this joint and only once did we see another potential patron and his son enter (only to turn around and leave once they saw the prices). Overall, the pizza was tasty but way too overpriced and the service did not at all compensate for anything. I wouldn't recommend this place to anybody - just walk a little more up the street and you'll find a friendlier and more affordable pizzeria. 

Also, don't lose your receipt or they won't give you your food when you come back up to grab it.

This place is amazing! When I first came here, I was a bit wary because of the old-fashioned look of the restaurant, but this place sure didn't disappoint.

Our waitress was very sweet and attentive. Our drinks were never empty, and everything was brought out hot. Their Fish & Chips dish is definitely the best I've ever had. The fish was extremely crispy, and the fries were deliciously seasoned. We also had the bacon popcorn, which was really interesting. Their prices were also very fair compared to the huge amount of food you get. 

Overall, this place is an awesome gem that I'm glad we found. Would highly recommend.

I really wanted to like this place. As others have mentioned, the atmosphere in this place is just weird. I was expecting this restaurant to have some sort of typical pizza joint feel, but I honestly think like they're trying way too hard to make this place give off a classy hipster vibe. 

Water is served from a glass bottle. Cool, but strange for a pizza place. The chairs aren't very comfortable if you're sitting at a table, but the super dimmed lighting is kind of interesting. I also thought it was kind of odd that this place doesn't offer any type of bread appetizer.

I had the classic pepperoni pizza ($10.99 and large enough for two), and I thought it was pretty tasty. Based on other reviews, I was expecting it to be super thin, but it was actually just right. The pepperoni slices were huge, and everything tasted very fresh. I do wish that the pizza included a serving spatula, but I guess our forks did the job decently enough. 

When all is said and done, I probably won't be coming back. The atmosphere is too strange and it just didn't have the most welcoming vibe. That doesn't mean you won't like it though!

I used to really like it here, but the service just sucks. Every Sunday that we come here, the same asshole cashier makes me wish I never came. The pizza itself is tasty, but a bit overpriced. For about $15, you can feed 2-3 people with a small pizza. Overall, this place is decent if the person at the register is anybody but the jerk with the crappy beard. Expect a lot of kids on the weekends, too.

I just came here for the first time this weekend and was very pleased with the quality of the food. This place is definitely in a bit of a hole-in-the-wall spot (it's located in a shopping plaza), but the restaurant itself is large with plenty of seating, very clean, and nicely decorated. 

The menu itself can be a bit confusing at first glance. There's not very much organization to it, but once you understand it, the menu is basic enough and limited. We decided to have the barbacoa street tacos (only $1.99/taco) and the tostaditas nachos (basically nachos with your choice of meat, beans, pico de gallo, sour cream, and guacamole).The salsa bar was super tasty - especially the pineapple habanero and the mango jalapeno salsa. I also liked that there was an unlimited amount of warm chips available near the salsa bar.

Overall, this place is definitely one of my new top Mexican food restaurants to eat at in Tucson. It's authentic enough, affordable, and has a very comfortable atmosphere.

My fiance and I came here on Wednesday night and were very happy with our experience. The atmosphere is western-like and the light is dimmed. There are some neat little paintings around that I think really give this place some great character. 

Since we came on a Wednesday night, he were able to get an unlimited amount of ribs for $20. The first set was delicious and the meat practically fell off the bone, but the next few sets were sort of dry and just didn't taste as great as that initial set. I had the three-taco plate, and even though the tacos were very tasty, I felt like the beans were something that I could make at home in less than five minutes. Either way, this place was definitely a great little find and we will be returning. Even though the prices are indeed on the higher side, I figure that we're paying for the atmosphere as well.

This place is great if you're looking for burgers that are tastier than In-N-Out. The regular cheeseburger is $4.99 and their regular gourmet burgers are $6.49 (there's also an option where you can pay to have a larger patty, but I personally can't tell the difference myself). 

The fries are also pretty good. They're thin, nicely seasoned, and can easily be split by two people. 

Overall, this is definitely a great place to go if you'd like a higher quality burger than other fast food locations. The restaurant itself is also very clean and the employees are usually very friendly - plus you can also sign up for their emails to receive free fries.

I decided to try PTY due to purchasing a Groupon a few months back.  I reviewed the menu and visited the area and was excited to use the Groupon based on the opinions from friends and reviews I had read.

My Experience was quite the contrary from friends and reviews.

I got there Today Monday around 2PM.  We were seated quickly as it was very slow.  There was a large event outside PYT the day prior and it seemed like they didn't get to finish cleaning up the place, yet all the other store fronts were spotless.

The music was VERY loud.  I felt like I was at the club.  When the waitress came over it was even difficult to hear her as we placed our order.

We ordered an appetizer the Chips & Drip Trio.  The appetizer was simple and came out quickly.  The Hummus was outstanding it stood well above the black bean salsa and the tomato salsa.  The app came out quickly.

Entrées ordered were the Lobster Burger and Krispy Kreme Sliders.  Again we were pretty much the only people in the whole place.  It took probably 15-20 minutes after we finished out appetizer for our entrées to arrive.  Both burgers were cooked to order and hot.  The items were fresh and tasty.  I would have at this point rated the restaurant a 3 with the possibility of giving the place another chance.  What occurred next was a drastic turn for the worst.

The staff was frolicking around the restaurant shouting at each other, not fighting but shouting parts of a conversation as they walked through the restaurant.  There was profanity used several times that was not shouted but still loud enough over the music to be heard clearly.  There were also several conversations that were completely inappropriate for anyone to be having in a place of business let alone it coming from the actual staff.  Conversations that included molestation as a child, people being fat, and drug abuse.  I will not go into the details of the conversations as they only make it worse.

At this point we decided dessert was out of the question and we finished out meals paid our check and left.

PYT has good food, but the staff leaves something to be desired.  Our waitress was very kind and polite but it seemed others working there thought they were at a friends house having a party and not of a place of business.  It is a shame that I will not be enjoying PYT again in the future because of the staff.

Donuts-exceptional!  In stock cakes-excellent!  Ordered cakes-hit or miss (have ordered many, many cakes from here-I don't always get what I specifically asked for...such as color, design).   

My main problem with this store is the customer service - they can be down right rude!  

The other HUGE problem I have is being ORDERED to vote for them in the ridiculous "sweetest bakery" contest every time I walk in the store!  I would think a "sweetest bakery" contest would be a little more organic, not hounding customers daily and beg for voyesI had to unfollow them from social media, emails, etc because it is all they post - it's absolutely annoying.  I hope whatever they gain from the contest is worth losing so many customers from the harassment.

Update:  I really have no choice but to change my review to a 1 star...the woman that owns the bakery has the absolute worst customer service!!  As a business owner you should learn from your reviews...use them as a tool to learn what you may need improvement on. We live in a world of social media, if you don't like the reviews your getting...fix it!  If you don't care about the reviews and growing as a business...keep doing what your doing.  However, don't be surprised or insulted that people are talking about it!  Are we not supposed to share our experience with your business because you may be offended?  Nobody is asking for perfection...however, customer service should be an area that you excel in!

-1,000,000 stars.  I was in town for a concert  and my friends brought me to this bar.  I was hanging out on th patio when a young lady sat next to me bleeding from her calf... So as a doctor I immediately asked her if she was ok.  What happened next was terrifying and unbelievable.  I was literally lifted out of my seat by A bouncer who took offense to my attempt to help the bleeding female.  For reasons I don't understand, he began screaming at me that I am not a physician, and the more I tried to explain that I was just trying to help... the more violent he became.  
I didn't fully grasp how dangerous the situation was until I was airborne and suddenly on the pavement gasping for air.
I  have no idea why their bouncer attacked me, but I figured that I would warn others to be cautious.  Especially here.

Overpriced. Not a great selection of menu items. Ate dinner with 5 people, and the general consensus was that the food was not worth the high price. The cheese grits in particular were terrible, though the sweet potatoes and mac & cheese were pretty good. The service was slow, and the server mixed up our drink and food orders and even our receipts. Certainly won't be returning here with all the other great places in the area.

Yikes!

This brunch setting was confusing because no one greeted us and no signs provided direction. After a minute of trying to find someone to help us, I resorted to the lady at the cash register. I started to ask her if we were supposed to seat ourselves, but she cut me off, waving her hands at me and shrieking, "Agh! Agh! Agh! Can't you see I'm trying to count money?! Hold on a sec!" I was speechless. She finished counting her money, then gave me a half-hearted apology, but chastised me again for interrupting her money-counting.

So we left. I called and asked to speak to the manager - whose name was Maury. He told me to be quick because they were really busy. (Again, yikes!) I explained the situation. Instead of an apology, he suggested that I shouldn't have interrupted his employee while she was trying to count money. 

If MoKaBe's is that inept with customer service, I will do them a favor and not trouble them with the extremely difficult task of counting my money.  And if anyone asks me if they should go here, I will tell them (waving hands and shrieky voice), "Agh! Agh! Agh! Don't do it!"

Review is strictly based on take out and I'm sure the experience differs. We ordered a chicken teriyaki bento with vegetable tempura and a sushi roll. Vegetable tempura were mainly onion rings in case you are wondering. The quality in sushi was not bad at all. If you know me, I am quite picky with sushi rice. I've found it to be pretty good. The only complaint I had was the wasabi was diluted and we didn't find any soy sauce when it was ready to chow down.

Last time trying Kaiseki was in Kyoto Japan and I enjoyed it tremendously. I was glad to find out that Yoichi's offers Kaiseki and I don't have to fly across the Pacific. As a fan of authentic Japanese traditional cuisine, I could not pass up on this opportunity. It was a great find during my visit in the lovely city of Santa Barbara.

There is definitely a difference when using all five senses of touch, smell, taste, sight, and hearing. The presentation and simplicity says plenty. The main ingredient of each dish were never overpowered but accentuated. Each course is presented with an introduction. 

The staff is friendly just like the service you get in Japan. The experience was unforgettable. Thank you Yoichi's!

After my first tantalizing taste of BB at their Rittenhouse satellite location, I had to make a trip to the mother ship in NoLibs.  So many more choices! 

Brown Betty, how do I love thy cupcakes?  Let me count the ways (in order of preference): 

1.  Lemon curd-filled vanilla pound cake with lemon/vanilla buttercream:  Holy wow.  Want lemon meringue pie in cupcake form?  THIS IS IT.  So good my teeth hurt.  You must try it. 

2. Almond pound cake with chocolate buttercream frosting and toasted almond slivers: simply divine!  The almond flavor was subtle and tempting, although I might love it even more if it were a touch more almondy.  When in doubt, add marzipan, I say.  Still, BB's chocolate buttercream on top mos def rules. 

4. Chocolate-on-Chocolate:  Nomnomnomnom.  What?  Yeah.  I got nothing.  These are heaven, and they did a beautiful job of making the fudgy frosting look like an elegant rose.   

Slightly lesser delights: 

4. Strawberry-on-strawberry:  Very good, but it didn't reach out and strangle my tongue.  Not strawberryish enough.  They need to figure out how to jam that crazy S-berry flavor in the buttercream like Naked does.  

5. Red velvet: I am not an RV fanatic, but this came closer to good than any other I've had (probably because it had more cocoa than most).  

6. Pineapple: My least favorite selection from BB to date.  It lacked the fresh-fruity brightness of citrus flavor I expected, and instead tasted of cloyingly sweet candied pineapple, bits of which appeared to be studded throughout the batter.  Nice idea, but I hope they re-conceive this one.  

Life is good (and yes, I work out).

No. This place does not deserve anything remotely more than 2.5 stars. Maybe 3-stars if I didn't have such a terrible overall experience. I went on opening night and there was plenty of tables and zero Yelp reviews. My intentions were to open a Yelp page for 7 ounce and become their first reviewer. But after the experience that my SO and I had, there was no way in hell that I was going to waste my time opening a Yelp page. Plus, it would be kind of mean to give them a 1-star as their first Yelp review. Upon calming down now and it's been almost two weeks, it's time for me to write this review.

Great atmosphere, but terrible service with decent food that was very overpriced. And on top of all that, my SO got an extremely injured knee when he left the booth because the grill grates under the table left a deep wound in his knee that is still healing over the last 2 weeks. Be careful when you get up from the booths.

Let's talk about the pros. Spacious seating, welcoming staff when you enter, and nice decor that makes this feel like a modern, up-end type of restaurant. Meats are fresh. Now, let's talk the cons.

Service- I understood it was opening night and it was somewhat busy. We were seated right away and asked for our orders. That's fine. I ordered the calamari and then we ordered one of the combos for the two of us to share. When we go to a Korean bbq place/restaurant, we go for the atmosphere, meats, and side dishes. When we asked for the side dishes, the waittress said sure they'll bring it. A good 30-40 minutes later was when we got our side dishes because "someone else took my side dishes in the kitchen." Okay, fine. She comes back with our food. She leaves. Comes back later saying it'll get busier so she's dropping off the check and we can just ask someone to help us when we're ready. Comes back again a few minutes later to check in and then says okay, it's getting very busy with the other table so I might now come back. It seems like she was trying to do her job, which I get, but it also made it seem like the larger table took priority while my table of 2 did not. Regardless, whether or not you agree with my depiction, my warning to you is that service is going to take awhile if it's busy.
Now for the food that's mediocre and overpriced. 

Calamari: The calamari appetizer came with maybe 5 small pieces in a breading that was bland. It was not crispy enough and the breading used to fry it had NO seasoning whatsoever. Sometimes that can be saved by a great dipping sauce which was definitely not the case here. Their dipping sauce consisted of some mayo with sriracha. The sriracha overpowered the mayo and all you can taste is the sriracha without anything to balance the lack of flavor in the fried calamari; unfortunately, this dipping sauce did not save the calamari dish. 

Side dishes were fine. Some of your typical Korean side dishes like cucumber, kimchi, radish, etc. This place is different than other Korean bbq places because their side dishes aren't unlimited, which of course no one told us so we were charged for them. There has been zero other Korean place that I have been to that charges extra for refilling a side dishes, without telling us. In fact, the waitress also failed to inform us about pricing for other things that are discussed below. 

Combo Korean bbq: We got the combo for two people with various cuts of meats. Meats are expensive so I'm fine with the price I paid for the combo. That was fine since meats are expensive, but what wasn't fine is the waitress taking our order and asking if we wanted garlic, lettuce, and onions without telling us that they charge money for it. Once again, this goes to service and common etiquette to tell your customers, when it's opening night so no one knows how your restaurant operates, that you tell them you're planning to charge like $2.00 for a small thing of garlic, another maybe $2.00 for another thing of lettuce, and another $2.00 for a small 1/3 onion that I wouldn't have wanted because there was already the same onion on top of one of my meat dishes. So yea, I paid an estimated $6.00 for some veggies under the impression that it was included since all Korean bbq places that I've been to, lettuce and onions and garlic are free, unless they tell you otherwise. And if I had known, I would not have gotten it. That's ridiculously overprice for a few pieces of garlic and extremely unacceptable.
Additionally, the grill that we got sucked. All the meats stuck to it tremendously.

Once again, I'd like you to keep in mind that I have been to numerous Korean barbecue places in various cities. There's at least one other Korean bbq place here in Tucson that I've been to and prefer over this place. Other than that, I make my own korean bbq or get my fix up in Phoenix where it's a lot cheaper and side dishes are free, including garlic, onion, and lettuce and service is much more attentive.

My wonderful Yelp Elite friend, Paige A. suggested this place for lunch. We came here with our SOs. I knew this place sounded familiar and realized that the chef was on one or more Food Network shows! I love watching Food Network so that's pretty awesome.

The interior of the restaurant gives a fancy, but also casual vibe. I am in love with the pink walls and light fixtures! I am also amazed at the huge selection at the bar and will definitely be coming back to try out some of their alcohol.

For our appetizer, we ordered the Frog Legs. The description of the frog legs is spot-on: The frog legs were seasoned with black pepper and came with a horseradish dipping sauce. Super flavorful and to me, frog legs taste like chicken. The dish came with four frog legs and rested on a bed of purple cabbage.

I ordered the Drunken Angel Pasta and my SO ordered the gumbo for lunch.

The Drunken Angel Pasta came in a rich lobster broth with a ton of seafood, including crawfish. The pasta was angel hair that was purple (maybe from the saffron?) and came with two slices of broth. This was an AMAZiNG flavorful and rich dish, but I'd suggest sharing this with someone else since it's extremely rich and very filling for one person to eat.

The Gumbo came with a side of crawfish hushpuppies that is extremely satisfying. The Gumbo was good butI would even say that their hushpuppies are to die for. They are sweet but also flavorful and not dry!

My SO and I were very excited that a Brazilian steakhouse opened up in Tucson. We made our reservation ahead of time and have been waiting for this meal. We were greeted by friendly staff and received excellent service throughout our meal. So, why only 3 stars for this review?

Unfortunately, almost all the meats were overcooked and not to our liking. We asked for medium rare or medium if not possible. What we received was well done and beyond done for the most part. In addition to being tough from the overcooking, the meats were bland for the most part. We added salt to all the meats. 

We love eating at Brazilian steakhouses so we're hopeful that this place will improve in the future. We will come back again to try the food again but not for awhile. In the meantime, the staff should work on cooking the meats better and work on the seasoning.

On a side note, the Brazilian limeade was delicious and came with free reviews. Two Brazilian limeades cost $7.70 in case you were wondering.

PYT was one of my favorite places to grab a burger or a beer in the city, but a recent experience has prompted me to be extremely weary to ever return!

I went there on my birthday with my girlfriend and her friend and our waiter was brash, lude, and downright creepy. He cursed because he thought it was cool to, he tried to force more alcohol on the women by pouring them more champagne despite their refusal. Even after they said they were driving, he tried to get them to drink more!

That's not even the worst part ..my girlfriend paid with a credit card and the  waiter FACEBOOKED MY GIRLFRIEND FROM HER CREDIT CARD NAME!!! He said he knew she was with me but decided he might have a shot anyway ...She was freaked out and I am not taking her back there again.

The waiter was a skinny, average height white male with piercings, short brown hair and a stupid hat. He talked in poor english and seemed to think he was the coolest hipster in all of Philadelphia.

I was so excited for this place to open. I have occasional ramen cravings and my boyfriend is a big ramen lover, and it's a pain to go all the way to Tampa to get it. So we followed Buya's progress and made reservations for opening day. 

Not to say I won't be back in six months or so once the menu has been fleshed out, but unfortunately I was very disappointed. 

We were not at all impressed with the ramen. It was salty, low on broth, and generally underwhelming. The menu right now is also very limited. I didn't want us to get the same dish, so when my boyfriend beat me to ordering the wagyu, I went with the crispy duck knowing that I might not love it. The wagyu was better, but still not spectacular. It actually tasked kind of like jerky. For $16-18 I expect some pretty amazing flavor and no skimping on the ingredients. 

I realize they just opened, but I definitely got the impression that Buya is trying a little too hard to be swanky and cool -- an upscale ramen place. OK, fine, but they're not quite there. At least not right now. Honestly, I wouldn't even pay a more reasonable $10-12 for a bowl of what I ate on my first visit, but I do think that's the price point this place needs to be around to keep people coming in.

Just a few other notes: the bell above the door ringing every time someone enters or exits is annoying. They try to get you to buy their special $2/glass in-house filtered water (wtf?) by presenting it to you right at the start, and then they serve you warm water when you decline. At least give me some ice cubes and some dignity!

Maybe when they expand the menu we'll see more worthwhile, reasonably-priced options, and maybe in time some of the other things will improve. But until then, I regrettably want to give Buya three stars. (Honestly, I was leaning toward two stars, but because it was opening day I'm bumping it up to three.)

It's hard to find a good lunch buffet on the weekend so I was excited to try this place. 

The buffet is big, with about 20 different options including curries, pakora, soups, vegetables, biryanis, rice, naan, etc. Also a very good mix of meat and vegetarian options. I was partial to the saag Chana and chicken Tikka masala, both very delicious!

The buffet was $15, which isn't the cheapest option I've seen but isn't bad. I always prefer to be able to try a few different things at Indian places than have to choose one!

I wouldn't have minded if there more curry type dishes (and some samosas!) but honestly, I didn't have room to eat more anyway. I would definitely come back here again in the area. 

Finally, the location is a little weird. The building is huge (you can't miss the NOW OPEN sign from the road) but you have to go in the entrance by the Shell Station and Jimmy Johns and drive around to get to the parking lot.

I think the time has come to review my second favorite place in all of Philadelphia.  Not that I want to encourage it being any more crowded, but the second I discovered Chapterhouse, I fell in love with this city all over again.

Since I moved to the city last year, I've made a mission of trying out almost every cafe in the city (still working down the list, but I've made good progress).  Yet Chapterhouse has fallen into the default category..... when I want to do some work on my laptop, write in my journal, catch up with a friend..... it's equitable to my home as far as comfort is concerned.  I've found the other patrons to be considerate but mostly in their own worlds; exactly the space I'm in when I set up shop in a cafe.

The servers are really nice (some nicer than others, but that's fine) and everything I've gotten here has been so good:  the vegetarian sandwiches are both great (try the vegan wrap!), the smoothies are delish (apple chai!), and I've had most of their teas hot and iced.  They also play great great music.

Despite the crowd (and occasional difficulty finding a seat), I generally feel a sense of relief when I walk in.  I think the communal aspect and variety of seating options really makes it feel like you're invited into someone's home.  I appreciate that.

Can I give it 77 stars? 

I cannot express the sheer happiness that ensued when I walked into Phileo last week. The fact that Philly would take this dazzling little concept and make it SO Philadelphian brings me great joy on a number of levels.  

Allow me to explain.

It's my understanding that NYC's Pink Berry and the subsequent DC chains (Mr. Yagato to name one), pride themselves on the idea of succintness. You pick one of three flavors, pick a topping or two, and there you go..... enjoy your trendy frozen yogurt experience. Um, k.

As a bona fide Philadelphian, I was not impressed. I like gluttony. I like variety.  And I'm perfectly OK with throwing trendiness out the door just to partake in a more satisfying froyo event.  

So what does Phileo do?  It PHILADELPHISIZES the trend.  It maintains the cute atmosphere but multiplies the excessiveness, negates the healthiness, and makes the whole damn experience significantly more delicious. I put snickerdoodle, cheesecake, cookies and cream yogurt into my happy little cup Tuesday night.  Oh, and then some Reese's and Mochi too.  

And best of all, I was in complete control (those who still wish to be healthy or simple have that ability as well).  Everything from the 12 froyo machines to the entire toppings bar is self serve and completely in your hands.

Think Maoz but in dessert form.

So I threw all my delicious things together, and my bill came to....$4.19.  As per usual, way to go Philly for redefining a chic NYC notion into something much sloppier, much cheaper, and much more awesome.

I hate to leave a bad review but my experience here tonight was one of the worst I've ever had. The server informed us that they were out of one of the menu items, which was fine. We ordered drinks and appetizers. The appetizers took nearly an hour to come out and when they finally did, it was one at a time. I'm not sure why it took so long because the restaurant wasn't even crowded. The server then again came out to tell us they had run out of ANOTHER menu item. By this point, we were pretty annoyed and starving. We never saw our server again after this point. 

An hour passes and a lady wearing an apron (obviously one of the kitchen staff or owner) approached us and told us they also ran out of shrimp for one of the entrees that someone in our party ordered because last night (Friday) was really busy. They basically ran out of half the menu. We were also told that there was a new chef in the kitchen and it was his first day, so that's why the food took so long. Another hour passes and the entrees come out one at a time, so half our group was sitting around waiting while the other half had nothing. Since our server gave up on our table, the hostess and bartender were the ones who brought our food and refilled our waters. No one came up to us once to checked on how our food was. When we finished eating, no one approached us with the check so we had to get up and ask for it. There was another group there before us and we heard them arguing with the server because they were unhappy with their service as well.

The food was good but having no service and super long wait time ruined the night for us. The manager ended up comping our bill 20% off and offering to buy us a round of drinks which we declined. After we left, I found out that Ruby Rose had eaten here last night and threw French fries at the server. I feel bad that they had a rough weekend but I will definitely not be returning or recommending them to anyone. I regret coming here tonight. Their only saving grace was the owner and bartender who were very apologetic.

Where do I begin.  Sue sue sue??.  Love Sandy and Walt!  They are the best!  but Sue you are going to kill what used to be a very unique place that gave a local seafood flare.  Next time you grab something out of my hand I might call the police for assault like you have in the passed based on customer reviews.  

I choose Walt's restaurant last night because of the previous experiences I have had over the last 10 years.  I had a friend in town that was locally raised and wanted some fresh seafood.  Walt's did provide a great taste in freshness in a small package. They loaded the plate with rice, slaw and a small piece fish for $30 a plate.  I'm glad I had it blackened.  The fried looked like a thin tasteless sponge cake.  Maybe the cook was over heated.  

There were a few bright spots in our dinner experience. The grouper cakes, key lime pie and conch chowder are awesome.  Walt's mother's key lime pie is the best.  I also enjoyed the sangria very tasty and refreshing in such a hot place.   Sue instead of blistering me for touching your $20 floor fan that cools the restaurant why don't you take the $300 I spent and reinvest it in adequate climate control for the restaurant and anger management therapy for yourself. Coming out during my dinner and lecturing me not to move your $20 floor fan because the kitchen is at 180 degrees and the cook is suffering completely changed my dining experience.  

If you have that big of issue maybe I should call a few of the federal and state departments to inspect the safety of the work environment.  You could be causing a long term health issue for your employees. The ACLU, OCHA and a few others would love to visit. They might change your attitude a little. 

BTW. I never touched your fan!

Thanks for the memories!

Went to dinner last night at Iozzo's for a date night with my husband.  I've been telling him about this restaurant for at least 2 years and we just finally got around to checking it out.  It's this hidden little gem on the south of downtown Indy.  If you go inside, it's so nice and cozy.  You forget you're in Indy and think you're in a little Italian restaurant in The Hill or in Chicago. 

We had the best waitress.  She was so nice, funny, and gave awesome customer service.  She alone is a reason we would go back. 

We started off our meal with the calamari (the only food photo I took).  It was amazing and fresh.  The tentacles were crispy deliciousness!  My husband said they were the best he's ever had.

Following our appetizer, we had salads.  He had the Caesar salad, which was good, but the star of the show was the caprese salad.  I was a little concern if the tomatoes would be good... and they were! Everything about the dish was perfect.  The balsamic demi glaze they use is awesome.  My husband, who doesn't like tomatoes, LOVED this dish and kept coming back for more bites. 

For dinner I had the lobster ravioli,  my husband had the lasagna, and we shared a side order of the risotto.  My ravioli was good and so was my husband's lasagna.  We read some reviews before we went to Iozzo's and a couple said the lasagna had too much sauce... we were like how is that even possible?! Come to find out, it is possible and there was a little too much sauce.  But again, it was still good.  The risotto though.... O.M.G. It was amazing.  It was so rich and flavorful. 

For dessert, we got a little crazy.  Tiramisu flute, scoop of spumoni, AND a scoop of the peach sorbetto.  It was all amazing!  Next time, we won't be sharing the tiramisu flute... I'm getting my own!  The sorbetto was so light and really cleansed your palette... who knows, maybe next time, I'll be a diva and get that in between courses!!

Just received a delivery order and was not expecting what I received. I got chicken tenders for my daughter and they got chicken patties cut it into strips and deep fried them. My wife ordered a sub, the lettuce had a weird taste and ruined the whole sandwich. I got chicken wings and they were not awful but the rest of the order was! Never ordering from here again!

********************** 1553 *****************

What not to love about Bacara Resort & Spa in Santa Barbara, although I wish I was here with my lover, instead of my parents ;) they enjoyed their stay tremendously. Everything was perfect from the valet guy, to the check in, from th bellmen to the housekeeping.

Their Oceanview room offers a private patio with view of the Pacific Ocean. Love the luxurious Frette linens and a spacious bathroom with a deep soaking tub, marble shower, and their junior suite is more spacious, the most intimate hotel suite, features a gas fireplace and a wide furnished balcony, with the views of Bacara's Mediterranean architecture and lush gardens.

The spa is a must try while you are here. Recognized as one of the finest spas in the world, The Spa at Bacara is spectacular in every way, from its beautiful architecture and incredible array of services to its expert staff. With treatments, you can enjoy a wealth of amenities, plus an adults-only pool (never worry about those cray cray loud kids), Jacuzzi, redwood sauna, eucalyptus steam room, fireside lounge areas, wellness classes and a rooftop terrace.

- No fee for valet parking
- Dinner & Dancing 
- Coffee and juice bar
- Live piano
- Welcome gift basket of fruit & wine for your special occasion 
- Just a short drive to Santa Barbara winery destination 

Even though we were the only Asian people during our visit, my parents and I have never felt out of place. The type of service we receive at Nordstrom and MLife Platinum member of the MGM Group. Bacara Resort & Spa of the Meritage Collection is truly a gem. 

My dad already plans a return this year.

Onion, mushroom on a Philly Cheese Steak, sign me up! Around $12 for a gigantic sandwich! 

It's the kind of food you eat when you are in college! Now I barely finish 1/4 of it!

All I wanted was a breakfast Cuban. 

I had realized this on Monday, thinking about my love for brunch and all the delicious Cuban sandwiches I had eaten since moving to Tampa a year and a half ago. But I hadn't seen a breakfast Cuban yet. 

I had forgotten about this dream in the latter part of the week. Work can be like that sometimes. So when we went out this morning for coffee, the coffee slinger referred us to Pinky's. He didn't say much specific, except that the lines were worth it. 

We drove to South Tampa, the theme song to Pinky and the Brain whistling from my lips. I scanned the menu, not sure if I was going to go Frittata or Eggs Benedict (my usual fare). 

But there it was. Tall, smoky, full of eggs, cheddar, and homemade bacon. The bread was crisp on the outside, warm and comforting on the inside. 

The first bite was a tease, and it took all my willpower not to devour it. I wanted to savor this sandwich of my dreams. 

I don't know if you've been dreaming of a breakfast Cuban or not. I don't think I'm alone in this, but it's your loss if I am. Do yourself a favor, and share a dream with me.

We were here last Saturday for a birthday celebration. There is a cute ox mascot display at the front of the restaurant. Inside the furnishing is modern, themed with electric blue accent-lighting.
