We arrived at 1:30 on a Saturday and there was ample seating available, even for our big party of 8.  It was all day dinner since it was a weekend day.  We pretty much had only 3 options:  1- Hot Pot with Sushi $23.50. 2- Korean BBQ with Sushi $28.50. 3- Hot Pot & BBQ, plus Sushi $30.95.  Everyone at the table must pick the same option for obvious reason: it's impossible to police anyone  from subsidizing another.  We came mainly for hot pot, but this was the first time sushi was thrown into the mix and I liked it.

We also had the options between mini personal hot pot, and one of the 4 big pots with different number of partitions. The big pot must be shared by at least 2 people.  We all went with mini pots. You can justify either way, so don't fret over the choices.

The sauce bar was impressively set up. They even have sauce recipes printed and displayed right at the bar.  That's helpful even for the experienced, because for once you don't have to be ad hoc, but learn a new sauce mix that you most likely have not tried before.

Our waiter was friendly.  He took orders from the table 3 times.  But that's the extent of his service. None of us had soup spoons and paper napkins and we had to get them ourselves from the service station. We also had to clear the used trays ourselves and put them on the busing cart.

Since it's a been a while since we had a group hot pot, we made a few mistakes, resulting in a rather frazzling experience along with low overall rating. I'm listing a few tips below for future visits.

1- Do not come with a big party.  If you do, you'll be seated at the big table and you'd be doomed.  Some people would be trapped and you'd be constantly passing trays and plates from one end of the table to the other.  You'd also be subject to a mandatory 20% surcharge on service. 

2- Break up your party.  Break up into parties of 4's and get seated at regular tables.  Ideally at tables adjacent to each other.  As long as there are separate bills, you're separate parties.  You'll thank me later.

3- For the "sushi", skip the rolls and go for sashimi, sushi, and other appetizers.  Just a general rule of AYCE, minimize carbs!

4- The birthday person gets to eat for free if the ID shows the birthday within a calendar day, and dine with a party of 4 (or more).

5- If you're fortunate enough to be around, come during a weekday lunch.  Not only are the prices $5.50 cheaper for the exact same all-you-can-eat hot pot buffet, you have 2 other lunch specials to choose from: $9.95 for a 5 ingredient mini pot plus 1 roll of sushi; $12.95 for a 4 ingredient BBQ plus 1 roll of sushi.  Can't beat that!!

6- There's a 2 hour limit. They will impose a 20% surcharge if you blatantly waste food; and for leftover sushi, they could charge you at menu prices.

PS. No dessert of any kind which's another bummer...

We were in the area and were about to revisit Dolsot House for some Korean fares. Unfortunately, the line was out of the door on this Saturday evening. After 35 minutes of waiting we were still standing outside looking in,  Rayaki was conveniently located right next door with great Yelp ratings, so we changed our plan as a form of making a statement :)   Ramen restaurants naturally have a quicker turnaround time. And we got a table for 5 after about 5-10 minutes wait.   

Upon entering the restaurant I couldn't keep my eyes off from the manga murals which covered all the walls.  To me that's one of a kind and super cool.

Menu was simple. The entire menu fit on a small order form.  We simply wrote the quantity next to the dish we want.

Now the curve ball:  We loved tonkatsu, the Japanese deep fried pork breaded with panko.  So 4 out of 5 of us all ordered the Tonkatsu* Ramen!!   When the ramen got served, we all scratched our heads -- where were the deep fried, breaded pork cutlets?!  In front of us looked like soy sauce marinated pork belly which could go with 2 small bowls of rice!!  

I asked the waitress twice to make sure they didn't give us the wrong dish. She reassured us.  Oh well...  Disappointment aside, the ramen's got everything, well presented, and price was super fair.  The broth was flavorful but on the verge of being too savory.  The marinated pork was what made the whole dish TOO salty. That was a shame because any other preparation of the same protein would have been fine.

Yep, the only other ramen we ordered, the Steak Ramen, was indeed perfect.

Despite the disappointment, which was partly our fault (see * below), I still appreciate this eatery very much:  great value, hip, BYOB, and simply fun.   I would like to try their Rayaki Fries next time.

*I later found out that we confused Tonkatsu with Tonkotsu -- yes, just 1 letter off !!!  The former is the deep fried breaded pork cutlet we were thinking, while the latter is simply one of the ramen recipes noted for its cloudy white pork bone broth.  Lesson learned.

The name Spice C rang music to my ear and I was quickly drawn to this noodle joint out of so many restaurants in Philly Chinatown. Of course, high Yelp rating was a major factor as well.  The exterior was quite nicely done. This red brick corner building was hard to miss, and the white-on-black signage with red accent looked current and hip. There's also a ramp to the side entrance for wheelchairs and strollers.  Commendable, especially in Chinatown.

Seating was quite limited inside the elongated dining area. Tables were small, mostly for seating up to 4 people, but you barely got any elbow space.  In general, the restaurant felt quite cramped.  Ambiance was so so, nothing worth mentioning.

There were 2 wait staff.  Service was mixed. At times they were extremely rude; then all of sudden they'd be ultra-courteous.  Very surreal to say the least. 

The menu was small so it took very little time to make up our mind. For every noodle dish you can choose between hand-pull or shaved noodle. For us, it was a no-brainer - hand-pulled noodle all the way!  We ordered 3 dishes:

House Special (Sliced Beef, Tendon & Brisket) $9.25.  The soup was rather bland.  I would have been better served had I chose the Szechuan Spicy version for $1.50 more.

House Special Stir Fry Noodle $9.25.  The serving size was noticeably small. The taste was un-impressionable. Nothing stood out.

3 Treasure Stir Fry Noodle $9.25.  Ditto the above. Not much different except for the proteins.

And, it was annoying that they accept cash only.  After walking out of the restaurant, I had buyer's remorse as soon as I saw the next restaurant a few doors down: ShangHai 1 -- my next target.

Now I know what you're thinking, why does Downtown Indy need another steakhouse? Well, let me tell you - Hyde Park Prime is the real deal. My wife and I dined there as part of their soft opening and it was OUTSTANDING. The service is impeccable from the moment you walk in, as you're escorted to your seat, and all throughout the dining experience. 

We only had access to a limited menu, but everything was absolutely exquisite. For an appetizer we had the Spicy Tuna Tempura - as good as any sushi spot. I had the lobster bisque after that and it was the best I've ever had. I could have sworn I was sitting in Maine, that's how good the lobster tasted. For the pièce de résistance, I had a 14 oz New York Strip with garlic and caramelized mushrooms cooked medium. There was a slight mistake as it came out medium well, but Devin our waiter was so observant and before I could take three bites, he took it away and brought us out new dishes. To top it all off, my wife and I split a small piece of cheesecake and some crème brûlée. The perfect ending to an amazing meal.

As the concierge of a private club, I often have to make recommendations to my members and overnight guests. I won't hesitate to send any that wish to dine at an outside restaurant to Hyde Park Prime Steakhouse. I will definitely be a returning guest as soon as I can.

So disappointed.

Our waiter, Jimmy, was very slow and inattentive. He sucks up to the older, presumably wealthy patrons though.

The bread at the table tasted dry and stale. For an appetizer, we started off with a shrimp cocktail. It was good...but not worth $22.

We then got lobster bisque...it was so bland and barely had a lobster flavor, we actually sent them back. 

For our entrees, my boyfriend got a 12oz filet and I got the salmon mixed grill plate. My dinner was alright...the salmon was a bit dry, but overall, wasnt bad. His filet honestly tasted like roast beef...not high quality steak.

We had ordered our dessert when we ordered our meal (apple pie a la mode), but decided at the end of dinner to get our dessert to go. Our waiter brought out the dessert and bill at the same time...umm...dumb move, dude! He put the container of ice cream right on top of the hot pie...it was already melting by the time he brought it to our table!

We waited 10 minutes for him to come by and grab the credit card/check so we could pay and leave, and he was nowhere in sight. We ended up having to flag down a manager to run it for us.

Overall, the experience was awful, considering how much we paid to eat there. We probably would have had a better experience at Red Lobster...seriously. So disappointed.

The food here, in spite of the name "GW Fins," which sounds like a bad chain eatery hawking seafood, is nothing short of spectacular. Which may be why reservations, even weeks out, are hard to find. So why two stars down?

You're not just paying for the food, at a place like this. You're paying for the experience. They want to create one.  Here's how they ruin that goal:

The cocktails, at the bar, were exceptional. Their sazerac,  mules, and other libations, were on point, and fairly priced, to their craft.  Getting a seat at the bar, which is loaded up with folks trying to grab a meal here, without the long wait for a booking, a bit more stressful, but we still managed. With four people on the bar, they're still largely cranking cocktails for the dining room. There's a vibe that is surely pleasant, and professional, but super stressed. I don't come to a New Orleans restaurant for stress. Chip off a bit for that. 

The front desk is a big fail. It sets tone. You have one of the most popular restaurants in New Orleans. The hosts are set upon by drop-ins. They're the height of professional. There is a coldness about how they do their business, though, that makes you feel most unwelcome, even with a reservation. I had one, with its threat of charging me a cancellation penalty, if I had to bail out. Understandable? Certainly. That, though, in combination with the chilly greetings? Not a winner. Read "The Disney Way," y'all. THIS IS THEATRE. A smile, and a warm welcome, go a long way.  

Beyond that, when they come to seat you, they have a dress code, of which they make you painfully aware. Do I understand the look-and-feel thing? Kinda-sort of. To me, a more formal dress code is always kind of an exclusionary thing. It's the "no riff-raff," e.g. dem poor folk, stay out.

Y'all, if someone has the cash to put down, for the price of a meal here, why, oh, why, do you give a tinker's damn about "business" grade attire? I watched women saunter in, with their outerwear on, for a cold day, and it go without a mention. This might possibly be because it's hard to keep your front desk working, when women, who get critiqued about their attire, will metaphorically behead them, and storm out.

It was 40°F outside. Their entry is chilly, at best. There is precious little space, up front. So you keep your outdoor wear on. I had my black jacket, and a black Sazerac sweatshirt underneath, that wasn't visible.

They called us. I unzipped my outer jacket, to get it off. Before I could enter the dining room, the hostess/fashionista gatekeeper gave me the, "Do you have the appropriate attire" shtick. "I sure do," I said, having to demonstrate this, by pulling down my sweatshirt to show her. 

"Do I need to take it off now, or can I remove it at the table?"  I said, politely.

She realized that she was being a bit too aggressive, and tried to down-peddle it, with a joke about liking my sweatshirt.  

I feel her stress, as she has to do this nonsense. That's really the two-star down problem:

I FEEL THEIR STRESS.

Now, collectively, I've entered a meal, in NEW ORLEANS, feeling the pressure-cooker hit me, yet again.

The food, and the lovely atmosphere, heal a few wounds. The cheddar biscuits, dropped as you sit down, were perfect. The Lobster Dumplings, and the Albacore crudo were both prettily plated, and delicious. Our mains, the Sea Scallops, Mahi, and a Dry-Aged Tile fish were all five star.

The service was excellent. The support staff, who keep water glasses full, and food moving, at the right temperatures, were a 10+. 

Our waitress was super pleasant, informative, and welcoming at the head of the meal. At the tail, she was in full battle mode, with the restaurant now full. Of all, she showed it the least, but her check-drop with that "take your time"which means, in a place that flips tables 3 times a night, please don't take your time, and her quick check-drop felt a bit more like a "don't let the door hit your butt on the way out," sort of farewell.

This is clearly a management thing. Maybe someone should take them all on a field trip up to Commander's Palace, to see how graciousness, at their seating volume, is done.  

Would I eat here again?  Against other choices, and in New Orleans, there are plenty of A+++ restaurants, is it worth about $80-100 pp to put up with this restaurant's cultural insanity?  I dropped Restaurant August, and a couple of other faves this trip, that do a far better job of allowing me to savor the experience.

That would be best remembered, at a place with a Red Lobster name, in the shadow of service, Antoines, across the street.

(Mic drop.)  Out.

Cafe Du Monde has given up. An outdoor cafe, there is no excuses for pre-making beignets, and tossing them into walk-away bags that are stone cold, with grease clotted powdered sugar, for both take out and  their sit down area which is outdoors. The joy of their cafe au lait and a plate of hot fresh beignets, coated in a pile of powdered sugar, is no more.

The tables are dirty. The chairs and cracked, or broken. 

The musicians at the corner, a long time busking tradition, was the only remnant of the fun here.

These people make so much money, between the cafe, merch, and spin off locations, that it's a shame that they're letting this place go to the dogs. 

Loretta's had far better beignets. I bring tourists here for the experience.

There's no experience anymore. 

Moving on.

Surprisingly great hot dogs and sausages on a bun. I had the Chicago Dog, which was true to form. We had a Guinness special, and a Bacon Werewolf, as well. 

The service, for a place with a long line, at one of the handful of fast-food joints on Frenchmen Street, was really friendly, from Sarah, the cashier.  

The kitchen was a bit slow, but, it's a go-to for those catching a break from the music and booze binging on Frenchmen Street. Seating is up on the balcony, at some really ratty picnic tables, up front, or there are a few seats at their bar. 

The bar is a minor fail. They notify you, after you've been through the food line, that they can't let you pay for a drink at the bar. You missed it? You end up back in the long line. The investment in a POS system for the bartender?  Might be a plus. #justsaying.

As smokehouses go, this one was kind of a nothingburger. The brisket was chopped up because it was dry. The andouille sausage was stuffed with distracting large chunks of black pepper. The corn bread was dry. Mac and cheese overcooked.

The location is fun. Made less fun by a duo playing music who sang painfully flat. 

Won't thrill ya, won't kill ya

Affordable Indian lunch? Hell yes! Great naan. Food is self serve, pay-by-the-pound style. You can eat there but it's much better suited to grabbing and going. If you want a specific dish, I'd avoid it. They make what they make and replenish it regularly. It's usually chicken tikka mansala, some rices, some biriyani, paneer, etc. samosas and naan are extra but totally worth it. 

Disclaimer: this is not authentic Indian food. It is to Indian food hat your local Chinese place is to Szechuan cuisine. It's tasty but not the authentic article. But, to their credit, they don't position themselves as the "authentic, home style Indian place."
I'm not real impressed tonight.  I waitress. Not very attentive.  Waited over an hour for food and ran out of drinks.

Why 4 stars? Here we go...
Super small restaurant that seemingly spills into an attached office/lobby/mailroom in the Alexander building. They do NOT take reservations, and they do NOT seat incomplete parties. There is a 'call ahead' list & I strongly advise using it. 
They serve the BEST POUTINE in Saint Petersburg. Period. 
The last entree in the menu... fat noodle something or other... Is SPECTACULAR, but don't share it. Honey, don't share anything because the portions just aren't large enough. I left hungry... & we went for my birthday dinner because I read on Twitter that it had recently been rated the #1 restaurant in Pinellas county. Well, it's not. No. And to say so is reckless & irresponsible.

Summary: The food is delicious, yet extraordinarily overrated. Like, whoa.

We had an absolutely fantastic stay at here in October 2020. In the midst of Covid, my step-daughter was married on the gorgeous grounds here. Every aspect of the wedding and our stay was outstanding. As difficult as it was to execute a wedding with all of the covid restrictions, every staff member went above and beyond for all of us. The grounds are gorgeous, the steakhouse was superb. The rooms are spacious and comfortable. Thank you all for your kindness, understanding and for making our daughter's wedding day so memorable!

My step-daughter was married at the Ritz Carlton in October 2020 and held her wedding dinner here. In the midst of covid, the staff at Angel Oak went above and beyond to accommodate us all and make the evening perfect. My husband and I greatly enjoyed our steaks, asparagus and potatoes. The bartender made us a couple of perfect martinis. What a fabulous evening it was. Thank you so much! We cannot wait to return.

So for the late post but better late .... 
So we were in the area and haven't had roadhouse in a while so we stopped by.  All the food was cooked to perfection and our sever AMY provided stellar service.  The prices were so much reasonable for the amount and quality.  No wonder there was a long wait to get in. (Well worth it) oh yeah on that not I forgot what the name of the 3 females and gentlemen out front was but they was awesome in getting Everyone in and seated in a timely manner

After visiting the Sunday Morning Market, we decided to grab a bite. 

My egg white omelet was good, but on the pricey side. 

Cleanliness was an issue.  After about ten minutes, I was informed of lipstick on my SECOND glass of water.  It wasn't my shade.  Earlier, our waitress took my glass from the table to go refill the water.  I thought that was weird.  I'm almost 100% sure she brought the wrong glass back.  To make things worse, we were never given straws, forcing us to touch or mouths to the dirty rim of the glass.  It makes me nauseous just thinking about it.  

Also, we had to bus our own table upon arrival.  The hostess walked us back to a filthy table, which was full of dirty dishes, napkins, and half-eaten food, then just leaves us there.  We couldn't even sit down.  We had to clear the tables ourselves.  Was it her first day on Earth?  I don't know.  The dirty glass with lipstick on it really got to me, though.  I was completely disgusted.

For me, cleanliness is a big deal.  If you can't keep the dining area clean, what does kitchen look like?

They haven't been open long, but I couldn't resist breaking my diet to try this place out.  The photos look so good, & I have a weakness for burgers.  This review is based on food, service, cleanliness, atmosphere, and value.

Excellent burgers!  I had the cheeseburger with blue-vein cheese and fries (lunch special for $8.99 plus a 50 cent upcharge because I wanted to try the Belgian fries).  The burger exceeded my expectations.  Fresh and juicy, with an excellent mix of flavors.  The blue-vein cheese was an magnificent compliment to an already delicious burger!  The Belgian fries were great. I had a bite of the Adam's Cheeseburger, and it too was awesome, though polar opposite from the one I ordered. 

We also ordered a Caesar salad.  We were told it came with anchovies, which is fine for me, but when it arrived, there was only one.  I didn't care for the house Caesar dressing, luckily we ordered it on the side.  On a good note, the romaine lettuce was fresh.

The service was great!  Our waitress was very attentive.  The dining area is modern & interesting, but I have to say, with giant windows all around, and nearly solid white paint on the walls, the glare was a bit bothersome.  I felt myself squinting the whole time I was there.  An easy fix would be to put some type of curtain, or shade.  Today there was nothing on the windows, and it was bright and sunny out.  The place is casual, and very very clean!

I know it's early, but to date, the prices are super high.  The lunch special was a good deal, I hope they keep that going, but ordering off the normal menu would be super expensive.  The value is why I'm giving 4 stars and not 5.

Overall, awesome burgers!  I want to try everything on the menu!

Hands down, this is the best place to eat in Brandon... or, Riverview.  This review is based on food, service, cleanliness, atmosphere, and value. 

Easily deserving of a 5-star rating, Boca is everything one desires in a restaurant.  Excellently prepared food from the freshest ingredients, outstanding service from the time you walk up to the time you leave, and an immaculate dining area with a pleasant and relaxing atmosphere.

As we were trying to decide on what to order, James (the SA) noticed our struggle and gave some very helpful suggestions.  We tried the Heritage Swine Flatbread, 60 Spice Chicken, and Shrimp and Grits.  Everything was bursting with flavor, and perfectly prepared!  The Shrimp and Grits was my favorite, an absolute delightful dish!

Between our server, the SA, and the assistant manager, the service was outstanding!  All questions were answered with great detail, drinks never ran out, and the food came out very quick.  The prices are higher than most establishments in this area, but worth every penny.  This is upscale dining at its finest.

This was not only a great dining experience, but a learning experience also.  The Peruvian cuisine is derived from a multi culture influence from all over the world, using local ingredients (from Peru) while creating a unique taste. The result is a delicious blend of spices flavoring different excellently prepared meats, vegetables, and rice.  

My favorites of the evening were the Pollo, tostones, and the cilantro rice; Mmmm, good!  Everything else was delicious also, but those three dishes stand out in my mind. 

This restaurant is nice inside and out, and conveniently located with plenty of parking. The food came out really fast, and like I mentioned before, all great!  We were served two sauces, and both were outstanding.  The thing that pushed this place over the 4 star mark was the stellar service.  Okay, the food would still get this place a 5 star rating, but great service is the "cherry on top".

The only complaint I can think of is, I wish the menu was bigger.  Not bigger physically, or bigger lettering...  bigger as in more delicious foods to try.

If I had to sum it up in one word, I'd pick DIRTY.  This place is disgusting!  The cigarette smoke was overwhelming, and for that one simple fact, I will not be back.  I've read the comments where David D. Of the casino talks about the "state-of-the-art complex air-filtration system that cycles the entire air in the building 4 times per hour".  Let me tell you, it's not working.  You got duped.

Not only is the air dirty, it sinks like moldy decomposing carcasses.  Also, the carpet is filthy.  I was only a small child in the 70s, but if I could imagine walking into a casino on the 70s, this is the decor I would imagine.  The place looks like it hasn't been cleaned since the 70s.

Also, there is a plethora rude employees.  It's it a prerequisite to have a jerk-like attitude? 

About 90% of the gambling available is video slots.  Of the tables available, 90% of those are Blackjack called something different at every table. They are definitely taking advantage of the monopoly they have. 

I had to take a shower immediately after leaving this place. My throat and eyes are still burning from the smoke. I know, you cater to your smokers, as well as your non-smokers.  Well, I guarantee you will not get hundreds of bad reviews solely due to not letting anyone smoke inside the building.  

I don't recommend this place, and there is no way I'll be back.

There were some major ups and downs during our visit.  To start, they'll valet your car but ask that you seat yourself.  I would much rather have a hostess than a valet attendant.  

We found a table over in the male dominated corner. Turns out a bunch of fire fighters decided to roll in for beer and shots. There was also another huge group in the back booths. Because of this the kitchen and wait staff were experiencing some major delays.

Even so, the wait staff tried to be as attentive as possible. Our waiter even tagged in another server when he became overwhelmed trying to close out the group of 20+.

For the good, I ordered the buffalo chicken sliders and they were tasty.  The beer breaded mushrooms were good, but very breaded and a little oily. You get a slider or burger and one side.  My meal cost $7.00.  For that price, I was satisfied.  You should know that you only get two sliders, not three.  We also ordered the fried cheese. You get three large wedges, two of the three were packed with cheese.  My only qualm is that I wish they gave you more than a drizzle of marinara sauce. The beer list is quite extensive and somewhat impressive. The Atwater Vanilla Java Porter was delicious! I also had a Napa Smith Amber Ale.

For the weird, customers stole every last one of their bourbon menus. When I asked about the bourbon our waiter said the list was just way too long to recreate from memory (understandable). Because of this I stuck with beer. This was 1. disappointing, they are a bourbon place and 2. totally weird. (Not the waiter's fault)  The management needs to print off another 100 menus, go to Kinko's and laminate it. I don't care if they need to do it every morning, it's an integral component of a diner's experience.  

Overall I would go back.  I'm aware that a new restaurant needs to work out the kinks so they are getting a little extra leeway. If they still have these problems six months out I'm not going to be as understanding.

I know I'm going against the grain here, but I just can't bring myself to pay $5 for a donut and definitely not $47 for a dozen donuts. Who are they kidding?! Donuts are the fun breakfast item you bring into work when you are feeling kind or thankful for your people. They are the breakfast item you surprise your kid with on a sunny Saturday. $47 for a dozen?! No way. Nope.

There is also the issue that they "borrowed" quite a bit from Mr. Holmes in SF. I want to support local, but I want to support your dream, not a ripoff of someone else's dream and decor. 

For people who are going to try it, we had the sugared donut, maple bacon donut, and the vanilla cream donut. Two out of three had the vanilla cream filling. I couldn't decide if I liked it. I guess it's good to offset the dryness of the donut, but I'm also not sure it needed it, but it did need something. 

Overall, it's a place I can tick off the list and happily go back to my $2 donuts.

I'm not sure if it's fair to review but I'm doing it anyway. We went on Friday when ramen master Nakamura was in the house. 

Oh. My. God. It was one of the best meals I've had in Nashville. Hands down, top two. 

We were offered five courses. They were as follows:

1. Edamame and Tsukemono (pickled veggies) paired with a Lovely Rita
2. Yellowtail jalapeno sashimi and sushi (a play on a Philly roll) paired with a Riesling
3. Kara-age with negi dip (fried Japanese chicken) paired with the Death of Meiji
4. Hatsu (chicken heart) and Australian Wagyu short rib with corn on the cob and miso butter paired with a German smoked beer
5. Tori Paitan (ramen) paired with sake

Honestly, almost everything was a highlight. If I HAD to pick, I would say for starters the sashimi. Now this is how sashimi is supposed to be cut and taste. Holy moly, I was in heaven. I literally died and woke up in Japan. The fried chicken was fantastic, the miso butter corn was divine and the ramen. Oh my goodness, the ramen. Sorry Otaku, I hope you went and tasted how a broth should be made. It was tasty, not too fatty, and bold. And the pork! it melted in my mouth. I am literally salivating writing this review. Someone please send me a bowl of his ramen! The drink pairings worked as well, no complaints there.

As for the decor and atmosphere, the place is slick. They really thought about the concept and made it come to life. I loved the lighting, the tables, the bar, the colors. Can you tell I liked it? Loved it!

Based on the first four courses, I have high hopes for the place! I am praying that Chef Nakamura left his ramen secrets for Chef Benefield and crew to replicate.

Easily my new favorite for Indian food in STL (2nd only to Bombay Food Junkies, which is more casual Indian street food).

Tried the lunch buffet and was pleasantly surprised. Each dish was flavored independently (some Indian places try to get away with sharing their gravy bases - but not this one!). They had lots of vegetarian dishes, multiple dessert options, and even masala chai included as a part of the buffet. I loved the fried pakoras, which were cooked perfectly. The naan was freshly prepared, and the kheer (sweet rice pudding) was divine. The spice level was mild, as you'd expect for a buffet, but the food was still flavored well. There was some dry vegetable pickle on the side, if you wanted to add heat, but would've loved some traditional Indian pickle as well. 

The waitress did say they offer an extended buffet on the weekends, with Dosa, Chana Bhatura, Pani Puri, and other delicacies. Visit Fri-Sun if you want to try something different than the usual buffet items.

Service was outstanding, as was the decor. We especially loved the Bollywood music and the Indian food channel that was playing on the TVs, as it added to the experience of traditional Indian cuisine!

Being that it was first time in Philadelphia, my trip wouldn't have been complete without some cheesesteaks.  However, rather than doing the typical "Pat's vs. Geno's" taste test, I asked my friends to take me to where they would normally go.  Although I am curious to see which of the two is better, it's not like their Yelp reviews are all that compelling (not to mention Geno's apparently racist reputation).

Now, when my friends told me they were taking me to a locals' spot, they meant it - I doubt I would have walked into Oscar's otherwise.  Both the inside and out scream dive bar, but in a good way - quiet, relaxed, and unpretentious.  More importantly though, the menu looked pretty solid - plenty of variety to choose from, like cheesesteaks, burgers, and typical bar snacks.

-- CHICKEN WINGS served with Ranch and Buffalo Wing/Hot Sauce...$6.50
(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oscars-tavern-philadelphia?select=Zybwf4Jl8tJSVAYR4BV_EA#TxsV_E53Nxr6iyzMg9MhGQ)
Easily the smallest wings/drums I've seen, but they were kinda cool at the same time.  The chicken was tasty enough on its own (I liked how they were just slightly crispy), but I thought the hot sauce made them taste that much better.

-- FRENCH FRIES...$2.95
(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oscars-tavern-philadelphia?select=Zybwf4Jl8tJSVAYR4BV_EA#wwGcdOMJxmiof_pnws0f2g)
The order wasn't huge, but it was proportionate to the price (and worth it).  The fries tasted great, but I liked how crispy they were even more.

-- BACON CHEESESTEAK - Bacon, Melted Cheese, Tomato, Onion, and sliced Steak on a Soft Roll...$6.95
(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/oscars-tavern-philadelphia?select=Zybwf4Jl8tJSVAYR4BV_EA#8zqUtbGgzw1GlIPidpi_WA)
Way better than the cheesesteaks I've had in SF.  The meat was thin yet flavorful and the toppings were terrific.  I ordered it without the tomatoes since it seemed out of place, but they actually would have been handy to freshen things up.  The roll was a bit too bready for me though.

Between the friendly service, decent food, and cheap prices (you get an extra half of a cheesesteak after 5:00pm), Oscar's Tavern is a pretty solid spot whether it's for drinks or a quick, casual bite (we were given plastic beer cups for water).  I wouldn't mind returning on a future trip, but I'm curious about more cheesesteak joints next time.

CASH ONLY.

Given how I had just discovered (and thoroughly enjoyed) Yogorino in SF before I left for Philadelphia, I was more than happy to oblige when one of my friends wanted to stop in for dessert.  How could I say no to such deliciously creamy frozen yogurt?

Walking in, everything looked about the same as the one in SF...but without the spinning wheel of gelato.  Quaint location, a few scattered seats/stools, and the same half dozen array of sauces waiting to be drizzled on said froyo.  However, while the frozen yogurt was roughly on par with the one from my first experience (just as creamy, though not quite as tasty), the sauce was lacking.  I ordered the same combination of toppings (strawberries with the waffle cone sauce), but it felt thinner and not as flavorful in comparison.

Considering how Vicky L. recently downgraded her rating for the SF Yogorino for a similar issue, I really hope this isn't a sign of Yogorino cutting corners to save money.  Although still good, only four stars for this Yogorino since I didn't leave as impressed as I did the first time.

Definitely a similar theme to the Rainforest Cafe, but without the cool animals. They have bird noises, flickering lights, water trickling down to sound like rain, & a lot of greenery.

For $21.99 per person, there are a lot of options to choose from, and for the price, it's decent. The quality of the food is average - there wasn't anything I ate which prompted me to go back for a 2nd taste. However, it seemed like most guests enjoy the seafood line. They have crab legs that are sliced in half & readily available to eat. Minimal work to stuff your face, hooray! 

They took awhile to clear out all of our dishes (we had a party of 6 at the table) but were helpful bringing out beverages and asking if everything was okay. 

Overall, it was decent, but I'm sure there are better buffets in Reno to eat at.

Everybody loves breakfast & brunch, For a place that's very busy throughout the day they actually get the customers in and out pretty quickly now for the food amazing simply amazing I've tried the BLT I've had their basic breakfast which consisted of toast eggs 
Some homestyle potatoes which were delicious, can't forget about the bacon board that too was delicious with six pieces of bacon plenty to share so everyone can get a sample, and my son opted for the breakfast burger with next time I come that's definitely what I'm going to get it looked simply amazing.
We opted to get the Mimosa Flight which was awesome I had a pineapple, the Tiffanie blue, Caribbean, and strawberry.
Come prepared to spend a little money but it is well worth every penny.

Having been here several times I'm surprised I haven't written a review yet. One of the staples here in Tucson which has been around forever and never fails!! I've come on different days at different times & I've always gotten the best & most flavorful hotdogs & fresh & hot crispy French fries. 
I'd suggest going with the hot chili dogs with grilled onions they are packed with flavor & just the right amount of kick to massage your taste buds in all the right places. If not in the mood for a hot dog they also serve delicious hamburgers fish & chips and fried shrimp. 
The prices are extender reasonable the portion size is excellent to fill up a grown man. 
Pats a place I'm always sure to bring out of state guests.

The ambience of the restaurant has a western look to it kind of old &  dusty that has indoor as well as outdoor seating with benches and tables and some old chairs, that are not too comfortable. 
With wall hangings some old out houses as well as mounted animals on the walls.
it's kind of cool that the fire pit is outside so as you walk up you get the smell the food as it's cooking let me tell you the food smells a whole lot better than the actual taste.
So where do I start let's start with the pricing. the pricing,  for what you get is a bit much but it's typical of a steakhouse so I did come prepared to spend money but I also came prepared for a good steak that did not happen. I like to get my steak medium well so that I can get some pink mine came dry and well done and I do not like to send my food back for fear of something happening to it so I had no choice but to tuff it up and eat the dry over cooked unseasoned steak; two others at the table who ordered well done theirs were cooked to perfection in fact was medium well, funny how that happened. The beans were runny with no flavor, there was bread provided salad that was overdressed & lacked tomatoes and cucumbers and had a few strands of carrots. 
I truly felt sorry for another guest at our table her chicken was so dry it look like it was chicken jerky she poured so much barbecue sauce on it to try to help the situation but that didn't help she couldn't even eat it.  A few people ordered the beef ribs and those were delicious I did get taste them.
My cousin ordered a slice of pecan pie to go when it came out we thought it was a joke the slice was hilarious it looked as if someone had scraped the bottom of the pie pan an placed it in the to go box good thing the waitress to realize that and stated oh I did not even put that on the bill yeah do you think we would've paid for that... 
I have to admit the wait staff was very attentive and friendly but I don't think I have any plans on returning anytime soon.

It is borderline treasonous how delicious this place is! 

Wise tip: if you're not Indian, do not let them convince you that you should get the "medium" spiciness. They conned me into this (probably because of my skin color) and my meal simply wasn't spicy enough. When I return, I'm going straight for the hot! 

I want to go back right now.

Walking towards Philter the first thing you notice is an eye-catching patinated bronze and wrought-iron sculpture above a colorful and vibrant planter box. This gorgeous example of metalwork was created by a local craftsmanship and is, pun intended, a sign of good things to come. 

I ordered their single-origin espresso, a Papua New Guinea Kunjin from Ceremony Coffee Roasters, grabbed their copy of Drift (Volume 3: Havana) and took a seat by the window.  Below I found a beautiful little garden with a tiny string of LED lights snaking through leaves and stems. It reminded me of the 'desert' wing at Longwood Gardens and I found myself slip into a pleasant daydream until my espresso was brought over by a smiling barista.  The espresso was fruit forward, mildly acidic, a complex body, slightly tangy finish with notes of caramel, blackberry and nutmeg. 

After finishing the accompanying sparking water I went to thank the person who crafted my beverage and was introduced to Chris, the owner.  That began a wonderfully engaging conversation about the genesis of Philter, his passion for coffee and a recounting of the half-a-year build-out.  

Among the many nuanced decorating decisions, Chris explained that the front counter used to be the woodworking bench of a nonagenarian carpenter.  The piece was purchased at an estate auction, cleaned up but with all the character intact; it even includes the original castors.  It is a subtle homage to the life's work of an artisan who spent the better part of a century crafting and repairing goods for innumerable families.  

The interior is simply stunning; a harmonious combination of reclaimed materials, plants and whimsical accents.  Hand pounded zinc counter-tops, copper light fixtures, hardwood floors, tables and shelving create an elegant rustic charm.   Regional prints and original works adorn the walls, a small retail section interspersed with succulents and a reference library of coffee related publications all speak to the aesthetic and cohesive vision wonderfully orchestrated by Chris and his team. 

I visited again a few days later as I made my way back to Baltimore and enjoyed another stellar experience.  


Final Verdict:  Philter serves the best coffee between Baltimore and Philadelphia.  More than that, it tells a story.  The narrative speaks of passion, dedication and the three-year anniversary of business that was ten years in the making; evocative of the past with plan for the future. I cannot wait to return!

I've been having a great time recently trying places I've passed tons of times. This stop it was Frey Smoked Meats. I've smelled the deliciousness of there smoked meats on so many occasions on my runs through mid city and never stopped in, #bigmistake. First up was the hard lemonade cocktail. It's not your typical vodka and fresh lemonade mixture because they add a special ingredient... A SPLASH OF VANILLA and it makes all the difference. I had the smoked sausage plate which was yummy as well. After my lovely visit down to Little Havana in Miami I fell in love with Cuban sandwiches so it was only fitting I tried the Bar-B-Que Cuban. It was everything I imagined. I wasn't going to go for dessert but I was talked into trying the Cookie Monster Shake. I wish they would have taken a picture of my face when it came out. It's massive and meant for 2 people. I tried to eat it all but failed miserably.

This place is awesome! It really is pint-sized, but they're moving to a new location later this month. They'll be at 313 Watson Road, St. Louis, MO 63139, right near Arsenal. The last day at this location is this Friday 4/8. 

I'm amazed that I haven't tried this place out earlier, since I live in the area and I have a weakness for sweets, especially as well executed as they do here at this adorable bakery. When you walk in, there's a counter display for all kinds of gorgeous goodies. There are cash registers at either end of the counter. 

My husband and I got a brookie (brownie with cookie dough baked into the center of it) and a dreamsicle cookie sandwich. It came to about $6 or $7 for both, but the brookie was huuuge and they were so delicious! The brookie, I have to admit, was actually a bit on the chocolately side, even for me (and I loooove chocolate). I think it would have been perfect with a glass of milk! I'll have to remember that for next time. Also, I really liked the sprinkles on top of the brookie, so that there was a small crunch whenever I bit into the top of it. The sammie was pretty good; less dense than the brookie, so it was nice to break it up. The filling was airy and complemented the cookies on the outside. 

It was worth the time and money it took my husband and I to check them out. It seems like they really emphasize using local ingredients. Also, they don't use preservatives, so evidently everything is baked from scratch every day. If that doesn't deserve 5 stars, then I don't know what is! 

They don't have an official opening date yet for the new location, but you can check out their facebook page for the latest details. I can't wait to visit them there and try other yummy things!

A solid four stars! This is a great restaurant with an awesome concept and vision, a nice, laid-back atmosphere, and delicious food! 

I came here for a quick dinner with my husband recently. We had just left the gym and neither of us were feeling up to making dinner (and no leftovers to fall back on). 

We had the buffalo cauliflower bites as an appetizer. It was really really delicious! It did get a tad bit spicy for me towards the end of finishing them off, but they were so tasty that I didn't really care. 

As for the entree, I had the winter quinoa wrap ($8.95). It had quinoa, shredded carrot, walnut parmesan, cranberries, kale, roasted butternut squash, cauliflower and caramelized leeks with kale pesto sauce wrapped in a whole wheat tortilla. Whew! I had to look that up on their website because I couldn't remember all the ingredients in there. The combination of flavors that the wrap had was incredibly complex and interesting and delicious. I loved the wrap! 

My husband had the Buffalo Blue Burger ($6.95), which he enjoyed as well, although he did say that he liked my quinoa wrap slightly better because of the unique and refreshing combination of flavors in mine. 

In summary, the food was great, the prices are reasonable, the atmosphere is relaxing, and the service was prompt and friendly. The only thing to take note of is the street parking, but that goes for pretty much every place on south Grand. So go try them out, even if you're not a vegetarian... you'll most likely still find something delicious and filling!

I've been looking forward to checking this place out since they opened, so I was happy to get a chance this past week. I wasn't disappointed! 

My partner and I got two kolaches and a doughnut. Both kolaches were delicious and I can't decide which one I liked more, the 3 cheese and bacon one or the everything one. The bacon was thick and savory and the cheeses on top were a perfect complement. The everything kolache was well seasoned and I enjoyed the cheese filling in the middle. 

The lemon poppyseed doughnut had a cherry glaze on top. The balance of sweet and tart flavors was great! The bread was denser than what I normally expect from a doughnut, but that didn't stop me from enjoying it! 

I love the space. It's pretty cozy, but they make it work. The decor is adorable and I love how the windows fill the whole space with light. Other amenities include a clean unisex bathroom with a baby changing table and high chairs if you need them. 

I'm so glad Knead moved into the neighborhood!

I really enjoyed my experience here. I came on a weekday with my spouse and baby just after they opened. Their lunch menu is smaller than their dinner menu, but we both still found enticing dishes to order. Our server did a great job walking us through the top sellers and her favorites, which was helpful since it was our first time. 

I enjoyed my pad Thai, which I got with shrimp and tofu instead of chicken and tofu. The flavor was great, not too sweet, and there was the perfect amount of garnishes like peanuts, sprouts, and green onions, to round out the well cooked noodles and the protein. The whole dish was only $10 and it was quite a large portion. If you're not super hungry, it's enough for two meals. 

The flavor of my spouse's dish was superb, though I'm not sure I would order it myself because I might not be able to make it through the whole dish on account of the spice level. He got the khao soi, which had such a flavorful sauce! 

The ambience is lovely. Street parking was fine for us but could be tricky during busy hours. Decently priced. Oh and the Thai tea was good - I could taste the strong and delicious tea base! I'd like to come back to try their dinner menu at some point!

I really enjoyed my visit here last weekend. It seems like a great local place. Our server was very attentive and friendly; she came by just the right amount - never let our waters get empty but didn't smother us. 

I ordered the smoked salmon panini and I really enjoyed it! It had capers and some kind of lemon-y sauce and small apple slices in it. I never would have thought to put salmon and apple together, but it was delicious! My sandwich came with oregano fries which were perfectly crispy. 

I was only inside for a minute, but the decor looks very modern and clean. My friends and I sat on the patio outside. It was wonderful to have that chance to enjoy the spring weather. 

I would definitely return again and I will probably have the falafel, which one of my friends ordered and thought was very tasty!

Ah, one of my go-to places when I'm at work (or immediately thereafter!). Great spot by the train tracks in East Falls--a swift hustle from the train station. They also have a private lot and usually a good bit of street parking.

The food is dern tasty. I've sampled pretty much everything on the menu and it's all freshly and finger-lickingly prepared. *Favorites include* classic buffalo wings, tater tots (yes! I said tater and tots!), the chicken or crab quesadillas and the burgers. 

I swear they done gathered 'bout 5 or 6 of my best uncles in that kitchen and they get. 
it. 
in. 

One time I even tried someone's fish and chips and chirren--the fish was piping hot, crispily fried and SEASONED. Usually folk don't know what to do with fried fish, but this isn't the case at Franklin's. 

The drink specials vary by the day--Troegs all day Tuesday is a good'un though! The Happy Hour specials are nize and there's a solid variety on tap. 

There's usually an event each night of the week--Quizzo on Tuesday nights, karaoke on Thursdays. If you enjoy people watching (i.e. side-eyes 'n snickers!) as much as I do then add one of these nights to your rotation. 

Seriously though--it's a really diverse, friendly, easy-going crowd. The place can get rowdy and rockin' some nights, but in spring and summer you can always bounce to the large deck for a quieter flow.

The service is pretty decent, and is pretty much what keeps this in the 4-star slot. I'm normally with larger parties, so I understand how challenging that can be--especially during happy hours. I've also been for lunch a couple of times and the service has been excellent.

I'm not a regular, regular, but Franklin's is enough of a sweet spot kind of place to make me keep trying to become one.

I've been eyeballin' this place for quite some time and am thrilled to report that it was worth all the oglin'! I can't remember what it was before, but I just remember it being a li'l too underwhelming to warrant return visits. Happily, that's not the case with El Poquito: Terrific atmosphere, super sweet, swift service, very tasty eats and a wonderfully tequila-laden beverage selection.

My friend and I shared a bountiful scoop of mega fresh, perfectly chunky 'n smooth guac. We each dined on chicken rice burrito bowls, which had me singin' serious notes of BYE CHIPOTLE . I don't know what kind of rice was in that bowl, but it was so delightfully fluffy and flavorful. As a dish, all of the flavors of the grilled chicken, the black beans, the queso and salsa melded together to create a really warm depth of flavor, and the portion was perfect. 

Try their seasonal margaritas fuh sho! Right about now they have 2 | the blood orange : tastefully tart :: the blackberry : sublimely sippable. The decor is a very inviting mix of rustic, a li'l funky and a li'l upscale, and it's one of a few places I've visited recently that had a volume level that didn't require constant yelling and the cupping of the ears to hear.

They do take reservations, but we went on a Sunday evening at around 7 and were seated immediately. It's lovely having a dependably delicious, reasonably priced Mexican establishment so close to home. If you're in Chestnut Hill, check it out!

We intended to hit up Grimaldi's, except that restaurant has still yet to be constructed. Alright BJ's you're getting our business... Seated within 5 minutes and greeted by Alejandra.  I like the interior of BJ's.  I like their beer selections.  Their menu has a good variety of choices.  It's a casual atmosphere.  TV's are even placed in the regular dining areas.  

Let's start with their limited edition Grand Cru beer and a draft root beer.  Hmmm that looks good - avocado egg rolls!!!  Lured by appetizing pictures, decided pretty quick on what to eat:

Salmon quinoa bowl - The winning dish in our lunch choices.  Enjoyed this very much; really tasty!  I can never get quinoa flavor to stick at home.  This bowl was really delish with the asparagus and red bell peppers.  Topped with a nice flaky flavorful salmon.  Nom-awesome!

Seared Ahi salad - Liked it not loved it.  Made sure we ate the ahi first cuz the rest of the salad was typical like any other.  The presentation was really pretty.  But our salad had to be redone due to a hair mixed into the salad.  

So how many of you say "can't dine at BJ's without having a Pizookie"?  Mmmhmmm... nobody's judging.  I think the same way hahaha!  Look I even ordered it to take out cuz Ness had to go to work.  It was still sweetly yummified and the vanilla bean ice cream scoop didn't melt on the way back.

Besides the salad hair mishap, our service during this visit was really good.  I hope the tips people leave for Alex all goes to her.  Dunno how it works there.  Thanks for taking care of our table Alex although we sorta rushed the end of our meal.

Beer lovers gotta try the Grand Cru before they run out!!!

After seeing a super cool movie Nessa was so eager to see, our temporary imagination escape made us work up an appetite.  Conveniently across the street from Century Riverside 12, she spotted movement inside Sierra St. Kitchen.  Let's go!

Immediately I'm admiring the interior charm.  Up a few steps is the bar, approximately 10 tables set, a wall with a see thru opening into the kitchen, and an entire wall that's a window facing the street scene.  Warm colors, cute light fixtures, and fancy likable art.  I have a crush on this place :)

Two waiters and two chefs... After 6:30 p.m. the restaurant was getting packed.  What an awesome job this small crew was doing though!  Very pleasant friendly and admittedly quick service.  

Wonderful Thanksgiving menu and fair deal.  But we went with small plates and hot toddies.  The only boo comment I had was the Lobster Ravioli was not hot (only warm).  However tying in all the plus factors, especially with the service on a holiday evening by a small staff, I'm weighing this on the most satisfactory experience for a first time visit.

Waited about 15 minutes, and as soon as we were seated we were asked for our drinks.  Then our actual waitress, Heather, approached a minute later.  Availability... very good for a busy eatery.  Hot chocolates please :)  Yes with whipped cream.

Their breakfast menu has eggs benedict!  It's Canadian bacon; no salmon or crab cakes benedict - still great!  Had the best creamy chunky clam chowder in yyyyeeeaaarrrss!  Last time was in San Francisco in a bread bowl.  Rosie's clam chowder gets bonus yay points! Eggs Benedict and Roast Beef Dip out to our table within 20 minutes.  Feeling full!

Ambience was what I'd call historical classic.  Except we see in color, not black and white.  It's as if a picture from the late, maybe 100+ years ago, came to life.  We went back in time a bit with the decor.  I love the ceiling detail, brass bars with glass, and the blue tones.

It was loud, but that just means people are enjoying their time.  It was busy, but that just means they have a well run restaurant.  There were Christmas Carolers - that's a treat.  You can play Keno while dining.  Nice experience to dine here this holiday weekend.

Sushi for days! I have been wanting to try this place since I moved here a year ago. My expectations were meant. The lunch specials are awesome and the sushi was absolutely delicious! 

$9.99 for 3 rolls and a salad or soup
$6.99 for 2 rolls and a salad or soup
$2 domestic and imported beer
Plus a ton of other dishes at great prices. 

I needed wifi and they gave me the password right away. The service was great and the servers were so friendly. This will be a regular spot for me now!

**400th review**

Amazing. Everything we ate was perfect. Our app, drinks, entrees and dessert were outstanding. The Berkshire Tomahawk Pork Chop was so tender and flavorful! I took a bite of my boyfriend's elk and it was just as good. 

This was our final dinner on our cross-country road trip and it was the best that we encountered. The interior decor is beautiful; we both fell in love with the blue wall and all of the little touches throughout the restaurant. We sat by the large windows and pretty much had the place to ourselves (4:30 p.m.) on a Tuesday evening. What a wonderful way to end an amazing trip. 

The chef came out to talk to us about one of the sides we were curious about. The service was great. But overall--I will remember that meal for a long time.

Absolutely great experience! I've ordered here before for pickup and had a great experience. 
Today we ordered lunch for a pre Mother's Day gathering. The food was ready in quickly. The staff were so sweet and friendly. They honestly have the perfect person at the register. 
We ordered the SuperDome, Bourbon St and bread pudding. They gave us two Dat Shyt drinks for free.  So with the Bourbon St I substituted my potato salad for lobster potatoes which was a very smart decision because those potatoes were so good. The lobster meat was tender the potatoes was smooth and creamy it was just a perfect combination. The chicken was fried perfectly it did not get soggy it was nice and crispy very very very tasty. Now for the Superdome The fish was cooked to perfection the potatoes again we're very good it was just a very delicious combination. The onion rings were very good the onions were not soggy the coating was crispy it was just a delicious combination of food. The bread pudding was a melt in your mouth delicious!!!! The praline sauce along with the taste of the actual bread pudding was amazing. 
I would order everything again hands down deliciousness.

I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed this restaurant. 
We gave this place a try out of curiosity. While looking over the menu the server brought over some warm focaccia bread and olive oil. The bread was light and airy and oh so tasty. For drinks we went with the frozen Limoncello and the house margarita. 
As an appetizer we ordered the crab cakes and asked for the kale mix to be placed on the side, one of my eating mates ordered a Caesar salad. Let's discuss this crab cake! Omg it was full of jumbo lump crab meat. It was extremely delicious and we considered ordering it as an entree. We made the suggestion to the Restaurant Manager who came over and chatted with us. He was very friendly and informative, he listened to our suggestions and was happy that we were enjoying our visit. The staff were friendly and helpful while making all of the choices on the menu. 
As an entree we chose Shrimp Pesto linguine which had a good amount of shrimp that were perfectly seasoned, the pesto cream sauce and pasta was amazing. We also had the lasagna, Beef short ribs which were very tasty and enjoyable. The lobster ravioli was cooked to perfection and a fair amount of lobster was in the ravioli and the sauce. The sauce was light and not to overpowering. The least favorite was the margarita pizza it was traditionally made but the cheese used wasn't to tasty. 
I will return for dinner and possibly happy hour. We enjoyed our visit for lunch so I know I'd enjoy dinner.

Awww man they've got something great over here. The Koran BBQ chicken sandwich is truly top tier deliciousness. 
Wasn't to crowded inside and the plexiglass around each booth, along with sanitizer and signs to wear a mask were great covid touches. 
Back to the sandwich it wasn't a large chicken sandwiches but sized pretty ok. Everything of course is a-la-cart I got the fries with the special Koran sauce. It tasted ok. 
I know this sandwich is probably a limited time offer so I will be going back soon to get another one!

I was served bad shrimp. Hey, it happens. What doesnt happen is I'm charged anyway and told to ask the manager to remove it. Yeah right. $50.00 tab later I've eaten my moms salmon and I'm fired up. Won't be back sadly. The manager was so sweet too, of course he didn't witness what his buffoon bar server told me. I hope he ate the shrimp in the back and got a bad case of the chimichurris! I drove so far for disappointment and possible sickness!

While visiting Philadelphia we decided to try out both Geno's Steaks as well as Pat's. We stood in the line for this steak shop to be dissapointed when we finally got our sandwiches.

The first issue we had here was that the staff was rude and short. I get it that you want to get the line moving quickly, but how about a "hello" or something more than "ya". The steak was greasy, the bread was hard, and the price was ridiculous for the finished product. Pat's was superior to this shop.

In the end the only redeeming factor about this restaurant is that it served it's purpose in filling our tummies with average steak and cheese. The next time we visit Philly we may try this spot again, but we will have to see how disappointed we are preparedto be.

Last note, your right, this is America but don't forget that this is a country of immigrants so how about you show some respect and remove those ridiculous signs from your storefront.

We're a crab house but we might not have any crabs or wet naps to clean your hands with. Oh yeah here's some gross fries since we ran out of the corn you ordered. We're still going to charge you for the price of corn though.

Never again.

Everyone has a bad day now and again, I get it, I do, but crappy food, terrible service and a manager who just didn't "get it" is enough for me to completely write this place off. 

After an event at La Encantada I suggested to my guest we go to Armitage for some lite bites. We decided to split the prime rib sliders and baked brie and when the food came I knew by looking at it I was going to be disappointed. The prime rib was fatty and the baked brie was SO baked it was sitting in a pool of oil melted beyond belief. I grabbed a slider and took a bite... dry, flavorless meat, hard to chew, hard to stomach. I moved on to the baked brie which was so over-baked it was near impossible to spoon it and make it stay on the bread it came with. I thought it was just me, but no, my friend Michelle agreed, both were nasty. 

And then began the waiting game, you know, where you're not happy with something, you want to bring it up but your server is MIA. So we waited, and waited, and waited. And maybe twenty minutes later our server showed up while Michelle was in the ladies room, and asked me if I wanted anything boxed up. Crappy meat and terrible baked cheese? No thank you. I explained that we weren't happy with either entree and she asked me if I had been to Armitage before (odd question). I explained to her it had been a while, and honestly the reason I don't go there is because of sub-par ingredients and terrible service. She apologized that the sliders were dry and said she'd take them off the bill and asked me if I wanted to box the cheese up. WHAT? I said no, the check please, and she promptly returned with the check for just the baked brie and sparkling water we ordered. Then the waiting game, the other one, where all you want to do is get the hell out but you can't find your server to run your card. Ten minutes later she showed up to process my card and when she dropped it off I started thinking, "I need to say something."

I walked up to a gentleman who looked manger-like and said "I'd like to speak to a manger if one is available." He said, "You are." Ok then. I explained my displeasure with the food and before I could even get the words out he said I know, I saw the sliders, they did look dry, glad we took those off your "menu" (Freudian slip anyone?), is there anything else? I told him that the brie was so over baked it was near impossible to eat, to which he asked whether or not I've had it before. Without being able to answer he explained that it came out exactly right, it's more of a dip. Really? Because it doesn't say that on the menu. I finally interrupted his worthless ramblings because he made it seem like that's how you get a word in, and said that the worst part of the experience, and the one I'm wanting him to know about, is that it took forever for our server to come back and check on us. His response, "I have to defend her there. She's not one of our best servers and if you look around we are slammed with people right now." Pssst, I'm one of those people, and although I give you credit for offering me a gift certificate to return, my experience with the staff and the exchange with the manager was met with so much displeasure, I'm fairly confident I won't return.

For future reference, "So sorry those two dishes weren't to your liking, come back try two more and we'll talk you through some of staff favorites. As far as service, I'm so sorry to hear that it was difficult to track your server down, I'll speak with her about why she may have been slow getting over to you and we'll address the issue once I know more." 

Know Before You Go: Yes, we all have our days, but if I can't even voice my concerns about my experience without be interrupted or shot down, I'll take my appetite and my hard earned dough elsewhere.

I could not have picked a more perfect place for me and my wife's one-year anniversary brunch. Not only is this the nicest restaurant in Philly, with by the far the best view of the city, the food is very good and the service is impeccable. I made reservations for a Saturday brunch and mentioned it was our anniversary. We arrived early and they sat us immediately at probably the best seat in the house. It was a white two-seater leather booth right up against the glass window with a Godly view of our beloved city. We got the four-course brunch, which was $88 per person (and totally worth it given the quantity and quality of food, ambience and service). We got a $60 bottle of sparkling wine. 

The wine was amazing. All of the food was delicious. The egg was like nothing I've ever had. So yummy. The tower was filled with extremely tasty selections. Everything was fresh and cooked to perfection. The almond pancakes with fresh berries was out of this world. The latkes were thin and crispy. I stuffed them with the smoked salmon. So good! The ham was Godsend. The avocado lettuce wraps were very refreshing. 

The entrees were so yummy. The Wagyu beef was perfectly cooked. The battered sea bass was unreal. The mustard aioli was very delicious. The dessert was super refreshing. I was very stuffed and we were on cloud nine after this meal. This was the most elegant and excellent brunch I have had in Philly. Be ready to drop a few hundo, but you wont regret it. We will be back for drinks and dinner. What a near perfect experience!

Always give wait staff the benefit of the doubt, but repeated rudeness and disregard for customer's concerns is insane. Original issue with waitress and then manager approached and downplays our table's issues. No apologies, no solutions. Accept our complaint, use a generic apologize and walk away. Thanks I

While Castleton Grill may not be my favorite restaurant of all time, I hold it very dear to my heart. As a Fort Wayne native, I grew up eating in the various local Hall's restaurants, so it goes without saying that I was pretty excited to find out that the Hall family had made its way into Indianapolis. 

Yes, the interior is dated and practically screaming for a contemporary update. And yes, I'm probably 20-30 years younger than the typical Castleton Grill patron. But they have a great beer selection, friendly staff, and a tasty menu, and isn't that all that REALLY matters? (And we can't forget the aforementioned hometown nostalgia!)

I've been here probably three times now; the service has always been excellent, and the food has always been properly cooked to our specifications. While I'm a creature of habit and have only gone back and forth between ribeye steaks and prime rib, the boyfriend has been a little more adventurous and tried both the salmon (Takaoka style - ANOTHER Fort Wayne staple!) and their burgers, each receiving thumbs up.

If you know what's good for you, you'll order Bud's brussel sprouts, which are flash-fried and served with cherry tomatoes, shredded cheese and a light, creamy sauce. Without a doubt, the best sprouts I've ever had - next to my own!

Thus far, the only mistake I've made at Castleton Grill was ordering a steak "garlic thyme" style. I enjoy thyme. I enjoy garlic. This, of course, lead me to believe that a steak "topped with fresh thyme and garlic steak butter" would be something I'd fall in love with. I was wrong. There was so much garlic on that steak it made me wince, and I spent more time scraping it off than I did eating the damn steak. On the plus side, however, I feel quite confident that I am now completely immune to vampires. *Please note this has NOTHING to do with their actual steaks, which I've truly enjoyed each time I've dined in. I simply won't order a "style" again. 

They had a fun promotion running in December wherein you received a red envelope that, inside, contained one of a variety of prizes (free dinner for a year, free movie tickets, free appetizers, etc). The shtick was to save your envelope, unopened, and bring it back in January to claim your prize. A fun thing to do for the holidays, and I look forward to  returning this month to see what's inside my red envelope!

So I went there twice more during my visit.  My mom drove down from Phoenix and we shared the adobo and the walnut shrimp.  The adobo was good - three tender pieces of chicken and lots of sauce.  For the walnut shrimp, Eric uses yogurt instead of condensed milk.  He says the yogurt is healthier but I also like that it gives the dish a bit of sourness which makes it more like a meal to me.  Some people make the walnut shrimp sweet and it tastes like some kind of weird dessert.

On my final trip, I had to order the Pad Thai because I had to know why my friends kept talking about it.  And...Wow!...It probably was the best I've ever had.  Lots of pork and shrimp and well-seasoned.  I couldn't finish my meal and took it home.  It's even better for breakfast.

When my partner and I pay 12 dollars including tip for two smallish coffees, we expect them to be warm. We were both served lukewarm lattes (milk not frothed long enough). When I IMMEDIATELY asked if they could be warmed, we were instructed to bring them to the microwave (as we were tipping). Excuse me? I just paid $6 for each coffee and was given a coffee that was about room temperature. This is completely unacceptable. First and last time that I will visit this establishment. Enjoy the tip, jerks.

I went to a Steak 'n Shake in Virginia and it was great, but this one is horrendous. It was honestly like a completely different place. I ordered a steak burger with seasoned fries and a shake. Well it took over an hour to get the food. I couldn't believe it, all the workers were incompetent and lazy. I finally got my food and it was nothing like the one in Virginia. My burger was average, the bun was a little soggy and the burger was small. The flavor of the burger was good, but not great. Even though I ordered seasoned fries they gave me plain ones which were generic shoestring fries with no flavor. The flavor of the shake was good, but there was chunks of ice in it. Overall, this place was bad and the service was garbage.

Today was my 9th Proper visit. Here's my summary of all things Proper.

Ambiance 5 stars
The bright and open feel of Proper is a refreshing addition to downtown Tucson. The space is comforting and multifaceted. Depending on your mood, you can sit at the bar, the communal high top, the booths, private group area, or traditional tables. Besides during dinner rush, they let you choose. 

Service 5 stars
Everyone here wants you to know that they appreciate your patronage. Right from the start you'll be welcomed by one of their polite greeters or managers, seated, and promptly served water by your waiter. Each of the five different servers I've had were knowledgeable, friendly and most importantly timely. I've never sat wanting of anything, nor felt annoyed by an overzealous waiter. On your way out, you will be thanked several times, including by the cooks who wave you out the door.

Brunch 5 stars
This is my favorite meal at proper. Hands down amazing. The portion size and price are spot on, and you will leave completely satisfied. My suggestions are the super flavorful Baked Egg. The tomato sauce is the best I've had in a very long time. Today, I feel in love with my Steel Cut Oats with macerated cherries, hazelnuts, brown sugar, and cream. It was the perfect amount of sweet while still feeling light and healthy afterwards. My Gramma loved her North West Bowl and the man actually couldn't finish his Proper French Toast it was so deliciously rich, so I helped. They also serve Exo coffee, so drink up!

Dinner 4 stars
Contrary to what some other reviews have said, the portion sizes here are what they say they are: bites, small, or big, and are Properly priced. The food here is not American Supersized. Please do not come here expecting a "big" dish to be a 3,000 calorie meal that is unhealthy and full of salt. You SHOULD come here expecting flavorful, well balanced dishes that will put a smile on your face and leave you capable of walking out the door, down the street, or wherever you may be off to next. My favorites so far were the Proper Salad, the Ricotta Gnocchi and Shrimp and Grits. My bf loved the Crispy Skin Duck Breast, but it wasn't quite crispy enough for me.

Bar 3 stars
While sitting at the bar with my favorite bartender Cassie with the windows open and people watching could become a past time for me, I unfortunately wish it were with a different drink in my hand. I am not a fan of beer, so if that is your style, you may not feel the same way as me. Their wine list is overpriced for the quality, the house red is too tannic for my tastes, and the wine I would like to drink on the list only comes by the bottle. I have tried all of their cocktails except for the ones with Tequila (which I unfortunately can't drink) and while I find them refreshing, they don't stand up to other cocktails you can get downtown. I would recommend trying the Porch Tea if you like rosemary, and the Sagacious if you like gin.

Late night (Bites) 3 stars
Unfortunately, this is the one time of the night when I wished they had something a little more, well, absorbent on the menu (besides $5 french fries). I don't eat a lot of red meat or pork, or wings, so this menu doesn't offer me much. I wasn't a fan of the pork belly sliders, although they were by no means bad. My bf eats A LOT of Sonoran Hotdogs, and was extremely skeptical of an $8 Sonoran Hotdog. However, he is now a believer. According to him, it is PERFECT. Try it.

Lunch I can't have an opinion on yet. I'll be back to update when I can convince myself not to order brunch for lunch.

Stopped in here for lunch yesterday after wanting to try for a while.

Breakfast menu looked great, but I opted for a fried chicken style sandwich. Portion sizes were enormous and there were loads of options.

The atmosphere in here is a cute updated diner, not too far off from the Atlantic, but updated with 1950s dinettes and benches. 

Seating is limited, so grab a seat while you peruse the menu!

Lee's has been a staple in this neighborhood for over 20 years. I have seen this place develop from a simple deli to a restaurant that serves items like: Game Over Cheesesteak (chicken topped with shrimp and broccoli or spinach). Trust me, this was not on the menu five years ago. Although it is a development due to the changing area of Cedar Park area, Lee's does it right. The food and atmosphere continues to be budget affordable and kid friendly. 

You want a quick tasty breakfast before jumping on the trolley? This is the spot. Looking for a midday bite? This is the spot. Thinking of dinner on your from work? This is the spot. Amazing food, great owner and a personal touch that many places are missing these days. 

I cannot comment on any of the vegan dishes, not my taste, but the cheesesteaks have always hit the spot for me!

OMG! Somebody take away my car keys! Just ate a few Pat's chili dogs and I want to go back for more! This place is always on my mind but I rarely get a chance to stop in. It's such a treat. Prices are great, you get a whole lot of food for a small price. Don't expect anything fancy, it's just a drive-in place. But that's what's so great about it. Drive up, order, get your dogs, and go home. 

If you don't like hot dogs, chili, greasy fries, then skip Pat's. It's silly to say but too many reviews criticize those very things. Pat's is great at what it does and doesn't pretend to be anything else.

Yes, this is a BBQ place. Yes, they have delicious whiskey choices. Yes, their brisket is to die for. Most importantly; however, is that Salt+Smoke has, hands down, the best mac and cheese that I've ever eaten in a restaurant! (Sorry, I don't think anyone can make better mac and cheese than my own mother!)

Located in the Loop, Salt+Smoke provides a buzzing ambiance that fits right in with the rest of the neighborhood! I've only been there when it's absolutely full, and I've never had an issue getting my food quickly. Salt+Smoke is always my #1 recommendation for visitors coming to the St. Louis area!

An Indian restaurant can generally be judged by the quality of its dal and roti--the staples.  So it was a pleasant surprise to enjoy the dal at The India Club--the best I have arguably had in years. 

The Club has a diverse menu--the usual suspects in North Indian fare.  The setting is casual.  You wait in line to order, and then wait for your food to be ready.  The process is extremely efficient, so you will likely not have to wait long.

Come to The Indian Club for casual Indian dining without the formality of a proper eat-in Indian dining experience.  Stick to the staples though.  I was not entirely pleased with some of their other dishes, including the chana masala.  Having said that, I could have their dal in perpetuity every day   I am ready to go clubbing again!

Tony's is a class act all the way from start to finish.  Find me a New York restaurant that delivers flawless service, a tasty three-course dinner and a drink, and a spacious setting, all for about $50 in my case, and I will find that elusive sixth star on Yelp to award it.  No wonder Tony's has earned more accolades than MJ has trophies.

To start with, valet parking comes into play as you approach the restaurant.  You are welcomed by what seems like an eager team of four or five, and then escorted to the table and seated with an honorable mention of your last name.  Thankfully, not my long one, the last time I was here.

The salads we ordered were fresh and appetizing, the risotto was next only to the one I have had at Gramercy Tavern, and the wine list, if you are into wines, is longer than the Elite membership roster of Yelp.  The desserts were filling, even if not spectacular.
