One would hardly expect to experience a restaurant of this caliber in St. Louis.  Make an evening out of visiting the arch and then dining at Tony's.  You will doubtless be pleased at how far your money can go.  And how endearing and attentive the recipients can be.  Only at Tony's.

DO NOT GO TO "ALL YOU CAN EAT SUSHI" WEEK

I'm currently at my table in pod, suffering through their awful attempt at all you can eat sushi.

We were seated at our reservation time, 9pm, and we have spent about ten minutes eating our first plates of sushi, and 2.5hours waiting while the restaurant grinds to a stop. It is completely packed, and totally unprepared for this.

People have been waiting hours with nothing, and although some are being comped appetizers by an obviously nervous and overwhelmed staff, the general mood is tense and aggravated.

The small amount of sushi that actually made it to our table was good, and the staff is doing well considering, especially our waitress - but the whole situation is a mess and has alienated us and I imagine most of the other patrons. (Table next to us is discussing walking out right now)

They are not equipped for this. What probably started at some pr guy's desk as a way to drum up mid week business has ended up as a huge disaster.  

As I'm typing this people have left, walked out, and turned away round three of free appetizers in disgust

This place sacrifices the basics of service on the altar of cool. 

The pizza might be great, but only those willing to jump through hoops all night or move to fishtown will ever get to find out, so who cares?

It's Sunday morning, 8:20 AM and I have 40 minutes until I meet the seller, inspect the goods and make the purchase (Shhhh!).   I've been driving around checking out the area and I see Joe's.   I prefer going to a local business rather then a nationwide chain if I can and this fit the bill perfectly.

DECORE & SERVICE:  It's not fancy and is a bit older, but it's clean and has a lot of character!   The service was friendly, efficient and FAST, even after ordering.   Three different servers tried to give me coffee, but I don't drink coffee.  My server checked on me a few times, which I appreciate.   Restrooms are on the back side of the kitchen, but you can't go through the kitchen, so you have to go out the door, to the right about 20 feet and in that door.

FOOD:  I ordered the Chorizo and egg scramble with hash browns "well done".   My food arrived VERY quickly after ordering (maybe 6 minutes?) and they did such a good job of scrambling, I was wondered where the eggs were!   LOL   The chorizo had a really good flavor and was NOT greasy (my biggest complaint about most chorizo).  The hash browns, while good,  weren't as "well done" as I think they could be or should be, but then I'm picky about my hash browns.

OVERALL:  It's a really great, friendly, LOCAL place with good food where they'll make you feel like a good friend.

If I lived in Philadelphia...I mean Philly cause that's what I would call it if I lived there right? So if I did live in Philly, I would be at Reading Terminal Market every day. I would also be 100 lbs heavier because I would be eating a dozen Beiler's donuts, a couple of cannolis from Termini Brothers, Philly cheesesteaks galore, ice cream at Bassetts...

You can find everything here. Not just food but other goods as well. It does get super busy though so try to find non-peak times. But if you want to soak in all the food goodness that is Philadelphia, just go here. You'll find everything!

Update: Look I don't want to argue with anyone about Korean food. However I am actually Korean, been to Korea several times, stayed with relatives and eaten out with relatives in Seoul and a few other places but mainly Seoul, so I am not as familiar with other regional cuisines. I have never been to Seoul Kitchen before so I have no prior affiliation with this place, staff, etc. I am always just looking for good food, whatever ethnicity.

Authentic Chinese food is very different from what is served in other countries. And in the US it varies quite a bit, even dishes with the same name. I have NEVER had pork bulgogi the way some posters seem to have had it. I am sure it is NOT authentic if it isn't a full porkchop--although that doesn't mean what is served is always the best tasting, however authentic. My mother is a great cook and that's the way it is made when she cooks it and how I was taught to cook it. I've gone to restaurants in the past that require Korean language to order anything-and they seem the most traditional. However, that doesn't mean restaurants don't serve pork bulgogi in different ways. Even Seoul Kitchen serves what I would call NOT authentic chicken bulgogi--I have NEVER had it served that way before. It was pretty tasty, just not traditional.

I will ask my parents about it next time I talk to them. They were both born and raised in Korea. I find a lot of people just don't know what is authentic ethnic food--I never knew what real Chinese food was like until I met a Chinese guy in college and he took me to a Chinatown. It's NOTHING like the typical Americanized Chinese restaurants that a lot of my friends enjoy.

By the way, I've been to more than a few US Korean restaurants, and I found they are often not authentic, seem to cater to the Americanized customers, which is good for their business. I found authentic Korean food hard to come by, even in places like NYC, where some are just a bit trendy.

As for being treated differently, unfortunately that almost always occurs in any ethnic restaurant. I've been to Chinese restaurants with a special Chinese language menu and Korean ones the same.

Just went there tonight. My wife and I thought it was very good.

We had japchae, the standard Korean style stir fried noodles, and my wife preferred it to the one at Takamatsu. There is a noticeable sesame oil flavor and it is not as sweet as some versions.

The BBQ chicken was good but I did not expect it to be a little spicy--I never had it spicy at other restaurants before. It's not really hot but my kids couldn't eat it. The quality of the actual chicken meat is just average but the marinade is tasty. I'd say the vegetables are a bit modern and not traditional but do not detract from the dish.

We also had the jampong( sp?), spicy seafood soup, and this was very consistent with the best I have had.  My wife pointed out that she thought it could use some salt, which I agreed with, but in retrospect I think it is no less salty than what I have had before, including in Korea.

The banchan, side dishes, were all good. I preferred the gakduki, spicy radish kimchi, over the cabbage kimchi--which I thought was a bit too salty, although my wife thought it was actually not as salty as what she had had at other restaurants.

We had the chicken yakitori as an appetizer, not a Korean dish, and this seemed very non-Japanese compared to what I have had at Japanese restaurants in the US and at a Japanese yakitori restaurant in Korea. However, my kids loved it so I can 't complain.

Service was prompt, polite, and the food came out quickly. It was not crowded but a telling sign was that almost every patron was Korean.

I'd like to add my own two cents to Maynard's complaint. Obviously never had pork bulgogi, which is basically a porkchop marinated in a spicy bean paste marinade and then cooked. He got exactly what that is. It's very simple. I've made it often myself. It's VERY different from the beef bulgogi and  understandably quite a shock to someone who assumes bulgogi means the same thing applied to different types of meat. There are several Korean dishes which sound the same but are VERY different so you really have to know what you are ordering.

I'm Korean by the way, although born in the US, but I've been to Korea as well as to many Korean restaurants on both coasts, so  I think I have some knowledge about Korean food.

1864 Tavern is now one of my favorite cocktail bars in Reno.  The first indication that they're good is that they have a big display of fresh produce.  Then I watched them mix drinks, and they used real juices.  To my dismay, however, I kid you not, people were ordering vodka tonics and Coors Light, despite their 16 or so beers on draft, mostly independent.  Then again, this is Reno.  If you want a successful bar in Reno, you have to sell the crap, and I used to be poor and sometimes $5 can be too expensive for beer.  I certainly don't blame the college kids who have to eat ramen and frozen burritos if they want enough money to party.  The bartender even gave this group a free Moscow Mule variant to taste, and they tasted it and LEFT IT ON THE BAR!  You know, if I went to a cheese shop and had a taster of disgusting French foot fungus, sure I'll leave the taster unfinished but alcohol!  Come on!  It would have to taste like French foot fungus for me to leave at the bar, and that has never happened.  I finish even Death & Taxes overly bitter cocktails.  Of course, that will never beat the dude at a bar who got a taster of beer, said he liked it and ordered a full pint, THEN LEFT THE TASTER UNFINISHED!!!!!  WTF???  Hey buddy, take a sip of your pint, now check this out, I'm going to pour the remainder of your taster into your pint.  MAGIC FREE BEER!!!!!!  

The place has that certain hipster retro Victorian décor you'll find at Death & Taxes minus the vampirish darkness.  It's a bit too open in my opinion and needs something to break up the room.  The biggest flaw in my opinion being a single dude is the lack of bar stools.  I also tend to drink quicker standing than sitting down, so I went through my four cocktails pretty fast, none of which were bad and most were great.

Very good Jackson Square diner located on the corner of Jackson Square.  Tourists and locals alike go here for bananas foster French toast, eggs Benedict with oysters or soft shell crab and standard poboys and gumbo.  If you can't make up your mind they will let you order two different dishes in half portions each.  The diner has a very casual vibe and fairly loud noise level and would be a good place to take rug rats.  Stanley may not have the hype of higher rated places but for a good local experience come here.

Mother's claims to have the best ham in the world but I prefer their standard New Orleans dishes whenever I visit.  I've had their ham before and it is good but I can get good ham in my own city.  I prefer their excellent poboys and gumbo.  There is a sign on the wall that says no tipping is allowed.  They are serious about not accepting tips which I've only seen in Japan.  The funny thing is the service at Mother's is better than most competitors.  Fast, polite, humble and I always get called darlin' or sugar.  Being from Seattle I've never been called darlin' or sugar, especially from strangers.  Eating at Mother's is like eating at your own mother's.

This place is just great all around. The environment is soooooo nice. The food is DELISH! Everything I tasted was full of flavor and smelled great. It's truly my inner fat girl heaven. The staff was very hands on and friendly. The owner came to our table and made us feel very welcome. There is seating at the bar as well as tables all around. If you'd like to chill and watch some sports feel free to do so here. I will definitely become a regular. 

There's $2 drink specials for happy hour. Also, buy 1 dozen oysters get a half dozen free during happy hour. 

Foodie heaven!

I tired this place with a bunch of my fiance's co-workers and my fiance. The pizza here is amazing and very flavorful. Like similar restaurants it is great for groups, but unlike similar restaurants they also have some good vegetarian options.

As for me... there is a reason I have a saying for how much cheese should be on a pizza. The saying? "There is no such thing as to much cheese!" And this place puts the perfect ammount of cheese on their pizzas without making them to greasy. Also, and this may sound odd to some, but for me the mark of a good pizza is one that can even be enjoyed cold the following day. Mellow Mushroom pizza not only tastes great cold, but in my opinion, it is slightly better cold.

The service here is also great with the wait staff being very accommodating and flexible with customer requests and orders. I look forward to returning soon for more awesome pizza from Mellow Mushroom (second only to Pie in the Sky for variety and better than CPK) as soon as next month when family is in town.

Finally, when I went there, we had 9 people splitting 4 pies  and some garlic bread appetizers; thus, the final cost came out to about $7.50 a person... not bad.

I was beginning to think Nashville didn't have any bad restaurants, but I was mistaken.  A birthday party of 6 of us were sat at 7:00 pm and it took 45 minutes to get our drinks and an additional 20 minutes to get our water.  We had to ask for water 3 times and then had to approach management before we had water at the table.  Our server was nice, but seemed like he had never waited tables before.  The table next to us had him as well and they requested another server.  
Now on to the food.  I ordered the filet and lobster.  No flavor whatsoever to the beef and the lobster tail was skimpy at best.  We ordered a few sides one of them being asparagus, which is $8.00.  I am not kidding you that the server brought a small plate of 5 ASPARAGUS SPEARS.  I asked him where the side was and he said that was it and asked if we would like to order another.  I kind of lost it at that point.  Was the asparagus gold plated?!?  Did they fly it in from Dubai?!  He then brought out a plate with an appropriate number of spears for the $8.00 price tag.  I also did not have a potato like the rest of the party.  I asked for my potato when we were served and did not receive it until after I had finished both my filet and lobster tail.  
When we finished our alcoholic beverages the server took our glasses and left abruptly without asking if we wanted any other beverages.  I could have really used another glass of wine at that point, but to no avail.  
Spare yourself a trip to Jimmy Kelly's and go to any one of the other steakhouses in town.  Worst restaurant experience in Nashville hands down.
I'm a Colombian far away from home, until yesterday. Mais has the taste and flavor of the authentic food of my country, excellent service, good price and the best food, it fills your soul.

Things are heating up in St. Pete over the best cuban sandwich...we now have a new contender. Tia's be thy name.

As usual with trying new latin food places, I typically bring my other foodie friends with me from work and 2 are from a Spanish heritage and have feasted on many traditional homemade-grandma style food at home. (I'm so jealous of them). 

We were drawn in by the lure of a new cuban and boy did this place deliver. (And they do deliver too btw) Excellently seasoned roast pork (pulled, not sliced),  the perfect amount of ham (I hate when places overdo this to cover up their lack of pork) and all the other fixin's. Two words: De Lish. It was pressed just right, warm throughout the sandwich (hate the cold center at other places). Pretty much, the best we've had in the area in awhile (Since Nita's closed). -pic attached

How can we go to a new place and just try the cuban? We can't. On of my spanish friends ordered the roast chicken which he described as being "fall-off-the-bone-good" and all meals are served w/ two sides...he got yellow rice and black beans and said everything was on par with how his grandmother would have made it. -pic attached

The rest of us got the roast pork (how could you not?!?!) and it was juicy, fresh, seasoned just right and tasted so good that I'm having a Pavlovian response right now just thinking about it. I had split the cuban and the pork with a friend so we could try both. We got the yellow rice and red beans. Now, a note on the yellow rice...it's not just yellow...its almost like yellow "dirty" rice...the kind you get at home with a bit of sausage and other bits in it to add some more flavor. Oh so good. -pic attached

All-in-all we all gave this place a huge thumbs up and will definitely be returning. Not to mention trying their breakfast burrito's which if they're half as good as the other things we had, we'll be in for a treat.

Worst service I ever experienced here. Food is often hit or miss but I still opted to dine here. Never again. The thin Asian woman (maybe the owner) was extremely rude! Our hot and sour soup was cold. My shrimp were undercooked and frankly not fresh. I asked to send it back for something else. She returned with the same plate that I returned. I again repeated I didn't want it. She refused to bring me anything else. She never returned to even refill my iced tea or asked if my dining companion needed anything else. When we finally asked for a refill (which we paid for) she ignored me, returned with a pitcher and slammed the glass down. There's more but I'm certain I won't return so it doesn't matter much! No need to return for mediocre food.

If I had rated this place after my first trip, it would have been 4 stars because I loved the carrot cupcake dessert - which was more of a carrot mousse sweetened with a date. This made my whole trip. They did have some problems on this trip, but I blame it on starting up problems. 

So fast forward to a month later when I decided to give them another try. 
... and my love for them was ruined - 

I CANNOT get over the fact that they served me water with lipstick still on it. I understand that some lipsticks are hard to wash off, so you go over it with a towel. They didn't do that. I touched the lipstick to see if it was just really stuck on. Nope, I was so disgusted. I'll spare you the details about the texture of the lipstick on the glass. 

I also CANNOT get over that they served me lukewarm coffee. Not iced, not hot - lukewarm. And when we asked the waiter about it, his response was that it must have lost some of its heat in the filtering process. 

The carrot cupcake was good, but not enough of a reason to go back.

Since it's been 4 years since I last reviewed the place, it's time to update my review. I love this place even more now with some of its great changes. 

The initial process is still the same: walk in, pick out your bottles of wine, and they will uncork it and give you glasses for your wine that you can then take outside and sit in their backyard. But now you have the additional option of going upstairs to sit. 

The upstairs has quite a few great features: less bugs than sitting in the back yard. They keep the windows open so you can look out the window and see the Mississippi, or at least the tops of the ships. They also have a full cocktail bar upstairs. 

They have also installed a permanent kitchen, so their menu is more set and consistent, and less on the whim of the invited chef. The sea salt chocolate is always a favorite. 

The only downside is lack of music because of complainy pant neighbors. Even without the music, its still a lively and fun place to go.

As the current Duchess of Mojo, I can speak with full authority that this place is awesome! Lots of seating, and plugs for you to work. I love their pastries, coffee and teas. Sandwich bar will be added as soon as the manufacturer makes it. And in awful summer heat and humidity, this place is a welcome respite. 

And they take credit cards!

Do you ever feel like sometimes you were born inside The Matrix? While everyone one else's brain is receiving signals that say the food is juicy and delicious, all you taste is 'a single cell protein combined with synthetic aminos, vitamins, and minerals... everything the body needs' but taste buds don't desire.


THE SCENE

I read the reviews and came here with the highest of expectations. Immediately this place began to sweet talk me. I saw the meat smoker, which was a huge turn on! The sides were open exposing delicious pink meats being slow cooked right in front of my eyes like a sexy dance! I also saw the real wood stacked out back below a large tree with branches full of REAL LIVE chickens... yes I said chickens! (BTW the way, did anyone else know chickens climb trees or am I still inside the Matrix?) As a final act of foreplay, the interior decor was just right, like candles burning around a hot bubble bath. It had that seductive gritty down home feeling I like when enjoying BBQ. The only thing missing from this BBQ romance was blues music playing live!

The chef allowed me to sample several items since I just couldn't decide what I wanted my sides to be. They'd run out of mac n' cheese, which would have been my first preference, however, the collard greens and chicken n' rice were amazing! This took my BBQ expectations even higher as I anticipated a foodgasm once I got my hands on the pork ribs I ordered. Unfortunately, this romance was not meant to be.


THE FOOD

The ribs were smoked to the point of tasting like cigarette ashes. I've learned since being  an active yelper than many people crave this type of smoky flavor, but it was just too much for my extremely picky BBQ palette. I would much rather have well seasoned meat with just a kiss of smoke than eat meat that should probably have a surgeon general warning label!

I also don't care for BBQ sauce. If the meat is well seasoned, to me sauce is unnecessary. Yet I found myself drowning these ribs in sauce to hopefully compensate for the ashy flavor. I emptied an entire table bottle on my order, and still with little desire to eat them, I threw away my leftovers later that evening. Other items to my disliking include the potato salad and baked beans. Growing up my mother used brown sugar to sweeten her beans and that is the flavor I'm used to, but these beans tasted of syrup or molasses, which I did not enjoy. They were also practically as thick as peanut butter.


FINAL THOUGHTS

I'm not sure why people find this place to be worthy of 5 stars, but I most definitely do not. This brief encounter felt very much like being in a relationship where everyone tells you how great the person is before you meet them. When you finally do meet them, they are presentable, attractive and say all the right things. However, in the end, they just don't perform!

I'm breaking up with you Al's Finger Licking Good Bar-B-Que I didn't lick my fingers, not even once.


SIDE NOTE - This review should really be a 2.5, but I really liked the staff. They were accommodating, hospitable and kind. Not to mention the chicken n' yellow rice was simply amazing! So I have chosen to round up instead of down.


2016/4

Bamboozle Cafe is a tricky review for me to write.

On the one hand, I love the downtown location, the interior art and the pho broth is quite tasty. In fact, it was the tastiest broth I found while visiting Tampa. So, when I spotted Oxtail pho on the menu, I decided to try it because A) I love oxtails and B) I've never seen oxtail pho on any pho menu before. 

However, to my severe disappointment, the oxtail meat was bland, tasteless, super fatty and completely untrimmed of the tough skin-like cartilage that surrounds the meat. I was totally baffled that this seems acceptable to serve to customers. Not to mention the gnarly bone in the middle made it very difficult to eat this as a soup. Too hot to use your fingers to hold it while using your teeth to grab the meat and not quite tender enough to use a fork to tear off the meat from the bone. Also, the size difference between their two pho bowls definitely lends to the term 'bamboozled'.

Service is kinda Chipotle-ish and the interior becomes void of natural light the further back into the restaurant you go. Being a person who enjoys natural light, I would have preferred to sit closer to the front of the store but there was no room for our party of nine there. The back dining area had interesting art on the walls, but the dark colored ceilings and lack of windows had me feeling very enclosed and claustrophobic. Sometimes you just can't put your finger on what bothers you about a business, but for me, the cave-like interior towards the rear immediately rubbed me wrong. If you want to torture me, put me in a place that has no windows, very little natural light and dark colors. 


FINAL THOUGHT 

As a reward for using the yelp mobile app to check-in, you will be offered a large cupcake of your choice. It was a nice gesture, but the cupcake itself was just ok. I do believe Bamboozle is a solid place for pho, despite the fact they don't serve a meatball pho (my favorite). The pho boats are enormous, but I would encourage the owner to braise & season the oxtail meat to help tenderize it and give it more flavor. It would also be nice to trim the fat/cartilage and debone it to make it easier to eat as a soup. 

I brought local Tampa friends with me to try pho for the very first time and they found the broth & noodle pho (no meat) to be pretty fantastic. Reviews seem to give high praise to the sandwiches, so maybe next time I'm in town I will give the Banh Mi or perhaps the seafood pho a try. 

Overall - Pho broth (4.5 stars), Oxtail meat and free carrot cupcake (1 star)





2016/26

If the term hole in the wall had a face it would be the exterior of Pho Kien Giang. 

Seriously, this place looks like somewhere you might get car jacked, but the interior is a tad bit nicer. It kinda feels like an old diner, like on the 1970's TV show Alice where Flo might tell you to kiss her grits! The lighting had that familiar old fluorescent glow, the chairs and tables were wrapped in that old 70's-ish red vinyl and the table tops were dressed in floral sheet linens topped with a protective glass cover. Spotless would be a pretty accurate description of the cleanliness of the interior.

Service here was lightening fast! I don't think we were seated more than 5 minutes before our pho was steaming in front of us! While my wife and elder son were a little pho'd out, my youngest son and I decided to spend a day together touring three Vietnamese restaurants. This was stop number two. We didn't know it at the beginning of out adventure, but Tampa pho is undeniably sweet, much sweeter than we are accustom to back in Atlanta. Today we also visited Saigon Deli and Tasty Pho and found the pho here to be the least sweet of the three. 


THE FOOD 

Meatball Pho (3.25 stars) | $7.75
The pho itself was a little better than average. What I didn't like were the quality of the bean sprouts. They were fatter than I'm used to and tasted earthy. Solid choice but not as flavorful as I would have liked. The meatballs were your typical processed globes.

Coconut drink (2 stars) | $3
Not what we were expecting.


FINAL THOUGHTS

I met a girl when we arrived that said Pho Kien Giang was her favorite place to eat pho in all of Tampa, primarily because the others are just too sweet in her opinion. While I would definitely agree with the sweetness factor, nothing about this pho would draw me back here for a second visit. They've got great ratings, but to me the taste was just slightly north of average. 

Out of the four Tampa area pho's we tried, I would say Bamboozle Cafe had the best broth, Tasty Pho gave the best overall experience, Pho Kien Giang was third and Saigon Deli was our least favorite (much too sweet).


2016/8

I can't place a lower rating on this restaurant because I think it would be unfair considering the only thing I tried was the Turtle Soup. But with that being said, if the Turtle Soup had a rating, it would be a 1. 

Never tried Turtle Soup before and heard this place and Commander's (also owned by the Brennan family) were the best. During my visit to New Orleans, a got a recommendation from a bartender to try the Turtle Soup @ Desire Oyster Bar on Bourbon. 

Although this soup is not going to be something I order regularly (possibly never again... lol), I found the soup @ Desire to be spicy but tasty and the soup & Brennan's to be pretty awful. Maybe I don't have the pallet for such a fine soup, but if I was to make a recommendation based on MY tastes, I wouldn't recommend Brennan's.

Disclaimer: PLEASE UNDERSTAND, I am not telling you that you don't have a life by what I am about to say! I'm simply saying that you ain't living until you've wrapped your monkey lips around this sammich!!!

God created the world in 6 days, and on the 7th day he rested... but I'm almost certain he made this sandwich as a snack!

How else could it be so divine!!! How else could a little hole-in-the-wall sort of place have gotten something so dang right that it almost feels wrong?

New Orleans is full of gems, and make no mistake about it, this is one of them. If you have plans to visit the city, do yourself a favor and come taste the ALL THAT JAZZ po'boy here @ Verti Marte. If you've got a few more meals to spare, venture over to Willie Mae's Scotch House for her chicken fingers (which to me are better than the bone-in chicken), Domilise's for their Oyster Po'Boy and Drago's for their charbroiled Parmesan oysters!

If you want to know just how poorly you've been living and how much you have deprived your taste buds, try these NOLA GEMS! Then send me a message of thanks for guiding you in the proper ways of yelphood!

2019/54

CHEESESTEAK WAR - Geno's vs Pat's 

I know nearly every food lover who wants to come to Philly has heard of Geno's Steaks and its rival across the street by the name of Pat's. I would also assume if you are a food lover, then you've seen the many challenges on the Food Network that pit them head to head against each other. 

Now, I might be making an even crazier assumption here, but if you are anything like me, you've been wanting to come to Philly just to do your own taste comparison. It's okay, you can admit it, you're in a safe zone here. No judgment.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

THE EXPERIENCE
Geno's and Pat's are indeed literally across the street from one another, probably within 300 feet. I had no preference which I ate at first, but it happened that Pat's had an open parking space just outside their place, so we stopped there. 

Less than 10 minutes after splitting a steak with my two young boys, we were ordering our second steak here @ Geno's. The time was about 11:45am, so there were no crowds. If there is one thing I immediately notice it was how incredibly clean Geno's is, both inside and out. I'm talking immaculate. The exterior counters were spotless, the sidewalks and table were swept clean and inside the kitchen was like stepping into an operation room in a hospital. It was so clean that it looked almost new. This was a huge unexpected bonus for a germaphobe like me.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

THE CHEESE-STEAK COMPARISON
Let me just say as plainly as I can that you probably will not be disappointed with either of these steaks. I spent hours reading through local blogs (not yelp) trying to decide who has the best cheese-steaks in the city. After all, I may not be back this way in a very long time and wanted the best experience. Pat's consistently made multiple top 10 lists while Geno's did not. I almost decided to try two other places instead, but stuck to my guns and fulfill a long standing food goal.

I'm not a fan of cheese whiz, which is an understatement. I hate the stuff and wanted to go for provolone instead. But I didn't. I wanted a real Philly experience, so  I chose the whiz and the whiz won me over. I can't explain why it tastes so different and so much better on an authentic Philadelphia cheesesteak, but it does. I was pleasantly surprised how much I enjoyed the flavor was and I am now a converted believer. 

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

FINAL THOUGHTS
These two cheese-steak Titans are worthy of a visit despite what you might read in other comparative articles on the internet. Locals may feel there are other places around town that are better, but I can say for certain I was happy with my first authentic experience being at these two long standing locations. Both have been in continuous operation since the 1930's. 

As an out-of-town tourist, I have to give the edge to Pat's. They seem to dice the meat more finely whereas Geno's gives you larger slices. I think that slight difference makes ALL the difference. I also liked the fries much much better @ Pat's but the bread was more to my liking @ Geno's.

Decide for yourself, but my personal taste preference leans heavily towards Pat's.

This place should read GYROS R' US!


THE SCENE
I came to Tarpon Springs with one specific goal in mind, well, make that two! 
1) Have fun with my family and 2) eat a fantastic Gyros from people who should know how to make them better than anyone. I did my homework before arriving. Yelpers from all over Tampa gave me suggestions on which was the best place to achieve my food goals during this recent vacation. One person said Hella's, but I'd eaten there a few years ago and wanted to try someplace better. Another said Plaka. So we went, ate, and threw three quarters of it away. I also stopped at one other restaurant where they allowed me to sample a slice of the meat before ordering... blaaaaah! 

Now I'm getting frustrated and beginning to pout like a toddler who didn't get the toy they wanted. Yes, my pouting was noticeable. So much so my wife AND KIDS threatened to put me in a time out!!!  But I was not going to leave until I found a great gyros no matter how many went in the trash. 

I was seriously starting to doubt my resolve until I walked through the doors @ Mykonos. We parked near the restaurant when arriving, but walked by them to investigate all the other choices along the strip. My nose told me this was the place, but I stubbornly decided to bypass it and stick with the recommendations given to me by other yelpers. Big mistake. Always believe the nose!!! It really knows.



THE EXPERIENCE
Unlike Plaka, the entire place here was alive with friendly staff. Welcoming, warm and eager to take your order. Lots of happy & smiling customer faces all over the restaurant really enjoying their food was another good sign. Since we had already tried a few other places, my family was no longer hungry, so I ordered the gyros (for myself) and we all shared a bowl of some sort of lemon pepper chicken noodle soup. It was delicious for the first few bites, but gets a little overpowering. We also ordered the spanakotiropita, which was flaky and satisfying.

The gyros soon arrived looking all kinds of delicious. I immediately sampled the meat before constructing my sandwich since the pita, feta, tzatziki sauce,  toppings and meat were all separate. It was heavenly, like the clouds parting and angels beginning to sing. "NOW THIS IS A GYROS!" I exclaimed, and the kids (who said they weren't hungry but managed to eat over half of it) agreed. The meat was succulent and full of terrific flavor, the tzatziki sauce was excellent and the topping were fresh. My only complaint: I had to pay extra for feta cheese. I don't know why this isn't standard on a gyros, but they did give me a generous chunk for the money.



THE VERDICT
I was so happy with my gyros I wanted to break a plate and scream out Opa! Maybe even bust out my happy dance moves. Great place to dine if you are visiting this area for the day. I honestly don't know why anyone would accept a gyros made any differently than this... so good!


Yelp100 [22]

Knowing that I love food, my sister insisted we go here for lunch! So I found myself wandering its gorgeous grounds on a beautiful 80 degree Tampa winter day! Although the area feels a little industrial, Ulele's was nestled perfectly into a space between Water Works Park and a bend in the Hillsborough River. The result is a gorgeous view from the lawn and patio areas. The name Ulele is taken from American Indian folklore. A sign near the sculpture on the lawn tells the 'Story of Ulele' as follows: 

"In 1528, the young daughter of local Tocobaga chief Hirrihigua, pleaded for mercy and threw herself over 17-year old Juan Ortiz. He was about to be roasted alive in revenge for the tribe's previous hostile encounters with European explorers. Otriz, a member of the Spanish Narvaez expedition, was spared. Whether love or pity prompted Ulele's reaction we will never know. But we preferred to believe it was love - just as we prefer to believe that the all too familiar Pocahontas-John Smith story 80 years later is based on this story." 

We arrived around noon to one of the most beautiful restaurants I've had the pleasure of dining. It's as if a Pottery Barn factory exploded. Each and every part of this place from the front door to the staircase and from the lower dining area to the upper patio was spectacularly done. Simple, yet elegant, rustic, yet well thought out. This is totally my kind of place!

Service was outstanding and the Executive Chef walked around in what looked like pajama bottoms with fruit prints, but I was told by our server those are chef pants. Either way, I thought it was awesome!

However, I clearly ordered the wrong items, because the food was not the 4 or 5-star dining experience I'd read in so many reviews prior to my visit.  

-----

THE FOOD

CHEESESTEAK WAR - Geno's vs Pat's 

We took a long road trip from Atlanta to Maine, making stops all along the way at places I've been wanting to try for years. Everything from authentic NY pizza and pastrami to authentic Maine lobster rolls were preset into my GPS navigation.  Well, I don't know how I could call myself a food lover and not have an authentic Philadelphia cheesesteak from the two originals, so on this trip I rectified that!

I've never been to any of the states north of the Carolina's on the East coast and decided last year we are going to curtail our preferred mode of vacationing (cruises), to spend more time touring all the great places we've been missing around our own country. After all, our boys are getting older and there is only so much time we have left before they might not think it's cool to hang out with us... LOL

~~~~~~~~~~

THE EXPERIENCE
I was a total tourist during my visit to Pat's. Taking pictures, laughing with locals and hamming it up with the kitchen staff. It may just be my personality, but we don't generally have problems with people. I've read a lot of reviews about the staff both here and across the street @ Geno's being rude, even saw it on a Food Network show. However, they were fantastic with us. My excitement to be there must have been infectious because they even came out to take pics and cracked a few jokes. 

As usual with touristy places, you are bound to run into others who came a long distance just to try them. We ran into one couple also doing a steak comparison and had just finished their first steaks @ Geno's. They made for an enjoyable conversation as we shared our crazy food adventures. It always make me feel better to know that I'm not the only person in this world that travels for food !

~~~~~~~~~~

THE CHEESESTEAK
I HATE Cheese Whiz. It is a violation of basic food decency and have been repelled from any establishment that even suggests putting it on my food. So when I found out Philadelphians prefer it, I made it up in my mind I would give it a try so as to have the most authentic experience possible. Under protest of course, because the backup plan was to throw it away if I didn't like it and order another with provolone, the cheese of the food gods!!!

I was stupefied at just how amazing whiz can taste on a Philly cheesesteak. Not in a million years would I have guessed I would love it as much as I did. But then again it could simply be the way Pat's blends it with the meat. It's not just poured on top as I expected. No, it's mixed into the blend of beef and onions during the cooking process, setting of an orgy of deliciousness.

I'm a Chicago native. The meat in our cheesesteaks is much more finely diced, almost to the point of looking like ground beef, which is how I prefer my cheese steaks.  Pat's does not chop their beef up nearly as much, but it is certainly more finely chopped than its rival Geno's for sure. It make the sandwich easier to eat, more tender and in my opinion, creates a more balance flavor between all the ingredients. Most people mistake the finer chop for a lesser quality meat, but nothing could be further from the truth. I'd be willing to bet the meat each uses probably comes from the same vendor. They just slice and season it differently.

~~~~~~~~~~

FINAL THOUGHTS
Food is a personal experience not always based on how good something actually is, but how good it is in comparison to other life experiences. It may be tied to memories with loved ones or a bad experience with a past relationship. Whatever subjective feeling you have, no one can really take away how the inner you reacts to it. 

As for me, Pat's was probably the singular most soul satisfying meal I had during my entire three week vacation up the East coast. Took me back, way back to simpler days. I love food (all food) but you should know by now I'm not fancy. If I were food, this sandwich is truly me on a plate. My eyes rolled back in my head as my taste buds screamed 'Don't stop, git it, git it!'   Winner - Pat's.




SIDENOTE: See my review for Geno's to get the comparison between the two.

HISTORY

Willie Mae Seaton was a woman who made the best of her environment through hard work and determination. She worked at a shipyard, a dry cleaners, drove a taxi, and was a licensed beautician when she opened a beauty/barber salon. Wanting more, in 1957 she added a small bar where the popular house drink was Scotch & milk. According to legend, she would cook in the kitchen on property and it smelled so good that customers encouraged her to open a restaurant. 

The salon closed in the 80's, but the restaurant thrived. A 1999 article in the local newspaper took the restaurant from a neighborhood secret to a city wide food destination, which is saying something considering this is home to some of the best cooking in the country.

In 2005, Ms. Seaton was honored with the prestigious James Beard Award for "America's Classic Restaurant for the Southern Region." That same year, Hurricane Katrina caused massive flooding throughout New Orleans and did not spare the Scotch House or her home next door. Volunteers worked hard to get her back up and running a little over a year after the flood, but by then the stress had taken its toll on Willie Mae and she was no longer up to the daily responsibility of managing the business.  She died on a Friday in September of 2015 at the age of 99. It is said she will be remembered more for her hospitality and love of community than her famous fried chicken. [source: NOLA.com]


FINAL THOUGHTS

Legendary restaurant where reportedly a president (Obama) and a Queen (Beyoncé aka Queen B) have dined! I like to include history when I can because (in my opinion) it enhances the experience. Knowing the blood, sweat and tears of an establishment can bring a better level of respect. I certainly respect Ms. Willie Mae for the legacy she created with her love of cooking and love of people. Enjoy.

Grab yourself some napkins and wet naps before you get started so you aren't walking around displaying your sauce hands and grabbing things with your elbows like I always do. 

The DAIQUIRIS are sooo tasty with the Gin & Tonic Daq (G&TD) as my number one choice (12oz.-$8 / 16oz.-$10). Make sure to ask to sample whatever their special batch is that day though because I've stumbled upon a rose daiquiri (not rosé) that was unREAL. I say silent prayers every time I walk in that someone has recreated it. 

Also worth note on the menu is their BOUDIN. I love adding a pork boudin ($3) to the meal that I unceremoniously dunk into my excess wing sauce. 

Is that a side of Mac? A tub of pimento cheese? BACON BEANS? MEAT PIES? CRAAACKLINS? YUUUUP I will take those too!

Seriously get ready to throw down when you get here. Grab a partna' and plan to tear through everything together.

As if these things weren't somehow enough to get excited about, Bourree also does char grilled oyster nights (Fridays), Smoked chicken and rib barbecues (Saturdays), and pig pickings (Sundays). The pig pickings are awesome with 1/2 lb ($12) and full lb. plates ($20) with unlimited sides or you can get just sides ($5). Sides include Mac, veggies, cornbread, etc. 

No surprise this place showed up on Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives. Well deserved!! Go here!

ALLIGATOR

I was determined to try alligator meat. Towards the end of the trip, we came to Felix's where they serve alligator 2 ways, blackened and fried.

My friend and I chose blackened since they wouldn't let us do half-half. 

The portion was quite small for $12. The meat itself was not bad, a cross between fish and chicken. But it was overloaded with spices that made it very salty and unappealing.

annual visit to grand sierra resort and finding continuing renovations and improvements....cpk added to the list of dining options....beautiful bar and restaurant...espn on the screens....lunch specials monday through friday....friday visit and sitting at the bar...full menu provided...a diet coke for $3.29 with refills....browsing the lunch specials and selecting the half chicken sandwich and mediterranean salad $10.95....complimentary toasty bread and seasoned olive oil provided before meal...snacking before meal delivery...sandwich was full of flavor and smokey grilled chicken and bacon goodness...salad was filled with feta cheese, black olives and more....a good meal at reasonable prices...recommend cpk visits for the weekday lunch specials...$18.42 total after tax and tip for a lunch special and a soda....

breakfast and lunch only....monday through friday 7am to 3pm...closed on weekends...quite crowded with people standing around waiting for their orders....move pass the crowd and to the short line to the order counter...order of the dirka dirka (corned beef, pastrami, cheese and coleslaw sandwich)...choice of bread and taking a dutch crunch...roughly $14 total after soda, tax and tip in the can...lunch hours and waiting about 5 minutes for name to be called...finally called and picking up food...most of the tables are communal and ask politely to sit..soccer on the tv screens...self-serve soda fountain...ready to eat...finding the quality of the bread good...hefty sandwich, but most of the weight coming from the bread....ratio to meat and bread seems way off....way too much dense bread and too little meat...very thin layer of meat, mound of coleslaw and way too much bread...

inside reno airport...spacious atmosphere...sports on the multiple screens...tables all around....full bar and self-seating with full service...order of diet pepsi $3.29 while browsing menu..free refills...simple burgers, salads, sandwiches and few more in the $12 to $14 price range before tax....taking and turkey bacon club sandwich $11.99....served with potato chips...pay extra $2 for fries or salad optional substitution....few minutes of waiting and plate delivered...simple looking sandwich creation...manageable size with deli sliced turkey and 2 slabs of thick bacon...cheese, lettuce, tomato and mayo spread...simple sandwich...thick chips served in mini-fryer for presentation and good...simple meal for $19 after tax and tip for sandwich, chips and soda...

saturday evening and crowded...every table taken and more waiting by the door...solo and taking a seat at the busy counter..bit hectic and some mistakes in food delivery...taking a large combination pho $7.50 after tax...about 5 minutes and a hefty large bowl delivered...typical sprouts, leaves, lime and jalapeno slices...squeeze of lime and sip of broth...flavorful and seasoned right...noodles cooked fine...decent bowl of pho loaded with meat and noodles...but, conditions of the restaurant is quite worn...a dirty rag left near and never taken away...search for your own hoisin and sriracha sauce...wipe down the chopsticks and soup spoons...a dive, but decent food...

All the hype through Yelp and friends of mine, it was finally time to give Ulele a shot. I came here with my brother and family members from Louisiana. Going to a fancy seafood place - you can't go wrong! The atmosphere was great and the interior was pretty inviting! Love the open kitchen concept, especially if you get to sit upstairs and look down.

We ordered multiple appetizers; 4 dozen Chargrilled oysters and requested to add some crab meat over the oysters for a wilder taste. I think we paid $9 for every 5 ounces, but the chef granted the request. The oysters were okay, a little on the salty side but they were okay. I understand the crab was an irregular request for a Florida restaurant, but I recommend adding that as an option then char-grilling the duo; that would be perfect! We ordered the calamari and that was good. Lastly, we ordered the crab Mac and cheese. I don't recommend this dish - the Mac n cheese wasn't flavorful and the crab was just thrown on top. 

For entrees, we ordered the seafood risotto, the filet mignon, and the Grouper dish. The seafood risotto was delicious. The filet was not cooked to order, but it was good. The grouper was over cooked and didn't have a lot of flavor. The green beans were good, but the mashed potatoes didn't taste anything like potatoes. 

Lastly for dessert, we went with their famous coconut ice cream and the guava cheesecake ice cream. The coconut ice cream didn't taste like coconut, but the guava ice cream was pretty good.  Service was pretty good throughout the evening.

Oysters: 2/5
Calamari: 4/5
Crab Mac n cheese: 1/5
Seafood risotto: 5/5
Filet: 3/5 - ordered Medium well got medium rare. It was still good, just not cooked to order.
Grouper: 1/5
Coconut ice cream: 1/5
Guava Cheesecake Ice Cream: 5/5
Service: 3/5
Atmosphere 5/5

Overall, it was not what I expected and this restaurant unfortunately did not live up to the hype. If you're looking for great atmosphere, drinks and light bites, this is the place to go. If you're looking to eat good food, I think there are better options nearby in armature works or down the street in soho. 

I'm usually the kind of person that will give my opinion to the manager if something was wrong with our experience, but there were too many things to count, I decided to share my experience here.

Oh my goodness! First time ever at Rock-n-Sake and everything was perfect. A late night Friday night was AMAZING, because of the environment Rock-n-Sake had. The music was booming and everyone had fun. The service was so kind, especially Hailey! Now, onto the food. Apps, delish. No question there. I was most excited for the rolls and I am a sucker for sushi rolls. I devoured every single piece of these rolls. I wish I could remember all the different types of rolls I ordered but I do remember some. The upside roll, Margarita roll, dragon roll (probably my favorite), and more. I highly recommend coming here.

I really wanted to like this better than anticipated.  First and foremost, our service was hands down world class customer service.  Marty and April were very informative, professional and eager to make our experience as enjoyable as possible.

Marty even took us to the 'haunted' table and showed us the 'party/poker' room on the other side of the restaurant.  Very cool vibes going on in that area of the joint.

The restaurant in itself is very charming with a lot of history.  It was the food that fell a little short for me.  The bread, although served fresh and warm was surprisingly tasteless and the butter wasn't much better.

The soup of the day was some sort of mushroom cream and it was very delicious, however boo had the seafood gumbo (short of seafood) and I was very surprised as how 'fishy' it was.  Our server had to go get more 'seafood' to add to the gumbo.  Boo seemed to like it, but I'm glad I didn't get it.

For our entrees I got the pork chop which was very yummy, i really enjoyed the sweet potato purée, collard greens and some sort of chutney on top.  Boo got the red snapper and found it to be lovely, light and full of flavor.  As a side dish he got the duck jambalaya...let's just say it was on the dry side and let's rank it as just okay.

Overall we had a lovely experience...however the food was slightly above average, but not by much considering there are other restaurants with the same menu and they are by far a couple notches up than here.

Not bad to give it a try, perhaps after the crazy holiday everyone is off their game.  Again, it wasn't bad, but it wasn't ALL great either.

Went here on a week night around 9 or 10pm and they were showing an "educational" documentary on their patio in which a small "demonstration" ensued shortly afterwards with protesters shutting down Arsenal and Grand for a bit. It was harmless, but not really the atmosphere I was looking for on a Tuesday night.

PROS: Great design. Great location. 3000+ of new and old slot favorites. Free parking. Table games. Slots appear looser than other casinos in the DelMarVa region. Naturally, it's not Vegas but I've been going here since it opened a year and a half ago and have had a lot of good nights with some amazing payouts.

CONS: Insanely crowded all hours of the day. Good luck playing your game of choice during the weekend. "Slot hog" heaven - lots of people play multiple machines with no management intervention. Ghost players leave coats, beer bottles, ash trays, etc. on seats so they can go to the restroom, ATM or lunch breaks. It's a smokers paradise - there should be a decontamination room near the exits. Serious gamers be warned: as with Atlantic City, there are a lot of gawkers, sleepers and seat warmers. It would be nice if they could create a little enclosed waiting area off the casino floor - just a suggestion. Players program is insulting to true gamblers although during the summer months they tend to have A LOT of giveaways/promotions. Drink service is scarce on the weekends, primarily because the crowds are overwhelming. 

Word to the wise: this place had revenues of over 1 billion dollars it's first year. Just something to think about.

**LEGALIZE ONLINE GAMBLING IN THE UNITED STATES** I'd rather lose in the comfort of my own home.

I dont know why this place has so few reviews? This is one of the best mexican places I have ever had food from. Their portions are very generous and the food is on point. The red sauce is perfectly spicy. I highly recommend this for delivery aswell. I think grubhub does free delivery for over $15. I loved my beef and chorizo burrito. Def worth a try and is also inexpensive compared to other mexican places in the city.

AMAZING sandwiches!! I had the wasabi tuna with ginger and it was a perfect compliment in flavor. My lunch date has a simpler palate and preferred Mozzaro's take on a classic Italian. Both were amazing!! The tuna was perfectly seared leaving a cool soft center (sashimi style), while the Italian classic tasted fresher than any sub I can remember in recent memory. 

The lunch was topped of with a canolli for each of us - crushed pistachio for me and chocolate chip for her. While I can't speak for her, mine was a perfect blend of salty / sweet and rounded out with utter freshness!!

Been here a couple times and was pleasantly surprised. The location is in a strip mall that never seems to make it. Hopefully these guys will stick around. 
I've had the antipasto salad, raspberry salad, and pepperoni pizza. All of them were really good. Service on friendly and on point. 
Great local place to grab a solid meal!

We really enjoyed this place. We called ahead to see if we needed reservations and they said to come on down. 
We sat at the teppan yaki table and it didn't disappoint. I ordered the scallops and shrimp. My side kick had the teriyaki chicken. We also got a spicy tuna roll to start. 
Everything was delicious! Service was excellent. And Mr An was walking around chatting with patrons.

I had high expectations from this place due to reading reviews. I decided to take clients here for lunch and opted for an early Thursday meeting. 
I didn't make reservations and it was suggested to me at check in that I do so going forward. (Presumptuous for sure!) I didn't think I needed them for an 11:30 lunch, but I'll definitely keep it in mind. All of the tables had a "reserved" sign on them, but the sign was taken away as they sat us. 
I must say from start to finish the service was awful. The young man waiting on us was less than attentive. Never filled water/tea, even after asking multiple times. 2 out of 3 entrees were salads, yet he brought the hot meal out first by itself. As I sat watching my risotto get cold, we attempted to get attention from anyone to find out where the salads were. They finally arrived and I was told they tasted good. I was slightly embarrassed that I chose the restaurant for these clients, especially when my food came first. Not good. 
The food itself tasted great, which is why I'd try this place one more time. 
The final head scratching moment in this whole experience is when the waiter brought back the "boxed up" to go leftovers. They were in styrofoam take out boxes. Maybe I lived in San Diego too long, but a restaurant of this caliber ought to consider another option (more environmentally friendly) for take out.

I expected to go there, try the veggie burger and leave without giving it that much thought.

It turns out a place that sells a lot of beef might become the new vegan hot spot of Philadelphia.

They label their menu which shows they are attuned to the concerns of vegans. So they meet the bare minimum. Good thing they surpass it.

For starters, get the pickles and slaw "bare snack". Two kinds of vegan slaw. The whole thing is fantastic. It made the perfect sharing item for a party of three.

They also have so many toppings and sides that are vegan. The vegan sandwiches they offer can be modified to add these items such as chickpea onions and stout onions. 

My wife and I split two vegan sandwiches, Guadalupe burger and the Mazuma tempeh sandwich. Both were great. I especially appreciate that they make their own veggie burger. No Morningstar Farms here.

For dessert we had the vegan carrot cake. The only item we ate that we didn't love. I would skip it net time.

Seriously, the meal I just had there compares very favorable to the many great all-vegan restaurants in Philadelphia. I am very very impressed.

Tried it for the first time on a Saturday and was promptly back there two more times over the next five days. And I don't even live in the city!

I am so excited that there is an establishment in Philly that is a cross between In-N-Out and Bobby's Burger Palace for Vegans! But you really do not have to be Vegan to love the food.

Here's what I have tried so far:

Udon Noodle Salad: Classic tasty Asian salad with Vegan chicken. Really nice taste if a bit overdressed.

Curry Tofu Wrap: I had this for lunch the day after I bought it. Still was delicious. I'm surprised there was such a great Indian taste on this menu. 

Ziggy Burger: Get this! And order extra special sauce. My new favorite burger!

Crispy HipCity Ranch: Good Italian "chicken" sandwich. Not as awesome as the Ziggy.

Sweet Potato Fries with cilantro black bean dip: my new favorite Philly fries. Sorry European Republic! Still love you but this great dip is Vegan!

My wife and I have also had the chocolate chip cookies which are quite good.

One negative: they have no customer bathroom. According to the very friendly people at the counter it is because they are not zoned for one.

Philly's Veg/Vegan scene was struggling compared to New York's. Thank goodness HipCity Veg opened to help close the gap.

I was invited to a business dinner here - checked yelp beforehand and there were two reviews that mentioned them being super accommodating to vegan patrons. 

My waitress was not. I asked, in front of a group of partners, if I could get the waitress' assistance and mentioned I heard they could accommodate vegans. She responded that their options were "super" limited and hesitated before mentioning they could steam veggies or leave off dairy and dressing from a salad. I was incredibly disappointed and aware that the entire table was watching this exchange. I asked her for an appetizer chopped salad and oil/vinegar and left it at that. 

Yes, I could have delved in to how the Brussels sprouts were cooked, or what was on the loaded baked potato that we could cobble together a meal with. But she was clearly not interested.

This new location will succeed.

Having experienced the old location, i think the new building is gorgeous with an intelligent layout. Much more seating, half the bar opens to outdoor portion that is roofed.  The new sushi bar is an island in center with more surface area.

They have had growing pains, probably with new staffing to accommodate a larger space.  That being said I saw a lot of familiar faces.

I never thought that they offered the very best sushi.  Just that they have struck the best balance between price and quality.  Tonight we were served by Brandi and the service was fast and attentive.  We sat at the sushi bar and our sushi chef was Ray, a veteran sushi chef from the older location.  Because my friend was in town he included some mochi ice cream into the tempura ice cream dessert.  It was a nice touch.

The food and service that I experienced was as good as I remember it to be.  Very surprising that some yelpers have had issues, so I'm sending all positive energy and good vibrations.  Sushi Alive needs to remain an exceptional foodie landmark.

P.S. half priced appetizers after 8 on certain days.

Yeah, this is my favorite newer place in Indianapolis.  The flavor profiles that the owners have created seem specifically targeted to me...stinky-funky-rich-oozing-pickled goodness.  The menu is very short, with typically three (3) breakfast items and 3-4 sandwich options.  They do sell out of the more popular items as the day progresses.

Love Handle serves the best biscuits and gravy in town, with shiitake-mushroom gravy rich in umami flavor. It is topped with pickled veggies to cut through and counterbalance the rich, savory flavor, and a not-so-voluntary headcheese egg.   Why no choice in the matter? The headcheese egg is a voluntary add-on, but you'd be very much mistaken to skip it...a single egg yolk, suspended in aspic made from a funky combination of pig's feet, pork cheeks, and other tasty meat bits. Where else could you find something like this is Indy? I've also had the breakfast sandwich, with pork belly and blueberry preserves on a freshly baked biscuit....fantastic.

If you're not feeling breakfast, then good luck choosing a sandwich.  Again, the owners do an exceptional job of balancing different flavors in their sandwich offerings.  I recently had the best sandwich I've tasted in years, made most excellent by that flavor balancing act; a grilled sandwich, with pungent Taleggio, sautéed shiitakes, fennel confit, apricot mostrada & pickles. Just when you think you'll be overcome by Taleggio, apricot sweetness and a hint of vinegary pickle save you...taste euphoria!

Love Handle's location is perfectly safe during its open hours, and I enjoy visiting Pogue's Run co-op across the street afterwards. The atmosphere is bare-bones and not cozy; I recommend sitting at the bar, if you're on your own. The owners are very friendly and typically run the whole place, cooking...service...and all, with just the two of them. I highly recommend visiting Love Handle; step outside your comfort zone, keep an open mind, and you'll be most pleasantly surprised.

DON"T WORK FOR THIS CASINO!!!!
I was just in poker school at Parx for the last 7 weeks. The class was great and I learned a lot, the instructors where awesome and really knew the game. I was in the morning class, there was also an afternoon class and an evening class that was held. Upon starting the class we were told that the class would end October 7th and the casino would open the end of October. Everyone in the class was under the same understanding that we would have off for 3 weeks, some of the students where even trying to plan vacations knowing we wouldn't get time off for at least a year. Back in June I started working with a company to donate my eggs so women who cannot have child would be able to have them. I was chosen to donate when the class first started, now going on what the management originally told us I was to have off for 3 weeks. I informed the egg donation place I was unable to start an monitoring till after the 7th of October. I then started the hormones that didn't need monitoring the second week of class, I got my monitoring schedule and knew I was to be monitored after the 7th and have a retrieval date of before the casino opened. I did this so it wouldn't effect my work schedule. Last week in the class we were told that class was going to be extended, right away I was in a panic not knowing what I was going to do because I already started my hormones for the egg retrieval. If they would have told us this in the beginning of class I would of never scheduled this to happen, I am not a stupid person and I really wanted this job. I am a single mother living alone with my child, I actually needed this job. Just yesterday upon returning to class and checking my dates of monitoring I went to the head teacher in the class and explained a little about what was going on and how I can't stop the hormones now and I was willing to come in the afternoon or even the evening but I am unable to come in next week in the morning times because my monitoring starts and I already started the hormones process that I cannot stop at this point. She informed me that there was nothing she could do and they weren't going to make any exceptions at all. I then went to the main boss and tried to explain to him what was going on, he talked to the teacher and wouldn't make any exceptions either. ARE YOU KIDDING ME!!!! I am going threw a medical procedure!!! Not taking a damn vacation or having some sort of fun. Also just last week we were all told that the part time people would not have a set schedule that every week we were to have different days, I can't do that raising a child by myself and trying to keep a second job because part time is not enough money to live off of. But again due to poor management none of us were told this in the beginning, and I am not the only one that is freaking out about this situation. There are others in the class that are not going to be able to work the part time schedule either. 
Its no one fault in the class its due to poor management and not letting the employees know exactly what was going on with the class and changing everything so much throughout the class.

A surprisingly solid experience. Went there on a lark for my pre- birthday dinner. Had low expectations due to the rampancy of mediocre, cookie-cutter mediterranean food. We arrived towards the end of the night, but we were fully accommodated.  The space is mid-sized, but well used. Low light & the deeper color scheme contribute to a relaxed vibe. The service was friendly, thorough, & professional throughout the evening. We ordered both the mixed grill & the appetizer sampler. They arrived quite promptly considering the amount & diversity of food involved in the dishes, but not fast enough to cause alarm. Everything was nicely presented, hot, fresh tasting, & cooked properly. We especially enjoyed the tzatziki & the tomato based dip on the appetizer platter, as well as the tasty spanikopita. One of main criteria for sizing up a Mediterranean restaurant is by their spinach pie. This one was well seasoned, & rich tasting very satisfying. For the mixed grill, we felt that the Greek meatballs, & the orange infused sausage stood out from the crowd. For dessert, we were presented with a surprising array of choices spread across a case by the front entrance, a tableside tray of selections, & a few choices from the kitchen. We tried both a Phyllo custard with caramelized honey, & a cinnamon ice cream with chunks of actual baklava in it. Both were unique & delicious, and came in ample portions as well. Though the honey on the custard dish quickly hardened & become a challenge to eat. One notable question for us though, was exactly how much of the food is made in-house,& how much is bought-in? The spanikopita, & some of the dessert.offerings seemed pre-made. Not bad, just not truly original. Overall though, the Olive Tree delivered a satisfying experience across the board. Will certainly return.

I decided to stop in at Lee's because of a staff member Dwight. The owner is customer service oriented and extremely outgoing. I ordered the spinach chicken cheese steak w/ shrimp. The flavored blended well together and the sweet chili sauce made the sandwich pop. I recommend checking this place out. Univ City is stepping up its game.

From the ashes of Pravda, Cane and Table emerges as a new and exciting alternative to the dive-centric lower Decatur street. It's beautiful, bright courtyard, pleasant atmosphere and creative rum-centered drink menu lead to a pleasant night out. Much hype and excitement had been building since the creators of Cure purchased the absinthe bar Pravda many months earlier. Nick Dietrich, one of my favorite bartenders from Cure, was tapped to become the head honco, so I was excited to check it out as soon as possible. 

Let me also mention that they have a full kitchen. The hummus was stellar, and I will definitely be back to try more of their offerings. I noted a large selection of vegetarian options, as well as rice/peas/sausage, and other Caribbean dishes. 

Their drink menu does feature rum, but there are also gin and whiskey drinks, so fear not, rum haters! There is also the exciting/adorable option of having your drink in a pineapple, for only $5 more. I had the Colada drink, and instantly regretted on passing up the pineapple. 

I can't wait to go back and update this review, as there are SO many more drinks for me to try!

This place is awesome! I have always put off reviewing the place because it's hard to put into words how well my husband and I have been treated every time we have dined in the establishment. 

This was our "date place" when we dated long distance. I would look forward to having a delicious meal and several desserts! We would get the roasted veggie entree(Checking the menu now, it appears that the entree has changed slightly, but still sounds damn good!), which was always perfect and was varied by the seasons. Of course, we LOVED the desserts. Most of them were made in-house, and presented beautifully. Creme brulee or bread pudding, paired with an Irish coffee were the perfect finish to a great meal. 

When we dine here, we show up early, go to the back courtyard bar, and bask in the great service while waiting for our table. I loved the bartender's knowledge of wines and beers, and I would often go out of my comfort zone (whiskey) and try something new! I was never dissapointed. 

I also planned an event here, my wedding brunch. My family was extremely impressed and enjoyed everything. We were showered with free champagne, compliments, and excellent service. We were able to all order exactly what we wanted, and the waitress quietly ensured that we did not go over our price range (we were about to get married, and slightly broke due to it), and made sure that my mother's dietary concerns were met. The event planner was polite, helpful, and answered all my neurotic questions quickly.

Give this place a whirl. It's beautiful, historic, and a great place to sit and people watch. It's expensive, but you get what you pay for in this case.

Sorry to disagree with the others that have posted such positive reviews, but this was hardly a five star experience.  You know you have been disappointed when the BYOB was the best part of your meal.
I was alone, and the service regrettably suffered from the syndrome that takes single diners, places them in the worst seat possible, then ignores them.  
I ordered ceasar salad and the supposedly "amazing" eggplant parmesan.  The salad dressing was good, but the rest would have been forgettable--lettuce with sparing anchovy (I requested them) and no cheese--had it not been for the fact that I realized after eating it that it had plastic bristles in it.  I spend the next ten minutes fetching several of them from inside my mouth.  Ugh! 
The eggplant was a great disappointment.  It was overbreaded and the breading tasted like unseasoned flour.  The accompanying spaghetti was fine, with a pretty tasty sauce.  
I was ignored throughout dinner until the end, when I got the following three words directed at me in staccato fashion--- "Dessert"?  "Box?" "Check?"   I tipped accordingly.
As many great Italian restaurants are there are in the Philly area....this isn't one of them.

What can't you find at Mazzaro's.  It's always busy so plan your visit accordingly.  Every area of this place is packed full of goodness and you can't go wrong with any food or drink option here.  There's a bakery for all your sweet tooth or bread needs, a coffee bar, deli, butcher, wine room, and fresh cheese area.  I'm sure I've missed something, but you get the jist.

Food options from the deli are limitless and everything I've had is generously portioned and flavorful.  There are also refrigerated and frozen take home meals that are ready to go and priced very reasonably.  All of the staff in every area of this place are pleasant and always willing to help.

I wish I had tried Simply Pho sooner.  I've been looking for a decent Pho spot up in the north Tampa area as my go to is farther south near work.  Service was quick and the wings we ordered for an appetizer were well flavored and rather large in size.  I didn't see a combination Beef and Chicken Pho, which is my usual, on the menu and the server advised they would be able to accommodate my request.  The small bowl I ordered came out in what I feel was a massive portion.  It was well flavored and had a good amount of meat to noodle ratio as well.  The only negative part of my experience was the odor inside the restaurant, which seemed a bit off putting.  Not sure if this was a one time thing or a regular thing.  I guess I'll find out the next time I dine here.

After many months of waiting, I finally got to try out Ulele on a recent weeknight.  The restaurant was quite packed and hopping for a Wednesday night and I know from experience that trying to make a reservation on a weekend will entail waiting for 2-3 weeks to get a decent reservation time.

I started off with their signature Florida Mojito cocktail at the bar and it was definitely refreshing with its citrus essences and flavorings.  Our table was ready very close to our 730pm reservation time and our server was quick to greet us and kept her appearances right on schedule throughout our meal.  She was also very upbeat and helpful in helping out a newbie like myself with the menu selections.  The calamari appetizer came with a very flavorful dipping sauce and I ended up sharing the menu Grouper entrée with my dining companion.  Despite sharing a meal, it was still plenty of food for both of us.  I'm glad I had the opportunity to partake in the Ulele experience and see myself coming back to try more of their menu.

I wasn't sure what to expect when I walked in here but from all of the reviews I've read I figured it made it to my list for a reason.  The restaurant is very bare bones and almost convenience store-esq as they also sell goods at the front.  Pricing is about average for tacos as I've experienced in other authentic taco joints around Tampa.

Food was quick to come out after being ordered and the Chorizo and Steak tacos were by far the best of the bunch.  Tacos are served on homemade corn tortillas, which were very fresh, and topped with chopped onions and cilantro.  They have various other types of fare including tortas, quesadillas, and burritos as well.  Overall, the flavors were there and the hot sauces served with the food were on point.

I hesitate to leave a 5 star review after just one visit, but this restaurant was SO good, I feel that it warrants it.  

My wife and I came here for our anniversary dinner on a recommendation from my father.  It's tucked away on the corner of a street that really gives it the perfect "local secret" kind of vibe.  The interior is warm and inviting and while a bit on the smaller side, it leaves you feel cozy and intimate rather than cramped and claustrophobic.  I highly suggest reservations as this place can be very busy.  They do have a very well stocked bar though, should you find yourself having to wait.
  On that note, we had about a 15 minute wait since we didn't make said reservation and had a chance to sample the alcohol at the bar.  I order a Manhattan (Maker's Mark, if you please, barkeep!) and my wife got a cosmopolitan.  I have to give it to the bartender.  That was a GREAT Manhattan.  My wife was slightly less enthused with her drink.  It wasn't amazing, but it wasn't bad either.  
  Once we were sat, we order the Roasted Wild Mushrooms for an appetizer and I put in for the Pappardelle Bolognese and my wife ordered the special for the night, Seafood Risotto.  
  The wild mushroom dish was incredible.  It's essentially an italian take on Poutine.  Polenta fries topped with a mushroom marsala sauce and gorgonzola cheese.  Absolutely delicious.     My pasta dish was big and meaty.  Large chunks of meat and sauce on similarly hearty noodles.  It gives one a certain feeling of manliness as he digs into his meal.  :-)  I have to give kudos to the kitchen on this dish as they really walked that line of meaty flavor vs tomato flavor and it did it to perfection.  At other places, you will often get a tomato sauce with meat in it or a meat sauce with tomatoes in it.  Marcella absolutely nailed this balance.  Well done.
  My wife's dish was on the completely opposite end of the spectrum in regards to flavor and texture, but equally well executed.  It was light and expertly cooked and really showcased the skills of the chef.  Risotto is not an easy dish to make, with it often falling to mush if you over do it.  We were both happy to see that the kitchen again rose to the challenge and delivered excellence in every bite.


  As a side note to any servers reading this review.  One thing you can do, which Marcella did in spades, was expert meal pacing.  This means controlling the times that you interact with the table and when the food comes out of the kitchen.  Greet your table as soon as they sit.  Get the appetizers going when you put in the drink orders.  Put in the entree orders when the appetizers come out.  When food comes out in sequence, with enough time to eat in between each course, it gives your guests to enjoy the food instead of getting impatient while waiting for the food.  Conversely, never, ever put in the entire order at once.  Food will sit and get cold and that makes for annoyed guests who feel like you are trying to rush them out the door.

  In summary, this place was incredible.  The staff was friendly, the decor warm and inviting, the pacing spot on and the kitchen on point.  Don't hesitate to try this little gem.

I really enjoyed it. I love the long table that runs along the main dining room . If you're alone you can feel like your not or just strike up a convo with your neighbor. 
We sat at a regular table on the back and we were seated right away on a Friday at 6:30 

We got deviled eggs two ways. Spicy and a barbecue. Spicy had just the right amount of heat and sweet and the barbecue was a mustard forward style that was also delicious.
