I ordered the chicken and hoe cakes . It was a small plate but it was more than enough . I even took some home . It had two friedchicken legs , homestyle pickles and the best hoecakes on the world ( sorry grandma) . There were two sauces. One was a drizzle of a sweet syrup the other was a spicy peanut sauce that i didn't care for. I think it overpowered the dish . 

My friend had fried chicken with Mac and cheese and the greens. I tasted the greens and they were a little sweet for me but still very good

Service was awesome , location great especially if you can sit outdoors. 

Parking is a challenge. I parked almost two blocks away .

New Harmony is an entirely vegan Chinese restaurant that blows most Chinese restaurants out of the water PERIOD.

I was introduced to this vedgetastic find in the best way anyone could possibly imagine: my friend LJ's catered 80s-themed karaoke birthday bash in New Harmony's party basement (open to the first page of their menu to learn more). There was singing, there was dancing and all celebrators consumed some pretty amazing vegan Chinese food....it was like a vegan Studio 54 (replace 70s with 80s) down there. I knew I had to come back some day soon for a dining room experience. 

I've returned to New Harmony a few times since then, but I believe that the next time I laid eyes on their food again after that was with LJ. We did take out and she ordered a couple of her favorite things from the menu, including the veggie pancake, which I loved. It was light and fluffy, 100% yum! I was curious about the turnip cake and contributed to the order in this way-- I had done dim sum once before as a vegetarian and all I remember is dissecting a lone turnip cake that kind of met my dietary restrictions, enjoying it, but hating all the picking out of meat that I had to do at the time. Wow! This became an instant hit for all! No weird science project-esque eating for us. Another friend ordered the vegetable lo mein and I loved the good quality of the noodles, crispness of the vegetables and the smokey element included in the sauce. 

The time I went after that, I dined solo as I was in the neighborhood and remembered the hot and sour soup. I stopped eating red meat at such a young age that I never had the chance to try the non-vegetarian version, and whoah, it kinda doesn't matter at this point! I love what New Harmony is doing with their vegan version. Agar is an amazing thing (this is my educated guess, at any rate)!

Since then, I've learned that their dumplings are good when both steamed and fried, although I kinda wish that the steamed version was a little less stiff -- this might be the only hit-or-miss dish in my experience. Otherwise, the sauteed bok choy is cooked to perfection and I love the garlic-y sauce that it's done in.

The last time we were there, Ming comped us ice cream, which was so good! I believe it was made with coconut, but regardless, it was a really tasty surprise! 

A recent fortune cookie from New Harmony basically told me to consider leaving my loving, handsome boyfriend to play the field, but that's neither here nor there. Readings like this beckons a bigger, general question to the Fortune Cookie Universe, "Who writes these things?!?". Now I'm convinced that no place is safe. 

I love New Harmony and will return and return and return again!

I was excited to try this restaurant today after being recommended by a friend. After driving 25 minutes to get there. We try to enter restaurant, and could not!! There were people inside dining and at bar. We can see at least 2 employees, who both see us through the door!!! One walked by door at least 3 times and didn't bother to open it. We knocked twice!! Ignored us both times. It was 8:14pm, so maybe they were closing early? I called the restaurant, and asked if they were open, the gentleman said YES! I told him we were at the restaurant and cannot enter, and all he said "Yea, it's open!" I told him, "it's ok, we are leaving." He hung up. At this point, my husband said "We are not begging anyone to spend our money at their business."
 I don't know if staff was being was being sneaky and shutting down early or they were racially profiling us and not letting us in.Either way, this  is poor customer service. I know people are very cautious these days, but running a business like this is not right. You are losing potential customers. They had many patrons inside, but to not even acknowledge people at the door is just plain rude!!! 
I had high hopes to find a new Chinese place, but Ming's will not be it. I have not ever been so furious at a dining establishment.

Was really excited to try this bakery since there isn't many cupcake bakeries around. Found the place on a busy road had to pay for parking. Went in the store the lady was talking to two people about a cake order and completely ignored me for ever 5 mins, the phone even rang she told someone to ask it. I will waiting more people came into the store finally someone came out to help. None of the cupcakes have flavor descriptions on them so I just had to guess what it will taste like. I got a red velvet and banana flavored one. I've had great cupcakes so I know flavor this cupcake was the worst cupcake of my life I could have gone to a grocery store and gotten one with more flavor. Never going back again found a cute farm store in chalfont that sells real cupcakes with flavor

Pod is an oldie, but goodie Asian Fusion style restaurant!  I have been coming here for years and they have remained consistent with their quality of food and good customer service!

I am a creature of habit at times and usually go for the crab fried rice-always fresh and tasty!  I had a few other menu items this visit-Korean Ribs; Spider & Lotus Rolls!  

The staff were attentive and service was prompt!

Pod is still around because they do it right!  If you wanna have a good meal in a cool space-check out Pod!

Larry's Steak's is among some of the top Cheesesteak spots in the City and had been in this neighborhood for over 20 years.  My usual orders consist of: cheesesteaks; pizza or wings that I would get for parties or girl's night because portions are large and a crowd pleaser! 

This review is based on take-out/delivery during COVID-19.  I ordered a small BBQ Chicken Pizza and small Stromboli -that Stromboli was huge..I have never tried the large because I would never finish it..lol 

The quality of food and the standards the I usually expect from Larry's was on point with this order!

I had the opportunity to checkout Taphouse 23 today for brunch with friends!  I have been there many times in the past, but I haven't been since COVID began..but glad we got the chance to give it a shot again!
I enjoy the openness of Taphouse 23...it was a beautiful day out and the windows were open ...it helped with the patrons comfortability level! 

The waitstaff were friendly and prompt and this helped with the extra star in my updated review!

The food continues to be consistently good!  Today, I had the Pork Belly as an appetizer and the Mussels for my main course!  Great decisions by me I must say..both were flavorful!

There are a good variety of cocktails and beer choices to compliment most people's tastes!

I am going to keep Taphouse 23 as a cool spot out in Bridgeport!

Dinner here was AMAZING!  I love the environment and the seating was spaced out (Meeting My More Than 6ft Standards)!  The staff (Wes) was our waiter and he was prompt and attentive throughout our dining experience!

Now..let's get to the main event...the food was cooked to PERFECTION!  I had the trout over shrimp risotto with green beans...Delicious is an understatement!

The Malbec wine that accompanied my meal was fantastic!

Overall, a great foodie night in Media! I will be back to sample other dishes....Oh Yeah!

Unfortunately-still sporting 3-Stars in this updated review!  Wish I had nicer things to say-but sometimes this is how it goes!

It is Blasphemy to sell chips and salsa in a Mexican restaurant and they aren't that great!  Lol

The staff are not friendly (still) and not attentive because they continue to screw up orders!

What continues to keep them with 3-stars is the 'Happy Hour' menu and good tacos!

The chicken skins tacos are tasty and spicy--saved the day!

Well...finally made it back to SOMO for brunch!  Somo has a great brunch menu!  I decided to give those Sriracha wings a try again and the heat has been turned down...Yaaaay!  The disco fries is a large portion and the Apple Cinnamon French Toast was so delicious!

The featured drinks were tasty...SOMO you are a bright spot to see during COVID-19!  Well spaced tables (indoors)!  Ample outdoor seating and staff wearing masks..Awesome!

Glad to support this business during this difficult time!

My update to this original review is that Willie Mae's still 'GOT IT'!  You gotta give it up for consistency and quality food!

This time around I tried the fish..shrimp and butter beans (large limas)...all were mouth watering and seasoned with a 'kick'..Yum!

We had a wonderful server 'Candy'..she made our visit so much fun..Thanks again for all the years of cooking good food!

I visited Felix's on Bourbon during the 'Day'..that is my 'tip' to you..You are welcome! Lol 

There are many choices available regarding oysters..but Felix's should be on the list!  

The service was questionable, but the staff were friendly and the drinks were tasty!

I came ...I saw...I Ate Oysters (1/2 Shell & Charbroiled)...Mission Accomplished!

BRU...what an interesting place!  I gave BRU a try for HH the first tome and my second visit...I came dinner!  The place doesn't take reservations, so try and go when it is not too busy because it fills up fast!

Great beer list of drafts and bottles!  Now the food is somewhat more of a journey that you need to prepare yourself or if you are not familiar with German fare!  The portions are large ...be ready!

I would come back for HH drink specials and pass on dinner!

I have been to Anthony's for lunch a few times, this visit was Happy Hour!  The Happy Hour is from: 4:30p-6:30p-$2 off beer and liquors and $3 off glasses of wine. Meatballs are $4 and Cheese Pizzas are $6.

I decided to try the famous meatballs and was disappointed after all the hype!  They were clearly reheated and flavorless!  

The staff were friendly and service was prompt!

I have had Interstate Drafthouse in my sites for sometime!  I was interested in the menu items that alligator was featured...so we tried the gator and beer chili and the wings!

I was satisfied with how well prepared the chili was and the flavors had depth!  The wings had a smoky kick at the end..off to a good start!

The beer list was just what I needed...I like the offerings of ciders; sours; ipas and lagers.  I sampled ..well actually had two..maybe three rounds of what was on tap!

The bartender was attentive and friendly..the place filled up quickly...so that's a good sign!  

I would return, but not making any special trips!

3 stars are for place and food..additional star is for tHe beer list!

What a surprising and delightful evening at J. Alexander's.  I was excited to be out to enjoy a meal with cocktails!  I sat at the bar while waiting for friends and had a delicious Vodka Gimlet!  There was COVID social distancing in place and that felt comfortable! 

When the friends arrived we choose to dine outdoors!  The patio area has about 4 tables that are spaced out nicely!  The wait staff were attentive and energetic!  The food was seasoned and cooked perfectly!

What a great time at J Alexander's!

This restaurant was a recommendation from a local and it was the BEST MEAL...Let me say it again..BEST MEAL we had on this trip!

The starter of our drinks...On deck:  Whiskey Sour; Tangerine Sour Beer and a Lemon Drop Martini!  

The food was so darn good:  The Peacemaker is (BBQ OYSTERS & BBQ SHRIMP w/Blue Cheese Crumbles)..Outstanding!!!

Blackened Catfish....Delicious and Jambalaya Crawfish Pasta...Sublime!  We were so impressed by the level of fee if we wanted to come back the next night (we got sidetracked..lol)

The servers were polite and food was promptly served!

Overall, if you are looking to grab a bite and you want 'excellence'..go to the Red Fish Grill..you won't be disappointed!

This is one of the coolest places on Frenchman St!  

No Cover ...lots of space to dance if you choose!

Staff is friendly..they serve good size bar food!

If you come to Frenchman St..stop in before you go to the other spots..it will get you hyped for the day/night--whenever you visit..space has good vibes!

You know hat you are getting when you go to a Chickie and Pete's establishment..good food; tons of TV's to catch whatever sporting event is on and usually good vibes from the waitstaff! The vibes this visit were off unfortunately!

This was my first dining experience since the area has been gradually opening up!  We picked this location because they have a large outdoor
Deck with plenty of social distancing spacing around!  

The pros:  
Waitstaff were all wearing masks!  Check!
 You use your smartphone to scan the QR code to access the menu..great idea!

The were using disposable cups for drinks and plastic cutlery to use for meals--ok..gotta get used to that..but I get it!

The food was yummy and flavorful!

Cons:

The waitstaff need more training in this new world of
COVID!  My party had an issue with seating that could've been easily resolved..but because of new policies that appeared to be implemented concerning table assignments-this became a bigger issue than what was necessary! 

The manager comp'd our drinks..great gesture and appreciated!

I think table payment option should be an option instead of having to exchange money or credit cards..lots of touching that is frowned upon now!

The trip to Vernick fish was planned months in advance as it took that long to get a great reservation that was at an usual dinner time vs. 10 or 11p offerings! 

This was a birthday celebration so I wanted to get dressed up and just enjoy all that Vernick Fish has to share with me! The decor is contemporary and fantastic!  The service was even better...that made the evening sparkle!

We decided to start with the warm shrimp cocktail and mussels dishes!  Both were outstanding!  The sauce on the warm shrimp cocktail was tangy with a lemon zest finish!  The mussels were in a Bolognese Sauce that wasn't over powering!  

Our entree's were the Grilled Branzino and Grouper!  Wow is all I have to say...seasoned well and the side of Blackened Cesar Broccoli topped off the meal!  

The cocktails were top notch and the red velvet cake was moist (most can't achieve that balance in red velvet)!

Overall, I can't say enough about the service from the wait staff--excellent!  I would come back and sit at the counter just to partake in sampling more of of menu items!

The Crossing Vineyards & Winery delivered (on customer service) like Dominos!  I thought-it's a beautiful weekend-why not take the drive to this winery!
Staff were friendly and warm upon entering the establishment!  We were asked if we wanted to have a tasting and it appeared we arrived 45 minutes before the next tasting!

We were given a brief tour and informed where to go for the tasting!  We decided to hang out at the bar to have some beer before the wine (why not..lol)!  The bar featured 'Naked Brewing' a local PA craft beer!  I went for the flight--The Pomegranate Wheat & IPA was theBEST!That got us warmed up and ready for the wine tasting!

There was a large group and of about 6 tables with about 6 people at each table!  

This is where we explain why the review doesn't get 5-stars!  Although staff were friendly..The tasting was rushed and the wines weren't that great?  I wish it weren't true..but it was an overall consensus from us amateur wine tasters at our table!  

Aesthetically Crossing is a beautiful location and the staff are wonderful...but you are selling wine-wish it were better!

I was feeling like I needed something a lil different tonight so while sipping a large Margaritas..because I plan my meals around my alcohol choices (don't judge me...lol) I decided to have a Mexican food...one of my fav places is El Poquito!

This is a COVID-19 review...I ordered and had delivery done by Caviar!  The food was packaged with care and I was pleased to have my side sauces included as well!

I decided to dine with real plates and treat myself like I was actually dining out!  

Keep up the good work El Poquito and I can't wait to have your Margaritas and Tacos when you open up after the quarantine.
#yelpsbignightin

It was nice to come to the Oyster House..I hadn't been in years..but truly the thing I remember is the quality of food and that hasn't changed!  Everything was delicious!  

It get crowded quickly...so keep that in mind!  I arrived during Happy Hour. but also had a reservation for dinner!  There appeared to be some rule about which drinks were discounted until 5p but the HH was from 4-7p?  So maybe it was me..but it was confusing? Lol

I had the seared scallops and my friend had the oysters and swordfish!   Each dish was prepared perfectly and the service was great!

Now, that I have returned..I will keep the Oyster House at the top of my list of places for good HH and dinner in a moderate price range!

Sophisticakes is the "go to" place these days when you want a "Yummy" Dessert!  Lately, when I have been at events that involve cakes - Sophisticakes as been the the feature attraction.  I have been satisfied with each type of cake that I have tasted.  My favorite has been the vanilla cake with buttercream icing.

My last occasion was a send off to college "Penn State" sheet cake.  The cake was decorated beautifully & tasted deliciously as well! 

Way to go Sophisticakes - Keep Up The Good Work!

Jake's & Cooper continues to be one of my favorite restaurants to dine at in Manayunk!  The Happy Hour From 4:30p-6:30p is still a great deal with: $5 house wines and selected cocktails and $3 select beers is wonderful!  The food specials are priced $5-$10!

I appreciate the consistency with the full dinner menu items -the spicy meatballs; jumbo lump crab cake & pizzas still hit it out of the park every time!  The wine choices are always pleasing as well.

Look out during the holidays for the 50% of gift certificates-I usually stock up and use them throughout the year!

I am a fan of this location of Di Bruno's Bros.  It is a convenient location near my office and although it is smaller it still has much inventory and options to choose from in all the important areas of cheese, cheese and more cheese!  LOL

I love the "free" samples offered and the staff are friendly and very knowledgeable about all the products.  I enjoy discussing what meats and cheeses should be paired with what wines.  Great suggestions have been made and followed to my delight.

I recommend this location!

Newest Fan of National Mechanics..this place has a cool vibe; great service and even better food!  I started out with the frisky sour drink special as we waited for our food!  This was a good call on my part..drink was well balanced with flavor and nice amount of alcohol!

The wings are so delicious and my friend love her burger! We were so full because we wanted to order the 'Pretzel', but that is for the next visit!

The server was attentive and made good recommendations!

I tried Stock's Pound Cake recently and it still holds up after all these years!  If it ain't broke...,

I cut up a marble pound and froze a few pieces!  When I returned from a recent trip..thawed it out and it was a nice lil treat!

While at Stock's I grabbed a few donuts and thought a lil too dense for my tastes...I prefer a more pillowy type!

Overall...Stock's is still doin it and doin it well!  Nice!

The anticipation of the Goose Island Brewhouse was high when I heard about it them coming to Philly.  I wouldn't say that I am necessarily a "Goose Island" fan, but all my Yelpers know - This gal likes her brews...LOL so I am glad I had the opportunity to give them a try.

I began with a flight and continued from there with trying out what I thought would be interesting.  The waitstaff was knowledgeable and able to answer my "beer nerd" questions.  I appreciated the info and friendliness.  I decided to have some food during this visit - I had the shrimp tacos and my friend had the BBQ Brisket Flatbread - once we realized that wouldn't be enough to keep sampling beer - we ordered the fries.  The food was ok - nothing special-but does the job of giving you solid food on your stomach while sampling brews.

I like the indoor space and the weather was nice when I visited and there were a few people playing outdoor games on the grass.   

Goose Island has a lot of beers, so I have to come back to try them, I think if they keep up the friendly and knowledgeable service they will be a hit in Philadelphia!

Great food, great prices and a friendly, welcoming atmosphere. You can't really ask for much else. I love the green onion cakes and the vermicelli bowls are my usual choice. I've also had the pho, which was really good. Spring rolls and curry stews are great too. 

It's nice to go to a local restaurant that really appreciates your business and treats you very well. I'm glad we found this place, because it's a regular spot for us when we go out now.

The chocolate chip cookies are awesome. But besides that, this place is overrated and VERY overpriced. 

I had some of the prepared food, including the ribs and brisket because the grill line was too long. I was not impressed. The brisket was dry and bland and the sauce on the ribs tasted like ketchup. I also purchased some fresh pasta and gnocchi. It was covered in so much flour that it tasted like chef boyardee. You can purchase much better fresh pasta at Mazzaro's. 

The worst part was the grocery. The mark up is outrageous. For example, the Savannah Bee Company honey was $60 here. The exact same honey (same size) is available at the new Publix on 4th (west side) and 38th for $16.99. I refuse to pay nearly quadruple the price for the same product that is available at Publix. 

Overall, this is a cool concept but the markup is absurd.


UPDATE: Revisited LM today. The prices on many products were reduced, such as the Savannah Bee Company honey comb from $60 to $20.49. It was less busy than the previous times I have been and the staff was rather helpful. I will only come here for speciality items because of the markup and parking hassle (they will validate parking upon checkout which is nice).

I read some good yelp reviews and was eager to try this place on a recent business trip this past summer. Donuts as buns, can't go wrong, right?

Well, I ordered a burger medium cooked and it was way overcooked and the toppings were messed up, tried to send it back but my server gave me a lot of attitude and said it'd take 45min. He was really creepy/agro about it.  The whole experience was uncomfortable for me and my guest. Next time we're sticking to cheese-steaks!
The best. Everything is good and it's always awesome. The atmosphere is fantastic and you get a carrot cake if you use the ATM. What more could you ask for??

Dia de los Burritos has its concept/brand on point but unfortunately the food does not live up to the hype at all.

The overall aesthetic and concept is what compelled me to stop in here. The inside was well decorated. They sell A LOT of Dia de los Burritos branded items, from multiple styles of t-shirts to hot sauces to skate decks. The stickers are free.

They have a board up that shows a small selection of the full menu. It was only until after I ordered at the register that I noticed the little menu card on the counter that had many more options. I ordered the vegan tacos but they have the "impossible" plant-based meat available too (not listed on their menu board, only on the menu card).

The tacos were very underwhelming. I'm not exaggerating when I say there was zero seasoning--no chili powder, no garlic, no cilantro, not even salt. The tortillas were straight out of the bag, not warmed or prepared in anyway. My friend who ordered the chicken tacos noted that the chicken was dry and unseasoned as well. They were overpriced. $12 and change for 3 tacos that were mostly lettuce.

The meal came with a little bag of chips but they were supermarket variety--a fairly lazy move considering every Mexican place under the sun fries their own chips in house. 

The food overall is a loose, hipster-ized interpretation of Mexican, where anything goes as long as it comes in a tortilla.

I was super excited to find a roti shop in the area and Hot on D Spot did not disappoint in the slightest! I ordered a dhal puri with fillings of pumpkin and chana. The dhal puri had a good proportion of split peas to roti. I asked for hot sauce and the amount was perfect to give the filling a kick of spice. The portion was massive and well worth the $8-I could only eat half and saved the rest for later. Service was quick, I placed my order for pickup and the food was hot and ready by the time I arrived 15 minutes later.

We were the only ones in the place on a Friday night.  BYOT.  Brought our own tequila for margaritas.  Friendly service and good food.  Very large portions.  Owner's entire family helped serve our meal, including their 5 year old daughter who brought out the salsa.

If you're looking for outstanding Neapolitan pizzas this side of the coast, Grimaldi's Pizzeria is where to find it.  

Grimaldi's is an institution in the pizza genre. It offers authentic New York style Margherita pizzas with its thin base and cooked in a coal-fired brick oven giving way to a puffed-up beautifully blistered edges. The center remains soft and one of the best ways to enjoy it is to fold the slices in half. 

Service was excellent! Our pizza took a little longer than usual to come out. In addition to our server as well as the manager coming out to check on us periodically, they also gave us a discount. 

Pizza is one of the universally loved dishes and the fantastic coal-fired pies that are served here are delicious and certainly destination-worthy.
Great cheese steaks and fried pickles...

Many people will tell you there is no such thing as a bad meal in New Orleans.  That isn't necessarily true, but certainly, the number of culinary gems in this city are hardly rare.  Still, even amongst immense competition, Willie Mae's manages to shine by offering what was clearly some of the best fried chicken I've ever eaten.  

The skin is what first catches your taste buds.  Subtly crisp and lightly crunchy, the texture itself is a sight to behold.  The cooking method retails a significant amount of oil, and the spice mix is stupendously satisfying.  The chicken stays juicy throughout the entire course of your meal.  I've eaten at a number of fried chicken joints in states such as Tennessee, Alabama, Texas, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi and South Carolina.  Other than an absolutely perfect rendition of fried chicken from regionally renowned chef Jeff McInnis in Miami, FL, this was the best I've ever eaten.  

As your side, I would suggest skipping the more common orders and going with the butter beans.  When they are prepared appropriately, they can be divine and Willie Mae's knows what they are doing.  We also really liked the green beans and the others at my table seemed to take a liking to the mac and cheese as well.  Still, the butter beans are on another level. 

In a city chock full of Cajun food, it's a little surprising that this meal was the highlight of the culinary aspects of the trip.  All that said, it's definitely worth your time.

Those Di Bruno Bros are alright!

Winding down our time at the Italian market, we decided to stop in and get some snacks for dinner, but it looked like the rest of Philly had the same idea based on the crowd inside!

Di Bruno Bros staff are top notch, not only explaining everything you could imagine with the thing you're pointing at behind the counter, but also in giving you great pairing advice if you want one thing to go with another.

We got the following things:

Blue cheese
Parmesan Cheese
liver pate
Prosciutto 

Man this was some good stuff!  Cheese is excellent, coming from "the house of cheese".  The blue cheese was both creamy and had these little crunchy ends to it which made me smile every time I took a bite.  The Parmesan was also fresh and really popped with flavor.

As for the meats, i'd never tried pate before Di Bruno Bros, but how delicious!  The prosciutto wrapping the blue cheese was some of the best things we'd eaten in Philly.  

Everything we sampled was fresh, and even if you weren't sure about a cheese or a cured meat, they'd happily slice a little off for you to try, and try we did.  I really didn't taste anything I didn't like.  The problem, it seems, was making a selection!

I didn't know what I was expecting when I walked in, but if I lived in the area, i'd be at Di Bruno Bros several times a month for snacks.  If you're in the Italian market, or even if you're not (they have a website), check these Bros out!

Gotta be honest...I had zero plans to come to either Pat's OR Geno's, especially since everyone in Philly that we met said only tourists go to those places because they aren't good.  But go we did, and eat we did, so that we could experience some of the more famous dueling Philly sandwich shops around.  

We started our adventure at Pat's splitting one Philly before walking across the street to have  another here at Geno's.

First off, i'll say that Geno's is definitely the cleaner of the two.  Shiny, polished, and ridiculously fast.  From order to sandwich in hand must've been 3 minutes. We split their Cheese steak with whiz ($10 with tax)

The Philly at Geno's has meat that is cut in long thin slices, comes with cooked onions and whiz.  Here's the thing....the sandwich was lacking in flavor completely, although it looked delicious.  My girlfriend on the other hand preferred Geno's to Pat's (so taste buds my vary).  

Geno's customer service was top notch, nice, informative, not pushy (like I thought Pat's staff were), and when we get our sandwich whole, they were more than happy to cut it in half for us so that we could share.

Do I have anything bad to say about Gino's?  No.  Outside of their sandwich having a lack of flavor.  I personally think they lose the war with Pat's, but my girlfriend disagrees so the war continues.  Don't take my word on it though....

If you're in Philly and you want to experience this place, check it out!  Just understand that there are far more flavorful Philly sandwiches around the city!

P.S. Cash Only!

Dalessandro's Steaks and Hoagies was a destination I was told by my girlfriend that we WERE paying a visit to when we arrived in Philadelphia. She used to live in Philly and Dalessandro's was the Philly place she took all her visiting friends to.  You know what?  This place is a great place to grab a sandwich!

We paid Dalessandro's a  visited on a Saturday night and dang....the line was not only out the door, but it was standing room only inside!  There is parking at Dalessandro's, but good luck getting a spot in front of the shop. There is street parking lining the road here though.  We found a spot that was probably a 2 minute walk away.

We ended up getting the cheese steak ($9) and a couple of Birch Beers (didn't catch the prices).  Expect a wait after you place your order, depending on the line.  We waited about a half hour but the sandwich was worth it!  

There's no being stingy with the meat when it comes to the cheese steaks here.  The meat is finely chopped and fills up the bread.  Cheese and caramelized onions fill out the cheese steak.  That first bite is ridiculous and i'm almost sad I had to share half of this thing!  You'll definitely want your own.  

Cash only at this (and seemingly many philly cheese steak spots), but if you don't have cash, no worries!  There's an ATM inside Dalessandro's.

At the end of the day, if you want a cheese steak from Philly and you're in the area, you really need to take the time to pay Dalessandro's a visit.  The only reason I didn't give Dalessandro's 5 stars was because without the cheese whiz it was slightly drier than with the whiz. The next time I'm back I'll change that, and likely bump up my review. 

Worth every bite!

Ishkabibble's was a site my girlfriend took us to eat for our first Philly when we were knee deep in our first night in Philadelphia cheese steak.  So what did I think?

We decided to start off with one of their original chicken steaks and split a Chicken cheese steak with provolone ($10)  This thing came out stuffed full of chopped grilled chicken, and was topped with melted cheese.  

The sandwich at first bite was really dry i'm afraid.  With that said, they do have some condiments to help out.  Ketchup and some oil later, and the sandwich was much less dry, but not my favorite this trip.

There's a few stools and bar counters for sitting but that's about it in this small area.  Customer service was nice and pretty informative too.

Operating since 1979, I really wanted to like ishkabibble's more, and maybe if I got one of their beef Philly's i'd have been blown away.  

I'll definitely go back to hopefully bump up my score, but for now, i'll have to leave Ishkabibble's with 3 stars.

Taking a break from Philly cheese steaks during our extended weekend in  Pennsylvania, friends of ours invited us out for dinner at Limoncello in West Chester.  How'd I like things?

They started us out with  a tomato and cheese bruschetta, which were pretty good!  Orders came next, and I decided on their Margherita personal pizza ($14)

Less is more with this pizza, being topped with tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella and basil, the pizza was almost too pretty to eat, but eat it I did!

Thin crust, the pizza crust was really crispy, which is what I like, but sadly, the flavor really wasn't there, at least not like other Margherita pizzas i've had in the past.

Serving size of everything that hit the table were great for the price, and customer service was ridiculously helpful. 

There is street parking here, but there's a few lots around that you can pay for a few dollars as well.  If you're just coming to dine, i'd recommend trying to find some street parking before you pay for a parking lot.

Great ambiance, really nice food presentation, but flavors, at least for me, missed the mark.  But tell me what you think!

''Hey, where are you?'

'I'm at old city coffee'

*looks around*

'Uhhh, I'm at old city coffee, I don't see you in line!'

'Are you at the one at the back?  I'm at the one at the front!'

'Ooooooh'

And that conversation with my better half was when I realized there were two locations of old city coffee within the popular Reading terminal.

So having two locations is convenient for sure, but what did I think of the coffee itself?

Not bad!

Old City has nice strong coffee and a series of freshly roasted coffees going as tame as french roast, to as interesting as the Sumatra Takengon blend.

I got their Old City blend, which was strong, and a nice cup.  

There are no booths or seating at either location for old city, but as mentioned earlier, being inside of reading terminal means there's a large amount of community seats and tables that you can sit and enjoy your cup. 

Speaking of cup enjoyment...I don't know that I would stand in the long lines that I both saw and stood in again for the cup of coffee I selected, but if i'm in the area, need a cup and lines are manageable, sure i'd stop in!  

Decent cup of joe!

"I don't like Jim's because when you go there for lunch you smell like cheese sticks all day"....words from a friend of mine who lives in Philadelphia.

I have to be honest with you, Jim's Steaks South st gave us a great sandwich!!

Paying these guys a visit just after walking around a few blocks to try to walk off a Ishkabibble's sandwich, we then stopped on in here when the aroma snagged us.  

We decided on the cheese steak ($9) with cheese whiz and caramelized onions.  OMG the smell of fried onions is 

SO

GOOD

!!!

It's a simple sandwich really.  Chopped beef, onions, cheese, nice bread, and that's it folks.  I enjoyed every bite, and because we split the sandwich, all the calories didn't make me feel so bad.

There is a seating area where the food is being cooked, but walk up a narrow set of stairs and it'll take you to an upstairs dining room where there's plenty of tables to sit.

Much more of a touristy place to get a bite, for me Jim's delivers and in a world where smelling like a cheese steak all day gets you a great sandwich, well I hope no one i'm sitting next to is a vegetarian!!

Great spot, good food!

So yea, go here!

The Reading Terminal Market (Pronounced as 'red', not 'reed') is a collection of restaurants, shops and stores that really could soak up an entire day here if you wanted it to.  Sadly we didn't have all day, and just a few hours, but I think we sampled a fair amount of what the Redding Terminal had to offer.  

Rather than list every store that's found at the market, i'll just list the locations we visited.  Those places were we visited were:

DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef
Flying Monkey
Old City Coffee inc
Termini Brother's Bakery
Beiler's pickle patch
Glick's rib shack

Again, by no way is my very small sample of the market a real representation of the market, but my tastebuds were happy and if/when I return to Philadelphia, i'll be back to the Reading Terminal Market to sample more of what this place has to offer.  

100% pay this place a visit, and bring your appetite!!

We, "Tommy Up", have moved to using obscenities because it is the only TRUE way to convey the utter Disappointment at coming to the "cool new spot" and getting the absolute worst service I have ever experienced. But not only that, watching the owner sitting at a table (though I must say I DID observe you getting off of your chair and putting out "CAUTION: WET FLOOR" signs when the rains fell) while his staff did the same. THAT is why Raiden needs to drop an "F" bomb when reviewing your spot. I'm all about second or even third chances so prove me wrong. I'm a chef, a burger nut, a foodie, and have a great pallet.....so prove me wrong party promoter, prove me wrong. My friends INSISTED on tipping. I personally wouldn't have given that waiter the steam off my lavender scented shit knot on a cold winter's morn...

After my Friday exodus, how do I not say "Woohoo! As good as it gets!?" 

Chris M is right... if this place was closer to my home, I'd eat here daily. With unlimited free sides & free tea, there's a good chance I'd just linger here or make it my new office. Wait, screw I'll do it anyway. 

Plus, I love running the flag up that pole (it's like The Maypole for Foodies). 

Maybe it was the sunny Friday, maybe it was the fish po' boy options for Lent, or maybe it's just that damn good, but Papa Roux was slammed when we were there. I have a thing for slammed eateries -- read: I'd eat at slammed New York delis daily if I could where men yell at me "take a number!" And this had that feel to it. 

How do I resist a roasted pork po' boy with the possibility of adding "crunchy bits of bacon goodness" to it? You're right. I can't. So I did. And, I was kindly rewarded with pork to the dome -- somuchso other patrons of Papa Roux were said to see me have a giant pink pig head on my body that day. 

Creole side: spicy, strong. 
Etoufee: peppery and creamy... the way it should be. I'll be back to order the entree with some sort of sea-faring beast. 

If you dine out in Indy at casual locations, there's a good chance you'll spend between $6 - $12, and there's no reason not to spend it at locally owned eateries -- especially ones with badass cajun eats, graffiti on the walls, service faster than the roller girls they support and ones (like Papa Roux) that give you a sense of ceremony, creativity and this is your last day on Earth, so eat here. Cheers to that.

Mothers was the first restaurant I hit up as soon as I landed in New Orleans. Locals, Yelp, folks at my job all mentioned Mothers and it's the place to go for lunch/dinner. I just happened to arrive at 2pm that day and dragged my cousin with me to dine here. 

The best potato salad I've ever had is here. I'm not a huge fan of potato salad on the first place, but Mother's definitely took the trophy for this one. The greens were perfectly cooked and they drain out the excess juices, but it's still very flavorful. I ordered the crawfish étouffée and there were a couple of crawfish on each spoonful entering my hungry mouth. The jambalaya was great too, with a little Louisiana hot sauce! My only complaint would be that it's a small mom and pop shop so the line can get really long. You order your food first before you can sit down anywhere. Some parts of my food was a little cold as this is like an assembly line for the sides, but I still smashed the whole plate.

This place was delicious! It's also dog friendly and it was wonderful to see other dogs on the patio for dining. 

Drinks:
BLTA Bloody Mary - avocado, bacon, lettuce and tomato in a Bloody Mary is a meal in itself! I wanted this because I thought the BLTA was smashed in between a couple of slices of bread like a sandwich. It's an unwich without the bread. 

Mojito - many different flavors, but we opted for the original. Delicious and highly recommended!

Creme brûlée martini - a little too sweet in my opinion but it's definitely a dessert drink!

Appetizer:
Barbecue prawns - a little expensive for 4 prawns but the dish was very good! A lot of flavors and a hint of spice. 

Entree: 
Beef stroganoff - super delicious and a must try! Big pieces of sliced steak. The sauce is so good, you want to drink it. 

Philly cheese steak - the salad is lightly dressed and the philly is served on a ciabatta bun. Weird to call it a philly cheese without the hoagie roll, but I enjoyed the crispness of the bun.

What. A.Joke.  

This place gets comically worse each time. 

For starters, apparently I had a broken water glass. So when I sat down and The waiter poured water, it spilled everywhere and got on my jacket, shoes, etc... but that was an accident. It got cleaned up, it's just water. 

The deal breaker today is the empanadas. The menu says empanadaS for $14 and only one one brought out. It was hilarious. We called them out of it and the waiter blamed it on the new chef who got happy hour mixed up. It was 22:00 at this point on a Tuesday night. The same waiter was also the one who brought out these empanadas. I mean empanadA. Waiter apologized and explained that he adjusted the price for one since it's supposed to be $15 so he charged $7.50. It's actually $14 so it should have been $7.00. It's not the 50 cents I'm upset about, it's White Dog. These types of things should not be happening - consistently cold $8 truffle fries, overcooked $19 burger, tepid food, and now  graduated to messing up portion sizes and overcharging.

White Dog is longer a place I recommend to people.  Only reason why we came this time is because of a 1000 point reservation on Open Table. I'd used to always  bring my family and friends every time they came to visit  since I moved here in 2012. Not anymore. The establishment has gone downhill and QA apparently doesn't exist. 

I would try Louie Louie instead, especially before it goes downhill since I hear management is same? :-0

When you pay for food, you are paying for the food and/or positive experience, yes? Well you won't get that here. Chances are, part of your food will be missing. It's luck of the draw really, no need to overspend to play food roulette. 

It is way overpriced for what it is.  You would also think that if you buy these overpriced baked concoction of flour/yeast (about $2 a pop) in bulk, they would pack it up more nicely.  I got two dozen for work and they were all dumped into a brown bag like I just went grocery shopping.  Panera at least puts in it a nice cardboard box with handles. Oh and not sliced.  At least Panera asks.

Customer service also sucked during the bagel purchase visit. When I got there, the girl continued her conversation with her co-worker regarding something superfluous and frivolous (as in personal gossip vs work related) as another patron and I stood there staring into space waiting for her to finish or notice. She also got slightly impatient when I didn't know where to get the cream cheese. Sheesh

Ah yes, and now The Cure breakfast bagel sandwich (Beef brisket, bacon, eggs, and smoked cheddar sriracha spread) for $11.50. I've gotten that 5 times and they forgot the cheddar sriracha three times. It comes with the bagel sandwich too so they're not providing me with the full product and still charging for it.  Actually today was the fifth time I got the sandwich and they forgot the spread again AND the bacon. Only FOUR things go into this sandwich.... FOUR.  Yet this place keeps fking it up. OMG and this place is called Spread and they keep forgetting the spread!!!!

So... 
1. Subpar "bulk" bagel purchase experience 
2. Forgot the cheddar sriracha spread
3. Forgot the cheddar sriracha spread
4. Forgot the cheddar sriracha spread AND bacon

Three strikes and  you're out! I've been more than generous with this place, but I'm done with this joint. It'd be a different story if it was a $5 sandwich, but Spread is charging someone  $12 to eat their negligence. It really makes me consider changing industries if Spread is getting away with this nonsense.

Here's another thing: if they are out of stuff and you're waiting in line for 20 minutes, they won't tell you ahead of time. One time we waited in line for about 20 minutes and when we got up to order, they said they were out of brisket and bacon. What a waste of time this place is.  Other places I've been to tell patrons in advance so they are not mindlessly waiting.

Welcome to Sparks Gourmelt!! So happy to have you in the neighborhood.
We came to visit the new Gourmelt location at Sparks Galleria three days after they had opened. I thought they were going to be overwhelmed with the opening, but they managed it like pros!   

The Place: 
Brand new everything! Colorful and cute little grilled sandwich shop. Inspired by old school restaurants, the shop reminds me of those 1920s ads. 
 
The Food:
Grilled sandwiches of course, salads, soups, and sides. Their menu has different types of grilled sandwiches and "Do your own" grilled sandwich. You can choose a combo with soup or a side.   

During my first visit, I had the "Croque Madame" American style, Provolone cheese, Chèvre, ham, dijon and fried egg on sourdough bread 
For side, I had their tomato soup and to share; we had some fries. 

The sandwich was delicious. I loved the flavors and how cheesy it was! The soup, in my opinion, could use more spices because it was a little simple. 
The parmesan garlic french fries were amazing! Perfectly crunchy and tasty. One side is definitely enough to share. 

My second visit, I made my own sandwich with lettuce, tomatoes, and ham and I had the sweet potatoes. Once again, a great quality sandwich at a  reasonable price. 


The Service:
The staff is friendly and they know what they are doing. In my two visits, they were busy but I noticed how the staff had their roles well assigned.
One member takes your order, the kitchen staff cooks, and other member delivers your food and makes sure the tables are clean.   

I am coming back! Too good, not to.

Time for an UPDATE! 
I finally found what I like the most at SUP 

The Place:
The restaurant is a small townhouse in the heart of Reno Midtown on Virginia street. SUP offers outdoor and indoor seating. They have a porch with tables and benches, a nice place to be on sunny days. The inside seating area reminds me like to be having dinner in a family's house: cozy and welcoming. 

The Food:
SUP specializes in lunches: Soups, salads, sandwiches and more. 
They have daily specials and combos where you get soup, salad and a sandwich. 
The reason I am updating my review is their "Crab and shrimp salad" I don't even know where to begin describing how delicious this salad is. 
Is it the generous serving of crab? Is it the giant shrimps? Is it their amazing blue cheese? Is it their perfectly picked avocado? Is it their fresh lettuce and tomatoes? I don't know what it is, but I am addicted to this salad! I love it and I crave it a lot!  My favorite dish, perhaps. 5/5

In my previous review, I was a being a brat, and I complained about the steak salad. Here is the deal: It is served cold, but you can request it to be warm and everything will be perfect! I like to have the steak salad with chimichurri sauce, in my humble Colombian opinion, they KNOW how to make chimichurri. The salad has strawberries, cranberry, lettuce, blue cheese, croutons. I love to put the sauce and mix all the ingredients.; I enjoy the combination and the contrast of the flavors. Their blue cheese, again, AMAZING! 4/5

On Thursdays, if anybody feels adventurous and wanting to try something new. I recommend you the "AJIACO" This is a Colombian very popular dish: Chicken, corn, potatoes, veggies, sour cream and more in a soup. Perfect for cold days or when you feel hangover ;-) I had it one time and I was glad to see that is now a weekly item in the menu. 4/5
 
Wait, I cannot finish my review without mentioning one of my favorite things about lunch at SUP, they give you a little homemade oatmeal and chocolate chips cookie...   OMG they make my day with this cookie. It's the perfect amount of sweet after lunch! 5/5

The Service:
Service is nice, the staff is friendly and they know how to deal with big crowds at lunchtime.

Online order:
SUP has online ordering, so you can order your salad, sandwich or soup and walk from work to pick it up (If you work in the Reno Downtown/Midtown District). They are pretty good at timing when the order would be ready. 
The online system will not let you order combos. I hope to see this option available to order online soon. 

Thank you, SUP for all the delicious lunches during my Busy season in Downtown Reno :-)

I met a group of friends at California Pizza Kitchen before J- Balvin's concert at Grand Sierra Resort. I was really excited because their menu is different and unique.

The Place:
The restaurant is cute and chic. They have nice booths and tables; perfect for big groups. They have a pretty bar and great cocktails on their menu.

The Food:
The menu has salads, pasta, soups, and appetizers. Pizza menu here is really interesting. They have unique pizza flavors. We ordered two medium pizzas for a group of 4 people. We got the "Carne Asada." -Yes! A pizza with actual Mexican carne asada! It was so good! They brought us salsa to put on it. 
We also had "The Works," a pizza with spicy Italian sausage, pepperoni, and mushrooms. -It was great pizza as well! 

While we waited for the food, we got the "Sangria Flight" Three different flavors of sangria. Orange, raspberry, and strawberry. My favorite was the raspberry sangria!

We also wanted to check the desserts, so we got "The Butter Cake," thanks to our server recommendation, and we also got a "Key Lime Pie." The butter cake, definitely inspired by Mastro's. It was delicious and decadent. The key lime was refreshing and sooo good!

The Service:
Justin was our server that night and he was awesome!! He did such a good job. He took our orders, brought our food and drinks promptly, he also gave us great suggestions for drinks and desserts.

Overall, a great place to meet with friends for drinks and pizza. I give them 4 Stars. Yes! I will be coming back!

My husband and I were looking for a new place to try for a late lunch. It was his turn to pick, and he chose Mexican. We filtered our search on the Yelp app, and Macho Tequilas came up.

The Place: 
The restaurant was colorful and full of decorations. They had pinatas hanging from the roof, paintings, and all kind of stuff.
They have a bar and table seating. The tables might remind you like your dining table at home. We got a big table just for the two of us.

The Food:
The server brought us chips & salsa and took our drink and food order. I got a Margarita (of course), and my husband had a corona. We got some guacamole for the chips and green and red sauce. The green sauce was SPICY, but I could not stop eating it!

For lunch, I had the "Carne Asada" no tortillas and white rice and husband got a chicken "Wet Burrito."  We were happy with the food. My carne asada was delicious! It tasted really good. I loved the rice and beans. 
The chicken burrito was enchilada style. The sauces and seasoning were very authentic. We were greatly surprised by the food at this place. We had no idea about it.
 

The Service:
A nice lady took good care of us during our visit. She made sure we had enough chips, waters, and drinks. The food came out in promptly and our check too. 

Yes, I will be coming back. Sometimes, I feel we have so many Mexican places in Reno, but they are all the same. So I am glad to find something a little bit more different finally.

A hidden brunch gem all the way on Dickerson road.
I have been here two times now and I am just OBSESSED!!

The place:
The restaurant is located on Northwest Reno surrounded by all these car shops.  The restaurant is a cute small cafe. It looks a little old school but very cute. They have lots of windows and a patio for sunny and warm days.  

The Food:
I have been for brunch and the food is delicious! I first came with my dear friend Rosie. We had the croissant sandwich, french toast, and the chicken fried steak. Everything was delicious! The highlight was definitely the Hawaiian French toast! It's sooo good! The croissant sandwich had the softest croissant with cheddar cheese. I loved it! 
I am a big potato fan and the country potatoes side did not disappoint! However, on my last visit, I had the fried chicken steak and the potatoes were a bit burned.
The chicken steak has a delicious gravy! OMG! I loved it.  

The menu has cocktails, coffee, soft drinks and more. I had the mimosas on both visits. The mimosa on my last visit was not good. It was warm and the champagne had no bubbles. 

The Service:
On both visits, I have noticed the service is a bit slow. The food comes out fast, but the service is not up to speed. You walk in and have to wait to get seated there are some open tables, but they still have the stuff from the previous customer. Both times I had to wait to be seated with plenty of open tables. 

Other than this, the service is good. The servers are polite and as I say, the food comes out fast. 

Despite the comments I had for this restaurant, I really like their food and I think I will continue to come. My husband loved it after I brought him and we cannot wait to bring some of our friends for brunch. 

I had the opportunity to meet chef Nate on my first visit, and he showed Rosie and some of the specials they make for dinner. I am interested in trying those out!  

 Overall 4.5 stars!

There are a lot of Mexican restaurants in Reno and Sparks, but I personally think that La Fuente has good quality and quantity food. 

The food has a traditional flavor and it looks like make from scratch. I hate going to those place where they give you microwave rice ewww. This place have an amazing white rice ( it reminded me the one my grandma used to cook for me), sadly they don't make it every day. But don't worry they red rice also taste good. 

The service here is good. The waiters are always taking care of you. If you are tempted to have a Margarita I should highly recommend a watermelon margarita! OMG! They are so good! But watch up because  they put some tequila on those. the guacamole here its good! It's not watery like in most places. 

My favorite items on the menu are: Carne Asada, Pescado Frito (Fried Red Snapper) and parrillada (which is a a plate for 2 people). The Carne asada is delicius, it comes with beans , rice and salad. Everything it's very tasty. The fried fish is good but it might be a little too spicy for my taste, other than that yummy!! The parrillada it's like a combination plate, you get sirloin steak, with pork, chorizo, rice and beans. 

The restaurant is cute, their seats are comfortable and they have a little water fountain. They also have a private room for events. I saw they have live music on Fridays and Saturdays.

I was happy to try Estella and Tacos finally. I remember when restaurants opened back, Estella's brunch caught my attention on Instagram. Their food looked fresh and flavorful and people seem to be having a great time. 
Well, that's the thing with Instagram; everything looks too pretty and then you face reality. 
Last Sunday, my husband, best friend and I went to Estella Tacos & Mezcal for brunch. 

The Place: 
The restaurant is located next to the Jesse hotel; an outdoor patio connects them. At first, we tried to walk into the restaurant, but they said that they were closed and that if we wanted something, we needed to order from the bar at The Jesse's. 
So we got there and met our friend. Their menu is small but very flavorful. We ordered our food at the bar and went to a table. 

The Food:
For Sunday brunch we got:
-Breakfast tacos, homemade tortilla tacos, eggs, pinto beans, red salsa and queso fresco on top. Delicious! Great flavor with the red sauce and tortillas tasted great but they were falling apart. 

-Pork Chile Verde: 
Pork in a green sauce with eggs and tortillas. Delicious dish! Very flavorful. I enjoyed the pork with the sauce ad the tortillas even though they kept breaking. The sauce, after a while, got spicy!  Yay!

-Torta Fregadero:
I tried a bite from my friend's torta fregadero, and this was my favorite dish. She had it with al pastor. It comes with mushroom, fried egg (which they never asked how she wanted it cooked),  queso, beans, pickles and chipotle crema. The torta tasted delicious and it was served on local bread. But I noticed that the tortas do not have a side. I enjoy my sandwich with a side -some potatoes/tater tots/something! 

-Fregadero Cubana:
This dish tasted like a really good Cuban sandwich. I loved the flavor and the bread but felt like they were missing a side. 

We had our meals with mimosas. 

The Service:

I know we should be cutting some slack to restaurants because everybody is understaffed, recovering, etc. But I got to tell you... I did not care about waiting a long time for the food to come or being completely ignored by whoever was the server. 
What really disappointed me was that when I requested silverware, the lady taking care of us looked up like I was an idiot for asking so she pointed at a metal basket where they put napkins, dishes, and silverware. Well, we have already checked the container and there was no silverware!  
Then she apologized and brought the metal container filled with supplies. 
The second thing that disappointed me was that nobody asked how the meal was or if we wanted another mimosa. In fact, we never got water. After we paid, I rushed to my water bottle in the car. I understand the vibe is bar go and order at the bar. Go and sit at any other bar and see how they are offer their customers water. 

The place was not busy; they had two more tables and a couple of people at the bar.

I'm so excited that I finally visited Death and taxes! I heard so much about this place and it did fill my expectations and beyond. 

The place: 
The place it's like a town house in Midtown, they have outdoor and indoor seating. They both are dark. Their bar is really nice, they have any kinds of liquors. I saw a great selection of whisky mmmm. 
There are some bar stools, sofas and tables, it's like a good place to hang out and have drinks. They have some music playing in the background but you can still have a conversation. 

The drinks: 
Oh man, I don't know where to start, first I want to congratulate Ivan, the mixologist, for his incredible drinks. He is so talented! I'm still amazed by his drinks. 
So we started the night with a "Caipirinha" - a Brazilian drink made with lime and cachaça, Ivan had the good brand "Fogo Novo" it was delicious and very cute presentation. 

Then we had the "Mojito" - the mojito was made with pineapple juice or something and it was really good and refreshing! Yumm cheers. 

Then I remember a good friend told me they had great "pisco sours" here. So I couldn't leave without trying them. Pisco sours are original from Peru, made with egg yolks, oh man! It was really really good! 

So at this point and after all the mixing, it would probably be a good idea to go home. I was almost ready to go when Ivan mention he made incredible "Mai Tai" he was not joking! It was amazing! I can't think of another place in Reno with amazing drinks like here! 

My husband and I were super impressed by the place. The only thing I couldn't get used to is the darkness. I guess because I'm blind, it was hard for me too see and get around. 

The place was busy, but Ivan make sure to take care of us. Overall great experience! I give them 4.9 Stars

Happy anniversary to us! We love trying nice, (new to us) places for our anniversary dinners. So I got on Yelp and started looking up some great options. I then gave my wife a list of restaurants to choose from. This place was her great choice, just like when she chose me. ;) 
The staff here was incredibly friendly and helpful. They were so glad to have guests dining in again after such a long hiatus when indoor dining wasn't possible in St. Louis County due to Covid restrictions. The decor is really great, and there is plenty of space between tables. 
The food was outstanding as you can see my photos of our shared meal. They even brought our dessert out with a giant sparkler on top to help us celebrate. That was so cool and much appreciated! 
We will definitely go back as our entire experience was really fun with high quality, really great food.

[Warning: The surgeon general warns that writing reviews after multiple margaritas may result in an inflated review.]

Well, being from California, I was some what skeptical of a Mexican place in the of the country.  I went to a Mexican place in Wisconsin and was disappointed so I was hoping it wouldn't be the case again being slightly further south.

Good things:
We split the 10 taco's dish which had 2 of each kind of taco so I got to try every style.  I'm much more of a fan of the taqueria style tacos and that's what these were like.

Pescado - 3.5 stars
Baja style beer battered tilapia.  A little too much sauce for my taste and the fish didn't really stand out.  So much sauce that the corn tortilla was starting to fall apart.

Tacos con Carnitas de Pato - 3 stars again
I think the duck was more of a novelty, but overall the flavor was there.

Pollo - 4 stars
Nicely seasoned, could have had a platter of these and had been happy.

Al Pastor - 2.5 stars
Definitely would have liked about twice as much filling in this one, and not so much of it the pineapple salsa.  The pineapple was threw the balance and this taco was the lightest for filling.

Carne Asada - 4 stars
Same with the chicken, well seasoned and a healthy portion.

Margaritas (3 stars) were recommended over the coconut mojitos (starting to wish I had at least one of each now).  Pretty standard.and served in a highball glass so the salted rim was somewhat limited.

The taco platter also came with tableside guac (pass, not a guac fan) and fresh salsa (4 stars).  I asked for the hottest salsa they had and they only used serrano peppers, which of course means it wasn't even hot enough to be called mild.  I suppose they wanted to keep it fresh, and while the flavor was excellent, it just was not hot at all.  The waiter was kind enough to bring out a habanero based sauce but noted it was not fresh habanero, however, it did the trick and made the salsa hot enough to make it addictive.  If they had hotter fresh peppers, this would have been 5 stars for sure.

Overall, 3.5 stars, rounded up to 4 because it's adjusted for Indianapolis.

Tucson, AZ: still awesome! 

Still love both our "Protein Style" Double Double and Hamburger. Our burger patties were generously enveloped in lettuce leaves, and beef patties seasoned just right. Really appreciate the option of grilled onions. Something is perculiar about their fries though. I saw the potatoes being cut, yet our fries, even my "extra crispy" that were not that much more crunchy, had the mealy texture of frozen fries, so loss of a star.  Service was friendly, staff was active in keeping the store spotless, and although the parking lot was full, the line to order moved quickly. Love the availability of fresh lemon wedges! Can't wait to come back.

Tucsin, AZ: busy, but so friendly

Hubby wanted me to try this Mexican restaurant he's been to a number of times on previous trips. It stood out once he pointed to it on a rise, being a bright, mint green building. Its crowded parking lot was a good sign. The short wait for a table gave me a chance to watch their fresh tortillas being made. I was told no pictures allowed though, so no up close photos there.

Menus were offered as we were seated. Water and house fried corn chips were served soon after. Love the thick, red, mild salsa that accompanied the chips.

FOOD
Three Machaca Black Angus Tacos ($11) 4/5
Carnitas, rice+beans+corn+      tortillas($15.50) 4/5
Corn tortillas to go (12-5" / $4) 4/5

Hubby very much enjoyed his platter of corn tortilla tacos, gluten free and delicious.  I later Googled "machaca" and learned that the meat is simmered, dried, and rehydrated. I had asked that the tomatillo jalapeno sauce usually ladeled over my carnitas be served on the side so the photo doesn't do justice to the tasty, crispy outside/tender inside pieces of braised pork. It was so delicious, I overlooked the guacamole and pico de gallo that was missing from my plate but mentioned on the menu. The house made corn tortillas were small but tender, and I ordered a stack to go. Portion sizes were small on the tacos and carnitas. Refried beans were average but I know that the rice was scratch made because the rice kernels' cores were still hard, indicating lack of adequate cooking time. Maybe next time, reorder carnitas sans rice and beans, but with a side of tortillas.
Service was gracious and with smiles. I noticed a service staff person (tall, thin, dark haired male) apologize and retrieved the correct menu for guests, at a nearby table, who were accidentally given an all breakfast menu during lunch time.
Would love to return to try other menu items.

Tucson, AZ (Rita Ranch): fantastic!

Awesome service and delicious food. We were seated immediately, arriving just before HH ended. When my House Margarita arrived in blended form instead of "over the rocks", the serving staff apologized, removed the erroneous drink, and promptly returned with my proper order, a simple but well composed drink where I could taste the tequila not in slushy form. Complimentary, house made chips, light and crispy, and salsa with a bit of kick, made for a great  start to our meal.

FOOD
Green Chili Pork Burrito w/rice & beans
Shredded Chicken Taco w/ rice & beans
Off menu Chorizo con Huevo 
Shredded Beef Chimichanga w/rice & beans

I was surprised at seeing just a 3.5 star rating. This was our friends' favorite Mexican restaurant. We had to agree it was good. The rice was savory and moist. The refried beans were creamy and topped with melted cheese. Hubby thoroughly enjoyed his breakfast for dinner, his chorizo con huevo (sausage with eggs). My chimichanga shell was crispy and the generous shredded beef filling very tender and flavorful. Both our friends' taco and burrito did not disappoint. Our server stopped by at least three times after our food arrived to see how we were doing, and even brought out a second bowl of chips. The water glasses and iced tea were continually refilled.There is a bar and Happy Hour (2-5pm every day) is also served in the dining room. Two separate non-gender specific restrooms. Excellent service, delicious food, located in a strip mall with a small lot, accessed from southbound Houghton, south of Rita. Would love to come back to try more of their menu.

We enjoyed an incredible meal today with outstanding service. We sat down and were greeted by our server Tanya. When you check in on Yelp you get a coupon for a free Margarita which is very good. Tanya thanked me for checking in and for any feedback that I could provide. They have a nice assortment of lunch time specials as well as appetizer deals for $5 and $7. We started our with the Crab & Shrimp Dip. It was delicious.  I chose the Cioppino special, my wife got the Hog Fish Sandwich. Everything was mouthwatering good. The servings of everything were especially large so we were easily filled. We had an amazing lunchtime experience and the service from Tanya was the best we have had in a long time. We can't wait to go back.

Oh how nothing else can ever fulfill a freebirds craving! And this is the real deal not the fake freebirds chain! My advice is to get the nachos. I really can't even write about it anymore, you'll just have to try it to understand.

So after originally hearing about Giordano's opening here in Indy I was really excited especially after going to the original location in Chicago. 

However, this location doesn't live up to the name. The sad part is I have yet to even eat at this location and here is why.

1. The wait. 

I get that there is going to be a long wait. However, after making a reservation at 4PM and being told that I would be seated at 8:30 I was expecting our party of 16 to be able to be seated as told. When we arrived at 8:15 we were than told by the host that we now has to wait until 10:30. 

Sorry but you don't ever set an expectation for a customer only to make them wait and not meet said expectation. That is bad business.

2. The restaurant.

The first thing I immediately noticed about the restaurant is well the size of the restaurant itself. If you've ever been to the original location in Chicago you know how good of a size the restaurant is. I was quite disappointed on how incredibly small they made Giordano's here in Indy especially on the North side of town. How did they not expect there to be that big of a turnout to one of the best pizza places closest to Chicago?

Updated review! 

Owed barfly an updated review since the first time I've been here. 

Well I've been here 4 times since, twice in the new location and everything seems to be a lot better.

First of all location. Less than a block away from the old but what a difference. Larger location, more seats, outdoor seating for people watching and live bands it seems like every night.

Secondly the food. Same menu but it seems as though things come out fresher and faster. Taco Tuesdays are a must! Along with the grouper sandwich another time visiting was the best grouper sandwich I've had in the area.

Third the drinks. Draft list is mostly all local beers with the exception to Bud light.
If you haven't been to the new location come by and check it out.

I am pretty blown away by this place, and not just for the food.  While waiting for my order, almost everyone that came in was greeted by name because everyone knew each other which was nice.  While waiting they gave me a free drink for waiting and then I was shocked when asked if I wanted some leftovers to bring home to my dog (the non edibles that they don't serve to customers); and then gave me almost a pound of meat!  I'm not a big fan of the dry rib BBQ but this place has me at an exception.  I have never had such tender ribs before this place, I had to keep checking my food ("is this still meat?") because it was. Just. That. Tender.  I am so impressed by the food and the hospitality I've been given.  Having a bad day, this place made me feel so much better.  I can't remember the last time that happened

Highly. Highly. Highly. Recommend!! We did take out/curbside service so unfortunately I can't comment on the inside but let me tell you--the food is hands down DEVINE. I love me some red beans and rice and this by far exceeded my expectations. My wife & I were doing a staycation & wanted a menu that had a little of everything we wanted so our meal consisted of: bacon popcorn, red beans and rice, cornbread, shrimp & grits (came with collards), pulled pork sandwich, edamame, & bread pudding so as you can see we FEASTED and enjoyed every last morsel. It was easy to order online and the food was ready right on time. A friendly text to let us know our order was ready and we were on our way--parking for curbside was right out front and they brought it to our car within a minute or two. All neatly packaged, condiments we asked for were included as well as utensils. 

Every thing we ate was seasoned so well, perfect portions and it knocked my socks off. BACON. POPCORN. need I say more?!! I can't believe we haven't been here before but now that we know what deliciousness awaits we will definitely be coming back.

I love it when the unexpected, but good happens.  A change of plans became a delicious surprise!  We were headed someplace else, but decided we didn't want to drive that far; we were tired.  I said, 'how about that new Italian restaurant, I believe it's right here.'  The front of the building is a little dark and hard to see at night.  We drove right by it once and had to start over.  It's on a one way street.  But one quick loop back around I spotted it on the corner.  It was fairly early so we were seated right away.  There was a nice crowd though...already...that early; good sign.
I love the feel of the place, like your favorite little Italian restaurant.  It's laid out nicely with lots of old brick.  Nice music in the background.  We found out that Mungo's isn't a new restaurant, it just moved to this new location.  Our server was very friendly and attentive.  You get yummy Italian bread and butter to get things started.  Then our food came!  My house salad was phenomenal.  It was just the most perfect salad, with small chopped lettuce, sweet Italian dressing with red onions and crispy prosciutto ham.  Hubby had the tortellini soup, he loved it. I tried it and wow...incredibly rich taste.  So good!  Then hubby had the Beef Tony, it's a tenderloin in a creamy cheese sauce.  I tried it and it was so tender; melted in your mouth!  Try it!  I'm getting that next time!  Although I had the chicken Marsala and it melted in my mouth too!  Seriously good food and I'm picky!  Thanks to changing our plans, we found our new favorite little Italian restaurant!  Bring on the garlic!

After a full day of shopping I was in the mood for a quick hamburger and fries before we headed home.  I checked on yelp and this place was close by and had fairly good reviews.  The pics looked nice too.  So we pulled in and gave this place a try.  The French fries are awesome; my favorite kind.  They are fresh cut potatoes that have bits of crunchy parts, yet soft on the inside.  The fries weren't over salted either which gave them the five stars!  I'm a French fry girl and if a place nails the fries they get my five stars!  However, a lot of other things also deserved the highest score!  Everyone was so friendly and helpful.  The hamburger was thick, juicy and very tasty!  I love the ice they use.  The tiny ice pellets, that's my favorite kind.  The place was very clean, including the bathrooms.  The price wasn't bad, but I only eat plain burgers.  I'm sure if you piled on tons of toppings the price would go up.  I have no complaints whatsoever.  Great place all around!  I enjoyed my burger, fries and coke!

Before things got too bad with Covid, we went out shopping and of course I checked on yelp to see where to eat.  We were really hungry so we ended up someplace else for lunch, but then had to find this place for dessert.  I love the building.  It's a quaint blue house with lots of gingerbread.  I would love to live there, it's such a sweet house.  I can only comment on the dessert, since that's all we had.  I had the snicker pie and it was rich, creamy and chocolaty with a flaky buttery crust.  The dessert case was like a sweet dream!  I concur with the other reviews; go here for dessert!  I bought some melt away cookies to take home and they were crumbling in a good way; melted on your tongue.  I can't wait to go back and eat lunch and have some more dessert.  This place is nestled among a wonderland of shops.  Next trip we'll go earlier so we can check them all out.  Definitely a place to spend the afternoon!

When I walked through the old wooden and glass door, memories so sweet drifted from my soul and caused my heart to skitter about;  I smile.  McGurk's will always have a little hold on me.  I've been coming here for a very long time; but it's been awhile.  I was grateful to see that nothing much had changed.  The old brick walls and wooden tables so worn and bare in places were familiar, comforting like your favorite faded sweatshirt.  The lovely Irish music surrounded me and carried me in, my step a bit lighter.  This Pub is one of my happy places and it felt good to be back.  A must from the menu; their famous potato soup.  It is filled with big chunks of potatoes and carrots that make this soup, thick, luscious and authentic. If the time is right, I think a Guinness would be called for!  The food is always good, the service wonderful, but it's the atmosphere that I adore.  Suddenly, you are in Ireland sitting in a little Irish Pub...sounds good to me!  Thank you John D. McGurk's for great food, drink, music that makes my heart happy and especially wonderful memories.  Hopefully, I'll be back soon...

Open for inside dining.  First visit here.  We were out shopping and got hungry.  We saw this place was open.  I had a hamburger (sorry no cheese). lol. It was small (my perfect size) and it was delicious!  The French fries are fresh cut and my favorite kind!  Our server was friendly and food came quickly!  First time eating here, but won't be the last!! Excellent!

I finally found the best restaurant for Mexican cuisine!  I love Mexican food, but I don't eat it a lot.  I have been wanting to check this place out for awhile now and I'm so glad I finally made it here.  What a nice surprise!  The inside is decorated nicely and the staff are very friendly and helpful.  I was truly surprised by the extensive menu.  Normally it's the usual Mexican fare, but this place has lots of unusual and more authentic dishes!  I had the chicken skewers on a bed of rich with veggies.  I love their Mexican rice.  It's not like any I've had before.  It has vegetables in it and it's very mild; really delicious!  Hubby had something off the 'more authentic' menu.  It was a stew.  It was filled with steak, beans, avocado and green onions.  He loved it.  We really enjoyed the chips and salsa.  Some of the best chips I've ever had and the salsa has the perfect amount of heat and it's a bit more chunky which I really love!  We decided to splurge and get dessert.  We had the apple burrito.  It tasted exactly like an apple dumpling!  I'm still dreaming about it because it was so yummy!  We had great service and fantastic food!  This is definitely our new favorite Mexican restaurant.  If you haven't tried this place, I highly recommend it!

Third times a charm!  We had come to eat here twice before, but the wait was too long.  We decided to try again today and it was not crowded at all so we got right in.
