Great for one stop shopping!  Hubby stopped here today on his way home to buy corn,  six ears, 43 cents each.  Styers is 20 cents each, if you pick your own.

You spin my head right round, right round, when you go down, when you go downtown. Yes, I did change the lyrics. How does one justify America's oldest Farmer's Market, the Reading Terminal Market, when writing a review... You don't. 

Your head literally does spin around when you enter for your first time. Once you know the market well and where your favorite purveyors are, I'm sure it's a walk through the park. I had to see it all. 

A portion of the market does have Amish vendors, but you will only find them here Wednesdays through Saturdays, even though the rest of the market is open seven days per week. 

There are over eighty vendors and covers over 1.7 acres. Two descendants of original shops are still there. This market has also been in numerous movies, including Trading Places. 

I walked into aromas of freshly baked chocolate chip cookies and convinced myself, it was too early plus it was only vendor one, even though ten minutes later I was eating some of the best and hot pepperoni pizza I have had. 

There are six bakeries, two of which I purchased baked goods from and one that I have reviewed so far. I was not thrilled with Le Bus http://www.yelp.com/biz/le-bus-bakery-philadelphia-2, but I was very happy with Termini Brothers Bakery, which I will review eventually. 

They have a nice wine shop and beer garden where I noticed a few drinking beer at ten in the morning, a tea shop, coffee, dairy shops and a juice bar, where you can get blended and frozen concoctions. 

A homemade ice cream parlor http://www.yelp.com/biz/bassetts-ice-cream-philadelphia, cheese shops, fresh flowers, organic produce and raw milk. One place that I really loved was Salumeria, what an awesome market filled with Italian groceries, hoagies, salads and international cheese. 

Local produce stands are huge and if you love variety this is your place. All locally grown and talk about a variety of mushrooms! Shops galore for cookbooks, used books, linens, pottery, crafts, handbags, a general store and Amy's Place filled with unique gifts, especially for a house warming gift or a new bride. 

There are a good dozen or more meat, poultry and seafood shops and some will cook it right there for you. I did notice that on each cash counter, they do have posted whether or not they accept credit cards and if they do the minimum amount to charge. 

Now I'm getting hungry, amazing pulled pork and beef brisket http://www.yelp.com/biz/tommy-dinics-philadelphia#hrid:kJ9LwByjlxBcrf_cNZyJUA/src:search/query:Tommy%20DeNic's, pizza, pasta to go or eat there, sandwiches, cheesesteaks http://www.yelp.com/biz/by-george-philadelphia, perogies or crab cakes at Coastal Cave, mac & cheese or fried chicken at Delilah's http://www.yelp.com/biz/delilahs-at-the-terminal-philadelphia-2 

You can sit down in one restaurant and have a wonderful breakfast, which gets packed, there is sushi, a spice shop http://www.yelp.com/biz/spice-terminal-philadelphia, a little Thai market and chocolates galore. 

Originally named the Jersey Market, since most farmers, fisherman and hunters were carrying their goods from the neighboring state to be sold here. After many complaints from the town folks of this non refrigerated outdoor market, it was dismantled and two new markets evolved from this, the Farmer's Market and the Franklin Market. 

This site has been in use as a Farmer's Market since 1860 on High Street, it soon was renamed Market Street and moved indoors in 1892, because of health risks, traffic nuisances and it needed to be controlled. The Reading Railroad built the Reading Terminal Market as part of their use for downtown passengers. 

The hustle and bustles, aromas and excitement fill the air and whenever I have out of town friends or family, who want to tour historic Philadelphia, I am bringing them here. 

The market is closed on certain holidays and they do not keep long evening hours. Parking at several local garages can be validated inside the Terminal and will reduce your $10.00 cost to $4.00, if you are there for two hours or less. 

Many places offer a seven dollar meal deal and have them well posted. From what I noticed they seemed like a good deal.  I am not sure what the story of Philbert is, I do know that he is a pig that was created by Eric Berg and he is surrounded by money. Anyway, he is pretty cool and located at the end of the central cafeteria style dining area. 

I do hope that I did the Terminal some kind of justice, it is too awesome for words! There are out door cafe tables for two & bongos playing outside..

So, as I am walking through the market, everyone was staring at me and I do mean everyone. Finally two police officers approach me and say "you can not wear that t-shirt in here"! As I am looking down to see what in the world I had put on that morning, my daughter said " Oh yes she can, six time Super Bowl champions"! The officers laughed and said, "yeah, I guess she can"!  What was I thinking?!

As an 11 year old boy, Dan Dizio sold soft pretzels on the curb and was dreaming of what it would be like to serve hot soft pretzels from his own bakery . At 11, he sold them 5 for $1.00 and took home $100.00 each day, after splitting the proceeds with his supplier. Today, they are still a bargain @ 4 for $1.00. Partner Len Lehman, who believed in Dan, has been rewarded by the storefront on Frankford grossing 1.7 million last year! 

Twenty five years later, from when he was 11 and with all the twists and turns, they are rolling in the dough and Dan did cut the mustard! 

Celebrating his 10TH year in business and franchising the Philly Pretzel Factory in 10 states, with 159 of them being in the Philadelphia & Delaware areas. 

Dan's dream was to bake pretzels all day and to sell them hot, as customers walked through his door. The pretzels are sold curb side all over, from Sesame Place to any part of Philly. 

The correct name is: Philly Pretzel Factory and it has won numerous awards, like "Best Pretzel of Philadelphia".   I do believe they are awesome and probably the best I have had. 

Dan loves to emphasize the fact these are "Real" pretzels. Their menu ranges from perfectly salted to unsalted and to minis and logs. They wrap pretzel dough around a hot dog and bake them off. Now this, I have to try!  They offer 10 different dipping sauces, but I'm a mustard kind of gal. 

Soft Philly pretzels have been coming out of Bakeries since 1920, but most of them have closed down. Dan created a lasting empire and added to the fame of one old and proud City, Philadelphia! 

Trivia: Did you know that Philly is also the creator of the Sticky Bun? But that's another review... .

Horrible Horrible wait time..... The Owners sisters' attitude was not professional to be in the food industry. Owner has special seating for his friend and family members.  And I guess city celebrities.
How can the manager have special seating in such a small place.
Well to make this a great restaurant the manager need to train his staff on how to approach customers with a cordial attitude. And the manager ( who is the owners sister) need to stop mean mugging people and rolling her eyes at customers . Instead of coming to make sure everything was ok or even tried to smooth things over. So then after waiting for 2 hours my food comes out cold .... how can you   Eat cold seafood.
My first experience here was good even though I had to wait. But this experience was the worst. I stopped the owner to let him know my food was cold and I was given another plate but  I was already disappointed with the unprofessional service I received from the Owners' sister.
That's why it's so easy to patronize other establishment and not support our own because when we do,this is the type of service we receive.

I have lived in Philly for over 5 years, and have been a frequent customer of PYT - or at least USED to. I think less than a year ago they started taking a lot of things off of the menu which was really disappointing. I used to love the randomness of their menu. Their prices also went up, and I just felt like it wasn't worth it anymore. Service is a hit or miss, you might get someone who is kind of nice, or a someone with a complete holier -than- thou attitude. I will never forget a waitress I had who was THE WORST. She was visibly annoyed when we inquired about our burger that was taking an hour to arrive, and when it was delivered, cold and soggy she looked disgusted that we would send it back and stormed off with her punk rock jorts and fanny pack. WIth that being said - sit at the bar, they are always pretty nice and quick with service. 

I go back from time to time. I would recommend joining burger of the month club-just to gawk at their interesting burgers each week and to muster up some inspiration to deal with the waitstaff and give it a try.

I wish my avatar could be a photo of my arse. You would know that I am no stranger to sweets; however, I do not love ALL baked goods, just a few. 

Here's what is non-paralleled at McMillan's. 

1. Creme donuts. Never had CREAM donuts there (the custard type), but when I brought these donuts into my school in Philadelphia, I saw students taking Patco into my town to get more. They are THAT good. I once had an argument with someone over who had the best donuts (they were a lawyer who is never wrong) and brought them to one of his infamous dinner parties. He never argued with me again. They are truly THAT humbling. Even more so about 5 years ago before flour/sugar prices caused cutbacks. One donut could feed your craving for DAYS.

2. The petite fours. I read someone say they were nothing special. Are they on CRACK? These are melt in your mouth fondant perfection. I used to ask for these for my birthday present from my parents they are so good. Do you think they could get away with charging nearly $20 a lb for something that wasn't absolute nirvana? I promise. The $1 you'll pay for ONE (unless you're lucky enough to stumble into a sample day) is the best $1 you'll spend. Great for kids. The perfect size and not so much sugar they'll get crazy on ya.

3. The sticky buns. Especially the mini ones, which is odd, because I like the center of them the best. They are like caramel on cinnamon dough. And not overcooked dough, either. The moistest, gooeiest thing you can imagine. I am PA Dutch, so I am no stranger to sticky buns. My grandfather used to make them with me at 3 am with half a load on from his Manhattans, so I know my buns (see opening line).

4. The apple fritters. While I love fried dough, I hate pie. Despise *almost* all of it actually (see #4). This is due to the fact that I once binged on raw pie dough (I am PA Dutch, after all). Anyway, these are not made with pie dough. This is some other supernatural dough, filled with still slightly crisp apples and DEEP FRIED and covered with glaze. It's like what the OLD apple pies cooked in lard from McDs would taste like if you were on acid. Even if you don't like pie, you need to try these.

5. Speaking of pies, have ever had or heard of a Chess pie? Me neither. Now, white cake is my favorite baked good, so I love birthdays. The problem is, everyone gets crappy birthday cake, so I have to wait for MY birthday to get a good one. So what does this have to do with pie? I'll tell you. Ever since having a Lemon Chess pie from McMillan's, I no longer even GET a birthday cake. I get birthday pie. And I hate pie. Chess pie is like a light, airy custard pie with a crunchy crust. Imagine Lemon Meringue were to make sweet love with Creme Brulee.. Yes, it's that good.

6. Butter cake. This too is one of those things you'd have to try before you'd ever think to order it. This tastes like the dough of a danish, made into the consistency of a cheesecake, and again, with a crispy, sugary crust. It's like a crunchy cheesecake, without the cream cheese flavor. Just buttery. It's like eating a cake batter danish in cheesecake form. Yeah, I'm not helping here, so I'll move on. Try it.

7. The non-pareil cookies. Usually they have these out to sample. If not, ask for one. I don't know what reviewer said they were mediocre, but they never had these. Buttery, sugary, crispy goodness. And the shaped sugar cookies, while horrifically overpriced, are still the best bought sugar cookies I've ever had. 

8. The raisin tea biscuits. I once cried in line (I was 8 months pregnant and had a craving, so cut me some slack) when the gigantor woman in front of me took the last 10 of them and wouldn't spare me ONE.  These are incredibly hard to describe. They are like a cross between a biscuit and raisin scone, but lightly glazed with egg.  These are actually what I get 9/10 I go to McMillan's because they are not too sweet and I don't feel like I'm doubling my waist size (although I do load them with butter). If it's your first time, ask for a tall one (they don't stay as moist in the middle if the top part has slid during baking). These are great to take to people's houses when you are traveling (as are the sticky buns) as they have the longest shelf lives.

Worth mentioning is the fact that McMillan's will make you ANYTHING you want, ANY WAY you want it, ANY TIME you need it with some advance ordering. And best of all, in any quantity? Want to try that lemon chess pie? Give them a call, they make you one any time you want. You don't even have to order more than 1 of anything. THAT is customer service.  The prices are HIGH for a bakery in my opinion, but well worth it, as I would pay anything to keep  this iconic bakery open as long as I live in Collingswood.

Also, the cupcakes are pretty decent, and so are the brownies and cheesecakes(pies), but if you can only choose a few things, stick with the above.

I was standing across the street from the Greenhouse and noticed this amazing two story glass building that was lit up with blue neon which caught my eye. Directly to the right was a hip outdoor bar that was packed with lots of people having a good time. My friends and I decided to give it a try not knowing what to expect. 
I'm so happy I did. When I walked inside I saw a few high tops all around the perimeter of the bar some even next to the glass windows that went floor to ceiling and all the way up to the second floor. 
In the front by the main entrance outside were a few tables to relax and have drinks. The vibe was very cool.
My friends and I sat on the far end at the bar Inside. I had a great view of my surroundings with all the glass windows looking out to South Main Street. There was an upper level that had a few pool tables. On the main floor near the stairs was a three piece band named BLIND LEMON PIE. These guys were really good. They played Eric Clapton, CCR, and many other rock n roll songs that everyone seemed to know. Me being a band person and knowing hundreds and hundreds of musicians, I was surprised  I never heard of this trio. They sounded like a 5 piece band. They were really solid. It definitely became a singalong. The crowd was a good mix of all ages just having a good time. 
The bartenders were very friendly and very attentive and they knew how to make a proper drink and pour a beer correctly.  
We decided to order some appetizers because we already had dinner hours ago, and saw lots of great looking food being served.. 
My friend wanted to try the SPICY CALAMARI. Across the bar I saw a women eating homemade loaded French fries that looked really good.
 I decided to order the "DUDE DON'T TOUCH MY FRIES" Served with your choice of toppings. Bacon jam and gorgonzola cheese, or shaved parmesan with fresh thyme and truffle oil. I chose the latter one. The fries were fresh and very tasty the truffle oil along with the parmesan cheese was the bomb. I must admit, I wasn't expecting much with the Spicy Calamari, because most restaurants don't know how to properly cook it, or they cut corners and buy it cut up and already frozen. 
The Spicy Fried Calamari was delicious. My friend who is a professional chef, and myself both remarked how tender the calamari was. Usually, when you order it in a bar it's rubbery and overcooked, not this time! 
A nice gentleman by the name of Wilfer who I later learned was the new owner and his wife Sarah and partner Mike couldn't have been nicer. Wilfer came over to us and explained he only buys and uses fresh calamari not frozen like so many other restaurants do. We both remarked that we could tell because it was so tender, and the presentation was lovely. The Spicy Calamari had  cherry peppers tossed with spring onions, diced tomatoes, and fried capers. It was served with a garlic aioli drizzled ontop. I couldn't stop eating it. I happen to love cherry peppers, it was a nice twist and the garlic aioli , tomatoes and capers really made the dish come alive!
Their menu is small but through. They serve gluten free and vegetarian dishes. 
When I'm in New Hope I will definitely be returning here and I will be trying some of their other dishes. Their burgers looked so good. 
If in New Hope , you must stop in a give this place a try.

Food is fairly good but I'm not a fan of this place. Will not be going back.

After three visits I be noticed an ongoing trend. The wait staff is always rude and the place is in general chaos. Again, decent food but horrible management.

These people need to learn they are in the hospitality business - not just the meatball business.

A little French wanna-be in the middle of nowhere Boise Idaho! I was there for a business trip and stumbled upon this little restaurant. I was intrigued with all the 5 stars on Yelp. I had to try it. 
I started with the escargot. It was on the chewier side and darker in color than I expected. The size was definitely much larger than the ones in France...possibly a completely different breed. The flavor was butter butter and extra butter. Perhaps they tried to cover up the less than superior quality of the escargot with extra butter and garlic. The next course was the restaurant's self claimed "Famous French Onion Soup". I'm not sure who proclaimed that title but it didn't live up to it. It was over-baked. The cheese was burnt and inedible after the first bite. The bread was soggy with no texture. The broth was watery with no flavor depth. It was almost as though they opened up a can of Campbell's Beef Broth and poured it over torn up Wonder Bread and topped it off Velveeta Cheese and threw it under the broiler for 15 minutes. Voila...French Onion Soup! 
The next course was Garlic Shrimp. It lived up its name...shrimp and garlic! Nothing to rave about other than don't order that on a date unless you're avoiding that good night kiss. The final course was Creme Brûlée. It was as expected...creamy, sweet and a little burnt. They could have torched the sugar more to allow for my spoon to crack the top shell. Instead my spoon just sunk in without the initial thrill of the crack. 
The wine selection was subpar. They take pride in taking you to their "wine library" to show you their collection. It was no different than waking down Safeway's wine aisle. There was nothing spectacular. Just overpriced usual suspects. I opted for a glass of their "French"
Chardonnay. When I saw the label, I laughed because I saw the same label at a gas station called Tom's Thumb in Scottsdale, Arizona (not France). I think it was selling for $14.99. 
Overpriced and mediocre food.

I'm really not sure how I haven't written a review for red Mesa Mercado before! I am a red Mesa super fan thru and thru. Out of the three (restaurant, cantina, Mercado) I go here the most! I love the casual atmosphere and it's great for a quick eat before any downtown activities. 

I've had pretty much everything vegetarian/pescatarian on the menu and you can't go wrong. Shrimp tacos? Delicious. Veggie burrito bowl? say no more. And the sangria... consider this my love letter to all red Mesa sangria. I love you. I cannot live without you!!

They seem to be taking all safety precautions, with "no mask no burrito" signs everywhere. Signs in the bathroom that they sanitize every hour. All employees wearing masks and gloves. Spaced out tables. I felt very safe eating there!

Wow. Wowwwwwww. WOWWWWWWW..

I don't like breakfast food. I hate eggs (not the restaurant, the food, calm down). I am a coffee snob (the first step is admitting it).... EGG CHANGES ALL OF THIS (not the coffee part, still true but their coffee is )

Get on their waitlist before you go because they are on a huge wait. The wait is for a reason! The food is SO good! 

I can't wait to go back but my first trip I ordered:

Coffee (if you like coffee, you'll love theirs)

Mexican Slinger - I did the veggie option and was so happy that I did! These are like huevos rancheros but taking the level up 15 notches on flavor!

French Toast - all of the flavors between the toast and the berry compote were perfect! You can get a half order, I thought of this as my dessert! 

Expect for the service to be a little slow, they're a busy restaurant that is trying to make due during a pandemic... but go with this understanding and place your order fast and order 2 drinks so you don't have to be THAT person!

EGG was awesome!! Go ASAP!!!

So here's what I think about Wok-Inn Noodle...  Believe the reviews that rave about the excellent food.  Ignore the reviews that are critical about the decor, the setting, slow service, the smell, or any of the random things strewn about the restaurant.  Why do we go out to eat?  Bottom line...  To eat.  And whenever possible, to eat good food!  Sometimes, we get to eat excellent food.  On rare occasions, we get to eat excellent food in a nice setting with all the trimmings.

In the case of Wok-Inn Noodle, you get to eat excellent food!  And for me, I don't mind the setting, I actually like the decor, and I fully appreciate the slow service.  The quality of the food outweighs any of the detractors you might have.

For our last dinner, we started off with Egg Rolls.  They were excellent, and tasted really, really yummy.  I ordered Fried Rice with all the meats (beef, pork, chicken, and shrimp).  All of the meats were cooked perfectly, especially the shrimp.  They were so tender and flavorful.  My wife ordered the House Noodle, which she loved as well.

I had the opportunity to meet the owner and chef of the establishment after normal business hours.  I had accidentally left something in the restaurant at our last visit, and I called to make arrangements to pick it up.  He is a warm and friendly gentleman, and greeted me with a smile.  I appreciate him taking the time to meet with me over my mistake.  Just as important, I appreciate him taking the time to cook the lovely meals for us!  Don't miss out on this little jewel of a dive-joint!

==========

Irony.  It is the opposite of wrinkly.

Fantastic Clam Chowder. It's all I stopped in for on the drive up to Big Sur. They serve it up with some complimentary sourdough bread. It's loaded with clams! (The chowder, not the bread).

Place was pretty busy on a early Friday afternoon. It's located on a mini wharf by the Marina.

Don't wait for a table. The bar is first-come-first-serve. The guys working the bar are really friendly. You'll be able to watch them prepare cioppinos and such. Nice views out the windows from here also. 

Parking: $4 outdoor private lot. Spots are not bad, but you'll have to drive a ways down in order to find a secluded space. May not have that option on a busy weekend I'd assume.

I would love to actually be able to review the food and drinks here, but sadly I can't even do that, because I was essentially turned away at the door.  

A few weeks ago, this nifty discount website I belong to (RueLaLa) had a special for XIX:  $25 for $50 worth of food.  Sweet!  My boyfriend and I were super excited about the chance to go, so we saved the voucher for a night when we had some time free, and meandered over there.   

When we walked in, the restaurant was essentially empty, except for a few staff standing around and watching "The Bachelor" (classy).  The host took us to our table (after informing us we couldn't sit at the famous bar because it was closed for renovations).  When we arrived at the table, I whipped out my  printed-out voucher and told the host we were planning to use the voucher for a few drinks and a couple of appetizers.  He said, "oh... you can't use that for drinks and appetizers.  You can only use that for a meal."  I was rather shocked, but I looked at the voucher again and NOWHERE did it say that I could only use it for an actual meal.  Not in the general description, not in the fine print -- nowhere.  

When I confronted him about this, he said, "Oh... you can tell from the hours they put on the voucher."  To which I replied, "what... you mean all the hours for the restaurant?"  What I'd wish I'd said was, "If you didn't want to honor this voucher, you shouldn't have signed up for it."

Since we basically felt like second-hand citizens, we left. Needless to say, I'm going to get my money back, and I'm never going back there, EVER.

When researching things to do in Reno for my trip I kept seeing this buffet advertised as "the best in Reno." So I had high hopes once we went to eat hear. Would't say I was completely disappointed, but definitely feel they should stop pushing the "best in Reno" angle. Our waiter was very friendly, attentive, and they sang happy birthday to me. I would give them 5 stars. The food was... OK. Decent selection, didn't have anything horrible. 

I read somewhere in a review they did a rain shower every so often like a Rain Forest Cafe. Full disclosure: I am sucker for themed restaurants so yes I will eat horrible food just for the experience (we all have our secret shame). Much like water to a desert, it did not come. If my fellow Yelper was lying, curse you. If "Island Buffet" stopped doing it, curses to you!

I was so happy when I went to OpenTable and was able to grab the last 9pm reservation for 4 this past Friday! I love Ulele and hadn't been in about 5 years. As soon as they opened back then, we moved...but we are back!!!!

Okay, so I ordered the Gouda Grouper and my BF ordered Shrimp and Grits. His brother ordered the Snapper and his wife ordered the Gouda Grouper too. 

Before rating the food, let me say...shouts out to Amy! Our server was bomb. Her customer service was on point and she knew the menu well. She had this energy and vibe about her that was refreshing and you could seriously see her smiling through her mask. Amy was great and she made our experience even better...

Gouda Grouper: I will have to order this dish the next 5 times I go and hope that helps my fix because I'm hooked! This plate was so good. In my opinion, the best on the menu. It came with rice but Amy, our sever, suggested to sub for mashed potatoes...so we listened. It was soo good with the sauce. Thinking about it right now is making my mouth water. It was not heavy but perfectly fulfilling and went fabulous with my 2 glasses of bubbly. 

Shrimp and Grits: The BF really liked this and shocked me when he said he loved the grit cakes more than the shrimp! He said the shrimp were definitely Gulf shrimp and satisfying but that grit cake was so unique and nothing like your normal grits.  

Snapper: So I don't have a photo of this dish, but let me just say...before my BF could ask him how was his food, it was gone. The plate was CLEARED...not a piece of evidence left. 

Oh! And I forgot to mention, I ordered the Key Lime to go and it did NOT disappoint. Can't wait to go back to Ulele in the prime River Walk area.

Didn't make a reservation for the late night show on a Saturday night but we snagged a couple seats at the bar (first come, first served). 
Bartenders were fabulous and drag queens were oh-so-very-entertaining. We had a blast!
Such lively groups of people and great music. Table and booth seating available.
Make a reservation or show up 30 minutes before the show and hope to grab a seat at the bar.
Bring your bills to snag pictures with the queens as they walk around!
We snacked on some fries while we enjoyed the delicious drinks the bartender made for us. The fries were great and the drinks were perfection.

Atmosphere is nice but BUYER BEWARE!!! The owner will scam you and bait you into buying a $45 glass without disclosure! This place won't last long at this rate in Tampa! NEVER going back.
****And in reposonse to the owner Joshua's comment below, thank you for confirming what we already believed. You are unprofessional and unscrupulous. I can assure you that I DID NOT suggest I wanted the best French champagne, I have visited Epernay, France and I am well aware of the cost of "the best". I believe my words were "brut and/or cuvee" and if memory serves me, I said I was looking at the 375ml half bottle of vueve cliquot for $43 or the $60 piper-heidsieck which you said you were out of. Instead, you suggested another option, which I acknowledge I had never heard of or tried, and I only learned that it was $45 per glass when the $180 bill arrived.  Upselling is one thing, but that wasn't even in the ballpark of what I was looking at and you know this. Further, this is not the first I've heard of this happening with you. You have established this reputation of "upselling" on your own in Tampa. You, my friend, are not Berns, where I'd expect to spend a little more, but where this type of misleading tactic would not exist. Trust in a business owner is huge and vital to success. I have sent this link to ALL of my Tampa Facebook friends as a warning and in the hopes they too will feel the "warmth" of your invite to never dine there. And, I will just choose to continue to enjoy my other options like Cru. Thank you.

Family owned and quality controlled... This is a treasure hidden in the midst of a busy strip mall.
Toby's Little Italy is located within a narrow slice of this commercial center. It's a friendly place with a happy attitude. When you walk in the door, your presented with the menu board hanging over the order counter. Whether by the slice or by the jumbo pie, Toby's is a bee hive of activity with sauce and cheese, garlic knots, salads and sandwiches. 

Dining in-  a narrow row of booths fills one wall. Passing by the outgoing pizzas and orders requires grace and timing. The row of booths seems to go on forever... or at least into a back room.  

Parking -- there's plenty. 

To go orders - not a problem, but you might end up waiting outside until your number is called. 

the food:  isn't that why we are all here?  Believe me, there are a lot of people here. In this case - it is a positive indicator of the quality. Toby's packs them in -- almost everyday of the week brings hungry humans ready for delicious pizza.  
The garlic knots come with a generous coating of real garlicky goodness (smothered or on the side) as well as an amazing marinara for dipping.  

This was an easy review to write... hands down, Toby's get a big high five.

The Smokehouse is an ideal destination for BBQ in Dunedin. Located in the heart of downtown the menu contains everything you'd expect to find from a respectable smokehouse. From brisket to ribs and pulled pork, they smoke it cut it and serve it up. 

Our large group pulled up on the large outdoor patio, tucked the napkins, ordered a round of pints (the craft beer menu has an extensive list of local and national beer) and placed orders on a Saturday night. The food was delivered quick and everyone enjoyed. 
The Killer Fry Melt app comes huge --plenty to share and enjoy. 

I love sauces. The Smokehouse provides three or four bottles on the table - sampling all of them is a must! 
All in all the food was good. But, sadly it wasn't over the top. The (Mac and) cheese was broken ( I think that constitutes a crime in the South). The brussel sprouts we're lack luster. 
I'll return - it's definitely a decent downtown option.

Amazing !! This is run by the same guy that owns Classic Red Hots. This place is a hundred times better. It's so big inside , and so beautiful and nicely decorated. The owner was friendly and welcoming as always. The waitress there is super nice. She took really great care of us. 

Now the food , it was incredible !! We had falafel, hummus, baba ghanouj, fattoush, mansaf, and veggie sambosik. My husband loved the lamb mansaf ... The meat was falling off the bone , he loved it. The fattoush was awesome , I've always loved his fattoush. Falafel was really good , my husband doesn't generally like falafel but he loved this one. Hummus is great and home made. Now , my favorite thing was the veggie sambosik .... OMG. I can't even describe how great it was , it was so amazing. I will come back no matter what cause this place was great. But I will ESPECIALLY be back for those sambosik. Will be back multiple times !!!

Awesome restaurant! I finally made it here, on a weekend night. Understandably, the only reservations they had open were at 10pm, but we came early (really early, like 5pm) and got an unreserved outside table. 

The atmosphere is amazing. I love the country home meets art deco feel. The huge fish sculpture is something I want in the 5,000 square foot log cabin (off the grid of course) I plan to have one day. The service, great - from our server, to the hostess girls, everyone was very friendly and accomodating. I also liked the exposed ceilings and the open kitchen. Such great design.

Food-wise I would say it was good. I wasn't blown away by everything, but it was certainly interesting. Charred oysters were tasty, but crab mac wasn't my style and kind of disappointing. The deconstructed seafood pot pie? Amazing! It was fun to guess what type of seafood was in my mouth. Boyfriend enjoyed the grouper as well. The honey beer was delicious. I would have liked to try the wedding beer but they were out. Wish they had mentioned that up front. Next time I'll do a craft cocktail.

...I'll also bring my dog! The outside tables are dog-friendly and I know she would love to come after an afternoon sniffing and doing her business in the park. 

Go here!

Finally made it here and was not that impressed with the burgers. The overall taste and seasoning was so-so. Personally they should not to press the hamburger patty so much and let it be a little fluffier and not so condensed and hard.  Reminds me of a preformed burger from Costco. I got the Funk Zone burger and the bacon was soggy and undercooked, I asked for the egg to be runny and it was cooked solid through. Asked for the burger rare and came out well done as well as the barbecue sauce on the side but came with it smothered on the top and bottom of the burger. They did make me another one but had the same problems. Not sure how a burger place does not know how to cook a burger to temperature. The fries were tasty hot and crispy between that and the attentive service is the only saving grace to give them two stars.

While visiting on business I experienced slow service, mediocre food, and rude staff.  The price of the meal did not reflect the quality.  The taste wasn't there, some items were overcooked, and the staff seemed less than invested.  Morton's may want to consider revamping this whole operation. Retraining and fresh blood could really benefit this location that is not up to the usual Morton's standard, pricing should really be brought inline with comparable places. Until then - stay away, much better choices nearby that care about your business.

I can't tell you how many times we've come here to celebrate something fun (a new guest in town, a promotion, birthdays, or just a simple Friday night out with friends). Although the restaurant is situated in what appears to be a standard commercial space (strip mall, even) - the atmosphere as you enter the front doors is modern, fun, and inviting (with wall planters and colorful art hanging on the walls). 

The service has continually been on point. Within minutes of sitting down- it's likely we have our drink orders in, a delicious small bread loaf placed on the table, and the server has provided recommendations or menu highlights. 

Although I recognize the wonderful assortment of diverse menu items, I tend to consistently order the same pasta dish each and every time (and explore other flavors by eating off my friend's plates)! The pasta dish I can't seem to get enough of is the Lemon Strozzapreti (with cream, cauliflower, and pistachio). My boyfriend loves the pizzas - and so we commonly order the two dishes- enjoy a cocktail before dinner- and then a glass of wine to pair with the meal. 

Definitely a favorite in my STL foodie black book!

i'm not in the habit of giving poor reviews unless it's to bash some douchebag spot, in which case i'm only all too eager.

however, based upon my one visit to dmitri's last night, i'd have to say that i'm not sure i went to the same restaurant as all these other people.

too add insult to injury, my original plan was to go back to pif night at ansill which is pretty much as sure a thing as there is in this town.

i figured seafood would be a little bit lighter after the weeks gorging and i love greek food so i thought i'd try dmitri's
(i had one good meal and one laughably bad meal of crap rotisserie chicken at estia where my dad and i got the pre theater dinner before going to the kimmel center)

got the grilled octopus which was chopped into slices and precooked before getting a hit of the grill. the octopus was not fresh and this dish tasted like charred rubber bands with olive oil and lemon.

a few years ago i spent three weeks in athens and  paros with greek friends and we'd eat grilled octopus and salad every day. now i'm not so stupid to think i'd be getting anything like that, but this dish was such a bummer. (to counterpoint: the stuffed squid dish at estia was really delicious).

almost got the pasta with blue fish. 
my question: what is "bluefish"? 
answer: "its more of a fish eaters fish"
what the hell does that mean?

instead, i got the cioppino. which essentially tasted like some clams, mussels, shrimp, and a  hunk of cod overcooked in a pot of boiling water with a handful of chopped tomatos, bell peppers and onions thrown in. dreadfully overcooked not fresh seafood with nearly no flavor. what a bummer.
another counterpoint: the cioppino at mercado (for only 4 dollars more) is delicious although you might ask for the capers and olives on the side as it can get pretty salty.

also, i'm not interested in getting people in trouble but the service left a little to be desired and i had to ask for my 2/3rds full bottle of wine to be returned after it had already been stashed in the back.  there were a few other things but i'll just keep it to the food.

sigh.... i could have eaten at ansill.... :(
and little fish was just down the street too.... :(

Ishkabibble's is one of my favorite places to get a cheesesteak. It ranks in my top 3 cheesesteak places to go to in Philly! They have two locations, but I've only gone to this one. It is a very small place with a counter in front of the grill that fits about five people and a small ledge/counter that fits three people comfortably. The service is great - the staff is very friendly and they will offer you water if you eat in. I once called an order in for ten cheesesteaks and three orders of fries the night before and they had everything ready to go for me when I arrived at our agreed time. 

The food is delicious! This time I tried their cheesesteak with provolone and peppers. It had a really good mix of melted cheese (as you can see in the picture) and the taste of the meat is much better than your typical cheesesteak - it tastes like real meat! Their fries are also perfectly crispy... I suggest getting them! 

They also accept credit cards for purchases over $10!

This place isn't on top of most people's lists when looking for a place to get a Philly cheesesteak, but I highly recommend adding Ishkabibble's to your list.

Initially, I was thinking 2 stars, but after my drive home, I decided that 2 stars was much too generous for this place. So 1 star for you. Let me explain...

First off, Ive never been here before. I've heard of Carolina Blue, but never really been interested in going out of my way to try a bbq place in Pitman, let alone one that costs a small fortune to eat at. Think about it -  I have Philadelphia in my back yard, why the hell would I risk a lousy meal at some wannabe place in South Jersey? So when the opportunity arose to meet some friends there after work, I decided to pull the trigger and give this place a shot.

When I got there, I made sure to check yelp and see what others were saying before I even walked in. The 3.5 star average was troubling, but there were a couple emphatic reviews, including one raving about smoked wings. And you know how I do wings.

When I met with my party, we all ordered different things, in an effort to try as much of the menu as possible. I went for the smoked sampler, priced at an unfathomable $22.  For mine, I selected the pulled pork, bistro filet, and smoked wings. Great, right?

WRONG. The wings were absolutely terrible. Im not even sure they are really smoked. Ive never had anything smoked that was still tough. That wasnt the worst part though, the wings were bland as hell, all I could taste was lighter fluid or something. I had others at the table try them too, and they all agreed the wings were God awul. Nothing to dip them in either. I was actually considering sprinking some sweet-n-low on them, I mean, you couldnt make them any worse, so why not?  I ditched the last 2 and dug into the "bistro filet" - a fancy name for a cheap cut of steak. This too was barely smoked, and oh-so-bland. It actually tasted like a hot dog (but not a Nathan's). I couldnt eat more than 2 little slices without laughing. Again, I had others try some as well, and again, all agreed it was pathetic. So I ditched the last 3 pieces.

So then there was pork. This should be your core competency as a BBQ restaurant. If you cant nail this, you shouldnt even be allowed open. The plate came with a little mound of pulled pork and 3 little toasted bread points (crostinis?). What the hell is this? Thankully, the pork was the least of the letdowns on the plate. Its not that it was good, it just wasnt as bad. Overall, still a huge disappointment.

I also got to try other things at the table, including the pork belly "special" and mussels. Im not sure how the mussels made it on  the menu, but they were actually decent. We asked for some bread to soak up the juice, and the waiter brought us a nice warm loaf. The problem was, it was far from fresh baked - it smelled like a dank basement, OR, like it was just thawed in the microwave. The pork belly was exactly what it sounds like - a giant hunk of pork fat with a sliver of meat at the bottom. It also tasted exactly llike it sounds. 

When the checks FINALLY came, reality set in, and suddenly $34 for sub-par food for one person, wasnt such a 2 star experience. Mind you, I had 3 domestic drafts, but still... for $20 I can gorge myself on fantastic BBQ at Sweet Lucys.

Its a nice looking establishment and all, but lets face it, people pay for food and service. This place is seriously deficient in both.

Very happy about this new location. It's much easier for me to get my El Gato fix, French Quarter location is a commitment, and Lakeview is too far from uptown for Mexican. I was so excited about this when I learned it was opening in the warehouse district. All my favorites are here including the carrot margarita. You have to try it, it sounds strange, but it's unbelievably delicious! I usually get tacos or chicken enchiladas, I tried the Acapulco salad with chicken and it was fresh and great. The tomatoes were a little underripe, but I'm pretty picky about a good tomato. I find this often in restaurants, I can't understand why they serve hard tomatoes. Other than that everything was as expected and excellent!! I will be back many times.

They were wonderful when they were on Harrison Ave. I placed and order a couple of weeks ago. I called in an order the woman on the other line not friendly at all! The food had no seasoning at all and came cold...hope they did not lose a great chef. This city is is very competitive  and restaurants go down quick if they are not on their A Game every night.

Wowza...my first time at Bricks and what a fantastic experience. Our server was Emily and she was so awesome! We ordered a bottle of Prosecco as it was my birthday celebration, loved it!
For starters we ordered the crab cakes that were absolutely delish...but the main attraction was the escargot that is served in mushroom caps and also blue cheese added, complete party in your mouth! Highly recommend! Can't wait to have again! Our soup was creamy 5 onion and it was so creamy and delicious!
I ordered the Wagyu New York (bone in) I have to say it was a new favorite steak of mine...juicy and flavorful. It came with broccoli and roasted potatoes served to perfection!
My BFF had the rack of lamb, she went on how wonderful it was (I'm not a lamb fan) her dish was also served with garlic mashed potatoes and broccoli.
Dessert was a wonderful and creamy Creme Brûlée to die for. Took a spoon knocked on the top to crack and that's all I have to say, other than that was my favorite dessert ever! 
I highly recommend Bricks...prices were not expensive for a wonderful 5 star restaurant.
Oh and we had such a fun bus man, his name is Luis and he ended our meal with his kind and absolute Witty self!

I had a long lunch break during my class at the Armory and I thought to myself - Self, I should take you to lunch.  Do you fancy Thai?  And my self said OMG I love Thai.  Let's go!  So I took myself on a solo date to Ginger Thai.

Luckily the place was not very busy so I could get seated fast and order.  I started with the Tom Yum Goong soup.  It was hot, spicy, and extremely tasty on a cold snowy day.  For my entree I chose Pad Kro Pow with chicken, medium spice.  It was just enough spice, with really fresh peppers and perfectly cooked chicken.  Served with rice, of course.  I liked it equally as much as my usual Thai place.  There's just something about hot, spicy Thai food.  I could eat it on the daily.  If only this place were a bit closer and less of a pain in the ass to get to from my condo, I'd put it in the regular rotation immediately.

The waitress didn't bat an eye that I was alone and made sure everything came out quickly, including the check, but didn't rush me when I sat and read my ipad for a while.  Plus I got to eavesdrop on the two gentlemen sitting beside me which was fun in and of itself.

Ambiance was nice, sleek, modern, although the location in a strip mall didn't hint at this type of ambiance.  It is off the main road so use that GPS and get yourself over to Ginger Thai.  I know I will be back again and again!

Mmmmm Thai food!  It's my fave, so when I saw that a new place was opening up then I knew I'd have to go as soon as possible.

First off, the location is a little odd, kind of set apart all by itself.  But don't be fooled, go on in, you won't be sorry.  They have ample parking around the building too so that's a plus.  

They have renovated this place and it looks sleek and modern.  There's a bar to the right when you walk in, and the rest of the room is tables.  There also appears to be a patio but it hasn't really been set up yet.

Both times I have gone I had the same server and she's a sweetheart.  She discussed the drink menu with us, the food menu, suggested things, chatted, etc.  I've two different entrees here: basil chicken and the garlic vegetables with chicken.  Both with spice level of HOT.  Once with regular rice, once with sticky rice based on the suggestion of the waitress.  This is LEGIT delicious yo!  Both times I ate every last bite. Heat level was as asked, not less as sometimes happens. The sticky rice was interesting to me but I also liked that.  I also enjoy their beverage menu as they have come up with some Thai inspired cocktails.  Think lychee and lemongrass and ginger beer and whatnot.  I know I love cocktails anywhere, but I loved them here too!

If you are doing a Thai tour of Nashville then you MUST come here and support these lovely folks.  They are cooking up great Thai food in a swank atmosphere with friendly staff.

A must stop on your Lower Broadway barhop.  Since there are tons of reviews about this place, here's my brief thoughts.

Free admission.

Decently strong drinks.

Cowboy boots on the wall, perhaps for sale?  I couldn't tell.

Always a good band, usually with a upright bass which is, of course, festive.  Tip the band - no admission so go ahead and give them some bucks so they can pay rent or buy some beer.

Totally packed out on the weekends but on weeknights much more manageable.  Plus if you are a tourist you don't have anything to do the next day right?  Drink up!

That's all you have to know.  Then you can stumble out and hit up another honky tonk.

I was excited to hear that Deb Paquette from Etch fame had opened a restaurant in my 'hood (and thank you for whatever happened that made it end up over here rather than in Sylvan Park) so I finally picked a night and made a reservation. I was not disappointed!

Etc. is like Etch's slightly less posh sister - it has a more neighborhood, friendly feel while still keeping a modern and swank atmosphere and high quality food. The dining area and bar were both packed when we got there for our reservation, but we were seated almost immediately so it worked out fine. We were seated right by the door, but the cool thing is that there's a wall there that blocks you from people walking in and out of the door, so you don't get a draft or people bumping you with their butts. 

So our waiter, Ernesto (I think?), got us our bottle of wine and told us about the menu. He was most helpful and even ended up guiding us to get the soup of the day which was maybe the best idea ever.

We started with the scallop crudo with watercress tempura and watermelon radish. I mean, this was an awesome appetizer. The scallop was cooked sous vide and was kind of like raw but cooked at the same time as far as texture. It was sublime. And watercress tempura was crunchy and unique and damn, this appetizer is awesome and you must have it.

Next we had to get the soup of the day. It was a bisque made with coconut milk instead of cream and it had cumin and other spices and also a samosa in it and tomatillo sauce on top of it. I don't remember the name, but Ernesto suggested it and said the sous chef is Peruvian (? maybe) and concocted this. So we shared this soup and he even brought it in two separate bowls. GET THIS IF THEY HAVE IT. Just trust me. I am putting it on the level of the two other best soups I have ever had in my life...(turtle soup at Restaurant August and the garlic soup at Bayona, both in NOLA)...and it deserves the praise. We both ate every last spoonful. God it was awesome. It gets 5 stars alone.

We also shared the roasted beet salad with goat cheese and bacon. I am just now finding out that I DO like beets (just not those nasty pickled beets that were around when I was a kid) so I like to try them when available. Add some bacon in there and some cheese...it was an awesome salad.

Basically at this point we should have been done with ordering because that's a hell of a lot of food to eat at one sitting but noooooooo! We went ahead and got entrees because OINK OINK. I got the fowl trio and the BF got seared tuna. So the fowl trio: cinnamon sesame duck breast, chicken confit with a chili sauce, and the date fois gras brûlée with grasshopper crumble along with masa grits. Each one was delicious in its own way and it is hard to pick a favorite one. And, honestly, I had to try some grasshopper crumble. The boyfriend's seared tuna was also awesome, perfectly seared.

At this point we were FULLY STUFFED and couldn't even think about dessert although I am sure the waiter was amused at us even considering it. But maybe next time I will try one of those too!

Man, Green Hills needs more locally owned restaurants to visit instead of more of the same old chain restaurants. And Etc. is an awesome addition to the neighborhood. I look forward to going back again and again.

I went to 7 ounce a couple times now and I've landed on 1 star.

I do not recommended this business to family and friends.

During the times I've been here I ordered the Korean BBQ that you cook at the table yourself. It started out as a good deal with good food but in the short time they've been open the prices have increased and the quality has gone way down.

Most recently I discovered what were essentially rocks in the steamed egg that's served with some of the combos. I think it was chunks of the clay pot the egg is served in and I just about busted a tooth. Then after calling them on it I never received a replacement egg which is cool because I paid for it. The start of the shady business practices was in progress...

After the egg ordeal the server said my meal would be discounted which was a lie. The check came out at full price and when we mentioned it they started trying to get out of giving us the discount! Shady and dishonest, a real winning combo.

The original grill was faulty as well. After several false starts they agreed to let us switch tables. The server asked which table we would like and when we told him he immediately shut us down and sent us to a different table. Why even bother asking??? Then nobody helped us move the 12 plus plates from the old table to the new table. Great service (I'm lying, it was terrible).

In total with the faulty grill and everything else it took us over 2 hours to finish our meal. Ridiculous.

We were able to finally get the discount which was like $5 and less than 10% of our total cost. Had I known I would have just left right away.

Another minor issue was that my water had foreign objects floating in it which seems to be their signature move.

This is a hard STAY AWAY. I would advise you to go anywhere but here. Don't support shady businesses that treat their customers like garbage!

This is delicious vegetarian food for non-vegetarians and vegetarians alike, but the service is incredibly slow and disorganized. On the weekend, the lines get super long and they don't see equipped to handle it.

The buffalo cauliflower is incredible. I wish we had ordered twice as much (which we couldn't do because of the super long line). I had the spring roll bowl with cauliflower, avocado, cucumber, rice, spring mix, peanut sauce and I added tofu. It was all delicious. I also stole a bite of barbecue jackfruit which was in the smoker right next to me; it had the consistency of a mushroom and was so flavorful and delicious. I wish I had discovered this place earlier in my time in St Louis because it's delicious, fresh, and affordable - I just wish the service was slightly better, but I suppose it's part of the charm.

The staff here will probably greet  you  with "Ciao Bella" or "Come va mi amore"! 

Pia's Trattoria Brings a Piece of Italy to Gulfport born and raised in Italy, experienced chef and business owner Pia Goff decided to call Gulfport "home."

Trattoria is an Italian word, and means "eating house".

Very rustic Italian villa and wine cellar vibe for sure.

Pia's Trattoria restaurant also operates a bar, so a round of drinks with dinner is not out of the question.

Make a reservation just to be on the safe side to ensure your table is ready when you are. The dress code and ambience at Pia's Trattoria are totally laid-back. You can sophisticated and be dressy or you can be in flip flops and a tee-shirt and still at the same time enjoy a meal worthy of a five-star rating. 

Pia's Trattoria offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner and serves up endless healthy meal options. 

Plan to spend about $30 per person.

I highly recommend this location and the Homemade Lasagna with Seminole Pride Beef served in a Cast Iron Skillet is Yummilicious and Tastylicious

Why 5 stars

They are inexpensive, made to order with fresh ingredients, Seafood is fresh daily. You can have fish, chicken, shrimp or andouille sausage - cooked grilled, blackened or fried. These are served as a meal, salad or sandwich. Beans and rice and fries are a must. From the kitchen to your table smoking hot!! It's a tiny space, just a counter at the window with four stools and four small tables out front.

The bread is brought fresh daily from Giovanni's Bakery in Largo, FL. and while it's not the traditional French bread common to po' boys in New Orleans, it is a reasonable alternative. Besides, biting into one of their perfectly breaded and fried shrimp or oyster sandwiches puts one in a forgiving mood LOL. They also have developed a different batter for each fried item, and it shows. One of the business partner Anthony Jack was the one who prepared our food and the service was OUTSTANDING and the food was Superb!!!

Honestly I've been going to Ker's Wing House for years and have never had a bad experience. The staff is usually right on point and friendly when the boys and I go for wings and beer to catch a game or 3 (LOL). Great place to watch any sport pretty laid back atmosphere with lots of televisions - some locations also have pool tables.

I found the prices to be reasonable as well, as an enjoyable atmosphere, very casual place. The naked wings (get you mind out of the gutter - these are wings that are skinless (oops) I mean no breading) are my fave with fries are good also the grouper blackened sandwiches. Oh and if you can get the Margarita Wings (perfect combination of salty, sweet, and tart, these refreshing wings are available in original or buffalo styles.) Yummilicious!!!

To be honest I've driven by the spot a couple times but would never had guess it was a restaurant...I would have pegged it for more of a café (light breakfast, etc.). To my surprise this is a hidden gem in the Dunedin area (newly opened about 10 months by a local extremely talented Chef)

Owners Erin "Cricket" Plunkett, 26, and Jason Borajkiewicz, 34 have certainly captured the essence of Modern European cooking. The dishes are not really large but very fresh, delicious and well prepared. For a party of 2 you can drop about $75 -$100 - but believe me its quality over quantity. You can taste the love and attention to detail in each dish. The menu changes 2 to 3 times a week to allow for fresh and creative dishes. So the menu is short in my book is a good sign because that allows for everything to be fresh. And they have the flexibility to make frequent changes. We should all be mindful of the restaurants offering pages of dishes and what are we really receiving...hhhmmm how fresh, frozen, in microwavable portions are we paying for. (Message...LOL) :)

The bathroom is very very clean, the interior of the restaurant was artful and again very clean. 

I had the wagyu beef cheek for 2, roasted vegetables, thyme jus...and it was yummilicious it is the pic in my check-in photo - when I say the favorites were very tasty and tender you can cut with your fork or butter knife.

The desserts in my book can be bigger for sure. I had the basil semifreddo, lemon curd, strawberry, candied ginger. Very Tasty  

I'll be back again for sure - oh there are closed on Saturdays and Sundays...but believe me well worth the weekday trip

Walk-ins only (no reservations) - hours...Monday-Friday...lunch 12pm - 2pm and dinner 5pm - 9pm

Currently wine: brut prosecco 5/22, dry riesling, washington hills 7/29, sauvignon blanc, atlantique 7/29, chardonnay, bernier 10/40, ​

pinot noir, moulin de gassac 6/27, grenache blend, bonpas 5/22, cabernet sauvignon, eod cellars 10/40...dessert wine 6...and beer:

m.i.a miami weiss 4, duck rabbit milk stout 6, big swell ipa 6, original sin eldberry cider 6

nonalcohlic: still/sparkling water, housemade sodas, coffee, tea

Eggs-actly What I Craved! LOL...Great breakfast cafe. Very good breakfast menu and everyone is excellent. We have had several different breakfast at the Broken Egg, my favorite so far is the sweet potato pancake. The restaurant was clean and tastefully decorated. Our waitress (Delaney C.) was pleasant and readily available despite the place being busy. She was outstanding. :)

Parts of Paris a French Bistro located in Safety Harbor...Nourriture excellence...comfortably casual, dress up or not, sit inside or outside in the covered front patio (also for those who smoke). Nice atmosphere, the service and the food was fantastic and worth the price in my book...The is a nicely converted older home. 

A must try cocktail is the cherry wood old fashion :)  All of our meals were plated very well and delicious...Looking forward to my next visit!!!

Authentic, Fresh, and Delicious...

East Bistro is a neighborhood eatery and coffee shop. Providing  flavors from east of the Mediterranean ( Lebanon, United Arab Emirates, Cyprus, Egypt, Morocco, Pakistan,Yemen to name a few) in my military career I've had the pleasure of tasting the truly authentic dishes from all over the Eastern Mediterranean region and let me say East Bistro hands down is as authentic and sitting at any eatery in any of the above mentioned countries. 

You must try the kebabs cooked to perfection. The Kibbeh hhhmmmm yummilicious I took a few quality pics (because we do eat with our eyes first) reasons television commercials makes us hungry LOL.

Try the Fatayer (which are traditional baked pastries stuffed with a variety of delicious fresh ingredients). 

For your sweet tooth Bosbousa, Baklava, and  Knafeh to name a few of the filo dough goodies. 

Drinks offered are coffees, teas, mochas, lattes, espressos and more.

Vegetarian Friendly with lots of Vegan Options and Halal. 

10/10 for Food, Value, and Service with price range of $5 - $15.

So make a trip to this fantastic Lebanese, Middle Eastern, Greek, Mediterranean restaurant for Yummilicious and Tastylicious cuisines.

*all meals are also available for take-out

Different location ~ same great food...Where do I begin? The new gem of Dunedin  healthy and fresh dining. Service is always stellar - and everyone is super friendly. For those with Celiac's it's even more terrific - offering numerous delicious options across breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Highly recommended.

Teresa is the owner of Ohana Cafe in Dunedin, You feel like you are home - you feel like you are family from the big aloha greeting when you walk in the front door to the warm and pleasant service that you will receive. My favorite is the Delicious pancakes and Organic Macadamia Nut Sauce with red potato home fries (The Ohana breakfast)

Themed after the 1972 Miami Dolphins' "Perfect Season," and with a restaurant in nearly every NFL city, Shula's has become one of the top-five steak houses.

The quality of food and service are fantastic.The Blackened Tenderloin Tips (seared with cajun spices, served with béarnaise and BBQ sauce) . Yummilacious 

Plenty of TV's to catch the games. Great atmosphere. I highly recommend Shula's!

Looking for something new for breakfast but lite and tasty so we tried this new spot...Located at the corner of Belcher and Nursery Road in Clearwater is a hidden gem with authentic European bistro. Jérôme the owner is truly a French master baker and chef with amazing croissants, tarts, and pastries of all types made fresh in house daily, as well as proper bistro meals. Excellent omelettes, crepes, sauces, salads, entrees, wines and European coffee.  

Great prices. The staff are all amazing with OUTSTANDING customer service. Amanda is truly a ball of life and fun.

This isn't "Frenchish" cuisine...it's the real thing. Jérôme  truly has the passion for the art of pastries. The menu is inventive and the food is always fresh. INDULGE YOUR SENSES WITH AMAZING FOOD AND PASTRIES at Flying with  Jérôme. Will definitely be back and would highly recommend to all my friends!!!

To all my Gluten Free Yelpers this is a must visit spot. Great selection of unique sodas and beers - The Staff is knowledgeable and can accommodate any vegan request and the also sell a variety of gourmet chips. The Homemade cookies are very delicious and the best handcrafted sandwiches on very tasty bread. The Sandwich shop on Main is truly a gem in downtown Safety Harbor and corner bistro. The owner Sally is sooo delightful and truly a pleasure to converse with. Our waitress Tori was amazing and very friendly and explained the whole menu of possibilities to us from their signature favorites to choosing our own fillings, toppings and condiments Checkout my pics do not leave the spot without trying the Homemade cookies baked daily by the owner Sally and she only makes a limited amounts so you are guaranteed fresh baked daily chocolate chip cookies.

My overall experience was truly exceptional...!!!

I must say La comida y el ambiente muy bueno! The food and the atmosphere very good...the best Cuban food i've had...small location but worth the wait...seating is very limited but more has been added since they took over the store front shop next door so you can also now seat inside (great on a very hot day) Bodega has amazing sandwiches.

I had the Guava and cheese pastelitos, Pollo Asado, Black Beans and Rice, Cortdito...Cuban coffee with a little milk added...everything was delicious. The authentic flavors YUMMILICIOUS 
*:*:*5.*:*¨¨*:*.Star.*:*¨¨*:*.

The Lemon Ricotta Pancakes with fresh added whipped ricotta cheese to our multigrain batter. Served as a mid-stack of two pancakes topped with marinated berries and creamy lemon curd. (which wasYUMMILICIOUS)

First Watch is a Cafe chain for health-minded with breakfast, brunch & lunch options such as omelets, pancakes, salads and soups.

What's in a name...? Since the majority of the people who visit First Watch are not sailors, pirates or sea-farin' scallywags, well First Watch is a nautical term that refers to the veryfirst shift of the day.

The Avocado Toast was served with thick-cut whole grain toast topped with fresh smashed avocado, EVOO, lemon and Maldon sea salt. Served with basted cage-free eggs.

The Million Dollar Bacon consisted of  slices of our signature hardwood smoked bacon with brown sugar, black pepper, cayenne and a maple syrup drizzle. (FYI...it does contain soy if you have an allergy).

I highly recommend this location!

Amazing little find...located in the heart of delightful Dunedin Florida. Hop on Broadway Ave just off of Main Street and you will find this wonderful gem right next to Rosie's Tavern.

Some days you just want to go to a place for a nice light breakfast...and Dunedin Coffee Company & Bakery checks this box. The lattes are artful (please see my pics), fun ambience, everything is homemade...and so fresh...you MUST try the Pistachio muffins and the Sweet Potatoes Biscuits.

Service is always prompt and friendly. Elena (the owner) is truly amazing. The coffee is particularly smooth and not burned or sharp tasting. The Dunedin Coffee Company & Bakery offers high quality locally roasted coffee, breakfast, breads, homemade baked goods, cookies, muffins, scones, cakes, pies, tarts, croissants, baklava, tiramisu, cannolis, vegan/gluten free bars and gelato! Meals are prepared when you order (which is great) I personally think the prices are good - maybe a dollar or two more than most places but remember everything is baked in house and fresh...not out of a bag and warmed up in a microwave. 

You can also have baked custom orders and cater special events and the coffee is Organic & Fair Trade Coffee.

This health food store/cafe is awesome!!! The staff is very knowledgable and friendly!!! Large store with ample selection for groceries and a really delicious hot food and salad bar with fresh vegetables and plenty of vegan options, and enjoy your meal in the comfortable and spacious seating area. Clean, pleasant, and tasty.

Thoroughly enjoyed myself. The food was amazing! The owners are retired Army and Air Force who are very friendly and personable. Super delicious fat oyster poboys companied by music and eating under the trees at picnic tables. 

Quite possibly the best cajun food in the Dunedin community.  The hush puppies are amazing! The customer service was outstanding with a relaxed atmosphere and good simple food.

I'd love to write a review of the food but after waiting 40 minutes past our reservation time, when finally, our table was given away to a higher profile party than us, we decided to leave and eat somewhere else. The only thing worse than a restaurant that cannot manage their seating schedule, is one who ignores you and feels no compulsion to acknowledge your very existence within their hallowed walls.

By far the worst casino I've visit. 
I've never been to a casino that doesn't offer free drinks while you play. 

The food here is sub par (please read my review of Rock and Raw). And the service here is just as sad.

The games here are pretty standard, but the property looks bigger than it really is. They are renovating large chunks of the property, leaving a lack luster appearance.

I couldn't find a table game to advertise my life! What casino doesn't have an active roulette table.

Did I mention the lack of free drinks? Come on! Even the location in Mississippi had free drinks as you played! The private casino in upstate New York (a private casino, not brand name) gives free drinks! 

It's so cheap and crappy that they don't offer drinks while you play. 

The service here is great weak and the amenities are even weaker. The only casino in the Central Florida area, and it's a flop.

So Sad, I went in June before it changed hands and it was great....but now there was nothing but inexperienced 20 somethings working there and the service was deplorable.   I could list the many things that were wrong but after reading some of the other reviews you'll get the picture.  We paid $1240 a night, and the only thing worth it was the view.  Don't go until they get their act back together otherwise you'll be wasting your money.

Oh and BTW, we were talking to a gentleman at their New Years Eve party and he said that he was a member at Bacara and that his job was to write reviews for them.  Isn't that a conflict of interest?  I mean you make someone a member with all the perks that go with it and then ask them to write the reviews?  I think that's very suspect.....
Cheaper alternative to Minado, which is located in Blue Bell area, but i'd rather pay extra $5 to enjoy better quality food at Minado.

I LOVE this place!  I am so excited to rave about them and I've been mentally writing this review for months - however I'm not going to be articulate how much I love this place as well as I could in my head.  

The thing that I love the most about this place is what incredible service they give to big groups- my friends and I have had two birthday dinners here and have been blown away! As a big group we get the all you can eat because then we can share and try a lot of new rolls.  (My favorite is the crystal shrimp!)  When I was there last night they were more than willing to put our cake into their fridge so it wouldn't melt which I really appreciated.  At the end of our hour and a half meal (which they didn't rush at all) our waitress suggested a quail shooter to cleanse our palette and settle the stomachs.  The whole meal was great and I can't wait to return!!
The fact that people are posting back reviews because of something the restaurant did is uncalled for. Base it off their delicious food.

This place... Where do I start?

I'm really not sure how I've not heard more about this location.  We had a business dinner with a few out of town folks that would throw out the old New Orleans names but a co-worker suggested we try this and I am really glad he did.

I started with Oysters and Angel Hair which seemed a bit more like ramen noodles but either way, the flavor was amazing and I will likely go back just for that and a glass of wine.

For entree, I ordered the Double-Cut Cheshire Pork Chop which was incredibly large and fantastically tasty.  I could not get over the size.  I would get that again for sure.

Finished off with an amazing bread pudding with strawberries, caramel and powered sugar. #Stuffed

I would recommend this place to everyone and plan to head back very soon while attending a conference in New Orleans.

Lüke was one of my favorites in New Orleans. Their happy hour is SOLID!

- Half off cocktails (I recommend door#three if you like fruity, refreshing drinks)
- $1.25 fried oysters
- $0.75 raw oysters!!!

We had oysters at Felix's and Acme Oyster House, but Lüke's are by far our favorite. 

The food here is delicious. List of stuff I had the pleasure of trying: 
- Crawfish Bisque
- Crispy Brussel Sprouts
- Fruge Farms Crawfish "Etouffée"
- Moules et Frites (mussels)

List of stuff I had the pleasure of staring at:
- Entrecôte grillée et frites: a few from our group ordered the ribeye and it looked like it was cooked to perfection. I haven't eaten meat in over two years and looking at that steak really made my mouth water.. 

ANYWAY, solid happy hour, drinks, and food. Highly recommend!! If you're visiting New Orleans, DO NOT skip this one!

Felix's char-grilled oysters are to die for. 

A local told us to order these while we were standing in line outside. Thank you, kind local! You've changed my life. 

We also tried a bunch of other stuff: blackened alligator, jambalaya, gumbo, po-boys, raw oysters, you get the idea. We thought everything was good but we LOVED the char-grilled oysters.

Seriously, get the char-grilled oysters here! They're way better than the ones at Acme across the street.

This is an awesome place for breakfast.

Our server was smoking hot, funny, and joy to be around. 

Food was awesome well cooked to perfection. Great presentation and big portions.

The decor is strange but who cares when you get great food and service.

Being the unofficial Mayor of Philadelphia in South Florida I'm constantly asked the question, which is the best Gino's or Pats? My answer is neither. Those are amateur moves because the best Philly cheesesteak is found at Jim's on South Street. It's just that simple.

It doesn't have the history of those places. You won't find a Boyz II Men shooting a video there (Motownphilly), you won't run into Joe Biden there, but everyone knows the Jim's is pound for pound the best in the biz. There are plenty of great places and chances are if you have never had a real Philly you're in for a treat.

I prefer Jim's because it's simply the better steak. I would advise anyone coming here to prepare to wait in line. Lunch time is no joke so off-peak hours would be best. Also, it does not make sense to just have one sandwich. Man up and get you two. Even if you just eat 1 1/2, it'll be worth it.

You have have it wit or without and it won't matter because the sandwich is great either way. How much more do I need to say about a Philly cheesesteak?

I'll rank the importance of Philadelphia landmarks and notable celebrities to show you just how Jim's stacks up.

Horrible sanitation practices. After getting sick from their chicken I spoke with an employee as well as frequent bar customers. Their kitchen staff has been told on multiple occasions that their food preparation practices are not in accordance with what city and state regulations state. My entire family got sick off of various menu items.

The original habit is a local landmark, a Goleta Rite of passage, this is where it all began baby. It started with burgers, chili burgers, malts, fries and two brothers with a vision. Quality food and great people catalyzed the exponential growth and success of the brand that has exploded in recent years, culminating with the distinction of  "the best tasting burgers in America" by consumer reports. 

Their original name was The Old Habit but Brent did not want his food to be associated with age, so he ditched that part and never looked back. Back in the day I spent a lot of time at the Habit. Locals from all over flocked in for the lunch specials, and at that time you could get a beer with them. It was not just out of convenience either. Owners of the best restaurants in town would constantly pop in.

And the Habit has not stopped getting better!  They have done away with their tuna melt sandwich and replaced it with high quality tuna sandwiches. They added veggie burgers and onion rings to the lineup and took care of the health oriented diner with fresh salads too!

So stop in and see for yourself, you will thank me later!

My extended family and I found The Mex Authentic on a Saturday night. We were looking for a fourth meal after a day in the park celebrating the life of my step brother. Mexican food is always a crowd pleaser and The Mex Authentic looked great. 

A friendly gentleman let us know that the kitchen would be closing soon so we placed an order  of veggie nachos to share and a round of drinks. Dayum, the nachos were a giant cheezy mass of deliciousness smothered decadent sour cream and guacamole. I doubt that anyone would miss the meat in this dish.

I was happy to hear that the beans were vegetarian and ordered a tostada with beans and shrimp. I discussed my intention to avoid any chicken stock or meat products and the tostada was a perfect option. The plates arrived quickly and everything looked fantastic, we had smiles all the way around the table.

I dug into my tostada and got a mouthful of Spanish rice which was not the preparation that I selected. My guess is that the chef intended to buff me out with more than I ordered, but that kind gesture backfired and I had to send back my meal. It is not easy being picky Vicki, try as I might, mystery meat stalks me.

The Mex Authentic erred on the side of being too generous with their food which would make most people happy, but their kind gesture was sent to the wrong diner. I would definitely return as the re-fired meal was outstanding.

Went to study with a group of friends, was immediately treated with a bad attitude by the management. After my friend purchased a coffee and we sat studying for awhile, the management asked us to stop taking up so much space, when there was another group with the same set-up that hadn't been asked the same thing. After this, we decided it would be better if we left, and the same person proceeded to tell us they hoped we didn't think it was about race (which we hadn't thought about at all). Overall poor experience, won't be coming back.

What a wonderful time, I bought a Groupon deal to take a river cruise as I had seen online that doing this at least once is a must and I don't regret a minute!! Riding on the Creole Queen is a great way to learn about the history of New Orleans and its rich culture. The tour guide was very well-versed and made learning fun!! On a nice sunny day, this ride is heaven! They stopped and dropped us off on a battlefield near the end and we could spend an hour milling about and enjoying the scenery. They also had a full bar on the boat and a buffet or a la carte items could be purchased for pretty cheap!! I would definitely suggest this!

Was in town with my family for the weekend and wanted a convenient lunch that my kids and wife would like.  This place seemed to fit the bill.  It's kind of hard to go wrong with anything on these steam buns (bao) no matter what you put inside them.  This place has some interesting filing for these buns, with influences from both Chinese and Korean cuisine.
