We ordered Pork Belly, KFC, and Shrimp baos.  I really can't pick a favorite because they were all very good.  All of them had a nice balance of sweet & spicy, but shrimp had the least amount of spiciness.  Combination of kimchi and pineapple in pork belly bao was an interesting mix.  Although it didn't affect taste, serving these in different colored buns was a nice touch.  Seems like they just recently started doing this because most of the photos show standard white buns.

You'll probably need to eat about two to three of these to be full, so just keep that in mind when ordering.  I only ordered four for a family of four so was still hungry afterward.  

The menu seems to change frequently so it's best to check its website if you are placing a phone order.  I was going off some of the recent menu photos posted on Yelp and noticed some of the items are no longer available.  This place also has a separate menu for lunch and dinner.

I plan to be in Santa Barbara again next weekend and will most likely come back here to try more items, including non bao items like Miso Black Cod Donburi and Kungpao Cauliflower.

The visit started out horribly when we pulled up to valet park and saw that it cost $20. Apparently, this is a new feature added in January 2015 to 'welcome their guests'. For $20 you would expect the valets to greet you quickly and be friendly but that was not the case. Since my mom has sciatica we had to valet. 

Onto the rewards center to get our cards. The rewards employees seem to not care at all just like the valets - not friendly or in a hurry to help. Because the noise volume in the casino is SO LOUD I had to hand write all my personal information on pieces of paper slid back and forth because I could NOT HEAR ONE WORD the gal asked me - ridiculous. 

Slots didn't pay out at at, no big surprise. There were hardly any drink servers on the floor and they too didn't seem to care about being friendly or quick when you could flag them down. The 5 stall women's bathroom on the left side of the casino was run down looking, not clean, and constantly had a long line. There is a gorgeous much larger women's bathroom far far away at the end of the left side of the casino where no elderly woman would trek (near the area where they cater parties) - very thoughtful casino scum lords.

If you are from the Detroit area, run, don't walk, to Detroit Coney Island! 

We've tried every coney dog joint in Pinellas and haven't found anything close to the Detroit area coneys that we've been missing so much. This restaurant delivers old school coneys and other Michigan favorites (polish platter a la Hamtramck; Sanders hot fudge cream puffs; Faygo, Vernors, gyros) in a super cool urban atmosphere (industrial steel tables, graffiti art) served with love by a great family from the Detroit area. 

Coneys were spot-on (chili, onions, mustard), fries were hot and crispy, Rock n' Rye rocked, and the hot fudge cream puff was delicious.

CANT WAIT TO GO BACK!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Thank you for bringing some Detroit Love to Pinellas :)

ps - next time I'm hitting the men's room for a photo op - heard there is Rat Fink art....

Went to Vango last night for two friends' birthdays. They spoke with the owner several weeks in advance and were promised:

1) $35 top shelf open bar for guests 10-12
2) A private bar for us
3)  Waived entry and free shots for the birthday girls

This was the reality:

1) $35 well drinks, all CHEAP liquor 10-12
2) A sectioned off part of the bar which ANYONE who was willing to pay $35 was allowed into
3) Birthday girls had to pay and were stuck drinking well drinks with the rest of us. He clearly only said this to get the girls to have their party there.

Some of our friends tried to stop in for a drink after 12 but were told they would ONLY be let in if they got bottle service. The owner even said to me earlier "If they are not willing to spend money, they should not be here." How RUDE. My friends are willing to spend money, but forcing everyone to get bottle service is completely unreasonable. 

The owner is a LIAR and a CHEAT. When I asked him why we did not get the private bar as promised, he said he never agreed to it. 

When my friends asked why it was suddenly well drinks and not top shelf, he justified it by saying "Well the other party upstairs is paying $40 so you're getting a good deal."

So basically he was ripping ALL of us off. 

The owner is a jerk who looks down on the patrons. His attitude was BEYOND unacceptable. We will never go back there again.

If you want to go somewhere where you will be ripped-off and scrutinized by the owner and most of the staff, Vango is the place to go.

So I am SOUTH Indian.  Like REALLY south Indian.  The kind of south indian that is used to eating dosa, idli, and vadai for lunch, breakfast, and dinner.  My mom's cooking is good, and it's really tough for me to eat out when it comes to South Indian food - however, sometimes you just crave a dosa.  While there are many great Indian restaurants in Philly - no good south indian places AT ALL.  So sad! 

UNTIL NOW! Philadelphia Chutney Company to the rescue! 

Samosa is good - not the usual kind of samosa - a little bit bigger, and they seem to use the same filing that they use in their masala dosa - which is fine - but tastes interesting.  Instead of fryed, I also think that either they bake their samosas - or they use less oil.  Either way, delicious. 

The vadai (or wada) is really good. It's JUST like my mom makes it - a litlte oily, crispy, and delicious.  The chutney and sambar are also REALLY good.  

Finally, the dosa is amazing. I had a masala dosa. I had a friend try the spinach / paneer chese dosa - which was good according to my friend.  

Finally, their prices are really very reasonable.  You have to try it! Cheap, good, and south indian? sounds like a winning combo!

St Louis needs more restaurants like Five Bistro. 

Five is a white tablecloth contemporary American fine dining establishment that serves only locally grown produce and locally raised meats. Mercifully, fish is an exception to the local rule.
 
When dinner is the night, I like to take my time, which means a drink at the bar before sitting down.  We arrived 20 minutes ahead of our reservation for a drink.  Joe (Chef/owner Anthony Devoti's father) greeted us at the door with a beaming smile and offered to seat us immediately, but we headed to the bar.  This is a small restaurant.  The bar area is directly across from the entrance and there are several tables between the door and the bar.  There is a larger dinning room to the right of the bar but the space is all restaurant - there is no separate bar room.    The bar tender was a real pro who asked a couple of questions and quickly recommended a wine that Mary loved and drank the rest of the night.   Pleasantly, the wine recommendation was not the most expensive wine in the house.

Five is not the only restaurant in town to focus on local food, but no other is so fully committed to local food or does it so well.  

I'm always suspicious of restaurants with enormous menus - they can't possibly do all those dishes well. The menu at Five (allegedly changes daily) is manageable and designed for four courses.   There were 5 appetizers, a soup with two salad options, 5 entrees (beef, chicken, pork, fish and a vegetarian risotto) with desserts or cheeses for the final course.  You are free to order ala carte do a four-course prix fixe for $45 ($60 with wine pairings). 

Mary and I both decided to do the prix fix.   My first course was the fish tasting menu which was excellent and made me feel better about my entree.  

My second course was an amazing trout chowder.  Too often chowders are as thick as pudding.  This chowder was buttery and hearty but with a broth base that felt a little light and perfectly seasoned.  This is how God intended chowder to be served.  

I have some firm beliefs about what to order in nice restaurants - don't order things you make at home or can be found on any menu.  Eat like a grown-up - try new things and go for the house specialties.  I never order a steak unless I'm at a premium steakhouse (where I will get a prefect steak perfectly prepared) and I never order chicken.  I went for a braised pork steak that was nothing like your dad's pork steak.  It was a think square of trimmed pork served on top of whipped Yukon gold potatoes covered is a red wine reduction that will change your life.   This was a pork version of braised short ribs. The sauce was deep, rich and complex and I ate every drop.   Mary broke my rule and ordered the roasted chicken (to be fair, it's the roasted poulet).  She was rightly apologetic about the choice but insisted that she had it before and that it was really something special and she was right.   The chicken looked and smelled great with brown crispy skin with roasted potatoes and turnups covered in a savory light brown sauce obviously made from the pan drippings.  She offered me a piece and I have to say it was the most amazing roasted chicken I've ever had.  It was so good I'm thinking about slipping back later in the week just to order the chicken and eat it at the bar. 

I'm an easy customer to wait on.  I don't expect slavish devotion and I tip well.  I have two pet peeves when it comes to service.   One is a hovering team of servers who over do it with constant interruptions (when you have a mouth full to make sure you are ok with the half glass of wine in front of you) and constant fussing with the table, all of which interferes with good dinner conversation.  The other is the server who is only a bittersweet memory after the menu and specials are explained with all follow-up service delegated to underlings.  Service at Five struck just the right tone.  Our server - Ian - was always handy but never hovering.  He never interrupted but was always there when more drinks were needed, etc.  Ian explained the menu well, was comfortable making suggestions (I hate servers too timid to offer a suggestion), and paced the dinner perfectly.   The service was pitch perfect. 

Five is exactly the kind of restaurant I love: Small but classy where the focus is on serving really good tasting, high quality food made from fresh ingredients.  No grand décor or elaborately sculpted dishes that look and taste like a movie prop.  This is bistro dining at it's finest.

Sorry,  a lose in my book. After reading advertisement about how this new restaurant has Happy Hour everyday from 12 noon to six pm, we decided to try it today only to be told: "Oh that's only Monday through Thursday ".? Well, menu board out front said 12 noon to 6 pm? When I pointed that out to them. I'm told "Oh, that's a mistake". I am not a fan of restaurants who do not stand behind what they advertise or what is displayed on their menu boards. After we were seated with no real explanation or apology we waited almost 10 minutes and no one had acknowledged us to answer my continued questions. I decided we would just skip this experience for now. The two stars are for the ambiance, great beach, ocean views. I will always give a second chance, so will try again sometime. Hope I can give a better review. BTW menu board was changed from 12 to 6 to 2 to 6 when we left.

What a wonderful experience. We stopped in to try new place on the block. Very relaxing, excellent service and everything was delicious. Don't let the menu turn you away, it is unusual Italian cuisine which makes menu a little intimidating. Just step in, take a risk and I promise you will enjoy. The restaurant space has been redone with nice clean lines and open feeling to the area. Wonderful bar seating with an interesting Italian wine list and great beer choices.
Menu is mostly pizza but there are enough other items added to have something for everyone. We had two children in our group and they were able to find something they liked and were delighted. 
The dessert menu is fabulous and anything you try will be yummy. 
We decided to be adventurous and have the shrimp black rice, the veggie black rice, the octopus side and three pizza pies. All were delicious. I would highly recommend the black rice dishes. Flavorful and filling. 
Dessert was an awesome experience, experience the fruit and ice cream for delicious and light or the chocolate cake and ice cream for decadent. Everyone really liked the pistachio ice cream dessert both texture and flavor. 
Second visit, still five stars.  We tried brunch this time, did not regret. Great service, wonderful, delicious food, fabulous cocktail, salud

I've been living in Florida for almost a year now, and Pass-a-Grille is by far the best beach I have found to date. The sand is white and usually free of litter and garbage, and the water is clear and warm (however all of it is here compared to the California water I'm used to). Moreover, this is my go-to beach because its never overly crowded and overrun by tourists, even on the weekends. It is a laid back, relaxing get away not too far from decent restaurants and shops. I absolutely adore this place, and most of my summer plans will surely involve this beach!

Friend and I went here for a dinner before a movie and we were sooooooooooooo
disappointed.  
My shrimp dish had 4 shrimp in it.  I had asked for a gluten free version and all sauce was removed.  So my shrimp were cooked and placed on my rice, without any kind of sauce. My cat could have done that!
My friend ordered another shrimp dish and she had 3 shrimp in hers.
We asked where the rest of our meal was and our waitress giggled and was surprised that we even asked.
Atmosphere is very pretty but we didn't go here for atmosphere. We came here because we had heard about all the great food and frankly we were surprised at what was put down in front of us.

I mentioned this to my group of friends and every single one of them said they had been here once and have never returned.
I guess that's the consensus.

We won't be returning, either, unfortunately.
**** don't forget to read the filtered reviews, a lot of low ratings in the filtered area, as well.

We must have come at a very good time.

And...... we must have ordered the right combination.
And... we must have gotten the best waiter.
And... the best chef on duty.

Our order was perfect!
We had the kale salad with the Pimento, Fried Green Tomato and Bacon sandwich with a side of fried okra..

Wow! Wow!

The Kale salad is the best in town.... No shit!
The Pimento, bacon and fried green tomato is the best combination for a southern sandwich. 
The fried okra was crunchy, abundant, yummy, dipped in the white sauce from the squirt bottle on the table.

Our waiter had back up so there was plenty of attention.
The fried okra was perfectly cooked and crunchy.
The kale salad was the large order so we could split it, and the pimento cheese sandwich with a CRUNCHY fried green tomato and bacon was the bomb....

Everything was delicious, freshly cooked, freshly prepared, good sized portions, yummy, yummy, yummy..

I know we'll be back for the kale salad because that was the reason we returned the second time.. and there will be a third and fourth time, as well.

The fact that they have their own parking lot is also wonderful for the mere reason there is never any parking in this area.
So with parking, a well stocked bar, lots of live entertainment, and lots of tables;
the attention was there.
the chef was on his mark and we couldn't have been more happy.

My friend and I have absolutely no complaints about a solid Southern meal, cooked perfectly for us - tonight.

You have to try the pimento, fried green tomato and bacon sandwich They call it the Pimento BLT.
That was amazing!
I am a true convert to Southern cooking... 
Seriously, I didn't gain all this weight with bad food!

No good foodie would make a visit to Pennsylvania without having a pretzel.  It would be like going to NYC and not having a bagel, or visiting a Jewish Deli.  Now, that's criminal!  So, I had my pretzel here.  

This is a small, "fast-food" pretzel shop, with pretty good pretzels! I got mine while it was still warm, and it was one of the best I've had, but I guess that's an unfair comparison, since the ones I've had in California are from ballparks, food carts or amusement parks where they've all been previously frozen.  These were fresh, soft and chewy with that unique pretzel flavor.  You can get them salted or unsalted.  Whichever you choose, just make sure to eat them while they're still warm!  

There's also an ongoing offer where you can buy something like 25 pretzels, and then get an additional 25 for free.  Whoa!  Pretzel party time!

Philly Pretzel Factory is a huge chain, with numerous locations throughout Pennsylvania and New Jersey.  I wish they had one in the Bay Area.  It easily puts Auntie Anne's and Wetzel's to shame.

Parisian bistro with outdoor seating...

I love walking up to a place that has outdoor seating in California because typically the weather is always pretty great and you'll spot a few fur babies. 

We ordered regular and vanilla lattes and my vanilla one was intensely sweet. I love it sweet but it was even too much for me. And no latte art :( 
With the prices here, you should at least get a little heart or leaf. 

We're also crazy about ham & cheese croissants and we always order them hot. This one was served to us lukewarm and some parts of the ham were still cold. We also love almond croissants and this one comes with a very heavy topping that overpowers the delicate flaky pastry. 

It's a very cute little bistro and I enjoyed the Parisian details but the cuisine & drinks were so so.

This is a very clean and convenient rest stop that's located along interstate 95. It's a great place to stop off when making the drive from NY to DC or similar. The welcome center has since been renamed as the "Biden Welcome Center" after former Vice President Joe Biden. 

The welcome center is large, spacious, and features a good amount of fast casual eateries, souvenirs, and a convenience store. The seating is cafeteria style and there are plenty of places to sit and relax. The restrooms are very clean and aplenty. There's also a small gas station and electric vehicle charging stations here as well. Totally not like the typical rest stops that I'm used to seeing in California. 

In addition, the welcome center also offers tourist information. It seems like many people stop here, including tour and school buses. I took the Flixbus here and this was our halfway stop. My only complaint is that most of the eateries are fast food shops, but that's understandable given the circumstances. Despite this, I still think that this is a very well maintained rest stop.

This tasting room is adorbs! I really love their whole outdoor tasting setup. It's so chic and dreamy. They've got such a cute little cabana setup with comfy booths and long white curtain drapes for privacy. Just about all of their picnic tables are covered, and they have heat lamps and string lights meticulously placed. 

Tastings at Carr Winery are by reservation only. I was able to easily schedule a tasting online before my visit. When I arrived, I was seated at my table right away and given a tasting menu. Jackie hosted me in the tasting room and she was wonderful! Very knowledgeable, sweet, and eager to tell me about each wine that she poured. Tastings are $20 for 5 tastes off of their current tasting menu, and the fee is waived with 3 or more bottle purchases. You can also purchase wine by the glass, and they have snacks and cheese boards for sale.

Their standard tasting included a taste of 1 white wine, 1 Rosé, and 3 of their reds. I personally preferred their red wines more than their white and Rosé. Their Pinot Gris was definitely a lot different than what I'm used to. It was very minerally and acidic which is different for me, but it wasn't bad. Their Pinot Noir was wonderful though. Very earthy but balanced. I also enjoyed their Syrah which was lightly tannic but not super bold. Their red wines definitely shine here.

The atmosphere is super chill and comfortable. It seems like this is a popular spot in town for group hangouts and tastings. I'm still dabbling in wines that are from the Santa Barbara/Santa Rita Hills wine region, so this added some good exposure for me. Really enjoyed my tasting experience and wouldn't mind coming back for another visit.

Ooooh, don't mind me. I've been drankin'. It's Friday night. During quarantine. And I'm writing this review while tipsy. During quarantine. And guess what?! I'm STILL gonna write it. During quarantine. Because... it's Friday night. During quarantine. So THERE. Ha!

Tonight I was craving for a steak. Unfortunately, many of the steak spots in my area aren't open for sit down, and the waits for takeout are just too long for me to bare right now. So for a split second... I thought about getting a cheesesteak. And then I thought about Jim's, and I just had to quickly change my mind. You see, I live in the great state of Cali. The problem with this is that the cheesesteaks here are nowhere near as delicious as the one that I had at Jim's. Nowhere NEAR it. I wasn't about to disappoint myself by getting a below second rate cheesesteak from a chain that isn't even all that great. 

The saying is true; once you've had a Philly cheesesteak from PHILLY bay-baaaaay... you will never look at a cheesesteak the same way ever again. Had my first real Philly cheesesteak at Jim's South Street and hunty; they did not disappoint. Didn't receive the warmest welcome from the staff when I stepped into that joint, but you gotta realize the sitch' right quick. It was late night, and most of the peeps who creep here in the late hours are probably drunk as hell. You gotta have thick skin to deal with the drunkards, so I understand. 

It's pretty simple; You walk in, look at the menu board (if you have to), choose what you want and tell them at the counter. Then, walk down and pay at the register. You'll wait for your food and then you can take it upstairs to eat it if you wanna dine in. Since it was my first time getting a real Philly cheesesteak, I had to go with the original. Yuuup. Ya girl got that good ol' Philly Phil sammich! Sh*t was the f*ck GOODT. Sorry to be so vulgar but it truly was. 

Just imagine this beautifully soft roll of bread, filled with most tender, juicy thin slices of steak, sandwiched between cheese so melted that it practically turns into strings when you pull the sandwich halves apart. And all of that tasty juice and oil dripping in pure glory. So, normally I wouldn't be a fan of the messy mess. I'm light weight bougie wit it (don't you dare judge). I just hate gettin' sh*t all over my mouth, hands, and clothes, especially grease. BUT... I just couldn't get enough of it here. Couldn't get ENOUGH. Gimme da grease puh-lease! Give it TO me. 

Not only was this cheesesteak juicy as all hell, but it was meatier than life itself. Flavored for the GAWDS. Givin' me all of this extra life that I didn't even know that I needed. Yes, I loved it. And yes, I want some more... damnit. Heavenly is what I'll call it. How I'll describe it. Yeah... that part. 

If you eat upstairs, they have this "guard" who just sits there and watches you while you eat. A little annoying, slightly creepy, and down right uncomf, but I understand why they do it. Some of these damn peeps be actin' REAL cray cray. You'll have a nice little view of South street if you choose to sit by the window. The "guard" also cleans the tables once people leave. I guess homeboy ain't so bad after all.

More than the cheesesteak though, I've gotta say, I truly enjoyed chatting it up with the staff. There was one older gentleman, didn't get his name. He was so hospitable. He heard my "accent" (I guess us Californians really do stand out, huh?!) and asked me where I was from. We instantly struck up a convo after that and he was so warm and welcoming toward me. That really made my night, especially since it was my first time there. 

Lawd. What I would give to have another one of dem cheesesteaks right about now. So damn good. If you're there right now, just make like Nike and DO IT. Have yourself a merry little cheesesteak and take full advantage of the drip. The grease drip that is. It's truly sensational. And you will love it. I can't wait for the day that I'll return to be reunited with that Philly cheesesteak again.

An. Absolute. Must.

MUUUUUST!!! An absolute must visit when in Philly, baby! This public market has everything that your little heart could ever damn desire! Fresh local and exotic produce, high quality meat and seafood, artisan cheeses, fresh baked goods, and an amazing array of different cultural cuisines! Food, food, and more food! So many damn choices that it'll make your head spin. 

All of the stands are from locally owned and family run businesses, making this market even that much more special. Seating is cafeteria style, so you can peruse the market, pick up several food items, and then enjoy some grub right there in the food hall. Aside from food, this market also features several stands with handcrafted jewelry, clothing, souvenir, and more.

Of course, lil' ol' me couldn't purchase something from ever vendor (I damn sure wish I could have though). So, I ended up getting some bbq from Frank's bbq. Ordered a bbq chicken wing plate with mixed veggies, mac n' cheese, and a roll, and it was scrumptious! The chicken wings were super juicy and the mac n' cheese was so lovably cheesy. Can't forget about their yummy banana cornbread! I got one of these for dessert and it was sooo friggin' moist and delicious! I'm dreaming about it now. Frank's is an awesome option if you're looking for a spot to eat at in the market. 

You have to... HAAAAVE to stop by here during your visit to Philly. It's an iconic 125+ year city staple that has so much to offer.

I can hardly believe that this place is still in business if they treat all customers the way they treated my party. 

At one point, a member allowed his friend to take a sip of a drink he had-- a single, quick sip through a straw, mind you-- and one of the employees grabbed them by the collars and physically pushed them to the door before shutting them out because the friend had not brought her ID. It is understandable to refuse drinks to anyone without an ID, but to physically engage and shove a customer shows a startling and unprofessional lack of respect for clients. 

Further, the employees constantly yelled obscenities at my party for noise (I.e. "I thought I told you I'm tired of you being so fucking loud. I'm tired of dealing with this shit.") despite that we had rented the venue and there was no one to disturb besides the employees, who spent more time talking with each other than they did doing their jobs. 

I will certainly never be giving business to such an aggressive and disrespectful venue whose employees treat customers like prisoners who are lucky to be there.

Oh my!!  This place...  Wow!

First off you should know I am a sushi snob. I routinely eat at Nobu and Matsuhisa in NYC so I'm not usually eating a ton of sushi in Nashville. 

I never would have thought that we could get this kind of Japanese food in the south. This place is super pricey but honestly it was worth it. We had the edamame with truffle sea salt to start and it was the best edamame I've ever had. 

Other appetizers were the agedashi tofu, oysters and pork belly. All were great.  For dinner we mostly had sushi. The Nashvegas roll was amazing. I hate cream cheese in rolls but this one had a goat cheese mousse which was phenomenal!  The fish was all incredibly fresh and buttery. The best thing was the o-ku nigiri otoro. Holy moly that was one of the best pieces of sushi I've ever eaten. 

The only weak point was dessert. Had the PBJ panna cotta and was underwhelmed but not enough to take off a star!
Bad Food; Good Bar... They should seriously invest in a legitimate Executive Chef, and revamp the Food Menu.  Otherwise, cool place. If you're a Gear Head, you definitely wanna come eat here.

When in St Pete Beach I would strongly recommend you try this place you won't regret it!

I was pretty much buzzed while on vacationing St Pete Beach so I won't remember all the little details but here we go
This place is huge I remember they have ocean view seats but I don't remember if I was on one SMH They had long line of people waiting and the place was pretty loud which didn't bother me.

Everything look so delicious I wanted to eat the menu!!
I started with the wedge salad which is my favorite, bacon was a bit dried other than it was excellent.
Of course I ordered a lobster dinner, I have a rule when on vacation eat a lobster at least one/once a day. I have been to quite a few places including Bar harbor Maine, still never had a 16 ounce lobster tail, so I loved this big gigantic scrumptious tail. Every bite was delicious and still couldn't finish it. When they said this tail is 16 ounce they mean it is 16 ounce tail.
I had sautéed broccoli and coleslaw for side, coleslaw is coleslaw sautéed broccoli was OK but definitely over cooked.
Overall I loved this place I would go again and again, wish it was here by me. I will definitely go next time when I'm in the area which I'm definitely going to Clearwater.

Unfortunate thing happened the next day I was ill and couldn't go out to dinner yet I wanted to eat something fancy not Chick-fil-A like my boyfriend had suggested Lol I dare him
This place is one of the closest to the hotel where I was staying so we decided to order from here. I ordered the same thing except ordered the mac & cheese not broccoli, didn't want the soggy broccoli.
Long story make it short I got a bad lobster tail, he was dead or almost dead before he got cooked. I didn't have the energy to call them to complain.
A few days later I was close by this place and I went to see the manager his name is Kevin he gave me the refund $55.
Thank you Kevin, excellent service, I will definitely be back!

A little bit of Paris right on St Lawerence Street here in Midtown  Reno.   

At times there's a line out the door.   Yes it's worth the wait but I rarely wait. It's just easier for me to get there early.  

Croissants are amazing.   There is a flakey squarish pastry in many varieties -- currently mostly sweet but I'm considering starting a petition to bring back the fig, Brie and bacon one!!! 

Currently they are offering take and bake gingerbread and chocolate chip cookie dough.   They will be closing for the holiday and rumor has it they will be offering take and bake begets.   

Yes the new parking spots are lovely but parking can still be a pain.  Park on Forrest and walk over that's the joy of Midtown.

It must be review amnesia I could swear I did this review before.

Sierra Kitchen is always a good idea 

Pre/post movies for a light bite 
Happy Hour offers $5 small plates & libations
Group Dining Options pick 5 items plus $5 beverage options ranging from $25-$40 depending on the menu selected
Live music
Specials menus for most holidays 

What I'm most obsessed with are their Wine Dinners.  4-courses paired with healthy pours of wine.  Much credit must be given to the fact that you can order the wine at the tastings.  I've been to may wine tastings in town that they tell you to go to Ben's or Total Wine.  

A few personal favs from the menu 
Daily tacos - never disappoint.
Brussel Sprouts - I'm obsessed. 
Bacon Wrapped Dates - Always seem to get ordered. I don't like dates but they tend to be enjoyed by those that do.  

Bret and Nicole have created a true locals' joint that welcomes everyone.

A taste of NOLA comes to RENO!

Located in The Sticks strip mall in the former spot of Uncorked.  Unfortunately I never made it to their old location.  Based on the reviews, I was ready to dive into some southern comfort food. 

The meal: 
Red wine options - Cab or Merlot - I drank water. 
Fried Green Tomatoes - The tomatoes were red and a bit mushy. 
Fried Chicken - WOW I've never seen a leg and a thigh that big.  THANK YOU for making a fried chicken plate with just dark meat.  The chicken was tender.  Not greasy.  Fried crispy.  A bit bland for my taste but they're was hot sauce from Louisiana on the table that did the trick. 
Collard Greens - This was the first time I was offered Malt Vinegar with my collards. I figured I'd give it a shot.  The green were tender with a spicy kick; no malt vinegar needed for my taste. 
Mac & Cheese - It's a vegetable in the south.  This is not fancy artisan mac & cheese.  It is macaroni and cheese baked till the top is golden brown the cut like lasagna and served.  Good stuff! 
Cornbread - They do offer rolls but for me cornbread is the better option.  Nice and dense served with butter and honey.  

No room for dessert and took a doggy bag home.  The service was nice, poor guy it was his 6th day on the job but he was on point.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed Oxbow yet!  

In truth it's a bit off my radar.  It's located on Dickerson Road in the parking lot in front a strip of warehouses.   I use to hit it up more on the regular when I was looking at apartments in that area or picking something up from the water gardens.  

The food is always on point:
Pizza great for sharing.  
Breakfast hits the spot. 
Rack of lamb - is a huge portion.  I was a bit concerned because it looked a bit over medium-rare yet is was moist and tender! 

The service inside is always stellar.  Outside during busy times service can be spotty.  Be patient it's with the wait!  

Seating options are tables, counter, private dining room and alfresco (weather permitting).  

It's a great little spot that's worth the trip to check out.

One of the best lunch spots in Reno!  

Yes it's a bit CHEESE forward in the menu but it name!!! 

They offer to-go and dine in.   This existed pre-COVID and falls in line with current guidelines.   

So you enter .... there are 2 line ... take out is closest to the door and dine in is to the right.  

Take out order.  Wait. Foods ready you go! 

Dine in order.  Find a seat.   There are socially distant seats in side or if your lucky you can score alfresco seating out on California Street!  

The menus consists of salad, sandwiches and entrees.  Plus amazing desserts!  Nice wine list.   Make sure you ask about the specials.  Rumor has it the lasagna special is AMAZING!!!!

My lactose intolerant self -- loves the tacos!!!

YELPERS proclaimed the best pizza in town - Truth! 

My Aunt insisted the owners are from Brooklyn, hence the pizza should be great - Not so true.  The owners are from Orange NJ.  A pizza maker in Brooklyn said the made the best pizza.  Yes the pizza was great! 

Dining for a Cause -  They train and staff people with disabilities - Truth! 

The joint was jumping on Saturday.  We called in our order.  Not sure if we arrived early but the pizza was not ready. Mom had a quick chat with the owner re: NJ. I went to get ice cream but that's another review. 

NY Pizza Large with sausage and mushrooms.  This is the 1st pizza I've had in Reno that is truly NY style. The crust was perfect and even had toasted bubbles on the crust.  The sauce was perfect not too sweet.   Mushrooms were fresh; ok I do kinda like the canned ones but this is not a complaint.  Garden salad was good it had pepperoni on it (who knew pepperoni grew in Reno) but I did miss the Peperoncino-not a complaint just a suggestion.  

The good:  
It was all good 

The not so good:  
It's no where near where I live and my Aunt is moving in July.   
Seating can be tight. 

It's worth the trip and the wait for a table!

Pine Street Reno NV = Little Portlandia! 

The latest in the Portland invasion is Pine State Biscuits!  

I've been waiting for this spot to open all summer.   Well worth the wait!    And wait you will if you arrive after 845AM.  The line spills out the street.    It's worth it!  

How it works 
Wait in line or got straight to the counter.  
Order, Pay, Get a number 
Coffee & Water is self serve 
Grab and seat
Food will be delivered to the table 
Eat & enjoy
Bus your table when done
Leave when ready

What I've eaten 

Reggie Deluxe sans cheese.   Biscuits it's in the name of the joint so when in Rome; right! -- butter, flaky, yum!  Fried chicken - white meat so juicy I forgot I don't like white meat! -- fried crispy not greasy.  Plus a fried egg - next time I will ask for the egg over easy - this one was firm.  Smothered in gravy - best gravy I've had west of the south.  Come hungry and skip your next meal.  

Brisket Biscuit- it was Friday's special plus it's fun to say out loud.  The brisket was good but I missed the gravy - if you're not a gravy fan this might be your sando if it comes up again.  

Seasonal Pop Tart - S'mores.  Flaky pastry crust stuffed with chocolate Grenache topped with homemade toasted marshmallows.   I think next time I'll ask them to bring it out 10 minutes after my savory order comes out.   Always good but better HOT! 

Great addition to the downtown area.  Can't wait to work my way through the rest of the menu and try the bloody Marys!

It is like I died & went to bakery heaven!

After 4 years of living out west I can finally give up bagel thins & chain bagel shops.  Definitely the best bagel above sea level!!! They got it right crunchy shell and doughy inside.  Pumpernickel & Rye Swirl are my favorites!   So good I'll over look the fruit bagels.....I'm a purest the only fruit I like in a bagel are raisins!

The donuts are so light & fluffy.  A brawl almost broke out because I only bought one Lemon Poppy Seed donut!   So well received with my family I didn't get a taste.  The donut hole I had while filling my order melted in my mouth.  The Fat Bastard aided my uncles's recovery from surgery ok on medical proof in that one but it made him smile.  

Not a Cronut - since I hail from the birth place of the Cronut I had my reservations but the one I got to taste was drizzled the chocolate and filled with pillowy pastry cream.  The raspberry & orange we hits at a dinner party.  

The breakfast sandwich or a toasted bagel with a smear are the best ways to start the day.  Can't wait to try more of the menu!

I love me some Poke.

How it works -
Step 1 choose a bowl - regular (3 scoops of protein, Large (5 scoops), Tofu 
Step 2 chose a base - rice (brown/white). Greens, wonton chips 
Step 3 pick- octopus, salmon, scallop, shrimp. Tofu, tuna, yellowtail 
Step 4 pick a sauce 
Step 5 pick toppings -- too many to list (see website for full listing)

Dessert - macaroon ice cream sandwiches - they're premade and mass produced but the yummy!

They have a frequent flyer program but I was not asked to participate.  Normally, I would've asked but I was bringing dinner to my Pop and it's never a good idea to keep him waiting for food.  

Pops bowl was brown rice (he hates it but it's good for him) with octopus, shrimp and salmon topped with crab and the most basic veg they offered.  He loved it.  Ate the entire thing. Said he'd have it again. High praise from a steak and potato kinda guy.  

I got brown rice with tunas and octopus topped with crab, seaweed salad and veg.  The poke took me back to the supermarkets in Hawaii--judge me if you like but my friend who's a local turned me on to the best ones! 

The only beat thing is limited seating and long lines!

Sparks Coffee Shop seems to be another local spot I'd never hear of.  I hate to admit that when book club said we were meeting there, my 1st thought was I don't want to go to Sparks.  What makes this even funnier is it's only a 12 minute drive from my home.   

Warning if you go on a Sunday which I did, the place will be packed with families, church goers and people that just don't want to cook breakfast/brunch/lunch. 

Let's start with coffee as breakfast tends to--they service coffee and espresso drinks in cups the size of soups bowls.  I loved this place the second the coffee was served.  

Per my book Club, they are known for their French toast and waffles.  They are enormous!  Got hungry or share with a friend.   I opted for the BLAT - perfectly cooked bacon, fresh lettuce and tomato and creamy avocado with fries. Very good! 

The staff was slammed but on top of everything.  We requested straws before the server could leave the table, two other servers rushed our table from each side with fist full of straws.   That's great service. 

You might need to wait for a table but it's worth it!

Horrible!! Just absolutely horrible!! My wife and I went to Royal China for lunch and how things have changed. We got there around 11:20 and ordered our food by 11:35. There were only another table there so food should come out quick right? Wrong!. As the place starts to fill up, we noticed that tables around us were getting their soup and appetizers while we're still waiting for our food. The owner said our food takes a lil longer cause it had to be steamed. But waited over 30 mins is a long time. Finally our first entree arrived...along with the table next to us that ordered the same thing. So either my food was overcooked or the other table food was undercooked. As entrees starts to roll out, we can tell that 1. All our food was over steamed cause it was very mushy. And 2. Its been sitting in the kitchen for awhile because the food was sticking to each other. Food was either very mediocre or bad. Had to return some entree cause it taste sour. Some tables around us was getting annoyed because food was coming out really slow. But strange there was a big party that had alot of steamed food and their food came out before mine. (My cousin inlaws was at that table so I know). An hour and a half in and we still didn't get all out order so we told the waitress to packed it all to go. We had enough. We left and went ordered some dim sum from Panda King and ate it at home. Tasted wayyy better. I used to like this place but my wife and I are never coming back. I would rather order take out from Panda King or even go buy dim sum from the grocery freezer isle then to dine in and have such an horrible dining experience. 

And as for the waitress at Royal China, she was walking around with her face mask right under her bottom lip exposing her nose and mouth while taking orders. Not safe at all.

First time ever at El Vez. Why? Because it's across the street from Sampan. However my dining companion insisted on Mexican going on and on about a guacamole craving so I acquiesced. 

Made a reservation so we didn't have to wait. The vibe as many others have noted is definitely cool. Who do I have to be to snag one of those gold velvet tufted plush ass banquets??? Oh well, my stripped booth was just as spacious and comfy. 

Vibe aside, I ordered chips and salsa, she got the big mocalete of guacamole. These were very generous helpings of both. I got the Mahi Mahi Crispy Fish tacos, she had the chicken tacos. These were not generous helpings. Quite the opposite. In fact I was shocked that I only received two tacos. At 16.00 that was 8.00 per taco.  At least my sister got three but again very small. Were they at least tasty? Well the red cabbage overpowered the fish in my opinion. If I were to go back it would to sit at the bar. The margaritas were so good. I'd probably stick to nachos as far as food is concerned.

So I guess this and the one with the flashy sign across the street are like some of those trendy tourist trap places in the city to get a cheesesteak at I could careless what it is that's said as Pats is like soo scrumptious the two times I've gotten to visit here in the past decade!

It's Philly so you know parking is going to suck wherever you try to go and if you park in the wrong spot they will ticket you so fast you won't know what hit your car so good luck on that endeavor just make sure you make it back to Pat's because it's just what's sooo good!

They have their own way of saying what you want here so read the signs to figure out what it is that you really want because you know you want everything on your Cheesesteak anyway so just get it wit it!

Cheesesteak oh so yummy like so much so that I wasn't even that hungry when I was passing through here I just remembered how amazing it was when I came here years ago that I just had to come back and get one seeing that I was in the area and who knows when I'll get back to Philly!

Cheesesteak oh so good just get then go to the next window and get fries or pizza fires like I did because what's better than pizza fries and cheesesteak!

There's like a little area to the side that has peppers those huge round ones that are so good when you take huge bites of the peppers and cheesesteak that combo you can't just get anywhere away from Philly!

Pat's is awesome no need to visit anywhere else when I come here but who knows I might have to go to Pat's and some other place in the same day just because I'm here and yeah cheesesteak I love you come to Cali in better ways then you are!

Not family friendly, nor disability friendly.

We came to Brauhaus early on a Sunday evening. My wife and I walked in with my two sons (10 and 7), and the maitre d paid no attention to us as I stood at her station. When I asked her about a table, she told me she was off-duty, and I could sit anywhere I wanted to sit.

We chose a table near the front window, because my younger son is vision impaired and cannot see in dim light. After a few minutes, another employee told us we couldn't sit there, because it was saved for a table for six, even though it was a table for two and a table for four pushed together, and there were other combinations that could have been made in the restaurant. 

I explained to her that my son couldn't see if we took a table deeper in the restaurant -- I even checked by walking back with him. And I explained that we wouldn't be able to eat there if we had to move tables. 

She told us that there was nothing she could do, so we left.

It's the first time that a restaurant in Philadelphia was unwilling to accommodate my son's disability. So very disappointing.

Happy Hour at Morton's The Steakhouse was definitely gratifying.  I started out with a not so  impressive Mojita Cocktail and decided to settle for ice water the rest of the evening, which was was just about on par with the Mojita Cocktail.  The great thing about the evening was the discount priced Bar Bites Menu, from which if you're really selective, you can get quite a deal.  Normally, these menu items are only served to patrons seated at the bar, but because Ann was in a wheelchair with a broken ankle, we were able to be seated at table.

We only had just slightly over an hour before the movie we planned to attend began on the third floor above the restaurant, so the light fare on the Bar Bites Menu was ideal.  The items we selected were the Iceberg Bite-Sized Wedge Salads served with Tomato, Egg, Bacon Bits and Blue Cheese Dressing.  We also had the Petite Filet Mignon Sandwiches Served with Mustard Mayonnaise.  When I left the restaurant after devouring those Bar Bites, and the overall over the top experience, I was feeling like the lyrics of songwriter Pharrell Williams' song "Happy" like a room without a roof.

There are enough businesses that need help in this economy. Take your business elsewhere. The owner acts like an infant and berates patrons. How about you clean up your kitchen and your language and accept some constructive criticism. Your abhorrent use of "retard" will not be condoned.

A neighborhood gem that I've passed many days.  I will not deny myself the pleasure of Mr. Lee's deli any longer!  I had the shrimp burger with just cheese, lettuce and tomato with the parmesan cheese fries.  I was delicious!  Lee's Deli has a few variation of the Philly cheesesteak I can't wait to try. Stop through if you looking for something out of the ordinary.

While writing this review I need to start at the top so that I provide the details that accompany what I'm about to tell you.

It was last night (Friday) and all I wanted all week was a blind onion pizza! Was craving it badly. My guy had been wanting to try Anthony's Chophouse; I let him decide our fate for the evening.

We called ahead and they said there was no wait or need for a reservation. We were sat right away when we arrived. It was dead when we first got there but still had to wait 10 minutes for our server to greet us.  We ordered cocktails of which took 30 minutes to receive. My guy ordered a whiskey neat that was $70. Our server did not disclose the magnitude of the price which I thought distasteful as it was a shock to see on our bill. Guests should be provided a whiskey menu (we asked for one but they are not offered there). Our appetizers came out before our cocktails came. My crab cakes were soggy and undercooked. My wedge salad was so depressing to say the least. It had hardly any dressing, lettuce was old and not crispy, blue cheese seemed old, and it didn't have the wedge salad excitement (it's one of my fav salads to order). My chicken parmigiana was soggy and messy looking but tasted ok. I ate 4 bites and was done with it. My man ordered the filet Oscar style and it was blue inside, completely rare. Now the sides, let me tell you about the sides. We ordered the Mac n cheese and scalloped potatoes. The Mac n cheese was right out of a box, was terrible and had been sitting for quite some time. It looked old and the cheese had hardened. The potatoes had a ton of oil in them. I flipped the jar of them upside down and watched the oil drain out. Was awful! We told our server our complaints about the filet, and the 2 sides and he said "I'll be back" and went to go help other guests while we sat and sat until the side server asked if we were ok and got the manager for us. He took off the fillet but not the Oscar add on lol. He took the sides off and bought us desert.
Now for desert we ordered the 24 layer cake. It was the best part of dinner. With the level of dissatisfaction (8.5/10) a $210 bill was not fun to pay. Nevertheless we tipped our server $65 as it is not in our character to be "those people." 
The verdict: we will NEVER go back and I should have had pizza in the first place.
Always high expectations when coming here, and they always deliver. Top-notch food flavors drinks and service can't be beat.
Great bar atmosphere, or choose the quieter dining room. Great selection of beers, both on tap and in bottles. Great bar style appetizers and food as well as good comfort foods. Great service!

Nice cozy place in downtown pitman. Nice selection of appetizers and meals. The wedge salad was great. The dressing was smooth and the bacon crumbles were so tasty. The duck with cherry demi glace was very good, as well as the penne vodka. Service was good, but do not expect to get in and get out. Food is cooked to order in the open kitchen fresh and hot. It was especially crowded on the night we went because of an event and show at the theater down the road.

Fun brewery located in industrial area with other businesses (hatchet throwing, indoor golf). They have sleep ball and other fun 'boardwalk' decor. The crazy mirrors and historical items as well. Beer selection was good and delicious. Helpful, fun staff.

Another great meal. The steak served on a hot stone, cooked tableside is awesome. Great paella. Great appetizers. The garlic shrimp is fantastic. The red sangria is the best around. The service is impeccable. The Malaga after dinner drink is also a great way to end the night.

After reading all of the glowing Yelps I was looking forward to dining at the Louisiana Bistro. Although I didn't find it to be quite at the 5-star level I wasn't disappointed - it's a solid 4 star restaurant. 

Friend and I had the four course "feed me" dinner - essentially a tasting menu. It's offered as a three, four, or five course meal that does not include dessert. Basically it's a series of small plates. Nothing at all wrong with that. Here's a breakdown of the courses: 

1. Crawfish Bignets with a Cayenne glaze and lemon butter sauce. Excellent! Little balls of deep fried goodness. The slight heat of the glaze was paired perfectly with the creaminess and slight sweetness of the butter sauce. Unearthly fantastic. 

2. Grilled gulf swordfish over a tomato salad with jalapeno hollandase. Yeah, it was as good as it sounds. The fish was perfect - simply perfect. Probably the best of the four courses. 

3. Alligator soup. This one wasn't quite on the level of the other courses but good none the less. It tasted like traditional New Orleans turtle soup - heavy roux based, a little smokey, good spice. In fact if I wasn't told that it was alligator soup I would have guessed turtle. It really tastes the same. As I said very good but not exceptional. 

4. 12 hour braised buffalo short rib (I posted a pic of this one). A perfectly braised short rib is a thing of true beauty and this one qualifies as such. The sauce was described by the chef (with the "feed me" options he visits the table and describes each course) as mixture of traditional southern sweet tomato based barbecue and Caroline mustard and vinegar based sauces. It also stated that it didn't come out exactly as he planned but he was still quite pleased with the flavor. I have to agree! The buffalo rib was served on bed of very good garlic mashed potatoes. Another excellent dish. 

Being very full at this point we decided to pass on dessert. 

As far as the restaurant, it is rater small but that's a good thing. The decor is minimalistic but it does retain the French Quarter charm. You never forget that you are in New Orleans. It's very nice without being formal. 

The only disappointment of the night was the limited and somewhat generic wine list. But I did find a pretty good rioja that paired nicely with the rich, spicy foods. 

Also, service was a bit slow at first but improved as the night progressed. 

Bottom line - this isn't quite a 5-star establishment but it with just a few little twicks (improve the wine list and work just a bit with the waitstaff) it could be.

What a great Mother's Day brunch I had here today! We sampled quite a few items from their brunch menu. I had the eggs Benedict and boy did they look and taste beautiful. Our table also had biscuits and gravy, two the the breakfast platters, French toast, deviled eggs, chocolate and ham and cheese croissants. Oh and the bloody Mary's were the perfect start. Ya I know that sounds like a lot of food but we had to try it all. The food was amazing. We loved the atmosphere of Turchetti's and it is definitely worth the drive from the north side of Indy. I like what they're doing there and am happy to see another great local business succeed. Can't wait to go back for a deli sandwich!

The Black Sheep is a true family owned local restaurant.  The dad runs the kitchen and the son manages the front of the house.  It maybe under the radar for people because it is located on a side street, but the food always shine here.  I have been impressed by the ingredients, flavor combinations, and the cooking technique here.  The price was not that cheap for a casual restaurant and do allocate 2 hours if you are not dining from the express menu.  We got the menu A and a few other a la carte items for 2 adults and 2 kids.  

Menu A came with a plump little oyster amuse bouche, topped with some flying fish roe.  Oyster shell was small, but has a deep cup like Kumamoto or Kusshi.  Then came a deconstructed prawn cocktail consisted of lightly dressed fresh greens and 3 poached and chilled prawns.  A large seared scallop came next, served on top of carrot orange reduction infused with cardamon and vanilla.  I would not have thought of that flavor combo, but it works.  The seared branzino had crispy skin and tender flesh and the rustic ratatouille and sweet chutney were flavorful enough to shine as well.  Lastly, the dessert was a perfectly poached tender peach topped with grand Marnier mousseline.  

For the a la carte items, we got 2 orders of ribs because it was too good to order just one.  The soy glaze on top was sweet and rich.  The bones on the ribs slide cleanly from the meat, but the meat was tender, not overcooked.  I sound like a broken record here, but I hate over braised pork, which takes on a stringy and dry texture, and many pulled pork dishes from various restaurants are guilty of.  Duck confit taquitos were also delicious and shoyu ramen, while not authentically Japanese, had a flavorful made from scratch broth.  Most of the time, I prefer the lighter shoyu broth or shio broth to a rich and gelatinous tonkotsu broth.  There was a snafu with the sequence of our dishes, the ramen and ribs came after the dessert, but I am not picky about sequence if each dish was cooked so well.

A city filled with Spanish architecture finally has a Spanish restaurant.  Like all the other Acme restaurants, the decor was beautiful and hip.  I agree with the other reviewers that the dining room was very loud.  I recommend sitting outside if you want to hear any conversation.  

The food was great and reminded me of the likes of Estadio and Jaleo in Washington DC, however, the menu was not as extensive.  I started with the savory and spicy gilda while the husband opted for the sweet date and chorizo pintxo.  The chicken croquetas was a ball of molten savory cream of chicken in a crunchy coating, served on a smear of tangy avocado puree.  Citrusy marinated olives were good for nibbling in between the dishes.  Husband enjoyed the albondigas, but I thought it was too sour and the meat mixture was overworked.  Pulpo was cooked to a perfect tenderness and sat on top of buttery potato puree, but I would have liked more black garlic.  What can I say, I am a garlic fiend.  The main was secreto served with a trio of tangy scallion vin, rich aioli, and sweet peach chutney.  I had this cut at Barrafina before.  Its fatty, flavorful, and the texture is bouncy and chewy like pork jowl at a Korean bbq.  I wish the serving size was smaller and the price was lower so we have room to try a few more dishes.  We ended the meal with a generous plate of crunchy hot churros served with chocolate, caramel, and raspberry dipping sauces.  I am excited for the only Spanish restaurant in the city and will be back to try other offerings.  I hope they will have some specials like salt cod, razor clam, chorizo in cider, etc.  One thing Loquita needs to work on was the pace.  Everything came out too fast.  Three dishes came out at the same time and didn't leave us much choice in savoring each bite.  One last thing that annoyed me was the bar stool overlooking the kitchen.  The view was awesome, but the chair was bolted down to the floor, and didn't work for a 5'2" shorty like me as I was too far from the table!

The only place where you can get more pizza for less is at Costco, so the value is there.  The store was clean and the pizza came out really fast.  The crust was too doughy for the amount of sauce/cheese/topping.  I told the person making the pizza that I want mushrooms on half of the pizza and when I opened the box at home, there were mushrooms on the whole pie.  I guess I should have type it on the order screen instead assume that a verbal instruction was good enough.  The passion fruit snow bubble was too sweet.  I added more milk at home and got 2 drinks out of it.

I have only been here twice before and both times the fries and the meat were dry.  This time I came at the middle of dinner time and figured the food would be more fresh.  No, still the same limp dry lukewarm fries.  The fried fish was also over fried and dry.  The brisket sandwich was tender, but it was more like pot roast, then bbq brisket.  It didn't taste like it met the smoker.  Overall, Woody's is not that great for bbq.  The best bet for brisket right now is probably Neighbor Tim's.

Went back again to sample other dishes on the menu and it was very satisfying.  Unlike other authentic Chinese restaurants, the service here was actually pretty good.  I liked the cheesy factor in the decor and the vibe.  The variety show on TV made me feel like I was eating at someone's home.  I don't expect most people to like it, but for me, there is definitely some nostalgia that made the food taste better.  
     
Green Sichuan peppercorn fish-tender fish filet, mung bean vermicelli, cucumber, and soy bean sprouts in a spicy and numbing broth.  The green version is lighter, less oily, but more numbing than the red water boiled fish.

Sweet and sour pork ribs-the ribs were fried and coated in a sweet and sour glaze, much better than the thick gloppy red sauce you see in Americanized Chinese sweet and sour pork.

Toothpick lamb-spicy with concentrated flavors of cumin and cilantro.   
 
Lanzhou beef noodle soup-different than the more popular red braised beef noodle soup.  The soup is clear, less oily, and more aromatic.  The thinly sliced beef was interspersed with tendon which resulted in a familiar texture, tender with some bites.

Once upon a time, Santa Barbara had no wood fire Italian pizza, then with the opening of Persona and Lucky Penny, the bar was raised.  Now the bar is raised once more with Bettina.  Owner Brendan Smith used to be a geologist, but his passion for baking prompted him to take a different career path.  I mean, this is the type of story that people make movies out of.  Bettina's pizza starts with 48 hours fermented dough.  The crust was perfection, airy and tender, dotted with leopard spots.  I dare you to show me a more perfect crust in this city.  The toppings were fresh and the flavor combinations were unique.  The classic Margherita was fantastic, but the unusual cauliflower and nduja pizza was even better.  The kids also liked the arancini, which they called cheesy rice balls, and we had to get a second order, after the first disappeared.

I was excited for Santa Barbara's first sit down Caribbean restaurant.  They did a good job of remodeling the old Aldo space and made it light and airy, but still retained the rustic feel with exposed beams and farmhouse tables.  The menu looked tempting, but unfortunately the only two items we enjoyed were lamb meatballs and the side of rice and beans.  The lamb meatballs were seasoned with jerk spice and served with fresh taziki and curry mango chutney.  The rice and beans were excellent and distinctly flavored with kaffir lime leaves and I enjoyed that citrus fragrance.  The plantains needed more cooking time as it came out cold and without much caramelization.  For comparison, the maduros at Cubaneo were much better.  The seafood pepper pot was like a Caribbean bouillabaisse.  It was huge and came with four jumbo head on shrimps, but all the seafood, with the exception of the octopus were overcooked and the shrimps were not at the peak of freshness.  The broth was watery and didn't offer much to complement the seafood and the fishiness of the canned crab meat dominated the flavor of the broth.  Jerk chicken was better than the seafood pot, but I always thought jerk chicken is grilled or smoked to get that smoky flavor, but this was braised or baked and didn't have much flavor besides of the jerk seasoning on the outside.  The chicken was also too mushy from being cooked too long.  

The front of the house had two very friendly albeit inexperienced servers.  There were no manager, hostess, or busser to help those two ladies with seating, rolling napkins, and expediting.  The back of the house, invisible to the guests is likely just as short staffed judging by the cold food and the many apologies to different tables when the food came out the kitchen.  The concept is exciting and it is the only Caribbean restaurant in Santa Barbara, but the execution needs a lot of improvement.

This is a popup restaurant started by the former chef and sous chef of Loquita.  They use the kitchen at Handlebar and only open on Friday to Sunday, 9AM to 1PM.  During the weekday, they also offer family meals that you can pre-order.  I enjoyed the pork belly bao, which is served like a Taiwanese gua bao.  The pork belly was tender and lightly crispy on the edge.  The char shu bao is more like a pan fried or baked bun with nice fluffy wrapper, a little salty, but very satisfying.  The yakisoba would be better with fresh shiitake.  They must use pickled mushroom, which was too sour.  The French toast was great, but tiny for $12, one piece of thick toast instead of two.  I was most looking forward to the tortilla espanola made okonomiyaki style, but this dish did not work for me.  The mushroom and spinach gave out so much water that the whole tortilla was soggy and watery.   I am sure they are still playing with recipes and customer preferences.  Overall, this is an exciting addition to the city serving fusion food with a Korean flair.

This used to be that Turkish lamp, rug, home decor store.  They closed the business a while ago and today I saw a beautiful Turkish coffee and sweets place opened up.  The owner lets you try any Turkish delights and they have dozens of different flavors.  I am sure in time they will have some signs explaining what's in all those beautiful Turkish delights, but for now just enjoy the samples.  We decide to get a box ($30), hazelnut, chocolate banana, honey, and berry flavors.  Quite expensive for what it is, but it is a unique treat that you can't get else where in Santa Barbara.  The baklava was also fresh and syrupy.  The turkish coffee wasn't made the traditional way in a copper pot.  I am guessing it is due to only 3 people working in the shop right now and they can't spare one person just stand next to the coffee and babysit it.

I remembered Buena Onda used to be a popular popup in Goleta and the first in the city to serve Argentinian empanadas.  Unfortunately, I haven't had as many chances to go there after they moved to Santa Barbara.  The empanadas are delicious, and some of my favorites are sweet and creamy humita, garlicky ham and arugula, and tender savory chicken.    They also have many none meat and none dairy varieties to satisfy everyone.  Empanadas are big and filling, 2-3 are plenty per person for a meal.  They now sell family meals and frozen empanadas so you can bake them at home whenever you like.  I hope they make it thru this pandemic and come out better than ever.

The tiny little bakery located behind Casey's garage was packed with people waiting outside on a Sunday morning.  They have birria tacos on the weekend, 3 per order, served with onion, cilantro, grilled pepper, and consume for dipping.  The tacos were so overstuffed that you can make at least 3 more tacos out of the meat.  Service was friendly and prompt, and the price was low for the quality and quantity.  This is a hidden local gem.

I am happy that Masala Spice has dosa, a southern Indian dish that I used to get at The India Club, but was not available in other restaurants around here.  The cauliflower bezul had a very fragrant coconut sauce, but I wish the breading was thinner.  The lunch thali came in generous portions and the price was fine for the area.  However, I didn't find the chicken tikka masala or the palak lamb to be very flavorful.  I also didn't like the texture of the chicken tikka masala, which was too soft from being braised in the sauce for too long.  The naan appeared to be made with whole wheat flour, which is healthier, but didn't have that super soft and fluffy texture that I am used.

We have ordered take-out, delivery, and eaten in this location and the food is generally good! My only complaint is an experience I just had regarding delivery. Last week on Halloween we ordered delivery and everything was fine. Tonight we tried to order and we were told they don't deliver past a 8 mile radius. I explained they delivered here a week prior. The person who answers the phone said that must have been a mistake and they can't delver now. I am now irritated so I ask to speak to the manager to get some clear understanding why this was happening: I was put on hold and when he returned he said the manager was busy and was unable to talk and I could call back later if I wanted to talk to him. I hung up and was amazed by this so I went online to find our we live 7.4 miles away so I called back and the same person answered. I told him we were 7.4 miles away and I wanted to let him know. He verified my address and said they still can't deliver here because his work tablet says 8.6. We won't be spending anymore of our hard earned money at an establishment that is already over priced and has zero customer service skills.
This place is awesome! We were only in Nashville 2 days and went here both days! The beer is great and the food is awesome!
Excellent food Outstanding service reasonable prices going to put this on our list favorite places when we come back.

Stop in with a few friends after calling for reservations.  They said we can seat your group in 30 minutes. Terrific!  We shared the roasted cauliflower. A tasty starter that had some almond & feta flavor. Two of us split the Etch salad & it was split in the kitchen without an up charge that so many restaurants like to do.  The salad had some green apple, blue cheese and a delicious champagne vinaigrette. Followed that with an entree of Lamb Lion & sweet potato korma plus golden spices turnips. Service was excellent.  Etch has a small but interesting wine list.  We truly enjoyed our evening.

Would never return to this establishment. I understand the challenges COVID-19 is presenting for restaurants but Attico is missing the mark. Among my grievances are the fact that I made a reservation for 4:30 and though there were only a few guests, the hostess tried to seat me and my friend in the back of the restaurant. She walked us past numerous empty tables to put us in the back, with no view of the skyline whatsoever. Might as well as have been sitting in a basement. We didn't consent to that so they miraculously found us another table despite having other reservations. For whatever reason, those other reservations mattered more than ours. 
The food was fine I guess - the sauce for the chicken wings seems like it's vinegar based so that was weird and not enjoyable. The drinks were small but tasty and strong. My friend enjoyed his burger. I didn't mind the fries. 
Because of COVID, we now all have to adhere to dining times and our meal was due to be up at 6pm. We were not allotted more time despite their snafu with finding us a proper table. The host came to the table with our check, bypasses me, and tells my male friend that it's time to start wrapping up. Funny choice because I was the one paying. Why not speak to both of us or drop it in the middle the table? Quite sexist. 
Oh and when we left, the tables with better views were still vacant so still not sure why we couldn't have utilized them. 
Basically, from beginning to end, this was an invitation to NOT come back.

Can't believe I never left a review for cafe du monde. Pre covid, I'd fly down from Dallas for weekend and eat everything. My usual schedule is hit up cafe du monde early before the line gets long. 

I get a bag of three beignets and a bottle of water. Then I find a bench by the body of water behind the wall outside their shop. The view, beignets, life is amazing! I prefer the beignets warm. Recommend shaking the bag up first to get the powder sugar coated on all beignets. Sometimes they just throw the beignets in the bag. I don't eat beignets anywhere else because this place has my heart. Everything is cheap, a bag of 3 for less than $4. 

CASH ONLY

I thought I would like this place but I didn't. I was visiting NOLA and I came here specifically for the affogato. The picture looked enticing but I was disappointed. Perhaps it was the bad attitude from the barista in the short curly hair and the glasses. I regret tipping her. She was already in a bad mood before I came along so I know it had nothing to do with me. The original cashier had to go to the back to get something. I didn't mind waiting but the barista insisted to take my order in a bad mood. "what would you like?" in an annoyed tone. Um...hi? I would like less attitude for no reason, please. Out of everybody in New Orleans, she was the only pissy mood one. Everybody was so friendly and culture from what I saw. This place is out of the way, I don't know if it's worth the trip. The affogato I got was less than stellar judging from my previous affogato experiences. They definitely "Americanized" it. NO! you should not "Americanized" anything Italian! I have never had an affogato with chocolate syrup all over the mug like that before. I gave it a try and I didn't like it. It was way too sweet and took away the espresso flavor. Affogato should be simple with just a scoop of vanilla ice cream and a shot of espresso, MAYBE chocolate shaves on top. They tried to do too much in theirs, it wasn't good to taste. I think you would like it if you didn't have other great affogatos. I did like the coffee ground on top though. It was a nice touch but leave the syrup out.

I've never been to a casino where I consistently lost everytime I went except for Parks. Odds are stacked heavily in favor of the casino. Which is why I don't go there any longer, even though it's 5 minutes from my home.

You've been warned. This place is over priced, has horrible service, and what's worse the food made one daughter sick AT THE TABLE, and the other daughter refused to eat her favorite food in the world, shrimp, after only a single bite!? Was talked into salmon, menu said $16 but on the check was charged $26 each? Explained the problem with food and check and was only given a dirty look and the check for $90! No offer to remake, remove foul items from check, or anything!? We only ordered the fondue, which tasted dirty and smelled, 2 salmons, and an appetizer shrimp with 1 ice tea that also had a weird smell to it. For $90? And there is no atmosphere, this place is a dump inside and out. I would never refer even someone I hated to eat here. (Okay, maybe someone I really hated, but they would have to have killed my dog or something major like that.) Like I said, you've been warned.

Next to one of my favorite crepe places, I just had to stop in and check out what "Butter and Salt" were doing with a new store front.

I know it's a cliché to say..."It's just like being in San Francisco".  And it's a little insulting.  But to be totally honest, that is exactly the feel I got of the place the first time I went in.

Prices were a little higher.  The place was set up very similarly to so many shops I have been in across the country.  I literally could take the whole footprint of the Bakery and drop it into downtown Chicago or SF or New York and the place would have a line out the door.  

The toasts that they make on the daily basis are what elevates them from just another Reno place, to a place that makes you realize just how cool Reno is.

The Salmon Toast was soo good looking I almost couldn't stop taking pictures and it was of course perfect when I finally got around to eating it.  

Parking here sucks.  Don't park next door.  They will tow you.

Two Olives walk into a bar.
The bartender slides over a bowl of bar nuts and asks..."What'll you have?"
One olive says to the other.
"What's with this guy, can't he see that I'm stuffed?"

We finally got around to getting down here.  We were in the neighborhood a little early for dinner with friends and decided to check them out.  I was still "stuffed" from sushi earlier in the day so I couldn't go hog wild on trying everything that looked good.  But the guy encouraged me enough to try one or two things.  I really want a good olive oil for my salads at work....but I just couldn't decide.

But I DID decide on a great balsamic.  It was on sale (of course) and now I have a bottle to come back and get refilled for a lower price!  Sweet!

Can't wait to come back and try the food service and see just what they offer.

Father's Day was the best day to check out the new digs at Noble Pie.   I'd been reading about this for a while.   So just wanted to see the inside.  And boy is the new place gorgeous!  This place is going to a hopping location on the nights when all the businesses are open.  Like a nightly block party.  

I also had never had the Frachos and Ly mentioned them so yes!  Also grabbed some zepps and wings.  All totally spot on and up to the Noble level of awesome.  

Service was good too.  Only the second day and everything seemed to be working smoothly.   

Pro Tip.  Know your beer before you get in line to order.  Or just order at the bar.  The beautiful large bar.  

And what a plus having Piñon next door.

I've never been to the original or knew much about it.  So much so that I actually thought the original was in New York.  So when I went in, I was a total noob.

I wasn't super hungry but I needed to do something.  I decided to get the pastrami and soup combo.  Fairly priced and not too much food.  The sandwich was a bit dry, but I loaded it with mustard.  The soup was as expected for Matzo Ball soup.  Maybe a little less salty than I expected so that was a plus.  We take too much salt in these days.

My daughter got a hot dog and asked for the kraut and onions on the side.  The kraut still came out on the dog.  Back it went, and then came out pretty quick.  I'm pretty sure they didn't just scrape everything off.  It didn't taste like kraut at all.

I did, however, get the kraut and put it on my sandwich.  Which was a good choice.  They had some Dr. Browns sodas in the cooler and Kiwi tried one, it's not very carbonated so if you like bubbles, go with something else.

Smoke didn't seem to be coming in too much, but this was the daytime so I can't promise that the smoke situation will be as good during a high gambling time of the day.

Pro-Tip - If you know your directions.  The northwest corner of the Silver Legacy street level is the closest door to Canter's so you can miss the long crazy trek we made trying to find it.

Packed with people. The bar held their own.  Lots of space here to bring a good sized group. This was their big sneak peek day.   Loads of bar space and some great patio out the side.  A good number of communal tables should be fine for any sized party. Love the huge front door.  


All three beers were good beers. The IPA had the most unique flavor profile.   Not tooo hoppy but still flavorful. The vodka was smooth and went down like velvet.  The bottle is cool but the logo makes it look like a well bottle.  Hopefully they will do something different.  

I'm sure that since this was just a sneak peek, the service will be just fine when all the taps are flowing and the staff has gotten used to the workspace. 

Parking right now is street parking and plentiful.  So get down there and enjoy it while it's just starting out!

Finally, after years of trying to make it to Daughters Cafe, we made it through the door for a meal.  Of course we had to make it a special dinner meal where there is a lecture that comes with dinner.

Daughter Cafe has been running a lecture series all last year and into this year.  Not sure if they are going to continue the series but this last one was very entertaining.  It was about Lewis and Clark.  Lots of stuff I knew, but tons more I didn't know.

As for the food, it was great.  The set menu for the dinner was a caper mustard sauce salmon with a arugula blueberry salad and succotash.  Served with wonderful rolls.  The portions were very filling and surprisingly I ate the whole thing.  Everything was properly cooked and the salad was perfectly dressed in my opinion, not too much not too little.
