And I had never had succotash before so I can't really compare it to anything.  But it was tasty and everyone at my table finished theirs.

The ambiance of the place is what you would expect from a home turned into a restaurant.  Not a ton of space but enough for the "ladies who lunch" crowd.  It's very authentic feeling, and how we sat last night with all the tables pushed together, made it feel a little basque.  I regret having not made it in here before.  For some reason I had the sense that this place was more posh than it is.  It's not posh, it's homey and warm.  It's lovely people making very lovely food.

I can't really comment on the prices for this trip because of it being a special event.  But I'm hoping to make the one or two of the remaining lectures.  The speaker (I'm horrible with names) had a good sense of humor and kept it interesting.

Parking is street parking so just be aware of the places you park.  It's close enough to downtown to be under the scrutiny of the parking patrol.

Stopped in for a quick take away lunch.  I over-ordered as I always do when I go to a new place...especially a new place that serves goat tacos!  The goat tacos were wonderful, tender and tasty.  And as I said I over-ordered.  I ate the entire #1 combo of taco, torta and enchilada.  It came with some of the best refried beans I have had in Reno.  For my meat I chose the Asada.  The small size of the bits of meat was taco perfection, almost like ground beef but not quite.

Service was quick and I was in and out pretty quick even though the place was reasonably busy.

"It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown upon the soil, though it is smaller than all the seeds that are upon the soil, yet when it is sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants and forms large branches; so that the birds of the air can Nest under its shade."

The inspiration for the name of this business is so perfectly appropriate.  From a small location at Cal Neva to this slightly larger and more fitting location, the Mustard seed is on it's way to housing all of the hungry birds that midtown may supply.  

The longtime master chef Robert took a second to answer my questions after our lunch.  His experience in the Reno food scene started in the 1980s. Working at various casinos and their respective steak houses, opening restaurants in Southern California for well known name brands, and being trained by world renowned chefs, he has developed the chops to run an efficient and successful restaurant. And if my first visit, on the second day open is any indication,  he will be giving Reno a great southern menu with a pleasing atmosphere and friendly service. 

Our food and service was better than I expected, especially so close to the doors opening for the very first time.

Sam, our waiter was friendly, helpful and ready to make our lunch a satisfying adventure. Admittedly I was a little needy this time around, forgetting to ask for this or that but his response was just right every time.  With others staff stopping by the table, it was refreshing to see the newly opened intensity being displayed with such calm. 

Our food was very good.  Three large fish nuggets held their heat through the whole lunch.  Her Bayou Blackened Burger, while being a little light on the "bayou" was super duper tasty on the blackened factor. Robert did mention that if you like spicy just let your waiter know and they can add a notch or two of spice.  I also did my usual over order of sides and apps.  The fried green tomatoes were of course delicious and the collard greens were solid, less meaty than some places, but still good flavors. 

This is a glowing 6 star review for a brand new place.  Darn Yelp for restricting me to only 5 stars. But really it's no surprise that this place is so good when you consider one of his past posts was a stint at Western Village Steakhouse. 

A few notes.
Beer and wine will be available by the end of the week and the liquor license is in the works and looks to be a few months out.

I love Yelp.

I love how it's become the "Yellow Pages on Steriods".
I love how they actually try and keep the reviews useful.
But most of all.
I love the cool people I have been able to meet through Yelp.

A group of those people decided to get together and try out Morgan's together.  That way we can get more "bang" for our adventure buck.  We were able to share the hell out of the meal and get way deeper into the menu.  I was still hesitant because the prices at lobster places are higher than what I like to pay.  But when I looked at the menu, I realized that this was just a little higher...not 50% higher like I expected.

With 6 of us on table, we were able to try...
Cioppino
Lobster Roll (wow!)
Salmon Burger 
Sliders
Reuben (my favorite)
Crab Roll
Lobster Mac
Fries
Ahi Poke App
Crab Cakes
Bread Pudding

All of it was well worth the price paid.  I totally will go back and make this a "splurge" night.  I regret that I never got into the Truckee location now.  I could have been enjoying this great food all this time.  If I was pressed to say what was my favorite it would have to be the Reuben rich and decadent.  

Service was just fine and friendly.  It's nice to see a recently opened place firing on all cylinders and running smoothly.

The decor isn't fancy at all.  The prices might suggest "date night" but the atmosphere is bright with clean lines and open space, which did lead to some louder than desired moments.  There is an upstairs space that might be a bit better for the date crowd.  The patio looks really inviting and will be awesome with some sort of fireplace that is already planned.

Visitor Index=Day 3

Salt.  Mountains and mountains of salt. Hell even the salad dressing has a sea full.  

We went because my daughter finds the fettuccine alfredo to be fetching. She played her last soccer game that day and I guess we lost our minds. Pasta for me is rare treat.  I usually save up my pasta splurges for a fancy pizza or a few other local places. But sometimes a dad is just a sucker for his daughter. 

Olive Garden has been reviewed tens of thousands of times over the years.  If you have read those reviews.  Good for you.  But why in the hell are you reading this one then?  

Anyway. Our server was great.   Our food was fancy!!  I mean Sous Vide to order for $11!!  Some Foodies have paid WAAAAY more than that to have their food boiled on a bag. 

One "pro" to eating at a chain like Olive Garden?   No need to take pics of the food.  They already did that back at the factory.

There is always space for a little backstory.  I'm on this new fangled website called "The Facebook".  And on this Facebook place they have a "Reno Foodies" group.  Lots of nice and some nasty people there.  And one day I saw this guy Kevin post on a few threads.  He sounded really cool and then a few days later he posted a sandwich that he had made from a Rounds Bagel and some Short Ribs they had at the restaurant where he is the chef. Chef?  He works at Zozo's?  I've been told that place is great now this cool guy works there too?   At that point I asked my wife if Italian was ok for lunch and we were off in just a few minutes.  No point in wasting time!

They are located in a strip mall off of Lakeside.  I used to live in this area in my "first apartment" days.  Not really a great place to be after midnight, but not really a bad place to be during the normal times of the day.  Parking here is a little funky but totally workable and I doubt that it is so full you can't find parking in the lot.

When we walked in we were surprised to see that the place was truly a kitschy looking Italian restaurant.  Adorned with empty wine bottles and plastic grapes this place could easily be a set for the next romantic comedy filmed in Reno.  Heck it even has the red and white checkered tablecloths.  Now don't get me wrong, I think this would be a great setting for a nice date if the noise levels don't rise too much.  We have lots of "fancy" date places in town that suck for a romantic dinner for two.  So this place even though it may not be super chic....still could be a good spot for a date night.

For our food choices, my wife ordered up the Risotto Shrimp off the lunch menu and I had the "off menu" short rib sandwich lunch special.  I liked my bite of her food, but my sandwich was simple.  It had a horseradish mayo, arugula super soft french roll and the short rib beef.  It came to my table open faced so I added some fresh grated parm, closed the lid and dug in. It wasn't a huge massive production but it was a very satisfying sandwich of perfection.  The inspiration was on a bagel, but I honestly think I got the better deal.  The whole thing melted in my mouth in such an elegant way....I can't imagine the bagel would be better than this.

Normally when we try a place for the first time we pound out a few "gauges" to see how they stand up.  But this meal was so good, no gauges needed to be checked.  We will return to get our Tiramisu and our Lasagna.  This time we tried the cheesecake and it was a great ending to the meal.

They officially opened today.  We wanted to be there at the opening but just couldn't make it.

So instead we went in a little later at about 10 hoping to miss the biggest part of the rush.  I don't think that worked.  The line was still decent sized and pretty time-consuming.  Not sure if this is by design because it keeps the tables turning, or if they will get a little swifter with processing the people at the register because Reno will get used to the menu and know what they want.

You walk in and order.  THEN you sit down.  Not before, no "scoping out tables" while someone else does the ordering.  There is a pretty big sign telling you not to do that.

No big menu to crane your neck up at.  For now, it's just a stack of well-designed menus to look through that are a perfect size for individual perusing and they have more than enough for everyone.   But look over the menu completely.  You may find something on that page you would be surprised to find.

After you order you get your pumps of coffee and find a seat.  Even though they were busy the seating situation wasn't bad, this probably is by design with keeping people in the line.  I'm wondering if this kind of action will go over well in Reno.  Or will they just be fine after the initial interest wanes and they get into a groove.  I forsee this place being very popular.  

You get a fancy table tag with your order number on it to take to your table for the food to be delivered.  Eventually your food will come out.  For our food, it was maybe a little faster than expected but not insanely quick.

I ordered up the Shrimp and Grits.  The dish was full of flavor and the grits were soooooooooo heavenly.  The grits were almost like a quality risotto.  Shrimp was perfect and the egg that I added was a great addition.

My wife ordered up the Moneyball and didn't share.  But neither did I.  I cleaned my plate of every measurable morsel of food.

The interior was all brand new!  Go figure.  ;)  Anyway, I would call the atmosphere "Elevated Fast Food".  Not completely devoid of character, but more about clean lines and clean surfaces than quirkiness.  This isn't a negative at all.

Plan on spending about an hour total to park, order, get food, eat and leave unless they are super busy.

So welcome Pine State Biscuits!  Looking forward to trying out those wedge salad options.

There is literally nothing wrong with a 3 Star Review.  It's A-OK!  It's neither indictment nor is it high praise.  It's just a place to get food that won't outright suck.

And right now, that's pretty much where I think I should leave it.  I've been twice and the food hasn't been anything worth noting.  The egg rolls have been near cold both times.  I think the density and the flavors would be there if they were hotter.  

The decor of the place hasn't changed too much since it was Cafe de Thai, it's still very nice and pleasant.  Maybe a little more comfortable with less hard surfaces.  

The service both times was fine.  It seems that they may still be working out the flow of the space and how to handle it all.  The servers themselves come across as really attentive and hard working.  

When I'm in the mood for dinner and someone says, how about An?  I will say...

OK

I'd Tap that.

Yeah I said it.  It was lame but I said it.

Wowzers.  What a great place to go and try about a billion different beers!  Not a huge beer fan, but they had some ciders on tap too.  But with having lots of beer loving friends I am sure I will hit this place up a bunch!  And you never know...with all these beers on tap I just might find a beer that I like.

Love the cool screens and the long bar and the women behind the counter were really friendly.  And I think I may have overheard that you can bring in food from surrounding businesses.

So yeah...even though Beer NV isn't my type...I'd still tap that.

Once upon a time...years ago, pop-ups were happening all over Reno.  A food artist would be "here" and then make something "there".  It was a grand golden age for foodies...way back in 2015....but alas, the work involved and the money made just didn't seem to justify the endeavor.  So now we are more returned to the status quo....almost.  In the place of the temp pop up, we have the growth of "space sharing" with businesses.  From Deluxe giving Thali a place to get a foothold in the scene in Reno to Vertical Roasters having space inside of Crafted Pallet 6 days a week we have people making creative decisions to find space for their businesses that benefit them, and the communities they are in.

That being said...The Pizza Collective is teamed up with Sol Kava and taking some of their square footage to add to the West Street Market.  The little funky mall doesn't lose any space while gaining an extra business to bring in the groups who have different palates and picky eaters.  "I want Vegan!"  "I want Indian!" "I want Pizza" "I want a Bowl!"  "I want a Sandwich!" The West Street Market has it all and Pizza Collective is a great addition.

The pizza oven itself moved from a classic Pizza restaurant in San Francisco.  A big blue brick piece of art that can't be missed!

The Collective part of the name may be referencing all of the wonderful local and nearby regional food sources that are being used to make the pizzas.  I like the open and honest informing of the customer of where the food comes from.  It doesn't just say "locally sourced" and then have one thing be from Lattin Farms.  Instead, they take the time to list each ingredient and it's source, which is worth a little bump in cost, knowing there is more effort being put into making this pizza instead of unboxing it from a US Foods truck.

The pizzas don't really seem to have names, at least at this time.  They just have a few different pies for choosing based on the available ingredients.  Our pie had parsnips, onion, mozzarella, cowgirl wagon wheel(?), rosemary and stinging nettle and pine nut pesto. It was good if a little muted in the wow factor of intensity that my brain is used to with pizza.  We sat at the bar, but there is tons of seating at the West Street Market.  I'm pretty sure they will bring your pie to you no matter where you sit, probably even outside or in Thali, these businesses seem to get along very well.

It's not really a fancy date location, but really who thinks pizza for a fancy date?  However, this would be a great place to have a more casual date or even hang out with friends and eat up.

I know this was long-winded.  I appreciate you making it to the end.

Protip:
Don't forget to get some Kava with your pizza.  Sol has some great stuff.

Happy Hour
This is based solely on my Happy Hour experience.  I can't speak for the regular menu at all.  I have never been.  But an acquaintance had mentioned that The Grill had some pretty good happy hour prices, so I decided to try it out.

We came in and decided to sit at the bar...the TV was right there to follow the game when our mouths were full.  And it seems you can always get a good vibe for a whole place if you are able to sit at the bar and see how things flow.  The gentleman behind the bar was professional and welcoming.  I felt more like a local at a local spot than I expected.  The Happy Hour Menu is tiered and each price point moves you into more substantial fare.  We decided on some Clams, Pot Stickers, Poke and some glasses of wine.

Nothing stood out in a good or bad way.   It was all pretty solid but nothing too surprising.  I know that The Grill has been around for a long time, so they need to make sure their menu matches the regular tastebuds that are constantly filling the seats and the register.

The clams were hit and miss, but overall I would have to say the Poke was the best of the three dishes.  

The atmosphere at the time was way early dinner so I can't vouch for it being a dinner date place.  It's definitely not super casual.

I probably wont be heading back anytime soon based on my personal experience, but I wouldn't rule it out if someone was insistent on going there for dinner.  And maybe then I will try one of their cocktails.

I'm not going to rave about this place.  I'm not going to tell you about their excellent sushi and their excellent service.  I'm not going to tell you that Rodrigo, Gerson, Jonothan, David and Duc (?) are super skilled and friendly chefs.  I'm not going to say that you will get a life-changing experience here.  Because I cannot guarantee those things every time that you might go in.

Instead, I am going to wow you with my photos!  (here is where you look through all of the photos I have posted to Yelp for Hinoki.  I will wait, imagine I am whistling a catchy tune while you peruse the images of tasty sushi).  Ok.  Wow!!  Weren't those amazing?  Did you see that shot of the Ikura?  I could almost eat my computer!  And how about all those pieces of nigiri?!?  And those rolls.  Those rolls looked sooooo good.  Didn't they?

And now that you have seen the amazing photos.  Remember this.  Sushi restaurants have so many different palates to please.  Some people love crystal shrimp and mayo.  Others don't.  Some people order what's on the menu, and some look at the menu and change a few things.   Some people just go in and annoy the hell out of the chef and say "make me something good."  I'm that last guy...I know I'm annoying.  But I also know that I have sat in front of most of these sushi chef's for years.  Developing a rapport that allows me to give them the freedom of making me something good.  They know I don't like cream cheese.  They know I like the nigiri and ponzu.  They have a good feel for the flavors that make my eyes light up when I take that first bite.

So will you get that experience the first time you walk in?  Or even the second or third?  Probably not.  The best way to enjoy yourself at any sushi restaurant is to go in and sit at the bar and get a feel for the chef and the place.  Sure, you are taking a risk, it is an expensive meal and you may get a dud for a chef (unlikely at Hinoki).  But it's just part of the whole Reno Sushi experience.  Next, communicate as best as you can.  If you don't like something or you have a favorite roll.  Tell them.  Introduce yourself and your companions.  Don't just sit there treating them like some servant.  And above all be appreciative of what they do!  They stand for hours and hours a day, rolling this stuff.

And if all else fails.  Invite me and we can go have some killer sushi together.

Now don't get me wrong.  There are some details that I have to pass along.

The Beer.  EVERY SINGLE PLACE has that crappy beer we all know will be at every Asian place.  What Hinoki has done is bring something better to the table!  Right now they have two Ballast Point beers and I am overjoyed.  The Habanero Sculpin compliments the sushi so well.

The servers are great! (so I lied) I wish I could call them all out by name because they are so good at what they do.  But instead, I will just say they all rock!

And now for my one negative.  Because reality has positives and negatives.  And the negative here is that I just haven't been impressed with their sake selection.

And yes, I've even had the non-sushi lunch!  The Chicken Teriyaki was so good.  Priced just right and came out in enough time for a lunch break.

Thanks for reading!  See you at Hinoki!
