I'm usually an early adopter.  This time it was different.  I was underwhelmed by the name choice.  I know, lame reason to not try a place.  But then I had some mixed reviews coming in from my friend feed.  Even though one friend was RAVING about it like it was the greatest thing since Dylan took over 1864.  I just wasn't feeling it yet.

But then that friend took us over there and we had a quick late night bite.    I had the wings...the fantastic Sticky Thai Chicken Wings.  Big, meaty and perfectly cooked with a Caesar Salad with actual anchovies.  My wife had the burger that was so good she didn't share.

The next two times I went in, it was for the most excellent Happy Hour.  Maybe....arguably....the best Happy Hour in Reno.  For the time being, they have a great $5 price on a very extensive menu.

1-10 scale
Irish Nachos - 8 surprisingly good.
Anchovie Toast - 10 salty-tangy-savory heaven
Street Tacos - 8 my daily selection was a white fish
Curried Chicken Lettuce Wraps - 7 Good Cold dish
Falafel - 6 Very different texture than I would expect
Sticky Thai Chicken Wings - 10 Best in Reno?!
Cup of Seasonal Soup and Grilled Cheese - 8 This is awesome
Cavatapi Mac and Cheese - 7 Nice menu staple
Wagyu Bulgogi Lettuce Wraps 5 - Not my thing I expected either sweet or spice
Jalapeno-Cheddar Fritters - 10 aka clouds of tasty mouth wow
Scotch Eggs - 10 Perfection

On top of that we had some of the different drink offerings at 1/2 off Happy Hour pricing.  The seasonal/daily cocktail was great both times.

**Disclaimer**  Please call before you head down looking for this menu at these prices.  Happy Hours can change at any time, but this review could be up for months or even years.  Just please check ahead of time.

Having sat at the bar two of the first three times I have been in, I can totally vouch for the service from Leala.  She is very good at her craft and does a great job of engaging everyone that comes in.  No sour looks or eye rolls just friendly service.

Parking after 5 is free just a block away in the courthouse parking lot.  During the day you have your choice of street paid parking.  The spots are almost never all taken.  There are also three TV's above the bar, this can be a good thing or a bad thing depending on what the picture of your evening is intended to be.  

The menu is exciting and yet still conservative enough to bring your old stick in the mud friends.  I can't wait to get back down there for another Happy Hour....dang it, too late today.

My belly is full.   The advertising is spot on.  

Fin.

Fine.  I've got some Elite cred to maintain.

It's almost like I could just walk in, close my eyes and point and I would get a great sandwich here.  This last time I ordered up the Dirka Dirka.  And the gal suggested the Jalalpeño Cheese bread to go with it.  Yes.  They know what they are talking about.  That was delightful.  Also had the super tasty chicken dumpling soup.  It was a creamy soup, I was expecting a more clear broth..but boy oh boy it was gooo....oooood.  

This place is always that way.  Good to the last bite, tasty to the last bit.  Service is lunch counter get your grub and get goin kinda service.  Nothing to complain about and nothing Oh My God we have to give them our firstborn child.  Just sturdy service!

Heck I think I like these guys so much I can even overlook their use of the word sando.....almost.

Get the 1/2 sandwich and soup combo.  It's the best way to brighten your day.

Parking may be a bit of a pain.  But call ahead and maybe you can just double park for the 2 minutes you are inside.

I have held back from reviewing Haru because I am intimidated by Ramen places.  I keep thinking I am just not educated properly in the Ramen of the world and instead have permanently incapacitated my ramen judging capabilities with my "poor persons diet" when I was much younger.  Top Ramen with baloney was a family staple.

But darn it, I think that at some point I have to accept that I am a pretty good judge of different styles of food, and I have a very wide range of foods I enjoy.  And Haru was definitely one of those places I have enjoyed all three times I have been there.  Once for lunch and twice for dinner.  Every time was different because I tried different parts of the menu.  The last time we went in, I just requested that the owner send out the stuff he thinks we would like.

For my wife to share he sent out a bowl of their most popular ramen, a rice bowl a kimchee app and also I definitely cannot pass up the chicken liver skewers.  All were very good, and one was especially fantastic.  My wife normally isn't a fan of ramen so she focused on the Katsudon rice bowl.  So much flavor and still fresh tasting!



I loved the bowl of Ramen and my chicken liver skewers.  Normally I have some sort of miserable reaction after most Ramen places.  Something about cheap noodles and my digestive system doesn't work.  But here I was pleasantly surprised to not feel all bloaty after eating here, my guess is that they get a better quality noodle than most ramen places that I have been to.  Everything is cooked in the open kitchen as far as I can tell.  The work flow in the kitchen seems to be a little hectic right now, but they will eventually get it all worked out.  Until then the quality of the food is wonderful and the service is good.

They also have the most extensive beer list that any Asian restaurant has, or at least any Asian restaurant that I've been in.  Beers from everywhere and lots of great flavors to pair with your favorite dish.  Someone really knows how to make a good beer list.

Parking is easy and they always have enough seating for everyone.  If the place is packed you might want to be prepared for a bit of a wait, just relax and enjoy your drink.  It will come and I promise that you will enjoy it.

I can has Cheesecake?

Sure!  I can has it at the Cheesecake Factory!  We wanted to try out this new to Reno place and so we planned our night accordingly.  

Prepare for an hour long wait?  Check.
Prepare for rewarmed chain food? Check.
Prepare for overworked and harried staff? Check.

So did our preparations actually help us?  Not much.

We walked in on a Sunday night to put our name in.  "30 minutes" she said.  "Cool" we said.  "What's your phone number?" She said.  "775-999-4444" I said.  "Name?" she said.  "Kiwi" I said.

We walked over to Lenscrafters to kill some time and about 10 minutes later we got "the text".  We were whisked away to a nice little table just off the kitchen in the bar area.  Then the Death Star opened fire on my wife.  The rest of this review is in memoriam of my beautiful wife as she was melted by the death star door that goes to the patio.  The sun may have been a beautiful setting elsewhere...but from inside, it was lasers of pain.  We moved positions and tried to make the best of it.  So if you can see the patio door near sunset time during this time of the year.....beware and avert your eyes.  

My wife ordered up a scampi and steak special.  You can read Ly's review when it get's posted for her take.  I ordered up a burger and it was nice.  But it was a little awkward on the roll it came on, so my meat slipped right outta the bun.....

.....ahem.....

...anyway, it was a tasty chain level burger that was cooked properly to order and I chose the salad to come with it.  The salad wasn't my favorite but my pickier wife was happy to help me with it.  Go figure.

Then came the dessert!!  Ooooh la la!!  It was my wife's birthday weekend so she picked the Reeses Cheesecake.  I took one bite and spit it out.  My wife and daughter almost finished the single piece.  But even one bite was too much for me.  Sugar death incarnate. 

The service on this evening was not so harried as just not really organized.  Most of the staff wasn't running around all stressed but they weren't hitting any spots that they should have hit.  

So in closing, our preparations were helpful in some ways and other ways we were over prepared.  Next time we go in, I am sure the experience will be different.  That happens when you have a chain restaurant experience.  Because staff never can stay.

One warning...most people who are into food have come to understand "Factory" as a bad descriptor.  You might want to turn that little warning light off when you go in....because they use the name "Factory" on everything.

If you haven't been to Mod yet and you are reading this review to "consider" if you should go.

Stop reading right now.  Just go down and build yourself an amazing pizza.  Or salad.  Or Both.  Just don't forget to have some lemonade and one Tuesdays they have $2 pint nights.  Yes, you read that right.  $2 local craft brews!!

Ok.  Still not enough to get you to go?  Fine I will do a regular review.
MOD Pizza is the pizza of your dreams.  You like Hawaiian Pizza but love to add mushrooms?  Done.  No charge.  Love a combo but would rather have Spicy Chicken Sausage instead of Ground Beef?  Done!  Love a veggie pizza, but would love to add some Anchovies because you are a pescatarian?  DONE!

It's fun to come in and get whatever you want, how you want it.  They shy away from adding too much sauce, but that is because they want their pizza to come out cooked just right.

Now....for the Salad.  SAME!!  (cept they don't cook it).
So many different options.  The only thing they haven't perfected is getting the meats onto the salad warm.  Other than that, the bar is your palate.

They have a handful of great tap beers from local breweries, and of course they have the famously awesome teas and lemonades.  Addictive.  But here is my trick.  I cut the lemonades with a bit of soda water to keep the carb counts a bit lower.  And it's sooooooooo gooood.

Parking is plentiful - pro tip.  Easier parking is on the Bed Bath and Beyond side.  More pull-through opportunities.

Ever been watching a TV show and then get RIPPED out of the experience by something that "just isn't right"?  Like when you see Palm Trees in the background of Reno 911 or on CSI when they have all that "high tech" crap in the Coroner's office?  Well that happened to me while I was at Death & Taxes.  I had spied the place pre opening and was really intrigued by the dark look and the "mysterious" feel the place had.  So coming in I expected something quiet, somber and mature.  Instead I walked into a standard bar with a loud din of background noise.  Not the music, but just loud people.  I sat my wife on one of the couches and headed to the bar.

I'm not a really a bar guy so I don't know how this stuff works.  Do you just stand here like a dork hoping that they see you?   Do you wiggle in, getting between two unconnected patrons?  All these questions weren't answered and probably never will be, a spot opened at the bar and I plopped down on the stool and waited my turn.  I ordered up the Moscow Mule and the Indian Summer.  11 and 12 bucks....or....12 and 11 bucks.  Either way the total was $23.  Gulp!  A bit pricey for an alcoholic drink!  Yes, I have already heard it all.  In New York they pay $15!  In San Francisco that is cheap!!  In Los Angeles....BLAH BLAH FREAKIN BLAH!!  Welcome to reality and look at a map.  We aren't in Manhattan or even Marin County.  We aren't sitting next to some of the most famous buildings in America.  We are in a newly refurbished section of Reno NV.  So no, the prices don't jibe with me.

Now let me counter this with a caveat.  The drinks ARE worth more because they actually seemed to care about making good drinks.  Time and effort are involved in making it right.  So I think the "increase" in price should come in the form of a bigger tip.  But when you are spending $12 for a drink adding $3 for a tip per drink is just cost prohibitive.  Maybe I am just an old fuddy duddy.   My wife didn't really like the Mule I bought her so we switched and she was fine with my Indian Summer.  She had originally wanted a White Russian but they didn't have cream.  Bummer for her.  I loved the heavy ginger in the Moscow Mule myself.

I probably will go back on a week night when the crowd is lighter and I've saved a few extra pennies to pay for my bar tab.  Because the guys working the place were really good at what they did and made me feel welcome.

In the olden days, I would have given Sakana 5 Stars!!  With exclamation points!!  I would have raved about everything in sight and been effusive to the point of nausea.  Sushi places almost always got a pass to 5 stars, unless they really sucked.  But now I've matured.  I've become less of a "fanboy" of sushi.

So that being said, 4 stars is where we start for this review.  The place is a great addition to the Reno sushi scene.  It's got a number of things going for it.  It's the first place you come to if someone lives in Somerset.  It's in a nice neighborhood yet upscale mall.  Parking is close.

We had decided to go here for our Valentines dinner, not because it's the most romantic gesture to do sushi, but because we like to get to the new sushi places as soon as possible.  We walked in 3 minutes before they opened for dinner at 5:00 and they cheerfully sat us with some sort of welcome from the chefs.  We were sat at the end of the bar where my daughter could have some space being an 11 year old.  Drinks were quickly brought.  A few minutes later our chef introduced himself as Chris. During our small talk he said that he had worked at both Sushimoto in Fernley as well as Reno, and has worked at Tha Joint.  He was friendly and paced the meal nicely, but this could have just been the newness of the place.  If we come back in a few months we might find the pace isn't as leisurely.

The food was top tier Reno AYCE sushi.  As many Yelpers already know, 99% of the fish at the sushi places in Reno comes from a single source.  So if you find yourself eating something "less than" you are used to, it's from how they have handled the fish you are eating.  For our first roll we opted for Chris's special.  Meaning we just asked him to make us something and to his credit he asked us what we like and what we don't like.  After a few minutes we had a really amazing roll.  I can't tell you what was in it for sure, but it hit the "spot" that needs to be hit.  From there we went ahead and ordered from the menu..

Firecracker - a very tasty app!  
Mussels - Large sized.  Let's see if they stay large.  And they weren't still stuck to the shell.
Potstickers - My daughter only eats potstickers so these were ordered a la carte.  She loved them.
Edemame - Good.
Coconut Shrimp - smaller, but good in the marmalade dipping sauce.
Seared tuna, good, but maybe a little soft for my tastes.
Tuna - standard Reno issue.
Salmon - Again soft but no bad flavors.
Yellowtail - less buttery and firm  than I would like, but normal for most Reno places.
Chimera - good but not great
Tarantula - Tarantula a nice variation on the Spider roll
Godzilla - poofy deep fried roll.  Not too big but still on the bready side.
Sunset - A "Baked" roll.  It was good, but not really extraordinary.
Salmon Skin Hand Roll - Good, not to big and filling
Spicy Tuna Hand Roll - mildly spicy could go up another notch.
Special ordered Hand Roll - My wife ordered this one up on spec.  Me made it perfectly.
Quail Egg shooter - Soy based but had a different flavor profile.  I didn't quite get it and forgot to ask.  I'll check the next time.
Green Tea Ice Cream - ice cream and mochi are the only things on the menu.

The atmosphere is nicer sushi place.  More along the lines of Sushi Pier 2 or Ijji.  Lot's of stone and black.  Hopefully they will be doing some final touches and covering some exposed water filters behind the bar.  The place could really be a nice date night place with just a few finishing touches.

The restaurant has 3 entrances and they aren't clearly marked, so pay attention to the signage the entrance doesn't actually face the parking lot.

$20 Lunch $25 Dinner  AYCE

We will be back.  You can only get through so much of the menu in one sitting, unless you go with a group.  So who's up for going with me next time?

It's always unfortunate when businesses choose a name based on a pricing point because sooner than later that pricing point goes to crap.  Sort of like the "Dime Stores" in the olden days or "Dollar General" or "Motel 6" or "Super 8".  Some survive the inevitable inflation and keep the name.  Others just buckle under.

So even though 399 sushi hasn't been open decades...they don't have anything on their menu for $3.99 anymore.  All of the half rolls are at least $4.99 and most are even more.  That can be a bit confusing when you look at the menu too.  Prices are all scratched out and updated with a black pen.  But nevertheless, he persevered....and just ordered up what I would have ordered anyway.

We ordered a full roll of spicy tuna, a short roll of the Hopi, and a short rainbow roll.  We also ordered up some Yellowtail nigiri and I added a spicy salmon roll at the end.  It was all very good!  The nigiri had been prepped in some way with ponzu or something in a very pleasant way.  The other rolls were big two bite pieces and very satisfying.  The rice to fish ratio was right on point for all of the rolls.  I will admit that I was pleasantly surprised at how much I did enjoy the food here, I was not expecting to be this pleased.

The space is small but they probably do some bang up business with to go ordering too.  We didn't get anything to drink this time so maybe next time we will get one of their specialty drinks.   I did notice that they have soda in cans instead of on a fountain and also they carried the standard Asian beers as well.

Our total before tip was $37.  We probably could have eaten more...but didn't really need to eat more.  So if you are a big eater, especially when it comes to sushi...take that into account when you choose 399.  I expect to go back every once in a while when we just don't have the interest in doing the AYCE places we love.   Also, I need to get back and try some of the items that were plastered all over the place on photos.

After waiting too long we finally did this place.  EXCELLENT service.  Excellent food.  If you are considering this place....just do it.  It's not even a question.  The quality of the food and experience is unmatched in Reno.

I've posted a few pictures to show the quality of the place.  This is the perfect place for a nice Sunday morning day date.  In fact I am going there tomorrow.

And suffice it to say I will be recommending this place to friends fo sho!

I've come to understand that I won't get a good Authentic Bahn Mi in Reno.  I've gone through the stages of grief and am now in acceptance.  

With that being said, the Bahn Mi here is super duper tasty. The bread is super soft. 

I've had the pho here and it's good.  Nothing wow-a-riffic, but no complaints.  The last time I came in I tried some shredded pork fat spring rolls.  Nice different flavor.

The prices here are pretty much standard for your Vietnamese place in Reno.  Nothing shocking about your bill when you are done.

The business has been through a number of incarnations.  This incarnation makes the space nicer than all of the previous...but it is still quick Asian cuisine.  Not really a "fancy date night place" but still quiet enough for a first date?

Downgrade, on account of bleh salespeople. 

It's one thing to avoid eyes or whatever--I prefer to not be followed around the store, so that's cool. But to make a customer feel like they are intruding in your personal space by entering the store? What kind of shopping establishment has sales people who don't greet or bid farewell to customers? I seriously felt uncomfortable.

Thanks, but no thanks.

We were dying to try something new.  I moved to the area and using Yelp found this little gem! I brought the parentals on Sunday for breakfast.  I arrived late so I can't speak to the seating but when I arrived they had a nice table by the window.  Our server was friendly and enthusiastic and took my drink order the moment I sat down.  
The food! Granted you must work really hard to mess up breakfast but you also have to work hard to make it great.  The biscuits and gravy was excellent.  Biscuits were fluffy light and the sausage gravy was rich as well as flavorful.  It didn't taste like grease flour but like the sage and pepper from the sausage.  The potatoes were cooked well too.  (Surprising that home fries are under cooked a lot)  I enjoyed the bacon and egg sandwich.  This came with a candied bacon ZOMG!!! Another was shrimp and grits.  I wasn't allowed a bite since apparently it was so good that someone couldn't share.  It looked great, grits were thick and shrimp looked like a beautiful golden pink.   I think I might get that next time.  For me though the house made apple butter and strawberry jam were the highlight.  UM.... Seriously it on an old shoe and I'd eat it.  We were lucky to find a whole strawberry in mine.  
The family is always on the look out for a regular breakfast place and I think we found it.  Simple great food and value in a no fuss but great atmosphere.  I THINK they are only open for breakfast and lunch so you might want to check on hours.  But come try it but try it after 10 so I don't have to wait for a table.

So I have driven passed this drive in for a long time.  I have ever tried it and I don't know why. What I do know is that recently I had had enough and drove 30 mins out of my way to give it a try.  I don't know if it was a craving for something new or the nice January weather  but I gave it a go.  And I am very happy I did.  
Is this place groundbreaking?  Absolutely not.  They have made a decent time out of making every day nostalgia food really good.  By the looks of it they have been around for a while!  You can go inside and eat or get it to go or eat in in your car.  A real live person will come to your car with a server pad. I wasn't offered a menu but I didn't ask since I kind of looked at the menu on Yelp before I left.
Their burgers will put you in the mind of a burger chain with the crispy edges.  In my opinion because they were not gross greasy. The adults ordered a bacon cheeseburger.  The burger was great and the bacon was good and so much of it compared to the other places.  We tried all of the fried sides .  Onion rings curly and regular fries, and cheese cubes.  I wasn't a fan of the cheese cubes, but I don't' ever like them but the SO and the kiddo had a fight for the last one! Probably the star of the show was my kids strawberry shake.  I didn't order one because most of the time they are bleh but this was rich and had real strawberries. She loved it.  TO be honest there wasn't anything that I thought " I'll skip this next time."  
I really liked this place.  Reminds me of the small joints back home in the boonies. I will come back I might actually sit inside the next time

This visit was a totally different experience.  We decided last minute to make a visit.  NO reservations and not wanting to wait so we sat at the bar.  That's ok because they offer full service there as well.  We were not alone parties to either side were doing a full dinner at the bar.  

The last time we came the service was sub par.  Everything from the host to our abysmal front server( yes she was THAT bad)(important to note* our back waiter was awesome though) to the manager touching tables.  This time the staff at the bar were climbing over top of one another to greet and serve guests.  We felt welcomed and well cared for, which at the bar is usually a luxury.  
Even the food was better.  The steak cooked how we liked.  We decided to share a steak and lobster.  We were even given another hot plate with jus to share "better."  The onion rings weren't hot but still managed to taste great.  The shoestrings that come with the fried lobster tail are still overly salted but they'll get the hang of that soon I hope.  

All in all this was far better than the miserable time we had a year ago.  We will be adding this to our repertoire and hope for the best.

I have been wanting to try this place for a long time.  I talked my party into something a bit adventurous and we gave it a go on a Thursday night.  We arrived without reservations.  It is a bit confusing since there is no sign, but just go straight to the counter in the back to get seated.  We were told that we can sit immediately if we didn't want a grill, or thirty if we wanted a table with a grill.  Personally, I thought that was the whole point so we waited.  No bar area, but they have a Pink Galleon next door 
if you want a drink while you wait.  They will call when your table is ready. 

Our party ordered the AYCE option.  We chose two meats.  Apparently, some of these you can only get once, short ribs being one of them.  They were ok but trust me when I tell you once was plenty.  Get the bulgogi and the spicy pork.  SO GOOD! You cook this over the grill at the table.  All the tools you need are brought to your table. They will also bring you rice, lettuce and other condiments.  The other items are of course secondary but still had good flavor.  We enjoyed a bottle of Soju for the table (small bottle) though we could have drank more. Of the flavors listed on the menu one was not on there, the white grape.  Get that so good...bit dangerous since it was so good. 

Next and most importantly the cleanliness. Now the floor was a bit greasy but to be fair we arrived at near close and the whole restaurant is cooking in the dining room.  I don't think this would be a good arrow to follow.  I noticed when I looked around that there wasn't a lot of dust, which I have found to be the norm in a few smaller places after a few years.  I will tell you that I watched the servers go in with a bucket and brushes after each table left.  I can say that our grill cover came fresh from the dishwasher and greased and ready and I can also say they brought us out a new one half way through. 
 
Go with a few people, make it an event.  But get down there such a great experience and can't wait to go back.

I'm literally still here and had to write a review. Please do not eat here. The food was not good. Cold, bland, flavorless. SO expensive for what you get, that tastes like nothing. We ordered table-side guacamole, which was not prepared table side, instead they excused the warm mush of avocado, for $12, because the kitchen was delayed.  We're still not convinced it was actually made in house. The salsa was equally disappointing, when we asked for something spicy we were given a bowl of mango habanero sauce. Which they then charged $3 for, unbeknownst to us, ugh.  

When our entrees arrived the enchiladas were cold, Drew's food didn't even look like what he ordered, including the wrong grilled vegetables.  My "molcajeta" fajitas style was terrible. $24 worth's of over cooked meat with zero seasoning. No spices, no melting cheese, no crispy peppers. Boo!

I wish I could blame it on just opening but this obviously goes deeper.  Maybe try something besides a Mexican restaurant here because this obviously isn't working for you.

It was a dark and stormy night and we had spent all day shopping so cooking wasn't going to happen.  My family was in town so we had a house full of hungry boys to feed.

I ordered a carne asada burrito for myself, 15 carne asada tacos, beans, rice, albondagas soup, chips and quacamole for the locusts that occupy my residence.  For basically $35 I fed everyone and all approved whole heartedly.  The only compliant and what keeps this from 5 stars, was how salty some of the carne asada was.  All in all not a big complaint.

Service was excellent as we got all this food to go and I felt a little guilty about the work load.  Not even an issue!  The guy behind me ordered 30 tacos to go!  The woman taking orders says it happens all the time, yay!  This pretty much means I will never go back to fast food Mexican again :)

Bogart's is my favorite out of all of the BBQ joints in St. Louis, and that's saying a lot given the relatively new, but rich and developed BBQ scene in St. Louis. I literally go here sometimes just to get a taste of their brisket baked beans. The flavors of the baked beans side dish are so defined and deep, and that's all before you even get to the meat of their menu. 

Like all of the BBQ places in St. Louis, expect to wait in line. Luckily, the service here is great and the wait is never too long, and definitely worth it. However, if you're not eating in, you can call in your order ahead of time and skip the line all together.

Whether you are coming in from out of town or a local, you have to try the ribs. St. Louis has their own style of ribs, and Bogart's does it right. Grab one of their house-made sauces that fits your taste and you'll be hooked. I'd recommend getting the full slab because once you eat the first half slab, you'll want to take the other half home, plus it's a better deal. 

If you're in a brisket mood, Bogart's also has some of the best smoked briskets in my opinion. The brisket is consistently smoked to perfection and has the perfect balance of smoky flavors, spices, and the natural flavors of the meat. 

Their other sides are the standard sides you will encounter any a BBQ place. Bottom line, get the baked beans. If you feel guilty after stuffing your face with only meat (I never do), you can always stop by the Soulard market and pick up some cheap veggies on your way out of Soulard.

Amazing pizza, but I'm one and done. Won't wait for this again.
Got there at 4pm Friday, shop opened 5:30pm, received pizza at 5:45pm. By the time I received my pizza, the people ordering wouldn't received their pizza til 9:30pm.
2 pizzas max per person and about $25 per pizza. Only 40 pizzas made each night.
There's a couple standing tables; otherwise no where to eat.
Unfortunately, by the time you get it home, it's cold.
The pizza itself is very delicious. Thin, chewy crust that is cooked perfectly (tiniest burn on some spots).
White pizza with kale was really good. Kale was nice and crisp. 
Red pizza with sausage and mushroom was very good also.
Although the pizza was phenomenal, I would never wait so long for this pizza again. There are too many amazing pizza joints in the city.

What a cool new place! It's just opened up last week and I have already been there twice. Both times I had a blast! Great selection of local beers. St Pete Orange wheat is my local fav, but they got something for everyone. The prices are very reasonable for craft. One also can't beat their $0.99 PBR. Bring a receipt from a local business nearby and you can take advantage of the deal. Way to support our local business! 
The place is very spacious. It consists of two levels. The bottom one has a bar, seats, tables, and large games (like a paintball machine). Large windows with a lot of natural light. Upstairs they have more games: pool, darts, Mario brothers video game, and "table soccer". There's also a shelf with maybe 30 different board games. We had a large group of people with us both days and because of the two levels and a large variety of activities it did not feel crowded at all. Felt like a great house party. 
Welcome to the neighborhood! Can't wait to become a regular!

You tell me. Is it wrong that when I think of Philadelphia I don't think of the birthplace and the cradle of the United States Declaration of Independence; the Liberty Bell; Ben Franklin; so many things that made this country, but of cheesesteak? If it's wrong, I guess I really don't want to be right.

The argument over Pat V. Geno's has gone on for years. Both tourists and the regulars usually have something to say about it. Some say neither. I say, meh. Makes no difference. It's a cheesesteak, not brain surgery. It's like arguing over the Atlantic V. the Pacific. Both have their merits and their purpose.

As does Cheeze Whiz. Who would have thunk it? That orange globular, plastic food substitute is actually delicious on fries and or a steak.

It's cheap, it's tasty and if you want to argue about it, go ahead. Be my guest. It's hard for me to pick a fight with a well-seasoned, long time resident of Philly. I hear they know how to throw a punch.

I was rolling around with the Reno Suspect Enforcer Big Mike and we were famished .

So Mike suggested oneof his Favorite  Mexican/ Salvadoran Places El Paisano .

They are Located in an Older Strip Mall so Whip Parking was Easy to find . 

We rolled in and went to the Front Counter where you Order and Pay for your meal and then they give you a number to put on your table and your drink cup.

They even give you a Plate Of Homemade Fresh Tortilla Chips to Munch on whileyou wait for your food.

I looked at the Huge Menu offerings that they have on the Wall behind the front Counter and Pondered my Order . 

I went with a Carne Asada Super Burrito and a Fish Taco . 

I paid with my Master Card and rolled to the Sauce Cart  and Picked up my Hot Sauce and Salsa.

I joined Mike at a Table and posted up my number on the Holder at the table.

10 Minutes a Waitress dropped off my food Piping Hot on the table . 

I added some Salsa on my Fish Taco it was a good sized Taco and it had very good flavors to it .  i would definitely order it again.

My Super Burrito was pretty Big . But it was tightly wrapped . It tasted very good . I added a little Tapito to it for Heat. 

I had a pretty good Meal and Would eat here again if I was in town .

I had get my roll on my Ankle Bracelet kept going off .

Maybe because I left California ?

I was in Reno rolling with Reno Elite Mike S in his New Colorado Whip . It was around Lunch Time . So Mike suggested Raising Canes !!! I was Down for some Chicken Fingers . So we rolled there. We ended up Parking in the 7 Eleven Parking lot and walking to Raising Canes. 

Raising Canes is a Brightly Lit Place and appeared very Clean . I Ordered the Caniac  Combo- 6 Chicken Fingers , Crinkle Cut Fries , 2 Canes Sauce , Texas Toast , Coleslaw and a 32 Oz Large Drink !! Definitely a Baller On A Budget Meal !!!

Customer Service was Outstanding !!!  My Food was delivered 10 minutes after I ordered it.  The Chicken Fingers were delicious !!! As were the Fries. The 2 Canes Sauce was Tasty !!! Texas Toast was a Crowd Pleaser. 

I'm a Fan . When I'm in Reno Raising Canes is definitely one of my Stops !! And Is Definitely Baller on a Budget Approved !!!

Happy New Years My Yelp Friends !!! 

1st Review of 2018 !!!!

I was rolling with my Bro Big Mike - The Irish Enforcer Of Reno in his 4 Wheeler Whip . He Knows that I'm a Donut Addict LOL .  Since my Bro Big Mike is a Donut Connoisseur also he wanted to show me his favorite Donut shop in Reno . 

So we rolled to Doughboy Donuts . Doughboy Donuts is located in a Large Strip Mall so there's plenty of parking . We were able to park right in front . We rolled in and there where Display Cases full of fresh donuts !!!! For this Asian Doughboy I was in Heaven !!! Plus there was 3 Cute Girls working the Counter . This was a Win Win Situation !!! My Associate Big Mike Ordered 2 Crumb Donuts and a Coffee .  I ordered my Favorite Donuts 2 Chocolate Bars !!!

I made my way to the Table where my Associate Big Mike was munching his Donuts and Sipping his Coffee . I could Swear He Was Floating In The Air in delight from those Donuts Lmao . I started in on my Chocolate Bars and I have to admit they where light and airy and the Chocolate Glaze was Delightful !!!

They have a LCD TV for entertainment . The place is Decorated with Sports Memorabilia. and they take Credit Cards .  

Doughboy Donuts is Baller On A Budget Approved !!!

Cute place for casual dining!  We enjoyed lunch on Thanksgiving here.  My ahi tuna salad was excellent & my husband enjoyed a portobello sandwich.  He loved the potato salad.   Menu was simple and is geared towards brunch.  Saw lots of people getting omelets and they looked real good & very large!  Service was good and friendly.    Parking is a little difficult.

This place is fantastic!  Warm inviting atmosphere, experienced staff that always make you feel welcome, don't rush you, & of course a menu with many interesting things to choose from. 

Place is very roomy & the kitchen is open so you can smell all the deliciousness coming from there!

Steaks are fantastic here & you definitely need to order the side of onion straws with it - sooooo good!   Seafood is top notch as well & the salads are always good.    Nice bar with a great selection of alcohol.

This place does not stay open too late so be aware if you are looking to stop in to have a drink around 10 pm or later.

3 1/2 stars!  Nice basic breakfast place with nice outdoor seating & a nice-sized interior.  Located next to Mixer's in the corner so a little hard to find.   Menu is simple with good choices.  My eggs, bacon, & toast were prepared as I ordered it & was good.  I like that I could get avocado as a side instead of potatoes - wish more places did that.   Service was good & friendly.  The interior is dated & could a refresh.  The utensils are very cheap & lightweight - not a fan.  Anyway, for $10.95 you can get decent breakfast & if you like coffee, it's $2.95.

I love this place!  Such a wonderful simple but delectable menu with so many delicious things to choose from!

Great location on a corner of a shopping area with many outdoor tables & a nice dining room filled with wonderful smells of italian food!    You can never go wrong with an order of the traditional wings that are not fried and have a great flavor!   The pizza's are on point & wonderfully crispy - something that is VERY difficult to get in Florida!

Salads, meatballs, etc. I go on raving about all of it.  Simply - a great place for families or a couple wanting a nice casual night out.  Mangia!

Several years later after my original review of this place, I can definitely say that this a great place with delicious Italian food.  The house salad that comes with the meals is the best from any restaurant I have ever had - you get the good type of greens with goodies in it.    The entree's are consistently excellent - veal marsala - delicious sauce, chicken parm - pounded thin with the right amount of cheese, & the best vodka sauce around!  

Service is always good & the happy hour drinks are awesome!  The pizza by the way is fantastic as well!

I'm not real sure what people are complaining about. This was great food. Our table of 8 shared most of the items on the menu and was not disappointed at all. Sausage pizza was great, sliders were great, enjoyed the wedge salad, and the drinks were great too!

Taco Riendo is so great and a go to spot for bringing out of town friends.   It is cheap, delicious, adorable, friendly service, and BYOB.  What else could you want, people?  I wouldn't come here for a romantic night unless it's warm out and you can enjoy their lovely patio! Nice lights, plants, etc. 

A wise, taco-knowledgeable friend once told me that you can judge a taco place by their al pastor.  This place passes the test with flying colors.  

Added  bonus:  Went here on a bike tour and got free tequila shots and coronitas.  

As others mentioned, it is cash only. But hey, they have to keep their prices low somehow.  Deal with it.

Talk to enough people about good beer and they will lead you in the right direction. That's how I found my way to the Brauhaus Schmitz and came back for seconds with my beer loving counterpart. 

I stopped in alone, after shopping the Italian Market for a beer. Although the place was PACKED for a Saturday I found a seat at the bar and ordered a Schneider Aventinus Weizenbock, 8.2%. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/8j3blTZChklt3j89jxx0fw?select=Sfzkib1BaW7jE97NnvkC2Q It was an excellent choice too.

So when I was back in the hood with the Mister, I brought him over for a brew. I decided to try something new and he went with his favorite, a Hefen-Weizen. I ordered the Julius Echter Dunkelweizen and he ordered the Julius Echter Hefen-Weizen, both really good and put us in the mood for strolling down South Street, taking pictures and window shopping.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/8j3blTZChklt3j89jxx0fw?select=UDcbb4us09oPMLlHVJgf6Q

The Brauhaus is fun, the waitresses look great in thier beer maid outfits and the service was good. Another great stop on a BEERcation in Philadelphia.

I've been wanting to come to Reno for years, as I never been as an adult. To convince my guy, I told him we were taking a road trip to Revision Brewing Company - it's only about 200 miles away, but he was down. 

If you haven't heard, Revision's beer is that good. Locally, it flies off the shelf as soon as it's offered and they have some of the best hazy IPA's around. We planned a whole trip around coming here, LOL! 

We decided to stay at the Nugget around the corner, which made it easy to sample whatever we wanted and head back to the hotel. 

Arrived and the place was somewhat empty, except for a group of guys all dressed like Guy Fieri having a fun bachelor party outing. The ladies behind the bar were very nice, we ordered two samplers - all hazy. 

We brought our growlers on the trip, so we filled up when we got there and again when we left town. When we left, we stocked up on hazy in cans as well. Talk about a beercation with souvenirs! 

So, if you haven't tried Revision and you like IPA's, just try it already. And just a little warning, Revision does not allow anyone under 21 inside, so it's best to leave those kiddies at home.

Alma De Cuba was on my "To Eat" list, from the moment we started planning our trip to Philadelphia. We decided to save this restaurant for a night on the town with another couple that drove down to meet us. 

To drink, I started with the Black Cherry Caipirinha. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=bizByQADDmBLjYQRyFN6kQ He orders the Cohiba Cocktail, made with a cigar flavored rum, http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=-0iN269hNycrbCXPadEqPQ - Both great cocktails. 

Since the place has a long list of mouth watering appetizers, our table let me choose a few plates for us to share. While you are ordering, they offer Cuban Sweet Rolls served hot and fresh. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=M41Sr0BqDpK-8wuYSPJCLw

Since I had to pick the right thing, I ordered the:

*Ceviche Sampler, Japanese Snapper, Thai Mixto, Yellowtail Kingfish: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=RkquSZIWRwkk7urzJPQ9oQ
*Chorizo Sliders: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=67Qd-PvaV0-mFu2dIQwUkQ
The Alma Sampler (Order by # of people):
*Royal Palm Dates, Bacon Wrapped Dates stuffed with bleu cheese in an endive: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=0uzJA5L8X5k958tnj382hw
*Oysters Rodreguiz: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=1QrTNXFu7Mli3rqkxA_IQw
*Smoked Marlin Tacos; http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=N7-kKKGQ6fCJZNql5uVwaQ

For dessert, they all ordered the:
*Vanilla Crepe with Bourbon Ice cream, chocolate and bacon bits: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=iMtlvZFgsY6r5Y40VPwT_Q
*Goat Cheese Flan: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=f7FJe17htgtqzHoW3-cwOg

Me? I really just wanted the Havana Old Fashioned (with Pemegranate) http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/R17gwW6zn9ilslbdvKdgsg?select=9uP_ihprBp1pFi2XpsovCg

This place was so amazing, it's more than Latin American and Gourmet food. It's amazing and oh so inspiring for those of us who love to cook and love Cuban food. Service was really great, it was a little pricey, but mostly because of a bottle of French Rose Champagne that our table ordered. 

Alma De Cuba deserves to be on your "To Eat" list too.

We tried out the Rotisserie Buffet for lunch on our way home after a weekend in Reno. This Buffet is located within the Nugget Casino where we were staying. 

Lunch was $11.99, all you can eat. Selection for lunch was not great, I found myself picking at the food on my plate and didn't really find anything appetizing. Although it was cheap, I'd save my money next time and try out some of the other buffets in Reno.

After finally finding a spot for dinner that night, my guy took me to the Row where we sat at the bar and talked with the bartender. 

I asked if there were any spicy cocktails and he had one that was made with an house made habanero liquid. I don't even know the name, but I know it was so damn good I had him hit it with some more pepper. 

For the appetizer, I ordered the pickled vegetables. I do a lot of home pickling and love to compare it to others. Especially southern style, I want to try them all. They were very good and healthy little appetizers. The beets were my favorite of the bunch. 

For our meal, we ordered the Rib Eye cooked medium to split with two sides. I ordered the cheese grits and greens on the side. They were fantastic, yet the cheese grits were the very best. I was so full, that I practically packed up most of my portion of the meal. 

I ate the leftovers the next day for breakfast and they were so good that people at the hotel kept asking me where I went and what I ordered when I popped into the lobby to heat it up. Damn good. 

I now crave cheese grits for breakfast.

The Oyster Bar was the best restaurant in the Nugget. Their Happy Hour is from 5-7pm daily and has some awesome choices. 

My all time favorite was the crab roll, for $6 you get two generous portions of real Dungeness crab. These were so good, we ordered like 3 plates of crab rolls. 

We had the oysters, ceviche, calamari and the peel and eat shrimp. It was a seafood extravaganza and cost us much less than the seafood restaurant we went to on the way into town. 

I highly recommend the Oyster Bar for Happy Hour, aka Early dinner.

Imagine one of the best food courts you've ever been to and you got the Reading Terminal. We came here in search of a sandwich we saw on the Food Network and tried not to get carried away with all of the mouth watering foods. 

I saw some of the biggest prawns I've ever seen, great looking "salads and sides" had some amazing desserts and of course we ate the sandwich we were looking for (review to come). We also stopped at Molly Malone's for a pint with our sandwich. 

My question is if you had the opportunity to come here every day, what would you choose? It all looks fantastic. 

The one thing we really missed out on was the Pennsylvania Dutch (Amish) vendors since we came here on a Monday and they were closed. We even tried back on Tuesday to no avail, so if you are headed to Reading - make sure to come Wednesday thru Saturday to make sure you get to try it all.

The food used to be so much better. When I've been here in the past, the food was so good. It made me feel like I was back east again. I ordered a cheesesteak with peppers & onions. I haven't been there in quite some time. But it DEFINITELY was not the same. All of it was changed: the meat, the cheese, the bun, they didn't even have condiments on the table. And when we asked for ketchup, we were given 2 little cups of ketchup, as if we were children & only allowed to have more of we finished that. It was sad. 
Please change back to the way you were. I would rather pay a few more dollars for some east coast goodness, than pay less for something that ALMOST is the right thing.

Drove to ECSS today at 11:35 AM and there was a chain blocking the front door; they were closed. 

Hours say 11 AM to 8 PM. 

Not sure why they decided not to open today. Also not sure if I'll drive there again since I'm not confident that they'll be open during business hours.

So it's a Sunday night, Week 9 Winter Quarter 2016. It was around 10.30PM. I want to get my favorite burger in Isla Vista at Dejavu Cafe. Their Gaucho Burgers are bomb. 

Recently, there's an app called GauchoLife in the app store. If you are a UCSB student you get a couple of deals in Isla Vista (You can get 15 per day) and one of them was Dejavu Cafe. The day before I wrote this review, I told my friend about it and he went to Dejavu and used the GauchoLife app to get free fries with a purchase of any burger.

I kept shaking my GauchoLife app and out of the 15 shakes, I didn't get any that was Dejavu cafe. I figured it wouldn't hurt to just call the place and ask if they were still having the deal or not. Called the guy, and he was so rude to me. Told me that there was never a deal like that and like hung up on me super quick. I try my best to be considerate and understand the other persons' point of view. So I thought, maybe this guy was just having a bad day. Despite being pissed that he was rude to me, not getting the free fries, I still decided to go get my Gaucho Burger cause I was hungry. -_-' 

So after taking a moment to think whether or not I should go get food, I decided to get on my skateboard and go. 

I come to Dejavu and I ask for the Gaucho Burger. I put my atm on the counter and waited patiently for the person (I think it was the owner, he had glasses and white hair growing already) to ring up my order. He asks me if I was the guy that called, and I calmly just said yeah. 

I asked him politely (with NO ASSUMPTION of getting anything at all except getting my Gaucho Burger) if he still had the deal going on with the free fries. I told him that my friend just got it the other day. He asked me what app I found it on, so I pull up my phone and show him the app. I had used all of my swipes and the last swipe was on a 20% discount at Naan stop, so he was like "It doesn't say dejavu."

So I responded, yeah but yesterday it was on there, my friend got the deal, so I'm not sure whether or not it was still going on.

This is the part where he pissed me off.

He literally says to my face, "Well that was yesterday. It doesn't show today." So I tell him okay... dude... I didn't mean to be rude or anything. And he keeps on saying, "Why are you coming here to ask me about something that was yesterday. Today is today so if it's not there, it isn't there."

I was so appalled by his reaction, I honestly couldn't believe that this guy was actually getting mad at me. I've been there several times and I've seen him work behind the register (before knowing the GauchoLife app) and he seemed like a nice person. 

I somehow must've said something wrong or something, because all I tried to say was, okay I was just asking. I don't know why you're getting mad.

He looked at me and was like, "You know what, give me your atm, I will refund your order so you can take your business somewhere else." 

As he was refunding my order, I tried to explain to him that I was just curious on whether or not the free fries deal was going on, and I didn't understand why he got all mad. 

As I walked away, he kept blabbing stuff so I just ended up telling him to eff himself. 

Ended up going to Naan stop and used my 20% off on the GauchoLife app. Win, win.

Went to Naan Stop and ended up tipping the dude $1 for not being a complete a-hole and accepting my GauchoLife coupon. 

STRUGGLE OF A COLLEGE STUDENT MAN. I JUST WANTED TO EAT. :'(  

TL;DR::
Never going back to this place again.
Had a question about a discount on an app called GauchoLife. 
Got a terrible, unexpected, very rude response.
Ended up refunding me for no reason and told me to take my business somewhere else.

We came here every night we were staying in New Orleans - how could you not?! It's open for dine-in til 2am, located in the back of a super chill gay bar that plays pop music videos on loop. Heaven.

My husband and I were obsessed with the piggyback fries, which were loaded up with BBQ pulled pork, cheese sauce, crispy lardons, homemade ranch and scallions. After a night of strolling & drinking, THIS is the ultimate high-caloric nightcap. We got those on all 3 nights we visited, but also tried the PB,B&J wings, which were also stellar. Thai-style peanut sauce, crumbled bacon, spiced grape jelly & scallions. YESSS.

The Yelp app totally delivered when we were looking for late night eats, and I'm so glad it brought us to Faubourg.

Best of Philly bakery? James Beard Foundation award for outstanding baking? Yes, please. My friend lives around the corner so she took me to Artisan Boulanger Patissier over the weekend to kick off my two day jaunt to Philly. At 10am, most items in the pastry case were sold out, which was understandable given the spot's popularity. After enduring a bit of a line, we left with a buttery croissant and a flaky pastry topped with creamy cheese and strawberries. Perfect treats to enjoy outside on a balmy spring morning - which was exactly what we did!

Cash only, no frills atmosphere, the baked good speak for themselves. Next time I visit, I'm arriving early and buying everything.

Very disappointed. Ordered a chicken parm hero, which the red sauce tasted like it was heated up out of a jar. When I called to see when my ordered would be delivered after 45 minutes of waiting, I then waited another hour. I was told that a baseball team had just came in so that I was going to have to wait. Very unprofessional and disappointed by the food

Best place for Mexican food in Philly. Hands down John is the best server who is always super sweet and on top of it. He makes you feel like a welcomed guest in his home...or something like it. Great place for large groups. No corking fee and the largest party gets to control the radio also. Love this place. And that's coming from someone who is used to Mexican food in California.

Two things I love about this place are location and tater tots! I am not a fan of tater tots in general, but these are not your typical tater tots. They are light and crispy with a very subtle hint of truffle and come with a lemon creme fraiche. They are absolutely addictive and a perfect starter to a meal or bar snack. 

I have to give credit to Anna for dragging me back to Anise for those tater tots. My first meal at Anise a couple years ago was unmemorable and I was never compelled to return. Since Anna's raving of their tater tots and ramen, I've been back a couple times and am now a fan. Even their ramen is pretty outstanding. The broth isn't overly salted and comes with crispy pork belly. The egg, fish cake, and mushrooms are also excellent additions to my new favorite comfort food. 

The stinky buns are on my list to try next. I had their shrimp taco, which would have been great, but it looked like it was sitting for a while and there was a dark "vein" in one of my shrimp. I was not impressed with their duck wings. Their jap chae is surprisingly really good!

Aside from the tater tots, you can't beat their location. They are in a prime spot across Curtis Hixon Park. The outdoor patio is ideal for those perfect weather days. You have a view of the stunning park, the beautiful minarets of UT, and dine along the towering buildings of little downtown Tampa. Inside the ceilings are high and the bar is elevated giving a grandiose feeling. I just wish their bathrooms weren't unisex. I'm willing to wait longer to not have to share. 

They have a decent happy hour crowd from what I've seen. Something that seems to be lacking in Tampa in general. The bartenders are friendly and efficient. Drinks are made well and quickly. 

Parking is either across the street in the lot or metered parking on the street. You'll be close to the museums, the park, the Straz Center, so it's a great pre or post party place if you have other plans.

Surprise, another Korean sushi restaurant, but both cuisines are equally great here! Most Korean restaurants offer sushi for mass appeal, and often either the Korean entrées are better than the sushi or vice versa, but both sushi and Korean foods are equally delicious at Sushi Maru.

The salmon rotika is my favorite roll, but there is a huge variety of rolls to choose from, and they range from simple to over the top busy. More importantly, the fish is fresh. The only disappointment I experienced was the volcano roll; I expected more spice and it could do without cream cheese. 

As for the Korean dishes, the spicy pork and beef bulgogi are always perfectly flavored and without much gristle. Vegetables are fresh and the fried rice is fluffy. I'm not a fan of fried gyoza and rolls, but theirs had a good amount of filling and wasn't overly greasy. 

Best of all, the restaurant is so clean and doesn't smell. They must have an excellent ventilation system, because most ethnic restaurant smells can be overpowering. Obviously, the Korean dishes are not cooked table side but in the kitchen.

This outdoor bar by the water is so inviting. Situated between Harbour Island and downtown Marriott and the Convention Center, it's perfect for both locals and tourists to walk/bike over for a relaxing time sipping drinks, taking in the views after meetings or before hopping on the water taxi just steps away - weather permitting of course; Sail is exclusively an outdoor bar without any enclosed areas. The most shelter is a roof over the bar. 

There is plenty of seating, cocktail tables, and umbrella patio tables surrounding the covered bar and on the concrete levels leading to the water. The empty tables were dirty and no one ever came to our table, so you will need to bus your own table and walk to the bar for drinks. My husband said he's always had a server visit his table, so it could be that their service diminishes on busier nights. 

A full bar including some fun slushy drinks are served along with a full menu. We only came for drinks, but the trays of food coming from the neighboring Marriott looked appetizing. 

You can't miss the lure of this cute little bar on a nice day. Drinks and relaxation will be calling!

I toyed with the idea of a 2 star review because Gran Caffe is a very spacious and impeccably clean restaurant in a nice area of Philly with very good service but in good conscious I couldn't give them any more than 1 star for the food they subjected us to. Gran has a few levels (the front of the street level is their coffee shop and gelato counter). There's a good chance if you're just coming here for gelato or espresso that you may get something of quality but that certainly doesn't carry over to their food. The fact that their prices are as high as they are just put the nail on the coffin for my wife and I who both agreed our meal here was one of the worst we've ever had, anywhere. Top 3 bad in fact (probably top 1 for her). It's also worth mentioning that the place also just feels like a large chain restaurant right down to the uniforms, borderline costumes, that the wait staff is forced to wear. 

For drinks she ordered a $12 cocktail called Sgroppino (lemon sorbet, processco, lemoncino vodka, fresh mint). This ended up being an incredibly weak and disgustingly sweet drink that she couldn't finish. Most of the beers were $7-10 but some as low as $5 or as high as $14 for a 12oz Italian beer with a 5% abv. I went with a $5 Peroni. For a starter we ordered their arancini ($10). This came presented beautifully and the texture was right but we both agreed it tasted a bit like soap and there was something definitely off with them. 

For a meal I had the Pappardelle Al Ragu Aquilano ($16.50) which is a wide ribbon pasta with slow cooked pork, veal, lamb, and chicken in a tomato based sauce. The meat had been pulverized to the point where it wasn't recognizable and the sauce was the worst tomato sauce I've ever had. It was the same tomato sauce that the aranacini came on and tasted like it came right out of a can of Ragu from the super market. I've had a lot of red sauce over the years and I don't hesitate to say that this was the worst and most store bought tasting I've ever had at a restaurant before. It was so disappointing that I have no doubt that I could have had a better plate of pasta from Olive Garden. 

As disappointing as my meal was, it was still edible which is more than I can say about my wife's dish. I felt so bad for her that I traded plates with her and couldn't even muster a second bite of her food after tasting it. To this day we both feel like gagging thinking about her dish and joke about how bad it was. She ordered the Agnoletti Al Tartufo ($19) which was ravioli stuffed with veal, pork, onion & herbs, topped with a butter-sage sauce and a little block of the chef's truffle gelato creation. The waitress assured us that the gelato wouldn't actually cool down the dish at all and would just melt over the dish infusing an extra flavor to it. Well this pretentious little gimmick did in fact cool down the entire dish to barely over room temperature and what it added to the dish was a disgusting overpowering truffle flavor that even a truffle lover like my wife couldn't stand. The ravioli's filling wasn't meaty either which was a big draw to the veal and pork stuffing. The mushy filling paired with this incredibly overpowered truffle flavoring, lowered temperature, butter sauce, and mediocre noodles just made this meal completely inedible. 

I've never been so disappointed not only in a restaurant but in Yelp's overwhelming praise for such a horrible Italian restaurant. Shame on you all for not knowing what good Italian food should taste like.

UPDATE:
I received one of the least professional business responses to this review where the manager Darren writes in part: "I believe the problem is that you have been subjected to so much Olive Garden style food over the years, that YOU in fact don't know what true, authentic Italian flavor is supposed to be."

Instead of engaging this guy privately I figured I'd just respond here. First of all I've only eaten at Olive Garden once in my life. 

Secondly, as far as my track record goes, with over 2,150 reviews on Yelp, only about 1% of those reviews are for 1 star so you can see I very rarely slam a place for being bad. Of those 23 one star reviews, only 8 of them are to food related businesses and half of those places have since gone out of business. About 40% of the restaurant's I've written 2 star reviews for have also gone under which is a stark difference from only about 12% of the restaurants I've written 5 star reviews for. With nearly 1,000 restaurant reviews and living not only in a mostly Italian neighborhood in Brooklyn but the area of the country with the most Italian-Americans and Italian restaurants I've eaten at more than my fair share of high quality Italian restaurants. 

Thirdly and most importantly when I visited, it was only 2 months after coming back from my two week honeymoon in Italy where my wife and I traveled all around the country searching out the best food possible. My taste in Italian food is clearly not the problem here.

Delicious food all around for us.  Olives to start, with a huge bowl of light, green olives.  Then we split and off-menu special caprese salad that had some great fresh mozzarella cheese )which was rough torn rather than sliced), and bright fresh basil.  The wife got another off-menu special of fresh made ravioli with sweet corn - she said it was delicious.  I went for the Roman gnocco - which had a deep, complex flavor with its pork ragu and other ingredients.

As I said above, the olives were a huge bowl for only $7.  We asked about splitting the caprese salad, and the waiter said it was plenty large enough to do so.  But when it came, it didn't really seem that big to me.  However, it turned out that it was just right for full entrees afterwards.  When both entrees came out, they didn't look that large either.  But my gnocco was very dense, and filled me up.  The wife, too, didn't finish all o hers.  So looks were deceiving.

For dessert, the ice cream sandwich was excellent.  I can't describe it to give justice, so I won't try.  But it's definitely not the grocery store kind - and the chocolate with crunches accompanying it was the decadent topper.

For some crazy reason, we also got cookies for dessert, but quickly realized those were coming home with us instead.

Service was also very good.  We arrived shortly after 5 pm opening, yet all tables were reserved.  Not a surprise, and we came prepared to sit at the bar. However they also had seats at he pizza pass through.  So we were able to watch the pizza chef work and chat with him during the evening.  Our waiter was refined yet friendly, informative, and attentive.

A good evening and meal was had.

Long before Emeril or Mario Batali became household names, Carl Oshinsky, a former dental technician from Oak Park, Mich., introduced me to Detroit-style pizza on his 1989 PBS show, the Pizza Gourmet. 

I had never heard of square pizza baked in auto industry parts pans. Or of having sauce on top of the pizza and cheese that oozes to the side of the pan and becomes crunchy good.

All these years later, I still have Chef Oshinsky's cookbook. I've used it often over the years, but until yesterday, had never had Detroit pizza in a restaurant. 

I was excited to hear about Spitfire Craft Pizza & Beers, but wasn't sure whether it was a pizza joint that served beer or a beer joint that served pizza. 

I dare say 95 percent or more of the people who come in Spitfire are likely to have never heard of Detroit pizza. So the first thing I would have expected the waitstaff to ask customers coming in was whether they were familiar with that style of pizza and explain what it is.

Even though I didn't need that explanation, it would have been nice to hear a spiel so I could judge what they knew about it and whether I could expect the real deal or just a poor facsimile.

Instead I was left to figure things out for myself. The menu was pretty straight forward, but again, didn't provide any explanation of what sets Detroit pizza apart. It also suggested they use two different kinds of pepperoni, but didn't explain what the difference is between the pepperoni under the cheese and a second, "natural casing pepperoni."

The pizza I ordered, The Detroiter with pepperoni under the hood and above, was good. Really good. The small was $11. I ate two of the six pieces and brought the rest home. The pepperoni was good, the sauce was flavorful, the deep dish crust was light and springy and the caramelized cheese from where it cooked against the pan was outstanding.

I understand that Spitfire is still in soft opening mode, so they haven't hit all cylinders yet. The waitstaff at times seemed confused about the tables they were covering. A man I assumed to be the owner took my order but 15 minutes later a woman came by and asked if I was ready to order. 

The woman who brought my pizza asked if I needed another plate. Even though I didn't even have one. I guess maybe some customers may eat off the serving pan itself.

Ice must be at a premium at Spitfire or maybe it doesn't exist at all. Water came at room temperature and I didn't see a single cube while I was there. 

While a sheet listing 16 impressive beers on tap was also found on tables, neither it nor the pizza menu provided any non-alcoholic choices. I was told they have Jones and local Ripsnort sodas, but it would have been nice to know what they had on hand. I opted for the room temperature water. 

The staff was friendly and I expect them to hit their stride when they've been open a bit longer. I'll come back and see them again. But please, get some ice. And don't wear your caps backwards unless they're fitted caps.

Sadly, there are few Asian restaurants left that make their own noodles. And that's in Hong Kong, the culinary capital of China. So to have an eatery in Boise where owner Chan Chun-Chung crafts his own egg noodles, that is pretty special. 

The Noodle is a place where many potential first-time visitors may be turned off by the clutter of plants inside the front door and the rather drab decor. However, this is authentic Hong Kong -- where Chan grew up -- at its best. It's not about the building, it's about the food.

If you think sauces dominate Chinese cooking and that a General Tso chicken is a real dish. you need to go to PF Chang's, Panda Express and their ilk. However, if you want bright dishes where the ingredients themselves shine, Wok Inn Noodle is the place for you.

Three decades ago, I was introduced to the Wok Inn Noodle on Idaho Street. Sadly, it no longer exists, but the original Orchard Street location remains in a nondescript strip mall at Emerald street, wedged between a smoke shop and a bar.

Chan is getting older and it's just him in the kitchen, so service may be slow, but oh, is it ever worth it.

I recommend the House Noodles, which includes chicken, beef and shrimp stir fried with an assortment of vegetables and noodles paired with a subtle sauce. 

Hong Kong Chinese complain that in the United States sauces are too dominant and become the taste of the dish, rather than complement it. Chan sticks to the authentic style and it's the reason he puts out the best Chinese food in Boise.

And don't expect a fortune cookie. Because they don't exist in Asia.

Since there was only two for Thanksgiving, we decided to let someone else do all the work associated with a multi course meal. After considering several different venues, we Decided to give Cafe Biscottis the task.          Well from the moment we stepped over the escalator, we began to be impressed. The decor is nothing less than stunning. And equally impressive was the staff, friendly and efficient. As soon as we sat down the waitress was there to bring us our beverages and just make sure we were comfortable and ready to enjoy a evening of fine dining. This was just a amazing buffet. Of course the usual delights of a full on Thanksgiving meal. Turkey, ham, stuffing, all the veggies and casseroles. But here in the food line was Rack of Lamb, Filet mignon, Fresh Crab, Jumbo Prawns, oh my goodness sushi here there everywhere. Oh a variety of fresh bread, of didn't mention the incredible salad bar. And for Desert there was an entire other room set up with a variety of goodies beyond my imagination overall just a fabulous meal certainly guess it didn't disappoint. We absolutely will be back to enjoy there extensive regular menu.

My girlfriend had a $25 gift certificate for Rickshaw Sushi so we had to give it a try. Actually conveniently located off of Longley Lane, as she lives in South Reno. I was pleasantly surprised how it wasn't that busy. I tried several different pieces of Salmon on traditional sushi pieces, plus a couple of the house favorites. I was rather disappointed with the fish not tasting fresh, which is huge when dealing with fish. In addition to that problem, we both had to ask for new plates as sat down dirty ones in front of us. The waiter did a pretty good job under the circumstances, but unfortunately I don't think we'll be back. I would not recommend Rickshaw Sushi

My family and I had lunch reservations for when they opened at 2p and we weren't seated for at least 20 mins. I'll attribute the slow service that we experienced to the fact that they just opened and were warming up.  The hostess was polite but cold; I've experienced better service at the DMV. Our waiter took our drink order and never brought them out, 20 minutes later we asked some random waitress to bring them out. The meats did not start to come out until almost 3p. By the time we left service started to improve, but it was a little too late and I was already annoyed. 

I was underwhelmed by the whole dining experience.  I have experienced good Brazilian BBQ and this wasn't at their level.  The salad bar wasn't as extensive as others, and they didn't have that many cuts of meat.  Also, our table was skipped over many times when they did bring out the meat. 

The restaurant did have a very nice, clean, classy ambiance.
A big plus is that my twins ate for free; most places do charge half.

Okay, okay, okay, okay. What is the deal with these bad reviews? Perennial Artisan Ales is one of the best microbreweries in the Lou. 

I have been there twice and both times the service was amazing. My husband and I went there this weekend and both waitresses we had were so friendly. 

The beer is incredible. Have not had a bad beer. On my last visit, I got the Saison De Lis. What I call a "Real Women's beer," it's a belgian-style ale with chamomile that tastes as fresh as it sounds. 

I am not sure what the wall color has to do with the experience. I think the decor is just as minimal-chic as 4 hands and Schlafly. 

Okay, what I will say, it's location is at the intersection of ghetto and nowhere BUT it's well worth it. And yes, when there is a lot of people, it takes a while to get a beer...because you know, there is a lot of people. 

Overall, Perennial Artisan Ales is wonderful!

My dear sweet baby Jesus. I had one of the best lunches at Salt + Smoke. 

My husband and I ventured there after some Sunday afternoon shopping. We sat outside on one of the first warm days of the year. We got the "Bestie Combo" plate with the mac and cheese and fries. This maybe just a pet peeve of mine, but I hate when restaurants don't do french fries. Salt and Smoke did not disappoint-their fries were delicious. And the popovers? Incredible  BUT nothing could prepare me for the main course. The brisket and pulled pork. Both so juicy, they literally melted in my mouth.  I simply cannot wait to go back.

I wish I could give zero stars to this crap show.
The whole experience was 6 bites exactly for $70 + the tip.
We sat down and mentioned separate checks, the lady server told us, no separate checks and that all dishes are shareable. It was 6 of us. Ok! We ordered 2x6 dishes and the pork shoulder at $50 which she mentioned was plenty for 6. There was only 5 slices. 5 tiny slices for $50? I got 3/4 slice
So when the check came I mentioned that I was still hungry and those dishes were not shareable sizes.The duck at $32 gave me one single slice. She went and cried to her boss which is also the owner. So now this guy comes to my table and proceed to scream at me and tell me that if I was still hungry on a $70 meals I should have ordered more food. But the truth is that if I had doubled my order I would still be hungry and now pay $140 for 12 bites. I am laughing now but this guy was in my face and screaming. I accidentally or not knocked a bottle of water on the floor because I wanted him out of my personal space and stop screaming at me, with his  less than pleasant breath , I felt threatened by this man and on my way out he told me I was lucky to be a woman as if this was acceptable he would actually put hands on me. He picked up the bottle and emptied it all over me and my friends and our phones on the table and finally called me crazy and to get the fuck out of his restaurant . I've lived in nashville since 2001and that has been the worst meal and experience EVER!! This restaurant owner is a bully. and his lady server needs to learn how to handle her tables without creating a drama. The food was salty and poorly executed. As a French woman and trained chef I would know!

This was our second visit to Anthony's. Last time, everything about our experience here was great with the exception of our inconsistency cooked steaks. I stated in my previous review that if that hadn't been the case, my review would've easily been a 5. Well, I'm thrilled to report that those "newly opened restaurant" kinks have been ironed out.

All the positives in my previous review still stand. The service is excellent and they hit a home run with the decor, lighting. My favorite cocktail, the 'Smoked Manhattan', is still being served and was as tasty as I remember. The bread was warm and full of flavor. It seriously the best bread I've ever eaten.

Now, let's get to the hero of the joint; the steaks. Last time, my filet was cooked half medium, half medium-well. That worried me as that usually occurs when dealing with a thawed steak. However, I chalked it up to them still being new. I'm not sure if they hired new Chefs or provided better training but either way, my filet was cooked to perfection (medium). The knife cut right through without resistance and the side-served peppercorn sauce was the perfect accompaniment.

I've been to just about every steakhouse in the Reno/Sparks area and now that Anthony's have stepped up their game, they are new favorite and "go-to" steakhouse. It most definitely will not be another year in between visits.

My wife and I tried our first Tapas Bar in Oregon last year and lately, we've been aching to find a good one here in Reno. After scouring Yelp, we decided on Sierra Street Kitchen based purely on the reviews. Believe me when I say; they live up to the hype.

We've tried numerous dishes and loved them all. The bacon wrapped dates, in particular, was my favorite dish of them all. I'm not normally an adventurous person when it comes to food, but Sierra Street Kitchen changed that. I'm not big on mushrooms but loved the chorizo stuffed mushroom dish and the seared scallops were cooked to absolute perfection. The meatballs, while good, ended up being the least favorite of mine. 

The Bourbon Bramble is the only cocktail I tried but it was delicious! Both the Bartender and the Chef are very skilled at what they do. The customer service from our waitress was also good. She was new and didn't have a great deal of knowledge about the menu just yet, but she made sure to get us answers if she didn't know. She was very friendly and prompt.

Due to checking in through Yelp we were offered a free desert and this did not disappoint. We selected the Decadent Chocolate Cake. It was rich and had (I think) raspberry sauce sauce drizzled around it. 

All in all, my wife and I were more than satisfied with our experience here. The service was good, the food was great, and the presentation of the dishes was outstanding. We will definitely return.

After spending the night at the Nugget, we were able to get a reservation for Rosie's for their opening time at 8am as we just wanted a quick bite to eat before heading home.

We were greeted and seated right away and our waitress got to our table quickly to take our order. My wife ordered the Denver scramble and I was craving something on the sweet side so I went with French toast.

All in all, it was what it was. I believe this restaurant is a remnant of the old guard at the Nugget and it does show. The interior is dated and the menu is nothing to write home about. The food was decent but you can tell they don't use quality ingredients and a lot of it is simply thawed and grilled/heated.

I would put it on the same level as what you would find at Denny's. All your typical breakfast fare is represented on the menu and not much more. The service was decent but we felt unnecessarily rushed by our waitress. We were literally one of 5-6 tables in the whole place. Not sure what the rush was for.

Hopefully they'll do here what they've done with their steakhouse. The one they had before was down right terrible but they've revamped and hit a home run with Anthony's. Fingers crossed as there isn't many solid breakfast offerings in Reno hotels.

Chick-fil-A, specifically this location, has been doing a spectacular job at handling this covid crises while still serving up amazing customer service and delicious chicken. While the interior has remained closed since the beginning of all this, they have become masters at running an efficient drive through and curb-side pick up service.

All employees wear both gloves and masks. With curb side pick up, you simply order and pay through the app, let them know which space you're in (also in the app), and they bring your food out on a tray. They won't hand you your stuff in order to limit the spread.
