There's been times when I've pulled up to my spot, ordered, paid, and  had my food before people in the back of the drive through line even ordered. It's seriously efficient.

PS: As stated in my previous review, I'm still patiently waiting for spicy nuggets to hit the menu. Come on Chick-fil-A, let's make it happen.

This was our first time to this one but we have been to their Midtown location a few times. The parking and bathroom situation was a little awkward as there is currently construction going on at the hotel the restaurant is attached to but it didn't damper the experience at all.

Much like in Midtown, the customer service here is good. This company is pretty good at finding and retaining friendly and efficient staff. The menu right now (and possibly for good) is digital and can be accessed by using your phone to scan the QR code.

While you will place your order with your waiter or waitress, you'll use your phone to pay your bill. The option to use Apple Pay was there which I was happy about. It's just so easy and quick to use. I'm not sure if they're accepting cash, though. You'll have to inquire about that.

Another solid experience here. Like everyone else, they're doing their best to navigate the ever changing covid situation by requiring masks (unless you're ate your table), keeping diners spaced apart, and sanitizing between customers. 

I highly recommend securing a reservation (as we did) to avoid disappointment. I witnessed a few parties turned away because they either didn't have one or they had too many people in their party and refused to sit at separate tables (current regulations limit just four per table). 

The food was, as always, good. Our appetizer, the fried Mac and cheese balls with marinara, were delicious. My white chicken chili was full of flavor and came with a HUGE serving. Come hungry if that's what you intend to order.

This wasn't my first time eating Doughboys Donuts, but I had 2-3 day old Doughboys (which were still good), so this was my first time at the actual location and my first time eating FRESH doughboy donuts. 

Sometimes you just get a craving for donuts and this was the day. We arrived and were greeted immediately. The employee behind the counter was friendly and helpful in our decision making process. We ended up leaving with half a dozen and a baggie full of (huge) donut holes.

Of course, the donuts were as good as you've been told. I tried the old fashion, sugar, maple glaze, and donut holes. ALL of them were delicious but my favorite was the holes. Seriously, these things were huge. Whenever that donut craving hits, be sure to give Doughboys a try.

We came here for brunch on my birthday and really enjoyed it. Food and service was exceptionally good. We parked in the parking structure next door which is convenient and free for first 90 minutes. They also offer valet service (they validate too).

We didn't expect this place to be part of Kimpton Canary Hotel. We absolutely love the ambiance. The atmosphere is warm and cozy. The dark wood furnishing, warm wall colors, leather seats, wood beams, hard wood floors and Persian-style area rugs provides relaxing sophisticated dining atmosphere. Their dining area is divided into 3 different sections. We had booth seating and it was really spacious.

For brunch, we went with roasted pork belly benedict and short rib & sweet potato hash. Our food came out reasonable time and was perfect. Good portions too. Oh man! The short rib was savory and sweet, braised to perfection and satisfyingly good. Chimichurri sauce marries nicely with sweet potatoes and eggs. Runny eggs and herbs adds umami presence to the dish. The pork belly was amazing in every way. It was super rich, fork-tender and flavorful. It was served on english muffin with carmelized onions, home fries and poached eggs, and drown everything in buttery hollandaise sauce. If I weren't watching my cholesterol, I'd definitely eat this stuff every single day. Just make sure to have defibrillator on stand-by.

Highlight of the meal was the complimentary smore pot de crème  dessert  that I got for my birthday. The staff came over to our table and belted out a Happy Birthday song. OMG! So yummy. It was like chocolate heaven in a jar, with a fluffy marshmallow cloud on top. It had the texture of chocolate creme brulee with a graham cracker crumb middle layer.

I'm a big fan of this place and look forward to coming back.

It's been a while since I've been here. Definitely one of my favorite stops in SB.

Place is popular dining destination and often times there's long wait. Fortunately, We came on late afternoon on weekday and it was hardly crowded. Got seated right away outside on the balcony which offers amazing view of the harbor. Definitely the best seats in the house. The restaurant is located on 2nd floor, accessible both by stairs and by elevator. They don't take reservation, but worth the wait. 

We started off with a craft beer and a cup of the clam chowder. Their clam chowder was really good and had a good amount clams in it. Excellent texture and flavor...reminds me of delicious clam chowder I enjoyed during my visit to New England. Between two of us, we ordered seafood cippino and seafood pasta. Love the cippino, which in my opinion is best around. The broth was plentiful and super flavorful. It was loaded with lots of seafood, which was perfectly cooked to plump tenderness (check out picture and video that I posted. Be prepared to drool!) Our meals came with complimentary bread, perfect for soaking up the incredible juices. We must have requested at least 3-4 more helpings of bread, so addictingly good. Seafood pasta was fabulous too. The shrimp and scallops were big and juicy, accompanied with a lovely sauce. We both ate every morsel, continuing to eat it for the flavor long after we were satisfied, probably would have licked the bowl if there wasn't too many people around...hahaha!

All in all, fabulous seaside meal worthy of many more returns. Good friendly and quick service too.

Wow - seriously under whelmed. the serve was not personable. Menus and later all dishes were dropped with no details or even a simple "enjoy". The waiter could not give good recommendations regarding entree choice. So we, started with duck based on other yelp reviews - it was the best dish of the night. the filet was cooked well but very uninventive - very bland. I should have asked for steak sauce. The red snapper was dry. Three glasses of wine later and two deserts and no sign of the server - the maitre d' finally stopped by to ask how the meal was and we finally had the chance to inquire on the flavors of sorbet. 

All in all a very disappointing "gem".

My husband and I decided to head to the Landmark for a burger and watch a few innings of the Phillies game. We were greeted by the manager, TOM. My husband asked for a table near a TV and his response was "It's a little too late to be picky, the game already started"...REALLY??? 

Overpriced bar food, friendly waitresses, terrible parking lot
Won't be going back.....


Update Jan 4, 2017
Still haven't been back LOL

The food is fantastic.  The bartenders are spiteful sectarian shrews.  After my party of four spent money on burgers, beer, and the juke box (I left a 40% tip) on a slow week night, my party was insulted by the bartenders. The woman behind the counter ordered one in my party to get up from the booth and come to her at the counter then told him we were not to play rap music on the juke box again. Not only did we spend money and tip well, we played music on the juke box that they supply with selections the patron has the choice to choose from and they are dictating what music we can select and ordering us not to play the music of our choice. I'll still buy burgers there but I'll let the shrews wonder why I never leave a tip.

Ordered delivery via app.  

On Friday, 7.31.15 it was awesome.  Tuna salad platter huge and tasty.  Onion rings the absolute bomb.  Fabulous.  

Ordered today, 8.2.15, tossed salad said on menu it came with meats and cheese on top - not so.  Forgot salad dressing.  Zucchini sticks wimpy and oldish... Maybe worth 2.25. NOT $5+.  Had high hopes after how awesome the onion rings were.  The sweet potato fries grease soaked and small.  Not very fun.  So sad, because two days ago they made me so happy.  Now I don't even feel I had a dinner.  Boo.

Four and a half stars. Where my clap emojis at? Because this location of Jeannine's has got it figured out! Awesome service despite a full house and growing waiting line-- three different people made sure we didn't need anything whenever I broke eye contact with my date. Park in their dedicated lot, and order at the counter while your dining companion snags a table. Try to resist the huge pastries, because portioning here is for feasting.

Large beverages are no joke here! I was proper caffeinated for the day with our sweet drinks; I preferred the dark mocha over the havana latte. Seasoning is DIY, but the fundamentals were delicious. I definitely had FOMO watching the banana kahlua french toast go by (challah for the yum), but I can't deny that our breakfast burrito and Dungeness omelet hit the spot. They weren't shy about packing my fluffy egg bed with crab meat, the fruit bowl was appropriately ripe, and the potato medley wasn't too greasy. A variety of hot sauce bottles are available to dine with by the water tap. Pick a biscuit instead of toast if you can, the sourdough is the dullest thing here.

Someday I'll be back to stuff my face and try: matcha chai latte, flat white; lemon tea bread, almond bear claw, blueberry streusel muffin, pineapple coconut scone; lobster benedict, apple jack or banana kahlua french toast, lemon poppy seed pancakes.

The hype is real, y'all. Four and a half stars to the best meal we had on our trip. The sides were the least interesting things, which is understandable. Green beans were grilled and seasoned lightly, and the pimention aioli with the fries was just okay. Cocktails were moderately potent and pleasantly balanced; all the local classics were available as signature options.

Special of the day was fried whole soft-shelled shrimp: evenly coated in a light batter, protein cooked properly, although a touch more moist a coating than you'd expect. Lamb neck was an exquisitely flavorful masterpiece: fork-tender meat mounted on a plateau of creamy saffron fideo, capped with seasoned tomato confit. Kurobuta pork belly was a close second-favorite at the table-- tender sliced meat needing a little more sear on the outside, perched on a similarly petite plateau of Cajun-seasoned risotto, and conservative on grilled greens and broth. Compared to these two all-star plates, the beef short rib that would wow at most other venues was almost a tiny letdown: definitely more traditional flavors that weren't nearly as robust, with a slightly smaller portioning of properly cooked meat.

Service was polite and attentive throughout a busy afternoon despite our party being clearly underdressed. I'd happily come back to devour more of their menu: gumbo, gnocchi with pancetta and parmesan broth, shrimp and fish ceviche, crispy goat, braised chicken with polenta, duck leg confit with dirty rice, jumbo shrimp and grits with tasso-stewed collards, rabbit fricassee, lamb and mushroom lasagna, bacon braised field peas.

Tasty, inexpensive and open late--all the attributes I enjoy in a taco place. Al Pastor tacos had the right amount of spiciness and sweetness, the fish tacos rocked, and salsas were flavorful and provided just the right kick. Big place with a bar... that doesn't serve alcohol, but it's BYO, which only adds to the greatness of this tucked-away spot.

Wish we could rate negative stars because this would be my first. It's a shame because it's such a cool, cute concept and decor. They say first impressions are everything but after almost 3 hours for an overcooked burger, I have lots more to go on than first impressions. First I have a bias because I detest restaurants that don't take reservations, I think they are lazy and disrespectful to their customers, but it seems to be pretty common in this type of "upscale fast food restaurant " LOL anything but fast, but quality...they do have call ahead seating but warm you that you're still waiting up to an hour. We had a party of 8, which was supposed to  be 10 and seated close to the time. Yeah! That's worth the star.
But, Kristen, our server was clearly disappointed that 2 of our 10 cancelled at the last minute. She was one of the most unfriendly and disorganized servers ever, however she was good about drink refills during the 2 hours we were there (not our choice btw).  Where to start, with the food? I think a laundry list would be best:
1. At 7 pm ,out of pasta for the Mac and cheese. Really we have to wonder if the lobster mac and cheese would also have been unavailable and why when surrounded by publix and Walmart somebody didn't pick some up like other restaurants do all the time. Better to disappoint the customers and tell them for the next 7 hours no Mac and cheese. Shawn the manager claimed no other store has that quality of pasta...hmmm, doubt it. 
2. A shiitake mushroom sandwich was ordered and the lady that ordered it painstakingly explained to Kristen in detail that she wanted the sauce on the side to prevent any sogginess. Guess what it was the most pitiful tiny soggy sandwich drenched in sauce.
3. One person' order was not even brought to the table and had to be re-prepared.
4. 2 orders served ice cold.
5. 3 orders served without fries, and had to wait longer for them as well.
6. Took an inventory while waiting for the other items, 1 burger missing the bacon and 1 missing the carrmelized onions.
     So, after placing the order and still waiting to learn about the status of the Mac and cheese I of course requested a manager. Well observed Kristen speaking at length to someone we assumed to be the manager and looking back at our table and went to the kitchen. He returned and checked on a few tables near us, started toward ours and retreated. When we called him over Shawn was abrupt said they "just ran out of pasta and no store carried the quality of the their pasta". He was abrupt, and frankly acted like he could not care less. And I'm sorry to say the man needed some mints bc his breath nearly knocked us over. Not cool as a "floor manager" and not being able to talk to customers. So when our food arrived asked for the GM to another server who said they didn't have one, but could bring out another manager. Enter Amber, who again acted as she had no concerns about the wait or the poor quality of food served, until her attitude was questioned. Well Amber went into super manager mode, and promised to have things revoked and correct right away. Well within 4 minutes everybody's order was in the table, and mostly correct (overcooked and dry burgers which is a shame because they had a nice flavor). 
So why does a 4 minute meal for 8 people take over an hour and be wrong? I guess they need to clone Amber. She also adjusted the checks to 50% off due to the "quality".
Noticed while waiting for our table numerous people leaving after waiting forever for their tables and were repeatedly told "you're next" and the hostesses also has the "I don't care if you leave attitude "
Well, this yelper won't be returning or recommending this place. Apparently it works for those that are gluttons for punishment or just generously donating their time and money to the Fords Garage cause.

ehhh, Can you hear me now!? 
I'm sorry, what did you say? Can you repeat that? This is what going through the order line was like. Both my server and i could not hear each other. I thought it was my advanced, aged, ears, 'til she asked me to repeat. ;-) Soooo, no stars for the acoustics... Did you hear that?

Now, i shall shout from the barstools, get yer crispy thin crust, personally concocted, pie to die for right here!  Yes, get  the mini or the 11 inch classic, or the 11inch double crust.  You can order from either their house Artisan style creations or create your own. Over 30 toppings to choose from. Choose your sauce, your meat, your veggies, your cheese and finish with a squirt of topping if you wish.  BTW, the pizza is done in a flash. I barely had time to mull my discontent with the acoustics. 

They also offer salads on the side. Deluxe, Caesar, or Simple.. 

Sit out on the patio, weather permitting, for a totally relaxing, conversation friendly, atmosphere.

So, after my first impression of audio shock, and thinking I had entered cacophony hell, immediately thinking (pre-pie) I will never come back... I grudgingly had a change of mind and heart upon devouring my mini creation. 

When  5 stars hits your eyes in the guise of their pies... it's Amore!

Covid-19 Review: 

We have been getting many of our fresh groceries from Shoefly, and I continue to be grateful for this service to the community! 

We have gotten into the habit of ordering groceries one time per week and making a gametime decision to add in a dinner order. Picking it all up at the same time is easy peasy.

Orders for groceries are requested to be sent in by 3 PM the day prior to pick up. Available items and pricing can be found on their website and are updated each day. On the day of pick up a Shoefly team member will call to get your credit card information. When you arrive at Shoefly state in your car call the phone number listed on their sign and a team member will bring the order out to your car and put it directly in the trunk or wherever you choose. Tipping can be done at the time you submit payment or at pick up when they get your signature! And trust me the service is so amazing you'll definitely want to tip!

During Covid fire by the Monon has committed to offering curbside only, and they are nailing it! We have been intentional about rotating our Weekly carry out dinners from different local restaurants in fire by the Monon was the next in line -- and honestly after this visit we might bump them up in line and order from them again very soon! 

The process was easy. We checked out the menu online. We called to place our order and provided payment. We pulled up at the designated time and called. They brought the bags of food out to our car. They asked if we needed any condiments or silverware. We got home open the bags to find everything neat and tidy! The hot stuff was hot. The cold stuff was cold. The portions were enormous. And everything tasted amazing!

The kids chicken tender meal was enough for another entire meal, as was the pork tenderloin. 

But the real showstopper? THE DESSERTS. 
Bread pudding (like a 1lb brick of it) with a caramel-ish sauce and INCREDIBLE ice cream. This also lasted us 2 meals (even after I snuck a bite the next morning at breakfast)! I don't order dessert unless it's house made or made by someone other than Sysco or GFS. This was definitely a special recipe and I'll be back for it. 

Everything from ordering to eating was smooth and enjoyable with this carry out experience!

After a day on the golf course and an hour of sunshine by the pool, we searched Yelp for a casual seafood restaurant and found Shells on a busy boulevard in South Tampa. 

Shells hit the spot with exceptional service, big portions and of course fresh seafood. Starting with an ice cold bottle of Corona and a house margarita, my wife and I both opted for pasta with our seafood...an order of Baby Lobster Pasta w/ Shells' spicy red sauce and an order of Classic Seafood Pasta w/ shrimp, scallops, clams and mussels in a garlic-white wine cream sauce. Topped with freshly ground Parmesan, both were right there. 

This is the FLA state so we had to sample a piece of deliciously fresh Key Lime bring a very satisfying meal to a close. Throughout our meal, our server did an outstanding job of attending to our every need. Great job Shells.

Just like everyone has their hometown pizza favorite, those who grew up in Philly have a hometown cheese steak favorite. That is one of the joys of growing up in this area.

My go to steak - my plumb line - has been Steve's Prince of Steaks. When they opened their first store on Cottman I was there and have never left. You never forget your first Steve's steak.

What distinguishes this steak house is they make the sandwich individually for you. Unlike Jims or Dellasandros, there's no big pile of cut up meat they move to the grill to heat up. Here you get it prepared fresh for you. Did I fail to mention they use whole quality lean rib eye meat that is NOT chopped up? There are no sins to hide here - unlike the choppers. 

I ordered the double meat pizza steak with provolone cheese and fried onions. I also ordered fries with their famous house made American Cheese sauce on the side. And a soda.

The steak was delicious. Great roll stuffed full of lean meat, tasty pizza sauce, gooey cheese and fried onions. A cardiologist nightmare but a true Philly feast.

The fries were very good as well.

Service is always friendly and fast.

Wish my neighborhood had a bar like the Blue Monkey. On second thought, maybe it's better I don't. I'd be there all the time. 

The place was packed at 5PM. The beer list of draft and bottled beer was extensive. But even more important, they had a stellar list of bourbon choices, all available as 2 ounce pours.  The menu looked spectacular with fare far beyond the typical bar menu. 

Things didn't start out great. When we arrived we were asked...did you make a reservation? I answered no thinking why would I need a reservation at 5. I asked if they had a table and they said yes but we recommend you make a reservation. Well thanks for the advice but I'm here today and it's obvious you have empty tables. They did tell we needed to be out by 7. 

We sat down and were greeted by our waitress. She gave us our menus and brought water. She did a good job for a busy place.

We asked for a pour of Angels Envy only to be told they've been out for two weeks. So we switched up to Jefferson Small Batch which was good.

We split the grilled shrimp appetizer - delicious. I had the house salad with vinaigrette dressing - it was good with craisens a nice touch. Had the burger - obviously made fresh - with really great tasting onion rings and Cole  slaw.My lady had the fish tacos and loved them.  

The coffee after dinner was made fresh and tasted great.
 
Definitely worth a trip back the next time we are close by. But we won't try it without a reservation!!!

This is one of the Best Pizza that I have ever had. Everything about the Gladiator was Amazing! The sauce was great, crust was great, cheese was great and the pepperoni was great! Just looking at the pizza will bring a big smile to your face. The service was outstanding and on point. They were very friendly and helpful. There's always a line from what I was told. We got there at 11am right when they open and there was a line out the door. We were about 15 people from the outside door and It took about 30mins to order and get our food. The food comes out fast. They are working nonstop making the food fast and fresh. The spaghetti was really good and it comes with this giant meatball with plenty of sauce. The side salad was good as well. The pepperoni calzone was really good. I was really happy with my experience here and will definitely come back and try everything on the menu.

For a restaurant in the suburbs of Bucks County, we would give this place a solid 5-stars. The flavors are what one would expect out of a good Thai establishment. Prepared "Thai-Spicy", the dishes have a fierce heat but are very tasty too at the same time. The palate grows on you over the years, low and behold you end up a chili-head. 

Stand out plates at this family-owned eatery include the staples:

* Thai Green Curry
* Som Tam
* Pad Thai
* Basil-Fried Rice
* Drunken Noodles

They can prepare dishes from Mild to Thai Hot (around a Habanero Spicy). Do try this family owned eatery and you'll instantly fall in love with their labor of love. 

To soothe off the burn, slurp on a sweet and cool Thai Iced Tea

Getting into a very philosophical mood as I write this review. If one goes to a restaurant with high expectations and if the restaurant doesn't deliver, the disappointment is even worse than if one never had any expectations to begin with. 

Note to self - Regardless of what the reviews say, always go to a restaurant with a blank slate.

As for the reason why we were disappointed:

We used to go to this Lao-Thai restaurant in Milwaukee on Farwell Ave that used to serve amazingly tasty and extremely fiery food that we were hooked onto like crack addicts! After visiting many restaurants in the tri-state area, we found a couple of restaurants that really did justice to Thai food and in this particular case, we were hoping to find some really good Laotian and Lao-Thai fare but alas some of the dishes that they served the night we were here really fell flat on their face.

We mentioned to the wait staff while placing our order that we are used to bold, pungent flavors and mouth numbing spice levels that are characteristic of food in North-East Thailand (the Isaan region) and in Laos and that we'd like to see the real McCoy. Ordered a Tom Zap soup, a Som Tum salad and a green curry (for us) and a Tom Kha soup and a Pad See Eww (for my mother in law because she doesn't eat too spicy lately).

The Tom Zap soup was pretty decent with chunks of stewed beef in a broth that had notes of kaffir lime leaves, lemon grass and garlic but we felt that it was a little too mildly spiced for our palate. The beef was delicious though.

The Som Tum Thai arrived next. One bite of the salad revealed that they had totally skimped on the nam pla (fish sauce) and the bird chillies. It was akin to listening to an opera performance with a muted singer. We mentioned it to the waitress and she came back with some nam prik pla and some red chilly powder and gave us an explanation that in the past they used to make it very spicy and some of the patrons would return the dish saying that it's too spicy or complain that their stomach hurt the next day.

The Pad See Eww (which is a mild chinese influenced Thai noodle dish) was very flavorful and had a very nice smoky flavor. Loved this particular plate.

The Green curry was very mild and on the sweeter side. Nothing close to a real good Thai green curry. I feel my wife makes a better green curry at home after learning to make it from scratch. 

We were thinking of placing a to-go order for the Larb but dropped the idea after our initial dining experience. It took us a little more than an hour to get here and the verdict is that we were pretty disappointed.

Fusion food is a double edged sword as it is subject to interpretation and we've found few restaurants that seem to meld diverse flavors impeccably. JJ Thai sadly didn't make the cut in our books.

For starters, the menu seems to have an identity crisis of sorts. There are traditional dishes from both worlds so one wonders whether to get Steak Au Poivre or Som Tum, Pan seared scallops or Pad Thai. As for the dishes that did have fusion elements in them, the combination of ingredients didn't seem too appealing to us (the addition of Brussels sprouts to Massaman Curry, a soy tamarind sauce for the Sea Bass, Basil demi-glace for a few examples - very coerced flavors in our opinion but we could be very wrong).

We ended up ordering Thai fare: Vegetable Spring Roll, Tom Kha Gai and Green Curry. All three were decent and if anything we felt that the green curry paste seemed freshly prepared. The flavors were definitely better than some of the Thai places in Philly but we've had better renditions of these dishes in other cities at traditional Thai restaurants (without dinging our wallets). Three stars overall for what we ate factoring in what we paid.

P.S. French fries? Mashed potato? Sautéed spinach? For a restaurant that claims to push the envelope by building a dining experience that evokes excitement, you have not piqued our interest by featuring those mundane side orders on the menu.

Some times you need a double take to really uncover a gem in the rough. The first time we visited this place, it was with our extended family and a majority of them preferred very mild food and our dining experience was quite forgettable given that a lot of the dishes were under seasoned and a lot of the bold Thai flavors that we prefer were missing (not the restaurant's fault). We weren't active yelp contributors back in the days and used it mostly to check restaurant reviews.

Fast forward a little more than 2 years, we decided to try this place out after looking at the yelp reviews (not realizing that we had been here before). It was only after we reached the parking lot that the light bulb turned on.

This time around it was just the two of us and we ordered everything Thai hot and my oh my the dishes were very much spot on and to our liking. Recommend their green curry as it is tastes freshly made and not out of a can. If you are a chili head like us, we would suggest that you try an order of their Pad Phed at a Thai spicy level of heat (it's got a red curry base with barely any coconut milk) and the dish packs a sucker punch filled with fresh green pepper corns, Krachai (rhizome) and Hot Thai basil leaves. We believe that we know Thai food really well and feel that this restaurant serves really good dishes.

Safe to say this is now the hottest place in Indy. Gorgeous restaurant, with the best patio in all of Indy. The spicy chicken is indeed SPICY, and awesome. Owned by the same company as Bakersfield (2 doors north on Mass Ave), it has that same friendly, trendy, (somewhat) loud atmosphere..... and will always be busy.

A wonderful addition to Mass Ave, with a killer location and patio. I can only imagine how crazy The Eagle will be once its warm enough to be outside.

AMAZING! There is no better way to describe this brewery. It's location can be deceiving but the beer is some of the best craft beer I have ever tasted. The rotating 40 taps will keep me coming back as often as I can. You will never catch me drinking a dark beer but the chocolate peanut butter stout is life changing. It's the only stout I have ever enjoyed. Every day they have a different food truck posted up in the parking lot for when the drunk munchies kick in and all of the ones I've tried have been delicious. You can get flights in a few different sizes and each flight size cup is $2. They have indoor seating and outdoor seating where you can listen to some local live music and play a few games of foosball or ping pong. The employees are super friendly and excited about patrons trying different beers for the first time. They are more than willing to give recommendations whenever necessary. This place is heaven for craft beer enthusiasts. It is 100% a place where genuinely good people work and hang out.

I'm almost reticent to ask, but does a better beer garden than McGurk's even exist? Anywhere?

Whether I'm craving a liquid lunch or a low-key evening out, McGurk's is my go-to pub in St. Louis. They do reubens and fish and chips well, hell, even the most discriminating Irish lad would be proud. And the live music-- the bands actually hail from Ireland and if you stick around late enough, you may find yourself in a battle of shots type o'war. Proceed with caution ;)

The service can be spotty... I lounged in the beer garden this past Friday afternoon and the late lunch rush left us waiting... and waiting... but 9/10 times, I'm a happy, full and sometimes tipsy girl.

Lots of good beer on draught. And did I mention the beautifully landscaped beer garden? Come, sit and tip back a perfect pour of Guinness with me... on that note, I may be heading there right now!

I like pretty, whimsical things. Jilly's Cupcake Bar is exactly that-- pink, white and cute all over. 

I also like bee stung lips... Ryan Phillippe, anyone? 

So naturally I HAD to try Jilly's 'Bee Sting' cupcake. Standing at about 5 inches tall including its tower of lemon cream cheese frosting, sometimes more IS more. 

Yep, this luxe cupcake set me back $4.25. But when you consider the ingredients-- Madagascar vanilla cake, honey syrup, toasted almonds, honey lemon curd filling, lemon candy dust, a sugar bee, and a white chocolate and lemon honeycomb bark-- you realize that this cupcake isn't just a pretty face. This is the Bentley of all cupcakes. 

Other premium toppings for the glorious confections include Tahitian vanilla buttercream, mango cream cheese frosting, key lime custard, dark chocolate ganache and marshmallow buttercream. Jilly's also serves a full brunch and lunch menu as well as specialty coffee drinks. 

Now please excuse me while I finish off my 'Bee Sting' and put on my stretchy pants! Sigh.

Divey. Diminutive. And honestly, a little dingy. 

But damn - Verti Marte sure knows how to put together a solid sandwich!

What started as a morning running errands 'round the Quarter quickly became a soggy afternoon... and I didn't need to glance at my watch to realize it was lunch time yet I hadn't even had breakfast. After a quick consultation with my know-it-all Yelp app, I realized I was only two blocks away from a quick-serve sandwich spot. Sold!

Walking into this convenience store I was met with a line about half a dozen deep. If you're even slightly claustrophobic, know that the space near the deli area is significantly tight - to the point that I may have unintentionally given the guy standing behind me a dirty look (hey, it was a reflex) for standing a little too close to me. Accidental booty grab aside, the wait was reasonably painless as the sandwich maestro was moving and sweating to get us out of there quickly. Once my small turkey was ready to go, I scored a Blood Orange Pellegrino and was happily on my way to the next destination.

And whoa - for such a tiny place with reasonable prices, Verti Marte delivers on the size! A sandwich size queen I am not, but having access to such a large beast of a sammie was really comforting knowing that I probably wouldn't be able to eat again for another 10 hours. The premise is simple but it hits the culinary spot: crusty bread overstuffed with fresh fillings on the quick and cheap. Oh, and Veri Marte is open 24/7 - don't pass this one by!

After hearing and reading many great things about Joy Tsin Lau's dim sum and the variety offered, I rolled in with my party around 11 on a Monday. Why? Because dim sum shouldn't be limited to just the weekends. However, the aforementioned variety was limited to your standard fare, despite the presence of the dim sum carts.

Where, oh where, were those flaky BBQ pork buns? "Only served Saturdays and Sundays."

With a full schedule ahead of us, we decided to stuff ourselves with whatever dim sum options were available and ordered a dish of beef stir fried with kangkung. To put it nicely, the dish tasted odd. Oyster sauce was apparent on the vegetables themselves, but the beef tasted overly sweet and lukewarm compared to the kangkung.

In terms of decor, anything goes inside this restaurant. I fear that they may, in fact, run out of space for knick knacks, newspaper articles, and the like.

I received the worst service and was discriminated against at this mediocre coffee shop. My friends and I decided to come here to study for our finals. Right when we walked in, the older lady with the short brown hair saw that we had brought a small brown bag that had our leftovers from where we grabbed breakfast and said that she hopes we will still support their business by buying a drink. We had every intention of purchasing coffee but we had not even sat down yet and I STILL had my backpack on. Once we were settled we purchased coffee. A few minutes later, the people at the table next to us left so we decided to join our table with the other table because there were 3 of us and the tables were small. Also, there were 3 girls who did the same thing across from us so we assumed it was fine. Right when we put the tables together, the same lady from earlier came out and told us that people were leaving because there was nowhere to sit and if we could separate the tables. She told us and then was going to turn around and go back inside but at this point, I was upset and asked her if she was going to say anything to the other group because there was literally 3 of them and they had joined the two tables just as we had. But of course, there was a difference which was our skin color. Once I pointed that out to her she felt pressured to do something and was like "oh I didn't see them" and of course that was because she was not looking! She was only making it a point to address my friends and me. So we took the tables apart and left. I will never return to this coffee shop and the discrimination that it serves.

The very first time I went here was my first year of college at UCSB. I remember that time being super delicious and flavorful. However, every time I go there now, I am very disappointed by the lack of flavor in the chicken and vegetables. 

It is a great price though, especially for the portion sizes! You have to get the creamy Sriracha mayo and teriyaki sauce on the side! That is what gives the food the flavor, plus it's just super tasty.  

I personally recommend getting the mini size. The container looks small, but trust me it's more than enough! The only difference between the mini and the small is that the small has more meat!

four words... BUFFALO CHICKEN CHEESE FRIES. 

I cannot count how many times I have had these fries. They are soooo freaking good!! The best IV drunk food, but I have also had it plenty of times undrunk and it is still the best. If you come to IV or you go to UCSB, you cannot leave without having these (unless your vegan or vegetarian of course)!! They are one of the most quintessential IV foods. Please go try it!

Good place to come eat and get messed up! 
Their drinks and food are both super affordable and tasty. 

I recommend getting any of the fish bowls! My personal favorite is the Shark Attack (comes with a toy shark) or the Electric Twist! ALWAYS A GOOD TIME HERE! 

Plus the food here is priced well and I would say on the cheaper side. So if you just trashed and ordered lots of food, the bill won't be super super expensive... hopefully!

My gosh, I've been on a good coffee roll!! This place hits the SPOT. Out of all the coffee shops I've had in SB county, this one is in my top 3. 

I love the aesthetic of the store. They have gnomes everywhere! They also have this cute little card shop right as you enter. Perfect study spots in the back of the store/ outside. 

For drinks, if you like sweet things I definitely recommend getting the snickerdoodle latte! I also really like motion potion (matcha, espresso, vanilla)! Other popular drinks are: the ray of sunshine and the fruit smoothies!

The best pastry dough I have ever had! So soft, pillowy, yet flaky and crispy at the same time! 

I definitely recommend getting 3-4 per person and mix and match flavors! Maybe even get one of each! My personal favorite was the hongos and the customer favorite is the carne. Whichever flavors you get, it will be delicious! Also, the filling to pastry ratio was just perfect. Not too much filling not too much dough(: 

Also, can we please applaud their packaging and how eco-friendly everything is? I should have taken a picture of the togo bag they gave me but it was so cute and recyclable!

Very solid steaks for cheap, definitely the best I've had in West Philly.  A standard cheesesteak comes with mayo and a slice of provolone cheese melted under the meat- just how I like it!  My sister loved her sausage, egg, and cheese sandwich on an everything bagel.  The employees are super nice and there's a great selection of soda, juice, tea, etc.  I don't think the decor or the ads and signs on the walls have changed for 35 years, but it makes this place all the more endearing.

CASH ONLY

Horrible!  Several weeks ago I inquired (both via their website form and leaving a voicemail during normal business hours) about having the Cake Bake Shop make our wedding cake.  After almost 2 weeks later, Janet (events manager, I believe) called me back and we scheduled a tasting appointment. She took my debit card information over the phone and let me know it was a $50 charge (which was fine because if we ended up moving forward it would apply to the balance).  Later that evening, I read reviews and decided I did not want to move forward with the tasting so called her back and cancelled the appointment - which she said was fine.

Two days later, I received an email from Janet responding to my original email inquiry asking to set up the cake testing.  I wrote back explaining we already canceled and she responded back saying she apologized for the error.  The next evening, I received a voicemail from Janet letting me know she would like to set up our cake tasting appointment.  I was really confused and called back and left her a voicemail explaining we had already spoken a number of times and we are not interested in working with the Cake Bake Shop any longer.  

Today, I looked at my bank account and there are two separate charges in the amount of $109 and $124 to my account.  I have never been to the shop, eaten any of their products and cancelled the appointment the same day we originally made it.  I'm very concerned why my account would be charged.  What.A.Nightmare! 

I had called two times this morning trying to talk to someone - during normal business hours - and again, No one picks up the phone so I called my bank.

She finally called me and and did apologize for what had happened and assured me they have since shredded my cc number.  She asked for my address as she wanted to send me a giftcard to at least come in and try them out.  I thanked her and gave her my address.  It has been 2 weeks since that occurred and still no giftcard in the mail (and both us and the shop are located in Indy).

Would not recommend working with this organization for your Big day as it will only cause headaches.

Well, a lot has happened since my last review on May 28th. A few days later, I got a very nice private Yelp message from the owner (the person I had met last fall). She was very honest and seemed to appreciate my comments. She said they are breaking in a number of new servers and while that was a fact, it was really no excuse for hit or miss experiences. I wrote her back and then focused on the appetizer timing issue. We then exchanged several messages that evening on the subject. She seemed very eager to not only fix the problems, but also to let me know she was actively caring about the business. I told her I'd be back sometime for another go, but I didn't say when that would be.

So I did that. And my experience was completely different: excellent in every way. I didn't check-in because I didn't want to draw any special attention to myself but to rather be a mystery diner. It was a great experience. 

It was early evening and it was crowded but we were greeted within a minute of grabbing a table. Our server was friendly and took our drink order promptly. She came back with the drinks and took our food order. We got a Shrimp appetizer (I think they were called Shrimp Poppers?) and they were one of the best things I've ever had at The Jug. They were fried crispy on the outside but moist and spicy inside and came with a sweet/hot pepper jelly that kicked butt. 

We ordered our entrees at the same time we ordered the appetizer, and the appetizer came out first. YAY! Just a few minutes after our server cleared the appy plate, the entrees came out. Each was hot and cooked properly. Our server came by to check on us several times, and offered drink refills when it seemed logical to do so. 

While this might sound like nothing special, it was to me because my last experience here was sort of like driving on a flat tire. This one was like cruising in a sports car, the way it was meant to be. It is apparent the owner listened to the feedback here on Yelp, did fix the appetizer problem and also met with the servers to bring up the experience.

Had there not have been a 45 minute wait at the Mexican chain restaurant across the street, we never would have come here. But there was, and we did. 

We used to live nearby to this place and we came in about once every 2 months. Back then, the food was decent, the salsa was unique and tasty, the service was good, and the prices were fair. But that was over 10 years ago. 

So last night, we found ourselves inside. And from start to finish, the experience was just as bad as all the unflattering reviews here would have you believe. 

2 little kids who belong to the staff or owners were screaming and playing in the lobby and running around the restaurant in the aisles where patrons were eating. Last night it was plastic sword fights. I got stuck in the leg on the way out the door. 

The prices were modest, but caveat emptor, yelpers. Those prices come with the worst, uninspired so-called Mexican food I've ever seen, poorly maintained public areas (like ripped up booths), pre-dirty tables (don't worry about spilling food on your table because there's already some there from the previous occupants), absentee servers, and extra attitude once you get a server at your table - he's obviously got so much else to do that is more important instead of waiting on you; no wonder he's miffed he's got to stop and take your order.  

And there's also an obscene corkage charge if you BYOB: three bucks for beers and four dollars for bottles. 

The cheese in my enchilada was weird, and the red sauce on top was thin and had the same taste as the salsa that was brought to the table. The delicious salsa I remembered from years ago is but a distant memory. 

Had I tilted my plate at a slight angle, the guacamole on my chalupa was so thin and watery that it would have run off. The tortilla on which the chalupa was stacked was cold, chewy, and stuck completely to the plate. My "beef" tacos were crunchy but beef was very dry and salty and reminded me of eating canned corned beef. To summarize my meal: YUCK. 

It's now the next morning and I am compelled to write this review because it was just that bad. We never thought to Yelp this place before we walked in because we had eaten here years before and it used to be good. It absolutely isn't good anymore. Save yourself the aggravation and go ANYPLACE else.

I will start by saying this:  I was NOT expecting to like this food as much as I did.  There was an enormous amount of flavor in every dish, despite incredibly simple names and descriptions.

First off, the ambiance in High Street is warm, cozy, and rustic.  Rustic is also a great description of their food.

My highlight:

- Seaweed Bucatini:  Wow.  This was my favorite of the night by far.  The seaweed is pulverized and used in the pasta dough, and that bright, ocean flavor leaps right out at you.  Salty, cured lobster roe is grated on top, and the salty brightness comes together to make you feel like your mouth is at the beach.  Terrific flavor.  Plus this is just *stunning* on the plate: the pasta is black, thanks to the seaweed in the dough, and the lobster roe is this vivid red... it's a really exciting thing to see and to taste.  I've posted a photo as well.

Every other dish was a huge success as well.  Tortelloni with asparagus and ramps, the lobster tartine (like an open face lobster roll... on house-made bread), the lamb tartare... every dish sang, and most were presented beautifully as well.  But the bucatini was so vivid I had to give it the starring role in this review. 

Pro-Tip 1:  The bread course is not included, but we ordered it.  I wouldn't do so again, only because I'd rather have tried another small plate in its place.  The bread was great, but it took up valuable stomach space!

Pro-Tip 2:  Three of us shared four small plates, the bread plate, and two pastas, and we were all satisfied with that amount of food.

Highly recommended!

Meh! I've experienced better!

( Beware: Mexican person reviewing a Mexican restaurant! )

The same way a Mexican kid gets excited with US (McDonald's) burgers, Americans get excited with Mexican (Cafe Poca Cosa) dishes.......

I'm not being racist, I'm just trying to give you a clear example that this restaurant is not the best or near the best of the dishes they pretend to serve. 

I was anxious and excited to go here because I've heard wonders about Cafe Poca Cosa in Tucson...... and it finally happened and I didn't like it! 

* Service?  the waiter talked so fast! that I was thankful I am Mexican girl who can talked 200 words per minute and clearly knew de definicion of: mole, aguacate, calabazita, chile huero, crema, chile ancho, zahanoria, birria...but....what about the older Anglo couple with hearing aids in the table next to us???

Is great and cute they write their menu in a chalk board, but i like to look at my menu on my own! and look at it longer than 2 minutes, then decide....

*food? hum...Mole: tasteless, Carne con chile huero: where is the chile huero?, tamal: is it a caramel tamal or corn tamal? salad: am I supposed to eat this or ....is this an exagerated ornament in the plate? 

I am not sure what people like about Poca Cosa.... I am always very neutral and positive but I got to say. I can cook the same dishes waay better and with so much flavor....

It was painful to pay $38 dollars!! I should've gone to Chipotle, at least their stake is tender..... 
sorry Poca Cosa, but you are exactly what your name states: You're a little thing when it comes to mexican food :(

I rarely get out to Meridian.  I mean, why?  I live a $7.00 cab ride from downtown Boise--why do I need to go to out to Meridian?  The Village in Meridian opened and I was unmoved.  Again, what do I need there that I can't get right here in B-town?  Let me be clear--I'm not a Boise snob...just more a fan of convenience.  I live in the north end...let me get what I can get right here in my hood and the rest be damned, thank you very much.  

Theeeen I heard a martini bar was opening in The Village.  Now...far be it from me to travel beyond a few miles for shopping of any kind.  Really, it's more than I can bear to deal with the traffic.  BUT...a martini bar?  I have been known to travel quite a distance on the promise of a good cocktail.  I've structured entire vacations on the allure of exotic cocktails...so...temptation finally got the better of me and on their second day of operation, off to Twigs I went (hey...I waited a whole day and a half...remarkable restraint, I'd say).

I am so glad I did.  They have a menu that includes a variety of cocktails and then they have their dazzling martini menu featuring 36 signature martinis.  So much to choose from!  I finally decided on their Razitini (vodka, Bols Black Raspberry Liqueur, lime) and my dining companion had their French 75 (Bombay dry, muddled lemon, float of champagne)--both were sensational.  I would have appreciated a healthier pour...but I'm a bit of a greedy lush.  

As good as the cocktails were, however, they are not what will have me trekking to Meridian on a now more regular basis than I'll care to admit.  No.  We can blame that on the Twig Signature Fries with gorgonzola fondue.

Gorgonzola!  Fondue!  My people!

The fries come seasoned with salt, pepper, rice vinegar, a light dusting of cayenne, and fresh chopped basil.  Perfect.  The gorgonzola...well...if gorgonzola is the cheese of the gods (which it is...don't mess with me on this people), then fondue is the perfected presentation of said cheese.  To quote our (quite lovely, attentive, and perfect in every way) server, "the gorgonzola fondue is liquid gold.  I'd like to take it home and put it on everything."  I completely agree.  It is just.  that.  good.

I also enjoyed their pear and roasted beet salad.  I got the half order, which was plentiful.  My dining companion ordered the full, which was huge.  This hearty salad is beautifully fresh and flavorful (and also features gorgonzola crumbles).  The pear vinaigrette is light and lovely.  The pears are fresh and sliced beautifully thin.  And...the final lovely touch is the chilled bowl in which it is served.  This really makes a difference as you get to the bottom and you find the leaves have retained their deliciously fresh and cool crispness. 

Beautifully designed, Twigs maintains an ambiance that is chic and modern.  There is really nothing to dislike...and no reason what-so-ever to delay....

Get to it!

Act 1, Scene 1: Get me outta here!

Black and white scene depicting Jack and Ophelia sitting in a living room with the sound of rain sprinkling outside.

Ophelia: (sighs, and walks to the fridge) What should we have for dinner?
Jack: I don't know...whatever...
Ophelia: Pizza? (rifles in freezer) Taco casserole?
Jack: Really. Whatever. (stares listlessly out the window)
Ophelia: Okay?
Jack: (unintelligible muttering while staring out rain drizzled window)
Ophelia: (slams fridge) No! Enough! We have got to get out of this house! Let's go out.
Jack: (looks up from sofa) Where?
Ophelia: Somewhere we've never been. Some place new to us! (consults Yelp app)
Jack: (gets up off sofa and looks slightly more energetic)
Ophelia: I've got it! Tin Roof Tacos! 

Act 1, Scene 2: Queso. Cuz I say so.

Tin Roof Taco cashier: Hey! What can I get for you?
Ophelia: I'll have the roasted corn taco and the grilled fish taco.
Cashier: Ok, and you? (gestures to Jack)
Ophelia: Wait! And, queso! You have queso?!?! Oh my god...queso! This is exciting.
Cashier: Yes! Got it. (looks again to Jack for order)
Ophelia: Oh and guacamole! Can I get an order of chips and guac?
Cashier: (smiling) Sure.
Ophelia: Wait. You have beer? Yes! (turns to high five Jack)
Jack: (begins to laugh) Can I order at this point?
Ophelia: Right. Sure. Of course. Are you getting beer? Because, (looks at the cashier), I'd like the black lager.
Jack: Are you done?
Ophelia: I'm just very excited. I think maybe I've been in the house too long.
Jack: Agreed. (to the cashier) I'll have a shrimp taco and a grilled fish taco.

Act 2, Scene 1: Technicolor

Server places food order before Jack and Ophelia on the table. 

Jack and Ophelia in unison: Thanks!
Ophelia: (bites into roasted corn taco and groans) Oh my god...
Jack: (takes a warm chip and dips it in the queso) Holy queso...
The scene continues with very little speaking and much groaning as the scene slowly transitions from black and white to color.

===============

Seriously, my friends, those were the best dang tacos I've had since my toes were buried in Mexican sand. Flavorful, fantastic, with a decidedly Tex-Mex flare. So much flavor! 

The prices are amazing, the food is bomb, and the service is friendly. 

Plus, they have beer.

And, queso. Did I mention the queso?

Tin Roof Tacos, you may have just saved my winter weary life.

Get to it!

I've been to Moe Joe's on a couple different occasions now and they have never disappointed.

My first trip here was for breakfast. I ordered the The Traditional, which is their basic Eggs Benedict (fine) but the star of the show was the side-order cinnamon roll. Their cinnamon rolls are huge, warm, and perfectly delicious. They are a complete breakfast on their own. They also serve a cinnamon roll french toast--which, given the pure awesomeness of their cinnamon rolls, I feel certain this would be A-mazing!

The second time I came here was for lunch. For lunch, I ordered their Avocado Melt, which our (friendly, prompt, and overall quite lovely) server immediately responded to my order by saying: That's my favorite thing on the menu!

Jackpot!

Fresh avocado, tomato, perfectly caramelized onions, smothered in melted Swiss, with a lovely layer of garlic aioli sandwiched between two ample slices of sourdough--it was a flavorful wonder. All sandwiches come with a choice of fries or salad--I opted for the salad and was glad I did. It was beautifully fresh. Even my dining companion (who had opted for fries with her sandwich) commented when she saw my plate, "Whoa, makes me wish I'd gone for the salad!"

Truly, their food is a cut above what one would expect from your average diner. They clearly display an attention to detail and an eye for fresh, quality ingredients.

Get to it!!

Two words, my people:  

Nutella Latte.

Yeah...you heard me correctly...they serve a NUTELLA latte (God bless these free thinking Baristas!).  In fact, they serve, to my knowledge, the only Nutella Latte in the entirety of Boise.  Need I go on from here?  Are you still reading?  Or are you grabbing your keys and running out the door at this point?

Ok...I'll go on--in case you need more or don't *gasp* like the sound of a nutella latte.  This place has a great casual and welcoming sort of vibe.  The baristas are always absolutely friendly and lovely in every way.  The service is a bit slow but I'll wait a couple extra minutes for a fabulously brewed and perfectly steamed cuppa heaven.  Yes, yes, I will.  (but something to think about if you are limited on time)

On Sundays, they have some sort of religious gathering and so though they look open--they aren't actually brewing.  
 
Get to it!

Came to Wok-Inn hot on the heels of the Yahoo Food article that utilized Yelp data to determine the best Chinese Restaurant in every state and which named Wok-Inn the best Chinese Restaurant in all of Idaho.

Wok-Inn Noodle is the perfect example of a hole in the wall.  It's in a run down strip mall on Emerald (next to dive bar spectacular, Navajo Room--if that helps to paint a picture of what you're dealing with as far as location).  As you approach, the front window displays a huge cluttered pile of discarded boxes.

Ok...

However, once you get past the eeek worthy entrance, the restaurant itself is tidy and the tables were all sparkling clean.  I'm not saying the decor isn't odd, though--it is.  From the art on the wall to the flat screen TV with VHS cassettes piled in front of it--it's definitely...eclectic.  

We were seated immediately.  I ordered the their Pad Thai, which was absolutely amazing.  Everything tasted so incredibly fresh.  I also tried their fried rice with beef and chicken and it was hands down the best fried rice I've enjoyed in Boise to date.  Per the Yelp check-in deal, I also enjoyed one of their egg rolls (for free).  It was fresh made and delicious.  A quick heads up for vegetarians, though--the egg roll did have meat in it. 

I was in a party of three and all of our meals came out at different times.  I attributed this to the fact that it's freshly made, they have one chef, and they get it to you the moment it's done--but a little odd, none-the-less.  Prices are right (less than $10 a plate).

I will definitely be back.  Likely, for the fried rice.  

Also likely?  I'll take my meal to go.

Get to it!

I waffled up this morning, my friends. I waffled UP.

Before I get to the intricacies of taste, ambiance, and service--let us simply take a moment of silence to reverently pause in admiration and wonder at a restaurant completely dedicated to the waffle...

...ahhhhh....waffles...

Waffle Me Up serves up liège waffles aka Belgian pearl sugar waffles. They're a yeast leavened waffle, topped (prior to cooking) with pearl sugar, which gives the waffles a lovely sweetness and crunchy exterior (while the interior is soft and wonderful). Waffle Me Up serves up 3 different types of savory waffles and 2 sweet waffles daily and offers 2 rotating daily special waffles. 

My dining companion and I ordered their B.O.B. Deluxe and one of their daily special "avocado waffles"with the intention of splitting them. The B.O.B is considered one of their savory waffles (as the toppings are more savory, but the waffle itself has the same sweetness). It's a liège waffle topped with havarti, a fried egg, bacon, maple syrup, and basil. Our server mentioned that it's their most popular waffle. I can see why. It was absolutely delicious.

The avocado waffle was a sort of version of avocado toast. It's a waffle topped with sliced avocado and cracked pepper. Wonderful in its simplicity. 

The restaurant is arranged so that you order at the counter, beverages are immediately given, they take your name, and you find a seat. Once your waffle is ready, they bring it out to you. The inside looks little different than when Guru could be found there. There are low tables as well as counter height tables to sit at in addition to a sofa if you prefer.

They serve Dawson's coffee (when I was there, their Sumatra, a wonderfully rich, dark roast) as well as milk, chocolate milk, juices, and soda. The service was wonderfully kind and attentive. Upon hearing that we'd not been there before, they explained how their waffles are made, their menu, and gave recommendations. 

I seriously can't think of a single thing this experience was lacking.

Oh! And, the waffles may not look huge, but are incredibly filling. We all left (after having eaten a waffle each) completely stuffed.

Get to it!

Came to Fork for the 4th stop of Cosmo-Con, a UYE/Cosmo tour of Boise Bars in search of the ultimate cosmopolitan.  I phoned Fork a day or so prior with the final head count for our reservations.  We had 15 confirm.  I made the reservations for 7:45pm, 15 minutes earlier than the expected arrive time of our crew (as I like to get there a bit early and make sure everything is prepared and ready to go).  I also phoned the day of the event to confirm and warn that our group would be needing separate checks.  I arrived at 7:45pm and unfortunately, they were not ready for us.  I was assured that the party that was currently occupying our space would be just another 5 or 10 minutes.  45 minutes later we were finally seated.  We ended up with a party of 17--so that meant 17 people lingering on their stairway for 30 minutes (the extra 2 people were not the issue as our table accommodated 15 and we squeezed the last 2 in).  There also was a few snafus with our checks (a drink I hadn't ordered made it's way to mine--and then after getting that removed, a drink I HAD ordered wound up on another yelper's check...oy).   

So, clearly, handling reservations and a large party in general, on a busy Friday night, is not their forte.

What they did right:

After we'd been waiting a while, they mixed cosmos for each of us and brought them to us on the stairs.  When we were finally seated, they brought us several platters of appetizers to enjoy on the house.  All the appetizers were quite good (one to note was the asparagus fries--yum!).  The cosmo itself wasn't a winner (our party gave Fork's Cosmo 2 stars of 5--personally, I gave it 3 stars of 5--but I had a sip of several others and their mixing was very inconsistent--some had lots of vodka, some too much lime, others tasted like mostly cranberry--weird but we've run into this issue at a few places, when ordering 15 cosmos at once, it seems to cause difficulty in dimensions).  

However, Fork has a great lineup of specialty cocktails to choose from.  I thoroughly enjoy their 3 in the Chamber and their A Thyme for Bourbon--both well mixed and well presented.  I also enjoyed a piece of their butter cake, which is haaaauuuuge.  My people, share it.  Firstly, because it is so ample that it is PLENTY for two people.  Secondly, because, it is butter drenched, sugar laden, and  ice cream topped--do you REALLY want to enter into the eye of this caloric sh*t storm alone?  No.  Of course not.  You must bring others down with you.

I loved Fork before this visit and I'm sure I'll love them again.  But, standing on the stairs with 16 people as we waited...and waited...and waited, I definitely wasn't feeling the love. 

Bottom line:  Maybe not the best place to bring an overly large party.  And, skip their cosmos, but don't fret, they'll have another cocktail you'll enjoy.  Of that, I'm certain.

Went here due to a tip from an out of state acquaintance who had seen it on Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives.  I, certainly, was not disappointed.  I entered to find this little hot spot hopping with activity.  The owner was standing at the beverage counter talking about wine as he poured some for a group of on looking patrons.  Pizza skins were being tossed, dishes delivered, and music playing.  Oh...and the place was packed!  They even have a sort of overflow seating area (it's an enclosed tent with heaters) and it was full of people!  

We made our way to the counter as we inhaled the heady scent of fresh basil and baking pizzas.  We went for their Mediterranean Madness which consisted of artichokes, feta, sun dried tomatoes, and kalamata olives--and then the whole thing was covered with fresh chopped basil.  It was madness!  Mad delicious, anyway!  And, hands down some of the best pizza sauce I've had the pleasure of consuming.  We also shared a Caesar salad that was fresh, crispy, and the very embodiment of what a Caesar salad should be.  

Everything was fresh, everything was delicious--and the owner and staff couldn't have been more charming.  Five star fantastic!

I've never once given a one star review of a restaurant. Ever. I never thought an experience at a restaurant could earn one star, but tonight's experience was humiliating for me. My husband, our friend, and I all chose to have dinner here after a night of rock climbing. We sat down, ordered, and got our food. The food was absolutely delicious! I highly recommend the Thali with the vegetable korma and a side of aloo partha. 

Once we were done eating, the waiter, the oldest man that works there, came over to take my plate away. He stared at me, then looked at my stomach, then back at me and asked where the food went. I went on to laugh about it awkwardly as I thought he was being funny or at least trying to. He then kept prompting me to show him where the food was, as if there was no way I ate the food, still jokingly. I thought at this point it was a little weird but was still laughing as he stared at us with a straight face. He looked at my husband and then back at me and shook his head still with a straight face. He continued to act in disbelief and disappointment that I ate all the food. He asked me to stand in front of the table to show them, kept looking down at my stomach, and even went so far as to check under the table. He asked me twice if I was done, the second time saying "are you sure you don't want more?". I watched as he went over to the table where his coworker was seated and showed him my empty plate and looked over at our table. When he came back he asked how old I was, and told me if I was that good at eating "thali" I would keep growing. I'm not really sure what that is supposed to mean, but I took it in a negative manner. He embarrassed me, my husband was extremely uncomfortable, and our friend was as well. When he came back with the check, he waited and watched what I tipped him, which as always was a 20% tip. Staring over my shoulder at the check until I was done signing. Then, when asked about dessert I said no thank you, as did my friend. We said no at least 4 times after him asking me if I was sure, and his coworker saying to me "it looks like you want dessert" and still they brought it out. 

The food here is great, the service is prompt and consistent, but this experience has ensured that I will never return. I have never had such a negative and embarrassingly awkward experience at a restaurant in my entire life. What a shame. It doesn't matter how amazing the food is. With someone like that working there, willing to be so outwardly offensive and rude to their customers, it is simply just a waiting game before they go out of business. One bad apple can ruin a bunch and whoever that old, awful man is, he has completely ruined that restaurant.


Do yourself a favor and look through the reviews that aren't "recommended" by yelp. You can do so by scrolling to the bottom of the businesses profile and select the not recommended reviews. There you will find Many examples of what I experienced, and worse. What an awful place.

Impossible. Just impossible! How does a restaurant open only two short weeks ago and manage to serve up 5-star service and food? Grapeseed wildly exceeded my expectations and gets a much deserved welcome to the neighborhood from me.

We started with a drink at the bar with a very-friendly bartender. I had the Macklind Mule, which was refreshing with vodka, ginger beer, lime juice and grapefruit bitters, served in a copper mug. Very good!

We moved to the dining room and decided to split a bottle of wine and a few small plates:

The roasted butternut squash salad - with arugula, pumpkin seeds, queso fresco and buttermilk dressing, this salad hit everything that I've learned (by obsessively watching The Food Network) is supposed to be happening in a dish. It had the sweetness of squash, with the savory and salty pairing of the dressing and cheese, topped with texture in the pumpkin seeds.

The spaghetti bolognaise with gremolata was so extremely flavorful, with perfectly cooked pasta. You wouldn't think a little gremolata would add that much to a dish, but it was a nice added zesty bite.

Finally, the gnocchi! Can we just all agree that everything is better with butter? Ok, well this dish was the star of the show with gnocchi, brown butter, brussel sprouts, pecans and topped with parmesan shavings. So decadent and fantastic!

I almost fell out of my chair when we split the bill in two and all of this, drinks and food, was only $33/each. Amazing value for what we received here.

You better check this place out quick because, once it catches on, I don't think you'll be able to get near it.

We just arrived to Nashville and the group that I was with decided to go to Hattie B's Hot Chicken for dinner.  Man I was glad we went here.  It was sooooo  good.  I got the Damn Hot heat level for my chicken.  Well let's just say that I was crying by the end of my meal.  Even the Mac & Cheese was spicy.  
The restaurant is a cute little place outside of downtown Nashville.   Even the staff was awesome that worked there.   If you like really spicy food, I would totally recommend the Damn Hot Heat Level.    

Well, if you are ever in Nashville you totally need to come here for Hot Chicken.

My expectations were too high after reading the rave reviews here on Yelp.  I should have listened to my instinct when I asked a few locals, and none of them were aware of this steakhouse.

I'll note that the steak, salad and sides were great.  They served an excellent cut of meat, which was well prepared, the wait staff were friendly and the wine list prices were the most reasonable I can recall seeing at ANY restaurant - Silver Oak (Alexander Valley) for $65 a bottle...  it's tough to find it at BevMo for that price.  

I was torn on how many stars to give, but felt a need to set reasonable expectations for others who are considering taking a 3-4 mile cab ride from downtown to an unknown place.  While the meal was excellent, in other ways they didn't set themselves apart from Black Angus or The Outback.

Examples?  Watching the cashier hold up someones $100 bill to the light to confirm it wasn't counterfit, listening to the staff discuss schedules for the coming Thanksgiving holiday (and how much they grossed the week before Thanksgiving last year), and too much smoke from the casino in a "Non-Smoking" restaurant.

Yes, it's tough to stop the smoke when your located in a casino (doors would help), it's always a good idea to check the big bills and I know people are going to talk...   but I don't expect to smell, see or hear it in the up scale place Cactus Creek is trying to be.

Cactus Creek offers a good price for a very nice dinner (especially if you're planning to buy wine), but they can definately use some more polish to become a premier steakhouse.

I am saddened that I can't work out how to give this place zero stars.

Positives: the "hook" of cheap wine.

Negatives: Decor is crossed between a vampire lair and bad English pub. Staff asked us over seven times if everything was ok, including two visits from the "manager"... it was okay... just ok... until I got home and was violently ill. Maybe I was just unlucky but how hard is it to screw up french onion soup?

The menu was limited and no specials or variation was available. 

Far better places to go for a fraction of the price

Dude. YES.

People coming here for standard (American) Chinese food takeout are missing out big time. You will be handed two menus -- order from the smaller one, not the bigger generic one!

I just got here from NY (via a year in Seattle) and was concerned that all the good Asian food would be hard to find. The jury is still out on that but my spice-loving palate was very very pleasantly surprised with the level of heat in these dishes. I'm definitely not the most precise on deciding authentic vs non-authentic Sichaun fare but I really liked the dried red chili peppers and huajiao in my dish, which was some kind of fried lamb (shang chao yang rou). $15.99 was a bit much for this but a huge amount of rice was included so I'll get over it.

Jing Jiang Rou Si strikes a strong balance between heat and leaving your insides intact and is now my regular dish (can't say the same about the Chongqi chicken). Sichuan-style cold noodles are good to start but I'd stay away from the dandan noodles here.

I lived in Seattle for 10 years. Walking into Sump feels like walking back into the Pacific Northwest, complete with interesting sophisticated decor, an ipad instead of a register, baristas with attitude and sleater-kinney on the stereo. It happened to be raining during my two visits as well.

Being a former Seattleite, I should be used to places like this. But somehow I feel intimidated here. Like, you can't order an iced mocha, for example. You have to order off menu.  The pour-over coffee was not to my taste. It tasted a little weak, actually.  I use soy milk in my coffee and it curdled. I tried a soy latte there once too and it was pretty damn good, but damn expensive.

I think this would be a nice place to take a lady on a day time date, if you want to pinky-out on a snobby coffee experience.

Every visit to NOLA, we find ourselves eating at Surrey's; it's a tradition. Located in the Garden district, this place is an old New Orleans shotgun home turned restaurant. It's extremely small with 15 or so tables. (Tight squeeze). They have an array of freshly squeezed juices and a small, simple menu that has a little something for everyone. I highly recommend the corned beef hash. Thick cuts of corned beef, boudin (my fave!), andouille sausage and tasty red potatoes- served with 2 eggs and toast or biscuit. Flavor overload in the perfect possible way! My husband wanted me to add that the bananas foster French toast satisfies his constant sweet tooth. "It is definitely delish". The decor (various paintings from local artist), the service, the amazing food and the complete vibe of this place will keep me coming back every visit to N'awlins! 
**CASH ONLY- ATM inside**

I have found my new favorite restaurant. The atmosphere was warm and cozy. Intimate without being loud. 

The food was every bit as delicious as I imagined from the menu. I started out with the fried oysters over some angel hair noodles. There was nothing about it I didn't love. It looks heavier than it was, but ended up being perfect appetizer for me. 

Main course was a difficult decision, but I went with the blackened scallops. That dish was perfection. It's going to be hard to try something new next time, because I'm just going to want that. 

Finally, since I couldn't stop eating, I got a dessert of creme brûlée that I think was coffee flavored with a few crisp beignets on top. 

If that doesn't sell it I sat at the bar and had Leonard take care of me. Along with his cheery demeanor, he also had some great recommendations, and made a mean old fashioned. 

Will absolutely eat here again. And again.

One of my favorite brunch places in New Orleans as far as the food goes. The only thing that could make it better would be bottomless mimosas. Although they do have a table champagne deal. 

The best time to go is early. If you get in before 10 am it's easy to get seating even for groups. If you wait until later it's always at least an hour wait. I can say the wait is worth it. Everything I've tried so far has been good. The iced coffee boozy drink is a great way to start a weekend. 

This is speaking to their brunch only. I have yet to go for dinner or tried the pastries.

Birthday dinner! WooHoo free dessert!!

OK.  I have to echo Jason S.'s sentiment a little bit.  (However, I do live in Brentwood/have lived in Franklin and am not a mouth breather nor a fan of chains.  I travel for business and get enough chains in Anniston, AL and Jonesboro, AR thank you very much.  When I'm home I want something authentic.)  That being said, when Gray's opened and there were so many crappy reviews on Yelp, I thought, "Damn, I was looking forward to that place."  Now I have to say, "Hold the phone just one minute here..." those reviews had to be rigged.  

NB:  When Gus' Chicken opened, much to my husband's delight...he left an enthusiastic review which got immediately filtered into the trash bin, so I know they are picky...but didn't catch a bunch of reviewers with single digit reviews and no pictures?

Ok...I'm over it.  We had a great experience and wonderful meal last night at Gray's on Main.  The service was spot-freaking-on.  JJ delivered friendly, efficient service despite the fact that the place was packed (yes, packed) and he gave us some great background info on the building that we really enjoyed.

I had two drinks, Royal Nectar and Southern Drum that were both scrumptious.  My husband had some bourbon thing that I don't remember but it was yummy too and he followed that with a beer he also enjoyed.

Dinner for me was 2 apps, shrimp & grits that was the best I've had...the cheddar grits are done as 4 cakes with BIG blackened shrimp on top.  I also had fried green tomatoes (because this Yankee girl cannot get enough of those things) and the breading was light and kind of sweet and they came with goat cheese.  My husband had steak and sweet potato biscuits.  We shared everything...all good.  I didn't waste tummy space on the fries he had but he said they were good.

Dessert (did I mention it was my birthday dinner?  It was.) consisted of chocolate cobbler, oh my so good and the only thing better was the red velvet gelato on top.

Good food/drinks, unique atmosphere, good service, an appreciative owner...we will be back a lot...a-lot-a-lot.

Take that phantom reviewers...who does that anyway?

We were searching for good seafood while spending some time at the beach. I had eaten here numerous times, but many years ago. So we decided to try it again. I'm glad we did! Awesome menu with lots of seafood and cocktail choices. 

As you walk in, there is a large patio outside facing the beach parking and Gulf Blvd. We decided to eat inside since it was raining off and on. The inside was clean and very well-kept. The service was exceptional! This was a post Covid visit, so the servers were all wearing masks and gloves. We got a booth, so we didn't feel crowded. 

The drinks were well-made. The salads and bread came out prior to the meal. I had the salad which was crisp and fresh. My friend said the bread was soft and hot. It came with a pesto dip that was very tasty.
