I ordered the rainbow trout.... it was very fresh and lightly fried to a crispy finish. It was topped with fresh crabmeat and a light lemon butter sauce. It was served with fresh broccoli that was not over cooked. I had a few bites of the garlic mashed potatoes...Both were delicious!

My friend ordered the sautéed shrimp. It had sun-dried tomatoes and a medley of other ingredients. Unfortunately, I didn't take a picture of the menu. But it was all amazing!

Will definitely return! Great overall experience :)

Added pics! Didn't take any last time!

If you are in Saint Pete anywhere near 22nd Ave., North, this is a must see! This business is an unbelievable store, deli, bakery, coffee bar, wine cave and much more! I've been to Italy and this is the closest place in the Tampabay area to having authentic Italian food. I drive many miles just to get a taste of this slice of real Italy!

Mazzaro's offers so much from the time you walk through the door.  The first thing you see is the meat market, where butchers cut the meat of your choice. There are frozen items to take home, that are prepared on the premises. The separate wine room has a huge assortment and tastings are available. 

MY FAVORITES:
1. FRESH MOZZARELLA! 
They make "the best mozzarella" I've ever tasted! So soft and flavorful, fresh as can be!
2. COFFEE BAR
There is also a coffee bar with items on the menu and all different types of coffees, lattes, cappuccinos etc. What makes the coffee bar so special is talking to the people that are there enjoying the food and coffees. Most people are either from Italy or have been to Italy and are so eager to share their experiences.

There is also a pantry to buy dry food items. these items are sometimes hard to find and always available here. There is a fabulous deli, where you can get cold cuts or prepared foods that you can eat on the premises. Lasagna to salads, they have it all! Lastly they have a bakery with hard to find Italian pastries, cakes, and cookies. There is an attached covered patio where you can eat your prepared items.

MY TIP:
I always bring a cooler with me and take things home :)

This is an Italian restaurant that specializes in homemade pasta with a rotating menu. It has about a dozen starters, another dozen pastas, a fresh mozzarella cart (which I'll explain in a few lines below), and two main entrées.

It is located across from Armature Works. The restaurant itself is in a brand new building, so it's also brand new. The decor is very comfortable and date worthy. There is a good size bar with full liquor and a great selection of wines. 

Onto the food! There were four of us, so we did a lot of sharing! 
Appetizers we tried:

1. PROSCIUTTO di PARMA aged 24 months. Very good!
2. CRUDO arctic char, heirloom tomato, pickled shallot, thai basil..This appetizer was amazing and I'd go back just for this dish! The fish was so fresh, and the pickled shallots were crunchy and filled with flavor. 
3. BREAD lemon butter, sea salt warm and delicious!

Pasta we ordered:
1. RIGATONI all' AMATRICIANA guanciale, tomato sugo, black pepper, pecorino romano 
2. RAVIOLI short rib filling, english peas, parmigiano, sage
3. TORTELLO all' UOVO egg yolk center, ricotta filling, roasted and shaved mushrooms /The egg yolk was cooked perfectly! When you cut into the pasta, it just was like an over medium egg inside! See pics
4. I Ordered the gluten-free pasta with the beef ragu, garlic, basil, 34 month parmigiano! All were very good!

For desert:
1. FIOR di LATTE GELATO -amaretto cookies, 25 year balsamic
2. BLACK CHERRY SORBETTO -luxardo cherries, maldon salt
3. BASIL CUSTARD -rum apples, streusel- very earthy 
All amazing!

* Back to the Mozzarella Cart... although we didn't order it, we watched them make it at other tables (table side) spectacular! (See pics)

Although it's a bit pricey, it was well worth it! 
I'd definitely recommend and return!

Amazing restaurant! I came here before and it was the same ....amazing service and food!

We went on a Friday night, it was busy... The weather was gorgeous, so we sat on the patio overlooking the downtown view. There were (4) of us... We ordered cocktails and a bottle of wine. The server definitely knew the menu, the wine list,  etc. 

I ordered the 3 course menu. ... appetizer, main entree, & desert. 
I had the tomatoes with burrata appetizer... fresh and seasoned with their famous salt. The burrata was soft and tasty. My friends ordered the calamari. It was delicately fried with a light batter and not over cooked! Great! Another had the arugula salad (good).

Main entrees: 
The Angus beef....It was sliced, medium rare (as ordered), with a side of mouth watering béarnaise. The side of brocolini was bright green and firm and fingerling potatoes (looked great, but I don't eat them). We also had Salmon and Grouper dinners. The Salmon was so moist and the skin was crispy! Fabulous! The server brought out the signature salts (see pictures) and also bread for the table.

Last was the deserts... The server brought out a huge ball of cotton candy (huge smiley face!) I had the crème brûlée with Kahlúa soaked dates on the inside... The top was perfectly crunchy and inside the center was so smooth & creamy! The dates were decadent! We had the sorbet too. 

This is a "must return" type of restaurant!

Fresh tasting food...clean establishment, covid protocols being practiced. Service was pretty quick and the atmosphere was ok.

Happy hour specials on beer wine and appetizers. We tried several appetizers:

The Tako Yaki, an octopus type fritter was really tasty. Soft on the ibside, crunchy on the outside. The octopus was tender.

The Gyoza appetizer are dumplings with pork and veggies. Definitely a good choice.

Last appetizer was the Shrimp tempura. It was good for tempura. The batter was light and crispy, but not a lot of flavor. Definitely needed some type of spice.

Onto the sushi rolls... all prepared really well. Also the smoked salmon was good. My friend had the Ramen soup.... Excellent!

Would definitely recommend this restaurant. Will return.
Still 5 stars! I've been here several times now, and the food is always consistently amazing! The breads and pastries are made on site, so good!

Good Mexican food, nice ambiance, and great drinks! Located in Sparkman's Wharf where the Hooters previously existed. They've done an excellent job of making it into an entirely new restaurant.

I had the frozen flight of drinks... Absolutely recommend! Seriously cold, sweet and delicious :)

Next was The Texas style beef and cheese enchiladas with the red sauce. The sauce had a tangy flavor and lots of juicy shredded beef. Maybe you could use a little bit more cheese. Rice and beans were very good as well.

Overall, I've been a few times since they opened and have enjoyed each time I've been. Will definitely return and recommend!

I have to start by saying that I don't normally post negative reviews unless something is drastically wrong. During this post COVID-19 pandemic, I have given a lot of grace to restaurants, as I know this is a very trying time. I think the owner/manager of this place needs to know how serious this is. If I could give the cleanliness of this restaurant less than a star I would have. I walked out before I even ate. I haven't walked out of a restaurant in years.

I went to wash my hands before ordering, and the bathroom was absolutely filthy! This was 10 minutes after they had opened! This looked like months of not cleaning!! The garbage was full and the floors looked like there was a back up and no one ever cleaned up afterwards (no, it's not a design in the floor, look at the caked up dirt in the drain). During this post covid time, there is no excuse for this type of filthiness!

I can't eat at a place if the bathrooms are filthy because that's what I can see! I can only imagine what the kitchen looks like where the food is being prepared.

I've been to a lot of restaurants since this pandemic began and they all seem to be taking extra steps to make sure that their place is clean. I'm not sure why this place is so dingy and filthy, but they definitely need to hire a good cleaning crew to come in and clean this place from top to bottom. 

Hopefully, this will be a wake up call to the owner to care about their restaurant.

Went with seven people in our party on a Sunday night. We did have reservations as this is a very small restaurant. Reservations are recommended.

They have a small bar. That night they were having half off bottles of wine, which was a really great deal!

Once everyone in the party arrived, we were seated. The server was very knowledgeable and very helpful. We had the crispy eggplant appetizer to share. It was a very tasty dish, but was fried.

I ordered the octopus salad and the house salad. The octopus salad was paired with fried cauliflower and some spicy peppers, olives, etc. it was good, however, I wish there was a little bit more octopus, as it was very light on the octopus.

The house Salad was good... It had a balsamic dressing with candied walnuts, greens, tomatoes, creamy gorgonzola & dates.

Others ordered the salmon dinner, pork shank, spaghetti & meatballs, risotto, & ravioli dishes. All were very happy with their orders. Especially the pork shank was falling off the bone delicious!

Would definitely recommend and return.

Wonderful restaurant!! The decor is fresh and interesting to the eye (see pics). We waited at the bar until the rest of our party arrived (12 in total). The drinks were good and we had an appetizer while we waited. 

We ordered the cheese board and the charcuterie board. They came combined on the same board... Three meats, three cheeses and some side accompaniments! Hard and soft cheeses were delightful ... chef's choice. The sides were grapes, petite pickles, spicy gourmet mustard, Marcona almonds (amazing!), and chestnuts that were preserved! I'd never had preserved chestnuts before... very sweet, but still firm and nutty in flavor! Excellent!

As most of our party arrived, we headed to a gorgeous large table (see pics) off to the side of the cheese bar. We ordered a lot of food. 

Some of the stand outs were actually the appetizers : the wild boar, stuffed red peppers, sausage focaccia and oysters were delicious! The salmon dinner was cooked perfectly! Everything was exceptional including the service! Will definitely return.

Very good venue... Came here for happy hour with friends... they have a decent happy hour. see pics of the menu... We had drinks and a few appetizers , everything was good!

We had to tuna carpaccio.... Sliced thin with a
little hot sauce and some pickled cucumbers .....delicious!

I also had the chicken piccata with the caper berries it was absolutely amazing! Substituted spaghetti for asparagus, roasted.
Thoroughly enjoyed the meal! Will return!

This was my first time in for the 2021 season, and the weather was beautiful. Throughout this entire evening I can't say enough about my waitress Aubrey. She was attentive, funny and made the experience better than normal. 

I have been traveling for work and decided to stop in on my way home. She asked what I was in the mood for and I asked her what she recommended. She said she felt like they had the best calamari in the state so I had to give this challenge a go. I think I'm going to have to agree with her! She suggested that I try the gumbo. It was good gumbo, but I will be honest there are 20 better choices on the menu so don't waste the space in your stomach on the gumbo. Save it for dessert! 

Next we get to dessert. I forget exactly what she called it but I remembered that it had lemon and blueberry with a blueberry sauce. I straight closed my eyes and went to heaven with this cake. It was so delicious that you wanted to take your time and savor each bite and you were so sad as you found yourself getting to the end of the plate because you knew it was almost gone.

The overall experience of this restaurant is always fun. Everyone's happy, the place is bustling and there's just a chattiness and happiness in the air.

I think it also helps that the windows are so large and so much natural sunlight comes in and you also always have a view of the water.

The food is great, but their staff made it even better!

Oh thank you for being pretty much the only restaurant we could find still serving dinner at 10pm on a Friday night!! We got so caught up in wine and beer tasting that time escaped us, and everywhere we had in mind previously was about to close.  We were very graciously welcomed in after checking with the kitchen. Our server was lovely! Name escapes me, but glasses, shorter hair-very polite, professional and sweet. Food was great. Boyfriend had a FANTASTIC Croque Monsieur, and I was feeling like I needed some vegetables, so I chose the endive salad with apples, walnuts, blue cheese and grilled chicken. I noticed some beautiful looking steak dishes on another table, if I am ever in the area again, I will definitely keep this place in mind to return to!

Sad that we didn't have the chance to review the food, cause the owner was terrible. 

They check your temperature when you come in, which is perfectly reasonable and something we appreciate! My mom made an off hand joke about why it's necessary since we're all vaccinated (maybe a little ill placed, but certainly in good humor), but nothing more was said, we got our temperatures checked, and we sat down to order. 5-10 minutes later, the owner comes out of the kitchen, and scolds my mom across the entire restaurant about how if the restaurant says we have to check temperature, we have to. "Scold" as in a very demanding, harsh, and loud tone. Which makes no sense, because my mom never said no to the temperature check! We're from the Bay Area mind you, where temperature checks + vaccine checks are everywhere. 

My parents keep asking what they did wrong, the owner keeps on saying we have to follow their command (which again, we did). I then try to step in, which the owner responds to by saying that he wasn't talking to me! The same person that was yelling at my parents said I couldn't speak up lol. Then he told us to leave, which we gladly did at that point. 

Terrible.

Edit: the owner claims I'm lying; would love if he could say exactly what I lied about!

Gung Hay Fat Choy..  Chinese restaurant #2 n the 2nd day of Chinese New Year.

Consistent good Chinese American food.  I love their egg foo young with the crispy outside and flavorful combination of eggs, meats and vegetables.  Pour some sauce over it and boom.. pure deliciousness.

The owners are very friendly.  They are always at the restaurant working.  I actually came here on the actual Chinese New Year's Day and was surprised to find that they had taken the day off to celebrate - good for them.

What brings me back to Chinese Duck House is the consistent servers, consistent small, quaint and clean restaurant and good, solid food.

I have been a tremendous slacker when it comes to Yelp reviews. It's only fitting that Resurrection was the place to revive my interest and get me reviewing again.

Let's start with the environment.  The space is open and airy, and the window opening out to Grey's Ferry makes it feel larger than it is.  I've seen some complaints about noise and overcrowding, but neither of those was a problem on the Monday that I visited.  The music was pleasant, if a little theme-y, and at no point did it feel like it interrupted the meal.

And the meal?  Yes.  Delicious.  The pickled fruit/veggie plate and the corn cakes provided an opening burst of clean and exciting flavors.  The Miatake Mushroom entree and the Twice Fried Chicken were both fantastic as well, and reasonably priced to boot.  It's nice to see the emphasis placed a little more heavily on the menu when compared to Local44, but the beer list is definitely solid, with a promise of future rotating craft and seasonal beers on draught in addition to a stable of excellent bottled beer.

It looks like another home run from Brendan and Leigh and I look forward to rediscovering Resurrection as it's menu and beer list evolve.  Approve.

I was about to give them four stars because I had to walk across the street to get a beer, but that seemed pretty frivolous.  New places always open with hiccups, and I arrived during the last hour of service, and had an excellent experience (an employee also showed up with more beer while I was in the middle of my meal).

I ordered the rib plate with the four cheese macaroni and the pork & beans.  The ribs came out naked, and I gave them a taste to check out the smokiness.  They were definitely spot on, and I immediately began sampling each of the six sauces that rested on my table (1 mayo-based, 1 mustard-based, 1 vinegar-based, and three of your "traditional" types).  Of the three more traditional sauces I really enjoyed the Nola East because it added that extra spiciness that helps you to appreciate your beer that much more.  The sides were very enjoyable and weren't just there to take up space in my stomach.  By the time I finished my mac-n-cheese I thought about getting up to order some more.  Thankfully I didn't because the owner gave me a free piece of sausage to try that was pretty spicy and delicious (I drenched that with the mustard sauce).  I really enjoyed the meal, the restaurant was pretty clean, and the staff was really friendly.

Mcclure's is definitely a very small restaurant, with around ten tables total in it.  I imagine eventually someone will write a review hammering them for a long wait, bad service, and "not that great of BBQ."  I would immediately avoid these reviews and trust the people that showed up when they were about to close and were still served delicious BBQ.

I wrote an honest review of our experience at this restaurant on Facebook & they reported it as abusive & had it removed. 

I suggested they change their info. It says "walk-ins are welcome", when they actually only take reservations. This would have been important information to know. When we arrived and asked how long the wait was for two, we were informed "We don't work like that." They suggested take out & said it would be about 10 minutes. We were there over 30 minutes & there were 6 empty tables the entire time. Had they seated us, we would have been at least halfway through our meal. 

Our takeout was in our opinion awful, but hopefully the food is better when you eat in. One of our dishes was miso soup. It was a Southwestern concoction with a lump of black bean paste, vegetables & a chunky cauliflower broth. I also disliked the nachos and Shepard's pie. The plantains were not bad, but not any different than you can make at home. It is all very expensive. 

Since they have nothing but good reviews, I think they do their best to remove anything that is not flattering. So if you do try Blue Sage, at least remember to make a reservation.

What a tucked away surprise!!! This place seats like 12 people maximally, so I would not recommend taking a group. But for the times when you're on your own for lunch or having a lovely lunch date with your bestie, Milque Toast is a go-to. The basic premise is this: a great piece of bread topped with something creative and wonderful. Many of us have all seen iterations of this type of food on Instagram with the familiar hashtag "fitfood" and have silently wished we were so creative as to put something similar together ourselves. Now, you don't have to. You can go to Milque Toast and taste their chef's most imaginative creations and classic remixes. Think lox meets a delicious slice of rye bread and makes their special, gravlax. They have a 3/$15 and a 5/$20 special so you can mix and match from their frequently rotating selections. The 5/$20 would be perfect for two to split for a light lunch. 

Please go here! You won't regret it!!!

Him noisily chomping on dungeness crab legs:  "Honey, are you going to Yelp this?"

Me, pouting: "Yep."

Him: "Wow, you keep this up and you'll be the utmost authority on buffets."

*crash*

*bang*

*ShAtTeR*

My dreams of being the millennium's answer  to MFK Fisher just flew out the window.  Oh my Ruth Reichl!   

So, as is becoming glaringly obvious, I eat at buffets.  I guess you could say I am a buffet connoisseur if that statement in itself were not so completely oxymoronic. . but there it is.  I never pictured this when I was growing up, dreaming of walking in Julia Child's foot steps but there I was, eating at the umpteenth buffet of the year.  

Carvings is a the new buffet in Harrah's and had been listed in a dining guide as an "upscale buffet".  All the other buffets just said "buffet" but I was suckered in by the "upscale" part.  I don't know what I was expecting but . . .well, this place sucked!  There, I said it.  I hate giving bad reviews to restaurants because I work in one and I know how hard the work is and so I tend to try to respect it but this place does not deserve my respect.  

When I hit a buffet I tend to walk the whole line, scope out any favorites and plan my eating strategy.  As I walked this line, my heart sank as my stomach did flip flops.  Grey guacamole on the "Mexican" buffet.  Refried beans so stiff you could use it as molding clay.  The most pathetic salad bar I have ever seen on a buffet - this salad bar made Sizzler look like The Bellagio buffet!  Maybe it was upscale 'cause it had one of those faux wood ovens. .. but when you're slinging pies that look no better than Tombstone out of that baby, what's the point?  Oh, and they had mushroom risotto. .. too bad it looked like baby vomit.  The other thing that bugged was the the guy with the big toque was walking the line back and forth but didn't correct any of the obvious flaws in his food.  WTF?

The only edibles for me were the "Kobe" roast beef that they sliced so thin you could still see your plate through it and the mashed potatoes - dirty style 'cause these fools were too lazy to peel them.  The honey was happy with his crab legs but  that's about all he ate which is unusual for him.  

The dessert looked promising but some were beyond stale.  They did have bananas foster which I enjoyed and a fresh crepe station which I planned to hit.  But this is where this place really lost any stars it might get. . .they announced that they were going to break down the buffet - essentially saying . . . slap on the feed bag double time kids, 'cause we're shutting down. . .and the first station they break down??  Dessert!  Hellooo????  Any fool would know that should be the LAST station broken down . . but no. . . and those little dessert station line guys were fast 'cause they had those racks filled, zipped up and in the walk-in within two minutes.  

One star for the waitress that was so diligent in keeping our drinks filled that I walked out of there sloshing like an old water bed.  

Skip this buffet, instead go to Toucan Charlie's at Atlantis - take it from me, your local buffet authority.

Bon Apetit!

Where cool cats bring their lady friends. 
Ciros is definitely one of the most romantic date spots in Tampa and just a really neat concept. 
Make your reservation over the phone or online (or on open table) several days or weeks in advance. The day before your reservation someone will call you to confirm and give you a password. Don't forget it! Dress snazzy, no shorts, sneakers, ripped jeans etc after all this is a speak easy where gentleman go. 
Drive to a parking lot, feel completely lost because there are no signs (they don't want the feds/coppers to find them, they are a speakeasy after all). You will finally spot the secret entrance under condos hiding behind the community pool. 
Knock loud. They will open a window and ask for your password. The door is locked so don't bother trying to sneak pass the lookout. Walk through a dimly lit bar to a dimly lit both with curtains they keep closed! There is a tiny plant stand as your table. We knew the small table issue I'm advance so we came here for drinks and appetizer spot before our dinner reservations. The food menu is lighted so no worries about not being able to read it.
The drinks are fabulous, every ingredient is fresh and mixers are made in house. You will pay a pretty penny because the atmosphere is from prohibition but the prices are not (13 dollars a drink).
The duck fat fries are worth every bit of the 10 dollars you pay for them so if you like french fries, get those.
This is a quiet bar, no loud rowdy parties allowed so don't bother bringing the bachelor party, but it's a nice stop on the honeymoon or in my case, our anniversary.

Very friendly service as soon as we came and great food! I had the single burger and was able to load it with lettuce tomatoes pickles onions and shredded cheese for no extra charge. The fries were salted a lot--delicious! Very cute and clean place as well, highly recommend

My favorite thing about the Green Hills location of this Shake Shack is the vibrant crowd that is always here.  When the weather is nice, the patio is full at all hours.  At lunch time and in the evenings you can see families, couples and hungry singles enjoying an All American experience. Have they reinvented the burger?  No.  Are you going to find this burger above all else?  Another no.  But are you going to get a tasty, burger, hot fries and a fresh shake? That's a 10-4.  
It is "fast casual" in that you order at the counter, and you get a buzzer to alert you when your food is ready.  I'm a fan.  The vibe is cool. And when I have teens and college kids visiting me, this is always an easy place to take them.  Then we can wander the shops in the area, which are very nice.
One tip: Use the app to order.  Even if there is a line, you can grab your food without a wait if you ordered before arrival. Just bypass the line and go straight to the pick up. They often feature specials on the app as well.

Fun Sunday Brunch Buffet ANNNND you take reservations?? Yes please!! 
I went with my daughter on a beautiful Sunday afternoon and we had a delightful time.  You may sit inside or out.  Valet only.
I am accustomed to buffet brunches, and they are extremely limited in Nashville.  Hopefully others will take note of this success and duplicate!! It's the highest form of flattery, right!!??  We were not offered a menu, so I think brunch is the only option on Sunday mornings.
The place was packed and loud, and I loved the energy.  You may need to eyeball the line before jumping in, as it can get quite long.  Start at the side with some fruit/yogurt/croissant, as that line is typically short.  Or just get a cocktail and chill.
The buffet is inviting.  Kale salad, squash pasta salad, summer tomatoes, fresh biscuits and whipped butter, frittata, REAL bacon, legitimate grits, whole roasted pig with house made BBQ sauce, shrimp, and the best gazpacho I have had in town... the watermelon relish MADE it.  You can watch the busy chefs prep and refill as you make your way through the amply stocked line.
There is also a dessert station.  The banana pudding was a miss for me, but the pecan squares with thick shortbread well made up for that!  Rich and chewy chocolate brownies were on point as well.
Now I know where to take friends on a Sunday morning.  See ya real soon!

It's hard not to give this place 5 stars... though their exceptionally inflated wine prices really rubbed me the wrong way. More on that later. 
This is an event. Arrive early and have a drink in the lounge or bar. It sets the tone for what is to come. Take in the views. Admire the aesthetics. 
When you do arrive at your table, your every wish will be granted. You will be treated to complimentary hot and crispy fries served 3 ways (truffle aioli is tops in my book). 
The table side menu items are an enjoyable show. Those include the tuna tartare and Lobster pot pie. Both signature items. Neither disappoints. 
I highly recommend truffle butter if you opt for a steak. My father says he will never order a steak another way now! My favorite side item is the mushrooms. Just the right amount of butter and flavor.
Dessert options are fantastic. The coconut sorbet is a refreshing way to end the meal. But if you don't have room, (and even if you do) you will be gifted a tasty bag of Carmel popcorn drizzled in chocolate to take with you. A nice touch.  
Be sure to request a window seat when you make a reservation. If they can accommodate, they will. 
As for the wine prices, we dine at every high end restaurant in Nashville. These prices are not in step. My husband is a wine collector and is very familiar with the ratings and retail pricing of most of the wines on the list. While we understand and expect up charges to cover the costs of operating such an elite restaurant, we felt insulted by the amount of the up charges. I feel this should be revisited by the management. It will not keep us from returning, but I did feel the need to point that out.

I can't even begin to tell you how impressive this place is!! The discreet location in the middle of the mayhem of downtown... the incredible attention to detail in the decor and ambiance.. friends, a new day has arrived in Nashville!!! Table levitation, ya'll !!
This is a speakeasy meets Magic Castle. (LA friends, note!)
We were seated in a plush velvet booth table, surrounded by the beautiful and elegant people, in dim lighting.  The dress code is strict and everyone follows it.  Get fancied up. You will fit right in. 
I know this was only night 4 of the business being open, but trust me when I say House of Cards is going to become an Iconic Nashville destination. 
3 live magic shows are a part of your evening... 2 in the dining room.. one in a private room. (The main show runs 4 times a night. Your waiter will give you your ticket) The quality is Vegas class. You will ooooh and aaaah and applaud! 
The bar, the food, the setting, the entertainment. I am almost giddy. I am making a list of the friends I want to bring along for the experience!!! There is an Oasis of a "secret garden". Check it out. Also be sure to request a song from Thurston, the piano player. You've never seen a piano player like him. Guaranteed!  Take a moment to explore the antique card collection. They even have a pair of Houdini's hand cuffs. 
Free valet. (Valet will direct you on how to enter. Concierge will escort you once you are inside the Johnny Cash Museum) No photos or video permitted inside the venue. Reservations required. 
Prepare to be AH-MAZED! This is an experience. Plan to be here all evening!

I haven't been here in literally years... 
need to change that!
Had a lovely lunch, AND found free parking on the residential street super nearby. 
They were kind enough to seat us without our full party being present. 
The hummus had an exotic flair to it. The standard pita chips were great but the roasted carrots for dipping were amazing!!
Believe it or not, all 3 of us ordered the beet salad. Must have been the warm break in our cold weather! Yummy roasted beets with pistachio and green apple. I added chicken. My daughter added avocado. Oh, and a side of sweet potato fries are always in order. Clean plate club all the way around. 
The soup of the day was lentil. People. It was like a vegetable garden in a bowl!
If you take away anything from this review, know that the farm fresh menu is plentiful, and if you are not in the mood for a burger, you will have plenty of fabulous options!!

This venue gets it right when it comes to live music. Period. The variety is fab. The sound system is great. The stage and lighting are great. Tonight we are watching a U2 cover band. Dang! They are incredible. I feel like it is 1987!!
We also enjoy the local artists playing original music. There is live music every single night! Weekend acts will be bigger draws typically. 
Not to be missed is the Journey tribute that plays here quarterly, Resurrection. You won't believe how spot on they are!!  The Time Jumpers are here regularly, Vince Gill often sits in, and they are awesome too. Very traditional country. Many of the acts aren't country at all. Just wanted to clarify! 
Arrive at least an hour early for the more popular shows. if you want a seat. The venue is spacious but only holds about 300. The perfect size if you ask me!
This is mainly a seated venue. But there is a dance floor. The food menu is pretty good. Their wine selection is solid too. Far better than many typical live music Clubs. 
Put this place on your list to check the entertainment calendar, whether you are a local or paying an upcoming visit to Nashville. 
Parking is free immediately in front of the venue. There is a parking lot next door that sometimes charges $5, but usually not. Uber is easy as this venue is right near downtown.

I lived most of my adult life not knowing what happens behind these doors. And I admit, on my first trip, it all seemed foreign. I didn't get it. NOW I CANT AND I MEAN CANT LIVE WITHOUT IT. 
You will have Green Hills traffic and a super fun time finding a parking spot... deal with it. You will be rewarded for your efforts. Will you have to jockey to get a space at the produce aisle, yes. Will you wait in a long-ish line to check out? Yes. Will they be out of a few things you are looking for? Yes. That's just the way it goes. But I count my lucky stars that I have access to this magical place. 
For a foodie, I never stop learning here. I follow lots of TJ shoppers on insta, and they inspire me to no end!!
They have products here that simply can't be replicated. These products help cut down on my meal prep while still elevating my culinary game. 
Do I wish they were twice as big with a Sams size parking lot?? I think we all know that answer. But for a girl who never even had access to one, you will NOT catch me complaining!! Print it.

The double burger is hands down my favorite burger in all of STL. Maybe the world. I normally like to customize my burger, but trust me, don't. For instance I don't like raw onion, so I omit it on virtually everything. But please, DON'T! You wouldn't change the Mona Lisa, so please don't change this burger. Just speak the words to your friendly wait staff "I'll have the double" and smile. The onion on this burger isn't raw but its not cooked either. Its perfect and if you find yourself thinking I'd rather not have it on there it's easy to take off. Same with the pickle, they're wonderful and are the perfect bit of crunch to the tender juicy meat and soft warm bun.     

Service is generally exceptional. 

This is a great date night place. Awesome for lunch, happy hour and dinner too. 

I've taken virtually everyone I work with here. At least 15 people. Everyone agrees the food is great. Many have brought their wives back for dinner. The report is always "The wife loves it!". 

I've had a variety of items off their menu, Hanger Steak to the French Dip & French Onion soup it's all great.  

Their side carrots on my first visit were some kind of amazing, large cuts of hearty carrot perfectly cooked (perhaps sousvide?). Not crunchy not mushy. Maybe the best carrots I've ever had. On other visits the carrots haven't been nearly as good. Brasserie does suffer a bit in the consistency department. But even on an off day the food is still better than most places. 

DON'T Forget to ask about their Happy Hour Specials!

When I saw the negative reviews of Xilantro I assumed people were just being overly critical. I assumed that the criticism of the pricing was just people expecting taco bell prices at a higher end restaurant. Unfortunately, my assumptions were incorrect. 

We arrived at Xilantro right on time for our reservation, but we ended up waiting for 15 minutes to get our table. The place is decorated similarly to other modern mexican restaurants in the area, but the acoustics are abysmal. It was annoyingly loud, so much so that we spent most of the dinner shouting at each other to hear. 

We tried a few different margaritas. They are all overpriced. The house margarita is called the "top shelf" and it is $11. The premium margarita is $15 and it was good, but not $15 in Wayne good. 

We started with the $10 guacamole and the $12 tuna tartar. The avocados in the guacamole were fresh but the guacamole was extremely bland. No spice and barely any salt. It was so bland that I actually asked for salt, which is something I rarely do. The tuna tartar was mediocre. The tuna was ok, but there was nothing to the dish. It was mayo heavy and not spicy at all. It reminded me of a an appetizer you might get a second rate sushi bar. 

My entree was the $32 sauteed shrimp. It consisted of six medium shrimp and a little bit of  white rice. The shrimp were high quality but the dish had very little taste to it. For $32 I was expecting a lot more, at least a few more shrimp and some vegetables. My wife got a $28 filet. It was literately a small piece of meat over a tortilla. It was actually the only item we ordered that night that had any taste to it. 

The service wasn't bad, but it wasn't the caliber I would expect for the pricetag. There was very little insight into the menu offered by the staff. Its a level of service I would expect for reasonably priced chain, not a higher end restaurant. 

Overall, this restaurant was extremely disappointing. The food was poorly executed and very overpriced. Skipping dessert our bill came out to $150 for two people. $150 for 3 margaritas, 2 appetizers, and 2 entrees. That is a lot of money to spend on bad food.

Unless you like bland overpriced Mexican food, I would highly recommend avoiding Xilantro.

Geno's ranks #2 in the cheesesteak wars of Philly!  But damn that's almost as good as #1. That coveted 5 star goes to Pat's across the street ( sorry it's my review) Let's face it anytime you have steak, cheese and bun, how does this culinary delight go wrong?


Now I like my sandwich with provolone melting on mine while others want that pump shit called WIZ. In the end buy it with anything you want on it cause it's all good. 

My suggestions is know what you want prior to ordering or face the wrath. Geno himself laid the verbal wrath of God at my friend Ross for asking a dumb ass question. 

*Ross - Excuse me sir where do I get fries?


* Geno -  ITSSSS OVER THERE!!!!!!!! ( pointing finger in Ross's face while veins bulging out of his neck)


I never laughed so hard as my friend trembled more than the cowardly lion as he left Geno's presence. Thanks for the memory's and RIP.

Ok now back to review. Order some fries , coke and steaming hot cheesesteak. It's so damn good!

From the whimsy and coziness to it, to the mix and match 70s table cloths layered that bring me nostalgic times with my grandma, to the peaceful yet hip neighborhood it lays on its own corner, this spot was the highlight of my trip to Nashville.

The seating available for my friend and I were amongst other patrons eating that implement togetherness which I saw come into play when a young man with her girlfriend making friendly convo with 2 women sitting next to eachother. It is a small cafe but I appreciated it. 

I was introduced to this place by Fodor's travel book "Nashville" and they recommended this as a vegetarian gem with hipster demographic which they hit the nail on the head. 

For drink I had hot coffee which looks like they harvest their own beans where you can take it by the pound home, which I thought was a great cup of joe (choose between medium or bold roast). To eat I had the Armadillo sandwich which was incredible... the bread is a toasted crust of colby jack outside, with sauteed peppers, portabellas, pesto, sour cream, and a touch of parmesan inside. All sandwiches come with a side in which the choice of sides were extensive. I opted for the sweet potato casserole which was stellar; not too sweet. For $9.99 plus $2.75 for the coffee with free refills, it was a great value for the tastiness and filled me up.

We made reservations on a "fourth Friday night" in Pitman. Its kind of a thing that Pitman does during the summer. A lot of fun, cool stuff going on. On the fourth Friday in July, we made reservations for 7:30 PM - 6 people. We get there, the owner says that there is a $5 cover for the "band". My husband tells her that no one told us that when we made the reservations, we are not paying it. She says that some of the staff isn't telling people, but they should. She seats us and we have a somewhat decent dinner except for husband's sea bass that wasn't cooked all the way, it was slimy in the middle. We sent it back and it tasted worse and was now overcooked and rubbery, like the bottom of my sneaker. Dessert was very good. We get the bill - total is $197, we add 20% even though food wasn't fantastic and the "band" ended being two people that were awful and you couldn't carry on a conversation it was way too loud. The owner comes back about 10 minutes later and says the waitress is upset, we only tipped $13. She showed us our bill again and it had a new number - $227 circled about eight times right next to $197. It was NOT there on the first bill. I even double checked the bill before we paid it because someone asked if the gratuity was added in already because of the size of our party. So three people looked at it and I double checked it. The owner tacked on the cover after we paid. When she showed me the bill again, I told her there is no way I missed the $227 circled a bunch of times when it was RIGHT NEXT TO $197! My husband, as a small business owner himself, tried to speak with her and she was just boorish and ignorant. I will never go there again. This not good business to treat your customers in this fashion. I've never had a bill changed after I paid it. I am disgusted and will never set foot in this establishment again.

I have been going to The Country Club since I was 18! Things have changed in 10 years and it just keeps getting better.

I am a member and it has it's perks! Daily membership can be anywhere from $10-$20. A yearly membership runs $300 and if your in the service industry its $200. A pretty sweet deal and pays for itself rather quickly.

The pool is clothing optional never uncomfortable but definitely interesting. Some people bare it all and others not so much. Regardless everyone is super respectful and absolutely no pressure. This is not a Miami or Las Vegas style pool its just a mellow oasis. The bartenders are all super cool, cocktails are $7 and happy hour wells are $3. Hate those summer rainstorms? If your at The Country Club when this happens no need to pack up and go home.  Just head on in to the bar (clothing required) because its always Happy Hour when it rains. Its a PARTY! 

The tunes are ever changing and at night they project fun movies and also show a few popular TV shows. All while you float in the pool with drink in hand. 

I have yet to try the bottomless Champagne brunch on the weekends.  The Korean Barbecue Skewers however are delicious.

If you are a fan of no tan lines, cocktails, and relaxation then get there!

THIS IS WHAT I'M TALKING ABOUT. Bogart's BBQ is where it's at. The experience was wonderful, from the very courteous and friendly treatment by the staff (despite our entire group being decked out in SF Giants gear on a Cardinals v. Giants game day), the mindblowingly delicious ribs, to the great location (in the heart of Soulard!).
I ordered the half rack of ribs with applesauce and beans as my sides. I'm seriously getting hungry just recounting this experience, but such is the burden of reviewing delicious food. The ribs were the best I've ever had (which actually isn't saying much, since I didn't eat meat for a decade), and they don't require any post-purchase saucing which I'm a fan of- the glaze with which they're served really speaks for itself. I felt like a wild animal, desperately gnawing at the bones in order to remove every last morsel and make sure nothing went to waste. The sides were definitely up to par with the meat, and they complimented the meal really well. The beans are a MUST HAVE- if you're feeling really crazy, get the beans and the chips and dip the chips into the beans. I mean, you're already eating BBQ, might as well throw caution to the wind. 
I prefer this place to Pappy's as it felt like the owner and staff really cared about our experience and the entire place was just more boutique rather than assembly line. From the location right by the Soulard Farmers Market (go get a Bloody Mary and some beignets post-BBQ!), the cute yellow facade, and the excellent service, I'm glad I finally made the pilgrimage and tried this place out. Don't miss it if you're in STL.

A great spot in Glenside. Their indoor area, though not open right now due to COVID, is lovely and themed. They have a nice outdoor dining area too, which is indeed open right now (or you can get takeout). 

Elia has a pretty extensive menu, and offers options for meat eaters and vegetarians like myself. Today I had their fried zucchini and feta cheese pita wrap which was yummy. It's also stuffed with Greek fries. The portion was pretty big. I ordered a side of Greek fries (which come seasoned and with feta cheese) but didn't even touch them because my pita sandwich was so filling. I'll save them and see how they reheat in my air fryer tomorrow. 

Their customer service is also pretty great. I originally ordered takeout through Grubhub and had an issue on Grubhub's end (it was resolved). My food was never delivered but I ended up reordering and picking up. Upon my arrival the employees recognized my name and were very apologetic even though it wasn't their fault. They threw in a complimentary dessert. I'm not quite sure what it was but it was yummy and the thoughtfulness was appreciated.

This was my first time ordering from Elia and I plan to frequent them in the future - in person too. I look forward to eating in their outdoor area.

This is going to be long, but so is 400 years. Tonight, my husband and I took the kids out for dinner to Deanie's seafood in Bucktown. We were craving seafood and Deanie's never disappoints, until tonight. We were seated behind a group of 4 black sorority sisters, and next to a large family party for a young boy who just graduated from Ehret.  I usually don't use color as a descriptor, but it's unfortunately necessary for this story. Our waitress, was the same as the other tables and I was immediately concerned with her service from our drink order. We asked for root beer and Diet Coke and we received water and Dr. Pepper.  Maybe it was a mistake, but it annoyed the hell out of me. I asked for the Diet Coke and went about ordering. The other two tables had been there before us, yet somehow most of our food was delivered before the 4 women got theirs. I noticed. I know they noticed. My husband's order hadn't come, but when she brought ours and not theirs, I noticed. One of the women called the waitress over and asked about their food. The waitress was flustered and immediately went to hunt it down, stating they were backed up and she sent the manager over. Not only was he dismissive, but as he said he'd look into it, their order magically appeared. He strolled off, arms folded, smug and removed. After about 20 minutes my husband finally got his dinner and the other family got theirs. This is of course, with another error on the servers part. At this point, I notice the large family having an issue and again the manager is sent over. Apparently, one of the women in the party had gotten something that was inedible and she asked to have it removed from her check, which he refused. She then asked for it to be remade and again, he refused. He walked away, rolling his eyes after their quiet discussion. The only reason I was even able to hear was because we were literally next to them. No one was loud, no one cut up and no one caused a scene. We paid our bill after 20 more minutes, because our waitress disappeared, and got up to leave. I felt so badly for this young boy who just wanted to have a nice dinner with his family after an amazing milestone. I decided to go over and congratulate him. When I did, I learned the rest of the story and a woman who I assume was his aunt or grandmother thanked me for coming over. They had been waiting to hear back from the manager, who never came back. As we talked we kind of walked out together.  As we turned the corner to enter the lobby there were two JP cops and my heart sank. I looked at this family, who did nothing, and my fear for them was palpable. Their eyes said it all, there was fear and hurt. As we walked out, I turned to my husband and told him to take the kids to the car, I couldn't walk away. I couldn't leave these people alone with this unresponsive restaurant, not knowing what was going to happen. Now, I'm not about to cry savior or martyr, but my feet wouldn't move...I had to stay and protect them. One of the cops stayed in the restaurant and one was outside. I told the family that I was going to stand with them, just to be there, in case. Every person in this family told the officer that I was a witness and to ask me what happened. I physically put my body in front of this family to tell him just that. I'm not going to wax poetic on my actions, they don't mean anything, I can't change the minds of the racist people who work there, but something inside of me was so afraid of leaving and hearing on the news later that a black person was shot at Deanie's because 'insert BS reason' they were at fault. Maybe me being there didn't change the outcome, but we all walked away together, and the  young man put his arm around me as we did and that was enough for me. Hugging this family, who were just trying to celebrate, in support of them was all I really could do. Any 'privilege' I had, I wanted to use to shield them. Deanie's, you need to do better. The 2nd cop even said he doesn't eat there for that very reason! You need to do better! You are color blind and irresponsible! I will not eat at Deanie's again. I will not, and I urge others to stay away as well.

Horrible service. I've ordered there multiple times now and I will go in at or after the scheduled time and my order will not be ready. Today my order was completely wrong. Without an apology from anyone. This is the third time this has happened in the past year. The girls working were all laughing and talking amongst themselves instead of being attentive to their customers. If it wasn't for my handicapped father liking their donuts, I WOULD NEVER GO BACK!

WHAT A GREAT FIND!!

Ever get that sharp pain in your stomach, the one that almost makes you double over and cry out for mommy? Ahhh!!! An empty stomach having a canipshin because you have been neglecting it far too long. Either that, or the Scooby Snack you had on trail has since wore off. The latter is what happened with me and The Crew. Our morning stroll through the Coronado Monarch Butterfly Preserve and along the beach left our tummy's HANGRY!

Thanks for the mighty Yelp app. we found ourselves here. The filters on the app are a god send when having to find eateries extensive enough to accommodate preferences, food allergies, and wallets, Siam Thai met everyone's criteria.

Located on the main drag in the charming little beach town of Carpenteria, Siam Thai's interior is modest in size but their newly added back patio is grand and a great place to enjoy yummy eats while soaking up some Vitamin D. The interior is decorated with gold colored elephants, statues, and figurines.

With so many peeps in attendance, I'm not going to list the dishes ordered, however, I will say we ordered a few appetizers, soups, entrees, including curry's, fried rice, noodles, and vegetarian dishes. Entrees, curry's, and, noodles come with a choice of chicken, beef, pork, or tofu, up-charge for shrimp or seafood.  Not only was everyone WOWED! by the friendly staff members ability to take our orders expeditiously, but also deliver each dish quickly and accurately. And let me tell you, some folks order the an item straight from the menu, only to ask to hold this or that, this or that on the side, and substitute this for that. Oy!!! We did not receive one dish incorrectly. Portions were plentiful and all hot dishes were served hot, all cold dishes, served cold, and beverage glasses were kept full. 

STAFF EARNED IT!
Free public parking lot nearby, as well as, free street parking, as it should be, Siam Thai was such a great find.  Our server was so accommodating, instead of one long arse check, she combined four orders per check. Phew!! That many peeps all on one check can be an accounting nightmare. Server and her staff so deserved the well over 20% tip we left. Great place, ya'll should check it out. Hopefully, you will have the same experience me and The Crew did.

NOTHING LIKE ENJOYING A COLD REFRESHING 805 IN THE 805!

BACKGROUND:
Dargan's in Santa Barbara was Established in October 1997 , but the name Dargan's has been associated with public houses in Ireland since the beginning of the 20th century.

In 1927, Lawrence Dargan built a Pub and grocery to serve the small population of Cookstown, a market town in the north of Ireland. He and his family ran a successful business, well known locally as a center of Irish traditional music and craic (Gaelic for good times).

The tradition has spanned three generations, with Paul Dargan, who moved from Ireland when he was 21, now

STATS:
Mon-Sun 11 a.m.-2:00 a.m.
Private parking lot
Bar
Flat Screen TVs
Pool tables

EXPERIENCE:
After a day of hiking the city streets of SB and Montecito and back to SB by way of  the beach, followed by ice cream on the pier, and scoping out the annual Old Spanish Days on State Street, friends and I came here for dinner. 

The restaurant was relatively empty when we arrived, but by the time we ordered and received our food, the place was packed. Eyes glued to the TVs scattered throughout, by more than likely locals, hooped and hollered, raising their beverages in good cheer in support of their sports team.

We were seated close to theentrance, near a window at a half booth, half bar stool table, which wasn't really big enough for the four of us, but we made it work. Transplant waitress was peppy and talkative. Openly told us that she came to SB for college, fell in love with the city, and became a permanent resident. 

Tasty beverages and food were ordered at the same time. Hanging in the (805) how could I not order an 805 by Firestone. Two fish and chips and two Corn Beef & Cabbage with mashies were ordered and delivered piping hot within a few minutes. The food is ok. The fries were not soggy, but just were crispy enough for my liking. At least the gents enjoyed their Corn Beef.  Very very bad when gents tummies are grumpy. 

Although both the food and service were good, highly unlikely I'd be back. There are just too many other establishments in SB to become a regular at any of them, especially when it takes a train ride or a long car ride to get there.

FROM SANTA BARBARA TO MONTECITO BY FOOT MAKES FOR HUNGRY HIKERS

BACKGROUND:
Los Arroyos Mexican Restaurant and Take Out is a family-owned and operated restaurant with three locations in Santa Barbara, Montecito, and Camarillo. We serve fresh, homemade Mexican food crafted each day from the finest ingredients. Tony's original recipes offer a variety of dishes from traditional fare such as Sopes, Tamales, and Pozole to modern cuisine including the Mama's Salad with grilled vegetables, our Ceviche with fresh fish, and the Garden Burrito.

STATS:
Monday - Thursday 11:00am - 9:00pm
Friday - Sunday 11:00am - 9:00pm
Offers Take Out
Full bar including over 100 types of tequila
Extensive wine menu 
Indoor and Outdoor seating
Event catering is available
Offers private room  for groups between 8-14 people
Offers private party room for 30-50 people
(see website for more details)

EXPERIENCE:

You think parking across the street or a block away from an eatery, try walking a little over three miles for lunch. After strolling through Chase Palm Park: Shipwreck Playground, up and over hills, and through tunnels, me and some of the The Crew stopped here for lunch before completing our loop urban hike in and around Santa Barbara.

The modest collection of tables were all filled at the time of our arrival and only sat up to four people, we were a group of eight. The inside of this eatery decorated with the colors and items of Mexico, not to mention family pics of the Arroyos and perhaps extended family both blood and non-blood related. 

We all squished into a booth that was made for six to sit comfortably, but we are all family so personal space isn't all that necessary, just give us a bit of elbow room to shovel the food into our mouths and we're good. While we shared with each other items from the menu that peak our interest, water and beverage orders taken and served, in addition to chips, two kinds of salsa, and guac.

The chips were served warm and went well with the "spicy" salsa, although it wasn't all that spicy, for me anyway. The second salsa was a the roasted type, which I don't particularly care for from any eating house. The guac was tasty, didn't come from a jar and it didn't last long on the table.

Several baskets of chips were consumed before our food was finally delivered. Granted, we were a fairly large party, the food took longer than it should have, based on experience and in my opinion. The establishment wasn't overly crowded and the plates came out very staggered. 

My two shrimp tacos came on homemade corn tortillas, with shredded cabbage, creamy chipotle salsa, & mango salsa, and I chose  the Caesar salad over the rice and beans that are available with this dish. The chipotle salsa added a nice baby kick to the tacos. Everyone enjoyed their meals, but the service wasn't worth more than 20% of the bill, once we ordered our server didn't come back until we started asking the extended help for more water and salsa, among other items. I wouldn't walk three miles for this place again, however, if I'm ever in Montecito again, I may stop by.

I-SCREAM U-SCREAM, THE CREW SCREAMED FOR ICE CREAM!!!

STATS:
Mon-Sun 10am-9pm
32 flavors of fine ice creams and sherbets, handmade locally
Paid parking on Wharf 

EXPERIENCE:
Following a nice stroll alongside the rolling waves of the Santa Barbara coastline and before hoppin' on the Amtrak to head back to LA, several of us Crew Members stop in to this tight fitting ice shop. 

With the line out the door, we were concerned that we wouldn't make it back to the train station in time, however, there were about half a dozen teenagers behind the displays of ice cream working feverishly scoopin, dishin' and blendin ice cream treats for their patrons. 

Although there was a line of people, havoc was running rampant, customers' orders were taken out of turn, orders were given to the wrong customers, and some money was exchanged in line as well as at the register. 

At last, we made our way through the ice cream shop all holding our cold flavors. I ordered my staple, one that I've enjoyed licking from a cone since I was a wee Climbing Stephie, Mocha Almond Fudge, only now that I'm older, I prefer it in a cup. 

Although they claim the ice cream is homemade, it was just ok, nothing special. There was no WOW factor to this cold lickable treat and no reason why one scoop with tax was just shy of $5.00.

Because we're not allowed to write a review based on a Yelp event, I eventually made my way back to Goody Goody because I wanted to try the signature burger itself and other lunch/dinner items not offered on my initial visit.

Strategically picking a down time to walk in the door and avoid the normal wait, I found a nice counter spot and a truly delightful employee behind it to wait on me.

She was terrific, unfortunately the kitchen staff did not properly prepare the item that I ordered to sample along with the signature burger.

However, upon hearing of my experience, there were multiple management folks at the ready to apologize and make things right.

I have honestly never gotten a faster response to something like this and told them how impressed I was with their swift attention to detail as it related to customer relations.

While I have not been back, I have been invited to return and plan to do so when I'm back in the neighborhood to give them a deserved second chance.

Cannot recall the last time I saw off-duty police working traffic at a restaurant opening, although when I passed the two officers they weren't really doing anything except talking to one another.

Rather than stalk a parking spot on pavement close to the entrance, I parked in the dirt further away and made roughly a 100 yard walk.

It was really, really loud in there. Like Brick House for Sunday football meets Blue Martini on salsa night meets Rachel drunk at a CMYE loud. Despite being a foot or so from the cashier, we both had to raise our voices to get my order correctly placed.

Picking up my order was chaotic and you really needed to pay attention and listen closely to hear your number called. This despite the numbers being called by a girl on a headset microphone...which proves my point about the noise level. 

At first, I thought Addison (Waveland must have been working the lunch shift?) was really annoying because she called most numbers with a clever phrase such as "Forty Eight! You don't have to wait!" I forget what her line was when she called my number, but she appreciated that I was paying attention and quick to step up right as she said it. Honestly, her smile won me over as she thanked me for my business and I kind of feel bad that she has that job where she is clearly forced to make up corny phrases nonstop throughout her shift.

As someone who has visited Chicago many times in the last decade for Bears and Blackhawks games, I wanted to discover if their Italian Beef looked and tasted authentic.

While it definitely passed the eye and tummy test, I've had two better versions here in Tampa: One at Mel's Hot Dogs where they do not upcharge for peppers and the other at the former Meaner Weiner in SoHo, which ridiculously closed awhile back in favor of a bodega nobody visits unless they go in the wrong door looking for cupcakes.

The highlight for me at Portillo's were their tamales. Yes, I know to order those at a place like this rather than waste time on fries, onion rings, etc. They were good. They were large. They alone will bring me back when there aren't more cars outside than a Rays game.

And some guy walked past me with a glass schooner of beer, leading me to look over to where he got it and see that domestics are only $3.50. Honestly, I'd do two tamales and one of those beers for about $8 and change and be really happy if this place ever manages to reduce the noise level below a concert featuring Ted Nugent opening for KISS.

My grandparents used to drag me with them when they came here about 40 years ago to buy fresh ingredients to make a particular pasta dish.

That meal was always one of my favorites, so I knew I could grab something good for lunch here on my way to play an afternoon round at St. Petersburg Country Club.

What I wasn't prepared for was the insanity in front of the deli counter at 12:30pm on a Monday. It was like the Soup Nazi episode of Seinfeld if you included a late afternoon selloff on the New York Stock Exchange.

This isn't made any easier when the majority of customers are of that "Traditional St. Pete demographic" who have absolutely no awareness of other customers.

Memo to that demographic: When you are in a crowded public space, you do not move sideways or backwards without looking to see if you have actual room to do so. This isn't the NBA and you are not trying to create position for getting an offensive rebound. By doing so, you are simply running into others who are being patient and trying to stay out of your way.

Rather than fight my way to the front to get a number, then fend off locals waiting in the same area for my number to be called to then approach the counter again to place the actual order and then go through the same process to receive the finished order, I took the path of least resistance (literally) in grabbing something appealing from the refrigerated case and headed for the cashier.

Besides, I'm still a Chicken Salad Snob on occasion despite the near fatal fallout from eating it at Lenny's in Clearwater a couple years back. (Please check that review, because they obviously never did.)

I'd always heard the chicken salad at Mazzaro's was worthwhile and their cranberry version inside what appeared to be a sun dried tomato wrap was definitely top notch.

Would have loved to try a couple more things, but I'll have more of a gameplan next time. Perhaps even wearing elbow pads as if I was vintage Bill Laimbeer attacking the offensive glass.

There are many Johnny's that I feel strongly about.

Johnny Bench was my favorite baseball player when I was growing up.

Johnny Carson was brilliant and created an entire new genre of TV entertainment.

Johnny Blue is pretty good for special occasions now that I'm a bit older.

I was really hoping Johnny Grits could be in this conversation, but they failed me yet again.

Despite their website saying otherwise, the huge sign out front touting "dinner" and even this Yelp page stating they are open until 8pm, they were closed when I stopped in this afternoon to try them after failing to get anything on my first visit nearly two years ago.

Sorry, Johnny. You're now on my shit list, and NOT my grit list.

Fool me once, shame on me. Fool me twice, especially when your damn website states you close at 8pm, shame on you.

After years of being a loyal fan of Boston's in this space, I'm so happy that the great people who ran this location have not changed.

I stopped in this afternoon to make sure and found peace of mind that Tony and Sandy are fully in charge.

The name may have changed, but the interior looks the same and the menu actually has some new items now that Tony and Sandy have a little more freedom to do what they want.

Same two for one happy hour all damn day. Same discount for bringing in your AMC movie ticket. Same experience as before just without the corporate name.

After Mr C's Grilled Cheese recently let us down at Cigar City, I've been on a modest GC quest around the area.

Central Melt offers a grilled cheese version of a sloppy joe, which always gets my attention because it is tough to find on its own.

The balance between the two elements was extremely good, allowing me to enjoy both flavors in each bite.

You can look for yourself, but obviously the grilled cheese gets the edge in optics and that's the way it should be here.

Make no mistake, the sloppy joe taste was definitely there and rather savory. The price of this particular sandwich also equaled the size in my opinion and delivered good value as no sides were necessary in a satisfying lunch.

Thanks to a check-in on Yelp, I enjoyed a complimentary taste of the tomato soup dip and found it to be of good texture and tang. (Yes, tang. That's tangy in the form of a noun to me. If you have a problem with that, then why give so many Yelp Elite TB award-winning reviews on here a free pass with their consistently brutal grammar? I actually majored in journalism at a four-year private university in Coral Gables, so I write to that level while others write as if they are sending you a text message.)

Service from both the cashier and the cook was a positive experience. I appreciated her candor in telling me to run my other errand across the street and how she would have my order waiting for me when I returned about 10 minutes later.

This wasn't quite a destination grilled cheese experience to get me to visit on a regular basis, but it more than got the job done and will stay on my radar for convenience sake when I'm in the area again.

After driving by this construction site for about a year, Ford's Garage is finally open as of Tuesday, August 15th.

Welcome to Westchase/Citrus Park.

My friends and I have enjoyed every previous visit to other locations in Estero, Brandon and Wesley Chapel/Lutz, and my first to this new location delivered everything that I enjoy about the brand.

As I've said in previous reviews of those locations, Ford's Garage is one of the most attentive to detail themed bar and restaurants. It almost feels like something you would visit inside a major theme park. They don't miss a thing...and even if you don't necessarily have to use the restroom during your visit, make sure you go check that out too.

There weren't any negative surprises about walking in the newest location. It was great to see Rhiannon's familiar face behind the bar as she has been taking great care of customers like me at another bar/restaurant brand for almost a decade. Her and Tina gave me excellent service and just show how this Ford's has hired some really quality people.

Our food was excellent. My friend loves their Chicken Cobb Salad and couldn't wait to attack it. I always put together a "Custom Built" burger and it was prepared accurate and tasty. The pickle chips and baked beans were also delicious.

There's very little on the menu I wouldn't order, so the fact that this location is about 15 minutes from home will give me the opportunity to explore more things.

For those of you who enjoy beer, Ford's has pretty much anything you wish. Vast selection of drafts and huge coolers full of other brands in bottles and cans. If you prefer spirits, their $4 specials on select name brands should get your attention as well.

Thanks for being worth the wait.

At the conclusion of my previous visit here (Which I detailed in my previous review), I used an E-Gift Certificate to pay for the meal.

While I thought it was odd that TdB does not do traditional gift cards, I gave my account number on the certificate and they pulled up the exact value. They applied it to the bill without any problems and told me my balance for a future visit.

Fast forward to last night, when I took a couple of clients to the restaurant for their first TdB experience.

They were excited to try it and I was equally enthused to be the one to take them.

Our service from Evan and the quality of the salad bar and meats was very good and we enjoyed each other's company throughout the dinner.

When the check came, I produced the exact same paperwork that I had used on my previous visit to exhaust the remaining balance on this check.

Shortly thereafter, I was approached by a very nervous store manager. He told me that their computer system could not produce my balance and it was "on hold." I asked multiple times what "on hold" meant and how I planned to use that balance to pay this check.

Instead, he simply handed me a business card with the main number of the corporate office and said I needed to call them. I said, "Let's call right now. I am using this E-Gift Certificate to pay this bill. This is why we are here." Of course, he knows that nobody will answer the phone at the corporate office at this evening hour. So this is not a legitimate option to assist me right now.

The manager is doing this in full view of my two guests. Not very professional and rather embarrassing.

He said there was nothing he could do, which is always NOT TRUE in these cases. He simply made the choice NOT to do anything and knew I was powerless to use the remaining balance clearly indicated to me when I left after my previous visit.

What I should have done was say, "Fine. Then my bill is "On hold" until I speak to someone in your corporate office. Here's my business card and phone number. " And then we should have walked out. Again, I've done nothing wrong here.

For the record, we didn't exactly run up a tab. Simply three men having the standard dinner with one round of domestic bottled beers and no dessert. This also takes the "intoxicated" argument off the table. We were quiet, polite and they completely blew this.

Next day, their corporate office (after five separate attempts to get an answer from a human being) said I had no balance on the E-Gift Certificate and there was nothing they could do for me. Don't you hate that line as much as me?

So, Texas de Brazil would rather lose customers and embarrass their guests publicly than properly handle a situation that clearly was not my fault.

I will never again attend any Texas de Brazil location and discourage anyone from accepting or purchasing any gift card or E-Gift Certificate from them in the future based on my experience.

This breakfast & lunch only diner clicks all the boxes.

They make the most of this space which I remember was once occupied by a YaYa's in a plaza where so many things have come and gone in the last 25 years.

The menu features so many options, that one can get mesmerized by it and miss a timely chance to order and start eating.

From the breakfast side, the Hobo Hash is scrumptious. It is basically a skillet meets an omelette with a side of biscuit and gravy. (Speaking of clicking all the boxes, right?)

And on the lunch side, their chicken salad sandwich looks and tastes homemade. It is one of many sandwich options that can be ordered between two slices or triple-decker style and each of them come with a choice of savory soups.

I appreciate that touch. It is classic to me. When you order a sandwich and soup comes with it, I just feel the ownership really knows what they're doing.

The employees here hustle, so be careful when you pay at the register because there's someone generally walking behind you with two or three plates of food on a regular basis. They also pay attention to little things and actually seem to connect with their guests rather than going through the motions and acting like you're just another faceless customer.

Challenged by a friend to write a short review, so here it is:

Many smiling employees who were enthusiastic to offer service.

The store is small, yet efficient and cozy.

I tried three different proteins on flour tacos and enjoyed the fresh taste.

For a $2 taco special offered every late afternoon, it is obviously cheap eats. However, not very filling unless you buy about five or six of them or some other entree and/or a side.

Parking lot is predictably bad for a place in SoHo and more than a bit tricky to get in and out of from Platt.

I'm often looking for a place that serves breakfast sandwiches into the afternoon, especially on weekends when I enjoy sleeping in.

Yelp helped me find this spot in a plaza loaded with other places that my friends and I are very familiar with...yet I honestly had no idea The Grind was right there too.

Modern interior featuring high-top tables, more casual type seating and counter space as well.

Plenty of fresh looking baked items on display including scones and muffins that were tough for me to ignore.

From The Grind's very nice website, I knew I wanted the egg sandwich on a toasted everything bagel and added turkey sausage to it.

The employee who took my order told me it would not take long and it took even less time than I expected.

Good sandwich, wouldn't call it great. No doubt it was made fresh, but perhaps it was a little bland overall considering there were plenty of ingredients to make something stand out from a flavor standpoint.

Still, I like the place, enjoyed the fast service and the convenience of The Grind being right there near so many other good spots right off Linebaugh.

When a first experience is as awkward as this one and you don't come home with what you ordered, it cannot be anything above two stars. This despite the food tasting pretty good, so my complaint is certainly not with the people in the kitchen here.

I've been using more online ordering since it is for people like me who like take out, and the Pei Wei website was not bad in terms of navigation, customization and convenience.

However, something specific to one of my items was not in my bag when I arrived at home and that just shows someone is not paying attention.

I'm 97% sure that someone was the employee I interacted with when I arrived to pick up my food, because she just seemed frustrated or pissed off. At one point, she told the only other employee working behind the counter, "Hey, you need to talk to this guy" when referring to a man to my left who had some sort of an issue with what was on his receipt. That just put the other employee in the same frustrated or pissed off state of mind while a lady stood right next to me for at least five minutes without even being greeted.

Simple deduction of body language gave me little confidence that my order would be correct, and I was right. Yet, since this was my first Pei Wei visit, how was I to know what was in those boxes in my bag and what was missing? Granted, I do like those places that show and identify everything AS they put it in your bag but the majority do not.

There were not any smiles, greetings or thank you's either. Just what's your name, here's what you owe and here's your order. Or at least most of it.

Get it together, Pei Wei. My recent take out experiences at one place to your left (Lime) and one place to your right (The OG) were both flawless and friendly. This plaza is very convenient to my condo, so those places clearly have a significant edge for my future business.

Considering how the Rays have parted ways with every significant name on the team other than Longoria in the last six months, my visits to downtown St. Petersburg will be even more infrequent than before.

Therefore, an unrelated appointment a little down Central Avenue was my motivation to finally visit Engine No. 9 and find out if they were worthy of the hype.

Easily found free parking on the street in the mid-afternoon, was greeted immediately upon entrance and was surprised to see all the Chicago Blackhawks stuff on the walls.

As a fan of hockey, I had no idea this was a major theme of Engine No. 9 and I very much appreciated the classic photos of the legendary Tony and Phil Esposito as well. (Both call our area home and can almost always be found at every single Lightning home game if you know where to look. Tony simply never turns down a request for a photo either, because his seats are across the aisle from mine.)

Now that I've covered the Blackhawks angle, let's get to the food.

There's a lot of variety in the burgers offered, but I went with the XXX because if featured a pretzel bun, jalapeno bacon and shares its name with one of the famous college burger joints just off the Purdue University campus. (I'm guessing that is just a coincidence)

I did switch out cheddar for pepperjack just to add more spice and the end result was very satisfying. 

My order did not take very long at all, everything looked and tasted fresh and the burger really held its form throughout...which is a big deal to me. Sorry, but I don't want to be reconstructing a sloppy mess after a couple bites. A truly well-built hamburger can be picked up and enjoyed with one hand until its completion.

While I almost always order baked beans as a side if offered, the scouting report said to try their tater tots and I was not disappointed at all in the portion and texture.

Pricing was on the higher side as every burger (with one side included) is over $10, although I honestly wouldn't hesitate to order the same thing again at that price.

Other than burgers, there were other things to potentially bring me back like the jerk short ribs over pasta dish and I absolutely must have their bacon baked beans on the next visit.

Looked like they had a very worthy bottled beer selection, so I could see myself and a fellow hockey apologist making this a destination for a future Blackhawks game.
