Hell, Engine No. 9 is probably going to be a better atmosphere, value and overall experience than going to Tropicana Field this year.

Many have been eagerly awaiting the opening of this second location, since the buzz was always palpable for the original on the other side of Tampa.

While I was very tempted to try something a little more creative, I wanted to just go with a couple of tacos to make my first impression. Especially since it clearly states right on the menu, "2 orders of our Amped Tacos are plenty for a meal. Trust us!"

Well, you can definitely trust them. One Pork Al Pastor soft taco combined with one Chicken with sauteed onions/peppers taco literally filled the entire box. I'd never used a fork to eat a taco before, but there's clearly a good reason why one was included with my order. 

While all of the ingredients worked perfectly together, the guacamole was exceptional and highlighted absolutely every bite.

Every single employee was smiling and keeping busy and while the dining area is small, it was spotless for those who want to sit and enjoy their food immediately.

I went back a couple weeks later for lunch and really enjoyed my Carne Asada California Burrito, which replaces rice and beans with crispy french fries. Much like the two tacos, it was not only enough for a meal...but I did not need to eat again until the next day.

Sadly, this review should have been so much better.

However, I ordered three items and received only two of the three. The third item delivered to me was not part of my order.

My receipt was accurate. The items were not.

I also left feedback on the company website specific to this location with details about my order and received no response.

So, I was driving by this location five days later and went in to get a refund for the item that was not included. 

I produced the exact receipt, yet they said they could not credit my card nor simply reach in the register and hand me a refund for the one item.

The first option was to give my phone number and that amount would be credited to my next order. 

First, I just didn't believe that would work. Second, why would I want to order delivery a second time since they did not get the order right on the first occasion?

I offer repeat business to places that do things right. They did not.

The manager on duty was Bobby and he professionally offered to give me some food of that value to make up for it. Honestly, I wasn't hungry at all, but I took two slices to at least get some resolution, thanked him and left.

Kids, what did we learn from this? Don't order online from Westshore Pizza. If they get the order wrong, the store says they cannot do anything about it in terms of a refund. They also claim the website feedback goes to a corporate office, so they cannot see it themselves.

Too bad. My pizza steak was a good one on the original delivery. I just don't want to go through this again and have other options for similar food at similar prices.

While I'm a regular here, I'd never taken someone to this Fleming's at their request for a birthday dinner.

Fleming's put effort into making the evening special by calling me in advance and asking the name of person having the birthday, so they could print up a personal happy birthday message and have it waiting on the table when we arrived.

They also offered a champagne toast, took a photo and framed it for us and when delivering a box of chocolate truffles after dinner, our server opened it and placed a candle in one of them and lit it for tradtional birthday purposes.

Speaking of our server, his name was Brad and I would enthusiastically recommend you ask for him on your next visit to the dining room.

I'm sure all of you who dine at upscale steakhouses know that some servers in this setting can be effective at their job, but almost robotic and a bit awkward in their communication. 

Brad is not like that. He has natural communication skills and easygoing body language which enhanced our evening overall.

Our food was not only delicious, but came out very fast and was plated perfectly. 

My sincere thanks to Brad and always to former Dallas Cowboys offensive lineman Jorge Diaz, longtime manager and partner at this location, for a comfortable and enjoyable night to mark this special occasion.

My visit was weeks ago, but I'm only now writing about the experience.

Why? Because I got horribly ill from eating here, went onto the website for a contact to let them know and ask if anyone had the same problems.

In my email, I was very specific about when I visited, what I ordered and how it made me sick for the rest of my weekend.

I only ordered one item, did not have anything else to eat that day, so clearly this was an issue with their food.

Guess they just did not care as I never received a response.

This was also my first-ever visit to Lenny's and I obviously will not be making another one.

Of note, the last time I became this ill after a restaurant experience, the restaurant not only had local and national representatives calling to ask about myself and my girlfriend...but offering to pay for any medical expenses as a result. (There were none, but it was still an impressive gesture.)

That was a chain casual dining restaurant and they sure raised the bar on customer care.

Lenny's lowered it back down to around my ankles.

I've been waiting for months to write about people who work the counter at restaurants who simply DO NOT PAY ATTENTION to the customer.

Today is that day.

This was my first trip to Hank's. And it will be my last. 

I walked in and ordered a bowl of Brunswick Stew for takeout.

That's it. Pretty simple. I'm a TV/Radio broadcaster and speak rather clearly.

For some reason, it took way too long to get my order. That's odd on its own when it is literally a bowl of soup and there's nobody else behind me.

What did I open when I got home? Gumbo. 

Gumbo was also on my receipt. This means the cashier was absolutely not paying attention.

I do not eat gumbo and there are ingredients in it to which I'm allergic.

Nice job, Hank's! What the hell are you doing?

I will be immediately returning to your store with this receipt, the gumbo untouched and a firm request for a refund.

No. I don't want any food from you, not your Brunswick Stew or anything else for my troubles. Save that free food for your next Yelp Elite event when the freeloaders show up and give you five stars because they didn't pay for anything. All I want is my money back for wasting my time coming into your store. 

Let this be a lesson to cashiers who are not paying attention to the customers. We're are simply tired of you not listening to us. Please pay attention or find a job where you do not have to interact with people.

Surprisingly good burger based on my expectations from the previous Red Robin experience a couple years earlier at a different location.

Normally, I order takeout from the bar in casual restaurants like this and have a drink or two while waiting patiently for my food.

However, I was told quickly by the bartender that I needed to order at the host stand.

No problem. Thank you for making that clear to me.

That said, I placed my order where instructed with a very friendly hostess and then walked the mall for 10-15 minutes instead of going back to the bar and spending additional money on beverages and gratuity. 

While I respect the store policy, it should not be a big deal for a bartender to ring up a takeout order and in this case, it costs him and the store an additional sale.

The Paul's in Clearwater is just not convenient to me except when I attend a show at Ruth Eckerd Hall, while this newest location does give more more opportunities to enjoy their consistently good product.

Many years ago, I lived in apartments next door to this plaza and know how many different dining concepts have occupied this particular space.

This new Paul's has been open roughly six months and the friendly employees who waited on me say they are happy with business.

I can count on Paul's to make virtually everything the right way, including the wonderful Italian beef sandwich that only locals in Chicago and their guests truly understand.

Paul's does not offer slices, and they have a legitimate reason why, so I tried their French bread pizza because it comes with two toppings and I wanted a little more chew than the normal thin crust they feature on their pies. 

Besides, the bread itself for this option is the exact same delicious bread they use for the aforementioned Italian beef sandwich.

Their toasted ravioli is also a must and this item in general remains the most underrated appetizer in the history of our planet.

My only complaint with Paul's is how they close at 8pm on Sundays. This is earlier than any other night and it selfishly sucks for me.

I'm often leaving the studios of BayNews9 at 7:45pm after taping sports shows and don't want to run in here at 7:59pm and place a takeout order.

I won't do that to these employees. Besides, anyone who arrives and orders food at any restaurant in the last 15 minutes before the posted closing time should know it is very much a dick move.

Ybor has never been for me and never will be.

However, I do love takeout and coming back this way from Orlando just after 11am allowed me easy parking and beating the lunch rush.

I encountered some really nice people working here. Cannot stress that enough.

Because of that, I bought more food than I planned and simply spread it out over a couple days.

While I'm not a soup snob, I do like soup and places like this attract me because I hope what they offer will be special or at least above the norm.

The two soups that I bought were both worthwhile and unique in their own way despite being flavors that I know blindfolded.

My sandwich (Of course I ordered the Jueban for politically incorrect reasons) was made fresh and was even better than the soups. Also, they gave me the option of a cajun slaw as a side that was no longer on the menu and it was delicious.

With soups as cheap as $4 each and a large sandwich with side for $8.75, the value is there too.

Menu seems to have tons of options and I was stunned to see three different flavors of Sprecker soda in bottles available for purchase. 

As a Dallas Cowboys fan, I can ignore all the owner's Steelers stuff on the walls as long as the food and price stays consistent with those smiling and helpful employees. (Not sure how Lightning fans feel about the Penguins gear for the next few months though considering the Game Seven loss in the East Finals)

This is the most attention to detail at a themed bar/restaurant that I have seen in at least a decade.

Oh, and that includes theme parks.

The fact that this chain of restaurants is officially licensed by Ford Motor Company is probably a major reason.

It would take me too long to list all the little things that make this place truly authentic and you can read about them in other reviews previously posted on this page. (Although it is too bad that ladies cannot see what the urinals look like in the men's bathroom.)

Short of serving the food in oil pans and the silverware being half fork/knife and half something from a tool box, the designers of this place did not miss chances to get creative.

That alone is good enough for me in a world where too many things are done half-ass.

The interior is exposed to a large amount of natural light and fresh air on two of the four sides and it works very well.

Also, I vehemently disagree with others here on Yelp about two negatives of Ford's Garage:

The noise level and the service

If you want a loud place that gives you a headache, try the Brick House. I had no noise issues here at 1pm for lunch and it was rather busy.

Despite how busy they were, my service was perfect. No complaints at all.

Besides, I've only been one other place that actually knows how to make a burger with peanut butter as a key ingredient and that was at a famous little joint near a Big Ten campus. (If you know where, shoot me a note. I'd love to see if anyone else has been there too)

At Ford's Garage, this is called the Jiffy Burger (guess I know it isn't made with Peter Pan or Skippy) and apparently is also enjoyed by a recent New York Yankees captain who wore #2.

If you've seen their concession stand at Lightning hockey games, it simply does not do this place justice. 

You have to visit an actual location to fully appreciate the insanely high level of authenticity.

Along those lines, here's my only suggestion to management:

How about reserving some of the best parking spots for those of us who actually drive Ford vehicles?

Not that parking for me was an issue, but my Ford Focus should be closer to the front entrance than say a Hyundai or Kia at a place licensed by the Ford Motor Company.

The best breakfast tacos I have ever had. Anywhere. In my life. And I'm getting old.

I've had these multiple times, both at this location and the Fuzzy's in Brandon, and they are spectacular.

As proven by the fact that I had them at 10pm last night, these breakfast tacos are served all day and the ones I always get (Egg, Cheese, Potato and either Bacon or Chorizo) are just $2.19 each.

The value, size and taste are consistently high.

That's also why I served Fuzzy's breakfast tacos to 110 players before everyone teed off in my most recent golf tournament. There were no leftovers and that never happens when catering a golf event.

I also like the interior space, the friendly employees and how the store is kept bright and clean.

My compliments to the Liebermans who own these stores. Great job, guys. My golfers thank you as well.

This location is conveniently located near the always busy Publix in Palma Ceia and seems to do rather well.

There's a manager named Jeff who is always actively working hard and offering to assist customers or even just say hello to make them feel welcome.

The store is always tidy and I was in here most recently getting some gift cards for one of my golf tournaments. A male employee jumped behind the counter and got that job done faster than I expected, since buying gift cards sometimes challenges employees elsewhere who treat the register buttons as if they are playing a video game they have never seen before.

Burger Monger's burger is a tasty one that I've enjoyed here and the Carrollwood location on multiple occasions, while I still battle with them on their choice of lettuce. 

On this visit, I noticed they were heavily pushing a signature selection of their special beef in hot dog form representing six cities across the US.

The difference was not the beef, but how each dog was dressed.

The Chicago dog was the classic Chicago style, while the other five city-inspired versions featured other items.

Cincinnati's included chili, Pittsburgh's featured fries on top, Kansas City's was slathered in BBQ sauce, New York's had sauerkraut and California's came with guacamole.

It was a creative way to market something a little different than other places do for the summer, while I still eat about one hot dog every presidential administration and completely agree with my golf buddy Drew Garabo that it is absolutely not a sandwich.

The latest option in the bar and restaurant explosion around International and Westshore malls near the airport is this World of Beer, although it is much further west and isolated than any of the other existing spots.

But, hey, at least WOB actually had a plan and got it open, unlike whatever the hell Lucky Dill/LBC is doing with the old Boizao spot for what seems like the last decade.

I've been in about five WOBs across Tampa and Orlando prior to this one and find this location to be nicer than all of them. 

Unlike most other stores, there's actually room to breathe in here and the multi-level outdoor patio areas are a very nice touch with various seating options that were well conceived.

The beer selection is as massive as advertised and the tablets offered to let you scroll through the choices work really well.

Now, let me tell you about how this first visit to WOB furthers a conspiracy theory my friends and I now have about some bars and a pattern of behavior by employees working behind the bar itself.

There were at least six or maybe seven different employees that were behind the bar at various times during my visit. A couple of them interacted with me more than others and I received plenty of attention throughout my visit UNTIL I was clearly ready to pay the check.

As my beer was approaching empty, I had at least three employees ask me if I wanted another. I kindly said no to all three and said I would take my check. When my check was produced, I placed cash across the check and put it on the edge of the bar closest to the employees while finishing my beer. 

For at least 10 minutes, I watched all these same employees who paid plenty of attention to me earlier just walk by, not make eye contact or grab the check and payment.

My friends and I have noticed this recently in other similar places and our theory is this:

Employees ignore you at this point in the hopes you change your mind and decide to order something else.

That's not right. And, if we're correct, they need to stop doing this.

Customers shouldn't have to wait an exorbitant amount of time or put forth significant effort to pay their bill. When we say we don't want to have another, don't ignore us...bring the bill and look for prompt payment. You'll get it, as we clearly are ready to go. 

We came, we drank, we're want to leave when we choose...not when you want us to leave.

Again, this WOB is not the only place we noticed this trend. However, we decided it was time to say something about it after this latest experience.

As a self-professed chicken salad snob who even engages in Yelp talk threads about chicken salad and shares chicken salad notes with other Yelpers, I was enthused to make the new Chicken Salad Chick a destination for lunch this afternoon.

Honestly, it takes a lot to get me anywhere near the USF campus. But I enjoyed golf today at Temple Terrace Golf and Country Club and Chicken Salad Chick was the next stop.

Tammy greeted me outside the store and walked me to the front counter making sure that I had samples of anything I wanted to try. She meant it too. 

After sampling three different chicken salad flavors and two of the side items, I ordered a chicken salad sandwich (Sassy Scotty) with two sides and even received a lemon cookie to go along with it.

Of the four chicken salad varieties that I tasted, I liked all of them and there was no doubting the ingredients of each one. Tastes were distinct and ingredients were tangible.

My original plan was to buy the trio of chicken salads on a bed of lettuce with crackers, but Tammy encouraging me to try various flavors AND the unexpected highlight of the side broccoli salad made me alter my plan on the fly.

This is a very unique place. Not only because I've never been to any deli, market or restaurant that offered more than three flavors of chicken salad (most only have one), but because of the feel of the dining room too. The decor really is like walking into a small restaurant in the deep south.

If you like chicken salad, seek this place out. Look hard for it using GPS or online maps and just know it is tucked in the farthest spot to the east in this plaza right behind the Chili's. 

Thank you, Tammy for your kindness and quality product this afternoon. I loved everything about my experience.

First, the beers that I had were enjoyable. I let the bartender Myles pick out which two brews I was going to drink. He asked me what my taste was, never hesitated and poured me not one, but two that completely fit the bill.

Next, it was just a very comfortable and welcome atmosphere on a Saturday night. They were busy, but there was plenty of parking, seating and despite coming alone, I never felt out of place among the rest of the more loyal customers.

Lastly, credit this place for having multiple televisions on sporting events that people want to see or at least keep an eye on. 

So many modern brew pubs are arrogant in not showing sports on their screens insisting that customers talk among one another and play old school games. I find that outright stupid.

At least Six Ten gives people the choice. No, it isn't a sports bar. But at least they accomodate those of us who want to follow the action while still offering a huge shelf of Toys R Us inspired games for people who want to keep themselves occupied otherwise.

Apparently, this place will be expanding greatly in the coming months. And I heard they won a significant gold medal for one of the great variety of 22 draft beers that were on tap that night. 

Good for them. I wish them well as they grow and I will continue to stop in here to enjoy the overall product.

First and foremost, I'd personally like to thank International Mall for basically telling Blue Martini to GTFO.

If you don't know, that's what mall management did in not offering to renew Blue Martini's lease on the space they occupied since the inception of this property a very long time ago.

Too many concerns and complaints about Blue Martini for years finally led to them being told to literally take their business elsewhere. And all those STD's with them. (As Yelp's own Anna M famously calls them, South Tampa Douchebags. Those are the men who frequented this place and their spending habits fueled a shitshow The Real Housewives of Potomac wouldn't even watch.)

In this case, what happens in South Tampa, should stay in South Tampa. Those of us who live and do business in the continually growing and coveted Westshore/International district have a much higher standard for our neighborhood than say the target demographic known best for stumbling across South Howard.

So whether it was International who kicked out Blue Martini before Rocco wanted the space or it was Rocco hanging out nearby at Capital Grille telling the right people that he'd like the space if it ever became available, the result is a beautiful new bar and restaurant that fits the profile much better than the previous tenant.

Rocco completely transformed the place so those of us scarred from the memories of STD's and male only cover charges to listen to horrendous cover bands don't get flashbacks. 

While Rocco doesn't have the luxury of a beautiful lake out back like he has for his wonderful Orlando location on Sand Lake road, he did a wonderful job creating an attractive interior with some comfortable patio dining as well that looks really nice tucked between Bar Louie and Doc B's.

Ironically, my first experience here could have been better. It took way too long for an employee to notice us at the bar and the only entree we ordered was not properly cooked and eventually removed from our check. 

Still, short of Rocco throwing me out himself, or worse, dragging me down to South Howard and dropping me off there next to a couple day-drunk Primrose moms...I will always make sure to visit here for a beer, a taco or even some $11 queso (What is this a Lightning game?) to show appreciation for the new tenant that helped kicked the old one out of my neighborhood.

Thursday, February 13th was my last dining experience at Roy's Tampa. This is only because ownership has decided to close this location permanently in a few days.

Not only was this and all other recent visits to Roy's Tampa highlighted by delicious food and attentive service, but the GM (Sean W) has been outstanding to me, my friends and my hundreds of Todd Wright Tour golfers.

Roy's Tampa even served as host to The Foundation's fantasy football draft last season in one of their comfortable private dining rooms. The lovely appetizers offered to all my fantasy owners as part of our draft package were an even bigger highlight that night than league MVP Lamar Jackson falling all the way to pick #123. 

As a homeowner nearby, I am sad to see Roy's Tampa go out this way. Clearly I'm not alone since their reservations book is near capacity for Valentine's Day dining this evening and tomorrow as well.

Thanks to Sean W, Amy K and others here who have always done nothing less than their best for me and everyone I have brought into this restaurant.

One word: Gazpacho. 

Finally. It is back. And hopefully they'll keep it around next month too.

Best $4.50 I've spent this month.

And for those of you who rip it as simply "cold soup," you just don't understand.

As a Bones Club cardholder, it doesn't take much to get me into any Smokey Bones as I know the specials and the menu and find the restaurants to my liking.

This location has more going for it than others (Especially the one in Citrus Park) based on my visit on a Friday night when the bar was full and there was a wait for seating in the dining room. Also, I'd done lunch here a few times over the past year and it was also very crowded and lively.

Employees were hustling, especially the managers and pretty young ladies behind the bar and all the food that came out from the kitchen looked outstanding. (We had ate nearby just before and were simply here for cocktails)

As a fan of the show Bar Rescue, I know that almost all "Specialty Cocktails" are overpriced and more for show than anything else. However, we ordered one of the them and were pleasantly surprised at the reasonable price, top shelf ingredients and taste. Then, once that one was done, a manager placed a different specialty cocktail in front of us to see if we liked that one even better...saying it was an extra and encouraged us to enjoy it on the house. 

While I didn't try that one, it was a huge hit with my friend and I'll always remember the name (Spiked Fruitcake) and how it came in what looked like a single-serve pitcher for excellent presentation.

We either were in the right place at the right time or just were viewed as friendly customers because when I finished a draft beer a little later, another employee walked over to me and put a fresh draft beer down on the bar saying it was also an extra and it was mine to drink if I wanted one more before leaving.

Our bill was well under $20 when Crystal (Look for her at Kay Jewelers as well) cashed us out and it felt like stealing for the quality and quantity of drinks we had over way more time than we initially planned to spend there.

Credit management also for putting the Lightning game on many of the TV's as soon as they were ready to face off that night. That always shows me someone is paying attention and not letting good TV's go to waste when something local or nationally significant is available to show.

As is normally the case when I'm trying a new BBQ joint, I took home a couple different items and as many sauces as possible.

My compliments to the employee who offered additional sauces with an order that didn't necessary need them. I always ask for one that I think I'll like and then take a recommendation for one from that particular employee serving me. He gave me his recommendation and offered me the additional two sauces so I could sample all of them.

The two hotter ones were a much thicker consistency than I expect. However, the mustard based and flavored sauce that I generally like, was too thin and unfortunately more like a salad dressing.

Still, I could taste the spices in all four and just that they had that many in those particular flavors gives them accountability with me.

The fried bologna sandwich in name alone usually scares most adults away, but the rest of us know it translates to a tasty spin on a ham sandwich. BnB's version is large, piled high and topped with complimentary ingredients and a sauce that work well together. 

The chalkboard special on the day I visited was the chopped rib Sloppy Joe and it should be on the menu permanently if they can afford to do so. Sloppy joes are rare to find in Tampa, and this massive and delightfully messy sandwich was also good value. Value that seems very difficult to find overall at "Amateur Work in Progress". (Sure, you may use that term as well.)

On a future visit to BnB, my next two literal takeaways will be the Korean Cheesesteak and the Chicken Biscuit to get more of a firm impression of this lunch spot. Neither are truly BBQ items, but both have obvious appeal and show diversity in the menu.

After a rain-shortened round of golf in Clearwater, I was in the mood to find a good slice of pizza from a new place.

Russo's did not have slices ready made, which is always my preference, but their menu clearly allows for single slices to be ordered at $5 each and custom made.

The slice is also clearly promoted as a big one. 

So, I invested the additional $1.50 and got one from a speciality pizza combination to enjoy multiple toppings instead of just choosing one from an impressive list of about 40 options. 

My hope is the picture attached to this review does justice on how impressively large this slice actually turned out to be. And, based on how tightly it fits in the single slice box, that means they are ALWAYS this size!

As the unassuming mother in Bachelor Party said to Nick the Dick, "Is that the footlong?" His response, "And then some!" (Thank you, Tom Hanks. Amazing Adrian Zmed was considered his equal in that movie) 

At first, I was disappointed that I didn't get a drink with the slice simply because that is a common lunch deal for pizza and it was 2:30pm.

However, the size of the slice more than makes up for the lack of a fountain beverage included with it. Besides, while I waited, the nice female employee behind the counter asked me if I wanted anything to drink anyway...which was nice of her to offer since I was being patient while it took about 10 minutes to make my slice of pizza.

Yes, the taste was very good. You can see I received plenty of toppings. Crust was perfect. Cheese to sauce combination was well-balanced as well.

I can only imagine how big a full pie of these slices would look. It might take me a week to finish something like that. If you are ordering full pies from Russo's, make sure you know what you're getting into.

Finally, before I left I made the nice woman behind the counter pull one specific bottle of beer out of the cooler. Not for me to drink. But for me to look at. 

Bud. Light. Orange. Huh?

No, this is not a fake. 

When I asked management how long it had been in there, nobody seemed to know it even existed in the first place.

Sure, I drink the Diet Coke slimcans that came out recently and particularly like the Twisted Mango before a round of golf.

But...Bud...Light...Orange?

Dilly Dilly appears to have gone Silly Silly.

Welcome to this month's example of a Yelp review where I talk about how other reviews are significantly overrating a business.

As a matter of fact, I'll admit that I'm being overly critical just to balance out the fact that too many other reviews go way overboard.

Sure, the lady who waited on me was friendly. However, that is not a reason to ignore many other obvious factors.

The place is located in a gas station. I prefer to get my prepared food in actual restaurants and I would never sit down at any gas station (Not even Wawa) and eat there. 

The wait for my sandwich simply was too long. You can tell me all you want about how something is made fresh, but wait time is important. 

Especially when I'm standing around a convenience store that I have no other reason to be exposed to a vast selection of wife-beater shirts, boxers and socks at the front counter. (See the attached picture to see if they have your size!)

No, the ability to order ahead does not change your wait time. I could do that virtually anywhere when ordering a sandwich or a meal in general, so it is not like they offer something other places do not.

Their hours are not at all convenient to most people. They are not open after 5pm on weekdays, close at 3pm on Saturday and are not open on Sunday at all. People wanting to swing by here on their way home after work (or in my case on my way home from a round of weekend afternoon golf), simply cannot buy their product.

The sandwich was fine. Yes, I used the word "fine."

Now, think about how you use the word "fine" to describe something to somebody else. 

That means it is not memorable. Nor worth going out of your way for and it was not worth the time I waited to receive it. As a matter of fact, it has been over two months since I stopped in here and I did not even bother to write my review until now because I keep forgetting that I was actually here.

Best Cuban Sandwich in Tampa Bay seems to get kicked around as a conversation topic just like Best Tacos, Best Steakhouse, etc. 

People putting this one in the conversation are trying too hard to be cute and obscure. (Kind of like the guy in your fantasy football league who drafts Ryan Fitzpatrick as his QB1 this season). Plus there's the obvious bias that many Yelpers have towards individually owned small businesses, who honestly should not get an edge over larger chain businesses just for that reason alone. 

Sure, the friendly lady working the counter has a nice smile and demeanor. That alone is not enough for a five star rating.

There is so much good stuff in this place. 

First, I'm glad I found it. It is tucked behind the Winghouse and there really isn't much of a sign on Brandon Blvd. to alert you to stop even if you're looking for it. Not a big deal, but without a GPS, some people like me may drive by on a first attempt.

I couldn't decide what to try, so I just bought enough food to last me for a couple days.

Best Cuban sandwich in Tampa Bay is debated about as much as any other food item on this website, so I had to try Moreno's version. Not disappointed one bit. That's also plenty of sandwich for $6.50. The quantity and qualify is there. 

They do mix mayo with mustard and one other ingredient. Since I firmly believe a tradtional Tampa Cuban does NOT have mayo, I just asked for it on the side. Tasted okay, but I'm glad I ate most of my sandwich without it.

The empanadas looked terrific and for just $2.50 each, a couple of those were coming home with me as well. However, my first bite of a chicken one produced no ingredients...just dough. The dough is good, but it just wasn't a good first impression. 

Once I got to the ingredients of both the chicken and meat empanadas, I could really enjoy the flavors. So, I'm guessing they are that cheap because the size is a bit misleading based on the amount of filling? 

While we're nitpicking, I really wanted to try the soups...but both the small and medium containers were just too tiny for me. Too bad, the soups clearly looked fresh and had plenty of wonderful ingredients, but I didn't want to buy the large container.

Of course, I had to search for the Key Lime treats opposite the hot counter and I found both a small pie and a small tart that I think a good friend bought me a year or so ago. However, I never see Kentucky Derby Pie anywhere and chose that one since I hadn't had it in years. 

Much like the Cuban sandwich, this pie did not disappoint either.

Even better than the superb selection of food in here were the tremendous number of employees who are happy to answer questions and get whatever you want. 

I knew this to be the case even before walking in the store, as I called in advance of one of my golf tournaments recently to get information on buying cookies, cupcakes or brownies for a large group of players. A woman named Jasmin (no, not the Brandon-area Yelp Elite who turned me on to this place in the first place with her great review) took all the time I needed to answer many questions on the phone and I was very impressed by her effort in helping me.

I'll be back to try the chicken salad...since I'm always on the lookout for the best in Tampa Bay and have yet to find anything better than Big Stein's Deli in North St Peterburg.

As a regular at the MVP owned restaurants, Carmel is the one that I do not visit very often.

However, we were looking for a martini and their Thursday promotion of $5 martinis brought us in to check it out. 

The bar was pretty full in the evening with others enjoying small plates and the inexpensive drinks, but we did find seats and received attentive and friendly service.

Those chickpea fries are a tasty item that go well with drinks and we enjoyed how they are plated like a small game of Jenga.

Both of us thought the martinis were just okay although we certainly cannot argue with the price. 

The woman I was with knows a good Cosmo and she felt these were a bit weak compared to other places we've had a Thursday cocktail recently...such as Charley's or Doc B's. My dirty martini could have had more kick to it as well.

Beer selection is decent, but bottles only. Nothing available on draft.

Also, what's with the valet out front? They have a decent sized lot and it seems unnecessary, so we both parked our own cars.

Hopefully, they'll keep the promotional nights coming so we can come back and try some more of those small plates.

It looks like there is a new boy in town. This is definitely my new favorite sushi place. The Rocky roll and tuna tataki are just delicious. The place is nice and cozy. The presentation of dishes is fancy and impressive, which added a lot value to the dining experience. I am totally hooked!!!!
It's $$$ experience for $ price! Highly recommended for all sushi lover!!!

I came here yesterday for lunch with a couple of my coworkers.  This was my first time eating here, and I do love BBQ, so I was anxious to try it.  Bogart's is just across the street from Mission Taco in Soulard.  I've heard the line can get long here, but we came around 1:00 or so on a Friday, and there was only a short line of people in front of us.  The first thing I noticed about Bogart's is that it's very small, and has many tables that are almost smashed together.  If you're claustrophobic, you'll probably want to get your food to go.  The ordering process here is very similar to Pappy's.  That is, stand in line, look at the menu above the register, order, and wait for them to call your name.  

I went with the half rack of ribs, which came with two sides.  I chose the baked beans and chips as my side.  I thought the chips would be home made, but they came in what appeared to be a prepackaged bag.  The ribs were excellent, and the sides were pretty good as well.  On a side note, one thing I did like was that when they called my name to give me my food, they noticed that there were no available seats.  So, they offered to keep my food warm until some seats opened up.  It was just a few minutes later when some seats came available, and they brought my food right out.  I thought that was a nice touch.  While we were eating, the line to order became longer and longer, and it kinda felt like the people waiting in line were right on top of you.  Again, this place is just really small.

Overall, I thought the food was great.  The sauces were really good, with my favorite being the sweet sauce.  I'm just knocking off a star for the tight quarters feel of the restaurant.  I'd like to come back at a time when I know for sure that it won't be busy, which I guess would be really early or later in the evening.  Either way, I'll be back.

On a trip to SB we decided to eat dinner at Shalhoob before heading home. Shalhoob is not located on the main street where lots of restaurants, bars and wineries are located.  I checked them on Yelp first was pleased that they had 4.5 stars.  

There is lot of free parking available.  Santa  Barbara has changed a lot, a lot of business here now charge for parking.  

We ordered the street corn which came in a pan, garlic fries, chicken wings, smoked chicken, ribs & mac N cheese; lot of food for 2 people...enough to feed four, buttered bread!!!  :-) The food is so tasty, they give very large portions as well.  They offer plenty outside seating with shade.  They cater events.  Some of the tables are barrels with umbrellas.  The service was GREAT.

I highly recommend this place, you won't be disappointed.

Amazing!  Best tasting Greek in Tampa.  They have tons of freshly baked items that sell out by early afternoon-- so don't waste time getting there!  Their brunch is delicious.  We ordered:

-Avocado Psomi
-Spanakopita
-Tyropita
-Kalamata olive + feta bread
-melitzanosalata 
-Baklava
-2 fresh drip coffees

We ordered a few overlapping baked goods to try them all and to be honest, it's very very hard to pick a favorite.  The feta is whipped and warm in each and the phyllo paper is very crunch.  In each item you get texture and taste.  The avocado psomi is full of flavor and is on their fresh psomi bread.  The melitzaosalata was VERY fresh and was served with warm pita.  We finished an amazing baklava.

This place doubles as an amazing restaurant and bakery.  At the very least, stop by and pick up a few baked goods-- you won't be disappointed!

First off, Thank you to our Community Manager, Michael T. for writing an amazing review on this place because I ended up ordering the Birria Beef at this place for the first time last night and OH MY it was amazing. I don't even know how to put into words the flavor packed in this meat but it is to die for and if you ever go to El Adobe (which you should try if you haven't) and you have to try this plate at least once. It comes with rice and beans and the meat practically melts in your mouth. They also serve it with corn or flour tortillas so you can make tacos. 

I loved the atmosphere and the service was great. I had never been here before and I have no idea why!! My friend suggested we go to Mexican and said if I have not tried, I am missing out! Now, I am taking a friend here for lunch! 

Another thing I love about this place is that they give you red AND green salsa. The green salsa has a little more kick to it but it is amazing and goes well with your actual meal! I also had a margarita that did not disappoint. I am not a major tequila drinker but the flavor was not overpowering and just right for me. We were seated quickly and our food came super fast which was good because I was starving! I will definitely be going back here many times to order everything on the menu! Next up are the Tacos for sure....

I would have to say this is one of my favorite restaurants to go to on the weekends. Not only is it close to my house (in sparks) but it is cheap and so delicious and I have yet you have a bad meal here. Poncho and Willies is located inside the Western Village Casino towards the back of the room near Primo Pizza Cafe. If you go there on a Friday or Saturday you will definitely have to wait, but I promise, it's worth the wait! 

The restaurant has a cozy feel inside which I really enjoy either going as a date night or even with a group of friends. They have big booths that are seated up high in a half circle and we always get seated there. Its a fun place to be able to mingle and eat good food. Another thing I love about this place is they bring you a HUGE bowl of salsa so you almost never run out that is also followed by plenty of chips. You can order green or spicer salsa if you like it hot. 

The one food item I almost always order is the Tacos al Carbon with Steak. The meat is SO tender and juicy. It is five tacos with onion and cilantro and comes with a big pile of beans, rice and guac. YUMMY! They have tons of great dishes there but that is may favorite. 

Anther huge plus is their margaritas. Not only are all of them in the $6-$8 dollar range, even if you order top shelf you are not paying a whopping $10 per drink. They have tons of different options for margaritas such as RUM-arita and its really tasty! 

I would recommend this place to anyone that wants a great Mexican food experience with delicious drinks and great service!

It seems that you fall into one beignet camp or another while in New Orleans.  And those camps are either Cafe Du Monde or Cafe Beignet.
Having eaten beignets on more than one occasion at both these places, I can say with confidence that I prefer Cafe Beignet.

For starters, it's a less hyped place; less of a tourist trap. 
The beignets are made to order and are pillowy delectable fried and fattening little treasures.  Thank goodness there are only 3 to an order.  I could eat more for sure in one sitting but my beignet gluttony aside, 3 is plenty.

There's no accounting for individual preferences so all I'll say is that to my palate these beignets trump the ones I've had at "the other place."  Try both while you're in town and make up your own mind, and then get back to us on Yelp. 

I do think however, you'll also enjoy less of a line and an opportunity to enjoy your treats in the tranquil and pretty outside garden here.
There was no line at all the last time I was here during the late afternoon.


A coffee, chicory or otherwise, and an order of fresh beignets is a perfect afternoon treat after a day of walking the French Quarter.
It's "High Tea" New Orleans-style!

In the meanwhile, can someone please close one of the one too many cupcakeries here in Boston and open a beignet cafe instead?  There's a cupcakerie space on Charles St. I'd love to volunteer for this endeavor.

P.S.  Happy Groundhog Day!  Please, no shadow!

Although Muriel's has only been around since 2001, the location it has in Jackson Square has a history dating back to the 18th century. 
The building was originally constructed in the mid-1700s as a home for Jean Baptiste Destrehan who was the Royal Treasurer of the French Louisiana Colonies..

The home changed hands a number of times and had portions rebuilt after a fire in 1788, was used as a store, became the home of the Heritage Hall Jazz Band and was then another restaurant before becoming Muriel's.

The current owners did extensive and accurate renovations on this property bringing the interior back to the look it had in the 1800s.  When you walk in you're immediately struck by it's beauty and grandeur but it doesn't feel fussy or too formal.

We'd made reservations ahead of time for the jazz brunch.  We were warmly greeted when we entered and brought to our table.  
We were seated at a corner table affording a little more privacy which was nice. There was a window to the left and then a clear view outward into the rest of the lovely room.  

The window seat turned out to be a mixed blessing.  Although it afforded a view onto Jackson Square, it was in the path of the ubiquitous carriage horses and mules which fill me with sadness when I see them.  Suffice it to say, I'm not a fan of this trade. 

The brunch menu offers lots of options including spinach salad, crawfish and goat cheese crepes, Gulf shrimp remoulade, crawfish omelette, smoked salmon and bagels,and a pasta, mushroom and vegetable plate and a number of others.
The shrimp and grits were served in a really savory and rich Abita Amber beer sauce .  It was a delicious dish.  I've seen the Abita Beer sauce used in dishes elsewhere around town and it seems to be a local favorite.

The brunch cocktails include Bloody Mary's, Brandy Milk Punch, Sazerac, Ramos Gin Fizz and an Absinthe concoction.

It's worth taking a stroll around the restaurant to check out the many rooms and nooks and crannies.  Other areas include an outdoor balcony, an indoor courtyard bar area and The Seance room where the resident ghost of Pierre Antoine Lepardi Jourdan is said to reside.

The jazz trio was fun and added an upbeat element to what was the start of another lovely day in New Orleans.

I've said it before but  it needs saying again: I love W.I.N.O. 

Of course we returned here during our latest visit to NOLA. I dream about this place when I'm back home in Boston.

In my opinion, this concept is brilliant.

The "Enomatic" machines allow you to try any number of literally dozens of bottles of wine in the pour size of your choice. It's all done by the push of a button on the machine to which each wine bottle is attached.

You can sample as much or as little as you want of any of the wines.  You can stick to reds, whites, sparkling or mix it all up.

I advise filling the pink plastic payment card you'll be handed, with a set amount of money and using it as a debit to pay for each wine you decide to try.  
You can easily add more money to the card but it's a better way to stay in control of your spending.  
It is ridiculously easy to get carried away here but you'll have fun while doing so. 

If there are wines you find that you love, you can buy them right there by the bottle to take away with you.

Best of all though, is hanging out here, wandering about the place determining which wine you want to try next.  
You're not stuck sitting down in one place if you're more of a mingler which I am.  It provides a great opportunity to talk to other W.I.N.O.-ites.  It's an interactive experience really.

The atmosphere can feel like you're at a wine-tasting party at someone's cool home.

Please do sample some food from the menu too as they have great plates of appetizers that go so well with the wines.

I'm waiting for someone to bring this idea to Boston.  I'd be there all the time.

I'm actually amazed I have not written a review here yet.
Solid 5 stars!!!!

OMG. Delicious Aroma slams your face the minute you walk into the door, yes. Even with a mask on the aroma is soooo delicious. 

Will start with the establishment before I get into the details of their items. 

Location is a bit hidden, my husband was actually the one who found this place on Yelp. Not really my stomping ground, so unless you planned on going in specifically or happened to stumble across the other small business in the area it really is hidden.  Parking is limited, but every time I have gone in was still able to find parking up front. 

Establishment is very clean, staff is always friendly and seems to be a family owned/run. 
Which is a win #Support local business 

My husband is tall enough to catch a glimpse of someone making the Sausages by hand and just adds on to the whole excitement of wanting to eat it asap!

Okay, let's get down with the food. 
#1.) All you need to know is EVERYTHING HAS BEEN DELICIOUS. 

#2.) Everything seems to be made fresh! From the variety of sausages, ground chuck for hamburgers, etc. Yeah, I'm looking at you all the places I normally go to get my ground meat and there is hidden old meat in the center. Yes, yes I understand that the meat is still fine to use, but why the dishonesty? Just show it as it is! Luckily, this is something I don't have to worry about at The Sausage shop! 

We have also bought some smoked bacon and the quality is unbelievable! 
Have also enjoyed some variety of lunch meat as well as the sliced pastrami-- drool!!! 

They do have a small selection of smoked cheese, but since our family is dairy intolerant we haven't tried it yet. 

They also have a variety of bread rolls to enjoy with your sausages, homemade pickled pickle, sauerkraut, potatoes salad, pasta salad. 

We have tried everything listed above except the cheese. The drinks are also refreshing and easily available for a quick grab and go. 
They also do provide other condiments like the Vienna brand mixed peppers if you want to make a Chicago style dog. 

If cooking isn't your thing, they also seem to provide sandwiches freshly made and ready to go. Saw several people stopping by to just buy a sandwich for lunch and was sooo tempted to try it as well. Will definitely have to in the future.  

*Disclaimer: I'm honestly not a big sausage fan, which was the reason why I was so surprised at how much I really enjoy their sausages. Quality ingredients, freshly made and well done taste made me realize how many people have not actually had a great quality sausage!

We have grilled, baked, sauteed and works great in every way! 

***Bonus note: they also sell these "Meat Sticks" lol that kinda remind me of a more delicious and better slim jim. Works great as a work snack or when hubby wants a little late night snack. Highly recommend! 

Don't forget to tip the staff for their help!
My husband and I both decided we could make better at home. Service was quick, as was the food. We split one sandwich and was glad we did. Plenty of better food in the city.

We went to happy hour here.  The menu offers some unique food options that are fresh and delicious.

We tried the Chicken Potstickers, Cucumber Maki Roll, and Penn Maki Roll from the Happy Hour Menu and ordered the Chicken Dumpling Ramen from the standard menu.  We enjoyed everything, but the Potstickers were especially tasty. The outside was thin and pan seared perfectly and the filling was generous.  The Ramen broth was flavorful and the dumplings were really good.  The noodles were average; probably not freshly made. Both Maki Rolls are also terrific.  

Pod has a futuristic interior feel to it with unique furniture and lighting.  The bathrooms feel a bit like airplane restrooms.  The service was personable and attentive.

L'anima provides good food, nice ambiance and great service, even amid a Global Pandemic. The name translates to "the soul" in Italian. And it's a BYOB!  The outdoor dining was not crowded on a Thursday evening.  Perfect when social distancing is a requirement.  The restaurant is located on the first floor of a condo building and it's the only nice restaurant within blocks in this residential part of Graduate Hospital.

We ordered the Potato Gnocchi Wild Boar Bolognese and the Eggplant Tomato and Mozzarella Pinsa (i.e. Flatbread). Both items were flavorful and delicious. The entree portion size was adequate. The Pinsa is large enough to share and my husband helped me polish it off.

Covid-19 Review
When restaurants first re-opened for outdoor dining, we headed to Jet Wine Bar.  Their outdoor dining space is inviting considering its South Street location.  The restaurant was very well prepared and staffed to handle dining during the "Covid-Era".  

We were asked to keep masks on until we were seated, once at our table we could remove our masks.  The tables were situated well beyond the 6 feet social distance practice. All tables had hand sanitizer and bug spray on them. All the staff wore masks and they were very professional and friendly.  

They have a menu specifically for outdoor dining, which can be located on their website.  No hard copy menus were provided, another thoughtful precaution.

We ordered the Veggie Burger and the Spicy chicken sandwich.  Both of us really enjoyed our food and the entire experience.  

Kudos to Jet Wine bar for handling an otherwise unprecedented situation in a very professional, safe, and cautious manner.

Although this is not the original City Tavern of the late 1700s, George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, John Adams and like have been on this site for meetings and dining.  City Tavern was demolished and rebuilt in the 1970s. 

They have decorated the Tavern with furniture and decor from the that era and the wait staff are adorned in the clothing from the time period as well.  We stopped in here for some drinks to get a "taste" of history.   It maybe a bit touristy, but worthwhile to check out.  

We got the Ales of the Revolution Flight inspired by Washington, Jefferson, and Hamilton. Also ordered the City Tavern Bread Tray.  Thomas Jefferson's sweet potato pecan biscuits were the best on the bread tray.  The other items weren't that exciting.

Under the Moon Cafe is a charming little place with eclectic decor of mismatched chairs and tables, which look like they could have been picked up at a consignment shop. The overall ambiance is nice. However, I found the interior a bit to dimly light, a few brighter lights would be nice.

I went here for lunch recently and we ordered the Crab Cake Sandwich and the Grilled Salmon Sandwich.  I found the portion size of both the crab cake and salmon, subpar.  My crab cake was completely overshadowed by the huge brioche bun. For a $13 sandwich a little more substance would be nice. 

Where this place excels is dessert, by far.  I literally had the best Coconut Cream pie I have ever had in my life!  It was a huge piece, yet light and fluffy.  The key ingredient is Mascarpone cheese. Calling it a coconut cream pie is a bit misleading, it's more like a cheesecake, but oh so delicious.  Indulge!!

Finally made it over to Los Camaradas.  The food is great, the staff is very friendly, and the place has a great local restaurant feel located right in the middle of a residential area of grad hospital.  

We ordered the Pollo Enchiladas and the Chicken Tinga Burrito.  Both were plentiful in size and flavorful in taste. The place was packed (inside and outside) for a Tuesday, so I think others in the area feel the same positive vibes for this establishment.  

I really liked the decor as well.  Lots of "day of the dead" type artwork in and around the bar area.  We will certainly be back, the next time the Mexican food urge hits us.

We had the best experience here.  The food is phenomenal, great ambiance and excellent service. I really appreciate the fact that they have a Vegan/Vegetarian menu that is not a knock-off of the regular menu, but instead unique, well prepared, and delicious alternatives.  Even my meat eating husband decided to order off the Vegan menu, because it was so interesting with enticing entrees. 

We ordered Tom Yum soup, Chatayee Kang Kewan (Vegan Green curry), Kang Rawang Hed (Vegan Mushroom based entree), and Pad Kee Mao Kai (Rice Noodles with Chicken). There were 4 of us that shared the food and we all raved how tasty everything was. 

Seriously, this place was so good and I'm always looking for a good Thai place to frequent and I think I've found it. So, if you love Thai food and perhaps catching a show at the Kimmel, I would highly recommend Chatayee Thai.

We were on the search for a casual eatery prior to a show at the theater and Tria café fit the bill. We arrived during happy hour which runs from 5 PM to 7 PM. There were no available tables so we opted to sit at the bar. There are also outdoor dining tables. 

The bartenders were very personable and professional. The happy hour menu offered a small selection of $5 wines, beers and snacks. We ordered the cheese and salami appetizer which was ok for five bucks. 

The dinner menu includes salads, sandwiches and small bites. We ordered the roasted beets and goat cheese salad and the roasted turkey ciabatta bread. The salad was fabulous and I didn't think I was really a beet person. One of the best beet salads I've had! The turkey sandwich, served cold, was very tasty and on great bread. A good sandwich is typically all about the bread. 

All in all, Tria café offers some nice food options at affordable prices.

I've eaten here a few times while visiting my dad, basically because its what my dad knows and for lack of other Mexican restaurant options.  And after most visits the food is just ok and not very memorable.  After this last visit, I don't think I care to return.

Which is a shame, because the Border Cafe located in Cambridge, Mass is actually really good.  Food is always consistent and that location is always packed with up to an hour wait. 

We ordered Blacked Catfish, Blackened Salmon, Filet Mignon Jim Bowie Style, and the fajitas with Blackened Chicken.  There is a sharp difference between blacked and burned.  All the blackened entrees, were burned to point of them probably being carcinogenic.  I've ordered these dishes before in Cambridge and the preparation has always been good.  But, the Delaware Border Cafe just doesn't seem to get it.  And those shoestring fries served with the Filet, just horrible... hard and crisp.  I didn't think it was possible to mess up french fries, but apparently it isn't.

We went here for New Year's Eve and we appreciated the fact they were serving their regular menu and not a pricey NYE 3 or 4 course prix fixe.

We had a wonderful evening. The food was awesome, service was great and I really love the ambiance here.  It was a very busy night given the occasion, but the entire staff and our waitress were on the ball.  The staff was all dressed in sparkly party attire, which was a nice touch for the night.

I ordered the Baby Kale and Beet Salad and the Spinach Ravioli.  The salad was great, but I especially loved the Ravioli.  I'm not one for thick heavy pasta dishes, but this Ravioli was prepared very thin. In fact you could see the spinach right through it.  It was really tasty! 

The rest of the table ordered the Seared Tuna, Salmon Sashimi Poké Bowl, Braised Short Rib.  Everyone enjoyed their meal. 

Dessert was the only thing that did not impress me too much. We ordered the Smores Cheesecake, and the Cookie and Brownie Sundae.  The desserts were good, but nothing to write home about.

White Dog Cafe is an awesome spot for Sunday Brunch.  It was bustling and very busy, but the staff and waiters were very attentive.  The waitress told us that White Dog was the first farm to table restaurant on the East Coast.  Therefore, all the ingredients are local and fresh.

We ordered a couple of omelets (the Kenneth Square and Lancaster County Three Egg Omelet).  Both were accompanied by home fries (essentially diced potatoes).  They were good omelets and stuffed with fillings.  I substituted carmelized onions for the bacon in the Lancaster and it was really great along with the roasted tomatoes, spinach and goat cheese.

The decor is rather cool with painting and other sculptures paying homage to dogs.

Kawaii Kitty Cafe deserves a 4-star on the concept alone. It's part cafe, serving coffee and ice cream, and part adoption center for cute little cats. And the term Kawaii means "cute" in Japanese. 

We stopped here on a whim on a Friday evening when recently in the Queen Village area. Because, we were limited on time, we didn't take advantage of the Cat Lounge.  Reservations are suggested, but on this evening there was no wait. The price for one hour is $11 and half an hour is $6.  The admission helps cover food, toys, litter and medical care for the cats. The cats are cage free and have ample area to sleep, hide and play.  

We did get some ice cream. The selection is limited, but the cafe is more about the cats. You are welcome to take your food and drink into the cat lounge.

Since moving to the neighborhood, we had passed Miles Table so many times and were looking forward to trying it. I'm torn with my rating.  We just didn't have a great experience with our food as every other Yelper to merit a 4-star. 

I ordered the Avocado Toast, which is accompanied by potatoes.  The eggs were not over easy (as my picture shows) and the potatoes were overly salty.  My husband ordered one of the specials and it also failed to deliver a solid punch in taste or flavor.  

The service and the employees were super friendly and we will give this place another try in the future, since we live so close.

When it comes to service, ambiance, and decor, Veda is top-notch.  This upscale Indian eatery offers a bit of a fusion infused punch to Indian food.  Traditional Indian food enthusiasts may not be too enticed by Veda, since the prices are higher than your typical Indian fare.  But the price is part of the Rittenhouse Square location and the trendy, upscale feel of the restaurant.  

The Food:  We ordered the Chicken Makhani, Chicken Chettinad and the Tofu Green Peas Curry.  The Chicken entrees were good, especially the Chettinad.  This dish was everyone's favorite.  The Makhani was on the sweeter and creamier side; more than any of us preferred.  The Tofu and Green Peas was a disappointment.  Primarily because, it was mostly gravy.  There were hardly any peas and the tofu was a bit skimpy as well.  The serving dish for the vegetarian entree was about half the size of the chicken dishes.  I would not recommend ordering this entree. There was no substance to it.

Whether you eat in or take it to go, Real Food Eatery is a healthy and quick alternative for lunch or dinner at reasonable prices. 

You can create your own plate or bowl by starting off with a base which consists of either salad, rice or quinoa. Add to that a protein of your choice (hormone & antibiotic free, grass-fed, and sustainably raised). The last step allows you to add 2 healthy sides. They offer a unique selection of hot and cold sides. 

You can also order one of their signature bowls or salads.  I went with the warm goat cheese and beet salad. I found the portion plentiful and it was a hearty and delicious salad. I never thought I would say this, but I've developed a new found fondness for beets!

This place was awesome.  We happened to be walking by, while looking for a place to grab some dinner after the Christmas Tree lighting.  1518 Bar and Grill was full of people and festively decorated for the holidays. We walked in and were immediately seated at a high top.

The place is small and the same waiter was seating people, taking orders, and serving the food.  He was doing a pretty swift job juggling all these tasks.

We ordered the 1518 Burger and Heavens Garden (sandwich with grilled zucchini, eggplant, peppers, tomato confit, melted swiss).  The burgers and sandwiches come with the option of salad or french fries.  We opted for the salad and both our meals were delicious.  I would order the Heaven's Garden again in a heartbeat.  It was a fairly large sandwich and I took half to go and enjoyed it for lunch the next day.

Have loved sprinkles since I first experienced tasting a cupcake from them in DC (Georgetown location).

They are insanely good to the point where I won't go anywhere else. First of all, can we talk about the moistness?! I hate places that make it out like their cupcakes are superior, when it turns out it's just a piece of dry ass cake and pounds of buttercream icing on top.

Sprinkles is none of that. Their cake is always moist, the cupcakes don't taste like a sugar overload, and the icing is infused with actual flavor and not just cloyingly sweet buttercream. 

I'm so excited the Tampa location is open! 
I stalked the website, found out when they had the flavors I wanted, and picked out four cupcakes. I got strawberry, banana, and salted caramel. The strawberry was divine, and I haven't gotten to the banana yet, but what I will say is that I underestimated the salted caramel. I'm usually not too fond of it anymore because that flavor is so over featured now, it's become pretty basic To me. But wow, was I wrong. I'm confident that is by far is the best cupcake they have! So moist, salty and sweet the icing and the sea salt flecks tied everything together in harmony...I'll  even admit that as a strawberry lover!

Please do yourself a favor and go to sprinkles!! Great location for a place like that!

They don't even deserve 1star, the owners daughter threatened me!
After I was served my side salad, I was informed I could not have the steak I ordered, as they were all out of "rare" prime-rib. I order another cut and was again told they didn't have that either. So I declined to order anything else, as the waitress had waited nearly 20min before telling me they couldn't make my steak, and I knew my friends would be served any minute. 
Halfway through his meal, the waitress, in rush to clean up, reached across my friends plate to take his soup cup, that still had soup in it. His soup wasn't anywhere near the center of the table, she actually had to reach to get it and she didn't even bother to ask if he was finished or not. He was NOT.
As we are paying our bill, I ask about an extra charge and am informed it's for the dinner salad I ordered. I begun to explain to the cashier/owner/mother, that I didn't order any dinner salad and that I had eaten a side salad that came with a meal they were never able to serve me, two meals in fact, because they didn't have the second steak I ordered either. The waitress served me my salad and allowed me to dress it before informing I couldn't have my steak and she never mentioned having to charge me for the salad or I wouldn't have eaten it. 
While I am explaining this, the waitress/daugher/spoiled brat, starts getting rude, saying things like "it's only salad, what's the big deal" and "you ate it so just pay for it, it's not that big of deal". 
So now I'm mad and begin to inform the owner of her need to retrain this most unprofessional staff. I start telling her how her server reached over plates to take food that was not finished and immediately the waitress starts arguing again, "there was barely anything in the bowl". I tell her "there was still food in it that he is paying for and that's all that matters".
Now the older gentleman standing at the counter starts to chime in, explaining to me why I couldn't have the steak I ordered. I'm beyond the dinner salad at this point, their waitress has been rude and yelled at me, all in front of them. I ask him if he's an owner and he says yes. I tell him he needs to correct his staff, he had been trying to shoo her off, but not very hard. As him and I talk, things start to calm back down, I'm not so upset, my friend is still paying his bill, it's nice and quiet. 
All of a sudden you hear "look at me one more time, bitch, and see what haopens"... Excuse me?! What??? I hadn't even been looking at her, I was talking to him. I look her dead in the eye and ask " what did you say?" And she repeated herself again. Oh I about climbed over that counter, and asked "what's gonna happen?" 
"Oh you'll see what happens, keep it up bitch" she exclaims.
So I step back and take out my phone, "I should've been recording her foolishness from the beginning" I say and then "I'm going to yelp you, google review, sc, fb, and tell everyone I know of how I was treated"... only then did he actually try to remove his staff/daughter and she's pushing him off the whole time. And they never even apologized for any of her behaviors or how we were treated in their restaurant.
I have never been spoken to or treated so badly in a restaurant, ever!
When did Big Ed's change owners anyways? They're horrible now!

This is a late review from about a year after the Stone House re-pened.  My girlfriend who is in a wheelchair because she has muscular dystrophy was made to feel unwelcome by the owner's daughter. Evidently, she did not like the idea of allowing my girlfriend's certified golden retriever service dog into the establishment. The owner's daughter politely asked if the service dog could stay in the car. The dog picks things up from the floor and opens and closes doors among other things. Needless to say, we left the Stonehouse without eating and never returned. One star for insensitive service.

I am being generous with the one star.  Restaurant smells of a urine like odor.  Kitchen staff including the owner talking and laughing in loud voices, we could not hear each other speak, food less than ordinary, extra small portions, my friend ordered a pasta with vegetables which looked like a teenager put it together, white corkscrew with a few peas and green onions and cost $17.  the house wine was $14. a glass, the salad looked like it came from the pre packaged salad section  at Ralph's.  

My friend and I should have left before we even sat down as the restaurant was empty at  noon while the restaurant across the street was full of people, I now know why.

After a 4 hour drive to New Orleans on the way to the WWII Museum, went straight to the American Sector Restaurant to refuel before starting my tour.  Layout is nice, open, and with a lot of windows.  There's a choice of cafe tables, booths, and bar seats.  Bellied up to the bar and ordered a local draft and a chicken/sausage gumbo.  The bartender was prompt, courteous, and attentive.  The gumbo bowl soon came- dark, rich, and great-smelling.  I was a tad hungry, so I wolfed down the soup.  It was tasty, though.  This is a café in a museum, so I didn't expect a cheap deal.  Beer, soup, tax, and tip came out close to $20.  It was certainly convenient to refresh your body before starting or resuming your tour.  Recommend and will repeat.

There are only three words you need to know about Dough: DUCK FAT FRIES!

The recently acquired Chef Domenica Macchia has risen Dough to a whole new level.  Small plates and desserts sets Dough apart from its Big Sister, Datz, next door.  Unique, creative gelato flavors and thinking outside of the doughnut box keeps Tampa runnin' on Dough.  Wash down your bacon maple doughnut with a bacon maple cappuccino topped with bacon crumbles.

Dough offers a private room which is perfect for small functions, such as baby showers or professional development workshops.  For these special events, Dough will create a menu tailored for your guests.

Danny was our driver for the Jingle Bus Holiday Tour for the OYE... Uh, can you say the BEST bus driver in SB? We had a great time because Danny took us to all the beautiful homes decked out for the holidays. His driving skills are excellent, safe, and not once did I get car sick (THANKS!). 

Danny was considerate of us lookie-loos as we gazed at the sparkly lights, he slowed down and even stopped at a few places for us. There are handles on the ceiling that make it easy to stand up with you enjoy the sights. Seats are converted so you can enjoy your company. 

The bus was very clean and seats were comfy. It was a bit on the colder side because it's an older school bus, but nonetheless, so much fun! Stereo system packed some bass and we had so much fun singing along to Christmas tunes. 

Thank you Danny for making our night and cranking up the holiday cheer :)

We came for lunch just as they opened for the day. I liked that they were ready to serve us as we arrived. Two bowls of chips, two salsas, and some guacamole came ASAP and our ice-cold drinks came immediately. Now that's service! We sat in the side patio with our small pup. They even brought water and a nice bowl for our dog. 

We ordered a variety of things: chicken fajitas, pork pozole, and an enchilada and hard taco combo. The food we ordered was more than enough for the four of us and our little pup. The entrees are shareable. The combo was a beautiful plate of black beans, rice, enchilada and taco (and the frilly lettuce and Cotija cheese sprinkling). I had the pork pozole which had tender chunks of pork, lots of hominy, flavorful broth, and a plate of the fixings (red radishes, oregano, cabbage, chunks of avocado, cilantro and onions). The fajita plate was as expected - plate full of onions and bell peppers and tasty chunks of grilled chicken, along with the fixings. No skimping here! The best part of the meal, aside from the company, were the homemade corn tortillas - we ate every single tortilla and even fought for the last piece. 

The restaurant is warm and inviting. The spanish decor has lots of warm colors like gold and orange. It's a classy date-night kind of place. At night there's live music where the bar and dining room meet. The service here has always been wonderful but the food... It's bomb!

I've had the Mole here too and its AMAZING! I recommend trying the spanish-style (Catalonian) tapas Pan con tomate and the torta espanola (takes 20min to prepare). You wont regret dining here!

Today, I was lucky enough to try some appetizers: truffle parmesan tater tots, calamari, guacamole, ceviche, and steak tacos. Never had tater tots like these before! I would highly advise staying away from the tots because they are delightful, little, crunchy bits of cheese-y, truffle-y goodness! So addicting and tasty! I wish i could take these by the truckload :D

The guacamole and ceviche were excellent too! I feel like you can either go right or wrong with appetizer staples like these... Well Arch Rock, you did good! 

Steak tacos were small, street taco style but were a lot juicier, meatier, and were just enough to whet my palate. I'd definitely come back for more. I really like the little citrus, vinegar-y red onions and paper-thin cuts of radishes on top. The garnishes complimented the tacos perfectly. 

Calamari were also delicious and was very pleased that they were NOT chewy and soaked in oil. TG! The lemon aioli was refreshing and delightfully paired with the well-seasoned bits of calamari, fried (not spicy) peppers, and green onion. Those fried bits of veggies were a nice addition to the calamari. 

Drinks are superb ;) Appreciate the heavy enough pour that doesn't overwhelm the taste buds. It's not about getting obliterated but enjoying your drinks here. The bartenders are friendly enough that if you weren't satisfied, they'd make it up to you... But i highly doubt any drink here could be subpar.

I just learned about the Sunday Funday all-day happy hour. And guess what?! I'll be baaack and I'm bringing a crowd too! Thanks Arch Rock. Keep up the great food and drinks.

I've had quite a few things here and I'll definitely be back for more! The menu is extensive and has a variety of foods to appeal to any cravings. Their desserts are delicious too like their version of chocolate and strawberry shortcake.
I had the pleasure of having the Parm (eggless quiche) which had a lot of hearty greens, tomatoes, and a nutritional yeast crust. Interestingly, it was shaped like a snowball or scone. Nonetheless, amazing flavors! I've also had the Mac & Cheese which was unforgettable... Not too sure of the ingredients or whether it's vegan but oh WOW, so good! Has hints of mushroom and is well worth the try.
All of these dishes are vegetarian and are so flavorful! They're all reasonable priced and good portions. I definitely recommend visiting this place and ordering a matcha tea or green pressed juice :) 
Thanks Boochies! See you soon...

So we tried Sierra St Kitchen since we seen all the good reviews and I must say this was the worst food place I've been to. First off our waiter was not so great. Madelein seemed like she didn't have any clue what she was doing or even cared to serve that night. The chefs in the back were sending out entree's before the appetizers. Seriously guys get your stuff together that's sad and pathetic as a so called restaurant. We had a party of 7 people so I understand the gratuity charge but damn I felt like they didn't deserve it with such crappy service and food. I wish I photo of the steaks but I gotta say they looked like TV dinner trays you can pick up at a grocery store. Rating I give a "F". Also the the owner (Brett R.) is completely rude to his customers. You should be ashamed of yourselves. It's sad that you can't take any criticism whatsoever. Instead of bashing on your customers especially the Californian's apparently you hate so much learn how to stop being a jerk. Brett you messed up and I hope you business closes to teach you a lesson. FYI sending private messages to people and calling them out makes you a punk. Grow up and grow a pair. 

Do not support this business or an owner like this. Covid might not have closed you but the people will.

I have been to Scoogis many times - and I must admit - I have never wanted to go back since my first visit - but it is close to my friends house and she drags me there.

I argue with here every time - I say the waitstaff is rude the food is never cooked to order.

Every time we go - we are disappointed - enough so for me to write this review.

The most recent experience:

My friends steak was prepared medium-well when she ordered medium-rare - OOPS! 
We waited for an hour so the first steak, but agreed to let them re-make the order. The new steak came out almost too quick - and when my friend cut it - it was soooo rare it may have walked off the plate. At this point - she lost her appetite and did not want the steak at all anymore.
