The bread, we were told would take a while since it was frozen and had to be de-frosted. We were told that they buy fresh bread from an Italian Bakery everyday - but then put it in the freezer if they don't serve it. 

Our server went so far as to tell us that the Italian Bread was frozen brick solid and we could BUY some garlic bread instead. (The italian bread is free with your meal) The garlic bread is made from stale amoroso rolls we were informed.

My meal, a pasta dish was also not so good. The Gemelli pasta was not cooked long enough and was kinda hard. I seasoned the bland sauce myself by asking the server for some garlic powder, and I used the salt and pepper on the table. ARG!

I had ordered some shrimp on the side - but I swear they were microwaved because they were rubbery and weird.

The end of our meal was not completed with coffee and dessert.
We were never offered any. The check was just smacked down on the table as a message to leave! (So we did)

I will never allow my friend to talk me into going here ever again! What a waste of money!!

The service here is fast and friendly.

The food is really good.  The pasta dishes here are amazing.

And the desserts are out of this world. My niece loves this place too.

Its great for kids.

Definitely get a reservation as this place gets packed on Friday evenings, and be ready to find street parking. We waited for about 20 mins even with a reservation, which was not ideal. However the food was great, especially the tiramisu at the end. Also really liked my Moscow mule, pacific shrimp pasta and the shrimp scampi.

Came by after lunch time on a Tuesday afternoon and met the very friendly and helpful chef and employees as the restaurant was empty. The food here is fantastic, including the beef and lamb kafta sandwich, falafel and baba ghanoush (free with yelp check in). Unfortunately they didn't have the knafeh but I'd return during dinner time to enjoy the wonderful decor and some other options on the menu like dinner plates.

If you couldn't tell, I am Indian and I am very particular on Indian restaurants mainly because my mom is an amazing cook and I rather eat her home cooking but I highly recommend Rasoi as an Indian restaurant that you would need to go to.  Unlike my favorite Indian restaurant in Tampa, Curry Leaves this restaurant is more towards the North Indian cuisine. 

I usually have gotten the chicken sagg, which is chicken in a creamy spinach sauce, it is yummy and I recommended. I have tried their butter chicken and it is also yummy and I also recommended it.  I of course recommend getting the naan , because you can't go to an Indian restaurant without getting nann (but I will give you a look if you call it nann bread) 

The spice level is ON POINT THOUGH!  I always get Indian hot and I am enjoying every spicy bite I have had. 

The decor is simple and nice, parking is a pain because the resturant is located in Ybor. 

I will come again and hopefully bring my parents as they are the real judges of Indian cuisine.

If you have friends visiting Tampa for the first, second, third time. Please take them here.  Gorgeous views, yummy food, and great drinks.  Trust me when I say, you have to take them. Even if you don't have friends, you need to get over and try out Ulele right away. 
On my most recent visit, we sat by the bar and had a few mimosas and some food. Service was great and our bartender/server was friendly and informative.  We had the carrot ribbions, which I highly recommend!  Carrots that are battered with something amazing and an ailoi that I want to eat on everything. I had the shrimp and grits and my friend had a the alligator hushpuppies,  and crab mac and cheese.  I happily tried the crab and mac and cheese and thought it was great. I was forced to eat the hushpuppies and was not a fan. I like hush puppies but it was not my favorite.  The shrimp and grits were amazing.  

I think this is a great place to bring family, friends and even that special someone!  Def a must have on places to go eat in Tampa!

Every time I have came here, I always had a great time! The first time I came here for my friends birthday and we sat at tables by the bar. We all got apps and drinks. I had the lone star lemonade, and that cucumber margarita. Both were super yummy! For apps we had the chips and dips. It came with three dips, a  queso blanco, a chili queso and guacamole. The queso blanco was a fan favorite. The second time we came was during a girls outing. We all had their mimosas and loved it!
The last time I came was when we had time between the wedding ceremony and the reception. We the ceviche and we again had the chips and three dips. I had the strawberry basil margarita this time and it was okay, a little too tart.
Every time we have gone, we have always had great service. The staff is incredible! I can't wait to come back to try their brunch and more of their food!

Hellfire's new location is leaps and bounds better than their last one (bonus points for being closer to me too!) Not only did they spend a lot of time creating a nice interior, that works for dining, drinking, or listening to bands, but they serve some pretty good food too.

Porky's Revenge (a throwback to the business that used to reside in this location) is a huge pulled pork sandwich with a massive pile of fries. This thing is messy, make sure to ask for extra napkins! The wedge salad is a lighter option, only in the sense that it's smaller in size. The lightness ends when you top a classic wedge salad with pulled pork. Yum! The Ogre was the only thing I was sort of disappointed with. It's a burritto filled with pork, beef, chili, beans, cheese, and pico de gallo. Sounds like it's be really flavorful, but no it was really not. There were so many wet ingredients that this just turned into a sloppy mess (especially when it's to-go and the to-go box is lined with a paper lining - not good). I found myself just dumping hot suace on it to give it the help it needed.

Besides the food, I've been just for drinks. It's usually kind of slow when there's not a band playing so there's plenty of room at the bar. The few times I have been in while they had a band, I really enjoyed them. I think all of times they've been a country-ish band. 

I think this a good addition to that part of town and I'll be back soon!

I had family in town but was also in the middle of doing the Whole30. My parents, understanding that there were some limits to what I could eat, suggested Morgan's Lobster Shack for dinner. Seeing the "Fresh Pick" section of their menu was awesome because there were so many options that would work for me.

We showed up maybe 45 minutes before closing time, which always makes me kind of nervous, but they happily sat us at a table. Unfortunately, outside wasn't an option since they had just finished their crab boil and were still cleaning it up, but they opened up the big roll-up door to let us get some of the fresh evening air. Our server was great - friendly, willing to get answers to the questions I had regarding ingredients that were used, and quick to bring drink refills. Although, considering that we were the ones there for most of the time, I wouldn't expect that service would be slow!

The "Fresh Pick" section of their menu lets you choose the kind of fish (or chicken), how it's cooked, what seasoning is on it, and how you get it (sandwich, wrap, or salad). I went with the halibut, grilled, with the chili-lime seasoning as a salad. Not sure if this is how they normally do it, but my fish seemed to be cooked sans-seasoning and then the chili-lime seasoning came in the form of a vinaigrette for my salad. This tasted good, but I think it would have been better if the fish had some of the chili-lime seasoning added during cooking. 

I'm looking forward to returning now that I can try the lobster mac and cheese or a lobster roll.

I was overjoyed to sample some of the innovative items offered at Ulele. I can highly recommend the Native Summer Cocktail (gin, Elderflower, fresh lime juice, simple syrup, and cucumbers), the okra fries with a to-die-for house-made ketchup, and I have been dreaming about the Crackling Pork Shank for days. I enjoy the way they pay homage to the past with items like the Jalapeno Corn Beer Quick bread, and I love the way they embrace all things Florida. There are also many comfort food type items done at a gourmet level. I was happy to relish all of this tastiness while in a beautiful setting. Well done, Ulele, you are a future gem of this community.

Quality of the food was just ok to sub par. The prices are ridiculously expensive for what you get.  Salads were 15-20$ onion rings $10 .  The food took forever to come out. 
Never again.

Really great burger/sandwich place in Maplewood with full bar. Very inventive choice of cocktails. You won't be disappointed no matter what you choose, and they don't skimp on the alcohol in those so be warned. Service was really attentive. Thing that threw us off a bit initially is (covid era) ordering where you have to order at the counter before sitting , but they helpfully said you can order something and then sit and look at menu and then add to it, which was fine. We got the Sam Elliott burger , fried chicken sandwich. Both were delicious, the Sam Elliott mayo was a bit patchy which is pet peeve of mine so one can order with it on the side if needed. We got a couple of desserts to go at the end of dinner and drinks (not pictured). All in all a fun outing for an early dinner with a toddler.

My sister's Veganism is rubbing off on me... I am starting to fall for Mr. Vegan... His Dashing good looks, those classic traditional styles with a hint modern day chic. And you know he's totally fit, fine, and healthy... too hard to resist... He's an acquired taste but if you acquire him he definitely has you hooked. Oh and did I mention he smells divine?

Tuesday night and my sister and I are starving for some wholesome comfort vegan Food. We drove around downtown and everything seems to be closed or closing. Then we thought Remedy! They must be open. We drove over and sure enough the bright open sign was on, thank goodness. 

This is not our first visit here, we have been going to Remedy south side for over 10 years so that's how we know that they must be open in downtown.

You first walk in and you know this place is the happening place. The rainbow of people from all walks of life has made their way over and I'm guessing it's for the chai or food. Our first reaction was to go to the dessert window and see what treats are displayed. It never fails how good the dessert look and sound, plus there are vegan desserts that look too yummy.

We decided to get food first (our stomachs were crying from neglect). I got the vegan butter chicken with naan and my sister got a vegan dish but I am so sorry I forgot what she had but it looked good( I posted a pic). We also got their famous Chai. I highly recommend dining in because I think the mugs are so much bigger than the "to go" cups.

Our Chai was hot, warm, delicious, and full of crunchy almonds and coconut bits. Oh to die for...

It did not take long for our meals to arrive. My vegan butter chicken smelled so good and the naan was fluffy, light, and easy to eat with my sauce. I know my sister loved hers because I just saw her inhale her meal. By the end of it I was ultimately full that I could not be tempted by dessert.

This place it's lovely, from the unique staff to the colourful patrons and decor. The food will always be the hearty comfort vegan meal that makes you're belly sing and the chai is amazing. If you're passing by grab a dessert it would not disappoint. 

This is our go to place, whether it be the south side or the downtown location it never fails to impress.

I will always come back.

We love Indian food. So when Cross Culture opened, we made sure to give this place a try.

The place is fairly big and bright with lots of room and appropriate decor... The service was friendly and fairly quick...

To play it safe I've ordered what I usually do - Navrattan Korma and Chicken Tikki Masala. The food was not bad, but it definitely did not justify the price for the lunch portion I've received.

If that's was all, I'd probably give them 3 or 3.5 stars and move on to other places...

But...

Sadly, out of four people who ate there that day, three ended up with (lets say) some pretty bad stomach issues and since it was the only meal either of us had and everyone is accustomed to eating Indian, the only conclusion is that it was the food we ate at Cross Culture...

Perhaps we were unlucky and it was just a bad day, but considering a plethora of good Indian restaurants in the area, II am not taking my chances again...

It's a staple and I just happened to be in the quarter on a rare occasion so I had to stop by. I missed the jazz, the setting and of course the amazing little powdered sugar goodness of Cafe Du Monde's famous begniets!! 

Whether you're in the quarter, in city park or one of the local places around the city it's consistent and delicious!

In my opinion this King Cake is top 3 in the city bar none! The bakery is solid and I like their macaroons too. If you get here during King Cake season do yourself a favor and go with the Pecan Praline.

I love the amount of choices at creamistry !! Oh so I'm lactose intolerant?! Fine there's two options and both are great! Depending on how many options you include the price can rise quickly but you kind of expect that? All in all I'm a fan and since it's frozen with nitrogen it stays cold much longer than normal...and it's really creamy especially the cashew milk ice cream
Love this little place, the pho is outstanding here and the staff is always genuinely pleasant and friendly. I've frequented often and will continue to do so.

This is another great little spot kinda tucked away in Harahan. The food is excellent fresh and tasty. Take out is a piece of cake and it's always right and fast. The Pad Thai is a win as is the Panaeng Curry!

Very cool place to go to, had to see what the buzz was about and wasn't disappointed in the least!! We had the breakfast sandwich and the French toast. I got a pour over with Rwandan beans which was very good no bitterness and I drink my coffee black. Really smooth and great finish to it. I was tempted to guzzle it but had to slow my roll a little and enjoy it. 

Give this place a shot!!!

Usually namese is on point and don't get me wrong the food is good. We had a terrible experience with a carry out order, the male on the phone was flat out rude and condescending. 

Our order was lacking one item we paid for and he swore that he put it in our bag so I asked that he check his itemized receipt since they never gave me one and after about 5 minutes on hold he came back on the phone and asked if I still wanted my food they had forgot!!! Serious bro !?!?? 

So I went back and picked it up mean while I have hungry in laws at home and all the rest of the order got cold. No offer of making it up to us or trying to provide any sort of an apology whatsoever. 

Namese your food is solid but folks seem like they're getting a bit too complacent. Step yo game up!!

Love the new location and the decor of Clesi's, the outdoor seating is awesome especially since seating is limited. 

We ordered shrimp, crawfish and an andouille po-boy. The boil for the shrimp and crawfish were the same flavor and level of heat. Just a small hit of heat as you eat it which wasn't bad at all. FYI you can't order in 1/2 lb increments, we asked lol. The shrimp and crawfish were both a little overboiled which made it harder to eat. The shrimp aren't peeled FYI. My daughter really liked the andouille Po-Boy and our jambalaya cheese fries were good.

I really liked our server the taste of the food wasn't bad just gotta pull em a little faster from the Pot :) I'll  come back and maybe they had an off day in the kitchen so they definitely get another shot.

We went with friends and the Pho was awesome, the chicken wings were amazing !! 

Two of us got the chicken and waffles and while I've  had roscoes in LA and Gladys knights in Atlanta, I suppose I'm spoiled.. the chicken and waffles here were like Asian fusion that's the best I can describe it ..?! Not the worst but next time I think I'd get something else.

The wait staff was awesome and everyone there just seemed upbeat, I'll definitely be back ... especially because it's close to me in mid city.

Eating my way through Tucson, Cafe Passé was probably the most relaxing environment for food and a tea break. There's a humungous menu plastered behind the counter in the first room with some interesting selections of breakfast items and drinks. After the order, if you're not planning to stay long, they're a few bar stools in the front to sit down for a quick bite or head over to the other room where the community tables are for the folks who are planning to hang out and stay awhile. 

Fruit Toast- Granola, a mixture of berries and quark spread on toasted sourdough drizzled with honey. Beautifully presented but a bit overwhelmingly loaded with fruits; still good though. 
Breakfast Sandwich- Bacon, an egg, mixed springs, slice of tomato, avocado, inside a croissant and for some reason they drizzled honey all over this making it a very messy sandwich. Everything was really fresh but I would totally recommend them to maybe put the honey inside the sandwich. 
Chai Tea Latte- Creamy cup of spice and cinnamony perfection. 
Italian Soda- I like simple syrup so why not have it in my carbonated beverage.

Overall Service: Everyone was calm and cool, it made us feel all mellowed out too. Kind of like contact high from good vibes.

What was that? Two pound steak? I'm there. This outdoor-indoor-steak-bbq joint is a casual dinner only spot with a fire grill right outside. To the left from the entrance, there's a little stage for live music that takes place later in the evening. So come on down and enjoy a slab of meat on one of their outdoor picnic tables when the weather is nice out, like we did, because it's going to be a feast!

Two Pound "Cowboy Steak- Yeehaw! I was excited about how enormous this cut was. It was delicious and simply seasoned with salt and pepper but the only minor issue was it came out a bit too rare. We devoured it anyways! They served this with unlimited Texas toast and beans. 
Corn on a Cob- Slather the butter all over this bad boy and it's a sweet and salty combo with lots of crunch.
Berry Cobbler- After the meal we just had, this was the way to finish it. Fresh berries in this sweet syrupy filling with crisp toppings. Yum.

Overall Service: Superb. They were constantly working, clearing tables, filling up water, checking on customers and when it came to the check, it didn't take forever. A+ in my book.

Decided to write my first review on a soft tofu restaurant (typical Korean I am) because I go here about once a month and also because I am doing NOTHING at work today.

I think this place has the best soft tofu in the PA/NJ/NY area. I've had BCD and Seoul Garden in NY and So Gong Dong in Palisades Park, NJ. 

Like all soft tofu/Korean restaurants, you get side dishes (banchan) but the pickled dishes here are great. For $10, you get sides, rice in a stone pot, and soon doo boo (soft tofu) in a stone pot as well. 

I usually get the "More Spicy" when I go, and for some reason, this level is spicier when I go with fellow Asians than non-Asians (judging..maybe?). This just might be me, though. I really would get some level of spicyness because the non-spicy soup is just meh and looks too pale. 

The table bell to grab waiters are a plus, too.

Wish this place was in the city.

I'll say it: I prefer E Mei over Han Dynasty (no hate mail, please).

Han Dynasty has a cult following (which I understand), and I also think that place is very good. If Han Dynasty is the trendier, more "hip" place, E Mei is the more family-oriented, down-to-earth place.

To start, you get some roasted peanuts and pickled cabbage/cucumbers. This screams authenticity.

I like the Dan Dan Noodles here better: the peppercorns pack a better punch in less of a peanutty/viscous sauce. The Chongqing Spicy Chicken is crispy and tasty, the Double Cooked Pork is great, Cold Noodle with Spicy Sauce is refreshing, the whole Sea Bass in Hot Bean Paste is filling. I really haven't had anything bad here, and the portions are bigger than that of its rival.

They also have the usual American Chinese: General Tso's etc., but skip these and go for the more traditional Sichuan dishes. You won't be disappointed!

Anthony's is nothing less than amazing. 

Located in the nugget hotel on the lower level. Parking is free, and this is one of those places that is unexpectedly a place to try. 

The service is five stars plus, and every aspect of the experience will leave you surprised that such a awesome restaurant could be located in a less than acceptable hotel.  

This is the type of restaurant that you go for a dining experience, not an eating experience. Expect to be impressed with the wine and cocktail menu, the appetizers, and the main courses. Every aspect is an experience. The wait staff is ever present, and yet at the same time, you won't even know that they're there. 

The cheese charcuterie board, along with a lovely glass of wine, or a lemon drop, is a perfect way to start off your dining experience. 

You literally cannot go wrong with any of the menu choices. the seafood, the steaks, oh so delicious! There are a variety of sides to choose from, and the restaurant absolutely can meet the needs of even the most discerning pallets.  

Reservations are highly recommended, and dress should be comfortably classy. Don't be one of those people that shows up in ill fitting jeans a polo, and dirty tennis shoes.  Kick it up a notch, and enjoy the five star experience.

Rouses Market was an unexpected find.  

The French Quarter is filled with plenty of restaurants, stores, galleries, etc. To find an actual grocery store I thought it was going to make my day. Like many of the places in the quarter, they are small cramped tight spaces, and if you did not know any better you would feel like it was New York real estate.  

Everything seems to have a pretty high price tag on it for just basic necessities. Bottled water is easily $3.50 to $4.50 at some of the other local stores. Gum, candy, and those type of items seem to have higher price tags as well.

When we found the market, I was hoping to find a few great deals that would beat out some of the other prices that we found elsewhere. Their prices are just as high, and due to the cramped quarters, there's a limit on what they carry. I found that as I was perusing one of the aisles shopping, it also happened to be the same aisle to stand in line for the cashier.

This really seems to be more of a go to if you are looking for a variety of liquor, and basic refrigerated grocery items. Not a bad find, just not anything to go out of your way for.

It's was time to get the shenanigans started, and what better place to do that then Shenanigans?!? 

A quaint local neighborhood pub, that is located in a small unassuming strip mall.  You may pass it by, but don't.   

If you're looking for a fun place to hang with friends for reasonably priced drinks, or you're looking for the best fish n chips locally, this is a must try.  

I found this watering hole by sheer luck.  The customers are friendly, ( think Cheers) the staff is not only friendly, but welcoming.  Thank you Samantha :-) 

The food ... I've only had the fish n chips, but just yum! The portions are generous, and made from cod.  Mmmm, mmmm, more please.  The chips are either regular fries, wedges, or over the top onion rings.  I went for the wedges.  They were perfectly seasoned, and matched the fish perfectly.  The tarter sauce must be made in house.  It was so good, I requested more for my fries.  The side of coleslaw is tasty. It's not overly filled with Mayo, just light and fresh.  The fish... it was served super hot.  It was tasty, crispy, well seasoned, and more fish than breading. It was perfect.   

I'm excited to go back and try some of the other menu offerings.  I spied a Monte Cristo that is calling my name.  

Go get into Shenanigans!! What are you waiting for ?!?

I have one word... Aebleskivers. 

If you are looking for a quaint place to enjoy breakfast, French Toast is the place for you!

We dined at this great little gem a few times for breakfast, and enjoyed it so much. I love the fact that it is not indigenous or typical to the area, but rather a unique and interesting find. In many ways, it reminds me of West Coast yumminess. It absolutely is worth going for breakfast.

Diners Tip- use the Yelp app for call ahead seating. It's a smaller restaurant, and they get busy pretty early in the morning.  We lucked out, and we were seated fairly quickly each time.

Each meal always included Aebleskivers.  If you've not ever tried them, it is like heaven to your taste buds. They are danish pancake balls that are traditionally served as a dessert. Remember, life can be short eat dessert first!
You have your choice of fillings-lemon curd, warm chocolate etc. you can order them in threes, or fives etc.
I highly recommend the lemon curd. It is the perfect taste sensation. They are brought to the table warm, and should be enjoyed immediately. They are pretty much hollow on the inside which allows you to easily open them up and add whatever your choice of filling maybe. Once you fill them, bite into that yummy goodness, and your life will be completely changed. I love the fact that while they are slightly sweet, they are not overly sugary, and it is the perfect treat to have with a good cup of coffee.

I absolutely loved my toast with the smoke salmon. It was rather odd to have it with a scrambled egg on top which is their recommendation, but I will tell you, it works. The smoked salmon is not overly salty, is a fairly generous portion, and the combination of all the flavors together make for a perfect harmony.

The crêpe that we ordered that was filled with the banana and the Nutella, was definitely way too sweet for me, and I preferred the savoriness of my salmon toast.  

This definitely is the perfect place for breakfast when you are burnt out by the heaviness of the local fried treats, and you are looking for something completely unique and wonderful. I highly recommend the salmon on the toast! The entire menu sounds incredible, and I look forward to going back and trying other dishes. They do offer other dishes that are savory, in addition to some of the sweeter sounding counterparts. This is definitely a place worth checking out!! 

Don't forget the aebleskivers !!!

It's been said that pictures say a thousand words, but my pictures don't come close to doing the food at Willie Mae's justice. 

FOODIE ALERT!!!
If you are planning a trip to New Orleans, you've not been here before, or you've tried Willie Maes, and it's been a minute, this is a must try. 

This is where the most amazing fried chicken can be found. If you are on a diet, want to be on a diet, you really need to pretend that this is part of your daily diet food LOL

First off, they do not take reservations. They are open most days, but I would strongly encourage you to call the day before you plan on going there just to make sure that they plan on being open. The hours posted are not always accurate.

Go hungry. You will want all of the food. 

Second off, be prepared to stand in line to get inside. It's not uncommon for smaller groups that may even be behind you in line to be seated before you if you happen to be part of a larger party. Relax, you will get there too.  When you do, you'll be met with incredibly friendly and expedient service, a clean table, and eventually the most amazing fried chicken you may ever have.

The fried chicken plates come with two choices-you may either order dark meat, or white meat, but no combinations. Ever. The white meat plate is one chicken breast that is so huge, I'm wondering where they grow these chickens. The plate also includes two large chicken wings, and a choice of one of the sides. All plates include peas. When was the last time you saw peas served on anyone's plate?! I have to say the peas were downright delicious. The dark meat plate, is one extremely large chicken thigh, one chicken leg, and a wing. You also were given a choice of one of the sides as well.

We ordered one dark meat, and one white meat plate. We also added on two of their corn muffins, and an order of their butter beans. I know, most people are ready to enjoy the red beans and rice, but I'm here to tell you go for the butter beans. They were the best damn beans I've ever had! The corn muffins weren't bad but nothing special.

The chicken. Omg the chicken. It's perfectly seasoned, with the perfect crunch, that makes me finally understand the phrase "slap yo momma".  The meat is juicy, and has a nice kick to it. You won't be able to get enough.  The portions are huge! We both had ordered the Mac n Cheese as our " side", And it was pretty tasty and cheesy. Have I mentioned that the chicken was freakin delicious ?!? 

Butter beans, where have you been my entire life?!? The butter beans are served in a big open bowl, with a huge group of white rice in the middle of them. I wasn't a fan of the white rice, but those beans... OMG those beans. I love the fact that they are prepared vegetarian style.  They taste like heaven.  Seriously wear your stretchy clothes to dine here.  You'll thank me later.  

Admittedly, I lack the ability to be a part of the clean plate club, and the waitstaff was more than happy to box up my chicken, some of the beans that we had not finished, and my muffin. I had such high hopes of enjoying it later that night. I also had wanted to try one of their desserts.

I'm pretty sure that there isn't a restaurant in New Orleans that does not offer some type of bread pudding. Willie Mae's isn't the exception.  Our waiter strongly encouraged us to try their bread pudding, and I am so glad that we did. They make one of the best bread pudding's in all of New Orleans.  We only ordered one because we were so full and sharing is caring.

The bread pudding is served warmed, with a light sauce poured over it.  I could eat this for breakfast.  It's oh so good.  Don't make faces at the raisins. They add to the yumminess.  It's light, moist, and you'll want more.  

Diners tip- wear your stretchy pants, go hungry, be prepared to stand in line, and order all the food.

Fried chicken is life.

Grimaldi's was a discovery that I made years ago, and it's now our go-to when in Reno.  

This is what pizza is all about. The crust is a perfect combination of light and airy, with that nice crispy pieces and parts that make you want more.  The toppings are plentiful and super tasty.  

Diners tip: order The Don.  It has everything that you will want.  The sausage is seasoned, the pepperoni is crispy on the edges, and all the cheese... mmmm, mmmmm, more please !! 

Reservations are not necessary, but definitely recommended. Parking is free and plentiful.  

Grimaldi's is a great family restaurant, a great fun date night place, or a fun place to go grab a few slices and drinks with friends.  Prices are super reasonable especially for such a quality pie. If you haven't tried Grimaldi's yet, what are you waiting for?!

This is where New Orleans hides their best french fries! Seriously the best damn french fries I've had ever.

We happened into what we thought was going to be a traditional bistro, but turned out to be anything but.

This hole in the wall amazing place is located inside and at the rear of the 700 club bar.  Initially when I saw 700 club on the outside of the darkened building, it reminded me of the religious group that used to be on TV Sunday mornings when I was a kid. A channel quickly flipped by

This little hidden gem has three high top tables, a few chairs, and seriously the best fries that you will find anywhere in the French quarter. Grab a menu from the wall, and head over to the window to place your order. Once your order is placed and paid for they will give you her number and bring the food to your table.

We ordered a plain cheeseburger... Meat, cheese, and the barn. Let me just say for a very plain cheeseburger it was delicious! Have I mentioned how good those damn fries were?! Seriously, I even asked the kitchen what they put on them or how they make them. All I know is that I was told numerous spices, and that was about all they were going to share.  

We also ordered what was called a cheesy burger. The concept in theory sounded divine.  Big chunks of meat slathered in cheesy sauce, horseradish sauce, and topped with shoestring fried onions. Who would not want that goodness?!

The pictures say 1000 words, and yes, the sandwich was absolutely huge. Did I mention that the price points were pretty reasonable for local food? A couple of sandwiches and order of fries, and a drink for under $30. That's considered reasonable in the area.  The sandwich was almost impossible to eat because as you can see in the pictures the cheesy sauce was everywhere LOL unfortunately, the meat was heavily salted to the point that it was practically inedible. In a regular restaurant I would've sent the food back.  This whole in the wall is pretty much a make to order place, which is part of it's charm.  I was able to pick around it but it something that I definitely would not order again, and less I had assurances that the meat wasn't going to be overly salted

Music from the bar spills into the area and definitely warms the atmosphere.  Here is where good food and cool vibes come together. With the tunes blasting, and the people drinking, they are sure to be random dancing and fun to be had.

Great place for a quality burger, and if you are in the area and don't try the french fries, you seriously are missing out on good eats. The guy that was sitting behind us was there just for the fries.  I now know why!! Seriously, this is one of the best hidden gems in the quarter

Who thinks of going to Reno to buy chocolate?? Dorinda's is a must when in Reno. 

As Reno is called the biggest little city, Dorinda's is big flavor packaged in a pretty little store, that will keep your eyes and tummy searching for the next great piece of chocolate. 

The beautifully displayed truffles, pieces of chocolate, and please let me try one of everything. 

For those that know me, know that I would give up food for chocolate. Chocolate is its own food group, and Dorinda's makes sure that there is something for everyone. The offer chocolate nibs, that are pure, no sugar, and made this girl oh so happy. Especially since I have cut back on my sugar intake. This helps take the edge off that I need my chocolate feeling. I snuck a taste of the sample being offered of caramel and dark chocolate. HOLY COW... it was spectacular. The variety of individual chocolates are amazing! Coffee bean topped, caramel filled, fruit goodness, and just pure bites of yumminess. Pieces are sold individually, or buy as many as you'd like. They even offer a nut enrobed piece of chocolate that will make you never want commercial chocolate again. 

If you're vegan, this is a MUST stop as well. Im telling you, Dorinda's is such a special place. 

i cant wait to go back! I am still drooling over the caramel, chocolate, pretzel thingy that I would give up my strict no sugar, just to indulge.

Step away from all that is downtown, and venture to this lovely neighborhood, and to this special shop to enjoy all that is chocolate. Just promise to leave a few pieces for me.

Special thanks to Reno Elite Yelper Donna B. for sharing this amazing place!

Bonjour mon ami! 

Cafe Fleur De Lis is très magnifique!! 

This was a great little discovery while walking through the French Quarter. I had spotted someone walking by with a coffee cup with Fleur De Lis, and figured it was a local coffee place.  Nope. It's a great gem of a find. Add this to your list of breakfast places to try.  

The wait staff was welcoming and genuinely nice. We were greeted, seated, and made to feel at home.  

The menu has a nice variety, and doesn't take long to read through. 

We ordered the crab cake eggs Benedict.  The eggs were poached to perfection. The hollandaise sauce was light, and was a perfect amount for the eggs.  The crab cake itself was flavorful, and oh so good. They fell apart fairly easily, but that didn't stop us from enjoying each tasty morsel.  

The sandwich. It was better than the pictures.  Melted cheese that was grilled on, turkey bacon, egg, and yum! It was filling, delicious, and have I mentioned the grits?? It's true, almost everything comes with grits. Traditionally, southerners add cheese to their grits. This southern girl adds butter and brown sugar. Don't knock it, until you've tried it. The grits were made perfectly.  Worth every single calorie. By the way, food eaten down south doesn't contain calories.  

My mocha iced coffee was okayish. Not anything that I'd order again. The hot chocolate was really good, and the house made whipped cream was a perfect addition. 

This is a great place to start your morning !

I grew up going to steak houses that had linen covered tables, linen napkins, and wait staff that was dressed like restaurant staff. You know those white crisp jackets, towels over their arms...You knew the impending meal was going to be delicious!

Rapscallion was no exception. It was everything that I had experienced as a kid, and warmed my heart to be able to dine in a traditional restaurant. 

The bread basket was filled with warm bread, the butter was curled rolls, and the water glasses filled with ice cold water. 

Menu choices were plenty... from seafood, to filet mignon. There is truly something for everyone. 

The waiter was a total hoot. He had THE best sense of humor! He checked on the table with just enough frequency to keep us happy. 

One of us had the chicken Parm, which was a large chicken breast, lightly breaded, and covered with a light "gravy". Its the type of marinara that you want to dip bread in, and just enjoy. The spaghetti was basic, and the sauce from the parm was supposed to be enough to cover the pasta, but it wasn't. 

We also ordered the 6oz filet mignon. It was tender, tasty, and gone in 2.2 seconds. Oh so good. 
The veggies, were on the light side, as were the garlic mashed potatoes. There's a fine line between too much food being served, and not enough. There could have been more goodness on the plate. It was THAT good. 

The chicken Caesar salad which I enjoyed, was tasty romain lettuce, lightly covered in dressing, and topped with grilled chicken. Im not a fan of the chicken, but the salad was delicious and filling. The chicken would have been better if it was slightly warmed, and was fresh. It tasted like pre-fab chicken, which surprised me. 

The warmth of the wait staff, dining with good friends, the welcoming atmosphere, and the delicious food, makes this well established restaurant a go to.

All joking aside, I do not care what people say about chain restaurants, Brio in Cherry Hill is fantastic.  Before I even begin this review I am going b to go on record to say the people that work here make the experience 5 stars all the way.  
         Tomorrow is my mom's birthday, so I brought her here for brunch.  From the moment we walked in, we were treated like rock stars.  I wish I knew the bartenders name because he is amazing and made our experience such a treat.  I went to the loo, while I was gone, he went over the wine list with my mom & suggested a wine we might like.  He was on point & there is nothing better than returning to your seat & having a drink waiting for you.  Did I like the wine he recommended?  I had three glasses - you tell me!
          We had the roasted red pepper bruschetta, my favorite, as an appetizer.    I had an all vegetable omlette & my mom had the salmon salad.  Delicious. The bartender was so busy, but he still found time to chit chat with us & I found out he is a fellow kickboxer - bonus!  The food was delicious, the wine was delicious & at the end of the meal our mixologist friend created a delicious white chocolate martini that I could have had 10 of.  At this point in time, chain or not, the food, drinks & service were flawless.  The cherry on the sundae was the candle on my mom's dessert.  I did not mention it to anyone nor did I ask for them to do it, we were overheard & I have to say hats off to our bartender for his attention to detail.  My mom was touched and that made my day.  Go ahead, knock chains all you want - people make an experience.  This Brio in Cherry Hill is exceptional.  I am the duchess & I am damn proud of that.  To all of the people who work there, you are a class act, thank you & cheers!

When I sat down to write this review, I looked at my overall YELP musings and realized I have 99 five star reviews.  The big tipping point for me is always the people that work in the establishment I am visiting.  People will make or break any business regardless of what it is.  
     So as I sit here wondering how to begin this review, I honestly wish that there was a way to give less than one star to this establishment.  The food here was delicious, but the people broke this location to the point where there is no coming back.  I have never, in the whole of my life experienced such a thing and I doubt I ever will.
     Saturday night, a friend and I went to the Blue Monkey Tavern for some late night snacks and a few beers before heading off to our next location.  We were here once before and noticed that everything coming out of the kitchen looked pretty good, however, at the time we were only having a few drinks and planned on returning to eat at a later date.
      When we walked in, there was a fair amount of people at the bar, we found two stools and sat down.  The bartender came over and put a beer menu in front of us - no smile, no greeting, no salutation, interaction of any kind.  Just plopped a menu down and stood there like a lump.  Half of the items on the menu were crossed off (as mentioned by some other yelper) and the remaining items were not things either of us were familiar with.  So my friend said hi and our bartender replied with the most strained effort, I think she died a little inside by saying hello to us.  My friend asked her what was good on the list, she said she didn't know what we like so she can't answer that question.  Ok, abrasive.   My friend said we are open to all sorts of beers and asked her what she recommended, what does she like that is off the menu.  We ask our servers that all of the time, that question is not so unusual to warrant a person walking away which is exactly what she did after saying everything on the menu is good.  She literally turned and left.  At this point, we should have left.  I think we were both stunned that she was so rude we thought maybe it was some sort of bad joke.
      Bartender number two came over, clearly the first girl with the pink hair was so appalled by us and our simple beer questions she couldn't stand to be on our vicinity a second longer.  Bartender number two took our order, though she had no idea where any of the beers were from and she had no interest in any other small talk.  We placed an order for food since that was the main reason we were there and honestly we really should have left at this point.  So as we are waiting for our food and drinking some random craft beer that no one knows anything about, we see a man who was most likely the manager or something.  He is pouring what looked like beer into a large container and I made a comment to my friend saying something like I wonder if they are going to cook with that.  Lots of places cook with beer - beer battered onion rings, etc.  And as I said that, the guy dumped it down the drain.  So my friend asked him why he was dumping all that beer.  The guy said, "Do I come to your job and ask you what you do?"  WoW!  Just wow.  
       The staff here on Saturday 10.27 was miserable!  All of them, I can almost get over one person having a bad day and will typically say nothing and just not return, but holy smokes I can't get over this collection of unhappy, sullen, miserable people in one place.  My friend asked bartender #2 why they don't serve Eclipse beer as it is across the street.  She said, "why would we, if you want to drink Eclipse, go there."
I will never be back here.  My group of nine goes out several times per week.  We spend a lot of money as there is a large number of us and there is nothing that would ever make me go back here.  I have never had worse service and I doubt I ever will, this was bad on a whole new level.  IF i could give them a zero I would.

Delicious!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

We came here Christmas day and we're so pleasantly surprised.  The place is cute, clean & spacious.  The service was fast & friendly, being Christmas day - the place filled up very quickly - yet the wait staff didn't miss a beat.  The appetizers were delicious, I had the scallion pancake - best scallion pancake I ever had - ever!  The main dishes arrived & they were HUGE - seriously, come hungry.  I have read some of the other reviews here & people claim the food isn't spicy enough.  Mine made me sweat, cough & my nose run - it was spicy & delicious.  The food was really great, everyone loved what they ordered and there were no left overs to take home.  Great place, will defiantly be back.

OH MY GOD the GUACAMOLE!!!!!!!!!  The guacamole at this place blew my mind!  NO, you don't understand how good it was.  There are no pictures because we ordered take out from here and when I opened the container there wasn't enough time to get the phone out.  Authentic doesn't even begin to describe it - it was so damn good.  
      I have only one complaint and that is that Restaurante Colosio is not in Marlton or Cherry Hill.  I wish they were I would probably be 400 pounds if they opened up near me.  As a vegan, I always ask how the beans/rice/vegetables are prepared.  They told me they only use 100% vegetable oil and so I got the veg & bean burrito as my meal.  It was big!  And yes I at the whole thing because I'm fat and greedy.
     If you are reading this - please believe me I am not exaggerating.   I have had guacamole in some of the highest end restaurants in NJ, Philly, New York and Washington - they can't touch the guac served here.  Everyone makes theirs differently, Colosio's makes theirs without the tomatoes.  It does however have extra cilantro and it has a nice spicy kick to it from the jalapeños - I love that.  The burrito was delicious - not soggy like some take out can be.  It was big and two people (or just me) could split one.  
    I wish I could give them more than five stars.  Someone was complaining that the price on the guacamole went up.  All I can say is I'm not mad at them!!!  You go ahead and you raise that price, I got cash, credit, debit - whatever you need!!!  You just keep that guacamole delicious.

My wife and I booked a reservation for The Catbird Seat for our anniversary.  We were incredibly excited to give it a try!

We booked a 9:00 dinner.  I did not know until we arrived that it would last for about 3 hours.  It was a Saturday night--no big deal.  Of course, we walked into the Patterson House next door not knowing which building was which.  This is actually a nice stop if you get there early to grab a drink.

When you arrive, you immediately go into a "holding cell."  You're in the right place if you walk into a tiny room with an elevator on the side.  You'll hang out there with a host until it is time to be seated.

The restaurant is fairly small.  I doubt that you could fit more than 20 people in it.  They have a horseshoe-shaped bar with seating around the edges.  All of the cooking and general prep work takes place inside of the bar.  It's a great way to talk to each cook to find out what they are making and how they are preparing each course.

The menu is constantly changing and so I won't list everything that we tried.  However, I do want to go through a couple of courses to give an idea of the uniqueness of this restaurant.  

One course was an heirloom tomato with "very old" ham.  The ham was cured on the roof of the building.  It had a distinct taste and was excellent with acidity of the tomato.  I also had beef tartare for the first time.  I've always been hesitant to try it, but it was excellent and the beef is not an overwhelming portion of the dish.  It's more of an accent.

There were a couple of beer-based dishes.  They made a beer cheese that was served in a cone (like a small ice cream cone).  It was incredible.  I also enjoyed a bread that was made using yeast from the local Yazoo brewery.  They seemed to use local ingredients as much as possible in their cooking.

The most exciting courses came with an alcohol pairing.  A potato soup was paired with a Brooklyn Brewery craft beer.  There were several wine pairings as well as a bourbon-based dessert cocktail.  They were all excellent and I felt comfortable driving home afterward (remember that you are there for 3 hours).  CBS also offers a premier alcohol pairing for $70 per person.  The one I had was $40.

The meal was wrapped by a couple of wonderful desserts.  One was blueberry based and the other was an ice cream salad.  Both were refreshing and light.

If you are a foodie, then the Catbird Seat is a must.  After you make awkward chit-chat with other patrons in a tiny closet and ride up the elevator with a super-creepy painting (of what a "CatBird" might look like), you'll have such a great time.  The chefs are amazing and incredibly engaging.  They love to talk food and preparation, but will leave you alone if you are just interested in eating.  I think we used our allotment of questions, but they were wonderful hosts and never seemed to busy to indulge us. 

The meal is filling, but not overwhelming.  It is pricey, but worth it.  I would do it again one day, but you do need to prepare for a $450+ price tag for two.  Still, eating at the Catbird Seat is a wonderful experience and the best way in Nashville to celebrate your major life events.

SkyGarten is a very interesting place right now. The hype for it has been ridiculous, and despite its publicity and all, unfortunately I didn't fall in love with it. I just think that the attention of SkyGarten is coming on a little too strong, so let's figure things out together.

Good: 
You'll take in one of the best and FREE views of Philadelphia. A top-down look ( with two spacious balconies) from the 51st floor, without an admission fee.

Eh:
As much as it pains me to mention it, I think there's nothing special about SkyGarten drinks wise. 

Random thoughts:
- Hours: Wednesday- Saturday, including CCD Sips.
- Entrance: Through the plaza "fountain" side.
- Parking: Available in the same building. $10.00 weekdays and closed on Saturdays.
- I was there on the Fourth of July to celebrate the Spirit of '76 ( 2 hour buffet), and to watch the fireworks from high above the city. However, Mother Nature had different plan for us. It was a stormy, wet night. Sigh! 
-Honestly, the event was so crowded and the food was mediocre. 

Philadelphia, may you please, and for God's sake, take it down a notch.
SkyGarten, I'm sorry but I can't give you more than Three and Half Yelps.

Pizza is boring, right? Not so fast. Try the Lobster Pizza originated here at Rittenhouse. 
Lobster pizza? Say Whaaaaaaat? 

At first, I ordered Pizza al taglio, the plum & honey one ( $6). I made the wrong decision by ordering it. I'm not a big fan of square thick pizza. So I took a second and closer look at the menu, that when I saw Rittenhouse. I knew I had to order it, and I wasn't sure what to expect. Rittenhouse is a 12-inch thin crust, crisp gourmet pizza, topped with absolutely tender lobster, delicious and tangy san marzano tomato sauce, garlic, and melted cubes of bufala mozzarella cheese, and red pepper flakes. It was delightful and SO.DANG.GOOD! 

Even though I just ate the whole pizza- all by myself! I still managed to leave a tiny space for dessert. Never underestimate the power of dessert.I got a cup of Affogato, a match made in heaven. A cup of Fior di Latte and Espresso. A cup that did the trick for me! Satisfied my sweet tooth with a kick of caffeine. An amazing WOW.

I have never been to the Spring Garden sister restaurant, so I can't compare, but I was impressed with the service. Suzana, one of the managers I think, took the pizza al taglio off my check, without me asking for it. Also, Rebecca, my waitress, was very attentive friendly, and patient. Talk about great customer service with a smile. 

Pizzeria Vetri prices tend to be on the pricer side, compared to other pizzerias( close enough to Nomad.) Their prices ranges start at $12 for Marinara Pizza up to $26 for the Rittenhouse Pizza. However, you can get pizza by the slice ( al taglio) for $6-8. I think you'd be better off if you get the 12-inch and instead of the al taglio, and pay a little bit more. The 12- inch is round not square, bigger, and way tastier!!!

This location is the birth place of the Lobster Pizza, hence the name Rittenhouse. I bet you Ritthenhouse peeps. This will be a hit! 

Vetri, I will be a regular! 
Four Yelps!

What? 
What does one do if one finds him/herself in the city of brotherly love, smacked in the middle of the Fairmount, Reading Railroad tracks? 

Where? 
Head to the down-and-dirty, the rusty J&J Trestle Inn. Believe me it's not exactly your quintessential entertainment venue. 
- Upscale retro & energetic atmosphere. 
- Classic cocktails. 
- French pop, soul, funk and disco music. 

Who? 
Go-go dancers, not only they can hold a beat, but they'll impress you with some perfect choreography. They'll dance for hours and hours straight, non-stop(Seriously!)

When? 
Back to '60s & '70s vibes. 
Hours: Wed-Sat: 5PM-2AM, HH: 5PM-7PM, Late Night HH:10PM-12AM (Wed-Thur)
Moonlight HH: 10PM-11PM (Fri-Sat)
*** Trestle Specials Mod Go-go dancers: Wed-Sat.***

Why? 
Because one of two things is true if you're still reading this review: 
1) You're really curious about what Trestle Inn have to offer. 
2) You just need something to take the edge off and have fun.

P.S: Don't forget to wear your dancing shoes.

Four Yelps.

Unlike so many adventurous eaters who seek elk or bison burger, deciding what to get at Bareburger was exponentially difficult. I was overwhelmed- so many burger options to choose from. The "Be My Burger" option was there to make my life easier by customizing my burger the way I want. 
My first was a grilled chicken in a collard green wrap, I never had collard wraps before. On my second visit, I got a medium well beef burger, also in collard green wrap. It was organic and all-natural. Yes it was healthy, but t's not my idea of deliciousness.

Three Yelps.

Don't let the name fool you. This is not your typical neighborhood tavern, it can be best described as modern, comfy place with a touch of upscale and refined American classic menu. Unlike its sister restaurant "Brauhaus Schmitz" that is more beer-orianted, Whetstone Tavern focus more on wine and few hand-crafted cocktails.

The classy bar, lime green walls, modern lighting and the alluring atmosphere won't exactly scream that are in a tavern. It is causal enough for drinks in a relaxed atmosphere, yet an upscale dining experience for the foodies out there!

As the soothing décor and the friendly service was wonderful, the food was delicious too. I had the Crab Cake sandwich. A very flakey and tender crab cake between martin's potato roll halves and topped with heirloom tomato, iceberg lettuce slaw and homemade pickled vegetable remoulade sauce, served with french fries. As a huge lover of Reese's peanut butter cup, I got the Chocolate-Peanut Butter Cake. It was the star of the show. 

I can't wait until I go back, and see what the brunch menu will look like, it will be served seven days a week. I'm so excited. 

Four and half Yelps.

It's cold outside!!! So we decided to try some Southern-inspired food at Headhouse square.  And as soon as we entered this casual and warm restaurant, a welcoming host walked us to our table and Ciro-our server greet us, told us about the specials and kept our glass full the entire night after he took our order. 

We started off with the charcoal grilled shrimp with creamy Avocado, and pink grapefruit appetizer which was ok. We continued with a mouthwatering yellow tail Ceviche and a" bland "wagyu beef tartare and not as sophisticated as I expected. For our main entrees we got the grilled flatiron steak, It wasn't the best I've ever had. Dry, flavorless and extremely salty!

Now being a huge fan of beignets I had to get them for desserts. A set of three Ricotta Beignets with bourbon caramel sauce came greasy and not that crispy, too dense to be enjoyable. However, my friend got a tart with coconut ice cream, and that was to die for, like a party in my mouth.

Friendly staff, great service, pleasant atmosphere, and over price for the portion they serve. Meh!!! I'm not wild about the place!
Four Yelps!

You go to Lo Spiedo. You go to Lo Spiedo at least once! 
Isn't It one of the most outstanding restaurants in America, at least according to GQ Magazine (2015). Boy, oh boy! I've been wanting to go to Lo Spiedo since then, but I couldn't drag myself to go away from center city Philadelphia soon enough. 
Recently, I spent my birthday here, with my favorite person, and I couldn't ask for a better way to celebrate. 

So, here's few reasons to drive 15 minutes away from center city Philadelphia, without raising an eyebrow, and not just to catch a game in South Philly Sports Complex.
- Fact: Marc Vetri's seventh restaurant and casual eatery, inside the Navy Yard gates. My partner and I took a Lyft back and forth( ~$30,) but there is plenty of parking.

- I got the Beef Brisket, and it was perfectly cooked on the spit, I think, hence the restaurant name. Lo Spiedo! 
My partner loved his Spit-Roasted Pork Shoulder, he said it was his absolute favorite. However, my favorite dish of the night was the Cast Iron Skillet Mac and Cheese. It is a must. Yelpers, Take my word for it. 
Convenient second fact: "Low Spee-A-doe" means the spit, as in rotisserie and grilled meats. 

- I have to say that I wasn't quite impressed by our desserts. I got the Milk Chocolate Sundae, and Tom got the Boston Cream Zuccotto. Both were ok.ish. 

- Yes it is one of the best restaurants in Philly, but frankly, I don't see it as one of the best restaurants in America. It is a bit over hyped. 
Well, whether, it is the best in American or the best in Philly, personally it doesn't. Lo Spiedo will always have special place in my heart. 

Three and Half Yelps.

I'm not Irish, but who won't like to be super-festive on St. Patrick's Day!
I started my day with a very green (and of-course, nutritious) salad, from sweetgreen, which did the trick just right. 

Feeling lucky?
Something calorie-savvy and exciting? 
Since I get to eat anyway, why not get in a celebratory mood and go all green? With a custom-mixed salad, I may just found the pot of gold after all.

As a first timer, I opted to custom a premium, Mediterranean salad (390 Calories.) It was very festive and nutritious (sourced locally,) with the perfect combination of healthy, vegan-friendly protein, and pleasant dressing.

My salad had a base of chopped romaine lettuce and basil, with fresh grape tomatoes, crunchy cucumber, shaved organic carrots, and healthy twist of baked falafel (vegan) and organic chickpeas. I paired it nicely with a gluten-free, cucumber tahini yogurt dressing (came on the side.) Now, who said dressings can't be truly healthy and insanely tasty? This made in-house, smooth, and light green dressing delivered an extra healthy nutrients from the yogurt, when drizzled lightly over the top of the salad, and I dug in. Yay!

The creative salad was so fresh and colorful. It was SO damn good ( and so expensive:$9.35.) My constant dilemma is should I be Barbie and broke, or fat and rich? And the million-dollar question is why junk food is so cheap and healthy food is so expensive? $1.29 Hamburger. McDonald's, anyone? Put your hands down, Yelpers. Thank you! 

Sweetgreen easily became my new favorite to-go spot, and it may be yours too if you give a try. Of course, only if you want to keep up with the body image the Kardashian/Jenner girls are promoting.

- Tip: Ordering can't get any easier. Place order, pay online and when it's ready pick it up in store. Or just order in-store. It is all about simplicity. 
- Bonus tip: Card-only, quick- service store. Expect to only use a debit/credit card to pay for your meal. No cash accepted. 

Sweetgreen, this was my first visit, and certainly WON'T be my last.
Four and half Salad Yelps.

It was like love at first sight. Then I took a second look, and still the love is there. R2L by far my favorite place in Center City. I think it is one of Philly's hot sophisticated spots. 

Everyone is smiling, very friendly and eager to please- always. Last week, we went for Restaurant Week (August 2015) and I had another flawless experience, thanks to our waitress, Alyssa, who was more than amazing. I started with the hot and juicy roasted shrimps, followed by flavorful, and tender beef short rib & butcher's filet due over a bed of steuben bean chili & basil purée. Delicious milk chocolate hazelnut pudding ended off the extraordinary dinner. R2L never fail to impress me. 
A side not to be missed, is the fabulous panoramic view. 

Note: This is " THE" perfect date spot, that will keep a the ideal balance between spaciousness and intimacy. 


Because everyone deserve to be pampered,
Five Yelps.

On any given Sunday, I don't even "think" of lifting a finger. Instead, I try to dig into a perfectly prepped meal. I'm also a firm believer that every (probably- most) spots deserves a proper tasting. 
One Sunday, I dined at Frankie's, and I had the classic combo Chicken & Waffles served with over hard eggs. I was satisfied with my sweet Belgian waffle and my savory golden fried chicken. I mean, they call it "brunch" because I'm supposed to eat two meals' worth of food, right?
Frankie's is a casual spot and it can get crowded, but the wait is worth it, so be patient.
Four Yelps

Some people need a plan to dine out, others may even need a flowchart. I, on the other hand, play it by ear most of the time.

I was going to show on a late Monday night at Play and Players theater, and I wanted to grab something to eat around that area. I didn't realize, most restaurants don't open on Mondays. 
So, I consulted my best dinning friend " Yelp!" La Fourno, was about a block away from the theater, and they were nice enough to serve me, even though It was very close to closing time.  
I only had the Gnocchi Al Gorgonzola, and it was creamy, but tasted fairly bland. It needed some kind of spices or something. The service was friendly and it had the setting for nice dates. 
If I was in the area again, I may give it a second chance.

Three Yelps

Yesterday, the temperature hovered just above zero, and the snow was accumulating up to 3 inches, I bravely decided to take a walk, fight the nasty storm  and avoid the fear of falling! Now I'm freezing cold and starving, and it hit me, nothing would be better than a comforting bowl of hot noodles in a frigid, wintry day like this. A light bulb moment. Cheu Noodle Bar!

Luckily I live less than two blocks away from Cheu, I got there covered in snow and I saw no single empty seat!!! OMG. All of those people- just like me- decided to take walks to Cheu instead of curling up and Netflixing!! The sweet and friendly hostess said the wait would be up to 30 minutes, so I opt for take out. I was on-call and I didn't have the luxury of wasting time waiting and dining in, in addition, sitting on my lovely couch, eating my hot noodles while binge-watching suddenly appeared to be a brilliant idea! At this point, I'm not even sure why I'm out! Yeah I needed something delicious and warm lunch, because nutrition and stuff.

I ordered the brisket noodles, dumplings in chili oil and a fresh juice.

Noodles: brisket - matzo ball, kimchi, sesame chili broth.
Tender beef brisket,firm and elastic noodles.
Not being Jewish, I never even heard of matzo ball before, but it is totally delicious!

Dumplings: Ginger Beef Dumplings.
All I can say is hands down to the best dumplings i've ever had.

Fresh Juice: Apple and Ginger Fresh Juice
Actually i didnt had the juice, they forget to add it in my take-out bag. It happens!
So I called them, and as I expected they were really nice and offered a refund to my card. 

I cant wait for this frigid winter to end, I may just hibernate until the sun shines again. Oh Noooo, Cheu doesn't offer delivery yet. 
So I'll have to suck it up this few cold weeks- thanks Groundhog- and just go back and try another intriguing dish, you know that noodles aren't the ONLY reason to go to Cheu!

Four and half Yelps!

This is where you'll go when feel fed up with the non-ending long lines at Chipotle! 
- Slightly pricer than Chipotle.
- The same simple menu: burritos, burrito bowls, tacos and quesadillas. 
- Quick service. 
Still, I think Chipotle is way tastier, and I wouldn't trade it for the world.

Three Yelps

If you still have doubts, that Cafe La Maude is one of the best places for brunches in Philadelphia, just take a peek at its badass menu. From rocking Green Shakshuka to the best Mediterranean platter I've ever tasted in Philly, you'll find something up your alley--or better yet, if I dare you to try out something new! Something like Saumon Fumé a cheval or Berrylicious Pain Perdu. 

Last week I ordered the Mediterranean platter. It was simple, colorful and very delicious, I was satisfied without being too full. I'm planning to go back soon and try the N-Liberties and Gypsy Eggs.

Five Yelps.

Nando decided that we should go on a journey to the land of Greek Gods, and superfood (well, not literally!) After all, we're in Philly, where we can find & eat anything we want. So, here's my big fat Greek dinning guide at Opa, beyond baklava.

Our journey began with fava hummus spread and fresh pita bread...And then it was a feast; plate after plate just kept coming. Some of the standouts were char-grilled Octopus, pleasantly chewy and tasty off the grill. Lamb gyro with tzatziki (of course!) Pastitsio, a lovely Greek lasagna. An impressive Shrimp & Lobster toast. And a Cinnamon Spice Cake, an indulgent dessert with a hint of spice. I highly recommend going with the Chef's 4 Course Pikilia, blindly. It's sort of astonishing that four simple courses--can reflect the Greek extreme generous hospitality heritage, from the sophisticated meal to the great service( thank you, Shannon.)

Everything you need to know about Opa ( almost everything, you know per to "Gus Portokalos!")
Opa, Opa, Opa. Ha! Of course! Opa is come from the Greek word Opa, is mean just drop everything and have fun. So, what do you use to have a good time? The Opa way. You see: Opa, Opa. There you go!"

Phenomenal. I'll just drop the mic here.
Four and half Yelps.

Simply, South is too good to keep to myself. Most people go to the South to listen to live Jazz music and indulge in scrumptious Southern Fare ( and the creep factor of course). But what if you could hit the jackpot without even stepping on a plane? Just Go to SOUTH.

- Jazz venue? Check. Jazz at South is where strangers -- rather than friends -- gather.
- Southern cuisine? Check. Carolina Shrimp and Grits, and Hush Puppies were so good. Everyone loves a delicious gumbo soup.
- Romantic ambiance? Check. Undoubtedly very laid-back and relaxed. Just book a table!

Four Yelps.

I'm not a big fan of cupcakes, so naturally, I opt for the pudding over a cupcake!
Light, fluffy, yet smooth and slightly sweet pudding-oh boy!

Homemade creamy pudding? Check. 
Sliced fresh bananas? Check. 
Enough happy scoop of whipped cream for an instant mood changer? Check.

Sensational bananas pudding, so fresh, like a morning on the beach. Enough said!

Four Yelps!

I totally enjoy dim sum.
By now, I'm sure those who read my reviews, know that typically my coworkers and I dine in a dim sum parlor about  3-4 times a year. Usually we go to Joy Tsin Lau, but due to their food-safety problem, we had to explore other options in Philly.  
I gotta say, Ocean City Restaurant does dim sum right. Once you see these dim sum carts wheel by your table, you'll want to eat some of this Shrimp Balls, and some of these Fried Crispy Squid, and one of those Egg Tarts, and probably you will end it with a Sesame Ball, if you still have extra room.

What I liked:
- Authentic dim sum experience.
- Adventuresome (Sauteed Frog, anyone?) No, thank you. I'll pass.
-  Attentive staff.
- Spacious and clean.
- Reasonably priced. 

What I didn't liked:
- Not well known, but worth a visit.

Three and Half Yelps.

Hey, it's OK if you have yet to figure out if you are in the mood for American breakfast, or smoked chicken hash. You know, everything at Franky Bradley's is tasty... and leave some room for some lemon ricotta pancakes. It's nearly impossible to choose. However, you can always start with a boozy bloody, and from there you can choose.

And if thats your style, can I suggest the Beez In The Trap, a Bulleit delight ?


I've been many times, never made to dinner yet. Soon Franky Bradley's. Soon.
Four and Half Yelps.

We wanted a low key Birthday evening and Ceviche, and I wasn't very excited -from past experiences. Little did you know, my friend said. 

I booked a table at the chic and sleek downstairs lounge, I didn't get my little black dress on,  this time- low key remember?I got there on time, and Liz, the extremely friendly waitress, became my best friend for the next fifteen minutes that I was waiting for my friend to show up. Now, should I order my dessert first? A thousand times YES! I don't feel guilty, and I deserve it, I'm the one who is waiting, right?

I couldn't resist ordering the Chocolate Peanut Butter Bombe. This irresistible creation of chocolate shortbread, with luxurious and rich vanilla and chocolate mousse filling, then coated with perfect sphere of smooth chocolate shell, with marshmallow ice cream goodness and crunchy caramelized bananas. I apologize for your drooling. Chocolate was delicious. Peanut butter was delicious. Ice cream was delicious. you are welcome. 

Finally, my friend showed up, in scrubs- a reminder: low key dinner. We ordered the ceviche tasting: a sampling of five ( Thai Young Coconut Mixto ,Agua Chile Sea Scallop, Rainbow, Ecuadorian Shrimp, and Lenguado 'Al Fuego'). Each one had a very fresh and unique tasting. Very lovely combination of colors, flavors and textures. I enjoyed this ceviche so much that I was dehydrated the next day.  For the main meal, I ordered the chicken Imperial. Very very good. 

You know the common phrase: stellar service can take your meal from delicious to divine, it's totally true, the service was outstanding. To end this spectacular birthday dinner, Liz our waitress, brought out a surprise. White chocolate chili ice cream- on the house! How sweet is that? No its not, was like fire in my mouth. Spicy and cold Surprise.
I've got to say, it was a very pleasant birthday evening. Incredible, everything!

Five Yelps!

I've been eating here for years, and by far this is the BEST Middle Eastern restaurant I've ever come across in philadelphia! 

Why? For this reasons:
1/ Yummy food that actually remind one of home.
2/ Lovely Arabic songs playing in the background.
3/ Chill atmosphere.
4/ BEST Shawarma in Philadelphia!!

I've tried almost everything on the menu and it's all tasty. The Kibbeh, Grape Leaves, Falafel, Mixed Grilled Sandwich, Shawarma,  you name it, I'm quite pleased with whatever I order. All Lebanese Style! 

I've got to say the interior is a bit dated, the deliciousness of food though makes up for it! Highly recommended for a taste of the Middle East.

I had an idea, to get together over some spicy delights. Last Friday's plan, was to make some of us Yelpers- me included, appreciate Indian cuisine. 10 adventurous foodies gathered to sample some spicy food, with an Indian cuisine Virgin... Nando!

We got there few minutes before our reservation, and the hostess,Danielle, smiled and welcomed us warmly. First thing I notice, was the lack of the typical Elephant paintings, or the Taj Mahal pictures on the wall. Yet, I could feel the Indian vibe. 

We were told that the dinner special was one glass of house wine, one appetizer, and one entrée from the menu. Our choices had to be either chicken or vegetable. Still it was a lot of choices. Danielle told us they don't serve pork or beef. I believe most authentic Indian restaurants don't serve beef, because cow is sacred in Indian. Karma is %100 Halal, that's why they don't serve pork. 

Right after we put in our dinner orders, two baskets of poppadum came to our table, with some chutney. I liked the herbal green one (made of mint.)  I didn't try the red spicy one, but I could tell that everyone enjoyed it. 

While we were munching on the poppadum, our appetizers came out. I ordered the vegetable samosa, they were crispy stuffed triangle flour turnover, stuffed with potatoes and peas. However, I was a little bit disappointed, the samosa lacked some kind of spices, they certainly tasted bland and dry. I'm not a stranger to Indian cuisine, and I'm used to super spicy samosa. This one had no taste, even with the mint chutney that I asked for. Vince S. ordered the Chicken 65, he love it, I tried it and I didn't think it was spicy. Nando F. enjoyed his Aloo Samosa Chaat, and I thought it was really good, the yogurt added some taste to the samosa! 

My Chicken Biryani was pretty spot on!!! It was served hot, both temperature 
and spice wise. The rice was cooked perfectly, the chicken was tender, and the mild yogurt dip (rita) was a nice contrast as usual. I had a bite of the Butter Chicken and Chicken Xacuti, I'm afraid that I didn't care much for either. 

Few more pieces of info:
- We all had slightly different tastes for the spice level we chose. Some of us were unsatisfied of what we received. So, be aware when you order you spices!
- The service was great and everyone tend to be friendly. I didn't see any empty water glasses. 
- The on-the-house treat ( Gulab Jamun ) was highly appreciated. Thank you, Rony!
- Easy-to-order, set menu ,and nice lunch buffet - for those who like buffets!
- Karma was very clean and simple restaurant, despite the slightly dim lighting and the tight seating.
- I was torn between three and four stars here and I am taking the fourth away - for now- because the hit or miss flavors.


From now on, Karma  will satisfy Biryani my craving!

"I saw that"
That's what karma said
Three and half Yelps- for now

I owe this place a long over due review, I'm really not sure how I haven't reviewed this place, yet!
Every time I go to the Reading Terminal Market, I keep browsing, and most of the time, I end up getting something from Beck's Cajun Cafe. It has to be my absolute favorite.

I believe I have tried just about every delicious item on their menu, except the Train Wreck and the Gator. Two legit reasons : The Train Wreck has pork and I don't eat it, and and about that Gator...I can't eat something that could have eaten me in different circumstances!!!  Otherwise, I was happy with every item I have had, and usually a nap would be needed.  

- Heavenly beignets, served four days a week, made to order. Oh boy! 
- Rich and creamy Blackened Chicken Alfredo, with a spicy kick.
- Fancy some Shrimp and Chicken Gumbo? Mind-blewing! 
- Pepper, eggs with provolone breakfast wrap. Its good.
- Blackened Chicken Po' Boy. Not my fav.
- Don't miss the Fried shrimps.  Uh, yeah.
- Fried mac n' cheese balls, they were a little bland and not as good as they sound. 
- Craving king cake, Beck's serves it during Mardi Gras season. I had it for my birthday! Oh, so good...
- Golden Sweet Cornbread. I usually don't like cornbread, but this one is so sweet and moist. 
- Bread Pudding. Okish!

Beck's Cajun Cafe staff is extremely friendly. They always greet everyone with a huge smile, and offer samples of their food. 

Want to try some of spice blends from Beck's pantry? Take some home, they have several: Devil Dust, Angel's Kiss, Rub-a-Dub, Creole Mayo, BBQ Onion Relish and 3 Devils Hot Sauce. 

Four solid Yelps.

At Cheesecake Factory...

And I keep asking myself, why I'm here? and why anyone would want to come here. 

If you are planning on going, I've got you covered:
- Grumpy, unsmiling staff, including the host!
- inattentive , slow, and totally uninformed waitress. P.s: she was friendly thou.
- No prices on cocktail menu. 
- Dirty silverware!!!
- Mediocre mango key lime cheesecake.
- I don't understand why it was so difficult to split the check. 

One and half Yelps is two generous!

I knew I was going out for Valentine's Day to a "surprise" restaurant, and I was excited. I didn't know that I fancy feeling like I was in a movie.

We pulled up outside Victor Cafe, and I didn't recognize it. We got inside the restaurant, and I still had no clue. It took me a full minute to realize this was the spot where one of my favorite movies, and few of its most famous scenes were set. After all those years of not knowing that "Adrian's" restaurant was/is real, I, innocently, discovered it's not a fictional one.

Seriously, I was so thrilled to find out that Victor Cafe is actually "Adrian's" restaurant featured in Rocky Balboa (2006,) and Creed (2015.) Oh my! I wasn't just having an amazing experience, in fact, I was creating a special memory, with a special person, in a special spot.

Now, let's cut to the chase, shall we?
If you love traditional Italian cuisine ( and who doesn't ?) you're going to flip over the simple, yet classic menu. Pleasant food, live classical opera, and intimate date restaurant? Oh yes!
We ordered Ravioli, and Tortellini and both pastas were presented nicely, with a well-balanced sauce, or gravy, whatever you want to call it. If you haven't had the traditional Ravioli lately, their version with the toasted walnuts will satisfy your taste buds, and maybe you'll come back for more.
Don't forget to leave room for dessert. Ooh you may have some of the scrumptious Crème Brûlée and maybe one of the delicious Cannoli.

It's needless to mention, that Victor Cafe is super classy, low-key and romantic date spot. What can be better than being wooed by operatic wait-staff while enjoying your romantic meal. Every 15-20 minutes, a small brass bell is rung and one of the waiters will be singing a short and wonderful aria.

Valet parking: Available which is a huge plus! (~ $12.)
Cost: It will not break the bank.
Dress code: Casual and relaxed. 
Staff: Very welcoming and super friendly ( also professional.) 


Victor Cafe, I will be back

Four and Half Yelps.

Continental Mid-town will always have a special place in my heart. 

See, last fall, I went here on a first date, and as you all know: Finding a "perfect" 1st date spot is hard. I impulsively chose this rooftop lounge/patio -- and I left it satisfied with the upscale, yet laid-back atmosphere, and their signature Astronaut. So raise a glass (or a grilled Thai chicken skewer)- Yummy.
While I can't recommend many items to try- for obvious reasons ;) I can still give some tips to make sure you have a good quality time.
