As a kid, my dad and I use to wake up early while my teenage brothers and mom slept in on the weekends. We would sneak out and head over to Spencer's for crispy pancakes and hashbrowns. It a special memory that comes to mind when I think back on my childhood (and those are still my favorite menu items!).

Nowadays, I make a point to visit my favorite breakfast joint anytime I'm back in St. Louis, typically 2-3 times a year. I'll tell you what, it's certainly not enough considering the love I have for this place! The renovations made have just made it cozier and more homey on the inside. The staff continues to be made up of friendly locals, and you can tell that they truly love what they do. Most importantly, the food is still as good as ever.  Whatever you do, don't come here without ordering the crispy pancakes and hashbrowns please! Come early if you want a seat on the weekend, as the rest of Kirkwood will be joining you. I'm thankful for all the special memories I've made at Spencer's from over the years.

Excellent service. Best Thai in the Nashville area, no competition! We went last night, we're going back today, and we don't even live near Smyrna. The red curry was like a dream. The sticky rice with mango was like heaven. Bravo, Thida Thai!

When your staying at the Ritz you expect a certain quality that is associated with the brand. Unfortunately like many other reviews have indicated, this location falls short of that standard. A good fiend of mine stayed here just 9 months ago and had a totally different opinion of what we experienced. 
1. Before my stay I was in touch with the concierge to plan a special surprise for my wife since it was her birthday that day. I ordered a specific bottle of sparkling wine to be delivered upon checkin. Unfortunately the wrong bottle got delivered and was opened upon arrival so we couldn't sent it back to get switched. Went up to the lobby and spoke to the concierge and she apologized for the mistake. A supervisor called me later and indicated that they would remove the charge. Went to dinner and when we came back we found a bottle of champagne waiting in the room. No note attached but I assumed it was sent to apologize since my original surprise didn't go as planned.  I appreciated the gesture. 

2. Went to the bistro for dinner. We sat on the patio since we had our dog. We sat specifically near two heaters since it was a little chilly and my parent are in there late 70's so I wanted them to be comfortable. As another table got seated one of the staff took our nearby heater and moved it over to the other table without any consideration for our table. We also thought the menu prices seemed rather high, most entrees were priced around $40, and the quality wasn't anything to rave about. My mother got the scallops and they were way overdone. The wife got a salad that was overdressed. Also $20 for guacamole was steep even when it's a resort. 
For breakfast we went to the coffee shop. $12 for a breakfast sandwich? It's not even fresh. Its just like Starbucks, it's premade in a package and tossed into a quick oven to reheat.  I may as well just ordered from room service for the same price, at least I would expect to get something that was made fresh.
I think I read another reviewers post and they jokingly suggested taking the cart to the golf course to get better and cheaper food at the club house.

3. As a few folks have mentioned the rooms are not cleaned very well. The wife said she saw some "suspicious" curly hair on the bed when we arrived and my mom indicated that some of her towels had stains. Also the rug on the floor looked filthy.  Also none of the tv channels worked.  Each station would play for a minute and then loose signal. 

4. When we arrived we were given a card that listed the amenities. The card indicted a free bottle of wine per stay. When we called the front desk they told us they discontinued the amenity 4 months ago. False advertising. 

5. Am I the only one who think a pet fee of $250 is overpriced? Most other hotels only charge $50-&100. 

6. So my aunt, uncles and cousin ended up missing a part of the wedding that we were attending on the property because it took 20 mins for the cart they ordered to take them down near the beach entrance. If they had known it was going to take that long I think they would have elected to just walk.

Overall For the price you pay per night, you would tend to expect more.  As much as I want to give this place a higher rating especially because of the way they handled item #1, there were plenty of other missteps or disappointments.

Geez. Where to start.... I know this place just opened, but even that isn't an excuse for what we went though tonight... First, from the time we ordered our food, we waited 27 min for it to arrive. TWENTY SEVEN. This isn't western village, it isn't Bimini steak house.... it's Steak 'n Shake... Once our food arrived, it was half wrong. Luckily my plate was correct, but my wife's was 100% incorrect. She ordered a grilled cheese steak burger, and received a grilled cheese. Now, this is an easy mistake, but our waitress, all 16 years of her, repeated the order back to us, twice. So she got it correct when she took it. So, after waiting 4-5 min to be asked "how everything is" we tell the waitress the issue... At this point we feel like assholes, because rarely do we complain, but no one wants to eat a grilled cheese at a burger place... So the poor waitress takes, 5min to "get approval" to exchange the meal. Literally has to ask to make it happen. By this point I'm sharing my meal with my wife, and it's nearly done. 15 min later her correct meal arrives... SMH. This is where we both nearly melted down. (See pics). Her "sandwich" had a HALF DOLLAR sized patty on the full sized bread. Literally. Two medallion sized pattys (think two pieces of Texas toast cut diagonally). At this point we are totally flabbergasted, but too pissy and too ready to leave to say anything. So, to summarize. 57 min, horrible service, overwhelmed employees (22 by my count) no discount for the mess up, no manager apology, and NO RETURN FROM THESE CUSTOMERS.


I get it. You just opened.
You have 17 year old employees.
You have one manager on duty.
You have a drive through.
You're busy.

But have your people multitask. We watched the "greater" just stand at the front door for 20+ min while not greeting anyone. Buss a table, refill a beverage. Do something. 18+ people in the kitchen. More than 5, standing around looking lost. If you're not "ready" to be open, train more. Because at this rate, there isn't going to be customers for all these people to not help....

It's open late. It's food. It contains steak and cheese. Automatic 3-stars. Beyond that, I think we all know that Geno's isn't the best spot to grab a Philly while in Philly. That being said, it's not bad at all! Make sure you know what to order (always opt for extra cheese and onions) or maybe try something new (the pizza steak is fun, still with extra cheese) and you'll have a nice little 'steak to chomp on. Add some fries and you're golden. In the area and like a shorter line (wink wink), hit up Geno's. You won't be sorry. Well....

Found a great rate including breakfast buffet on Travelzoo, so I pulled the trigger for the Hilton Garden Inn - Center City. 

The Staff: Front desk and lobby staff were great! Check in was fast and friendly. Popcorn machine and flavored water in the lobby when you walk in? Win!
The Room: The king suite was large! Only $10 more than the regular room and well worth it. Lots of space to stretch out, a couch with separate TV, and a nice desk area. Bathroom was standard, but clean, and stocked with towels. Keurig coffee machine with pods was a nice touch. Didn't hear any street noise (yaaaaas)
The Area: You're in Chinatown (which I loved), but walkable distance to many other areas of the city. You're super close to Reading Terminal, so go and get your eat on! Bonus that many Chinatown restaurants are BYOB. (Sad that the local WAWA closed though) 
The Other: Why oh why do housekeepers try to get into your room at 930am when checkout is at 11am? Wifi was fast and free. Gym/bar on premises. Parking was $34/day in the attached garage, which is high for the area. 

Overall, a good deal and a nice stay for one night this Saturday. Will be back!

Protip: Grab some wine and eat soup dumplings at Tom's Dim Sum directly across from the hotel :)

Had a nice little rooftop brunch with the fam here for Mother's Day. The servers were so helpful with my family's requests and I have to give them major points for that. We're an annoying bunch (sorrynotsorry). They don't take rezzies on the roof, but there was plenty of room up there for a lot of diners. Though the interior hasn't changed much since their heyday of 10 years ago-ish, it's still a cute looking spot. Here is the eats rundown...

Huevos Rancheros - Solid presentation and delicious, but on the smaller side when compared to the other dishes
French onion soup dumplings - Avoid at all costs. Conceptually great, but the execution is poor. 
Asian chicken salad - HUGE portion. Solid though. Def go splitsville with a friend. 
#solcialite - Pretty awesome champagne/vodka cocktail. Sweet (blueberry + lemon) but very drinkable.
BLT - Nice sized portion and a pretty solid version of this classic. Lots of turkey and bacon. 

Even though the area is now packed with fresh eateries, I would come back here for a chill brunch and some drank. You could do better, buy you can most definitely do worse. 

Side note: Their website is possibly the most annoying thing I've encountered in 2016 thus far. It pops up into a mini pop up... which then becomes the browsing site (WHY!!!!!!!!). Oh, and non one like website music. Come on now. Web 101.

No brainer 5-star review here. $4.50 for an egg white omelet with spinach, rye toast and homefries. WHAT. Sure, it wasn't a behemoth omelet, but it did the trick and I walked out stuffed. And sure, it's not the nicest spot, but it's large enough you're not cramped if you want to take out and there's plenty of tables around if you want to sit and eat in house. For a quick meal in the area, come here, bring a 5 spot... and leave with change. 

Bonus: you can order via machine ala Wawa

The only time I eat hot dogs is in Chicago at Portiilo's. This joint is a game changer. I'm so glad my friend convinced me to try it!!

It's small but super clean and the workers are amazing. Tons of classics and a bunch of yummy combo toppings. The French fries are to die for, get them loaded. This place is a hidden gem.
Friendly up beat staff. I ordered mocha latte. Absolutely delicious and a great pick up before my run.

Best greek/med food I've had in a long time. The presentation of food was beautiful. The staff were awesome. Went with Mediterranean sampler so my friend and I could try a lil of everything.  The dolmades were to die for. And authentic gyros. They don't skimp on portions or fresh ingredients. Restaurant really nice quiet and quaint. Totally recommend can't wait to go back

I went during the week, so not crowded. It's a landmark. Can't help but love all the food is $3 and under. They do have a one drink minimum. Me and friend stopped buy we both got the big Elwood on a stick and shared fries. Everything was delicious.  Waitresses are super friendly and attentive. Also a great place to have a few really cold beers and people watch

This review is based on my being a Reno resident and NOT a Hotel guest or a VIP player.

My friend and I took advantage of the M-TH Reno Residents get 15% off deal. This is my 4th time here and what happens each time I am here while getting my massage, I am silently thinking "why do I spend the extra money to come here and not just find a great massage therapist?"

I know you are paying the extra money to use the spa services, but all 3 times that I have been here, I feel that it isn't really that nice,  and it wasn't very clean when I was there on a Tuesday around 11a.m. Bathrooms were messy. Locker room is cramped and if there are more than 2 ladies in there, you can't move around. 

My massage therapist was not the best either. Very nice but talked to me the whole time while I was receiving my massage. I even didn't answer some of her questions to try and show her that I was there to relax but she didn't take the hint. 

So now that I have tried it 4 times and again I walked out feeling jipped and disappointed, I now know that I won't return.

One star BC I had to give it that. What a scam!  We went to the restaurant and ordered a $12 bowl of soup. We expected to spend a couple hundred dollars easily as it advertised as a nice steakhouse!  That's rubbish!!! 

After ordering a $50 steak that my husband and I wanted to share, and two sides totaling almost $20 dollars, and two sauces to go on top of the steaks at $24, a manager comes to our table 10 minutes after ordering. We were consuming the soup and a split of champagne.  She told us that we could not share the steak and that we would have to order a second steak. We are out of town and only share food when we are out of town so that we don't waste any extras.  This also allows us to order soups and apps well as dessert. 

She spoke to me in a condescending way and everything she said was demeaning.  It made no sense that we would have to order two steaks as there is fish on the menu for $23 each person and a steak for $50!  What if we each came in table of one? Couldn't we order whatever we wanted?  

She pretty much told us that she would NOT fill our $75 food after we already ordered $30 of soup and champagne. 

I've never in my life heard this from a restaurant without a menu disclosure. Nowhere on the menu does it say any of this or that we cannot share a dish (see pics).  We planned on crème brûlée and cocktails afterwards as well.

The manager said her name was Dina/Deena. This was tonight at 7:45 pm. 

Obviously there was something else about the way my husband and I appear. Not cool. Sounds very much like our money is not good enough for them. 

Will be making sure to contact who I must as I feel completely discriminated against.   I am saddened by this and I think it says a lot for the full out act of discrimination of the manager (in pic) or owner, who she claims orders her to make all people at a table order at least one entree each.

I've never in my life experienced such horrible customer service!! We went to Deanie's on this past Friday night and didn't leave until nearly Saturday morning because we were held "hostage" by their security guard for nearly 2 hours after the restuarant had closed until the New Orleans Police Department arrived to "arrest us" for not paying for cold "charbroiled oysters" that were served to us. 

Our bill was over $100 and we paid for everything else except for the dozen of cold "charbroiled oysters"..which only ONE was eaten and the rest were returned to the kitchen. Their manager, Chris, was very rude, nasty, and unprofessional about the situation and their security guard literally stood in the walk way with his hand blocking my friends. I will never again support this establishment and am embarrassed that this resturant is open in the beautiful city of New Orleans.

Coming from NYC, this TJ's is huge! 
Typical great produce, prices, and people.
Staff is helpful if I'm looking for those chili-lime burgers that are always snatched up before I get there... and friendly at the register.

My only complaints:
No Two Buck Chuck!  But that isn't TJ's fault.
Avoid shopping on the weekend at all costs!  Parking is horrendous.

I don't think there is a restaurant that deserves 5 stars more than this place!

Now first of all, well, I'm dumb because I thought this place was one of the few Bouchons that Thomas Keller owns! Having been a few times to the one in Beverly Hills, I was thinking this one was way better... but now that I know they're not owned by the same person, I guess I can't make that comparison!  

Anyway, the wonderful Pumpkie took me to Santa Barbara for my birthday and we went here for my birthday dinner! And I loved it! I highly recommend this place!! All the high praise and accolades are definitely spot on!

Why you ask?!

Well first of all, this one is way more intimate. It is a smaller restaurant and the seating is a bit more tight but the executive chef brings the plates and your food! And basically waited on our table! Can't beat that!

We started with the scallop appetizer and it was absolutely AMAZING! I love scallops and these were absolutely cooked to perfection! They were so fresh (I mean it is Santa Barbara after all - but you never know) and the 4 presentations, preparations and flavors were all so different and just so delicious! I loved this dish and it was definitely one of the best things I've ever eaten! Dare I say these scallops were better than the one at Gordon Ramsey's (psss - they were!). If it's on the menu, get this! It's absolutely amazing!! 

French Onion soup - well, this was for Pump but this was also one of - if not the - best French onion soups I've ever had the pleasure of eating (and I've had a good amount). The bread and cheese at the top were just so good and that deep onion flavor could only come from many hours spent developing a complex and deep flavor. Another absolutely delicious dish! 

The little amuse tart - the chef was kind enough to bring me this tiny tart while the Pump was having his soup! So very kind! My goodness! Even something this small and tiny was absolutely delicious! The fruit was just so sweet and this is the beginning of January mind you! The crust was flaky and buttery and the cream was so good! Delicious! 

The venison - I contemplated ordering this because I wanted to try something different but the Pump was nice enough to get this so I could try it and then get something that I knew I would like - the chicken! This is my first taste of venison and it was good - very lean and I could see how some people would call it slightly minerally. Definitely good! 

The chicken- obviously a Mary's chicken and cooked to perfection! Juicy, flavorful and delicious! And that's asking a lot of chicken! :) The mashed potatoes were also mascarpone whipped and amazingly delicious! Yum! 

Also, the portions are not chintzy at all and because of this and all the food we got, we were both too stuffed to have dessert! This is my one regret as I am sure they're dessert is amazing!! I definitely want to come back and next time, I'll make sure to leave room for dessert!! 

Honestly, I can't wait to come back again soon!

Cafe Beignet on Royal Street is a nice chain restaurant in NOLA. I was drawn in by the big jazz band playing inside and the place is bright, clean and well-appointed so the only thing left is to get me some coffee and beignets :-) 

there's no table service here as you order and pay at the counter. The coffee is good and an order of beignets is three beignets coated in powdered sugar but all of us felt the beignets tasted a little doughy in the center. I may give them another try because lots of folks rave about them. Just not impressed with their beignets, seriously disappointed!

This is a cool looking Nawlins bistro that has sidewalk dining and it's located diagonally across from our hotel of choice "Lafayette".

The were busy when we arrived just after 8pm on a Tuesday. The maitre de greeted us with one word "reservations". Okay, my response was a one word "nope" and there we stood looking eyes. You know what they say "the one that speaks first loses" LOL. She spoke after a long moment, not checking a screen or paper but simply with a "this way" .... lol I win.  To be fair I was hot, tired and hungry so after driving for 3.5 hours, navigating the nightmare construction traffic in New Orleans, checking into the hotel and trying to adjust to the 800% humidity that is all typical of Nawlins, I wasn't in my normally chipper and fun loving mood :-) 

The interior and the server were just fine but there was this guy who kinda stood around peering around the room was a little odd. First of all he was dressed in a formal black suit and looked like he combed his hair with buttered toast and struck me as a guy badly imitating an Italian used car salesman waiting for a bus. I mean he wasn't talking to the servers, chefs, customers or even fetching napkins, just adjusting his hair and clothes while looking at everyone and no one, like I said odd. 

We were hungry but we were going to turn in early for a 4am wakep to catch a train so we didn't want anything to big or spicy before returning to our room for the night. 

We both got waters and ordered right away. My sweetheart ordered the spring lettuces and fir me I ordered the beef short rib. The spring lettuces was small but okay but OMG the single teeny tiny cube of meat I received was not only comical but was burnt, flavorless and too tough to chew, seriously rediculous. I don't know why my phone failed to record the picture I snapped of that beef dig treat but maybe my phone doesn't have a sense of humor. 

We waited a little too long to get this meager "meal" and is was over $30 and as stated I was too tired to put up a fuss and just wanted to get out of there and that's what we did. What a disappointment because I always look forward to a culinary experience when I blow into Nawlins but this was a cruel culinary joke. 

Bottom line: They staff kinda act like they're a bit overwhelmed, the chef(s) are definetly out of their depth, the food is just plain bad, the portions are small and the prices are high. 
Fail

We recently had a limited time in Nawlins and  it's always a dilemma to try to pick and choose the best spots to eat and visit. This trip was to bring my honey to the train station but also to grab an afternoon and evening for ourselves before she left for New England to help out a friend post-surgery. This time for dinner I got some excellent advise from a real Nola guru and Yelp friend Shannon S. He recommended this gem of a date night spot that indeed was spot on for ambience, service and food, nicely done Shannon!

On this Saturday I called for a reservation but they were all booked up but were welcoming walk-ins so we took our chances and headed out for an early dinner. We were fortunate to be seated just inside the interior on the edge of the lovely courtyard. I soon going out that it's the desirable courtyard that gets fully reserved for the dinner service but the interior is open to the courtyard so the ambience is still quite nice. 

While I don't want to rant about the whole "mask thing" it did become very apparent that the restaurant and other business staff are VERY uptight about their New Orleans local government mandates. I had my mask in hand and before I could put it on the hostess starting waiving her hands and motioning at her face towards me while I was still on the sidewalk outside, seriously. I will stop here LOL

Anyway, our server Sue was very pleasant, warm and welcoming and did a good job with explaining and recommending dishes. I started with a very nice gumbo. I my was fresh and delicious with very nice flavors and tender chicken and sausages (no seafood). My sweetheart had the seared salmon with roasted potatoes, sauteed snow peas and green beans and horseradish butter. Her salmon was perfectly cooked and nicely seasoned as we're the veggies and that horesradish butter was amazing. I opted for the  Pork Chop, which had rave reviews, that was served with old mill stone grits, Marque choux, green beans and snow peas. The thick pork chop was very well seasoned, slightly overcooked, and the sides were excellent. 
* Maque Choux is a classic Cajun recipe of corn and peppers sautéed in bacon grease until softened and spiced with a blend of Cajun seasonings.
We enjoyed our dinner experience and I would likely return in the future to try some of their other dining options. It's a bit pricey with moderate portions but it's in the heart of the French Quarter so it's the norm. 

The parking situation, especially anywhere on it near Royal and Bourbon streets, is rediculous. I recommend an Uber, Lyft, cab, trollies, carriage or anything other than your own car. Nuff said.

The origins of this restaurant dates back to  2005 and Café Amelie was named for Amelie Miltonberger, the mother of Princess Alice, the first American Princess of Monaco, who lived in an accompanying townhouse in the mid-1800s. 

Bottom line: Good quality food, indoor and outdoor seating that is a very pleasant experience with a mostly classic New Orleans menu. Recommended

Happy Hour 3-5
 .75 cent RAW Oysters
1/2 of Cocktails, Draft Beers, & Wines by the glass
Fried Oysters (6 or 12pc) *i forgot the price

You have not lived until you tried the Monday lunch special (tabasco honey chicken w/ red beans & rice). It comes with your choice of a soup or Luke salad (bibb lettuce, celery root, carrots, beets, & buttermilk dressing) for 17$. The chicken breast is fried to a tender crisp, the meat still juicy and succulent. The red beans and rice, cooked perfectly, seasoned perfectly, drool worthy!

The chicken & rabbit pate (11$) is a table pleaser too!

Definitely make a reservation on OpenTable so you don't have to stand around waiting! I am always able to score one for the time I need.

Eek! Hell no! Eek! How the hell is this place open?!? Eek! I just spent over $100 on food I could have made so much better, and I DON'T COOK!!

This is that place where you wish 0 Stars was possible!

Okay, I know, it's my own fault not checking the ratings before I go in. Yeah, I'm that tourist that is only sitting down to eat because the view is worth a poor meal. This is the only possible reason this place is still open. Okay, now that I have got that off my chest, let me state the ways this place needs to either find new management or a new chef.

Let's start with what the kids decided to eat. The mini sliders was first and were dry, completely tasteless and definitely not worth the $15. Next was the Salmon. $30 for a meal that could have been picked out at Trader Joes and cooked at home for a fraction of the costs. The wife and I decided to do a clam chowder and chili. The clam chowder was boring (living in SD there are plenty of true seafood places that take care and pride in their chowder). The Chili might have well been Hormel. I swear, it tasted just like it. $9 for a small bowl of chili that was only bearable for a few bites. I understand that a meal could be off, but all of them to be off was not only telling about what this place serves, but it also is evident that quality taste and service is not what this place is about. 

I couldn't believe we spent over $100 for two entrees, two bowls of soup and 3 drinks. I am one who hates to write reviews of places that disappoint, but it some cases I hope this review will either save someone's belly and money! Save your pocket and stomach and go somewhere else. Eek! Methinks not!!!

The Sonora Dogs here are delicious! 

Let's start with a brief review of the bun -- OMG probably the best I've ever had. This is authentic, fresh, and absolutely worth every penny ($2.50 for a Sonora Dog -- cash only at this location!). The hot dog had great flavor and the bacon was cooked well (unlike some places where you get soggy bacon wrapped around the dog). Lots of authentic toppings and a pepper come with the Sonora dog. But they also have a small bar of other condiments if you want to add something like cheese, pico, etc. 

So glad to have found this place during the "Search for Tucson's Best Sonora Dog" challenge. Yummy! 

Definitely coming here instead of my "usual" spot now, as this actually is much better.

With little energy left and thunderstorms in the area, I had no desire to return to French Quarters area.  Using my trusty Yelp app., I searched for the neighborhood favorites near my hotel, and discovered highly rated Drago's House.  This is a family owned restaurant since opening in 1969 by Drago and Klara Cvitanovich.  Klara is still around greeting customers, and Drago being 88-year-old no longer selects the oysters himself, and has passed the torch to his son Tommy.  I've noticed a pattern with family owned restaurants, they are simply passionate about their business and their customers.

The interior was aged with a lot of character and extensive wood work.  I loved the large arched windows, although surprisingly the lighting was a bit dim. The place could use a bit of refreshing; I prefer more modern atmosphere even for seafood dining.  The hostess and staff were very nice and this being my first visit, the waiter assisted me with the menu and recommendations.  I also had trouble getting on the WiFi network, and they were happy to assist me with the password.  It was obvious, the staff's objective was for me to leave the restaurant with a memory of pleasurable experience.

I wasn't to hungry so decided to try something modest and of local flavor.  I started with Mama Ruth's Seafood Gumbo.  It was very authentic but it didn't meet my expectations; maybe it's my lack of familiarity with gumbo.  Since I didn't have oysters while at the Royal House in French Quarter, I just had to have them at this place.  I had the famous and raved about Drago's Original Charbroiled Oysters.  At first bite, they completely changed my attitude after the mediocre gumbo.  The parmesan cheese and garlic butter all charred to perfection made the oysters quite memorable.  If you don't like raw oysters, this is the dish for you, the infamous sliminess of raw oysters is gone up in smoke.

I think this place is far better enjoyed with family, as in my parents or grandparents, but I'm not sure if it's a place to dine at alone or on a date.  Yeah, the service was family like and outstanding, but there was something missing, maybe a touch of new age.  In the end if all you want is some delicious charbroiled oysters, definitely come here.  I just could not match the 4 star rating, it was more of a 3.5 star establishment to me.

Rare visits to Philadelphia amplify my craving for the local favorite, the Philly cheesesteak.  During my last visit, roughly 7 years ago, I visited the famous and celebrated Geno's and Pat's King of Steaks in south neighborhood of Philadelphia.  Since my hotel was located in the northeast suburb an hour from the city, I was unable to revisit neither one of them.  It turns out, that was not necessarily a bad thing.  Talking to a few locals, they assured me that those two places are nothing more than a celebrity and tourist traps, and going to Jim's or Steve's Prince of Steaks would more than satisfy my craving.

Again, with luck on my side and Yelp aiding in the rescue search, I was surprised to see that Steve's was just over mile from my hotel.  Perusing the photos on Yelp, the cheesesteak appeared gigantic.  So to enjoy each last bite, I strategized the next day and skipped all my meals.  The moment came, my hunger was on the brink of starvation, and the couple of beers consumed at the work social took the edge off, but quickly turned into munches.  Upon arrival I realized this place was cash only with an ATM machine inside.

Finally, I ordered the cheesesteak with American white cheese instead of the whiz (recommendation by locals). The cheesesteak was amazing in all aspects, the bread, meat, cheese and grilled onions.  I don't recall the taste of Gino's, so I don't dare to compare.  Nonetheless, the name speaks for itself, and could even be renamed to Steve's King of Steaks.  The bread roll had a light crunch with a delicate interior, which gracefully collapsed into a well balanced amount of bread with each bite.  The steak, a perfect lean cut, was chopped to perfect sized slices, and grilled to perfection.  The onions added light sweetness, and the silky white cheese closed the deal.  I also added some banana peppers, to give it a slight kick, as a personal preference.  Their bread is freshly baked daily and the meat is carved without sacrifice in quality.

The interior looks as if a mobile truck pulled up to a three walled building, with its stainless steel walls and neon 'steaks' sign.  It's more of a take out place, as the seating is limited to the perimeter bar stools along the windows.  For the record, this place has received many accolades from multiple newspapers and has many locations including the original in Philadelphia, so I would take this place seriously.  The staff was polite and made the process painless and without drama like Geno's or Pat's cheesesteak nazis. 

If Yelp had a 'Super Fan' six star rating, this would definitely earn it from me.  All I need to do now is find an excuse to travel back for work, so I can have my prince of cheesesteaks.

Traveling for work, I stayed in the outer suburbs of Philadelphia.  The worst thing about that is the lack of respectable dining besides the mall neighboring restaurants.  It's like knowing the menu before you even get off the plane, boring and without adventure.  Luck was on my side, and with help from my best travel buddy, Yelp, I was able to find a seafood restaurant with a catchy name, Bonefish Grill. Although a corporate chain, I've never had it before.  In addition, it was conveniently located with quarter of a mile to my hotel.  

Immediately impressed by the front entry, with a heat lamp and cushioned outdoor couches, I was also blown away by the lavish interior decor.  The use of soft tones with rich wood grains throughout, was a perfect marine scene, appropriate for a seafood restaurant.  Since I was dining alone, missing my Janet, I sat at the bar to enjoy a drink and dinner.  

To start I ordered from their Bar-Fresh Cocktails menu, which includes specialties for around $5.  I sipped on the Spiked Blackberry Elixir, which was a impressive delight of Malibu rum, fresh blackberries, sage, fresh lemon juice and coconut water.  I couldn't believe how cheap the drink was, this would be an easy $10 specialty at any other place.

I was straying from anything battered, as my palate was craving fresh grilled fish.  I discovered the Chilean Sea Bass (6 oz for $27.50) garnished with sweet and spicy mango salsa, and grilled to moist perfection over wood burning grill.  The piece was quite thick, allowing the exterior to be blackened with the interior preserved moist.  Eavesdropping on a conversation between the manager and another customer, I deducted that the fresh fish comes from a well respected source, the ProFish distributor (featured on the TV show Bizzare Foods America). I also chose the steamed asparagus, which was crunchy and buttery in flavor.  The dish came with garbanzo beans garnished with bits of spinach and garlic, if I recall correctly.  Nonetheless, it was quite fantastic.  I left the place with a healthy conscious mind, as I skipped dessert; however, it took about five minutes of mental negotiation regarding the coconut pie with hand made whip.

The staff and service at the bar was excellent, and on par with most fine dining restaurant's table service.  They helped me navigate through the menu, as I was specific with my dining needs.  They also made my drink less sweet per my request.  All in all, I had an delightful experience without complaints.  The experience would have been even more memorable if Janet dined with me.  

I'm certain, I'll be returning to this neck of the woods, and will definitely visit to discovered another great catch for the evening.

Traveling on business and unfamiliar with the area I decided to consult my handy Yelp app.  Being in the south BBQ cuisine was in order, as this cuisine is quite limited in northern California in terms of quality.  The Joint got my attention, as it looked very authentic and with 4.5 star average rating I was assured it was going to be at least on par with California's offerings.  The Joint opened in 2004 in the Historic Bywater District east of downtown New Orleans.  Over the years, it has developed a national reputation for some of the best barbecue around. According to their website, it has been in top 10 BBQ lists in publications from Bon Appétit to Zagat. In July 2008, The Joint was featured in Guy Fieri's Food Network program "Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives."

Driving there was a bit concerning with the rough neighborhoods I was passing through, but the raving reviews motivated me to give it a chance.  When I arrived I was very impressed with the interior and the ambience, as it was what a BBQ restaurant should resemble, full of character and smoky aromas.  Immediately I was impressed with the friendly service, as if I was a regular.  The server talked me through their menu and suggested I give the W Special a try since it's my first visit.  It included a little pork, a little brisket and two ribs (menu description), and I chose the potato salad as my side.  Based on the amount of meat, the menu description of "little" does it "little" justice, even with serious hunger,  I was a little overwhelmed with the huge portion.  All three meats were simply amazing, very tender, smoky flavor, and plenty of love oozing from them, exactly how BBQ should taste.  The three sauces offered were awesome, with my favorite being the original.  The potato salad was the best I have ever had, no doubt.  Not sure exactly what was in it, but undertones of egg yoke flavor were present.  It's definitely home grown and I've never came across something this tasty.

If you want to experience the perfect BBQ taste, don't miss this place if in the area. I will be back for sure, it's a matter of when.

We ended up here on an afternoon after we intended to go downtown to the St. Nicholas Greek Festival - however, it was 100 degrees, we had a toddler with us, and the lines were extremely long and that meant gambling with our toddler's patience and our own iron will to get good Greek food. 

So, we decided to do a little research and find out what St. Louis thought was the best gyros in STL... and found this place. A corner hole in the wall on the edge of Affton/South City. Upon entering you see a glass case but you can't miss the rotating lamb meat skewers sizzling next to the counter. There isn't a lot of seating, but its counter service so its not like you're waiting for a table for waiter service. Food is served hot and fast. 

I asked for my own little concoction of a Gyro salad and asked for double meat and wow that meant A LOT of meat... (see photos)... It was delicious and so filling. The meat was lightly salty and a little crisp but delicious. The kid's box was perfect for the littlest, warm pita, tzatziki, and slices of meat - does well for a little guy who is on finger foods. We even had some to take home. My  husband ordered the classic gyro and said that it was delicious and exactly what he was hoping for when we were originally in route to the Greek festival and those gyros... Ultimately, a good decision for us that day - and we found a little south city gem with awesome Greek food. 

We, also, took home some baklava to my mother in law. ;)

I am not even going to lie to you, Foodies... I love everything Rick and Elisa Lewis have done or been a part of...

One of the first things that ever stood out to me is that Rick remembers EVERYONE... (even if he is faking it, you'll never know it)... he comes out of the kitchen and greets you, he does all the things - all the things necessary to make you feel like you're a regular at one of his joints. Hugs, playing with the kids, and remembers where he met you from...

All Lewis (and Elisa & family's Quincy Street Bistro) ventures mean a lot to the husband and I because we started dating and spent a lot of time at QSB when Rick was the chef and Elisa was our bartender (often, or her mom)... My husband used to take his late father there and he and Rick used to talk about cooking and pies and baking as if they were old friends and you never know how much those moments mean to you until the person is suddenly and unexpectedly gone...

All of that said, you won't ever EVER not feel at home at one of the Lewis' establishments. Truly.

Now. We got the mush out of the way. Food.

You walk in and its southern diner feel, like you've stepped back (aesthetically) about sixty plus years... The old mattress springs and succulents on a gorgeous navy wall up against shiny maple wainscoting and wood trim... gorgeous. 

I love that the table markers are note cards indicating all different locations around STL.

You have your choice of booth and table - along with lots of potential options for seating large groups. This is a family-friendly establishment (we brought our infant) so there are high chairs available.  

I ordered the sweet tea brined turkey leg as I had been lusting over it for quite some time... I ordered in pre-pulled from the bone, as opposed to eating it haunch-style and they dusted some seasoning and some green onions to make 'pretty'. Juicy, flavorful, just the right amount of salt... and you know - keto friendly for those of us who don't do carbs... *if you're a ketogenic eater and don't do a lot of carbs, you could totally find a TON of options here that fit into that lifestyle - including several options of unsweetened tea to drink. ;)

Their country ham deviled eggs were awesome - a mix of savory salt and creamy and mustard... I genuinely could not get enough of these... I could eat just these...

But... let me tell you of one of the most envious moments I have ever had with my husband... The prime rib sandwich was on special this day... and Rick warned that there may only be enough to do 1 or 2 left this particular day as we were doing a much later lunch during a thunderstorm. My husband ordered it and since we always share.... OH. MY. GOD... the prime rib sandwich is one of the top 3? Maybe number 1?.... sandwiches I have ever had - this perfectly cooked prime rib, juicy, coated in a lovely creamy horseradish that even those who cannot handle the spice could easily handle this... with a tiny dash of greens (that is it, that is all a good prime rib sandwich needs, not a bunch of other craziness)... and a 'gooey' soft sandwich bun. Now, I am not sure if I go back I could stay true to my "Try something new so you can blog about it every time you return to an establishment..." rule... I only want that. (Call to find out specials beforehand - assuming they aren't posted online.).

The baby devoured the mac and cheese - so clearly he provides a solid thumbs up - and no less than three times he attempted to steal our country ham deviled eggs. 

We love the Lewis' crew, what they represent, and their product (both service and food) is top notch and unlike anything else you'll find - even in the most 'pretentious' of establishments...

I have no idea where to start.

This place shouldn't stay in the Delmar loop for long... In just a year it has most definitely outgrown the space. The wait times can get excessive but they are always worth it. 

First, get the brisket. If you have a chance, get double the brisket. You don't need a knife and likely won't need sauce at all. The mustarolina on the table is good-looking but ask for their white BBQ sauce that isn't out on the table.

Also, the deviled eggs appetizer is not your co workers pot luck contribution...... These are deliciously crafted deviled eggs with proper seasoning, topped with bacon. Get it. Worth it.

While you're at it, pair a few fingers of bourbon with your meal. The Bowman options are really delicious.

Ask for the bacon cheddar popovers.

And St Louisans I know you're going to be mad... But they have some of the best toasted raviolis I've ever had...

The only cons:

Very limited wait time seating area. You can sit at the bar as well. 

Cracker Mac is a bit bland, but up against so much flavor...

*Add the tangy sauce to your brisket chili.

We waited a really long time to come here-- not only that, it was really difficult to get into for a while and ultimately we knew that this was a smaller and more intimate joint and that standing around would be a while.

If you are even considering going...ever... Make. A. Reservation... and if you change your mind, you can cancel it later. 

There is a center-of-the-room long bar for standing at and having cocktails, some people were sitting one one side of it having small bites, and across from that is a bar.

One of the first things I noticed once we arrived was that the hostess acknowledged it was our anniversary. Nice touch. Then, as we were seated near the kitchen I noticed the kitchen were all women and in a male-dominated industry that was pretty amazing.

The cocktails were on point. I got the #27, a bourbon cocktail was fresh herbs on top. Delicious and refreshing, nice balance of flavors. 

We ordered the barbecue shrimp appetizer and fried green tomatoes. The grits beneath the shrimp had soaked up all of the delicious heat from the chili sauce. The fried green tomatoes were a touch too much acid for both of us, but still very good, considering I had grown up with those being made in our home and either way these were far better than those. 

I ordered the burger as people raved about it and I was told that bun used for my favorite breakfast sandwich next door at The Clover and the Bee was also used for the burger... um. Sold. Two amazing smashed burger patties, deliciously juicy with two different types of cheese melting all around with crisp pickles. Those fries though... Oh my god. They served me these fries with this zesty aioli made with malt vinegar and it just simply changed my life. I sometimes catch myself thinking about those fries when I am starting to get hungry. 

My husband ordered the dip, which is lamb meat, on a delicious soft, almost corn bread bun that does not fall apart when you dip it. The lamb is amazing. The textures are perfect and I can unequivocally say it is the best beef dip I have ever had - first only above the one I used to get at the Elisa and Rick Lewis' family's corner venture and south city icon, Quincy Street Bistro (Rest in peace...ugh). 

We were stuffed beyond stuffed... and since it was our anniversary we decided to get a little something sweet for dessert.  We got the cookie... and it is not at all just a cookie... it is a warm cookie, under-cooked, in a crock with ice cream melting on top of it. My god, you just don't think of some of the best desserts in your life being a gooey cookie with a single dollop of ice cream - but it was perfectly chocolatey and a nice little sweet touch to split for two; too rich for a single person to enjoy to its fullest. 

Service was expeditious and solid even on a busy Friday night very close to Valentine's day. The ambiance is intimate, romantic, and industrial modern (which I loved)... and you, also, as a nod to owner's family story - you can make a donation to the heart foundation they are deeply invested in right on the receipt. I love that.

We will return, it was truly a lovely experience and you will be hard-pressed to find this restaurant not living up to its' worthiness on Ian Froeb's Top 100.

Much like my fellow Yelper, Steven B below, I am torn on how to rate this restaurant.

We were getting ready to head out of town and we had a ton of errands to run, and in general, I am your girl for tacos. I can talk to you about all kinds of tacos. Authentic Mexican tacos, Americanized tacos, signature tacos that are a restaurants spin on certain types of popular tacos... I am going to say that you can probably find more reviews about tacos in my repertoire than anything else...

I saw this place when I was leaving dinner with a girlfriend the week prior, and honestly, had no clue it existed, and thats kind of a big deal to me - so, quickly, I needed to write this off the list of taco places that I have tried. 

First and foremost, when you walk in they give you the option of sitting at the bar or sitting at a table, there is no "waiter service" by definition unless you're at the bar and then the bartender is your server. We went on a Sunday evening and the place was empty and there were tons of employees there wandering around. Restaurants committing to that kind of staffing when they aren't making any money yet can be disastrous. 

The bartender was very kind and very attentive. 

The street corn was probably my favorite thing on the menu. Is it sad that the street corn was the best thing...at a taco joint?

We ordered three tacos each, two servings of street corn, and waters. No booze. Nothing else.
$38... I will spend money on good food, because I build it in to my expendable income! Travel and food are my luxuries that I make it a point to have money to spend on it. Do not charge me $38 for three tacos and two small sides of street corn.

Overpriced, point blank. I feel like they are making it a point to overprice items because it is in Kirkwood and "people will pay it"... I really think that is a major mistake for a new restaurant. "Oh, look at this neighborhood! We can charge $5 and $6 for street taco sized tacos. They will pay it."

That's crazy. I know, perhaps, I am overthinking it --- but...

The Koren BBQ taco was the best thing, that we both had. Likely, because it is a fattier cut of meat and that helped it to not be so dry. 

The bisteca and chicken tinga were intensely dry, and when they are served with no sauce (as traditional street tacos are) they cannot be dry. The bisteca was overflowing with meat and falling apart. I would have been perfectly happy with less meat in the taco, knocking two dollars off the taco... but, it still can't be SO dry. 

I found myself drowning the two of the three in hot sauce just to prevent extremely dry whole mouthfuls of meat. The hot sauce was good, but its purpose is not to moisten the meat just so that you can eat it. 

Club Taco, there is work to be done... and you have to start with the intensely dry meats and re-evaluate the pricing on the menu. I know you had to have someone who did market research on the cost of tacos that are similar to yours. 

I would much rather spend $38 at Mission Taco and get FOUR tacos each, and the best guacamole, and street corn...and maybe even a margarita... and LOVE the tacos.

This place is truly a hidden gem. Enormous patio, mostly covered, and bistro tables inside. 

First of all, I love that you can buy wine by the bottle inside in the "store" area and pay for the corkage fee. Loved that, because when I walked in I saw a wine that I had on my wishlist in Vivino (thanks, Yelp CM Aaron) and I wanted that wine, not the Hess option on the menu. Awesome! (It was delicious by the way, C3 Cabernet). 

The experience is a weird mix of upscale and intimate. Grocery and restaurant. We felt like we received very attentive service, people were walking in acting like this was "their place". I like that. 

We had the medium charcuterie board, that came with a variety of meats and cheese, olives, and pickled veggies. The blue cheese on the board was hands down the best I have ever had and there have been many nights where I solely eat cheese, meat, and wine. The medium board would be perfect to split between two people over a bottle of wine. However, my husband, when we go out, insists on trying several menu items even if we have to take some home. He got the mussels, the fried ribs, and we split an asparagus salad. You will notice that in the photos I uploaded, I missed the asparagus salad because we literally immediately devoured it. It was perfectly prepared with an eggs and delicious greens- perfect citrus and asparagus can easily get over cooked and be gross- this is perfect! I will get it again!

The fried ribs were seriously delicious. It comes with this zesty sauce that complements perfectly. 

I wish I could pick up this place and move it closer to my house, I would walk there and have a bottle of wine and a board. 

Love the setup of this place, and I hope for it to have wonderful success. We will be back again. :)
Not authentic at all. Good food but just not the flavor you would expect from a 4 star Yelp review. Disappointed at best. Not the restaurant. The reviews

Let me start by saying the number of stars does NOT reflect how great the food was, nor how attentive the service was. This is strictly about my experience getting INTO the restaurant. I'm visiting home during Essence Festival, and fully expect a longer than normal wait time. Every restaurant is PACKED! However, the more established restaurants have a great system in place to combat the lines and waiting for a table. While I understand Morrow's is still very new, I would like to offer some constructive criticism:

There was a very long line to even get on the waiting list for a table (see photo attached). My party of 4 waited 1.5hrs just to get our names on the list to wait for a table. The staff said they didn't want excessively long wait times, but the system they had in place didn't fix that AT ALL. It would have been MUCH BETTER to simply take all the names in line, places us all in order on the waitlist, and let us wait for a table. Instead, there were virtually 2 lines to wait in. One for getting your name on the list, and the other for actually getting your table. This created chaos and disarray for getting into the restaurant. My suggestion would be to have an online system in place that allows people to wait in line virtually. This way, customers wouldn't be standing in 2 lines for one restaurant visit. 

Also, I understand the importance of having endorsements from celebrities, and how important it is to have those celebrities post about your business, but to have celebrities pull up, hop out, and walk right in, in front of the same customers who have been in line for hours doesn't make "regular" customers feel appreciated. Having the celebs use another entrance would keep everyone happy. 3 celebs came in either while I waited or while I ate, and each time they walked right through the front door, as the other customers waited in line. Again, I get how important their endorsement is, but handling it in a different way would make all the difference. 

My food was EXCELLENT. I had the Salmon & Grits, with a side of eggs, bacon, and hashbrowns. My party cleaned our plates. With a few tweaks, this place will be 5 stars easily. Our server was Fernando. We tipped him over the mandated 20%. Ask for him!

Came here while staying at the Peppermill and I'm glad that I did! Had an overall great experience with the service and food.
We came around 8:30pm and waited around 10-15 minutes for a table. They asked for our phone number and texted us when our table was ready which was convenient since we were able to explore around the hotel while waiting.
We ordered the Biscotti's Melt with crab and a side of fries and the Mushroom Sausage Pepperoni Pizza on Flatbread. The food was fantastic! The Biscotti's Melt with crab was definitely my favorite! I definitely recommend getting it with crab because it went so well together and the taste was amazing. The pizza was good as well and pretty big so we had a lot of leftovers.
For dessert we got the warm skillet chocolate chip cookie which was delicious but decadent. I would definitely recommend if you have a sweet tooth because it is definitely sweet but still really good. 
The service was great as well. Our server was super attentive and friendly. The ambiance was nice as well. It is quite expensive but that's expected inside the hotel.
Overall a great experience and would recommend giving this place a try when in the area!

I'm honestly very confused by all the high ratings for this place...we ordered takeout and I was very disappointed in pretty much everything I got. 

The good: egg rolls are great. Probably should have just eaten those 

The bad: everything is severely lacking in flavor -- seriously everything is bland. Even the dishes that usually are a bit spicier were lacking. All the chicken was extremely tough and tasted as if it had been reheated. 

We got an order of the sweet and sour chicken and it's not your typical sweet and sour dish (like the puffy fried nuggets) it's like they fried a chicken breast and chopped it up. Was very disappointed and it was incredibly dry. 

The general tso was underwhelming and the Singapore mei fun didn't have any curry flavor to it. All the noodle and rice dishes lacked a very basic flavor we're use to with Chinese food. 

Overall, I'm really upset we spent all this money here when nothing was good. Will not be ordering again.

I made reservations here about a month ago. Not knowing what to expect but after reading all of the great reviews I knew I had to try it. First off if you want a quick meal, don't come here. The courses went on and on, almost to the point of exhaustion. The flare and originality of the dishes was top notch BUT I saw something that really threw up a warning flag. While the cooks/chefs were making the sauces and preparing our meals I repeatedly saw one of them use a spoon to mix, taste, mix, taste. The lack of hygiene with the bare hands and the community spoon really was a hype killer for me. Once you are there you are trapped to eat what you are served and you are never advised about the price. I went with a co-worker and I was horrified when the bill came at the end and it was for $318 for 2 people! They also included a generous 20% tip to the tune of $52 for just the 2 of us! I will not be back and if the owners read this I hope you will do something about the chef's using their tasting spoons and mixing after tasting in room temperature sauces. It was an interesting concept for a restaurant but definitely not worth the price.

"If you really want to make a friend, go to someone's house and eat with him or her... The people who give you their food give you their heart." 

This quote is so true and real. I feel so fortunate and blessed to have experienced so much love, kindness and warmth from the lovely Mouna,
owner with her dear husband of the " The Mediterranean Chickpea". This is a classy establishment where Mouna welcomed me like I was family. I was then spoiled with hearty samples of each and every of those beautiful seven hummuses and then the lentil soup. 

I opted for the Falafel wrap with this crazy good and addicting Cauliflower Babaganoush and this delicious beet salad. The falafel was fresh, the seasoning was perfect, the balance of crunch vs soft was spot on. Everything came together in the wrap so well. I also got the yellow/crushed orange lentil soup that had me dancing in front of the restaurant. The spinach pie inside the fresh bread and sumac was mind blowing. Mouna asked me to dip some of my spinach pie in the soup in addition to the fresh pita chips she had just made. OMG!!!! She then had me try her special Moussaka that had a taste like I had never experienced prior.( the sauce was out of this world). 

The other items on the menu :mixed Mezze platter, the Mediterranean butter bean stew, the salads - fava bean, tabouli, fattoush, couscous, lentils with sundried tomatoes, white bean; the soups - 2 types of lentil when I visited.

The portions are substantial and very generous, an extension of the owner's love. The prices are incredible. The quality - superior to all!!

They are closed on Mondays. They accept orders via their website as well. They do provide curbside pick up. 

I made it to The Mediterranean Chickpea 3 times on this trip to Tampa. BTW Tampa, Florida is about 6550 miles west of the beautiful cities of Alexandria, Damascus and Beirut in the continents of Africa and Asia. It took a Super Bowl trip to Tampa Florida to reignite those great memories of amazing folks making spectacular food that they present you with their heart.

Went back for brunch on Saturday and took advantage of the coupon for free biscuit beignets. Three large fried pieces of biscuit dough, rolled in cinnamon and sugar, with a dipping sauce of some sort of creamy sweet goodness. Yum! I followed this with some of the best french toast I've ever had. Rich and sweet, with a drizzle of same sweet sauce. No syrup needed. Really. 

I think I like this place!

The only reason to come here is for the food and outdoor space. But don't sit too long, the manager will make the waitress drop the check and force you to get up (with full drinks).

This really happened to me on a Wednesday night. Went for dinner and drinks with a few friends. They had an okay crowd, not packed, but good for a weeknight. We sat outside, ordered apps and drinks. About an hour later we ordered our third round of drinks and we see the manager come outside and say to our waitress "start dropping checks, they've been here too long (motions to us) and they've been here for too long (a table of 4 girls seated in the corner).  The waitress promptly comes over and drops the check. Doesn't apologize (she knows we heard him) doesn't ask if we need anything else, just says "I'll take this whenever you're ready". 
Next, someone else comes over and starts clearing the table AS we were finishing our full drinks we had just ordered.

Again, this was a Wednesday night, it wasn't packed, and we were seated for ONE hour. Oh, and after we were forced up, our table wasn't seated again for about a half hour. So no one was waiting. 

I used to be a regular and I won't go back. This place has gotten way too cocky. They started out as one of the only bars in the Northeast area with outdoor space and craft beer. Now there are more places than I can count, with better drinks, better prices, and actually appreciate paying customers.

The baked goods are amazing, everything I that have ever purchased has been fresh and delicious, especially the cakes and cupcakes. The low star rating is because the people that work here are the most miserable human beings on the planet. They don't smile, they don't greet you when you come in, never a "thank you" or "have a nice day". This is crucial for small business owners, at least make your customers feel welcome and appreciated. At first I thought it was just me, but I noticed that every person that walked in the door was treated the exact same way (at least they are consistent...) I won't be back again, I would rather spend my money at a bakery where I actually feel welcome.

Wanting something light on this terribly hot summer day, so I decided a chicken kabob wrap was the perfect choice. I don't work too far from this place, so I placed an order online, and headed out on my lunch break. They are still not offering dine in, but have their patio open, and lots of easy-to-follow online ordering and pick up options. 

I opted for text alerts, which informed me when my order was ready. I pulled into one of the numbered stalls, and called the number, which informs the restaurant that you're there. Before I could enter my stall number, I was greeted by a gentleman who asked my name. Gave him my name and he quickly returned with my order. 

I just ordered the wrap because I knew I was going to eat in my car, and really wasn't hungry enough for a plate lunch. The wrap hit the spot, and was delicious! Perfect amount of crunch, juiciness, and freshness. 

I can't wait for them to open up their dining room, but on another day that isn't so hot, the patio is a nice option for dining. Area around us construction going on, but it's still pretty easy to get in and out of.

Came in on a Sunday night after not having gone here in a few years. We should have checked the menu first, because one of our favorites (house made tater tot appetizer) is no longer on the menu. I feel like it was one of the main food items they were known for, so it was a bit of a shock to see they no longer serve it. The whole menu was really scaled down from what it used to be, but I'm thinking that Covid and staffing issues probably have something to do with that, so I'm not holding it against them. 
 
Menu is on their website, and since we came in on the weekend, I asked them what their "weekend chef specials" were (website says to ask server) and was told they didn't have any. 

I opted for the Cali chicken sandwich. Description said it had chicken, jack cheese, avocado, sprouts, tomato, and house sauce. When the sandwich came, I noticed that there were no sprouts and it had lettuce instead. Nothing was mentioned by the server about the change, so I was slightly irritated. I am also particular when a description specifies avocado as I am thinking they will have sliced fresh  avocado. This was an avocado spread, which I'm not a fan of because of the weird preservative taste. If they had just put the word "spread" after avocado, I would have opted to not have it. 

Hubby got the BC Burger and garlic fries and gave them 5 stars. Also got a Dirty Wookie (one of his favorite beers). 

Overall, I would say the review is 3.5.

Great breakfast in New Orleans!  I had a Gulf shrimp omelette and an outstanding gin drink called hello sunshine. My wife and daughter had salmon avocado toast. We shared an order of candied bacon. Very popular/ busy breakfast spot in NO. We waited about 30 minutes for outside seating. Beautiful restaurant. Service was quick and friendly. This will definitely be a must do for breakfast on our next trip to the Big Easy.

I know this is touristy thing to do, but we had an awesome time. We walked from our hotel and we were hungry! The beignets and coffee were really good. We were in line about 15 minutes. Got a table and service within 5 minutes. Food was out in 10 minutes. What an operation, and we were there at a peak time. Fresh, hot beignets and hot coffee got us ready for walking around Jackson Square, which is right next door. 4 stars only for the indescribable condition of the bathroom.

Our last major stop in Nashville was one of my favorites. Hattie B's is real deal Nashville hot chicken and it was wonderful. They also serve beer! We walked from the country music hall of fame. We were tired and hungry. We underestimated the distance and walked about 3 miles. It was ok and we were ready to eat! There was an hour wait/line but we were determined. It was a full hour plus, but oh so worth it. This is off the chain great chicken. I had half a chicken,  three sides and a beer. I could not finish. I also ordered HOT for the full experience. Next time I will get medium. This is a walkup location and they bring your food to you. Everyone was very friendly. It is also fairly inexpensive based on the amount of food you get. When I go back to Nashville, Hattie B's will be one of my first stops.

Day 2 in Nashville was all about getting a healthy start and preparing ourselves for the nighttime bar scene. We started with brunch here. A little surprised they were still serving communal style with the pandemic still raging. They were and we shared a table and homestyle dishes with 4 other people outside my family. It was awesome. 3 meats and a variety of sides, plus biscuits. The meats were fried chicken, fried catfish and a tortellini. It was some of the best fried chicken I have ever had. Lightly breaded and crunchy. Perfectly cooked. The fried catfish was delicious. Could have been a little hotter. I had about 4 different veggies, all very good. I was too full for the banana pudding, but it looked amazing. This is a beautiful setting for having a meal. Our brunch was served as we sat down and service was perfect. Inexpensive too.

Unfortunately this was the only place we could find to listen to live music on our spring break stay in New Orleans. As I alluded to in a few other reviews, the city was still pretty much corona closed while we were there. It's ok. We will be back next spring break. This was a great outdoor venue for live music. Open, with plenty of seating. Food and drink vendor right in the middle. There was a large ground floor area for bands. On this gorgeous day there was a jazz foursome of older gentlemen. They were terrific! Definitely checking this area out the next time we are in town.  4 stars and not 5 because the beer was so dang expensive.

Great breakfast in New Orleans! Walk up order. Sat in a beautiful outdoor courtyard. Wonderful morning. Restaurant was crowded, but service was nice and quick. We waited at our table for about 10 minutes before our food arrived. Of course we all shared the beignets. They were hot and really good. Food was very good. We will definitely return on our next trip to New Orleans.

I really liked this restaurant. It was a suggestion from a friend for the crawfish etoufee. My mind was set on the jambalaya and it was wonderful. My daughter got a huge shrimp po boy. She thought it was great. My wife went with the crawfish etoufee. She did not like it. I tried it and I didn't like it either. Service was very matter of fact. This is a no frills kind of place. Inexpensive for the amount of food you get. I would definitely go back. There are alot of other places in New Orleans I want to try first.

Second stop on our first day in Nashville.  Same results......wonderful. Great local beers here. I found out the next evening that this bar was owned by the Ernest Tubby record store. Great, live music was on full display. Once again, expensive drinks, but incredible service. Nashville servers do not let an empty go unnoticed. They are on it quick. Couple of rounds here before moving on.

5 stars for the service!! The food was just so so. We walked in at 10 minutes til 9pm. They closed at 9pm due to covid restrictions. The staff was so welcoming and we were pretty hungry from walking around all day. There were a few customers finishing up and we were seated right away. We ordered beers and a couple of appetizers. While waiting we had a great conversation with the manager about things to do in New Orleans. She was a local and had great information. Our food came out pretty quickly. The fried green tomatoes were a little undercooked but they were topped with a fabulous piece of saucy shrimp. I can't remember what the other appetizer was, but it was ok. The restaurant space was beautiful. Big open air dining area with giant open windows. Big dining areas all throughout. It was a great way to end a Monday night in NO. We will definitely be back on our next trip.

Great place to workout. I agree with the previous reviewer, it's great to be able to workout rather than have to worry about what I look like before I go.  My only complaint is that although I usually just use the weights, pilates classes or the pool, when I do want to use the cardio equipment it seems as though there is always way too many of them out of service, and then there is only a couple of the machines that have their own TV screens, so  those are always gone and I'm stuck just having to watch some boring news show or espn sportscenter repeating over & over from the universal overhead TV's.  Not super motivating when you're trying to push yourself.  It would be nice if they would upgrade the equipment.  Membership fees are substantially more than many other gyms in the area.  They should be able to afford it.  So I marked down my rating based on the condition of the equipment.

Overall I love this gym, but if another came along that offered me similar choices with better equipment, I'd jump at it...especially if it was closer to my house.

Omg! Believing is believing ha! 
No seriously though, this has to the best best freakin fried chicken ever from the South. So flakey butter milky and super juicy! Amazing fried chicken
-the fish was so so freaking flaky it's was definitely cooked to perfection omg! Battered so well and seasoned perfectly
-red beans with a sprinkle of rice was freakin perfeccccccctttt and so delicious 
MAC was amazing 
And the corn bread muffin is to die for I even took two to go! 
-place is a cute mom and pops place 
-service was ehhh. (Busy and lots of tables to serve, you get it) 
-wait is always long! It's popular but so worth it 
I really loved everything we tried and ordered

I accidentally ordered a delivery to the wrong address outside of their delivery range and I was totally ready to eat the cost, but Eds called Yelp and got me a refund. So while I can't speak to the food, you should give these guys a shot for being bros.
Some of the best, fresh, light food I've had in St. Petersburg.  Simple elegance for the decor, great service and outstanding food made with quality ingredients.  I can't wait to go back!

20 min from downtown wilmington

I got the salmon avocado ($5) and chicken pad thai ($13). 

The salmon avocado roll was packed with salmon and avocado and I think 5 bucks is pretty cheap for 6 decent sized rolls.
The chicken pad thai was a good amount that would prob feed 2 people if you get some rolls on the side. I was super hungry and ate everything. 

I saw other people order the specialty rolls, looked good! Service is friendly, place is clean, and food comes out pretty quickly.


BYOB!!!

GOOD CHINESE FOOD!!!

I got the beef tendon from the app section and the shredded pork with bamboo.

Beef Tendon in hot chili sauce- spicy but super flavorful! Comes with some fat pieces but not too many fatty pieces. 

Shredded pork with bamboo- comes with a decent amount- lots of sauce so you might want to drain that a little if you don't care for it

I really enjoyed the flavor and the prices are reasonable for good Chinese food in the burbs! I will def come back for take-out. The total was around $21.

BEST fried chicken ever! 

Willie Mae's is absolutely worth Ubering out to the historic Treme neighborhood for their signature fried chicken. It is a landmark in New Orleans, established in 1957. Owner and namesake of the restaurant, Ms. Willie Mae Seaton was awarded a James Beard Award for "America's Classic Restaurant for the Southern Region." Many people, both locals and restaurateurs, have named Willie Mae's Scotch House as "America's Best Fried Chicken."

Willie Mae's recipe is a wet-batter seasoned only with salt and pepper, maintaining a crispy skin and tender meat. Naturally, we ordered the fried chicken, which comes with three pieces of mixed chicken served with a side for the mere price of $15. We opted for red beans and also ordered extra sides of butter beans and mac and cheese. 

Upon first bite into the chicken, I was blown away. The crispiness of the skin, the juiciness of the meat, the perfect seasoning. It's perfect. Every bite is satisfying and flavorful. I wanted at least three more orders, and I almost cried thinking that I could never get this kind of fried chicken back home in D.C. Thank goodness we found time to squeeze in some Willie Mae's before our vacation was over. The sides were fantastic too. I highly recommend getting both the red and butter beans. 

Service was friendly and thankfully, we went early on a Monday so there was no line. I already miss Willie Mae's phenomenal fried chicken. A MUST in New Orleans!

What a cute market to explore! It reminds me of a larger Dean & Deluca. I visited for the first time to meet friends for dinner on a Wednesday night. Love the set-up. Outside has nice tables and chairs with a gorgeous view of the Sundial plaza. Inside is vast with different food/drink stations to explore: there is a burger/fries station, meat area, seafood, Italian, ice cream/gelato, etc. I explored all of the downstairs trying to decide what to have for dinner. I opted for the BBQ Salmon burger. I paid and received a buzzer to pick up my food when it was ready. It was decently busy there for a Wed night. Prices can be a little up there for some of the items, but I like the uniqueness of the food/drinks. I think my Salmon burger was $13.

My burger took some time until it was ready but sitting outside chatting and enjoying the scenery passed the time. It was a unique salmon burger: BBQ salmon, kimchi, and other various veggies I can't remember. Not bad. I liked the bun it was on. I was still hungry afterward and ventured upstairs to look at the sweets. Cute setup up there as well w/ a full bar. I paid for a strawberry cupcake and brought it back downstairs to eat. So good! Frosting and inside filling were delicious.

I will definitely stop by again when in the area. Cute place to take out-of-towners as well.

My sister took me to Pueblo Vida during my last visit to AZ and I have to say, I was super impressed! 

Right off the bat I was drawn to the beautiful display of cans at the top of the bar. I mean, literally every single can that comes out of this place is a piece of art. I wanted to collect them all! 

I tried a couple different beers but my favorite was definitely the Rice Cream with peaches. It was perfectly flavored. It's an IPA and I typically don't go for those but this one was amazing! 

I loved the overall feel of this place and our beertenders were awesome. I really wish I remembered their names so I could give them a shout out! I love it when the bartender enhances your experience and makes you want to stay longer, and that was definitely the case here! 

I highly recommend this spot for a good beer and a good time!

So...still trying to figure out the hype surrounding Anthony's.  Undoubtedly because Carmel has finally received an upscale steakhouse.    While we were very hopeful that Anthony's would knock it out of the park, it was a total swing and a miss.  The best feature of the restaurant was the light on the table.   We encourage you to push the button on the bottom and bring some personalization to your your experience.  There are multiple options and it was quite fun.   Use it to countdown the minutes until your drink arrives or perhaps change the colors to flag down your waiter.

So...let's discuss the experience.  Knowing that Anthony's is new and there will be a learning curve on their part, we were expecting the usual growing pang kinks.  However, we weren't expecting them to be completely oblivious to the fact that they weren't up to par.  

We were seated upstairs immediately next to the bar.  This might be considered a bonus in regards to your beverage experience.  Not the case.  Upon being seated, we waited 30 minutes for our first cocktail.  We observed our waiter approach the bar repeatedly, only to be shooed swayed by the bartender whose main concern was those sitting before him. All other drinks were an afterthought.

We opted to start with salads and forego the appetizers.  My wedge was a generous portion and flavorful despite being a touch dry.  My wife went with the grilled watermelon salad.  The presentation and grilled watermelon were perfection, but much of the flavor was drowned in dressing.

Our entrees included the ribeye and salmon.  Both flavorful, but basic in regards to presentation and accompaniments.  Neither worth their hefty price tag. 

Throughout this experience, we watched our waiter repeatedly walk past our table and empty drinks.  We had to request the bread that should have initially been brought to the table and sadly we sent back the gnocchi side to the entrees that was luke warm at best.  We had also requested the wine menu upon being seated and had every intention of ordering a bottle, but that quickly went to the wayside when our experience continued on the downside and our server never asked us if we would like something other than water.

When all was said and done, our server thanked us for our patience, he suspected we weren't impressed with our experience, but not insightful enough to figure out why.

We went to eat at Snow Peas yesterday for lunch. There were two of us moms, each had our respective 3 year old boys, her 5 month old girl and my 1 year old girl. The boys immediately went to the play corner while we ordered meals. We were blown away by the (CHEAP!) prices and the menu options.
