After we ordered and settled at our table, we were brought some crispy wontons and sweet and sour sauce that tied the kids over until the food arrived. We got pea sized portions for our meals, and vegetable lo mein for the boys. My beef and broccoli was delicious. Just enough sauce, but not drowning, rice was great and the broccoli was cooked but still crisp. My son's lo mein was great. He ate (almost!) all of it before he returned to the play corner.  
Definitely a restaurant we will return to because of its great prices and kid friendly environment!

My husband, son, and I came in for lunch today. We had a bad experience at this location but it seems to be under new management so we gave it a shot. The renovations were a huge improvement. My waitress was helpful but poorly trained.

 My husband ordered a burger that was to have come with frizzled onions. It came with sweated onions. We mentioned it to the waitress and she went back to the kitchen. Someone in the back of the house told her to tell us the onions were right. I should mention too that the burger was red and cold in the center. He asked for Medium Rare.  

In the meantime, I am looking at this bowl of crud that looks and tastes nothing like what was described on the menu. Pasta, with asparagus, mushrooms, grilled chicken and prosciutto with two type of cheese. 

In my bowl sat canned, wilted asparagus and brown goop that hid all chances of me locating any prosciutto. Rather than be told that the thick brown saucy bowl of mush in front of me was what I ordered, I grabbed a menu. Sure enough there was no mention of this tomato pasty-beef bullion-y heavy graze in the dish....and what do you know? Hubby's burger was supposed to come wit frizzled onions. 

 I asked the manager to the end of the counter, away from her customers to discuss our problem.  She made excuses and it was clear that I was horribly boring to her. I asked her to visit my table and take a look at what I was served. She came and took the plate but did not even look at it much less admit there was a problem. She acted as though we were being too demanding.

By then, we had waited an absurd amount of time for poorly plated, cold, underdone, and all out gross food so I did not want a substitution. 

I waited in the car while my husband paid the bill. As a professional courtesy, he introduced himself as a Chef nearly 30 years experience and voiced how upsetting it was to be told he was wrong by his waitress. The customer is always right...especially in cases when they actually are. The manager was dismissive and condescending insuring that we will not go back.

Drove by Trolley Car Café one sunny day on Kelly Drive, and was beyond thrilled that there was a cute café - BYOB, to boot - that we had not yet tried for brunch.  That moment, when I was still blissfully ignorant of the awfulness of this place, is the only positive experience that I can attribute to the Trolley Car Café.  

Not sure where to even start with this place, so let's just take it from the top.

1. This place is incredibly hard to get to.  I have lived in the area for almost 5 years, and it basically takes a treasure map to get from Ridge Avenue to the parking lot.  You can see it ... but you just can't get there.  Complicated is an understatement.

2.  After parking in the tiny lot, with no outlined parking spaces, we walked in and had no idea what to do.  You literally enter the restaurant and are immediately standing in the middle of a small, oddly shaped space.  And, maybe this is just our experience, but we felt invisible.  There is no hostess to direct you, no "seat yourself" sign - no direction whatsoever - and you are literally standing on top of people who are trying to eat. After standing there like fools for 3 minutes or so, we finally had to catch the attention of a staff member that breezed by without even looking up at us.  Not a great start.

3.  We were quickly handed a menu and told to order at the counter.  First off, this place is overpriced across the board.  They want $8 or $9 for a sandwich (more than $10 if you want a side) and they provide almost no service.  I was willing to overlook this (before I tasted the food) because they are BYOB.  Had we thought ahead to bring champagne for mimosas, I would have happily paid the extra couple dollars.  In fact, we had a view of a then-snow-covered patio, which is dog-friendly in the summer, and I was already envisioning coming back in the warmer months for a lazy brunch complete with champagne/mimosas.  But then...

4.  The food came.  And it was bad.  Just bad.  We both started with soup.  The French onion soup was virtually tasteless and the potatoes in my potato leek soup were practically raw.  And it was bland.  Then came the sandwiches.  My portobello wrap was lukewarm.  Not hot enough to make you think they actually heated it up ... not cold enough to know if they were serving it cold on purpose.  My boyfriend ordered the chicken pesto sandwich and actually didn't have too many complaints, until .... wait for it ...

5.  After taking a couple bites of his sandwich, he looked down, and pulled out a 4-inch black hair.  He was totally disgusted, as any normal person would be, but let's be honest - that can happen anywhere.  He wasn't sure what to do, since we didn't have a server, no one was at the cash register, etc., so while he tried to figure out how to handle it, I took another bite of my wrap.  And, now, here's the kicker.  I felt something funny in my mouth and, sure enough, pulled out an identical black hair.  That's right, I had actual hair in my mouth.  Yeah - totally disgusting.

6.  So what could be worse than that, you ask?  The staff and manager's completely unprofessional handling of this issue.  Until I saw how they tried to deal with this situation, I honestly thought that the only reaction any respectable restaurant would have would be to comp the meal, be mortified, and do whatever it takes to make it right.  Instead, the cashier/waitress offered for the cook (whose bangs were ... you guessed it ... 4 inches long and black) to make us two more sandwiches and, when we said no, she assured us it wouldn't take long and we should just get new sandwiches.  We absolutely refused, and then had to ask them to take the charges off of our bill.  They did charge us for the soups and the drinks ($9).  The absurdity of the situation didn't hit us until we left the place, and we were so furious that we called the restaurant back to ask to speak to a manager.  The manager was unprofessional, unreasonable, and refused to see our point of view.  And, when my boyfriend conversationally let the "s-word" slip (God forbid!), she accused him of "cursing at her and being offensive."  When he tried to end the conversation, she actually had the nerve to call him back and continue this behavior.  It was clear from the get-go that this place was reeking of pretension, but how anyone could be less than mortified as the restaurant manager in a situation like that is completely beyond me. 

7.  Flash forward to a week later, when we have had a dozen good meals to erase the terrifying memories of Trolley Car Café.  My boyfriend looks at his bank statement, and they actually have the gall to charge gratuity on the agreed-upon $9.  When he called to dispute this, the man he spoke to was surprisingly nice and took care of it.

BOTTOM LINE: Terrible food, even worse experience.  Will never, EVER return.

For Geno's Steaks 1177 review I will simply say it's a good cheesesteak but not worth the wait and there is really no place to sit and eat. My homemade cheesesteak is better and the couch very comfortable, more importantly I will not be assaulted for wearing my Rangers Jersey like this poor guy in the video http://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/Rangers-Flyers-Fight-Winter-Classic-Woodbridge-NJ-Police-Officer-Iraq-War-Veteran-136706328.html

It's just a game!
I won't bore you with some long winded review about this place, it has 1,400 others if you care for the details. Pat's wins, Gino's is good but, my homemade cheese steak is better than both.

The Eastside of Tucson is sorely lacking in restaurant / bars, so I was really looking forward to trying out The Heist.  It wasn't what I had hoped it to be.  It wasn't bad, just kind of ...eh.  First off, I think their food is pretty overpriced.  An appetizer of wings was $8.99, and quite small.  They tasted ok, but I've had much better, and wouldn't order them again.  Our pizza was on the small side for $11.99, but tasted pretty good.  We even tried dessert, and for $6.99, the tiny sliver of chocolate cake with a tiny scoop of chocolate gelato was a ripoff. 

 Their bar had two large tv's (always a plus in my book), but the beer was priced strangely.  You can have a small 12 oz for $3.99 or a large 20 oz. for $5.99.  No standard 16 oz, and I think those prices are high, especially when one of the choices is PBR, and it was just as expensive as the premiums.  

So, I'm not saying we won't be back, but we will stick with pizza only, and try to hit the happy hour when the beer is cheaper.

Back to one star. I am here now. I followed Gina Ms, the managers' who wrote me, advice and asked at the door for the none smoking floor. The doorman could barely conceal his dismay when I assured him a manger told me there is a none smoking gambling floor. Nope, nada! It does not exist, he said. Was that a hoax email, I wonder. Does a Gina M exist? If Gina exist did she figure I would never return.
So again, as a none smoker I had a 12' x 12' game room of slots. When you walk out that door you are blasted by smoke, cigarettes and cigar. You'll smell like sh***y smoke by the time you leave. Phew! Cough. Here smokers rights prevail. HR disrespects none smokers. That is it for me. Never again.

Superior Seafood & Oyster Bar is located in the historic Uptown New Orleans.  According to their website, they are known for its authentic Louisiana seafood and Creole inspired dishes.

We were there for the Happy Hour!!
- Raw Oysters
- Fried Alligator

HAPPY HOUR DETAILS:
4PM to 6:30PM Daily
Double Frozen Drinks
- $4 House Wine
- $4 Draft Beer
- $0.75 Oysters

NOM NOM NOM!!  ENJOY!!

What an amazing experience we had.  So relaxing and what a beautiful setting on the water .  Chris was our waiter and he was amazing.  We were seated immediately and we sat on the back patio .   There are so many great choices to pick from on the menu.   I had crab cakes , my daughter had a burger and my other daughter had a cat fish sandwich.  All our food was so fresh and plentiful .   I definitely recommend this restaurant!

Some of these reviews kill me.

"It's too smokey." -- I'm not a smoker, but come on...it's a casino. I would expect nothing less. I think it's part of the ambience of a casino.

"Drinks aren't free if you're gambling." -- This isn't Las Vegas. You want to gamble in Tampa your choices are limited. This place is in business to make money, not feed booze to penny slot players at no cost.

"There aren't many (or any) $5 tables and on the weekends the $15 tables are full." -- Once again, this is Hard Rock in a city that has no other viable options. This isn't Lady Luck on Freemont Street...bring a bigger bank roll and ummmmm...GAMBLE!

"The ATM fees are high." -- Seriously? If you use an ATM machine at a casino you either forgot your money (in which case you should pay a convenience charge and it should be steep) or you lost all your money and can't keep yourself away from trying more (in which case you have bigger problems than worrying about ATM fees). Either bring enough cash with you (preferably an amount you can actually afford to lose) or get with the casino about a marker.

"The food is overpriced." -- There's a Steak N Shake about 1/2 mile down the road. Go there and quit blocking the aisle.

"The slots are tight. They don't pay. They're rigged." -- What person in their right mind comes into a casino thinking they're going to leave with money? I'm all about going in with a good attitude, but realize that you are paying for entertainment. You may win. You may lose. But for sure, don't to play a slot machine for 3 hours and EXPECT to go home with anything but a sore ass. 

Try going with this attitude: Be Happy. Prepare to have fun. Prepare to possibly lose everything you bring in. Prepare to smell like smoke. Prepare to pay for everything you consume.

Had to do a quick update since I've been here few times already...  So I guess I can say that the freshly made tortillas are really good!  The adobada tacos are delicious too!  I'm not a fan of their carne asada tacos.  It's just ok.  Parking situation is pretty bad unless you get lucky and find parking on the streets.  This place is located off of the 101 freeway.

The hubby and I are so happy this location opened up! The one in Reno was so up and down with their service and food quality, and this one is so much closer to home. We ordered our usual BBQ mix and chicken katsu plate. Both were so heavy, meaning the food portion was huge! We both had leftovers which were both still just as delicious the very next day. The macaroni salad was still kinda "bleh" in taste but the BBQ mix and chicken katsu was cooked perfectly and they were good pieces of meat. The one in Reno was always either overcooked to where you couldn't even chew, or there was hardly any chicken and the pieces were so tiny. I hope the food quality at this location stays this way! We can't wait to come back!

I haven't had Pizza Guys in a really long time but since Pizza Hut has been super greasy, more than usual lately, we decided to order Pizza Guys and give them a try. We are so glad we did! We ordered online for delivery. They even had a special going on for free garlic cheese bread which is nice since I was going to order that anyways. They do charge per topping, so keep that in mind. We got a large pizza...on the left side, my hubby's order. Red sauce, pepperoni, mushrooms, and jalapeños. On the right side, my order. White garlic sauce, chicken, bacon, and mushrooms. It was cool that we were able to get two different sauces on one pizza instead of having to order 2 pizzas. I was kind of upset the pizza didn't have mushrooms though since we do pay per topping here. But that's just a $1 waste, so whatever. We really enjoyed the pizza and the garlic cheese bread! The cheese was actually so melty and gooey! The garlic cheese bread was delicious. Most places when they arrive, the cheese is not melty anymore and it's usually close to being stale. We really enjoyed our orders here so we will definitely be back!

Isn't there an option for a rotten tomato?!?! They don't even deserve one star. I find it hard to believe people actually spend money in this place. The owner is rude and is horrible to his customers, and the bartenders are right there with him. I'll never spend my money there. Avoid this place.

Seafood literally means two things in NOLA: Lobsters and Oysters!  Since I've been eating oysters in other establishments, I had the baked lobster here.  It was a decent size lobster about 1.5 lbs, comes with a nice complementary dipping sauce.

Wow!  I did not expect to have such great BBQ from here.  We ordered the barbeque ribs and the jumbo chicken wings... it was delicious... mouthwatering... and keeps you wanting more and lingering for it.  Just thinking about those jumbo wings makes me want to go back.  Seriously, they are JUMBO wings.  

They are located off the beaten path in the industrial area, but it's right below NOLA Brewing Tap Room, so it's nice to compliment the beer tasting.

Well well well, I am sure if I had known Rostizado was part of the Taco Shop (I didn't know these cool kids called it that!) it would have affected my experience.

A friend of ours asked us to go here for a semi-late dinner on a Monday night. Situated right besides Mercer's parking wasn't available and we opted to pay for it.

Upon entering you'll notice the layout is a bit different from some restaurants in the city. Quite a bit of shared tables with the kitchen in the middle. The wood accents on the walls were very prevalent and on one side there was a neat looking book shelf with retro TV's showing Hispanic shows. It was a really cool design choice: 50's décor with a little bit of an updated twist. 

Our server came by and gave us helpful suggestions (she takes orders on a tablet. Are we in the future?!??). I ordered the El Emperador which brings you back to a sunny beach. The tequila was wonderful and the accompanying vanilla and basil and syrup made sure you didn't get too sloppy. Tina and our friend both had the Rosita and you definitely could discern the burnt orange. If you like smokey, this is your drink mi amigos.

While we waited for entrées, they have these wonderful little bowls with spiced chips and chickpeas that you can munch on. Absolutely terrific. Classier than beer nuts but tastier to make it cool. I wish they gave us a few or 8 or 9. It went perfect with your alcohol.

We decided to get the platter of two which feeds more than 3 I felt. It was basically rotisserie chicken and slow roasted pork with a plate of tortillas, potatoes and the fantastic salsa. UNF. Yes, I literally made that noise as I wrote this. The salsa was amazing.
The mild sauces were nothing to scoff at. They were so unique and flavorful with either meats that I really wish I was of Mexican descent so I could ask my parents to make me some at home. The spicy salsa did have a kick but hey, you did order an alcoholic drink didn't you???

We also ordered a side of roasted cauliflower and Rostizado did a great spin on it incorporating paprika (I believe?) and other spices.

We were often visited by our server who was very gracious and even called over, Danny, one of the owners to chat. Regardless if you review or not, I think it's so interesting to talk to people such as Danny whom you can tell just loves food. He's passionate, knows the history of what he's making and where it's going. An absolute pleasure to speak to.

To end off the experience, we tried the churos and Odin's beard is it ever amazing. I love fried food and this totally destroys the lame churo's you get at K-days. The special condensed milk was simply the icing on the cake. It just dances on your palette (probably the tango because I was being dipped left, right and center).

Dinner for 3 was about $130 with drinks.

TL;DR: owner was interesting to talk to and discuss food; amazing platter; drinks that bring you back to Mexico; top-tier churos

Came to this place based on the recommendations of SEVERAL friends insistence when we shared that we were going on our first trip to NOLA.  We were in town for a graduation, the entire group wanted to go out to eat for the occasion.  This was one of the closest restaurants, so we packed up the group and headed over in several cars - party of 20 please.  
WHY colleges insist on having graduation on Mother's Day, I will never understand.  As if the crowds would not be plentiful enough, graduation is thrown on top and just makes it uber messy.  I go up to the host station to let them know that we had a very large group, completely understood if we had to be split up, and was braced for a wait.  We were told that we would have to wait about 45 minutes, the group could be seated together.  I turned around, looked about and figured that the place must be a LOT alrger than it looked, there are a TON of folks who will need to flow in and out if we were getting 45 minutes.  Sat down, talked to a bunch of friendly folks and slowly started to realize that the opportunity to have a true wait time was slipping away.  My hubs went to the seafood house next door (also owned by Drago's, but MUCH MUCH better, the only bright spot in what turned into a very bleek day) and purchased some steamed shrimp for the group to snack on prior to our meal.  
After 2 hours, we were finally called to be seated.  All seemed to start to go as well as possible with such a large group at this point.  We were split into 2 tables of 10.  6 of the 10 folks at our table all decided to split the large seafood platter, 3 ordered their own full meals, one was only able to order soup (gumbo) due to some recent dental surgery.  The individual who ordered GUMBO was later misunderstood to have said COMBO.  The restaurant brags and boasts that there is SO MUCH food on the very large seafood platter (~$60) that the combo plate was placed on the end of the tabe with the seafood platter, so no one ever noticed that it was 'extra' food.  (I will make mention that this group frequents a place in Atlanta called Bay Breeze that can teach this place a thing or 10 about HUGE serving sizes)  First, we were confused about why a person who only ordered overpriced ($9) gumbo was charged for a full meal ($16), eventually we figured out what the issue was, we explained the honest mistake to the waiter who had the owner come over.  She showed her behind.  She claimed she was the owner/manager, but I refuse to believe that a person who has achieved such an accomplishment would behave this way in a completely full dining room.  Several of the patrons overheard the manner in which she went off on me and asked me about the treatment on our way out, so could this possibly hurt her in the long run?  
I pulled the server to the side and explained to him that I was initially impressed with his performance, but after this - it was quite obvious that he had no issue with throwing us under the bus to save face.      

Parking sucks.  The manager/owner is a bully, her own employees are afraid to stand up to explain a mistake to her.  The fish had no flavor.  The portions are really not as generous as they claim.  There is no reason why the fries are as soggy as they are.  The cole slaw is disgusting.  The wait is ridiculous and the host needs lessons in communicating wait times if they are consistently as busy as everyone claims.  

Never would I return to this disaster of a place.

I'm not sure if I went to the same place as the other reviewers.  I'm shocked that the reviews thus far are glowing.  Utterly baffled.  I can only comment on the "Korean" BBQ, as I didn't go try the shabu shabu.  

In short:  avoid.  even the marinated meat is sadly lacking in flavor, and there's no ssamjang.  WTF?  No seasoning and no sauce on top of that= fail.  I'm heavily biased, as I'm Korean, and I've been eating KBBQ since on the teat, but jeez, this place is bad.  

Yes, there's meat here and yes, it's all you can eat, but that's about it for positives.  

Issues:  

1. Management isn't Korean and it appears that they didn't bother to google Korean marinade recipes.  It's seriously not that hard:  sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger will make everything taste good and it's as simple as that.  For pork and chicken: add gochujang (red pepper paste) and korean chili powder to the aforementioned 4 ingredients.  Seriously, not hard.  

2. You need ssam jang- mix of gochujang and korean miso, sugar, sesame oil. Imagine getting a burger from a restaurant and they don't have ketchup or mayo or BBQ sauce or aioli.  On top of that, the beef isn't seasoned- no salt, no pepper.  Sorry, no flavor for you!  This is what happened to me- I asked for pepper paste, I got a small plate with ground black pepper, straight from the can.  Baffled.  

3.  Your grills suck.  Anything with a non stick surface becomes toxic when it gets hot enough, and as a precaution, your non-stick grills can't get hot enough.  So, there's no chance of actually grilling meat.  You're merely sitting at a table and slowly steaming your meat away.  No maillard reaction, no caramelization, no flavor.  Yes, it's a lot less work for you, because you don't have to swap grates for people, but it results in a terrible product and experience. 
I tried to cook some raw shrimp, and it took over 5 mins a side, because the grate can't get hot.  On a home stove, the same thing would take 30 seconds a side.  That's how bad the grills are.

As the average yelper's probably off instagramming their artisan gelato by this point, I'll end here, but in short, this place blows. Never again.

Please refer to the first lines of the very apt review posted by Jason K. below.  He is absolutely spot-on in his assessment, and although the similarities between our experiences basically end there, his thoughts, along with mine, suggest that Seven Stars has something of a deficiency in the "gracious hospitality" that is touted in the menu.

I moved to this area from Manhattan about a year ago and aside from Philly restaurants, have been interested in finding good inns and places with solid local character.  Seven Stars Inn had come up as a possibility several times, and as a way to celebrate a special occasion, we decided to make reservations and check it out.

Our seating was at 4:30 on a Friday, and while the dining rooms on the main floor were bustling, they were far from being packed or overwhelmed as it was still quite early.  How surprised we were to be taken through these rooms -- with their warmth, music and occupancy -- up to the second floor which was considerably colder and less unoccupied, marched down a hall and through a completely empty room to be sat, entirely by ourselves, in what had to be the most isolated area of the entire building.  No other occupied tables and no music -- only the mildly hushed banter of the busboys in the adjoining room setting the empty tables and joking about their weekend plans and the waitress asking them "if we had been watered."

Since this was essentially a house at one time, the experience can be likened to showing up for a dinner party, being escorted by the host past all of the other guests and sat in that semi-dark back bedroom where all the coats get dropped in a pile on the bed.  So much for "gracious hospitality."

We're still wondering exactly why this happened.  We were dressed in office attire and probably a little more presentable than many others we saw on our way in; I feel obliged to mention this because we've since been scraping for ANY reason we might have been swept under the rug and gotten the very distinct and unfortunate feeling that the host must have gone out of his way to put us in this hidden corner of the building.  All of this was compounded by the fact that when we asked to be moved, we were  met with what seemed to be very thinly veiled reluctance and irritation.  I might add here that I'm far from picky and regardless of where I have eaten in the past, I have never once found it necessary to be moved to a different location before this.  It really was that weird and uncomfortable.  If we were smart, we might have actually just left.

Anyway, I wonder how much of this off-putting introduction to the restaurant tinted my thoughts about the rest of the meal so please read the following with a grain of salt:

The table service following being reseated was fine.  But to be quite objective, I frankly don't understand why this place has gotten the accolades that it has.  Quantity does not equal quality and "old" does not equal well done.  If you feel "good eats" requires your cut of meat to be the size of your head, then this place is for you.  If you think that an "upscale" dining room should be furnished with the trappings of a circa 1980 old age home, then this place is for you (and it seems the menu ceased evolving about this year as well.)

If, however, you can see past the epic portions, the Seven Stars Inn is ultimately pretty basic and your time and dollar could easily be better spent elsewhere -- especially if you have some occasion to celebrate.  Since being in the area, I've had just as compelling meals at lesser chain steakhouses and been to any number of other "olde" inns in the area that maintain more true-to-period, less geriatric decor.

And as for the "full measure of comfort and enjoyment," that the inn writes about in the history section of their menu, clearly a few guests out there are receiving this or the place couldn't have sustained.  We, however, did not.

This is the 2nd time we have tried this place and I really wanted to like it as I love Greek food.  I will have to find somewhere else to fulfill my desire for Greek food as I will never go back.

Service, what service??  We went here for lunch and about half the tables were empty. We got seated right away and Server A brought us water but then we sat in our booth for over 25 minutes before anyone came to wait on us. We asked about ordering an appetizer but was told "You will get hummus and pita soon". Um okay. We flagged down Server B to inquire about our hummus and pita bread and he just nodded and walked away. About 5 minutes later he came back with the hummus and pita and asked if we were ready to order - YES, we were ready 20 minutes ago!

So he takes our order and we waited another 15 minutes to get our food. The gyro meat was very good but my dining companion's spicy chicken was dry and had no flavor. They served a weird tasting sauce with this chicken that was something I wished I hadn't tasted....ewwww!  The hummus' texture is chunky, very odd.

Halfway thru our meal, Server 3 stops by to refill our water - first time we were offered a refill.  When we were finished, we had to flag down Server 3 to get our check.

The gyro meat is wonderful but not worth putting up with the poor service and the other crappy food.

WOW! WOW! WOW! I am so glad we tried this restaurant on a whim one day! 

The patio is awesome as we really like to sit outside on a patio.  

I tried the lavendar lemonade vodka that others had talked about and it was delish!

Our service was superb - Jo the owner waited on us and she is just a lovely person! We certainly enjoyed talking with her.

My husband ordered the Quinoa Bowl and I had the Lemongrass Coconut Curry with tofu.  The Quinoa Bowl was so darn good that we almost licked the bowl clean! My curry dish was very good too - I just prefer my food spicy and Jo was quick to bring us chopped serranos and siraccha to spice it up.  We also shared the polenta fries and enjoyed them too (we loved dipping them in the sauce that came with the Quinoa Bowl).

We will definitely be back and I encourage everyone to try this restaurant! This is a great place for vegetarians to dine.

We met some friends here on a Tuesday early evening. The place was pretty full for a Tuesday! We sat upstairs on the patio and WOW what a view! The view is 5 star for sure! 

This is by far the most beautiful restaurant in Tucson - the décor is unbelievable! You can tell that no expense was spared when the owner rehabbed this building! I only hope that he can fix the problems with the servers and make the food more enjoyable and less weird otherwise he is not going to make it.

The service was not very good but Rose (floor manager) made up for it. They definitely have some kinks to work out with the service.  It seemed like a lot of people buzzing around but no definite role for any one of them except the water boy as he kept our waters full!

The food....not really sure where to start. First of all, it is so eclectic that nothing really goes together. Granted we were in the upstairs bar which I understand is completely different from the other areas; however, I would suggest that no matter where you sit - you should be able to get food from any menu offered - that is my tip for the owner.  

Back to the food - we had several appetizers and the food was just okay, not great. We had the guacamole, shrimp/scallop ceviche, beef tacos, hummus plate, and some very strange sombrero "pizza" that was so odd it should be taken off the menu immediately.  You cannot share the "sombrero" and you have to hold the tip of the hat in your hand while you eat it - it was not very good as it was doughy.  Stay away from the sombrero!

We will definitely go back and try it again and I will update my review when I do. If anything, this place is great to go for drinks and enjoy the magnificent view of the mountains and golf course.

We stopped in here around 3:30pm on a Friday afternoon. We told the hostess we were just stopping in for a drink and she pointed out the bar to us as the 21 & older bar upstairs didn't open until 5pm.  Off we go!

We grab a table near the window so we can watch guys working on cars. We wait. We wait. We wait and after 15 minutes with nobody coming to take our drink order we decide to go to the bar. The "bartender" takes our order and we get our drinks pretty quiclkly. I had the "Toolbar" and it was good.  We start looking around and notice that there are LOTS of staff just standing around BSing...hmmmm, yet we couldn't get waited on at our table.

We decide to have another drink and the "bartender" asks if I want another "ToolBox" and I said no, I want to try something else. I said I'll have the "Sparkplug" and he said you should try this one instead. What? He points to this other drink and I told him I don't like Midori. He clearly looks disappointed and off he goes to make me a "Sparkplug". 

Now I am watching him make my drink. He takes the shotglass out of a glass of water and while filling up my glass with vodka, the water from the shot glass is streaming into my drink. Ewww. He makes my drink and I look at it and notice there isn't any cranberry in it like the description says and he says "Oh I know. I left it out - I think you'll like it better" So I taste it and it is sickenly sweet so I tell him "It has to have the cranberry so its not so sweet".  So he reluctanly adds cranberry and it tastes much better.  This guy is clearly not a bartender and the lone shotglass is plopped back into the glass of water. I wonder how often the water is changed, how many hands have been in this water and.....I decide to stop wondering because I'm getting grossed and hoping the alcohol is killing all the germs.

Two people sit down next to us and the gal orders a glass of wine. The "bartender" serves her a glass of wine and the glass is so spotted that I actuallyl don't think it was washed between guests! I couldn't beleive any one would serve a glass that looked like that and was suprised the lady didn't ask for a different glass.  

The food being served on either side of us and at the tables nearby looked like your typical bar food - frozen, deep fried Famous Sam's type food.  We did not order any food so we cannot comment on the taste - just what it looked like.

The bulding and atmosphere is really fun and this place has a lot of potential to be a unique place to go; however, there is a lot of improvement needed in order for this place to succeed.

We were here on their 2nd day of opening the Oro Valley location.  I like the atmosphere and was happy that they have a full bar with tasty margaritas. :-) My husband ordered a Cadillac margarita and a shot of tequila. The shot had ice in it (?) and cost more than the drink! We were a bit taken aback by that.
. 
Love their chips and salsa! We like our salsa spicy and when we asked if they had a spicier salsa they replied YES we have a habanero salsa and it was some of the best salsa we've ever had and it had a definite kick to it

They do have your typical Mexican fare and offered a couple vegetarian choices. Since we are vegan, they accommodated us and made the veggie burro without cheese and the black beans and rice were vegan as well.

We will definitely be back! Our server, Nellie was awesome.

After reading about this restaurant on a Tucson Vegan Facebook page, I was very excited to try it as I had never heard of it before and it is located close to our office.

I walked in and was a bit overwhelmed at all the choices on the menu but the owner was so patient and he explained every single vegan item to me. He was so enthusiastic about his restaurant and the vegan choices they had.

My husband and I ordered a couple vegan burritos and the cauliflower tacos and all were so yummy!  Best cauliflower tacos we have ever had!!! They have several vegan options and we are excited to go back and try various combinations. The lemonade was the best I had ever tasted and they make all their own Mexican drinks.

My only regret? Not knowing about this place sooner!

My husband and I have been to the Persian Room in Scottsdale many times. We were so happy to learn that they were opening a restaurant here! 

The interior is absolutely stunning so as soon as you step through the doors, you are immediately surrounded by beauty.

We came here with 2 other couples and everyone absolutely LOVED their meals.  One couple had never had Persian cuisine and they said they can't wait to come again. Everyone ordered something different and each entree was superb. 

There is something for everyone - vegan, vegetarian and meat dishes. The portions are huge so you will be taking food home and having another meal later.  The food is fresh and superb quality.

They offer a full bar and a great wine selection too.

This is the nicest restaurant in Tucson and I am so happy that they are close to my home (although I would drive across town to dine here as it is that good)!!!

Try it, you will not be disappointed!

I really wanted to like this place as I have heard great things about it.  Perhaps its because they just moved to this location?  I will give it another try and update my review.

We were shown to our table in a nearly empty restaurant and there we sat and waited. And waited. And waited. My husband thought maybe we had to place our order at the bar because we didn't see a server in sight.  Finally after 20+ minutes a server came up to us and asked it we had been helped.  We told her no and that we had been waiting quite some time so she apologized and said "I will remedy that and get you some drinks out right away".  Well, about 20 minutes later, our drinks finally arrive! Keep in mind, there are MAYBE 15 total people in the restaurant and we were the last ones to arrive so the bartender was not busy.

We ordered the fondue - cheese was gritty and had an off-taste.  My mushroom risotto was very good but my mom's mushroom soup was just so-so.

After dining here several times since the opening, I will not be returning. I really like the salsa when they make it in front of you to your liking. But the food quality has been decreasing and this last time was the last straw for us.

I ordered a cheese enchilada with a chile relleno.  The plate arrived and the cheese was not melted inside my enchilada. The enchilada sauce on top had absolutely no flavor - a watery tomato concoction.  

My husband ordered his normal vegetarian molcajete which he really likes. Normally, it arrives and you can see the sauce boiling. This time it arrived and not only was it not boiling, it was lukewarm. The outside of the bowl was cool to the touch.  Normally at the end of the meal, the liquid is still bubbling and you can't touch the bowl.  He took two bites and said his food "is gross and inedible".  

We told our server that the food was not what we typically get and I even inquired if there was a different cook because the food was so bad.  He removed my husband's meal from the ticket.

This experience was so bad I'm making sure every damn site across the internet has it. I'm pissed and upset and no one should be treated like this. I'm sorry that I have to give a review like this during covid but its warranted for the horrible treatment we recieved at this restaraunt. The food was alright,  nothing to really complain about. It's the service that was disgusting. We had a good waitress, forgot us a few times but was good. Let me start there. She wasnt the problem. It was another man who worked there, gorbstarters this man completely ignored is when we waited for a hostess , passed over us and asked if another family needed to get seated... hm. It was an older guy, bald white guy who walked around asking everyone if they were okay and if they wanted something (everyone but us) we did kept seeing him glance our way occasionally during the entire time, with a funny little glance.  funnily enough we were the only black people in attendance but for now we wont make this about race... let me just explain the crappy experience first. Towards the end of our meal he rushed us. They didnt have a wait or anything but for some reason he wanted us to leave. To the point where he started forcibly cleaning up the table even with us sitting there. He then proceeded to repeatedly tell us we had to leave. That it was time for us to go, etc. Weren't we done yet. I told him to give us 5 seconds and he literally hovered over me aggressively staring into my face and counting up to 5!! I've never met anyone so rude in my life. He literally stood beside me, too close for my liking.  Shoving all my stuff towards me in an attempt to get me to leave.  Literally everyone was just staring at Us in shock. We tipped really well and there were people at the restaurant who were there even longer than us. It really makes you wonder if he was just a racist?? Is this the type of people that stogie Joe's employs!?... I wonder... well I will see you that without a doubt he was definitely 100% a jerk. I have read so many good reviews about this place and I have such high expectations and they really met the market to the end. My experience was so horrible that I had to leave a reply and a one-star.

I had a very odd experience today at Lochels. The little bakery was packed and while standing in line, I took a photo of one of the many cakes, sitting out uncovered, on the counter to send to my family and ask if I should
purchase it. One of the workers in the back asked if I was taking a picture, I said yes? And she first said, " I would rather you not." Feeling uncomfortable, I said "okay" but my mother who I was with asked why. She got rather rude and said "the board of health doesn't allow photos to be taken." I thought the situation was rude and I could tell something was odd about that comment, as in many other bakeries, I have been encouraged to take a photo. I looked it up later because I found it so uncomfortable, come to find out, the board of health would likely be more concerned with the amount of uncovered cakes to be sold out amongst such a large population of people. I've always shopped at Lochels, the baked goods are good, but after this weird experience I question what else they may be doing that the board of health would find concerning and I will not be returning.

Short Story - Burger with cockroach, horrible management. 

 
Long Story - 

Oh Varga bar...I hate to put a one star review on you but I will never go back. Unfortunate because it had one of the best burgers in town. 

I went with a few of my friends on our routine ritual of eating a burger and cheesesteaks at varga bar. I was enjoying my burger, almost 2/3 done when what jumps off the burger and onto my hand? A cute little cockroach. Which then jumps off my hand and onto the delicious truffle sauce for the fries. Then all over my friends dishes all over the table until I squished the little sucker. 

The worst part of this was the restaurants reaction....

We had to wait 7-10 minutes to get noticed by the waitress even though the commotion made it obvious something was amiss. Finally, i told the waitress of the cockroach and her reaction was emotionless, as if this was a regular occurrence. Her and another waitress immediately picked up (all) our plates without even asking us what exactly happened or apologizing for it. 

She went in the kitchen and came out to say "the manager is willing to take off the burger off our tab."  and they took of the cheapest thing off the receipt without checking which burger it was.  

Even an iHop in the ghetto would've had a manager come out, apologize and comp the whole bill. At varga bar, no one came out, no manager, no chef...no no one. Just a waitress coming back to tell us they took of one of the burgers (the cheaper one, not the one that had the cockroach) and gave us our check without asking us if they can do anything else for us...

Not having the patience and quite honestly shocked at their response, we decided to pay the rest of the bill and leave and never ever come back. 

These restaurants are dime a dozen in Philly, why risk a chance of biting into a cockroach?

Full disclosure: I. Love. This Place. 

Seriously. 

PuraVegan is completely vegan and gluten free and about 99% of what the serve is also raw. If you'd like to know the complete break down of what's not quite raw just ask em and I'm sure they'll be sure to tell ya everything you'd like to know about the food. If I'm not mistaken (which I could be) the vast majority of their foods and ingredients in said foods aren't heated beyond 115 degrees which means when you eat at PuraVegan you get the most possible nutrients from all the foods. 

Oh yes PuraVegan is so healthy and oh so delicious but serving awesome food is really just scratching the surface. The folks at PuraVegan hold cooking and being healthy classes, I've taken two; Raw Vegan 101 and Healthy Vegan and have walked away from both with a head full of knowledge (and a belly full of raw vegan food).

My Sister mentioned Lee's Deli to me on a few occasions. So a few days before my birthday, we decided to take a 15 minute drive & grab something to eat. It's a pretty small restaurant sitting right on the corner of 47th Baltimore Ave. Clean, ATM, Big Menu & awesome service. I can't remember the exact name of the cheesesteak I order, but it had Shrimp & Broccoli on it !!! It was SOOO good.. I had cheese fries that were a bit salty, but it wasn't a big upset for me. I plan to visit again in the near future...

This had to be the worst Italian food I've ever eaten and I'm Italian. 

The entrance outside is filthy with gum splattered spots and beat up entry door to tell you to hang on to the door if it's windy outside. We were immediately escorted to a table and then forgotten. I noticed 4 waitresses standing at the bar chit chatting. I waived my hand up to try and get someone's attention after 10 minutes. Finally a waitress came to our table and apologized saying she didn't know this was her table! Huh?

I ordered the Chicken Fettuccine and my husband ordered the Chicken Parmesan. The Chicken Fettuccine was so bland. For sure the sauce was NOT homemade. It tasted like boxed white Mac and cheese. So gummy and tasteless. No color on the plate. It needed broccoli or asparagus mixed in. Or a dash of parsley. I could hardly eat it. 

My husbands Chicken Fettuccine looked good when served but trying to cut the chicken required a steak knife it was so tough and thick. It should have been tenderized and thinner. The sauce was watery on the angel hair spaghetti. 

The salads were fresh but drowning in dressing and my blue cheese dressing was certainly out of a bottle-not homemade. 

You also get two cold rolls. 

After swatting away flies during the entire meal I couldn't wait to get out of there. I mean at least put the ceiling fans on maybe that would've helped. 

For all the great reviews I'm not sure people get out much to taste good Italian food. Surprising!

FOOD HANDLERS NOT WEARING MASK

Have loved Dickman's and enjoyed everything I have ever gotten there but saddened by my most recent visit on Christmas Eve. Manager was in the back handling and cutting cuts of meat without a mask, touching his beard every time shouted and order to the workers.  
Working in the medical field it was shocking seeing someone handling food without a mask and worst yet it was a manager who was exposing his customers and workers. Asked a worker why the guy who was handling all of the meat wasn't wearing a mask who sheepishly replied because he was the boss.

An authentic Italian bistro that's a hidden gem in Tampa.

I did take out for Valentine's Day. Their phone line kept ringing busy so I decided to check if it was open and sure enough it was! It's a cute small restaurant that has about 7 tables got 2, catering to couples or intimate gatherings with a close friend! Their food was awesome and the owner himself is from Italy so I had high expectations! The pasta was delicious but was slightly overcooked for one of the dishes but it was so flavourful that I didn't care too much! The menu is small so I'm
Sure that helps make sure the dishes are made with great quality.

Price was very fair for the quality of food you get. Not overly expensive for the quality of food you get. Each dessert was $7 while the chicken carbonera was $16, osso bucco was $26 and the ravioli was $23. All well worth the price! 

Beef Ravioli- my favourite dish of the night! This was not on the menu, but it was one of the dishes of the day! I'm so glad I chose this because it had a beautifully rich red sauce that had wonderful seasonings, herbs, mushrooms and drizzled with truffle oil on it! The ravioli was cooked perfectly Al Dente and the filling was soft and delicious. 5/5

Chicken Carbonara- the spaghetti was cooked Al Dente and had wonderful flavours all around. The bacon was wonderful and the cream sauce did not drench the pasta so that it cheapened it. It really made you appreciate it. The Parmesan was a wonderful touch and prominent in the dish! This was my partners favourite dish! 5/5

Pork Osso Bucco- the red sauce in this was delicious and the pork shank was nice and tender! Not as flavourful as the red sauce in the ravioli but you can tell the sauce absorbed the pork flavours nicely as it braised in there. The pasta it was served on was slightly overcooked. 4/5

Tiramisu- the best tiramisu from a restaurant I've had in tampa as of the time of writing this. The lady fingers were wonderfully soaked in the coffee; you could actually taste the marscapone cream layers (something that tampa seems to have trouble doing) and it was nicely dusted with lady finger crumbles! 5/5

Limoncello Marscapone cake- this was a moist, vanilla and lemon cake with wonderfully light Mascarpone cream frosting. It's so light you would think this was a weight watching dish (it's not ) 5/5

Cannolis- they come in pairs and are humongous! The filling was delicious and creamy but a little on the sweeter side (but not so sweet that I couldn't eat the whole thing) and the shells had the bottom dipped in dark chocolate and the sides dipped in chocolate sprinkles. 4.5/5

If you are in the mood for great Italian food, Mungo's Italian Eatery is the place for you! 

I love going to the Hill in St. Louis and most of the Hill is closed on Sunday. Mungo's was open, so my wife and I gave it a try! 

I am so glad we went to Mungo's! Their food, staff, ambiance matches everything you can find on the Hill and we didn't have to cross the river to get there. 

I got the pasta carbonara. That is my favorite pasta. It was delicious! My wife ordered the shrimp pasta. We ate every bite! A glass of Pinot noir and a cannoli topped it off! It was the perfect night out. 

We can't wait to return!

I don't really like to gamble but this place is awesome. Drinks are $1 and the waitresses walk around asking if u want anything. It is wall to wall to wall slot machines ranging from 1 cent to big dollars. You can use cash or a loadable play card. Their are even many tables of black jack,poker etc. Along with several bathrooms stragetically located throughout the place. Theirs a food court. An Asian noodle place, high end parx grill and many cash out places. This place is quite grand and huge in scale. They also have a dance "club" which has live bands on weekends with a dance floor and bar. It's nice to have something closer to Jersey than Atlantic city. There's also a Chickie and Petes restaurant located inside. So if you're a jerseyite looking to gamble but don't want to drive to A.C. this is definitely the place to go. They also have Valet parking which is great bc the parking lots (many of them) can get filled rather quickly especially if the buses come. Just make sure you tip. So definitely worth a check out..

Best bar in the Parish! We checked them out on Cinco de Mayo and were amazed at the renovations that were done. Really amazing to see true Louisiana style ambiance and decorative touches throughout the whole place. Super friendly waitstaff and very attentive. Just stopped by for a quick drink while in St. Bernard Parish but it was so worth it to check this place out. Drinks are super cheap and for every drink you buy it feeds a dog for the day at Villalobos Rescue Center. Money 100% well spent. Great drink specials and donating to the local animal shelter is such a great feeling and so rewarding. Makes you feel like you've done your good deed for the day. The whole place has been completely renovated and live bands perform on the weekends. It was truly a pleasure visiting Tahyo Tavern on a laid back Monday night & well worth the trip. Amanda the bartender was exceptional. Very attentive and welcoming. She made our visit memorable just from how kind and friendly she was. She informed us of all the specials they have and what events take place on what nights and even went out of her way to make sure I found the right size shirt I was looking for. Really great bar and will definitely go back when I'm in town again. If you are in the Parish this is a must. Don't pass them up. They are literally right off of St. Bernard Highway on Paris Road. Overall 5 stars for location, quality, the people, and the proceeds benefit a non-profit organization.

This place was the bomb.  I ordered delivery through here from Caviar and 10/10 would order again.

Menu is super varied and offers a lot of fresh/healthy options, which is always a plus.  It was so hard to choose just one since they all sounded so delicious, but we decided to start with the basic and ordered two of the Standard Burgers, one regular and one subbed with bison (!).

They came with colby cheese, caramelized onions, dill pickles and special sauce on THE perfect toasted brioche bun.  Meat was perfectly cooked with a nice crunchy char, and all the toppings blended perfectly to form a delectable burger.

Got onion rings on the side of one and fries on another.   Onion rings were DOPE (super crispy and well seasoned batter and fresh onions that snapped and didn't sog), although I didn't realize I wouldn't get the special sauce to dip them in unless I ordered a full order, as opposed to just on the side.  Fries were okay, nothing special, but I chalk that up to getting them delivered.

It can get a little steep with delivery surcharges, but I think it was totally worth it.  Will definitely try another variety of burger or sandwich from here again.

Yass I think I found my new favorite neighborhood joint!

Cry Baby Pasta is simple, straightforward Italian food, refined in taste and presentation.  Menu is just right - not too much and not too skimpy.  Don't come here with expectations of massive South Philly slop portions.  It's a PROPER serving of pasta.  Trust me, I like a big ol' bowl of carbload like the next person, but sometimes it's nice to not feel pressured to finish or have to take a doggy bag home (especially when it's a late dinner and you're going out somewhere immediately after).

With that said, next time I come, I'm ordering a ton of apps and wine for the table and going that route.  We started with the grilled artichoke, smoked ricotta/mushroom bruschetta and the arugula salad, and then each got the tagliatelle bolognese for entrees. Everything was absolutely delicious (although I will say the very tasty bite of artichoke was pretty small to be considered a shareable appetizer, so it left me wanting more). The arugula salad was perfect.  Our tagliatelles were dope and perfectly portioned.  I've never seen or tasted a bolognese of that variety, almost like a blush/cream vodka sauce. I said to my BF: "I mean this is the nicest way possible...this reminds me of Hamburger Helper."  But like ELEVATED.  If HH went to Cambridge and got all bougie.  Effin' delicious.

But we both agreed that the best part was the bruschetta...it was FANTASTIC.  Plus, they have a few different varieties to choose from and I want to go back to try them all.  My mouth was watering for it the next day, and still is.  In fact, it was so good, instead of dessert we ordered the buffalo mozzarella bruschetta AFTER our entrees cause we needed another taste. The mushroom one was oh so salty and smoky and the honey drizzle on mozzarella one was a delight.  Both  were creamy and crunchy - truly the perfect bite.  Would I classify it as "bruschetta"?  Probably not.  But a damn good appetizer nonetheless.

We paired our meals with really good red and white wine (the menu is expansive in this area) and plus, our server was on point even for the super busy Saturday night crowd.  Prices were reasonable for the quality of what you're getting.  Will definitely return!

You guys...I finally found it. Fries that held up during delivery. I didn't think it was possible. Plus DOPE sandwiches. Found my new favorite go-to when ordering through UberEats.

We ordered from here last week and are now officially hooked. BF ordered the "OMG" sandwich - chicken cutlet, tomato, mozzarella, pesto - and I'm pretty sure he definitely said "OMG" when he bit into it (but maybe with a few more curse words...like goddammit this sh*t is good, or something like that).

I got the "Mozzarella Bella" hoagie - fresh, homemade 'mootsarell' marinated in EVOO and topped with roasted red peppers.

Both were fantastic. Fresh AF hoagie rolls and MASSIVE in quantity. (We got the medium sized, which is their standard hoagie size, and was enough to split into 2 meals...all for only like $8-9).

Also got a side of waffle fries and they arrived wonderfully crispy and seasoned and hot (maybe waffle fries are the key to ordering fries to-go).

Then the following week we visited in-house since we were on the road. He got the OMG again cause he loved it so much, but I opted for the meatball parm sub. Holy hell, was that amazing. Those meatballs were like racquetballs. Huge, seasoned perfectly, and soft without being mushy. Gravy was nice, too.  Took a look around the shop when we were there and picked up some munchies. Had a gander at the freezer full of homemade pastas and soups and had to tear myself away from it before I bought it all.

Staff was super friendly, as well. I will absolutely be making this a regular spot when I've got a hankering for good subs.

What a fantastic experience outdoor dining here last Saturday!  Definitely make reservations if you have yet to experience the surreal, cozy joy that is heat lamp dining in the freezing cold on a city street (for the record, we were adequately TOASTY here, so much so I didn't wear my winter coat or scarf the entire meal and wished I didn't wear a sweater either). Get on down here!

Our server, Paul, was THE best.  Insanely knowledgable about the expansive wine list and the best pairings for each section of the menu, pacing our courses with calculated precision.  Plus, super friendly and attentive (especially considering servers have to cross the street in traffic to deliver our food!)

A breakdown:

The Sauce: started with two glasses of white, then moved on to a bottle of red (a lovely licorice-y bottle of Barbera, per Paul's recommendation)

The Starter: addicting, toasty & not shy of seasoning foccacia bread served piping hot in a mini cast iron skillet and served with delightful whipped bee pollen honey butter (can you eat this if you're allergic to bees, serious question) & an addition of silky farmer's cheese (I would literally go back just to order 5 these - bread lovers, REJOICE!)

The Small Plate: lovely, bitter chicory with a smattering of pistachios and a hefty dousing of a fresh and herby rose vinaigrette, topped with plump figs (very large portion for being labelled "small")

The Shareable Pastas: creamy duck ragu gramigna and lemony saffron calamaretti (that gamey duck won the battle, especially paired with the red, but that calamaretti was also fantastic)

The Sizable Entrees: peppery NY strip steak and a decadent roast suckling pig (wonderful crust on the steak but a *tiny* complaint is that the steak knives were not sharp at all, and that pig was 1000% worth the high cholesterol)

The Sweet(s): fried apple donut and a butterscotch gelato served with all the fixins' (this was 2desserts and we did not need 2desserts - it was excessive but worth every delicious bite)

It feels like you're in a fort, with a tall heat lamp and two smaller heat lamps ensconcing you in a warm, orange glow.  The street pavement itself was covered in some type of outdoor carpet and the clear plastic tents with a greenhouse assortment of hanging plants and strung lights, openings, and socially-distanced tables allowed both air flow and privacy, a must in these troubling times.

Will I be back? Hell yeah!

If not a good service , I would give zero to this place for the food with this prices ... 
hostess, waiter were good. 
That's it . 

We were 4 people , bill was over 200 ... plates were big , full of different junk which we even didn't eat , just tried , cause it looked messy not tasty, weird sauce on top of everything , we even didn't finish meat among this mess , mashed potato was awful in these entree . Lemon merengue desert was awful , I took one spoon and had to go to toilet to throw it away . Mussels were just okay , but after I had acid reflux, which I didn't have for many years .  I hate to write bad comment , but true is true .  Thank you , but no thank you . I'd rather eat pizza in Sauce .

Service was great! Food was ok. The Mac and cheese was made with a slice of American singles....I think they should try a little harder than that. It is definitely over priced. The lighting is terrible, extremely bright. It also smells like partical board.

This is was my hidden treasure until Yelp came along. I can't say anything bad about Kitchen 519. Taste like service is subjective. We've been fortunate to have both excellent service and food.  I go in I want to try their brunch menu and I always get Fish and Chips. Tempura battered with hand cut fries. Served with malt vinegar aioli and spicy ketchup. Jeez!! So good. Try the brunch, hit me up and let me know how it was. I'm sticking to the Fish and Chips. Recommend.

*forgot to post back in March 2013

such great food! Went here for my 1year anniversary with my boyfriend, and we were so happy with our choice in restaurant! 

They have a great craft beer selection. Being from Louisville, KY we stuck with Nashville craft beers. So good!!

Fried pickle appetizer was hands down THE BEST fried pickles I've ever had!! They're cut real thin and long ways, coated in a light batter and topped with a white BBQ sauce that is to die for! For dinner he had fried chicken (juiciest ever) with mashed potatoes and greens. I had the Kale Slaw (kale, apple, goat cheese, candied pecan and honey vinegarette) with bacon Mac and cheese. The Mac and cheese was the cheesiest I've ever had, and that salad was beyond! It had great textures and the sour note from the goat cheese really added a pinch to my salad! 

For dessert we got the "flight" which showcased 4 mini desserts: bread pudding, buttermilk pie, banana pudding and chocolate mousse/pudding something. They came in mini mason jars (cute!!)

Presentation of the food was totally on point, and taste was amazing. Price was fair for what you're getting. 

From the outside of the place you wouldn't think it would be as nice and beautiful as it is on the inside. Next time we visit Nashville we are DEFINITELY coming back to The Row!

The Cheesecake Factory used to be my favorite chain restaurant to go too when I was living in South Jersey. I frequently dined there until I moved further out into Delaware. IDK if I can even speak for it the same now. Maybe it's just the location?

The wait is usually long. Very dreadful on the weekends. Sometimes the pager doesn't work and I get irritated with annoyance to the hostess. Some days you're in luck with great service and other times you're shrugged off the shoulder while they continue to chit chat. Especially in the dessert finishing area. 

IDK why I keep coming here knowing that they are not consistent in their service, portions, and as well as taste. Like I've mentioned before... Maybe it's just this location. Anyways, no longer interested in eating here and if I do, it's only to grab cheesecakes on the go. Enough said.

Finally came here for the first time even after living in Philly for over 10 years. Tried many places besides the typical Pat's & Geno's (they don't count)! All I have to say is sorry. Why? I refuse to follow with the hype on their Cheesesteaks. Not saying I hate it that bad.

Just way too overly crowded in such a small confined space. Even when calling in your order ahead of time, you must check in with the counter when arriving before they start on yours. So I'm squeezing my tiny self while waiting nearly over 40 minutes. Customers are getting impatient with attitudes and employees are arguing behind the counter. You're also better finding luck for parking in a residential area than you would find seating. I mean there's a few tables and chairs outside, but it's a cold winter day. Plus it's a Cash Only establishment, but at least there's an ATM by the door. 

Took the Cheesesteak to my car and took a few bites. The meat was too minced to my liking and I ate more largely chopped onions than I did of the meat. I wished they would melted the cheese a bit over the griddle instead on laying it on the roll first. Gave the rest to my boyfriend and he liked it. Can't blame him because he eats anything. So I give Dalessandro's a solid 3 Stars.

I'm pretty sure a lot of Delawarean commuters can't help but notice a large blue sign that is attention grabbing with the three simple letter word that says "EAT". Shoot, I'm even guilty for driving on the opposite side and bussed a quick U-Turn to dine in. Now don't let the swarming of cars out in the lot intimidate you. It's particularly busy on most days, but you'll get seated. 

This is my go too spot for an inexpensive meal if you're ever in the mood for Tex-Mex/Cajun. Enjoy complimentary chips and salsa as you skim through the menu. I experimented most of the dishes here and can never seem to utter a bad word about it. I love the Pastelitos as starters though. They are nice, hot, and flaky filled with chicken-cilantro and comes with a chime verde  sauce. Entrees, I usually switch it up every visit. However, the sides I tend to stick with the Jambalaya and their twist of sliced Avocado (Delicious as it is grilled and filled). Kind of a whimper that they do not offer desserts though.

My parents are frequent regulars here since they've opened back in '98. With me and my annoying baby brother just tagging along of course. Until this day, two decades later, I still walk into this place, just not holding hands with mama or papa. I've pretty much seen it gone through evolution. 

This is basically an all Vietnamese grab and quick on the go spot. It used to be a Pho joint too, but they're no longer servicing that. Many Banh-Mi's options with different fillings/toppings, drinks, desserts, and platters. Over time, some of the items deteriorate in flavors and quality, especially their cold desserts which I no longer purchase. Banh-Mi's are ok, can't consider them my favorite from here. However, I do like their Banh Tet (rice cake), but overly priced at $16 each. Besides that, their hot foods are decent.

Place can get crazy hecked and you got to go through a battle to get to the register because these customers in here are something else. Prices can be decent, but knowing myself, I always buy more than what I need. Parking is tight, yes even in a plaza depending on the time and day, but you're bound to find an empty spot.

My surprise birthday dinner was held here on a Saturday evening. Upon arrival, I wish the Hostess(es) would extend one's hand with proper greetings because I didn't receive any of that. First impressions does make a difference! However, my waitress was decent enough to get us through the night. Slow service though. 

Starters
-Freshly Shucked Oysters on the Half Shell
Quite a few selections to choose from. If you don't know your oysters, they do have a chart that provides brief information and details. 
-Hot Crab & Artichoke Dip. Not the best I've had. They came with sourdough croutons. If I had known, I would have saved the complimentary bread to use for dipping. They are more to happy to serve you more if you ask for it.

Entree
-Harry's Award Winning PRIME RIB AU JUS. I went with the 12 oz Grill Cut cooked medium. Alongside with Exotic Mushrooms. Definitely the highlight of the experience. It was cooked just right and both very good. 

Dessert
-Creme Brûlée
-Apple Crisp
Everything is made in house.

This place usually gets filled up pretty quickly so I suggest making reservations beforehand. For my first time being here, I rate it a solid 3 Stars. I had higher expectations out of Harry's, but it left me a little disappointed. As a lot of people I know rave about this restaurant. However, I will return back just for the Prime Rib. Hopefully service would be better as well.

I've been carrying on a mission to come try out Mango Mango over a  period of time now. All my family ever do is keep on raving about it over and over and over again. So much that it has became my main priority that if I ever land my two little feet in Chinatown, I would make the extra effort to stop by this place and judge it for myself.

Little did you know, that day has finally happened! Arrived here on a beaming hot Saturday afternoon and the place was already filled up. Yes it was scorching outside, so what a way to treat yourself to a chill delight. The only negative thing I can say about my experience was narrowing down to what I really wanted to try. 

My Mister and I decided to get the Strawberry Mango Juice Sago with Rice Ball & Ice Cream. Also, the Mango Strawberry Slush. The portion seemed small, but decent enough to share. Both were delicious. My favorite part was the mango ice cream indeed. Service was great and our overall experience here was good. Seriously can't wait to go back.

I came here solely based off of the photos and reviews. They were good enough to lure me into thinking that this place would be promising. Being that this establishment is relatively new, I had expectations.

After being seated, I was given a menu with NO markings. So I'm thinking to myself like wow, this place has some items that local Vietnamese eateries does not. Yes, I got a bit excited. Sadly to my disappointment, I've failed three times while attempting to place my orders because they no longer offered those dishes. The waiter got impatient and handed me a menu with crossed out items. 

In the end, I eventually got a bowl of Bun Bo Hue. The broth was not flavorful nor fragrant to what I'm used too. It really lacks in the spicy department because there was ZERO heat. Not even a hint of kick. Meat selections were decent though. The only thing that my family and I enjoyed from this dine in experience was their complimentary infused water and the egg rolls we ordered as appetizers. 

This Pho joint does has potential. It would be considerate if they printed out new menus. Also work on having better customer service. Other than that, I don't think I'll be returning.

Celebrating my love and & I anniversary and a change of career path, I decided to spontaneously opted a reservation for two at none other than, Barclay Prime. It was one of the most finest dining experience we've ever encountered thus far. Which eventually leaves a mark for another return. 

I honestly didn't care too much with the ambiance that carried a library theme and a very dimmed setting. A few chit chatters as we're surrounded by large parties. However, not enough to ruin the intimate atmosphere. Comfy seating and marble topped candle lite tables. Great service and staff all around.

-Complimentary Popped Over Bread with butter. 
-Wagyu Slider's. For appetizers, they are most amazing little pop of juiciness and burst of flavor. 
-Jumbo Lump Crabcake. Not the best I've had and wouldn't reorder again. 
-Barclay Prime Cheesesteak. When you take a moment and think to yourself if you would ever pay $120 for a sandwich and for a Philly Cheesesteak at that. Go for it! I can't describe in full detail, but this was one of the best things I've ever eaten in my life. Worth the tastebuds... And it also comes with half a bottle of champagne. Winning.
-Lemon & Vanilla Bean Creme Brûlée - Amazing as the sweet and tart compliments well with one another. 

Overall, everything was superior.

Don't know where to start.  How about how slow food come out, even when there were only a few other folks in the restaurant.  Went twice and both times and was extremely slow.

We have asked for water refill, the lady comes back with a nice full pitcher, but only refills one glass.  Could pay more attention to the surrounding.  Have asked for Hot water, a hot water pot came out, but no hot water cup to go with it...

The food taste was a bit above average for Thai places around the South NJ area, but the price and portion is pretty bad.  The price set for most items on the menu could be prices if the restaurant was located in a big city. 

Update: 

See my photo that was attached on how the owner also responded back to me on my review.  My review is not for you... but the Yelp community.  If i wanted your business to do badly, I wouldn't have given you an above average on taste.  Service/Presentation is just as important, and also how you treat others.  With that said.. I am dropping my review to a 1. You are very welcome!

Killer find near our hotel. All of the normal boring dishes and tons of unique choices on your favorite breakfast foods. Feel free to have bacon and eggs but I enjoyed my chicken, egg white and artichoke hash. Lots to choose from if you are a breakfast lover. Good service, good coffee, indoor and outdoor seating if you come during one of the few nice weather weeks here. Hahahaha.

I had the pleasure of dining with the owner of my company on a trip to Nashville. He wanted me to Fina place walking distance with live music. When I showed him the pictures of the food and told him there was NO music, he still wanted to eat here. 

Service was excellent throughout and the ambiance was classy, quiet but not stuffy. All Covid protocols were in place and we felt quite safe eating here. 

Classic cocktails and unique appetizers got us started. They are well known for their roasted cauliflower and it did not disappoint. Served with three different sauces...it was wonderful. They also have a unique twist on their bruschetta and we enjoyed that, as well.

While the boss man had the veal and mushroom meatballs, I had a fresh fish special served over gnocchi. 

It was really a delicious meal.

During Covid, this area is really quiet but you can find live music in many places up and down the street. We wanted good local food and a much quieter meal so The Stillery was perfect. Excellent service, a diverse menu and spread out tables. 

I had a local canned IPA which was excellent, as well as a Maker's Mark, neat. Good way to start the night. My buddy and I split a plate of fried pickled chips. We may have finished about 1/4 of the huge plate. Delicious but how many pickles can one guy eat? The chop chop salad was also huge. Quite good but I was not a fan of the dressing. Their famous dish is a flaming hot skillet of mac n cheese, topped with hot chicken. I had never heard of hot chicken but it's basically sliced chicken breast seasoned like buffo wings. Amazing dish. Eve the mild version was quite spicy. The mac n cheese was just perfect, too. This spot was exactly what we were looking for.

We've been here thrice now, and I can't say enough nice things about it. The first time we went just because, and I enjoyed it so much that I couldn't wait to go back. The food here, to me, is next level pub style. The menu is varied with a lot of cool items mixed in (a burger with grilled cheese buns?!) to make it almost too hard to choose... Almost. 

I ordered the fish and chips, which is dicey since most "pubs" can never seem to get it right. It was outstanding! Lightly battered and tender as it should be. The fries were tossed in vinegar and sea salt... I'd probably eat a a whole plate of just the fries. I'm not a huge beer drinker, but they always have something on the board that intrigues me. 

We've also been to their Sunday brunch. Chicken and waffles, bloody mary, and live music. How can you go wrong?

My only complaint is that coming south on 309 makes it a bit difficult to get into the parking lot, but it's worth it once you get there. Every server we've had has been friendly, and every meal has been great. Will be back soon... maybe this weekend!

Chef's kiss for Latea. 

I am a big tea drinker. So, when I visit places dedicated to serving tea, I become exceedingly happy. Latea serves hot tea (the kind I prefer), but they also offer cold tea drinks, including boba tea, aka bubble tea. I do like a boba every now and again, but because I was visiting on a cold, slushy, winter day, I chose a cup of hot French Lemon Ginger, which was decaffeinated and freshly brewed. The kind woman behind the counter told me that French Lemon Ginger is one of their most popular flavors.

I should mention that I was visiting Latea because it was the place to pick up the Yelpie award that I won (Trailblazer of the Year!). So thanks, Yelp, for making me travel a half hour to pick up my award, so that I could discover Latea. I got a free lemon tart when I picked up my award, but I purchased the tea with my own cash-money because I just had to get some tea. How could I not? The menu of tea is so vast and tantalizing.

Latea also sells little nibbly things to eat with your tea, like delicate shortbread and sable cookies, madelienes and the like. They also sell coffee and smoothies, so I'll have to come back and try those.

If you're visiting on a Sunday, parking is free! Otherwise, you will have to pay for street parking, because Latea is located on Mass Ave where parking is at a premium.

I'm not even exaggerating a little bit when I say that these are the best donuts in Indianapolis. 

You see, I am a donut fiend, and I try every donut when possible. I've eaten a lot of donuts in Indy. Pana Donuts are it. These are the donuts. It sucks that they are so far away, though -- past Beech Grove and almost to Southport. But, I will drive to Pana to get their donuts, because they are worth the drive. 

My go-to donut when I'm trying a new donut joint is the glazed twist. It's a simple donut, but it's easy to get it wrong. Pana got it so right. It was fluffy, soft and fresh (even though we visited in the afternoon!), glazed and chewy yet had a slight give at the ends. It was a perfect glazed twist. I don't even know what else to say to you guys except you need to go to Pana and get some donuts.

So, I got a glazed twist, and my husband got a Boston eclair that he said was "beautiful." Who even says that about donuts? My kids got a strawberry iced sprinkle donut and a vanilla iced sprinkle donut. Now, my kids love donuts but they almost never finish their donuts. But these donuts? They ate them all. 

Pana labels all their donuts in the display case, so you know what they all are and can easily order what you want. I don't know why more donut places don't do this. All the donuts are arranged neatly and everything is visually pleasing.
