It's just a great donut shop all around, and I think other people agree because at least 10 people came in and ordered during the short time we were there.

If you eat nothing else here, you need to eat the tres leches cake. Chuy's has the best tres leches that I've ever had, and I've had a lot of tres leches from some hardcore Mexican establishments. This is the tres leches to end tres leches. It will satisfy your soul.

So now that you've had the most important part of any meal (dessert), the next thing you must eat is the queso. Now, I'm not a big queso person, because queso in Indiana is usually white and watery. But Chuy's queso is perfectly orange and housemade -- the cheese is balanced perfectly by the chiles that are added, which give it a nice kick.

You'll need something to wash down all that sugar and cheese, so you should naturally order a margarita. The lime juice is squeezed fresh here (no
mixes), so I suggest the house margarita on the rocks. It's not too sweet, and you can really taste the lime. If you're not into lime, they have a mean watermelon margarita. (Yes, I tried both, because por que no los dos!) 

I could make a meal on those three things alone, but if you want "food" food, I suggest ordering something with sauce, like an enchilada. In fact, order the tomatillo enchiladas, because that sauce is bomb. I had the pleasure of talking to the owner during my visit, and he let me know that they make all of their sauces from scratch. From scratch! They also make their tortillas from scratch, which I tasted when I ordered a chicken quesadilla. You can really tell the difference when you eat a quesadilla made with a housemade tortilla. 

This restaurant is super family friendly, and there are lots of tchotchkes and art on the walls to look at. They have this game going where they've hidden a bunch of tiny dogs everywhere, and kids are encouraged to find them. Speaking of dogs: If you bring in a framed photo of your dog, they will hang it on their wall! That's so great.

If you build a restaurant with a playground outside, the parents will come. I mean, it worked for me! I had to drive 30 minutes to get to Baby's during rush hour traffic, but the promise of a restaurant where I could relax and get a meal and a drink, and where my kids could just play while I relax and get meal and a drink, was too good to pass up. Have you ever been a parent? Do you know how hard it is to take a child to a restaurant and actually have a good time? If so, then you would agree with me that Baby's has the right idea: create a kid-friendly, family-friendly place to relax, play and eat a meal. Offer good food. And that's it, really -- that's all you need to do, and the parents will come.

So, they have a little playground on astroturf that's accessible from the patio seating. Parents: Opt for the patio seating and don't worry if it's cold outside, because Baby's has outdoor heaters that will keep you warm.  

They also have magnetic tables and magnetic tiles that kids can play with. I love it! My kids spent most of their time building houses (when they weren't playing on the playground), and pretty much zero time complaining to me that they were bored. Yes! More time for me to actually enjoy my meal.

I ordered the regular smash burger, and I was able to customize it how I wanted. They have things like grilled onions and pickled jalapeños, so of course I got both. We got our fries "glitzed up" and ordered them Talbott Street Style: They came topped with white cheese sauce, bacon bits, white bbq sauce and pickled jalapeños. 

I also ordered the vegan milkshake, and the flavor of the day was key lime, so of course I got that. It was delicious and fabulously tart, but be aware that it is way thinner in consistency than a dairy shake because it is made with coconut cream. I got the boozy shake, but honesty, I couldn't even tell it had any booze in it! (Does that say more about me and my liver or the way Baby's makes their boozy shakes -- who knows?!) Next time, I will save money and just get the vegan shake without booze. 

The showstopper of the evening was the Sriracha Broccoli Slaw. I am seriously thinking about getting more as I write this review, because it was excellent. I highly recommend getting the slaw here!

The service was top-notch, too. Our server was very knowledgeable about everything on the menu, and he was very attentive and friendly. We had a great time and we will definitely be back again.

I had high expectations for The Cake Bake Shop. That was my first problem. But how can four stars and nearly 420 reviews be wrong?! Oh, they can be wrong.

Let me start by saying that we got the berry cheesecake and the Million Dollar cake. They were both in the $12 to $14 per slice range. They were both delicious. Were they worth $12 to $14 per slice? Not at all. Let me tell you why in this rambling, semi-coherent diatribe. 

Now. I am not a conspiracy theorist at all, but I have a conspiracy forming about The Cake Bake Shop after visiting their establishment and eating my slices of cake. My theory is that they raise the price of their food and make you wait (and wait, and wait ... more on that later) in order to build up a false idea that they are better and more exclusive than they really are. They want to be that place that sells you $14 slices of cake and makes you wait 25 minutes for it. Because if they are that place that people will wait 25 minutes for a slice of $14 cake, then they are on top. 

If you've been here, then you probably know that my mentioning a 25 minute wait for a slice of cake is not an exaggeration. I've talked to several people since my visit, and every single person has confirmed that they, too, have waited an exorbitant amount of time for a to-go order of dessert. So, we waited 25 minutes for two slices of cake. Everyone in the shop with us waited at least as long as us. There was a whole mob of people, just like us, standing around waiting for someone -- anyone -- to hand us our desserts. Maybe one of the two hostesses (yes, there are two hostesses)? Maybe one of the six (yes, six) people behind the counter could, perhaps, pitch in and start putting orders in the boxes? We saw one guy not move, at all, the entire time we were there. He was standing behind the counter just ... I don't know. Contemplating? It became a running joke to see if he would move before we left. He didn't. He stayed, not moving or doing anything, behind the counter for almost a half hour. 

What made the wait even more frustrating is that all of the cakes are right there, in the display cases, waiting to be cut and delivered to waiting customers. I'm not quite sure what kind of system The Cake Bake Shop has going, or if they even have a system. It looked utterly chaotic behind the counter, with several people standing around but not doing anything to actually fulfill the orders. I feel like they wanted to make people wait, so that a line would form out the door, so that passersby would look at the store and be like, "Wow, this place is really popular! It must be great! We need to check it out." 

So 25 minutes later, we got our two slices of cake to go. No silverware was offered. I ate my cake with my fingers in a car speeding down College Avenue like the animal that I am. Like I said, the cakes were delicious, but not worth $14 and 25 minutes of my time. This was the first and last time that I'll visit.

I've walked right by this restaurant countless times and never saw it. It's hiding in plain sight! So if you're like me and are sometimes blind to things that are right in front of you, The Pint Room is located in the Carmel Arts & Design District, near Main and 1st Street. 

They posted a photo on their Instagram of a delicious-looking tuna burger that I needed to make mine, so I did. Good job, whoever is doing The Pint Room's social media! You made me visit because of a good photo. The fish burger was only on the menu for a short time (for the Lent season), so I made haste.

The burger was great! I had only ever eaten the flaked kind of tuna that comes in a can that you use to make a tuna sandwich, so this was an unusual (but delightful) experience. It had a spicy aioli sauce, red onions and lettuce.

My husband got the cheeseburger, and he said it was amazing. My kids enjoyed their sliders, too. The kids sliders that come in the kids meal are relatively big, and there are two of them. They come with your choice of a side and a drink.

Because we're still living through a pandemic, we decided to get our food to go. There were a lot of people dining in, but very few at the bar. But the tables were spaced well enough apart. Once things get back to normal, I'd love to come here again and eat in the restaurant and get one of the many beers they have on tap. They have lots of local beers and other good things to drink.

This is a family-owned, family-run Mexican restaurant, and the food tastes like it came straight out of a Mexican grandma's kitchen. It's really, really good, people. I can always tell how much care is put into Mexican food from the beans. If the beans taste good and fresh, that's a good sign. And these beans taste homemade. 

Bugambilias serves up specialties that are unique to their family (like Mexican spaghetti!) and recipes that originate from Puebla, Mexico. So you will see things on the menu like mole, mixiotes (a barbecued meat dish), tortas and more. But they also serve Tex-Mex, so you can get enchiladas, burritos, fajitas, tacos, queso and other Mexican favorites. Chips and salsa are served complimentary, and the chips come out nice and warm. 

Whenever I see mole on a menu, I must order it, so that's what I got. Holy mole! (Get it?) It was delicious. It comes served over skin-on chicken thighs and a pork rib, as well as rice and refried beans and corn tortillas. The mole was dark and slightly sweet and just perfect.

My husband got the mixiotes -- you can choose either chicken or beef, so he chose beef. His dish was a little more spicy, and it came with charro beans, corn tortillas and either rice or Mexican spaghetti. We had never had Mexican spaghetti before, so of course that's what we had to get! Apparently, this is their family recipe, and it's creamy and warm and comforting. If you like spaghetti, you should take a chance and try it.

They have a kids menu with several items to choose from, including non-Mexican things like cheeseburgers (of course, one of my children had to get a burger. Children -- what are you gonna do?) My other child got a bean, rice and cheese burrito, and he said he loved it. Kids meals come with a choice of side: fries, beans or rice.

The service here is excellent and very friendly. The family is in the kitchen and serving in the dinning room, and at one point the cook came out from the kitchen to ask how we liked our food. (We loved it!) 

I love when restaurants do something different and do it well. Especially in Indianapolis, where Mexican food can all kind of taste the same, Bugambilias is cooking food that you can tell comes from the heart.

This is one of those instances where I wish Yelp allowed for halfsies with the star ratings. Wahlburgers is a solid 3.5 stars. The food is good, but it's not unlike what you can find at other burger restaurants around Carmel and Indy. 

I visited for a lunch date with my husband, and we got there right when they opened at 11 a.m. We were seated right away, and we chose a seat at the bar because it was just us two. I feel like we were attended to faster at the bar -- I noticed that we got our food before some of the people who got there before us who were sitting in the booths. So, if you're dining in and you're in a hurry, you might want to consider the bar.

We both got The Our Burger, which is a basic single-patty burger with cheese and condiments. The burger is cooked in a smash burger-style, so it's nice and thin. The burgers come with a Classic Side, which is fries or tater tots, but we were feeling supremely decadent that day and chose to upgrade to thin crispy onion rings, which is a Signature Side. The thin onion rings is the side that has the fewest calories on the menu, so people who are counting calories and want a side: consider the thin onion rings.

The burger was great, the thin onion rings were great, and the service was fine. But it cost around $40 with tip for two The Our Burgers, onion rings and water. I don't have a Dirk Diggler lifestyle, so if I'm going to pay that much for a burger lunch in Indiana (without booze), it needs to be better than the burger place down the road where I can pay half as much and be just as satisfied. 

Wahlburgers is still drawing crowds and lines, so if you're interested in visiting, I suggest getting there on a weekday when they open.

I joined a group of 6 for dinner over the past weekend.  A friend reserved an outdoor igloo which is perfect for people with Covid concerns.

Service was excellent.  Our waitress was prompt and checked in frequently.

I ordered the Parker House Rolls for my app and the wedge salad for my entree and both were very good. We were also given a chefs tasting which was also tasty.

We took advantage of the Yelp Check In Offer and scored a round of champagne for the table.

Unfortunately I was full of bread so I didn't have a chance to induldge in dessert.  I guess that gives me a reason to visit again

I came across Maryanne's on Yelp while searching for a new breakfast spot a few weeks back.  It's in a strip mall and is easy to pass without noticing.  During our first visit on a Saturday morning the place was packed and had a 30+ minute wait so we left.  We tried again on a Friday morning assuming it would be a little easier to get a table during the week.  It was still crowded but luckily we were able to get a table right away.

We were hungry so we over ordered slightly.  We ordered the breakfast sandwich with home fries, loaded potatoes (ham, cheese, spinach, prosciutto and more) and the stuffed French toast.  The food was delish especially the potatoes!  My only complaint is that the French toast is not actually stuffed its layered with cream cheese.

I would like to visit again to try some of their other options.

I stopped her around Christmas time with a party of 4.  There was only a couple and a small child inside when we arrived.  The lack of patrons made me worry we made a bad decision but boy was I wrong!

The food is excellent.  During this visit I got to try the Lamb Tikka Masala, Curry Chicken and mango chicken and they were delish!  To pair with the entree I ordered both the classic naan and garlic naan. My only compliant regarding the food was the entree portion.  The rest of my party was "full" but I could definitely enjoy more.  I can be a bit greedy though...

The waitress was nice but very timid. Service was a tad slow considering we were one of the few guests there.  

I intend of coming back again soon!

I stopped here for brunch this morning after finding it on Yelp.  The restaurant is tucked away in an apartment complex which so you can easily drive by without even realizing it's there. 

Once you find it there is plenty of free off street parking.

The dining area is relatively small which may be an issue during peak dining times but we were greeted and seated by the hostess immediately upon entering.  The friendly hostess also doubles as the waitress.

Food was served promptly-I don't think we waited more than 15 mins.  I ordered the Huevos Rancheros which consists of eggs, potatoes, cheese and quac between corn tortillas.  Portion sizes were perfect and the food was very flavorful.  My bf ordered the churros pancakes which were absolutely decadent.  So sweet and rich it almost felt like you were eating a dessert.  The fresh fruit was and added bonus and makes you feel a little less guilty having dessert for breakfast.  

I left full and satisfied.  I absolutely plan on visiting again to try there dinner menu items!

The only information you need to know about Stocks is that they offer one of the best, if not the best pound cake in Philadelphia.  Their pound cake is available in chocolate, vanilla or both and in loaves or rounds.  You can also have your choice of chocolate or vanilla icing.  Regardless of the combo you will not be disappointed.  I prefer the round cake with vanilla icing because you get more icing on the round cakes than you do loaves.  If you do stop in I recommend picking up some of their cookies as well.

what can I say about this place that isn't already said? 
This has become a mainstay of Philly dining in the time of Covid 19. But here is why I keeeeeep coming back...

You know when you're on the couch and want to eat a huge bowl of cheezy pasta? But you end up making a ton of it and you feel ashamed of the amount of pasta you have to now eat all alone. And it's so good you don't share. --This is that food. This is the food you see on TV and tell yourself "I'm going to go to Sicily. I'm going to drink wine in the Mediterranean. I'm going to Be Mama Mia!" This is the kind of food that makes you wish the restrictions were gone, and you could gather a bunch of friends and share alike. I have been here a few times and the take out orders really hold up. I mean it's a fairly long ride home, and it's legit. 
I am impressed fully but the level of talent is this restaurant.

One of our favorite places in between home and Santa Barbara.  Love the setting, the menu is great casual beach fare, and prices are fair.  Our visit yesterday was half disappointing, though.

Dear Hubby had an island blonde lager on draft that tasted harsh like the cheap beer we used to drink in college.  Not a winner.

His teriyaki burger was delicious, and I was grateful to be able to sample a few bites of the sweet/tangy flavors.  We had also ordered a side Caesar salad and chili nachos to share.

Thumbs up on the simple Caesar, dressed up with some fresh cherry tomatoes, croutons, and grated Parmesan.  I'd order it again as a counterpoint to heavier fare.

Unfortunately, though we've had stellar nachos here before, yesterday's version looked and tasted largely pre-made, with only the guacamole, sour cream, and salsa added before serving.  Beans were dried out, and cheese already starting to harden.

On the plus side, the staff was friendly and helpful, and we snagged a spot reminiscent of a tropical get-away, under lush greenery.

We'll be back, but will probably not order nachos.

Maybe I should have been an ugly Cougar in a tight fitting dress because the table of two who arrived half an hour after we ordered got their food before we did and the manager/owner sure as hell paid a lot more attention to them than he did to my table. They even got a couple of glasses of sparkling rosé because as the waiter said, "(muffled dudes name) would love for you to to have another drink with us."

Instead, we were a table of four who waited an hour and a half for our entrees to come out. I know that there are reviews out there saying that they take their time to prepare dinner but an hour and a half is absolutely ridiculous and absolutely unacceptable. 

The worst part was, the food wasn't good. Okay. Some of it was. The alligator/crawfish gumbo was the best we had this trip to New Orleans. Maybe that isn't saying much but I really enjoyed it. Even the pork belly appetizer was okay but dry (dry pork belly, I mean you have to hate the food to do that). That's about it. 

We ordered the stuffed soft shelled crab which was bland and uninspired, the scallops were super salty. Yes, I know they are blackened, they were still not good. And the tomahawk pork chops that everybody was raving about? Holy crap, they were raw and overcooked at the same time!  I don't usually send food back but the chef must despise his customers to do this. 

Because it was my dad's birthday, we ordered the creme brulee which might be the best part of the meal. I take that back, second best. The best part was leaving. The experience started off promising but ultimately ended up being super disappointing considering the occasion this was supposed to be the highlight meal of the trip. 

Run away, unless you're an ugly cougar with cellulite hanging out of the bottom of a too tight dress. Then, by all means, this is the spot for you.

It seems they don't even want you to be there. There's actually a sign outside, that I hope is tongue-in-cheek, about how they don't want to deal with you. 

It's also way overpriced!  The food is good, but not exquisite or all that plentiful. For $30, you get a piece of fish with beans and slaw.

I would not go back.

I had to look at my last review and wonder why it was not a 5-star experience. Many meals and my own maturity later, I'm giving Gran Caffe L'Aquila the rightful ratings boost it deserves.

I love sitting upstairs. It's a pleasant, cozy place to dine with plenty of natural light. 

They have plenty of fantastic Italian dishes but my favorites are the savory gelato and pasta combos. I love the Carbonara and the agnolotti al tartufo. Truly unique and equally delicious.

Service is always charming and professional. I love ordering Italian wines I don't know much about and relying on their accurate descriptions.

Their gelato brings out the closeted dessert appreciate in me. Today's pick was tiramisu and caffe. They hit the spot without being overly filling.

Gran Caffe has become one of my Philly favorites and a place I'd proudly recommend for anyone in Philly looking for a great Italian meal.

Little Pete's was a go-to prior to the pandemic and is now my go-to lifesaver. 

I don't even know how many times I've gotten delivery from them the past few months, and I will continue to support them as long as I can.

I usually customize an omelette: turkey bacon, American cheese and broccoli with mashed potatoes instead of home fries (or French fries later in the day). Did I mention they serve breakfast all day? It doesn't get much better than that.

The other day I was feeling ambitious and also added the Manhattan clam chowder and a grilled cheese. The grilled cheese came with a pickle and bag of chips.

I can't close out this review without mentioning their awesome staff. The staff who answers the phone is always polite and friendly. The delivery is always quick and the food comes hot. 

During this season of gratitude, I want to publicly declare how grateful I am for Little Pete's.

I learned two things today.

1) Dalessandro's sells gift certificates.

2) I have no willpower to pick up a gift certificate without ordering my own cheesesteak.

I ran out over my lunch break and wasn't sure what to expect in terms of crowds however I was easily able to find parking on Wendover Street. Once inside I saw that several of the counter seats were occupied, and there were about 5 people waiting on line to place and pick up their orders. Within a minute or so I was able to place my order. I really just wanted to pick up a gift certificate but figured that when in Rome...

So glad I did! I'm no Dalessandro's first-timer but I forgot how good the steaks are. My cheesesteak with American cheese, banana pepper, sweet pepper and raw onion hit the spot! The meat is chopped finely, just the way I like it. The hoagie roll is large and was stuffed to the brim with cheesesteak goodness. Taking my sandwich to go, the whole experience must have taken 10 minutes max. No regrets from this girl on today's lunch. 

As far as the great cheesesteak debate goes, Dalessandro's definitely is up amongst Philly's finest! I honestly don't eat cheesesteaks enough and have never done a side by side comparision, but they'd make my short list if I had to make a recommendation.

Okay, so I learned one more thing. Their beer selection goes well beyond what is listed on their menu. They have an awesome 6 pack selection including Flying Fish Exit 4, Troeggs and Leinenkugel and other craft options. I had to pass on the beer since it was my lunch hour, but I can see many good pairings for the future.

Fourth and final lesson of the day- it's cash only, kids. 

Happy steaking!

Do you want to hear a secret? Maybe I shouldn't even put this in writing? Maybe you already know this one and are about to laugh at me, but....

Go to a brunch place during non-brunch hours! Ingenious, right? 

So I ended up at Honey's Sit 'n Eat last week with my husband and a friend. We had been across the street at Ten Stone with Honey's just staring us in the face and calling our names. So we wandered across the street sometime in the 4 o'clock hour. 

We were greeted and seated right away. Now I was a newbie to Honey's, but this wasn't my first brunch rodeo. I've heard the hype about this place and couldn't image that ever happening in the prime of brunch time on a Sunday morning. 

The solid service continued. Although they were closing around 5, but never felt rushed or unwanted. 

I went with the breakfast quesadilla which consisted of scrambled eggs, cheddar and pepper jack cheeses served with refried beans, pico de gallo and avocado sour cream sauce. I opted for an additional avocado and it was like half an avocado. You could tell the quesadilla was freshly made with a nice tortilla and the eggs were recently scrambled. My only grip was that there really wasn't much of the beans, pico or avocado sour cream. They were almost hidden under one piece of quesadilla. The extra avocado was a clutch addition. 

They don't take credit card but they have an ATM on premise. 

I had a quick and tasty experience, and would definitely return at a similar odd hour. Sunday morning brunch is so last year. Sunday late afternoon brunch is where it's at.

Destination Dogs is actually a destination. Having only read (stalked) the menu previously, I was a little taken back to see what a formal establishment it was. There was a host, a formally dressed server to go with the table service and candlelight. And here I thought I was just going to a hotdog shop with a bar. 

Having a gator obsession, I had to go with the Andouille Armstrong, which was a combined gator-shrimp hotdog with cabbage, tomatoes, jalapeno remoulade, scallions and a lemon wedge on top. My husband went with the Hebrew Hammer, which included a beef hotdog topped with potato latkes, onion and mustard. 

After placing our order, it took a really long time for our food to come out. During that time, we second guessed the portion size and if we needed a side or appetizer. We also contemplated a beer, although we really weren't there to drink that night. These are gourmet dogs, but is the wait warranted? Apparently, not. Without a single complaint and complete patience on our part, our server took 50% off our check at the end of the meal and told us this wasn't the normal timetable. Phew, that's a relief. 

So our food came and our side second guessing was laid to rest. This was not your tiny wiener from a hotdog stand. We had before us sausage sandwiches. I'm in the camp that the insides make the meal, but that luscious, toasty roll made a great thing even better.  Bonus points for each dog coming with a small side of chips. 

The gator was no NOLA gator, but still really tasty nonetheless.  Between a hearty dog, a stellar roll and fun toppings, the Andouille Armstrong was a wiener...I mean winner. 

I'm so intrigued by so many of the fun hotdog combinations and meats (kangaroo, I'm looking at you, mate!) Their beer list had a few brews that caught my eye to warrant an elongated visit. 

As their name eludes, this chain knows what it takes to be a destination hotdog spot that can be fun, intriguing and a place you'd want to hang around for longer than it would normally take it eat a hotdog.

While I wasn't enamored by my total experience at Tired Hands Fermentaria, I was enamored by their beer. While overall experience is important, sometimes having good beer can trump everything else.

During my visit my husband and I sampled 4 ounce pours of everything single beer they had on tap, which equated to 11 beers total. Standouts included the "Whatever, Nevermind," "Alien Church," "Punge," "Season of Perception" and "Altar." Their list was a little IPA/saison heavy, but there was something for every taste on draft. Of the 11 beers I tried, I gave 9 of them a four rating or higher on Untapped. It was a deliciously good time. 

While we were having 4 ounce pours, we weren't able to order flights. It was a little irritating that we had to order one drink at a time per person. It would have been nice to strategically order our beers in groupings larger than two. Prices for each 4 ounce pour were decently.

It was the growler of "Whatever, Nevermind" that was hefty at about $30. They also have a policy where all beer must be sold in their growlers. You can trade your growler in for theirs at no additional charge. I didn't have any personal attachment to my growler, but that could have been an issue if I had a sentimental reason to hang on to my growler. 

The place was packed on an early Saturday evening. When we arrived no bar seats or tables were available so we were able to sit at one of the barrel tables by the door. It was super drafty and I kept my coat on the entire time. As others mentioned, the setup had a real industrial feel. We opted for a server but theoretically could have gone to the bar for each round. I feel we would have been inconvenienced if we went to the bar, but also felt we were inconveniencing the server by requesting our little pours so frequently. 

With all of that being said, I really enjoyed the beer and am definitely hopping on the Tired Hands wagon.

Meat me at Butcher Bar. Give me meat and meet me there, after my first visit those are two things that will need to happen again. 

Dining with Mariella S. and Kathleen D., we had a cute corner spot upstairs. I would've loved to sit right by the window, but I bet those spots are hot commodities. Noted for next time. 

Everything about our visit was standout, including our server. She showed an enthusiasm for the menu and for her job. If a server didn't need to be efficient, I could've seen her highlighting the menu and specific items for hours. I would've enjoyed listening. 

She sold us on a new salad that wasn't even on the menu at the time. It was the most fun spin to a Caesar salad-  crispy pancetta, baby romaine, roasted red peppers, shaved locatelli, panisse croutons, chipotle caesar dressing. It's now on the menu, so I'd absolutely recommend getting it. It's large enough to share with one or two people if you are getting other appetizers. 

As for the rest of the menu, maybe I went into the meal thinking the portions would be small based on Yelp pictures, but I was pleasantly surprised that they weren't. The Applewood smoked bacon with a maple glaze was much bigger than similar style bacon I've tried elsewhere. It was a really hearty, cured piece of meat. 

The Italian meatball was delicious, but probably the most "standard" of the items we tried. It was made up of pork, veal, beef, fontina stuffed, slow roasted pork gravy, pecorino romano and basil. I guess there's only so much you can do with balls. 

The best of show was the boar short ribs. I'm a short rib snob, but the combination of the sauce and the boar meat made these something to write home about. They were fall off the bone and delectable. It looks like they change up the menu and the short rib is now being prepared differently now, but as long as it's the same quality meat and cooking, I can only imagine it being a stellar dish with any preparation. 

They had a small, but solid beer list in addition to some fun cocktails. I couldn't make up my mind so I opted for the Win Win, which consisted of IPA and liquor. Win-win for me! 

Everything was delicious, the portions were solid, our server was great and the environment was nice. What more can you really need? 

Meet me at the meat...who's joining me for the trough?

Since my last review over half a decade ago, Angelino's has become a staple in my household.

They temporarily closed at one point in 2019 and I cried. Thankfully they are backing and still delicious during the pandemic.

We ordered a few sandwiches over Grubhub; living in Fairmount, they came delivered so warm. I've had food get colder being carried across a restaurant; from other establishments, of course. 

Thankfully Angelino's is still with us and thankfully they are still awesome.

Totally premature review alert. I had such a good, but brief, experience at Tap Room on 19th that I can't resist sharing it. 

On Saturday, 11/7 they had a big party to celebrate their 2nd anniversary. One of the biggest draws for me was a ridiculously amazing beer list. They also closed off the street for a block party which was pretty cool thing to do.

So the hubby and I stopped by specifically for one beer. The staff was so warm, welcoming and knowledgeable about beer in general. They chatted with us about all things beer and were just really chill people. 

Unfortunately, we had to leave after one drink for another commitment, but we could have stayed there trying different beers and chatting all day.  We left with the immediate urge to go back to this establishment for both the beer and the staff.

Let's just say that I don't feel that enthusiastic about a bar that often.

Most of what I said in my original review holds true still.  Primarily, I think it's great that there's an actual brewery in Brewerytown. Please refer to that for my general thoughts.

I'm giving Crime and Punishment the extra star because the beer deserves it. After a few visits and about a dozen beers under my belt, this brewery has what it takes to standout and succeed.

Most recently I had the "Interrobang" and the "Peaches and Crime."  If you like hoppy double IPAs, Interrobang is fantastic. It can totally play the game with some of those rare DIPAs bad boys that like to float around Philly. On the other hand, the Peaches and Crime was light and refreshing. Not as peachy as the title would allude to, but very complex. Bottom line is that their beers have the complexity needed to differentiate themselves in a growing craft beer world. 

And guess what? Having Crime and Punishment in Brewerytown has gotten myself and many others into that neck of the woods, including other businesses like Spot Burger. Bravo! I'm seeing even more good things to come with this brewery and neighborhood.

Standout happy hour alert. Roar! (That's what a happy hour alert would sound like in lion-ese). 

Finding a happy hour that excels in both the food and drink department can be a challenge. At the Little Lion, you can have it both ways. Bonus points for being able to enjoy happy hour anywhere in the dining room. 

To drink, I had to the Reviver Red IPA by Starr Hill. A full pint of delicious craft beer for $3? Yes, please!

To eat, I split the Poutine with friends. This dish is only available on their happy hour menu. Never having had Poutine before, I didn't know what to expect. I can tell you that their combination of egg, fries, short rib gravy, pork belly and cheese was quite tasty. 

Although not on their happy hour menu, I also split the Kale Pesto Pasta with a friend. Split two ways it became happy hour priced, while still being larger than normal happy hour portions even after split. Oh man, oh man, oh man. It had pesto, cauliflower, roasted tomatoes, orecchiette and cheese. The balance of all the ingredients was perfect. I will be back for this without a doubt.

The atmosphere is also something worth mentioning. The large, wall-wide windows and extravagant stairway give the room a grand, spacious feel. The restaurants touts itself on comfort foods, and has a comfortable, yet trendy feel.

Our service was nice, but the service was a little slow. It wasn't really too crowded so maybe they were understaffed. It just took a long time for everything to happen including receiving our drinks, receiving our food and settling up the bill. I enjoyed myself otherwise so I'm not going to let that ruin my opinion of the Little Lion. 

Let's just say, Simba would be impressed.

Best pizza in America. AMERICA. Not just Philly, our entire country. Bon Appetit awarded Pizzeria Beddia this coveted title back in 2015. 

This little shop in Fishtown had been on my radar for a while and as I finally planned my first trip there, I went with both excitement and nervousness. Can this pizza REALLY be that good? 

Well, it lived up to that hype and then some. While I wouldn't say the pizza was life changing, it was life confirming. It confirmed all my previous preferences and biases for pizza were correct, as this pizza was just so wonderfully delicious. As friends have warned, I think it has also ruined pizza for me. There's SO much mediocre and bad pizza out there that will be even harder to stomach after this experience. 

I'm sure most of you've heard the drill now, they make a limited number of pies per day and you need to get there early. If you want this pizza, you or someone in your group needs to be prepared to wait. If you want this pizza that badly, I'd recommend just making your entire day centered around it; and yes, that would be well worth your time. 

I would like to thank my friend for doing the dirty work and ordering the pies for our group. My husband and I arrived just in time for our first pie to come out of the oven. We opted to dine-in. There are only two tables and you only have a limited amount of time to eat based on the number of pies you order. These tables are high tops and don't have chairs. They also don't have forks and knives in the restaurant. They do have water, and cups if you want to BYOB. 

For a business that has earned such a holy title, Joe and John couldn't have possibly been any more down to earth and humbling. They know to make an extraordinary product and run a successful business. 

Onto the pizza...

We ordered three pies
-A plain pie
-A pie with broccoli rabe, roasted pepper, cream and garlic
- An arrabbiata pie 

Our plain came out first and was the perfect baseline. If you can't perfect a plain, you have no business making pizza in the first place. It came out piping hot, with a butter crust that was both crisp and doughy at the same time and the most perfect whole milk mozzarella anyone could have asked for. 

The broccoli rabe pie was similiar to the plain, yet with toppings (well duh). As the pie cooled, the broccoli rabe began to crisp and the garlic began to soak into the crust. My friend warned us to wait a little until the pie cools, but it's hard to resist when it lands on your table. A slight cooling actually allows for more synergy between all the ingredients, with less chance of burning the roof of your mouth. 

The arrabbiata was hot. There were two types of peppers on the pie and they had kick. There was also a spice to the pie itself. 

As I'm not a professional writer nor professional food critic, it is hard perfectly articulate perfection. I can tell you that all three pies left me smiling and filled to the brim with happiness. The flavors, the textures and blend of ingredients hit my taste buds in the most favorable of ways. Of course, there is countless subjectivity with this statement so take it for what it's worth. All I know is that my expectations were met and well exceeded with a new pizza on my personal pedestal.

Suraya lives up to all of the hype, as you momentarily get whisked away from Fishtown and into a Lebanese culinary delight.

I snagged a dinner table for two at an early evening time slot of a holiday week. There was also an option to sit at the counter, but I was happy with our cozy table against the wall. 

Suraya was much brighter than most Middle Eastern restaurants I've ever been too. That made it open and relaxing, while still a nice atmosphere.

Our server was very patient as we asked questions about the cocktail list. I ended up with the Joy and Sorrow after concerns of allergic reactions with the sumac in the Optimist.

We started with the baba ganoush and fatteh, which were excellent compliments, as the former was cold and the later warm. I've never had the Lebanese versions of these dishes before, and they were slightly less oil based than others I've had. I loved the pomegranates in the baba ganoush.

The standout rock stars of the meal were the lamb entrees. I will be citing these as some of the best dishes I've ever had for a long time to come. We split the Halabi Kebab and Kawarma. Both were prepared differently but were packed with flavor and fall apart tenderness.

We also had to try the Lebanese wines. The Sauvignon Blanc was ok- not as sweet as from New Zealand. I really enjoyed the Cabernet Sauvignon.

I'm not a huge dessert person but had to try the Tehina and Carob Mousse Glacee because it was something different. I can't properly describe the creaminess and flavor, but I'd recommend it.

I can see why Philadelphia and beyond has fallen in love with Suraya. I will be fantasizing over my lamb dishes until the next time I return.

My experience at Barclay Prime was exquisite. This is the place to go if you are looking to impress or are being taken out to be impressed. 

The clientele seemed very upscale and was business oriented. Although I was there on business myself, I didn't feel as fancy pants as the other patrons. Once seated, I did real relaxed and comfortable in this fine dining establishment with my view of the bookcases. 

Our server was the utmost of professionals. He knew everything from the liquor in each cocktail to the massive selection of wines, to the different types of knives without missing a beat. He could provide descriptions of each course that went well beyond memorizing the ingredients. He embodied Barclay Prime. No one in my group ordered the crab cake, but his description of this dish had us all dreaming. 

Aside from our cocktails, wine and popover rolls, my group started by splitting the wagyu ribeye & foie gras cheesesteak. They pre-sliced the sandwich in the back so we each could try a piece. It came with a bottle of champagne that we split as well. This cheesesteak may have ruined cheesesteaks for me. To have such special meat prepared in a made-to-Philly form, took meat and cheesesteaks to the next level.

Our server's description also had a large part of my group sold on the bone-in filet versus the regular filet. Yet another type of food ruined by Barclay Prime's perfection. It's going to be hard to beat this melt-in-your-mouth, medium rare yet warm, seasoned and flavorful piece of meat. 

I also found it fun to pick my steak knife out of several offerings- I've never gotten to do that before.

Without over indulging, we passed on the desserts and after dinner cordials. 

I'd obviously want to go back any day of the week; however, it's going to be for those special occasions where I'm being wined and dined like royalty. Impressed would be an understatement.

We can now have a bigger taste of Chicago in Philadelphia. The Goose Island Brewhouse is a long time coming.

First, Goose Island saturated the beer market. Then, we learned they were bought by InBev. We continued receiving the Goose Island "good stuff" and then finally the Brewhouse opens. Debate it all you'd like, but if we can easily access beers like Juliet, Madame Rose and Bourbon County Stout, I'd say it's a win.

The Brewhouse is large, open and industrial. It has a modern feel that utilizes the space well. There's a large U-shaped bar in the center of the dining room, which was crowded, but not impossible to get beers.

It's the beer list that makes this place great. I've only seen this much great Goose Island together at a takeover, and have had to go out of my way to track down some of these individual beers. You can't beat having so many of them in one spot.

As some of their brews are specialties of sort, the draft prices are fair, but on the higher side. If they offer happy hour, we'd have something quite good going on there.

The food menu was standard bar grub, and not overly impressive. I had the beef barley soup, wings and Brussels flatbread. Nothing to write home about, but accompanied the high ABV beers nicely. 

I can't see myself as a regular here, as it's not exactly close to Center City, however there's no shadow of a doubt where I'm heading when I need my Goose Island fix.

I drove all the way from Phoenix for this?!?! The brisket here was disappointing. Not sure if they didn't smoke their brisket long enough but the smokey flavor was definitely lacking compared to what I have in Phoenix at Little Miss BBQ. The chicken corn chowder was ok. The pulled pork and green beans were decent & tasted better than the brisket & corn chowder, but definitely not worth the drive from Phoenix. U won't find me piggin' out here again!
Best cheesesteak in town! Just the right spices, real meat and heavenly  Asiago cheese sauce. Served with fresh cut French fries! Great selection of beers. You can taste before you order you brew.

I have been to Stern's Wharf many times and I always have passed this restaurant many times. I only have taken pictures outside with Moby Dick (the whale that is outside) pretending that it is biting my head off. 

This year one of my co-workers told me that on Valentine's Day they have a pretty good dinner for two. She told me to make a reservation since it is a holiday and pretty much every restaurant is busy. I went to their website and saw the menu for Valentine's Special and made a reservation and within an hour I got an email confirming the reservation. 

When I got there with my significant other, we did not wait that long to be seated. Here is what we got for $99.96 (plus tax and tip):

1 Bottle of Listle Cuveé Pink (Champagne)
Salad or a cup of clam chowder
2 Prime Top Sirloins with a baked potato and fresh sautéed vegetables
1 Main Lobster (split in two, one half for me and the other for my significant other)
2 velvet cupcake (one for each)

Everything was great and the service was amazing. I guess their busy time was earlier than our reservation at 7:30 p.m. The server had more time for us.

 I hear that they also have a great breakfast so one of these days I would make my way to Moby Dick (not to take a picture outside), but to enjoy a breakfast with an amazing view.

P.S. we also had margaritas and they were fantastic. They served them in a glass that had a stem in the shape of a cactus.

I've been hearing that they have really good food, so I had to go and check it out. 

The food truck parks right in front of Big Brand Tires on Milpas Street in the East Side. They do provide tables and chairs under a tent or you can get your order to go. I order the three tacos for $5; carne asada, chicharron, and papas con chorizo.  

The crane asada was good, but I would not say it was the best. The chicharron was not what I expected, it has the texture "cueros" (rubbery texture). Usually when I think of chicharron I think of it being deep fried and it was not that way. The chorizo con papas was delicious, I really liked it. All of the tacos were served on a hand made tortilla which is a plus for my taste. I also ordered a gordita with barbacoa and I think so far the best meat at this place is the Barbacoa. 

They have couple of different salsas. A green salsa made with tomatillos, it was delicious and the right heat. They had another green salsa with I believe avocado and the third one was a red salsa which it was also really good. If you like cactus they have a cactus salad which includes tomatoes, onions, cilantro, and I believe jalapeños (don't quote me on the jalapeños). I ate the cactus salad with the gordita de barbacoa and the red salsa and it was out of this world.

Since it was cold, I also ordered a champurrado and it was amazing. This thick warm drink is a chocolate-based atole made with corn masa. I had to order another one before I left (for the road). 

I would like to try the Chicken and the Pastor meats. And other items on the menu, like tortas and sopes, huaraches, etc. So I'll be coming back.
i started getting breakfast here and all i can say is damn the food is good.

Beignets? What more can one say? Coffee? Yes, please! This wonderful place is usually the first place I want to go when I fly in to New Orleans. Make sure you have CASH for this place. No debit cards. Highly recommend this place.

I ordered a "Jean's Road Trip" birthday cake for my mom's surprise party. I called the Tuesday before, and spoke with a very friendly and helpful young lady, who assured me that it would be ready on Saturday.

 Fast forward to that Saturday when my nephew and I stopped in to pick up the cake. We had to wait a few moments while they finished writing "Happy Birthday" on the cake, but that was no biggie because it took us that long to thaw out from the Tundra-esque temperatures from outside. 

Well, let me tell you, to say the cake was a hit is definitely an understatement. Everyone loved the cake - including the birthday girl! It was moist and very rich, and the icing was stupid sweet and delicious! To top it all off, we brought half of the cake home, even with all 15 of us having had a decent-sized slice. I will absolutely order another cake from Brown Betty...seriously, ab-so-lutely!

ABSOLUTELY NOT RECOMMENDED

I would rate zero stars if I could for their bad-tempered Korean owner. My friends and I ordered AYCE ($25 per person) and found the chicken smelled bad and that's not the point. Three of us tried it and agreed to ask them to exchange for something else. After that, the owner brought the chicken plate out and yelled at our table that their chicken was always fresh, everyday a lot of customers always ordered and had no problem. 

She said "Only you have this problem."

She also asked if we wanted to try the chicken again. We were shocked and didn't respond anything back. Then, she threw the chicken plate away loudly to the table at the back of the restaurant. I should have said she should be the one trying the chicken. 

We had enjoyed the rest of the food and the service until this happened. It was so embarrassing of her doing this in front of customers and her employees. She should leave her ego at home if she wants to do business. We will never come back again.

Heard there was a new seafood place open in Middle Tennessee. We're talking all kinds of shellfish, crustaceans, fried fish options, and RAW OYSTERS!!! So made a date with my foodie buddie so we could get our hands dirty. We were seated immediately and started scouring the menu trying to decide what and how to order to get the best sample of the offerings. Our waiter Shawn provided us some guidance and we started off with a dozen oysters. While waiting for the oysters we finally decided on two "Get Your Hands Dirty" with Shrimp, Crawfish, Clams, Green Mussels, Black Mussels, and Sausage. The meal also comes with corn on the cob and whole red skin taters. We both decided on the Garlic Butter sauce at the mild level which was a great choice although there are other options with varying levels of "spice"

The oysters arrived chilled and very plump...these were a great deal and very tasty. When the "bags" of dinner arrived we were as happy as kids on Christmas morning. Having the freshly boiled seafood tossed in the garlic butter and Cajun spices in the bag was incredible. You get a bib and gloves, open the bag, and DIG IN! I have to say, everything in the bags was really good and the flavors from the sauce was spot on. A few highlights...the crawfish were huge and provided a lot of meat, the sausage was really good, and the green mussels were some of the best I have had in a long time. You need to break open the red skin taters and allow them to soak up some of the sauce...incredible. As for the corn on the cob...yes corn on the cob...just WOW with the garlic butter and spices.

Sarah (the manager) visited our table and checked on us a few times...she was a pleasure to talk to! Shawn provided us great service and on our way out reiterated it was a pleasure meeting us and to come back soon. This type of service, along with great food makes it worth the trip out to Hermitage. There are several other options and combinations to try here. Just letting folks know...not a low cost option for dinner BUT you are getting some delicious food that is very well prepared.
The vegan wings are sooo good. Happy hour drinks were ok but I'll be back for the food!

Outstanding food , I always get a salmon platter with egg & broccoli to me on the healthy side. & when I wanna kick it up a notch I'll take a salmon & broccoli steak with shrimp  can't say enough love it !!

Always love coming to Waldens.  It is anything but a little coffee place .. they have some of the best breakfast!! The huevos rancheros is super good made with a turkey chilli.. very unique.  I love those bagel and pesto spread and the specialty coffees are yum too.  They share an outdoor patio area with Eclipse pizza .. service is always great..a few changes with Covid but nothing negatively impacting in my opinion

I used to like their cakes & cupcakes, but recently ordered some cupcakes, and when I was waiting to get them (since they weren't ready for me), heard a lot! 
 
#1- they keep everything in the freezer... apparently, they stock the freezers then pull from there- you are NOT getting a freshly baked cake!  They asked when they were going to be eaten & when I said the next day, the counter girl said "OK, that will give them time to thaw- ha ha"- OK, if I am paying that much, they should be FRESH!  

#2 When I was asking about a cake (which I ultimately ordered elsewhere, obviously), I dealt with a "designer" who had the vocabulary of an uneducated 12 year old who swore a lot.  Now, I am very liberal, but when you work with customers, you have to be careful about that type of thing.  Super unprofessional, and very, very  much a turn off.  

#3 I didn't bother complaining to the owner, since I have seen her in action (while I was waiting forever for my cupcakes, she was in the midst of an argument with a customer on the phone & then hung up & talked about it with the other employees- at least I know where her employee got her cue for unprofessional behavior), but I will make sure everyone I know from the area goes elsewhere for their bakery needs... 

Don't wast your time- you can get pre-baked previously frozen dessert items elsewhere for much less...

Came here with my girls to celebrate my bday. The service was great we were seated quick and the waitress khadijah was very nice and got the orders correct. The food presentation was nice I ordered the Thanksgiving sandwich with mash potatoes . The mashed potatoes were delicious the sandwich was dry the turkey was over cooked and hard. It could of used more stuffing and cranberry on the bread it barely had anything on it. 
I ordered oreo cheesecake to take home that was really good. Just disappointed the sandwich wasnt as good as I thought it would be.
Nice concept, too bad the food and service are not to par. It was also pretty pricey!

For the last 3+ years that I have been in Philly, I have been waiting for good Indian/South Indian restaurants to open in the city. Every time I crave for good Indian food, I have to drag one of my friends to drive 30-40 mins to King of Prussia or New Jersey. I was beyond ecstatic when I heard Amma's had opened on 15th and Chestnut. First Thanal (check it out if you haven't already) and then this? This year is turning out to be swell! 

Went there last night with a friend and we literally couldn't decide what to get! I am salivating right now even thinking about last night's dinner. Anywho back to reality - we ordered the spicy Idly Podi, Mutton Kheema dosa and Chicken Lollipop. Everything was so delicious and flavorful - not sure how to even describe it better than that. 

I am NOT a coffee person, I can only drink coffee made by my mom and here in the US (no offense) even the smell of coffee makes me nauseous sometimes. But I had to try the Madras filter coffee because why not?! It was probably the best coffee I have had after coming here to the states. It is bitter enough and has like a hint of chocolate somehow - like how I had always imagined in my head a Mocha should be. I can totally get addicted to this coffee. Try it! 

If you trust my reviews - you have to head over to this place now. I can't imagine what'll happen once everyone gets to know about this gem - will I ever get to sit peacefully and devour all the South Indian goodness this place has to offer just like last night?

This place is the bee's knees! It's a little tricky to find, but once you do, you'll be coming back over and over again. 

Dining on their outdoor patio is always tops, but dining inside is just as nice. Clean, comfortable, with just enough accents to warm up the atmosphere. This is one of those places where you will feel just as comfortable in jeans as you would in a suit or a dress (my future hubs and I have been here wearing both ends of the spectrum). 

Their food is consistently amazing and I love the way the waitstaff will steer you toward (or away from) a particular menu item. They are BYOB, but they do offer a handful of New Jersey wines (we normally pass on these). We've had everything from the Crab and Avocado salad down to richer pasta dishes. There is truly something for everyone on their menu. My family loves this place also! 

Nice local place to hit up for a delicious dinner. And don't pass up their desserts...they're worth it!

Megu is a nice Asian restaurant in an unassuming strip mall in Cherry Hill. Cripes, is EVERYTHING in New Jersey in a strip mall?! Don't answer that :) 

Hottie Esq and I came here for a late lunch on a Saturday. I think they were nearing closing time for their own lunch break, but they sat us and served us with a smile. We ordered several rolls off of the express lunch menu (good variety here). Lunch menu items come with the standard miso soup and ginger-dressed salad. We enhanced it with an order of edamame (lightly salted and perfectly steamed). 

I hate when you order the sushi roll and pieces combo and they give you that limp-ass butterflied shrimp that's as thin as a piece of paper, or that nasty hard-as-nails fluke. I was thrilled that my pieces were tuna, salmon, and yellowtail only. It's like they knew what I like best...they KNEW! 
 
Their sushi rolls were well-sized and the fish was the right temperature. The rice was seasoned nicely. Esq was very pleased, and his happiness is paramount to me. Thank you, Megu! 

The interior was swanky without being "cold". The outside really doesn't do it any justice. Parking is located in both the front and the back. 

Solid choice for an express lunch. I look forward to returning for dinner!

Dear Healthy Garden,

Please open a location in Northern New Jersey. I don't mean to whine, but it's not fair that Southern New Jersey gets to have a place as fantastic as you, while we're left in the breeze up here. Granted, I have no issue driving to see you, considering Sexyman lives so close to you and that's super-motivating in and of itself, but sometimes I desire a fresh and sassy salad at lunch and I simply cannot make it there and back in time for my afternoon meetings. Plus, he has taken to sending me pictures of said salads (Caribbean, etc), and it's making me green with envy. 

Anyway...thank you for taking such good care of us on Sunday. We had the Breakfast Scramble (organic eggs, quinoa, tomatoes, spinach, portabella mushrooms), the Fresh Start (organic eggs, tomatoes, portabella mushrooms, peppers, cheese), and we split the strawberry/banana/Nutella crepe. In my mind, that crepe was healthy (delusional maybe, but I am going with it). 

Your space is causal and comfortable and your waitstaff is so accommodating. And your drinks have that fun crushed ice that I love so much. Blissful! 

Until you grace us with the glory of a Healthy Garden up north, I will continue my infatuation with you and promise to visit regularly. You may force me to move to the area if you don't honor my request. Just saying.

Until next time,
Lor

El Vez has 1,629 reviews...does it really need another? Uh yes, because there isn't one from Sexyman and me. 

This place was hopping at around 1:30 PM on Saturday. No-seats-open-by-the-bar kind of packed. Aren't weekend afternoon cocktails the best? We snagged a table in the bar area for a martini and some apps.

- Bazooka Limon Guacamole...goat cheese, roasted tomatoes, and pistachios. This was effin amazing. The textures and the flavors complimented each other beautifully. "Goat cheese in guacamole??" you say, while looking perplexed. Yes. Do it. 

- Taco Tasting Platter...Sea bass, chicken, beef, carnitas, mahi-mahi. We liked the mahi best and the sea bass least. This tasting platter was the perfect portion size for what we wanted. Nice presentation also. 

El Vez is very festive and fun. Friendly vibe with enough tequila options to keep you entertained for days. And the bathrooms are communal, so no, you didn't walk into the men's/women's room by mistake. A few margaritas will do that to a person, or so I've heard.

We dig! 

We've dined-in and gone the take-out route at LaScala's and we've never been disappointed. This is our go-to place when we decide to calorie-splurge on pizza. Their crust is neither too thick nor too thin, and you're never left wondering "where the hell are the toppings?" My better half and I typically order two specialty pizzas and we usually have leftovers for lunch the next day. Their pizzas are larger than personal size, but not large like the ones you'll receive at a pizzeria. 

The Ricotta Cheese Board is killer. We split this with my parents at lunch one day and even my dad who's a bit on the non-adventurous side enjoyed the honey and cheese combination. Whoever came up with that dish (and the cool presentation) deserves a medal or at least a salary increase! 

The layout of the restaurant is fresh, bright, and inviting. The outdoor seating is key in the warmer months, and they'll give you a giant chrome bucket (or two) to keep your adult beverages just the temperature that you like them. 

LaScala is family-friendly, couples-friendly, and even pet-friendly (outdoors, of course). Just don't try to bring a pet peacock or something asinine. 

Pizza, pizza, pizza!

My favorite restaurant I've never stepped foot in! 

Amma's has become a staple in our rotation during COVID. They closed for a bit at the beginning of the pandemic, but they opened shortly after and didn't skip a beat. 

Our favorites are the Dosa, Malabar Parotta, Gobi Manchurian, Chicken and the Paneer Tikka Masala, and Mutton/Lamb Chukka (to name a few). Their basmati rice is oh so light and fluffy and it stays that way even a day or two later. Portions are generous, so takeout from Amma's means that I will always have lunch for the next day or two. 

We like to order ahead (you can call it in or order online) and my Love will pick our order up on his way home from work. I am always excited to see him, but even more so on the days he has the Amma's takeout bag in hand :) 

I look forward to actually seeing this inside of this place someday!

Olives and cheeses and meats, oh my! Di Bruno Brothers is pretty rad on a normal day, but my Love and I got to experience the after-hours magic and boy, were we happy.

For $70 per person, you have the entire store to yourself between the hours of 7:00 PM through 9:00 PM (advance reservations are a must, along with a deposit). There were 10 of us in total and we felt that it was just the right amount of people. The friendly and funny cheese mongers put together numerous plates of cheeses, cured meats, olives, nuts, and even chocolates for us to sample. They explained the rationale behind the pairings as they went along, so essentially, this is not only a food-based event but it's educational also! 

Happen to see a bag of breadsticks on the shelf that you feel compelled to try? Hand it over to the mongers and they'll open it for you. Literally, you can sample anything in the store. And you'll receive a discount on anything you purchase that night also. We purchased some cocoa covered almonds that didn't stand a chance in our home. Fantastic!

The highlight of the event was sampling a very special prosciutto that runs about $100 per pound. Perhaps the pig was a gift from heaven? It must have been, as it was melt-in-your-mouth delish.

The funniest aspect of the evening were the passers-by who tried to enter the store and join the party. Tough noogies! Book your own event and experience the indulgence yourselves :)

Bring your favorite alcohol and bring your favorite foodies. Great night out in South Philadelphia!

~THIS REVIEW IS FOR THE CASINO ONLY~

Las Vegas this is not. Atlantic City this is not. But for what it is - a small casino nestled near the King of Prussia Mall - we had a great time. 

The Circle Bar is staffed with friendly and attentive bartenders. Drinks are pretty reasonably priced and the people-watching is on-point. The DJ kept things lively and there was a small, mixed crowd of people who were tripping the light fantastic. The Marquez/Bradley fight was being broadcast throughout the casino on Saturday night, which was a nice bonus. And the man won $400 at Blackjack. 

See, you CAN have a great time here!

We met some interesting characters and had a lot of laughs. If you go, just treat it for what it is (again, a small casino) and let the night take you where it will. Leave any pretense at the door (along with your $10 cover charge, which is waived in the future if you enroll in the VIP/Player's Club) and have yourself an experience!

Friday Saturday Sunday is just as good on a Thursday! 

We decided to sit at the beautiful bar and order up some later-evening cocktails and bites. I love a dimly-lit, cozy bar. It feels so intimate. The kitchen closes at 10:00 PM, so we made it there in the nick of time. 

Their drink and food menu is streamlined and for good reason. It's better to have a few great selections and rock our worlds with them. Their cocktails are fun and fresh (the "Control State" for me and the "Alternative Fact" for him...what unique names)! We sampled the Carrots Confit, the Charred Cauliflower, the Octopus, and the Roasted Potato Gnocchi. Each one was more delicious than the next. Portions were large enough to be filling but small enough to share a few.

The staff takes pride in their menu and that was obvious from the start. And is there anything better than an expertly-crafted cocktail that's made with love?  

This place has a nice local feel and we were welcomed just as warmly as a regular would be. 

If we lived in this area, then we'd be "locals" for sure!

Swanky lil' joint with a small bowling alley in the basement. Who thought of this great idea?

We visited Harp & Crown on the first Friday night that they were open. Reservations were difficult to come by due to the anticipation of the grand opening, so we opted for a late dinner at 9:30 PM.

The decor is a modern twist on all-things-vintage (if that makes sense). The bar space was hopping but we had to wait a few minutes by the check-in area for some room to become available before we could grab a drink. I presume they were aiming for crowd control by the narrow bar. Within a few minutes we were barside, awaiting our much-needed spirits. They offer some inspired cocktails that are crafted with fresh juices (always a plus). There is something on the drink menu for everyone. 

Small plates are where it's at here. We sampled the roasted olives, chicken liver mousse (surprisingly good!), artisan cheese plate, oysters, and a flatbread that was devoured so fast that I couldn't even tell you what in the Sam Hill was on it! Margherita, I presume. 

New establishments always need some time to work out the kinks, so I am not going to ding them for little service issues. We encountered smiles among the staff even in light of a very busy evening. We made reservations for a few weeks out and we are looking forward to returning. And I am hopeful to kick some bowling arse in the downstairs lounge next time around!

Views galore! 

After visiting the Sky High Bar several times for cocktails, we decided that we needed to experience a dinner service at Jean-Georges. The restaurant is in the Four Seasons hotel, way up high. The views are phenomenal! Reservations for a Saturday night book-out 2 months in advance, so patience is a virtue. 

The highlights for us were the extensive wine list, the atmosphere, and the impeccable service. Usually the food is what shines for me, but it was the service that really wowed us. 

We went out of our comfort zone with the wine we selected as well as with some of the plates we shared.  We started with the Egg Toast and Caviar and the Caviar with Vodka Whipped Cream. Unique! Our entrees included the Sea Bass, Lobster, and two specials. We created our own dessert "sampler" and it was a great way to round out our experience. The food was very good, but truly, the service was on-point. Nary an empty water nor wine glass, and great attention to detail all around.

This is definitely a special occasion kind of place. And hold onto your hat because it ain't cheap! 

Pro tip - if you have reservations, then you can bypass the inevitable line at the elevator and head on up to the Sky High Bar for a pre-dinner cocktail. Alert the hostess and away you'll go!

Hash House A Go-Go was on our radar and we finally made our way in for Sunday Brunch. Two seats opened up at the bar when we arrived and we made a beeline over to grab them.

The bartenders were mega-friendly and offered up some cocktail and food recommendations. The BLT Bloody Mary was a cool concept, but eating/drinking it was confusing. Do you pull the BLT accoutrements out of the drink and eat them on the bread (adding mayo from the mini packet)? Or do you dip the bread into the drink? I guess there is no "right" way to enjoy it, and the bartender admitted that the regular house Bloody Mary is more popular. 

My Love ordered the Crab Cake Sandwich/Burger and I ordered the Veggie Hash with poached eggs. The hash needed a few kisses of salt, and the biscuit it came with was so very bland and dry, dry, dry. That was a bummer. The crab cake on his sandwich was about 70% filler. It literally tasted like a breadcrumb burger with a hint of crab flavor. He's a member of the "Clean Plate Club" (unite!) but he left more than half of the sandwich behind. That being said, the sweet potato fries we ordered on the side were flavorful. 

One thing we bar patrons experienced was being served our food without silverware. Every person at the bar had to flag down a bartender for silverware after their food was served. It was almost comical. The people next to us were super pissed about it, but we just let it roll.

And there are only two stalls in the bathroom, so be prepared to wait if the restaurant is busy.

We may give this place another go in a few months. For now, we'll stick to our usual brunch haunts.

Hottie Esq and I came here for an early lunch and it was a good thing we did because we needed the entire day to burn off the insane calories we consumed. Please note - those calories were well worth it. 

I had a very different vision of what this cheesesteak would be like and I was all wrong. Kudos to him for not giving me any details prior. Poppy seed Kaiser roll, sautéed onions that marvel what you would find in an excellent French onion soup, and velvety American cheese. I believe that you can ask for Whiz, but the American cheese is where it's at! They have a side of hot peppers that you can add to your sandwich also. I hesitated doing this because I feared ruining it, but it added an amazing layer of flavor. The seasoned fries were fantastic, with just the right amount of crunch and softness. We said we'd only try a few but who were we kidding? We finished those bad-boys off in 10 minutes. 

And I was able to get a bottle of diet root beer there. Friggen sodatastic! 

We saw a lot of to-go orders going on while we were slowly slipping into our blissful food coma. The employees were super cool and friendly as all get-out. 

This place makes me never want to eat another salad again.

Hot damn, this was a great breakfast place! There was a little bit of a wait on a beautiful Thursday morning, but they'll graciously text you to alert you that your table is ready. But you better move your arse when you receive that notification because they'll only hold your table for 5 minutes. 

- Blackened Shrimp and smoked gouda grits...Sexyman ordered this and I helped myself to more of it than I rightfully should have. The blackened shrimp was cooked perfectly and the cheesy grits were an amazing compliment. I would have licked the plate if we weren't in public. 

- Lobster Brie Bennie...eggs Benedict with chunks of lobster and a melted slice of Brie cheese? Oh yes I did. I substituted grits for hashbrowns (when in Rome). Finding grits in Northern NJ is like finding Bigfoot. And they were grit-tastic! 

- Almond French toast...sweet, crispy, and served with cinnamon-infused butter. Add some syrup to it and get ready to swoon (and gain 5 pounds).

They have a full bar and offer several variations of mimosas, including peach and passion fruit. Parking is a bit tight in the lot (it's shared with a handful of other stores) but you'll find something nearby if it's full. Friendly and inviting waitstaff.

Get your name on that list and sit outside if you can!

Catelli Duo has it all...a fun outdoor bar, a comprehensive menu complete with vegetarian and vegan options (clearly labeled), and some of the friendliest waitstaff in the county. 

Live entertainment on the patio is where it's at on Wednesday nights. But fear not, the volume is comfortable enough to have a discussion with your dining partners. They offer daily generous Happy Hour drink specials (until 7:00 PM) and a great bar menu with lots of specials. Their pizzas always hit the spot and I am a huge fan of their grilled vegetable board with that silky hummus and creamy ricotta (swoon). 

While we've never had a full dinner here per say, everything we've tried has been well-presented and delicious. We love this place for a little mid-week, almost-to-Friday-Eve outing. Who needs a full sit-down dinner when you can enjoy a variety of appetizers and cocktails? That's our motto! 

This is the place for it.

Oh Han Dynasty, how we love you so! 

This is one of our fail-safe restaurants that we find ourselves visiting time and time again. Their food is always consistent, and it is just as delicious when it's enjoyed via take-out as it is while dining-in.

We've sampled all areas of the menu, but my Love and I find ourselves favoring the same dishes. Dry Pepper Chicken for him, and Kung Pao Tofu for me. The breading/coating on the tofu is divine. It's the perfect blend of sweet and sour and tang. The white rice soaks up the sauce, and it creates a delectable flavor-bomb. It's a well-balanced dish and it's never overly-garlicky. Heartburn is not my bag, baby! And the best part? I always have leftovers for lunch the following day. Two-for-one! 

We seem to always have the same waiter when we visit, and he's super friendly and attentive. And the hot tea you're served upon being seated is the perfect way to begin your dining experience. We just feel happy when we're getting some Han lovin'.

I think we need to visit again tonight...plus I need lunch for tomorrow!

Our destination was a tasty pre-game lunch before our St. Patrick's Day shenanigans began. Enter Destination Dogs! 

We opted to sit by the bar (our favorite spot) and Solomon created for my Love and me two of the best Moscow Mules we've ever had the pleasure of enjoying. For our dogs, he selected The Oscar and I selected The Hebrew (I substituted in the vegetarian sausage, which was fantastic). Our dogs arrived to us piping hot and begging (pun intended?) to be devoured. The toppings were plentiful without being overbearing nor overly messy. The buttery lobster roll-style bun rounded out the whole package. A small side of kettle cooked chips are served with each order, and it was the perfect addition of crunch for us. 

Destination Dogs offers tons of topping options as well as protein options. You could safely visit 50+ times and never indulge in the same item twice. 

Creative concept, chill vibe, a fun game-room area, and delicious food. What's not to love?

Not for anything, but for a place that is supposedly known for its crabs, Chickie's and Pete's sure didn't rise to the occasion.

Hubs and I were happy to (finally) find a couple of seats at the outdoor back bar (weeknight at 7:00 PM). There were a few older gentlemen who were bogarting their seats with no drinks in front of them, while gawking at the bartender. Nice touch, fellas. Had they left when they probably should have, there would have been ample seating for us and everyone else. 

We ordered a couple of beers and decided to peruse the menu. King crab legs are my jam, therefore, I ordered a pound. He ordered the dry-rub wings and a buffalo chicken sandwich. I was presented with three king crab legs (that was a pound?) and he was presented with the most Sahara Desert-looking wings I've ever seen. I didn't try any, but he said they were "Alright". Not a great vote from my fellow foodie. They forgot the blue cheese on his sandwich (which was the whole point of ordering it) and he stated that the chicken was quite dry (I am noticing a "dry" theme here)! 

Oh, the king crab legs. They were rubber-o-rama. I couldn't even use the claw cracker to break them. They were bending like a plastic straw. And I cannot stand establishments that do not give you a pick when you are served crab legs (king or otherwise). How are you supposed to dig out the meat, especially when the legs won't break open?  The "broth" at the bottom of the bowl was oily and not overly flavorful. I was actually pissed while I was eating these king crab legs. Can you flipping imagine?

There is a slim chance that we may return on a nice evening to take in the outdoor atmosphere and have a few drinks, but we will surely eat elsewhere first.

Remember those fun days of playing ping pong in your basement with your friends as a kid? Well, you can relive that same excitement as an adult, without having to chase the stray balls around!

We happened upon Spin on a random Wednesday evening. Our group is quite competitive, so anything that allots bragging rights is right up our alley. The atmosphere is attractive and swanky. There are several sections of ping pong tables throughout the space, so it feels private yet still communal. We loved that they have what felt like hundreds of balls in buckets at the tables. No need to run around and collect your strays. That alone is worth it! The staff was super engaging and fun. We spent about an hour and a half playing and laughing our heads off. 

They have a great cocktail list and I love, love, love that they give you two giant bottles of water without even having to ask. Hydration is key, folks! We arrived too late to order snacks, but we will ensure an earlier arrival next time. We are already planning a return visit!

This is a great place for a unique work event, birthday party, or just to get the gang together for some laughs.

Forget bowling and axe throwing - ping pong is where it's at!

My favorite breakfast/brunch place in South Jersey! We've been here a handful of times and we always leave satisfied.
