Amy's is normally crowded and it's with good reason. Their menu is very comprehensive, with a ton of omelet options (among other breakfast and brunch favorites). Maybe a bit TOO many options, as we are normally ravenous when we arrive and we become quickly fatigued by viewing the dozens and dozens of omelet choices. He and I always seem to land on the same thing - The Marathoner (egg white omelet with spinach, tomato, avocado, and turkey) which is served with toast and a cup of fresh fruit. We normally negate the healthiness of the omelet by ordering a huge bowl of grits and slathering it with butter, but we earned it, okay?

The waitstaff is always smiling and they check on you regularly, in spite of being super busy. Their decaf coffee is smooth and you don't have to get all decked-out to come here. You may not want to wear your PJ's though. The line has to be drawn somewhere :)

Parking can be a little tight but it seems that you can park in the neighboring lot of one of corporate buildings. But you didn't hear that from me...

Eggtastic!

Our go-to Szechwan place had a busy signal on their phone for over an hour during the pandemic. Busy signals are still a thing? A quick Yelp search led us to a great restaurant just a few miles down the road.

We ordered the Wontons in chili oil, the Kung Pao Tofu, and the Dry Pepper Chicken. What I liked best about the tofu was that it was not swimming in sauce, and the batter remained crispy and light even after a ride home. Esq enjoyed his chicken and liked that it was not overly crunchy. It was the perfect blend of tender and crispy. I didn't sample the wontons, but he swallowed the entire order in about 3 bites. That is a glowing endorsement, trust me! And the accompanying white rice was sticky and fluffy - perfect! 

There were a lot of deliveries going out and several customer pick-up's while we waited for our order in our car in the parking lot. They seem to be doing well during this challenging time and that made us happy.

We look forward to dining-in soon!

We're big Zahav fans and looked forward to our reservation at Laser Wolf. We had high hopes based upon the reviews.

The ambiance for me was a bit off-putting. You're basically sitting in what feels like a garage with tables donned with fruit-inspired plastic tablecloths. I get what they're going for aesthetics-wise, but it was more casual than I expected. 

We enjoyed the Salatim for the table, but the main plates were excessively priced for the quantity.The short ribs were $112 and were just enough for the four of us to have a few pieces. The Bronzino was $88 and was nicely deboned, but quite a hefty price tag. Again, just enough portion size for the four of us to have a few ounces.

We knew going in that we'd be dropping bank for this dinner, but we were underwhelmed by the experience overall. We never nickel-and-dime our culinary adventures, but this particular experience just didn't wow us.

We are going to stick to Zahav.

I don't even know what the inside of this place looks like. Is that crazy? Well when you have an amazing outdoor patio and bar like Redstone does, then I don't see any reason to go inside! 

Redstone is in our rotation of great local restaurants with friendly bartenders, great wine/cocktail lists, and creative cuisine. We find ourselves here often, especially when the weather is agreeable. And the outdoor patio/bar is covered, so no need to run for the hills if a rain shower rears its ugly head.

We've been here for everything from Saturday afternoon cocktails, to dinner with our parents. Their menu is inspired and plentiful without being fatiguing. Patrons and staff alike are truly friendly. Striking up a conversation with other people at the bar is welcomed and we love that. Who needs stuffiness in such a nice atmosphere? 

Parking is a-plenty, but it's also an easy place to Uber in and out of. 

Cheers to mild weather and outdoor dining. May winter forget to show up this year!

I tried giving them feedback before I left, saying that the tea want strong enough in my honey roasted milk tea with egg pudding. They wouldn't let me leave until they got the order right. 
Customer service: 6/5

And I love that you can tell them to customize it the way you want it, as a barista would in a coffee shop. I'll definitely be back. 

And yes, I think that the egg pudding here tastes better than Bing's.

I had been here once before during the week in the middle of the afternoon, and the experience was alright but should have set off some warning flags. Yes the cupcakes are expensive, but it's a "boutique" kind of place so I figured that they may be a bit much. The cupcake I had was just ok, but I figured it was a result of I just picked a bad cupcake to try.

This past Sunday I took my wife and daughter out to Jilly's for a surprise cupcake breakfast. We walked in the front door and there were quite a few people there, some waiting off to one side or another, so we walked up to the case and started looking at the cupcake selection.  Some people had come in the door a little bit after us and I noticed they went and put their name on a list to wait for a table. I mentioned it to my wife so she went to go put our name down, that must be why everyone is standing around, waiting to be seated, it's a busy weekend...I get it.

We wait for about 20 minutes until we are seated, the person seating us points to the far register (there are registers on both sides of this C shaped counter area, with the cupcake case in between) and says I can go place my order over there. So I find out what my wife wants and go over to where I was directed to place my order. The guy taking my order looked confused and said "I'm not supposed to ring out cupcake orders over here" and I was just baffled. I told him I was directed over here and he sort of rolled his eyes and said "Well if you were told to come over here. I'm just not supposed to ring them out here, that's what the other register is for". I had pointed to the table where we were sitting, and the cashier said "Wait, you're just having cupcakes?" and I responded that we were. And he kind of chuckled under his breath. I asked what the problem was, and were we in error to put our name down for a table, he laughed and said confirmed that no we were not supposed to be eating here.  I was speechless.

The person who sat us walked by and he commented to the person "Hey they're just here for cupcakes!" like he couldn't believe that someone would come into a cupcake place to order cupcakes and eat them at the tables provided. The person kind of smiled and said "Well, it's ok they can go ahead and eat them here" like we were being done a favor.

Apparently there is a breakfast buffet, in another room in the back and that is what the seating is for. However there was no signage and no one informing us of this when we entered, so I really do not think it is too much of a stretch to assume that we could purchase and eat cupcakes at a place that is called a "cupcake bar". 

After all that we finally dug into our cupcakes. The description on mine mentioned banana flavor and that was just completely absent. I tasted nothing banana in my cupcake whatsoever. So not only were we made to feel like fools who didn't belong, but our cupcakes were also not really all that great. I most definitely will not be coming here again, and that is unfortunate because the place has potential. But with the sub par cupcakes at high prices and the elitist staff, I really can't recommend it on any level.

Staying in the Gulch and heard this place was good. Home football game today, so of course it's going to be busy. Dropped by around 10:40am on a Sunday and waited in line awhile to check in. When we got to the host stand, we were told 1 hr 15 min wait for a party of 2. We put our name in. The host was very kind and said we could actually text back and forth with him, regarding any questions or changes etc. 
Nearby, we grabbed a couple Lime scooters and toured around for an hour. When we came back, we waited a short while and then a text came to say our table was ready. It was 12:00. 
We stood by the sign that says wait here when your table is ready and we were greeted and seated within seconds. 
Our table was outside; beware the bird crap. It was on the chairs, but it was dried. But that was our sign that birds may be an issue. 
Our server was super nice. He told us some funny dad jokes and made some recommendations. We started with waters, the cold brew and a dirty London fog, which was delicious. The burrata and fig appetizer was large enough to be shared among four people
 They had differing levels of toast on their bread- some very toasted and some minimally toasted. I think this was on purpose and I appreciate it. Some people like crunchier, some like softer! The burrata was a small serving but there was a TON of prosciutto, fig jam and arugula on the plate. I did wish for a little more cheese and blue cheese crumble. Just as we were finishing up, our plate was decorated with fresh bird crap from above. Yuck. Good thing we were pretty much done with that plate. 
For breakfast, we should have shared. The hodgepodge hash was a huge plate and we added an extra egg. I think it's chicken sausage pieces? But there's a lot going on there and it was hearty and good. The mushroom omelette was full of cheese and mushrooms.  Pretty standard. We did appreciate we could get egg whites for that entree.  We kept an eye on the birds above while we ate, which is bit annoying. I'd like to eat without supervising. Next time I'll wait longer for an indoor table. 
Everything was great with breakfast except two things- we were not asked which side we wanted with the omelette so I guess the default is fruit, which we didn't want, we wanted the potatoes. I wanted a biscuit with a side of gravy, but instead of charging the biscuit and gravy as an added side to the omelette, we were charged the actual biscuit with jam /honey entree plus a side of gravy. Obviously that made more money for the restaurant, but it did not have to be ticketed that way. The biscuit was crunchy on the edges and soft in the middle. The country gravy was thick and delicious. Lots of large pieces of sausage inside. Yum. 
In the end, I asked for the check and two salted caramels to go. Our server brought the check but forgot the caramels. When prompted, he apologized and brought back two caramels, no charge. So that sorta makes up for the above issues. The caramels are delicious, btw. They're individually wrapped too, so you can take them to go very easily. 
Outside there are no TVs. I'm not sure about inside? So don't bank in catching the game while you eat. Inside, the line for the restroom was LONG. Plan accordingly. 
They have a little bakery and coffee shop inside, with store merchandise for sale as well. You can place to go orders, which take about 20 min. If you don't wanna wait for a table. 
There is a parking lot across the street from them, but you gotta pay to park. I'd eat here again, but not on a busy day. I'd prefer to be inside, safe from the bird crap.

I work in the same neighborhood as Ah Juice and would go at least 3x a week with my co-workers, but after my experience this morning with the owner, Alfred, I will not be visiting Ah Juice again. 

I called in an order for a Breakfast Wrap and although it comes with Arugula, I asked to substitute Spinach. The employee on the phone said it would be no problem. When I got to Ah Juice, the wrap rang up for a few dollars more than normal and when I asked why, Alfred said it was because I added spinach to my order. When I told him that I had asked to substitute it, he replied "We don't do substitutions here" I then said "I was told on the phone that it would be no problem" Alfred replied "Well, it wasn't me that you spoke with on the phone" Trying to give Alfred a chance to provide a decent customer service experience, I said "I work right down the street, come here all the time and I've ordered this wrap with spinach before, I don't understand why you are charging me extra" to which he looked at me and said that he was not interested in talking about this with me anymore and stuck his hand out for my card. 

After paying extra (which I could have bought an entire bag of TJ's Spinach with btw), I got back to work and opened my wrap to find that they did not actually add the Spinach in addition to the Arugula, they substituted it. Ironic, right? Go elsewhere for an owner that cares about his business and customers!

Anyone who knows their way around a kitchen knows that quality spices and seasonings are a must. So after sipping a latte next door at Old World Coffee I ventured in to see if they had anything to add to my collection.

Salty-Savory-Sweet has quite the collection of spices and teas. It's a good thing I had a time limit or I would have spent my entire morning in here trying everything.

They've got the basics in bulk to stock up on too, but my attention drifted towards the harder to find spices on my list: Za'atar, Ras El Hanout, and ground Sumac. I also picked up a fantastic fine grain Sicilian Sea Salt that I now prefer.

The owners are incredibly knowledgeable and friendly. They even have low cost flate-rate shipping for the out of towners.

I am definitely coming back when I'm in Reno next and can't wait to try their teas.

Shout out to Reno's #1 Vegan Stef M for suggesting Homegrown Gastropub for the UYE I set up - this place was fantastic!!

They may be new, but if I hadn't been told that I wouldn't have guessed it. Our server, our bartender, the pastry chef and even the owner were absolutely stellar. Great service from all.

And the food? So satisfying for both vegans and meat-eaters. I came for the pizza, which was really good topped with a drizzle of garlic oil, but ended up sampling the roasted brussels sprouts, the korean jackfruit tacos, and the falafel plate. I would have also attempted a bite of the vegan burger but they're still working out the kinks of finding the right vegan bun. 

The game changer is in the hands of their...wait for it.... Vegan pastry chef! I swear to you the best desserts are made from the palette of a vegan and this further proves my point. Her coconut cream pie is out of this world phenomenal!! If it's available you may want to order two haha. The brownie sundae was also quite good.

I can't wait to come back here the next time I'm in Reno. I'm hoping they make a killer vegan Bloody Mary by then. And a brunch. Can we get a decent vegan brunch in Reno please? Just sayin...

Added bonus, they carry Belvedere :) 
Thanks again Stef!!!

Finding a vegetarian-friendly restaurant in downtown Reno is hard enough. Finding a spot open til 3am? The answer to my veggie prayers.

Usually when I go to a Vietnamese restaurant "veggie pho" translates to odd looks from the server and inedible bowls of chicken broth. Golden Flower was the exception. Not only did they accommodate with a delicious bowl of vegan pho, they even added fried tofu. 

Service was also good in an otherwise packed restaurant in the early morning hours. The location is an easy walk from the main casinos. 

Definitely coming back here next time I'm in Reno.

Detroit style pizza????? Delicious!
We wanted to give Detroit style pizza a try and we are happy we did. 
Upon entering the restaurant the staff greeted and treated me very nicely. The place was very clean and has a good layout for a group or just couples. They offer about a dozen beers on tap with 4 stools at the bar to enjoy them.
We ordered a Detroit style pizza to-go. Since the pizza is a thick crust with crispy- crunchy edges, the pie takes a bit longer to bake. So grab a beer while your pizza bakes. It is worth the wait! The thick pizza dough has great flavor and is "airey" and crunchy. The red sauce is your traditional red sauce but they seem to add a good amount of oregano which takes it to the next level. 
We highly recommend this place for a great pizza! We look forward to our next visit.
Cheers Always!

4 stars for food, 4 stars for service, 4 stars for ambience

Occasion: eating with two friends on a weekday night out

Ambience: outdoor dining in a little curbside spot, not particularly well heated or cold, but well sectioned off

COVID19 precautions: Wait staff with masks and encouraging of patrons to keep masks on between food

Service: Hostess a little short at times with how she spoke to us, but overall was fine. A bit of a delay in between appetizers and entrees.

Food: 
Garlic bread - pretty great flavors, cheap at $5
BVP Meatballs - $13 - pretty sizeable, 2 for the plate, nice red sauce to pair with the bread
Rigatoni alla vodka $19 - sausage and pasta in little tubes shaped. Large plate. Pasta was maybe a little more firm than I was expecting, but overall was a great plate of food, worth the price. Slow to come out after the appetizers.
Tiramisu cannoli - a cute little way to end the meal, airy, light, sweet.

Tips/Takeaways:
-A beautiful restaurant
-Would recommend returning, the rigatoni dish is pretty great and I am always a sucker for garlic bread. Overall, a restaurant where you can't go wrong.

NOT AS ADVERTISED!  

I purchased a room with $75 free slot play and breakfast. Enrollment in their player card is required and comes with $25 slot play, but you must play for 30 minutes minimum (on moderately high loss machines) to receive a $75 voucher mailed someday. The breakfast is a cheap sloppy  bare-bones buffet in the other hotel. The room had badly stained carpeting, a malfunctioning coffee maker, stinky bathroom, nearly non-functional (yet free!) and room service was initially unavailable. 

The worst is the casino bar. No matter how long I stood at the front of the line to order - and face to face with the bartender - everyone behind me was served first and I was ignored and invisible until I started yelling at the staff for service, and even then only addressed reluctantly. No visible management to be found, no staff supervision or effective training, nobody cares- just another fuck-you-customer dump that deserves to be closed or go out of business. 

Don't bother with these assholes. Instead, go to the Bethlehem Sands Casino, or just stay home with a DVD or NetFlix.

There's only a few days left till the impending closing date of 3/31 mentioned in the Philly voice article.  If you want to solidify a pizza at this location read below:

1.) Get there before 3:45
I had two prior attempts before I succeeded on my third attempt.  It took getting there on a Wednesday  at 3:55.  I was the last pizza served that night!  My two prior attempts I got there after 4pm and both times was shut out. 

2.) Be ready to wait possibly til 10:30pm
If you're not getting there around 2pm or earlier to be the first person in line and get your pizza at 5:30 you'll most likely have to wait several hour.  There's two hour street parking around so you'll prob have to change parking spots to avoid a ticket or go home and wait there.

3.) If you are 21st in line you still may not get a pizza.  
People can order up to two pies each and most do!  I was 23rd in the line and got the last pie of the evening.  Don't believe the misnomer that you're 30th in line and he makes 40 pieces a day that you're going to get one.

4.) Police the line yourself.
As it gets closer to 5:30pm friends and significant others seem to hop the line next to the people the know.  This isn't cool and what was 2 pizzas ahead of you could very well be four.  
Specifically I'm talking about the dude who hop the line last Wednesday Feb 28th to meet his girlfriend in the maroon shirt. Yep total douche move the guy who got his pizza at 10pm that night.  Other people were considering asking the people if it was okay if they could leave real quick to grab beer but keep their spot.

Abiding by all the rules above you should be good.  Bring cash and get ready for some of the best pizza of your life!

Also, please click helpful, funny or useful below if you appreciate these tips!  Happy pizza hunting!

This place is one of our go to restaurants! The service is phenomenal. The food is fast, hot, and very generous proportions. The food is delicious and never disappoints. If you haven't tried Sparks Coffee Shop, you are missing out. The new spot is clean and well maintained, and the staff is always helpful and they take care of you without fail. Can't say enough good things about this gem!

Like consulting Pythia beneath the Castalian spring, I saw my mortality in the brick red chorizo oil. 
"Don't do it. Don't do it..."
"It will be delicious...delicious "
Echoes of an ageless battle between good and evil, between righteous and wretched...

Who am I kidding? Chorizo and queso blanco melted together with fresh jalapeño?
- I dove in with floaties made of soft warm flour tortillas!
The Choriqueso at Taco Giro is delicious. Dirty dirty delicious.
I've read this theory before (John M's review of Birrieria Guadalajara) that the scarier a Mexican restaurant looks on the outside, the more delicious the food will be on the inside. I gotta believe this to be true, and this certainly is the case for Taco Giro.
The restaurant is located on a semi-sketchy stretch of 22nd street, right next to a DQ and a Guero Canelo. 
The parking lot is rough, the neighborhood rough- but inside is some pretty tasty Mexican food.
Chips and magical refried bean sauce were brought to our table quickly. 
FYI, you get your own salsa from the salsa bar which has both hot, mild, and fresh tomato-onion-cilantro, pickled onions and roasted jalapeños. All good stuff.
(I mention this only because I stared at the empty bowl that was brought out with the chips...for like 5 minutes. It bugged me. What the hell is this for? Where is the salsa?)
Oh. Get your own, gringo.
I ordered a Bohemia...cold. No glass no lime, as intended.
My wife and I shared an appetizer of Choriqueso which comes with a small side of guacamole. My only gripe...only two yummy flour tortillas to gobble this molten love mass down. I'm sure I could have asked for more, but I didn't want to be that fat kid.
My wife ordered cheese enchiladas, which she enjoyed very much. She is a self proclaimed Mexican food snob, so when she says it's good- it's good. I ordered a shredded beef taco, cheese enchilada, rice and refried. All good- classic Tucson Mexican chow.
Service was good and pleasant, so thank you Lucía!
Taco Giro also serves up some mean Mexican seafood, super cheap fish tacos on Tuesdays, and some badass breakfasts- all with a full bar!
Taco Giro you are a keeper.

The fries were best part of this meal... Womp Womp.

It was opening night so we were ready for a decent wait. That being said we waited for over an hour and a half. It's a BYOB so at least we had a six pack that we completely finished before any of our food came out.

When it finally did we got our fries first, which came with a side of aioli- they are McDonald's style, maybe a little thinner and pretty delicious. The high hopes we had for our burgers was immediately diminished upon site of the bun- way too big and worst of all it was COLD (like it literally just came out of the fridge). I got a burger with gouda, the special sauce, and an onion ring on top (basically the P'unk burger without the bacon). Let me break it down, a great burger, to me, is all about that perfect balance between the juicy patty, the melty cheese, the crisp lettuce and maybe a tangy pickle in unobtrusive bun that just holds all the goodness together. This burger just tasted like sadness that tried really hard not to be so sad. 

Between the cold, thick bun, the beef patty was really dense, overcooked to a rubbery texture, overseasoned, and oversalted. The cold bun negated any meltiness the cheese would have had and the "special sauce", managing to be at the same time really acidic and really watery just served as another discordant flavor in this already haphazard burger. To top it off, the onion ring that I'd hoped to bring a nice crunch to the burger was mushy-- not crunchy in the least. That someone labored over this flavor profile and came out with this result leads me to think that it wasn't just a problem with execution, although better execution might have had me writing a slightly less scathing review... 

I appreciate that they are using organic, hormone free, grass fed beef, and I am all about paying for quality ingredients (base burger starts at $7.95), but all this means nothing if it doesn't taste like a delicious burger at its core.

I don't think I'll be back and I would not recommend this place for a burger on Passyunk. Fountain Porter and POPE both have way better burgers for a better price as well. Sorry!

Terrible customer service for sure and to me that is HUGE. On that note, it wasn't the worst experience I have had.

We made a reservation via a discount travel site for a night's stay last Wed. We were hitting up a show at the Amphitheater so it's a perfect location since it's literally a hop away.

Since the concert started early and we were driving from Orlando, we called the day before to confirm an early check-in and were told "sure, just arrive at noon and you will not have to wait more than an hour to check-in, there are tons of rooms available" so we thought we were good to go. Cut to the next day at noon when we arrive in the lobby and are told "Our system is down for maintenance so we can not currently check anyone in." Really? So it's routine maintenance and you didn't know this was going to happen yesterday? Fail. So we were told to wait an hour, which was reasonable... we will just go lay by the pool and relax... OH WAIT... The pool is under construction FOR THREE MONTHS. WHAT? Who fixes their pool in FLORIDA in SUMMER??? Huge fail. And on top of that, since we booked through another site, we did not receive the note that the pool was closed, which I think is also the hotel's fault for not making sure it was clearly stated. Also, when we called to get early check-in, they didn't note the pool closure. 

Well, one hour, ok, we will go grab a drink, check-in an hour later, we are told it will be at least another hour, so, being so passionate about customer service, I approached the third, yes third employee to discuss the situation and I request a Manager so I don't have to keep repeating what we have been through communication wise. The manager was clearly un-phased and did not offer anything to compensate for our terrible experience. Think about when you are stuck at an airport for a layover and they offer meal vouchers, nope not here. Not even a drink voucher. 

Then we check in again... YES, almost 4 hours we had to wait... so by this time it was regular check-in time of 4 pm... are you serious??? We asked for an upgrade since we waited so long, nope, just told "no." Jessica R was with me and she took the time to call home office and request that corporate be aware of the situation and she was assured they would contact the hotel. We never heard anything about it during our stay. Another customer service fail. 

So beyond the terrible customer service, which they had various times to try and recover from, the stay wasn't all that bad. Yes, there is smoke EVERYWHERE but it's an old person mecca because of the gambling and lack of nightlife in the area. 

The room was very nice but had a horrendous view, just the roof of a part of the hotel. The beds were very comfortable and a lovely tub. Other than that, pretty normal. 

I am still so underwhelmed due to the customer service and no huge selling points. Bad customer service makes me so sad. 

If I ever feel the need to stay at a Hard Rock Hotel in the near future, I am heading to the one is Fort Lauderdale!!! And if I need a place to stay in Tampa... this ain't going to be it folks!

St. Louis you have delicious BBQ! Thank you.

We were in this city for 2 hours, that's it. We went right to the source and asked Aimee (and Yelp!) what the #1 spot for dinner was that was open and had no wait. The Shaved Duck was it! It was a Friday evening so we did wait about 15 min, not bad at all. There was seating outside so we grabbed a table out there as it was a gorgeous evening. Loved the local, neighborhood vibe of this location too, truly a fab experience. 

Our server was fabulous! So very welcoming, charming and funny. He truly added to the experience and helped us cruise around the menu with some great suggestions. 

Everyone has to start with the Buttermilk Cornbread, right? Right.
Served in cast iron skillet with side of honey butter it was delicious. I could have easily taken some to go for breakfast. 

One of my favorite dishes to make at home is meatloaf. I reluctantly ordered the Smoked Meatloaf as it's super hard to impress me. I have to say, I am not a huge smoke fan but the root beer glaze served with this made the dish. It was a heavenly addition and was the star. Such a robust flavor that added the pizazz you want when you order meatloaf. 

The Baby Back Ribs were legit. House rub, smoked with cherry wood, glazed, yes. 

Our sides were the Mac n cheese and Sautéed Brussels sprouts - perfect pairing here. 

Thanks for your evening hospitality, St. Louis!

Yelp to the rescue! In town for the afternoon with my friends, we were looking for a place to eat before our trek back to Orlando. I yelped "lunch" and this place popped up and we couldn't deny the amazing reviews.

By the vampire costume outside we knew we picked a cool place. We chose to sit in the front near the large windows and comfy booth. We were immediately greeted by our amazing server and she was on par the entire visit! 

Cider you ask, YEP! Guacamole to eat for hours on end, yep! Just wish the tortilla chips were a little less wholesale club tasting. I went with the pork quesadilla amazingness and it delivered! I tasted Lisa D's German potato salad and WOW... delicious. 

This place was so chill that if I lived here, I know I would use this spot as my office. It was clean, the decor was fun and it was extremely open and relaxing.

I'm always hesitant to try a new Tex-Mex place. It's like trying a new move in bed...either you come off as a certified rock star, or, well "it happens to everyone."
The atmosphere in velvet is spot on. Great patio...open sports bar...decent indoor seating...and lots of local characters for people watching ( I saw a twenty something year old girl fending off 3 old dudes...reminded me of a scene from the old Mutual of Omaha wild kingdom).
The margaritas were just what a city that prides itself on boozing demands and was lacking (see superior grills pre-fab Rita as how not to do it). Not syrupy sweet, made with fresh juice, and muy fuerte ( that's strong for you gringos).
But the food...meh. Not bad, not great...just there. The ingredients were indeed fresh, but the execution was off. Mole is not red...ceviche is not tart...pork pibil is smokey, not verde. 
I think this place deserves 3.5 stars and the owner seemed determined to perfect the food (heard him admit the recipes need tweaking). It's that pursuit of good eats that will bring me back here. I'm sure that much like the nice, tame librarian who proceeds to porn star you...the potential is hidden. 
Buen provecho!

It's a crazy thing when you have a business with a name nobody can pronounce!  It's hilarious to listen to folks give it a shot.  Lots of folks don't even try and just say- "Let's go to that great ice cream place behind MickyDs!"  I don't care if the name is Satan's Playground.  I just want great ice cream and you can find that here.

You can drive through the Trooper/Egypt intersection a hundred times and not spot this place.  Like I said, look behind the McDonald's. 

There are two important points you need to know-

1. In addition to chocolate and vanilla they only have one other flavor per day.  Actually they usually change flavors every two days.  One example is Monkey Business.  Its banana ice cream with walnuts and chocolate chunks and it is delicious. A regular cone is $2.50.  You can check for the flavor of the day on Facebook.

2. Their ice cream is less sweet (less sugar) than most.  I know that sounds strange but it really is a pleasant change.  When you see the mob of people on a nice summer night you'll know that I'm not the only one that enjoys it.

You can purchase lots of other sweets here like candy and cupcakes but the big draw is the ice cream.  Sometimes I stop in and just get a shake.  A small with tax is $3.98.  It's thick and creamy and really hits the spot.

Although it can get busy I've found the customer service to be just fine. Lots of folks that are doing stuff around the KOP area make the quick detour and stop here for a tasty treat.  It's worth it.

If you want to visit The Porch you need to like three (3) things-

1.  They don't call it the "Tavern" for nothing.  You need to appreciate the decades old historic building look and feel.

2. A classic New American menu with everything you have come to expect from this style of cuisine and no surprises.  The crowd here is mixed in age but a notch older than most.  Those older folks don't like no darn surprises.

3. The pleasure of suburban dining with a nice big parking lot and minimal traffic hassles.

If these things appeal to you than you should have a nice time.  It's not a cheap date but it's in line with fine dining in the burbs.  Entrees tend to be split between high teens and the twenties.  For example Chicken Chesapeake (Boneless breast, crab imperial, lobster sauce, Yukon gold potatoes and vegetable) is $18.99.  Lobster & Shrimp Risotto (Sautéed shrimp & lobster meat, rich shellfish broth, and creamy risotto) is $21.99. 
 
Expect your diner to be well served and the portion size to be at least normal and usually more.  With an appetizer you should leave pleasantly full.  As mentioned no surprises here.  You will walk out with a small smile on your face but you won't be raving about the innovative cuisine.  It's a solid three star place.

In every large city there are eateries that if you ask a native about them you'll hear "tourist trap!"  Is the City Tavern popular with tourists?  You bet but don't dismiss them so quickly.  They deserve a look and a taste.

The atmosphere is wonderful and you are surrounded by history complete with period costumes for the staff.  Said staff is also very knowledgeable about the early years of our country.  

As for the food, as many have said the recipes are supposedly from this time period.  Most of it is quite heavy.  I find it good but definitely not great.  I do have a problem with the price point of the menu.  With a drink or two, if you're not careful you can easily blow past $50 and head towards $75.  For that price I expect a lot and for me they are not quite there.

I suggest you try them for lunch before you commit to dinner.  Even lunch won't be cheap but it will give you a chance to see if you like the style of food.

I'm passionate about patronizing local businesses so I go here from time to time and keep hoping and praying they'll change.  Unfortunately they don't.  They're surviving because they have a decent location and are open 24/7. 

Every time I visit I experience mediocre food, service, and atmosphere.  By the way, don't let the pastry case fool you.  The selections look beautiful but the ingredients are not high quality so the taste is definitely substandard.  

If you are thinking about this place you're likely on West Chester Pike.  Do yourself a favor and keep on driving.  You won't need to go far.  Luckily for you there two other great diner choices and one is in each direction.

As I'm a helpful kind of guy, I'll give you a hand with the directions.  Go two miles west and you'll find the Hot Spot Diner.  It's on the same side of the street as the Country Squire.  It's not open 24/7 but they do have extended hours and you'll have a much much better meal.

What if you prefer to head east?  Travel 3.5 miles to the route 1 intersection and turn left.  As soon as you turn you'll be staring at Llanerch Diner.  This place is a Delaware County institution and is open 24/7. Once again you'll enjoy a much better meal.

So if you decide to try one of my alternative choices your taste buds will thank you!

Google "Sign Language" before you visit and get up to speed as that's the only way you'll be able to communicate!  The noise level here is simply stunning and the loudest I have ever experienced in decades of dining.  I've spoken to several folks that have visited here and it's sad when every conversation has a "but" in it.  "Great potential but..."  "Yummy food but..."  "Wonderful pizza but..."  Of course that but is that you can't hear yourself think!  

The lovely wife and I visited Wednesday night around 7 pm.  It was packed with a twenty minute wait.  They kept their promise and we were at our table in fifteen minutes.  The atmosphere is casual contemporary Italian and would be warm and welcoming expect for the noise.

Our waiter appeared promptly with wonderful warm, fresh bread and dipping sauce.  We expected that as we are huge fans of Pizzeria DiMeo's.  So often in new restaurants the customer service is lacking as they work out the kinks.  That was not the case here as we had excellent service throughout the evening. By the way, don't forget to bring your wine as these folks are BYOB.

We decided to begin our evening with. ASSAGGI DI SALUMI & FORMAGGI. This is a tasting of artisan cured meats and cheeses accompanied with condiments for $25.  This is clearly an appetizer meant for sharing.  It arrived promptly on an expected wooden board and included three high quality meats and three delicious cheeses.  The quantity of condiments was very sad and would barely qualify as a garnish, never mind something intended to be part of the dish. Everything would have fit in a teaspoon.  It would also help if a bread product was added to the board.  For $25 we expected more.

The owners are well known for their pizza and we ordered the MAIS ($16).  The toppings on this amazing creation are roasted corn, baby heirloom tomatoes, speck and fior di latte.  It arrived promptly and we'll remember it for years!  Incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked.  Just a little char on the crust.  Every bite bursting with flavor.  This is the kind of pie that makes you roll your eyes with delight.

So what's the verdict?  Unfortunately the noise level tainted the experience for us and overshadowed everything else.  The lovely wife said it best- "I'd rather drive to DiMeo's in Andorra and enjoy very similar food in a much more pleasing atmosphere."  I agree.

A little slice of South Philly in the Burbs!  Hoagies from here can truly hold their own against Italian Market completion and they're on Route 1 in Drexel Hill.

To me, the first characteristic of a great hoagie is that you need to be able to taste every ingredient.  If the taste of any one overwhelms the others, that hoagie was botched.  Pagano's has really got their act together.  The ingredients of every hoagie I have tried blend together in a happy Italian marriage on my tongue.

Of course my second characteristic is a great roll.  Once again these guys get it right.  I get a little crunch on the outside and a nice soft interior.  The icing on the cake is that delightful taste of yeast from the bread intermingling with everything else.

One hoagie I really enjoy is the 49th Street Special.  It includes Ham, Ham Capicolla, Di Lusso Genoa Salami, Prosciutto, and Sharp Provolone Cheese, with lettuce, tomato, onion, oil and seasonings.  A large is $7.79 and a serious meal.  Another is the Italian Hoagie Pagano for the same price.  It includes  Ham, Ham Capicolla, Di Lusso Genoa Salami, Broccoli di Rabe, Sharp Provolone Cheese and Roasted Sweet or Fried Hot Peppers.  Once you include Broccoli Rabe in a hoagie I tend to fall in lust!

One final note on this place is the knowledgeable and pleasant people.  Every time I walk out of here I have a little smile on my face.

I love the smell of a dive bar in the morning!  A little bit musty along with that stale beer tang and just a hint of cleaning products.  I stopped in for an early lunch yesterday at 11:30 and smiled at the aroma.

If you are looking for a classic dive bar you've found it. It has zero presence from the outside.  It's long and narrow on the inside with lots of dark wood and dim lighting.  If you plan on looking at the menu, plan on using your flashlight app. The grill is behind the bar and visible to all.

Speaking of menus, expect bar food.  We're talking burgers and cheese steaks and sausage sandwiches.  I ordered a cheeseburger and fries and the two went for just under $10.  By the way, CASH ONLY.

My burger was a frozen patty that was not very thick. It was served on a soft Kaiser roll.  It was hot and juicy but otherwise nothing to write home to Mom about.  My fries were frozen from a bag and had that weird coating on them that doesn't ring my bells.  However they were hot and crispy.  I have a good friend that would call this kind of food fuel.

My drinks were cheap and the bartender was excellent.  The guy working the grill was also great and interacts with the customers so overall customer service was just fine.

I'd be happy to stop back for an adult libation or two or three.  I'd give them another shot on the food and try something different.

Best Bloody Mary in America!  That's not a bad thing to be able to crow about if you're trying to make a name for yourself. Check out the link.

http://www.delcotimes.com/lifestyle/20141030/tavola-restaurant-in-springfield-voted-best-bloody-mary-in-america

I've visited here many times over many years and have watched it evolve.  Keep in mind that it is part of the Springfield Country Club complex.  It's also interesting that a Marriott Courtyard recently opened in the complex and as a result they have enjoyed a significant increase in business.

The atmosphere here is the star of the show.  There is lots of wood and subdued lighting. The bar is comfortable. On a beautiful summer night it doesn't get much better than the outside seating.  It's clearly one of the classiest places in Delaware County.  So folks come here expecting upscale service and food and they don't get it.  Read on and I'll explain why I think that is.

The country club does a booming banquet business so much of the staff that touches you at dinner could be working on banquet lunches etc. at other times.  So they act like hotel severs and don't have the refinement you would expect in this beautiful space.

The same is true of the food.  There is something for everyone on the menu and it looks and feels just like a hotel menu.  The prices are not bad.  Chicken Parmesan goes for $13 and Salmon Dijon $16.  It will be OK but you'll find yourself expecting more.

So to me it's mismatched expectations.  You're in this gorgeous upscale space and the service and food is what you would expect at a Sheraton.  Until they can resolve this mismatch, I'm going with three stars.

Location and atmosphere are huge contributors to the success of a restaurant and this place has both in spades!  Add some seriously decent pub grub and you have a joint that has some staying power.

The atmosphere incorporates two floors. I would call it classy lite.  If you are having dinner you'll be on the first floor and the bar is on the second.  Both floors are deep and narrow and when it's busy it can get a little tricky to move around.  The trees growing through to the second floor are a wonderful accent as is the second floor window wall that opens in good weather.  On a nice summer evening the bar would be a great place to bring out-of-town guests.  One negative note; the bar stools that are also used at the upstairs high-top tables are very uncomfortable.  If you are there for any length of time they will literally be a pain in the butt!

The upscale pub grub menu is not particularly big but all of it will be decent.  My fellow Yelpers are correct in that this will be 3 or 3  1/2 star food.  There is one exception.  The hand-cut fries are INSANELY GOOD!  A large portion served in a metal bucket for $4 is a hell of a deal and they are completely addictive.  It should be a crime to visit here and not order them.

Adult libations are priced fairly.  There is a decent craft section and a solid list of specialty drinks.  Expect plenty of Happy Hour deals.  I'd happily return here any time for a solid 3 star or better experience.

I'm a fan of this chain.  The lovely wife and I have been to the Plymouth Meeting location many times.  I have also visited the Kennett Square location.  So I'm up in the KOP area running errands and I thought I'd check out their newest location for lunch. They have been open about a month.

I was stunned when I walked in the door.  The décor is much different and much nicer than the other locations I've seen.  It's clear the owners were going for an upscale look and they have succeeded.  This is one beautiful restaurant.  I was seated at the bar where I could watch other folks entering and just about everyone had this pleasantly surprised look on their faces as they experienced the look and feel of this place.

Speaking of the bar, it seats about twelve and is very nice.  My bartender was from the Plymouth Meeting location as were some other employees.  As I sipped on a beer in a nice frosted mug and chatted with him he noted that the menu and the prices are exactly the same as Plymouth Meeting.  He also mentioned that the tequila selection here was not as large due to space issues.

I perused the very familiar menu and ordered a standard taco-enchilada combo lunch for $7.99.  It arrived quickly and was nicely plated on the usual very hot plate.  It was delicious but seemed a little under seasoned compared to Plymouth Meeting.  Maybe it was just me that day or maybe the chefs need a little more practice with spices.  I'm sure I'll be back to check it out.  I did not experience any of the kinks so common in a new restaurant.  Keeping in mind that this is a chain you can expect a solid Mexican meal at a decent price.

RELIABLE!

If you're a chain, and of course they are, that's a good word.  I have a habit of going here before I go to the movies and that was the case yesterday.  Who wants to pay concession stand prices!

The wait staff and bartenders have been reliably friendly and mostly competent.  

Most of the entrees are reliably huge and too much for most folks.  I find that slightly annoying if you are dining alone and have no one to share with.

I find most of the food decent but reliably under seasoned except for salt which is   used with abandon at least to my tastes.

As many have said, the waffle fries are reliably amazing!

I spotted DEVILED EGGS ($7) on the menu and I can never resist them.  There were six of these bad boys and they were topped with Applewood-smoked bacon, fresh tomato, and avocado.  As you can see from my pic they were plated beautifully and looked damm good.  Fortunately for me they were!

To me this is a solid three star place.  If you are there to watch a game probably 3 1/2.

As you look at the front entrance in this small suburban plaza, you would never guess what delights lie within.  Step inside to experience casual yet fine Mexican dining done exceptionally well.

First timer's heads swivel a bit when they walk in as they try to see the other rooms.  Guess what, there are no other rooms!  One glance and you've seen it all.  The décor is over-the-top Mexican but the overall effect is warm and inviting.  The lovely wife and I enjoyed it.  We were seated on time with OpenTable reservations.

We perused the large drink menu and the lovely wife went for the 100 calorie Skinny Margarita for $10.  I ordered the Patron Marg for $12.  Both were excellent and served in interesting non-standard glassware.  The wife was incredulous that her drink was only 100 calories.  It was that good!

We went crazy with a shared appetizer and ordered the PLATON DE BOTANAS for $20.  This is their appetizer sampler and it's meant for more than two people but we wanted the variety. It was the perfect decision!  Explosions of flavor from several different well-seasoned delights.  In included the best guacamole we have EVER had. EVER!

Our waiter this evening was Paco and he was excellent the entire night so customer service was not a problem.

For entrees my wife ordered SALMON TROPICAL - This was broiled fresh Salmon marinated and seasoned with spices and herbs. It was covered with citrus-tamarindo and mango sweet sauces and served with flag rice and spring mix salad for $18.  

I ordered ALBONDIGAS AL CHIPOTLE - Mixed ground meats, formed into delicious meatballs with a cheese center. Simmered in smokey spicy chipotle-chorizo sauce. Served over our refried black beans with rice on the side and garnished with cilantro and corn tortilla strips for $15.  

We both agreed our dishes were inventive and superb!  Nicely plated and correctly seasoned.  Portion size was just fine.  This was one of the finest Mexican meals we have ever experienced and we'll be returning again soon!

You may say "What the hell is Steven B. doing sending me to this hole-in-the-wall, parking challenged, and out-of-the-way joint."  Just look at the reviews and trust me, I know these things!

Doc's ten steps to eternal life!

1.  Check your cholesterol before you visit and buy any ginormous cheesesteak or hoagie.  If you are by yourself and order fries you are INSANE!

2.  Marvel at the price vs. quantity equation.  This place is a GREAT VALUE!

3.  As it's take out only, run to the car tearing off the paper with one hand and wiping the drool off your chin with the other.

4.  Gaze at the massive amount of meat and cheese and roll your eyes and moan.

5.  Wolf down bite after bite of high quality perfection and wonder as your stomach swells.

6.  Wrap up the last half, rush home and TAKE A NAP!

7.  Wake up and agonize over eating the other half.

8.  Give in; eat the other half and TAKE ANOTHER NAP!

9.  Wake up and Google high cholesterol.  

10.  Take a few minutes and write a wonderful Yelp review.

Chef Ferro didn't know it but we seriously put him to the test one night last month.  Not one, not two, but three Yelp Elites and serious foodies showed up to put him to the test.  Although not a Yelper the lovely wife was along for the ride and she has a very discerning palate.

SO WHAT WAS THE TEST?  We ordered four DIFFERENT entrees and four DIFFERENT appetizers to see if Phil had the depth and breadth of experience and talent to blow us out of the water.  Guess what he did it!  After many many visits this wonderful BYOB is easily the premier dining destination in Havertown and challenges many restaurants in the surrounding towns!

My Yelp Elite daughter (Jennifer B.) posted several pics including-

* Herb roasted pork chop with golden raisin and white peach chutney.
* Coconut crusted shrimp with roasted pineapple gastrique.
* Pesto roasted salmon.
* Strawberries over pound cake.
* Cheesecake topped with berries.

We had an amazing meal with a diversity that would have challenged any chef and Phil did a superb job!  Forget going into the city.  Stop by here and enjoy suburban fine dining at its very best!

Everyone makes mistakes myself included.  My mistake was not coming here sooner! I had a very good lunch here yesterday and I'll definitely be back for more.

This place is easy to miss as its set way back from Chester Pike and is very small.  One way to find it is to roll down your window and zero in on the amazing aromas coming from the smokers. 

Any discussion about ATMOSPHERE will be quick.  It's a takeout only hole-in-the-wall with only a tiny little room to stand and place your order.  There are two picnic benches outside where most folks wait for their orders to be ready.  Of course you could also eat there.  That happens quite a bit because everything smells so damn good you don't want to wait until you get home.

CUSTOMER SERVICE is not a problem.  These are friendly folks and as you place your order you can see into the open kitchen and chat with everyone.

The menu was completely as expected.  All the typical BBQ joint choices are there.  I went with the two meat combo which comes with two sides and cornbread for about $14.  I chose smoked kielbasa, brisket, corn and coleslaw. I was asked if I wanted caramelized onions on my kielbasa and I told them to go for it.

I gotta tell you, the meats were 5+ stars delicious.  The brisket was sliced very thin and perfectly sauced.  The kielbasa was off the hook amazing and the onions were perfect on it.  It may be the best kielbasa I've ever had.

My sides were just ok. The corm was good with some bbq seasoning.  The cornbread was moist but nothing special.  My coleslaw was very fresh but the dressing was seriously lacking in flavor.  They were all compliantly overshadowed by the amazing meats!

On my next visit I'll likely try one of their huge sandwiches and skip the sides.

If there is a heaven for carnivores this is it. So assuming you partake of flesh this is my Top 10 Tips for first timers-

1. If your MD is watching your cholesterol have it checked now before you go.
2. Don't eat all day.
3. As you dress for this occasion make certain your pants/skirt waist and accompanying belt easily expands.
4. Consume enough adult libations to dull any silly thoughts about diets or the evils of gluttony. Fogo's drinks are pricy so consider getting a head start elsewhere.
5. Once you arrive, gaze at the beautifully arranged salad bar and make one pass with just one plate please.  Marvel at the taste of fresh produce and cheeses.
6. The plate of warm cheese bread delivered to your table will be calling you.  Resist as long as you can but realize that it's inevitable and that you will succumb.
7. Watch the Gauchos swirling around the other tables and begin to make preliminary choices in your head.  Be sure to keep wiping the drool off your chin.  It's unsightly.  
8. Turn your poker chip to green side up and let the Gauchos attack!  Keep in mind that Fogo's meats are wonderfully seasoned so you may find unexpected delights.  Go "red" when your plate is covered with delicious flesh.
9. Repeat step 8 several times.
10.  Laugh hysterically when desert is offered.

If breakfast is the most important meal of the day it seems like it's often difficult to find a good place.  Fortunately as a huge supporter of all things Havertown we now have the Havertown Grill.

These folks are in the short strip of stores between Hoopty's Pizza and Katz Pharmacy.  Parking is a breeze thanks to the public lot next to Hoopty's.  It's a tiny place with stools at the counter for maybe six and about ten tables.  Most are 2-tops with a couple of 4-tops thrown in.  The spacing is tight so be prepared to love thy neighbor!  You're not coming here for the atmosphere but because you're hungry.

The lovely wife and I stopped in this morning at about 9 am and the place was very busy.  We snagged a middle seat and perused the simple menu.  It's a single 8X10 sheet with one side for breakfast and the other for lunch.  These folks are not open for dinner.

The best way to describe this menu is standard comfort food.  Fortunately it's comfort food done very well.  We both ordered omelets.  I choose Florentine and my wife picked the Greek version.  They come with your choice of toast and hash browns and go for about $7.  

They came out quickly and were plated nicely.  The fillings for the omelets were plentiful and fresh.  The hash browns were excellent and not greasy but need a little seasoning.  I would have liked a few onions in them but that's a personal preference.  The toast is served dry with plenty of butter and jams available. 
 
Throughout our meal the service was outstanding.  Never a problem with coffee or water refills.  We were in and out with our bellies full in well under an hour.

There are a few other spots to grab breakfast in Havertown but these folks will be on our short list.

I was the first to review this terrific restaurant back in 2011.  Since then I have been back many times and it's easy to see how they have earned a solid four star rating.  Note that these folks are BYOB and many folks think that a good beer goes well with the often spicy food.

The lovely wife and I stopped in tonight with a friend. The three of us often visit the restaurants along this strip and we all agree that these folks have the nicest décor and their establishment is always immaculately clean. 
We ordered-
Tom Yum (chicken). One small and one large for $3 and $10.
Chicken Spring Rolls $4.
Grilled rib-eye steak with spicy jaew sauce $7
Chicken Satay $7
Pad Thai with shrimp 8.50.

The large Tom Yum soup would feed a family and was seriously spicy.  My wife pronounced it excellent.  The spring rolls were crispy on the outside and packed with chicken.  This is the third time I've enjoyed the rib-eye steak and I'm in love.  Note that it is an appetizer portion.  It's served thinly sliced and cooked to a perfect pink in the middle.  You can taste the grill flavor and the jaew sauce goes perfectly with it.  As I type this I'm smiling with the memory of it.  The Pad Thai was a large portion with nice sized shrimp.

Throughout our meal the service was excellent.  We have been served by the same young women many times and have always been pleased.

There are certainly many Thai restaurants in the area but we keep returning here again and again.

If you are looking for fine Italian dining with a full bar in the Western suburbs, this is a solid choice.

I'm going to get the two negatives out of the way first so I can focus on the many positives.

The lovely wife and I had 8:15 OpenTable reservations on a recent Saturday.  Parking was INSANE!  The closest public lot was full. Uggggh.  We just barely parked in the next closest lot and had to hoof it a couple of blocks. 

When we opened the door to the restaurant we were greeted by a blast of noise. Once again the word I would use is INSANE.  The front bar was three deep and there were boat loads of folks waiting for tables.  Thank God for OpenTable as our table was waiting for us.  Just to be clear, the noise level was through the roof!

Note to self- Visit on a weekday night!

Our waiter was Bill and he was beyond superb.  How is this for an opening sentence- "I'm here to exceed your expectations!"  I have visited restaurants with Michelin stars and experienced lesser service.  Kudos to the management

The menu here is extensive and it's hard to believe it couldn't satisfy almost everyone.  We ordered the antipasto plate.  We consider ourselves experts with Antipasto/Charcuterie plates and this one was up there with the best we have ever experienced.  The accompaniments were numerous and delicious.

For entrees I ordered the Braised Shortrib Ravioli ($19) and the lovely wife ordered the Hanger Steak special. Both dishes were an easy four stars.

So what was the tab? Complimentary bruschetta, an excellent antipasto plate, two entrees, four drinks and of course complimentary Limoncello shots to end our fine meal equaled $100.  For us this was a solid value.

I'd visit here again in a heartbeat but only on a weekday night!

I hope the vegans don't burn me at the stake because I'm giving this place a solid well deserved three stars. Wait a minute; if vegans are burning me at the stake they are cooking meat and they'd never do that!  Let's try again.  I hope the vegans don't throw me off the Ben Franklin Bridge.

I've only been here for a weekday lunch but I've been several times, usually as part of a party of three or four.  One look at the menu and you know the vegetarian folks are going to be on cloud nine.  If you are a true carnivore like me it's clear you are not their target customer but you will be able to find some flesh to eat.  I've tried their Cobb Salad (with chicken), Grilled Chicken Breast sandwich, and Mexican Cheese Steak.

In Yelp terms three stars is A-OK and that's how I feel about these folks.  Every lunch I have eaten here has been solid. I've never had a bad meal.  The wait staff has been solid and the atmosphere is pleasant.  The pricing is appropriate.  

So why three stars?  In order for me to go four stars I need for something to occasionally make me go wow!  Not every time but once in a while it needs to happen and that has not occurred for me.

If you asked me about going to lunch at Farmicia I would say "Go, you'll enjoy yourself."

The word "Fermentaria" connotes strange things in my mind.  Does it mean that this is where very old beer aficionados go to die and get turned into ashes?  In this case it might mean die of happiness as this is a very good beer emporium with excellent food to boot.

I blew in here on a Thursday around 2:30 for a late lunch.  Even at this odd time the place was jumping.  I can't say I'm a fan of the ATMOSPHERE.  It was a warehouse and it still looks and feels and echoes like a warehouse.  A place for a romantic dinner it's not.  I can say I'm a fan of the parking.  $.25 for 30 minutes in a lot directly outside is a very nice convenience.

There is a law that says you can't look at the menu without sipping on a BEER.  I ordered Alien Church.  I'm told this excellent IPA has been the fastest selling brew since they opened and I loved it. I also tried Reactionary and it was tasty but didn't compare to Alien.

My bartender was just fine with the appropriate amount of knowledge and attentiveness.  It was amazing how many growler orders he was filling.  I had no problems with CUSTOMER SERVICE.

For lunch I ordered Carnitas Tacos for $10.  The fillings were braised pork, guacamole, pickled red onion and queso fresco.  I was quickly served two 5 STAR tacos plated beautifully.  These bad boys were heavy with fillings and worth every penny of the $10.  They were excellent!  Others have complained about the pricing but I must say I didn't feel it with this dish.

I can easily overlook the unusual atmosphere in return for great beer and interesting delicious food.  I'll be back.

Every once and a while the missus and I like to sneak down to the Wilmington area for some tax free shopping.  We usually hit the malls along route 202.  

Harry's is across the street from most of the stores.  This is a serious steakhouse with prices in line with others of this genre.  It has a huge parking lot so finding a space is almost always a snap.  The building doesn't look like much from the outside but don't judge this book by its cover.  Inside the rooms are impressive and elegant.  As others have stated, this is probably not the time for jeans and a t-shirt.  

I'll spare you several paragraphs on the food.  Expect a fine steakhouse meal.  Their specialty is prime rib so it that's your craving you're in the right place.  By the way, the prime rib sandwich for lunch is amazing!

The bar here is especially nice.  I'd make a point to have a pre-dinner drink here first.

A homogenized, pasteurized, suburbanized Vietnamese experience.  That's not necessarily a bad thing but it's a far cry from the tiny family-run joints in downtown Philly or Terminal Square in Upper Darby. It's also entirely different from giants like 11th Street's Vietnam and Vietnam Palace.  

So imagine you are blindfolded and plopped in the middle of this restaurant.  Your blindfold is whipped off and you examine the room.  You'd swear you were in a New American restaurant in anytown USA.  To me there is zero Asian influence in the décor. In fairness, it's bright and clean and contemporary.  It just feels a little weird to eat Vietnamese cuisine in this atmosphere.  If little hole-in-the-wall joints bother you, you're going to love it here.

The lovely wife and I both agreed that our waiter today was just fine.  He was friendly, competent, and attentive and didn't appear to be of Asian descent.  That seemed to be true of most of the wait staff here.  If you are one of those folks bothered by a bit of a language barrier in an ethnic restaurant, you'll be pleased here.

The menu here is gigantic with everything you would expect in a Vietnamese establishment.  The wife enjoyed Banh Hoi Bo Nuong - This is charbroiled beef with fine vermicelli; served with lettuce, herbs, cucumber, crushed peanuts, and fish sauce for $9.95. She has enjoyed this dish dozens of times in Terminal Square and pronounced it yummy and about equal in taste, quality and price. She wanted a glass of bubble tea to go with it but sadly that tasty classic brew was not on the menu.  Our waiter specifically told her that management felt it would not sell in the suburbs.  Hmmmm.

I ordered Crispy Spring Rolls for $3.95.  They were beautifully plated, tasty and not oily but a little heavy for me.  I followed that with Banh Hoi Bo Nuong La - This was grilled seasoned ground beef wrapped in grape leaves with fine vermicelli; served with lettuce, herbs, cucumber, crushed peanuts, and fish sauce for $9.55.  Like my wife, I found it tasty and the price was similar to other places.

These folks are a BYOB and there is a $5 per table corkage fee.  Bring in a single bottle of beer with a twist off cap and it's going to cost you five bucks to open it!  That is out-of-line, incredibly annoying, and needs to change.

I agonized over awarding my stars to these folks.  As I can't do 3.5 I'm going with 3.  It's the atmosphere that's throwing me off.  I love those little hole-in-the-wall joints but I can easily see how others would go 4 stars.

So you're a tourist and it's a beautiful sunny Saturday in the City of Brotherly Love.  What to do, what to do? The heck with the Liberty Bell.  The heck with climbing the "Rocky" steps.  Why don't you make it a market day? 

Put on sturdy walking shoes and grab a couple of reusable tote bags.  If you don't have them don't worry, you can easily buy them when needed.  Stroll on over to the Reading Terminal Market for breakfast.  If you are staying in center city it's likely and easy walk.  You may want to try the Dutch Eating Place but there are lots of places to choose from.   As this is an Italian market review I'll save a detailed description of Reading Terminal for another time.

Now it's time to head for South Philly.  I strongly suggest you walk to the Italian Market.  Yes it may be a bit of a trek for some but here's the deal.  You get an up close and personal look at one of the most interesting parts of Philly.  You are going to be spending a good part of the day here.  You'll have lunch and maybe even dinner.  You may even have an adult libation, or two, or three.  Your tote bags are also going to be loaded with great stuff.  Tonight will be the time to take a cab back to your hotel.  It's only a few bucks and you're going to be tired.  Trust me it's the way to go.  

So you made it!  You're at 9th and Fitzwater which is the top of the market.  Before you begin you have two big decisions to make.

Decision #1 - What is your plan of attack.  The great majority of folks are loop people.  They go down one side of the street and up the other and end up back where they started.  There are a few wild and crazy folks I call the zigzag nuts.  They bounce back and forth from one side of the street to the other.  When they get to the bottom of the market they are done.

I strongly suggest the loop method.  Actually, assuming you are a 1st timer, I suggest you do the loop twice.  The first time, just stroll past all the wonderful shops without stopping. Marvel at the variety.  Sometimes folks emit soft moans when one of the many wonderful aromas wafts by.  Don't worry the market folks are used to that.   An occasional OMG is also fine.   It will take you about thirty minutes and give you an idea of what you're in for.   Now do the loop again stopping at the shops of your choice.

Decision #2 - You also need to determine your eating method.  Most folks are the nibblers.  There are so many interesting and delicious tidbits to try they just can't resist.  The problem is that leaves no room for lunch and/or dinner.   Of course you can try to resist temptation and save yourself room for real meals.  I suggest you split the difference.  Nibble away but save room for a late lunch.  Nibble some more and pass on dinner at the market.  You'll be too stuffed anyway.

So do I have any recommendations you ask?  Absolutely!  Definitely have lunch at Paesano's II.  You'll have one of the best and most interesting sandwiches in your life. Some other places worth of a visit are Dibrunos, Fantes, Espisitios, Claudio's and Tortilleria San Roman.  When it's time to rest your feet and enjoy an adult libation try The Wishing well especially if you appreciate a good beer selection.

It doesn't get much better than spending a sunny day at the Italian Market.  Definitely a five (5) star experience!

Perhaps the finest BUFFET BRUNCH VALUE on the mainline @ $23! The lovely wife and I had an excellent dinner here in May (previous review) and learned of the Sunday brunch.  We returned and found it simply amazing.  It was so good and such a tremendous value that this week was our fourth visit!

So what would you say about omelets made to order, a free mimosa, and twenty or thirty buffet choices, and UNLIMITED FILET MIGNON for $23!  "What the hell" you say, "how come I'm missing this!"

First, a word about the atmosphere- This is an elegant restaurant with beautiful décor.  What's great is you can still dress casually.  There will be some folks dressed up but that's the exception and definitely not the rule.  Nice jeans are not a problem here.

Second, another word about the customer service- I realize you don't need to be a rocket scientist to staff a buffet but never the less our servers have always been excellent.  Our plates have been cleared quickly and our drinks served promptly.

Third- What is the adult libation situation?  There is a solid, inventive specialty drink list and also many wines available by the glass.  Expect most to set you back about $10.  Don't forget that your first mimosa is complementary! 

Finally, WHAT ABOUT THEIR FOOD?  I know it sounds strange but they offer both American and Japanese choices.  On the American side there is an omelet station, bacon, sausage, crepes, chicken wings, veges, the all-important filet mignon and on and on.

The Japanese side includes a large assortment of Sushi rolls and Nigiri.  There is much much more and you can check the web site for a more detailed list.

A Sunday buffet brunch can be pricey on the Mainline.  These folks are so affordable that instead of making brunch a destination event you can just say "Let's go!"

If you eat in Delaware County you know that EDGEWOOD is one of the finest restaurants around.  This new place has the same owners so I was expecting to be impressed.  My expectations were met!

The LOCATION will surprise you and it's easy to drive right by it.  They need to work on their signage.  It's the restaurant that supports the Days Inn so look for that sign and you're there.

The building itself is basically a box so they didn't have much architecture to work with.  However you can tell they spent some serious $$.  It's bright and airy with a beautiful large copper-topped bar.  The ATMOSPHERE is not typical pub.

They have handled their ADULT LIBATION offerings very nicely.  There is a decent beer list, a very nice specialty cocktail list, and plenty of wine as well.  Some folks might say that a "Pub" should have a bigger beer list and they might be correct.  They're new so we'll see how they adjust.  I enjoyed a house Merlot for $6.50.

If you are eating a pleasant surprise is a complimentary basket of incredible house-made potato chips and gorgonzola dipping sauce.  They are served beautifully and my fellow Yelpers have posted a couple of pics.

I ordered the Filet Mignon Egg Rolls with Wild Mushroom & Smoked Cheddar, Horseradish Chive Sauce and accompanied by Crispy Onions for $12.  For the rest of my life I will be comparing every other eggroll to these.  To me they are the best eggrolls on the planet!  Bursting with flavor and beyond stuffed with tender filet.

My bet is that for most folks this is going to be a 4-5 star experience as it was for me.

I lost my steakhouse virginity to Morton's.  This was decades ago and in another city when I was young and inexperienced.  I thought it was fantastic but I had nothing to compare with it.  

And time marches on and I'm much older, much more experienced and have eaten at dozens of steakhouses all across the USA.  So here I am in Philly which has become known as a serious steakhouse town.  Sadly the Philly Morton's is not keeping up with the fierce completion.
  
There is really no sense in discussing specific pricing as it's in keeping with the competition.  Expect a big tab.

The atmosphere is worth discussing.  Morton's seems dated and not in a good way.  It's in need of a serious remodel.  If I'm going to pay a big tab I expect great atmosphere and I don't get that here.  The completion is blowing them away.

The wait staff is ok but nothing special.  Morton's can't attract the top steakhouse waiters and waitresses because they're not doing the volume.  For these folks it's all about the tips and for that they need volume.  Take a look at the number of Yelp reviews for Morton's compared to other Philly steakhouses.  That should give you a hint.

Your steak and sides will be fine.  You're not going to have a bad meal but for the same dollars you can do much better elsewhere.  This is a three star place and on a good night 3.5.

The restaurant group that owns Seasons 52 also owns Olive Garden and Red Lobster among others.  Before you scream and vow never to visit read on because it's a whole different world here.

For those that have lived in the area for a while these folks are at the former Bennigan's location outside the KOP mall.  As soon as you step out of your car, the aroma of the grill is distinct. That's always a good sign.  This is a beautiful restaurant with a very high-end feel to it.  There are water features and a nice fire to add to the atmosphere. 

For those that are uninformed the menu might come as a bit of a surprise.  The emphasis here is on healthy food.  Their claim to fame is that every dish is less than 475 calories.  So what does that mean to you, the diner?  No bread and butter will be served with the meal.  Speaking of butter, that's a no no here.  It's rarely if ever used.  There is also no fryer here so French fries or anything batter fried will not be on the menu.  Any dressings or sauces will be very light.  Expect the liberal use of spices and herbs to add zip to your meal.

So the lovely wife and I stopped by for lunch.  We made an Open Table reservation as it was the Xmas season.  We were seated right on time by a pleasant hostess.  My wife is a scallop fanatic and she spotted the entrée right away.  Of course it's one of the most expensive items you can order.  Caramelized Grilled Sea Scallops with roasted asparagus, sun-dried tomato-mushroom pearl pasta ($20).  It arrived promptly and was plated beautifully.  She pronounced it excellent.

I ordered the Grilled Chicken Caesar Sandwich with lettuce, tomato, Caesar dressing, on soft grilled Mediterranean bread ($8).  It came with a small salad and once again was plated beautifully and delicious.  I also ordered a side dish I couldn't resist.  I love mushrooms and I love spinach and when you put them in one dish I'm in heaven.  So the spinach stuffed mushrooms were incredible!

If you are one of those folks that enjoys and adult libation or two you'll find it here but you'll pay for it.  The drink menu is extensive and wines and specialty drinks are numerous. It's easy to spend $10 or more for a drink here.  Several beers are a more reasonable $5.50.  

If you are thinking of visiting you should know that in order to meet the "475 calories or less" claim many but not all of the dishes may be smaller than you expect.  They seem to fall in between tapa sized and a typical entrée at another restaurant.  Now that you know that you may want to order and extra dish to share.

The wife and I both agree that we had an excellent experience and plan to return.

If you're surprised about the prices at an airport joint you either just crawled out of a cave from a twenty year hibernation or you have the IQ of a Styrofoam peanut!  Enough with bitching about the prices already and let's move on.

Why Oh why do you stop at an airport eatery/drinkery? 

1. YOU NEED TO CHARGE YOUR PHONE!  This place is perfect for that.  The bar is lined with an unbelievable number of outlets.  Just watch the patrons smile as they see them.  You will to. 

2. YOUR FLIGHT HAS BEEN DELAYED/CANCELLED AND YOU DESPERATELY NEED AN ADULT LIBATION OR TWO OR THREE!  These folks have got you covered with beer, wine and specialty drinks.

3. YOU'LL DIE UNLESS YOU SEE THE CURRENT WORLD CUP, BASEBALL, FOOTBALL, BASKETBALL OR WHATEVER GAME!  Not a problem here as there are plenty of good quality screens.

4. IT SURE WOULD BE NICE TO EAT SOMETHING OTHER THAN FAST FOOD!  Try the Breakfast Fried Rice ($10) with your choice of meat.  Vegetarian also if you lean that way.  Absolutely delicious.

If you are in Terminal C you should give these folks a shot.

What do you say about an amazing place that already has over 600 reviews?  I know; put the ten (10) most important things you need to know all in one place.  So, especially if you are a 1st timer, read on.

1. Be prepared to embrace the crowds.  It's part of the Reading Terminal experience.  Think about it.  All those folks are there because the place is so amazing!

2. Don't visit on Sunday, Monday, or Tuesday.  Why you ask?  There are over a dozen Pennsylvania Dutch (Amish) vendors that are definitely worth visiting.  They have special hours and don't open on these days.  It would be a mistake not to see them.

3. If you want the very best deals make sure you end your visit during the last hour of each day.  That would be between 5:00 and 6:00 PM Monday -Saturday and 4:00 to 5:00 PM on Sunday.

4. If you are a foodie be prepared to be overwhelmed, stunned, amazed, and generally blown away.  You won't be able to do it justice in two (2) hours.  Think three (3) or more.

5. Speaking of two (2) hours, it will cost you $4 for that amount of time at the 12th & Filbert garage.  All you need to do is spend $10 and any vendor will validate your ticket.  Even better is to not park at all and take public transportation.  

6. Check the website for cool events especially to see the live music schedule.  http://www.readingterminalmarket.org/events/

7. Some folks say the place is touristy and they are partially correct.  That's true of some of the vendors but anyone with half a brain can spot them in a second.  If that's not your thing just walk on by.

8. If you want to stay in the market and have an adult libation, check out Molly Malloy's.  It's a great place for a beer.

9. If you are thinking about lunch at prime time (11:30-1:00), please think again.  And then think again and again.  Trust me; it's complete and utter craziness.  Eat early or eat late.

10. Last but not least let's talk Tommy DiNic's as this legendary emporium deserves special mention.  I know, I know, you saw Man vs. Food and you want "The Sandwich."  Is it worth it?  Yeah, it is.  Stroll the market and stop back occasionally to check on the length of the line.  If you see it below twenty five (25) folks, go for it.  It really is an amazing sandwich.

As just about everyone says this place is a must for a Philly visitor.
