Don't let Penn Valley in the name confuse you as they are located on Montgomery Ave. in Narberth.

And don't let Pub in the name confuse you as the menu goes way past pub food and is seriously extensive. 

And especially don't be confused into thinking this is just another local dive bar as it decidedly is not.  

On my last visit I blew in for a late weekday lunch and adult libation. The ATMOSPHERE is certainly like a pub.  It's warm and comfortable with lots of dark wood.  It's beautifully maintained and spotlessly clean.  BTW- there is also a small outdoor seating area.

I didn't feel like a huge meal so I perused the very large menu and began with Ham & Bean soup.  It was served quickly at the correct temperature, packed with ingredients and as tasty as one could want.  For my meal I ordered Roasted Peppers with Asiago Cheese, Kalamata Olives and Crostini for $9.  As you can see from my pic it was nicely plated and hit the spot perfectly.  It would make a great shared appetizer.  Overall my FOOD was well above average.

Speaking of above average, that was also true of my bartender.  So CUSTOMER SERVICE was solid.  

So take a look at the menu on their web site.  If it looks good and you enjoy a pub atmosphere, add these folks to your list.

A solid, classy HAPPY HOUR experience!

I had heard rumors that the happy hour (4:30-6:30) was very popular. I stopped by mid-week right around 4:30 and folks were just pulling into the giant lot.  By 5:00 the place was jumping with happy folks and more coming in.  I can imagine what it would be like on a Friday night.

So why is everyone so happy?  The 1st reason is the ATMOSPHERE.  The bar(s) area is quite simply gorgeous.  That's right, I said bars.  There are two in close proximity.  The second bar is a pizza bar.  You can sip your drink and watch the chef create and cook your pie.  I gotta say, the overall bar(s) area is classy and impressive.

The 2nd reason is the happy hour PRICES.  All the typical wine varieties were $4.  Not only that the pour was quite heavy.  There was a specialty martini on for $7 and some drafts for $3.  Those are great deals almost anywhere and amazing deals in an atmosphere this nice.  I was enjoying some very nice Merlot.

The 3rd reason is the happy hour FOOD specials.  I tried the Meatball Al Forno with fresh ricotta for $6.  As you can see from my picture this was one big ball.  The flavor was spot on.  I wanted to try the Margherita Pizza at $10 but I was too stuffed from the meatball.  Fortunately my neighbor saw me eyeing hers and offered me a slice.  Remember, we watched it being made.  It was very good and at $10 a great value.

The overall Yelp reviews have not been particularly kind to Teca but my happy hour experience was 4 stars.

You can't throw a stick now days without hitting a chain restaurant or two or six and this is just one of the pack.  I fly a lot and this chain is on a mission to put one in every terminal at PHL.  They are fine for getting a drink while waiting out a flight delay in Terminal E.

I'm not a huge fan of the free-standing locations but that's mostly because the market they're looking for is just not me.  If you are half my age, looking to guzzle some average beer and pound done some average bar food this may be the place for you.

This location is just off Trooper road behind that SUPER WaWa.  It's clean and I've found the staff to be friendly.

There is a huge focus on beer here and they have tons of taps.  Some would say they have a bunch of craft beers but I would say eh.  Now days they are just the brews that are almost everywhere.

The food of course includes the Crab Fries and lots of pub grub.  If you like fried or heavy food you'll be in heaven.  If you're coming here for a salad you're out of your mind!

I work very close to here so I'll be in from time to time usually when I'm invited by a coworker.  I think it's fair to give them three stars.

Found this place by happenstance. The Mexican place down the street was closed and wandered in here delighted to find a wide assortment of yummy stuff including vegetarian and vegan options for me. Don't worry - meat for you carnivores, but I was happy to find fake bacon to round out some of the interesting wraps, sandwiches and Panini's.  I loved the pesto tofu Panini! Next Time, I've got to try the beer cheese soup and the vegetarian Philadelphia cheesesteak.  The espresso machine was a big + too-they brew local roasted coffee.  A nicer and if it is discovery - there will be a 'next time'soon.

The experience of Ciro's is so much fun... I feel the experience truly starts before you ever even get to the door. Google maps places the restaurant on Bayshore although it is on the side of the building opposite of the street. Searching for the 'secret door' was part of the adventure for our first visit. Once we got there we had to knock and tell the password to the hostess through the little window. We were taken into the dark restaurant and brought to our own cozy space. There were 4 of us so the space we were in was more like a small room than a booth. The seats were comfortable and had pillows, the tables reminded me of being in a living room more than a restaurant, which added to the intimate vibe of the place. Our server gave us a rundown of how the cocktail menu was divided and brought us water while we looked it over. I ordered the Russian Spring Punch for my first drink and it was delicious. It tasted like lemonade and was refreshing. My second drink was El Diablo and it was a bit spicier, made with tequila, and equally refreshing. As it was our first time and we had heard so many good things, we decided to try a bunch of different items from the menu. The duck fat fries were everything and then some. They lived up to every review I have ever read. The truffle popcorn was delicious, the candied walnuts were good, and the fried chickpeas were differently wonderful. I was expecting savory from the chickpeas and they were sweet which somehow worked. We also got the escargot which were more like rangoons and were great. We had chicken and waffles which was moist and well seasoned. Our table also had crab cakes and I was told they were good as well. This is a great place to bring guests from out of town as a very different and fun experience or for a date night. We enjoyed ourselves and will be back.

I've tried and tried to love this place because they have the best soy drinks I've ever had but this might be the final straw (pun intended).

the first time I went to soy cafe, they overcharged my credit card. I got a $5 drink and my card was charged for $14. they had me waiting for 25 minutes because they forgot about my drink. they then made me the wrong beverage and gave me a chocolate chip cookie for the trouble.

I've been back twice with average service. it's a little slower than most.

today, I went with my boyfriend. he got a disgusting green tea coffee (so bad he couldn't drink it and we threw it away) and I got a blended ice peppermint coffee and found A PIECE OF METAL IN MY DRINK. (see pictures).

it's safe to say I'm done with this place.

Have you ever felt the need to escape to New York for the evening but the thought of sitting in a dirty NJ Transit train or on the NJ turnpike makes your stomach turn? Save yourself the trouble and escape to James instead. Sure it's around the corner from the most Philly of all areas, the Italian Market, but James is worlds away from the sausage shops and water ice stands its neighborhood is known for. Inside, it's warmly lit and feels very modern. And while the decor is great and all, the food is the most incredible part of it all.

After grabbing drinks at the bar (I absolutely loved my elderflower and prosecco cocktail) we took a seat at an abnormally long table-for-two. We decided to go all out and try the "chef's tasting", a five course meal selected by the chef himself based on your personal preferences. We told the waiter that our only request was no sweetbreads (calf pancreas, no thanks) and he went into the kitchen to tell the chef to get cookin. What followed was five courses of amazing and exotic fare. After a free sampling of some sort of pate on a spoon, we received the first course-- scallops topped with caviar. Incredible. Next up was the Risotto 'alla Kristina' (the chef's wife) with raw oysters which was absolutely magnificent. The main course was London broil cooked to perfection and topped with porcini mushrooms in a mysteriously delicious sauce. And finally, the dessert (by far the most bizarre ending to a meal I've ever had) was a triangle of frozen gorgonzola with poached pears. The thought of eating frozen blue cheese scared the bejesus out of me but I sucked it up and tried it out. I was pleasantly surprised-- it tasted like ice cream with a different texture and a bit of a sour aftertaste. Maybe that description still doesn't have you sold on frozen gorgonzola but trust me, it's worth a try. 

If you're any good at math, you'll realize that I forgot to list one of the five courses. Not that it was a forgettable dish, it's just that my aging twentysomething mind tends to let bits of information go sometime. Forgive me for that and just take my word for it that James is the perfect place to escape Phillydom for a night and lose yourself for a while. The best part of a local escape? When you step outside with a pleasantly full belly, you'll be happy home is just a quick walk away.

Finally, a restaurant so close to me that I absolutely LOVE! This place is small, and there was a wait when we went, but it's so worth it. Service is amazing. Everyone is so nice and willing to help in anyway shape or form. 

Parking is a bit hard, as they are located in a lot with a laundromat and this laundromat seems pretty adamant about reserving certain spots just for them, so we had to go into a neighborhood across the street to find parking.

Moving on.... seated at around 10:45am. Looked over the menu and knew we wanted to try the wings, but it wasn't 11 yet! Server says "No problem" and put in the order anyway. (like I said, service is amazing). The wait for the food was a tad on the long side, but they were extremely busy, so we didn't care cause the food still came out hot and delicious.

Twice baked wings - if i received the worse service in the world, i will still come back for these wings. Yes, they are that amazing! So moist, yet the skin was so crispy. And the seasoning on it was just yum! I'm drooling just thinking about them.

Biscuit with sausage gravy and eggs - So good. The biscuit tasted so fresh and it wasn't dried out like I've had at other spots. I think this was my son's favorite meal. He kept asking for more of the biscuits with gravy.

I can't wait to go back. Philadelphia quality food near my house...SCORE!

Omg omg omg !!!!! I literally found heaven. I have been looking for a place that reminded me of London and Toronto and I have found it. In fact, it's actually better. All the flavors I tried were so creamy and you can definitely tell it's homemade. They had tons of Asian flavors available along with a few standard ones.

I tried almond cookie, taro/ube mixed, lychee lavender, and the pandan flavor. They were all so good and it took me some time to finally decide but I settled for the pandan. I decided to order it in a coconut bowl bc it came with sticky rice and unlimited toppings. If anyone knows me, sweet sticky rice is my jam! The fruit on top of the ice cream were so pretty (as you can see from my photos) and went really well with the coconut and ice cream.

My kids ordered the taro and almond cookie in a red velvet cone. Again, it was amazing! Husband ordered pandan in an egg waffle. Now these egg waffles are by far the best I've had ever. He had original one and I ordered green tea flavored (without ice cream). Soooo chewy and perfect flavor. 

Ahhhhh, I'm craving more and I just left. Can't wait to be back.

What a great new addition (prob 8 months old) to my area. I loved every second of the experience and the food. Service was top notch, I loved the look of the restaurant, and the food was filling and delicious.

Filet mignon egg rolls were quite delicious. It wasn't too greasy and had the perfect flavor. Presentation of this dish was also nice.

Pork Mac n cheese - I didn't really get to eat much of it. Had a taste but it was so good. It was literally baked to perfection. My son loved it so much, he almost are the whole thing himself

I chose one of the specials for my meal. Salmon stuffed with crab meat on top of parmesan risotto. Oh my, it was so good. The salmon just melted in my mouth and loved the risotto so much. It was creamy and had the perfect amount of parmesan. They definitely should make this a permanent on their menu.

It's a bit pricey, but the portions are a good size, so you do get what you paid for. Can't wait to try other things in the menu.

First of all I have recently been put on the paleo diet. Rice is not paleo however I read an article about how you can request that the sushi chefs use cucumber instead. My boyfriend and I have eaten here probably 15+ times in the last couple years. Since we ate here so often, I figured they would be happy to help me find a couple rolls. Sooooo not the case. 
Before we ordered anything, I asked the waitress who is also the manager if it would be a problem. First she flat told me no but I could order fish. At this point I am thinking no problem, I don't need sushi. Then she proceeded to give me a 15 minute lecture on how customer's dietary restrictions are difficult for them to deal with and if she let them make me rolls like that today then I would expect it next time and she wasn't going to do that. Feeling humiliated and frustrated we were about to walk out when she finally agreed to ask the sushi chef if he would but "only" if I ordered no more than two rolls. I went ahead and ordered what she told me she was willing to have them make for me. I really should have just left,... but I didn't and she continued to come back by and ask me why I have to eat like that and can't I just have a little rice, etc. 
I am well aware that the restrictions to my diet can be a pain which is why I asked if it was a problem before we ordered. A simple, "I'm sorry but we are unable to do that here," would have been just fine. The lecture was completely unneeded and embarrassing. We will not be going back.

Nestled in the far back of the Nugget Casino, which is directly across from Harrah's Reno, this diner is most famous for the "Awful Awful" burger and fries which is a 1/2 lb burger with lettuce onion and tomato, over a pound of seasoned fries. I do remember when these used to be $4.99, but alas that was a long time ago and they are now $11.50.

There is a little A Frame sign in front letting you know of the diner, and it's kinda sketchy with all of the tweakers and drunks hanging around. In fact, going thru the casino is depressing in itself as there are nothing but solo people who clearly don't look like they are there for a little light fun. And, when you actually arrive at the diner, you might be a little unimpressed with the venue, but venture on. 

On our visit, the waitress was a hoot and very friendly, despite having and "edge " with what I assume to be the local regular patrons. Overheard when one asked what was on the Southwest burger, "It has bacon and some other shit on it", and when someone asked how much fries you get, the response was, "As big as your face!". 

Out burger were as we remembered, and for us, 1/2 burger was really enough and we both combined couldn't eat all of the fries. Still a solid deal at $11.50 and a fun experience.

Tried this place as it was attached to my hotel, the Magnolia Hotel. The restaurant is located on the bottom floor and has several tables on an outside area which faces a small open area park like setting. On this day , there was also music being played, and it was very relaxing and pleasant on this nice Summer day.

I only got to try the Figgie Piggie, which was a calzone creation of applewood smoked bacon, figs, balsamic onions , boursin, mozzarella , garlic, ricotta , honey oil and red sauce. It was magnificent ! The sweetness of the honey and figs, and the contrast of the smoky bacon and onions really set this on off! Cooked to perfection, this place left me wanting more. I can't wait to explore the rest of the menu at my next visit. 

Service was super friendly and helpful, and went out of their way to assist !

Stumbled upon this place on my way back to the hotel. Very clean and modern venue with high open ceilings and spacious bench and small table seating. You form a line on the right side to place your order. Meats and sides are served open directly on a paper lined tray, no plates needed in this venue. 

I got to try the brisket, pulled pork as well as the baby back ribs. Sides were the Mac n cheese and fries. The brisket was flavorful and you could really taste the smoky flavor and the pulled pork was nice as well. The hit for me was the baby back ribs which were cooked to perfection with just the right fall of the bone texture. I accompanied that with their Honey Badger sauce and it really delivered. 

Staff were really helpful and courteous and the overall restaurant was super clean, maybe too clean as it did have more of a franchisee or corporate feel to it, not a bad thing, just different than some of the ambiance from some of the other BBQ joints that I have few quoted in St Louis.

A Testament to Youth --  The Blue Moose Restaurant was originally founded in 2006 by two teenagers, aged 14 and 15, searching for something new to do on the weekends. Together they embarked on an adventure to run the nation's first 100% youth-run restaurant with absolutely no knowledge of how to run a restaurant.

They began serving family and friends on a small scale basis out of one of their homes.  Word soon spread about what they were up to and their weekend supper club developed quite a following.

One of the boys moved on in another direction but the other, Skylar Bird chose to expand his culinary experience by apprenticing in restaurants both in the US and France and then enrolling in the French Culinary Institute in Manhattan.  All that hard work has paid off because today he and his team at the Blue Moose deliver exceptional food and service in New Hope.

And you can't beat $30 for a three-course dinner!  BYOB

We ordered take out, my wife got lasagna and I got egg plant parmigiana.    My food was barely okay, her lasagna was that bad we just threw it away.  It was very greasy.  Their sauce is not very good. I definitely recommend you go somewhere else for good food.

So I am home visiting my parents over the holidays and finally got to try Katie's.  All I can say is - I have no idea what all the hype is about.
We came for lunch - got there and got seated.  Waitress came over, friendly and pleasant.  Since we're on vacation, we ordered some drinks.  I asked for a bloody mary - "Can you make a good one?"  "Oh yes, we have our own mix and they are awesome!"  well, I am not sure what an "awesome" bloody mary is to her but - this was a glass of store bought mix (tasted like zing zang) with a (small) shot of vodka in it and some pepper and salt.  No garnish, no nothing.  

Then we decided to order off the lunch menu - you get half a salad with your choice of entree.  I asked for the insalata mista and the margarita pizza - i specified "red sauce" (not garlic and oil) and even asked for extra sauce on the side.  My mom ordered the artichoke salad and the prawn sandwich and my dad asked for the mixed veg salad and the porchetta sandwich.  The waitress didnt write anything down, but I didn't think anything of it at the time.  So our salads are brought out - two insalata mistas and a artichoke.  Nope, thats not right.  So they take away one of the mistas and we sit and wait for the third salad... and wait... and wait. Finally, five minutes later, they bring the third salad.  A few minutes after that, the waitress comes back and says they are out of the porchetta - so he asks for something else (we have no menus at this point so we have no idea what the other options are).  
The food comes out - and sure enough, my pizza has no sauce on it.  I say "um, this doesnt look like a red sauce pizza, it looks like oil and garlic"   - yup.  So now everyone is sitting with their sandwiches getting cold while they go back and cook another pizza for me.  It comes out.  No side of sauce.  Whatever,  at this point, it is what it is.  I try some.  It's fine.  It's a thrown together last minute pizza.  Nothing special at all.
The check comes - no apology, no offer of taking something off the check for the TWO mistakes.  $75 for lunch for three people - no thanks.  I won't be back the next time I am home.

Absolutely Gross, Piss poor costumer service, I told him we had a Groupon and he seemed even more pissed off. All the food is wrapped in tinfoil and kept warm. When you come in to pick it up, it's then all chopped up and places in a large tinfoil tray and smothered in BBQ sauce. If you closed your eyes and ate the pulled pork or beef brisket you couldn't tell them apart because it all tasted like the BBQ sauce. Clearly they have never experienced real BBQ. Basically you get cooked meat, in a shit ton of sauce, an a attitude. Clearly they need Groupon with an average 2.5 star rating.
One and Done Son......

Cute little German restaurant that's a one man operation, serving delicious German food with vegan options, in one of the popular parts of Downtown St. Pete.

Before meeting up with a former coworker, I was checking out new restaurants in Downtown St. Pete and German Knoodle pops up due to the high rating. I'm a fan of German, and my friend also was curious to check it out, so win-win!

When you arrive, just grab a table inside or out. The owner/chef will soon greet you with a warm welcome and some menus. The menu is relatively simple: some German plates, sandwiches, salads, and a lot of options for wine and beer. Especially the German kind. Both my friend and I were eyeing similar dishes, so we did the smart thing and split them, which was super simple.

Currywurst Plate: Two delicious pork sausages in a homemade curry ketchup sauce and some sauerkraut. These were delicious and easy to share as there are two. A juicy, perfectly cooked sausage with an outside crunch but tender inside, and the curry sauce was really flavorful. Most patrons I saw had ordered this and for good reason. Definitely a must order!

Jager Schnitzel: I love schnitzel, so this was a must order for me. Likewise it came with two fried cutlets which also makes it easy to share. The mushroom sauce was lighter than I was expecting, which was actually preferred! Very flavorful, perfectly breaded and fried. As you'll see, this combo is ordered by many couples. 

Both dishes came with a side of his fries, which are seasoned with garlic, which makes them amazing and hard to stop.

He also has three German beers in bottle, ranging from light to dark. We got his recommended beer (said it was the best German beer in St. Pete, throwing shade at Hofbrau!) and it was a solid beer for a warm Winter day.

Now there was something messed up that I saw from other patrons. Because this is a one man operation at the time, the owner/chef is taking orders, cooking, busing, and more (German efficiency at its finest!). One older couple sat down, ordered some beverages, and because it took more than a minute they got up and left. They weren't even down the block when the owner came out with their beverages. So if you're an impatient asshole, don't come here.

That said, if you enjoy delicious, local sourced German food in a cute locale, with a great chef/owner, check this place out!

I'm a fan of the Trolley Stop for really affordable breakfast items. I've only tried one thing on their menu, the early bird special, but in the future, I plan to try other items. I just can't get away from the steal of getting a complete breakfast, with eggs, grits, bacon, and toast, for $2.99! You get to have your eggs any style you like, and you can choose between white or wheat toast. I do have to say; the grits need to be seasoned... I usually end up adding a little butter, salt, and pepper to help my taste buds out, but once they're seasoned, they're great. I leave with a full tummy, and I spend less than $5 even if I end up getting some OJ. They have a lot of other steals on their menu, like their omelets and pancakes, but I've stuck with my early bird special because it can't be beat!

I don't understand all the hate on WalMart. I love WalMart! It always has exactly what I need, and even more of what I didn't know I needed! This WalMart is my go-to place for deals on the essentials like meat, Greek yogurt, fresh vegetables, fruit, cliff bars, and spaghetti. Also, they have a large selection of beer, wine, and liquor that's way cheaper than at a liquor store for the same exact thing! What's more, is that WalMart has things for everyone, even gifts for your nieces, nephews, and grandparents! It also has a large pet center, where you can buy food, treats, and kitty litter on a bargain. Plus, there's still the WalMart app, which has the "savings catcher" feature, so you can scan your receipts and get money back if your paid more for an item at WalMart than you would have paid at another shop nearby! That's huge for me, and since using this WalMart, my additional savings have been slim to none, which means they have the best prices around for what I'm buying! But wait, there's more! Have you ever heard of Mr. Ghetto? Google him and his Wally World video, it was done at THIS WalMart! :)

I like Milk Bar, and was so happy to find their location on Delachaise because it's closer to where I live! I've never been disappointed with my sandwich choices here, and I've tried a bunch! I like the gourmet sandwiches the most, like the Christmas in July sandwich and Shrimply the Best. I think Milk Bar makes use of great ingredients, which really sets them apart. I recently discovered their hot po-boys, and I have to say, they're an amazing option! They're actually a dollar or two less in cost than their gourmet sandwiches, but they tend to be bigger and come with just as much flavor, if not more! If you're up to it, try the Thai Chilli Chicken poboy! It's made with roast chicken, mozzarella, tomato, red onion, and a delicious Thai sweet chilli sauce - all for $8! It'll make you lick your fingers.

Cafe Amelie is located in the French Quarter neighborhood in New Orleans, LA. When you're walking on Royal st., as you reach Cafe Amelie, you'll turn your head and behold what feels like a secret garden amongst the chaos that French Quarter is known for. There's a ton of outside seating, and to be honest, I've never sat inside. The place is quant and romantic in a way, with old fountains and numerous flowers and foliage surounding you and your guests. I recommend getting a reservation, as the wait times can be pretty long. The food is quite flavorful, and what sets Cafe Amelie apart, is that they host a wide range of natural and organic ingredients! The service is exceptional, our servers were on point, and even take the time to take pictures of you and your guests for you if you ask! All in all, if you're looking for a nice restaurant to go to in the French Quarter, away from the buzz of Bourbon street, Cafe Amelie is the place for you!

I'm a huge fan of Hoshun Restaurant! It's my go-to spot on Saint Charles Avenue for General Tso's Chicken, fried rice, and miso soup! I was honestly surprised the first time I ate at Hoshun, because of the high quality ingredients... Like, really, they use REAL chicken (cut it in half and see for yourself)! I love it that Hoshun doesn't have time for those plastic-y, small, chicken bits covered in a flavorful sauce that some other restaurants try. Their miso soup was mi-so-salty, but I loved it. They also have a great ambiance, with their dim lit rooms, intimate booths, and tables. The food comes out fast, and the service is on point. They also have an exceptional lunch menu (12-3pm discounted food, but same size and quality as dinner time), and happy hour menu (3-6pm, discounted wine, beer, and food... No happy hour on Sunday's though). They also deliver... but, its $25 minimum, plus $2 delivery fee, without miso soup... so I guess I'll keep showing up at Hoshun! :)

My Amici experience was great! I love italian food, and I'm addicted to pizza (so are you, don't lie), so Amici is perfect for me. I came for happy hour after a stroll on Magazine, and I was happy with my decision. I had the margherita pizza, and red wine. The pizza came out hot, the cheese was melted, and the coal-fire charred bubbles in the crust were poppin! Don't sleep on a coal-fire grill, but definitely eat any food that simmers there! I loved every bite. I definitely need to go back and try all of their antipasto items, salads, more of their pizza, and their entrees! I can't wait to update y'all.

Drove though and stopped by but should not have! Place was very dirty, and person at the counter making racist comment. Made me very uncomfortable. I threw out coffee due to I did not trust it did not get spit in

I was born and raised in Puerto Rico where we had a Fondita de Leo nearby, so when i was (very) homesick and searching for some puertorrican food on a yelp search, i was excited to see they had one in Downtown Clearwater. I was a bit skeptical that it would have the same sabor but really wanted to find a festive puertorrican place to celebrate my birthday.  
On our first visit we sat in the spacious bar area. To my delight they also had salsa music playing in the background which makes the place lively (we could hardly contain ourselves and started dancing). It was pretty tough to choose what to eat since there were so many good choices. We decided to try the Queso con guava (instead of sorrullitos), Bistec encebollado with rice and beans, and Mofongo. For dessert, i was eyeing the nutella or guava cheesecake but got the recommended fried cheesecake with guava. I do NOT regret any of our choices... everything tasted like back home. Most of the wait staff is bilingual and i had an amazing time reminiscing and sharing stories with them and with fellow puertorrican patrons. Overall, first visit was fun and was just what i needed for my homesick birthday celebration. 
On our second visit, we told some puertorrican friends (who were visiting from Boca Raton) to meet up with us here. I recommended the Sangria (reminiscent of Fido Sangria from Puerto Rico) and it did not disappoint. They came with an appetite and had the Chuletas Can Can with Mofongo. They have since returned (even without us). 
My third visit, we went with my sister and my brother in law and they really liked their Churrasco and Mofongo. Although the Arroz Mamposteado i ordered tasted good, it had a slight pimiento morrón aftertaste (which can be hit or miss...i liked it but Leroy C didn't). Leroy C decided to try the Chicharrones de Pollo with Mofongo this time, but the portion seemed small and although it tasted good, he decided to stick with his original order from then on. 
This last visit was less than favorable because after ordering we had to wait 15 min for my Sangria and almost 1 hour for our food. I just attribute it to the ridiculously high volume of customers that evening ( most were 4+ parties). Another bummer was that they stopped bringing Medalla Light (beer made in Puerto Rico), but hey, they still have the Sangria...so i will be back. Love this place!

I'm not sure how many of you had the pleasure of visiting the establishments that preceded the Wild Garlic Grill in this quirky spot on 1st Ave., but if you did, then you're in for quite a shock.  Where there once was a divey greasy spoon, and before it a ramshackle Jamaican joint, there is now one of the best new restaurants in town.  The interior has been so completely redesigned that I almost couldn't believe I was in the same place, and the food has jumped up a number of levels as well.  You owe it to yourself to check this place out.

When you go, the first thing you should notice is that they are charging obscenely little for everything on the menu.  You can get a big plate of barbecued ribs, delicious homemade potato salad, and some yummy sauteed greens for $14 -- FOURTEEN DOLLARS!  They also make an enormous and killer salad with lots of grilled veggies and goat cheese for $12 that fed Amy for two days.  We've really enjoyed their grilled salmon dish (which I'm really glad I ordered, given that it doesn't sound that interesting on the menu -- trust me, it's not something you could make at home), and we've also been happy to break the bank for their $24 lamb shank special, which seriously rivals the masterpiece at Tavolino (I should point out that Tavolino's lamb shank is probably my favorite food item in Tucson, so this is not faint praise).  We haven't had as much of an opportunity to explore the cocktail menu, though we did adore the Sidecar.

So here's the bottom line: the Wild Garlic Grill is serving some of the best food in Tucson, and they're charging about as much for it as you'd pay at Applebees.  Go get some before they wise up and start raising their prices!

I am a huge new fan of Lee's!  I just tried their black bean burger, and oh my!!!  SO delicious!  It's HUGE, with the perfect amount of spice.  Just yummy!!!  Thank you for doing what you do so well, Lee!!

Amazing!!!!
I literally have been here 3 times in the past month. The service is always great. I am horrible at names and don't remember the servers names but Allison, she is phenomenal and goes above and beyond!! With everything going on with Covid they have taken a lot of precautions which made me feel very comfortable with eating out during this time. They converted some parking spaces into outdoor seating and it is perfect. 
Every time I got the chicken jambalaya which is completely different than any jambalaya I have seen and tastes amazing - very fresh and the flavors and seasonings match perfectly. I also told them about an allergy which they took very serious and I appreciated. Another person in my party for the salmon, which they ate quickly because it was so good so I didn't even have a chance to taste. I also got the donuts for dessert which tasted so good and melted in my mouth. 
I wish I could remember the names of the drinks I got but every time I told the waiter or waitress what I wanted and they were able to pinpoint exactly what drink I should order, and every time I was pleased.

Unbelievable that you can go to a restaurant with a 5:00 reservation and they are out of all vegetables including the spinach that your protein was supposed to be under. Entrees brought at long intervals. Others eating while you waited. Food not really hot   Food not cooked properly sent back and returned 15 minutes later after having to ask for it and then still not right. Waitress knew all of the mishaps and never offered anything complementary.  Don't they realize this affects their tip?  Will be a long time before we return only for pizza

My boyfriend and I stopped by here today because he was freaking out that a Roberto's was coming to Reno- and I was pretty excited too, seeing as I haven't had ANY Mexican food since moving to Reno a little over a month ago.

We ordered togo since it had limited seating and it was fairly busy; 1 order of Carne Asada Fries, 1 order of Rolled Tacos w/ Guac, and 1 Carne Asada Taco.
(Didn't realize until our order was almost up that the cashier had made a mistake and charged us for a Taco Salad instead of a Carne Asada Taco, but the owner quickly resolved the issue and gave me a refund.)

Afterwards we stopped by their salsa bar which was AMAZING! It included their delicious house-made green and red salsas, as well as whole green onions, chopped cucumbers, cut limes, and carrots that were marinated with white onions. The spread was impressive, I hope it stays that way because it is a definite plus-side that sets this Taco Shop apart from all of the others.

After coming home and eating the food, I definitely enjoyed the Rolled Tacos the most, the shell stayed crisp despite being smothered in guacamole, the boyfriend liked his Carne Asada Taco as well. We both agreed that the Carne Asada Fries were just OK- the fries themselves could have been cooked longer to withstand all of the stuff that's piled on top of them. The color of the fries themselves weren't golden brown like they should have been, instead they were a pale yellow and very lightly fried. BUT, it's a new shop, probably with new cooks, so all is forgiven...we will definitely be back, perhaps we will order our Carne Asada Fries well-done next time?

Our family was in the mood for pizza and we were wanting something other than a pizza chain.  Stopped in here after a recommendation from my daughter and reading some reviews on Yelp.  Each of us got our own small pizza and I ordered some wings.  The pizza was nothing to write home about - blah.  No flavor and what was up with that dough, it tasted like it was made 2 days ago.  Since they don't have a fryer the wings are oven baked and the sauce was just poured on top - once again blah.  It is safe to say that I was underwhelmed.

I cannot believe I actually found a restaurant in Nashville that serves real Mexican food. Not even just real Mexican food, but even authentic Aztec dishes. I would say that I could die now, but I really want to go back to Fogatas.

Virtually all the food at every Mexican restaurant in Nashville I've eaten at tastes exactly the same as every other, and I've eaten at dozens of them. It's like they all share the same gigantic automated kitchen somewhere in Metro Center, where re-fried beans and salsa are stored in enormous silos and then pumped all over town through a network of tubes.

And none of it tastes like it's supposed to. I lived in Los Angeles for more than 20 years, and I understand the difference between authentic Mexican and Mexican-American food. Both of the can be great, and neither of them involve cheese dip. Fogatas does Mexican food best.

The owner, Junior, actually sat down at my table, and pulling up pictures on his smartphone, explained dishes and ingredients to me that I was not familiar with (which is amazing, considering I have been eating Mexican food all my life)...then he had samples of those foods brought to my table for me to try.

Shut the front door! That right there is some fantastic freakin' customer service! I was blown away and the food was off the chain.

I sampled two dishes I cannot pronounce. One was made from Corn Smut--like I'm not gonna try something called 'Smut'. Corn Smut (I encourage you to look up a picture) is a fungus that grows on corn. It looks like a big cancerous corn tumor. I really cannot say anything nice about the appearance of corn smut and am convinced that this food was first eaten as some kind of punishment. 

The corn smut is pureed, which turns it into a loose, black slime. It is cooked with onions and peppers and other spicy stuff and served in a folded, grilled corn tortilla. It did not look delicious. It looked like a baby had pooped into a taco and then sat on it.

However, it was delicious. The homemade corn tortillas were freakin'  fantastic and it was the best tasting smut I had ever had! Smut tastes kind of like pureed mushrooms (which also doesn't sound great, I guess) but it is deeply earthly and salty, kind of like mushroom and miso. Vegetarians in particular would love this dish. It was awesome and I would definitely order it again.

I also sampled another Aztec dish that was made with sqash flowers and squash meat, onions and other veggies. It was quite spicy, had a little cheese on it and was also served on a folded grilled tortilla. Fantastic. Again, vegetarians should run, not walk to this restaurant. It was fabulous.

The "sample" dishes were huge (although according to Junior, they were tiny by comparison to the actual dishes) and I was full, so ordered carnitas to go, which were also quite good, even many hours later.

Junior clearly loves to educated people (especially us gringos) about authentic Mexican food. So if you have questions, I wold certainly ask for him. I found the staff very welcoming and the prices were very reasonable. 

I will be visiting Fogatas often in the future.

This place is wonderful the food is great the drinks are very good all the drinks here are made to order with fresh fruit nothing from a plastic bag or bottle .The cranberry beans are perfect to taste a must have comes with banana chips on the side .There prices are perfect you get a lot for your money and I must say the service was great very friendly. If you can find parking in the front that's great or park on the side streets .Right outside of the French Quarter  I suggest trying there mint drinks with rum .There open six days a week they have lunch and dinner hours .I am from California and I will be back to  new Orleans  to eat here

Finch & Fork! What a cool name, but the food was definitely a letdown for me. I came here for brunch on a Saturday afternoon.  Finch & Fork is located within the Canary Hotel.  Parking is a little hard to spot, but there is a lot next to the hotel.  I made reservations, so it was a breeze to get seated.  I came at the earlier part of brunch so there wasn't a lot of people, but I could see it start filling up as I was there. 

I looked through the menu (brunch menu is a little limited) and decided on the 2 eggs, toast, bacon and potatoes.   Once I ordered, I looked down at my cup and it was dirty with leftover food. Yikes.  I requested a new cup.  My friend mentioned that the water tasted weird, so I tried some and it definitely had a weird plastic taste.  I think this might have been due to the unclean cups.  I didn't try to drink from the cups for the rest of the meal and I have to admit I was a little wary of the food due to the uncleanliness of the water cups. 

Once the food came out, I have to say I was rather disappointed in the food itself.  I ordered my eggs over medium and it was definitely overcooked.  I also tried some of my friend's poached eggs, which was also way overcooked.  The toast, bacon, and the potatoes were all average.  With other options for brunch in SB, I definitely recommend going somewhere else. Definitely a disappointing experience for a restaurant with a cool name.

Geno's is another famous cheesesteak place in Philly and as you may already know it sits right across the street from Pat's.  The difference in this place is that it has underlying tones of racism.  The previous owner was known for retaining an "American's Only Speak English" mentality and he made it known with various signs around the restaurant.  He's since passed, and I won't speak ill of the dead, but they've gotten new management, and they've said that the new owner, who happens to be the previous owner's son, does not share any of the controversial views of his father and that they were working to remove the racist undertone from the establishment; however, I have two questions.  

Question #1: Why was my Muslim friend, who has a full grown beard, completely ignored when he was trying to order his food?  Not a "he's not speaking loud enough" kind of ignore either, they just blatantly acted like he wasn't there.

Question #2:  Is it really possible to remove a racist undertone from an establishment that has been in place for so long?  Because from recent experience it still seems to linger.  One could also ask does the apple fall far from the tree with regards to the undertone, but I don't know the guy personally so I can't really speak on that.

All in all, I really want to like and enjoy this place as it seems to be a Philadelphian staple; however, it's left a bad taste in my mouth (without having even trying any of their food.)  But I'll end this review with a lighthearted quote in the words of Rupaul's Drag Race season 7 contestant Kennedy Davenport "Girl Please! No! Sorry! NEXT!"

We went there for family dinner. Food is ok. Waiter offered to refresh the soda glasses each time when he passed by. When the bill came, they charged us 20+ glasses of soda. Cost us $40 just for the soda. If the refill is not free, they should let us know and should not keep offering to refresh our glasses even when they were still half full. We will never come back and never refer this restaurant to anyone.

If you have to place an order, or have any reason to deal with Kathleen, would highly recommend avoiding this bakery. 

 I truly feel bad for those that have to work with her. In my opinion, she is rude, unprofessional, and has no understanding of what it takes to be a small business owner. 

 While we had their cakes many times in the past, after the way she spoke to my wife when they made a mistake on the price quoted for a cake we ordered, we will never be able to go to this bakery again.

You want a burger that looks just like the picture and won't break the bank??!! Well this is your place!! The burgers are so delicious and so beautifully presented!! Like most locations that I have ever been to it's PACKED inside and out! When we arrived the line for the drive thru was average but as soon as we were in line the line was just about at the entrance of the restaurant. 

I will tell you to caution on the well done fries. I have had my fries well done before I i also had them animal style and since I ordered them well done and no sauce they were extremely dry which is not their fault just a side of caution to others. The other order of fries that were regular it was delicious. 

The milkshakes are delicious as well! They really aren't anything too special but they do the job! 

If you are ok with carbs and more carbs stop by and get your fix!!

I have been totally blessed to have had some of the best vegan eats in the last month, and among them was Pura Vegan's Lucisous Live Food.  Although I will eat any vegan food that is healthy and gluten-free, I prefer uncooked, raw foods.  And I got some of the best raw food I have yet tried, at a sneak peek gathering at Pura Vegan, located at 307 Belt in the Debaliviere neighborhood of St.  Louis.  The Vegan & Veggie Support Group (founded by "No-Diet" Natalie, an up and coming veggie nutritional goddess) organized a gathering at Pura Vegan this March, and I was lucky enough to be one of the first 30 to RSVP, as the spots filled up quickly!  Pura Vegan is in a hip neighborhood close to the Loop, The Central West End, and just steps away from Forest Park.  Think Running groups in the morning, and post run "Magic Mushroom Coffee" and Green Elixirs!  This place is great!!  The owners, A.J. & Leah,  aren't the breatharian, zero fat zealous raw foodists types.  They are a hip young couple living in the real world.  While Pura Vegan is serious about it's healthy eats, they aren't "stuffy",  pretentious, over over-priced like a lot of raw food joints.  There isn't that uber anorexic, supplement promoting, exclusivity vibe here.  Just great eats, healthy raw sweet treats, and fun owners who "take themselves lightly".  Making raw food fun! They also offer all sorts of vegan & raw food preparation classes, for those of you who would like to be a raw food flirt at home!

    While you can get greens & sprouts, this place is offering much more! Dehydrated Crackers concocted from goodies like Flax, Seeds, and Nuts, Nut Cheezes, Elixirs packing in pounds of nutrition in one glass, and Cosmic Desserts that have "Cashew" cremes (AMAZING!!), cacao, and Cheezecakes.  You will walk out of this place both full and nourished and you won't have that guilt an hour later, "Why did I eat so much food?  Ick, I shouldn't have eaten SO much of that greasy, floury food!".  Nope, you will be planning your next visit to Pura Vegan because you are blissed out on Raw Cacao Balls!  The Veggie group was great......comprised of Vegans, Veggie Flirts, Runners, Rawbies, and friends of all of the above.  Some of my favorite conversation excerpts included "clogged chakras" and "but wouldn't everyone want to be a primary?".  Super fun peeps.

    I don't know whether it was the Contact High from being around so many other high raw peeps, the Cosmic Coffee Blend that owner A.J. created, or the "Power of the Prana", but it was impossible not to soak up the energy of all the life energy permeating the cafe that afternoon.  Pura Vegan will hopefully make their debut in about a month so maybe the end of April.  They are ready to go, but just waiting for "red tape" stuff from the city to give the "Green Light" to start sharing their "Life Food" with the world.  You must make a trip!

Get Skinny, Go Vegan.

The Falafel aren't awful, in fact they're divine. 
Gyros and Shawarma, but they don't serve wine. 
Tabouli and Kibby, tea with nuts pine. 
Kebabs off the grill, it's here you must dine.

Heard great things about this place and I am so glad that we tried this last night.

We did to-go order and because they were so busy it did take a bit longer for them to prepare everything than they had initially projected.  Unlike other restaurants that are running into this issue with COVID-19, they prevented a PACKED waiting area, by limiting the number of patrons in the restaurant to two at a time.  Pretty smart!!!

We ordered the Vegetarian Spring Rolls and they were even better than our other favorite spot for these yummy little starters.  I think the difference is the quality of the rice paper that they use and the way that they prepare their tofu.  They did not fall apart no matter how many times I kept dipping them in the AWESOME peanut sauce.

For my entree, I got the STIR FRY LEMONGRASS, CHILI, BELL PEPPER AND ONION / Xào Xả Ớt.  You can get it with pretty much any protein: Beef, Chicken, Pork, Shrimp or Tofu.  I am vegetarian so I went with the Tofu and found it to be very well prepared and extremely flavorful.   If you like Seafood, they also have a Seafood Combination version served with shrimp, mussels, calamari, and scallops.  Could be your new fav!!!

Next time we come there, we will have to sample their extensive list of bobas.  If we had known, we would have added these to our takeout order PHO SHO...

Yelp is all about finding the local flavor and boy does this place deliver.

Their menu is simple but the flavor is ALL THERE in every bite

Ordered a big mess o' stuff for a client that I was bringing lunch to.  Pressed Cubans, something called a Cheeseburger Cuban, Strawberry Shakes and a Pork Cuban.
Even though I called it in, this place was already JUMPING on a Tuesday at 11:30 and so I had to wait for about 10 minutes to pick it all up.
That's okay because this is also kind of a meeting place and folks were being patient and "neighborly" and just enjoying each other's company.
Can you imagine that?
Made me smile... which prompted someone else waiting to smile and before you knew it... my food was ready.
Oh my great googly moogly was this food incredible.
It was like all of the goodness and awesomeness of the 1950s was still here, including the plain simple white wrapping paper and paper bags.
I felt wholesome just holding it...
Then when I got back to my client, they were thrilled to know that I stopped at the Strawberry Hut and could not stop raving about all of their happy memories from there.
Our food was delicious and I could not believe when I looked down... that I had devoured the entire sandwich in one setting.
Apparently the other folks around me had more manners and more sense and saved the other half for later.
Ooooops!

Ahhhh I'm in love....with this place!!! The bestie and I hit this spot to begin our night. We intended on having just a drink at the bar - which let me add is a very classy bar that I wouldn't mind sitting at on any given evening with or without a drinking partner! 

Well the longer we sat to drink, the more tempted we were with everything passing our noses. They offered us some fresh bread which was just warm & scrumptious. 
We were eyeballing a yummy cheese platter someone else had so of course we had to order that. 

Bestie asked me if we should order some French onion soup. It was my deep dark secret that I had never tried it, ever, anywhere, in my lifetime. Not only was she blown away but so was the friendly server/bartender...so we ordered it and it was served to us with 2 spoons. 

I really can't brag enough about the service here. They really pay attention to their patrons, it's almost like they can read your mind and get you what you want before you even have to ask for it. 

The drinks were outstanding! Priced just right, mixed to perfection cocktails make me happy!!!! 

Since we were celebrating my birthday we also had some desserts. The chocolate mousse was MY JAM. You guys already know I'm a lover of all things chocolate. Like mmmmmmmmmmmm. 

No doubt about it we will be back. We'd like to be those cool regulars that the staff know by name. And Sonny (server/bartender) has a fantastic personality, asked us our names, chatted kindly with us when he had time, offered up food advice and flavor pairings, and even took a pic of me and my bestie knowing that it was a special night for us - ask for him & tip him well, he deserves it!!

2nd visit here will be my last. Had 10:45 reservations for 8 people. We get there at 10:40, and upon us checking in is when they decide to get a table ready for us. What is the purpose of a reservation if it doesn't help them prepare for your arrival?!?! 

Service was slow today and the restaurant was practically empty. 

They over cooked poached eggs.

A few of us added onion to our hash browns and they charged us $1.00 each...those are some expensive onions!!

Also, the only thing that made me return was the delicious Reese's pancake (see my picture from last time) which was unbelievably disappointing this time. Instead of a beautiful pancake loaded with tastiness, I got a mediocre pancake with some chopped up peanut butter cups thrown in the batter. When I told the waitress it didn't look the same, she asked if I needed some chocolate or something...or something is right - this thing was missing bananas, strawberries, whipped cream, and FLAVOR! But you better believe I got charged full price for half the pancake. 

I tried to like this place but I just can't figure out why the ratings are so high. Breakfast is my favorite meal, I won't waste it on a less than average eatery.

If I could give this place 10 stars, I would!! I am SO blown away!

First of all, service was absolutely outstanding. My bestie and I had never had Ramen before (yes, we have been living under a rock for a while) so we asked our server, Armando, for his recommendations. He went above and beyond explaining the menu and his favorites. Mind you, we showed up only about an hour before closing, so to get full attention & willingness to help so late in the day is impressive. We took his expert advice and ordered everything he was recommending:

Gyoza - OUTTA THIS WORLD DELICIOUS!! The best I've ever tasted! 

Seaweed salad: fresh & unique presentation 

Crispy Duck Ramen: where have you been all my life?! We had actually wanted to play it safe and order the short rib Ramen but we trusted our server and are so thankful! Please try the duck!!! You won't be sorry. 

Pork Belly bun: Simply a flavor explosion in our mouths! We were shying away from anything pork belly because of the "fattiness" (yes I made up that word) but it didn't taste fatty AT ALL. 

Drinks were superb. Cukes of Hazzard was a tasty gimlet & Godzilla had a wonderfully delicious kiwi purée that made it a pretty vibrant green color. 

I can't say enough good things about this place. Just go see for yourself!!

As of July 2018, I still think this place is 5 stars. The Krab Rangoon have changed since my original review a year ago & they're no longer a favorite of mine but still good nonetheless.

It is VERY easy to drive passed without even realizing it...Parking is minimal too.

We ordered:

Gyoza - they looked meh but the flavor was there. I'd definitely order them again. The sauce that is served with them was a little heavy with vinegar so I used soy sauce instead. 

Seaweed salad - Yum! Fresh and flavorful as usual. Needed soy sauce though.

Triple threat - sesame tuna with spicy scallions, spicy mayo & eel sauce. Scrumptious and a very large portion for $15! This is my favorite item of theirs although when I looked online I didn't see it on the menu anymore. It's possible I missed it but they still made it upon request so I'm a happy camper. 

California roll - I enjoyed this very much.

I consider myself a breakfast connoisseur and this time I was slightly disappointed. Maybe I had anticipated an amazing visit for so long that I over-hyped it. Don't get me wrong, the food here is good but the options are minimal and the prices are high for what you get. 

Pretty much everything is a carb. Think heavy comfort food.

Their biscuits and gravy is delicious. It has a spicy little kick but not too much heat. 

The grits were bland. Thick and full of texture but no flavor at all. 

I satisfied my curiosity and am glad I went. I wish I'd had gotten a cinnamon roll.  It's very doubtful that I'd return because there are so many other amazing breakfast options available.

After hearing great things for so long, my boyfriend and I decided to go here for his birthday. Neither of us have ever been but we have high expectations. We were greeted immediately as we entered the door. The restaurant was beautiful. We both got the Ruth's Classics, which is a prix fixe menu. I got a Caesar salad while my SO got the house. Both were good. 

Now onto what we were really here for, the steak. I ordered the filet at a medium temperature, while my boyfriend got the ribeye at medium rare. After waiting for some time (and eating a bunch of the complementary bread), we were served our steaks. Mine came out how I wanted, a nice pink color throughout. On the other hand, my boyfriend's steak was cooked medium well, so it was slightly pink, when he specifically requested medium RARE. So we told our waitress about it and she took it back saying they would make us a new one. Well after waiting a bit, they brought out his new ribeye, and after cutting through the middle, the steak was even more done than the previous one! The waitress looked at it and said that that didn't look right either. She brought us another plate to put it on so it wouldn't cook anymore and she asked if we wanted to redo it yet again. Having been there for so long already, we decided against it. She said she would tell the manager and have him have a word with us. Lo and behold, he doesn't come by. You know, as a steak house, I would expect them to know how to cook steaks at the temperatures requested. 

All in all, I'd say this place was a disappointment. The salad and the dessert were good, not amazing, but the fact that they had messed up on the ribeye twice is pretty unforgivable... Especially considering the price! If I'm spending nearly $200 on a dinner, I expect a lot. I now know to take my business elsewhere.

So far this is my favorite stop in Philly.  It is such a special, genuine Italian cafe serving lunch/dinner, gelato, coffee - both naughty and nice, beer, wine, you name it, they serve it. 

I sat at the bar cause I promised myself it would only be a mini meal. I was served by the friendliest, most accommodating fellow, and you could discern that he actually liked his job.  He was personable to all of us that sat there and gave suggestions as requested.

I got myself a hot chocolate, which wasn't just any hot chocolate.   My server offered to throw in a small bit of espresso because it was just better that way.  And my god it was a perfect blend of slight sweetness, decadently bitter and oh geez I need to have another one. I thoroughly enjoyed every sip and was disappointed when it was gone.

I imagine I'll find myself here every day that I'm in town... Maybe next time for the hot chocolate and gelato.

3.5 stars. 

I planned a date night for hubby and I during our stay in Philly. Prior to this, I had essentially been eating my way through the town alone since he got stuck working late daily. 

Making reservations was easy and so was finding the restaurant. We were able to park in the garage around the corner, though mind you, parking anywhere in downtown is ridiculously expensive ($27). 

The restaurant is beautiful, high ceiling, dim lighting, what you would expect from an upscale steakhouse. Service is good, not overbearing, but you definitely don't get forgotten.

The bread that started our meal was just OK. Bit tough on the outside and the inside was airy, but lacked that warm softness that would instantly melt butter.  I also ordered a ceasar salad, which was pretty good.

My hubbs ordered himself a ribeye, medium rare of course. I ordered a filet mignon, also medium rare.  We also ordered creamed corn and the stuffed hash browns. 

Filet mignon - tender, seasoned well, cooked to a medium rare
Delmonico - I unfortunately saw my hubby wrestle with his steak a bit, so it was tougher than we would anticipate from a high end steak house, seasoning and temperature were good, however
Stuffed hash browns- Just ok, I didn't set an expectation for this, but I wasn't impressed with it
Creamed Corn - meh, don't get it, it was quite liquidy, too savory and lacked some sweetness

Overall, great service and ambiance, \though our actual meal was just on the slightly better than OK point on the scale.

I absolutely loved this clusterfxck of food vendors jampacked into these tight quarters. I may even have been more excited about coming here than my visit downtown.  There are tons of people, super noisy which I think just adds to the appeal of this Philly staple.

This is a foodie's paradise. No joke. There are vendors everywhere selling every palatable whoozits and whatzitz imaginable.  cheesesteaks, pizza, pastries, cheese, meats, seafood, they have everything here. There's a lot of scattered tables for sitting and you can literally eat your way through the market if your belly and wallet allowed. 

Some shops are cash only, but most take credit cards.  Parking can be found in the neighboring areas for a small fee. 

In my one hour here, we managed to get a half dozen donuts, a cheesesteak, and pizza.  That didn't include much browsing time though.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to truly enjoy walking around and soaking up the atmosphere.

I was told I absolutely need to try Philly Pretzels while in town. Something about the water makes the bread that much better.  While that certainly was true when it came to my bagel experience in NY, I wasn't too impressed with these pretzels.

While searching for Federal Donuts, I chanced upon Philly Pretzel Factory.  Their menu is simple, no fancy shmancy, just pretzels in varied forms.  I got a pretzel with some cheddar.  

Unfortunately, my pretzel wasn't soft and pillowy as others had mentioned.  It was slightly stale and really not any better, in fact, not as good as what I would get from Wetzel's or Auntie Anne's. 

Service was good, however.  Just sad the pretzels weren't [as good]

Fighting out of the red corner, weighing 2 pounds, with a professional record of one thousand two hundred plus reviews and a nearly impeccable 4 stars... A native of New Orleans, Louisiana, and current pound-for-pound the best fried chicken in the woooooorrrrrllllldddddd........!!!!

Willllliiiieeeee Mmmaaaaaaaaaaeeesss!!!!!

I normally write reviews until I get back home in SoCal, but this could not wait. I feel like I owe this review to the community.

This is the best of the best of the best fried chicken.

You have not gone to New Orleans until you set foot beyond Willie Mae's doors, and taste their crispy, juicy and orgasmic fried chicken. Forget the other offerings. Just go straight to their best fried chicken and choose your sides according to your mood. Pair it with sweet tea, and savor the goodness of your meal.

NOLA, you are so damn lucky.

Unfortunately, I only discovered South a week or so ago, which means of course that I only had the option of getting takeout. With a little luck, maybe I'll be able to catch some jazz there in the next year and see what it's like to eat at the restaurant. But for now, I have only the quality of their food to judge on, and thankfully it was delicious.

We ordered a fried chicken platter that came with one each of breast, thigh, drumstick, and wing, as well as fingerling potatoes and collard greens. We also added an order of cornbread and an order of macaroni and cheese. I would say that the highlights were the chicken and our carb-y sides, though there was nothing in the order I didn't enjoy. 

The chicken was flavorful and moist and no worse for wear after my brief bike ride home from picking it up. One thing that amped up my enjoyment of it was the honey hot sauce that came with it. There's nothing particularly nuanced about it, but that doesn't mean it wasn't highly satisfying. The sweet aspect was present but never threatened to overwhelm and I guess you could say the same about the heat; if you like spicy food on most levels you should be able to enjoy it - a real spice junkie won't find it crazy hot, but will still get a nice, flavorful kick from it and someone with limited spice capacity who's maybe still building their tolerance will find it strong but bearable (especially if you can factor the cornbread in - more on that later). 

Rounding out the basic fried chicken platter, I guess I would point to the fingerling potatoes (normal and purple mixed) as the last remarkable part of the meal. They were kind of just there without much special preparation seeming to have gone into them...so thankfully they're potatoes and potatoes are just awesome additions to any meal and easy enough to season with a few shakes of a spice shaker. The collard greens, on the other hand, were definitely a pleasant surprise. They list as "turkey collard greens" and I can't say I would have been able to tell you there was turkey involved just by looking and tasting. But the flavor of the greens was excellent, with a little spicy kick on the back end. It was the most I'd enjoyed collards in a while. 

As for the additional sides, thumbs up on both. Both were large, shareable size (don't get me wrong, it would be a ripoff if they were normal side-size at the price you pay for them, but it's fine for what you actually do get). The cornbread was on the sweet, almost desert-y side of the cornbread spectrum, which went fine with the otherwise savory, somewhat spicy rest of the order. The macaroni and cheese were rich and heavy, but the right levels of those adjectives. I've had any number of mac and cheeses from restaurants that go way too far down the richness rabbit hole to the point where any more than two or three bites feels excessive and like a free pass to heartburn city, but I ate a proper side's worth of this along with everything else I've mentioned and felt a-ok. 

The little service you could say I had - ordering on the phone and picking up the order - was pleasant and friendly. I'm looking forward to ordering from here again and, whenever the time is deemed right, to going in for the full experience.

Horrible. Complete horrible. Food was cold. Served stuff we were allergic too and owner wouldn't take it back and got in our face saying it's really good. Will he pay the hospital bill? Ugh disgusted.

Game show host- "welcome back to the price for dinner, next up to guess the price for dinner Aaliyah P ..... Come on down...

Aaliyah P - omg !!!! I'm gonna be on the price for dinner!!!!

Game show host - Aaliyah P tell us a little bit about yourself .

Aaliyah P- I live in Wilmington DE and love to yelp and dine out!

Game show host- ok Aaliyah are you ready? 

Aaliyah P -I was born ready!

- last nights experience at The UYE @ Sycamore was amazing from start to finish ... Each course was prepared with not only Fresh seasonal ingredients but love and attention . You can tell Chef Sam really puts an enormous amount of thought into the food he prepares...
I'll tell you all what you missed ..( and you can drool over the photos)

we as a table shared cheese board ( can't recall the cheeses except for one that was bathed in Chimay...) the accompaniments were equally amazing ... Date spread ... Olives and apple slices .

The chilled carrot soup was next - not quite cold room temperature with a velvety texture . You could actually taste the carrots and there was a hint if curry lingering along with the lime scented creme fraiche.

Tria's sultry sophisticated sister moved in a few blocks west and is doing amazing things.
For those that know me are aware that I love the following in no particular order... House music , champagne and all things Tria. When the rumor mill began a few months back about a brand new Tria I was more that intrigued. Based on my first visit to Tria Taproom I'm sure I'll be a repeat diner/imbiber.
As others have stated its ecxactly what the name states a tap room. Don't come expecting a bottle of anything. Both the beer and wine list are equally impressive and I had a chance to sample the Tempranillo as well as the locally made cab franc. In comparison to the other tria locations I will say that wine list is more purse friendly, but still offers amazing known varietals and something you may have never tried.

I'm sure the wine list will rotate but I will say the cab franc was a 5oz glass of jammy goodness and I would highly recommended it. 

The food options are very different from the other locations more kitchen fare is how I would describe it. Options range from flat breads, wings , ribs and a few dips sprinkled in. I think everyone will have options here if dining. I opted for the garbanzo purée to accompany my two glasses of wine. It had a slight spice and came  inside a jar layered with feta and roasted peppers. The grilled flatbread served along side it was chewy and still crisp, exactly how I like my flatbread to be. It was the perfect dinner and very filling and well priced at 6.00 for the jar. 

The atmosphere is still very tria awesomely seductive , with low lights and instead of candles there are  lots if industrial lights scattered throughout. 

There's plenty of seating along a 8-12 seat bar and a few high top chairs, the back space has a few high top tables and a long bench that would be  perfect for a crew the size of the former team fun. 

I think this tria tap room is a great addition to this neighborhood and though i lost my favorite gayborhood tria manager Chris I can visit him a little closer to work at Tria Tap room.

Go . sip . Eat and repeat

For a fried chicken experience that'll make you poop hot fire the next day, I expect excellence on all fronts. Gus's "World Famous" Fried Chicken, while tasty, does not live up to the hype or the price.

We went around when it opened last month and the chicken was average. As a person who eats chilies the same way fat kids eat popcorn, I was disappointed that there was no option to make my memphis style fried chicken cayenned to the point where it would be physically painful to ingest. If you're the kind of person who thinks adding cabernet sauvignon to your pot roast makes it too spicy, Gus's might be right up your alley. Those of us who enjoy our curries at 11 on the scale of 10 might be let down by the default level of spice.

What really gets me about this place is the cost. The basic chicken plate is pricey and comes with slaw and beans as a default. If you want any of the higher end sides like mac n cheese or potato salad be prepared to shell out extra for each side substitution. A meal here can get expensive really quick, especially if you opt for a slice of their artery clogging pies for dessert.

Gus's is worth checking out once or twice but seriously, you can get better fried chicken for much less at a swanky grocer like Straub's (who I swear put garam masala in their chicken batter) than this gimmick export from Tennessee.

Typical seafood restaurant with a great location. Longboards Grill is huge with two stories and was jam packed when we arrived. Well...the World Cup Soccer was on that weekend. 

The good news is we just walked right in and sat upstairs.....however we did not get prime seating. They have roasted peanuts in a huge barrel and the floor is covered with peanut shells.

The menu is extensive and we asked the waitress their most popular dishes. She recommended the Turkey Burger and Fish and Chips. We asked whether the fish was fresh and she of course replied, "yes".

The Turkey Burger was actually pretty descent. The Fish and Chips was disappointing...It clearly looked like frozen breaded fish you can get at Denny's. The Shrimp Pasta was a little heavy for lunch. 

The overall bill came to $100 (with tip) for 4 people which we thought was pretty pricey for lunch. But then again you're paying for real estate.

Their restrooms are located downstairs. The women's restroom was tiny and stuffy with only 3 stalls....to accommodate people in their 2-story restaurant.

Overall the food was a hit or miss and the service was okay.

The room was fine. However, I'm truly disappointed and angry by how they handle the billing. 

We stopped in without a reservation and asked was initially quoted a rate of $261. I told them I would be back to start the paperwork. When I came back in to the lobby  agent #3 started my paperwork at which point she offered us a room at a rate of $151. I couldn't believe my ears! I was ecstatic and asked her why. Her response was because it had an accessible tub. I didn't know what that meant and probe a little but more about what that meant. I even double checked and verified that I was hearing the price correctly. She confirms. 

The next morning we get a bill under our door for $100 more so I went up to the front desk to explain the situation. They made the adjustment. I was thrilled that valued our patronage and honored the price quoted. 

A week later, we find out they readjusted out bill up. I called the hotel again three times just to get the run around or no call back. 

When I eventually got on the phone with the front desk manager. Although he was on shift that night he admits to not hearing our whole conversations, doesn't own up to his employees mistake, and basically calls me a lair. 

The disappointment isn't about $100 but it's about principle. Big ole' multimillion Hyatt is willing to sacrifice customer satisfaction over $100.  

I've worked in the travel industry for many years for a very successful car company. We were willing to go to great lengths to keep our customers happy especially when it was our mistake. We always gave our customers the benefit of the doubt. Shame on you front desk team on 12/28/14.

Recess is one of the best restaurants in the Midwest.  I loved the fact that high quality food was served in a relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere.  If I lived in Indianapolis, it would be a weekly destination.  

Perhaps the most amazing thing about Recess is that the menu changes everyday.  Nonetheless, the food is executed at a high level, as if the chefs had been turning out these dishes for months.  The highlights of our meal included a piece of whitefish with a crisped skin that was moist and delicious.  Two diners at our table could not eat shellfish, and instead of a seafood broth received a sunchoke puree that was fantastic.  The ribeye was also tremendous.

Surprisingly, dessert was my favorite part of the meal.  The rstaurant ran out of grapefruit sorbet (part of a larger desert) and instead we were brought cookies that were made with chopped up candy bars, with a side of fresh whipped cream.  My description cannot do justice to the flavor; the very best cookies that I've ever eaten and one of the best deserts as well.

Wine pairings were astute and the server (Alex?) and chef (Greg) could not have been more hospitable.  An unbelievable experience.

Went to lees on a whim after drooling over their Instagram page for a few weeks. Got a shrimp and chicken Alfredo cheessteak with spinach. It was aaaaammmaaaazing. The food is good the place is clean and cheery. The price is up there but the quality of the food particularly the bread and seafood is  worth paying more than I would normally. Mr Lee and staff are very friendly and patient while you choose from their endless selection.  Make it a point to stop here if you are in u city and on the prowl for good eats!!

Truly one of the most delicious meals of my life. Showed up for our 8:30 reservation and we were greeted & seated. The restaurant is small, but comfortable. They have it set up well, so you're not smothered. Our server was friendly and very helpful while explaining the menu. 
   We started with the gnocchi/Gorgonzola in a brown butter sauce. What a fantastic start to the meal!! Talk about melt-in-your mouth flavors and just some of the best gnocchi I've ever tasted in my life! For my entree I had the fisherman stew, which was amazing. One of the most flavorful things I have ever eaten in my life. Loaded with seafood, cous cous and the most incredible sauce. My boyfriend had the roasted chicken which was also so so so good. It was so well executed and flavorful. Last but not least, I HAD to get the zeppolis for dessert and they did not disappoint one bit. Fluffy and airy, with Nutella... you cannot go wrong there. 
    Honestly, make a reservation ..... you will not be disappointed!!!

I am really trying to like Al Pastor. 

I live in the neighborhood and have been here 5 times since it has opened and I can honestly say I have only had one real positive experience with both service and food, the other times have been mediocre.  I truly wish and hope they can  master what it takes to provide good food and equally as important good service. I feel this restaurant has good potential, they just haven't been able to be consistent. 

I should start with stating I am a "foodie" and love going to great restaurants and experiencing new places. I have traveled to many many places around the world and the highlights are always around the culinary experience. I don't mind spending the money when I feel the quality, value and experience is aligned with the cost. 

With the above stated I feel as though Al Pastor is very over priced for what you receive. 

Case and point, my colleague and I went to Al Pastor this evening after a very late night in the office. I called first to make sure we weren't inconveniencing the kitchen/waitstaff since it was already after 9pm. The associate who answered the phone advised me the kitchen was open until 10pm. Perfect, we work 3 min down the road. 

When we arrived no one was at the hostess station therefore, we thought since it was late, it was a seat yourself. We sat down and it took a little bit for someone to come greet us. A very apologetic and embarrassed waitress made her way over to us while other associates in the restaurants didn't take notice. 

Pro's: 

Guacamole tastes great, octopus tacos were very good. I love octopus cooked the right way. This is all I have for pro's. 

Cons:

Guacamole does not come with salsa, it was an additional $3.00 total cost for guacamole and salsa is $11.00 (ouch), Tacos are good with zero sides, my octopus tacos were $13.00 without a small side.
