I would have been hungry without the chips. The waiters  made a mistake with my colleagues dish, completely wrong order and all the waitress did was apologize. Truth be told, she was upbeat I didn't feel she was attentive. It wasn't until I said, do you want her (the waitress) to get you what you ordered, the waitress only then offered to put in another order at no cost. My colleague didn't want to bother and settled for the dish she was given. The waitress seemed more interested in socializing while waiting for my margarita. I was already done with my tacos (I didn't mention above the tacos are small too) when the waitress arrived with my second margarita. Yes, the margarita's are good however i am putting this under cons due to how small they are. My first margarita had a plain rim, by second margarita had a flavored rim yet we were never asked if wanted a flavored rim. 

Our bill for chips, guacamole, salsa, two order of tacos and 5 margaritas (yes they are small) was over $85.00 before tip. To top it off, the waitress never offered to comp my friends meal or at minimum the guacamole for not giving her the right dinner. All she did was apologize and then stated "I hope you liked it" 

The service level, cost and value do not align. Again, I truly hope they can reel this in and provide the neighborhood with a good quality wth good service  Mexican restaurant. I have been cheering for them however, as mentioned above my overall experience has not been overly positive.

This is probably one of the few perfect restaurants that I have been too. Food was amazing I was stunned. The service was quick and friendly and eager to help don't know why people are saying it was slow but I guess people will always find something to complain about. The price stunned me two we got huge portions of delicious food for a great price so overall great food service, price and food. What more could you want?

Okay, I will admit that if you were to rewind about three years, I'd say that I wasn't a fan of Poco's, but after reading an article in the D-town magazine about them, I was inspired to give them another chance. As many other Yelper's have mentioned, this is definitely a tex-mex kinda place. If you're looking for 100% authentic Mexican, you're better off going to downtown Quakertown (where some of my favorites are). Poco's puts a different twist on Mexican food which I appreciate. My recent visits have left me satisfied and wanting to go back. The atmosphere is fun and lively so just going for drinks can be a blast, but I wouldn't leave without having their new fried ice cream. This is the real deal people - not just ice cream with corn flakes or rice krispies sprinkled on top...they fry the ice cream which is coated in a crispy outside layer and cover it in toppings of your choice...soooooooo good.

Okay, this one's a stretch, but play along anyway:

1. Picture everything you love about Golden Corral.
2. Multiply the goodness factor about twenty times.
3. Now picture everything you hate about Golden Corral.
4. Poof! It's gone. You are now having lunch at Monell's at the Manor.

Pretty lame? I can't hit home runs all the time. The bottom line is $13.95 gets you the best weekday lunch deal in Nashville, with two meats & a whole bunch of sides. This particular Monell's appears to be a two-story mansion, and I bet they do a lot of weddings here. Very picturesque, and the second floor is fun to explore. 

You're going to sit with a bunch of other people, you pass to your left, and no one wants to hear your cell phone. It's Southern Comfort family style. Vegheads will go nuts with the sides. I could argue my fried chicken was a bit dry & the catfish a tad batter-heavy, but that's small stuff - I kept feeling I was a foreign exchange student invited to some Southern professor's family home. I'm sure this place is an icon, and I kept wanting to call everyone "Colonel." Monell's at the Manor is definitely worth the trip. "More corn puddin', Colonel, Suh?"

I could probably make this one of my longest reviews, so for that reason, I'll keep it short:

The Catbird Seat was my favorite dining experience in Nashville. They did everything I love - prix fixe menu, small plates, innovative preparation & presentation. You sit at a big square surrounding the chefs at work, and whichever chef made your current dish will present & explain it to you. You'll meet all of them.

You know how I define a great restaurant experience? It's not about a particular dish, but walking in some highly regarded place not quite sure what'll happen, and two hours later merrily chatting away with complete strangers who were merrily chatting away with me, because all of us were genuinely stoked. Seriously, are there a lot of restaurants where that happens? 

You make resos here a month in advance, and you don't see the menu until you leave. If you really enjoy restaurants, you should simply do this place and treat yourself. In Nashville, the Catbird Seat is on top of my list.

Here's an easy review. You know, every city has some local born & bred coffeehouse that does well and gives all those "Let's-hate-on-Starbucks" peeps a place to go to. In Nashville, we wound up at this Frothy Monkey place. I thought it was pretty cool. I also like anything with "Monkey" in its name.

I pretty much stick with hot & black, I don't care about coffeehouse food and muffins, and the booze/food/coffee menus here are up front by the cashier people. My straight coffee was good. A neat house, friendly staff, and a wonderful vantage point for sitting outside people-watching, in this apparent hip & cool trendster area of Nashville. A most pleasant respite. How can I not be a fan of that?

Ordered Takeout.

Easy to order, food was ready when I arrived, pretty quick service, place looked clean/fine.

Food was very bland. Like, NO flavor. Didn't taste like Chinese (or any Asian) food at all. It's in 70124 so I wonder if 1) the cooks are Chinese 2) they are tailoring their food to Anglo tastebuds. 

Ah well...

God bless Lee's Deli. The most delicious, reliable option in the neighborhood. A real gem. I recommend it to out of town visitors and center city folk as the best example of great West Philly food. I love the buffalo chicken cheesesteak, the egg and cheese croissant, the carrot cake. If West Philly didn't have Lee's Deli it would be a food wasteland. It's definitely greasy, in the best way possible.

This place is tucked in a strip mall off of Binford Blvd. my first time ordering from this place, I opted for takeout. I love the delivery window they have that you can walk up to after parking. The customer service was great, and we promptly picked up our order. I tried the Wood Stock pizza, Dough Buds, and Hip Hop salad. The salad was fantastic, with very fresh ingredients. I absolutely loved the dough buds and all three sauces. The pizza topped the cake, was so good. I'm definitely adding this place into my pizza rotation!! 

Update: 

Shout out to Missing Brick for having carry out so I could get my fix! So grateful to have their comfort food during covid19.

I'll put the TLDR first: MEH. Mostly basic menu, bad food and okay service. And too expensive for food that was not fresh. Now on to the details.

I was really looking forward for this place to open. They did a lot of work in the building formally called the schoolhouse. They built a huge deck out front, and added lots of wood and TVs inside. Its pretty nice and does have a New England feel. Now, I realize this is a Boston themed restaurant, but the Red Sox and Patriots stuff was too much. You're in FL now, so maybe some support for OUR teams too would be nice. I'm not letting let bias my review.

We started with a beer. Decent beers, moderately priced ($4-$6) and a full cocktail list. Our server gave us the wrong beers. I know you're new, but something like getting the right drink doesn't take months of on the job training. 

On to the food. They were out of lobster so we couldn't try the bisque. We decided to start with the "stuffies". The clams were chewy and inedible. Gross really. The rest of the menu was extremely basic bar food. They had a few special seafood dishes, but not enough to stand out. For our entrees, I got a buffalo chicken wrap, and my boyfriend got the fisherman's seafood platter.  My wrap was just a notch above the mcdonalds snack wrap: dry and boring. The fries were good. The $20 seafood platter wasn't much better. The claims were horrible. They were so chewy they tasted frozen, or not cooked right. There was also only 2 shrimp on the plate.  I don't mind spending money on quality food. But if I can go to the grocery store and buy frozen claim strips and popcorn shrimp and be more satisfied than with a restaurant meal, we have a problem. 

I left $70 poorer, and dissatisfied. I feel like the mistakes were too much that I can't chalk them up to this place being new. I won't be coming back. Do yourself a favor and choose one of the many BETTER pubs within a 10 minute drive. I give this place less than a year.

EDIT: this might be a case of yelp being dishonest. Some of the poor reviews are not "recommended" meaning they don't show up in the ratings. It's mostly people with one review, but how come the positive ratings from 1 review people show up? It's fishy to say the least. I'm Hoping my review continues to show up. This place is NOT a 4.5 star. The real rating with all averages to about a 2.5/3.

I was SO impressed by draught house. We went their opening weekend, and everything was perfect! 
They pretty much gutted the entire building. The bar is large and opens up to outside which is large with plenty of tables and a dog friendly area. Inside is small-ish but also has the garage style doors that open up for max air flow. 
We sat at the bar outside and were greeted immediately by our two great bartenders, Tanya and Chris. They were so friendly and efficient! True to their name, they have an extensive beer list: local brews, crafts, and a large selection of Belgium's and other imports. They also have an interesting signature cocktail menu. All the drinks I tried from it were A+!
What really sets this place apart is their food menu. It has a little Asian flair, featuring noodle bowl and banh mi, is also had lots of pork belly and vegetarian options. We tried the jerk wings...so juicy and served with a pineapple chutney. We also had the fig,   prosciutto, and goat cheese flatbread. Outstanding! The flatbread itself was homemade, chewy and delicious, and the toppings made it out if this world. 
Draught house is just what Dunedin needs! I'm so happy I live a short walk away because I NEED to try everything on their menu!

This new coffee shop is located inside the wine and brew, which is right next to Dunedin House of Beer. I've been 3 times and all have been great. They have an extremely knowledgable staff who will teach you about different types of coffee and brewing of which I was totally unaware even existed! 
Being a creature of habit (and because it's florida in the middle of summer) I've gotten the cold brewed iced coffee. It's amazing. Doesn't get watered down, and tastes so smooth! I add a little bit of their organic sugar cane syrup and it's like heaven. I took my boyfriend to 9th today and he ordered the iced pour over. I had no clue what a pour over was before I watched the owner, Omar (who is amazing btw) make it! Basically it's a hand brewed coffee, but rather than explain it, go check it out for yourself!! 
9th bar also has some crazy cereal concoctions. Cereal drizzled in chocolate with fruits and espresso and some other wild and creative ingredients. Today they were testing out their donut collaboration with Hren's nest. Both donuts, a chocolate espresso and Captain Crunch, we're delicious. 
9th bar is wonderful! Come hungry and thirsty and I guarantee you will leave happy :)

I'm not a fan. 

Hippot Shabu Shabu seems like one of those places that should thrive but doesn't for some odd reasons. But once I sat down to eat I realized why. 

To order you'll first pick a base -- i chose the half/half which is a bone marrow + spicy hot broth. The soup alone cost $19.95, then I added a vegetable combination which cost $8.95, a plate of beef - $6.95, a plate of 3 frozen (and fishy smelling) oysters for $6.95, and bean thread vermecelli for $2.95. 

with one drink added, my total came out to be $55 ish (not including tip), which is just too much to spend on what i feel like is a subpar hotpot experience. 

I lived in Taiwan for a year where hotpot was just a common thing-- but here in philly it's feels like such an overpriced novelty and even in other cities, hotpot isn't this expensive! At the minimum, a hotpot "meal" typically comes with a small plate of meat + vegetables and you can add more for extra cost. But not here. 

to pay $20 for just the broth is just a step from ridiculous to me. 
What am i going to do with just a broth, swish it around?!

I won't be back.

I think alot people forget about this place. Right next to the Abbys Desert Lounge and Fu Wah, Lee's kind of gets the cold shoulder. It really isn't the most welcoming place in the world and it's not really a deli either. But it is a tight spot for some alright grill food. West Philly is devoid of good greasy spoon type of breakfest places except for Philly Diner. But Lee's is the real deal. The eggs are cooked to order, crisp bacon, hearty sausage patties and potatoes with tons of fried onions. Get some toast with it and a decent cup of black coffee and the day is on!  Oh and that jam is served all the live long day.

Doing NOLA in 12 hours drastically limits your choices, so one must choose with a great deal of discernment. This is where yelp bridges the gap, where I rely upon my yelp peers to provide knowledge where I lack.

Because Mathew M and I were unable to have breakfast at Lüke, we opted for the 340+ review, 4.5 star rated Surrey's Café & Juice Bar.

Service was a mixed bag. We arrived before opening, gained entrance at 8am sharp, and was let in and greeted with a tepid response by one gal who remained that way the entire time we dined. The other gal was much peppier.

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/vN6v8m4DO45Z4pp8yxxF_w?select=vr8oK9ZjwFb-qWoWH1Iysg
I really dug their decor, tables, and condiment racks affixed to the wall and off the table and it was cool sitting at the table where Matthew McConaughey sat, as was depicted by a framed photo on the wall. Needless to say, this hipster dive made me feel like I was back home in Los Angeles.

Surrey's is part juice bar, so it only makes sense to order some juice, right? My order included Orange Beet Juice and Surrey's renown Bananas Foster French Toast.

16 oz Orange Beet Juice ($6.65): 2/5
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/vN6v8m4DO45Z4pp8yxxF_w?select=FJM9qjF5_iWKU0FeMFDhBw
Seldom do I complain about price, but $6.65 for juice is rather ridiculous, even for organic juice. Organic juice in Los Angeles isn't even as pricey as Surrey's! While there was no disputing the level of freshness of this organic juice, my juice was particularly tart and frankly, could of had benefitted from more beet. Perhaps it was my fault for not requesting a higher ratio of beet to orange...

Bananas Foster French Toast ($9.25): 2.5/5
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/vN6v8m4DO45Z4pp8yxxF_w?select=86z5qt7a_wNKglhHJrt-YQ
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/vN6v8m4DO45Z4pp8yxxF_w?select=tMH8lL6r67ihRNTxavQ3MA
Sorry, but this was not as mind-blowing as many have lead me to believe. Yes, the banana creme cheese was rather tasty but overall, this was way too rich and sweet...so sweet that I started getting the sweet sweats! In spite of the high sweet level of this dish, you won't have any difficulty devouring these stuffed toasted baguette slices because it is just so light. You surely will not have your fill and will have to order something else to supplement otherwise you'll leave hungry.

Mathew M ordered Orange Juice and Surrey's Scrambled Eggs with Salmon and was not totally elated...and he footed the bill, which came out to $35.21 after tax before tip. Let's do the math, shall we:
Premium Prices + Mediocre Food + Leaving Hungry = EPIC FAIL!!!

As much as I really wanted to love Surrey's, there just wasn't much to tip the scale north of 2 stars. Sorry yelpers but you led me astray this time...

Time to let the hateful compliments roll in...flame on!

=/

I'm going to be honest here - I am a Fat Lady. I've had a donut or two in my day. 

THESE ARE THE BEST DONUTS I HAVE EVER HAD. There is no question - there is no competition. They are the best, hands down and that's all there is to say about it. 

This stand was recommended by my hotel - they were like "oh my god, if you're going to the Market you have to get a donut" and I was like "whatever, it's like 2pm and who eats a donut at 2pm?" But I walked by the stand and saw a fairly long line and I'm a joiner at heart so I waited too. Prices are CHEAP (just over $1/ea) and that staff is as sweet as the items they sell. 

For science I had 2 (see: Fat Lady, above) - a glazed which is a good baseline and a blueberry fritter recommended by the staff. It's not something I would have picked because I was worried it would be heavy and dry - it was most emphatically not. It was the most perfect, delicious thing - feather light, still a tad warm and everything you ever wanted a donut to be. I wandered around the market, getting glaze flakes all over myself and I cared not a whit because who cares when you are eating the best donuts ever? 

Now I'm going to really have to impress these clients at tomorrow's meeting so I can come back often and EAT MORE DONUTS.

Awesome Food here.  Margaritas are stellar, they know how to make margaritas, yum .  Great Staff, wonderful food.  I ordered the chili relleno and chicken enchilada.   So good. I Love coming here to eat.  I am not a fan of rice in general, but this place knows how to make it..  sooo good to the last bite and I eat it all.  I love getting notices in the app for specials here on my phone.   Ya gotta go to happy hour.   Thanks Murriettas!!

Great.  Delicious.   Did not go in as we were super busy that day and it was pouring down rain so we decided to order out.  My husband went to pick it up, what a really classy place he said. Very nice on the phone so we ordered two ribeyes medium rare,  salad and a baked potato.  Yum, we could not wait to eat that it looked delicious. 
Hubby comes back and says guess how much it was?    I said what,  he goes just guess , I said 50 bucks he says no it was $100 for two steaks, I about fell  off my chair.   But we were starving.  He said it was a really nice steakhouse.   
Salad was tasty, baked potato perfect, and the Ribeye was cooked perfectly and seasoned great.     I cut mine in half, 14oz petite they said, was big.   It was sooo good.  They also have a 20 oz one too.  Can't wait to see what that looks like.  The meal was perfect.  Thanks.

I'm heartbroken. Learned tonight when we stopped in for a take-out craving that the place has been sold to a new owner. No more off-menu appetizers in the front case (the real, authentic items like tendons, tripe, etc.). No pork belly. No Chinese only menu that the other owner would ALWAYS translate and taylor to our tastes. No more Kung Pao beef that has just beef, peanuts, and scallions. And to top it off, the new owner acted like we were crazy for wanting such things. My boyfriend pulled out of him that the previous owner has a new spot, but he wouldn't tell him where! I understand not wanting a customer to go somewhere else, but it was painfully obvious that he wouldn't be offering the things we wanted..... Sigh. I hope we figure out where she went or find a new place soon. I'm hungry.

I really don't even know where to start. I wanted to give this place the benefit of the doubt and try it myself instead of relying on other reviews. We had the fried ravioli for an appetizer. Mediocre to say the least. Then for dinner I had the roasted garlic cream sauce with chicken. Also mediocre. I make a better cream sauce at home...not to mention the ridiculous amount of garlic cloves in the sauce. My husband loves spicy food and had the spicy penne with vodka sauce. It was so extremely hot that he could only stomach a few bites. My step son had the spaghetti and meatballs. His meatballs were chewy and tasteless. We had two martinis and a soda. Our bill came to $122. Overpriced and under seasoned...it's a NO GO on Zolo's.

This restaurant is run by a bunch of dumb ass half wits...we come into the place the other day after they JUST opened up after being shut down for COVID ....not ONE freaking waiter or waitress is wearing a mask...(I'm assuming the cooking staff who is out of sight isn't either)...I hope they get their asses sued off...or vandalized in a riot....eat here at your own risk...

I have dined here a dozen times and I am always impressed! Each time has been on business so I do not have any photos to share (unfortunately). It's hard to resist taking a photo of food that is plated well!

The restaurant is consistently clean and the servers are attentive as well as friendly. I always see the same smiling faces working which is a good sign. The manager has been here every visit and makes it a point to check in at each table asking "how is everything." 

The menu is crazy long so the first couples time I went I didn't have high expectations for the food being good. Well I was wrong. I will say their chicken and waffles are amazing! Corn beef hash is solid. For lunch, Margherita pizza is amongst the top three margarita pizzas I've ever had. Their Greek salad with juicy grilled chicken is huge and beautifully prepared. I especially like their twisty seasoned fries. 

I have never experienced a wait however I have dined before or after prime time. I'm sure this place gets busy. Take note that if the parking lot is full there is a gravel lot one building down that you can park in. 

Great spot for the little town of Dunedin!

When I used to live in the area, I ate at this place probably two or three times. First time, food was not bad, so we returned.

Second time, food was unedible. Absolutely could not eat it. They tried to help out, or though it seemed. Nothing happenes. Burger was the same...unedible.

Moral of this story...you MAY want to come here, but you're better off buying and eating a raw block of instant Ramen.


I didn't want to write of review on this place, because I only had negative things to say before. However, the stunt that the management pulled was extremely unprofessional, and now I feel my true review is necessary

A rest stop on 95 to get fuel, food, coffee, basic necessities and use the restroom. Considering this is on Highway 95, the restaurants should be operating 24/7 but instead most close at 10pm...how does that make any sense? Especially on weekends! 

I stopped here at 10:05pm and most restaurants were closed except for Burger King and Starbucks. They were just closing up and still had food on the counter. I asked if they were still open? And the worker rudely said to me "What does it look like to you?" And shook his head. Wow! Rude service! 

2 stars for this place because of starbucks being open...not a fan of burger king.

Won't stop here again unless a dire emergency.

Currently my favorite fried chicken place! The fried chicken here is unimaginably light and flaky. It's nothing like I've ever had! How is it so flaky?? You won't need any sauce on your chicken because it's well season and so tasty. 

You get 3 pieces of chicken, either dark or white, plus 1 side dish. I chose the green beans, which comes with rice and gravy with meat. This side dish is surprisingly pretty big. The green beans were soft and delicious. 

The place is pretty big. There's multiple rooms where they seat people. We came right when it opened on Saturday, so we avoided the crowd. 

I look forward to coming back again!

Its a Tuesday night and a bunch of us are out celebrating my work friends birthday.  Off to the old pub in bordentown for my second visit.  It was $5 margarita Tuesday so of course I got one.  Served in a mason jar with a nice sweet sour taste.  Appetizers calamari and pork nachos.  Both were tasty however the pork stood out being sweet and delicious.  I had the Mani Mani tacos with fries.  You get 3 of them with French fries.  Thier topping sauce was excellent and the fish was done right.  Prices are $15-$30 and all the food was good.  Dinner for 7 with no desert was $200.  All in all very nice experience and good food

COVID SAFETY ISSUES HERE.  AND MAJOR CA HEALTH CODE VIOLATIONS. 
We went in today for lunch and not one person who prepared our food was wearing gloves or washed their hands before preparing our food. 
Number one, this is a violation of basic, basic CA health code (even if you're unfamiliar with health code, a simple Google search would tell you this).  Number two, how could you refuse to enforce CA health code during a GLOBAL PANDEMIC. 

The guy who made our nachos stuck his bare hands into their box of cheese (which by the way, is just sitting out), and sprinkled the cheese onto our chips.  Immediately we looked at each other and were like uhhhh wait, wtf? 

We asked them why no one was wearing gloves and they said they didn't have to.  (Again, this is against CA health code). 

They also had about 9 employees working on their tiny assembly line shoulder-to-shoulder.....is that really necessary?  

Also, just as a basic note:  our food was not that tasty and small portioned.  Completely not worth the money. 

The last time we came here was about a year ago, and after today, we will never be back. 
If we get sick, I know who the prime suspect will be.

Great place!

Come support them as they recently just reopened dine-in due to covid

They have great service!

If you're on a date, ask for that special seat that Johnny and Mrs. Johnny sat (which is the only seat you'll find attached to the bar counter)

Request that special New York Sour and tell them Johnny told you.. you'll be glad because the bartender is great and he makes excellent drinks especially that Manhattan which is probably the best I had

We also had a snack of fingeling potatoes as they require you to have a snack if you're only coming in and drinking

Definitely a place that has a downtown feel as it is in downtown where you would come in and drink after work.. I mean if I lived here, I would go here after work.. you know what I'm saying

Best Cheesesteaks by far.. I tried tourist friendly Pat's and Geno's and more local Ishkabibble's and this one.. and yes.. Tony Luke's was closed too early and also on the next day as well on Sunday as we were leaving to go back to Seattle..

this place's cheesesteak had premium, thinly sliced beef on a tender, soft hoagie and the cheese.. it had a queso feel to it.. indeed, this sandwich was very comforting and good!

good staff, great service

shout out to Mikey Chen for highlighting this on his video.. indeed a good one

Used to come here years ago when the restaurant was known for their "Cheers" atmosphere. 
Had to make a trip back into town and I love the hotel.... so was looking forward to heading to the restaurant for some food. I arrived at the bar at 9:15 pm. Place was pretty empty. But I do like how they re-did everything. Looks great. 
Took a seat at the bar. There was a total of 4 people there. ( Friday night)
I waited. I waited. Bartender seemed more interested in getting his hot sauce bottles lined up. 
Finally I said.." Can I get a cocktail?". You would think he would have said.. "gee.. sorry I didn't see you come in? " or something to that affect. 
Nope. Tossed a napkin my way. I asked for a vodka club soda. He says" house?" I say do you have Tito's? Didn't answer.... just went and placed it in front of me. No lemon or lime. He never asked. Really? 
Okay... so I ask for a food menu. 
Put it in front of me. Once again.... never came back over ... I had to say I'll have a Pub burger. 
He mumbled something... and I said " The Pub Burger" he said "Temperature?". Ugh... medium well. 
That was our food order exchange. Put a silverware roll up in front of me and ketchup. I wanted another drink , had to get his attention to order. 
Dude.... the place is empty. You should be soliciting for us to drink and eat. 
Sad part is... Burger was great. Thank you. 
Bartender..... useless. No personality. 
Never asked if I needed anything. 
I had to ask for the check. 
Left a bad tip... and  I never do that.... but I had to. 
Get rid of that guy. 
Oh and the live music was great. Would have stayed and drank more.... but didn't want to have to beg for more drinks. 
No thanks.

This was my first visit to Gulfport and O'Maddy's Bar and Grill. My friend just moved to the area and was showing me around.

This spot is across the street from the waterfront. They have indoor and outdoor seating. Part of the outdoor seating has AC units overhead which was a nice touch.

I ordered one of the specials of the day which was lobster pizza. It looked so bright and colorful with plenty of lobster. If you see this on the specials menu don't hesitate......just order it! 

You could purchase a metal straw for $2. This was the only straw option available. It had the restaurants name on it so I purchased one as a souvenir. I could also use it in my thermal cup.

The service was average as it felt as though they were missing a server. He was friendly but seemed very preoccupied. 

I'm looking forward to visiting my friend again and stopping by for another lovely meal.

While visiting New Orleans my friend suggested our group of eight try Jimmy J's Cafe. I checked out the Yelp reviews and it looked like a good choice.

My friends and I were about a 7-10 minute walk from the restaurant so I called to see how long the wait would for a table for eight. The gentleman that answered the phone said it wouldn't be long. We arrived and the line was long. So long that we waited nearly two hours. I was not happy that I was lied to in order to get business. First fail.

No complaints with the food. The food was a five-star. I ordered the Cochin De Lait, slow braised pork with jalapenos, Creole coleslaw and pork jus. The shredded pork was juicy and plentiful. I have never eaten slaw on a sandwich but the Creole coleslaw was on point! 

I also shared the fried green tomatoes with a friend. This dish was not traditional but was still tasty.

The biggest issue came when we went to cash out. You could not split checks, which seems to be a common thing at most NOLA restaurants. After everyone put in the cash they owed we were short on the total payment of the check. After much deliberation (20 mins), and no help from the staff, one of my girlfriends put the total bill on her credit card and the bill lowered nearly $30. 

They were trying to charge us a fee for paying cash but without showing it on the receipt or explaining why we were short after adding up each person's total multiple times. Not cool and actually illegal. If you go with a large group DO NOT PAY CASH!

Psss-A-Grille Beach is at the southernmost point of St Pete. One of the reasons I love it so much is that it is not a heavy touristy beach.

There are two large restaurants across the street from the beach and they are both owned by Maryland natives. This is another attraction for me as I can order true Maryland crab after a long day at the beach:) 

The beach itself has many seashells so I would recommend water shoes so you don't hurt your feet. Parking can be tricky but paid parking is available. 

Paradise Grill is another plus here. It is right on the beach and has many food and drink choices including beer and wine. And they accept credit cards and have a public restroom.

Check out my pics and let me know if you agree that Pass-A-Grille has the most amazing sunsets!

I stopped in to Ricky T's for breakfast while visiting Treasure Island. I sat at the bar and had a few spicy Bloody Mary's which I highly recommend!

Our bartender was busy but attentive as it was a Saturday morning. I ordered an omelet that included home fries. The bartender talked them up so I wanted to try them. The food took around 20 minutes to arrive but the wait was worth it!

The omelette was delicious! I built my own with bacon, tomatoes, onions and cheese. They were generous with the toppings! And the home fries...well the bartender was right! You must try them! Seasoned to perfection with a little sea salt. Yummy!

I would absolutely recommend Ricky T's for breakfast! Great food with a lovely atmosphere!

I took a ride on the Paddlewheeler Creole Queen while attending the 2019 Essence Festival with my girlfriends. It was a Friday night cruise the day after 4th of July.

It was a white party with a splash of red. Entertainment was provided by DJ Biz Markie who did a fabulous job! He played the classics as well as current jams.

The ship had three levels. My friends and I were about halfway through the line for boarding. We had to go all the way to the top level to find some seating once onboard. 

They offered food to purchase which I did not as I ate a bite before I boarded. My biggest complaint was the bar lines. At one point I waited more than 20 minutes for a drink. A few more bartenders would have been helpful.

The ride was nice and smooth down the Mississippi. We turned around close to New Orleans downtown Skyline then headed back to Riverwalk. It was a great night!

I had the pleasure of eating at Felix's Restaurant & Oyster Bar twice while visiting New Orleans. Two of my friends kept talking about wanting oysters. Oysters have always been my least favorite seafood until I walked through Felix's door. I hopped on the Yelp app and found this gem on Bourbon Street.

Felix's has been in business for more than 70 years. Their oysters are locally harvested off the Louisiana coast. They are bagged and tagged straight from the boat, placed in the back of a refrigerated truck and delivered to Felix's. It doesn't get fresher than that!

My first visit I ordered the blackened gator bites with a garden salad. My gator bites were delicious and my salad was fresh. I tried my friends char-grilled oysters and fell in love!

Our last night in town we brought the rest of our friends back to Felix's. This time we sat upstairs and were able to go out on the balcony overlooking Bourbon Street. What a charming old building with so much character! 

I ordered the char-grilled oysters with a caesar salad. This was honestly the first time in my life that I've ever ordered oysters. The oysters were cleaned properly as there was no grit or sandy feeling in my mouth. The butter sauce and parmesan cheese were so deliciously blended to make a perfect oyster dish! I prefer the Caesar over the garden salad, although the garden salad was good too. The croutons were super fresh and not overly crunchy like most places.

I will probably not be ordering oysters anytime soon as I fear there is no other place on earth that can make them like Felix's.

I found the Faubourg Bistro on Yelp. My friends and I went here for lunch on a Sunday afternoon. Don't be confused as the bistro is located inside the 700 Club bar. Walk in the back place your order at the window get a number and you will be served at the table or bar.

My friends and I all enjoyed our lunch. I ordered the roast beef and cheddar with onion rings and share the brussel sprouts with bacon with my friend. 

My roast beef sandwich was absolutely incredible! There were huge chunks of juicy roast beef seasoned to perfection. The addition of the fried onions and cheese sauce topped off the sandwich just right. The pretzel bun was a nice touch and it was soft. The onion rings were crispy and lightly breaded just how I like them. There was even pepper in the batter which I've hardly ever seen.

The service at the Bistro and the bar were great. We waited less than 10 minutes for our meal. When in New Orleans this is I must stop for lunch!

My niece and I ate at Shells Seafood while vacationing last month in St Petersburg. Her birthday was the next day so we were celebrating early.

We both ordered the Crab n Shrimp Trio. This was a half pound of snow crab, half pound of dungeness crab and a half pound of peel and eat shrimp served with a side of coleslaw, red potatoes and hushpuppies.

The crab was served hot, tender and juicy and came out of the shell with little effort.  The shrimp was fresh. The sides were tasty too. We both enjoyed are meals. 

Our server was friendly and checked on us regularly. It was a Sunday evening so it wasn't too crowded which was nice. We sat outside on the patio and enjoyed our meals.

I would recommend Shells if you're looking for a good seafood meal at a reasonable price.

I stayed a few nights right next door to TuttoRosso Pizzeria. I ate here my first two nights in town for dinner.

The first night I sat outside on the patio and had a banana pepper pizza with garlic knots and Alfredo sauce for dipping. The pizza was incredible! I loved the flavor of the sauce and the amount of cheese and toppings were perfect! 

Now on to the garlic knots. First I have to say I typically do not eat bread with dinner. However, once I took my first bite I was hooked. The garlic knots with the herb flavor were to die for! But I would prefer to dip in marinara as I am not a huge alfredo fan. But I will say their alfredo was not bad, meaning it was not overly rich in flavor. 

My second dinner me and my guests at inside. I ordered the meat lasagna. There was so much cheesy goodness layered in this meat sauce. The flavors were exploding in my mouth like popcorn in the microwave! All of the guests with me enjoy their meals as well.

I also sipped their house red wine which was pretty mellow and tasty. I would absolutely recommend this pizzeria! In fact I will be sure to stop through here on my next trip to St Pete.

Okay, so this is a preliminary review. If you think this might be a place you'll want to frequent for years to come, DON'T GO HERE FOR ANOTHER FEW MONTHS. 

I can't even get in to the food because I sincerely am not sure if it was good. There are a lot of new restaurant kinks to be worked out here- it took 52 minutes to get our order of 3 burgers & a pulled pork mac and cheese. Two managers (Jeff & Amber, both very nice) came to help out after one "medium" burger was bloody & sent back. The two other medium burgers were okay. 

They took 20% off our checks and comped the bloody burger. 

A lot of miscommunication amongst staff, but I'm going to wait it out to return for one more try, maybe in October? 

There is a lot of potential in this place, I hope it works out.

Do yourself a favor and come here.

We came for Happy Hour and had the best Old Fashion cocktail for $6. YEOWZA. Quality cocktail, made with class, sass and a little badassness.
We also had a mule and it was tasty! 

For food, we dug in to the Fremont Burger, which was to die for. The beef was perfect and flavorful, all of the layers were complimentary and my taste buds were singing praises. The homemade ketchup that came with the fries was amazingly delightful. The freshness of the product at PSB stands out during the experience. 

The environment is cool, very chill and offers games and lounge areas in an upscale, hip manner. 

I see this establishment becoming a regular rotation in our repertoire. 

Highly recommend.

Dive my ass. (although they do have a bucket of rolling rock for $10 as an all day special).  

It was about 10:30 and an event I attended at the Continental was winding down. I knew the Phillies had been losing to the Cubs all night, but I got no signal inside the Diner (arrrgh! no updates!) and it was getting late, so I walked outside only to get a signal just in time for  Chase Utley's game-tying 2 run double in the top of the 8th! I admit it-- I panicked-- what to do? where to go? Must see Phils! Now! Desperately casting my eyes about the intersection of 2nd and Market, I started to drift south when what to my immediate relief should appear? A vision of Phillies through the picture-window front of (Saintly) Nick's! I raced across the street and dashed inside, and was greeted with looks of understanding and an ice cold lager, i hardly even had to form the words before it was open and in my hand and the bartender was backing away to leave me to the game. Things I noticed before I left:
               *a giant and pretty aquarium running the length of the bar. Niiiiiiice. I can sit and drink and stare at fire, oceans, and aquariums all day long. I think they could get more interesting fish, though. 
               *above noted bucket o' rolling rock special, amongst lots of others my otherwise occupied brain can no longer recall.
               *clean bathrooms with locking doors, toilet paper, soap AND paper towels! 
               *friendly bartenders and patrons, most of whom also seemed to be Phils fans.

So, I'm no regular, and as I said, I only made it to Nick's once so far, and for only 2 innings of a Phillies game. But they were a crucial 2 innings and Nick's was there for me when I needed it the most.

This is a phenomenal little place with a great sign-- the only reason I stopped in, actually (considering Veracruzana and Los?/Tres? Jalapenos are only blocks away). They also have a cart, but I haven't figured out where they park it yet. It appears to be family run, but I'll learn more, seeing as how I plan to become a regular.

I gotta be honest. I am a spicy food wimp. BUT I loooove fajitas (sans beans) and tacos of all kinds (except fish). I want to give the place 5 stars, but considering my wimpiness,  I'm not gonna eat enough from the menu to really feel like I can do that. At any rate, in my humble opinion the food here out of this world delicious. And unbelievably cheap. The people are nice, and though small, the storefront is bright and clean.

I'm thrilled to have chanced upon this incredibly, wonderfully, authentic (in thsi gringa's eyes, anyway) Mexican food. I plan on doing my part to ensure that they stay in business, and I hope that you will, too ;)

I give this restaurant 5 stars for their ambience and service. The restaurant is pretty, full of windows, open while remaining intimate, and comfortable;  the service is absolutely impeccable-- someone else mentioned being treated like royalty and i must agree wholeheartedly and offer up my personal proof that even with gaps of months between visits, these waiters remember me (and my drinking habits) and manage to mock me politely and quite hysterically the entire time I am there (and occasionally, according to friends, even when I am not).

I give this restaurant 1 star because the food is always pretty when served but doesn't always taste so great . (for example, I found their chicken-- in several different incarnations-- to have been pretty dry most times). I admit to knowing someone who was a mere four numbers away from having ordered and eaten every single food-item on the menu when they re-did it and he had to start all over again (at the time of re-menu-ing, there were something like 69 or 75 foods and 88 or 90 numbers?). Although it seemed  a challenge to do, the challenge of picking which was the first one he'd order again when done the circuit  turned out to be bigger, (which also says a lot about the food to me, too). I treat it like tapas now and stick to combinations of appetizers when i must...

I give this restaurant 5 stars for the quality of their drinks but 3 stars for the prices-- for an average of 4 stars. They have awesomely huge mug specials that my friends all love, like the Flaming Volcano, Angry Bachelor, Drunken Maiden, etc. (I don't even remember if those are the right names but the mugs are cool) but for me, what makes Vietnam Cafe stand out is that they offer the consistently best Amaretto Sours I have ever had in my life and keep my hand filled the entire time I am there. (I love a good, crisp amaretto sour more than anything in the world). If they ever sink so low as to have Phillies games on at the bar, I might just rent a stool. 

so, in the end I find that 10 total stars divided by 3 aspects is actually 3 1/3 stars for the whole experience. I want to give them more, but I feel like it would only deserve more if it were a bar, which it's not, so... since it IS a restaurant and I have yet to find a go-to, consistenty good meal to order there, the vietnam cafe is stuck with a hard-earned 3 from me.

So, it's around 6:00 on a Saturday evening, I'm leaving Finn McCool's for the subway and a visit to my oldest younger brother's new house in south philly as the cap for what has been an absolutely fantastically fun, beer and rain-soaked day with another of my brothers, and what do I see? no, not shorter sentences-- a sandwich board advertising a live band in Fergie's! Oh, who would have thought this day could get any better? Needless, to say we dipped in and it did! I saw the sign above the door as we sat down and remembered that Bebe's had moved here, too! Talk about Joy of joys and instant hunger pangs!

I ordered the mac and cheese, bro ordered a pulled pork sandwich and side of fries. Regretfully, at this point in our day my belly was so full of beer that I couldn't handle the unbelievably creamy cheesiness of the traditional, though absolutely phenomenal, mac and cheese so my brother ended up eating it. Fortunately, I got to devour his fries instead (my second favorite appetizer/side after mac and cheese) and they ranked right up there with the best of them. In fact, i might have to go back tomorrow night and see if they were as thickly handcut, salty and crunchy and filled with explosive potatoey lava as i remember... Service was friendly and very prompt and, beng so early on a Saturday night, the bar was not quite full. Food came out extremely quickly, and not just for us, either.

Ultimately, Fergies is Fergies-- great beers, good food, good times had by all. Fergies with Bebe's BBQ? great beers, outstanding food, better times had by all. Fergies with Bebe's BBQ *and* a cool bunch of people gathered around a big table drinking beers and playing irish music with pennywhistles, fiddles, mandolins, and even a concertina-- incredibly awesome ...

p.s. in fact, it's probably only that the band lacked a bodhran that kept me from giving them that elusive 5th star...

I've visited this Philly icon a handful of times over the years.  This time around, I broke the most essential cardinal rule:  'Come hungry.'  Indeed.  You see, a couple hours before, I'd stopped with hubby and kid at John's Roast Pork.  A meal I'd ultimately regret, but that's for another review.  Point is, I was still so f***ing full, the mere sight of all the food here made me feel a wee bit queasy.  I tried to power through, though. I really did:

Miller's Twist:  I've eaten Pretzels from an Amish Market before, but not this particular one.  Happily, the classic Pretzel we chose did not disappoint. I have a secret (well, maybe not so much now) thing for Auntie Ann's Pretzels and this was an elevated, buttery, soft, warm version of that.  Even in my semi-nauseous state, that was clear.  We'd ordered some cheese sauce for dipping and both hubby and kid declared, "This tastes just like butter and not in a good way!" I'll concede they were right.  It was more fatty tasting than cheesy. I'd go with Mustard next time.

Smucker's Grill:  Since I knew from previous disappointment that the Amish stands tend to close earlier than many of the others here, I'd made a point of looking up the hours.  According to the official Reading Terminal site, on Thursdays, this stand closes at 5pm.  So imagine my chagrin when we were told at 4:30 ish that they were no longer serving.  After explaining that the stated hours indicated otherwise, they were very accommodating about whipping up a Pot Roast Sandwich for us.  I asked them to add horseradish cheese, sauteed onion, and horseradish.  We wound up eating this after our two hour drive back home to Brooklyn and were shocked at how delicious it was!  I can only imagine how good this is freshly made and warm.  

This was all we could um... stomach on this visit...  But fwiw, have tried the famed donuts from Beiler's and while they're fun to experience once, I'd say there are way better ways to spend your dessert calories in Philly.  DiNic's on the other hand...  That Roast Pork Sandwich is worth everything.

Random Thoughts:  At 3pm, this place was bordering on annoyingly crowded, but by 4pm, it was downright pleasant.  This also happens to be when three hour street parking kicks in v. one hour. We were able to find a spot on N. 12th. Street, right near the entrance.   I believe there are also a couple nearby lots, including at the Hilton Garden Hotel, that with a validated minimum purchase, only charge a few bucks for two hours.

Bottom line:  If you don't like this Market, which is the soul of Philly in so many ways, then you're just not doing it right.  Go at a less crowded off time.  And since all the various options can feel overwhelming, read through some reviews to help narrow down your picks.  In this particular case, at least, Yelp is your friend.:)

Hungry for pizza looked up yelp reviews and ordered a Monster specialty pizza here. You can order a 12" or 16"
The 12" would feed 2-3.

They have a list of specialty pizza and we ordered the monster : onions, sausage, and peppers. The crust was chewy, hot, and pizza cooked perfectly.

Overall a great pizza, would definitely order here regularly if I was local. Wood fired pizzas are the best and this restaurant did not disappoint.

On the Sunday night after the blizzard in January my wife, daughter and myself braved the cold and snow and finally made it to Bar Bombon. We were greeted right away and given a table in the small and pleasant dining room. It was also at this point we learned that Bar Bombon is an entirely Vegan restaurant. Whaaaaaaaat?

Our server saw the confusion on our faces and assured us we would like the food.  It was all good, we just didn't know and went into our meal with open minds and empty stomachs.

We started with a Mojito and this was very good. It probably would have been better on a warm day but it still was as good as any we have had in Miami. Our server said all of the drink recipes were created in house.

For appetizers we had the Yucca fries. These were fantastic, crunchy and not oily and the soy-based cream sauce was excellent. We also shared the Rellenos and the Empanadas. The Rellenos both looked and tasted great. The portion size was large for a starter. I think one would be hard pressed to tell the difference between meat and vegan Empanadas here. The crust was light and not oily. The last small plate we had was the Arepas. I really like this dish and the corn bread/patty was very tasty and light. The Chorizo substitute they used was pretty darn good.

We also had the carne Tacos. These are marinated 'beef' ropa vieja, plantains, cilantro, and fresh lime. This also was a decent size with 2 tacos and I thought better then the tacos at Buena Onda.

For soups we chose the Tortilla soup and the Arroz con Poilo soup. Both soups were again large portions and could easily be shared with 2 people. The flavors for the soups were great and if not for the consistency of the "meats" I would not have known they were vegan.

For dessert we went with the Bar Bombon version of Tres Leches. Again this was different then our favorite at Tierra Columbiana or Mixto, but still really good. The cake was dense and the coconut milk gave it the right amount of sweetness. We also shared a Mexican hot chocolate with just a hint of Cayenne Pepper to cut the sweetness.

Our service was 5 stars at the Bar Bombon. The restaurant is simple, smallish and charming. The bathrooms are very nice and a cleaver use of space. For 3 people with one cocktail, one dessert, coffee and hot chocolate our bill was around $75.00 or $25.00 a piece. Not bad considering we ordered a lot of food and the also the high quality of the food.  4.5 yelps.

We were very pleasantly surprised with our first visit to Pho Vorhees. The space is large and modern with high ceilings. It also has a more modern vibe going then most of the other Pho places we have visited.

We ordered two staples we usually order at Vietnamese restaurants. The Pho with beef brisket and vermicelli noodles with spring rolls. The pho here was really good and the broth was well developed. The brisket was also well seasoned and tasty. The vermicelli noodles were also very good and the ingredients, such as the chicken and shrimp, seemed a little higher quality then some of the other local Pho shops.

Very happy to have this new addition and option locally. We look forward to returning and trying out some more of the menu. This was a really great first visit.

4.5 Yelp stars

I had always wanted to try Kensington Quarters as we love Bufad, which is owned by the same group. My daughter and myself headed over to KQ on a beautiful Sunday night in late July. It took a few trips around the block and some feeble attempts at an awkward angled space before finally finding a decent parking spot just a couple of blocks away on Frankford.

We didn't have a reservation, but that was not a problem as KQ had plenty of room on the nice outdoor patio. It was a really nice night as I wrote before, so we were glad to be outside. My daughter described KQ as a combination of Butcher Bar and Wm. Mulherin's Sons, which was very accurate. The restaurant is fairly large but not overly huge. 

We arrived at 6:00 and KQ has happy hour  from 5:00-7:00 on Sunday's. That was outstanding and we ordered the Mixed Charcuterie, KQ Burger (raw cheddar, garlic chili aioli, house brioche) and a beer off of that HH menu. The Mixed Charcuterie was only $5.00 and had lamb sausage! This was excellent. We also ordered the Dry Aged Pork Chop off the main menu and this was crazy good. It has this smoked and grilled taste and was super tender. My daughter and I savored every bite. For dessert we ordered the Buttermilk Custard Cake with hazelnut dacquoise, cherry compote, and fudge. This was so good and not overly sweet.

Our server was excellent the whole night and gave us some excellent recommendations and suggestions. We really liked KQ and if one has the desire for a meat forward meal, this is the place to go!

5 Yelp Stars!

I had been wanting to try Rayaki since their opening and finally made it over last Friday. I can't believe it took me this long as I live and work so close by. There are not really any true Ramen restaurants among the multitude of Asian restaurants in my native South Jersey, so I was very happy when they opened. (Whole Foods in Ellisburg has a Ramen counter and Zushi Dozo also serves Ramen). 

The inside of Rayaki is pretty cool and one can easily forget that they are in a strip mall. The anime and artwork add to Rayaki's hip vibe. The bathrooms have bidets and although I am not sure how I feel about that, they were very clean anyway.

We ordered the spicy Edamame and this was really good and came out hot. It was so good we kept burning our fingers opening the pods. I chose the Spicy Miso Ramen with Miced pork, seasoned egg, bean sprout, bamboo, scallions, mayu oil, miso soup base (pork soup base). I thought this was delicious but it brought the heat and plenty of it. My daughter ordered the Black Garlic Ramen with Cha Shu (Marinated Pork), bamboo, kikurage mushrooms, red ginger, fish cake, scallions, black garlic oil, pork soup base, seasoned egg. I would definitely order this again.

The prices for a bowl of Ramen are about $10.00 more or less. There are some other cool things on menu I would like to try. 3.5-4 Yelp stars and a nice addition to Route 70.

P.S. The bubble milk tea really helped to cool some of the fire from the spices.

I am usually not a fan of restaurant week. I really would prefer to order what I would like and not what the three or four items the chef has created for restaurant week. I was pleasantly surprised with Jamonera's restaurant week menu and even better, they also offered their regular menu.

This was the first night of restaurant week 2017 and also the first time we have visited Jamonera. I had heard a lot about Jamonera and we were excited to try it. We arrived 30 minutes early for our reservation and were given a choice of waiting about 15 minutes or sitting outside. It was a beautiful evening so that was an easy choice. My party of three was hungry anyway so the sooner some food arrived all the better.

Two of us chose the restaurant week menu including myself. I thought this was a very good value at $35.00 per head. The first 3-shared dishes were all excellent, the charred eggplant puree had this grilled garlic bread that was outstanding. I had the Gambas al Ajillo for my main course or second course. The shrimp were sweet and juicy and full of garlic. I never had a whipped salt cod but that was very good with the shrimp, chili and pimento. My daughter had the Bronzino and my wife ordered the lamb chops off the main menu. We shared all or dishes and everything was packed with flavors fantastic. All of our plates were wiped cleaned.

For the dessert course of the menu we had the flourless chocolate cake and the brown butter bread pudding. Both of these desserts were pretty darn incredible and not too sweet or heavy.

We had a truly great meal at Jamonera and we are looking forward to going back soon.

5 Yelp stars

We were very surprised by our lunch at Pinto Thong. The restaurant is in an older and nondescript strip mall. It doesn't look like much from the outside. However, upon entering Pinto Thong it is a pleasant, attractive, clean and simple space with seating for about 30 patrons.

Pinto Thong had a good selection of lunch special menu items that all came with either a salad or the soup of the day. My lunch partner and myself both chose the soup of the day. I don't know what it was called but it was outstanding. I ordered the Pad Thai with chicken which is my measuring stick for Thai restaurants. Pinto Thong's version was not the best Pad Thai I have ever tried but it was still very good. We also shared the Thai fried rice with chicken. We both thought the flavors at Pinto Thing were more refined then our usual go to Thai places. We finished off our lunch with the fried banana and ice cream dessert.

Our server was very pleasant and attentive. We really liked Pinto Thong and will return again soon. It is really a great little family owned restaurant in an area so full of chain and franchise eateries.

4.5 Yelp stars

I have had Apricot Stone bookmarked since they opened six months ago. We tried to get over there a couple of times but we never quite made it. Recent reviews by Yelp friends Sari A, and Nando F. made me finally get the wheels in motion.

We went to Apricot Stone on a hot, humid and intermittent rainy Sunday. I was able to find parking about 2 blocks away and it is always a good omen when I nail the parallel parking in a tight spot on one shot. Usually that takes several attempts and can be embarrassing. The restaurant itself is smaller then I imagined. There is at most seating for twenty inside. There is outdoor seating available also but not on this day because of the rain. The interior is simple, bright and clean and has framed photographs on the wall.

This review is only for brunch as that is all Apricot Stone offers on Sunday. The brunch is $20.00 prix fixed and includes 5 courses and also included coffee and orange juice. The food we had was excellent, it all was extremely fresh and made to order. Basically the five courses included a warm dish, a bread, an egg dish, a green or salad and dessert. I chose the Mamounia, which was similar to a sweet oatmeal but 1000 times more delicious. Then came Zakhatr bread and Falafel salad. Both of these dishes were a good size and had excellent flavors. My egg dish was Khachapuri a dish of homemade dough, cheeses and egg. This was also really, really good and I would reorder again and again. For dessert they gave us an excellent Baklava, a macaroon and another pastry. These were all pretty special.

Service was very attentive and we felt relaxed. On this day there was only one server, but he did a great job and did his best taking care of off of Apricot Stone's customers. Apricot Stone is BYOB and there were some tables having Mimosas and such. We did not partake in alcohol and I was very glad as I could barely move after so much food. If I had a few mimosas, I would need to find a bench nearby to take a quick nap. As it was, we walked around Northern Libs a bit before we felt we were ready to get back in the car

Apricot Stone lived up to the hype and I will be back soon to try the dinner menu.
5 Yelp stars!

We really did not know about Organico Pizza until we received a coupon and decided to give it a try. Organico is located just off of Route 70  in a little strip mall right before Main Street. The interior is bright and clean. The staff was super friendly and helpful.

We had a couple slices of pizza, a hamburger and the soup of the day. We shared these three dishes and everything tasted  fresh and homemade with care. The soup of the day was excellent.

COVID restrictions were good and we felt comfortable dining in. Will definitely return soon. Wishing Organico well in these difficult times.

Not much to add about the Reading Terminal Market with over 3,000 Yelp reviews but it still is a must stop for anyone visiting Philadelphia. My father used to bring my brother and myself there when we were kids in the late 60's and early 70's. I remember all the butchers and only a few restaurants and saw dust on the floors.  He would treat us to Bassets ice cream. We used to always get our turkeys from Moyers and once borrowed their large Phillies banner to take to Shea stadium when the Phillies played the Mets (my Uncle lived in Queens). The building's history can be felt when walking around.

The Reading Terminal Market has evolved and now has a lot more eating establishments. Yes it is touristy, but it still remains a really cool place. It does get crowded but that is part of the charm. There is something to eat for everyone and deciding what to choose or finding seating might be difficult, but the experience and diversity of food is worth it. Tommy DeNic's and Beiler's Bakery are probably the most popular and naturally the most crowded. There are so many other establishments worth trying and the market is something that is uniquely Philadelphia. I just wish I could go back in time and be there again with my parents.

Things happen.  In this case, there was a baby cockroach in my food. 

I had planned to enjoy at least a plate or two at the buffet, but at this point, my appetite was gone, much like the life from the baby cockroach lying on my shrimp. Both my stomach and the poor bug had wanted so much more, but were tragically cut short in their prime.

So... the restaurant had a hiccup, but it's how you bounce back, right? Let's see how that went. 

I quietly called the server over (as not to upset other diners), and discreetly showed her the bug. I told her, "I'm sorry, but I'm just not hungry anymore," to which she replied "Oh... [sigh] OK." 

I took this as a sign that the bill would be comped, but it turns out, she was just indicating that I'd be permitted to not finish the plate and get charged for leftovers per policy. Um, thanks?

Long story short, she gave me the bill, and both she and the manager said they couldn't do anything to discount the check (like even take off the soda or something?) Management, in a rather hostile manner, refused to let me leave without paying full price. No comps, no apologies, just cash or credit.  

For a second, I was tempted to ask, within earshot of diners, "I'm confused. There's a bug in my food, and I still have to pay full price?" but I decided against that. Hence, my PSA instead. 

Way to bounce back, New China.

So, if you eat here, you:

CAN expect some extra protein in your food.
CANNOT expect them to care one bit.

I ordered a birthday cake last year, paid $80

This year I went in and tried to get a cake, they try to nickel and dime you for just asking to switch a color on one of their catalog of cakes... Seriously?? A color? Wanted to charge $3 per letter of name... Every little thing for a smaller cake. It was such a headache, I left. 

I really enjoyed our cake last year and have often grabbed desserts to go but I refuse to go back.

I understand running a business and making profit... But at some point it's just too much greed.

Today was my second foray through Winslow's.  My first experience left me less than pleased with the cold and distant sales associates.  I try to never assume the "race card" when I encounter these situations, but the clerk was downright rude and arrogant - only to me. And this was AFTER I made a purchase.  I had to ask for a bag to put my numerous items in!  Very chummy and gushy with the other patrons, I noted!

So today, I had something specific in mind that I wished to purchase, so I gave it the old college try.  NEVER AGAIN! Even though I had the most scrummy grilled cheese sandwich and a great salad - AND a bag of Billy Goat  Potato Chips (yay!) - I'll just have to find another place that can match the creamy goodness that is Winslow's grilled cheese creation. 

Along with my lunch, I purchased $60 bucks worth of goodies from the general store.  The clerk took one look at me and said he'd keep my bag in back while I waited for my to-go food.  (BTW I saw him give other diners/shoppers - of a different persuasion than I - their bags while they waited).

I can do without the deep south treatment Winslow!  I'll take my business elsewhere, thank you very much.

Horrible- Avoid if possible. 

We were drawn in for lunch by the beautiful ambience however things went way down hill from there.

There is a touch screen ordering system which is confusing and does not give you the option to customize anything (such as specifying no beans on a wrap).

Once we ordered we attempted to get water from the staff. Nobody is technically front of house staff. They are all in the open kitchen making food so you just have to stand there until someone comes up. I also told the woman that I would like no beans in my wrap which I was unable to specify on the screen. She was nice to me about it then proceeded to scream at one of the "cooks" (dont know what to refer to them as- they aren't actually cooking anything) about it, which was awkward as it's an open kitchen set up.

Our food came (a Mexican chicken wrap and salad) after about a ten minute wait and wow. It was horrible. Everything was ice cold, including the chicken in the wrap, and absolutely flavorless. We could have had a way better meal at a hospital cafeteria. The salad came out with no dressing, despite ordering it, so we had to get up and ask for it. Still tasted bad even with the dressing. The chicken strips tasted like they had been pulled out of a pre cooked grocery store bag. We asked for salt to try to make it taste better but it was still practically inedible. 

We expressed our disappointment to one of the employees on our way out but he just stared at us and didn't say anything. 

Overall, the ambience is nice, however the concept doesn't work at all. They need front of house staff, an area with forks, drinks, etc which is accessible to the patrons (presently you have to request from the cooks anything you need like napkins or cups), and more edible food.

I'm sure this place will not stay around long but in the interim, I will not return or recommend.

Took the bf here for his birthday and they had rose petals and a birthday card waiting for him at our table! 

MAPLE-GLAZED CALIFORNIA DUCK BREAST & CONFIT OF THIGH (MEDIUM) (28)
succotash of sweet corn, fava beans, leeks, applewood-smoked bacon and Windrose Farms butternut squash, port-thyme demi-glace
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bouchon-santa-barbara?select=3Gc5NdGoLzNL-onJNYi43g 
Super tender. But my favorite part of the entire dish was the butternut squash mash. So sweet and delicious. 

GRILLED VENISON MEDALLIONS (RARE TO MEDIUM RARE) (30)
white bean purée, braised black kale, crispy pancetta, sherry-shallot jus
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bouchon-santa-barbara?select=w7FWudh-io3lNjmS1NNOEQ
Boyfriend really enjoyed the venison and the kale was tasty. 


BLUEBERRY-LEMON UPSIDE-DOWN CAKE (11) 
McConnell's blueberries & cream ice cream, crème anglaise and berry coulis
Their most popular dessert! Personally, I didn't care for the cake because I found it to be a bit dry. As for McConnell's ice cream, my boyfriend loved it! You got yourself another fan McConnell's! We were debating on going to McConnell's 5 minutes away, but we were so stuffed from everything. 

Bouchon is beautiful, the service is great, and the food is delicious. It's a restaurant that serves high-quality food that has generous portions compared to most high-end restaurants and won't break the bank.

The Rim Cafe is a cozy little hole in the wall on the southern edge of the Italian Market. I'm really glad that I'm in book club, or else I'd have never ventured into this place. Hell, I didn't even know it existed, and I only live four blocks away! 

When I stepped inside (after making sure that I was at the right spot), I was promptly welcomed not only by Rene, the eager-to-please, extremely amiable... owner? host? barista? chocolatier? all of the above?... but also by the warm (albeit fake) fire and my amazing fellow bookclubbers. Even though their space is small, the friendly owners were more than happy to accommodate a group of eight, and for that I am grateful. 

Now, onto the chocolate. The chocolate! I wish I had words poetic enough to describe the way I felt about that damn chocolate. I ordered the Dirty Volcano, which consisted of a heap of sipping chocolate (various different kinds, most of which were dark and, thankfully, not overwhelmingly sweet) with a dollop of creme fraiche in the center and myriad flavors of chocolate shaved on top. Truly heavenly. And if that wasn't enough to put me into a diabetic coma, I decided to also order a cannoli. Not only was it entirely delectable, but the presentation was adorable. There was even a brightly colored flower made out of different syrups. All in all, a thoroughly enjoyable experience, even with the incessant "You've Got a Friend in Me" playing from their television (that did, admittedly, drive me kind of nuts at the time). Rene, I hope you're ready for me, because I'm coming back to collect my free second round!

Horrible slow service, sat at our table for 20 min before being acknowledged... or should I say until I went to the bar and ordered my food and drinks myself and brought it back to my table myself.

Snobby stuck up, lazy college kids for staff. More interested in their facebook than working, which is ok I imagine mommy and daddy pay for everything anyway.

Wow ...set in the heart of Ybor what else could you ask for!  Great food, atmosphere and BEEEEEER! I was thankful for the great Yelp reviews and I am so happy I decided to go.  Lets start off with the Calamari...OMGAWD! Like totally the flavors were outstanding.  The mix of peppers and ginger tantalize your tongue. If I had a choice I would probably eat that calamari every day.  Now the beer.  I like wheat based beers so asked our lovely waitress to make a suggestion and I loved it!  I went there with quite the hungry bunch so we also ordered the bagguettes that came with honey butter.  That butter is addictive so only try at your own risk.

I was really wanting to eat a good burger so I ordered the Bison Burger.  It was good but not outstanding, it was bland and I asked for it medium and it was over cooked but still good enough to finish.  Throughout the evening our service was on point with constant check ins.  If your in the area I highly recommend you stop by.  I know once I return I plan to hit up that joint just for some out of this world calamari.  Whoop Whoop! Yeah!

I have been coming to Taqueria Feliz since it opened but I will no longer patronize this establishment. If you are Black you probably shouldn't either. 

My sister and I went in on a Sunday night to grab nachos and a drink at the bar. This was the first time my sister had been to the restaurant and just stopped by to visit me and grab a snack. 

Food and drinks aside, we were verbally and physically violated by a drunk patron. The bartender continued to serve this guy drinks while he continued to harass my sister and I. We are African-American and this man went on a racist rant about his "White Privilege" while the bartender and manager did ABSOLUTELY NOTHING to stop him. The other patrons also just watched, which is whatever. But after my sister and I asked for him to stop bothering us, he only became more disrespectful. We asked for the check and the bartender was either in shock or oblivious because he just stood there. He even gave the guy another beer. After aggressively asking for the check and telling the guy to get out of our face, we finally left. 

I came in later to make a complaint and all I got was a "we're really sorry that happened". I will never go back to Taqueria Feliz, which is unfortunate. However, I refuse to give my money to an establishment that condones this kind of behavior. Their response was repulsive and I am surprised because I would go there fairly often. However, to them I am just another tab. Once I find their other social media page I will continue to share this message. We can not allow this behavior to continue and it shouldn't be tolerated. I'd rather spend my money at a place where I am respected.

The owner stopped by our office and dropped off a menu so we decided to give this place a try for lunch. Delivery was fast and the pasta was delicious. I had the diavolo...just spicy enough, very fresh and perfectly al dente. This place is definitely my new lunch addiction!

I stopped by here after running a few errands to grab tabbouli salad and a kofta kabob sandwich to go. Both were delicious. The food here is very fresh and made to order. Also, the customer service is outstanding. The owner greeted me and offered me complimentary mint tea while I was waiting! Its great to find small business owners who place an emphasis on customer service. 5 starts for both customer service and the quality of the food! Hands down the best Middle Eastern food in Philadelphia.

So happy that our sever at Datz recommended we stop by here. The owner of Datz owns this place, too. It has been featured on the Travel Channel and the cashier told me they're known for their creme brûlée donut. I had it and it was amazing! Options were endless of baked good, too. Cashier was friendly and store was nice and clean.
Great service, location, food and drink menu, and bar. Wife ordered a veggie wrap with sweet potato fries and enjoyed them. I had a Caesar salad and it was good.

Great spot near he Gulf and great service. Food was average. Wife ordered huevos rancheros and she wasn't too excited as they came with nacho chips instead of the traditional corn tortilla. I enjoyed my egg white Mexican omelette but the toast was room temperature.

Came on a busy Saturday morning but my party of 2 was seated right away. Hostess and waitress were friendly. Waitress did great recommending items and really knew the menu well. She was quick, too. We started off with complimentary assorted sweet breads. They were good, my favorite was the cream cheese danish. Wife enjoyed her fresh nova lox on a pumpernickel bagel. I ate the eggs Benedict with home fries. Eggs Benedict came with Canadian bacon (ham). Muffins were toasted just right and the hollandaise was perfect. Home fries we're topped off with grilled onions which were the perfect touch.

Small place but great atmosphere. Hostess let us choose our seats and took our drink order for us. Waiter came by soon after and took our food order. Both were friendly and quick. We ordered the eggplant rollatini for an appetizer and it was hot and very good. Eggplant was fresh and well seasoned. It meshed well with the marinara and mozzarella. Wife ordered a spinach fettuccine pasta dish with veggies and she liked it. I loved my personal margherita with pepperoni. The pepperoni was mildly spicy but it was delicious. If you like a lot of cheese on your pizza make sure to specify that as the pizza here isn't loaded but I didn't mind. Highly recommend coming here for pizza.

Louie recently reopened for dine in and I jumped at the chance to finally having a dining experience here. 
The service was some of the best I've ever had at a restaurant! Everyone was so kind and courteous without being overly attentive. 

What we ordered: our server gave us a run down of the specials and we decided to start with the sweet potato ravioli. It was topped with a delightful smoked ricotta. Then we got the broccolini pizza which had a lovely lemon flavor that paired well with the other toppings. To end this wonderful experience we had the panna cotta which was drizzled with olive oil! The oil was surprising, but paired well!

Louie might be in the running for my new favorite restaurant!

I think we did it wrong. In a city with the highest concentration of Vietnamese folks in the US (according to the locals), we picked just an okay place to eat our one Viet meal. 

I'm a huge phonatic of Viet soups. I eat the stuff once a week at home in PDX. And this pho would not even make it in to monthly rotation. The broth is light and lacks any sort of depth of flavor. There's plenty of sodium though, as my puckered lips informed me. The pho here is in limited options, with flank, round and meatballs, but they do have chicken and vegan pho, and you can add on quail eggs, steamed veggies and more. Non-standard, but a nice touch. On the upside, the noodles have a nice resiliency and bounce to them. 

Staff is friendly but the seating policy consists of basically forming a line at the door. With no lobby, this is pretty tight and uncomfortable. How about a list, ladies? I felt bad being in the middle of everyone's way, trying not to get too close to the tables nearby as people squeezed past on the way in/out, but I wasn't the only one, and wasn't about to lose my spot in line. 

The ca phe sua da is not bad here. High octane, rich and tasty. So that's a plus. 

I guess we should have headed across the river to find the real stuff. This simply is not that legit.

I have no idea what the coffeehouse scene in Reno looks like, but if it looks anything like this, I'm impressed. While Coffee Bar may not have that interesting of a name, the offerings inside definitely deliver on creativity and quality. 

The coffee? It's pretty damn decent, and the baristas seem to know what they're doing. I enjoyed my Americano thoroughly. Aside from the quality of flavor, the service is friendly and on point. Even with a steady line, my drink was up with haste. 

The food? Yay! They have more than just the token coffeehouse pastry case. Of course they do have pastries but they offer hot food, sandwiches, and full on meals. I'm always appreciative of a coffee shop that goes beyond just a few sweets in the case. I didn't sample the food, but the stuff coming out to the folks around me looked tasty. 

The space is sort of a long, shotgun layout, but there are plenty of tables, bistros, nooks and crannies to plug yourself in to with your laptop and suck up the free wifi. Lots of power outlets.
