Even a solid community table. We planted ourselves and worked for a few hours here with no wifi or other issues. And the music? Decent. 

I dig this spot. I'll definitely return when I'm in town!

"What just happened?" 

"That just happened."

This was my internal conversation as my head reeled about, all the blood in my stomach digesting the monstrous sandwich I had just ingested. A foot-plus-long sandwich stuffed with many meats, melty cheese and sauce of some sort. All That Jazz, it's called. And Verti Mart is, I guess, legendary for it. My post-lunch pre-dinner meals will never be the same. 

During a week in NOLA I had been stalking this place on Yelp and via friend recommendations. Open 24-hours and offering delivery (including beer and smokes), this is seriously like a pipe-dream to me. If this existed in my town I'd be ordering shit just about every night. Especially with how good the sandwiches are. 

The Green Giant is like a philly minus the meat, but with all the cheesy, gooey goodness and piles of veggies. It's fantastic. The All That Jazz is scary good, and heart-wrenchingly huge. 

Why didn't I find this place earlier in my trip? Why did I follow the hype out to a just-okay po'boy at Parkway? Why am I such a tourist sometimes? 

Seriously though, these are not the most gourmet sandwiches you've ever had, but in the level just below culinary wizardry, these stand out as simply damn delicious, hot, melty subs/po'boys. Don't mess with anything else on this level. Come here and bask in the glow of a melty sando. 

Warning, there's no place to eat inside, and quarters are tight. Call ahead if you can. And be prepared to find a curb to sit on as you bliss out and devour your prize.

From my deep and extensive research on John Besh (basically watching one episode of Top Chef New Orleans), he seems like a nice guy. So I'll try to be delicate and say this the right way...

John, you need to spend less time in front of the camera and more time in your restaurant. 

Staying in the Hilton for a week netted me many opportunities to dine here. I experienced two brunches, a few happy hours and many just-before-closing cocktails. Each time was a different experience but the bad easily outweighed the good. 

Both of our breakfasts here were terribly disappointing. For breakfast one I sampled the "Eggs in a Jar" which, for $22, is not really that great. It consists of 5 shrimp stuffed into a jar with jalapeño cheese grits and eggs. Yup, eggs, shrimp, cheese and grits for $22. Oh, I forgot the jar. But you don't get to keep the jar. The dish was actually ordered by a table-mate and when it first came out, the eggs were not just undercooked, they were not cooked at all. My Korean friend who eats the snottiest eggs I've seen anyone eat had to send it back. My "Healthy Start", which was house-made granola and fruit on yogurt was sparse at best. The granola was sticky and chewy, not crunchy at all, and while the yogurt was delicious, it wasn't good enough to salvage my image of this $12 dish. I'll say this, the coffee was good. At $6 for a double espresso, it better be. Oh, and the beignets were proper, even though they sent out the wrong sauce with them. 

Our second breakfast here allowed me to sample one of the $14 biscuit sandwiches - the sausage, egg and cheese biscuit served with a cup of fruit. My North Carolina friends make better biscuits in Portland, and load them up with all sorts of meats, gravies, eggs and what-not for half the price. The biscuit here has decent flake and is fairly buttery, but it didn't stand up to the small sausage patty and cheese. One word comes to mind when I think about what I paid for this dish - ludicrous. One member of my table ordered the home fries and when they came with meat in them (no mention of meat on the menu), she sent them back and said "I actually am fine without these". Instead of just taking them off the bill, they sent back potatoes minus the meat. "But we don't want these" we said. "Oh you'll like them, trust me." she said as she walked off... and left them on the bill.  

Despite two food issues with each of our meals (not cheap meals mind you) no apologies, comps, or any other customer service was offered either time. How much balls does it take to not even verbally apologize for such an expensive dish sent out totally wrong? Especially since we're pretty nice in our response/request to have them re-done?

My bar experiences here were quite opposite to my meal experiences. Any time I could find a seat at the bar and order a drink, it was decent, and priced well. The whiskey list is short but there's some good stuff on there. The bartenders are friendly. The $.50 oysters and half-priced drinks at HHour are an insane deal. 

So it makes me wonder. Why go to lengths to offer such an amazing deal at HHour and good service at the bar, and then offer poor service and bad value for those wiling to sit down and spend more for a meal? Who knows. 

While I think this is a mighty fine hotel bar, as a restaurant it fails on value, on service, and frankly on quality of food. Had I been faced with half the prices, I might find this fare to be passable, but at the sky-high menu prices, I'd expect much, much more. 

I'm sure John Besh (if he ever reads these - probably not) doesn't expect his restaurant to be run this way. But c'mon. You send out completely see-through, uncooked eggs in a $22 egg dish and offer not even a verbal apology when the food is returned, let alone any other customer service on a $100 brunch for 4 people (no cocktails ordered)?! Yikes. 

We wouldn't have returned for an actual meal after the first visit for breakfast but had to grab grub on our last day on the way to the airport. Can't say I'd come back outside of happy hour. Maybe dinner is better? At least the bartenders are nice.

What elevates one location of a homogeneous fast food chain above any other? Sometimes it's the layout, sometimes it's the employees, sometimes it's the parking, and in rare cases, it's the food. Here, it's the lines, or lack thereof. I will say this in one separate line so it's clear:

I came here twice, and both times there was no line. 

This is like bizarro In-n-Out. Every other location I've ever been to, regardless of day or time, has a standing line. Often almost to the door. However here? Nope. I mean, it's not like the lines take forever. But still, just walking in and walking straight up to the counter is a unique experience for me. 

That aside, the burgers here are as fantastically delicious as those at other locations. And the fries are just as bad. Just get the burgers or grilled cheese and a drink and call it a day. I sampled both protein style w/ fresh onions as well as a regular double-double animal style (on two separate occasions... don't judge) and both were top notch. 

Another great location of a great chain.

Have you ever seen that show Drunk History? Well, it doesn't have really anything to do with Arnaud's French 75 except that this place is full of history, and one too many of their strong, craft cocktails may get you drunk. Maybe if you bring a historian with you to this classic spot you'll end up getting some drunk history. At the very least you'll enjoy some of the best cocktails in New Orleans in a classy (yet smoky) environment. 

I came here for drinks from Chris Hannah, who I met at Portland Cocktail Week. He surprised me in PDX, and I couldn't help but make a pilgrimage to his home bar when in town. Twice. Both times I enjoyed some fantastic versions of classic cocktails as well as some dealer's choice action. Everything from the classy old school decor, to the tasty drinks and white-glove service nails it for me. 

Protip - there's a room upstairs with a bunch of old Mardi Gras costumes - you should go check it out. Just ask.
Worst place to eat in vail. Service sucks food is horrible. Wait time is for ever I will never go back.

Ventured out for lunch today!  The Sasquatch is always a great place to go in Verdi. 

We ate outside and each of us had something different!

They're was a Blackberry and Mango Salad with a balsamic vinaigrette.  It was big and looked delicious.  There was a prime rib dip with sweet potato fries, also delicious. A huge serving of Fish and Chips that was also excellent!  And I had the Ribeye Steak Sandwich with Garlic Fries!  It was perfectly prepared and was delicious!

If you're hungry in Verdi make sure to stop here!

Huge Fan!   Happen on this place be accident and LOVE IT.    I am not a big fan of fast food burgers, but this place is awesome.

After a long hike and needing lunch I pulled into the drive up, and grabbed a chicken burger......   OH. what a burger it was, could not eat the whole thing in one sitting.  
Plus, the service was awesome.   I have a soft spot for people that love dogs, and after my hike with Luna I was also getting her a burger.  After ordering Luna's burger and me telling them it was for my dog, they let me know if I just wanted the meat they would only charge me 3.00.   :)     Ok, that right there won me over, a place that loves my doggie!!!!!    I'm a fan, plus the chicken burger for me was amazing!!!!!

I will be back, thank you Burger Me!!!!


~S

Updated to add that I now have the 2-Thumbs-Up from my 3 year old for Omoni as well. He's a pretty adventurous eater, so I try to introduce him to as many different things as I can. There's only so many cheeseburger joints a parent can stand, right, so why not bulgogi tacos? He LOVED them. Admittedly he may have had a *little* help on his 3rd from Mom and Dad, but he devoured the beef, the zucchini slices, carrots, daikon--anything mild works, though I've seen this kid pound down some mild-ish curries before-- and, voila! We have a new fan of Omoni. Yay!

Oh Charlie, whatever your sins may be, I am oh so smitten with you!

Beautiful space, posh, but not so posh that I feel out of place. In fact, I feel like even I become just a little bit swankier simply by walking in the door. Thanks, Charlie!

I'm not normally a lover of cocktails. Give me a Belgian beer or a cider & I'm thrilled, but I actually adore the signature cocktails at Charlie's. So far, I've experienced the Hasty Tasty, Les Fleurs du Mal, & the Bodhisattva. I loved all 3 of them & will definitely drink them again...after I try all the other cocktails on the menu!

Ahh, & the food. Small plates, super tasty, all vegan. My favorites include the Little Hot Dogs, the Chickpea Fries, & the Bucatini & Meatballs. And the desserts...love the chocolate cake, which is unlike any chocolate cake you have ever had & the apple fritters with chocolate sauce--SWOON!

Charlie, I am digging your sinful ways. Highly recommend.

My husband and I dined here for our 1 year wedding anniversary. I had made reservations a couple weeks beforehand, and had read that dining on the patio was the way to go. Good thing I did, because it was romantic, warm, intimate and there were only 2 tables with a 2 seater and then around 4 other tables that sit 4-5 diners. Make sure to book on the patio - so pretty!!!

We arrived early for our 715p reservation, and we were told it would be a couple mins until our table was cleaned and ready. This gave us an opportunity to take photos in front on the restaurant. The host came out and since we were celebrating our anniversary and that we were waiting, he offered us a couple glasses of bubbly while we wait. HOW AWESOME! Then he came back out to take our photo.

A few mins later we were seating in a cute table next to the exposed brick and pretty lighting. There were heat lamps so it was perfect. We brought our own bottle of wine and the corkage fee was $25 for weeknights and $35 for weekends and holiday. You are only allowed 1 bottle per 2 persons, so take note! We brought in a 9 year old J. Lohr Cab reserved, and the manager came over to open our bottle, brought over a decanter and came by with an anniversary card and rose petals for our table. How romantical!

We ordered the Goat Cheese and Pecan Tart as a starter. I was a little weary about this because I really wanted the Savory Foie Gras, and the hubby didn't care for it. I was pleasantly surprised that the tart was amazing. Very light and the warmness of the tart really made the flavors pop. A must as an appetizer if you're into smooth and creamy cheeses.

My husband went with shallot glazed rack of lamb (med rare) and I ordered the staple maple-glazed duck breast and confit of thigh (med). My husband lamb was delicious and meaty; however, my duck was to die for. The breast was so much better than the thigh and I'm more of a dark meat eater. The sauce and crispiness of the duck was so good, and the knife just simply sliced the meat tenderly. Super filling that I had to take half of the entree home.

For dessert, my husband ordered the blueberry lemon upside down cake and I ordered the warm Santa Barbara chocolate molten lava cake. My husband really enjoyed the cake as he is into fruity and tart desserts. My dessert on the other hand was awesome. If you're a chocolate fan, you MUST get this dessert. This is how a molten lava should be, just pure warm fudge coming out and all in the center. The crust was crisp and crunchy and definitely not overcooked. Coffee paired well with desserts, and my husband ordered a cup while I finished the rest of my Cab (red). 

The service was impeccable and we couldn't have had a better experience on our 1st year wedding anniversary. Such a special and memorable place. We will definitely come back on our next trip.

Very good pizza that is thick and the homemade pizza sauce on it makes it a very nice treat. We were up here and got some we are visiting some of my wife's relatives so we went to this nice local pizza joint. I liked all the sites on the inside they had cool monkey designs and statues in the breadsticks with cheese sauce is fantastic I must say. And their pizza we got a mini pizza and a cheese pizza and I eat the meat pizza and it was really good the flavors on it was terrific. So definitely will be back the next time we're in town

When we were in St. Louis my wife and I did the Budweiser tour. Anheuser Busch tour whatever it's called but we had a great time they had Clydesdale horses out there they had all the Anheuser Busch logos you got to sample beers at the end of the tour see how they were made is an excellent tour that we really had a great time with

This is one of my favorite barbecue establishments that I've ever had. Happy smokehouse is an excellent barbecue establishment in St. Louis. We got the ribs and pulled pork and split both of them and they were both excellent. We both really enjoyed our food and our time at the pappy smokehouse we will be back when we go to St. Louis

Well in Philadelphia of course you have to do the Philadelphia cheesesteak challenge. So looking up a lot of different places it seems like Pats and Gino's are the two most popular are the ones that they say to try or do. So we got Gino's first I was all over the place trying to figure out how to order cause you to order somewhere else and you want fries or drink it or somewhere else the people there and we're just OK I'm in there East Coast guys I guess they weren't really that friendly here they were probably tired of people not know how to order so that's cool anyway we got a meatball sub for my daughters and I and my wife split a cheesesteak with whiz cheese only. And you know it's OK it was pretty good but I'm gonna give it three stars because I like Pets better and we tried it next so if I had to compare the two I like Pats better I'll give it a four and I'll give Gino's at three but overall still a pretty good place but the bread was the number one thing I tasted so I would fill up pretty quickly on this

This is a fun and cool restaurant that my family and I visited while we were in Tampa. Tampa is a great city that offers many different neat places to eat and visit. We sat here and I got a big ol burger and sat outside and watched the gators in the pond next to me. It was a lot of fun

So while we were in Philadelphia we had to do the cheesesteak challenge between Pats and Gino's next door so I looked up some things it's a cash only place I had to go to ATM and pay a fee and do all that I hope my bank reimbursement but we'll see what happens anyway with the Pats second with genos Forest genos I am not giving a three I'm gonna get packs of four because I like the taste of it a little better and the guy that waited on me with a little nicer than the other ones but that's OK you know just got it so hot summer day reset the shade wife and I both agree that we like Pats better than Gino's so both were good sandwiches but overall I'm gonna give it to Pat

Very nice museum that is huge and offers so many great statues and public displays of art. I love everything about this place. It was very neat to see all the famous pieces of art. I would highly recommend this to anyone that loves art and appreciates things like this.

This is an excellent Mexican food establishments that we stopped in when we are in Greenwood Indiana visiting family. Always enjoy their chips and salsa good flavor the hot sauce is very tasty. Can't go wrong with free chips and salsa. It's a big burrito with cheese on it is where it's at and I usually my go to with ground beef on the middle and it is very tasty tasty

I love Nashville I love Margaritaville I love Jimmy Buffett I love music food beer all the fun stuff. So Nashville is filled with a lot of great places and a lot of fun this Margaritaville is definitely a great example of fun as well. My wife and I went in here and we had food and drinks and listen to music and had a great time while somebody was babysitting our daughters for the weekend so we had a great adult outing. Definitely check it out it's a great place

While we were in Philadelphia we visited a Lotta different sites and sayings. One of the cool things that I enjoyed seeing was the Italian market yeah and seeing all the little Italy signs and just everything I thought was really cool. I remember in Rocky where he was running down the Italian market and people were terraforming I got the room and orange that was all improvised and they kept it in the movie so I was kind of cool nobody through an orange at me while I was walking down so that's OK but overall it was a fun experience

The last time we were in Nashville my wife and I stopped in at the wild horse saloon. We had an excellent experience and adventure and a lot of fun was had for sure. It was a great experience we had some live music and drinks and dancing and had a Lotta good photo ops and this is a great place to check out

I really love Nashville I love Jason Aldean I love country music I love food I love beer all that's great. So when you combine it all together how can this not be a five out of five? Of course it is this is an excellent establishment my wife and I visited while we were in Asheville we partied it up on the rooftop and had a great time with drinks and music and just a lot of fun

When you walk in you instantly want to be here. It's a cool space. The line was long on day 1 at about 11:30. It moved quickly enough and was much longer at 11:45 and 12. I ordered the risotto balls and the bowl with rice, red pepper sauce, pork, garlic, and Peppadew. Everything was great. The risotto balls were crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside. The rice and pork were tender and well cooked. The red pepper sauce had a nice mild flavor. It says a lot that they were this prepared to handle such a large crowd on day 1. This is a nice addition to the downtown dining choices and I am a fan and will be back.

We were headed to the new pizza restaurant next door but decided on Layla since it is open. They have a small Happy Hour menu for M-F. We got the Spicy Hummus. It was delicious and very spicy. Bargain @ $3! For dinner I ordered the Shawarma. I chose the pomegranate lamb, traditional Lebanese pita, Greek style with fries on the side. It was good! The lamb was spiced right and all the sandwich components were fresh. The French fries are delicious. Nice and crisp with a lot of black pepper. I loved the tzatziki sauce as well. Creamy and just a hint of cucumber. This was a happy surprise because as I said we were headed next door. My dinner date loved The Royale with Cheese (burger). Friendly service and cute place. We'll be back!

Two observations: 1. Soda machine didn't have the proper CO2 cartridges. 2. Lose the house made ketchup and have Heinz on the table!

You know you're in a peculiar environment when there are folks walking around with oxygen tanks in one hand and a lit cigarette in another.  We saw three within our first five minutes.  We visited this fine establishment for Chickies and Petes.  The cigarette smoke in this casino is absolutely awful. There is no ventilation. We left and it was like the olden days, our clothes stunk and we were gagging from the smell of cigarette until we could change. If that's your thing and that doesn't bother you, then go here.  We went to the restaurant, then raced for the door. Not even one quarter in a machine because we couldn't breath.

The short:
Go here now! Best ramen in New Orleans. Hands down. Their broth really makes the meal.

Food:
Small menu but they do it all really well. You can't go wrong. They also have a few appetizer selections - try the dumplings. They're adventurous and pretty unique. They usually also have chicken wings. 

Service:
Great service but know that it's a small space. Probably about a dozen bar seats and one long table.
Food takes some time to make but that's fine

Tips:
BYOB - they don't sell alcohol so bring some beer. Goes great with ramen. 
Reservations - only for more than 6 people. 
Bathroom: one bathroom
Parking: street parking 
Chairs! Some of the bar chairs have names on them. They are people who contributed to the restaurant in some way!

Growing up in Philly it was widely acknowledged that Geno's was better than Pat's, though Pat's had the name recognition.  Nothing has changed through all those years.  Pat's may be the worst cheesesteak in all the city.

There are four types of people who prefer Pat's.

First, those who are loyal to a brand.  Maybe they were just brought on Pat's and they stuck with it.  This is not much different than the Coke v Pepsi situation.

Second, those who actually like Pat's steaks.  This is a small number of people I am sure, but they do exist.  Some people actually like Little Debbie's.  

Third, politically correct, leftist, haters who don't like the food, but go to Pat's just to tell their leftist, PC friends that they didn't eat at Geno's. 

Fourth, hostile illegal immigrants with a chip on their shoulder who think the world revolves around them.

Fifth, tourists who don't know any better.

Pat's cheesesteaks are tasteless, undersized and come on a plain, squishy roll that tastes like it was made by Wonder.  There is just nothing to recommend about it.

Maybe the worse thing is that Pat's is usually dirty.  Look across the street at Geno's.  It is spotless.  At Pat's you never know what you might catch.

On second thought, the worst part is that tourists come here expecting to get a real, top quality cheesesteak and end up with perhaps the worst possible example.  It is too bad Pat's doesn't have more pride in their product.

I like the food here, it's a little over-priced for what it is, but most breakfast places are. My problem is that they were super sneaky about the pre-added gratuity to the bill. I wrote this so ppl can be on the look out. We had 5 ppl in our party, 3 adults, 2 kids so I wasn't looking out for it. We got our bill and it seemed off to me. I had left $14 on the table while I went to pay the $70 bill. I kept telling the cashier the bill didn't seem right and nothing was market on the hand written ticket. I pulled out a menu and  the calculator for my phone and showed here where it didn't add up unless the tax was around 30%. She then told me about the gratuity. I don't mind gratuity, but I have never had a place go so far out of their way to cover it up. I went and got my $14 back. I loved this place but I don't like being played like that, so I will not be back. I had been there about 6 times and frequently took visiting family and friends there.

If you've ever been to Blaze Pizza, this is a similar concept. Get in line and choose a bunch of stuff to put on top of your pizza and then they cook it for you. Because the crust is pretty thin, it's fast so it's not like you're waiting for very long. Maybe 5-10 minutes. 

What I really like about this concept is that you have a say in how much stuff they put on. If you're a freak about pepperoni, they will keep piling it on until you cry for mercy! 

And here's the best part! They don't charge per topping. You choose the size crust and it's just one price if you want one topping or all of the toppings. I guess if you're not a toppings person you might not get all that excited about it, but if you like a lot of stuff on your pizza this will save you a small fortune!!!!

So, I got a grilled chicken pizza with garlic and the pesto sauce. They were a little light on the sauce but luckily I was there to coach them through putting on a bunch more. They were totally cool about it and in fact we had a good laugh (I told them I was from corporate and just testing them). 

I tend to like my pizza crispy so I asked them to see if they could crispify it and it ended up coming back a little burnt on the bottom. 

Otherwise, it was awesome!

European Republic has the honor of being one of the two yummiest things I tried while visiting Philly. Definitely one of the most satisfying comfort foods I've had in a very long time.

Though the reviews were amazing, I was really skeptical about these wraps because it looked so simple and unassuming. After my first bite of the fried chicken wrap the flavor sensors throughout my body began firing at every cylinder. OMFG!?! Was that really just a humble piece of fried chicken, a fancy tort and secret sauce? The best way to describe the flavor: KFC on the greatest day of KFC--like when the Colonel was still out back plucking and frying up the chicken! YUMMY! Don't forget to check in to get the special price!

I know, I know I gave them 5 stars! What was I thinking? Well....the service isnt spectacular, I have had an average 3 out of 4. Some times we get a very attentive, friendly and prompt waiter/waitress other times not so much. But, I will always come back, it simply isn't enough to keep us from eating here. The food is 5 stars for me! 

I had no clue this was a chain. I am not from the South and had no idea there were others around but it doesnt matter much to me, this place is great! 

It is obvioulsy more expensive than say "Whitt's" or another chain place, but it is obvious why when you eat the food. 

The cheddar biscuits are so delicious. The chicken is so tender it falls apart. I love the sauces, I love the veggies. My other half always gets the sausage and adores it. 

Everything is made with real butter - in the culinary world this is a very positive thing (note my spouse is a Chef). Apparently there is loads of butter in most prepared foods that we actually like, little fact I was unaware of until about a year ago. Yes hidden fat and calories, but yes that is why the food has flavor! 

This is not a place for you if you are watching your waistline unless of course you are on a protein diet, skip the sides and eat the meat! But it is delicious, it is very kid and family friendly and it is one of my Nashville/ West Nashville Faves! 

Oh and one more note, DO NOT turn left out of the street near this place! ;) there is apparently a sign posted, and the cops know we dont see it, and continually ticket overly-stuffed cheddar biscuit loving folks like us!

Its been a minute since I've had a favorite sushi place and I think I have found one! We stumbled across Sunflower Cafe on New Years day by chance. We weren't looking for sushi or anything of the sort but fate  insisted otherwise and I'm glad she did.

The fries oysters are crisp and delicate. The Tako Yaki is delicious but the sesame balls are second to none! Warm, toasty, slightly sweet balls of perfection. 

The sushi is fresh, made to order, very balanced flavor and executed consistently on each visit. I've tried about 9 different rolls so far and have not been disappointed by any. Of course there are rolls I prefer but that is a matter of preference, not a reflection of the quality. My top 3rolls so far are, the Tata Roll and the Hana Lulu Roll and Energy Roll!

I grew up eating at Wright's pretty frequently but Its been a while since I have been to here because  the last couple times were nothing to write home about. This visit was so much better! The sandwich was as even better than I remember! The service was quick and friendly, the restaurant is extremely clean, with team members constantly wiping surfaces and cleaning, while checking on and assisting customers.
So glad I stopped in!!!

The food wasn't spectacular, and I've definitely had better service and ambiance at "lower-end" restaurants. Can't say I'll be coming back... ever.

Ordering: My date and I arrived at the restaurant closer to 8:30 pm, where we were promptly seated in the corner by the entrance. Oddly enough, we had several servers: one to distribute the menu, one to pour drinks, and one final one to take our order. Each one was fast and methodical at their task, but they weren't very personable. We were served lukewarm water in a glass bottle to start, so I asked for ice for my warm water. Our server, gave us extra time to look over the menu, and finally came back after 15 minutes to take our orders. We ordered the following: antipasto (for two), penne with sausage (that was substituted with spaghetti), and grilled chicken breast. 

Eating: The antipasto came out first... without the bread. Our server feared that our food might get cold, so he served it without all of its components. I tasted the warm vegetables and it was alright, nothing special. There was a bit of smokiness from the grilling and roasting of some of the vegetables, but the strongest smell and taste came from the garlic paste on top the spinach and asparagus.  The missing bread came out next, lightly toasted and warm. I thought the bread tasted better than the vegetable plate. Next came the main courses. My grilled chicken breast dish consisted of a ribbon pasta with broccoli florets and strips of carrots that were generously dressed with olive oil. To the side were a bed of three grilled chicken breasts that were butterflied, and slices of grilled eggplants. The finishing touch was a striping pattern of balsamic sauce on top the eggplant and chicken. The vegetables were overdone and soft, almost like it was heated up from frozen, and the balsamic reduction was too syrupy and thick.

Leaving: Upon paying the bill, my date and I overhead a group of senior servers talking about their customers. A male server was saying how a female customer seemed unhappy with her date, and was surprised if she even smiled once that night. After I gathered all of my belongings, I used their restroom, only to be surprised by how unkept it was. There were strips of toilet paper littering the tile floor, and the trash bin was overflowing. The cherry on top was when my date told me a male employee used the bathroom and returned to work without washing his hands. 

Conclusion: This Italian fine-dining restaurant was a nightmare. The service was slow and their servers were awkward. I felt uncomfortable having to make so many requests that I felt were standard at other places. I think the restaurant needs to re-train their employees and re-evaluate their goals. Having to request ice for luke water in this 100 degree heat is a bit absurd. More importantly, as a paying customer and not a member of the establishment, overhearing employees making negative comments about their customers is infuriating. This should not be done at all in front of customers, or if it is unavoidable, should be done while being off-duty. However everything pales in comparison to what I thought was the most repulsive event that night. My date had told me that a restaurant employee returned to work without washing his hands. These series of events have led me to believe that it is more than just a bad day at the restaurant, but a habit that won't break any time soon. If I'm spending $70 on a meal for two in Tucson, I would expect the services and food to be more elevated than this. Thanks Vivace, now I know better than to come back to this establishment if I want to overpay for mediocre Italian food, and support questionable restaurant hygiene.

This place has great food and fantastic service.

I usually come in on a Tuesday or Thursday for their $0.50 wing deal. The wait for a table is never more than 5 minutes even when a game is playing, and food rarely takes more than 15 minutes to be served.

The only food I've tried are their traditional wings, and loaded steak fries appetizer. They never disappoint: full of flavour, and comes out pipin' hot! Their wing sections are normal sized (not mutantly large or scrawny), and always come with a side of dressing of your choice (ranch or blue cheese) and celery sticks at no additional cost. The wing sections are never overcooked or undercooked, and are good to the bone. Here is my attempt at describing the chicken wing flavours:
Hot: traditional buffalo style, hot and vinegary sauce
Honey BBQ: sweet and smokey sauce
Barbeque Hot: spicy incorporated BBQ sauce
Honey Hot: spicy and sweet sauce
Asian Garlic: garlicky and sweet sauce
Pineapple Teriyaki: traditional teriyaki sauce, sweet glaze
Asiago Parmesan Dusted: butter drenched, powdery cheese confection
Out of all of these flavours, my favourites are the Hot, Pineapple Teriyaki, and Asiago Parmesan Dusted.

Overall, this restaurant is a Tucson rare. I'd never thought I'd support a chain-restaurant, but this is an exception. This branch incorporates courteous service, great food, and cleanliness for an exceptional experience. My favourite one-stop wing-stop in Tucson!

Diamond in the rough!

So we drive past this building a million times trying to figure it out. And I'm doing a Groupon search it popped up. Boi am I glad it did! From fries to fish everything we had was seasoned well and prepared beautifully. 


The building is really weird looking because is says like pay your bills here and something else not typical of a restaurant on the side. It's really small so don't bring a party of more than 4 and expect to dine in. Don't let people calling sketchy be a deter you from visiting here, their jerks who only want to be in gentrified or tourist New Orleans. Come off the beaten path and get some good food!

Amazing spot for dinner and drinks!  Great atmosphere and delicious menu items. We had the guac & salsa and fried pickles - both tasty!

Hot chicken, chicken fried chicken, braised beef and the cobb salad were all great choices recommended by our server, Sarah. 

The bourbon sweet potatoes, brussels sprouts, and bacon mac n' cheese are a must!!

Fantastic service!
Decent joint. Wine & beer lists are pretty good. Food menu is ok. More seafood than most. Food and service is average and what to be expected.
Very nice! We happen to hit their anniversary and they had tapped at least a dozen different sours. Most were so good! Be sure to stop in when you're in downtown Tampa
Loved our meals! Huge portions and tasty food. The spice could be turned up a notch for me but the choices are many and the staff super friendly and helpful.
Very average lunch place. Portions are plenty. Food tastes so-so, nothing bad but nothing special. Price is moderate to high. Draft beer options were limited when I was there.

I had the pleasure of dining here last Thursday.  My wife surprised me with reservations and said she'd researched and this was an absolute must try. 

As I'd not researched, I had no idea what to expect. 

I'm privileged to have dined at many fine restaurants around the nation, especially Chicago. So privileged, I've become jaded and avoid the super high end to avoid the crowd of fussy waiters delivering plates of fussy food while hovering to make sure you ooh and ah over the precious and complicated morsels.

Catbird serves small plates of food, but in an environment and service that is not fussy or precious. The food thrives on the simplicity and quality of the ingredients. The potato is clearly a potato, same with a tomato. If anything, the restaurant is all about the preparation and delivery of each ingredient. 

Being able to chat with the sous chefs during prep and service, combined with the excellent food, made this the best dining experience I've ever enjoyed.

We've been here a couple of times now, and this was the original location that I went to for my first trip to a "The Pub". For those who don't know, this is a British pub, but more on the fancy side rather than a dive. Speaking with a server this time, we also learned that this is their test kitchen location, which was fun.

We were there at an early lunch time, and more or less had our pick of where to sit. University right away. The server was friendly, and chatted with us several times while we were there. The food came out super fresh, super fast, and was delicious. We split a Scotch egg, and each got an order of the fish and chips. They have a full bar, which we took advantage of.


Overall, it was a great experience, consistent with the experience we had last time.

Although the Reading Terminal Market had been described to me, I was in no way prepared for what actually awaited me.

Options. Millions of options, as far as the eye could see. In my two visits here I saw an oyster bar, Indian food, sushi, Greek food, an Amish baker.... I could go on.

The first time I went, I chose a New Orleans's themed booth and had what I thought was the best sandwich EVER. That is, until I went back the next day to Meltkraft where I definitely had the BEST. SANDWICH. EVER!

It gets crazy packed in here, and waiting for your order often means standing right in the middle of a crowded walkway. Not good for the agoraphobic or claustrophobic, but so worth it if you can get past the insanity.

Happened to drive by Nicoletto's the other night and decided to stop in to try it. So glad we did! 

It's a small shop and you go in and order at the counter. You can choose from some pastries/baked goods/refrigerated goods they have out. You can also choose fresh pasta to take home and cook yourself if you so choose! 

I ordered a pasta bowl and chose the bucatini pasta, with the pink sauce and beef meatballs. The bf ordered a vegan meatball sub. We shared the Italian "poutine".

My pasta bowl was so, so friggin' good.  I went to italy a few months ago and this was definitely the best pasta I've had since then. Well-made and cooked perfectly al dente. The sauce was creamy/cheesy/tomato-y goodness. The parmesan was so fresh and good and added the perfect amount of saltiness. It was a very nice portion size, and I probably should have taken some home, but I sat there and at the whole thing and made myself miserably full. Worth it though. 

I assume the vegan meatball sub was good because my bf finished it before I was even 1/3 of the way through my pasta, and he didn't even bothered to offer me a bite! -_-

The Italian poutine was good! Fries topped with a nice, chunky marinara...fresh pieces of mozzerella..finished off with some parmesan and basil.  Really yummy!

We really, really enjoyed our meal here. Definitely plan to go back!

I heart The Country Club. That's just the way it is.

A few months after I first moved to New Orleans, a friend of mine said, "I have to take you to this clothing optional country club I went to this weekend!" Uhhh, come again? I was so intrigued that I couldn't refuse and boy, am I glad that I didn't! 

First of all, the exterior of this place is enough to charm the pants off of you (no pun intended). It's an old grand Bywater mansion with a manicured lawn, stately columns, and a tiny neon sign reading: The Country Club adorning the top of the porch to add just a little cheekiness (again, no pun intended). I've had brunch a few times sitting out on the porch and it's the very definition of contentment.

The inside rooms are all pretty cool. The front rooms are reserved for dining, the back rooms make way for a pool table, some lounge-y chairs, and the indoor bar. Cool, local art adorns all of the walls. I love that they keep the door to the kitchen open most of the time. It looks spotless and the cooks/chef always look like they're having a good time.

NOW, onto my favorite part: the pool. There is always a healthy mix of every type of person you want to (and don't want to) see back there. Yuppie couples, hipster dudes with scrawled crotch tattoos, impeccably toned & tanned hairless twinks, lesbians with half of their heads shaved, hot MILFs, and the occasional creepy old man. People are friendly but respectful of your boundaries. I've spent time back there both fully clothed and naked as the day I was born and never felt out-of-place either way. They recently switched the pool to salt water and it's heated during the winter months. The hot tub is spacious and can get pretty rowdy. They project random movies/TV shows/music videos onto the back of the house and the last time I was there the most amazing Pandora station was playing the entire time. 

The changing rooms are clean and always smell like wood (again, no pun intended) to me, which is cool...it's all "Aspen cedar wood ski lodge" feeling. They used to keep bowls of condoms out but the last time I was there, they were absent. Hmm. 

The bartenders, for the most part, are all really great. Kris is awesome! There is one guy that has worked there forever that can be a little bitchy, but..whatever. They have lots of fun themed nights (Ladies Night, White-trash Wednesdays, etc.) with drink specials.  

Honestly, this place can do no wrong in my book. If you're looking for a unique and fun experience (really, where else can you sit naked in a hot tub eating a steak?) then check out THE COUNTRY CLUB!

As theaters go, not too bad.

What I liked most about this place is it's comfortable and roomy. It is clean as well. The bar is reasonable and I like having a drink while watching the movie. The service is decent, but needs to mature a little.

Where it falls woefully short is the quality of the food. The menu is small and has some interesting descriptions, yet that is where it ends. This is definitely a "frozen/canned" kitchen. Very bland flavors and lack of freshness. I would not go here expecting a decent or even edible meal. If I were rating just the food, it would get ONE STAR.

I would suggest eating out prior, and going here for a drink and a movie.

Lastly, while I rated the service as decent, they need to really smooth it out from an operational standpoint. I'm not taking anything away from my rating because they are fairly new and probably working out some issues.

As chains go, Changs is #1. (#1 Chinese....inside joke)

In all seriousness, I have been going to P.F. Changs since they opened at this location.

I like the decor and the layout of the restaurant and bar. It is very different from any other chain. It's a cross between traditional and modern chinese. If it's your first time in a Changs, you'll appreciate the atmosphere.

Here comes a rant...

The only thing that irks me is that stupid revolving door. It's cheesy and detracts from the visual experience. Even worse, when it gets busy in the waiting area, I've actually seen people pushed (accidentally) into the door stall and spun right out of the restaurant. It was pretty funny at the time. Also, may sound silly, but I actually like holding the door for my date. Lastly, I've watched many older folks struggle with that thing.Okay, enough about the door...just remove the stupid thing.

Service has always been consistently good to great. Rachael and Dennis (managers) are always visible and on the oft occasion where there is a service or food issue, they resolve it quickly. Some of the reviews really knock the servers. It is a restaurant, so anyone can have an off night. I've seen the staff bend over backwards for people I would have tossed out the front door after the first insult was fired. 

I will agree with the scripting of the welcome that other reviewers have commented on already. I APPRECIATE the ask about allergies. It's smart and demonstrates a genuine interest in the health concerns of the patrons. Every restaurant should take a cue from Changs on that. What I really get tired of is the "special sauce" thing. I know the servers are trained to ask, so I put this one on the franchise management. The whole thing just seems gimmicky to me and you can tell the servers hate it as well. I've joked with several and they just roll their eyes about having to ask/tell the "sauce story." I don't have a great idea on how to improve that part of the service, but I am certain the servers do. Why not ask them?

Lastly, why the hell do they box leftovers at the table? I appreciate that my server boxes it up for me, but I find that a little detrimental to the overall experience. And I've watched my server boxing at other tables while I waited for her/him to get back to me.  Again, I think this is a franchise management requirement, but I would try to change it. 

Our meals have always been very good. I know some folks call this Americanized fare. While I agree somewhat, it is unique. And for those who slam the food as fake, well thats just stupid. I know there are some copycats out there too (what better compliment). For instance, the Dynamite Shrimp is one of my favorites and a version of it can be found on a few other chain restaurant menus. That's to be expected. Places like TGIF's, Applebee's and Chilis have no creativity so they look to other chains for ideas. I find the menu to be very different from those other places, which is why we go there even several years after it opened. And how many chains offer a GLUTEN-FREE menu? (it has a lot of choices) BTW, I won't step foot in any other mid-priced chain restaurant. P.F. Changs is it.

Some of my other favorites: Mongolian Beef, Mandarin Orange Chicken, Oolong Marinated Sea Bass (awesome), Chengdu Lamb (this is the best dish, but don't mistake it for the Wok Seared Lamb which really should be removed from the menu).

The bar area is small, but the service is just as good. And on a busy night, it may be easier to get a walk-in table there than wait an hour for the dining room.

Overall - Best chain restaurant in the area, great staff and management, and solid unique food.

I really don't think you can go wrong with a visit to P.F. Changs. And if something does, Rachael will make it right anyway. So what do you have to lose?

The bar area is spacious with lots of tables and bar seating. The one thing I don't get is that there are several TV's above the bar, not all showing sports. Let's go to service. It's solid, especially at the bar. I will admit I do go here often for the bar. It gets a decent crowd on the usual nights and the staff does make it enjoyable.

As for the food, I'll actually start with the menu. Classic mistakes here. The menu is way too big. Another reason the food can only achieve average taste levels. But that's not the worst part. The actual menu is a visual nightmare. Think of it a throwing up words, visuals and colors on page after page. My friends and I laugh every time we see it. As designers, this is clearly a case where the restaurant wanted to save a buck. Instead, it makes it very hard to read, and leads to less than stellar opinions about the food itself.

Most of the menu items have a very familiar taste. I've eaten here many times because I know what I'm getting. My advice to the owner: Drop the menu to 30 or fewer items. 100+, it is impossible for the kitchen to excel. Start buying obviously fresh ingredients. Remove the tacky decor and video games. Let the property speak for itself. And get rid of the lame DJ on weekend nights. It's awful and distracting. The three drunk girls and really lame guy that take to the floor strikes me as a bad vegas show. Finally, allow more input from your staff. They're actually pretty good and can tell you what works.

So average across the board but a little up-tick for the staff.

Really, in my back yard?

Craig Laban (Philly Inquirers master restaurant reviewer) gives Hans three bells (Excellent) out of four. For those that follow Craig, we know the rarity of a three bell restaurant as most of his reviews are one or two bells. So this obviously caught my attention.

Hands down, Hans Dynasty is the absolute BOMB for Chinese cuisine. Simply awesome.

I ordered take out only, so I cannot comment on the table service. Although, the dining room was completely full and smiles could be seen everywhere. The staff seemed friendly and were attentive while I was waiting for my order to be completed, quickly welcoming new guests as they walked through the door.

The decor is modern Chinese and definitely reflects the origin of the menu. Visually, it is a mix of complimentary textures and colors, Large slate tile married with natural woods in warm red tones. The space is small, and fills quickly, but the noise level didn't seem too bad.  In the back of the dinning area was a finishing station, mirrored with a large frosted window behind which the primary kitchen. Every so often you see bursts of flame through the frosted glass as dishes are prepared. Way cool.

The dining area is very clean, even after a full year in business.

So here's what we got witha brief review for each.

Sweet and sour cucumbers - Crisp, bright with a nice sweetness and hint of spice. Each diagonally cut wedge was nearly the same size demonstrating real attention to detail and of course, some serious knife skills.

Dumplings with chili oil - Savory and salty (not too salty though). These are the best dumplings I have ever tasted. The sesame seeds added a nice texture to the soft dumpling.

Dan Dan Noodles - I have to say, this was not a hit for me. The flavor was obvious and the spice well-balanced. The noodles have a licorice overtone. Thats not a criticism, it just doesn't favor my palette. I can see why people like this dish.

Chicken with broccoli - Again, this was a huge winner with myself and my girlfriend. Nice sweetness and a really unique flavor. I NEVER order chicken, but I would order this again.

Double cooked pork - This was my favorite dish on this visit. The pork was tender and juicy, thinly sliced in a wonderful sauce. It did have a little kick, but like all other "spicy" dishes, it was never overpowering.

Pork lo mein - This is my usual favorite noodle. Again, this may sound repetitive, but the best lo mein I've ever had. Tons of flavor, perfectly cooked. Period.

In all of our food, the freshness of the ingredients shined through. The flavors were well balanced against the spicy ingredients. In addition, each dish was unique. Nothing had a similar taste or flavor. 

My girlfriend and I could not stop eating. Even after three plate fulls, mixed with eat menu item, we were ready for more. We settled on saving the rest for lunch the next day. The portions are pretty good for the price. All the food listed cost a total of $54. A great value.

Look, this is a must stop. Wether you go to the Philly, Exton or Royersford locations, just go.

When you walk in you would think this is just a standard boba place but the food is actually really good! I tried the combination soup and my partner had the beef rice and they were both great. Although for me the shining star of our visit was the boba! 
They have a ton of different flavors for slush and snow boba, and they have teas as well. The screen was a bit overwhelming and the young man up front was so kind and patient with my questions. For that alone I would go back.

We eat here more often than I would like to admit. They can be delivered through uber eats which is how we first tried. Our food arrived hot and fresh and we picked what was listed as "local favorites". Well believe you me they are favorites for a reason! The popcorn chicken is so delicious it's got a unique flavor I can't quite describe but I haven't had anywhere else. The black pepper noodles listed as an appetizer are actually my favorite meal. There is a delicious fried egg on Top and I can go there without getting that. 

If you do have the chance to go in they have great lunch specials and the service is quick. You can tell everyone is so nice and they want to do their best. I don't think I've had a single thing I don't like. They have a giant pork Bao it's $5 but it's sooooo good.

I got the "Jane" - it's a red pizza with mozzarella, aged provolone, grana padano, and  fresh basil. The crust was decent, the service was good and fast, but the sauce was really salty and I think maybe there were 4 leaves of basil on the entire pie. 

Then again, I am comparing it to the pizza gods of Tacconellis where you have to reserve your dough in advance. That place is just phenomenal but was closed the day I went to try pizza brain...and I likely won't be trying a new place again. 

No need. I explored, and I haven't found pizza yet that can beat Tacconellis. I will, however, come back for the ice cream next door.

I can't imagine giving Hattie B's less than 5 stars.  Nashville's finest piping hot fried chicken establishment is worth going out yo way *Migos voice*

We got literally everything on the menu.  The half fried chicken is the way to go.  Meal with sides  - you will be over joyed.  Get the collard greens and mac and cheese.  Corn bread was gone in 15 seconds. Bean salad is creamy and tart - great paired with the fried chicken.  Even the pickles are something I would buy again and again to keep and feast on at home (by themselves, just saying).

The chicken, you ask?  Hot and juicy.  Temperature wise and spice wise.  Spice level has a few different levels and is customizable.  I went for the medium and thought it packed a kick while still being delicious and flavorful.  Pitchers of beer are optional and highly recommended and are this chickens soul mate.  Ask for a few samples as they have local brews on tap.

Banana pudding is pillowy soft, silly and delicious.  I'm sensing a major pre-trend here. Marshmallow topping is otherworldly and is heavenly on top of the actual pudding, yet nestled under neath the wafers and drizzle.

If you are in Nashvegas Hattie B's or bust.  And get a hat or tshirt to commemorate the experience.  Or it didn't happen.  And please, bring some back to NJ for me.

Fantastic food & exceptional service!

Owner Gabe really hooked it up. He shaped the perfect takeout menu for our group of 11 women, and everyone praised how absolutely bomb the food was.

I wish I had a 'before' pic of our wonderful spread--shredded chicken, carne asada, sautéed veggies, rice, mix of tortillas, onion & cilantro, chips, salsa, guac--but everyone seriously dove in and devoured the deliciousness!

And that guac, oh my - get two quarts of it!

There's so many Mexican food options in Santa Barbara, but Gabe really makes the takeout experience so effortless. He's super patient & unfailingly helpful, and the professionalism of Mex Authentic makes it the best spot for Mexican food in the area.

...but I hear there's only five of them, so good luck.

We were first matched with an older room, and honestly I was surprised that this is what Hyatt is doing to their guests. Dingy, outdated, and smelled of cheap air freshener (bad sign!)

Fortunately Maria at the front desk was able to shift us into one of the remodeled rooms, and our experience automatically took a 180. Our new space was clean, modern, and overall more of what I'd expect from a beachfront hotel in Santa Barbara. 

Hyatt is just steps from East Beach and a short drive to State St. All of the staff is friendly & helped shape a relaxing getaway weekend.

She wouldn't sit us anywhere but one table which was close to all the people walking by. From reading these reviews this is pretty common from her. She's crazy.

I made reservations here for brunch on a Saturday morning at 11:15 AM. We got there right when they opened (11 AM), and there was already a line of people waiting for them to open. 

It was a relatively chilly morning, and they tried to sit us outside. We requested to sit inside which they accommodated. They host was super apologetic of sitting us outside when we wanted to sit inside, very nice guy. The waiter was to the point and had a dry sense of humor which we appreciated. He told us the specials and took our drink orders. We also decided on getting the shrimp and grits, the gumbo, the jambalaya pasta, the poutine, and the banana fosters waffles. Our waiter split it up so they came to the table at different times and the bananas fosters waffles came out as dessert.

The shrimp and grits & the gumbo came out first. The shrimp and grits were hands down my favorite. Peppery and well spiced. It came with 3 pretty sizeable shrimp. The gumbo was good, my husband and sister loved it. The poutine and jambalaya pasta came out next. I enjoyed the poutine, the jambalya pasta was okay. It was pretty expensive for what it was, we definitely wouldn't get that again. The bananas foster waffles was so good. That waffle didn't rely on the toppings like most. That waffle could have stood on its own. It was damn good, crispy but fluffy and light. The bananas fosters topping just added to the perfection. It came with maple syrup which we did not use, that would have been way too sweet.

I would def. come here again. Def try to get here as soon as you can to try to get your choice of seat. The gardens/outdoor area was very nice, and if it was a nicer day, we def. would have preferred to sit there.

Move over, Texas.  Alabama, Georgia, and both of you Carolinas with your runny vinegar-ey sauces, step aside.  Good BBQ is comin' through. From Louisiana.  

In another of numerous recent additions to the BBQ landscape in New Orleans, Blue Oak is staking out a corner--literally--as part of the Chickie Wah Wah bar space.

This is what I call "21st Century Barbeque". Specifically, this means the meats are high quality, cooked to appropriate tenderness but not overdone, and with flavor that can stand alone without sauce.  It means a choice of regional sauces, and none of them taste like Kraft. Just as importantly, it means the sides get equal attention.  The mac and cheese here is dense and garlicly (but not as tart-cheesy as I personally prefer), but the real standout are the Brussels sprouts.   Shorn from their usual tight ball and grilled to a partial crispness, this "side" alone is worth the trip in the same way Charlie's Steak House's onion rings are.  

The portions are not that big, but neither are the prices.  Across the room against the wall is the Chickie Wah Wah bar, so one has more than the usual bbq joint choice of libations.  

Our visit coincided with a music performance and a cover charge. This probably isn't the best place to unload the minivan and bring in the Little League, though it might be earlier in the day.  (Then again, probably not: the Brussels Sprout does not have a great reputation with the grade school set).

Let me guess: You're on Magazine Street, it's Sunday morning, and you're looking for brunch.  All the usual suspects have lines down the street (some even have their lines now, here on Yelp!, where you can register to wait).  

I offer the Munch Factory as a good alternative, and it's still on "Magazine Street" even though the address says Sophie Wright Place. 

About the worst aspect of the place is the name:  "The Munch Factory" sounds like a place I would have found in the Clearview Mall 25 years ago.  (On Sundays, the menu has it renamed "Brunch Factory", a cute variation on what is still a corporate-sounding name).  Despite the name, this place clearly has a real chef working in back. For example, a recent Sunday had an oxtail offered as the special.  Oxtail is a challenging cut, gristly and boney and interspersed with tasty shards of meat and fat.  What came from the kitchen was monumental: a bed of kale, atop that a dense and perfectly cooked savory risotto cake, then a huge fist of oxtail, and finally topped with two eggs poached just right.  It reminded me of Mile High Pie, except with meat and kale and eggs instead of ice cream and meringue.  That may sound decadent and even a little disgusting, but it was actually delicious and not terribly heavy.  (Or is my judgment on what constitutes "heavy" failing with age? It's possible.)

The Shrimp and Grits is based heavily on Worcheschire and has a dark, almost black sauce.  It's a robustly flavorful dish that does not rely on bacon for its kick (though let the record show I habor no ill will toward bacon on my shrimp and grits).  Any shrimp and grits fan should plan on at least one visit to the Munch Factory.  

Five stars for this place, because both the oxtail and shrimp and grits were near perfect creations.  

The staff is helpful and prompt, and they will work with children despite having no children's menu, offering burgers, grilled cheese, etc.  

Munch Factory is in a corner cafe with lots of light and space, big comfortable chairs, and banquette seating all around the sides. FInd it right just where Magazine comes out of downtown as a one-way, on the edge between the Garden District and the quirky and charming Coliseum neighborhood.

Should Gendusa's get four or five stars, I wondered?  

Spoiler alert: my answer is right at the top of the page.  If I could give 4 1/2 stars, that's where I'd place it.  A five-star experience should not involve the kind of long waits that are consistent feature of Gendusa's, says my brain, but my heart--or actually, my mouth and tummy--say 4 stars seems too low.  (And what about my heart?  After a plate of their sublime Alfredo, my heart says "No comment.")  

The five stars is for the food, with maybe a side note for attitude and atmosphere.  This is top-shelf Italian, the kind you find on Arthur St. in the Bronx or what's left of Little Italy in NYC.  Specifically, that means the great traditional American-Italian dishes like spaghetti and meatball, eggplant and veal Parmesan, and a slap-you-in-the-face sharp Caesar salad, among one of the best I've had in New Orleans.  The thin-crust pizzas are on par with much tonier (or should that be Tony-er? This is an Italian place, you see, and.....is this thing on?  Hello? Nevermind.) places like Ancora on Freret minus the exotic ingredients (and also exotic prices).

The pasta, the red sauce, the Alfredo cream sauce, all of it tastes fresh and homemade coming from the busy kitchen, which brings us to the four or three star part of the review: the wait.  Food here takes a long time to come out.  You can have a five star food experience, but expect two stars on service time.  A 6:15 pm seating left our party barely enough time to make it down the street to see Ricky Graham's latest show at Rivertown at eight. 

The annoyance of long wait times is mitigated by the cheerful staff, who acknowledge the delay but do so with an unspoken sense of "good food is worth waiting for, braugh".  As it turns out, they're absolutely right; you forget the 80 minutes you waited once you take in that first forkful of Italian manna.  

The chefs and owners are visible and clearly enthused about what they're doing, which is too rare in restaurants these days.  That attitude makes one feel really guilty about bitching about delays.  Enjoy the extra 20 or 40 minutes of table conversation (and put that phone away! Except, of course, to check into Yelp!).

Before I begin, I must state that I am a Philly native working and living in AZ. I'm not saying that because of this my review/opinion holds more weight over others, but basically, it does. :) 

I gave this place two stars so I'll start out with the place itself. East Coast Super Subs (ECSS from here on) has a pretty kickass divey, sports theme going on and I can definitely see this place being a great hang out when it's busy and full of people watching the game. Every square inch of ECSS is decked out with sports memorabilia of some kind, many of which are east coast teams and in the older designs. I think that's pretty cool and I'm not even a huge sports guy. 

Now that is said, I have to sadly move on to what I felt was a let down. I had business in Tucson and specifically looked this place up to try a cheesesteak. I'm sure their other offerings are delicious, but like I said, I'm from Philly and I wanted to see if ECSS would do me right or wrong; I didn't want anything else. 

To start off, my cheesesteak was a bit light to say the least. I felt shorted on meat. Any time you bite into a cheesesteak, or any sandwich for that matter, and get a mouthful of bread, your day is a little less joyous. Well, I figured out why. When ordering, I assumed it would be east coast style and I told the waitress to hold on the lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, or whatever the hell else they were putting in there, because who puts that shit in a cheesesteak? At ECSS, the majority of their cheesesteaks are fluffed up with this stuff. 

OK, not the end of the world...until I tasted it. The meat tasted like some kind of soy or imitation beef product. I don't even know how to begin to describe it, but the "beef" felt flimsy and powdery and fell apart in your mouth, and not in way that people will describe BBQ, but like it was "deatomized" or something. 

Now, before I'm labeled as just a Philly prick who only believes a cheesesteak can be a certain way, keep in mind that I gave praise to Forefather's out of Tempe. Also, the friend I was with who is originally from VA shared the same sentiment. See? Virginia, a neutral third party state. 

I'm sorry fellow Yelpers, I do not approve (at least not their cheesesteaks).

Let me preface this by saying that it is very seldom that I give a place I've been to "one star", but after going to this place, I wish they had the option on Yelp of identifying your experience by a "black star" because this place should have a big fat one above their restaurant sign.

Firstly, the service was POOR. I was in a party of five and I realize that the server was the only waiter for similar sized tables but this guy was extremely aloof and appeared like he just smoked a field of marijuanna when he greeted us. Tell me if I'm wrong, but when more than one person settles at a sit-down restaurant, shoudn't we all have a menu? He obviously thought that it was a luxury to have as he placed one food and drink menu on the table and expected us to pass it around- prolonging the time we could have ordered- it was hard enough to read with such dim light that had absolutely no effect on the ambiance. He didn't bring out silverware too which he also might of thought was an indulgence to have. What a nut job this guy was!

Needless to say he also forgot about bringing out one of our orders, which was another blow to our dining experience. But it was nothing compared to the quantity and quality of the food. Perhaps it was what we got- but the food was mediocre, nothing to brag about, and was not justified in the amount of money you pay for it. To put it in perspective, my lamb kabob dish was about 3 oz of unseasoned rice with an equal amount of lamb parsels that were tasteless. They served it on an appetizer plate. Go figure.

The server at the end topped off the night with charging us 46% gratuity, which was an obvious error in his calculation. I expect that from a pothead, but the chefs know better! 

If you're looking for an delicious place to eat, a place that signifies the beautiful arab culture with their art, food, and service... THIS IS NOT THE PLACE... especially if you're a novice at this type of cuisine- steer clear- this is NOT authentic.

Trust me- there are better restaurants in the city if you're looking for genuine middle eastern food- and Fez does not qualify as one of them.

Forget about Jim's or Geno's ... PAT'S is the place to get the best, most delicious cheesesteaks!

And that makes it the _best thing in Philly!!_

(Ok, Jim's and Geno's aren't bad ... but Pat's is still the best!)

and you can't beat the fact that they are open 24/7!!  Sometimes a cheesesteak for breakfast is exactly what I need!  (Don't laugh, I'm serious!).

Quick and easy service! Called in my order ahesd of time and picked up in ~10 minutes. Food is enough for 2. Also comes with a small side salad and tzatziki sauce. Well seasoned & delicious!! Location-wise, very easy to get to and plenty of parking around the site.

I've been to the Casual Clam many times and given the fact that it's laid back as the name clearly states, I could handle this. However, this past Saturday, i was there with two friends for lunch and encountered a situation that I feel was handled poorly by the management. My friend ordered the clam roll and after about 2 bites, put the food down and said the clams had a foul taste and could not eat it. The server who was nice, was notified. After some time, the server came back and offered my friend a cup of soup! What the....?! 
The worst part was when we received our tab, she was charged FULL price - she ate her cole slaw, but $13.99 is a bit much for a side. She clearly did not eat the food and we all felt that this may be our last Casual Clam outing after this.
I know the place has been around a long time, but clearly not the way to handle the situation.

THEY NO LONGER HAVE SOFT SHELL CRAB BENEDICT... I was lured into Stanley's with its Yelp front page picture. I have never been so disappointed to hear such bad  news for breakfast, and it has been a year since they stopped serving soft shell crab.. A girl can only dream now. sigh.

Regardless, Stanley's is just one of those breakfast places you probably won't get anywhere else, breakfast that surrounds everything n'awlins, I loved it.

- Breaux Bridge (boudin) Benedict - http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/stanley-new-orleans?select=85ko-LVMln_O2M8WPoBIwg#WEfW_IEGhOpW2Ttxh5L46Q
- Fried Oyster Benedict - "Eggs Stanley" - http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/stanley-new-orleans?select=85ko-LVMln_O2M8WPoBIwg#hc_jQ6ERL_lt0AgcCakncQ

It was my first time trying boudin, and further a boudin benedict. It was super delicious, both benedicts were covered in creole hollandaise sauce. Both the eggs on the benedicts were #yolkporn quality poached.  I liked JY's Breaux Bridge benedict better than my oyster one (cheese and boudin, c'mon now).

We sat at the bar where the waiter helped us out with suggestions. He was super helpful and attentive, along with other NOLA-centered advice. Loved the hospitality! 
I regret not trying the Banana Fosters french toast (dessert home to NOLA, who knew), but I'm not one to eat sweets first thing in the morning :)

man oh man oh man oh man.

JY and I took a 4 mile (roundtrip) walk to The Joint for some real authentic southern BBQ. So, we were insanely hungry by the time we reached The Joint, ready to sink our teeth into some melt-in-your-mouth BBQ ribs. The star average was high, and we couldn't wait to try their ribs (also, a break away from cajun-style seafood gorging).

The ribs were so dry and difficult to swallow (tNOTwss!). The ribs were in a dry rub, and I loved the flavor but couldn't get over how tough the ribs were. The dryness was somewhat relieved with some BBQ sauce, one was good and one was really spicy. 
Maybe we should've stuck with brisket.  

Mac and cheese wasn't super cheesy, but I actually enjoyed it. The baked beans were also good. We finished off the meal with a peanut butter pie, which was the highlight of our meal.

Washed it down with my strawberry margarita (tart & really refreshing) and pretended those ribs never happened 

:*****(

"America's Best Fried Chicken"

Fried chicken is seriously my weakness, so I was more than excited to try Willie Mae's. A trip to the south would not be complete without trying a local fried BIRD.

Willie Mae's fried chicken's crust is straight up super flaky and the chicken inside was extremely juicy and moist. I did think that the batter was a tad bit salty, and had some sort of expectation that it was going to be a little sweet (not sweet at all).

This fried chicken ---- you absolutely have to eat it in one sitting. Left overs do not taste as good and the batter soaks up all the grease, making it a soggy and sad (still delicious doe!).

To counterbalance the grease overload, we also ordered some rice & beans (very good!), grilled chicken salad (standard good), mac & cheese, mashed potatoes. 

Service was very friendly and there is a long line that forms outside of the restaurant.
You are not allowed to stand in the doorway because it's nicely air conditioned inside, you must wait in the humid weather with the other fried chicken fiends. 
MUAHAHa.

I think one really cool thing to note about Tremé is that it's the oldest African American neighborhood in the US, very historic. It's where we stayed in NOLA, and were pleasantly surprised to see how friendly the locals were. 
It's where Louis Armstrong is from, word UP.

So really.  When you see a large group of girls coming to your restaurant, for a BACHELORETTE party, you best be sure you have your service pants on.  What is one thing that comes to mind with a party like that? Alcohol! That equals higher check with higher tip.  

I'm going to lay this out so simply...really simple.
-From the time we ordered our appetizers and the time we got them was close to 30 minutes (cheese board and french fries, probably the two most low maintenance ones on the menu).
-From the time we ordered our entrees to the time we got them was close to 1 hr 30 minutes.  -Drinks on average took almost 10 minutes. 
-My friend went up to the bar at one point and asked why a gin and tonic was taking so long, she of course got the run around about large parties.  There was a party that got there and ordered after us that got their food before us. 
-They brought out an appetizer on the house (which was nice), but WE WANT DINNER! 
-My friend who is allergic to nuts (and told the server), ordered a simple sourdough loaf to snack on since she couldn't eat the other items we ordered (and was eating hair at that point).  They brought her bread out with...you guessed it...PESTO. SMH
-The bartender brought out a bottle of champagne (on the house) while we were still waiting for our food (after my friend had already complained).  When we researched it, that bottle retails in a liquor store for $5.99.  Sure, its the thought that counts, but really dude - you couldn't splurge for a little bit of a nicer bottle? Don't assume your clientele doesn't know bottles, some of us worked in restaurants. 
-When the food finally came, three of the dishes were cold and had to be sent back.  My duck was overcooked and my friends drink never came. 

We also never got a visit from the Manager to apologize and our server was so embarrassed by everything that he basically dropped off our checks and ran.  I just don't understand why the waiter or manager could have come over and been honest with us "So sorry, our kitchen is so backed up tonight" blah, blah, blah. It wasn't until we made a fuss that they did something. They did offer to buy us dessert, but um, no. 

When all was said and done, they only comp'd our appetizers...2 of them.  They should have comped our drinks at the very least.  I only had 3 drinks that whole time and you would think for being there so long, I would have had more.  Our reservations were at 7:30pm and we left close to 10:30p - all in a bad mood...there were only 8 of us too (one doesn't even drink!)!  

The 2 stars (which is generous) come from the awesome ambiance of the restaurant and the amazing cheese board and french fries we had. 

Agustin, take note. When a bachelorette party (or any large party for that matter) comes in, make sure they have a drink in their hand the whole night.  Then they don't have time to sober up and realize what a mess your kitchen is in.

Next best thing than your own backyard.

+ Great beer!  Tons of choices on draft and bottle. 
+ Beautiful inside and out. The inside bar area has a lot of seating and a great bar perfect for a quick drink or the outside area is super comfy and set up with tables and patio furniture.
+ Pet friendly
+ No kids after 3 (I'm not kid friendly) 
+ Different food trucks there daily (except Sundays,  more on that later)  offers a good mix up
+ Food truck less Sunday's they allow any outside food to make up for it.

This is justifiably the most famous cajun restaurant in New Orleans.  Chef Paul's restaurant is ground zero for this rich and flavorful cuisine.  There's a ton of reviews so I'm going to just give you a few tips for your visit.  

They deliver a bread basket just after you place your order.  It comes with 2 kinds of rolls and 2 kinds of muffins.  One for each person at the table.  If you eat the basket, you will not make it through their enormous entrees, an appetizer and dessert.  Unless you're planning on taking your leftovers, you will need to plan your order carefully.  We order an app, and two entrees between us and never finish.  I literally had trouble breathing after we ordered an app, 2 entrees and split a dessert and I still didn't finish my entree.  

I do wish they would cut the entree portion and the price so that you could finish and app, entree and dessert.  Maybe just a 3 course option with reduced portions and price! 

It's all good.  Try the blackened redfish, the eggplant pirogue and the stuffed mirliton.  I've never had a bad dish.

The service is excellent and they have a very good bar.  A must visit on your trip to New Orleans for authentic cajun.

I have had this bookmarked for a long time.  It's a drive from Uptown New Orleans so it took me some time to get there.  I was really looking forward to this place after looking at the reviews and the menu.

The place is very cool. I like the menu and the staff is a bit harried but friendly and helpful.  I ordered an oyster dinner with a side salad and some red beans and rice.  My wife ordered the stuffed peppers with mashed potatoes and gravy and a side salad.  We both chose Italian dressing.  

There is very little that is homemade from scratch about their food.  They use highly processed ingredients and cut lots of corners.  I don't mind splurging on food that isn't necessarily healthy but you have to make it from scratch and you can't serve me this level of bad food choices.  

The mashed potatoes were instant.  The salad dressing, cocktail sauce and breading for my oysters were bought in from their jobber.  Fake butter with our bread is unacceptable.  Margarine was introduced after WWII in a time of need.  It's since been clearly shown to be 3x as likely to give you a heart attack.  We all know that highly processed food is a bad choice.  I can buy this at the supermarket.  I don't want to go out for dinner and be served this.  Do some cooking!

The oysters were fried perfectly and the portion was great but the cornmeal breading was terrible.  The red beans were probably a can of blue runner with a few pieces of sausage thrown in.  They were bland and the worst example of this dish I have had in my many years here.
