There was nothing redeeming about this dinner.  I guess people come here for the portion sizes and the vibe but for me I care more about the quality of the food and the care that goes into it.  There's no food knowledge here or care about what they are serving to their customers.  I can't recommend you try this place at all.

This used to be one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans but I'm absolutely sure they've lost their attention to detail here. The last few times have been amiss. 

Everything I had today was way over salted. Last time I had to send some slaw back for the same reason. I really like salt. This was way over the top. Both times. It's easy to taste your food as a chef. It's your job. They either aren't or their palates are burnt. 

The duck terrine dish today was too salty, the tuna sandwich and cucumber salad were both ridiculous and they're serving them with chips on top of it!  So much salt I had salt sweats. Ridiculous. I got a bowl of gumbo and it was over salted too. This after I sent the sandwich back. Our server said she'd tell the kitchen. I'll bet it didn't faze them a bit. 

I've been eating here for 10 years. This was really sad.  My wife said the gulf fish today was very good. I tried her salad and it was very good as well. 

We ordered coffee. I really like their coffee service. It's terrific.  I've always had great success ordering desserts here so tried the coconut pie. It was so sweet I couldn't eat it. My wife usually will eat whatever I cannot and she couldn't eat it either. 

Seems like a theme here. A lack of touch. $130 with tip for 3 after they took the sandwich and dessert off made me sorry I showed up today.  Cochon Butcher suffers sometimes from the same. Too much heat and too much salt. Hmmmm.  Never had a problem at Cochon so the theory that it's a Link restaurant thing is a little blown. 

I can't leave my 5 stars up anymore and I'm not sure I'm a fan right now. Disappointed.

I cannot remember the last time I ate somewhere and was as disappointed and felt as financially violated as I do right now.  I will start with what I liked about this place.  It won't take long.  I liked that it's in a nice residential neighborhood and is unmarked by signage.  I also thought that both my waiters were very good.  The coffee is French Truck and was also good.  That's it.  That's everything that I can say that passed for me.

I ordered the "Crispy Sweetbreads with Jumbo Lump Crab, spinach, bacon, quail egg and pommery mustard 15.00"  I had to copy this from the menu because all I could taste was the bacon.  I didn't order a drink and I don't smoke so I do have a palate.  In fact, I didn't realize there was mustard until I copied this for my review.  This was a ridiculously small portion all around.  Possibly 4 bites and the sweetbreads were so minute that you couldn't taste them under the breading even if there wasn't just an overbearing amount of bacon.  Why didn't you just bring me a few slices of bacon?  Moving on before I explode.

Next I tried a snapper dish that doesn't appear on the website currently but was on the menu tonight.  I can't actually describe it as it was written because there wasn't enough of anything on the plate where you could identify it.  The snapper was dry and on top of some nice farro.  A nice textural addition to the plate.  There was a puree of what I think was sunchoke?  There was maybe a tablespoon spread out on the plate.  You couldn't taste it and there wasn't enough that it matters that I can remember.  Why bother.  Then there was a similarly sized streak of a truffle vinaigrette.  I also identified part of a julianned chanterelle.  This dish was dry, really arid, dry.  Underseasoned because of not enough vinaigrette?  It wasn't a sauce exactly.  I am disgusted.  I asked the waiter if this is how the dish was supposed to look and if the amounts were accurate and he affirmed it.  I wish he had said it was a mistake.  The manager asked if she could bring more puree and vinaigrette.  I didn't bother.  It wasn't going to help a lot the dish needed a sauce.  I was mostly done and had lost some interest in the dish at this point.  

Not to be deterred and since I was really really hungry for lack of food on my plate we ordered desert and coffee.  I forgot to mention that the entree was minuscule.  I ordered the banana split. "Caramelized Banana Split with vanilla ice cream, warm banana bread, butterscotch, chocolate sauce, toasted walnuts 14.00"  Unbelievably lame waste of $14.  I can barely stand to write this.  The bananas were underripe and needed to be caramelized.  These had a little caramel on them.  Cook them like a Foster a little.  The banana bread was dry and wasn't warm at all.  I couldn't find the butterscotch and the chocolate sauce was hardly present.  Was this ice cream out of a tub?  There might have been 1 walnut altogether. A 3 year old could make a better split in a home kitchen.  I am appalled that this less than average desert came out at this restaurant and for this price.  I am stupefied.  

They should have bought us desert after I complained that my fish was dry and it was on the check.  It was $150 with a tip for 2 without drinks.  I can't believe it.  I have to make sure you understand that I would have been disappointed at 1/2 this price and I don't want the comments about the money to detract from the message about my experience here but it is relevant nonetheless.  I don't leave 1 star reviews often and without serious consideration but I am really unhappy with this restaurant.  The only thing more depressing than the food is the decor.
Services is okay on attitude but they are fast and prompt!  The food is what makes this place a one of kind breakfast, lunch, but so good you will wish they were open for dinner too!

I had very high hopes when I rolled in here with a crew of ladies to celebrate my belated birthday. I was looking forward to some hot delicious Korean food and then a nice 2-hour digestive period while we watched Les Mis at the movies nearby. Nobody left disappointed!

The morning of, I called in to reserve a table for 4 at 6pm, no issues. When we arrived the place was PACKED, but we were seated promptly. Get a reservation!

The menu is extensive and very affordable. We got 3 apps to share: jap chae noodles (couldn't stop eating these), pork and chive dumplings, and honey soy BBQ wings. Everything was fantastic, as well as all of the yummy salad noshes they give you. Love those spicy cucumbers.

For mains, two of us opted for the spicy pork bulgogi dolsot bibimbap style (includes all the yummy veggies), one person got a combo tray, and one got a hot pot. It was silent at the table when the food arrived, which is always a good sign. I inhaled that hot, crunchy, spicy, delightful bowl of goodies in about 15 minutes flat. Even though it was burning my mouth because it was still sizzling.

The whole meal only ran $22/person after tax, which is a real steal! We were in and out in perfect timing to get to the movie (about 1 1/2 hours). Service is a bit slow because there are only 3 ladies working the whole room, but they manage. Get aggressive (politely) when you want more water or they will ignore you.

Wow! Booziest $6 happy hour drinks in the city! I had two and accidentally got drunk. The first one was a gin drink that was a bit too sweet for me (Time after Thyme I think it was called), while the second one featured tequila and citrus and was much more well-balanced.

We decided to have a quick bite as well before a performance at the nearby Kimmel Center. I went with the crab cake and side of XIX salad (only $2 extra to get a small salad with the crab cake). The crab cake was really meaty with very nice chunks of lump crab meat. It was fully coated with a light layer of breadcrumbs and I believe was fried, which was OK but I prefer a crab cake without the coating and broiled. The side salad was tasty and worth the extra $2. It made a nice, light dinner.

My companions had the mussels and the calamari. The mussels were overflowing their pot and swimming in a tasty wine, butter, and fennel broth. The calamari was house made, lightly coated, and perfectly fried. All in all everyone was very pleased with their meals.

This place is a little pricey, and the food is good but nothing special. You're paying for atmosphere, which is admittedly quite tony. Come here to feel fancy.

I cyber-stalked this restaurant for many months leading up to its opening, pretty much from the day it was announced that Chifa would be replaced by a Cuban diner concept. Chifa had a special place in my heart, and it was a great place to take gluten free folks like myself. Rosa Blanca is a fine replacement in that respect, with a majority of the items on the menu being based around rice and corn rather than wheat. The food all around was really great, with a few slight misses, but I had to deduct a star for value.

$4 for one small empanada, no matter how good that empanada might be, is criminal. Make it $6, and put two on the plate. Then I'd be a bit more satisfied. That being said, the picadillo empanada was pretty much perfect (it maybe could have used one more minute in the oven). The ham and cheese empanada I didn't like as much. It had a different style of pastry and was fried instead of baked. Cuban ham and cheese empanadas are usually made with cubes of ham and cheesy super thick bechamel, much like the croqueta filling, and use the same type of pie pastry that the picadillo empanadas had. These were solid cheese and had serrano ham layered on top of the cheese. It was just a bit too rich and salty for me.

The salt cod croquetas were also a bit too salty for my taste, and I really love salt. The croquetas be jamon were absolutely perfect, however, and the dipping sauce was also delicious. You get 4 to an order. Get these. They will make your tummy happy.

For entrees, E went with the picadillo, his all-time favourite Cuban dish (he's Cuban), and I went with the vaca frita. You get to pick two sides from the list to accompany your entree. We both got the arroz moro (rice with black beans mixed in), I got the maduros (fired sweet plantains), and he got the tostones (smashed discs of fried unripe plantains). His entree had white rice underneath the picadillo stew, and had he known he probably would have selected a different side than the rice. 

The picadillo was absolutely delicious, even better than my own and I make awesome picadillo. My vaca frita was everything I hoped for and more, tender with a perfect crisp exterior and a sizable portion, but it needed a hot sauce of some kind to bring some moisture to the plate with the rice and beans. There is no hot sauce on the table, and this needs to be rectified. A bit of the house salsa from the complimentary chips and salsa, though, did just the trick! Those chips and salsa, by the way? Worth coming for just themselves. The salsa was absurdly delicious. There was definitely some balsamic vinegar hiding in there...

We washed all that down with a mojito temparado each, which was crazy delicious and really refreshing, and I also tried a rum cocktail made with blackberries. I'm not usually a big rum fan but I loved both of my drinks. E also had a cafe cubano at the end, which was excellent- I stole a sip.

Total damage was $101 before tax and tip. We racked up the bill quite a bit with drinks ($10 each, we had 3) and four appetizers, so a couple could easily get away with spending closer to $40 or $50 for a nice midweek meal with more careful ordering. The entree portions were plenty filling. Service was more than capable, the food and drinks were a bit slow to come out but it was very busy when we got there. Noise level tends toward deafening when it's a full house. I liked the update in decor, they really managed to change the vibe.

On our way out, we spied a surprisingly well-stocked pastry case for a late Tuesday evening. We snagged two guava and cheese and two just guava pastries, which was another $12.50. I just had mine for breakfast. It took all my willpower not to steal E's while he slept. Puff pastry so flaky and perfect you can't help but make a huge mess while eating it. They were heaven. Can't wait to come back for a lunch and breakfast!

Over the years of literally living across the street, this became known as the "bad weather restaurant", because it seems we always thought to come when the weather was awful. Well, tonight is our last night living across the street because we're moving down south- Deep South Philly that is. And it was cold as a welldigger's arse and snowy, so to le Viet we went!

Get these things: #2 crispy vermicelli noodle spring roll, pop's wings, #69 ginger shrimp, and #64 country beef. If you're two people, or very hungry. The shrimp alone is worth the trip. When you order these things, the server will be impressed, and say these are the house favourites.

Also get a cocktail! They are strong and delicious. We can vouch for the mojitos and the Mai tais. 

At the end of all that your bill will be embarrassingly small. Leave a nice tip for your server- they all seem to genuinely enjoy working there and it seems like a positive environment. I like supporting that kind of business!

I had always heard great things about this place but I was wildly disappointed. I think part of it for me is that I am 100% over the tiny BYOB where everyone inside is wasted and screaming at each other. This restaurant is TINY- about 30 seats? There had been a big party dragging their feet so a bunch of folks were outside waiting in the cold last no after their reservation times (including us). Once seated, my claustrophobia kicked into overdrive but I am willing to deal with a lot for great food. One of the most enjoyable dining experiences of my life was a restaurant the size of a large elevator in Portugal containing roughly 50 people. 

Unfortunately, the food was not great. In fact, mine was downright bland, boring, and poorly executed. I had the braised short rib ragu over polenta. Allegedly there was truffle and ricotta in there somewhere but I caught not even the tiniest whiff of either. The polenta was chunky and lukewarm, not creamy. The sauce was so bland I had to ask for a salt shaker. The meat was well-braised, but overall the dish just fell so flat. Husband got the famous lobster pyramid pasta and it was excellent- I was very jealous. He very kindly offered to switch but it felt unfair so I declined. I had previously had my eye of the 'nduja bolognese but saw it come out to the table next to ours looking more like a bowl of soup than a pasta dish. You could've gone for a swim in there. 

Maybe it was an off night. Maybe they're resting on their laurels. Maybe people drink enough here to not taste the food much (it certainly sounded that way). Who knows? I won't be returning to find out. The prices were also kinda steep for unimaginative and pedestrian food. $18 for a grilled octopus app? GTFO wit dat.

In honour of my newly-won Duchess title, I thought it would be a good time to post a review update.

I love this place. It is the breakfast spot everyone needs to have in their rotation - a place where you can go by yourself on any given morning, belly up to the bar, and have a fantastic, affordable breakfast while chatting with friendly regulars and the lovely staff. I come here by myself all the time, and often find myself making excuses to go get something done with my car at Pep Boys and then come over here to wait. 

People who say it's hard to find parking in this neighbourhood... don't know how to park. There is ALWAYS parking within 1 block of their doorstep. Also, do you see that massive parking lot for Pep Boys right across the street? Yeah, you can park there too. Even without that resource, there's plenty of legit street parking nearby. 

I almost always get either an omelet or a breakfast sandwich, and they are both pinnacles of culinary perfection. Nothing cures a hangover like one of their breakfast sandwiches. I usually double-down on the carbs and order a side of home fries with the sandwich, because this place does home fries right. Well-seasoned, GRIDDLED shredded potatoes. None of that deep-fried potato chunk business. Those are not home fries. The tater tots are also a good look - they are seasoned with some kind of magical blend and they are super addictive.

Aside from the breakfast stalwarts, they have more creative items like bacon-stuffed pancakes and salted caramel french toast, plus specials that will knock your socks off with flavour and originality. This past weekend I shared that caramel french toast and an eggs benedict special that was supposed to come with red miso ham, but they had run out of the ham, so they let us sub in curried pork from another special. Holy cow, it was delicious. Perfect hollandaise sauce and the eggs were expertly poached. The french toast was out of this world, I only wish it had more of that delicious bourbon whipped cream. The salt really came through with the caramel and it was awesome.

I could seriously go on for days about how much I love I have for Grubhouse. There's rarely, if ever, a wait for a table, but if there is and you spy a spot at the bar, don't be shy! Those are the best seats in the house. The baked goods are all fabulous and made from scratch by the stunningly fabulous Susan, resident server extraordinaire. Don't leave without picking out something for later, you won't regret it. Coffee, both hot and iced, is always delicious and your bill will feel criminally inexpensive. Go out of your way to support the little guy and you won't regret it!

I came in at around 4pm on a Friday while killing time for a friend to get off work. It was dead, but I was perfectly happy with that because all I wanted was air conditioning, a great drink, and a quiet place to flip through my new Harper's Baazar. B&B delivered on all fronts! I asked the bartender which of their cocktails were the most refreshing and he suggested the one with ginger beer, can't recall the name, before he offered to make me a Mai Tai. That man must be a mind reader, because I had been thinking about Mai Tai's all afternoon!

It was seriously potent, and delicious. I was pretty buzzed just from the one drink. They didn't seem to mind my being there just chillin with my magazine, and all was well in the world. I will be back for sure.

Oh, the Mai Tai was also a crazy-good deal. $10, when the rest of their cocktails were priced around $12 or $14 if I remember correctly.

I've had good experience with Roberto's downtown and this location is just as good. I was really excited to see that they opened a location closer to me, and even better that they added a drive-thru! The downside, however, is that prices here are more expensive than the ones downtown. On the upside, this location is like three times bigger, clean, and friendly. There's people constantly coming in, so at least it shows people are interested. As for the food, it's great. I got a torta and it was filled with plenty of meat. The tacos here are also very good - especially on Wednesdays, when they're half price. The salsa bar offers good options. Overall, a great improvement but I would have liked to see the prices remain the same. I'm definitely coming back.
Everything at Lee's is SO GOOD (and cheap and fast) all the time. Great options for vegans, vegetarians, and carnivores alike. Definitely get the Dijon sauce.

Dear Pho Viet, or AKA Beef Pho Baby. Thank you for keeping your dining room open, you were our last hope! So many pho restaurants are still take-outs only and as a true pho-eater, I have been distressed and anxious for months until I discovered this place. When I saw that they had the dining in option, I still doubted it (sorry Yelp! COVID-19 made me distrust information on the web, even the Yelp a bit) so we had to call to make sure they were truly open. Our family of four made our way down from New Tampa to Brandon just to enjoy noodles. Yes, send NOODs like my daughter's t-shirt with noodle bowl picture says! Instead, we went to get NOODs. The restaurant was very busy with the Sunday lunch crowd. They only had two servers (one of them may have been a manager, even) but they handled us all like pho serving champs they were.  The pho bowls were ordered and delivered back to our tables within 10 minutes, which is one of the many things I love about ordering pho. Super fast! The broths just  hit the right spots in all of us. I ordered seafood pho and the rest of the fam ordered their beef brisket pho noodles, including our youngest one. She was given a choice of Kids pho noodles for $4.99 which lovingly was annotated as "Beef Pho Baby." 
I think I may have to change my Instagram handle to that. Thank you!
Spread the word, this place is open!

Surprised I haven't reviewed this market before, it's fab!!  They make you feel like family.  The seAfood counter has fresh options you sometimes  can't get at the grocery store.  They have made entrees for grab and go, a meat counter, spices, coffee and Italian staples.  They do catering or trays for pick-up and special holiday menus too.  My favorite 4 areas are the fresh pasta, bakery, wine room with tastings and cheese "cave."  It can be very busy, especially around holidays with long lines.  They have a home goods store located in the parking lot.  They have a "coffee bar" and sandwich counter.  They also hold classes..   Enjoy!!

A group of us went out for my co-workers birthday.  Based on the St Pete Times review and because we like to try the new places in St Pete we headed to Brick & Mortar.  We arrived around 8:30pm and it was busy with only a couple of tables open, keep in mind it is pretty small (and very, very loud).  We were able to get a table put together for 5. We decided to share some of the small plates and ordered 4 dishes for 5 of us thinking we would order more if needed . . . octopus special, onion tart, flatbread and I don't even remember the last dish (must have been really good, ha).  While the octopus and onion tart had decent flavors they were some of the tiniest portions I've ever been served.  

The flatbread came out a while after the other dishes (we'd actually finished all 3 other items) . . . it was a decent size for sharing, however when we started to break it apart we found a BUG crawling on the micro greens.  We remained calm and told a passing server who saw the bug and grabbed the plate.  She said we won't charge you for that, really, I'd hope not.  There was no real apology, the owner stopped at our table and said everything here is organic and no pesticides are used so sometimes there are bugs . . . this is a restaurant and there should be quality control.  We were grossed out and asked for our check.  When we received it the flatbread was still on the check, in fact our server did not even know of the problem so we had to ask for it to be taken off.  Unacceptable in my opinion and no try for recovery or care in the world to do anything that would bring any of us back.  It is unfortunate because we work downtown, we work someplace that influences others decisions on where to dine and we told people that this place is a miss.

We were excited to try it; however based on the bug, lack of recovery and meh service I will not go back, my friends won't be back and it won't be a place we recommend.

I live in st Pete and I would drive all the way to Tampa if I could every day for this place! Not only is it the cutest spot ever (perfect day or night date spot) but the doughnuts are amazing, I'm so glad it's not close by or I'd be a million pounds.

There are so many amazing flavors to try from. The coffee beyond exceeded my expectations, talk about deliciously addictive (not too sweet, not too bitter!)

The customer service was fantastic, the ladies here are sweet, warm and welcoming! Plenty of seating and once you sit down and look around you'll feel like you've been transported to a far away magical candy land

A small market located at a corner. Easily accessible! Nice selection of kombucha! Nice selection of sushi and pre made food such as roasted chicken and Mac and Cheese. 

What's really cute about this place is how they sell New Orleans festive products like Korbel Champagne with a Mardi gras label on it. Coffee Flavored King Cake. Nice selection of fresh veggies too!

Basically this store will carry your basic needs. The staff are very friendly. It is a small grocery store. Don't expect a lot of space in the aisle.

Rustic place. Don't expect fancy. Expect good beer. ;) We just came for the beer.
Stout: nice dark color. Had a nice sweet after taste.

My friends had some of their sours and they were all good.

(One had a hibiscus sour, coconut, grapefruit, and one had a IPA... I had a sip of each one. And they were all good!!!)

Not much choices for food here. They have a gal ready to serve a vegetarian mac&cheese and vegetarian sushi. Didn't try it because we were just here for the beer.

Don't come here for comfort. Come here and expect rough edgy style. The bathroom. The chairs. The tables. All the furniture are basically being repurposed. 

Come here for the beer. It's good!

Oh New Orleans got me walking! Glad this coffee house was right here. Plugged my dying phone. Took a potty break. 

And had a lovely Tall Cold Brew. Black! No creame. No sugar! Black!

Probably the best cold brew I ever had. It was heavy on the ice or did I just sipped it too fast. Next time, I'll ask for a side or ice.

What made this drink so special is how lovely the flavor was. It has a nice see sweet floral coffee taste. Very smooth! It was lovely.


Plenty of seating area and good places to plug in your device to recharge. Lots of choices of coffee beans to take home. 


Definitely a blessing to had the opportunity to stop by at this coffee house!

Located at a corner by the Garden District. Since I really had to use the restroom, I had to purchase something first before using the restroom. There was a sign on the door, restroom is for pay customers only.

Glad they had a refreshing Diet Coke in a can here. I didn't have to a wait for my drink.... Paid it. Left it at a table and used their restroom.

I didn't have their coffee. I only experienced sitting in the coffee shop to drink a soda. And I used their single stalled restroom. 

Staff were nice. The soda was pricey. It was almost 2bucks for that can.
Lovely inside. They had a mini gift area.

A hidden gem... A local told us to come here. And I am glad we did... Located in Bacchanal in front of an abandoned Marine Navel Base that is just falling apart since Katrina filled with graffiti.... Here stands this lovely restaurant that is alive with music, twinkling lights, wine, beer, spirit, and amazing cheese plates that you will create!!!

Came here to drink and check out what this place has to offer. As you open the door inside, your jaw will drop how beautiful this place is!!!! Adorn with twinkling lights with various wines to choose from a fridge filled with various types of cheese. This is the place to be!!!!

Alot of history this place has to offer especially after Hurricane  Katrina hit. This place was a place for hope. From being just a backyard event. Being a place that was closed down because it didn't have a permit. People getting together to make sure this place stays open...  And it did. It got a permit and this place is packed. 

Live music. Plenty of tables that immediately fills up. And a 2nd floor that offers a balcony that looks over the backyard and the party!
The 2nd floor also host a private party. 

It's not cheap. It's on the higher end. A cheese plate with all the trimmings was $45.00. but so worth it especially if your a cheese lover!!!!

Down stairs there are buckets to place clean ice for your beverage or your wine. And there complimentary bug spray to keep those critters off you which is a common thing here in NOLA!

One thing that I do love is how the place continues to support it's community. They had a gal selling shirts, books, and DVD that supports the local shelter.

I hope you visit this place when you are in town!

Listen, if I didn't care about seeing this restaurant become successful I would absolutely make it my best kept secret. Sadly for me, I'd love to see this restaurant with a line out the door every day because they deserve it. The food is absolutely phenomenal and the staff is so kind. 

I have never been a huge fan of vegan food, but I would definitely become a vegan if I could eat food like this every day. No only was the Soulfood rich and delicious, but I didn't leave feeling as heavy as I normally would eating this kind of food. I felt full and refreshed. 

This place is truly worth trying. It won't disappoint.

Never again.

I took my wife out to the Melting Pot because she really loves Fondue. The food was okay, although there wasn't much of it considering I dropped over $120 on this meal. On service and food alone, this place merits three stars.

However, leading up to Valentine's Day I decided to make a reservation using the code they sent me via-email. I did this about 4-5 weeks in advance and called the first hour of the first day they were taking bookings. They said the best they could offer me was a 9pm seating on the 14th. I took it at the time, but the more I thought about it, the less enthralled I was about being in a restaurant at 11pm on a work night, a point of which, my wife agreed. We instead decided we'd grab some pub grub and see the new Die Hard movie, and postpone dinner until the next night when we went to The Bothy.

So I called them up several times. In most cases their line was busy--seriously, what restaurant doesn't have voicemail box, or a pay to just leave your number?--but after literally two weeks of trying to actually get someone to answer the damn phone, I got through and said I wanted to cancel. The girl on the other end said it was a pretty good idea that I did cancel because I wouldn't be able to enjoy a meal I'd be afraid I couldn't afford. Flabbergasted, I said that while we were going to the Bothy the next night and would be spending the same if not more, but that my reasons were none of her concern. She replied by saying "The Bothy? well there's no accounting for taste, is there sir?"

W.T.F. So I'm poor, or cheap, and have no class because I don't want to eat at a time when I'd normally be going to bed? Pfft.

I will never be back. My wife will never be back. We will both tell this insulting story to anyone we hear even thinking about eating at this classless dive.

WOW!!!!! What a great hideaway. Had lunch here today & what a surprise!!! 

Top Shelf Margaritas were AMAZING!!!  Not skimpy on the liquor at all & served in very large mug, not the little foo foo glasses..

Staff so friendly; felt like we've known them for a while!! All were efficient & Knowledgeable of entire large menu.

Chips & salsa(s) AWESOME!!! Hearty Corn Tortilla Chips with Green & Red salsa(s) that were both fresh, full flavor & just hot enough to make you want more!!! Staff never let the chips or salsa get too low!!

Plates were large with great proportions as well as prices so reasonable. FLAVOR throughout. I could actually taste ingredients without being smothered in sauces & cheese. Top Fresh Ingredients with just the right amount of spices. I had #4 Chicken Taco & Chile Relleno; LOVE IT!!! Beans were fresh tasting without the heavy oil taste.  My Sweety had #7 Chile Verde Steak Enchiladas; the meat so tender it truly fell apart in your mouth. I hate the frozen tiny squared pieces of vegetables in my rice that most places use; NOT HERE!!!! The rice was fluffy with fresh hand cut pieces of bell peppers, carrots & onions; I could make a meal out of that!

We never once saw any of the staff sitting or talking in a group. They were cleaning, dusting, doing dishes, stocking glasses, you name it; they were doing it. So impressed!! I thought one last place that is a tell- tell sign for me is the cleanliness in the restrooms; YEP!!!! Looked Clean, Smelled Clean & they even had hot water, nice hand soap & not so stingy paper towel dispensers!!! 

Anything that we would change??? NOTHING!!!!! Beautiful restaurant, Beautiful & Fun Staff!! Awesome Food & Cocktails!!! We loved it! We were so impressed with the quality of food that we asked if they catered & happily they said yes!!! Our daughter is getting married in June & we truly hadn't found that perfect Caterer. So we brought the soon to be Bride & Groom to dinner tonight & they LOVED IT!! We booked them tonight for the June Wedding!!!! Woo Hoo......

Talk about a Family owned establishment!!! I will certainly hand out business cards; I don't often do.... But I feel that GREAT about this place!!

This is a grocery store known for their great (&somewhat expensive) selection of goods. 

However, that does not give any right to racially profile a customer. According to the manager there were "many complaints" of a customer that was "stealing" a Hydroflask when in fact the item belonged to them... and they were putting it away in their backpack.

Didn't the customer pay for their items & have a receipt for it? ... Yes, they did. And yet, still stopped for "stealing" and just "needed to check" the young Mexican lady with all her bags walking quickly to catch a bus home.

I'm not from Tucson, and to be honest I had pretty low expectations for a boba joint in a city that appears to have low diversity (referring to Asians). But this place is amazing. The tea itself is legit. Along with the milk. I got a regular chatime milk tea (30% sweetness) and it was THE best original milk tea I have had. I'm incredibly surprised it beats all of the milk tea spots I've tried in Los Angeles. The milk tea at chatime really has the tea flavor that you can tell is high quality. The people behind the counter said they use loose leaf tea to make it which is demonstrated through the delicious flavor. 

I highly recommend this place for their milk tea as I can't comment on anything else, but I'll definitely be coming here often when I visit Tucson.

OPEN EARLIER PLEASE

EDIT (9/16/16): THIS IS SUPER IMPORTANT. They make their own toppings in house. The ginger tea comes from ginger they grate in the back. The banana milk tea comes from real bananas condensed in the back. Same with the strawberries, rose, etc. I thought this was ubiquitous to ALL chatimes but it isn't. I found a chatime in LA and was SUPER excited cause I thought they had the same menu as this Tucson one. bigmistake. The Chatime in LA had NONE. It was all artificial and fake flavorings. SINCE WHEN DOES TUCSON BEAT LOS ANGELES IN A BOBA CONTEST?!?!! The Tucson Chatime that this review is for seriously is amazing. I am in disbelief and disappointed that I only get to go to this chatime four days a year (but twice a day when I'm there).

EDIT (December 2017): Sigh. All good things must come to an end. As you've probably read, management has changed. I've gone there several times in 2017 (April, August, October and December) and the drinks have been pitiful each time. They no longer make ingredients fresh, the boba has been stale, and the workers are so unhappy. The staff in 2016 was absolutely amazing and proud of the drinks they made. The current staff must be Quickly employees sabotaging Chatime because they really don't want to be there. I got my usual Ginger Milk Tea each time I visited and it just isn't the same. Today there wasn't even Ginger. I'd avoid this place. I think Bing's will be my new go to. Goodbye once loved Chatime. RIP.

The sandwiches are the best subs available in Tucson, the wings are incredible, the sides taste good.

My quest to find a good sandwich near the university ended tonight.  I have been searching and sampling every sub place in a 5 mile radius of my house.  To my surprise, the best sub place was in walking distance of my freshman dorm.

The restaurant is made up of two main rooms, a bar-type room and a dining-type room.  The dining room has booths on the side and a big table in the middle.  The tables are plastered with old newspapers and the walls and ceiling are filled with various sports paraphernalia and Philadelphia souvenirs.  The whole restaurant has a very sports bar feel.

The one wait person I talked to was very nice and very friendly.  I obviously looked lost, coming in through the wrong door and scanning the place, trying to figure out what to do.  She asked me what I would like, and followed me to a booth to take my take-out order.  I had very many questions, and she happily answered them and gave her suggestions.

I ordered the Jimmy McKenna (turkey swiss LTO) for myself and the eggplant parmesan for the boy.

If you are not going to order an Irish sub and/or wings and/or sides, don't bother coming here.  The regular sandwiches are better at Silvermine and cost less.  The Irish subs have amazing bread.  It is slightly crunchy on the outside, chewy on the inside, and taste fabulous.  I devoured the sandwich before I was able to decipher which aspect I liked most.

Non-Irish subs just don't stand up to their Irish subs.

The boy's sandwich, the eggplant parmesan, was drowned in marinara sauce with a hardly noticeable eggplant.  After I picked out a piece and could actually taste it, I could tell that it wasn't fresh.  The bread also didn't have very much taste to it and there was nothing exciting about the texture.

Also ordered were 12 wings: the Shreiner wings, a mixture of BBQ and medium hot.  When I say a mixture, I do not mean that 6 are BBQ and 6 are hot.  All are the same flavor, and the flavor is a mixture of the two.  Awesome wings, better than Wings Over Broadway (which until now was my favorite place for wings).

The garlic bread was recommended highly by the waitress but this was not good.  The curly fries were standard fare.

Another upside to this place is that they deliver!  Wooo!!

The food is very good.  The sauces, curries, naan breads in particular are good.  The naan bread is the softest, most fluffy naan bread in Tucson.  The tandoori chicken is not at the same level.  The mango lassi, which is my favorite drink and will never hesitate to order one, is thick and tart.  It has a strong, strong taste of mango, not a sweet light taste that I prefer.

Service is fast when the restaurant is near empty, but this restaurant is hardly ever near empty.  So if there are a lot of people you will be waiting a long time before getting your check, or the other half of your meal, but your water glass will always be full.

The decor is hideous.  White and light green, glass table tops, white paper place mats.  The dining area is limited to one oblong room with a window facing south.  Each time the door opens a series of sun streaks sweep across the interior and onto everyone's faces.  It also gets quite loud making an intimate conversation difficult.

Our standard Indian cuisine includes a 1/2 order of tandoori chicken, shahi paneer, one order of garlic naan and two mango lassi's.  This comes out to $24 at most places, here this comes out to $29 (before tip).

I have given you enough chances, Magpies.  The last FOUR deliveries have been awful.

#1) Completely wrong order
#2) Forgot the herb seasoning, used regular instead of sourdough crust
#3) Gave ground meat instead of Italian sausage
#4) Burnt pizza

Magpies remains to be the best pizza delivery place in town.  But just not this Magpies.  There is absolutely nothing wrong with the Speedway/Country Club location, other than they won't deliver to my house.  For now, I'll just have to drive for my delivery pizza.

The coffee and scones here are amazing. When I lived closer I used to come here regularly and my husband always gets me a coffee and scone on my birthday and anniversary because it's MY FAVORITE. 

After what happened yesterday however, and I very rarely say this, I will not be back. My husbands mask broke and he was trying to fix it so it stayed in place and the staff behind the counter were extremely, extremely rude. 

I understand the emotion and fear behind Covid19, he was more than 10 feet away from the staff (behind plexiglass) and the say they spoke to him made me so mad.

After he left the building, I was standing behind waiting for the scone he ordered. The cashier stated: Um, is there something else you need? To which I replied "didn't my husband order a scone? Did we pay for it?" And they all just looked around like it was an impossible question. 

I was so uncomfortable I said don't worry about it and then they placed the scone in a bag and just put it on the counter. I know we paid for it and they did not even apologize.

I've never left somewhere feeling chastised and embarrassed but I was treated like a child and basically talked down to. I'm so, so sad to say this, but I will never be back. It was such an unpleasant/embarrassing experience. Wished it wasn't the case. Manners and grace go a long way.

Now that I've lived in New Orleans for over a year and a half (and visit this cozy restaurant every chance that I get), I feel compelled to update my review. Years after my first review, the oysters here are still out of this world. Fresh, plump, and local.  The same guy is there shucking oysters that I remember from my first visit, and happy hour still includes $.50cent oysters and half-priced cocktails from 3-6pm. 

My cousin came to visit, so her stay had to include an homage to Besh (my chef crush). Alas, no Besh sightings this time, but stellar meal and service all the same. We walked in with a reservation, were immediately seated, and quickly two servers joined us to take our drink orders, water preferences, and recommend starters. 

We started with the baked P&J oysters that came out piping hot, along with crispy pork belly with roasted Brussels sprouts and beets. Savory, herbaceous, briney, and delectable. We immediately wished we'd ordered more oysters. 

For cocktails, we both had the New Orleans streetcar - pear vodka, St. Germain and a little lemon. Light, but still with a kick. 

My cousin ordered the shrimp and grits, while I ordered the moules et frites. Big, sweet Gulf shrimp in savory sauces over creamy grits. Ginormous portions of mussels with a light, garlicky wine broth and perfect, salty frites that we couldn't stop eating. 

Now, THAT was a meal.  See pics.

This particular location, though possibly the busiest, is my favorite. The people here are wonderful. 

Whether I show up with a group, or I stop by alone to eat at the counter, the staff here are incredibly friendly. Most of them even remember me and my friends that come to visit. 

I love the Migas plate. Eggs scrambled with chorizo atop tortilla chips and with melted shredded cheese. The plate also includes sliced fresh avocado, pico de gallo, and a chipotle sour cream. I'd like to get a side of bacon. The bacon is cooked perfectly, and it isn't too salty. The coffee is a local brand, it isn't too bitter or too strong. I always get a cup to go when I leave. 

If you don't like waiting or dealing with crowds, my friends and I will often plan to arrive right when they open on a Saturday morning at 8am. However, I would definitely tell you that this place is worth a wait. 

See pics!

Best brunch spot for a pre baseball game day adventure!!  The food is amazing and the staff in top notch.   If you are looking for a great place to get a drink or a bite before or after a game this is the place for you.

My girlfriend and I went for our first time tonight and our experience was shocking seeing as we didn't make it more than 5 feet from the door before we were confronted by who I'm assuming was the owner/manager who wanted to know if we were there for the show. We told him we came for beer and BBQ and was informed, in a very rude manner, that this was NOT a restaurant, but a music venue with a cover charge, and we would have to take ourselves outside to eat..... WOW. This guy must have failed How to Treat A Customer 101. 

Still somewhat taken back by how unwelcoming this guy was, we decided to not spend any money on drinks here and instead just ordered BBQ and ate outside.

The kicker... when we went to bring our empty BBQ plates back in, we didn't make it inside because he opened the door, took the plates, and shut it before we could step in to see about washing out hands. 

It's a shame to see places that look like they have great potential literally turn away customers in their tracks because of unfriendly and outright rude management. Won't be back.

LOVED MAYPOP!!!! I absolutely love Thai food and the Thai- southern mix was something I'd never heard of before and it didn't disappoint!!! 

Service was great and helpful in us choosing which we wanted. They also were kind enough to do a substitution for me of shrimp and oysters without an extra charge on a dish. We got complementary appetizers and a desert taster from the kitchen and both were INCREDIBLE. Such a classy touch and we will definitely be going back because of that kindness and customer service. The chefs were also out in the dining area saying hello and thanks to patrons. 

The lunch and dinner menu are different and I felt the lunch menu was a bit limited. I hope as they expand their menu does as well! 

Loved MAYPOP and it TRULY deserves 5 stars.

Wow, I am so impressed with this place. The Mr. discovered it a few weeks ago when he was working in the area and found it via Yelp. He told me that he had one of the best vegan cheeseburgers he's ever eaten. 
Fast forward to a couple of nights ago we decided to make the drive out and go for dinner. Sure enough, I ordered the vegan cheeseburger as did he. We also got tater tot's, fries, and I got the vegan ice cream sandwich. 
The vegan cheese burger was so good! I agree with the Mr. in that this is definitely one of the best tasting the vegan cheese burgers I have ever had. The patty was thick and so flavorful, the caramelized onions were smoky and perfect. The bun held together well and was mild enough in flavor so as not to take away from the yummy taste of the burger itself. 
Also, this place is decorated and laid out so cool! There's an area for kids and dogs, as well as an adults only area. We chose to sit in the adults only area, which I really appreciated that there weren't little children running around. I love kids, but I don't always enjoy dining in the presence of them. 
This is right on the beach so you've got a beautiful view. There are plenty of picnic tables and even a nice big fire pit you can sit by. 
They have a regular menu and then a vegan menu. I'm looking forward to going back, I already have my eyes on the nachos for next time !

I found mesa burger via Yelp when I searched for vegan food options in the Santa Barbara area. I have only eaten there once so this review is based off of that visit. 
I was with my daughter as we were returning from a mother-daughter trip to the Madonna Inn in San Luis Obispo. We were hungry and wanted some thing good on the way home. 
Mesa Verde is pretty small and the parking lot is quite limited so keep that in mind. But that is really the only "con" about this place. 
I was happy to see that they serve the hungry planet vegan patty which is probably my favorite vegan patty! I ordered a burger, fries, and iced tea and everything was totally on point! 
The food came out pretty quickly and I feel like the prices were reasonable. 
My daughter got a pasta and sweet potato fries which she said was absolutely delicious (as she wolfed down her meal). 
I wish this place was closer because I would definitely eat there more often. 
I do want to go there again soon and try the burger with a few other toppings and get one of their beers on tap.

Found this place on yelp as I was interested in a crunchy granola cafe to have lunch at. The menu looked good so I decided to give it a try. 
They have lots of vegan options. Everything is GF.
I ordered the pulled mushroom burger. 
The mushrooms were good but the spread was not fitting flavor wise, and the bread totally did not go. The mushrooms were bbq flavor and the bread was a very thick sprouted seed filled dry thing. 
Burger came w a side salad which was arugula and pickeled onion-that was good but lacked enough dressing.
I also ordered the mint choc matcha- which was somewhat bland. 
Ordered a few vegan desserts, the brownie was pretty good and a matcha choc ball which I haven't tried yet. 
Overall it's a cute little cafe w plenty of options for vegans, but the flavors and value just didn't knock me off my socks.

Long story short, I was disappointed with La Fourno.

The Mrs and I arrived for our reservation and were met, by name no less, by the host, and sat immediately. He asked us if we were using any promotions, and we gave him the Groupon that we were indeed using. Right off the bat, La Fourno deviated from what was on the Groupon. There were options on the Groupon that weren't available at the restaurant. That immediately put me off, but we decided to push on. When the host saw our bottle of wine, he informed us that BYOB is only on Tuesdays and Fridays. It was $20 to open our bottle. Ugh. Anyway, we went with our new Groupon options; I got the Caesar salad while the Mrs got the soup de jour. In what turned out to be a running theme, the Caesar salad wasn't exactly a Caesar salad, but the wife enjoyed the soup. For the second course, we got what the menu says is a "margherita pizza," which every where else on Gods green earth is a pizza with sauce, fresh mozzarella and basil. At La Fourno, a margherita pizza is a cheese pizza. The pizza was very good, but seriously, it was a cheese pizza. The entrees were the Pollo Valdostana, which is a boneless chicken breast stuffed with prosciutto & fontina cheese & finished with portabello mushrooms & sun-dried tomatoes in a marsala wine sauce and a Pollo Salsiccia; boneless chunks of chicken sauteed with sweet Italian sausage, mushroom & sun-dried tomato in a balsalmic reduction. Both chicken dishes were way overcooked and chewy, and I couldn't taste ANY of the fontina cheese. And for all that, the bill was over $70.

The only real upside was the service. Our water glasses were dutifully filled, and our waiter was personable and professional. 

I could see myself getting a pizza from La Fourno, but I really don't see myself going back here for anything else. The veal parm is supposed to be the best around, but I'm not willing to gamble that $28 based on my first experience.

My first trip to New Orleans would not have been complete without coming to Drago's for the charbroiled oysters. I had intended to take my friend out for a birthday dinner, but alas, they are closed on Sundays. We came in the next day for lunch before we headed home. Parking was not an issue for us because we came early but it is indeed a tight space. 
Walking in, we were immediately greeted and welcomed. The gentleman guided us to the dining area. You get a view of the open area where the cooks are busy grilling up the famous charbroiled oysters. He takes us to a huge dining area. Huge. I can only imagine how crazy this place would be for dinner. We were seated and our waitress promptly came over to introduce herself and get us started. 
I started off with ordering a half dozen charbroiled oyster because my friend has never had oysters before. What was I thinking? I could eat a dozen by myself easily. It came out shortly and I nearly gulped. The oyster were still sizzling with the garlic butter in the shell it was cooked on. With a bit of lemon juice squeezed on top, the first bite was heaven. The bread was used to dip in the garlic butter. Do it. Oh and my friend? Love it! 
We also ordered a shrimp po'boy to share because we weren't too hungry. Luckily we did because the sandwich was huge and came with fries. I wasn't too fond of the shrimp. I'm a shrimperman's daughter. Those were not fresh shrimp which surprised me because we are in Louisiana right? Very disappointing. 
I'm still thinking of how good those oysters were and kicking myself for not getting more but we were on a time crunch. No future trips to NOLA will ever exclude a trip to Drago's for those wonderful charbroiled oysters!!

Ok so there's this breakfast sandwich on the menu...Hot Chicken & Honey Butter French Toast Biscuit. Get that! It is a fried chicken thigh seasoned beautifully, topped with a pat of honey butter, and nestled inside a fluffy, sweet biscuit. I was so excited for this sandwich! I knew I would like it and I was not disappointed. I am a big fan of sweet and savory and this breakfast sandwich hits the mark and so much more.

The biscuit is buttery with a sweetness that is not overpowering. It is tender and fluffy on the inside and is toasted to create a slight caramelized exterior which makes it perfect as a sandwich bun. I love that the chicken is a thigh instead of the typical chicken breast which can be dry when not cooked well. There is just enough breading which is seasoned really well. You get a bit of the hot chicken taste that balances with the sweet notes of the biscuit and glorious honey butter. 

I also tried a few of the donuts. They rotate their flavors and I was really hoping to try the Vietnamese coffee one but unfortunately it was not a featured flavor for that day. I opted for the Christmas King cake that was recommended by the staff. It was really sweet but that should have been expected with the colored sugar on top. The cream cheese filling was sparse and I found the texture of the donut itself was too dense for my liking. 

I went back the next day to bring some of those chicken biscuit sandwiches home, four to be exact, to share with family. I also picked up the turtle cheesecake donut and cinnamon roll to try. The turtle cheesecake was like the other donut. The filling was lacking and texture was dense. The brûlée topping on the cinnamon roll didn't work for me. I'm just not a fan of their donuts, but I can eat the heck out of those chicken biscuits! 

The employees were fun, energetic, and very welcoming. The atmosphere was hip and lively with an industrial building vibe. They have a few tables for dine in with alternating ones blocked off for social distancing. I was also told they have patio seating in the back. You order online for take out and there's a place on the wall to simply pick it up. They also offer lunch and dinner and I plan to try the sliders. Definitely a place I will have to go to the next time I'm in town!

Stopped in for a quick bite after the Hop On Hop Off city bus tour. It stops right at the French Market which is where this was located. The band was playing great Jazz music. I saw a lot of people just having drinks and enjoying the music. We were starving so we ordered the jambalaya and half a muffuletta. My friend also got a Long Island iced tea and it was delicious! The rice in the jambalaya was a bit over cooked but had a really good flavor. The muffuletta was delicious and served warm. Service was awesome. Our waiter saw our lost looks because we weren't sure if we just sat ourselves as it was just an open cafe. He came over and took very good care of us. He was very personable and accommodating to not only us but everyone around us. I wish I could remember this name. Lively atmosphere, friendly staff, good food, great drinks!

A little history about Cafe Napoli:

Cafe Napoli is a family owned restaurant, established in 1989 by Tony and Kathy Pietoso. Quickly becoming a success, they moved the small basement restaurant to a larger location at the corner of Forsyth and Bemiston in the heart of Clayton. In 2003, sons Ande and Kye expanded their family restaurant by adding Bar Napoli, a swank cocktail lounge. A few years later, Napoli Reserve was added onto Bar Napoli allowing for private event space and an additional bar and lounge for the weekends.

After years of a flourishing business, Kathy and Tony decided to take their ventures West to Town and Country where they opened their second location, Napoli, managed by Ande. Kye has taken the reigns from his father and is now the front man for the 8,000 square foot establishment in Clayton.

Cafe Napoli and Bar Napoli have recently undergone a face lift inside and out. Inside the kitchen, Executive Chef Chip Bates was added to the team, bringing fresh ideas and innovation to the regional Italian specialties. 

Food:
Calamari Fritti - $9.50. Large portion size. Delicious!
Bruschetta di Pomodori - $7.50. Fresh ingredients and one of my favorite appetizers here.
Caesar salad - $9.50. Was pretty close to the traditional caesar dressing that is made with garlic and anchovies. However, not over powering and tasted smooth.
Veal Marsala - $13. De-Lish-Ous! This dish won me over immediately. The meat was tender and cooked to a perfection. The sauce was delicious.

Service:
Excellent service from our waiter. Attentive to detail, came around and checked on everyone at the table. 

Ambiance:
Upscale and classy. Nice place to take clients or dates. 

Overall:
Be prepared to spend a little more than your average budgeted dinner spot. Prices here are slightly higher, particularly on their wines. Nothing really spectacular, but a good experience overall.

I've been to this restaurant a handful of times, both for take-out and dining in, and received mediocre service as I watched others receive different treatment. I choose to give them the benefit of doubt each time. As the only woman of color when in this establishment, I couldn't help but wonder if the lack of customer service that I received each and every time I visited this place was because of lousy service or my skin color.

Tonight I went in to simply order two cheese slices. The dismissive man at the register took my order. I waited for about twenty minutes, to get my food. After waiting for a while, the man at the register asked me if I wanted my two slices warmed. I wondered why he assumed I would want cold pizza. I asked for my money back. The man gave me my money back without being apologetic. It was confirmed that this is a racist establishment.

Great neighborhood deli! I recommend calling ahead as the wait times are sometimes long. My favorite hoagie is the Game Over cheesesteak which is a chicken cheesesteak topped with spinach and shrimp. I come here when I want something delicious and artery clogging.

Like a woman who goes on too many failed first dates, where the man usually ends up being a) older than his profile picture (bald patches on the head and groin don't lie); b) *portlier* than what he's led me to believe (AVERAGE BUILD does not mean turning around in a restaurant and knocking the wine glasses off of everyone's table that's within a 10 feet radius); c) *more depressed* than what his profile insinuates (becoming maniacally jovial after 10 shots of "the hair of the dog that bit me" doesn't count)  - I approach Italian restaurants with undeniable dread.  And although, at the end of the date/meal I vow NEVER AGAIN, somehow a month later I'm back with some self-professed Jabba da Butt or Long Schlong Ranger.  And if I'm with these people in an Italian restaurant...it's time to assume a fetal position.

Ended up here, as friends on the suggestion of some friends (it's their anniversary spot).  Converted from the previous Anthony's, aka. Your Myopic & Senile Grandma's Living room - the one who likes to collect dentures and balls of twine, Vivace has livened up the space considerably with warm colors and down-to-earth decor.  We were in the larger "sunken" room, and the acoustics were terrible - I couldn't even hear my jawbones as I was chewing.  It was Vivace's first "real" opening night at their new location, and we were assured things would be upgraded in the coming days.

The food was...quite ordinary.  I had the pork chop Parmesan which came with a side of pasta.  The pasta was wonderful, al dente, the pork was just OK.  Other dishes included stuffed shrimp, which was pretty yummy, but nothing extraordinary.  The antipasti plate was huge and good.  Thinking back on the other Italian restaurants I've been to, Vivace wasn't particularly inventive, nor extraordinary.  The food was just solid.  Cocktails above average (had an old fashioned).

The service, however, was effusive.  Our server had been working at the restaurant for a while and knew our friends.  He was attentive and considerate - our water glasses were always filled.  

The only reason why this is not the three stars Vivace deserves - when I had a wine glass with a very noticeable lipstick stain on the rim sent back, the glass was returned...WITH THE STAIN STILL ON...albeit slightly more smudged.  I'd expect an (expensive) place like this to have way more class than to do a half-assed job of wiping down the glass instead of dumping everything into a clean one.  Seriously?  Like that date with Jabba da Butt, don't think I'll be back anytime soon.

Sometimes you just gotta leave your frou frou fra fra pretense at home, take a deep whiff of tasty garlic-infused food from the packed parking lot, and plunge into the ex-converted drive-in burger joint in the middle of nowhere that is known as Wild Garlic Grill.  

If you do this, you will be greeted with some of the best food you've ever had...anywhere.  Wild Garlic was a total surprise.  Wednesday night, with half of Tucson dead, Wild Garlic was packed, so we could only sit at the bar...

...which is highly recommended.  At the bar, you'll witness the genius of the Chef as he single-handedly personally prepares ALL of the food - about a dozen concoctions going on at any one time.  It was like watching a cooking automaton.  For the entire 2 hours we were there (and we eventually *happily* missed our movie and opted to watch the show behind the bar counter instead), the Chef didn't stop, pounding out one dish after another.  

We split the grilled seabass entree and had the beet salad, wild mushroom soup and garlic shrimp.  Apparently, at 6:45pm at the counter it was Happy Hour and all glasses of wine were $2 off, and well drinks -$3.  From the solid drink list (none of that Basil-Greco-Pomegranite-Lemon Martini Drop crap you get at trendy restaurants), I had a solid Old Fashioned and a Sidecar, which were well done.  With better spirits and ingredients, they could've rivaled cocktails at any old boys' club watering hole.

The soup and shrimp were wonderful - a meal in themselves (both were hearty, and we saw them blasting our brie for the shrimp with the flamer, which made it all the more exciting to ingest).  The beet salad was just OK.  The sea bass had a great combination of flavors.  

If you're as excited about gorging on good food as I am, sitting at the counter and watching the chef and his assistants at work are a must.  The service we received at the counter was also awesome.  Our bartender/server always made his rounds to make sure all diners were attended to (there were probably about 10 seats at the bar), in addition to making drinks for the entire restaurant and helping with prepping the food.  

Coming from Seattle, I've also no problems with the price... $14.00 for a dinner ENTREE?  Honey, we could pay that easily for a coffee, green eggs and ham breakfast any day.  

The only *suggestion* I'd have to this restaurant is its decor.  Something between your grandmother's living room and one of those shows where the designer goes in to rehab somebody's design nightmare.  Not expecting the color of the walls and servers' uniforms to match, but something more befitting of the great dining experience.

If you can't get into the more famous beignet place down the road, this place sells them too, with just as much powdered sugar. The outdoor lanai had live music going all night, with a very lively atmosphere. I love that they also have jambalaya and other non-beignet food to order (unlike Dumonde which only serves beignets)...and oh the strongest mint julep you'll ever taste. Everyone will compare this to Cafe DuMonde, so here are all the differences:

-Credit cards accepted
-they serve alcohol
-they serve real food
-they serve other pastries too
-they have FORKS, knives, spoons...
-the servers are nicer here

Took an Uber here from downtown so we could buy prepackaged salads to eat during our convention-packed days. You know how it goes, you go for one thing and end up leaving with 57. It was the beginning of pumpkin everything season when I went in September but my suitcase was already at it's limit so I didn't buy too many of my pumpkin favorites here...but my favorites are:

Gluten free pumpkin pancake mix
dark chocolate sea salt almonds
ABC bars (almond butter cocoa)
dried tangerines
spices

On this trip I also got bananas for 19cents each, and nice looking fruits too. I threw them into my smoothies during the mornings and they were great for on the go snacks. 

Wish we had a Trader Joes.

Some local Reno folks recommended this restaurant to us for a lively place to dine for restaurant Mexican food that won't break the bank. So off we go. The lovely Isabel was our waitress. She handily took care of our rowdy bunch of 10. We dared even to walk in 35 minutes before closing. They accommodated us. She was a bundle of high energy. Sassy and fun. She didn't rush us out, but we are not lingerers. She provided great drink and food recommendations. She knows her tequila brands ;) 

The interior was colorful and vibrant. Family friendly vibe. Fun lively place. They have a small back parking lot. 

Onto the food. The meatballs in the albondigas soup had a spongy texture, but it did came out hot which is a plus. A bowl cost $5.75. The ground beef in the small plate taco platter ($6.95) was a bit dry, over cooked. It was understandable that it was close to closing time and possibly the food was what was left for the day.  The folks in our party enjoyed their plates. So I'm chalking up my experience as an anomaly versus the norm. I am apt to try this place out again and not so close to closing time.

This cafe is open 24/7 in the Peppermill casino. It is a wait service restaurant. It began in 1971  as the Peppermill lounge and coffee shop. As a hotel guest, I sure appreciated this being open in the twilight hours. The menu includes price burgers, salads, and sandwiches, American entrees, and Chinese food. The prices are higher than diner prices.  No late night discounted prices. 

The place was clean and our waitress was great. But a big old shout out to the Keno attendant. She was a sweetheart. For working the night shift, she was peppy and so darn helpful. It's been awhile since I played Keno, she happily talked me through it. She didn't pressure me to play more. 

The Food: 
I shared a cheeseburger and fries. It was ok, not bad at all. $15. The prime rib plate isn't served after 11 pm plus it's pricey at $32. The Conquest sandwich has been on the menu since 1971. It's a hot sandwich of roast beef, Chedder cheese, sauted onions and peppers, tomatoes, and thousand island dressing on grilled Parmesan sourdough $15.50. I'll earmark that sandwich for another time. There must be a reason it's been a menu favorite for close to 50 years.

One of my favorite food pleasures is a good ole Chicago dog. So when I was on Reno driving through downtown casinoville I noticed this joint, "Taste of Chicago". So off I go. In the end, the dog was decent but overall dining experience was unfortunate. 

We stepped in on a Friday 3:25 pm. The dining room is next to the bar in the next room. There was no one eating in the dining room. The bar was hopping though. A waitress come out from the bar area and sat us. The interior is basic. They have 2 pinball machines and arcade Ms Pac-Man. That was retro cool. 

We ordered the HH food special of the tavern pepperoni pizza $6 and Chicago dog $6.  27 minutes after placing the order, I asked the waitress about our food. She returns 6 minutes later to tell us it's coming. 3-4 minutes later, she returns to the table and presents a burnt pizza... no dog in sight. She asks if we want this one or a new one. Having been in the joint for over 40 minutes now with no food, I asked if we can be comped instead. I explained that we are traveling through and don't have the time for a re-fire. She says she'll check. She comes back with our Chicago dog and promptly says " good news, the pizza is at happy hour price".  Huh?!? Of course it is... the tavern pepperoni pizza is the advertised Friday HH special. HH is advertised as being Monday- Friday 3-6pm. I get it. I get it, the manager in the back is calling the shoots not her. The waitress was cordial and pleasant. So basically, my options are to pay for the burnt pizza or wait another lifetime for a redo which may or may not come out burnt with extra love from the kitchen. 

I split the Chicago dog with hubs. The dog was served room temp... odd. They use Vienna beef dogs, nice... but it wasn't served hot. We paid and took the burnt pizza to go. 

I'm one and done with this place. But I understand everybody's experiences is different. If you like Chicago dogs and/or pizzas AND have infinite time on your hands AND don't mind a 50/50 chance that your pizza will not be burnt  ... then try this place out for yourself.

First visit to this restaurant was tonight. The food was very good and the service was great. The problem I had was they were over capacity for COVID restrictions. There was not distancing between tables and they were seating groups more than 4. It did make me nervous eating there and I won't return.

Excited to fill the whole in my heart left by the closing of Peruvian Corner I decided to try Mama Irmas today for lunch.

I was expecting them to have a very cheap lunch special like almost every other Peruvian restaurant I have been to. Unfortunately there is not one nor a cheaper lunch menu. The prices are comparable to any other Peruvian places however the portions were much smaller. 

I ordered the Arroz Chaufa (Peruvian style fried rice) and the Parihuela (a seafood soup). The Arroz was similar to others I have had but certainly not spectacular. 

I want to precede this statement by saying that Peruvian style soups are one of my favorite dishes. This was the blandest one ever. No depth or really any redeeming qualities except being slightly spicy. 

The place is pretty small so I could clearly hear the owner SCREAMING at the waitress because my friend and I wanted an extra bowl so we could share the soup.  This is ridiculous especially after spending 30 dollars on lunch when we could have gone to Machu Pichu and had soup, salad, an entree, and a drink (all better quality too) for 6.99 a person.

Well, we now jokingly call this place "zero's". It was my good friend Maren's bachlorette party which she had called several weeks in advance to reserve the back room so we could all hang and converse and you do bachelorette-ish type stuff. We had planned to all eat dinner there, drinks.. the works. We give the password the hostess doesn't even smile just points to all of her friends in the bar area which we assumed they were waiting for us.

They say they were seated here.. wait, what? At some shoddily pushed together tables in the loud, crowded bar area... She tells the hostess she spoke to someone weeks ago and had reserved the back room. I swear the hostess was a robot "sorry, talk to your server" while Maren was still standing there she goes back to reading her book? Umm.. ok.

We talked to the server and get basically the same reply.. he said "Ya, well there's a minimum purchase for that"... not sure what you're implying? You have 10-12 professional and well dressed women who were planning on doing drinks, apps, dinner, the works. We decide to try and make it work.

The service is awful. The server only had one other table across from us which he waiting on intently (perhaps friends of his?) and yet we got next to no service. I understand this is a craft cocktail place and we all totally understand that it takes time to make the cocktails.. oddly enough, that wasn't the issue. Our DD just wanted a diet coke, it took 45 minutes, yes... FORTY FIVE minutes. We all had our cocktails and when I stopped and asked where her coke was he said "he rang it in awhile ago". Not sure if you have ever worked in the service industry but if someone has been waiting for the bartender to pour your coke for you... you step behind the bar, pick up the gun and push "diet". She asked for a refill several times and never got it. 

Almost everyone had ordered apps but we decided we didn't want to wait another 30 minutes to get our servers attention and perhaps another hour or so for dinner, especially since we were all seated so awkwardly. You think I am joking but it took an additional 45 minutes to cash out. 

Craft cocktails are expensive - we went in knowing that but their prices even exceeded what we were expecting. 

Just stay away. I love speakeasy's but they obviously don't care about their customers. I don't live in the area but hopefully I can save you all a headache.

Cheesecake stuffed snowballs?! Sno-La puts ALL snowball stands to shame! I do like Hansens, but instead of waiting in a super long line in the heat I rather make my way to Sno-La. Because I love chocolate and can't seem to ever try new flavors once I find a new love for one, I always get the same flavor - Beam Me Up Scottie (chocolate stuffed with peanut butter cheesecake)

Be prepared to pay a little more than your average snowball here. After all, it is a whole cheesecake stuffed in a cup. It's worth the extra bucks, treat yo self!

Went to PYT last night with some friends, and was really disappointed... I wanted to love you, I really did.

The service is pretty bad at this joint, and that's why it only gets a 2 in my book.

First off, it's really hard to figure out who is staff and who's a patron. I'm not saying to stick everyone that works there in a uniform, but maybe a cool name tag or something... It would really help.

The hostess is super-clueless and looks dazed. Quite frankly, I don't think she's ever been a hostess before. My friends and I weren't greeted at the door and just stood there for a while. Eventually, I figured out that the person standing in front us was the hostess. There seemed to be a small line to sit and eat, so I asked her if there was a list that I could put my name on. She told me no, but if I wanted to sit at the bar or walk around the Piazza there should be something opening up soon.

Every time a waiter or waitress walked by, she would ask them if there was a table open... Um, isn't it the hostess job to know that?

We didn't go anywhere, because we were afraid she would forget us... Seriously, She looks like she's high.

So, after a few minutes we get to sit down. The place is super cute, but the table we got was really rickety. Okay, fine... These things happen.

Our waiter comes over and takes our orders, and we have to repeat it to him a few times. It doesn't impress me that you are trying to memorize my order if you need me to tell it to you a few times over. Please just write it down, I'm okay with that.

We wait for quite a while to get Diet Cokes and water, we wait even longer for the food. 

Hey, is that my waiter sitting at a table outside chatting with friends? Oh yeah, it is... maybe that's what's taking so long.

I actually saw this done by a few members of the staff, and while I'm all about saying hello to people you know, you shouldn't be hanging out while on the job when it's packed. You wanna turn those tables around, get that line up front moving, and get more tips... don't ya?

The food was quite good, and this is the saving grace of PYT. I had the grilled cheese with bacon and boursin. It's downright amazing. The bread was crusty and buttery, the fillings were ample, it was really nice.

The downside to this is that it came to me kinda cold, and my onion rings didn't come at all. I had to ask for those from the totally different server that brought our food out. 

I really hate to see the work of a good cook ruined by a bad waitstaff.

So please Tommy Up, if you read this... Send your staff to waiter bootcamp or something, they need all the help they can get.

Ugh. PYT. 

Pros - delicious and creative burgers. Plus, alcoholic ginger beer. 

Cons - everything else. We had to wait 45 minutes, then another TWO AND A HALF HOURS before we got our food. Our waitress was very rude, probably because we were a party of 10 and she was guaranteed her 20% tip. Then, to pour salt into the gaping wound, she accidentally charged me $117 instead of $17 on my credit card. (Causing me to overdraft, but that is a financially irresponsible story for another day). When I pointed this out, she was rude, gave the least sincere apology I've ever experienced, and then just handed me $100 in cash. 

While my buffalo pretzel crisp and lasagna burger (don't judge, I split with a friend) were mighty delicious, I would never go back thanks to the service alone.

This place was really easy to find and really pretty inside, but the sushi was so-so. I went late the other night and it was empty so I got everything pretty quickly and service was good, I just had the California roll & the shrimp tempora and they were both alright but the best part was probably the desert I had the vanilla mochi which was very good. If i go back again it will be for the mochi ahaha.

Lovee the cheese fries here, and the 'Gremlin drink'. I come here after work sometimes since there open after 2am. It's kind of expensive for snacky-type food but when it's one of the only places around open after 2am (besides Lorenzos & sons pizza) then it makes it worth it.

The foods good, cheap and plentiful for the price you pay. My only complaint is no matter what time I come in here at it always takes forever for me to get my food, even if I only got like eggs, it takes forrrreverr. I feel like thats just a 'Philly-diner-thing', because most diners I go to in Philly always take forever for me to get my food, it's not like that in New Jersey, but in NJ the food is also a lot more expensive and you get a lot less, so it gives and takes I guess. Besides it always taking long to get served everything else here is good.

When my guy and I were looking for something tasty in Indianapolis, we didn't expect to pull up to a strip mall and find Thai Taste. Unassuming, hole in the wall, and every other cliche small business saying would describe this spot. Aesthetics aside, service is great and the food is good. 

What's great about Thai Taste are the extra little touches they put into things. Plating is actually quite beautiful compared to your standard grab & go Thai place. Also, the adorable rice shapes! There's nothing better than getting rice shaped like a heart or star - so cute and put a smile right on my face. Even when we sat down the owner said I get the special pink menu while my fella got some other boyish color, ha! 

I had their lime chicken ($12.95) which was great but could have used slightly more lime sauce. It wasn't a huge portion for the slightly pricey tag but it got the job done. It had some seaweed topping which was an interesting touch and added some salt to the flavor which was nice. I also had some of my guy's Mango Chicken ($11.95) which was slathered in sauce. It had so much sauce I was dipping my dry pieces from my dish into his sauce. The mango chicken was packed with veggies and fruit pieces with small pieces of meat...not quite enough meat, but the flavor was sweet and delicious.

Service is more than accommodating at Thai Taste, food was good, prices were a buck or two too high for the portions, but overall we had a very good experience at Thai Taste.
