Most hipster coffee shop ever! And I live in Logan Square in Chicago so I know my hipster spots. Moving past the baristas with rolled up jeans showing an inch of skin and the wooden menu boards (this is the most amazing thing I've ever seen, by the way), Barista Parlor has some good offerings.

When you walk in, it's a bit more pristine than I've ever seen a coffee shop. Amazingly high ceiling with tons of light flowing in. Every seat perfectly positioned and I even saw them adjusting seats as people got up to keep the instagrammable symmetry. Not gonna lie, I took a pic and posted it on Insta. It had to be done.

Their drinks seem to change a bit with the seasons and they don't have a huge menu. But what they do have is really interesting! I enjoyed my latte quite a bit. Order at the register then they bring it out to you.

They have a few locations around Nashville and I went to the location in Germantown. Lovely spot, great atmosphere and a bunch of great food & drinks.

Laura's Candies is one of the best places in New Orleans to buy goodies for friends back home. I picked up some fun souvenirs for my friends and co-workers! Laura's Candies is NOLA's oldest candy shop, opened in 1913.

You can get the New Orleans treat of pralines here! A half dozen will run you $11.99 and they have a bunch of fun flavors including chocolate and the classic praline. Pralines are sugar upon sugar upon more sugar, but just delicious! They have some samples of each flavor you can try. For me personally, that was just enough pralines for my belly. However, I did end up buying a good amount for loved ones.

My friend and I actually popped into Laura's a few times and sometimes had great customer service, but once were ignored. 

Overall great little candy shop full of tasty treats! It's a bit pricey but well worth the lovely gifts you can bring home to give friends a taste of New Orleans.

While I was in Orlando, I skipped over Pat O'Brien's. I heard they were fun but knew it was some chain, not from Orlando, so just bypassed the joint. However in New Orleans, it was one spot I had to try because it DID start right in that city. At Pat O Brien's in NOLA, they invented The Hurricane and this has become their signature drink.

Pat O'Brien's serves their legendary Hurricane in a tall plastic cup with their branding on it. You can then easily take it out and walk around with it. However if you were counting on some fancy glass, you'll need to request that. It's a rum cocktail birthed during World War II when other hard liquors were in low supply. The Hurricane mix added is sweet & syrupy but I (surprisingly) rather enjoyed this cocktail. My friend insists they gave him a healthy pour as he got a bit buzzy off of one!

We ordered our drinks out on the back patio where the bartender moved through thirsty patrons quickly and was friendly to boot! We then sat out on the patio and had a great time chilling out in the breeze with our cocktails. They even have a gift shop out there so you can buy Hurricane memorabilia to your heart's content.

I know some people get the hand grenade at Pat O'Brien's but stay true to their game! Get that Hurricane and sip away on the patio!

Is it a donut!? Is it a croissant!? Is it an insane hybrid of the two!? Why yes, yes it is. Five Daughters does 100 Layer doughnuts or what you & I have come to know as cronuts. Not gonna lie, before coming here I just thought it was one of the fleeting foodie trends. After having it from Five Daughters, holy goodness! It's delicious!

They are a bit pricey at $4.50 but in my opinion well worth it. So soft (even the next day!) and such great flavor. One will surely fill you up. I actually do well splitting one with a friend so I'm not stuffed to the brim.

Flavors for the 100 Layer Doughnut are rotating but they have some staples like Chocolate, Vanilla, the Purist and King Kong (maple bacon). The rotating flavors though are a ton of fun with October options like apple crumble, cracker jack, S'mores, Huckleberry, Snowball, Pumpkin Spice, Pumpkin Chocolate Cheesecake and Cookie Dough! Call ahead if your heart if after something in particular though because they aren't guaranteed. I have tried the Cookie Dough, Chocolate Sea Salt (which is chocolate filled!) and King Kong all of which were so soft & well made with insanely good flavoring. I'm a cookie dough girl so for me that was perfection. I was very impressed how good the cronut...errr...sorry....100 layer doughnut tasted with no artificial cookie dough type flavors. Tasted like the real thing, baby. It takes them 4 hours to make 100 layer doughnut - wowza! The effort truly shows. I read this on their site "Weight for weight two 100 layer doughnuts weight about the same as 10 glazed krispy kreme doughnuts." Dang, explains why I can barely eat one of these things.

Five Daughters also has cookies, vegan donuts, and  paleo donuts. Not gonna lie, they looked great. But when faced with those options vs. 100 Layer Donut, I'm thinking I made the smart move. 

Can someone pleeeeeeeeeeease open a Five Daughters location in Chicago!? I'll love you forever!!!!

It's Bluebird Room without all the stress of reserving tickets but with all the same talent performing.

I had such an amazing time at the Listening Room - why are there not things like this in Chicago!? Seriously one of the best things I did on my last trip to Nashville. 

All of the singer songwriters on the night we went were incredibly talented. Some better than others and some just mind-blowing. My favorite of the night was Kyle Reynolds! Loved his acoustic boy band but way more talented vibe. 

Beer selection wasn't great but I found one that I stuck with for the night. And prices weren't bad. Also our server was super friendly and attentive which was nice.

While in NOLA, you must try a John Besh restaurant. Maybe two. And I know most go for August. I promise you though, Luke has damn good grub and will not disappoint. Everything we dined on at Luke was just delicious.

We went for the lunch as it was right near our hotel so it worked out quite well for us. They do a daily rotating special and if you're smart, you'll go on a Monday for the Tabasco Honey Fried Chicken for $17. The chicken was crispy and the tabasco honey sauce it comes with? Divine! It also comes with a good size helping of red beans and rice. A more than filling midday meal.

I also was able to try the Croque Monsieur $16 - you can make this into a Croque Madame, as well, which is simply adding an egg on top. The amount of ham was inches thick on this beastly sandwich. Drenched in gooey cheese, it was anything but a basic ham & cheese sammich. 'Twas a monster.

Service was just lovely from start to finish and the dining room was a chill, business casual type vibe. 

For good eats, with non-jaw dropping prices from a signature John Besh restaurant slightly off the main drag, check out Luke.

While in Nashville, it's all about the hot chicken. My buddy and I went on a bit of a hot chicken rampage while down in Music City and hit up many places. I'm sad to say Hattie B's was our least favorite of all the spots.

Hattie B's may be a good option for people looking for a more gentrified hot chicken experience - it's closer to the hub of activity, there is a clear set menu to order off of, it takes a while for food to come out but not nearly as long as some of the other spots and then of course the more hipster leaning clientele. Don't get me wrong, I love a hot bearded plaid wearing glasses sporting hipster as much as the next chick. But it doesn't add nor devalue anything to my hot chicken experience. It's all about the food for me!

I tried their tenders & on the bone chicken, as well as the pimento mac & cheese and red skin potato salad. I didn't have a bad bite - it was A-OK, absolutely fine, but there are just other places that are better in Nashville. Chicken wasn't quite as moist or flavorful as other spots, plus both sides we got can be skipped in my opinion.

Parking at Hattie B's is a bizznatch! And def factor in waiting in a long line to order, then more time for your food to come out.

If you need drinks in Nashville, Frugal MacDoogal is the spot. It's similar to Binny's for us Chicagoans. I made a stop here before driving home to pick up some local brews. I am a beer chick after all!

They did have a good selection of beer including a wide assortment of local suds. I was slightly sad they didn't have a mix & match six pack for $9.99 but they did sell a very small amount of bottles for $1.99-$3.99 each. I looked through things and found what I thought I would be best spending about $50 on various choices. 

If I had more time, they actually had a small tasting table with some drinks you could try out before buying. I was short on time though plus felt slightly strange drinking at 10am. Only slightly, no judgement! 

I was happy with the selection though it wasn't quite the plethora I was hoping for and prices weren't exactly frugal, just seemed like list price. I honestly may just stick to buying crowlers & growlers at various breweries I go to next time I'm in town because those were hella cheap.

If you are hungover as !@#$%^, don't go to Monell's for breakfast. I mean,the food is perfect for it, don't get me wrong. But you sit at a big table, mostly full of God fearing people, and you have to gather any bit of energy you have to engage in thoughtful conversation with complete strangers.This was rough. Real rough.Learn from my experience, kiddos.

That being said, everything at Monell's is great. You are served in a huge group family style and the food is bountiful beyond belief. There was so much food, we didn't even make a dent in some dishes! At a table of ten! It's hard to even mention highlights because seriously everything was so gosh darn good. Some of the items they had were: Smoked Sausage, Bacon, Biscuits and Gravy, Country Ham, Fried Apples, Pancakes, Scrambled Eggs, Hash Browns, Cheese Grits, Skillet Fried Chicken, Corn (my fav like a creamed corn), coffee, tea.....so many things! 

You can eat as fast or as slow as you like, but it's kind of awkward getting up from the big group. 

All in all, now knowing exactly how it is at Monell's, I'd def go back. But on a day when I'm completely with it and up for some friendly chit-chat.

Good pizza on Bourbon Street!? Who knew such a thing could exist!? 

Nestled between bars full of drunkards lies Crescent City Pizza Works. Basically, it's exactly what you need walking home at 3am after a long night. It's open until 6am every single day to serve the drunken masses! 

I don't know if it's because it was late at night and I was starving or because it's really that good, but my pizza slice was sent straight from the heavens to enter my mouth and reside in my tummy. The crust was crispy, ingredients tasted good, slice was large, I was 'bout that.

Service was what it was...could have been better but they packed our pizza to go so we could chow down in the hotel room and that's really all we needed. They had a few interesting combinations outside of the usual pepperoni, cheese & sausage and I loved that! I had their "Chicken Bacon Krunch" pizza and would highly recommend it to other slightly intoxicated New Orleans goers!

I loved Loveless!
#mesocheesy #tooeasy #ilovelove

If you've got some time to kill, head 30 minutes outside of Nashville to the Loveless Cafe. It's known by many in the area as having the best gosh darn breakfast in all of Tennessee! Yeehaw! And biscuits are their jam!!! (get it...? biscuits have jam on them...? sooo....biscuits and jam...? yeaaaaa).

The menu is so expensive it's nearly impossible to pick which delicies to scarf down. My usual thing is I want to try as many things as possible at new places so I went with the Biscuit Sampler Platter for $11.99. You can then choose 4 biscuits from: Fried Green Tomato & Pimento Cheese, Barbeque, Country Ham, Fried Chicken, Bacon, Sausage or Steak. I went with the Ham, Chicken, Sausage and Bacon because meat! All were good but let's be real, bacon makes everything better. Actually the plain biscuits with some jam preserves were the best thing of all - even better than my meat between the bread.

If you have to wait for a table, they have some cute shops outside the restaurant. Even if you don't have to wait, they are worth a stop in after dining. I bought a couple of floofy headbands for myself while there.

Loveless Cafe was a fun place to go, but the hype might have slightly exceeded the experience for me. I'm glad I went, think everyone everyone should go, but it's not a place I could see myself driving distances for again. Been there, done that.

Not gonna lie, most of what drew me in here was the name. It's all sorts of adorable! When my friend and I popped in, it wasn't very busy but there was a 20 minute wait for a table as they shifted into dinner service. 

Once we sat down, our server was incredibly nice, friendly & knowledgeable about the menu. My friend was happy they were playing NFL games, hurray. I was all excited to order my beer flight but WHOOPS! They don't do beer flights anymore. Our server explained they changed their beverage program but that was a bit disappointing for me. Also, their draft list was on one chalkboard far, far away next to a table so when you looked at it, you looked like you were staring at the patrons at the table. I could just barely read it when I zoomed in on my camera and am wondering what diners on the other side of the restaurant do. Me thinks that needs a bit of fixin'!

The place has some cool old photos as wallpaper which were fun to look at and made a great background for a couple of my pix. They were really nice about speeding things up for us a bit so we could make a show, too. 

So the food! We tried:
~Fried Cheese Grit Cakes $8 w/strawberry jalapeno jam - This was just calling my name from the menu like EAT ME! EAAAAT ME! And I ate it up. I'm happy to say it was everything I was hoping for with a crispy outside & smooth inside pairing really well with the jam with a touch of heat. I would highly recommend these - my favorite part of the meal.
~our beers were Little Harpeth Chicken Scratch $6 & PBR Tall Boy $3.50 - The Chicken Scratch wasn't bad for a pils...and the PBR, well, it was a PBR.
~Chicken Tenders $12 asked for chips, got fries - Fries were decent, the really thin style. They were pretty good and moist, just a tad dry when reheating my leftovers the next day but that's the way it goes. They had a good number of sauces to go with them!
~My bud had the hot chicken and said it was pretty darn good. He'd rather go somewhere like here and not wait then Prince's and wait 2 hours.

Overall, good food, great service, decent prices...but up your beer game, Party Fowl!

I popped in for their happy hour which happens daily - even on Saturdays! On Saturdays, happy hour is from 4-5:30pm in the lounge area. You can get a few $4 beers and a few discounted appetizers.

This was honestly one of the unhappiest happy hours though because our server did not seem to be in a good mood. We all have off days, so I'll try not to hold it against her too much. But my friend and I came in bouncing and bubbly happy. By the time we left, my buddy was in the crabbiest mood and he attributed it to the service. That's unfortunate.

That aside, Etch is a beautiful restaurant. The hosts were very friendly and I could see coming back here for a full meal. They have 3 beers on tap and during happy hour they do $4 drafts, however one was out. So...there were just 2 beer options and only 1 of the 2 was local...so....I had the Asgard Voyager. When I ordered it she seemed confused and I had to repeat it a couple times then finally point to it on the menu. If you have two beers on tap, know them.

Roasted Cauliflower $8 (normally $10 at lunch) - Loved this dish! Roasted cauliflower with a light truffle oil on it and a side of pea pesto with almonds, feta and red bell pepper sauce. Loved all of this and grabbing some cauliflower with the pea & feta was just divine! 
Cheese & Crackers $7 (same price at lunch) - Chilled blended Italian cheeses, tomato, arugula, pepperoncini vinaigrette, rosemary crackers...sounds good, right? Nu uh. We didn't like this dish at all. We ate about a third of it but the vinegar taste was insanely overpowering and it was a weird presentation. Nothing worked for us in this dish. 

If you want to try Etch and think you can actually experience it by going to their happy hour like I did, think again. Prices aren't really discounted, pickins are slim and it's very meh. Honestly I think they should do away with this piddly happy hour or revamp it a bit. I'd go back to try a full lunch or dinner service here, but skip the happy hour for sure.

Best fried chicken in New Orleans! 

If you go to New Orleans, head over to Treme for some of the best fried chicken you'll have in your life. The batter is delicious and done just right covering perfectly cooked, moist chicken. My friend and I tried both the normal bone-in fried chicken and the fried white meat chicken tenders. Admittedly the regular chicken was slightly better, but the tenders were still some of the best I've had. They tasted like real chicken, not artificial random gizzard pieces.

With each meal, you get one side of your choice plus it comes with peas. The peas were really good with a bit of mush to them. Macaroni & cheese was the casserole style served in a ball, good creaminess to it. You can add their cornbread muffins for 75 cents and you must do this! I'm not big on cornbread but could not stop eating these babies. I normally don't like crust and edges but I just loved the edge on this cornbread. 

Portions are incredibly huge! Neither of us could finish! I really wanted to try the cheesecake but I'll need to save that for next time. And yes, there will absolutely be a next time.

Lines can get long and string down the block but we got there at 11am on a Saturday and were seated right away. However around Noon when we rolled out, that long line was present.

The chicken tenders meal ran us $15 while the proper chicken meal was $11. Well worth the price! And incredibly friendly, non-intrusive yet attentive service. 

The legendary Willie Mae's delivers!

I liked Courtyard Brewery, I really did. The beer was good but there are a few areas begging for improvement. My friend and I came on a very busy Sunday afternoon. Courtyard has a bunch of random outdoor seating, but they could add a few more tables of varying (including smaller) sizes as there wasn't quite enough space for all patrons. 

I wouldn't go as far as to call the staff rude, but they were short & not anywhere near friendly. I found that disappointing as one of my favorite things about breweries is the passion of the staff for their beer. 

What's interesting about this brewery is they had nearly 30 beers on draft. Only about 8-10 or so were their own beers. Not sure I completely get that approach, but most seem to love it. Honestly it may be better to focus on just their own beers, as what I had was actually quite good! Offer them in various sizes, including taster sizes. Most of their beers which I wanted to try, I wasn't able to get in a taster size.

Then the bathrooms. Really creepy and I dreaded going in there. It was such a nice beautiful day out, but the bathrooms were dark, single stall, with no lights at all, sliding door which I was never sure was locked and always left a little space so I could see out...just felt weird & uncomfortable being in this dark room looking out. Then walking out and washing my hands in front of everyone.

So even with all the downfalls, Courtyard makes some solid beers. Some had funny names and were overall quite tasty. Equally Dreadful Cities was one of the best beers I've had in a long time, a 12.5% Braggot.

Overall, I'm glad I came to Courtyard and enjoyed the beers, but in the future I'd love to try other NOLA breweries while I'm down there.

Is there anything better than relaxing with a beer outside?! The guys who work here are passionate and so friendly, plus they have some darn good beer! Tennessee Brew Works is one of my favorite places to go in Nashville - so chill and relaxing. It's a bit off the beaten path, but once you've found it you'll realize it was worth the search.

If you know me, you know I love a beer sampler/flight. TBW has a sampler of 5 beers for $10. If you take their Saturday tour (offered a few times during the day), it will run you $12 but that includes the $10 flight. 6 beers is all they have on tap but that's plenty enough for me. If smaller portions aren't your thing and and you want a cold, refreshing pint, it can be done for just $5. All of their beers were 4.5-6.25% so nothing overly potent, but that's a good thing when you want to sit for hours having beer after beer on their patio.

Ahhhh, their patio. When I think of their patio, I get visions of unicorns jumping over rainbows with tiny kittens on their backs holding trays of brownies with no edges. It's that good. Since it's away from all the hustle and bustle of more busy areas in Nashville you don't have the congestion you may be used to at other spots. Sometimes people watching can be fun but when you need to just get away from it all, the TBW patio is where it's at. They have live acoustic music! I liked the playlist but once the live music started in the evening --- well that's where it's at.

And if you're lucky, you'll go on a night there's a food truck hanging outside. Other than a random food truck, they offer popcorn for $5 but no other food options. I'd think it's a bring your own food type of establishment.

Service was beyond top notch while we were there. Everyone there was so friendly and when we were seated outside, one of the guys actually sat down with us for a bit and chatted Chicago beers. I really enjoyed talking to him - he educated us on the brewery a bit and gave us some Tennessee Brew Works stickers.

Beer!!!!
They have a sweet potato stout! So cool! It was my least favorite of the bunch but still thought it was a solid 3 stars. The extra easy ale, basil ryeman, southern wit and cutaway IPA were all a strong 4 stars. I love a good witbier so Southern Wit was probably my favorite of the night.

This was the best craft beer I had in Nashville. This was the best atmosphere during my days in Nashville. This goes down as being top 3 places I went to in Nashville. It's only open Thursday to Sunday & usually closes at 8pm, except 6pm on Sundays - early closing so plan accordingly.

My friend and I went to Craft Brewed in the middle of the afternoon on a Monday as our last stop in Nashville. No real surprise we were the only people up in the joint. My hope was to purchase some of the locals brews to take home to Chi City! I went to so many amazing Nashville breweries and wanted to spread the wealth with my buddies up here! 

Sadly for me, so many of the breweries don't bottle their liqs. I ended up not purchasing any to go, my friend bought some whiskey and while he shopped around, I had myself a sampler of beers. The sampler at Craft Brewed was a bit more pricey than at any of the breweries I went to but still was a good deal. I got to try 7 beers for $16 (and that included tip) from various local breweries including a couple from Kentucky.

The sampler comes out in a handy dandy wooden holder that you don't want to rock too hard or it will all come crashing down. They write all the beers out on a post it note & off you go to drink to your heart's desire. While at Craft Brewed I tried:
Green Man Brewery Porter
The Duck-Rabbit Craft Brewery Brown Ale
Lexington Brewing and Distilling Co. Kentucky Ale
Depot Street Brewing Crazy Train (really interesting IPA, I was tempted to buy a growler!)
The Black Abbey Brewing Company The Fortress
Jackalope Brewing Company 7 Cities Pilsner
Tennessee Brew Works Extra Easy Ale

I had a great time talking with the guy working about beers and he was familiar with some of our Chicago suds. I also told him about some of the must try breweries for the next time he's in the Chi. Pleasant guy, good service. 

I wish upon wishes that a place like Craft Brewed opens up by me. Not only do they sell a huge variety of craft beers, wines & hard liquors but the fact that you can get your drink on tap room style is amazing. They have darts inside and what looks to be really relaxed seating outdoors.

Theo's Food Truck! Yep, that's a thing. While recently at the Courtyard Brewery, this food truck was hanging outside serving the masses. They only had basic types of pizza on hand that day but the slices were quite big and tasty for the price. It surely got the job done and was the perfect antidote for hunger while sipping on brewskis.

Is it a donut!? Is it a croissant!? Is it an insane hybrid of the two!? Why yes, yes it is. Five Daughters does 100 Layer doughnuts or what you & I have come to know as cronuts. Not gonna lie, before coming here I just thought it was one of the fleeting foodie trends. After having it from Five Daughters, holy goodness! It's delicious!

They are a bit pricey at $4.50 but in my opinion well worth it. So soft (even the next day!) and such great flavor. One will surely fill you up. I actually do well splitting one with a friend so I'm not stuffed to the brim.

Flavors for the 100 Layer Doughnut are rotating but they have some staples like Chocolate, Vanilla, the Purist and King Kong (maple bacon). The rotating flavors though are a ton of fun with October options like apple crumble, cracker jack, S'mores, Huckleberry, Snowball, Pumpkin Spice, Pumpkin Chocolate Cheesecake and Cookie Dough! Call ahead if your heart if after something in particular though because they aren't guaranteed. I have tried the Cookie Dough, Chocolate Sea Salt (which is chocolate filled!) and King Kong all of which were so soft & well made with insanely good flavoring. I'm a cookie dough girl so for me that was perfection. I was very impressed how good the cronut...errr...sorry....100 layer doughnut tasted with no artificial cookie dough type flavors. Tasted like the real thing, baby. It takes them 4 hours to make 100 layer doughnut - wowza! The effort truly shows. I read this on their site "Weight for weight two 100 layer doughnuts weight about the same as 10 glazed krispy kreme doughnuts." Dang, explains why I can barely eat one of these things.

Five Daughters also has cookies, vegan donuts, and  paleo donuts. Not gonna lie, they looked great. But when faced with those options vs. 100 Layer Donut, I'm thinking I made the smart move. 

This location also has some cute outdoor seating you can snag up when the weather is nice.

Can someone pleeeeeeeeeeease open a Five Daughters location in Chicago!? I'll love you forever!!!!

Hello! I'm Johnny Cash.

I was quite impressed with this museum. It's not a huge museum and can be done in 1-2 hours but it houses a ton of interesting information and memorabilia. I was also surprised with how high tech it was compared to other museums I have been to - music videos on iPads! How cool. While we were there, an employee was walking around helping people who needed it and answering questions. He's got to be the Johnny Cash trivial pursuit champ - he knew everything! Apparently they have Johnny Cash friends & family that will work at the museum occasionally. 

You can take pictures anywhere within the museum and there are some great photo ops! Like posing in front of the wall of records.

Tickets are normally $15 but I was able to snag a Groupon for half the price or you can use the Total Access Pass for admission. Keep your eyes open to score a deal on entry!

I like Johnny Cash's music but aside from the movie with Reese Witherspoon, I don't know much about him. I learned quite a bit at the museum and enjoyed watching his performances. I was in the theater room alone watching various bits from him on TV shows and such for quite some time. One of the big highlights is the handwritten lyrics to Walk The Line and Folsom Prison Blues. My personal favorite thing in the museum was the Valentine's gift from Johnny to June.

You can't miss the museum - it's a huge red brick building with Johnny Cash written all over it. There isn't a private parking lot but there is a paid parking lot adjacent to the building. 

In my opinion, it's a must do while in Nashville.

Cafe Beignet is pretty darn good! I was very highly recommended to go here for the beignets with many telling me they preferred them over Cafe Du Monde. I'm not gonna front...I didn't. However, I did think they were very solid. And honestly, they seemed like a much different style - bigger in size and a more puff to them, plus a bit more crispy on the outside. $4 for 3 huge beignets. 

It's a much more chill environment than CdM, that's for sure. Service was super friendly and at this particular location, they had live music while we were there! A cute little touch while sipping some coffee and gnawing on beignets. They also had a more full menu than their competitors which could appeal to some, including a full bar. And most importantly, there was no line at all - at least when we were there.

Really enjoyed my time chilling out at Cafe Beignet and loved trying their baked goods. It's definitely worth a pop in if you're in the 'hood.

Looking for something classic to do in New Orleans off the beaten path? Head over to the Columns Hotel for a cocktail.

Built in 1883 as a private home, in 1915 it became a boarding house and the rest is history! This hotel has been seen in 12 Years a Slave and was the main setting for Pretty Baby, a Brooke Shields movie.

You can easily get here on the streetcar but it truly is nice because it's far away from all the chaos of the French Quarter. It has so much history and kind of feels like you're in your Grandma's house full of antiques when you're exploring inside.

I went to The Columns Hotel with intentions of sitting on their huge elevated front porch and sipping on some drinks. Turns out you can only sit there if you're dining and on the day we went it was a set menu for $50pp. Meh, pass. So what do you do if you just want drinks? Fear not, I got you covered. 

Go to the bar inside the hotel and order your drinks. Close your tab out, take your drink outside and on the side on the main ground level, there are some relaxing tables & chairs. Sure, you won't be on the porch so you won't have a great view of passing street cars. But you'll be outside relaxing all the same and still be able to take in a bit of the views.

When we went, this side area was being seriously neglected. One table housed all the used glasses people had been piling up there all morning. We were there for about an hour and just when we were leaving someone finally came to clean up a bit. 

When you go to the Columns Hotel, try the Mint Julep and the Pimm's Cup. My friend thought the Pimm's here was the best of any he had in NOLA (And he tried it at about ten locations). I spent $12 with tip for my cocktail, not too bad.

The Columns Hotel is a must do while in New Orleans for a chill time, fun drink and to experience some NOLA history!

Yes, YES, YEEEEEEESSSSSSSSSS! I might not have screamed this while at Las Paletas, but I sure was thinking it in my head. Las Paletas was not even on my radar until I was having drinks with a couple of Yelp buds. They heard we were coming to Nashville & said Las Paletas was a must do. (Thanks A&C!) The friend I went to Nashville with is a popsicle fiend so i decided to surprise him one hot day while we were there & drive over.

Not only did he like Las Paletas, he loved them so much we went right back in after eating one and had a second. On warm days, you can guarantee driving by and seeing a ton of people sitting & standing outside enjoy their popsicles. We did the same thing, grabbed some ice pops, crossed the street to a greenish park area & sat along a cute stone wall to eat & people watch.

Las Paletas ain't your run of the mill rocket pops. They are the Mexican style full of fruit or creamy flavor type, depending on what you get. I know I've bought them from the carts ringing bells around different neighborhoods, but Las Paletas amps it way up.

Both popsicles I had at Las Paletas were smooth, creamy and full of flavor. The first one I got was chocolate mint chip. For round 2, I upped the ante getting a chocolate cookie DIPPED in chocolate. I would highly recommend both if you're into cocoa treats. All popsicles are just $3 and if you add a chocolate dip, it's just $1.50 additional. And so worth it. Chocolate is my weakness but I am really wishing I got to try some of their fruity flavors --- Road trip to Nashville anyone?

Why oh why am I in Chicago & not able to come here on the regular!? Curse you & your gourmet icey treats, Las Paletas!

Hops & Crafts is a cute little beer bar located in the Gulch near a bunch of other poppin' spots. When we went in on a Sunday, they were playing a NFL game so my friend was happy. Personally I could take it or leave it but if you're looking for a place with TVs, this is it.

They have a good variety of beer types on tap plus a good number of local drinks which was my main aim coming here.

They were out of a couple of beers listed which was slightly disappointing but everything I decided on in my flight of 6 was decent to delicious. I think the flight of 6 ran us $13.

They do a "Hoppy Hour" har har har M-F from 3-6pm where pints are $1 off. They also do specials on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays.

Friendly bartender and very chill craft beer room full of games with a couple of outdoor tables. Really liked this small taproom.

Place looks good from the outside but it is disgusting and dirty inside. BOH should take a look at it. 

Service from a college waitress is what you'd expect...random.

Mike the manager is completely useless. He has the attitude of a teen but he is in his thirties. Grow up and act like a mature adult business manager. Learn how to respond to legitimate articulate complaints about the establishment. If you wont perhaps the owner will.

This place is awesome and definitely on my new rotation list for dinner dates/happy hour spots. Last night my BF and I were starving so we gave Xiandu a try, with a 6:30 PM reservation on OpenTable. On a Friday, you can probably get seated without reservations, because the restaurant was pretty full but not too crowded.

Everything about the restaurant really impressed us. I asked if it was new because the interior was SPOTLESS. Absolutely immaculately clean, and even still smelled like fresh new wood. Apparently though, they just keep it that way, because they have been around! The inside is very modern and the tangerine walls give off an exciting vibe. We felt like we were somewhere fancy (but both of us were in jeans!). 

Like other reviewers mentioned, the food is more fusion than Thai, and I would not call it "authentic Thai", more like "American Thai", so just expect that going in. Every single dish was well executed, delicious, brought out on time, and hot. We started with the duck tacos because we wanted to try something new. We were not disappointed. This was a very rich appetizer, due to the duck and fried roti pancake, but the lettuce, tomatoes and lime juice cut the fatty taste very nicely. It was so satisfying. We then ordered pineapple fried rice, Chicken pad thai (spicy) and Green curry with Chicken. I can confidently say everything exceeded expectations and we left stuffed with leftovers for lunch the next day. Most importantly, we didn't feel completely grossed out/in food comas/bloated like you can sometimes feel after ordering from some of the greasy Chinatown places.

The pineapple fried rice was really tasty, and I will definitely be ordering it again. The Green Curry was not the best in the city but still delicious nonetheless, and my boyfriend enjoyed the pad thai. 

All of this food for a little under $30 a person and lunch the next day plus impeccable wait staff and a gorgeous atmosphere? You really cannot beat it. I will be back!

Being a novice to Indian food, I was curious yet skeptical each time I passed Mumbai Bistro. Finally after a little encouragement from friends, I got over my hesitations, and finally tried out this place. If you are unfamiliar with Indian food, this is the right place to come try it out. The buffet holds many options with very clear descriptions of what it contains and how spicy it is. I can't really tell you what I got other than the chicken masala, dal, and a couple of vegetable things. They were all REALLY good, but extremely salty (is Indian food always like that? I have no idea). I ordered garlic naan on the side because carbs are carbs, and its hard to mess up a good thing. 

I would say that I brought home the plastic container and placed it in my fridge because I wasn't hungry yet, but then I didn't feel like microwaving the plastic later on was a good move, so I microwaved it on a plate. A lot of the things got mixed together. While that was not a bad thing flavor wise, it just left me with even more confusion over what I just ate, so I would advise dining in (its so nice inside!) or eating immediately when you get home. 

I need to mention that I have a SERIOUS hesitance to buffets. Like, I refuse to eat at them. This restaurant is so clean, well maintained and modern that I did not have any reservations. You really wont feel wary about dining here (something that I have high standards for!)

I am looking forward to coming back to Mumbai Bistro, hopefully next time actually knowing what I eat :)

2 stars and pricey as well.  We arrived here for a late dinner at 8:50pm on a Tuesday.  We darted in from a rare pouring rain in Tucson to see an empty restaurant, chairs on the tables and 4 startled employees that blurted out something along the lines of "We're not closed!"

Since we were cold and wet we decided to get the food to go.  We planned on sharing chicken satay and pad thai.  The satay seemed expensive at around 7 bucks for 6 skewers.  The pad thai was similarly above market price.  While we were waiting we asked for some tea to warm up.  Cha-ching again x 2.  Another 4 bucks for "2 teas".

You know, I started my review at 2 stars but 1.5 is more accurate.  The pad thai was very bland (how can you make Thai food bland?!).  The satay was mediocre.  

I will say to their credit that I interrupted the cleaning of the bathroom so that I could avail myself of the facilities and they were spotless.

So how much for 1 pad thai, 1 satay and tea?  'Bout $22 bucks.

Went in for a quick lunch while we were picking up a few things in the area. They're currently offering indoor and outdoor dining, but it was a drizzly day so we opted for sitting indoors. They have a hand sanitizing station at register where you order your food and drinks and the staff members were wearing masks and gloves. 

It's been what feels like an eternity since I last ate at Dat Dog so I went with my old faithful order - the bacon werewolf. It's a smoke brat topped with all kinds of yumminess - bacon, relish, grilled onions, sauerkraut, spicy mustard, and tomatoes. They provided a fork and knife but I just picked it up and dove right in. The brat was nice and juicy and the toppings pair well with it. We also got an order of the cheddar bacon ranch fries to split. These are delicious as well and we had none leftover. I also ordered a mulled wine since it was chilly with the doors open, and wasn't sure what to expect ordering mulled wine from a hot dog place but it was a delicious hot drink.

This is a new place, so I don't expect it to be perfect, but I didn't expect it to be like this. The diner itself is very cold, therefore it made the food, and our coffee, cold very fast. My daughter ordered pancakes and they were very thin and not tasteful at all. We never got refills on our coffee and I never got my scrapple. To add on to the problems, our server, who didn't even tell us her name, came to check on us once and didn't clear anything that we were finished with and was not friendly at all. Overall we went in hoping that it would be a new breakfast spot, but the mugshot diner just didn't deliver.

Holy freaking chalupa. We were on our way to Mama's and found this place nuzzled in a strip mall. So of course, we decided to try it and man am I glad that we did. For $31 + tax and tip you get unlimited meat, side dishes, and rice. We ate to our absolute fill! The portions were incredibly generous and the service was impeccable. I'm so glad that we found this place after our hike today. It'll definitely be one that goes in the rotation! 

The bulgogi was hands down the best I've ever had, the short rib was succulent, and the chicken was delicious. We opted to not get the pork (belly and sliced) that also comes with the unlimited meat. 

We paid by credit card and the staff automatically included the tip, just something to note.

Being an oyster fiend[1], I was allured into giving Luke a try on a warm Sunday in early September.

Given the choice, I always prefer to seat at the bar, and the bar is absolutely gorgeous, with dark wood and wonderful decorative columns. Also, check out the beautiful tin pressed ceiling. Overall the atmosphere is that of a refined, yet casual (if a bit detached), brasserie. Mid-afternoon there seemed to be mainly business people here, but I wonder what the ambiance is like in the evening.

For drinks, I asked the bartender to pick one of the local beers on tap, and I was given a glass of Luke Fru blond lager ($6.5). I don't do lager[2], and I wish I was given Luke Amber Alt instead. The draft menu, albeit limited, includes two of my favorite beers: Maredsous tripel ale ($9.50) and Aventinus dopplebock ale ($8).

Having come here specifically for oyster happy hour (P&J oysters $0.50/ea 3-6pm), we started with a plate of 24 P&J's.  Getting two dozens for two people was, in hindsight, a bit overoptimistic: these oysters are about double the size of your average oyster! However, as it often happens with these mollusks, flavor is inversely proportional to size. Apart from a nice, mineral aftertaste, I found the oysters to be bland, and the meat too soft. This oyster probably gives its best when fried.

The entree of the day was fried Mangalitsa pork loin with Belgian waffle, pecan butter, and bacon-apple hash ($15). The dish was impeccably executed: the meat was perfectly fried on the outside, and nice and tender on the inside; the presentation in a skillet was quite pleasing. Overall, however, the dish was rather heavy[3], and skewed towards a dominance of sweet notes that I found, at times, overpowering.

Nice, solid place. The food is a bit heavy, but portions are generous and prices decidedly reasonable.
-----------------------------------
[1] And being a cheap ass, you may add.

[2] My bad for not telling the bartender.

[3] This meat already has about double the marbling of average pork.

A paddlewheel cruise along the Mississippi river is a very nice way to spend a relaxing time while in New Orleans. Just don't expect anything particularly stunning in terms of views: the banks of the Mississippi river downstream of New Orleans has little to offer in terms of nature and scenery. Nevertheless, if you're recovering from a night of heavy drinking, or if you just want to spend some relaxing time doing close to nothing, this is definitely a good way to spend a few hours of your day.

There are two paddlewheel steamboat cruises you can take in New Orleans: the Natchez and the Creole Queen. We picked the Creole Queen as it is smaller and somewhat it felt more intimate. We took the morning cruise, which takes you down river to the site of the battle of New Orleans, and then takes you back at around lunchtime.

What makes this cruise stand out is Charles. Charles is the narrator, and a very good one. On the way to the site of the battle of New Orleans he told us in great details about the history of New Orleans, its origins, the cultural relationship with France and Spain, its architecture, etc... On the way back he told us all that happened during and after hurricane Katrina. This was a particularly intense and moving narration, something anyone who visits this amazing city should listen to. Really, this guy is amazing.

As far as the rest of the cruise, once you get to the site of the battle of New Orleans you have the possibility to listen to the history of the battle thanks to a park ranger. As you are only allowed about 30-45' on the site before boarding back, I suggest to skip the park ranger and just roam around. There are some beautiful old trees covered in Spanish moss, and some cannons that make for some nice photo ops.

Finally, if like us you're on the morning cruise, as you get back at around lunchtime, the dock is strategically located very close to Drago's, where you can get some of the best chargrilled oysters in New Orleans[1].

Totally recommended.
--------------------------
[1] https://www.yelp.com/biz/dragos-seafood-restaurant-new-orleans

Not that good.

When you get to Geno's the first thing you'll notice are the ultra-bright, white neon lights that look like the cross between a cafeteria and an ER waiting room.

The cheese steak (I got one with provolone) was limp, semi-cold, and devoid of flavor. I couldn't even tell it had cheese in it. A disappointment.

Also, maybe I just don't like whiz, but the fries with whiz were just inedible.

On a side note: what's with the sign that warns patrons "This is America, speak English!"? This just sounds xenophobic. Why so confrontational towards foreigners? Are people who work at Geno's able to speak the local language every time they travel abroad?

French fries here are indicated as Freedom Fries on the menu, and I don't think this was a joke. Perhaps Geno's even donated money to return the Statue of Liberty to France at the time of the Iraq invasion.

Finally, all the various police emblems, which under other circumstances could have been seen as a colorful, interesting collection, end up contributing to the overall unwelcoming, menacing ambiance.
----------------------------
PS: If, like me, you're planning a nice, long walk from downtown to get to this neighborhood in the evening, think again. Although not necessarily unsafe, you'll walk through dilapidated neighborhoods with completely empty streets before reaching your destination.

For the same price as Geno's, you get a cheese steak sandwich that has more meat (and the meat is actually warm!), and the provolone had a nice, sharp taste. Overall this sandwich packed more flavor.

Although not a huge fan of cheese steak in general, I was happy and satisfied with what Pat's had to offer.

I would come again.
----------------------------

This place has been around since 1938, and it shows.

And that's a compliment! I liked the old feel about it, the casual  no-nonsense vibe, and the simple yet very tasty food[1]. This place is somewhere in between a restaurant, a diner, and a cafeteria.

Ordering food here is somewhat cumbersome:
- you stay in a line to order the food,
- you stay in a line to pay,
- you grab a seat wherever you want and
- wait until a server comes and gets your receipt and will then bring the food to your table[2].

I tried their Ferdi Special with baked ham, roast beef, debris, and gravy ($10.75). This po-boy is large enough to be shared. This is an excellent po-boy: the ham is tasty and tender, and the roast beef juicy. The debris ( i.e. "the roast beef that falls into the gravy while baking in the oven") sounded really yummy but was kind of lost in the po-boy. My only complain is the bread: I think this sandwich could definitely use a bread with a crunchy crust rather than this limp, industrial quality French bread[3].

The jambalaya ($6.25) was perhaps the best I've had in NOLA: simple, packed with flavor, and yet each ingredient kept its own identity in this dish. Also, the rice was cooked to perfection, with the grains nicely separated.

The turnip greens side ($3.25) was decent, and the bread pudding ($4.75) surprising: the consistency was very soft, unlike any of the bread puddings I've tried at any of the West Indian places in Brooklyn. I enjoyed it.

Mother's is certainly not cheap for such a no-frills place, but it's worth a visit. This place is very popular: come early, and be prepared to long lines.
----------------------------------
[1] AND they share their recipes! http://www.mothersrestaurant.net/recipes_dictionary.html

[2] This whole ordeal is somewhat reminiscent of Katz's Delicatessen in New York City: http://www.yelp.com/biz/katzs-delicatessen-new-york

[3] This seems to be a constant for po-boys in NOLA, though. On the other hand, aren't po-boys supposed to be really cheap sandwiches for, well, poor boys?

I am disabled and tried to use the elevator, and it turned into a huge ordeal. The bouncer who was in front of the elevator was incredibly rude and dehumanizing. He wouldn't let me up because I looked like I could use the stairs. I explained that I have a disability. He said I had to use the stairs unless I have a special VIP card. I even showed him a card I have in my wallet that shows I am disabled. His tone was super rude even after I explained my situation. He kept saying the elevator is for those who can't walk up the stairs. And I was like, yes, that's why I came to the elevator. After about ten minutes of trying to get upstairs, my friend asked to speak to a supervisor. At this point I was almost in tears because he kept insulting me. Just because someone doesn't look disabled, doesn't mean they aren't. I look "normal," but exertion can cause my heart to pause and then I pass out, but I shouldn't have had to explain that anyways. I also have autoimmune issues that affect my joints. But again, that shouldn't be their business. 

The supervisor came over and almost didn't let us up. He finally said, fine go ahead. But then he said, "I'm being nice; I could just kick you out for having a bad attitude." My "bad attitude" was me almost in tears because of how badly I was treated. Do you want me to bow down to you for letting a disabled person use the elevator? Your bouncer was treating me like a criminal before you came over, and your tone was just as rude. There was no apology or anything remotely close to it. Some illnesses are invisible. What you did is not only illegal, but incredibly demeaning. I will be filing a complaint with the ADA.

I went here for an anniversary celebration this week.  What a great little, informal, spot for dinner.  High Street encourages sharing and family style dining.  Having said that, this really isn't a family dining spot.  The menu may seem simple but the dishes are very complex and satisfying.  The "snacks" are wonderful little appetizers from crispy and light shrimp rolls to homemade breads with delightful condiments, all carefully prepared.
The salad we ordered was a special delight with Pecorino Romano cheese, apples, and a mix of greens--wow!  Delicious!
Our mains were equally good, don't miss out on the spicy crab spaghetti!  Deserts were also a complex surprise with crunch, sweet and sour, and creamy deliciousness.
Service was light and friendly.  Overall this place is a wow for dinner!

TERRIBLE SERVICE!!! Help!  IF YOU DON'T LIKE THEIR SERVICE OR FOOD, THEY WILL TELL YOU OFF AND WILL NOT TRY TO ACCOMMODATE.

I have been here before and although the service was never this horrible, the way they treat their customers was never right. I've been wanting dim sum for the longest time and unfortunately, my boyfriend wasn't a fan but he loves Chinese food. 

Upon entering, there is a terrifying mannequin with a blonde wig holding up a paper sign that says "Please wait to be seated." The party in front of us gets seated and the waitress holds up her hand and says, "Hold on." Despite that being rude, I was understanding because I thought maybe there was a language barrier and she didn't know how to appropriately speak to patrons. 

We get sat and I immediately order water and I even tell my boyfriend to hurry with his drink order because I can clearly tell the waitress was overwhelmed with the 5 tables that she had at the moment. I opted for the dim sum menu while he got the regular Chinese menu. I get a couple of things off the dim sum menu and he orders Orange Beef... My dim sum comes out slowly but I don't mind it. She comes to our table and I ask her for the pitcher and she ignores me and walks away and never comes back for us. 

My boyfriend's orange beef was so horrible. I'm not even saying this because of their service. It was genuinely horrible and so dry. They cut their meat super thin and deep fry it. What do you think happens? The meat dries out to jerky. Unfortunately, no one checks on us so we are forced to eat what we have and despite my boyfriend being a big eater, he eats 1/3 of his plate. They also bring me an extra plate of dim sum and ask, "how many shrimp you have?" She quickly takes it away and realizes it's for the other table.

We wait for so long and I wish I checked how long we have been there, and we see a lady in a burgundy button up dash out and get people water and run a couple of food and disappear again. She refilled and checked on the table next to us atleast 5 times. Our table? 0 times. She made eye contact with us several times and dashed away. 

We finally get our check and my boyfriend is clearly upset. He told the lady in the burgundy button up the service was horrible and the Orange beef was dry and no one came to check up on us and how we are doing on our food. I told him prior they might do nothing about it since when I came before, I disliked their taro cake and still charged me for it and gave me 10% off the taro cake and told me my taste must be weird. He said that is not right and still tried to tell them that he didn't like their orange beef. She told him in exact words,"you still pay!" My boyfriend said he refused to pay for food he doesn't like and he would walk. I thought him saying he would walk out was too much but I could tell her was outraged. I told her that me being a waitress myself, the establishment should either have made him a new dish or make him something else on the menu. Also, if they don't do refunds, they should post it in the front where patrons can see part of their policy is no refunds. Anyways at this point she says she is going to call the police because my boyfriend didn't want to pay for the food he didn't like. 

She calls the manager saying it's her cousin and she hands me her phone saying to talk to him. How immature is this and I'm still shocked that I'm placed in such a surreal situation. I tell him that she is being rude and I told him to listen to the way she is shouting and speaking to me in the background when I have been nothing but polite. He tells me he will offer 20% off the dish and at this point, I just want to get this over with and leave.

The waitress tells me I don't know what I'm talking about because she has been doing this for a long time and the manager is her cousin.
