She then proceeds to blame the other girl that sat and took our drink orders stating that she is new. If she is new, you should be watching and helping. We still tipped around 25% because we felt bad for the new girl. This place is horrible and people should not support this place.

Oh Blue Monkey, I had such high hopes. Too bad the food and service is so terribly bad! The only saving grace is the beer selection and the fact that every time I've been here the bartender or waitress was rude, it's not much of one. 

My co-workers and I visit this place at lunch from time to time for lunch, but without fail one of us has a terrible experience. Today for example, the chili served to my buddy was WATERY and without any meat. We asked the owner if the chili was supposed to have meat in it and his response was "it's not vegetarian if that's what you mean." What?!? Chili's meat and beans and there were only a few of those as well. 

My other co-worker's meal came out wrong - so he sent it back. By the time it was delivered we were ready to go. I asked the waitress if they would do something for him since he didn't get to eat lunch, when the owner butted in with some comment about how it was our mistake! WTF?!? Rude!

Hey owner; wake up. You've got a potentially good thing here. Too bad you lost 5 customers today. We'll be finding somewhere else to go from now on.

Really, I don't get what all the hype is about. I tried a few of their very expensive cup cakes and honestly, they are no better here then anywhere else I've been recently. Cupcakes are all the rage these days, but I just don't get it. The cake to frosting ratio is way off and I can't see paying these kind of prices for a few bites of cake. I will say that they do have a very extensive and unique selection. I tried two different flavors - some kind of peanut butter chocolate which sounded much more exciting then it was and the other was more traditional vanilla cake. I was really anticipating my visit because I heard so many good things about these cupcakes, but they would need to bring the prices way down to get me back in there. 

The staff were friendly and helpful.  The atmosphere of the store is perfect for their product and they seem to really care about what they are doing.

Note: This is an update to my review. Like another reviewer noted, just after posting my review I received a nasty note asking me to change my review. WTF is up with that? I figure it's a friend or employee of the shop and will surely never return.

I went to Sump because I had seen it mentioned many times before on Twitter and in local publications. It was easy to get to, being right off Jefferson, and parking was easy.

Although I do drink coffee a lot (espresso, regular coffee, iced coffee), I consider myself a pretty average drinker, not a connoisseur, and typically I visit a coffee shop for the atmosphere as much as the coffee itself. The atmosphere here was pleasantly contemporary, but deliberately rough around the edges, and not unique. The space is shotgun style: the left side had tables, each occupied by single people with laptops, and on the right was a large counter.  

I usually order the same thing at most coffee shops when I first try them out: an iced coffee with milk or a (iced/hot) latte and a pastry of some kind. So I did. The menu was a single piece of paper that apparently is redesigned/reprinted every day. There was a single bearded man in a Pussy Riot T-shirt behind the counter. I asked about their cold-brewed coffees, and after he explained them to me in great detail, I picked the less-caffeinated option and asked if I could have some milk and simple syrup in it. 

Everyone in the room, including the man behind the counter, laughed at me. And the man behind the counter replied, "I'm not putting milk in your coffee." He then suggested that I get a latte if I want milk. "Okay..." But I had it in my head that I wanted iced coffee.

My instinct told me to just turn around and leave, but I wanted to still give the coffee a chance. I consented to the plain iced coffee. I asked if they had anything to eat. LAUGHTER. "You'll have to get here earlier if you want something to eat." There was a single pastry left under a glass dome on the counter, so I asked about it. "It's a French pastry," he replied indifferently, as he stepped from behind the counter and walked away. Given his tone from the beginning, I took this as insult. It's a French pastry. Great. That tells me nothing about what it's made of or what it tastes like. Apparently it didn't matter because when he came back, I asked about the price of the singular little pastry ($2.25), and as he told me, he took it out, put it on a plate, and walked it to a man seated behind me. No pastry. I told him I wanted the coffee 'to go' at this point because 1) I wanted to leave and 2) I realized the place closed at 4 pm and it was already 3. My single plain iced coffee cost $4.00.

The coffee turned out to be good, but good coffee does not make up for terrible customer service, lackluster ambiance, lack of food, and short hours. 

To quote 30 Rock:
"One word: coffee. One problem: where do you get it?" 
"Anywhere! You get it anywhere!" 

This is not the only place in St. Louis with good coffee.

I think I actually need to take another day before I fully write this review.  I know if I write it now, I'll say a lot of things that are not appropriate on a public forum. 

This is my first one star review, ever. I am against one star reviews.  But I wish I could give it negative stars. 

I have never seen people treated so poorly by staff, ever in my life. 

After a lovely night of dining and drinking with two close friends, we ended up here. My friends loved in.  One especially said, "Out of all of the places, tonight, this is my favorite.  It's loud, it's dirty, the people are obnoxious, and the bartender is hot.  This is my kind of place."  My friends over tipped the bartender (this is important to note, later, when she ignored everything going on). 

The bartender, in my opinion was awful.  She ignored my presence for about a half an hour while my friends drank beer.  In that half an hour, she never once asked if I wanted anything, not even when my friends were ordering. That seems strange to me.  But what really pissed me off is when she rolled her eyes at me when I ordered a club soda.  Really, though? Did I really offend her by ordering a club soda? Is it that hard to put some ice in a cup (yeah, I got a plastic cup, not even a glass) and then spray some soda in the cup? 

But last call is what dead set me against Rotten Ralph's.   It's last call, so my friend orders another beer.  That's it.  One beer.  And we pay our tab. 

A good 5 minutes before closing time, the bouncer starts yelling "Drink up and get out!   Drink up and get out!   Drink up and get out!  Drink up and get out!" Incessantly. Yelling.  Maliciously. He was not loudly reminding people that it was time to leave, he was very angrily and meanly yelling at the customers to leave. So, still before 2 a.m., he goes over to a group of 4 (the only other people in the place) and starts yelling at them, at closer range.  Before 2.  They down their drinks and leave, so he heads over to us.  And starts yelling at us.  My friend, who would like to finish her 1/4 of beer, gets mad.  It's not closing time, yet, and there's a big guy, in our faces, yelling at us. And so he proceeds to tell us that (and by tell, I mean yell at us)... so he proceeds to yell at us that "This is the bar business.  This is the way it works. You drink up and get out or you get thrown out. This is the way it is.  It's not friendly.  It doesn't matter if we lose costumers, because customers know this is the way it works. Stop talking and drink up and get out! Stop talking! "  

I'm sorry, I missed the memo where patrons expect to be yelled at and feel threatened because they would like to finish a drink that they ordered 5 minutes prior. 

And you know what, I actually did feel threatened. He was malicious.  But what makes me upset the most is that one complete waste of a human being, with obvious anger issues, was able to put such a damper on our otherwise lovely night.

I thought living a block away from Capogiro was bad news but now I live a block away from Capogiro and Yogorino... that spells sudden death for this glutton. 

As the ladies behind the counter will tell you, this is not technically frozen yogurt since it's a probiotic yogurt. Pro-yo! (please, don't blame me for that joke). But they apparently use 6 types of probiotics in the yogurt. 

The flavors were lovely. The workers were helpful and friendly.  Believe it or not, the prices were lower than I was expecting. I am afraid I will be back a little too often.  

Word to the wise, don't watch Spaceballs before writing a review of a yogurt shop. After that movie, the word "yogurt" is dead to me forever.

I love National Mechanics.  Before I even went there, I wanted to love NM. It's so cool looking. Also, when I first wanted to try it, they had Yards Pynk on tap.  Pretty awesome. 

But, then, one fateful day, I tried to go to NM. The story goes like this: I finally convinced a friend (the lovely Jill F.) to try it with me, and as we're standing, within the columns of their porch, reading their menu, a pigeon hits us! This pigeon must have eaten the worst food (and I assume some cruel kids had fed it laxatives). In one go, it hit my head and arm and my friend's arm! It was the mother-load of pigeon poo!  So we used their bathrooms to rinse of the green gooeyness and went home.

A month or two later, I hosted an Unofficial Yelp Event here (with the lovely George R.). We came without warning the establishment because we had no idea how many people to expect. The servers and managers were extremely helpful and friendly. The manager even came over and talked to me about Yelp and also told me that they put up pigeon guards since I was last there.   Then, the management gave all of the people in our party a shot on the house. Pretty awesome. 

Having been back several times now, I can say with confidence that the servers and bartenders are great, here. 

The food is tasty and really reasonably priced.

I just wish they were open for lunch on the weekends. 

And one more time for luck: Pretty awesome. 

Snag a seat. Grab a pitcher. Enjoy yourself.

Ugh. I don't even feel like going into the shitty details about this place. I feel like it isn't even worth my energy. What I will say is that I would NEVER recommend dining here and that out of our party of eight that NONE of us will ever return. 

The service was bad. The management was bad. The food was mediocre at best. The prices are WAYYYYY too high for what is being served. 

The prices are $7 to $10 dollars more than their website...time for an update, that didn't happen over night. On top of that, the menus themselves had different prices so some of our party had one set of prices and others had another set of prices. 

They have a very large happy hour crowd and it's an older crowd. It gives a false sense of this place being popular and worth a trip but it is all a facade. 

I actually never realized how low their yelp rating is until I checked in. I haven't been here in YEARS and if I saw that star rating I wouldn't have even bothered. I don't go to restaurants that are rated this poorly. 

The bathrooms were fine. The place is pretty small. There is street parking available. 

Just stay away unless you want to overpay for mediocrity and poor service!!!

There's not much that can compete with Sunday Brunch in the French Quarter. We decided to be tourist in our own city and made reservations via OpenTable app at French Toast. Our hostess and  server were attentive. It's during COVID and masks were worn. Once seated indoors, we were instructed on the mask rules. Of course we can take our mask off to eat and drink however when we needed to alert the server we did so by putting on our mask. Now to the food: we shared an order of Aebleskivers (Dutch Pancakes), sprinkled with powder sugar and so moist on the inside. Get them! My mother- in-law ordered the French Toast and Irish Coffee (She said it's definitely for coffee lovers). My sister- in-law enjoyed the chicken and waffles. I had the fried fish, eggs, and grits. The fish was fried perfectly and the grits were buttery! Mimosas were not bottomless at the time of my visit. I would definitely recommend this brunch spot and I'd highly recommend making a reservation. Also, if your local--- Uber or park in the lot behind Dragons Den on Esplanade for a 4 block scenic walk.

Enjoyed New Year's Eve dinner at Maple Street Cafe. I've ordered via UberEats a few times but decided to dine today for the holiday. The dining room is quaint and romantic vibe. 

Waitstaff were very attentive and offered wine pairings with our meals. Gabby was our waitress. She wore her mask, friendly vibes, and offered off the menu specials while visiting. 

We started off with stuffed shrimp for appetizers, very delicious and the crust was buttery and flaky MUST TRY! Our entree were shrimp angel hair pasta, and red fish topped with lump crab and pasta. One of the best dining experiences I've had all year! Everything was fresh, flavorful and savory.

Updating my review 3 years later! My niece and I dined at Morrow's. This was her first time dining here and she LOVED the food, service and overall vibe of the restaurant. So did I. 

Our waitress was attentive and the overhead music played a  playlist. Social distancing procedures and mask were enforced and worn by the staff. 

We ordered the crawfish bread, redfish with lump crab meat and fried shrimp platter. All warm upon arrival, well seasoned, good portion size and SAVORY.

Vegan done right! Fast and friendly service. We ordered curry, fried mushrooms, jasmine rice, and potato salad. All dishes were fresh and flavorful. I highly recommend getting one of there homemade juices, I ordered the strawberry lemonade it was refreshing for a hot August day.

There's no better way to cool off than to go to the pool in 90+ degree Louisiana weather! I came across an article highlighting hotel pools where local New Orleanians can swim (for a fee). The Chloe was listed as a swanky, backyard tropical oasis and it was ALL THAT! First of all the hotel is absolutely gorgeous, however this review is specifically for the Resturant and pool area. 

We sat poolside and ordered the shrimp etouffee dumplings(A MUST TRY), chicken and french toast, steak and truffle frites, and an unlimited rounds of Prosecco and Frosé. Everything was flavorful and the presentations were on point! After eating we took our drinks to the pool and relaxed for another hour. I will also note that the staff members we encountered were attentive, helpful, and friendly. 

Pros: Unique pool setting with real European vibes that you cannot find anywhere else in New Orleans. There's also a full bar in the pool area and cute straw hats for sale ($50 each). 

Cons: You will have to reserve your lounge chair or table at 8am for same day reservation only. There are only 4 "non hotel guests" spots available. Not sure how things were before social distancing, make sure to call beforehand.

My wife insisted that we stop and try this place one afternoon after picking up one of her orders from DSW. Instant gratification! First and foremost the staff is amazing extremely courteous and helpful, they give a person a welcome feeling, and will gladly give details on a dish if a person has any question.  I had never to my knowledge, had Mediterranean food. The food is delicious and fresh it was love at first bite, seasoned perfectly. The food portions are perfect as well. There's is not a guilty feeling after eating here. My wife had the lamb shawarma and had the chicken kebab. Give Wrap it Up a chance you will not regret it, plus There is also a just a good feeling supporting a local family owned business.

A fellow LEO recommended this place to me. I have been here twice now in the last two weeks. The food is amazingly good, as well as the desserts. The Pizza is one of a kind, definitely not your everyday pizza. The staff at the restaurant is very welcoming and accommodating. A customer does have the option to order online and pick up from the restaurant. Don't forget to sign up for the enews letter and receive a free pizza on your birthday.

It had been a long time since I been to a Buffalo Wild Wings, no reason behind it just hadn't been. I do not regret the decision of going this time. The food was excellent, and our order was accurate. The drinks we ordered were made correct, and the beer was nice and cold. By far the best part about our visit was our waitress Shannon. Shannon is amazing! Shannon took her time and explained the new items on the menu, as well as conversed with us about our day. Shannon noticed that I was on crutches and asked about my injury and wished me a speedy recovery. Once we received our meals, Shannon checked on us on the regular and made sure everything was good. We never waited for our water glasses to be refilled because she would refill them soon as they were at half or a little below. It was a great evening of food and drinks, and to have Shannon as our waitress was a bonus.

The location of the restaurant is not wrong; however, there is a lot of foot traffic through the parking lot. My wife and I walked in and was greeted then seated. We ordered a couple of pops, and they were in 10oz mason jars, definitely not larger than 12oz for sure. The lady returned to take our order, and I asked for a refill on my soda I was told there are no refills. So 2.50$ gets a person a child-size pop with no refills. I wanted to order Bar-B-Q chicken and was told it was unavailable because they ran out. So I settled for garlic rice, adobo chicken and pancit bihon. I ordered my wife's food, and we ordered chicken wings as an appetizer. The adobo tastes bland, but I am use to having homemade adobo. The pancit wasn't bad, Kare Kare and Lechon kawali weren't either. The odd thing was our appetizer came out last; we were halfway through our meal when we got the wings. Overall it was decent, but I was expecting more.

I am a huge fan of the Row. I have dined there multiple times and have never had any issues. They have amazing deviled eggs and sweet potato skins but I would have to say my favorite thing on the menu is the kale salad. I typically don't care much for kale as anything more than a garnish but the salad dressing, which I believe was a honey vinaigrette, is amazing. I tend to sit in the patio area, so I can enjoy the live music (which has gotten immensely better throughout the past few weeks). My favorite servers are John and Mike, they always give great recommendations. The row's beer selection definitely rivals many of the local craft beer establishments as well as their drink menu. During brunch they have a Bloody Mary bar, can you say AMAZING?! I could go on and on, the row is definitely my favorite restaurant in midtown.

Top reasons to come here over other bubble tea places in Chinatown -
1. HONEY BOBA
2. Lactaid milk
3. Greater REAL tea variety

Number one - honey boba. Nuff said. If you don't know what it is, you're missing out on life. Lactaid milk for all the unhappy tummies after a much needed milk tea pick-me-up. Unhappy tummy no more, go and enjoy your bubble teas guilt free! Lastly, KFT has, by far, the widest tea selection. My personal favorite being the oolong (great hot or cold depending on your cravings). 

Top choices -
Oolong tea w/ bubbles, milk green tea (made with Jasmine, not matcha)

They also have the obligatory jenga set-up, along with every other bubble tea place in the city. Make your mark on the already worn-in pieces!

What a cool place - you absolutely have to try it. The hotdogs were $3 each, so a great deal. We got two - a classic one and one with pickled jalapenos and a few other things, both of which tasted great. So much flavor packed into a little hotdog! Great vibes too.

I had been anxiously anticipating the opening of Trip's in Seminole Heights for some time.  When I read that the soft opening had occurred, I quickly popped over for brunch.

From the second we walked in the door, the staff was very friendly and approachable.  It was a bit slower when we were there, so we actually got the chance to chat with a lot of the staff.  They were all excited that it was opening day and I have a cute baby that was getting lots of attention!

The décor is upscale diner, which I like.  I'm not a fan of a greasy spoon so I liked that it was a bit more upscale.  The menu is pretty extensive with breakfast, lunch, dinner, dessert, and beverage options.

I like that you can do half sandwich/salad/soup.  I went for half sandwich and half salad.  The chicken salad melt was so good!  Perfect amount of cheese on a crispy piece of wheat.  The salad was also great with candied pecans and blue cheese.  Husband got the patty melt, and you can never go wrong with that!

I will 100% be back.  This is in walking distance of my house so being a regular is the plan!

2 stars because of the view - otherwise it probably would have been 1.

I had heard about Hurricane for years so when we were in Pass A Grille at sunset time, I knew I had to stop in.  It was chilly, so we decided to sit inside on the second floor.  I was shocked at how outdated the décor was in here.  It was like we had stepped back into the 80's.

We went for drinks and the grouper nuggets.  The nuggets just weren't very good.  They were kind of chewy.  The menu seemed to be a bit pricey for this type of restaurant.

The worst part of the experience was the dirty bathroom.  There was no toilet paper in the stall I went in and the door was broken.  It really grossed me out.

I won't be back....

I scream, you scream, we all scream....  you get the idea!

I have recently become obsessed with eating sweets (which is strange because I have never been a "sweets person").  I am in the middle of a very stressful time in my life right now and sweets have a way of making me feel better.  Needless to say, I was extremely excited when I saw the Facebook post noting that Revolution Ice Cream had opened just up the street from my house.  My husband and I went over on opening day.

The shop is located in the Graham Building on N. Florida Avenue.  They offer scoops by the cup or waffle bowl as well as sundaes, which combine Revolution ice cream and other toppings.  I went for Matt's Fatty Rolls, which was a cinnamon roll flavored ice cream.  My husband got Blueberry Muffin Tops, which was flavored like blueberry muffins.  Both types were extremely creamy and clearly homemade.  We decided to mix them together and take a bite from each - truly sinful.  I proclaimed that this was probably my favorite ice cream I have ever had.

The employees were friendly and explanatory.  The atmosphere was laid back with funky art work and benches lining the walls.  We both had a very good experience.   I can't wait to come back and try some more flavors (Chocolate Shock, I'm looking at you)!  Welcome to Seminole Heights, Revolution!  Thanks for choosing our neighborhood to sling delicious ice cream!

O Cocina is really good!

I first found O Cocina because I saw a photograph of their décor on Instagram.  Their bar is all succulents and the lighting is super cool.  When I saw they had bottomless mimosa brunch, I was sold!

Came in on a Sunday with a group of friends.  The waiter was very generous with the bubbles pours, which I much appreciated.  We ordered a bunch of different items, but I decided to stick with ole' faithful and get a variety of tacos.  All were fresh and delicious, made in the style of Mexican street tacos.  We also had guacamole for the table and it was made just right.

Our waiter was really friendly and we had a nice time here.  I would like to come back for dinner and try some of their heavier dinner items.  Not a bad option in this area.

Methinks I have found a new favorite Italian spot!

My husband and I have been doing "week night date night" as of late (less crowds and helps break up the week).  Based on the glowing Yelp reviews, we decided to give Osteria Natalina a try.  First impression:  this place is small, quaint, and obviously family owned.

At first, I was a little disappointed by the fact that the menu mostly consists of seafood as I was in the mood for more traditional Italian food.  I was quickly un-disappointed (is that even a word!?) when the server came over and told us the list of specials and that they can make any Italian dish we desire...SCORE!

Onto the food - we ordered a bottle of Chianti, which is always a great choice at an Italian restaurant.  We ordered an appetizer at the recommendation of the server - Shredded Beef with arugula, aarmesan, and tomato.  It was absolutely delicious and like nothing else I have tried before.  I went for Chicken Parmesan, which came with a heaping serving of pasta with cream sauce and some fresh veggies.  It was soooo cheesy and enough food for two meals.  Husband got a Pear Pasta in a Gorgonzola Cream Sauce - it was perfect.

I loved the family vibe in here and the fact that they really cater to their customers.  I would not recommend coming here with a party of more than 4 as it is quite small.  I am going to Italy in September and I feel that Osteria Natalina helped prepare me for my upcoming food vacation!

This is a great movie going experience.

I was shocked to find out that a fancy movie theatre with food and beverages was set to open at the University Mall.  I was happy, however, to get tickets to Gone Girl at the last minute on a Saturday night.  My husband and I arrived and hit the bar.  I was happy that the tickets were only $9 and the drinks were reasonable.

Upon entering the theatre, I was pleased with how comfortable the seats were.  I would recommend sitting near the back as the screen is up very high.  We ordered some food (he got a burger, I got a quesadilla) and a bottle of wine (25% off bottles of wine on Fri and Sat nights) and had a very nice time.

Honestly, Cinebistro is still my favorite, however, this place is a lot more friendly to the wallet and a good spot for a movie.  I shall be back!

I have always been an Ale House plan.  For cheap beer, good wings, and tasty bar food - I think it can't be beat!  The Mandarin Ale House in Jacksonville was my hang out growing up and I have a few go to's that I always order from Ale House.

This location is nicer than most.  It is brand new and I was really impressed with how nice the outdoor patio was.  It was a breezy day and I enjoyed the fresh air while perusing the games on the tv.

We went with an old favorite, the chicken nachos.  Although the recipe has changed a bit, they were absolutely delicious.  My husband got one of his favorite beers (All Day IPA) on draft and we really went to town on the nachos.  The service was good, too.

This is a spot I will return to catch a game in the future.  It is a nicer sports watching atmosphere and the food can't be beat.

This review is long overdue!  I visited Mekenita the day after it opened and am just now getting around to giving the accolades it deserves.

My husband, baby, and I came in for lunch one day.  We started with the chips and salsa.  I especially liked the salsa.  It was very fresh and had the right amount of spice.  My husband ordered a margarita and I got a sangria.  Neither of us were impressed with our drinks.  The margarita tasted like sweet and sour mix with tequila and the sangria was very heavy on the club soda.  That said, I've heard from many friends that the cocktail game is now on point at Mekenita, so definitely don't write the drinks off!

The service was good.  Our server checked on us frequently and the owners also checked on us a couple times.  I got the chicken enchiladas for my meal and they were absolutely delicious! I've heard very good things from some foodies I know about the beef and seafood entrees, but I haven't yet tried them.

I don't get to go out to eat very often due to my busy life and having small children, but as the kids get older I expect this to be a favorite spot for us!
I love this place! You must get the Caesar Caesar Pizza, Buffalo Wings, and the Bruschetta! Those are the best : )

What a great find in Tucson! I visited this place after a few recommendations from the locals and I couldn't be happier. This Tex Mex style restaurant features some authentic traditional dishes along with some non-traditional options. The minute I stepped into this place for lunch on a Friday afternoon, I was immediately impressed by the ambiance and decor. The restaurant is quite large with a ton of seating and even a private room for bigger parties. It is completely colorful and inviting, as were the hostess and waitress upon our arrival. We were seated immediately and chips and salsa were delivered to the table. I decided on the chipotle shrimp burro for lunch. 

The chips and salsa were tasty, but the chips were not fresh. They were a bit salty and stale, but held up to the salsa very well. The salsa, on the other hand was fresh and had the perfect amount of kick to it. I enjoyed it so much that I was dipping my burrito in it. The entree took some time to come out but was worth the wait. The chipotle shrimp burro was served with Mexican rice and refried beans and topped with gooey melted cheese. It was filled with a generous amount of deliciously flavored shrimp, charred carrots, zucchini and onions, cheese and creamy tomato chipotle sauce that will rock your socks. I'm probably missing a few ingredients but if that doesn't convince you, I don't know what will. The burro is extra stuffed and super large, so its definitely a sharable item (but I ate most of it alone). The beans were creamy and flavorful and the rice was perfectly spiced. This is a meal that I would absolutely return for and order again. 

The service was decent and the waitress checked on our table quite often. She refilled drinks promptly and asked how the food was several times throughout the meal. I did order my burro enchilada style, though she must have forgotten since it came out with only melted cheese on top (though I was secretly glad because the sauce that filled the burro was the perfect amount). The restaurant was clean and the ambiance was inviting. The restaurant has ample parking in front though I imagine it gets filled up for dinner and the weekends. I will definitely be back on my next visit to Tucson.

I had HUB bookmarked on my go-to for Tucson since I knew I was heading this way. To my luck, HUB was closed for a summer remodel/expansion but a pop up was open in the Martin Drug Co. just down the street. I decided to give it a try since the menu features most of the HUB favorites. I was surprised at how eloquent the little pop was designed given the limited amount of space in comparison to the actual location. The ambiance was trendy with a few interesting pieces such as shag rugs on the walls and some fun lighting. Interestingly enough, the pop up had a full bar and was suitable for an intimate date, a family outing or a casual dining experience. The pop up menu featured a variety of items and I went with the prime fries as an appetizer and the roasted corn and avocado salad add ahi.

The prime fries (recommended from the waitress) were crispy fried, thin cut fries topped with a cheese sauce, caramelized onions and prime rib. They sounded similar to animal fries from In n Out sans the thousand island dressing and with the addition of prime rib. The fries were tasty, but oh so salty. The cheese sauce was creamy and delicious and complimented the meat fairly well. The mild sweetness from the onion coupled with the prime rib were a nice duo. Definitely a shareable item and super tasty if you're looking for a crispy, salty app.

The roasted corn and avocado salad was defined by the waitress as the most popular salad option on the menu. Mixed greens, roasted corn, avocado, pistachio, queso fresco and chili lime vinaigrette on the side (per request) minus the grape tomatoes and with the addition of the ahi tuna was super tasty. It was served with a toasty piece of bread on the side. In all honesty, I wish I ordered the salad without the ahi. The fish did not seem like a great addition to this, already flavorful, salad. I would definitely re-order but without the addition of a protein.

I was so bummed that I did not get to experience the real HUB because I was so looking forward to the famous ice cream. Nonetheless, the dishes were tasty and the service was decent. Initially, I asked her to replace my cup because there was a stain on it and she kindly obliged and apologized. The food overall did not blow me away but the overall experience was a hit. I look forward to visiting the actual HUB on my next visit and getting a chance at the ice cream. Tip: In the meantime, The Screamery is open and they're ice cream is fantastic!

OVERPRICED AND CHEATED!!

I went out for dinner here by myself on a Friday night. I ordered a meal and a beer. Place was empty, just me and one more table. A guy was waiting me and he seemed ok. The food comes, decent quality and taste. No complaints till then. A bunch of young girls came in and sat in the other extreme end of the diner. My waiter goes over and forgets that I was seated there. I finished my meal and waited for 10 minutes to get a TO-GO box, the waiter was still happily chatting away there with the ladies. I then walk over to the counter and ask another person for the box, wrap up my food. I wait for a few minutes for the check, still the waiter doesn't move from that table. I then go up to the counter and give them my card. They call the waiter who then comes up and gives me my check. It was $19 for a meal and beer, definitely overpriced for the food/service/place. Having waited tables myself for a while, I am pretty generous when it comes to tipping. However due to the really annoying behavior of the waiter, I ended up tipping only around 10%, making the total to $21. The waiter was looking at me and the receipt when I was writing the amount and signing, he then gives me a stern look. I knew he was going to do something with it and sure enough I check my credit card statement after a few days, HE HAD ADDED ANOTHER $4 TO THE TIP AND TAKEN THE TOTAL TO $25! 

I have been trying to call the business and talk to the manager for the past one week now. The manager is either unavailable or if he gets on the phone is busy. The person at the counter would take a message but the manger never calls back. I thought I will make one final attempt today and got hold of the manager. He was free indeed. So I'm on the phone with him for 10-15 minutes at 7 in the morning explaining the whole thing and when I am done he says he's the morning manager and I will have to call in the night to talk with the evening manager since I was there for dinner. I am done, not wasting any more time with these lame people. I disputed the charge with my credit card company and am never going to set foot in there again.

Black Lab Bistro, what can I say?  It's all good.  I recently met the owner and his family while dining out with friends, at another establishment, so i decided to check them out.  I was very impressed with the service and the ambiance.  The food was top notch, my companion was gluten intolerant, we told the server this and they made arrangements for him.  I have to say that this family works very hard trying to uphold the high standards they set for themselves, and I give them praise for this.  I will be back whenever I am in town next.  BTW, Phoenixville is a cool place, there is a lot of good competition among eateries, this is one worthy of checking out.  Thanks for a great experience, Mr and Mrs.Shi, it was a fun night.

I love this place for kids and families.  When my kids were younger this was the place to go for a treat.  Catching the shrimp, watching the fire and smoke come out of the onion volcano, even the silly jokes, it was all awesome.  The chefs have to be good chefs and good performers.  I never had a bad meal here.  Absolutely never.  I never had a bad experience here as well.  But as your kids grow up and move out, the place loses its luster.  Not because of anything other than the fact that kids make this place.  Their reactions are priceless.  For my wife and I we go, we are satisfied, we always do the early bird, it's the most economical way to go, but if you want to be Dad of the year or Mom of the decade, or Uncle of the century, take some young ones to this place, do the grill, and enjoy a fresh, well prepared meal and the experiences that good showmanship will provide.  Enjoy.

Last night was the first time at Zeppoli with 9 other of my friends. Zeppoli is a BYOB and the hostess of our party organized a game involving the 8 bottles of wine we brought. The waiter gave her the cork screw and let her handle the uncorking and pouring out of the wine throughout the evening. 
The waiter also mentioned that, for parties of 6 or more, there was a sampling menu which involved sharing dishes family-style, from appetizers to dessert. Everyone was led to believe this was a comparable option (financially wise) to ordering a' la carte, but making things a bit simpler as far as ordering. We decided to follow his advice and go for the tasting menu. 
We were given small plates from which we pretty much ate everything, from bread to mussels to pasta, to rabbit. At one point some of us even asked for a fresh dish, but were told there were none available. 
Overall the food was good, although nothing exceptional. We arrived at dessert and we were all blown away by the delicious zeppole, also the namesake of the establishment. As we were only given a handful for a table of ten, we kindly asked for a couple more and were told there were not enough available for everyone in the restaurant. We were bummed but understood.
The one star rating I am giving today is due mainly for what happened at the end of our meal, when we received our check. The total for the evening was $802.50, NOT including tip. I'd like to point out as a reminder, that we also didn't order any alcohol as we brought in our own wine. 
With the tip included, we all put in $96 which is ludicrous. I understand the idea behind a tasting menu: it allows you to get an idea of the various dishes the chef has to offer, without limiting you to one thing. It is also true though, that with a tasting menu, you are simply "tasting" each dish, not getting anything even close to a regular portion. By the end of the meal I did not feel full, I had had a couple pieces of olives, cheese, some arugola, a piece of sausage, a couple mussels, two rigatoni and one zeppole. Had I ordered myself an appetizer, one main dish and a dessert, without sharing it with anyone, I would have left the restaurant full, and I would have spent a considerably lower amount of money.
Overall I was extremely unhappy about our experience at Zeppole. I think the waiter should have been more clear about what the tasting menu cost, and knowing the price, it wouldn't have been a bad idea to give us those extra clean dishes and those extra zeppole. I can' help by compare this experience to many others I've had living in center city Philadelphia, where the food is sometimes ever better, the service is definitely more accommodating, and the price is way lower and it includes wine. 
Unfortunately I will not go back to Zeppole nor will I recommend it to others.

Buffet-O-Rama!  In an immaculate and inviting environment, imagine a expansive eclectic Indian buffet with a few Thai elements thrown in for extra-eclectic-ness.  There's plenty for everyone - and I don't mean quantity, but rather, variety.  There were 5-6 vegetarian main dish selections, numerous chicken options, goat, fish, salad-bar-ish things... and desserts. 

Standouts in my mind were the chicken biryani and chicken madras - really good flavor and heat.  I know you must be thinking I'm just a silly gringo (shout out to my Mexican relatives) and probably don't know a good madras from a Cheerio - but I did hit Brick Lane (London, UK) for curry meals with great regularity for several years.  Don't get me wrong... I'm not suggesting I'm an expert, but I do have some frame of reference.

Please be careful though as the chicken is rough cut with relatively random bone shapes and sizes to be dealt with - I thank the restaurant for clearly marking the dishes that were "Bone In".   Silly things like bones aren't going to seriously deter me from thoroughly enjoying well-spiced meat!

I lament the fact that I didn't see any of my favorite Indian vegetarian staples in the buffet (saag paneer, gobi matar, palak paneer, aloo gobi, chana masala, dal ... well 'dal' anything).  Perhaps this is my ignorance speaking... for I didn't inspect the menu... nor am I familiar with the different regions/styles of Indian cuisine. That said, the dishes I did partake of were interesting and well-seasoned.  

The service was polite, friendly and attentive.  The atmosphere was exceptional: immaculately clean, open, airy with soft music gently creating a very comfortable ambiance.  

I must state one serious peeve.  I take issue with the strong smell of bleach that descended upon our table on two occasions.  Both times staff members were cleaning nearby tables as diners completed their meals and left.  While I appreciate rapid cleaning of tables, I really don't want wafts of bleach impeding the enjoyment of my meal.  Perhaps it would be preferable if the management would consider using less malodorous cleaning methods while customers are dining. 

Apart from the bleach interference, I enjoyed the meal and would look forward to returning for a diner to order off the menu.  I think I would really enjoy the food... just please hold the bleach!

When you are in Philadelphia, eat Philly Cheesesteak! I had heard about this place on a number of different occasions so finally got to try it with a couple of friends. The space is pretty large with yellow walls, brown chairs and booths, as well as light pink accents. It wasn't too busy when we arrived and we were able to grab booth seating by the window. 

I decided to try the Ishka Special Cheesesteak, which included mushroom, sweet peppers, onions, pizza sauce, and American cheese. I am not a fan of American cheese, so I asked if that could be substituted with Provolone, and they were able to do so without any problems. 

The wait time to get the Philly Cheesesteak was minimal and it came open faced, piping hot, wonderfully cheesy, filled with plenty of steak, tons of veggies, with a tantalizing smell. The steak was tender, flavorful with plenty of tasty seasoning. The veggies were nicely crisp and fresh, while the pizza sauce added a lovely layer of yumminess without being overpowering. The Provolone cheese was delicious. All the ingredients complemented one another and the bread was soft. I liked that the sandwich was not overly greasy. Also, the sandwich was quite large and definitely makes you full. 

I also ordered their signature drink: Gremlin, which is a mix between grape soda and lemonade. This was absolutely delightful, refreshing and not overly sweet. There was a strong taste of lemonade, which blended perfectly with the grape and I enjoyed the bubbly, sparkling effect of the beverage. 

I enjoyed the cheesesteak here and am glad I tried it. I would possibly come back, but there are so many other cheesesteak places in Philly that I would want to try those eateries first.

I came here with two other people for lunch and we sat in the outdoor patio on the side of the restaurant which had lovely views of palm trees and the beach right across the street. There was no wait time so that was nice. 

We ordered two salads: the Beet Salad and Strawberry Fields Salad. The Beet Salad was just 6 slices of beets (3 red and 3 yellow) with basil olive oil, goat cheese, pine nuts and a sprig of mint. The basil olive oil was really infused with the basil flavor and the creamy cheese was delightful combined with the olive oil and beets. Also, the pine nuts were a nice touch that added a bit of crunch. 

I preferred the Strawberry Fields Salad, which consisted of mixed greens, strawberries, carrots, baby tomatoes, candied walnuts and goat cheese, tossed with strawberry-garlic dressing. The sweetness of the strawberries, walnuts and dressing paired perfectly with the other more savory ingredients. All the flavors came together beautifully. I especially enjoyed the candied walnuts, which were beautifully crispy and sugary, as well as the rich goat cheese.

For my entree, I had a tough time choosing between the Skuna Bay Salmon, Grilled Halibut and Macadamia Nut Mahi Mahi. After our waitress recommended the mahi mahi, I chose that one. The mahi mahi is baked with roasted macadamia nuts, topped with pineapple sauce and served with a round ball of yellow rice and sauteed vegetables: Broccoli and yellow squash. The mahi mahi was wonderfully moist and tender, as well as succulent with nice flavor. The macadamia nut crust was good with a strong macadamia nut taste, but quite salty - Too salty for me. The rice was nice and fluffy, the vegetables were fresh and cooked perfectly. Overall, the meal was quite good.

I also got to try some fish and chips. The type of fish was Atlantic Cod, which was fried crispy golden brown - Just the right amount.. Not too much or too little batter. The french fries were yummy as well.

Our server was lovely and accomodated us well. We had a limited amount of time, so when we let her know that, she made sure that the appetizers and entrees came out in a timely manner. I would definitely come back if in the area.

The service and selection was great today as always. Today I tried some new flavors worth note: Midnight Pleasures (non-alcoholic), Peppermint Bark (boozy), and Manhattan (boozy). All three flavors were really great but I went with the Manhattan and my old favorite, Chocolate Cabernet. The Manhattan tastes EXACTLY like a Manhattan cocktail and even has bits of real cherries in it. I loved it. I hope it stays on the menu. Also, I love that there's so many variations of chocolate on the menu here. I'm a chocolate ice cream fan so I'm a firm believer that there can never be enough chocolate on anyone's menu.

p.s. as alwaz, show a sista some love if u found what i spent time on to be of help ;-P ..thx in advance & may there be more noms in our futures!...

A friend of mine and I have been talking about coming here forever, and last night we finally made it happen... SO glad we did!!  
We came during happy hour on a Wednesday and there were only 2 other people in the place.  We asked for a Sparkler (Sparkling wine with peach balsamic and basil olive oil... super rich, but delicious!) and decided to sit outside.  The lovely lady working (I've forgotten her name!) took amazing care of us, evening bringing a tiny speaker out to us so we could enjoy the background music playing inside.  We ordered a cheese and charcuterie plate and sipped on our Sparklers.  When the plate came out we decided to have one glass of wine with our snack.  The waitress brought wines to sample out to us on the patio so we could make a decision, we both ended up going with the Gewurztraminer (a lovely crisp white) which paired well with our cheese and meats.  
Before we left we came back inside for a quick balsamic and oil tasting.  Again, SO glad we did! The waitress walked us through a few of the pairings and they were all VERY delicious! 
We would have stayed much longer but there was a private event coming in so we had to leave.  We will definitely be back!  More wines to drink and flavors to taste, plus there are quite a few things on their food menu that I MUST try! 
If you find yourself shopping at any of the shops nearby I HIGHLY recommend you stop in and check them out! Plus if you check in on Yelp you get 20% off (Which I KNEW and somehow still forgot, dang it!)

THE ELITE OF ELITE snowballs live here! Look nowhere further in the New Orleans area!

They have amazing flavors, each snowball is made with extreme care, the ice is softer than anything you've ever had (yes better than Pandora's Snowballs), and the BEST part is you can get CHEESECAKE in the middle of your snowball if you want it which is delicious! 

I live about 30 minutes out from this place but every single time I go it is DEFINITELY worth the drive.  

I'm a plain guy but I personally recommend the Ice Cream CREAM with Wedding Cake CREAM. Pure bliss.

This is absolutely the best diner ever!! It's always packed. The portions are huge. Since Covid I only get take out. Everything including dessert is great! I need realized the circle of the road it's on is called red lion.

I asked my husband if we can do my 30th birthday dinner at Rostizado because I love Tres Carnales. I have to share how disappointed I am! There were 14 of us and we were squished in a tiny corner. It was hard to go around. And they charged us for one extra person since my sister had to cancel last minute but clearly there wasn't even a table sitting for her- so I thought that was quite odd. The whole restaurant was too warm. To a point where it got too uncomfortable. The food was okay.... Mediocre. Not what I would expect from the same owners of tres carnales. And not worth the $45 per plate we had to pay. I was soooo embarrassed my friends had to pay that much for a terrible meal. The manager wasn't very personable either. She would only come out to address my husband and didn't acknowledge myself or my friends and family. Again, I might have high expectations from other places that have gone above and beyond. Not the greatest birthday experience considering the anticipation I had for the last few months. DEFINITELY won't be coming back.

And the GUEST SERVICES COORDINATOR (Who can't be named for privacy reasons) when was NOT drinking ever frowned upon? I feel that your response is disgusting. I probably would have had a better time at Rostizado if I were drunk!!! You should learn not to make personal judgements just because a person doesn't drink.

Amazing market and a must visit for anyone living in or visiting the area. I've ordered cakes from the bakery a few times for birthdays and they have never disappointed. Everything is freshly made here, including their gelato. So good. The bakery is delicious!  I normally get sidetracked when I come here looking at everything. From the prepared foods to the grocery items to their merch store. I haven't had the pleasure of trying many of their food items but everything looks so appetizing.

This place is normally packed on the weekend and parking can be tight. I've come late in the afternoons during the week and it's not as busy. Great place to bring out of town foodie guests.

My first experience having real ramen, and not one that I prepared from a package at home. So glad I came to try it here first. Atmosphere inside is friendly and laid back. Love the light fixtures and modern, simplistic theme. I felt like I was transported to a ramen shop in Japan!

I ordered the spicy Dosunco ramen bowl. Once our orders were in, it did not take long for us to receive our bowls, considering how busy the restaurant was. Broth was delicious, not too spicy for me and definitely not bland. Pork was very tender and I loved the bites of bamboo I got with my noodles. The mochi looked good, but was too full- next time for sure!

Service was excellent. They were very accommodating of our table as well as with all of the other patrons in the restaurant. Definitely car pool if you can, parking is tight. This was well worth my drive over from St Pete during 5 o'clock rush hour traffic. That ramen bowl hit the spot. Actually, the whole experience satisfied-- I had a very nice time here. Now I will never look at my packages of Shin Ramyun ramen the same again.

SO happy to have this on our side of the bay! This place is HUGE. Prices are great and they have an amazing variety of every food imaginable. Brand new store so it's very clean and all shiny and new inside! 

Awesome variety of veggies and fruits. Better priced than American grocery stores. Unique items as well that you won't find anywhere else. Aisles packed with anything you might need for cooking. It's just fun to go up and down all the aisles looking at all of it lol.

Fresh bakery, seafood, butcher, and hot food item areas. AWESOME! Lots of check out lanes so no long wait while we were there even though the store was packed. Will definitely be coming here more often than not for all my grocery needs!

Figured I should update my review since I have been here so many more times now. Still a fave place to come whenever I'm craving a boba tea or a banh mi. They've redecorated a bit so there is more counter space up front which is nice. Brian and staff are always friendly and treat us well.

I've never had bad food here. Their weekly specials are a great deal and taste delicious. Big portions and come with a flavored iced tea. Papaya salad is still some of my favorite I've had so far in the area. Pho is decent, fresh ingredients and big bowl. Fried quail is very good. Chicken wings are always a good choice as well. The curry noodle dish is a must try if you havent had it yet. Boba tea is always great here. Tapioca pearls are soft and chewy. Lychee and coconut flavors are refreshing. Taro is always a good go to for me as well as Thai tea.

A great place to hang out and get good grub.

Well, not sure what happened guys. This used to be a reliable, never fail Vietnamese restaurant, but we will probably not be back. My friends always want to come here when they visit- but they said they will look for better restaurant options next year.

Our visit this past weekend was a pretty big disappointment. I came in with three friends and our visit from start to finish was pretty horrible. Our server only came by twice- once to take our orders and then at the end for our checks. We never got refills and he never came back to ask us if everything was ok during our meal. The pho I ordered was bad. I am not a very picky pho eater, but this was not good at all. Noodles were hard and not fresh. The meatballs tasted a little off too. Not enjoyable and I did not finish it.

Moving to Tampa Bay from an area that had only a few Vietnamese restaurants within an hour drive, I never expected to be surrounded by so many of them here! I told my husband we would have to try each and every one just because we have a chance to.

We stopped by Pho Kien Giang last night (Sunday) with two other couples. I have been hearing rave reviews about this place from friends. It's in a strip mall off 49th Street and there's a banh mi deli next door (this place was closed last night, is it new? We'll have to try it out!).

Good sign for a Viet restaurant- all of the patrons were Vietnamese. So you know the food has to be pretty good! We ordered the canh chua (sour fish soup) as an appetizer because my sister and her boyfriend said it was delicious and just like mom's. And it was! The flavors were just the right amounts of sweet and sour. The fish was firm and veggies had a nice crunch.

My husband ordered the broken rice dish with the porkchop, egg, chinese sausauge and some other stuff. It was a huge dish! He said it was very good, as I could tell from his almost clean plate (he was too full to clean it completely!). My son had the broken rice with sliced pork (thit nuong), and he said it was pretty yummy! He's very picky and other Viet restaurants he did not like the meat as well as he did here. I had the vermicelli dish with the pork and eggroll. The meat and eggroll had very good flavor and were not bland. The veggies and noodles were fresh. 

Our server was very friendly and accommodating. He brought out that soup as an app, even though it isn't considered an app and brought us soup bowls and silverware for it. All with a smile on his face and he didn't seem put off about it. The restaurant is very clean inside and decor is nice without being too much. Food came out in good time and drinks were refilled when getting low. Awesome service!

So overall, our meal was delicious! And the prices here are very reasonable/comparable to the other restaurants in the area. Very happy that we got to go here and we will definitely be back to try some of the other family style dinner dishes!

So glad we came to try this place out. Cool space, it's got a industrial, modern vibe. Love the bright orange color. Lots of natural light from the windows. It is right across from Round Lake Park, which was nice as we took a walk around the lake after our meal.

I had the chili and it was AMAZING. So spicy and flavorful. I've never had a chili this flavorful before and now my homemade chili seems sad when compared to what I ate here LOL. The sweet cornbread that comes with it goes perfectly. It was the perfect portion as well. Soooo good, highly recommend.

Service was friendly and attentive, there were not too many customers when we were there for lunch. I believe the owner or manager even came out and checked on us during our meal.

Lots of tasty sounding menu items, will definitely have to come back and try. I don't come this way in St Pete often but will have to make more trips over to visit the bier boutique!

Yum! Did not think that italian ice and ice cream would be so good together, but it is! The lady at the counter was friendly and helpful and explained the menu and ordering to us as it was our first time.

I went with a small size gelati: scoop froggy frog (mint chocolate chip) with chocolate soft serve. Soooo good! They had so many flavor options. My son went with a root beer Italian ice with vanilla soft serve. He basically made a root beer float lol. It was really good too. They really pile it on high when filling the cup. I thought the small was more than enough for one person. 

Seating only outdoors. They have some fans going so it's not too hot. Will definitely visit more often when I am up this way.

Having convinced my bride we needed fish and chips, and having seen Pete and Shorty's ad in the Saint Pete Times for weeks on end, I finally got my way.

This Pete and Shorty's is located in a strip mall on the NW corner of 49th St.N and Park Blvd. 

The restaurant is definitely "Blue collar" nothing fancy here, but tasty food. It's definitely loud and fits the bill of a sports bar.

It's a Iowa Bistro, from the Midwest that has great Comfort food, burgers, and pub style food. Pork tenderloin sandwich, loose meat sandwiches, meatloaf, and beer cheese chip chicken to name a few.

But we came for the Friday fish fry which consists of two pieces of Alaskan Pollock, fries, and coleslaw. All for $9.49. Well worth it! For starters we had a order of homemade onion straws with the spicy  dipping sauce. It was delicious!

To us it was definitely a four star meal from a pub. So why did we give it five stars? The service that we received from Holly was outstanding! She was very attentive, while always smiling on a very busy Friday night. Thank you Holly!

Haven't been to Johnny's in many a year. But I've got to tell you, our party of four had one of the best meals we've had in a long time.

We arrived on a Saturday night at about 5:15 PM, and just missed the rush. We had a slight wait for our waiter to get to us, but once his pretentious self acknowledged us it all went smoothly.

Myself and one of my dinner companions had Linguine with White clam sauce. It was beyond delicious! There was an over abundance of clams in a very flavorful clam sauce. We had arrived before the 5:30 PM cut off for early bird dining, So the cost of this delicious meal was under $10. I had a side Cesar salad with anchovies, fantastic!

My friend had ordered spaghetti with meat sauce, when he had finished his meal it looked like he had licked his bowl. 

My bride had chosen Veal masala with a side of fettuccine Alfredo, this too was a huge hit. 

But the true favorite of the night, was the Johnny bread and it's dipping sauce. I swear they must've put crack in this sauce. We all tore into our Johnny bread and sopped up every last drop of it. Embarrassingly we asked and received more! 

We will be coming much more often, can't wait for more Johnny bread!

Okay, it's a good, standard "N.Y. Style pizza" but..........then there's the attitude, which you wouldn't expect from the millennials running this place. Just try asking for some pepper flakes to go for your carry-out pizza and see what happens. You'd think you were asking for a kidney!  Tell me what pizza place WON'T give you pepper flakes and/or some grated cheese to go with your take out order? We even offered to BUY some pepper flakes to go. They said NO! Instead they said we could "put it on in the restaurant" but that doesn't work when several people are sharing a pizza and not all of them want pepper. 
              So, based on that really stupid policy of being too cheap to give you a tiny container of pepper flakes with your order, we're never going back. There are too many other, better and friendlier pizza places in this city. Try Vetri or Nomad. (Their pizza's are also much better and there's no moronic attitude there.)

Thanks to the lovely Anna M and the multi talented Steve E for all their hard work in being my partners in crime setting up this surprise send off for the hubster, Eric C. 

Ulele was the perfect crime scene with its beautiful and unique decor.  We had walked along the river walk the day before and wandered into it even though they weren't open. They did tell us they'd be opening soon for lunch.  But we were seated near the open doors by the horse sculpture and was much quieter area (at least before we took over)

Very historic building with an urban trendy feel. The bar area is near the open kitchen and gets very loud. 

We enjoyed a drink at the bar before being escorted to our rather large group of 12. Wish we could have invited all our yelp friends but space was limited. I enjoyed the wedding beer. 

We were escorted to our table and everyone had their menus up hiding their faces!  The look on Eric's face when they yelled surprise was priceless!  A Kodak moment for sure!

Our servers were delightful and so glad we got to share food among our group. The lobster cake with cucumber ginger salad was well seasoned. The crab Mac & cheese was a combo I'd never tried before, would get both of these again. I tasted the okra fries and while a bit on the salty side, surprisingly tasty!  Never tasted okra before and I liked it!  I ordered the squash gratin as my entree even though it's a side dish. The crust was made with manchego and the smell was intoxicating and tasted even better!  Highly recommend this dish, only thing I'd change is swapping out the red onion for more zucchini. I tasted Jason's jalapeño corn quick bread and loved every bite of that as well.  

The ulelee salad was made of arugula, watercress, cranberry beans and fire roasted peppers with a balsamic vinaigrette. Yummy goodness. 

For dessert I shared the house made toasted coconut that was served in a half coconut shell. 

It does get pretty packed for good reason, excellent craft beer, superb local food, eclectic ambiance complete with rooftop area and primo service is what we experienced. 

Thanks again who all came out to make this surprise memorable for Eric. And a special nod and wink to Anna and Steve for his finding some cute winter accessories in Florida!

If you are a die hard gambler then the hard rock will fit the bill. I'm more into tangible spending but have dropped a few $$ in the slots. When I come here it's usually with out of town guests. 

Not as nice as Foxwoods in Connecticut and doesn't compare to Vegas but will serve your desire to live the dream. No free drinks and no ventilation. If you walk about a mile you will find its a bit cleaner and newer towards the hotel side. 

Lots of slot machines and poker rooms for your donating er um gambling pleasure.

I scream! You scream!  We all scream for ice cream!  Love the abundance of choices of gelatis, which at first confused me. Is this some new form of gelato?  More than one gelato?  No. Gelati is a concoction of soft serve vanilla, chocolate or swirl layered with your choice of flavored Italian ice. 

Service was friendly and efficient. Having told her that I was a first timer, she offered as many free samples as I needed to decide. Salted caramel won this time and it was fabulous!  Not heavy like ice cream. 

They offer so many different flavors and change them up often. The covered area to enjoy your gelati totally makes sense. 

Glad to welcome Jeremiahs to my hood!  I foresee more visits in my near future.

My childhood is filled with memories of enjoying the annual Philadelphia Flower Show and then walking to Vietnam for some lunch/dinner with my family.  This has happened more times than I can count, and each time its been wonderful.  It may not be the typical family tradition, but it's mine and I love it.  

Even now that I live in CO, any opportunity I have to come back to Vietnam is an exciting day indeed.

I've been to Vietnam more times than I can count and two things are guaranteed, my Mom and I order the Flaming Volcano for two, and the table shares the BBQ Platter.  If this is all you eat and drink at Vietnam you'll be in heaven.

The Flaming Volcano for two includes rum, vodka, gin, brandy, grenadine, Bacardi 151 and fruit juice.  This is a boozy beverage and will leave two people feeling the buzz as they suck down every drop.  And don't let them take the drink too soon, as the ice melts and mixes with the remaining booze and juice you can have a "second drink".  Don't forgot to blow out the flame and drink the rum from the center, it's a warm burn as it makes it's way slowly down your throat.  

The BBQ Platter includes, crispy spring rolls, beef stuffed grape leaves, char-grilled chicken, grilled meat balls, rice vermicelli, lettuce, and rice paper sprinkled with crushed peanuts.  They say this serves two people but I think this easily serves four to five people, especially if you're ordering entrees.  The crispy spring rolls are those addicting spring rolls that you dream about.  If I was on a desert island and could only have three things, I would want these spring rolls to be one of the three items.  In addition to the spring rolls, the grilled meatballs are delicious and I love taking the lettuce or the rice paper and making a wrap with the rice vermicelli, char-grilled chicken, pickled vegetables and topping the whole thing with some peanut sauce.  The BBQ Platter will feed the table and people will fight over the last bites.

I've tried multiple entree items and they have all been good, but nothing has the variety that the BBQ Platter offers.  The BBQ Platter gives you multiple items and a mixture of tastes that a single entree cannot offer.  Take my word for it, order the BBQ Platter!  And if you're feeling a bit crazy, the Flaming Volcano for two is the perfect accompaniment.

I went there over the 4th of july weekend and thought nothing more of this little shop when we first walked in. But wow i was really surprised when the food came out! It was rly delicious actually. We got dragon roll, spicy tuna roll, and this roll with the rice crispies which i forgot but a hidden gem. Theres also a patio, might bring my dog next time!

Kind of a long review.  For those not inclined to read the whole thing the moral of the story is their employees don't know squat, their drinks suck, they misadvertise the price of their drinks, and then they proceed to charge you more than you authorize.

My friends and I went here on a Monday night after dinner on a warm night looking to have a couple drinks while relaxing upstairs on the roofdeck.  What ensued was a less than pleasant experience.  

Getting in was quick and easy as it was a Monday night and the place was anything but packed.  We had asked the bouncer whether or not the roofdeck was open as it had rained earlier in the day and he assured us it was.  As we got upstairs though and tried to get up to the roofdeck which we were just told was open, we were informed by the guard of the stairs that it was closed for the night.  A bit disappointed, we went back downstairs to find another place to go to and as we passed by informed the bouncer at the door that it actually was not open.  Turns out, guard of the stairs is a complete idiot as we were allowed upstairs and he apparently forgot he had let apx 10 other people upstairs as well.  But fine, no biggie.

It being what was apparently Salsa night, we ordered a round of what turned out to be the worst possible Caipirinha's ever known to man.  Advertised on their menu as a $10 drink, we were charged $11 each for the drinks and given some random excuse that they incorporate the drink tax into the total per drink charge.  But fine, no biggie.  

Pay for the horrible drinks and leave to go somewhere drinks don't suck.  Look online today to find out that in addition to the charge and tip which I authorized for them to place on my card, there was an additional $3.60 charged.  Now in the grand scheme of things, I'm not going to die over $3.60, but it's the principle of the matter.  You don't charge people more than what they authorized you to do.  I pay for my bill and I leave you a tip, you do not get to give yourself additional money.  Maybe if their employees were not incompetent, and their menu reflected the actual costs of their drinks, and their drinks did not suck donkey balls I wouldn't care as much.  But you gave us a less than tolerable experience and then you steal my money!

Save your tastebuds and save your money.  Go somewhere else.

We took a friend here for his bachelor party recently. Most of the food was amazing. The bone-in ribeye and the short rib/filet mignon combo were both very tender, cooked precisely to our request and very flavorful. Our flatbread appetizer was very good, though a little expensive. Our sides, the lobster mac & cheese and the alsatian pasta, were highlights of our dining experience as well. 

We missed on the chilled seafood appetizer ($48) which wasn't anything special. I could have gotten a lot more food at a chain seafood restaurant (minus the tuna sashimi) so it wasn't worth the hefty price tag. 

And the main knock on this place is that I think the server was a little disappointed that we didn't order more food (and consequently run up our bill). One of my friends was originally going to order the seafood boil and we were going to pass on the appetizers. She pressed us to order an appetizer, so my friend decided to cancel the seafood boil and order two appetizers (mentioned above) and we would share all of the dishes. She tried, but it was clear that she was disappointed that we modified but didn't really add to our order. 

Overall, I don't have a bank account that can afford this class of food regularly. It was a great dining experience and the view from the 37th floor is very nice (I am acrophobic, but it wasn't an issue at night being seated in one of the inner tables). But for one night, it was nice to splurge a little.

Stopped in over the weekend for a couple sandwiches around lunch time. A handful of other patrons inside, all of which seemed to be regulars. We read over the menu and went with tuna salad on wheat and a turkey/avo/provolone wrap. Staff was super friendly, we paid up (about $17 with a drink), and lunch was served up quickly.

Both sandwiches were fairly simple, but had plenty of good flavors and lots of fresh veggies. The turkey wrap was slightly better but the tuna salad and wheat bread was solid. 

They also have a good variety of reasonably priced fresh produce and groceries. It's very much a Greek deli, and next visit I'll be sure to get a gyro and/or Greek salad. They also appear to do a lot of take-out. Great spot, I'll be back!

Oh happy day!  I was pleased as punch to hear about a new oyster bar that opened up near my house.  My folks were in town visiting and my dad is a self proclaimed oyster fanatic.  It was a given that we would give this place a shot.  

It's not very big.  I think I counted 8-10 tables and about 6 barstools.  They don't have a liquor license yet so they are allowing patrons to BYOB.  The servers were attentive, but didn't seem to be completely comfortable/knowledgable about the operation.  Example:  I had a Yelp coupon for 15% off a dozen oysters and the server was completely unaware of the offer.  They were a little slow too.  I'll give them the benefit of the doubt and say that they're just working out the kinks of being a new restaurant.  That said, I hope they get their act together quickly!

The oysters were delicious.  We got a dozen raw, a dozen chargrilled, and a half dozen blue cheese/bacon.  The oysters only came with ketchup.  Very weird.  We asked for a side of horseradish and they brought it out.  Problem solved.  In the group we ordered the shrimp poboy, redfish, and shrimp salad.  All wonderful.  I really hope this place makes it.  We'll definitely be going back.

This is a easy 5 star hole in the wall.  I'm almost hesitant to review this place for fear that too many people will show up, but it is my duty as an elite Yelper to help you out as per the Yelp Elite oath-to-office I took (didn't you take one too?).

There is absolutely no way you'll find this place if you don't already know what you're looking for.  The sign out front has a big red square on it.  That's it.  No words, no nothing.  Inside boasts a no frills diner style restaurant.  The food however, is delicious.  

There was a big group of us so we ordered all sorts of things.  I can't begin to tell you what they were.  I ordered the General Tso's Chicken.  Instead of the normal chunks of fried chicken, it came out as whole fried chicken wings.  Awesome.  Just plain awesome.  It had a hint of sweet to it so if that isn't to your liking, you may want to steer clear.  

Service was "family" style with the entrees showing up on serving dishes instead of individual plates.  

This place is worth the trip.  Go and enjoy an awesome dinner.  Stop thinking about it...just go.

My teenage daughter wanted to go here as we were staying at the hotel next door. I ordered the pulled chicken sandwich which was not quite warm and not at all pulled. Daughter got the chicken fingers which she liked and I liked the sauces she got (not sure what they were) for my fries. Waitress seemed disinterested. Wasn't crowded but it's very overpriced for mediocre food at best. Plenty of other/better options in the area.

This place is AMAZING. I went here with a large group of friends on a weekday and we were quickly shown to a table. This restaurant is BYOB so we brought some
champagne and split a pitcher of fresh squeezed orange juice to make mimosas. They have a machine that makes the juice right in the restaurant. 

Our waiter was friendly and very helpful. He made sure we all had coffee and water as soon as we sat down and helped open all of our champagne bottles. 

He suggested one of the specials which was a mac and cheese pancake with a gold fish cracker crumble on top. Being curious and also a little taken back by the combination we decided to order one and split it. It was the size of a large plate so we all got a good size sample. This is one of the greatest things I've ever had and I'm not sure I will ever eat a normal pancake the same again!! The Mac and cheese was mixed into the pancake batter and was such an interesting and delicious combination. It was served with a side of syrup but I liked it better without.

For my main meal, I had the honey's platter which was 3 pancakes, 2 eggs and your choice of meat and potato. I had the bacon which was really crispy and the breakfast potatoes. This entire meal was a huge portion and every aspect of it was super tasty! 

This place has delicious food and friendly, attentive service. The atmosphere is lively and the prices are great for the portion sizes. Just remember that it's cash only!!

Sit back and relax and grab yourself a glass of wine because this is going to be a long one.

Just know this, there really is something for everyone here. I feel like we will be able to pop in and belly up to the bar and share chicken wings and a salad on a night we are too tired to cook. It's the place you can stop and grab some delicious chicken soup for the sick kid at home. Need a sit down meal with some comfort food and casual vibe? You found it. Having a dress up date? It's the place you will be able to make a reservation for your special event and enjoy a prime meal with attentive service. How can it be all of this at once? I am not sure, but it is. 

We arrived in the area of the restaurant and honestly, we weren't sure exactly which store front was it. There is not a lit sign but I did see the neon heart that sits behind the bar so I knew it was OK to park. Parking was easy, street parking and very close. I am not sure if Webster doesn't allow lit signage, I was so excited I forgot to check if other's had it. I don't think this is a huge issue but it did catch my attention enough to write about it.

Right away upon walking in the door, I knew this was a place we would feel comfortable. It very much has that neighborhood restaurant and bar feel. It's open, there is walk in seating against front window. There were people sitting at the bar eating and drinking and most of the tables were full. We had made a reservation for 6:30 and arrived about 15 minutes early. We figured parking was going to be more complicated than it was. They were able to seat us right away though. I would highly recommend making a reservation if you want to sit at a table and have a meal. I understand they are already booked on the weekends for the next few months. Know that the high tables as you walk in the door are reservation tables, not bar seating.

There are touches of love everywhere. The wall of photos of Congenital Heart Disease children and families just makes you want to hug a stranger and weep at the same time. The hearts representing our beloved Ollie and Oakes remind you that the people that own this place are living their dream despite having been thru the most awful experience a human can have, losing a child. What I think I love the most is that their names will be said over and over and over again and they will never be forgotten. They are now woven not only into the hearts of family and friends but now the hearts of the community.

We spent quite a bit of time exploring the menu. Our server, Grace, never made us feel rushed. My husband Den has severe allergies to cooked tomatoes and chocolate and she asked us to give her an idea of the items we were interested in and she would check with the chef. Honestly, I had to do a bit of googling. There were some things I had no idea what they were. They turned out to be fancy words for familiar items. We love food but we aren't fancy folks. Knowing that the owners are so much more open as eaters than I am, did cause me a bit of worry before I saw the menu.  We were even unable to try everything that we wanted to. I could have ordered so much more. We ordered too much and went home with a full size shopping bag of leftovers but we couldn't help it. 

So here is what we ordered:

We were offered the bread service. It was fresh bread from Union Loafers which is a wonderful bakery in the Grove neighborhood. We had a sourdough and also some kind of brown bread.
