They were both delicious. Olive + Oak makes their butter in house and it was also served with olive oil. I can't remember what is in the butter but try it, I think it might be honey? but its not sweet. Sea Salt? Fresh herbs? Heck! I should have written it down.

We really had trouble choosing from the starters. We wanted to try the Smoked Chicken Meatballs, Crispy Chicken Wings and the Beef Tenderloin Slider for sure. Our first google was the description of the meatballs. What the heck is "agro dolce". Well, I know dolce means sweet and agro sounds like agriculture. Sweet grain? Nope. It is Italian sweet and sour sauce. ohhhhhhh that sounds good.

We finally ordered the Crispy Chicken Wings. They are $12 and the description is "chili mustard butter". I know we love wings. We really love mustard wings and they are pretty hard to find in St. Louis. We love chili but were a bit nervous since that was the first thing listed that they would be too spicy. Den doesn't love super spicy.  I believe there were 8 wings on the plate. Really at first I thought they were a teeny tiny bit too expensive but the flavor and quality made them $12 very quickly. They were perfect! They are crispy on the outside and so tender on the inside. The thing is, they aren't in a traditional sauce. They aren't in any sauce. The mustard on it is a dry rub and it is outstanding! I can easily eat these weekly. And the worries about being too spicy? Not. They are way more mustard than chili. They have a lot of spicy flavor but spicy as in spices, no

By far the worst service, the worst drinks, and bland food! How hard is it to make a vodka with a splash of cranberry juice or to keep my water glass full? I have never been treated like I didn't belong somewhere before in my life and I have been to some 5 star facilities. The next time a patron tries to explain to you without being disrespectful how their experience was before you fly off the handle regarding the "appalling $1 tip plus a sad face on the receipt" LISTEN!! ALL PATRONS SHOULD BE RESPECTED by all means we all keep the doors open for you regardless of race or gender! 8 african-american men and women and we all experienced rude behavior yet we all arrived at different times!! Don't be so quick to judge those of a different race because we too hold degrees, we too have prominent positions in our careers, and we too have the financial means to pay for the items we order.

I am going to write this review to compare it to Tucson restaurants because if I start comparing it to other places- it'll start dropping stars and I want people to patronage this place and other such places so Tucson can thrive and improve instead of them go down in patrons and close.

I went to Proper for my birthday in May. I read other reviews and saw their online menu so I was fully aware of the prices (really, its not so expensive, and not so much for pork belly, etc).... I was expecting the small portions- one thing however was that they were OVERLY small. 

It's 2013- small dish, big price isn't the sign of a good restaurant anymore. We've moved past the early 90's!

The taste is great! Dead on for everything. The pork belly I ordered was a bit too fatty for even pork belly but who can complain when it tasted great. The lamb was great. Leeks gratin were amazing- however a bit too similar to mac and cheese. Better to get the leeks and go the "healthy" way. 

The dessert is the real disappointment. Not even the taste could make up for the small size in the enormous dish. Think about those mini round brownies you get from costco. Yep. That size for $8 and not one dash of "chili" it claimed to have for a kick. It was dry and unshareable to even pick off of. That was the most disappointing and its sad because it's supposed to leave your visit there as the "extra cherry on top" of last course. 

Wine prices are good, foods good, portions are TERRIBLE even for a small plated food type restaurant.

Oh yea, we ordered a bottle of wine and each time it came in this glass bottle carafe- are they filling wine themselves on tap? Are they serving boxed wine? Why didnt it come out in a wine bottle with a label??? WEIRD! I dont care if it looks trendy that way, i want to see that the wine I ordered is the wine I got in its original bottle. Stick it in an ice bucket if you want it to look fancy.

who cares that i have no idea how to pronounce iztaccihuatl because this spot straight up delivers (literally).  ever get intimidated to order authentic mexican food because you don't speak much spanish?  well worry no longer, online ordering from my couch just brought my anxiety level down a few notches (plus there's also those times i'm just a little too lazy to wander over to the italian market for my taco fix).  at iztaccihuatl each taco meal is only six or seven bucks and comes with three generously stuffed tacos with the meats sauteed in onions and cilantro, and wrapped in double corn tortillas.  they also come with a couple slices of radish and lime and three different spicy salsas.  the tacos al pastor are definitely the way to go.  lightly charred sweetly marinated pork with sauteed onions and cilantro.  yum.  you'll thank me later.

I was underwhelmed with my meal. I ordered the chicken fried chicken. The portion was quite small with barely any chicken and tasteless, and the stuffing was very dry. The waitress was very nice and attentive.

Very nice museum dedicated to Johnny Nash. The museum is small and it takes about 45 minute to get through if you watch all the videos. The tickets are quite expensive for how small the museum is and how quickly you get through it

Felt like a milkshake and went through the drive through to order it. They have soooo many different flavors to choose from. I went with the chocolate malt and it was an excellent choice. The thing that amazed my most is how cheap it was. Very generous portion and very reasonably priced.

I really enjoyed this restaurant from the service to the music to the meal, overall a great experience. We are in the jazz bistro but started by visiting the bar (got a French 75 obviously and am now obsessed) and visited the museum upstairs. Museum is a small but totally interesting if you want to learn a family story, see costumes and gain some insights into Mardi Gras of old. 

Ok on to the food, selecting oysters was a challenge as they prepare them so many ways. We went chilled for 6 and the Bienville. The chilled were excellent and the Bienville were made with the right amount of wine and seasoning so not to overpower them. We also had to try the famous soufflé potato which are light and puffy with bernaise for dipping. They were fun to try.  I tried the duck with blueberry port as I was craving duck after so much seafood that day, it was great although a lot of sauce so not as pretty to look at. My husband got the most perfectly cooked filet au poivre, the sauce was decadent and just the right amount. 

After dinner we tried the cafe brulot instead of dessert and what a show they put on table side for this. The Orange is peeled with flair, the ladle is used to crush spices and ceremoniously add liquor into the bowl and it's set on fire. Finally the coffee is poured and the drink is presented. The whole place was watching and lots of other tables got it after we did. 

The jazz trio was excellent and traveled to tables taking requests. I personally loved the ambiance of the jazz bistro room with the dark lighting. The elegant dining room looks lovely too but the jazz bistro was the better choice in my book. Service was lovely, impeccable and the manager even joined our table for moment to chat as he had moved there from California. Don't miss this spot!

Pros:  The adult milkshakes and onion rings were both fantastic.

Cons:  Service took forever-  about 50 minutes to get our burgers.  The serving size for the buffalo chicken waffle fries was small in comparison to the price tag, and overall everything was very expensive.  My burger was good (I had the sriracha chicken burger) but not worth the money or time in the end.

Three Monkeys Cafe is a bright spot in a neighborhood devoid of cool places to hang out.  It's located on James Street, just off of State Road (near the City Line in the far Northeast) and directly across the street from the SEPTA R7 Torresdale station.  

I ventured into this place last winter, when it was cold and snowy, and I was waiting for someone to pick me up from the train station.  I didn't notice anything special, and the cloud of cigarette smoke coming from a group of grouchy old men at the bar soon drove me from the building.  Luckily, however, I recently stopped into Three Monkeys again with my mother for lunch, and I discovered, to my delight, that the place had expanded and improved.  The interior of the bar/restaurant reminds me of a cozy English pub, complete with hardwood floors, wooden walls and booths, and old-style ceiling fans and bar decor.  Since last winter, the cafe has also added a charming, shady outdoor garden complete with a monkey-shaped fountain, so patrons can eat or drink outside when the weather is nice.  Also, the cloud of smoke is gone, thanks to the Philadelphia City Council.

I was also pleasantly surprised by the menu this time around.  I didn't remember there being anything special on the menu the first time I visited, but this time, I found that they serve delicious American food with a twist, such as Asian wings, panko-fried chicken fingers, salmon BLT's, mussels, and drunken shrimp.  I ordered the veggie burger, which I usually never eat, and it was delicious.  My mother got the salmon BLT sandwich, which was a little undercooked at first, but the waitress was so pleasant when my mother asked to have the fish cooked a bit more, and her sandwich arrived back at our table fully cooked so quickly that it really was not an inconvenience at all.  And the food was delicious.  Check out their menu online at www.3monkeyscafe.com.  

They also have your usual assortment of beer on tap, mixed drinks, and the like.  I didn't have any alcohol at lunch, but I can't wait to go back and have some mussels and "Horny Monkey Ale" while sitting outside in their garden.

Every Monday is 3M Monday, when patrons can enjoy $3 Mojitos, Martinis, and Margaritas all day.  This place really is a hidden gem in the far Northeast.

UPDATE:  I've had the "Horny Monkey Ale" and it's pretty good.  And I really like their filet mignon cheeseteak with provolone.  Yum.

After seeing all the negative reviews I understand as a customer at other restaurants how sometimes places are a real letdown, however I LOVE this place! I started coming for the $5 cheese and $5 chocolate in the bar but because of how amazing our service and food always is, I have come back 2 times recently with family and have had a bill total of over $100 each time. SO WORTH IT! The meats are not something I would seek out just because I'm not to much of a carnivore  (i am a total carbsavor haha) but even  the two times we have gotten the 4 course it was amazing. Even the meat. As far as the cheese and chocolate goes...holy amazingness. 
    The sides are always fresh, the servers always make great conversation while they make your food and answer all our questions. My friends and I always stop in at least one a week about an hour before they close because our restaurant closes an hour before. As a restaurant worker I get how annoying It is to have people come in so late but everyone here is always so chill and understanding! Plus now I'm 21 and they make amazing drinks! The love martini and the amaretto nightcap are a personal weakness! Long story short I love this place and will always come back!

If you're the kind of person who enjoys hooking up in bathrooms, Triumph is your place. They're almost like mini-rooms with ample space for movement; stalls be gone! 

Aside from that, it's a hit or miss crowd. On busy, South-Jersey-invades-Old-City-nights, Triumph might be the last place I'd go, but it beats the other area sleaze asylums. 

The space is very accommodating for groups and the beer selection is great. I'll take their home brews over Philly Brewing Co.'s any day. Personal fav is the Irish Red. The food also scores, try the Cuban sandwich.

Could it possibly be that one pays a lump sum to devour delicious steak, delectable sides, and classic cocktails while still being treated like a normal human being rather than a "yes sir," "by all means, madam" upper class snob? Yes. This place has the goods without the stuffy, old money pretension. And thank god for it. 

A note to those who like their meat more medium and less medium rare: the correct way to state your preference is "medium rare plus."

As its name would suggest, Resurrection Ale House is digging through the Grey's Ferry trenches and giving this blossoming neighborhood the quality bar it needed. 

The proprietors of Memphis Taproom and Local 44 have once again brought spectacular beer into an otherwise desperate (but growing) neighborhood. Same as they did with Memphis in Fishtown and Local in West Philly, it seems they have a knack for discovering these bustling communities of beer-starved zealots and giving them the finely crafted beer it they crave. 

My friend and I shared 6 glasses of suds: Brewer's Art Resurrection Ale (hurry and get some, they've only got one keg), Russian River's Pliny the Elder (a personal hoppy favorite), Schlenkerla Helles (tastes like nothing you've ever had before, bacon turned beer...awesome), Dogfish Head Pumpkin Ale (taste like autumn, gush), Lagunitas Lucky 13 (piney, slightly sour, and delicious).

We also sampled the edibles: beef sliders (!!), rich cheese spread over mini bread crackers (!), hoisin braised pork ribs (!!!), fried chicken wings with drizzled honey (!!!). Even though opening night brought out the entire neighborhood, the staff managed the crowd with the utmost grace and composure. 

Now I can bar hop in Grey's Ferry. 

Grace...Sidecar...Resurrection. This is awesome.

I stopped in here last night after wandering around the neighborhood wondering what to eat. I often find myself frustrated with the local options. But really, I'm just a baby, my neighborhood is rich with possibilities. Not feeling particularly inspired by any cuisine, I settled on Varga where they had exactly what I never knew I wanted: PAN ROASTED CHICKEN BREAST (organic free range chicken) with herb-shallot potatoes, baby carrots, and snap peas. Sweet baby jesus. This was good, great even. My friend and I split a bottle of Russian River Damnation and while her Kobe beef burger was delicious, my chicken stole the show. 

Their ever-changing beer list is worth a visit alone, but if it's chicken you're after, check them out. I'm adding this entree to my growing list of main dish must haves around town.

Ok, clearly I'm not the first person to feel this way. Mad Mex food and Mad Mex cocktails warrant two separate reviews. 

If you order the Big Azz frozen strawberry margarita, you're in for a treat; there are real strawberries in there...ish is tasty. 4 stars.

If you order the food, you're in for it. Blah blah bland. 2 stars.

To compensate for my lackluster meal, my date devised distractions to keep me from whining over my food. So we played seven minutes in heaven in our booth. 7 stars, 1 per minute.

Hold the phone! Union Trust is offering a $7.17 lunch menu!! While I had trouble choosing between the three options: Duck salad tossed with cranberries and candied walnuts, fish and chips, and the Kobe beef burger, I ultimately caved into my beef calling. Delicious brioche bun, perfectly seasoned meat topped with melted American cheese. Simple but awesome.

To think you can now experience UT without have to dive deep into your wallet. Wonder if Tommy Up's going to pull another receipt stunt.

If I hadn't gone to Copa last night at 11pm, I never would have met Silk, the man who would later instruct my friend on how to pick up women.

Ferry (my friend), Giles (my dog), and I sat down to enjoy an impromptu margarita and fajita salad. Just as Ferry is talking about how effective Giles is when it comes to picking up women, our cute waitress (Sarah) walks over and starts gushing over his doggish good looks. She scratches his belly, he gives her his paw and kisses, and just when she's already impressing the hell out of us, she asks for his name.

Me: Giles
Sarah: Giles! From Buffy?!

Ferry and I are both visibly giddy. Another Buffy fan lives among us! She leaves our table and I start chatting up the two guys at the table next to ours. 

Me (looking at Giles): Don't mind him, he's really friendly
Guy 1: Oh, no bother. I have an Italian Mastiff. 
Guy 2: Yeah, his dog had me pinned up against a wall. 
Guy 1 (hollering at a group of girls): Hey, how you doin? (One girl turns around) I see you looking, that's alright, you can look.
Me: Do you really think that works? 
Guy 1: You just gotta have confidence, girls love confidence. 
Me: How do you think my friend Ferry can pick up the waitress?
Guy 1: Just say "I like you" 
Ferry furrows his brow in panic. 
Me: I like you? That takes courage...something easier
Guy 1: Just compliment her on something...(Sarah, our waitress, walks back out just as he's talking). 

Sarah: Hey guys can I get you anything else?
Guy 1: Ferry and I were just talking about your hair. He was saying a lot of girls can't pull off that hair style and you work it really well.

Sarah, blushing and clearly excited, moves to our table and makes a b-line for Ferry.

Me to Guy 1: Whoa, that was money!
Guy 2: Yoooo dude! That was smoooooth. I'm gonna call you Silk from now on!

As it turns out Ferry and Sarah end up exchanging geek comic book talk and other nerd code; it's clear they'd have a lot to talk about. Did he get her number? No...but here's why: an epic ending to an already memorable experience...the firefighters crowed the street and blocked  it off due to an electrical fire a few doors down, so we were forced to leave. Nevertheless, we found out she works on Friday nights.

Silk (hollering at another group of ladies): Excuse me, Ms. (one girl turns around). I like you. (She smiles). You have a beautiful smile.

As for Silk, he and I exchanged numbers and promised to reconvene at Copa soon enough. His farewell text? "We'll hang soon. Long live KING FERRY." Turns out he's a minister. Good things happen with the right combination of strangers, margaritas, and a good server. Well done, Copa.

I don't know another late night happy hour like this around town. You order drink after sophisticated drink and suddenly, though your legs develop cocktail bruises, your wallet doesn't. Before you know it, you've bought drinks for many other bar patrons and your bill doesn't exceed twenty one dollars. Am I just really charming or is this place just -that- special? It's that special, and my charisma merely won me smiles from the bartender, not any special discounts. $3 drafts and half off specialty cocktails.

If you appreciate an aesthetically pleasing ambiance with in-the-know folks, go here on a Tuesday night between 9 and 11 when Meghan is behind the bar. Most likely, you won't be sorry.

When my dinner date-friend exclaimed, "take me to pleasuretown...and make it Mexican," I knew just where to go. I grabbed a bottle of tequila and down the street we hopped. 

I half-expected it to be crowded, thanks to the night's lovely weather, but thankfully there were tables abound! We were seated outside and within minutes, we placed our drink and appetizer order: Blood Orange Margarita, traditional guacamole, pork carnitas. With speed, the items dropped like kisses on my forehead. Except they dropped on the table, not on my face, and they were delicious. The guac maintained the perfect salt balance; the carnitas were served in a lovable DIY sloppy fashion; and the pitcher of blood orange margaritas took us to where we needed to go.

We split the short rib entree and found ourselves scarfing down every last bite...but it was just enough to leave us feeling full and bloated, but not the uncomfortable variety of bloated. 

Um, what else. Oh yeah, we got dessert. This was sadly very disappointing. The Tres Leches came out very stale and hard to gently scoop into the spoon and then chewing took a bit of effort too. 

Nevertheless, Lolita scored...and then I did too. 






j/k
This coffee tastes like campside marshmallows in the Redwood Forest. I love it.

Brauhaus. What happened? I came here with a friend last night and we were both incredibly disappointed. In looking for a middle-of-the-road option (nothing dressy or too expensive, but something nicer than say a hot wings corner bar), I suggested we head to this spot.

We each got a 1 liter beer, an entree, and potato pancakes to share. 

The beer: My friend and I wanted to drink out of a boot, one of those glass 1-2 liter boots we'd seen others enjoy. After selecting the Ayinger Oktoberfest brew and my friend getting the Hausbrau liter, the waitress informed us that his pick didn't come in a 1 liter serving (because the manager doesn't like to offer that beer by the liter). Without really explaining why, she walks away, but only to come back with both of our selections in a boot! Super! Except that my beer was warm...and later cost me $19.50!!!!! She explained that they didn't have a way to charge me for the boot (um, hello, why do you even have them then?) so she just charged me for 3 beers. Based on a general rule of thumb, whenever there are, let's say, 3 different sizes of things, each one costs more, yes, BUT you've got to save a little for going with the larger size. Think of it as if you were ordering a large drink over a medium one at a movie theater ("for only a quarter more..."). My friend's beer, $11...exactly what that boot should cost.

Food: My friend ordered the Wurst plate ($16) and I went with the Rouladen ($20). The wurst came out cold. Cold! As for the Rouladen, I should've ordered the Wiener Schnitzel.

The most redeeming part of last night's dinner were the potato pancakes ($6)...not because they were amazing (they're just potato pancakes), but because they were still warm when they hit our table. 

Our grand total came to $78.49. I would ordinarily have no problem paying that much for excellent food and service, but here, I felt swindled. 

Final thoughts: completely overpriced for food and beer that's half-assed.

Even if you live nowhere near West Philly, Dock Street's worth checking out. Tucked away on the corner of 50th and Baltimore, this monstrosity of a building offers the yuppies of the now gentrified West Philly an oasis for freshly and finely brewed beers. The building's exterior looks like a bank turned brewery.

I'm a fan of the pilsner, and the pizza even lives up to its reputation. I only tried a slice of the plain, but the rest of the menu's offerings looked pretty appealing. The desserts, not quite as tempting and should I say, slightly boring.

It's great to sit outside and enjoy the soundtrack of kids playing in the park across the street. It's definitely one of the best spots for beer in the city, and being there makes you feel like you've discovered something no one else knows about...until you run into a fellow yelper.

After downing one too many last night and waking up to find one shoe at the bottom of the stairs, the other at the top, my inside-out jeans in the hallway, the rest of my clothes in the shower, and my hair wrapped in a towel, nothing can get me back on my feet like a filet from The Capital Grille. 

Clearly the only class I have is the kind I can buy. 5 stars Capital Grille. Thank you.

Despite the recent Yelp dissatisfaction with this place, I had a better than average, dare I say exceptional, experience last night. My friend and I sat at a table outside, the place was busy, but entirely manageable (it was a Tuesday night). Our hostess/server greeted us the moment we walked in and brought out our drinks promptly. She was attentive, but not overly/annoyingly-so and engaged in friendly banter when it was called for. Turns out she's from the Bellevue restaurant XIX: Nineteen (read: she has experience).

I'm thinking the overwhelming complaints about service might have moved these guys into action and they're starting to tighten up their business. 

The one thing I will say is their burgers and onion rings are FANTASTIC. The rings are soaked in Kenzinger! 

If you're interested in going there to take care of burger business, check it out on an off night, you'll probably be treated with excellent service and awesome food.

Like a poor orphan I entered Soy Café with a mere 8 dollars to my name. I examined the menu and carefully selected what I thought was my best option for a lunch meal. 

The Funky Monkey called my name. Bananas, peanut butter, oatmeal, soy milk, and honey blended in smoothie form? Yes. I might say it's been the best $3.75 I ever spent...and now my new favorite smoothie in all the Philadelphia land. At 5:55pm though, I'm hungry. A blended beverage is no meal replacement unless there's whiskey involved.

When my roommate asked me for a Sunday night date spot recommendation, I suggested Tria in a hurry. She's been excited all week for the date she was supposed to have last night. Low and behold, her date cancels 15 minutes prior to their actual meeting time. LAME! So, in good roommate form, I took her out instead. 

Tria offers a Sunday School special where they feature one wine, one cheese and one beer. The featured wine was an Australian Mataro/Shiraz made by Some Young Punks. The bottle is called "Drink'n'Stick." For only $6, we ordered glass after glass. You can't beat a Sunday night at Tria. Even if your date stands you up, find a friend and go.

Not even a flash mob can stop these people from serving me a late night cheeseburger. Even though I nearly got tear-gased on South Street, I ate my bacon cheeseburger in bliss and then fell asleep into a dollop of ketchup. Yay, I'm a fan.

After a serendipitous weekend of meeting random eccentrics, my main mate and I felt it necessary to round out our experiences with a visit to RIM - reading about your stories of Rene had us feeling like he'd be the pot at the end of a rainbow.

Rene is the best, he knows he's the best and he won't serve anything that isn't completely fresh and made to order. I enjoyed the most ambrosial chai latte. It came topped with freshly shaved chocolate, bits of pistachio, and other spices he scraped, drizzled, and dribbled into my steaming glass. Rene's got a culinary arsenal of spices and chocolate off to the side and it isn't until your drink is in the glass that he adds the final touches. He even has a chocolate covered block of Parmesan cheese!

My friend's chocolate cappuccino was ridiculous. First of all, Rene served it in a margarita glass and spread melted chocolate on the inside using a brush. I mean, yeah. Once he poured in the steaming milk and espresso, he added a circular airplane shaped chocolate piece to the top of the glass and used a BLOW TORCH to melt it into the beverage. To say it was the best thing ever isn't saying enough. 

While at RIM, we met a couch surfing nomad and her Spaniard boyfriend. She's been "surfing" for 10 months and swears it's how she's going to spend the rest of her life. Once my friend and I left, we just stared at each other and smiled. This weekend was sublime.

Those of you who struggle with gifts to get for mom or wife or girlfriend or other leading lady, take note, Verde has a wealth of options. Even if she loves to cook, an iron skillet might not be better than that tennis bracelet. Or that food dehydrator, despite its obvious cool points, might not cut it either. 

You should probably get her something she wouldn't get for herself. A nice piece of casual jewelry to dress up those jeans. A cute pair of flats for those vacations to Martha's Vineyard. A clever Philly-inspired tee (that costs way too much, Verde). A selection of chocolates made in the experimental looking lab just in the back of the store. A nice handbag. A Goorin Bros fedora. Or, gasp, a flowery apron (anyone who said women don't belong in the kitchen needs a lesson from the 50s).

One moment I was picking items up with excited fervor and a second later I was putting them back with ticket shock. An adorable Philly tee should not be more than $40. Likewise, an "indie" tee with screenprinted feathers shouldn't be over $30. But don't be dismayed, there were other things there that seemed fairly priced. All in all, a finely curated selection of gifts and goods.

You can walk into this frozen yogurt shop, grab a cup, and self-serve away. It's easy to load up on tons of flavors (tart yogurt, mango, green tea) and have your toppings (fresh strawberries, captain crunch, kiwi) follow suit. But don't be greedy, you'll pay for your glorious yogurt mountain when the cashier weighs your cup. I'm waiting for them to add mochi to their arsenal of toppings...do they still not have it?

I have a friend who's been to every "cool/unique/off the beaten path" spot in Philly. So, while I can impress my less in-the-know friends with random urban discoveries, this one buddy keeps me on my toes. I finally one-upped her at Carman's. It was actually the first time I'd been there too. 

We walked into this diminutive diner (there's bar seating for about 4-6 people -there's no liquor though- and a few tables) and were seated right away. Our server came over, asked for our names and proceeded to rattle off the specials. I can't remember exactly what they were, but I got the feeling that Carman's the type of woman who goes shopping the day before and buys whatever's fresh. Figuring out what to make with it seems like an afterthought. Somehow she manages to pair the most unlikely items together and keep it delicious.

There's subtle penis iconography strewn throughout the diner. It doesn't come off as tasteless though. While I was sitting at the table, I remember looking out the window and glancing over a little plush piggie. How darling! Upon closer inspection, his little bits were hanging out.

"Carman puts the C U N(ext) T(uesday) back into country." That's what the sign reads, folks. 

Oh! You can call in advance and have your name put on the waiting list. There never seems to be too long of a wait though.

Last night was frigid and the streets were abandoned. It seemed everyone was wrapped in their snuggies at the precise moment when I was wandering the streets, looking for a warm bar to enjoy a neat bourbon. 

When my mate suggested Misconduct, I gave him a double-take. You mean the bar I've never really thought about patronizing? Since he's a man of fantastic taste, I obliged his suggestion and on we trudged. 

I ordered my Maker's, he went with Knob and after the kind bartender informed us of half price burgers, we got one of those too. I'm a total snob when it comes to burgers (there's a bun to meat ratio that needs to be adhered to) and theirs was fantastic. So good that I'd say it's one of the top 5 simple sandwiches I've had in the city. 

Next time I'm hanging out with a bar snob of a friend, I'll suggest this place, it's unexpectedly awesome.

Listen up Philly pizza haters, I've found the good stuff. Not only does Little Italy serve up my favorite slice, they also make my favorite cheesesteak. 

So, here goes: 

BEST PIZZA.

BEST CHEESESTEAK.

Yeah, I said it.

One thing I can say about every Starr restaurant is that the service is top notch. The employees will literally bend over backwards, put their coat over a puddle, and hold every door for you. It's impressive. You don't like your food, send it back and get something you will like; at a Starr restaurant, it seems the customer can do no wrong. 

I did, however, pay $13.75 for a "Courvoisier Margarita" aka a "Sidecar." This wouldn't have been as startling at say, Butcher and Singer, but at Jones, I felt a little robbed. 

The food? Well, it's good. I'd say this restaurant appeases the junk food eaters who dislike going to restaurants because it means they can't eat cereal for dinner, Kraft Mac n Cheese, DiGiorno pizza, or a tray full of ready-to-bake cookies (I've just described my roommate). Jones has the stuff for them. This is Steven Starr's way of glamorizing 1950s TV dinners...good for most, but not really suitable for someone who demands a Newtown Pippin over a Granny Smith apple. Exactly.

I was sold when the congenial man behind the counter said, "the turkey chili has a little tequila in it, but not enough to get you drunk." I'll take it! Match that action with the herb chicken salad sandwich and there completes my half soup, half sandwich, whole beast of a petite lunch.

As I brought my brown-bagged kill home, I delighted the whole way about how quaint that little Fishtown treasure is. Ample room for those work/study people and even a cozy couch with a coffee table for Sunday morning newspaper readers. 

If you're wandering the hood in search of all things hearty and homemade, look no further than Soup Kitchen. A great name, by the way.

Pietro's boasts my favorite salad in Philly. Like, FAVORITE. Here's how you can't go wrong:

Mediterranean Salad with the sauteed chicken. It comes with grilled shrimp by default, but do yourself the favor and sub those out for the chicken; you'll be the envy of the table. The salad's large enough to have as a meal and props if you can finish the thing yourself. 

I'm also obsessed with their rolls and how they consistently serve them right from the oven. Mix some olive oil, salt, pepper, and crushed red pepper together for the perfect bread dipping sauce. 

When it comes to brick oven pizza, theirs is the best. I'm particularly fond of the mushroom topping. 

Pietro's is my reliable fall back plan when no one can decide where to eat.

When I'm in the right mood (by myself, driving around on an early Sunday morning, listening to XPN's Sleepy Hollow), there's no place I'd rather be than Mugshots in Fairmount. The busy but quaint ambiance sets it apart from most other coffeeshops in the city. Green Line on Baltimore arguably offers a similar vibe. I think it's something about being a nice-sized, corner coffeeshop in a greenspace neighborhood.

The food misses though. One of my favorite things is a bacon, egg, and cheese with a tomato slice on a slightly toasted English muffin. They don't have English muffins, so that's the first minus and their eggs are often scrambled and flavorless. Their saving grace is the Jailhouse Rock. Fresh, organic peanut butter spread over multigrain toast with banana slices and drizzled honey. Nothing beats that. 

If I want to hang out by myself, read a book or the paper to the slight bustle of a coffeeshop, Mugshots is a choice spot.

All I wanted was 7 margaritas last night, but after a number of "closed" signs reared their ugly heads, my friends and I settled on Moriarty's. We all walked in grumbling a little under our breath (this isn't even CLOSE to being Mexican!) but my former roommate/friend (who's ever so hard to please) got excited about being able to watch the Phillies. So we stayed.

Lindsay (friend) waited and waited for the bartender to change channels so she could enjoy the game...but it wasn't until the 3rd inning that she switched it on. Lindsay got dangerously close to smashing pints, Mutton Chop ordered far too many genetically enhanced chicken wings, and I didn't really enjoy the cheese fries.  

As far as Irish bars are concerned, Moriarty's gets 2nd place in Center City (McGillin's gets 1st). But then again, I typically avoid places like this. And no, not the best wings. Hooters still takes the cake in that department :)

When I used to live around the corner on Croskey Street, Cafe Lutecia was my everyday lunch spot. The small cafe had a few tables inside and maybe 3 outdoors. It's a quaint establishment with a mere 3 people on staff. You can't mess with the food though. Fresh baguettes, crisp veggies, savory meats. I always ordered the chicken salad salad. That's a scoop of chicken salad over a bed of lettuce and other veggies. Even though it sounds simple, it's the best chicken salad I've ever had. No joke. The dressing is also perfect. Order the soup too. Everything's homemade and fantastic. 

When you're in here, you feel like a friendly Francophile couple opened their doors and invited you into their country kitchen.

So I went back for one of these magical cupcakes today and learned a new thing; their gluten free, dairy free, egg free, corn free, wheat free, peanut free, soy free, casein free treats are good for me. Oh man.

Great spot for lunch. $6 beef and veggie burgers, Anchor Steam on draft, and the veggie burgers are actually homemade and slapped together using actual vegetables. It almost looks like shoestring veggies pressed together into a patty. Top that off with cheese and it's awesome. 

Their house infused liquors are killer as well.

Coolest bar in Old City if you ask me.

I saw "Geno's Steaks" on my local TV news in New York. They claimed to be the best in Philadelphia. After trying their competition across the street, I was going to see if Geno's was king. Geno's has no inside seating. They also don't take cash. This to me is always a disappointment, because I almost never carry cash. Geno's had a small line when I arrived. You goto  one window to order the steak sandwich and a second window to order the fries. I got both and the service is quick. After getting my extra cheese steak and fries I sat down to try. The streak they use is long and square. They give plenty of onions but not much cheese on the extra cheese steak. When it was time to eat it however, I was truly impressed with how flavorful the steak and cheese were. The bread was a bit chewy, but it didn't take away from the hero. The french fries are stringy, but you get a lot and they are packed with flavor. I must say I definitely enjoyed Geno's. Based of this I would recommend the location to all my friends coming to visit. I mean it's the Philadelphia thing to do!

The night life was kicked off with a small hole in the wall bar named "Oscar's Tavern." Why is it named Oscar's? Was it named after someone special? Or was it named after the owner? No one knows, mostly because I never asked. The bartender was a wonderful and personable server. She talked and joked with everyone. The bar has seen better days, probably before I was born, but it felt homie. It was crowded, drinks were pouring, and plenty of conversations were generated. A few locals talked to us about Philadelphia's history and the best places to get cheese steaks. One of them traveled the world and busted New York. She said there's no place like Oscar's and I was slowly starting to believe her. I never found out why they called it Oscar's, but for that one patron, Oscar's name came from love. That's Philadelphia's way of saying welcome. If you want to be part of the culture and enjoy the full experience of the city, than you need to make one stop at Oscar's  and throw a few back. And would someone please find out why it's named Oscar's!

The one thing I hate about vacation is when I find a spot that is "the one!" This restaurant is worthy of that title. "Khyber Pass Pub" was on a list of places to eat at in Philadelphia, so I made it my business to get here. From the outside it looks like a small bar, that if you walked to fast you may not even see it. But heading inside, judging by the loud music upstairs, I knew this is a very hip spot. It's low lit, with a comfortable vibe. It has two floors and a bar on each. Downstairs is the restaurant, where you can eat and socialize. Upstairs is where they have a live band, where you can dance the night away. But dancing would wait because I was hungry. When I got to the hostess stand, I was told to find a seat and I did. My waitress, Mikaela, came over and she was amazing. She was friendly and recommended all the best food. She joked about not knowing about them being on the best spot list. But after a short conversation I ordered the Mac & cheese to start. Those Mac balls were incredible! The were placed on a home made sauce that seemed to bring all the flavor out. I asked for a side of the sauce for my sweet potato fries it was so good. I told her I wanted the burger because it came highly recommend. That recommendation was on point. I didn't change anything about the burger, I got it according to the menu. I'm so glad I did. The beef was sensational, the bacon crunchy, and the dry cheese complimented the entire burger. Topped off with the pretzel bun and sautéed onions, and you got the best burger in Philadelphia. I will make it my point to come again. Atmosphere, food, and service! Who can beat that?

"Pat's King of Steaks" was good. The building has no inside dining, so dress warm in the winter. The building is older and The you line up on the side and the have two windows. One for the famous cheese steaks and the other for fries and drinks. After heading to both windows you find seating located around the restaurant. They don't take credit so remember cash. It was time to find out if they were king. They give you a ton of cheese and onions on the hero. The steaks are chopped up small. It does have a lot of flavor and the bread was soft. I was disappointed in the fries. They were thick and delicious, but they don't give you a lot. I would say I liked Pat's, but king is a lofty expectations. I would go back, but  I definitely wouldn't recommend it as a goto.

The "Philadelphia Museum of Art" is know more for Rocky Balboa running up the massive steps than the impressive art inside. I pictured myself climb the steps to the background music of "Gonna Fly Now" as motivation to get to the top. The massive pillar columns house some of the world's most important artifacts. Inside the museum is beautiful, clean organized and more importantly, educational. This museum has modern art to some dating back to 200 AD. So when you think of the museum and you run up the steps and raise your arms high, remember to head inside and raise your mind as well.

I don't want to take up to much of you time. Just want to say I love New York Cannolis. "Cafe Creme" was creative with a variety of cannolis, but they fall short on the filling. The building looks distressed, but I think that's the look they're going for. However the equipment was not part of that plan. One machine how towels around it because of leaking and some of the ice cream looked old. The floor needed to be mopped and I had to whipped the white powder off my table. I couldn't believe it. When I ordered the cannoli, to my surprise, it was six dollars. I was surprised, but on vacation so I paid. However I quickly regretted it when I tasted this flavorless pastry. It had nothing going for it, not even the light baked crust dipped in black and white chocolate. I almost asked for my money back. I'm so glad I live in New York, if I want a real cannoli, I can go to any store around my area.

Against my better judgment and countless recommendations, I came to "Jim's Steak South Street" last. What a huge mistake. First off, this place deserves six stars. Second this place is crowned king of cheese steak. Everyone I talked to in Philadelphia said come here and again, I waited. It's nice that it's indoors. Today was cold so not freezing while you eat was a plus. It's two floor and full of history. In fact this place has more history than some museums in the area. You wait on line and they make your order at the counter. The cut real steak and cook it up so it's piping hot. They put the toppings on in front of you as well, so you see how much your getting. They don't sell sides, but they make up by selling beer if you like. Once you smell that amazing hero, you truck up to the second floor. There's plenty of sunlight and seating to enjoy. But the view and the seating paled in comparison to the taste of the cheese steak! The meat must have been seasoned because it was a work of art on my taste buds. The onions also tasted great. The cheese tasted like real melted cheese and they gave so much. Again I'll see it, they gave cheese (Did I ever mention I love CHEESE)! This hero, set itself apart from the other places I've been. I definitely recommend it, and trust me this is your first stop. Don't make the same mistake I made........Twice.

I have been wanting to visit this brewery since they opened. Just the patios outside alone made it look like a fun place to visit. I was definitely not disappointed. This is now one of my favorite breweries in Nashville and I will definitely be back. The staff was so friendly and you could tell they actually love their jobs there. Their food is also very good. I got the grilled cheese and it was possibly one of the best I've had in this town. I would recommend going on a Wednesday night because it's 2 for 1!

I absolutely love this traditional Italian byob  restaurant .... Hearty , tasty satisfying beyond my expectations. 5 STARS! 

Service was great and fast last night.

We had the medium size antipasta, the clam conch mussel shrimp white wine linguine and the veal pork beef meatball w house made sauce and pappardelle!!! House made pasta ... Delic! Also complimentary rosemary bread and olive oil.

We were so full that we took leftovers home and had no room for the desert. But we are def going back and next time I'm going to save room for dessert.

Crispy
Cheesy
Garlicky 
Large slices that can hold on their own.

What's everyone complaining about ?

I actually really liked my open slices here...  I tried an eggplant parm and a 4 cheese slice. 

 Cheese heads would love the latter--there was a fancy swiss I think on there, along with ricotta and a couple others.   Eggplant parm slice also had ricotta on the base, which gave it a nice lightness.  Enjoyed both.

I appreciated the dollops of sauce on both--the sauce here is, oh my goodness, SEASONED (unlike so many bland pizzeria bases out there). The right amount of salt and sugar, no bitterness, with a little fresh garlic.  

Much better than the typical cheap cardboard pizza joints.   Plus, the staff was very warm and friendly.  Bonus.

I can see myself,coming back for a quick, cheap, and satisfying bite.

The definition of a nice but trashy-ish casino in a suburb.

I came to Parx on a recent weekend evening - the place itself is pretty nice, feels a lot in design like the Borgata inside, but with a much less classy clientele.

There was a general feel of loserdom in this venue - the high table minimums (all but 2-3 (always full) were $25 minimums.  For Blackjack they had those cheap video screens table setups with prerecorded scantily clad women, all done by computer.  Watching this for 3 minutes was 2.5 minutes too long - people not knowing it's their turn, the choppiness of the video play, and the way the game won too easily, going from a 16 to a 21 twice in a row.

The people there were not exactly of a high class - definitely a local, townie, slightly hick crowd.  The slot denizens were doing their thing.  The waitresses were dressed in tiny outfits that some couldn't pull off.  One of the restaurant (Chickie & Pete's) was really crappy, see my review for that.

Yes, I still gambled and yes I didn't do well, but the aura here is just not great.  I was happy to leave when I did, and will never come back - for me, gambling is about the fun, the energy, and the thrill - this was just a place to gamble.

Ciro's has such a romantic atmosphere, the small booths draped with sheer black curtains allows for privacy  and the compact space makes it feel very intimate. Ive been coming to Ciro's since Fall of 2010 when I first moved to Tampa and it quickly became a favourite date spot & I highly recommend it to those looking for a more unique experience. I truly miss the floor to ceiling saltwater fish tank that dominated the main wall, it was beautiful and provided a nice pop of colour to the interior. 

The ladies have plenty of eye candy thanks to the suspender-clad bartenders. I highly recommended sitting at the main bar where you can observe the barkeep skilfully creating prohibition era craft cocktails. This is definitely not a bar that you're going to order one of the typical bar cocktail, the menu is specifically designed to the 1920's during the time when the US Government banned alcohol. The drinks are always amazing and I think I have almost finished having each menu item at least once. Speakeasies revived the cocktail culture & most are fun to go to. I love that Ciros has remained steadfast with having a password to enter. Although the cocktails are a bit overpriced for most people, once you see the work and cost that goes into creating the drink you'll understand the price. 


The food I always delightful although I am sad they took several of my favourites away. The lighting is very dim which was typical of the era the bar is themed from, so make sure to have a phone Hamdy to help illuminate the cocktail menu. The food Menu is on a lighted book making it easy to see. 

They are always busy so make sure to go online or call for reservations and the password.

I love the rustic charm of the wood tables here.  I love even -more- the counter-height six-tops.  I really really love that every single morsel of food was delightful.  But I think I love -most- how obscenely gorgeous our waiter was.

Just envision this: He's reasonably tall with a lithe figure.  Probably a runner (or possibly a swimmer).  Fills out his clothes with a solid build without looking beefy.  That killer combination of brown hair and light eyes that I'm such a sucker for.  Pulls off a perfectly-groomed effortlessly scruffy look.  Sexy, confident voice.  And adorable dimples, to boot.  *swoon*  Really, he -has- to be a starving actor looking for a role in some steamy soap, right?

Yes, I realize that I just dedicated an entire paragraph to gushing about our server.  And yes, don't lecture me about how I'm taken.  Just because I'm on a diet doesn't mean I can't look at the menu!

Aaaanyway...

Yeah, grub's great.  Can't go wrong.  I had the fortune of dining with not one, but two exceptional food experts and took their lead on everything from the charcuterie (hellooooo testa!) to dessert (choux crème).  In fact, the only thing I decided for myself was the duck confit salad (read: tender juicy duck with a sprinkling of frisée).

Couldn't ask for anything better about dining at GTC.  But seriously... I'd come back for the eye-candy alone.  Not only is it mouthwateringly delicious, it's calorie-free... unlike everything else I consumed!

I've had cheesesteaks before, but this was an altogether different experience.  For starters, I learned that ordering a cheesesteak in Philly (or at least, at Pat's) requires its own language, specific syntax and all.

As an example, to obtain a cheesesteak with Cheez Whiz (really, is there any other type?) topped with onions, one would walk up to the window and state "Steak, Whiz, With."  That's it.  Pay up, your sandwich, if that's even the appropriate term, will arrive at the next window over within a moment.  They don't mess around back there.

For those looking for something a little more formulaic, it's...

[Sandwich Type], [Cheese/Faux-Cheese Selection], [With/without Onions]

-------

All that said, I didn't have any cheesesteak on this excursion.  Just their fries.  Which, considering their pricing at $2.50 and the quantity, don't seem to be much of a deal.  Particularly given the lack of overhead, since it's only outdoor seating.

On the other hand, they were amazingly satisfying fries.  Ultra-crisp on the outside, nicely salted, and starchtastic on the inside.  Just the way I like them.  Mmm.  Fried fantasticness.

Would repeat.  Perhaps after a few hours on a treadmill.

Tried this place multiple times.  They are hit and miss.  One time you have the best burger of your life, the next time you have the worse.  Lately it's been the later.  Service is terrible and it's not uncommon to wait 45 minutes to get your order taken and another hour for your food or beer to arrive.  Last time i was there my food was burnt and turned over to hide it.  Like you wont notice and egg burnt black on one side.  I gave up on them

Why five stars? Because i love hole in the wall diners! First time at El Cap and i was so surprised, the decor is a flashback of Tampa Bay history. The walls are loaded with events from our history and man did I flashback! I am sure the events have been on the wall since they happened, if it ain't broke don't fix it. The whole place screams history and i bet you Burg types have some drunken el cap stories!! 
The staff is exactly what you expect, older ladies who look like lifers with new blood added as they retire. They all joke and talk with each other and the customers, i did. 
The menu is loaded with all sorts of lovely delights that'll send you to an early grave, but what a way to go. Burgers, fries, cheese, & beers; the four main food groups. 
I had a cheeseburger with bacon and fries. You can tell right away it's fresh beef, and the bacon was crunchy. The burger itself was 7 inches tall and i had to Scooby doo smash it down. The fries reminded me of McDonalds a little, but better flavor. 
Do yourself a favor and try El Cap just for the Tampa bay history decor!

Second trip to Chuys during Covid, tables distanced and servers masked up. I got Fajitas and margaritas, was happy with both. The inside is full of framed photos of dogs. I asked my server what that was about and he informed me if you bring a framed photo of your pup you get a free app. The walls are covered already, and it was obvious Land o' Lakes loves Dogs.
The rice and beans were average, the free chips were good as the dips were tasty. Margaritas were standard with many variations as is the usual these days. They were refreshing and cheap if you dine in. Is it the best tex mex in town, no; but it'll do. 
If you're so inclined swing on by and get some Decent Tex Mex.

Popped in here after The st pete pier grand opening weekend. I could sure use a cold one, it was hot. Upon entering we were greeted by a black golden doodle (i think) and made our way to the counter. Not a terribly big place a few tables and spots at the bar, it had a few other couples. 
The menu is tv screens on both side of the bar and I saw a favorite craft, and started drinking right off to cool down. Dark and delicious it was perfect temperature. 
The decor is as you might assume from the name, could be boat props i suppose but in this case it's airplane props. One is even above the bar hanging like a treasure. We got a table in a little back room and got to talking. Nice and quiet cool vibe. 
We were already full but they have a snack menu which I only glanced at. Just enough to get you thirsty again.

After a few stops for drinks and apps, we walked over to the Rusty Lyon. It was only 8:30 but the place was full, outside seating, inside and a rooftop bar. The outside seating was a covid thing and not that great. The rooftop bar was a nice alternative, great view of the street and surrounding buildings. Cool breeze and after drinks we ordered some food. I got the pork chops and I shouldn't have been surprised it came in a to go box. The chop was delicious, though hard to eat with a plastic knife. The tater tots i got were great, hot and crispy. I had nachos earlier so i wasn't terribly hungry, but everything was already to go. The drinks were strong and i loved the blue old fashioned. 
They had all the necessary covid precautions and the open air made me feel safe. 
Will I come back, probably not; but You can have a good time if you swing by and check out the roof top bar.

Nestled in a dumpy strip mall is one of the best Pho spots in Pinellas. Homeless people on the benches by the road are a common 
Occurrence. Once you get inside the decor matches the outside al la 1970's bingo hall. 
The food is what people come here for, and the prices are awesome as well. 
I almost always get the #10 Pho and a Thai tea. It's the one with all the crazy meats most people turn their up at. Tripe!! Mmm chewy!!
At lunch usually I go early at 11:15 or so and the Pho comes out quickly. I wolf down the hot  soupy goodness and escape like I stole the 
Sriracha.  I tried the egg rolls once and they were delicious and fresh.
Don't care about trendy decor? Do yourself a favor and try this place. If you go at night watch out for crackheads, they are super sneaky.

I've been going to the pub for a few years now, when I first went we sat upstairs. Before covid they had a wall of beers, the server gives you a card. You walk up, tap the card, and pour your own beer! I was astonished, I can get my own beer anytime?!! Haven't checked on if that is still a thing. 
Family birthday dinner walked up to cheesecake factory....2&1/2 hours wait. Wow, the cake is not that good. My bro in law went on a search for an 8 top at 5pm on a Saturday. The pub had an upstairs outdoor table, Yay!
We sat down and two members were missing. The server took our drink orders and left. 
I got the bangers and mash and they were good, not great. English food is already behind the 8 ball IMO. 
It seemed like everyone else got fish n chips, they had several sizes to choose from. The photo is the large fish n chips. Everyone loved the fish n chips, so they must be good.
We talked and laughed, I got tipsy. We had a great time.
It's not Yeoman's but Do yourself a favor and swing by the pub. The beer cheese is damn good too.

An hour wait on a Tuesday?!? Apparently the blue haired retirees love this spot and they take over from 3-8, after that it's Matlock reruns, ben gay applications, and bedtime. One of us remembered to check and make a reservation, so we only waited like 20 mins. After we sat we chatted and ordered drinks as soon as he came with the menus. The table got two bacon apps, crab cake, some kinda shrimp deal, and I got the lobster bisque. The soup was fabulous, thick, and creamy. It reminded me of Bern's steakhouse bisque! I tried the bacon and wow that was amazing. It makes first watch's bacon taste like Hot McDonalds dumpster garbage! So thick!!
My entree was the pork chop, no sides as they are   À la cart. I chose the glazed baby carrots but never received them hence the four stars. The poor server looked frazzled as most hospitality workers look in 2021. The chop was cooked perfectly and I would get it again. No dessert. 
My buddy Vic paid for the whole table as this was kinda a business meeting. If it's free it's for me!! 
What a great way to try this place for the first time.
Do yourself a favor come on over the bridge (Tampa yelpers) and try this highly rated meat dispensary.

Had this place bookmarked for a long time now, I made my way down to the young mens fight club,Ybor city. I walked in and it was slow, two tables and I. Got my drinks and ordered Lamb vindaloo with some garlic Naan. The food came out by the time I was done snapping pics and scrolling Yelp a little. The Naan was delicious and slightly burnt in some spots. I love a little burn on bread it changes the flavor. The rice was good after I covered it in Spicy Vindaloo. I ate all the meat and half the rice, and dunked the Naan into the leftover Vindaloo sauce. I didn't order 3 stars or 2 stars. It was the way they make it in India. Hot! My lips were burning afterward and I loved it. The meal was fantastic, it was quick and steaming hot. I will be back sometime soon for this amazing Indian food. 
If you want good Indian food and can brave the perils of Ybor. Do yourself a favor and come try this place out.

Since my journey into social media I have reconnected with some old friends, Brian I have known since high school. He's a great guy and I found out he has a restaurant. So off I go into parts unknown(why would I go to hernando beach, clearwater is right there) and there I was. I was seated immediately and asked for the chef. I explained who I was and she happily walked off to get Brian. We chatted, caught up, and I asked what's good. He showed me the colored choices on the menu and that's what i got. Tostones with crab, and the signature grouper with plantain 3 ways. 
Growing up in Tampa I have lived my whole
Life with easy access to amazing Cuban food, Ybor city. So I was stoked he has a Cuban American restaurant. I got the Smoked 17 for a libation and it was just as good as any old fashioned variant. The tostones show up and they are delicious, I might have burned my tongue because i couldn't stop. The grouper came and it was like an art piece in downtown, beautiful. I love when chefs take the time to make the food visually pleasing. Anyone can slop some mash on a plate and sprinkle parsley. 
The meal was great, the prices were amazing for what i got and yes I'm going back to try his ribeye. 
Why should you go out there and check it out? I'll owe you one and I never welsh a promise.

Stopped by southern brewing without eating and after a few porters my friend and I were hungry and getting buzzed. Quick check of yelp earlier I already had a game plan to come here. We arrived and it was already abuzz with hipsters. This one guy had jeans so tight we thought there was going to be a fire. We headed up to the counter which is in the exact same place the original store had their window. A board next to the window had the menu on it. I already knew what I wanted, the Korean cheesesteak. The sides all looked good but I was in the mood for some onion rings. The beer selection was just enough that anyone could find something they like. I got the hidden springs seasonal,which turned out to be the Deja Moo. 
Paid the bill and sat on the "inside seating" which was a lovely addition to the building,the garage door was open but it was nice and cool inside. We had a chance to observe the hipsters in their natural habitat. The food cam and it was great. The bun and meat and kimchi blended perfectly. The onion rings were awesome,drizzled in aioli and bacon chunks.  The mostly unused portion of the old store was transformed into a hipster playground. Ping pong,shuffleboard,bocci ball and corn hole. Fans were placed around the perimeter but it was nice so they weren't fighting the heat. It's brand new and a great concept, parking is kinda small. 
Do yourself a favor and come do some hipster watching,just be wary of tight pants fires!

Arriving 30 mins after they open on Sunday turned out to be a great idea, this place filled up quickly! 
They have a sign proclaiming they are yelp top 100 and boy did they deliver on the hype.
They have outside seating and a big dining room with bar seating available as well. 
We started with coffee and tea respectively and the coffee was great. From what I could see the tea selection is vast, the box they brought was huge. 
After careful scanning of the menu I got a combo that was huge, the pancakes were way bigger than i anticipated and I was stuffed by the time we left. Everything I ate was delicious, and I would recommend it highly. The server gave me the option to substitute and I chose grits instead of taters. 
We ordered  Mimosas and had to wait until 8 to drink alcohol, what drunks we are!
Do yourself a favor and try this Cafe it lived up to the hype.

I am second generation Tampa Native and I have been going to O'Briens pub since i was legally able to drink. My friends and I spent many a St Paddy's day getting smashed and fighting in the parking lot at the old location. 
I love this pub, and it has a ton of regulars that show up every single weekend and weekday to drink, eat, socialize, and have a good time.
There is inside and patio seating (dog friendly& smoking allowed) a stage, and an area to chuck some darts. The patio has huge A/C units for summer and heaters for winter.  There is live music on weekends and trivia on Wednesdays, and other things going on during the week. 
The bar is fully stocked with whatever you need to get your Guinness fix or hard liquor buzz. They have a great happy hour and I have enjoyed it many times. 
The food is typical Irish Pub food and I really enjoy the Shepards pie, bangers and mash, and their burgers. It's a big menu with many different choices for the whole family. 
The St Patricks day celebration is a huge event with all kinds of locals and regulars coming out of the woodwork to Party like the Irish. 
Do yourself a favor and give them a try, maybe you'll become a regular too.

Came in for lunch on Thursday at 11:20, only a few other customers. We were socially distanced in our seating with hand sani and a sign that said "1. sanitize hands 2. Masks on 3. sani wipes and wait to be seated."  As I sat down someone else was leaving and the table was bussed and sanitized immediately. I already knew i wanted Pho. I ordered the Tasty pho regular size and it was huge. I got Thai tea with Boba and deep fried egg rolls. The tea came quickly and was followed soon after by the egg rolls. The tea was great, sweet and chewy boba gathered at the bottom. 
The egg rolls were hot and crunchy with a great sauce to dip them in. 
Looking around I saw a nice decor clean, sharp and 4 or 5 televisions on the wall. The server area and prep area were clean looking. 
The Pho came right on time after my app, the regular size is big for Pho standards. Meat was plentiful and delicious, the noodles were a clump in the bottom and I had to pull it apart to get at them. Once the basil, jalapeño, sprouts, hoisin, siracha were added i mixed and pulled and off we go! Went a lil hard on the heat and my nose started getting runny, but i love it. Pho really cleans you out and fills you up at the same time, amazing hangover cure btw.
I completely enjoyed the meal and the staff was just attentive enough without going over board.
I will be back again and again. 
Do yourself a favor swing by Little Saigon sometime and dive into the amazing Vietnamese food culture.

I've been going to Crab shack for years and never had a bad meal. I love this place. It's old, small,and looks like it was made of driftwood. The dining room has picnic tables and the bar is shiny from all the wear over the years. 
Quick 2021 update, the supply chain is broken and They didn't have any mullet, the crab selection was limited. Call ahead to check availability. 
Took Pops here for his birthday as this is his favorite seafood restaurant. He got there ahead pf me and ordered a dozen raw sea boogers(oysters). I sat down and immediately started wolfing down said pearl makers. They were big and delicious. No mullet, no king crab, so I got Dungeness crab with fries and some cajun soup. It was just as I expected, amazing. The crab could be eaten without butter it was so good. I think people don't really like seafood, they just want an excuse to eat more butter. 
The fries were smokin hot and kinda look like Mickey D's fries. The soup was chonky & filled with all kinds of ocean dwellers. Pops makes a mean gumbo and he said this was better than his. 
I will continue to eat at crab shack till I die, worth every penny.

Having seen A lot of my yelp friends going here and leaving great reviews, here I am jumping on the band wagon. What a great meal and a good experience, i kept laughing every time a bartender climbed the ladder. 
I started off with a Knob creek-rocks and yes they have the Giant ice cubes. I started looking at the menu and stopped at Candied Bacon! 
I kept going and thought why not continue the breakfast theme and i ordered the Chicken and Waffles. After a few more drinks I ended the madness with a Whiskey Cake, and boy was it good. Hand whipped cream beats cool whip any day and i was so satiated i almost fell asleep in my seat. 
The Bacon was amazing, pickled veggies paired well with it and the sauce to dip in was creamy and amazing.
The Chix N Waffles was a thing of beauty. The gravy really put me over the top, it was good.
What can I say about the Whiskey Cake? Mmmmmm! You seriously have to try it for yourself, words don't do it justice. 
Valerie the bartender was great she had great drink variations and I let her pick my cocktails based on my Knob creek order and man did she deliver. 
Great meal, great staff and man this is a hot spot. 
Do yourself a favor and Go get a Whiskey Cake.

Back from the dead, The Bricks rises like the phoenix from the ashes of Covid. I've been keeping an eye on this place for a while now. They are open again! 
The menu has been chopped down to a manageable size. The staff is almost all new but the vine is the same. 
I came on a friday night early, like 7pm and they were kinda slow. Sat at the bar and ordered a bartender special, ask them what their best drink is and let them make it. I got a tiki type drink with mezcal that didn't have a name. It was pretty good and I liked the dehydrated lime, nice touch. 
I ordered the bird and pig sammich, i just saw honey and brie. It was fantastic, i ate every bite. The cabbage slaw was decent but I'd pick something else next time. 
They have coffee, full bar and creative meal ideas for a decent price. What else can you ask for in Ybor? Do yourself a favor, be the brick just waiting for a window to smash!

I like a good burger, and well executed it's amazing. Butter's did not execute well. I came on Friday night and the place was a ghost town. 9 people maybe, everywhere else was packed. Now I see why. I ordered an old fashioned and got a strange variation which wasn't bad just not authentic. I guess he was new and seemed a bit tipsy, maybe he was sad about the empty dining room. I ordered the smoked fish dip because a burger place doing a great fish dip can indicate how the rest of the meal will go. Or so I thought. 
I chose the franklin burger because of all the glorious pork added to it. Medium rare was my request and Dude even repeated it back to me. He also went back to tell the kitchen to make sure. It was dead, my order should have come out to perfection. After I showed him my burger fully cooked he said" i was worried, I've been having problems with the kitchen. I realize covid has made it hard to find good line cooks, it's all over local news. Burgers are real easy, McDonalds has built an empire on them and they suck. 
2 stars is for the front of house staff, they were friendly and attentive. The giant TV wall was kinda cool. There are great burger spots all over Tampa, and Butter's might not be one of them.

I have been eyeing this place on Yelp when i do map searches and finally got some takeout.
I ordered the lunch  special with 1 entree and one side; $8.99 which seemed reasonable. I got the Pad Kee Mao because i love those fat brown noodles and i got it hot because i love Thai spices.
 The side was egg fried rice and it was decent ;clumpy , so i could grab it with the chopsticks.  The Pad kee mao was really good with the heat and spices perfect to light up my taste buds. After i ate it i was full, totally satiated and, happy. 
The inside was small and clean and plenty of light from the windows, and i only got takeout because  30 minutes isn't enough lunchtime. 
The place has good reviews and i thought i might as well add mine to the mix. Do yourself a favor and stop by for a good meal at a good price.

Tryed this out on a first date, and the meal was fantastic. We had a little wait and were seated. Server comes and we order drinks. She got a tea and they didn't have Splenda.(they have the pink and blue ones) i had a Knob creek and it was a good pour. Drinks come and we order food, i got the volcano roll. It's Tuna and was great with plenty of flavor. She got some sushi too not sure what it was, we were too busy talking and laughing. It took about 30 mins for the sushi to come out, but the chefs were right next to is and they were chopping their butts off. 
The server was kinda new and forgot to bring my date a water but other than that it was great. 
Like sushi? Stop by and get rid of those blues!

First time in Glory Days during Covid was a strange experience. I was alone in the dining room for 90% of my meal. First impression was this is built for watching sports, but the lack of sports was apparent. I saw a round of cornhole competition with the players in masks. 
I often pick something simple during a first visit, if they get this right then game on for my next visit. I chose a Bacon cheddar burger xtra bacon, waffle fries come with it. The burger was cooked perfectly. The fries were crispy & just average not bad but not wow. Dessert was great, an Oreo slider which is exactly what showed up. It was an amazingly sugary treat with chocolate sauce to dip it in. 
The server took great care of me and wore ppe during the meal. I am not worried about covid, thanks to my amazing immune system. I felt like they were serious about safety during the pandemic. 
I was happy with my meal and I will come back again if i want to stay close to my house.

This is a great bar, and Bryt and I always have a great time. The drinks are stiff and decent selection, the staff is great and Bryt's brother fired a bartender in key west and saw her here when he visited!!! Ackward, i was laughing.

Now that i have been to three different Frenchys in Clearwater beach, I can say they're pretty much the same. This location is  right on the main drag of the South beaches, hence the name. It has big outside seating and decent inside seating although they could use more, it was packed! 
The food was just as good as the other locations and service  was great. We sat in the bar, because the rest was full and had a great meal. The thing that caught my attention was the seasonal drink, It was an apple martini  with a holiday flair, slice of apple and cinnamon. It was delicious and I had two of them before we left. 
The bar manager swung by to check on us and i told him i liked the drink. He was so happy as he was the one that created it. 
Frenchys has been around Clearwater beach a long time, so do yourself a favor and find out why!

I liked the vibe, and This nice Lady was shooting her shot at me. (When women look at you for 10 seconds then look away and hope you notice) Sadly dating over the bridge is a deal breaker, so I didn't engage her. I parked in my free parking DTSP spot and walked over. Parking is sketchy so it was a good idea. Bier boutique is an gastropub located on the bottom of an apt complex. Built in customers! It's across the street from a beautiful park, so the outward views are great. I sat at the bar after trying to open the door that was locked, I walked past the outdoor seating and there was an opening. The bartender was busy, so I popped the QR code and perused the menu. Drinks came up first and I saw some great choices, all of them were variations of popular libations. I asked the bartender for his most requested drink and was rewarded with a Paloma that used Mezcal instead of tequila. It was smooth, complex, and delicious.
Casually swiping up on the page it continued onto food. Most of it I scrolled by till the bottom, usually the entree and/or dessert spot. I saw Steak and Horseradish sammy. Everything on this meal looked like an amazing combo of flavors and When I ordered it the bartender said" Yeah, that's the one!" I shouldn't comment on the candied bacon as if will draw you yelpers in like moths to the flame. Ever had million dollar bacon @ your local chain brunch spot.... it's garbage compared to this bacon. The bacon is so dark I almost thought it was burnt, I quickly discovered it was the Candy coating. I scarfed it down like a missionary coming off a fasting session! 
My next drink was a Peanut butter Russian, PB whiskey and a white Russian had a Baby!  It was great after that stellar meal. The prices are fair and It was full outdoors the whole time I was there. I will be coming back just to try some of the other booze and nom nom choices.
Do yourself a favor! Come by ,plop down, order a variant drink, and enjoy.

I just got this message from "M L" who is, I'm guessing, the Michael L who has left numerous responses to peoples' reviews here (said "M L" also uploaded the Philly Cupcake logo for the store on Yelp):

"you sound like you are from west philly and shop at the gallary or kmart.  we serve the Chanel of cupcakes, like it or leave it missy!  Brown Betty is old news and you go get your kmart pound cake dumpcakes.  Keep it movin silly girl and go back to west philly.  peace out"

These cupcakes are HARDLY "the Chanel of cupcakes".. and as to his like it or leave it comment, I already decided I'm leaving them, thanks.

Way to knock yourself down to a one-star review by insulting your paying customers.

Havertown isn't exactly a dining hotspot, but we do have some choice spots.  In a location which almost seems doomed, this newer little thai joint has survived.  It's an adorable little tiny spot, there can't be more than 20-25 seats available in this place.  They don't have a very extensive menu, which isn't a bad thing.  They have the standard thai fare.  I tried the pad thai (which isn't something I normally eat) and the spicy noodle (which is normally drunken noodles in other spots) and loved them both.  It's totally family run and the service is just fine.  The food came out freakishly fast.  I have many thai choices in my area, but honestly, I prefer this underdog!

This restaurant was the highlight of my week-long stay in Philadelphia. 

The Korean BBQ cheesesteak was incredibly flavorful and satisfying, blending the sweet tanginess of Korean barbecue with a gently-toasted bun.

But the Korean wings were the standout. They were crispy on the outside while also being moist and tender on the inside. When you bite in, the flavor explodes in your mouth; you won't be able to stop eating until they're gone!

And then there's the carrot cake. They don't say it's the best in the city for nothing.

Stayed here during our annual Food Blogger's Conference. When they close off Bourbon street for the day and your cab/lyft/uber can't get onto Bourbon...so you're forced to walk through the mayhem. And holy shit, is it mayhem. Whenever I walked out the door, the doormen would ask if I needed a cab and I'd just say no and catch a Lyft. No issues, no hassles. 

My room was on the 4th floor and was quiet. I didn't hear any street noise. The room was large. There was my own thermostat to control the temperature, a large television, a comfortable chair and a desk to do some work, a comfortable king bed with comfy sheets. No bed bugs, hallelujah. There was plenty of hot water, the water pressure was standard, I ordered room service breakfast my first day (filled in the card that hung on the door) and last days (called on phone) there and had spongey pecan pancakes with browned edges, crispy bacon and some good coffee. Had the same personable room service server. Both times breakfast was about ten minutes late, but I feel like that's almost every hotel ever.

All in all, this place was so comfortable that I didn't feel homesick. I had no problem sleeping. I'll definitely stay here again on my next trip, if I can afford it.

Ordered three beers during the UofA women's championship basketball game. Third beer smelled of urine and entire table confirmed the smell. 

Manager took one beer off the tab.

Unacceptable. Avoid this place.

I'm going to tell you before I even review it. This is the best Thai restaurant around. 

Since moving back home from the West Coast, I was having trouble finding a Thai restaurant that satisfied my need to equal sweet to hot. Thida Thai nails it. Every time. 

Jazz music? Check. Bring yo' girl, too.

Going back to my roots...
