Renee's has been my first DDD review is a very long time. Used to do one whenever traveling to a new destination back in my early days on Yelp.

After a good part of the afternoon sightseeing we came in for a late lunch. First of all after ordering our food, I always look for that Guy Fieri stamp of approval. Which wasn't all that hard to find. Although this place was a little. You see it's located in a strip mall set back on Tanque Verde. 

What we had,

The Tailored Tony. (Think of this as a updated version of a sloppy joe.) Organic beef in marinara, roasted red peppers, basil and provolone served on their organic toasted focaccia. Served with a small side salad.  

The wifey went with a small portion of apple, walnut & goat cheese salad with grilled chicken. It was a pretty good size for salad. Must mention the apricot black teas that we had. Which was mentioned in others reviews. They definitively hit the spot on a warm afternoon.

Classic Old Tucson... 

People out here just love preserving this area. This building itself is located on the site of El Presidio San Augustin a Fort dating back to 1775.

Their are several different boutique style shops inside covered open air courtyard.A few that should be mentioned are Art House Centro plus La Zia. A native arts & crafts store selling Native American jewelry. Old Paint Records was another that caught my eye. With new and used vinyl records, t-shirts and vintage old magazines.

Live music is played a few times a week in the evenings. Makes for a very chill kind of atmosphere. Great place to catch up with friends and or family. They do have a fairly large selection of local craft beers & several different margaritas. Which our group couldn't resist.

Do enjoy.

This is for a lunch review in the Audubon Bar.

It may be a bit skewed because of their landmark status, being built in the 1930's and not many reviews for the restaurant/ bar only.  

Upon arriving, we were informed that seating in the main dining room was closing shortly but the same menu was being served in the bar/patio. This was quite alright as both rooms were equally nice and were not too crowded.  

We were seated right away and while our drink orders were taken, fresh bread was left with us while we perused the menu.  

I decided on the Chicken Chorizo Carbonara with Quinoa pasta.  It was a very nice looking plate with lots of chicken and veggies in a cream sauce, I was just expecting a little more heat.  The chorizo was not as spicy as I am used to.  My wife went with small plates, the Rosemary Gruyere French Fries with house made tomato jam and the mini BLTs.  The tomato jam was the greatest. It had more heat than the chorizo and went well with the fries and the sandwiches.  

Next time I am in Tucson I would love to stay here for a couple of nights as there are so many positive reviews and stories about this charming inn.

Our first meal after a long journey...

We were pretty hangry after flying a good part of the morning getting down here. Bar Fly wasn't our first choice, but that's because stop #1 was closed on a Monday. Local beers for me and ciders for the better half are always something we like trying. That being said...

- 3 Daughters key lime cider
- Sweetwater mango kush is a good starting point. While perusing over the menu. I do especially read Yelp friend reviews when coming to a new place. This turned out a excellent choice for an appetizer. That being a Lobster Nibbler with warm butter and bread.

Most times when traveling to me it always seems like the Wifey orders a large meal. So I have leftovers for a late night nosh. True to form she ordered a Cuban sandy. And only could finish half. My sandwich turned out to be a Island Reuben with Mahi. Very nice place with outdoor seating that you can bring your furry friends. Our server Truman was very nice in offering up popular options for our meal. 

Live music available a few times a week. Makes for a very chill atmosphere. A good start to our trip. :)

Solid establishment.

I  have my fair share of thai food consumption and I will say Xiandu Thai is one of the best options in center city if you're craving for Thai food. I also want to comment on the customer service as we always get greeted by the front desk staff (regardless of the busiest lunch hours) and get seated with minimum waiting time. Waiters are very pleasant and provide us with plenty of space and time to decide on what we order, I never feel rushed and they're also knowledgeable with the menu items in case you have questions. Water is constantly being filled - I know it's a small thing that people may overlook but I do appreciate the small gesture.

Now onto the food, I often order their pad thai and pad kee mao (drunken noodles), both dishes are consistently good. Come in here for lunch special you'll get complimentary salad or tom yum soup. Other items that I would recommend include their tom yum noodle soup, if you're into bold flavors and craving for a bowl of hot noodle soup. I also loved that they don't skim on the ingredients, the tom yum noodle soup I got have plenty of seafood with good sized prawns and scallops! I've tried their green curry from my friend and it's also very good.  I've sampled some of their appetizers like wings and roti canai, it's as good as you can get from Penang and Banana Leaf in Chinatown. Thai tea is a bit watered-down and lack flavor, but still quite good and refreshing.

Overall, solid 4-star and I'll be coming back for lunch!

A Hidden GemOne of my favorite places in West Philly, almost all of philly. Great local spot for just damn good food at a great price. Amazing breakfast, Cheesesteaks, burgers, fried rice, bulgolgi cheesesteaks!?? Plus Lee and everyone working there is cool af. Great service, great food, what more can you ask for?? I actually moved out of Philly years ago but every time I come back I make sure I stop by Lee's at least once or twice when I'm in town. Do yourself a favor and just go to Lee's.

I found this place from a groupon offer and was excited to try it as I LOVE italian food. 

Upon entering, we were asked multiple times if we were using a coupon or groupon... not sure what the difference is, but ok... 

We were seated in the middle of the dining area in an awkward path between the bar and kitchen. There was a lot of traffic and it made dining less than great. 

The website mentioned BYOB, but we were informed there was a $20 corking fee (on Saturdays?). Yikes! We opted for a glass of wine instead... Wine was meh.

First course was potato leak soup, I've had better but it wasn't terrible. (this was the only option for soup.)

Second course we ordered a margharita pizza... what arrived to the table was clearly a regular pizza (sauce and cheese), no tomatoes or basil. Pizza was delish!

Third/Main course we ordered a pasta dish with chicken and sausage ( I don't recall the name of it). The portion was a good size, but the dish itself was bland. 

The staff was clearing the tables faster than we could eat, accidentally taking away my full wine glass. 

The waiter was good... very attentive and pleasant. 

We did not stay for dessert!

I was not overly impressed and will most likely not be returning. 

Plus: The "margherita" pizza was VERY good.

I've eaten at Joe's Crab Shack before when I was visiting the Houston, Texas Area and the Orlando, Florida Area when I was on vacation. I had a craving for it so I decided to look up for locations where me and found out that there's three within driving distance so I chose the one in KOP.

First, let me tell you that when me and my girlfriend walked in we were a little disgusted. It took a while for us to get seated when the place was not even busy. There were tables that still have dirty plates on them and the Hostess started cleaning the tables up while not asking us how many in our party or anything.

Second, there's really no supervisor to maintain order with their waitresses as she did not even come by often enough during our dine there. We were waiting for our drinks for a good amount of time and also when we needed refills that was a problem as well.

Lastly, when our food came I always take pictures of my food so i get give you Yelpers an idea what I ate before I actually try the food and let me tell you the food looked TERRIBLE. The food was over Seasoned and and the steampot I chose was The Bean Town Baked which consist of two whole Main lobsters, corn, a pound of sausage, potato, and clams. You can look at my picture I uploaded in the photo gallery watermarked DNP on the right hand corner. The lobster was all over the place and had no meat inside it. The shell is SUPER soft where you don't even need to use the cracker which threw a red flag something was off. The potatoes weren't even cooked all the way as it was still raw. The clams in there were mostly empty.

THE WORST PART ABOUT MY DINE HERE IS I GOT FOOD POISONING. I tried calling back the next day trying to talk to the GM of the place but the girl who picked up the phone was rude when I was trying to stay calm and be professional on the phone with her. I will never come back to this place again and I recommend others to not do so either.

Was treated to a birthday dinner with a party of 7 family.  We were greeted with enthusiasm and respect, which continued through the meal. Korean respect for the aged was well demonstrated with the owner talking us through the menu and making good recommendatiions. When I expressed interest in kimchee as part of the sides, she complied in abundance.  We ordered several apps including a nice kimchee pancakes and great steamed buns. Then we ordered a variety of entrees, including beef and pork bulgogi and shared. We actually got 3 sets of five sides with ample kimchee.  I very much enjoyed the pork bulgogi. And to cap the celebration, we got complimentary cinnamon tea with a mochi ice cream treat to share.  Now this is  our favorite Korean, having tried 3 others.;

Still feeling the heat from our ramen dinner date I was very much looking forward to something cool to put out the fire. We scouted out Krem while finishing dinner and headed over. We were greeted right away and were introduced to the ice cream, cake, and sauce concoctions that they make.
Despite some of the exotic flavors we played it safe with vanilla ice cream, vanilla cake, and chocolate ganache. We did not sit for long before we were presented with a tower of ice cream atop a cup of cake and chocolatey goodness!
 They really topped off our night as they were not too sweet and just the right amount. Service was quick and friendly. We are definitely planning on returning and maybe trying something a little more exotic!

I've gone back numerous times without updating, and it's about time that I do so.

Unfortunately, based on service by the older woman with the dark hair - whom we were informed was the owner (EEK, I'd hate to work for that woman if this is true) - the rating must be changed. It needs to reflect how poor this woman's attitude is. Watching her belittle wait staff (when they've been perfectly great and on top of things for our table, and seriously was one of the best we've had there, but will keep from naming names), belittle ELDERLY WOMEN that were just confused with where they should wait to be put on the list (and the fact that they arrived before me, and yet I was spoken to first and THEY were given attitude), and just generally have a snooty attitude that says, "I don't care about my customer service, it's not what I'm here to do"....... just no.

As much as I used to love this place, it's very difficult for me to convince anyone I'd like to have a meal with to accompany me to this restaurant anymore. It's disappointing, since this is one of the few restaurants that I can go to and sit outside WITH my dog after a nice morning at the dog park, but with that woman treating customers like crap and favoring other customers (you can watch her act snooty to some, and then overly happy with others depending on appearances), it's just hard to find anyone that wants to go anymore.

EDIT 9/15/11 (original second review made 8/23)
- I was just informed that this woman is not the owner. I will leave my original wording and review, as I mentioned that we were only TOLD that she was the owner (it IS good to find out that she isn't). This woman has been there every time I've eaten at this restaurant, and has had an attitude every time - either with myself and the party I was with, or with people before or behind us. I was also informed by the same person that I shouldn't lower my rating based on customer service, and should solely review on the quality of the food... Sorry, but customer service plays a HUGE role in someone's experience when dining. If I didn't want to experience the service, I would only ever order take-out.

Just like in paris. The smell is enticing once you open the door. 

Macaroons. Cheese croissants.  Madelines. The duchess cake. Lime tarts. Brioche.

I miss the days when this place just opened and everything was in stock and clean. Now its so popular the tables are dirty and my favourites are sold out by 3 pm. Ive come here for years when it was just half the size and there was only 1 or two staff there. Service was impeccable. I guess thats the price you pay for being the best parisan bakery in edmonton.

All the best of paris delicacies in a large cafe. Plenty of seats but they always seem full. The desserts are the closest thing to parisan goodies that u can find in edmonton. The only thing missing is the selection of crusty bread sandwiches in every delectable flavours like smoked salmon or mixed meats. But hey duchess cant be perfect. They do got sandwiches and soups but they are not what you come to this place for. 

My favourites are the salted caramel macaroons, lavender and the rose ones. Delicate and not overly sweet. 

The only issue is that there is so much sugar in everything I feel like im in diabetic ketoacidosis bc my sugar is through the roof. You cant eat too much of this stuff even if you tried. 

Ive had the coffee and chai latte which were both nice. A bit small for me as I am used to the ventis but I guess it leaves more snacking room. 

My only vice about this is that its not cheap. $1.50 a macaroon. And everything costs about $3-$8 an item. Only a small box and it can end up to over $50 easily. But for quality you will come back and pay those prices. When im feeling like being swept to a parisan bakery. I come here. I never leave without a smile. And who could with all those delicious treats.

Casual or romantic ambience.  Great tasting french food. Great service. 

The marc has been around for several years. And during the first year of opening I had several issues with the food. Initially quite disappointing flavours and poor service. But now this has all improved and has uped my rating from average to outstanding!

Located just off of Jasper avenue in a little corner (you wont drive by it unless you are looking for it) Theres ample street parking after 6pm. Before this its rather awful downtown metered parking. Reservations are easy to make via opentable. ANd make online bookings super easy. I did this about a month in advance and scored prime seating for a 630pm seating on valentines day.

Once arrived. They have a little coat check area to hang your jackets and the hostess is great for assisting with this.The restaurant is dimly lit and  has a modern feel without being too cold. It can be a casual dinner out with family or friends or a romantic dinner with a loved one. Although I personally think it would be a nice first date kinda place to impress! Lol. I was seated in a large booth in the corner right behind the hostess area. And I would have to say these seats are prime seating. Large enough for 2 people to little sprawl out and lay down. Nice. It was very intimate and I didnt feel cramped at all. This was one of my annoyances in the past. As previously I felt the seating was a bit cramped and too close to other patrons for comfort.

The food on my particular visit was outstanding. The complimentary bread was soft and warm. The steak tartar was decent. A bit mushy to my liking. The escargots were buttery and rich. The pate was a good portion. The Scallop entree was outstanding and highly recomended.  Every item on the plate complemented the dish. The flavours were rich and buttery and cooked to perfection and seasoned just right. The lobster sauce on top of the scallops was delicious. The steak  was cooked a perfect medium rare with lots of marbling but not overly fatty. This was not the case on one of my first visits for a pork belly dish which was basically a huge chunk of fat which was extremely unappetizing. I would have to say that these 2 entrees ( the steak and the scallops) are a must order. 

The beignets were soft but not as tasty as i imagined. But the sauces served with it really upped the wow factor as the caramel sauce was delicious. I personally dont understand all the rage about the beignets (Ive had better). But the chocolate cake was a delicious end to our meal. A rich chocolate dessert not overly rich or too sweet. The sauces accompanied with it and the crunchy walnuts made this dish. And I will definetly order this again.

The service is great. A great balance between friendly, helpful and nonintrusive. Everything was provided for without prompting but is brought fast upon request.

Mercers pub is a beautiful building with some tasty vegan dishes. 

My cousin is vegan so we came here for lunch. Suprisigly the dishes we ordered were good. I cant recall exactly but I did leave somewhat impressed. So the food was good. But what left a lasting impression was the amazing building and the hip bar that it encompassed. A neat vibe that was a breath of fresh air in this rather boring city. 

It felt like it had that big city old charm. And edmonton is really not that big. I love the charm and I could frequent again.

I have been going to melting pot for years since it opened. Everytime i have come there has been disappointments with service. The first time a waiter spilled sauces all over my brother when clearing the table OMIGOD. the second time they screwed up our order. the third, fourth, fifth times the service was mediocre. (for the high prices you expect decent service). but finally after three n half years...finally the service is up to par with the food.

The food is fantastic. Exotic and unique. I love the spinach artichoke cheese fondue. The coquevin cooking style really brings the seafood n meats to a new level. Dont skimp out on this.
For dessert, all of them are great but the yin n yang is simple and not overly sweet. 

so initially i would rate this 2 stars. but my experience today has upped it to a three! If they keep the service up to par for the prices in future visits. this place deserves five stars! love the food here. I cant believe its the only one in Canada!!! For once edmonton has something toronto or vancouver!!!!

i've come to realize that there are so few things i need when i go out to eat, and yet many, many a place fall woefully inadequate. 

when i first moved to philly, and by chance discovered oyster house, their late night happy hour was something of a destination. i would choose restaurants based on their proximity to oyster house, or even leave the house again just to go. i've aged considerably since then, and now struggle to stay awake past 9pm. it's no loss though, their brunch and dinner options have been just as delightful (though admittedly less budget friendly, i mean, buck a shuck is insane!), and without the horrendous wait.

brunch cocktails are solid, and a steal at $18 for endless refills, or the very reasonable $9-13 for the less ambitious. the boy and i agree the "judi is" is the best punch on the menu, but we're both partial to passion fruit, so you should just try them all and judge for yourself. 

clams and oysters always fresh, plump and sweet. i've never had a grainy, poorly washed or mushy, old raw product here. i think that's quite a feat. 

a summer ago i had a side dish for dinner with roasted yellow zucchini, parsley, goat cheese served with lemon wedges. i still make this side for dinners at home; it's simple, but a stunner. 

same goes for my sauteed scallops at brunch. the dish features bitter greens, corn, okra, and scallops in a light orange saffron sauce. the worst thing i can think to say about it was that the greens were a bit overpowering, and i would've perhaps liked to see another sweet element (sweet potato?) or a stronger acidic component (orange not very apparent in the sauce) to balance out the bitterness. this is a matter of personal taste though, and i really am splitting hairs.

i love this restaurant in the day. it's airy and bright; it's very casual but not dirty or rundown. the stairs leading to the bathroom seem a little perilous to me, but i am beyond clumsy so i won't hold this against them. 

the walls are decorated with ornate and unique oyster plates, which happen to be one of my favorite things. i like most of my life to run as efficiently as possible, and cannot tolerate clutter or excess. my only weakness is anything that goes in the kitchen. i love kitchenware that are so highly specific they are useless except for a single purpose. bonus if they're beautifully crafted, then hung on a wall rendering them completely useless. be still, my intemperate heart.

service is attentive but relaxed. i never want to flag someone down, but i also do not enjoy staff practically breathing on me as i'm easily made uncomfortable. oyster house has never strayed from that delicate balance of easygoing helpfulness. this place is a winner, guys.

What happened???
The bar was set pretty high for this restaurant, as my family & I used to frequently dine here. We haven't been back in a few years due to relocating.
While we stayed at the Peppermill across the street, the opportunity arose to come back for some yummy, authentic chinese food. So, we jumped on it & came by to grab some food to go. 
Upon arrival, we were greeted by blank stares.. From everyone including the employees. 
It was awkward. I felt like we were intruding.  After a minute or so, an employee came up to us (never said hello,) & asked if we were dining in or placing an order to go. We said we wanted to order to go & she directed us to the front counter & gave us menus. She came back to take our order a few minutes later. In the middle of taking our order, she randomly walked away. We felt really rushed to order.. 
Our bill came out to be 31$. I would've rather went to Panda Express! Atleast Panda Express can make better chow mein & chinese food in general, for way cheaper. 
We don't mind paying for quality food, but during this last visit, we felt really let down. Our food had no flavor. It wasn't made with love & that was evident. More so, just cooked & thrown together. 
Our crab rangoons were frozen & then fried. They had very little filling & I couldn't find any crab meat inside.  
I could've bought frozen crab rangoons from the store & fried them at home.
Neither myself nor my family, will be back.
This place has greatly changed over the years.. Not for the better! 

Cons: Mediocre food, sweltering restaraunt that has the dining room in the same space as the kitchen, awful service, expensive prices.

Pros: There was a cool fish tank that kept my son occupied while we waited for our meal.

Will I ever get tired of coming to Doughboys? No!
Why not? Simply because Doughboys makes the best donuts on planet earth!! (No exaggeration whatsoever.) I've had a lot of donuts from many different places, but these donuts are on a level of their own! 
Doughboys is a place that I could visit every morning for a pillowy soft, fresh donut.

Love coming in & picking from the wide arrangement of cute donuts; sprinkled, jelly filled & more.
Doughboys also has yummy bagels too. Their bacon, egg & cheese bagel is the BOMB. 
Employees who've helped me are always in a great mood & are willing to assist! Cleanliness in the store is a 10/10.  
It's convenient that there's a drive thru here too ! 
Doughboys deserves 5 stars for their donuts, their customer service & their cleanliness! 
Do yourself a favor & try even just one of their donuts. Promise you'll be hooked for life!(;

If you're looking for a solid burger, run to Lucky's. This restaurant is one of the best in Main Street Manayunk, from their food to their service, they do everything right!

It took me a couple of visits before I got the courage to order their infamous peanut butter, jelly, and bacon burger because let's be honest it sounds so strange. But I'm so glad I finally did. It's now my go-to item on their menu full of many, many other delicious options. In my opinion, it definitely deserves all of its awards. It's served on a crispy brioche-like bun, strips of bacon, slathered in melty peanut butter with a side of homemade jelly. Who knew peanut butter and jelly would taste so good on a burger?

All of their other burgers are solid choices as well. They have quite a few options to suit many palettes. I've also tried their tater tots which are superb.-- served cripsy and hot just like any potato should be. 

The servers and bartenders are amazing people. Everyone I've encountered here is always super friendly, there's absolutely nothing I could complain about.

PROTIP: get a feel for your table's airflow before picking a seat, because being downwind from a grill spewing meat smoke is NOT ideal. OR leave it to fate to russian-roulette who gets the smoke chair. I was not so lucky.

Meat speaks spiritually to a good amount of people, in dulcet yet carnal tones, so it's no surprise that KBBQ is the breakout star of the moment for Reno -- not quite as hounded as bottomless sushi yet more sought after than artisanal salad bowls. SIU's meat-first focus taps into a quintessentially American craving ("beef, pork, chicken, mmm"), but it also highlights the trickiness of mainstreaming Korean and Asian flavors.

To start with the pros, the meat's good. The marinade on the bulgogi cuts, both chicken and beef, is tame but tasty. The lemongrass pork was delicious, and the spicy pork belly is DANGEROUSLY addictive: not to be missed! Comparing quality, freshness, and flavor to other KBBQ cuts in town, SIU takes the cake. Their side dishes mostly harken back to standard Chinese delivery fare: not really elevated, but reliably tasty. The fried wontons and dumplings are great, if not pork-heavy, breaks from grilled meat, and the sweet potato fries are decent for snackage.

I think my biggest gripe with this place is that even its AYCE set-up leaves me unfulfilled when it comes to Korean cravings. The banchan was disappointing: everything was a little bland save for the fish cakes; the lack of standout taste made the spread of four default sides seem smaller and even less varied. The kimchi soup had no kick to it. And most importantly... no haemul pajeon?! I don't necessarily expect KBBQ to accommodate expansive á la carte options (meat is the prerogative, duh), but as of now, SIU seems to specifically fall short in delivering uniquely Korean touches in favor of more familiar, broadly Asian taste. If anything, SIU's flavors are Korean-adjacent... if that. Luckily, what this place lacks in well-rounded authenticity, it makes up for with filling and delicious quantity. The promise of meat is more than enough.

Regardless of whether it's the trend du jour or a revolution on the rise, for now, KBBQ is an absolute welcome burst of fresh umami air for a market that so far has been a little iffy on tackling bolder Asian options. There's yet another foot in the door for Korean flavors in this city with SIU; they may not be the ones to fully kick it ajar, but here's hoping they grow to let some more authentic kickass eats in.

This past week has been full of back to back fudged dining plans and frantic Yelp searches for last minute backup restaurants, which tells me that I either need to start making a better habit of calling ahead to snag tables or just keep letting fate haphazardly guide me to new restaurants.

After finding Centro packed to the brim for a noon lunch, I rallied my party of five to book it just down the street to SoDo. It's exactly what you'd expect from a New Americana spot. The interior is simple, clean, and sleek; just hip enough to feel unobtrusively casually modern. The lunch menu mirrors the vibe of the interior, offering up a compact set of standard options with enough sprinkles of nuanced influence and flavor mixed in to feel tactfully bourgie.

Eager for a meatier bite, I went straight for the SoDo Burger. It's definitely one of their most basic true to form offerings; it's just a regular midscale cheeseburger. Reasonably good, but I was a little disappointed that it wasn't cooked evenly. I asked for it medium rare, but it ended up being a weird gradient of mostly medium well. The burger also comes with a chipotle chutney (be sure to ask for it on the side if you want it; it's not a given!), which I had mixed feelings about. I appreciated the punch of flavor, but the blend of bright and smoky just wasn't balanced enough for me. Luckily, the regular burger pulled through with enough beefy goodness to stand on its own.

The fries were most definitely satisfying, but I can't quite get over the fact that they were basically Burger King fries with a better crisp and cut. I love me some BK, so it's not a hard and fast complaint but drawing that connection kinda left me needing an extra dash of flavor from them: garlic rosemary, perhaps? Overall, I was satisfied but not super impressed by my lunch here, and the bump to a four-star is mainly because I finished my mom's fajita wrap leftovers later that night, and it was frickin' delicious.

Ultimately, SoDo was s'alright. Like so many downtown spots, it offers up some reliably tasty options. With so many more enticing menus and surefire flavors in the area, though, it may take a while for me to double back.

This place is a 4 minute drive for me, but for some reason I've always skipped over it for taquerias that are waaaaaay more out of my way. Feeling a little drained after today's morning workout, I was hankering for some good ole carne goodness and, in typical Taco Tuesday fashion, set my sights on Super Taqueria. I opted to travel on foot; adding an easy two miles to my running log for the sake of tacos is a win-win for me.

One scenic mile of jogging through office space limbo later: I skipped over the combos and went straight for a simple taco trio. Trying out chicken, pork, and beef is a pretty simple litmus test for any taqueria, and it tells you a lot about how they work with their meats. Of the three, I was most impressed with the carne asada. Fantastic flavor and perfect for a beef-fiend like me. The tacos al pastor were solid and tasty but seemed a little tough. The chicken was pretty mediocre and was in need of a lot of tenderness. The salsa verde was a great way to brighten up the flavors, but the salsa rojo seemed more like Tapatio in a dispenser to me. Still a little hungry, I opted for one last taco: the chicharron. I made the mistake of not asking how they serve this, and got a few hunks of chicharron guisado rather than the fried pork I was expecting. For those wary of fattier cuts, steer clear: this is pretty much gelatinous stewed pork rind. Decent flavor: I dug it, though I admit I probably won't make it a regular order. I grabbed an agua de jamaica to go for the mile back. Four tacos, a hibiscus tea, and a two mile run: I'd call it a successful quickie lunch.

I have to admit, I was a little put off by the ambiance. It was a gorgeous sunny day outside, but all the shades were drawn. The little light coming through felt more apt for an afternoon at a dive bar. Each time I tried to flag someone down to ask about brightening up the place, they'd run off to take a call or run an errand. No huge deal as I wasn't planning on staying for too long, but it just struck as weird that the feel read more as funeral home than taco shop. To top it off, the front-facing service felt really jaded and blasé. I'm not one to ever need service with a smile, but a smile definitely could have added some much needed light to the already dim space.

My takeaway from this meal was that the most "super" thing about Super Taqueria is its "super" heaping helpings of meat. These tacos were jam packed with a lot of meaty goodness, and that is absolutely nothing to complain about. I do wish the all-around quality could line up with the quantity, but at the end of the day, picking out the strengths of a restaurant you intend to frequent is a duty that falls on the shoulders of any avid eater; from my perspective, they do beef the best, and that's what I'll resign to stick to. The food here is solidly good but pales in comparison to the other taqueria gems that the area has to offer. Though far from my favorite in town, the sheer proximity and the opportunity to squeeze in some cop-out quickie cardio will keep me coming back to Super Taqueria for more beefy bites. Next up: caldo de res.

In honor of President's Day weekend, I decided to start my Friday night at City Tavern. Although horribly touristy, I was amused by the server's 18th century inspired costumes and overall feel of the bar area (I didn't eat any food there, just went to the tavern area). 
We decided to try the sampler which included all 4 beer choices, all of which are made by Yards. The beers are all old recipes from the time of our founding fathers, including a recipe made by Jefferson that is exclusively made for City Tavern. My favorite was the George Washington one, a very tasty porter, followed by the Poor Richard's spruce ale, which comes from a recipe made by Ben Franklin. The Hamilton one didn't do it for me, but it was nice to try. They give you a good amount of beer with the sampler too, so I'd definitely suggest at least starting with this. 
I'm not really thinking I'll make this a regular stop for me, but it was fun to do something somewhat touristy for President's Day. This would be a fun thing to bring out-of-towners or history buffs to.

This is a good place in the city for a happy hour when you have nothing else in mind. There is nothing spectacular about Ladder 15 but you know they will always have the same specials so it's worth keeping in mind. 
Happy hour every week day 5-7: 4-5-6 
$4 Beer besides Guinness (this makes me sad) 
$5 House wine and call drinks 
$6 specialty cocktails 

They used to have a martini that tasted like a thin mint girl scout cookie that made the $6 cocktails worth it, but last time I went they didn't have it. Sad. The lack of Guinness on the beer list also tends to keep me away from here. Hoegaarden, Victory, and Blue Moon are included among others, why leave off the deliciousness that is Guinness? 
Also, they have truffle fries that are pretty good bar food if you need munchies while you're there.

Each meal from PYT should probably come with a complementary "roll you out the door". That's right, I ate/drank myself into an i-cant-move-yet-wait-a-minute situation. Do I regret it? Absolutely not. When can we go back?
After being told that no one in their right mind could start their night with a milkshake and keep on drinking, I immediately ordered the double espresso milkshake which rocked my world (and got me quite buzzed... win) I ordered chicken sliders which were a-mazing. I don't even know why I ordered them. I hate chicken burgers. Always so so dry. Not these. Yum
I also ate part of my friends burgers, even though they didn't offer. 
The lamb burger almost caused me ordering envy. It was delicious, juicy, and huge!   Next time...

This is my go-to place when I have visitors in the city. The Afghan food is something a little different but is very approachable. And Ariana's does it right!  A couple can eat here for easily $35 including tip. My favorites include - Appetizers/Sides: Aashak, Burandee Kadu, and Buranee Badenjan (you can pick three as a sampler kind of thing) Entrees: Lamb Corma, Norange Palow, and Badenjan Chalow. Go for the lamb over chicken, it is so tender! Also, they have delicious ice cream that is definately worth trying. The service is very unassuming but great. It is also a BYO, so don't forget a bottle of wine. Side note: if you have a group of four, ask for the table in the window. It is traditional style dining (sitting cross legged on the floor).

Warning: if you bring out-of-towners to Reading Terminal Market, they are sure to show up on your doorstep again asking to go back. Reading Terminal is also known to cause sensory overload. 
This is THE primary choice for lunch when I have friends from out of town visiting. I have yet to eat at the same stand twice and have never been short of pleased by my meals. Be prepared to be a bit overwhelmed with your culinary selections: there is everything from Amish comfort food to Iraqi inspired treats.
The actual market is also worth visiting. Extremely fresh fish, vegetables, and fruits can be found on the side near Market East; a great place to stop on your way home from work (the market is open until 6 pm on week days). Also, the prices are fabulous! 
The best part of Reading Terminal for at-home cooks though would have to be the Spice shop, located near the Beer Garden (yes, there is a beer garden; beer selections are meh though). They have every spice you can think of all for MUCH cheaper than you'll find anywhere else. Note: the spices are packaged in little baggies, so you'll need to have your own containers to transfer them into.
 I will be here soon to stock up on my fresh foods for the week, and cannot wait until another friend visits so I can try yet another stand!

Iovine Brothers is my go to for any and all fruits & veggies i may need. I have somehow never spent more than $20, even after trying to purchase through this threshold. The staff is always super pleasant (even when I show up at 5:50 pm when they close at 6). I find the selection to be quite impressive, I can't really think of a time I wasn't able to find an ingredient. Glad to have this as an option!

Good cheap eats that delivers!  After my second visit, the owner, Scott, has managed to remember me and what I ordered and make new recommendations accordingly.   The cheesesteak ($4) is greasy and delicious, and the handmade crab cake sandwich (onlh $3.50!) is equally satisfying.  Definitely check out this cozy neighborhood joint.

Having tracked O's progress up until its opening in April, I was excited to try it out. The place itself is BEAUTIFUL and successfully delivers the perfect mixture industrial and organic elements (take a look at the succulent wall behind the bar). Unfortunately, that is the most positive thing I can say about O. 

I went on a Monday night soon after O opened. It was about 7pm and it was not busy at all. There was a large party in the middle of the restaurant and a few people at the bar, but the restaurant itself was overly occupied by staff. A host wanted to sit myself and two of my friends at a table right next to the party instead of at a table away from the party or any table for that matter since the restaurant was empty. I requested a booth and we were seated there. The server we had was very friendly and attentive, but the managers were overly attentive especially when we were the only table other than the big party. It was an awkward environment overall, because the industrial look of the restaurant and the lack of music playing made it feel cold and empty despite the staff walking around. A group of hostesses were gossiping with one another at the hostess stand. The restaurant seemed overstaffed for a Monday night. 

I tried the following menu items:

~Table side guac ($9.5)- The person making the guac did not try to interact with us and did not ask us how we wanted our guac made. He made it too spicy. It was a very silent and awkward experience.
~Pork belly norteño ($12)- This is comparable to a bagel bite, but with pork belly. I couldn't tell there was even pork belly on it.
~Carne asada with chimichurri ($24)- This was your average steak with chimichurri sauce. It was served with a salad. For the price, you'd think you'd get more bang for your buck.
~Assorted tacos ($18)- An assortment of 3 tacos. This is very overpriced for not so memorable tacos. 
-Gaucho steak ($35)- This was actually delicious. It was served with fries and butter on the side. 

I think I caught O on a bad night, especially considering it was their first week. I hope they have grown since then, but the mixture of mediocre food and high prices does not make me want to return. There are so many inexpensive Mexican restaurant options in Tampa and all of them are good, but if you're looking for an upscale Mexican restaurant, go to Besito. It's delicious, warm, and lively. O would be the choice if you want to pay more for what you get.

Visited Fusion Bowl earlier this week with a group of friends and it was a hit with everyone. I usually am scrambling to decide what to order, but not this time. Someone recommended getting the pork and egg roll bun, which I did. I did not regret it. I also tried the iced honey green without boba. It was tasty and refreshing. If anyone's familiar with honey green tea from Kung Fu Tea, it has a similar taste, but not it's not too sweet.

Each part of the pork and egg roll bun was good. The noodles were just the right texture and temperature. The pork was marinated nicely and tender. The egg roll was good. The sauce is just right. The portions are also reasonable for the price. 

My friends also tried the same kind of bun, the tofu banh mi, and the udon. All of them enjoyed what they ordered. I can't wait to return to try the banh mi!

This is a hidden breakfast gem that we discovered from doing a yelp search for breakfast spots in the area. We were going to do the occasional outing with Cracker Barrel, but wanted to expand. Thankfully we read reviews about lengthy wait times in the morning and we ordered ahead of time.

My wife went and picked up the food about 25 minutes after they opened and she said it was already a 40 minute wait for a table. Calling a to go order was the best idea that day :). 

The food was quite delicious. The French toast was thick and cooked perfectly with a ton of strawberries to top it off. The bacon was decent, but average at best. The chocolate chip pancakes were large and delicious as well. We will be ordering here again to enjoy this lovely gem!

Four words to describe Duck Donuts: Deliciousness in a box! I was familiar with this donut concept from another amazing donut franchise in Tampa, FL, but my wife and I moved shorty after we discovered it, so we were only able to indulge for a few months :(. This was heartbreaking for me because I have a huge sweet tooth. My face lit up after we walked in to Duck Donuts in Marlton.

We finally went to Duck Donuts yesterday, as it was highly recommended to us by a co-worker. Pretty much everything mirrored that of the other franchise, except the Donuts were larger. Unfortunately, the lines were extremely similar. We waited in line for about 15 minutes to order and then another 10 for the actual donuts to come out, but man were they worth it.

The Donuts were perfect. I had the maple bacon donut as it is my absolute favorite. The donut almost dissolved in my mouth with the bacon pieces staying intact to finish each bite out with a crunch. The donut was not overpowering with sweetness and was the perfect combination I was looking for.  I do feel bad for their washing machine as their aprons were covered in icing, lol.

We ordered a 1/2 dozen donuts and 2 regular coffees. The total came to about $15. This will be a regular stop for us, but we know we will have to carve out some time for the line. Don't let the line discourage you. This is a hot new location that will be buzzing for months! Yelp will assist in blowing this up even more and bringing attention to these amazing holes of deliciousness!

This place is way over rated! I thought about giving them 1 star to offset the current biased reviews but 2 is much more accurate. We eat out quite a bit and are regulars at places like The Refinery, Edison, Side Bern's, Elevage, Pane Rustica, Mise en Place, CRU, etc. so we know good food and we are not gluttons. 

So, where to begin...

Positives: The food is fresh and very well prepared, yet the servings are miniscule.  The place is well designed, yet very small. The staff is extremely friendly.

Negatives: The servings are ridiculous and the price is very high for what you get. We ordered a nice array of plates from their menu, approx 3 per person, and honestly were ready to go eat dinner afterwards at the Refinery. 

Overall Summary: This place needs to increase their food portions or lower their prices. Plates like cauliflower should have more than 3 little pieces on it. They say their food is for sharing. What are we supposed to share the crumbs? 
We spent $40 per person on food alone and all left hungry. As of now I would Rate this restaurant as Avoid.

If it ain't broke don't fix it.  When it comes to doing one thing right and repeating it Café' Du Monde has that down to a science.  You get one thing to eat beignets, and about 5 drink choices and that is it.  You want an egg go get one not there!  They've got it down so good they only take cash, have only spoons.... why you ask?  Because you tear the beignets apart with your fingers and a few plates.

We arrived each day we were there around 8:30-9:15 got in right away and they're open 24/7.  We got our table, placed our order and before you could yell HOWDY!!!!!!!!!!! we were well on the way to a doughy sugary induced food coma and God love them for that.

It sounds touristy and it is but sometimes you just have to say to heck with it and go somewhere everyone else goes.  We did and are better people for it.  Oh and if you're carb counting, on a diet, gluten free, vegan, blah, blah this definitely not the place for you.  If you're looking to recuperate from a hangover, get a little sugar, caffeine, dough and lard in your belly then jump in the water is fine.

we've all seen the Desire sign the restaurant is in the Royal Sonesta and as an Oyster snob I flat out love this place from the bottom of my grimy heart!  They source great seafood, good beer and for an Oyster Bar that is all you need.

We sat down and had our beer before you could blink it came so fast we almost got "beer burn" then once again the oysters were soon to follow!  So thank God for whomever invented stretchy pants.......... Why don't we know this persons name?  Why no Nobel prize?  National Holiday?  We live in an unjust world.  Ok tangent over.

When you go to a tourist area you expect some digging into your pocket.  We had a meal with booze for just about what we would of paid in Atlanta for the same thing so you've got that going for you.  Again the staff were all the nicest folks, and they took excellent care of us and when I'm in need of Adult Disneyland I'm heading back to NOLA!

Holy Crow the last time I saw that many fine specimens of dogs was at The Westminster Dog show!  We were headed to Frenchman's street a true jewel in and of itself......... beats Bourbon street up and down the block!  This is a semi local area where the beers are $5, great entertainment, and everything reasonably priced.  I digress so we asked the concierge at the hotel, a policeman, the cab driver, and a security guard at a bar where to go on Frenchman's street for great food everyone said Dat Dog and man were they all right!

We both got the alligator dog $8.50 and the tater tots covered with etouffee' oh Mylanta the tots I could eat for a year straight and hope to be encased within them when I die!

We went upstairs and sat on the balcony and viewed all Frenchman's street had to offer and gazed upon the Star Wars Museum/Church/Mecca with sheer awe!  The food came out fast, hot and delicious....oops did I steal that from a pizza box?  To heck with it, everything was just that way.  The atmosphere was NOLA adult Disneyland if you bring children that's on you.  I don't go to Space Mountain so when in NOLA if I drink a little too much, get too loud, or an just obnoxious well I'm in NOLA. 

Dat dog is a really good place to eat not too expensive good food and great people.

I think people may be unclear about what kind of noodles are served here. This is (by and large) a Japanese style noodle house. That means they serve ramen, traditionally accompanied by nori (seaweed), a soft-boiled egg, and some type of pork. If you have never had ramen, or think those things are weird in noodle soup, then you might not be inclined to give this place a good review. 

That being said, their house ramen is really good! Pretty traditional, except that the broth didn't seem to be tonkotsu (pork bone) and was instead a beef based broth. Still, very tasty. Noodles are homemade, respect! I'm from San Francisco and have been to Japan, and this ramen is the best in the city (not saying much in Nola...). It's not as good as ramen in California, NYC, or Japan obviously, but it holds its own. 

I like that there are two different bowl sizes, so you can save room for pie. Also you can get extra noodles, or add more pork products to your bowl. Yay options! 

The small plates are more "Asian fusion." We got the short ribs, which were falling off the bone delicious. Also got shrimp korokke, which are like shrimp croquettes. These were ok, but the filling was like a paste with no discernible shrimp and the whole dish was really sweet. Too intense for me. Fried brussels sprouts were good, but how do you go wrong with that? I guess they were made Asian-y by the inclusion of panko. Although the panko was just sitting in grease on the plate instead of covering the sprouts. 

Pie!!! Ok so this is such a weird combo and I think that's why I resisted coming here for so long, even being the noodle soup lover I am. And I'm not going to say it works as a dessert for Asian food. But their key lime pie and chocolate pecan (I think it was pecan) were so yummy! In the future I would come for one or the other. 

Everyone was happy. This place is solid for either noodles or pie, whichever your heart desires. And so far, best ramen I've found in Nola!

Edit: people, this is NOT expensive! My bowl was $10! Do you have any idea how laborious it is to make ramen broth?? And they make their own noodles! That speaks to a higher quality product, which you should be happy to pay for.

Simple, fun, informal, good. This is NOT fine dining, and we loved it.
We stayed at a nearby hotel and wanted to try Reading Terminal Market for our late breakfast after a late night of election returns. Even though we both are trying to avoid grains and watch our diets, we opted for the Hershel's and the classic bagel-lox-cream cheese-tomato-onion sandwich. We are not meat eaters, the meat sandwiches looked great.
Very informal: order from the guy preparing food, go down to the other end to pay and get coffee. We are decaf drinkers, they only have caffeinated, so they sent us (my wife went) around the corner to a coffee purveyor. By the time she returned, our sandwiches were ready.
Lox piled high and very fresh. Bagels toasted to perfection. I inhaled mine, totally delicious.
Picnic tables with chairs nearby were convenient and luckily not crowded; I've been to RTM during lunch hour and it's nuts, forget finding a table anywhere. Our table was dirty from previous occupants. When I asked for a wet rag, I was pointed to a container of sani-wipes, pre-moistened, and I quickly cleaned off the table and chair. No problem.
I will definitely return to RTM and to Hershel's.

Never before in the history of my 400+ yelp reviews (wow, how did that happen?) have I encountered a business that had two missteps with me, and yet I give them 5 stars.  RH Cafe did just that.

Hubby and I visited on a rainy Sunday afternoon just wanting to experience the insane 4 story ultra-beautiful Restoration Hardware.  We had no intention of spending three hours, but we did, and we had no idea there even was a cafe.  And I have a lot to say about it, so get ready!

The environment is simply beautiful, I quite literally could not stop looking overhead at the gorgeous crystal chandelier, joined by amazingly realistic looking trees, and a 4 story domed sky light roof.

We now know after our bonding with staff (you'll learn why soon) that this RH is modeled after their Chicago property which is built in a former women's college, and the courtyard where the cafe is along with the lovely fountain and reproduction cast iron framework surrounding the arch windows is all to replicate Chicago.  It's a stunner.

We loved the solid marble dining table, and the fact that we sat on a yummy couch or if we had opted to there were grey upholstered rolling chairs, all loaded with great accent pillows.

Our server greeted us and about one minute after our beverages arrived, the building fire alarm went off.  And kept going, and going, and going.  This courtyard has a marble floor, huge panes of glass, and my head was pounding after about 30 seconds and this went on for probably 5 minutes - not kidding.  We saw managers running about and finally a guy from Nashville Fire came in and mercifully slayed the shrieking beast.  

I will say we had been about 2 minutes from leaving at that point, (it was really loud), but so thankful it stopped.  A manager came around a few minutes later apologizing again, and offering us a card from their hospitality director for a return visit on them.  OK, yes the alarm went on for a long time and yes it was annoying, but talk about a save to immediately make you realize they really do care and they acknowledge the fact that there should have been a quicker remedy.  (They've only been open a month). Wow.

We thoroughly enjoyed our appetizer, the smoked salmon.  It wasn't what I was expecting more accustomed to restaurants offering a smoked salmon dip, but you basically made your own bagels and lox but on Texas toast - the toast was still warm and buttery when we got it - nice.

For dinner (it was 5 PM by this point) I had the Truffled Grilled Cheese with fries.  It was good, but I'll be honest, I've got to stop ordering things with truffle oil just because it's popular and "the thing."  I will totally get the french dip that I almost picked next time.

Hubby had the Restoration burger that when he took his first bite, he was surprised that his "medium" burger was quite rare.  We used to own a beef farm, y'all, so we're not wimps, but this was too rare.  Our server popped by and when we showed her and asked if that was medium, she looked a bit puzzled and said yes, but she'd be happy to take it back to the kitchen for a refresher.  Well, hubby had cut the burger all adorned in half, and by that point taken 3 bites and convinced me to try a bite, so a re-do seemed a waste at that point - we should mentioned to her that they should warn diners their medium is a cool center.  I think she realized her misstep there, because a few minutes later the hospitality director stopped by our table and asked if the burger was perfect and wanted to take a look.  She appropriately insisted that a new burger be prepared and apologized, and when his new burger came out, he and I both agreed it was one of the best burgers we've ever had... I'm so glad she was on point and saved the day.

At this point we are happy - it's a beautiful place, we are stuffed, there were some hiccups but again they've only been open a month.  The bubbly manager came back to check on us with a plate of three of the most delicious cookies I have ever tasted (and I have eaten a lot of cookies!), apologized again, and said today's meal was on her as well.

We protested, gesturing to the card for a free dinner when we come back, and she insisted again saying there were too many hiccups today and she just wouldn't feel right.  We then got to chatting which is where we learned the history, Chicago references, etc. - such a delightful young lady.

Will we be back?  Of course we will, we have a free dinner card waiting!  But more importantly, we'll visit again after that because the entire team here really went over and above any customarily expected levels of customer service, and that's simply not something you find every day. 

And because I didn't work it in earlier, the cookie has two different types of dark chocolate, served warm, and sprinkled with sea salt on top.  Seriously, amazing. We had to split the one we brought home the next day to be fair - it's that good.

Wow! What an experience! Our server Justin also made this dinner experience memorable and was very prompt with our service as well as being such a great help and instrumental during our food selection process.

To start off, my partner and I have been eyeing Maypop for over a year. We came to New Orleans when Maypop had recently closed due to the pandemic and have never experienced it, and was saddened to hear they were closed until recently. 

When we found out they were opened again we were excited to try it, but we couldn't find time out of busy schedule to make our way in. Our friend is in town from Los Angeles and we thought it would've been a nice occasion to take him out to something we haven't tried yet so we chose Maypop because we wanted to go. 

We called around 15 minutes ahead of arrival, and luckily they had outdoor seating for people who did not make reservation. On a Monday night they were packed inside but they did have outdoor seating, roughly around 2 tables that can fit 4 people and 2 more tables that can fit a party of 2. Mind you, they also have a bar but we wanted to dine family-style so we can try everything and a bar was not great for 3 people.

Justin really helped us choose our drinks and us three really liked it, for the exception of one of the drinks.

Bangkok Mule: Delicious! Acidic, tart, a bit of lemongrass, and was a refreshing treat.

Masala C-A-B: It had hints of cinnamon and it was pretty tart. Very great drink! One of my favorites

Pikapika: this was the drink we weren't extremely fond us, but it wasn't bad. We just liked the others more. 

For starters Justin helped pick out:

Birb Lettuce Salad: They were bit lettuce chunks tossed in a very tart vinaigrette served with some type of Indian/South Asian hard-crunchy flat bread. It was really delicious! It was so refreshing, and it really helped cleanse the palette of the Bone Marrow Dish.

Crispy Oysters: Wow! This was the first bite all three of us had when it first landed on the table, and I can tell you we were so impressed by this dish. It had everything you wanted in a well rounded meal. It brought the fat from the fried portion of the oyster, it had the acidity in the pickled vegetables that garnishes it, it was seasoned well, and it was so flavorful. Great choice!

Roasted Bone Marrow and Green Garlic Curry: My partner and my friend has never had bone marrow before so they didn't know what came out. But with a little instruction (it really only takes like 2 seconds to show them where the bone marrow is) they quickly scraped some off, put some on the Roti (which is really puratha bread but Thais call this type of bread Roti bread) and scraped some of the green garlic curry onto the roti. Delicious! Extremely fatty and coats your entire mouth with fat, but worth every bite. We ate some of the Birb lettuce salad which has that nice tart vinaigrette to really help cleanse our palette of the fat. 

Entrees and Noodles:

Maypop Crawfish Ettouffee over Gnocchetti: this was the most bland out of all of our dish, but I was the only one that liked it for that blandness. My two dinner companions didn't care for this dish that much, and it was sadly one of the two that made it's way into a to-go box because it was not finished. 

Gulf Shrimp in Smoked Paprika over grits: The curry was good but was not very flavorful. If anything the shrimps on this dish was extremely salty and pretty much encapsulated the seasoning of everything else that it seemed to have made the curry lose it's curry taste. This was the second dish that our table did not finish and made it's way into a to-go container. 

Hot Smoked Duck Ham over Cashew-Sticky Rice: WOW! I LOVE THIS DISH! I'm Thai and do a lot of Thai cooking. I'm not sure where the chefs got their inspiration from, but the raw garlic, the Thai chilies, the acidity from their onion-ginger saute sauce definitely reminds me of home cooking, but definitely elevated. This was mine and my partner's favorite dish of the night. It was spectacular!

Beef short rib in Rendang Curry: This was my friend's favorite dish and our second favorite dish of the night. The beef short rib was braised so well, it really had that perfect balance of fattiness and tenderized braised meat. It was garnished with some type of pickled radish sliced thin (likely daikon), and another type of julienned radish that was sliced. It had a really great flavor overall and we really appreciated the craftiness of the chef's creation.

Overall: The drinks were awesome, the food was amazing, and Justin was an amazing server. We definitely enjoyed our first time at Maypop and will definitely be back!

Horrible. Took us 20 minutes to get silverware. Ended up eating salad with our hands. My steak was seared on a flat top not grilled. Corners cut like crazy. I regret every minute of being here. Steak was shit too. I just wanted a simple meal. Dammit. -rob bailey (my first official restaurant review)

And "best meal I've ever had in Philly" goes to.... BUTCHER BAR! Hands down, best steak, lamb and ribs I've ever had. Holy crapoli, I seriously hit the jackpot! I am in love with this place.

Seriously... words could never fully express how good the food is. I HAVE to recommend the lamb, steak and fries along with the wild boar ribs. Trust me, go with a partner and split these dishes down the middle. Your taste buds will thank you! 

The lamb, steak and ribs are cooked to perfection.  The steak and lamb are so perfect you don't need any sauce accompanying it. As for the ribs, it comes with a BBQ sauce that elevates the dish to a whole new level. The meat is smoked for hours on end. The meat just falls off the bone - just pull those bones out and go to town! Oh and the cornbread that accompanies the ribs... oh my goodness!!! It has a little kick with a beautiful glaze! 

Want something in addition to your entree? I recommend the stuffed mushroom caps and/or the baked beans with candied bacon and the mac and cheese. 

After you finished eating the best meat of your life move on to dessert. Omg... the key lime pudding.... the best I've ever had... and the best my family has ever tried. The flavor just explodes in your mouth. It's easy to see that they pay attention to details. Not much of a key lime pie person? Then go with the thick cookie baked in a skillet. Perfectly crispy on the edges topped with refreshing vanilla ice cream.

Uh, I cannot say enough about this place. The staff are incredible. They really add to the experience and give the best recommendations if you are undecided. 

The drinks... order some! The bartenders know what a nicely balanced drink is. They are so delicious it's hard to stop at just one.

I've taken several friends and family (because I feel that everyone I know must know about this place) and every single one of them stated it was the best meat and desert they ever had. So what more can I say?! Get a reservation and enjoy!

Had the pleasure of enjoying the ambience and food at Red The Steakhouse with some friends. I took part in the Savor menu as well as had a cocktail and tried a Pinot noir. The Just Peachy was very light and a great summer cocktail. Apparently, Ketel One vodka has a botanical line with no sugar added. The stuffed pepper was delicious. The waiter did warn that it was spicy and I am a fan of spicy but I was a little caught off guard. The marinara sauce on the pepper was great! It paired well for dipping the complimentary bread in. My entree was good. Cooked the way I like, medium. Portions were just right for the sides. The doughnut holes reminded me more of beignets but they were still the right amount of sweet to complete a great dinner.

Additionally, the service was great! Aaron and those assisting him were timely, helpful, and attentive. And they have daily specials. Monday is 1/2 price bottles of wine up to $150, just FYI.

This review is based on dinner & drinks & doesn't involve anything with the live music. I know I live in music city, but I really don't care much about live music. We went for dinner on a Friday night around 8:30 & I didn't hear or see any live music.

Parking - good luck finding a parking spot. After doing about 10 laps around the lot, we got lucky and was about to get a spot. The building is fairly new, & the inside decor is nice, but not amazing. I do have to say that love the booths. They are walled off, "U" shaped & can fit 7 people nicely. 

The place has a cool vibe without trying to be hipster. I wished I remembered our servers name, she was great & friendly. We had a order of pickles that I randomly got free from checking in on Yelp. We also had a cheese board what had different cheeses & crackers. It was good but not amazing. 

For drinks, I felt something simple & order just a diet & bourbon. The drink was strong & I very much. A friend ordered a Moscow mule, which the server didn't seem to know of, but the bartender was about to create it. 

Food - I order the hot chicken with macaroni and bacon on top. I'd read the reviews & wanted to try it. I'm glad that I did. It was very hot, but not in a "I can't eat this" way. The chicken came with slaw, cornbread and honey on top. Maybe it was because I'd had a few to drink before I sat down for dinner, but I didn't notice until I looked at the picture a few days later that the macaroni has a small, pinch of bacon dust on it. Nonetheless, the macaroni was great, I just wished it had the bacon on it. Overall, a great place to conversant in the large booths with friends & get a drink or two & some yummy food. If you like music, they supposedly have that too.

I had to work late in the area so I decided to order a to go order of chicken pad Thai. I know, it's a boring dish to most but I LIKE IT! Anyway. I used their website to order my food which made it really easy and I was able to pay with my card at the restaurant. After placing the order online it said that it would take about 25 minutes. I think that is just a safe estimate because I came over about ten minutes later and my food was bagged up and ready for me. 

The restaurant is a little small on the inside. When you enter, there is a hostess stand and then the pickup/cashier is located to the back, right of the store. The young lady who rang me up was friendly and I was in and out in about 30 seconds. I felt the bag and it was heavy! How much do they give you? A LOT. I came back to work a was surprised with the amount of food you get for $9.95. It was very fresh as well. From the shallots to the bean sprouts and cilantro, everything tasted very fresh. The noodles were also cooked well. There weren't sticky and clumpy like some can be. The chicken in the dish was pounded flat and cooked well. There was a nice amount of chicken in the dish as well. I was starving and I could only way about 3/5 of the dish. I'm looking forward to trying other entrees from this place. Next time I need to remember put in the special instructions about the spicy level because I would like it a little more spicy, but it was my fault to not voice it in the online order.

A few weeks ago I randomly got a notification on Facebook about how Mcdougal's on Nolensville had changed their name to Outlanders Southern Chicken. Does this mean it's no longer a McDougals? Did someone buy it & change the name? I'm not sure of the specifics, but it looks like someone bought the restaurant, changed the name but still sell most of the same food items. 

We stopped in on a Sunday afternoon around 1pm. The place was PACKED. I never came to this location when it was McDougal's, but I've ate at the location off 21st avenue & it looks the same. Lots of stuff on the walls, tables with paper towel rolls in the middle. If you've been to the McDougals before, you'll be used to this setup along with the menu. I picked the 5 chicken fingers for $9.99. A better price than the 21st Ave location. It used to be 8.99 there, then they raised it to 11.99, took away the free water option & the free birthday dinner, Vanderblit discount. I won't go there anymore. 

The five fingers comes with an order of fries, a piece of thick toast and 3 dipping sauces. I picked 2 blue cheese and one of the outlanders sauce. I wouldn't get the blue cheese again because it was very runny, I didn't care for it at all. The outlander sauce was good though. You can get them tossed in one of 5 or 6 sauces. I did fried chicken tossed in thunderbird sauce. It's their version of a spicier buffalo sauce. I like spicy & I found it to be rather spicy. 

You can get the fries loaded with cheese and bacon. The bacon is good but the cheese is just that cheese topping stuff that they serve with concession nachos, not my favorite. I liked the fries better plain with the seasoning they put on there. I got the water from the drink fountain & it tasted a little off. Kind of tasted like water from a garden hose, hard to explain but next time I won't be cheap & get a soft drink. Phillip said the tea wasn't that great, I don't drink tea but he's kind of a connoisseur of the stuff.

We are out on the patio. The seating inside & on the patio is tight. If you sit near the front door, be forwarded that it bangs loudly whenever it closes. Overall I liked the chicken & fries. It's just like McDougal's was, just with a new name. I'd stop by here if I was in the area.

I tried shawarma on the run for the first time today. I will be a repeat customer because the food was delicious. The portions were big and the food was fresh and hot as well. 

I ordered falafel appetizer and 2 chicken shawarma platters. The falafel was nice and crispy. Came with a side of sauce and was your standard falafel. The platters come with hummus, salad, rice, chicken, 2 pieces of pita, and a side of white sauce (I think it's garlic sauce?) The portion sizes were enough for two meals for me. The chicken was flavorful and moist. I've had chicken shawarma be dry before, but this was not. The rice was seasoned nicely. The hummus was very smooth and to my liking. Everything had flavor. I didn't feel gross after eating the food because everything was nice and light. A really refreshing meal versus some fast food. Speaking of fast food, they are fast! My food was ready quick even with delivery, but it came hot still. My mom is really picky. I convinced her to try the chicken shawarma with me and she really liked it. She even liked the hummus which she is not a huge fan of to begin with! 

All in all, I would 100% come back again when I want some shawarma. I had special instructions for double rice instead of hummus for one platter and the request was followed. I also had a side of tzatziki which was a nice compliment to the meat versus the other white sauce. Both are equally good. Prices are reasonable as well.

I had been here once prior, having a late night study sesh at NAIT and starving for something other than cafeteria food.  
I only went in for take out and vaguely remember even being there or even what I ordered.

Now, after working, I had a craving for Thai and hit up that hotspot with a colleague of mine.  Surprisingly, the son actually remembered I had been there once before!!

After looking at all the yummy things on the menu, and having a chit chat with the owner of the place, we settled on the red curry with chicken and potatoes, the tom yum pho and spring rolls.

The atmosphere is super comfortable and the owner and son are very nice and accommodating people.  Apparently the daughter is the cook which is nice that the owner and family are taking care of the place.

The food was amazing, of course.  And being able to order in varying levels of spicyness is a great idea.  The curry comes with a level 2(?) and I would have preferred it a little spicier, so next time I will order it a level 3.

There was little no wait each time I went there and highly recommend this place for almost everyone as it is quite chilling to go with friends, or quaint to bring a date.
July 29th, 2018 - They changed the way they cooked the pork and it was extremely better! No more dry pork chashu, thank you!!!

I can  not imagine  staying  anywhere else other than the W if in Nola again!
I can not think of  a reason not to give it 5 stars. And I was informed it was renovated right before we stayed here! 

It is chic, the  employees are mostly model beautiful and warm,  the beds were comfy , the grounds, property, and rooms were lovely and charming, plus the W has their own signature scent!

It reminded me of being  at  the  Bellagio pool in Vegas only this scent  was every where! It made the package complete! We are  going to order one of the candles.  http://www.hotelchatter.com/story/2010/10/8/2646/57656/hotels/This_is_the_W_Signature_Scent_and_Here%27s_Where_You_Can_Buy_It

They also have a car  available to drive you around  town  complimentary. I think that is what gave it 5 stars, and the shower.

 We did use the car  to go to Cochon  in the car  and the driver was excellent! His name  is Daniel if you want to ask for him! He was very knowledgeable about Nola and it's cuisine  and culture! http://www.starwoodhotels.com/whotels/property/features/fas_detail.html?propertyID=2030&fasXRefId=1001986043

We chose the W hotel due to Steven I's review. http://www.yelp.com/biz/w-new-orleans-french-quarter-new-orleans#hrid:vL0xD4-bULeJhlUiEMO66g
I am  familiar with the W brand  from  baby sitting  at  NYC hotels in  between jobs. I  usually suggest the  W as where to stay in  NYC I like it so much! If you are not familiar with  the  W brand it is like a cross between the Sheraton and  A loft brand.
I found this video on line about the W.http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9NNNC0KX59Q
I like the  W for it's style and  comfy beds.
We booked through Jet  Blue. Jet Blue sent us a confirmation right away.
But trying to get  an  e-mail  confirmation from the W Hotel  proved to be at the  very least frustrating and stressful. The communication  between Jet  Blue and the W was  not very good.  But once we checked in it was smooth sailing!
The service was amazing!  The beds were comfy I give them an 8 out of 10 with the  Sheraton  Sweet Sleeper being a 9. http://www.sheraton-hotelsathome.com/productGroup.aspx?itemID=SH-124
I have a bad back and have had multiple back surgeries and the  bed was fine for me so if you have back issues the beds will be good for you!
The rooms and every part of the hotel was stylish and chic.  The scent was awesome!
The W has its own music in the car and hotel.  They have an XM station. You can purchase the CD's of the music at the hotel. They have  a Facebok page where you can purchase their brand items. https://www.facebook.com/NOLACollection?group_id=0

There is an outdoor court yard with  a fire pit and the small pool is heated and lights up at night!

 But for me the best part was the shower.

 The shower  may be the best shower I have ever had!

It is a rain shower (see pictures)  and the floors in the bathroom are tile like a spa bathroom so it's okay if they get wet. The shower was constructed in such a way  that the water drained into the pipes so none of it gets out of the shower onto the floor and you can leave the shower door open if you want to which I did so I could take a steam shower at least  several times a day! I needed it for my back!  It was amazing!  

The shower was also large and stylish enough to be romantic!

It is a small boutique hotel and really made our stay enjoyable.
If we had stayed in  a large  hotel that  looks like a big box the way the other hotels did, I can not imagine  it  would be  as enjoyable! The only complaint I have  is how the hotel was built. 
The rooms do not have drawers big enough for clothes so we hung up the clothes that were dressy and everything else had to stay in  the bags. Other than that no complaints! It was like a spa experience just taking a shower!
The guests were more upscale a classy crowd not a bunch of drunks which you do see if you go to Bourbon Street.  For Nola the location of the hotel  could not be better!  

I was trying to think of a reason not to give it 5 stars but I can not. I do not give out 5 stars easily. But there is no real reason  not to. I have only given one 5 star  rating to  a hotel in  Maui Hawaii. Nola is not Hawaii that's for sure but for Nola it is 5 stars.
The service was over the top and so was the experience!
I can not imagine a nicer hotel in  Nola!

Okay let's just say, I absolutely love this place! Their food is fabulous! On my last visit there I enjoyed the fish tacos and they were amazing! They did have a bit of a wait last time but it was the holidays and people were off work and also visiting from out of town probably. The service is great, the hostess at the front that day seemed a little lost and overwhelmed but hopefully she got through the day. I enjoy their salsa very much. Everything just seems so fresh and food comes out pretty quickly. They have a wide selection of food choices.
I definitely recommend the fish tacos.
They have a cute little enclosed patio in the back which was nice to be seated at away from how loud everything was. So the only down fall is that when they are busy it gets loud due to how small the place is. It does have great views though!

Excellent Excellent Excellent all around. Dont be fool by the outside let the smell lead you inside. Once you walk-in you will not be disappointed.. The lay out is amazing, feels like your having an indoor picnic. 

I ordered the rib dinner which comes with 3 large rib bones and 2 sides. My sides were mac & cheese and baked beans. The ribs were very tender and full of flavor and there signature sauce puts it over the top. I highly recommend them to anyone. Also there "Brenda's Sweet Tea" is a must have!!

I've been eating here every Tuesday for about a month now. My kids really look forward to Taco Tuesday each and every week. I really enjoy the atmosphere here. Customer service is always super fast and friendly. Food is always on point never had an issue. Awesome sauce bar from sweet to hot, they have a sauce for you. My favorite is the "Smack My Ass and Call Me Sally." I wish they had more outdoor​ seating, the inside sometimes gets crowded and becomes very noisy.

After buying a Groupon and checking out the reviews on Yelp we were excited to check this place out. Scott M's review is a classic and will go down in Yelp history as the review to end all reviews, so I was a bit intimidated. Was the place that clean? Was the food traditional Mexican cuisine? Is Gino the waiter of legend real?
Well I have done my research and here are my findings.

Super clean and nice restaurant. Tables spaced comfortably so you aren't sitting on top of your neighbor. We were promptly greeted by a charming hostess and seated immediately. Our waiter would be Gino!!' So he did exist! No sooner were we seated and Gino himself greeted us and welcomed us to Casa Ramos.
