So much passion and knowledge about the menu that we felt we were in his home. We had to tease him about being the Gino whose fame grows on Yelp and he just said he wished other staff members were mentioned as much.

My husband asked for recommendation which Gino based on what my husband liked and he ended up ordering the carne Asada and chili Relleno. I knew I had to test out my three favorites which I could do by ordering the Macho plate. Chili Relleno, tamale Piccadillo ( pork) and chicken enchilada. All served with perfect retried beans and rice. 

Servings are huge- plates like the steering wheel of a 57 Chevy huge.

Fresh, fresh, perfectly seasoned, piping hot and delicious. We loved everything we tried but we hit a wall and had to take home enough for lunch the next day. 

So I agree with all the 5 star reviews. The one star people must have been at a different restaurant. We are so happy we came here, so happy to have Gino as our waiter! 

Gino agreed to let us take his photo as evidence that he exists. Also photos of our dinner selections. Cannot wait to go back and try some of the other options.
You will appreciate the service and food.

The food overall was bad, nothing tasted Brazilian.  The pasta salads are all pre packaged and are no different from Denny's.   everything was mayonnaise based and tasted the same - bland.  The other salads were all over dressed soggy and gross.

The meats - overall were over cooked, may have been carried over from the night before, no flavor, except the chicken thighs.  The beefs were chewy and tasted over cooked.  The only seasoning were pre made marinades you buy at Schnucks.   Basting already cooked meats is disgusting. The pricing for this experience is way out of whack.  

The Brazilian grill concept is popular, this is the worst of Brazilian grills.  Though it was crowded I see this to be a failure and not making it for one year, unless a complete overhaul on the food preparation is enacted.  People are not going to stand for crap especially at their price points.  Nothing here reminds of Brazil or a pleasurable dining experience as we had hoped it would be.  With what seemed to be 6-7 managers running around they should be tasting the food prior to being served.  The 15.99 Buffett at Ameristar is far better deal.  Waste of money, time, and palate.

Still have that bad meat taste in my mouth and hungry an hour later.

Easter brunch at the Blue Bell Inn is marvelous!! Tim our server advised that this was the first brunch they have done buffet style (lucky).

I started with the Blue Crab Bloody Mary. It had loads of crab flavor without drinking old bay. 

There are several stations to choose from. 

The raw bar (which is extra).
Carving station (roast beef ,turkey, ham)
Muffins & pasteries
Bagels, lox, spreads
Chef created omelette table
Chef created pasta schedule
Chef created waffle bar
Chaffing dishes with eggs, French toast, breakfast potatoes, breakfast meats 
Roasted veg & salad bar
Dessert table & ice cream bar

All were better than your run of the mill buffet brunch. A few of the highlights are pastry chef makes homemade ice cream & amazing petites. The roast beef was off the chain (my husband went for seconds), and the ambience is elegant and sophisticated.

We waddled out like stuffed Easter chicks. Great occasion spot.

I feel like I stumbled on a neighborhood secret walking into Sunday brunch here. The vibe at Pro Tap is laid back cool. A tad hipsta but what great brunch place isn't nowadays?

We needed 3 things: carb items for my daughter, eggs and sausage for my son, area proximity due to party proceeding...ok maybe four...bloody marys...always a requirement.

We were greeted with smiles and the wait was nothing (5 mins) compared to other brunch places. Albeit this is a bar but the brunch game is strong my friends.

I definitely recommend getting the Bloody Mary. It's spicy and garnished with homemade pickled veggies. Your choice of vodka.

We ordered a chocolate, caramel donut for the table to try because it was $2 and it was ridiculous. Hot out of the fryer made it crunchy on the outside with a cakey inside and whatever goodness they garnished with was off the plate and devoured within seconds.

Kiddos ordered the chocolate chip pancakes  as well as eggs and sausage. The portions are enormous. The toasted sourdough that comes with egg dishes is superb and you can order as a side. The pile of seasoned fries are a crispy nice addition instead of home fries.

The stunner is the chicken french toast with sunny eggs, kale and cabbage slaw, and peppered maple syrup. The combination of the crunchy kale and cabbage slaw and the saltiness of the fried chicken coupled with the gooey sunnies and peppery sweet maple syrup was insane. I will go back for that lovely dish.

Overall I was really impressed and would recommend!!

Gotta say Im truly digging Harp & Crown. Would have never found this place if not recommended by a friend so I figured I would write a review so others can get a lil H&C in their life.

We walked by Harp & Crown twice on Sansom because they are doing construction out front. They do have a big sign but to make it easy its right across the street from Ladder.

Huge ceilings and laid back speakeasy vibe with B&W portraits on the walls. Even tv's in bar area are B&W for the throwback feels. We went in to pre-game before dinner but I have to say their menu looked delish and HH specials were great so I will go back for dinner.

The bartenders were super friendly and really educated and offered up great suggestions. The Meridian Peak was my fav...had a few. Let me start by saying Tequila is my last choice but I sipped a friends and my tastebuds were sizzling. Spicy, fruity, and with the torched rosemary stem aroma hitting you after the first sip, it was a fabulous cocktail. Everyone loved the drinks.

We had the charcuterie and cheese plates to pick at and both were very good with a nice variety.

Im going to put it out there...the bathrooms are gender neutral so prepare yourself. The lil old gentleman in there with full bathroom door open while using the facilities didn't get the concept and was shocked when I walked in. I got a giggle but he was a little unnerved so advise your peeps to shut the door. 

Oh!! Almost forgot the coolest part! The two lane bowling alley and small cocktail area down the long dark hallway downstairs. Very intimate and  would be awesome for a party. Comfy chairs, a little competitive game, and some kickin cocktails. A great night out.

Turning point is a great addition to the otherwise lacking breakfast arena in the North Wales, PA area. There is a good amount of shopping in this area with the Montgomeryville Mall down the street and The Shoppes at English Village (which include a brand new Sephora) where Turning Point is also located. This is a fast growing franchise with three other locations in PA and a new location coming soon to Newtown, PA area.

What I love about this place:

French Press Coffee! If you have not had it, your missin' out.  Kenyan, Hawaiian Kona, Costa Rican, and Jamaican Blue Mountain.  They serve in a large french press carafe enough for two with a rock candy sugar stick (even though I smuggle in a napkin home for the kids) super cute.

Extensive breakfast and brunch list waffles, pancakes, french toast, egg skillets, avocado toast, the list goes on. My favorite is the Popeye skillet and the Wilbur Skillet extra avocado. Lunch options are savory sandwiches, salads, and create your own combo with 1/2 sandwich, soup, or 1/2 salad (choice of two).

Outdoor Eating:

They have a great patio area out front so on a sunny day enjoy your coffee with some fresh air. 

What could be a little better:

The wait time can be brutal and there is no calling ahead so if you are a big party or in a rush...don't get your britches in a bundle cause your gunna wait. Grab a cup of FREE coffee in the waiting area and stare at your phone or perhaps have a conversation. Its a good sized bright space with lots of natural light. Just realize that you may have to have some patience.

Overall a great spot. I've eaten here several times with the family and I'm sure we will be back for several more!

Finally getting down to my Sabrina's review. If you are in Philly, Sabrina's is a must try for your brunch fix. Several locations but I am partial to the Callowhill location due to its proximity to the art museum area. 

Sabrina's  can be a long wait based on when you go so during off hours and weekdays is the way to go if you can swing it. Street parking is also a little hairy so give yourself time to find parking and get a table. We brought a bottle of champs because Mimosas are life and you can BYOB. 

The food was delicious I enjoyed my huevos rancheros, which is one of their specialties, and my friend loved her light and fluffy french toast. 

Some things are worth the wait and I do believe that a Sabrina's brunch is one of those things!!

What a beautiful addition to the Fishtown neighborhood! 

Ive been dying to get into Suraya since I heard of the opening and it did not disappoint. A wonderful collaboration between Root owners Greg Root, chef Nick Kennedy and Cafe La Maude owner Nathalie Richan. 

The decor is a Mediterranean dream. Tiled floors, glass lanterns, and neatly stacked shelves of unique scrumptious foods. As you walk in you feel transported to Eastern Mediterranean without the pricey airfare.

My husband and I stopped in for a working lunch. This is a great place to get work done. Lots of natural light and not too noisy.

We started with cappuccinos and the Za'atar + Cheese with an added egg. A delicious pita with 1/2 melty cheese and 1/2 spice with egg. It was heavenly. You can fold in half and eat or rip pieces of the pita off and dip. The cappuccino was so good I had another breaking my cardinal rule of caffeine. 

I can not wait for this city to thaw so I can bask in some sunshine in the outdoor garden area. You will see several check ins at this spot. My new favorite!

Who would have imagined this concept could be so good? James Beard award winner Mike Solo and foodie/Yelper Felicia D, that's who. 

Though I haven't been able to try the fried chicken yet, this opening morning's coffee and donuts were exceptional. With 10 varieties of "fresh" or "fancy" donuts, you'll have to choose wisely. Fresh sugar glazed 'nuts are fried to order in flavors like chili-lime and Indian cinnamon. 

I chose the fancy nutella tehina donut, topped with pomegranate glaze and sesame seeds. One of the most interesting combinations of flavors I've had: there's barely a hint of nutella, as the fruity pom juice dominates, followed by the slightly nutty taste of sesame paste.

Federal Donuts (or FedNuts, as the kids are calling it) is a corner spot on S. 2nd street, just past the Mummers museum. The bright blue awnings will draw you into this cozy space, with its sunny wooden counters and swirly glass coffee contraptions (which look to me like props from a scientist's lair, but it makes a damn good brew). 

There isn't much space to hang out inside, but service is friendly and quick, manned this morning by the lovely Felicia D herself. Would love to see a cafe table or two in the spring, and a more mobile/user-friendly website once things get rolling.


EDIT: Finally got a chance to try all the donut varieties, since my boss brought in a dozen this morning. The Indian Cinnamon is by far the best of the bunch, with a warm, spiced flavor. What is that extra spice? Cardamom? Delicious. Many of the filled cake varieties err on cloying at times, but I'm a sugar/dessert lover. The key lime, with graham cracker crumb toppings, is my favorite "fancy flavor" after the Pomegranate Tehina. If you're not a big sweets person, stick to the fresh-fried and maybe ask them to dust with less sugar...just not when there's a line.

So... I hear this place always has a long line of people even waiting outside to get food from here. I hear this place is one of the must go to places when visiting New Orleans. I have one question... Why?

From the looks of the food while waiting to order, nothing looked appetizing to me. I hate to waste my money on bad food, so I decided to settle for something smaller and ordered some jambalaya. It says it comes with andouille sausage and chicken in it... The sausage wasn't andouille, and the chicken... Where was it? It was none in it at all! I went with a group of 4, and no one got anything that was good. One person got a shrimp po boy. I thought the shrimp was suppose to be hot... Maybe this day it was a special day and they were only serving the "cold shrimp po boy." A couple people had leftovers, enough to take back to the hotel to eat later... Yeah... They didn't do that. 

The prices at this place are ridiculous. The inside was filthy. Food all over the place on the floor. Someone told me that's how they do it in New Orleans, but I didn't go to any other restaurant that looked like this. I was just waiting and anticipating seeing rat come out from under something. I'm sure you'll notice the sign that says something about servers don't accept tips. Well... Then you'll be greeted by a server that will tell you something to the effect... "We're not allowed to accept tips, but if you want to tip, please tip and we'll take it." Whaaaaaaaat!?!?!?!? 


It's too many other good places in New Orleans to go to and settle for this place. I expected it to be better based off the reviews I saw on here, and the amount of reviews on here. Y'all can have this place. I'll never be back here.

TIP: They don't take reservations but you can call ahead and put your name on the wait list - do this! Weekend brunch time has about ~45 minutes wait. 

BYOB note: Do it. Also, if you're thinking about having mimosas, a pitcher of OJ is $12.99. 

By now, I've been to nearly all of Sabrina's - Philly, Ardmore, and now Collingswood. And yes, the food has been consistently amazing! 

They currently have a special 2017 menu, with twists on their classic favorites. Friend got the stuffed French toasts - just as huge and delicious as the regular ones but with different fruit/no bananas. 

I opted for the (IMO) elevated version of huevos rancheros, with cinnamon-coffee rubbed short ribs over home fries, loaded veggies, lime sour cream, & 2 over easy eggs. It was SO good and even better than the classic! The short ribs were so flavorful, and the home fries great as always. New favorite dish. 

If this is your first time, you'll find that portions are generous, and you can easily walk away with leftovers. Evaluate at the halfway point whether you want to save enough to go, or truck through the rest (I did the latter).

My only gripe with this visit was the cleanliness: one of our glasses was brought out with 2 chapstick prints at the lip. And my knife had a small piece of dried food stuck to it. But this was amended by the deliciousness that ensued. 

Lastly - service was fine, and this location is the most spacious and chic. The street is filled with stores and restaurants to browse if you do end up waiting during peak hours. Best brunch option in the area!

I'm a sucker for aesthetics so I'll admit this place had me at its window displays. But seriously, can you blame me? A few weeks after it opened, I ventured in bright-eyed, bushy-tailed. 

Verdict: At least they have nice staff and nice decor. 

Honestly I wasn't clear on the difference between Parisian crepes and Japanese-style ones but I hope what I tasted at T-swirl isn't representative of the latter. We split their lychee romantic crepe with raspberry and rose cream. Sounds lovely, right? Well, fellas, don't count on this to woo your lady friends because it was anything but romantic. Actually it was more of a sad romance gone bad. 

First, I don't know if the crepes here are supposed to be made fresh because ours definitely wasn't. It might be different if served with ice cream but this one isn't. Maybe you're saying, okay, so what? Well, read on. 

The crepe came out flat with a smidgen of cream, torn bits of canned lychee sparsely spread on top, two visible raspberries and maybe one pistachio grounded to pieces (see pic). Half way through we'd already forgotten what we ordered because there was nothing left but a thin layer of cream. Was it 40% off? No, but it probably should've been because it felt like 40% of it was missing. If you're coming here, at least don't get this. For $7, my friend would've made something better - and I doubt he even cooks. 

Ok maybe I'm being slightly dramatic (not really). Maybe we messed up and went with the only bad option on the menu. Maybe they were running out of ingredients. But as much as I'd like to think all of that, I'm just not convinced to give it another chance anytime soon.

I have to give it to them - they have a great interior. 

Don't believe the hype though that the waitresses instill in you when you arrive - their pizza is not the "best in the world". The waitresses appear to be brainwashed that they have the "best cheese" on their pizza that has been aged for awhile.

I tried their : margarita pizza, and meatballs. Both sucked.

They gave us complementary bread - which was the BEST part of all. I would come back for only their bread (albeit which isn't much to come back for).

I leave with $35 less in my pocket and feeling like I'm ready to puke.

Overall, with all the places in Wayne for pizza - try Paola's across the street or Anthony Coal Fire down the road.

As a native San Franciscan/Californian, I've lived in Nashville for little over a year and the ONE ethnic food that was lacking authenticity was Chinese food. Yes, I know there are plenty of "Chinese" restaurants in Nashville, but those restaurants are catered to those who are not open to try the real authentic dishes of mainland China (Duck over rice, Peking Duck, Shanghai Dumplings, Steamed Sea Bass, Hot Clay Pots, Bean Curds(Tofu),etc). I was depressed that there wasn't at the very least a some-what authentic Chinese restaurant that would satisfy my cravings for good Chinese food until I found this place.  

If you're the type that loves the Americanized Chinese dishes such as General Tso's Chicken, Sweet and Sour Chicken/Pork, etc... you can still find it here. But let me warn you, ever since their reopening, their forte is NOT the Americanized Chinese dishes and instead their forte is their ability to cook authentic Asian dishes that range from Taiwanese, Shanghainese, Hong Kong, Central China, and Cantonese (tip: food in China varies by region so Chinese food is very broad). As a Chinese-American myself, I and grew up with home cooked savory Cantonese food, and great variations of Chinese food throughout California. In addition, I've lived in China and can confidently say this restaurant is the Holy Grail of authentic Chinese food that is comparible to that of the aforementioned. 

Before their reopening, the cooks at Chinatown traveled to all parts of China to learn the different techniques to the variouis types of cooking styles (contemporary and traditional) of Asia (mainly China and Taiwan); I know this because I asked the owners and the authenticity was explained after trying the dishes. You really can't get more authentic than that. I've spoken to other Chinese restaurant owners in Nashville, and many know the type of authentic Chinese food I'm talking about but ALL believe that Americans, especially Southern Americans, are not ready for REAL authentic Chinese food. So I applaud Chinatown for their bravery to make this move.

Tips to Yelpers: Don't be afraid to try the native Chinese dishes. Ask the waiters/waitresses how to eat certain dishes if you don't know how. It's very common in the Chinese culture to start off with soup (Taiwanese Won Ton soup is goood), then move on to appetizer, and share many plates of vegetables and meat dishes amongst your party. Dine in Chinese food is meant to be served family style.

I'm not affilated with Chinatown, nor have they asked me to post this review. I write this because this is definitely a gem of Nashville and want them to survive and keep serving me these great dishes (or else I may reconsider moving to the coasts for better variety of authentic food :) )

My babe and I just finished dinner at Dickie Brennan's tonight.  We arrived at 7 and were seated at a table in the main dining room.  The decor is very old school with dark woods and white tablecloths.  After we ordered our Whiskies, we ordered their Steak Tartare and Fried Calamari for our starters.  For dinner, we ordered NY Steaks and sides of Creamed Spinach and Macaroni and Cheese.  For desert, we tried their Coconut Cream Cake.

All the dishes were perfectly prepared.  To be honest, no dish stood out...but they all tasted awesome!

The Coconut Cream Cake was totally yummy and was a great dish to end a wonderful steak dinner.

Throw in the great service and the awesome sourdough warm bread and we had an awesome dinner in NOLA.

After watching Man Vs Food, I had to try this place.

I ordered the bacon, mushroom, grilled onion burger with a side of tator tots..........Just fucking awesome....!!!

The burger was so flavorful.....the mix of onions, mushrooms, bacon and hamburger was soooooo good.

The tots came with a special sauce (thousand island dressing).....
loved it.

Great place.....and supercheap!!

I had the rib-eye steak and creamed spinach.  It rocked.  The best steak in Reno.  Old school steakhouse...........just like Morton's or a Capital Grille.  Full of dark woods, wine, cigars and plenty of juicy steaks.

The service and staff were outstanding!

At the end of dinner.....the mgr came by and comped our meals at our table.....we happen to be special guests that night.

WOW...we go the full VIP treatment.  11 time Wine Spectator Award Winner for excellence.....and counting!

I am a pretty big fan of the Link restaurants and Gianna is good but not damn good.  My expectations were too high.  I wanted Gianna to be this  go-to Italian restaurant.  Instead, I found it to be decent with room for improvement.  I ate at Gianna shortly after they opened, so I anticipate some of dishes will improve.

I dined here with Jacob C.  We ordered a bunch of food.  We were starving.  Actually, I was starving.  Jacob C can routinely eat a ton of food.  

My entree was the veal saltimbocca.  I thought the dish was a bit dry and lacked the saltiness flavor I was expecting.  It had capers but not enough for each bite.  If it had prosciutto, I couldn't taste any.  

My pasta dish pasta asciutta was simple, straightforward and exactly what was expecting.  Really enjoyed the flavor.  My gripe about the pasta was the fact it was overcooked, which made it congeal.  It's that situation when you try and take one bite and the entire bowl of noodles is on your fork.  It was not horrendous but for an Italian restaurant, subpar.  

Our apps and dessert were solid.  These made for great bookends to an otherwise very ok dinner.  I really enjoyed the upscale atmosphere.  Our hostess and waitress were nice and for the waitress, pretty attentive.  Overall, Gianna is a strong 3 star.  I suspect their dishes will improve.  I like a handful of Italian spots in town, and I hope that Gianna will be one of the really good ones.

We went on a Saturday night, a party of 5. The bouncer asked of we were drinking, eating, or both. I  told him just drinking. He checked all of our IDs, and neither he not the hostess made a move to seat us. They were not busy. Im not sure why the hostess wasn't paying attention. The outside section was mostly empty, so we sat down at a nearby table. After sitting for about 10 min without service, I realized we may have made a mistake. When I turned around to get up and approach the hostess stand to apologize and ask to be officially seated, I saw her point to us and tell a waitress, "they just sat on their own, so don't serve them." 

First of all...we made a mistake. So, we probably shouldn't have sat on our own. But, really? You're not going to tell us? You'll just let us sit and hope we leave because you're offended by our faux pas? Get over yourselves. 

I got up anyway, and apologized, asking the bouncer if we should have waited. His response? "Well, did you seat yourself? That's your fault. That's why I asked if you were eating, drinking or both, you know." 

No, I didn't know that, mostly because you didn't follow that question up with anything, partly because you watched us sit and ignored us. 

We left. I'm sure they don't care, they get enough business that they probably don't give a shit. Id have been happier if they'd asked us to leave. Ignoring us was so rude, and really immature. 

Their food is okay. I won't be going back.

We had a very enjoyable ladies lunch here. I actually went to Whiskey Cake while living in OKC so was pleasantly surprised to see one open in Tampa. Everything on the menu is very fresh. The menu is diverse enough to make most everyone happy but not too big where you know they can't do all that food well you know what I mean? 

We all ordered the soup and half sandwich with different sandwiches and everyone loved what they got. I have to mention my cocktail because it was very good! The Left Hook Lucy is not too sweet and very enjoyable. 

We ordered one of their famous whiskey cakes and shared it between the three of us. This thing is huge! I don't even thing we finished it. Honestly it wasn't my favorite. Don't get me wrong, for whiskey cake it's very good but it's just not my thing. 
Also our server was very nice. Definitely above average. She made our experience delightful. 

We will definitely be back to try out brunch and maybe even dinner!

No pictures because we ate everything way too fast! It was that good! 

I was craving fried oysters so I turned to Yelp and turns out this place isn't too far! Yay! And omg are their oysters done right. Big, and delicious. Not over breaded and not over cooked. Luckily the very helpful lady at the take out window pointed me to the dinner (vs sandwich or plate) which has 40% more oysters (Whoopi!) and comes with two sides. I went with the house made onion rings and baked beans. Both really good. 

As if a giant plate of oysters wasn't enough, I couldn't leave without trying the foot long lobster roll. This was so delicious. The bread to meat ratio was spot on (way more meat than bread). Not too much dressing so you can let the lobster shine. Cooked perfectly. 

Mind you i had a 10min drive home before we ate and I'm still raving about food that should been eating right away. Just imagine how good it will be fresh in the restaurant. I will definitely be eating here again, probably this weekend.

Fusion Bowl is a very enjoyable Vietnamese fusion spot in downtown Tampa that is popular for lunch. It's a casual but clean "order at the counter" establishment. It does get crowded during the lunch hour, making a table hard to grab at peak rush. 

I ordered the pork banh mi while my husband had the seafood pho. The banh mi was very enjoyable. The bread was crusty and the veggies were fresh. I enjoyed the saltiness of the meat with every bite. The pho was also very good. The broth is flavorful although not as robust as other bowls in town. The seafood is a mix of shrimp and imitation crab. Next time we may add some spice to kick it up a notch. 

We also tried the avocado spring roll. This freshly made treat is served with a peanut sauce on the side. This is a nice starter if you are looking for something light. 

Overall a very enjoyable lunch for less than $30 including 2 sodas.

Look, I am all about mixing my evening dining experience with a nice dose of history, but this place ain't the place to do so.

My first visit to City Tavern was wonderful and, alas, biased.  It was a first evening date with my fiancé in his hometown.  Scratch that and fast forward to our second experience at City Tavern where a large group of us were celebrating my soon to be Mother in Law's birthday.

Nearly everything failed my expectations.

Our first suggested table was horrific.  I quickly changed that.  Our waiter was slightly drugged and boring.  I laughed.  The room we were seated at was cold and sluggish, which too describes our waiter.  Our food had not one bit of historic quality or recipe to it.  Our 21st century  menu choices were bland, undercooked/overcooked and my brother-in-law had to send his steak back, wait 30 minutes, then finish his dinner whilst we were snacking on birthday cake. 

If you would like a taste of Philadelphia history you can either hunt and shoot your own pheasant and blandly season it with a side of undercooked fingerling potatoes, or, you can take a beautiful historic walk in the streets of Philadelphia and then enjoy an avant-garde meal in one of the many wonderful restaurants of our first and now modern city in these great United States.  

Your choice ..  but I am not too fond of pheasant feather in my meals.

Came here on a weeknight last week. Unassuming location but fixed up very nice inside. We started with a smaller plate for an appetizer - lamb meatballs. They were great. and then had a couple larger plates. We ended up getting another appetizer- watermelon gazpacho with shrimp. We finished the meal with a dessert of goat cheese with some figs and a nice sauce. Overall the meal was great. We will be back!

Ordered "Carne Enchilada y Cesina Platter" delivery via Seamless.  Food came in 30 minutes in a fabulous presentation.  Portion was enormous for the low price.  This was my second time ordering from them...will order a third time

What a lovely hotel.

Here are the perks and keep in mind we were two gals sharing a queen room.

For the three nights that we were there to essentially eat, drink, be merry and party, this spot could not have been better.  It is in walking distance to everything that was on our hit list.

The room was immaculate.  Even though there was some sort of snafu with the Living Social deal that put us on a patio room instead of a balcony and left us with one queen bed instead of two.  I did not complain about sleeping on a cot.  It was comfortable enough and I am NOT A WHINER.  I was fine.  By the time you are as drunk as I was as 4AM, you really don't care that you are sleeping on a comfy cot.

For you fuddy-duddy complainers about the din and debauchery of Bourbon Street, go get a room elsewhere; like in Gretna.  No offense to Gretna, my aunt and uncle live there and they love it.  

But seriously, what the hell do you think is going to happen getting a hotel room in the heart of The French Quarter, right on Bourbon Street.  Don't make me use the "Duh" word.

I've literally NEVER been a popsicle person in my life until I had The Hyppo. The sheer variety of flavors (traditional and crazy) is impressive and the quality is fantastic. Personal favorites include: Chocolate Cheesecake, Avocado Serrano, Blackberry Ginger, Pineapple Hatch Chili, and Watermelon Basil.

Variety of Flavors: 5/5
Quality: 5/5
Service: 5/5
Price: 4/5 (a little pricy for a popsicle)
OVERALL: 5/5

While I wish I was a spa person, I'm not really.  Maybe someday in the future I will be an experienced spa goin gal...  before I went to the Spa Atlantis, I'd only had separate treatments- you know: where once you're done, you leave.

Ooooh, the Spa Atlantis totally blew that mindframe out of the water!! 

(And boy, they have really good water.  Bottled water, citrus water, cinnamon water, fruit water... all kinds of water.)

I went in March and again last week, each time I had booked a 1 hour massage from Nicole.  I just loved the whole experience.  

The 1 hour massage turns into a four + hours when you add time in the locker room to relax in the tea lounge (complete with goodies & fruit to much on, magazines, and comfy chairs), the three different rooms to relax in (one with pools, one warm dry heat, and one room I can only call what they call it: the brine inhalation and light therapy room.  Then back in the ladies (or men's I guess) locker room, there is a super steamy aromatherapy steam room and a sauna, and the best effing shower ever!  Holy geez, I would like to stay in there forever using their endless supply of Aveda products and their shower that showers me from like five directions.  Good god I left clean!!

And pretty. It's nice to use their new equipment to dry my hair and their nice product to style it.  Nice to sit around and take my time to look good after I've just become as relaxed as I've been in months.

And that was only because I was in a hurry!  There's also the regular full-size pool and fitness room to spend time in.  What a deal to spend a day in paradise for about $100. 

I really like the staff who seemed extremely sweet and accommodating. 

Also, of course, its brand spankin' new so get it while the gettin's good.  

But hey you guys... don't go when I go, because I liked that on the days I have been the whole center was almost empty of guests.

Gus is back people!! My husband and I came here on a Wednesday night for their dinner special. Which is still awesome! Soda-salad-entree-dessert ~$12

You can't beat the price! And our waitress SHIRLEY was the nicest waitress I have ever met. She took the time to take our order and wrote everything down on her note pad so she wouldn't forget our special order. Of course I was difficult and wanted my dressing on the side with no croutons lol ( sorry shirley if I was difficult lol) but she made sure everything came out perfect. 

I ordered the goulash over noodles and my husband loves the chicken croquettes with mash potatoes and french fries. Everything came out hot and very tasty. 

The cinnamon swirl bread is coming back too! Which I can't wait for! The soup was super hot which soup should be and Shirley made sure to tell us it was hot so we didn't burn ourselves. Entree was awesome- the goulash was a little salty for me but it is okay I still ate half of it and having the rest for lunch tomorrow.

Overall this place is coming back together and all the servers were super nice and Shirley is awesome!

It's #FridayNightFoodie time again, and though restaurants are open again in our area, we're still playing it safe and ordering in.
This month we went with our favorite burger joint in the Bay area, Engine No.9! Admittedly, this decision came from a desire to support a local favorite who we know might be struggling to find a way to operate at 25% capacity for dine-in customers AND learning that they're offering delivery now!
And before anyone asks, apparently the ordering/delivery service they're using, ChowNow, is built right into their website -- when you order through the website, 100% of what you pay goes to the restaurant! We've tried to be better about ordering directly from local businesses rather than utilizing the corporate delivery services charging third-party fees, so we were very happy to learn that wasn't going to be the case tonight!
If you've never had Engine No.9, just be aware of a few things: 
1. The burgers are why you go. Yes, they have amazing gumbo and jambalaya (their head chef is New Orleans-inspired and trained), but the creativity with ingredients, the quality of the beef, and the presentation all make their burgers supreme.
2. Don't feel bad if you can't finish your burger. They're generously sized, and when served with their perfectly fried tater tots, you'll fill up FAST. Just plan on getting two meals out of it!
We actually did something tonight we normally don't do at No.9 and ordered an appetizer. Honestly, this was just to pad the order and give a little more to them -- we didn't need the extra food! BUT if you just want that extra something to start off your meal, you can't go wrong with their fried dill pickle spears. Fried golden brown, served with house made ranch, they are delish - just don't eat too many of them! Remember what I said about the burgers!
Our burger selections tonight were a little conservative - Mel went with the Goat Head, which features roasted red peppers, sour pickles, and tons of goat cheese on top of a burger patty cooked to medium rare perfection. 
I went with a new one for me- the Wine-O! Red wine BBQ sauce, aged white cheddar, bacon, and onion rings! 
As you can see from the pictures, presentation doesn't suffer that much due to transit. Everything still looked great and tasted as delicious as ever.
Look, right now places like No.9, who are limited on dining room space and thus will struggle while having to operate at limited capacity, need our support now more than ever. We're thankful every time we have the opportunity to enjoy them, and hope to do so many more times in the future.

This place is the absolute cutest. I love the whole upscale market trend, and am also a huge fan of Michael Mina so loving Locale Market is not hard for me to do.

Located in a lovely indoor outdoor mall in St. Petersburg, Locale Market offers a fast, delicious way to eat and shop. While I didn't snag food there - I was instantly drawn to the beer and wine section. Love a place that lets you enjoy a glass or a cold one while you shop.

I ordered a nice glass of prosecco and we picked up some craft beers too. The beer and wine is towards the back of the shop - and there is some fresh pasta, charcuterie options, and cheeses too. There are lots of specialty grocery products at Locale which I think makes it a perfect spot to shop if you're hosting a nice dinner party or date night.

For food, there's sandwiches, salads, sushi (which looked incredibly fresh), and some other things too! Seems like Locale has something for everyone - and is a really nice atmosphere to shop.

You know those dinners where the service is so good, that you feel kind of in a daze of food and friendliness, and forget what you ordered?

Well, that was precisely my experience a few weeks ago at Samurai Blue thanks to Sue. I dine out quite often, and at times it can be hard to get great food and great service in a large group. Thanks to our superhero, Sue - our group of 11 had a phenomenal meal our first night in Ybor City.

Our group of 11 hungries ordered quite possibly everything on the menu. Led by Brett N - he selected our culinary adventure that was absolutely delightful. 

I wish I remember what I ate, but some highlights included:
+Blue Crab Rangoon: the best crab rangoon I have ever had.
+Hamachi - wonderful hamachi with ponzu sauce.
+Sashimi Platter: this was incredible quality. I loved the monkfish pate that came on the plate - super different and delicious.
+Uni and Fresh Scallop Hand Roll: this was divine - so buttery and smooth!
+I don't know the name of the roll, but there was a roll with spicy shredded crab on top, and I loved it.

The bottom line is, everything that graced our table was awesome, and the service from Sue made the evening even better. Food never stopped coming to our table, and our wine glasses were never empty. Solid choice for sushi in the area!

This place is always a yummy breakfast spot. I haven't tried anything other than their breakfast. Their pancakes alone are worth going. They literally are the size of a large pizza.....and there's 3 of them! Thankfully taste isn't sacrificed for that wow factor. They really are delicious pancakes, I always get blueberry. The place itself could use a little face lift but it's always super clean. The wait staff were extremely sweet. Made us feel like we were appreciated. And the chef who brought our food to the table was one of the most pleasant people I've seen in a restaurant in my life. You can tell he oves what he does, and he loves his customers. The food was really good. We had a waitress who was being trained so there was a couple of mess ups BUT she and the other ladies were extremely sweet about it.

Oystercatchers is an upscale restaurant with the best brunch in all of Tampa located off of the Causeway and part of the Grand Hyatt Hotel. Oystercatchers brunch features a make your own omelet station make your own banana foster station, oysters station, dessert station, Bloody Mary bar, salad bar, seafood bar, and tons of amazing options for a delicious and large brunch. The decor of this place is very spacious and modern with large windows overlooking the bay and beautiful views. This place was definitely a little bit tricky to find and you will have to kind of know where you're going to get here. Oystercatchers is in a place that you would not just see on the road and you could stop at. It is a hidden gem! I'm lucky my friend told me about this place because otherwise I wouldn't know. Leaving Tampa towards Clearwater, you take a left turn at the first light, and then take a left at the Grand Hyatt Hotel main entrance. You then go down a long winding road, go straight through a stop sign, and then park on the left side parking lot, walk through some gazebos and private bungalows, and then you find yourself at the waterfront Oystercatchers restaurant. I really love coming here but this is has to be kept for special occasions only because it is definitely not inexpensive!

The night before our flight, I Yelped places to eat for breakfast.  We were trying to eat as much food as possible before our flight back to NYC.  Stanley was the first result that came up when I searched for breakfast.  With over 1000 reviews, I said, "we're going here."

It was a 10 minute-ish walk from our hotel.  We got there, I think before 9am.  There were not many tables that were occupied but eventually, the tables started filling up.  I ordered the Breaux Bridge Benedict and shared the Shrimp Po Boy with Miss Eva.  We were hungry and trying to fit as much food in as possible...Yolo, right????

Of course, everything was delicious.  The boudin was delicious and it went well with everything.  Instead of the usual English muffin, it was served on top of sliced french bread.  

The Shrimp Po Boy was delicious also.  The shrimp was perfectly cooked and it went well with the crunchy cole slaw that was in the sandwich as well.

Meh...I should've checked the reviews before wasting my money on the food.  

I ordered the jambalaya which came with a biscuit and potato salad.  The biscuit came out of a package which was kept in a warmer (that looked like a mini fridge)..the bottom part was kind of soggy but the whole biscuit was dry.  The jambalaya came with only 3 small pieces of chicken and two small chunks of sausage.  The whole thing was just sad.  

It was my fault for not wanting to walk further down to see what other food offerings the terminal had.

I wanted to try allllll the beignets in Nola.  On our last day there, I Yelped beignets and found this place.   We gave it a chance and thank goodness we did..

These beignets are different from those from Cafe Du Monde.  These are flakier, lighter and less doughy.  I still like the ones from Cafe Du Monde just the same.  These are just different and good in their own way....we came in a little after they opened up.  There was no wait and the lady serving us was very sweet.  

We ended up just sitting outside and enjoying our beignets and cafe au lait in the beautiful weather.. (75°)...it was kind of bittersweet, in my opinion, because we were taking of in a few hours....we ended up ordering another batch.  Later, we were contemplating on buying some to go, but I was afraid they weren't going to sit well, being fresh out the fryer into the bag = soggyness and pasty confectioners sugar.  We ended up not ordering it to go...I should've asked the lady to fry some up but then let it cool down a bit before putting it in the bag and dumping the sugar in it.....ahhh, regrets...

On Mardi Gras day, we were originally going to go to Cafe Beignet for breakfast but as we got there, we saw that the place was closed.  We realized that, yea, Mardi Gras is a big deal down there.   It's a holiday and many businesses are closed for the day. 

So we're on the sidewalk looking for a place to eat.   We found this place and another.   Gave both a call to make sure they were open for business.  Both places were opened but we decided on this place, which was a good idea.

We arrived shortly before 8am, and we were the only ones there.  We had to walk through a bar to get to this place.   This place is also inside a hotel. 

I ordered the Boudin Benedict...I didn't know what boudin was so I quickly Googled it.  Sounded good.  We also ordered a side of smoked sausage and a Johnny cake to share.  The Johnny cake was a pancake made with cornmeal.  So it's like a cornbread pancake.  The waitress informed us that it's very very filling.  How most patrons can't finish their Johnny cake breakfast plate which comes with three.. luckily the side was only one. 

My boudin Benedict was very good.  The boudin was very flavorful.   It sat on a bed of collard greens which went well with the food.  It also came with homefries...yes, we were hungry.  The smoked sausage reminded me of a brand named Kielbasa..still good.

If I was a resident here, I'd definitely be a regular customer.

Came here with a large group (20) and it was a great experience. They have some nice patio seating as well as indoor. I had a small New York style pizza with sausage (they make it in house), mushrooms, and olives and it was amazing. Their garlic knots were also delicious and they had a vegan option which made some group members happy. Their salads are a healthy portion and are absolutely delicious. While the food is great, you're also supporting a worthy cause!

The bf and I loved this buffet when we stayed at Peppermill! We actually went twice during our stay here. Compared to $50 in Vegas, a $20 buffet price is not bad at all!

My favorites:
- Oyster shooters: huge oysters!!!!
- Prime rib: one night we went and it was DELICIOUS, the other night it was just ok... Guess it's a hit or miss
- Crab legs: only on weekends I think. They had large snow crab legs and also smaller dungeness crab.
- BBQ ribs: tender and bbq sauce is sweet!
- Fried butterfly shrimp: eat with cocktail sauce!
- Mashed potatoes: buttery and soft
- Asian sweet and spicy chicken: not sure what the name was... 
- Salad bar: can't forget veggies, even on vacation!
- Dessert: gelato and cheesecake!

Service was very friendly and we didn't have any problems! Would love to come back if I were in Reno.

What's in a name? 

I asked, and got the answer...
Chef/Owner Robert Perez told his kids "Don't follow in my footsteps. Stay out of the restaurant biz." But did his black sheep of a son listen? 
Nope. And lucky are we. 
Manager/Co-Owner Ruben Perez may not have seen his dad much as a kid(thanks to the the demanding work schedule that his father had) but they are catching up on lost time by running Black Sheep together. And expertly done, might I add. 

No, I'm not their publicist. Just one of the many devoted regulars who dote on this SB gem. 

The comfortable interior is classy, without being pretentious, and casual, without being complacent. 

Basically everything I've had is outstanding. 
These are some of my top picks...
Oyster Shooters
White Anchovies on Crostini w/orange zest
Scallop Crudo
Wagyu Beef Carpaccio  
Sautéed Sweetbreads
Wild Boar Spare Ribs
Shoyu Ramen
Braised New Zealand Lamb Shank
Beef Bone Morrow Bruschetta(absolute perfection, and my favorite thing on the menu)

I highly suggest doing the Chef's Tasting menu. It's an incredible value for all that you get to try. You can even ask for it to be customized as vegan or vegetarian.

Not only in their menu and in the expert execution of these dishes has attention been paid to every little detail, but also in every other facet of this establishment and the way it is run.

The staff genuinely seem to enjoy being at work and being part of the Black Sheep family. Furthermore, they make us regulars feel like family too.

I'll definitely be back soon!

Craving spicy Asian cuisine, I was contemplating queuing up with the crustpunks for free Indian grub at the Hare Krishna temple when inspiration struck: I had a Groupon for Sukho Thai! No standing in line tonight!  I'd feast on takeout  AND keep my budget under control. WIN-WIN. I phoned in an order of drunken noodles and shrimp-in-a-pouch and was told to pick it up in 20 minutes.

I showed up at Sukho Thai 20 minutes after phoning in the order and played a round of The Un-Staring Contest with the woman staffing the counter. It's kind of like a staring contest, except the first service industry worker to make eye contact with a customer is the loser. This lady ignored me like a pro; she managed  to avoid looking in my direction at all, even when I was standing feet away from her trying to maintain a pleasant expression. (In her defense, she was jotting something on a pad that was probably very important.) She disappeared and an affable young man said the food wasn't ready yet. I joined the other two hungry-looking individuals in what was to be a long wait for our orders (one of them was Peter of Satsuma, and Peter, you truly run a fine establishment. Much better than Sukho Thai). 

After 50 minutes, the master ignorer appeared with my drunken noodles. I whipped out my Groupon. "Oh, we don't take those for takeout orders. They're dine-in only," she said. 
"OK." I gave her my credit card.
"It says so right in on the Groupon. Look. It's very clearly stated." 
"I'm not arguing with you. But what if I just sit here and eat? Can I use it then?"
"I already ran your credit card," she said before reminding me AGAIN that the no takeout policy was very clearly stated on the form.
"Guess I need to read the fine print," I said.
"Sorry about that."
"It's not your fault."
"It never is," she said. "I'm innocent."

I ate my overdue, overpriced food, and the taste was the overly salty flavor of defeat. They didn't put tofu in the veggie drunken noodles (according to the menu, tofu is part of the dish), and the shrimp-in-a-pouch still had their tail fans on, which is weird and annoying, because you have to sift through an oily wonton pouch to remove them.

So, in a nutshell, my complaints: 1. The food was underwhelming and expensive ($23). 
2. It took 50 minutes to arrive when it was supposed to take 20.
3. The service was lackluster.
4. The Royal Street location isn't wheelchair accessible, so me and my boyfriend (he's disabled) have to sit outside on the sidewalk like second-class citizens if we want to eat there. 

I vowed never to eat at Sukho Thai again, but I probably will because I still have that damned Groupon. After that, we're through.

This is a good place to go after a bad breakup. The bar is dark, so nobody can see your tears. The music's loud, so nobody can hear your sobs. The mac and cheese is reliable and nourishing, everything the lover who spurned you is not. But it's also cheap ($3), so they have that in common. The drinks are stiff yet nuanced. It's smoky and just a little dank inside, so you don't feel like a downer when you're weeping into your Praying Mantis.

Not that I would ever create such a spectacle of myself.

We were in the area and just had to try the number 1 rated pizza place on Yelp. They did not disappoint.
 
I called as soon as they opened to place an order and they were already out of regular dough, so get your orders in early people! That turned out to be a blessing though, because the nice woman who answered the phone said they could make us a Sicilian style which we had never tried before. We chose ricotta with red sauce and basil and mushrooms and olives for toppings. I also ordered a cannoli sandwich for dessert.  

When we arrived to pick up our order there was a line outside and I know why. This pizza is delicious! The staff was friendly and fast and all wearing masks. We took the food back to our room and I almost didn't make it because the smell was so great, I was tempted to open it and try a slice in the car.  The dough was perfect, with a nice crunch and still so soft and moist. You could taste the freshness in the toppings... heck, you could practically taste the love they put into the pizza as well. 

But as scrumptious as the pizza was, the cannoli sandwich was to die for. It was so fluffy and delicious. The cinnamon was heavenly and I swear I thought about that thing for a week straight. I cannot wait to patronize this business again!

As good as it gets indeed.  5 stars for overall dining experience.  3 Brits and an Hon. Brit out on the prowl for curry  as is expected of a Saturday night.  Large room, probably seats 100, buffet set up down the middle for lunch. 

Batata Dal Puri - potatoes, noodles, onion, yoghurt and sweet sauce (8) - delish
Tandoori Paneer - 4 large  pieces - delish
Chilli Fish - sweet and spicy - more indo chinese - 8 pieces delish
Muligatawny Soup - one of the best in a long long time - we used it as a dipping sauce

Shrimp Tandoori - delish - dipped them in the Muligatawny - yum
Lamb Vindaloo - delish - oh yes hot but not too hot, more Madras than Vindy
Lamb Achari - delish but a tad salty for my taste.
Methi Malai Mutter - for the love of god, this was heavenly, for those not in the know, its chopped fenugreek leaves, peas and cream.

Huge amount of food and we polished most of it off with the remainder for brekkie today.

The menu in the Taj is extensive and creative, offering much more than the other places in Nashville.  There are extensive veggie dishes and Dosas in additional to all the usual suspects and a good selection of puri's.The Patel's who have the supermarket up the road own the place and are showcasing their ingredients off nicely.  The service is almost invisible, quiet and polite without any pushiness.  What I really liked was how the place went from almost empty to full when we left and the noise level never got any louder.

$90 for all the above bounty plus 1 Flying horse and a Ras Malai for the table -really good value for the portion sizes. 
Have tried lots of Indian Places throughout the USA and this is one of the best.

continuing the Happy Hour Crawl. ...Small bar area with the mandatory TV screens, volume off and some nice music playing.  Arguably the most expensive martinis in town and easily some of the worst.  $13.95 for a blood orange martini, large portion BUT horribly made with Skyy Orange Vodka (corporate rules I guess). Artificially nasty in every way.  We split this and had the steak sliders(4)  $7, meat was delicious but the bun so ordinary all bread was left.  Crab cakes (3 mini) $7 very tasty.
I could get the same dirty martini here for $17.50 instead of the $5 perfect one I just had at Flemings.
Value for Money - Meh not really
Service - Meh - polite but had that "Like I give a toss that you really don't like our Skyy Orange Vodka, we know its horrible."
Would not go back here for Happy Hour and also do not care for their dinners either.
This place needs some help.  Hate to complain brought my son to show him this rad facility, however the service and wait times .... didn't roll well.

I love this place! We arrived ~25min before closing time but they still took our order, thank you! There's a cozy feel about this restaurant-- self seating, but with a large and clean indoor area and a well-kept patio area. 

They give free tortilla chips and have a nice salsa bar. One order of the steak molcajetes was plenty to share between two people. Comes with 3 home-made corn tortillas, delicious! I also got their passion fruit iced tea, which is just one of the fountain drinks. Still refreshing, just not fresh. 

I felt bad for being the last ones out of the restaurant but Los Agaves never rushed us and even gave me a refill of the iced tea.

I have been here a number of times and am never disappointed.  From the salad and garlic bread to the entrees and service, everything is top notch.  I came in on a Saturday night at 6 pm without reservations and was promptly seated even though they had a nearly full house and reservations arriving shortly.  My server, Jen, told me the specials, which sounded delicious, but I ordered the sauteed shrimp with a basil cream sauce.  I asked if it was served over pasta and she said yes.  When the dish came out it was served over risotto which was a pleasant surprise.  The meal was delicious.  The cream sauce was light and flavorful.  I was given a full basket of garlic bread and ended up eating the whole thing.  I would be perfectly content just eating their salad with house Italian and a basket of garlic bread.  On the upside, I have enough leftovers to have a meal tomorrow so that is a win. 

I love Zozo's and have come in for their lunch specials as well as early bird dining.  I would recommend it to anyone looking for good food with a quaint Italian feel.

I hesitate to write this review because I don't want to give away the secret. Beer NV recently started an Adult Game Night. I have been interested since the first time I heard about it and was finally able to get a group together to go last night.
OH MY GOSH!!!!! I haven't laughed so hard in ages. Up to 5 teams of 4-8 people play three games for 40 minutes each. Winner on each team wins a gift card to Beer NV. Don't worry if you don't have enough people to make a team. They will add singles and smaller groups together to make a team.
As busy as it was, service at the bar was still good. If you like beer and haven't been to Beer NV, what are you waiting for? They have a huge selection of beer and ale on tap. Their tap list is even online!
In addition to Adult Game night on Wedensdays, they also have DJ Trivia on Tuesday nights.
Looking for food to go with your beer? Beer NV doesn't have a kitchen but there are a few places in their shopping center that will deliver food and you are welcome to eat in. Choices include Los Compadres Mexican, Yosh's Unique Deli, and South Creek Pizza.
Can't wait to go back next week!!!!!!!!

Don't let the outside fool you. The inside is very nicely decorated. Not overstated. Our party of 5 opted to go with the Chinese buffet for our first trip. The quality of the food on the buffet was surprisingly good. There was a wide variety of seafood including mussels, oysters, shrimp, crab legs, crawdads, and white fish. There was also beef, pork, chicken, tofu, and vegetables.
Everything was very clean. My only disappointment was that the soft serve ice cream was not available. The sesame balls with red bean and the coconut balls with mango were quite tasty according to my dinner mates.
Next time we will try the hot pot.

Sandwich and service lived up to the reviews. The girl that helped me explained the process for build your own but then I saw the French Dip and decided to go with that. The bread was nice and fresh. The amount of meat was sufficient, not too thick. The flavor was good. 

Upon checking in on Yelp I noticed a free cookie offer. She came around to the front of the counter to show me my options which I thought was very nice of her. 

I was going to take my sandwich to go but noticed they had a small seating area so I decided to stay. Good thing I did because I forgot to grab my drink cup and she brought it over to me. It seems like when that happens other places I remember later and then have to go back up and ask for a cup. Service here is excellent.

She even gave me a punch card to buy 10 get 1 free. This place is closer enough to work and the service is quick enough I'm sure I will be back.

My friends took me here to celebrate my birthday on a Wednesday night. They are regulars here but it was my first time. They called ahead for reservations and told them we were celebrating a birthday. When we arrived there was confetti on the table along with a birthday card. Our server, Tim, took our drink order then went over the specials for the evening. 

I was thinking about ordering from the early bird menu because Sterling's is a bit pricey. My friends insisted I order whatever I wanted so, after they went with the special (Filet and Prawn) I decided to go with the smaller cut of Prime Rib and French Onion Soup. YUM! 

I started with a Moscow Mule. I'm not a connoisseur by any means but I enjoyed the drink. The French Onion Soup followed and it was cheesy and flavorful. Next came my prime rib and, OMG, it was phenomenal! Cooked perfectly to medium rare, it was just the right size. It came with au jus and horseradish, both straight and creamed, The au jus was completely unnecessary. The meat was juicy and delicious.

Desserts...I went with DEMOLISH THE DOME - White Chocolate Shell, Coffee Chocolate Mousse, Vanilla Chiffon, Raspberries, Hot Raspberry Caramel Sauce and Crème Anglaise. The presentation was the best part. The hot raspberry caramel sauce is poured over the white chocolate shell which causes it to melt and open up. Decadent. Unfortunately,I was so full there was no way i could finish it but I enjoyed every bite. Tim also brought us a Creme Brulee Flight to share, complements of Sterling's.

Will I go back? Yep! I ended up going back a few days later for their Sunday Brunch. It was another amazing meal. Lamb chops, Filet mignon, salmon, shrimp scampi, cold shrimp, crab legs, omelet bar, dessert bar, meats, cheeses, fruits, and more. Oh, and bottomless mimosas! Well worth the price. Tim was our server again and did a wonderful job, even with some of my dining partner's special requests.

An excellent contribution to the St. Pete community. This business truly cares about the city and the citizens they serve. It is great to have an establishment open late without it being "just a bar." You can sit and have a conversation, play board games, view the art on the walls or write a chalkboard message. 

The food is health conscious, fresh and made to order. I had a Tuna Melt on a Lenten Friday and was very happy and satisfied! My tea was very good too. 

The staff was extremely friendly and talked to me at length about the goals they have to serve the community. 

Be sure to stop in and support mid-town and St. Pete!

I used to work at Fireside back in 2007, so you are getting the inside scoop from a former server who has seen and tasted all of the food and can tell you what Fireside is and what it isnt. I left on good terms, and when I visit Ambler from time to time I stop in, usually for an Eagles game.
What Fireside is:
-Best place in Ambler to get a steak. Sure, you can go to Bridgets, but be sure to take a small loan out first and keep foolin yourself that somehow their cows are  from a higher society than the ones yer gonna eat around the corner.The best day for this is on Sundays for their Prime Rib special. You are essentially getting 2 days worth of steak, and it comes with sides and a salad.
-A place you can HONESTLY get lunch on a 1 hr lunch break and not be late getting back. If things are running behind, I assure you its not due to appathy. Its most likely because of thos pain in the ass nurses accross the street at the nursing home who call in  EVERY DAY, an order for 30 people, everything on the side, and seperate checks. I dont work there anymore so I can say this......those nurses are criminals when it comes to proper customer etiquette. 
-Best quality steak sandwich. Its called Pete's Favorite. Its filet mignon on a fresh roll, and you're not getting that kind of quality from anywhere else in Ambler for that price.
-Great happy hour. And the neighborhood knows it. Its packed. If you're lookin to drink off the work day amongst Ambler's hardworking populace, and even get some complimentary pizza at the bar, go for it. 
-Salads to be proud of. HUGE. A real meal. Need meat too? They'll put more than enough on it. 
-Great wings. Not those stupid, breaded pizza shop wings. Good ones

What Fireside is NOT:

-A place to go for a quiet dinner where you are going to have your husband's attention. The bar gets loud, but its a friendly kind of loud. There are TVs however.....EVERYWHERE!!!!!! You can't escape them!! They are at every turn, and each one has something different on them. If you need eye contact from your spouse or you are on a date where you actually care about what the other is saying.....save this spot for when your relationship has no more surprises and you aren't finishing each other's sentences.

-A craft brew/foodie Mecca. This it is NOT. Domestic Beers, maybe some Dos Equis. This is not the land of microbrews, and none of the food is going to ever have qinoa or safron infusion in it. Nothing innovative. This is food the way your Grandpop wants it , and that  the doctor warned him about 2 months before his triple bipass. And its delicious.

-A place to show up with your kids for a LATE dinner. Fireside is certainly kid friendly. But the bar is seperated from the dining room by a  simple half wall with some frosted glass partitioning. You can hear everything. If your kids are already cursing like sailors, and that flies well with you, then by all means Sailor, rally up your daughters to put on their finest booty shorts, share a smoke with em outside on the way in, and fist pump the night away watching UFC guys beat the Jesus lovin Hell out of each other over some Veal parm. Families that twerk together, stay together. I think.

-

The quality for Center City Restaurant Week seems to be declining year after year. There aren't too many restaurants that bother putting out a worthwhile prix fixe menu. That is not the case for Gran Caffe L'Aquila though.

For $40, you get 4 courses, instead of 3. They didn't have to add that extra course, and I can definitely appreciate that they did. Sure, the portions may not be huge, but they are reasonably portioned, and you are sufficiently full if not satiated by the time dinner is over.

The wine list is extensive and well-priced. We selected a bottle of Dugal to pair with dinner.

Some highlights of the night were the Flash Fried artichokes served with lemon, Wild board & long hot pepper meatballs, Gnocchi alla Bava e Tartufo, and Papardelle al Ragu Aquilano.

We concluded dinner with two scoops of gelato each.

We came on a Friday night, and it was busy for sure but service was fine. Dinner lasted about 1.5 hours, which is standard. Overall I would say, a successful Restaurant Week experience.

We've been getting dim sum takeout from China Gourmet for quite some now. Even though China Gourmet is in Northeast Philly, and a lot further than Chinatown's Ocean Harbor and Ocean City, it is worth the 50 minutes roundtrip drive. 

We've never eaten inside the restaurant, as it's just my husband and I, and we've gotten used to getting dim sum to go since the pandemic started. Also, I can't imagine how long the wait time can be during peak dim sum hour. 

Anyway, The variety and quality of the dim sum dishes here are just so much better. And the fact that I have not gotten food poisoning from here gets an extra star from me. Yay China Gourmet!

It's 5pm on a Friday. The work week is over and I am ready to get out of my house. So, we hit up Jet Wine Bar. The outside setup was perfect -- for a romantic or a casual friend date. The whole place was beautifully lit.

As we looked through the menus, we see a variety of drinks to choose from. The Spiked Mexican Hot Chocolate caught our eye, but in the end, we opted for a bottle of the Macedon pinot noir. We were at a wine bar after all. We also ordered the smoked BBQ wings to munch on, as it seemed like it would pair well with the pinot noir. 

My husband and I spent a good two hours sitting back, enjoying our wine and wings under the night sky. It wasn't a super cold night, but each table had its own heat lamp and the option of adjusting the heat to their preference. 

I see us coming back alot to hang out in the wine garden and also to try other wines.

I've been meaning to check out Bar Hygge after seeing other Yelpers post delicious food pictures from the place, so I made a reservation for my husband and I for a Wednesday night. 

The weather had been getting a lot colder, but we lucked out this Wednesday night and enjoyed some mid 50 degree weather. Since indoor seating at Bar Hygge isn't ready yet, everyone was seated outside. The outside seating was more than fine. Every table was spaced out and had a heat lamp next to it or above it. The hostess even offered us blankets if we didn't find the heat lamps sufficient, which was a really good idea. I'm not sure if other restaurants are doing this too, but this definitely gets Bar Hygge extra points. 

For our drinks, I had the Lemon Meringue IPA and my husband had the Cast Iron (Nitro), which is a dry Irish stout. The Lemon Meringue IPA drinks like any other IPA but was light and refreshing. My husband enjoyed his Irish stout. Other than their house-brewed beers, Bar Hygge also has a small but decent wine selection, and delicious cocktails -- cold AND hot.

For food, my husband and I shared a Hygge Board, with pork speck, fried artichokes, blistered Shishitos, crispy brussel sprouts, and the Sottocenere cheese with Truffle. 

The Hygge Board was all right, fun to pick on. The fried artichokes were delicious, but they only gave us 4 lil bite size pieces. Serving sizes for the other items were pretty generous. The Shishito peppers were served with a pesto sauce, and were on the spicy side. The brussels sprouts were good. The pork speck was nicely sliced and arranged in a nice big pile. Finally the Sottocenere cheese had a truffle rind, and had hints of truffle as I ate it. I am a truffle fan, but this cheese was just ok. 

Then my husband and I split a Toddy Time, a hot cocktail to warm us up. Overall, I liked the drinks but not so much the food. You do have to order food if you're planning on ordering drinks. And you have 90 minutes to dine, which is pretty standard in restaurants in Philly during COVID times.

Missing Hawaii and was craving poke, so we decided to get some from Red Poke Express, since the reviews look promising.

This was our first time ordering from Red Poke Express, and our expectations were adjusted, because mainland poke just isn't going to be as good.

When we first saw the takeout container it looked small, but once we started digging in, we realized how big the portions actually were.

Overall, Red Poke Express exceeded expectations. The raw fish was fresh and cut up in nice medium chunks. For the price, quality and portions, this was pretty great. This will be our choice spot for poke for now. The sauces were okay, but so is the sauce everywhere else.

Placed an online order for a bagel and coffee before my commute this morning and received a call from the restaurant confirming my order.

When I arrived 10 minutes after my confirmed time, I was disappointed to find that my order was not ready. What was the point of calling me earlier to confirm the order if you're not going to make it until I get there?

They are also not allowing customers inside due to COVID. So, I stood at the door and relayed my order to the staff to make my food. Thankfully, it did not take too long for my order to be prepared, as there was no one ahead of me. 

The nice lady went back and forth to collect my payment and to bring my food over to me as I waited at the door. They need to have a better system than this.

Overall, the bagel and iced coffee were both good. I would recommend against mixing schmears unless you know they taste good together.

There is also $10 minimum for credit card.

Szechuan Four Rivers has been around for years. Last December, we tried them for the first time, and we've already ordered from them 4x, within a month.

I am not a fan of Szechuan food. I find Han Dynasty overly salty and spicy, and I dread going there when my husband craves it, but Szechuan Four Rivers is different. They don't overdo it with the peppercorns.

The food is mildly spicy, yet so authentic, and so good, it's dangerous. You just can't stop eating until you have finished everything in sight.

We've enjoyed everything we've eaten so far, but right now, our favorite dishes are definitely the griddle cooked lamb or griddle cooked cauliflower, cold chicken with spicy sauce, and fish with bell pepper. I am obsessed, OBSESSED, with the griddle cooked dishes. This version is different from the dry pot at a lot of places, and I love how theirs has Chinese cauliflower and fried potato in it. I could just eat the cauliflower and be okay with no meat.

Szechuan Four Rivers now holds a permanent spot in our weekly takeout rotation. I cannot wait to try everything on their menu, but for now, you know I am getting that griddle cooked dish once a week.

After being to Ba Le many more times, I have come to appreciate their banh mi's a lot more. The banh mi's are big, refreshing, and delicious. That one time I ordered a banh mi that had a certain smell must have been an off day, all the banh mi's we've had after that did not have any funky smells. My favorite banh mi is the #2 with the pork belly.

They have recently raised their prices (only by a little) for inflation and while there is no longer a credit card minimum, you have to pay a credit card fee if you do not meet the spending minimum. So just bring cash, unless you're buying 3 or more banh mi's.

The aromas of delicious grilled meats emanating from Apricot Stone would make you salivate. You can smell it from blocks away. I don't know how it took us so long to finally come here, when we have been tempted by the smells wafting over while chilling on the roof on so many Saturday afternoons. 

Anyway, we finally made reservations for dinner last week during Restaurant Week.

For the first course, we chose the eggplant salsa and the Eech. The eggplant salsa was refreshing and acted as a nice palate cleanser but was just ok. My husband had the Eech, which is a grain, kinda like a couscous, cooked in tomato paste - flavorful and quite tasty.

For the second course, we shared the Khnkali Dumplings and the Jingyalov Hats. Both of which we enjoyed. The Khnkali Dumplings reminded me of a soup dumpling but with much thicker dumpling skin. The Jingyalov Hat is a flatbread filled with green veggies and herbs. And if you ever watch that picnic episode on Worth It (Buzzfeed web series), you know what I'm talking about. It was cool trying it for the first time. Very delicious and very healthy as well.

For the third course, my husband ordered the lamb shank, and I really wanted to as well. But thought I would get the Bamia so we can have variety and try more things. The Bamia was a tomato-based beef stew with lots of okra. Don't get me wrong, the Bamia was good and I can imagine it would be perfect for a cold night, but after tasting a piece of that huge lamb shank that was grilled to perfection, I was really kicking myself for not ordering it. Hellooo, the "Mediterranean Grill" is in the name for a reason. 

Overall, it was a great dinner, and I hope they will bring back the lamb shank even after Restaurant Week is over. We are definitely coming back to dine and for takeout.

Stopped by Philadelphia Distilling for some afternoon drinking last Saturday and loved every minute of it. You can't tell from the store front, but inside, it's Industrial meets Mid-Century Modern. Even their bathrooms were consistent with the theme.

We didn't realize they were checking vaccination cards, but thankfully we all saved a pic of our cards on our phones, so make sure you do that, or you won't be allowed in. You may not even be allowed to sit outside, as our reservation was made for outside, but we were still required to show proof of vaccination.

Normally, the menu is accessible thru QR code; however, the website was down while we were there, and no one was able to access the menu. The staff did manage to print out some menus. In the meantime, our server, Alfredo provided our table with suggestions on different cocktails our table might enjoy. Also, checking their Instagram profile can be very useful. You can find pictures and descriptions of some of their featured cocktails.

The cocktails here were delicious and everyone seemed to love what they ordered. Can I just say, service here is impeccable! Our server, Alfredo was so sweet. He took care of us and made sure our water glasses were full at all times.

From pictures, it looks like they offer board games for their guests' enjoyment, but we didn't make use of that. Philadelphia Distilling is my new favorite cocktail spot. Can't wait to come back and check out their distillery tour.

Finally ate at Kyuramen with some friends over the weekend and was pleasantly surprised!

We arrived at 2pm for a late lunch, and strangely the place was packed. After waiting about 10 minutes, we were led to the side of the restaurant with a bunch of private booths styled to look like Japanese rooms, which was very, very cool. Inside each booth, there is a button you can push to call on the waitstaff.

Kyuramen's menu is extensive! And they have omurice! The server brings out the omelette and slices it in front of you as you watch the inside ooze out. And it tastes great too!

If you just can't make up your mind on which ramen to eat, you have the option of having two different flavors in a bowl separated with two compartments. The chewiness of the ramen was perfect. Broth was tasty and the chashu pork was not too lean, and not too fatty.

Food was sent out of the kitchen as it's ready and was taking quite some time for everyone's food to arrive. Understandably, they are very busy as it's their grand opening week.

I do hope they add alcoholic beverages to their menu. Currently this location only serves sodas, lemonades and teas.

Last Sunday was our first time trying Xun Yu Si Kao and we really enjoyed it. I don't typically seek out Szechuan foods as I don't particularly enjoy the numbing spiciness of Szechuan food; however, a friend was in town, and was interested in trying the cuisine.

We arrived right before noontime on a Sunday and did not have trouble getting a seat. For food, we ordered the Fish pot (highly recommended by Yelpers), and a Spicy pot. Both dishes were customizable, and you can choose the spice level and toppings for what goes into your Fish or Spicy pot.

There are also plenty of other options on the menu to choose from if you don't feel like the Fish or Spicy pots. We were pleasantly surprised to see the menu contained many, many pages. But, we were committed to ordering the pots as they seem to be the featured dishes.

The Fish pot was served in a shallow broth, in the most majestic looking, rectangular tray. Our tofu, noodles, and vegetable toppings were laid under the two whole sea basses to absorb all the flavors of the broth. The sea basses seemed kind of small, but there was definitely more than enough food between the fish and the toppings for everyone. It was delicious, but not as delicious as the Spicy pot.

The Spicy pot, also a dry pot/stir fry was served in a round majestic looking pot. It ended up being everybody's favorite. Personally, I would recommend the Spicy pot over the Fish pot.

I almost forgot, but dessert was a complimentary grass/turtle (not made of turtles) jelly. A quality, tasty, slightly sweet and healthy dessert.

Definitely glad that we stopped by Xun Yu Si Kao. The servers were very nice and checked on us several times.

P.S. they do not take reservations.

All these years of living in Philly, we never thought to check out EMei. But after reading so many acclaimed reviews of EMei, we just had to check it out for ourselves.

We stopped by for lunch with a group of friends last Sunday. I made a reservation for 12pm, but it wasn't busy. From the outside of the restaurant, you would not expect the interior to look the way it did. Inside, it was farmhouse décor with mid-century modern furniture, and felt like you're in a little village, in a cute way.
