As for the food, the food was freakin delicious. I was under the impression EMei was a Szechuan restaurant, but they have Cantonese dishes too. Not only were the Szechuan dishes well done and sufficiently spicy, but the Cantonese dishes were on point too!

Our entire group enjoyed everything we ate. EMei is definitely taking over as our new favorite restaurant in Chinatown!

We were first gifted a Stock's pound cake by our realtor a few weeks back. Like a fellow yelper said, how good could a pound cake be? It's a pound cake! 

Well, this pound cake with icing on the top is possibly THE best pound cake I've eaten in my life. Rich, buttery and kind of reminds me of Sara Lee. My husband and I polished off the entire loaf in two days. And then bought ourselves three more. 

We arrived 10 mins after the bakery opened on a Tuesday morning, and waited about 35 minutes in line to get inside the bakery. A pound cake costs between $12-13, but it's worth it. 

I also overheard the tea biscuits are delicious, but they were already sold out. I will have to come back another time for those!

Don't forget to bring cash!

Had dinner at Fork last week to celebrate our anniversary. While Fork is located so close to us, it never occurred to me to check it out.

We started dinner off with the Unlitro Tuscan blend, and it was deliciously easy to drink.

Per our waiter's recommendations, we decided to go with the pate appetizer and the feast for two with the whole black bass (you can also opt for the short rib).

Our appetizer arrived, and we dug in. It took some time for us to realize this wasn't the pate appetizer that we ordered, but the Yellow Springs cloud nine cheese. An error made by our waiter, but this local French styled goat cheese handmade to look like a snowball was sooo yummy and tasted much better than the pate that we had after. I highly recommend ordering this.

The feast for two took 30-40 minutes to prepare, which we were warned about. In hindsight, we should have gotten the short rib instead of the black bass for ease of eating, as the feast involved wrapping the protein in a lettuce wrap with Korean noodle salad. Even though the black bass was already deboned, there were the occasional bones.

After all that food, my husband still wanted dessert, so we ordered the olive oil cake. I took a bite of the olive oil cake, which I was so glad I did. The olive oil cake was amazing, and the BEST thing I ate that night.

Fork is underrated for sure. The food was good and the staff were very nice. Would love to come back again if not for dinner, maybe brunch.

Frankly, we miss the Big Fat Greek which was great for a business lunch or a good dinner so we went through a bit of angst wondering what might take its place. We drove by today and were happy to find Heist open. We started with the shrimp appetizer which was excellent though a bit overpriced. We split the roasted beet and chicken salad which was very good with lots of roasted chicken, beets, and bits of bright green apple. It was tasty and would have made a nice lunch by itself. 

We are limiting gluten intake so ordered pizzas with the gluten free crust. My wife chose the wild mushroom pizza. We didn't particularly care for the crust, though it was as good as we have had gluten free. The tomato sauce was light, full of herbs, and very garlicky. Delicious. The fresh cheeses were also excellent. It probably could have used more mushrooms but we both liked it.

I ordered the pesto laden Green Eggs and Ham pizza. The manager had them re-fire it before it was brought to our table because he thought it overdone but it still came out just minutes after my wife's pizza. He even brought out an extra egg that he said he 'owed me' even though I hadn't complained and wouldn't have known it was missing. That was nice. I liked the blend of flavors, but my wife preferred the tomato sauce on her pizza. 

The server was a pleasant young man who kept our tea and soda glasses filled which is always an expectation of mine. The glasses were smallish so he made lots of trips, but he did it with a pleasant smile. He also asked us to come back which was a nice touch. The manager was a guy who used to be part of My Big Fat Greek and it was nice to see him again. When my wife mentioned that the music was too loud for easy conversation he apologized and immediately turned it down and then returned to ask if it was better. That is just good management.

If you remember the old building you will remember that the restrooms opened directly into the dining room which was awkward when you walked out and were still checking your zipper. The remodel puts a wall between the dining area and the restrooms which is a good addition. 

Good food. Good service. Good management. And it is close to home. We'll be back.

Excellent coffee for on-site consumption or whole bean, to go.  Several restaurants in town serve one of their blends.  Great service.  Spotlessly clean shop and restroom.  Very limited food offerings, but you're here for the coffee, so Java up!

First time trying Wakin' Bakin' since they opened their French Quarter location in this space previously occupied by Eat NOLA. The vibe is comfortable and casual with a bright, cheery ambiance that fits nicely with their breakfast/lunch business model.  

We got lucky and were seated immediately at 10:30 on a busy Sunday morning.  Friendly and efficient service.  Started with a cup of French Truck coffee, which is one of the best cups o' joe in NOLA.  For entrees, I went with the biscuits & gravy with sausage and scrambled eggs.  The biscuits are awesome, with a honey cornbread taste & consistency.  The sausage gravy was pretty good, but a little saltier than I'd like.  My bride had "the usual", which she enjoyed.  The bacon confit (a little softer than regular bacon) and Cajun hash were the stars of the plate.  

Bottom-line, better than average breakfast option in the Quarter, but not quite worthy of making my list of the top 10 best breakfast/brunches in NOLA.

I love to see an establishment grow and add locations, while maintaining perfection at their original store.  As good as District Donuts was years ago, it's actually better now.  

I'm not gonna lie, when I tell you that I was more than a little bummed to see my former favorite Monte Cristo sandwich gone from the menu.... until I tried the new chicken biscuit.  The biscuit is a bit crispy, dripping with spicy honey, holding a perfectly spicy, breaded, mouthwatering chicken breast.  

The coffee and donuts are all amazing, too.  Great service, spotlessly clean and safe during the pandemic, too!  Kudos DDSB!!!

Five stars for the hip ambiance & funky patio with live Latin music.  A solid four stars for the authentic, upscale Mexican cuisine, including ceviche, guacamole, chips & salsa, chicken enchiladas mole, tacos, gulf fish, etc.  All very good!  Great margaritas, but at $11 and up, they should be incredible!  

Sadly, the two-star service, left a lasting impression.  I like the fact that they don't rush you, however it would have been nice to have been paid a visit by our server in the 30-45 minutes after finishing our meal.  We finally had to track him down to pay our tab (w/20% gratuity included), which could have been higher with more drinks, had they been offered.  

Sure, you can get food & drinks every bit as good (and much less expensive), at Juan's and La Casita, but the "experience " makes Casa Borrega a viable option in the rapidly up-and-coming OCH corridor.

Old school NOLA 5-star dining at its finest.  By "old school" I don't mean outdated or past it's prime, but simply that this is the kind of restaurant that keeps New Orleans the envy of the culinary community.  The ambiance is dressy, but not stuffy.  The service is world class.  The food is amazing.  The wine list and cocktails are all you'd expect.  

Dickie Brennan's is the kind of restaurant that you'd choose for a special occasion.  In our case, a wedding anniversary.  Every member of the staff recognized the occasion.  Following a bottle of wine, salad and vichyssoise, we opted for the black drum and petite fillets for our entrees.  Dessert, complete with "Happy Anniversary" spelled out in chocolate, consisted of creme brûlée and chocolate praline mousse.  Everything was perfect, start to finish!

Locals and tourists alike know that the best neighborhood bars in the city are off Bourbon.  MRB is one that you won't want to miss.  In addition to great drinks, they've got multiple TVs to catch your favorite game, an awesome kitchen with excellent fresh oysters (raw or chargrilled), ostrich chili (sorry, Big Bird) and some of the best nachos around!  Super friendly service and a chill courtyard, too!  Don't miss it!

Very hip little taco/mezcal spot on Capdeville, in the space formerly occupied by a bar/restaurant by the same name. A couple tables outside, but you definitely need to step inside to appreciate the ambiance.  

I've had EM bookmarked for a year or two and finally made it in for lunch today.  We were seated immediately at a table in the bar area (after vax verification, of course).  The server did a great job.  Started with a mezcal margarita and chips with two salsas. The drink was outstanding.  The chips and salsa, were just okay IMO.  Admittedly, I'm more of a fan of salsas with some texture... not necessarily chunky, but not the total liquid variety like their mild.  The medium was a little better, but nothing to leave you wanting more.  

For entrees, I had a fish taco, a shrimp taco and elote.  All three were very good, but that elote was amazing!  My bride had the chicken adobo torta, which is served with fries.  This is a very large sandwich, loaded with flavor.  (They could get away with calling it a poboy, if only they used Leidenheimer bread). The fries were awesome.  Dare I say probably the best I've ever had at a Mexican restaurant ;)  

In a town that has stepped up its Mexican food game considerably over the past few years, Espiritu Mezcaleria has established itself as a legit contender!

The Vampire Cafe has been on my short list for a few months, based on earlier reviews and numerous times walking by.  

Finally decided to give them a try today for a late lunch.  We were greeted and seated (inside) promptly.  The dining room is fairly small, but they do offer a few sidewalk tables, as well.  The vibe was pretty good.  Sure, a little kitschy, but not bad.  The service was exceptionally good.  Decent specialty drink menu, with all drinks assigned a "blood type".  I went with the mezcal jalapeño margarita (aka O+).  It went down so easy, I needed two.  My date had the "Vangria", a red sangria, which was great.  

We started with the elephant garlic appetizer, with was nothing special, but not bad.  We do them at home on occasion, so knew what we were getting.  We then split the little gem salad and mushroom pappardelle, both of which were ok, but here again, not in the same league as Sylvain's pappardelle dish, which is world-class.  The salad was good, but definitely not 5-star quality by NOLA standards.  

The tuna tar tar looked amazing. I've heard the filet is great.  The wine flights and charcuterie boards looked tempting, as well.  I'll possibly give them another try sometime, based on the great service and good drinks, but they've got a ways to go to earn 5-stars in my book, even with the complimentary "vampire bite" tattoo.

Great atmosphere!  Open & inviting space on St. Charles, with the distillery as the backdrop for the dining room and bar.  Fairly limited menu, which is fine with me.  I opted for the lemon grass shrimp.  Very unique dish with perfectly seasoned head-on jumbo shrimp served in a bowl over french fried potatoes and a few other vegetable, including snap peas.  Highly recommended!  My date had the steak salad.  She loved the salad, but found the skirt steak to be a little less tender than she'd like.  Next time she'd ask to have the steak prepared medium rare.  Others at our table enjoyed the quail and fish.  Both dishes were outstanding!  The service was best-in-class, as well.  

Looking forward to my next visit to Lula, perhaps over happy hour to indulge in their signature spirits!

I do my best to avoid Bourbon Street restaurants, with very few exceptions.  Mambos has joined that short list.  Don't let the location fool you.  This is a legit restaurant that deserves the support of locals and tourists, alike.  

Friends visiting from out of town wanted to try "local" food.  With so many places still closed on Tuesday nights, I decided tonight was the night to give Mambo's a try.  The friendly host was able to get us onto the rooftop patio, where we were offered our choice of tables by a very friendly, professional and efficient server.  

We started with drinks from the decent cocktail menu and wine from the limited offerings, then shared the spinach dip, which was cheesy and good.  For an entree I opted for the crab cakes and a side salad.  I highly recommend both.  Two of my dinner dates shared the red beans & rice with chicken, which was just so-so.  The other had the burger with looked good.  

I'd return for crab cakes or one of the pasta or seafood dishes, in spite of the Bourbon Street curse.

I'll let you in on a little secret... Bayona's 23rd Anniversary, 3-course $23 lunch, with .23 there martini (gin, vodka, manhattan or lemon drop) is the best deal in town!  

The food & service is off-the-charts amazing anytime, but this deal is almost too good to be true. Start off with a Bayona salad, followed by your choice of four solid entrees and a bowl of ice cream, all for $23. Can't beat it!

I'm always hesitant to review a delivery order because so much of it is beyond the control of the restaurant, but in this case what the restaurant could control was very good.  Ordered the three meat platter.  Excellent brisket (burnt ends, as requested), great St Louie ribs and an awesome piece of smoked chicken, which had the perfect spiciness to it.  Two extra little cups of delicious BBQ sauce for dipping.  The meats could have been a little warmer, but it's a chilly day, so having them cool off a bit on the 12-15 minute drive isn't a dealbreaker.  

The coleslaw and potato salad were both fantastic.  

Unfortunately, I didn't get the mac & cheese or cornbread that I thought I'd ordered, so guess I'll save those for an in-house expensive.

For those of you who have missed the bahn mi tacos during Covid...  BREAKING NEWS!  It's back!  Not on the menu, but you can order it, and order it I did!  Still the freshest taco in town!  Full of spicy goodness!!!  The happy hour double house margaritas are sure winners, as well.  

Honestly, Juan's is still a "must visit".  The tacos, burritos, chips, salsa, guacamole are all phenomenal!  

Don't be afraid to visit during the pandemic.  Additional outdoor seating has been added.  Plenty of space to distance and hand sanitizer available.

CC's puts out the best iced mochas in town.  Not my favorite cup of coffee in the neighborhood (Spitfire holds that distinction), but if you're in the quarter and looking for a refreshing mocha latte, don't miss this location.  The baristas are friendly and efficient.  The store is always clean, and practices COVID safety protocol.

I find it rare when an establishment can find a way to open satellite locations that are as good as the original.  In the case of this location, Ruby Slipper has successfully done so.  The food is as good.  The drinks are as good.  The service is as good, or better.  The atmosphere is definitely better.  It's hard to beat an historic bank building!  

We walked over for breakfast this morning.  Due to ridiculously cold weather, we had to sit inside, which we've been avoiding, in general, during the pandemic.  We felt perfectly safe due to the cleanliness of the restaurant, spacing of the tables, the masking of staff and availability of hand sanitizer.  

The hostess was pleasant and professional.  The server was awesome.  Wonderful eggs benedict.  The biscuits and gravy, while not the very best in the city, are easily in the top 5.  Great mimosas.  The candied bacon appetizer was pretty good, but doesn't quite compare to the praline bacon at Elizabeth's.

It's clubs like Bamboula's that make this two block stretch of Frenchman Street one of the hands-down best places for live music in the country.  Pretty much anytime from late morning through the wee hours of the next morning you can listen to amazing local music (usually with no cover charge), in a clean, family-friendly club, with great drinks and service to match.  The historic ambiance is best in class.  If you get a chance to visit during the daytime when the crowds are more manageable, don't miss it.

I was a little harsh last time in and dedicated a star for slow table service.  Now that I've found a work-around that's never an issue.  Insider tip: if your party is small enough, sit at the bar (first come, first served) for fast and amazing service.  

As good as the service is, the food is even better.  If you've read my reviews, you'll know that I consider myself somewhat a biscuit & gravy aficionado.  I've tried all the top rated ones in NOLA and travelled to Nashville, Charleston, Savannah, Charlotte and Atlanta to sample their offerings.  

I've found a lot of very good ones, but none better than Willa Jeans.  The biscuits are crispy on the bottom, but still light and flaky in the middle.  This kind of biscuit deserves the world's best sausage gravy, and (sorry Grandma) but that's what you'll find atop your biscuit here.  Plenty of sausage and perfectly seasoned.  If you're one to instantly reach for the salt & pepper shaker when you get your plate, resist the temptation.  You seriously don't need either with this dish.  Do yourself a favor and don't order the biscuits and gravy to go.  You want them served hot on a real plate with a knife & fork to cut through the crispy bottom of the biscuit for best results.  

Biscuits aren't all they do well.  The pasties, soups, amazing cornbread, coffee, the drinks and are some of the best in the city.

New Orleans is blessed with two extraordinary food markets; St Roch, and now Pythian.  Both offer great food and beverage options.  Both have a very cool, welcoming vibe.  

This was my first visit to Pythian.  I couldn't resist the wood-fired pizza just inside the front door, while my lunch date went with a light Mexican lunch from the Latin cantina.  We both thoroughly enjoyed the food, and washed it down with a very good, and refreshing margarita, from Bar 1908.  

Plenty of indoor and sidewalk seating.  We opted for an outdoor table on this gorgeous afternoon, with a great view of the local park and city hall.  

You can't go wrong at either of our awesome food markets, so take your pick... or try both!

Finally got back to my favorite wine venue after a nearly two year hiatus.  Yes, it's changed, and I miss going into the wine shop, but it's still one of the coolest places in town to enjoy wine,  cheese, world-class tapas and amazing live music in a funky, only-in-NOLA garden setting.  

Instead of entering through the wine shop and picking up your wine and selecting your cheese from the fridge, you now wait on the sidewalk for space to open up and enter into the garden directly.  (Our wait was just over 30 minutes on Saturday evening at 6:45pm). Pick up your wine glasses, water, plates and flatware on your way to your assigned table.  Then either step up to the window and order your wine, cheese & tapas (cocktails are upstairs) or order from your table via an easy to use QR code. 

The wine and food is all still amazing and affordable.  (Don't miss the bacon wrapped dates, ceviche, bread & butter).  The music is still incredible.  The chairs and tables still don't match.  They've added several tents for the occasional NOLA downpour.  The staff is still phenomenal. 

Bacchanal is still tops on my list of places to take out-of-town visitors, because a lot like NOLA... it just works in spite of its imperfections.

Finally got the chance to take the short walk over to Budsi's for dinner tonight.  Everything about this great little neighborhood Thai treasure met or exceeded my expectations.  The comfortable sidewalk seating, with classy fire heaters beckoned me from down the block.  The cool interior space felt so welcoming.  The menu tempted me to order way more than I needed.  Finally, over a delicious gin cocktail, called the south side, expertly crafted by Charlie, I decided on the dishes I couldn't resist.  The Tom kah soup was perfect.  The pork dumplings were awesome.  For entrees, we opted for the Thai fried rice, with chicken and shrimp (real gulf shrimp with heads & tails intact) and the chicken pad see ew.  Both were excellent.  Dare I say, some of the best Thai in town.

Can't wait to go back for the drunken noodles and the crispy pork.  I've got a feeling I'll be a regular!

I can't speak to the restaurant experience, but I can assure you that the delivery option is top-notch!  Not sure how I've missed this little gem for years.  Possibly because it's overshadowed by better known establishments like the Italian Barrel?  A neighbor raved about it and mentioned the delivery option.  After a long Monday, that's all the encouragement I needed.  Reviewed the menu on Yelpand decided on the Mardi Grad pasta and the paneed chicken.  Made the call.  45 minutes later I had a call from outside my gate.  A very friendly gentleman on a bike handed me a bag full of delicious food.  The entrees were both outstanding.  The salads were very good.  The cheese bread was a pleasant surprise.  I'll be back!  Maybe even dine in next time?

Ok, it's been three weeks since my original review, and I'm here to report that the only thing better than getting Mona Lisa delivered, is dining in.  Quaint little dining room with Mona Lisa pictures and paintings everywhere, and I do mean every where.  Old-school red & white checkered table clothes. Perfect service.  Now, for the food... I had to try the pizza and I'm glad I did!  The Mona Lisa special is fantastic! 

Bottom-line, amazing old school Italian, in a homey setting, with great service and prices that will leave your wallet as happy as your belly.

Just a quick follow up to day THANK YOU!  #thankyouthursday #nolayelplove

This place is HOT... and I don't just mean the sake and wasabi.  The vibe is hot.  The servers are hot.  The clientele is hot.  The hip hop is loud and pumping.  It's not for everyone, but they've clearly carved out a niche with the club crowd.  (Not my scene, so add a star to my review, if you're into clubbing.)

The service was solid, although I did feel like we were being pushed to the higher end items, and I get it, but if you don't receive the sashimi menu, with the more affordable rolls, ask for it.  Can't blame them for promoting the $20 rolls, but sometimes a $6.50 roll will do, and without the other menu you'd never know they had one.

We started with the hot sake, edamame and hamachi.  All very good.  For entrees, we went with the red dragon and upside down rolls along with an assortment of sashimi.  The best sushi/sashimi in town?  Not likely, but that's not what you're really here for, is it?

Finally had a chance to try Tujague's at their new location, during the summer Coolinary event.  First impression was the bar area is much larger, but still has a very homey feel, with the same distinctive historic NOLA vibe.  Same awesome bartender from the original location, too.  

The hostess greeted us promptly and seated us in the rear dining room, which here again, had a very similar feel to the original location, which was a pleasant surprise.  You'll recognize the mirrors, flooring and shadow boxes displaying over 100 years of little liquor/pharmacy bottles.  

The service was outstanding from start to finish.  The food was all delicious and perfectly prepared.  After a signature cocktail and glass of wine, we had the oysters Braden, creole tomato toast, airline chicken and swordfish entrees, followed by the blueberry white chocolate bread pudding and peanut butter & jelly cheesecake.  Outstanding!

Sure it's a little touristy, and a bit pricey, but on a hot sultry Saturday afternoon, it was the perfect place to grab a cold drink (or two) and a light lunch... in the AC.  We were warmly greeted and immediately seated in the bar (our preference).  Very nice, historic ambiance.  The bartender was friendly.  Our server was outstanding.  The drinks were good... & strong.  The crab artichoke dip was fantastic, with plenty of delicious baked parmesan rounds.  The "seafood platter" was okay, and large enough to split between three of us.

After checking in to our hotel in Nashville (we were visiting from Vegas), we knew we HAD to make Hot Hattie B's Chicken our very first spot. I was told by countless friends & family to make sure we made a trip here. After pulling up my collection on Yelp of all the places I wanted to hit up on my vacation, I was so happy to see that this location of Hattie B's was within walking distance of our hotel.

We took the leisurely 10 minute stroll and as soon as we turned the corner, we saw the line outside. Normally, long lines is something I avoid. I tell myself, I'll come back another day. But since we were visiting and only in town for a few days, I knew this was my chance. It was a Thursday, and if this was what it was like on a Thursday between lunch and dinner, I didn't want to know what it was like on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday haha.

We got in line and anxiously awaited. They have signage up that mentioned if you went inside and asked for a beer, they'd bring it out to you in line (as long as someone from your group showed that you are over the age of 21). I thought that was an awesome touch since I'm sure the lines are pretty long here often. In the hot humidity summer of Nashville, we waited in line nearly an hour. "This better be good..." I kept telling myself and my husband who is far more patient than I.

We got to the front, and put in our order. By that time, we had some time to look it over. The inside is on the smaller side, but they do have a little patio outside, too with fans blasting. My husband and I both ordered the Mild Chicken Sandwich, with came with a side. There are a few different options of "heat" for the chicken, and we went with the lowest one haha. I mean, it's hot chicken IN Nashville... I knew we couldn't handle heat, so I was thinking mild would probably be just the kick we both wanted.

The sandwich came with a side, so I got mac n cheese and my husband got fries. It didn't take too long before our food came out and we even got a table inside. It was a little stuffy in there, but better than sitting outside. 

Oh. My. God. Remember how I asked myself if it was worth it?! Well.... pardon my french. But shit yeah, it was worth it. This chicken sandwich was the chicken sandwich of my dreams. The mild spice was exactly what I needed. The chicken was tender and delicious. The sauce.... wow that sauce. My mouth is literally watering just thinking about it. This is the chicken sandwich to end all chicken sandwiches.

We loved it so much, we ended up going to another location before we left (the one on Broadway). That review will be posted another day. For now, damn. Thank you Hattie B's for the delightful meal and the incredibly southern hospitality. This is one meal we had there that I know I'll be talking about for a while. Plus, I realized that you have a location in Vegas at The Cosmopolitan... might need to make a trip there in the near future.

When I told people I knew that my husband and I were going to Nashville, this was one spot people told me I couldn't miss. And the people are right.

This museum is amazing and goes over so much Johnny Cash history. It's located right off Broadway so a really easy spot for tourists, like me, who are visiting and want to get some history. It starts from his early childhood and goes through his entire life. There are artifacts everywhere, from clothes he wore on stage, to letters he wrote to friends (even before he was famous). I was completely taken aback at by how incredible this was. 

The tour is self guided and you can just walk through and enjoy everything. There's lots to read and enjoy and they even have some videos and music you can listen to. I also appreciated that there were bathrooms inside the actual museum because they let us know once we were in there and left, we wouldn't be able to come back in. We took about two hours to soak up as much as we could. They allow you to take photos but no videos.

The last part of the museum is where they play his music video "Hurt" and even showcase the chair he sat in, as well as the ring he wore. I felt so completely moved by it.

Definitely would recommend this as a must-see and must-experience in Nashville. And since we visited a week ago, I can't get the song "walk the line" out of my head, but not complaining.

I was in Indy visiting for a friend's wedding and had countless locals tell me this was a spot I needed to check out. We actually ended up coming in here on Friday and Saturday night.

Friday night, we walked in and sat in the bar area. This bar is a great sports bar with a really nice patio area. Our server was outstanding and let us know that it was late night menu. They have a few selections, so we ordered some pretzel bites, fries, and sweet potato fries, along with drinks.

The second night we were seated in another part of the bar, but still were taken great care of. We ordered some other food, too, since we were there earlier than late night. It was pretty busy, but we were taken good care of. My friend got a quinoa quesadilla which was really good, just a little too spicy for me haha. But those fries and pretzel bites were delish so we got them all again. 

Can I just say I love the prices in Indy?! Our bill both nights were so cheap, especially as a group of friends that come from expensive cities. I can totally see why our friend that lives her told us to try this spot out.

Not sure the next time i'll be in Indy, but I would definitely recommend.

Okay. I am obsessed with this bar. I was in town visiting for a friend from college's wedding and with my other group of girlfriends, we decided to look for some local bars to hit up. This was one of them.

First of all, the ambiance in here is beautiful. Definitely a cocktail bar through and through. It's dimly lit, with a little patio area, too, but mostly lounge furniture throughout. When it gets darker outside, they light some candles at your table, too. We got there pretty early in the evening on Friday and decided to grab some drinks before heading out to dinner. We ended up ordering a lot of food though. They have some good shareable items like cheese & meat platters and dips and whatnot. Everything we ate was so tasty.

The names of the drinks are so great. They have entire menu selection dedicated to Stepbrothers and names of drinks associated with the movie. I wish I could recall the drink I got, but it was a mezcal drink because I loooove mezcal. It said it had some chile in it, so I asked our server if it was spicy. He was super honest and said not too spicy, just a little kick. He was absolutely right. It was definitely the right amount of spice. I ended up ordering two, which I hardly do with craft cocktails.

Definitely would recommend this spot if you're looking to grab a drink with a friend or a date. Such a cool spot.

Ok, I thought for awhile about if I should write a review or not.  I am not a member, but I went in about 3 weeks ago to find out about joining.  I am going to be moving to the area permanently.  I currently use 24 hour fitness, but I'm looking at other clubs that offer more spin classes.  My husband and I walked into the club, and asked if we could speak to someone about membership.  We looked to the left of the desk, and saw that the lady in that office was with a client.  The guy at the desk said it would be a minute.  We said fine, and then he asked us to fill out forms - give our names, address, phone and email, etc.  We wondered why we needed to do that, given we just wanted to ask a couple of questions.  He said we had to.  Hmmm.  While this exchange was happening, another gal came toward us from the other side of the counter.  She said if we were not members, we could go no further into the club.  I told her that was fine, that we were just waiting for the membership lady to ask a couple of questions.  She again restated that I could not walk any further forward, and I told her not to worry, that I was not going to.  I was starting to feel a little weird about their attitudes.  The guy behind the desk then told my husband he would need to see our IDs.  Really?  What the heck for?  We weren't joining, we wern't buying anything, drinking any alcohol, why did they suddenly need to see our IDs?  The gal looks at me and says, "You have to sign the forms for liability reasons."  I said, "What liability?"  She said, "you may slip and fall, and try to sue us."  I told her, "We're just standing here in the lobby.  I don't see any water on the floor, so I don't think we'll slip."  Then she says, "Well, you might get hit with a flying dumbell."  Um, are you kidding me?!?!?  Do people in this club worry about being hit with flying dumbells?  Why would dumbells be flying around?  I think I may have even asked her as much, and she said something like, "You never know."  
So, I guess the gist of this is that you can't go in and find out how much membership is without giving up your personal details.  I later spoke with the membership lady over the phone, and she apologized for the treatment by the front desk staff.  She said they have enacted these policies because they don't want a "fataal attraction" scenario to happen.  I have no idea what that means, but I am practically afraid to walk in that place now.  I think I will stick with 24 hour fitness.  It's much cheaper, and they don't strip search you at the door if you're interested in joining.  I felt less invaded by airport security.  This is really a note to the owner.  You should seriously consider changing your aggressive policy of obtaining information from people who are not even your clients.  And you are embarrassing yourself when you allow your staff to give multiple, crazy reasons as to why you need this info.  Come on, we all know that you are using that info for future marketing schemes.

Last weekend I met a buddy in Moorestown to hang out.  It's a nice town to spend the afternoon.  He didn't want to go to a formal restaurant, so we stumbled onto this place.  

I actually really, really liked the concept.  Passariello's is a marketplace-style fast casual Italian restaurant.  You have the option for all kinds of pizza, more formal Italian dinners, and also for soup and salads.  I really like how it's great if you just go by yourself for a quick bite, or if you go with a larger group who all have different tastes.

The guy who served me the Eggplant Rollatini really seemed to have his act together.  I had my choice of entrees and sides, too.

The only reason for four stars instead of five is because the prices are a little high, but I understand that Moorestown is upscale.

Don't let the recent rebuild and updated decor fool you.  You may not even think it is so bad if you just go here once.  But every time I stop here, I get more and more sick of it.  I need to remind myself to not stop here ever again.

1.  The CROWD that hangs out here is VERY UNSAVORY.  There is no visible security anywhere.  I wouldn't want to bring my wife or kids here.  The other reviewer who said that he got approached by someone wanting to buy drugs is most likely not kidding.  There are crowds of people just hanging out there because it is a public place, and no one tells them to go home.
2.  The "eco" BATHROOMS ARE JUST DIRTY.  I am sorry, but I think a urinal should flush.  It is disgusting what does not get flushed.  There is pubic hair inside them.  They do not get cleaned enough either.  They smell like a farm.  The older location here before had more effective bathrooms, even if they weren't "green."  Why even stop at a rest stop if the bathrooms are dirty???
3.  The food options are limited to FAST FOOD ONLY.  There are no healthy dining options.  These days people would appreciate an independently owned Mediterranean restaurant, for instance.  Nope, they don't have it there.

Next time I am passing through on I-95, I need to remind myself to avoid stopping here even though the location is central.

Beachcorner came recommended by several people I had met at Second Line Brewing.  It is located within walking distance from the brewery.  They told me that their burger was really outstanding, and that I needed to go.  Turns out they were right.  I would have never stopped in there because it doesn't look like much from the outside.  I recommend going there for food after the brewery because breweries usually don't have food.  They are open later, too.

They have a dive bar atmosphere, but it is in the sense that Jon Taffer says makes everyone feel welcome, and you can come as you are.  They have lots of games in the bar, too, so you can stay a while.

The bartender was extremely efficient and very helpful giving me advice of other things to do in New Orleans.

They are located in a non-touristy part of New Orleans, which I really liked.  There are cool cemeteries around that area, too, if you are visiting from out of town.

While waiting for my walking tour of the French Quarter to begin, I had an hour or two to kill.  Normally I do not like paying high prices in the middle of any tourism district, but I thought that I could squeeze by with one cup of coffee.  This coffee bar got excellent reviews on Yelp, so I gave it a try.

Turns out that their coffee really is delicious.  I like how they were able to make me an individual pour from sourced beans.  The staff were really friendly and welcoming, too.  

However, no wifi -- which I was aware of --, and it is pricey.  But that is to be expected in a tourism district.  Definitely recommend for coffee addicts who are exploring the French Quarter and can't wait to leave the neighborhood for less expensive coffee elsewhere.

While I was in Philly, I swung by the Reading Terminal Market for a quick bite.  Turns out that I got there just as the whole market was closing, which was only at 6 pm.  I found Hershel's East Side Deli, and I gave it a try.  They were very nice to still be serving even though the whole market was about to close.

Really quickly I just ordered the corned beef on rye with Russian dressing.  I just found the meat to be so incredibly tender and flavorful.  It really melted in my mouth, and I can still taste it now.  The rye bread wasn't anything special, but it didn't matter as a whole.  I would definitely go there again.

Tired Hands is a fairly large brewing facility, with everything under one roof.  Unlike many breweries in my home state of NJ, they do in fact have food, and it's good, too.  They have lots of seating, with waitress service.  The focus is still on the beer.  They have a counter with cans for sale, too.

The location is in Downtown Ardmore, which I had never visited before.  It's actually a really nice spot with a younger crowd.  The only problem is that there isn't enough parking.  I was able to park about a half mile away and walk in, but I can imagine that might be difficult for others.

There are no flights available.  While that may annoy some people, it didn't really bother me because I just got three 8 oz pours.  The service was efficient with that, too.  However, I do have to say that the beer is slightly overrated.  The Hefeweizen I tried tasted nothing like a German Hefeweizen in Germany because it was light, not nearly as wheaty as a German Hefeweizen, and it had a stronger citrus flavor built into it.  I would call it a "Light Summer Citrus Ale."  I still enjoyed it, however, once I got used to it and got over the fact that the name was wrong.  Their hazy IPA had no substance to it; it was just bitter on the edges with no middle.  I finished by trying their Strawberry Milkshake IPA, which has lactose and a natural, mild strawberry flavor, and that was definitely the finest beer of the three by far.  The way that the lactose balanced with the genuine strawberry flavor was delicious.  So, I didn't leave totally disappointed.  My recommendation is to be a little more discriminatory when choosing their beers because some are delicious, and others are not as advertised.

The food looked pretty good actually, although I didn't order any.  The crowd was standoffish.  The bartender also wasn't the chattiest person.  Nobody asked me whether I enjoyed the experience, and the people at the hostess stand didn't acknowledge me either. Overall, the place felt like a factory to me, but I imagine it's fine as long as you come with a big group.

Bacchanal is a wine & cheese shop with a fairly large added "Heurige," which is an Austrian word for outdoor wine garden.  They also have a bar area with specialty cocktails upstairs.  

They have a neat concept.  You pick out the sliced meat and cheese you want from the fridge.  Then they will nicely plate it for you.  Then you pick up a glass of wine and sit down outside to listen to live music.  A jazz quartet played while I was there.  

Bacchanal is located in the Bywater section of New Orleans, which is up and coming and also far from the touristy French Quarter.  

Definitely recommend.

I almost hesitated to write a review about the Reading Terminal Market because there are just so many written already, and what else can be said.  But when I have told people in my area of New Jersey about it, most don't know how good it is.  So, I feel it is my duty, in a way, to get the word out.

The selection of food items is really one of the very best of any market in our country.  They have so many things that you just can't get outside of PA, such as Amish cheeses made from unpasteurized dairy.

The two negatives are that there really isn't a convenient parking lot because it is located right in the middle of Center City.  That makes it harder to buy a lot of products because you can't just wheel your cart out to your car.  The crowds can also be intimidating.

Still, this market deserves 5 stars because the selection and the overall experience are rare and hard to find anywhere else.

At first I was a bit skeptical to try this place after seeing 5 star reviews from yelpers with 1-2 reviews, but am glad I gave it a shot.

The concept seems to be slightly more upscale decor and quality Indian food. They have a buffet in the afternoon and a la carte dinners. 

Naan is served tableside and is made fresh and served piping hot, so remember to order your second helping, should you so desire, about 10 min before you need it.

The tandoori chicken was moist and delicious and if memory serves correctly, consisted of mainly chicken drumsticks and thighs, which is consistent to what one might see in India.

The Chicken Makhani was rich and slightly sweet from the cream as it should be (and perhaps a helping teaspoon of sugar). 

The Mutton curry was delicious but every piece of the mutton had bones, which may not suit every Americanized palate. 

Chicken Manchurian (Indo Chinese) was authentically spiced, thus a little too hot for the typical Americanized palate. This is a good dish to order a la carte as even the best version gets a bit soggy when served buffet style.

The mango lassi served with the buffet is made with Alphonso mango (know as the king of mangoes) pulp, which is a nice authentic touch. Alphonso mangoes are not cheap, especially the fresh mangoes (I paid $110 for a dozen a few months ago).

Based on what was presented in the buffet today, the rice and desserts could use some work and the Saag Paneer (spinach with fresh cheese) was lacking salt or any detectable seasoning.

Service was very gracious and friendly but a bit disorganized since there does not seem to be a waiter assigned to each section, thus, you get "over served" - drink order inquires by 2 servers, same with extra naan and water queries, etc.

Decor is upscale compared to the other Indian restaurants in the area, though they need to do address the uneven laminate flooring. The space was larger than I had envisioned.

I think one of the owners is the guy who owns Spice Kitchen in East Norriton but can't say that for sure. There were also quite a few Indian families during this Saturday visit and many seemed to know the owner.

I will be back to try the Chicken Kati roll, Koliwada fish, Tandoori shrimp and Chicken Chettinad.

Once they work out a few of the kinks, Shagun (which means Omen) might be a good one for other ethnic restaurants to follow in the area.

This place needs new management. Plain and simple. 

The service is poor and gross.  I've been their two times and had to wait over 10 minutes for someone to acknowledge me once I was at a table.  This seems to be the trend I am seeing on yelp.  The last time an individual who was working behind the counter was juicing something (I believe carrots) and came around the counter to seat us.  His hands were covered (no exaggeration) in orange gooey pulp, he grabbed our white paper menus to seat us and sat us at a dirty table (smeared with jelly and crumbs) and placed our menus down, which were smeared with the orange material that was covering his hands.  Every part of the menu his fingers touched was orange.  Super, old sticky table, freshly sticky menus.

Then I had to wait 10 minutes until someone asked me for my drink.

Generally, I am very fair when it comes to the service industry, I've been a caterer, dish washer, hostess, and a waitress.  This place is not fine dining, however the service behavior I have experienced at this restaurant it pretty close to inexcusable.

The perks are the food is pretty good.  I tend to stick to their sandwiches and have been very pleased with them all.  However, it is a little over priced.  The inside/outside of the restaurant is nice and appealing.  I enjoy the over all style.  I really think this place just needs a manager and an overhaul on their customer service.

Listen to me. Go here. Drop everything you're doing and go here. Now. 
Have a seat in the courtyard or the inside dining room or the bar room. Sit anywhere. The atmosphere & decor are superb in all areas. 
Order an Indiana brewery beer on tap or wine by the glass/bottle or a fancy cocktail. The beverage list is excellent.
Pick anything from the small, medium or large plate menu or the snacks, charcuterie or cheese menu. Everything is wonderful and will far exceed your expectations. But, make sure to order several items and share with your party. You'll want to try everything and I highly recommend doing just that. 
Bask in the atmosphere. Relish your delicious food & beverages.  Enjoy the impeccable service. You will not find any finer dining spot in Indy. 
This is it folks. This is the place we've all been waiting for.
Go. Soon. Go now.
Bad coffee that's overpriced.  I really hate the vibe in this place.  Never again!

$40 Pizza.

My friend asked the workers, "how do you sleep at night?"  They laughed.

The pizza was actually pretty decent, which is the only reason I'm giving them 2 stars.  However, we were asked to leave when they saw me taking a picture with my phone.  Really?

It PAINS me to downgrade Brasserie so. 

Here's the thing, my friends, I've been driven to an end
And the problem with this place is the inevitable wait. 
A wait is fine if the given wait time
is accurate and true and you've nothing else to do.
But when I'm told 30 minutes and my wait far surpasses
Those 30+ minutes and in the meantime the masses
of others who're waiting for a table to be freed
have all been instructed that they will soon indeed
be given a table, but the hostess is unable
to give us an accurate timeframe to sit?
Then I'm sorry but that practice is absolute sh*t. 

And the food is delicious so we keep coming back
Which is why I am pained to go on the attack
And this has happened not one time, or two, but three
So i'm not being an unreasonable snide little "B"
But I tell you, my friends, that it's a simple fix
Doesn't require magic or time-bending tricks
Just give me a time that is accurate, you see
I'd rather wait an hour than have it feel like three
Because when I'm told that "any minute" I'll have a seat
And every fifteen minutes you give the same speech
Well the time it passes like a slow step in the grave
And forces me to finally give in and cave
and eat at the bar which I've had to do twice
and I'm sorry but the experience just isn't as nice.

I know I can fix this and reserve my own slot
But this isn't the same issue, really it's not
Sometimes we show up to dine on a whim
but we won't again if we can never get in. 
I can wait quite a while for table or booth
Just give me a wait time that's close to the truth!!

(Cause sometimes we're trying to catch a movie, too. That's all.)

Delis, in general, are shitty places to work. They're like busy non-chain cafes. Lines are long, you're always understaffed, and people order things like they would at the chain version of your place ("yes i'll take the mr smokey turkey dripper please") so you're left to try to figure it out based on the name ("mmmk...turkey...mayo...bbq sauce? Mustard? Umm..peppers. Microwaved? Grilled? Dunked in pickle juice? Fml....")

Point is, the job is difficult enough as it is, and nothing twists my neck like an observably snappy, rude, inconsiderate employer. 

And that's what I saw here. 

Don't know her name. Don't want to make a point of potentially an 'off-day', but damn, lady, when it comes to delis, your employees are half the experience. Love them. This woman, who I assume was the owner/manager, was snarky and rude to the woman who was manning her register. That's a three snap and a hell-nah from me. 

The sandwich was good. But the experience was marred. I'll probably be back but I hope the person in question has changed her attitude. 

Go sit in the corner and think about your behavior. Cause the sandwich isn't chasing off patrons, you are.

"I'll take the 'Luke's not-so-warm Mediocrepalooza with Meh-sauce', please". 

I'm literally (using the word in it's correct form) grimacing as I write this. Because it literally (maybe not using it correctly anymore) hurts me so deeply to do it. 

I grew up in Truckee/Tahoe. 
I was an Origi-Squeeze! 
I've even delayed writing this for about 2 years in the hope that things would turn around. 
*Cue prolonged exhale that slowly dissipates into a grumble.*

So, here's the deal, I GET that breakfast places need to capitalize on volume and up-charges in order to make a profit. I understand that breakfast is the hardest meal of the day to run a business on. But if my table of 4 is going to spend $66 on breakfast, no alcohol, then I at least expect it to taste like $66 worth of eggs and potatoes. 

I ordered an omelet. Because....duh. 
The cheese to make the omelet something more than just a mass of veggies was an extra dollar. The option for a gluten free side was tortilla chips, which sounded nasty at 9am, so I ordered a $3.50 fruit cup. Add a cup of coffee and all of a sudden, my breakfast meal costs as much as my weekly lunch budget. That's FINE. I expect to pay a bit more at Squeeze. But my omelet was cold. It was runny. It was pretty...bland. Shocking, given the Super Ridonculous Namey-name it had. (And actually I like those namey-name's). 

The eggs on my friend's benedict were a half-minute away from having been served hard-boiled. And I mean...a benedict with hard yolks? What the WHAT?

My brother ordered some sort of twice baked scramble thing...which turned out to be mostly potatoes. It was like a plateful of indiscernible potato-ness. A mess of potatoes served with a side of "Spudz". Which, again, is FINE, but they were overcooked and came way later than the rest of the food. 

All in all...after having been here more than a handful of times over the past couple of years and not once leaving feeling like "yeah, that meal was delicious" or "yeah, that was worth it!" I'm forced to now leave this scribble of drivel on the wall of the Squeeze's Yelp page. Which I hate doing. But I want it to go back to the way it was....back when they were quaint and delicious. 

But perhaps that's what happens when you grow to five or six locations. Things get harder to keep consistent. You have less control of a larger staff. You have to adjust and change the menu and focus on different things. And things start to become a little more....Mediocrepalooza. Ah well... I'll give it a few years and then give it another shot. Because nostalgia always wins, in my book.

You know that guy who shows up to a party and he's all decked out in the latest, most up to date garb, totally looks the part of whomever is the most currently popular hipster icon, and everyone kinda follows him with their eyes like "who's this new guy and what's his story?"   

Yeah. That guy. 

And so you keep watching him and you're intrigued so you eventually walk up to him and you're all "hey man, so, what's your deal?" 

And what you get in response is basically "I don't actually know. I was popped-collar guy like 5 years ago. Before that I was A&F t-shirt guy. Before that I was spiked hair and puka shell guy. So I mean, I guess I'm a guy who kinda follows what everyone else is doing. I just look really good doing it." 

And that, ladies and gentlemen, is The Brewer's Cabinet. 

It LOOKS amazing. Raw wormy pine wall chinking, barn wood in both raw and stained textures, and some of the coolest custom booths I've ever seen. Their pulley Edison light fixtures are THE coolest. End of discussion. 

But when it comes down to the meat of the issue, Brewer's Cabinet comes up undercooked. Kinda like my boyfriend's Devil burger.  

They were out of a significant number of their beers on tap. My veggie burger was decent but dry. And the couple we were with were left underwhelmed by their meals as well. Dry, average, boring. Which is fine if what you're expecting is boring.  But, I mean, by all outward appearances, you'd think this place would be bold and on their shtuff. 

Ah well. We've all been duped by the wannabe in a good outfit. Even if there isn't much substance underneath the well dressed mirage, at least the ambiance doesn't suck.

Racist...won't be back

Went there w/ a friend.  She ordered a burger medium well and when it came back well done, she asked for another.  The server took it back w/ a slight attitude and the cook actually came out.  Would have been a good move, except that he felt she should keep the burger b/c "black ppl usually order their meats well done."  Ha!  The audacity.  We left and will continue to spread the word.

Let me start out by saying that I LOVED this place and I am honestly very sad to give them a poor review, but there is good reason for this which I will get to in just a moment. Their food selection is very diverse (same with the beer list!) and has never been anything short of excellent, the atmosphere is very cool and low key and the service has always been on point at both the restaurant, the bar and the pick-up room. We would frequent this place on a regular basis, until our latest experience this past Friday. 

My fiance' and I were here on Friday, 8/7/15, and we had a server by the name of Jack. Jack was a strange guy- he seemed way too comfortable with us right from the get-go calling me baby and stealing french fires off of our plates when he would come to check on us. It was a little uncomfortable, but we just chalked it up to him being overly confident/friendly/comfortable as my fiance and I are pretty friendly, down-to-Earth people and easy to have fun with. All was well and good until the end of the night when we had asked for a to-go bag. Jack brought them over to us and wrapped up my food and then my fiance's. He asked what my fiance's name was and I told him. Thinking he was writing his name on the bag, he set the bag down in front of us and walked away. He wrote "DICKHEAD Thanks for eating at Rons!!" on my fiance's to-go bag. WTF?!? SERIOUSLY??? Joking or not, that is NOT cool. The picture of the bag is posted here as well.

Needless to say, we were both fuming. We found the floor manager, Steve, and told him about it right away and showed him the bag. Steve looked at me in disbelief and I told him this way over the line and uncalled for. I explained that we are all about having fun with people, but this was completely inappropriate and that Jack did not know us at all to be joking around with us in that sort of a way. Steve said he understood and I asked him what was going to be done about it and he replied that this will cost Jack his job and then we were ushered out the door. No profuse apology or offer to comp our meal or speak to the owner, etc. 

Your employee just blatantly insulted a regular-visiting, paying customer by calling him a dickhead on paper and all we received was a non-concerned apology and were showed the door. Not satisfied with the way this handled, I called back and spoke with a female manager. She did apologize to us more than once which we appreciated and told us that this was unacceptable but we didn't need to hear the obvious stated again- the option to allow us to speak with the owner, comp our meal, or follow-up as to how this would be handled would have been the right way to handle this. Very disappointing and we won't be back.

We decided to take the PCH on our way home from Ventura, when a craving for crazy tacos came to my belly!  We pulled off the highway and found our way to this very tiny taco shop at the batting cages! You could blink and miss it, but thanks to Google Maps you'll find it fast. 

The menu was mostly tacos all with fun names and flavors for everyone. The Earl and I ordered  The Triple play (your choice of any three tacos) and The Beachball. With a less than two minute wait your name is called. I was hangry, so when they called my name I was pleasantly surprised!!!

Batter Up: had fried fish with a spicy sauce, cabbage, pico, radish
It was good the first few bites until the batter became soggy. Probably my fault because I couldn't get my off that Beachball!
Bahn Mi: were classic bahn mi...

Anyhow, the tacos were crazy and who doesn't love a twist to taco!  

The place deserves a home run, if you ask me...Get the Beachball.

Hearing all the buzz about this new place, my wife and I decided to pay a visit last Saturday, and boy, it's so worth our trip.
We walked in around 5:30 pm, 1/2 hour after they had opened for dinner.  The place was 2/3 full, so we were greeted right away with a very friendly waiter.  He told me that almost all servers are in the family, so they do care to make sure their customers happy to keep the business moving.  They sure did, the service was excellent during our dinner!  The place is very clean, and they are proud to cook in open space so you can watch if you choose to sit by the bar.  The decoration and lighting are unique, noise level is average.  My wife loves the embroidered pictures of the Vietnamese models wearing  "ao dai" on the wall.  Another thing I should mention is your clothes don't smell when walking out of the place, a 5 stars for their ventilation system. 
Now, let's talk about food.  My wife ordered the grilled chicken vermicelli (bun) with extra egg roll, and I had pho filet mignon.  We also ordered a grilled pork sliders per our friend's recommendation.

Vermicelli: My wife loves it!  The vermicelli is boiled just right, the chicken and veggie are so fresh.  The fish sauce is mixed well, not too salty, not too plain.  I like their bowl, it looks...cute :)  I took a picture so you guys can see.

Egg roll: Very crispy, fresh, and perfectly cooked.  This is a must have if you eat here.

Sliders: My friend is right!  This food is new to us.  The closest I had before was Peking duck with steamed bun.  This is steamed bun with grilled pork and vegetable sandwiched inside. It tasted so good!

Pho filet mignon: When it comes to pho, I'm very picky.  I intentionally ordered pho to judge their cooking.  The pho is excellent!  I can tell it was cooked with all fresh ingredients, no msg, no commercial power in order to raise profit.  If you want to taste a true Vietnamese home made pho, this is the place.  The filet mignon was very tender and just melt in your mouth.  I couldn't tell myself but wondering how they make their money when making their pho at this quality.

Obviously, I would recommend this place to anybody who wants to try Vietnamese dishes.  I haven't given any 5 stars to any establishment, but I must make an exception here.  We will come back  for sure to try other dishes.  I hope this restaurant's food/service will be be kept intact for good.

I feel the need to write this review. We have 4 sons that have been married in the last 6 years. I have ordered many many cakes between showers, birthdays and now baby showers, christening and first birthdays too!  We started out with them loving everything we ordered. Suzanne has always taken time to design my ideas for the event. One time they messed up the filling for my grand daughters first bday cake, I let it slide even though it was a very big, very expensive cake. Then I ordered 60 cupcakes which I may add was a hefty bill, and I get there to pick them up and they are all wrong !! Kathy the owner who knew me from coming in never gave  me eye contact or try to rectify it, so the very next day I was back picking up a large cake for my other grand daughters christening and expected a monetary discount and yup you guessed it - nothing !! I have never had a problem with freshness but they are getting to big for their britches. They should remember without their faithful customers they have nothing !

When it comes to hotels, I always prefer staying at Hilton or their Hilton suites hotels. This location has both their establishments right next door to each other. So be mindful when checking in that your going to the right hotel. Upon entering Hilton, you notice a beautiful open lobby with many comfortable chairs. There is also a restauran/bar (Delmonico's steak house) towards the back of the lobby. Check in was very easy and the hostess named Jackie was very friendly. She gave us suggestions to places we need to see while visiting. But my question for Jackie was this, Philly's claim to fame is their cheesesteaks. So being a foodie I had to know where can I get their best from. She told me two places, Dalessandro's Steaks and Chubby's. Chubby's being the better choice. So hopefully I get a chance to check them out. The room was very clean and neat, for some reason we got a wheelchair accessible room. I don't mind it one bit, the bathroom is spacious as well as the main room. The shower is just a bit different. Some may knit pick about some minor cosmetic flaws, such as wallpaper peeling and paint chips. But it's not so bad that you think your in a motel waiting to shoot up heroin. I feel they are doing a very good job in keeping up with the place. I have no problem rebooking this location again.

TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE!

First, they decided to seat us in the take out area...the food court has nicer tables and chairs!

As we waited for our food, we were grossed out by the cooks. We later learned that they don't need to wear gloves since they have hand sanitizer. However, not once did we see it being used while one cook worked between raw meat, touching his face, and touching prepared foods.  The best though was watching a cook lick his thumb and then clean the rim of a soup bowl. Are you kidding me!

As much as we wanted to leave, I justified staying since we were getting calamari and burgers.  The calamari was good but my partners medium well burger was served raw! My dining partner called it quits.

The couple next to us also received a raw burger. The gentleman asked for it to be prepared correctly.  They returned with a new bun but the same burger! As I learned later, taking a bite out of a burger and then tossing it back on the grill to cook longer is A-OK. Little did I know!

The WORST moment was yet to come. The patron next to us asked to see the manager. The waiter sent over the GM (looks like the guy Fringe & Dawson's Creek) and the Chef who immediately became defensive and very unprofessional instead of saying they'll bring the matter to the attention of the guy making the burgers (my guess, since he burned my bison burger, he thought beef cooked just as quickly which isn't true).

To cap off the evening, after the GM left, the patron quipped to his wife, "The guy's full of sh**."  The GM turned to the patron and told him, "If you think I'm full of sh**, then get out of my restaurant!" WOW, talk about a Gordon Ramsey wanna-be! I'm still flabbergasted by the complete lack of professionalism. I mean, what an ass! All he needed to do was walk away, Exton isn't the place for hoodlums and gang bangers!

Note, the patron made this comment to his wife and not the GM who already had his back to the table and was standing several feet away. I would feel differently if he said it to his face but the GM response was entirely unacceptable. Absolutely ridiculous.

Me? I won't be back, ever!

Really like this place
 Have gone back a few times. I like the black tea with boba. My sister loves the mangoe sweet rice. The staff is rigidly and they have little feet on the floor for social distancing. Everyone who enters and works has a mask. They have outdoor seating and they also sell masks if you feel the need to purchase one for adults and children. They also sell  bao's if you want a snack. The i.side is super xute with swing seats for customers to enjoy. They also have hand sanitizer ready for your use. Should check them out. They are impressive and is upping the game for boba. They are always busy, but the wait is not gruesome like other places.

I love this place. I got the chicken basket and added some hot sauce to the perfectly crunchy wing and it tripled the amazement. You get to choose a side. I got the macaroni and cheese and it was superb.  Wish it was a little spicier. Eh, that's me with a lot of things. They're give enough food and the service is great. The staff is friendly and you feel the family owned company really cares. The place is well designed. You can tell they really wanted people to feel at home in a cozy place. Next time I go, I want to try the jambalaya.

When it comes to the food, if you've been to one P.F Chang's, you've been to them all.  As to the restaurants themselves, it seems that no two look exactly alike on the inside.  Some have good spacing between the tables, while others cram in as many tables as possible.  This particular P.F. Chang's is the latter.  So, with crowded conditions and poor acoustics (all P.F. Chang's seem to have this acoustics issue), it doesn't make for a great dining experience.

So, when going to P.F. Chang's go with reasonable expectations and you won't be disappointed.   For a chain restaurant that serves Americanized Asian food, the food is A-OK.   We all liked what we ordered.  However, our daughter asked for extra spice in her dish.  Instead, of her dish getting the extra spice, my husband ended up getting it in his dish!  On top of that, the kitchen was on the slow side.

Service here was good---prompt, friendly and efficient.  They have call-ahead seating which was big help as we were there on a busy Saturday night.

We decided to eat lunch here on a Sunday.  On Sundays, Harry's is the only place that's open in the Riverfront Market.  Before going inside, we looked at the menu that was posted outside the door.  It was a lunch menu and the prices seemed reasonable---so, in we went.

We were  seated and given menus.  It was then that we realized the menu posted outside was a lie.  It seems that there is no lunch menu on Sundays---dinner is served all day long, and dinner is more pricey.  Despite the deception, we decided to stay and eat.

Looking around, most of the customers were senior citizens.  By senior citizens, I mean in my Dad's age group---80 or older.   A little while later, a family came in, sat down, looked at the menu then left.  I'm sure, that like us, they were expecting to eat off the non-existent Sunday lunch menu.

Our server was prompt and friendly.  I decided to have a soda to drink while my husband had a Yuengling.

For my main course, I chose tempura soft shell crab which comes with:  "herb and salt roasted Yukon potatoes, Brussels sprouts, firecracker slaw, pickled ginger aioli".  The crab was fresh and  was perfectly prepared.  The firecracker slaw was over spiced which ended up masking the other flavors.  The potatoes were properly cooked but the pickled ginger aioli, which was also drizzled on the crab, was very bland.  The Brussels sprouts were forgettable.

My husband had pan seared Cape May scallops which comes with: "roasted poblano tamale, blistered heirloom tomatoes, corn, ruby red grapefruit, queso fresco, prickly pear vinaigrette".  He said that the scallops were perfectly prepared but none of the sides impressed him.  I  tasted some of the tamale and tasted no poblano pepper at all.

Where we sat, we had a view of the kitchen.  They were clearly doing their jobs but, considering that the place wasn't very busy at all, they were still slow in getting food to the tables.

I don't know if we would eat here again next time we're in town.  If we did, I would look to actually try their lunch menu as the prices are much cheaper.  For what we spent for the dinner menu, we really didn't think it was worth it.

So...Wow!...I was shocked to see just how wildly popular this place is!  We came here on a Saturday at 5 p.m. to celebrate my husband's birthday.  Our daughter made a reservation and let them know about the birthday.  When she called, they told her that the main dining room was booked up but that they could put us in the bar.  Two years ago, we went to the Capital Grille in Tysons Corner at 5 p.m. on a Saturday.  When we arrived, there were only a small number of others who also had reservations.  I figured, being that it is Tysons and there are other upscale steakhouses competing for business, that was the reason it wasn't busy.  Still, here we were in KoP where there are other upscale steakhouses in the same vicinity but the place was solidly booked at 5 p.m.  What's up with that?  I ask rhetorically.

When we arrived, the area by the host stand was understandably, crowded with those waiting to be seated.  We were told that they were setting up our table and apologized for the wait.  Soon, we were lead to our table.  We found out that the tables in the bar are generally for those who don't have reservations.

Our tablecloth had some glittery items on it.  After we were all seated, my husband was given a birthday card that was signed by the staff.  As it turned out, sitting in the bar was just fine as those who were there for drinks were well behaved :).  Plus, it wasn't very noisy.

Our server was prompt, friendly and efficient.  We started out with  drinks.  The kids all had water.  I got a mixed drink that had a large basil leaf in the glass---and I forget its name.  Overall, it was a good drink as I could taste both the sweet and savory aspects of it which blended well together.  My husband and son-in-law both had Bloody Marys which they both liked.  Our daughter got a mixed drink that she enjoyed.

One thing that I ding Capital Grille for --- they have "specials" which never seem to change.  Why not just put them on the menu already?  My husband thinks that by not putting them on the menu, it is their attempt to make you spend more.  For example, the filet mignon on the menu is a 10 oz. one.  Yet, the specials that are always on offer have a 4 oz. one (which is geared to kids), a 6 oz. and an 8 oz.  Also, lobster bisque is always just a special.

So, most of us got an 8 oz. filet, while my husband opted for the 10 oz. one.  Our daughter and I each got a cup of lobster bisque, while my husband had a shrimp cocktail.  The kids menu isn't printed up, the server has to tell you what is available.  In the end, the kids all got chicken fingers with fries.

For side dishes, my husband and I shared grilled asparagus plus lobster mac and cheese.  Our daughter and son-in-law shared truffle fries with parmigiana cheese plus creamed spinach.

As for the food --- I like the lobster bisque here.  With a cup, you get a whole lobster claw.  Plus, when it comes to the table, you are asked if you want any sherry added.  That is a nice touch because often places that make lobster bisque tend to be heavy handed with it.  I opted to not have any sherry for that reason.

The kids liked their fried chicken fingers.  I had to remind one of them to not fill up on the fries as he really liked them.

We all liked our steaks.  They were cooked properly and were tender and flavorful.  As for the sides --- we were very disappointed in the lobster mac and cheese.  It came out watery and the lobster portion was stingy.  That's a shame, since the last time we had it, it was quite good.  I tasted the fries and thought that the truffle oil and parmigiana worked very well together.   The grilled asparagus portion was very generous and properly prepared.   Our daughter and son-in-law liked the creamed spinach.

When we were seated, our server said to my husband, "So how old are you?  25?"  My husband jokingly replied, "No, I'm 39!"  We all laughed about it and didn't give it another thought.  Then when we finished our meal, our server brought out a complimentary dessert sampler for my husband.  Using chocolate syrup, it was written on the plate "Happy 39th Birthday"!  Ah, yes, my husband wishes he was 39 again LOL!  He offered  us all some samples of his dessert and it all was tasty.

Before we left, our server took a photo of us all, then returned with it in a cardboard frame.  That was a very nice touch!

So...if you want to dine here on a Saturday, be sure to make your reservation well in advance.  Otherwise, you can take a chance and hope that you don't have to wait too long for a table at the bar.

Despite a few missteps, all and all a good meal!

This year Seasons 52 started serving Thanksgiving dinner.  When our daughter found out that they were doing this, she made a reservation.  I decided to update my review as a result.

We had a reservation for 4:15 p.m.  When we got there, we were taken to the exact same table we had on our previous visit.  This was not lost on the grandkids who all commented on it, with one even saying that he was sitting in the exact same place as before.

We were given a card with the Thanksgiving dinner menu along with the regular menus since this was also a choice for a meal.  The Thanksgiving menu was simple.  There was an adult dinner which cost $24.95 each plus a kid-sized portion for $12.95.  Along with this menu were suggested wine pairings.

For all of us, the choice was simple---we wanted the Thanksgiving meal.  My husband and our daughter each had a glass of wine with each choosing one of the suggested wines.  Both were happy with the quality of their wines.  I had an espresso martini and was surprised at how strong a pour it was.  Our son-in-law had a soda while the kids had milk.

Our server was friendly and efficient.  At one point, the manager came by to check on us all.

As for the Thanksgiving meal---It consisted of sliced turkey breast plus a small amount of dark meat.  It was plated in such a way that the breast meat obscured the dark meat.  Gravy was put on top of the turkey and the amount given was very stingy.  It would have been nice to have more.  Also, there was a scoop of stuffing which was mildly flavored but moist.  A scoop of house made mashed potatoes, evidenced by the occasional lump, was actually tasty.  There was cubed butternut squash that was properly prepared and well seasoned.  Also, there were green beans that were tender crisp.  Finally, there was a very stingy portion of whole berry cranberry sauce, which looked to me like it was only a couple of tablespoons.

After we were given our plates, a food runner placed a dinner roll on each plate.  The roll had both sesame and poppy seeds.  They weren't bad---crispy on the outside yet soft on the inside.  It would have been nice if they were served hot rather than at room temperature.  We were given a small plate of softened pumpkin spice butter.  I was the only one who tried the butter as everybody else thought it was a strange thing to put on a roll!  Actually, it did have good flavoring without being too sweet.

We all agreed that the turkey was a bit dried out and we all felt that there should have been far more gravy as we didn't have enough for the stuffing or the mashed potatoes.  I'm wondering if this was deliberately done as Seasons 52 is all about keeping the calorie count low for their meals.

I find this Seasons 52 to be cavernous with poor acoustics and when full, it gets noisy.  While we were eating, they had a performer playing the piano and singing in the bar.  However, the music was piped into the dining room.  She sang mellow songs, yet some of the song choices were strange.  For example, a soft mellow version of John Cougar Mellencamp's "Hurt So Good"...!  

Apparently, if Seasons 52 finds that serving Thanksgiving dinner was profitable for them this year, they will do it again next year.  Would we go again next year?  Well...the jury is still out on that one.

We are visiting from out of town and were excited to try this place because of the great Yelp reviews. We were looking forward to trying a slice of their famous Key Lime Pie. 

Unfortunately, we left the restaurant right after we were seated. The owner that "greeted" us at the door was very passive aggressive and rude. This is not a child-friendly place. 

We brought a very well behaved two year old and they would not let him sit by the window to look out at the dolphins, afraid he would break it. They were not accommodating of our "large" party (5 adults and 2 children), wouldn't/couldn't seat us together, and would not allow us to bring a stroller into the restaurant. 

We select our dining experiences based on Yelp reviews, and were extremely disappointed in our experience at Walt'z. I cannot recommend it.

Lochel's is a nice place. Has ready to go cakes that they ice with a message on the spot, and they sell so many different pastries (almost too many tbh).

I guess I'm just very tired of the same old, dated looks that most bakeries around this area have. Everything just feels the same.

Is this place fhreaking real?!

Hubby and I were bummin' around and checked Yelp to see what tasty eats were nearby. Seeing the raving reviews, we chose Fharmacy Nola. 

It is really easy to pass right by this unassuming little joint if you're not looking for it. So make sure you look for it, park, then have your life changed!

The wonderful menu has all of the best of bar food, with Louisiana influence, and kissed by some Vietnamese love. Trust me, it all makes sense. The owners are operators and have obvious passion for what they are doing (and they are doing it so so SO well). 

We ordered the Fharmacy Burger and we were asked if we wanted cooked to "medium". This was a very good sign that they know what they're doing. We also got an order of wings, half jerk and half lemongrass.
