The food came out quickly and was beautiful. I took a bite of the burger and almost cried. The burger was cooked perfectly to temp (which almost never happens for me), the olive mix situation was unlike anything I have ever had before, and the bacon jam, sweet mama OH the bacon jam. Everything was situated in just the right way to delight my taste buds with all of the goodness. 

And then the wings happened. Hubby is not easily impressed with wings. He almost swallowed the lemongrass wing whole, he was so into it. And then he tried the jerk wing and had an "oh my God" moment. I concur. "Oh my God," indeed. These might be the best wings we have ever had. 

Before he brought the check, Mr. Nguyen brought us over a plate of cut melon. Not sure if this is a regular thing or if they just had some left over, but we lit up like Christmas morning and were sent over the top with joy as we appreciated the cool sweet treat on such a hot day.

No joke, we actually pulled up the zillow app to search nearby homes to rent and browsed for about 30 minutes until we came back to our senses.

If the Devil vomited a miscarriage, it would be the Foodery. 

I cannot think of any other place in Philadelphia that exploits the b.s. alcohol laws in this state and the lack of product knowledge in its customers harder than the Foodery does.... 

That's right, spend 20 minutes putting together a six-pack you know nothing about, wait on a line, bitch about the other customers, sweat the fact that you should already be somewhere else, and finally get to cashier and have him tell you that you owe him $55. 

Honestly, try to put those beers back and get new ones... your allowed... but, it's not gonna happen.... you'll buy them out of guilt or because you already wasted too much time.... 

It's a joke. 

No one but a few bartenders, alcoholics, and the staff at the Foodery know how much these things cost. Yea, there's the extremely intimidating price guide to gaze through if you have an extra 40 minutes of being-cheap-time to shuffle beer back and forth....but if they wanted you to know the prices of their products, they would tack the price of the product on the shelf thats holding it... 

They want you to goto the counter blind.... Flat. 

This isn't a bar. Its a convenience store. 

The Foodery participates in price gauging, and another convenience store needs to come along and undercut them to even this garbage out. 

Absurd.

I absolutely love this restaurant! There's no bad option on the menu, it's just hard to get a table so make reservations. 
I went for dinner with a couple friends after a brisk walk through Tower Grove Park. 
We were hungry and started with drinks and appetizers. Krab rangoon is definitely a favorite item on the menu, I plan to try the krab cake option on my next visit. Then came the brussel sprout salad and I never get enough brussel sprouts, so I could eat this dish daily. Finally we tried the madura app, plantains with the housemade tofu based vegan cheese and "queso" sauce. The plantains were cooked perfectly, crispy and tender and just right sweet. So yummy!
I ordered the wild mushroom ravioli and loved it! The flavors are mild but complement so well. I was happy because I got more brussel sprouts as a topper on this dish. I would order it again. 
Susan was our waitress but we had attention from the entire staff with recommendations and ensuring we had anything we needed. The music and service were impeccable! I can't wait to try out the brunch menu!

Can't say one positive thing about this place. The staff were not welcoming, and I understand that might be because of the virus. But our waitress didn't even say hello, she jumped right to drinks. And when we only asked for water since we hadn't seen the menu she just rolled her eyes. 
We ordered flavored margaritas, which weren't good. 
I went for something safe, fried shrimp poboy and fries. Sadly, it wasn't that good, unseasoned shrimp, soggy bread. Pass.

Absolutely delicious brunch!! I can't believe it took me four years of living in the city to finally check this place out. I would have been coming here way more frequently!! 

I came here on a Saturday around 1 pm with one other person, and the wait was about 20 minutes. There is an adorable plant shop next door that we were able to walk around in while we waited. We were then seated in the front room where the coffee bar is, and the room had a really cute Parisian feel. The place is BYOB, so we just ordered a couple of coffees which were bottomless and they later let us take a cup to go. 

The food here was incredible. The entire menu sounded so good that we had trouble deciding on what to order. We ended up going with the green shakahuka and the cordon bleu waffle sandwich. The place is definitely pricey for a brunch, but the servings are pretty large. The shakshuka was very filling and was probably the best one I've had in the city. It came with bread and different veggies, and the eggs were perfectly cooked. The cordon bleu was also incredible and contained pretty much every breakfast item in one dish including waffles, eggs, fried chicken, pork, fried, etc. We were very full after this meal.

Cafe la Maude is now one of my favorite brunch spots in Philly and I can't wait to go back!

This was a true disappointment.  It was a Wednesday night, 5pm. We did not have a wait and were excited to have our first time here be a good one.  We ordered the special $1 martini ( we got mini olives) who does that?  We then ordered calamari which was good except the sauce tasted bad. Entrees were Eggplant lasagna and veal parmesan. Low and behold it was the same flat sauce with no flavor. Tasted like old sauce. Suggestion don't eat anything with the Red Gravy. We had to scrape it off to even get a bite. My husband had a side of Italian sausage that was so dry he had to give it back. I won't even go to try the pizza due to the rancid sauce.   The cannoli that I had taken to go was not good either.  If this is your first time, don't go! WAIT til they get another chef! Fresh needs to be emphasized with all ingredients not day old sauce.
really horrible service! I found a bug in my food and tried to get a refund but they wouldn't give me one. Never going again.

While the pizza was a little too greasy for my liking, I loved the sauce to cheese ratio. It was absolutely delicious! The pizza was huge and you can tell this was fresh. The crust was toasted to perfection. The sauce was rich in flavor and brought me back to the best memory of pizza I had in New York. I promise this place won't disappoint.

Pho Loc Tho is a hidden treasure in riverview. I'm so happy I found this place. I mainly order take out from here but the inside is clean and quaint. The staff is friendly and they always confirm I have everything I ordered on the phone. I request chili oil on the side and while it's a small amount, it definitely turns the heat up. Everything is neatly packed so it avoids any spillage and you don't have to carry multiple bags. 

I normally order the House Special Pho. It includes tendons, meatballs, tripes, brisket, and ribeye. There's obvious rice noodles, bean sprouts, onions, cilantro, and scallions. The broth is delicious and it comes hot but it's bearable to eat. Everything is fresh and of great quality. While it's so simple, it all brings it together. The pho place knows how to pack a punch. I love this place!

This here is a wonderful place to get some breakfast! No, I really truly mean it. Since I contracted a case of Mid City madness I was looking up new restaurant hot spots. I found this place on yelp when I was looking up breakfast places. Since it had rave reviews on here I figured I would give them a try. It was a decision that I do not regret.

The lady at the front counter was pretty friendly. When I asked her about the special she was very explanatory. The little waitress lady I had was very nice. When I say little I mean she was about 4 foot 8 inches tall. Still she was pretty nice though.

I ordered the Ghost pig special. It is a breakfast special that has chorizo sausage, cheese, and ghost pepper jelly on a fresh baked english muffin. A bowl of grits was also with the order. The ghost pig sandwich was very good! It was a very spicy but good sandwich. The grits were phenomenal as well. I could tell they were real grits with real butter. The beverage I ordered was a glass of orange juice. The best part was that it was fresh squeezed with no pulp, just the way I like it.

What Kind of baffled me about this place was the fact that they deliver! They deliver all through the mid city area. The reason I asked is because someone asked me about it. I really wouldn't ever call for delivery. I would either drive their or walk, (I do live close by). The menu is quiet extensive. Besides Breakfast,and lunch items they have baked goods and pork sausage for sale. The only problems you may encounter is finding seating or parking. Most of the seating is outside it is a small building after all. The parking is street parking and we know how difficult that can be in New Orleans.

In short fantastic food, and great service. But parking and seating might be a little tricky.

You guys! 

I just had some of the best pizza in Nashville!! Run do not walk to try the Tuscan Garden pizza: Fresh chopped kale, tossed in pepper infused 100% olive oil, homemade sauce (w/ merlot wine & chopped garlic), mozzarella cheese, sliced garden mushrooms, dolloped with labne. For those of you unfamils with labne: soft, marinated Middle Eastern cheese. Delish

Ah!! That Greek salad!! OPA! The dressing was ridiculously good. Made in-house as well!!

The service was great! Paul, the owner, was friendly, knowledgable, and passionate about food. It's unfortunate that folks had less than stellar experiences, but if you read the reviews closely, they are from years ago. 

I hear there is a new lunch menu coming soon. 

Loved it and will totally be back. 

http://www.pizzereal.com/menu.html

Easily the most elegant grocery store in Reno, the items sold at Whole Foods are seriously overpriced.

That's fine if you are good with giving money away, but I'm just not that philanthropic when it comes to supporting a corporation.

While I understand the desire to get "organic" with it, Between Wolf Pack Meats, Trader Joes, Raley's and Great Basin Co-op, there aren't many items available here  that aren't available for 20-40% less somewhere else.

However, it's so relaxing to walk the broad, beautifully displayed aisles that I'm sometimes almost glad this store is the only purveyor of my favorite shampoo. It costs me about $30 to lay in an 8 month supply -- coincidentally, the same time interval between my visits to this store.

Each time, the excellent displays beckon and the gently helpful staff members rave about something new I've never tried, and I end up spending another $30 on stuff I really don't need!

I give Whole Foods credit for having the most extensive selection of teas available at any grocery store, so I've made an unscheduled trip or two just to buy tea. The catch? If you buy one of the teas that is available locally elsewhere, get ready to fork out fiftty cents to a dollar more per package to buy it here.

Damn you Whole Foods! You are a bunch of robber barons. Whole Foods ought to create an IRA account for each of its regular shoppers because that's the only way they'll have any money left to retire with after shopping here.

When Krista E. and I decided to meet for lunch, she suggested that we try King Buffet. It's one of her favorite spots in Reno and certainly offers an astounding value for the price. 

Krista is correct about the beautiful sushi they offer. I don't do raw fish, but it was very appealing and looked fresh.

I was very impressed by how busy they were at 2:30 PM in the afternoon, a time when most restaurants are dead. And the buffet food was amazingly fresh, not "starting to turn, or dried out."

There's a bountiful salad bar, and  plenty of fresh fruit, but I went straight for the Chinese food.

I spotted a green bean dish, and loving the one from PF Chang's, had to try it. There's no comparison, but King's version wasn't bad.

King's offers every Americanized Chinese dish you can imagine. Some of my favorite items were the Mongolian Beef and the Sweet and Sour Chicken. They also had kung pow and chow mein and fried rice, sweet and sour pork, and the other standards. 

I really like that they serve the Sweet and Sour chicken naked, you add the sauce from a warm bin -- or not -- according to your taste.

The Desert bin is plentiful, although I was very full and had trouble finding items that attracted me. There's a cafeteria look about most of the deserts, so I wasn't too motivated to go for it.

I settled on the thick yellow Jello cut in squares. It was oh-so good. This reminded me of the jello at my college cafeteria and gave me warm fuzzies. Nostalgia really is what is used to be!

I tried a jellyroll cake. It was fine, but nothing special.

Unlike many buffets, they clear away your dirty plates pronto.

Though the value here is excellent, the reason I can not give them 5 stars is that the tables and chairs are somewhat cheap and uncomfortable. 

Perhaps the best way to save costs on an all-you-can-eat-buffet is to limit the all-you-can-sit-there-comfortably time.

I've been meaning to update my review for some time, but I forgot about it. My Bad!!! 

Daughters is such a quirky place. The service is uneven, the food can be great or ridiculously overpriced, but the final verdict is that I like it, and will be their customer as long as they're open. 

Late last year I went to special event for women put on by the mother who is the chef, and one of the daughters (Bianca) who is the main server. For a mere $10 per person, they served a dinner of high quality cold cuts, fancy cheeses and artisan breads and crackers, along with a beverage prior to the event.

After the event, they served their trademark, wood smoked coffee, and at least six different deserts. Patrons were encouraged to try as many as they liked. 

Since I was with a friend, we each got a desert and shared. The deserts alone were worth the $10. Super, labor intense preparations yielded high end tortes and 3-layer liquor cake, orange sponge cake, pecan tarts, custard tarts, fruit tarts and more.

They did it right, but didn't charge enough to make a penny though there must have been 30 women turning out for this enjoyable event.

That's the way it is at daughters. One day it's great service with a smile and wonderful food, the next day the staff is grumpy, slow and the food isn't up to snuff. 

There's a genuine, raw quality about these people. They are emotional and unpredictable, but generous, and incredibly hardworking. It's as though they are close to the earth in that everything they do is done themselves. I respect that.

In the future I am going to gage their mood and if that mood is cranky, I'll just have a coffee and leave. If they are happy and the food looks good, I'll eat there. 

This is a flawed -- all too evidently human establishment. 

Call me crazy, but I like it.

The snobby vibe of this place is funny considering they don't serve very good coffee.

On my first visit I tried their drive-thru at about 4PM (They're open until either 5 or 6PM). They make several coffee brews daily that are posted on a board. They were out of all but the house brew, and refused to make another pot due to the late hour. They could have made 1/2 a pot, but wouldn't do that either.

The coffee was no better than Costco coffee but it costs a lot more!

The second time I was there, I went inside to order a latte. After taking my order, the barista got a drive-thru order for 3 drinks. She made these before making my one drink. I was surprised to be "bumped" until I saw her flirting with the customer bigtime and him tipping her $5.

After that, I didn't tip her and have never been back.

There is a cluttered sort of cool about the Purple Bean, though cleanliness hounds might rightly be concerned that the work area doesn't seem to be set up in a hygenic manner.

I have no interest in trying to be "in" with Baristas that operate in whatever manner they like because no one's watching the hen house. Combine that with mediocre, pricey coffee and the question I have is how do they stay in business?

Trader Joe's has the absolute worst sustainable practices of any grocery store in the area. They sell 15 of the 22 Red listed seafoods, and by selling these, they are at the top of the list for endangering the ocean and sensitive fish populations. When they buy orange roughy they promote ruining our beautiful, diminishing coral reefs.

Just so we won't know what they're up to, Trader's repackages what they sell to make gullible consumers feel the store is "green conscious." But Trader's, more accurately, TRAITOR'S is pulling a fast one.

If you like TJ's please complain loudly because these practices are unacceptable!

Here's a website to learn all about it:  
http://www.traitorjoe.com/products.htm

That said, I do occasionally go to Traders to buy a select few things. Frozen deserts and some unusual frozen foods, along with cereals.

Their parking lot is out of control. I only stop here when I'm in the area already and have the time, but when I see they're super busy (at least half the time), I turn right around and leave. The aisles are narrow and the shopping lanes are positioned horribly so that when you exit an aisle at the front of the store you are crashing into other shoppers. I get tired of saying excuse me and even more tired of feeling like a sardine in Trader Joe's Can. 

Having recently learned of their traitorous irresponsibility to our planet, I am vowing to avoid shopping at all TJ's as much as possible until this company stops behaving as though our oceans are to be raided without a thought for the consequences. 

Your pirate logo is starting to look incredibly accurate Trader Joe. It's time to shape up or ship out!

If you want to know more, click the above link and send Trader's a singing fish telegram. The ocean will thank you.

This is one of Safety Harbor's newest gems. Tucked away off Enterprise and McMullen is a restaurant with beautiful food, an outstanding selection of wine, and passionate staff. The beautifully selected decor feels warm and clean, and the food is plated with as much care. I fell in love with the Sausage Stuffed Pork Tenderloin on Roasted Garlic Mash and Brussels Sprouts in a pan sauce. And with a decadent crème brulé for dessert, and a glass of La Crema Chardonnay, one could not have designed a better way to spend the evening. 

The staff and owners, John and Dana, are so considerate and gracious. From greeting to completion, there was such appreciation and even additional wine education as requested. This establishment is recently opened it's doors, and is obviously dedicated to providing a home for Safety Harbor residents to engage in their passion for delicious cuisine and wine.

Note:  the food section of this review is for the sausage & peppers sub, as I've tried nothing else.  

Cesarina Deli is a simple but nice dining location on East Bay.   While it looked like most coming in and out were there for the deli sandwich choices, they've got a few shelves of the most popular Italian grocery items.   In the deli prepared food section they carry cured meats, cheeses, olives, about half a dozen pasta choices & and some more cold salad dishes.  They also have several cases with bakery items, bread & cookies.

If you want to dine in there are tables to the left that seat ~20 or so.  But I was here to taste test one of my favorite subs, the sausage & peppers.

My order at the counter was taken fairly quickly even though there were about 5 people in line.  It was well-wrapped in foil to keep it take-out hot and I appreciated that.  And the size of the wrapped sub quickly showed that Cesarina definitely delivers an extremely large sub for the price.

But while it was still hot when I arrived home, when I opened up the foil wrap I found the sorriest looking sausage & peppers sub I've ever seen in my life.  The green peppers and onions were cooked to death in heavy oil to the point they had virtually no flavor.  The oil almost completely soaked the sub roll, and the dry portion of the roll I did manage to taste was not that flavorful and a bit tough to chew.  To top off this sad collection was the sausage link.  While I'm a huge fan of meat in tube form, and I've had many sausages in different ethnic cuisines, most all Italian sausages I've ever found have been a nice mix of  full meat flavor and spice.  But this link was the most bland taste with only spicey hot flavors.  Worse yet, the inside of the link was just ...well, just a disgusting grey color.  I'm not foolish enough to think sausages are made of any prime pork cuts, but hey, if you're going to leave out the flavor at least throw me a bone with some red dye #3 like a hot dog so it resembles something that might be meat related.   Sure, it's a carcinogen, but I'd trade that even up if at least fooled the cro-magnon portion of my meat-eating brain into thinking I was dining on something edible.

Combining the tasteless grey sausage link with likewise sad, soggy sausage and peppers, after two bites I found the entire sub completely inedible and tossed it in the trash.  And I can't think of hardly any food I've ordered in a decade or two that turned my stomach as bad as this sub.

Again, this food review is for one sandwich and nothing else.  And while this experience would normally make me write off Cesarina completely, the other reviews of the cold subs or prepared foods would not stop me from stopping by again and trying one of them.  If I do, I'll update my review and scores accordingly.

My scores on the deli scale are:

Atmosphere:  3
Service:  4
Food:  0....and that may be too high
Value:  0

Update 2/13

I've eaten here many times since my initial review and the flavors have always been very consistent.  Every person I've dragged here to join me has raved about it.

 Also, they now have $1 tacos from 11a-5pm (I recall), Monday through Friday.   The $1 tacos are a bit smaller, there are only a few meats offered, and include either rice or potatoes.  Definitely not as filling as their standard size, but still great taste.

WOW!  What great tastes.

Since my first bite at Cielito Lindo (CL) this week, I've been compelled to eat there 3 days in a row, and I just might eat there again today, too!

I've eaten at over 2 dozen Mexican restaurants in Pinellas over the past few months, and Cielito Lindo has knocked my socks off.  It's definitely landed in the top 3 on my "Most Authentic Mexican" list:
http://www.yelp.com/list/most-authentic-mexican-restaurants-in-pinellas-clearwater

I can sum up all the flavors in one word:
Delicate

I've rarely tasted Mexican food like this in the East.  Most Mexican in this part of the country seems to use a pretty heavy hand with strong flavors and spice.  Cielito Lindo takes a much more subdued approach, where every incredibly fresh ingredient balances between standing on it own and enhancing the other flavors.  Like Laura said previously, this is definitely authentic SoCal style flavors.

Cielito Lindo is located on Tarpon Ave, just a few blocks east of the heart of the downtown village area of Tarpon Springs.  It's in a very narrow storefront less than 20' wide, sitting just to the right of a conveniece store on a corner, and is very easy to miss if you're not looking closely.  The interior is simple and very clean, with just 2 tables with 6 chairs total, and two high tables with 6 barstools total.  I was there at 2pm on of their $1 taco days (Monday and Thursday, noon to 6p), and it was so crowded I ended up sharing a table with a friendly local and enjoyed a great chat while eating lunch.  They serve lots of takeout orders if that works better for you.  Orders are taken up at the counter, and are processed and served up promptly by friendly staff.  Unfortunately there's no beer available, but there's a cooler just left of the order counter with bottled drinks and water.

The menu is not too big, with breakfast serving 9 choices of eggs ($5) and 6 burritos (only $3 from 7a-11a).  The regular menu has 11 different tacos, 10 tortas, burritos, enchiladas, quesadillas, tamales, sopes, tostadas, taco salad and nachos.  They also have combo platters of steak, chicken, pork red chile and chile rellenos with rice/beans/tortillas ($6-8).  On Wednesdays burritos and quesadillas are $4 (noon to 6p),

I've had the chicken, steak, carnitas and chorizo tacos, and with each of them, the meat was bursting with flavor.  While you can top them traditionally with just cilantro, they normally serve them with cilantro and just a small amount of lettuce, diced tomatoes, and white Mexican cheese.  Normally I'd opt for the traditional approach, but after having one their way, I've stuck with it with no regrets.  My favorites are the carnitas and chorizo, but with 11 choices, you can certainly find your favorites. The steak and chicken enchiladas I had were similarly light and very fresh tasting, with a light cheese topping.   And wrapping up both tacos and enchiladas are the thinnest of fresh, hand-made corn tortillas I've ever seen, in fact, so thin they're translucent.  And while you might expect such a thin tortilla would break and fall apart, these don't at all, and give you just enough texture and flavor to know they're there, but let the ingredients steal the show.  

While I usually use liberal doses of salsa on Mexican dishes, more than once I started in on a taco or enchilada, just to taste all the pure flavors, and finished it without adding a drop.   I've never done that anywhere else.  Cielito Lindo also has a great creamy green salsa, very unusual in the Tampa area....I've had it before in Texas, but not around here.  It's a fantastic flavor in a creamy consistency which reminds me of the spicy mayos used on sushi.  They usually have several salsa choices just to the left of the cash register.

If you're every in the Tarpon Springs area, definitely stop in and check this place out.  Highly recommended!   On my Pinellas taqueria scale, I rate it:

Atmosphere:   5
Service:  5
Food:   5
Value:   5


Update:   As it's the one week anniversary of my first visit and review, and I have proclaimed it Cielito Lindo day.  First I stopped in for breakfast.  Had one of their breakfast burritos (a tasty chorizo and egg), just $3 from 7a-11a.  Of course, later in the day since I was still in town I had to come back for a late lunch of their Thursday $1 tacos.  Supper will be a take home box of assorted items.  It's sad isn't it....I am hopelessly addicted to this place!   Just incredible food at great prices.

I could distill this review to two words:

Roast Pork

But then I would be overlooking the great yellow rice and beans, and the friendly owners and staff that cook up that pork with the most incredible marinade I've ever tasted anywhere.  Just a perfect balance of flavor, herb and spice.  Indescribably delicious.  I talked to the owner so long about how much great it was, he brought out the container he mixes the marinade in just to let me take a look at it and have a sniff.  

I haven't tried anything else on the menu because I haven't eaten enough roast pork here before I die.  And without question Tia's passes that critical measure of any great family restaurant/diner.....the cop test.  I counted 6 there during a recent lunch, with 2 more that stopped by for takeout.

There are not a lot of places to get Latin flavors in Largo, so it's great to have Tia's to save trips all the way to Tampa.

Atmosphere:  3

Food:   5
Value:   5

Really dig the vibe here at United by Blue.

Thoroughly enjoyed a red-eye coffee and breakfast sandwich. I had a bacon, egg and cheese sandwich on a sesame bagel. A small splurge well worth the extra carbs.

Cool flagship store in the heart of Olde City. Warm and welcoming staff as well.

Nice to see a company that is trying to make a difference in the world and our oceans. 

UBB removes a pound of trash for every product sold so if my coffee and sandwich count that's 2 pounds from me yay!

My fiancé's family and I went here last night as a group, and everyone raved about it! We'll definitely be back again, for many reasons. 

First of all, the whole place is authentic. Seriously. From the pizza sauce and flour to the buffalo mozzarella, everything is from Naples (via Baltimore). They even brought masons from Naples to construct the pizza oven.

Second, they know how to cook a pizza Napoletana reallllllly well. I lived with a guy who spent a couple of years managing an authentic "pizza Napoletana" restaurant. You have specific requirements for thickness of dough, sauce, heat of the oven, ingredients, etc. I spent many meals eating at his restaurant...and Vecchia is better! The crust has a crunch on the outside and an awesome "tug" when you bite. Perfect amount of sauce and ingredients.

Last but not least - THE PRICE. Monday specials include a 12" Margherita pizza for FIVE FREAKING DOLLARS. That's seriously unreal regardless of the pizza, but something of this quality makes it truly incredible. 

I plan on getting fat eating here, and you should too.

Dearest Donna, thou art truly mad.  And I'm mad about you.  No, seriously, let's go out some time and you can make me that fantastic breakfast pizza that I just enjoyed today for brunch.  Speaking of 'mad', you're crazy (in a good way) for creating a breakfast pizza.  Breakfast... pizza... pizza is not cold... pizza is not a day old... um, YES, please.  

Flatbread + sausage gravy (the "sauce") + scrambled eggs + two cheeses (the "toppings") = a breakfast orgy in my mouth.  Donna, you're dirty, mad, and created an explosion of yummy.

Did I also mention that if you like to consume a little adult beverage with brunch that Donna's has 2 for 1 mamosas on Sunday brunch?  Oh, I didn't...  Well, they do!  Black raspberry, peach, orange, grapefruit... all sounded yummy.  Black raspberry and peach were the delights of choice by my partner in crime today.  She had one of each (because, again, one is not enough).  I tried both.  They were terrific.  

She had for brunch the Donna's Omelet, which is a brunch filled with queso, black beans, peppers, and madness.  Omelet... queso... um, yes, please.

I will be returning with further reviews of Donna's for "Taco Tuesday" ($2 tacos), "Wings Wednesday" ($0.49 wings), and for drinks at night.

Donna, you are UHHHHH-MAZE-ING HOT-NESS.

City House is good.  People enjoy City House, and I enjoyed City House.  But, this is another "it's good, but there are better" places in Nashville.  And, since the 3-star rating says "A-OK" next to it in big capital letters, I have rated City House for what it is:  A-OK.

The wine and cocktail menus are quite nice -- although disappointing that they did not have spherical ice for my whiskey aperitif but that's OK, I suppose, as so few do here.  The whiskey was still nice as were the appetizers: cauliflower served with pomegranate and almonds was one and the other was a Salami and cheese.  Good.  Yes.  Blow me out of the water great.  No.  The cauliflower at Josephine and Etch are better.  

For dinner, I ordered a nice chianti (sans fava beans and sans some victim's liver).  But, I did order the House Made Belly Ham, Mozzarella, Grana Padano, Oregano, and Chilies pizza.  The pizzas are thin crusted and can easily serve two normal sized humans.  Again, I thought it was good.  But, it was not any better than eating at Mafiaoza's and Mafiaoza's is not all that great.  Both are just A-OK.  Was it edible and good?  Yes.  Did I leave wanting to shank anyone on Yelp who blasphemed City House's food?  No.  I wouldn't fight anyone over returning to the place. But I'd go back if asked. 

So, you can go give it a try.  It is OK after all.  Just please do not blame me if you leave thinking it was just OK.

Party like a Thai star, party like a thai star... it's like totally dude.  

Yesterday, one of the last food trucks that I have been stalking to try was at the Whole Foods in Franklin supporting (with other food trucks) NPT channel 8 with some of their proceeds.  That truck is the Deg Thai truck.  Deg Thai is a food truck servicing the Nashville, Tennessee (and suburbs) area.  The truck serves traditional Thai food on the go.

I had the pleasure of trying the special of the day which was, in the immortal words of Flanders, "scrum-ditilly-umptious".  The dish was Kao Mun Gai and consisted of chicken, raisins, a medium spicy soy sauce-based sauce served on top of Jasmine rice.  The portion size is perfect for one person, and the meal hit the spot on a cold, cold day.  Moreover, my wife had the green chicken curry served medium spicy.  The curry comes with baby corn, red peppers, green peppers, and fresh basil.  Including the chicken, the curry is served atop jasmine rice as well.  The truck also offers that all of their dishes may be served over egg noodles or Thai noodles (I am assuming that means rice noodles).  But, she is a Celiac, we chose not to risk it and avoided the noodles.  

The truck did seem a little bit clueless about allergies, particularly a gluten allergy so I would be curious to hear about the experience of others with either allergies or with those who are vegan.  With that said, I am going to say that this is the best Thai food that I have enjoyed in Nashville.  It's really quite fantastic and I highly recommend it to anyone out there, especially if you are really into food trucks that source locally.  The truck takes both cash and credit - which I thought I'd mention because some of the trucks do not take credit.

What is more southern then catfish and okra? That is what I had and it was cooked to perfection. The meal was complete with a biscuit and mashed potatoes. 

The establishment is quaint, very clean and has a variety of seating options (outdoors, bar, dining). 

For price, options, speed, quality and small town feel in the city The Row cannot be beat.

Came over for brunch and had... 
yeah, that should pretty sum up my review for this one. I can't really remember what I had. And my taste buds have almost perfect memory. I imagine it couldn't have been extremely offensive.. or notable.. so I'm gonna look up the menu...
Ah yes! the spinach and mushroom frittata (3/5 stars). I knew it had eggs, and it's all coming back to me now.. mushy, kinda greasy, and overall insipid. 
The bacon we ordered on the side (3 strips for $4) wasn't crispy, so that was a let down as well. 
I guess I'm giving them a freebie star because of the beautiful locale and extremely friendly waitress or maybe it was the mimosas..

When I moved to West philly, everybody told me to try Mr. Lees breakfast... specifically the egg cheese susage bagel which is amazing. Just enough butter and cooked properly.

Mr Lee touts his spinach chicken cheesesteak as the best in philly and it does not fail to impress. Personally I enjoy the chicken cheesesteak with broccoli instead.

If you want good food at an extremely affordable price come to mr Lees! 

Also try the Hungryman breakfast special. 4 eggs, 2 orders of meat(SUAsage, bacon?) hashbrowns (whcih are DELICIOUS) toast

We reserved a table for an early dinner on a Saturday night to celebrate my birthday. We arrived early and were seated right away.  I immediately loved the atmosphere.  The wall that changes color is cool. Our waitress was very attentive and helped us navigate the menu. We decided to order the tasting menu.  All 9 dishes we ordered were equally amazing. The rock shrimp, pad thai, scallops, general tso dumplings, and short rib lo mein, are all highly recommended.  I want more. The bonus mini ice cream cones were the perfect finish.

I used to love this place. I was a regular - I knew everyone who worked here. I miss it, to be honest.

One night at 9pm, while playing trivia with my regular team, I put my arm around my girlfriend. The owner, Dave, asked us not to touch because 'there are children here.'  We felt sad, and we left. 

Despite the fact that it was 9pm, that it's a PUB, that children (including my gf's children) can see two women touching without probably being scarred for life, and that I was a regular customer, the owner went out of his way to make us feel unwelcome. It wasn't a mistake. It was just homophobia. 

This probably will encourage some Main-line-ers to GO, rather than to stay away, but I would prefer to spend my hard-earned money where all customers feel welcome.

I'm am not a soup person, 
Let me say that again....
I am NOT a soup person.  
But Kin convinced me that I have never know a good bowl of soup in my life.

During a recent planning of dinner with friends, Kin was suggested (sideways face, gaaaaaw soup).  I cheerfully agreed.  The photos were so delicious looking. I was actually excited.  It's a small place and the crowd was beginning to swell as the Pirate and I waited for Jey and Yay to arrive.
A nice young man in line offered a beer to Jey as she and he chatted up beer and Atlanta.  Good sign. Nice people come here.
We were seated at the bar(this place was packed on a Tuesday at 7:30pm) and started with an order of Mac n cheese dumplings and wings.  The wings were delicious but way hotter than I expected (I was assured by others they were not hot at all....ummmm okay). So delicious! The dumpling was good too, but a second to the wings in my books.
Each of us ordered a different ramen(yeah it's not soup, but anything brothy is soup to me so).  Oh and it was filled to the rim with lots of junk , I love junk! I gobbled it all up with glee.  Then I glanced over,  and Yay's bowl looked so different. Ohhhhhh I should have sipped the broth first. I guess I don't have to, but that would have been so much better for me.
Surprisingly I ate every drop? What I'm not a soup person!?
Wait......I AM a soup person and apparently Kin is the only place I want to go to eat soup.  Thank you Kin for setting me straight after all these years.

By the by, I loved the wings so much I ordered two portions to go. And yes my mouth was on fire after I ate them, but I was still smiling and thinking of Soup.

When I first moved to Louisiana, I frequented this area quite a bit......
I actually remember when this was an actual auction house, full of furniture, paintings and antiquities.

But now.............its full of food, drinks and macaroons!

The first time I went I wasn't exactly sure what was in store....
The interior is light and airy, it sort of takes your breath away.  The plants from Luna Botanicals are everywhere and add to the ambience in a big way.

The bar is located centrally and food stations are located on the outer edge.  There is something for everyone.  I personally have dined on raw oysters, ceviche, poke bowls, mediterranean dip trio(ask for extra pita, the fancy indian street food, macaroons, coffee and dark & stormys from the bar.

Poke Bowls are not new to me and I love the freshness of them.  Tracy and her staff make a mean bowl, if I do say so myself.  I heard the empanadas are scrumptious, so I definitely need to try them real soon. 

I really like this location, lots of street parking and lots near by, close to the museums and galleries.  Its probably why I've been so many times now...happy hour meet up, out of town guest lunch, business meeting, after event dinner and after dinner dessert with my dietary restrictive brother in law (Thanks Mac & Moon!.....he gobbled down your version of an ice cream sandwich).

Still more food to enjoy.  I'm not going to get into a rut by selecting the same place every time.  

That would be too easy.....let the adventures begin.

I've been shopping at Trader Joe's for so many years, that I actually remember what it used to look like with rows of nuts, dried fruits and muesli, isles of wines(when 2$ buck chuck was actually 2$), no frills.....and the staff in Hawaiian shirts.  

Then they grew and added bright colored signage and reusable totes, expanded their stocks.  It was my number one go to for everything I needed in California.  Then I moved in 2005 and I longed for TJs....every time I visited I purchased copious amounts of stuff that I would pack as souvenirs to bring back with me.  I even requested a certain kind of bread for family and friends to load into their carry ons when visiting or returning home.

Then the heavens parted and Trader Joe's came to New Orleans.  Anyone from California will understand why we all cried tears of joy.

I laugh at people who I see shopping now, long gone are the health food people or laid back beach residents; Now replaced by yoga attired folks, hipsters and ladies from Metairie, it makes for a good giggle.  

I can't wait to see if they build one down in the bayou.....I can only hope and pray or change my address.

HOT TIP!: Read and shop from their flyer mag. Not only is it good fun reading, it will alert you on special limited supply items. Like the Magnums of Prosecco I bought for a song at Christmas, that made the best hostesses gifts over the holidays, I only wish I had bought more....

I'm stuck at the Whole Foods.   The unpredictable weather here in New Orleans makes a West coaster like myself nervous.  it looks like a typhoon is approaching.  I'll sit for a moment and tell you why I love me some Whole Foods.  Honestly, it takes away my yearning for California. It smells like California, yep it does.  The produce is fresh and abundant.  The smell of cut flowers hits you as you enter the doors.  The endless bites of yumminess in the bakery, baguettes and Central Coast wines whisper for you to go on a picnic, thinking about grilling up some brats? How about 15 choices! PB & J? Grind your own butters!!! Hungry right now? Shame on you for shopping, but wait.....why not have a bite to eat before or after shopping? There's a breakfast bar for you early risers or plenty of pick your choice ..... This morning I grabbed the smoked mozzarella pasta salad a d a turkey sandwich. I ate every bite and now the rain has stopped so I must move on......I do love you whole foods and thanks for my little Cali boost, I needed that today!

Ohhhh lawdy it has taken me 10 years to finally eat Willie Mae's chicken....is it the best? It's light and crispy, a little spicy.  But not unto the chicken itself, is the over whelming feeling of sitting at your grandma's table as she serves you up a plate of food.

I was lucky enough to have a friend visiting..... she was specifically going to stop into Willie Mae's Scotch house, I sort of inserted myself into her plans.  

Super easy to find with the GPS.  We parked on the street.
As you walk in, a sign requests you to wait to be seated.  It was wide open this day(2:30pm), and a gal appeared out of no where and offered us a few choices.  
We ordered sweet tea right off the bat.....

2 orders of chicken(15$), one with Mac n cheese, the other with green beans, and additionally we ordered the peas, red beans and rice and rice with brown gravy.....and a couple of corn bread muffins.  

Oh yeah the chicken is delicious.....and so was everything else.  They were out of something, but I can remember what.  Plenty to eat and enough for another meal for sure.....
We tried the bread pudding and it was good.....heavy on the rum sauce, but no one had to twist my arm to keep eating it.

I loved every minute of the experience....the food, the atmosphere, the staff......

The true meaning of Winner, Winner, Chicken dinner.

Hands down, my new favorite restaurant! I had reservations about a catering company going full brick and mortar (get it?) But Hope and Jason have no doubt about it scored big!

When my favorite restaurant, The Brasserie, left St. Pete's downtown corridor, I was at a huge loss of where I loved! 

We tried B&M the other evening and I am still having dreams about their onion tart, beef carpaccio with perfect gooey egg and their lavender pana cotta. 

I worry so much since the reviews and write ups in the paper rave about them that I may not be able to get in so easily next time. I do want them to succeed tho anx they are well on their way.

Food - 5 stars 
Service - 5 stars
Ambiance - 5 stars

Crazy bowls and wraps was closed so I decided to try this place out. I was surprised that the place was still open being it was Easter weekend. 
I was glad that I came here. This place is voted the best Pad Thai food restaurant in St Louis and I can understand why.
I tried their red curry platter with tofu and their tofu was perfectly cooked. In addition, the sauce was pretty spicy so I made sure to have a glass of cold soy milk with me. The dish was packed full of flavor. 
The food did also come out fairly quickly as well. The price was not bad as the quality of the food here is astronomical.
I highly recommend this place. It's decent for a good take out but it is pretty small for a decent dining experience.

Doesn't look like much when you drive into the plaza. Our coworker and the drummer of Anima Stereo invited us to their show on location! Check the Macho T's Facebook for future shows and updates!!

Service was nice at 8:30 pm. The waitress was apologetic when plates were running slow or when we had to make last kitchen requests for the chef. The tables are a bit close, but I love how big they are. Also like the western feel to the place.

We started with chips and a Grande margarita. This Cadillac was refreshingly strong! We ended up ordering another two later.

We ordered three plates, and were upcharged for any meat change requests. Plates were tasty, and our party of three made it more than halfway through our plates until we hit a wall..slowed down to finish the rest. 

For dessert we were determined to share one fried ice cream, but decided on two since we were indecisive at the same time. can I say yum and grand with the plating! Cinnamon sugar tortilla bowl with Bailey's like ice cream with chocolate shavings. The only odd thing was the jelly candy toping that got too hard to chew. The waitress was upselling since we already had a hard time finishing our plates!! 

The music was awesome, acoustic rock songs tonight. It would be better knowing Spanish and moreso if you are familiar with dancing cumbia variations.

Night scenery is great due to the red lighting at the bar.  The art throughout the venue is admirable, but the best part is a headshot of a lucha libre "The Macho T" at the bar. It glows badas$ery :)

If you're an apple strudel lover come through! And come early. This deliciousness was referred to us by my cousin. The plaza is cute and plentiful with parking. Quite the view after a powdered layer of snowstorm.

According to the server we lucked out being able to order fresh apple strudel when we did! We tried an arrangement of pastries and everything's flakey good consostenly. The cake was so soft and creamy.  

The auntie gifted us with blueberry coffee cake and apricot tart/shortcrust pie and that was amazing. We even waited a few days to oven heat and devour, and it was delicious!! At times bit sweet tart for my liking, but the shortbread crust balanced this out.

We reserved AYCE sushi dine-in for Saturday afternoon at 2pm. 
I was impressed with sign that let's you scan code and read the menu via phone. This scan is only for Chinese food. 

You are not allowed to order crab ragoon if you are eating AYCE sushi...oddly they cant even offer you to make it an additional side purchase.

Staff doesn't explain the difference between AYCE lunch $19 and for an additional $2/person Special AYCE lunch..so we ended up checking a part of the paper menu that isnt labeled or communicated until a later waitress gave us the breakdown. The chef scoffed at us for ordering more in the end "you better eat those!"

The servers in white button up shirts are more communicative. There's a lot of crew members in polos walking around. Most will refill your drinks..they did seat us very promptly with sets and water glasses too. Food also came out fast. The guys in the polo's were first contact and we wish they had gone over the lunch price breakdown.

Tea per pot is $3 and they charge you $1.50 PER cup. Midway through the server took away one of our cups -_-.

Appetizer: We enjoyed the wings..my tastebuds were searching for a garlic flavor though!! 
The sliced cucumber in sweet sauce was refreshing.

Most rolls were bland...sweet sauce is a reoccurring trend.
There was a deep fried roll that stood out. 

Aha, At least we ordered most of what's on the SPECIAL roll menu section, but 
 they all ended up tasting too similar..again with the sweet sauce.

More than two of our nigiri orders were missed!! Communicate if you're out of supply!!
FYI lunch does not come with dessert. It is $3 for a single scoop of black cherry ice cream.

I ignored my gut knowing fusion restaurants are usually a miss!! Location convenience was why we tried Jazmine.
We would like to try Chinese take out someday, but this dine in experience was such a cold experience..upcharging patrons for every little doggone thing. We weren't even allowed to order crab ragoon for goodness sake!!

Skip Jazmine and just drive the extra few miles for legitimate AYCE sushi joint.

We have always driven by their catering and food truck and finally was able to make it on a Saturday for lunch! Walking in all but one booth and center tables were open. The seating was cozy and the scene was upscale. We managed to sit at the one bench booth where you could find the cool alligator head sculpture and college football was on. I was able to read about the restaurant bio's on the wall. It was awesome having the owner check in with the tables during our meal!!

We were seated right away and the waiter soon followed up with drink orders. 

We loved the 20+ oz Mason jar for drinks, it's beautiful to look at delicious to sip on without having to worry about feeling held back about finishing your drink too soon!!

Spicy vinegar: This condiment is a first I've seen at a cafe...it reminds me of home cooking, so I was thrilled for this! It pairs best with the alligator stick and the fried oyster po boy plate!! I was disappointed that the fried oysters had heavy batter, but the vinegar was able to balance seasoning.

We also ordered the meats plate: The hot link sauce comes with a sneaky kick. And the fried chicken option was four chicken wings freshly fried, so the crisp was just at the right crunch! For sides the hush puppies are good, and mac n cheese was cheesy good. 

I would definitely be back for alligator, and sweet tea :)

You can see the staff's smiles through their masks! The service is friendly and fast with accommodating you as they multitask. I made a last minute order change and they adjusted my order no problem! 

Seating is based according to social distancing. 
 I did wish my bowl had more shrimp in it!!otherwise the noodle bowl was refreshing...made me miss backyard barbeques! 
If you like extra crunchy chicken get it here. The pieces are a bit big and firm in texture, but it fills you up. my dad fries them this way too, so the chomp in ng on that crunch was nostalgic for me!
Also grabbed iced coffee before leaving, which was brewed and sweetened to order. sealed securely as milk tea take out.

Simple. Thanks for being genuinely nice while making dine in so easy!!

This place is very good. My husband and I basically ordered half the menu and I can't say anything bad about any of the dishes. My favorite was the mushroom tortellini and the beet salad was also very good. My husband ordered the lamb and he said it had the best flavor. We will definitely come back again!

I am very familiar with the Rotisserie Buffet. I worked at the Nugget for 25 years and remember when the Rotisserie was THE buffet in town, going there was very special and so many lovely foods to choose from, as we expect when we go to a buffet.
We went for lunch, the Hotel seemed quite empty so was surprised to see so many people in the buffet. The cold salad stations were sparse looking and lots of space between the bowls. Nothing there looked tempting or unexpected. The hot stations had more selections that appealed such as salmon, ribs, baked potato with toppings, turkey pot pot casserole, fried chicken, to name a few. The seating areas seemed perhaps darker than I ever recall, but not in a good way. The dessert station was always a highlight and had everything you could think of..... not now. I was beyond amazed at the half inch sliver of chocolate cake they were offering. Photographed it!! The few pies they had were small but that's fine.  The eclair I was craving measured a square inch, not okay. The overall experience was such that there was nothing that would prompt me to go back again!

Find the food here surprisingly good as first went here for convenience. I have since been back several times and the family all enjoy the menu selections as they can find their favorites. Sometimes the noice level is extreme but not really a problem as going in, you know this as wquie open. There is outside seating the main interior section and this would be my favorite and my suggestion if you don't want to be inundated with their music, tv, etc. My favorite as it is usually later in the evening, is just to have their appetizer of roasted brussel sprouts. always delicious with the right amount of balsamic and roasted perfectly each time. The men in the family choose their meatloaf or their french dip with a side of cole slaw.

No so great customer service today. We three are here for dinner, really enjoy sitting in their booths against the wall.
No one sitting there but we have to sit five paces away as that server isn't here yet! Ordered cheese fries no jalapeños, came with jalapeños. The very minute we got our appetizer, they carry in the entrees. This happened last time also, this time I said they need to send the food back till we are ready. Disappointing visit as the food itself is delicious!

This place is ridiculously expensive and for absolutely nothing!!!! N-O-T-H-I-N-G!!! 

Limited cocktail menu. 
$19 drinks
Mediocre food
Mediocre desserts 
Shitty service, the kind that takes 20 minutes to bring water but then checks in on you every 5th minute when you're actually trying to have a moment and a conversation. 


And imagine a world where 3 drinks, one small appetizer, and 2 desserts come out to $96!! Next time I wanna feel like this, I'll flush some cash down the toilet!

I don't know what the fuss is about, honestly. Found this place on yelp while in SB and because of the amazing reviews we decided to give it a try. 

So disappointing. The place itself is nice but tight. Lots of tables way too close to each other. 

The service is so bad. You will have to wait forever for everything. I was amazed that after having waited for so long to get a simple pasta dish, the waitress had the nerve to ask "anything else" with an attitude when they had barely done the bare minimum. Barely!!! I wish Meryl Streep had been there to use her Devil Wears Prada voice and curtly say "your job." 

The menu was interesting enough but not too special. The only amazing thing on there were their prices because after the food arrived, let me tell you, it wasn't worth the $20. I've had better pasta from the frozen section at trader joes. 

And the bread they brought us...my guess is that it had been sitting out from the previous morning. Accompanied with olive oil that didn't taste like anything, not even olive oil... 


Let's just wrap it up with the biggest 'Eek! Methinks not!' of my life!

Owner could not be more rude and nasty! I decided to add key lime pie after she closed out Bill and she wouldn't ring up for less then $10...threw my credit card at me and said "now I know why you are divorced"! In my life I have never seem anything like it....they are not grateful for their customers - they just don't care"!!!

Fork has been on my restaurant wish list for years so my husband surprised me by taking me here over my birthday weekend. The interior is beautiful with high ceilings and gorgeous chandeliers. I commented to my husband that I can't wait to come back and sit at the bar one night when covid is a thing of the past. We felt very comfortable with the spacing of the tables per covid procedures and loved our cute little table for two. 

Their specialty cocktail menu was limited so I didn't find anything I loved there but the bar was happy to accommodate any request and french 75 was delicious. For apps, we tried the dew drop cheese and the octopus. Generally speaking, octopus is not my favorite dish but the way this was done, with the flavor accompaniments, was divine. I told my husband this octopus dish was my favorite octopus I've ever had!! And just when I think it wouldn't get better, we tried the dew drop cheese. This dish is one of those dishes where you THINK you know what it's going to be and then you taste it and you're left wondering how they improved upon the two best things in the world: cheese & bread. The flavors were so interesting and unexpected but somehow worked perfectly- I couldn't get enough.

For dinner, I ordered the burger because I had heard from reviews that it was amazing and the reviews were right. The brisket was so flavorful plus I think every burger should have caramelized onions on it. It was pretty epic.

Dessert came around and I could barely eat anything else but I couldn't pass up one of my favorites: carrot cake. Honestly, this was the dish that fell short for me. The 'icing' was certainly not sweet, likely by design, as if it was a yogurt or sour cream based icing and while it was good, it wasn't the traditional carrot cake I was thinking it would be. The flavors in the cake itself were great though- spicy, just how I like it!  

Our service was great and I'm sorry it has taken me so long to get here but Fork was worth the wait.

V-Steak ! Paper was saturated in grease, but the sand which  was very dry, from bread being over toasted . (See pics) Also the staff who prepared my food was not wearing gloves and was drinking and  soda and playing on her phone.
When asked She assured that she just washed her hands! Also, I think it's unprofessional for staff to be fixing there hair where food is being prepared.Next thing was the Mac & Cheez, very dry and lacked the creamy consistency, ( it was like they didn't have anymore or was leftovers from the burnt edges of the pan) which it use to have. I don't know if they change the recipe but not a fan. Won't be back for a while which is sad cause I really like this place and it was local.

When I recently visited my big brother in Indiana, this California girl was dying from lack of decadent food and a cool place to hang out.  Thank God Louie came into my life. He truly made my trip to Indianapolis memorable. This place came highly recommended by locals. 

This place is spacious, causal yet trendy joint. They have friendly and attentive staff. The food here are bursting with deliciousness. You can taste the freshness and in the quality of their food. Also, the waiter is great in recommending harmonious pairing of my food/wine.

This wine bar is California girl approved. It definitely satisfied my insatiable appetite. Thanks Louie for a great and fun night. You  definitely will  be on my stop on my next visit

It's great that there's been more sushi options in the area, and the staff here are really nice...but Kei serves pretty average sushi. The rolls were decent, but the sashimi wasn't particularly fresh.

Like most standard sushi places in Philly, Kei is not run by actual Japanese. This is very obvious if you try their appetizers. Their braised eggplant and spicy tofu and mushrooms are similar to the sweet garlic sauce dishes you find at takeout Chinese restaurants.

Previously I've gone to Taj Mahal for dinner but now I've had the great fortune to experience the buffet. The buffet may look small but that actually works as an advantage. You can be sure that everything is fresh because they're bringing out more of it almost constantly as it runs low. There are several selections for both vegetarians and those of us that eat meat. Typically there's naan, 4 or 5 entree selections, rice, salad, and dessert. Don't fill up too quickly or you'll miss out on killer rice pudding. Yum.

Overall it's a great deal. If you want to sample different things before coming back for dinner or want to save some cash vs the slightly pricier entrees you can't beat the lunch buffet.

Well this has been an incredible Valentines weekend an what really set it off was finding Meaghyn at &27 (Ampersand27yeg) on Twitter & instagram. She made sure we were treated like royalty without even knowing us. That is first rate customer service...I wish we could hire her and her crew! If you are out on Whyte ave and needing a great fix of food I highly recommend you stop in! 
It started out with us showing up unannounced on Friday night without a reservation. There was no room to get us in, but that did not stop her from trying to assist as she put in a call to a neighbouring restaurant down the street! Wow, who does that? 
We did make a reservation for the next night and when we came in it was to a complete made for Valentines menu. What a selection they had set up for everyone. The recommendations were bang on and they had no worries when I let them know of my gluten allergy. Quite a portion of the menu is already gluten free. Again this I found impressive. 
We spent an incredible evening there, the details on the amazing food and dishes you will see soon from Carla N when she posts her review. My thing is service.
We decided to return the next day for the Brunch, again we had no reservation. There were plenty of tables open but they told us they needed to ask the server if they could take on another table. Say what, empty tables are money lost aren't they, they would rather focus on the amazing service than take on another table they could not handle. This is some serious commitment to service, and for me this pays off big time as I will do nothing but rave about Ampersand27 to all my friends and clients. They treat you like you are their most important customer, and I felt like it. Well done!
Great greasy deli/breakfast food.. amazing fries and decent cheesesteaks. Love the charm of the spot and good service

So amazing! We made a detour just to go this this restaurant and it didn't disappoint. The vegetarian platter is so tasty. We ordered two platters for two people and we were so sad when it was gone. It is vegan. If you have any questions about ingredients, they are happy to answer questions. The Shiro wat is SO DELICIOUS. I'd recommend ordering more of that.

After all these years and incarnations of business' that have occupied this building I have never been inside.

I really like the look and feel of the interior, well exterior too. It reminds me of my childhood. 

We were seated right away and soon after asked what we might want to drink. I did order wine, something I very rarely do and it was good. 

A person I believe the bus person brought a very small white place with three very small lumps of bread. When he placed it on the table all three of us just broke out laughing. For heaven sake folks why bother? It had no real flavour and if anyone of us waned to use a bit of butter to get some flavour it would have been gone for the other two since that too was minuscule. We at that point were hoping this is not a sign of things to come.

Gus ordered the lump crab for a starter, but they has just sold the last one so he opted for the Grilled Scallops and Calamari Steak. He said it was wonderful and was quite pleased. I had a Romaine "Wedge" Salad, I know boring but I did very much enjoy it as it was crisp and the blue cheese was fantastic. My sister has the Spinach salad and she too enjoyed. The one thing I did notice at all other tables getting salad they were offered ground pepper, we were not.

For our mains Gus ordered the Rib Eye Steak medium, although it did come out a true medium rare it was very tender and tasty. The steak came with very white mashed potatoes with horse radish. If it had been for me I would have found it too strong in flavour, but Gus liked them and ate it all. My sister got lucky with one of the specials it being Short Ribs, something she really enjoys and did so here. Her potatoes too were of the horse radish flavoured and they were a bit much for her and did not eat most of them. I had the Fettuccini Pescatore which had scallops, shrimp and lobster in a parmesan cream sauce which turned out a bit more loose than I had expected but was very good none the less. So yes we all enjoyed our dinners and this is one of the few times in the last couple of years where we went for a birthday dinner and it actually turned out well, so Thanks.

Oh and the service was very friendly if not a bit disjointed.

Whew....my wife me I shared the fried plate, choosing shrimp and catfish, with green beans (instead of fries). About half of the shrimp had shells, and the catfish had an after taste. Just before we asked for Boxes to take the fish home (why? I dunno!), the waitress took the remaining four potatoes away. We could've packed those small potatoes in our little blue boxes. Maybe that's it: we were sharing instead gorging and not spending the normal amount to make the waitress happy?
I cannot recommend this place.
Overall, we were disappointed and are not planning to return.

Tattered menus, unintentionally funny service, and some pretty fine Vietnamese cuisine...

All of this just mere feet away from the Asian food paradise known as Lee Lee Supermarket.  In fact, Thuan Kieu has an adjoining door that enters the premise of the market.  Anyway back to the review.  For me, the place is a hoot.  But I think accidentally so.  Allow me to break it down.  

First off, let's discuss the menu.  The menus, at one point in time, looked like one you'd find at a nice, sit-down restaurant.  However, the menus here appeared to have been through the last two world wars, with a stint in a kindergarten classroom, and then forgotten in a jean pocket in the washing machine.  This will be the first time I'm using this expression on an inanimate object, but the menus are truly torn up from the floor up.  

Appearances aside, the contents of the menu are very extensive.  It may very well be longer than the Book of Genesis.   Everything you could desire for in Vietnamese food probably is on the menu.  That includes the traditional noodle soup, pho, the vermicelli noodle dish, bun, and other rice dishes, com tam.  The latter is what takes up the vast majority of the menu.  My personal favorite choice is their charbroiled beef, simple yet executed so well.  

As for the service, I'm not going to knock it, but it isn't exactly what you'd expect in an Applebee's or TGIF sense.  To illustrate this better, allow me to impart a story for a minute.  It was my very first visit to Thuan Kieu, just days after it's and Lee Lee's grand opening, on a Saturday afternoon, and the place was jam packed.  I was by myself and was quickly seated at a table for four.  

Perhaps two or three minutes later,  another patron was seated at my table.  No big deal, I've shared tables with strangers before.  I opted for a noodle soup, but not pho as it wasn't available then as it is now.  It was brought out mere minutes after I had ordered, impressive given that the place was rocking with customers.  Well, I came to surmise later that it was brought to me by mistake.  

How did I come to that conclusion?  The staff pointing to me and looking and sounding exasperated gave it away.  In fact, the entire staff the whole time I was there looked and sounded like they belonged on a pit crew during an Indy 500 race.  On other, less chaotic nights I've visited, the staff always seemed a bit harried.  The place does offer a wide selection of drinks that have to be made by hand, including boba smoothies or shakes.  Those suckers literally consume several minutes of one server's time.  Each.  By the way, I've never sampled the boba drinks, but they do seem popular.

The service at Thuan Kieu can be characterized as quintessentially Asian.  You're not going to get that smiling, back-slapping, 20 questions kind of server.  Like I said, Applebee's this ain't.  No, more times than not, if you want something here, you best be prepared to flag someone down for it.  On my last visit, I had to catch a server's attention three distinct and separate times; twice for refills and once for the check.  That's how it is in pretty much all of the Chinese restaurants I've been to where the Chinese language can actually be heard.  

With all of this said, the service friendly and helpful enough.  The owner is an extremely cool dude.  I came in one night just before closing for a to-go order, and the owner was kind enough to offer me a can of Coke.  Just for having to wait for my food.  I don't think anyone at Applebee's would even care to fart my way if I had to endure a wait for their crappy food.  

The end this epic review. the variety of Vietnamese food here is quite extensive.  The quality, while not the best I've ever had, is perhaps the best for our little town.  The fact that it's literally connected to Lee Lee and is blocks from my house makes me want to put up with the raggedy menus and overworked waitstaff any day of the week.

I was very excited to hear about a an upscale  seafood restaurant opening. So I have to say I have a bit of a conundrum...but, I digress the atmosphere was pretty chic the wine cellar or tower is a glass encased tower next to the bar with a high lift inside pretty cool to watch. It has a loft feel to it with the exposed ducts etc. I can not really say I feel I was in an ala carte or upscale seafood restaurant as the staff was dressed in a manner which reminded me of my brother wearing dungarees in the Navy(blue jeans and what looked like a denim shirt). I was disappointed with the service, I was sitting at bar and anytime I needed something I needed to flag the staff down. I was not offered bread although it appeared everyone seated near me had a bread basket. I was not given a glass of water. I ordered the peach Manhattan is was ok nothing that makes me want to come back. So here is my conundrum the food was absolutely amazing and flavorful; I ordered a honeyed beet and peach salad, the red snapper, and the date creme brûlée. The food was excellent but, really disappointed with the service for an ala carte restaurant. I may give the service a second shot because of the quality of the food.

Delicious food, elegant venue, exceptional service and great wine selection made Stella Mares an easy choice for a special birthday celebration.  A friend who is local to the area says this is the nicest restaurant in town and I would have to agree.

The dining area is charming, replete with a fireplace, high ceilings and an abundance natural lighting.  The waiters are top notch and are attentive without pretense.  The food is amazing!!!  It is everything I desire with French cuisine: highest quality ingredients, perfect cooking technique, beautiful presentation and attention to detail.  The mussels are a MUST--cooked till just done, they are swimming in a perfectly balanced white wine and garlic sauce--perfect for sopping up with the complimentary bread.  The escargot is also phenomenal and drenched in the most vibrant pesto sauce.  I had the sole meuniere which was perfectly seared and served on a bed of fresh vegetables.  It was buttery and full flavored without being too heavy.  I also tried the salmon with beurre blanc, which was also delicious and perfectly cooked.

They have a great selection of wine and also a wonderful cocktail menu.  This is a great venue for a special occasion or date.  Parking is easy in their lot and while not always necessary, I would recommend making reservations on prime nights.

A trip to Santa Barbara is never complete without a stop at Los Agaves.  The namesake Los Agaves burrito is one of my favorite comfort dishes of all time.  It might even be my all time favorite burrito.  The burrito is stuffed to the max with succulent jumbo shrimp and chunks of halibut then topped with a savory and creamy chipotle sauce.  I love everything about this dish from the fresh ingredients to the heaping serving to the best Mexican rice EVER.

Los Agaves really specializes in elevated, fresh Mexican cuisine and I like that the menu has usual suspects like tacos and burritos, but also more rare dishes like molcajete and even salads for those who want a lighter bite.  The salsa bar is the best ever!!!! I love that it is self serve with the most selections I've ever seen.  I get a sample of every one and enjoy each with the complimentary chips.  My favorite is the avocado green sauce but they are all worth a try.

The interior is spacious and clean, and while it is an order at the counter and take your number type joint, it still feels more upscale that a casual Mexican joint.  They have a small parking lot next to the restaurant and there is some street parking as well.  Prices are average but worth every penny.

Coffee house? Gas station coffee, maybe. The wife and I are avid coffee house adventurists, and this was the most disappointing place we've been to. The vibe is slightly off and the coffee is horrible.

I think I stop in at least twice a week since this place has opened its doors.

Reminds you of Root the second you step in. Funky decor with a mad men feel and a super welcoming vibe. The staff is overly friendly and the place has an overall great vibe. 

So nice to have Stumptown in the area. The croissant I had was hands down the best one I've ever had in my life. I have no idea how they made this but it was so delicious sweet with honey and perfect crispy -- make sure to try it!

The Herb Falafel ($10) is very different and a bigger portion then you'd expect. The pickles on it were out of this world mixed with Tarator not to mention their perfectly baked pita wraps. Tried the spiced French fries as a side ($5) big portion but over priced and a LOT of seasoning but still something different and a nice addition to the side. Can't wait to come back and try the hummus platter everyone around me had. 

They are still working on the outside but it looks beautiful with a fireplace and tons of room for the springtime. It might be a little pricey so coffee shop items but the decor and atmosphere make this place top notch... can't really get anything else like this on Frankford.

A friend and I are in town for the Jay Z concert and I tell the hotel staff that I need some brunch with good food and good drinks.  The wonderful lady at the front desk told us to go to the Ruby Slipper Café, which happens to be right next door to our hotel.  I go to my trusty Yelp app and make a reservation although we were only 500 feet away from the restaurant.  We were greeted by the host that got my reservation and had a table ready for us.  We get seated and begin to review the menu the waitress suggested we try a variety of eggs Benedict that they have.  We both opted to go with the Peacemaker which lets you choose two signature eggs Benedict.  I ordered the Eggs Cochon, the Chicken St. Charles, a side of cheese grits and a Peach Bellini to make my brunch just a little better.  After my friend and I shared some stories and a drink our food came right out.  The presentation of the food had my mouth watering.  The Chicken St. Charles Benedict was a warm biscuit topped with a fried boneless chicken breast, a poached egg and a cream sauce.  My favorite of the day is the Eggs Cochon Benedict also served on a butter milk biscuit, topped with pulled pork, a poached egg and hollandaise sauce. Talk about Heaven all on one plate!!!  If you are a grits fan then you must try the grits with the pepper-jack cheese, just trust me! The food was made with love, the biscuits were moist, the chicken was season and cooked just right and the pork was slow cooked to perfection!  If you are not hungry just from that description I do not know what to tell you!!  Ruby Slipper Café turned me into a fan quick because I ended up coming back the next day for brunch.  We sat at the bar the second day and had the same great service and great food.  I highly recommend stopping into the Ruby Slipper Café for all the yummy goodness that they serve hot, seasoned and with a smile!

Update: My po' boy was not $9 as I thought, it was $6.50. 

It was still not great, and after 4 messages from Spot Burger, having my receipt creepily messaged to me - versus just sending a copy of the menu - and being asked to bump up the stars on my review -TWICE- simply bc I made a $2.50 error.......I am still sticking to my original 3 stars and seriously questioning ALL these other perfect 5 star reviews.

Literally the most delicious food ever. We had not been in quite some time and decided to grab some take out on our way home and it blew our mind how good the food is. 

We ordered a chicken pad thai, that was a bit on the sweet side, but a HUGE portion and very delicious. My husband and I fought over the last bites because it was so good. 

The chicken satay was a yummy and calorie friendly option to the pad Thai. It was also easy to feed our 3 year old with, and the sauce is perfection! 

But let me tell you, the REAL WINNER of the night was the Massaman Curry. Oh my goodness, I could like the plate with this amazing sauce. We got it with shrimp which was unfortunately were very few in the order (4 total). We were still really happy to have the sauce and just dumped all the rice in and gobbled it up. 

If you have not had a chance to check them out in a while, make sure to stop by and get some delicious curry!

In times when a cupcake is not enough for a celebration, you need to get a good steak. I came here with a low bar, considering it's a chain restaurant and looks like a log cabin. This is a long review so here are the 3 major points:

1. Get the loaded taters to share.
2. Get the Sirloin Steak
3. Skip the chili

I will also admit, I was in the crappiest mood, with a beaming headache and starving when I arrived and the place was pretty packed for a weekday, so I expected some heinous wait - but alas the food gods were with me and we were sat promptly. 

Our server noticed my nearly explosive hungry woman mood and got our table deliciously warm rolls with sweet cinnamon butter. She was also helpful in answering all my questions about steak (I am always confused with all the cuts) and suggested a 17 oz sirloin that was reasonably priced at $18. Then she kindly asked if I wanted my side of chili to be brought to me ahead of time to alleviate my growling bawls as well.

There were a million birthdays (and thus "yee haws") and my headache went from a nuisance to a full out migraine before our appetizer even arrived. But this is a chain restaurant so this is expected....

We got the loaded tators and OMG were they huge! Definitely a heart attack provoker with all the cheese and bacon they pile mile high. On a brighter note, this was the best served loaded fries I have ever seen - restaurants are usually pretty cheap with the bacon and cheese.

My chili arrived and it was also loaded mighty high, it was too much after all that cheese and bacon on the fries and the flavor wasn't that great either. This is not something I would order again.

THE BEST PART:
