The Sirloin Steak. Wow. What great flavor, nice and soft - crackling on the plate so you could tell it came running out from the grill - perfection. I order my steak well done - yes, major faux pas in a steakhouse, sorry I don't like my meat partially alive when I eat it - SOOO it's easy to mess up a good steak and get it either char-burned or dry as heck. I was pleasantly surprised what good meat came out of the kitchen considering I've been to longhorn and outbacks and usually pretty disappointed with the size, flavor and price of entrees. I had mashed potatoes that I barely touched because my taste buds were love making to that steak.

I will definitely be returning to Texas Roadhouse, especially because of the great service considering I was not the nicest person to deal with.......and I still daydream about their steak.

It should be noted that with nearly 100 reviews and an almost perfect 5 star rating, this bagel place needs no introduction. They make great bagels here and you should come on in. 

As for me, as a super bagel snob, and having being lead to a few "Meh" places, I was still skeptical. I actually came on Mother's Day after an atrocious 60- 80 minute wait time announced at my original plan. As I walked in, I knew this was a local favorite - it was tiny, PACKED and toasted bagel smell perfumed the air. If it wasn't for the line, I would have never even bothered to look up at the menu and just ordered my everything with pork roll, egg and cheese. Thankfully I had a minute to glance and I now have a new favorite! Bacon, egg, tomato on an everything bagel! Those slices of tomato make me feel less guilty about the bacon. 

As for the bagel itself, it was doughy and perfect. A good amount of everything seasoning - I hate when places overdo it. The Bagel Train also sells their cream cheese spreads and a good cup of coffee. If I lived just a few minutes closer, this could be a serious addiction. Regardless, it is great to have found a good bagel spot nearby!

Having been at the Hill school for 4 weeks, I thought the food chain started and ended with Dunkin Donuts, but thankfully I found Los Aztecas! Hidden next to a buffet in a strip mall with Walmart, this ray of sunshine will fill your soul with fresh guacamole and fresh made tortillas!

As soon as we walked in, we knew this place was going to be great bc it was a small restaurant that was family owned...since the young man behind the counter looked 16. We were fortunate enough to sit by the kitchen where orders were being given in spanish and you could hear the oil popping.

After spending a number of minutes trying to decide on the perfect entree and eating a full basket of tortilla chips smothered in salsa....I opted for the Enchiladas Aztecas. As they arrived pipping hot,topped with salsa verde, sliced avocados and sour cream drizzle....I knew they were the right choice. Right from the first bite, I knew this was one of the best Mexican meals I have had. The chicken inside the enchiladas was smothered in cheese and well seasoned. It was the perfect combination of savory and crunchy with the lettuce sliced on top. 

I sadly did not know it was BYOB, or else a few margaritas would've been the perfect ending to my meal. If ever in Pottstown, hit up the strip mall for some good grub!

This place is on regular rotation on my New Hope Brunch trips, with it's great food, cozy ambiance and BYOB-ness. If you are on a hot date, make sure to request outside seating on a beautiful warm day for extra points and added privacy. 

For entree items here are my TOP favorites:

#1 LBGT burger - is a guacamole lover's dream, unless your a vegetarian, then maybe not because of the delicious beef...and well the crispy bacon, but both those things combined with guac, might bring you to the dark side. Consider yourself warned. 

#2 Skylar's Egg Sammy - is a sandwich on a multigrain bread, with scrambled egg, avocado, cheddar and spring greens. Don't let the multigrain bread and greens fool you, this is a decadent sandwich that is super filling and will have you dreaming of it for days. 

#3 Crabcake Sandwich - When you are feeling like a baller, for $15 get a giant crabcake with cajun aioli. Just add a mimosa and who needs a yacht? 

#4 The Tohickon - consider this an early thanksgiving treat with full of turkey, cornbread stuffing, cranberry, toasted country white bread.

I also love that many of their brunch items come with a fresh selection of a bakery item, it makes me feel not so guilty about having  a chocolate croissant as a side...plus u get a little cup of fruit that always makes you feel healthy.

An added bonus is the actual story of the Cafe, which makes you fall in love a little more with it's tiny outside porch, the creative kitchen decor around and the delicious food. Parking is super crappy all over New Hope, but thankfully Cafe Blue Moose is about a block from a lot. So go visit and let me know if you loved it as much as I did!

This spot is relatively new in DTSP and I've been waiting to try it solo, since my boyfriend isn't into "healthy food". Luckily I talked him into going with me and we both LOVED it! There are about 8-10 choices for your base, two sides and your protein on top. If you don't eat meat, you can get an extra side instead of protein. We loved everything we tried and it was a TON of food! We were stuffed at the end of lunch and we'll definitely be visiting Naked Farmer again.

We ended up here for a low key bachelor party dinner. If I lived in Reno, I would probably pop in here- no doubt. Love the decor, menu selection, and the bar. 

We showed up right after 9 on a Saturday. What blew me away was that they were just closing- at 9PM on a Saturday! No way a place like this should be closing on a Sat until 11-12. But I guess I am more accustomed to places in SF.

Anyway, I will come back here. Good steak and service.

Wish I lived closer so I could try more of the unusual and mouth watering burgers.   Tasty and fresh.  The competition (for charity) for best topped fries combo is a great idea!   We had fries topped with caramelized onions and blue cheese.  Great idea and plenty to share.  Never go to a chain restaurant again if you love nearby.

the cupcakes here are definitely at least 2 servings, probably 3 each, which is good because they are like $5 each. Not only are they enormous every flavor is super rich. I don't even want to think about how much butter, sugar goes into these. They are a rich treat tho I wish they offered some lighter fare. My friends in ny ask me to bring them whenever i visit.

That said, the staff here is crap. I expect a business that opens at 9am to have product available for purchase. They seem to disagree and think they can open at 9 and then slowly put out product at like 945 or so. wtf. If i come by at 9am for a cupcake I want a damn cupcake. Don't open at 9 if you can't be ready til 10. 

Staff also has an attitude, as though they have better things to do than sell cupcakes at $5 a pop.  Its a recession people, if you have customers willing to hand over $5 for cake wrapped in paper cups, smile and say thank you.

Stop by to pick up a fabulous dinner just because we were in the area. 

Parking as always was hard to find a spot since it is nonstop busy. Once we enter the building, it see wall to wall of people chatting, smiling, and having a good time whether they are eating a meal their or planning a meal for later. 

One of my two favorite spots is the cheese room. It has every thing your heart desires for cheesy goodness. I grabbed the freshly shaved three cheese Italian blend for our salad I am making later. The fresh mozzarella is just perfect for a salad, too.

Next, we work our way to the pasta area. They have a huge selection of fresh and frozen pasta that is made in house. Today, I snatched up the frozen spinach and cheese ravioli and gnocchi. These are some of our favorites. 

Then, I snuck into the dessert pastry area for a cheese and tomato bread. I also was able to get a walnut fudge brownie without the hubby seeing. Nice surprise for him later. 

Finally, I had to restock our dipping spice seasoning. If you have not tried their dipping seasoning, you have not lived. We put it on everything like roasted potatoes, fresh cut tomatoes, and their fresh mozzarella cheese that they make in house.

Always expect this place to be a happy mad house.
Take your time and enjoy the wall to wall ideas of tastings for your immediate pleasure or enjoyment you can bring into your home later. This place is always worth the trip across the bridge.

Stopped in this morning for a breakfast date with my angel. Was in need of a coffee and grub. I ordered the cold brew coffee with cream and sugar, gluten free pumpkin donuts, spinach quiche, and apple tart. 

The cold brew was to die for and gave me my guilty pleasure with a caffeine kick. The pumpkin donuts were scrumptious and did not last long with my little. The apple tart was her favorite and gone in a blink of an eye. She said the crust was her favorite part as it was crunchy (not burnt at all), crumbly, and the perfect touch to the apples. The spinach quiche had a delicate flavor with a light, airy texture. It just melted in your mouth with goodness. 

We love coming here because of the great food and relaxing atmosphere. We highly recommend this place. If you have not tried it yet, stop on in.

After enjoying a day at the Florida Strawberry Festival, we decided to stop in for a second round of strawberry shortcake and guy fresh produce for the week.

The parking lot was packed as it seemed everyone else had the same idea as us. The line moved very quickly for the food quick service and just like the fair,the strawberry shortcake was amazing. There is seating in the back located in the beautiful garden.

We were able to fill an entire yellow shopping basket with my groceries for the week for only $30. Of course, we bought fresh strawberries. We also purchased poblano peppers, lemons, red and green tomatoes, cantaloupe, broccoli, red and russet potatoes, fresh herbs, and so much for for fabulous cooking. Love this place!

After attending an event near Curtis Hixon Park, we thought that we would finally try experiencing the Sparkman Wharf. 

We found parking at a parking garage located across the street from the Florida Aquarium and Sparkman Wharf. It was a very short walk from the parking garage to the Wharf. 

As you walk into the area, you hear the sound of a live band playing on the stage in front of the lawn. The lawn and lower area on the water had umbrellas and a variety of seating arrangements. The swings were nice. People seemed hanging as kids played. The outdoor Biergarten was busy. 

The selections of drinks and food establishments made it simple to satisfy everyone's taste in our party. If you need air conditioning, I would suggest enjoying some fun games and food within Splitsville. 

It was a relaxing and fun time at the Sparkman Wharf. We are looking forward to coming back.

After leaving Costco, I thought I would finally stop by MOD Pizza which is located in the same area as Costco. It was nice to just jump on over without worry about traffic to get a bite to eat.

I was pleasantly surprised by the setup and efficiency of this pizza restaurant. The wall had suggested pizza and salad ideas displayed and also the list of items you could choose from we're on cards. I gave a list to each of the kids so they could create their dream pizza. Best idea ever for kids! 

I ordered an 11" with white sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses, bacon, and grilled chicken. This was so good. I like the crust a lot.

One kid order the 6" with red sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses, and pepperoni. It tasted great. 

The other kid ordered the 6" with red sauce, mozzarella and Asiago cheeses, black olives, and pesto. It looked weird but tasted really good.

I am definitely coming back as it tasted great and was very affordable.

Finally had the opportunity to enjoy this fantastic restaurant. What a fun and happy environment. The hostess was happy to seat us. Our bottoms had not even fully rested and we were already greeted by our server Fitzy. He seemed to truly enjoy his job. Our drinks came out quickly and correctly. We made our order of giant pretzel with a variety
Of cheeses and mustards (highly recommend), spaetzle (German noodles) with mushroom gravy, and kartoffelpuffer (German potato pancakes) with sour cream, applesauce and added smoked salmon ( you have not lived until you have had the potato pancakes with sour cream and smoked salmon). The food came out at a decent time and correctly. It tasted good.

The environment of this place is what makes is such a wonderful experience that is worth driving from all over to enjoy. The talented man running the entertainment through patron interaction, singing, telling jokes, playing the according, and using a giant horn to play music. The staff looked as if they live where they work. Everyone was having an amazing time. This is a great place to bring the family or like we did meet up with friends to have a fun night out.

Came in for a date night out with the hubby without the kids.

The hostess greeted us as soon as we entered and was seated immediately to a both located at the front of the restaurant.

Our waitress, Abby, greeted us and took our drink orders. She was just a delight and super sweet. When she returned with our drinks, Abby took our orders for for the $14.99 three course deal. My hubby ordered salad, chicken on the Barbie with loaded potato and loaded Mac & cheese with caramel topping on his cheesecake. I ordered the potato soup, 6 oz sirloin medium rare with loaded potato and steamed broccoli with chocolate topping on my cheesecake.

Each of the course cane out quickly and correctly. Abby did a great job keeping our drinks full, clearing the table after each course, and doing it all with a smile on her face. Best customer service we have ever had at any outback and probably any restaurant we have ever attended.

When I crave BBQ I hit this place up. I always order the meat platter with chicken and pork. The platter comes with slide white bread and sides. I usually get fried okra and macaroni and cheese. My hubby got the burger with cheese and a side of fries. My platter is so big the kids pick off of it. The service was good. The menu has a pretty good variety of grilled/ BBQ items. The kids menu is good but my littles always want what I order at this place. They do offer beer and soda as drink options. 

Only three stars because the meat was dry this time. I have learned over the years as food here can be hit or miss. When it was in the little food truck on the corner just pumping out food it was always fresh and incredible. If they would go back to the roots of the original tiny but super powerful tasty food truck, this place would be rocking. I keep coming back because when the food is spot on it is mind blowing good.

My girlfriend and I had dinner and cocktails the other night....AMAZING! They have an awesome Nashville and southern draft selection!

We started out with the Row Poppers! BEST APP IN MIDTOWN! Hands down amazing! Bacon wrapped around jalapeño pimento cheese and deep fried, served with a maple glaze!

We both got Hot Chicken for dinner  and it was Nashville Authentic! They truly do an amazing job and the service was awesome, we had a very charismatic server! 

We will definitely be back again!!!

The BEST Cuban coffee in Tampa.  Period. Starbuck's got nothing on these guys.  If you are a coffee junky, order a double espresso.  I swear that the spoon almost stays put upright when you stick it in the cup held by the pure caffeine goodness in that tiny little shot glass. Be warned though - it will land in your stomach like a bomb, so definitely not for the faint of heart (or stomach).

La Bamba is a lunch joint open from 7am to 3pm weekdays. Its been open for at least 15 years that I know of personally, probably a lot longer.  They have a cafeteria line style menu with the traditional Cuban staples, such as white and yellow rice, black beans, plantains, roasted pork, ground beef, etc.  Sometimes they have specials with breaded steak covered in mozzarella and tomato sauce, or fish.  And their sandwiches are delicious. Their Cuban sandwich is good (not the best in Tampa, but not bad).  My personal favorite is the breaded steak sandwich. Yes, you read that right. They take a steak, they put breading on it, fry it, and put it between two pieces of fresh Cuban bread.  Add cheese, grilled onions, and press it on their toaster, and you have sandwich Nirvana.  

Breakfast has their world famous (my world at least) Cuban cheese toast.  Order it with extra cheese and order a cafe con leche with sugar.  Dunk the toast in the coffee.  Rinse, chew, and repeat.  Weight Watchers cries at the sight of this overdose of cheese and sugar.  And don't get me started on the bacon, egg, and cheese Cuban sandwich. Yum.

The place is nice and clean although not a chain restaurant by any means. It gets packed for lunch and I take clients and out of town guests for a taste of the local Tampa flavor.  In over 15 years not one has walked out of there disappointed.  Now that I've lost 90 pounds I'm adding La Bamba back to my regular rotation.  Not too regular lest I put all those pounds back.  But a breaded steak Cuban sandwich once in a while is good for the soul.

Well, I got to try Texas de Brazil.  For those unfamiliar with the concept, basically you have waiters walking around with 3 foot long skewers with all sorts of meat hot off the grill, filling your plate until you explode.  That's the short version.

TdB is my favorite restaurant of all time.  I had driven to Orlando and Miami just to have dinner there, since Tampa did not use to have one.  A while back Boizao opened, which is the same concept, so I stopped traveling 3-4 hours because Boizao was "good enough".  So in this review I can't help but compare the two.

There are subtle differences in the bread, the beans, and the side dishes.  TdB has shrimp and salmon and lobster bisque in their buffet, while Boizao had mostly veggies.  Boizao had Swiss and cheddar cheese, TdB has fried provolone.  Boizao has roasted garlic cloves, TdB does not.

Meat wise they are very similar, although I have to say the filet mignon at TdB was outstanding, the best I've ever had.  Both restaurants have a variety of meats, such as bacon wrapped filet, Parmesan crusted pork, sausage, chicken, lamb, flank steak, and the list goes on.  Along with the buffet and the never ending procession of meat skewers they also provide mashed potatoes, fried bananas, and cheese bread.  The bananas are supposed to be to "cleanse" your palate between meats, but I gorged on them as they were coated with cinnamon sugar.  And the cheese bread should be classified as a controlled substance.  It is addictive!

Price wise they are similar.  Expect to pay $50-60 per person with drinks, dessert, tip, and tax.  TdB is running a $79 per couple special which includes soft drink, dessert, and a bottle of wine.  Boizao, not to be outdone, came out with a 50% off coupon.  It only applies to th entrees, but a decent discount nonetheless.

So which one is better?  I have to declare a draw.  I love both of them, and will have to go back to both (often) to see if I can find a winner.  How in the world will I fit this "research" into my Weight Watchers plan? Lots of exercise... :)

They have peanuts!  Just like Logan's.  

So I saw a post on Yelp Talk about this place. I had been here several times years ago, but for some reason we never came back.  Don't remember why.  I don't think it was anything bad.  It just didn't impress me enough to add it to my standard rotation. 

So, we came back.  The place looks nice. I mean, not in a Charley's kind of nice (meaning fancy) but clean and well organized.  Think a notch less fancy than Red Lobster with lighter colors.  They brought us free peanuts, but you can't throw the shells on the floor.  

We ordered the Jack Daniels Buffalo Shrimp appetizer but subbed chicken for the shrimp.  If you are expecting the dark, sweet Jack Daniels sauce from TGI Fridays, you will be disappointed.  It's more buffalo sauce than Jack Daniels, and a bit spicy.  I liked it, but remain puzzled by the Jack Daniels reference in the menu.  I took a picture and posted it.  The portion size was very generous for an appetizer. 

My wife ordered pasta primavera and I ordered the grilled seafood combo platter, which consisted of grilled tilapia and grilled shrimp.  I posted pics. Both plates were outstanding!  Very large portions, very good taste.  The grilled shrimp seem to have a very light glaze that is not overbearing, and the grilled taste comes through.  All in all, both the Mrs. and I were very happy with our dinners. 

Service was competent and the prices were good.  Key ingredients to a pleasant dining experience.  I'm a seafood fan, so I will definitely be coming back to try some of the other menu choices.  So for know I will declare myself a fan and shall return.

OK, I was extremely excited to try this place when I moved to the area.  I came with my young daughter and we were eying the croissants.  I then noticed something dark and tiny go by-- a fruit fly!  I looked again and I saw a whole swarm of them!  I told the man behind the counter (possibly the owner)  and he dismissed them by saying, "it's just fruit flies."  My daughter really wanted the Gruyere and prosciutto croissant, so I asked them for a specific one that I didn't see flies on, and I asked them to reheat it.  I have to say that the croissant was unbelievably good, but I was still grossed out by the fruit flies.  

I came back to this place a few months later with my daughter,  wanting the same croissant.  What did I see again??? Yes, fruit flies all over the cupcakes and croissants.  I walked out of there without buying anything.  Please, fix your bug problem!  Until then, I'll steer clear of this bakery.

Tried this place out on Taco Tuesday! Their TT deal is $2 street tacos and 50% off other tacos and $2 off lobster tacos. I got the steak ($2.75), Grilled chicken ($2), and Salsa Verde ($2). The steak was cooked medium well so it was pretty juicy and the flavor was standard. I liked that there wasn't a pepper taste or seasoning to take away from the steak taste. The grilled chicken was a really good healthy option and the salsa verde was marinated very well. I'd have to say my favorite was the steak, but I am a little biased because I love steak. Came with a group of 12 so service was a little slow (being seated, food coming out), but understandably because the party was large.

I Love the Mayan mocha, creamy chocolate goodness. The location is cute, walking/biking area, outdoor seating. No congestion, easy parking.  The menu looks appealing, makes me want to try something different every time I visit. I do hit the bike trails near the area and yelp guided me to this perfect spot for my coffee fix.  On my trips heading north I will make this a must stop for sure.

Solid steakhouse in the heart of center city. Barmen consistently demonstrate their knowledge of building pleasure through flavor. The mastery at the broiler and grill will not disappoint you. The room's two-story ceiling brings memories of grand days gone by, once a bank lobby? So cool. 

BAR
Liquor list features many local Pennsylvania brands, and if you're daring, ask your barman to make you one that takes you off the beaten path!
Mine was my simple sapphire martini ($20), in and out, twist, stirred. Excellent. 

SERVICE
Tuxedoed servers and staff are the norm, and the formal style of service is the standard at steakhouses like this across the nation. 

AMBIENCE
Dishwasher station is busy and loud. The "plate clanking" and pot banging volume is quite high, as is the symphonic buzz of kitchen printers heralding your order in concert. It would make a marvelous background-noise track, "busy restaurant"! I'd certainly buy it for my Apple TV!

Music tracks overhead are a mix of big band and fast trio jazz, accented by bursts of trumpet and scatty Singers. 

But my favorite is the discreet sculpture of a bull's head with horns, mounted at the center of the far wall. Ha!

THE COURSE
Tonight's oysters ($19)  were huge, creamy samples from Maryland, and some delightful briny ones from Massachusetts. 
The mignonette was wonderfully chunky at the bottom, not the watery vinegar with "floaty bits" one usually gets elsewhere. Great flavor. 
And the horseradish was freshly shaved, airy, and dare I say, light? also a special treat.  

The 8oz filet mignon ($46), "black and blue" arrived perfectly hard-hard-broiled and then raw and cold in the center. 
Not that charcoal shoe-leather black you get from the chef to punish you for ordering "well done", just perfectly done. Bravo!
The warm plate brought up the temp so it was cool instead of cold as I made my way through it, Wow!
I added some finishing salt to each bite, and realized this is truly the way to enjoy a steak. This size. This way.  
The delectable mushrooms and onions ($12) side was the perfect accompaniment. 

Finishing sweetly was a delightful baked pear sorbet ($9) and Calvados ($20) digestif. 

BUT THE BUGS
Special flying insect friends were companions tonight, interested in  beverages, the butter and bread and more. They only swarmed every five minutes or so, but Shucks!
Honestly with more "pre

BOBBLING ALONG
On a more personal note, with my E-badge not renewed for '22 after 13 in a row and 14 in the community, I must admit some relief that I can now review more casually, tell more of a personal story, and without the pressure that "mine will appear before others, so I had _better_ be "just the facts ma'am" concise,  do it right, and not waste your time with rambling!l" 
Now I know that these will disappear into the babbling swath of bobbleheads, never to be noticed, well, except for you followers and dear friends from so very many years together!! 
Let me know if you line this more narrative casual style better.

Brasserie on the grand scale (300+ seats (?) including Covid-encroached street lanes beyond the sidewalk) stretches its kitchen and bar well beyond their facilities and ability to execute.

PUSHING LIMITS
This spot was already pushing limits before Covid. Two host stands, one inside, one out to manage the horde of guests. (Actually, I liked this arrangement; otherwise, there's a cram of people waiting inside and glaring at you if you happen to have one of the tables near the front door)
So many places created outdoor dining to survive, but now that inside dining is allowed, all those extra seats are still in play. Except that kitchen, bar, host, and the rest are not designed for so many seats!
Don't get me wrong, I'm all about recouping losses incurred over the last year, especially as restaurants try to deal with the tsunami of pent-up consumer demand. But this is not fair to the professionals who already were stretched thin running twice the distance to outdoor tables, managing auxiliary prep areas in alleys and corners, and the massive crush for ingredients amidst dwindling supply!

HIT AND MISS
** Steak Tartare. Always a win here. Pre-mixed (ultimately for speed of prep i think), the blend is a nice balance of sweet and savory. Toast points warm and crispy.
* Cheese Omelette. HUGE. But very well prepared and not rushed. Books have been written about the proper treatment of eggs, mine is about oh-so-gently bringing them up to texture. This one will fill you up for sure. And your choice of cheese is a hot-pack inside. MMmmm.
# Pamplemousse cocktail. Tonight's was just a sour mess, starting to taste off. Is it a pre-mix, poured on demand? "Slush" of fruit sat at bottom. Had it sat on the bar for 8 minutes? Maybe.
## Seafood platter. Always a hit-and-miss. One or more of the selections will be _off_, as in going rancid. I have never had a successful platter here. Really. You should be ashamed of yourselves.

AMBIANCE
In a word, Intense. Warm lighting gives a retro vibe that might take you to your memories of France. This place is HUGE. Two large dining rooms, tables at the front door, tables along the sidewalk, and now two massive street-built table rows, one on each side of the restaurant.

RESERVATIONS
Are absolutely necessary. They're on opentable, and resy.

Apologies to the plain clothes security man I hassled. While I understand that you were just doing your job, I feel that you exercised extremely poor judgement when you stopped me as I exited the store in the wee hours of the morning. Not that I don't look like a criminal, but on this early morn my bag was laden with legitimately purchased food items. I also wanted to thank you for making me go back into the store to empty out the entire contents of my bag, even after I presented you with my receipt. 

That about sums up my shopping experience.

Liked your college dorm experience so much and don't wanna lose that vibe when you move up on in to the real world?

Have I got a place for you!?!

It's called the Piazza at Schmidt's.

Dude, what's happening on the Quad today?
I hope something really ultra bitchin'.

After reading the reviews of local restaurants while visiting the area for the weekend my wife and I were excited to try the food at Trattoria Mollie however we weren't even able to make it that far...

We were in the area about an hour before they opened for dinner service and (based on the reviews about the food) decided to wait for a table. After waiting outside for half an hour a couple walked up and a staff member unlocked/opened the door for them, sat them, and took their drink orders (all of this 30 minutes prior to their official open time).  When I walked up to her to see if we could be seated as well, my wife and I were told that the other couple was "an exception to their rules" and that if we wanted a table we would have to wait outside the additional half hour as there was no one ready to take care of us.  Before we could even ask why would couldn't just sit down with a glass of water and wait for the kitchen to open, she turned around and walked away. She didn't try to accommodate us at all let alone apologize for the inconvenience.

At that point we felt completely disregarded. It was as if we didn't even matter to them. When we go out to dinner we love to have the full experience; a nice staff, a good bottle of wine, appetizers, deserts, ports, etc. We both have experience in the food service industry and were shocked that this sort of discrimination had happened to us.

Such a pity, we would have loved to taste the food but unfortunately we will not be coming back.

It's always great to get an educational lesson when having a meal with family. Tonight, I learned from the owner/manager, Assad Khoury, that Kuzina was "not like other restaurants",  and that  I should know that it was normal for the food of my party to take over an hour.

An apology for a late arrival of food was of course unnecessary , I should have known better Of course, no apology was received, either by our waitress, who disappeared during this long period, or from Mr. Assad. My father requested that he had roasted potatoes instead of french fries, and of course, his meal arrived with french fries. When he requested that the fries be replaced, he was granted the honor of being served with a heaping portion of three potato wedge quarters.

I had no complaints about the food we received, in fact, it was pretty good when we finally got it. Maybe the restaurant was purposely starving us so that our palate would be intensified.

I made it a point to take out my calculator and give the waitress her 18% to the penny, contrary to my usual 20-30 percent gratuity. 

Assad, may I call you Assad? I thank you for the education tonight, and if you should be open to it, I'd like to return the favor. Your attitude tonight truly had an effect on our family, as we will never eat in your establishment again. I truly hope that you don't treat your employees the way you treat your paying customers, because they don't deserve it, and neither do we.

Oh, I'm from Maryland, and my family lives in Cherry Hill, so you are definitely losing multiple visits.

I'm going to go back to those other prompt, friendly types of restaurants,  and may suggest that you find a field that is not customer facing.

The reviews here are funny. Seriously a 3 star average? Ya'll are Yelp Elites too.. Don't fuck it up for small businesses!! 

Anyway with that out of the way, decor is nice, place is clean, service is friendly (not that I care, to be honest, it's not that I prefer rude servers either, it's just that I come for the food and beer, whatever). Place has free wifi I think but probably password protected. Didn't ask, didn't care, have TMO (T-Mobile) and it's fast at least in this part of Boise.

Food is bar food, it's good though. Lots of TVs. Good beer selection.

Plenty of parking outside, and there's a movie theater too with plenty of walking opportunities. It's not Boise Downtown, but for this part of Boise, it's alright. 

Not much else to say.

I really wanted to like this place but I could not. The food is good/decent. The staff were rude. The concept is more of a novelty than a better way of eating.

The good food was the fried chicken, banana pudding, and pork chops. Decent food was stuffing, green beans, and bread. The non-desirable food was the coleslaw and broccoli salad.

I felt as if the staff was rude. It was difficult to find someone to ask for refills of certain food. The staff started clearing our plates before we were even done.

The highlights of coming here is that you get to eat at an old manor, and you have family style seating. Pretty nice for a party of 10 to eat at one table and pass food around. This makes since to do at home but no sense for everyone to pay $16/person and do this at a restaurant. You do not get to have all the food you want and you are forced to eat food that no one really wants. 

I will not come back.

I was visiting friends in Nashville and my nose was stuffed up because of the cold weather. My friend suggested hot food could clear my nasal passages. I asked, "Where can we get some really good hot food?" The smile on his face was priceless...................

This is some very good chicken! The sides are also amazing!

I ordered the large dark meat with two sides. The sides are baked beans and mac n cheese. Both sides are simply amazing. The mac n cheese had the perfect consistency and the baked beans tasted amazing. I wish I could have the sides delivered.

To review the chicken, I got one piece "Hot" and the other piece "Shut the Cluck Up". The Hot was seasoned perfectly and had a great blend of spice and flavor. The Shut the Cluck Up cleared my nasal passages some but was more heat than flavor.

I will return

This place has some of the worst customer service I have ever experienced. It is not that the waiters here are horrible. It just looks like they are permanently under staffed. All night, this one waiter was running around trying to service everyone. 

This place has some very good food specials and drink specials. I was able to order a 64oz pitcher for a very good price. They have a ton of beer on tap. I heard that the cocktails are very strong also.

My friends ordered wings, steak, and burgers and they all thought the food was good.

It took a long time to get any of the TVs changed to the correct sporting event, get refills, or even get our food.

By far our favorite restaurants on the Hill!  Every time we have come here with groups of adults, family or just a couple we have a wonderful experience. 

The service here is probably what I like best. These are professionals who have worked here for some time. They know how to provide service without interfering with your meal. Very European and a welcome relief from most of today's over the top attention. Ask them about anything on the menu (or off the menu) and they will be able to assist. 

Appetizers are all really good. My new favorite is the carmelized cauliflower.  Everyone in our large group was impressed and it disappeared. Even my brother in law who hates veggies liked it. The toasted ravioli are a must as well. Hand made on site they blow away the other frozen product in the area. Also get the frito misto, not too heavily breaded and oily but just right to be crunchy outside and chewy inside. Also the flash fried spinach it's served on is worth the price alone. Don't let that delicacy go to waste. 

For entrees i have had 
- lasagna: wonderful and not the typical junk dish on most menus. It is with it just to get one to share for the table.
- risotto: you can't go wrong with any of their variations. Crab, lobster, combo, they all are perfect. 
- osso buco is phenomenal. If you are a meat lover this is a must. 
- chicken caneloni are great. Wonderful mix of vibrant marinara and cream sauce to sweeten it up. 
Specials: gnocchi (if on the menu get it!  Hand made and delicious) squid ink pasta (always one of my favorites)

For dessert get the tiramisu. Strong coffee taste with just the right amount of custard to sweeten it up. The creme brûlée is definitely a solid option as well. 

To top it off we find their wine list very intriguing and well priced. Who doesn't want wine to go with their pasta!
Nashville has some great restaurants but this has been one of the highlight restaurants of our trip so far. Fresh creative food. Great atmosphere especially on the bar patio. Exemplary service!

Slay the Beast and Receive $500! The Pointersaurus is a 28" two meat or four vegetable topped pizza that weighs over 10 pounds! It is one of the world's largest delivered pizzas! The Largest, Fastest, and Most Delicious Dinosaur in History! 
Contest Rules: 
Two people must consumer the ENTIRE pizza in ONE HOUR without leaving the customer area at Pointer's
The pizza must have any combination of TWO meat toppings or FOUR vegetable toppings
ALL crusts and toppings must be swallowed ENTIRELY for the contest to be ruled complete
Competitors must pay $50 in advance. In the event of winning the contest, the $50 will be refunded along with a check for $500
A maximum of SIX spectators are allowed in the customer area at any given time, and must stay out of the competition area
Contestants must call at least ONE DAY in advance for reservations to try the challenge, preferred to be at 3pm any day of the week. Any derivations are at the manager's discretion.
Napkins may not be used to absorb pizza juices.
Promotion and photographs of your success may be used by Pointer's Delivery.

We attempted to complete the Pointersaurus, with FOUR people and still could not complete the challenge.. The last team to do this was 4 years ago. Pizza was decent, tons of toppings but quite doughy. I'm an IMO's fan when visiting St Louis but had to try this challenge out!

The Hurricane used to be one of my favorite places to come have a drink, some grouper, and watch the sun set. After today, I will not be coming back.. Front Hostess and Bartender were not friendly or inviting. I do not remember remember this type of rude behavior at all in the past! I then took my friends to the top deck to see the Sunset but we only had one drink and then called it a day. How embarrassing.. It is my notion that you want to keep patrons at your bar and greet them. I guess not. We ended up having dinner in Downtown St Pete because with the service on the bottom and top floors, I cannot imagine it could be any better in their restaurant. They better get their act together if they want to keep their establishment going.. I thought this was a famous spot in St Pete Beach?

Late night munchies? This is the place to go in St Pete. We ordered take out from Toby's and were very satisfied. Our ordered consisted of his Large "Meat" Pizza including Pepperoni, Bacon, Meatball, Sausage, Ham, and Extra Cheese, Garlic Knots, and a Chef Salad w/ Lettuce, Tomato, Provolone, and Ham. This meal fed 5 Adults due to the Pizza toppings and appetizers. For under $30? I would say this was a great deal! Restaurant was clean and inviting but wasn't there for more than 5 minutes. Next time I would like to try their famous subs or philly steaks.

One of my new favorite spots in the Tampa. From their Disney garden to Ponds with fish to their restaurant, this venue caters to all different groups of people. We came in on a weekday afternoon where almost the entire outside patio was to ourselves. Beautiful views on the water and you could take a nap out on their lawn chairs. The scenery is enough for you to drop in and pay them a visit! We ordered beer and cocktails only this time around. Look forward to ordering from their dinner menu as their kitchen smelled of grilled meats and veggies when passing by. Staff were very friendly, attentive, and never kept us waiting for our next drink. If you are into happy hour patios or nice views while you watch the sunset, this place should be on your list in Tampa!

Came in on a weeknight and had a great experience! Our server Kelsey was outstanding and would come back again when she is working. We ordered the Volcano Shrimp, Conch Fritters, Fried Oysters, and local brews. During their Sunset Happy Hour (Monday-Friday, 3-6pm), select appetizers are $5 and Domestic beer $3. Yuengling is a part of this deal! Everything was fresh and delicious. Our table was dockside, giving us the perfect view of the boats coming in and the Sun mirroring off the water. I HIGHLY recommend coming in here if you want a Caribbean/Florida feel with good seafood, low prices, and fantastic service.

I'm sad to write this review. I've been to Zinc many times, and their food is great. In fact, in an area like Medford, where there's not that many great brunchy options, Zinc is always packed and sometimes hard to get into.. which is why I called to make a Mother's Day reservation 2 months in advance. We were planning to have a large group. My husband's parents are local, and my parents were coming from the shore with my brother and his girlfriend. It was unclear whether my brother in law and his girlfriend were going to come (their schedules can be somewhat unreliable), so I made the reservation for the 4 parents, me and my husband, my brother and his girlfriend - 8 people total. I was told that there was availability at 11:30 for my group, which was perfect, since a number of us would be coming from the shore.. so we needed time to get up and out. 

A week before Mother's Day, my brother in law told his parents he was planning to come without his girlfriend. I called Zinc and spoke to Robin, who I was told is co-owner with her husband who is the executive chef, and confirmed that the reservation was at 11:30am, and that it would be okay to add one person but no more. 

Two days before Mother's day, I get a call from Zinc confirming my reservation for 9 people at 10AM... and I pause. 10AM?? so I said - "well, yes we have a reservation for 9 people but it was for 11:30am, we would never have taken 10am since a number of us are driving from the shore that morning." A very terrified sounding hostess said "you're going to need to talk to our manager, Robin." And here is where the transaction went straight downhill. Robin got on the phone, already angry. She said "I spoke to you earlier this week and already confirmed your party and you can't make any more changes!!" And I calmly replied that the issue was the time - that now I was being told my large party reservation was for a completely different time. Robin didn't care. Robin had her own agenda, her own difficult schedule to deal with - and her tone made it clear that it didn't matter what I said, there were no apologies, no acknowledgements that perhaps someone there had made a mistake, no customer service whatsoever. It was topped off by the fact that now, all 9 of us had nowhere to go just two days before Mother's Day. 

I called my mother to explain the situation to her - and she also called Robin, who proceeded to yell at her as well. Even my mother had to say to Robin - "it's okay to make a mistake, and it's okay to be frustrated, but you are in the customer service industry and it's not okay to talk to people like this." 

It's a shame, because the food is tasty, but an attitude like that will be the inevitable downfall of any establishment. And well, we won't be back.

I'm not sure what all the hype is here. The experience that I read about and saw in other yelper's reviews is not what we got at all. We came here for the charbroiled oysters. Only about half of them were edible. 3 of the dozen were all shell and no oyster. Horrible. The crawfish pies were undercooked and underwhelming. The crawfish spinach artichoke dip was ok. The gumbo was ok. By the time appetizers came out I still hadn't gotten my Diet Coke and had to ask for it again. Keep in mind also everything came out super slow too. There was plenty of time to get the Diet Coke to the table. Next we ordered the pasta jambalaya. This was a horrible idea... it was like chef boyardee from a can. It was soupy and just not good at all. Again when I go look at the pictures of the same dish mine looked completely different. The experience here was pretty miserable. I'll skip Mr. Ed's on future trips to NOLA. I feel like we wasted 100 bucks here. The only enjoyable thing about this place was the new guy busing tables. It was his 3rd day and he was happy to be there. We had a short conversation and I think he should be promoted to general manager. He cares and wants to do a great job while providing excellent service.

If you are looking to taste rum, learn about it and tour the distillery then I'd definitely recommend stopping here. It's kinda off the beaten path and it wasn't crowded both times I've been in here. An Uber ride from the French Quarter area is definitely worth it and inexpensive. The tour was very educational and interesting. The tastings were smooth. One thing that stands out to me and makes this place unique is the gingeroo and other ready made cocktails they bottle and sell. All the ones I tasted were delicious! Our recent visit we picked up a bottle of special edition 1718 tricentennial blend and it was also smooth.

A 1-star review flying in the face of all these 4s and 5s, what could possibly be my beef?

Well, it wasn't the food (that was decent) and it wasn't the waitstaff (they were friendly and accommodating). Carman, however, UNBELIEVABLY rude.

I recently went for my first outing, based on the recommendation of a friend. It was early Sunday afternoon, the place is tiny, & I hadn't called ahead, so I was okay with the 40 or so minute wait. Went for a stroll around the block and was seated soon after returning. The waiter introduced himself, asked for our names, and welcomed us once we sat down.

So far, so good, right?

The place is tiny, I mentioned that right? It's relevant because that meant that our table was literally within arm's reach of the kitchen. That becomes an issue in a moment.

While finishing our brunch, my companion & I both slowed down the rate at which we were eating but were by no means stopped & loitering. However, it seems we were not eating fast enough for Carman, as she actually leaned over and says to us...

"If you're not eating, leave, there are people waiting for that table."

Thinking back, I wish I'd had a retort ready to throw back but was awestruck by the sheer disrespect she was showing two paying customers.

I don't know what your problem is, Carman, maybe daddy didn't hug you enough growing up or you watched Seinfeld's "Soup Nazi" episode one too many times, but you don't have to worry about me occupying one of your precious tables ever again.

I'm never going back. And I'll be telling everyone I know the same.

This was the worst restaurant experience I have ever had. The service was terrible, the food was cold and not what we expected. I was mortified that we invited friends to join us for dinner there. The owner was rude and his son was drunk and obnoxious. We ordered cannolis to see if the dessert was better than the food and the owners son grabbed them from our table and proceeded to hand them out to the tables around us. It was utterly the worst experience ever and we will never go back. We noticed how they were also treating other patrons at the restaurant and it was a miserable night for most. We have travelled and eaten all around the world and could not believe how terrible this experience was.

I just arrived to Philly from Chicago and was looking for a great Greek restaurant in the area. Yelp you came through again. This place is great. I had the Gyro sandwich and wow! The salad that came with it was fresh and the lamb/beef was cooked to perfection. Not greasy and full of flavor. The food was so good I ate there two nights in a row. Next time I'm in Philly, I will be coming back.

Before I get into the details, let's get to the bottom line here: This was one of THE best seafood meals I have ever had....

Let's talk about the ambience. You walk into a perfectly lighted space, not too light not too dark. There must be a lumen rating for that but I don't know it. But these people are right on it. As for the look and feel - It has a kind of upscale, trendy, reclaimed warehouse vibe going on. Open, but intimate. Engaging and mysterious. 

Nice bar area for waiting with friends with friendly and knowledgeable bar staff (They knew how to make a Boulevardier - few people do). 

Once you make it to the table you meet the first of several servers that function as a kind of "service team" with one person at the Lead. For us that was Marlon - as in Brando - except our guy was cooler. Professional, attentive, knowledgeable and just smooth. 

And then it was ON. And everything after that was a culinary home run. Hot biscuits/scones that were lightly crisp on the outside and fluffy inside with the slightest hint of sweetness to them - these showed up almost instantly. Water and cocktails next. I tried a house specialty - "Redemption" - nice and complex. 

For the appetizer we had the Crispy Porkbelly with "compressed pineapple" and a little slaw - it was everything you would expect from the name. After that the mains: Wild Redfish on a bed of sweet potato and corn and - for me - Parmesan Crusted Sheepshead on a bed of asparagus with crispy capers and crabmeat. On the side was a generous serving of Shaved and Roasted Brussels Sprouts. 

HOLY CRAP THAT WAS GOOD....All of it. Simply delicious. I would have licked my plate but I was told that there would be severe consequences for doing so. 

In my heart I licked the plate anyway. Twice. 

Seriously - what a meal, what a combination of flavors and textures, and all blended together in a subtle under-stated sort of way that let the different flavors all get a shot at the limelight with nobody stealing the show. 

To finish it off there was a Chocolate Mousse Bombe and an Espresso Martini....

Culinary Perfection from start to finish. Impeccable service. Wonderful ambience.

I haven't written a review in a while and I can't think of a more perfect place to get me back into it. This place is godly. 

I've been waiting to try Humble Bagel for a while. Now that I'm at Tulane, it's conveniently in my neighborhood. The people who work here are friendly, funny and inviting. The bagel itself is way better than even the reviews cracked it up to be. The only bagel I've had that comes close to this quality is a place called Zuckers in New York. 

Did I mention I'm from New York? 

Not only was the bagel sizeable, delicious and crunchy but the lox itself was of amazing quality. I will be back here every Monday morning to do some reading with my bagel.

This place is my staple and has been for years. It's on a beautiful, mystical spot on St Charles where you can see the houses and street cars go by. Their outdoor seating is very spacious and their indoor seating is intimate. They don't have WiFi readily available to customers but if you have a personal hotspot, you can plug in to the outlets they have around. Drinks wise you can't go wrong. They have the wisest selection of wines but you might not get there because they have everything you'd ever want (red, white, sparkling white, still rose, sparkling rose) for $5 all the time and housemade frose for $8. They also have cocktails for the non wine drinkers (who?) you'd wanna bring. 

Their food is as much of a draw. Most people love their goose fat fries with aioli. Their mussels are said to be great and my husband loves the lamb burger. My best friend always gets the steak bruschetta and I always get the cheese plate. They have a wide selection of cheeses that come with the most amazing bread, spiced nuts and apples. You check off the cheese you want on the menu they give you with a marker. 


This is my home spot in New Orleans. Definitely a must see if you're in town or live here.

I tried to give this restaurant another chance yet STILL I am VERY DISAPPOINTED...I paid $33 dollars for burnt zucchini sticks, smashed mozzarella sticks that look microwaved out of a BOX, 1 chicken tender CUT into 5 small pieces w/a side of fries and a piece of cheesecake.....NEVER AGAIN!! COMPLETE RIP OFF!!

This used to be one of my favorite breakfast eateries till we ran into a minor incident where they messed up one of the orders. Now normally, this wouldn't be a problem, but the owner angrily took it back to the kitchen and it came back exactly the same and then lectured my wife on how disrespectful she was. My wife's been working in the kitchen in the food service industry for over fifteen years, so I don't think she was being rude or disrespectful, and she certainly knows what's reasonable. If something is missing in a burrito, it's a pretty simple remedy to put that thing in a burrito. The owner comped the meal without saying anything, which was appreciated, but the owner's seething anger at merely being asked to fix something was absolutely shocking to witness.

So, I'd love to come back here with the family every couple of weeks like we used to, but now the mere mention of the place's name will launch my wife into a tirade about how if she ever let anything out of her kitchen like that and didn't fix it when asked, she'd be out of a job.

An apology and a little less attitude would have gone a long way, instead, I am stuck being unable to return to one of my favorite restaurants unless I want to eat by myself. Maybe the owners of this restaurant should consider that just because its a family business and you can't get fired, doesn't mean you're any more perfect than anyone else in the restaurant business.

The food here is just ok, definitely overrated. We started with the frog leg appetizer which wasn't bad. We had the salmon which was "meh" at best  (Barbacoa's salmon is much better) and we finished with the flourless chocolate cake which tasted the same as everywhere else that serves it.  Overall, we weren't impressed and won't be back. Thankfully, there are other restaurants in the TV to get a good meal.  I'd recommend Crave for its upbeat atmosphere and delicious food and drink. You'll thank me later.

If Heaven had a market I strongly believe that market would be Mazarros. Also, if I lived closer I'm almost certain I would weigh 800 lbs. The food and products they stock are on another level, one that I'm certainly not used to. What a delight it was for me to be introduced to this culinary haven. I have mixed feelings and am hesitant about sharing its greatness to you, as it doesn't need anymore foot traffic ;) 

I pretty much loathe food shopping as necessity however a trip to Mazarros makes me one happy chubby chick :) When I enter I'm transported to this market of sublime goods. 

From prepared food to fresh produce and killer made to order sandwiches and the most enticing of deserts, it's always a challenge for me to not want to buy one of everything. There is a produce area, a refrigerated prepared foods section, a cheese and wine room, a separate deli and bakery area, and a goods section filled with virtually any type of specialty item you could want. Out back past the bakery/there exists a covered patio seating area to consume what you order or what you can't wait to consume for when you get home. 

Check out this special spot for yourself. I don't think you will be disappointed.

Alessi Bakery is a mainstay in the south/west Tampa area. For over 100 years, Alessi's has been providing quality local products to those looking for bakery items. 

The selection alone is something to experience. Alessi's boasts a hot food area including made to order sandwiches and meals, deviled crab and empanadas as well as refrigerated sandwiches and salads. 

There is a room to the left of the hot food area to sit and enjoy your meal (if time permits) so you don't necessarily have to take it and go. This room was renovated and added on a few years back. 

Their cake selection is something to see, with meticulously decorated cakes in an array of colors and flavors. I also marvel at the individual cakes, tortes, tarts, and pastry whenever I am there. Alessi's takes orders for specialty cakes for events and some of their creations are displayed on top of he cold case in the middle of the store. 

The scachatta is yummy and a great for groups; I have bought many scachattas in the past while either hosting or contributing to a meal for a party or event. I have not seen this type of cold pizza available anywhere else in the Tampa area. 

I also like the selection of pastries and cookies offered. I adore the rainbow cookies and almond crescents. There is also a cold case with items like fudgy brownies and flan. There are BOGO offers every week (usually displayed on their marquee sign) so be sure to look out for those. 

On the times that I have been, the staff is lively and helpful. Be sure to check out this longstanding Tampa gem. 

Side note: I love that Alessi's branched out and packages their own products for retail, such as their salt and pepper shakers, pinenuts, ladyfinger cookies, etc. I always enjoy seeing their products in sale at stores or see their salt and pepper shakers on the tables and restaurants. In addition, I think it's awesome that the retail stores support local business.

When looking for a night out with the girls or special someone Ciro's comes through with a great atmosphere. The speakeasy concept requires you to call for a daily password which you furnish at the wooden door for entry, even if you book a reservation online through Open Table. Ciro's is located at the base of the Bayshore Royale Condominium complex and parking is strictly valet, as the parking lot only offers resident parking. There is virtually no other parking available aside from the minimal on street parking outside of the assisted living place across the street but your best and most reliable bet is the valet parking. 

Staying true to the style and trends of the prohibition era which is celebrated and imitated at Ciro's, the eclectic and innovative cocktail menu offers drinks devoid of vodka. More recently the cocktail menu has been updated in booklet form (which I particularly like) to include new craft cocktail offerings and organizes them according to the type of liquor used. I have been here several times ranging from quiet date night to large group birthday party. Half of the bar/lounge area is a booth which lines the right half and has two tables. There are also four high top tables and about 13-14 bar stools which line the "L" shaped bar. There are six more private, intimate booths in the back of the restaurant which are decorated with curtains to separate the booth from the rest of the establishment, keeping it more intimate and private. The back booth has walls with mirrors and can probably accommodate up to 8 guests. I would highly recommend making a reservation depending on your purposes for going out, as if you walk up for the bar there might be available seating. Once I called for a reservation for three as I took my mom and my sister who were in town visiting and they gave us a high top table by the fish tank. 

I enjoy coming here for happy hour, weekdays from 5-7pm, as they have drink specials for $7, select apps for $8 including their delectable Gruyere cheese fondue with apples/pears/bread accompaniment, and $3 bar bites such as truffle popcorn and duck fat fries and deviled eggs. I enjoy sitting at the bar and Bobby is a knowledgeable and gracious bartender. The other servers I have had are also very attentive and amiable. Thank you, Ciro's, for being a gem in the South Tampa restaurant scene.

This place is the spot if you're looking to break a fast or have really built up a tremendous appetite. A friendly word of advice: you might not want to go on a date here if you're not already in an established relationship and lack willpower--you don't want to scare a potential away with your gluttony. Lol. 

In all seriousness, Texas de Brazil serves up some pretty nice fare. There is an enormous and varied salad/sides bar and a great diverse selection of meat. I love the salad bar and indulge in a bit of lobster bisque when I'm there despite it not being very lobster-y (ok, it's not at all). Brazilian cheese bread is served before the meal and bananas (?) with cinnamon sugar coating are given as well as an accompaniment. One of my favorites from the salad bar is the grilled carpaccio pineapple-deeeeelicious!

I have been here on a date and in a group to celebrate a dear friends' birthday and found the restaurant suitable for both types of occasions. I enjoy the variety and customizable aspect of the food. The grilled meats sure are tasty. You can have as much or as little as you like, just be sure to flip your round card over to green if you'd like more meat or red if you want to stop the skewers from coming over to your table. I favor the leaner cuts and am partial to the lamb and beef. 

I recommend getting on the email list for specials (I believe there is still a birthday deal) or complimentary dessert offers.

Don't save the Drama for your mama!!!

I went to Drama Burger for the third time this afternoon to try the Berlin special burger (featured during March 2016). I like to try specials at restaurants and Drama Burger rolls out a new one each month. The burger was delectable and a whopper of a size--I shared. I enjoyed the combination of topping: lettuce, mixed greens and arugula, fried Emmental cheese, housemade pickles, TWO burger patties, bacon, housemade BBQ and chipotle aioli on a brioche bun. WoWza, how many calories did I just gladly consume?! 

The Lithuanian breadsticks were excellent (like nothing I've ever had before) and the accompanying blue cheese dip was great (even better than the time I'd had it previously). 

Joshua was a most attentive and friendly server. He was quick and informative and very helpful. Service was on point. 

If burgers are your thing (and even if they're not like they aren't mine) I think you'd appreciate this place so check it out and support a little slice of Lithuania in Tampa!

Indian in Ybor? Awesome! This restaurant fills the void left by an elsewhere popular pizza chain. At first I was sad to see the pizza place go, and felt the space was very fitting for that venture, but then I learned what a great fit Rasoi is for the space! I love sitting outside on the cute patio with my loved ones (furry dogter included). 

This review is based off my experiences for lunch and their offerings. I have been to Rasoi several times for lunch (as a new mom I do not make it out at night anymore). We have always encountered a fresh lunch buffet as in the components were cooked that morning (yes, I can tell). There was also a medley of sauces and fruit available at the buffet as well. Additionally, other items selected from the menu were made to order. In our experience service has been great and the restaurant is clean. We enjoy the atmosphere at Rasoi and the service we receive. The food is very flavorful and I have never tasted anything I didn't like. While the food may not be served "Indian hot" spice level, several of the dishes are hot in their own right. I am a huge fan of their vegetarian offerings, specifically the lentils and malai kofta!! 

We will continue to patronize Rasoi. If you haven't been, you should check it out!

Driving home from the beach we literally passed this little gem. I had always wanted to try this restaurant after moving to Tampa so we stopped in for a late lunch rather than go to our already planned spot and I'm very glad that we did! 

Where can you get delectable and varied vegan and ASIAN cuisine without having to wonder if meat products are in your food? This restaurant is on the smallish side but welcoming...it seems that the building housed a Pizza Hut or something of the like back in the day. There are tables and a buffet area which is only offered once a month currently (?). Our server was friendly, helpful, and efficient in taking our order and filling our drink glasses. 

Although we were tempted to get the hot pot which looked phenomenal (an order was visible on a nearby table), we decided to sample a bahn mi sandwich (sans mayo which they offer), a bowl of congee, a durian smoothie, and a three bean pudding. There was very little wait time for food.  The bahn mi was constructed on a perfectly light with crispy exterior French bread. The taste was wonderful. The congee, although not the prettiest esthetically, was very delectable and had good flavor (albeit perhaps a tad sweet)? The durian smoothie was out of this world. I've never seen such an offering on a menu and my dining companion sprang to order it. The flavor was rich and like nothing I've ever had before. The three bean pudding was tasty and something different, served in a parfait glass. The ice chunks on top were a bit different than what I am used to but ultimately worked well with the dish. The flavor combination was unique and delicious. 

After eating the culinary delights offered here we were full and feeling great. I can't wait to try more items on the menu as well as go back for the vegan buffet which is offered this month on Saturday, January 16th. The prices are reasonable and I think the food is fresh and of high quality. 

I'm so glad that this restaurant exists. Thank you for making fresh and flavorful healthy non-meat options for those with preferences and/or dietary restrictions.

Delicious. All of it. Go here, you will not be disappointed. 

This restaurant is situated a block from the beach. Parking on premises is not available to my knowledge but that does not deter people from getting some delectable eats here. That should be a clear indication of how good it is. 

I have had the pleasure of having both brunch and lunch here and have savored my selections. On my most recent trip (in the fall--ehh its been awhile) I took one of my best friends and her love here while they were visiting the area. I had my little one in tow and the staff was more than accommodating to find us a great location to sit at and was attentive with our needs. They even accommodated my not-so-little stroller in the front of the restaurant while we dined! There is a nice little patio out front for al fresco dining and the interior is relatively small yet inviting and comfortable. 

On this particular visit I devoured the Seared Tuna Salad. Each component was perfectly prepared and the veggies were fresh. My friends, although seafood eaters themselves, were in the mood for burgers and once eaten exclaimed that they were the best they have had in recent memory. They loved them and were impressed. I have never had a bad seafood menu item here but its also great to know that they do burgers really well also. 

TDLR: When at Clear Sky Cafe my experience is always sunny. Check it out, I think you will be pleasantly surprised.

Psomi is a GORGEOUS new bakery/cafe ("rooted in a Greek foundation") that just opened in North Hyde Park Tampa today, Nov. 4th. The concept melds Greek and American aspects while including influences from other cultural cuisines as well. "Psomi" literally means "bread" in the Greek language and this bakery/cafe offers much more than that. Being Greek American myself I appreciate the concept and design of the space.  

The space was literally stunning! The owner did a complete and extensive rehab/remodel and the old building was completely overhauled. The new space looked like something you might see in Greece quite literally. It is very beautiful and aesthetically pleasing! I cannot wait to dine here but for my first visit today I took some items to go after ordering at the cafe counter. There are baked goods for purchase as well as locally roasted Bandit Coffee (St. Pete). There is also full service available as a dining in option where you can sit in the indoor lit outdoor dining areas. 

The staff I encountered today were incredibly amiable and welcoming. I enjoyed seeing their menu items although today I only had time for drop in service. I have not tried some items I bought but I must tell you the "spanakopita" was excellent, fresh and flavorful. I liked how the spinach, cheese, and onion filling was nestled in a croissant vessel of sorts which was lightly sprinkled with sesame seeds. The delicate pastry really complimented the delicious filling. I cannot wait to dig into my tyropita which is a more traditional example of tiropita you would find commonly...a cut square of a mixture of cheeses housed between layers of phyllo dough. 

To some the price point may seem somewhat high however you are paying for great quality ingredients. I am all for paying more when this is the case. Psomi proudly uses local sourced and organic foods "to their fullest abilities" and the meats are antibiotic and hormone free. In addition, the breads and baked goods are made fresh daily! Check out the menu and give it a try yourself!

Parking is found on the side and in the rear of the building as well as parking on the street.

Enjoy!

James Joyce is a cool Irish spot in Ybor City. I like the authentic pub feel and the selection of food and drink that's offered. 

There are theme and food specials nightly during the week (check Facebook for postings) which are displayed in the back on a blackboard as well as shot specials daily on the chalkboard in the bar area. 

The ambiance is nice, mellow and cozy. This is the type of place you can go and feel comfortable in groups or one-on-one. Not pretentious and welcoming atmosphere and staff make this a great place. On my visits here the service has been consistently great. 

A group of us very much enjoyed our time on trivia night. If this is your scene, grab some friends and/or family and head out there for some fun. The appetizers are tasty and my friends rave about the burgers. I had he opportunity of visiting when they had the ME lobster special (RIP) which is no longer but they have replaced it with a very southern-themed crawfish boil. 

There is a small parking area on the premises but 2 hour parking on close nearby streets to utilize.

Fulfilling my desire to dress nice and celebrate the end of yet another week we selected Haven as our posh spot of choice. We thoroughly enjoyed our trip to Haven this past Friday for happy hour (5-7pm Mon.-Fri.) Lauren, out most attentive, personable, and knowledgeable bartender/server definitely enhanced our experience. John, also a bartender, was also quite helpful and checked in on us. 

The restaurant has tastefully been redone and has modernized decor. There is a lovely lounge area as well as perhaps the largest bar I have seen at a restaurant. There is also outdoor covered patio seating for you to enjoy the lovely Florida weather. 

We sampled some craft cocktails and beer. The wines on the happy hour, as I was told, are some of those that are on the regular wine list. My friend delighted in the fact that they offered Louis Barnard Cotes-du-Rhone as a happy hour wine selection.

As a restaurant with a revolving menu (every few weeks), we were informed that the happy hour specials change weekly or close to weekly and that the staff only finds out about it day of (as we asked how we could know about changes). 

We chose the cheese and charcuterie selection, the elk skewers, boudin balls as well as the oysters with a Thai mignonette. The cheeses and charcuterie were quite excellent and the server who brought out the cheese and charcuterie explained what each selection was when we were presented with it. The board came with an abundance of thinly sliced baguette bread to utilize which was appreciated by my dining companion. The boudin balls were tasty and the oysters with the accompanying "Thai" style mignonette were excellent, fresh, and had a complex flavorful burst coming from the mignonette. They were like nothing I had had before. The elk was really something out of this world. A bit hesitant to try at first because of its elusiveness on restaurant menus, I'm very glad we tried this delectable appetizer. We enjoyed it so much we had two plates. The awesome chef Courtney Orwig  brought our several of our food plates and we had the opportunity to chat with him. He was personable and passionate about his craft which I love.

Overall the ambiance and the service was impeccable. This is a nice place for date night or when you want an evening out with friends or want a great culinary experience. Thank you, Haven and staff, for delivering a lovely and memorable dining experience.

If you appreciate good, inventive culinary creations and atmosphere then Rooster & Till is where you need to be. Rooster & the Till delivers an upscale modern yet somewhat casual dining experience. The dining area is classy yet chic and I very much enjoy the open kitchen concept and the rectangular bar. On my most recent visits I have sat at the bar twice and I enjoyed watching the chefs and cooks prepare the menu items. 

Parking can be found at a lot adjacent and on the side street next to the strip of store where it is located.

It is refreshing to have a restaurant of this caliber in Seminole Heights. The preparations of food items leave nothing to be desired. The flavor and food combinations are unique and inventive. The staff on my visits have been very attentive and knowledgable about the menu, offering information and suggestions. While being energetic and dynamic, it is a treat to watch the chefs prepare the food from the open kitchen area. 

Do not skip out on dessert. The innovative concoctions of the pastry chef are delightful and unlike anything you have had before. The deserts we had were an intense flavor explosion in my mouth. 

Check this place out for a fun date night or meet up with friends.

Stopped in here with family for brunch during MDW. It wasn't as busy as we expected but it was a pleasant surprise to find they had a Jazz band there.

We sat in what I'd describe as the main room and our waiter was friendly. Two of us ordered frittatas and another the waffle.

The frittatas were huge and came with tasty home fries. The waffle was a little smaller and actually came with real vanilla ice cream on top. 

We also had a side of bacon which was actually perfectly crispy. 

Everyone seemed to enjoy the dishes and the band was great. We left full and happy. 
I'd love to come back for dinner or another meal!

My boyfriend took me here for dinner for the first time and we had a nice meal on Sunday night. The place became very busy just after we arrived so while we may have been fine without one, I was glad we had a reservation. 

The restaurant has romantic lighting with candles on each table and has a classy feel while also still a cute neighborhood atmosphere. It can be hard to hear when the tables are all full and the music was a little loud for my taste. 

Our waitress was very nice and although she seemed somewhat flustered from the busy tables she did not rush us. 

We started with the olive oil tasting which has 3 olive oils and comes with bread. The olive oils were fine but nothing spectacular. I'm sure they have complimentary bread and we'll likely just have that next time. 

We shared the following as well: 

Rucola Tuscan thin crust pizza was delicious 5/5

The Pappardelle with wild boar ragú was soooooo good 5/5

The Roasted Brussels sprouts were so disappointing, I like mine a little crispy but these tasted like they had been drowned in olive oil with no seasoning or flavor 2/5 

We also each had cocktails which were good but I'll likely have wine in the future instead. 

Overall a nice spot for date night or drinks with friends as they have a large bar area!

Why do people eat here?

We had decided to do a Geno's vs. Pat's tasting after a concert. However, the signs around Geno's about no outside food, and condiments being only for Geno's customers, lead me to believe there is some sort of cheesesteak civil war going on here so we decided against it.

Also maybe it was the way this one guy kept hanging out the window watching us, and asking how the food was, that I never made it across the street to Pat's. It's pretty intimidating actually.

About the cheesesteak, We got the one with the cheese whiz. I can't believe I wasted $10 and about 15 minutes trying to chew this god awful sandwich. I could have done better with Steakums and a loaf of stale french bread. The meat is so fatty and fibrous, MY GUMS ARE ACTUALLY INFLAMED, the next day. I have never chewed so hard in my life. Beef jerky feels like it's softer than a feather filled pillow compared to this. The bread was not exactly pillow soft either. This is not a place to go if you have TMJ, dentures or bridgework.

The only thing entertaining about the night was all the pics of celebrities with Geno and that apparently one employee's parole officer came by to check on him (actually a friendly conversation). Honestly, I would have thrown that sandwich in the trash in the first two minutes but that dude kept watching us so to me polite I just sat there eating gristle while people watching. Never again.

Tried Pinto Thong last night because of their strong Yelp rating & it certainly didn't disappoint. I have one suggestion for them, get a website, use Yelp or your Facebook page & post your menu, please!!! I've been in the area for 18 years, I'm a restaurant professional, and I want nothing more than for this place to succeed. 

The food was excellent, it's a much needed change of pace for this area. I don't do chains or fast food, so it's about time we're treated to the fresh, clean flavors of Thailand! Curry was excellent, as was the Crispy Duck Pad Thai. I haven't had crispy duck forever & this duck was excellent! I can't forget their apps & Thai fried rice. Couldn't have been happier! Also grabbed a menu for the next time! 

I really hope ownership takes my advice and publishes a menu somewhere online. The pictures on Facebook don't do them any justice. Remember, I want this place to really do well & stick around for a long time! Inside of the restaurant is very clean & cozy, it's definitely a destination point & worth the drive!

This was going to be a 5 star review until I had the butterscotch pie. More on that later. I visited Goody Goody midweek at 8:45pm thinking it might be slower at this time of the day. Wrong! The place was jam-packed. The hostess said it would be at least an hour wait but if a seat became available at the bar, it is first come, first serve. I spotted an open seat but lo and behold, it was already taken by someone who had stepped away.
