Well after five minutes of waiting, a lovely woman gave up her seat for me as she was just waiting for a table to open up to sit with her family. Lucky me!  

Took a quick glance at the menu knowing I already wanted to try their POX cheeseburger. (POX standing for pickles, onions, x for their secret sauce) and a side of fries. While waiting for my food, I chatted it up with the patron next to me, who is a long time Tampanian, about the history of Goody Goody and other eateries.  About 20 minutes later, my food arrived. Not bad considering how busy they were. 

I loved the burger, although it was on the small side. Juicy, some may say greasy. Soft bun, tasty sauce. Right amount of pickles and onions so they're not overpowering. I could've had two but it was late at night and I wanted to save room for dessert. The fries were also very good. Not too salty. Fresh and very hot. Just the way I like them. 

The butterscotch pie was disappointing. I'm not going to lie. It was excessively sweet and this is coming from someone with a sweet tooth. It is not something I can recommend at this point unfortunately. Perhaps, try one of their other pies (apple, banana cream, coconut cream) which may be less sweet. 

Given how bustling it was, service was fine. Prices are decent. Burger,fries and two butterscotch pies (bought one for the lady for her kind gesture) was $15 after tax. Decor is really nice. Love how much detail went into the whole restaurant. I'm sure I'll visit regularly and hopefully can bump it up to five stars.

Cool place brought to you by the Ciccio Restaurant Group! I ordered a charcoal/matcha swirl soft serve. Where else can you get that in these parts? Nowhere. Perfect texture and flavor and easy on the wallet at around 4 bones. In addition, they have smoothies and acai bowls.I didn't even bother with that part of the menu as I already knew what I wanted going in. 

Aside from that, it was fully staffed and my server was nice. One of the owners was also there earning his keep. To top it off, there are picnic tables outside, a ping pong table, a garden with a silkie chicken and a bunny. Unsure if those are secret menu items.

When I first read last year that Drama Burger, a Lithuanian gourmet burger joint, chose Tampa as their first US location, I was pretty excited! Their pictures on their Facebook page looked awesome!! So I happened to notice their Open Now signage today and stopped in.  I was given the rundown on the menu by a lovely Lithuanian and her equally friendly employees and opted for the double BBQ burger. Hot, tasty and juicy!  At about $13 (no fries), it's their priciest burger but they do have cheaper options. In addition to angus burgers, they also have a chicken burger, salmon burger, portobello burgers, lamb burger, chorizo burger, pastrami sandwich, salads, etc.  Very diverse menu!  Even the drinks and desserts are intriguing. I got a ginger caraway lemonade but I'm looking forward to trying a blueberry shake. For dessert, I got the creme brulee topped with freeze dried strawberries. Excellent! They also gave me samples of red velvet cake with ice cream and their "chocolate salami" (like a brownie with biscotti bits in it). Both great!! You can't go wrong with any of the desserts. Aside from the great food and service, the restaurant has a cool vibe with sofas and other comfortable seating. Great addition to Tampa!

Caffeine is a cool,new coffee shop located downtown across from the Element apartments on the north side (between the bike shop and the cigar lounge). I've stopped by a couple times since they first opened about ten days ago. The first time I stopped in, they weren't even officially open. Their doors were open and they were still getting things ready. But they were so gracious to offer anyone who came in a free coffee. Not only that but even more generous with their time as they talked to me for an hour or two over their origins, how they came from Lithuania (one of the owners also is co-owners of Drama Burger) where they own a very successful coffee chain in Europe called Coffee Inn. They seem to have a unique approach and are very excited to enter Tampa's growing coffee market. They partnered up with Zeal Coffee Roasters out of Land O Lakes. I liked what the owner told me about how they chose Zeal as their roaster because they wanted to grow together with them as they are also in their beginning stage.   

Stopped by again last week for an after work pick-me-up. I ordered a cold brew which hit the spot, although it wasn't perfect because I had to add the milk and sugar myself and I can never seem to get the right taste. It always seems to be better when I have a barista take care of that for me. Guess I won't be quitting my day job anytime soon to become a barista!  Next time though I want to try the cold drip, which is stronger than a cold brew.  Brewed in a similar way but the "cold brew" is a little more diluted. Or maybe I'll get the iced creme brulee, which sounds tasty.  

The ambience is very hip with comfortable seating, free WiFi, conducive to working and studying, even pet friendly!  They offer some snacks, including the chocolate rocky dessert from Drama. As of now,they have two tea options (see tip). The menu is still a work in progress as they are assimilating into Tampa to see what the demands are. The owners were very receptive to my thoughts and suggestions so I'm sure if you express what you like, they will try to accommodate you. The customer service here is great. It's been a real pleasure talking to them and I'm excited to see how they evolve.

UPDATE: try the Aero Cappuccino (iced) - frothy, creamy, very flavorful

Sweet Buns Bakery and Cafe opened up yesterday in the Fowler Ave plaza where Grain and Berry and Chicken Salad Chick is. I had been following their progress since the beginning of the year so I was anxious to try them out. 

The Chinese bakery, owned by Yummy House, also has a location in Gainesville. It is similar to Sweet Hut, a popular Chinese bakery chain in Atlanta. You grab a tray and tongs, and select from a variety of freshly baked items, sweet and savory. The prices are around $2-5 for each item. I tried a few (see photos) and they were all tasty. So many items to choose from so I'm sure I'll visit often. Only wish they had boba or a greater selection of drinks. They do have coffee and tea, as well as some other drinks in a cooler.

Plenty of seating and staff to assist. Nice, clean atmosphere. Definitely a welcomed addition to the Tampa foodie scene. Hope they expand to South Tampa at some point.

Happened upon Don Rigatoni while considering ordering through UberEats. Come to find out, it was their official opening day so I decided to go there in person instead to check them out. Such a cozy little place! Very nicely decorated. Unfortunately, they are take-out only due to their permit. However, they do have a couple tables outside. Inside, they have comfortable seating and a TV for your viewing pleasure while you wait for your meal.

The friendly owner explained the menu, their back story and concept. First, you choose the type of pasta, which is made in-house, then choose one of their many homemade sauces, then choose any accompaniment (see menu photo). There's an infinite amount of combinations! This isn't your average takeout food...this is gourmet Italian brought to you by the people behind La Casa della Pasta in Carrollwood. 

I ordered the gnocchi with principessa sauce (princess/pink sauce) and meatballs (includes a mini loaf of bread). I was very impressed. The meatballs are some of the best I've had. I'll definitely be a frequent customer as I often drive by on my way home from work. Looking forward to exploring more of the menu and I'll update my review accordingly with other recommendations. Yelp out this new hidden gem!

Snobachi is the latest addition to Ybor and the third? shop in the Tampa area which makes ice cream rolls. They're located right next to Shrimp and Co and have their own parking lot, plus street parking. 

I got frozen yogurt as my base, with a coconut syrup, caramel and bananas mixed in. Flavor was fine but they really need to tighten up their presentation. Both of the workers were a little sloppy with that. Rolls should be tighter so that they don't have to be forced into the cup. Though it wasn't crazy busy, it also took 25-30 min to make it, which I wouldn't usually fault a new business for but when you factor in the workers chatting with family instead of focusing on customers, that's an issue. Plus they had many workers there and three cold plates to make the ice cream but only two were being used. Perhaps they hadn't been trained yet on how to make them. 
As far as the atmosphere, the decor was nice and adequate seating, though it is very dark and there was no A/C. A light and bright atmosphere works best for an ice cream shop I think. Easy fixes though.

I'll give 3 stars, leaning more heavily on flavor and texture than the other issues.

Second visit: Flavor was weird, not anything like hazelnut that I ordered. Place is dirty, vibe is terrible, hate the lighting. Where did they find the employees?? Not exactly ice cream shop material. At least they were much quicker than first visit.

Not the best first impression, but I wouldn't completely rule out a return visit. Overall, I thought it was pricey for what it was. Maybe it was an off night? Maybe I didn't pick the best items as an accurate representation of what they can do? I'm not entirely sure.

I accept full responsibility for this oversight and won't let it sway my stars, but I wanted to mention that I'd searched for Breaded Pork Tenderloin Sandwich and this had been a suggestion. Unfortunately, it's not a regular menu item. The server did confirm that they've had it before as a special but it seems to be offered sporadically. Honestly, that's the main reason I'd stopped here and it's hard to say if we'd have come otherwise since there was another restaurant closer to where we were staying.

I looked over the menu and went with the Grilled Chicken Salad. My husband got the Half Pound Bison Burger and added cheese. I also ordered a Black Pear Cider that was featured on the wall. The drink was the standout, unfortunately.

The grilled chicken was dry and the vinaigrette served with it was very bitter. I came around to it the more I ate it, but it wasn't an immediately enjoyable salad and not something I'd go for again. It wasn't an almost $10 salad, in my opinion. I think it's going to be an acquired taste. They have 4 other salads available that seem like they might be a safer bet.

The burger was good, but it's truly just a burger on a bun with some basic veggies for nearly $14. It's an additional $1 to add cheese. If a burger is going to be more than $10 then I want it to wow me. I'll allow a +$2 difference for a specialty burger, like bison. But the flavor's gotta be there to justify it. This didn't do it for us.

Our server was OK. She answered a few questions, took our order, brought the food and ran my card after the bill was dropped off. I can't recall if she asked us how everything was. We were in and out pretty quickly. I didn't find it very welcoming as a dinner spot, but I'm not opposed to returning to try something different.

At the very least, it seemed like it would be fine if you just come to drink and chill with some friends. They have a decent selection of their own beers and "OPB (Other Peoples Beer)" guests' on tap and in bottles.

Come here on an empty stomach and you will definitely be leaving chicken full! Ordered take out and tried the rule-breaker: Chicken was great and went well with the jumbo shrimp. My bf ordered the chicken club sandwich which was also amazing for a great lunch.. spared half of it for leftovers. Garlic Parmesan fries are loaded with cheese but wish I tasted some more of the garlic. I've also tried their bulgogi cheesesteak on a separate occasion and it's definitely my favorite from their menu thus far.

Everything was delicious even if they sweeten up their food for the American palate which is typical of most Thai places.  Their flavors are excellent.  We had ginger beef, green curry tofu and ginger tea.  All were seasoned nicely but a little too sweet for me.

This just became our favorite nice restaurant in the Reno area.  The place is trendy and cool. Place is hard to find as it's upstairs in a corner complex. Service, ambience and food is great here.
Had $26 galbi ribs and it was plenty.  Wife had the black.cod with miso and it was excellent and the best she has had since Roy's in Hawaii.  Also a bargain at $26 and it was plenty of this super delicious fish.
The owner knows his food and drinks as they had my favorite beers and their menu had lots of choices that I would love to try next time.

Located near a batting cage area and limited parking .  Super fun offerings of tacos like bahn mi Vietnamese style tacos.  Grilled and battered cod tacos were great.  Outdoor seating with lots of picnic tables and noisy street next to us.  Not fancy but great lunch place to bring the wife.
One of the better fish tacos I've had!

Good food
in a
great building

Mount Holly seems to have quite a few cool old restaurants that use to be something else in a past life. The Robin's Nest is no exception. 

It doesn't look particularly special from the outside but once you get through the doors things change.  Such a cool old building, it's look walking through a portal in time.  Great Victorian décor and lots of cool old things to look at.

We had a great time just walking around and looking at all the great stuff.  Almost forgot we were there to eat.  The old house was just so cool and the great staff seemed to enjoy showing me all the unique features. 

We did eat and the food was very good.  Sure I'm easy to please but I would eat here again even if the building wasn't so cool.  Of course I would eat here again even if the food was crappy just because the building is so cool.

There is even a little patio where you can eat outside by the river.  I usually love eating outside but that river looked so nasty that inside seemed much better.

The Robin's Nest is a wonderful, quirky and unique restaurant in a wonderful, quirky and unique town.  Lots of cool and weird stuff like music and psychics occasionally show up at the restaurant but the Robin's Nest is cool enough without them.

Very pleasant and interesting staff, good food, and an incredibly cool, old building is about as good as it gets in my book.  One of my favorite restaurants that just happens to be in one of my favorite towns.

When traveling to St. Louis over the Summer there was a place that friends familiar with the city recommended as a must do. Crown Candy is a city landmark of sorts. After a visit you will see why you will in turn tell others they must go!

Don't let anyone tell you the area is too shady. It is an older neighborhood with eclectic landscapes, will leave it at that. My visit during the day was uneventful in a good way. I felt safe. At night I'm not so sure to be honest since I'm a tourist any may get lost.

Parking is all street surface on the curb. There was litter every where. A vacant lot a half block away where I parked needed mowed and had debris. The sidewalks and entry to the store for the most part tidy. I'm providing some flexibility to not be overly harsh.

Featured on numerous shows including Food Network twice. Man vs. Food for their malt challenge of five 24 ounces in 30 minutes. Adam Richman failed in the 2009 episode. He returned again in 2012 for his "Best Sandwich in America" episode featuring their Heart Stopping BLT.

Some how our group of eight got very lucky scoring two booths on a weekday afternoon around 5:30. Our female waitress was right on top of us and got waters and silverware. 

I just had to get the signature Heart Stopping BLT / thick sliced bacon, lettuce and tomato w/ Miracle Whip served on white toast w/ side of chips & pickle spear. Paired w/ a chocolate malt. Incredible!

The rest of the group got various sandwiches, shakes and malts. The kids were disappointed that there are NO BURGERS on the menu. Everyone enjoyed what they had and that included picky younger kids. The grilled cheese was a big hit. Service was strong throughout the meal. 

Founded in 1913 and in its 3rd generation of the Karandzeiff family. The restaurant operates much like it did from the very beginning. A small menu of sandwiches, malts, shakes and candy. Crown Candy is one of the oldest surviving soda fountains in the country.

I would without hesitation return and hope to be lucky enough to hear the music outside by a long time street musician. It most certainly is a St. Louis original and recommend.

So much awesome to report from a first time visit over the Summer. So my apologies for a tardy review, but it's no surprise that my rating is identical to the overall. A solid 4 Star experience. 

The downtown location is on super hip Massachusetts. It's a strange block for locating on GPS, so be ready to turn in even when there appears to be the road. Parking is by street meter. Look at the schedule because they cut off when you have to pay. 

So why McNivens, Scotch Eggs. That was the draw, I've never had them. The pub has a great Irish theme with lots of wood, a super cool bar and even live music on designated days. The space is dived up into separate rooms. Bar on one side, tables on the other. A few TV's are around. 

My friends and I took a seat at the bar and was quickly greeted by an energetic male bar keep. He provided menus after we told him we would be eating. He also went over his tap list. I quickly settled on a Three Floyd's Robert the Bruce and put in an order of Scotch Eggs to come on prior to my entree of fish n' chips that were recommended. 

The bartender chatted my group up on down time and was so friendly. My Scotch Eggs came out within 10 minutes, or so. I had no idea what to expect, they are kind of like a deviled egg is how I would best describe them. However their fried up and have an aioli dipping sauce. Scrumptious! My fish n' chips followed 10-15 minutes after. The cod was fresh, the batter crisp and tasty. The fries were adequate. Yum! 

Next time I'm in Indy I'm doing this again and will hope for live music night. Recommend checking them out.

If burgers and craft beer are your thing you will adore Engine No 9. While on vacation this was a place recommended. 

An extensive list of burgers and beer in a quaint downtown St. Petersburg setting was a perfect lunch getaway today. The dining room is 70% bar and 30% Family area with tables in the rear where I sat with four. Everything was clean including my restroom visit. 

My order the Wine-O / red wine bbq sauce, bacon aged white cheddar & fried onions. Side of tasty tots. Fabulous! Paired w/ an Orange Blossom Pilsner by Orange Blossom Brewing. The rest of the party got other burgers. All agreed quality beef and downright tasty. All the cooking temperatures were correct as well. 

Table service was friendly and attentive. My bill was accurate and quickly processed. The staff in general from my observation did a fantastic job serving their respective customers.   

My son and I had a second visit prior to leaving town which was a take-out order. The staff was asked to recommend one for me and Windy City it was. There was discussion on the peppers, but ultimately I decided it was ok as per staff the heat was not much. I cannot recall my sons order. 

Within 20 minutes our to go order was done! Bill processed ahead of time to expedite. Our hotel was 5 minutes away and the plan was to enjoy in the lobby with friends. Unfortunately the burger was way too spicy for me and was a disappointment. My son liked his however it was undercooked from a medium to medium-rare. He still ate and devoured it. 

Shout out to a good friend that was spot on the recommendation. Although the first visit was stronger than the second I'm still at a 4.5, rounding down. Would love to have them in my town.

I thoroughly enjoyed my meal at Sauce on the Side and was taken back by the 4+ composite score when I checked in. Could they really be that good I wondered. There are two area locations, but it's not chain. 

Parking is meter off street or nearby parking garage. The establishment is small, so you could easily drive by. Signage is adequate. The area in front of the store was debris free. 

The restaurant is larger than it appears as it's deep. I found the dining room and empty tables cleared and also clean. Ordering is in the back! 

Order at the counter. There are paper menus to review. The menu is simple and they really do one thing and they do it really well. A variety of calzones with salads. Soft drinks are self serve. My order was "Meet me in Saint Louis". Our party of six all got different calzones. 

We sat at a large table by the window and enjoyed the street view. We received a number for delivery to the table of our meals by staff. Food came out of the kitchen within 15 minutes or so. My meal was fantastic! It was large, hot, flavorful and the right amount. The sauce on the side was the perfect accompaniment to the calzone. The rest of the table felt the same. 6 for 6. 

I will absolutely return. 4.5 rounding up.

If you're in Nashville this is where you go for chicken. But not just any chicken, the best Nashville Hot Chicken in the area. 

Never heard of hot chicken, well I hadn't either. I researched Nashville places for lunch over a Summer visit and Hattie B's popped up with stellar reviews. I happen to be downtown where their original location was and had to try. 

Nashville is the city that invented hot chicken and Hattie B's is famous for perfecting it. When pulling up our family saw a line out the door, down the ramp and down the sidewalk...yikes! I was able to squeeze in a space on the side of the building. Parking is extremely limited around the joint. Nearby street and garage parking is available.

On a hot August day it was not exciting for the family to wait in line. The kids moaned and groaned and my wife thought I was out of my mind. After around 40 minutes we finally arrived at the door. Regulars I spoke to said the line easily gets over and hour and a half during Summer peak. 

Once inside there are menu boards. Start getting it together so the line is not held up. The staff was over the top friendly and patient. The family decided on the mild Southern. Sides of baked beans, slaw, French fries, macaroni and cheese, mash potatoes and gravy and peach cobbler. They have a few local craft beers so I decided on a Jackolope. 

The seating is pretty limited, I could not even tell you how many interior. I moved to an outdoor picnic table. The patio was clean. Food orders are called out, so if outside pay attention. We got our food in around 15 minutes. So total investment is now over an hour and the family was starved. We realized the cobbler was missing. I alerted the staff who brought it out minutes later. 

Everyone loved their chicken and sides. The chicken not surprisingly was the hero. Flavorful fresh and juicy. The Southern Chicken offered a slight hint of spiciness and a wonderful texture. The peach cobbler was fabulous! 

I had to go the distance with a full 5 STARS! This was a wonderful find and is now a great recommendation for others to try. The prices are fair, the staff super and the food marvelous. There is also merchandise for sale. Try them out, you will not regret it.

I really, really loved my visit and to go order from Casita. A local friend recommended I give them a try since I was from out of town. Unfortunately it had to be a take-out. I would have preferred eating in with such a cool space, but time did not permit it. 

The location is in an eclectic hip section of St. Pete called the Edge District. It may look a tad sketch on the periphery. I found the area I walked safe during my daytime visit. Parking is off street and free. The walk up displayed no debris. A cool picnic patio is in the front and they also have even more tables in the rear too!

The building's bright orange color is striking. The block appears to have been a gas station. I had some time to spare prior to ordering so I poked around. The dining room has a combo of booths and table and chairs. Every table not occupied was clean as was the floor. The Mexican themed decor was attractive. The restrooms are in the rear. I found the Men's room clean with proper supplies. 

So when it was my turn standing in line maybe 15 minutes. The male cashier was great with several choices he would recommend and was patient with me. Ultimately I was told what they do best are tacos. So tacos it was. 

My order, the Carnitas which has slow roasted pork salsa verde, quesco fresco, cheese and cilantro. My sons order, polo verde braised chicken topped with salsa verde quesco fresco cheese and onions and cilantro. For sides it had to be chips and salsa. 

Order was up around 20-25 minutes later checkout was easy. The staff was super and check-out flawless.

Arrived at the hotel with food and cracked it open. My son quickly reported that his Polo Verde was yum. The carnitas was also fresh and great! With some transport it could be have been warmer. The quesco paired. with chips was ridiculous yummy. 

Places like this do  exists. I loved everything about it from the beautiful interior to the exterior color and design. I would love to return and will dream about their queso.

First time at Half & Half based off local friends recommendation for brunch. 

Parking is in the rear lot, or by street. The walks out front were tidy as was the front patio. However, no chairs and tables were set out Our party was not interested in the patio anyway on a warm late August day. 

Our server was immediately attentive and remained that way throughout our service. She was very busy with a slam packed Sunday brunch crowd, so there were sometimes she was absent when refills were a bit low on water and coffee. Also initial check-in with food was a bit tardy. She however, was friendly, smiled and took care of our needs when present. 

My order the Salmon Hash / two sunny eggs, potatoes, spinach, cream, capers & hollandaise served in a hot skillet. Side of sourdough toast. Paired with a house coffee. The sourdough is a must choice out of the few varieties to choose from. A fabulous dish. Others in our party loved their meals including my sons S'mores French Toast which was huge and tasty. 

When back in St. Louis I will be returning.

I had two visits to Bella while visiting from out of town. One was a pick up order and the other a group dinner I set up for our travel swim team. 

The location is on busy and trendy Beach Street just off the waterfront in downtown St. Petersburg. Parking is by street, or nearby parking garage. Both are pay to park. On weekends know that parking will be very challenged. An option is to taxi/Uber. 

My experience with take-out was great! I called in the order, placed it and picked it up within 25 minutes. The food was hot and the checkout efficient. I would rate the spaghetti and meatballs 3.5/5. The margarita pizza 4/5. 

The second visit days later was for a group of thirty. The restaurant was very accommodating without a designated room. A text follow up was generated to confirm the reservation the day before. The business provided a 30 minute window to arrive between 8-830. 

Upon arriving I was thrilled that Bella had everything set up in a corner area by a exterior door. Waters and bread were placed on the table. It looked great! It was a perfect space to have 30. They ran two tables parallel with a path to exit the door. The kids, roughly 12 and adults roughly 18 sat in different tables. The restaurant was up front with a flat 20% gratuity on all bills. Also I confirmed a $15 fee for corkage. One misstep that I wish would have been discussed prior was the bills to be attached to parent and child. 

Two waiters a man and a woman took orders and the adults matched up who the were with at the other table. Everyone thought this method would work. A floating waiter assisted with keeping waters filled. The staff earned the extra star on the review. They constantly smiled, were patient and friendly with the kids and stayed on top of our party. 

After all orders were taken our waiter opened up the bottles of wine that myself and a friend brought in. The staff started out fantastic. With a group this large you figure there would be challenges with timing of food and its accuracy. However, to my surprise the kids table had no missteps on either. The orders were brought out first to them which was perfect! The adults waited another 20 minutes, or so with orders strung out. However, to my knowledge the orders were accurate. No one had issue as we were enjoying a leisurely dinner. 

The food was loved by the kids and I never heard of complaints from the adults. The warm crispy loaves of bread with butter resupplied once was a hit. My dish, a smoked egg plant parmesan recommended by a friend was tasty and had a gorgeous presentation. A bit of a disappointment nonetheless on a Wow factor 3.5/5. 

So at the end, approximately 1.5 into service was when the bills were requested. No one ordered dessert or coffee thank goodness. This would have added to additional confusion of the tab and parents knew it. Unfortunately this is where Brava fell apart. It took the staff around 30 minutes to generate the bills. At 10 the kids were ready to move on and we arranged a shuttle to get them back to the hotel. Some of the adults stayed back to resolve paying. Another 15 minutes passed and our paperwork was in hand. Mine had a slight inaccuracy of corkage x2 as they put a friends on mine. This was minor, everyone else had a correct tab. The biggest issue of the night was not the delay for me but the fact 20% was never placed on all the bills. Some guest believed it had and left. 

There was far too much positive to write a par review. The staff did a marvelous job overall serving a big party and the kitchen's timing although not perfect for the adults was when it counted the most for the children. The food for me was an average variety and not elevated as I hoped with prices that would have customers expect more. I would place them at a 3.5, but rounding up with an extraordinary effort for our party and strong take-out experience. The atmosphere was ideal for an end of swim meet get together. Thank you Bella.

This dive got my immediate attention when I happen to walk past and gave a yelp check to see what's up. So with no recommendation and not being on my to try list I gave it a try. The killer reviews made my mind up to get in the door and I was thrilled I did. 

Most importantly is don't worry about the appearance, it scares off some I bet. The white cinder block building with colorful birds is a bit odd, but let's just call it unique. The location is on the shoulder of the not so great St. Pete. I felt safe during the day. Parking is off street. There is a sidewalk patio with two tables. A line out the door provided an idea this place is legit. 

I waited a minute to find the line was waiting on orders and proceeded to the counter. A nice Venezuelan woman assisted me. I pleaded with her to help a poor tourist on foot and she laughed. I had no idea what to order, but wanted an arepa. After a little discussion because the line was building I decided on the #7 Bao arepa fried.  

The dining room is tiny, maybe five tables tops. A couple bar stools for the counter. The area was clean and the aroma from the kitchen and food pouring out was heavenly. The customers were a mix of young and old, White, Black, Latin. The atmosphere was lively and light. If I had not known I was in Florida I could have been in South America. All the staff was Venezuelan. 

My arepa was delivered around 15 minutes after my order. The Bao is described on the menu as Sweet & tender Asian pork, carrots, spinach, scallions, cilantro sesame & house made sauce. I did not have to take a single bite to tell you it would be marvelous. The presentation was exceptional. The first bite confirmed it was to die for. Everything worked harmoniously and exploded with flavor. The textures the taste it was all there and authentic as hell. 

There is a reason they are recognized locally as the best and on Yelp's top 50. They are masters of Venezuelan fare. The driving force behind my rare 5 stars is the incredible food. However, will add they also know customer service too! I want another one so bad right now. Closed Monday's.

As seen on DDD. This is the real deal for St. Louis soul cuisine and should be on your short list if out of town. Awesome vibe and service.

The location of the business, okay...don't worry, be happy. It's not bad, but the surrounding residential neighborhood's appearance is aged. Don't let the rough hood deter you. During the day I would have no issue of returning. But with being out of town and not knowing the area at night not so sure. Parking is by street. 

The cool old two story building added to our anticipation of opening the faded antique wooden doors in the front. A couple of tables are in front and a few more picnic tables on the right. The front entry way was clear of debris. 

Our party was immediately greeted by a hostess on a weekday around 1145 AM. A bar is up front with tables, chairs and a few booths in the rear. Wood floors, exposed brick and beautiful woodwork. Also nice artwork hanging on the walls. 

A male waiter was Johnny on the spot getting drink orders. I was with two children in their early teens that were very skeptical of soul food. Menus were placed on the table and shortly after waters out. 

Our party needed recommendations, especially the kids. Our waiter was a rock star and provided lots of ideas for the kids, mixing things up, asking questions and being very patient. It was a bit embarrassing how long it took, but the server never flinched. 

My order was a Combination Plate / burnt ends on a slice of bread, tri-tip, ribs, brisket & caramelized onion mash. Side of in-house BBQ sauce. Kicked it off with their classic appetizer smothered fries. 

The verdict. The burnt ends and brisket were home runs, the mash was off for me. Be brave if you go solo on the smothered fries. The others in my party enjoyed their dishes as well. The kids dishes worked and they enjoyed. 

The price point for lunch pushes to a high range. At the same time the quality and preparation of all the dishes made me feel at though it was worth every penny. Our waiter checked in multiple times and when time for a check was efficient. By this time there was a wait out the door. I've been told at peak service it can be over an hour. 

Loved the atmosphere, loved the food and the service was phenomenal. An extra star does go to our waiter. Unfortunately I failed to get his name to recognize in this review darn it. Would love to return and recommend. 




.

I've had a two visits to Bodega. Last Spring it was a late night with friends after drinks. I recalled I loved my dish and the bar service was fun and efficient. When moving to a table however the service was not as good thus a four star.

Bodega is known for their Cuban sandwiches and they are phenomenal! The location is in downtown and they now have a few stores, but keep in mind same owner and they are local. Parking is off street. They are touristy in that everyone recommends, so expect busy! 

I was dropped off in an uber on a Saturday night around 1045 and they were packed! The line was to the street. Seating up front is not big, a few tables were occupied. The bar had one seat that I grabbed. There is a larger area to sit in the rear. The vibe was cool with elevated music from hot rod cars and loud motor cycles. 

Service was immediate and friendly by female staff. I looked over a menu provided and ordered a café con Leche which is a Spanish beverage consisting of strong coffee and scalded milk. I adore the drink as it reminds me of days in Little Havana when I lived in Miami. Friends pulled me to a table in front for dinner so I cashed out. 

Service at the table was slow to get orders, but the young male was nice. I ordered a Lechon which is pork, black beans and plantains. Prices are fair for basically Latin street food. 

My dish arrived around 15 minutes later and was hot. The pork was plentiful and super! The beans alright. The plantains scrumptious and too few of them. The meal was a little skimpy for my appetite but nonetheless great! A prior visit I had the Cuban sandwich and it's hype!!! A must try for a first timer. I recall the spicy slaw that gets raves was a miss for me. 

I have them on my list for a return trip and you know it will be the Cuban sandwich again. 4.5 rounding down. Use a yelp check-in for a FREE Cuban coffee.

As it so happen I was in town just weeks prior to greatest spectacle in racing and the running of its 103rd race. I've not once attended a running after residing in state for two decades. However, I've been to the track multiple times for Carb Day and other events when in my teens. 

The location is in Speedway Indiana which is on the Northside of Indianapolis. Just miles from I70 and not too far from the airport. 

The track has been in the Hulman family since 1945 when purchasing it from Eddie Rickenbacker. The track was broken down and dilapidated and needed lots of money. Terre Haute native Tony Hulman resurrected the property with his wealth from the Clabber Girl product he manufactured. This Spring was a historic day in the family as ownership of Clabber Girl transferred to B&G foods. 

Just last month I reflected back on my visit to the museum a couple of years ago. It was so enjoyable for the kids, well me too! The fact I'm a Hoosier also holds sentimental value. I even got to be on the track with a tour. Check out the museum it's open year around. 

They also have a Pete Dye designed championship golf course which is open year around. It's ranked as a top 100 of Public courses. The Brickyard Crossing holds a major PGA event. 

The Indianapolis 500 is the Holy Grail of racing. It is the oldest major car racing competition in the world. I feel confident even if your not a Motörhead you would enjoy learning about the track through touring the museum. Or maybe attending a pre race day event such as Carb Day. Better yet experiencing the thrill of attending a race. One day I will attend a Indy 500.

First time at a 5 Star Burgers and I was blown away. Awesome burgers, shakes & local brews on tap.

Parking by street out front, or lot in the rear. Both areas clear of debris. The business had a front patio perfect for nice weather and people watching. 

Service by Sara was friendly and attentive for my party of three. The place has a cool vibe and comfortable atmosphere. This is a casual place, so come as you like. I also chatted up the bartender who was knowledgeable about craft beer. 

My order was The Cheeky Italian is the August Burger of the Month / Hormone and Antibiotic free Black Angus Beef, topped w/ Griddled Guanciale, buffalo mozzarella, caramelized onion, basil pesto. Side of pickles, LTO & fried pickles. Awesomeness!!! 

To drink American Brown Ale by The Civil Life Brewing Co. which was delicious. They offer 8 brews on tap. The kids chocolate shakes which they adored. 

Restrooms are located in the rear. I utilized the facility and found it so disgusting around the stool area with poop on the seat, in the bowl and paper every where. It appeared to be very recent. I alerted the staff. You can't get that out of your mind. 1 star deduction. 

Three locations in the St. Louis area. Highly recommend for a great shake, beer and burger fix.

I'm gonna toss down a 5, it's that solid of an overall operation. This location is now there highest volume store in Nashville. Expect a line. 

Arrived close to 130 to a line that moved quick. Ordering process is made quick by large menu boards visible from the door. My family of three got different items. I ordered the hot chicken sandwich with fries and peach cobbler for dessert. Prices are fair, but don't expect Chick Fil A pricing either. Tipping is up front by card. 

Dining room was packed, but we scored a table and it had already been cleaned. Sodas are self serve. They bring the food out and find you by a number system on table. Time was 15 minutes or less and everything was correct and delicious! I messed up and forgot to add ice cream to my cobbler. A staff in the area checked on us and I mentioned. Quick as a flash she came back with a scoop. WOW! 

What a fantastic operation from front to back. Solid bites and friendly staff. 5+ and absolutely recommend to everyone.

We came here for lunch on a Saturday, and it was enjoyable.  There were great beer selections, and the food was pretty good.  We ordered a bowl of Mulligatawny soup and Fish and Chips to share, and a couple beers.  I've never had Mulligatawny soup before, so I cannot attest to its authenticity, but it tasted pretty good.  It was chunky tomato based, and included ground beef and lima beans, and those simple flavors came through nicely without heavy spices.  The fish and chips was excellent!  It was fried extra crispy, and the Cod was super fresh, flavorful, and flaky.  There was no mistaking the fish was fresh, not frozen, as verified by our friendly server.  I would definitely eat here again.

CinCin is the kind of restaurant that when you're hiking the Tour du Mont Blanc, and pausing on some alp to chat with another couple you've just met, and it turns out they're from the Philly area, they'll say that they come to CinCin every Sunday night for dinner.  The place has that kind of well-deserved loyalty and reputation. 

We did a recent takeout order. If you haven't been there, they have a very good COVID compliant pickup arrangement. In fact, the riskiest thing is probably driving into and out of the fairly small parking lot. It is, however, very convenient.

We started with an order of pan fried dumplings (note, the printed menu does not specify, but these are meat dumplings), which were rated very high by a Deputy Yelper in the household. Eggplant in hot garlic sauce (not super-spicy, just right) was excellent with perfected cooked Asian eggplants. The Tofu in Black Bean sauce was a bit plain, but satisfying just the same - tofu with a fried-chewy texture, and the accompanying veggies perfectly al dente. Deputy Yelper described their Szechuan Pepper Basil Lamb as "fabulous." 

The really nice details: yes, brown rice. Also, if you want leftovers, their serving size sets you up very nicely. I'd say that the typical vegetable or poultry order ($12-$13) is really two adult servings. Some other entrees are priced a little higher, but this is a very affordable menu overall taking into account serving size. They included enough mustard, soy and duck sauce packets for small army, plus numerous teabags. Nice touch for a takeout order.  And, as you guessed, fortune cookies with some pretty funky fortunes - and not at all stale!

This was my first time at Movie Tavern and overall it was pretty good. I do agree with the other reviews that the food is like an Applebees. 

Honestly I was more excited about the Red Robin across the road than the Movie Tavern food. I had the catfish fingers for about $10 and a Blue Moon draft for $5.25. 
Next time I will just eat before I come and just drink. 

I did looovvveee being able to have a beer with the movie but the food I can pass on.  The seats are very comfortable and spacious.  The only other thing I disliked was sitting with my empty food tray in front of me for majority of the movie because our server didn't come back until he had the check. So if you are picky about service like I am, just be prepared for that. 

One tip: make sure you purchase your ticket online at least a day or two before because it gets really packed.  You can just tell them the confirmation number at the cash register and they give you the tickets.

In 2007 we stayed there for 3 days in a luxury suite with a big jacuzzi, rented a poolside cabana each day, and spent a lot of money on food and whatnot. We easily spent several thousand dollars just on the stay alone. Never mind what we brought to gamble with.

The entire stay was great. However, when we called down to checkout, they sent someone up to take our bags down to the valet area. The guy came up to the room with a luggage cart. We loaded it up ourselves. Two medium suitcases a small suitcase, and a small black Bally's duffel bag. The guy left with our bags several minutes before us. However, when we got down to the valet station we had to wait about 10 minutes for the bags to still arrive. The car was pulled up and we waited with the trunk open. The guy finally gets there with the bags and insists we get in the car and he will load them into the car. So I thanked him and tipped him. A minute later he closed the trunk and waved that it was clear to go.

When we got home, the small black Bally's duffel bag was not there. This bag just happened to be a bag containing a Sony PSP and about 30 games. At least over $1000 worth of stuff in the one bag. We called the hotel and was put through to the lost and found. I explained to them that I put the bag on the cart myself and it never made it to the trunk of my car. They took my name and number and insisted that I contact the Lost & Found. I called several times over the next few weeks explaining to them that I didn't "lose" the bag. It disappeared on it's way down from the room to the car and that it was odd that the guy who brought the bags down took 10 minutes longer than us to get down there.

Needless to say, my bag was never "Lost" nor "Found". It was stolen!! The hotel had a VERY lax attitude towards the whole situation and didn't seem to care in the least. To this day, it still puts a bad taste in my mouth to think about it. We would have gone back many times and spent thousands more if not for this incident. Sadly, we have not returned since.

If you look at the review highlights for this restaurant, they mention the fried rice, hot and sour soup, and crab rangoon. Since I've never had any of the Americanized Chinese cuisine here, none of those dishes (or anything similar) will be covered below, but I hope this review is useful for those who are interested in the authentic cuisine. Ask the servers for the Chinese menu!

My family has been looking for a delicious authentic Chinese restaurant in the Nashville area for quite some time, and I think it's safe to say that we've finally found one. Our usual dishes are the spicy beef tendon, tofu bao, fish fillet with Chinese pickled cabbage soup, stir-fried garlic pea tips, and cumin beef. They're all delectable, but I find the tofu bao, fish fillet with pickled cabbage, and pea tips to be the best - they're cooked perfectly and taste absolutely incredible.

Despite the fact that Corner Asian Cafe is quite a far drive for us, my family still takes the time to come all the way to the Brentwood area for the cuisine - it's definitely worth it, if I do say so myself. I am hoping to try the Chongqing chicken and spicy fish fillet soup sometime in the near future. :)
