Definitely WAY overrated. Also a tad over-priced. "Hipster" friendly scene though.

The wine list looked better than it was. Reminded me of the days when I first got into wine and didn't really know much other than, "there's red and there's white." And that's pretty much the wine options Tria gave; red or white (nothing special about them).

The food was EXTREMELY disappointing as well. I don't know if the chef was having an off day or what. But the food was just sloppy and not thought out. Flavors clashing evrywhere... it was upsetting.

- Roasted Beets with Bulgarian Feta Cheese: Just some beets and feta cheese thrown on a plate.
- Tuscan Three Cheese Potato Chips with Smoked Paprika Aioli: Actually doesn't come with the aioli, according to the waitress. The chips were tasty, but you only are served two chips per person.
- Gorgonzola with Fig Jam Bruschetta: Too much fig jam, not enough gorgonzola. I love fig jam too... but they slathered way too much on.
- Smoked Mozzarella, Crispy Prosciutto & Tomato Brushetta: Best dish we got. The vinaigrette on top was very good.
- Tomato Brushchetta: It looked like this dish was literally made by a young kid. The tomato was all cut WAY too big for bruschetta, making it very messy and sloppy to eat. Only good part was the vinaigrette on top.

On the plus side, we had a very prompt and friendly waitress. But I'd just skip Tria and go somewhere worth it.

Mac & Cheese: Quite yummy. Reminded me a lot of my grandmas homemade mac & cheese :) Loved the texture... Only thing I didn't really understand was the tomato jam on top. If you're one of those people who like ketchup on their mac & cheese, then this would be awesome. However I haven't had ketchup on my mac & cheese since I was a little girl; didn't care to much for the tomato jam on top, so I just scooped it off...

Pulled Pork Sandwich: The fries it came with were like McDonalds fries. ICK. The cole-slaw tasted just as gross as it looked. It seemed really old... The sandwich, however, was yummy. Typical pulled pork sandwich. Only disappointing thing about the sandwich... the leftovers were really bad :(

Our waiter was really nice and attentive. Kinda cute too :P haha.

As far as cheap, yummy food goes... Jean's is the best.

Jean's serves as a hot spot for many college students and hungry people in the Center City area. Getting fairly busy around lunch time. So make sure to get there before the rush!

As far as sandwiches go they use Boar's Head deli meats, which is the best. But I go for the breakfast sandwiches. I absolutely love them. Especially the sausage, egg, and cheese on a bagel. Making any morning (or even lunch) awesome!

Create your own Mac & Cheese?! Cool!

I really liked this idea of Misconduct Tavern's... They offer their Homemade Mac & Cheese with about 15 different ingredients you can choose from to incorporate into your Mac & Cheese. I went with tomatoes, onions, roasted garlic, portobello mushrooms, and chicken. My lunch mate just went with the sausage.

Wow, was I sure in for a treat! My dish was absolutely overflowing with yummy goodness. Chunks of mushroom and tender chicken... Nice crispy mozzarella cheese, baked on top... And a homey, light fondue sauce covering a lot elbow pasta. Definitely a very hearty meal.

My only complaint is that with the more ingredients you choose, the more inconsistent the cheesy-ness was. My lunch mate's Mac & Cheese, with just the sausage, was a lot cheesier. Mine was somewhat runny, leaving something more to be desired. I think that inconsistency is due to the larger plate of Mac & Cheese you get with the more items you want in it.

But would I come back and try their Mac again? Definitely... I might just go with 2 or 3 ingredients, instead of 5, or just try it plain! Oh and their chicken tenders have a very tasty kick to them too (the dipping sauce was awesome).

Overall our service was ok and the place was clean. A nice place to grab a bite during the blizzard!

This is my favorite gourmet grocery in the FQ. I always shop here when I visit & take a lot of stuff home. 

Fabulous wine selection. Fabulous cheese selection. And the half pork half alligator sausage y'all carry is my absolute favorite. I bought the last one while I was there, was hoping for more but it was Madi Gras & we all know what happens on Fat Tuesday in the FQ. LOL 

I also just wanted to give y'all a shout out for your impeccable, superb service. 

This past Madi Gras 2020, hubby & I bought 3 bottles of vino from you and tons of other stuff. Somehow the 3 bottles of vino did not make it in our bags. In all the chaos, this happens. 

However, after an hour or so hubby & I made it back thru all the Madi Gras chaos & you guys saved our vino for us!!! 

"Thank you again! Your honesty & integrity made our Madi Gras possible & it will never be forgotten.  

Laissez les bons temps rouler!" XOXO 

See you next time! 

Highly recommend.

This place is just ok, it's touristy. I usually don't do the touristy restaurants bc I part-time grew up in NOLA. It's a oldie but a goodie. Has a fabulous bar & I LOVE the classic vintage style bathrooms with the oyster wallpaper. 

We were actually on the waiting list next
Door at acme oyster & it was too chilly to stand in line so we ducked in here for a drinkie & to
Charge my phone. Lol 

Hubby started drinking their signature purple drink the "Jessica rabbit" first he says "it's horrible" & kept on drinking it saying it taste like cough syrup. 

I opted for the Champagne by the glass, as it was my birthday, disappointed they offer only one kind $17 a glass. It was very nice. 

We decided to try their signature oysters MP while there. They come topped with crawfish. $40 bucks a doz. 

They were good, but not as good as Acme. We then went next door to Acme & had two more dozen there :)' 

The oysters & crawfish were super fresh but slightly under seasoned. Wouldn't order them again. 

Great FQ bathroom stop. Great service. 

Too touristy for moi.

A local favorite that is always open & I mean 24 hours a day 7 days a week, even Christmas Day. 

Christmas morning, after a fun night partying Xmas eve in the Quarter, hubby & I rolled out of bed at Soniat House next door, jumped in the Jacuzzi tub then headed over to Verti Marte all refreshed & super hungry! Lol 

 I bought liquor, wine, coffees, a giant spinach salad, green beans & hubby had to have a "all that Jazz Po'boy" for the ride over to my fathers new place. 

I been coming here for years, as my family lived here for years. I was lucky enough to be born here. 

The French Quarter has tons of good eats in little corner groceries. This place is in my top 2. 
I love this place bc they do have excellent food & have the best hours. Their dirty rice, Mac & cheese, chicken parma & all that jazz po'boy rules. 

My other favorite, Quarter Grocery & deli, isn't open on Christmas Day, however, they have a better fish po'boy, crawfish pie, French fries & red beans & rice. 

This was the first time I had the spinach salad that I got to take to my dads. It Rocked! Everyone loved it. 

The chicory coffee we had for the ride? Excellent as always. 

Highly highly recommend.

LOVE!!! Excellent wine bar! Hubby & I L.O.V.E The Delachaise! 

Hubby & I slept thru Sunday Brunch so we decided to start drinking Champagne from our hotel bar & find a French Restaurant for breakfast at 5pm. 
Hey, that's what happens when you visit NOLA. Oh well, Oh la la. 

So, we decide to hop the streetcar & go to The Delachaise. Then, we realize it's like 108 degrees out. So we do the next best thing, have another glass of Champagne & get a Uber. 

We arrive in Uber style, there is only one other table & some stragglers at the bar drinking wine. We get a awesome table with a marble top. 
The whole place oozes a 'petit café parisien' like somewhere in Paris. 
Outside, the sounds of the streetcar rattling, screeching & squeaking making its subtle mysterious music in the background only adds to the edgy, bohemian chic, hypnotic ambiance the tiny space exudes. 

Inside, the beautiful long vintage bar backed with rows of French wines, hand written chalk boards & tiny twinkling  lights reflected off old frosted mirrors were channeling Coco Chanel herself with burgundy lips. "I only drink Champagne on two occasions, when I am in love and when I am not." 

We thought we were back in Montmartre! 
Hubby & I went straight for the wine list. "You live but once; you might as well be amusing" I say, as I channel my inner Coco Chanel. 

We started off with a bottle of the Malbec. It was phenomenal. We ordered another. We ordered the 4 cheeses plate & it was completely divine with the wine! Parfait, très magnifique. 

Then, we ordered the mussels. MON DIEU! The best mussels we have ever had. Parfait, très magnifique !!! These mussels were cooked perfectly in a broth made by The Delachaise gods themselves. Very unique in a Thai style with garlic, ginger & lemongrass etc., sublime. One of the best things I have ever eaten. 
Hubby & I actually fought over the broth. We should have just ordered another but we had already ordered steak frits. 

The steak came out way too rare so we had it re-fired to med & it was great. However, the butter on top was very salty maybe get it on the side & use sparingly. Of course 
the goose fat fries are great, they came with the mussels & the steak. Hubby ate ALL of them unapologetically. Our dinner lasted like 5 hours. 5 hours of pure bliss. 

We have had some amazing dinners in NOLA but I don't recall any as brilliant as this lately. As a matter of fact, I don't think I have ever been to a Parisian style wine bar & cafe quite like this one. 
A petit trésor, very romantic, with fine wine & unique Parisian inspired cuisine right on the streetcar line, in New Orleans? Why yes. It is true. 

Like the legendary Coco Chanel says, "In order to be irreplaceable one must be unique" and The Delachaise has that in spades. 

We can't wait to return. 

Highly recommend.

LOVE! 

Love love love love this place. It's modern, it's stylish, it's fresh, it's French fabulous. 

I love that they have a "small plates" section on the menu. The drink menu was cool. The champagne cocktails were the bomb & the wine list was fantastic! We LOVED all three bottles of wine we choose.
It was all fabulous! 

Hubby & I with two colleagues tried all the small plates. We ordered everything on the menu! The grouper was super fresh & cooked perfectly. It was a little bland for my taste but the greens that accompanied it were amazballs!  I did not get pics of the tuna sashimi dish bc it disappeared so fast! Lol 
It was fabulous :)' 

The house speciality dish, the spaghetti with the poached fried egg was as interesting to look at as it was to eat. Everyone's favorite. 
It was fabulous :)' 

The rabbit pasta was divine. The flavor of this dish was Incredible. I'm salivating just thinking about it. In fact I can't stop thinking about it!
It was FABULOUS! :)...

The service, the food & the atmosphere was superb. 

GO NOW! 
It's freakin Fabulous! :p

I had some amazing Korean chicken in New York City two years ago, so when I heard Tampa was finally getting a spot dedicated to that, I was excited. Oh boy.. I usually try to keep things positive, but Gangchu, this ain't it. I was one of the first people at the establishment today, and the gentleman that took my to-go order at 4 pm on your first day was polite. Unfortunately, the food let me down. 

I should have checked things before leaving, but I gave them the benefit of the doubt. They wouldn't mess up on an easy order of bone-in chicken wings, right? When I arrived home, I saw that they messed my order up. I asked for bone-in wings, and they gave me boneless. I wouldn't have worried about it that much if they charged me for boneless, but they charged me the higher price that comes with bone-in wings. The one thing they didn't mess up on was the price they charged lol. I tried the Korean BBQ flavor and their Korean dry rub. The Korean BBQ wings were chewy and bland, and the dry rub wings were flavorless. The fries were soggy, starchy, and only had a whisper of salt. Talk about a let-down. It's sad when you go to a spot and you don't taste any love in the food there. I hope the kinks get worked out there, but it will be a while before I go back.

They do charge a 10% service charge with take-out, so keep that in mind when you do go there.

Well if anyone should know it would be me.  I have been to the new Miramar on 25+ occasions, starting with the soft openings and as recently as yesterday.  Why you might ask do I continue going back?  Because I just can't believe that a resort like the Miramar will never be able to get its act together!  I mean they have to figure it out eventually, right?  Well, not as recently as yesterday, lol.  I have lived in Montecito for 4 years and am a huge fan of it's lifestyle, shops, restaurants, and casual elegance.  Miramar was conceived to be the crown jewel of this impeccable seaside village.  But when will they figure out that the SERVICE STANDARDS MUST BE ON PAR WITH THE QUALITY OF THE PROPERTY.  Currently they have A+ marks for their venue and a D on their service resume.

I have dined at Caruso's (3 times), Malibu Farm (5+ times for breakfast, lunch and dinner), cocktails at the beach bar (5+) drinks in the Manor Bar (10+), wine and snacks at the outdoor fireplace (1) and had coffee on the lawn (2) while working away on my Mac.  I have NEVER had good service and there has always been delays, excuses, mismanagement, disorganization, confusion, food errors, food quality issues... you get the point.  It has become such a joke that pretty much every person I come across who is an overnight guest, or is there for a meal or drinks, says the same thing - "The service is terrible."  

A random sampling of some of my experiences:  
I called to make a reservation for my anniversary, never a return call.  I had a dinner booked another night and when I arrived they told me they had no record of it and could not seat me.  I have ordered food that has taken so long to come out, I've had to speak with the server and manager on 3 occasions during the same seating.  Bartenders at the main bar do not remove dirty plates and they just sit there until you stack them up as high as you can, so they will finally get noticed.  As recently as a week ago, we sat in the bar dining area in Caruso's for 15 minutes and I counted 11 service staff on the floor.  Not ONE of them asked us if we wanted a drink or a food menu.  I asked a concierge for a dinner reservation for a non-Miramar restaurant when my in-laws were guests, and we never heard back.  I left the Beverage Director an email and phone message once to discuss some of the issues we were experiencing about 2 weeks after Miramar first opened, and there was no return call or email.  Valet is a whole other issue- the wait times took so long I vowed never to use them again.  I park down the street now and walk through the side entrance of the hotel.  I could go on and on, poor service reigns every time.

The weird thing about it all is that the service staff is extremely nice, accommodative and pleasant.  Also, there appears to be an abundance of them most of the time (although I routinely hear they are short-staffed), the service standards are so lacking that maybe there is a misalignment between the owners and the management company.  Since Rosewood is one of the leading hotel groups in the world, how can they have such a difficult time with this place?  Have they forgotten how to train their staff?  Have they hired managers who don't know what they are doing?  Are their service standards different in Montecito than they are at Rosewood's Hotel de Crillon in Paris or The Carlyle in New York?  I have a feeling the public will give the Miramar a long leash because of the spectacular architecture, design and setting the owners have perfectly executed.  However, I come from the view that when you open anything in hospitality, you always want to put your best foot forward to ensure that you benefit from as much favorable word of mouth as possible.  The good kind of reviews are typically what helps grow a concept for the long term, not the other way around.

In closing, I will soon be back to Miramar as summer's weather is on our doorstop and where else would you want to have a drink around here.  I can't imagine I'm the only one who continues to come back after so many poor experiences, but I am pretty sure I am near the top of the list!

Ignorant, racist scumbags that make a half-assed steak and do almost as much to denigrate the image of Philadelphia as the asshole sports fans...

I can't believe the goofy, schlocky appeal hasn't worn off for people yet...maybe the tourists haven't ever seen the Geno's cooks come out and gang-beat a Pat's customer before...like a lot of locals have. I myself have seen this everal times while eating at La Lupe 50 feet away.

The only silver lining is that they actively manipulate the Deleware Ave wannabe-guido nightclub-tourists into shelling out $8.50 for a terrible steak.

Tony Luke's or Delassandro's have far better steaks. Screw both of those festering neon distractions. They are a psychic tumor on the city.

Located in the former Cafe'Terra Cotta building, they've redone it up (BIG)- in deep & dark Cherry wood/Chicago Mafia style paneling- complete with stained glass, frescos, chandeliers, and elevators... Yeah, it's quite over the top- for Tucson! After many months of construction and fine tuning, they finally opened April 1, 2013. 

There are two bars and a restaurant, plus some sort of membership social club that they will store your cases of wine that you buy there (supposedly at their cost) for a fee- so when you come back, you can tell all your friends that you're part of their exclusive "CLUB." 

The upstairs bar is (according to the staff) "more casual." Before they opened, I went to a private party in the downstairs bar, but since they've opened- I've only tried the upstairs bar. Although it seemed to have the same degree of ostentatiousness as the downstairs bar- the upstairs bar boasts a great freebee of a beautiful patio, complete with a dynamic and panoramic view of the La Paloma golf course and twinkling city lights to the south. 

They have a happy hour, with some drink specials (well drinks and beer only- no wine on happy hour) and the happy hour also features $6 appetizers until 7 PM. The restaurant seemed pretty packed tonight, albeit mostly the out of state 'snow bird set.' I'll have to go back and try the food. Despite the obvious mafia theme, it seems like a good new hot spot in the foothills. Anyone who lives here knows that we definitely need some new venues on the foothills dining scene.

Wildflower is my favorite "go to" restaurant in Tucson. It's the place I always suggest when no one knows where to go... Why? It's consistently good- both the food and the service, and that is a hard feat to accomplish in Tucson. I know it's a Fox Restaurant, and as such, it's part of the Fox chain concept. But there is, to its complete credit- only ONE Wildflower. 

My most recent dining experience was last night (4th of July). I'm on their email "VIP" list, and I recommend getting on that list, simply because you will get emailed coupons for 25% off your bill on all major holidays. The coupon is good at any Fox Restaurant, but my first choice Fox concept- by far- is Wildflower. 

My son ordered a Prix-Fixe four course summer meal ($35) that came with a starter course (small serving of brushetta), then he had a calamari salad, which was very flavorful. A skirt steak dish that was perfectly prepared and came with some greens. And for dessert, he had doughnut holes with a cherry custard. I wasn't very hungry, so I had a few bites of my son's food (to taste the different courses), and ordered the mussels. I have had the mussels here on numerous occasions, and I think it may have been an off night for the mussels (two were closed and two were empty). No worries, with a glass of Petit Sirah ($8), and the mussels, I was a happy camper. I did manage to save room for dessert, and the butterscotch pudding ($5) was out of this world! It is prepared slightly salted, and the taste of the salt with the butterscotch is fantastically delectable. 

I recommend Wildflower for lunch too... They used to have a salad on their menu called "The Everything" salad, and when I go for lunch, I always ask for it, and they always oblige. If you want predictably good food and service, you can't go wrong with Wildflower. Trust me- Wildflower is almost always my first choice restaurant in Tucson. And I love their patio too!

Not my cup of tea... My first time at Cafe' Poca Cosa, and it didn't wow me like I thought it would. This place comes at you with a lot of hype, a trendy contemporary space, and the guise of having interesting food, which maybe they did at one time twenty years ago in another location before they got too full of themselves... Bottom line, they need to get over themselves, because this wasn't a good experience at all. I ordered the plato special- which is whatever the chef wants to give you for $25. I only ordered it because I could't see, read, or understand how the waitress described the features. They don't have a real menu. Everything they have for the night is written on a chalk board in cursive writing that is not only impossible to read, but impossible to have any idea what it is, and it's placed in front of you for two minutes while the waitress stands there waiting for you to decide. All of this is in attempt to sell you the chef's special, so they can give you whatever they feel like giving you... I was not impressed!

When our food arrived, it was half way covered up with a green and purple FOREST of mixed lettuce that I literally had to dig through, in attempt to try and get to the bottom of the plate to reach my entree! It was highly unnerving, and unappetizing, especially considering that since I ordered the "chef's special plate" I had absolutely NO IDEA what I was eating... In my opinion, this is not a great restaurant concept. Yet, the staff acts like they have reinvented the wheel by churning out a virtual factory of "mystery meals!" Consider yourself warned.

Since I couldn't even see what I was eating (and I didn't know what it was), I wanted to ask for a separate plate to shed my plate of all the excess lettuce, but I didn't want to be the only one at the table to do so, so I just dealt with it. I think they were covering up the plate with all the lettuce because there was virtually no food on the plate. My plate consisted of a small green corn tamale pie, which was flavorful, but tasted like sweet corn cake. I also had about a two ounce portion of some sort of white fish that has one piece of zucchini next to it (all wrapped in foil), and three small pieces of skirt steak, that were overcooked, and flavorless, covered with a wanna be chimichurri sauce (no relation to the real chimichurri). Additionally, the lighting was especially dark, which only exacerbated the problem of not being able to see the food. Maybe that's how they want it though, because in addition to being such small portions, the food didn't have much, if any flavor. 

There were four of us, and sorry- but I don't understand how a picture of margaritas (even designer) could cost $60?! The check for drinks, dinner, and one dessert ended up being $230! This isn't New York, yet the sky high prices and attitudes/stuffiness of the staff left me scratching my head when I left as to how they stay in business. Save your money, and head down south 6th Avenue if you want Mexican or Latin food without the fuss, the attitude, or the high price tag.

Want a nice hearty breakfast? Well this is your kinda place great food good prices and friendly service is what I found when I stopped in here Sunday morning on the way to a friends house in Reno. Thanks to my Yelp friends, this looked like a good place to try. We were lucky to get a seat right away. Luckily I had looked over the menu while we were driving but my husband didn't get that chance and he was a little overwhelmed with the choices. But he opted for the Monte Christo which was french toast with ham and cheese kind of made into a three-story sandwich and I had the veggie omelette which was fabulous and filled with yellow squash, zucchini, broccoli, cheese and mushrooms (could have done without those, but menu doesn't say what's in it and I forget people even eat those things lol) all in all it was a really great breakfast start the day I would certainly come back on my way through town again.

I debated between a 2 and 3 star review on this one.  Tucano's has definite potential but they have a LOT of bugs to work out.

I actually went twice in one week with different meat loving groups of friends.  The first was a Tuesday night, with a decent crowd but at times there were more servers than patrons.  It was a little awkward having so many people standing around.  The meat was ok, everything but the pork.  Don't tell my mom, but it was so dry that I had to spit it out.  Some of the meat needed more seasoning, there were several items that I couldn't have said what type of meat it was.  The service was decent but it came out pretty slowly and we never saw all of the offerings.   No seafood, no vegetables ever came by.

Despite this, I was drawn by the $20 for all the meat you can eat aspect of it and decided to give it another try on Friday night.  This is where they were more of a 2 star experience.  They are pretty new and they were NOT ready for the big crowd that showed up. 

To start, they have probably 5 hostesses standing around awkwardly at the front.  We arrived, asked for a table for 6 and after a very brief wait we were walked into the side room.. only to find that another hostess had sat a party of 4 at our table for 6.  This is where it gets frustrating.  Instead of asking that party to move (they had JUST sat down) and instead of putting together the adjacent and empty two tables of 4 for us, they had us stand there blocking traffic for a minute before sending us back up front.  We were given another pager and told "Don't worry, we'll have a table in 10 minutes".  FORTY FIVE MINUTES later and many, many people seated already,  I witnessed them seating a party of 9 that had walked in *after* us.  At this point I'm frustrated and starving - NOT a good combination.  I walked up, quite irritated, and was told "five more minutes".  Luckily this time they really meant it and we were seated.

The manager did come over to apologize for our "mixup" and offered us free drinks.  Nice, right?  Yeah.. except the bar was so overwhelmed that it took 30 minutes for those drinks to show up!!  Once they did, the beers were the only ones with any discernible alcoholic content.  The mojitos were mostly club soda with a few pieces of mint on them.  Very disappointing.

They have a ton of tables set up here.. almost too many.  It was like elbowing your way through a black friday sale to get to the salad bar between the servers, the gauchos flying in and out of the kitchen and the patrons.  The meat service was SO disorganized.  We had pineapple offered to us three times in about 5 minutes but even after asking twice for the sausage offering it never showed up.  I finally flagged down the one guy I saw carrying sausage and begged him for the last piece but he never did come back for the rest of the table.  I saw fish at one point but they missed our table entirely and again never came back.  Completely disorganized.  Portion sizes varied wildly from gaucho to gaucho.  At one point I was given a paper thin slice that was literally no more than the burnt skin from the outside.  Asking for more resulted in an even smaller piece.  This time I skipped the pork but the filet wrapped in bacon was extremely over done and so was the garlic steak.  Such a waste.  This time I got smart.. when I saw how overcooked they were I didn't even bother trying to eat them.

Bottom line?  $20 is super cheap compared to other Brazilian places.  The salad bar is huge and you can easily fill up on just that.  I do think you should give it a try, but avoid the busy weekends until they (hopefully) get their act together.  Stick with non alcoholic beverages until they train the bartenders.

Pricey... but good. I love baklavas and this place didn't disappoint. They have so many varieties of sweets and pastries I was overwhelmed. The staff is really nice and they even allow you to sample certain items before purchasing.

To celebrate our 11 year first-date anniversary mark, my husband and I opted to dine at Sterling's Seafood Steakhouse, located in the Silver Legacy Casino. Surprisingly, Reno had sparse options for an upscale dinner choice, but Sterling's fit the bill perfectly. I was sold once I seen that they had a vegetarian option on the menu.  

HOUSE SALAD (FREE!): An artful house salad is included with he purchase of any entree. Hooray for freebies!I was super impressed with the presentation and taste of the salad.

VEGETARIAN NAPOLEON ($26): It's like a precisely arranged leaning tower of veggies topped off with a mound of buffalo mozzarella.The asparagus, quinoa, and portobella mushrooms were my favorite parts of this delightful entree. I found out from eating this entree that I do not like purple yams, so unless you're a fan I'd recommend taking those out. All in all, worth the price! 4/5

ROASTED ROSEMARY BREAST OF CHICKEN ($28): A hefty portion that even my husband was unable to finish. He approved. 4/5

CHOCOLATE DESSERT ($14ish): We went with a platter of various chocolates for dessert, and although they looked appetizing, the dessert simply was not worth its calories.

SERVICE: Our waiter was very nonchalant and not the most attentive fellow, so we ended mostly dealing with the busser. He was awesome. 3/5

AMBIANCE: Definitely upscale here. The dark colors of the restaurant creates a nice romantic vibe. We loved our booth and the fancy wine lists displayed on tablets. 5/5 

PRO TIP: The servings of wine are generous, so enjoy a nice glass of wine! We both were pretty buzzed off one glass of wine. 5/5

Aside from the dessert and service, I would definitely recommend eating here for those looking for a nice restaurant to dine at in Reno. Be ready to spend around $100 for two diners though.

YELP 100 CHALLENGE 2016: #24

I'm so excited this bar/restaurant is here!  Such a cool vibe, lovely decor, amazing food, wonderful chef willing to explain it all when it's not busy busy, and the GARDEN!!  It is so gorgeous! There is a wonderful lounge area in the front with stylish sofas and I just want to get my picture taken there!!

*If you are hungry, you need to have the "kimchi and oaxaca cheese empanadas".  They are done in a puff pastry dough that is to die for.
*The "Rebellion burger" could not be more delicious and it's ORGANIC and GRASS FED and you can taste the difference!  It's perfectly charred on the outside and juicy on the inside.  
*The sliders are amazing and will make your mouth water for more!
*The Rebellion ramen is so absolutely tasty, hearty, and oh so flavorful.
*And the "katsuo fries" are WOW.  I can eat those all day.

Right now, they are only open for lunch 11am-3pm Monday-Saturday until their liquor license comes through, but so worth stopping in.  I want to go again as I speak!!!  

I can't wait until they expand to dinner and drinks in a few weeks.  I hear the drinks are going to be a treat!

The Wylder in 5: Sleek, upscale, unpretentious, justifiable hype. 

Eat here they said, it's amazing they said...
Usually when I read glowing review after glowing review about a restaurant, I don't get too excited because sometimes hype is just that. Hype. Sometimes, I am wrong. 

Fancy & Fun
Upscale joints can often lack whimsy which I completely understand. They are meant to be stylish, not for kids. However, this place surprised me. We had the choice of dining inside or on the patio, we chose the patio and we chose well. The waitress, Iris, was a delight and Indigo just loved her. Their interaction was just adorable. 

The Honey Badger (don't care, he don't give...) 
Aside from being a hilarious reference, the Honey Badger pizza had me at Italian sausage and caramelized onions. I am usually unimpressed with pizza but this one was kind of brilliant. It was unique but not in an outrageous way. The side salad was simple and fresh. We were served promptly (salad first) and everything was fantastic.

This is how Boise does classy
I am genuinely impressed with this place. The waitstaff are all professional, kind, and personable. Their pizza is high quality and worth the price. That patio is where it's at and the string lights make it fancy. The Wylder hit the trifecta of exceptional service, food, and ambiance.

It would be difficult for me to give this place less than 5 stars.

Indigos take: Can we come back tomorrow?

Fly M Coffeehouse Downtown Boise in 5 words: Students, hipsters, gifts, chaos, lattes. 

Mayhem
There is clutter, there are teenagers, and more frighteningly, there are hipsters. Just kidding, the tweens take the cake in the frightening department. There is a small nook just for little kids and I've never seen a coffeeshop with one before. I like the concept. I would usually avoid this much chaos but they're one of the only coffee places open late that serve an excellent latte.

Almond milk latte on a green couch
My favorite seat in the house to sip a latte is the green couch, it's got personality. The lattes are consistently fantastic despite the cluster muck that is this place. The baristas are very nice and the baked goods are a mixed bag. They aren't terrible, I just have high standards for baked goods and more often than not, theirs are too dry.

I just want a pretty fern
My only actual complaint is the latte art. I get hearts. Every. Single. Time. Come on guys. What do I have to do to get a fern around here? 

Could I interest you in some sarcasm? 
Their gift shop is the best. Snarky coffee mugs, kitchen towels that swear, unicorn faux taxidermy. Whatever you're in the market for, that isn't mainstream, they'll probably have it. 

If you're into great coffee, fun gifts, have a high tolerance for teenagers, and hipsters, you're probably going to love Flying M in downtown Boise.

Indigo & I have frequented Form & Function several times. Here is my attempt at being honest while being kind. 

The Excellent:
The atmosphere. I love marble, natural lighting and clean design. This place checks all the boxes. 
The people who work here are low key, calm, & have a genuinely friendly disposition. Who could ask for anything more? 

The Food:
The assortment of baked goods upfront is fine & I have no complaints. The avocado toast is delightful. I like the brightness the lemon zest brings to the party. I prefer bread with a soft crust for avocado toast but that's just a personal preference. Unless you plan on eating it like a pizza, you're going to need a steak knife. 

The Good Coffee. 
I have had their mocha which I enjoyed because it wasn't overly sweet & I could taste the rich chocolate. Their iced hot chocolate is also delightful, just ask Indigo, she's an expert on iced hot chocolate.

The Bad Coffee: 
I'd say it just depends on what you order & what you like personally. Twice I've had an acidic honey lavender latte here. I ordered it the second time just to give it another chance. I did my best to enjoy it & I won't be ordering it ever again. I was physically uncomfortable drinking it & I'm not fussy about coffee. It wasn't bright & florally, it was acid. Every time someone orders that drink, a unicorn dies. 
 
Other than that, this place is great. 

My pro tip: When in doubt, always go with chocolate. 

Indigos pro tip: Banana Bread.

Fork, in 5 words: A stainless steel eating utensil. 
I'll try again: Stylish, excellent service, pedestrianly sophisticated.

I'm just always late ok?
My sis was in town recently I met her, along with her friends, at Fork for dinner. Being very late to the party, I showed up 25 minutes to closing (cringe). Sebastian, our waiter, brought me fresh coffee and then took my dinner order at around 10:40, no problem. I ordered the tomato basil and grilled cheese fondue and it was fantastic. #grilled_cheese_for_adults 
I would have not usually ordered food that close to closing (it's just not right) but on a scale from 1 to hangry, I was about to start flipping tables. 

The Waiter
Fork must have excellent management and high standards for servers or maybe they were just fortunate to hire Sebastian. When I show up anywhere 25 minutes to closing, I expect consequences and a less than amused server. I was pleasantly surprised. Sebastian never once rushed us, and if he was annoyed he didn't show it.

Fun
Despite a bit of mischief, which I had nothing to do with, Sebastian was unfazed. He handled our shenanigans and was a champion at banter. I can confidently give Fork 5 stars for excellent customer service and ordinary food dressed up fancy in a classy atmosphere. 

I don't always have extraordinary servers, but when I do, I leave an extra good tip and then write nice things about them on yelp.

Juniper 
This swanky establishment is sleek and not at all pretentious. Food is ordinary dressed up fancy and drinks are a steal during happy hour. We're talking $5 a drink.

The scene
It was Thursday. I was headed back to my car and decided that I need to eat something, as you do when you're out late downtown. I strolled into Juniper, sat at the bar and ordered a cup of vegetarian chili. 

Patrons & shenanigans 
A couple of guys were having a heated discussion a couple seats over and I quickly joined the fun.  After sorting out the technicalities and details, the argument was settled. Walter White would lose a street fight against Rick Grimes. Feel free to message me with arguments. 

Ambiance
The atmosphere is one of my favorites. Industrial chic with a personality. There's a gorgeous brick wall, nice lighting and a great bar. It has a very clean polished look without being too sterile or hotel restaurant looking. I recommend sitting at the bar or upstairs.

Overall thoughts
I've been to Juniper several times and they have been consistent in the quality of food and service. Impressive. Their menu consists of pedestrian dishes executed with a bit of flair and a lot of creativity. Their drinks are masterpieces. Masterpieces. Do happy hour. 

Juniper. A gem that I'm happy to have rediscovered. There's just something about it.

Ugh...I'm saddened to see that not knowing what a growler is, will warrant a 2-star rating. Now THAT's Sad. 

After sitting pool-side a majority of this hot day, the wife's rumbling stomach was in sync with mine. Retreating back to the room, we weighed out our options...Red Feather Lounge? Bittercreek Alehouse? The wifey exclaimed, "ITALIAN! I would love some spaghetti!" Okay then, SHE has spoken. 

Yelping netted us Old Spaghetti Factory, Asiago's, Cucina DiPaolo & Olive Garden to name a few. After relaxing in our air-conditioned room for several minutes, she decided on not wanting to get all ready & whatnot. Her suggestion? "Would you be a dear & just walk over to Papa Joe's on the corner for takeout?" Following her lead in not wanting to get ready for an evening in Boise Downtown (BoDo), I play the ever caring hubby. "Sure! Why not?" I knew she was still fighting a cold & besides, we've already painted BoDo red the past couple nights.

Staying a stone throw's away at the Residence Inn, its hard not to notice Papa Joe's as you have to pass right by it when driving to & from the hotel. It almost looks like a log cabin converted into restaurant. I walked in, sat at the bar & the bartender immerged from the back. 

"Hey man, I'd like to order for take-out..."
"No problem!" as he handed me a paper fold menu. 
I scanned it quick-like & found the spaghetti. "This come with garlic bread?"
"I don't see why not..." he replied.
"Awesome! I'll get an order of that w/marinara sauce and..." I spied the hot sandwich column, "...the Sausage sandwich...thanks."
"It'll take a few. It's made to order..."
"Sweet, it'll give me time to suck down one those Sockeye IPAs you've got on draft."
"Cool.", as he slid that frosty pint of that liquid gold over.

Bartender was cool & easy chat up. We talked about California & Idaho & everything in-between. Fifteen minutes had gone by when a waiter came out from the back with my order all neatly wrapped up & ready to go.

I thanked them both & headed back to the room.

The wife inhaled her spaghetti, but didn't finish it. It was much too much for one person to consume. She said it was average, but the highlight was the cheesy garlic toast of which she said, "...is some awesome stuff!" 

My sausage sandwich was a Hot Spicy Italian sausage, marinara sauce & covered with melty mozz. The sausage had a little bit of heat & was tasty to my tongue & palate. It was hot. It was good. I devoured it. I expected less & was pleasantly surprised.

Ugh...now I'm in food coma mode & all I wanna do is lay down, rub my belly & watch tv. 

I'm rounding up from a 3 STAR rating to make up for an earlier & undeserved 2-star review by someone who probably doesn't know what a sommelier, gig-line or a "let" is . G'hed buddy...lookit up on the interwebs!

...advantage deez®, I'm out.

T'was a Thursday afternoon & the wifey and I were hankerin' for a lunchtime joint that was new to us. So whatta we do? We Yelp of course! ...and together we came up with Fork.

Our hostess showed us to a table in a nearly empty dining area. It's just before noon, so I'm guessing Boise's work force hasn't let out for lunch just yet. As we perused the menu, Steve, our waiter brought over our rubber corked bottled water & filled our iced water glasses (a nice touch I might add) as he proceeded with his schpeel on Fork's organic dishes in which they use only the freshest local ingredients from vendors, suppliers & farmers in the Idaho & Pacific Northwest regions.

He recommended a few starters & we settled with the Grilled Jumbo Artichoke. By the time I had consumed half of my Outlaw IPA (by Payette Brewing Boise, ID), the Artichoke made it's arrival to our table. Larger than other artichokes we've had at other establishments, this one had a nice slightly grilled char on the inside halves, but didn't taste all charcoal-y like others we've had in the past. Nicely seasoned, it also had a hint of lemon. It was served with a mayo based rémoulade which had hints of roasted peppers & garlic. It was a devine pairing with the lemony 'choke leaves.

The wife ordered the Brisket/Sirloin blend Sliders served with glazed onions for her main lunch course & I, the Urban Burger w/bacon cooked at a juicy medium. I placed the fresh tomato & red onion slices under the top half of the soft pillow-y bun. At first bite it was perfectly cooked w/hints of red meat mingling with clear juices & the melted Tillamook cheddar. Put a dollop of Fork's burger sauce on that bite & it's OH SO effen GOOD! The burger came with a side of these Rosemary/Parmesan fries that the wife & I shared. She really liked them, but for me, though hot & gave off the aroma of rosemary, they were "dry" as if baked rather than fried in oil. The powdered parm cheese that lined the fries left a chalky aftertaste in my mouth that I didn't care for. HINT: It's better when dipped in the Fork burger sauce, yo! So ask for more. I washed it all down with my 2nd beer, the Sockeye Dagger Falls IPA (by Sockeye Brewing Boise, ID).

Steve never left us wanting & always kept our water glasses topped off. All in all, this was a solid dining experience & is on my list of places to revisit when back in the Boise area. Nicely done FORK, you've made a loyal customer out of me! 4.5 Stars!

Eat well & drink responsibly...this has been another deez® review because you need it & want it. Enjoy the day.

I haven't posted a one star review in perhaps years--honestly, if I have a mediocre experience somewhere, I just avoid posting a review on it. But when I write a specific one star review it's for another reason. The main reason why it's a one star is because this restaurant seems to build itself on having a "classier" environment and reputation. However, after being seated at the bar, I overheard the bartender make a racially offensive joke to some other patrons. Terrible. Then, I felt like I was essentially pegged as someone who wasn't going to end up spending a lot of money there, and felt like I was being rushed out the door. The combo of this supposed classy service with what's actually going on is really gross.

Finally, as another Yelper reviewed--I also grew up in New England, and if you're to put a lobster roll on your menu--that's risky but to me, I decided to go all out on it. Didn't taste like anything you'd get in New England. Another reiteration on why getting seafood in the desert is often a risky proposition...

Honestly, I would have given this place 3 stars without the offensive comment made by the bartender, but this place needs to be put on notice for crap like this. Unacceptable. With so many places to go out to eat in Tucson, why patronize institutions like this employ staff who go out of their way to make these types of remarks?

This place should be a St. Louis tourist attraction! 

Hopefully they branch out to west county, or closer to downtown.

When my family went to Vancouver, people were falling in line (sometimes for over an hour) to get a taste of the Japadog - Anthony Bourdain and Samantha Brown were big fans.  Well, I've tried the dogs at Japadog, and they have nothing compared to the offerings at Dogs and Fries. This St. Louis restaurant has the best fries and hotdogs I've ever tasted anywhere.

Location is not the best, but there is plenty of parking. Oustide it looks a bit run down, but inside the decor is industrial cool, sort of like Guerilla Street Food. 

Try them, and I guarantee you you'll be addicted.

At the date of this post Club Congress is by far Arizona's best music venue.  It just is, bar none.  It's small and they book GREAT national touring acts on a fairly regular basis (esp considering it's in Tucson).

Rooms upstairs, a side bar, and cafe all connected by the hotel lobby ... I mean seriously ... super cool.  Hell, if this place were in a larger city it would be one of the best places to see a show in the country (IMHO).

Viva La Club Congress!

Not precisely the easiest place to find in New Orleans, GPS coordinates leading potential patrons to a parking space on the exact opposite side of a row of buildings in the rejuvenating Warehouse District, Restaurant Rebirth represents a modern look at Creole-Cajun Classics crafted from Farm-to-Table ingredients, dinner on Halloween seeing everything from a Kill Bill Ninja to Darth Vader enjoying dinner in a space that is at once rustic and elegant, but not pretentious in the least.

Toqued by Chef Ricky Cheramie and featuring a menu that evolves seasonally to offer the very best of his native Louisiana, Restaurant Rebirth at first looks a lot like many hip eateries in bigger cities, but for those who sit down at one of several white-clothed tables surrounding the walk-in only bar a decidedly different sort of place is soon evident, the servers offering genuine "Southern Hospitality" with purchasable art on the walls showing off Mardi Gras photography and modern Jazz playing lightly overhead.

Justifying slightly elevated pricing with locally sourced goods from the region's top purveyors, it was with a smalls slice of Corn Cake doused in Molasses that the meal got started mere minutes after seating, three appetizers to follow including two daily specials and one 'signature' item, the Oysters & Angel Hair a briny amalgam of Crispy fried Bivalves, Tasso and Bottarga nicely balanced by grilled Mushrooms and Pepper Cream Sauce over housemade Noodles, the Gumbo du Jour a spicy pot of Dirty Rice in nearly black Roux dialed up in Duck, Chicken and Sausage while the Soup du Jour saw Cajun spices enliven Fish, Crab, Oysters and Crawdads in a New England Style Chowder.

Not shorting patrons on printed descriptions of plates, entrees all large enough for two adults to share, it was with wide eyes that a juicy and tender Double Tomahawk Pork Chop from Heritage Farms was brought forth atop porky Green Beans and cubed Potatoes beneath a veil of house-squeezed Sugar Cane Glaze, the eggplant stuffed with Shrimp Meatballs crispy yet oilless with Cracklin', and Pine Nuts all lightly drizzled in lightly spiced Red Pepper Gastrique. 

Nabbing the very last Seafood Platter du Jour that evening, a pair of fried Soft Shell Crabs packed to the point of bursting with more Blue Crab Meat alongside Crawfish Hushpuppies and Lobster Maque Choux, a side of pan-seared Potato Dumplings were simple yet compelling when tossed with pan-seared Mushrooms.  

Foolish to ever pass on dessert in New Orleans, the menus almost universally offering some sort of Bread Pudding or Beignet, Restaurant Rebirth's only flaw was three 'beignets' that were hard, cold and oily atop Café au Lait Crème Brûlée, the Chocolate Torte a masterpiece of flourless fudge presented simply with candied and fresh Fruit, the White Chocolate Bread Pudding amongst the city's best that was completely soaked with custard, yet still managed to maintain a springy consistency.

Greeted almost immediately upon seating by my friendly server - a young man who managed what appeared to be the entire front room without difficulty and maintained the demeanor of someone trained under the Thomas Keller Empire - the service would be perfect throughout.  Bread was timely, coffee and water refills spot on, plate descriptions accurate thorough, and all done with a friendly down-to-earth demeanor and a smile.  Going over the daily special with me I was left to decide while he went to get my coffee.

Listening to the room - lively but not loud despite the parade going by in the street - I labored over the menu for some time because everything sounded quite good - essentially bistro fare with a southern twist.  Returning with the coffee - a great thick blend with a bit of chicory but more prominently cocoa notes (I'm rather certain the same as that at August) I decided to go with the "express lunch" special - a $15 soup and main combo plus an added appetizer.  Smiling my server told me I'd made a great choice and slipped away to serve his other tables.

Arriving shortly after my order was placed - yet another crispy and golden French loaf, this time served with a delightful and grassy salted butter.  While the bread was not quite as delicious as that at Clancy's it was my second favorite of the trip and the butter put it over the top - thankfully I limited myself to just the one loaf because it turns out Luke's "deal" lunch is not for the faint of heart (or stomach.)

Arriving first, my soup - the daily special of crawfish bisque.  Clearly tomato and cream based with heavy spicing and ample crawfish the dish was unlike any bisque I've ever tasted, but certainly not a gumbo either.  Loaded with chunks of fresh crawfish and spicy without being "hot" I liked the bisque and as it would turn out (oddly) to be my only experience with crawfish on the trip I was glad I'd chosen it even though I likely would have preferred the daily gumbo.

My second dish, an addition to the prix fixe, was the Foie Gras - quite frankly, if a place is offering a terrine of Foie I'm probably going to order it.  Presented elegantly this terrine proved not only good, but exemplary.  Featuring a thick cut of slow cooked terrine painted on all sides with a Gewürztraminer reduction, topped with micro greens and a coarse sea salt, and drizzled with thick and sweet balsamic I can favorably compare this $16 preparation to the $30 supplemented version served at The French Laundry - though it wasn't quite as airy or delicate.   Served with toasted brioche (I was brought more on request) and beautifully textured I would strongly recommend any fan of cold foie to visit Luke for the experience.

Arriving next was the daily special - having looked at the menu I was surprised when it arrived because I expected a sandwich...but the surprise was the good kind...the really good kind.  In describing their cochon du lait prep my server told me how the slow roast pork is reduced down similar to pulled pork and then "rehydrated" with a dairy, onion, and garlic reduction (plus the chef's special spices) and then pan fried crispy on top.  If that description doesn't do it for you - try it...almost a sweet yet creamy pork meatloaf with a crispy and salty skin akin to pork belly.  Accompanying the pork on the plate were not only the advertised stewed greens and vinegar laden cherry mustard, but also a hefty helping of cornbread dressing.  Call it bistro food, call it soul food, call it comfort food - I call it one of the most unexpectedly delicious dishes I've had in some time.

Asking me if I was interested in dessert I told him I didn't even need the menu - just bring the bread pudding.

Arriving about 15 minutes later as I read a complimentary copy of the New York Times the bread pudding was an absolute masterpiece - the best traditional bread pudding I've ever tasted.  Described simply as cinnamon raisin bread pudding with vanilla bean ice cream and hot buttered pecan sauce the complexities of the dish were astounding for a bread pudding - piping hot with the smooth and creamy ice cream slowly melting the bread pudding itself was marvelous in custard/bread ratio and the sauce had minimal alcoholic kick while instead focusing on notes of caramel, pecan, cinnamon, and what may have even been honey.  Having had a whole lot of bread pudding in my time this was undoubtedly my favorite non-chocolate version to date.

Taking a trip to Belle Meade Plantation between meals three and four it was just prior to the post-work rush that we entered the original Hattie B's, and finding almost no wait where a nearly two hour line would be noted just a few days later when we passed by it was on the outdoor covered patio that we indulged, nearly every item selected proving exactly how much quality ingredients benefit everything from soul food to fine dining as the fried chicken proved to be amongst the two or three best I've ever tasted, a subjectively high standard to say the least.

Opened near Vanderbilt as recently as 2012 by a father and son team known for their previous work at a nearby Meat-and-Three, Hattie B's has skyrocketed to the top of most local "hot chicken" lists and receiving long lines of patrons as well as accolades a first bite of the juicy bird immediately explains the fervor - a light bit of heat found in the medium while a great depth of spice but no unnecessarily scorching peppers permeate the "hot" option, a few more degrees available to those interested but not something my Midwestern-born palate was willing to chance on that particular day.

Equally impressed with Pimento tinged Macaroni and Cheese, and truly surprisingly by skin-on Potato Salad that eschewed all the mustard in favor of cream and acid to balance the bite, it was with a duo of desserts that the meal finished up, the pudding a rather standard rendition with some of the 'Nilla Wafers left crunchy while the cobbler with fresh peaches was an early summer treat with a whole lot of sweetness that I rather wish I'd have ordered a la mode.

Owned by Chef Rick Lewis, and featuring upscale Southern cooking with counter service, Grace Meat + Three has earned its fair share of accolades, though based on a midday Sunday visit in December the Food generally seems overpriced and unbalanced.

Located at 4270 Manchester Avenue, 11a-8p hours from Wednesday through Sunday featuring separate menus for Brunch, Lunch and Dinner, it is upon entry that guests see the Restaurant spread left and right, the overhead menu not entirely accurate - though apparently neither is the tri-fold near the door considering the difference between what was served and what was printed.

Taking orders from a central counter, a fact not obvious to first timers including a family who went and sat down before realizing their error and joining the queue, it was after inquiries regarding portion sizes and Grace's "Daily Bread Puddin" that a three part order was composed, Sourdough Beignets described as coming with "Persimmon Mousse + Pickled Pears" the first disappointment as they arrived doughy and flavorless with Blueberries and floral Citrus in a perfunctory pan.

Waiting perhaps ten minutes for course two, juicy Fried Chicken performing well atop a thin Waffle while buttery Cornbread outpaced Grits that needed more salt and less Herbs, Desserts sold for $8 each proved rich but small, the Pudding eaten on-site an enjoyable riff on the classic while Salted Honey Custard Pie taken to-go was visually compromised and mostly just sweet.

Conveniently located just off the route from Nashville to Memphis, Loveless Café and the small village of stores around it are nothing short of a Tennessee Landmark, and fresh off the redeye from LAX our arrival at the former hotel preceded its opening by a mere fifteen minutes, a line of six already formed with the sizable restaurant nearly 100% full by the time we left just after 8:15.

Featuring concepts of sustainability, scratch-based cooking, and a menu of Southern diner classics spanning from breakfast through lunch to supper, it was almost immediately upon seating that water was poured while coffee was readied and although the brew itself was a bit acrid without sweetener the refills were spot on and spontaneous, though food did take a bit longer than would be expected as our server was spread thinly throughout the largest room in the house, at times even drawn to the al fresco seating to assist others at a table of twelve.

Sipping coffee with orders placed it would not be long before a plate of Loveless' signature buttermilk biscuits was delivered, and paired with a trio of housemade jams plus requested sorghum and honey it goes without saying that the fluffy golden rounds are indeed quite delicious, though for my money there are better to be found not only in Nashville but also parts of the Carolinas as well as at Yardbird, still the reference standard, though admittedly theirs are not refilled freely on request.

Moving on to entrees, another piping hot cup of coffee poured, it was largely a matter of sampling widely that led to an order of even more biscuits and with each of the four golden rounds topped differently one would be hard pressed to name a winner amongst the group, the crispy chicken and tender pulled pork rousing curiosity of just how good a full plate dinner at Loveless might be while the tart green tomato topped with spicy pimento cheese was as 'Southern' as it gets, certainly not the sort of stuff you see served for breakfast anywhere back home.

Moving next to the French Toast and Pancakes, suffice it to say that both are competent takes on classic American breakfast staples, and with the buttermilk fresh plus the bread homemade the only real question is whether to indulge in Maple Syrup, local Honey, or thick amber Sorghum as the topping of choice, from my standpoint a decision that entailed a little of each before deeming the decision a tossup, the Sorghum almost a bit *too* sweet on the vanilla and cinnamon dipped toast but absolutely delightful when mellowed by the ample amount of toasted pecans added to the pancakes for just a buck.

Unwilling to forgo desserts, 7:45 in the morning or not, what started as a sampler of three miniature pies and puddings quickly expanded to a quartet when the server brought chocolate chess instead of original, and with a pure butter crust serving as the base to both reference standard iterations it speaks volumes that the pecan pie was actually the best of them all, a dearth of 'filler' allowing the caramelized nuts and brown sugar to shine without being overly sweet - a similar degree of subtlety offered by banana pudding that used house whipped cream and softened vanilla wafers amidst thick chopped fruit and a smooth yellow base to deliver an experience that was not only texturally pleasing but also shockingly natural, a quality far too infrequently found in a dessert where boxed pudding is far too frequently meant to suffice.

At this point nothing short of a New Orleans institution, the Treme neighborhood favorite now more accessible than ever by way of Uber or Lyft, Willie Mae's Scotch House has accumulated countless accolades for "America's Best Fried Chicken" since adding the item to lunch service nearly 50 years ago, The James Beard Foundation even going so far as to deem the restaurant on St. Ann Street a 2005 "America's Classic" winner, mere months before Hurricane Katrina shuttered the space until a 2007 privately-funded rebuild. 

Named after Willie Mae Seaton, the original owner and cook who died just over one year ago at the age of 99, recent times have sparked some discussion that the combination of her passing and recent "foodie" hype have somehow diminished the appeal of a visit, the small line present prior to a 10am opening occasionally expanding to over two hours, though a second location on St. Charles Avenue does offer the same recipes in an expanded dining space.

Handing down her recipe for Wet-Battered Bird to a Great-Granddaughter after re-opening, nothing about the simple Salt and Pepper flavor changed according to longtime fans, a quick look at Willie Mae's shows signs of a "do one thing, do it well" concept, each three-piece serving made-to-order and worth the wait, served with one side for just $11.

Occasionally offering Veal, Pork, Fish or Shrimp, the newer location more prone to daily specials, it was at the center of a room featuring family photos, awards and the Bronze Medal that we sat, severs friendly and efficient even amidst heavy traffic with a mere fifteen minutes separating walking through the door and hot Chicken on the table.

The sort of food where sight and smell alone tell a story, golden-brown Batter adhering loosely to moist, almost-creamy flesh, each bite of Ms. Seaton's Chicken speaks volumes about time and tradition, the sides no less impressive whether one favors Mashed Potatoes in Brown Gravy, Mac n' Cheese or crispy hand-cut Sweet Potatoes.

Impressed by lightly sweetened Cornbread, each Muffin tender and springy without any need for added butter, more sweetness was delivered by a duo of timeless Southern Desserts, the Red Velvet Cake exceedingly dense with Cocoa but balanced by Cream Cheese Frosting while the scoop of Bread Pudding was a perfect combination of toasted and custardy beneath a generous spoonful of Crème Anglaise.

Long ranking on my American dining bucket list it was almost serendipity that The Catbird Seat returned from a team vacation to noma during my final day in Nashville, and having contacted the restaurant directly when the online reservation system continued to show no seats for the whole week prior it was a true measure of generosity that saw a seat offered even before books opened for my coveted first seating, a 5:30 arrival finding just one other couple present as we watched the team work diligently preparing canapés while completing last minute mis en place.

Reported by some to have slipped a notch since the departure of Chef Erik Anderson and promotion of Trevor Moran to top toque, it was immediately on downstairs entry that the experience began and treated to the a glass of bubbly verjus the quick ascent in an elevator soon saw me seated with a head-on view of the kitchen, potentially the best seat in the house with a beef tendon puffed like a chicharron ready in wait.

Assuring the team of no allergies or intolerances, and opting for the $35 non-alcoholic pairing that generally lacked inspiration with not only redundant flavors but also a repeat of the floral soda at dessert, it was with great rapidity that the next four bites arrived and although the ham amidst aromatics and light smoke was truly delicious both the oyster and razor clam seemed strangely out of place, the herbal tea a clever enough concept when used to reinvigorate the grilled seaweed oil, but mostly just filler and a sign flavors to come.

Undoubtedly taking on some of the terroir as plates progressed, the first proper course of the meal was perhaps the most intriguing of all, and although the pairing with sweetened grapefruit did not really do much to improve the silky beef topped in snail eggs and puffed rice both the flavors and textures were more than enough to tantalize the palate while also showing the kitchen's ability to do more than just accent everything with smoke.

At this point joined by several other diners, many regulars that saw gifted plates from the kitchen extend out their tasting while the rest of us stood by, it was with more smoke in hand that the next plate arrived, the puree of pommes not particularly photogenic but creamy and almost ethereal beneath foam from local brewer's yeast and yet another top note of smoke.

Settling in for what seemed destined to be a long meal of dynamic, if not entirely unique, bites it was next in almost comically smoked caviar that we indulged and although the dollop of eggs was quite generous I almost couldn't believe my ears when the follow-up of crispy pork tail was presented as the 'final savory' - a mere sixty-five minutes passed as the hibiscus tea accented with dill proved a challenge to stomach, let alone understand.

Sure enough transitioning here from savory to sweet without so much as cheese, sorbet, or even a new drink it was to an elegantly decorated cake of textures beneath light tang that the first few diners were treated and receiving another glass of the verjus just a few minutes later the pairing unfortunately proved a bit too floral when melding with pearls of hibiscus, a far better sip found in the blend of herbs and apples with which the last two courses would be had.

At this point hoping that the menu had not entirely morphed from earlier days I was thankful that the penultimate plate was Catbird Seat's famous "Ice Cream Salad," and utilizing the gentle sweetness of sorrel with chilly citrus and southern staples of bourbon and pecan the flavor was as dynamic as the texture, a similar compliment paid to the potato shaped Toppel that spilled forth cream to create a sort dip-and-bite experience with 'dirt' that balanced out the sugar with careful bitterness, a final bit of whimsy that left me with a good taste in my mouth and a smile on my face despite walking out a mere 2-hours after entry still feeling hungry, perplexed by the hype, and wondering how, exactly, a place like this survives in Nashville at greater than $200 a head after tax and tip.

Again exiting the conference for an extended break as the City of Nashville's humidity finally gave way to rain, it was perhaps an oversight of Vanderbilt's love of a boozy brunch that saw us arrive at Tavern to the tune of a 90-minute wait, the time largely spent wandering nearby Centennial Park beneath umbrellas until a text called us forth from the Pantheon to be seated amongst a mass of humanity with well lubricated co-eds screaming to be heard above the loud tunes echoing from high ceilings overhead.

Dining with a pair of ladies from the era which several of the restaurant's 1960s tunes were sourced, and thus clearly not of a demographic common during the hour of our meal, suffice it to say that the ninety minute wait was further compromised by overstretched service that saw our table ignored until a manager was flagged down fifteen minutes later, the kitchen itself equally stressed but trying to make good by sending out four scoops of luke-warm "White Trash Hash" as the wait-time for plates was extended another twenty-five minutes after the order was eventually placed.

Already aware that my memory of the experience would be marred by the aforementioned events no matter how good the cuisine, it was unsurprising that when all items were brought out at once there was evidence of a good bit of heat-lamp treatment to found and although the Kaya Toast was actually quite impressive in its balance of textures as well as flavors despite the unnecessary decorative hot sauce, the biscuits were leaden and far too soggy, the supposed cheddar almost undetectable beneath gravy that tasted little of spice and closer to oversalted ham.

Unable to pass on sweets, but unaware that the "fondue" featured both Red Velvet and Blueberry waffles since the later was not amongst the menu items listed, it was with an unnecessary plate of the crispy cornmeal checkerboard that the meal progressed and faring far better than the doughy red velvet iteration which lacked any semblance of coco suffice it to say that any suggestion of 'cardamom' in the 'maple' syrup was so faint as to be imperceptible, the snappy spiced sausage and cornflake crusted French Toast saving the otherwise lackluster shared plate.

Informed that desserts are only offered at dinner, and as such going even sweeter than usual with mains, it was finally the restaurant's thinly poured flapjacks that crossed our lips and although a better effort could have been made than a topping of pretzels straight from a bag it would be difficult to find any other fault in the buttermilk triplet, the sticky-sweet caramel finding an unexpectedly willing dancing partner in light chocolate mousse that produced a flavor not unlike that of tres leches as it soaked the pancakes straight down to the plate.

A longtime Garden District favorite - certainly not the sort of place one will find teaming with European Tourists in the French Quarter - Surrey's Café and Juice Bar is one of those kitschy places with fun decorations and a unique menu where service comes with a smile, the waits sometimes quite long given the limitations of the space, but the experience making it worthwhile.

Located at 1418 Magazine Street and blending in so effortlessly with surrounding homes that it is barely noticed from the sidewalk to passers-by, Surrey's Café approaches New Orleans classics with a Latin Spin alongside a lengthy menu of seasonal fresh squeezed Juices, the seating somewhat tight yet somehow seeming appropriate as the walls are given splashes of color by vibrant depictions of nearby architecture made by a local artist.

Described a few daily specials by the server, a man circulating to fill both Coffee and Water also providing some advice of his own, it was with tough choices made that three plates were selected while taking a pass on the juices, though the ones that were ordered at neighboring tables did look refreshing with no lack of choices including everything from Orange to Apple, Carrot and Watermelon.

Waiting perhaps ten minutes for food, the quoted time for a two-top approximately twenty minutes at 8:20am on a Monday, suffice it to say that housemade Boudin on a Buttermilk Biscuit with Scrambled Eggs presented a significant upgrade on the typical "breakfast Sandwich" ordered at the Drive-Thru, a moist Pumpkin Pancake thick and rich with Cinnamon also proving to be good despite the lack of pure Maple Syrup while the Creole Cream Cheese stuffed triangles of French Bread were pudding-soft beneath the pan seared exterior and plenty sweetened by the Rum flamed and fruity Sauce.

Named to several "Best of" lists in various online and print media, Fox's Donut Den was the first stop after hopping off the plane at BNA and arriving just moments after the sizable storefront unlocked the doors it was even before pulling the handle that the smell of yeast mingling with sugar could be smelled, even over the scent of exhaust as a stream of locals literally drove up, parked with engine still engaged, and ran in to grab a donut and coffee before heading back to the road.

Every bit an oldschool doughnuttery, though happy to experiment with the occasionally novelty such as baked donut bread or the donut-croissant hybrid, a first glance at the Donut Den would lead one to believe there are hundreds of options, but instead featuring several duplicates spread across several cases the best approach is to stick to the left side of the space and choose amongst favorites - a lack of buttermilk bar or blueberry leading to a Half-Dozen +1 approach tallying $14.17.

Taking a seat at one of several vinyl booths, the Formica tabletops telling tale of just how long Fox's has been serving the city of Nashville, our tasting began with raised, yeasted options and with both the chocolate frosted star and Simpsons-style Strawberry ring proving light, fluffy, and virtually oilless the craftsmanship was immediately evident, a wispy cream filled pocked proving equally well crafted as we transitioned to cake based options and other novelties both new and classic.

Speaking first to the 'new,' it must be noted that Fox's 'Cro-Do' is a good riff on Ansel's invention with well separated layers and a lightness that allows buttery notes to shine, and while the substantial apple fritter was equally low in grease amidst ample cinnamon-laced apples neither the chocolate cake nor the old fashioned managed to impress in the least as the crumb of each was far too dry - the old-fashioned, which was described as a 'cruller,' nearly inedible without a beverage in hand, and even than not worth the cost or calories...a damned shame as the maple icing was itself quite excellent, a flavor far less 'sweet' than would be expected given its thick application.

The situation:

Google Maps and Apple Maps will take you to an empty lot, keep driving about a mile or so and you'll see a big sign on the left.  

If you want a sandwich you order that at the bakery side.  

The woman who helped me didn't speak English so I made a rookie mistake and forgot to look up on Yelp what the best sandwich is and I wasn't able to get feedback from the staff.  

The grilled pork I ordered was AMAZING!!  Like, so good I couldn't wait to make it back to my office because I had to eat it in the car RIGHT THIS SECOND.  The bread had just enough crunch that it made a crunch noise but not so crunchy that it tore up my mouth.  My dress was only lightly sprinkled with crumbs.  I'm kinda gross, I know.  It also didn't overwhelm the sandwich as all the flavors from the meat and toppings stood out.  

The gigantic pho bowls around the restaurant looked incredible, too.  This will be on my pho radar.  

Summary: 
You will get a DELICIOUS sandwich 
In about 2 minutes 
For $3.25 pre-tax.
Add in a cinnamon roll or treat and we're looking at the best lunch ever for $4.21
And discovery a part of New Orleans you probably didn't know existed.  
Road Trip!!

I've been here twice in six days and can't stop thinking about it. I'm pretty much in love right now. Like, a lot. 

I first tried the trio sampler which is a great choice if you can't narrow it down to one. The steak and pulled pork ones were outstanding!! The cold chicken was ho hum, if you're ordering the entree I'd choose a different one. These are small and open faced but filling nonetheless. I mean, I still had dessert...don't expect to be full. 

The next time I tried the chorizo arepas and it blew my mind. What's better about the entree portion is the addition of cheese and it being more like a sandwich with a side of plantain chips. 

What takes the meal to the next level?? Adding the vinegar slaw, a $3 side item to every bite. Do it. Seriously. I don't even normally like slaw. I don't even like the word. 

You get a choice of sauces. Splurge and spend the extra 50 cents to try all three. My favorite is the creamy mayo based one. 

Ok so what are the downsides? I first went on a Friday with a group of six. The restaurant was so loud I couldn't hear the other half of my table. Or am i old? I don't know. I then came on a Thursday night with two others and although it's still kind of loud it was much more manageable. I'd encourage you to come in a smaller group and make reservations because it's pretty small.

Garlic beef is amazing! I came here for all you can eat lunch on a Monday and even though it's a small place and a small selection of meat but it's worth the price of $20/person. 

Let the waitress know that you're there for buffet then you can start picking up the hot food bar or the salad bar. The meat will be brought to you slowly, so don't worry.

Cute cozy little cafe near Pat's and Geno's cheesesteaks. 
The cappuccino I had was just made perfect, rich and smooth and not sweet but not bland. 
I'm upset that I didn't try the cannolis, hopefully in 2 weeks when I have a chance to stop by. 
The front has chocolates and sweets for sale, on the side has an interesting display of very interesting chocolates! See pictures hahaha 
The waltz was on that day and my legs wanted to dance as I was sipping my coffee.

Lloyd is my new favorite bar in Fishtown... and all of Philadelphia for the matter. With its cozy atmosphere, cool background music, and great friendly service, I've already become a regular in just the first couple weeks this bar has been open. From the food to the cocktails, Lloyd knows what they're doing and they are doing it right! This bar is just what the neighborhood needed and it will be a hotspot for locals and visitors alike for a long time!

Here's what I've tried so far:

The Food:
Texas Tommy- This delicious and decadent hot dog is served smothered in cheese sauce, wrapped in bacon, and topped off with bourbon soaked bacon. Maybe the best hot dog I've ever had. I could eat these things all night!

Lloyd Burger- I order my burgers medium rare and this one came out perfectly. As the menu states, they use a special house blend of beef, muenster cheese, pickled onion, lettuce, tomato, on a brioche bun. Delicious! It also comes with awesome fries.

Goldfish-Crusted Mac & Cheese- Creamy cheesy goodness. Can't go wrong with this dish!

Green Tomato Grilled Cheese- Provolone, gruyere, and muenster cheese on sourdough. Grilled just right and served with a field green salad.

Crispy Fried Deviled Eggs- The caper aioli is the perfect accompaniment for this tasty appetizer.

Desserts: I've tried both the rice pudding and the bread pudding. Each are a perfect way to end you meal (unless you'd prefer another whiskey!).

The Cocktails:
I can honestly say Lloyd served up the best Manhattan and Old Fashioned I've ever had! The happy hour is from 5-7pm and some of their cocktails and beers are on special. I recommend the Jack & Wendy and The Overlook (simply because I'm a huge fan of The Shining). I hope one day I'll find a "Delbert Grady" on the cocktail menu.  Looking for something quick and easy? Go with "The Lloyd", only $5 for a can of Miller High Life and a shot of Old Grand Dad.

With dozens of bourbons, ryes, Irish Whiskey, and Scotch Whisky on the menu, you can't go wrong. Whiskey isn't your thing? No problem! Lloyd has plenty of beers, wines and other spirits to loosen up your inhibitions. 

As you can tell, I've been sampling a lot of the menu and haven't been disappointed yet. I'm looking forward to trying the chicken po' boy, the beef stew, and BBQ turkey meatloaf in the near future. 

"I like ya Lloyd, I've always liked ya. The best damn bar from Timbuktu to Portland, Maine...or Portland, Oregon for that matter." -Jack Torrence, The Shining

First off, the food is 4.5 stars, service is 4 stars, and seating area is like 3.5 stars.  I had a 6:15pm reservation for me and my mom on a Saturday night.
