I'd heard about Melt Kraft (RIP), which was THE place for grilled cheese sandwiches. Unfortunately the stumbling block for me was its location-Reading Terminal Market. My late friend Dee offered to go with me to help me work through my childhood associations with the market. I readily accepted because-anything for a good grilled cheese sandwich, y'know? 

We went on a Sunday. The insidious smell of rot and vegetal decay hit me as soon as I walked in, but it was not as intense as I'd remembered. The press of the crowd was, though. Dee got directions to Melt Kraft, we pushed and shoved through slow moving bodies in winter clothing and found the vendor. And a very long line of people who also shared my love of gooey, hot cheese. I said I would skip the sandwich but if she was up for it, we'd walk around. 

Since I don't like donuts, roast pork sandwiches, cheesesteaks, hoagies or looking at meat and dead fish, I don't drink coffee nor do I care for pancakes or iterations of waffles, that left a lot of places for us to just pass by and skip. I am acutely aware that I am a neurotic person, so I asked Dee if RTM was as dirty and unpleasant as I perceived it to be. She said she honestly felt it was fairly clean for a market of this kind, but she understood my feelings. We made it to Iovine's produce which oddly calmed and soothed me, but not enough for me to spend any more time there. 

Even if I was forced to entertain out of towners that I absolutely loathed, I wouldn't torture them by taking them here.

My travels have taken me to the Casbah in Morocco, public markets in Africa, butcher shops and green grocers all over Europe. I adore Chinatown and the whole Italian Market area. I can spend hours in either place walking around, eating, drinking and shopping. To me, Reading Terminal Market is nothing but a huge, smelly, crowded tourist attraction, a so-so sub par food circus and a place for me to avoid. This is, of course, simply my opinion and your mileage may vary. More power to you if it does. 

If you are a visitor to Philadelphia, please keep in mind that we are much much much more than RTM, the Phillies baseball team, soft pretzels, cheesesteaks, the Liberty Bell and the "Rocky Steps" (which are merely part of the building and lead to one of the entrances to the Philadelphia Museum of Art).

We'd pass by this restaurant every time we walked the pup. I couldn't help myself but to Yelp it! 3.5 star average rating trending to 4 so I said let me give it a try. 

When we walked in it was pretty packed but the wait wasn't bad. Ten minutes or so later we were seated at a lucky table. 

We started off with the Spring Rolls. My wife ordered Cold Noodles - with Flamed Broiled Shrimp and Pork. I got their Flamed Broiled Pork Chop served with Steamed Rice. 

Some entrée items on the menu had two pricing columns one for lunch and one for dinner (slightly higher priced), which I found interesting. Other items on menu included pho, Chinese soups, stir-fried noodles and clay pot dishes. 

After a few minutes the spring rolls made its debut. My mouth was immediately filled with a nice refreshing minty flavor. The peanut sauce premixed with sriracha gave it a nice bang. Priced at four ninety-nine for two rolls cut in half, it was ok. There's really nothing special about these rolls versus the ones I've had in other places. 

Sad to say, my wife did not like her cold noodles. It lacked bean sprouts; the pork was short in flavor and the shrimp tasted boiled. 

I on the other hand, loved my pork chops! My wife took a dib and she agreed. It was perfectly cooked. I couldn't stop myself from shoveling steamed rice as a chaser. Bottom line it was the bomb! 

This place offered plenty of seating and group friendly. Service was fair. 

Overall, the Golden Flower experience was a-okay...

Food was fine. Nothing to write home to mom about. Had a weird time here. I have a minor allergy to tree nuts and this place is making me feel like crap about it. Allergy is pretty managed, not severe or life threatening and I am A-okay when I just avoid eating nuts. Places that cook etc. in the same space are fine for me and I worked at an ice cream shop serving up nuts for 5+ years. I do not warn everywhere I go that I have an allergy because if a dish features nuts that's nearly always called out because it's a pretty known allergen and my life isn't at risk. When I do end up eating nuts, I become extremely uncomfortable but I'm not going to dive into my symptoms ha but I'll say that walnuts are the worst. 

The ~pastry of the day~ was a zucchini muffin which was cool because you don't see those very often. My friend gave me a small bite and when put it down I saw a walnut baked in and knew I was about to have a time. Was traveling that day and was saved when my friend had a spare claritin. I was pretty disappointed that there was no mention that this was a zucchini nut muffin because I could have just not taken a bite. We told our waiter who gave an apology because what else was he going to say? The manager noticed our table's distress and reaction to this lack of remorse and came over to address the situation which from what I got from it, was that it was on me for not mentioning my nut allergy at the onset of the meal. That was MADDENING! Sure, I can ask and let everyone know, but how about the server ask if anyone has an allergy too? Or better yet, label the item on the menu (not the special menu which was where this was) as containing such. Putting a disclaimer at the bottom of the main menu that 1. doesn't mention nuts only shellfish and gluten and 2. just requests the customer speak up doesn't cover any kind of base. You can't guarantee someone reads and you also aren't stating everything! We were appalled that there was no accountability from the restaurant and that not listing that muffin as containing nuts was the bigger issue for me over not having a conversation, which is something I don't typically have to do because allergens are stated. 

I'm upset too because the business owner replied to another review on my friend's experience here and called my eating at a restaurant and not saying "I can't eat nuts" as "reckless and disrespectful" and that I need to take responsibility for myself. What good does it do to say that to a paying customer? Where is the remorse? If you weren't going to print the allergen on the menu, at least let the team know that day that there are nuts in the baked good. I'm sorry I didn't come in with my allergy on my sleeve that day but I'm even more sorry that an establishment had the reaction that they did over someone else's discomfort. It's one thing to not state that this dish has nuts but it turned into a completely other issue when the reaction from the business was to shift the fault onto the customer. I have never felt so uncomfortable speaking up for myself and I can't believe a restaurant has let that happen.

The Pub offers Casual Waterfront Dining on their Outdoor Patio with Covered Seating, Fans for those Hot Summer Days/Nights, and Complete with an Outdoor Full Bar! Indoors you will find spacious seating along with Water Views and another Full Indoor Bar! They also host Live Music! 

Parking is abundant here whether you arrive by Boat or Car. Their Private Parking Lot does get full during Peak Hours so arrive early and catch an Early Bird Special that runs Daily from 11-6pm! Also, on the Weekends they have Breakfast! Saturday is served from 8am-12pm and Sunday Brunch Buffet is 8am-12pm for $11.95. 

On both occasions here we have come for Beverages and Food sitting on their Outdoor Patio Dock. Their Draft Beer is served Cold, Cocktails are good if you stick with the basic's; but for a rather poor/watered down cocktail they seem to hit the mark if you order Margarita/Rum Runners/Mudslides/Etc.. 

Food is nothing more than Casual Pub Style Fare.  On our first visit my husband and I decided to split the Captain Sampler. This is NOT a sharing plate. Neither one of us left satisfied or any bit of full although it was not a fulfilling dish the Seafood was not horrible. Their Salads always come out fresh with a good portion sizes. As for our last visit we came for a couple of Appetizers. We ordered the Seared Sesame Tuna and the Blackened Wings! The Wings were Gigantic and Flavorful but as for the Tuna the Temperature was off leaving it a bit flat/dull tasting. 

A Waterfront Style Hangout spot that is perfect for relaxing and watching the Boats go by! The views are amazing and the service will allow you to enjoy oneself! Stop by their Gift Shop on the way out of you would like to take some Pub Merchandise Home with you!

Their steak sandwich slapped! This was my second time eating a Philly cheesesteak (hold the cheese) sandwich and I can without a doubt say Ishkabibble's surpassed my first experience. 

I haven't quite mastered what to get on my sandwich yet, but the guy behind the counter was patient and guided me through the options. In the end I got a steak sandwich, no cheese, with peppers and onions and fries. What I got tasted incredible. Unlike my first experience, Ishkabibble's loaded the sandwich with meat and actually gave it flavor! And the bread--oooh the bread!! It was chewy and amazing as it should be! Half a sandwich is honestly enough to fill you up. I had to eat the other half at another time.

The only downsides are the fries and the price. The fries were too soggy for me. It was okay, but soggy fries are just not my preference. And the price was way too much. It might be because it's located on south street, but I probably could have gotten the same quality or better for cheaper somewhere else in Philly. 

Overall it was a good experience. I don't know if I'll come here again because of the price, but this was definitely a good start to my Philly Steak sandwich lifestyle!

This was a really cute chill spot for dessert and bubble tea. I took a few of my out of town friends here on a "walking tour" in the city. I really liked how each seating area is a bit sectioned off so you can have some privacy. 

Once we arrived we were immediately seated and we ordered through their website on our phones. That was pretty convenient since we could browse, select our choices and pay separately. More restaurants need to do this!!

They had a lot of optioned to choose from. I ended up selecting the molten lava cake with vanilla ice cream. It was pretty good but if I come back, I'd definitely choose a crepe cake my my friends did!

Interesting concept - no phone, cash only, 2 tables, no chairs, open Wednesday - Saturday 530-1030pm, can only buy pies (no slices), 1 cook, average wait time is 1-2 hours. 

Is the inconvenience worth it? No. We had the tomato pie which is made with whole milk mozzarella, old gold aged cheese, and extra virgin olive oil. We added Cremini mushrooms and arugula. The pizza tasted very, very fresh. You can tell the ingredients were good quality. We liked the pizza a lot. 

However, the aforementioned inconvenience will probably make us not come back. If I am in the mood for pizza, I'm not going to walk/drive to a place, order, and then come back in 2 hours to pick it up. There are other great pizza spots in the city that make their pizza more readily available.

Delicious gin and tonic homemade daiquiris! They are known for their wings but I havent tried them yet. I have been here for their whole roasted pig and live music out front. I adore this place. Festive, fun, inexpensive!

I came in on another afternoon, a Monday, while brunch/bar hopping with a girlfriend in the middle of the afternoon. While we were there, Susan Spicer stopped in for wings. Just as she left, Bruce "Sunpie" Barnes came in for boudin. Now....those two things alone should be enough of a stamp of approval to get you there. Another great one by Chef Nathaniel Zimet!

Forget the food for a second. It's always sweltering hot in New Orleans. Wherever you go, you sweat. Every part of your body is moist - and not in the "I just ate a deliciously moist cupcake" kind of way. You're walking all over town. You're hungry, but you're not thinking about food. You're thinking about cooling off. You could go to the casino, or perhaps stop into a hotel lobby for a quick respite from the heat and humidity. But if you really want to cool off - if you really want to turn your body's moistness into a chilly frost and bring your temperature down to almost absolute zero - stop into Lüke.

Lüke restaurant is, without a doubt, the coldest restaurant on Earth, and perhaps beyond. If you sit directly beneath the cooling vent like my wife and I did - both times we visited, no less - you could probably die.  Or, if you're like me, you'll absolutely love it. I'm a polar bear and find myself in my natural habitat when I am here. Thank you, thank you, John Besh. Thank you, Lüke. Thank you for being a freezing cold oasis in an otherwise deathly urban desert.

Now onto the food...

As I mentioned before, my wife and I came here twice. That is, two times, during a 4-day vacation. In a place like New Orleans where there is SO MUCH good food everywhere you look, it is almost sacrilege to eat in the same place twice in one trip. (Good thing it was so hot out.)

The first time we came in for breakfast, and it was awesome. I had the classic southern staple: a fried chicken biscuit with a spicy mayhaw glaze. I have no idea what the hell mayhaw is, but it was so yummy and decadent, I felt like I needed to be spanked afterward. My wife had the egg white frittata, complete with burrata cheese and Covey Rise vegetables. (Whatever that means.) For a healthy dish, it looked absolutely delicious. She loved it. 

Of course, breakfast in New Orleans would not be complete without the obligatory basket of powdered beignets.  You can get them with chocolate dipping sauce or a fresh berry jam. We opted for the blueberry jam. Absolutely amazing. 

Lüke also makes a mean Bloody Mary - almost a little too mean for my taste. It's not that I mind the spiciness.  In fact, I love that. But the Lüke Bloody Mary is just so crimson red and flavorfully intense, with an eerie viscosity that reminds me a little too much of actual blood. Still, try one. Just one gave me a buzz that lasted all morning long.

The second time we came for brunch. No chicken biscuit on this menu, but lots of other options. I was so hungover during this meal that as I am drafting this review on a plane with no Internet, I can't even remember off the top of my head what the hell me or my wife ordered, but I do remember it being really good. (For more on my hangover, see my review for the Clover Café.)

UPDATE: Having cheated and looked back at the menu, I can now recall our bizarre order: the heirloom tomato salad, Mimi's buttermilk pancakes with the honey-pecan butter, and an order of the house fries. We just shared it all, and no evidence remained once we were done. Yeah, everything is that good.

All in all I would give Lüke a solid 4.5 stars. But since Yelp doesn't allow half-star ratings, I'm more than happy to give Lüke a 5.  Service was very friendly both times, though they do get busy and it may be a little difficult to get your check. But at least they don't try to rush you out and turn your table. I really hate that. (For more on how much I hate that, see my review for Emeril's.)

Bottom line: Don't skip Lüke if you come to New Orleans.

Kyoto Restuarant in Santa Barbara has been around since 1981, but over the years, its has been open with 5 different owners. Currently it is Korean owned and Sushi Chefs are Korean, too, although like most Korean owned Japanese Restaurants, they have learned how to say "Welcome" in Japanese to fool the non-Japanese who come here. 
(Hai, Irashai, [Yes, Welcome] Irashaimasen [Welcome, a little more formally])

Aside from the little Sushi Bar, Kyoto has a pretty complete menu of traditional Japanese dishes, Hibachi grill items like Yakitori or Saba Shioyaki and about 4 different Teriyaki; Tempura, Noodles like Udon and Soba, including cold Zaru Soba and fried Yaki Soba, and Sukiyaki. They even have Oju dishes, which you might recognize as Donburi (Tempura, pork cutlet or chicken/egg over a large rice bowl.) Although Una Ju (Eel) is usually served in a special little bento like dish with a cover.

They do have 3 larger combo Special meals, too. They have a very reasonable mix and match Lunch special for only $7.95, so prices are reasonable here, and they have a lot of local regulars, although business is slow right now. 

And of course, being Korean owned, they offer a Yaku Niku, which is a Japanese version of Korean Barbeque. 

Imagine that: A Korean owned Japanese restaurant offering a Japanese version of the classic Korean barbeque, eaten by Caucasians in Santa Barbara, home to the Haas Avacado, which is popular in a California Roll, which is a US invention and is hard to find in Japan.

I am confused!

Ijji Sushi is sort of like AYCE Sushi meets a Korean owned Chili's, or something like that. 

It appears to be Korean owned, with Latino Sushi Chefs and wait staff, serving Americanized Japanese food to all comers here in Sparks, Nevada. 

This place is huge, with dozens of tables and a long, long sushi bar that seats perhaps 30 people.  The decor is modern and new looking, pleasing and clean. The service is very attentive and on the spot, and friendly. 

The food is another matter. 

Like when you were a fussy eating kid at your parent's dinner table, this is one of those AYCE places that penalizes you for not eating all your food. NO, they don't make you do the dishes, and no starving kids in China and India will die because you didn't finish your plate. However, you will have to pay for your eyes being bigger than your stomach, it says so right on the menu. 

Personally, I don't like sushi places that are AYCE at all because the sushi is never good nor authentic.  And fearing a penalty is even more ridiculous and a good reason not to come.

So why did I come here? Well, there aren't that many Japanese restaurants in Sparks, Nevada, and this was the closest one I could find. I knew that hoping for good Asian food at Trader Dick's inside of John Ascuaga's Nugget wasn't going to serve me, well, a nugget of an authentic Asian meal. 

So we ordered combo Bento boxes for dinner. These sounded good and reasonable on the menu. But when I was served the Sashimi, Tempura and Salmon teriyaki combo, I was disappointed. The Sashimi consisted of 2 small slices of Salmon. That's it.  I was given a lot of edamame and salad to fill me up. The Tempura was meh at best with the wrong type of dipping bowl, and the Salmon was probably the best part at just OK.  At least the Salmon pieces were in the shape of fish. 

If you are from Sparks, Verdi, Mogul or Minden Nevada and eat Japanese food once every other year, this place may be great for you. Oyster shooters for you yahoos with your AYCE. But If you are from SF or LA, you may consider passing, or accept that it is what it is, if you are just desperate for some Asian flavors, not Japanese food. 

BTW, my favorite relative, who had chicken and beef teriyaki with california roll combo, had diarrhea for the next 48 hours after eating here. And she didn't have a shooter, at least not from her ingesting orifice.

Finally made it! I had heard great things and it definitely lived up to the hype. It's owned by a guy who came from Pappy's, so you know it's got to be quality BBQ.  We got there for a late lunch on a Sunday, so the wait was only about 5 minutes. The Tri Tip (Sirloin cut) sandwich with the allure of a better cut of meat than brisket won me over. Paired with potato salad and beans, all were fantastic. They have 3 sauces, Cranberry Cayenne (fruity, but with a good kick), Sweet Jane (sweet and smoky), and Carolina Vinegar (thinner consistency, tangy and kick-y). I got outvoted on sauce preference, so the table's vote went to the Cranberry Cayenne (Jane was my preference). The potato salad wa sone of the best I've ever had and the beans were smoky and delicious. They have about 10 tables inside and a few outside, perfect for a lazy Sunday afternoon. 

Pros: great food, good sides
Cons: limited seating

I love this place. They recently (6 months maybe?) moved into their new location from their old one by the Debaliviere metro station. The old restaurant used to be the Rhine Haus - a poorly run German restaurant. Though I do miss the free happy hours that the Rhine Haus provided, I am extremely glad the Kitchen Sink moved into the space. 

So far I've had the etouffee, jumbalaya, and the IDK (I don't know) and have never been disappointed. The etouffee with andouille sausage was very good, but had a good amount of heat (like it should I guess), but fair warning. The jumbalaya ($9) was a little less spicy, and was awesome. The IDK is a fun concept -- the chef prepares something totally random for you -- you can't have any dietary restrictions or preferences though -- totally up to the discretion of the chef. I got a skirt steak that was incredible -- they had to have marinated it overnight for how tender it was. Definitely a winner. Oh, and the corn fritters are little pieces of heaven. 

Special note: currently, they don't have a liquor license, but you can BYOB and they don't even charge a fee!

Also, it takes a decent (not too long) amount of time to get the food out, but it's well worth the wait -- I wouldn't want fast Cajun food anyway. Also, this place is cheap for the quantity and quality of food you get. Check it out!!

Pros: great food, inexpensive, friendly staff
Cons: no alcohol, but you can bring your own; atmosphere could be improved a little

The outdoor setting is fantastic and the service was exceptional!

However, the owner, Serena, might want to focus her gossip elsewhere! We had some wine (with water and food) only to hear her discussing us with the bartender! We were quiet and friendly the entire time!

FYI SERENA if you're going to talk about your customers, make sure they can't hear you! I've heard through the years that you're a terrible employer, now I understand why! 

We were quiet and reserved throughout our experience at your restaurant. Hearing you discuss us was a complete disgrace! We likely won't be back. I'm writing this as I sit at your bar...

Ah, Carnivore, I have always wanted to try you!  It was destiny.... just a street away from our original destination of " ___ on the Hill".  After an unwelcoming reception there and promise of an hour wait, we simply walked a little farther and around the corner and into Carnivore. It's in a big historic warehouse type-building that was lovingly restored and quite magnificent inside with marble floors and  grand woodwork. The upstairs is an event space, downstairs the restaurant. While the building lobby and restroom floors could really use a good sweep/scrub, the restaurant itself was immaculate and pleasing to the eye.
We were looking for some yummy appetizers ala STL like toasted ravs, to introduce a guest from out of town to one of our most famous neighborhoods. Even though the original plan was not a steakhouse, I knew others had spoken highly of Carnivore. They even had toasted ravioli on the menu, as well as pastas and flatbreads, so we decided to stay. So glad we did. The whole staff was friendly, attentive and warm. I just got a really good vibe and after the delivery of our appetizers, I knew we made an excellent choice. The toasted ravs were perfect: parm dusted and crispy , the meat filling velvety and rich, and the accompanying marinara was very good. We also ordered the Bruschetta, which was a wonderful version: the tangy fresh tomato and basil mixture blanketed with a bit of gooey cheese atop the crisp bread rounds. Addictive....
Our guest ordered the juicy house burger with pepper jack cheese which was huge, perfectly charred and looked like someone made it just for her at a family cookout. It came with a choice of side and she got a white sauced pasta. She said both were exceptional.
My daughter and I ordered a Caesar salad and an Herbivore salad (mixed lettuces, spinach, feta, pimientos, parm, croutons, Italian viniagrette). And since the restaurant is named Carnivore, we had to try the steak, so for a few dollars extra, added it to our salads. You can also add chicken or shrimp. The salads were fresh and beautiful looking, and tasty!  I especially enjoyed the house made croutons!  Sadly, our steak came in small chunks and was cooked well done  (I should have asked, but I mistakenly assumed since this was a steak forward restaurant, it would be served medium rare/medium and/or cut in slices from an actual sirloin. It was still " just okay", but was just missing that good steak sear and flavor).

We had a very good experience here overall. The service was excellent, food nice, portions large, and I would highly recommend. When we come back next time with bigger appetites, I want to try the real steaks or chops. They also had a sweet Happy Hour menu.

Yes, it's a chain and yes you could compare it to Applebee's or Ruby Tuesday but I find Cheddars to be far superior. In fact there is a Ruby Tuesday right next door, that CLOSED for business within six weeks of Cheddars showing up. In the world of cards, that's called a "tell"

I love the food here. The prices are really good, serving sizes are generous and they pay attention to detail. I've had many of the menu items and while some are better than others, none of them are bad and you always get your food served at the proper temperature and freshness. Hot food is always hot, salads crisp and cold. 

I find the fried shrimp to be a stand out. It's plenty to split between two people and leave full. Served with two sides for $9.99 you just can't beat that. Love the club and Monte Cristo sammys, onion rings are good and stacked but bloated me after eating like three or four so I pass on those but what a value for $4.19 The tortilla soup is also really good. The sides don't dissapoint either, I could (and often do lol) make a meal out of the broccoli casserole alone.

Drinks are good but the "Painkiller, limit two" is a joke with little alcohol in it. Menu gimmick fo sho. Rum Runners and the Bloody Mary's are good.

I will close with saying that I have never had bad food here and I always recieve excellent service. Like I said, you CAN compare it with the other chains but there is really no comparison at the end of the day.

We had dinner here tonight and it was wonderful.  We were warmly welcomed and seated at a table for 4 and given menus.  Water was poured and we were each given warm jalapeno cornbread muffins and brioche rolls, both small, along w/ a ramekin of butter w/ a paper  covering w/ the NOLA logo to share.  Sherri ordered a Manhattan, I ordered a Lemondrop, Alan ordered a Turbodog and Ron ordered a glass of Malbec.

The restaurant is a spacious renovated warehouse w/ a second floor balcony reached by a glass elevator.  Our server was professional and friendly, backed up by the people who poured our water and gave us bread.  Alan and I decided to share a salad of Maine lobster and celery root tossed in a green onion-buttermilk dressing w/ roasted beets, spiced walnuts and arugula.  It arrived divided and it was divine, a savory mixture of tastes and textures.  Sherri had a Caesar salad, which she enjoyed.  Alan and Ron ordered garlic crusted drum cooked in the wood burning oven with Brabant potatoes, crimini mushrooms, bacon and sauce beurre rouge;  Ron substituted sweet potatoes for the Brabant potatoes and their accoutrements.  Sherri ordered gumbo and I ordered the hickory-roasted duck w/ whiskey-caramel glaze, buttermilk cornbread pudding, haricot verts-fire roasted corn salad, natural jus and candied pecans.  My duck was a generous portion, beautifully cooked and presented.  It was one of the best ducks I've had and the cornbread pudding and the salad of haricort verts and corn were totally delicious.  Sherri loved her gumbo and Alan and Ron were both pleased w/ their drum, although Alan commented he won't have it again after having it twice today.  Service and food were comfortable and unpretentious and we very much enjoyed our dinner.

This morning Alan went out walking and shopping w/ Sherri and Ron while I stayed back to sit in the garden and read.  He returned around 1:00 w/ lunch from Verti Marte, a grilled shrimp po'boy and a roast beef sandwich plus a couple of bananas.  He joined me at the table in the garden.  Both sandwiches were on seeded rolls and were still warm.  The roast beef was on a bun rather than a po'boy roll and was in smallish pieces w/a delicious dark gravy.  The po'boy was cut in half so we started w/ it.  The shrimp were plump, sweet and mildly spicy, everything the shrimp in the first po'boy we had at Market Cafe were not, and the bread was wonderful, soft yet sturdy and studded w/ sesame seeds.  After finishing the po'boy we just picked at the beef, which was excellent and flavorful, but more food than we needed and we ended up throwing most of it away.  The po'boy was $10, the same cost as the one from Market Cafe, but well worth the money.  The beef sandwich was only $4.50, an astonishing price given the quality and quantity of the food.  Verti Marte was an excellent find on Alan's part, thanks to his iPhone and Yelp.

We had dinner here tonight.  I had bookmarked it after reading Joi's rave review and then this morning Vincent our innkeeper gave it high praise.  We hailed a cab and were delivered to Mimi's.  Our cabbie was funny and knowledgeable, even giving us a dining recommendation for another night at Mr. B's when Sherri asked about crawfish etouffée.

We walked in to the ground floor bar and were greeted by two friendly black dogs before heading upstairs.  There are two worn flights of stairs w/ handrails that were slightly wobbly, but they got us upstairs and down.  We walked into a dining room that was empty save for the bartender who also served as our waitress.  The decor was interesting, a series of mounted tattooed baby dolls hanging on the walls that reminded me of the weird Barbies at Rudy's Can't Fail Café.  We were pretty hungry, having eaten only lightly at midday because we were on a city tour that started at 1:00.  Sherri ordered a martini, as did I.  Ron ordered a rum and coke and Alan ordered a mixed drink whose name I forget.  It was like a mai tai but different.

Tapas are about as ideal a way to eat as I can think of.  Lots of little bits, bites and tastes.  We ordered mushroom Manchego toast, a steak which Vincent had recommended, the goat cheese croquettes, shrimp and garlic and a grilled romaine salad at the recommendation of our hostess.  As we ordered, a party of 12 arrived and gradually more people filed in.  Every dish was delicious.  We next ordered braised pork, mixed olives from the cold tapas menu, and more steak and salad plus an order of mushrooms, garlic, herbs and white wine.  Dishes were brought to us singly and in groups and they were most satisfying.  The mushrooms were huge and wonderfully flavorful, but everything was good if not great.  Service was warm, friendly and fast.  Sherri and I each had another martini.  A band was due to start playing at 10:00 but it was 9:00 and we were tired after our city tour and ready to move on.  The room was pretty much full when we left and more people were arriving.  The bartender ordered us a cab which arrived shortly and we were on our way back to our B&B.  Except Sherri and Ron, who were on a hunt for dessert.

This didn't start off well.  We walked in to the restaurant  and the woman at the hostess stand was on the phone dealing w/ staffing issues.  She didn't acknowledge our presence.  As Alan remarked later, that's a back office thing to be doing and it's tacky to do it at the hostess stand.  Fortunately there was another woman there who was dealing w/ customers and she took us to a table.

We were given menus and a wine list.  I ordered a glass of Malbec and our server responded, approvingly, "Argentina!".  Alan ordered iced tea.  I was debating between prime rib and chicken but when Alan asked whether they had ribeye, I was seduced when they said they had.  We ordered half an order of onion rings and opted for the salad bar rather than soup.  Beans came w/ the steak and we both ordered a baked potato w/ fixings on the side.

The salad bar was pretty good, w/ pickled beets, broccoli florets, red onions that I didn't take and Alan pronounced "sharp", cherry tomatoes, baby corn and a variety of already prepared salads.  The blue cheese dressing didn't taste much of blue cheese.  The lettuce was crisp and fresh, although some of the tomatoes were a little mushy.  The onion rings were tasty.  The steaks were pretty good, though not as flavorful as we've had elsewhere.  I regretted not ordering the chicken or the prime rib.  The steak knives were not up to the task of cutting the meat.  They were much too lightweight for a steakhouse.  The potatoes were good, just the right size.

The high point of our evening was our server, Laurie, who was enthusiastic, personable and really cool.  She made good, authentic contact and kept things running smoothly.

Not as stellar tonight, although the tableside salsa was delicious, as were the chips, and the lobster stuffed portabello was marvelous.  But the margarita mix didn't taste freshly squeezed in our house margaritas and I found the pollo molé very disappointing.  The molé at Juan's Place or 3 Hermanas at home is much more complex.  This was heavy-handed and the chicken was on the dry side.  The rice and beans were good.  Alan had the molcajete w/ seafood, chicken and steak and he found the chicken and steak dry.  The seafood was delicious.  It was a huge portion, which he couldn't finish.  I had flan for dessert and it was lovely.  A trio came around to sing and they were wonderful.

Last night we  met a man Alan had gone to high school in Sioux City w/ and his wife for dinner here. We sat in the enclosed covered front patio which was kept warm by heaters.  You enter the space via a cement ramp from the sidewalk.  It almost feels like crossing a moat.  They were already seated when we arrived and F. recognized Alan despite not having seen him for more than 50 years.  That was pretty cool.

We looked over the menu and decided to split a farmers market salad.  It contained roasted squash, brussels sprouts, baby beets, quinoa, goat cheese and marcona almond.  It arrived split and was just as delicious as it sounds.  I ordered one of their cocktails, the Lavender Bees Knees, consisting of Tanqueray gin, local honey and lavender bitters.  It was well balanced, the honey evident, but not too sweet.  Very good drink.  For mains, Alan ordered ling cod fish and chips and I ordered crisp skin chicken, citrus braised thighs, crimini mushroom and smashed potato while F. ordered trout plus a salad to start and H. ordered a farmers market salad.  We had a plate of crusty slices of bread accompanied by delicious, fruity olive oil. Alan was very pleased w/ his fish and chips and my chicken was very tasty.  Our server was very patient as we chatted before ordering.  It was a well prepared dinner and a nice evening of catching up and conversation.

After a lovely afternoon of listening to groups in the Crescent City Jazz Festival, a two day outdoor collegiate and high school jazz festival, we walked over to Cafe Beignet for...what else?  Last time in NOLA we had gone to Cafe du Monde, but after Ron and Sherri strolled through a couple of mornings ago and were put off by offensive smells, we decided to try Cafe Beignet, which had been recommended by my friend Alexandra, who praised their less hyped freshness.  We ordered two orders for the three of us, since Alan doesn't eat sweets.  I had iced tea, Alan had iced coffee and Sherri and Ron had coffee.  We sat out in the patio, where we could hear music from just up the street.  There were several groups playing in Royal as we walked along. The street was blocked off for music.  As we drank our drinks and awaited our beignets we watched one of the local cats curl up on the shelf beneath the adjacent table after washing himself thoroughly.  Soon the delivery man came out w/ our beignets.  I protected my blouse w/ a napkin and enjoyed first one, then another.  They were heavenly.  I'm not a fan of doughnuts, but I definitely a fan of these.  Thank goodness there are no beignets in California to match them, or if there are, I haven't tasted them, so I'm safe.  These were a great treat.  Later I realized I had not protected my black pants, which were now dusted w/ white which had drifted through the open work table.  Happily what I couldn't brush off washed off when we got back to our B&B.

We enjoyed the jazz brunch here this morning. We walked from our B&B and were a little late but were seated promptly nonetheless.  As we walked in we passed in front of the trio that was playing and they smiled and greeted us.  We were seated at a 4 top right in front of them.  We looked over the menu and had some questions.  Our server, David, was courtly and helpful, particularly in answering my question about the spice level of the shrimp and grits, saying it wasn't too spicy for him but those w/ a low spice tolerance might not be comfortable eating it.  Just what I wanted to know.

Alan and I had iced teas, Ron ordered coffee w/ his entree and Sherri ordered a mimosa w/ hers.  Alan and I shared a Salad Midi w/ sliced tomatoes, avocados and basil chiffonade w/ crumbled feta, dressed in a tasty champagne vinaigrette.  Alan ordered pecan crusted puppy drum, a small drum fish w/ oven roasted pecan and Louisiana crawfish relish, laced with a lemon butter sauce.  The rest of us ordered Muriel's Eggs Benedict, which are served on house baked buttermilk biscuits, w/ thinly sliced Chisesi ham and poached eggs topped with chive Hollandaise; served with grilled asparagus and Parmesan broiled tomato.  The Eggs Benedict were wonderful, the biscuits a nice alternative to English muffins, the ham sliced paper thin so it cut easily, the eggs perfectly poached w/ runny yolks and the Hollandaise flavorful and nicely balanced.  The asparagus and tomatoes were lovely and tasted so good.  Waters and iced teas were refilled promptly.

Our dining room was painted a strong,dark red, w/ a collage celebrating absinthe on one wall above an ornate and elegant piece of dark wood furniture whose function I couldn't determine.  On another wall was a gorgeously intricate carved wood framed mirror.  The dining room opposite had brick walls and the third dining room near the bar had once been outdoors in the original house.  After playing a set in our dining room the group moved to the dining room across the hall to play another set, then on to the bar/dining room before returning to us.  It was a good way to spread the music around.  The setting was beautiful, the food was excellent and service was smoothly accommodating.  We would return.

We met our friend Bleep here tonight for dinner.  This place is amazing.  The ambiance is not elegant.  It's a former A&W Root Beer stand and you can still see its fast food bones, but who cares?  We sat out on the patio.  Our server was attentive and helpful.  She described the night's specials and they all sounded good.  Alan and I decided to split a beet salad.  Had we known how big the portions were we wouldn't have done that, but it was soooo good!  It came unsplit so we asked for an extra plate and split it ourselves.  Alan's not a fan of goat cheese, so I got that, but we both loved the beets and the tomato slices and the lightly dressed field greens.

Bleep ordered a glass of Chardonnay and I a glass of old vine Zinfandel.  The pours were generous.  We were brought bread and butter.  Alan tasted the bread and confirmed it was as crusty and tasty as it looked.  I didn't have any.  Bleep ordered the sea bass, Alan ordered the pistachio crusted New Zealand rack of lamb and I ordered the New Zealand venison.  I haven't had venison in decades, but remember seeing domestically raised deer in pastures as we drove in New Zealand and decided to try it.  All three were specials, so I don't have a menu to check for details, so they will be lacking.  Portions were enormous, the mains well cooked and the sides interesting and well seasoned.  None of us could finish our meal.  Bleep had enough to bring home.  Alan left one of his chops, there were so many.  My venison was delicious, a large chunk and not gamey in the same way wild venison is.  We couldn't even contemplate dessert.  Prices were extremely low for the quality and quantity of food.  The one off note was the styrofoam containers for leftovers.  Living close to Berkeley,  which has outlawed styrofoam, I expect containers to be either compostable or recyclable.  Styrofoam doesn't fit w/ the excellence or consciousness of the food and I hope the owners will invest in more eco-friendly containers.  We would be willing to pay an extra premium for that and I hope others would too.  We left mightily impressed w/ this fine addition to the Tucson dining scene.

So this burger joint probably best in town..this location bast in town..I don't like the other two locations Glendale and S Mccaran the one on S Mccaaren is a EXPRESS Why? Some please tell me so I can tell Yelp..But back to This Baddass location...no matter what you order..no matter how you order it..no matter how many items you order..it will come out to you They way you ordered it! To perfection!!! Just a heads up it is a bit pricy but worth every Bite every Sip ever BURP and every  DAM THIS IS BOMB And better grab a lot of napkins! I usually double cheese burger no veggies mix only and chilli fries So So Good! If live in Reno/sparks/Carson and you haven't had Juicys..do me a favor kick your self all the way here..and thank me later...time to eat..

Attached to the Grand Hyatt hotel right on Tampa Bay, Oystercatchers had a terrific view of the water and a nice intimate outdoor deck overlooking it.  Sadly, this was late January and the sun was well set by our 6PM reservation so we didn't see any of it, but we were assured of the marvelous view by the staff and other diners.  Happily, the food was no disappointment and the ambiance and service quite made up for it!  My colleagues and I started with their Grande Seafood tower, 3 large trays filled with oysters (New England provenance - which amused us as we were from RI - MA Wellfleets and CT Bluepoints), Gulf shrimp, big stone crab claws, and a (Maine) lobster.  It also came with domestic caviar (a bit blander than the Russian sturgeon, however, but still a nice bougie treat).  The accompanying sauces were good too, with a spicy mignonette and a surprisingly good mustard sauce for the lobster.   I followed that with a local fish - pan-roasted gulf grouper - which was excellent and meaty, big chunky pieces.   It was accompanied by a solid goat cheese risotto. Their desserts were also well-executed; we shared an outstandingly good peanut butter cup in phyllo pastry (very flaky!); an excellent key lime pie, and a good creme brulee.  Next time we'll time our meal better to coincide with a spectacular sunset, and then I'm sure I'll raise the rating up to 5 stars!

Tony's famous tomato pie is a staple in Mayfair. People seem to worship this Tomato pie. I am not one of them. I like it dont get me wrong but I am not one that worships at the altar. It is a very thin pie with a crunchy crust and is very tasty. There is only off street parking and it can be very tuff at times. The restaurant has a strip of booths alongside some raised little tables. The staff is very professional and courteous. The atmosphere is that of a normal bar restaurant. It is pretty dark and very cozy. I have not had many other things off of the menu besides the tomato pie but what I have had was very good. I am completely satisfied with this restaurant and would definitely recommend it to anyone. I will continue to pop in every once in a while like I have been for years.

From the owners that brought you Bamboo Terrace a new exciting midtown Mexican food restaurant. You always feel like you've had everything you could imagine here in Tucson and when it comes to Mexican food. But now El Chinito gordo brings you a new twist. A nice revamped formally club 21 location right off of miracle Mile and Oracle. Space is great renovated and very clean. They have a very nice bar area where you could sit and order drinks. Seating was very fast and did not take long to get a seat for three. It was opening weekend and we were excited to try it out.

Once we got our table, the server came over very quickly. Gave us our menus and let us know what the specials were and what they recommended. Everything on the menu looked very good and the pricing was pretty comparable to most restaurants around the downtown Midtown area. It was a little higher price for Mexican food but understandable since it is more of a modern twist. They had a nice drink menu as well, plenty of different drinks and beers that you could order.

We decided to try out the green corn tamales, the chile relleno with shrimp, and some wings as an appetizer. The wings came out first and we were pleasantly surprised with the flavor. The flavor was a jicama barbecue sauce that was very flavorful and stuck to the bones very well. They were very delicious and complemented our drinks really well. I personally just got a beer, and my wife decided on the watermelon jalapeño margarita. She said that it was one of the best margaritas that she's had and she definitely recommends it to whoever goes to the restaurant. We received
We received our entrées, and they were a nice portion. The rice and beans were fantastic and we also got Calabasitas with our order and those had lots of flavor as well. The corn tamales were nice and big, they also had a lot of flavor and they placed a tomatillo salsa on top of them that complemented the corn tamales very well. The shrimp chile relleno was amazing. It came with Culichi sauce that had tons of flavor and made the dish. This was the best dish that we had out of all three of them. Definitely recommend getting this when you go.

Overall we were very satisfied with the portions and the flavor of the food. The drinks were very well-made the beer was nice and cold and we will definitely be back to try some of the other entrées that they have to offer. They do offer a weekly specials as well and happy hour specials also.

My date took me here for my birthday last week and I was a bit disappointed with the menu but overall, it was a good experience. I saw their menu on their website beforehand so I knew what I wanted to order, but when we arrived and got seated with the menu, the menu was totally different from what was online. There were no escargot with blue cheese (I was intended to ordering that), no elk, bison, etc. For appetizers, we had calamari and porsuitto. Entrees, my date ordered the peppercorn ny steak and I had the veal. Both entrees were filled with flavor and the steak was cooked perfectly. Dessert was the best part, we ordered the tiramisu and the armeritto ice cream. They were divine, especially the ice cream because it was homemade and fresh.

I'd heard all the hype in the paper on this new restaurant, so I decided to try it out with my girlfriend and four year old daughter on the evening of 5/7/13. As I walked up to the open front door, the hostess asked me if I had a reservation or if I had just decided to stop in. I told her I did not have a reservation, but would like to eat dinner. She then smiled and told me that there was a 45 minute wait. I quickly glanced into the restaurant and noticed it appeared to only be about half full with several open tables. The hostess then told me that there were several reservations set for 7pm. I glanced at my watch and realized it was approximately 7:10pm. I told the hostess I couldn't wait 45 minutes and turned around and walked out.

I walked less than  1/2 city block and realized that nothing that had just occurred made any sense to me. I pulled out my cell phone and googled the number for the restaurant (520-396-3357) and called at approximately 7:13pm. The young lady that answered the phone advised me that there was no wait time for a reservation set for 7:15pm. She even clarified that 7:15pm was only minutes away, and asked if I was close by. I assured her I was, and promptly walked back  1/2 city block and immediately asked the hostess to speak with a manager.

I pulled the manager to the side to avoid making a scene. I explained facts of the night to her, to which she advised that she was the lady that had set my reservation on the phone. She then told me they had re-arranged seating and there was more space available now and that a reservation had cancelled. The seating inside looked the same to me. I asked her when that reservation had cancelled. She told me it was cancelled 10 minutes prior. I pointed out that 5 minutes prior, I was standing at the door trying to get a table. I suggested that in the future, perhaps they should try to re-arrange seating when a customer is asking for a table. The manager was polite, but totally unapologetic about the service I had received. I never told her that I felt the incident could be racially motivated, but asked her to try to look at this incident from my point of view and to try to see how this incident looked. Again, no apology....but she offered to seat me at that point. I declined to be seated after explaining that I only returned to inform management of my experience and that I would eat at another restaurant down the street. I then walked  1/2 block away and had a delish dinner at The Hub. I know this was a long read, but felt this needed to get out.

My girlfriend and I visited Parc while on a weekend vacation in Philly from where I live in DC.  We were looking for a nice dining experience with a less-than-formal setting, and that is exactly what we found.  Don't get me wrong - Parc is very nice, but it's a brasserie, so not as formal as "fancy" restaurants.  

The service was perfect-attentive and immediate, but never overbearing.  I'd say more, but really don't feel it's necessary.

As for the food - if you've been to Les Halles in New York (Anthony Bourdain's old stomping ground) you'll be familiar with the concept.  The food was simple french brasserie food, but executed well.  I would still give Les Halles a slight edge on the food front - specifically the fries are crispier and a bit more flavorful, but this was a very close rendition.  Additionally, Les Halles is slightly less expensive, but since Parc is in probably the most expensive real estate in Philly, and Les Halles is (slightly) further afield, I won't argue with it - it's still quite reasonable given the food quality.

In short - we found this to be a very pleasurable dinner, and it was quick and smooth to boot.

Highly recommended!

This place never fails to satisfy, from the super friendly staff to the complimentary pickled veggies right when you sit down.  We first started eating here about a year ago and it's slowly starting to become a craving. 

90% of the time we share a monster sandwich but our most recent visit I ordered my own meal, which was half of a chicken salad sandwich on rye bread and a bowl of the matzo ball soup.  This was my first time ever trying matzo ball soup and it was delicious!  In fact my mouth is watering for some right now.  If you're going to eat here I definitely recommend ordering from the NY deli options rather than boring wings, fries, and various bar food because it looked pretty standard from what I noticed atop the other tables as I was walking out.

They are extremely generous with the amount of meat they put inside the sandwiches and everything is always very tasty, however, they are a little expensive (hence why we normally share).  Also, I can never leave here without ordering a gigantic $5 slice of their amazing carrot cake to go, it's my favorite carrot cake on this side of town.    

The interior is rather comfy, open, modern, and clean.  It's never too crowded, we get a table right away, I always get a good vibe from the staff, and we leave happy.

777 is the coolest address.  I think there were that many people waiting for a table on a Saturday night at 8:00 p.m.  After waiting a good 20 minutes, some pristine seats opened up at the bar and we were not opposed to sitting there in the slightest.

Quickly glancing at the mouth-watering menu, I HAD to choose an option from the Vegan Chef Challenge menu.  I wish I had chosen the Vegan Japchae but nervously pointed at the Vegan Bibimbowl.  To say the least, it was extremely tasty but rather filling for a late night dish.  

We started with the Crab Tofu appetizer which was hard to share because I wanted to eat it all myself.  Then I ended up eating the last of my dates' dish, I think it was the teriyaki chicken bowl.  All the flavors are hoppin' at this amazing Korean restaurant in midtown.  I was blown away at the crowd, service, food, smiles, and all around livelihood.

This will definitely be a go-to hot spot in my books.

I've experience better is exactly right.  I keep trying this place over and over again, yet each time I forget how unhappy I was the time before.  Why do I keep coming back?  Probably because I bought a couple of the Restaurant.com vouchers.  

I was craving a Louie Louie salad this particular day and had envisioned something great.  The pictures below show what I received.  Yes, the crab was the best part to the salad but see the veins in the shrimp, how about the yellow asparagus, and not to mention the pit on the tomato.  To me this screams sloppiness.  I wouldn't even serve this to a family member if I made it at home.  Sorry, but I think the chef was a bit lazy this President's Day.

Wow it's been 7 years since I've eaten here.  I'm sad and embarrassed to say I paid $16 for a terrible breakfast burrito.  Lately, I've been trying breakfast burritos around town and so far Paisan's wins ($7+/-).  

Today was a toss up between Peg's and Squeeze In.  Squeeze In has a better online ordering site so I went with them.  I noticed they automatically add in gratuity, even for pick-up, whatever.  When I went to pick it up she handed me this little bagged container, it was so light!  Not like I wanted something heavy but the description of this burrito online sounded epic, hence the $16.  

When I got home to devour, there was no salsa, no hot sauce, no ketchup with the hash browns, no sprouts, and I don't even think any salt.  The sprouts were an option online, which I thought was a weird free add-on.  No chiles within the burrito either, just a little bit of egg, cheese, and avocado.  Oh, not sure why I chose the turkey sausage from the list but I really wish I hadn't.  The sliced chunks were still cold and the casing was very visible on the sausage bites.  Total turn off.  I think the best part of the burrito was the ripe avocado.  

Feeling robbed I want my $ back.  I think it'll be another 7 years before I try them again.  :(

After having a drink at the Jesse we went outside to see if there were tables so we can finally grab some good tacos in Reno.  Had heard a lot about Estella's and I was excited.  Come to find out, they were already sold out of everything on a Friday night around 8; such as guacamole, fish tacos, and shrimp.  Golly!  So we ended up with two chicken and two smoked mushroom.  Holy cow, I LOVED the smoked mushroom tacos.  The mushrooms were sorta crispy and chewy topped with pumpkin seeds and a nice Mexican cheese.  Two were plenty, I will definitely get these again if I'm in the hood.  The outdoor patio super nice in the midst of summer, what with all the hanging lights and the surprise  fireworks display you can see and hear after the Aces Friday night b-ball game.  What an evening!

This place has been on my list for a while.  After deciding NOT to go to Tahoe this last Saturday because of the windy weather, we chose to stay in Reno and check out a new place we hadn't been to yet.  

Mexcal was pretty poppin' when we showed up through the back door where we parked.  We got lucky as we made our way to the bar because those were the only seats available and perfect for us because the bar is our favorite spot to sit.  We ordered two margaritas to start and then got to chatting it up with Rene (the owner we think) and the bartender about all the tequilas they have on the shelves and which ones we should sip on.  Rene brought us a complimentary appetizer dish consisting of fresh octopus and a bright cilantro mango salsa (pictured).  Such a nice gesture, hand clap for Rene!  He also said he would bring in a nice bottle of tequila we could try next time we're in.  See that, Rene, bring in the tequila you were talking about!!  :)  jk jk.  

I was so happy to finally check out Mexcal because I'd driven by so many times.  My man and I looooove tequila so we WILL be here again in the near future.

It was late but I'm glad this place was open for indoor dining plus I wanted hibachi. I realized that afterward that the hibachi experience wasn't available due to Covid but I can still order the hibachi dinner on the menu. I got the steak and salmon with vegetables and fried rice. I wanted noodles instead of rice but they couldn't substitute so I decided to get a side of noodles as well. The rice was ok, a little bland for my taste. The noodle was not that good. Don't recommend. The salmon and steak were cooked well.

I also got the tuna dumplings which is my favorite!! Highly recommend. I also got otoro sushi and Kobe sushi from their special menu. Very good. The quality of the fish and the meat were great! Also got a sushi platter that has salmon, eel, tuna, and yellowtail with some California rolls. Love the variety of the rolls and sushi. 

I would come here again for other items on the menu. Wish next time there is a hibachi experience but I understand due to covid there are limitations

Limited menu during COVID-19 crisis.  Employees are helpful and wearing masks.  We stopped for ice coffees around 5pm on a Saturday and the restaurant was virtually empty.  We enjoyed our drinks and visiting inside.  Restrooms were well-maintained and clean.  Conveniently located right off the interstate.

Such a great recommendation from Rebecca W. This was my favorite meal in NOLA.  We came for an early dinner after skipping lunch while walking around.  Although I was starving, I couldn't help but pause to look at the beautifully plated dishes.  My sweet potato appetizer was tender and flavorful.  Maypop is a must dine in NOLA if you are a fusion cuisine fan.  Many gluten-free, vegan, and healthy options are available. The server brought me a special gluten-free bite before I enjoyed my Shrimp Bibb salad.  My daughter and I left very full but feeling good about the fresh, healthy dishes we consumed.  I will definitely recommend and return!

In August 2021 we were able to walk in without a reservation for brunch mid-week.  Staff was attentive and amiable and the presentation of the food was beautiful.  My daughter had the prettiest Chai Latte and even my hangover bowl managed to look cute.  I ordered my Hangover Bowl with scrambled eggs rather than poached as a personal preference, but the rest of this Southern dish was as listed:   braised short rib, cheese grits, crispy garlic, and caramelized onions.  I didn't realize how much I loved Southern Food until I dined at Willa Jean!  This was my favorite brunch in NOLA and prices are good for quality food.  The menu also has gluten-free, lactose-free, vegan, and other food allergies and preferences marked on the menu.  Great place for the entire family!

If Ruby Slipper was located in my hometown, it would be a five-star restaurant. However, there is much better Southern brunch cuisine to be had in NOLA.  Portions were enormous and the servers were friendly, but I did not think it was worth the wait. There are no reservations, but one can add their name to the waiting list.  We did that on a weekday morning in August 2021, and waited about 45 minutes to be seated at the bar.  It's definitely a popular place.
     I appreciated the variety of choices on the menu as well as gluten/free and vegan options.  I chose the Gulf Shrimp Omelette, which came with potatoes and fresh fruit.  The potatoes were too overdone to enjoy.  I didn't love my omelette either.  I love shrimp.  I love eggs. Maybe I just don't like the two together. Maybe I should've ordered something else. I'm unsure but it wasn't my favorite and my brunch partner agreed with my assessment.  The restaurant and it's dining area was clean and all customers had to show a vaccine card or negative COVID-19 test within the last 72 hours to dine.

OH no.  I grew up down the street from this place.  Who wouldn't want to love it?  I mean, seriously?  And I'm all about the small-farmer Michael Pollan nonsense.  And I hear about this place trying to save their farm from the evil developers by starting a local ice-cream stand.

But see, they pissed me off here.  I don't think they make their ice cream.  And even if they do, honestly, their ice cream is nasty.  Just nasty.  Zero, zero flavor.  

But even worse, their packaged ice cream to go is all about the chemicals.  There are chemicals in there there is no way they have on a farm.  They must just order it from whatever local melamine-filled Chinese factory supplies any old ice cream factory, considering what I read as ingredients on the package.

Total, total bummer.  I mean, total bummer.

This little gem is the epitome of a restaurant that does just a few things, but does them very, very well!  Sandwiches, pizza, wings, salads, capiche?!  

For around $7.00 US American Currency (Sacagawea gold dollars accepted also) I got a Buffalo Chicken wrap, and since I had a mighty hunger I tacked on an order of fries (big mistake).  The wrap was actually (2) wraps.  So imagine an 8" griddle toasted flour tortilla stuffed with shredded white meat chicken, lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, and somewhat mild wing sauce.  Now imagine two of them.  That is what you get in one order.  

My hunger sated I am now on the brink of a food coma of epic proportions.  People at work are starting to stare as my eyes glaze and my computer chair groans under my recent weight gain.  

The staff is extremely friendly and helpful, the decor is warm and inviting, and the food will rock you in a cradle until you fall asleep by the fire on your grizzly bear throw rug.

Go there.

We called the restaurant earlier in the day and made reservations for 3 people for 5:30 on 2/22/14.  When we arrived at 5:20, the hostess told us there were no tables available and that we could wait in the bar.  (there is absolutely no place to stand and wait either unless you wait in the bar area which is not that big).  As we looked around the restaurant we noticed 3 tables were empty in the front room, 4 tables were empty in the back room, and 2 high tops in the bar were empty.  As we continued to wait, at least 10 couples came in and were turned away because they did not have reservations and they did not want to wait at the bar which was now full.  At 6:10 a group of 4 came in with reservations for 6:30 and the hostess said, "Oh, you are early, I can seat you now".  My wife immediately went over and asked why we were not seated instead as our reservation was for 5:30 and the hostess said it was because we made our reservation that day and they made theirs a few days earlier.  After waiting an hour and seeing at least 3 other groups seated we asked again why we were not being seated and they continued with "sorry" there is nothing available", which came across as very insincere and no estimate of when we would be seated.

After an hour and 15 minutes we gave up and ate at the bar.  The bar tender was very attentive and refilled our drinks continuously throughout the meal.  Otherwise she was not very personable, except it you were "a regular".  The food came within 15 minutes of ordering.  Each of us enjoyed our meals.  The food is a little over priced but the portions are good and it is not the style of cooking you would find in most restaurants and it is a style (new orleans) I enjoy.

The restaurant is just a house that was converted so it is very narrow and small, and it quickly gets very crowded.  The tables are very close together so you don't get much privacy.  The tables in the front room are right next to the entry door so you get a blast of cold air and the non stop hostess/customer interaction throughout your meal, and the pleasure of that going on right next to you.  The atmosphere otherwise is really cool with losts of New Orleans charm.

I will probably never come back here to eat because the seating policy is totally jacked.  The hostess fumbled through a little scrap book of papers everytime somebody came in and even with reservations you had absolutely no clue of when you would be seated.  I am not sure why with so many empty tables why we were not seated.  At first I thought it was because they were understaffed, but then groups of people were immediately seated at though tables when they came in, over an hour after we had come in.  Any restaurant I have ever been too you were at least given a time frame when you would be seated with or without reservations.  So unless you are ok with waiting for however long it takes, or you are willing to eat at the bar when a seat becomes available, I would strongly encourage you to eat elsewhere.  While the food is good, it is not great.  It is a little over priced.  The waitress's are understaffed and over whelmed.  It will not be an enjoyable experience and that is what dining out is all about.
Tacos and Sopes are some of the best i've had in the neighborhood, especially the  Chuleta Ahumada. Also very friendly staff.

I came here to eat before going to the Rodeo and I really love how you can try many different dishes without getting full or having a lot of leftovers. 

We ordered the Sierra Selection which allows you to pick four small plates (each less than $10) for $30. We ended up getting the Prosciutto Wrapped Asparagus, Crimini Stuffed Mushrooms, Mac n Cheese, and Kobe Sliders. The sliders were above $10 but our server was great enough to include it in our Sierra Selection and just charge us the extra amount above $10. All the food tasted great! The salty prosciutto balanced well with the asparagus and the cheese with the mushrooms were very tasty. The sliders were very tender and the onions on it added great flavor! 

Along with the great food, this restaurant has a great location overlooking the river. There's outdoor seating which is perfect for the summertime as well as indoor seating with a nice view. 

I can't wait to come back and try their other small plates. This place is definitely a must if you're in the mood for tapas.
Food was great!!  I had a HUGE burger cooked MEDIUM!! And it was actually MEDIUM. VERY FRIENDLY service. Reasonable prices. Ill be back

Sat immediately. Had a small carafe of coffee in about 30 seconds of sitting. Waitress was very friendly. I personally love diners. I havent been here in years. Place has been remodeled and updated. Very clean. Even the bathrooms!!  Breakfast was very good and extremely fast. 

Have nothing but good to say. I had a ham and cheese omelet which was delicious

There was a time when I never thought I'd be able to love again. When Franco broke my heart after 10 magical years together I gave up on feeling emotionally connected to another restaurant [single tear rolls down cheek]. But this place is a handsome new boyfriend.

Lemme break it down for you.

The steak tartare. You. Guys. The slow cooked egg yolk. Gasp. Like nothing I've ever experienced before. At first I thought it was lemon curd or like a weird gelatinous mustard and I was looking through my monocle all like idk about this. BUT THEN I TASTED IT. Holyshitballs. Somebody call 911 and ask them if I have a pulse. Let's just say we cried big blubbering grown man tears when it was gone.

For dinner I had the tagliatelle with braised rabbit ragu. It was simple but perfect. He had the prime aged strip. They actually listened when he said he wanted it "as rare as you are legally allowed" (!!!) Praying hands emoji! For dessert, we had the Butterscotch pot de creme with some crunchy salty shit on top. And I quote "Will you be embarrassed if I lick the bowl?" Not telling you how that one ended.

Now for the most important part: THE DRINKS. 2 million gold stars. So good. Like make-Stephen-Hawking-believe-in-God-good. [insert gif of Southern tent revival preacher here] The bourbon pineapple sage cocktail was oh, I dunno, the only thing I want to drink FOR THE REST OF MY LIFE. And everything else just made me incandescently happy. Did I mention we sat at the (very slammed) bar and still got A++ service? I'm pretty sure Chelsea Little is a witch. There is just NO other explanation for drinks that good. HEY GIRL HAAAAYYY I SEE YOU.

Takeaway message: Olive + Oak, I think I'm in love.

*In case you think I'm getting paid for this/a liar/a sex robot I will say the #91 cocktail (orgeat, rum, chai, lemon, lavender, topped with a torched vegan marshmallow) had a little too much of the "old lady candle shop" flavor/vibes. I still liked it though.

Was quick to review the new Miramar Beach Hotel by Rosewood yesterday while waiting to order drinks, upon reflection I have reduced my rating from five to four stars.   

The hotel is gorgeous as you can see in the photos.  I was impressed that it looks very finished, the landscaping is beautiful and you can't tell that a few weeks ago it was a chaotic construction site.   The staff is wonderful and I was especially impressed by the valet Parking attendants.   They were good sports, more than happy to take the cover off of the Fiat Jolly and let us sit in it.   When we walked in, the lobby seemed almost over-staffed, again by helpful and friendly people.  They didn't seem to have a whole lot to do as the hotel opened quietly and is fairly empty.   Our focus was to get a cocktail at the bar.  

The Bar off of the lobby is very pretty, lots of dark wood and classic decor.   The lighting is dim and romantic.  As a result menus are hard to read.  The light gray type is attractive but not friendly to anyone who needs reading glasses...guessing that will be the bulk of their clientele. They have many unique cocktails and as you would expect they are about $17 each. 

We ordered three and waited a fairly lengthy time to get them.  Sadly one arrived with the promise that the others were right behind.   Five minutes later we had the second one and ten minutes after the third.  They were very tasty but a little small.  Finding our server to pay the bill was another 20 minute experience.   We hope that over time this bar learns to function more efficiently. 

I left my credit card and when I went the next day to retrieve it they didn't have it at the bar and sent me to the front desk.  They didn't have it either and called the security office which is where left behind cards are domiciled.  It is not near the lobby so it was 15 minutes til someone brought me the card.  Of course I had to provide ID, and sign and date the official paperwork.  

Our favorite part was walking through the grounds to the beautiful beach deck.  If you stay there certainly the beach front rooms will be the way to go.   There is a beach front fine dining restaurant that will be open shortly.  It will have magnificent views.  There were a few people inside at the bar and evening a few people enjoying meals at the tables.  We are assuming they might be friends of Rick Caruso's enjoying a special meal. 

As a local who grew up in the neighborhood, took swim lessons from Jacque and and provided hotel security my senior year of high school I'm excited to see the Miramar back in business after such a long absence

This isn't the first review I have written for Brophy's.   It was five star then and it is five star now.   I am writing this review because I feel that I have wronged the place and kind of feel guilty.   I love the view, the people who work there, the people who go there, the strong margaritas, the clam chowder, the beer boiled shrimp and all of the things I wrote about before.  I love the place and recommend it A LOT but I have always told people to order the "Oyster bar" food, that it was that kind of a place, not fine dining.   I suggested that if they want Seabass or Ahi with side dishes and sauces that they might be better served going to one of the competitors (all who seem to be owned by the same group.)  But yesterday I stepped out of the box.  Ordered the blackened Seabass with the tarragon sauce that they serve with the Ahi.   It was absolutely wonderful!!   My friend had the crab cakes and they very well could be the best I have eaten.   The entrée was one of their most expensive, $24 and well worth it!  So again Brophy's, my bad!  You rock it on the fancy food too.  

I would like to add that if you go to Brophy's expect it to be busy.  It is very rare that you don't wait for a table!    The wait is fun, you might meet Harbor John or another regular, or some fascinating person who are in town on vacation.   Order a drink and enjoy the sourdough bread.   There are worse places to have to wait for a table.    

And when YOU Yelp them, don't knock them down for being popular, that is to their credit!   If you waited an hour, or the place was too crowded it is because they are good.   It would be like bashing a Ferrari for being too fast and scary to drive, Hawaii for being too warm or Mount Everest for being too big.

You can't live in Santa Barbara and not experience  Baja Sharkeez!   Just too many friends seem to want to have happy hours, birthdays or whatever there.  So sometimes I just grin and bear it.  I eat the bad food and drink the crummy drinks, even put up with the bad service.   I guess there are some pretty cheap eats sometimes.    Taco Tuesdays, actually had a halfway decent taco once.     I would give them a two star rating based on what it is... but....

When I am browsing Yelp and see four different five star reviews, all on the same day, all from Yelp Newbies and all just a single sentance.   I loose all respect for a place.    I am sure that Yelps wonderful screening processes has by now moved them to the filtered section.   But what is done is done.   Like the Harvard student who gets caught cheating on a test or the Tour de France cyclist who gets caught doping... the business that abuses Yelp isn't soon forgotten!   

Note to Sharkees:  You are a two-star place!!!!    The only way that your Yelp rating is going to go up is to face the music and cook better food, serve better drinks and give your customers better service!

Every morning the folks at Los Agaves have probably looked into their magic mirror and asked "who's the fairest of them all?" And every morning the mirror would faithfully reply that their Mexican food was the greatest in all of that land.  That is until recently when the mirror has probably informed them that there is now one fairer still and it is a little hole-in-the-wall called Monys Mexican food. 

Santa Barbara has seen so many different top dogs in the Mexican food arena!   Of course Julia Child started things off by raving about La Superica many, many years ago.    Then we had Lily's hit the scene, tacos and only tacos in flavors that made us gringo's wince!  But oh so good.  Then of course Los Agaves which actually gave you a pleasant place to sit with the great Mexican fare!   But there is a new King in town and it is Monys! 

The food is fresh, it is creative and delicious.   Add to that the finest selection of salsas imaginable.   How about Pistachio salsa?  or Peanut?   All the basics are there too.  

Unfortunately with the new found success it isn't the hidden Gem it once was!  Yes,. the food is still just as good but there are only a few tables and you might not be able to sit down.   Expect to wait 10-15 minutes for your order to be ready.  But you can take it to go and it is most definitely worth the wait!!

It was more than two years ago that I reviewed the Lark. We were the first customers that first day. While I loved the restaurant I have to admit I was skeptical that it would survive.  They have a large staff which seems to be the secret of their success.  Since my first visit I have been here about 70 more times so I guess you could call me a fan.  I enjoy the bar or the community table.  

What impresses me the most is that a restaurant that serves only dinner has a full staff of chefs who arrive early in the morning to prep the food.  During the dinner service there are at least a dozen chefs in the kitchen.  The attention to detail is beyond belief and every dish is worth trying.  

Since my first visit the menu has changed and the specialty cocktails have changed as well. I miss some of the previous items yet their replacements are equally amazing.  I have always enjoyed the Wedge salad.  Lots of wonderful bleu cheese with candied bacon and pecans.  If you sit at the bar their burger is one of the best you will ever eat and for $13 or $14 it is a bargain.  It is "off the menu" so you feel like a regular when you order it.  Another entree to consider is the half chicken.  A dish that two people will share with leftovers for tomorrow's lunch.  Like all the dishes the preparation is wonderful as it is brined for 24 hours+ before cooking.  You have my guarantee that it will be moist and fall-apart good.  

If you want a unique experience you can ask to have your reservation of two in the confessional booth, a very cool relic from the 1700's imported because the owner thought it would be a nice addition.

Me and the wifey had a little 340 month anniversary and thought that we would try something new so we went to Seven.   Awesome little spot that is more of a bar with food than a restaurant with a bar (embrace that Seven--it is what you are!)    It is a cozy place with natural brick walls, stonework, effective lighting and a very user-friendly bar (thanks Pub for the overall design)   They have added some nice tables and comfortable seating as well as a great outdoor patio! 

Sin is the name of the game or at least the name of the restaurant because seven is based on the seven deadly sins (I meant to look to see if they have 7 deadly Zins on the wine list).  The first sin I experienced was GREED since I saw on the happy hour menu $5 Hornitas margaritas as well as $5 Alagash white pints... I wanted both!   The margarita was very tasty and of course Alagash is a great beer.    My wife ordered the cucumber infused vodka lemonaide,  it looked pretty good and I was quite ENVIOUS.    

Seven doesn't just have drinks it has a menu too.   No happy hour deals on the food but the prices aren't out of line.   Most items are $12.    My wife had a sandwich and I had the Chicken and Waffles, interesting combo which came with maple syrup, fries and a very tasty slaw!    While the sandwich was fresh and the chicken and waffles were piping hot, the fries were cold and soggy.  The wonderful waitress quickly extiguished my WRATH by bring us a fresh plate of fries.   I loved my dinner.    It was a very full plate and to my surprise, chicken is better with maple syrup.   I was reluctant to share with my wife and had to curb my GLUTTONY so that she could try a bite.
