All in all chicken, waffles maple syrup, fries, ketchup and beer make for a pretty wierd combination and I don't think beer will replace orange juice for breakfast any time soon.   

It was a very nice evening and I was PROUD of the fact that I came up with a new and fresh idea for our monthly anniversary.   While the food was delicious it sat a little heavy and I was a total SLOTH the rest of the evening.    

Oh, and that seventh sin (?)   I am keeping that one to myself.

Cuernavaca is a city about 30 miles south of Mexico City.  It was founded 3200 years ago and is nicknamed "City of Eternal Spring".  Cuernavaca is also a wonderful Mexican Food restaurant on Carrillo Street.  

I have been there a few times.  The first time a made the mistake of ordering tacos.   Yes they were good, actually they were better than good, they were excellent!!!! But as I learned in my next visit you don't go to Cuernavaca for their tacos!!   You go there for their plates!!!   

As you look at the menu of all the different plates and all of the different choices, don't be too stressed.  One with pork, another with pork and chicken and another with carne asada and pork... It doesn't really matter because they all have a similar flavor and you can't go wrong.   It would be like choosing between Ferraris and Lamborghinis, there just isn't a bad decision. Last time I made it easy and just ordered the #1.

The plates come with a small stack of tortillas and have a generous portion of avocado sliced on top!    I think that they are all priced around $9 or $10 which is a deal!  If two people aren't too hungry sharing would most certainly be sufficient. 

Beyond the food they have a good space.  The back room is large and open and is pleasant place to enjoy the great food.    They have salsas which are as good as any and better than most.  The chips are included in the cost of the meal.

I went the other day with my son.  He didn't take my advice, ordered the tacos -- He liked mine better.

I had been thinking about going to PuraVegan for a really long time, so I was so happy when I finally had the chance! I was in the neighborhood and snagged a spot right out front of the place and made my way in. The first thing I noticed was that it was REALLY quiet in there... awkwardly quiet. I took a second to look at the menu and decided to order a few things to go.

I knew I wanted a smoothie so I ordered the super chocolate banana with cocao powder and fresh banana. It took her a while to make, but wow that thing was delicious! I almost drank the entire thing while I was waiting for my food. I would absolutely go back for that smoothie. The food I got to go was the marinated kale salad (kale, carrots, red cabbage, red onion, red bell peppers, tomatoes, sesame lemon dressing) and sweet potato pasta (sweet potato noodles, celery, green onions, sunflower seeds, red onion, currants, marinated mushrooms, cabbage, tossed with herbs and spices.) They both sounded flavorful and amazing, but wow, I was so disappointed with how they both tasted. Not much flavor at all and I had a hard time eating both of them. Vegan fail, Aimee.

I might go back for that shake and I might eventually try something else, but I'm not too big of a fan of PuraVegan. Give it a try if you're in the neighborhood!

Anywhere I can get boozy breakfast cocktails and breakfast tacos is a home run in my book.

We stopped by for Sunday brunch a few weeks ago, and were lucky enough to snag a table right away. This place buzzes with positive energy, and was full of happy diners, bloody marys traveling to almost every table, and friendly staff. 

If you're in the mood for a morning drink (who isn't?), do not pass up the hot espresso martini. It's made with double espresso, vodka, hazelnut liqueur, and coffee liquor. It was one of the best breakfast cocktails I've ever had. The breakfast tacos are topped with scrambled eggs and you have your choice of: chorizo & queso, carne asada, veggie & queso fresco, or spicy rib. You really can't lose here.

We also ordered sides of potatoes and bacon. The potatoes were A-OK and could probably be skipped, but the bacon was wonderful (obviously.)

I would totally come back here and anticipate doing so very soon. Awesome place for a fun and casual brunch!

I get a mean craving for Vietnamese every once in a while, and I immediately thought of Pho Grand when the craving hit last because I always drive by it but never go. One of my favorite things to do on a weekend rainy day is pick up something delicious to go and bring it home while watching all of my shows on DVR... pure heaven. Pho Grand was a great addition to that equation.

I called Pho Grand and placed an order for pick up and the guy on the phone was really nice, and he gave me a wait time of about 15 minutes. I got there about ten minutes later and scored a parking spot right out front, walked in, and my order was already ready! Also, $13 for an appetizer and an entree? I'm definitely okay with that. 

When I got home I found that they packaged the food in a great way to where everything was still hot and nothing was running all over other things... that's a common problem when I get things to go! For an appetizer I got the veggie spring rolls, and wow. I know for sure that I'm going to be craving those again sometime this week. They were so fresh, so full of veggies and rice, and if you're a cilantro lover like me you'll be very happy with these. The sweet and sour sauce was pretty standard but a nice compliment, and the lady who gave me my food made it a point to tell me to use the s&s on both the rolls and my entree. For the main course I had the Ga Xao Xa Ot (stir-friend chicken with hot chiles and lemongrass) and it was just alright to me. It was kind of sweet which I didn't really like, and I wasn't crazy about the taste of the chicken. Luckily, the two huge spring rolls filled me up plenty.

I like this place quite a bit! Next time I'll try and dine in to see what else they have to offer. If you're craving a good spring roll or want Vietnamese with really fast service, Pho Grand is your place.

Sasha's has a little sister and it's as cool as you would expect!

I live close to Sasha's on Demun and I'm obviously a huge fan, so I was eager to check this place out. It actually looks quite a bit like Sasha's on the inside, and I appreciated the familiar scene. The outdoor patio is much bigger here, though, and would be so much fun on a nice night.

Obviously the wine selection is incredible, and you're going to find something you love. I hear the cocktails are five stars as well, but cannot speak from experience yet. What I was so thrilled with was the food - the menu is really great and features sandwiches, salads, wood-fired pizzas, and tons of yummy meats and cheeses. Since we went around happy hour time and were starving, I decided to try the caprese salad and the chilled cucumber soup. What sold me on the soup was that it comes alongside avocado toast, my all-time favorite thing in the world. The soup was tangy, refreshing, and satisfying, and the avocado toast made it even better. Who knew avocado and feta could be such great friends? The salad was great as well.

I can't wait to spend some weekend nights at this cool neighborhood spot. So happy to have another great choice in the West End!

So impressed by this place!

I'm glad someone gave me a heads up on the location because it's basically tucked behind Tucano's Brazilian Grill. I wasn't sure what to expect, but when I walked up during lunch I was very pleasantly surprised! It was a nice day and the entire place was opened up. There was an awesome breeze inside but we decided to grab a spot on the patio anyway. Our waiter laughed at us several times because we ended up being absolutely freezing but not wanting to move. The space is so beautiful - seriously something special to see in St. Charles.

We were sad to see they were only serving sushi for dinner now instead of lunch, but found plenty of things we liked. Here's a quick rundown:

-House hummus: loved the veggies that were served with this, but the hummus was lacking some flavor. 
-Chorizo tacos: yes. Just yes. Order these and thank me later. Perfectly spicy, fresh veggies on top, and everything I wanted them to be. My sister also loved her shrimp tacos.
-Roasted beet salad with goat cheese: fresh, flavorful, and healthy. The beets and oranges made the flavors pop, and it was dressed with a lemony vinaigrette. 
-My cousin (who's a vegetarian and entirely too picky) had a simple cheese omelet with house potatoes & was very happy.

I'll definitely be back here and I can't wait to try dinner. I do think they need more staff during the day... our server was sporadic and you could tell he was stressed out. Otherwise, we had quite the ideal lunch! 

Way to go on this one, St. Charles. Way to go.

Where did I have the best brunch of my entire life? Pub & Kitchen. It sounds dramatic but it's true.

If you're a bloody mary fan, order the Wrangler without question. The Wrangler alone is five-star worthy and is perfectly spicy. I dare you to try to stop at one! We ended up having a few and then moving to a bottle of rosé, like proper brunchers do.

We decided to start by splitting the Dutch Baby Blueberry Pancake, and it was absolutely amazing. First of all, it's huge, and more like a cake than a pancake. Second of all, be ready to force yourself to stop because it's just that good. It's topped with key lime curd and dulce de leche, sooo yeah.

After that, I ordered the sausage and biscuit with a soft scrambled egg and bacon morney sauce. It was even better than the pancake somehow, and the breakfast potatoes on the side were perfect.

After all of that, I had someone roll me out of the restaurant so I could go take a nap.

Really though, you don't want to miss brunch here.

Lucas Park is one of those places when you tell your friends you're going to go during a night out, you get one or two "uggghhhhh"s or "noooooo"s. For me, it's always been a reliable stop while partaking in a little drinking on Washington, but until last night, I didn't realize how good the food actually is! It's funny how different it looks during the day, too, compared to after hours with a few rum and diets. Yelp sponsored Iron Bartender this Sunday so we got to sneak a bite in between set-up and the event.

We tried a couple things... my fiance had the oysters and was really shocked at how small they were. The presentation was nice, but unfortunately there wasn't too much there to eat. I had the mini burgers and they were really good! They were topped with cheese and mini tomatoes and pieces of lettuce, and came with sweet pickles and a ketchup/bbq sauce. The giant pile of sweet potato fries in the middle didn't hurt, either! Other than that, we just had a cheese plate that was really sweet & salty all at the same time. I was craving more of that brie earlier today. 

I feel like the nighttime crowd at Lucas can be a little shady. It seems like lately it's a lot of men on the prowl. Since the food we had was pretty good, I'd be interested to try their brunch I hear so much about. 

I'm really sad my favorite bartender Schmitty left, but I'm sure I'll be back in soon!

I'm going to keep this simple.

This Sasha's is 10x better than the other Sasha's because there's a lot more room and more attentive service. The patio is also bigger and the ambiance just can't be beat.

Order the Bin38 Shiraz from California. Get the Tres Quesos cheese plate, and eat your heart out on Mahon, Rosemary Manchego and Murcia (drunken goat cheese). I swear to the good Lord above this combination is heaven on earth. 

Great date spot, and it won't break the bank too badly! It''ll also leave you in a wine and cheese haze that lasts throughout the night. 

Just. So. Good.

Just a quick addition to the review of what has quickly become my favorite tapas spot in St. Louis (and I'm not sure if it's because of the tapas themselves or the magically hand-crafted cocktails.) 

1) Order the jalapeno cornbread! It comes studded with jalapenos and is served with honey butter & topped with smoked tomato salsa and is something close to heaven on earth. Cabrales cigars still deserve a standing ovation as well.

2) Skip the cocktail list and just tell your server what kind of drinks you typically like, and let them surprise you... it's the best way to drink here and you're probably not going to be disappointed.

3) If there's a girl serving with short blonde hair and a lot of tattoos named Kentucky, request her. The lady is a wealth of information and made my last experience the best so far.

4) Please take me with you every time you go.

I waited a long time to write this review because I have to admit, I wasn't feeling it in the beginning. When I first visited Sump it felt cold and unwelcoming, and I really think I went on an off day... because I love this place now. Maybe it's that I know what to expect, maybe things are running more smoothly, maybe there's more chemistry in there... not sure, but whatever it is, it's working.

I've never had a better cup of coffee in my life, and I feel confident saying that. I've had a lot that have come close, but seriously, this coffee is good. Let them explain the different beans and methods of brewing, and trust their recommendations. Be careful, though... one cup and I'm literally ready to blast off right out of my seat. Caffeine jolt, anybody?

What I love the most about Sump is how laid-back and fitting it is for the area. It's the perfect place for meetings or just to relax while working on your computer, and it just kind of feels like you belong there. When you place your coffee order, they just write it down and trust you to pay for it before you leave. That itself makes it feel more relaxed, and props to Scott for having the badass (and easy) iPad credit card machine deal, too. I don't have a problem with the tip prompter, and you can always choose zero if you don't want to add anything (I usually just throw in a dollar because I like what they're trying to do.)

Sump has a huge fan in me and I'll definitely be back soon.

Park Ave Coffee is by far my favorite coffee shop downtown. My waistline? Mmmm... maybe not so much, but it's not the one writing the review. I'm so glad it's here!

Parking at Park Ave downtown is decent because there are usually meters open, but make sure to bring a nice sized stack of quarters if you're going to stick around and get some work done. It sucks to be in the middle of a good afternoon of work only to look out and see a parking nazi stuffing your windshield wipers with tickets. Complete coffee buzz kill.

Park Ave's colors are so zen, welcoming and perfect. I adore the light blue and orange combo, and the inside of the place is really pretty & calming. The lighting & furniture are great, too, but the best part is being greeted by the giant case of gooey butter cake & other treats right when you walk in. I absolutely cannot say no to the gooey butter cake... I swear one of the pieces was looking at me, and later I heard it whisper my name. I've had gooey butter cake plenty of times, and this tops them all. The friendly guy who was working behind the counter also made me an iced chai coffee which tasted like a liquid version of pumpkin pie, so yeah... you can see how the waistline didn't appreciate.

It's oddly quiet during weekdays, so come here if you need to work or study. Or begin your path to obesity.

I really, really like McGurks. I go there more for dinner than the nightlife now-a-days (myself at 22 would probably gasp at that statement) but I'm consistently impressed by the food. Yes they have great fish & chips, but there's so much more than meets the eye on that menu!

The spinach & artichoke rav's are a great option for appetizers, and they come with an addicting & tangy ranch sauce for dipping. I'm also a huge fan of their baked potato skins & the baked spinach and artichoke dip. Pair it with a cocktail or glass of wine & you're on your way to a great meal!

Where McGurk's really shines is in their house specialty offerings. Bangers and mash, corned beef and cabbage, and Irish stew? Yes please! Make sure to always ask what the special of the day is. Most recently they had seared grouper with mango salsa over new potatoes, carrots, and spinach, and I was completely blown away. 

When the bands are playing here it's a little loud, but it's all part of the experience. It might not hurt to stick around to check out the nightlife scene, either. You can't help but love that giant patio!

We've always loved Katie's, and we love them even more for not only offering frozen pizza and pasta, but for delivering it at our door.

I've never cooked more in my life than I have during this pandemic, and it is such a wonderful treat to get to enjoy Katie's on nights when I need a little break.

We ordered two margherita pizzas and two orders of lemon strozzapreti (my favorite!) and we're thrilled. The pasta bakes are huge and feed four, which makes for nice leftovers too. Everything you can order is on their website.

I've been back to Mochi several times since the visit where they flopped, and it's been consistent and ohmyGod so incredible. It's officially, indeed, the best sushi I've ever had in St. Louis. 

Five stars, even though I have to send my sushi back every single time... I can't have fish eggs on top, but they forget every. single. time. The sushi is good enough that I don't even care. The Godzilla, white tiger, and volcano roll are still the must-trys, and I'll probably never stray from that order.

Go! Eat good sushi!

Everything is wonderful at Brasserie, but for me, brunch might be the best. Especially this past weekend when there wasn't a wait at 11am on a Sunday (what?!) We grabbed a two-seater towards the front of the restaurant and had a really great time.

I order eggs benedict on the regular pretty much everywhere I go, so when I saw it on the menu at Brasserie, it was a no-brainer. I'm so glad that's what I went with, because oh my God, it was definitely the best plate of benedict I've ever had. The dijon-hollandaise was so perfectly tangy and seasoned, and the smashed potatoes were out of this world as well. 

The only so-so part of brunch was my bloody mary - it was just way too salty. I still was able to enjoy some of it once the ice melted a little.

I'll be back soon to try more, or just to get the eggs benedict again.

Dear Mud House,

After several minutes of inner turmoil and serious decision making, I decided to --GASP-- order something besides the Portabello Reuben for lunch. Since it's what I order every single goddamn time, I thought it appropriate to go for something different for the sake of keeping things interesting and exciting. I took a chance on your chickpea salad sandwich and didn't think it would be able to come close to satisfying all of my fresh & hearty sandwich dreams, but boy was I wrong. The chickpeas, perfectly half-smashed and seasoned, were topped with pea shoots and sandwiched between two expertly toasted pieces of bread and it was truly love at first bite. The mixed greens on the side rock my world as well and made me feel even more like a healthy eating champion.

Thanks for putting a smile on my face and keeping me full well past dinner.

Faithfully yours,
Aimee

One thing I can't stand is being too full. You know, that Thanksgiving dinner kind of full where you just feel miserable and all you really want to do is sleep. It's so gross to me and I don't think there's ever really an excuse to stuff yourself that full of food... but there are now two exceptions in my life. 1) Thanksgiving dinner, for obvious reasons. 2) Dinner at Milagro. 

This place doesn't just do dinner right, they do every single thing right. When it was time to order drinks my eyes automatically went to the skinny margarita (I hate the heavy sweet & sour in regular ones) but my cousin swears by the sangria, so sangria it was, and OH YES IT WAS. Hands down the best sangria I've ever had -- it was so fresh, full of fruit, and had the perfect amount of booze (the perfect amount for me is something that gives you a buzz but doesn't make you act silly after one glass.) Best sangria I've had in all of St. Louis.

For an appetizer we just ordered the guacamole which was also very fresh, but we probably would have been alright with just the salsa alone because the flavors were just right on. I'm pretty sure I was full on chips/salsa/guac by the time I ordered an entree, but like any good American I pressed onward in hopes of trying everything I could regardless of my full stomach...

I almost got the veggie burrito but asked Adam for a recommendation and he pointed to the Chile Relleno which was going to be my second choice, and I went for it. The Chile Relleno is a lightly battered Chile poblano stuffed with Mexican cheeses, chayote squash, and mushrooms, and comes with Chile morita salsa, Mexican rice, and that "off the cob" street corn that our waiter correctly described as "crack." I was truly blown away by how good this dish was, and I'm afraid that I'll probably never branch out at Milagro because I'm ordering that entree every single time. 

We finished with the house-made churros & chocolate sauce, and it was about that time that I realized what I had done to my poor, unsuspecting stomach. Stomach was a champion though and understood my dilemma of not being able to stop eating, so I'm glad we're on the same page.

Fun atmosphere, way above average food, great service. Put this on your list and get ready for several repeat visits.

I had lunch at Mission Taco today, and I'm actually mad at myself for not getting over there sooner... it was that good. We went around noon and there were plenty of places to sit, and like a bunch of dummies we kept waiting for menus before we realized they were already on the table! They want to keep this place feeling like you're havin' some street food which makes it pretty casual (which is A-OK with me.) I wanted to have a margarita but it didn't feel right at noon on a workday, so I sadly went with coffee instead. For what it's worth, the coffee tasted great.

We started with some salsa & they brought us two varieties... I really enjoyed the habanero version that was simply loaded with flavor. The chips were so fresh & salted the perfect amount, too. Our server (who was nervous and charming) brought us some queso to try and I will absolutely be ordering it next time. Just so good. 

I loved reading about all the varieties of tacos they offer, but ended up going with a burrito. It was loaded with grilled chicken, black beans, rice, veggies, and some kind of cheese, and topped with fresh guacamole. It really was one of the best burritos I've ever had. Next time I'm going to make sure to try a few different tacos just to see how great the creations are. 

Mission has a creative menu, a cool staff, and the overall vibe is so relaxed and fun. I live five minutes from this place and can promise you I'll be spending a lot of time there this summer.

The Post is officially my favorite sports bar... especially after tonight. I'm pretty sure at least half of Cardinal nation was crammed in there wearing their red, screaming like a bunch of freakin' crazy people... So amazing...

There are so many TVs at the Post that there's no way you can't see whatever game you're looking for, and the best part? THEY PLAY SOUND. There's nothing worse than watching a big game and listening to a bunch of top 40's pop hits. The service is steady and friendly, and I've just never had a bad time here. 

The 20% off your food you get when you check in on Yelp doesn't hurt at all, and their menu has something for everybody. Wings, nachos, burgers, chicken fingers, pizza, even a good veggie burger... typical bar food but kicked up a notch. The drinks come strong, as well. The best part about tonight is that the bartender would occasionally pick up the microphone to cheer on our team and bash other ones we didn't want to win... made it fun and pumped everyone up even more.

This is my go-to sports bar, no doubt. And with that I say... WE WON THE NATIONAL LEAGUE WILD CARD!

This was the conversation between a friend from out of town & I as we were leaving the History Museum:

Him: I'm hungry.
Me: I am too, what do you feel like eating?
Him: Do you guys have any good barbecue here?
Me: Uhhmmmm... you could say that, yes.
Him: Let's do that.
Me: YES, I've been dying to go to Pappy's and we're not that far away!
Him: It's a good time to go, too, 'cause it's 3pm so it won't be busy.
Me: Errrr... yeah, you don't understand.

It wasn't until we pulled up and he saw the line out the door that he knew Pappy's BBQ is some serious ass business. We waited in the line that stretched down the hallway for about 30 minutes before we made it in, and I really wish they'd do something besides put a sad little fan out there. It was HOT, and people were getting a little restless. Once inside, it was a good 40 more minutes until we made it to the counter! Needless to say I was starving and ready to do some serious damage to a plate of BBQ.

I of course got the pulled pork sandwich, and my friend got the pulled pork & brisket. For sides we had beans, green beans, potato salad & sweet potato fries. (Btw, pair your food with some Fitz's rootbeer... amazing!) The pork was ridiculously phenomenal as always (the brisket just okay), and I alternated between the Pappy's sauce, the sweet baby Jane, and the hot sauce. The not-so-awesome part of the meal was when said sauce landed right on my white shorts. So typical. This is exactly why I carry a Tide pen with me at all times.

I love Pappy's a lot and I'll obviously be back for more, especially when someone innocently asks me if "we have any BBQ here." However, I'm still waiting for the day when they offer mac'n'cheese as a side. Hooray for meat!

Big fan of Anthonino's! Greek and Italian? Yes please. A choice between a gyro or a plate of homemade pasta? Well, if you really insist...

I was recently here with the Yelp International Supper Club and I was so impressed at how well our server handled our big group! It was pretty seamless, and I never had to wait long for anything. Our checks came quickly at the end of the meal and not even all of the separate checks threw her off. Props!

I didn't try too much of the menu, but I certainly plan on returning to try even more. I must say, I really love the fresh bread with garlic olive oil that they serve at the beginning of the meal. So good! I was also jealous of everyone who got hummus or other appetizers beforehand. For my meal, I had the Italian sausage pasta with fresh marinara sauce... I can't even begin to explain how good this was. The sausage was really, really spicy, and the sauce was perfectly homemade. The pasta itself was perfect, too. I wanted to keep eating more but I was way too full. My only critique is that the dish might appear more... appetizing... if they sliced up the sausage instead of serving it as one huge link. That's all I'll say about that!

I can't wait to go back to Anthonino's mostly because I want to try the gyros... they are huge and everyone at the table loved them! This place has a lot to offer. Go and enjoy the busy & happy atmosphere!

Today a very sick Aimee wandered into Cafe Ventana and sunk down into a chair with a mac and a lot of work. I literally walked up to the register and asked one of the girls if they had anything that could cure a sore throat. Five minutes later I had a orange herbal tea served with honey and a big orange slice, and it actually did the trick. I don't think I've ever been so thankful for something!

Lacking energy today, but I couldn't let Ventana's continuously great service go undocumented.

Forever a fan!

New dinner menu favorite: Saltaldo de Champignones - button, shitake & portabella mushrooms, sweet onions & tomatoes sautéed in olive oil, white wine, aji amarillo, Peruvian spices & garlic with white rice. Hooooly heaven. It's pretty rich but so good.

The Yuca Frita (yuca fries & creamy aji amarillo cheese sauce) is also very good, but wow are those things starchy. Share with a group because it's hard to eat more than a couple all alone.

Mango's hospitality is one for the books -- they hosted International Supper Club's holiday dinner and even gave us a shout out on the seasonal menu. Our server was so fantastic and I don't have a single complaint!

Side note- if I have cocktails here, keep those plantains away from me that they give you at the beginning of the meal! Similar to chips & salsa situations (not in taste or anything other than the fact that they're addicting) at Mexican restaurants, I literally cannot stop until the sauce & plantains are gone. So delicious.

Go now. Peruvian FTW!

I always hear people talk about how impossibly busy Half & Half is and that it's just too much work to get a table there. Here's the key: go for brunch during the week. Work during the day? Take a morning off and go. It's 100% worth it and there's usually only 8-9 tables full for brunch, and the service is just that good.

I've also decided that I like the brunch menu way better than lunch, and after trying the steak & eggs, I'm not sure I'll ever order anything else there. Perfectly cooked steak, two eggs, potatoes hiding underneath, all topped with fried onions and some kind of creamy hollandaise (just uploaded a photo.) It's a lot of food so prepared to be full to the max, and if you're really brave, order the house-made donuts. Perfectly fried with an almost gooey inside, rolled in cinnamon and sugar... jeezus. 

And yes, their coffee is still my favorite. If they had wi-fi there I'd be sitting at their coffee bar every single morning. Which would be great because of the coffee, but bad because of the donuts... 

Go for brunch and experience it for yourself. It's just lovely.

WOW. How cool is this place? (Answer: extremely cool. Think deep reds, dim lights, incredible decor and seating for maybe only 20-30 people.) Intimate, special, and classy. A perfect way to spend an evening, at least in my eyes. This new spot is worthy of a visit and has the potential to be something awesome! 

It sometimes bugs me when St. Louisans (or people visiting) make comments that our restaurants and bars aren't as cool as those in bigger cities like New York or Chicago. I personally think that the STL is kicking ass in the restaurant scene, and I love all of these great new places that keep popping up! This is the perfect example... Bar Les Freres reminds me of an amazing find in Montreal or Paris, and it's right here in our awesome city. Seriously. These folks are taking it to a whole new level!

I gotta be honest, the server who took care of us wasn't the best. When we walked in, he just kind of stared at us for several seconds before awkwardly telling us where to sit, and was a little cold and even borderline rude during our visit. It was almost like he wanted us to leave (which might be true since we weren't ordering entrees... but is it not cool to just order drinks and apps anymore?) Regardless, he didn't ruin our visit and I really enjoyed the experience.

The drink list is pretty interesting and I couldn't decided what I wanted... I was eying the champagne cocktail but ended up getting a Manhattan with a splash of club soda (my go-to.) The owner had us switch seats when we first got there so he gave us some delicious salmon which was greatly appreciated and fun to try! We ordered the cheese plate which is always my favorite thing to graze on, and it was fantastic. They gave us a perfect amount of crostini, and go figure my favorite cheese was the triple-cream that was 75% butter fat. Just so delicious. There were three types of cheese in a generous amount.

The entrees looked insane and I want to go back and try the filet. My only fear with this place is showing up and it being full, because there's literally no area to wait for a table to open - it's that tiny! My advice is to get there early and be prepared to make a night out of it. Luckily, I don't think you'll be disappointed. Can't wait to discover more about this adorable little spot!

PS. Be prepared to sit VERY close to other people. We actually shared a couch with another pair and ended up joking that we should all be friends and share our conversations. If you're a freak about personal space, Les Freres might not be for you... but I actually found this quite charming.

Uhhhh... hum...

I'm going to need to take this moment to tell you about a menu item at Ernesto's (yes, they have a full menu of small plates, cheeses, and entrees) called the "Best Grilled Cheese." It comes with wild mushrooms, prairie breeze English cheddar cheese, black truffle fontina and white truffle oil. If you're like me, you probably read that and thought, "what the hell does that even mean?" It doesn't matter because it's that ridiculously good. Pair that with one of their chardonnays and you're set for the evening. That grilled cheese is dynamite.

The service here is so great, and they'll let you try whatever wine you want before you order it. Go through the place to the back to sit on the patio... it's spring and summer perfection! I love that it's so tiny and intimate. It's places like Ernesto's that make me appreciate St. Louis and its small businesses!

I had a great experience at Salt + Smoke last week. A group of four of us stopped in before a show at the Duck Room, and we used NoWait to make sure we weren't getting hangry while waiting for a table.

We were sat pretty quickly, and holy hell this place gets busy, even on random weeknights. There were so many people enjoying the weather, their cocktails, and great BBQ, and it was definitely busy (and pretty loud.) 

We started off with drinks, and it turns out they make a really impressive old fashioned. It was one of the best I've had in a really long time. Also, they make a mean dirty martini, which I think is impressive and unexpected for a BBQ joint. We were thrilled with what we ordered.

Next up: BBQ, obviously. I chose a caesar salad (I know, I know.) I'm trying to eat a little lighter these days, BUT, I did get it topped with pulled pork, and that was a really great choice. The meat was absolutely fantastic. I also got a few bites of my fiancee's white cheddar cracker mac, and that was so great as well.

I really enjoyed my evening here and will be back! Salt + Smoke is a really fun choice for dinner in the Loop.

Picasso's is a delightful little coffee house on Main Street in St. Charles. I don't find myself out that way too often, but when I am, it's my go-to spot. I like to snag a table towards the back and work away on my computer over a latte, but it also makes a great lunch spot or just a good place to relax! They open at 6:30am which I always appreciate in a coffee shop, and on Thursday, Friday and Saturday they're open until midnight! 

They book local musicians and artists, and each month they showcase work from someone new. The current artist is Jim Koetting, who specials in underwater photography, mainly shipwrecks from around the world. How cool is that? It makes it fun to look around and you might even learn something new. They often have live music, too.

The coffee drinks are always on point, but I can't speak much to the food. I've only had the hummus plate but I can't quit raving about it! The garlic hummus was so filling, and I loved how much fresh cucumber and bell pepper came along with it. It's not easy to eat healthy away from home, so I love a place that loads me up with veggies.

The place isn't huge so be prepared to have to hunt for a few or wait for a seat to open... your best bet is in the afternoon during the week. Great little spot in St. Charles!

I first visited Fiddlehead Fern for a coffee meeting, and immediately knew I'd be back many times afterwards. This place is so great! The street parking outside is always a breeze, and there always seems to be a table open. Maybe I shouldn't be sharing all of my secrets on Yelp so it stays that way. However, I think the people deserve to know.

FF can accomplish many things: a coffee meeting, a lunch, quiet solo time, or a place to catch up with friends. It's airy and beautiful, and the simplistic style is relaxing and a breath a fresh air. The staff is always very friendly as well.

You can't go wrong with any of the hand-brewed coffees. Tell the barista what you're in the mood for and they'll pick out the beans that are right for you. The coffee is served in beautiful, ornate coffee cups, and is strong and brewed perfectly.

If you're looking to up your Instagram game, you need to get a couple of their toasts. I'm a huge fan of the smashed avocado, the chickpea, and the brie. You really can't go wrong. Luckily, the toasts all taste as well as they photograph.

They recently had a brick thrown through their front door as part of a robbery, and now display the brick with flowers coming out of the top right by the register. This place has the character, beauty, and heart that make up the best of St. Louis' businesses. Give them a visit!

A five-star restaurant in every way.

I Fratellini is such a beautiful place. If you're looking for an impressive date night spot, this should be on your list. If you're celebrating something special, this should be on your list. For no special reason at all, this should be on your list.

The vibe inside reminds me a lot of New York City for some reason. It's so busy and bustling, it's dimly lit, and you really do get wrapped up in the art of great food and wine. The wine list itself is really nice... I'm not too big into Italian reds, but our server during our last visit had us taste a few things until we found one we really liked.

The food... well. Words don't really do it justice. If you want something to start, I highly recommend the speck with artichoke hearts and shaved parmigiano-reggiano. It's drizzled with olive oil and I think I'd order it every time. When it comes to pasta, I can't say enough about the tagliatelle with prosciutto and mushrooms in garlic cream. It's so rich and flavorful, and will make everyone else at the table very jealous.

End your meal with the blueberry nut tart topped with vanilla gelato, and you'll be the most satisfied diner in the world. This place is pure magic!

Wow - color me surprised. This place is fantastic! I visited on a weekday with my mom for lunch, and I have to admit, I wasn't too excited when she said she wanted to go there for lunch. I believe my exact line was "that's fine, but I don't really feel like bar food." Well now I feel like an idiot because as I was walking through the door, I saw this written on the wall: amazing vegetarian Russian menu. Say WHAT?

Vegetarians, run to this place. Hell, even meat eaters should run here too. Sure it just feels like a standard bar inside (although the huge mural on the wall is pretty cool,) but you're going to fall in love with the menu. I had no idea what to choose, so I ended up going with the Red Goat sandwich which comes loaded with roasted beets, avocado, goat cheese, arugula and dill sauce. It was absolutely heavenly, and basically combines all of my favorite things into one sandwich. That being said, my mom's lunch won. She ordered off the Russian side of the menu and went with the Veggie Pelmeni, which is house made Russian style dumplings with vegetarian fillings, served in vegetable stock and topped with seasonal greens. I swear there was some yummy dill in there too. We were so surprised! Next time I'm just going to order them both and call it a day. Because there WILL be a next time.

I cannot wait to go back to HandleBar to explore the rest of their menu. I feel so ignorant for not knowing how cool this place truly is. If I can walk out of a lunch totally satisfied without feeling like I ate too much, that's a winner. Get to this place as soon as you can, and order a few things so you get to experience how great the cooking really is.

I absolutely loved the recent dinner I had at Tree House and am already planning my next visit. These people know what they're doing.

A friend and I went on a Thursday evening and it was pretty quiet inside! Right away I noticed the cute little bar they have... it only seats a handful of people, but is adorable and pretty cozy. We grabbed a table by the front windows and our server was right over with a cocktail list. I ordered something fizzy with strawberry (I'm a bad Yelper and don't remember the name), and it was wonderful. I wanted to try more but decided I should probably save that for the weekend...

We started off with the beet hummus which I loved! The flavor was spot-on and it was a great starter to share. The star of my meal, though, was my entree: the stuffed eggplant. It was filled with fennel, leeks, potatoes, bell pepper, onion, and kalamata olives, all on top of curried cous cous, dried fruit, preserved lemon yogurt sauce, and toasted pecans. For a moment, I died and went to vegetarian heaven. I want to try something different the next time I go, but I'm not so sure this dish can be topped.

We somehow resisted dessert, but I had my eye on a few things. I also want to try out their brunch! Can't wait to explore more of the menu and enjoy this awesome South Grand spot again.

I am all about that Sunday lunch buffet life.

House of India is exceptionally good. There's a reason it gets so busy on the weekends. If you're heading in for lunch, be ready to wait a few minutes... but don't you worry. It's definitely worth it.

The variety on the lunch buffet is awesome. There are a ton of vegetarian options and meat options as well, all with so much flavor. I always get pissed because I'm full way earlier than I want to be. I blame the naan.

Also, less than $10 per person? When you consider the amount of food you get during the buffet, that is a huge steal. 

Not much else to say here -- House of India is some of the best Indian food in St. Louis.

I'm partial to the Delmar location since it's so close to my house, but any Mission Taco Joint is getting five stars from me. What a great, casual place to get some of the best tacos around.

When deciding on a drink, just tell the bartender to make you a spicy margarita. You won't regret it. I do recommend having some water nearby because they make them very (*very*) spicy. You'll never see me complain about that.

I always like to start with the guacamole and then queso con chorizo. Don't forget to save room for the tacos! I recommend trying the taco of the month (whatever it might be) along with the beef brisket and baja fish. Speaking of the taco of the month - they once partnered with Mai Lee on a creation and I so hope they bring that back one day (hint, hint.)

Download the NoWait app so you can put your name in before you go because there's often a wait for a table. I love this spot and I'll definitely be back soon.

The Yelp Eats train stopped at the Duck tonight, and boy am I sure glad it did! I've written two reviews already (some of you have to be thinking, get over it...) so I'm going to keep it short and sweet. Here are the must-haves off the Yelp Eats menu:

-Hush duckies (fried carbs + bacony, oniony goodness)
-Gumbo sampler (because you NEED to try all three)
-Pulled pork flatbread (beyond satisfying and savory, and comes cut with the pieces pulled apart so you really have to do minimal work here.)
-Meatloaf with a side of mac'n'cheese (comfort food to the extreme.)

The best part of my dinner was seeing my fellow Yelp Eaters, Marjie and Lyn! The two glasses of a California red blend was the second best. The third was getting to listen to the live music while we waited out the rain.

I'm pretty sure after three reviews the whole world now knows how I feel about The Shaved Duck. My work here is done.

Listen. As healthy as we all try to be, there's nothing wrong with waking up on a Sunday morning craving a freshly-baked donut. It happens to me quite a bit (probably way more than it should), and when the feeling hits, Donut Drive-In is where I go. I can confidently say that they have the best donuts anywhere in St. Louis, hands down. 

Heads up, the parking lot is a little small and can be interesting to navigate if it's busy inside. That brings me to my next point, which is that the inside of Donut Drive-In is smaller than you can imagine. As in, if there are more than a handful of people inside you'll have to wait out the door small. Which is something I'll gladly do, but I would've liked knowing that before my first visit. Third note: bring cash. You won't need a lot... if you're buying for less than three or so people, five bucks should cover it. On my most recent visit I had a chocolate long John (oh my God, drool-worthy) and a vanila custard donut for a grand total of $1.89. I felt like I was stealing. 

The donuts here just taste fresh and have the perfect texture and consistency... and I love seeing all the action behind the counter! The young girls that work the register are as sweet as can be, too. Just a wonderful, tiny, thriving local business. I'm a huge fan and there's a big chance you'll spot me if you stop in on a Sunday morning. Hooray for donuts!

I don't go to Ameristar with hopes of winning a lot of money... I really just go because it's a hell of a lot of fun. We usually end up here when we have something to do in the area beforehand, and it's cool because there's a handful of fun things to do when inside! 

The Lixx bar inside the casino is usually where I go first, and the drinks never disappoint. They have a martini called the Full Tilt Pomtini that's really good, but my standard rum & diets with lime are always made perfectly, too (though I guess that's not too hard...) You can sit at the bar here (plenty of seating) or grab a booth while you people watch. It's so fun to sit and sip drinks while watching everyone gamble under all of the bright & blinking lights... it's like sensory overload in the best way possible. As far as the gambling goes, I've only played the slots here and also roulette, in which I did NOT win. I did the opposite of winning, actually. Charlie Sheen would be very disappointed in me.

I like Bottleneck, too... see my previous review. Live music & booze heaven. And of course Pearl Oyster Bar. They're serving Creole and Cajun cuisine and surprisingly also some Asian-inspired dishes. Just straight up fun. The diner is cool, too, and has everything you need for an after-gamble dinner or breakfast... I used to eat here after dancing the night away at Home nightclub, but alas, Home is gone. Which is kind of okay with me actually.

Solid place to have fun and make a night out of it. Take a staycation and enjoy the gorgeous hotel rooms, too!

Five Star Burgers? No... five star everything. I was completely blown away on all fronts when I lunched at this new Clayton spot. Parking in Clayton during lunchtime is such a pain in the rear, but it was very much worth the hassle. 

I thought about grabbing my friend and I a table outside but it was pretty warm (in late October? St. Louis is weird.) I ended up going inside to the hostess stand and the owner himself came over to seat me. He was so friendly and welcoming and thanked me for coming before I even ordered anything! We scored a two-seater in the very back of the place and it was the perfect spot for two people. There were bigger tables available for larger groups, and also a couple of bar-type areas for those lunching alone or not worried about sitting at a table. 

Our server was so friendly and told us his name right away, and you can tell the staff here is committed to giving their customers a positive experience. I love that they leave a bottle of water on the table, and the ice tea I had definitely hit the spot. After just a minute I knew what I wanted to order: the magic mushroom burger. I had it cooked medium, and it comes topped with sauteed Ozark Forest mushrooms, caramelized onions, and Swiss cheese. At first glance it may just look like a regular 'ole mushroom burger, but it's not. I don't know what the hell they do to the meat, but it was so tender and flavorful. I cringe when people say the phrase "it melted in my mouth" but it literally did... there's no other way to put it. I also scored bigtime on my side when I ordered the sweet potato fries with salted maple cream. Yes, I said salted maple cream. I can't explain how good these were... I will never look at sweet potato fries the same again. 

So many other things caught my eye here, including the $1 Serendipity Ice Cream shooters in vanilla and salted caramel. They also offer a huge list of specialty cocktails, beer cocktail floats (!), and boozy shakes. The Rattle & Roll is made with Serendipity vanilla ice cream, peace vodka, bourbon, whipped cream and orange zest. Isn't that reason enough to visit this place again? On the way out, two servers plus the owner thanked us for our business and wished us a nice day.

I'm very much sold on this place. Make sure to stop by and enjoy... but do so with an empty stomach! Nice job, Five Star.

Yum. Yum. Yum. Yum.

Yum.

Okay I'm done.

I love the food at Lemongrass and have officially found my favorite dish! The curry eggplant, or com cari ca tim... steamed rice and stir-fried eggplant with carrots & onions in a curry and coconut milk sauce. This one is so good and the flavors pop right out at you! I might make a request for them to make it spicy next time, but this is likely what I'll order the next few times I'm in. Sweet and sour tofu (or com dau hu sot chua ngot) is also pretty good. Nothing beats that curry & eggplant combo, though.

I have tons of love for Lemongrass because they're open from lunch until dinner without closing in between like most of the surrounding restaurants! What's a girl to do when she's hungry at 3pm, you know? It's pretty quiet in there in the middle of the day though... abnormally quiet. I wish they'd turn some music on or do something to make it not as awkward. 

Cool place, good food!

It's patio time again and this girl is in heaven. I still stand by my previous review but feel compelled to share a new menu favorite... the vegetable gratin. It's loaded with fresh vegetables and also has some gnocchi added in, and the flavors are absolutely perfect. A couple of warnings, though... it's not very big, so order something else if you're starving, or partake in the bread and herbed butter they bring out. It also has a ton of onion so do not order if that isn't your thing.

Another menu favorite is definitely the vanilla bean creme brulee! Odd reference, but the top of it tastes like burnt marshmallows... straight from the campfire. Underneath the hard layer is creamy, vanilla-y, sweet goodness.

Still love this place very much and can't wait to work through some more of the menu.

My best friend Kate & I had our weekly dinner this week at Five Bistro and I've been wanting to get in there for a long time, and it turns out that Tuesday night is the night to go! Plenty busy but still a bunch of tables available... it's nice to see a place come so alive during the week. It's situated on the Hill and there was plenty of parking if you can parallel (I don't mean to brag but I'm kind of great at that, sooo...)

We were greeted by a very friendly guy who sat us by the front windows and I immediately loved our surroundings & the vibe of the place. Clean, tons of natural light, bright colors... scenery fit for a restaurant serving up unique dishes made from local ingredients. Definitely my kind of place! Our server was right over and had glasses of wine in front of us within a few minutes, and went over all the specials and the ever-changing menu. He was very informative but pretty dry and so trained that he was almost like a robot... It was almost awkward whenever he came over. I even cracked a funny joke (more corny than funny) and he didn't even budge! He also brought out "a gift from the kitchen" which was a tiny pastry filled with some kind of trout salad which was yummy.

The salads we started out with were fantastic, and I had a field salad with an egg cracked on top, and it also came with a slice of tangy brie & an olive relish. The best discovery? The chunks of homemade bread underneath the salad all soaked in the dressing. Heavenly...

For dinner I had a ravioli filled with vegetables and Baetje Farm goat cheese, all topped with mushrooms and a gorgeous lemon creme sauce. The only bad thing about this dish was pretty glaring... it came with two ravioli. Yeah, only two ravioli. It's a good thing I wasn't starving! I mean, I know it wasn't one of the bigger entrees, but really, two ravioli? It just seemed a little silly to me. Kate's mussels were okay but she said the sauce had way too much lime in it and she only got halfway through it. I've seen the girl put away some mussels, so I could tell they weren't the best. We made more wine at this point so I cared a little less about the entree.

For dessert we had a pastry with a sugary goat cheese filling in between two homemade sugar cookies, with a side of honey gelato. Dessert was also just okay... there were some odd flavors going on and the cookies were really hard.

I'm not really sure on Five yet. The place itself and the quality of the food is excellent, but I'd be interested in trying their entrees... was eying the beef tenderloin for next time when I'm more hungry. It was a good night, though, and it's definitely worthy of a second trip!

I was so happy to finally get to try this place! I stopped by for dinner with a good friend of mine on a cold weekday and we decided to hang at the bar instead of waiting for a table (which honestly is much more fun anyway.) 

The reason this review is four stars instead of five is because I didn't like either of the craft cocktails I tried, which really never happens to me. I switched to wine and that was wonderful, but the cocktails were not doing it for us. I'll definitely give that another chance on my next visit.

Everything on the menu looked so good, but since we couldn't try everything, we decided to start with the bacon jam and melted brie spread and the deviled eggs with bacon chips. The deviled eggs were A-OK - definitely good but not mind-blowing. The jam, however, I could eat every day for the rest of my life. Just so good. It's impossible to stop after a few bites.

After that came the avocado tacos and a bahn mi burger (that was a special the night we were there.) Both things absolutely blew us away. The tacos had amazing flavor and texture and were perfectly spicy, and the burger was five stars and beyond. I sure hope they add it to the regular menu.

I'll definitely be back to try more, and I'm glad to have a new awesome spot in St. Louis!

I'm just here to rave a little more about Sardella, particularly their brunch.

Did Gerard Craft just wake up one day and think to himself... "self, why don't you try putting Eggs Benedict inside of ravioli?" I'm sure there was more thought behind this, but I don't really care how it happened, because WOW. I have found my favorite new brunch item in St. Louis. If you haven't tried this yet, you need to break all of your other plans and get here fast. It's just so impressive. How do they keep the yolk perfectly runny inside of a gorgeous homemade ravioli? My mind is blown.

Other recent highlights include the warm cinnamon roll, and the heirloom tomato egg toast on Union Loafer's bread. I am so impressed by this place and cannot wait to get back here soon.

Fast Eddie's is perfect for a sunny Sunday afternoon, but last night in honor of one of my best friend's 25th birthday, we rode an obnoxiously large party bus to the land of meat and beer. Yup, we were "that group." She somehow found a party bus that had a real DJ in it, and we managed to fit 40 people inside. Bob the bus driver drove us out to Alton and we filed off one by one.

Realizing it was 10:57pm and the kitchen closes at 11pm, we literally ran to the food counter to order everything they had. No, seriously. 3 of us together ordered three cheeseburgers, three big elroys, three fries, pork kabobs, and hot chicken on a stick. The timing of this is pretty awesome considering my last review was about healthy living, but I will say that I just tried everything and let the boys wolf all of it down. It was a sight. But the food at Fast Eddie's is, well... fantastic! I don't know what they do to that beef, but seriously, those cheeseburgers are out of this world and the beef/green pepper combo on the elroys makes you want to bring it to bed and cuddle with it. 

We sat outside on the patio (which is still closed in right now) and watched a band of 5-6 older men who were blaring on the sax, bangin' on a piano and singing familiar tunes so the crowd could get down! There is such a wide variety of people that hang out there and it's just nice to see everyone so happy and having a ball. Places like this really make me love America & the Midwest even more. Good food, good beer, smiling faces...

The free popcorn rocks and we decided to take some back on the bus to eat while traveling to our next destination and a girl, who I'm not quite sure was invited by, told us we were gross for eating it. She said that people come out of the bathroom and reach their hands in there. We had even more fun after that comment because we kept eating it and called it "coochie corn" as we watched her roll her eyes and cringe in disgust. Don't make the trip if you can't hang with the big boys.

Epic night, great food, lots of memories! Very much in agreement with Jen J. that this is a 2-3 times a year spot and not a weekly hangout... but bring a camera. And wash your hands before you eat the popcorn, will ya?!

Oh no big deal, I only had one of the best meals of my LIFE last night at Scape. I seriously don't know what's going to be able to top it anytime soon. I was so surprised because I wasn't expecting to be blown away like I was... I've only been to the bar at Scape but last night was my first time eating dinner there, and I've heard mixed reviews. I can honestly say I don't have a single bad thing to say.

Per usual, dinner started off with a drink at the bar and I had a mix of wild tea vodka & lemonade... it was the perfect ode to warmer temps. We sat down a few minutes later and ordered a bottle of wine (the booze holds priority on weekends) and we took a chance on a red zin that ended up being phenomenal... it was dry with a touch of sweetness and had a little bit of pepper at the end. I was in wine heaven, for sure! It was around this time I noticed how magical the dining experience actually was (don't make fun of me for being this corny) and having the fountain right outside, seeing the buzz all over Maryland, and dining in the gold hues inside Scape just made for an incredible experience.

For appetizers we had the Black & Blue Mussels & the Bistro Cheese Board. I'm not a mussels fan, unfortunately, but I was plenty occupied with the goat cheese, bleu cheese, and almond/apricot loaf I had in front of me. It was served with warm, soft bread, and was a carb & cheese lovers paradise. I wanted to save room for an entree, though, and I'm so glad I did...

I'm just going to admit this to you guys right now before you hear it somewhere else... I broke off my engagement last night. Yup. I decided to marry Scape's Macadamia Nut Crusted Chicken instead. You would have made the same call had you been the one eating, trust me. Perfectly cooked chicken, papaya marmalade, sho-yu cream sauce and mashed potatoes better than my grandma made. When I go back, I'm ordering the same thing. Check out all of the photos that go with this review because our table of four also ordered the Seared Yellow Fin Tuna, Classic Steak Frites, and the "It's 7 A.M. Somewhere." (In case you're curious on that last one, it's farmers cheese pancakes with lemon curd, fresh blueberries and warm Vermont maple syrup, all served with thick sliced Neuski bacon and three eggs to order. Uh huh.)

What a surprisingly great dinner & evening! The chicken & I are registered at Crate & Barrel if anyone's interested.

Being from the East Coast, I was looking forward to having a GOOD pastrami sandwich on rye bread while here at the U of A.

I honestly was so thoroughly disappointed with my sandwich. Especially, after the waitress had said "it's the best pastrami in Arizona". Totally far from true. Also everyone knows any real deli serves Dr. Brown soda, which they do not.

If you want a decent sandwich head to 5th Street Kosher Deli. That's where you can actually get a GOOD pastrami sandwich!

This was one of my favorite live music experiences in Nashville. I could easily picture the talent we saw Amber's Drive at the Listening Room Cafe breaking out and making it big and I assume their other scheduled gigs are equally impressive. The sound system and acoustics were excellent! The venue is spacious and clean with friendly staff. You can reserve a seats online and they start seating 15 minutes before the performance. The hostesses have the system nailed down and quickly seat guests. We placed a drink order and our waiter had our cocktails well before served before the show began.

The drink menu consists of an excellent selection of drafts, cocktails and wine. While we only partook in drinks the food smelled delicious and looked to be large portions. I ordered a malbec and later a champagne cocktail named berries and bubbles. 

If you love live music seeing a band at the Listening Room Cafe while in Nashville is a must.

We stopped in during a tour of Music Row. The restaurant pays tribute to many great musicians with themed booths and relics throughout the building. The bar is located at the front of the building and extends out to a large patio. The bar is open to the elements and they do not keep their liquor or red wines cool which is a no no in my book so I opted for a chilled Sauvignon Blanc. They offer free fried pickles with a Yelp checkin but our tour also included a sample. I am usually not a fan of fried pickles but theirs are really good! Thinly sliced, lightly tempura fried and served with a tasty spicy sauce.

They have a stage with a cool backdrop which makes for a good photo op.

Decided to try a new local eatery for our Anniversary.  When we arrived, they weren't busy at all. There was one other couple in the dining room, and they turned out to be the owners of the place (Which is really cool because that lead to a lot of info being shared and a nice chat).

Our waitress, Gina, is the owner's daughter. She was warm and friendly and very good at her job. We started our meal with a Cappuccino and a frosty Sam Adams which was perfect as we looked out over lake Tarpon inlet.  The fresh bread and Pesto (It's the best-o) is amazing, the pesto is absolutely DELICIOUS and made in house.  We ordered their Brussel Sprout starter as well, and we were NOT disappointed, ZOMG I could eat that EVERY dang day.  It was crispy, full of flavor and I need it in my life, and so do you.  It is also keto friendly.  Get you some. 

For mains, My husbeast ordered the house made lasagne and I got the Duroc maple glazed pork chops. We were warned that the chops had a longer cooking time, and I assured the owner that this was fine. We'd wait without a problem. They were only too happy to let us know about their experience (Previous owners of a pizzeria in Oldsmar that was really popular as well as another venture so they're familiar with food) and that the family is in the kitchen and much of the staff.  They are passionate about food and it shows. This place is amazing and I really hope it stays. 

Our food came out and we were thrilled. The lasagna came in a cast iron skillet and my HUGE 14oz double chop and sides (mixed veg and mashed sweet potato) Were served on a cutting board, beautiful presentations!  But it wasn't until we tasted the food that we knew what we were in for. 

Guys, You all know that I'm all about what a place is like for service, and this place has that.  BUT THE FOOD!! ZOMG ! The food here is incredible, and I mean that. The pork was tender and so flavorful, The maple and garlic glaze gave it kind of an Asian influence, but OMG so So SO good! The lasagne was tender and so full fo cheese and meat sauce.  

Neither of us could finish it. We both left with enough for another meal. 
We didn't have enough space for dessert but their big thing is Creme brulee and Tiramisu, so you know that I'll be back. 

I look forward to being a regular here.  Grand opening is this coming weekend May 16-20th, I'm told that they'll be doing give aways and what have you, so make sure you come out and see what they have.  This place is going to be a go to for my family, make your reservations accordingly!

It was a roll the dice day, and I wanted some place I've not been before... The pointer landed on Johnny Grits. It was close to home, and that made things Easy.  We made the short drive to Klosterman and to Johnny Grits. 

It wasn't terribly busy, and with food this good, I'm Surprised. They're hidden, perhaps that's why, but what ever the reason, the word needs to get out. Granted most days they're only open until 2, but on Thrusday  - Saturday they're open until 8. Get there!

We were seated immediately, and noticed that the place was Clean and fairly large. The staff was happy and did a lot of work to keep busy. No one was idle or just hanging around. Something you see at places that just don't care. 

Our Waitress, Renee, was AWESOME. She really seemed to care if we came back in the future. We asked what was good, and she mentioned the Shrimp and Grits.. She RAVED about it. Said that once you had it, you'd come back, you'd crave it.  Well, that sold the Husbeast, and he ordered it with the andoullie sausage.  Me, I went for the chicken and waffles with 100% maple syrup.  Once the order was placed and our coffees were on the table, we didn't wait terribly long. 

The food was Beautiful when it was presented.   My chicken was golden brown and the waffle was light and fluffy.. absolutely delightful. It came to life in my mouth. THe husbeast nodded.. he said to me "Yep, She was right,I'm going to crave this.." and so now I'm going to have to go there on Tuesdays when the shrimp and grits is $2 off!  

Go and find this little gem, You won't be wasting your time.

I had been excited to try Texas de Brazil, and my first chance was going to be with my friends at a birthday celebration.  We were a party of 5 and seated near the salad bar. Our server was polite, and the bread that was dropped at the table was interesting. 

Our meat cowboys didn't seem to pay any attention to the red or green signs that our table displayed AT ALL. They simply were there, Ready to serve you meat. Some of which was very tasty, some.. eh. it was ok. 

The salad bar was good, I enjoyed the selections there in, and my friends love the bisque.  We had trouble getting the friends birthday discount applied to our checque.

So when I first visited back in 2013, I gave them a 2 stars. They've improved but not a lot.  I have found the non smoking area, but found that many of the machines there were in need of repair ( a whole bank of wheel of fortune machines was cordoned off with tape and half taken apart) and many were just not up to snuff - by sound not working or just having the blue screen of death. 

Quite honestly, the area needs to be larger, as it was the most crowed area of the casino.  I did not appreciate the people who walked towards the bakery STILL SMOKING. That was wholly inconsiderate of the non-smokers. 

Also noticed that they are now charging a $10 parking fee for every car.  Your first half hour is free, but "All day" which lets be honest, can be 2 hours or 12 hours, in my opinion the $10 parking rate is ... kind of steep, especially for those who are there frequently (Daily) or those who come only for a little bit of time. Let's also talk about the issue the parking meters have on getting into and out of the parking garage (South), there is inevitably a hold up because they're new, and it takes folks some time to get their ticket and get through the barrier.

I'm not sure I know what they're doing with this fee, but sure, it's a revenue generator. Yet I think it will limit people coming as well.

I didn't even know that this one existed, but the husbeastie and I were driving by so we stopped in. 

The first thing we noticed was how spic and span it was, how clean it appeared to be. How everything it shined. The waitress was extremely warm and friendly and the food came up really quickly. We both ordered ourselves Chili 4 & 5 way respectively - the husbeastie even opted for their new spicy cheese because for him, anything hot is good. 

We liked out dining experience. If we're in the area we'll stop in.

Tucked away in a partially defunct strip mall, between Pinch a Penny and an empty Winn Dixie, is Bj's Asian Fusion.  You can't miss it because of the blinding LED lights that surround the windows and door.  Once inside, it smells great and the place is very neat, a wall booth and tables w/chairs line one wall, the center is filled with tables and chairs and the other wall is filled with booths. Plenty of seating for everyone, and of course there is the ever popular take out. Mind you, this is not your everyday Asian take out. 

The menu is THICK.. there is Chinese, Thai, Japanese and Sushi on the menu, and plenty to choose from, you can't possibly leave here with an empty belly. If you do, you must not have eaten for a week! 

We started with an appetizer, this was a mistake, we had no idea how big the portions were, so... in the future we won't do this. We started with the Thai spring rolls, they were very fresh and very tasty, but their peanut sauce was a bit too sweet for me.  Since I ordered the hibachi dinner, I also got a salad and soup with my meal, I HAD NO IDEA there was going to be so much!  The won ton soup was DELICIOUS, the Salad was good, but there was way too much dressing (One of the reason for not 5 stars), the Hibachi style steak and shrimp was good, but the the steak was over cooked, to the point of being dry and tough.   The husbeast had one of the chef's specialties, the Dragon and Phoenix (?) The way he ate it, I can honestly say he LOVED it.  

All in all it was absolutely delicious, we will certainly come back.

All the press has reminded me I've never given PYT a review!  I'll keep it brief:

-I've always been given excellent service
-I've never been shamed for ordering one of their intense veggie burgers (enthusiastically encouraged, in fact!)
-Food has been delightful- BF loves every meaty burger he has tried, and I was shocked by how much we liked the fried pickles!
-Awesome happy hour deals!


Bad service deserves 10% tip.  Less than that is stealing.  And PYT has never, in my experience, warranted less than a 20% tip.  Sorry for jerks, guys.  Keep up the good work :)

Ultimate idiot lemming experience. 

They make OK pizza served with a massive dose of pretension. "We don't have a phone..maximum order of two pizzas per party...there are only 40 pizzas a night."

Wow- awesome, I want to wait in line to be treated like crap and pay $29 for a pizza.

Bad experience after bad experience at this place. Horrible service, horrible product, and can't believe they are still in business.

Emailed to bring up my complaint and experience and they never bothered to reply. I will make sure to tell everyone to avoid this place like the plague.

New Orleans has been my favorite place to visit for over 35 years... Dec 2018 was my first visit to Willie Mae's Scotch House. I'm thinking "Finally!"

I do not have patience. I will not wait two hours to eat fried chicken. Or four plus hours to eat BBQ in Austin. I'm not that kind of foodie. Although I do admire dedication of those that do. 

We drove overnight approximately 9 hours to get to NOLA from SATX. We checked into hotel then headed to WMs about opening time. It's was a holiday, Christmas Eve, so I will say the line started off slow. There was still a line but 20 min is nothing. When we walked out after lunch, that line was probably two hours. 

We ordered chicken and fish. We really enjoyed the chicken. Really moist and full of flavor. Gotta have macaroni and fried okra, definitely a southern thang. We also enjoyed the red beans and rice. Hubby had a salad. We rolled out there... 

MUST DO! At least once If you love legendary dining in NOLA.

My second trip to Nawlins in 93, brought me into Frank's for lunch. My friend and I ordered the stuffed artichoke and muffuletta to share before we even knew what a muffuletta was (reminded us of a Schlotzsky's original but oh so better!).... and here we are 25 years later and it's still around!

Over the years, I have had muffulettas in several other places in town including Central Grocery which the sandwich originated down the block, I like Frank's the best!

We typically sit upstairs on the balcony overlooking the Joan of Arc statue and the French Market... or just take it to go and sit by the river! 

Enjoy the "MUST DO" sandwich while in NOLA!

Little dive diner in the middle of the French Quarter on Bourbon St... what more could you ask for when you are starving... 

... some good diner food!

Our burger was awesome and just what we needed!

Bugs crawling up the wall and on the table is not very appetizing. Manager admitted they have a problem right now. Ok, sure. How about shutting down the place until the problem is resolved? What would John Taffer say? SHUT IT THE F DOWN!!

The food and drinks were fine. The service may have been the worst I've had in years. The main course came before my guacamole and chips( which took 45 minutes). Our cocktails came after the guacamole. Waiter kept apologizing. Hope they get it together because the Mezcal drinks were great.

Raging is golden in my eyes. I felt almost guilty cheating on them. As soon I walked backed into their arms, I was greeted with a big smile, a willing attitude, quick hands and salivating fresh baked goods.

Whether it be tea, coffee or almond milk cappuccino, the fellas behind the counter here know how to throw it down.

If I were go to go back to Renee's, it would only be for their 10" gluten free pizza (it only comes in one size) or any regular pizza over 12". Everything else that I tried on their on the menu (the desserts & the regular 8" pizza) can go on with their bad selves. 

The gluten-free pizza was a crunchy, thin, palette pleaser. Two out of five of us ordered the personalized versions and I couldn't get enough.

Papa ordered the 12" regular crust for his barbecue (cage-free, organic) chicken pizza subbing Daiya (vegan) cheese in place of the regular. As we parted the table, there was precisely one slice left! Score!

The rest of us (two more), ordered the smallest pizzas (8") with regular crusts. Grandma ate all of hers--at this point in her life, her tastebuds are not as discriminating as the rest of us. My personal pizza, on the other hand, was wrong, but I must mention they kindly took it off the bill without any hesitation. Perhaps it was my fault in my choice of toppings, but there was more than one of us that did not have a liking for the odd taste of the crust and lack of flavor in the ingredients.

Between the vegan, gluten free "whoopie pie" that seemed to have no cream substitute (for my favorite creamy middle part) and the "pistachio" aka the vanilla ice cream with pistachio nuts scarcely placed throughout, we could have easily enjoyed dessert else where.

They did have a handful of impressive wines (even carrying a yummy cab from M. Cosentino in Lodi), mixed cocktail drinks and hand-crafted beers (including a gluten free pilsner!) 

Also, there was nothing but goodness in the customer service department. For being in a fairly larger group than most of the other tables...we were served quickly and attended throughout our visit with timeliness, tolerance and great attitudes. 

For dine-in or take out I would for sure come back. Just writing about that gluten free pizza makes me hungry and craving for more. Yum!

Blue Willow's gift shop filled with miscellaneous novelties could easily keep me occupied and entertained for hours. Their novelties vary from magnetic poetry, PG13 versions as well as rated R, all the way to skull candies, gift cards, snoozie slippers, scarves, jewelry and so much more. They even have baked goods for sale at the counter, on your way out the door. 

The food is something special too... maybe not as special as their shop, but close. Gluten free and vegan inserts in the menu are a great start. When a restaurant cares that much about the clients special needs, it shows me that there is a good chance they care about their ingredients and where they came from as well. The blackened cajun-spiced salmon ceaser salad tickled my belly pink, seasoned to perfection and cooked just right. 

All the yoga teachers that joined in for our lunch retreat, indulged in various items featured on the menu, and then semi happily consumed. 

~Stir- Fry Veggies - good
~Huevos Rancheros - 2 stars (avoid the "Mexican" breakfast dishes here ;) )
~Apple Salad- If they actually remember the dressing and nuts, this salad is delightful

The atmosphere is what I would consider a very southwest-esque decor, paintings of sahuaros (cactus) hanging throughout, along plain white walls trimmed with cerrulean blue baseboard and moldings. White and blue floral painted on ceramic frames along the shelves and iron rod dividers near the fireplace and the floor.

Once again, it was another descent place within walking distance of the yoga studio I've been at all week for teacher training.  The food was great for me, okay according to the rest. The service was so-so, kind of disorganized and all over the place and took a long time after we ordered.  

Would I return? Oh yeah. I barely even scratched the surface of exploring all the items available.. Must go back!

Rating an entirely vegan restaurant can be a little difficult to discriminate good from bad. For one, I am happy they exist; for two, there should be more of them. 

Due to the close proximity to Yoga Oasis' Central Tucson location, and their pure existence I give them 4 stars. 

They are a great go-to for lunch or even a casual dinner. Order at the counter, grab a numbered wooden spoon stand, fill your tea, water, yerba mate or beverage of choice and have a seat at one of their tables or booths.

Every meal I've had at LS has been filling (almost big enough to share with two people), 100 % vegan, and created a feeling like I just got served a dish from mom's kitchen (homestyle and comforting.)
The staff and owner have always been great hosts and wonderful waiters (catering to us from order to finish.)

There is an entire (and extensive) gluten-free menu as well. I've tried a few things, but so far I'm particularly fond of the Adzuki (bean) burger that comes with your choice of potato salad, cole slaw or my favorite pick, the carrot-raisin salad. Yeah, give me some more lovin' spoonfuls of that anytime.

Came in for the bison chili and HH menu that was filled with appetizers and drink discounts. Server Amber friendly and helpful.

The bison chili is chock full of meat. My nose happily ran, no need for Tabasco. Can also get it in a sourdough bowl but was afraid that I'd eat the whole bread. The HH chix taco were 3 med size soft white flour filled with a lot of chopped up chix. Mr Bland loved it, although it was on the edge too spicy for him.
