Love the varied menu selections, from pub grub to chioppino, salads and desserts.

Do a Yelp check-in!

Server Martin took such great care of us.

Big draw here is their Nerf sized sourdough bread. Crispy on the outside, warm and soft in the middle. (Like me!)

Ordered the split pea soup and it was delicious. Excellent for dunking their buttered sourdough bread into.

Sashimi platter of course is fresh and the pieces soft. No stringy pieces.

Also the miso salmon was a HUGE chunk of fish with a sweeter shoyu sauce.

Their craft cocktails are intriguing, too. Enjoyed a prickly pear margarita which was NOT your usual margarita! Smokey tequila and black salt rim.

Beautiful, airy and spaced out restaurant. Covid standards adhered here.

This is a fine dining experience. The sit down restaurant is connected with their bar and Sushi & Sake. Some parts feel like a Paris street.

There is a dedicated bread Fairy. She has warm bacon-cheese or olive bread carried in her basket. I love my bread & butter and am appreciateful that this restaurant values their bread as much as their main meals.

Manager even stopped by to check on us. Nice.

Do a Yelp check-in, too!

A quick and quality ingredients of grilled cheese sandwiches. A hipconcept, adorable mustard painted take out shop. There is a small indoor eating area and 1 restroom. Limited parking. Sandwiches are served with a small cup of home-made tomato soup tucked in a white to go box.

This is no ordinary sandwich shop. Freshly baked soft but firm bread. Fun bomb sauces and garlicky dressing. Good amount of ingredients within sandwich.

I got my sub to-go and I could feel the hefty weight of the amount of ingredients.

Extra plus, it maintains its shape even when kept in fridge to be eaten later.

Lots of choices of toppings/ingredients.

Streamlined pasta menu. Pick your pasta, sauce and your protein. Of course, they do have featured specials. Their pasta and ravioli are freshly made so be prepared for a different noodle consistency.

Their complimentary rustic breads are served warm with olive oil.

The burratta is very rich.

Service is very personable. Owner very friendly.

Lots of parking.

BYOB.

Covid standards adhered here.

No spicy pickles appetizer given.

Marvelous tasting cabbage rolls with a cinnamon tinged red raisin sauce topping 

Huge pot of corner beef cabbage. Broth light and tasty, too.

Desserts look great but never had room in the stomach for more.

Covid standards adhered to in this brick and wood interior local restaurant and bar. Friendly service.

Loved the pricing, flavor and the dish choices. Not the usual pub grub or deep fried items. ie. Prime rib Stroganoff, salmon tacos, lamb chops..... like a higher end menu at a down to earth price.

**lots of seating on 2nd level at back and more at the patio!!        Everyone tried to squish in the active 1st floor but the 2nd level is temp cooler and also has all the fountain drinks, iced tea and bbq sauces you want.

Friendly workers. Easily used a spoon on the St Louis ribs. Brisket had a heavenly thick soft black bark, points of perfection.

The opener bread was a rustic crunchy delight. 

Enjoyed the duck tagliatelle that was  filled with a lot of duck morsels in a rich sauce. The crunchy duck skin was awesome.

In and outdoor seating.

The service started off well, but after our dishes were served we were left in the dust. Water wasn't refilled and no offers for a 2nd glass of wine. Seemed one louder more requestful of requests table demanded all the attention. After 15 minutes or so, we eventually got another workers attention and was finally able to get our bill from our original server.

In and outdoor seating. Best to get a reservation during these Covid times.

4.5 stars for this chain Italian restaurant. Sign up to be on their email list and they have many generous take-out and dine-in offers.

Large, clean restaurant making Covid standards easy to adhere to. The servers, though, need to walk far for their drinks and plate pick ups.

Large square rosemary bread given with EVOO. 

Got the chicken parmesan and it was thick and huge. Mild on the sauce, good on the melty cheese! All the tables took home leftovers!

This location does a lot of curb-side and to-go orders.

Super friendly and generous service.

Clean, friendly, welcoming Persian/Mediterranean restaurant. Interesting camera curio cabinet in the corner. Friendly guy.

Had the lamb tabouli salad. Loved the thin sliced lamb, kind of like lamb bacon! Tabouli had a wonderful amount of parsley. Meats are pleasantly spiced, not overwhelming salty or garlicky.

They make their own brewed tea, too. Tea kettle and all. Ice or hot.

Easy parking.

Ordering update**    There are 3 kiosks to order your sandwich and to pay for it. If you want a custom made sandwich, be patient and expect a lot of screen swiping for all their available ingredients. 

Sandwiches are still hefty. Workers there are still friendly as well as the cashiers. Clean tables.

Expanded outdoor seating.

Daily specials are the value here.

Almost every table had a version of a margarita. I got the Cadillac on the rocks.*punch* Nice and strong, but so easy to drink.

You can see the spices and the deep red ingredients in their rice. I actually enjoyed it.

Overall, mild recipes. They have soups, seafood and other Mexican dishes.

Felt very comfortable in this patio style but enclosed restaurant.

The salsa that came with the chips was mildly spicy. Wish the chips were warmed, though.

Sushi, soup pots and seafood is their forte here. One is overwhelmed by the signature garlic/celery salt aromas that greet you.

There is complimentary bread and butter.

The location is built over Virginia Street so one can view the traffic. Sunset mountain views are beautiful, too.

Go early to put in your reservation.

Efficient service.

Good sake selection.

Massive 4 floors, 2nd & 3rd banquet floors. Go straight to the top! Views, drinks and sushi?

Bottom floor drinks and bbq!

Had my eye on this specialty pizza joint for 2 years now but always came by too early and too late. Finally, we stopped in to enjoy their thin crusted but crispy crust yet chewy dough perfection of an East Coast Pizza. Thought it was "Guido", but it was a cool and friendly pizza guy and family with a heart of gold.

Great price, wonderful tasty pizzas, large LARGE sized pizza/calzone, friendly service and lots of parking. Reasonable prices on the quality of pizza. On top of it, this business supports fun young persons and community events in Reno.

To go, dine in, large salad servings, clean and spacious dining area, Maria (great server), seated quickly by hostess, quick delivery of food, tastes great, generous with the grated parmesan, table top payment, nice selection of wines and mixed drinks, pleasantly air conditioned, upbeat jazzy music,lots of parking and great prices.

Can't pick on anything. Left feeling happy and full.

Dining room is open now. Best to call with a reservation.

Love the wide bowl wine glass! Feels so festive!

Complimentary garlic bread given.

I like the ambience with the ceiling decorations. Celebrated mom's birthday here. Lots of good memories here.

Got the cioppino and it was filled with clams, mussels, shrimps and fish.  Fettuccine noodles.

Got the lemon blackened shrimp ravioli appetizer. Quite a refreshing creamy treat. 

They have port wine.

Expanded parking lot, more other drink selections and even limited snacks in fridge. Still air conditioned indoor seating and open-air outside warehouse seating.

Same great service, location and selection of bottled and beers on tap.

Lots of take-home purchases. They have a lot of merch. from shirts, cups, growlers and flasks.

Get the napkins out! Wonderful char burgers with a wonderful selection of reasonable priced fresh proteins. I got the bison and it was juicy, crispy and thick!

Cooked onions and standard toppings free! Extra for cheese and special toppings.

Fries. Hand cut thick and thin crispy and hot yumsies! Like the combination.

Beer on tap and other alcohol drinks available.

Fresh brewed iced tea, lemonade and standard soda fountain available.

Super friendly staff. Locally owned!

*sniff sniff* Has to be beautiful bbq!

Love their hot sauce and jalapenos. Made me happy. Their regular but great flavorful bbq sauce made Mr. Bland happy.

So they do make and bake their food items fresh so beware that they do run out out of things.

The brisket is a juicy dreamy super soft of heaven. Chicken wasn't on steroids, but the taste and skin, excellent. Chili was mild.

Comfy diner atmosphere. In, outdoor and bar top seats. Large parking lot. Server Danielle, sweet and efficient!

Drove past here how many times to see couples in the restaurant windows smiling and eating. Hey, I want to be smiling and eating wonderful food, too!

Came in on a busy Friday night. Check in with the hostess. Go to the little upper floor and get a kerpowy good Margarita while you wait for your table. Very good, not the bottled syrupy stuff. I got the Cadillac.

Chips and salsa served right away. Great service. Enjoyed a tasty chicken mole plate. Tasty, not spicy. Enjoyed the medium spiced salsa. Not overly salty.

Finally gotsta try the infamous spicy chicken sandwich! Virgin no more! Bun was soft, crunchy coating and a whole piece of chicken breast.

Easy and clean place. I really love their Popeyes sweet and un-sweetened brewed tea.

Want to try the sides and whole chicken pieces next time.

No grilled quail served here!

Sorry, couldn't resist! Lol!

A beautiful open kitchen designed restaurant with in and outdoor seating.

Servings are huge and saw lots of ladies sharing their meals this lunch visit. I shared my Asian chicken cup salad. Fresh and plentiful. Menu overall sounded fresh and they do have daily plate specials and soup of the day.

Did notice the clientele looked to be a little more mature professionals as opposed to younger college students. No children/babies today.

They are also open for dinner which is inviting, especially with the outdoor yellow umbrellas and gas light water fountain by the entrance

Came for the seafood buffet and enjoyed the outdoor tropical ambience, complete with huge trees.

Crab legs crackers and plastic cutters were already provided on the table. A plus, since other buffets, I need to ask for it and usually get only the plastic cutter ones.

Plates were cleared. Buffet trays were kept full. Good selections.

Perhaps some items, like the watermelon chunks were soggy, but understandably, it's not the season. The egg drop and the lentil soup were quite salty for my taste. Aside for these unusual nit-picky exceptions, a great buffet.

Take out only for the Covid era.

So this is a more upbeat and milder version of a Korean food establishment. Something's taste sweeter and not so spicy or heavy on the garlic or char.

They have brewed iced tea. A plus for me.

The sporks and containers are biodegradable and also fun to eat out of. I like the black drinking cups, too.

I paid $2 for a upgraded size and it was enough for a couple to enjoy.

They serve food, bar top gambling, their brewed beer and it turns into a night club with bands or DJ for dancing.

Bring your ID as they upload your info to their record, so behave.

I look forward to their specialty brews. This time it's a session Belgium, they do exist! The 9% Russian Stout did not dissapoint. Of course other standard variety of Brewer beers are here.

This place is still a success. It expanded its dining area, has fun shirts for sale and has maintained its standards for their sub and special sandwiches. Friendly staff overall.

Turkey subs come with a choice of shredded or thick sliced turkey. Like the choice. Of course, pick all your toppings, spreads and spices. Tastes like a homemade sub, but better.

The green chili soup was filled with cheese and cheese.  Full of flavor, a beautiful green hue. There are hot sauces.

Love the interior!! Transported to ones great-great grandmother's drinking room parlour. The curtains, exotic rugs and heavy plush furniture, awesome.

Gentleman bartender great and jovial. Introduced me to their homemade ginger soda, made with real ginger. Love the warmth.

There are outdoor benches. Love the flashing exterior lights that beckons you in.

Gem in Reno! 

Also came in for generous pours of the Dickle for the Yelp whisky hunt. I found a really awesome special place.

I keep coming back mainly for the M-F meal specials. My go to is a gravied up London Broil with mashed potatoes! So good. They also have other comfort specials priced right.

Other items are ample in serving size. Most people leave here with to-go boxes.

The variety of dishes, serving sizes and service here keeps me coming back. A lively Cafe, level above a diner.

Clean, that Japanese mirin smell and taste, great price, friendly service, and great beer and good sake selection.

Got the chicken curry rice and it came with multiple huge chunks of white chicken. Yummy carrots and pumpkin served with it. Surprised it had just enough rice with a warming curry sauce on it. Some places give way too much rice, it's perfect here.

Now to the extensive Japanese beers. They had some I still haven't tried. Many are super special brews and collaborations.

Nice sake selection, too.

I liked how they spaced the tables, provided disinfecting bottles and even a paper bag for your mask. I like these little but important touches.

Yelp offer not good unless manager is there and other web 20percent off coupon only good if it's printed out. Accounting, really? Shouldn't have to go through a hoop and ask a server the awkward "I have a Yelp offer" to be turned down. Best to remove the offer than try to offer 50cents off/5percent off Yelp offer than to embarrass or dissapoint the table humbly asking for it. Anyhoo....

The margarita was strong and tasty. It's served in a big glass mug.

The mole chicken plate flavorful but light on those fragrant spices and mouth heat. It was a top mole pick for me.

Sat outside on a marvelous Reno day in a black gated outdoor area.

This is for HH and our server Audrey, 5 stars. Server Audrey super cool and efficient. Felt very welcomed.

HH has such good discounts on most appetizer items and on almost all types of drinks.

The 1/2 nachos were HUGE! Lots of vinegar jalapenos on it, besides the real melted cheese, salsa, guac and sour cream. The Tabasco products were perfect for me. The salmon plate was standard with melted butter on the side, was good.

Came for the variety of dishes and bison chili, but HH veered to the mega half nachos.

The blue cucumber martini was yummy. A little sweet, cucumber taste is there and the color was not blue. Lots of bottled and draft beer to choose from.

Thanks Yelper Robert V for letting me know that Silver Peak Brewery was bought out by Sierra Nebada. Now I know why the don't carry Silver Peak brand beer. 

Covid standards adhered to here.

In and outdoor seating.

There is a happy hour on appetizers.

Full bar. Mainstay familiar beers available. Really wanted the Silver Peak, though.

Got a huge flat chicken sandwich and subbed the salad for fries. They have their fried beet chips that should be served as a main appetizer vs. just as a side topping on salads. Love it.

2 hour validated parking.

Great service.
Super friendly bartenders and patrons. Bbq joint, in and outdoor seating.  Music some early evenings. Some art works dot the area. Fun.

Wonderful house of white looking restaurant, but fell in love with the backyard bar area. Craft drinks out here with all the ingredients. With all that, I was totally happy w/ vodka orange fresh squeeze. Gotta be healthy right?!

Friendly bartenders. They serve food outside, too.

On this magnificent Reno day, we drove up, got outside seating, enjoyed the leaves falling, liked that patrons were not drunk and loud, nor boring and quiet,....liked the varied alcohol selection, the great service, large water glasses, how the staff worked well together, how clean and organized in and out of the restaurant was, clean large restrooms, bar area and.....of course the food.

A wide variety of dishes to choose. We got the breakfast and lunch dishes to choose from. I actually had difficulty choosing as so many plates popped out.

We got the chorizo Diablo patty with white gravy,  yep that would be me, diablo! It came with perfect eggs and crispity big thin cut hashbrowns. Gravy had beautiful dots of sliced meat chunks. Graveee.

The kale omelet was filled with a lot of spiced hamburger bits (not heat jalapeno hot) and kale. Nice and mild. He ate it all.

What a burping delicious 6 years for me visiting this location. Time sure flew but improvements are noted.

20 beer taps and a wonderful variety of styles. Also, a bunch of large specialty bottles, cans and ciders.

Parking in their lot and street. They expanded their seating back left and they also have outdoor seating.

Very generous with their "tastings"! Mahalo!

Super friendly staff and easy to get into. They take CC but got a luscious Bav cream maple doughnut and a coffee for $2 special! Gave a tip.

In and outdoor seating. They have a drive-thru though a lot of people just pop right in.

Judging from my one doughnut, the dough was rich and substantial, filling. Not painfully sweet or mouth drying.  Not those super light dissolving ones. I know I'm eating a doughnut! Liked it a lot.

I'm really appreciating this diner that never closes. Dependable, variety of dishes and tasty.

#1 fave is the all you can eat soup and salad buffet. It's also served with a choice of warm bread, too

#2 Asian dishes are great!

#3 Quinoa pancakes were so good. Crispy and luscious. It's served with 2 eggs and 2 sausages/bacon. Butter and warm syrup, yumso.

There is also diner seating. Usually quick service and food delivery. Bring check up to cashier. Like the waterfall sounds, too.

This is NOT your typical Mexican restaurant.

No complimentary chips & salsa, nachos, large menu selections, or platters with rice and beans.

BUT, the appetizers, soft and crispy/toasted tacos & ceviche are heavy and flavorful. What they have is super good and filling. Tacos are their specialty. Not the taco bell/del taco style.

I need to emphasize that if you like avocados, get the guacamole dip. It's almost pure avocado snowed with a thick layer of unmelted Mexican white cheese.  

They serve a variety of drinks and margaritas. Mexican beer, of course. Friendly service. Indoor seating.

It's where Fin & Fillet used to be.

A short notch below fine dining with fine dining level of food!

KALEOB was a great server answering our questions and giving us welcomed opinions. He even split the plates for us which was a wonderful surprise!

I got the prime rib sandwich that was stuffed with a ton of meat and tucked into a sturdy toasted white bun/roll. It also includes a side salad choice! I felt like I had a prime rib dinner, minus all the cutting and chewing needed with the usual slab of ribs meat. I know, but being able to continually stuff my mouth with all that wonderful slivered slices was easy.

There is a bar area with bar top games and a tv.

To the right, is a Biscotti coffee, gelato and dessert stop.

Blown away by the price and fun to be eaten here. Got the outrageous fiery Cheetos taco tots bowl. Its oval tots topped with taco meat, cheese, jalapenos and those red Cheetos. But wait! There is a salsa bar with mild, med, hot sauces and pico de gallo with cilantro. No sauce packets here! Now I'm in mouth warming nose running heaven.

Mr Bland got the beef taco's that were topped with cheese and shredded lettuce. He said it was like Del Taco, but spicier. I thought the taco beef tasted like a spicier Schilling type spice mix with chunkier beef filling. He was sweating. I was squirming with delight.

Easy parking, clean indoor seating and bathroom. Very friendly workers. Loved it.

As of 8/12/20, everything on the menu is $2 more as notification taped across front of menu. Just wanted to inform you.

So it's a smaller family restaurant with their own style and flavors. That's what separated a lot of similar dish serving restaurants.

I got the Tom Yum soup. Lots of chicken and shrimp pieces. Extra basil, jalapenos, lime and bean sprouts come with it. Caution**This soup was nose running happiness for me with the pre-added jalapenos. Tell them if you DON'T want it that hot. Perfect for me.

Mr Bland had the flavorful thinly shaved beef pho. He enjoyed it.

When we exited, I peeked by the kitchen and the cooks waved good bye. So awesome.

Did I see the Liberty Bell on my first ever Philly trip? Barely.

Independence Hall? Ummmm, no.

Have the raved Philly Cheesesteak? No.

Hear naked and chocolate in the same sentence and drop everything to find a place where they coexist? YES!

Nothing naked here (maybe a good thing, can't say the place was radiating with hotness from too many people...). Chocolate in abundance though--- from chocolate Easter bunnies and croissants, to fondue and enormous basins of hot chocolate. 

And those single little chocolates (those darn little buggers wouldn't stop jumping in my mouth!)...  were perfect with my plain black coffee- which I'm glad I had ordered to balance out the sweet sweet sweeetness.

Cool new addition to the Warehouse District! I will def. return. 

Came here after the Saints game with the family and was quite impressed. This place reminds me of a less rustic Tchoup Yard, with food. 

Our server Paula, was fun, upbeat, and had some really great recommendations for food and drink, as they have just opened in the last week. The servers and their managers are very attentive, which is a breath of fresh air. She recommended the nachos and the Hawaiian Shish Kabobs, which we got and they were both very good. They also have a few specialty drinks, that are good too. I'd recommend the Bushwacker if you want something frozen or the Streetcar if you want something a bit stronger.
What a great place for Lunch.  The food is really great.  Many different types of seasoning sauces.  Many traditional dishes from India.

I was famished. We were desperate. They were near enough that I didn't have to gnaw off any appendages (don't be dirty) to soothe the hunger pangs. 

Simple sentence structure style for now. Too busy dreaming of more Adriana's to stress the mind.

It was a gamble. It was kind of a dive. They had very few veggie options that looked like they would satisfy. We were already there, and like I said, I was ready to gnaw the crap out of something, anything really. 

My partner and I split a veggie pizza and the Sunny's Veggie sub. 

Synopsis. 

The pizza cheese was somewhat strange, but good in a way I can't describe. I could've eaten 2 myself. 

The sub, made with hot garlic bread and topped with mozzarella and parmesan cheeses, lettuce, tomato, onion, green pepper, artichoke hearts, and pesto dressing, was giant. We were regretting ordering both a little pizza and the sub since the sub looked like more than enough for 2 people... until we tried it. It was the single most delicious hot veggie sub I have ever eaten in my entire life. I could've eaten 3 of them myself... if they weren't so messy and the oil dripping out didn't make me feel like such gross-o glutton. I would drive back to St. Louis just for this sub. If you like Italian subs the way your momma used to make 'em, this is THE place for you. 

Service was friendly and appeared to be family owned and operated, less the community college kids that help in back- who were also sweet peaches. They're open 6 days a week, but only for 4.5 hours each day- so get 'em while you can. I recommend a stop in there before or after your botanical gardens visit since it's so close by. 

If I had to pick something to gripe about, it'd be the teeny tiny water cups (not conducive to eating salty Italian subs and pizza) and the lack of napkins given. That sub might have been the messiest non-sloppy joe sandwich I've ever eaten and anything short of a beach towel was defo not going to tide me over. I basically took a shower in their sink when I was done and still felt oil & vinegar-y... but it was worth it times a trillion. 

For sure, one of my top 5 picks for St. Louis eats.

I can't be 100% certain, but I'm about 97.8% sure my server was Joseph Gordon Levitt's twin brother. 

I can live with that. 

I fell in love with 3 Sisters the moment I pulled up to this Broad Ripple estate. I was seated right-quick, and immediately ordered up a coffee. It was delicious, by the way. 

The menu was chock full of vegetarian goodness and made it really hard for me to decide... especially since I'd eaten exactly nothing that day and it was nearing 7pm. I sat there and waffled over the menu for about a million years, then I had an 'aha moment' and thought, 'f*ck it!' I'm an adult, sandwiches are like $7... I'll just everything. And so I did. 

I started with the vegan sloppy joe. I think it was based with lentils and smothered in vinegar, my second favorite food group. It was a lot like chili in how hearty and filling it was. I could only eat a quarter of it before I moved on to the pretty huge side it came with, which actually was chili. Vegan chili. It was dang good... I would have loved a little cheese or sour cream in there, but of course that would defeat the vegan. 

My second sandwich was the 3 sisters sandwich with apples and brie and again, it was absolutely divine. And for a side I got the coleslaw because I knew someone back at my house would probably enjoy it, though I'm not really a big of coleslaw in general. 

For my third sandwich (See, I told you I got everything), I got their grilled cheese with avocado and some other goodies in it. I think the official name of the sandwich was 'The Kevin', or some other kind of boys name like that. Again, another hit. It didn't have as much avocado as I imagined it to have, but the bread was perfect and I'm not normally the kind of person who cares for bread at all, just gets in the way IMO. And for side I got a thing of their house soup which was some kind of heavenly and seasonal apple soup.

For dessert, (yep, I got dessert too) I got this like chocolate brownie lava pie something or other that was at least 40,000 calories and for the sake of my future and the hopes of living without diabetes, I probably shouldn't have, but I did and it was divine. No regrets, homie. 

My bill for endless coffee, three gourmet sandwiches, 3 huge sides, and a whopper of a dessert was under $35. Can't beat that. 

Without a doubt, I will come back every time I'm in or around the Indy area.

Let's play a game. 

It's called 'Pretty Pretty Popsicles'  and it's about to become your favorite past time. 

Alls ya gotta do is order up a bundle of Las Paletas Gourmet pops, then suck 'em down or eat 'em up (depending on if you opted for a cream or fruit based set of pops... or went rogue and got a bit of both, as we did) before they melt in their tiny single serving popsicle jackets. 

We basically came from Chicago to Nashville for these pops (well, sort of) and they didn't disappoint in the least, though I was really hoping they'd have the chai pops I'd heard so much about. My boo and I ended up getting the Spicy Hot Chocolate (cream), Avocado(cream), Hibiscus (fruit), and Coconut (cream). All were at least 11 times better than I could have ever imagined but the real stand out was Avocado. I don't know why they even continued making more flavors after they broke the mold with that one, but I guess I'm glad they did. 

After all, variety is the spice of life. Suck some down.

Definitely one of the best places to grab breakfast in Clearwater!!!

Breakfast out on the patio is beautiful on a nice day. My partner got the square deal meal which was a great breakfast that he was happy with (and they make the best potatoes around here!). I got the blueberry pancakes that were delicious. 

I would recommend Clear Sky for breakfast. They also serve lunch and dinner!!!

BE STILL MY HEART!!!
I missed the recent Supper Club visit to China Szechwan but thanks, Yelp, for introducing me to yet another gem. I have been here a few times in the past couple week AND IT JUST GETS BETTER!
 Best chow fun in town--and I know it, too: I'm canto, not mainland Chinese, so this saucy, wok-flavored dish is PERSONAL. Oh, and the crispy Cantonese noodles are nothing to laugh at, either. The szechuan menu is fantastic, featuring quite a few authentic dishes (salt fish clay pot anyone?). They don't overcook their veggies and the produce is pretty damn fresh. Nice portions. Two of my favorite dishes are ma po tofu and fish-fragrant eggplant... these guys nail it. Want something to drink? Try the home-made soy milk (a touch sweet for my tastes, but at least they're not cracking open an overpriced Yeo's).  
 If you're not that adventurous, the standard menu looks good and the lunch special is a killer deal. Talking to the owner, it seems they used to have another restaurant on the east side but have really enjoyed the move closer to campus, as it provides them opportunity (and audience) for more authentic dishes. 
 Lastly, I appreciate that they run a pretty clean ship. I used to say "nothing ruins a chinese meal more than a chinese restaurant bathroom," but this adage does not apply at China Szechwan...I can sum up my recommendation for this place by saying:
 GO HERE! NOW! 

p.s. if anyone ever orders the pork blood/bung/omasum/  I HAVE TO KNOW ABOUT IT! please yelp it!

First time visit to Metro....went with a friend for brunch on a Sunday. Place was understandably busy, and I was pleased that we still only waited about 15 minutes for a table. I decided to try the famous chicken and waffles. Beware, portions are huge! You get an entire 1/2 chicken and a full Belgian waffle. They serve the waffle with a delicious strawberry butter and the chicken with a unique syrup/hot sauce mix that I really liked. (And my son said it was just as good the next day! ) Our waitress was so friendly and accommodating. I couldn't get enough of the flavored coffee of the day, Jamaican Me Crazy, I must have had at least 4 cups! I've already decided on a second trip to Metro, and I'm pretty sure the shrimp and grits are next on my list to try.

The best doughnut ever! We found this doughnut store when we were visiting Nashville. After having these croissant-style doughnuts, I can't go back and waste my calories on the mediocre. We tried the 100 Layer: huckleberry, king kong, chocolate pumpkin cheesecake and a mini white chocolate mocha. Huckleberry seems to be popular as I saw lots of customers in front of us ordered this. It actually turned out to be my favorite of all.

The doughnuts tasted amazing with buttercream infused between the layers. The mini looked so cute but did not give the same experience as the full size. I know they are not cheap but definitely worth the money.

The building of this location has a very similar look and décor to the one I visited in Chicago a few year ago. I have had their famous items: Italian Beef and the polish hot dog. I like the Italian Beef more and you can ask for how dry/wet the sandwich to be prepared. The big beef is good size for 2 to share. I have heard their chocolate cake is really good but still haven't gotten to try it as I was full.

This place was very very good! The restaurant was very clean and the wait staff extremely friendly and knowledgeable. 

To start off they brought a small bowl of marinated peanuts. They were an interesting starter and we mixed some of the spicy sesame paste at the table with it, which really kicked it up a notch. 

They have a small selection of tempting appetizers. It was hard to choose just one but we settled on takoyaki because it is my husband's favorite. I have never had one before but I liked it. He has eaten a lot of it at other places and said it was extremely good. 

I ordered the vegetable la mian and my husband had tonkatsu ramen. First of all the portion sizes are huge the bowl was like three regular soup servings for me. I tried really hard to finish it because it was so good and because my husband insisted I could never eat so much at once but unfortunately he was right :( 
He had no trouble finishing his. 

After tasting both I believe the la mian to be superior in texture. I preferred my dish entirely; however my husband preferred his broth despite enjoying my la mian noodles more. 

Overall the entire experience was delicious and enjoyable, and in my opinion this is the best place to get ramen in the area. We will definitely return again... but next time I will probably not be quite so ambitious and just accept that I need a to go container for leftovers.

I'm not particularly needy in the vegetarian/vegan/raw food area but give me good ingredients & flavor and I'm happy.  Seed opened in early April and seems to be doing a nice business from the beginning: the space is understated & nice and the food is good, plus the location will end up being perfect.  There are a bunch of film industry folks working a block away that I'm confident will flock here for lunch.  And it's only a block from St. Charles Ave. so anybody can easily take the streetcar and walk down - or driving is also easy because there's typically plenty of parking in the neighborhood.  Did I mention they're open 7 days a week for lunch & dinner plus brunch on weekends?

You don't have to eat healthy - there's a fried tofu "nugget" appetizer in addition to gumbo, chili "cheese" fries and even a couple po-boys (fried eggplant and fried tofu I believe) as well as a bread pudding dessert that's awesome.  That being said, everything in house is vegan and there are a ton of healthy options on the menu such as virtually any salad you want and tons of unique menu items that are both "raw" and cooked.  "Noodles" made from vegetables for Pad Thai or spaghetti dishes?  Nice.  Kale & Mango Salad?  Wow!  Eggplant Po-Boy?  The eggplant is sliced a bit thin for my preference but they use Leidenheimer bread and include a great sauce and the flavors are excellent.  Most everything on the menu appears very well done.

It's a large food menu, and they've got a full liquor license set up from opening so you can have a good cocktail or a tasty glass of wine with your meal (the wines are limited but solid).  For some reason you always have to ask for the wine & cocktail list but at least they have one.  As for pricing, it's a bit high for the food - and especially for their juices of all things - but they certainly have more overhead to cover than a neighborhood dive so I'm okay with it and decent crowds suggest a good number of others are too.

For those living or working in the neighborhood it will be easy to end up at Seed once or twice a month - and that's for people who aren't even vegetarian.  For those who abide by vegan or raw dietary rules it may be more often - I've seen a number of vegan/raw restaurants in Chicago and Portland when living there, and Seed compares to just about anything I've run across.  Bravo!

Came here for dessert on cold night, just looking for something sweet. I walked in, and I felt like I had stepped into a European cafe, it was delightful. The service was great and fast. We ordered a tiramisu, which was super soaked in strong espresso... a crepe brûlée that had an orange taste to it (I prefer the classic vanilla bean)...and a cannoli which was just okay. 
I want to come back one day and try their gelato because I've heard it fantastic! 
But this place is definitely a cute, cozy destination that the city needed.

Made reservations yet still had to wait to be seated. Ppl ahead of me got in first though they were just off the street

Became worried when I was finally seated but didn't see a server for over 15 minutes. I was ready to walk out when she finally came. 

This place is cool, the menu is varied from Poke bowls to typical pub delights 

Pricey but expected in this touristy area

Too much something here for my comfort and joy... rules? attitude? righteousness? Not sure but it starts with the policy and fudged-up logic about refusing to fill anyone else's growler (I can hear someone from Tired Hands arguing this point as this is being read). It continues through to the food delivery from the runner that doesn't include the question before disappearing: "Is there anything else I can get you?" ...and goes on even more with the "flights are not available" statement on their postcards. This last one is pure, unexplainable, nuts. Although Fermentaria sells a 4oz. tasting glass, they INSTRUCT you to order it 1 at a time. Seriously?  I'm going to wait for the waitress to return to order my next 4 oz. sample? And then do it again, 4 more times?? Our waitress came to our table about as often as trains run on the Septa regional rails. For this reason alone I would not come back. AND I DIDN'T EVEN WANT A FLIGHT tonight! 

Fortunately (or unfortunately), the food would keep me from coming back too.

So how was that food and beer? I had 2 very good beers (Pineal, Baltic Splendor) and 1 not so good beer (Saison). The saison had an up-front sourness that I was not expecting from the description. I am not arguing whether it's a proper saison or not - because God knows, there is someone from Tired Hands reading this that will want to argue the point. Let me also say that I love saisons and I also enjoy sour brews too - but generally not in a saison, and certainly NOT when the description, which goes into such detail, fails to highlight or include it... "lemon zest, pear, barnyard, hay, guava, juicy fruit and earth". And if someone thinks lemon zest = sour, think again. Lemon is sour but lemon zest is a lovely, etherial aromatic that should play off the other notes.

So what about food?  Tacos we had were just OK: decent but overpriced (2 for $11). More problematic were the corn tortillas that the taco filling sat on. They were apparently not warmed on the grill first. Warming a tortilla brings up the toasty flavor and tightens them up. When this is not done and they come right out of the bag to the plate, they usually, eventually fall apart as they moisten up -- as these did. Burger was priced fairly but was NOT good - overdone and on a wimpy bun that disintegrated before my last bite. It was one of those burgers that kept reminding me over the next 5 hours that I ate it.

Cheffy food out of a Styrofoam container? Don't knock it til you've tried it! Heard Dat is one of dozens of hole-in-the-wall kitchens you find in the, shall we say, not-so-touristy neighborhoods all over New Orleans. But behind this order window (and right now there's not much more) is some SERIOUS southern cookin' goin' on!

Yelper reviews and the guy in line ahead of me had me thinking hard about ordering the Superdome, but it sounded like way more food than I needed for lunch. A friend at home who's from New Orleans had tasked me with eating shrimp & grits for her, so on this day, I obliged. GURRRL, I told her, here dey are! I'd never had corn in S&G, but it works! The grits are creamy and the shrimp are bathed in delicious sauce. When I got home I put a little bit of salt on it, but otherwise they're perfect!

The girls behind the counter are sweet and patient with first-timers. Right now the place consists of only an inside order window and a few tables on the sidewalk outside; a sign said they're working on an indoor seating area. I took a seat outside to wait, and the girls kept me posted on my order; it took awhile, but DAMN, it was worth it. I'll come back hungrier next time for that Superdome, some Crawdat Fries, and with a friend to help me eat it all!

I have only been here for brunch once so I can only speak to that. (But I cannot wait to go back!) First off, for brunch they have a $25 all you can drink mimosa special! Simply amazing! The mimosas were the perfect mix of champagne and orange juice ( not too heavy on the juice). Our waitress was so attentive and kept them coming! It was totally worth the price if you're looking for a boozy brunch. Others at the table had bloody marys and said they were great! (although no special on those).

I had an omelet. It was very large and delicious! Apparently the thing is the hot chicken sandwich! I was in the mood for eggs, but next time I need to try this sandwich. Everyone loved it! The service was great! We had a large party of about 10 and they put us in the back at a long table.

We've been to Varga a few times to grab drinks, but this time we decided to order from their ever-rotating food menu. Food is a craft here, and everything they do, they do it well. The wall is decorated with pretty pin-up girls, one in particular that I really like. ;)

Needless to say, they have a great craft beer menu that even features a lot of local brewers (we decided which brewery we'd like to visit next after our drinks this evening!) We ordered a Hefeweizen and tropical IPA that were both so good, we ordered them twice and switched beers! There is a great variety of beers on the menu too, so there's certainly something for everyone.

I ordered the mac and cheese, because once I saw their instagram post with the photo, I knew I had to come in just to try it. It was so tasty, in that little cast iron pan! The portion size doesn't  look that big, but it was actually just the perfect amount. My fiancé really enjoyed the popcorn chicken as well. Service is always just right too. We'll be back again for sure.

Stopped by for dinner on a Friday evening and we were seated right away and I immediately started noting the intricately painted chairs and tables in this place, there's certainly a lot to look at while you're sitting and waiting. The lighting is relatively dim and calming, unless you're seated in the front during the daytime.

We were brought our waters and complementary chips and salsa pretty quickly. The chips tasted fresh and warm, while the salsa was cool with a tiny bit of heat and some flavor, which was great by my standards. When I was ready to order some beers and get a refill on the salsa, the waitress was nowhere to be found- well I think I found her, but she was hanging out with the hostess at the front desk, I believe. She just about stayed there until she darted past us to get to the kitchen and then bring our meals out... so I never did order those beers. But, I think this place would honestly do better as a BYOB. Their beer selection is nothing impressive.

I ordered the enchiladas verdes with the refried beans and Spanish rice, but I had the enchiladas made vegetarian with only cheese (no chicken). The rice was as expected, but the refried beans were more flavorful than I'm used to, which I enjoyed. The enchiladas were delicious, but afterwards, I still felt a little hungry. My boyfriend really enjoyed his Quesadilla Mexicana, which came with a side of rice.

Overall, great food at an interesting place tucked away in the shopping center. Food came fast, but we didn't get checked on enough to get the chance to order anything other than water. Normally, I'd say that we'd return again, but there's so much good Mexican in the area that it's hard to say for sure.

We stopped in on a Saturday evening after coming to KOP to go to a different Mexican joint that we'd just discovered had closed. The place looks pretty dimly lit, but somehow the tables are situated under the lights, providing plenty of lighting for dining. After being seated, we were brought complementary chips and salsa, which was actually pretty good.

I ordered three of the cheese enchiladas, which came with Mexican rice and refried beans. I received only two enchiladas, and just decided to call that third enchilada a loss because I didn't really want to wait any longer. I did mention their mistake, and asked them to make sure the bill reflected what I'd received, instead of what I asked for. I also asked for jalapeños with the enchiladas, which I thought they'd forgotten but it turned that the jalapeños were inside the enchiladas- but I was glad that I had more jalapeños to put on top of them because the chili sauce was very bland. The cheese was sharp, which made them taste very cheesy, but the sauce tasted like close to nothing. The refried beans were also a bit bland, but the Mexican rice was okay.

My boyfriend, however, found his Mahi Mahi tacos to be very flavorful- and they certainly looked it with a nice presentation that had a beautiful array of colors.

Our service was actually pretty slow. A little bit after we ordered, we heard a huge crash in the kitchen, which could have been our waitress and also potentially our dishes- as we didn't see her for quite a while after the loud crash.

Overall, I wouldn't be opposed to coming here again, but I wouldn't travel all the way out to KOP for it.

Stopped in during the halftime show at the Super Bowl to catch some of the game and grab a few beers. The place was just packed enough that every bar seat was taken, and all of the tables were available. It was mostly filled with what felt like people who all went to a local high school together, many of which were quite loud.

There are a good number of TVs, and a great craft beer selection. You have to go up to the bar to order if you're seated at a table. There's also a back porch, though it reeks of cigarette smoke to the point that I have to hold my breath to walk through it. Also, strangely, this place is in a dead zone (at least as far as Verizon service goes). It's somewhat dimly lit, though, which I appreciate.

The food menu is mostly bar bites and sandwiches. I don't know if I'd come here for dinner, but I'll be back to try the food sometime soon. The beer was ice cold and the service wasn't bad. There's a room with pool tables in the back, though they were empty at this time. I'd come back again if nothing else but that extensive beer list!!

He was on a mission for some Pho, so we decided on Pho and More. It was a Monday evening, and there wasn't any wait to be seated- plus, the place was just about empty. I ordered noodles with tofu, and a side of steamed rice, and my boyfriend went with the Pho. We started off with veggie spring rolls, which were actually really tasty, and served with a sauce that is both spicy and sweet.

It wasn't too long for our food to be brought out, but when he put my plate in front of me, we'd all realized at once that he'd given me chicken instead of tofu. Luckily, it wasn't too long of a wait until the correct order was brought out. When he came by to check, I asked if my steamed rice was on its way-- good thing I'd asked, because he'd apparently forgotten. The food was pretty good. Nothing special. The Pho was a great portion.

I'd also recommend you wear a jacket-- I was pretty cold in here wearing a T-shirt. Overall, they'll settle the craving if you have it, but nothing too impressive.

Stopped in on a Saturday evening just after 7pm, and we were surprised to see that there was no wait and that they were not very crowded. We self-seated ourselves and were brought our menus and waters very quickly, and we also sipped on some of the beer we brought since it's BYOB here.

The complementary chips and salsa were very yummy, and the chips came topped with a little refried beans and cheese. We added some of the table hot sauce to the salsa to turn up the heat a bit and they were super tasty!

I ordered the enchiladas with red sauce, and asked for no meat, lettuce, or sour cream. I did ask for a side of rice and beans (not included, unfortunately) and some jalapeños to put on top of the enchiladas. The rice and beans were standard, and the enchiladas were very good. I've eaten at enough authentic Mexican places to know that the cheese they use is more mild than ours, and the enchilada sauce flavor is a bit different. Although I don't prefer it all of the time to the Americanized flavors, I can appreciate it and enjoy it for sure. My fiancé ordered the beef burrito, which he says he enjoyed, although he did leave a little bit hungry still.

I'll give Juanita's the full five stars because everything came quickly, exactly as ordered, hot and tasty. I wouldn't go out of my way to come back, most likely, but I'd definitely stop by if in the area!

Stopped by as I'd never been before, but I was in the area for a work event. I didn't have too much time and they were pretty busy on this Saturday early afternoon, but we were seated immediately and in and out relatively timely.

Of course I had to try one of the handmade shakes. I was going to try the plain chocolate, but there were a few others that caught my eye. I decided on the Death by Chocolate, which was chocolate ice cream and fudge mixed with chocolate chips. It came in a big metal cup- the only appropriate way for a specialty milkshake to be served. It tasted chocolatey and rich for sure! My only complaint was that they should have used thicker milkshake straws. These ones would not hold up with the chocolate chips, which kept getting stuck in them and clogging the straw, so I had to keep declogging the straw.

I also ordered the spicy fries, which I was pleased to discover come with plenty of spices, and not any strange kind of sauce mixtures. They were very light on the heat but heavy on the flavor, and were fresh and enjoyable. I'd certainly try this place again sometime.

Stopped by after local shopping during the playoffs to grab a bite and catch some of the game. They sort of look closed from the outside, at least during the day. But once you open the door, the delicious smell is very welcoming.

First things first: no complementary chips and salsa here. This is a little bit of a pet peeve of mine. You can order them, and there's a pretty big selection of salsas to choose from- although, only one of them was labeled as hot. The hot one was pineapple and habaneros, so we had to try it. Initially, it's too sweet- like, pineapple overload, and then the heat comes a moment later. Great heat, overly sweet, and I wish some of the heat came with the first bite to tone down the sweetness. I think next time I'll try sticking to a tomato-based salsa, and adding some hot sauce for heat (the table was set with 3 hot sauces to choose from).

I ordered cheese enchiladas with jalapeños (strangely they had habaneros for the salsa but couldn't add them to my dish). It came with black beans and Mexican rice, which were average. It also came with some salsa, which was good, and lettuce (which I asked them to leave out but they included anyway). The enchilada is tasty though, and actually comes lasagna style. The menu says you can choose from a red or green sauce- I asked if I could have both on the side so that I could try each of them. However, I suppose the waitress forgot, and decided to serve my enchiladas with what I believed was the red sauce, but it could have been a mixture of the two. It was great though, whatever it was- and certainly cheesy.

Great place for brews though! Good craft beer selection, and also it seems that they feature a brewery every so often. At our visit, it was Dogfishhead. For the featured brewery, a beer was $5 and some change for what I believe was a 22 oz!

Overall, service was pretty good and prices were only a tiny bit higher than your average Tex Mex restaurant chain. I look forward to returning!

One of the best dinners you can have in NOLA. Honestly I don't know where else you'd even find arepas in the city. 

But first. The margaritas. They're huge! And you have a choice of whatever fresh fruit they have that day. LOVE those margaritas. 

The appetizers/starters are all fantastic but I cant seem to pass up the shrimp ceviche served with plantain chips. 

All the arepas are delicious. It's impossible to pick a favorite. Very filling. 

It always takes a while for the arepas to be made so be prepared for a long meal. This is no fast food joint.

Good times will be had at Prohibition Taproom. Come here one night during the weekend and take a set at the bar. Get a drink (There are some good beers on tap). Maybe order some food (Veggie Tip: Vegetarians and veggie friendly peeps have some solid options here). Then just take in the atmosphere and enjoy. 

Prohibition Taproom is a close-second to my favorite bar restaurant in Philly (which, in case you are interested, is Khyber Pass). I would recommend it, hands down.

So this afternoon, my partner and I tried TBBC in Ybor City spontaneously. I'm glad we did because Tampa Bay Brewing Company was one of the highlights of our time in Florida. Tampa Bay Brewing Company is a fantastic gastropub! Great beers on tap, food from the kitchen, friendly vibe, and music spilling out of the speakers. It's a guaranteed good time! 

Anyway, here's the gist. Below is what we ordered and what we would recommend you try - 

FOOD: 
- Shrimp Tacos - Delicious, fresh, and flavorful. The guac on the side is also tasty.
- True Blonde Hummus Dip - Freshly made hummus that comes with pita points and veggies
- Brew House Pretzels - One of the best soft pretzels I've had at a gastropub. They have a very good pretzel bread recipe, plus you get two pretzels (lots of places I've been to just give you one). 

DRINKS:
- ABC APA (limited)
- Eggnog Lager (seasonal)
- Florida's True Blonde Ale (my favorite! a TBBC core beer, so it should always be there)
- Wild Warthog Hefeweizen (another core)
- Grand Cru Belgian Amber & Dark Strong Ale Blend
- McBrews Scotch Ale

One last thing, all of the staff were super friendly. Our waitress Melissa was really cool and funny, and she always checked in with us to see if all was good with our food and drinks. TBBC takes care of its customers, and it feels like they genuinely care and want to make sure you're happy with everything... I'm a TBBC fan! I hope to visit their other Westchase location as well.

This place is truly a farce. It is not organic (the owner said only the
lettuce is and the chicken is  and he cannot afford to buy organic).
His fruit is loaded with pesticides and his food is not really the
best quality though it might taste good. He also advertises this
place as healthy food but we know it is not. His smoothies also
have no taste not to mention the chemicals in it. His salad 
dressings are Kraft which is loaded with high fructose corn
syrup and MSG. Does all this food sound healthy? You be the
judge. I don"t think so.!

I was casually eating when an obvious autist walked in waving his arms and sticking out his tongue. The manager stormed in with his boys, waving guns and said "you're dead moose meat" and proceeded to destroy the poor mans equipment and started a ruckus. The chicken was good tho.

We came here on a recommendation from a friend.  I immediately knew I was going to like the place based on looks alone, lol.  I know, sounds superficial but it really had a cool feel to it and lots of cool decor, like a wall covered in cigar boxes!  

We were seated and greeted promptly by a very friendly waitress.  Smile on her face and just the right amount of attention to our needs.  Along with a food runner, we were well taken care of.  

Excellent beer selection and lots to choose from.  They also offer "Limited Time Only" brews, so hop (no pun intended...or was it?) on those fast because they don't last long.  (great to see them helping out local breweries like Round Guys too!).  

We started out with Fried Pickles and they were perfect.  Lots of pickle flavor and just enough breading.  Served with their super awesome white cheddar/asiago cheese sauce.  

My girl had the bruschetta chicken and I started out easy with the Great White Sharp burger.  Cooked perfectly, lots of cheese sauce, fresh bun and fresh cut fries.  Excellent flavor on everything.  

This place is truly running on all cylinders, they turn tables quickly which keeps business consistent and flowing, they serve you with a smile and they fill you up with great beer and food.  Highly, highly recommend this place.  It's dangerous because it's addictive.  I can't wait to go back and bring others with me!

Here for a soft opening.  Ordered the blue crab gratin ($12) the hand cut steak tar tar ($12) and the gnocchi ($18).  All excellent.  The crab was creamy and spicy. The tar tar was served with warm dollops of slow cooked egg yolk.  Exquisite! The gnocchi is served with a lamb ragu and goat cheese.  The creamy goat cheese plays well off the the lamb ragu, and the gnocchi have a lovely soft center. Entree sizes were perfect. I was left wanting more without feeling sick and over fed. 

I sampled the #1 cocktail, a combination of bourbon, pineapple cordial, byrrh, lime, mint and sage. Refreshing!  A total of six cocktails adorn the menu and bar top. 

The space is warm and intimate. White subway tile lines the wall behind the bar. Blue banquettes line one side of the dining space right up to a modern glass fronted wine cellar. Family photos and large mirrors line the walls leading to a bright open air kitchen.

Power outlets, USB ports and purse hooks are hidden underneath the bar.

Another fabulous find for our bookclub forays =)

I almost completely walked by the cafe huddled under my umbrella last night, tucked into a quiet corner shop in the midst of the neon and noise of the Italian market. Inside is a little bit of a mix of your grandmom's living room and attic. The couches are well worn in, the fireplace was sadly fake, and if you're ever not sure which country the owner's from just look on the ceiling. The bathroom is also a must see, with a kind of red light, boudoir feel.

I got the Dirty Volcano to start off with, and enjoyed Rene's finesse while mixing the drink as much as drinking it when he was done. I particularly loved the 7 or 8 (I lost count) types of chocolate that he shaved over top of it. It was so rich it really could have been enough, but my arm was easily twisted with the allure of a free second round, and tried the Killerrr. Molten chocolate in a martini glass, the flavor reminded me a little of a Kandy Kake, and I'm not complaining.

YUMmy

Everything we've tried here so far has been delish; my favorite so far is the vegetable samosa (nicely cunchy, not greasy, and a tad spicy), and the chicken saag (most flavorful I've had, and this is my go to dish for indian food). They have a nice size menu, and prices are in line with most places around, which may be a little high, but the portions are really big. Good to share an entree for two, or have enough for lunch the next day. The guys that work here are super nice, happy to explain what any mystery sauces are, and we've gotten complimentary rice pudding with the bill.

*We just got delivery from them the other week: they delivered down to GHo, quickly enough that the dishes and naan were still hot.

One of the few things I miss about my native Pennsylvania is the plethora of small but really good Italian restaurants. Seems like when I was growing up they were ubiquitous and you could find a great pizza place or sub shop on almost every street corner. Now that I live in Maryland I can't get a good slice of pie or a decent cheesesteak not to mention a stromboli. So whenever I head back to my roots I'm sure to check out a place like bacco bistro.

Located on the northern edge of Doylestown in a strip mall, the bistro  doesn't really stand out from its surrounding businesses. Inside there are probably 20 tables but there's plenty of space and you won't feel cramped. Every time I've been there the service was top-notch. They also always start you out with some complimentary garlic bread which is wonderful, crunchy on the outside soft on the inside and drenched in garlic butter.

Today we tried the eggplant pomodoro, the homemade chicken soup and the cheese steak. All of it was very good. I think the cheesesteak rolls might have been made in house. Although the cheese steak was excellent the one minor flaw was that the cheese to meat ratio was a little bit off and you could taste a little bit more cheese than steak. In a perfect cheesesteak, the marriage of meat and cheese should be undetectable and just result in pure heaven. This cheesesteak was good though, and I would certainly eat another!  Prices were certainly reasonable for the quality of the food and everything came out quickly. If you're in the area give it a try, you won't be disappointed.

Sometimes when I read bad reviews on yelp, I assume the person is a crappy customer. I almost always think 'That person was probably just being an ass'. I wish so badly that Bareburger hadn't disappointed me over and over and over and over (you get the point)...

The biggest problem- Orders for pickup and delivery are ALWAYS wrong. This is not an exaggeration. On more than 6 occasions consecutively, they have either given wrong orders or food has been completely missing. On other occasions they'll call and tell us they are out of something, offer to sub it, then the order is still wrong. My boyfriend and I have, more than once, made bets that go like this. "How long before they call and tell us they're out of (insert desired order)", or "What's the over-under on our sides being missing?"
We've complained, politely, we've given them chance after chance because we love the food. But we can't anymore. Their promises that it won't happen again and their offers to reimburse aren't worth the frustration of half a meal being missing or wrong. Tonight's missing slaw was the last slaw straw.

Other problems- "Business hours" seems to be a loose term. They will stop seating, stop serving, or down right be closed before their posted hours. I have no idea how to determine the rhyme or reason for this. This type of willy-nilly schedule must be a luxury...I wonder if they're hiring...
-Service is questionable. I understand working in food service, I've been there. And I'll be the first to admit that people are the worst (some people take to the internet to rant about food...). But faking enthusiasm is a must if you are truly miserable and work at a restaurant. The people working at Bareburger are somehow able to make you feel like YOU have kicked a puppy in front of children when all you did was ask a friendly question. The DMV would be proud.

The food is great...when it shows up. Sadly I've missed out on tasting most of it. I won't be trying again.

Ooooo boy do I love this place! One of the best spots in Saint Louis for an amazing vegan menu. 

Each time I have come, I've had great service. Prompt, friendly, and inclusive folks running this place. Shout out to Victoria, one of the managers, is super rad. 

I'm on a kick of getting their Buffalo Bleu Burger. It's completely vegan. It's the most delicious black bean burger with buffalo sauce that has the perfect amount of kick. It's drenched in their house-made vegan bleu "cheese" sauce and comes with fresh greens and red onions. Last time I was there I also tried their tots, which were awesome!

On nice days their patio is such a beautiful and relaxing place to be with Grand liveliness all around. 

I'm excited to try their new upstairs bar that recently opened. This place is all around great and is putting Saint Louis on the map when it comes to vegan friendly restaurants.

Sasha's on Shaw has been killing it. I had a couple really dope experiences here recently and it's turned me back into a regular. 

Tonight we got a salmon plate and shared a bottle of the Annabelle. Both were perfect, per usual. The weather was perfect, music soft, vibe... just right. 

They're really running a tight ship with COVID circumstances and it's really appreciated. 

Thanks for all you guys are doing and for being open!

Went on a run downtown today and popped into Park Avenue after realizing it was open! 

Ordered some gooey butter cake, an iced americano and a mango smoothie. All were perfect. He forgot I ordered the cake for a moment, and after reminding him we were out the door. It was super efficient. Staff was being cognizant of distancing. All seating areas were closed. 

Once I sat down to eat my gooey butter cake, I realized he included two slices, I'm assuming because I had to wait for an extra moment. 

Great experience, I'll be back! Glad you can get good coffee downtown right now! I surely needed it!

First time is the charm. Holy smokes. I've heard St. Louisans talk about this place for a while now, and I finally found the perfect opportunity to check it out. My best friend in town, in the spirit to try something new, and no where to be on a Saturday afternoon. The perfect storm to try Mac's.

We arrived around 2pm, and there was still a substantial line. It seems like the lunch rush doesn't end. While we were waiting, we decided on out order and were chatting, but noticed everyone was grabbing Busch beers out of a bucket on the bar counter. We discovered that on busy afternoons the kitchen buys beer for the folks who have to wait. Game-changer! When we were in line, we were talking about how long it seemed like it was taking. Once we got to the counter, the guy who took our order gave us so much undivided time and attention for any question we had and explained their concept. It gave me a totally different perspective on the line. It is a part of the experience and I loved that. 

Julia R got the double Pimento burger, which she raved about how it was piping hot with gooey cheese. My buddy got the vegi burger, she has been a vegetarian for years and said it was the best one she has ever had. For me, since it was my first time trying Mac's I went with the Classic. It had two patties. They are smashed, flat, 2 oz. patties, but two was perfect for me. From the bun, to the thinly shaved onions, to the absolutely delicious beef patties, I was literally in heaven. It is my new favorite burger in town. It's hearty, but manageable. All of the toppings stay on when you're eating it. It made me so happy. 

Free Busch that day, too? Steal my heart why don't ya?!

It is hard to overstate how amazing this restaurant is. Approachable and elegant. Not only do they deliver on the excellence they promise every time, but this place means a ton to me. Why you ask? This is where my wife and I got engaged! It is also where we celebrate so many things: anniversaries, dear friend's birthdays, etc...Come here when you're trying to treat someone, or hell, #treatyoself! 

Sometimes you help friends move and they buy pizza for everyone and sometimes they take you to Brasserie. That's why I came last night with some friends and holy smokes, it never disappoints...I'm telling ya! Hospitality is always on point. We had a reservation, so upon arriving, the very accommodating host seated us. We started off with some bubbly rosé while looking over the menu. We took full advantage of their carafe of house red wine, because #happyhour. It was plenty for three people to share ($15). Bonus: one of my friends doesn't drink, but they have mocktails, yay! 

We started off with the Fromage, their charcuterie plate. It was so satisfying. Also, the delicious cheese puffs. I have no idea how they get these so right, but oh my. Their food menu is French/American comfort food, but they do it in such a sophisticated way it's hard calling it that. We almost got every entree as a table, Julia had the trout. She's got a tiny stomach, but her plate was CLEAN. I had a bite, and can confirm that it was amazing. I got the chicken dish with shiitake mushrooms, another dish that knocked it out of the park. 

We finished with one of each of their desserts (all delicious), they were on the house because our entrees apparently took longer to prepare than they were supposed to? We didn't even notice from enjoying the vibes and each other's company. Side note: I'd like to say that *THIS* is the way it should be at every restaurant. They have their own hospitality goals, and when they are missed (regardless if the guest notices or is unhappy) they go above and beyond to make up for it. Beautiful. 

Thank you for the amazing evening, Brasserie. That's exactly why you are one of my favorite restaurants in Saint Louis!

Recently I stopped in on a Saturday evening for a friend's birthday gathering. Overall, I like their concept and the ciders themselves are good, if you like cider. It was a beautiful night and they had the large front doors open and it felt just right. It's great to have a local cider brewing company in Saint Louis, because so many people enjoy it. 

I tried the Rosé cider they had on draft and liked it a lot. It wasn't too sweet, which was something I am always afraid of with cider beer. One thing I really liked... they have other local beer options, even on draft, in case you don't want to drink cider. 

As far as my actual experience goes, not super impressed. There was one lady, our server who seemed to be doing all the work and had the entire dining area to herself. There were maybe 10+ tables in the restaurant, so our service was pretty slow, which was not her fault. There seemed to be two other folks, a bartender and a manger not really helping out when there were clearly things to do. I didn't get food, but I have heard really good things about it. Definitely will be enjoying some next time I'm in. 

As someone who doesn't drink a ton of cider, I don't know how often I will be back, but it's a nice place to spend some time with friends.

Oh Handle...

**Insert nostalgic memories from my mid-twenties**

This bike-themed bar is a really fun STL spot, especially if you have friends in town who want to paint the town. Every day of the week, they have awesome happy hour specials on all different kinds of drinks! Sunday Funday is a favorite of mine: $5 for a beer and a shot! 

There are many great reasons to come to HandleBar all year 'round. Spring, summer and fall are amazing on their really hip patio. Top Coat Sign Company, a local Saint Louis sign painting company, has adorned the entire inside of their patio fence with amazing murals of art and signage. On colder fall and winter nights, the patio can still be enjoyed because of their huge fire pit. On the winter Wednesdays they host an event called BikeBlitz, where people race stationary bikes and get free PBRs if they win. Thursday nights are always trivia, I have never been on a winning trivia team, but here's to hoping!

Twice a month they have a dance party called London Calling. The music is lit and the photo booths are always out of this world cool. Did I mention that they have an automatic bike pump if you're running low on air? For FREE! Bike on over to HandleBar for your next pool game or patio hang and check in on Yelp because they offer $1 off your first beer!

Went to Louie last night to celebrate my wife's birthday. It was utterly fantastic. This was our second time in, and an even better experience than our first.

Jordan was our server. Freaking character, man- in the best way! He was attentive, knowledgable, and hilarious. He brought us fresh bread while we decided on drinks and looked over the menu. My wife and I shared a bottle of the Nero D'Avola Zabu from Sicily. IT WAS SO DELICIOUS. Our friend ordered a glass of a red blend and said that was phenomenal as well. Off to a great start.

For starters, we ordered the brussels sprouts, which were crispy and perfectly seasoned with lemon, capers, and some delicious cheese. We also got the charred eggplant dip, and oh my gosh, this was so rich and creamy and there were ripe heirloom tomatoes on top and it was served with the freshest, warmest bread. Yum.

Finally, for the main course, my two friends and my wife ordered the sweet corn ravioli and were thoroughly pleased. The portion size was great and the uniqueness of flavors was phenomenal. I told Jordan to choose between two dishes because I couldn't decide - I ended up with the roasted chicken and it had me in my feels, ya know? We finished off the meal with the ice cream sandwich dessert - chocolate mousse if my wife's favorite and was the perfect ending to her birthday.

I highly recommend this place, from the atmosphere to the drinks to the diverse menu and amazing service, we'll keep coming back here for special occasions.

Tonight was my first time to Grbic. It's a little off the beaten path, so I'd never heard of it. If it weren't for Sarah coordinating a little ISC action, I don't know that I would've tried it. 

Tonight I started out with their house Pinot Noir. It was yummy and did the trick. Best part, it was only $6. 

Before our meals, Julia R and I shared the Grbic salad - it was a bed of chopped feta, tomatoes, and lettuce tossed in their house made Greek dressing. Refreshing and delicious. 

Chicken cordon blue and the chicken roulden were our meal choices and they were both great choices. Chicken was tender and all white meat. The skin was perfectly cooked. On the roulden, there was melted feta and spinach stuffing and in the cordon blue creamy cheeses and ham. They were both delicious. 

We were too full for dessert, but they had some tasty options I look forward to saving room for next time I'm in!

I think my experience was a little unique and I am willing to try them again, but I was totally disappointed. I've read a ton of reviews where folks describe there awesome experiences here, but unfortunately, mine last week was not as they described. 

It was almost 100 degrees outside the day I visited and I was really looking forward to getting inside for obvious reasons, but the AC was not working. They had a huge loud fan to try and compensate, but it was just blowing super hot taco-air everywhere. Maybe it's always empty on a Thursday at noon, but it also could have been because of the AC. Not surprisingly, the staff seemed to be having a difficult time, I would too! 

I got chicken tacos. Overall, they were pretty tasty. I wish the lettuce was crunchy and fresh, but it wasn't and the tacos didn't come with cheese. What's a taco without cheese? Next time I will have to remember that it is not included. My wife got a chicken and cheese quesadilla, which was thankfully better than my meal. I really want to like you guys, hopefully next time is a much better experience.

Where do I even start?!

Sardella is certainly in my top 3 favorite restaurants in Saint Louis. There brunch is unlike any other. Their food is so consistently delicious no matter what you get.

The most recently time I visited was on a Saturday afternoon. We started off with rosé mimosas and a donut while we looked over the menu. If you ask me, this is the only way to do brunch. 

My main in the morning here is usually always the eggs benedict ravioli. Listen, as long as you're good with a little egg yolk, there is nothing anyone couldn't love about this dish. The ravioli noodle is cooked perfectly, with rich ham and creamy hollandaise sauce. It's perfectly satisfying. 

If you have not been, go. If you have, go again!

This restaurant was the worst restaurant we have ever been to. Not only was the food extremely bland with no flavor but the owner(who I confronted) was extremely unprofessional and obviously doesn't care.

Really great spot! We were lucky to be able to get in with a quick reservation by calling this weekend (vday weekend) and it was pretty busy. They have great dining areas and we didn't feel too close to anyone. We started off with the Abbey fries ( has pork,cheese,onion rings on top of fries) DELICIOUS and just the right amount! For being as busy as they were the service and timing of the food was unbeatable! We couldn't believe how fast everything was coming out!

I got a rosies drink and a delicious cocktail that our waiter Michael had created with some Hendricks. I used to come here for their happy hours and they have a great beer and whiskey selection but since I was feeling a cute refreshing cocktail and that's what I got!

For the main entree, I got the woodland burger and my husband got the brisket sandwich. I really loved my woodland burger. It was cooked just right (medium) and  the bun was so warm and soft, it had a sweet fig Jam that really took this burger up a level! The brisket sandwich was okay, my husband said it had too much sauce which the flavor was overpowering.

In all we can't believe we have been missing out on the good food here! We will definitely come back to try other items! The price is okay for the food. The drinks however were a bit pricey FYI.

Updated: I cannot believe the owners response to this review. I can order whatever I would like to. It's on your menu so if you don't think it's adequate enough for someone to order, then don't serve it. That's not my problem. As other people have written, it's clear he takes no responsibility and doesn't want to keep a successful business going because this will not cut it. Good luck. The owner also deleted his response to this but luckily I have screen shots. 

I was hesitant to write this because of covid and the struggles that people and businesses are having. HOWEVER after reading the owner's response to other reviews and thinking about other restaurants who are actually contributing positively and putting out really tasty food, I had to. 

Super disappointing. Really poor quality, cold frozen fries and I'm sorry but if you can't properly cook a hard boiled egg and then turn around and charge me $10 for a half an egg and two bites of lettuce, it's not my jam.

As somebody who spends a ton of money on booze and food in and around the Music Row area - I can positively say I have never been more dissatisfied with service or been treated so rudely by anyone than I just was by the manager at The Row Nashville. I will never spend another dollar there (because they're going to take more than you ask them to, anyway).

First things first the place is way overpriced and the food is decent, but not great. There are several better priced restaurants, with better food, within walking distance of this place. 

Outside of that, I had a horrible experience with them this week. We went for a group happy hour - they told us what the specials were and it changed 47 times. Then halfway through our event (first drink was paid for by the organization on a ticket, and then we all opened tabs for our other drinks) they pull my friend aside because she said the event up and the manager said "Your group isn't f'ing (yeah, he said the f word) tipping!" and throws $6 at her. Well, nobody tipped yet, because we all still had tabs open. We had like 100 people there.

SO I call to just discuss with the manager - my opening line is - I know this is just a dollar and ordinarily I wouldn't call about it, but I wanted to make you aware that not only did your manager yell at my friend regarding tips (when, after it was all said and done, they were tipped graciously) - but I want you to be aware that people were being charged all willy nilly. He then decided to argue with me about what the drink specials were supposed to be, to which I asked him to explain why I had 2 different amounts charged if there was NEVER going to be a discounted sale on Abita. Instead of trying to explain that to me he cut me off rudely midsentence and said - "fine, what do I need to do to make you happy?" So I said - well, first I'd like for you to not be rude to me - and he said ma'am I work in customer service let's have a conversation like adults - and I told him I thought we were. Then I told him that I actually would like my dollar back now if he was going to treat me so rudely because it was on principle and he told me I would get it when I came back in and ordered food, he would take a dollar off my bill. I told him I didn't want to spend any more money there and he said well then I guess I cant help you.
