-cole slaw - disappointing, but comes with a lot

-clam chowder cup - HOLY MOLY. MY FIRST CLAM CHOWDER AND AM BLOWN AWAY. 10x better than santa barbara shellfish company down the street. comes with the oyster crackers and the flavor of the clam chowder is out of this world. PLUS with the free sourdough bread I dunked the crap out of it. MUST GET.

-fries - came with so much!!!!!! these were perfectly delicious and just banging. LOL get it!

PROS:
-SWEETEST server. 9/11/20 served us at 7:30pm on the upper deck. female with dark hair. she was so sweet and nice. even the other gentlemen working the deck were nice when we encountered them. JUST 10 STARS for the staff working the tables.
-free bread...
-best clam chowder
-beautiful view
-MADE US FEEL SO DAMN SAFE during covid. omg. I haven't really been dining into restaurants except this trip and they had a hand sanitizer bottle of GOOD hand sanitizer (not the bad smelly ones) sitting on the table and you could tell they were very clean and respective of our space and wearing masks.

CONS:
-seafood pasta is just a no for me
-staff at the front taking names down aren't the nicest

OVERALL:
im recommending everyone to come here. worth the wait. left a lasting impression on us during our first trip out here. thank you brophy bros!

I love to see small businesses still surviving through this mess. Function has a special place in my heart from my high school days back when I first discovered a world outside of Starbucks. Things look a little different and sitting indoors is something I'll have to wait a little longer for, but the Vanilla Latte still slaps, the baked goods still taste yummy and fresh, and the bottom line is that if any place is surviving the apocalypse, it's definitely this place. Stand outside in the cold watching people nearly get into car accidents and play the "how do I stay 6 ft away from the family coming towards me" hokey pokey, but when you get your cuppa, it's all worth it. Give love to the small biz as a solid to the ones we've lost this year.

I am IN LOVE with this place. I'm not exclusively vegan but I'm pretty flexible and have a few intolerances so it's nice to have the option. You can sit down but you can tell management thought about how to keep overhead low to keep prices down, so you have to bus your own table and you pick up your food from the kitchen yourself in addition to seating yourself. I kinda like it but I can see where people might take advantage. The chicken and waffles was awesome, the breakfast tacos were super delicious, and the cold brew was real cold brew and not iced coffee! And getting oat milk at the fixings station? Holy crap, this should be industry standard.

I can see why this place gets so crowded and I can't believe it's taken me so long to get here.

The first weekend of September 2014 is a big win for Philadelphia; this is the weekend Dilworth Park opened and this is the weekend Hippot Shabu Shabu opened. The appearance of Dilworth and Hippot Shabu Shabu indicate that Philadelphia is increasingly the place to be.

Why is Hippot Shabu Shabu opening here big news? Because Hippot Shabu Shabu, a very successful Chinese restaurant (founded in inner Mongolia) with locations around the world (Beijing, Macau, LA, etc.), must have done the math and decided that Philadelphia Chinatown is now a place they can succeed. (You maybe can't tell from the English name, but 小肥羊 definitely identifies this place as the very popular Chinese hot pot restaurant and apparently translates as 'Little Sheep Hot Pot' and thus explains the sheep on the outside sign and logo.)

The Hippot Shabu Shabu brand is good and staff say the soup base really is from  小肥羊. The interior of this restaurant is modern and sleek, and the tables, although they have cooking surfaces (with places for big hot pots and places for smaller personal hot pots), are clean and elegant. They have a liqueur license (although maybe not fully approved just yet). They also sell bubble tea!

Looked at my credit card statement from the last few months and it's clear that this has become my go to place for Chinese food. In fact, a bit unfortunate, as I rarely go to Chinatown to eat anymore. I eat both in the restaurant (for the soup dumplings) and also takeout (generally an order of shrimp fried rice, an edamame tofu strip dish, and a Peking duck dish). Consistently very good. 

I find that the service that they use for takeout delivery is very expensive and so I generally order over phone and then pickup the food myself.

I'm almost hesitant to give this place 5 stars, but when I think back on my meal, every morsel from service, to seating, to food and drink were perfection!!!

We were a large group, midday on a Friday, which meant the restaurant was near-empty, and we were seated in a quaint little room with a large wooden table and sun-filled windows. Our server was casual and efficient with excellent recommendations.

The bread and olive oil with sun-dried (mash?) was outstanding. I had a late-day, perfectly spiced bloody-mary. 

We had the Salmon di Capri, which was really delicious. I've been into horseradish lately and was pleasantly surprised when I saw this combination on the menu. But it was subtle and well executed.

The Bruschetta was heaping with fresh tomatoes!

I had the Di Rucola e Parmiggiano and added shrimp ... just fantastic. Everything was so fresh, and the shrimp was warmed, added bonus for attention to detail.

Other highlights included the La Primavera, Pesto Rosso and the Lasagna.

I didn't have dessert or coffee, but my fellow diners seemed quite pleased.

Overall, Gulfport Florida is a sweet and cute little area I highly recommend.

I went here with my fiancee and some of my coworkers last year. It was my first time here and the food was delicious. The cheese pizza that I ate was tasty, and their garlic bread was awesome. It was also very affordable, as we split our bill separate ways. The service was also wonderful, and the staff is very friendly. 

I hope to come back in the future to try more food! :)

I have eaten there a couple times now. It is one of the best buffets I have gone to. Food seems fresh and tasty!
Nice quite place to use there WiFi after lunch rush

I love Gourds Gone Wild from Tampa Bay Brewing Company and this was my first time visiting since they tapped the keg this season.  Gourds Gone Wild is 1000% my favorite fall beer. 

Tampa Bay Brewing Company is also fantastic outside of this perfect beer.  

We visited on a Saturday for lunch a got really nice seating outside.

One of the daily specials were these fantastic loaded french fry dish with gouda and bacon, it was delicious. 

My husband and I also split the meatloaf and they did a fantastic job of putting it onto two plates for us. It was superb as well but had a little bit too much mashed potato and not enough meatloaf.

Will be headed back to TBBC many times this fall to continue enjoying my favorite beer! 

Please do try, maybe we can get it all year!

I hardly ever ate BBQ before 4 Rivers Smokehouse opened up in Carrollwood conveniently located steps from my work.  We now frequent this location for takeout lunches for the office.  You can buy all of their meats by the pound so it's perfect for a potluck style lunch or catered party. 

We frequently order the Burnt Ends which made me love BBQ.  I lived in NC, and grew up trying to love Carolina BBQ as much as everyone else did.  

This happened at 4 Rivers though, the moist smoky flavor and texture of the Burnt Ends make it stand out from the rest.  My second favorite meat item is the beef brisket, I always ask for lean which is not on the menu but they will cut it that way for you.  Same moist smoky flavor obviously different taste due to the type of meat.

The sauces are fantastic as well but I don't always use them.  I also love the jalapeños!  

For birthday lunches at my work, no matter where we get takeout from, we come here for deserts.  The salted caramel brownies and the chocolate brownies are decadent but all of their bakery items are great.

Checked out Sparkman Wharf Saturday of opening weekend.  They have made very positive changes to the once Channelside portside shops that were a huge failure. I didn't get the chance to eat, but there are a ton of boxcar restaurants from local establishments such as Edison Food Lab, Restaurant BT and Mise En Place plus many more.   

The lines were long so we grabbed a beer from the beer garden and plan on going back to try the food.  The beers are pricey, between $8-12 so you may go broke drinking too many here.

Splitsville was renovated and is now open, the water front area is now open to the public so you can enjoy while visiting the venue unlike before when the water was not a feature to enjoy.   

There is tons of seating to just relax and enjoyed the scene or play games such as shuffleboard and corn hole on the lawn.  

Can't wait to go back and try the food!

I visited 7th + Grove for curbside to go.  Got a beer while a waited but the food was ready before I finished my beer.  I order the Rock The Boat which is fried catfish, gouda grits, and collards.  It was so so good.  I thought I had already had the best catfish possible but this might just be better.  Can't wait for restaurants reopen completely to enjoy this meal fresh out of the kitchen.  

I will definitely return to 7th + Grove in the future.

The new location is not your grandfather's Lakeview Harbor and SOOO disappointed.  While it is a larger location, the only thing colder than the atmosphere, is the food and attitude of the waitstaff.

I had ordered a grilled chicken sandwich and the cheese was two cold slices of cheese.  If you are going to go with sliced cheese at least put it under a broiler.  I had asked for a wheat bun which came out as white bun and when I asked it to be changed, the waitress returned with a cold (not toasted) bun and not my chicken was cold as well.

I used to work in the service industry and probably more forgiving than most when it comes to restaurant service.  I could understand if the restaurant was busy and the kitchen could be overwhelmed or a little slow.  But on Wednesday night, 7pm, there were only 3 tables being occupied and 6 waitstaff - absolutely NO reason for poor wait or kitchen performance.

Terrible overall experience.

Saw Cowboys and Aliens last night at the movie tavern(good rental movie)...we really wanted to check out the theater since it opened a couple weeks ago, I had High Hopes...they were crushed... 

Movie Tavern is starting off with 2 stars. I may head back and reevaluate, but that's all its worth at this time, I'm shocked there are so many good reviews, but I see at least the 5 star reviewer hasn't even been there yet...

The best part about the movie tavern is the seats. They are over sized and well spaced, each with it's own tray table and "service button" attached. Very comfortable seating. That's the best thing about the place. Next I guess is the price of the ticket...Only 9.50, which is sadly, a decent price these days. 

The worst part about the movie tavern is the food\pricing, which is sad because that is really the reason we are here!  Not for a movie, but dinner and a movie...The food is mediocre and overpriced. Our burgers were served so quickly there is little doubt they were sitting under a heat lamp a few minutes earlier...including the Kobe beef sliders(Please!  Don't order Kobe beef at a place called the movie tavern!) 

The 4 members of our party all ordered shakes as well. They do not have chocolate ice cream, but vanilla with Hershey's syrup, just so you know...2 of our shakes were filled to the brim then topped off with whipped cream and a cherry...2 of our shakes, including mine, were 3/4 filled with shake and the rest was whipped topping, not even a cherry. Additionally, they didn't even blend the ice cream\syrup, you could see lines of it streaming into the vanilla ice cream. I was extremely disappointed at the quality\quantity. For the price i was expecting a big silver cup to fill my glass from, but we only got the partially filled glass. 

The coffee was also disappointing...it took almost 15 minutes from the time i pressed the service button till i got my warm cup of watery coffee. Not hot, warm. Another cup? No problem, but it will cost you 2.50 more. No refills on the coffee here...Altho I heard they do refill your soda, which isn't a bad deal for 3.50. 

Skipped Dessert after the disappointing shake... so can't speak on it, but definitely suggest you order early as Amelia M ran into a snag eating her dessert after the movie ended!  

Also a bit odd...we were all done our dinner before the movie even started! They ask you to place your order before the movie starts...what they really mean is place it before the 20+ minutes of commercials and previews...The food came quickly, as I don't think they had to cook anything, just grab it from the hot lamp and serve it...so all 4 of us finished our meals before the movie even started...which made me wonder...what's the point? Why not have people stand in the concession line and take their food into the theater? Or for that matter, eat anywhere you like then head to the movies...of course you are welcome to press the button and order refills and more food, but thats the only perk I see, not having to get up once you are seated. Of course, if you are drinking beer and not worried about food, this can be a wonderful service, but as far as dinner and a movie, I'm going to pass. I'd rather stuff my pockets with Chic Fil A sandwiches. 

As far as the movie experience...I already mentioned the seats, top notch...i was not blown away by the sound, but that could be the movie itself, not the theater. The price was actually good at 9.50. But dinner cost $20(w/tip) for a burger\fries, shake, and coffee, so you offset the dollar or 2 on the ticket price pretty quick... 

We were in the 4th row and no patrons sat in front of us, so I can't say how much the servers interfere with the movie experience for everyone else. But I am glad I saw Cowboys and Aliens and not Harry Potter because having a server come up to you in the middle of the movie and whisper to you can be a bit distracting if you are really into a movie. Obviously, with cowboys and aliens, a little missed dialog isn't going to hurt too much! So I actually like the movie theater portion of the place, I'm just put out by the foods quality. Still relatively new, so I will try it again, but my first experience is not so hot... 

Overall...Its a neat concept...I like the idea...but wish the food was better. I do think drinkers and families will like this...Kids will like it for the novelty, and the drinkers won't have to getup until they have to  hit the bathroom...But as a foodie who loves movies, this is not what i was hoping for.  A neat experience, but I was not wowed to say the least.  I'd think this format would work better for reruns like Blazing Saddles\Pulp Fiction\The Holy Graille but not my thing for first run movies.

This isn't your Vietnamese grandma's pho, but it's still good (yet different). Think of it more as a modern foodie impressionist version of Vietnamese. It doesn't quite look or taste like the authentic "real thing," but that doesn't mean I don't really like it. 

Where else are you going to find boba tea cocktails? That shit is genius and delicious!  I also really enjoyed the shrimp spring rolls and vegetarian pho.  Boyfriend got pork pho with pork belly, duck sausage, and greens. He loved it.

Will Mopho push the more authentic Vietnamese restaurants out of my regular dining rotation? Nope.  But will Mopho be added to the rotation? You beat ya.

Wow!  The Vinoy Renaissance is a premier hotel property with incredible first class service, amenities and bay views!  We were fortunate to get a room here this weekend since our stay coincided with the St Pete Triathlon / Marathon weekend!  

Although we requested early check in, we took advantage of the delay by checking out the local lunch spots of which there are so many terrific choices (we enjoyed Sushi Inc downtown)!

After lunch we opted to check with the front desk and lo and behold our room was ready!  Very cool to be upgraded to a corner Bay view King Suite with pull out sofa bed- beautiful accommodations and views of the Bay!

I also appreciate that this hotel like the Hotel Del Monte in Monterey, CA has such a rich history going back to the 1920s as well as brief period serving as a WW II hospital for the military.  Oh did I mention the additional cool factor - the Vinoy Renaissance is purported to be haunted!

I have no doubt that we will be back again to this beautiful property!  This is a must stay hotel in St Pete!

This is a must stop in Nashville for dinner but gets packed at weekends so get there early. Upstairs is finer dining, downstairs is more a bistro feel. This is a place where the ladies can really dress up, or go casual either works as a very mixed crowd. There is a great vibe at the bar if you're by yourself too. 

Staff are awesome, very chatty and the food is always good. Check out the menu on their site it's all good stuff, steak and fish are superb here. Good selection of wine and scotches. If you are in Nashville for a romantic weekend, make this your first night for dinner and let your date wear that sexy dress, then head down the street and cross over to "crossroads" for some great music.  Welcome to Nashville!

Would not recommend this place. Ordered a cake and paid for it to be picked up the next day.
Not only did they lose my order and not make the cake.  The cake they gave me was not the right kind of cake at all.  Taking my business elsewhere.

I feel like an obstinate teenager writing this review.  "Okay, FINE Mom.  Aqui Con El Nene's Sonoran Hot Dogs were just as good if not maybe better then Guerro Canelo."

You see, I hold every hot dog to the Guerro standard.  I am something of a Sonoran Hot Dog connoisseur, and when someone told me these were better, I went along to humor them, knowing in the depths of my heart that they could not be better.

Well, I will (reluctantly) admit that I was wrong.  They were at least as good as Guerro, but I have to try them again to make the full judgement of if they were as good or if they were better.  The bun, while also divine at Guerro, at Nene's was less doughy and....glutony?  It was softer and more airy, though it could still definitely hold all of the fixins!

Also, something that I judge very harshly at any place is the avocado sauce.  I could drink the stuff most of the time.  This one was absolutely better than Guerro.  Don't get me wrong!  Both are delicious!  But the one here actually had a tiny little kick of heat to it, and as it turns out I super enjoyed it.

This place.  I have such mixed feelings about this place.  The food, on one hand, is pretty good, especially if you grow up here with our Nico's and Los Beto's places.  I always get the veggie burrito and it's fine.  We used to come here pretty frequently, but man, that super rude, into her cell phone young female (she is by no means a lady) who cannot be bothered to do her job sent us running.

She is always so rude when we go in, but three days ago or so just took the cake and I decided I needed to write a review.

There was this family that was there, a mom, a dad and two young boys.  My husband and I were at the counter ordering, and the dad came up to the counter and said his enchiladas were cold.

"what do you mean?" is her reply.  I don't know what the devil she thought he meant, since there is really only one meaning to "my enchiladas are cold".
He put his finger into them and repeated that they were cold.  Now, me being a nosy girl, looked into the enchiladas.  The cheese that was on top had literally never even melted.  It was still in it's shredded form.

So then, SHE sticks her fingers into his food and tells him it's because of the lettuce.  Because lettuce has the magical power to leech all heat from hot food.  But she asks him if he wants the cheese melted, he says yes, and she takes it back to the kitchen.  

Now, apparently this girl thinks it's totally fine to say mean things about the customers in Spanish.  Nevermind that we are in Tucson, Arizona, where even the snow birds know at LEAST the dirty words.  Nevermind that though I look white as can be, Spanish was my first language and I can understand every insult you are hurling at this man in the kitchen.  Nope.  It's fine.  We don't look like we understand.  But guess what.  Even my very white husband knew what you were saying.

What was the big deal?  All he wanted was hot enchiladas on a cold night.  It's not like he wanted gaspacho heated up.

She was so rude to us the entire time, until Mr. Swag came in.  Some guy just walked in through the front door, behind the counter and to the kitchen.  He then emerged to canoodle with the cashier woman.  Really?  Do you work here?  Because you look like you are just some dude that knows her and walked into the kitchen to get a snack.

Anyway, once he gets there, she is just all smiles.  I have been here probably close to 30 times, and you are NEVER this nice.

There was another time she refused to help a man sitting at a table in a wheelchair, even though he was waving and calling to her for some help in getting some more soda and a bag to take his leftovers in.  She looked up from her phone, rolled her eyes, and went back to texting.  I was the person who got up and got his bag for him.  It was just too inconvenient for her to go around the counter with a plastic bag.

So, will I be back?  Probably.  It's the closest place to work that has a decent veggie burrito.  Should the owners read this and have a crash course in customer service with their employees?  Yes.

I LOVE IT HERE!  

I came in for my first time tonight about 15 minutes before close, but there were still people inside playing board games and hanging out.  I looked at their menu, and ended up asking the people behind the counter what their favorites were.  The staff was playful and informative, and we ended up getting one of their recommendations and one matcha slush with boba.

The recommendation was a pearl tea, and it was a delight.  It was not too sweet, had delicious flavor, and a great amount of boba.

The matcha was amazing.  It's my favorite boba tea flavor, and I am a little finicky about it's flavor.  This was spot on, not too sweet, actually almost no sweetness, which is good news for me!  The boba was chewy and perfect!

The people behind the counter made jokes, were very polite, and really made us feel welcomed into their shop, even though they were closing in just a few minutes.

I also got a stamp card; buy six get the next free, and I have a feeling within a week and a half I will be getting my free boba tea.  I will absolutely be back, especially with their late hours.

I came here for the first time for a Yelp event, and was so impressed that I brought my cousin in for a back-to-school dinner.

Tonight, the bartender recognized me from Yelp and offered to bring us a tray of the Tapas that they had so we could look at them from our table.  We got olives marinated in cumin, the amazing toast with tomato and manchego, and potatoes with a red pepper sauce.

Then we ordered the soup of the day and I got duck tacos.  I have never had duck before, because from what I hear it is very oily and fatty, and also, it was a cute little duck!  But in light of turning over new leafs and trying to things, I decided I wanted that.

I asked the waiters opinion before ordering and he spoke highly of it.  It came out very fast, and while I have no way to compare duck to how I have had it before, this was amazing.  The smokey sweet duck was served with a slightly spicy slaw and mandarin oranges, and it all came together like angels doing the can-can on my tastebuds!  

I think I may have a new favorite thing in the world.  It might be the duck tacos at Contigo.

I walked in and was surprised when I saw a menu written in chalk on the left wall and what looks to be their workers behind some sort of bulletproof window. Before I could order, I was forced to listen to all types of profanity coming from behind the window (their workers were talking about their recent visit to a nightclub). No one greeted me, attempted to take my order... Etc... As I was walking out, the man shouted "alright, na..." Ummm... Pleasures all mine???  Horrible customer service and not the type of establishment you should bring your child in... I will NEVER eat the chicken from here (which sucks because I heard it was really good). They need to replace the workers that they have, and perhaps hire people who have worked in the service industry before or people that even have a little bit of respect for themselves as well as others. I blame the owner for obviously hiring friends or family, and also for the whole set up, I mean there is a brand new shopping center right next door as well as other restaurants and I don't see their workers hiding behind a prison glass...

I was super pumped to finally experience The Catbird Seat after convincing my husband that we should splurge and check this place out for our five year anniversary. Dining here had been on my bucket list since it opened a few years ago, although I felt like I missed out after finding out the original chefs left. However, after reading about Chef Trevor Moran and his background, I was excited once again since he is a Noma alum, and I come from Danish roots myself. 

To get the point, I'll just say that this is definitely the been the best culinary experience for a foodie living in Nashville hands down. And Nashville has really come a long way in the culinary world and offers a lot of great choices these days. But The Catbird Seat offers the kind of experience you typically have to go to New York and other major cities to experience. And... at $400 for the two of us, it's only about a third of the price of The French Laundry!

To get a reservation, I had to stay up to midnight exactly one month prior to the night we wanted the reservation so I could get one online. Even then, by the time I clicked the link, I was left with one of the latest reservations at 9:15 p.m. This turned out to be a blessing as UGA played South Carolina that day in a game that got delayed two hours and then we lost, so I didn't miss the ending (wish I had now). However, the excitement of our anniversary dinner at The Catbird Seat helped get me out of the bad mood my Dawgs left me in.

We really loved how relaxed and fun the experience was. The 80's music in the background was fun and set the mood. Chef Moran and his sous chefs were all very personable and talked to us throughout the night. Every dish was described to you as they set it in front of you. They told you about the ingredients as well as how it was prepared. As expected, there is no menu, you just sit down and are presented with twelve courses throughout the night. Actually, I lied, there is a menu... they give it to you as a souvenir as you leave!

The food was amazing. There were so many unique ingredients that I have not eaten before. Although I didn't fall in love with every dish, I would say that most of them were incredible, with only a few that didn't agree with my palate. With a twelve course tasting, I did not go in thinking that it was possible to love every single dish. I would say there was only one that I didn't really like, a few that were good but not great, and the rest I thoroughly enjoyed.

Instead of going into every course on here (some are similar to ones previously described), I'll upload pictures with descriptions of some of the courses we got to experience. I wish I would have taken a pictures of each course, but we were enjoying ourselves so much that I forgot!

One final note, they offer water, a non-alcholic beverage pairing, and a standard and premium alcoholic beverage pairing. I believe the non-alcoholic was $25, standard was $40, and premium was $75 per person.

The downtown Franklin Mellow Mushroom is awesome. The food, service, and atmosphere is better than the Nashville restaurant. They have great pizza and unique specialty pizzas. My favorite is the Magical Mystery Tour.  This location has some items unique to this location that are amazing, including their homemade cheese and mustard dips made with beer that you dip hot pizza dough bites into. 

They also have a great beer selection with some lesser known breweries represented. That is always an added bonus.

We aren't the only ones who loves this place. Expect to wait up to an hour to be seated on the weekends. We like to go a little earlier to avoid the long wait, but even before 6 pm, you may still have a short wait. The good thing is they call you on your cell phone, so you can stroll downtown Franklin while you wait.

Haven't been here in a while and I remember why.  Way overpriced!! 2.00 extra for a small portion of burnt fries instead of baked potato?!?!  
My son got the spaghetti and meatballs and the flavor was horrible. Don't get it! 
The burger...ZERO flavor and $15. Wish this restaurant was as good as it was when it was on Harrison.   If you are looking for the old lake view harbor, it just doesn't exist anymore.  
Last, the service was great though.

Remember Tahoe Burger ; The terrible overpirced burger joint at this same location that closed?

Ya, this place is Tahoe Burger  with a new sign.

To sum up: The food tastes OK. The fries are OK. The selection is OK.

My complaints are exactly the same as Tahoe Burger. If you're going to serve mediocre food, the value for the customer has to come from the price. My wife and I paid $27 for 2 bacon cheeseburgers, 2 fries and 2 drinks. Yes, in this economy...   $27 bucks for two fast food service small portion mediocre hamburgers. 

Either serve me food that tastes amazing and no complaint will be heard about the price or give me value for my dollar. You will find neither here and you will also not find me here.

Maybe it was fate, or perfect timing, or being awake and functional prior to 9am on a Sunday but I went to Honeys, and was seated immediately. 

Service was outstanding. My coffee was promptly served and never empty. The waitress was friendly and seemed genuinely glad to be there. 

Ordered the breakfast salad topped with a poached egg and was not disappointed. It was the perfect blend of warm and crisp and overall dreamy. I'm salivating just thinking about it. Ordered a (very pricey) slice of toast just for the jam that was on the table. It was delicious. 

Really enjoyed this place. I'll be back for certain.

Full disclosure: Visit and review during Covid-19 pandemic.

So this is a hard one to write up.  I love St. Elmo's so I really wanted to love 1933 Lounge as well.  Service was great, but the food was just ok.  Maybe I just ordered the wrong thing...

My friend and I started with Calamari - honestly this was probably the best thing we had that visit.  The calamari was a generous portion for an appetizer.  For my entree I ordered the 12 oz. Prime Rib and opted for the Navy Bean soup (I usually get the soup from St. Elmo's in dt Indy, so I knew I couldn't go wrong.  The Prime rib was not even luke warm.  It was medium rare, as I requested, and the plate was super hot, but the actual meat was practically at room temperature, which I thought was odd.  When I mentioned it to the server, he said they can heat it up, but then it wouldn't be medium rare (?!), so I just powered through and didn't finish it.  I think someone actually did mention that in a review recently so you think they would have addressed it by the time I visited.  My recommendation is NOT to order the prime rib.

We did end our evening with the Mousse pie - it was really delicious, and although it looks rich, it was light and airy, just as a mousse should be.

Would I visit again?  Maybe, but I think I'll stick with their rib eye next time.

Vegetarians and vegans take note of this little place! My usual DTSP hangout was a little too hectic for me recently, so I had to find another option for coffee/snacks nearby. I had bookmarked Community Cafe a while back because of the crazy nighttime hours. Open until 3am sometimes? Sign me up!

The clientele ranged from tatted and pierced punk rock types to hippies and a dude gaming on his laptop... To me, braiding fake hair that night. So, I made my order - a large latte and a chicken salad sandwich. A couple minutes later, my drink showed up. Shortly after that, my sandwich. I'm going to be honest, I'm incredibly biased against sourdough. I was pleasantly surprised at the bread though - it looked pan-toasted and I really liked it. The chicken salad had a mix of grapes, walnuts, and dried cranberries in it. It wasn't overly mayo'd, and was just a little sweet from the fruit. It had a small pile of corn chips with it too. I would definitely order that again because it wasn't massive and it had a nice flavor profile. The coffee was pretty solid too - it didn't have any weird bitterness going on and the milk wasn't scorched. Gerardo's caprese salad looked delicious too. All thumbs up on the eats here.

I was also really thrilled to see all the local artwork on the walls and mini art things for sale all over the place. I could definitely see this being a place to pop in for affordable art for gifting. While we started out at a regular table because we were eating, I eventually relocated to one of the comfy sofas and commandeered a corner of the cafe to work on my weird hair thing since it was a little slow. I got to chatting with the owner, and I have to say, she's a total bad ass. She seems to have a lot of great ideas (like the "speed friending for movie buffs" event I saw coming up there) and wants to great a true community. Businesses like these are rare, and much needed these days. I'm sure I'll be back again!

DON'T DO IT! RECONSIDER! READ SOME .. of my review! 

Tried this place twice hoping my first experience was a spontaneous occurrence - NOPE. 

The first time we went on a Sunday afternoon around 1. Our waitress (blonde captured in the photos) was bouncing off the walls, running around like a chicken with her head cut off - almost certain she was under the influence of some kind of substance. She could barely focus on our requests and disappeared while we were waiting on our food. Ordered the calamari to start. Took over 30 minutes to come out. Overdone and super salty - the best thing I can relate the taste to was pork skins. There was 3 times as much salty breading in the bowl as overcooked greasy calamari. I ordered the Mighty Mo & my boyfriend ordered the Sink. We waited OVER AN HOUR AND FIFTEEN MINUTES FOR OUR FOOD. Our waitress disappeared and once she reappeared she seemed to ignore us trying to call her over. We had to ask SEVERAL floor employees to get her to come over. After witnessing her make comments to a hostess while making faces and staring at us, she came over to the table and explained to us our food would be ready any minute. I requested to speak with a manager. She said there was no manager available - although another employee said "she" referring to the manager was in the back. When I confronted the waitress about this, she said that the manager was currently cooking and wouldn't be available to speak with us. She also explained that there are 2 managers YET NOBODY COULD SPEAK WITH US Our food finally comes out with his being steaming hot and mine cold. It also looked like someone swiped a finger through the remoulade on my crab cake - the mayo had already settled into an oil (for you to get an idea of how long this food had been sitting). I AGAIN try to get a manager - "manager" finally comes out. Apologizes but blames the poor service on the party of 10 that came in 40 minutes after us. He offers us a free meal next time we come in and offers to recook my food personally. 30 minutes later I finally get a hot plate of food. He reduced the price of my entree but did not offer to comp our meal for this CATASTROPHE of an experience. I held back writing a review thinking this was an independent incident - haha! 

After both of the options we chose for dinner this past Sunday being closed on Sunday's, we decided to give Kitchen Sink another try. Bad choice. We explained our last experience to our waiter as he chuckled and offered no apology or opportunity to confirm the experience with a manager. Whatever. I requested to substitute the jambalaya on The Mighty Mo with etoufee and was obliged. When my food arrived, I knew something was off. I love Cajun/creole food & KNOW the difference between jambalaya and etoufee. One is a roux wine creole trinity base - the other has tomato based sauce .. These ... EXPLETIVES... Took some jambalaya sauce added crawfish & poured it over rice - tried to fool me into thinking it was etoufee - WITH BIG CHUNKY TOMATO SAUCE. Another party at my table had the jambalaya - she tasted my "etoufee" and confirmed it was the exact same. I told the waiter I think there was a discrepancy and tried to explain it to him. He laughed and tried to argue back no and walked off. He offered no further assistance, we paid full price for our meals & left. Waiter this time was a GRADE A creep! 

I will not be returning and will be deterring everyone I hear about even considering it! The food is mediocre at best and the ATROCIOUS service makes it even worse.

 We attempted to go to the other location prior to the second experience - saw our old waitress and walked back out. 

STEER CLEAR OF THIS WASTE OF TIME if I could rate it a ZERO NO GO I would - I strongly recommend Evangeline's or Broadway Oyster Bar for delicious Cajun/Creole food and a great experience!

Such a disappointment!!! 

I was really excited to check out The Organic Banana while visiting NOLA because the pictures I saw online of their frozen smoothies looked so freakin' yummy and I could get alcohol in it BUT the frozen strawberry daiquiri that I ordered was watery & not frozen at all. 

For $8.50 plus tip I was really disappointed w/ my drink & the bartender had no customer service skills at all. 

Well at least I can say I tried it but next time I won't waste my money.

-Rebecca out

I found this restaurant thanks to Yelp and so glad I did. I haven't dined inside the restaurant since I always order my food to go. Every time I call and place my order for pick up they are always nice and helpful. My order is always ready at the time given and always right. They also write the name of the rolls you order on the box so you are not guessing which roll is which.

Some of my favorite rolls: 
Jabadahut 
Torched Salmon roll
Japanese Bagel roll
Crunchy FL roll.

I try to order something different every time and I have never been disappointed. The rolls always taste fresh and delicious. This is definitely my family and I go to place for delicious sushi and maybe one day we will dine in instead of ordering to-go.

Before moving to Tampa from California I looked up several restaurants and bookmarked places I knew I had to try and this was one of them. I've been here a few times and ordered different items each visit until I found my favorite thing. Carne asada fries is definitely a Southern CA thing. I missed it so much that was the first thing I ordered when I came here. In my opinion it was just OK. The carne asada did not have much flavor or seasoning. I drenched it with lots of salsa to add more flavor, but was not a fan of the salsa. The salsa did not have much taste and tasted kind of watery. The one thing I did enjoy was the fish taco and shrimp and chorizo taco. I ordered both loaded (cheese, sour cream, and guacamole) but EASY on the onions. I like onions, but the onions were cut in different sizes some were diced really small and some were as big as my pinky. They should probably invest in a chopper lol. 

This place can be busy especially during lunch time so be prepared to wait. You can call your order ahead of time, but the last few times I did my orders were wrong.

I just got a nasty message from someone who seems to work for Philly Cupcake or is connected to them in some way. And, from reading other reviews that weren't dripping with hyperbolic praise, it seems like they're going after people who aren't handing out four and five stars.

To put it simply: I'm not giving Philly Cupcake another chance, and I'll be letting people know about their shady online business practices. Shame on you.

And I'm a professional athlete I do not like GMOs fillers and MSG ...Funny story these people did nothing wrong besides be to embedded in their opinion. I was treating a group of friends to a nice evening meal at any restaurant that they wanted to go to they chose Mandarin Palace.  I'm a professional athlete who plays for the Philadelphia Eagles I don't eat Chinese food but I do like to go out and eat with friends. So I compromised I got a salad down the street at Sweet greens great salads they have excellent service. So I walk in with my sweet green salad and I ask the server who was very kind and understanding if I'm able to bring this salad in while my friends sit and enjoy their food we were seated and given menus. While my friends looked at their menus I started to eat, I had my food already and I hadn't eaten all day. Just when we where l about to order the manager comes out and says we don't allow outside food you have to leave. I proceeded to explain to him that I understand but I'm paying for this meal and that I don't eat Chinese food and on a strict diet so I would just like to sit here enjoy a nice meal with my friends at their location. He stayed persistent and insisted that I leave. Now I understand a restaurants moral code and belief system but I also believe that the customer is always right and being that the restaurant is BYOB ( bring your on beer and or alcoholic beverages) you would think that they would make accommodations for person in a party of people that doesn't partake in eating Chinese food. And they caused a scene I'm never been more embarrassed in a restaurant. Myself and all of my Friends left the restaurant , they lost out on a lot of money because I planned to do it big for my friends who had just graduated from Drexel. I'm asking you the people of Philadelphia to not support restaurants that treat customers this way. 
They're worried about one salad opposed to making some money if I was the owner of this restaurant I would be pissed about the management.

The first time my husband brought me to his home in St. Louis, he also brought me to Crown Candy Kitchen...sigh.  If you like feeling you're in a movie from around the 40's, you will love Candy Kitchen.

Crown is almost 100 years old.  The interior contains layers from various decades:  authentic Coke memorabilia co-mingles with old menus posted on the walls, a checkerboard linoleum floor and old white booths that are tight and high with coat hooks on the end.  You really get an authentic taste of the past, for better or worse!

Reviews need to break down the 3 components of the store:
Ice Cream (Soda Fountain)
Candy
Food

It's too one-dimensional to rate Crown simply on the food and service; it's a soda fountain.  Crown's business is selling nostalgia - mainly through ice cream & candy!

If you come here primarily for a sandwich, you've missed the point.

This is a legit soda fountain.  The ice cream is made in-store, so it is unique.  It's also rich and dense, with 14% butterfat!  Old school:  In addition to hot fudge or caramel, sundaes with things like fruit salad and pecan pralines rule the day.  You can get a chocolate phosphate or vanilla Coke.  The shakes ($5) are huge and come with their metal mixing cups.

Chocolate here is very good, made in house and - to my thinking - should be noted primarily for the antique molds they use.  I still have an Easter chocolate my husband got me:  a bunny couple dressed in clothes circa 1930's looking like they're going to the Easter Parade!  But they have 100's of old molds which cast the most beautiful and unusual designs.  Any chocolate freak needs to stop here for the molds alone.  Crown is noted for their nut clusters and old fashioned fruit candies they still sell...you have to see the counter yourself!

If you want food harking back to a mid-20th century lunch counter done capably, eat here.  I usually am here only for sweets but when I eat food here, I know I'm eating a lunch fairly authentic to the menu's inception.  To modern eaters this would be an insipid ham sandwich or innocuous tuna fish...but to nostalgia peeps, it's a little bit of fun.

My advice:  don't come to Crown for stellar service or food...come for a taste of the old days, and you'll leave satisfied.

A very pleasant dining experience the food was delicious the decor was beautiful and the service was awesome. 

I would come back here just for the apps.  Some of the best apps ever.  Pan seared scallops over fried cheese grits. With a buttery garlic sauce.  Also the crab cake special was amazing.  I had crab cakes from two other spots in new Orleans and both failed   Briquette had the best tasting crab cake. Not much filler and lump crab meat.   And the oysters artichoke casserole was bursting with a cheesy garlic creamy flavor.  All these three apps were enough was so satisfied I didn't even order dinner.  Butu cousin and friend ordered the blackend red fish with gulf shrimp. That was really good I had a taste.  And the snapper Pontchartrain which was also delicious but I was so full from the apps I just tasted thier dishes.    

A great sit down Resturant if your craving quality food.

Willie Mae made my dae!!!

Coming down to new Orleans I heard about their good food but didn't know I would be getting the best fried chicken.  It's definitely worth a trip here if you never tried it. The 2005 James beard award winning fried chicken is why it's a must.  

Pulling up iny LYFT rode it looks like you're walking into someone's house.  And with plenty of seats me and my coworker were sat down instantly.  Candy our waitress was very sweet and with her NOLA accent she welcomed us to Willie Mae's.  I glanced at the menu but I already knew what I wanted 3 piece dark with Mac and cheese. With a half lemonade and half unsweetened iced tea to was it down.  

The chicken is made to order so it was a good 20-25 min wait. But when it did come out it put me in fried chicken heaven and Willie Mae putting her hand on my head welcoming me to her home.  

Needless to say the fried chicken was magnificent. A golden Light but crispy batter covering the seasoned juicy meat every but was a fried chicken bliss.  This fried chicken would have made me slap my momma if she was there.  Sorry Mom.  Lol.  The chicken was so good it over shadowed an amazing Mac and cheese. This Mac and cheese was also amazing it was baked and had a little spice to it and was a wonderful compliment to the amazing fried chicken.  Damn as I'm writing I was some now. 

I usually don't eat dessert but this chicken was so good I had to try the bread pudding.   I'm glad I saved room because that bread pudding was like eating a cinnabun.  Every bite had a cinnamon sugar-brown butter explosion with a little vanilla pudding mixed in.  A great end to a great meal. 

I thank the staff and cooks as I walked to the bathroom for an amazing dining experience.

Maybe I'm just a typical Hispanic? Or maybe I'm just from Texas and know really good Mexican food...but I can understand why people here love it seeing as there isn't much else in Nashville. Just really underwhelming reading all these crazy reviews.

I had the orchata which was very good (a creamy drink, try it!) I also had the fish taco, which, not sure what happened, but was VERY fishy. So much so that I couldn't eat it. It tasted like old fish. The other taco was chicken. Eh, forgettable. 

The tortilla soup had high expectations reading everyone else's reviews but honestly it was bland. Not sure where you guys are getting tortilla soup. But then again, maybe I'm spoiled. I don't live in Nashville.

Also, this is a "Guy Fieri" restaurant with his dumb head spray painted on the wall. And there were NO mexican people here. Which says something. Everyone was a tourist that got on yelp and saw all these amazing reviews.

Overall as a tourist from Texas, skip it. We waited an hour for this on lunchtime on a Thursday. Not worth it in my opinion, but to each his own.

No way! This is just about the cutest little bakery I've ever seen; and I love me some bakeries, so I've been to quite my fair share.

A friend of mine asked if I like macarons and when I realized we were headed to buy some, I about flipped my lid. I don't want a cake for my wedding. I want macarons. THAT'S how much I love them! So we pop in and not only are the baked goods delicious and beautiful, the place itself is gorgeous. It's so clean and bright that I asked if it had just opened. Turns out it's been here a few years and they just happen to take great care of the space and ensure that it's always spotless and precious. 

There's free WIFI, plenty of small and large tables to grab a seat, and a long, long steady line of hungry people eagerly waiting to place an order. I thought visiting the mall made my Edmonton visit special, but really it was Duchess Bake Shop.

I'm super impressed with The District. If there are only a small handful of places you visit while in Boise, add this spot to your list! The coffee is great, the service is great, and just about everything about this place is worth telling friends about. I thought the space was really cute, many of the chairs are mid century modern and though the space is really large and sort of austere, it still feels warm.

I ended up here for a few hours during a work day recently and enjoyed the free WIFI and the coffee. In fact, I liked it so much I ended up coming back here the same day and trying another drink as well. 

The staff were all friendly and helpful, the restrooms were clean, and the music was the perfect volume and type. Nothing that was distracting or too loud. Perfect if you're here to do work, meet friends, or just relax over a cuppa. 

It's rather busy though so large groups may not be ideal. Just looking for a table for two was tough. Especially if you want an outlet. Of the options for tables and soft seating, only 4 or 5 locations have access to a nearby power source. I also had trouble with one of the yellow garden-style chairs near the windows. I wanted to report it to the staff but the line was so long for coffee and I had to leave for the airport. Is it turns out, this chair that I sat in had been worn a bit in the seat and part of the metal of the chair was exposed and tore my pants. Which sucked because they were brand new! It wouldn't keep me from coming here but it would keep me from sitting in that same seat again until it gets repaired.

I was only in Boise for a few days but this was my favorite business to visit. I felt like I really captured the vibe of the city and the local business culture by visiting. And being here for so long over a full day allowed me to see what types of people come here and hang out. It's a mostly young (20s-30s crowd), people who are pretty relaxed and quiet, and people who seem to love to support local. Very impressed with this cafe!

Cookies, ice cream, tea, local art and awesome coffee? Sold!

Having never been to Nashville before this recent trip, I was really glad to have used the Yelp app and found Fido. The neighborhood was great, the people working there were friendly, the space was cute, the coffee was great and all in all it made me fall just a little bit more in love with this awesome city. So glad to have stumbled in here and made it part of my quick, but lovely trip to TN.

What a tasty dinner I had here last night!

Having never been to TN before, I was really excited to see a lot of new-to-me dishes, housemade sauces, and locally distilled spirits on the menu. It made it hard to choose what to eat and drink, but what a great problem to have, right?

I settled on some fried pickles (the best I've ever had!) and also ate a BBQ brisket sandwich with a side of bacon mac n' cheese. Among the three sauces on the table to choose from, there was a white BBQ sauce - which I'd never heard of before - and a sweet and a hot sauce. I played around with all three and settled on dousing my sandwich in the sweet sauce. Waking up this AM and thinking about that meal makes me want to eat it for dinner again tonight. I really, really loved that sweet BBQ sauce and if they sold it at the restaurant I'd surely buy a bottle or two to take back to Seattle. 

If there's one thing I could change, it'd be that the BBQ sauce bottles were looked after a bit more. My friends and I found the bottles to be really drippy and sticky to handle. Totally expected for a divey or family friendly spot, but this place has a slightly upscale vibe and I cringed a little every time I picked a bottle up to pass it around the table or pour some sauce on my food. It's nothing that would keep me from coming back but it was something that irked me a tiny bit. Everything else here was spotless and the table service was awesome. I got a lot of recommendations and explanations on various menu items, the prices were extremely reasonable, and the food was de-licious! Definitely a solid first meal in Nashville.

Truly as good as it gets! I popped by Red Feather late on a Friday night and it was hoppin', but the staff never skipped a beat. Though the place was packed we were treated like the only table in the house.

The friends I dined with are regulars and so they partake in a super cool cocktail club that anyone can join. You pay for a card (I think you can redeem it after a certain purchase of drinks?) and then you get to try dozens of classic cocktails off the menu over the course or weeks, months, or years. Anytime you visit you can ask to see your cocktail card and they'll bring it to you. It'll have a signature or stamp over the drinks you've tried and the rest are left for you to check out. There's info about the cocktails at each table and the map itself also has descriptions. It's a great way to learn more about cocktail culture and history - all while sort of playing a game! Educational + fun = awesome.

While not a member of the club (since I'm from out of town), I still got a great drink. Ok, two great drinks. No, maybe three! 

The food here is also outstanding. Every single item was awesome - the Brussels sprouts, the smoked trout, you name it - we ate it and we loved it. I don't think I could visit Boise again without demanding we go here. Loved it to pieces.

What a charming little weekend brunch spot! 

I was just in town visiting so I've been only once but Addie's was just what I needed before heading off the the airport. This casual little diner/cafe appeared to be chock-full of regulars. The staff seemed to know just about everyone and were quick to warmly welcome us into their space and outfit us with menus and a table.

Along the walls you can find booths that fit about 4-6 people and then in the middle of the space there were plenty more 2 and 4 tops. No wait to sit down on a Saturday before noon? Perfect!

We chose a booth and just as we sat someone popped by to take our drink order. Coffee came fast and in the 40 or so mins we were there we'd had multiple staff visit our table to top us off. I loved that the servers tag team here and basically work the room together to make sure that everyone's needs are met. 

The menu is really extensive! So much so that I needed a few more mins to decide what to eat. In addition to class savory breakfast dishes (eggs, toast, omelets, etc) they also have sweet dishes (pancakes, waffles) and even sandwiches for people wanting more typical midday/lunch type offerings. I went with the breakfast burrito with sausage and was extremely happy with my choice. 

This was unlike any breakfast burrito I'd ever had! Though it didn't really have any flavor of seasons or salt/pepper, it came with a side of salsa and sour cream. Inside the absolutely massive burrito they'd somehow beautifully folded in thin-cut soft potatoes and a sheet of egg. So it wasn't lumpy or chopped ingredients, they were all folded neatly in sheets. It was like a work of art to see this thing come together! And tucked inside among the other ingredients were the pieces of delicious breakfast sausage. No veggies, but that worked because I added both the sour cream and salsa to mine to pack in some more flavor.

Prices were reasonable, service was prompt and friendly, and the location was great because there was a small lot out front and also street parking around the corner. On a hot day we didn't have to walk far to pop in and they had the AC running so it was much cooler inside than out. There's also a large patio to take advantage of on days that aren't so warm. Overall it was lovely!

A man walks into a bar, sits down and watched as the bartender serves everyone but him. I watched him literally serve everyone at the bar and a "skirt" and not once acknowledge that I was sitting there...waste of time. Never going back.

I am an area event planner and helped coordinate a friend's joint bachelor/bachelorette party. I had made arrangements with the manager and followed up a couple of times leading up to the evening of the party. 

With a guest list of about 40 people pre-submitted and the word that we would have a private area reserved for us on the roof, we were ready to party! The ladies arrived, the staff seemed unsure of what was going on even though the manager I spoke with was there to greet us at the door...but we still all proceeded to go upstairs anyway. We attempted to sit on the beds on the roof and were told they were reserved for bottle service only. We were a bit peeved since there wasn't much of an area reserved for us, but we brushed it off and awaited the bachelor party's arrival...and this is the part where I say, 

"I WILL NEVER CONTACT OR SOLICIT VANGO AGAIN AND WILL BE SURE TO LET OTHERS KNOW HOW POOR THE SERVICE IS HERE" 

...they refused to let the bachelor party of 11 guys up to the roof deck, insisted they wait in line, treated us like we weren't important enough because we didn't pay to have bottle service (by the way, there was no mention that bottle service was required for us to reserve the space for our party beforehand), and pretty much let us know that if the rest of our party wasn't willing to wait, we could leave...that's about 40 people spending at least $50-$60/each on drinks, if not more. They made it clear that they didn't want our money and didn't care to accommodate us even though arrangements were confirmed and made beforehand. 

As we proceeded to leave, one of the girls in our party forgot to close out her card...she went to run back up to the roof deck and the security and staff REFUSED to let her go back up to get her card. 

Needless to say, this bar has overpriced drinks, extremely poor service, and is nothing more than a washed up club.

Very disappointing visit! Chicken was overcooked, primavera consisted of limp carrots and onions, pizza dough was horribly undercooked even after waiting an extra 10 minutes for it. Staff is still great but the food was awful. They comped us a dessert but it was too little too late at that point. Not sure if there's a new manager, owner, or chef but something is wrong with this place at this time... Buyer beware...

I'm really befuddled by the general hoopla over this place. Befuddled...not a word I use often. But I don't know a better one to describe my reaction to my experience at Big Gay Ice Cream. 

The prices are on the high side, yes, but that's the standard for any fancy ice cream place, so to be expected. It's the product that I can't understand the enthusiastic reactions to. I ordered the American Gobs, and my husband got the Mermaid, both in cones (regular for me, waffle for him). The toppings were good and abundant - American Gobs has chocolate-covered pretzels, which are two of my great loves, so hard to go wrong there, and for the Mermaid it's key lime curd and graham cracker crumbs. I'm told the Mermaid is refreshing on a hot day but don't take my chocolate pretzels away from me.

Except if it's this particular ice cream sundae concoction. The soft vanilla ice cream is so unremarkable, and so meager in comparison to the topping - I mean, it's not even just a topping, there were pretzels IN the ice cream, chocolate at the bottom of the cone, I mean, this was more like an order of chocolate-covered pretzels with a little ice cream as a garnish. And the chocolate-covered pretzels were tasty, but it was so over the top that I couldn't even manage to finish it, and I really wanted to! 

Next time I'll just get a soft-serve cone from McDonald's, add some pretzels and chocolate sauce, and basically have the same effect as American Gobs, but with more ice cream. Never wasting my time or money here again.

I took my brother here for a belated birthday dinner on a Friday night. I'm a Stephen Starr fangirl, and I was determined to take him to the best of the Philadelphia restaurants in his empire, and I really couldn't have chosen better than this. 

At the time that I made the reservation, only bar seating was available. I was initially disappointed because I didn't want to sit at the bar to eat dinner, but where we were actually seated was in a pretty lounge area in the front room, with plush seating and lovely lighting provided by candles and shaded wall lamps. Our server was extremely friendly and informative, going above and beyond in service quality (more on that in a bit)! We started with glasses of water, the Clover Days cocktail for my brother, and a delectable basket of popovers, which were flaky, light, rich and delicious all at once, and came with a whipped salted butter, though the popovers were so good on their own they didn't even need the butter.

I'm a vegetarian, so I decided to go with the Caesar salad (I make an occasional pescatarian allowance), and an order of tater tots. My brother loves a good steak, but he never treats himself out to a steakhouse. So like the bossy older sister that I am, I told him, get whatever you want! And so he got the American Wagyu NY strip steak, and an order of truffle whipped potatoes. He's not as effusive as me, but he finished every bite of his meal with enthusiasm, and declared it one of the best steaks he'd ever had. He insisted that I try his whipped potatoes, and while they were very flavorful, the super-smooth creamy texture isn't for me. The tater tots, on the other hand, were incredible. The waiter thought I was nuts when I told him I've never actually had tater tots before. Pretty sure if I ever have them again, nowhere else will they have such a shatteringly crisp and deliciously salty exterior, with a perfectly cloud-like mashed potato interior. I confess I had to take most of the tasty little bites home because the Caesar salad was huge, and the dressing and grated cheese so good that I shamelessly mopped up the dish with the last of my popover. 

Now, getting back to the above and beyond service by our waiter - the steak and salad were brought out by a another member of the serving staff, (sooner than I expected), but no whipped potatoes or tots in sight. When our main server returned to check on us moments later, he exclaimed over the absence of our side orders, (turns out they were sent to another table) and remedied the oversight within minutes, all the while apologizing for the mixup. It was barely a delay at all, so my brother and I hardly minded, but he insisted on removing both items from our bill, effectively making them on the house. Maybe it's because I'm not used to restaurants with such stellar service, or maybe because I'm more used to having to point out missing food to the server myself, and getting an annoyed reaction, with the missing items eventually being brought out later. 

Yes, Barclay Prime is quite expensive, but it's worth every penny, from the amazing service, to the beautiful decor, to the insanely delicious food. For a special occasion or if you want to super-treat someone (or yourself), this is definitely one of the top options in Philadelphia.

Over priced for what you get. Food was not that great. It's been in business for ever and not sure why. Always seemed to busy at old location. Had shrimp plate must be called that for how small it was. Club wrap looked ok didn't try it. Won't be back
Food was very bland. Atmosphere of the restaurant is nice but I'd prefer to go somewhere with good food. Wouldn't try it again.

I went in fully expecting to hate this place but they won me over. 

This building has been 3 different restaurants since we moved here and none of them have lasted very long so I wasn't expecting much. Visited on 6-30-19 at 11am. Our server was very friendly and attentive. $30.36 got us two adult entrees. 

I had the $14.99 titanic which came with 6 fried shrimp, french fries, and corn on the cobb. The shrimp were big and plump and juicy with a crunchy outer shell. The fries were crispy and smoky. The corn tasted like a frozen variety which they had doctored up but not bad. I loved the Guiness barbecue sauce served with it. Everything was seasoned well and hot and fresh. 

Husband had the $12.99 mums curry which had chicken, onions, and mushrooms in a creamy curry base with basmati rice. It almost tasted like a mild Japanese curry and was so delicious. I was very jealous after trying his dish and wanted to switch with him but he refused. 

Maybe this one will last. They certainly have what it takes.

A gorgeous fancy asian fusion restaurant located inside the Wyndham Grand Hotel in Clearwater Beach. 

Visited on 6/24/17 at 8PM.  $107 got us a sushi roll, two appetizers, two entrees, a kid's meal, and two desserts.  Our server was Halle.  The restaurant is probably one of the prettiest and fanciest I've ever been in.  They have real cloth tablecloths, proper glasses for each beverage, and a whole lineup of silverware where I never know which one to use next.  They have unbeatable views of the white sandy beaches of Clearwater.  

My only gripe with this visit is the timing.  They had one waitress for the entire restaurant.  Our poor waitress was busting her hump serving every single table inside and outside.  She was a true professional and never looked frazzled or lost her sunny demeanor.  But the night went like this: 
Got seated...waited 15 minutes...got our order taken...waited 15 minutes...free edamame was brought to the table....waited 15 minutes....first appetizers came out...wait 15 minutes...appetizer plates were cleared...wait 15 minutes...entrees brought out...wait 15 minutes...entree plates cleared...wait 15 minutes...order dessert...wait 15 minutes...dessert plates cleared...wait 15 minutes...ask for check....wait 15 minutes.  You may think I'm exaggerating but I'm not.  It took F-O-R-E-V-E-R to eat here.  I feel sorry for our server because I know it's not her fault...the management should really make sure there is more than one waitress on a busy Saturday night. 

My appetizer was an $18 "spiced jumbo prawn" which came with a pile of cold brown noodles and a green puree of some kind.  The prawn was hot but the noodles were cold which is kinda weird and I didn't like that.  The prawn itself was delicious...hot and a little spicy and perfectly grilled to a succulent finish.  But, ya'll, come on, 18 bucks for one fancy-pants shrimp is kinda crazy.  If you're going to charge that price you really should add another prawn or drop the price altogether.  It feels like a ripoff.  

Husband got the $16 tiger roll which had tempura shrimp, asparagus, and salmon.  He is still talking about how good it was today!  I tried a bite and thought it was wonderful as well.  They brought out my son's entree at the same time which I thought was very thoughtful.  He had the $7 kid's hot dog and I asked for fruit instead of fries.  The fruit was really something to behold...it looked like the fruit was expertly sliced by the sushi chef.  All the fruit was perfectly ripe and they gave him a great variety with pineapple, honeydew, cantaloupe, strawberries, blueberries, and watermelon.  Worth every penny.  

For my entree I had the $16 pork belly ramen.  The presentation was stunning because all the dry ingredients were placed artfully in a bowl and then the food runner poured the broth over the ingredients in front of my face at the table from a tiny red teapot.  The pork belly had me over the moon...it was freshly cooked and tender and I'm still thinking about it today.  Unfortunately the noodles were a mushy mess and the broth was HORRIBLE.  It tasted like 2 parts soy sauce and one part water...in-edibly salty!  I just picked out the pork belly and the eggs and some noodles and then pushed it to the side. 

Husband had the $30 Peking duck breast which is served with two rolled-up tortillas and dubbed "duck tacos".  I know ya'll are tired of hearing about me bitching about the prices here but come on...30 bucks for one duck breast and two tortillas?  This entree needs to be about $24 honestly.  I will have to say that husband was very pleased with his dish and had no complaints.  

Desserts are $10 each (not printed anywhere on the menu) and we tried the creme brulee and the chocolate mousse.  Both were gorgeous and tasty.  The creme brulee was very thick and tighter than any custard I've had before.  I wish they would have added more sugar on top and bruleed it properly.  I was missing that "crack" through the hard shell that I normally get with creme brulee.  

At the end of the night I was feeling like this was a 3-star experience but I would never complain.  Our waitress must have known it was less than stellar because she brought the bill with an adjustment.  Even in her overworked state she was observant and thoughtful enough to do that for us without us even saying anything.  That's why I bumped it up one star.  

Upscale, romantic, and the food has the potential to be great.  Hopefully you have better luck than I did and go on a night when they are properly staffed.

I'm such a sucker for mid century interior design that they could have served me a white dog turd and I'd still give it 5 stars. 

Visited on 12-15-19 at 12pm. The interior is like a 60s diner with formica tables, chrome barstools, incredible tiled floors, and they have these awesome MCM chandeliers. I love everything about it. $28.32 got us a kids meal, a chocolate milk, a piece of pie, a burger, and fries. Our server Breeze was friendly and attentive. 

I had the $12.25 royale with cheese wrapped in lettuce. It had onions, fried egg, tomato, bacon, cheese, mushrooms, and a juicy burger patty. I loved every bite. Their fries were hot and crispy and had a delicious seasoning on them. 

For dessert we split the butterscotch pie which was really rich and decadent and didn't taste at all how I'd expected. I was thinking it would be like butterscotch pudding but it was more like a caramel...like sweetened condensed milk that's been heated. It's topped with some sort of marshmallow fluff. It's amazing. 

When the building looks this cool...you can coast on the food but this place doesn't!

So...disclaimer...I am not a fan of chicago-style foods normally.  I don't want a soggy beef sandwich or a gigantic pizza that's five inches thick and raw in the middle or tomatoes on my hot dog.   However, so many people recommended this place that I had to try it so I stopped by on 12/3/16 at 11:30 AM.  

The first thing I  noticed is how adorable the decor in this place is.  It is decorated with Chicago-esque items, old cars, antiques, and 1930's prohibition items.  There is counter-height seating, booths, tables, and they also have a drive-thru.  The menu is mainly salads, sandwiches, hot dogs, and ribs.  

$25.25 got us a small side salad which came with a piece of baguette and butter, a hot dog, a fruit cup, a slice of chocolate cake, a soft drink, and a beef sandwich.  After ordering we sat at a table and waited for our order # to be called.  I like the amusing way in which they shout out the order numbers..."NUMBER 27! COME GET YOUR PIECE OF HEAVEN!.....NUMBER 35! YOUR FOOD HAS ARRIVED!"    They scream the order numbers at the top of their lungs on a speaker system so there's no way you'll miss it.  

My husband got a beef sandwich on a croissant and offered me a bite.  I was expecting a soggy sack of shit but this sandwich was....remarkably crave-able.  The beef was plentiful and tender...perfectly seasoned and hot!  Each bite had a nice bit of crunchy and spicy peppers in it.  I can see why people like this.  If I ever ordered one for myself I'd get it on the regular bread instead of the croissant which is very rich and buttery.  

I got the hot dog with all the fixins....tomato, celery salt, pickle, relish, onions, and mustard.  The bun was nice and fresh and covered in poppy seeds.  The weenie was cooked well and had a nice crunch to the outside of it.  It was quite possibly one of the best hot dogs I've ever had. Pairing it with the crinkle cut fries was perfect and they were served hot and fresh.  The guy at the table next to me had a cup of nacho cheese to dip his fries in which I will definitely try next time. 

Their "famous" chocolate cake was a bit dry but had good flavor.  I wouldn't order it again but it was a pleasant enough experience.  The side salad was probably one of the best "fast food" salads I've ever had.  It had spring mix, romaine, chopped cucumbers, tomatoes, and cabbage.  Their ranch was a pre-packaged commercial ranch which was thick and not tasty.  I'd definitely try a different dressing next time. 

I can see why this place is always so busy.  Cheap, fast, delicious, unique, and consistent chain restaurants are hard to find.  My only complaint is that they have no kids menu whatsoever.  I really wish they'd think about adding one but other than that I was very pleased.  I'll be back.

Average ramen and good sushi at above-average prices. 

Visited on 4-27-19 at 4pm. $50.45 got us a bowl of ramen, some edamame, two sushi rolls, two beers, and a kids drink. Our server Christy was fast and friendly. 

I had the $13 kiwami ramen which had a tonkotsu base, egg, corn, chasu, menma, scallion, and ginger.  The noodles are the thinner variety which I am not a fan of although they were plentiful. The broth was transparent and savory, not milky and complex like a real tonkotsu broth. The pork was paper-thin and fatty but had a nice smoky flavor. I'm not a fan of ginger in ramen and this bowl was full of it. 

I do not like sushi at all but I tried my husband's $12 yummy roll and it was fantastic. It had tempura shrimp, avocado, spicy tuna, and spicy mayo wrapped in pink soy paper. I'd gladly eat a whole roll by myself. It had 8 pieces...$1.60 per bite. 

I ordered a kid's coke for the boy and it was $2.50 which I think is a little ridiculous. Also my bottled Sapporo Light was $5 which is nuts cuz you can get a whole six pack at total wine for $9.79. 

It's not bad but they'd have to make some price adjustments before I'd go back.

Classic diner with affordable and fantastic food.  

Visited on 12/9/17 at 5PM.   The outside of this place doesn't look very exciting.  It's surrounded by newly gentrified stupid hipster gastropubs with dumb names... but looks decidedly plain from the outside.  The inside is clean and cozy.  Service is fast and friendly.   $19 got us two adult entrees and a pancake.  

I had the $2.99 dinner salad and the $4.79 chicken wings.  The five chicken wings were delicious.  They were cooked perfectly...crispy on the outside and juicy and tender on the inside.  They were served piping hot with just the right amount of zesty mild sauce on them.  Their ranch dressing is incredibly good...it's that real watery kind which I love.  There's nothing worse than getting a nice salad and having some disgusting Hidden Valley shit.  I throw that shit right where it belongs- in the TRASH.  

My kiddo got the $2.99 "mini pancake" which was actually a ginormous pancake.  It was huge and fluffy and cooked perfectly.  I was able to snag a bite (okay, maybe 4 bites) and loved every second of it.  It's one of the top five best pancakes I've ever tried for sure.  My husband really enjoyed his french onion soup and BST sandwich.  A BST is a "bacon, spinach, and tomato" sandwich.  

I wasn't expecting much out of this place but was pleasantly surprised.  Every element of the dinner was perfectly executed.  I'll definitely be back.

Finally found a casual, traditional ramen-ya in Tampa! With real Japanese people working there! OMG!  

Visited on Wednesday 3/15/17 around 6PM.  $48.73 got us three soft drinks, edamame, two bowls of ramen, and a slice of crepe cake.  From some of the reviews I thought it was going to be tiny inside but the space was fairly large with booths, tables, and even a large bar.  Our waiter was incredibly kind and efficient. 

My dumb ass spilled my oolong tea all over the bar and our waiter was super nice about it and cleaned it up right away and even brought me a replacement tea on the house which I thought was hella nice.  

I got the $13 tonkotsu ramen which came with thin noodles, one medium-sized slice of chasu, menma, scallions, and a huge pile of ginger.  First of all, I *despise* the thin noodles...they were like angel hair pasta!Nowhere on the menu did it mention the thin noodles.  I glared at my husband jealously as he chowed down on his regular ramen noodles in his Abura Soba bowl.  The chasu was tender and tasty and the broth was wonderful...milky, porky, complex, and piping hot!  The thing that ruined the bowl for me was the huge pile of ginger.  There was so much of it that halfway through the bowl the broth had turned pink and my palette was ruined because ginger was all I could taste.  

Next time I would get the same dish but substitute thick noodles instead of the thin noodles, add extra chasu, add two marinated eggs, ask for NO GINGER, and then see if they have corn to add to it.  This dish is about $3 too expensive in my opinion but with these substitutes it could be worth it.  

Could be 5 stars...will have to wait and see! But for now, I'm a fan.

I disliked the Tampa location and I dislike this one too. Another restaurant capitalizing on that one time they were on the food network...trying to make 100 instagram-worthy dishes and failing with the execution. 

Visited on 6-13-20 at 4pm. $79.04 got us two adult entrees, two alcoholic beverages, one kids meal, and an appetizer. Our server Megan was very attentive and nice. Looks like they've made some renovations on everything but the bathrooms and they're still sticky, warm, dark, and mis-matched. There's a tiny little sad glass-front cooler at the front with some sweaty cakes and cupcakes lazily decorated. 

We started out strong with the $10 "nom noms" which are soft pretzel sticks with mustard and warm cheese dip. The pretzels were hot and soft, clearly freshly cooked. The mustard was nice and sharp and the cheese dip was warm and decadent. 5 stars all the way. 

I had the $12 "cluck yeah!" sandwich which had Nashville hot chicken, lettuce, and pickles on a fresh challah bun. The chicken was room temperature and dry. The pickles are some kind of thin, home-made variety with very little flavor. A chik-fil-a sandwich would have been 1000x better....at least it would have been warm and moist.
