The chips were really great, however, hot and crispy, salty and sweet. Like the best BBQ chips you've ever had. 

My husband had the $13 "Havana hottie" sandwich which the menu said had pulled pork, ham, Swiss cheese, dill pickle and Honeycup mustard. The menu doesn't say anything about horseradish but my husband said it was "absolutely smothered" in horseradish. I thought maybe it was the Honeycup mustard but I googled that and I can't find any reports of it being spicy and there is no horseradish in the ingredients list. Two bites in and he was sweating. Four bites and he was coughing. He loves spicy food but there was so much of whatever this sauce was it had to be a mistake.

When it was time for the bill instead of getting an itemized receipt, a card-reader was thrust in front of us. There was no total on the screen...I guess you're just supposed to trust them? And no receipt was given. The tip suggestion for 20% was twenty dollars...math seems a bit off for a bill that (probably) totaled less than 80. I still don't know how much the drinks were. Seems sketchy and I didn't appreciate it. 

It's a one and done for me.

I loved it. 

Visited on 11-17-19 at 12pm. $34.45 got us one beer, a kid's meal, a bottle of root beer, and one adult entree. Service from Jordan was efficient and professional. 

I told Jordan I wanted a beer but I'm boring and only like Bud Light and he was nice enough to let me sample three of their light ales without me even asking! I ended up choosing a pint of the Double Coast lime lager for $6.75 and it was really good. Not too hoppy, not too bitter...really great. 

Very rarely do I eat meat these days but I heard about this burger called "the bomb" on DDD. It's a burger with bacon, cheddar cheese, and fried onion straws which is wrapped in pizza dough and then baked. It's greasy, it's salty, it's cheesy, the bread is hot and fresh...honestly maybe one of the best things I've ever eaten. I've tried several items from the show and very few of them have lived up to the hype...but this $14 burger is worth every penny. The horseradish ale sauce paired perfectly and was great for dipping the fries into as well. The fries were also hot and crispy and my favorite thick pub variety. 

Kiddo had the $7 kids pepperoni pizza which was absolutely enormous, baked perfectly, and overflowing with gooey cheese and huge pepperoni. (pepperonis? what's the plural form??) This pie is perfect in every way. I adore their crust. 

The parking situation in downtown Ybor gives me anxiety but for a meal like this I'd definitely return. Can't wait to bring my husband here.

*military discount*

This place is pretty unique...you can build your own mongolian stir fry! I visited this place for the first time on Saturday 12/24/2016.  When I checked in a coupon popped up for 2 regular bowls with drinks for $24 so we decided to do that.

From the other reviews I had assumed that this was a fast-casual-counter-service-typa-place but to my surprise there is a hostess and you do get seated.  Then the waiter comes around and you can order their house dishes or build your own dish.  Our waiter, James, was extremely knowledgeable, friendly, and helped explain all the options to us.  I ordered the build it yourself bowl and James gave me a small receipt to give to the grill guy (be sure and take that with you!!!) 

I had read all the reviews and tips online...people get really serious about piling their bowls as high as possible so as to get the biggest bang for their buck.  I tried the most common hack which is to put your meat in the bowl and then stick snow peas in the meat to make the sides of the bowl extend and then pack it with veggies and then more meat on top, then dry seasonings, then put the sauce on the side in the little bowl provided.  

After I loaded my bowl to look like the leaning tower of Pisa I carefully took it over to the grill.  Now this grill is unlike anything I've ever seen before...it's huge and flat and round and SPINS.  There are sticks separating each person's order.  The grill guy asked which two starches I wanted and I picked white rice and fried rice.  They also have lo mein noodles, spiral noodles, and brown rice.  

In a few minutes my bowl was delivered and HOLY CRAP it was enough food for 4 people.  I think next time I'd definitely do the small bowl....even the kid's size bowl was huge.  I really enjoyed this unique and healthy dinner experience!

Wasn't impressed the first time but lately they've been getting some great reviews so I thought I'd give them another try. 

Visited on 04/06/2018 at 12:15 PM.  $8.51 got us an order of chicken tacos and two cups of water. 

I had the $7.95 chicken tacos which came with grilled chicken, corn salsa, avocado, sour cream, and fresh limes.  The chicken was good but the rest was awful.  The avocado was brown and rancid.  There was just way too much corn salsa and it had small pieces of ice in it like it had been in the back of the refrigerator or something.

It was pretty hard to eat because we were never given silverware or napkins.  

I don't understand all the 5 star reviews.

A beloved Tampa bakery that's been open over a hundred years.

Visited on 6-16-19 at 3pm. $4.44 got us one cupcake and a coconut macaroon. Service was fast and friendly! 

The macaroon wasn't toasted very well...maybe not cooked long enough? It was really greasy and sugary. Not my favorite but edible. My child who has a mouth full of sweet tooths took 2 bites of his cupcake and declared he was full.

I couldn't get a feel for what type of bakery this is...they seem to cater to all genres of baked goods. Italian cookies, Hispanic favorites, soul food goodies, caucasian girl Instagram cupcakes...they had it all. 

They have cold sicilian pizza which comes pre-sliced in a box and apparently it's a real hit at parties. I also saw some really cool sampler trays with just a tiny bite of each type of cake they offer. 

Parking is hectic (traffic has changed in the last 100 years lol) and it's a bit dark inside. The fake display cakes are old and faded and dusty which makes em' look creepy. I give them props for the sheer variety of items but they look better than they taste.

Sad and expensive middle eastern food. 

Visited on 3/9/18 at 12:25PM. $11.75 got me a lunch platter and a fountain drink.  You order at the counter and they give you a number then bring your food out when it's ready. The restaurant has the most gorgeous light fixtures inside! Very unique ones unlike anything I've seen before. 

I had the $8.99 shish tawook lunch platter and chose rice and french fries for my sides. There were 5 small chunks of dried up chicken. Seriously the corners of the chicken were so hard I had to tear them off. My kiddo spit his out. The fries were room temperature and soggy. The best part about the meal was the rice which was hot and cooked well. For this meal I waited 23 minutes so beware if you're in a time crunch or here on your lunch break. 

The fountain drink was $1.99 which is too expensive in my opinion. It's not even a cool or modern soda fountain...it's one of those old school deals with 6 options.  The cups are over by the soda fountain and you just help yourself. 

There's a few other things I didn't like but I'm not gonna be nit-picky. Lunch should be fast and tasty - period. And my lunch was neither.

A brewery so cool and popular that they can treat you however they want. 

Visited on 9-6-20 at 5pm. $36.87 got us two adult entrees and a kid's meal. The hostess told us it would be a 20 minute wait and gave us a buzzer. She said we could wait upstairs and grab a beer....so we did just that. She took us inside and showed us the elevator. The decor is really cool and industrial...the building looks like an old warehouse. They have a gift shop out front and bottled/canned beers to-go in a cooler. 

The moment we got our $7 beers (about 3 minutes after getting there) the buzzer went off. So we waddled back downstairs to our table. We told our server we opened a tab upstairs and asked if he could close it out or do we need to go back upstairs and do it? And he started looking around the restaurant and gave a really vague and confusing answer...mumbled he "might" be able to "try" to....so my husband went upstairs and closed it out himself.

They were out of chicken so I ordered the Greek sandwich with falafel. I asked our server if I could have the kale caesar instead of fries and he spent a good 30 seconds explaining why it would be tricky to get that request done. He said if he put that in the computer the kitchen would probably just make a regular house salad with caesar dressing so if I wanted the kale caesar he'd have to walk back to the kitchen to explain it to them. Then he just stared at me. So I said something along the lines of "well I don't want to be a bother...a normal house salad is fine" and he waved his hand and said he'd make sure I got the kale caesar.

48 minutes later the food finally arrived. We hadn't seen our server in that time so I begged the runner for some water for our child. I was given a normal house salad with caesar dressing, not the kale salad that I requested. The falafels were good but room temperature. The pita was raw and cold so I ended up just dipping the falafels in the whipped feta and tossing the bread aside.  My husband said his burger was room temperature and the fries were rock hard, soaked in grease, and cold. 

I could forgive slow service, and crappy brewery food, but I can't forgive service that is snarky and innatentive. When we left, our server was on the outside patio sitting down with 3 guys laughing....is that where he was for 48 minutes while our food sat there and got cold?

Hipster bar with fancy food that you need a password to get into. 

Visited on 9/22/17 at 6PM. $94.16 got us three happy hour cocktails and two entrees. I gotta preface this review by telling you I wanted to go to Bern's for my anniversary but my husband decided this place would be more fun. 

The decor is nice...lots of dark wood and low lighting. They have some cool private booths with curtains but apparently you have to specify that you want to sit in those when you make your reservations. We sat at a high top table near the bar with a gigantic round fish tank behind us that was completely dark and empty and a little creepy. 

Honestly nothing on the menu looked good to me when I went. Half of the items were raw like a cheese plate, oysters, steak tartare, etc. which are too elegant for my unrefined palate. They had octopus, popcorn, a plate of rice, and duck legs. Super weird and honestly none of it sounded appealing. 

For an appetizer we got the $17 shrimp cocktail which had 5 shrimp. $3 for each shrimp is pretty pricey for average small cocktail shrimp. The shrimp were good and they were served with crostinis and a nice little bowl of homemade cocktail sauce. Normally fancy restaurants really throw the horseradish into their cocktail sauces but this one was very mild...almost like ketchup with chunks of lemon zest in it. 

I had the $36 "steak frites" which came with the skinniest new york strip steak I've ever seen and a cup full of limp, soggy, room temperature fries. On the plate they had set a piece of rosemary on fire just before serving and the smoke was choking me. 

I'm obviously not cool enough for this place. The concept is very neat, however I would not go back.

*military discount*

Visited on 7/15/17 at 6PM.  This restaurant sits in an un-assuming strip mall next to Aldi and has blackout-tinted windows so I was shocked when I walked in and was transported to a modern yet traditional Thai restaurant.  The lighting is dim and each table has a candle and the ambiance is romantic and classy.  They have gorgeous wood carved tables, wall decor, and fresh flowers everywhere you look.  It is truly spectacular inside and the ladies who work there wear the most gorgeous dresses.  $30.76 got us an order of chicken satay, a curry entree, two bottles of water, and an order of pad see ew.  

We ordered the $6.95 "sateh chicken" for my boy.  I've only ever seen it called chicken satay but whatevs...It came with an order of 4 chicken skewers.  They were nicely seasoned and well cooked.  They came with a peanut dipping sauce and a tasty ramekin of fresh pickled vegetables.  My son enjoyed it a lot.  I really think they could come down on the price by a lot or add more skewers to each order because $1.75 each for a stringy ounce of chicken on a skewer seems kinda ridiculous.  

I got the $11 pad see ew which is what I usually get at Thai restaurants.  It's kind of the benchmark for me and by now I know pretty much what it will look and taste like...but this place threw me for a loop.  The noodles, instead of being wok-cooked and slightly dry were swimming in a weird brown gravy.  It smelled like my grandma's house and tasted so weird.  The chicken was plentiful and it had carrots which I've never seen before in a pad see ew but they were good.  I thought it was kinda weird that they used regular broccoli instead of chinese broccoli, too. 

I am rounding up a lot since my husband loved his curry and the decor is so nice.  I'd probably go back...next time I'd try the pineapple fried rice.

Visited on 5/18/17 around 7PM.  This place is very cute inside and reminds me of an old fashioned soda shop with their big wrap-around counter and tiled floors.  It looks like they have a big variety of treats like donuts, ice cream, cakes, coffees, milkshakes, brownies, and cheesecakes.  

They had some adorable cupcakes in their glass case.  Some of them were totally instagram-worthy...such as one that had blue piped clouds and a candy rainbow!  I even saw a few that looked like they'd been piped with russian piping tips.  Pretty neat.  

We had just eaten next door but I wanted a little something sweet so I selected two macarons which were quickly retrieved from the freezer.  $4.82 is a little steep for two frozen macarons.  Save yourself the trouble and get a whole box at Sam's Club for $10.  

My biggest gripe with this place is there is a line on the receipt for a tip.  When a restaurant has counter service only I do not expect to be solicited for a tip.  Honestly....it's pretty tacky.  

I wouldn't go out of my way to come back.  I am giving extra points for how cute the place is, cleanliness, and cuteness of their pastries.

Un-Pho-King-Believably good. 

Visited on Sunday 2-11-18 at 12:30pm. $13.80 got us a kids bowl of pho and an order of fried rice. Service is somewhat slow but adequate and friendly for how busy they are. 

The building itself is a bit neglected...they still had their Christmas decorations up. It's not the cleanest restaurant I've ever been in...especially the bathrooms. And there's a weird abandoned fish tank right as you walk in the door full of algae. But the delicious food certainly makes up for the ambiance. 

The $4.95 baby size chicken pho comes with noodles, broth, and chicken chunks. The chicken was freshly cooked and juicy and the noodles were perfectly cooked. The broth was very mild and not very herbal like most I've had. I liked it a lot...but I'm not a purist. 

The $7.95 chicken fried rice was absolutely delicious. It had big chunks of freshly cooked juicy chicken, peas, carrots, egg, onion, and bean sprouts. It had a slightly charred umami flavor that made it delightfully crave-worthy and the bean sprouts were still crunchy. I give it 5 stars! 

Perhaps it's a little dingy and a little too Americanized but enjoyable nonetheless. I'd definitely go back.

The CRG does it again. Shut up and take my money! 

Think of this place like a hipster chipotle or a mexican Fresh Kitchen. 

We ate here on 9-22-19 at 11:30am. $28.25 got us a bowl, quesadillas, a dip trio, and a drink. I spent about an hour this morning memorizing what I wanted cuz' I hate being some annoying noob clogging up the line at a confusing place like this for the first time. The man who took my order did not ease my anxiety because he made me repeat myself twice for each ingredient, was unfamiliar with the ingredients, I had to remind him of ingredients, and was generally bewildered. Maybe it was his first day? I thought I was prepared but this dude made it so stressful. 

I had the $9.91 "all in" bowl and chose the chilled super greens and avocado rice for the base, the sweet potato mescla and black beans as the veggies, steak and orange chicken for the proteins, cotija cheese and sour cream for the "Mexi things", and I have no idea which sauce I got but it was yellow and very mild. The bowl was fantastic! Very fresh and full of nutritious quality ingredients. I give this bowl 5 stars! 

The queso was warm and heavenly. The salsa is a strange color ( like orange transparent barf) but it tastes phenomenal. The guac is fresh and full of big chunks of avocado. The chips are a little on the thick side but enjoyable.

I'd rather go to FK honestly but this place was really good.

I love you, Trader Joe's. I love you so much. 

This location is so busy they have their own parking lot attendant. They have a ton of overly friendly employees ready to help you. Seriously they're like deranged stepford flight attendants and I'm here for it. They must be getting paid well because they act RIGHT.

Everything is always well stocked, clean, and they have two squeaky clean gender-neutral restrooms. Free coffee and samples all day errrrrday. I've heard that they'll pretty much let you try anything if you ask nicely but I've never tried it. 

I come here for the flowers, snacks, wine, dried fruits, and frozen entrees. They won't have everything on your list, but you'll leave with things you didn't know you needed. Each product is the perfect blend of ethical, high quality, and low price. 

You can return anything, even if it's been open or tried. This gives me peace of mind because I think if lots of one thing was getting returned, the big wigs would get rid of it, so in turn I believe that most things in the store will be tasty. 

They care. It shows. I like.

It always warms my little heart to give a good update to a review.  My stone cold tiny little grinch heart grew three sizes today after giving this place another chance.  

Visited on 4/7/18 at 1PM.  $37.45 got us a frittata, a steak & grits entree, and a kid's meal.  Our server, Rebecca, was fast and friendly even as she trained another staff member.  

I had the $15 "steak & grits" which came with mushrooms, leeks, two scrambled eggs, grits, and boca gravy.  The steak was absolutely heavenly...cooked perfectly to medium and tender enough to cut with a fork.  It was so flavorful and juicy I was savoring every bite.  The scrambled eggs were nice and buttery, salty, and ever-so-fluffy.  The grits were pretty fantastic...they were a bigger texture than what I'm used to but I loved them.  I'm still not a big fan of their gravy...I'm not sure what they put in it but it tastes very strong and bitter...almost fermented?  Like they use blue cheese or wine in the gravy.  It ain't my thing but you might like it.  

Kiddo had the $8 bacon and eggs plate which came with scrambled eggs, one piece of bacon, a random slice of french bread, and a pile of tasty roasted potatoes.  Everything was cooked well and very yummy. 

Their gender neutral restrooms were impeccably clean and well stocked as always.  It's always a real treat to find clean restrooms when you're a germaphobe like me.  

I always try to give places more than one chance and I'm glad I was able to bump this place up a star.

Fresh hot donuts served out of an airstream trailer. 

Visited on 8-2-19 at 10am. $3 got us four of the cutest little donuts I've ever seen.

They were served warm and fresh! From the instagram photos I assumed they were in a case or something and you just choose which ones you want but I was wrong. They are fried up and then decorated and served warm. 

I didn't try them but my kiddo ate 2 of them with zero complaints which is saying a lot for a picky 5-year-old. I could hand him ice cream covered in chocolate and he would find something to complain about so the fact that he sat there in silence and ate two of them says a lot. 

They have three little tables outside which is nice. Unfortunately it's been raining like crazy here and the seating area was flooded. It was a bagillion degrees out so hopefully I can come back when it's drier and cooler.

Like a fast casual Panda Express.

Visited on 4-25-19 at 5:30PM. $31.40 got us a kids meal, two adult entrees, and two soft drinks. Order at the counter, take a number, find a table, they'll bring out the food. You know the drill. 

I had the $7.99 wok tossed fresh vegetables with tofu. It had zucchini, mushrooms, carrots, snow peas, and broccoli. I chose brown rice as my side and it came with a big tasty egg roll. The tofu was crispy on the outside and the veggies were tender...a bit overly sauced for my taste but still very good. 

Not bad at all. I enjoyed it. If you're craving Chinese and want something a little more upscale than Panda you'll enjoy it here.

Pho-king delicious. 

Visited on 5/21/17 around 6PM because I was craving some pho!  $20.32 got me a medium bowl of pho, a baby bowl of pho, and a can of Pepsi to drink.  As soon as you walk in the door there is a big tropical plant in your face!  You have to duck underneath it and then you can sit anywhere you like.  

Our waitress was so funny and charming.  Probably my favorite waitress I've ever had.  I wish I had thought to get her name for this review.  I placed my order and not 5 minutes later our food was in front of us which is a sign of a good pho place.  

I got the $9.50 medium sized meatball pho and asked for no veggies and it was perfect.  The broth was piping hot, but not burn-your-mouth hot.  It was so complex, herbal, spicy, salty...mmmm heavenly!  The noodles were plentiful and so were the meatballs.  The medium bowl was too much for me!  I think next time I would get the small or the baby size. My eyes were bigger than my belly.  

For my boy I got the $5.95 baby size chicken pho with no veggies.  It was perfect for a toddler because it was just broth, noodles, and shredded chicken.  I like that their bowls are priced by size....no matter which combination of meats you get it's the same price.  I've never seen that at a pho place before.  

This place is legit.

Fancy-schmancy building, killer location, above-average steaks and seafood. 

Visited on 5-15-18 at 4PM. This place is located right on the riverwalk next to the waterworks park. There is some street parking but they have a huge parking lot about 500 feet down the street on the other side of the road. It's surrounded by lush grass, trees, and fronted by the most gorgeous little marsh full of fish, aquatic plants, birds, and turtles. No expense has been spared inside...seriously I'm sure this cost millions to build. Every single thing looks like it was custom made for this place. I'd run out of space tryin to describe just how beautiful and clean it is so I won't even try.  Bravo! 

$43.87 got us 6 charbroiled oysters, a chicken salad, a cup of chili, a kids meal, and a coconut ice cream dessert. Service was cordial and efficient. 

I had the  $15 charbroiled oysters and LOVED them. There were six fresh oysters on the half shell which were smothered in garlic butter and parmesan & romano cheeses then charbroiled under a barbacoa grill. Each one was tiny and would have easily fit in a teaspoon without touching the sides but boyyyyy were they delicious! I got the smoky flavor from the grill, the richness from the butter, a hint of bitter from the cheese, then the luxuriously tender oyster just melts in your mouth. My only gripe is they served 5 crostinis with 6 oysters and there were several pieces of shell in 1 of mine which is no fun to find with your molars so chew carefully. I would eat this even if I didn't like oysters...it's truly legendary. 

For dessert we split the coconut ice cream and I nearly shat my pants it was so good. Velvety, creamy, perfectly softened, and a generous portion. The flavor is delicate and natural but incredibly strong. I found myself closing my eyes and savoring each bite. Next time I'm just ordering 5 of these and not sharing. Seriously one of the best things I've ever eaten and the 3rd best ice cream I've ever had. 

It's nice to find a place that lives up to the hype.

I saw this place from the road the other day and there was a line around the building and I asked my husband what the sign said and he said "farmer's market" and I was like there is no way people are lining up for fruits and veggies LOL 

So I hopped on my trusty Yelp app to see what all the fuss is about and I just KNEW I had to come here for one of their famous strawberry shortcakes.  Finally nagged my husband enough to where he caved and brought me here on 2-20-17 around 10AM.  This is a good time to come because there was no line...yay! 

I got the $4 number one which is a classic strawberry shortcake with whipped cream.  The strawberries were sliced thin and macerated with sugar and so fresh.  I did not care for the cake which had a consistency like cornbread but was more savory than sweet...less like cake and more like a biscuit.  The best part was the mountain of real whipped cream on top.  I could eat a five gallon bucket of that stuff by itself!  

They have a really nice greenhouse that has picnic tables to eat at and after we were done we perused the marked.  They sell jams, veggies, fruits, and various t-shirts and knick-knacks.  None of it was overpriced at all which was a refreshing surprise for a tourist attraction like this.  

Now I know what all the fuss is about.  Next time I wanna try the strawberry milkshake!

*25% military discount* 

Visited on 4/21/17 around 6:30 PM.  $34.22 got us two adult dinners, a queso dip appetizer, and a margarita.  I love the decor in this place...it's kind of like an industrial cantina and has flags from a lot of states and countries hanging from the ceiling.  They have an open area where you can watch the tortillas being made!  And I absolutely love their little 1950's turquoise chairs and aluminum-bordered tables.  

Right as we were seated they brought us a big basket of fresh and hot chips and two bowls of delicious salsa.  We ordered a $6.99 bowl of white queso which came next and OMG I almost put a straw in that bowl and drank the whole thing.  It was amazing!!!  And it came with 4 fresh hot tortillas that they must have just made because they melted in my mouth and made me wanna cry.  I loved every bite.  

I got the $11.04 "pick two" combo and chose a chicken tamale and a chicken enchilada.  It comes with rice and for my side I picked refried beans (when in Rome).  Everything was nice and hot and pretty darn good.  My only complaint would be the masa to chicken ratio on the tamale was a little off but it was still great.  

My husband got the $9.99 top shelf margarita and I nearly died when they brought out this tiny margarita in a tulip glass.  I tried a few sips and I really don't think they put the good stuff in there and it was clearly bottled margarita mix...ya know the kind that makes your mouth pucker and gives you horrible heartburn later?  I think this cocktail is about $2 too expensive and would it really kill ya'll to invest in some margarita glasses?  Come on, now.  

Overall I liked this place a lot.  I'd definitely go back.

My husband said "Baby imma take you to Chili's but don't be lookin' at them expensive steaks in the back of the menu cuz' we gonna do the 2 for 22 deal" and I said HELLZ YES and hopped into the passenger side of his F-250 diesel ready for a hot date.  We sped out of the trailer park so fast we kicked up a dust cloud a mile high.  I was praying I didn't drop any food on my Reba McIntyre shirt cuz' I don't wanna ruin it. 

Visited on 4/14/17 around 8PM.  $34.87 got us a 2 for $22 deal and we chose 2 house salads for the app, husband got a burger, and I got fajitas.  We also got a  Sprite, a side of fruit, and an additional appetizer of queso because we are fatties.  Our server was very friendly an efficient and took care of us very well.  

$7.59 "loaded queso" appetizer is served in a cute little skillet and consists of queso, guacamole, cotija cheese, shredded cheddar, seasoned ground beef, and cilantro.  It comes with a big pile of the hottest freshest saltiest yummiest chips you'll ever have and also a lovely side of their delicious salsa.  The queso itself was not so great...it tasted less like cheese and more like a creamy alfredo sauce.  I am not a fan.  

My house salad was a good size and came with spring mix, onions, shredded cheese, tomatoes, croutons, cucumbers, and I chose ranch dressing.  The ranch was phenominal...it's the real watery kind which I love.  The cucumbers were frozen which was kind of a turn off. It didn't ruin my hot date, though.  

I got the carnitas fajitas which came with a big pile of carnitas on an iron skillet and I chose to have it "loaded" by adding queso and tomatoes.  It came with 4 tortillas, sour cream, shredded cheese, tomatoes, and guacamole.  I like fajitas cuz' it's kinda like a "build-your-own" type of thing and I dig it.  Only want a little cheese?  Go for it!  Don't like tomatoes?? Don't put em' on there!  

Luckily I didn't spill anything on my Reba shirt and had a wonderful date at Chili's.

I been eyeballin' this place for a long time...patiently waiting for this 8 million dollar tiki-themed riverside restaurant to open...finally they're open! No opening night jitters here...the place was thoroughly organized and the staff plentiful and well trained. 

Visited on 9-13-20 at 4:30PM. $71.03 got us an appetizer, a kids meal, an adult entree, and two alcoholic beverages. Service from Kristi was fast and friendly. We sat outside and enjoyed the view of the river. 

I had the $14.99 peel & eat shrimp dinner which came with a spiral potato and corn on the cob. The shrimp were cooked perfectly, flavorful, and split down the back for easy peeling. The corn was nothing special...a little mushy so I'm guessing they grill frozen corn for a few minutes. The potato was crispy and covered in a tasty garlic butter. I enjoyed it very much. 

My husband had the $14.99 crabby wings. The wings were huge, seasoned well, fresh, hot, and grilled to perfection.  They were topped with a generous heap of real lump crab meat. Fantastic. 

My kiddo had the $5.50 kids cheeseburger meal which came with a side and a drink. He gobbled it down so it must have been good. I like that they offer fresh watermelon as a healthy alternative to fries. A very good value.

The alcoholic drinks were beautifully presented and garnished, nice and strong...well worth the $7.50 price tag. 

Beautiful restaurant, nice views, excellent service, not too expensive. I'm very sad to be moving away from this.

*military discount* 

Visited on 5/4/17 around 6PM.  $29.54 got me a steak and lobster dinner, a side of fruit, and a caesar salad.  Every time I'm craving steak and lobster I head over to my local Outback Steakhouse....I challenge you to find a better steak and lobster dinner for the price! 

For $27.49 you can get a big juicy steak, a gorgeous steamed lobster tail, and two sides.  The 6 oz. fillet is so tender you can cut it with the side of your fork and so well seasoned you don't even need steak sauce.  The lobster tail is so sweet and succulent and comes with a ramekin full of real drawn butter.  Their baked potatoes are out of this world...not dry at all...silky and smooth as if they were boiled!  And their broccoli is perfectly steamed and buttery and always a generous amount.  

I added a caesar salad to my meal for $2.99 extra because Outback has one of the best I've ever had.  They only use the top of the romaine lettuce so your whole salad is a nice dark green color.  They chop the lettuce into small pieces and very lightly dress it in the most delicious and spicy caesar dressing.  It is truly my favorite caesar salad.

Our server Michaela was prompt and efficient.  It just doesn't get any better than this.  I love steak and lobster dinners at Outback!!!

*military discount* 

Seriously tasty seafood in a casual environment. 

Visited on Sunday 12/18/2016 at 6PM.  I was feeling skeptical due to the sketchy location of the restaurant but inside it's super nice...like a more casual version of Red Lobster.  $59.46 got us a free margarita with yelp check in, a coke, a kid's sprite, a pound of crab legs, a clam strip dinner, and a shrimp taco entree.  

After we ordered an old lady at the table across from us collapsed and had to be carried out.  I secretly hoped I hadn't ordered what she ate.  

I ordered the $10.99 clam strips because I looooooove clams and asked for french fries instead of parsley potatoes.  What arrived was unlike any clam strips I have ever seen before...very skinny and dark in color and clearly hand-breaded.  I guess I have gotten used to the frozen varieties which are thick and slightly chewy.  We didn't eat them and the waitress noticed and took them off the bill without us saying a word.  I appreciated that!  I'm non-confrontational and never mention dining mistakes or bad food at restaurants.  

I also ordered a pound of crab legs for $24.99 (market price) and they were perfect.   They were huge, hot, perfectly cooked, and served with all the butter and lemons my little heart desires.  My husband taught me to squeeze lots of lemon juice into the butter and then dip the crab in and that's my favorite way to enjoy crab now.  I was able to pick my sides so I got rice pilaf and seasonal veggies and both were very good.  

I liked this place a lot and our server was super cool.  I'd definitely go back.

Visited on Saturday 10/29/16 at 8PM.   $84 got us two hibachi dinners and two drinks.  This place is not really a "steak house" but rather a teppenyaki place that also serves sushi and alcoholic beverages as well as desserts.  

We came at a peak time and had to wait about an hour but they have a nice outdoor waiting area with plenty of seating and the weather was nice so it wasn't so bad.  We signed up with the hostess and she gave us a buzzer to alert us when our table was ready. 

We were seated at a double table that had two griddles and seated 15-17 people.  First came the drinks and then the waiter took everybody's order.  I chose the $30 steak & scallop combination.  The waiter took everyone's menus and in a few minutes brought out soup for everyone. 

The soup was touted as an onion soup...the broth was hot and delicious.  It was full of those shitty fried onions that your grandma puts on green bean casseroles and raw mushrooms which I did not enjoy very much.  I think they'd be better off if they'd just use caramelized onions and cook the mushrooms a bit more.  

Next came the salads which were nothing special and looked identical to the bagged iceberg mix you can buy at any grocery store complete with shaved carrots and purple cabbage.  It was doused in a generous amount of ginger dressing which was good but there was just too much of it.  I had to dig pieces of lettuce out of the bowl of dressing and wipe them on my napkin to eat them. 

Next the chef came out and began his routine.  He was young and cute and very good at what he does.  He had a cheesy but good sense of humor and really wowed us with his skills.  He  knew all the good tricks like the fried rice heart, flipping an egg into his hat, flipping a shrimp into his pocket, and of course the onion volcano. 

Fried rice and noodles are served with every entree and they were very tasty.  I loved my steak and scallops and there was SO MUCH FOOD!  Seriously I spent the whole next day trying to eat all the leftovers. 

Our dining companions all raved about a sauce called "yum-yum sauce" which I tried and did not care for much.  It was like somebody added sugar to ranch dressing.  Everyone else at the table was requesting double and triple portions of the stuff and just pouring it all over their food so it's worth a try if you go...you might like it that much too! 

Like any other teppenyaki place, you go for the show and the atmosphere and less for the food but the food was also very good here.  It's a great place to celebrate a special occasion and I enjoyed it enough that I'd definitely go back.

**20% military discount**

Visited on Monday 11-14-16 at 4PM.  The decor is bangin' in this place with vintage Ford products for decorations.  There are many old cars on display and car details can be found all over the restaurant.  My favorite thing was the door handles made from gas pump nozzles...adorable!  

Between 11AM-7PM you can get bloody mary's, margaritas, and a few other drinks for 3 bucks which I thought was a deal until I saw how small they are.  My margarita was served in an 8 oz. glass which was filled to the brim with ice so I maybe got like 5 sips of margarita. You get what you pay for I guess.  They have literally hundreds of beers and cocktails to choose from so whatever you like can be found here.  

$10.95 spinach artichoke dip- more like hot mayonnaise with flecks of spinach.  I did not see a single artichoke in the whole dish.  And it was served with those shitty tri-color tortilla chips from a bag. I was done after 2 bites...can't recommend and I would never order this again here.  

I watched in horror as my husband ordered the $11.95 "jiffy burger" which has peanut butter on it.  And to make matters worse he ordered it medium rare.  I almost gagged watching him eat it.  Raw meat and peanut butter...thanks a lot Derek Jeter....you twisted mofo.  

I got the all-american burger for $10.95 which came with cheddar cheese, a pickle plank, and your choice of a side.  For my side I got the fries and they were good albeit room temperature.  The burger was meh...I like that the patty was thick but I spent the next 8 hours or so burping up this burger.   My delicate tummy did not like this burger and it wasn't even spicy or anything so it makes me wonder if it wasn't very fresh.  

My son got the kid's chicken bites with macaroni.  I fed him a piece of macaroni and he spit it out so I tried it and I'd have to agree with him...it was room temperature and completely devoid of salt.  Chicken bites were undoubtedly from the freezer but were very good.  

So definitely come here for the atmosphere and the booze.  Just be sure to get really drunk before you try the food and you'll be happy here.

I prefer Gold Star but Skyline is pretty darn good.  

Visited on 7/10/17 at 3PM. Our waitress, Devon, was from Cincinnati and although she had many tables to take care of she still made sure we had everything we needed and was super friendly. 

Husband if from Cincinnati and he's the one who introduced me to this delicious phenomenon known as chili spaghetti.   The chili is very unique...it is dark brown and the meat is very finely ground and the sauce is spiced with a tiny bit of cinnamon.  It's unlike anything you've ever tried before and it is good on ANYTHING.  Baked potatoes, noodles, hot dogs, french fries...slather that stuff on an old boot you found on the side of the highway...it'll be delicious...I promise!

But the most magical part of this place....the thing that you cannot replicate at home which keeps you coming back here is the CHEESE.  Their cheese is finely shredded into long strands which make it ridiculously fluffy and light as air.  The cheese is MVP if you ask me.  

My favorite meal to get here is a small three way, two cheese coneys with mustard and onions, and a diet mountain dew. A three way is a dish containing spaghetti noodles on bottom, then topped with that special chili, then smothered in that magical cheese.   It's the perfect amount of food!  

Thank you Skyline for being here in Florida!!  Please build a location in Brandon!!

What do you call the white part at the tops of crab legs?? Hips? Knuckles??

Visited on 6-16-19 at 12:45 PM.  $41.20 got us one entree and a kids meal. Our server Betsy was a true professional waitress...one of those sweet OG ladies who are fast, pay attention to detail, and efficient AF.

I had the $30.99 pound of crab legs which comes with potatoes and slaw but those don't tickle my fancy so I asked for a caesar salad and fried mushrooms instead. 

The salad was crisp, fresh, cold, and dressed perfectly. It had lots of croutons and a generous amount of shredded parmesan. I enjoyed every bite. 

The fried mushrooms were a bit on the mushy side but not bad. The orange sauce that came with it tasted like mayo...I would have preferred a more horseradish-based sauce (i.e. the sauce that comes with the bloomin' onion at Outback).

The crab legs were average sized but fresh and warm. You know that wide white "knuckle" at the top of the claws (if I were to guess I'd say it's the crab's....hips?) anyhoo...there's tons of meat in those little pockets but depending on where you go you have to be cautious on eating that part. Don't try it at a cheap Chinese buffet...it's gonna taste like licking the underside of a barge. I dunno how they prepare them here but you can totally eat the "hips" here because they are sweet and delicious.

Shells delivers another tasty meal.

*military discount*

Visited on 7/29/2017 at 6:30 PM.  We were able to get a table right away in this very nice-looking restaurant.  The lighting is low and the decor is classy which makes for a romantic meal.   $61.26 got us two entrees, two side salads, a margarita, and a side of sweet potato fries.  Our waiter, Brian, was fantastic and anticipated our needs and was incredibly efficient and attentive.

On Yelp it says this place is not good for kids but I'd have to disagree.  We saw lots of kids when we went.  They have a pretty great kid's menu and wiki stix for the young'uns to play with while they wait.    They also bring you a nice basket of warm bread with soft butter which my little one enjoyed.  

I had the $27 twelve ounce prime rib with garlic mashed potatoes.  The meat was cooked perfectly to medium just how I like it.  It was a generous portion and although the flavor was very good the quality of the meat nearly ruined it.  The piece I got was very fatty, tough, and had lots of connective tissue and tendons.  My hand was hurting from cutting the tough meat and my jaws were sore when I left from all the chewing.  The horseradish sauce was so amazing...just the right amount of heat and creaminess!  The garlic mashed potatoes were pretty horrendous.  I scooped up a fork full of the potatoes and they crumbled and fell off the fork.  I've never seen a drier batch of mashed potatoes in my life.  They were gritty and unpleasant.  

Husband had the $16 pork marsala which he said was bland.  They cook the pork medium well which I thought was pretty gross for pork.  Trichinella is nothing to mess with...you basically spew out both ends until you die.  Not pretty, folks.  The sauce was watery and the noodles were overcooked but it had a good flavor.  The crust on the pork was very good.  

Nice setting, great service, iffy food.  For the price I'd say skip it.

When's the last time you drove by a non-chain restaurant and saw a line out the door and a packed parking lot?? That's what drew me into this place...I thought "THIS HAS GOTTA BE GOOD!" and I was right, dammit.  

This place has been open since 1980 but looks really nice inside.  There are a bunch of fish tanks and everything is made from wood and I dig it.   $63.62 got us a prime rib dinner, Jesse's special dinner, a kid's meal, two soft drinks, and a slice of key lime pie.  Our waiter was very quirky and friendly and if I wasn't married to the most handsome man on the planet I might dare say he was easy on the eyes.  After ordering he brought us a nice warm loaf of bread with soft butter which we all enjoyed. 

I had the $22.95 "queen cut" 12 oz. prime rib which came with a caesar salad and a baked potato.  I became kind of a prime rib connoisseur when I lived in Vegas and lemme tell ya this place has got some amazing prime rib.  It was perfectly cooked to medium rare, so tender and juicy!  It was swimming in it's own au jus and served with mushrooms and a nice dollop of horseradish sauce.   After one bite I felt like a cave man and just wanted to grab it up and sit in the corner and devour it and growl at anybody who walked by.  It couldn't have been better! 

My husband spotted an item on the menu called "Jesse's Special" which is $12.50 and touted as being the #1 selling menu item for 20 years.  It is a hamburger patty topped with onions, cheese, bacon, mushrooms, a liberal amount of shredded lettuce, ranch dressing, and diced tomatoes.  Okay..hamburger salad...I've seen it all now!  Husband reported that it was very good.  

For dessert we split a piece of key lime pie which is made by the owner's daughter.  It was decadent!  The graham cracker crust was nice and thin, the filling was tart and creamy and sweet, and the whipped cream on top tied everything together into one perfect piece of pie.  You gotta try it if you go! 

Jesse's is serving up the classics of yesteryear and I'm eating them!  I'm a fan!

I don't hand out a lot of five star reviews but this place deserves one! 

Visited on 12/30/2016 at 11:17 AM.  $51.31 got us two bowls of ramen, an iced tea, and a ramen lunch special.  The decor is so other-wordly...the floor is made up of matte hexagonal tiles, the booths and tables are gorgeous, and the paint scheme is matte black throughout.  It's completely classy and gorgeous.  I loved the cloth napkins and was surprised to find cloth hand towels in the bathroom which was so nice.  

I got the $16 braised short rib ramen which has a tonkotsu base, shitake mushrooms, green onions, and a perfectly prepared egg.  The broth was piping hot, complex, salty, and warms you right down to your bones.  The short rib was so tender and flavorful and I was wishing I had more of it.  The shitake mushrooms were thick and meaty and the noodles were fresh and plentiful.  I was in absolute heaven...it was all I could do not to lick the bowl clean!  It's the second best ramen I've ever had.  

I was expecting some pretentious hipster ramen by the location and decor but was pleasantly surprised by the ramen itself...they have mastered it!

Uninspired Mexican food.  

Visited on 9/30/17 at 2pm.  The restaurant has very high ceilings and nice decor except for the booths which appear to be very shoddily re-upholstered in a cheap white vinyl. $26.91 got us two lunch entrees, a quesadilla, and a cheese dip appetizer.  

The chips were good and the salsa was alright.  The salsa was the very runny variety with no onions, cilantro, or tomato chunks.  It was almost like pureed salsa but I liked it.  

All the entrees were brought out and our waitress asked if we needed anything else and I had to remind her that she never brought out our cheese dip appetizer.  She brought it out shortly after being reminded.  

I had the $7.25 lunch special #3 which came with one beef enchilada, one taco, rice, and refried beans.  The beans were bland as hell and the rice was one big mushy clump.  The beef was swimming in an orange grease and extremely salty.  The tortillas look like they came from Publix and weren't even warm.  All of it was edible but utterly forgettable.  

For the price, I'd rather go to Tres Amigos.

*military discount* 

Visited on Saturday 11-5-16 at 5PM.  $31.30 got us a half pizza for the boy, a salad, a wrap, and two soft drinks.  Oh and BTW this place is pronounced "Chi-chi Oh" if you are curious like me.  

I love the cute little area this location is set in.  It looks just like a small town square from the 50's complete with a courthouse and city hall.  So cute! The inside of the restaurant is modern, fresh, and inviting.  

This place seems to be heavy on the healthy/organic/gluten free/vegetarian/vegan meals which I enjoy from time to time.  The majority of the menu is prepared entree bowls in which you can pick your base (rice, spaghetti squash, noodles, etc.) Our waitress was very thorough and pleasant and I was impressed with her question of "do either of you have any dietary restrictions or allergies" because I've never been asked that in a restaurant.  I immediately knew that this was a different kind of restaurant! 

We got the $4.50 edamame for an appetizer.  Portion size was average but the beans were large and fresh and perfectly steamed.  I love the coarse salt they put on them which clings to each pod and makes for even distribution.  Five stars for this edamame. 


For $7 I got the kale salad.  The kale was incredibly tender and not bitter at all and it was loaded with onions, white beans, sunflower seeds, and sun-dried tomatoes.  The lemon agave vinaigrette tasted like pure oil.  Each bite was like licking a teenager on the forehead and I could feel the oil dribbling down my throat.  After I was done with the salad there was a pool of green grease on the plate.  Hopefully it was olive oil so I can feel healthy about this affront to my gut.  I think they need to adjust their recipe and add more vinegar to that vinaigrette.  Otherwise the salad was quite tasty so perhaps next time I'd ask for the dressing on the side.  

For my son I got the $6.50 half pizza with pepperoni and olives.  He gobbled it down with no complaints.  I snagged a bite myself and I enjoyed the Neapolitan style crust and ample toppings.  

They brought us a free chocolate chip cookie for it being our first time there and it was delicious!  I'm pretty picky about my chocolate chip cookies but this one was realllllly quite nice.  It was chock full of chocolate chunks and chips! 

I left this place feeling quite good about what was in my tummy and it was not toooo hard on the wallet.  I can't wait to go back and try their "$2 Tuesday" cuz' that sounds like a deal.

Yummy lobster but everything else was meh.  

Visited on 5/17/17 at 6PM. The hostess sat us at the very back next to the bathrooms which was kind of a bummer.  I could hear the toilets flushing the whole time.   $33.14 got me a sweet tea, a kid's meal, a lobster dinner, a side caesar salad, and an ice cream sundae. 

First I got the side caesar salad and it was a bit disappointing...about half of the leaves were limp and transparent...almost like it sat under a heat lamp for a moment and cooked a bit on top.  After picking the top part off it was alright...but had lots of big stalky parts that aren't my favorite.  I'd rather have more of the green top parts of the romaine.   

I got the $16.95 whole Maine lobster dinner that came with one side.  For my side I chose the rice which was a mistake...it was more like pasta shaped like rice.  It was mushy and all stuck together in a big lump.  Yucky!  The lobster itself was so good....huge and succulent and perfectly cooked.  I wished I could have had more lemons but my waitress disappeared for about 15 minutes so I let it go and just ate it.  

For the boy I got the $4.79 fried shrimp kid's meal which came with about 12 small shrimp and one side.  For his side I got the applesauce and he got water to drink.  The kid's meals come with your choice of a free ice cream...you can get a scoop of ice cream, an ice cream sandwich, or a push pop.  

Our waitress was MIA again for about 10 minutes after we were done eating.  I asked her to bring dessert and the bill at the same time cuz I never knew when she'd come back.  

For dessert I ordered the $3.99 "ale house sundae" which is two scoops of ice cream with hot fudge, whipped cream, and a cherry.  This thing looked like a mess...it didn't even look appetizing.  The ice cream was hard as a rock and the chocolate ice cream was freezer burnt.  There was no love put into that bowl of ice cream.  

I'd go back for the lobster but I'd definitely get a different side.

Cool casual eatery/bar in Ybor City that claims to make all their items in house except for the bread.  

Visited on 1-11-19 at 6PM. Finding a parking spot was difficult as there is street parking only and about 8 coveted spots within a 25 foot radius of the place. $39.76 got us one adult entree, two appetizers, and two sides.  Service was fast and friendly.  The ambiance is what I would call "broken-in-hipster" because the brick walls and industrial features probably looked very cool 10 years ago but now it just feels comfortable.  

I had the $8 bricklayer nachos which came with corn tortilla chips, pickled jalapenos, queso, salsa, and a black bean/corn relish.  If they're gonna claim they make everything in house I'll go ahead and pick em' apart and say these chips were from a bag.  The salsa was watery and made the middle section of chips soggy and cold.  Not something I would order again but it wasn't horrible.  It's really hard to f*ck up nachos.  

My dear sweet beloved husband had the $15 "tuna BLT" sandwich which came with lightly seared raw tuna, bacon, swiss, tomato, mixed greens, honey mustard, and toasted hawaiian bread.  He got to choose one side and he chose the quinoa which is cold and under seasoned.  He said the tuna was room temperature, had no seasoning, thick cut, and pretty much the same texture as all the other ingredients in the sandwich so it was like eating a raw mushy fishy meatball.  He started gagging about halfway through the sandwich but we are not the type of people to complain.  He choked it down.   

For the kiddo we ordered a side of mac n' cheese and a side of fruit since this place ostentatiously doesn't have a kid's menu.  The macaroni was under cooked and very dry.  If there was any cheese sauce to begin with I don't know where it went.  But the pineapples and blueberries were fresh and delicious.  

If you're a burgeoning 20-something who just happens to be walking down the street and you get a hankering for a craft cocktail and some hummus you're gonna love this place.  I, however, am a skeptical suburban mom and while I can appreciate what they're doing here, I did not enjoy the food and would not go back.  I'm too old for this shit.

Below average pricey Thai restaurant with a full vegan menu.  

Visited on 12/2/17 at 5PM.  I must have passed by this place a hundred times and never noticed it which is ludicrous because the sign on the outside of the building is absolutely enormous and they have a unique round entryway around the front door. It sits in a small strip mall next to a consignment store and a laundromat.  

Inside it's rather un-inspiring with plain tables and clutter.  It is one of those sketchy looking places where you want to order "something safe" if ya know what I mean. We were seated very quickly and service was fast and friendly.  $41.57 got us a seafood entree, a chicken satay appetizer, and a kid's meal. 

I got the $7.95 chicken satay appetizer which came with four chicken skewers, a bowl of peanut sauce, and a bowl of cucumber salad.  The cucumber salad was fantastic...chock full of fresh jalapenos and onions and fresh cucumbers.  The peanut sauce was a little bland but a very generous portion.  The chicken skewers were yellow, hard, dry, flavorless, and barely room temperature.  I am certain that they were cooked either yesterday or earlier today and re-heated.  For the price, I'd expect some freshly cooked chicken.  

My son got the $9.95 kid's chicken pineapple fried rice which came with apple juice and a spring roll.  I do not like paying ten dollars for a kid's meal at any restaurant but I will say their portion was enormous.  They give 3-4 times more than any child can possibly eat.  It was the best thing I tried tonight...hot and fresh and well seasoned. I found it unusual that it was smothered with fried onions which I wouldn't think is very kid friendly.  My advice would be to cut the portion in half and lower that price and nix the onions.   Also the meal was supposed to come with a dessert which they never brought out. 

I watched in horror as my husband's dish arrived.  He had the $20.95 "seafood basil delight" which the menu said had shrimp, calamari, mussels, and scallops stir fried with basil and onions and an herbal sauce.  What arrived was a plate full of green peppers, onions, calamari, shrimp, and mussels.  The scallops were missing and the green peppers were not on the menu description.  This is not the sort of place where I would order something like this but my husband is a brave man.  He said he'd give it a "4 out of 10" and that it was hot but bland.  

The prices here do not match the quality of the food.  Serving old chicken is absolutely unforgivable.  I would not go back.

*military discount*

Visited on 1/2/18 at 6PM.  $40.15 got us four appetizers and two sushi rolls.  

First impressions:  the restaurant looks very trendy yet casual inside.  They have a traditional sushi bar and lovely square plates.  Each table has a button which you can summon your server with which I've never seen at another restaurant and I thought it was really cool.  My husband said it's a very common feature in restaurants in Japan.  

I hate sushi so I ordered four appetizers: 

$5.99 crab rangoon-triangular variety chock full of krab and cream cheese.  There was more krab than cream cheese and it was very well seasoned and perfectly fried.  10/10 would eat again.  

$4.99 edamame- a good size pile of perfectly steamed and salted edamame.  No complaints.  

$5.99 chicken tempura- 6 strips of chicken fried to a golden brown in a tasty tempura batter.  Absolutely declicious!  Served with a sweet soy-based sauce.  

$2.50 white rice- fabulous sticky white rice.  One of my all time favorite things to eat.  

Husband loved his nasty raw fish rolls.  I did not try them.  

I'd come back.  Solid sushi joint.

I think this building is cursed.  Seriously, it's haunted or something.  This is the third restaurant that has tried to open in this location in a year and it's a spectacular shit show.  

Visited on 02/17/2019 at 12:15PM.  I stood at the hostess stand for a good solid six minutes before a surly asian woman with tattooed eyebrows stomped over and barked 'HOW MANY' and I said two and she wordlessly thrust a paper card at me with the number six on it.  I took a seat in the crowded foyer and waited.  

Finally the lady called my number and a hispanic family tried to jump in front of me with their number 9 paper card (you can't tell it apart from the number 6).   An innocent enough mistake I suppose but they had the audacity to throw a fit even though they came in 20 minutes after me and were sitting right across from me.  The asian lady and the hispanic family were having a hard time arguing in broken English and I was just standing there like a dummy like "ehhh, can I go to my table now??" Super awkward.    

When we were walked back to our table I was shocked to see that the restaurant wasn't even a quarter of the way full.  Super weird because there were tons of people waiting in the crowded front area.  I noticed terrified asian children bussing tables and every customer in the place looked pissed.  It's clear that this place was overwhelmed and the staff weren't trained properly. 

After about 20 minutes our server came over and took our drink order.  I ordered water for myself and Sprite for the kiddo and she brought out two waters.  Another 10 minutes later when I was able to get her attention I asked again about the Sprite and she said all they have is water.  o.o  I ordered our food and she didn't write it down.  She came back about 5 minutes later and asked me my order again.  

Another 14 minutes go by and I'm trying really hard to keep my toddler from melting down and to relax and our server comes over and sweetly explains that she just got assaulted by the manager and she's walking out.  She apologized and walked out the front door.  

About 10 minutes later an asian teenager came over and asked what we ordered.  I told him we ordered a full pound of headless shrimp with the classic seasoning, not spicy, and a kid's fried shrimp basket with applesauce instead of fries. This is the third time I have ordered.  I tried my best to be very pleasant and pretend like everything was okay but I was screaming internally. 

Shortly after that  he brought out a fried shrimp kid's basket with fries.  I didn't even bother explaining that I asked for applesauce instead of fries.  I was just thrilled that we had some food on the table after this almost two hour ordeal.  It wasn't long before my order showed up, and it was wrong of course.  What showed up was a half pound of shrimp and a half pound of snow crab legs.  I was starving so I didn't say anything and just ate it.  

Perhaps the saddest part of this whole experience was the food was amazing.  The shrimp were plump, tender, sweet, and were so perfectly cooked they'd just burst in your mouth.  The crab legs were absolutely the freshest I've ever experienced.  I'm used to the crappy frozen ones that still have barnacles attached to them but these were sweet and perfectly steamed.  I give the food five stars.  $28.19 was the total for the $4.99 kids meal and the $20.99 crab and shrimp bag.  Mind you, I ordered the shrimp bag which was three dollars cheaper. 

After we were finished the teenage asian brought us a cup of coleslaw and I told him we didn't order that and he took it back into the kitchen.  Employees were scrambling, tables were walking out, all the tables around me were bitching and complaining.  I asked for the bill and they took off 10% "for the inconvenience" without me even complaining.  Gee golly gosh thanks, almost makes up for the price difference between what I actually fucking ordered and what you brought me.  

I was super excited to see a crab-boil-type place open up in Brandon but this place was an absolute nightmare.  Easily the most stressful and awful dining experience of my adult life.  Hurry up and come try this place before it closes again.

Disclaimer: I got reallllly shnockered here and it may have influenced my review.  

Visited on Thursday 11-10-16 around 7PM.  This cute little restaurant has a tiki/boardwalk theme and is right on the ocean. The view at sunset is breathtaking and undoubtedly the best reason to come here.   The menu has lots of tropical boozy drinks, beers, seafood, burgers, nachos, etc.  (typical bar food with a heavy seafood influence).  

I hadn't eaten since breakfast and I got bored while waiting for a table so I headed over to the bar and scored a huge bud light draft and by the time I finished it and we were seated I was fully inebriated.  Yeah, I'm a light weight like that. 

 They tried to seat the 8 of us at a standard picnic table which was laughable.  We all tried to squeeze in and then quickly realized it wasn't going to work so we asked the hostess and manager for help and they just shrugged their shoulders.  We asked if we could push two tables together and they would not accommodate so two people in my party did it anyway and after that nobody said anything to us so I guess we got away with it.  ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

I ordered a "mermaid juice" drink which was rum based and had blue curacao and coconut flavors.  It was a beautiful drink and very tasty as well and pushed me from buzzed to trashed.  My family had to hold me back from skinny-dipping in the ocean or dancing on a table.  

My peel & eat shrimp appetizer came at the same time as the food which didn't bother my drunk ass but I know a lot of people don't like that.  The portion was yuuuuuuge *insert Donald Trump voice* and I swear it must have had 2 dozen fresh, delicious shrimp.  I like that they split them up the back which makes them easier to peel.  

The fried clam strips were abso-fuckin-lutely delicious and I loved their fries...they are the batter-dipped kind that are crunchy on the outside but like mashed potatoes on the inside.  I inhaled every bite of those clam strips and would have gladly eaten more.  

After eating I stumbled out to the bathroom to drain the lizard and wow they have pretty much the worst restrooms I've ever seen.  They are absolutely filthy and in complete disrepair.  Luckily they have an ice cream bar and I was able to score a double scoop of fudge ice cream to console myself after the traumatic bathroom visit.  

So...take my drunken review with a grain of salt.  I was so boozed up I would have gladly eaten anything but I swear the food was legit.

Every time I come here the waiter goes home with sore arms from cranking so much cheese on my dinner.  They always crank a little bit on and then look at me like "Is this enough?" and I motion them to keep going until it gets awkward and there is more cheese than food on the plate.  

Visited on 5/11/17 around 6PM and was able to get seated right away!  $18.97 got me a kid's meal, one adult entree, and a Bellini Peach Iced Tea.  If you've never tried the Bellini Peach Iced tea DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND TRY IT!  I've had it every time I go for the last 15 years.  It is a sweetened ice tea with peach flavoring in it and it'll blow your mind, son.  Up until about 5 years ago they used to put a real frozen peach in each glass but I guess they had budget cutbacks or somethin' cuz' they don't do that shit no mo'.  

First came the obligatory salad and breadsticks.  There is something magical about that salad.  I could eat about two bowls of that salad and be perfectly happy.  I dunno what everybody sees in those breadsticks tho...I think they're kinda bland and chewy.  

For my boy I got the $4.95 Macaroni and cheese dinner which came with two sides.  I chose grapes and broccoli for him.  For $1.04 you can add a drink to the kid's meal.  The mac n' cheese looks and tastes a whole lot like Velveeta shells and cheese.  Not a bad meal and my toddler enjoyed it.  

I got the $9.99 "cucina mia" which is like a build-your-own-pasta type deal so I chose the cavatappi pasta with the five cheese marinara sauce.   The pasta was cooked perfectly and the five cheese marinara was amazing as always.  The sauce is almost like a mix between marinara and alfredo and is pink in color.  It's creamy and salty and acidic and I love it.  

I used to get takeout a lot from Olive Garden and it is so convenient...you just order online and park in the designated parking spot and call the # and they'll bring it right out to your car.  Everything is packaged so well....it's very impressive.  

Look no further for your corporate Italian food needs!

Fancier place than I expected with gourmet fresh Thai food. 

Visited on 12-27-18 at 1:30PM. $30 got us two adult entrees including tip. 

First impressions would tell me this is a fast casual type place but inside is fancier than I expected. Nice classical music playing softly, a real Christmas tree in the corner, professional looking signage and menus. 

I had the $10.95 stir fry chicken with cashews. It had tons of fresh veggies which is exactly what I was after.  It had cashew nuts, chicken, onions, bell peppers, carrots, broccoli, snow peas, celery, zucchini, mushrooms, and came with a big side of white rice. The plate had a flower made out of a carrot for garnish which I thought was a nice fancy touch. 

This is exactly the sort of food I like to eat at home except they do a better job than me so I'll definitely be back.

A sit-down upscale burger restaurant with phenomenally flavorful beef.   

Visited on 1/7/17 around 5PM.  $46.30 got us a salad, a burger, a kid's meal, a beer, and a pepsi.  The decor is red and black and reminds me of a redneck vampire.  There are chickens and mounted cow horns amongst red crystal chandeliers and cloth napkins.  It sounds bizarre but it works.  

I got the $14.99 steakhouse salad which the menu said had mixed greens, toasted pecans, red onion, blue cheese crumbles, diced tomatoes, ash-seared sirloin, and bleu cheese dressing.  I am one of those weird people who don't like bleu cheese and asked to nix the cheese crumbles and dressing and add ranch dressing instead and they were nice enough to oblige.  This was one of the tastiest salads I've ever had.  The sirloin was so tender and flavorful and cooked perfectly to medium just like I asked.  I'm not ashamed to admit I cleaned my plate. 

I was able to snag a bite of my husband's "jucy lucy" burger and I was blown away...it was an explosion of flavor!  The angus beef, cheddar cheese, dijonaise, and carmelized onions worked together so well.  His sweet potato fries were crunchy and sprinkled with cinnamon-sugar which I loved.  I would have been jealous as hell if I didn't have the world's best salad in front of me.  

Everything I had was friggin' delicious and I wouldn't hesitate to go back!

Tasty and fast Amerianized Thai food in a strip mall. 

Visited on 6/8/17 around 6PM. This restaurant is located in a strip mall with a Walmart neighborhood market.  It has an open kitchen and about 8-9 tables.  The vibe is very casual and if I had just walked in without prior knowledge I would not have guessed it was a Thai restaurant.   $27.90 got us an order of pineapple fried rice, an order of sticky rice, a curry meal, and two soft drinks.  A nice white lady was our server and the food came out pretty quickly.  

I got the pineapple fried rice with chicken for $10.99.  The rice was cooked with canned pineapples, onions, and carrots and had a lovely creamy curry flavor.  The chicken was so tender and juicy.  I think the dish is about $2 too expensive for what it is but it was very good.  Usually pineapple fried rice is served in a fresh pineapple half and contains fresh pineapples....now I would expect that price if it were served that way but it wasn't.  

The sticky rice was served in a bowl and the rice grains were a bit shorter than what I'm used to at Thai restaurants.  Typically sticky rice is served wrapped in plastic in a little round bamboo container.  It wasn't as toothsome as I've had at other Thai restaurants but it wasn't bad.  $3 is a little steep for just a scoop of rice in a regular bowl, TBH.  

They have a counter that borders the kitchen that is "decorated" with thousands of foam stickers which was killing me.  Such a bizarre and tacky decoration for a Thai restaurant.   Ya'll really ought to think about removing those cuz' they look horrible.  That's just my opinion tho.  

A little pricey for what it is but it was tasty.

I swear this restaurant has had a "coming soon" sign out front for an entire year. I've been patiently waiting and stalking their social media and finally one day I drove by and a big "NOW OPEN" sign was outside. I nearly shat my pants I was so excited. 

Visited on 7-21-19 at 12:15PM. $62.39 got us two pounds of seafood, a shrimp basket, an order of sweet potato fries, and a Sprite. Our server Karen was timid but very attentive and efficient. 

They really did a bang-up job with the renovations in here! They had loads of tables and a new bar. I even saw a party room. Tables have plastic tablecloth and all utensils, flatware, cups, etc. are disposable which I'm a big (germaphobe) fan of. 

I had the $19.75 pound of headless shrimp which came with two potatoes and a corn on the cobb. The shrimp were perfectly cooked, pink, and juicy. Each shrimp was split down the back for easy peeling and deveined. The red potatoes were velvety soft and delicious. The corn was the frozen variety and nothing special.  I tried the cajun seasoning on the side and it was very tasty.  The portion was enormous and I ended up bringing about half of them home! 

I'm a huge fan of these asian seafood boil-in-a-bag-type places. If it wasn't so darn expensive I'd come here once a week. I loved it.

Good food. Large portions. Bait and switch pricing. Filthy bathrooms. 

Visited on 1-23-18 at 12:30pm. I tried to visit the day prior but they are closed on Mondays. $10.33 got me a lunch special and one order of dim sum. 

The menu stated the dim sum was $3.50 each so I ordered some shrimp dumplings. The filling was very coarse with small whole shrimp and flavorful but dry. The skins were too thick, bland, and had too much starch which made them unpleasant. Like chewing on tasteless boba balls and shrimp. Definitely one of the worst Har Gow I've had. I do appreciate the presentation in the cute little metal steamer basket and they were very hot. When I received the bill the dumplings were listed as $4.15. When I asked about it they immediately called the manager over and she stated that the prices had went up but they were still waiting on the new menus they ordered. I mean it's only 65 cents but isn't that illegal? I'm no lawyer but it seems shady. Check your bill carefully here. 

The $5.50 lunch special we chose was much better. I got the veggie lo mein which came with rice and soup or an egg roll. We got the egg roll and chicken fried rice instead of white rice. The rice was so amazingly good...it had that smoky charred flavor unique to Japanese fried rice. Unfortunately the chicken tasted like it had been in the fridge for a few days...it tasted really old. The lo mein was hot and fresh and full of yummy vegetables. I give the lo mein 5 stars! Fantastic flavor and the portion size was absolutely enormous. We took home enough food for two more meals. 

The bathrooms are really bad. I'm not trying to be mean but they really need to be cleaned and repaired. The rest of the building is nothing special but at least clean. 

I'm giving two stars mainly because I woke up with horrible gastrointestinal illness and this was the last thing I ate. I can't say for sure that this food is what caused it...hence the two stars instead of one. 

Their food does have good flavor but so many quality control issues that I can't recommend it.

I was expecting a stupid hipster restaurant in a gentrified neighborhood but I was somewhat delighted with my meal here. 

Visited on Friday 12-14-18 at 7pm. $98.44 got us a glass of wine, a beer, an appetizer, three "small plates", and a dessert. The interior is pleasantly clean and features artisan tiles from a shop nearby, open kitchen, ikea sinks, and succulents on each table. Our server Elischca was absolutely fantastic. 

I've always wanted to try a fancy cheese board so we tried that for $20. It featured 4 cheeses with accompaniments and some flatbread crackers. I was already a little hammied  before I got there so unfortunately I don't remember what kind they were but they were all terrific except for the blue cheese which I uncerimoniously spit into my napkin because it tasted like a moldy cow barn smells. 

Next up was the $14 brussel sprouts which came with onions and ham. It was absolutely heaven on a plate! Charred, smoky, salty goodness. I could eat a plate of these every night. My favorite part was the little leaves that had broken off during cooking and became crispy. 

Husband had the fried quail for $18 which came with 4 wings atop a spicy aioli. They were crispy, salty, and had a surprising amount of meat on them. Very tasty. 

I had the $18 sea bass which came with a coconut relish, glass noodles, and a panang curry sauce. The fish was crispy on the outside and cooked perfectly moist inside. The noodles were nice and light and paired well with the curry and coconut. Once again, I could eat this every night.

For dessert we split the $10 coconut panna cotta which came with a sorbet and assorted berries. It was light yet decadent and satisfying. Absolutely fabulous. 

A very memorable and enjoyable meal. Don't let the facade or the price tag fool ya...there's love in every bite.

Artsy-fartsy hipster ice cream with funky decor and unusual flavors. 

Art from local artists hangs on every wall and it's all for sale. No two seats are the same which is kinda cool. My child loves coming here because they have board games and he can sit on a couch and eat his ice cream. He calls it "the couch ice cream store" and begs to come here. 

Recently they've started making CBD infused ice cream and it's fantastic. It's a little pricey at $6.99 per scoop but creamy and soothing. Today I tried the oreo variety and it was full of cookies, soft but not melty, and I felt the effects within about 30 minutes. It's so nice to be able to get a serving of CBD when you're out and about running errands without having to buy a whole bottle. 

I really like this place. You can't go wrong with any of the flavors and it makes me feel good to support a local business.

5 stars for a sandwich??  You bet your sweet ass.  

Visited on 08/02/2018 at 1:30PM.  $25.15 got us two soft drinks, two cupcakes, a sandwich, and a fruit salad cup.  The building is huge, clean, and looks newly renovated.  Service was fast and friendly. 

The layout of this place is kinda confusing.  It's got two different counters but the cashiers are in the middle.  From what I can tell you're supposed to order your main items, pick up any bakery items from the shelves, pay, then wait for your food and once it's ready you pick it back up at the main counter.  

I had the $10.50 beef martini sandwich which has rare roast beef, mushrooms marinated in white wine and crisp bacon slices with garlic and herb spread on buttercrust white bread.  Sounds simple but this sammich is: 
1) Fricken huge.  One sammich is more than enough for two people. It's piled high with ingredients (they ain't skimpy at all).  
2) The roast beef is shaved thin and rare, nicely salty, and incredibly tender.  
3) The mushrooms are SOMETHIN ELSE, MAN.  They're sliced thin but sauteed to a perfect golden brown in that white wine sauce.  
4) The bread is FLUFFY.  SO FLUFFY YOU'LL WANNA DIE.  
5) Those bacon slices are thick and CRISPY.  
All of these elements together in your mouth create a cacophony of deliciousness never before experienced in my throat hole.  I loved every second of it.  

For dessert I split one of the $3.25 Hawaiian princess cupcakes.  When I picked this thing up I thought DANG THIS IS HEAVY but it was surprisingly fluffy.  The cake is delicately flavored with coconut, it's filled with a generous amount of pineapple, then topped with a fabulous cream cheese frosting.  The frosting is very sweet but not grainy and slightly savory just like a good cream cheese frosting should be.  

I'm hooked.  Can't wait to go back.

What's a butter burger?? I made it my mission to find out.  

Visited on 6-17-17 around 12PM. $22.21 got us a kids meal, a single butter burger combo, a mushroom and Swiss burger, a small drink, a turtle sundae, and a single scoop of chocolate custard. 

The employees here are extremely friendly. Like scary friendly. Like they're hostages and you're a crazed maniac and they're trying not to piss you off and get shot in the face.  

I got the  $6.59 single butter burger basket which came with fries and a drink.  The burger had onions even tho I asked for no onions but it wasn't a big deal...I just picked them off. The meat patty was thick and juicy and had so much beefy flavor! It tastes like the most delicious organic grass-fed beef you've ever had. I give this burger two thumbs up. They have crinkle fries too which are my all time favorite!

The custard was chocolatey and silky and luxurious. I found myself wanting to lick the container when it was all gone. 

I gotta say I think I prefer Freddy's but I did enjoy my first trip to a Culver's and I'll be back!

Delicious fresh seafood in a comfortable, casual environment. 

$20.86 got us a shrimp appetizer, a kids shrimp basket, and a diet coke. There is a small amount of parking in the front of the restaurant and you can park in the grass on the side of the building as well.
