 There are 5 or so small tables inside but loads of seating outside covered by a large shade. I can imagine sitting on the outside patio having a beer and listening to live music. It feels very comfortable! 

I had the  $11 half pound of U-Peel 'em Shrimp. There were 9 shrimp and the shells were split for easy peeling. They were cooked perfectly, sweet, succulent, and juicy. They were presented on a bed of lettuce and garnished with sliced green onions. They were served with cocktail sauce but you hardly needed it because the shrimp were seasoned well and flavorful. 

In my opinion it's a tad overpriced at more than a dollar per shrimp and no sides. I know of several places where I can get 10 grilled jumbo shrimp, fries, and a drink for less than $10. I hate to be a downer like that but my white trash tastebuds can't tell the difference between frozen and fresh shrimp. 

Nonetheless I appreciate what they're doing here and the food is phenomenal. Definitely check it out!

A cute little old fashioned mom n' pop ice cream place!  

Visited on 12/29/2016 around 8PM.  The inside is very small...there are maybe 5-6 tables and a self-service freezer full of ready-to-eat ice cream treats.   I love their cute 1950's decor and the little kid's play area in the front.

Once the gal behind the counter was done with her conversation with her co-worker I was able to order my $5.09 banana raft supreme.  The menu said it came with chocolate and vanilla ice cream, hot fudge, bananas, crushed peanuts, bananas, sprinkles, whipped cream, and cherries on top.  Mine only had vanilla ice cream (no chocolate like the menu said) but the soft serve ice cream was phenominal....not too cold or sweet and very creamy.  The bananas were perfectly ripe and there was a good amount of decadent hot fudge.  The sundae was visually stunning and they took a lot of care in the presentation which I enjoyed.  

Most their food I've tried is phenominal! The wings are perfect!! Crunchy on the outside and hot & juicy on the inside. It's a bit of a wait but worth it for those piping hot wangs! Their ranch dressing is like crack and I just want to pour it all over my face. 

I'm hooked.

This place is incredible inside!  If you have a sweet tooth (or are just a fat-ass like me) you'll love this place!

Visited 8/4/17 at 8PM.  It's like sensory overload in this place because there are huge cases chock full of every sugary pastry treat you can think of! The cupcakes alone are worth going here just to see...they are huge and elaborately decorated! They also have a huge bar full of hot cuban foods which you can eat there or take to go.  

$7.25 got me a rainbow cookie bar, a pecan pie bar, and a cookie.  The cookie was probably my favorite...it was an orange flavored sugar cookie decorated with icing.  It had supreme bite and texture and just the right amount of icing.  The italian rainbow cookie was delicious...soft and huge with just the right amount of tart raspberry jam with a sumptuous chocolate glaze on top.  I have yet to try the pecan bar but if the other two items are any indication...I'm in for a damn treat.  

I have read in a lot of the reviews about the homeless dude who hangs out on the porch and he was there tonight.  When I walked out to my car he was drinking coffee and crying.  I feel sorry for the dude but I don't see why this place lets him hang out there 24/7 because it's kind of a bummer and scary for kids.  Ya'll can call me heartless all you want to but I came here for cookies, not to have an existential crisis.  

But still I literally can't wait to come back! Maybe I can talk my husband into going tomorrow.

Authentic street tacos CHEAP and tasty! 

I go to the Lighthouse Ministries every week and always relish the good smells coming from this place...finally visited on 8-22-20 at 4pm. $15 got us five tacos and two bottled drinks from the cooler. 

I ordered at the window and then took a seat at one of the tables out front. In 26 minutes they called out our name and I went to the second window to collect my food. 

I ordered 3 corn tortilla tacos al pastor...what was given to me was half pastor and half mystery meat...the dried up remnants of pastor was on the bottom and it was a different shape and texture and flavor than the mystery meat on top. The tortillas were soft and a little greasy but in a good way. The onions and cilantro were nice and fresh and the dipping sauces are very flavorful and tasty. They were very generous with the mystery meat portions, too. 

In an air conditioned building with no flies trying to eat your food, I'd give it 5 stars...even with the long wait time and mystery meat. I'll be back.

Lovely views and a fancy brunch worth every penny. 

Visited on 7-7-19 at 12PM. The Sunday brunch buffet is $55 for adults and our 4 year old was free. Our server Nathallie was very attentive yet unobtrusive. 

The buffet had loads of options and was clean and replenished often. The middle has a pasta bar, an omelette bar, and about 20 hot burners full of everything from sirloin to sea bass to cinnamon French toast. They have loads of fresh seafood, sushi, vegetarian options, caviars, and pastries. 

I had shrimp which were outta-this-world amazing. They were plump and juicy and cooked to perfection. I also had two different types of salads and roasted veggies which were delicious. 

The dessert area is overwhelming in the best way. Every single thing looked exciting and tasty which made it super hard to just pick a few. I tried the coconut cake, ice cream, a pecan tart, a macaroon, and a lemon cupcake...each one was fresh and decadent. 

After brunch we took a stroll through the hotel's villas by the pool and found an adorable little koi pond full of gorgeous lilly pads. If you could get past the sound of the airplanes flying over every 3 minutes it would be a beautiful resort to stay at. 

I loved it. I'd go every day if my waistline and wallet could handle it.

Does Not Disappoint. How have Cactus Club got it so right?
They have introduced a new Happy Hour menu, all your favourites for a little cheaper. I'm into it.
I went with some friends recently to the West End location which was a first for me. It's handily located by WEM with ample parking!
I ordered the truffle fries - oh man, these are so morish. Delicious and great sharing dish and there are lots of fries. I also got the spicy chicken which is a menu fave of mine. If you tell your server you are sharing they always split it into two plates for you. I like that, then you still get a nicely presented plate and don't need to worry about being the greedy one.
The service was fantastic. Cactus Club always impress me with knowledgable and very attentive staff

I finally went to The Marc. I wish it had been for dinner but I ended up having lunch and it was delightful. I wasn't sure what to expect but the lunch menu is small yet enough to appeal to most.
I had the soup which was a lamb and more like a stew served with fresh bread. my dining partner had the same and a caesar salad on the side. which looked amazing. That crouton!
It's smaller inside than I expected and they fit lots of tables into the space. The waitress took our coats obviously to make more space and I could see into the kitchen which I liked. Open fresh vibes in here.
Service was exceptional even during a busy lunch hour rush. I'll be back for dinner - don't you worry about that.

I never got to try the food so I can't comment on that.
I tried multiple times to make a reservation over the phone throughout the week but there was never any answer. 
This was me trying to book a birthday dinner for my husband by the way. We decided to just go there and see if we can get a table. Sure it was busy but not one staff member so much as glanced our way never mind acknowledged us. 
We also had a four year old with us so standing by the door for ten minutes can be loooonnngggg. All they had to do was sit us at a table and give us some crayons and we would happily wait.
We ended up walking out and I never do that. I heard the food is incredible so maybe one day I'll go back when I'm over the disappointment.

I visited Stella Mares on valentine's night, they had a special 3 courses menu for a fixed rate of $69. For $80 you could get unlimited Charles Lafitte Sparkling champagne.

It was my second visit there and I can tell that their food definitely tastes good. From their soup to the meats they have, I tried some of the ribs as well as their chicken roulade.

The plates are well presented hats off to the Chef.
The high prices are justified by the atmosphere and the service which is pretty good. They often check on you and the servers are very polite & smiling.

However, I regret being served Costco baguette at a restaurant that is "French" themed, especially considering all the other elements of the restaurant. 

Also, if it's cold outside, avoid their "closed patio" area. It's windowed all around, it can get pretty cold in there.

Very romantic restaurant and great experience overall. I will be back!

Hands down the best Mexican restaurant of the area. I have been to The Mex Authentic multiple times and they have never failed to please me.

Prices are affordable, about $10 for an enchilada, $11 for a burrito/bowl at most on the menu. Portions are pretty big, very filling and SO good! I always go for the chicken enchilada it tastes amazing with sour cream and guacamole.

Service is always on point. They often check on you, refill your soft drinks, waiters are always very nice and polite. They split checks for large parties. 

If you like margaritas, try the Mexarita.
Wanna add a little spice? Get the Jalapeño Cucumber Mexarita, it's not too spicy, you won't regret it.

DO NOT EAT HERE!!! This is an official warning!!! I'm never coming back. If you want horrible service from top to bottom then look no further. It's hot as hell in there and the management is a total disaster. Everybody was sweating in there.Customer service is not a priority. Don't count my 1 stars because this place doesn't deserve a star. This is an individual owned Deanie's and it's not affiliated with the other 2 locations. The menu is limited as well. Save your hard earned money and go somewhere else.

Loved my experience here @ Yats and I'll tell you why! 

Some background information, I'm from San Diego and came to Tennessee for a business trip and was able to go to this delicious restaurant with a huge and awesome group of people from all over the U.S. One of my fellow employees discovered this place and wanted all of us to try it with him; he's been in contact with the owner and warned him that he was bringing a big group with him!

When we walked in, we were greeted by Joe, the owner, and another gentleman that was working that day...oh how I wish I got his name as well. Both of them were extremely welcoming! They explained what was on the menu (only a select few is available at one time) and even gave us a plate of four items so we can try before ordering.

After taste-testing all four items, I could really tell I was about to enjoy what I was having. I think he had us try the Chili Cheese Etoufee, drunken chicken, Maque Choux, and Chorizo. ALL of them tasted great, but I decided on a half and half of the Maque Choux, which has corn, and the Chili Cheese Etoufee, which had crawfish. The two dishes were poured over rice and 2 slices of seasoned buttered bread are included.

IT WAS AMAZING! The New Orleans, Cajun flavors were so good! Many of my colleagues claimed it to be "spicy," which it probably was.... but I eat spicy food all the time so I barely felt the heat. I even added more hot sauce to it! Anyway, the combination of the two settled well and complement each other. They pour each dish next to each other on the same plate and the flavors do not conflict at all. I also love love love eating foods like this over rice. The bread itself was uniquely tasty as well, when you bite into it you get a strong taste of butter....but you also get that hint that it's not just butter in here. We asked the server and he said they mix in some seasonings and spices to that butter... YUM

It was a big serving for me, so I ended up taking it to my hotel. I enjoyed it a couple hours later and it was still tasty. He also let us taste some Peanut Butter pie which was good good good. Strong taste of PB and he had two different crusts at the time, one of them being chocolate. 

The service was extraordinary. Joe really got all the plates out pretty fast considering we had a party of about 30 people + the other customers he was helping. The other employee grabbed our plates as soon as he noticed them, asked if everything was okay, and even chatted with him a bit because he was been to San Diego before. 

The place isn't too big, maybe with around 10-15 small tables around? But it was big enough to accommodate over 30 people. Interesting decor. 

Joe mentioned he does have a few other locations, in different states. I wish we had one on the west coast tho. THANK YOU JOE FOR HAVING US!!!!

A fantastic impromptu date night!

Made last minute reservations and had no idea what to expect; just saw their high rating on yelp.

Parking structure next door and is free for the first 75 minutes.  But after over 2 hours, our parking fee was only like $1.25, so very reasonable.

Stepped in and they sat us at the table for 2 at the front window.  Cute smaller restaurant; great tunes (heard everything from gorillaz to amy winehouse).  Menu definitely had an asian flair with fish sauce popping up in many of the dishes.  Excellent, in my opinion. Ordered a bottle of Pinot.

We were intrigued by so many dishes and then we saw that you can do a tasting menu for $50/person.  Seriously?  What a great price!  For the next couple of hours, the chef treated us to a variety of dishes.

Mixed cocktail olives
white marinated anchovies on crostini w/orange zest
Burrata on mixed greens (Fresh!)
Wagyu Beef Carpaccio
Beef Bone Marrow Bruschetta
Risotto special of the evening (EXCELLENT; my favorite of the night !)
Cheese plate (3 options including a humboldt fog) 
2 desserts 

Yes, I had to tap out.  Am I missing something?  Probably; I couldn't keep track of all the dishes.

Finally, staff was friendly and attentive.

A great evening and would highly recommend.  Plus, just a block away from State, perfect for an evening stroll (but we were too full to stop for a night cap).

Oh, how I've missed southern bbq and fix-ins.  I'm especially partial to the Missouri region, but my preferences were formed in the bootheel.

Needless to say, I loved the BBQ I bought from Big Woody's.  Needed to grab lunch and found this spot via Yelp.  Located in a strip mall, stepped in and the place was packed.  Not a seat available.  Oh well, I'll just order it to go and take it back to the hotel.  I should have known that while I was waiting, a patron would offer his seat.  Yes, I've been missing that Southern Charm, too.

Pulled Pork Sandwich? Perfect.  Smoked pork was savory.  Just a bit of bbq sauce, so if you like to douse it, grab more.  I prefer a bit of sauce, so I can taste if the meat is quality and it was.  Memphis style would have a vinegar slaw, but their slaw is a mix of vinegar and mayo, so no slaw for me.

Sides? Fried Okra & Fried Pickles.  The fried pickles were spears and served with a jalapeno ranch.  Both the Okra and Pickles were fried perfection.

As I was leaving I noticed quite a few patrons had the Hog Balls, but I didn't get to try. Next time...

While dining at Dolsot House next door, I was always curious about Kuzina by Sofia because there was always a crowd. We decided to come on a weekend for lunch and it wasn't too busy. We stood at the door for a few minutes before they finally sat us down even though one waitress acknowledged us and walked by us, and another waitress finally got menus to sit us down at the table right by the door. It felt like forever before we got any service after that, or we would have to grab the waitress in order to ask for anything. It was really frustrating. We saw another table come in after us, get seated, and got their order placed and served almost immediately. I don't think we had ordered anything complicated, and it was only two of us, but we just did not feel the service was there. They also didn't have the lamb gyro we initially ordered, so we had to get the lamb souvlaki. Whatever, fine. 

Another issue I had was that the salad with the dressing, pita, the meat, and tzatziki sauce were all on the same plate and getting mixed in with everything else. The oil from the salad was mixing into my pita bread which made it a little soggy. Ugh. The food wasn't all that great in my opinion. 

So for us.. we received horrible slow service (all I ask is that I don't have to go hunting for you to get what we need). didn't get the food we initially wanted. taste was ehh. Would not come back. I really wanted to like this place. 

Sundays, they serve brunch from 11-3pm.

FINALLY!!!!  Some good Mexican in this area.  I have always wondered why this area lacked solid Mexican food establishments.  The VIP lounge on the beach has usually held top spot, but we have a new heavyweight contender-Taquitos Mexican.

Tucked into a strip center across from the Bay Pines VA, Taquitos Mexican is great across the board.  We started off with chips and guacamole.  The chips were perfect, crisp with a little flavor and the guac was homemade and delicious.

The namesake taquitos-of the chicken variety-were very tasty and came covered with lettuce and white flaky cheese.  Again, delicious!  The three tacos we tried were the carnitas, shrimp firecracker and barbacoa.  The only miss in the entire evening was the barbacoa, which was strangely off point-a little dry and lacking flavor.  The other two were excellent and we even reordered the shrimp firecracker.  We also had a chicken tamale which was soft, delicate and full of subtle flavor.

For dessert, we had the churros, four to an order, and they were great as well.

The service was very friendly and the prices were reasonable.

Like the Terminator, I'll be back.

Tried Sparks Coffee Co for the first time Saturday  and the food is excellent-the same said for the service.  We had to wait 45 minutes before we were seated but things from a service  perspective went quickly. 
When  the food came, it was fabulous. We ordered the Seafood Benedict, chicken fried steak and eggs, Corned beef hash/eggs and pancakes.  Everything was hot and delicious and very fresh. Excellent quality  ingredients and everything was prepared perfectly. This is not the  cheapest place in town but it is well worth it. Large portions and high  quality food really set this place apart The staff was great. Will be back for the lunch menu. for sure.

this is the first tasting room that Captian Jack's took us. 

there are actually two different sets of tastings here:
1. Kunin Winery
2. Westerly Winery

This modern tasting room is pretty cool. You walk in and you're greeted by friendly staffs. The tasting area is in the center of the room. 

The place is quite small and it can get stuffy when there are a lot of people. The wines are okay. I think I like the westerly's more than the kunin's. 

If you and a friend are here for wine tasting, get one of each and share, that way you'll get to sample wines from both places! 

If you're here w/ a wine tour, then i think it's about $8-10 for 4 tastings.

Great dining experience in santa barbara!

restaurant - great ambiance, romantic, and cozy.
service - excellent!
Food  - excellent!

french onion soup - soo good! for $9 you get a nice big size of soup loaded w/ a good amount of caramelized onions, a big crouton and gooey cheese. The broth was good..perfect balance of wine and beef stock.

crab cake - every bite was filled w/ dungeness crab meat. Although they were not the jumbo lumps, they were the finely shredded it was still good. it was light breading. only thing i'd like to have less of is celery. On my crab cake, i can taste bits and pieces of celery which overwhelmed the crab meat / seafood taste. All i can taste was the celery flavor. Other than that, it was definitely good crab cake. The crab cake itself had enough flavor that the red bell pepper coulis was not even needed.

Bourbon & Maple-Glazed California Duck Breast - lets just say it was sooo good that i had to cut the duck meat into smaller pieces so i can enjoy it longer. the duck confit was good too! the meat just falls right off the bone. mmmmm i can still taste the flavor. I was not a fan of the vegetable side that it came with: succotash of corn, fava beans
applewood-smoked bacon and Windrose Farms butternut squash - it was too rich for my taste.

Grilled Kobe Ribeye - amazing!!!! the meat just melts in your mouth. I'd like to eat this everynight! 

As much as i wanted to order a dessert, i just couldnt. I was waaay too full. 

Service was excellent, he was attentive, made sure our food was good. And he even brought me a free small plate of organic berries to end the night as a bday treat! 

I'll definitely come back here again!!

Let me just start off by saying this place is definitely over hyped. 

My friend and I met up for dinner here and once we got to the establishment we were waiting in front for a good 10 minutes and we weren't greeted or anything so we were unsure if we had to seat ourselves or if we'd be seated. We waiting a couple more minutes and a hostess finally showed up and took us to our table.

They have a good variety on their menu. Not only do they serve pizza, but they serve salads and pasta as well. They also have small plate options to snack on. We ended up ordering their garlic chicken on a cauliflower crust. I thought that was a unique option because I don't know many places here in Reno that offer cauliflower crust. We also ordered their Mexican corn, which is like elotes, and we ordered the chicken and shrimp Alfredo. The pizza was good, I really liked the cauliflower crust because it doesn't feel too heavy. The corn was pretty decent, I definitely enjoyed it. The pasta wasn't the best. It was too dry, it definitely didn't have enough sauce, and I felt like the noodles weren't cooked all the way.

Overall, I probably wouldn't go back but at least I got to try it out for myself

A hidden gem! I honestly didn't know about this place till a food blogger in Reno posted about their French toast. After seeing it on Instagram, my good friend, Salma and I knew we had to try it out.

Once you walk in, there's a sign that says to seat yourself to wherever you'd like. We wanted the table near the window that had good lighting but since the table was still dirty, we weren't able to sit there. There were many seating options, but we specifically wanted to sit there for photography purposes. Still we were waiting for the table to be cleaned, but we ended up just sitting elsewhere. Probably the only downfall to the experience. 

The food was absolutely amazing! We came for what we wanted and that was the French toast, but we also ordered the breakfast sandwich and the chicken fried steak. The breakfast sandwich comes with either a bagel or croissant topped with two eggs, your choice of bacon, ham, or sausage, and your choice of cheese. This was one of our waiters recommendation and it's definitely a breakfast item I would recommend as well. The chicken fried steak was delicious! It comes with 2 eggs, home fried potatoes, and country gravy. The gravy was definitely the one that tied in the whole meal. It had great flavor to it and the steak was cooked perfectly. Now for what we really came for, their French toast! It's a Hawaiian bread topped with powdered sugar. This isn't your typical French toast, let me just tell you that. It has a crunchy coating and has a very sweet taste to it. It was so good, and we even ate it cold! It probably would've been 10x better if we ate it warm, but still, it was so good! 
To me, it tasted exactly like a crumb donut! I would go back for this any day! 

Chef Nate saw us taking pictures of the food and came over and shared his photos of his dinner specials, which are plated so creatively! I've honestly never seen anything like it in any restaurant in Reno. After seeing his collection of photos, I knew that I would have to come back for their dinner specials. Once I do, I can't wait to share it with you all! 

Nate was also kind enough to let us try one of the desserts that was featured on their specials that day. I honestly forgot what it was called, but it was a mousse that tasted pretty much like a pumpkin spiced latte. Even though I was full from all the food at this point, the mousse is very light and has a whipped cream texture so it wasn't too filling, which was perfect! 

Thank you for the amazing dining experience! I can't wait to try their dinner items and come back for their yummy French toast!

First time here and heard good things so checked it out.

Venue  - Place doesn't look as big from outside, but when you walk inside and check out the levels it's actually really big. They have a nice size bar, restaurant with great looking food, dance hall with a nice size stage, and a rooftop patio that's a lil smaller than most.

Service - If you find the right bar then you can get quick service with great pours.

Prices - Same as all the other bars 

Lines - Depending on time and day you can get in right away or expect to wait a few minutes to get in. 

Decor - Great props for the ladies and pretty cool decor all around.

Overall it was a good experience and had fun here.

Location  - I believe in in the downtown area of Nashville,  near some other hip restaurants and art areas.

Service  - Service was good and prompt. 

Food - Had the brunch special and it wasn't as great as I expected,  selection wasnt as great and some items didnt taste as good. 

Parking - Plenty of parking and valet available. 

Venue - Very clean and bright.

Prices - A bit higher than what I'm used to paying for brunch but not too expensive.  

Overall wouldn't probably come back and would like to try other places.

Second time here and the food quality has gone down. 

Location  - Great location near the main attractions and was walking distance to hotel. 

Service - Very nice staff and the service was good. 

Food - Not as tasty or as fresh to be hyped up anymore. The first time I came it was great from what I recall, but now it's nothing wrth checking out again. 

Prices - About the norm if anything maybe a lil higher than normal. 

Venue - They keep it well kept up and looks identical to 3 yrs ago since I was last here.

Overall will not be coming back and find myself a new spot to try out.

Venue - Its a nice modern cozy lil place with music.

Food - Small tacos with not the greatest flavor. 

Service  - Got overcharged on my bill (B.S.). One of the guys in our group left after closing out his tab, and they didnt ring him up on his tacos accordingto waitress. I was the last one to close out, and waitress charged me for his food, I was cool with it but then I asked my friend and he said he didnt order tacos (He had left at that point). I was taking her word for it but also its not my responsibility for her screwups, but once my buddy told me he didn't eat tacos that was annoying.  It was a few bucks so didn't bother going back or disputing charge but its a shame. 

Will not be recommending the food or service here.

Venue - Very clean and open place, with great views from the patio.

Staff - People here are very chill and nice.

Prices - Fair pricing for food and drinks.

Crowd  - Its more upscale than most of the bars on Broadway. 

Music - They have a DJ upstairs and he mixes up the music. 

Overall great place and highly recommend checking it out.

Location  - In the outside area of Downtown Nashville,  ended up walking here and it was about a 10 min walk from Downtown.  It's in a new up and coming trendy area. 

Parking - Seems like they have nearby lots to park.

Venue - Very nice well kept up place and what looked to be be a nice patio area as well. 

Service - It was good but I think they could of stepped it up a bit.

Food - Honestly I've been to a few Italian spots and for the type of restaurant I was expecting it to taste just as good or better. I feel as if the flavors wasn't on any of the dishes I tried and same goes for the pizza. Everything tasted fresh just needed more kick.

Desert - The only thing that was over the top here was the best tasting Tiranisu I've ever had.

Location - Just about 5 minutes or away from downtown Nashville. 

Venue - Clean newer looking place similar to others and large bar areas.

Staff - Friendly staff and very nice and helpful. 

Tips - Place gets packed and need to make reservations in advance for sure. 

Cost - Same as all other spots. Gotta pay the price to play. 

Overall cool place and worth checking out. If you feel like chilling then head to the lower level and chill at the bar with music.

Location - Great spot in the center of Broadway st.

Venue  - Huge spot with multiple levels of different bands and sometimes music. Large patio with a large bar, lots of tables and seating. 

Staff - Workers here are very chill and look happy to be working. 

Cost - Going rate is the same at all places here on Broadway St. 

Food - We ordered appetizers and it was a good portiin with good fresh taste.

Overall great spot to chill at and would definitely be back on my next visit to Nashville.

Venue - Since Lukes 32 and Jason Aldean's bar connects its one of the better spots to hit up here in Nashville with a huge rooftop. On the weekends it gets so busy you can experience a long wait to get upstairs. 

Service - When its slow the bartenders here are very cool and chill, but when its busy the service can be a bit slow getting a drink..

Food - Didn't try the food here.

Prices - Regular prices for drinks here just like any other bar on Broadway.

Music - Great options on music here since they have multi levels of bands, the upstairs room has a dj that will switch it up on music including hip hop.

Crowd  - Its a bit of everything on the weekends when everyone is in from other places visiting for events. Also can suck cause it get very packed and hard to get around with crowded areas.

Great spot and a must to check out.

Venue - Since Jason Aldean and Luke Brian's bar connects its one of the better spots to hit up here in Nashville with a huge rooftop. 

Service - When its slow the bartenders here are very cool and chill, but when its busy they still keep the bar moving fast.

Food - Didn't try the food here.

Prices - Regular prices for drinks here just like any other bar on Broadway.

Music - Great options on music here since they have multi levels of bands, including hip hop for the ones that want to switch it up. 

Crowd  - Its a bit of everything on the weekends when everyone is in from other places visiting for events. 

Great spot and a must to check out.

Geno's is not getting no love on Yelp. My cheesesteak with wiz was outstanding. The bread makes the sandwich and Geno's has the best roll.

Why not 5 stars, well Geno has some customer service issues like no public restroom and cash only. Parking can be a challenge but it comes with being on Cheesesteak Corner.

It's worth a trip for the legit cheesesteak experience. Being from out of town like me it was on my bucket list.

Bucket list is checked, so I'm not sure I'd make the trip back unless I knew I could find parking and my bladder was empty.

With all the negatives you'd be hard pressed to find a better cheesesteak. So 4 stars

I know this is a 3 star review but I do recommend you at least stick your head in and at least check it out. I'll explain why it's only 3 stars in few more lines. 

So this is a pretty cool, way old and very popular spot. We stopped in at 8pm on a week night and it took a little while to get a seat. The energy in here is awesome and the beer is cold. So for that reason alone I recommend you stop by.

Now what I didn't like so much was my meal and the reason for only a 3 star rating. This was my first night and first meal in Philadelphia so I ordered a "no brainer" a Philly Cheese Steak. It's not that the cheese steak was bad it just wasn't OMG AWESOME. I expected to be dazzled by the sandwich and I was thinking is this sandwich any better than a Subway Sandwiches Cheese Steak ($5 foot long) back home in California while you're a super cool bar in Philly. If my mind even went there, this missed the mark big time. 

I did get a couple cheese steaks at those famous places in the city and they were to die for. Maybe order something else besides a cheese steak here. That's my suggestion. Be prepared for a crowd but this is always the sign of good bar.

I rarely hand out two-star ratings, however, I've rarely received such rude treatment. I also try to always include both the positive and negatives, so the positives: the decor is beautiful and the location is very convenient. And in the summer months, maybe the patio is nice.

On Saturday evening, March 12th, my husband and I planned to meet another couple here for a drink before our reservation for dinner at another establishment. We arrived first. It was raining, so getting inside quickly was on my mind. As I approached the door I could see the backs of two servers against it on the inside. I thought that was odd to have your back facing the customers. When I reached for the handle, one of the servers saw me and moved the other out of the way so I could open the door and enter. My husband I entered and one of the gentleman who had been backed to the door said hello and welcomed me with a smile. He asked for our name. I told him we didn't have a reservation but were just wanting to grab a drink at the bar. He said reservations were required. I questioned if he was saying reservations were required for the bar to which he said no, feel free to have a seat at the bar. Now, to clarify, there is one entire half of the place that is empty, and the other half, including the bar, which is full. There are exactly FOUR seats at their bar. Can it really be called a bar with four seats? Isn't that more like a bistro table? I digress. At this point he had turned away from me and we're now standing in the doorway with no room to move in any direction. Sardines anyone?  I asked him if we were to "sit" at the full bar to which he said no and opened the door and gestured for us to leave. Yes, you read that correctly. 

I totally get a place requiring reservations. I actually prefer that and most of the places we frequent do. So, if someone shows enough interest in your establishment to show up, albeit, without a reservation, and you're full, there are a hundred ways to handle it in a manner that leaves a positive impression. You could:

1) Say thank you for coming in. We wish we could accommodate you, but it just isn't possible tonight. May I make you a reservation for...

2) Thank you for coming in. We are very busy tonight but let me see if I can determine if any of the seats at the bar  (4...remember?) will be opening up soon.

3) Thank you for coming in. We are very busy tonight but let me see if I can fit you on a bit later. Would that be okay?

Of course we already had dinner plans, and he probably guessed that, but he had every chance to make a wonderful impression but instead he was a complete jerk.

I'm going to chalk this one up to one bad apple and/or training issue. We may try it again sometime. Maybe when the patio is open so there is more seating and less of a need for the attitude.

Seriously, what is the hype about? The cheesesteaks are average (at best) with regular bread, regular meat, and cheese that tastes like processed nacho cheese. On top of that, the guy at the counter is SO RUDE. We sat near the window where guests were ordering, and we probably saw/heard 20 transactions. From these transactions, I gathered the following:

1. He's racist. NOT nice to Asians (even those that speak English PERFECTLY). There are a handful of signs that say "This is America. Speak in English." We asked him what the score was for the Eagles game (the game was playing on a TV right behind him), and he said "I see cheesesteaks, I don't tell people what the scores are." 5 minutes later, a Caucasian guy asked him the same questions, and he told him what the score was. He also gives out pens/souveniers, but not to Asian people.

2. He's rude. One guy asked for mushrooms on his cheesesteak, and he said they didn't have mushrooms. The guest paused for 2 seconds, and the guys goes "so, do you want it or not? yes or no? make a decision? come on come on." There was NO ONE behind this guest waiting to order... I don't know why he was in a hurry.

I'll never go back here again!

Sigh. It pains me to do this, but I have to downgrade my review significantly.

I like the food at LPE and it's the kind of place where everyone can find something on the menu they'll like. Plus, the beer selection is decent and cold. Everyone's happy right? When my 18 year old cousin came to visit us from BC for the week, I thought we could take him to Local Public Eatery for a casual south side bite and a pint before catching a movie.

We stopped in on a Monday night and the place was very quiet - not unusual for a pub on a Monday night, so I wasn't put off by it. Our group of 5 strode across the entire place and found ourselves a booth (it's seat yourself style) at the opposite end of the restaurant.

Then we waited. And waited and waited. There were maybe four or five other tables of customers in the whole place, and at least 2 or 3 servers. We watched as the servers hung out at the bar, talking and laughing. No one ever came over to our table in the fifteen minutes that we waited. We all got up and left to find a different place to eat. The end.

I have high hopes for Mercer Tavern, and it's clear that they're figuring a few things out along the way.

I've been twice so far - once at around 10 PM on a Thursday night for a birthday, and once at around 5 PM on a Monday evening for drinks and food with friends. 

Thoughts on my 10 PM visit:
- A very, very cool space mixing a vintage aesthetic with a trendy crowd. I loved the nods to the tavern's warehouse history in the bathrooms and on the menus.
- The clientele is cooler than Hudsons but not as hipster as The Common
- It was surprisingly loud for only being about 75% full
- The waitresses in little black dresses feels too much like Earl's or Moxies
- The Mercer Iced Tea is fantastic!

Thoughts on my 5 PM visit:
- Why are the waitresses still wearing little black dresses? This is a casual tavern/pub, not an upscale date-type restaurant or nightclub
- The food is seriously lacking. The pretzels are way better at The Pourhouse
- Our server didn't know that Yukon Gold is a type of beer. I know this place is new, but still.

The space is awesome enough and the soundtrack is cool enough that I'll still keep visiting Mercer, but I hope that a few things change.

Not good.  Long wait for lunch even though we got there at 11:00.  We were given the wrong menu.  We were given the brunch menu.  We asked if there was another menu and were told no.  All the sides were wrong, all four.  My toast on my fish sandwich was burnt.  Good concept poor execution.

Yes I do still think about you Tony. My experience was so horrific that I can't forget it no matter how hard I try. You may have moved but my horrible experience there with an abusive screaming drunken owner was a once in a lifetime experience that I will share every chance I get for the rest of my LIFE.  It stands out so memorably because I have never been treated so disgracefully anywhere in my life. When you channel your inner Gordon Ramsey, it should NOT be at your customers. I see you still remember me too. How flattering.

The best Indian food I've ever had, hands down.  The decor is very simple, don't judge this book by its cover.  I had their lunch buffet.  So many choices including breads and desserts. I sampled several dishes, they were all EXCELLENT!  This food put a smile on my face and sent me straight to a food induced comma.  Just the right amount of spice, heat & sweet.   Very reasonably priced.  Very attentive service.

This is a fancy little restaurant with a not too huffy vibe. Our server was very sweet and good at her job. She even perfectly rattled off the 5 million specials of the evening. (does anyone ever really order those??)

I had the free range chicken pasta. It was ok. The sauce was too thin and had a tangy-ness to it that I didn't really appreciate. But the chicken was cooked perfectly and wasn't fatty or creepy.

The bruschetta was pretty good. It was made with fresh mozzarella instead of parmesian... which I think may be the traditional way.. but I prefer parm because it has more flavor.

I enjoyed the dinner experience but I could have gone someplace else and spent half as much and enjoyed my food twice as much.

I am thinking I am not cut out for fancy food!

They have a lot to learn about service. The male bartender was super apathetic and seemingly annoyed by our existence...ex: when taking our brunch order he just walked up and said "Food?" In general he couldn't be bothered to interact with us, let alone do it with any hospitality. 

Lousy drinks --  the mimosas are a ripoff. We ordered a carafe, but it was 90% juice, only the neck was topped off w/ sparkling wine. We're not ordering juice here, people, we're ordering drinks! A mimosa should be mostly sparkling and topped w/ juice. I asked if he could add more but his adjustment made no difference. But here's the kicker -- when a friend of the apathetic bartender sat next to us, she was welcomed with smiles and jovial hospitality, and when she ordered a mimosa guess what she got? 90% sparkling wine, topped with juice! You know, the way they're supposed to be made.

Clearly there's no front-of-house manager to oversee and ensure good service.

Food-wise, it's meh. The forgettable $13 & $15 entrees didn't come with sides, so you gotta pay extra to have potatoes or grits or bacon w/ those eggs.

Sorry guys, but New Orleans is a food and hospitality town....You aren't even trying. I don't imagine Morrow's will be around unless you step up your game in a major way. (and writing yourself fake reviews wasn't the solution -- glad Yelp removed them!)

I have never been treated so rudely at a restaurant in my life!
I have a 10lb service animal that is contained in a small  bag.
The waitress challenged me and asked what service she provided and told me that she could refuse to serve me. I shared nicely with her that according to the ADA act I do not have to share my personal disability with everyone and asking me to leave or refusing to serve me is discrimination and is not compliant with the law. She argued this point as well. My date and I were so offended and upset at her continuing challenges and arguing, we decided to dine elsewhere.

Loved this market! So many wonderful options! 

I sampled a Gouda cheese and a pumpkin spice cheese. I liked both. I also sampled some honey.

I bought the fig mascarpone gelato. It was very good!! 

Everything looked so fresh and the prices were reasonable!

I've been driving past them hidden gem for 2.5 years and decided to stop by. Loved the vibe and atmosphere. The staff were amazing and so friendly. They truly made you feel at home and welcomed. 

I ordered a bacon cheeseburger with lettuce, Mayo, and onions. Oh my goodness! So good! A little greasy so bring on the napkins. 

Would definitely come back!

Such a fun restaurant and dining experience! They had a dancer, they threw napkins, and had great music! Loved the vibe in here. Two level seating and a balcony. Outdoor seating as well. 

We ordered the Saganaki, which is grilled kefalograviera cheese flambè with cognac. It is served with pita. Amazing!

WE also ordered the Stuffed Mushrooms, which are mushroom caps stuffed with tirokafteri, garlic and herbs, coated in panko bread crumbs and crisp fried. It is served with creamy Acropolis sauce. This was so good!

Additionally, we ordered the Spinach Dip, which is artichoke and spinach dip in a creamy white cheddar cheese topped with tirosalata. It is served with lavash cracker topped with diced tomatoes and cheese! Incredible!

Would definitely come back here!

Amazing! Ordered the Flautas with carnitas. They are three flour tortillas filled with Oaxaca cheese and your choice of shredded meats or veggies, rolled, fried and topped with crema and a side of salsa. Perfect portion! Very fresh and flavorful!

This is a tough review.  Early April, four of us came because of the crab salad pictures.  They looked lovely, we could hardly wait.  However, one bite, and those eager faces took a downward trend.   I seemed to not be as disappointed as the others in my party who swore the crab was canned.  I thought the crab had been frozen and thawed.  Not as washed out as some we recently experienced in the Pacific Northwest, whatever that means, but surely not fresh.  

The salad was pricey.  Overall it was ok but nothing special. 

I did appreciate the freshness of the salad's leafy greens, a mix of different kinds of baby lettuce, iceberg, and romaine.  The buttery avocado was a nice touch, as was the fresh grapefruit.  I found some redemption by squeezing lots of fresh lemon as well as lightly dressing the crab with their house dressing (tasty but most likely had some sugar in it, something I try to avoid), plus some salt and pepper.   But that said, I will never get Mr. B to return here.  This definitely did not meet his standard of a crab salad.  I agree.

Strangers to Boise, yet Yelp Boise was good to Mr. B and me.  Moe Joe's gave us good, solid memories of a meal we would like to repeat.  This is the kind of place that every hungry traveler (me being one of those types), every non-local, hopes to find for a satisfying breakfast.

I trust my friends.  And if they say the Garden Hash is good, I say, why not.  The two of us shared.   A huge plate came out, two eggs topping a large serving of artichokes, sautéed cherry tomatoes, zucchini, bell pepper, chipotle, mushroom, melted swiss cheese, and avocado over a raw spinach bed.  I had to nix the garlic only because  Michele R said it was strong, and I did not want to be burping the remainder of the day in the small confines of our car as we made our getaway toward new adventures.  That would not have been pleasant.   

Let's not forget their beautiful (Idaho) breakfast potatoes.  A great temptation here.  And I had essentially sworn off potatoes.   Right.

And the Chicken Fried Steak.  Possibly one of the best to have ever crossed my lips. It was not  mine to share, but somehow a chunk with the most amazing gravy magically appeared on my plate.  I shall have to thank the CFS gods, or was it really Mr. B instead? 

Lucky locals!  Not only is the menu creative and appealing, it is clean, spacious, upbeat and welcoming.  The prices are most reasonable.  My tummy says, "Hey Yelpers, you certainly got this one right."

I shall keep this one for my bookmarks.

Frankly, I have never been known to turn down a true pastry experience, but even I am aware when in the presence of a master. This is an extraordinary patisserie. 

This quiet little neighborhood French cafe oozes with the smell of buttery goods and great coffee. The cases are filled with perfect little pastries, sweet and savory, the interior enveloped with a clean white glow, with white laminate tables inside and bistro tables outdoors.  I found myself transported to the other side of the world where the L'arc de Triomphe and La Tour Eiffel cast their shadows, mimes and street musicians entertain, and a little bossa nova and jazz whets the appetite for l'amour and a pat of butter.  Hey, I can dream, can't I?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wwLtHGZHelA

Needless to say, we ordered too much.  Needless to say, no one twisted our arm to eat it either.  But pastry in one hand, excellent coffee in other, we happily blew through our choices and licked up the crumbs when no one was looking.

Spinach quiche, almond croissant, quiche Lorraine, and kougin amann filled with raspberry coulis, they were all quite special.  I had to suppress my envy.

This is where genius and pastry royalty reside. You should go pay hommage.  Not to be missed.

Hot Prime Rib sandwich - do it !  You won't regret it.

My beau has been coming here for years, and his company ordering lunch often - I finally got to check this place out with him and I'm sad I didn't get a chance sooner!

He recommended the prime rib sandwich, he got one as well.
Fries, and a side of home made pickles rounded it out.

The bread, garlic bread I might add, was awesome.
We spoke not a word to each other, and just ate in silence.
Giving winks and smiles to each other here and there noting how good the sandwich was.

The fries were great also, requested well done.

I retracted a star, for a few things.
The plates were seriously old, like scratch marks and chips out of the plates, dark marks that wouldn't come off.  Granted it's not a frilly place, but...I think the plates should have been replaced.  The prime rib had a LOT of fat.  I was able to work around it and it was still delicious, but this was seriously fatty...fattier than any prime rib I've never come across.  The price, the prices of sandwiches are high - but you do get a gigantic serving.  

Service was stellar, friendly, attentive just enough during the busy lunch rush.
Place seemed popular with the locals and not locals alike.

I can't wait to go back!

Nothing to write home about! Just ok food. I had the Del Mar taco (grilled shrimp). $4.75 taco with 3 shrimp and a gang of cabbage and sauce. I've had way better. The chips and salsa was hit-and-miss too. The chips were good but that salsa was bland and watery. My sister ordered the Mexican Pizza and only ate 2 slices and tapped out. My mom had the chicken nacho, which were good, except for some of the burnt pieces. Considering there are many other Mexican eateries on State St., my recommendation is let this restaurant be your LAST choice!

Wow, this place is fantastic!  My food arrived more quickly than expected and it was delish!  The portions were really big and the prices not bad.  I'll definitely being ordering from Iztaccihuatl again!

I wanted to experience Gendusa's so I invited a friend to lunch. I ordered eggplant Parmesan and it tasted great but the spaghetti must have been warmed under water because the whole plate was swimming in water. It shocked me that I was served cold pasta! That's not how true Italian's do it!

Omg. Omg. Omg. What an amazing place to eat. I have never been so satisfied with a meal. Guru is the place to go if you are looking for delicious Indian cuisine. Firstly, the service was superb. Our servers name was Kevin (ask for him, he is great) and I couldn't have been more pleased. From the moment we walked into Guru till we left he made sure we were taken care of, but it definitely wasn't over kill. When I wasn't sure on the wine I wanted he brought me a sample of one he thought I might like... he was right, I loved it. He did the exact same thing with the boyfriends beer. Over the course of the evening he gave us numerous recommendations, all of which were spot on. He was also charismatic and funny! 

But, onto the food. The butter chicken samosas are amazing, they have won numerous awards in Edmonton and I can definitely see why. For our main course we had more butter chicken, mango chicken, coconut rice and garlic naan bread. Let me just take a moment to tell you that the naan bread is to-die-for. Order it. The food came quickly, and I just wanted to keep eating more as I let it melt in my mouth. God, I wish I was there right now! We ate about half of the food on the table and were stuffed, but Kevin graciously offered to pack up all our food in separate containers so it would be easy for us to take to work  the next day. 

At this point I didn't think I could handle dessert, but we were told these little tin-bit like donuts dipped in honey and put in this creamy sugar sauce was amazing, yet again the recommendation was spot on. Thank goodness this dessert dish was tiny because at this point I was thinking I would need to be rolled out of Guru. 

What a great restaurant, the dishes are a little pricey, and the location is in the west end, but you get so much food and it's totally worth the drive! It wasn't busy when we went, but you can email ahead for reservations! I wish Guru was located downtown because then I would definitely frequent it more often!

My first time dining here. Was in town for Titan game and stayed in the area. A friend invites us to meet them here for dinner and was pleasantly surprised. Reminds me of Houston's restaurant that use to be near Vandy and also Atlanta. Very warm atmosphere, low lighting and great bar. 

Service is excellent throughout the night. I had the ribs which are fall if the bone good. Sides were fried and cream corn. The corn was  so good I could have eat more.  Wife got the Prime rib and was very pleased.  

We had some minor issues with a drink that was not prepared right and they were very quick to replace it and took it off our tab. We need one of these in the Chattanooga area.

Food really not that great. Fried shrimp was small and barely warm when it arrived. Drinks were ok, but over priced for what you get. Two drinks in and no sign of a buzz, little alcohol in drink. Hostess down stairs was cute and helpful and found us a seat upstairs very quick. 

Not sure if we would come back with so many options in the area.

Outside of above average cheesecake I don't see the overall appeal. I have been to several and the wife wanted to eat here while in town. Reasonable wait of 30 minutes then go out table in center of seating area. Of course they are out of what I set my mind to. Order shrimp but after 5 minutes inform me they are out. 

I ended up getting catfish dinner but breaking was thick and too hard. Just not what I wanted. Decided to cut my losses and save room for the cheesecake. Good choice!

Never go wrong with the desert.

Great place to sample the seafood and oysters right off Bourbon St.  Acme has the longest lines but I think this place is at a minimum very close to same quality. 

During my week I sampled several styles of oysters and shrimp and loved it all. It's crazy with service as crowded as they get during normal dinner hours so I tried to get in a little early. 

Also they have more than one entrance. Check both to see where you want to enter.

This is the second choice for Beignet's in this town after the famous Cafe Du Monde.  The difference is not in the quality or taste of the Beignet's.  Its more the atmosphere here vs mass produce at the other.

They have several in town but we loved this place because of the outside area off Royal St.  You walk in and get your order and then sit and they bring out your order.

The hole-less donuts or Beignet's as they are called are incredible and go perfectly with the hot chocolate or cafe Au Lait.  They have more choices on the menu here too, if your with someone wanting to back off the sugar magnet.

Without a doubt, one of the best meals I had over the week in New Orleans. Our server was Ike and he was a show all by himself. This guy knows the menu and can explain every dish with bold statements and humerus tales. He made his recommendations to the table including the incredible deserts and we were ready to order. 

Red Fish has a pretty diverse menu so I ordered the BBQ Chicken as my main. Loved the BBQ sauce and chicken was tender and great over rice. Our table of 5 all ordered different items and loved them all. 

For appetizer we got the BBQ Oysters and OMG were they good. Best oysters I had all week. Even if you think you don't like oysters you would love these. 

They also have great bread.  Bread is one of my vices and it was warm and perfect. 

The chocolate desert with ice cream was a perfect ending. The pour white and dark chocolate over it at your table. It's a group desert, too much for one. 

This will be my number 1 place when I return here.

This is just your average mom and pop shop breakfast diner-- nothing more, nothing less. I was honestly a bit disappointed since I found this place through yelp when I narrowed my breakfast search to 'best rating' 

Denise K and I parked across the street and walked over. We were immediately seated at a table for two in the back. 

After studying the menu, Denise K got a small orange juice ($2.69) and the avocado omelette w swiss cheese (their omelettes are made w 3 eggs) and she chose hashbrown and wheat bread ($9.49). Since I was craving something a bit sweet, I ordered the french toast special: 2 eggs over easy w bacon ($6.69) and a small cranberry juice ($1.99).

I don't recall what Denise K said about her OJ, but I felt like my cranberry juice was syrupy and weird tasting, worst than the juice they have in the dining halls back in college. The food was okay though. I tried her omelette and it was good, but good because we like avocado and swiss, not because it was extra special or anything. My french toast was kinda bland. The egg white part of my over easy were a bit slimy -_- which defeats the purpose of why I wanted them over easy to begin with... And the bacon was dry. 

I wouldn't mind this place if I actually lived in this area and I was just waking up w a breakfast foods craving, but definitely not somewhere I would recommend to a fellow tourist...

My boyfriend and I couldn't get a table at Olio Pizzeria, one of our favorite places in SB, due to SB Film Festival crowds so we decided to try Relais de Paris, about which he'd heard great things. 

I loved EVERYTHING about the experience (including the prices). I gave it 5 stars not because it is "the same" as Bouchon, our high-end French restaurant in Victoria Court. But the food, the service, the decor, the value are all top notch and the prices are truly below what such food ordinarily costs in LA and SB. In NYC, there is a place on the Lower East Side which serves terrific French bistro food. It's vastly cheaper than the same food on the Upper East Side of course, with the highest concentration of French in Manhattan. But here in LA or SB, French is always at the very top price point.  

There is a range of starters including the mussels and French onion in the 8 to 11 range. These are fine to pair as an entree and there are high teens dishes which can be enjoyed without an appetizer, keeping the bill down.

J ordered the steak--perfectly seared on the outside and rare inside--in the signature secret sauce. I must bring a cooking friend or two here and they can analyze its contents. 

The bread is from Brea Bakery in LA. Usually this is very hard and crunchy crust with thin (rather than dense) dough inside. I have never eaten a baguette from Brea anything like this and will avoid buying a loaf in LA as it's highly addictive, particularly when dipped in the secret sauce or my buerre blanc with the mussels, an appetizer which functioned as my entree with a glass of 6 dollar champagne (more than adequate) and a 9 dollar glass of Sauvignon which replaced the Brander. It was good but a bit sweet for my tastes and I'll try another wine on Valentine's Day where J and I will go to celebrate our third such holiday as a couple. 

We saw many dishes and all looked equally scrumptious. The wine list is good and cheap! Bottles range from 20 to 48 and glasses from 5 to 12, with far more in the under 10 than over 10 range. 

I was truly blown away and it's also a comfortable restaurant with real space between the tables. We sat at the only available table not right by the door--the banquette--and it was a nice view of the bar and the original brick of this building. 

The chandeliers--four--are all gorgeous and different. 

There is nothing bad to be said about this place and I am looking forward to Valentine's Day. 

The most expensive entree is this special steak which comes with pomme frites (fries). J subbed veggies and they were plentiful and delicious. Entrees come with a lovely small salad with walnuts and a vinaigrette and they bring you as much of the bread with the sweet, fluffy butter as you desire. 

Just terrific and less than Opal, Olio e Limone, Bucatini, Tre Lune and other restaurants at this price point I like. Bouchon and Downey's are a notch higher than the aforementioned places though I think Tre Lune can definitely be in that range if you do appetizer and entree and drink well.

This review is solely for the Gorgonzola cheese bought to me as a gift from my darling brother and his lovely gf.

Jesus, Joseph and Mary (in an Irish brogue)!!
This cheese transported me to an out of this world experience. After the initial bite, I left the planet, flew to the moon, danced and wined with aliens then landed back to Earth. Holy cow! It literally melted in my mouth, there's no chewing required whatsoever. I already had my crackers out to elevate the cheese, but after that bite, I put them away. It's so smooth, has the perfect texture (not too firm or too soft) and has the perfect amount of buttery creaminess, that it totally stands well on its own. The taste is so subtle but flavorful where nothing else is required besides a beautiful glass of wine to accentuate that wonderful aftertaste. I'm not a fan of blue cheese but this one, won me over.

If you're looking for a gift or souvenir, look no further, this is you're wining ticket.

Oh.  Hell.  No.  

Look, I think good food is great - I can even make good food myself but instead I choose to go out because I can pay for food and service. 

I consider service a very important part of my experience.  

I do not consider "good" service to be free from mistakes.  People get busy and everyone makes mistakes.   A personable staff member can navigate even the most complicated situations with a glad attitude and I'm happy every time.  So no need to be perfect, just have a good attitude about what we are all here for.  Some people get this and can make your experience shine even when the food isn't great.  

Some people don't get this and quite frankly I don't even need to stick around for the food.  I won't hand you my money.  

Miguel's on this particular night featured four people who seemed to SCREAM "WE CANNOT STAND YOU" to their patrons.  I was one of them, so I left, but listen to the impressive job they did of letting us know how much they hated us!  It's entertaining if nothing else!

I immediately knew the atmosphere at Miguel's is terse, full of staff who bristle because patrons make their job harder.  Just the lady who seated us made that perfectly clear.  

We were a party of four, and we're seated in the center of the tiny dining room. It's very tight, loud and uncomfortable.  Eight feet away was a section with luxurious booths and spacious tables. I asked if we could be seated there.  Ewwwww boy, did the little baby boy who wanders around the dining room, aimless and clueless, being barked at by the rude staff who trained him, bubble with glee as he supped loudly on the satisfaction of telling me, "No, that section is closed."

Fair enough.  Time to order while munching on decent chips and salsa.  

Me: "I'll have this."  Her: (annoyed) "Yeah, that's the lunch menu."  -silence-

Me: "is that on the dinner menu?"  Her: (annoyed) "Yes." -silence-

Me: "Ok I'll have that."

Just some "Human Interaction 101" here, you don't need to be a "restauranteur" to grasp this logic, but wouldn't you, after the initial "Ill have this" offer something like, "Ok the dinner portion is 8.99 and comes with a salad, that ok?"

You can even say it rudely, I don't mind.  Just put your hatred for your patrons on pause for four minutes while they order, then you can go back to hating them when this happens...

"The little one will have a small Horcha-" I'm cut off with, "Horchata only comes in one size".  Ok I'll take it.  I'm still hopeful this third person I've encountered tonight here at Miguel's doesn't fall out from hatred-for-her-patrons overload.  

The Horchata (ordered for a child) arrives in a huge 32oz glass.  I know it is way too much to ask for this staff to see for themselves that this child trying to lift this full glass would be a disaster, so I (always very courteous) ask the hatred-riddled waitress, "Could I have a small glas-" I'm cut off with "We don't have small glasses".  I accept that because, well, I'm not sure what I am experiencing here.  It's either hatred burning like the fire of a thousand suns inside each of the staff at Miguel's or staggering incompetence.  I'll let you decide.

About three feet to my right is a tray of water glasses about half the size of my child's 32oz Horchata glass.  I glance at them and the waitress sees that.  She says, "You mean like those glasses?" and immediately gestures to the clueless, aimless baby boy (I expect he's someone on staff's son and nobody knows what to do with him) to get me one.  So without looking - and seething with hatred like he's been taught by the staff he's surrounded by, he fills it with water and puts it on the table on his way across the room. Ugh.  

My kid continues to gaze longingly at his glistening tower of Horchata, so I take the very simple matter into my own hands.  There's (what appears to be) a nice older man behind the bar.  I walk over to him (dodging the clueless baby boy) and ask politely, can I have a small glass?  It's a BAR.  The bar back is LINED with small glasses just PERFECT for what I need.  I'm so full of hope at this moment...

He walks around the bar, leads me through the dining room and hands me a water glass from where the day-care kid got one earlier.  

::sigh::

Ok at least it's empty.  We use it for the Horchata, and my little one is now getting Horchata-wasted while I'm pondering what the hell the last ten minutes have been about.  I'm getting mad because either they hate us (and the rest of their patrons) or are suffering from debilitating incompetence (I suspect it's a combination of the two) and I don't want to hand my money over to either of those two class of business people.  

Then I see the baby boy seating a party in the luxurious section where I had asked to be seated earlier.  You better believe I said something.  

Me to day-care kid: "Is that section still closed?"  Him: "No but there was nowhere else to seat them." (I look around at three empty tables).

Nope.  Goodbye.

This place is disgusting, bread was soggy, the meat had no seasoning whatsoever. We looked in the window and we saw that the workers were not even wearing gloves while preparing our food. Dont go here, you will be only wasting your money.

We read about their soft-opening, starting today. Decided to risk going on their first day of business!

So glad we did. WGG is small, not fancy at all, but with a great menu of tasty items.

 We had two starters. (1) Gilroy garlic Swiss fondue, $7, and (2) Steamed PEI Mussels, $10. We shared an entree of Las Cruces chili spiced mesquite honey BBQ ribs, $14..

A nice, reasonably priced wine list too.

Sit at the bar and watch Chef Steve Schultz work his magic.

Food and value is excellent - we will be going back.

So I'm staying in an Airbnb nearby and tried this deli out for breakfast and was blown at how amazing the food was. Something as simple as a bacon egg and cheese was practically orgasmic highly recommended !!

The rooftop views and decor are really nice BUT if they don't improve their customer service they will have problems winning over Philly foodies. I wish I got  the waiter's name that was extremely rude to me and my party (5 of us) , so we'll call him "Ass". The female manager, the hostess, servers and the bartenders were nice and helped redeem that "Ass", so that's the reason for my 2 stars instead of 1. I may go back and give them 1 more chance but I really hope I don't see that "Ass" again.

***Just checked my instagram account***
