Never going back and telling all of family and friends not to go either.

We came here because of 3 reasons it was on the Yelp, Nearby trending restaurant and 2nd reason the hotel concierge recommended this restaurant 3rd the breakfast pictures. 
We loved this little cafe. Is always a good sign you the restaurant is full and not a table, seat available.

The staff are really on top of their game cleaning a booth and they quickly offered us a table or booth, two clean cups are already set up on the table, they bring the coffee and always have it almost to the rim because the waiter is always there offering more coffee great service.

Yelp picture were really helpful we ordered as shown on the most popular picture the Spicy Sausage-Chilaquilles,
The Chilaquilles, are layered in such way that the eggs are next to the avocados and the sour cream is next to the layer of the hot and spicy sausage.
Chicken Fried Steak and home fries and choice bread, delicious and a  bit heavy for breakfast, However, there is always room for the 
Sugar Sprinkled Beignets it was paired well with our coffee.
Let me tell you the power of the pictures was huge here because, we ordered two separate breakfast meals that  we saw on Yelp, the portions are huge and we could have ordered one of the breakfast dishes and shared it and would have been satisfied and happy.
No we could not take it to go since we are on vacay and do not have a refrigerator. Our next stop is UCSB.

My tip order one and share it the portions are big enough for two people.

The service was great! from bus boy, waiter they were really friendly and always keeping the coffee to the brimmed. 

Parking is behind and on the side of the cafe. Easy breezy.

Found Los Arroyos Restaurant by using the Yelp app and it was very satisfying. After a long drive we were starved.
They have indoor and outdoor dining and we dined outside they have outdoor heaters to take the night chill away.
Our sever Marco's, provided professional service. By greeting us with a friendly tone and a big smile.
He quickly, brought out tortillas chips with both a mild salsa and a hot salsa. 
We order consisted of the following Green Chicken Enchiladas with black beans served in a cute fried tortilla in a vase. Quesadilla entree it was more like a appetizer  it was very tasty. Also, a Hand made tacos but the Chimichanga stole the show because of its size. Everything was just perfectly plated perfectly delicious with perfect weather to enjoy our outdoor dining. 

Definitely recommend Los Arroyos Mexican restaurant in Montecito.

This is such a cute place!  There are pink walls, a big chandelier and a  large  sofa flanking one wall.  In front of the sofa is a table filled with free samples, which everyone seemed to be partaking of as well as a stack of pink menus.  When I walked in I was greeted by one of the workers who handed me a menu.  He pointed to a gorgeous cabinet filled with cupcakes and said that he will get me whatever cupcakes I wanted.  I was like a kid in a cupcake store!  After much deliberation, I decided on the Red Velvet cupcake with Cream Cheese Icing.  My cake was so moist and fresh and the icing was nice and light and beautifully decorated for the holidays.  They also have mini cupcakes if you just want a little bite too.  The staff is very attentive and everyone was so happy and cheery.  They are located right near my office, so I know where to go if I need a little something sweet to eat.  If there is a cupcake heaven, this is it.

Wow! Just wow! I just discovered this amazing sushi place last week after reading about it on a foodies page. We went back again tonight. 

It's. That. Good!

At this time, they are just doing curbside pickup and delivery. I have been doing the curbside pickup after calling them to order. It is super smooth, quick, and friendly service. 

Last week, I ordered more to my son's taste, which is more straight forward and without too much spice or sauces. I really enjoyed it (obviously, since we already returned), but I was missing out on the potential a bit. Today, I ordered a bit more towards my style and it was even better... and he enjoyed it all, too. Stretching those taste buds!  ;)

Everything has been extremely fresh and tasty. Not too much rice, either. They also have a deal right now, since you cannot do the AYCE. It is basically 3 long rolls for $18.95 (and maybe 3 for $24.95 if you order certain ones? I didn't quite catch that part). Basically, it's the price of AYCE per person. They also have some kind of special for some of the appetizers and such. Just ask when you order.

We have enjoyed everything we have ordered. Some of the dishes are sure to be ordered every time in the future, too!

Over our trips we have enjoyed the following:

Appetizers: Calamari, Mussels, and Yakiton. They were all tasty, but we did not reorder the calamari or mussels. We probably will sometime in the future (especially if doing the AYCE), but we had too many other things we wanted to try the second time instead.

My son especially likes the Yakiton. This is basically a cream cheese and seafood roll that is similar to an eggroll. It is cut in half at an angle. Different and pretty tasty!

Nigiri Sushi: My "Sushi-Buddy" and I are big fans of Nigiri. We have tried: the Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck, Goofy, Upside Down Shrimp, and IKA (squid). 

The Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck are very similar to each other, but should not be missed IMHO. Oh my! The Mickey Mouse has tuna, avocado, crab, and sauce. The Donald Duck has salmon, avocado, crab, and sauce. They come in orders of two each. I just say get an order of both! 

Goofy is rather tasty, too. We added that tonight. It has tempura salmon. Oh ya... 

Another one of my favorite bites is the Upside Down Shrimp. It's full of shrimp, crab, and rice... just the right amount of everything. My son loved the IKA, which is a squid Nigiri. It was tasty and fresh.

Now for the long rolls. We have experienced over our times of feasting aka "AYCE at home" the following: Snow Mountain, Rainbow Roll, Pink Lady, Paradise, Rocky, Tornado (minus the jalapeno), California Deluxe, Black Tiger, and Spider Rolls.

My absolute favorite at this time is the Tornado! It has tempura salmon, jalapeno, spicy crab, avocado, scallops, green onion, and Tobiko. We ordered ours without the jalapeno, so my son would probably like it, too. It was perfection and I will likely order this every time! I honestly don't think I will order it with jalapeno at anytime, though, because like I said, this was already perfection.

Snow Mountain was sure tasty, too! It has avocado, crystal shrimp, assorted fish, and spicy crab on top. We love most rolls with the assorted fish and the spicy crab is not too spicy for my son. These were a big hit. 

Paradise was a big winner, too. It has crystal shrimp, crab, cucumber, hamachi, salmon, scallops, Tobiko, and onion. This was the one with the most going on that my son rated so highly. He wanted more of this roll, for sure!

Because of our love for the assorted fish types of rolls, we obviously enjoyed the Rainbow Roll, which has avocado, cucumber, crab, assorted fish, and Tobiko on top. My son is also a huge fan of the Tobiko.

The Pink Lady was yummy, It has spicy crab, crystal shrimp, and some crab on top.

Rocky was "different", but in a refreshing and tasty way. It has spicy crab, cucumber, hamachi, lemon, green onion, and scallops on top. Of course, we enjoyed the scallops, but the lemon was a bit of a shock to the taste buds with the first bite (didn't realize it had the lemon until then). I love lemon, but usually only it certain places. This was a pleasant surprise.

The Black Tiger was good, but not as flavorful as several other options. It has tempura shrimp, avocado, seared tuna, and unagi on top.

I was a bit underwhelmed with the Spider Roll. I really had my hopes up when I read that it has soft shell crab, cucumber, and avocado. It didn't travel as well as the rest, either. There really wasn't anything wrong, it was just "there".

My son has been a longtime fan of California Rolls and this Deluxe version was nice and fresh. Great price, too.

Would I change anything? I do wish that there were more raw items and not so many rolls with cream cheese. Also, even though the crystal shrimp is really tasty, I would love more variety there, too.

All in all... a new favorite of ours and I love that it can easily be on our way home.
The big guitar reminds me of the one in Universal Studio in Los Angeles. In a very busy location. Very nice restaurant. Food is always decent. Service is great as well.

What a great museum! The architecture is beautiful. Love the sculptures and fountain in front of the museums. Also, the Rocky statue and the famous Rocky stairs!! This is a popular tourist attraction stop. All the hop-on hop-off tour bus stop at this location. 

Definitely a must visit place!

If you like "varieties" of food.... this is the MUST GO place!! So many different vendors selling food, beverage, dessert, etc. One of the popular place in town for sure~

This place reminds me of Grand Central Market in Los Angeles!! 

There are different bus lines pass by this market. Also, if you are taking the hop-on hop-off tour bus, there is a stop at this location as well.

Traveling solo isn't for everyone, but I find great joy in moving on your own clock, admiring the details usually circumvented by chat tennis, and drowning in a good game hanging above your head.

Flew out to St. Louis for business last week and after a long 2 flights, found my way into the Brewhouse. Home.

A 'U' shaped wooden bar beckoned as I comfortably found the corner slot. A cold Stella eased the drowning of crying babies and marriage issues which littered the plane.

Multiple screens hung above, like an aerial buffet of baseball games.

Luckily, the Giants were on and everyone else had succumbed to the fact that their Cards were done.

The menu is straight up Mid Western. Brisket, burgers, pulled pork and ribs. 

When in St. Louis attack the ribs. Ordered the full rack with a side of fries and slaw. Served on a large platter, you can recall what life must've been like for our neanderthal brothers.

Smoky, with an even layer of bbq sauce, the pork was as tender as the steam rising above it. The boneyard grew quickly, and there wasn't a wet wipe that was going to stop me.

Up front service, kept tabs on me well, and the brew came on a consistent basis. 

Not sure I'll be in St. Louis again,   ( I saw the entire 5 blocks of it. Solid ), but if I do venture back, I'm sure I'll build up another graveyard.

BBQ without bandanas, tin plates and peanuts? Blasphemy thou are not! The Shaved Duck takes bbq out of the country clown costume, kicks it off the turnip truck and brings it to a respectable, urban neighborhood dwelling. I like that TSD sounds a bit fancy pants, that you don't smell cooked pig a half mile away, and that you don't smell like it coming out.

TSD is actually quite intimate, the dining area is small, and the bar area in front is decked in dark woods and tall chairs. The beer menu is excellent; a list full of interesting craft beers with descriptions, which makes them fun to read and fun to order. By the end of the night the nameless one and I sampled about 5, my favorite was the Lagunitas Lil Sumpin' Sumpin'. I love Lagunitas brew, and it's always a treat to find new varieties of it in places you don't expect.

We ordered the hush duckies and wings as an appetizer. The wings came recommended by Erin G. so I knew that we had to get them, and they were awesome! I love when wings are dry rubbed and cooked thoroughly instead of those slimy chicken arms. As a side but very important note, if you get the wings you get the mango barbeque sauce with them. This stuff is SO GOOD. Like our waiter said, he would dip a roof shingle in that stuff and eat it. We ended up using that on all of our meats instead of the three flavors at the table. For the main we split the sampler dinner, which had pulled pork, pulled chicken, stl ribs, and brisket. If you are a picky brisket eater, you must go here. I have a hard time finding brisket that I like. At most places, it is thick hunks of fatty meat that you have to cut with a knife. Brisket at TSD was so tender you could cut it with a spoon if you needed and there was hardly any fat in it. It made me wish that I didn't have to share it with boy nameless. When anyone talks brisket I will definitely recommend TSD.

Live music is also part of TSD culture. This totally makes the experience for me because I love when small places have a local musician playing in the dining room or bar with you, and, from reading the upcoming set list I could tell they were playing the right kind of music, American, Roots, and Blues. Well at least that week.

Leaving the TSD I was envious of the houses next door. I wish I lived so close to a place to take friends and family for an awesome dinner and also just to have a nice relaxed bar to hang out after work with an appetizer and some good beer.

I smashed the shit out of that baja burger today for lunch. Jalapenos, spicy cheese, chipotle sauce, and guac on a toasted onion bun, what could go wrong? Nothing!  

Smashburger has got to be my new favorite place in the Saint Charles/Peter's Vortex of no return. Def a spot to hit for work lunch on days after binge running or binge drinking, Smash is where it's at. 

Those sweet potato smash fries were the best I've ever had. Ferreal.

Better go early, we got there at 11:30 and just after we sat down, there was a line up to the door. All those sad line people watching me smash a burger, made me feel bad for like a second. 

Smashburgerworkers even come by to refill your drinks, totes awesome when you're scrounging on a spicy baja burg.

Next time I'm back to try a shake!

It's Friday. I'm recovering from a sleep deprivation hangover. So what do I do? I go and get myself Bo Funged. And I liked it.

Bo Fung is like a block from my house, and ever since I moved here I would look at this place and shudder. I actually thought it wasn't even open, it looks like a vacant crack house or dead body storage or where that rat from teenage mutant ninja turtles keeps his lair, if he were Chinese and stuff.

Anyway, that noise below about Hot Braised Chicken is no joke. I didn't even know what in the Chinese calendar hell Hot Braised Chicken was but I got it anyway. Why? Because if that many people are going into Bo Fung We Really Don't Hide Dead Bodies Chinese Kitchen and talk about one specific dish at a chinese place for fried rice's sake, that shit has got to be good.

I mean that chicken meat was tight and white!

The rice, lo mein, egg roll, and rangoons were also better quality than you get at the chain chinese like the china gardens and friends that you see everywhere. 

So like, Fung Off my friends. Tell em Splinter sent you.

COWAFUNGA!!!

I always get a croissant with salami and turkey, smokey cheddar cheese! Never has it not been amazing!

Can you think of anything else you could possibly need on a sandwich? 

They also have soups that's change daily, and premise salads. And since it is a gas station, there are plenty of chips drinks and other smack to choose from. You need to try it! At least once! :)

This place has great service, and a large menu. You can get breakfast or lunch. 

When you walk in the door you feel at home. This place is usually pretty busy, which doesn't usually scare me away. If people are lining up to eat here, they must be doing something right!

Today I ordered lunch, a wrap with their homemade potato salad. Service was on point, fast, efficient, and friendly as always.

Food came out quickly and correct. It was flavorful and hot! My husband ordered breakfast and it was cooked to his liking. 

We were checked on several times, and taken great care of. We will be back to eat at this cute place again.

I am not a DIY Korean BBQ AYCE expert by a long shot. But I had some fun and a great meal here and look forward to going back. 

First, make a reservation and consider going at unpopular times such as mid-afternoon. They are sticking to the pandemic plan of distancing and limiting seating capacity so an already popular place becomes even more difficult to get into. I actually like the pandemic odds of eating here given that every table also has an exhaust ventilation hood operating over it. For those that have either had COVID-19 disease, the vaccination, or both, dining here when there are fewer people AND you have some negative ventilation occurring seems like a good risk:benefit ratio in my calculations. For the record, this is the first place I have eaten at (indoors) since the pandemic started. 

Lunch pricing is less than dinner (dinner starts at 4pm and is about $12 more and you can pay the dinner price during lunch hours if you ask) but dinner opens up several things on the menu that are worth it in my opinion. Primarily the Woo-Sul (tongue) and the Galbi (Bone-in Shortrib) were pretty amazing on the dinner menu. On the lunch menu, don't miss the fried oysters, the baby octopi, the refreshing sesame dressed salad, and the Chardol (thin-sliced brisket). All of those items were a table favorite during my visit. Be sure to ask for some lettuce leaves and hot bean paste and wrap the brisket up in them for a tasty and palate cleansing option. And shame on you if you don't gnaw on the Galbi bones until they are clean!

The process of eating here is really at least half the fun. Cooking your own food means you are assuming the risk of making your own bad meal but it is such a social event with everyone reaching in and getting grease-splatter burns so who cares if some of your items go over done? Besides, it is AYCE so if you screw up and make yourself a slice of charcoal, just order it again after you choke it down so you can take another run at getting it perfect next time. I did find that things cook much quicker than you anticipate and taking it off early allows it to continue to cook on your plate from the retained heat so pay attention and watch your times (hard to do when this is such a social process) or you run the risk of grilling a great piece of leather. 

For the haters that have given this place a bad review, I do understand since there are many world-class Korean BBQ spots in many big-cities all over the world. Siu is not in this caliber so I agree that there are going to be things they could improve upon such as increasing their selection of banchan. However, the flip side of that is recognizing that you are enjoying AYCE Korean BBQ in the middle of a NV cow-town surrounded by a desert and a mountain range with no other places that even come close to offering this genre of food for over 300 miles in all directions. I think that alone gets them an above average rating just for making a reasonable attempt at delivering in this setting which they succeed at. Add to that a very friendly, helpful and attentive crew of waitstaff and a price that is worth it especially for big eaters and I really can't find a reason to look to deduct stars from their review. Yes, you might find a better selection of items or more variety of banchan in LA or San Fran but you wouldn't care if you had to get in a car or plane for several hours to get there to enjoy it. My perspective is that Siu gets it nicely done for the people of Reno that are looking for just this type of experience.

This was a great discovery near my hotel in Reno. Not sure how I have missed this on previous visits but am happy to have found it now. Yes, it is in the genre of Mexican "fast food" but it is not particularly "fast" (since they cook and assemble everything upon order and things are not sitting under heat lamps waiting to be used) and it does not suffer from the typical US influences into Mexican fast food that turns it more into Tex-Mex versions of things or worse. 

It passed many of my subjective wants in this type of food place: 1) It is open 24/7 and it has a drive through (convenient for jet-lagged travelers like me seeking sustenance in the middle of the night). 2) It appeared to me to have Mexican people in it running the place and everyone in line ordering and eating there also appeared to be of Mexican descent (Food authenticity is best tested by those cooking it and eating it in my book). 3) It was clean. They were clearly complying with all of the COVID-19 related mandates and their employees were prompt, friendly and efficient. 4) It was affordable (as my photo shows, $7 for a meal of authentic food available anytime is well worth it). 5) And for the bonus round, they have some great complimentary condiments (normally inside has a salsa bar that is not available during COVID-19 but on my drive through order, I received salsa rojo, salsa verde, individually bagged limes, and some classic escabeche (Mexican pickled vegetables) to go along with my meal!

Having been there only once, I can only comment on the Carne Asada Tacos I had. They were great. Tasty, stuffed full with coarse chopped thin steak, pico de gallo and a thin schmear of avocado paste. Really delicious and satisfied the craving. My only complaint is that they are single corn tortilla-wrapped which is probably how they keep the cost down ($3.25 each!) but a single tortilla is insufficient to effectively contain the volume of ingredients. Upon picking them up and trying to stuff them in my mouth, the tortilla promptly burst on both of them and I end up eating my meal more like a salad with a fork due to all the spillage. Oh well, small price to pay for greatness!

Given all of this goodness, based on my single visit, I found nothing to dislike and lots to love about Roberto's!i

The greatness of this place may be lost on you unless you are really into food from all aspects. If you are someone with a sophisticated palate and your bucket list does not go beyond Michelin 2 and 3 star establishments, you will likely disavow The Habit as a legitimate contender for a solid meal. It is a small, nondescript greasy hovel which most people would drive by if they didn't know any better. But if you are like me and look beyond fine dining for the real story behind great food, there is a lot to like here. 

This particular location in Goleta is the original Habit burger stand established in 1969. It is a less well known but just as important institution in the So Cal burger genre along the lines of In-N-Out. And while In-N-Out is still my favorite burger, The Habit has better add ons so I can be happy eating at either and maybe even both in the same day!

The story here is a tasty charbroiled burger at a decent price. The chargrill taste does add another dimension to the burger which is a nice touch. Their fries are solid and crispy but the newly found show stopper for me on this visit were the Tempura Green Beans. Who knew? I also love that they have a condiment caddy at the window stacked with 3 free kinds of peppers: sliced jalapeños, whole pepperoncinis, and tiny whole mexihots that are full of heat and make you sweat. Those little addictive add-ons are awesome!

The menu is a bit more expanded than a typical burger chain too since they have a Santa Barbara Burger (Sourdough plus avocado...really fantastic!) and also things like chicken sandwiches, Ahi tuna sandwich, Tri-tip sandwich, and a veggie burger(!) which almost seems blasphemous at a burger joint. No one around me ordered those things so I can't really vouch for any of them. And seriously, if you come to The Habit and order a veggie burger you probably deserve to be choked out and put in the back dumpster while waiting for your order. 

Don't miss this little gem of a burger stand if you are in the area. There is a small parking lot in the rear which is a pro tip recommendation as parking is tough to find on the street. And don't miss those hot peppers. Nothing completes the foodie look more than to have rivulets of sweat and burger juice running down your face while seated under the awning of a 1969 original.

If you want some damn good pretzels, Gus' is the place to be. This St. Louis institution makes some of the best pretzels I've ever had. Dare I say it, I think they might be better than my Auntie Anne's pretzels (see what I did there, lol).

My friend and I wanted a light snack before dinner so we ordered a garlic butter pretzel with gooey cheddar cheese dip, a cinnamon sugar pretzel, the salsiccia pretzel sandwich, a stick and a twist. 

The pretzels come out piping hot and after taking a bite, you know they're as fresh as can be. My favorite was the salciccia pretzel sandwich which consist of a pretzel wrapped around a spicy sausage. I recommend dipping in the cheddar dip. My only complaint is that the stick and twist pretzels had a really thick coating of salt -- had to rub some of it off.

There's plenty of street parking as well as a super small parking lot in the back. Be warned, this place is cash only and the line can get super long.

First off it's instant seating on Easter Sunday dinner. The place was packed, but very large seating area. 

The waitress that greeted us was chipper and very nice. I didn't expect that in a holiday. She asked us for a drink/appetizer order. We were not ready, and she was back within 5 minute. Very commendable. 

I ordered the Patron Margherita and my wife ordered the the special 'deep eddy' strawberry marg. Both were strong and delicious. 

For dinner the kids had 2 x the 2 for $25 that included an appetizer or 2 salads, one of many entrees with 2 sides, and a shared deserts. One dinner 3 for $10 which is basically the same, but includes a drink.  Wife and I shared 3 meat fajita platter with chicken, steak and shrimp. The kids chose:

Chips and guacamole 
2 salads
Sirloin steak
2x Margherita grilled chicken
Bacon cheese burger
1/2 rack ribs
Cheese cake 
Pan cookie
Sides included: fries, loaded mash, lots of steamed broccoli, more broccoli...

First off, guacamole was quite delicious. They didn't have that fake powdery or watery style that you find in a lot of restaurants. There were real, large chucks of fresh avocado. The salads were standard. 

The salads and appetizers arrived really quickly, the dinner took abit more time. That is expected on Easter Sunday.  
 
The ribs were perfect, Tender and Smokey. The 'just Bacon' Burger was HUGE and cooked perfect. The fries were fresh. The meats for fajita were grilled and spiced really nice. 

The desserts arrived timely and both baked Cookie with ice cream and cheese cake were good. Not great but good. 

Overall the food was excellent, service great, price was amazing for the quality and quantity of food given. We will come back.

5 star all the way!

Flor 1 Star
Food 5 Star
Service from Erica 5 Star

I have to admit all of the sushi was absolutely delicious. There was no downside to the food. We will most definitely return here as Erica was awesome and the sushi was perfect.

They almost lost 9 customers due to a rude person, maybe this review can be used to help

What a great place. We arrived at 11:45 just before the lunch rush. I feared that having my 5 kids with me that it would be extremely expensive. $61.00 pre-tax and Tip. Not the cheapest, but not bad. I can tell you, I ordered 6 items for 6 people and we went home with 1 order of pancakes and 1 whole Club Biscuit/brisket. So yeah, very filling. We got some extra plates and shared everything. 

What we ordered:

2 orders of Blueberry Cornmeal pancakes
1 Reggie deluxe
1 The Club with Brisket
1 The Weggie
1 Hash UPS with Bacon

First the Pancakes...holy crap goodness. My oldest son said 'super-premium-awesomeness' or something like that. Light and fluffy, fresh blueberry goodness. It could have had more blueberries and I only wish I had room to eat more. The biscuits were big, fluffy and fresh, buttery with great texture. I really liked the Reggie Deluxe with the egg over easy. I was given a choice of sausage or mushroom gravy, we did sausage. It was perfect in flavor and texture. The hash Up was a great addition to the breakfast. Potatoes browned nice and golden, topped with mushrooms, cheese, onions and we added bacon. We didn't get a chance to touch the brisket as everyone was stuffed, but my son tasted the meat and he said he wished he had room to eat it as it tasted so good. 

There is a lot of self service  here. Likened to up-scale fast food. You line up to order as you enter. There is a self-service coffee station with 3 types of coffee, milk, cream, raw sugar, white sugar and a substitute. There are cups for water there also. There is a sign to please help clear your own table, but the dish tub was way in the back. The counter girls are very friendly and helpful. The parking out front is metered, but worth it as we paid like $1.00 to park right in front. 

The kids can't wait to come back again. Things we want to try would be the shrimp and grits, homemade pop tart, cinnamon roll, The Moneyball, and some of the alcohol. I really need to take my wife here for a nice brunch style bloody Mary's and biscuits and gravy... Yummy Yum Yum Yum!

Had to go to homedepot this morning to order a casement window and wife wanted to try this place. We normally go to the Two Chicks downtown. 

The first thing that I liked was the parking. Each time downtown we had a tough time parking. Next was this place was nice and big with plenty of tables. Though the restaurant had a lot of customers, plenty of empty tables. 

We were seated immediately. We asked for a booth and the hostess was friendly and accommodating. The waitress came and took a drink order and I ordered the coffee. I loved the coffee downtown and remember asking about it and the server telling me they roast their own. The waitress walked to the server station and started talking. I waited for coffee and watched her converse. My wife told me that maybe they were brewing fresh coffee? I saw other servers with coffee pots re-filling other patrons coffee. The waitress greeted other customers and still no coffee. After 10 minutes, she showed up with coffee. She brought cream and sugars. I had to ask for more sugar as these cups are about twice the size of normal cups. It was a bit strange she didn't ask us if we were ready to order. She went back to the serving station to converse with other workers standing around. 

I don't mind a relaxed pace, but 15-20 minutes before asking for our order is not good. Especially if they are not that busy. We finally got our order in. I ordered eggs Benedict with vegetable fritters. My wife ordered French toast combo with scrambled eggs and ham. She also ordered lemonade. 

The coffee was good and I was able to finish the giant cup before breakfast arrived. The server never once offered more coffee. I watched our waitress Stand around talking. Finally another person delivered our breakfast. The hollandaise was cracked and hardening. The French toast hard and scrambled eggs were dry. As you can see in the pictures. It was obvious that our food was sitting around along time before it was brought out. At this point, our waitress still had not offered more coffee. I finally got her attention and asked for more. 

The food would have been amazing had it been served fresh and timely. I do so love the veggie fritters in place of potatoes. I had such high hopes for this place as I really loved the one down town. 

May try it again and see if it was just a negligent waitress.

After having and amazing poke bowls 2 weeks ago, we decided to try the ramen here. We were not disappointed! At the end of the review I'll tell you about the loyalty card and parking 

The crew remembered us and seemed genuinely happy that we returned. After a very nice welcome, we told them we were here to ry the ramen menu and had a couple of questions. They happily answered our inquiries. 

They also have sushi burritos and a nice list of appetizers/sides  (like pot stickers, seaweed salad, Edamame, Sirimi crab tofu pockets) 

What we ordered:

Wine:
Bottle of Jas D'esclans Cru Classé (nice imported French wine from Cotes de Provence) 

Food:
Star of the show
Chicken paitan 
Ohh lala 
Garlic lime shrimp 

There was an issue and the counter guy guy informed us that one of the Ramen machines was out of commission and it would take some time. It did take about 20 minutes, but we had a nice bottle of wine to enjoy. They do have a unique selection of wines by the glass (Zinfandel, Riesling, Chardonnay and some imported wines) along with a nice beer selection. 

The Ramen bowls were excellent. The Star of the show was the favored, but all 4 were really good. You do have the option to build your own bowl, but we went with the 'signature' bowls. 

They have a nice loyalty program that gives you a regular poke bowl for 100 points and a large poke bowl for 150 points (or a ramen bowl. With 5 kids and a bottle of wine, we stacked points up fast lol. May take others longer, but the food is so good, the price is excellent, and such a large selection that it will be worth signing up! Free is free lol. Oh yeah...1 point for $1 I think.

Parking is tough in this area and Finbomb has a few parking spots in the back alley. The parking spots are free with validation. It's a pretty easy process and the system remembered my info. Just text Fbom to 25023 and you get a reply with a link to enter your credit card. Once you order at Finbomb, ask for a validation number and enter it on the parking page. It gives you a free hour.

Came here for valentines with the wife. We wanted to go to a steak house, however all the places had a 2 hour waitlist. We drive by this place taking the kids to wrestling so my wife called and asked if there was a wait, there was none. 

The first red flag is that almost no cars in the parking lot. There was only  3-4 tables full when we walked in. I can't imaging why on a Saturday 7:30 pm this place would be deserted. 

Next red flag, were were not greeted with more than an 'how many'? And no smiles or chit chat. The guy asked for a drink order before we made it to the table. Just water I said...

He asked us if were having Buffet only or the Hotpot - sushi. We ordered only the Buffet. The presentation is actually quite nice. All of the food looks quite delicious. However, the fried foods were a bit mushy like they were stale. There was almost no flavor to any of the food. The crab legs look quite good, however they were boiled until there was no flavor. The generals chicken had no spice. The Peking duck had no duck meat on the bones whatsoever. Skin and bones. The sushi rolls were very stale and flavorless. Hot and sour soup was neither hot nor sour. 

The squid Tentacles, peel-n- eat shrimp, as well as the oysters were actually decent. The shrimp were fairly large, and only two mushy shrimp out of like 20.

The Hot pot is Hong Kong style with a conveyor belt that circled and patrons just take plates as the pass. I would like to try it sometime, but fear the lack of flavor as well as the staleness of the Buffet... on the belt I saw: Blue crab, muscles, shrimp, tofu, egg, sprouts, veggies, crawfish, root veggies, kelp, mushrooms, fish balls, glass noodles.

I may return to try the hot pot, or to fill up on the oysters and peel-n-eat shrimps!

It was time for some Vietnamese food and had not been here for a couple of years I think. We don't really get downtown often. As previously yelped, the only reason we don't come here more often is the parking. They only have a few spots out front. There's also a bar next-door and some other business that all use just the five or six parking spots.

They close at 9:30 and we arrived about 8:45 PM. There was plenty of seating, and we sat ourselves. I forgot my mask in the truck and figured were eating so didn't really matter. The waiter brought us menus and put a disposable mask on the table. That was a nice touch. Nobody really had masks on but probably due to regulations they provided one without question. 

The waiter was the same as we had a couple years ago. He was very friendly and very professional. There was about four or five other tables with customers.

What we ordered:

Green tea 
# 30 BBQ Beef Ribeye on fried rice
# 21 Shrimp, pork, meatloaf on egg noodle
# 19 Flame broiled shrimp, pork on rice noodle
# 25 shrimp, roasted pork on fried rice

First off the portions were huge. We got to take quite a bit of leftover noodles home. The service was fast. Also the food was really good as well as a good value. Covid did not seem to affect service or quality of food here. 

Will definitely come back.

Warm and delicious! Warm and friendly!

This is my go-to donut place. Each time we go, we get 1 dozen and I let the kids pick the one they want. Needless to say, they enjoy this ritual very much. Huge variety, always fresh tasting, delicious.

A Special Treat!

The last visit, we followed the routine as usual. After we chose 12, my son asked how much for a HUGE twist. The counter girl told him it was like a dollar extra. I told my 14 year old that we already had 12 so maybe next time. He then asked if he could use his allowance to buy one as he really, really wanted a big twist. The kids were all drooling as they stared at the twist. Being frugal, I told him better to save his money as he had a donut already. No need to "waste" his allowance. There was clear disappointment on his face and I started to reconsider...I mean, sometimes you just got to splurge right? Well the girl waiting on us grabbed a second bag and stuffed 2 twists in the bag. She handed them to my son making him promise to share the treat. The girl went to the back. My kids were elated and already trying to tear into the twists. My son went to the counter and asked for the girl that helped. The other girl showed concern and asked if everything was ok. He said yes, but he needed to talk to her. I stood by, typical parent, wanting to go as we had things to do. The girl came out and my son told her he needed to hug her. She hugged him warmly and the other counter girl started to tear up. It was quite touching. He thanked her again and we left feeling all warm and gushy. 

Now I can't promise you the same experience. Definitely can't expect a free donut. But I can promise you these are the best donuts in town. Go early as the last hour pickings might be slim. If you time it right, you can get a nice warm butter milk. Nothing like catching a donut before it has had a chance to cool all the way.

Drop the kids off came here for a late valentines dinner. The wife and I really get to go out alone. So we are shooting the works. Drinks, steaks, lobster and crab (Oscar). 

Wife bought some gift cards from Costco so we could try this steak house. $100 for the price of $75. Its always a great deal while trying a new place. 

First I must warn you, that if you do not like country music, you should not come here. The whole two hours we were here, it was like a country western Radio station without the adverts. Decor is also full of cowboy memorabilia, cowboy boots, hats, saddles, ropes And electric guitars all over the walls. Plus a deer head....

We ordered a ruby tini and an ultimate Margarita (substitute the 1800 for Patron) for drinks. For dinner we ordered the 20 ounce prime rib (medium rare) and the bacon wrapped filet, Oscar style, with an ad on lobster tail. We don't normally go so decadent, however it's a Valentine's Day celebration, even if late. 

We are allowed to choose two sides and I chose the mushrooms and asparagus, my wife chose the garlic mashed potatoes with white gravy and the roasted tomatoes with Parmesan. For dessert we ordered the fresh apple cobbler (Togo)

The steaks were cooked perfectly. The Filet with crab/asparagus was perfect. Had a nice Smokey flavor. Probably from the bacon wrapped around it. We did have an issue with the 20 ounce prime rib, as you can see in the pictures it was about half fat. I remove the fat and I showed it to the waiter. He did acknowledge the he noticed a lot of fat. He said he brought it to the managers attention, and she took $10 off our dinner. I Told him I didn't think that was good enough as half of the steak was fat. The manager never came by our table. She took another five dollars off, but come on, the chef should be trained in recognizing this and adjusting the cut. Also, since there Was so much fat, Why not just comp the steak? The mushrooms were great, all of the sides were great. 

We probably won't try this place again. The quality control was lacking. The service was great. The price is just too high considering you pay $30 for about 10 oz of meat. Maybe they need a little work on keeping customers by fixing problems on their end. I am not a picky customer, but I do expect High-quality  for a $30 twenty oz prime rib.

One of the most horrible experiences - we would like to write about it, but every time we do, or our friends do, we get harassed and threatened by the business owner. So, we will just leave his last reply as a comment & you can see for yourself.
The food was gross like vomit and the service was terribly rude- do NOT go to a business that speaks to their customers like this! 


Update- we have received many threats and hate messages, and will no longer be directly responding to them on Rashon's behalf. No, Megan F. You are not going to bully us. No, Branzino restaurant we will not remove the review. No, you may not go to his school and harass him there.

The restaurant claims if we don't remove a one-star review, they will harass the reviewer and interfere with his life and go to his school.

So at work today we all decided to order from east coast subs because we had ordered it a week ago and it was good. We all ordered with our own separate cards. Our secretary did the ordering and it took her about 40 minutes to place the order because it seemed as though Chris, who took our orders was having a difficult time understanding our group order. Our subs arrived, and Chris who delivered our subs had very bad body odor and everyone could smell it. Then, when one of the nurses checked her account realized that she had been charged $30 for one sub.  The rest of us checked ours as well and realized we also had been charged extreme charges for $7 to $8 dollar subs. Some were charged $20 and some $15. We called them back and they tried to tell us they had charged us delivery fees separately...to the effect of $100 between all of us who ordered. They they said they would refund it. I checked my account 3 hours later and I never received a refund so I called back. I asked for a manager and the women on the phone stated she was the manager so I explained what had happened she then gave the phone to Chris. He said they were not going to give us back the money because we were charged a delivery fee and it wasn't refundable. I told him that we had ordered last week and he tried to tell me that we had never ordered from there before, so basically called me a liar. I hung up on him and then he proceeded to send me several very rude texts. So do not order from this place unless you want to pay $15-$30 for a mediocre sub and very rude lying employees with extremely bad body order!!!

This place could be seriously addictive and it's more expensive than Starbucks. After seeing a few Yelp buddies check in I bookmarked this place as a must try next visit. 

I did not know what to order and I had no idea that placing an order and receiving the order would take as long as it did, but it was worth the wait. 

If you are a fan of the the Berry Chantilly Cake at Whole Foods or any other store in the area, the Chantilly cake snoball is a must try! The concept of cheesecake, fresh strawberries, fresh blueberries AND condensed milk in a snoball is simply ingenious. It was very rich but absolutely wonderful. 

March 2016----My new favorite is the Strawberry Lemonade. It is a lemonade sno-ball with a lots of freshly cut strawberries throughout.  

Nicely done.

Finding a good restaurant after 8:30p in the new normal is quite a challenge! Lucky for us, Gianna was still seating and the dining experience was great. Rather surprised that complimentary bread isn't offered. Our app, 2 entrees, 3 glasses of wine, sorbet and side of potatoes was $144 before gratuity. 

Sausage provola - 5/5 
Mildly spicy, served sizzling and a unique find. 

Veal Saltimbocca - 5/5 
Thin, pounded to perfection and the lemon added an amazing flavor. The pasta a perfect compliment and full of flavor all on its own. 

Fire Roasted Chicken  4/5
The most tender chicken I've ever had. Also bursting with flavor. Deducted a star bc it's not accompanied with a pasta or veggie side despite it's almost $30 price tag.

Rosemary Potatoes- 4/5 
Very tasty but on the almost too heavy side. 

Pear Sorbet - 4/5 
Perfect dessert after a pretty filling meal. 

Wait Service 3.5/5 
Friendly, but somewhat absent. Get it was end of the night but there were several times we needed water refills, wine, to order something else or the check. There was at least one smoke break and towards the end, we were ready to leave and he was the only thing standing in our way. That said, when he was around, he was knowledgeable and engaged.

I didn't think love like this was possible. South exceeded my expectations and has me pining for more after one visit.

The service is impeccable and Miles is the man (so request him if possible!) The food is a modern take on some Southern classics, but minus the heaviness that traditional Southern cuisine sometimes has. The Pimento Cheese is super tasty and I kinda wish that it would come with crackers instead of bread so I could eat more of it! The Berkshire Pork was succulent, almost melt-in-your-mouth and my husband raved about the collard greens. 

We stayed for the jazz performance, which is held in a quaint, spacious area of the restaurant. I probably could have listened to the sweet, soothing music all night in that space. Philly needs more spots like South. Great ambiance, performance and service. I am already planning our return visit!

We ordered Christmas dinner from Miles Table and not only was the food phenomenal, but the ordering process was seamless. 

Alysia was super friendly and helpful when I called to place my order and once it arrived within our 2-hour delivery window, she sent a follow-up email detailing how to heat everything up. It couldn't have been any easier.

The food was amazing - we loved everything from the potato leek soup to the braised short ribs and roasted veggies. The bourbon pumpkin pie was delish and our parents thought so too since we shared half of it with them.

I had never dined at Miles Table pre-pandemic, but once things open back up, I certainly plan on doing so. Until then, I highly recommend online ordering or catering.

Seriously, some of the best smoothies in NOLA. Need a buzz? They've got ya covered, too. Smoothies are available w/ or w/o the liquor. For those of you that believe in day drinking, there's no better way to soothe that slurp with a little somethin' somethin' that will chase those worries away. Visiting NOLA for the first time? Yes, it is okay to walk around with an alcoholic beverage in hand and not get cited! Yup, I could hardly believe it myself my first time around the block. Need something to beat that NOLA heat? A tall cup of of any of these refreshing smoothies will pick you right back up from your sizzling slump. So, when you're strolling through NOLA, pop by the French Market and order a smoothie to help you conquer the quarter! You will be very happy you cam by here.

Gosh, this restaurant simply took my breath away. I was so excited to dine here because I have had a taste of it before at an event, but never got to actually come check out the restaurant. So, I was super excited at the opportunity to get to finally try it. It was so close to the Ace Hotel, where I was staying, which sweetened up the deal even more. Our party was warmly welcomed and seated immediately for lunch. I could hardly believe this place was not packed during lunch time. The waitress was fantastic and was able to answer all our questions about the menu and make adjustments where needed to accommodate our party. Oh the food. They won me over immediately at amuse-bouche. My table ordered gluten-free fried oysters and they were sensational. I could hardly believe I was actually eating a fried oyster that was gluten-free. The lettuce cups were an absolute hit. After all that, I almost forgot I ordered a main entree. When it came, not only was it flattering to the eye, but it was aromatic. So many strong flavors popped out at every bite that could hardly keep me from taking the next bite fast enough. Everything was so fresh and unique. I have thought of going back to this restaurant everyday, since I left. Now, I cannot wait to go back. All I could think of is how much my husband and daughter would love that place. I will definitely be back. If you are looking for an exceptional dining experience and unforgettable food, this is where it's at.

This was my 1st time having "hot chicken". I was told and I read that this was a must-have in Tennessee. My family and I are pretty healthy eaters, but we always have that occasional splurge and this was our night to do that. We had spent most of the day taking it easy in our hotel room, so by the evening we got hungry and decided to venture out for some grub. I searched on here for "hot chicken" and this place popped up. The reviews were good, so we decided to eat there. It wasn't super busy and our order was taken immediately. The hot chicken had different levels of heat. Since I don't do well with too much heat (and neither does my daughter), I went with the mild heat. Customer service was great and our food came out in a timely manner. In comparison to another hot chicken that I had (of course I had to try another spot before writing this review), this was a 4/5. Would I eat here again, when back in the area? Why of course! It was tasty and service was great. I definitely recommend, if you are craving hot chicken in the Franklin area.

So, I was busy showing my mom the Reno food scene and she was craving Japanese. As you know, when moms want something, there's no way of saying no to that. SO, I lived close by to this place and we gave it a shot. I'm a huge fan of AYCE so I took advantage of that. First of all, out all the places I've tried appetizers, this was easily one of the better ones. Takoyaki is one of my favorite appetizers so I was beyond excited to taste it. Quality work in that department. 

The sushi itself was pretty good. I really liked the Sakana roll because it showed off the fresh fish options all in one roll. Definitely one I'll regularly get when I come here. Everything else was the standard type rolls you'd find anywhere. 

Being with a friend of mine and my mom, they decided on the Udon. They both were pleasantly surprised and thoroughly enjoyed their food. They were happy that they were able to also get an appetizer along with all of the Udon. 

The server was great. She was more than helpful when it came to suggestions about which rolls were best for what I was looking for. I also appreciate that she didn't come over to our table constantly. I always have a hard time enjoying my experience when servers are checking up between each bite you take, so that was a definite plus. 

Overall, the service was great, sushi was above average, and appetizers were BOMB.

Poor service. Watching the owners berate other diners left our party speechless. I don't understand how they stay in business. Save yourself and your guests the misfortune of dining here. There are plenty of other establishments in Eagle and I highly recommend you try any of them over this place.

My wife and I decided to give this place a try after hearing about it from an Instagram food blogger.  

Unfortunately, in Nashville it takes more than just some cool looking blocks to serve as plates and trendy water bottles at each table.  Here is their first mistake;  Quit hiring servers based on how they dress and look.  Just because they look trendy doesn't mean anything.  They need to have personality and hustle.  Second off, find an incredible Chef.  This menu completely misses the mark.  There is very little choice, and within that very little choice is a bunch of items that are popular around Nashville.  Here's the problem, every other place does each item way better!!

The first and most important thing about your Restaurant is service.  Customers have to be greeted fast and sat even faster if possible.  Then they need to be tended to.  Customers are a bunch of entitled brats who think they deserve everything perfectly.  Your job is to cater to that.  That is, of course, if you want your Restaurant to be successful.

The "hot chicken johnny cakes" - I got the tiniest little piece of chicken on my plate.  Needs to be 2-3 of those on there.  For $10, come on thats just laughable.

The "brisket" is very tasty, but extremely dry!  I suggest bringing your own little bottle of bbq sauce, cause theirs is the worst in town.

- - All in all, quit trying so hard to be cool and work more at being GOOD.  Some of the best food in Nashville is at the least trendy spots.

Finally made it back to Yamitsuki! Service was excellent but they did not refill our waters. We ordered cocktails this time around and both were great. I had the Lychee Martini which wasn't too sweet and was a beautiful pink color. 

We had a few appetizers to start. The gyoza was fresh and delicious. Our favorite was the takoyaki which came out piping hot so we had to wait a little to actually eat it. I also ordered the Miso Ramen. The seasoned egg was loaded with flavor and my favorite part. The broth itself was flavorful. My fiance had the Spicy Ramen which had a great kick to it. I actually wished I got his because it was that good!  

We ended the meal with a Tiramisu in a glass which was delicious!  Not overly sweet and it had a cute little strawberry on top cut to look like a flower.

I was looking over the happy hour menu before we left and realized it's a steal! Great drink and food options

I knew Winkel was going to be good but I was really blown away. We went on opening day and I could not tell they opened hours before we arrived. We were greeted immediately by our cheerful waiter and opted to sit outside. My only complaint is I wish there was more covering (i.e. umbrellas or an extended awning) in the outside area. The sun in the city can be so hot.

Everything on the menu looked amazing but our waiter suggested the Deep Fried French Toast. It was SO decadent and delicious. It had a beautiful thin crispy crust and the bread even had strawberries in it. The french toast was surrounded by a pool of almond custard that was so light. It was topped with homemade whipped cream that (thankfully) didn't have any sugar in it.  

My fiance had the Parker House Roll Breakfast sandwich which should be in the running for the best breakfast sandwich in the city. I do not know how Chef Joncarl made that bacon but OMG was it amazing.  Don't even get me started on the aioli and the cheese.

They also have their own nitro brew coffee which is so smooth.  Service was impeccable.  I cannot wait to go back!

This is my "go to" restaurant for any ocassion: birthdays, celebrations, or just because. Service is usually always good. 

It's the best place in Philly to get oysters because they have a large variety, they're fresh, and they know how to shuck them. Out of the many times I've been here over the years, I've never found part of the shell in my oyster. I tend to go with the West coast oysters (kusshi, kumamoto, and recently had goose point for the first time) because they're less salty and have a refreshing cucumbery taste. Their raw bar menu is always changing and the servers are always knowledgeable about the type of oyster or clam available. 

If it's your first time going, you have to get the lobster roll. Best in the area and arguable better than most NE lobster rolls. It's a super buttery roll overstuffed with large chunks of fresh lobster.  Everything on the menu is great with my other favorites being the fried calamari, fisherman's stew, and pan seared scallops.

Don't be afraid to get their desserts too! The menu is always changing but I'm always impressed with the dessert.

Another excellent restaurant in the CookNSolo group! I've been waiting for almost a year for this place to open and was not disappointed. If I could describe this place...it's like Zahav and Dizengoff had a baby.

Menu is super easy to navigate. Essentially you pick a main meat/fish/veggie and it comes with hummus, pita and never-ending salatims. Yes, like Olive Garden never ending breadsticks but with the best Israeli salads they'll keep refilling. All of the salatims are delicious and it's so hard to pick a favorite. It's definitely preference thing and a great debate to have with your fellow diners! This course also comes with their famous hummus which is literally the GOAT.

So far I've had the Lamb Merguez, Trout and Branzino.  The lamb was super flavorful but maybe slightly overcooked. The trout was delicious but I wish it came with more of the salsa. The whole grilled branzino is to die for! You cannot pass this up and it's a great deal for two people. Both fishes had super crispy skin that I couldn't get over! 

Dessert is kept super simple with varying versions of vanilla ice creams.  The first night I went it was a vanilla ice cream sandwich with pistachio, crunchies on the outside and a cherry in the middle. The second time I went it was a vanilla ice cream sundae with pistachios, crunchies and a cherry on top.

As always with this restaurant group, service was excellent.  I cannot wait to go back...especially with warmer weather approaching!

I had an out of town guest and wanted to take them to a Florida Gulf Coast beach-side seafood restaurant which met three criteria.One, it had to be authentic and not feel like a touristy/chain (ie. Crabby Bills, Bubba Gump Shrimp), also it had to not rely on an overly breaded and deep fried everything on the menu approach to dining, and lastly had to offer great fresh seafood- frozen food need not apply.  Watl'z Fish Shak came through on all counts. 

It is located on the far east end of John's Pass not directly on the intercoastal boardwalk, and the moment I saw its exterior appearance I knew the previous good yelp reviews were going to be spot on. This place looks great, just what you want a beachy seafood restaurant to look like. Growing up in the area  I can remember this location formerly being a coffee house. The Fish Shak is definitely a step up. While it feels like a small converted house, the place exudes plenty of quaint charm, and is very inviting. 

So enough about the location, how was the food? 

In three words fresh, flavorful and delicious. There is no set menu instead a chalkboard highlights what was fresh and being served that day. That day the menu consisted heavily of grouper, shrimp, and crab offerings. Two of our party of three had the grouper sandwich which was offered at 12 dollars. I had it blackened and my friend had it fried. The grouper was huge with almost half of it was actually hanging off the side and out the bun. The blackened one was spiced and cooked perfectly as to not overwhelm the flavor of the fish. The fried option was very lightly dusted perfectly crispy, and did not suffer from the heavy oiled mess that is so prevalent at chintzy seafood places. The fish tasted great on a simple yeasty kaiser roll and came with some lettuce, onion, and pickle. There wasn't any sauce present which was fine by me as it let the fish flavors take center stage, but I can see some people wanting a sauce of some kind.

I have a great suggestion for what sauce to ask for, and also the perfect side to go with the sandwich. 

My wife is a vegetarian, and thankfully she had menu options to select from which included a black bean and jalapeno hummus spread along, and maybe the best part of the meal fried yucca. The golden brown yucca sticks were accompanied with a chitpole remoulade, and this sauce not only  tasted great with the perfectly fried potato alternative yucca, but also went very well with the sandwich.  Being a bit of a yucca aficionado I can say it was some of the best I have ever had. Plus it was a definite plus for a fish place to offer solid alternatives for those diners who don't dine on meat! I don't know why this is so much to ask for at so many restaurants. 

The only miss during lunch was a cup of crab and shrimp chowder which was lacking a bit of flavor mostly due to the fact that the soup base was simply not creamy and thick enough. It felt a little watered down. A little bit more butter, flour, and half and half in their recipe would have made it perfect. With that being said, I still finished the whole thing so it must of not been that bad! =-) 

Lastly, they offer a decent bottle selection of beer and do have a central bar area with stools. The two draught selections were Stella Artois (served in its proper glass) and Peroni. 

I will definitely be returning to Walt'z in the near future, and hope to further explore their ever changing menu of fresh daily selections.

Ohhhh I am just going to rave about this restaurant. First timer having crepes. My sister suggested anything that involves mushroom sauce. So went with chicken and arugula. Sweet baby Jesus!!! I wanted to just drink the sauce out of a cup! Amazing! The crepe was so wonderfully delicious! The chicken was tender and tasty. 

The very close tie for first place was Amie, our sparkling, charming and so very endearing waitress. She was so very attentive, friendly and lovely. Amie made lunch so enjoyable. 

So go eat a crepe, especially on Tuesday when Amir is definitely working! Haha!

Probably the only legit chinese food place in reno. No wonder it was crazy packed--the sushi place next door had no one, but this place was so full there weren't any seats.

The food is definitely legit. The portions were huge--the mapo tofu was served in a crazy big bowl. The beef noodles were ok--the noodles were the right texture, thick and springy, and there was a lot of beef, but the soup wasn't spicy nor red enough, and for some reason they put in a bunch of random leafy greens on top. Not sure why.

The drinks are also definitely legit. In fact, it was so legit, that they only sell the milk tea in cold flavor in bubble tea clear plastic cups. When I asked for some hot lemon tea, they actually gave it to me in a plastic cup and served warm instead of hot so the plastic wouldn't melt. Haha that's how you know they're legit--they don't serve anything other than the main cold bbtea, which they specialized in.

Overall, a good place for real chinese food. If I lived in Reno this would be my hangout spot

I called and asked if they could make me a jumbo Elmo cupcake for Monday. I was told they are closed on Mondays and couldn't do it and couldn't help me. I wasn't even given the choice to pick it up on Sunday. That would have been the customer friendly thing to do!! I will never order from there again!!

I think this is my second favorite cupcake shop in the city (Brown Betty, you know you're number one, girl). The cupcakes are kind of small but the range of flavors is really impressive. The icing and cake are both perfect consistencies. Moist, rich cake and thick, creamy icing. 

The folks working there might want to tone it down a bit, in regards to customer service. I felt like I was being attacked with 'HELLO CAN I HELP YOU's the minute I walked in. Chiiiill, let me scope things out before you start talking to me. Their efforts are appreciated but there is a fine line between being helpful and being in your face.

a friend discovered this place and so we went the other night, and i'm giving this one five stars for a few reasons. i've lived in thailand and have certain foods i love and others i'm not so crazy about, so i was happy to have a new place to check out. 

it's tucked away off thompson lane, so check the map about where -- it's nice and clean and comfortable, a welcoming little place. 

ok, the reasons for five stars: first star:  the service. i loved walking in and we were warmly welcomed, because one of the waiters recognized me from the other place he works. then our waitress, whose family owns the restaurant and the grocery next door, was so helpful, making suggestions and telling us the difference between their thai-style options and their laos-style options (since the family is from the eastern issan of thailand, they have both influences). 

she suggested ginger tea with honey, which is without a doubt the best thing you could have on a cold winter night. 

the second star: they have khao soy on their menu. this is a noodle dish in a coconut broth that is from the north of thailand, where i spend a lot of time -- it wasn't what i'm used to in chiang rai, but it was still delicious and hit the spot. 

the third star: when i asked the owner if they had sai ooua, which is a northern thai spicy sausage, she said they did, but it was in her store next door frozen, and she'd be happy to go get some, defrost it and cook it for me if i didn't mind waiting 15 minutes. i decided to pass this time, and next time i'll call ahead or just go buy some and bring it home. they even have two styles of it in the store. what a find!

the fourth star: the som tom, or fresh green papaya salad. this was as good as any i've had in thailand, tart and crunchy and we asked for a #1 level (of 5) for spice, and it was plenty spicy for me. super tasty and super authentic.

the fifth star: when the waitress came out to bring me chopsticks for my noodles, she explained to our table how thai people eat (a big spoon in the right hand, and fork in the left to push food onto the spoon). chopsticks are only for noodles, but most thai places don't tell people that, and you have people eating their thai food with chopsticks which sort of annoys me, mostly because the spoon method is far better for foods with sauce and broth. 

my friends all had veggie and tofu curries, all so spicy that i wouldn't even dare to taste it, but they seemed to polish it off. 

oh, if there was a sixth star, it would be for the dessert! they had a special purple sticky rice with coconut milk treat, with purple and white ice cream on top-- and honestly, i have no idea what the purple was from, but it was fantastic. four people sharing it was just about right. 

go to ginger thai. it's awesome.

This tourist trap has a sign that says " Order Only In English". The Late owner, Tony Vento, was a fan of inflammatory conservative vocal-vomit. He was a darling of the  'Merica idiots that think waiting in line for 30 minutes for a tasteless cheesesteak is authentic. You'd think someone with the  surname Vento, which stinks of steerage, would be more sensitive to our countries long history of immigration. But whatever, I digress. 

Three Things: 

1. Getting a cheesesteak from the corner bodega when you are staring at a double shift at your soulless wage job, working for the self-satisfied Tony Ventos of the World is authentic. 

2. Scarfing down a cheese steak made from steakums your mom bought on sale from the Acme is authentic. 

3. Getting a cheese steak for 4 bucks from a food cart during your too short lunch break from a guy 'Merica idiots think is taking their jobs is authentic. 

Paying over $7 in line with people from places I've never wanted to visit who put cheezewiz on their steak is Not AUTHENTIC. 

I grew up in South Philly and have only been here once. Rude subhumans serve the food and Rude subhumans wait in line. I'm ashamed to have gone here.

Not impressed with this place.   Wasn't as clean as I would like in general but also with Covid I expect people to just be on top of cleanliness.   Silverware on table was dirty and hair on the cloth napkins. Asked for a new set but still it's already a turn off.   The server was friendly and attentive.  The food was okay nothing spectacular especially when reviews are so high and that's what brought us to this place, it was disappointing.  Their sister restaurant is Skyline Restaurant apparently and we were surprised to find that out.   Skyline is great and we have been there a couple times.  Sierra St. Kitchen misses the mark by a lot! We will not be coming back as there are so many other places in Reno that are outstanding..

I wanted to add that the only thing I remember ordering was the stuffed mushrooms and wonton ceviche.   But the other two items my husband and I ordered were not even memorable.   The mushrooms were extremely greasy-good flavor but very very greasy. The wonton ceviche flavor and presentation was much better at skyline.

The Black Sheep was a cool little spot that has amazing service and food. They were so busy and packed on Saturday night but the uber friendly staff made everything go smoothly. Though, they could have been a little more attentive of when we needed water refills and such. Not a big deal at all, to me at least. Especially since they were so courteous about it all. All the food was really good but I felt it was a little bit oversalted. They were very receptive of it. I enjoyed the burrata salad with the lemon zest and plums. The bone marrow was yummy and so was the wagyu sirloin ranchero. The latter was definitely a cute take on a ranchero dish. The meat on the spare ribs dish was so tender the meat fell off the bone without any help. The rice pudding paired well with the fresh tart berries. Definitely recommend to check this place out. ****4.5****

Almost overwhelming menu as everything you'd ever want from Italy is here...but when it's delivered to your table, it's nothing you'd ever want to eat.

While looking over the menu, we ordered two mixed drinks; Negroni and an Aperol Spritz.  The Negroni was too heavy on the vermouth and had a full orange slice (a proper Negroni has a burned orange peel to bring out the oil in the skin).  The Aperol was missing the prosecco and bubbles.  We sent them both back and asked to have them removed from the bill, and ordered wine instead.

I started off with the prosciutto de parma and speck alto adage pgi plates.  Both were served in identical fashion, thin strips laid over a salad and on a wooden cutting board.  The salad had a purplish and thick dressing on it, resembled a balsamic like flavor, but way too sweet and overpowering for the light side salad.  It also had green olives in it that didn't fit the flavor profile.  At $9.50 per plate, this was way overpriced.

The "Salumi Sushi", I had the Friuli dish, prosciutto and strawberries wrapped in a roll and then sliced down like a sushi roll, a balsamic reduction in between.  Not a bad dish, but at $11 for the dish, it was again a little overpriced.

The Fritto Misto was average, but not what I was expecting for an authentic Italian restaurant.  The calamari and zucchini were good, but the shrimp were the really small previously frozen kind and ruined the dish.

The mozzarella dish was buffalo mozzarella, we chose "caprese".  It was 1/4 of a ball of mozzarella, then cut into 4 smaller pieces and placed at the corners of the plate while a tomato/green olive/pine nut mixture dominated the center of the plate.  At $11, I expect a whole ball of mozzarella (a ball of buffalo mozzarella costs $6 wholesale).  Huge failure here.  Just go to Di Bruno's down the street and get a full cheese serving if you're after a cheese plate.

Next up was their "ROME" special of the week.  The waiter explained that they picked a different region every week and featured dishes and wines specific to that region.  I opted to try the Spaghetti Carbonara.  What I received looked good, except for a scoop of bacon gelato on top.  The pasta itself was slightly overcooked, missing that slight "thickness" that properly cooked pasta in Italy has.  Maybe they're just using cheap boxed pasta instead of making it fresh?  The sauce was too much egg and not enough liquid, maybe by removing the bacon from the dish, they lost the bacon fat which kept the sauce thinner?  Combine the cool pasta temperature and the cold gelato on top, this dish was a huge failure.

The parmigiano ravioli also came with gelato on top.  This was supposed to be yellow tomato with basil but it tasted like some form of mango (and way too sweet).  Again, the cold gelato on top of the lukewarm pasta was an unpleasant combination.  The ravioli's were also overcooked and I'd swear they were a prepackaged and previously frozen pasta.  We ate one bite and left the dish.

The meal at this point was so disappointing, we skipped the post dinner espresso and the gelato they're famous for.  The check came to a shocking $180 with the tip, and we would have been hungry except for the pains in our stomach from the unpleasant meal...

The interior space is very nice looking.  We were told it was made in Italy, and then shipped here for assembly.  Impressive...but what would have been more impressive, and more effective, would have been to bring over an actual Italian chef instead of serving what tastes like pre-packaged pasta and foodservice prepared foods.

I was expecting great things from Michael Schulson and his wife Nina, but I couldn't be more disappointed.

The space itself upstairs looks nice but the layout is pretty bad.  It's like a half-assed bar that they then decided to add dinner tables to, and sitting at a table you feel like there's a constant stream of people walking by.

We were going to a party downstairs and it's apparently a huge production with the girl at the top of the stairs radio'ing downstairs to tell them she's "sending people down".  You go down into the basement, past a bunch of swinging doors for the kitchen, and then into a small room in the back that looks like it was decorated by a bunch of stoned college students with weird panels glued and nailed to the ceiling.  The crowd down there is anything but VIP, it was a bunch of older married guys dressed in loose fitting button down plaid shirts and drinking beer at the bar while all hitting on the two lone cougars who happened to be standing around.

On the way down, we were stopped in the hallway while Nina was in the process of screaming and yelling at a group of guys trying to leave because they wanted to use the elevator due to a cast on his leg.

After getting downstairs, it only goes downhill.  Food is mediocre, but service is even worse.  Ordered drinks, then after she brought over 1/2 of the drink order, we ordered food.  Food was delivered, we reminded them we were still waiting for 2 of our drinks.  15 min later, still no drinks.  Had to grab her a third time to finally get her to bring me my drink . . . and it's not even crowded down there!  I will say that the burger was good, as were the fries (but not worth coming back for).  The duck foe gras dish was also good, but portion size was way too small.

When I went to use the bathroom, I had to go back down the hallway to the kitchen area.  The single bathroom had towels and toilet paper on the floor and looked more like what you'd expect from a subway station than a nice restaurant.  

Given the staff's lack of service, the overpriced menu, the condition of the facilities, and the cherry on top -- the wild and rude owner Nina making a scene -- it's easy to recommend avoiding this spot and going to any one of the dozen+ other options within a 2-block radius from here.

Great place...can not believe I did not discover till my last day.

RUN to this restaurant...well worth it..

Told others about it and they ate they and raved about it as well.

Clean, non heavy fresh foods...I could go on and on and the Hot and Sour Soup was the best I have had...Delicious..

The place was busy with long lines and I was looking forward to seeing what all the buzz was about. Unfortunately I didn't like their cookies. They were very sweet and the frosting too. The frosting was thick, about 3/4 of an inch thick. The texture of the cookie was too soft, almost cake-like.

Service was disorganized. The lines are long, they were out of three cookie flavors, and the place inside was packed because it's small, and they had a line for folks to order, but after ordering people didn't know where to stand to wait for their cookies. They seemed to have a lot of employees, for the volume of customers. Some customers commented that there were some employees standing around when the people waiting for their cookies were waiting awhile.

Love their food offerings and the ambiance of this place. Great casual setting for such high quality baked goods. 

5 stars - Milk bread. What is this...magic? The fluffy texture, subtle sweet flavor, and pillowy bites make you forget you've already had 3 slices and you're going in for more. The crust too has a dark bake to it that compliments the interior flavor. 

5 stars - Croissants. I've gotten the butter and the everything croissant. And it's flaky, crispy, and buttery. Highly recommend. 

5 stars - Chocolate chip cookie. Only the best I've found in Indiana. It's got such a good cookie-kinda chew to it. And the chocolate-y-ness of it. This was a "I'm going to share it with others when I get home, but... I finished eating it in the car before I got home, whoops" situation. 

Their glass display case of pastries and desserts is beautiful and I can't wait to try more goodies from them. Especially more of their bread offerings!

Stopped in for lunch and we were glad we did. From the eclectic menu we chose two options to share:  the prime rib dip sandwich with fries and the salmon tacos (server said they were a best-seller) with a side of slaw. Everything was delicious - the fries were piping hot and well-seasoned, the prime dip sandwich was loaded with tender beef. Two salmon tacos were more than enough to share - very tasty. Really enjoyed the slaw - made with Napa cabbage, red apples and shredded carrots in a sweet, tangy mayo sauce. Great service, too.

I really wanted to love this place. And I really do like the food - they have a huge menu and lots of great choices.
But. . . . recently, the "manager" has been so rude, I am having a hard time recommending the place.
Last month, I was meeting a new friend for lunch and we decided a central restaurant would be the Stone House. It was a week day and I did not realize I would need a reservation. The manager scolded me for showing up without a reservation and even though it was a cold day, said that I could wait outside. I patiently waited about 45 minutes or so, and finally, was called when a table opened up. Since my new friend showed up late, it worked out ok.  A few weeks later, however, I called to make a reservation a WEEK in advance for lunch. The manager rudely said, no, they were closed that week (it was around Easter time) and if I had "checked their website, I would have known."  And then, the final cherry on the cake:  yesterday afternoon (Saturday, around 1:30 pm) my friend called to make a dinner reservation for next Sunday. She waited patiently, ON HOLD, for over 20 minutes. Finally, the manager answered and scolded my friend for calling when it was so busy - and said "next time, to call on a Tuesday in order to make dinner reservations."  My friend was so mad, she just said, "No Thank You!" And hung up.  The manager called back and left a voice mail saying that she was sorry that my friend had "taken it the wrong way."  It's so odd that this restaurant would have a manager who is so unwelcoming and who makes her customers feel "wrong" for only wanting to eat there.
