Tujague's is an oft-overlooked classic New Orleans eatery / bar, over 125 years old.
Having eaten there with family numerous times "in me youth", I hadn't been in several decades.
We dined there Sunday evening.  It was every bit as wonderful as I recalled.  
Had the "prix-fixe" six course offerings; filet for me and pane'ed veal for Wife.   Both delish and price very reasonable for such "fine dining" !
The interior is unremodeled old N.O.  The food is unabashedly yuppie-chef-less !  Just classics, all done to perfection !
I live here and am very familiar with ALL of the other area places.  If one wants classic old "N'Awlins", this is IT.  Others should go to their usual chain places.
Notice the addresses of those others who give negative comments.
Please, please spend one evening meal here; don't miss this fine dowager of classic N'Awlins restaurants........

Big beer selection! 
This place is cool! I came in looking for Tennessee whiskies, and they had a whole section of whiskies and bourbons. It wasn't really sorted by the type, except for the flavored varieties. I enjoyed checking out all the whiskies- I had heard that this is one of the largest liquor stores in the state, and therefore has the biggest selection, I suppose. 
But the best part was the beer selection. They have long aisles of coolers keeping the beers cold, and aisles of beers stored warm. It's sorted by local, regional, mass brew, etc. They had a wild variety of stuff that this Texan had never seen. I was proud to see that Shiner Beers from Shiner, Texas were being promoted so heavily! 
The parking was a bit challenging, and I ended up parking across the street, which I wouldn't recommend.

Matt B. and I took my father-in-law and his girlfriend out to dinner in November, to celebrate my father-in-law's 77th birthday. We were able to snag a last-minute Friday night reservation at Barbareño, for a party of four at 6:15. The place was busy, though, and we weren't guaranteed indoor seating. I was thankful when they squeezed us inside, as it was cold out, even though the patio did have many heat lamps. We had to be out by 8:00, but as it turned out, that gave us just enough time to get dessert.

The restaurant was hip and attractive, with a dim, intimate, bustling vibe. We had the table next to the kitchen, which was visible through an open entryway. I think Matt's dad and his girlfriend were initially confused by the place--they found the food and the format pretty exotic, whereas Matt and I thought it was comparable to many a nice new restaurant in Los Angeles. They came around, though, and we had a very nice dinner. It helped that the service was great, attentive and forthcoming, and the food was delicious.

There was a lovely house sourdough bread to start, and then we shared a couple of appetizers. The grilled avocado was superb, rich and flavorful, prepared with black garlic ponzu, yuzu mousse, and fresh horseradish. The wings were also fantastic--tender on the inside, crispy on the outside, glazed with date syrup, bergamot, and pistachio, served with micro cilantro and tarragon cream for dipping.

Matt and I shared two entrées, and both were excellent. The Santa Maria BBQ was the standout, perfectly cooked wagyu tri-tip over pinquito beans, pico de gallo, and garlic butter. The beef was silky and full of juice, and I loved the hearty beans. The black cod was buttery and generously seasoned, served with bourbon masa miso, pumpkin, Fresno chilis, and roasted pepitas in a black garlic broth. I also tried a little of my father-in-law's plate of pork. The pork was cooked just right, firm but tender, and it came with lacto-fermented apple, bacon, grilled broccolini,
and parsnip.

The desserts were definitely more experimental than the rest of the menu--it was kind of funny hearing our server explain the Baked California to a 77-year-old white man who mostly eats at Italian restaurants. This was a mango and herb semifreddo with hop cake, lemon, lavender candied pine nuts, and OG kush. No THC involved, but the dessert was somehow weed-flavored. I actually didn't like it very much. I wasn't a huge fan of the semifreddo texture, and that dank taste was a bit overpowering. I preferred the inside-out affogato, another semifreddo made with Handlebar coffee, served with ginger snap, eggnog caramel, and hot vanilla cream. The eucalyptus tart was interesting, too, with Twenty-Four Blackbirds chocolate, berry compote, pistachio miso caramel, and hazelnut. One thing these desserts had in common, though, was that the less tricked-out version would probably have tasted better.

I didn't have this reaction to the rest of the food, though, which I found stellar across the board. I'm glad we got to try Barbareño and introduce a couple of senior citizens to some precious, trendy, new Californian dining.

Matt B. and I took our two basset hounds and had a nice outdoor lunch at Shalhoob's Funk Zone Patio this weekend. It was a fun place, relaxed and vibrant with a casual atmosphere, counter ordering and open seating. The patio was busy at 12:30 on Labor Day Sunday, but we were able to find a sunny spot to sit right away, and moved to a shady spot when that opened up.

There were lots of people and dogs out, so our bassets got plenty of attention--from grown-ups and children and even from another basset hound. i really enjoyed the easy, communal brewery vibe (Shalhoob's does offer beer; Matt had a fresh pint with his lunch).

The food was good. I guess Shalhoob's has a butcher shop, so you know their meat has to be solid. Matt got a quarter rack of baby back ribs, and these were great, tender and juicy and slathered with sweet BBQ sauce, served with salsa and pickles and garlic bread. At $8 for four meaty ribs, these were also kind of a steal, especially considering he paid $5 for a side of fries. The fries were tasty, at least, crispy and thin. My dog Duke made a scene howling at one fry on the floor just out of his reach (it was under a chair at the next table, and a kind man who was able to reach ended up getting it for him). I had the Baja fish tacos, which are probably not Shalhoob's specialty, but I thought they were solid. The fish was delicate with a satisfyingly crispy batter, and it came with chipotle aioli, pico de gallo, cotija cheese, and cilantro lime slaw on housemade blue corn tortillas. They were big and messy and there were three of them, a sizable lunch. The tortillas kind of fell apart but I liked them.

Shalhoob's was a great spot for a lazy Sunday lunch with our bassets. I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a lively, casual place to eat and drink in the Funk Zone. Bring your dogs and enjoy.

When I went to Julienne, it boasted a 5-star average with thirty reviews.  It has since come down to 4.5 due to a whiny 2-star review.  When I checked out the website, I noticed it was hilariously organized into three sections entitled "Menus," "About Us," and "Theory."  Point is, when I went into Julienne, I was almost resigned to disappointment - I wanted five star food, but was afraid I would get a lot of pretension.  Instead, Julienne blew my mind.

The place is small, and it filled up quickly on a Wednesday night.  My boyfriend and I were at Julienne for a late post-bar celebration, but to our surprise, the rest of the crowd was made up of families and random people out getting weekday dinner.  The place is pretty casual, despite the price point, and I liked the relaxed unassuming air.  It seems like a small operation, run by a young, talented couple, with a few young, knowledgeable servers on staff.  The kitchen is tiny, with the chef manning around six small burners at any given time.

The food that came out of it was absolutely delicious.  We decided to go with the five-course tasting menu for $65 each, with $25 wine pairings.  Between the two of us, we tried ten different things and I would order almost all of them again.  The wine pairings were all lovely and well thought out.  With ten courses between us, we tried nine wines, and at the end of the meal, our server wrote them all down for us.

We started with the charcuterie and foie gras torchon.  The charcuterie was impressive, all the more so for being housemade.  It came with copa, pork rillette, wild boar salume, and finocchiona, a Tuscan fennel salami.  All were excellent, as were the accompanying grilled ciabatta, pickle salad, golden raisin compote, and seedy German and spicy English pub mustards.  The foie gras torchon was superb, served with grilled sourdough and strawberry-balsamic preserves.  The cold foie was fatty and creamy, perfectly paired with the tart preserves.

Next we tried both of the pasta options, and considering Julienne is not a pasta restaurant, these were wonderful.  The smoked ricotta cappeletti with house-cured lardo, shaved market squash, and lemon-herb vinaigrette was rich, but balanced by the salty cubes of lardo and thin circles of yellow and green squash.  The squash also added a nice textural element, as it was just a step more resistant than the al dente pasta, with a little bit of crunch.  The green spinach fettuccine with skinless cherry tomatoes, French feta, and toasted pine nuts was another decadent on.  The heaviness was cut by the acidity of the flavorful tomatoes.

Course three brought a duck duo and mussels and chorizo.  The duck duo came with pan-roasted breast, fresh sausage, red lentils, green beans, and plum sauce.  The breast was perfectly tender, the sausage well-spiced with excellent texture.  I loved the lentils, too - everything just came together.  The mussels and chorizo might have been even better, in a hearty sea broth with pinquito beans, Tuscan kale, onions, and grilled ciabatta.  The mussels were fresh and the housemade chorizo piquant and delicious.  The earthy kale tied it all together.

For our last savory course, we ordered the beef short ribs and crispy Niman Ranch pork belly.  The short ribs came with cannellini beans, baby market vegetables, and sofrito.  It was probably the weakest dish of the night, but it was still pretty nice.  The short ribs were cooked to a tee, but they were a bit lacking in flavor.  The homey accompaniments didn't help too much.  The pork belly, on the other hand, was one of the strongest dishes in a very strong dinner.  The pork belly was ideal - crispy on the outside, fatty, and full of flavor.  It came with a mesmerizing summer succotash with sweet corn, vibrant lima beans, and unreal starchy, resistant cubes of potato.  Market braising greens and a spicy maple gastrique finished the heavenly dish.

The dessert menu was a bit bare, which was unsurprising in light of the busy chef and small kitchen.  We tried the nitro sorbet and nitro ice cream.  The flavors were tangerine and Heath bar, and they were both delightful.  The sorbet was snowy, like Italian ice, and very refreshing.  The Heath bar was a great mix-in, and the ice cream had a light creamy texture, melting fast in mouth but not in bowl.  The portions were also not tasting portions - when I cleaned off the bowl in front of me, my boyfriend asked, "Did you really just eat three scoops of ice cream?"

Between the two of us, we sampled a large portion of the menu, and everything was consistently fabulous.  I cannot send enough compliments to this talented young chef.  Our meal was the best I've had in Santa Barbara, and one of the best I've had anywhere. It was absolutely special and I recommend it with all my heart.

We stopped by Lucky Llama Coffee to refuel on our way home from Santa Barbara Monday afternoon. It was a cute, happening little coffee shop in downtown Carpinteria, with its own parking lot and a line stretching out the door (to be fair, the door was near the register). It took about fifteen minutes to order and get our stuff, but service was friendly and the pace wasn't unreasonable for a busy spot.

I went in by myself while my husband hung out in the car with our dogs. While I waited, I checked out the Lucky Llama merch and the artwork on the walls, all for sale. There were several landscape paintings, I'm guessing by the same local artist, and they were all very expensive, like one had sold for $2,500. That makes Lucky Llama a kind of high-end art gallery in addition to a coffee shop.

I didn't try the coffee, but I did get an açaí bowl to tide me over until dinner. The mango bowl came with blended açaí, mango, and bananas topped with granola, strawberry, banana, and honey (you can also get agave). It was a nice, light treat, and all the toppings were excellent--crunchy granola and really ripe fruit. My husband is a coffee fiend, so he got a latte.

Lucky Llama is slower than Starbucks, but it's also cuter, and you can get açaí bowls and pricey landscape art to go with your coffee. I'd recommend it if you're looking to get your caffeine fix in Carpinteria.

This place has really fallen off the map. The BBQ meats are thin and flavorless. The enoki mushrooms are days old.  Even the grill is underpowered to get a nice crust on the meats.  I would stay stick with hot pot, during our time, we saw staff who used the bathroom and did not wash their hands before proceeding to go back to preparing food in the back.  So if you are getting hot pot, make sure your food is thoroughly cooked.

Very disappointed.

Please just try it.  It will change your world.

Be patient (the wait can be 1hr+, sometimes as short as 15 minutes), be willing to spend a little more cash than for your average pizza ($20-$30 depending on toppings), and then fall in love with some of the best pizzas in the city made by one of the nicest guys around.  I've been fortunate enough to have eaten Joe Beddia's delicious pizza a few times, and I usually only have to wait about 15-30 minutes.  Just standing there witnessing the master make each individual pie with care and love is a show in of itself.  

The menu changes seasonally - usually contains one red pie (add toppings as needed), one white pie (unique topping, delicious), and one spicy pie.  My favorite pizza of all time is his white pie with heirloom cherry tomatoes, sweet corn, basil/pesto, and a little sausage added.  The corn is crisp and sweet, the tomatoes burst with flavor in your mouth, and the sausage....ohhhh, the sausage! Just phenomenal.

Joe is a great guy.  I remember the first time I came here, I literally saw Joe sell a local some cheese and just told the guy to pay whatever he thought was fair.  What?!  Just a local guy happy to help another person out.  He's always happy to shoot the breeze on different pizzas and styles.  Most importantly, he always thanks everyone for their business and is genuinely excited that people enjoy his pizza.


Cash only.  No phone orders. Limited dining in option (2 tables, standing room only).  Still absolutely 5 stars.

Hours of operation:
Wednesday-Saturday: 5:30pm-10:30pm

Please enjoy!

Went for dinner last night and will never go back. The menu is interesting and the chef is clearly talented. But the decibel level makes it impossible to have a conversation. A dining experience is more than the food. We were a party of 6 and could not hear across the table. 

If that wasn't unpleasant enough, service was slow (being kind) and inaccurate. Our friends asked for a salad without onions and it came with onions. And then it took about 20 minutes for replacements to come. We endured a 2.5 hour meal in a setting that made any conversation impossible  

This was not a pleasant experience.

Although I was a bit annoyed we had to wait, even with a reservation. I still want to give 4 star because the food was very good. Lisa was the person who took care of us and she was very nice and helpful. We had started with the lobster flatbread, which was delicious
And perfect for sharing with my partner. Then we offer filer mignon which was tendor, juicy and well cooked.

Finally finished our meal with a perfect portion of desert. Overall great atmosphere and service. Will be back..

IMHO! I'm usually pretty much a compulsive Yelper!

If the line is "to the pole" that is an hour wait. (20-25 people)  They only have (3-4) kiosks open & are taking orders by staff.  The burgers are "slightly larger" than a Crystal burger.  I think  that it is more of a fad.

The best part of the entire meal was the "concrete" dessert.  I guess the overall theme of the restaurant is recycling combined with tech can make the user experience much better.  I prefer to view it as the movie "The experimenter" based upon Yale psychology professor Stanley Milgram. 

When you walk down a street and everyone is looking up, you look up to see what they are looking for.  Milgram proved that "peer pressure" can influence individuals, just like shake shack does.  Because this place has a customary "line out the door" - it encourages others to wait in line.  Because some of the kiosks are down (they are ready but not logged in for use) they "Create the illusion that this burger is in high demand ".  It is a brilliant "blue light special" type of marketing that draws in the millennial crowd.  

The truth is that they are "understaffed" and "overworked". (Although there are two employees that just STAND NEXT TO THE LINE!!!  Like "it's ok , I'm waiting an hour here with you.  Truth be told, other places are a better value.  I sincerely felt when I left that place I would have been better off (health, time, monetary) getting Mediterranean food down the street (you can deduce which one from my profile check-ins)

So if Yelp! "scrubs this review" because I honestly express my "true user experience" I am done  
I could name a 1/2 dozen hamburger places that are better than this place.  But if you want to eat somewhere "just because it is a fad" - feel free!!! 

P.S.- please look  at the photos and notice the scale of the bun is only slightly larger than a teaspoon.  In all actuality the bun is about 2"x 2" and the lettuce  was slightly larger than a silver dollar.  The bacon was exactly (4) strips - 3 in a row with one  on the end!

Usually not a huge fan of Asian fusion, but the Korean BBQ cheesesteak and cheese fried rice SLAPPED. Would also highly recommend trying out the munchies and desserts (the wing dings and carrot cake were my personal favs). 

My girlfriend and I literally went twice in one day while we were visiting Philly, can't wait to go back.

Stopped by Friday evening about 8 to grab a food truck bite and a beer. Looked like things were hopping outside but starting to quiet down inside. About three quarters of the  tables were taken outside, the others hadn't been bussed since their occupants had left. Grabbed the least messy table and went inside to the bar to grab the beer that I desperately needed.

Inside almost none of the tables were occupied and the remainder were clean and ready for seating. The bar was large and an oddly configured semi-circle that creates a large open space behind it and places the customer farther away from the beer menu than necessary. Only about a quarter of the bar was occupied and fairly quiet. I tried to locate the spot for walkup orders and read the beer chalk-board menu. After deciding on a beer choice I stood at the most open section with money in hand and looked as thirsty as possible. Almost immediately two of the four folks behind the bar disappeared. Of the other two, one stood with her back to the crowd trying to reconcile something at the register and the other continued to talk beer and present tastings to the customer he had been focusing on since I walked up and continued to focus on until I gave up. Eventually what empty space was at the bar when I had walked up was taken by other walkups. Finally the bartender at the register barely looked back to notice the person closest to her, whom was the last to walk up, had a bottle of wine on the bar to purchase and helped her. I gave up when I figured out there was very little interest from behind the bar in service and returned to a food truck and bought a Coke to drink with my food.

I'd love a decent place just around the corner to grab a beer, but Three Canyons needs to work out some kinks. It appears from another review that this may be a trend and hopefully they'll figure it out, or I see an episode of Bar Rescue in their future.

A few suggestions...

- Work out your bar service.
- Hire a high school kid to bus tables.
- The beer menu needs help, it's only readable from one side of the bar. Make it larger, write neater and/or center it.
- The parking outside the fence needs lighting.

I've never had Shrimp and Grits - I know I know, if you're reading this and from the south, you're probably wondering, "well what the hell do you Canadians eat up in Canada - Snow?" First things first, snow is delicious especially with Maple Syrup on it, and second, Shut up, we don't have a spot like Surrey's up our way otherwise this wouldn't have been such a big deal to me!

Surrey's is a tiny cafe/diner focusing on high quality, feel good brunch and lunch meal options at silly low prices. Everyone I spoke with during my time in NOLA said you gotta do Surrey's for Shrimp and Grits... so I did.

My thoughts: Well I definitely had a food based orgasm that started from my first bite and basically ended... about 30 seconds ago - that's over 1 week in a state of orgasm, do you even know how uncomfortable that is. It's amazing! But everytime I thought about those succulent shrimp, those cream grits and that *smacks lips* gorgeous sauce, well let's just say I ain't standing up anytime soon.

I apologize if I happened to make a scene when as I ate, I'm pretty sure I used my finger to wipe the edges of my bowl (and by edges I mean the whole damn thing), but if Surrey's will have me back, I'll be there with my mouth open and waiting.

This sexually charged review is brought to you by the travels of ...

Eatcrest OUT!

Menu - WOW, what a menu. First place in Tampa to absolutely wow me with the amount of vegan options on their menu... Four whole pages of vegan options. 

Appetizers - we had vegan spring rolls and sour soup.
My Vietnamese boyfriend approved of the sour soup. The spring rolls were fried and included imitation meat. Pretty tasty.

Main - I had vegan rice vermicelli with spring rolls and he had pho. He's a super picky guy when it comes to pho and his fav place in Tampa is Pho An Hoa. Don't even talk about going to Pho Quyen to him, he'll write you off as someone with bland preferences. Anyway, I am SUPER happy to report that Trang Viet is now his 3rd favorite pho place in greater Tampa bay! My rice vermicelli was ok, but not my favorite. I prefer more pickled veggies and less noodles. Still tasted great though.

Service/Ambiance - Very friendly service. Large dining area with weird decor and music. Any Vietnamese place I've visited with great food has always had this weirdness, so I find it oddly comforting.

Overall, 5 stars. We are going to be coming back to try more of the vegan options on their menu.

I just experienced a meal so horrible that I have stopped everything that I was doing specifically to write this review. 

It's Memorial Day Weekend and with the constant prattle of BBQ on my social media, I found myself craving some after work.  Specifically, I wanted pulled pork and a good mac n cheese.  I pulled up the GrubHub when I got home at 6pm and searched "mac n' cheese" and this was the second search.

I have ordered from Phoebe's once before.  For the life of me I could not remember if I liked or disliked it or what I would have had.  I do recall once after that initial order a time I was craving BBQ and trying to call the place to order a $14 meal that GrubHub wouldn't let me complete because of their $15.00 minimum (with $2 delivery fee by the way....and then tip, of course).  I was so angry that I couldn't call the actual place that I remember not ordering at all.  

Since I still couldn't remember if I liked them or not and assumed if I had hated it I would remember, I decided to give them another shot.  I put my order in around 6:05 and GrubHub told me it would get to me around 7:05-7:15....which I expected because deliveries usually take about an hour.

Ugh, GrubHub.  I had to hit that $15 minimum and decided to order some to take to a friend's tomorrow (the kind of friend who loves eating leftovers with me...I also consider if a place's food makes good leftovers to be highly important)   I ordered the $14.49 rotisserie chicken that came with 2 pieces of cornbread, mac n cheese, and potato salad.  I also ordered the $5.99 pulled pork sandwich that came with cole slaw.  

My food was here by 6:32 and I was extremely impressed by the quick service! 

I'll start with the sandwich since that was what I planned on really eating....first I took the bun off immediately.  The bun was extremely dry and felt almost stale, as indicated by how the top was hard and then shattered into crumbs when I poked it with my finger.  The pulled pork was pretty flavorless, which was weird because it wasn't really dry.  It came with a tiny cup of really dry coleslaw.  After about 3 bites I was totally over it.

I'm a bit of a mac n' cheese snob...I fully own up to this.  Admittedly, if I don't see some kind of crust/topping (usually from breadcrumbs or toasted cheese) I am immediately disappointed; but still give it a chance as there are some delicious "easy mac-style" (as I call them) mac n cheeses in this city.  This was not a delicious one...I would even go so far as to say I would have been happier with an actual packet of Easy Mac.  This side sucked.    It didn't have any taste of cheese and would have been super-bland except there is some spice in it that just makes it....spicy.  So it basically was a weird spicy consistency in my mouth that did not remind me of mac n cheese at all.

The potato salad was flavorless.  Even a little salt and pepper would have helped....but it tasted like it had nothing.

The cornbread was BURNT BLACK ON THE BOTTOM.  It was crumbly and sucked.  I took one bite of non-burnt bit and it just wasn't good.  How can four of the five items I ordered be so freaking bland?  

The rotisserie chicken was decent, which is the only nice thing I can say.  For almost $30 I feel very ripped off and will now remember exactly how I feel next time I've got a BBQ hankering on GrubHub.  I'm actually mad at Phoebe's for being so horrible that I was so compelled to write this biting review.

After working here over the summer, which tends to be the busiest season, I've come to learn so many aspects that come with the hospitality business and also some tips I'd like to give you all if you plan on coming here: 

1) If you want to check in early, call a couple hours before your arrival. 
2) If you get here and your room isn't ready, they can hold your bags for you while you go roam around. They can also valet your car for you as well while you're waiting.
3) Please don't get mad if your room isn't ready by check in time. I understand there is a guaranteed check in time, but things do happen, such as not enough housekeepers showing up, Diamond/Platinum members having later check outs =  housekeepers service the rooms later, or other factors. Thus, refer to tip ONE!
4) Please don't yell at the front desk agents. They work their hardest and have to deal with communicating with everyone in the hotel. Not only do they have to communicate with people of all departments in the hotel, but also they have to deal with the worst guests I can't even begin to describe. 
5) If you have a request (such as ocean view, double beds, connecting rooms, third floor, accessible, first floor, close to pool, etc), CALL. Even if you put it a note on your reservation upon booking a room online, a front desk agent may look over it and not see it. If you call, the front desk agent can put a note on your reservation which is separate from what you may have put when booking the reservation online. I recommend calling a couple weeks in advance. The earlier, the better. The note will stay on your reservation. 
6) In addition to tip 5, CALL again either a couple days before or the day of to make sure the note on your reservation is there and they can accommodate for you.
7) Also in addition to tip 5, there are certain things they can't guarantee. Depending on how occupied the rooms will be, they can't guarantee many things. But they obviously try their best.
8) Staying at an ocean front hotel does not mean you get an ocean view room. I cannot stress this enough. I have had so many guests come to me booking the cheapest room and getting angry as to not getting an ocean view room. If you look online, there are options for OCEAN VIEW ROOMS. That's why they are more expensive; they GUARANTEE the ocean view for a higher price.
9) Pro tip: If you decide to visit at a time where it's not that busy, you can ask the front desk agent if there are available "room upgrades". If you booked a standard room, you can upgrade to one that has a balcony (which BY THE WAY, again, does NOT guarantee ocean view) or one to an ocean view room. This will, of course, come at a price. 
10) To address the complaints about the Santa Barbara building, it is the most newly renovated building but it is located a block and a half away from the building you check into. Thus, it does not have any ocean views but all the furnishing is brand new. It also comes with free parking.
11) Valet only on property. There is first come first serve, free parking on the street which is right outside.
12) There are 5 buildings on property: Santa Barbara, Santa Clara, Santa Maria, Santa Cruz, and Santa Rosa. (Santa Clara, Santa Maria, and Santa Cruz are the only buildings with ocean view rooms.)
13) If you want to bring a pet, Santa Rosa and Santa Barbara are your options. These buildings do not have ocean view rooms. 

Hope these tips come in handy! I wish the best of luck to this Hyatt, the people I've worked with are some of the friendliest and hardworking people I've met.

Mellow Mushroom. Gah. Just thinking that name makes my mouth water.

They are a consistently good restaurant and they make me SUPER HAPPY because they have VEGAN CHEESE! :O Granted, sometimes they put a little too much on for my taste buds, but it's so awesome they have that as an option. It's the only pizza joint I know of with Vegan Cheese. MAJOR PLUS.

I'm always seated right away (good timing, eh?) and the service is generally pretty en pointe. The waiters are always nice and are helpful with menu suggestions. 

Depending on what time of the day you go in, they'll have different stations on the TV; one day I went in and Nickelodeon was on. Another day it was ESPN. *shrug*

A friend of mine liked their beer/wine menu; he was surprised at some of the options they had (in a good way).

I'll continue to dine here because it hasn't disappointed me yet. GO MELLOW MUSHROOM.

I feel a little torn about writing this review.

I don't even live in Philly, but I kind of feel the need to protect Max's. I don't want it to become insanely popular and eventually hear its name mentioned in the same sentence as Pat's, Geno's, and Jim's. But at the same time, it would be a shame for any food enthusiast to not experience the greatness that is Max's. 

If bread and beef were to procreate in heaven, this cheesesteak would be their progeny. The boyfriend and I ordered the regular-sized cheesesteak, better known as the "giant." A cheesesteak at Jim's is about half the size of this giant. It truly is massive...about 2 feet long and ridiculously overstuffed. 

The cook (who was so friendly and really funny) knew the second we walked in that we were absolute cheesesteak noobs. We told him we were visiting and that we trusted him to construct our cheesesteak. He proceeded to slather a huge scoop of mayo onto the bread and then laid down slices of American cheese and of course, Whiz. Next, he chopped up a huge pile of meat into perfectly sized bits on the grill, and then smothered the bread with the beef, sweet and hot peppers, and mushrooms. The whole sandwich was then put back on the grill. The grill master puts LOVE into his creations. Yes, you have to wait a bit to get your cheesesteak here, but in the end, it's so worth it. 

The hot peppers are an absolute must; they added a great kick to the overall flavor. The beef here is just seasoned to perfection, and the bread was so soft and sopped up all the meaty juice. I've heard/read some people say that the meat here is dry, but I didn't think so. Be sure to grab tons of napkins and a fork to pick up all those delicious bits that are sure to come out of your sandwich with every bite you take. 

We went around 12:30 on a Saturday afternoon, and even then, you could tell that this neighborhood isn't the greatest. We definitely didn't feel like we were in any danger or anything, though. This is real Philly, an area where tourists don't really venture out to, and you know what? That's fine by me. I'd like to keep Max's my little secret.

Chinese Cravings-- 100% SATISFIED. This place can ruin your diet because everything is good! The place is well maintained, quiet and clean. Everybody is so nice and the staff are super friendly. 
This is now my favorite chinese place. You have to try the lo mein!

Food was your typical Persian cuisine, so no complaints there. I was very offended by the owner however, which is why I can't give them a higher rating.

I had found from their website that they were running a special on their entrees. They had several offers, and so when my family came, we picked 2 of the offers. After paying, I noticed that they applied only 1 of the offers, so I asked them about that. The cashier said the owner told her to only apply 1 offer per sale, and so I asked her why she didn't mention that when I pointed at the different specials, why wasn't it written anywhere, and if I could speak with him. When he came, I asked the same questions and he told me rudely to read the fine print next time. I read the entire special in front of him, and told him all it said at the bottom in small lettering was their website domain.

He took the flyer from me, read it, and then crumbled up the paper. He then started screaming, "I will never do discounts again!" and then he went around the restaurant and ripped up every flyer while still talking very loudly. Several customers were startled and the whole affair was just annoying, embarrassing, and took away from my experience. I'll never be back.

UPDATE: The owner wrote as a reply that I spent only $25, and I'm not sure where he got that number from. I spent over $55 that day, and received underwhelming customer service even after that. I've been to Pennsylvania several times, but rest assured, I don't plan to be back there.

We came in on a Saturday mid-day and waited about 20 minutes for a table. The atmosphere is wonderful and the employees are kind and caring. We each ordered a different dish from the fried chicken to my rib basket. All of it was amazing! Even the Kool-Aid was a treat. They do not serve alcohol if that's your thing but the food is excellent. Highly recommend.

If you don't know the definition of nicety, pay this restaurant a visit and you will experience Nicety (Nice and Nasty). They sound nice but they are really rude with nasty attitudes. I live on a yacht across the street and I have had to eat from here. The soup was good but the menu online will make you look like a fool. They don't have the items on the menu and their hours of operation are incorrect (at least that what they told me). Don't get your hopes up because they WILL disappoint you.  Call first and ask the right questions.

Avoid this place like the plague, unless you like eating roaches!!
I ordered today 04/07/18. I had a taste for some Chinese and spotted this place on Germantown Pike. It even said "best chinese food" in front of the store. After I paid for the expensive food, I wanted to try some before I pulled off in my car due to my hunger craving. When I opened my shrimp lomein I started digging in and even eating some until I spotted a roach. I threw it up back into the container and immediately sought for a refund. I expect this kind of quality of food from the hood Chinese food but not a restaurant that charges twice for what I usually pay.

Top 10 reasons I love this gourmet Italian market:

1.  The sandwiches from the deli counter.  Hot Italian and Mozzarella/Tomato are my favorites.  Their sub rolls are to-die-for.
2.  Coffee counter in the middle serving delicious lattes and espresso.
3.  Fresh handmade pasta.
4.  Fresh homemade breads, pastry & desserts.
5.  Fabulous cheese room with samples.
6.  Wine shop with tastings every time I've been there.
7.  Ready-to-go cold salads, soups, sandwiches, fish dip, etc.
8.  Open air, covered, large patio to enjoy your food, if you so desire.
9.  Olive bar.
10.  Fun, eclectic, and different brands of jams, jellies, sauces, ethnic food, etc.

FACT:  My cat Jack said that the accidentally-left-out-Napoleon pastry was DELICIOUS.

Tip 1:  Get there early!  Since they are not open Sundays, they are PACKED on Saturdays.

Tip 2:  They just opened a separate building (across their parking lot) as a gift shop, selling housewares, kitchen implements, soap, coffee pots, candles, etc.  Great place to pick up some holiday gifts as the prices are very reasonable.

I have mixed feelings about this place, so that's why its taken me so long to write a review.  I keep wanting to love it, because the Owners are so nice, and they were so friendly to us when we had a UYE, but in the end, the food is always just okay.

This most recent visit we had a very pleasant server who didn't speak English. We gave her our order multiple times, trying to make sure she understood.  Things were definitely lost in the translation, though - my friend wanted "light" onions on her Jaleo dish, and it came with no onions at all.

For starters we had plantains 4/5 and the Yuca a la Huancaina (yuca covered in a creamy, cheesy sauce), with the sauce on the side. This dish was 2/5, with the small pieces of yuca overcooked, dry, and just marginal.  I had the Ceviche Mixto for my meal - I get this at every Peruvian restaurant I go to.  Just a 2.5/5.  The dish was a soupy mess.  Plus, the fish itself didn't seem to have any flavor.  The portion, including the hominy and the fried corn, was also much less generous than the other places I frequent. The onions had not been marinated long enough and had far too sharp of a bite.  It was a pretty disappointing dinner.

My friends dish, at $15, did not come with a single side item, so she had to order a side of corn for $4.  It also did not come with any sauces, so she had to order them at $.50 each.  That is bizarre to me, and a real turn-off.  

I might be back for convenience sake when the ceviche craving hits, but most likely I will try and visit one of my favorites.

Ulele is one of those restaurants that you think there is no way it can live up to all the hype, and then you go, and it surpasses all your expectations!

I couldn't picture where this was even located, so when I pulled up I was pleasantly surprised at its location next to a park, near the water, with plenty of room to have tables outside.  Valet parking is offered, plus there is free street parking.

The building both outside and in is fabulous.  Made of brick, fitted with industrial-style pipe accessories and cool lighting, they have interesting sculptures scattered everywhere, and unique artwork lining the walls.  TIP 1 - there are at least 2 Picasso signed/numbered prints - find 'em!  I also heard rumor of a Dali, but didn't get to see it.  

At the small but efficient bar, I had one of their specialty cocktails - the Native Summer, a light refreshing Nolet's gin drink which was delicious.  TIP 2 - the unique pictures next to the bar represent their signature drinks - see if you can figure out which is which.  

We were lucky enough to get a behind the scenes tour of the brewery with the charming brewmaster, and you could just tell how passionate he was about this aspect of the restaurant.  There is even a beer garden courtyard area which would be great for hanging out.

Now, on to the food - it was so fun going with a huge group of people, and the passing of plates and sharing of food was a constant.  I was so pleased to taste so many different things.  My personal favorites - okra fries, roasted beet and poached pear salad with goat cheese, charbroiled oysters, Florida Native chili, and the special berry ice cream.  

Other items I enjoyed getting to try but wouldn't necessarily order (again):  white Lima beans and collards (too garlicky), corn beer quick bread (not enough flavor), the chocolate torte (too intense), and my dessert - the Guava Pie.  The pie sounded awesome, but it just had a very odd flavor that even the guava reduction on the side couldn't save.

Everybody we met working in the restaurant was welcoming and engaging.  Our two servers were spot on - friendly, efficient, and knowledgeable - although they need to recognize that when people ask for entree recommendations, they shouldn't list every item! 

So happy to have a place like this in town! Uh..la.la...

Wow, do I love this place.  Nothing much to look at on the inside or out, but the deliciousness of the food makes up for lack of ambiance.

Their burgers are crazy good. They have about 13 different varieties of burger offerings, plus they run specials all the time. They also offer steak and cheese sandwiches, chicken sandwiches, and salads (but why bother with a salad at an amazing burger joint?). 

Side orders of onion thangs, and loaded french fries are wonderful - but every burger order includes a side of french fries, so I rarely order another side item.

They also offer ice cream, milkshakes, and usually have an assortment of cakes for dessert.

Service is super friendly, and the food comes out surprisingly speedy, which is great because they do not accept phone orders. I wish they were open later hours, but consider myself lucky the few times I have made it in time after work. You are crazy if you go to a nearby fast-food restaurant; the food is way better here, and cheaper, too.

I go to Fleming's about once a year.  I know that while it will be expensive, all the food will be good, the service will be friendly, and the atmosphere will be clean and comfortable.

My friend and I sat in the bar - first at the bar for cocktails, and then moving into a bar booth for dinner.  Our server was efficient, although a little slammed with all the tables she had going.  Great deals for happy hour from 5-7 - they offer 5-$6 drinks, and 5-$5 appetizers.  

Taking advantage of the discounts, we shared the pork belly and tenderloin carpaccio to start with.  The pork belly was just okay - the best part of that plate was actually the creamy goat cheese grits that accompanied it - yum!  The sweet onion chutney was just not enough of a contrast with the rest of the plate.

The carpaccio was excellent.   It was a generous portion, sliced extremely thin, with capers and a creole mustard sauce on top,  with cheesy crackers to put it on.  My one wish would have been more 'bite' to the sauce.

For dinner I had the French Onion soup and the small plate of New Bedford Scallops.  This was one of the best French Onion soups I have ever had.  It was baked with both gruyère and parmesan cheeses, with a nice crispness to the bread inside.  The cheese topping was incredible, and the broth was flavorful without being too salty.

I liked the scallops, but didn't love them.  The sauce had flavor, but the scallops didn't really seem to.  I  know, I know, only eat steak in a steakhouse, but I'm a seafood girl!

For dessert  we split the carrot cake.  Since I am a carrot cake connoisseur, I will rate this one 6/10.  Very moist which I love, it did not have even close to enough frosting on it/in it.  I guess that's why they serve it with a side of homemade whip cream - there needs to be some sweetness to contrast the non-sweet flavor of the cake part.  More than just a tiny drizzle of dark rum caramel on the side was needed, too.

Final thought - GET WIFI!  Sheesh - close to the airport, close to many businesses - enter this century and make the upgrade - thanks!

I had an absolutely fantastic meal here last night, and I can't wait to go back. This place used to be a sushi/Thai restaurant, and the new owners have removed the booths and middle knee-wall, added new tables and lighting, and put up fun wall décor, and as a result the space is much cleaner and brighter looking than before. Parking is available both in front of and behind the restaurant.

They have a happy hour where all their saki cocktails are only $6, so I decided to try one. It was just fruit juices and saki but it was very refreshing tasting. They also have a few appetizers that are on happy hour, so we had the tako yaki.  I've never had it before, but it was an interesting combination of chewy octopus in a soft dough ball.  My favorite appetizer was the shiso rangoon however.  These are a must have!  Crunchy and delicious and not as heavy as regular rangoon because instead of a wonton wrapper as the filling vehicle, they use a shiso leaf; it was all flavor. 

We split a side dish of the garlic butter bok choy, and I can't imagine ever coming here and not ordering this dish.  They were grilled and perfectly cooked, and the sauce was not too heavy or too garlicky, which I loved.

I finished with my typical go-to meal, a sashimi platter, and I can honestly say this was one of the best I've ever had.  Large assortment of different fish, perfectly sized to be one bite each, and incredibly fresh tasting. I was so full but I had to finish the platter because it was so amazing.

Service was spot-on the entire visit, their plate presentation was outstanding, and the food was all delectable-I highly recommend a visit.

$600+ (with tax) per night rooms?  hahahahahahahahahahaha ::wipes tears of mirth from my eyes::  Oh Hard Rock Hotel, you have a seriously over-inflated opinion of yourself!  We booked six rooms for our holiday party with no discounts, and I seriously feel we are owed half that money refunded.

The hotel is currently (12/2018) under 7 days a week/24 hours a day construction.  So, you hear constant banging as you maneuver around all the different roped-off areas. The pool is also closed for construction, so that was unavailable as well. But - even if there had been no construction, and the pool was available, there is no way the quality of the room was worth that much.

At best, it was a $200 per night room. Comfortable bed, television, two sinks in the bathroom, yet no bathroom door, and a tinny wifi clock radio to listen to music through.  A nice touch, but not worth $600.

Staff was excellent - from the bellboy to the front desk to the security team available to answer questions, yet even that does not justify the crazy price tag for the hotel rooms.

3.5 Stars

I thought the ice cream was good, but between the high cost and the extremely sloooooow service, it really is just a three point five-star joint.

They have a pretty complicated ice cream menu for the uninitiated, so I think a lot of people settle for one of their cool nitro ice cream combo's which also comes with a syringe of flavor (chocolate, honey, etc.) for $8.50.

I ordered a simple scoop of cotton candy ice cream in a cup, which comes with your choice of one topping for $4.50.  With rainbow sprinkles on it, plus a tiny fluff of actual cotton candy, it was delicious.

Jon ordered one of the combos, and watching the lady make it was like watching a movie slowed down to half-speed. I don't know how they'll manage when they are actually busy. When he finally received it, he enjoyed the combo of flavors.

They also sell candy in bulk, with candy dispensers along the wall, as well as in bins along the bottom, so it's a good place to satisfy your sugar cravings.

Since I was meeting a friend for dinner at 6 pm, I went early to take advantage of the great "Social Hour" (happy hour) I had read about. All the seats at both the front (air conditioned) bar area, and the back (more outside, not so air conditioned) bar area were taken. I went to the hostess, who had no problem seating me at a table in the bar area.

The long communal table was very dimly lit, and it was almost impossible to read the happy hour menu. My server was very personable, although she did disappear for long periods at a time. The bar area was pretty loud, and I felt like the groups of people on both sides of me were yelling at each other in order to be heard.

I really enjoyed my food, although my friend did not her chicken sandwich at all. We started with the mini corn dogs, which were very tasty, served with a spicy ketchup.  For my meal I had the rotisserie chicken with kale salad, and it was fantastic, although it could have used more chicken. The kale was diced nice and small, the goat cheese added a nice contrast, and the dressing used on the salad made the whole dish sweet and flavorful.

For dessert we had to share their Whiskey Cake and it was fabulous - served warm, topped with pecans, sitting in a bourbon anglaise, with a bowl of fresh whipped cream to add as needed.  Crazy good!

M&P is a brand new place in Seminole Heights.  Normally, I give a new place a few months to work out the flaws before writing a review, but there were no glaring flaws, and I probably still won't be back for a meal, so the time to write this is now.

Cool, semi-industrial looking interior, with their own parking lot directly behind the restaurant.  Entrance is on the side of the building.  There was a hostess there, who is obviously still learning her job - a smile and a friendly 'hello' would go a long way.

Since we were there at 5:30 pm on a Sunday night, there were plenty of tables to be had. The bar part seemed to be doing a busier business than the restaurant part.  Our waiter was obviously new to the job (forgot to remove our menus, never asked us if we wanted a soda refill, etc.), but he was fine, and will obviously gain experience the more he works.

The food menu is ambitious: not a huge offering of items, but many, many ingredients in each dish.  In my personal opinion, there was too much going on - my cobia crudo starter was described on the menu as "Passion fruit juice and seeds + jalapeño and lime white balsamic + tarragon honey and oil + pink Himalayan salt + nitro watermelon radish + watermelon ice" - for $13.50.  While the fish was obviously fresh, the only hint of flavor/texture I had was from the tiny piece of watermelon on each, the crunch of the passion fruit seeds, and the salt.

I also had the Heirloom Tomato salad, which I enjoyed more than the cobia.  A nice piece of burratta (an Italian cheese made from mozzarella and cream), fresh tomatoes, and watercress in a balsamic dressing.  The cheese was outstanding, and really complemented the fresh tomato flavor.

Dinner for two, including two sodas, was $57 before tip.  And therein lies the true problem - I didn't feel like the meal was worth the price.  I felt like the portions were surprisingly tiny, especially for the cost. My boyfriend's fresh fish for dinner was a miniscule portion of fish, served over a tiny scoop of lentils for $23. I have no problem paying good money for great good, but when the food is just okay, and I leave still hungry, that is a red flag to me.

Yes, I'll probably be back to try their coffee, or perhaps have a drink at the bar. But for dinner, I'll be hitting any of the other numerous restaurants in Seminole Heights that seem to have a better grasp of what it takes to provide a satisfying meal.

A good, solid breakfast. This is what you hope a breakfast place will be when you go out to eat. Friendly servers, clean atmosphere, and delicious food.

We started with the beignets bites, and these were my absolute favorites. The bowl was chock full of very crispy yet fluffy mini beignets that were loaded with powered sugar - perfect.

For my meal I had Shelly's Pancakes combo.  I'm not usually a pancake person, but the pictures I saw of the pancakes topped with fresh strawberries, blueberries and banana slices looked so delicious, I knew I had to have them.  I had them as a combo, so they came with bacon and home fries.  The pancakes were great, the bacon was okay, and the potatoes were a bit greasy, but overall the food was really good.

Service was okay - our waitress was very nice, and she was efficient at the beginning, but seemed to slack off near the bill-paying time, in her efforts to clean tables, etc.  I love that the Owner came over mid-meal to inquire how everything was.   All in all, I look forward to returning and working my way through their menu.

After extensive research, I can officially declare Samuari Blue in Ybor the best sushi in Tampa. It is by far the tastiest, freshest, and most innovative sushi place around.

Start with the ahi tuna tataki, which is my favorite. Not only is the tuna cooked perfectly, but the ponzu sauce is so amazing I could drink it with a straw. Then they also tease you with a tiny bit of crunchy harusame salad on the plate, and it is just perfect.

If you are with a non-raw fish lover (crazy!) then start with the blue crab rangoon.  You have my personal guarantee that every person will be mmm-ing from bite one.  The edamame is also a good option, because it is a generous portion and perfectly cooked each time.

For my meal I either split a couple of rolls with friends, or splurge and have the sashimi platter.  The platter is not cheap, but every single fish item tastes different and distinct, and I love leaving sated on sushi.

I have tried many, many rolls here.  My boyfriend's favorite by far is the tuna summer of love - which is made spicy with chili oil, and wrapped in cucumber instead of rice like majority of the other rolls.  My favorites are the gooey volcano roll, the crunchy soft shell crab roll (aka spider roll), and most recently I had the red devil roll which was outstanding and spicy!  The caterpillar roll is usually a crowd pleaser for those that don't want spicy.

Samurai Blue has a full bar and an extensive cocktail menu, and I love their specialty martinis.  The venue is gorgeous, with both booths and tables, but if you get the opportunity, sit at the sushi bar and watch the sushi chefs work their magic.  Not inexpensive, but always worth it!

We loved our meal here!  Located in a busy strip mall, Cazador Grill is bigger inside than it looked like it would be from the outside.  Nicely, if simply decorated, it had both tables and booths available for dinner.  The restaurant offers beer and wine, and next time I'll definitely be trying the sangria.

Our server (who turned out to be a son of the Owner) could not have been friendlier or more attentive.  It's a pretty simple menu, essentially a page of appetizers, sides and seafood dishes, and a page of meat entrees. I went with one of their house specialties, the Arroz Con Mariscos (rice with seafood).  I loved that the shrimp in it were large and fresh and plentiful. The flavor of the dish was outstanding.  One other person in my party got this dish as well, and we both could not stop raving about how good it was.

For dessert they have a separate menu, and I went with the traditional Peruvian cookie called Alfajores - a shortbread cookie sandwich with a layer of dulce de leche in it.  These were, by far, the best I have ever had in a Peruvian restaurant.  Light, flaky, not too dry, just perfect.

After trying most of the local Peruvian spots in the Tampa Bay area, I have to say this is one of my new favorite places due to a nicer atmosphere, more attentive service, tastier food, and better business hours than most of the other Peruvian options.

What a wonderful place to come for lunch! And the express menu is an absolute steal; I had a food coma to prove this! Nineteen has a beautiful atmosphere and rightfully so atop the Bellevue with a view of the city skyline. Every place to sit is comfortable and clean and ambiance is sophisticated.

For the express lunch, you are tempted by a buffet display of appetizers, a set entrée, another display of delicious desserts, and choice of soda or iced tea as well. I ordered the grilled marinated pork as my entrée with gnocchi and then proceeded to the display. There was a cheesy Caesar salad, pasta with sun-dried tomatoes, another salad of greens with feta cheese and Portobello, some cheeses to sample, and curried shrimp. I was also introduced to that delicious little delight of a kumquat. All delicious. The pork was soft and delicious and definitely filled me up by that point. But how could I resist all those desserts? Delectable cheesecake bites, strawberry shortcake, fruit tarts, and cookies! I would only complain that there is a little bit too much cream on some of these desserts, but otherwise, great!

At first I thought it was annoying to take the elevator just to go to the bathrooms below just one floor, thinking the elevator would take a long time to come, but they are fast. So don't you worry.

Some mishaps: the hostess who greeted us was not very friendly at all. Granted, some of us may not have been dressed to dine here, but mind you, lady, we will be back at some point paying good money to keep you from being unemployed. Everyone else was very friendly.

For $19, an absolutely, hands down, solid deal!

Just another place serving sonoran hotdogs you say... well yes, BUT these dogs are the best I have had in town, even beating my usual favorite El Guero Canelo! Maybe its eating outside, maybe its the huge condiment station, maybe it was the real Mexican coke I sipped on while waiting... Whatever the reason, I am VERY HAPPY to have some great Mexican Food so close to where I spend 40 hours a week!  El Nene is fast, delicious and reasonably prices.. $2.75 for a Sonoran Dog shouldn't hurt your pocket book too much!

So i bit the bullet, paid a few extra dollars and finally stepped into the roadhouse theater. It was a little overwhelming at first but the guys behind the ticket counted are super helpful. And so instead of getting distracted by the gelato bar, the popcorn samples and the large bar standing in the center of the room I walked into my theater found my big comfy seat and settled in. The seats were so well spaced out, comfortable and they recline with a foot rest! Its sort of set up for groups of two to go together as the seats are paired up with a little counter every two seats. Next step - order some food! They have an ok menu of burgers, pizza, poppers, chips, popcorn with some really creative flavors and of course a bunch of yummy desserts, gelato and milkshakes! Most of the items have movie themed names which is corny and cute. But the best thing about the menu is the entire draft beer selection is Arizona beer. I ordered a Sentinel Peak Dunkel and the Ghostburger. The Ghostburger was spicy spicy spicy with jalapeños and onion strings. I will definitely order it again. They were out of waffle fries so they substituted curly fries which were pretty tasty. I recommend not getting the parmesan on the fries but it was an interesting combo. We got there about 20 minutes before the show so we were almost finished eating by the time the movie started. I definitely recommend getting there with enough time to eat because as soon as the lights went out it was hard to eat. The other super neat thing about this place is you can order during the movie with a pen and a notepad! The servers pop over barely noticeable - grab your order and next thing you know you are comfortably watching a movie and beer is hand delivered to you. Great experience watching a movie, well worth the little extra!!

SUMMARY:  Great atmosphere, clean restaurant, professional service, and great food to boot! 

BACKGROUND:  On a business trip for a client in Belle Chasse. Decided to Yelp a few restaurants in this new-to-me area. Not the toniest part of town, but safe enough.

FOOD
The boss and I each had different meals. Since I had the smallest of small lunches (I hate having a full stomach while flying), I was starving from mid-morn to the time we landed. Thus I got the biggest thing on the menu I could find (under $25 :), which was a 1/2 rotisserie chicken with 2 sides. I opted for the bbq sauce because the table next to us had ordered some bbq ribs and the family was really enjoying their food.  The two sides I ordered were different in taste to me. The better of the two was the Thai pea pods. Really yummy with a light Asian sauce. Enthusiastic 5/5. The collard greens w/ bacon was unfortunately disappointing. The greens seemed like it was handled too much or stirred to much and was lacking structure and almost chopped up into bits. I did like that it wasn't as sour as some greens I've had, but for a big collard greens fan like myself, I'd give it a 3/5.  

The bbq rotisserie chicken was outstanding.  Now true, I was hungry. But even in my worst pangs of hunger, I will stop eating if its not that good. The chicken was really moist on the inside and the sauce was really well balanced. Not to sweet, not too tangy.  Just right for my palate.  I ate the whole thing to my surprise. 5/5.

ATMOSPHERE
As mentioned, clean and well done. 

SERVICE
A super wonderful waitress whose name I forget (young African American lady) was really pleasant, visited us at the right time to check up on us, and brought us what we needed with a pleasant smile. Sorry I forgot your name but we ate on 12/7/21 in the back corner and we both wanted to say you were really great.

RETURN VISIT?
If I was in the area again, yes for sure. But we're out here one more day and possibly if the boss isn't too thrilled with my other recommendations, we'll come back.

1864 Tavern is a classy bar with old west flair. You don't need to step off of California Ave. to be transported back in time where the drinks are strong and the hallway to the bathroom is built like a mine shaft.

I was here for the grand opening last week, and had a blast at this unique, new, cocktail bar. There was a very diverse crowd, and everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves. The decor is very Virginia City, which is great for those who don't want to take the long drive out there. I ordered the VC Mule, which was their take on the Moscow Mule. No copper cup, but there was definitely some kick in it. All of their drinks are made with quality ingredients, and definitely worth the above-average Reno cocktail prices.

I was impressed by the skills of their mixologists, and the fact that they had mostly independent beers on their menu. It will be interesting to see the type of crowd that eventually calls this place their home bar. Next time I'm dying to grab the Abraham Lincoln booth.

NEVER AGAIN.  We had a mini class reunion this evening that has been set up for the last month.  We chose this restaurant since it is away from the normally busy areas of Santa Barbara during the Old Spanish Days Fiesta celebrations.

We had a good time until we received our bill.  Now I don't have a problem with having an automatic 18% gratuity added to the bill but they really do shortchange the staff since I normally leave 20%.  BUT, when an extra $150.00 was added to the bill as a "rental fee", well that was just too much.  It was never told to our group coordinators.  None of the three remembered ever hearing about this extra charge.  When confronted, they were told, "Well it is Fiesta and you did take up 3 tables".  

Yes, we took up three of the 8-10 tables outside.  During our 3 hours there, only 2 other exterior tables were ever used, and more than 1/2 the inside dining room was empty as could be during our whole time present.  What a rip off.  For the management to arbitrarily add this extra fee is disgusting.  Now had the restaurant actually been busy or had we been advised of this fee, that would be a different story.  But to put it in the middle of the itemized bill is theft at best.

Don't patronize this restaurant.  You can't trust what they will do to you.  Crooks.

I've been wanting to try this place forever and finally decided to. I ordered online, which was an easy process. I couldn't figure out how to order a drink, but that was a minor issue and decided I could probably just buy one once I got there. 

The confirmation email said to allow up to 45 minutes for your pizza. However, I immediately headed there. Once I arrived, the employees greeted me and asked for my order number. Although it had only been 20 minutes, I was told my pizza was being cut. I added an order of cookies and a bottled water. I noticed once inside that there's also a window on the side, so you don't actually have to go in if you don't want. 

I HAD to get The Trap Pizza. I'd just seen too much about it. Let me tell you...I opened that box and was stunned. It looked amazing. I took a bite and got angry! HOW DARE THESE PEOPLE MAKE SOMETHING SO DELICIOUS. That pizza was cheesy, dripping in butter, and loaded with crab and shrimp. It was decadent. It was rich. It was incredible. I will say, it was so rich in flavor that after 3 pieces, I was full. I wasn't sure how it would heat up if I took it home, so I picked off the seafood and took a few more bites before saying goodbye. And yes, I immediately regretted not bringing it home and trying to heat it up the next day! 

The cookies were also delicious. You get four for $5. They do just come in a little sack. I wish they had a little pizza box for them to be carried in, but not a huge deal. 

The women that assisted me were AWESOME. Overly nice. Came out and asked if I wanted them to light the candle on my table to warm me up since it was chilly. I passed but appreciated the gesture. I liked being able to eat outside and they had music on as well which created a fun vibe. 

I'll definitely be back! Totally worth the hype!!!

Oh man. I'm really torn, y'all. I have been following along and waiting on this place to open. As someone raised in Tennessee, I enjoy good Southern food and struggle to find it in Indiana. I also recognize we went as soon as they opened and there are going to be kinks to work out, so I'll try to focus more on the food. 

Spodie-Odee was the drink I started off with. Tasty! Think red wine mixed with Sprite (and I believe orange soda). We also started off with the cornbread, which was good! It comes with sides of butter, honey, and pimento cheese. They could have just put three sides of pimento cheese...it was yummy! 

For meals, my table got two pork loins, shrimp and grits, and I got the catfish. My two friends said the pork loin and sides were cold. I believe there was a mixup because we waited about an hour for food, and the shrimp and grits came AFTER the other three of us had finished eating. The two said the pork loin was good but wished it was hot. Once my friend got the shrimp and grits, he enjoyed them! He said he wished the grits were cheesier but besides that, he enjoyed it. 

As for mine...Well, let it be known that catfish is my favorite, so I was really looking forward to it. It's pecan crusted, which I enjoyed. I wish it had a bit more seasoning, but the pecans provide a crunch that I enjoyed. It came with mashed potatoes and okra, although our server said okra wasn't available (asparagus was being put in its place). My mashed potatoes weren't hot and needed some salt and pepper. My asparagus was fine. Overall, I missed the depth of flavor that I find in the South. I wanted layers and seasoning...and I just didn't get it. It was also a LOT of catfish to have no sauce (if even on the side). I appreciate the thought of the pickled onion, but the catfish was too dry to not have something to accompany it. 

On a scale of 1-5, we all said our experience ranged from a 2-3.5. Everyone said they would return again, but would try something else. I think I'll wait a month or so...give the servers time to get everything down, give the kitchen time to get their timing down, and I'll try it again!

Been excited about this place opening, and was looking forward to having lunch there today. To be in a location that is challenging, there was a very long line at lunch. Pro- people want to eat there. Con- the lack of staff resulted in the line remaining long for quite a while. 
I got the #1, and as far as flavor, it was there. However, the overwhelming thought I had when trying the food was...it was cold. Not hot. Not warm. Not room temperature. COLD. Cold to the point that I asked my friend if it was supposed to be cold. 
I recognize that the place just opened and I'm willing to look past a few things...temperature of the food isn't one of them. I'll try it one more time and see if it's any better. Maybe I'll try takeout next time...that way, I'll have access to my microwave. You know, just in case.


Update: Went back in for lunch today. Had the bibimbap again but this time, got it in the stone bowl. More expensive. Longer wait to get it. Totally worth it. My only feedback is that the employee has to list the vegetables for every customer. I heard her do it today probably 15 times. Make a list for customers and put on the glass. Will save time in the line, as well as for the employee.

This place is in the back of a Mexican grocery store and a real hidden gem! The server brought chips and two salsas to our table once we sat down. The chips could really benefit from a little salt when they're straight outta the fryer. Both salsas were spicy. One was straight up hot. I like spicy but they were both a little too much for me. I got three tacos for dinner- one each of steak, shrimp, and chorizo. The shrimp one was incredible. Simple with cilantro, onion, and lime to squeeze. The shrimp was chopped up, which I liked. There was also a ton of meat on all the tacos. The steak one was good as well. I was not a fan of the chorizo. It wasn't horrible but the meat was dry and not super flavorful. But I would go back time and time again for more shrimp tacos!

I was at Blooming grove for a holiday work party, with a large crowd so we had pre-ordered food being served buffet-style. The place itself is quaintly located in Ewing surrounded by mostly homes on either side, in a Victorian style building.

Since it was a buffet, got to sample a few things, garlic bread, bacon wrapped scallops, grilled shrimp, meat balls penne pasta and cheese cake. Everything was well made and was flavorful, but the garlic bread was awful (soaked up and felt like eating oil), the cheesecake though was perfect, not too heavy, yet deliciously satisfying.

Hope to come back sometime soon may be for a quick lunch this time around.

I've been here a few times.  The food is good, but my recent experience last weekend was very unpleasant.  I had dinner with my friend who introduced me to the restaurant and has dined there at least 5 times; in fact she was greeted by the manager when she arrived.

Our visit was marred and unpleasant because of our very rude server Amber.  My friend asked for her daughter's burger to be cooked in a separate frying pan because she has celiac disease (the restaurant had done this before for both a burger and I believe eggs).  Our server,  proceeded to argue with us that they don't do this.  My friend asked the server to ask the chef, indicating that the chef had done it in the past.  When the server returned she told us that the chef would do it this time, but proceeded to tell us that the chef said he never recalled doing it and that he couldn't do it again.  She also added that he was very busy and it was hard for him to do it.  Really, did the server have to argue with us?  Make us feel bad?  Even our 12 year old daughters recognized how rude she was.  

When it came time for dessert -- 12 year old girls love dessert - our server argued with us again about the ice cream and blueberries (that we had ordered before) so we gave up and went somewhere else.  My friend, determined to make this right so she could feel better about dining here again, asked to speak with the manager but was told he was too busy to speak with us.  

I live in Queen Village, like this location and frankly, I like the Whetstone salad a lot.  Not sure I can bring myself to go back right now.

I have been to a lot of the newer style nice restaurants. I have never felt as welcomed to a place as this. Max was wonderful. Even if the food hadn't been as amazing as it was, I would  come back for Max. We were right on time for our reservations, but had a little bit of a wait for our table. Not a problem. Max got us a seat at the bar and apologized for our wait. By the way, reservations. Make them. This isn't your typical St. Louis restaurant where you can always just walk in and get seated. It's small and if you want a table, call earlier that week. (We called earlier that day and could only get seated after 9)
The food? To die for. You'll see my pictures. We had mussles (big, juicy delicious mussles with crispy bread and crazy good savory broth), mushroom polenta (creamy, amazing. Even my boyfriend liked it and he hates mushrooms plus it was a huge portion!), and the butternut squash agnolotti (dark horse favorite of my boyfriend. He usually hates the vegetarian options, but he loved it. I loved it too, but I already knew I love little pockets of squashy goodness). Plus foccacia to start, just brought to  your table. That's an amazing amuse bouche. Drinks were whatever, but really reasonably priced. Really everything was. The portions were bigger than most restaurants of this type. I could never leave hungry. And the prices are super reasonable when you're talking about the quality of food. 

Go go go!!!! Just call ahead. Like a few days ahead.

Let's make a pro/con list:

Pro: Cool location. The penitentiary looks awesome lit up at night across the street.

Con: $10 cover for the improv show we saw (a friend was performing). This isn't Second City. 

Pro: $2 Brooklyn Pumpkin Lager (I think lager?)

Con: The waitress told us it was so cheap because they're trying to get rid of it.

Pro: Macaroni and Cheese! With tomato soup?

Con: Macaroni and bland with tomato sauce

Pro: Solid bloody mary.

Con: The bartender would rather text and eat than serve patrons to earn tips.

Dammit, Brendan, you're going to make me go broke.

The owners of Memphis Taproom and Local 44 opened this little gem, and I'm in love.

I went opening night, and it was PACKED (I biked by last night and again, packed). But oddly enough, for being dimly lit, nighttime, and full, it seemed open and airy. The beer was great, the food was great, the staff was great. People were extremely helpful and happy to be, despite the crowd five strong at the bar waiting to order. They were also handing out free "samples" of key menu items. 

I will definitely be back here. Especially because Brendan recognized me from Local 44 and came to say hi (I paid entirely in quarters, once, and he didn't even care).

OH OH OH!
Just be aware, both Local 44 and Resurrection use peanut oil. I don't know if Memphis does, but I'd watch out if you have a peanut allergy.

Luckily, beers are peanut free!

This place rules. Hard.

My lunch pals and I were discussing whether or not to try this place the day before the hard opening or the day of (they were offering 30% off!) and we just couldn't wait. And it was awesome. So we went back. The next day.

The food is nothing like I've ever had. I don't think it's authentic south Indian, but rather a fusion of Indian, Indo-Chinese, and American flavors. I've had the Masala Deluxe (ask for it without onions if you don't want to be tasting onions all day) with goat cheese instead of American, the curry 'chicken', and the something avocado dosas. All so good. 

I want to see if I can manage to get each dish on the menu.

This is the best place in Philly to get a cheese steak and the experience was priceless. They said cash only FYI so go to the ATM first they do have ATM inside but it was blocked by the massive line. The line was ridiculously long  and chaotic in a small space. Be prepared to wait because it seems to take forever and a day just to get a philly cheese steak, however it is super large plus good and we was able to split it three ways. The staff were friendly and even joked around with us while we waited in line and they restocked items. They have this bar or club next-door where you can sit down to eat your food. You can even get a drink with your cheesesteak. The great part is that you can shop or get several items without even leaving your seat. Several people come inside and sale all kinds of goodies such as earbuds, clothes, etc.  If you do step outside there's people who have tables set up who sell laundry detergent, soap, etc. Its a one stop shop! It's a busy area so there's a lot of people in and out and around the corner, but a definite place to visit in Philly. The atmosphere reminded me of south Chicago.  As a foodie I recommend.

Who doesn't love a simple atmosphere with amazing coffee and food?! I loved this place and will definitely be back. We stopped in on a Saturday morning before heading to a festival. Its in Germantown and is very open and almost Scandinavian. There was a simple coffee menu, fresh baked pastries and a light lunch menu. I went with a latte while my hubs had the flash chilled brew - both were great. For food, we shared a goose salami sandwich on focaccia served with a german style potato salad. We absolutely loved the flavors of the sandwich, although there was a little too much olive oil added. The potato salad was fresh and clean in flavor. 

This is a great spot - I will be backs for dates with the hubs and sister chit chat!

This place is great! If you love beer, go here. 

First, the atmosphere is really awesome. Inside there are tons of beers for purchase -by a six pack or single servings. They have a whole area dedicated to home brewing too. At the little bar area, there is tons of beers on draft - some traditional that you love, along with a great selection of unique beers - nitro, basil ryes or even kombucha. The staff is extremely friendly - knowing in detail the types of beer and tasting notes. You can (seemingly) try whatever you like and order a pint to stay. You also can order a tasting of either 4 beers ($7.5) or 7 beers ($13.5). Although they don't have food, they have a food truck almost regularly out front and they said you are welcome to bring your own food. 

Parking can be tricky since it is limited but it is a great and fun place to sample beers or restock your inventory

What an unassuming place to grab a great burger and delicious fries! We were out in the 5 points area of East Nashville, when this preggo lady got a craving for burgers. Normally, we go the Pharmacy, but noon on a Saturday meant a wait. Well, I checked my handy dandy Yelp app, and this place had amazing reviews - why not try it out! 

Its literally a little 'grillshack'. No bathroom, no indoor dining. Its takeout or picnic tables. They make all their burgers fresh, with Porter Road Butcher meat. You can get it regular (which comes with cheese) or with bacon. So of course, any carnivore adds the thick cut bacon. It took about 15 minutes for the burgers and fries, but they were fresh, hot, crispy and juicy. I was in love! They put Old Bay Seasoning out on the table to sprinkle on your hand cut jumbo size fries. Which by the way, it had to be like two huge potatoes worth of fries! They have a bunch of dipping sauces too - I opted for the sriracha ketchup and honey mustard. 

It was wonderful- we have been back a few times since to get take out and I would love to try their breakfast. Yum!
