Ernie C and Michael T are men of refinement, men of taste. When they both told me that my knowledge of Reno's taquerias was incomplete without a trip to Los Gallos, I had to listen. So, yeah I went, and yeah, they are were both right...it's amazing. 

As nearly everyone has noted, unless you are a huge fan of murals depicting Riña de Gallos, the decor here is nothing special. Lots of seating. 

Of course you'll want some tacos. Seriously, get some tacos. The al pastor is nicely done, the lengua satisfying and toothy, the cabeza is exemplary. Their carne asade is a stand out. It's flavorful, delicious, with just the right amount of char. 

The carne asade plate comes with rice and beans (nothing earth shattering here), lovely grilled onions, a little guac and thin sliced steak. Not the best in Reno, but in the top 3 certainly. 

While they do serve the standard ceviches, it doesn't seem to be their "thing." Los Gallos is about meat. Seriously, get meat. 

There is, of course, a nicely appointed chips and salsa bar with pico de gallo, a red sauce, a green sauce, pickled carrots, and radishes. The chips are fresh and you can serve yourself. 

If you are still with me, gentle reader, I've saved the best for last. The spicy chicken is not even really on the menu, it's on a kind of side menu, so that you might not notice it. But notice it, and order it, you must. It's grilled chicken chopped and slathered with a slightly tomato-y sauce (bbq?), and loaded with spicy sauce. Get it. Savor it. Use the provided tortillas to mop up the sauce. It is, indeed, somewhat spicy. It's distinctive. It tastes GREAT. 

They do not have iced tea, which is a shame. But otherwise it's a great place to watch some Mexican Variety Shows, people watch the folks strolling on Virginia, and eat some amazing food. Highly recommended.

Gentle reader, before we go any further, I'd suggest you look at the name of this establishment. A pescador is a fisherman. If you go into El Pescador and order something aside from fish...well...I don't know what to tell you.

El Pescador has a decor stuck somewhere in time and somewhere not terribly recent. I, for one, am fond of the ambiance...but then I'm a sucker for those tropical pictures that have speakers in them that play sea sounds...also...plastic sea life stapled to fake fish nets. 

The best things on the menu are the most "auténtico." The tostada mixta is a delightful mix of shrimp and octopus. A bit toothy just like it should be. I'd also suggest the grilled fish tacos and the shrimp tacos. Both feature a nice slaw and fresh pico. The grilled fish tacos come with a slice of avocado. The Vuelve A La Vida is an insane gallon sized portion of sea life in a tomato broth. Delicious but huge. Take note that most of the tostadas and cocktails are served with ketchup, just as in Mexico. Thankfully it's on the side. 

The chips and salsa are good, but nothing out of the ordinary. The iced tea is brewed. The margaritas are huge. 

El Pescador is not the cheapest place in town, nor the fanciest, but when I'm craving some octopus tostada action, it's the best in town.

Came here for Happy Hour yesterday.  Absolutely amazeballs.  My tastebuds sang with joy.  Panko encrusted shrimp roll was delish!  This is the best sushi I have ever had in STL.  Service was great.  Ambiance was dark & inviting.  Get here early to avoid the crowd.  Parking is typical for South Grand.  But, totally worth every single penny.

OMG!  This place is really good.  Better than any BBQ that I've had.  I came here on a Saturday night knowing that there was no sports game playing nearby.  Less crowded around 5:30 p.m..  The pulled pork sandwich was tender & delish!  The mustard potato salad was sooo good & crunchy!   Foodgasm after foodgasm.  I am soooo glad that I listened to my friends about this place.  Parking is a bit of a pain in the butt, but totally worth it.  There's an upstairs room that I didn't even try going.  Tiny hole in the wall.  I am sooo coming back here to try other things.

Just a forewarning that this review is going to be very long and detailed, so if you're only going to read one thing from my review, read this: THERE WAS A LIVE, SQUIRMY, MOVING WORM IN OUR FOOD, with NO REPLACEMENT OF FOOD, AND ONLY CREDITED $2 OFF OUR ~$150 BILL. YES, TWO WHOLE DOLLARS.

Now, rewind. When I first walked into this place, I was hit with a wonderful aroma of pine trees mixed with lattes; this place looked, felt, and smelled wonderful. We were seated in a green-house like setting, with an urban yet natural decor. We were greeted with an attentive server for our brunch, and I'm thinking that this will be a 5 star place...then the food came out, and it went all downhill from there. 

Food was not on par with the venue - our omelettes and breakfast sandwiches were just above any ol' breakfast food. Still, because of the setting, I was still loving the place. BUT THEN! Out of my friend's $25 breakfast steak, she picked up one of her mushrooms/salad, and on it was LIVE WORM, SQUIRMING AWAY FOR FEAR OF BEING EATEN. We immediately called the server over, and kindly notified the him that there "was a little friend" in our food. His only response? "Oh, I wonder how that survived the oven." He took the mushroom and friend away - and said and did nothing else. SO, I guess the expectation is just to proceed to eat the contaminated plate of food?! Well, lucky for Terrain, my friend didn't seem to mind as much that there was just a LIVE WORM in her plate, and she continued to just eat around the salad/mushrooms where it was found. 

When the check came, we noticed they did not credit us anything at all for the fact that there was a LIVE worm. We called the server back over, and he brought over someone else, who I would assume was the manager. ALL she stated was, "I don't know how the worm survived the oven in 400 degree temperature." OKAY, is that all you guys care about?! It doesn't matter HOW the worm got there (for all we know you guys could've put the worm in there yourselves), but the point is there WAS A LIVE WORM IN THERE. Maybe they would've actually cared a bit if the worm actually died in the oven? She then let us know she would be giving our coffee and truffle oil ($7 total) for free. Gee, thanks for the generosity when you ruined a $25 plate. But after we paid the bill, we realized we were tricked and she actually had only taken off the $2 truffle oil! TWO DOLLARS OFF FOR A LIVE WORM, EVERYONE. 

And still, because we had a party of 6, our server, who handed us a live worm and no apology, still walked away with 20% tip. Thanks for being generous with yourselves while literally feeding your customers dirt.

This is probably one of the nicest and biggest Chinese restaurants in the area. When you walk in you see a large open space with multiple dining rooms and attention to decoration. But, some of that wears off when you sit down and your table is the stereotypical Chinatown dirty table with a paper menu. 

Still, the food is authentic, even with English speaking servers! Soup dumplings have a thinner layer of skin than at dim sum garden or toms dim sum, making for a tastier experience! 

Prices here are slightly above average Chinese food ($11 for string beans with no meat, anyone?) but service makes up for it (although they did give us the wrong item but it was easily switched out). 

Btw, beef scallion pancakes is a must :)

Excellent food. Really great!
Came here this past Sunday . We ordered chicken flautas , a spicy chicken burrito and fajitas. 
As soon as we sat down, we were given chips with 2 kinds of salsa. One was red and mild. The other was green and slightly spicy. Both were really good. 
Chicken flautas , we scarfed these down. Actually we both burnt our mouths. It was worth it. 
My chicken burrito was very good . It wasn't super spicy, just a mild heat to it. 
My husband had fajitas that were gone as quick as the flautas. 
Our server was quick , nice and on the ball.  
Nice spot, we came at 2pm on a Sunday . Perfect time as there were only 3 other tables taken. 
We will definitely return, SOON.

You know a meal is great , when it's the next day and you wish you could go right back there and eat the meal again ! 


I am love with the vodka pizza here. 
My first apartment almost 20 years ago was around the corner. I am upset this place didn't exist then. I might still be living there. 

My husband and I ordered individual pies. 
For the first time ever, I saw him struggle to finish his heavyweight pie. On the other hand , I had no problem polishing off my vodka pie. ( I have a problem. I don't care. ) 

The fries are the only thing I wasn't crazy about. They were the beer battered type. Not my favorite BUT they were good. 

Our server was nice, the space was clean. 
We got here around 4pm right before it got crowded. 

Maybe I should move back to the neighborhood? The vodka pie has me thinking about it.

My niece chose this spot today for lunch. 
I was pleasantly surprised. I don't expect too much from diners but I'll do just about anything for my nieces so I wound up here. 
The place is open 24 hours. My father in law raves about their breakfast. Which is why he got an omelette for lunch. 
There is a section on the menu labeled mini meals. I ordered from here thinking it would be small. Far from it , I ordered stuff shells . I believe 4, maybe 5 came with my order. Plus they offered soup or salad & bread. 
Here's what really blew my mind. The sauce on the stuffed shells was pretty good. Not as good as mine but pretty great for a diner with hundreds of items on the menu. 
My niece was happy with her chicken parmigiana. My husband said his burger was good. His only complaint was the ketchup wasn't Heinz. That's a serious offense in our family. Our waitress was nice enough. I'm not looking for a friend when I go out. Just bring my food and be decent about it. 
Would I return ? Yes, probably in the near future as my nieces love it here and I liked it. 
Definitely one of the better diners in the area.

Once again, the Cunningham Restaurant Group blows us away. I don't think there's a single dish we've tried at any of their local restaurants that wasn't spectacular. The first thing I noticed about Rize was that their dishes are stunning. They each look so fresh and vibrant. 

I went before the pandemic, but they're currently offering takeout, outdoor seating and sit-down dining. The staff are wearing masks, requiring masks for customers and implementing social distancing. 

I ordered the massive cinnamon roll and it was divine. We then shared the farmhouse waffle (with maple whip, brown butter crumble and bacon crumbles YUM) and the avocado toast (with pickled onions and pistachios).

Go enjoy!

This place is simply spectacular. Not only is the owner Jack one of the nicest, most impressive guys you'll meet, but their entire story is fantastic. After watching his grandmother make homemade teas and boba growing up, Jack learned that many tea places use artificial ingredients to save money, and wanted the community to try fresh, natural teas. He put a glass window in the shop where you can watch them make fresh boba and also has a traditional Taiwanese tea ceremony set on display as homage.  

What you need to know: you can get WAY more than just boba tea here. You can get all kinds of teas, espressos, smoothies and these homemade biscuit-cookies. You also choose if you want your drink hot or iced, how sweet you want it, and what kind of milk you want (they have oat milk for those dairy-free people!). 

I got the House Milk Tea with oat milk and an earl grey biscuit. They tasted super fresh and complemented each other well. The biscuits are only $0.99 and there's an entire array of types. My milk tea came out to only about $4, even with the oat milk, which is usually expensive. 

The person at the counter was incredibly friendly and helpful, and the atmosphere was wonderful. There's so many outlets and different nooks and crannies for you to sit in, depending on what you need to do. There are sofas, benches, bar tables, and desk-like areas. There's even a fun staircase up to an open, second level of tables. 

Other big bonus? The cups are such a cool design and are recyclable. Yes!

FINALLY came here! I've heard from several people that this is their favorite restaurant in Indy and it finally took being quarantined for me to venture out and score some delicious take out. My first three interactions rocked: 1) whoever runs their Instagram is super nice, 2) whoever answered the phone was super cheery and 3) the man who handed me my food was super thankful for the business and smiley as well. Is this the same person I interacted with all three times? I don't know but they seem GREAT. Okay, now onto the food. 

Brugge is a Belgian restaurant that specializes in mussels, pomme frites, steak, sandwiches, salads, soups and the sauces... oh the SAUCES. You can choose to have mussels in tons of different sauces that all sound amazing - everything from jalapeno jerk to ginger peanut. That's what i'll be coming back for. This time around, we ordered take out and both got the steak frites. You get the option of two dipping sauces for the frites, and I chose roasted garlic aioli and sauce andalouse. Both were incredible and it was so fun to add your own flavor to the meal. 

If you're reading this during ~quarantine~ time, they are doing both curbside carryout and delivery. They are also doing 'family meals' where you can get a pound of raw mussels, container of broth (your choice), charcuterie and frites. How amazing is that?! It's a good price as well -- see more info on their Instagram and... support local!

This spot is located in the touristy craziness that is Broadway Street. It's next to all of the honky tonk bars and is a great place to load up on food before hitting the town. I got the brisket, mac & cheese, and cornbread. It was all super delicious. The environment is very hole-in-the-wall-esque, but there's always customers going in and out.

Big props to the manager here for personally delivering a second cocktail to my friend who didn't get what she originally ordered. He brought it out, profusely apologized, was incredibly kind and professional, and gave it to her on the house. It was a sparkling water margarita, which she said was fantastic. 

We were excited to sit outside here on a nice night and kicked it off with queso (of course). I loved the consistency and taste of the queso - oh, and the fact that they have SEVERAL different queso options. We opted for the original queso - non-spicy and delicious. 

I also ordered two tacos - one that I created and one that already had a pre-designated recipe. Both had different meats, but were both a bit too spicy for me. I'd love to know if there's a way to discern which meats have a kick to them. Besides that, we enjoyed our food and the reasonable prices! 

PS: Love the paintings on the walls!

Finally stopped in after seeing hundreds of delicious photos of their 'za on social media and Yelp. I'd also briefly met the owners before at Indy Pies & Pints and they were so friendly and enthusiastic. I love supporting people like that! Here's why The Missing Brick rocks: 

- They support other local bizs: Hank's Smoked Brisket and Chef Oya in particular by putting their items on their pizzas. Yum!

- They have a sliding window where you can order and pick up your food, making it easy and safe to stop by during COVID19.

- They have a big side patio with picnic tables and fun music (and usually fun outdoor games when social distancing isn't happening).

-  Their staff were super friendly, as was everyone who was hanging out outside.

- The Trap pizza is one-of-a-kind: crab, big chunks of shrimp and Chef Oya's Trap Buttah make it a truly great spread.

I've heard that the dough bites are delicious as well, so will try those next time. My husband got the OG Pizza and couldn't finish it because of how salty it was, so I personally would recommend going for The Trap 
 pizza! The pizzas are craft pizzas and are therefore on the pricier side, so know that, as well as the fact that it's a 21 and up pizza spot. Enjoy  and snag a cocktail for me!

I loooove BBQ, okay?!

This place is usually crowded and I've heard amazing things from my St. Louis friends (where Sugarfire originates).

I ordered a brisket sandwich, coleslaw, and cheesy broccoli. My husband ordered pulled pork and a side of mac & cheese. 

Everything was slapped onto our tray with not a lot of care or much presentation. I don't need anything to be fancy, but it wasn't as appetizing as I would've hoped. There was a ton of fat clinging to my brisket and the coleslaw was basically a bowl of watery mayo. By the time I cut the chunk of fat off and ate the parts of coleslaw that weren't drenched, it was not a lot of food for it being almost a $40 bill between the two of us. 

The man walking around the store was super kind and friendly, but I would've just liked for the food to be a bit better quality for that price.

Hey Delicia, I'd like my future house to look like you. The interior is absolutely gorgeous. White painted brick, Aztec pillows, and a glowing bar create a beautiful atmosphere. I always take my friends from out of town here because hey, it's impressive.

Breakfast is incredible. The chorizo biscuits and gravy are creamy and delicious, with the right amount of spice. The several omelette options are also fresh and fulfilling. I have yet to go for dinner but I know they have a different dinner menu and great cocktails, especially the "Fire and Ice." Service is impeccable and very professional (not to mention randomly so attractive- not complaining!).

Surprisingly fast service for a lunch hour in an area full of offices. Our server was incredibly speedy and honestly didn't take us much more time than it would've standing in line at a grab-and-go spot. 

Their food is great quality and there's a lot of options. I had a decked out salad here (I forget which one, but it was in the cobb family) and it was delicious, large and filling. My husband loves the buffalo burgers here and insists that they're even better than a normal burger. 

Our server was no-nonsense and barely looked at us, but that maybe comes with the territory of knowing that everyone eating there is hurrying to get back to their jobs (as much as we'd love to overstay our lunch hour!). :)

On this particular #ThankYouThursday I am singing the praises of Ruth's Cafe! I've been in before (pre-covid) and they're always PACKED! This local spot is tucked into a strip center across the street from Keystone at the Crossing Shopping Mall and the interior is super fun, quirky and cozy.

This morning, I was out of breakfast foods and had a lot of meetings lined up for the day. I didn't want to start my day off with no breakfast, so was pleased to see that Ruth's was one of the few breakfast spots nearby where I could order a breakfast sandwich for delivery. I went for an egg, white cheddar and turkey bacon sandwich on a biscuit, with a side of fruit. It was a $10 sandwich, $16 total with delivery (next time I'll choose pick-up to save that moolah!). 

The sandwich was excellent, specifically the biscuit. Looking forward to the day that I'll come back to eat in person!

I ordered the miso ramen for delivery and ohhhhhh was that a good choice. It was still piping hot when it got to me and it was packaged in a really smart way. The broth is packaged separately than the toppings, so all you need to do is pour the broth on top. I loved the subtle miso flavor, as well as all of the toppings. You can order takeout or delivery on their Yelp page or their website. I also love that you can order from their connected sister business, Tsaocaa, as part of your noodle order as well. Tsaocaa has hot teas, boba teas, cold teas, desserts and more. I'll be ordering again soon!

This spot was even cooler and swankier than I imagined! Upon arrival, you'll notice the wall of glowing red lanterns, which sets a beautiful, relaxing vibe throughout the restaurant. At the moment, they have limited capacity, require masks for the staff and require masks for diners walking through the restaurant (but not at the table). Because it was limited capacity, they had a 30 minute wait on the Saturday night, but there were tables open outside, so we decided to do that instead. 

Our server was super fast, efficient and attentive. We always had water, our drinks came out quickly, and she brought the dishes out one at a time so we could enjoy them properly. 

I got the Samurai Saketini cocktail which had sake, vodka, lime juice and a cucumber floating on top. It was super smooth! We also shared the brussel sprouts which were DELICIOUS. I also got the Philadelphia roll which had raw salmon, cucumber, and cream cheese. Also great! 

Their menu has SO many sushi and nigiri options - more than I've ever seen on a menu. It was fun to pick!

We attended a holiday dinner here and had a wonderful evening. The family hosting the dinner booked the upstairs private room and it was beautiful. There was a huge table and a private bar for us alone. The service was also amazing. Our server had the perfect balance of continually filling drinks and timing the meal right, while also leaving us alone to catch up. A team of people brought all of our apps and meals out at the same time like a parade, which was also impressive.

I got the Fumo & Flora cocktail which had gin and elderflower. The bartender lit a piece of rosemary on fire, which made the drink nice and smoky. We also had some great red wine that was continually topped off for everyone. The host ordered the broiled goat cheese, tempura cauliflower, Charlie's pounders (meatballs), buttery bread, and Caesar salad appetizers. They were all amazing... specifically the meatballs, bread, and salad. Don't miss those!

I had the filet with truffle butter and it was well-seasoned and melted in my mouth. Sooo good. My husband got a ribeye and agreed that the filet was his favorite. Our host ordered the twice broiled yukons, shoestring frites, calle corn, and creamy mac sides for the table as well. You better believe that I tried everything! The mac and corn were my personal favorites. The twice broiled yukons were the only side that I'd change, as I would've preferred creamy mashed potatoes and not the thick potato. 

We were so excited to have had this experience and hope to return in the future!

Best first impression I've ever had of a business! 

We walked in at 9am on a Friday and there was a line out the door (always a good sign in regards to the food!). The owner was stationed at the door, enthusiastically greeting every guest individually when they arrived. How impressive is that!? 

The other owner was passing out menus down the line of people so that the line would go quickly. It was so clear how much they cared about their business and the whole room had a great energy. 

The main space is quite busy and noisy, but they also have a great, quiet side room to work in!! What?! It's perfect for someone who always works in local coffee shops. The owner himself showed us this room and as I was working, I heard him tell another customer that businesses can bring groups in and takeover the room for a meeting while one person orders for all of them (so they don't all have to wait in line). They really cater for everyone and werre just so nice and friendly. 

The bagel sandwiches are delish. You can choose breakfast or lunch and choose one of their combos or your own. I got scrambled eggs and cheese on an everything bagel and it was delish. It's the perfect type of meal that I want to accompany my morning tea to power me for the day. 

I'll def be back!

Bru Burger still has the best burgers in town, hands-down. (You already know that though). However, they also have the best salads. The Gorgonberry Pecan salad is UNREAL. It has spinach, cranberries, candied pecans, bacon, and an incredible cranberry-poppyseed dressing. The dressing is light but also flavorful and one of the only times I've ever craved a salad. Also - Mark is the sweetest, best server ever and we love visiting him here! Such a friendly, kind person.

This place is top-notch. Located on the Monon in downtown Carmel, this restaurant has amazing outdoor seating options. There is a big patio with covered tables, an inside/outside bar, outdoor fire tables, and billowy curtains. Because it was an insanely hot day, we opted to sit inside, but we'll be back for that patio magic. Inside, they have a dimly-lit bar, cool light fixtures, a sit-down sushi bar, beautiful chairs and tables, and great light streaming in. 

I ordered the soy ginger glazed salmon and it was sooooo good. The salmon is crusted in sesame seeds and comes with "forbidden black rice, broccolini,
wild mushrooms, and scallion curls." The plating was stunning and it was a big portion that I ended up taking home too (it was just as good later). I really liked the menu and am excited to come back for the seabass, miso soup, sushi, and crab cakes. Everything on the menu sounded AMAZING to me.

Our server was incredibly friendly and on top of things and we left incredibly impressed. We'll be back for another date night soon!

The first nice day of weather of 2021 and we were looking for a patio to relax on. We were driving through downtown Carmel and saw an amazing patio that was in the sun, with tables surrounding a big fire pit. Bingo!

We went inside to ask for a table. They had one table left outside, so we hopped on it. Our server was over quickly and because we were starving, we ordered immediately. I got the grilled citrus shrimp tacos and my husband got the hot honey buttermilk chicken strips. 

My tacos were sooooooo good. The shrimp was great, as was the flour tortilla and creamy sauce on top. The tortilla chips that came with it were okay, but my husband's fries were AMAZING, so I kept reaching for those instead. I also tried his hot honey chicken and it was perfect - crispy, chicken falling apart in the middle, and a slightly sweet zing from the honey (wasn't very spicy which we liked). 

We were so pleasantly surprised by this spot and will definitely be coming back. Everyone on the patio seemed to have a pitcher of sangria, so that'd be a fun thing to order next time we return!

Now THIS is a wonderful spot. Located on the base level of one of Indy's most gorgeous hotels, Le Méridien, it's a sparkling gem in Indy's downtown. On the left half of the main floor, there's an amazing lobby that's open to the public. There's a huge fireplace, amazing art, and rows of mini barrels of custom cocktails. On the right side of the main floor is Spoke & Steele, complete with a cozy dining room, unique (and stocked!) bar, and attentive service. 

While I initially thought that this was more of a "treat yourself" spot because of how luxurious it feels, I learned that they LOVE to have folks stop in for a cup of coffee at breakfast, quick sandwich or snack mid-day or a full-on dinner. This would be a great spot to even bring your laptop for some good bites and a quiet environment during the day.  

They also have incredibly SPECIAL private rooms that you can rent. There's a super awesome room for about 10 people that has super cool art, dim lighting and crazy fun lights. You can also rent out the bar area, the entire restaurant, the lobby, or have a group  of about  six people do their special barrel experience in the secret bar they have underground. It's soooo cool.

Food wise, I've had the The Spoke Burger, house salad and yogurt parfait. They've all been absolutely delicious and are very appealing to the eye as well. If you haven't stopped in -- you should! This is an Indy bucket list spot!

Round two and our server was amazing this time. The hermanaki wings are as good as ever. They've expanded, and it's the ideal place to watch a game with friends. We loved the upside down Christmas trees hanging from the ceiling - so fun! The deep dish pizza wasn't our favorite, but it doesn't matter when the wings are that good!

I wanted to write this review because the pizza here was really good and I want them, as well as downtown Indy, to succeed. With just a few changes, I think it could be a really awesome, hopping place. A few things: 

- Pizza case: When I walked in and saw the pizzas all just sitting out, uncovered, it made me hesitant. How long had they been sitting there? They definitely either need to get a glass case to cover the pizzas, or have them lined up in the back so the customer doesn't have to wonder. The staff were unmasked, which is fine, but watching them hover and breathe over the pizzas was not appetizing. 

- Staff: I know there's a massive staffing shortage right now, so I have a lot of compassion towards this issue. However, the person working the counter made me feel incredibly uncomfortable, as in the five minutes I was in there, he started talking at me about sex education in schools (um, what?!). That felt inappropriate, especially towards a woman who is in the shop alone.

- General: I didn't feel cleanliness vibes that I'd like to feel when ordering food and think the place could use a bit of a refresh and scrubdown. 

Again, the pizza slice was really good when it was warmed up and handed to me. I like how the crust got crispy and the cheese was all melty. However, I chose cheese because I didn't feel great about the slices with meat that had been sitting out, as well as the entire ordering experience. 

I truly hope to be able to update this review to more stars in the future!

Every single thing you order will be special and delicious. Promise. 

Food (their menu changes constantly): 

-pickled fruits & veggies board (colorful, delicious and my fav were the pickled apples- that's new to me!) 

-Amelia's Bread: comes before your meal with an assortment of creative spreads (anchovy butter, garlic oil, popcorn butter); also probably the best bread I've had in town 

-Brussel Sprouts: doused in a vinaigrette  type of sauce with pickled red onions 

-Sandwiches: amazing lunch assortment, French Dip is a must (range from $10-$14 for lunch) 

The service was great, quick, and friendly. The space is rustic and antique. The bar top is an old bowling alley, the lights above the bar are from a concert venue, and the tables are all made out of old Indy trees. There's also vintage typewriters everywhere that they have collected. 

I can't wait to come back in the summer to hang out on the outdoor patio!

We loved the live music here! The drinks were super affordable, we ordered some delicious apps, and we loved being able to sprawl out in a booth and just enjoy the music without it being too crowded. It's a solid spot just off the main Nashville strip, which makes it a little less touristy than the other bars nearby.

Feeling uber-Thanksgiving-thankful for this delicious restaurant that completely nailed their delivery this week. We ordered delivery on their Yelp page and not only received it early, but it was still piping hot and oh-so-good. 

I got the chopped romaine salad, 4 meatballs (3 original and 1 Turkey), and my husband got the meatball sandwich. First of all, the meatballs are huge and super filling (definitely a whole meal). They also came with two pieces of warm, rustic bread that was delicious as well. It's so fun ordering the meatballs because you can choose the type of meat you want, as well as they sauce (and they have about five options!). I personally love the marinara, traditional meatballs the best but you can't go wrong. 

The salad was also super good and I really loved the dressing. Overall, I was blown away and we'll definitely be ordering back from here again soon!

This place is still soooooo good. I always crave the Matt salad and really enjoyed my pork tenderloin when we went for my husband's birthday. The pretzel bites are probably my favorite app I've ever had and the flatbreads always hit the spot. You can't go wrong! The fish n' chips are also incredible and fresh.

Since I last reviewed, I've eaten Pad Thai around Indy like it's no one's business. I've even attempted to make it myself. 

But at the end of the day, I'm always craving pad thai from Pad Thai Restaurant. The pleasant ambiance, quick service and dish's proportion of sauce-to-noodle consistency is just *magic.* 

I had no choice but to bump this review up to the highest notch!

Happy #YelpsBigNightIn folks! We've been here MANY of times, but most recently stopped by for curbside pick up (during quarantine) of their newest orange vanilla cream ales. You heard that right! They made a new twist on a classic favorite and it's absolutely delicious. 

On a typical night (not in quarantine), you can come to Sun King Spirits and know you'll have the best of nights. From their outdoor lawn with fun seating, bench swings, ping pong tables and more to the their rooftop patio and fun indoor bars, there's something for everyone. Literally everyone too - all ages are allowed inside! 

Inside, there's four food vendors: Pi Indy (pizza), La Margarita (Mexican food), The Den by FoxGardin and there was Oca, but it's recently been replaced by a different biz that now sells a variety of sandwiches and a brisket mac n cheese. You can go up to any of these food stands to order and you'll be given a buzzer to come back when your food is ready. In the meantime, you grab a table and a bartender will come by and ask what you want to drink (only drinks are table service). 

Now onto their drink menu: if you're from Indiana, you already know they brew some of the best beers in the state (and in my opinion, the nation), with their cream ale and mexicali being my favorites. They also started distilling liquor at this location, so you can also choose from a wide range of cocktails and interesting mocktails (one of the few places with so many cool mocktail options).

If you still haven't caught on to the idea that this place is a lot of fun, note that they also have tons of games inside for you to bring to your table and are also located on the Monon, making it a fun place to bike or walk over to. This is def one of my favorite Carmel spots!

A trendy, downstairs speakeasy. 

Walk in the street level entrance, and take the stairs down to the bar. The dimly-lit basement is the perfect date spot or intimate friend hang out. 

There's only about 10 wooden booths that you can sit at and the rest is standing space. Sometimes they have pop up menus (last time I was here they had a pop up Mexican food menu and had fun, fiesta, twinkle lights scattered throughout the bar for a celebratory vibe. 

The craft cocktails are special snowflakes: unique, well-made and gorgeous. I had an amazing gin/pineapple cocktail that I'd definitely come back for.

This cute ice cream shop is a Broad Ripple staple. During COVID19, they've been entirely using their outdoor ordering window and have distanced spots on the ground for everyone waiting in line. Props for pivoting so quickly! 

The staff here is always great and on (non COVID) days, they'll let you sample a flavor before deciding. My favorites are the chocolate peanut butter, grasshopper (mint ice cream with fudge), and the monon tracks (vanilla ice cream with fudge and mini peanut butter cups). They also offer several vegan flavors too - awesome!

Inside, they have little conversation cards on the table to make it a  fun environment. I also noticed that they have a cute little BRICS ice cream truck in the parking lot, so I'm sure you can hire them for a wedding or event.

Welcome to the neighborhood, Leviathan! One peek at your bakery promo video and I was sold for life. Everything is amazing -- from the friendliness of the staff when you walk in to the tastiness of the baked goods and beauty of each item they make. 

We walked over and first saw people enjoying the cafe tables out front (a great quarantine seating option) and were greeted as soon as we walked in. I had a hard time deciding what to get because I was so mesmerized by each delicious baked good, dessert and cake in the glass case. I went with the Saag paneer croissant and it was incredible -- beautifully folder and stuffed with spinach and goat cheese. 

They also sell an array of beverages including coffee and iced tea. When asked if they serve hot tea, they said "we don't, but it's been requested, so we'll try to have some soon!" If that's not a sign of a great business owner, I don't know what is!

I'm so excited to return and try more!

OH MY GOSH. Just tried my first turkey burger ever and was FLOORED by how good it was. I wouldn't have changed a single thing. It was served on an English muffin and had tomato jam and an incredible, creamy cheese. I ordered this initiatively to be healthy (not expecting to love it) and now I'm going to start coming back for this dish alone. So exciting! Thanks Twenty Tap!

Tlaolli was just named the "best taco in Indiana" based on Yelp data and reviews. Why, you ask? Owner Carlos is one of the nicest and most caring people in town. Their tacos, tamales, and soups are out of this world. They have a TON of vegetarian and vegan options. They're located in a cute, purple taco house with a colorful interior and patio. Are you sold yet?!

I bought the NoNoNo taco, one of their most beloved items. The name stands for: no meat, no dairy, no gluten, and the taco comes with roasted poblanos and soy chorizo on puréed black beans. Listen up -- I'm not even vegan and this is a go-to for me. I literally eat meat, dairy and gluten and love this. Their chicken chipotle tacos are rockin' too.

Don't forget to try their hibiscus hot tea, made from fresh hibiscus flowers. You can order it hot or iced, and it has a unique tartness to it that I really appreciate (I'm not a big sweet drink person). 

During COVID, the inside of the restaurant is closed to the public. Instead, you can place an order either on their website or by calling in. They'll then ask you to park outside when you arrive and they'll bring your food to your car. They label the food so you know what you're eating, and make it incredibly seamless.

I truly cannot get over the magic that is Harry & Izzy's filet sliders. For $6/slider you can get a massive chunk of quality, well-cooked filet on an adorable crispy bun, partnered with a mouthwatering creamy- horseradish dipping sauce. Seriously, it's so good. 

This restaurant also happens to be the home of one of my favorite salads: Romaine Hearts. With sugared walnuts, apple slices and an incredibly light dressing, it's perfect. 

Our server at this airport location was also incredibly sweet, kept our drinks topped, and brought our check over instantly (an important quality when you're trying to catch a flight). 

PS: You can also get a table up next to the glass wall that overlooks the planes which makes the experience fun.

When we heard there was an area of St. Louis with a ton of Italian restaurants, we were sold. We couldn't NOT go, right?! We waited just a little to be seated and then were brought outside to the glowy patio. They had a beautiful guitarist playing and it set a romantic mood. We ordered two bolognese dishes and they were both delicious. Parking took awhile to find and we'd recommend getting reservations next time, but we'd definitely recommend to anyone else and would love to return!

You know those spots that make you feel like you're on vacation even when you're not? This is one of those.

The restaurant offers indoor, screened-in pitch, and outdoor eating. The outdoor eating is on a deck overlooking the farm and is absolutely stunning. Some of the tables have outdoor sofas for customers to sit on, as well as decorative umbrellas and an herb wall. There are tiki torches at night as well. 

The food is fresh and beautiful. I ordered the summer salmon salad and loved the proportion. There was a lot of salmon and not as much lettuce as a usual salad, but they balanced each other out well. I also tried the cheeseburger and its one of the better ones I've had. 

Trader's Point Creamery has outdoor events every Friday during the summer. These have live music, picnic tables full of food, and outdoor games. 

I didn't have time to hit up the indoor Dairy Barn (milkshakes, ice cream, smoothies, milk), but I've heard it's awesome and will stop by next time!

Baby's is bumpin'! With a mini outdoor playground for kids in the front, a neon pink sign in the window, and a big patio with heat lamps, you'll be sure to notice it if you're driving by.

This restaurant was highly-anticipated for two big reasons: the owners were the same ones who opened the swanky Ball & Biscuit bar on Mass Ave. It's also in an area of town that's starting to become developed and get more attention for incredible, local businesses. Love it!

I was immediately impressed by how friendly both our hostess and server were. They knew their stuff, had smiles on their faces and were incredibly helpful. Bonus points! The interior was gorgeous too. With sparkly pink seats, neon signs and an old-fashioned-diner atmosphere, we felt good just being there. 

I ordered a single smashburger with lettuce, onion and tomato, and a side of fries. I also got the white BBQ sauce for the fries and that was the star of the show!! The burger was pretty good (next time I want to try the double smashburger for more meat) and while thicker fries are more my jam, they were great to dip into our yummy chocolate milkshake. The boozy milkshakes sound great too and you can get the key lime shake if you want to opt for no dairy.

This place is cute and cozy! The owner was making his rounds to all of the tables and seemed to be familiar with many of the patrons. Located on Main Street in downtown Carmel, this is one of the few spots that has remained here for many years, and before a lot of the development. 

They serve authentic Italian food, and I appreciated that the menu noted that they make their sauces from scratch, so be prepared to wait a little for your food. This note made it feel as if we were in someone's home and I appreciated the heads up that this is not a place to be if you're in a hurry or with a time restraint. I'd had pasta the night before, so I went with a simple shrimp cocktail and house salad. Both were really good and I enjoyed the salad dressing. My husband got the pasta and it looked great. I believe that they had a few specials, and know that they had several pasta dishes. The dishes are on the pricier side, so I'd say that this is a nicer spot. We got free bread on the table that was good as well and enjoyed the night. 

I took one star off because I stopped in here a few years ago, asking to speak to the owner because I was sharing about a local Carmel event that was happening on Main Street. The woman (co-owner? employee?) screamed at us that she didn't have time for us and it was very shocking, as we were just two college kids who were coming in to give them an update about the city they're in. Knowing this, I felt strange seeing her while we were dining in the peaceful environment, knowing that happened. Hope she's doing better!

The Diner Burger is amazing. I had to upgrade my review from years ago to spread the word on its double-patty juiciness. Bonus: the man working the host stand was down for a laugh and I loved his upbeat attitude.

Steak 'n Shake is Steak 'n Shake. You usually know what you're going to get, and the food is usually pretty decent. This location seems to always have a long wait and slow service (or maybe it's me only stopping in when a huge event is happening in town). Regardless, it's still solid for a burger and fries, but you're going to have to wait.

Such a bustling spot! We were excited to check out this Zionsville staple and were enthralled with all the baked goods we walked by on our way to our table. Our server was quick and efficient, and when she handed us our menus, the first thing I noticed was that they serve breakfast alllllllll day. Yay! 

From omelettes to buddha bowls and bulky sandwiches to unique salads, it took me a while to decide on one option. They offer a soup of the day and today was the chile and cornbread. I went for the Cobb salad and really liked the dressing. All of the salad toppings (egg, tomatoes, bacon, bleu cheese) were all fresh and delicious individually and combined. Excited to come back here for brunch!

Rosie's does basics in a great, quality way and I appreciate it. They have lots of tables, so even when they're busy, you might not have to wait that long. Come check them out!

Their menu is super unique and it's the type of place where you can just point to something on the menu and know that it's going to be made in a delicious way. The chefs are top-notch, quirky, and inventive with their dishes. I'm also in love with their colorful and bold graphics and interior. They're located on Mass Ave, a cool street in Downtown Indy full of local shops, restaurants, and bars (for the out-of-towners reading this!). 

This is the spot where you're going to find a hearty meal. Think: biscuits & gravy, smoked brisket sandwiches, pork belly entrees, waffles, country breakfasts and more. The menu has always seemed very heavy to me, so go when you are H-U-N-G-R-Y. I also just read on their Facebook page that "if no vegetarian option is listed on the menu please ask - we are always happy to put something together." Awesome to know!

They also just created a burrito spin-off business within the restaurant and they look absolutely amazing. Going back to try those shortly! I've heard they're amazing!

Quarantined at home? As of 3/25/20, they're only doing carry out at this Carmel location and have an updated menu on their website! They have a few salads, pizza, pasta and entree options for you to choose from and their food is delicious as usual! My favorite is the Margherita pizza or... let's be honest, ANY of the pastas. We placed an order and picked it up easily.

I actually think that this might be my new favorite restaurant. It was absolutely fantastic. First, the design is beautiful, with greenery and wicker lanterns hanging down from the ceiling, a tiled bar in the center of the restaurant to set a fun vibe, dim lighting, and dance music. The energy was high.

The menu was fantastic as well, with photos that made each dish look absolutely amazing. I also loved how the menu has unique items (and a slight Spanish flair) with octopus, paella, ceviches and more. Right off the bat, you get free chips and salsa, but I definitely recommend getting the queso or guac too. We started with the queso and it was probably my favorite queso that I've had. SO GOOD.

I then went for the shrimp fajitas, which is enough food for two people or amazing leftovers the next day. I loved the shrimp, as well as the guac and sides that came with it all. Mmm. 

Be aware that people/tables didn't really feel socially distant at all, so maybe get takeout or come when it's warm out and you can sit on their great patio.

It's 3am and you need a snickerdoodle cookie?! It'll be in your arms (where it belongs) in about 20 minutes. 

I was a frequent orderer in college and it usually rotated between the sugar cookie or snickerdoodle. Feeling extra? You can order a cookie ice cream sandwich: choose both cookies and the flavors of ice cream in the middle. It'll arrive to you cold. 

There's also a storefront where you can go in and order if you're not doing delivery. There's about 15 types (maybe more?!) of cookies and about six ice cream flavors. 

Insomnia Cookie hack: get a scoop of vanilla ice cream and they can put a scoop of cookie dough on top.

I was craving tasty Korean food and because it's COVID times, I've been really looking at restaurants' health scores on their Yelp pages before purchasing. When I read about the cleanliness of this spot in other reviews, I felt like it'd be a great, safe choice. The photos of the interior also look super clean, orderly and beautiful, and major bonus points for having their health/safety updates posted on their Yelp page! The staff are wearing masks, limiting capacity, offering contactless payments, providing hand sanitizer, sanitizing between customers, and enforcing social distancing. I can't wait to dine in person, hopefully soon!

I ordered the beef bulgogi entree and a side of brown rice. The flavor of the beef was amazing. It was well-seasoned and had green onions mixed in. It came with white rice, so I ended up eating it atop both the brown and white rice. It was enough for two meals, and was just as delicious the next day. 

I'm looking forward to going back in person for the Korean beef lettuce wraps, pan seared Korean dumplings, and the Korean stir fry soft noodles.

This was such a fun experience! From seeing the massive Clydesdale horses in real life to sampling beer, and seeing behind the scenes, the tour was well done. The grounds, stables, and factory areas were all aesthetically pleasing and the facts that were shared during the tour were interesting too. This is a St. Lou must-do!

A whole new culture of food has opened up for me. 

Who knew I'd love EVERYTHING on an authentic Korean menu?? My Korean friend brought me here and introduced me to lots of different menu items. I already knew I loved edamame, but I had never tried kimchi or any Korean entrees. 

I got Dol Sot Bi Bim Bop (veggies, beef, white rice and an egg on top) which came in a hot stone pot and tasted awesome with hot sauce. I LOVED IT. 

The best part? We got way more than simply our entrees. Every meal begins with a small salad (with amazing ginger? dressing), several sides (including kimchi, pickles with hot sauce and one more) and concludes with a small bowl of fruit. We even got handed free seafood pancakes with our meal. They were AMAZING (could barely taste the seafood). The price we paid was definitely worth all the food we received. 

The servers were insanely polite, efficient and ready to fill up our glasses at any time. There were so many other things that looked amazing on the menu that I will definitely be back. Thanks Cafe Korea!

There are certain places that you decide you'll support for life. This is one of them. Why, you ask?! The owners are some of the kindest, smartest, hard-working people I've ever met. When Cinco de Mayo sold them out of ingredients last year, they ended up calling every single customer with a deal to come back. That's just one story to show how much they care and how much effort and passion they put into this restaurant. Owner Seni started this business back in 2014 as a single mom and has grown it to two (almost three - stay tuned!) locations in Indy. She's a boss for sure! Her husband now helps with it as well and will rave to anyone about her stellar entrepreneurship. It's adorable and I love it.

Okay, now onto the food. I ordered the elote kit for a Yelp elote-making  virtual class that we had with the owners. Because I was starving when I  ordered, I also added two asada tacos as well and I'm so happy I did. They came with a few different spice levels of salsa and were delivered right on time. Now that I've made my own elotes, I can't wait to try their (I'm sure better) already-made elotes, as well as their breakfast burrito, (which I've heard rave reviews about), churros and lengua tacos as well.

Paco's also offers a few various sizes of "family taco boxes" (they look AWESOME...fiesta in a box and dinner for the entire family) as well as catering for any type of event (office meeting, wedding, etc.). Go for it!

COVID19 note: You can currently (as of 8/27/2020) go in to order, order takeout or delivery on their Yelp page (GrubHub) or head to their website. They also built a great front patio where you can eat outside.

I was blown away by how impressive the owner and our server was. We had just seen an article about how onions from Chihuahua were recalled nationally, and since we had a pregnant woman in our group, I felt that I had to ask. Our server shared that their whole team had gotten fresh onions the night before and remade EVERYTHING in their kitchen late the night before. It was impressive that they already knew, cared, acted on it, and were equally interested in customer safety. All was good, and we ordered drinks. The owner then came over and also explained that they had acted instantly on that national recall because "it really shows the customers how much we care about them." It was so sweet and heartfelt, and I just instantly loved the place based on those great interactions.

We ordered a few Coronas and I've heard that their margaritas are made with fresh ingredients too (not mixers). We were then given free chips and salsa and they even gave each of us our own mini salsa bowls so we didn't have to share. So great! Our server replaced our chips instantly when we were getting low and the salsa was delicious. We ordered queso and guac and I thought that the guac tasted incredibly fresh. It tasted like pure, fresh avocado and I could've eaten a bowl of it.

I got the shrimp fajitas and really enjoyed those as well. I also liked that they took the tails off the shrimp before serving it and I thought that was another testament to their team caring about every detail. My husband got the classic enchiladas with the mild red sauce on top and enjoyed that (heads up that there's still a kick even with the mild option). 

We'll be back, as this is absolutely the type of place and people that I want to support with my money. I think their perfect Yelp reviews speak for themself too. You all are doing a wonderful job!

Upland funk gon' give it to you. This place rocked my mind in a good way. I was pleasantly surprised by almost everything here. 

The layout is awesome. The bar is angled so that when walk in the door, the bar area is the first thing you see. They used really pretty wood and the decor makes the place very unique, relaxed, and inviting. They have a cute side patio with tables under starry string lights too. 

I came here for lunch with the fam and fell in love with the salmon tacos and the mandarin ginger salad dressing (can I get a cup of it to-go?). Mmmm. I ate some of my sister's fries too (of course) and they were might tasty- not to mention Upland beer-battered.

We didn't have beer while we were here, but I think it's cool that a brewery like Upland is able to attract so many people there to simply eat. There were young couples at the bar as well as families at the tables, making it a great diverse group! 

Our sever was honestly probably the best server I've ever had, which makes all the difference for a restaurant. One of the bar tenders was super jolly as well and him and our server started dancing around the place when Christmas music came on which made for a fun atmosphere. Mostly I think I just want to be friends with them. 

Congrats on the impressive visit Upland!

When this place won Yelp's Top 50 Restaurants in Indiana last year, I added it to my list of spots to visit. Then, they made Yelp's Top 10 Restaurants in Hamilton County THIS year and I realized that I just had to visit. 

It was so good!! Wish I had gone earlier! It's a fast-Korean restaurant with incredible, hot dishes at decent prices. 

I ordered the Chap Chae Noodles which was essentially sweet potato noodles with mushrooms and beef. It was insanely delicious and piping hot. My friend ordered the Bibimap and enjoyed that immensely as well (and she knows her Korean food).

I was blown away by my experience here! I had about an hour to kill and needed to finish some work, so I popped in, thinking that it was a fast-casual spot. I arrived right when they opened and quickly saw that it was a nice sit-down spot (you can get takeout of course too!). I went ahead and took a table by myself and was quickly greeted by an incredibly kind and  attentive server.

The entire  restaurant felt so clean, thoughtful, and welcoming. Everything from their signs to their logo to  their menus are beautiful. Their team of sushi chefs were in their chef whites, chef hats, and looked incredibly polished and professional. I opened the menu and was wowed by the colorful, appetizing photos in the menu. I've truly never seen better food photography. It made me want to order literally everything. 

I went for the miso soup and Spideman Roll. It had crabmeat tempura, avocado, soft shell crab, eel sauce, spicy mayo, scallions and caviar. It was super delicious and the plating was beautiful. I was pleasantly surprised by the price too. For such a high quality spot, my meal was $15. I will absolutely be back for their ramen, udon noodles, and if I can get enough friends together, a future sushi boat. Do yourself a favor and visit this spot. It's unique and special... who else has a sweet potato sushi roll? YUM.

The cocktails here are delicious, the inside is super swanky, and the bar is located on Mass Ave, which is a fun and happenin' street in Indy. We had a big group, so we sat outside on their front patio so we could fit everyone. I got a cucumber-gimlet-type cocktail that was delicious, albeit quite sour. We had a good time within our group, but our server was incredibly rude. We were all very taken aback, as our group was being very polite, offering to help him, tipped well, were smiling, etc. He would NOT smile at us, so much so that it was like he was trying not to. He also made several incredibly slight and sarcastic comments and might have even been the manager, as he wasn't in a server outfit. It was a frustrating experience, as I know this spot is high quality and has a good reputation, but I was just sad that it tainted my friend's birthday a bit.

Holy sushi roll. 

This place is tiny, yet such a gem. You walk in and are immediately greeted. You're given menus and a paper to mark what you'd like to order and are relived because you won't have to wait long for food. They are heavily staffed for the amount of tables there are, so you'll never have to wait more than a minute for your water to be filled or more than ten minutes for your food. 

-Miso Soup: yummy, warm, only $2, delivered to the table within 2 minutes

-Red Dragon rolls: incredible, filled with tuna & avocado, mild

-Christmas rolls: heard they're a favorite, yet spicy 

There's a small, personal room off the front of the restaurant that houses a huge round booth, covered in cool shag carpet. Wow, I'd love to be cool enough to sit in there!

They have an incredible patio and a huge menu. Their food is also relatively cheap, but taste and quality are not compromised. We had the friendliest server in the world and I swear I've never seen a guy smile that much. Overall great experience and you can't go wrong by coming here!

We were really looking forward to enjoying a lovely patio bar with drinks and some good food this evening.  Your website seemed to indicate that you were open all day...  "Summer Specials Available All Day."  I admit we missed the actual opening time of 4 pm.

So when we arrived, about 10 to 4, we were told you were not open but the bartender upstairs had arrived a little early and we could go up there.  We asked about the "Summer of 3 M's" Margarita, Mojito, or Martini for $5.00 and everyone had no idea.   My wife had to look it up on your website on her phone and show it to the female we thought was taking our order.  Nope, someone else took the order for two mojitos and served us the worst cocktail I have ever tasted...

Asked for glasses of water multiple times and never received any.

The "club soda" was apparently bad but the young man explained it as he makes the mojitos very strong and we were not used to them.  They were not refreshing, had no lime, no sugar (or sweetener), and were flat and warm.

So, the flat club soda was just the beginning of the problem. 

Asked for glasses of water multiple times and never received any.

The margarita replacement was no better.  It was a poorly made drink by an amateur bartender.  Drink was warm, no garnish, forgot to salt rim (but actually got that fixed before serving it).

Asked for glasses of water multiple times and never received any.

Wife wanted a Vodka tonic replacement and asked for bottled tonic due to the previous flat club soda issue.  Bartender brought out a bottle of Pellegrino and another bottle of sparkling water and asked if they would be ok for the Vodka tonic...  We explained to him that they were not tonic.  My wife asked for a taste of the tonic from the machine and accepted it as "good enough."

Asked for glasses of water multiple times and never received any.

Went to "The Abbey" and told everyone within earshot of my wonderful date night with my Wife.
..
Overall.  A miss from the greeter, to the first person at the bar, to the bartender, to the kid that brought our food, to the gentleman sitting at the bar who seemed to be in charge, saw everything wrong that happened and did nothing.

Really wanted to try some of the food but just left.

Any feedback???  Good luck.

The Hubs and I had reservations here on Saturday at 7pm. We arrived a tad early, so we settled in at the bar and each enjoyed one of their signature cocktails. The Parisian was terrific, but the rum based drink The Hubs had was just...eh (I can't even remember the name of it). 

When our table was ready we followed the hostess to one of the very last tables in the room next to the kitchen. It was a cozy two-top situated next to another four-top, which incidentally, held 4 of the most annoying people I've ever had the displeasure of eavesdropping on. Sheesh. They thought they were better than everyone else in the world, spoke crazy-loud to each other about said greatness, and ordered the stinkiest seafood EVER...very annoying. I'll never know why people order seafood in the middle of the country. We're land-locked, people! It isn't fresh! Their meals made our area of the restaurant smell like the penguin house at the zoo. 

As we perused the menu I noticed that The Hubs didn't have a napkin and mine was soiled and folded awkwardly. And let me tell you, it's all in the details for me. If the table is a mess, what's the kitchen look like, ya know?? I don't really mind when a place uses butcher paper to cover the tables. That is, if they are changed after every diner leaves. Gross. Ours had chunks of food still stuck to it and upon further investigation, I realized we didn't have spoons in our tiny salt and pepper dishes that sat open on the table. Seriously? It really made me wonder how the people who sat here before us seasoned their food (with their hands...gasp!). All in all the table was a mess, but our night was about to get much, much better. 

We received new napkins and new salt and pepper, and then the server announced the specials. We settled on the goat cheese tart as an appetizer (special) to start. WOW. The cheese wasn't all goatie and funky like it sometimes can be, and the crust was buttery perfection. Even the small salad of greens and sweet beets was delightful paired with the creamy, salty cheese. Score one (finally) for the chef. 

I ordered the frisee salad and it was also phenomenal. The egg was cooked perfectly and the oozy center spilled out and mixed nicely with the crispy chunks of bacon and croutons. And what could make a salad with bacon even better? Bacon vinaigrette, of course! Delish. 2 points now, for the chef. 

Once we decided on our entrees, we also ordered a half carafe of their house red wine (Cabernet) and it was very good. Not great, but just what we were looking for in that price range ($7!). That's 3 points, for those of you keeping score at home. 

My cassoulet arrived in its own cast iron skillet, and was piping hot (a good sign!), as did my cauliflower gratin. The pork belly was silky and rich, the house-made sausage was perfectly garlicky, and the duck confit fell right off the bone. Amazingly prepared. The cauliflower was good, but I didn't particularly enjoy the nutmeg. Bleh. Guess that's what I get for ordering a veggie. Cassoulet = major points 

The Hubs ordered the Bistro steak and fries, and was instantly swept up in memories of his own trip to France and the wonderful steak he had in a cafe similar to Brasserie. Bravo, chef. Point for you. 

All in all the food was 4 stars, but the table setting and fellow diners (not the chef's fault) were at about a 3. Luckily, it's mostly about the eats for this foodie! I highly recommend this place, but be sure to make reservations...it was packed!

As if this place wasn't disappointing enough when I actually visited...

The owner herself had the audacity to contact me today to tell me not to come back to her establishment!  My review is a year old, yet she felt the need to send me a note telling me "it's probably best if you don't come back".  Probably not your most professional moment, Casey M.  Or your wisest business decision.

I will continue to avoid the Mud House, and now I will tell everyone I know to avoid this place as well.  

Cheers!

We stayed at El Encanto from May 21st to May 23rd.  We were in Bungalow #2201.  The resort is stunning, the landscaping is impeccable, the pond, waterfall and other fun hidden treasures such as the beautiful pigs.  A little taste of paradise for sure!

We ate at the restaurant on site for lunch and two breakfasts.  The food was fantastic and the service was VERY good, the prices are high but they are an Orient Express Hotel in Santa Barbara, so it was "expected".  Great cocktails in the bar and good pours for the money. Below is the pro's/con's of our stay at El Encanto.  Overall a great experience with some minor improvements needed in housekeeping and room service.

Pro's:

Premier Bungalow #2201 was beautiful!! Huge deck in back, front porch, super comfy bed, nice décor, large bathroom with carrara marble, hardwood throughout the rest of the bungalow and great little touches like the personalized bed pillow with the "B" on it (for our last name).  Wonderfully warm heated bathroom floors with a thermostat we could adjust to our liking, the lighting in the entire unit was nice, great flexible reading lights on the headboard.  Great linens on the bed and the most fabulous "throw" that was so soft, I took a picture of the manufacturer tag so I can order one for my home.  Great mini bar selection for snacks and beverages, although quite pricey which is to be expected.  The best rain shower head "ever" in the shower.

Con's:

The location of the bungalow was not private enough or quiet enough for our liking.  Main walking path for other room's right outside as well as the parking structure was very close so we could see & hear the valet's getting cars in & out when were on the deck.  Upon checking out, we asked Max at the front desk to show us other rooms that would be more private and he showed us two as well as gave verbal recommendations for other rooms for our next visit - thanks Max!

There was only one washcloth in our bathroom when we arrived and I called and asked for more to be delivered.  They never showed up and I had to call again in the morning, and then they delivered 4 of them.  If there are two people staying in a room, there should definitely be more than one washcloth!

The first day when they cleaned our room, they did not restock the coffee pods, replenish the sugar, or replace the coffee cup that had been used, so they left us with one coffee cup and one coffee pod.  I called housekeeping and they promptly showed up with the items. 

We ordered room service the 2nd night and Michelle in the restaurant was very helpful!  However, I ordered a bottle of wine she highly recommended and then I got a call back about 15 minutes later and she told me they did not have it, she was very apologetic and another one was recommended.  Then about an hour later, I called again to order cookies & ice cream and again Michelle was great and gave me a list of cookies/ice cream to choose from.  I placed my order, sat back down outside and a few minutes later, the phone rang and she again had to apologize to tell me they did not have the cookies we ordered and we had to make another choice.  They really should know what they have available before offering it.

Overall, it was great and I am sure we will go back again someday!

The service is somewhat quick but you're still able to sit down and enjoy the ambiance. The view of the pier, waters and cloudy skies made it such a pleasant experience for a nice Valentine's day lunch.

I ordered the soup/salad combo. The salad was a simple house salad but the portion was perfect. As for the clam chowder...it was delish! Not too creamy and not watered down. It was almost quite perfect! It doesn't beat Boston's but so far it truly is the best in the west.

I would definitely come back here and may be next time I'll try the garlic clams or their famous Bloody Mary.

The good: You can't beat the views and the food is pretty good.
The bad: The prices are high and I had a bad experience with the manager.

I ordered a seafood cocktail plate that was over $40. It came with an assortment of yummy meats. It was printed on the menu to include "two crab legs". When I received the order it had one crab led split in half. It wasn't that big of a deal. There was plenty of seafood on the plate. But after the thought of paying over $40 set in, I thought I would mention it to the waitress. She said she would look into it.

The manager came over to the table to argue that one crab leg split in two was the same as two crab legs and that's how the chef prepared it. Unbelievable. 

I don't plan on going back. They need a lesson in math, language and honesty.

***I wrote a three star review until I felt as if I was under attack by a female who may be the owner or manager.** First I must say another very pleasant and helpful manager came over and went over my experience 25 minutes before.  I told him it was fine, it could be me I was just picky, everything was OK and I would be returning because I've had their wings in the past and they were good. But this blonde chick (her behavior does not dignify being called a woman!) comes out of nowhere wearing black pants with hair and dirt all over them telling  me the menu specifically says 'thick' pancakes, they do not!! Please view the picture of the menu they say fluffy not thick. Her comprehension of words and Customer Service leaves a bit to be desired. Then she went to break down to me how the waffle recipe is an authentic Belgian recipe she broke down each component and explained how they take 6 hours to make. Excuse me?! I think at a waste of precious time! I have Belgian family members by marriage and these waffles are not familiar at all!!' 

The live music ALMOST saved my experience! My reservation was 11:15 I arrived 11:20, most places allow a 15 minute window. Although I was seated I received a text 11:28 after being seated about 6/7 minutes saying my reservation was cancelled. Huh?(in my Scobby Doo voice)... but the piano player had my attention with Elton John, Billy Joel, Carole King and The Temping Temptations!

The decor is lovely, a large bar area with high and low top seats. In the separate dining room a variety of upholstered high back chairs, other tables with standard wood backs and black vinyl cushions. Very clean and neat place!

I will say the staff is friendly, engaging and helpful! But breakfast may not be their thing. Without ripping the restaurant let's just say the pancakes were basically wide fried high biscuits and they use the same batter for pancakes and the waffles which is a breakfast NO NO!!!

The food is fairly good and my food server was excellent. My concern is I stood at the host desk for about 5 minutes waiting to be seated for my reservation. When someone showed up he immediately looked past me to seat the white couple behind me. Now everything is not about race however since I was the only brown person in the place and other workers clearly watched me the entire time standing alone I can only express how it made me feel. NOT GOOD!!

So I keep my order at a minimum because I'm here and I'm YELPING!!! The sangria was good but filled with ice, wine, blackberries and nothing else. The Peruvian mussels are divine! The fire roasted salsa is great and the tomatillo salsa pretty good but the pico de gallo lacked flavor or any familiarity. I was told the pico de gallo is a Central American twist ok but, they didn't twist any lime over it and that's for sure. The food is good enough but in the words of Maya Angelou 'They may forget what you said (feed)-- but they will never forget how you made them feel'. They didn't make me feel good at all! I won't be back.

If I don't stop watching 6 ABC FYI edition on Saturdays I will be in financial ruin. While watching TV the day before I decide to go out to dinner I happened to see information on TV about this restaurant. I'm not necessarily that big on pasta but pictures can say 1000 words. The overall look of the restaurant and how the meals were plated it was very intriguing to me. I called the restaurant about five minutes before they opened and I was able to set up a reservation for the next 15 minutes.  

When I arrived I was immediately greeted and seated. My server was prompt and friendly.  Although she pointed out the specials on the menu there were no suggestions made and no offers to answer any questions asked. But I generally do not require assistance choosing food. 

The restaurant has a nice layout, the newness allows the restaurant to have a bright appearance although it's dimly lit. But the ambiance and decor is on trend. The bar is a fairly decent size, it's needed as people immediately gravitated towards it. It could have been the friendly and animated server at the bar mixed in with the presence of one of the owners.

I ordered the Rigatoni it's served with smoked chicken and red cherry peppers (finely chopped)., it was to die for. Sadly I'm one of those Americans who believe you should have some bread or rolls before or with your meal. It was not to be,  which put a slight damper on things for me.  I understand it's a 'me thing'. But I like bread!Nevertheless the service was great as was the food so, I'll get over it! I'm sure to return soon.

I so wanted to like this place it has all the elements that one would want when dining. Tuscany café is convenient because it's local, serves a variety of food. the prices seem to be fair, the ambience is great, the service is friendly and it is has a relaxing decor vibe. But it just wasn't meant to be. After navigating the horrendous parking situation I was acknowledge and seated  immediately. My server was very nice although she did not give me her name but immediately bought a nice plate of homemade pastries that was very tasty. Of course the La Columbe coffee they severed was delicious. But it was downhill from there the pancakes they serve were like three biscuit frisbees, The bacon was thin sparse and almost translucent meaning mostly fat some cheap brand. The home fries look like a baked potato cut in chunks and thrown on a plate, The scramble eggs we're average nothing negative or positive there. Everything outside of the pancakes were cold, not room temperature, not lukewarm, cold!

In my estimation they take shortcuts and use inferior products the bacon served look like something purchased at a Save a Lot or Aldi's!

5 for ambience Starbucks meets lounge decor
1 for parking as it's the absolute worst
4 for service, my server was very friendly and they were prompt 
1 for food and it was served cold and very small portions

I can see why this restaurant receives high marks however the service impacts most of my review. We arrived on time and seated immediately. This was after a barrage reminder text, I do understand people can be 'no shows'. Our server I believe his name is David only because the table to my left addressed him. When he spoke his delivery was low and somewhat mumbling. He offered very little information about the menu until asked. Compared to the server to my right who enthusiastically went over the menu, very descriptive and can be clearly understood. He volunteered the information and was not prompted! I had to prompt my server for information his lack of delivery didn't inspire us to order additional items. Listening to the other server did. We later added cauliflower. 

Let's go over the decor. Nice wood tables with a smart use of the space. Being able to see the stove/oven was a nice touch. As for my food we ordered the cauliflower which was tender but it along with the pesto etc., it was tasteless. The Roni cup pizza was very good flavorful without being oily it was a great presentation but it and Pide Merguez was less than warm the pizza in spots was cold. This could all be based on the efficiency of my server as I watched food sit for a while before being picked up. He was less than attentive often retreating to the corner near the bathroom doing what appeared to be nothing. The Chocolate layer cake with tahini cream the cake was good but heavy and the cream lacked taste.

Will I return? Probably for the pizza and not David as a server!

I started lucky enough to get parking directly in front of Pretty Girls Cook. It's nice inside and I was immediately greeted then seated by a Pretty Girl. Beware all of the seating is pub style and I'm 5'3" sitting at the counter, I had to uncomfortably reach up. This is unlike other restaurants counter space. However the counter does have hooks for your purse or coat. Accommodations for special needs are available upon request. The Pretty Girls cooking wore head coverings and gloves when handling the food. That's a great start for my dining experience! Although it took a minute to be greeted by anyone other than the host my server was pleasant. And yes she's a Pretty Girl too. The decor is black, pink and rose gold accents.

As for the food what I had was fair didn't seem at all like 'buttermilk pancakes' but they were large a filling. The pancakes are so large they are enough to share. the beef bacon it was cooked crispy not burnt and very meaty.

In all it was a pleasant experience just not inspiring enough to drive 30 minutes to get to. If I'm in the area I will stop in for dinner. For now this Pretty Girl is moving on.

Met a friend here for a breakfast, the location initially made me nervous thinking about the parking situation on South Street. Well this Sunday I was in luck I found and parked approximately 20 feet from the restaurant. My friend who arrived about 15 minutes later was almost as lucky, less than a block away. Let's start with the entrance, the steps are very high with no railing for those who may need 'assistance' this could be problematic.  Additionally I did not see a method a person who requires wheelchair access could enter. But they absolutely need a railing at the minimum.  Once inside the place was nice and neat with plenty of tables and chairs, they can accommodate small or larger parties (about 10 in group). I prefer table service but it wasn't an option. While at the counter I went over the menu and stated to the staff 'hum so many choices', no response just a smile. So I went with my gut. 

My pumpkin spice waffle was delivered to my table very timely. With that being said it was room temperature and soft although I asked for a firm waffle. I really dislike spongy waffles especially if they're not hot. Once you add syrup the waffle becomes soggy or mushy, ugh....However the roasted sweet potatoes were good, the candied pecans delicious but I must say the whipped cream was fresh and flavorful just outstanding!
