The coffee was okay nothing to write home about and nothing to make me return. The restaurant only had three other guest and several delivery or pick up orders. No reason not to serve hot food!

The hosts had a look like 'how can I help you?' without saying it out loud so I said, 'it's just me'. With that I was immediately seated and given a comfortable few minutes to review things. My server approached and offered drink special information. I went for a local beer, 'I like beer'!  Churchville lager I like a lot. After a few questions about sandwiches I went for my go to pizza. The Americana (?) is just basically pepperoni pizza. It came out in less than 7 minutes but it was perfection. The crust was the right thickness not doughy or or too much sauce. The only thing that was off was it was hot just not piping like fresh out of the oven. But I have no complaints about the food or my server.

The decor is wood paneling walls and exposed beams, a nice above ground basement vibe. The pizza was good the restaurant clean and organized but slightly expensive for a personal size pizza. If they have Happy Hour deals during the week I would consider returning if not, it's not worth another trip.

I really enjoyed the familiar taste of Korean cuisine. I love there are always plenty of sides when you dine at a Korean restaurant. During our meal we shared the Kimichi Jjiage , Korean crispy wings and La Galbi all were very good. If only they had beer and wine!

The main dining area was nicely but simply decorated with an open view of the kitchen. I really liked the 'call' button for service on the table. When you are ready to order press the 'order' button and the 'check' button when its time to pay. 

I found the portions more than fair!with a great taste and the service very good. Nothing was too salty, the beef was tender, the food was served timely and hot. I would highly recommend this restaurant as I will be returning soon. They are participating in Ardmore's Restaurant Week starting July 16, 2018.

Restaurant week was a great introduction to Jake's and Cooper's Wine Bar. From the beginning I was pleasantly surprised with parking out front, pleasant service and a excellent dining experience! Entering a warm, inviting, earthy and muted yet rustic tones with a large bar area leading into a visible hearth for pizza making. The menu offers a lot of food and drink options. But it Restaurant Week lets go for that.

The homemade mandilli pasta was fabulous the pasta, asparagus and mushrooms were cooked to perfection. We both really enjoyed the filet Bronzini in a butter sauce over asparagus. All of this was quite delicious. Desert options, Lemon Curd with a caramelized topping reminiscent of crème brûlée or the other choice Carrot Cake Cheesecake both were rich in color, texture and boasting the described flavor.

The owner or manager visit our table when our meal ended and we had a delightful conversation about our wonderful experience.  We were informed of specials during the week,  I was very pleased to hear about pasta night each Thursday for $20 you have your choice of homemade pasta and a glass of wine. What a deal. See ya next Thursday!!

I've been coming here when visiting family in Tucson for over 30 years.  And, I'm sad to say, the last few visits have shown a downward spiral that just doesn't seem to be getting any better.

My wife and I were here at 7 on a Friday night which, in the better days, would have meant a good wait.  Not this time.  No one outside, and we were immediately seated in a dining room that was maybe a third full.

I ordered a full rack of pork ribs, and that's just what I got.  A full rack of pretty well tasteless ribs that had not had any seasoning, marinade, or basted sauce.  Just a bowl of something out of a jar on the side.  Now normally when I have ribs, I finish mine and start looking to see who can't finish theirs and offer my help.  Not this time; in fact, I didn't even finish mine; left three or four.

So we asked our waitress for the check.  Nothing.

A while later we asked the busboy.  We watched him tell the waitress. Nothing.  She went to the table next to ours and took drink orders, and then hung around the bar while they were being filled .  Obviously no time in her busy schedule to bring our check.

We finally got up and headed to the front, passing her face to face as she delivered drinks.  Upon arriving there, the bartender asked, "Two for dinner?"  No, we want our check.  He went in the back, told someone we needed our check.  Nothing.

Another 3-4 minutes and the hostess returned.  "Two for dinner?"  No, we 're trying to pay and leave.

Five minutes later, yet another person showed up and we were finally able to pay and leave.

And given the rather pricy, poor food and incredibly pathetic service, not likely to return

Oh Yes, oh my!

As someone who comes from Asian mecca (San Gabriel Valley & LA), I was skeptical coming to Kimchi Korean BBQ. All the past reviews below 3 stars were from management long ago. THIS Kimchi Korean BBQ, and THIS management is absolutely great and each of my experiences have been positive. To my knowledge, there is not another AYCE (all you can eat) KBBQ spot in town.

I typically go on the weekends and past a certain time the only offer options 2 & 3 which are the pricer options. The restaurant IS on the smaller side so expect to have a wait during busier times of the day. if you don't know what KBBQ is, you will typically order what you want and cook your own meat on the grill in front of you. Besides meat, there are plenty of other dishes you can order (steamed egg, kimchi fried rice, dumplings, vegetables, fish cake). 

The quality of meat is pretty good and the marinade is good. The service is IMPECCABLE and my water was always refilled. 

I definitely recommend SBnatives to come check out this place if you haven't before, it is a lot of fun sitting with friends and grilling your own food. The Korean cuisine and kimchi flavors are amazing and you will be happy with your experience here. 

They DO have an axxess deal, so take advantage!

SYOY,
Jess H.

I do not dole out single stars lightly, but in this case I would give 0 if I could. 

I first tried Belcourt Taps (& tapas? Didn't they used to have tapas?) last year and had a very meh experience. I waited for another visit to review since a first time bad experience could always be a fluke. My husband bought a groupon for 2 beer flights and an appetizer this month not knowing I wasn't a huge fan based on previous experience, but we thought, hey it's pretty hard to mess up beer. I guess we jinxed ourselves. 

The inside was pretty full when we arrived on a week night, and it looked like a band was about to go on. I'm thinking this place is best as just a music venue where you happen to have a beer rather than a destination for a meal.

We opted for the patio since it was nice outside. We told our waitress up front that we were going to redeem their groupon, which she seemed super confused about and told us they didn't have a current groupon, their old one expired. Not her fault, but the staff was clearly not educated on the offer (which didn't expire for 3 more months). If you have a groupon out there, maybe tell your staff about it. 

We asked about the beer flights (not on the menu) and she told us that it was "local stuff."  We were fine with that explanation since we knew we were getting whatever their groupon deal was and couldn't be picky. However, when the "flights" arrived, it was one big service tray with 10 mini mason jars (those were cute, I'll give them that), each about a third full and nothing was labeled or in any order. They were also not cold. We asked her what they were and she said "mostly local stuff, it's good" and then walked away. Ok..... 

We ended up finding out through taste testing trial and error that we did not, in fact, have 2 flights (I incorrectly assumed we would each get the same 5 beers since it was supposed to be 2 flights...), just 10 random different beers. We also deduced that TWO of them were some kind of HARD CIDER.  I have no problem with cider if that's what I ordered, but I don't really find it acceptable to put it in a beer flight with no warning.  

I won't even address the appetizer we got except to say that I do not recommend the nachos. 

The waitress informed us that if we didn't order anything else besides just redeeming the groupon there would be 20% gratuity charged. We had initially planned to order more, but the app was so bad that we decided not to. We were planning to tip all along, so the gratuity charge was no problem. The receipt listed the 10 beers, which included Sam Adams and Angry Orchard (aka, not local and not beer).  We asked if those were our beers since they weren't labeled and she said no, I just pushed 10 random buttons to get the bill printed so I could charge gratuity. Great. I am convinced we did get the angry orchard, though. There's no mistaking that for beer. 

The excuse for a beer flight would have been disappointing anywhere, but is especially puzzling from a place with "taps" in their name who is specifically advertising beer flight deals. 

Since this is 2 bad experiences in a row a year apart, it's not a fluke. I will not be returning.

Been going here over the past three owners and decided to check it again after reading that the previous owner had repurchased it and did a renovation.  Thought it odd when we entered and the man behind the greeting station kept his head in paperwork.  Later found out he was the owner.  This was found out when midway in our meal he came to the bar and asked the bartender to see if he had a type of sherry.  We learned the tender was only on the job one week and was involved in trying to ring out a customer's bill.  A few minutes later the manager returned with the owner and asked if he had found it.  The bartender announced he was busy but started looking in the wine area before the manager barked for him to look in the refrigerator and promptly steered him to where the sherry was.  This whole incident seemed like a test to see if a one-week old employee knew where sherry was maintained.  It also appeared like they were trying to embarrass him who, by the way provided excellent service to my wife and I.  Also, the rigatoni with self described "Sunday gravy"  was anything but.  The chef needs to spend a few days in South Philly to learn about gravy.  Anyway, although the atmosphere was good and service excellent, an owner who treats customers and staff like this is not worthy of my business.  I would ask the owner to refute any of these comments.

We had been hearing good things about Elaia, so we decided to try it for a romantic Valentine's Dinner. At $50 each for a four-course dinner that exceeded $200 after tip, I would have expected a sublime taste experience that's out of this world. It was out of this world all right -- in fact, it belongs in the underworld. 

About the only good things were the waitress and the wine -- and even the wine was overpriced at $15 per glass. I don't mind paying for value and high-quality cuisine, but neither are truly to be had here. The food was just... OK. The flavors were nice but unremarkable. and the portions were almost literally microscopic. Think of a normal tapas-sized plate and then divide by half while multiplying the price by 50%. It almost seemed like a parody of a post-modern dining experience that you might see on Saturday Night Live.

Given the marginal quality of food, the oddly sized space, the decidedly un-charming atmosphere and the outrageous prices, we won't be returning.

I was here for the first time on a busy Saturday night, and I had high expectations. It seemed like a cute joint with live music and amazingly spacious enough to accommodate numerous birthday parties! We were all set for a really fun evening. 

My party ordered a couple beers and a pizza from the bar, and the bartender told us it would be delivered to our table when ready. Simple. Right? 

When the pizza arrived, the server simply dropped it off and ran away before checking to see if we had plates, napkins, utensils. My friend went up to ask the bartender (who had taken our order) if we could get some plates. She literally told him she was too busy remembering bar orders to go and find us plates! So, we would up finally "stealing" them from another table who didn't need all of their plates. 

As if the pizza experience wasn't bad enough... I was trying to buy a drink for the birthday girl after we ate. I went up to the bar (since our table had no server) and literally waited 10 minutes. There was a barback stocking glasses who wasn't able to assist, and then there was a service bartender who couldn't look up from his job. I waited at the bar, with a line of other thirsty folks... and waited, and waited for a bartender to arrive. I finally told my friend I'll just buy her a drink when we go out next time because I was tired, bored, and not willing to purchase my drinks there any more. And then we left. 

I do give this place one star for tasty pizza and decent beer, but the overall experience was very bitter.

Pat's and Geno's got nothing on this place. Stayed away from the tourist trap and headed to where the locals get their eats on! They were right!

As you can see from the photos that are posted on each of these restaurants pages that you get these puny little steak sammies and P or G's. But at Ish's the meat is over flowing and plentiful. 

I have seen other reviews stating that Ish's meat is bland. Mine was covered in cheese wiz. I had no complaints on the tastiness of the sandwich. The addition of their world famous fries with their Gremlin drink (Lemonade and Grape juice  and you got one scrumptious meal that you don't have to wait in a huge line and get insulted if you don't order your food the proper way.

My wife suggested we eat here on a whim. They were closed. Then we came back just as they opened. Most people dining at least had a jacket or sport coat, but they do not have a dress code. 

We had a great meal. Everything came out perfect and tasted great. Our trip was during Lent so seafood was on special. I had the fried lobster. This is out of character for me as I usually prefer turf over surf however I'm glad I took the chance here. 

The atmosphere is upscale for southern Illinois without being pretentious. Mostly younger people as staff that we saw but competent at their positions. 

On a whim I ordered an old fashioned. The drink was like water - in a great way. Nothing was wrong with it and I long for another shot at one. Normally I drink zero alcohol so if you're a professional you may have another opinion. 

Stop in for a great dining experience and be sure to try a cocktail.

Wow! Literally everything has such a blast of flavor! Even though it's sold as a bowl, I kept everything separate. I loved everything on its own. My husband mixed it a together and loved it all together. The sauces were fabulous too. The coconut rice was amazing. We bought a bag of chips too because who can resist lime salt?!  Can't wait to go back and try more things!

Before starting the review of the restaurant and the food I have to shout out to YELP in general and to Shannon S. in particular. Yelp is just the bees' knees in finding new places and learning whether they are worth a look see. And the members of YELP go the extra mile to assist you in passing a grand time in the Crescent City. When Shannon learned we were moving to a new area of Uptown New Orleans he was right on the mark with places to visit. There are many on the list and this will be my report on one of them.

Jamila's Café is located on Maple St. a few blocks off South Carrollton Ave. in a very active part of town for restaurants and bars. It is what I would call a neighborhood type of place with different sitting areas and set up in such a way  that conversation with your dinner guest is never difficult because of noise. 

Another major plus outside of the delicious food served here is that we were treated as regulars on our first visit. My kind of place! The owner visited our table throughout the night and even opened our wine. After dinner we were escorted to the kitchen to meet the staff and his wife and namesake Jamila. They made us feel like long time regulars and that was appreciated. 

The food is not typical New Orleans of course. Jamila's promotes itself as a Tunisian Mediterranean restaurant. And the difference is welcomed and appreciated when you desire good food with an enjoyable new taste and flavor.
After being seated, and reservations are accepted, we began to take in the aroma, sights and sounds of the restaurant. Our server was Karim and he was most attentive. Our cocktails, Grey Goose and Maker's Mark over ice, were delivered with a full glass pour. That made be happy before the first taste of food.

We started with two appetizers: The Steamed Mussel Marienieres and the Brik aux Crevettes. The Mussels were fantastic and one of the best dishes we enjoyed on our first visit. The Brik aux Crevettes in a dough were nice but overshadowed by the Mussels.

The wine list is varied and reasonable. We ordered and enjoyed a Pouilly- Fuissé. One thing stood out here in the serving of the wine. This has never been done in my history of drinking wine in any restaurant in my life. The owner did the honors of opening the bottle for us. And as is the custom to pour a little wine in the glass and wait to see if it is acceptable Moncef poured a little wine into both our glasses. Equality has come to the tasting of wine before a meal at Jamila's. It was nice and both my fiancée and I highly appreciated this procedure.

The Mussels were so good that Bethany ordered a main course that contained shrimp and more mussels. Served over linguine pasta it was more than she could handle and I was able to do my duty and finish it for her along with my delicious selection.   

My choice was the Mediterranean Shrimp that was sautéed in garlic, white wine, and prepared with sundried tomatoes and spinach over linguine pasta also. Servings are a nice size and we left stuffed. 

And that was after a Jamila's pastry and some very good strong coffee the way coffee was created to be served.

Raising this restaurant to a Five Star. The consistent top quality food that is always prepared fresh and with flavor and taste is one of the main reasons. The service staff has never provided anything but attentive and professional caring service at all times. And recently we used the catering service of the restaurant for a party at our new home. The food prepared and the reasonable price of the catering service has raised this New Orleans gem to a Five Star.

This restaurant has my Seal of Approval!

I forgot how much I like this place for whatever reason took it out of the normal rotation of lunch spots.  Needed to pick up dinner for the fam at home as all were sick and me spending time cooking was time that could rather be spent being nurse Dad if you know what I mean.

How do you rate soup, I ask that as a legitimate question.  Only home made soups I grew up with were clam chowder and chicken noodle.  Cambells soup never steered me wrong either.  At the deli/buffet there is soup hanging out in a big vat that was always a don't even think about it for me.  Now comes in a place (ok theyve been around since 2007 I know) that loves soup so much its in there freakin name. To judge soup I did it this way Aroma, Appearance, Heartiness, Taste, and Texture, 

Ordered the Tomato Bisque and Broccoli Cheddar, both had great aroma spices used were definitely fragrant (5/5), the soups had color and more than I would expect for soup, this is probably do to fresh ingredients and not canned (can't confirm that) appearance (5/5), these 2 soups will fill you up did a quart of each and there was plenty left over fat, heartiness (4/5), taste was a split the tomato bisque while delicious needed spice (pepper sauce did the trick) for me and the wife added garlic shrimp to hers (3/5) broccoli cheddar had great flavor no modifications needed (5/5), lastly texture is well thick, as you would imagine on these soups, not chunky just a good consistency (4/5).

We added a pesto chicken sandwich and that came with a nice side salad, also a few small cookies thrown in for good measure which were delicious.  While I waited for my order to go someone came over to let me know happy hour prices on the beer were about to end so if I wanted to sip on one while I waited to buy one now, kudos on that great service.

Place is packed and busy, service was awesome, and the local vibe is alive and well here!  Only docked a star as this was a little spendy for my usual soup and a sandwich budget $40+ with tip and beer.

Beautiful place I stopped by on a backroad back to Fort Campbell. The Cafe is closed on Tuesdays, but you can go to the gas station next door and try some of the food sold at the Loveless Cafe. Definitely a place to go to in the future.

Warning:  Hungry Man on Board

Could I make it from downtown Phx to downtown Tuc in less than one and a half hours for an early supper? I was up for the dare and I bet you'd like to know what my driving time was...
...but I plead the fifth.

Yelp reviews led us to Tasteful Kitchen on 722 N Stone Ave. I would never expect to find this restaurant in that area so it was definitely a pleasant site. Walked in without reservation. Luckily a table was available (weeknight!) and we were seated within a few minutes by friendly smiling staff.

Small place, small menu, small portions, big service. 

The business offers cooking demonstrations, catering, and dine-in or take-away meals. In a time where the trend for every new-american restaurant is to sell the same dishes, it was nice to see a bold diverse menu. I can say it was one of the best vegetarian meals I've eaten.

I was so hungry and prepared to eat twice as much than I originally planned. The question was, would a four course meal ($25 pp) be enough? Nah, decided to order several separate dishes. 

Funny enough, though, the bill total came out to roughly the same cost per person because the Taro Root Croquettes ($8) and Mushroom Medallions ($10) I wanted were unfortunately unavailable. However in addition to the regular menu there were four other specials being offered.

Tasteful Kitchen's website states: "We cook with ingredients as close as possible to their natural state with a minimum amount of processed foods." Well, I will testify to that. TESTIFYYYY! I ate yummy vegetarian and vegan food not overly-soy sauced or drowned in pungent vinegar flavors. 

Of course those flavors are in some of their dishes - if you want them - but I was happy to find my plate filled with food that tasted like the food it actually was. I felt the earth, the heart, and the health on my plate. That's real food.  

Appetizer: plate of yam wedges ($6) with curry dipping sauce. 
Decent size. Wedges were thick, crispy outside and melted when I bit into them (Yum! How did they do that?!) I could not stop eating. Curry sauce was just so-so, but if it was served spicy the level of tastefulness would be ten-fold.

Salad: Green house salad. 
Small plate of fresh crisp veggies. Would prefer larger salad. Gotta. Get. Greens.

Entree: Portobello mushroom with mushroom marsala sauce ($16) accompanied by smashed potatoes, cherry tomatoes, and sauteed greens. 
The patty-sized portobello was well flavored with homemade sauce. Greens were mixed with green beans and that gave me the crunch I look for in lively food. This dish could've done without the cooked tomatoes - I think red peppers would be much more tasteful.

Entree: Spaghetti squash ($16) with tomato sauce and bean croquettes of herb pesto and cashew parmesan. Spaghetti squash all the way! It was laid atop arugula, and covered with tomato sauce that was absolutely delicious. I wish this was the food that I grew up on instead of flour made paste noodles. 
[Sorry, italian chefs, but pasta is not good for the body.] 
The three bean croquettes were just okay. They reminded me of falafel, but were weirdly different. Tasted soaked, but had crunchy texture in every bite.

Dessert: Banana Cake ($7) topped with dark chocolate sauce, blueberries, and a mint leaf
Wow! A vegan dessert, similar to a bread pudding. It was moist and warm and full of nanas. Chocolate was bittersweet. Kudos to cooks who can make vegan desserts without the dry and grainy outcome that curse so many vegan sweets. 

Dessert: Carrot Cake ($7) with carrots, pineapple, walnuts and cream cheese icing
This was a fail for me. Cake? Yes. Carrot cake? Not! This cake was the same colour as the banana cake and as hard as I tried, I did not taste carrot, did not taste pineapple, and did not taste the cheese in the cream cheese icing. The walnuts were there, but they were chopped small and were easily forgettable.
But of course I ate it. It's cake! Okay, so maybe it was only a partial fail.

So, folk wanting good vegetarian fare in downtown Tucson, be a guest at the Tasteful Kitchen. Never mind any complaints about its size, slow service, and lack of options. If you're looking for food that tastes like food and want to take the time to enjoy a meal, make a reservation and drive yourself to this 5-star restaurant.

Go on, I'll race ya.

DO NOT COME HERE FOR BREAKFAST!
How can you call a restaurant "Breakfast" and not serve the meal by said name?? WTF?

I've been here twice. The first time was good maybe, but definitely not great. I was seated in a dark spot close to the mean street of Tucson downtown, and I could hardly see my food. I ordered some cilantro-heavy chicken that was quite bland to me, and had to chow down a big plate of unseasoned raw leaf. It was a lot of jaw movement. So, I thought I would never be back.

Husband, on the other hand, for his love of Mexican food of all and every kinds, really enjoyed his meal. So when his parents were in town, he suggested this place again. 

Second time's a charm! I'm quite in love with this place now. Maybe because I'm now getting used to its chalkboard menu, dim-lit ambiance, and its non-traditional approach (aka non-Sonoran heavy lard and cheese) to Mexican cuisine. If you like chicken, get the mole combo -- so delicious! Husband got the "surprise me" / chef's choice plate, and according to his rare lip smacking, it was awesome.

For some reason, I always thought Cafe Poca Cosa was impossibly expensive. It turned out I was biased and mistaken. For $20-25 per entree, you get an enormous plate of flavor combination. On a side note, it has some of the best chip and salsa in my book, crisp, non-oily, and addictive. 

The servers are all cute, charming, and courteous, if you like people watching.

**Updating this review because the Founder/President reached out to me with some kind words about this experience. It's great to see these efforts and are very much appreciated.**

We were really hoping to enjoy this spot and left disappointed. 
We stopped by here on a short weekend trip to Nashville last weekend. We wanted to avoid the main downtown strip and loved that this location was a little more quiet. We got lucky with parking right across the street when we visited on a Saturday night. 

What originally drew us to this spot was the dog-friendly patio and beer selection. There were so many beers my husband and I each wanted to try, unfortunately we weren't given the opportunity. 

When we walked in we looked for a host or direction on where to sit. The host was a tall young lady with brownish hair (didn't get her name) that welcomed us with a "there's no seating inside." Because the bar and seats were full inside with plenty of wait staff, we found this confusing and were waiting for her direction on where we could sit. We then had to ask, can we sit in any open seat out here? She said, "yes if you can find one." Okay great, we found a spot and looked up the menu right away to figure out what we wanted to order.

Twenty minutes+ went by and she hadn't visited our table. Had she stopped by and mentioned she was unbelievably busy, to take a peek at the menu, and she would be back, we would have been 1000% understanding. I ended up finding her inside talking to someone so I patiently waited for her to finish and then asked how we can order food and some beer. She responded with, "I'll come to you when I can" with an attitude unfortunately that caught me off guard. She seemed proud of the way she said that and I thought it was very unprofessional.

My husband and I were being as patient as we possibly could for service but with that type of response, we thought it wasn't worth the wait any longer. I worked in the restaurant industry and do understand busy days and stressful hours. By the look of other empty seats around us, it was hard to rationalize why we weren't able to have the opportunity to try the menu and beer here. Sorry to your team for the low review but it takes the same amount of effort to be kind than the way she treated us. We wished for a different experience and hope others have a better one than we did.

Until now a visit to Santa Barbara has always been bittersweet - yes we love the pristine Spanish mission style promenade... yes we love the long stretches of ocean shore.... ohhhh...but the Japanese food....yikes

THEN... like a gift from the sea comes Yoichi. A former chef from Nobu Tokyo, Yoichi brings lovely, thoughtful, wonderful Kaiseki to this off the strip dining room. 

This (reasonable compared to  other equivalent spots) set menu is delicious - and nothing like any other dining experience in SB. 

This is maybe the first 'destination' restaurant I have found in SB to date - and against the rather meager competition I give it easily 5 stars on the Santa Barbara scale. 

Here is the hitch... this place is NOT packed - and SB seems not to get what they have here... Ladies and Gentleman of the coast - get your collective heads out of your spicy tuna rolls and celebrate what you have here - before you loose it! 

Thank you Yoichi - Great spot!

Meeting friends in Philly, was invited to do as many tourists do which was go out for Philly Cheese steaks. As an invited guest, I didnt check Yelp (huge mistake) as to the choice of venue. The only thing I did confirm is that they had a non-beef option...Roasted pork.

Overall, no easy way to put this...But the roasted pork on a hero roll was one of the worst tasting foods I have ever put in my mouth...Or should I say the most tasteless thing I have probably ever eaten. The only positive, if it was a positive was that it wasn't bathed in grease like the beef cheese steaks. The hero roll itself was tasteless and obviously made 1-2 days earlier in some mass production bakery. The roasted pork or what they claimed was roasted pork could better be described as a non-beef steak-umm. It had NO taste whatsoever. Obviously the short-term cooks never heard of salt, pepper, or any spice for that matter. One good thing...The diet soda was able to wash down the barely edible sandwich. 

Unless one is near starvation or every other restaurant in Philly is out of business, one should avoid Pat's

Parc is a really nice French bistro in the heart of Rittenhouse Square in Philadelphia. The food is consistently high quality and the dishes are prepared in a traditionally French manner. 

A few personal favorites at Parc are the French Onion soup and the apple tart. And of course the breads are simply wonderful...and they do have a solid selection of French wines by the glass.

On the downside, Parc definitely requires reservations as I have never seen it not busy and one could find themselves waiting for quite some time as a walk-in. With a reservation I have also always found myself seated at a nice table vs. one that is next to a busy aisle. Service is  generally solid and well intentioned, but it can vary a bit from server to server. Overall, when in Philly, I can think of no better place for a French brassiere experience

Inn of the Hawke is located in Lambertville and is a bit off the beaten path, so it tends to be frequented by locals more than tourists. I have been to Inn of the Hawke many times and have always enjoyed the food and atmosphere. They have an extensive bar menu with a wide variety of craft beers. On this occasion given the season I indulged in the pumpkin ale which was awesome.

For dinner I had the swordfish sandwich which was very well prepared and quite tasty. Inn of Hawke doesn't do French fries, but rather they make their own pub chips which are quite tasty and can be a bit addicting. On this occasion I also indulged in a piece of cherry pie for dessert which was also very good. 

Overall the service was friendly and quite attentive. I'm a big fan of Inn of the Hawke and look forward to my next visit.

Don't judge a book by its cover
The front of the hotel looks okay, the lobby is nice. The staff was friendly . In the morning they give you a breakfast on the go pack in the lobby.. Water
, coffee and fruit. Kinda cool... Now the room I stayed in was something totally different.. I have never stayed in anything similar to this, I'll let the picture speak for them selves ..( see pictures )
I talked to front end manager , explained the spots on carpet the smell and her reply is I will make a note so you don't get charged for the spots or the tear in the chairs or Couches.   I smiled and thanked her for her time.  call me a sucka but if I didn't get thru her with kind words she wasn't going to get the point..

One night I was playing with the yelp app on my phone (procrastinating) and noticed a place called Lemongrass that had an incredible 4.5 stars - I quickly realized it was just a stone's throw from my house, but I'd somehow never even noticed it. 

It didn't take much convincing to get a friend to try it with me, so we headed there early on a weeknight.  The place was empty, but several other parties came in over the next hour or so. The waitress was super friendly, pouring us tea and bringing over a vegetarian menu for us to peruse in addition to their regular menu. 

We decided to split the lobster roll, which is an innovative take on the traditional.  Lobster is wrapped up with lettuce, noodles, cabbage, and fresh apples in a clear, sticky wrap and served with peanut sauce. It was pretty unlike anything I've ever had, but was totally delicious.  At $9 for two (easily sharable), this appetizer was a total steal.

I had shrimp pho as my meal, served with plenty of sprouts, a lime wedge, and house made hot sauce.  At $11 for a large bowl, this was another steal- there were also 5 or 6 large shrimp in the soup. My friend had the sweet and sour chicken, and judging by her empty plate she also enjoyed it. 

We were offered the complimentary dessert, but after finishing our meals we were full. This ended up being an excellent, inexpensive meal. I can't believe I hadn't been here before, but you can bet I'll be back!

The newly opened Pioneer brings fancier fare to Fountain Square. The building looks like most trendy rehabs with lots of exposed brick and industrial beams overhead. Rather than an extensive menu, they seem to focus on just doing a few dishes well. I have a hard time classifying Pioneer's cuisine since it doesn't seem to fit one category. The menu offered a few starters, snacks, and sides (vegetables), three different pasta dishes  (gnocchi, cavatelli, spatzle), and three proteins (chicken, steak, sausage). The protein offerings were pricey, so we stuck to ordering a few small plates and sharing everything. The cavatelli was tasty but simple. The potato pancakes were nicely salted and topped with delicious garlic aioli and apple compote. Our favorite was the broccoli rabe which was flavorful and enhanced by the crunch of toasted pine nuts. I tried a cocktail (Stereo) that sat perfectly in the balance between sweet/light and strong/boozey. Draft and bottled beer selections were also available. My favorite part- dessert. The night I visited they had an apple strudel with crisp, flaky crust served with generous amounts of caramel sauce. For a $9 dessert I thought the portion was small. I shared, but could've eaten it by myself. :) The two of us filled up on menu samplings, dessert, and a drink or two each for around$90 (including tip). It would be tough on my wallet to be a regular here but the food and drinks are worth checking out. And in case you missed it, save room for dessert!

Gotta say that the owners treat you right here.  They know all about customer service and I hope that their business does extremely well here at the RTM.

Corndogs are not an everyday food unfortunately.  But when you want a food that will bring back memories of fairs and circuses this has to be the go to item.  Fox and Son has the absolute best tasting, freshest foods imaginable.

Besides a wonderful corndog, I tried the fried cheese curds.  OMG.  Light puffs of cheese lightly fried that almost taste like funnel cake to me.  Add in the dip and it will be gone in seconds.  They have to be some of the best things in the RTM.

Add in some fresh lemonade and you have your trip to the fair all complete!

I'll absolutely be back - but not everyday!

Very pleased with my experience at DiBruno Brothers. I needed a meat and cheese platter for a party and after a surprisingly unsuccessful trip to the Reading Terminal Market (see my review!) I checked a search of Yelp and was happy to see how close DB was. I took a short walk and met Asa. He was a huge help. We just had to discuss an approximate price, if any guests had allergies, and was was liked, if anything in particular. I set a window of time to pick it up the next day.

The next day I got my two-tray order; one with crackers and bread, and one with a well-set selection of cheese and meat. Then, disaster. While Asa handed it to me, the bag dropped and the food jumbled a lot in the container. I said it wasn't a problem and I'd just put everything back in place, but Asa said it was. He ended up giving a 10% discount and offered for next time to bring it personally wherever I needed the food. He was genuinely concerned to make sure things were right.

The store has so much to offer with a bottle shop, sandwich shop, cheese shop, coffee, and more. All staff were very helpful. 

The cheese and meats were a big hit at the party, with all of the "fan favorites" that Asa picked out along with the candies cashews were quickly eaten. 

A big thanks to DiBruno Brothers for excellent customer service and tasty food!

I had to wait a few days before writing this review because I was really floundering between three and four stars and after some thought, my friend and I both overall that all the hype over this restaurant was not worth it.

We had a reservation and made it in time to pay $25 to park in a lot on a Friday afternoon as street parking is a PITA. 

The coolness and vibe of the rather full restaurant was right up there. Everyone seemed to be having a good time. We ordered "remotely" using our phones and a QR code. The process was very easy and our food came quickly. 

Don't get me wrong; the pizzas were quite good. We ordered the "Angry" which was loaded with the jalapeño and other was mostly a red pie with the anchovies on the side. We devoured them both, but had no dreams of nirvana pizza gods smiling brightly. I truly think pizza, like cheesesteaks and hoagies, are a huge personal preference, and Pizzeria Beddia was not our ultimate favorite. Additionally, maybe the ingredients used justify the $25 price per pizza and $4 toppings, or maybe it's the hype price, or the area of a bunch of young people with cash to blow, but these prices are too high. But, that's me.

We also "splurged" for the soft serve; I had the cream and my friend had the espresso. Again, nice but not blow my mind ice cream.

Service was very friendly and almost too attentive. 

My friend and I overall enjoyed going out and good conversation, but agreed that we won't come back.

$100 for two cocktails, two pizzas, and two soft serve not including tip.

Not sure why this place got good ratings...Rude hostess (I think she was the owner). We were told to that we had a wait. We waited and moved a chair from one empty table outside to another empty table. We were told not to rearrange the furniture. Really?  You want to wait...but don't sit together.  The person working as a hostess was very rude to us for no reason at all.

Pretty sure they don't read this...(but if you do, you can't deny this). As a valued Yelper, this is not a place you want to go to....regardless how good the food is suppose to be.  I would be treated better on an United Airlines flight.
I was in Cherry Hill for a Birthday party. This was the perfect place for dinner. I appreciate the service and the attention to detail. The food was excellent as always and I can't wait to go back.

Philadelphia has soooooooooooooooo many cheesesteaks and I will probably never try them all.  Some of the best cheesesteaks will come from
the smallest unheard of places in Philly! I grew up 15 minutes from Philly and my parents took me every weekend to see and do everything they wanted to do. 

So I grew up with this as my playground. If you wanted good food, go to Philly. If you wanted good fun, go to Philly, If you wanted good music, go to Philly! So whenever I am in the area I make sure I stop at some of the places I missed along the way. I have never been to this spot and I could kick myself.

The sandwich is delicious. You can only order a whole due to covid (the new cv-19 hustle) and it literally takes 3-4 minutes! I was pleasantly pleased with this cheesesteak and to be honest it may be my last. I am working on going meatless in 2021 so if this is my last than I'll be a happy man!

I've heard about this place for many years... Even when I owned a restaurant in Camden I couldn't get there in time to get a fresh one before they ran out. They close early in CMD so I've driven past the original donkeys, but never actually eaten there. It has been around forever(Over 71years) in Camden, but The late TV chef Anthony Bourdain really put it on the map when he featured them on Parts Unknown a few years ago. 

I went to Donkeys 2, which is set in a more affluent neighborhood sandwiched between Cherry Hill (where I use to live) and Voorhees the place is small, but comfortable and mainly a take out causal eat in spot. You can't fit 50-100 people inside but you can sit around 20-30 comfortably. There are pictures on the wall of the original owners and the original location in Camden. 

The steak is amazing and the bread is unlike anything you've ever tasted. It comes together so well with the topping and French fries. You can't eat the entire thing and you will want to take a few home for later. Try this place before you go to Philly and get some commercial cheap cheesesteak.

What a great experience for a Friday night! I just arrived in Nj and I wanted to check out this location for a while now. Every time I come to Nj I want to visit, but the wait before the pandemic was astronomical. 

In the midst of the pandemic, they told me the wait would be 45 minutes. I saw a sea of empty tables and thought to myself "why!" and guess what it was only 5 minutes after I sat in the VIP couch section that they called me to come eat. I got the first seat and I ordered the crab fries and the mussels with white sauce. I usually get the red, but this time I tried the white. (I like the red better) everything came out super fast and I was able to people watch and enjoy the beautiful atmosphere. I will be back.

FINALLY. A well-known Indy NE side institution taking over a prime piece of real estate on Geist Reservoir! I've lived in the area for 7 years, and this is the first time I've been to this location due to the well, frankly, terrible places that have been here previously. On to the food/service! 

It was packed on a Wednesday night, but the weather was just about perfect so it was a great time to go! There is ample parking even though some people were already getting "creative". The nice thing about this place is that there are plenty of windows throughout so even if you end up in the dining room or bar, you still have lots of natural light and great views of the reservoir. This location is a bit different in that it's not quite as rustic/sporty as most of their other locations. That's likely due to the location, clientele, and layout. I like it! We were informed that there was about a 30 minute wait, but we were fine with that. Guess what! The host/hostess takes your phone number, and you get a text when your table is ready! No more carrying around pagers or having to listen for your name. 

There's actually a really nice waiting area down the hall where you can still sit on the patio, and you can order drinks! If I'm sitting on the patio with a drink in hand, I can wait for some time for a table! Libby was our server out there, and I liked her immediately (the sharing of a name helped)! I honestly don't know how long we waited, but we got a text and headed to our table. We had said we'd be willing to sit in the bar or first available since we weren't set on being on the patio. Well, it just so happened that they gave us a table on the patio! I think due to position, it was probably the best one out there. 

Keegan was our server, and he was very friendly but did seem a little new to the job. (That reminds me, it was so fun to see Debbie from the Fishers location in the bar area!) The menu is the same as at other locations so it was pretty easy to compare. I got one of my favorites - the fish tacos with fries. They were exactly as they should be! My husband got the Woodbury burger which he enjoyed, but the fries were a bit skimpy. (I told him to ask for more, but he declined.) 

There is also a covered patio area so it seems that even if it's raining but still warm out, you can get that outdoor dining experience. I noticed that there is an upstairs, but I believe that is for private parties/events. I'm very curious whether Wolfies will be taking reservations now for the fireworks over the bridge on Independence Day! 

Solid, solid Wolfies experience, and I know we'll be regulars!

A great addition to the neighborhood! These guys are doing a real bang up job. The menu has lots of choices for everyone. They have vegetarian items as well as seafood and chicken. My move is to usually choose one of the signature dogs and then split an order of large frites and an order of sliders with my wife. I have been several times, here is a rundown of what I have had. 

Signature dogs: 
Sweet and Spicy Corn Fritter Smash - Very good, with nice spice! 

Thai Satay - Just ok, needed more flavor. 

Jersey Shore Breakfast - EXCELLENT! 

Backyard BBQ - My Favorite, just delicious. 

Hawaii 5 -0 - I wanted the sauce to be hotter. 

Gourmet Sliders: 
Pulled Pork - Same Pork that's on the Backyard BBQ dog. WINNING 

Cool Burger - Combo of the Pesto, Brie, and Caramelized onions are YUM. 

Punjab Chicken - Meh, needs some work. 

THE FRITES 
They are really good. They even serve them in these little brown bags which helps keep them crisp, and warm. I personally think they could be a little more crisp. Maybe fry them for 30 more seconds? Very nice product nonetheless. 

The staff and owner seem really nice and are very professional. I LOVE the Iced Tea machine they have. Keep up the good work Cool Dog, I'll be in this weekend to try the NYC HomeWrecker!

This restaurant is overrated by far. My husband and I were excited to stop in as we live in Downingtown, and this spot looks super cute from the outside. Business is really starting to pick up in the area which is good for the town.

Unfortunately the tacos here were extremely underwhelming and lacked flavor. We ordered several and the only one worth mentioning was the smoked chicken thigh, which had a nice bbq flavor that came through instantly. The briscuit taco was dry and tasted oddly like chorizo, almost like it was cooked mixed in with the other meats, and the seitan taco was completely flavorless and flimsy - the tortilla was soggy and fell apart instantly when I picked it up. 

I saved room for dessert but this was mediocre as well.  The sopapillas were dry on the inside, and the chocolate cream they're served with was super heavy and oily. The banana pudding was okay but had way too much whipped cream and not enough fresh bananas. The best thing I had was the refried bean dip and chips.  

With the above said, I did like the atmosphere and do think this would be a fun spot to stop in, grab a drink and hang with a group, but you can get much better tacos elsewhere. I have had tacos in Austin, Texas and these don't come close. This spot missed the mark.

The restaurant cancelled my online reservations twice with no explanation or email. Thanks guys! Clearly you must value your customers.  ** update ** received email after posting my review telling me they had a private party and instructing me to revise my review ** response: if you have a private party don't accept and continue to accept online reservations. If you value your customers then use words like sorry and don't instruct me to revise my review, which I certainly won't be doing.

** here is the restaurant's exact message (from the owner named Brett R) to me. Make your own judgement regarding customer service:

"Fuxx you cuxx 
Don't ever come in stay in California where you obviously belong"

For something so easy to make, MANY Filipino establishments can't make it because they can't seem to make it right. 

As a Filipino, I know and realize that a lot of Filipino restaurants are notorious for over pricing and being stingey on products and portions. I get it. I understand it. But it's stupid and disheartening. In an area with a smaller Filipino demographic and no competition, it's easy to "just be ok" and get away with it since you're the only one in the area and I've seen it happen throughout the years here and in Orlando, but Filipiniana truly has my respect on not falling onto that track. They seem to impress my every time I come back by improving since the day they started.

+Halo Halo
Yes, they don't have ube ice cream, and that in itself would already be a deal breaker for me. But they were innovative enough to have the ice that's usually mixed with evaporated milk, be already flavored with ube in it (GENIUS). They have a scoop of (vanilla or mango?) ice cream on top and a nice serving of ube halaya on top. The toppings on the bottom aren't limited and includes a chunk of leche flan on top. My only complaint is the pinipig (green crunchy topping) that is the Vietnamese brand which isn't as good as the Filipino one, but will certainly make due since I know how hard it is to find that around here.

+Mais Con Yelo
My favorite especially when I don't want the extra flavors from the Halo Halo. Let me tell you how happy I was that they didn't cut back on the amount of corn or evaporated milk they put on it and the fact that they put leche flan on it since even the big named chains like Max's won't even do that for you. 

You can tell that I've had really bad experiences with Filipino places (mostly in Florida) and that I've been jipped and over-payed for something I couldn't believe places would think is acceptable to serve. I love Filipiniana and would come every time I come into town from Orlando.

Soooo much better than those other places around town offering the same concept of made to order all you can eat sushi and hibachi. (Not pointing fingers)

I came here on March 9 so about a week after they had first opened. We dined around dinner, which keep in mind is $25 rather than $13 for lunch, so keep that in mind and see what's worth it for you. They have more dinner entree selections, a wider arrange of specialty rolls, and the best part, sashimi.

I was mostly excited that they had hand rolls here where other places don't offer but my dad went IN on the sashimi platters. You're only allowed 6 per type a person so my dad gladly took my 6 each. 

The specialty rolls are presented much better and have more filling to them as well as the hand rolls. 

+Salmon Skin Hand Rolls
Being someone that refuses to even buy my salmon if the skins removed, I indulged in my hand roll full of crispy strips of happiness. (I mean omega's are good for you, eat up)

+Sashimi
For buffet quality, this is definitely good. I know you can order sushi with the slice of fish on rice, but these are much thicker cuts specialized for sashimi. The selection was great and plated it nicely.

+Hawaiian Roll
We're all guilty of getting that fake sushi roll with fruit and cream cheese, and I know you've seen it packaged up in the sushi section of Publix. And I've tried it and Publix was even better (who admits Publix has a better roll than a restaurant... It is fake though). The slice of mango and the sauce on top just tasted more artificial than fresh and tropical to me. It's like sipping on a Capri Sun wishing you were drinking a piña colada out of a pineapple.

+Specialty Rolls
However, all the other rolls were incredible and am impressed at the selection they have and the menu here is much better than the competitors. 

+Spare Ribs
This was the only entree we ordered and is available only during dinner time. It was nice and tender with nice flavor but just a tad bit salty but nothing horrible not to eat.

Overall happy that more places are starting to come up in Wesley Chapel it just makes coming home here more exciting. I just hope that unlike the rest, the quality remains the same rather than downfall eventually.

If you are looking for a REAL Philly breakfast, this is the place. The food is always cooked perfectly (I have been coming here for years and it's been consistent).

The home fries are among the best in the city. The omelettes are also delicious.

Lee's now has a Veggie Steak and a Black Bean Burger to become more veg-friendly. It's always a risky move, considering a lot of places can't seem to pull of making a solid fake-meat hoagie. Lee's GOT IT RIGHT:

-The veggie steak was made with seitan (wheat meat) and was smothered with cheese and the right amount of seasoning. It was filling and not too salty.

-The black bean burger was also delicious, and I'm kinda a veggie burger snob. 

-The 16 bean soup is flavorful and creamy. Definitely get it if it's available.

The environment is great for watching people walk by on 47th street. You MUST go to Lee's Deli NOW!!!!

My cousin made a really good selection today when choosing Riccobonos The crowd was behing me as we walked in as the lunch crowd started to flow in. My Mom was in the mood for Breakfast and after hearing about the Special, "Chili cheese  Omelet " so was I. Home made Chili was not the thick kind but very flavorful. The Potatoes were cut thick and were crisped up on the grill before serving. Honestly I would go back for the Potatoes. Maybe add some cheese sour cream and a  bit of that Chili. I don't know if that's on the Menu  but it should be. I had them to put the Biscuit on the grill, and if you get to this spot you should do the same. You can thank me later. My Mom had Fish and grits. An ample serving of Catfish from what I saw. I tasted the fish and to be honest it was nothing special but she enjoyed it . She doctored up her own Grits, which honestly is how it should be done. Service got slower as the crowd poured in but it was understandable.  I've never had to wait to pay that long before lol. Nice neighborhood place that is a bit out of the way for Tourists but loved by locals. I would go back in a heart beat!

I have heard a few people around the City of New Orleans speak of Red's Chinese and was planning on going there. I saw Guy from Dinners, Drive-ins and Dives on TV when he visited and decided to move it up the list. Today was my lucky day. Of course I had to have The Generals Chicken. As far as taste goes you can't go wrong. The chicken was coated in a tangy, sweet sauce covered in everything they could find that was good. Even though the chicken was pretty soaked in the sauce it was still crispy. Now as far as value goes I didn't think 4 pieces is worth 17 dollars. My fault I guess because I saw on the menu they offered small and large. Silly me I thought a small was maybe 3 pieces and a large at least double that. My bad. The chicken comes with a side of steamed rice and your choice of sauce. Now back to the Chicken. I tried the Breast which I don't need to tell you can be easily overcooked and dry. Not today. That was the juciest piece of Chicken I've had in some time. Flavors were all over the place in a good way. 
 The Restaurant is located in an area that is not where most would have thought to put a Restaurant. Parking can be a Beast as it is on a main Street in the city. Eclectic is the best way to describe the people of the area as well as the Employees. I'm not saying that in a bad way at all, after all I survived several weeks in Austin lol. What I mean to say is that if you are a Snob, Church Lady, stuck up or a Mike Pence style Evangelical you will be instantly offended by the amount of Tattoos, piercings, Goth clothing and Gender Rebels in one location. ( Their just people) But if  you just happen to be one of those people who love to live, laugh, love people and eat then you will love this place. I really like the fact that the kitchen is wide open and the Staff appear to be really nice. I hear the Hamburger fried rice is phenomenal. By the way they have a tendency to put a twist on several of your favorite Chinese dishes. I'm digging this spot and I'm looking forward to going back again.

Have y'all ever had a person who might be 100 for 100 on Restaurant suggestions and if they were wrong you would be inclined to give them a pass immediately? How about if in that scenario you were told that you were in for a Burger experience of epic proportions? I'm talking about the type of experience that would make a Vegetarian eat meat kind of experience, or at least that was the hype man's way of hyping up this Burger. Well this ain't that type of party. In fact when I see him I just might hit him in his throat for suggesting it. I am at a loss as to why any person in of all places, New Orleans, would find a need to wait in line for a Burger at Shake Shack! Ok, at best it was really just ok. The size of my Burger was less than the size of a 99 cent hamburger on most Menus. Now I know size isn't everything, ( Gigidy) but as  Randy Moss would say, "Comonmaaan". The Shake was better than the Burger to me. Change the name to, oh wait, Shake is in the name with no mention of it being a preferred Burger joint. (Y'all didn't see that coming huh)? I won't be in a rush to head back for a second chance. I'm afraid I might run into the person that suggested this spot and end up going home with a Misdemeanor Assault. I have to say though the service was excellent. If your looking for fantastic service, great Milk Shakes and mediocre Burgers, head on down to Shack Shack on Veterans Blvd in Metairie La. In fact head over to one near you because they are popping up all over the place. I predict that this is a trend like when people stood in line for an hour or so when 5 Guys hit the scene to be a Burger Bully. Now you can walk right up to the counter. The 3rd Star is for the service, in the event your wondering. Peace, with 2 fingers.

Wow, that was a very good Po-Boy. The PB came loaded with Beef and fixins, or as they say in New Orleans, "Dressed".  I usually like pickles when I order, "Dressed" but could have been left off by accident. Bread was ok, which most New Orleanians will tell you makes or breaks the sandwich. I am also used to sliced Beef and not chopped. Gravy was thin but made the sandwich nice and sloppy as it should have. I also had a side of Onion Rings which were very good. All in all I will definitely be back, most likely today lol. I feel you what, a 9'' Po-Boy and a side of Onion Rings for around $8.00? You can't beat it.

From food truck to brick and morter!! Recently opened in SoHo, they opened on the corner of Platt and Howard.  We tried their tacos opening night and really enjoyed them and the guacamole. It was super busy and chaotic opening day,so I held off on my review until I went back. 
The amazing food and wonderful service didn't change. This time, it was early and not busy at all, so we were able to sit and enjoy the quiet. 
The inside space is small and packed witht tables, so it gets noisy when its crowded. The have a parking lot and street parking available. Lots and lots of options on the menu. The burritos are huge! The tacos are all fresh and tasty. The crema is a little runny but the freshness of everything else makes up for it. 
Make sure to like them on Facebook to keep up with any specials and add an order of churros to every order.  They food is delicious!!

You know when you have those staple foods that you assume people can't mess up? Well burgers USED to be one of those foods for me until I ate at Goody Goody. After hearing mixed reviews about it, I had to try it myself. 

Let's start off with their selection of burgers. You'd expect a place that prides itself on its burgers to have a wide selection of burgers, right? Wrong. You literally get a choice of a few burgers, each with a slight variation. You either get a normal burger, a burger with cheese, a burger with too many toppings, and a burger with normal toppings. That's it. 

I ordered the cheeseburger pox...oh what a mistake. This is considered their crown jewel burger, but I would say a McDonalds cheeseburger ranks higher. The burger comes with cheese and their special pox sauce. The pox sauce is literally...and I mean literally unseasoned marinara sauce. I would rather have ketchup. The buns come out soggy so you get this disgusting texture to the burger. The only saving grace were the fries, which also were not too spectacular. 

Let this be a warning: either people's taste buds changed greatly from the 1930s or these burgers have always and still suck. There are plenty of other places to go in Hyde Park. 

tl;dr - Soggy buns and flavorless sauce. Is this even a burger anymore?

Settled in the middle of Channelside, Thai Thani has become one of my favorite places to go for Thai food in Tampa!

The atmosphere is very surreal. From the first step inside, you immediately get transported to Thailand. The decorations and the atmosphere is very authentic and feels almost like a Thai temple. There is a seating area in the back that looks very intimate and traditional Thai seating. Unfortunately, we didn't sit there.

The food is very good. The consistency of the noodles and the combination of ingredients will literally melt in your mouth. I got the pad see ew and it is on point! 

Warning: Their mild spice level is medium to most. I ordered mine with medium spice and felt like my tongue was going to burn off...thank god for multiple water refills!

tl;dr - authentic food and experience, can't go wrong here!

Great food and great company! Took the family to this restaurant today and met some fellow yelpers...what a great time.  We arrived at 11 (ish) so it seemed the perfect time to enjoy brunch.

The vibe reminds me of an upscale pub that you makes you feel very welcomed as soon as you walk inside.  I love to visit places that do not feel like they have a cookie cutter design and the Brasserie has succeeded in providing a warm environment.

I had the eggs benedict, which was served in a short amount of time with a beautiful presentation. (see pictures)  It was served with fresh fruit and seasoned potatoes with a cheese sauce.  While all of this sounds very heavy, the sauces were surprisingly light.  The eggs were cooked to perfection, although one of the English muffins were chewy (the other one was delicious).  I loved the seasoned potatoes and the fresh fruit gave the meal a very balanced feel.  I did have the bottomless mimosa's (who would not enjoy that?) where you get as many mimosa's as you want within an hour....brilliant!

Hubby had the biscuits and gravy (hey we are from the south) served with poached eggs on top.  They were served with seasoned potatoes with an artisan cheese sauce that he stated  "were to die for" and fresh fruit.  As a southern man he has been pretty disappointed in the west's inability to capture southern cooking, but he said he very much enjoyed their version.  The gravy was lighter  with an herb sauce that was a new twist for him on an old classic.

Loved the restaurant, the food, the vibe, and the company.  I can definitely see this being one of the family favorites.  When our 13 year old looked up from his phone (rarely) he seemed to enjoy it as well...so that seals the deal.  Make sure you check them out!

Just not getting it.....and I have tried.  Third time trying Lampost because it is close to home and I keep thinking it will get better.....but it doesn't.  I have tried lunch and dinner and neither impress.

Last night we stopped in after a basketball game wanting a fresh pizza.  We walked into total chaos with kids running around everywhere.  This does not bother me because I expect parties and such with kids, I only mention it for people who do not like this kind of atmosphere.

Next we went to place our order at the counter.  Two employees at the counter having a conversation let us stand there for two minutes while they continued to have their talk. After placing our order for a salad and pizza we went to find a clean table (not easy).  We sat down and my hubby went to find someone to wipe the table down.  When he found her she asked him, "which table do you want me to clean, the one you are sitting at?" They did come and clean the table.

We had a few other customer service issues but I will say it wasn't like the servers were trying to be rude it was more like they weren't trained.  However it is like this whenever we visit.

Our pizza did arrive in a timely manner but it was burned slightly. Honestly it didn't have much taste.  We didn't want to wait any longer so we ate it and left.  Like I said their proximity makes it a great place to eat but there are so many great pie shops in Reno that seem to have it down.  I hate to give two stars but unfortunately this has been our experience every time.

Taco Tuesday at Mexcal! Best place for epic tacos in my opinion! Wow!
We made reservations for 6:30 for two. We arrive about 10 minutes early... our table is not ready yet, so we sit at the bar. We order one of their cocktails - everything is made with Tequila... I can't drink Tequila so I ask if they can make it with Gin instead... sure! I order the Alyssa Loca
Gin replaced the Blanco Tequila, Fresh Mint, Fresh Lime Juice, Fresh Raspberries, Organic Agave Nectar, Topped with Chandon Sparkling Rosé-DELISH! Natalie ordered the Paloma Azul
Lunazul Resposado Tequila, Fresh Grapefruit Juice, Fresh Lime Juice, Organic Agave Nectar, Splash of Club Soda-she said it was the best she's had! I'm not sure how much they were (drinks on the house since our table was not ready) And chips and salsa too! Such wonderful service!!!

We are seated, maybe around 7'ish and already had decided on what we wanted to order... to start we shared the Charred Octopus
Citrus - Microgreens - Black Bean Sauce ($13) I have to say, next to Puerto Vallarta MX this was next to the best Octopus I'v had! So tender and flavorful! Next we ordered TACOS DORADOS Quesabirria House Specialty served with Onions - Cilantro - Broth ($6 ea), Chicken
Spicy Braised Chicken - Onion - Cilantro - Salsa ($4.5) and a DE LA CALLE Duck Confit Maple Leaf Duck - Red Cabbage Slaw- Pickled Red Onion - Cilantro ($6.5). The service was exceptional, checking on us, making sure we had everything we needed. I loved this place!! It is totally worth it... the prices are great too! I will definitely be back to try more!!

Get on over to Mexcal, you will love it!

After three weeks of covid 19 self quarantine, hubby and I were going crazy. We decided to order take out. It may be that anything not cooked by us had an advantage. Fine. I'll say Bangkok was just what we needed. We doubled up to make sure we had two meals. Hubby started with veggie sushi while I stepped it up with sushi nachos. Both excellent. The dinner premium is the way to go; for two bucks you get soup, salad, or appetizer. The Panang curry, pad see-ew and teriyaki tofu were all yum. Bangkok did a bang up job packing things up. The nacho wontons and seaweed salad dressing were packed separately to keep things crisp. They gave us heaps of silverware (assuming based on the number of entrees we had loads of people). A great experience. We'll be back (hopefully in better circumstances).

RACIST club, with RACIST people and RACIST thieves working in it.  DO NOT open a tab at the bar if you're not WHITE.  I've gone to this place 2 times and both times I opened a tab I find out the next day that the bartenders bought there buddies a couple of drinks on my expense. This never happens to my white friends, only to my black, asian, and spanish friends.   I've never felt comfortable at this place. NEVER had a good time.  If your white, this is the perfect place for you, but if you like a mixed diverse crowd STAY FAR FROM! 

Hyde Park is  sort of a cheap version of 90210 with a false sense of pride!

We went to Beddia for the first time last night. I moved into the neighborhood about a month ago. Since day one, I've been dying to try this place, but I'm not into standing and eating. I'd been wanting to take it to-go and bring it back to my apartment. The brutally cold weather has kept me on a strictly delivery diet when craving pizza. The mild 30 degree weather last night finally got us there. 

We had read mixed reviews online and were expecting the owner to be pretentious and dismissive. We experienced the polar opposite. We were greeted with smiles and courtesy by both the owner and the cashier. I don't do spicy, but he does, and I felt like he needed to experience it. So we ordered the Arrabiata and a pie with roasted onions and baby arugula, and decided we'd just have leftovers. We were told it would be about 45 minutes, so we went to Johnny Brenda's for a few beers while we waited. 

When we came back, one pizza was ready, the other was almost ready.  I made a comment about how amazing it smelled in there, saying they should bottle the smell and sell it as a perfume. The owner proceeded to tell me someone has bottled the smell of pizza, but as pizza-flavored beer. He reached under the counter and grabbed a bottle of said beer, explaining that someone brought him a six-pack as a gift. So we split the strange beer while we waited for a few more minutes. 

We got to my apartment and the slices were still hot after 4 blocks (maybe a 5 minute walk) in below freezing temperatures. I took one bite of his pizza and it was way too angry for my taste. I absolutely loved mine though. The crust was definitely among the best I've ever had. Perfectly crispy. I drew the line at 3 slices, he drew his at 4. I think it's on par with Pizzeria Vetri, maybe better. It was so good, the dog only got one crust from each of us. :)

Overall, it was a great experience. It was definitely pricey and hard to say that two pizzas would ever be worth $50. But we'll definitely be back and I can't wait to eat the leftovers tonight. But that was the first and last time either of us will drink pizza-flavored beer.

UPDATE: heated the leftover pizza in the oven and it was ALMOST as good as when fresh.

Ok I'm hesitantly giving an extra star, however this Arizona Pizza Company makes their pizzas so bland, we drive ourselves into town to go to the other location, where the pizzas are divine.  The only thing they have going for them is that they're the only place that delivers.

You would think that since they're owned by the same company, they'd be at least similar.

I'm so jealous that this is all the out in Santa Barbara. This is the kind of food that we need in the Valley. And to have these quality of tacos inside of a batting cage park, I think we are spoiling children. Or they're really lucky to have this amazing food instead of high sodium hot dogs and chips.

What an amazing breath of fresh air East Beach's tacos are. So clever with their ingredients and flavors. Makes you not look at a taco the same ever again. And after having East Street, why would you?

Honestly, all their tacos are delicious - you cannot go wrong - but the best and most unique taco here is the Ahi Poke Taco. All the flavors from the Hawaiian ahi poke bowl but substitute the rice with a wonton crispy taco shell instead! Me and 11 girls bombarded this joint and literally ordered everything on the menu so we could try and bite different things. 

Winner: Ahi Poke Taco
Runner Up: Beach Bomb - rice ball stuffed spicy tuna.

WATCH OUT! Don't buy 1 taco for $4, but 3 tacos for $9. I know, i know. Trust me, you will want 3 tacos. Oh and drink refills are free.

I posted food pics on my instagram and I had my followers drooling & begging me to bring some home.

This is where the locals in go for their beignets while in the French Quarter. 
1. Their beignets are BETTER!!!
2. The line is SUPER shorter
3. The dining space is not so crowded!
4. The beignets here are just better!

so a vegetarian and 2 omnivores walk into a fancy steakhouse. oh wait, you've heard this one before? nevermind, then.

i won't bother telling you that the vegetarian didn't go hungry. she didn't even eat a salad. no siree, bob! she was - get this - able to order off of the special prix fixe lunch menu without requesting a single modification. unheard of, right? wrong.

said vegetarian very much enjoyed her bowl of curried cauliflower soup followed by a plate of cavatelli pasta in a light sundried tomato sauce with generous dollops of goat cheese. all for $15. who knew? now, you do.

i'm buried up to my eyeballs in bookmarks of places to review... yet it seems only fair that my first review of the new year is for the very first restaurant i patronized in 2010: resurrection ale house. 

if ever two people (or four, taking into account the friends we met up with) needed to rise up from the dead stupor caused by excessive NYE partying, we were it. for reals, people. 8pm may as well have been 8am the way we were carrying on with our lazy day of flipping between football games and mummers. the desire to remain on the couch unshowered was tempting...but the promise of good food, good ale and good company won out, and so we began our new year's day sojourn.

parking was easily found off of grays ferry...a welcome change of pace from the tough-to-park-for-free streets of center city. once inside, we were quickly welcomed by the warmth of the cozy space, our on-point bartender molly and a one-drink-in michelle C. while la fin du monde, amongst others from the extensive bottle & draught beer list, was calling my name, i opted for the lower ABV franziskaner hefe weisse, another personal fave. molly poured, spun and poured that bottle like the professional she is...twice actually, as michelle later ordered one for herself. i foolishly thought i had it in me to keep pace...but alas, only managed to nurse a single beer throughout the course of our night. yes, really!

when it came time to order food, i was overwhelmed with vegetarian options - each one sounding better than the next. taking molly's advice, i selected the roasted maitake mushroom which came served with a celery root puree, glazed carrots, hazelnut breadcrumbs and baby watercress salad. a lover of mushrooms, i had actually never had maitake before and was very pleasantly surprised with the taste and texture...not to mention the appearance. this single shroom looked leafy like an underwater coral, and was the size of a meatloaf - completely unique, and most importantly, delicious!

to top it all off, the entire time we were there, i had the sneaking suspicion someone had stolen my ipod and was playing it on shuffle. from belle & sebastian to the faint to neutral milk hotel to the talking heads...the music couldn't have been more ideal, for my taste at least.

i walked in a zombie...i walked out feeling revived...resurrected, even. happy new year!!

a few weeks ago i embarked upon a guys nite out. yup, you read right. a nite on the town for yelpers christopher R, yuri, bill mcthrill...and me. being the lone girl (tho one with a guy's name, for whatever that's worth), i was along for the ride while the majority ruled our various destinations.

i first met up with the boys for a drink at the irish pol where i was, um, fortunate enough to witness the wonder that is boobie bingo. we then headed to the ritz to see 'the men who stare at goats' of which, coincidentally, the starring cast was all men and one woman. after staring up at the screen from the very front row for what seemed like an eternity, we all agreed that more drinks and some eats were in order, and, in hindsight, it seems only fitting that we then ventured to pinup girl themed varga bar to close the nite.

the varga girls are far more demure than those one would find at a typical last stop on a guy's nite out (or, er, so i've been told...) and were way less in your face than i was led to believe from other reviews i've read on here. and really, we hardly paid them the attention they were seeking, as all eyes were focused on the phils v. dodgers game on the single screen at the bar (volume on, fyi).

whatever beers we drank escape me now...but i can further attest to the fact that the beer menu is stellar. the food menu was a lot more limited, at least for vegetarian me, but i already knew what i was ordering before walking through the door: the veggie burger, which comes topped with tomato, cucumber and a [not-so] spicy avocado creme fraiche and served with a deliciously simple side salad. chris advised that he'd had this burger before, but found it fell apart rather easily making for difficult and messy consumption. good to know...so i cut mine in half before eating and had no problems. i recommend you do the same! as veggie burgers go, this one was homemade and with uniquely refreshing toppings - i'd easily order it again. the guys enjoyed their meals as well, plus we all shared a tangy pot o' pickles that, tho heavy on the cuke, was quite good and a steal at just 4 bucks.

the nite was capped with j-roll's 9th inning, game-winning double....high fives, hell yeahs and hiney slaps all around. guys nite out, indeed.

oh, lolita... i just visited you for the first time on friday nite, and, much like the nabokov nymphet for which you are presumably named, i find myself smitten and longing to see you again. soon....i hope!

the guac? delish. the BYOT factor? love it. but what really sparked my love affair was how wonderfully vegetarian friendly lolita is. a glance at the menu will have anyone exclaiming "say what?!" but it's the little asterik @ the bottom declaring that 4 dishes can be made with a substitution of pan seared three chile tofu or grilled portobella. i opted for the tofu (duh) prepared a la duck - so it was served atop sweet & warm plantains in a sour cherry salsita (chock full of dried cherries) with a garnish of jicama orange slaw. "yum" would be an understatement.
