the thing is, it's not just about how tasty my particular entree was, it is the fact that i actually have more than 1 veg meal option combined with the fact that it's not just taking out the meat from a dish and charging me the same price or offering some mediocre pasta/risotto/beans+rice option. dining at lolita, i can actually order a protein-laden dish straight off the menu, with the same sauces and sides as my meat-eating companions!! you have no idea how appreciative i am of this....or if you are a veg, perhaps you do?

thank you, lolita. MWAH!

ok, i was called out on my previous 3 star rating/semi-glowing review, so now, after my latest iron hill experience, i am rounding that 3.5 up to a 4. took the folks here for dinner en route to dropping them off at the airport. no one was in the mood for any particular cuisine, so IH was the perfect solution as the vast menu has something for everyone. 

i insisted that we start with my fave sweet potato "fries" which were a big hit with everyone. *patting myself on the back* my dad raved about his seafood bisque and my mom & bf who sampled it were also fans. the three of them also shared a baby octopus app special which featured the tiny tentacle creatures served atop crispy tortillas with pineapple, avocado and a sweet sauce.

my dad ordered the angus burger, my mom the mesclun salad, the boy the cabo shrimp salad (in honor of our recent vaca) and i got the portabello mushroom sandwich (layered with roasted peppers & goat cheese). everyone was happy with their meal, and my folks proclaimed that they'd be happy to come back another time when they are in the area - huge compliment coming from mr. & mrs. f!

ps. we ate in the main dining area, but it's worth noting that there is a lot of table seating around the bar, which has TVs in almost every direction for sports enthusiasts looking to catch the game.

:: the birthday kid, part III ::

hating on starr restaurants is like cobra kai beating up on daniel-san. just because all the kewl kidz are doing it, don't mean it's for me...at least when it comes to alma de cuba.

i'd previously only been to alma for drinks - probably about 5 times in as many years - and each time i enjoyed sipping sangria in the swanky downstairs lounge. this past december, lucky me got to head upstairs for more than just a trip to the ladies room when the boy took me here for a day-after-my-birthday birthday dinner. it was a bitter cold nite outside, tho you'd never know it inside the invitingly warm alma interior with lights low...candles aglow... were we instantly transported to cuba? not even close. but the mood was perfectly set for a budding romance on a special occasion.

drink orders placed - mojito for him, dark & stormy for me - we diverted our gaze from one another and towards our respective menus. my selections were easily made as, in typical restaurant fashion, the veg options are limited. while the boy continued to peruse, i dug in to the warm mini rolls placed before us by our server. only a little tho, as to not ruin my appetite for the black bean soup (topped with crema fresca & 3 rice croquettes) that would soon be my first course - and good thing for that, as i savored every thick, soupy spoonful!

meanwhile, the boy was gushing over each bite of his yellowtail ceviche. he pleaded with me to change my non-meat-eating ways...assuring me that i wouldn't regret my decision upon tasting the other-worldy magnificence upon his plate. 'A' for effort, but i of course declined, to which i believe he was secretly grateful in that he did not have to relinquish a mere morsel of his new-found heaven on earth.

his second course, the vaca frita, was destined to pale in comparison to the ceviche, of which he continually wished he had ordered a double portion of instead. my entree, the pionono, was a puerto rican sweet plantain roulade of zucchini, basil-tomato sauce & queso fresco served with roasted garlic & broccoli rabe - and it delivered. the flavors and textures of each ingredient meshed perfectly, altho i refrained from cutting into the stinking rose on date nite...instead pushing it to the side to be wrapped up with my uneaten half for lunch the following day when the promise of a kiss was not in my immediate future :)

dessert, having been skipped the nite before, was inevitable, however, when our banana tres leches was brought to the table, it arrived sans candles, despite the boy having made mention of my birthday when he made the reservation. shame, shame, alma! all in all, a small hiccup in an otherwise stellar birthday celebration.

this is not only my favorite indian restaurant, this is my favorite restaurant in all of phildelphia, hands down. i say that in part because it is the only restaurant that i have frequented on a regular basis over the past 13+ years. it's hard to put into words what i love about this place...but i shall try...

my first new delhi experience was october of 1995, yet it seems like just yesterday. i was a freshman at drexel, and a sophomore friend who was helping me with a film class project suggested we get some take-out while watching movies. he called in an order to new delhi and we trekked from powelton village thru penn's campus in the cold. i was bitter about having to walk so far to get our food, wondering why we couldn't get something closer, or better yet - delivery! after walking all the way back in the cold and then unwrapping the tightly sealed packages with nearly frost-bitten fingers, i pretty much would have been satisfied with anything. i wasn't satisfied. i was blown the eff away!

since that first experience (tho not my first indian endeavor, mind you), i have ordered off the menu a mere handful of times compared to the number of visits where i opted for the buffet. now, i am not one for buffets as i generally am weary of the vats of food sitting for long periods of time, however, just as the clientele at new delhi is constantly turning over, so does the food. in one short visit i have seen the naan replenished 3 times - that's a lot. the staff on the other hand? talk about low turnover rate...i gather this must be a family operation because i have seen the same men working there since '95.

and the food, oh the food! while the buffet items are typically not as spicy as ordering a la carte...i have been quite grateful for the pitcher of water left at the table on many an occasion. as i'm the type of eater who takes a bit of this, and then a bit of that, and often mixes flavors and sauces, i can never be sure which was hot and which was not, but who really cares? all are tasty, and that's what matters.

my favorite dishes are the malai kofta, gobi masala, palak paneer and [sorry, i don't know the exact indian name for it] the vegetable pakora in a lemon chickpea sauce...tho i have yet to have anything i disliked here. at least 2 of the above items are always on the buffet when i go in (typically on weekends) as well as naan, basmati rice, samosas and of course a few meat dishes...ya know, if that's your thing.

since the renovation about a year and a half ago, they have also been offering rice pudding (on the side, next to the salad bar), but you still get your choice of dessert as well as coffee or tea along with the buffet, which is already a steal at $9/lunch, $12/dinner. i'm a sucker for gulab jamun and kulfi, tho lately i have been filling up on my food and haven't had the room for it - sacrilege, i know! speaking of which, who else remembers when the front/waiting room housed a sweets counter? man, that was some good stuff...

what can i say? i have requested to be taken here by my bf on special occasions ... i have driven out of my way to come here when other options were closer/easier ... i have opted to see movies at the bridge over other theaters in order to dine at new delhi ... i have been eating here for nearly 14 years! clearly, i love this restaurant, and if you haven't tried it yet, well, what are you waiting for, a UYE? if so, you're in luck - check the events page! http://www.yelp.com/events/philadelphia-new-delhi-uye

remember that feeling of anticipation when you were about to head to disney world for the first time? you could barely sleep the nite before...you'd heard everyone else rave about mickey mouse and space mountain...and now you were finally going to experience all the magic and wonder for yourself! yeah, well, that was me as i awaited my virgin visit to blue sage.

oftentimes built up expectations work against places. space mountain? nothing but a lame roller coaster in the dark. but not blue sage. after 4 years of people telling me that i MUST try this restaurant, that, as a veg, i would absolutely LOVE it, i can honestly say that my experience most definitely lived up to the hype.

for starters, i was in great company with dining companions heather M & tom C. tho they're both eaters of the meat, this was heather's third visit to blue sage in two months and tom exclaimed that the menu read like veggie porn...which it does. with the description of [cue slow, sexy voice here] "fresh blue corn tortilla chips with smokey adobo black beans, roasted corn, grilled julienne red peppers, ovendried cherry tomato halves & creamy roasted onion goat-manchego queso," the adobo goat cheese nachos sure sounded like a must-have app. not surprisingly, they were as delicious as we'd hoped they'd be, and the portion was so large that the 3 of us couldn't even finish it!

there were two entree specials being offered - a poblano pepper stuffed with caponata and another one featuring squash blossoms - which tom & heather ordered respectively. i went with a menu item, the cubano supper, featuring [sexy voice again] "flaky plantain pastries stuffed with sunflower seed-smoked red pepper pesto surrounding a tower of yellow tomatoes & avocado corn salsa and served with chipotle jicama slaw & mango-papaya relish." let's just say there was as much color and flavor in this dish as there were adjectives to describe it. 

dessert items like a chocolate panini and a hazelnut toffee basket sounded tempting, but were quickly forgotten when our server informed us of the nite's special: a pumpkin bread pudding with whiskey caramel sauce and scoop of ice cream. wow! a delicious seasonal treat that i highly recommend whenever available.

i knew going in to this meal that there was no tofu or faux meat, just straight up veggies, and i'll admit that i thought i would miss it...but ya know what? i didn't. not. one. bit. all that said, the drive from my office in media, pa to the unassuming southampton strip mall where blue sage resides took me close to an hour. for food this good, i will gladly make that trek again.

after a crazybusyfuuunnn thanksgiving weekend, i finally caught up on my zzzzz's sunday morning as i woke up around noon and didn't motivate off of my friend's couch until well past 2pm. by that time, nausea had turned to hunger, and my belly needed food...my head needed coffee.

seeing as it was a chilly day, the belly was fed a piping hot bowl of tomato basil soup with rice. it came served in a giant bowl along with a sizable slice of sourdough bread, which i used to sop up every last drop of the soup. if you see this on the menu - get it!

along with my hot soup, i enjoyed a hot coffee. (i repeat: chilly day.) no fancy latte or cappuccino for my hurtin head....just a straight up cup o' joe. i had the medium roast (nice that they offer this along with light & dark roasts) with vanilla soy milk (just ask, they keep it behind the counter) and it was simply lovely. bonus points for being fair trade.

for some reason i was expecting a dark nook of a cafe and was pleasantly surprised to walk into such an airy, well-lit and spacious....space. tho nearly every table was full, it didn't feel crowded. no barking dogs or unruly children (or parents). if my vagabond lifestyle leads me to waking up in this 'hood again, i'll surely be back.

delancey stays at a strong 4 stars, after all, i am there at least twice a week - they make a mean bagel. tho high prices & skimpiness often abound, i have finally found a way to get my beloved soy chicken salad samidge at a cheaper price!! 

what was once a ridic $7.35 is now a preposterous $8.29 - yet i still keep forking over the monies. not any more! instead, i have discovered that i can purchase a toasted bagel for 99¢ and a container of moshe's vegetarian chicken salad from the refrigerator section for $5.29, totaling $2 less than what they are charging for the same made-to-order sammie, just sans veggies & side pickle.

oh, and the container yields way more chix salad than they ever put on the bagel, unless you're like me and you complain and make them give you more. it is also the EXACT same salad they are using in the kitchen - not a housemade variety. trust me, i eat it every week; i can tell.

so there you have it. consider this my gift to you all on how to save $2 on the main line. you're welcome.

as fellow yelper vinny P and i wandered about the trenton street arts fest on this superbly sunny saturday, a craving set in: ICE CREAM. there was a mister softee truck with a short line, but we were willing to wait a little longer for the intriguing flavors calling to us from the little baby's truck......

coffee toffee!!
bourbon bourbon vanilla!!
cardamom caramel!!
earl grey sriracha!!

we got a scoop of each of these 4 and faltered between wanting the other person to try the amazing flavor we had just eaten, and wanting to save it all for ourselves. ultimately, we shared nicely. and yes, you read right, earl grey sriracha - as in the tea and the cock sauce - which tasted exactly as you would expect it to: awesome. not only are the flavors unique and robust, the consistency is so creamy; you can tell this stuff is homemade. 

can't wait to sample more little baby's ice cream throughout the summer!!

i hit up parc for dinner in its opening week last summer - loved it. since then i have been back a handful of times for drinks and light fare, and with each visit the novelty began to wane. 

most recently i had my first parc brunch...and while good, it was simply not as great as i had hoped it would be. i get that it's a [starr] french bistro doing the minimalist chic thing, blah blah blah. and yes, most places tend overdo it on their portion sizes, so it's nice to have a small plate for those of us looking to eat healthy. and yes, my omelette (with herbs and raclette) was quite good. BUT...$13 for an omelette, with not a single side?!? 

interestingly, parc has a breakfast menu on their website showing sides like lyonnaise potatoes for an extra $3 and fresh berries for $6 as well as a few reduced prices compared to the same items on the brunch menu. perhaps this is the weekday menu (it does not say) tho i am curious why sides would not be offered to those of us indulging on the weekends.

like many upscale brunch spots, parc does provide a basket of assorted breads for the table, HOWEVER, we did not realize this until after our meal when making our way past other tables and eying up their tasty looking assortments. our server had recommended a pastry basket (for $8) which was enjoyed by all at our table, but she apparently decided we had enough carbs and didn't need the bread as well. um, ok...

while explaining some dishes and simultaneously pouring water (two things one would think are quite manageable), our atkins-friendly server also inadvertently spilled a little on my boyfriend's menu, and then filled my glass so high i literally had to slurp it before i could pick it up - all without so much as a 'pardon me' or 'i'm sorry'! not the kind of service one would expect when forking over $13 for an omelette.

after wowing the pants off of my parents (not literally - ew!) with brunch at honey's, when it came time to grab a bite to eat for dinner, the pressure was on to impress once again.

our shopping endeavors had taken us to main street, manayunk - my old stomping grounds - so the folks were familiar with quite a few of the local restaurants, but were eager to get back to home in jersey and hesitant to spend too much time at a sit down meal. my solution: couch tomato! though i was convinced (still am, really) that they had enjoyed take-out from them years ago when i lived there, they claimed no memory of this. ah, the joys of getting old.... (sorry, mom & dad!) 

regardless of their alzheimer's moment, one look at the menu, and they were sold. dad ordered the pollo pesto personal pizza (hold the roasted peppers), mom ordered the pear-fection salad, i ordered the pump it up portabella salad and she & i also ordered one slice of the garden of eating pizza (white pie with spinach, feta & sun-dried tomatoes) to share.

much like at honey's, everything was delish and everyone left with full, happy bellies. and our over-ordering after a huge brunch paid off, as we all packed up leftovers for tomorrow - woo!

i did something tonite that i've never done before - i dined alone! sure, i've grabbed a quick lunch by myself and sat solo at a sushi bar, but this eating-out experience was a major first in my 32 years. 

so here's the deal: i was driving home from the airport which takes me down lansdowne ave. as i neared sycamore (which i know quite well from my previous 5 visits), i began to crave the wild mushroom & truffled duck egg appetizer i had recently seen featured in city paper's meal ticket. suddenly, i was turning my car into the small parking lot behind the restaurant, walking inside and declaring "table for one, please" much to my own disbelief.

despite already knowing what i wanted, i glanced at the menu and my eye/belly was immediately drawn to the chilled cauliflower soup with yogurt & pistachio. it sounded like heaven in a bowl...and it was. perfectly cool and crisp, and was that a hint of fennel i tasted? yum. equally taste bud tantalizing was the dish that brought me in this evening; it was like breakfast for dinner, only better. i'm so glad i decided to put on my big girl panties and take the solo dining plunge! 

chef sam is constantly tinkering with the menu based on fresh, local, seasonal ingredients which brings a welcome variety to his loyal clientele (like me), but also means that what's here today is not always offered tomorrow, so get it while you can! to that point, the vegetarian entree i raved about in my previous review? no longer available. fear not - in its place is a delectable indian-spiced lentil & quinoa cake, served over a bed of maitake mushrooms with a fried egg over top, and no doubt another meat-free masterpiece will be taking over for this one in due time.

oh, and ps. that rumor of a sycamore expansion i mentioned? true! i saw the beautifully renovated space today!

From what I've read, I would not visit here on a weekend morning for a few months. BUT, a Tuesday morning is perfect, at least it was for us. The space is on the smaller side with mostly communal seating. I'm not a fan of that, but there weren't many people there so I didn't have to rub elbows with a stranger. It's bright and welcoming. The staff are cheery and helpful.

I ordered the nest egg-basically a huge biscuit with an egg and bacon cooked inside. It was just enough to not make me bloated, so I also ordered the cream puff. That did the trick. It was a good size, bigger than a hockey puck, and stuffed with whipped cream. Highly recommend it. 

A guy nearby ordered the classic breakfast, it was massive, and definitely convinced me to come back soon.

There's a glut of amazing restaurants to get a burger fix. It's a good problem to have. But if you want a fresh, beefy, humanely-raised beef burger, go to Mac's. The burgers are smashed, so they're a bit smaller, but that's easily remedied with an extra patty. I did 3 patties with cheese and a side of Red Hot Riplet fries. I'm a big eater, and this put me to my limit. We sat outside on the patio, another hidden gem.

The owner was fun to talk to about the burgerevolution going on. It's clear he's proud of this place, and with good reason.

Very small and cozy but also cool and secluded if you sit in a booth. The waiters were very attentive especially since my date came 45 minutes late! After waiting for about 30 minutes I decided I needed to order something before I got kicked out  I got a steak tartare which and an asian spin on it that I absolutely loved! I got the fancy af drink which unfortunately I have no pictures for because I took a video but it way absolutely beautiful and if that wasn't enough it tastes delicious as well. It was a wonderful night and I appreciate the patience of the staff.

My husband and I had a COVID date night this weekend. We ordered our meal around 2pm for 5:30 pickup and paid ahead over the phone.

We ordered the Maki Combo, Drunken Noodles, Tuna Tartar and spring rolls. Everything was delicious and fresh. They were a little backed up when we went to pickup our order but the takeout process was pretty seamless.

Highly recommend for local sushi at reasonable prices!

When you advertise "breakfast with the Grinch 9a-1p" but stop serving breakfast at 11am, you're doing it wrong. The Grinch thing was cool, but I can't review the food as we didn't get any. After waiting in line for 45 minutes, we went to get breakfast because... you know... "breakfast with the Grinch." This was approximately 11:10a. The woman at the register noticed us looking at the breakfast menu and told us they weren't making breakfast anymore. As we were completely surrounded by tables full of breakfast food, this came as a shock. We went elsewhere and had a great breakfast.

Not the best first experience with a business. I'm sure events like these are great for getting people to your cafe, but if you call the event "breakfast" and don't actually provide breakfast... you're going to lose business.

I just ate lunch here this afternoon and everything I tried was delicious. Our group of 4 consisted of two vegetarians and two non-vegetarians. As one of the non-vegetarians I loved this place. I had the curried chickpea salad sandwich and a side of plantains. If I could eat vegetarian dishes this flavorful every day I'm pretty sure I could give up meat. 

With regard to the complaint about the smell of fresh paint one reviewer made, there were no issues today. And bear in mind this place has only been open for two weeks. I'm not sure how they expected there to be no "new" smell in a newly remodeled space, magic perhaps. 
 
You can expect to pay a bit more than other restaurants serving similarly sized dished. However, knowing they source their ingredients locally I think that's to be expected. I personally don't mind spending a few extra dollars if I know it's going back into my local community. 

I'm giving this place 5 stars because the quality and flavor of the food is top notch.

We had a great breakfast at Egg this morning! I started off with a double shot of espresso and my husband ordered the beermosa. I didn't try his, but he liked it! The espresso was delicious! 
We each ordered the specials. I got the cheesy grits and shrimp topped with two over easy eggs and green salsa. It was phenomenal! The spice was right on, the grits had a silky texture, and the shrimp and eggs were both cooked perfectly. 
My husband had the other special which was ribs, bean, some type of sauce and was topped with two over easy eggs. It also came with bread. He said it was great, but I didn't try it. 
We will be back!

Friday night sitting at the big back booth devouring the best ramen I've had in Philly ever. I added a poached egg to my pork miso, pro move. If you sit in the back you can hide from the club music. Water comes in chem lab beakers, nice touch. I'll be back, takeout would be nice too. 

If you're a ramen novice, this is your jam.

Arepas are one of my favorite things, and this place did not disappoint!   

We started with the appetizer special, which was a mixture of plantain, pork belly and a few other things mixed together and deep fried into balls of gooey, delicious goodness.  I couldn't even begin to tell you what they were called, but they're not on the daily menu.  

We followed that up with arepas. Again, I decided to go with the special.  It included shredded skirt steak, plantains, cotija cheese, and black beans.  Holy moly, it was incredible!  I can honestly say, it was the best "sandwich" I've had in a long time, probably ever.  They came with plantain chips and a sauce. We each ordered one of each sauce so we could try three of them.  All of the sauces were delicious as well. 

We had drinks to compliment our meals.  My hubs, Marcus H, had a Columbian beer or two, and my SIL, Candace T and I both ordered mojitos.  Don't say I didn't warn you - the drinks are stout!  

This kitschy little restaurant has about 10-15 tables and is located about a block from St Charles, so you can hop the trolley to come and go from here. There's also street parking if you're a great parallel parker and lucky enough to find a spot.  We opted to park in the pay parking lot under the interstate ($6 for 10 hours) then hop the trolley to the quarter and back.  

I will say, the service was a little slow, so if that's a problem for you, be aware of that possibility.  I rarely ever complain about slow service and I'm not going to start now.  We were seated promptly and enjoyed visiting with each other while waiting on our food and drinks, so it was no big deal to us. 

Our final tally, which included an appetizer, 3 arepas, 2 mixed drinks and two beers, set us back $88, and it was well worth every penny.  

I'm bookmarking this place so we'll be sure to stop in during future trips to NOLA.  We can't wait to eat there again!

Willie Mae's is said to have the best fried chicken in America, and I'd be hard pressed to argue that.  

There's a good reason the line to get in are so long. It's worth the wait. Get there early, right before dinner time (4:30-ish), if you don't want to wait. We lucked up!

I've tasted some legendary fried chicken in my life and Willie Mae's is at the top of the list.  I can't pin point what was so special about it, but it was flavorful, crispy and juicy.  The sides were incredible too.  I had yams and my hubs had mashed potatoes and peas. For dessert, we shared some delicious bread pudding.  Every bite of everything was divine.  

The service was incredible and the prices were pretty cheap for NOLA.  We spent considerably less on dinner than what we had payed for lunch. 

We've got our go-to restaurants in NOLA and Willie Mae's just got added to that list. Remember, go early.

New Orleans is synonymous with its food culture and one family name stands out high above the rest: Brennan.  Red Fish Grill is owned by one of the Brennan's and the food is just as spectacular as you would expect it to be.

We eat at Red Fish Grill about every second or third trip we take to NOLA.  On our most recent visit, we were meeting a friend and his 12 year old daughter.  I knew she'd love the funky decor, and I was really craving my favorite dessert in all the world, so I suggested we meet RFG.    It was a great call because they both loved the place.

We started our meal with BBQ oysters and fried green tomatoes with crawfish tails.  Both were incredible.  Even our friend who doesn't love fried green tomatoes liked the tomatoes.  I ordered the wood grilled redfish topped with crawfish tails, my hubs and our friend both had the catfish etouffee, and the little girl had the shrimp pasta.  

Okay, let me stop right there for a minute...  When my kids were young, they didn't order chicken strips or burgers every time we went out because I wanted them to expand their palate and not be picky eaters.  Kudos to RFG for putting a real dish on the kids menu.  I would expect no less from NOLA legends.

Back to the entrees, my redfish was as fabulous as always.  I love the potatoes and peas it's served with as well.  My hubs and our friend loved the catfish and etouffee.  But the star of the show, as always, was the bread pudding!  We typically order the double chocolate bread pudding, which is my favorite thing ever.  We also ordered a bananas foster bread pudding on this trip and it was equally delicious.  Seriously, the best desserts you will ever taste!  

The service is always exceptional and the prices are on par with most of the other restaurants in New Orleans.  The location is easy to access, on Bourbon, between Canal and Iberville, and it's an area of Bourbon you wouldn't mind taking Grandma or the grandkids to visit.  The vibe at RFG is perfect for a casual lunch, business meeting, or dinner on date night.  You really can't go wrong with the place!

I stopped in for some tasty wings and they were so good! The wings were the biggest I had ever seen. I ordered the medium heat and they were perfectly cooked. 

The chicken was so fresh, they cook it when you place your order. 

I highly recommend trying this place if you are hungry for some wings! The fries were also cooked to perfection!

I drive by this restaurant often and decided to try it out for lunch today. I had the lasagna and oh my goodness it was so delicious! The fresh bread was yummy! 
The service and atmosphere was good. Very quaint little place that I cannot wait to go back to and try another delicious dish.

Great place for a quick and delicious lunch or dinner. The salsa is delicious and the servings are large. Easy parking as well. The service is good and the decor cheerful. My server was very attentive and had beautiful nails, lol!

This is a fantastic, beautiful place that everyone should check out. The interior is stunning! The ghost piano is fun. The outdoor patio is relaxing and you are welcome to smoke a cigar out there if you want to. Even the bathrooms are something not to be missed. 

We enjoyed the food although it could have been hotter, my wild boar was served warm and my friends fish was warm as well and not hot. We both liked our food and thought it was worth the dollar amount that we paid. 

There were magicians throughout the restaurant and a theater with a 30 minute magic show that was fantastic! We did not get to watch the magic throughout the restaurant because of our time frame. We were there from 6-9:30 and could have easily stayed another hour. 
We felt rushed during our meal, we wanted to relax and enjoy each other's company and the server kept coming over to let us know how much longer we had before the theater show. We finally ask if we could go to the 9: o'clock show and it was not a problem. The time being rushed and the food not being very hot is the reason for the 4 stars. If these two blips were improved I would definitely give them a 10 if it were available.

From the minute I left my car with the complimentary valet service to walking in the door of Chauhan Ale and Masala  House,  I had a great feeling of how my evening was going to go. I had read Johnny and Rachel's Yelp reviews previously so I had a bit of a advantage on what to order. I arrived early and sat at the bar and had a delicious French 75 cocktail that was made perfectly. Both of the cute bartenders were so nice happy to be there doing their job. 

Rachel's review said that the gol guppa shots on the appetizer menu was life changing. I thought wow, I definitely have to try those. I had talked to the bartender about them and when I was going to order them my great server was already having them prepared. I will have to say that the gol guppa shots are definitely life changing fun to eat and should definitely be part of your food choices. I also tried them with the tequila option. I personally like them better without the tequila but the tequila that was served was smooth and enjoyed alone. 

The recommendation was on the traditional menu. Lamb with a red sauce that I ask my wonderful server to choose for me. I also ordered the garlic Parmesan naan bread. Every single bite of my dinner was a fantastic, delicious and plated beautifully. The rice was so light and fluffy it melted in my mouth. I would have like a little more rice just because I practically scraped the bowl of the sauce; I could not stop eating, it was so yummy. 

My server was outstanding and I enjoyed everything about my dining experience. The decor is beautiful, sexy, intimate but not stuffy. 

I think anyone would have a great time eating here. It's just fabulous! I can't wait to go again.

I can't say enough about this fabulous restaurant! Anthony our server is amazing and helped make my birthday dinner extra special with candles for everyone. He was also a wonderful attentive server that made our evening perfect. 

The appetizers and entrees are outstanding! 
If you don't want to have to wait for a table I suggest going early, around 6 because this place fills up fast. 

The margaritas were just okay but the guacamole was a 10! 


Parking is easy which is a great plus for Nashville. I will definitely be back. I highly recommend the shrimp fajitas.

Lots of energy and good atmosphere here with wonderful views of outside for people watching. 

We ordered the macaroni and cheese, it was a huge order! We also ordered the tater tots and they were the biggest order of tots that I had ever seen. It looked like there were at least a 100 on the plate. They were accompanied by 3 awesome sassy sauces. Needless to say we were not able to eat a entree and had enough of both to bring home for another meal. 

The service is always excellent as well. It was my birthday and unexpectedly our server brought me a huge root beer float! 

What a treat!

I really enjoy coming to this local spot. The drinks, service, food and atmosphere are always consistent and delicious. I like the outdoor seating as well and they have good happy hour specials. 

The outdoor seating is spacious, tent style and mostly quiet and soothing. You can have a nice meal and hear each other talking. 

I highly recommend eating here often.

Not very impressed with this busy and overcrowded museum. I would have enjoyed it more if I could have seen what was in the museum. Less people better time, I would suggest calling to see when the slowest time is to visit and hopefully you will have a better experience than I did.

I really enjoyed myself at the Hampton Social. The drinks are fabulous and pretty but not too sweet! The service at the bar is A+! The decor and atmosphere have a sexy vibe! The appetizers are some of the most yummy in the area. 

I highly recommend trying everything!

The food here is so special! I love trying different ethnic foods and hearing the stories that go with the restaurant. You must go and check out this family owned restaurant! I am a huge supporter of family owned business and this one will not disappoint your taste buds! 

Dee the owner will probably come to your table and even welcome you, how cool is that? The food is delicious and the restaurant is quaint. Located in the fun Berry Hill area it's a must try while you are in Nashville!
Thanks locale market always get nice service here everyone that works there is very nice very knowledgeable of the food and the food is always delicious.

OK I'm going to try and kept this short.  If you've been to NOLA you know that there is no shortage of oysters and certainly no shortage of restaurants serving oysters.  

What the hubby and I discovered is that if you want chargrilled oysters then Felix is your place.  They serve 4 different kinds of oysters:

1. Chargrilled 
2. Du Jour
3. Rockefeller 
4. Bienville 

Any of the above can be ordered by 1/2 dozen or whole dozen.  We tried all four and the verdict:

1. Chargrilled...ABSOLUTE BEST, I can't describe the texture and taste but it was exceptional.

2. Du Jour...meh they were served buffalo wing stye and were ok.

3. Rockefeller...again ok I didn't like the texture of the spinach with the oyster there were possibly my least favorite

4. Bienville...good, they had a nice coating of cheese and herbs.  

We also ordered a cup of gumbo and jambalaya, neither made much of an impression on my husband.

I HOWEVER RECOMMEND THE CHARGRILLED ONLY

Prices were reasonable, service well it was busy and it was slow.  I don't know if it was slow because it was busy or if it's just always slow.  With that being said our server was very nice and pleasant.

For our last meal in New Orleans, the hubby and I decided to go to the Red Fish Grill.  It is conveniently located in the FQ on Bourbon St. next to the Hard Rock Cafe.  It's rather large and spacious with a full bar in a sectioned off area with plenty of seating and tables.  Not to mention that they had one of the cleanest restroom of any business I've seen in the FQ. 

We had had a large breakfast and wanted a light lunch so we opted for:

1. RED FISH GRILL SEAFOOD SAMPLER
BBQ Blue Crab Claws; Gulf Shrimp & Tasso Fritters; and Creole Marinated Gulf Shrimp

2. BBQ OYSTERS
flash fried, Crystal BBQ sauce, housemade blue cheese dressing 

I can't think of one that that was better than the other.  Each items had it's own distinctive taste that was full of flavor and just as good as the next.  But, I suppose if I had to go with  favorite I'd recommend the BBQ Oysters (like at Felix's Oysters) they are served buffalo wing styles (at least the taste) at Felix the oysters were a tad dry.  The ones here at the Red Fish Grill were warm, moist and the sauce, although tangy, did not have the sour pucker factor that tabasco sauce often does.  

Everything was absolutely delicious and the service was equally amazing.  This is a restaurant I'd visit again and again. 

NOTE:  If you go to the tour office on the corner of Canal St. and Royal St. you can get a coupon good for a free bottle of wine with 2 dinner entrees.  FREE WINE!

If ever there is a place that can be wrongly judge by its appearance it is this place Bacchanal Wine.

During our recent trip to New Orleans my husband and I learned about Bacchanal Wine through our pedi-cab driver.  A former San Diego transplant, our driver said it's not a high tourist area and mostly visited by locals.  

When we actually went there, our cab driver had never heard of it and I had to give him directions to get there.  So though it was a bit wearisome at first my husband and I liked that we would be going out of the French Quarter and hanging with the locals.  

At first glance it looks like the area Bacchanal is in could be rather shady but it's just more quiet than anything.  It's only located about 3 miles away from the French Quarter but it feels like a world away (a good world away).  For my LA Yelpies the area reminds me of the Arts district in LA along Santa Fe/Mateo and 5-7th St. 

Ok so when we arrived we entered a room full of wines rather haphazardly organized and a counter at one end with a number of refrigerators next to it.  People were standing in line but for what, we had not clue.  I finally decided to ask than risk trying to figure it out myself and just mess things up.  This is how it works.

They help you "create your own adventure," You pick out your own wine (from a nice selection of lower to higher ended wines).  If you want a meat/cheese platter you pick the cheeses from the refrigerators.  They are individually priced and you pick the size accordingly to the number of people in your group.  You do the same with the meats.  You then pay for the wine, cheese and meats.  You'll get your bottle back (uncorked) and they you pick however many glasses of wine you need and literally if you need a bucket of ice you can get one. Your cheese/meat are place for you in a platter with nuts and fruits and brought out to you.  

You then walk out back to a dirt/gravel back yard (gives me the back yard wedding feel).  They have little lights hanging and at night the tiki torches and lights give the place a very romantic and sophisticated feel. 

If you want food your order from the kitchen (not the front where you get your wine).  The food is also brought out to your table, you get a number like you do at Carl's Jr. 

There is also a full bar and seating upstairs but my husband and I got cozy in they years and we didn't want to loose our table to we didn't look upstairs.  

Alright now that you know how it works were are some tips and tricks and stuff:

1. BRING CASH...IT'S A CASH ONLY ESTABLISHMENT.  If you forget your presidents there is an ATM by the kitchen.  My only worry would be that with my luck it would break and I'd be penniless.  

2. Get there early and grab a table, mark it, pee on it do something it gets busy very fast and last thing you want to 

3. Try and get a table towards the stage and around the fence.  You get a nice view of the band and you don't have steady foot traffic walking past you. 

4.  Try their food.  It is gourmet quality...absolutely delish!!

5.  Ladies DON'T it repeat DON'T wear your best pair of heels.  You're going to be walking on dirt and gravel. 

6. Do dress it up, despite the looks it a nice place to get dressed up, though it's not necessary but you might feel under dressed if you show up in a tank top and shots. 

7.  Just sit back enjoy your wine, cheese and meat creating platter and the band.

While we were there The Courtyard Kings jazz band was playing.  When I first heard them play the movie Chocolat (with Juliette Binoche & Johnny Depp) immediately came to mind.  They were amazing and gave the whole experience that special added touch.  I liked them so much I had to buy one of their CD's...not I just need a CD player :(  (check them out at courtyardkings.com)

Quick note on the food:  We ordered the mussels, braised pork shoulder and broccoli barbe.  I have nothing bad to say about the food it was fantastic.  I didn't get to post a picture of the mussels because my husband and I scarfed them down by the time I realized I hadn't snapped one.  The pork shoulder...amazing, tender and lots of it.  The broccoli nice and crispy not overcooked and nicely coated in oil and sauce.

I'm always shocked at how much fresh produce such a small space can carry. I've been able to get my basic fruits and veggies here as well as that more obscure thing I'll need just a little bit of for a recipe. In addition to the amazing selection of fresh fruits, veggies, and herbs, Iovine's also sells containers of nut mixes, candied fruit, and other yummy goodies. Every thing is extremely reasonably priced and there are sometimes even sales on seasonal items (e.g. $1/lb broccoli, local apples, tomatoes on the vine). There are many cash registers so the checkout process is pretty quick even when there's a high volume of customers. Bring your student ID on Wednesday and Sunday for a 10% discount!

You have to know what to expect when going to a place like Biscotti's. While it looks like a restaurant you can't get into without reservations, it's actually more the equivalent of the typical casino cafe that offers a wide range of food options for guests. With that said, it's one of the nicest casino cafe's I've been to!

You immediately notice a more upscale atmosphere when you arrive with the nice decor and well dressed staff there to greet you. The restaurant is large and looks like it can accommodate large groups or the more intimate dining for couples.

There are several different types of entrees and overall I would say they are reasonably priced. Since it's a casino, the drink prices were steep, even for basic beer it was $6 a glass and $3.50 for a soda.

The kids menu was good with several options for $7.95 and the portions were huge (see pictures).

The Monte Cristo sandwich is one of the best I've had and is usually something either I or my wife have to order every time we come here just to make sure we get our fix.

We also ordered the wedge salad to compliment our slightly less healthy entree and it was also large and full of delicious wedge salad ingredients (bacon, avocado, blue cheese, etc)

It was quiet while we were there and our server was very attentive and polite the entire time. Overall a nice dining experience for the family for a reasonable price.

Pro Tip: 20% off for locals with players card and you also get %50 off expresso drinks with Yelp check in!

A fun new (21+ only) board game and beverage parlor, serving beer, wine, tea (coming soon), coffee & sodas. No food, but they said they may allow guests to bring some in (please be mindful of anything that might ruin the games). They had their "soft open" today and things seemed to go pretty smoothly. Several tables had games going less than an hour after they opened. Owner is very nice and personable. Really had an enjoyable time! It is a welcome addition to the Midtown area for those who want something more than pool and darts to enjoy with their adult beverages.

Their full game library isn't set up yet, but there were a bunch of games available to play. I saw Scythe and other "new hotness" there, and they are planning to add a LOT more soon.

A successful Kickstarter campaign resulted in some nice swag for the backers, including custom mugs for those who backed at the "Mug Club" level, along with t-shirts, stickers, and buttons for VIP level (membership cards coming soon). The funds raised will go towards more awesome games for the library!

Parking lot is small, with about 8-9 spots, but there is ample street parking. It's within walking distance of some great Midtown Reno eateries, and is only a block off Virginia St. in its own standalone building (the upper level of the building is still available for rent, so depending on what goes in there, parking may get tight). Several people were sitting outside today, enjoying the beautiful weather, so hopefully that will be a gaming option for the coming summer months.

They do allow people to bring their own games, but ask that people check in when they do, which is understandable.

I'm thrilled that I can now get good wood fired pizza in CWE and that I live about a stone's throw away (so this review is a tad biased). 

I'm going to talk about the pizza first bc that was the main reason why I stopped by. The pizza is good. I kept it simple and ordered the margherita. The crust was the most impressive - Scarlett's oven "imported" from California certainly pays off. It is crispy on the outside and supports the cheese and toppings above. No soggy pizza here - a huge importance to me bc not a lot of pizza places here do it right. Inside, the dough is soft and chewy. Really just an impressive pizza. Not that I lend much credibility (it's freakin Yelp after all) but as a St. Louis transplant from NYC, I'm pretty darn happy!

The menu boasts several specialty pizzas that I expect to try out in the future, including one that has several varieties of mushrooms with truffle oil. 

Scarlett is a wine bar (first and foremost?) - the atmosphere, decor, music are great. It is conducive to conversation and relaxation. It also has a small but diverse beer menu for the beer lovers. On the lighter fare side, it has a boatload of appetizers including pate and a large selection of cheese boards. 

They use iPads as menus which tbh as it stands right now is more of a nuisance than it is helpful. Once they add photos of the food, additional/useful details of the wines, etc., then I can see how it would be really useful. 

I know that I will be back....a lot. 

P.S. They also have a brunch menu

---
July '16 Edit: Now that the fervor has cooled down a little, i will say the following - although I'm happy to have Scarlett's in my neighborhood, it's not an establishment that I would be able to frequent on a regular basis for me (on a monetary basis - insert Bridesmaids "help me, im poor" meme here). Wines and cocktails start at $9+ and the hummus plate and other apps start at $10. Would LOVE to see some happy hour specials - I'll be there!

First and foremost:
The black spaghetti (squid ink spaghetti with clams, shrimp, scallops, and roe) is not just one of the best pasta dishes I've had in St. Louis, but one of the best dishes in St. Louis, period. I love squid ink pastas and I've had my fair share stateside and in Italy. Katie's rendition is perfection in a bite - flavorful, well cooked seafood (scallops were fork tender), zesty from citrus, perfectly cooked al dente pasta, and the kicker is the addition of the roe, which brings a subtle brininess to every bite with an Asian touch (props to this creative addition and it certainly elevated the dish). Get this dish now.

Now, onto the rest of the review:
Katie's is airy, casual, and family friendly - a quintessential neighborhood restaurant with strong repertoire. The pizzas are good, their dough is pillowly and soft, the ingredients are fresh, but I do wish that the crust is just ever so slightly more crispy so the pizza doesn't go "limp" upon picking it up. Needless to say, I do think their pastas are on another level here and I would recommend them over the pizzas as your entree (but hey, share everything). 

They have a full brunch menu on Sundays with choices such as ricotta pancakes and a large selection of toasts.

I'm officially a fan girl.

3.5 stars due to tonkotsu-ness/flavor vs price/value.

Perfecting ramen can take a lifetime. Creating a ramen identity that is unique to a personal brand is even harder. I get it and I appreciate what Nami is trying to do here in STL. 

Onto my meal. I stopped in for lunch on the second day of opening. I ordered the black garlic oil tontoksu; my husband ordered the tsukemen. Our ramen arrived 13 minutes later, which was more swift than expected. Staff was working hard and very friendly. We didn't experience any hiccups that others encountered. My mayu tonkotsu was pretty good - I'm most impressed by the toothiness and firm chew of the noodles - exactly the way I like it. The broth was somewhat lacking in tonkotsu flavor, but it was still tasty. It lacked the extra richness and milkiness of tontoksu broths, so I quickly ran out of broth before I could finish my noodles. This was rare as it is usually opposite for me as ramen broths are usually so rich that I wouldn't be able to finish. The black garlic oil was already mixed into the broth, instead of it spooned on the side of the bowl, so I wasn't able to see just how much as added in. But I definitely tasted the black garlic oil, and it helped elevate the broth. The chashu pork was flavorful and soft, and the egg was very well cooked (yokes were perfect). Overall, I was happy with my ramen, and I see potential for an even better tasting bowl in the future. At $14+ a bowl, I couldn't help to be extra critical, given a less than expected richness to the broth. To be blunt, it just did not taste like a $14 bowl of ramen. One of my fav ramen joints in the NYC/Japan, Ippudo, charges the same price for a life changing bowl of ramen. It was hard to not directly compare the value differential given the same price levels. 

My husband's tsukemen, unfortunately, was a disappointment. Tsukemen is his favorite ramen style, which is served with thick noodles on its own, and dipped into a separate bowl of broth, then slurped. The broth did not go well with the noodles at all. The tsukemen broth should've been even richer and thicker to their standard broth, and neither was the case. The toppings were good but that was all he could compliment on regarding his tsukemen. Tsukemen is a completely different animal in the ramen world and should be treated with the same reverence as the standard styles, and not just be added to the end of the menu board for the heck of it. Maybe this needs to be taken off the menu until the recipe improves significantly? 

I appreciate what Nami is trying to do here and we get it, it'll take time and effort to perfect. Overall, I applaud the efforts put into this long awaited opening. Nami is a good addition here in Stl, as long as it addresses its fixable shortcomings.

The second time I went to this establishment was the last time I will be at this establishment. While the sandwiches are good, the service is terrible. The woman who takes your order, who is also apparently the owner, is awful. 
I went here for the first time about 1 year ago and had a similar experience. I thought I would give it a second chance...my mistake. 
Upon giving my uncomplicated and quick order I was met with blatant rudeness. After giving my card to her she then threw my card across the counter at me.
I am a second generation Renoite and I am proud of and support our small businesses but this woman's treatment of her customers is not worth my time, my money or the sandwiches.
She will never get any further business from me or my friends.  I support local business who care and appreciate their customers.

I didn't have a good experience here. The food was not good. Most of it was overcooked or didn't have any flavor to it. Moreover, some of my food was cold, like they just defrost the food. For a dim sum place the portion were really big. In addition, the menu is misleading. The food we ordered was given to us wrong. Also the owner had a really bad attiude; she overcharged us for items we didn't order and was really mean when we ask her to take off the charges. The staff were okay. We are never coming back here.

If I could give this zero stars I would. We have eaten at a lot of restaurants across NOLA (and the world), and this was one of the worst. We both felt sick after ordering to-go from here, then I spoke with the manager and owner on two separate occasions. They said there was nothing they could do except give us 10% off next time (why would we go back haha), and that it wasn't their food that made us sick. They said we must have sensitive stomachs or drank some bad water. Horrible customer service to follow a terrible meal.

Mas Tacos made me uncomfortable. Is ANYONE who works there Mexican? Didn't seem so, so holy appropriation, Batman.

The food QUALITY was solid, items were fresh. Recipes were simple and decent. Nothing extraordinary. The atmosphere is hipster-y but sorda dirty.

The most problematic part of dinner here was one of the employees in full racist glory, being incredibly rude to a woman of color, and LOUDLY so. 

There are actual authentic Mexican places to eat at in Nashville. Don't throw your money away at a place that exploits a culture and mistreats POC.

This is such an awesome spot. Skee Ball, pinball (I sense a theme here) and arcade games galore. I haven't seen or played any of these games for a long time, so it definitely pulled at my nostalgia heartstrings. On Wednesday, all of the games are free to play! Except Skee Ball, I think.

Also, they serve Ski products, which is fantastic for me, seeing as how I will always choose a delicious craft soda over anything with alcohol in it. Ski AND Skee Ball? I'm sold.

Parking can be an absolute nightmare at rush hour or when there's a Cardinals game at Busch (it's, like, three blocks away from the stadium), so plan accordingly during home games. There's a ping pong table outside, so even the smokers can stay entertained.

Will definitely be coming back, and I'll definitely know where to take my friends when we all want to go out some random evening.

forget the dueling heavy-hitters in the city... if you want a bangin' cheesesteak, hit up dalessandros. those other guys are greasy, bland, and way overrated. this joint totally lives up to the good reviews and popularity, though. 

- get whiz. trust. no, it doesn't make you a tourist. yes, it does make you fall more in love with the cheesesteak. 

- bring cash. yeah, there's an ATM... but don't be that guy. come prepared. 

- come early for the best chance at finding street parking & a smaller line. there may not be mimosas and bloodys, but cheesesteaks make a fab brunch

- there will be a line. deal wit it. 

- bring your out-of-town buds. show them a real cheesesteak. they deserve to know.

roots has quickly become one of my favorite local spots to dine out... great chill vibe, frquently rotating craft beer selection, locally sourced and seasonal ingredients keep the menu interesting. 

everything from the steak frites to the soy ginger salmon to the buffalo chicken sandwich has been fantastic. they had a crab cake app special which was super yummy, and the seared tuna sandwich was unique and delicious. the meatballs in the pasta w/ meatballs dish are crazy tasty (the sauce is on the sweet side, which some folks might not like, but i did).and omg the short rib grilled cheese! chocolate empanda dessert is sinfully sweet, with vanilla ice cream. there honestly hasn't been a dish here that i didn't like. 

the vibe is low-key enough for a relaxing weeknight dinner, but nice enough to bring the in-laws, too. the staff has always been friendly and welcoming (and patient and inforative, since i can never seem to make up my mind about what i want to eat and need suggestions!)

i can't wait to dine outside on the patio once the weather improves a bit, and i'm also hoping to venture over for brunch one of these days (did someone say bloody mary bar?)

anything you want, amy's omelette house has got it... the true definition of 'have it your way'!

200+ omelettes (and the choice of creating your own if any of the listed combos aren't good enough), pancakes, french toast, non-omlette eggs, hash browns, fruit parfaits, lunch options, dinners, salads, a kids menu, desserts... 
you'll find something for everyone. 
and best of all, it won't break the bank. they even have weekly specials where kids eat free, etc.
and you'll have leftovers.

my favorite part: you can make just about any substitution you want (many for free), so you can totally customize your breakfast. don't want home fries with your omelette? swap em out for a fruit cup (good fruit- not just melon and pineapple!), or some pancakes. or french toast. or a yogurt parfait. or load up those home fries with bacon and cheese. or have your side of home fries (which are amazingly seasoned and fried up with lots of onions), and add 1 pancake to your meal (cuz what is breakfast without a pancake?!). want to sub turkey bacon in your bfast? do it. want to switch ingredients in an omelette? do that too. you really really can have it your way. 

expect your service to be a bit unpolished... this is a jersey diner after all. 
expect a gigantic menu with hundreds of options... this is a jersey diner after all.
expect heaping portions and boxing up leftovers... this is a jersey diner after all. 
expect sticky tables and mediocre-but-quickly-refilled coffee... this is a jersey diner after all.
expect to get a ton of food for not-a-ton of money... this is a jersey diner after all.

I ordered on Uber Eats so I can't speak to the look of the restaurant but the food is excellent! I am so glad I didn't wait for covid to pass before ordering and I will definitely order lunch for work from here again. I had the medium size mushroom soup w side of bread, smoked salmon blinchiki and farmers cheese blinchiki with raspberry jam. It was plenty for me and to share with friends. The soup was excellent, nice and peppery and the fresh dill on the salmon blinchiki was a nice touch. Love their packaging choice, sustainable and secure as well as a nice presentation. A+

I've only been to the Row once, and I went to sit at the bar and order a beer...just to get a feel for the place. The bartenders were friendly and the ambiance was chill with a hint of "I'm here to pick up anyone who will talk to  me". I don't know if I'd go back to hang out at the bar, but I might try the food next time.

The only thing that is consistent with the "PYT" experience is the service.  While I've given this famed establishment several chances, I just can't get over the waits and the disinterested staff.  The special burgers are pretty good, but can't justify the inevitable frustration with the overall experience.

There's not one bad thing, I could possible say about Guido's....
Whether you order tapas, pasta or pizza, everything will be homemade and delicious and the service will be too notch.

First, they have family deals that are just amazing. For $25 you can get 2 orders of pasta, garlic cheese bread and a large house salad or a pizza, toasted ravs & salad. Portions are large and everything is so unbelievably fresh!
Second, they offer free delivery within a 3 mile radius, so you don't have to use a 3rd party delivery service and can support the employee delivering. 
Third, they deliver or offer 1/2 gallons of Sangria to go - OMG. 
They are doing a wonderful job of social distancing and appropriate precautions with indoor dining, to make everyone's experience (dine in, delivery or carry out), exceptional.
Take advantage of the free delivery and fantastic specials from this fabulous, family owned, small business!

Thank you to all the lovely folks at Convivo who made our last meal in California so special. With apologies to Dr. Maya Angelou here: I may forget what we ate and drank, but I will not forget how this experience made me feel. 

I made a reservation for an early dinner, ahead of a very early flight with little ones the next morning. Uber had other ideas, and I ended up being 40 minutes late for our reservation. I called to tell them, and they said to come on! When we arrived, they were gracious, and placed us at a beautiful table, even though I would have understood if they had stuck us in the corner by the kitchen. 

We loved our patio dining, our beautiful surroundings (bougainvillea everywhere) and the menu was fantastic. Our servers (one veteran, one trainee) took great care of us, and were sweet to our kids, who were hungry and road weary after the drive from Pismo, yet another hotel check-in (this time near the airport) and the long wait for the Uber driver. The kids pizzas were a big hit with my kiddos, and my husband and I both loved what we ordered - especially the salad with the roasted chickpeas, which I now must learn how to make! 

We never felt rushed, and we were never made to feel like they needed our table, even though they very well may have, given how late we arrived. They made us all feel so welcome and so well taken care of. 

We left feeling refreshed enough to walk along the beach up to state street and for a long stroll, a little shopping, and more wine. I hadn't really expected that, since we were so tired when we arrived. But it provided exactly what we needed to get that last little boost of vacay mojo. 

To everyone at Convivio, from the hostess who told us to come on, to the servers and the kitchen staff, thank you for your hospitality!

This place is adorable! The staff is so friendly and it is a great place to have an afternoon drink or meet with friends after work. City winery also has some amazinf  music line ups which I think is such a great use of the space as well. They have a great array of wines on tap which are fun to try with the flight options. I will surely be back again!

Really fast service. Great amount sand which for what you pay for. I my self enjoyed Cuban. And receiving it fast on hungry lunch hour. Yes great fast service. Big portions. Kind like jimmy well jimmY is still rapid fast. But this deli has selection and portions. Think I even took break between half sandwiches.

Because I can't leave zero stars: I was on my way to eat at The Grill based on Yelp reviews.  I lucked out that it closes at 4:00pm because through the windows I saw no less than 6 rats running around the kitchen. I understand that restaurants might have to deal with rodents from time to time but this is beyond disgusting.

We figured that on another beautiful Santa Barbara day we should be eating on the waterfront, and after hearing so much about Flor de Maiz we figured we just had to finally experience it.

Both the bar area and outside dining areas were pretty busy, so we walked up and wanted to get our names on the wait list. As luck would have it a table opened up right away on the patio . . . which was perfect.

Our server Aldo greeted us and got everything started pretty quickly. Both the Margarita Guadalajara and Margarita Picosa were our top picks, and were both delicious.

Aldo was very helpful some food suggestions, and got us started right away with the chips and guacamole, and Ceviche de Pulpo. Next up was the Enchiladas Oaxaca and Tacos de Pulpo Guajillo. 

The many flavors of the food and the zesty Margaritas were all delicious. And with so many more things on the menu we are looking forward to another visit soon.

Such a perfect spot on Cabrillo Blvd, and located between SB Fishouse, Oku, and Blue Water Grill. Valet parking behind the restaurant was also a plus.

The wait might be long (take a newspaper or the latest gossip magazine), but it's worth it. The most authentic Mexican Food I've ever tasted, comparable to a lot of the food we've enjoyed in Mexico. Also a fun place to take friends who've never had a true Santa Barbara experience. Friends always ask me which dish I most recommend, and that is difficult since everything we've tried is delicious.

MA

With all the recent COVID dining restrictions in Goleta and Santa Barbara, it's nice to have Ca' Dario Goleta offering their delicious menu and comfortable patio seating.

This year we wanted to make our Thanksgiving meal as special as possible, and knew that location, location, location was important. Their patio area was warm and inviting, and our server Michael took very good care of us. We all chose the special Thanksgiving Meal, and they did a great job on making sure it was traditional and delicious. We also complimented our meal with several of their Italian specialty appetizers. 

And as usual their wine selection is stellar. Thanks again Michael for making some spot-on wine suggestions. 

We're hoping that the outdoor seating service is offered throughout the end of this year, and are anticipating that Ca' Dario will have a special Christmas menu.

Ah yes, total Comfort Food with a wide selection of local and delicious craft beers. 

Or as they say, a fabulous [gas-troh-pub].

Finney's has set up a nice outdoor space, and even with it being a cooler evening, the tower heaters were on full blaze and kept us warm and toasty.

Special thanks to server Paige who took very good care of us, and made some stellar recommendations for both food and beers. She also joined us in our "name that tune" game/evening, as the turntable was spinning.

We stuck to the Starters & Snacks portion of the menu, with some delicious results. #1 - Crispy Coconut Shrimp, #2 - Yuzy Hot Wings, #3 - Chicken and Waffle Bites, and a nice side of french fries to compliment each.

Also nice that they are conveniently located on the border of the SB Funk Zone on lower State Street, across the street from the Hotel Californian, and within crawling distance of Stearns Wharf.

As a long-time resident of Santa Barbara I thought I had experienced most hidden gems for food and beer, but after seeing the impressive article about The Brewhouse in the SB NewsPress, we realized we hadn't been there yet, so we high-tailed it over for their Happy Hour and dinner.

Most my friends know that I am a Stroganoff-kinda-they/them, and having tasted it at other restaurants in SB and Goleta, their Beef Stroganoff with Filet Mignon is now my new favorite. Wild mushrooms and onions, and served over fettuccine noodles . . . simply delicious. My dining companion had the Pork Chop, and they/them swore that it's the best one they/them have had in a long time. Also have to note that their Fish and Chips are really good.

Serves Dan and Harmony always make sure we have everything we needed throughout our visits, and were spot-on with their suggestions.

And of course being there for their Happy Hour we just had to try some of the many appetizer choices. Too numerous to name here, but there was something delicious for everyone (my favorite being their calamari, prawns, and fire roasted artichoke). We would have tried the other choices but was committed to leaving room for that Stroganoff.

And also thoroughly enjoyed their beer selections. IPA's, Wheat Ales, and that Porter they have were all delicious.

Conveniently located on Montecito Street between Castillo and the Morton Bay Fig tree, and next to The Neighborhood Sports Bar.

Growing up in Santa Barbara, with regular trips down to So Cal, Santa Claus Lane off of Hwy 101 in Carpinteria was always a necessary stop for food and visits to the old Santa Claus Village area. Now with all the changes it's nice to have Thario's Kitchen there as a stop for good food either heading south during lunch time. Or dinner on the way back to SB.

Their lunch specials are always good. Fresh salads, pastas and pizza. And perfect for both adult and kid-friendly appetites.

A fun and delicious pit-stop along 101.

We've always enjoyed the wines and hospitality at Jamie Slone, and now that they are reopened for tasting on their outside patio area, we're excited to once again be there in the El Paseo with Jamie, Kym, Julianne, Tommy, Jake . . . and Sophie.

Always enjoy their wide variety of Red Blends, with their Lozier (GSM Blend) leading the way. Usually hard to pick a favorite, but the BoRific, P1, Apex and Super Tuscan are also rich and delicious. And don't forget to taste their Pinot Noir.

In their world of white wines, our favorite being the Mrs. B (Grenache Blanc), with their Chardonnay, Sauv Blanc, Albarino also tasting wonderfully. We're also anticipating the release of their Rose of Grenache . . . always delicious

.

Fiesta in Santa Barbara is always pretty festive, and we discovered that LAMR&TO in Montecito was the perfect place to be on the final night.

Along with the delicious Mexican dishes and Spicy Margaritas, they had an incredible Mariachi Band serenading us all. We even got in a couple song requests which they sang wonderfully.

And even with it being a busy evening, our server Melissa kept on-top of everything, made some spot-on food suggestions, and made sure the evening went along smoothly.

We will definitely have this on our go-to list year-round, and for next year's SB Fiesta event.

So many favorites on their menu, but top choices are the Mama's Hand Wrapped Pot Stickers, Green Papaya Salad, and they have a noodle dish for everyone's taste preferences. My all time favorite has been the Hangover Noodle. Which have flavors that encompass all your senses. 

They also have a very good wine and beer list. And there is nothing better than those amazing Gourmet Noodle dishes with a nice glass of Prosecco, flavorful Rose, or that local brewer Draughtsmen's Japanese Lager.

Conveniently located in the Public Market, directly behind the Arlington Theater.

While visiting or working in the SB Funk Zone, or preparing for a fun ocean-side picnic, Metropulos Fine Foods has always been a sure bet for delicious food and drink, and always served with a smile by their friendly staff.

And now with the on-going virus crisis, Metropulos Fine Foods continues to feed us all with special pre-made meals, and with special pick up hours of Monday through Saturday, 10 am to 4 pm, all to-go, and all delicious.

Today their selections of meatloaf, pastas, and fresh salads, were much appreciated as we ventured through the deserted Funk Zone.

It's also been fun to keep in touch through Instagram. They are good at posting regularly to keep us hungry people informed and to let us know what's happening in their kitchen. 

Remember to support local businesses, especially ones like Metropulos Fine Foods who really care about our community.

Authentic and delicious Mexican dishes right here next to the new Goleta Target. Small and intimate, Pollofino offers everything from ribs, tri-tip, fajitas, and tasty soft tacos. Also a nice salsa bar to compliment everything. 

Quick and easy for lunch.

During these crazy pandemic times we high-tailed it to Montecito to check out Coast Village Road, and found that Lucky's Steakhouse is well prepared with outside dining and are following all the recent pandemic guidelines.

On another beautiful SB night we got a nice table outside, and were greeted by our server "Five-0," who took very good care of us. He made numerous suggestions that were spot-on. Starting with cocktails and a delicious French Rose, we then moved on to appetizers of Gianni's Escargot, and Giant Shrimp Cocktail. "Five-0" was then very helpful with his suggestions of Steak and sides. We thoroughly enjoyed the Bone-In Rib Chop, accompanied by Hash Brown Potatoes with Gruyere Cheese, and Snap Peas. 

And just when we thought things couldn't get any better, "Five-0" brought over The Salty Turtle Sundae . . . delicious!

Conveniently located on Coast Village Road, in-between Montecito Inn and The Honor Bar, and across the street from Los Arroyos and the Folded Hills Tasting Room.

In a town that closes down fairly early midweek it's nice to have SB&K for late night vittles.

And right in the middle of the Funk Zone, it's always fun to be amongst party-people who are out having a fun time. Right across the street from Test Pilot, and around the corner from Figueroa Mountain Brewery.

The inside bar area was a buzz of activity, and we headed out to their outside patio area for a nice table. Under the stars and with heaters full blast, it was pretty comfy cozy as the night went on.

Server Hilary was very helpful with recommendations for both drinks and food items, and got us started with the oh-so-tasty Westside Gin Cocktails. And then with all the possible food choices, she recommended the Beef Sliders, Mac Daddy (incredibly delicious), and Chicken Bites. 

Still so much on the menu to try, and looking forward to being there for their Happy Hour. Nice to have SB&K as an option for late night dining. Thanks again Hilary for taking such good care of us.

After experiencing Buena Onda Empanadas at Old Town Coffee in Goleta, I just knew I had to go to their Mother Ship location on Haley Street. And so happy that we did. Also happy to support this amazing Latinx-owned business.

Their handcrafted Empanadas are incredibly delicious, and with so many different tastes available. I am a total carnivore and am loving their vegetarian/vegan selections. 

The fun part is that with every visit there is something new to taste, and you can never go wrong. Starting the day with their Buen Dia (breakfast empanada) is perfect. Then at lunch their Carne, Serrano, Hongos, and a new favorite the Hakuna Batata. Their special Combos is always a nice choice too. 

And of course no visit is complete without their desserts of either Tia Lupe Apple Pie and/or Tarta de Coco.

It's been four years since I moved back to Santa Barbara, and Cristino's was one of my first reviews. Cristino and his wife Lorena had just opened his bakery/restaurant and I had the privilege of being one of his first regulars.

And now congratulations to Cristino and his staff for staying committed to our community and serving up some of the most delicious Mexican foods and bakery goods. Their menu of regular items and weekly specials has been consistent even through these crazy COVID times.

I have been a regular fan of their assorted burritos, with their Burrito a la Mexicana being my favorite. They now they have been featuring their Birria with Consume and all the fixings, and fresh Tamales each day. The Tamales do sell out regularly so I recommend getting there early for them. And Sundays have been made extra special with their delicious Menudo.

Chances are you'll notice where they are by the line of people waiting to place orders. Don't be afraid, the wait is usually quick as Cristino and staff are there to keep things moving along nicely.

Their small unassuming space is tucked behind several businesses, at the stoplights at Hollister Avenue and then right or left on to Aero Camino. First driveway on your right.

They now serve a delicious Lunch Buffet daily, 11:30 am to 2:30 pm. A nice way to experience a wide variety of the Indian specialties. And thank you Jaela for being such a wonderful and helpful server.  Looks like we now have another lunch spot in beautiful Goleta.

I want to start off this review by saying that I loved, loved LOVED the food. It was amazing and everything I hoped it would be. I got the vegetarian $25 course menu but swapped the main course with the raw one.
It had:
-homemade garlic hummus to start with carrot sticks and jicama
-hot butternut soup of some sort with two croutons
-watermelon mint juice (simply amazing)
-a salad with orange slices and pomegranate seeds, among other things, served with apple/carrot blend of juice
-main course of raw thinly sliced squash with a pesto blend in between each slice, atop a layer of apples
-and for dessert, a banana cake drizzled with chocolate that was probably the best banana cake I've ever had.

That being said, I am docking two stars for the service. I know this will be a bit controversial since this place has nothing but 5-star reviews. 

According to what I see here, our waitresses are also the owners of this restaurant.  While I totally respect that it must be hard to run a business and be a server at the same time, the person who served us was - how do I put this? - totally unsociable and disagreeable, albeit knowledgeable. 

Let me explain. My mom and I went there with two livingsocial vouchers, one that was mine and one that was hers. What we didn't notice at the time was that in the fine print, it said that only one can be used per table. When I told the owner that we had vouchers, she said, "Sorry, did I hear you say voucherS?" and when I said that yes, we had two, she said, "You will ONLY be using one. You will have to come back to use the other one." But she said it in quite possibly the curtest and brusquest manner I've ever encountered, as though the discussion was over, the case was closed, and we were rather stupid to assume that we'd ever be able to use two vouchers at once. It was the tone of voice as if she was talking to a small child, actually. I tried to brush it off, since i figured that it really was our fault for not looking at the fine print, but it was disappointing nonetheless, and I didn't like the attitude she had about it.

Throughout the meal, we had decent service...nothing special as we had to wait a few times for water refills, etc. It was okay.

But my real complaint, and what prompted the review, was the fact that we got pressured into tipping a lot.  And it wasn't just us, the couple sitting behind us used a coupon as well, and I heard her give them the same spiel.  I HATE being pressured to tip more. Disclaimer: I always tip on the pre-discounted amount, and I usually give a good tip according to the service received. 

So anyway. The lady brought over what appeared to be a phone that the total was entered into, and said, "Enter a tip here. Unfortunately, it calculates the tip based on the couponed amount and not the full amount, so make sure to figure out what the pre-discounted amount would be and tip on that." Uh, what? I'm sorry, but we are not required to tip on the pre-discounted amount. Like I said, I normally do, but the fact that she brought it up and basically bossed us into it rubbed me the wrong way, so we actually ended up tipping on the discounted amount. Seeing the amount we entered (which, talk about awkward, I don't like that she's hovering around you as you tip!) she said, with obvious anger, "Oh, well if I had KNOWN you weren't going to tip on the full total, I would have just entered it the other way." Who says that?! I guess it's hard to communicate a tone of voice over a review from the internet, but trust me, it was snotty.  It was a bad way to end the meal, to say the least, and kind of confirmed that we did the right thing by tipping a little less.
