Anyone who has that kind of entitled attitude when it comes to tipping is someone that needs a reality check. :/ I don't owe anyone a fabulous tip, they have to earn it. Maybe I'm alone in this, but that is the reason for my 3-star review. I was uncomfortable with this and probably wouldn't return to The Tasteful Kitchen if it weren't for the fact that I have another voucher. I will enjoy the food, for sure, but I can't say I'm looking forward to encountering the service for a second time.

The freaking cutest place ever! I love this gem! Amazing staff and cute setup! I went right before the shutdown of the world and I look forward to going back after everything starts to reopen! 

My gf had her birthday party here with some of her favorite gals and they were very accommodating and assertive. The food was absolutely delicious and the wine was mega yummy too. I highly recommend just getting a bottle and everyone at the table ordering stuff and making one huge board!

I will not support any establishment that doesn't respect me as a patron and feels that they can take pictures of me in their establishment and post it on social media or for their own editorial purpose.  

"Teachers at local sports betting establishment for lunch inquiring about drink specials. Cause nothing says in it for the children like a vodka and a few wagers right? "

I'm going to preface this by saying that I used to love Nachomamas. That's the only reason I'm even giving this 2 stars instead of one. It's a small joint, but I always got my food quickly even during busy times. I can always appreciate a place with a drive thru as well. The fajita tacos were a staple in my diet; I often found myself craving them. The salsas packed a good amount of heat while still maintaining great flavor. In addition, they serve jaritos, my favorite Mexican soda. 

Unfortunately, my most recent trip to this establishment will be my last. I ordered food to go for my mom and I; we live about ten minutes away and it was raining that day. I ordered two tamales and a fajita taco platter with no cabbage. After the cashier told me my total, I asked to add an additional fajita taco with no cabbage. He even read my order back to me correctly. I got my food and went home. When I took my order out, I quickly noticed something was off. The two tamales were each in their own boxes, and two fajita tacos were in a brown bag. I called back and told the manager I was missing a taco and the rest of my platter. He explained to me that the order was rung up wrong, and that they couldn't give me what I didn't pay for. I was peeved, but was not going to drive all the way back to buy more food. So I set about eating my tacos, only to realize that the tacos were made with cabbage and no onion. I called back again, and the manager said there was nothing he could do. "My boss would kill me if I just gave out two free tacos." He argued that there was simply nothing he could do. Now, I've worked in food service for over 5 years and NEVER IN MY LIFE have I heard of food cost being so high that they could not spare two tacos after THEY screwed up. Finally, after having MY MOM call back he agreed (begrudgingly) to give me two free tacos next time I came in.

It is far, far too late. They have lost a loyal customer, simply by having abhorrent customer service. A local business should pride themselves on customer service, whether it's to a 22 year old or a 60 year old. I will not be coming back, and I will urge all of my friends and family to go elsewhere from now on.
I had bacon and brocoli cheesesteak here with my girfriend and it was amazing. Definitely going to come back to this place again for some cheesesteak or try something new.

Ok, so yes I'm giving it 5 stars.  And before people panic, yes it's expensive, yes the restaurant is sandy, yes it will take a while for your server  to get to you but it's all part of the charm. 

This is my go to beach spot living in DTSP.  They do all the work of 'beach visiting' for you.  They have the chairs, the umbrellas, the BEER, and the food!   There's no need to spend 30 mins finding your cooler, finding your beach tent, loading chairs in your car, parking etc... With Caddys you just arrive and go!  Be sure and bring a tip for the nice young men who set up your chairs and umbrellas.  Also, parking is $5. but hey beats feeding a meter all day.  

So far everything I've tried on their menu I've enjoyed.  But by far the best is the fried grouper fingers.  Get them, you wont be disappointed.  

just remember, yes this place has a mark up, MY GOD YOU'RE ON THE FREAKING BEACH and sit back, sip and enjoy.

I remember this spot in New Hope since I was a little girl. My parents and I would drive from Brooklyn to spend the day in "haunted" New Hope. It was one of my favorite places to go.
This building was there at the time and housed a little restaurant. I always wanted to eat there because it looked mysterious and enchanted.
I haven't eaten there since... until today.

NH is a very different place since the late 60's and 70's. And I can't say that I really like the transformation. F and I have been to the area many times but today we went to Nektar. 
They did a nice job renovating the existing structure. You will feel like you are sitting in a really comfortable treehouse. 
I would imagine on a beautiful weekend this place is packed but, today a rainy week day, we had the place to ourselves. 
F did a delicious draft Stout, like coffee malted. I did the rose flight. 3/3 oz. pours for $24. I thought a little pricey. They were all different and very good.
For food, F had duck foie gras, pheasant pate, and French prosciutto.
I had the burger.
The food was very good. The service was steller. But, I just felt the prices were a little high for what you are getting.

I would definitely give it another try, maybe just for cocktails.

This was a nice surprise.
F and I were hankering for Asian food, but our first choice was not at all what we had in mind. So what now... Yelpers to the rescue!
What was close? We were damp and starving, and what was open? Golden Triangle 4.5 stars and basically a block away.
Don't let first glance fool you. This is not a run of the mill Chinese place. The food is Malaysian, Thai and Burmese.
As we walked in we saw every table was taken but one...Yay! And the smell of some yummies...
This is nothing fancy but the service and the prices are great. 
The food was wonderful. Appetizers of steamed dumplings with ginger vinegar dipping sauce, and Roti Canai with magical dipping sauce were a great start.
F had pineapple chicken fried rice and I had Rendang (I think I messed up the spelling).
Both were bursting with flavor and exactly what we wanted.
I want to go back right now!

I have been wanting to try this piano bar for such a long time. This year we were in an apartment right up the block. On a Thursday night before meeting friends for Christmas dinner, F and I stopped in for a cocktail. The scene was totally relaxed and cozy. CJ Steinway was playing a variety of tunes. Christmas, show tunes, etc. We absolutely loved it. So much so, we came back later and sat at the piano. It seems everyone knows each other, but we didn't feel left out. 

We came back on Friday night, but it was a different vibe...much more crowded (which is expected for a Friday night) and there was club music playing over the piano...

So, we will DEFINITELY be back, but not on a Friday or Saturday night.

We wanted a place close to the Christian St Y and to nearby friends. Los Camardas was suggested... yes!
On a hot, muggy night all you really want is a cool refreshing cocktail. The special blackberry margarita was exactly what the doctor ordered.
Coupled with the short rib enchiladas. Perfect.
The service was prompt for a busy Wednesday night, but nobody came back to check on us. I definitely could have gone for another margarita...alas it was not to be. 
Our food came and we devoured it. But I even had enough to take home for lunch.
I'm dreaming about those margaritas right now...

I have been wanting to give Jamonera a try for a while. So when friends suggested it after seeing Creed ll. I was up for it. We were going to dine here but we didn't realize what a popular night Thanksgiving Eve was for eating out. 
We didn't have a reservation and every table was spoken for, but the hospitable host went out of his way to try to accommodate our party of four. We sat at the bar and ordered drinks and apps. Everything was really good. From wine, beer and cocktails to food. The barman was really helpful and friendly.
I liked the looks of the room. A wonderful, warm spot for a cold winter night.
We ended up moving on, but I look forward to having a full meal here someday soon.

This is our go to place for storage, curtains, seasonal items, bath mats, lighting...and cool thingys. F and I usually come here first and check out all the interesting decor. This is where we get ideas. We recently purchased the Pax closet system... I absolutely love it. It has totally reorganized my bedroom. We also were able to add on as we needed.
The service has always been helpful and friendly, too.

WOW! What a wonderful experience. 
I took F here for his birthday surprise. He was so excited when I told him where we were going, and The Victor Cafe did not disappoint.
From the confirmation phone call from Sandy, the owners daughter, to the last moments of the evening...everything was special. 
Talking to Sandy, I really got the sense of the history, love and pride this family takes in their restaurant. 
As soon as we walked in the lovely hostess Elena, greeted us warmly and invited us to have a seat because a song was about to start. What an entrance! 
Every server is a trained opera singer and they each take turns. Every one was beautiful. 
It's not in any way corny or tacky. It's is truly a class act.
And of course there is the Rocky connection, which was why I chose The Victor Cafe for F.
He was in heaven.
The food also measures up to the surroundings. 
The service is stellar.
We definitely will be back.
Thank you The Victor Cafe!

Our fifth year doing the Brazilian Steakhouse.
And I think the best.
This year we decided to do lunch so we could spend the rest of the day exploring Philadelphia. 
We arrived at 1pm and we're greeted warmly and seated immediately. The service was wonderful. Steak kept appearing whenever we wanted it, water glasses were promptly refilled, dirty plates removed.
I love all their cuts of steak, especially the Fogo specialty. But I have to say I could have been perfectly happy just having the salad bar. Soup, cheese, cured meats, salmon, fresh vedge...
Everything was great. I don't know if I can wait a whole year to go back!

Three of us came here really hungry. F wanted all-you-can-eat, but alas they don't offer that.
No matter, we ordered various rolls and hot tea.
Everything tasted fresh and was well made. 
The decor is dark, modern and clean.
The service was very prompt and friendly. At noon Sumo was pretty empty, but more people arrived as we were leaving.
This is a nice, serviceable, local sushi place.
PS They made a delicious coffee frappe for us to go.

McGurk's is not just a pub, a restaurant, or a great Irish place. McGurk's is an experience.

In my my opinion, McGurk's is the very best bar in all of St. Louis. Why you ask? Because it has everything a bar needs in one place, and does it well.

- Live Music: The bands that play here are always phenomenal, and each has their own unique twist on Irish music. You can't help but want to stomp your feet or sing along.
- Patio: My God, this patio goes on forever. Complete with small gardens, fountains, and tables to post up at. It's great on a beautiful summer evening, or even in the winter, because they do a great job enclosing the patio so you can still enjoy it.
- Great bartenders: They work quick, and keep it lively. It also helps that there are more than a few different bar sections throughout the place, so your wait is never too long.
- Good/cheap drinks: The selection is excellent, as an Irish place should be, and I'm always pleasantly surprised by my bar tab at the end of the night.
- Great clientele: As a transplant, I've come to find that St. Louis isn't always the most friendly city right off the bat, but the crowd at McGurk's is one exception. I've never made it through the evening without making a few new friends.

What can I say, I love this place. When someone visits me from out of town, this is the first place I take them, and it becomes their fast favorite as well.

We were refused service due to having our two children with us, which was a first for me.  I was doubly surprised since one of the pictures I saw on Yelp before driving here showed a young kid with the caption "Even kids love Sparky!". I suppose that Sparky doesn't feel the same way about kids.

Our children are well behaved and have dined at much more upscale restaurants than this one.  Needless to say, we won't be back.

Great experience at the preview tonight with my mentor S!

Service was a bit slow but we expected there to be some kinks for them to work out, and they comped a round of drinks even though we were enjoying our conversation and didn't complain.

The bread service was biscuits with bacon butter and honey butter. The honey butter was very aromatic but neither S nor I could really taste the bacon in the bacon butter.

We started out with the conch croquettes and pig ears. Very generous portion of pig ears! The croquettes were good but we felt we could've used some more of the conch flavor and less cheese.

Next we had the shrimp and tuna tartar. The shrimp required some work as they were served shell-on, but was definitely worth it. Very nice flavor and well cooked. The tuna was very nice as well. It was served with plantain chips, which were slightly spicy, and the spice went great with the tuna.

For our main course, we got the curried goat and the pasta with crawfish. Our sides were potatoes and semolina gnocchi with corn. S lived in the Cayman Islands for quite a few years and she approved of the flavor in the curried goat. The meat was so tender it was ridiculous. The pasta was light, not swimming in a creamy sauce. The noodles made me think of yakisoba. The corn and gnocchi was very good. Potatoes were also well cooked but we were so starched out by that point.

I probably could've stopped eating there but we still has dessert. One look at the menu and you know I had to indulge. We ordered the horchata panna cotta and the banana/chocolate/hazelnut zeppole. The panna cotta was served with melon ice cream, which was perfect, and the zeppole was amazing. Probably my favorite thing from the meal, although there were many heavyweights throughout!

I mentioned the service being slow, but other than that, we felt very welcome and all of our needs were met. The server was great, and we even got to meet Nina and Larry!

Also, those cute little cast-iron skillets!

I'm excited to see this place do well. I'll be back to try more things!

I like Boswell's. I went for the first time a couple of weeks ago, and before I even arrived at the restaurant, I was starting to worry about what to get from the menu, because I wanted everything. But when I got there, there was a buffet! Problem solved.

Both my friend M and I enjoyed the buffet. I did not need seconds, but I had to have some more. When I was returning to my table with a less-than-full plate, someone at another table told me I should eat more. I wished I could. Lol. The price was very reasonable as well, at slightly over $10. 

Having read the reviews, I would like to try items from the menu as well. Maybe that's what I'll do next time! :)

I LOVE Marjie's Grill. First, I walked in and the place smelled amazing. And when I tasted the food, I was still just as impressed. My friend L and I ordered a bunch of stuff that I can't remember anymore, but everything was very tasty. If they are serving grilled sweet potatoes, get them. I also really loved the pork knuckles. 

Do yourself and favor and eat here!

Here in the Midwest, it seems that a good tamal is elusive in the wild. You often hear rumors of such, only to be disappointed when you've managed to track one down. That was not the case for me during my first visit to Tlaolli.

We were greeted by several smiling faces as soon as we walked in on a sunny afternoon for a late lunch. It's a small, but pleasant joint and it looked very well kept. For some reason, I can't seem to recall what was in this building previously... There is a small bar along a wall & a table behind the building, so seating is a bit limited, but I enjoy those types of cozy hole-in-the-wall places.

They offered a daily special, which I can't seem to recall at the moment, but I was there for tamales. As it was my first time in, I was given a succinct run-down of their story, including the fact that the tamales are made with olive oil rather than the traditional lard, as well as the two options of the day -- chicken and cheese & poblano. Yes, please.

We ordered three of both choices plus a large salsa verde for the two of us and grabbed two sodas from the self-serve cooler. I'm thinking the total was about $25, which seemed more than fair to me for the amount.

Man, those were some good tamales. I literally said, "This is exactly what I needed today" as we ate. I really enjoyed the chicken tamal, completely covered in their salsa verde, but then I tried the cheese tamale and was extremely pleased. The texture was perfect, the ratio of filling to masa was ideal, and the filling itself was awesome. No shady ingredients and these things really tasted homemade -- especially in comparison to the bought-in options at other places around town.

I also feel obligated to specifically point out how much I enjoyed the salsa verde. So many other places treat salsa as either an afterthought or a tool used to disguise sub par dishes, but that was not the case here. Great, fresh flavors and a nice consistency... I could see myself putting this on just about everything. 

tl;dr: Cute place with great tamales made with olive oil and awesome fresh homemade salsas.

Let's get this out of the way, no matter what they claim, Parx is not a "Las Vegas style casino," heck it's not even close to an Atlantic City style casino. Parx is basically a nice big room jam-packed with slots, and some tables located in the suburbia of the Philadelphia area, that's it. I would venture to say that the vast majority of the clientele are locals in the area who don't want to make the journey to Atlantic City. So many factors about Parx really make it not an appealing casino. This place isn't designed to attract people from out of town, but rather people who live in the area to gamble rather than travel two hours aways. The smoke is another factor. Oh my, I felt like I walked into certain areas and I was developing pre-mature lung cancer, it's that bad. Parx is also not the full package, and by that I mean there isn't entertainment or a major eating establishment, it's just all gambling. They don't even have many tables, and the ones they don't have any lower stake bets ($20 minimum bet is what most tables are here).

What elevates this casino for now is it is decently nice inside, and mostly clean (not including the smoke). I wouldn't say the place is a sight to see, but it appears to be relatively hip and trendy compared to other locations with slots. While it still appeals to an older crowd, the actual look of the place says something very different. Every Thursday they have a free blackjack tournament, and while you only get to play 10 hands, it is free and an opportunity to win something from nothing. If your looking to strictly gamble, and that is literally the only thing that matters, Parx is an acceptable place to do that. If want an experience or something else, I recommend making the two hour trek to Atlantic City, it's worth the travel time to not have to come to Parx.

Had the Korean BBQ Cheesesteak and Thai Chili Wings while my wife had a Turkey hoagie and Buffalo wings. The food was phenomenal, and the Korean BBQ Cheesesteak is unlike other cheesesteaks I've had. Portion sizes are great too. Lee's Deli is a highlight for West Philly for some great food and great service!

Relish is a soul food restaurant located in the West Oak Lane section of Philly.
I've been there many times and felt it was time to give them a review.
This is one place I really miss since everything has shut down.  I was more than excited when I got a email saying they were going to start having take out Thurs -Sun.

I ordered through Grubhub with no problem. 
We got 2 platters, Turkey wings ( 2 big ones), that came with sweet potato mash & collard greens & cabbage mixed. The 2nd one, Smoked bbq Brisket with the same sides. The Turkey wings were fall off the bone good and enough for another meal. The brisket was tender and a generous portion. They could have put a little more greens and cabbage on the platter though!
I loved the sweet potato mash as well. We also got a pan of honey butter cornbread,  which I feel they are famous for. So good! Sweet and buttery with kernels of corn in it! Forgot to mention the appetizer...... Honey Hot Wings! So gooood! Only complaint,  not enough for the price. You only get 6 :( for $12.95. But still very good!
My food came on time, still hot too!
We really enjoyed everything and ate on it for another meal!
Relish is a upscale, black owned and operated soul food restaurant that normally (when they open back up) is a very nice sit down restaurant.  They have live entertainment, Jazz, karaoke nights, nice bar and all you can eat breakfast and dinner buffets on the weekends. 
I would highly recommend Relish!

Wow! Such a great experience! 
A nice Italian restaurant, filled with history, delicious food, great service. and entertainment.  What more can you ask for!!!

As you can see, I really enjoyed myself  :)

My family took me to Victor's Cafe for my birthday and it really was a lovely present. 
I have never been here before so wasn't exactly sure what to expect. 
The waitress was well informed, pleasant and patient with me trying to figure it all out.
Our drinks and appetizers came out pretty fast. Decided on a Arugula Salad and Burrata. Everything was so fresh! My husband can't get away from the beef and got Filet Mignon which he said was tender and delicious.  I got Dido & Aeneas w/angel hair pasta & sauteed spinach and warm chocolate cake and vanilla ice cream for dessert. It was delicious!
The best part was the performances.  All the waiters were trained opera singers and about every 20 minutes they rang a bell , tell us a short tale of the song they were about to sing. Then belted out a great operatic tune.  
They surprised me by singing happy birthday which was the greatest performance of the night. It took my breath away. Once you get it sung to you like that you're changed forever!
Unfortunately we were not allowed to take pictures of them singing  :(

Victor's Cafe is located at 13th & Dickinson with just Street parking.  They do have valets to park your car for $12. 
The restaurant is on the small side, which makes it intimate. The seating is pretty close together, but we were still pretty comfortable. 
Only drawback for me was the bathrooms are all on the 2nd floor with pretty steep steps. 
They also have a nice bar and lounge upstairs.
I would recommend Victor's for a special occasion or some place different to explore.
Would definitely go back!

I called The Farmer's Daughter to make a reservation and that particular night they were booked with a wedding reception in the main dining room so I would have to be seated in the bar area which I said was fine.....but will get back to that in a minute.
I should of read closer that it was inside a hotel. Driving up to the place my GPS kept saying " you have arrived ", but didn't see a restaurant! I had to park my car and walk up to the building to see it's inside the Normandy Farm Hotel.
Once inside, everyone was very helpful, directing me to the restaurant. Was seated right away! Unfortunately,  I never saw the main dining room, but the bar area was very nice and big, with a fireplace too! There were lots of people dressed formally coming in and out from the wedding party.

Meeting a good friend for dinner we decided on the Goat Cheese Cigars as a appetizer.  They were delicious, just could've added about 4 more on the plate! My friend ordered the short rib flatbread pizza and the Octopus as a entree, Pennsylvania Dutch Apple pie for dessert. She said it was pretty good, but nothing  outstanding.  I decided on the Overnight short ribs  spinach & cheese grits (which was very good flavorful and tender) also the broccolini (which was very hard). Could cook for about 1 more minute. I got the Molten Lava Cake/vanilla ice cream for dessert. It was more lava than cake, but not bad!
I really struggle between 3 stars and 4, because somethings were not as good as expected, but service, atmosphere, and some of the food were really good. 
Guess I need to make another vist to figure it all out.

Vegetarians of the World, HipCityVeg is a must try! Fast food for vegans/vegetarians is so hard to come by but HipCityVeg delivers with great execution. Every meal that I have had here has been flavorful and interesting. The focus here seems to be on alternative meats rather than the vegetables but the veggies and sauces do compliment well. There is very limited seating at this location but multiple times I have grabbed my food and ate in Rittenhouse park where there is ample seating.

Last night I got the the Curry Tofu wrap, which is a little greasy, but still delicious.  It's packed with curry covered tofu and fresh veggies. I also tried the green lemonade. To me, it tastes like regular lemonade and was very refreshing. My boyfriend a omnivore enjoyed the Udon Noodle salad. He said the fake chicken was pretty good. I also tried the sweet potato fries which were very crispy and tasted good with sriracha dip.

Can't wait to grab another meal here!

Brown Betty is very convenient to pop in and pick up a cupcake. They always have a bunch of options that are all equally delicious. I do tend to find there cake to be drier than I like but there is ample frosting to help fix that problem. 

I do have to say the shop is pretty small. They have a weird room attached to the main purchasing area and I 'm not sure what it's for. The credit card minimum is $9 so you have to buy 3 cupcakes to meet it. 

Overall, I would recommend stopping by if you have a chance.

I'm really grateful for Luhv Deli coming to Reading Terminal. I recently visited the Herbivorous Butcher in Minneapolis and was hoping Philly would get something like that. Lo and behold, Luhv Deli IS just like that! So much so that when I mentioned Herbivorous Butcher to the cashier when I visited he said that they actually import some of their supplies from Herbivorous Butcher.

I ended up getting some Pepperoni from this stall and using it on pizza. They perfectly nailed the taste and it's perfect for that application. I hope to try more of their offerings like their veggie burger mixes.

I think regret is the best way to describe my experience at Cafe La Maude. My boyfriend and I made the spilt second decision to visit this establishment after passing by another brunch establishment. I can see why people do like this place but it's just not for me.

It's a cute little cafe with an ethnic twist. We were seated quickly by whom I am guessing was the owner. He was sitting with his family and we were seated a table down from them. I looked over the menu and my heart sunk. Nothing sounded good...but I settled on an omelette. Maybe cause I'm a vegetarian? Not sure.

The coffee arrived first which was quickly followed by the meal. The coffee here is La Columbe and it's SO good but you don't go out for brunch just for coffee. I took a few bites of my omelette and just felt sad. For ~$18 I felt more regret for choosing this location.

Parts of the meal were okay, like the fresh fruit and potatoes - these were actually very good. But the fact of the matter is I couldn't find anything on the menu that sounded good. Usually I do more research on places before just showing up but I failed to do that here. 

It makes me sad to leave this review but I really can not recommend this place.

Bourbon and branch has had a major glow up. Their menu is at least 50% vegan and they have a ton of deals. Even with all the vegan stuff this place will even have food to keep my mother happy (her name's literally Karen so you can imagine).

After seeing an Instagram post of their nachos yesterday I visited on a whim. I also ordered some seitan wings cause why not? With Blackbird and Soy Cafe down the street, this place really brings them some competition. Wings were great, the Korean bbq sauce was not my fave but they have like 5 flavors so plenty of things to try. The nachos were earth shatteringly delicious. They actually layer them properly so you don't get to the bottom and have empty chips. They also have great prices for beer. My husband got a pilsner they had on special for $5 so I can only imagine it can get even cheaper if you go for happy hour. They also had the eagles game on so if you're a sports person it's a great place to catch a game.

I think the bartenders we're training last night but they were super friendly and helpful. I didn't order a drink so something I know that can turn them off but I really appreciated the great service (sorry I didn't catch your names!) 

Honestly, I can't wait to come back. They have so much other stuff to try plus they carry beyond burgers/sausage (yum). Take your vegan friends here.

Wow, I really enjoyed my time at Pietro's Pizza! I came here for an early dinner on a Saturday. The place was empty but it was around 4:15 when we arrived. The atmosphere is really cool. They have all they empty bottles on the wall (which I should have taken a picture of but alas I didn't). They also have a cute little terrace that I'd love to eat at when it's a bit warmer out.  

My party of 5 was seated quickly they have an average sized menu but nothing really balance for a vegetarian. I like to see a protein option for a vegetarian so that's the biggest flaw. Most things are very carb heavy but I was able to find some kind of healthy things. The fact that they have zucchini noodles as an option really made me happy even though the serving was small. The kale salad is huge! It wasn't all kale but I don't mind a variety of greens. The apples and apple dressing were really sweet but I prefer sweet salads. The nuts on top added a great crunch! 

The people I ate with ordered pizza which they seems to enjoy but I didn't really look at. I think one pizza could feed 2 (just cause I know we have leftovers in the fridge).

By the time we finished our meal, the place was really full and getting a little loud.

Overall, I wouldn't mind coming back to this location. Maybe I need to save up a cheat meal so I can eat some pizza next time!

Tired Hands is one of my favorite local breweries. Located right outside of Philadelphia, it's a great place to escape to on the weekend. The beers here are interesting while also carrying some of the ones I have seen a bunch of times. I found the prices to be reasonable. You can get 4/8/16 oz pours and 32/64oz growlers (growler is $5 regardless of size). I opted to get a 32oz growler because anything larger is too hard to consumer in the 48 hours they recommend. There is a bigger beer selection here compared to the smaller brew pub that Tired Hands owns. 

The food here is very good. I tried the chips and things which was fresh made tortilla chips with guacamole and salsa. The guac was weird but the salsa was amazing. I also ordered a veggie burger while my bf ordered the regular burger. We both though the burgers were exceptional. The side of fries were the perfect additional to the burgers. I thought the guac on my veggie burger was better than what was provided on the chips. I do wish they had pretzels or something so they could feature their housemade mustard which is delicious. 

The atmosphere of the place is great. You are literally sitting in the middle of the brewery surrounded by large tanks and fermentors. When we first arrived we were told the wait was going to be 45 minutes but it tooks less than 5 minutes to get to a table. Also the parking situation is a little weird - there is a lot but everything is metered parking. The parking is cheap but still - bring quarters.

I go through ebb and flows of really liking this place and being utterly disgusted. I settled on 4 stars because they get points from me for being the first date of my long term boyfriend and I.We were freshman in college and needed something cheap but also fun. 

The ambiance is nothing to write home about. The first time I came here was the day after Valentines day (re: first date) and though the pink and red table settings were for the holiday. After making many trips back to this place, they are a main stay of the decor. They play some....interesting music. Some of it being weird Chinese remakes of American songs (I have definitely heard the Titanic song here in Chinese). 

The normal food can be hit or miss. Some of the "regular" dishes like sesame chicken, etc. can be over fried and give you instant stomach regret. But some things like the pork buns and wonton soup are honest to god vegan dreams of a dish. It makes being vegan/vegetarian worth it. 

Yesterday I dined in for the first time in a long time cause I was really craving buffet style Chinese. It was exactly what I imagined. Spotty warmed food but delicious salty Americanized Chinese. I recommend the creepy shrimp things (they are creepy cause they look so much like shrimp), spring rolls, and the fried rice. 

You can have a solid meal here but none of it is really healthy - this is the definition of a cheat meal. I would recommend it to anyone whose looking for some Chinese!

I am fundamentally changed after having a pizza from Pizza Gutt. I found out about this pizza from instagram and had been following along for while. About a week ago I saw he posted that he won Best of Philadelphia "Pizza Destination" and I knew it was time for me to go.

I made a reservation through the website on the Tuesday before I wanted to go. It was easy and the link is accessible through the pizza_gutt instagram. 

When I arrived I was seated quickly in an almost full restaurant. Win win is very cute and has a very hipster vibe with local art for sale hanging on the walls. I made my reservation in a time slot where I would be able to get Happy Hour beers (HH is 5-7). They had a decent selection of styles so everyone should be happy. On the menu they also had an assortment of cocktails. 

The pizza came out in a reasonable amount of time. It was very steamy but it wasn't burn the roof of my mouth hot lava hot which I appreciated. Upon first bite I knew I was in love. A nice thick crust, cripsy edges, the perfect amount of toppings. The pie is cut into 6 slices and I felt two was a good portion/person. We were able to take the other 2 slices home and they made for a great leftover cold pizza. 

I can't wait to come back. 5 stars, best pizza ever. I would make special arrangements if I wasn't from the area to specifically get this pizza.

Between A-OK and Yay! I'm a fan, I'm really going to have to go with the A-OK, 3 star choice after my meal at Valanni. 

Last night I attended restaurant week at Valanni. I was meeting up with someone from Yelp to get the restaurant week experience and just chat. We were quickly seated at our table and our waiter was very friendly. The location is small so definitely make a reservation. I would also say the vibe here isn't too romantic, just chill. It's perfect to meet up with a friend for dinner! Maybe even split a few apps. Also, if you are coming for RW, you can't combine it with the free sangria with check in, which is kind of a bummer. 

So we go to order and we were taken aback because we thought we could order 2 from the appetizer section each, must have been a typo on the restaurant week page that's now fixed. I ended up ordering the Vegetable Empanadas, the Vegetarian Paella, and the Oreo Beignet. Looking back, I wish I would have chosen a fresher app. 

Vegetabke Empanada - the filling was flavorful, the outside was not oily, and the dipping sauce was pretty tasty, but these did not blow me away
Vegetarian Paella - this was kinda meh, i wish it had more flavor in the dish itself. there was this side sauce that I had to mix in to give it more flavor....shouldn't the dish be flavorful enough? makes me feel like the chef is not confident in cooking veggies.
Oreo Beignet - this saved the meal for me. I love ice cream and this was so creamy and tasty. Plus I love the combination of the warm beignet with the cold ice cream. I would definitely order this again.

Overall, I had a great time at Valanni but I'm not sure if I will be running back here.

-it's cash only!!!!-

I seriously love Brunch! Green Eggs Cafe is a solid place to go and get your brunch on. Usually GEC has a super long line outside of it but today I was able to walk right in. I came after going to a cycling class at City Fitness. I am not really an alcohol for Brunch person plus I'm trying to be semi healthy so I can't really comment on the BYOB situation.

The waitress that we had was very attentive and brought over coffee right away. She also quickly grabbed some splenda for me - it's important when the coffee is sitting right in front of you and your watching it cold waiting for splenda. 

Our food cam out in a timely manner. I ordered the Ultimate Tofu Scramble which was curry tofu with a bunch of veggies. It also had potatoes, vegan sausage, and toast. Just saying, the toast was perfect when it came out, not cold - again super important cause cold toast is terrible. The curry tofu scramble part was really tasty and interesting. I haven't had anything like that.

The only other thing i should mention is that I have been here previously and had a Salted Caramel Latte. It was gross! Wayyyy to much salt. I drank it but like was definitely not worth the calories (it had a mountain of whipped cream). I had to remove a star because this drink was seriously terrible.

It's overall a great place for brunch and the lunch menu also looks really good. I will definitely be back to this place.

In one corner we have Iovine Brothers, in the other we have a grocery shopper. Who will win out in the battle weekly grocery shopping!!!
-ding, ding-

Iovine Brothers has the freshest produce in the market. This place is great to hit up during week in the morning. When I was in school, I would come here at 8am on Mondays and there would be no one so I could easily get my shopping done. 

Even though the market is very crowded on Sundays, Iovine Brothers has a student discount. They also have dollar grab bags with slightly overripe products - but still usable! Even with these two things, I still recommend comparing prices with OK Produce (who always have a student discount) to get the best deal.

Many people just notice the produce, a pro tip is to check out their fresh pressed juices that are delicious and the wall of prepackaged nuts and dried fruits. Just keep in mind, Iovine is not always the cheapest when it comes to these products. 

In the end, Iovine Brothers can be your one stop shop for your weekly grocery shopping but you might end up spending a little more than you expected.

Tried this pound cake when a coworker brought some into the office and it tasted amazing! I just had to have more. My birthday was over last weekend so I picked up 2 pound cakes and a butter cake which cost me about $25. I was happy and on my way so I thought. 

I put the cakes in the fridge when I got home and took one out about 3 hours before it was going to be served. I was having a paint party that night and was super excited to have this cake with my girls. We cut it using a butter knife and the cake was crumbly and CHOKE DRY. Talk about disappointing and I had raved about this cake to my friends. Just terrible.

I called the next morning and asked to speak with a manager. She asked me if I still had the cakes and would be willing to come in. I made the trek again from the northeast section of Philly which took me a good 30 minutes and 15 miles. When I arrived I waited a few minutes for someone to get her and for her to wash her hands. She smelled of smoke. I hope she's not doing the baking. Side eye.

First thing she asked me was if I put the cakes in the fridge? And what kind of knife used? I stated I did and that I just used a butter knife because I wasn't in a kitchen/cooking area. She then spoke to me like I was an ignorant child and stated you never put cake in the fridge because of the condenser and that you should use a bread knife etc. She stated that their cakes were extremely moist and putting it in the fridge just dries it out. OO Well excuse me! Did anyone state that when I purchased it ? And yes using a sharp knife is better but your cake should not fall apart if you don't use one!

She then brought over another manager who then looked at the icing on my cake and stated that they need to stop using the machine because there was barely any icing. Just another factor of the lack of quality in the cakes I received.

Needless to say as appalled as I was by her explanations I kept my mouth shut because I wanted my cakes replaced. She gave me two more pound cakes and they tasted a bit better, still did not compare to the first time I tasted them but about 3 stars. I won't be back. Quality is sporadic, cost is high and service unacceptable.

This place boasts a fun atmosphere, stellar service where customers are friends, and authentic eats. It is a winning combo.

For my first visit at the Old Bay Cafe, which is quickly gathering a strong and far-spreading word-of-mouth reputation, I had to go with the signature crab cake sandwich. I let out an audible "oh my god" when I saw this thing...5 ounces of luscious crab meat, formed into more of a softball than a flat cake. No filler is used in this beauty -- only as much tasty binder that is needed. The spicy mayo gives it nice flavor. 
The kind owner also gave me a sample of the crab bisque, which was also very flavorful. I will be ordering some on my next visit, as well as the much-tooted-about fish tacos.
Even their Arnold Palmer is special: Made with good tea and even better stratch-made lemonade, shaken in a cocktail shaker and exuberantly delivered to your table. 
Yeah, you'll wanna try this place. 

As a side note, it becomes pretty clear after skimming the profile of cranky naysayer below and reading his countless nasty reviews of local joints that this guy clearly gets a hard-on from blasting restaurants with use of as much excessive, colorful, and likely false details as possible. I'm not affiliated with this or any restaurant, but I don't like to see small businesses starting off the world getting a phony bad wrap from some cranky poo-poo-er.

With that being said, try this place. It's likely that you'll like it.

Knowing they have 3 locations in New York and this one in Philly, I knew I had to give it a try. I got their salty pimp specialty cone, which consists of chocolate dipped vanilla soft serve, dulce de leche and sea salt topped with rainbow sprinkles. My daughter and I thoroughly enjoyed every bite. Every lick and bite was filled with sweet goodness to her and she said mommy, this is the best ice cream ever. What kid doesn't like ice cream?!

The vanilla soft serve itself was rich and creamy, although it was lacking in dulce de leche and salty flavor, the crunchy chocolate dip made up for it, which was my favorite part of the cone. I'm trying the Bea Arthur (nilla wafers) next time. We came here around 2:30 on a Saturday and there were surprisingly no line at all. Service was excellent, place was clean and the desserts are reasonably priced. It's definitely worth a try!

Took my mom here for dinner to celebrate her birthday on a Saturday. The place was pretty crowded around 6:30; we had a party of 5 and I was worried about a possibly long wait but luckily, we were seated right away. There is Wi-Fi available and a two hour time limit seating policy per visit, which I don't think they really enforce unless the place is busy beyond belief. There are 2 options to choose from- AYCE Hot Pot for $22.99 and AYCE BBQ for $27.99 or you can choose to enjoy both BBQ & Hot Pot for $32.99. We opted for both since my mom can't live without her veggies but me on the other hand, isn't a fan of hot pot and simmering meats. 

We ordered practically everything off the BBQ menu (chicken wings, gizzard, beef tongue, sirloin steak, fillet beef, beef short rib, pork belly, pork chop, duck, sausage, etc.) and also a good amount of hot pot items as well. They offer 6 different types of soup base and we chose the original style (the spicy style is probably the most popular but my mom doesn't like spicy). The raw meats and seafood came out right away but seem like they took forever to cook since their grill is small and isn't hot enough (unlike the ones in NY) but it still got the job done...after a while. The seafood pancake were my favorite, so crispy and tasty that I finished the whole thing. 

However, the "marinated" meats were tasteless and some were tough to eat (not overcooked). Definitely help yourself to some sauces at the condiment station. Service was a bit slow and disorganized; the girl gave us the rudest look when we asked for seconds, seriously? Overall, the whole experience and meal wasn't bad, it was OK and my mom had a great time. The quality of everything was decent, pricing is reasonable so you get what you pay for. Just an FYI, this isn't authentic Korean BBQ, the only Korean thing about it is the style of cooking the food on the grill, the owners, staff, marinates and sauces are all Chinese.

3.5 stars-I've been here with my family for lunch a handful of times after visiting the cemetary that is 5 minutes away. It gets extremely busy on the weekends since it is connected to the mall and we always come on a Saturday so I would make reservations the day before to avoid the wait. However, the service and food is not consistent, sometimes it's good, sometimes it's not.

But for the most part, despite the slow service or food being cold, dry or overcooked, the server that we get every time has always been polite, attentive and apologetic. The food itself is not bad, my mom and I love their miso salmon with brown rice and they have some good appetizers as well like the sweet corn tamale cakes, stuffed mushrooms and avocado eggrolls. 

With their extensive menu, indulgent desserts (lots of cheesecake options) and convenient location with ample parking, I can't think of a better place to take my family than here.

Well, I reviewed Trailhead a while back and the review was less than stellar. I received a note from the management after that review asking what they could do better, etc.  (my review comments gave certain "clues" as to where things were "lacking")

My wife reconnected with some old friends and this is where her friends were getting together.  

I made a comment to the server that my vodka and soda was all soda and no vodka.  He took care of that and the drinks got a bit better.  We ordered dinner and the food was "ok" but nothing to write home about.

When I received my bill, I realized our bill was triple that of the other couples at the table.  When I checked the tab, I found that I had been charged for 11 cocktails.  I queried the server about this and he told me that since I wanted more vodka in my drinks than they put in them I was charged for that "extra" vodka.  We had a $130 bill for our food and beverages whilst the other couples bills averaged about $45.  

I guess the comments in my previous review were completely ignored regardless of the "concern" shown by the management. 

They get one star because ripping people off isn't cool and the service was still sorely lacking.  I will not patronize this establishment again.

I love and live for a good brunch spot! I had been eyeing this cafe the entire time I was in New Orleans and finally decided to come on the last day before leaving. I'm so glad I did. The food was amazing! The service was quick and the server was nice. I like that they get you in and out. I also signed up on the Yelp waitlist before arriving and it helped. When I signed up there were six parties in front of us. By the time we walked to get there our table was ready. It was perfect, so yes the Yelp waitlist works. Our table was ready when we arrived, and those that were walk-ins had a 25-30 min wait. Whoo hoo, go Yelp waitlist!!

I ordered the Catfish & Grits and my husband ordered the Bananas Foster Pain Perdu with a side of eggs and sausage. I grew up on catfish & grits. My mom use to cook it once a week, so when I saw it on the menu I immediately knew what I was ordering. I'm glad I did. It touched on my childhood memories as well as provided great taste. It was simple yet tasty. The fish was fried perfect and went so well with the grits, and the Pork Tasso Cream Sauce was the cherry on top! This dish was yummy! Now let's talk about the giant homemade biscuit that it's served with..OH MY, delicious! You could tell it was homemade and made with love! It was soft, flaky and just tasty! It had the perfect consistency. The honey butter it was served with was a plus. My husband's French Toast was pretty amazing as well!! It was a little sweet for him but he still enjoyed it. I loved it! The bananas, raisins and syrup with the French bread toast was ahhhhmmmazing! It was a party in your mouth! 

Overall, I enjoyed my experience and food! Ahhhmazing food! Even the Benedict's looked amazing! We didn't order any but the table next to us did, and my oh my they looked fantastic!

I finally got to try District Donuts. After seeing them on my Instagram for some time, the time finally had come! Yay! I'm glad I tried them. Their donuts are good and taste homemade. What I also like about their donuts is that they are thick and have a nice chew. I ordered the Hibiscus Donut and the Cinnamon Roll. Both were really good but of course lent different flavors. One was more fruity and light and the other more cinnamon and warm. The hibiscus was my favorite. I loved the fruity notes that came from this donut. It even had a candied orange on top. The orange was a nice addition. The cinnamon roll donut was good but for me a little too much. It just seemed heavy. While the flavors were different they were good to try. Overall, I enjoyed District Donuts.

Stanley is a good breakfast spot. It is expensive but I guess that's to be expected with it being located in Jackson Square. The breakfast we had was very standard and simple but very tasty. The staff was nice and they get you in and out. Our waiter's name was Breezy. Her real name was Briante and she was very cool and a good waiter. Everything was very good here, my only complaint is that it was expensive for what we ordered. For 2 Stanley Classics, 2 sides of grits, 1 mimosa, and 1 orange juice our bill was about $55-$63 including tax and tip. 

My husband and I ordered the same exact thing. We both ordered the Stanley Classic with a side of grits. The Stanley Classic consisted of Scrambled Eggs, Smoked Bacon, Creole Breakfast Potatoes, and Multigrain Toast. The Grits were a cheese and bacon grit. I mean homemade, not just topped with cheese and bacon. They were so good. The Classic was very good in flavor. Neither of us had any complaints. The grits were very yummy and homemade. I loved this as I love grits. I originally thought it was going to be grits topped with cheese and bacon, but I was wrong. You can tell they put time, love and effort into their food!

Overall, we enjoyed our expensive breakfast at Stanley. Lol!

Saba was amazing! I was in NOLA for my 6th year Wedding Anniversary. We didn't really have dinner plans and planned on winging it. We came across Saba after watching someone I knew story on Instagram who was also in NOLA. I said ok, perfect! Well try it! I was a little skeptical because it's so hard for me to eat anything else in New Orleans other than New Orleans cuisine. However, I'm glad I thought outside the box and gave Saba a try! The food was awesome! This was the best what I call "fancy" Mediterranean food I've had. I've had a really good "home-cooked" Mediterranean restaurant but the styles were different. 

Saba is tapa style in my opinion. Meaning small plates for sharing. We started with their Spicy Lamb Ragu Hummus. I mean you can't come to a Mediterranean restaurant and not try their hummus. This hummus was theeeee BBEESTT ever! They offer different combinations of hummus. This spicy Ragu hummus was the bomb.com! Like so good! It was flavorful and had different texture elements that I loved. It consisted of crispy garbanzo beans and scallions. Also, what I loved about their pita bread was it was thick! I've never had a thick pita bread. This was different and a nice surprise! The oil dip that comes with the pita bread was also very good and went well with the pita bread. We also tried the Ikra dip! It consist of three simple ingredients (cream cheese, salmon caviar, shallot) but this was such a good dip. It's so simple but flavorful! I am not a fan of Caviar but it went so well with this dip. This dip was yummy!! After we had our dips, we had some Grilled Louisiana Shrimp. This dish was delicious. Of course it had a Mediterranean flare, but it was amazing. It was served with roasted cauliflower tzatziki, zhoug, pomegranate, dill. The tzatziki brought the cool aspect to the dish and the zhoung brought some heat. I loved this cool, heat dish! Delicious! Lastly, we had a brownie that had some Mediterranean flare as well. Duh! Lol! This brownie was so yummy and soft! It did have a slight flavor I wasn't sure I liked from the Carob or the tahini but I could deal with it. The Tahini gelato was also good. I love brownies and ice, cake and ice cream, cookies and ice cream, etc. This was right up my alley! Overall, I absolutely loved Saba and would come back when in NOLA! The food was awesome and we left happy! It was the perfect way to spend our 6th Anniversary Dinner.

Compère Lapin is the bomb.com! However, you already knew that. They won a James Beard Award. The funny thing is I almost missed out on this restaurant. For New Year's Eve Dinner it was between here and Luvi. We decided on Luvi because of the menu we saw online. At Luvi, I was talking to the guy next me to me who is also a foodie. He said you have to go to Compère Lapin. It's amazing! I said ok I'll make reservations for tomorrow which was New Year's Day. I am so glad I did! This place rocks and all of the food was delicious. Of course like anywhere, there are some dishes you like better than others but all the food was good. 

My husband and I tried quite a few things to be able to get a good tasting of this restaurant. They started by bringing us these amazing biscuits with bacon and chive butter and sea salted butter. Scrumptious! The biscuits were amazing and the butter was the cherry one top. We then ordered Conch Croquettes, Crispy Dirty Rice, Whipped Ricotta, Broiled Shrimp, Snapper, Tagliolini, and Chocolate Cookies with Daddy's Milk Punch. ALLL of it was good!! All of the dishes lent a different flavor and taste element. I loved and appreciated them all. I see how they won a James Beard Award. Delicious food and good service. I honestly have nothing to complain about. 

Overall, a great restaurant with amazing food. I even got to meet Chef Nina. If you have a chance to go, definitely be sure you go! You'll be happy you did!

Cool restaurant with a cool vibe. Luvi (pronounced Lou - V). The restaurant is named after the owners two daughters Lulu and Violet. How cute is that?! I came here with my husband for New Year's Eve Dinner. We made reservations the night before. It was a four course dinner for the price of $65 per person and included a 20% gratuity. They offered two seatings, a 6:00 pm and an 8:00 pm seating. We went to the 6 pm seating. We arrived 30 min early as we Uber(ed) and didn't want to be late. They were nice enough to let us in but told us service didn't start until 6. That was nice of them. As 6 pm approached the restaurant started becoming packed as everyone started to arrive. The owner was also working the line with his staff. I love seeing this. He was super cool and friendly. We sat at the bar where he was working on cutting fresh fish. The staff was nice and the food was good.

The dinner on this day was from a pre-fixe menu. What I loved was that everything was served family style throughout the restaurant. Meaning they prepared everyone's dish at once and served each course to everyone at the same time. Although, everyone came with their respective guest and we didn't know one another it felt like a big family dinner. It was nice. 

There was two options for each course and three for dessert. My husband and I ordered the opposite of one another for each course and shared so we could taste everything. We started with some edamame. It was light and yummy. We also had drinks as well. That were tasty. I had the Lady in Pink and my husband had an Old Fashion.  We had Tomato Roasted Garlic Soup and Steamed Egg Custard with Gulf Shrimp for course 1. We shared Raw Scottish Salmon and Sashimi Quality Tuna for course 2. We shared Seared Jumbo Scallops and Beef Short Rib for course 3. Last, we shared the Black Sesame Coconut Ice Cream and the Magnolia Black Tea Ice Cream. All four courses were amazing. The food was fresh and the quality of ingredients was good. This was my first time having raw salmon and I must say chef aced it! I was hesitate at first. However, it did not taste fishy at all. It had a good flavor and the texture was better than I thought. The ice cream was also really good. I thought by the name of the flavors it would be very odd. However, I was wrong. My husband and I devoured both scoops of ice cream within minutes. The appetizer and main course meals were also nice and flavorful. Overall, Luvi is a good place to dine. Good people, good food at an affordable price!

Wills Mae's made my day! The food was soo good, like everything! We did have to wait 1.5 hrs, but the wait was so worth it. It is a smaller location so that is why the wait is a little long. However, once you are seated the food comes out at a fairly reasonable pace. Our waiter was also very nice and helped by making suggestions based off of our questions. It is a little pricy for fried chicken but it is worth it. 

We ordered fried chicken and fried catfish with all the sides. Lol. The sides we ordered were rice and gravy, green beans, red beans and rice, candied yams, fried okra, peas and mac & cheese. The fried chicken and catfish were served hot and fresh. I loved this! They both had the perfect crispness and brownness of the batter. They both were seasoned great! The fried fish was so good! The chicken was good as well but I liked the fish a little better. Add a little hot sauce to both and man, this was amazing! I'm a sauce person so I have to have sauce on anything, even if it may not need it. ALL of the sides were tasty as well. The only side that was just meh was the rice and gravy, everything else was seasoned so well and so flavorful. I had the best green peas from here that I've ever had in life. Everything was seasoned so well. My husband and I were shocked. We figured we'd stand in a long line and wait for mediocre food, but we were wrong. The food was great! We literally felt like we were having dinner at someone's grandmother's house. 

Overall, you may wait awhile to eat at Willie Maes but it's worth it! Don't be discouraged by the line or wait time, just wait! I promise you won't be disappointed.

I was very disappointed! I've heard of Felix and someone suggested them so we decided to try them. Needless to say by my two stars, this place wasn't good! We waited for an hour in a line that Felix had. I'm not sure why we did! The food totally was not worth the wait. I assume they are known for their oysters. We do not eat raw oysters but we eat the Char-Grilled ones. We started by ordering a dozen of Char-Grilled Oysters. To be honest, I wasn't a huge fan of these. The ones we had at Drago's were way better. Felix's butter tasted a little off. My husband kept saying he felt it was the texture of these were off. I don't think it was the texture. It was their garlic butter that comes on the char-grilled oysters that wasn't on point. After the fail with the oysters, we decided to order food.

My mom and I ordered the Crawfish Étouffée and my husband ordered the Jambalaya. To be honest, this was the worst Etouffee I've ever had. If your roux isn't right, it just messes up the entire dish. Roux is suppose to be darker in color. This roux came out super light brown. It also tasted pasty as if it had a lot of flour in it and only a little bit of the fat content. I also make a bomb Crawfish Etouffee at home so I knew when this came out, it wasn't right. It was bland and needed some more seasoning. I like that some of the crawfish was steamed and the other half was fried. This was the first time I've ever had it like this and this was something new and different. The fried crawfish added a nice textural element and crunch. My husband's Jambalaya was actually decent. It was flavored ok. I didn't really have any complaints regarding the jambalaya. It was much better than the Etoufee. 

I wanted to try some dessert but after tasting the flavorless food and waiting all that time for nothing, I wasn't convinced their dessert was any better so I didn't order dessert. 

Overall, Felix is overrated and their food is not all that great!! Again, totally not worth an hour wait!

OMG, I finally got to try Five Daughters!!!!! I was so excited to try them. The thing about this visit was it was so unexpected. We saw Jeni's on the corner and stopped to get some ice cream, only to be super surprised that when we pulled into the parking lot, Five Daughters sat in the distance. I got extremely happy, hopped out the car and ran to Five Daughters . My husband was so lost as to what was happening. LOL! It's been on my to-try list for the longest! It was an amazing moment.

These donuts are the best amaze balls! I ordered the holiday donut flavor which was the Egg Nog Custard Donut, Glazed Donut and a Molasses Cookie. The Egg Nog Donut was the best ever besides the Cronut I had from Dominique Ansel in New York! These are seriously some amazing donuts!! So flavorful and fluffy. All the layers are delicious! The glazed donut was yummy as well. Unfortunately, the cookie feel short. I did not like their version of a Molasses cookie. For whatever reason, it tasted weird to me. 

Overall, as you can tell from reading my review, I was soooo excited to finally have tried Five Daughters!! I think they have the best donuts behind D. Ansel's Cronut, so second best I guess! Lol! Nonetheless, amazing either way!

Doctor Gumbo Tour was awesome! Our tour guide Ben was amazing and very knowledgeable! He greeted us with his amazing energy at Red Fish Grill! We all met at Red Fish which was the first stop. We walked around for 2.5-3 hrs through New Orleans and tried different staples. You start at Red Fish and end at Tableau Restaurant (there was one more after this one but I can't remember). You try different dishes as well as cocktails. To be honest, the food was just ok to me. I had more fun just walking and talking with the group that came that day. I also enjoyed spending time with my husband, my mom and her friend. It was a nice to-do. I also enjoyed learning about the food history of New Orleans. 

You start at Red Fish tasting Gumbo and a Hurricane 5 cocktail. The gumbo was actually decent. The cocktail was ok. Next, you go to Pepper Palace to try different salsas, bbq sauces and spicy sauces. My husband and I tried the hottest sauce in the store which was the ghost sauce. That sauce was no joke. It had my eyes watering and it burned the back of my throat and lips for about 30 minutes. If you like EXTRA, EXTRA, EXTRA, EXTRA X 10 heat then this sauce is for you! After, you head to Leah's Pralines. To be honest, I don't like pralines or brittle. It taste like nothing but sugar and the texture is way to hard. It got stuck in my teeth. I tried a tiny piece and that was it. It wasn't for me. Then, you go to the Napoleon House for a Pimm's Cup and a Muffuletta. I just took a sip of the Pimm's cup. I was excited to try the Muffuletta because I've heard so much about them but never tried one. It was different and pretty good! I'm not a fan of olives so that makes it a little less tasty for me. However, it's like the sandwich needs the olives to make it what it is. Probably the only sandwich I'd ever eat olives on. We then headed to New Orleans Creole Cookery House for some Red Beans and Rice. To me, these were a little bland and needed more seasoning. I ate them but I've had better. After Red Beans and Rice,  we went to Tableau for a French 75. This drink had a distinct flavor profile. You certainly get that cognac flavor. It wasn't for me but it was different. Lastly, we ended with plantains, pork skins, and daiquiris from well I don't remember. Ooopps! Sorry! The daiquiri was pretty strong. The plantains had a good flavor. They seemed a little over cooked and were a little more mushy. The pork skins were cooked perfectly but they were sweetened. I'm not use to sweetened pork skins. They were different. I certainly like savory pork skins better than sweet pork skins. 

Overall, I enjoyed the tour and it was a good experience. I wish the food would have been a little better but it wasn't bad.

Ruby Slipper is one of our go-to breakfast spots! I would highly suggest getting there earlier or right when they open. If not you could be waiting as long as 2 hours. We got there early and we had to wait about 30-45 min. It wasn't too bad. The food and service were good! 

I went with three other people so we ordered different dishes. We ordered two different omelettes, Chicken & French Toast Bites, and Biscuits & Gravy. Everything was good as it usually is. I had the Biscuits & Gravy. You could tell the biscuits were homemade. They had a good flavor as well as they were thick. I could have used a little more gravy but I made it work. My mom had the Chicken & French Toast Bites. She let me try them. The French Toast Bites tasted like a hybrid of French Toast and cornbread. It was an interesting taste. The chicken was ok. It tasted good where the spicy sauce was but where it wasn't, the chicken was a little bland. I tasted a bit of one of the omelettes and it was good! 

Overall, Ruby Slipper has a pretty decent breakfast and we come at least once during any visit to New Orleans.

My boyfriend and I were here for date night after he said he had a craving for lobster and I can always go for oysters.

They don't take reservations, so we just stopped in a little before 7 on a Saturday night, and hoped for the best. It was pretty packed but, success: we were seated immediately! As I was looking over the menu I spotted shrimp and grits, and since I hadn't had that in while, I decided to go with that. We also ordered a dozen char broiled oysters.

As always, the oysters were out of this world. Char broiled oysters is one of my all time favorites and Drago's does theirs right with lots of butter and French bread so that you can sop up all of the buttery goodness once the oysters are gone. Then came the shrimp and grits and I loved their version! Big, fat peeled shrimp served with creamy grits, tasso (ham) and a sauce that is out of this world. I'm not sure exactly what was in the sauce, but it was rich and delicious. Talk about a dream come true! The grits were nice and creamy and they were topped with rosemary, which was a very nice touch. My boyfriend had a stuffed lobster which looked delicious and he enjoyed. I couldn't have been happier with all of the food.

Caleb was our waiter and he was excellent. Even though he was waiting on many tables, he was fast about taking our order, checked in on us regularly and had a friendly demeanor, which is always appreciated. I will absolutely go back for more of the goodies I had here.

I was in the area, and in the mood for coffee, so The Bean Gallery was a natural pick.

Parking was easy on this particular day- plenty of street parking, and there was a good crowd in the place. I like the atmosphere here and there are plenty of tables and sofas where people can spread out and do work. WiFi is free with a password.

The man working was really nice. I got my usual large iced coffee and I found the coffee here to be good, without being too strong. While I would say the coffee should definitely be sipped, I didn't find it overwhelming at all.

There are some tables and chairs, if you want to sit outside on a nice day and they also serve an assortment of sandwiches if you want to stop in for lunch.

FINALLY!  After years of hearing about how fantastic Yo Mama's food is, I got to check it out for myself!  

I was super hungry when I checked out what Yo Mama's had to offer.  I kept it simple and ordered the "Yo Mama" burger with a side salad (yes, a salad.  Shutty!).  It was incredible and I finished it in about ten minutes.  It was easily one of the best burgers I have had in the city.  

My only complaint was that I ordered it medium and it was cooked medium well.  That's not a huge thing.  I still ate it and it was still good.  Also, be prepared, this place tends to get really packed and you may be waiting about 30 minutes for food, but that's a small price to pay for such a good burger.

I want to go back and try their famed "peanut butter" burger.  I just wanted to try something basic my first time in there.

I couldn't wait to review this spot after I was here for lunch yesterday!

A friend and I both like trying new places, so as soon as we heard about 14 Parishes and their Caribbean food, we immediately made plans for lunch. I was here about 10 minutes before they opened (they open at 2) and the co-owner was nice enough to let me in so that I could sit down and look over the menu while I waited for my friend.

It was hard deciding what to get because everything sounded fantastic, but I settled on the Portland which is a plate of jerk chicken served with cabbage and two choices of sides. For my sides I got the plantains and the mac and cheese. The food came out and WOW- this is a lot of food for $10! Check out my picture! 

First of all, I loved the chicken- it was juicy and tender and had a lot of flavor without overwhelming the meat or making it too spicy. I sometimes hesitate to order chicken at restaurants, because some places tend to overcook it, but 14 Parishes cooked theirs perfectly. The mac and cheese was just like homemade and you could tell that it was made from a family recipe. The plantains were out of this world- sweet and soft and a perfect compliment to the rest of the meal (I should mention there was a whole bowl of plantains that I didn't get a picture of- super generous.). The cabbage was also a nice touch and it combined well with the chicken.

I don't usually mention drinks, but I had a mango and carrot juice that was quite tasty and they also serve ginger beer, if that's your thing. The co-owner is the one who waited on us and she was so sweet and friendly and made sure that we were happy and had everything we needed. This might be one of the best lunch deals in town, so be sure to add 14 Parishes to your "must visit" list if you are in the mood for something different.

My visit to Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29 was about 5 or 6 months in the making. I wanted to visit this place as soon as I first heard about it and after hearing all the raves, my excitement had reached it's peak by the time I finally set foot here. Something you may or may not know about me: I LOVE tiki drinks. Come on, how can you go wrong with fruit, sugar and spices? Sadly, it seemed like every time I had plans to visit LAT 29, something came up. I finally made it here and my experience did not disappoint.

We stopped into this cute restaurant and bar located in the Bienville House Hotel. Oh yeah, they serve food too! I didn't know either until about a month or two ago. I'm going to get to the drink reviews in a bit, but let's start with the food. We were seated and because I had already scoped out the menu online, I knew exactly what I wanted. We started with the pork and beef dumplings. We got them steamed and they were delicious. Each one was wrapped in a differently flavored "wrapper" and I wish I could remember the exact details because they were incredible. 

For my entree, I got the Hawaiian Cuban Sandwich which is pork belly, ham, creole mustard, cream cheese, coronations, on buttered pineapple bread. It was RIDICULOUS. I mean it was insane how good it was. Before you ask; yes, it was a pressed sandwich! Don't you hate when you order a Cuban sandwich and it isn't pressed? One of my major food pet peeves. I got the fries as my side and they came with kimchi Ketchup & sriracha mayo. Yeah, they have a sriracha mayo and it's as delectable as you can imagine. The sandwich was so rich and delicious that there was no way I could finish it all. Soooo good.

Now for the drink reviews. We tried a bunch, so I'm just going to go ahead and list them with my thoughts.

Kea Colada: My first drink. Their version of a piña colada. Delicious, especially since I wanted to start slow with something that I knew I would like. Sweet and perfect in every way. Probably my favorite drink of the night.

Hawaii 504: My companion's first drink. Spicy with a lot of kick. This one packs a punch. For my taste, good for a few sips, but I might have some trouble drinking a whole one.

Zombie: My second drink. One of my Tiki "go to's". Rich and delicious with a bit of a kick, but not so much of a kick that you will want to call it quits while drinking it. Let it grow on you.

Navy Grog: My companion's second drink. This thing is no joke. Very strong and tastes like straight liquor. Has a spicy and fruity under taste, but it's definitely a "sipper".

Espresso Bongo: My third drink and second favorite of the night. Coffee and rum and fruit? Yes, please! SO good. It's sounds like a weird combination that shouldn't work, but what you end up with is a drink with a lot of flavor and a lot of kick without being overpowering. I can see myself getting this if I were to ever stop in for lunch. A nice pick me up.

Pontchartrain Pearl Diver: My companion's third drink. Sweet and spicy with a lot to offer. Over all really yummy and easy to drink. I definitely wouldn't hesitate to order this one for myself in the future.

As you can probably tell, I loved this place and I really can't wait to return. The decor is perfect and I like that it has a nice Tiki feel without being "in your face" about it. They have expanded their hours, so there's really no excuse to not check this place out, especially for a night cap. Word on the street is that they stop taking food orders at 10, so stop in early if you are looking for some grub.

I can't wait to go back and try more of the cocktails and food. This place is an absolute winner in every way. I should probably stop here because I'm starting to gush.

This place has sure taken off, considering it opened just a few weeks ago.

Decided to stop in here on a Saturday afternoon for lunch. Even though it was about 2, the place was packed and the line was nearly out the door. Yes, you read that right. The place where you order is right by the door, so things tend to get a little bunched up right there. I would have put the order place in the back, but that's just me.

My dining partner was kind enough to wait in line, while I secured a seat at the bar area. You can sit at the bar area overlooking where the food is made, or you can sit in a booth. Since there were only two of us, I decided the bar was the best option for us.

Now, the whole process took a while. From the time we walked in to the time we were actually served was probably 30 minutes, so this isn't the place to go if you are in any kind of huge rush. One thing that was kind of annoying; we ordered coffee with our meal and actually had to track someone down to bring it to us. They had totally forgotten about that part of our order. Not a huge deal, but worth noting.

I got a cheeseburger slider and a fried chicken slider that was topped with cole slaw. Both were really good. I actually think that I preferred the fried chicken slider, simply because of the cole slaw. At $3.50/each, the sliders were a great price for lunch. We also split an order of waffle fries, which was pretty typical. I got a regular iced coffee that was really good and had a lot of flavor. I don't eat donuts, so none for me.

The staff seemed really friendly and eager to please and one man even apologized profusely when there wasn't anymore milk available for me to put in my iced coffee and he took my coffee and put milk in it himself. I thought that was nice.

I will definitely be back. I like that they open early and they stay open until midnight. It makes for a cool place to grab dinner before a night out or on your way home. I probably won't return during the busy lunch rush, but it seems like a great place for a later lunch/early dinner or quick bite.

I always like my "milestone" reviews to be something a little special. For #1200 what better place to review than the restaurant where I spent my 33rd birthday?

For my yearly birthday dinner, I knew that I wanted to eat somewhere special. After hearing raves about GW Fins and even recommending it to people and telling them that I had HEARD it was really good, I finally got to try it for myself.

For starters- make reservations. Yes, they take walk-ins but we had a 10 minute wait even with reservations, and while we waited we heard walk-ins being told that the wait was 45 minutes to an hour. This is a very popular restaurant that gets very crowded, so just open table this thing.

We were seated in the large dining room, and our waiter Morgan came over and took our drink order and explained the specials. I had done my research, so I already knew that I was going to be starting with the shrimp and grits appetizer. This appetizer came with fully peeled shrimp, sautéed and covered in an amazing sauce. An appetizer size serving of grits was under the shrimp and sauce and mixed into the dish perfectly. This appetizer was out of this world incredible and was a perfect start to the entire experience.

For my entrée, I got the pan crusted Sheepshead. It came topped with jumbo lump crab meat and included asparagus and capers. This dish was simply amazing. The fish itself was lightly fried and it was perfectly flaky. The capers added a nice little salty touch to the dish and the asparagus was a perfect accompaniment. It was all topped with brown butter which added a richness to the food without making it too filling.

Of course, I had to get dessert. I decided on the Salty Malty ice cream pie. This was delicious salted ice cream that came on a salty pretzel crust which was then topped with caramel, whipped cream and chocolate covered pretzels.
