The mussels are the best in Tucson - classic - butter, wine, garlic, hint of tomato and basil. My friend took the remaining broth home. So good. I order these every time I dine here. 

My entree was the sea scallops. Six perfectly cooked huge scallops done medium on a gorgeous array of seasonal vegetables. No two plates are the same, with variations on the vegetable selections. Served with a beurre blanc sauce and risotto. Highly recommended.

Was just looking for something to snack on after work and been wanting to stop by one of these food establishments in Verdi for awhile.   Decided to walk into Sasquatch Tavern & Grill to check out their menu. Asked a couple who was leaving how the food was here, and they said it was really good. Another couple eating at the bar overheard and said the same thing. I even asked the waitress what was good, and she said "everything". Well, we took their word for it and decided to try the place out. 
  We only ordered the Sweet Buffalo Wings and Onion Rings but, if you wanna know if it was good, we were back there 2 days later ordering the same thing. Plus, it doesn't hurt that I love the Verdi area and overall feel of the place. 
  All the employees are so so friendly and welcoming and all seem like they truly enjoy working there. The chef/cook even stopped by our table to say hi and see how everything was as he walked by. 
  Only negatives, which is kinda weird to say and not a huge issue but, the water taste a little weird. I heard it's because it comes from the Truckee River, which I guess having fresh water isn't really a bad thing, but a good thing. And the Big Sasquatch Statue in the bar made me miss my dad back home in Hawaii. 
  Definitely want to try their pasta next time and maybe some other Sasquatch recommended items on the menu.

Well we made our second visit and clearly this place is catching on. It was Tuesday evening and the dining room stayed about 85% full the whole time. 
This time we sampled grilled salmon, baked ravioli and the sirloin. The salmon was nicely done, not overcooked, and topped with a mild lemon/wine/butter(?) sauce. The baked ravioli was prepared as baked ziti would be but with ravioli in the center. The steak was prepared medium rare and was tasty and reasonably tender. It was seasoned with some "secret " blend that almost reminded you of the rubs used to smoke briskets. A very nice complement to the meat. 
If they keep a steady course this is likely to become the go to place for beef on the hill.

This bar is literally the worst bar in Philadelphia. If you are thinking of paying money to reserve this bar, DON'T. The staff are so rude, from the bouncers to the bartenders. First of all, the bouncer gave me such a hard time for a REAL ID...I am 22 years old and I genuinely can't fathom that a "legit" bouncer cannot tell a real ID from a fake one.  Instead of admitting his incompetence, he took it out on me and berated me. After much harassment, he begrudgingly let me in. He was on such a power trip that he sought me out in the crowd and came over to me multiple times throughout the night to make me re show him my ID. I would like to reiterate that I am 22 YEARS OLD. This is nothing short of harassment. This is unlike any experience at a restaurant, bar, or club, that I have had in Philadelphia. I truly cannot believe that this company thinks they can treat customers with such disrespect and still have a lasting business in Philly. Truthfully, I wish they would make the city a better place and close down right away. Additionally, the bartender spoke badly about every single person there, going so far as to diss individuals and their appearances, assuming that we wouldn't hear him. To me, this is the ultimate show of disrespect when the party I was with paid over $5,000 to rent ONE PART of this ill-designed bar. If you are going to charge such a tyrannical price, at least be able to deliver a fraction of the experience you promise. What a sham. 

I would urge anyone considering using this venue to think twice and perhaps book with another, more competent, venue.

Gotta love the Ol' Iguodala. The beer selection here is pretty large and stocked with ones I've never heard of, but I like that (don't bother looking for a Bud Light). The food at O.E. is also well above par for a local bar. Many a Phillies' game I have stopped by on the way home, and they didn't even get angry with my repeat attempts to steal their one-ton (must be the wieght if I can't lift it) cigar Indian statue; for some reason their beer always makes me feel powerful enough to throw it onto my shoulder and walk home up the hill. If I'm not feeling particullarly strong, they always have a real cork dartboard, a pool table, and a shuffle board bowling game to get into. Everyone's friendly there, bar dog included, even when I occasionally return to pay tabs I forgot the night before (and especially when I return to pay tabs I thought I forgot, but actually did not). Great bar to go chill in any night of the week, or at least to jump start your night on Main st.

***they do 6 packs to go!***

Dined with my lady on a Friday evening around six, predominantly because it is BYOB, and I was very glad to have finally done so. Quaint little place that seems to be a local favorite; many families arrived while we were eating and seemed perfectly pleased to wait outside until tables opened up (I gather they accept no reservations). 

Started out with a tasty order of the fried mozzarella, which is admittedly hard to screw up, but I appreciated that they were more like fillets than sticks. Dipping sauce was tasty, though it did seem to be lacking something that I couldn't put my finger on, flavor wise, but it's abundance meant I had something to dip those oven hot garlic knots in early on in my meal. 

Moved onto the entrees with my lady's Chicken Siciliano and my Chicken Parmigiana, and we were both pleased. I found her dish to be much too sweet for my liking, as it's Madeira flavor reminded my highly of maple syrup (a taste I have grown particularly disenchanted with since a mishap involving ipecac a few years back), but she enjoyed it there, and even more the next day when it was reheated for lunch. The two breast came swimming in sauce, with a thicker than normal slice of prosciutto on top of each, as well as a piece of eggplant, a shell of provolone cheese, and a chunk of fresh and cold mozzarella. She also got the pleasing and satisfying Penne Vodka with her meal. 

My chicken came in the same two breast style, but with that good red sauce and a heavy handed (in a nice way) shell of melted mozzarella cheese surrounding it. No faults in my dish, only praise, especially for my gnocchi side. Normally you get large jelly bean style gnocchi when you order (at least the half dozen times I've tried it in my life), but these were about the size of one inch cubes; I found it to be much more appealing to my style of eating, and I really dug their airy consistency and mild flavor. Also included in my meal was an extra side of sausage, but it was weak as far as my sausage usually goes, with no heat whatsoever and a bit too much anise. 

Didn't get to try any deserts because we over ate, and yes, you can take that as a compliment, but maybe next time. The only other thing worth mentioning was that the service was very good, and, even though there was a line at the door, at no point did our friendly waitress make us feel rushed to finish.

Typically, I'd consider a 30-minute drive to the 'burbs for a fast-casual meal to be completely out-of-the-question.  I have more than a dozen restaurants of the sort within ten minutes of my home, all serving quick, but high-quality food: sushi, pizza, Mexican, you name it.  What we don't have within close proximity of the near-Northside is Korean cuisine, let alone that of the absolutely delicious sort.  Thus, the drive to Omoni is justified.

Omoni Fresh Fast Korean Grill has been dubbed "the Korean Chipotle."  That moniker should be rejected: it is a travesty.  Chipotle is a chain that is two notches above Taco Bell. Omoni, on the other hand, is a purely original concept.  It serves food with​ tremendous taste and quality, equally as terrific as is served in a more formal setting. Trading sophisticated​ decor and traditional restaurant service, Omoni offers the best meal on-the-fly in the metro area.

​Omoni is a family-owned restaurant serving popular Korean fare.  While admittedly lacking many traditional dishes, it still leaves the diner with plenty of savory options.  I suggest trying the dolsot bibimbap.  The dish is prepared and served in a heavy stone bowl, stuffed with your choice of rice (white or multigrain), meat, and vegetables.  I found the beef to be wonderful, and I don't think this item would be complete without adding the fermented, piquant flavors of the three homemade varieties of kimchi. While many dishes at Omoni are prepared and served on the spot, the dolsot bibimbap requires a little of the kitchen's tender loving care.  Fear not, for it will arrive at your table in a fast-casual jiffy.  The portion sizes at Omoni are ample, and no one will leave with an unsatisfied appetite.

At most fast-casual eateries, excellent service is not expected. The service at Omoni is quite the opposite. I have found the staff going out of their way to be both informative and helpful.

Omoni Fresh Fast Korean Grill is a winner.  It might be fast-casual, but with the quality of the food, you'll hardly notice.

As one who has visited Mexico over 20 times, I have experienced many aspects of the nation's culture.  As a man whose favorite pastime is eating, my trips are often best recollected by my sense of taste.  I've eaten delicious chicken and beef dishes, world class mole, fresh seafood, and even crickets roasted by Mayans.  While I might get to spend one week per year in Mexico, the rest of my year is spent in an eternal struggle to find truly authentic Mexican cuisine 1,000 miles north of the border.  Luckily, in Indianapolis, the struggle ends in Pike Plaza at Carniceria  Guanajuato. 

Carniceria Guanajuato occupies a massive space.  For longtime Indy residents, one might remember it as being the former home of Galyan's Sporting Goods.  If you ever shopped at Galyan's, you understand what just how large this space is.  From the outside, Carniceria Guanajuato appears to be a massive Mexican goods market.  From fresh meats, seafood, cheeses, to glass bottles of Coca-Cola, if you're looking for something Mexican, you're bound to find it in the store.  However, the real magic, in my opinion, occurs in the back of the establishment.  Once you wind your way through the many isles and kiosks, you will stumble upon a huge restaurant, which is often quite crowded.  From the first moment you see it, only one word can come to mind: authentic. While the restaurant is rather loud, chaotic, and lacking of a romantic ambiance, once you're seated at one of the huge wooden tables, you know that you are in for a one-of-a-kind experience.

The menu choices at Carniceria Guanajuato are myriad.  From fajitas, tacos, and burritos to shrimp and seafood dishes, this restaurant can satisfy any of your Mexican food cravings.  However, my recommendation (which is likely the same as many other customers) is to order one of the "meat tables."  This item is very true to its name: it is literally a small table packed with chicken, steak, carnitas, and chorizo.  To add to its glory, the meat tables also come with generous portions of delicious, homemade pico de gallo, guacamole, and corn tortillas.  Be sure to bring some friends with you, as I can't stress enough just how large these portions are.  For example, the meat tables don't come with serving forks or serving spoons; they come with tongs.  Yes...tongs.  A seafood table is also available.  While at Carniceria Guanajuato, you also owe it to yourself to begin your adventure with one of their famous (and very large) shrimp cocktails.  If you're dining solo, or just looking for a really healthy meal, the shrimp cocktail is certainly perfect by itself.

Hey, foodies!  Forget your foo-foo restaurant with its minuscule portions for an evening.  If you're in Indianapolis, have a voracious appetite, and want a truly authentic Mexican dining experience, you would be doing yourself an injustice by not trying Carniceria Guanajuato.  You'll be a repeat customer.

This place holds a 5 star rating for a reason: great location, delicious lemonade, and sandwiches that are so good you might just dream about them.

The first time I came here I just popped in to get a lemonade. I ordered their strawberry basil lemonade and just about sipped down the whole thing in 5 minutes. This ain't your minute maid powder beverage, this is dang-good, fresh, made from real fruit lemonade. And, it is so reasonable, $2 a glass!

Yesterday that strawberry lemonade popped in my head and it wouldn't leave me be. I decided to go and pick some up and along with it, a sandwich. The gal at the register told me she recommended the sausage and pear. I am so glad she did--crumbly and savory sausage, goat cheese, greens, pears, and some kind of sweet chutney of sorts. What a treat! I ordered it on GF bread, which upped the price by $1.75. The sandwich also came with a side (there are like 4 different options to choose from). 

The inside of this shop is adorable. Splashes of yellow in every direction, bar stool seating, low table seating, and also options to sit upstairs and overlook the rest of the restaurant. 

Prices are not expensive, but not cheap. This is the kind of place you save for a treat yourself lunch outing. I paid $16 for my meal with a tip included. Worth it for how yummy it was, but definitely a treat and not something I'll do often (though if I am being honest, I would like to).

So many words come to mind: delicious, hospitable, prompt, inviting, unique. 

I found this restaurant on Yelp last week while looking around for new places to try. The photos of the food immediately stood out to me and sparked my interest. Aside from that, the fact that this place has an overall 5-star rating really got me curious. Last night my roommate and I stopped in around 6 pm and were able to get a table immediately. There were a few other parties in the restaurant, but it wasn't packed out by any means. It's open seating, so you grab whatever table you like. We snagged a booth and were instantly greeted with waters and menus.

Food:

After looking at the menu for a few minutes, we both decided to get Samosas for an appetizer and the Beyinetu combo plates with six items for our main dish, we wanted to try out as much as we possibly could! (Side note: the fewer items you get, the bigger the portions are--likewise--the more items you order, the smaller the portions are.) We had a hard time remember the name of six items, so we made lists to help us when we ordered (this amused our waiter). With all that said, here's what I ordered-

11. Red (Lamb) Tibs
14. White (Chicken) Tibs
20. Kae Mesir (Red lentils)
22. Shiro (Bean & chickpea dish)
24. Tikel Gomen (Potatoes, cabbage, onions and carrots)
28. Rice (Tumeric flavored)
(The Beyinetu also comes with a salad in the middle)

YOU GUYS- I ATE ALL OF IT. I am not exaggerating. It was THAT delicious. And you know what? I didn't even feel bad about it. The bulk of this meal is meats and veggies, so even if you go a little overboard and eat a lot of food here, your body won't get mad at you for it (at least mine didn't, hehe). I felt (VERY) full and satisfied after this meal, but without the feelings of remorse that come along with finishing something heavy like a giant bowl of pasta--ya know what I'm sayin'?

Aside from the guilt-free attributes of this food, it is just flat-out tasty. The spices they use, the textures, the flavors, the smells. All of it is delightful. Savory and full of flavors that will make your palate do a happy dance--that's how I'd sum up this food!

Service:

So kind and hospitable! The staff was quick to take care of us and answer any of our questions about the menu. Also--talk about fast--we got both our samosas and Beyinetu within 5 minutes of ordering. When they saw that our injera bread was disappearing from our plate, they brought us a little basket with some extra.

My favorite part?

You eat this all with your hands...no forks, no knives, no spoons! It feels a bit awkward at first, but after 2 minutes of this, your memories of utensils are long gone. #DitchTheFork

Visited this Sandwich Spot today for the first time with the wifey.  As we approached the counter I thought Tormund Giantsband from Game Of Thrones was taking our order.  For those of you that haven't watched GOT, Tormund is a bad ass warrior and leader of the Freefolk that is main character Jon Snows battling partner and friend.

Tormund commented on my wrist watch and asked if I was feeling crazy!  I said yes I like crazy!  He said I'll make you a special off the hidden menu sandwich.  We quickly ordered and sat inside.  Minutes later Tormund brought a huge hot pile of Sandwich.  I don't want to give away the ingredients but if you like meat, bacon, and cheese the DARK DIESEL sandwich is for you.  South Reno has been in need of a sandwich shop like this.  We will return.  Thanks Sandwich Shop.

Sorry no pictures of the DARK DIESEL I want to keep this thing secret, and honestly most of you couldn't handle it anyway!

This last Wednesday I had the pleasure of going on a date at Burger Me.  It was dinner and a movie.  The south Reno Summit Mall Burger Me is located next door to a Century Movie Theatre, talk about two birds with one stone, plus the boo was dressed to impress with her witchy fall outfit.  I dig her fall boots!

I've always enjoyed the north west Reno location along with the south Reno spot.  People always give me a hard time because I often order a hot dog at a burger joint...I'll tell you why folks look at my pictures, their hotdog is so legit I ain't about to quit!  

We rolled in and ordered the boo a slider, for me a hot dog with bacon, cheddar, and grilled onions.  And to finish it off we shared an order of sweet potato fries Lady and the tramp style.

My hotdog was awesome, it's a classic go to food order.  Trust me when you step up and order this hot dog you are telling all of man kind to move over and watch out, because you live on the edge.  BME's hotdog continues to put my ass in the Burger Me seats.  The sweet potato fries were sweeter than two soulmates head over boots in love.  And boos slider was just how she ordered it.  Plain with cheddar, bacon, tomato, and avocado.  We were living the American dream Yelpstars.  

After we finished this five star feast we walked approximately 50 yards over to watch a throwback Halloween flick...Beetle Juice!

When in a rush to get some tasty eats with options from turkey chili to elk burgers.  I highly recommend Burger Me south Reno prior to a movie.

Burger Me up, Scotty!

From the moment we walked in, the owner was rude. It was a Monday night. 4 adults and 2 children. The place was nearly empty. As you've done in response to a previous review, please don't tell me customers complained about the children. They were well behaved. Excuse me if they took a breath and laughed like children. It was most apparent that this restaurant is not friendly in general, especially toward children. 

Right after we sat, the owner immediately questioned if we had a reservation. I looked around and responded "no." Again, the place was nearly empty. As you've done in response to a previous review, please don't tell me it's customary to make a reservation for a party of 4 adults and 2 children. It's not. I travel all over for business each week and eat almost every meal out with groups of people (4-5+), and hardly make reservations. If I walked in with a party of 10, I would of made a reservation. 

From that point moving forward, the owner paced around and was very rude. The waitress was rude as well. She barely made eye contact. How was the owner rude? There were 2 other tables (nearly empty) who he made frequent visits to. Not once, other than his rude reservation question, did he come up to our table. You're a small establishment and its CUSTOMARY for an owner to ensure I'm enjoying my meal. 

I am an extremely well traveled person who has eaten at restaurants all over the world. The food is subpar at this restaurant in comparison to other Thai restaurants. The portions are mediocre at best and the pricing is not equivalent to the quality or quantity of food. The horrendous service and subpar food earned this establishment this rating.

Lee's is my place! This was the first restaurant my partner and I dined at upon moving to West Philadelphia. The staff is great, and the food is comforting and delicious. 

I've certainly appreciated the vegetarian/vegan options for comfort food / cheesesteaks when hosting family with these preferences. For the meat-eaters, the Korean BBQ Cheesesteak is a fun, tasty spin on the classic. You also can't go wrong with a cheeseburger or chicken fingers! Lee's offers a variety of dipping sauces for your fries, chicken fingers, etc - give em all a whirl, they're a nice touch!

The portion sizes are very generous which makes the price quite a deal overall. Lee's is great for both dine-in and pickup orders!

Pro tip: Only make the trek here for drinks, but make sure to eat elsewhere.

Yes, their beer is good. They are a brewing company, so thank goodness they get that right. Tired Hands does have some strange rules for their bar service, only allowing one tasting glass at a time to be served which ultimately creates unnecessary work for the bar staff and a lot of laps from my server.

The food, though. We started with nachos - a pretty safe bet, I'd say. At minimum, this is an editing error in the menu as it should have read as "Queso Dip." What we received was just that, queso dip - with a few toppings of meat and raw jalapenos. Not awful to the taste, but misleading from the get-go.

On to dinner. Hands down, this was the worst burger I've ever experienced. Children on backyard BBQ grills could do a better job. I had a premonition when the server didn't ask for our desired level of "doneness." This usually means it will be cooked well done which is no way to enjoy a burger.

Needless to say not one, but two of our burgers were cooked to a crisp. Like, "I can taste the charcoal from the grill crisp."  These shameful burgers were held between the smallest, saddest, bargain-bin bun you can imagine. The only slight glimmer of hope was in the house-made mustard which had a nice flavor. But mustard alone cannot salvage this disaster.

This was a mistake of a dinner option, and it will be a long time before we build up the courage to try again. Even for their delicious beer.

The Good: I've been a Vivace fan for years; I go with friends, family, even solo to eat at the bar. Consistently outstanding food & service. Worth the price for the most part. Their homemade pastas are papery thin delicacies like I have never experienced before.

The Bad: Sadly, last week I was eating at the bar and was deeply disturbed to hear employees (primarily wait staff, primarily female) talking about customers in a rude fashion, imitating them in an unkind way, joking sarcastically about so-and-so needing a new Porsche, etc. WOW- I was stunned. It seems that late in the evening staff cut loose and no longer worry about being professional, even if there are still customers present. The owner was even there, not engaged in the conversation at all, but he was in the restaurant. Apparently staff had no concern about being overheard by customers (e.g. myself) or the owner. This tells me it's a habitual behavior, not an unusual one. I have not been back since, I'm not sure I will be. It may have been because I was dining alone, and wait staff are far less professional towards a solo diner. (I've seen other reviews on Vivace addressing this issue.) When off the clock and off the premises, whatever, it's a free country; make fun of your customers all you want. But that kind of disrespect toward patrons while among patrons is inexcusable. Vivace may be an exceptional restaurant, but they are not the only great restaurant in Tucson.

Not the worst restaurant in Tucson - the worst restaurant in Arizona. 
Waited 10 minutes to be seated while numerous staff hung out behind the bar chatting and texting (one of them I later realized was the manager!), drinks had little or no alcohol in them, chile rellenos were soggy and bland, beans horribly over-salted, rice extremely greasy. When placing food on the table, the waitress slammed the plates down then stormed off. When we asked to speak to the manager, the waitress literally sighed heavily and stormed off (again, she was far better at sighing than serving). When speaking to the manager, before my mother could finish a sentence the manager said, "Oh so everything was bad? Just everything was bad?" (Actually, yes it was.) She was pissed off, even though my mother had said, " I'm not looking for a discount or anything, but I think you should know about my experience here tonight." The manager was annoyed that we were taking up her texting time I suppose.
Horrible service.
Horrible food. 
Horrible drinks. 
Horrible response from management.

Is it possible to give a place ZERO stars? 

Let me start by pointing out that my average rating is often very high and I tend to avoid writing nasty things about local establishments, even when they deserve it. However, my latest experience at Pour House was so abysmal, it is my Yelp Elite duty to share it with you. 

My first visit to Pour House with Marcia M. earned three stars. I was unimpressed, but willing to give it some time to grow since it was early in their opening. However, it seems things have only gone downhill since that first visit. 

Last Saturday night, a friend and I were on the hunt for a new atmosphere and casual place to grab a drink before heading out. My friend hadn't yet been to this new place on 8th Avenue and it seemed like a good idea. After having to move our car twice to find an area where it wouldn't be towed, we realized we should have cut our losses then and found a better solution. But, we like to take risks I guess, so we ventured on. 

Once inside the formaldehyde-smelling restaurant - seriously, this place has an odor that makes me wish I could cuddle up for hours in Red Door's smoke infestation - we found a spot at the bar. There's no drink menu, so the ordering process is kind of a crap shoot - and crap it was! They opened a tab for me and set my debit card in a small cup near the POS. 

After we choked down our drinks and tried to pretend the smell wasn't giving us a headache, we asked the unfriendly, unhelpful bartender to close our tabs. After a few minutes of her shuffling through the THREE (count 'em, three) cards in the cup, she turned to ask me if she had taken my card. Indeed she did only moments before (Hello, remember?!?! Idiot!).  As she continued to lazily look around the bar area, I did a little research to find that my debit card had been charged another amount. 

You're following correctly... they closed someone else's tab on my debit card and sent them on their way with it. A result I don't blame the customer, who may have not noticed, for but rather the Einstein's behind the bar. The bartender called her manager over, who was equally as unhelpful and unapologetic. He offered to void the transaction that they charged (UMMM, you think?!?! Duh!!!).  Meanwhile, the at-fault bartender handed me and my friend our ticket for the drinks. Seriously? 

The manager quickly disappeared into the back and it was up to me to find a solution. I grabbed a piece of paper and pen and wrote my number on it, "call me if the customer comes back in with my card please," I told the bartender. I then took a separate piece of paper, not trusting that she'd actually remember what had happened at all in 5 minutes, and asked to see the manager. He came out from the back and I told him the same thing. He said he'd call if it turned up - although he's done nothing to apologize or even check in. 

I never heard from them, so I had to close my debit card and sat at home for a week waiting for it to arrive. (Awesome.) And here's the best part: they never voided the transaction - at least not the one they charged to my card. I was expected to pay for another customer's tab? I don't think so. This is single handily the worst experience I've had in Nashville to date, and needless to say, I will not be back. 

Final note: I understand things happen and mistakes are made, but the way it was handled - not to mention the disgusting food and drink selection - has me hoping this place is gone as quickly as it went up.

I LOVE PHO GRAND!!! I've been frequenting this place for years and just now thought to leave a review for this fine establishment. 

Vietnamese food by it's nature is very light, fresh, and sits comfortably in one's belly. Pho Grand excels at all three. I've never had anything bad at this place. I always try something different, yesterday going with the Deep Fried Tofu Noodle dish. YUM.

Only recently, did I discover the amazing Vietnamese Coffee offering! They brought the whole set-up to make the coffee to our table. It is a hand-poured method and the coffee is VERY VERY Strong. Once the coffee is ready they pour it into a glass which contains some sweetened condensed milk and add ice!! They stir it all together and WOW! It is a kicker! Strong, flavorful, delish. It's like a desserty treat. But WARNING: it is STRONG, so don't drink it too late or you will be scrubbing your floors at 2AM not knowing what else to do with that energy.

I was recommended to come check out this amazing restaurant by a very sweet lady saying it was the best place in town.
 I have yet to dine in but have gotten take out twice already. The owner (a young guy named tom) has been nothing but polite and has made each experience wonderful. Hes always dressed in his suit, which is typically very out of the ordinary for any Asian restaurant. The one thing I would have to say is that this place deserves to be in a better location than it is currently located. It's tucked in a stripmall by the value village by the traffic circle off of the 97th, blocks from nait and across from the Boston pizza. 
My second visit, I went in to order some take out again and this time I was greeted by name. 
The sauces are hand made and they use organic ingredients, so you don't get that buzzy msg after effect. It seems to be a family affair, as Tom mentioned that his aunt was in the kitchen. 
When you check this place out, I would definitely recommend their salad rolls and a potato curry stew they have! It is unbelievable.

I read a review that vaguely mentioned Vegan chicken tacos at Hussong's. I checked their menu online but didn't see anything listed at the time for Vegans. Lo and behold as we were walking from our hotel room towards the casino, there it was... A sign out front asking us to try their new Vegan menu. Why hell yes we will!

Since we had $50 in dining credit for the Silver Legacy that this "cantina" is a part of, we put that to good use and then some for two meals at Hussong's. Out of the two meals we shared, we deduced that the Gardein chick-non needs to be flavored with more spices. You're better off going with the "beef" in whatever you order. It seems the cooks here haven't figured out how to season the Gardein or perhaps it's thrown in at the last minute without any real cooking at all. 

The service was great, their free chips 'n salsa dangerously addictive. I could've eaten several trays of those chips. Especially if you order a side of their tasty guacamole. 

As for the entrees, the thick, Daiya filled Quesadilla was the clear cut favorite between my sweetie and myself. My next favorite were the enchiladas. I can't really recommend the chicken tacos as the aforementioned chick-non was bland direct from the package Gardein with no Mexican inspired flavor to it at all.

So it appears the food can be a 2-5 star depending on what you order. I understand the 2 1/2 star overall rating  for Hussong's but I'm giving them an extra star because I appreciate that they offer a full blown Vegan menu. If it were just Gardein as a substitute I would be happy. The fact they have Daiya AND Vegan Sour Cream makes me ecstatic! Hell, I'm just happy when the rice & beans are Vegan at a Mexican restaurant. Now if only Hussong's can work on the overall flavors of their food, they would be THE place to eat in Reno.

Hussong's made this cutie happy and she didn't even order one of their gigantic margaritas: http://www.yelp.com/biz/hussongs-cantina-reno-reno#hrid:GKe8pbn1Ao48_cHnk0MMMQ

An excellent place to fulfill a sweets craving! 

They've got a mix and match option for small chocolate pieces into a box or you can buy a pre-made chocolate bag. The goodie bags are perfect as a small gift for your boss or friends!

Every time I've been here, they've had samples of their chocolates out by the register. The best ones I've tried had marshmallows and caramel in it. 

They're also right by Hub Coffee Roasters, so might as well grab some coffee while you're here. And they sell Rolled Mountain Creamery ice cream in the same building, but towards the back.

I've been on a burger kick lately. By lately, I mean my entire life. I was born with a cheeseburger obsession and, as I get older, it seems to only evolve into broader definition as to what constitutes a cheeseburger. I was formerly a strict traditional cheeseburger-eater. Mayonnaise was as crazy as I got. Now - bring it on. Give me your weirdest concoction. 

Imagine my delight when I opened the Pint Room menu to find the P-B-B & J Burger. Definitely not the weirdest concoction I've ever tried, but definitely one of the tastiest! Let's take this house down to the studs. The burgers here are made with a mix of Kobe and prime chuck. A seriously solid foundation for any burger. Now add sea salted peanut butter, candied bacon, Monterey jack cheese, strawberry preserves, and fresh strawberry slices. If you want to know what heaven tastes like here's your opportunity. Take a big, messy, delicious bite. Feel your heart swell with love. This burger is the best thing about Pint Room, in my humble opinion.

That is not to say there aren't other great things! The fries are pretty good. The onion rings are clearly superior. The Apricot Melt was fairly okay. I'm glad I had it, but probably won't ever order it again. They calamari was divine. Pickle chips, eh. Jo-Jo's a solid good. The root beer is on tap behind the bar and de.lect.a.ble.

To say their beer selection is impressive is an understatement. I fell in love with Illusive Traveler Grapefruit Shandy in a comfortable booth in the back on a sunny afternoon. Our introduction was thanks to Crystan - the lovely woman who provided some seriously top-of-the-line service. She delivered the right amount of friendly and pleasant, without ever hovering. Product knowledge wizard. She knows her stuff and if you're lucky enough to sit at one of her tables, take her advice.

The inside is comfortable, if a bit hipster. That staff has not been short on smiles in my experience. Last, but not least, the location is great as well. Just off main street and shares a sidewalk with a parking garage. If you hate street parking as much as I do, this is a really big plus! 

Bottom line, this place is great!!

Thanks to my fellow Yelpers for the recommendation of Silver Saddle! We had a great meal there last night. We were greeted warmly by the hostess and led to a booth. Immediately our server, Guisela, was at the table. She was one of the best servers we've had in Tucson. She had the qualities I value in a server: prompt and helpful, but not pushy and intrusive. Very knowledgeable about the menu, also. Husband and I got the prime rib, the daughters ordered ribs. Thank you again to Yelpers for mentioning the cheese sauce on the baked potatoes. Based on comments, we knew to order them with just butter and sour cream. The salad bar led me back in time, much like the decor, to eating out with my family as a kid. It's not very big, but all we wanted were four basic salads. The chilled plates and forks were a pleasant surprise. Another nod to Guisela, as soon as we were finished, the salad plates were cleared. 
Now the entrees. My daughters loved the ribs, especially the sauce. The fries were standard steak fries and the beans were an unneeded side. Husband got the Cowboy Cut, medium rare, and said it was perfect. I ordered the King Cut. Unfortunately I learned the hard way that Silver Saddle cooks their meat exactly as described. Usually to get medium I have to order medium well. This time, I actually got medium well. Finally a place that cooks meat correctly! The mistake was my fault so I will not blame them for the prime rib being overcooked. Next time, I know to order medium and I'll get it cooked that way. The baked potatoes were cooked perfectly, which sounds like an easy task, but we've gotten more overcooked, rock hard potatoes at steak places than you can imagine. Last, the decadent Mud pie for dessert. Absolutely delicious and big enough for all four of us to share. Paying the bill again took me back in time. I can't remember paying a cashier for dinner in years. Silver Saddle is old fashioned and nostalgic, but definitely in a good way. All in all, a great experience. We were searching for a new family steakhouse and we found it, thanks to Yelp.

This is the place in Tucson for candy! They have classics from my childhood that I thought were long gone, like candy cigarettes. The chocolate covered almonds, pretzels and English toffee are indescribably delicious and decadent. My daughters love all of the novelty candies like candy buttons, candy crystals, necklaces and old fashioned suckers. Another fave are edible, stackable Legos. My oldest commented on our last trip, " We're literally kids in a candy store! ". The employees are always friendly and helpful. They even put a bag of ice in the bag to keep the chocolate from melting. Great local treasure for kids of all ages.

I've spent a good portion of my life in New Mexico, so I was so happy when I heard that Tucson was getting a Blake's Lotaburger. I hope that what we experienced was due to the fact that they just opened. First of all, there didn't appear to be anyone in charge. All of the employees were obviously under 20 and didn't care at all about customer service. We ordered four burgers and they were all wrong. They looked literally thrown together and were undercooked. The fries and milkshakes were good, that's the only reason I'm giving two stars. The burgers didn't remotely resemble what I've had in New Mexico. We'll try them again in a month or two, but if what we had is the norm, this place is doomed.

You have probably driven by Trattoria Pasquale's a hundred times, without realizing that you're missing out on one of Tampa's hidden gems. This place has probably 10 tables and doesn't look like much from the outside, but your life will be changed for the better at this restaurant. The intimate nature of the restaurant makes it great for a date or a small family gathering. 

To make a reservation, you need to call their number or visit their website online. When you're putting them in your maps, don't forget "trattoria" or it will not pop up. They are also BYOB, so don't forget to bring your favorite wine to pair with your delicious food. 

And, speaking of the food...I highly suggest you arrive on an empty stomach. You will get classic Italian bread to your table with oil and roasted garlic in it (see pic - yum). I highly suggest the burrata appetizer, it's full of flavor and absolutely delicious. You cannot go wrong with anything on the menu, so choose whatever sounds good to you. 

They also have a "Big Night" where they host special evenings featuring cuisine from various regions of Italy. Check out their website for more info on this.

I really like Philly Cupcake. The cupcakes are not only works of art, they're also yummy! The only problem is that they're a little dry and I think there's waaay too much frosting. But I do love the creative flavors they have come up with, i.e., Green Tea & Honey, Carrot, Jewish Apple, etc. The staff there is helpful, friendly and personable and the decor is fabulous. Cupcakes are pretty pricey at $3 for regulars and $4 for "specials"  like the flour-less chocolate explosion, but sometimes it can be worth it. They also have vegan options which are surprisingly tasty. Not as good or memorable as some of the treats I've had from Brown Betty, but definitely worth a try.

If you're planning on eating here, don't eat anything else all day.  Be prepared to be extremely gluttonous and carnivorous.

The architectural design is impressive.  The restaurant is in a historic jewelry building and has high ceilings and beautiful chandeliers.

Our service was a little sloppy. Meat landed on our laps/ not on our plates a few times. The servers seemed very rushed.

All of the meat is juicy and delectable. The waiters and waitresses mostly come around with various types of beef (e.g. rib eye,  strip steak, filet mignon, prime rib) but there's also lamb, chicken, pork, and some seafood. They generally ask you how you like your beef cooked and will give you a piece to your liking. The end pieces are obviously more well done than center cuts. For me, the answer is always as rare as possible. 

They will also start your table off with sides. We were given polenta, caramelized bananas , and mash potatoes.  And there is a pretty spectacular salad bar with Brazilian salads, meats, and soups.  

They have some tasty cocktails and wine too.

The food will circulate until you tell it to stop. Each person gets a small piece of cardboard with a green side and a red side. When you want them stop coming around, simply flip it to the red side. It's not a great system if you have poor impulse control like myself.

Fogo is expensive but a really worth while experience.

The host here was so snotty. He urged us to go to another restaurant as soon as we arrived. As soon as we walked in he said "I think your group would be more comfortable at the restaurant across the street." He said there would be a wait but there were tables open. 

Our Australian friends jokingly asked if he didn't like Australians. He curtly replied "If I didn't like Australians you'd know about it." He was just rude.

One of us was Asian and there were mixed race children. Maybe he was racist. Who knows.

Sure we had kids with us, but so what? Others were eating with kids as well.

We went to another restaurant and had a great time.

He was working at 215pm on Sunday June 24th in case if his manager happens to read Yelp reviews...

This review is for customer service.  Haven't tried their boba yet.  

I go in on a Friday at 4pm and was told they are out of boba(tapioca balls) and I need to wait 30 minutes.  I can understand stuff happens and places run out of items.  But for a boba place, boba is an important ingredient...

What disturbs me more is the manager or owner hears me talking to the cashier about how I came just to try the boba (in a drink of course), but does nothing.  Customer service is important, especially for a new establishment.  We as consumers can choose to go where we want.  Aside from quality of merchandise, we look at service.  

The owner/manger didn't try to do anything to rectify the situation.  Not even like, "hey how would you like to try a drink without boba?"  Regardless if she would have offered a discount on the beverage for the inconvenience of them running out of boba.   Or "hey come back next time when we do have boba, here's a coupon for a dollar off."  Or something like that.  Bottom line she didn't seem to care to try and sale me something or earn my business.  

Perhaps I'm more into service and customer treatment then the average person.  For me regardless of the price point; from a coffee shop selling $3 coffee to a 3 Michelin star restaurant, I remember how they treat me and the customer service provided.  That's what helps base my decision of going back or not.  I still remember one of the first coffee shops I visited when I moved to Tucson. When the guy found out it was my first time at their place he told me the drink was on the house.  What a nice gesture.  Now I don't expect every place to do that.  But I'll tell you this, I still remember that nice gesture two years later.

This was the only restaurant I visited during my trip to New Orleans that was worth repeating. Marjie's Grill serves a type of fusion cuisine that I had never seen before, pairing Southeast Asian flavors with Gulf Coast barbecue dishes. The chefs slow grill their meats over coal Santa Maria-BBQ style in the restaurant's backyard. The selection of spices and produce used to prepare the vegetable sides are purchased from local farmer markets.

This type of food gets me excited, because it's inventive, local, and demonstrates culinary sophistication, unlike some trendy (but boring) Asian fusion concept nowadays that may involve permutations of tacos, buns, french french fries, heavy sauces, and meat.

I stopped by Marjie's for two casual lunches. The menu was simple during lunchtime with a few weekly options. Essentially, you build a one dish meal consisting of a meat, vegetable sides, and rice. You can add as many vegetable sides as you want to the plate, I would recommend trying two at a time.

During my first visit, I had the BBQ pork shoulder that was thinly sliced, slightly peppery, with charred edges, glistening of pork fat, topped with a garlicky and sour relish that tasted like a Thai or Vietnamese dipping sauce. On my second visit, I ordered the spice-rubbed Gulf fish that's delicately charred on the grill and topped with a orange peel-like citrus seasoning. The white fish was buttery soft, perfect to pair with rice, which is also locally sourced. Both BBQ meats were exceptional and perfectly grilled.

I thought that the vegetable sides were equally as brilliant as the meats. All of the vegetables seemed to have more pickled, bright, and sour flavors than expected, which makes them more complex and interesting. My favorite was the spicy arugula mixed with fresh mint, studded with sliced kumquat and dressed with sambal vin. What made this side special were the pure sweetness of the kumquats (even the peels) and sourness of the citrus salsa. I loved tasting these "dressings" derived from whole natural ingredients. The braised greens in chili vinegar was what I believe to be a creative take on Southern collard greens, but not prepared the Southern way of being bland. It's glazed and spiced up to be bright and pungent, reminding me of Thai flavors. I also enjoyed the cabbage w/ scallions & carrots, all briefly charred on the grill and topped with sesame. As for the most interesting side, I would pick the spicy green beans, apparently pounded in a mortar and pestle.

If you're in New Orleans, I would recommend checking it out. This place would be my first stop the next time I'm in town.

Several months ago we visited Stone House Cafe for dinner on a Saturday night. We didn't have reservations, but since it was nearly 8PM I wasn't expecting any trouble finding a table. Stone House Cafe gets busy on Saturday nights, so make sure to have a reservation. There was a bit of a wait, presumably because the empty tables needed cleaning, but we were seated an ordering food by 8:30P.

I ordered the steak filet, which arrived after about 15 minutes cooked as I requested. Unfortunately, it arrived without a steak knife. I waited a few minutes for the server to pass by our table so I could ask for one, but after five minutes I left the table and go find him. When I requested a steak knife for my meal, he told me there were none, and that he was waiting on fresh silverware from the dishwasher. I went back to my table, and patiently waited. Almost ten minutes later he returned with a knife, but by this point my steak was cold inside and out.

We didn't see our server again until he walked by our table and dropped off the bill. No follow-up visits to the table, and no water refills. My wife's pasta was fine, but I was made to eat a cold dinner after she had nearly finished hers. When I explained this ordeal to the cashier, she simply said 'sorry'.  I'm sorry I spent as much as I did on a cold steak and horrible service.

I left Stone House Cafe that night with the feeling that we were treated like we owed them something just for seating us without a reservation, and I should swallow the cold meal and be happy for it.  I'm not sure if Stone House Cafe is primarily a breakfast spot, but their dinner service and customer care that night was seriously lacking.

This place is amazing. This is not Boba. This is natural fresh juice/tea combo. This is so tasty and refreshing. Plus they are doing a BOGO this opening week. 

I am addicted. I think I'm gonna try and come here everyday for the BOGO deal. You can taste the pulp in the drinks and it tastes so healthy but in a delicious way.

Wish Special Fruit Tea is bomb. The Orange Tea drink is also bomb. Honestly, just take their recommendations. They also have free samples. 

This is my new spot.

Whiskey-filled, with equal parts craft and cheap beer and women dancing on platforms, you want your life to be Trestle Inn.

Trestle carves their niche as a literally stripped down resurrection of the former J&J Trestle Inn, which did the lord's work by serving such delicacies as the Fat P***y cocktail and posted signs to proffer you need not bring in your weapons. Raw, unadorned walls give the impression Bubbles from The Wire used to hole up here for several heroin-fueled days at a time. Personified, this place is the Black Keys before people like me heard of them. Maybe better yet, Trestle is a mostly recovered meth head. You still wouldn't lend them money.

The crack head chic decor is spread across two rooms. In one you'll move to beats that haven't been touched by Diddy, Flo Rida, or anyone interviewed by Ryan Seacrest. In the other you'll sit and drink up the courage to dance with someone on that elusive other side. In both you'll stare at go-go dancers tastefully shaking that ass. Tip 'em if you do.

The beer list is strong, but it's strong every where in Philadelphia. Drink whiskey here. If you're not drinking a whiskey sour ($8), that's fine, but you're missing out on the camaraderie. Bucking its role as the wife beater of drinks, there's almost a working class hero feel to the way they do it justice. The acidity is mellowed by the frothy egg white, which lays on top like a blanket of snow on a double wide trailer, making the inherent sour bite more fetish nibble than vampire wound that store-bought mixes lay on you. It's suspiciously refreshing for a whiskey drink. 

And, because your friend will ask, the bird isn't real.

Bartender is sexually abusive to female patrons, literally called a friend "slut tits" as she attempted to order a beer, and that wasn't the end of the sexual harassment to her or other females in the bar. Management was contacted, but didn't feel it important to call friend back to discuss with her. A post on their Facebook page was quickly deleted by the bar, but still didn't feel the need to talk with my friend. Great tap list, but it doesn't matter how good your product is when your staff is verbally abusive to a customer that's about to spend money in your establishment...

Finally they're back open after a remodel. Bathrooms have been redone so there is no longer a TV screen on the sink. 

Flowing Tide is your perfect hangout spot for food and drinks. Happy hour is the best and only time to go. Drinks and food are reasonably priced and is a perfect place to get your night started. If you plan on going to Happy Hour from 10pm - Midnight seating might be hard to find especially on the weekend, so come before 10pm if you have a big party. Service can be iffy at times but that's understandable when there's only one server for a big section. If you're looking for a drink with a few friends they have a fish bowl which is literally a fish bowl and is $20. They taste good and there's a decent amount of alcohol in there so it's a good choice to share. Overall, food and service are good and flowing tide is the perfect place for you to catch up with some friends and grab a drink.

I love their food but I haven't been back since they put up those white supremacist "Don't tread on me" flags on their building. It sends a real clear message about the owners. So I guess they don't want my business any more. ‍

Absolutely love Mr. Wish! I'm surprised I haven't yet reviewed it since I come here so often. I cannot walk by it without getting something for myself or the whole family. I love all their fruit drinks, you really can't go wrong. I love that they use fresh ingredients. 

I will say that I wasn't too much of a fan of the wish special fruit tea. My go to's are: apple sorbet and colorful fruit tea. The apple sorbet is refreshing and there are chunks of apple fruit and has a light yogurty flavor. The colorful fruit tea has many different fruit pulps and seeds in the drink- also very refreshing and delicious! I've tried their smoothies before too and they were good, but I tend to stick to my usuals. Give this place a try, you won't be disappointed!

You're in for about an hour wait on average.

Pork Ribs are the star here but they also offer brisket, turkey and pulled pork (among other things)

You can also add a 1/4 of any meat to your platter for $4...pretty cool.

You will see and smell smoke from the smokers located on the street...that's a good thing.

Pork Ribs - good
Burnt Ends - good
Baked Beans - good
Fried Corn - GOOD

It would be tough to make this a regular stop since the wait is so long and they run out of meat daily but it's worth a stop if you're in the area.

Nashville Yelpers, I know y'all don't know me, but I swear I'm a nice person. I give restaurants the benefit of the doubt, chalking up slow service to understaffing, or gross food to an abrupt kitchen change or a bad shipment. Then there's always the "off night" argument. But this, this was just straight up bad. 

Based on the reviews, my cohort and I chose Park Cafe as our dinner selection for our one night in Nashville. We pulled right up to the valet, asked him if we needed reservations, and he assured us that the place was typically packed, but tonight we'd be okay. We then walked in to an empty restaurant. Curious. 

The place feels more suited to those paying with Social Security than our young hip selves, but we decided to give it a fair shake and settled in with the menu. A lot caught my eye, but seriously, could this place have less of an identity? The menu was ALL over the place, from bread with chimichurri  to chili mac and cheese to crabcakes to caesar salad. Pick something and run with it, people. We decided on an assortment of appetizers: crab cakes, shaved brussel sprout salad, szechuan green beans, and the cheese souffle. What we got were "crab cakes" that tasted exactly like chicken, overdone and underseasoned green beans, a brussel sprout salad that tasted nothing like the sprouts I love, and a four-cheese souffle that reminded me of sweaty cooked brie. Needless to say, we left most of it behind, and nothing was even remotely good. 

Our server started off quite friendly and attentive, but after being assigned an admittedly high maintenance table of regulars, we were completely ignored. There was no mention of the amount of food left on our plates, and while we dined a seasoned waitress came through the restaurant to train a newbie, all the while loudly pointing out where the liquor was stored, how the owner likes the tables set, etc. 

If this is great stuff for Nashville, I'm seriously concerned for y'all's sanity.

Found them on Restaurant.com. We had a $25/certificate which means we had to spend $50. We got 3 - 14 inch sandwiches. Fries, onion rings,home made chips and a slice of cheesecake. That would have cost $57.50 before discount and tax. Too many $$$ for what we got. The meatballs and sauce had little flavor, roast beef cold sandwich was full of fat and the meat was close to frozen. The pastrami was OK but they did not prepare as requested. We were disappointed. Everything was pretty bland and flavorless.

Okay I'm gonna make it sweet and short, although delivery time was half the waiting time. Our food was just a disappointment the bread was soggy and chewy, super greasy. The salad that we order was just a bunch of wilted mixed greens and a couple of pieces and tomato, the Italian dressing was like jello. Over all no bueno we won't be eating here, especially when we can go to a Jimmy John's and get better quality at a great price.

The Ocean Hai is an Asian fusion restaurant in the New Clearwater Beach Wyndham Hotel. The hotel is new and the restaurant is fun and upbeat. 

My husband and I were excited to see the Omakase ($75.00 per person) option on the menu. After a long day it was nice to sit back and let the Chef surprise us. I made a request that red meat not be included in our selections since we visited a steak house the day before. 

All of the 6 selections were delectable and rolled out of the kitchen beautifully timed. This really enhanced our dining experience. I recommend dinning this way at the Ocean Hai. It gives you an opportunity to explore a large selection of the menu in small plates and does not disappoint.

I wanted to stop into Goody Goody Burgers for a quick bite. I don't know many restaurants that were established in 1925 and I wanted to experience it. The fact that they serve breakfast all day and have really good burgers is a bonus. 

My husband and I ordered the Original Goody Goody burger to share. It is made with their special sauce, onions and pickles. The hamburger was very good and I would order it again. We added fries and Goody Goody slaw to our meal. Our waitress suggested milkshakes so we went with strawberry and vanilla. They were perfect and complimented the burger.

The restaurant stayed busy the entire time that we were there. The staff was friendly and the kitchen was accurate and fast.

I wanted to try Alessi Bakery because of how long it has been in business. Over 100 years is impressive. The bakery was very busy when we arrived and the sales staff actively work at up selling. 

We ordered cookies, macaroons, eclairs, cannolis and brownies. The cannolis were filled with something close to a marshmallow. I was extremely disappointed in them. All of the other items were good. The macaroons were the best and a must order. The brownies taste like fudge and were very gummy.

I loved shopping at Dough. I am all about sweets and this cute little shop was a dream come true. The bakery is super cute with nice sitting areas and a comfortable laid back atmosphere. As soon as I walked in I was greeted by a very friendly employee and given a run down of all that is offered. Donuts, cakes, cookies, homemade ice cream, brownies and more. You can pre-order special occasion cakes for pick up. 

I purchased some cookies as a gift. They were boxed in the front of the store and looked wonderful. I did not order something for myself because I just helped devour Monkey Bread with bacon and an order of Funnel Fries at Datz. Although the entire bakery was tempting I could not take another bite. I did receive a glowing report that the cookies were complete deliciousness....Fresh, delicate and high quality.

After reading Yelper Rachel M.'s review of her visit to The Nona Slice House I had to go see for myself what a Death by Pepperoni pizza  taste like. It is almost a two hour drive each way from my house but if the pizza was as good as it looked it would be worth it. 

I arrived an hour before closing and was immediately seated with a menu. My waiter (Connor) was very personable and friendly. I ordered the pizza, wings and garlic knots. 

The garlic knots were wonderful. They came out crunchy on the outside and soft in the center. They were loaded with garlic and had a nice amount of fresh basil tossed on top.

The meat almost fell off the bones of the baked buffalo wings. They taste fresh but were not really spicy. The order came with a decent amount of blue cheese for dipping. 

I loved the Death by Pepperoni Pizza. I never had anything like it. To me it was like eating pizza toppings on the best focaccia bread ever made. It was amazing. The crispy edges were to die for. I took Rachel M.'s advice and ordered spicy honey to pour over my pizza. That brought it to a new level.

Mr Ed's Oyster Bar is a quiet little restaurant with great service. The atmosphere is relaxing and during our two visits the music was straight jazz. This made for a very enjoyable dining experience. 

Chargrilled oysters are what my husband and I eat in New Orleans and they do them right. ($18.95) They are the only place that we visited that had a price of under $20.00 a dozen. They are not as good as Acme's chargrilled oysters but they are the closest second in my opinion. 

Our oysters were fresh and not over cooked. The parmesan cheese mixed with the garlic butter was delicious. I really like the extra attention that they gave toasted bread. It came out with cheese baked on top. We  also ordered the Crawfish Bread. ($10.95) Since this appetizer is made to order I thought that it was going to be bread with crawfish baked into it. It is actually toasted bread cut open down the middle with crawfish dip stuffed inside. The dip is loose so it's a little messy. My husband loved it but I thought that it was just ok.

Jeni's Splendid Ice Cream is pretty special. My waiter recommended that I stop by on my first night in Nashville. He told me that it will be the best ice cream that I have ever had. He was almost right. Jeni's is definitely one of the best tasting ice cream that I have had. I have already planned a second visit. 

I ordered a half scoop of Brown Butter Almond Brittle and  a half scoop of Cold Brew with Coconut Cream. The  brown butter with almond brittle was hands down my favorite. I loved how light the ice cream is and how the flavor pops. In addition to my flavors I also tried the Pineapple Upside Down Cake and the Gooey Butter Cake. All of the flavors taste amazing. 

Covid has the restaurant closed down for dine in but there is plenty of places to sit outside.

I loved the atmosphere at Felix's Restaurant & Oyster Bar.  There are two areas for dining and my favorite is the small side area that feels like a diner. It gives you the opportunity to join In the conversation with the raw bar employees. They are a couple of old timers who have been working at Felix's for over 15 years. 

There is almost always a long line waiting to get inside and today we were lucky enough to beat the lunch crowd. We ordered our usual chargrilled oysters and loved them. They arrived at the table perfectly cooked and delicious. The only thing that I did not care for was the lump of butter that laid smack in the middle of the bread. The bread is supposed to soak up the garlic butter oyster drippings so the added butter gets in the way. 

I had a great time and the service is fantastic. I feel like Acme beats them when it comes to chargrilled oysters but they are a strong contender.

I loved my experience at Savannah's Candy Kitchen. As soon as I walked in I was greeted by the friendliest employee ever. He was making fresh pralines and offering up free samples. After my first taste I was hooked and had to purchase a couple. I thought that New Orleans had the best pralines but Savannah's Candy Kitchen proved otherwise. I will be back before the end of my trip so that I can bring some home. 

In addition to fresh made pralines they also sell loads Old Fashioned Candy, ice cream and a huge variety of chocolates. The women checking me out was just as friendly as the gentleman working in the front of the store.

This location is not as good as Acme Oyster House on Iberville St. This is more of a fast food restaurant where you order your food at a counter and have a seat with number. I just stopped in for their chargrilled oysters and immediately noticed that this location charges $3.00 more for a dozen oysters. ($22.99) The oysters were dry and the parm cheese was cooked into the shell. This made them not as good as the original location. The original location uses more garlic butter and this keeps them from over cooking and drying out. I also ordered the Boom Boom Shrimp and was disappointed that the shrimp taste old. The sauce on the shrimp was delicious. 

Acme is located in the Harrah's Casino so it's pretty loud and super charged with energy. There is lots of opportunity to people watch and enjoy the excitement. The staff was really friendly and the food arrived quickly.

For me the Gordon Biersch Brewery can be described as a solid "good" restaurant. Everything was good... the food, service, atmosphere and prices. Nothing stood out as fantastic or spectacular. 

Our table started with a salad, coconut shrimp and the pretzel with sausage. The pretzel was huge and came with about two table spoons of cheese sauce and two types of mustard. The sausage was on skewers and was dry and bland. The coconut shrimp taste good and was served on a nice bed of chopped mango. The fruit was refreshing. The steak and pasta entrees were served quickly and at the perfect temperature. Both of these dishes were average tasting....not great and not bad. The best item served at our table was the brownie dessert. The brownie had a deep chocolate flavor. It was served scorching hot with a side of vanilla ice cream

I heard that The Thirsty Marlin served excellent seafood so I stopped in to see for myself. It's a popping place that reminds me more of old Florida over a shiny new tourist type place. 

I ordered fish and chips and loved it. The fish was served hot and fresh. I could not have asked for more. 

The staff was friendly and upbeat. I will definitely return.

The Rutledge is a modern and upbeat American grill restaurant and bar. Like most bars and restaurants maneuvering through Covid the number of customers was down but it was still loads of fun being out. The staff was friendly and the service was attentive. 

I ordered the spicy tuna roll and a charcuterie board. Both of these items taste good with the tuna roll being the better of the two. The cheese on the charcuterie board was warm so it made me wonder how long it had been sitting out. Some of the edges on the cheddar cheese were hard. Since they are cut in cubes this is a good indicator of age. I was also disappointed to see that several of the grapes were mushy and should have been weeding out befor serving.

Lastly..they have delicious hand crafted cocktails that are the real star of the establishment.

Bittersweet Confections is a comfortable and trendy little restaurant on Magazine St. They serve breakfast and lunch items but I was there solely for the bakery. I ordered lemon, strawberry & grasshopper cupcakes...lemon & peanut butter bars ...and a turtle brownie. I left behind for another visit beautiful cakes, gelato, pastries, chocolates, croissants and tarts. They also offer mimosas, lattes and Irish coffees. 

The young women assisting me was quiet but warm and friendly. I could tell that she took pride in her job by the exceptional way that she boxed up my items. Every item was able to maintain its lovely presentation during its transition from bakery to hotel. 

I am not a huge frosting fan and dislike it when it overwhelms the cake. The grasshopper cupcake had a big ball of frosting on it so I scraped it off before eating. The cake was exceptional and the little bit of frosting that I tasted was very good. All of the other items were eaten quickly without a single complaint.

I spent several hours enjoying the JohnnyCash Museum.  It was voted the number one music museum in the world by the National Geographic Traveler and two other reputable sources and is located in downtown Nashville.  

The museum is stocked from wall to wall and room to room with every kind of artifact and memorabilia that you can imagine. You are taken through all of John Cash's life from the very beginning to the very end. There are music videos and interactive displays. 

At the end of the museum the door opens up to a store where you can purchase music, shirts and other souvenir type merchandise.

I stopped by on Monday (July 23) to inquire about the times, cost and what to expect from the classes being offered. The women at the desk was completely uninterested in giving a sales pitch or any information needed for me to make a decision on whether to participate or not. I felt as if I was imposing on her time so instead of signing up for a class I just ordered some pralines and left. 

The pralines were very good and the little store was pretty cute. They sell a small assortment of spices and tourist type merchandise. On my next trip to New Orleans I plan to stop in and give them another opportunity to inspire me to participate in the cooking school.

Big Ray's Fish Camp is a little shack on the side of the road. I never would have stopped if it wasn't for the great Yelp reviews announcing fresh seafood. Their motto is "From our Bay to your belly." 

I asked what was the best that they had to offer and this brought me to the Grouper sandwich. It was incredibly fresh and cooked perfectly. You have a choice of blackened and grilled or breaded and deep fried. I decided on blackened and was not disappointed. The Lobster Corndog. ($24.00 with fries) was the second most highly regarded menu item. I don't eat traditional corn dogs so this was a stretch for me. I decided to order one to taste. The  presentation of the Lobster Corndog is undeniably ugly but the lobster meat was sweet and juicy. I also ordered their coleslaw and enjoyed it with the grouper. It is vinegar based and has small chunks of pineapple.

We had a wonderful meal at Cafe Amelie. I definitely recommend making a reservation because this is a popular restaurant. The courtyard is lovely and completely relaxing. The service is fast and friendly. 

My husband and I started with the Amelia Baked Oysters ($14.00) and the Brussel Sprouts A La Planca. ($9.00) The baked oysters are made with creamed spinach and artichokes. Crostini is served on the side. The brussel sprouts are made with bacon and dates. Both of these appetizers were amazing even though the brussel sprouts were accidentally served cold. They were heated up quickly and taste good cold or hot. For entrees we decided on the appetizer size Shrimp & Grits ($13.00) and Pasta with Shrimp. ($27.00) The pasta dish is made with shrimp, corn and andouille macque choux. It is wonderfully cajun and spicy good. 

We ended with Affogato. ($8.00) It was served in a pretty martini glass and was the perfect ending to a great meal.

One star, only because I had to in order to write a review. The conveyor belt sushi is mediocre,  gas station variety but the rolls on the menu are better. There's better places for sushi in Boise. The reason that we will never go back to this place is because they are SHADY. after we closed out our bill and tipped one of the sushi chefs gave us a roll to try. We ate it, it was pretty good- fried jalapeño cream cheese it was really pretty good. But we did not order it, and we had already closed out our bill. We ate it because we thought the chef was being nice and we didn't want to be rude. So as we left my b/f put $10 in the chefs tip jar and we turned to leave only to have a waitress run us down to tell us we owed $6 for a roll we didn't order ! So basically we spent $16 on a fried jalapeño. Well spend that $6 dollars well rotary sushi because its the last dime you will get from us, and I have a big mouth and will be sharing this experience. Also, the name of your restaurant is horrible. Beware this shady establishment !

Some of you may not be familiar with the tart flavored yogurt or Pinkberry so I'll give a brief description. Think of what normal plain-flavored Yoplait yogurt tastes like but now in a frozen yogurt form and that's what you get! Hmm, maybe that didn't make it sound as good as it actually tastes. :P

Anyway, try this place! I love Pinkberry and all those yogurt places that are popping up everywhere but I was quite sad to see that Philly didn't have one until now. Woohoo!!

Steps to getting yogurt:
1. Grab a bowl
2. Head over to the 15+ different yogurt machines
3. Pick your poisons (go crazy with the flavors!)
4. Add dry and fresh fruit toppings (MUST get MOCHI and fruity pebbles!!!)
5. Weigh the bowl and pay per ounce
6. ENJOY!!!

My usual order: plain tart with mochi, fruity pebbles, mango, and kiwi. 

This place is actually part of Yogurtland so if you've ever tried that, it is very similar in terms of flavors. There are many different flavors here including the classic chocolate and vanilla. Other flavors include green tea, mango tart, strawberry tart, blueberry tart, plain tart, cookies 'n creme,  taro, snickerdoodle, and many more. I'm not a big fan of the green tea here. Either way, you will not get bored! While the vanilla and chocolate flavor is the typical creamier yogurt, the tart flavored yogurts are a bit icier and less sweet (which I like!). In terms of the flavor and texture of the plain tart, it is very similar to Pinkberry and not too tart as is Yogurtland (although it's from the same company). Texture is also good and does not melt fast. They also sell smoothies there but I haven't tried yet. 

In terms of their toppings, there's not much you can't get. They have all the traditional stuff like chocolate chip, nuts, cookie dough, sprinkles, oreo, etc. In terms of the more interesting stuff, they have MOCHI (again, MUST GET!!), cereals (fruity pebbles, coco puffs, captain crunch), and candy bars. They also have a good selection of fresh fruit such as strawberry, kiwi, mango, blueberry, peach, raspberry, etc. Like I said, how can you get get bored with a place like this?! :)

The place is also very clean and cutely decorated (see pic). The downside here though is that there isn't too much seating. Maybe enough seats for 15 people max.

In terms of price, it is a bit pricey. Definitely pricier than I'm used to. It's 49 cents/once (I'm used to 38 cents) but this place is definitely still worth it. 5 star just for being the first in Philly! :D

Just what I've been looking for! I've been having my cravings for cheap, good, and quick Korean food and restaurants in Center City just don't do it for me. Thank goodness for this place! It is very accessible in University City and is a great lunch spot for a study break. It does get pretty crowded but it's worth it. Most of their dishes are under $10 and since it's self served, no need for tip. Don't be expecting the greatest quality of food but this definitely hits the spot when you're craving some kimchi fried rice or ja ja myun. :)

Such cheap grocery!! Screw Superfresh ... this is so the place to go. Where else can you buy 4 lbs zucchini for $2.00... or 7 tangerines for a buck... or 2 bundles of asparagus for buck! Okay, I'll stop listing my great deals :P But really, this is such a great way for anyone on a budget to get good and cheap produce. They have everything you may need including bell peppers, apples, zucchini, peaches, grapes, broccoli, carrots etc! 

Besides the farmer's market, there are also a lot of great stores surrounding these few blocks. I like Darigo's Fish market as well as the various meat stores they have. It is also fun to check out all the yummy cheeses at Di Bruno's! Another one of my favorite stores is the Spice Corner where you can get just about any herb/spice you will ever need!

This is also a great spot to go for fresh pastas and to cook a great dinner. It might also be fun to take visitors here as well.

But way to go on commenting on a conversation  you never heard 100% of .

Ugh... I'm so turned off by this place. 

I recently took my out of town family here to try a cheese steak for the first time. We wanted to try both Pat's and Geno's so we ordered one cheese steak that we all could share. I asked if they had any plastic knives that we could use to cut the sub up, they said that I had to bring the sub back up here and they would cut it for me. I asked if she could cut it in four pieces, she scoffed and said absolutely not and that she shouldn't be cutting it at all for me... wtf? 

I'm not sure what the hell that means. They weren't busy, so it's not like I was in their way. They also have all of this shitty propaganda up that says, "we live in America, order in English" and they call their fries, "freedom fries". Uhhh... it's been ten years since that cute little joke came on the scene... we're friends with the French again. 

I think they're rude and the cheese steak was just okay. 

Go to PAT'S!!

During Covid they are limiting how many customers can enter the store. Makes it very pleasant to shop there. 

You can call and order items for my the fish or butcher counter ahead so it will be ready for you when you get there. Especially if you have a large or complicated order. 

Most of the other items you can't get online and they will also be waiting when you arrive. 

I loved how they did the Christmas cookies one or two at a time but you still buy them bu the pound. 

Also they  are slicing the bread for you instead of having the slicer out in front of the bread counter. Super convenient. 

They had plenty of cashiers and people stocking in case something was out of stock.

Wanna get chocolate wasted?
If you answered yes and if you happen to live in Santa Barbara then Chocolate Maya is the place to be!
 
Chocolate Maya is a small shop dedicated to all things chocolate. Right when you walk in you'll come face to face with large bookshelf's fully stocked, from floor to ceiling, with gourmet chocolate bars from around the globe. These shelves also house other chocolate flavored goodies such as hot chocolate mixes, chocolate mints, chocolate dipped goodies and more.
 
To the left is a long glass protected display case where their truffles are housed. They have truffles made from milk, dark and white chocolate and almost all of them are either filled with or topped with other creative ingredients. All the truffles in this case are made in house using the finest ingredients and they're all hand dipped and decorated by hand.
 
All of the chocolate I tried from Maya was great. We got one dark chocolate bar filled with figs and almonds, which was amazing. I also tried a few random truffles that were spectacular. My only issue with any of the chocolates I tasted was a white chocolate truffle filled with habanero milk chocolate filling that had absolutely zero spicy flavor. I was expecting some heat from this truffle but sadly there was none.
 
The woman who was working the day I visited was super friendly and worked as fast as she could to help all the customers in her shop.
Prices are a tad high but that's always the case with fine chocolate shops like this.
 
If you live in the area then I highly recommend you check out Chocolate Maya. Next time I'm in the area I definitely want to try their Spicy Sacrifice Hot Chocolate. I just hope it's spicy.

I lived in the Navona building from June 1st, 2009 to November 2010.
