Here is what you should know before you consider leasing here.  The Piazza is a ton of fun, and your friends will LOVE to come here and hang out.  But YOU will have to be here 24/7.

1.  Only VERY social people who don't mind music thumping through their walls, screaming drunk girls downstairs, mass crowds of the local city folk attending weekend events in their front yard, and light peeking through the blinds should live here.  

2. Northern Libs, and especially the Piazza, are very pricing per square foot.  $1800 a month won't get you much space here.  Definably go for a place with an outside deck. 

3. We have experienced two murders while living here.  One in the building, and one as the girl was leaving the Piazza about three blocks away.  "Todo, we aren't in Kansas anymore. "  Don't let the crowd fool you...No Libs is still central Phila.  

All in all the 18 months were fun, but I moved out and on to quieter pastures.  

Good luck!

Great place for an evening out.  The fried pickles were my favorite, but everyone had something delicious.  Excellent selection of beers, decent live music, and servers that knew the menu and walked us through a terrific evening.

A very comprehensive menu consisting of good Vietnamese dishes. Simple decor and swift, friendly services. 

Of the three dishes I sampled, the grilled shrimp was the best: faintly sweet peanuts over grilled shrimps on the bed of radish and lettuce, delivering a combined taste of alternating bursts of char, bitterness and refreshing sweetness.  

The second was a very passable lettuce warp. They may have forgotten to drain the excessive fat of the crumbled dark meat and the chicken mixture was a bit runny. And you have to peel the leaves yourself. 

The restaurant name should be reflecting the dish in which they are supposed to specialize but the Pho turned out to be a disappointment. 1. Underneath the soup bowl the coaster plate was missing. Be careful if you try to move the bowl; it was very hot. 2. They forgot to include a spoon with soup. 3. The bowl was small that the soup almost spilled out, leaving very little buffer space to put the herbs in. I decided to eat some soup to lower the water level, but again, realized that there was no spoon. 4. The beef was fulled cooked instead of being medium rare. 5. The broth had a very strong star anise-like flavor. The additions of basil and bean sprouts failed to manifest. I'm OK with the spices but I'd prefer balanced layers where subtle flavors can shine.

Interesting Chinese masks and bowls on walls and  wooden booths inside the long, stylish space. We came here for the Sunday brunch. 

The restaurant seems to have steered the food further towards the Southeast Orient and we found some dishes come with a southeastern twist on the foundations of eastern Asian cooking, with western touches also in evidence. For instance, the Breakfast Ramen bowl came with Chinese wheat noodle in a pho-soup like broth, topped with slices of Japanese braised pork belly. While the southeastern connection is indisputable, the dominant palate seems to be Korean. Expect, then, crispy fried chicken wings tossed in sweet and hot sauce that echoes a kimchi marinade; beef bulgogi over tater tots in a dolsot bibimbap stone pot with gochujang paste and a sunny-side up egg. 

We chose two shareable plates and both were sensationally good. The Korean chicken wings were simply irresistible: the flavors are splashed on with vigor. The steamed sticky rice in lotus leaf has glutinous rice mixed with a heap of ingredients such as chicken and mushrooms. The food parcel was served unwrapped but the aroma lingered; we enjoyed smelling the wonderful scent imparted by the lotus leaf as we tuck into the rice. 

I'm going back for the Sunday brunch. Just hope the kitchen can create new classics or seasonal items to enrich their menu.

Somehow it's easy for me to miss Bubble Tea's narrow frontage. The interior is just as small as you might expect and the room rather dark and drab like a dimly lit basement.  

For milk tea I would prefer C17. But long queues on some days indeed be the testament to the fact that this place has carved out a reputation for serving some nice flavors. Staff was friendly and never hasten customers despite long lines. 

The menu covers Chinese and Taiwanese standards, such as soy sauce chicken, beef stew noodle soup (succulent meat) and crispy chicken (very salty). The cooking usually takes forever. Last time we ordered two dishes to go. After 15 min wait, we were bored and starting to count how many fruits there were in the mural paint.  My friend and I couldn't get consensus because he had a tally of 27 fruits but I got more than that... Whatever, that killed time. Our food was finally ready by the 30th min.

The bubble teas are artificial but nontoxic of course. I have never seen a single tea leaf or a drop of milk being used as the ingredients. Maybe they had the tea steeped in the morning I don't know. There are flasks of colored liquid, quite iridescent being displayed in a row. A few drops of the flavoring agents your sensory cells will tell you this is your favorite strawberry. Service is quick: you can get your drink in a minute.

I enjoyed coming there for weekend brunches (dim sum) because they serve some of the most authentic Cantonese food in St Louis. It is not exaggerated to say that they have the best dim sum and I really love their food, until we found a broken bobby pin, (or something like segments of a wire) in their custard tart. That day my friend and I were having dim sum, and he told me something clogged his esophagus. He swallowed it after some first aid. We found there were more broken pieces left in the food.

He did not want to make a big scene so we paid the bill and left. But I probably need a while to forget this incident before my next visit.

We ordered a dozen of tacos or so. The tacos arrived beautifully arranged on a specially designed metal board, sophisticated and in good taste, displaying complex layering of flavors with spices, citrus and chili. Among the fillings were fried fish in Chipotle Baja sauce, fabulous pork carnitas accompanied by beef brisket or roasted duck, grilled chicken with bbq sauce and onions. Carne Asada came in both tacos and the Carne Asada fries.   

Inside the restaurant was a bit nightclub-like at night, dim and loud, not a perfect place for food photographing. There is an impressive bar for those looking to settle in. By comparison, wood tables and teak benches outside the restaurant provides more room for friend gathering. 

The biggest issue is the dimension of the menu. The menu is very simple, containing sections of tacos and tordas to burritos, but short of other varieties such as quesadillas, enchiladas or ceviche plates. I didn't find dishes containing shrimps in any form either. Churros feature on the dessert part.

Overall,3.5/5.

We visited pappy's thrice in a fortnight, and found the food consistently excellent, the service informal but informed. 

Menu is concise and short but there's certainly plenty to get your teeth into. Pork ribs, beef brisket, burnt ends, pulled pork, meat combos... Smoked pork ribs oozed flavor, grilled to melting softness, with sides further enhancing the credentials. Go hungry.

My friend and I are both fond of this creole bar and kitchen, not least for the fish and seafood that features heavily on the menu. Seriously good taste of creole cooking of shrimps, fish and all types of meat. Wings, burgers also feature and as expected, breakfast with waffles, proper biscuits. Our lunch kicked off with Jerk wings and three pieces of different charbroiled chicken breasts (S.O.S), followed by two orders of entrees. Both were very generous in portion. The 4 Horsemen were partitioned by 4 sample dishes ranging from black bean stew, crawfish in creole sauce to shrimp and sausage jambalaya, chicken with garlic prawns in Cajun spices. 

We were surprised by the imagination of the extemporaneous instantiation in the entree IDK, which was loved by my friend, besides, the deviation from our preconceive vision as reminiscent of a beach hut like maritime-themed furnitures or jazz, soul and blues music. The atmosphere was laidback, fun and welcoming, helped along by the emollient nature of the staff. The walls are painted with spring-green and grey paintwork, and in addition to simple blond-wood tables and chairs, the spacious room was decorated by arcade machines and a pool table. Expect, also, games and matches and occasional yelling, providing the soundtrack to the bites and booze.

Heaven for milk tea aficionados, but do not expect Chinese green tea or English Earl Grey in here (they don't serve breakfast either). Available is a big choice of fruit and milk based bubble teas, featuring a generous number of boba per cup. 

The place also serves a large choice of East Asian desserts like juices, smoothies and fluffy ice. One can also choose from a range of toppings (red bean, flavored jellies, aloe vera, etc.) and sweetness level.  

The new menu is pretty, with three chapters introducing their bubble teas/juices, freshly made noodles and some authentic Chinese and American Chinese cooking, where dishes are clearly explained in colorful diagrams. Dishes were very well represented and the ingredients were fresh with impeccable provenance in our last visit. 

There is also a spin-off takeaway called Joy Luck on the eastern side.

So... quite a few things that make this place unique. And quite a few things that make this place a disparate world from a stereotypical Chinese restaurant. Oh, and they won't give you fortune cookies after the meal.

We came here largely for the ceviche but were also happy with the grilled meats and skewers..

The ceviche was obviously the star of the show. Ceviche de Pescado came as a sublime starter. Cured fish teamed with mussels and shrimps, speared with fresh onion slices and sprinkled with toasted corns. The fleshy cuts of halibut (or sea bass I'm not sure) soaked in tongue-tingling leche de tigre were very well thoroughly marinated and the lime juice was amazing. Perfectly sharp acidity, tempered by sweet-potato chunks, with an excellent kick from the chili. I'd recommend it to anyone who loves ceviche and leche de tigre. 

All dishes we tried were carefully crafted, playful and imaginative. I sampled Saltado de Langostinos. Jumbo shrimps sautéed with sweet onions and tomatoes, nicely matched with a rice dune garnished with sliced pepper slices and corns. The dish was enjoyable. Waiters with a warm smile. Amazing service and handsome decor.

Friendly staff and quick service. Food is good and fresh and reasonably priced. 

One of my major cavils that barely costs them one star is the location. Secluded and sequestered, residing in an abandoned, deserted mini-mall (or more precisely a dilapidated remaining of a former mini-mall), with its shopfront evading from the street, the restaurant posed a real test for my google navigation and it couldn't seem to find it easily as it found other Vietnamese places in the area.

Buggy water: They served me a glass of ice water refill --- with a dead bug in it. They must have seen that we did not order any nourishing snacks and gifted us this supplementary bug protein water. Nice treat. I certainly wouldn't miss such rare occurrence and took a few pictures. 

Too bad that I forgot to take pictures of their kitchen and how they processed ingredients. Please do not be deceived by the cosmetically clean and well presented dishes, and be aware of the unhygienic food.

I have visited many Vietnamese restaurants of all sorts, from small traditional pho house run as family business to fine upscale dining restaurants. Pho of Pho Long is by far the best I've ever had. The broth is fabulous, perfect texture and noodle cooked just right. High quality beef brisket, slices of round steak and ox tail. The tail is so tender the meat falls off the bone. We're now back for the second time.

Offering Vietnamese dishes alongside a selection of options from elsewhere in Asia, the place seems to pride itself on using all fresh ingredients and fine herbs and spices. Vietnamese dishes range from spring roll varieties to Com Dia, egg noodle, vermicelli (Bun) and a solid range of pho noodle soups of beef, chicken, seafood and tofu. 

The pho was great; flavors were full and true, and textures good too.  The spring roll peanut sauce was impeccable we all love it. 

We experienced two negatives. 
1. Menu scope. The menu exhibits fairly intimate authenticity in Vietnamese, versus some attempts on traditional Thai, a barely light touch on Chinese, and a separate catalog of basic sushi. 
Teriyaki Wok and American-Chinese stir-fries show the versatility of the menu, but we expected more culinary expertise, technical depth and capabilities under each category, for example, Banh Mi or green papaya salads were missing on the menu, Thai food options were minimal.  

2. The place seemed to be understaffed on our Saturday afternoon visit. We never saw the waitress again after the meal served. Later we had to troop across the room to the cash desk to pay.

The cute little restaurant takes its name Truc Lam from the word for 'bamboo forest/grove'. The interior decor, therefore, showcases different bamboo paintings on walls and ceiling. The tome of the menu contains nearly 100 dishes, filled with recognizable Vietnamese dishes, ranging from all types of rolls and  salads to bahn mi sandwiches, seafood like sea bass and a range of pho noodle soups, rice platters and noodles. 

The previous review stated that this place makes the best pho in STL, which is quite a claim, but the version here is certainly excellent. Less sweeter than the souther Vietnam pho soups, the broth here was appetizingly more salty with cleaner flavors. The starters were excellent too. The shrimp spring roll was generous with shrimp and fresh herbs, shredded pork skin, and came with a well-seasoned dipping sauce. The beef banh mi had a crisp baguette crust, and filling of fresh flavored aromatic vegetables and marinated beef.

Food is first class and good value, flavors bringing the best out of each dish. Service prompt, efficient and friendly.

At first I didn't put high expectation on this place because of the name. We tried the Chirashi (Chirashizushi) and several Nigiri, and we were wowed by all. 

The Chirashi was awesome. This place offers great Edo-style Chirashi, which is served with several kinds of seafood (raw fish and shrimp) that are arranged artfully on top of the sushi rice in a bowl. The fish were fresh and nicely cut. The sumeshi (sushi rice) could be a bit softer but does not mar the overall quality. Since we did not have United State-style sushi I couldn't comment on the special rolls. 

Hole in the wall. The decor is fine, not great, but it gives the place character. Nice friendly service too.

We found this place a little plonked on a silent side stretch of the Olive Road, at the corner of a strip mall, but definitely worth a visit despite the location. 

The menu incorporates traditional Korean dishes such as sizzling stews and bulgogi, together with the All You Can Eat grill and also, some Korean-Chinese dishes; with both English and Chinese descriptions supplementary to menu items. Service was good and informative and the interior was slick. Clean furnishings, including tables fitted with grills, good for family-style eating and table-top cooking. 

The AYCE barbecue meats such as beef/chicken bulgogi and short ribs were well marinated, and grilled at the table by efficient helping staff. The unlimited LA galbi was wonderful. So was my friend's favorite: pork belly: gently charred, with a tender center and a decent line of buttery fat along one side. There will be a scallion pancake, a stone bowl of umami-rich soup and a dozen of banchans. 

One minor complaint: we left the place with a very heavy cooking odor and my friend's glasses coated with a layer of oil. Hope they could install an exhaust pipe system.

Went there on Saturday. Endless meat and great service. BUT... this place suffers from fly infestation. 

The food we got from the salad bar attracted a fly and the abominable pest had been haunting us for the next 45 minutes until we left. The fly hovered over our food and kept trying to land on our meal. We waved it away multiple times but this persistent little creature just wouldn't give up any opportunity to share the plates with us. 

I finally surrendered to it and decided to let the fly make entrance. The dignified and graceful fly landed on the stage of my check folder and crawled up on my fork. Then with skill and dexterity, it cheerfully flew to my raspberry cheesecake, started slurping the whipped cream and laying parasite worm eggs in the sweet cradle of my cheesecake. 

More than just a paltry nuisance, flies are a symptom of a greater problem inside a restaurant and reflection of poor management as well. They eat poop and garbage and lay eggs in the food coming out of the kitchen. Food was really good at this place but please terminate these bacteria transmitters.

Stylist decor abjectly fails to counterbalance poor hygiene and dirty utensils. Inexpensiveness scarcely makes up for the substandard food quality. 

Refills of water hardly dissolved the dirty coat in the seemingly unwashed cups and empty plates boldly bragging about stains and dried food residue.  

Very limited selection of food, (less than 25 items) and mostly American Chinese fare such as crab rangoon and General Tso or the like. The sushi fish was stale. The sushi shrimp tasted rotten. The rest of the food was lukewarm and dry like it's been sitting there all day. A small live cooking station that mimics the Mongolian grill. Diners watched the bored chef at work as they make stir fry over the teppanyaki. 

A bonus star for the low price.

An authentic Korean Restaurant in Greenwood?!

I was shocked (in a good way) that a Korean Restaurant appeared in my google search so close to home. When I moved down to the south side I left behind the few Korean restaurants on the north and east side of Indy. I was CRAVING Korean food today so I stopped by after work.     

The three ajumma's (respectful word for women) run this restaurant called Unnineh (sister's). They renovated and recently opened Sister's on Feb 12th.  

When I entered I was greeted and sat at my table. First thing on my table was a nice warm glass of tea. Following the tea healthy poritions of bonchon (side dishes) took over my table. The bonchon was all very tasty and they would stop by and ask if I wanted more of a certain kind which was nice. I ordered the Yukgaejang (spicy beef and vegetable soup) which came boiling in a clay pot! If you get a soup that comes this way, be careful as it is extremely hot. I would recommend letting it simmer down and indulge in some more bonchon! The Yukgaejang was cooked just right, just like grandma makes it in Korea. 

The experience was excellent, the ajumma's are all very nice and accommodating, and the food was authentically delicious. This is definitely a must try for south siders. I will definitely be coming here often! 

If you aren't into Korean food or haven't tried it before I would recommend the following to get you started:
Jjajangmyun - black bean noodles YUM!
Bibimbap - rice, veggies, and meat that you mix up!
Bulgogi - broiled beef, can't go wrong with that!
Kalbi - korean staple. It's main ingredients are soy sauce and brown sugar which makes it a very sweet and tender short rib!

If you love calzones, then this is the place for you! I had heard about this place from a coworker, so we decided to stop by here on the way to a Cards game one night. I wish we had gone on a normal night as the calzones were so big we couldn't even finish them, and since we were heading to the stadium, we didn't take our leftovers. Next time we will know. 

I ordered the Meet me in St Louie, and my SO got the Which Came First? All the calzones come with a side of dipping sauce. You can get the recommended sides, which we did, or pick one of your choosing. The Meet me in St Louie is basically a big meat pizza calzone with meat sauce as the dip. Very big, and very cheesy! This is what I imagine as the prototypical calzone. The Which came first had chicken, bacon, jalapenos, egg, and cheese with a salsa verde side. This one was very tasty and a great combination of ingredients, and the salsa verde was a nice touch to go with it. 

We will be back to try their other calzone concoctions!

First and foremost, I love St Pete and the entrepreneur spirit that it has. It is my utmost desire that all businesses grow and thrive. 

With that being said, just coming back from my first experience with 2nd & Second, this was the most disappointing dining experience I've had in my 4 years of living here. 

For starters, the poor host seemed to be absolutely drowning, between trying to clear and clean tables, take names and seat people, I was tremendously confused why there was no one busing tables. In fact, there was a manager standing behind the counter the whole time we were there, and instead of busing tables that looked gross, he just stood there, chatted with customers, and occasionally ran food out to the wrong tables. 

Our server was an incredibly nice lady who was a victim of the circumstance of a poorly run restaurant, who apologized more times than I could count for the wait time (which was just fine, I can't remember the last time I didn't wait on Sunday morning at a diner) and food serving time. 

Once the food was served, the amount of homefries we were given was laughable. I know that may sound ridiculous, but it was served on a massive plate, only to have the homefries maybe take up a 1/4 of 'their side' of the plate, with the BLT+AE on the other side. Also, the homefries tasted like the previously frozen (wether or not they were I don't know) kind I was served at camp when I was a kid, as did the extremely burnt bacon. The BLT+AE was absolutely delicious though, so big win there.  

I understand that this is their opening week, but I have been to so many restaurants opening weeks, and none were even remotely as bad as this. 

My advice to management is you need to get your hands dirty. If you set up your staff so they are overwhelmed due to too few on the floor, lack of training, or whatever, it is absolutely unacceptable to stand behind the counter and survey your kingdom while they are trying as hard as they can to provide a pleasant dinning experience. 

In the land of diner options in St Pete, 2nd & Second has a long way to go before doing battle with polished behemoths like Trips Diner. 

I'll give it another shot at some point, but for now, my suggestion is to give them some time to hone in their operation.

What a cool place! I read that they had spiked hot chocolate which was my only motivation for coming here, ha. We walked in a little after 6 on a Thursday and the place was hopping. 

Community tables are everywhere along with the typical games you find at the area beer gardens. They have a good happy hour drink menu from 5-7 consisting of cocktails, beer, and wine. 

We didn't get anything off the HH. My husband got the pear Moscow mule, which he loved. I got the spiked hot chocolate with the mint liquor. Bonus that they have a table off to the side to garnish your hot chocolate with (caramel, marshmallows, chocolate chips, etc). We also loved the caramels and chocolates. 

Before we left, I had to check out the view from outside (even if it was frigid!). Those views are unbelievable. I can't wait to go back in the summer!

Fun casino, but so smoky!!!!!!! I was there for an hour and a half on a Sunday and left smelling like an ashtray. It is a nice, upscale casino, with several bars. I was there on a Sunday afternoon during happy hour and there was a good 80's band playing in one of the bars. 

Servers seemed to come around often and the penny slots paid out often. I had alot of fun and like to come back when I am in the area.

I came here during the first brunch service which also happened to be Mother's Day. Since they are just fresh off their opening, it was pretty easy to get a table. Albeit, the table was so crammed into a corner that it also made the table next to it completely unusable. It seems they might want to do something about that arrangement. Onto drinks! I had a fresh and spicy Bloody Mary and damn if that tomato juice had not been fresh squeezed. Tomatoes from our locally famous Wilcox farms down the road? I wouldn't be surprised. The Man had the Country Breakfast which was beautifully prepared and a side of bacon. We were a little worried about the portion sizes so we all ordered sides, but I think it was probably unnecessary. But the bacon was fantastic and really, who argues with bacon? I had the biscuits and gravy and it was perfectly executed. I'm a real biscuit and gravy purist, coming from Ohio and all. Most restaurants should be banned from even having it on their menu. However, Proper did a creamy, thick gravy loaded with sweet sausage over a fluffy biscuit. Perfection. I can't argue with the prices. They seemed quite reasonable, at least for brunch. Sure, this place sets a new bar for the hipster foodie set (really apothecary jars for your water???) but I think it means Tucson has finally arrived.

Okay, I don't mean to wax poetic here but this is the real deal. This is fresh scrambled eggs, generous hunks of bacon, a balanced amount of perfectly cooked potatoes, just enough cheese to hold it all together, and an enormous fresh tortilla bundling it like a small swaddled infant. This is the platonic form of breakfast burrito. 

I'll briefly mention the salsas which have just enough acidity and spice to play off the richness of the burrito. The star was a smooth guacamole from the bar with a real kick. Watch out, gringos! This ain't your guac from the suburbs. 

Look no further for your breakfast burritos. Cast aside your Nico's, your Los Betos, and dare I even say it - your Ponchos. Because we have arrived.

If you want to "wow" some city slickers, this is the place to take them.  As you walk up, you see the biggest BBQ pit ever and old timey western music floats out the open doors.

This is really Tucson, at least, as you imagine it 80 years ago.  And then to boot, the food is fantastic.  You can never go wrong with the filet but the beef ribs are great too.  The beans are basic and good, the salad is smothered in heart-stopping dressing, and the texas toast, well let's just say it brings back the only fond memories I have of elementary school lunches.

They often have live music performed by a geriatric (in a sweet way) County-Western band.  And don't go requesting any bluegrass because this is a WESTERN band.  Sometimes the geriatric band is feisty.  

Per a fellow yelper's request:  There are no prices on the menu, but everything is around the same price.  The waitress always tells you what cuts of meat they have that evening and the prices hover around $20.00-23.00.  Usually the cuts are filet, ribeye, porterhouse, beef ribs, pork ribs and chicken.  I think the prices are really reasonable, because the meat is better than Outback quality, not quite a Morton's, so somewhere in between.  All the steaks get so smoky from being cooked on the pit, way more flavor than you get from your gas grill at home.   

Great atmosphere, good prices for quality meat, and fond memories for your city slicker friends.

I have been pretty underwhelmed by the cheesesteaks I have had in Philly till today, I have found a clear winner, thanks Molly T! So the place looks like a small, narrow diner and has very little going on in terms of decor but that's fine, the cheesesteaks are great and that's all that really matters. Also, it's cash only. 

The food:

Cheesesteak Wit Whiz- I was so surprised how much I liked this, I always had the preconceived notion that Whiz was for tourist. Well, I am a Philly tourist and I enjoyed the cheese in a can on my cheesesteak. It was surprisingly really moist and my hands down favorite cheesesteak. Also, the onions were no teeth required tender, they were so good and added a nice richness to the cheesesteak. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=1MgcIcgDXBNjTzFV_hStgQ&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Cheesesteak Wit Provolone- It was good but it was missing some sexiness. It was solid but felt like it was missing something and this cheesesteak also came out less moist. The bread is nice since it holds up to the meat and doesn't fall a part, but I do wish there was some type of crunch on the bread, but that's just me. Adding a touch of ketchup does a nice job cutting some of the richness.

Overall, it was a sad meal, I was so excited to try this but at the end of the deal, our meal was a miss. We were one of the first groups to come in on New Year's Day and our food was disappointing on various levels. Pro tip: if you are waiting on line, there is a grocery store across the street you can grab some beers and wait on line.

The food:

Fried Chicken- I ordered dark meat because I think dark meat is the way to go. This was the main reason we went and it was our biggest disappointment. The good thing was the chicken was juicy but the bad thing was it was so incredibly salty and greasy. This was a miss. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=q3JdLQJIb18Pa4Hya38qRA&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Mac and cheese- This was another miss, the noodles were cooked to death and the mac came off really oily, you could actually see the oil coming out of the mac. Also, the peas kinda threw me off, I don't think they really added anything.

Fried Okra- I normally love fried okra but the one I had lacked flavor, lacked seasoning and it was oddly firm for an okra. 

Cornmeal Muffin- This was the highlight of the meal and it has to be eaten once served, once cooled, it becomes gummy. Overall flavor and texture when warm was great.

It's a pretty popular place at the Reading Terminal, the place had a bunch of employees and a pretty decent line but I wasn't sold on my sandwich.  

The food:

Hershel's Pastrami on Rye with mustard. I think my expectations may have been a little high since I am used to the great Jewish delis in NYC. The pastrami here missed the mark for me. I thought the pastrami was chewier than I expected and it didn't have that nice velvetiness that I am used to in pastrami. I also felt it had some gristly pieces that were off putting. The rye was standard but the mustard did have a nice pop.

I found this place from a Yelp search since I was swinging by Reno and I was happy with my meal. The place is a popular option and the prices were very reasonable and there is a 10% discount via Yelp when you spend over $40. The restaurant itself is very basic but the service was friendly

The food:

Crispy Popcorn Chicken- In the New York area, we call this Salt and Pepper Chicken. I thought these were great. They were perfectly fried without being greasy at all. They were nice and crunchy and had a nice seasoning to it. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=XeKjNKTRhnb3tauYlryk7Q&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Spicy Chicken with Basil- In NY, this is three cup chicken. This is a staple dish in Taiwanese cuisine and the one here was respectable. I enjoyed the flavor but it was too sweet for me and the chicken bones were kinda dangerous. There was a good amount of chicken bone fragments throughout with tiny points, so be very careful. The stir fried ginger pieces were excellent, but make sure to not eat the chili, they pack a punch.

Sautéed Green Beans- These were simple but it was prepared well. It was stir fried string beans and the flavors were respectable. It's a good veg dish to get.

Zha Jiang Mien- I thought this was just OK. I thought the noodles were overdone and kinda gloppy. The flavor of the sauce was alright but it was on the greasy/salty side.

A La Mousse is a very cute place to grab dessert, it's a cafe/dessert bar in the heart of Philly Chinatown. The shop is very similar to what we have in NY and the one here was well represented. The decor is modern and a comfortable place to sit, relax and enjoy your dessert. The place is trendy and the atmosphere is nice so it is really popular amongst the college kids, kids love this place since they offer sweets and girls really love this place since it's pretty and they offer stuff with sugar. lol 

The food:

Double Chocolate Cake- I thought this was really good, it was nice and chocolatey but it was shockingly not as sweet as I was expecting. When I first saw it, I automatically assumed it would be really sweet but I am glad it was not. It had a nice balance of chocolate flavor and sweetness, I am a fan. The best way to describe this, it was a chocolate mousse cake and a really good one at that. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=NT54NdFiqUh97wXUEAwxGw&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Bubble Milk Foam Black Tea- This was nice and refreshing, the tea had a good black tea flavor and the texture of tapioca was nice. It had the right amount of chew without being too soft. The flavor as a whole was good. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=C-wFhjX0zi4v7lRPXpCvzA&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Original Crepe Cake with Whyy Experience Ice cream from Bassetts. I thought the crepe was nice but a tad too soft for me and it was on the eggy side. The Whyy Experience ice cream was good, it was vanilla ice cream with chocolate covered pretzels swirled with butterscotch, it went well with the crepe. https://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=Jf9LiAZIEjDfk43-7ob7qw&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

After reading all of the glowing reviews of this place, I decided to finally try it out for myself. I chose Sauce on the Side for my birthday dinner with my husband. We came about 6:00 on a Friday night, which seemed to be a good time. When we arrived, we had our choice of open tables, and by the time we left, people were stalking us for our spot. 

The concept is easy... pick your calzone or salad from the large menu on the wall, order at the counter, choose a seat, and wait for your food to be brought to the table. 

My husband started with a caesar salad, which I wanted no part of. I saw the dessert calzones listed on the menu too and I was saving all available space in my stomach for that... not lettuce. He claims their caesar is one of the best he's had though. I ordered The Roasty Toasty (pesto chicken, arugula, red onion, toasted pine nuts, mozzarella, ricotta, garlic, and a pesto sauce) and my husband ordered The Duke (BBQ chicken, applewood smoked bacon, corn salsa, smoked cheddar, mozzarella, smoked chili oil, and a BBQ ranch sauce). Both calzones were enormous and delicious. We somehow finished every last bite and still had room for dessert. Hey, don't give me that look! It was my birthday! The nutella banana with mascarpone cheese won out over the caramel apple pie. We couldn't finish this chocolate monster, but made an impressive dent. I could come here just for dessert... it was THAT good!

There were several other unique combos that I'd like to try, so I will definitely be returning. And yes, I probably will order that nutella banana calzone again even if it's not my birthday. Nutella can make ANY day special.

Why yes, brunch. I SHALL go to you. 

Bloody Mary bar from their own vodka? Why, yes please!

Delicious veggie omelet? With a side of bacon? Why, yes thanks!

The food is solid and the bloody mary bar, while spendy, is worth it. The food prices are slightly cheaper here than at comparable higher end places in the Garden District/Uptown. 

I would definitely go back and try out their other offerings as well!

Let me first state I love how any stupid idiot can write a review. First before you go to this place know that it is a asian restaurant. So guess what their will be asian dishes?!?! Omg so many people complaining how the lobster is prepared. Or how this restaurant is trying to make dumb white people happy and yet they complain. 

Let me start with saying I'm so glad someone finally brought a higher class buffet to Tucson. The sushi is good and their dishes are on the higher end scale of what other asian buffets offer. 

Their dinner menu is far better then their lunch but it comes at a price increase. Raw oysters and raw fish alone makes it worth it. They also add crab. Asian prepared lobster and asian ribs. 

Only thing I can think is people are under the impression that somehow for the price of 14.95 that they are getting Vegas Buffett quality. And no it is not on that level. But for 1/3 a 1/4 the cost it's at least half as good which is amazing for Tucson. 

One thing I will note is it seems to be quite a few struggling people in Tucson. But to give a review as though 14.95 is expensive a part of me feels sorry for you. 15 bucks would be $ dollar at the most $$ and their are some here making it seem like it broke the bank and then put unrealistic expectations for a cheap buffet.

i stopped into philly cupcake today and had such a pleasant visit!  the first thing i noticed when i walked in was the magnificent smell!  it reminded me of how my house would smell when my mom went on a baking binge.

the next thing i noticed was how cute the space is.  indeed, i kept saying, "this place is SO cute."  

the owner (i think) immediately greeted us.  he handed me a menu and was very friendly.  i told him i wanted to buy cupcakes for my mom's birthday, but would have to sample the wares first.  i ordered the red velvet cupcake and my husband got the jewish apple.

i only recently tried red velvet.  this is probably the fourth red velvet baked good i've ever had.  philly cupcake's red velvet is a bit different than my previous examples of RV.  it's less dense, but more moist.  and, i swear it had a hint of a crunch in the outer layer.  hard to describe, but it was a good thing.  not an overwhelming chocolate taste.  i might have preferred a bit more chocolate flavor, but i am a chocolate addict.  the icing was light and not too sweet.  there was almost too much icing for my taste.  but that's not really a complaint.  i just wiped some of it off.

my husband enjoyed his jewish apple cupcake.  he said it tasted like his mother's.

after such a successful tasting, i ordered a half dozen assortment of cupcakes for my mom's birthday.  philly cupcake is cash only.

i wish this business much success.

Alright, so I've been to this place twice before, but both times with groups of friends on a summer weekend night...those experiences were pretty good, but yesterday's experience requires a one-star rating.

I have NEVER had such poor service in my life! And I used to be a waitress, so I know how I am supposed to be treated. Like a few other people who rated PYT recently, I had a groupon that expires today, so on my way back from the shore for Memorial Day weekend, my husband and I decided to stop at PYT on the way home to use it. We also had our dog with us, which I didn't think would be a problem since I've seen several dogs in the Piazza before. 

When I asked the host how long it would take for a table in the shade (it was like 95 degrees yesterday), he said maybe 30 minutes. That's not too bad, so we decided to stick it out. We hung out in the shade, I gave my dog a bowl of water, and we patiently waited for them to call my cell, to tell me that our table was ready. The host eventually called me after about 45 minutes, to tell me that he didn't think a shaded table would be available any time soon since people have just been hanging out for hours and hours. He said there was a table that wasn't quite in the shade, but if we wanted to sit, he could set us up. The table had a little bit of shade, so I thought that was okay since we had our dog, and after all, we were hungry.

He sat us down and gave us menus, and quickly brought out waters for us, which was nice. He said that the servers were switching shifts right now, so we should expect a delay in service. Okay, that's fine...thanks for the warning. We didn't think the delay would be as long as it was. It was actually so long, that we ended up leaving without a server coming to see us! There was a table of 3 people right next to us that had their server come out a few times to check in on them, and the server was even talking about buying them shots on the house. Not once did he look at us, not even to tell us that someone would eventually come over to take our order, or even to refill our waters. HELLO PEOPLE, WE HAVE MONEY TO SPEND HERE TOO. 

Needless to say, it was an awful experience. I won't be going back there anytime soon.

I'm not exactly sure why I had such a hard and persistent bagel craving whilst I was in Philidelphia... but I can tell you that I didn't just happen upon this bagel place. I sought it out in a similar fashion to an addict seeking out his next fix. 

It's one of the highest rated bagel places in Philidelphia, and for good reason. The bagels are delicious, the service is fantastic, the place is clean as a whistle, and that matzo ball soup #PlacesOpenPalmOnChestAndLooksAway. Man that matzo ball soup. That matzo ball soup gives my matzo ball soup a run for it's money, and then snatches its wig! 

I kept sipping at it and trying to figure out what was in it... being like... my matzo soup will become better if I can figure out what herbs/spices I'm tasting. Dang Honeychild! 

I got a bagel with everything on the side. I'm very methodical about my bagel set up. Gotta get the cream cheese on the side if you're toasting your bagel. And you should ALWAYS toast your bagel; brings the bagel to life. If you have them put it on, the cream cheese starts melting and all because you need to wait for it to cool down from the toaster. 

Also, I like getting some whitefish salad, tomatoes, and if I'm feeling indulgent (swiss cheese) on the side. That's Mike's perfect bagel. Everything toasted bagel, scallion cream cheese on top, white fish salad, then tomato, then swiss cheese. I know what you're saying. That's a lot of cheese. Well of course it is... we're going for perfection - not just greatness. 

Everything here was super fresh. I would go back in a heartbeat when I find myself in Philadelphia again. Also a great place to work! They have wifi and a good deal of space. In a really cute neighborhood too!

The amount of horseradish on the shrimp cocktail warrants a Physical Activity Release Waiver or at the very least a disclaimer from the waitress with memorandum of understanding. 

After putting a whole shrimp drenched in the sauce squarely in my mouth, I felt inextricably connected with the Mike B. in another dimension that was just dared to eat a fistful of wasabi and rose to the challenge with gusto. 

My lord almighty. 

I mean... I never thought I would be able to hit the high note in Alone by Heart but then I had the shrimp cocktail at Harry & Izes
 
Prime rib slider is a must have. 
The salad I got was quite good and the salmon was cooked perfectly. 

You just watch out for the shrimp cocktail.
Is gonna get you 
Even after I swiped off like 80 percent of the sauce, it was still like eating a cup of spicy mustard dipped in liquid nitrogen on a parasailing trip in Alaska during the winter. 

It' ain't playin'

Located in Reading Terminal Market - Four Seasons Juice Bar is pretty unassuming. 

Looks just like a little stall... with a bit of wheatgrass for decor... and I'm assuming juice. 

But man... did I have one of the most delicious smoothies I've ever had in my entire life from this place. I asked the cashier what was in the smoothies and she told me that it was just fruit and ice. 

So I decided to order the Tropical Island ( I believe it was called) cause I've randomly been craving a Pina Colada recently... and this pretty much sounded like a Pina Colada (Pineapple, coconut, banana). 

The cashier told me that this was like one of the only smoothies that they use canned coconut milk because they can't get legit coconut to blend into the smoothie well. I completely understand that. Have you ever tried to dissolve or cook down coconut... it has like the strength of a thousand anvils. It doesn't really break down easily. 

So I get my smoothie... go across the way, take some pictures, and then have a sip and fall in love. 

I'm telling you... it has to be the freshness of the fruit their using and the quality of the coconut milk... cause that smoothie with pretty much only 3 ingredients was so stupid good. I want it right now... and in perpetuity... every day... for the rest of my life. 

Not surprised that Four Seasons has 4.5 stars with 114 reviews. 

I'll gladly add my resounding excellent rating to this small little spot that you should definitely visit if you're in the market. 

Also, fun fact - Brian Wang the owner of the juice bar has worked in Reading Terminal Market since he was 25. I'm not sure how old Brian is now... but lets just say... he's clearly not in his 20's anymore. The juice bar used to be a noodle bar before it was a juice bar. Just learned all this from a little video on the Reading Terminal Market website. 

Thanks Brian and team!

I've been waiting for a long time for a good boba place to open, and this place passes all of the tests!! I ordered a specialty drink, just to see what they were made of - the strawberry shortcake. Milk smoothie with strawberry boba and jelly, topped with graham crumbles. I added some Matcha pudding, since it peaked my interest. I'm glad I ordered 50% sweetness, because the jelly's had a lot of sweetness already. But it was all so tasty!!! Definitely coming back to check out the rest of the extensive options. Oh! And to try their shaved ice!

Café B. is a new Ralph Brennan restaurant Old Metairie.

I was so excited to be at Café B on the night of their grand opening, Tuesday, 10 May 2011!! I found out that I now hold the honor of being the very first customer to eat a meal at their cool bar! The bar is where most of us single people tend to gravitate to vice a table, which can be a bit isolating for one. I'm so glad this bar is spacious and comfortable. My only recommendation is to add bar hooks (for purses and such).

The decor is light and fresh, with hints of the Bayou area reflected in the artwork. The bar is well stocked, with a decent wine list, which boasts wines from the 1920's, 30's, 40's, 50's and 60's+. The staff was attentive and curious about whether the guests liked each dish and cocktail. The staff was casually dressed in starched white shirts, blue jeans and striped waist aprons. Parking is either in the adjoining lot or via their valet service (which is a nice feature if the small lot is full).

I started with the "drink and 'b' merry!" menu and had the sparking pear. It's made from Absolut Pears vodka, a hint of peach schnapps and topped off with sparkling wine and floating pear orb. Overall, a refreshing and subtly strong cocktail but it could stand a hint of sweetness or possibly a muttled pear vice an orb. My orb was turning brown. Eric, at the bar, made me a second one and added muttled pear and a splash of simple syrup. It made ALL the difference.$8.50

Next, I chose the Creole Crab Dip, which boasts Lake Pontchartrain lump crabmeat, housemade Creole cream cheese, scallions, toasted chevre and brioche points. Overall, the delicate sweetness of the crabmeat was masked by the heavy use of scallions. Interestingly, the culminating flavor was bland. Also, for a dip, it was VERY loose, akin to a sauce, not a dip. $13

The soup and salad course was two-fold for me. I first had the Crawfish Tomato Bisque made of Breaux Bridge Crawfish, roasted Louisiana tomatoes and hints of brandy. This was very light, bordering on bland. It reminded me of the reason why such soups are started with a seafood broth vice water. Since this is a "Bayou" dish, they might consider adding a generous dash of Tony Chachere's seasoning, or the like. $6

By contrast, I thoroughly enjoyed the Pear and Pecan Salad, which celebrated the marriage of ripe pears, farmers market greens, toasted Louisiana pecans, Steen's cane syrup vinaigrette and manchego cheese. This was delicious! Fresh, crunchy, bitter, sweet and savory, all on one plate. The salad is accompanied by two warm, delicious rolls that are clearly the rich cousin of croissants. Flaky and light.$8

On their 'b' sweet eats menu, I ordered the Pecan Praline Bread Pudding, which featured housemade pralines and bourbon toffee sauce. It was warm and tasty and garnished with strawberry, blackberry and delicious chunks of pralines. A beautiful presentation. The texture of the pudding was perfect- the bread was not overly heavy and the pecans added a nice layer of flavor and texture. The sauce was a well-executed complement. I highly recommend this dessert. $8

Like many of us younger folks living in Old Metry, it's so nice to have a dining option in the area past 9pm! On Friday & Saturday evenings, Café B plans to be open until midnight, serving a limited bar-type menu.

This would be a great place for a Yelp event!

I'm a huge fan of spicy. I started out weak but I feel like I have a decent resistance to anything high on the Scoville Scale with the exception of the hottest ghost pepper sauces. I walked into this dimly lit establishment and decided to sit and their bar area. 

I was craving curry chicken... 

The place was fairly empty for a Saturday but the Yelp reviews reassured me that this is decent Indian food. The bar tender quickly set me up with the cold Coors Light but I assured him that I did not need a menu. "Curry Chicken, extra spicy...throw in some Naan too". He seemed to hesitate for some reason but none the less put my order in. Shortly after, a gentleman came up to me to clarify that I did in fact ask for this curry to be extra spicy. I confirmed and sealed my fate. 

I shook hands with the devil. 

This was some of the spiciest chicken curry I have ever eaten...but not unfairly spicy. I seem to have a problem finding an Indian restaurant that has tender chicken but this place got it right. Each bite was a fiery inferno of deliciousness. I chatted for a little while with someone who seemed to be the manager. He told me about how they grow their own chilli peppers and some other ingredients as well. Oh, and the naan was fluffy and perfect for dipping. I haven't eaten Indian food too many times unfortunately but this place ranks up there as some of the best I've had.

The vibe to this place is great and so was the brunch, definitely recommend making reservations, we did through Resy. 

We sat in the lounge and the ambiance with upholstered chairs and sofas was that of anthropology meets a whisky lounge. They had hand sanitizer on all the tables and the staff were all wearing mask 

The French toast were incredibly decadent and more like a bread pudding. The potatoes were so perfectly crispy and accompanied with a nacho cheese sauce, avocados, pico de Gallo , chives and the unfortunate part a hard poached egg. Even though the egg didn't have the runny consistency of your traditional poached egg, the meal did not disappoint. Honestly cannot wait to go back! The service was great too

We started the meal with the fritto misto and buffalo mozzarella. The fritto misto came out first but I wish that it never came out. This was terrible the seafood was overcooked and felt terrible in my mouth. The seafood also had a stanky odor which detracted from the taste. 

Buffalo mozzarella was served on nice thick slices of toast which was quite good. The basil honey was a quirky color and is surprisingly good on cheese and toast!

The pastas came out and I laughed my ass off. The tortellini looked like the world record holder for smallest bowl of wonton soup. This was $20 btw. I'm a pretty tiny human but I could actually eat ten bowls of this. Please reference my photo attachment.

The tagliatelle was not great. The noodles were left to boil in the water a bit too long and were tough to chew through. 

Dessert was a fun little treat. But nearly impossible to cut apart with a fork. I should have asked for a knife or chainsaw. No real flavor in the custard. 

Service was great! Drinks were brought out in a timely fashion and plates were cleared between courses. Bravo!

Not sure what others ate here to warrant the rave reviews. Maybe I just ordered all the wrong stuff. If I ever come back I'll just order four servings of the buffalo mozzarella, I'll pass on everything else.

Went here for a quick coffee and breakfast during the weekday. Atmosphere is very chill with a feel of a community learning center that serves craft coffee. We sat in the front window where the chairs were vintage and the area was open air. The comfortable ambience was perfect for the mission of the cafe-to serve the community. Staff was friendly and prompt. The only downer I experienced was that they had a special breakfast burrito on for the day but ran out of tortillas?! Ayeee, for the special at 10am? It was ok. I recovered and ordered the scramble which was splendid. House coffee was superb and overall enjoyed the experience. This is a place where I can enjoy great coffee and get work done.

it's probably a 2.5 buffet. I give 3 stars because the service was great.

First make sure you get the buy one get one free deal otherwise it's absolutely not worth it.
(This buffet offers quite low quality food, even though there were some interesting seafood selection, their selection feels, looks and tastes a bit cheap)

I doubt the seafood is fresh (by fresh I mean live or at least non-frozen) but I ate a lot and didn't get any troubles.
You can find every declination of seafood, steamed, in sauce, Mexican style, boiled, sauteed...etc
Crab legs were poorly cooked, it was a real struggle to get the meat our of the leg.

Desserts are OK and there is a large selection.

Of course I write this review when I am once again (read: always) hungry. Went here because I was craving good clean food. This place did not disappoint!!! It will definitely be added to the rotation. 

So, I ordered the nachos, because they sounded amazzzzing. They WERE amazzzzing, too! They were loaded with goodness and vegan cheese (YESSSS), veggies and cilantro and beans and guac and ohhh, that sounds so delightful right this instant.

For dinner, I ordered the Taco Salad. It also was delicious. the nachos, though - I am telling you - were like rays of sunshine on my tastebuds! I am a cilantro lover, so there could have definitely been more cilantro, but that is my preference. 

Service was great, food outstanding, and i like that they don't try to rush you through your meal. I appreciate that, Thank you! The prices are reasonable, and I cannot wait to return.

Thank you for the wonderful experience - cannot wait to sample everything on the menu!!!

Dear WalMart, this is your official "Dear John" letter. I am not going grocery shopping in your store ever again.   I am sick and tired of your shelves not being stocked on Monday morning.  Other stores do it. Why don't I shop on a different day you ask?  Well, Monday works out for me. 

I am sick and tired of you only having two or three lanes open for check-out.  I am sick and tired of your card readers not working properly.  I am sick and tired of your cashiers not knowing how to work 

We have been together for a long time and I'm sure that my not coming back anymore isn't going to hurt you at all.  Guess what!  It's not going to hurt me either. 

Bye bye Felicia.

Charlie Gitto's on The Hill is one of the best Italian restaurants on the hill.  It out ranks it's own Charlie Gitto's downtown.  I suggest that you make reservations. Although the restaurant is rather large, it fills up quickly and early.  They do have valet parking. 


We started with a Sicilian garlic dip. If you love garlic, you will love this dip for bread. It is a little messy so be careful you don't spill some on your shirt or blouse (we both did). Next up, the veal cordon blue for him, the special ravioli (shrimp and ricotta cheese) for me.  His came with a side of gnocchi.  His veal was very good (he let me try it) but the gnocchi was gone before I could get a bite. My ravioli was outstanding. Of course I took the left over garlic dip and poured it on them.  They were great. I had two left over and took them home for breakfast and put an egg on them. Delicious. 

Dessert?  Yes, you are at Charlie Gitto's. You have to try a dessert. I didn't feel like sharing that evening so I made him get his own. I went with tiramisu, he went with the Italian cream cake. They were both outstanding. 

Would I come back here?  Yes and I'm not going to wait a long time. I saw a few items on the menu that had my name on them.

When my husband asked me where I wanted to go for my birthday dinner, I didn't hesitate to yell out Twisted Tree. As I've said before, this is my favorite steakhouse in St. Louis. Even on a Tuesday night it's packed so be safe and make reservations. We were lucky that two people were leaving the bar so we commandered their bar stools. Luckily for my husband the baseball game was on their television. 

After getting our drinks (a birthday margarita for me) we decided to share their crab Rangoon. This is delicious and I think that it is made in house. It is stuffed to the gills with crab and comes with two different sauces that were both outstanding. I actually wore some of it home on my shirt. 

Onto dinner - WHAT!! You get a salad and a side with your meal. That's what makes Twisted Tree my favorite steak house. He chose the regular salad and I went with their Caesar salad. I do have to say that I preferred the way it use to be served - brought to you on a plate. This time it was served in a salad bowl for you to serve up. As usual, their croutons are the best. 

We both ordered the prime rib. He got the asparagus as a side and I got a loaded baked potato. I seriously could have eaten my entire prime rib but i felt I shouldn't act like a pig. The next time I will. The steaks and sides were yummy.   Dessert?  Of course, the best dessert in town. Wedding cake with ice cream. We had a choice of three different ice creams but being a traditionalist, I chose the vanilla. The cake just melted in your mouth. 

Would I come back here.  Yes, I will and I'm going to try the onion rings that everyone raves about. And that's the way it is.

We have passed Trattoria Marcella many times on our way to Ted Drewes and we finally decided to give it a try.  After reading fellow Yelpers reviews and reading about reservations, I was a little apprehensive to be going without them.  We were able to grab the last two seats at the bar.  The bar area wasn't crowded until a little later on and the restaurant itself was packed.  I'm not sure about parking because we Ubered there.  After ordering cocktails, we looked over the menu. As we were looking at the menu, bread and hummus was given to us.  What a surprise that was.  The hummus was outstanding.

We decided to share the toasted ravioli.  The menu says it is house made and I believe them.  Just the size alone was enough to convince me of that.  They were very good as was the sauce that came with them.  Our main courses consisted of chicken and spinach cannelloni and spaghetti and meatballs for me.  Our food was brought out and we dug in.  I did get to try his cannelloni and it was excellent.  My spaghetti and meatballs was very good also.  The meatballs (2) were huge.  Yes of course we wanted dessert and we got the traditional Italian fare - tiramisu.  It was the best either of us have ever had.  I would be surprised if this wasn't made in house.  It was so fresh and the lady fingers were so soft and spongy.  Delicious.

Would I come back here?  Yes and I also think I would make reservations just in case.

How do you go to Tony's and not give them five stars.  The service was impeccable, the food is to die for and the atmosphere is lovely.  They have relaxed their dress code although some men are still wearing sports coats or suits.  There is valet parking in front along with a coat check in the restaurant.  No sitting at the bar here - you want the true Tony's experience.

We started with appetizers, the steak tar-tar for him and the carpaccio for me.  Both dishes were outstanding.  Then we decided to get the primi cannelloni for him and the special of a white asparagus salad for me.  I did get to try his cannelloni which was the best I have ever had.  The white asparagus salad was also topped with blue cheese crumbles along with the dressing.  It was delicious.  On to our next course.  The veal trio for him and the Dover sole for me.  Both dishes came with a choice of sides so the potatoes for him and the creamed spinach for me.  I was able to try one of his veal (piccata).  Melt in your mouth.  My sole was outstanding and they debone it tableside.  A lot of the dishes are done tableside.  Even though we were full, we had to get dessert.  The cheesecake was wonderful and they also brought small sugar cookies with it.  Both dishes were delightful.  

Would I come back here?  Yes, there are so many items on the menu that I would like to try.  If you see me here, stop by and say hello.

We had a wonderful stay here. No lines to check in and we were actually able to check in early to our standard king room at 12pm. Plus!

Room was located on the fourth floor and it was clean. Bathroom had a magnifying mirror that works well when applying makeup. The bathroom door was right in front of the toilet. Strange spot for the toilet to be there, but there really wasn't a spot to put it at so it worked.

The staff at the hotel was very friendly and helpful. If you look lost they will approach and help you. That is very rare as most places, they just ignore you. 

Our room didn't have a view, but we didn't spend much time in our room as we spent it walking in the mall (hotel is connected to the Outlet Collection Riverwalk) and the RTA is a short walk to catch a cable car. The RTA in front of the hotel is temporarily suspended so the cable car doesn't go that way to pick up. If you walk near the aquarium the Canal St station is working. This hotel was conveniently located to all the tourist spots we needed.

The hotel is renovating the main pool, but the other pool is open. They are really trying to maintain the hotel since we saw the maintenance men painting rooms, working on the air conditioner and steam cleaning the carpets daily.

The health club is fancy! It closes at 9pm. Indoor tennis courts, racquetball, squash, volleyball and basketball courts. There is an observation deck where you can sit and watch games from above. Sauna and whirlpool inside the ladies locker room. Gym was a good size with plenty of machines where you don't have to wait for anyone to get off the machine. I was pretty amazed about how big and cool the health club was. It is $12/day for hotel guests to use the health club. There is a salon and massage rooms inside the health club. Pretty cool spot.

While catching a flight back home it was convenient to eat at the airport since we wouldn't get back home until after 2pm. I remember seeing a Zatarain's in the airport so I decided to grab a gumbo to go. Zatarain's is known for their spices and herbs so I had to try it.

I walked in around 11am on a Saturday and found a spot at the bar easily. The server took my order of shrimp and sausage gumbo. She warned me that they were out of bread and I was ok with that since I wanted to try the food. The server was courteous, attentive and packed the gumbo nicely. Despite the other reviews, I had good service. Thank you!

When I got to my seat near the gate, I was disappointed. I couldn't find any shrimp at all. I did however see chicken and sausage in the gumbo. Pretty disappointed that it didn't have shrimp. I added Tabasco for spice. The gumbo was ok. I was expecting something with more flavor since they are known for their spices and disappointed it did not include shrimp. I would not recommend ordering the gumbo.

In lieu of the fabulous $4.99 breakfast at Cal-Neva's Top Deck, my Amtrak travel partners from Walnut Creek practically railroaded their L.A. counterparts into trying the notoriously pricey and abundant offerings of Reno's Hash House A Go Go at Harrah's hotel-casino.

The night before this breakfast, I had an enlightening chat with the Hash House greeter, who encouraged me to share an entree because almost everything on the menu is enough to satisfy two patrons, and is priced accordingly.

He had told me sage-fried chicken breast is their signature menu item, so I suggested that two of us split the SFC breasts & waffles ($14.95).  Our chicken tasted great, the coating was crunchy, the meat was moist.  I added salt and pepper to perfect the flavor.  Fried leeks as garnish lent a unique taste sensation.

The waffles were another matter.  Pressed with strips of bacon inside and drizzled with a maple reduction, you'll want extra syrup, which will be Log Cabin or its ilk.  Further, the batter is dense and the waffles are served soft and doughy.

My travel partners' basic breakfasts were A-OK and sensibly sized and priced.  The only service issue was having to ask for butter and jam for biscuits, and extra syrup for waffles.  Refills of ice water and their hearty coffee were frequent.

One last story:  The restaurant was nearly empty as we were leaving, and I asked a waiter whether on a future visit the chef would accommodate my request to deep-fry the waffle to make it crispier on the outside.  After consulting, he returned to say that the chef would give it a try, and asked if I'd like to stay and sample the result.  But, of course!

The waiter brought out a waffle quarter with syrup and said that kitchen staff liked the modification.  I did, too.  So if you think you'd like your waffle prepared this way, let's start a movement--order it "Frisco style."

mmmmmmmmmmmm sooooo good! 

Cute teeny shop w a v. nice selection, including vegan choices. Not the cheapest around, but pretty fun/out of the ordinary flavors makes that ok. 
Even the packages are cute! 

I recommend the ice tea to wash down the sweets! 

The storefront is very eye catching! and I LOVE the display cases

Saying what everyone says- we love Mr Lee! And the food is great too. Went and threw an order for 15 different sandwiches at them when I was hosting a meeting in West Philly, and they handled it like champs, with a smile, and gave us some free cheesy fries and carrot cake to boot. :) Amazing Philly cheesesteak, and a whole variety of other sandwiches and comfort food. Vegetarian food with good flavor! Cole slaw with a perfect balance of sweet and sour! Swing by west philly and make friends with the lovely staff, and you'll get a delicious meal out of it too.

Not sure why everyone thinks this place is the bees knees. Yeah, it's a cool kind of retro diner with modern accents with clean lines and open to the outdoors. The wait staff are super friendly and prompt. The place looks busy all the time so I guess people do like the food.

Since they claim to have "famous hamburgers" that is what I tried. The first time I came here I tried the Royale with Cheese. It's a solid burger and tasted good but nothing to write home about. Reminded me of a Fatburger out in California but smaller, I still remember Fatburger because they are so good (they used to have them in Tampa but are all gone, did not taste the same for some reason). The next time I tried the Cheeseburger Pox. Smaller then I expected it to be. This Pox sauce does absolutely nothing for me and this is supposed to make the burger "famous" I had to throw some ketchup on it half way through to make it taste better.

There are much better burgers in this price range, I realize it is not a $10+ gourmet burger. There are other fast casual places nearby that taste better at this price point.

I ordered coleslaw and the waitress told me not to get it because she thought it was horrible so I ordered onion rings instead. They were ok, both times on the greasy side.

They do have other food stuffs here and their pies look really good as do their shakes. So maybe people like the other things on the menu but I won't be coming back for those POX burgers. I will probably come back as I have an office down the street but I would never make a special trip to come here, especially since it is a busy place.

This is probably one of the best BBQ joints in the St. Pete/Tampa area. I was expecting to walk into a grungy hole in the wall but it was so nice and shiny clean inside with shiny wood tables, wood paneling and a long bar area with flat screen TVs on the walls. They have a decent selection of local beers as well as the standard Buds.

The BBQ itself was delightfully delicious! Tried the three meats combo with Pulled Pork, Spare Ribs and Brisket. The pulled pork was great with no overly fatty pieces in it, the spare ribs were cooked to perfection and the brisket was the best I have had in a very long time. It was so good that my very picky wife who didn't really want BBQ for dinner actually said this was a great choice for dinner tonight! This was the fastest I've seen my family eat BBQ with no leftovers, we usually always have leftovers!

They have two sauces, one spicy and one sweet. The spicy was more tangy than spicy, kinda like a North Carolina style but not exactly. It was good but could have been higher on the scoville scale. The sweet was not that sweet at all which was great because I hate overly sweet BBQ sauce like almost every other place has.

The sides were quite good as well. The coleslaw was awesome, again not too sweet but tastes like coleslaw should taste. The Baked beans again were not overly sweet, the beans I thought were perfect. The fastest side to go was the bacon mac and cheese, I was only able to get one bite in before it vanished so I really can't comment on how good it was. 

The only thing I wish they had here is baby back ribs, they are my favorite bbq item and not a lot of places have this. I must say that their spare ribs are so good that I don't mind not having baby backs. I also would not mind if they had burnt ends. Perhaps in the future. This will be my go to BBQ joint.

You need to try this place. I've bee to 4Rivers for lunch a few times and as recent as just a few days ago (S Tampa) and this place is superior. This place is definitely the best tasting BBQ in St. Pete - I've tried them all. I will definitely be a repeat customer.

This place has good Indian food, one of the better ones in the Tampa Bay area one of of two that are the best in St Pete. I have been here several times for dinner and lunch buffet and have used bite squad to deliver to downtown St Pete. 
The dinner menu has all the essential Indian fare and all of it is really good and spice level from zero to Indian hot is an option for all the curries. 
The buffet usually has some good stuff including lamb and goat which is usually missing form other buffets. 
The space itself is large but does not have the usual decor that most Indian places have, there are a few posters on the wall and a Ganesh at the cash register and they were playing new age music last time I was there. I actually prefer the overly Indian decor with the customary sitar or Bollywood music playing in the back ground.
The food is top notch, the beer selection is good, they do have a full bar. The wait staff is friendly and service is relatively fast.
If you want good Indian food go here, you will not be disappointed. I still miss the really authentic places in NYC but this one is pretty close. Namaste!

Came here because I was told they had the best Scotch Eggs in town. They were quite good but not as good as I've had in London, the yolk was not soft enough and the outer crust a little too thick but they tasted good. Would order again though. I really think it's where you source the eggs from, fresh organic would turn out better me thinks.
The big surprise was the fish and chips. These were the best I've had in a long time. Big piece of fish, thin crust crust and not greasy. 
In fact I was in Vegas a few weeks ago and went to Gordon Ramsey's pub for fish and chips. The ones I had at Jack's were less than half the price and tasted as good if not better than at Ramsey's! Bloody good these were.
These guys seem to be Manchester United fans so another plus for me. It is on the cozier side but a cool little pub it is. They have all the standard British pub fare. 
Yes I will be back for those Fish and Chips and scotch eggs! 
Cheerio mates! Go Man U!

4.5 Stars. This place has big rolls! Biggest rolls in the area and they are tasty to boot. Sashimi pieces are large as well, probably twice the size of most places in town. The name states Japanese Fusion. There is no fusion whatsoever, they have sushi, they have ramen, they have tempura and other noodle dishes. The owners are not even Japanese, they are Thai, maybe that's what he fusion is all about. But I don't care because they have very tasty food in generous proportions and at very reasonable prices, the prices compare with most sushi places. 
This place is easy to pass by because it's sandwiched in there with a lot of the popular places on Central avenue. Don't pass it by if of want some good Sushi/Japanese/Thai food. I will return.

Let me start off by saying this place has a lot of potential. Only being open since Monday (1/12/2015), BBSK is a new face to mid city. The menu features some of my favorite soul food items such as greens and pork chops, but with a nice little twang to them. They also will be adding new menu items gradually within the next couple of months to there brunch menu so I look forward to that. The inside of the restaurant is sizable with little touches to it that make it unique. 

Getting to the food though, my friend ordered the potato, ham and kale soup which had a really good flavor. It tasted very similar to the juice thats swimming in the pot after my mom has just cooked a big pot of collard and mustard greens. My friend agreed. I ordered the chicken and waffle sandwich with a side of fried brussels sprouts with lemon salt. I didn't read the description thoroughly and expected an actual waffle as my bread, so I was a little disappointed but thats my fault. Rereading it I realized it's really sourdough bread thats pressed in a waffle iron which is still good nonetheless. I really enjoyed my sandwich. The brussels sprouts were also a nice accompaniment. A tad bit too salty, but still good.  

Overall I would gave 3 stars for my meal today and an extra star for the customer service which is huge to me. They seem to really care and that's rare these days. I didn't leave blown away, but I definitely left yearning for more and will gladly return. 

*Side note*- Don't come if your looking to get in and out. My lunch lasted a little longer than expected, but it takes time to make good food :) Plus there still working out kinks so you gotta give them a break.

ZERO STARS. 

With not much being open due to Mardi Gras, we came to this location in hopes of getting a hot meal. After being told it would be a wait of 45 mins for a party of four, we put our names on the list and patiently waited outside for our name to be called. After 45 mins going by and seeing several people who arrived after us get seated, my husband decided to go see what the status was. I came in shortly after him and was told we never put our name on the list and that the hostess had never even seen me before.

Being 8 1/2 months pregnant and starving, that's the last thing you tell a pregnant woman. At this point the "owner" stepped in and rudely told us that there was nothing she could do. No apology, no trying to accommodate us, nothing. Livid at this point after being accused of lying, I was told to get out the restaurant.

Never have I been treated so poorly and disrespectfully in my life. I hope that no one else experiences the same in humane treatment that I've had to experience today (2/9/15). Sad to say, I will never be returning to this restaurant and will make sure that all my friends and family know not to support this business either.

Why does this city not have a lot of chicken wing spots? Every now and then I get a craving for some good wings that aren't steroid injected and five times the size that wings are supposed to be. 

I wouldn't say these are the best wings I've ever had, but they aren't bad at all. This is your typical hood chicken spot, but with a lot more flavors than most places. Recently I went and tried the Cajun Ranch which came with a side of seasoned fries and a drink. For $6.49 this isn't a bad deal at all. I sampled some of my friends wings, and the Cajun ranch was the best out of all of them. I didn't try any of the punches (Obama, Michelle, etc) but from the looks on my friends faces, I wasn't missing out on anything and saved myself an injection of insulin. 

I would give this place another go if in the mood for wings again although Wing Stop just opened across the street and those are my jam and my jelly.

A few side pointers:
-They always seem to have a groupon for C & W so I would try buying one first before you try them out. You'll save your self a couple of bucks. 
-If your claustrophobic, do not attempt to use the commode. You'll immediately go into a panic attack and will have to claw your way out of the bathroom.
-Carryout is probably your best option unless you want to eat with strangers butt's in your face.

Indian food is not something I frequent, so I don't exactly know where the best places are to go when I do have that occasional craving. Thank you yelpers for not failing me and directing me to the perfect spot.

Keep a look out because this place is extremely easy to miss, located in a small strip off Williams. The inside is nothing fancy, but the food....OFF THE CHAIN. We ordered the butter chicken and the goat biryani. Both were excellent, my favorite being the butter chicken. It was probably the best I've ever had seriously. Served piping hot in a unique little pot and accompanied with naan bread that was equally delicious, it was just the right amount to leave my satisfied but not overly full. I'm not a huge fan of goat, but I did sample my husbands and the spices were excellent. Spicy, but not too spicy to leave your mouth on fire. We also ordered a side of basmati rice and Indian soda with the total coming out to around $30 so it wasn't a pocket killer. 

The owner served us and was extremely nice as well. I know exactly where I'm coming to get my Indian food in the future. Support this place!

I finally made it to Juan's. After hearing so much hype about this little place, I was determined to come here one day, especially with it being so close to my house. I'm gonna skip right to the basics because I really have nothing but good to say.

Wait: This place was packed for a weekday evening but why wouldn't it be? It's great. We put our names down and were quickly seated about 10-15 mins later.
Atmosphere: Awesome. Eye catching menus and art work posted all over the place. Loved the fact that they play 90's r&b hip hop while u eat. Very chill and laid back staff. 
Dranks: Two thumbs up. We missed the happy hour by about 3 mins but it's okay cause their drinks are reasonably priced ranging from about $6-$10. I ordered the tiger woods which is sweet tea infused vodka with lemonade and mint. Hubby ordered the frozen lemon berry which was delicioussssss.
