Food: The most important part of this whole review lol. We split the jerk chicken nachos. Sooooooo stinkin good. Layers and layers of cheese, beans, avocado, some type of delicious infused sour cream, pineapple salsa and jerk chicken chunks. Highly satisfied after eating this. 

All in all I will definitely be returning to Juan's.

I didn't mean to end up here, but I did. Attempting to go to Domenica with a group of foodie friends from out of town and being told we couldn't get in until later that night, we were super disappointed. Hesitantly, we made our way over to Pizza Domenica and I must say our experience was great! 

The garlic knots are a MUST. If I was by myself I probably could've ate the entire tray of them. Served with a warm, whipped aged provolone, it simply is delicious. Do not refrain from ordering. Moving on to the pizza, we ordered the tutto carne which is covered in all kinds of delicious meats. Loved it! I also ordered the smoked chicken pesto which i wasn't crazy about. 

Overall do not hesitate to give this place a try. It's completely worth it during happy hour, especially being half price. I look forward to coming back and trying some of their different beers once I pop this baby out.

Great new addition to the Carmel restaurant scene. Fresh is certainly an accurate description but family and good should be added. Recently visited for just the third time, and the owners of the restaurant, local, are beyond friendly and explained the menu and made their recommendations. It is certainly helpful for 'rookies' and appreciated.  I chose the #6, Dolsot Bibimbap bowl and was happily surprised with my choice. I mixed the recommended veggies with a couple of my own choices. My son went with the #8 Quesadilla Trio and love the bulgogi beef and the recommended sauce that he added. My wife copied my choice on the #6 and added her veggie choices and she loved it as well.  We will be back for sure as I hope the locals find this place and keep it in business. It is not too visible from the street and sits in the CVS plaza at 136th and Meridian.

Yeah... really not a fan of this iconic New Orleans biz. The Hurricanes are good, but note that they charge you for the glass in case you steal it! They will take it off the bill if you ask, but you HAVE to ask.

I wasn't thrilled with their menu and actually opted for the chicken sandwich! UGG this is New Orleans where all I want to do is eat the amazing food!

My friend got the special which was a prime rib sandwich. He asked for horseradish and the server explained that they didn't have any. Really, with prime rib on the menu? He said it was super tough and overdone.

Our server was nice, but others seemed bothered. One even walked around with a toothpick in HER mouth.

I have to say it, there are FAR better restaurants in the French Quarter to check out.

5 stars ALL THE WAY! I actually found my new favorite wine at this joint! If you're a wine lover, ask for the Lock & Key Meritage! I am still bummed I can't get this wine in Georgia! Ok, Ok... enough about my sorrows :-(  The food here is absolutely AH-MAZING!!! 

I was able to eat at this fine establishment with a team of the most AWESOME people in the universe! That being said, eating with a team of foodies allows you to sample from many plates!

We started with an array of appetizers;

Grilled Octopus - HOLY Sea Creature! This was tender, flavorful, and grilled to perfection!

Tuna tartare w/ shrimp chips - This chick LOVES her shrimp chips. Tuna was fresh and melted in your mouth

Carpaccio - As a carpaccio virgin, I didn't know if I would like this dish. MIND BLOWN!!! Amazing!!! I look for this dish now when dining out.

Meatballs over Polenta - HUUUGE Polenta fan! This is a must try!

Poutine - Ok people... STOP THE PRESS... other than the Carpaccio, this was my FAVORITE!

As for the main dinner (Don't judge me! I was sharing)

Gambas Ajillo - Shrimp sauteed in garlic, oil, and white beans with a toasted baguette - The shrimp was cooked to perfection. The seasoning was not overwhelming and brought out the flavor of the shrimp. The bread was used to sop up all remaining items on the plate (yes, I would have licked the plate if not in the company of my boss)

Charred Romaine Heart - Just like your own fancy caesar salad - but on steroids! I'd never had a charred salad, so I wasn't sure what to expect. Again, MIND BLOWN. The parmigiana shavings were perfect added on top!

Did I mention the Lock & Key Meritage?

If you can't tell by the caps, multiple uses of MIND BLOWN & AMAZING, this place is a must try!

This review is based on a takeout order. We having a working lunch and our host decided on TuttoRosso and what a great decision that was! I ordered the Calamari Salad and it was TO DIE FOR!!! Like seriously guys... this salad was legit!

The calamari was cooked perfectly! It also had capers in it which I love!! The dressing that came with it paired perfectly with the lightness.

I have been dreaming of this since leaving Tampa. This salad has made all other salads dead to me ;-)

I WANT to like this place...was so excited about a brewery in the neighborhood. It lacks ambiance and reminds me of a high school cafeteria. The food is mediocre at best - definitely doesn't stack up to all the other great SoBro options. 

I tried giving Bent Rail the benefit of the doubt and visited a second time, but was equally underwhelmed.

Varga Bar, oh how I love you! It truly is a hidden gem tucked away on the corner of Spruce street. There is something so comfy, cozy, and intimate about this bar. 

It is a fairly tiny bar so it is an ideal spot if you're looking to grab food and drinks with a couple of friends. Varga Bar has a nice ambience and gives off a chill vibe. The Pandora playlist that played throughout the night was on point. A lot of well known old throwbacks... Third Eye Blind, Chumbawumba, and Jack Johnson just to name a few. The bar is dimly lit and there were tiny candles placed on the bar. Really set the mood! Paintings of pinup girls adorn the ceiling and walls. The bathroom was very clean which is always a plus.

The food was so tasty. I tried the truffle mac and cheese, fried pickles, and chicken and vegetable soup. All three were phenomenal. The soup was very hearty and the perfect choice given the cold weather. The truffle mac and cheese was also very good. The truffle flavoring is what really made the entree. The portion size was decent... it definitely was enough for a meal for me. The fried pickles were delicious and served piping hot. They came with a side of chipotle mayo. The drinks were just as good too!

Service was awesome. Our food and drinks were prepared very quickly. All of the employees were really friendly. 

I'll be back soon! Already craving the truffle mac and cheese again...

I think I died and went to heaven! Seriously, everything about Nektar is pure perfection. From the ambience to the food and views, this place as it all.

I've eyed this place from afar for the longest time. Its picturesque location is what really drew me in. Nektar is nestled on the corner of Mechanic Street amongst plenty of greenery and moving water. The outside patio is decorated with string lights and pretty hanging potted flowers. The outside area is by far one of the selling points of Nektar. It is so quaint and charming, making it the perfect spot for a date night. 

Nektar has two levels and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. We were seated along the back widow which, in my opinion, was the best seat in the house. It had a gorgeous view of New Hope. I'll admit, we were a bit cramped (I was practically bumping elbows with my neighbor) but the view made it worth it. 

They have a very extensive drink selection given the fact that they are a wine, beer, and whiskey bar. I tried a glass of the Harlaftis Dry white wine which came highly recommended by our waiter. It was so good... my friend and I couldn't resist having a second glass! 

The food was delicious. I tried the following small plates: portobello fries, panko crusted shrimp, and spinach & chickpea. Let's start with the fries. They might have been my favorite (although it was a close call). The truffle and mustard aioli dipping sauce was out of this world.  The shrimp dish was another hit. I loved that they were super crispy. The Thai sweet chili sauce that was drizzled on top made it that much better. I swear I could have eaten that sauce by itself... it was just that good. The spinach and chickpeas were good but I'm not gonna lie, I thought it should have been served with some kind of pita or chip to eat it with. Regardless, it was still good. 

Service was top notch. Our server was extremely friendly and offered great suggestions when asked. Our food came out in a timely manner. We also never felt rushed which was an added bonus. 

I can honestly say that although it was the ambience that initially drew me in, its the food and drink that will keep me coming back.

A restaurant that specializes in just breakfast? Yup, sign me up! I've been dying to check out Turning Point for awhile now. So we decided to check it out after a Saturday morning goat yoga session. 

I was with a group of 6 people and we didn't have a reservation. We were told it would be a 20 minute wait. I must note, it did seem to take a bit longer than that, but the food was worth the wait. 

The menu is EXTENSIVE. I'm not kidding... literally an entire page is devoted to just coffee. I'll be honest, the menu was pretty overwhelming. My friends and I found it a little hard to read as there was a lot of text and a lot on each page. After sifting through the menu, I finally decided to order the big easy benedict. It was delicious! So flavorful and a big portion. The only thing I wasn't crazy about was the cornbread that it came with. It wasn't bad by any means but I probably would have preferred toast or an English muffin instead. My friends seemed to enjoy their meals as well. A couple people got coffee which we were told came with free refills. Just something to note if you do end up getting a cup of coffee. 

The meal was cheap, after splitting the bill it came out to around $15 per person. Not bad! Service was good too. The food came out in a timely manner and our waitress was attentive and friendly. It was a good experience overall. I would recommend Turning Point to others and I would come back again the next time I'm in the area.

Welcome to the city of brotherly love, SPiN! So happy to have you! 

I previously visited the location in downtown LA and had a blast. Needless to say, I was super excited to hear that SPiN would be coming to Philadelphia. The Philly location certainly lived up to my expectations. TBH, I actually liked it more than the LA location. Speaking of locations... it is perfectly placed smack dab in the heart of Center City. Super accessible and in walking distance to many other restaurants and bars.

SPiN looks like an industrial warehouse which gives off a modern yet trendy vibe. I couldn't get over how huge and open to space is.... you can pretty  much see the entire bar from no matter where you are standing. It makes the place feel bigger than it actually is. With that said, it is still broken into different areas; there are two separate bars, a private red room, and of course Olympic sized ping pong tables scattered all around. 

There are a few specifically noteworthy aspects of SPiN. First, all of the amazing Philly themed artwork on the walls was done by local artists. Wow, talk about being talented! There is a bathtub full of ping pong balls right in the center of the bar - need I say more? Don't forget to post an Instagram of it because... did you really go to SPiN if you didn't get a picture in the ping pong ball tub?! Another fun fact: the cherry printed walls leading to the bathrooms are scratch and sniff! Disclaimer: I couldn't reallllly smell the cherry scent, probably because they've already been scratched a million times before. But it was definitely still cool nonetheless! Lastly, the infamous red room. Ah, where do I even start with this one. It is considered the VIP private room which you can rent in advance. It is still very much a part of the bar but there is a long curtain you can pull to make it more private. Everything (and I mean everything - decor, lights, floor, walls, etc) is red, hence the name. It certainly makes for a cool picture, that's for sure. 

I ordered a Moscow mule which was honestly probably the best mule I've ever had (and trust me, I've had my fair share considering it's my go-to drink!). It came in a cute branded SPiN copper mug. Cocktails are priced between $12-13. They also have beer, wine, and food. 

The DJ was good and played upbeat music throughout the night. There was a decent size crowd but I must admit, it wasn't nearly as full as I would have expected it to be. The lighting was brighter than your average bar... it wasn't a huge deal but something that definitely stuck out to me. I couldn't help but to have wished the lights were turned down lower at least near the bar area. 

The biggest (and only) downfall is that this place is more on the expensive side. Although we didn't rent a table, it seems that it can get a little pricey especially if you're there all night. Thankfully, there was no cover charge when I went on a Friday night. 

All in all, I would definitely come back and recommend for others to check it out at least once. Whether you're going to play ping pong or just stopping by for a drink, it is certainly a good time.

So this morning I woke up craving a shrimp poboy. Anyone who knows me knows, I live and breathe shrimp poboys!! Today I decided that I wanted to try a new spot and man did I hit the jackpot!! Not only was the food delicious but the service was truly heartwarming. I am a sucker for good hospitality and this place beams it! The cashier/waitress was such a ray of sunshine from the moment we walked in. Such a bubbly personality and cheerful demeanor. You can tell they take great pride in their business and value their customers. I overheard on two occasions while eating the chef offer to make two dishes that technically were not on their menu. No one complained, they just went with it. The restaurant is located on magazine st. across from the art academy. They offer both indoor and outdoor seating. Their walls are cover in unique paintings made by local artists. Our order came out super fast and the French bread was so soft and fresh. Shrimp were fried to perfection. My husband also ordered some gravy cheese fries that were delicious as well. We were surprised to see there were actual pieces of roast beef on the fries!  They offer weekly specials and other cool dishes. This was great lunch date and they will most definitely be back!!

A good brewery to check out that is on the outskirts of Armature Works complex and a 20 minute walk or so from Ybor. Since it's located a little distance away from these busy areas, it's more low key and relaxing.

The inside is clean and modern with some good beer to choose from. Their menu focuses on sours and lagers with some that can be really sweet, but tasty such as the Tigers Blood or Electric Pegasus. The 'Above My Paygrade' is a good easy to drink beer too.

This. This is what I'd consider the epitome of elevated Florida cuisine. The vibe is laid back yet refined. The service is friendly and proper. The ambiance is sophisticated yet approachable. This place is a must for visitors and locals alike!

Where to start? The booze of course! I ended up having a fun morning with three different drinks. First I started out with their Wedding Beer. This was served in a chilled mug that was fit for toasting with others. The beer was fresh with a well-balanced profile that had a welcoming character. 

Next, I got the Fresh from Florida Mojito. Beautifully presented with mashed mint and oranges that screamed vacation. It made me more than ready for Florida sun and good times to come.

My appetizer came next. I went with the Native Chili based on the unique selection of Florida meats such as alligator, duck, venison, and boar. Let me tell you, all this game and it was not overwhelming or too wild. Everything melded together beautifully with a slight sweetness from the cranberries beans. The crunch from the chips was perfect too.

Then the main course! I was tempted to go with seafood, but I was really feeling steak and went with the 8 oz Flank Steak. I was more than pleased! It was skillfully cooked with the right portions of mashed potatoes and crunchy green beans. The chimmichurri sauce was phenomenal as well! Avocado and citrus brightness made each bite of the steak mesmerizing. The random addition of popcorn was playful and I enjoyed it. Don't take everything so seriously--just like Florida.

I had to finish off with my last drink and dessert. I went with their Ulele Spring Hard Seltzer and Coconut Ice Cream. Perfect combo because the seltzer was almost like a palatte cleanser and complemented the Coconut Ice Cream as well by bringing a bubbly clean take between the creaminess of the ice cream. The Coconut Ice Cream was gorgeous and velvety. It was also served in a coconut shell. Presentation on point! 

Overall, one of the best meals I have ever had! Ulele is a sparkling gem amongst Florida cuisine and is worth eating at. High regards to this place for sure!!

Silky smooth and indulgently thick! This places knows how to make flan from a variety of options from fun flavors such as Fruity Pebbles or Cinnamon Toast Crunch to more traditional such as Dulce de Leche or a modern twist of Arroz con Leche. If you like eggy, custardy desserts or something similar to cheesecake or creme brulee then you have to check this place out!

They also have a full breakfast and lunch menu too so you can grab a meal here as well!

I got the Dulce de Leche and Arroz con Leche Flan and both were incredibly creamy. The Dulce de Leche is pretty traditional and very sweet with the extra caramel. The Arroz con Leche was incredible with blended rice within the flan. Smooth with a subtle texture that made it stand out. Between these two, go for the Arroz con Leche!! You get both of best worlds--traditional yet modern all the one.

I also got their Horchata Iced Coffee. Not crazy sweet, but that great horchata taste throughout backed up with a bold coffee taste. Really good and will get you buzzing!

Overall, great place to get excellent flan and coffee! Will have to try their food another time!

Their service was way off when I went. Not sure if they were stressed or where dealing with some issues, but it was pretty off-putting and I just ended up getting their Ube Cake to go instead.

They don't have really have a menu, but have some of it on their Facebook page and some posters of their desserts around. They have a cafeteria setup of their food up front. So, you just pick and choose what you want to eat.

Anyways, the Ube Cake was good. Light and fluffy, but kind of wished that it has some more of the the starchy ube filling to have more texture.

This is a quaint and charming small Italian restaurant serving food with heart! Chef William is certainly personable and his care shows through his food. His love for Italian cuisine shines brightly with each dish freshly made!

I ended up getting the Bolognese and it was hearty with plenty of pasta, ground beef, and sausage accented with fresh basil in a tomato sauce. A rich and savory dish that will make you feel all warm and cozy inside.

The interior can be a bit crowded so I recommend coming for and early dinner or later lunch to be any crowds. You can also order out too!

The parking lot can be a little precarious when crowded so be careful so you're not playing bumper cars!

Delicious, soulful New Orleans style comfort food. The chef here has some chops and executes the food with skill and even restraint. We've had this place bookmarked for some time, and finally decided a pre-movie lunch was in order. We parked on the street and made our way inside to what is essentially the to-go area. Tia, the chef/owner's daughter and our host for the meal, told us we were the first arrivals and met us on the sidewalk to let us into the main dining room. I mention this because this building can be confusing to new comers, and it's easier to just go through the grocery store entrance. The dining space is small and homey. I was very comfortable and we were treated to excellent and friendly service. Tia is obviously proud of the food and knowledgeable. We started with the filé gumbo, which featured shrimp, chicken and andouille that day, and comes with a grilled cheese sandwich and potato salad. The gumbo was delicious, and I'm a fan of this Cajun style potato salad, which is creamy and rich, flavored with mustard and pickle. The grilled cheese sandwich was made with the type of white bread I ate as a kid and American sliced cheese, and was the only off note in an otherwise wonderful meal. 

I ordered the Bourbon Street, which features boneless fried chicken with a creamy crawfish sauce served over Mac n cheese with a side of that potato salad. This chicken was delicious, well seasoned and perfectly fried, and I enjoyed the mac n cheese, with its al dente pasta. The potato salad was carb overload for me on this plate, and I would have preferred a side of collard greens or green beans in its place. When I mentioned this to Tia, she said next time I could ask for a vegetable substitution, so they're flexible, which I appreciate. My partner chose The Superdome, blackened fish (basa that day) with a lobster cream sauce served with sweet corn and onion rings. I usually avoid blackened fish when I go out, as most chefs overdo the seasoning and you can't taste the fish. This chef understands how to make this dish (that's the restraint I was taking about earlier) and I would come back and order this plate myself. The fish was expertly seasoned and perfectly cooked, and I liked the sauce and thought the sweet corn was a nice touch. My husband and I were both unfamiliar with basa fish, and I've read up on it since our visit. It isn't local (Gulf fish) and comes from fisheries in Asia. For me, this is another reason I didn't go with 5 stars on this review, as I prefer it when local restaurants take advantage of our amazing Gulf fish. You may think I'm splitting hairs here, but basa is on the list of fish to avoid. I will return to this wonderful neighborhood spot and try more of the menu.

Hmmm. I'm not sure what the 5 star Yelpers are eating at this restaurant, but it certainly isn't what I had. 

I like the exterior of this restaurant, but found the dining room drab and, frankly, depressing. The walls are painted in a trompe l'oeil swag design that would be fun had it been done in a livelier color. While I appreciate understated elegance, the dark gray walls and olive carpet do nothing to enliven the small room. Unfortunately, I found the food similarly uninspired. The salad I ordered...honey crisp apples julienned and tossed with bleu cheese, walnuts and romaine in a walnut vinaigrette...was not bad, but lacked any real interest. It was OK. For an entree I chose halibut in a grapefruit buerre blanc. The fish was cooked perfectly, and the elements on the plate went together well; in fact, if I was reviewing on this plate alone, I would be giving this restaurant 3 stars, as this dish was good. It just wasn't terrific, or anything that I haven't had before. For $33, I want to be a little more wowed. My husband and I shared the banana split for dessert. After a few bites I realized this is something anyone with just a little skill could make in their own kitchen. I never, ever make dessert at home, as I live with an ex pastry chef, but I was remaking the dish in my mind as I was eating it, coming up with improvements as I ate. I must admit I don't get the excitement over this restaurant, especially in a town that has such amazing food. 

Moving on.

Five years and many visits later, and I'm still going with 5 stars. I've tried many things here since that first visit, and it's all very good to great. The shrimp remoulade po boy may still be my favorite, but the fried fish and seafood, salads and red beans & rice are terrific too. I tried the jambalaya on my most recent visit, and thought it was excellent. The staff here is unfailingly friendly and helpful.

Wow, the newly opened Big Storm is Beautiful and SPACIOUS. A lot different from the Odessa location which is great too, and still opened there. When I was driving on the road, and GPS said pulling up in 900 ft , I made sure to look very closely so I wouldn't miss it . Sometimes these breweries are so hard to see from the road. Well, let me tell you , don't worry, no need to squint, you won't miss it! Lol you'll see when you get there . Of course, still serving up your favorite selections at a reasonable price for craft beer at a Brewery $4.95. I did have the Special Release Imperial Chocolate Cherry Stout which was $7.95, but I didn't mind. I liked it that much. It wasn't very chocolatey or very cherry-ish, but just right . I'm glad I had the chance to try it. You know I'll be back . Big Storm is one of my favorites.

I'm so torn on the rating of this place so I'm going with 3 for now. If I was judging on Pupusas I would give it a five, but yesterday for my main dish I tried to go with a meal that looked straight out of a Nicaraguan restaurant, but clearly I made a big mistake after I took my first bite. 
From the outside they advertise a Nica flag and even have some decor in the inside, but I don't think anything on the menu is Nicaraguan whether it appears to be or not. 
Nothing on the plate had any flavor to it. I would not recommend the carne Asada to anyone, you will be disappointed! 
Everything on the plate tasted the same. No distinct flavors, just grill and salt. It was bad, and the cabbage salad that accompanies this meal tasted like it had lemon instead of lime, and not fresh lemon, the one out of the bottle, which I hate because it has a soap detergent taste. 
That was the first time ever I didn't like the Queso frito, it was slightly rubbery like, so salty and tasted like I said, the grill. Thumbs down. 
Now, we also ordered pupusas. The chicken&cheese, and the pork. Both awesome ! Loved them. Highly recommend! Passion Fruit Juice is house made and FANTASTIC! 
Now when I come here again, I will just order more from the food items made out of corn because they clearly excel in that area. The tamales, tacos dorados, pupusa loca I want to try because it's a mix of all the meats, enchiladas, pollo con tajadas looked good. 
The people next to me ordered that, and looked like they were really enjoying it. I wondered how it tasted. Plantains w/crema also looked great as a side, and I've read a lot of good things about the soup. Combinacion guanaca hmmm maybe. Probably not. 
This place was packed when I walked in so I know it's good, I may have just had bad luck the first time, and I'm not giving up on this place yet. I was happy about the fact that I did find Bags of these little Nicaraguan corn treats called rosaquillas. They are not for everyone, but I love them

Mazarros is  located in a rather strange location in a back neighborhood somewhere, but it just goes to show if your place is good, people will find you no matter where you are. 
Once u turn on 22nd you cannot miss this place, it sticks out like a sore thumb. If you never been there, you will know exactly what I'm talking about when you see it. The reason I love Mazarros is not really for the shopping . 
Yes, they have great things, but most of those things you can find anywhere, and cheaper. 
The reasons I love Mazarros is for the Deli section, Espresso Bar, and Bakery. 
You can get a huge quality sub for $5, and they are delicious . My Favorite so far is the meatball. It is extremely messy so make sure u grab 10 napkins! They also have a huge fridge in the front and a small one towards the back patio door filled with all kinds of sodas, juice, beers, etc to grab something to drink before u enter the patio to eat. I'm usually grabbing a beer. A nice La chouffe is usually my top choice if they have it at the time, but if they don't, it's not a problem because they have a vast selection of all kinds of beers to choose from. Just make sure u grab a number at the deli to order. 
It's really chaotic and fast paced in there most of the time, so when they call your number, be ready .
The bakery is filled with the best Italian desserts and gelato. everything I've had has been good. 
If I could get a seat at the coffee bar, that would be nice. It is usually filled with a bunch old Italian men sipping on their espresso drinks and socializing. I don't blame them. That's where i'd be hanging out all day too if I could or lived down the road :-)if anyone can inform me of a slower time to catch a seat , that would be nice. 
It's always so packed with people surrounding it waiting for people to get up. Aint nobody got time for that! I always have to yell my coffee order out to go and take it outside with a nice bakery goodie. 
I've tried their to go pizzas and wasn't crazy about them, but others seem to like them because they fly off the shelf as soon as they put them out. I still need to try their fresh made pastas and to go meals. Haven't gotten there yet, but I will. If I lived closer I would have already conquered that place.

This Place is Delicious! Best Po' Boys around! Take everything they give you..  The spicy spread , tarter, AND COLESLAW which is vinegar based( no mayo)and put it on your sandwich. Very good, with just the right amount of slight kick from the spices, and zip from the coleslaw. Love The food , and owners are very nice. Good Peeps. :-) This is a very small hole in the wall type place . 8 seats outside, and 2 stools inside. My kind of place . you all know, I love hole in the walls. I sat on the stool inside, and people watched out the window. Their customers are very friendly . Talkative. That was a great sign for me that I was about to get something good to eat. Happy talkative customers waiting , means good food.

Best Shrimp and Grits that I've tried yet. Ingredients included were fresh diced tomatoes, green onion, Applewood Bacon, all with a white wine creole cream sauce over the top. It was fantastic, and they didn't skimp on the shrimp. There was I believe 6 medium sized plump shrimp in there. I Love the Applewood bacon sprinkled in, nice touch, and the fact that they use Organic GMO free yellow corn grits is really appreciated and awesome! For those worried if it's spicy, do not fear, it's not spicy at all, but full of flavor. For those who love spicy like me, u can always add the hot sauce. The only reason I've been giving this place 4 instead of 5 stars is because they do not always cook their side potatoes made to order,  and half of the times I've been here, they've been cold. If that happens to you, make sure you ask for fresh ones because they're  really great when fresh.
Every time I'm in the Pinellas Park area I stalk this place. Love the Banh Mi's! They also have the best Boba Drinks hands down with the best selection of flavors and add ins. Addicted!

This place is awesome. They make the best Real European Crepes, the way they are supposed to be. Brings back memories of Greece every time I'm in. I was really hungry for food today so I went with a Savory. I really love Caribbean and Indian food so with no hesitation I chose the Bon Curry Chicken crepe. The chicken is really curried deliciously, it has true island flavor. I dab every bite I take with the sour cream they include on top of the crepe. Yum, yum.. U know u want some . 
The fruit crepes are really the highlights though, all amazing! They also have specialty coffees which draws me in more, great cappuccinos. 
I wished I lived closer to Ybor because I would be here every week.. If you haven't been, go in and see what a real crepe is supposed to taste like.

UPDATE: March 31 still good, but overpriced Breakfast/Brunch food that's on First Watch Level.
2 breakfast meals- 1 Laffite Tortilla wrap, 1 Mardi Gras omelette w/ 1 rg.orange juice , 1 tap water =$30.35 without tip. Add tip, and where does that put u? 
That's waaaay too much for breakfast. 
I still agree with my original review. I will still come here occasionally when suggested, but it's not my first choice. It just doesn't have that Wow Factor for the price.

On my last visit the plan was to get all Passion Fruit, but 2 others caught my eye that I hadn't  tried. Banana Foster, and Mexican Mango. While the Banana Foster was good , I wish It packed more of a Rum punch. It would have been way better. 
The Mexican Mango is suppose to be filled with a layer of green Chilis and Habanero, but packed no heat at all. I was not crazy about the overall flavor either. I've tried a bunch of William Dean Flavors, but if I go down the list, this review could get long, and I'm trying to keep it as short as possible. 
They're good chocolates, but the only ones that I will jump in my car for, from now on, when the WD craving hits are...  #1 Passion Fruit. Tangy Deliciousness with strong distinct flavors of Passion Fruit made with White Chocolate Cover. Oh man, it's so good it actually makes me crack a smile, and close my eyes when I bite into one.  :-D 
Peanut Butter Crunch , I hate to even say this word in the same sentence , but Reese's on Steroids. It kicks a Reese's ass though. So Peanut Buttery with little Crunchy pieces that make it extra special and different , and the shape.... Well, coolest shape and Color ever . A Gold Crown. It is really the King of all Peanut Butter candies . 
...And last but not least,  Tropical Caramel which is Passion Fruit and Caramel mixed in one. Good , but not as enjoyable as the Plain Passion Fruit. This one is also made from White Chocolate. These 3 are my personal favorites. If I'm in the mixing mood next time , these will be the 3 winners or else I'm just filling the box with all Passion Fruits, and maybe 1 PB Crunch;-) 
I give WD 4 stars instead of 5 simply because it's not better than my other favorite chocolatier that has more enjoyable flavor choices, BUT the WD choices that I do like are Delish.

If you're in the mood for some good Cuban Food you may want to try this place out. During my visits pre-Covid19, I really enjoyed eating here. Friendly staff, and they are opened right now during these troubling times. You can place your order, pay online and they will bring it out to you.

Wildflower is one of my favorite places to eat. I have always been satisfied with all of my choices here. They have an nice menu, small, but filled with a handful of interesting choices. These are some of my suggestions..
I suggest you always look at the specials on the blackboard. They have never let me down, and I order a majority of my choices from there. One of my favorites was the Panko Wild Crusted Cod fish sandwich on Naan bread. If you ever run into that, (served for sure on Fridays)I highly suggest you order it with the kale salad.. Don't be afraid of the kale side item choice, its tasty, and you should get it if offered. You will be pleasantly surprised. It's chopped so small that it's really easy to eat, and they use this delicious sweet vinaigrette dressing that you will really enjoy. 
Try their specialty soups (there is an up charge)or else they just offer tomato. The specialty soups are worth it. The tomato is good too if that's your thing. FYI it's slightly on the sweeter side.
Don't order fruit as a side unless it's with breakfast where they will actually serve you a bowl. If you order with a sandwich, they will serve it to you like a garnish. Very small serving.
If you want breakfast get there before 11:00 because they cut it off right on the dot! They're really strict on that. They will not serve you even 2 minutes after. Their Waffles are amazing! the Wildlower Triple is the Best if you want a little protein too with your breakfast. It's served w/eggs &Bacon. Go with biscuit option instead of bread for Breakfast, they are homemade and served w/ fresh jam & sweet butter. French toast is awesome. Don't order an omelette, it's the most boring thing on the menu, there are so many other awesome things to try. 
Last thing, this place serves good portions of Quality food, not huge. So if you're the kind of person who like to go to diners, and order huge breakfast meals loaded with home fries, or lunch/dinner items with gravies and mashed potatoes(the works) just to get so full, that you a wheel barrel to roll you out, this place is not for you. Either way, you should give it a try because it's awesome.

Absolutely delicious. I ordered the Trifecta so I could try a little bit of everything.  It consisted of Beef Kebab, Kibbeh, Chicken Kebab, My choice of Babaghanouj or Hummus, rice and choice of salad.. 
I chose the Fatoush . 
Everything on the plate was very enjoyable . The chicken Kebab definitely stood out. Very flavorful, and tender. The hummus and pita were great, and I even ate all the yellow rice which was spiced perfectly. 
The only thing I'm not crazy about here is the tabouli. It tastes like they use lemon from the bottle. They might do the same for the fattoush salad but it's not as noticeable as the tabouli. They should work on their salad dressings. 
I came in with family and we were all very impressed with this place that we even bought a bagful of desserts to go. 
You must MUST MUST order the Katayef for dessert! There are 2 kinds, One filled with cheese, one filled with walnuts, order both! They are deep fried, then soaked in honey, and sprinkled with pistachios. Kind of like Greek loukoumades , but better. AMAZING! We also love the honeycomb bread. So good when you warm it up a little in the oven at home. I would love to still try all the breads, spinach and cheese pies. Go in and try this place, you won't be sorry. It's owned by a very nice family . Go support your local businesses.

I really like the food here. It's the more authentic menu you will see in Greek Town. Better than Hellas in my opinion. 
The only thing they don't beat Hellas at is the Broiled Octopus. They do not serve it broiled here but chargrilled which can be a little on the tough side. 
Every time I come with family the Mykonos or the Kalymnian Salad are always ordered and shared within the group as a side to go with our meals. This is a must for us. 
I really like their Dolmades. 
The Lima Beans w/dill as a side.. very tasty and so Greek. Lots of great things on the menu here. 
Great Appetizers. 
I love how they serve the wine in the aluminum cups to pour yourself just like they serve in Greece at the Tavernas. 
My only complaint is that I wish they would just remodel this place a bit . After all the years they've been here,  they have not remodeled or have they? I can't tell if they did. Greeks are known for this and it's ridiculous. 
This restaurant is all table & chairs but there are about 3 or 4 booths in the back. Same booths for years, and when you sit in them you either sink straight down or get a spring in your ass. 
How much could it possibly cost to change out 3 or 4 booths? Let's get with it already. Panayia Mou.

This place was good, but it wasn't as good as I thought it would be. The Sides were salty. Chicken was very moist , fall off the bone, but the sauces that are very important for dipping, were a disappointing. The yellow one that I'm use to being creamier, was watery, didn't have much flavor, it just tasted salty. The cilantro rice was decent , but like I said, just a tad salty , and even the French Fries were a bit overly salted. Hey! I like salt don't get me wrong, it's a very important ingredient used to bring out the spice in food, but in this case I felt salted to death. 
Another thing that bugged me is that they are very stingy with choice of sides. I didn't want fries so why couldn't I have fried yucca instead? I did order some on the side which raised my bill another 4 bucks. Thumbs down for that. Another thing I would not have chosen is rice , but they don't offer other options with the combo meals like my favorite place Pico Rojo. If you want the good sides, you have to order them separate. Blah. 
I should have never cheated on my Pico Rojo. Oh, I loved my Passion Fruit juice, almost forgot about that. Wrapping it up, I would try this place again if I was in the area and a friend wanted to eat here, but I will not come out of my way because I wasn't very impressed. My lunch was too expensive for sides i didn't want

I'm sorry, but I cannot go with the masses on this one. This place is still not very good. I went in the other day to give this place another shot and while food was A-ok , I was not impressed. Plus, the ladies that make fresh corn tortillas are not there anymore. They were using tortillas out of packages. Not sure if there was a split with partners because there is a new place on US19 which had the same name, but now name is changed. It's All pretty confusing. At least the place didn't reek like the last time, but kitchen, and kitchen floors were a complete wreck and dirty. My friend wanted to walk out and was pissed with me for ordering. no lie! I'm sorry, no disrespect , but clearly these reviewers have never been to Drew St. or some really great places in Tampa like Loli's .

Where the hell is the Red Skin Potato and Bayou Bleu pizza? Mellow Mushroom's new menu sucks . 
They've discontinued some really great specialty pizzas, and left us with nothing special to choose from . 
Lets see here, we still have the Great White, Kosmic Karma. Both taste the same . Anything with pesto overpowers and tastes the same no matter what other toppings it may have. You really just need one pizza with pesto. 
2 pizzas with BBQ chicken(gross)..chicken should not be put on pizza. So unappetizing. 
Why in God's name would we need 2 BBQ chicken specialty pizzas on the menu??? The ingredients are pretty much exactly the same , except one has a BBQ swirl, and one has a Ranch swirl. Wtf. Waste of space on the menu .Smh. 
Pacific rim has pineapples on it . Not something that everyone likes so when ordering with family, that's out. House Special & Mighty Meaty are basically the same pizza , one has no veggies. 
Hmm.. We have the Veg out, big shit. 
You should finish it off and get rid of the Holy shiitake too. Why not?
Thank You House Special for always being there for us while we go through these difficult times .
I hope this menu doesn't last long .

Fresh, Authentic and Delicious. I ordered the beef shawarma which was highly enjoyable . The beef was seasoned nicely, and I just told the guy making it to add pretty much everything or whatever he thought would go good with it. There was a good selection of toppings, and I didn't want to miss out on the good ones. He added pickled purple cabbage , lettuce, onion, pickles, a tomato & cucumber mixture, tahini of course, and a spicy sauce. I loved it. I also ordered a side of hummus which I highly recommend to go along with your shawarma. It's only 1.49 extra if u order it as a side with your wrap. It was well made , and they also drizzled olive oil over it which is a must. The olive oil they used had a nice strong flavor, and I was surprised with the high quality taste of it. Very good. I've had this bookmarked for a while now, but live almost an hour away. So, when I knew I'd be in the area today, I really wanted to finally get over here to try it out. Why don't they have a quick place like this in my area? I'd be a regular customer for sure.

Fresh, Buttery, Fluffy, Crispy and Delicious.. 
That is exactly how I would describe my Sandwich at Flying with Jerome today. 
From the Crossaint that's baked in house, to the crisp Bacon, Fresh Spinach & Tomato, and perfectly cooked over medium eggs that dripped with each bite. I'm sorry , but I love that:-) and Real Swiss Cheese. Yes Folks, I said real Swiss because sometimes you go to restaurants that advertise real Swiss In the sandwich and it is not. It's more like white American (Ghetto) They're not fooling anybody with that. It was Perfection. My mom agreed, and also loved hers with the Salmon . 

Last time , I had the Cheese Bread Sandwich. That sandwich is definitely NOT for the weak cheese eater. It is strong!!! So, if you're into strong cheeses you will love it. If not, you won't be able to handle it. It has Bleu Cheese, Parmesan and Brie that will literally drop kick your tastebuds, and it's also served on .. Surprise! Cheese Bread . They also throw yellow raisins to sweeten it a bit and balance out the saltiness , nuts & greens , with a dab of dressing which I believe is a Vinaigrette of some sort. Again, interesting and tasty sandwich, but not for the weak. 

I usually like a crispier Crepe which is not served here. The Crepes here are delicate, kind of like a Swedish pancake, very enjoyable. The Tropical fruit on top made it smell and taste extra delicious, and I loved the cinnamon cream sauce or fruit jam they serve with it. It really made this crepe unique. 

The Eggs Benedict is SO GOOD, but I think they only have this on weekends. Call to make sure if you're coming for this. Get this with its usual side of mashed potato & salad with vinaigrette dressing. You won't be sorry. So so good.

.. and the Brioche French Toast.. Fantastic, Period!
Fruits served along with it varies depending on what seasonal fruits are available, but just Outstanding French Toast. One of the items that I've personally ordered on several visits. My Favorite.

I enjoy this place. Everything is made in house with love , using quality ingredients, from all the breads they use for the dishes, the jams, sauces etc. They even use organic eggs, and it's always a pleasure supporting my local businesses. Next time I fly into town, I will definitely take flight with Jerome again.

I'll keep this short and Sweet. Tried again after I was sent a gift certificate after another bad experience. First Watch use to be one of my #1 choices to eat , but the food has really gone downhill. 
Ordered lemon ricotta pancake trifecta . It arrived with Fermented old strawberries on top, brown/black mint shriveled up garnish that I picked most of it off before the pic, and scrambled eggs that were not cooked all the way through. Raw! If you look at the pic , you can see the slime. Ew! Didn't eat the eggs, told the server,  and just had it replaced with fruit bowl which had rotten grapes in it. 
The only thing good was the coffee and service. Guess how much I paid ? $13.89! With tip add another few bucks to that. Almost $20 for for 1 pancake, 2 pieces of old bacon, raw scrambled eggs , and coffee?!?!?! Really? Why?! Because that meal was so special? Hell no. 
I'm done with First Watch. They're Not as good as they use to be like back in the day, before they started switching the menu up with new items. They Should have stuck with original, when the food was good, like 10 years ago. 1 star for coffee , 1 star for service. Goodbye . I will never eat a half ass meal again.

Excuse me? They serve Craft Beer and Wine at this coffee shop? That alone is 5 ***** A-W-E-S-O-M-E! 
It's not a big selection but there were some Cigar City selections amongst some other choices that made me say Hmph, Interesting *smile* 
I almost forgot what I actually came in for, and ordered one. Then I was like, oh yeah , wait.. COFFEE! Concentrate Sofia , CONCENTRATE!
So glad I came across this place on Yelp. How long has this place been here and I didn't know about it? 
I've been on a mission lately to find nice coffee shops to relax my mind and this has definitely squeezed it's way in on my top 5 list. They make a pretty good latte , one of my favorite coffee drinks. They also have pastries, cookies, breakfast and lunch sandwiches if you've got the munchies. 
This place has plenty of seats from table seating to individual cushioned chairs, and sofas. They also have board games if you're In The mood. Free Guest WiFi so you can get work done or just surf the net . 
It's very cozy, with a dimmer setting which I personally love.  It reminds me of the cafes in Europe because they serve alcohol. I still can't get over that. This is the perfect place to come to with friends and catch up. I shall return.

I was a little skeptical about coming here at first, and have had this place bookmarked for a long time. I kept seeing Hendo and Tori B checking in all the time , and wondered, What's  going on over there? Those two were keeping this place all to themselves , Checking In all quietly, and not telling any of us to come here? ! Ok, guys , I see how it is;-) 
Firstly, let me tell you, that the pics posted in the pics section, do not do these sandwiches Justice at all ! They look smaller, not that they're huge , but definitely bigger than what is seen there, and I was completely stuffed after finishing one. More importantly, they were both absolutely delicious! 
My mom and I got the Reuben & the Cuban and split. With every  bite I took, I examined it like, How do you taste this good? 
My Cuban Came on Portuguese Bread which was really impressive. I haven't seen this bread served in any sandwich shop in Florida that I've been to, only up North. So soft and moist. The meats were also tender and flavorful.  
The Reuben was just as good, and shut my mom down because at first she was complaining as usual. Ah, Where did you take me? What is this place? This place is not going to be good. Blah blah etc. etc, You know, the usual parents complaints ? About  half way through the sandwich she started saying how cute the place is, pointing at all the decorations lol Compliments just coming out , one right after the other... I was like, Praise the Lord! Yes! God is Good! 
If you haven't been in, its worth the drive. I'm just sorry I didn't try the place sooner. 
My only complaint is that, I had not had my coffee in the morning, and was really hoping that they served some. They do not, but should! 
I noticed that 2 people outside, and 2 people inside brought their own from other businesses. So, why wouldn't they serve coffee here so they can make the extra money? It Doesn't make sense. You can make a lot of profit on coffee, it's so easy to make, and it's in Demand. 
For drinks, they have crafts beers, sodas, lemonade and bottled water of course FYI. If I was not with my mom , I would have had a beer , but I didn't want to kill the fact that she wasn't complaining haha it was too good to be true:-p

Liked Mike's sushi. Server for one had a great personality and was fun. My sister and I went for happy hour so all the rolls were $5! All very tasty, and despite it being so busy (line at the door) they had it under control. Sushi came out in a timely manner. Every customer who came in had smiles on their faces, greeted and were greeted by other customers and staff. Everyone knew everyone, a very popular place amongst the locals. Wow, who knew?! I seen this place while going to Carrabas, and heard about Mikes sushi, but didn't know this was the spot. Sign outside in the plaza just reads Sushi(no Mikes anywhere lit up visibly ) FYI. I'll definitely have this spot on sushi rotation. Between specials and service, Mikes and Hot Tuna, best places for sushi in the local area so far.

I'm a very laid back kind of chick. That is one of the reasons Why I really love this brewery . Great place to sit, relax and watch the people pass by on the sidewalk in downtown St. Pete, while hanging out with friends. We have seen some pretty interesting things around these streets. :-D makes for great conversation and laughs. Besides all that goodness, they have one of the best IPA's around . I Can't get enough of that Crank

Cute Place, I liked it. Friendly service. Limited seating(about 12) filled with regular customers. Everyone seemed to know one another which is nice. 
My latte was good, not as frothy as I like , but good enough. They also use Kahwa which is good quality and has nice flavor. 
I like the little Baguette sandwiches. Very European style. Simple, Not big , but just right to go with your coffee. The fruit impressed. There was papaya, pineapple and kiwi with grape and banana( very fresh) . Glad to see some exotic fruits in there besides your typical Apple, grapes.. Etc.. 
The item that impressed me the least was the Anesta. Not sure if it's just not all that or I got a bad one. I'm positive it was a bit over baked . I was thinking when I saw it in the case,  that it was a bit darker in color,  but the description read rum soaked, so I thought well maybe it's supposed to look like that because of the rum. I took a bite... It was a bit dry, and tasted like it was on the verge of being burnt. Plus, I didn't taste or smell any rum flavor. Bummer. 
The quiche was light, fluffy and enjoyed. 
I wanted to try the French Toast :-(
That's what I really came In for after seeing the Brady S pic. It looks amazing , but they do not serve that on weekdays, just weekends along with a couple of other egg items. Only sandwiches, salads, quiche and Pastries.. FYI. 
I'd come back when in the area. It would def be my first choice over any chain coffee shop like Starbucks, etc.

I loved the vibe of this little place. With no inside seating, this place was still surprisingly comfortable. I was lucky enough to get a seat at the bar, and enjoyed a beer while I waited for my food to go. We ordered a Cuban, Lechon sandwich, and Frita Burger. All great! 
The Lechon Sandwich was one of my favs. The pork was perfectly moist, and I loved the onions & cilantro. I did put some hot sauce on mine only because I love a little heat, and then it was perfection. Frita Burger was ordered by accident, but what a delicious accident it was. It was juicy, very flavorful and I love the little Fritas sprinkled all over the place. 
Bodega is right there neck and neck with my favorite Tia's, but I do like Tia's Authentic Latin Food more simply because I'm in love with their Cuban Reuben. It can not be beat. Tia's pork really just packs more of a flavor punch to your mouth :-) but like I said, Bodega is right there nipping at the back of their heels. 
What I do like a lot from this place though is the interesting selection of sandwiches, plates, and sides. I need to try the Jicama Slaw next time I'm in. I totally forgot about it until I saw someone order a side. Boo hoo. Love the large variety of drinks to choose from like juices, smoothies, soda frescas, specialty coffees, wine, and beer. Always a plus. 
Love the fact that they have a few craft beers on tap from some of the local breweries in the area. Plus! Plus!  Staff was very friendly too. Plus! Definitely way worthy of the 5 star Yelp Rating. I think they just earned themselves a regular customer:-)

I really want to like this place, but the service sucks ass big time, and the 3 times I've been here it has not even been busy for it to suck so bad. 
I don't understand the problem. It also takes forever to get your food here. If it was busy ok, but if there is no one else that is waiting for food except one table(me) then why does it take 20 something minutes for a black bean burger? 
It already took about 15 to order the damn thing, it was missing ingredients, and even came out with the wrong side. At least I got to keep the wrong side, and also got my ordered side which was one plus out of the situation. Seriously, if my friends didn't want to eat here, I would never come here at all. 
The food is decent when you get it, but don't count on it being hot . Sometimes, it's lukewarm to cool. I got lucky and got hot food last night. 
I was not crazy about my black bean burger . It had a weird dark orange center, and I wasn't too crazy about the consistency. The fries were really good even though I didn't order them. They were my free mistake. 
I would really like to give this place a higher rating, but it's just not there for me. The flavor is there, everything else, not so much. Tighten up, Meh. 
Draught Haus, you are my desperate late night destination for food when no one else is open or getting ready to close ... Wha-wha-whaa.

This is the most underwhelming Mexican place ever. I knew what it was, but for some odd apparent reason my friend actually likes this place and wanted to eat here. You know when you walk in a restaurant and u can smell all the delicious aromas coming from the kitchen? Well, this place smells like frying oil right when u walk in the door. I tried to order the safest thing on the menu which were nachos. They were bland. How can nachos be bland?.. I have no idea, but they managed to pull it off. Completely flavorless. My friends molcajete looked like a grease pit with meat. So much oil. I can't , I won't again. Not worth the calories

I've been wanting to try this place for a while now, but I'm Greek so I tend to be a little harsher on Greek restaurants and bakeries, and don't really go because I'm always like, Meh! I kicked myself in the butt that I didn't try this place sooner.. 
Great Spanakopita, perfectly stuffed.. Great flavor. Some places make their Spanakopites too sour because they add too much lemon. I don't know why they even add lemon at all. I would say that is more of a middle eastern thing, not Greek .. (Just my opinion), but this place does not go overboard and they were very tasty.
Delicious Bougatsa.. I'm over indulging in it as I type this right now.  
Fresh baked breads
Good Coffee  
Sesame cookies & Koulouria 
So many other pastries, cookies, breads to name. They even make sandwiches using their own fresh baked bread, salads, etc. I don't know, I couldn't concentrate when I was in there. I was a little kid in a Greek candy store:-) I went early so the place was filled with goods, and the owner was baking still so A.D.D. kicked in... I was like, ooh look at that, then off pointing at something else before they could even answer me back.
Very surprised to see Koulouria, I don't see those too often in the states, and the Greeks just love to eat those with cheese, olives and their coffee in the morning, including me :-) the only time I get to eat fresh baked ones is when I take vacation in Greece. My first time here so of course I did not try everything. There was so many other things that I would have liked to try and buy, but I didn't want to overdo it. I left with a bag of 30 dollars worth of stuff. If u decide to try, make sure u get there early for the biggest selection. The owner is there baking continuously throughout the morning till the early afternoon. So, the earlier the freshest (still warm). Noticed they also have cappuccinos and Lattes.. Next time!

I would say off the 2 things I ordered that the Lomo Saltado was very tasty , I would give that a 5 star .. Delicious! But unfortunately, that wasn't my meal, I only had a couple bites of that. My meal was the Pescado a lo Macho which was so so.. Everything in it was cooked to perfection. The fish was fried perfect. Tender and flaky. The shrimp and calamari were tender... The only thing lacking was the flavor in the sauce. There wasn't any really .. I added some of a creamy orange hot sauce that I asked for to kick it up a notch and see what happens, but it still was lacking. I thought Pescado a Lo Macho was already supposed to have a little spiciness to it already, but this one did not have one hint.. I can't put my finger on what it needed. Definitely salt though, I know that, but there was none on the table. I looked around, but there were none on any of the tables in the whole restaurant ! I still half enjoyed it after the addition of the hot sauce. I'm glad I had the $10 check in offer from Yelp. It definitely made it more ok. I would go back and try something else, I know this place has much more to offer.

If Yelp had a half star, I would give this restaurant a 3.5 rating. 
I ordered the oxtail, and can say I liked it, but I did not get the same experience that most Yelpers have expressed here. 
They were lukewarm. They were not fall off the bone tender. They did not come with any butter beans or dumpling cooked within. This would have made the meal a bit more filling and tasty.
We also ordered the Jerk chicken. I did enjoy this item more than the oxtails. Nice and spicy. The spices were cooked deep within the meat. Lips were burning which I like. 
Both dishes came with the thinnest slices of plantains. That was pretty disappointing. 
I liked the food, it's good. 
I would give this place another shot and try some more items because I wanna looove ya, I wanna love and treat you right. I wanna looove ya, every day and every night, but could improve on some things.

I have one hand on my sandwich and one on my phone writing this review! I couldn't wait to write how delicious it is.. Uh-M-A-Z-I-N-G!  I ordered the Cuban Reuben and as soon as I took my first bite I was In Heaven. There was nothing else in the room but me and the sandwich . I was fully focused on it. Usually, my friend and I are talking up a storm, but there was not a peep between us two while eating, and that is rare. If you haven't been here, get here now. They just moved to this newer location which is 2 stores down from the old location a couple of months ago, So they're back and re-opened for business! It's clean , spacious, new booths, and bar.

My favorite Health Food Store in Pinellas County. I can wander around here for hours reading labels and just checking everything out. 
They have some of the most reasonable prices around, and keep sales on heavy rotation . I love that I can get Nutiva 54oz Coconut oil here for around $23, and great price on Braggs Apple Cider Vinegar, 2 items I use heavily at home. I also bought Organic Dandelion Greens today on sale for only $2.29 for a bunch. I love juicing and eating those. Besides all of the great sales, and other things I can talk about, is the juice , sandwich, salad, hot, and espresso bar. Love their sandwiches! Pressed Turkey Chipotle will bitchslap your taste buds . Can't get enough of that sandwich. So simple, yet so delicious! Great bread.

2nd visit has earned the 5 star review. Although , not my favorite Po'Boys(but still very good) in the area, I feel that they earn the extra star because of these reasons..

Side choices- they have them :-D a variety to choose from, and made in house, not just chips or fries. 

Specials. I think they only offer one item daily or one item and run it for the whole week, not sure , but they do offer something that's not on regular menu. 

I love the location. Who doesn't love downtown Dunedin? They have a cute little place right underneath a huge Oak tree. Plenty of outside colorful seating. I love to people watch.  

Alcohol! Whoo Hoo! Get your drink on and enjoy your favorite Po'Boy with a nice cold Brewski or Wine. 

Desserts. They have a couple of JJGandy items. Who doesn't love Love JJGandy? I do. I love Jodi too, the daughter . Sweetheart:-)

Extra Bonus.. They're very friendly . 

I tried the Alligator sausage Po'Boy(sorry no pic this time)on this visit, and it was thoroughly enjoyed. The potato salad was Fabulous. When I got in the car , I was like shoot! I forgot to put hot sauce on my potato salad, but when I took my first bite , I was happy to discover that it's already spicy. I was a Happy Camper. 

My first visit I had an Oyster Po'Boy and I think the oysters were too well done? Idk. I might try again one day because I've seen a lot of compliments on it , but first I've got it make it down the list before I come back around. I don't know what I'm getting next , but i know it's going to involve those hush puppies everyone's talking about .

Awesome little Brewery! I can't believe I've never been in before. What the hell was I thinking?. I love that they have the $2.00 4.oz sample option. They also had a lot of interesting choices that I couldn't pass up so I went a little beer crazy and tried 6. I think I might have found my new favorite brewery. When I was leaving I seen them tapping a new beer and now I'm wondering what I missed. Love Public Love!!

I've been here 3 times to catch an apple fritter and on the 3rd try I finally scored one. Not my favorite. Too much cinnamon for my taste. Really sweet. It's big enough for 2 people so keep that in mind when you order one of these monsters.
The donuts are awesome.
Their Maple Bacon is the best! Oh my god , it's heaven. 
I try not to be greedy and buy them all when i stop in. 
All the donuts happen to be very sweet so if you're sensitive to that just a little FYI. 
I just don't use sugar or honey in my coffee/tea when I eat these. 
I'll be back to try more of the basics, I really don't care for all the extra crafty ones with candies etc., these donuts are already sweet enough. 
... God Bless this place for having a Drive Thru.

If you're in the area, this is a good place to get a great coffee to go. The latte I ordered was made with a nice creamy froth on top and tasted great. Good beans! I'm pretty sure they are just starting up so there wasn't any food offerings like pastries and such that I seen. I looked on the little blackboard and they do offer cereal, but not anything else visible on sight besides that. Not much of an atmosphere yet, but like I said they are just starting so that could change. The barista(owner maybe)Omar was very pleasant and took time to explain the coffee choices and how they are made with us. I will definitely go back if I'm in the area and haven't had my fix yet. It isn't easy to find places who can make espresso drinks that have that kind of amazing froth.
Convenient, friendly-neighborhood deli. It is cash only, but there is an ATM on site. Vegan friendly options, if you're into that. Mr. Lee is a hoot and food ain't half bad.

The ambiance is great. Loved the look of the place but upon entering into the bar on the 2nd floor you noticed a 20 degree temp jump. We ordered a martini upstairs and noticed the happy hour specials. There are no real appetizers unless you want to call a taco one. We sat for a few upstairs and decided it was best to move to the bar downstairs to finish our dinner. 

Downstairs is cooler in the summer of Tucson. We ordered food in that bar area. Service is VERY slow. If you are an advertised high end establishment I should not have to notify anyone (waiter, bartender) my martini needs a refill. They should be all over my needs. This was imply not the case. I had to hail down someone even for my water to be refilled. 

Steak was good, but the end price of $66.00 for it was a bit pricey when the service to support it was not there.

Hey guys you have been open for a while now. Let's train your staff in customer service and turn down the AC in the summer of AZ.

Probably one of the few spots in the city to get a somewhat healthy bite at. 

LOL! Hey, the Big Easy is not the kind of place to stick to a diet!

Had the grilled shrimp po'boy while shopping in the French Market and it was decent. Seats around the counter or tables across to take a load off.

Affordable menu of items, and very friendly service. Also, check out their selection of hot sauces, spices and Louisiana entree mixes if you're the adventurous type and want to do some Creole cooking at home.

Be a tourist. Walk around a look at all the old photos and plaques stating Pat O'Brien's history.

Sit in the courtyard. Hang out until the sun goes down and see it's famous fountain come to life with fire and lights.

Order up a super potent Hurricane. You can just get it in a large plastic cup, or purchase it in the souvenir glass to bring home for an extra $4. If you decide to not take the glass you get the $4 back. It's a bit sugary but also packs a punch.

Maybe take in a dueling pianos show at this classic bar. Pretty classic thing to see here in the Big Easy.

Sip away life's problems and enjoy the scene. Heck, you're here to kick back and drink. Have at it.

You will get seriously buzzed. Enjoy life. I know I did when I was here.

Beignets.

That's all you need to know. Just do it. It's a must to make a pilgrimage here when in the Big Easy. It's sacrilege if you don't.

Those sugary doughy puffs of powdery goodness are magical. Along with cups of delicious cafe au lait. Sure, it's a tourist spot, but it's part of New Orleans history. Have a seat and take it all in.

Oh, and we were here pre-covid so we got to have a real experience. Take all those giving bad reviews who visited during the pandemic shutdown with a grain of salt. It's not the same.

I'm sorry but I just don't get all the recent negative reviews of this place. To me it just looks like a lot of people seem to find things to complain and whine about. 

Hello - it's a CASINO. Not everyone wins.
Hello - it's a CASINO. People are allowed to smoke there in Florida.
Hello - it's a CASINO. On weekends most tables will have high limits.
Hello - it's a CASINO. In Florida. Agreement with the state is to not give away free drinks since it is a Native American facility.
Hello - it's a CASINO. They are in the business to make money.

That all being said, I had a fun time here this past weekend celebrating Father's Day with my parents. Contrary to some of the previous reviews here this casino does offers some great comps based on your level of play and frequency of visits. That is how it is determined to whom gets what. My mom got free rooms for both of us, we were compted on all our meals, and even received a nice discount on the poolside cabana we booked for all day on Sunday. Make sure you join the players club and use your card on all slot and table games to build up your points. I have only been here a few times before and received mailings for free rooms, free slot dollars, and free meals already.

This casino is huge, tons of machines over multiple gaming rooms, and table games of blackjack, poker, and others. Table limits are in the $15-$50 range on weekends. Live band and DJ plays in the small bar/ lounge area up front by the check in desk. Mixed crowd of mostly older 20's up through seniors. There are a few bars to hang at. Gets crowded and jumping on weekends. 

The rooms are terrific. Nice size. Super comfy bed. Large flat screen TV. Great bathroom and toiletries. Tivoli stereo system. In-wall safe. Bath robes. Very clean. Cool decor. Rock star portraits on the walls. The whole casino and rooms are in the process of being outfitted for wifi in the next few months. Also has a nice little gym to get a workout in that is free to use if staying there. Spa services too.

The pool area is wonderful and chic. Long rectangular pool surrounded by tropical plants and trees, cabana's all around, bar area, hot tub, waterfall, waitress service all day, and lots of lounge chairs to kick back in. I partied all day Sunday with my dad for Father's Day there. We had a cool waitress who served us a lot of beers, bloody marys, and shots throughout the day. Nothing like hanging out in the cabana with cigars, cold beers, and the ball game on our flatscreen. Not to mention the fun people watching at poolside.

Had burger platters with fruit delivered to our cabana for lunch. Burgers here are pretty tasty with applewood smoked bacon. Large fruit cup in a large martini glass came with it. Also had dinner at the buffet. As most buffets go it has its pros and cons. Nothing special here but nothing too bad either. Reasonably priced, but line to get in can be long. Mom got a casino host to usher us right in - yes! Had breakfast at the Green Room which is their diner. Breakfast there is always good. Large farmers omelette with grits and an English muffin. Tasty coffee too. There is also a small food court to grab a quick bite, a steak house, and a sushi bar.

Staff and service is nice and attentive. Most I have come into contact with have been friendly. I thought the casino floor and bathrooms were pretty clean overall. Can get a bit smokey, but that can be expected at a casino. Rock music is playing all day, and there is a lot of music memorabilia to discover everywhere here. Slots can be tight but my mom won a good amount over the two days. Sometimes you just have to be lucky with what machines you play. Blackjack was fun and I broke even so nothing to complain about. The casino is bright and hopping. We all had a great time here. Is it Vegas or Atlantic City? No, but it does a good job as a gaming spot for the locals in the Tampa area and surrounding towns. Will definitely be back!

When walking around the French Market on a warm day and in need of a cold refreshing drink the Organic Banana is a decent enough choice.

This spot features a menus full of boozy frozen smoothies. Juicy and fruity for around $8 - $9 each these concoctions hit the spot. They also have some beers to choose from, and non-alcoholic options.

Grab your drink and meander around while shopping, or take a spot at one of the tables close by with something to nosh on.

We had to go with the Pina Colada and Almond Freeze. Both were pretty tasty, and with Kahlua in the almond smoothie "The Dude Abides"!

If you are ever in New Orleans as we were during Christmas season a must visit is the Royal Sonesta. Even if you're not staying here you're welcome to walk through the lobbies to take in their terrific holiday decorations.

Each area you look at and wander through has beautifully decorated Christmas trees, flower arrangements, lighting, and even a ginger bread house version of the hotel ( complete with that creepy Elf on a Shelf ). You can tell they put a lot of effort into this. 

I'm sure the staff here must get tired of the tourists coming in to look around, but the desk staff was nice enough to answer some questions we had.

It was a nice little break from the crazy fun outside for a few minutes.

Greasy spoon hole in the wall that is cheap and open 24/7 to help soak up all the booze one consumes on Bourbon Street.

Pretty much the only true diner in the area. Since 1939, and looks the part. Small and gritty with a nice/patient/understanding staff, this is the kind of joint you roll into during the wee hours of the morning in a drunken drooling stupor to order up some breakfast, a greasy burger, coffee, and some tater tots to recover.

I enjoy these kinds of places. A piece of Americana from simpler times.

Small spot with a few tables and some counter seating. The grill is right in front so you will be covered in the smokiness of the food being fried up. It at once smells a bit off-putting and amazing at the same time. Like you need to be here. Like you need to walk out smelling like week old fried food. Take in the aroma in all it's glory. Breathe in deeply. 

As for the food? Actually not too shabby, just don't expect a gourmet experience. It's down and dirty diner eats in it's most simplistic form. Our breakfasts and coffee were decent enough and did the trick. Sent us back on our way for more debauchery on Bourbon Street. 

Also, read the menu closely. There are some funny one-liners written throughout it in between the food listings.

When vacationing in New Orleans sometimes you need a break from the raucous crowds, loud noise, bars, and partying. 

There are some good spots to eat in town more on the outskirts of the French Quarter. We found Saint Lawrence not too far from our hotel and went there for dinner one night.  

Terrific gastropub. Nice atmosphere, tasty food, quality cocktails, local beer on tap, decent prices, and friendly service. Nifty joint for a more subdued dinner away from the craziness of the Bourbon Street area.

The fried chicken here is on-point, as was the lemon butter gulf fish. A highlight was the mac & cheese - so good!

Worth a stop if you want to relax and take a break from the madness.

Nice spot to stay for a trip to the Big Easy. 

Located right along the mighty Mississippi River, Harrah's casino across the street, outlet shopping mall connected to it, and just a few minutes walk or cheap Lyft ride from all the action in the French Quarter. It's also connected to the convention center so if your company is doing an event here this is a prime spot.

Hotel is huge, no really, this place is sprawling. Multi-levels, restaurants, meeting rooms, business center, bars, convenience store that serves Starbucks coffee, you name it.

The gym here is terrific, and the upper level is a sight to see as there is a gigantic area filled with tennis, volleyball, basketball, and paddleball courts. My one gripe is that there is a fee to use the gym ($12) even if you're a guest at the hotel. In my opinion, registered guests should have free use of the facility. This is kind of petty to me. Yet, Hilton Honors Silver, Gold and Diamond guests enjoy complimentary access so there's that. 

We had a good four day getaway here. The rooms are clean, safe in the closet, large flat screen TV, well maintained bathroom, and the staff is very professional. Easy to get around to all the sights and sounds of New Orleans. It's off the beaten path from the craziness of Bourbon Street, and offers a quieter option to get a good night's sleep, but close enough to be right back in the action the next day.

Ok. So I have seen ads for this place on my Facebook for months. Otherwise, I would have never known it existed. It was the $25 bottomless mimosas that caught my attention enough to make sure I visited. Bottomless mimosas?!? Yes please!!

My sister made the reservation, which she moved to a later time without any issues. There are paid parking lots across the street and adjacent to this venue. I paid $20 for all day parking on a Sunday. I probably could have found free parking, but I didn't feel like it.

Walking it, this place is definitely a sports bar. TVs are everywhere. Upon entry you walk into a classic bar. If you walk further back, it is more of an open space, with lot more TVs, and tables set up for brunch. We had to pay a $100 deposit for the table/mimosas.

The menu was better than I expected (I meant to take a picture, sorry!). I ordered chicken and waffles. My friend ordered strawberry cheesecake french toast, and my sister ordered eggs Benedict (all pictured). Honestly, I was scared to order chicken and waffles from anywhere but Roscoe's... But what I got was a good play on the dish in general. It was fried chicken breast strips (thank God, I didn't want bone and I took a gamble by ordering and not asking). These strips were super crispy (which I loved, loved, LOVED), and seasoned very well. There were not traditionally fried either. Whatever they did, I liked it. The waffles came with lots of butter, and strawberries on top.

We went through 4 rounds of bottles. So the bottomless mimosas definitely worth it! They played house music, which wasn't a problem at all. Our waitress Jennie was very attentive. The bathrooms were super clean, which as  female is very much appreciated.

We had an issue with billing. The manager came right to our table, grabbed a seat and tried to resolve the issue as best as he could. He also gave his card with his phone number for us to follow up on the issue with him. Very, very professional.

Would I come back to this place? Most definitely! It is definitely a hidden gem!

This place has been around for years... and as a West Indian, I am ashamed to say it has taken me this long to get in here.

Usually, I hear about this place for the lounge. I just never got around to it.

This past Saturday night, my best friend suggested we go and eat. I wasn't really hungry, so I ate something lighter.
