I got the jerk chicken cheesesteaks with calypso fries. I was SHOCKED. I usually gravitate towards anything jerk chicken. So this was definitely not my first jerk chicken cheesesteak... but this was the BEST I have ever had. Even the fries were good.

I did not eat my whole sandwich, so I had some for later, which was a plus! I would definitely return here for food.

I did not go up to the lounge aspect of this venue. But the music was on point.

I won't be going back.

I visited on Labor Day. It was hot. Most restaurants bring you water but I had to ask three different people before I got a glass. No one came by to refill it until I was done. It seems like the staff decided to stay inside where it was cool rather than attend to their customers.

My burger was ordered medium-rare and was served gray-brown throughout. It is certainly not worth the money.

My wife and I gave Sam's a try on a Friday night - 30 minutes before sunset.

The place was packed, and we were told there was a 30 minute wait for a table.

We went to the tiki bar and had 4 margaritas - taking them back to the waiting area, so we wouldn't miss our name...

Two hours passed, and we were never seated - the staff and manager were unsympathetic/unapologetic.

Of course, I have no review of the food, but the (lack of) service was poor - and we weren't the only people leaving out of frustration.

With a babysitter deadline, we resorted to Greek take-out on the way home... 

Parking in Hudson Beach is pretty bad - two lots are typically full, and the third is for vehicles with boat trailers only...

Omg, the peanut butter & jelly cupcake makes me drool thinking about it in retrospect. I loved the adorable owners who were super friendly when I went on a Friday night. Also, huge props for vegan cupcakes. I'm not a vegan, but I'm lactose intolerant so it was awesome to not have to worry about dietary restrictions at a cupcake joint.

I was visiting semi-nearby Longwood Gardens with four others and decided to try this place for dinner because of all the positive reviews. I was not disappointed. Yelp really works!

Upon entering, we were immediately greeted and asked if we wanted any drinks. While they don't take reservations, we only had to wait 10 minutes for a table that could accommodate us. Service was so personable and prompt throughout the meal.

I started with a "small plate" of Fried Artichoke Hearts which came with a lemon-garlic aoli. So good! Then I had a Pulled Pork sandwich with my choice of sauce (North Carolina or Cumin BBQ), cole slaw, and hand cut fries. I chose Cumin BBQ for the sandwich and it was super delicious. I inhaled it! The pork really seemed to be pulled by hand and was very tender and tasty with just a hint of spice. The cole slaw was well-balanced and on the crisper, dryer side which I personally appreciate. I sampled my friend's Thai Red Curry (vegetables over basmati rice and served with homemade naan and your choice of protein- this time, tofu). Slightly peanutty, smokey, deep flavors- yummy! We were all full, but to finish, we shared a Cheese Plate (from their "Small Plates" part of the menu) which was served with honey on the comb, fig jam, what seemed to be Asian pear slices, and small bread slices. That evening, we chose a bleu cheese, raw cow milk cheese, and the earthy, tangy, and grassy Birchrun Hills Fat Cat which was my favorite. Mmmmmm. Station Taproom has pub food elevated beyond your wildest dreams!

I believe this is the Boise area's first poke bowl restaurant. It's in the Roseauer's lot on Eagle Road, next to Togo's.

I ate here for lunch (actually carried out) on opening day, with my wife. We shared a "regular" (3 scoop fish) poke bowl on white rice, with wasabi shoyu, crab, seaweed salad, green onions, cucumbers, and sesame seeds. I was impressed...service was quick, and although $12 for a bowl seems pricey, it's a lot of food...basically de-constructed sushi...so really it's like $6/person. It was opening day, so they didn't have credit cards working yet; cash only.

Logistics:
You can see from the pix what the menu is and how it works. Basically it's Chipotle-style, they build a bowl for you. The fish was good (maybe not the best in the world, but still tasty) and the serving sizes were reasonable (of course they could've been bigger, but they were decent-sized). The interior was clean and nice, and I was surprised by how many people were there.

Food:
No complaints...shoyu had a nice amount of wasabi, fish was tasty, rice was fresh, and toppings were quite good. It feels like a pretty healthy lunch, but I suspect if you check it might be less healthy than you think. Still a nice indulgence.

We will be back...this can easily go on the lunch rotation. Tasty and filling, and kinda scratches the sushi itch. I hope the place sticks around...based on the volume of business today, they'll have no trouble.

We had an engagement on the west coast of Florida so I figured let's make a weekend getaway out of it.  First stop was dinner so of course I went to Yelp for suggestions.

Here's what I don't get about Yelp. The purpose, as I understand it, is to give honest reviews. I understand we are all different and our opinions may vary, but come on . How Bumpa's has an average of 4 Stars with 162 reviews is criminal. 

Here's our experience....  Friday night in Clearwater Beach and there's about four tables occupied including us. Oh, BTW they have live music, if you want to call it that. Remember Adam Sandler, in the "Wedding Singer". This guy was 100 times worse. Could barely understand what he was singing.

Next we open our napkins to find dirty greasy knives and forks. An apology from our waiter and replacements.

We order an appetizer to share. "Shark Bites". They come to the table and are set down in the middle. Can we have some small plates? Waiter.. Of I think we can do that. 

My wife has grilled lobster tails with, I assume is their version of drawn butter. I dipped my pinky in to taste. I'm not sure what it was but it wasn't butter, it left a coating in my mouth with an after taste.

Let's move on.  Next my wife's sister orders their 1 pound of snow crab legs. No cracker, small fork, or bowl for the shells.  Same story with her drawn butter. When she's done she asks for wet wipes. You know the little packets you always get with shell fish. The waiter is not sure if they have any but will check. He comes back with " the last three they have". Must be kidding right?

I had the " Hog Fish" which was Ok.

All in all a big miss. Don't know the next time I'll be back n Clearwater Beach, but when I am you won't find me here.

I'm just trying to be honest, so please, my Yelp brothers and sisters, please do t give passes to restaurants that don't deserve it. If you give them high ratings you're just telling them the fact that they don't care is OK.  See you on the beach.

This review has been a long time coming. In fact it got lost until this week when I was in the area for business.

Located on the beach with an ocean view, the location can't be beat, but unless the food is good, location alone won't cut it. 

Ok let's get this show on the road. Very nautical atmosphere. Wood picnic style tables with bench seats. Not my favorite but I get it. We were s party of three, my wife, her brother, and me.

Our waitress was a Maryland transplant and very personable. In fact she sat down at our table with us to chat while taking our order. 

I look at the menu and see "Rock Shrimp ". No need to look any further, my order is in. 

My wife and her brother order burgers. OMG I'm speechless. We're on St. Petersburg Beach and you guys order hamburgers. I'm beyond embarrassed.

Well here comes my Rock Shrimp, In all their glory. OH MAMA.  Have fun with your hamburgers and just leave me along with these succulent Rock Shrimp. I think there was a side or two with them but I couldn't concentrate on the sides, just those beautiful shrimp.

Slight downside. All drinks come with paper straws. An effort to save the birds and seas life from idiots who throw their plastic straws on the beach. Jerks.

Here's the thing with paper straws. After three or four sips, they become water logged and collapse. They have to come up with another type of material for straws or people have to stop being jerks. I think I know which way that is gonna go.

Enough tree hugging. I loved this place and I know you will too. It's a casual relaxing atmosphere. Most importantly, TRY GHE ROCK SHRIMP.

I've been on a kick with this style of restaurant. First I love shellfish, so a "Crab Boil" is just the right meal for me.

I've been finding these restaurants in many cities around the country, particularly in the south.

So I'm in Nashville, Tennessee for work and before I check into my hotel I must eat. "Juicy Seafood " pops up and I'm all in.

It's in a shopping center so plenty of parking. It's a little late on a Wednesday evening so not too may people eating and no wait.   Desare is my waitress, sorry for misspelling, but she was great. Took my order and made a couple of good suggestions . In asking about the heat levels she thought I was asking for "Hot". Oh no she says, it way too hot, stick with the medium.

Next she shows up with all necessary utensils, claw cracker. Claw meat picker, and of course a bib.

I ordered the King Crab, sausage, and Shrimp, which comes with  corn on the Cobb, and potatoes. Of course in a delicious  sauce.  Claws were a good amount, and it seemed like an endless amount of shrimp.

You got me with the shrimp.

Sausage was really good, but sliced very thin. Corn was tender and juicy. I didn't eat the potatoes because there was a lot of food  . Just didn't have room for them.

Before I leave, Deserie brings a to go cup for my drink.

Ok, you don't have to ask, I highly recommend  "Juicy Seafood ", so if you go keep a lookout for Deserie she's the best.

I'm in Nashville for work and everything is going smoothly. I love when that happens. So as I'm driving I notice this restaurant. Looks rustic on the outside, but remember this is Nashville, Country Music where everything is sort of rustic looking.

I walk in and am seated immediately. The place is huge with a few large dining rooms. I'm in a room with a large water feature. Did I say huge? Like an inground pool huge, with a water fall and a fountain.

Ok. My waiter is a pleasant young man, who  welcomes me to Nashville and goes over the menu with me. Compact menu but covers a host of entrees. They have a section on the menu for game meat. Not for me, thank you.

I settled for the 12 oz marinated rib eye. So he takes my drink order and meal order and is off. 

Just a couple of minutes pass and he's back with my drink, and holy moly, a food runner shows up with my meal. It was so fast I'm in shock and so is my waiter. In fact he says " cut that steak open and check the temp".  It was cooked so fast he's concerned that it's may be under cooked. Kudos to him. 

I cut into the end and accept the steak. My mistake because as I got closer to the center it's rare, very rare, and to boot, half way through the steak I realize it's not marinated.

Well I finished and ask for my bill and am on my way. If yes my waiter was very apologetic but he was not to blame. In fact I'm willing to accept part of the blame for not sending it back,

For me, unfortunately not a good experience.

Update 6/7/2020: In light of the social unrest in our city and country, and as a Black woman, I had to address how disappointed I was in this company's response to concerned patrons. 

A few days ago, patrons asked them how/if they planned to support their customers and workers of color in the fight for equity and against racism. The org immediately got defensive on social platforms, began blocking users and arguing with others. I've said many times in my reviews the customer is not necessarily always right, I still believe that. However, the customer deserves to have their concerns addressed. Unfortunately, the exact opposite happened. Saying you don't see color when many of your patrons and and staff are Black is concerning. If you don't see color, you don't see my struggle, my pain or my joy. 

I've always been intentional about supporting local and buying from businesses whose values align with mine. Unfortunately, General American Donut has shown me that we are not aligned and so, I can no longer support this company. 


My partner and I always venture out for a donut on Saturday mornings, this morning we decided to try General American Donut after seeing so many post about it on social media. The service was quick and kind. 

I ordered The Indiana, a fried chicken biscuit with jam on it. Instagram swore by this sandwich, but it was only okay to me. Separately the flavors were all good, but together it didn't work for me. The chicken was hot and fresh (as it should be) but the biscuit was lukewarm and very dry. It crumbled after one bite. I expected the jam to really stand out, but it did not. It was just kind of there, not spectacular, but not terrible either. Lastly, I would've liked my chicken seasoned just a bit more. 

I ordered a side of fries as well, which I'd say you can skip. They're shoe fly fries, which I don't like (just personal preference, not their fault!) and mine had way too much salt on them. 

I also tried a bite of my partners cake donut, that was really good! One of my favorites I've had in the city. Their creative donut flavors sound good, and I'll probably be back to try a few, but I can't say the chicken sandwich is one I'd order again. 

Just a note I feel I have to mention as I write this during a pandemic: none of the employees had masks on. That was concerning and frustrating to see. I believe every customer I saw walk in was wearing one and they did have a clear barrier up between where you order/pay and the customer. But I've gotten so used to seeing food workers in masks, not seeing them wear them was something that jumped out at me.

I haven't had a single thing I don't like here, and my order is always correct. The homemade burgers and breakfast sandwiches are my faves, and the fries are always well-seasoned. I particularly love that they have (delicious) beef bacon as an alternative to pork (that's better than turkey bacon).

Wow what a total bust, there are such high ratings but this place definitely fell below my expectations. We were on State St and my Husband was craving a burger. I found this place through Yelp and was excited to try it because of the high ratings. First off the service was horrible, the girl didn't even provide us refills on the drinks, she was actually headed out and was too busy counting her money than to pay attention to us. It was so hot too a refill on water would have been nice. I ordered the chicken panini with a side salad and he ordered their fig burger with fries. When the order came out, our sides were mismatched, he got my salad and I got his fries, how annoying is that. In addition, I specifically said no tomatoes on the salad and what did I get? Tomatoes!! The fries were awful too, very soggy and not fresh. The chicken panini was not that great, there was a big piece of mozarella cheese which I love however it wasn't melted, aren't panini's supposed to be hot and melted, that wasn't the case with mine. My husband hated his burger he barely ate half.  All in all we had a horrible dining experience and the service could have been better. I definitely wouldn't come back and wouldn't recommend it.

My taste buds are still buzzing from my dinner at Vista Ramen last night...oh man...this place is special.

Right when you walk in, your cool points skyrocket.  The space is beautiful with a polished rustic interior.  The exposed kitchen is buzzing.  The music is interesting and upbeat, played at just the right volume.  And the people working there have style.

This isn't just a ramen spot, there's a bunch pan-Asian dishes with various influences like Korean, Japanese, Thai... Kicked off with a cocktail special made with gin, mint, yuzu syrup and machta green tea ($10).  Quite fantastic.

Then there's the food...the Korean fried chicken sliders ($10 for 2) are essential.  Everything about these was perfection.  The hot crispy chicken...the Korean spicy sauce that hits you with a punch, and then the sweet Hawaiian bun.  And the pickle. All in a nice little non-messy package. My god this was good.   

If you like beets, definitely get the beets w/ black sesame bread, burnt lemon, and popcorn ($7).  The plating was an absolute work of art, and the flavors & textures were on point.  Very cool and creative dish.

We went with the veggie ramen ($11) and were not disappointed.  The broth was rich, veggies were delicious, and the soft-boiled egg was just right.  The noodles were al-dente and cooked perfectly.  If I could make one suggestion, it would be to add some mushrooms to it, just because.  Along with the ramen we got a side of cucumber & tofu with lime, ginger, and chili ($6).  I highly recommend this!  The tofu was some of the best I've had, and the brightness of the dish was the perfect contrast to the savory veggie ramen.

I normally don't get dessert when eating out, but the thought of lemongrass-basil ice cream with ginger wafers ($5) was too good to pass up.   Yes, this is as amazing as it sounds, maybe even better.  It was beautifully plated, the ice cream was super creamy, and the taste almost brought tears to my eyes it was so good.  It's worth coming in just for this alone.

Creative and delicious food, great service and a lovely atmosphere to boot....Cherokee Street has definitely upped its game with Vista.  You need to eat here.

DING DING DING ... we have a winner!

A Lebanese buddy of mine (well his grandma is Lebanese) was in town so I decided this was the perfect excuse to revisit Layla and try out some of their meat dishes.

Along w/ the makdoul (baby eggplant & spicy walnuts $4) we ordered the hummus w/ beef appetizer ($8).  I've never combined hummus & beef before but I'd say it was pretty damn good.  The beef was strips of tenderloin and there was PLENTY of it and the presentation was quite nice.

My friend said that lamb chops are a good litmus test of a Lebanese restaurant, so we ordered that for the entree ($15).  When prompted, we asked for them medium-rare.  They came out on a large plate w/ seasoned rice, green beans, and potatoes.  

I swear when I picked up one of those chops and sunk my teeth into it I heard angels sing. These were SO tender, SO moist and juicy, I was just in awe.  The flavors were amazing. Lets say that Layla passed the lamb chop test with flying colors.  Everything else on the plate was very good.

Our super-friendly server guy also brought out a complimentary plate of pickles, olives, and radishes that was very tasty.

Layla is a true gem and I highly encourage everyone to check them out, vegetarians and carnivores alike.  They're open pretty late every day and have a parking lot so you have no excuse...just GO!

So I'm about a month into my resolution to eat every item on the Kitchen Sink menu.  Progess is being made, but I need to step it up...

You can't go wrong w/ the breakfast items here.  The Sink ($8) is a spin on the classic slinger.  Biscuits, sausage, eggs, tots, gravy, jalapeno bacon, and cheese. It is served in a metal tin and is absolutely outstanding in every way.  I'd suggest splitting it with someone...eating a whole one of these can't be good for you.

The Phat Cat ($7) is a Belgian waffle, eggs, meat and tots.  I'm not a huge waffle guy but this place might convert me.  This waffle was fantastic, the perfect texture (crisp on the outside, soft inside) and it had a sweet vanilla flavor.  I did not need to use syrup on this waffle.  It was delicious on it's own.
 
El Classico -- a steak quesadilla w/ eggs over easy, hash browns, cheese ($7).  It was love at first bite.  The steak was thin cut and marinated to perfection.  The tortilla had the perfect crispness and was a bit buttery.  It was HUGE.   This is an absolute no brainer.

The coffee-rubbed steak platter ($8) also impressed.  I could definitely taste the coffee and it was unique and tasty.  Steak, eggs, and tots?  Sign me up.

The house salad ($4) is lettuce, tomato, cukes, onions, egg, (cheese?).  Simple enough.  But what makes it great is that all the ingredients are diced up and evenly distributed, so in one bite, you can taste all the components of the salad.  This is another example of the Kitchen Sink's great execution.

The Falafel sandwich ($6) is one of the few vegetarian items on the menu.  I thought it was decent.  The falafel was tasty but not crisp.  Nothing else made it stand out.  Ah well, can't win em all.

Another thing that's great about the Kitchen Sink is the diversity of the crowd.  It's always a mix of people from all different ages and backgrounds here.  I definitely think it captures a great cross-section of St Louis.  I guess one thing that everyone can get behind is great food at great prices.  

Oh, and I totally broke 100k on the fast and responsive Ms. Pac Man machine, which is kind of a big deal for me.

I wanna throw a little more love to India's Kitchen after an excellent Sunday lunch buffet experience.  It is really fantastic, with 6-7 dishes each of meat & vegetarian dishes.  Good stuff too, like goat curry and palak paneer.  There's also a good salad bar AND dessert, which featured gulab jamuns -- . fried spongy milky balls soaked in rose scented syrup.  An unlimited supply of those can be deadly.

Even better, they had an idli station.  Idli is like a South Indian pancake made of fermented lentil and rice (gluten-free).  You can then trick out your idli with any of the 8 chutney/relish options available. The sweet spicy ginger one was insane! And the coconut cashew also did the trick.  There is also all-you-can-drink serve-yourself masala chai.  They let you sweeten it yourself.  

And the shocker -- all this was just 11 bucks.  Crazy!.  No wonder the place had a good crowd around 1pm.  The buffet is served from 12 to 3 on Sunday.  Just a note -- most of the stuff on the buffet was pretty spicy.  If you can't handle spice you might want to order off the menu.

I believe there is new management there now.  I spoke to one of the new owner/managers and she was extremely helpful and friendly.  Definitely check out the Sunday buffet.

Oh man...I'm seriously crushin' hard right now on this place...

It's been forever since I've had a Chicago beef sandwich, so when I saw the pictures and read the raves, I knew I had to have it.  So I placed a to-go order for a regular-sized sandwich ($6.50), along with a side of spinach rice ($2.25) and an order of baklava ($3.25).  The last 2 items were for Yelp research purposes only, I assure you...

When I saw the sandwich, my first reaction was "Damn, that's a regular size?" .. This sandwich is BIG, with tons of beef and peppers. It is moist and delicious.  And messy.  I would suggest eating this sandwich in the restaurant rather than to-go...it does not travel that well.

Next the spinach rice...I had no idea what to expect, but this stuff was awesome.  Perfectly cooked rice mixed w/ spinach, tomatoes and a nice seasoning.  It was warm and surprisingly hearty.  And a huge portion for the price.  Highly recommended.

A previous review recommended the house-made baklava, so I went for it.  It is AMAZING, both in construction and in taste.  The rose-syrup is so flavorful and really takes this over the edge. The flaky crust, the crunchy nuts...this is absolutely perfect. By far the best baklava I've ever had.  Wow.

I got to share a few words w/ Vinnie (who seems to do everything around there) and he's a really nice and friendly guy.  He showed me some cherry turnover he'd made earlier...it is clear that he is passionate about great food.

Oh..and the place smells awesome!  The moment you step in, you'll know you made the right choice.

What a shame!  My husband and I have eaten at Mortins for special occasions a number of times and we've never had a bad experience.  So when my parents came in to town from Florida we decided to treat them to Morton's. We went when they had the special $49 four course meal... My husband wanted to change out the salad for the French onion soup which was offered as an appetizer to begin with. The main reason is my husband really cannot handle eating any kind of salads  And he explained this to the server.

We were told absolutely not!  This was surprising since we had eaten at Morton's a number of times and we had never had any trouble Requesting this substitution. My husband was in the food industry for a number of years and he understands the cost of meals and the profitability factor so this was a fair exchange... Especially since we had ordered several martinis and also I was drinking wine.  The server forgot to bring my wine and a totally separate person had to get it for me. Then whenever the server would stop by our table it was if she was breezing by... Finally at the end... My husband complained to Cory the Manager.  He said that if we had gotten the $59 special we could've exchanged out for the $11 soup of which there was no indication that any other special was going on. In fact, in the front room there was a big easel with only the $49 special being advertised So one would've thought that this mysterious $59 special would've come up in the course of conversation with the server no? The ultimate embarrassment was when the server came to the table and threw the bill down and dramatically double checked it in front of everyone and declared that it was correct!! If this is what Landry's has done to Morton's Steakhouse... then what a shame.
Lee's has great veggie and black bean steaks. I've been going there for a few years, and it's the spot I frequent most in the neighborhood. Lee and the other employees are always nice.

the prime days of the bacara are over.

work brought me here 9 yrs ago and the memories of this place was still fresh.  9 yrs later i returned and though everything still appears the same, but with close looks at the details, everything has deteriorated and aged ungracefully.

our shower handle was broken off but was never replaced, the in-house tubs were jet tubs but the buttons were all broken...  the flooring showed serious aging, and some lights in the room didn't work...  and the most alarming was we found blood spatters in the bathroom wall that wasn't cleaned.

we were assigned to a 2 bd ocean view room with a massive living space, a bit gratuitous for a happily married couple, but we still appreciated the thoughts.

the pools are still as magical as it was 9 years ago, the spa however, had cracking tiles and poor grout job.  

apparently this resort has gone through a series of different owners and management companies, and it shows :(  it's still as picturesque as ever, but just wished it was better maintained to uphold the ritz standards.

there really isn't too much to do around the resort besides lounge around the pool or go to the spa.  we opted not to visit the beach because there was a tar warning that you may get tar on your feet / shoes...  thanks but no thanks.

oh, and don't even get us started on the food & beverage pricing.  $42 for a breakfast buffet that lacked sustenance...  no wonder everyone opted for the cafe located at the entrance atrium, even that, was $12 for a starbucks quality breakfast sandwich.

A trendy spot right of the campus. With newly remodeled bathrooms and seating out back, this place has the U of A vibe. Eating and drinking alfresco is the theme here.All that being said, the supply is not meeting the demand.

The service was slow, and the server could not keep our drinks full.  We were large group and some of our party did not get their food served in a reasonable time.  One would consider the cocktail size to be small and served in cheap plastic cups. Not a good value... Our food was decent, as we had a wide variety of items from appetizers to sandwiches.  

Consider this a good spot for a quick drink but not ideal for a group dinner.

Salute!

We went back again with 4 other people on another Friday night a few weeks ago. The food was good, not as good as the first time we went.  We got the same mozzarella appetizer and it wasn't nearly as good as the first time, nor was it as large.  My entree was so unimpressive that I can't even remember what I had.  The chicken parm was supposedly not as good as the first time either.

The kicker however, and the reason I lowered it to 2 stars was that they asked us to leave because they had another group waiting for the table, while we were in the middle of eating our dessert.  I understand you don't want to keep people waiting, but you never ask a table to leave. We spent over $250 there and you ask us to leave.  Ok, fine, we'll leave.  And believe me, we will never be back.

Santa Barbara's Funk Zone is such a cool area. Over the past few decades, this district, which spans the area between the ocean and Highway 101 and is adjacent to the Amtrak station. There are so many boutique tasting rooms, cafes, galleries, and shops. 

Converted warehouses and buildings decorated with graffiti murals and contemporary art pieces is where you will find Municipal Winemakers (whose wine club is known as Club Awesome). 

It's a cool vibe inside with a large patio in the front. Try the Mumble; it's delicious. The rest of wine was decent and the fast it's literally surrounded by multiple other wineries is amazing.

I hate to say it, but I have to say that this place has gone way down in the last year or so.  

The food is still good, but the general atmosphere is why I can only give this one star.  It's the subtle things - like no more napkins on the tables (we were told it was because people were using too many) to now, unless you want to sit outside, you cannot choose your table. Yes, this sounds  petty, and yes, I understand that they do not want parties of 2 sitting at a 6 top table when it is busy, so I get it. 

For me, the last straw was the 2 of us having to sit at a 2 top table, with a pizza just as large, and having no place to set your plate.

Because our 2 top table was against the wall, between 2, 4 top tables, I could not get a side tray to set the pizza on because it would block the access to either of the other two tables. 

When that happened, I asked to speak to the Manager, who would have clearly seen the big picture (so I thought), who told me that they would not allow me to move to one of the open 4-6 top tables (this was just after  9:00 pm on a Saturday - they close at 10:00 pm), because it was their 'policy' I was so aggravated that I asked for my money back - not expecting that that she (the Manager) would offer it. 

I asked her if she'd rather give me my money back and lose me as a customer (been going there for 4 years now), and she said yes.  I was floored. 

Poor judgement on her part, combined with my aggravation of having not eaten until after 9:00 pm, meant that this experience was terrible.  I have now sworn them off and have since taken my business elsewhere. 

The most amazing thing is that I was sent a survey (I belonged to their email and text programs until that night), so I wrote a more detailed review of the events, to which I have never been contacted about. I guess they don't need my business. 

Move along.  There is better pizza to be had, for less money, and less hassle.

Horrible Experience. 

I usually would never post a negative review, but my horrific experience needs to be shared. My dish last night arrived with a 2 inch piece of rusted metal in it. This should never happen at restaurants but if it does an apology and or explanation should follow and I received neither. After I walked my dish up to the counter and the server responded with "oh my god", my dish was taken away and eventually a new one was brought out which I didn't touch because I now felt sick to my stomach. My dish was comped from the bill, however this is all that happened. There was again no apology, no additional compensation and I can confidently say I will never return and neither will any of the guests at my table.

Probably the best Thai food in the area but you'll probably spend a little more than you want to on Thai.
Brought a bottle of red (why hasn't anyone mentioned the $3 corking fee?) and swung by here with my new roommate for dinner. We were seated and the waitress came by promptly to fill our water glasses and open our wine. My roommate ordered the special: grilled lamb with bell peppers ($23)and I ordered the beef red curry ($15). The waitress asked if i wanted it spicy, I looked up and said "very spicy" -pause- "extra spicy" and I swear I saw the twinkle in the waitress' eyes. Our dishes were presented beautifully and flavorful. Something about their curry felt like silk in your mouth. The spice level made my lips tingle and my nose run (attractive, I know). Since the curry has milk in it, it was not as spicy as my roommate's dish. His was so spicy that Im pretty sure he ate the flower garnish because the waitress couldn't keep his water glass full. We skipped out on dessert and they gave us some ginger candies with the bill. yeah it sounds nasty but it was actually tasty and settled the tingly sensation from dinner. I'd definatly come back. . . anyone up for some Thai?

Oh *nostalgia* 

I grew up on oversized portions of Italian food, and the Rizzutos did not disappoint. We went in for happy hour for $9 specialty cocktails and half off select appetizers.

First, the bartenders are amazingly talented, and really know what they're doing. I got a gin fizz that was the perfect amount of sweet, sour, & air from the egg whites. I'm determined to go back and try another one of their handcrafted cocktails, you can't go wrong with any choice from these cocktail craftsmen. 

Next, we order the kobe sliders and the meatballs as we decided to take the road toward a beef binge after much convincing from the bartenders. The kobe sliders were huge, basically the size of a regular burger. Perfectly seasoned, perfectly cooked, and dressed to perfection...and for the price? Come on, it's cheaper than a Big Mac, and made with USDA Prime beef. Next, came the meatballs. Wow, I felt like a was sinking into deep marinara memories. How I've missed Italian food. But, I didn't realize HOW much I missed it until I visited Rizzutos. Oh, and I forgot to mention: the meatballs are the size of your head. We were stuffed from one slider and one meatball, but probably shared about a pound of beef between the two of us :O. 

I haven't tried their desserts, but I will be back! I look forward to seeing how Rizzutos evolves, and I'll definitely be keeping an eye out for new additions on the cocktail menu.

Came in this morning to study & have a nice cup of coffee & a pastry. Ive been here many times last year to study & thought it was time to come back in. Unfortunately i was very disappointed with the poor service. 

While still getting set up at a table one woman with dark brown hair who worked there approached us & told us that we had to buy something & wanted to let us know before we got "too comfortable". 

We let her know that we definitely planned on buying something but needed more time to get set up. She then came back about 3 minutes later & told us to leave, while imitating us in a high pitched voice claiming we were were giving her sass answering her question earlier. 

Overall, this was a shocking and disappointing experience. However that was one experience from one employee which does not represent the entire business. Hopefully this is not a reoccurring experience for other guests.

Does it smell like smoke?  Yes.  
Do they charge for a membership for admission?  Yes.
Is it the only Casino in the area?  Yes.  
Have I won money here?  Yes.
Does the DJ turn it up on Saturday Nights?  Yes.
Do the waitresses wear skimpy outfits?  Yes.

Membership here is $20 for 3 months and you can bring a guest.  This is the only Casino I have been to that does this.  They have prizes (mostly horrible watches) you can win and lots of sweepstakes drawings.  They give you comp dollars that you can use at the restaurant.  The steak house wasn't that bad at all.  The Italian restaurant was closed when I went.  If you dine here they will give you free passes to the casino.  The cocktail waitresses do a pretty good job at serving you free drinks here.  Plenty of tables and slots to play.  $15 minimum bets on a busy Saturday night.  

It is something to do in the area and it will scratch that gambling itch you may have.  I wish they would do away with the smoking or have a better way to ventilate so it isn't so horrible.  Also the membership fee is a little tacky.

I came here for the grand opening with some friends.  We all had a great time sampling several of the beers, which were fairly reasonably priced (approximately $5-$7 per beer).  We all liked the beers we tried, especially the Eye for an Eye (imperial IPA), which clocked in at 10%+, but did not have the strong alcohol taste of many of its higher ABV relatives.  On the other end of the spectrum, we all also liked the Ghost Station, a raspberry Berlinerweisse, which was a perfect mix of sour, salty and sweet, with this style of beer quickly becoming my go-to summer session.  The space is nice.  It reminded me a bit of the decor in La Colombe's flagship.  All-in-all, the grand opening left me excited to see what Crime and Punishment will churn out.  I have yet to try the food, but I can see this brewpub becoming part of my bar rotation.

The space is huge and rustic.  All the beers I've tried thus far are awesome. Food menu more on the "bites" side, but nothing wrong with focusing on beer. Tried the camellia sinesis, and it is truly delicious. Tea flavor is very subtle. The Vietnamese coffee stout was also good, though a bit on the sweet side for me.  The lemon thyme saison tasted light and refreshing but still packed a punch.  The beer here was my favorite of three breweries I visited this weekend.

The menu is very vegetarian friendly.  This visit, I just went with the olives, but they were tasty and well seasoned.  Will report back on future food visits.  I cannot wait until spring when we can get those giant garage doors open for a fresh breeze.  

Entrance is on McKean, not Bancroft.

"You HAVE family in Santa Barbara that I don't know about?!"

My husband was shocked. 

That's how you keep it interesting and fresh! who says you stop discovering things about each other once you're married? ;-)

To be honest, I've been a bad cousin. No matter how many times we've gone down to SoCal, I've never really made it a point to connect with my long lost cousin. (it's been a decade!) 

Fast forward to last weekend when he recommended Los Agaves. We arrived first with my parents and were welcomed with a very PACKED and noisy Saturday night atmosphere. It was self explanatory: fall in line, order at the counter, grab your utensils and sit yourself at a free table. We needed assistance since there were 6 of us.

We only waited a short while until they showed up and it was quite the reunion! We kept ourselves busy while waiting for our food, stuffing our faces with the fresh made chips and varieties of salsa. You're a spice wuss? good luck. Even the most "mild" salsa has a pretty good kick to it. I'm def a wuss (wah, wah) but the green avocado salsa was thick and had a nice flavor to it, that I couldn't stop at just one chip!

Soon after, the real party came: massive steak burrito mojado ($10.95), several tacos del mar ($13.50) and grilled chicken fajitas ($16.25). I really loved the sweet mangoes that topped my fish tacos and that chipotle sauce worked its magic! All plates come with a nice heaping of Mexican rice and side salad. My mom and husband enjoyed their margaritas, but declared that the blood orange margarita had a better taste than the regular one. I was just jealous, since I couldn't partake because of lent :(

Los Agaves gave us a pleasant experience and definitely lived up to its reputation as an upscale Mexican restaurant. I love the generous portions too! I'm curious to try one of their Molcajetes next time I'm in Santa Barbara and I wouldn't let another 10 years pass by before I see my cousin again.

Fido has unfortunately evolved into the epitome of Nashville's lost heart and soul.

My experience tonight at Fido was so awful and disappointing I had to take it to Yelp. This is the first time I've ever written anything on Yelp but I am just so disgusted with what this place has become I had to let ya'll know. 

My friend from high school just moved back to town so we go to our old favorite spot to catch up. We've been going to Fido for 12 years. We have spent so many nights in there drinking black coffee and indulging on PC muffins, playing cards and talking with friends and strangers for hours. We would roll in hungover for breakfast and sweet potato fries and never have to wait for a table. The people who worked there were friendly. Strangers would share the long tables and leave friends. This has all changed and evolved into the pretentious, superficially trendy reality that Nashville has become. Tonight, we wait in a line stretched back to the bathrooms. A grilled ham and cheese is $10. A salmon bagel is $10. We laugh at how ridiculous it has become but just decide to do it for old time's sake. We are given a location tracker device to take to our table so they can find us with our food. OK.... My friend and I are catching up and getting super hungry. We both have worked in the service industry and are not ones to get riled up or impatient but our food is taking forever. 45 minutes later the guy who rings us up comes over to our table to tell my friend they are out of smoked salmon for our bagel. I was like you have got to be kidding me. He asks her what she wants instead without bringing her a menu. His attitude is completely unapologetic and like we are somehow inconveniencing him. After she asks for a menu and looks it over, obviously flustered as this was completely unexpected and 45 minutes too late, she just says to bring her the same bagel with no salmon on it. Not a choice I would have made but ok. I speak up and say that she should also get some of her money back because there is no way a person should have to pay $10 for a bagel with cream cheese, lettuce, and onion on it because the restaurant ran out of smoked salmon. Really, she should just be refunded because we have waited so long for our food and he is just coming over to tell us they don't have what she ordered. I am informed that is now how this works and that I should always expect to have to wait this long for my food because of the long lines and high volume of people at this restaurant. 

This was just too much for me. I was born and raised in Nashville, I've been coming to this place for over a decade, and some guy in a fedora and a bad attitude I've never seen before in my life is going to tell me what to expect coming to Fido. And is going to tell me that getting a refund on a bagel that is $10 because of the smoked salmon on it isn't possible because that's not how that works. Please, get over yourself. I can think of 30 places in Nashville better to eat than Fido, one of which is right next door: Jackson's. I am just appalled at how rude this guy was, how long it took to get a grilled cheese and bagel sandwich, and how it took 45 minutes to let us know they were out of salmon with no apology offered and a refund straight up refused. I will most certainly never support the joke of a place Fido has turned in to again and will say RIP to the Fido us Nashvillians knew and loved for years.  

Please don't come to Nashville and waste your time waiting and paying to eat at Fido. And please stop gentrifying our beloved city.

*5 star view and ambiance. The place is a great scene.

*4 star bartenders. They do a good job.

*2 star food. Over priced and very, very mediocre. 

*1 star for Stacy the hostess and her possie of roughneck co-hostesses and waiters, shaking paying customers down and asking them to move constantly.

A party of 10 of us nurses came here for a wedding celebration evening for a fellow nurse. We arrived at 7pm Friday night on memorial day weekend. The city was dead and Attico was busy, but not packed. We waited for 90 minutes to be accommodated with a table, meanwhile no less than 5-8 tables through the place were empty at ALL times. 

The hostess Stacy said she was holding tables open and empty for reservations 45-60 minutes in the future. We said we only planned to be there for about that long. We were bar hopping. She wouldn't accommodate us. We nicely asked another 2 times checking in to see if she would reconsider or if anyone had not shown after we realized how tables were remaining empty 20 and 30 minutes later. We said we wanted to buy a few rounds of champagne and a few apps. Nope. We said we were willing to be moved if that group got there in 45-60 minutes. Nope. She wouldn't budge and got even more short with us.

We decided to stay because we ran into other friends but for 90 minutes we had to STAND next to empty tables/couches (Stacy would sick her crew on us the moment anyone took a load off on the couch of any of these reserved tables telling us promptly to get up, "you cant sit there, a group is coming in 45 minutes." This is not an exaggeration. 

We were still waiting on the waiting list so we went and checked in every 10-15 minutes. After the 3rd check-in, Stacy FLIPPED OUT on us, screaming that we are "really rude to keep checking in when she told us she couldn't accommodate us and she doesn't appreciate being harassed". Yep. The hostess, whose job it is to speak to guests as they check in and inquire and wait for a table, said that doing her job meant she was being harassed. 

Three of us nurses stood there, 8:30pm on a Friday night, stark sober waiting to give her business our money, completely stunned at this woman. This is a new venue. This is how they're acting? We are all philly locals and work with 100 other women who all heard about the ridiculous treatment this new place is dishing out. She treated us this way after we had still decided not to leave despite how unaccommodating she was and that she rather tables stay empty for 45-90 minutes than take the money of 10 women standing there willing and ready to provide you business.

 The service here, clearly, is terrible. They truly know the meaning of not valuing customers or practicing customer service. 

Yeah Stacy, me thinks not.

This place is adorable. It's small with cutesy colored walls, & they've got all their cupcakes lined inside brightly lit armors. I was immediately attended to when I walked in the door with a menu & a smile. While I was eating a had a nice conversation with the owner & gave me a little back story on the place.

I had the Red Velvet cupcake and it was excellent! The cream cheese frosting on it is not to sweet which is perfect. For $3 you get a pretty large cupcake. I felt a bit in the spotlight since I decided to have a seat on the couch (which is actually only for waiting customs). I ate my cupcake in a matter of a minute.

Holy disappointment Batman! 
Do you like condescension and unprofessional behavior from hosts?
Do you like awkward tables?
Do you like having a group of 3 split between two small tables?
Do you like serving yourself?
Do you like being rushed?
Do you like being ignored by waitstaff?
Do you like under seasoned food?
Do you like over cooked dry fish?
Do you like staff taking chairs from your table mid meal without asking to accommodate another table?
Do you like a waitress waiting like a vulture for the check?

If you answered yes to any or all the questions above XIX is the place for you. 

To start off the host who greeted & sat us asked us if we wanted bottled water, sparkling water, or "Philly's best..."
Now this I would let slide if I were in a more casual place but I'm sorry that is obnoxious. But was only the beginning of the unprofessional behavior. So we are sat a two small tables in the corner that are oblong and so our party of three felt disconnected and basically eliminated conversation for one person, and we could not get any of the famed view of the city from there. 

The first course was an assortment of salads, cheeses, etc that we had to get from the center of the room ourselves. Fine, but at least toss the damn salads before putting them out. All the dressing and croutons and such were left hidden under the bare greens. 

So on to the second course. The only thing the kitchen had to cook and the waitstaff has to serve. Well the hosts brought out our entrees. Cleared my places and the places of the person across from me but neglected to clear the placed of our 3 party member exiled to the secondary table. She was left surrounded by dirty plates and had her entree given to her before she was done with her salad. I got he lamb & pasta dish. This consisted on about a teaspoon of ground unseasoned lamb, bland pasta, and a "sauce" that was more like broth that proceeded to splatter whenever I attempted to eat a noodle. There was also a sprinkling of some cheese like product that the menu claimed was ricotta. I have had better pasta made by 12 yr olds. The other two diners in my party ordered the fish of the day which was striped bass. It came out and instantly it was obvious that it was overcooked and dried out. I don't eat fish and I could tell that from across the table. The beans it was resting on were only half cooked and disgusting. Now keep in mind this is the only course that the kitchen had to prepare. The salad assortments and the dessert offerings were pre-made and out on the buffet in the middle of the room. How do you mess this up? You have one thing to do, you best do it well! To add to this we had just begun the desserts, after waiting for the waitress who was doing nothing more than refilling drinks to wander by and clear plates, and she slapped the check down already. Then one of the other staff comes and steals a chair from the second table. Now it wasn't be used and we were on the final leg of the meal but seriously ASK IF IT IS OK TO TAKE JUST DON'T FERRET IT AWAY! Not like you are disregarding our existence or anything. Then our waitress came back to stand behind the person across from me like a vulture waiting for the credit card to run the check. We felt extremely rushed and poorly treated, and from the looks on the faces of the other diners we were not the only ones.

Perhaps I need the point of Restaurant Week reexplained to me. My understanding was that it was a way for restaurants to draw by offering a cheap set menu to get in new clientele because their bottom lines are hurting. With that said I understand that for the cheaper price tag you are going to get cheaper items but shouldn't those items still be prepared well since you are trying to entice repeat customers. Meaning that you want them to considering coming back and ordering off your regular menu? As of right now I see no reason to ever go back to XIX.

You don't come here for health food. You come here because it is good diner food that makes you reminisce about breakfast as a kid. I personally love the sausage gravy and biscuits. Get the home fries as a side along with an order of kielbasa and you are set. 

Couple of notes - you are not charged for refills on coffee, but you will be charged for refills of all juices and iced tea. They are only open from 6am-2pm everyday. So getting there if you work a 9-5 job may be tricky. Also the parking lot behind the building is mainly for the staff. I got yelled at trying to park there but the metered street parking is cheap. You get an hour for a quarter. So all is good.

Yes you too for only $6+ can construct a giant burrito  with your choice of fixin's. Once said burrito of massive proportions is handed off to you, you may then adorn it with one of their many hot sauces or just dive right in. When you get about 1/2 way through you will be super stuffed and question your addition of so many goodies as the last 1/2 stairs back up at you.

Good stuff.

When going here be ready to unleash your inner carnivore. Vegetarians beware! Especially if you are sensitive to seeing large pieces of often rare meat on skewers. 

 The waiter service was excellent. Our waiter was very friendly & well spoken, our glasses were never more than half empty for over 30 seconds and he exchanged any plates which became too messy. The meats were all well cooked (depending on how you like your meat cooked but they are more then happy to bring you any type or prep of meat you wanted.) The fillet mignon was wonderful, by far the favorite of our group. I was impressed with the quality of the salad bar as well. The presentation is nice and it was constantly being restocked with fresh ingredients. 

One small complaint on the decor though. The decor is beautiful with impressive walls full of wine. However the ceilings are very high, while this gives the restaurant a great look it allows all the noise of all the diners to echo around the room and compound the noise level, killing any ambiance. 

My only other gripe is the price tag, but then I guess the bite to the wallet is a good deterrent from visiting the place too often. Dining like this is one of the many things that makes me wish I lived downtown.

Ok, maybe I am just not getting it. The food was mediocre. The decor was nil. Our server seemed incredibly distracted. I will give them one star for trying to and having a different menu then the typical Mexican place. But there were two incidents that will make me never go back. 
1 - our server picked up the dirty, dripping wet, front door mat, took it outside, beat against the railing and then brought it back inside and laid it back down into the same dirty puddle it was originally in. She then went back to serving food and working in the kitchen without washing her hands. Check please!
2 - server number two picking up trash & trash can in bathroom and once again returning to serving food without washing hands. 
I will admit I am a bit of a clean freak but seriously this was gross. 

So in short my first visit shall also be my last.

I'm not a beer lover. I'm not a fan of hops. With that in mind I still try beers to see if maybe it is just never had one I like since there is such a huge variety. I found one that while it would never been my go to drink given other options I was able to drink. That is huge praise from me! (please no hate mail!) They also serve a couple of wines so there is something for non-beer drinkers. I had the Chardonnay and it was crisp and light. The service was good. The food came out super fast (the kitchen must be a well-oiled machine), and we rarely had to wait to order new beers or get water refills. Our waitress also was awesome enough to split the check for us without us warning her up front. If I lived closer this would definitely be on my short list of places to go to but I will keep it in mind for places to hit up again when back in the area.

What can I say about Zaika that others have not already said in great detail? Not much. Mohammad is the best Indo-Pak chef in the area. We have literally stalked him. Following him from Malik's to Best Taste of Asia and now to his own place Zaika. The food is always fresh and flavorful. The naan is a great balance between chewy and crisp with a light sweetness. My personal favorites are the palak paneer, and the chicken tikka marsala. But we have systematically ordered almost every dish on the extensive menu and have yet to really hate or even have a strong dislike of anything. The place has converted a bit to also be a mini mark selling pre-made food items and spices. I think he might be selling cuts of meat as well. Seriously I order from here almost every week I love it that much.

Try the redskin potato pizza-so different! This was an amazing pizza.  Very unique combinations for others too.  The greek salad is great too.  My husband was very skeptical of this pizza but couldn't stop raving about it.

This is the best Vietnamese restaurant I have been to in the USA. 

So if you are in Tucson, make sure you make your way out here and give this place a try. You will not be disappointed. 

The restaurant is located adjacent to the Lee Lee Oriental Supermarket (which is also fantastic and better than any Asian supermarkets in NYC). 

There are ample selections for vegetarians, so if you're an herbivore, this place will satisfy your veggie wet dreams. 

I've been battling a stubborn bronchitis for many days now and all my deplorable body wants is soup. I was worried that this place wasn't going to have a veggie based soup as most Vietnamese places only serve up beef/chicken based pho. 

To my pleasant surprise, this place offers a veggie based broth and you can choose either rice noodle or egg noodle for it. I do eat seafood on occasion to supplement my protein needs as I sometimes slack off with my tofu and bean intake. I asked for shrimp, tilapia and squid to be added. 

I was preparing for a bland soup with no flavor (as NYC had trained me so well to believe), but with the first sip, my taste buds woke up in sheer delight! The soup was so flavorful that I actually thought the chef screwed up my order. But sure enough, it was a veggie-based soup! Wowsers!

This place is very reasonably priced (average $10/dish), has a large dining area, efficient and quick staff and excellent authentic Vietnamese food. I highly recommend this place when in Tucson.

Saturday morning at Mazzaro's. Miracle  or luck? Found a  parking spot right away,  must have hit between rushes...bread/pastry line quick , even deli line short. Total spent within budget. Love & enjoy everything about this market except the distance from my house. So we don't go often enough. Food terrific,stocked up on some  prepared dishes,  cheeses, meats breads, and  of course,  desserts. No line even at checkout. Our lucky visit. A MUST SEE  and shop market. As we left about 11:15am place was getting crowded.  Advice: go early on Saturday .

My quest for the best cheesesteak is officially over now. This place here is hell!! The meat they put on your cheesesteak is outrageous!! I needed a fork to help me eat it. The flavor was there and everything is on point. 

I've found out something. North Philly and South Philly has a different variation. South Philly is on the cheez whiz kick and North Philly isn't on that as they like to give you the choice of real cheese on your sandwich. I'll head back over here before I leave to go back home. After eating this, I don't even want anybody else's cheesesteak, REAL TALK!!! This is MY SPOT now!!!

I'm really laughing at some of these four and five star reviews. Look, I am going to give you guys the real tea. This place is absolutely trash. Its not because it's a bad looking hotel- it's because of some of the people that are employed here and their horrible service. It's a shame because the hotel is actually really cute with swanky decor-also it is in a prime location. Only a few blocks from the French Quarter and not too far by car from the convention center. However that's all this hotel has going on for them. 

Strike one was valet. We pulled up expecting for valet to help us with our luggage. We actually waited in our car a few minutes to see if he would approach us-but to no avail. He didn't even try to help us until I went in the hotel to get the cart and began loading our luggage myself. 

Strike two was the incredibly rude display of ignorance that the concierge extended to us. Upon walking out of the lobby minding our own business- he yelled out verbatim "Y'all been here all day and y'all can't smile!". I was totally floored. First of all I shouldn't have to pay to stay somewhere to be harassed. I get that for free out in public. Second, whatever happened to professionalism and being a gentleman. I proceed to tell him off for his audacity to tell women he doesn't know to "smile" for him. This ignorant amoeba follows us outside trying to make us feel bad because I put him in his place. It was an incredulous experience to say the least. I can't believe a hotel concierge would be as ghetto and ignorant as what was displayed that day. He was arguing with me because I wouldn't allow him to disrespect us. What a tool. When the idiot finally stopped harassing us we again waited for valet to acknowledge us. This time it was about six men 
Standing around the podium doing nothing and wasting space. We spotted our truck and proceed to our vehicle. Our truck was the only vehicle there-one of guys finally comes to give us our keys. Why didn't you give us our keys when we came outside when the concierge was harassing us? Incompetent. So incompetent. 

Strike three was front desk telling us when we were trying to check out to come down and get a cart ourselves because they are "busy". You can't make this stuff up. That's the attitude that most of the employees had the entire weekend we stayed. It's like they didn't want to help us and when they did help it was done with a begrudging spirit. I literally ran into only three employees that were kind and professional. That's shameful since we stayed for four days. 

This place doesn't have a pool. Instead they have a top floor lounge that I heard is pretty nice but I wouldn't know because I refused to give this hotel anymore money other than the rate for our room. They also have a restaurant but again I didn't patronize because of reasons aforementioned. They have a pretty descent fitness room. Rooms are small. Even the lobby area is cramped. 

When you find yourself in New Orleans, please-for your sanity stay someplace else.

Come on, Mother's! Yassss hunty. This place is so good! My first time here was my most recent time in New Orleans. It's mad small so we made our selections to go. It was a long line of customers waiting to get their hands on the good food here so that should give you an idea how popular this place is. The people that work here are straight to the point. Don't expect syrupy sweet politeness. But hey, the amount of people in this small establishment probably wouldn't make me extra friendly either.

I ordered a po' boy, red beans and rice. Fried fish. Everything was good!

Modern menu and rustic in the upcoming and surging Warehouse District of New Orleans.  Very clean, charming, and even could be romantic, but perfect for a vendor partner dinner.

1.  Oysters & Angel Hair Pasta [$15.00, 4.0 stars] -- the fried oysters were fantastic, the sauce good -- grilled wild mushrooms in a parmesan black pepper cream, but the fresh pasta was not enjoyable -- al dente, almost crunchy, not so much.

2.  Pork Belly Appetizer [$15.00, 3.5 stars] -- huge portion, but overcooked.  It was all meat, like a pork chop.

3.  Tomahawk Pork Chop [$32.00, 5.0 stars] -- speaking of, quite possibly the best I've ever had.  Double-Cut Cheshire Pork Chop, HUGE and perfectly cooked, in a sauce, sugarcane Creole Glaze, that I'd like to bathe in.

4.  Bread Pudding [$10.00, 5.0 stars] -- wonderful finish to a phenomenal dinner.  Great.

Service was fantastic.  Our waiter was totally pro, knew the menu, gave suggestions, and was very attentive.  Someone at my table had a food allergy, and when her dish was brought out with the item she asked to leave out, he came out and apologized, and agreed to make the item again in jiffy.  He brought it out, and made sure she was okay with it.

Overall, a 5.0 star experience.

Butcher and Singer has steaks, fine wine, and cocktails.  An old bank building gone modern -- it's sexy, even swanky.  Equally perfect for a romantic date or business group dinner.  It has a great vibe.

I loved my Delmonico steak [$49, 5.0 stars] -- 18 oz of meat, about 3 oz too much...but flavorful and seasoned perfectly.  BTW, my understanding is that a Delmonico is a boneless rib-eye.  Sides my party of 5 shared: Mashed Potatoes [$11, 4.0 stars], Creamed Spinach [$12, 4.0 stars], Mushrooms & Onions [$12, 4.5 stars], and Bacon Macaroni & Cheese [$15, 4.0 stars].

But, who are we kidding.  It's all about the rolls.  Yes, ROLLS.  They make all other things served an excuse just to get them.  Served with honey butter -- whoa!  Think Pillsbury rolls with all the mini-layers, but these are the real thing, fresh, and warm. I'd give'em a 10.0 star.  Yes, I had 2 of them...and I would've eaten more if I knew, for sure, I wouldn't be judged.  Plus, my gf could be reading this review, and she'll give me crap!

Our server was a total pro, knowledgeable, friendly, and funny.  The food, along with the service, was total first class.

It's a one of a kind experience.  A sandbox for the kiddies, very large outdoor area with casual picnic and regular tables.  Issues: Not enough table umbrellas on a hot day, no dogs allowed (really?), and it's on the beach, but has bushes so tall you can't really see the sand.  For sunsets, for sure, yes.

Get in line.  Counter ordering, not full-service, is what causes the long line to be formed.  Allow 30 mins to get thru it.  The menu has a mix of fast foods, sandwiches, salads, and on Sunday - BBQ (I think 11a-3p).

I got an order of the Shrimp Tacos ($9.95) -- grilled tequila-lime shrimp, shredded cabbage, tomato, avocado, cilantro cream sauce, handmade corn tortillas, chips, pico de gallo.  The chips were the best thing on the plate.  The shrimp was just okay (costco?), but mainly the problem was it swimming in the cream sauce.  No bueno.  (2.5 stars)

My gf ordered the Beach Club Sandwich ($7.50), and had to send it back...so darn greasy.  She got a salad instead, and it was the wrong one and way too simple at that.  Not worth getting back to the counter and waiting again, so she ate it like a good sport.  Again, no service so you are forced to do it yourself.

If you have small kids and need a break from it all, this is your place.  Overall, I wouldn't come here for the food, or the live band (ma & pa band doing 1970's covers).

I finally went.  Finally!  After hearing from Sayeh Z for many years "the nachos...the NACHOS", well, she finally took me along and PAID.  Sweet!

Inside, it's not what I thought.  It's plain and boring.  It is the original Freebirds, so they have that going for them.  And, they are still standing.  Many (actually most) of the chain has closed, and we're also decked out with Rock & Roll and motorcycles and featured godzilla-sized burritos.  This is like Chipotle with no branding.  Note: the godzilla-sized was no joke, they offered 4-5 sizes, and this one once lasted me 4 days.

The nachos with the build-your-own concept was quite exceptional and large.  Two much for 1 person.  Delicious.  $13.25 + $2.75 for a side of quac.

Yes.  Do it.

I came here for lunch with a few vendor partners.  Wow.  It's a busy SOB, and it feels special, definitely like your in the place to be.  Counter seating may be quicker, but we waited for a table.

Along with the daily special "Nashville Catfish", the menu has some cool things: Banana Pudding Stuffed French toast, 'Goo Goo' Cluster Pancake, BBQ Shrimp & Grits, Eggs Cochon, Shrimp Boogaloo Benedict, Corned Beef Bennie, Bananas Foster Pain Perdu French Toast, Bacon Praline Pancakes, and a slew of burgers, sandwiches, and omelets.

I went with Croque Madame [$12.00, 4.0 stars].  Described on the menu as "Coffee-glazed ham & swiss served on brioche bread, topped with Mornay sauce & a fried egg".  The ham was a-m-a-z-i-n-g, but the bread was way too thick, extreme excess.  I ate a few bites, then picked out the ham & cheese, and ate the egg.  Served with french fries that were very much like McD's.

Overall: This feels like the south, and it's great for that.  Big food at moderate prices.  Our server was great.

I'd like to love, but not as lucky as the llama.  I found it cold, in both temp and service.  Located in the center of a very cute and charming Carpinteria, it's lovely to find a non-chain coffee house, and this one is very charming despite. 

The coffee, however, is great.  They serve coffee by Castle Coffee Roasters.  Not bitter, not overly dark, not burnt -- in fact, just right.  You can buy by the pound, too, and besides the standards Columbia, Ethiopia, Papua New Guinea, they have Zip Zinger (Dark Chocolate, Stone Fruit, and Caramels), SantaRossa (Chocolate and Cinnamon), and Holiday Blends for a little of something different.

It's quite fantastic to have all the stadiums and arenas in one spot.  To have shared parking lots makes a lot of sense, and a central place to have multiple bars and restaurants proved to be a lot of fun.  Last week on Monday night, I went to Xfinity Live before the MNF game between the Eagles and Redskins.

They charged a $10 cover, but that's cool.  Surrounded by the Miller Lite stage with live band and outdoor bars, then inside, numerous restaurants, bars, and fast food eateries, all-the-while, TV's with sports everywhere.  Because it's open and all connected, it has the feel of a party.

My co-workers and I had a blast, and it was a great way to spend a couple of hours before the game.

Located downtown towards the upped end on State Street.  However, welcome to Turkey!  An absolutely stunning place, Lokum offers all kinds of goodies and lovely things.

They are very generous with samples of all -- everything from baklava, Turkish delight, halvah, kunefe, katmer, rice pudding, Turkish coffee, and tea.

So, go already.

Cute as a button little coffeehouse: 1/2 little store, 1/2 little cafe.  A few spots to sit inside, a few out.  Mostly, a "to go" place.

I had an incredibly sounding "Brown sugar latte", and yes, it was all that [lg $4.75, 5.0 stars].

Minimally friendly barista drops this down to a 4.0 star.  Still, it's a definite stop to/fro Santa Barbara.

#29 on Eater Philadelphia's 38 Essential Restaurants inspired my co-worker Mike to choose this place over all others (yes, I'm naming him because he gave me crap that I referred to him as "co-workers" on another recent review.  Done, their ya go Mike!).  I obliged, of course.

This is no ordinary Jewish deli.  Dark and kinda sexy, it's like a cool bar with appeal and a deli with abnormality.  That is -- the food is kicked the normal into high gear (with high prices at that).  Server James set us straight with wit and professional moxie to give clarity to hard-to-figure-out menu.  Mike and I along with Bethany -- all of us are bright but struggled mightily.

We went for the $72/pp "Montreal Style Smoked Short Ribs" [5.0 stars].  Served with deliciously 3" round housemade rye bread, pickles, and various mustards.  It was absolutely amazing, but not short ribs.  It was sliced up and had more similarity to traditional Montreal smoked meat (although, it was served atop a large bone).  It also came with a choice of 3 of their 5 sides.  We chose chicken liver mouse [4.5 stars], potato latke [4.5 stars], and borscht tartare [4.0 stars].

Additionally, we ordered the hanger steak [$18, 4.5 stars].  Delicious, cooked to perfection, and lots of seasoning.

I loved the experience, but I love traditional deli, too -- I'm so confused.  Still, I whistled, hopped, and skipped all the way to my hotel.  Why 4.0 stars and not 5.0?  I wouldn't rush back.  Small menu, I felt like I tried most of it, and it's too pricey to go back to often.

* More on server James: the best waiter I've had in a long time.

Great bruch location, if you don't mind the exessive wait! The food was really good so when we left we knew why it took so long. They take your number at the hostess stand, our wait ended up being about an hour and forty-five minutes. Luckily it is in a really nice area with numerous shops and places to shop while you wait. We ended up having to wait until about 2p until we got a text. The do have a large to-go ordering section for bakery items, coffee and ice cream if you are not wanting to wait around. The place was very large with lots of indoor seating, large bar and a covered patio area with heaters and fans for the weather. The decor was very cute and they have items and cookbooks for sale. 

We ended up being seated on the outdoor patio and even though it was hot we were comfortable because of the fans. Our waitress was very sweet and knew the menu. I ordered a bloody mary to start with and my friend ordered a vodka and grapefruit, both with Titos. Our drinks came out very fast and were really good. For me it was a choice between the bacon, egg and cheese biscuit or the avocado toast. I went with the egg buscuit on sourdough as the bread. It was really good. My friend loved her food and looking around everyone seemed to be very happy with their meals. 

If we came back to this location it would probably be just to get something to-go. The food was good but there were other brunch places that were good, it's just too long of a wait.

No matter what you're craving, and honestly, no matter how late you're hungry (up to 3am, that is), Pizzava has your mIdtown Reno pizza habit covered!  From your basic cheese, to their cheeseahokic and then all amazing creations in between, you will find everything you want and more!  Calzones are huge!  Really huge!  Pizza is up to an enormous 16" XL SIZED masterpiece 

If the fresh flavors don't grab you, the CRUST... OMG THE CRUST certainly will!  And spare no air bubbles in their crust because if you're lucky to have them, there's joy in those air pockets that you have to experience.  

Pizzava - the pizza of pizzas!

Another win!

They say a first-time experience can make or break your perception.  Trying new foods and places is no stranger to a Yelper, but given our need to support everyone we can right now, this was a push outside the normal box and try out these guys via GrubHub!  What a great choice!

The fish was sushi grade perfection!  Veggies fresh and colorful. Sauces, not overwhelming and put it all together. And the presentation makes you snap a picture and remember it in your mind as you mix and devour the dish as a combined work of art. 

Absolutely fantastic and I cannot wait time try other combinations and maybe even embark on the larger bowl although the regular bowl is more than enough for most appetites.

If could give less than 1 star I would. So I called ahead a week in advance to ask if they were accepting larger parties as I was getting married and staying at the Cambria Hotel and wanted to bring my bridal party for drinks the night before the wedding. Whoever I spoke to must have been new or did not understand because when I asked if they were accepting parties of 8, I was told that would be fine-they could seat us in the lounge area and any additional  people were free to stand at the bar for drinks. So I made the reservation for 8 people at 7:30PM. At 7:30PM I am waiting downstairs in the lobby, not allowed to go up, even though I have a reservation. I ask if any of my party has arrived, they say no. Me and 1 other member of my party are not allowed upstairs until 8:15- 45 minutes I had to wait even though I had a reservation! Once I'm upstairs I see that 2 people from my party are already there! When I get settled and ready to order a drink I'm approached by the manager Stacey saying I'm not allowed to have 8 people in my party (even tho they allowed the reservation) and that they could possibly squeeze two extra chairs in (at this point there are 4 guests). I tell her there are 4 people waiting downstairs who are not being let up and she says that there's nothing they can do and that they have other reservations coming in. I wasn't even able to get my entire party of 8 seated! The rest of my guests were left in the lobby!!! I was thoroughly disappointed. If the reservations are only for 6 then they need to communicate with each other before booking larger parties. When I tried to talk to Stacey to see if anything could be done because I still had guests downstairs she was beyond rude telling me that nothing could be done. I asked if they could come up and stand at the bar, she said no. No apology, no attempt at a solution. I get it was a busy Saturday night and she was probably flustered already with the volume of people, but I was expecting better customer service from the manager. So we decided to leave, I didn't even get to order a drink, after 45 minutes of waiting! The best part was when we left the elevator "security guard"  told us to NEVER COME BACK. As if we started a bar fight or did something ridiculous! What was supposed to be a relaxing and fun night before my wedding day turned out to be a complete disaster. The management is terrible, if you have an event or a larger party, take your business elsewhere. Unfortunately my best friend who is an event planner in the city recommended this place. Her business will no longer be booking with ATTICO. DO NOT COME HERE.

WHATEVER, Chipotle. 

This place is so underrated and I cannot believe how many times I forget that. If you're looking for something quick, satisfying and delicious, this place is it. The fact that they use local meats and ingredients really sets this place apart. Don't even get me started on the fully stocked hot sauce shelf. Amen. 

This place saved my life the other day when I literally felt like I was going to pass out from the amount of 'Hangry' I was feeling. I had just left work, Green Hills was a nightmare and I couldn't even make it to Chipotle due to traffic. It was fate. I called ahead for an order for fish tacos and it was ready when I walked in 10-15 minutes later. IT'S A MIRACLE. Definitely flipped my hair a few times as I passed a Taco Bell on the way home. 

There are three fish tacos in an order and all three of them were amazing. The fish was not overly battered and added a delightful little crunch with the corn tortillas and cabbage inside. I've heard great things about their blackened salmon tacos and I cannot wait to try them next time I'm in...which might be in a couple of hours. 

Word of warning: when this place is busy, it's BUSY. Parking can be tricky but believe me, it's worth it.

ONE LOVE!  That seems to be their motto as seen in this Reno location.
Raising Cane's where I live in SoCal has lines and lines and I was never interested in the super long waits to check it out.  Inn Reno at 10:00AM it was just my hubby and I along with two other customers in the restaurant.

Our cashier was so enthusiastic and professional.  Yay for awesome service.
I'm not much of a chicken eater to begin with but, my curiosity had me ordering the kids meal with a few chicken fingers, fries, and a drink.  I like the Raising Cane's sauce, chicken fingers, and toast!  Fries are were ok.  My hubby also found both tasty as well.  The walls had the cool framed posters of Chuck Norris and Muhammad Ali.  Had to take pics of those.  

We will mostly likely not go to the SoCal ones with the super long lines and waits but, most definitely return to Raising Cane's if out of town at a not-so-busy location.  One love.

Woohoo, great experiences here!  First one was a to-go order of a garden omelette, breakfast muffin, decaf coffee, scrambled eggs, bacon, toast and a pineapple juice.  The wait for them was not long at all shortly over 10 mins.  The order taker and cashier were pleasant.  As for the breakfast itself, it was nicely packaged for me to take back to my room.  The portions were huge and all was tasty!  Even saved the muffin and toast for later.

We were here for dinner on a Monday night.  Milano is a open 24 hours and they were quite busy.  It's diner for comfort food kind of vibe.
