We were fortunate to get David from Sacramento, CA (their nametags say where they are from.)  Although the restaurant is very busy, our server was on top of his game!  He had everything down from attentiveness, recommendations, personality, and efficiency.  5 Stars on customer service.  

Our dinner was about a 3/3.5.  My husband had the 1/2 tuna sandwich, soup, and salad.
I had the special for 9.99 which was called the "adult grilled cheese sandwich" which had spinach and pepperocinis in them.  Kinda tasty.  Fries were nice and crunchy just as I like them.  We chose the cherry pie a la mode for dessert and that did not disappoint!  So delicious!


I'm sure we'll be back when visiting the Peppermill again.  Cheers!

The 3.5 stars rating for 472 reviews to date is about right.  I do like the vibe here.  Although Peppermill, categorizes Biscotti's as casual dining, it feels like a nice "date night" kind of place.  On a Saturday evening, our server was top notch.  Professional, kind and attentive.  Although my husband asked for his prime rib medium well, he received it medium rare.  He is more patient than I am so, he rolled with it.  Overall the prime rib was fine.  As for my garden melt, it was super tasty!  Spinach, tomatoes, avocado, mustard aioli, and jack cheese on sourdough, yum!  I got a taste of the watermelon salad and did not care for the herbs (oregano?) on it.  Chocolate gelato was much better though.

The next evening, we dined here on a Sunday afternoon.  Unfortunately, we had the most inattentive server.  He seemed like he was a nice person but, he was overwhelmed.  He explained that he was serving a large party in the back.  He kept apologizing for having us wait and for his lack of service to us.  He brought me hot water which was useless because he had neglected to bring the tea bag which I waited quite some time for.  Anyway, my fettucine alfredo was ok.  My husband waffled brioche grilled cheese and tomato bisque were good.  Since this visit, we dined elsewhere at the Peppermill which was even busier restaurants, yet we received better service.

Biscotti's was hit and miss for us.  Just 3 stars.  Thank you, friends and readers in yelpland for reading this.  Cheers!

The best meal I had in New Orleans hands down.

I couldn't stop talking about this place when I got back.

Let me say that the food here is FANTASTIC! Who knew that there was such a thing as chicken crackling covered fish. So not only do you get the crunchiness of fried chicken, but you get the health benefits of fish underneath! ****POOF**** My mind and taste buds were blown. It wasn't heavily battered, in fact it was so lightly coated that it looked like regular fish, but it tasted like chicken. It was delicious.

And one with more delicious food, let me say that the fresh lobster ravioli was worth the flight. I think it was something like $14 and man was it filled with fresh lobster in homemade ravioli. It was 5 stars all around.

Then we ordered another fish dish, this one was wrapped in seared scallops. Perfectly cooked and the sauce was delicious.

I topped off my dishes with 3 glasses of sweet freshly squeezed orange juice and man, was it a meal to remember.

 My hats off to you GW Fins! I shall return!

Cafe au lait with chicory, coffee and hot milk and beignets are the thing to get here.

The line stretches around the corner if you're waiting for a table, so you can always go through the faster togo line.

Here's the thing, I get people like their beignets but to me they are not out of this world delicious. 

They came with a whole pile of powdered sugar that you'll see dumped over all the chairs, tables, and floor. 

It's raining powdered sugar like it's free y'all!

Service is quick but unhappy. Even though we tipped well it was clear they just wanted us out for faster turnovers.

The beignet is hot, kind of dough tasting and the coffee has a bitter kick to it.

It was okay hence the 3 stars but it wasn't the best dessert or snack I've ever had and definitely was not worth the 40 minute wait.

Cortado was decent. 

This is a hole in the wall coffee shop, and though I enjoy supporting small businesses,  the coffee itself was just average, and I felt that they tailor to locals rather than tourists because although they were cordial with me they were very nice and accommodating to the locals that came in and explained in great derail the roast of the day and different flavors, whereas when I asked them about their local roasts they were quick to respond and didn't  give much detail.

Best cheesesteak per the locals word of mouth.

Long lines and the smell of grilled beef and cheese wafting in the air tell you that you're close.

Because you'll have to park a block away or you can be a jerk and double park and try to hit pedestrians like us that are crossing the street.

Super tender beef, great flavors, love the peppers.

Hands down one of the BEST cheesesteaks I've ever had.

Average chocolate macademian nut cookie and poor service even though I was the ONLY one in line make this 3 stars.

True story I broke off a piece of this cookie to try and found it too hard and too sugary for my taste that I gave it to the homeless woman outside who was asking for food.

This cookie was a no go in my book.

This is the competitor to Cafe Du Monde, and we'll, honestly between the two I kind of find them similar in that both of them were just 3 stars and didn't knock my socks off.

This place is less busy than it's well know counterpart, and the beignet was just okay. I wanted it hotter and I felt that the dough was a little soggy.

3 for average. Probably had been sitting there for awhile.

Maple bacon doughnut and their blueberry fritter will blow-your-mind!

I've never had a fritter that good or that fresh.

They were selling them as fast as they can make them. 20 minute wait for fresh ones since they sold out. Worth it though.

Excellent service by both women at the cashier. Friendly and gave us advice on what to order.

Coconut doughnut, chocolate doughnut, apple fritter, strawberry filled iced doughnut, we bought so many I lost count.

All were fluffy and fresh and delivered on the flavors that they promised. 

If I could wave a magic wand and transform every Dunkin doughnuts to Belier's I would.

Because this is what a crave worthy doughnut should taste like!

Average coffee at average prices.

They have a San Francisco blend and some special regional blends but unless you have somewhere to brew it you can only get their coffee of the day.

I asked if they could do a single French press and they looked at me like I was a snob.

The blend of the day was like a light water.

See picture of what it's supposed to be.

Tasted like a light french but it wasn't.

Nobody in line and five of us are waiting for our burgers.

There are 15 workers joking and laughing and saying "let me shake that for you" but not doing anything to really help the two cooks get the orders out.

15 minutes later there are still too many people on the register and in the kitchen not doing anything except chatting.

My burger was good though, that I can say, but they really need to work on getting those orders out instead of goofing around.

I love Xiandu Thai! It's very close to where I live and I've dined in as well as gotten take out from here multiple times. They always have seating, even on weekends, without a prior reservation. Ambiance is well-lit, quiet, and spacious. My favorite thing to order is the drunken noodles (pad kee mao) with chicken, less spicy (the regular dish is very spicy!) it runs about $12 plus change and is enough food for 3 meals for me! I also love their dumplings and side dishes. I come here every few months and a warm noodle dish is especially great now that the weather is getting cold. 5/5 for me!

A buffet is a buffet is a ...!

Look, when I was younger I ate like there was no end and that made any buffet a 5 Star eatery on my book! But now that I am older and counting calories, I just want one, I repeat one, full plate that I can finish and fully enjoy. Carvings Buffet did the job. They offer plenty of choices, the food is good and they are reasonably priced.

If you are staying at Harrah's, make sure to take advantage of the coupons that they hand out to you when you check in. You make get huge discounts if you are there   in mid-week.

Hungry? Come on in!

Hash House A Go Go has twelve or so locations around the country, but my experience is limited to this one locate in Harrah's. We were staying at Harrah's for three days and had one breakfast and one dinner here.

I am a big fan of big American breakfasts. You know what I am talking about; eggs, ham/sausages, home fries, toast and coffee! You'll fill up and won't have to worry about calories until dinner time!! Hash House A Go Go serves filling and tasty breakfasts

They do a fine job with their dinner items as well. We ordered a few small plates, all good. I liked my salad and pretty much everyone at our table was satisfied. My only suggestion to management, improve the service! I am not too tough on my servers as I was one during my college years and I know it is a tough job, but the service here could be improved. So a 4 Star for food, and a 3 star for service.

I still wear slip on Vans because even though Im fast approaching middle age; shoe tying is one of those things I never quite mastered...I biked up to Revolution wearing a wife beater, locked my bike to a pole and as I crossed the street heading into the restaurant I finally slipped on and buttoned my shirt, hoping the maitre de didnt catch that move through the window...what Im trying to say is I am not a man of class...but that has nothing to do with my desire to eat good food. I don't like white table cloths (can't keep them white) and waiters that call me sir, so I figured when I went to Revolution, I'd do it like I do everything, from a bar stool, so this review is just from a food point of view. And Revolution was really good.

Since it was my first trip and I was very curious, I made it simple: Gumbo, Shrimp and Grits, and the 'Coffee and Beignet's' dessert...thats a lot of cliche local food to slop up, and a fair way to judge. The cocktails looked awesome, I liked the setup and originality, but none looked like they would match what I was eating, so I skipped them.

The gumbo was something like 'gumbo to kill for' or 'gumbo to die for'; I can't remember the name, but there was a hint of a threat of death in the name. Turns out it was a quail who was stuffed with oysters and sausage (not a bad way to go). The gumbo broth they pored around it was awesome. Dark. Delicious. If I was in a date, I would have had no idea if I was to rip the quail apart or perform surgery with a spoon and knife. I had no one looking at me, so my solution was worse. As a low IQ eater, I may have needed instructions, but it was a great gumbo (there is no such thing a 'best' gumbo, that's a myth)

Shrimp and grits. The standard to compare for me. The shrimp was really good. Giant, cooked perfect (not always done with such large fellows) and again, the way the shells were flavored, I went mannerless again. Not enough grits, but Id say that even if the gave me a dumptruck full. Really good. Small for a main, which is good for me cause I needed to gorge on dessert. And it was a lunch course.

Cafe and beignets was all kinds of cool. I never met a pot de creme that i didnt love, the fruit syrup and fig jam and hot mini beignets were fun and delicious. They are not only open for lunch now, but 2:30-5 you can order $10-$15 sandwiches and pastas and pates and such from the bar...but i'll probably be a regular during those hours so i can work through the dessert list without emptying my wallet out on dinner. 

I didn't have the Revolution experience, but I spent $64 including tip on a memorable lunch. Easily worth it...

Ideally, New Orleans Yelp exists so visitors can find places like this. If I could grab random tourists (and lazy-butted local friends with cars for that matter) by their lapels and kidnap and drag them out to Chalmette to eat here, I would. Id never be prosecuted, my kidnapping victims would thank me...and even if they were still peeved, they'd be so stuffed that lifting the pen to file the police report would be too dificult. The perfect crime...and community service.

Rent a car. $25 at Enterprise, hidden spots abound on the outskirts of the city, and doing what you gotta to get to the places like R&Cs is worth it for all kinds of reasons, main reason, of course is to fill your gut beyond any normal boundaries. And juggle your calendar accordingly as to maximize eatingness pleasure, the journey is best made on Wednesdays or Fridays. Wednesday is brucciloni day. I don't want to digress into the theories and various spellings of brucciloni, that is best covered by Sara Roahens book Gumbo Tales (pretty much the must read book to grasp what and why to eat while here). Friday is crabcake day! Hooray! Rocky and Carlos crabcakes...darn, no adjectives, I wish it was Friday afternoon right now. Oh, jebus, they good.

Ordering is a bit confusing, everybody will know whats going on but you...I will share my little trick though- Just keep ordering, just say stuff, dont stop. You should over order, you are going to want them mac and cheese leftovers later. So knowing the portions are huge, and you will not be able to finish your food regardless, don't let that affect you, still order twice what you need.

Some sides that I never resist are the eggplant sticksand onion rings (only if you have an army with you, there is no small size for that, just a large...and large is really an understatement on that one.) But, most importantly, Rocky and Carlos has (by a smidge) the best Wop Salad in the area, and considering outside of New Orleans the word isn't really gracing menus too often, possibly makes it the best Wop salad in the world. Its just olive-licious, think a muffaletta for vegetarians, very classic NOLA Italian Creole cuisine.

And of course the Mac and Cheese. One of the best traditional Macs in New Orleans (3 muses, Cochon, and the Country Club roll modern style so different). Perfect noodles and it gives you a chance to toss around local nomenclature like red gravy. Red Gravy is New Orleanian for tomato sauce. Its fun to say, and traditionally served on the mac and cheese here, but I get it on the side so I can enjoy all worlds.

This is ridiculous, I'm getting a ride there tomorrow, I don't even know if I will make it until then, writing this has my mind stuck on those eggplant sticks.  Rocky and Carlos rules. Go. Ill try and make a list of places that make renting a car while visiting NOLA worthwhile and this is right on top.

I've been patiently waiting for Katie's to open!

I loved the ambiance: very modern, chic & rustic. Fresh roses dotted the bar & the stools were a wide variety of styles. Basically, it was exactly how I decorate at home, a mix of vintage & modern.

Service was good. The bartender introduced himself & attempted to initiate a conversation. I want feeling so hot, so I left him hanging a bit. In the end, we did have a nice chat about beers (my favorite subject).

Food was delicious. My fried artichoke salad came out of the kitchen quickly, with hot artichokes & fresh, cold greens. It also had some goat cheese, asparagus & pistachios.  I really, really enjoyed it BUT wish that there were a tad more greens. Sorry, ya'll but for my money I want a big ass salad. Maybe it's just the fatty in me. 

I think next time I will definitely split a salad and a pizza with a companion. I am really looking forward to returning, the area was so in need of a locally owned, quality drinking & dining establishment. Yay! Thanks for everything.

We just left the Kitchen Sink.... I hate to say it, but it went down the drain. Ha ha... But really.

The new space is nice, lots of light but the ambiance is totally lacking. There was a juke box, but since no one was requesting songs, there were several periods with no music whatsoever. There seemed to be something fun going on in the back room, TVs and laughter, but our area was boring (no TV, no music).

The server approached our table and said nothing, it was awkward. She was standoffish, offered no help with the menu & couldn't tell us what dressings were available for the salad. She did tell us that they were out of anything charbroiled... Disappointing because we wanted Oyster Rockafeller to start.

I am not sure how long the food took but the table next to us sat down after us, got their appetizer & entrees before we got any food. I ordered a salad but it came out with my entree, which honestly defeats the purpose for me. The only reason I order salads out is because I can't wait for something to cook!!

Finally, the menu boasted a gumbo full of chicken, craw fish, shrimp & sausage but none of the seafood was present. My cheese steak was served on burnt bread & the meat was over done/ dry. The salad was fine; iceburg, a few tomatoes & onions... Nothing special.

The worst part of the evening (besides not having a liquor license!) was when we told the server that we were disappointed with the food. She apologized & sent the manager over. The "manager" was wearing sweats & flip flops. He had an aggressive tone with us & basically said that the food was exactly how it should be. He offered to take off half of the cost of the entree at the end, but I didn't want anything for free, I wanted seafood! I wanted to be heard, and understood with empathy- even if it was fake.

I'm so disappointed. My husband had been telling me great things about the Kitchen Sink but I well never, ever return. What a shame.

Methinks we just had a bad night, a really bad night.

The boyfriend and I went to Sage earlier this summer for a romantic little dinner for two. The patio was lovely. Weather was ideal. Not a mosquito in sight!

We ordered cocktails. I was in the mood for a dirty, Grey Goose martini. The boy had a mixed drink... probably gin and tonic. His drink came out okay, my martini was green. I apologized to the server. I explained myself. I bartend. I drink, a lot. My martini really shouldn't be this salty or this shade. He apologized and took it back. After quite sometime (I am in the industry... I understand, shit happens) he came back and explained that the very last of the Grey Goose was used in my martini and asked if I would like another brand. Of course, I didn't care what liquor was used, but it dawned on me that the bartender was initially short on Grey Goose, and tried to cover it up with olive juice. Who does that?

Appetizers and side salads were delicious.

Entrees come out. I have pasta with blue cheese. It's rich and I love it. Boyfriend cuts in to his medium-rare steak to find it cooked medium- well.  We share my pasta while waiting for the server to check up on us.

He never returns.

When we're done eating and drinks are empty, here resurfaces our lovely waiter. We tell him about the steak and he apologizes and takes it away. 

The rest of the story IS NOT A JOKE. This really happened.

A minute later the chef comes out to our table, with the steak in a cardboard box, and asks us if we'd like to take the steak home. We tell him that we're not really interested in eating a medium-well done steak, and prefer it to be medium-rare to rare. It is at this point that he tell us that we are incorrect; the steak is medium-rare. Then he opens the box and shows us the steak, cut in half, grey in the middle. "See, it's definitely  pink." 

We say not a word. We couldn't. We were so dumbfounded. I suppose, since we're in our mid-20's, he thought he could pull a fast one. Or, maybe he thought we would believe him.... or maybe he was high on crack. I'm not sure. I will never forget this experience. EVER. Seriously, who does this guy think he's dealing with?

I'll go back someday, I suppose. But only if the chef is long gone. Or, if he writes me a formal letter apologizing for his shenanigans, which were all a terrible side effect of his medication that he is no longer taking.

Best American deli in the area. Simple, hearty food, done well. Menu is long, prices are cheap. Cute retro-ish style. Although they serve all the Americana staples and seem a grease joint (in the best way), they also have vegan and vegetarian options. 

And Mr. Lee is great.

STOP! Just pull over and go in! Seriously!

I had passed here a few times in the last couple weeks and hadn't stopped and today I decided to check it out and see what it was all about.

From the outside you start with a big funky mural and the mural artwork continues inside. The inside is sleek and modern with a couple booths and tables and at the far end of the room their own coffee roaster.

Before I could get 10 steps in the door someone was welcoming me and sharing their menu with me; he then gave me a couple minutes to soak it all in.

The menu shows you the options of how they are packaged: 3 pack $2.25 - 6 pack $4.50 - 16 pack $11.65 - 25 pack $18.15 - 35 pack $24.95.

Then they have a list of about 16 of their flavor creations OR you can create your own by picking a donut, icing, topping and drizzle... and to make it even harder they have a SECRET MENU. Which I'm sure won't stay a secret for very long.

And then they have a list of coffee drinks, they roast their own coffee on premise and its really nice, not bitter at all and has a robust flavor.

I went for the six pack (by the way the guy working there has a cute six pack shirt) and picked a few from the menu and a few suggestions. I ordered Honey Nut Crunch, Strawberry Cheese Cake, Cookie Dough, Sweet Pig, PB&J and Cannoli. AWESOME!

The Honey Nut Crunch had vanilla icing, Cinnamon Toast Crunch, cinnamon and a drizzle of honey. The Strawberry Cheese Cake had strawberry icing, piped cream cheese frosting and a sprinkle of graham cracker. The cookie dough (not the official name) was chocolate icing, cookie dough pieces and chocolate drizzle. PB&J was dipped in chopped peanuts and drizzled with jelly (they wrote PB&J in jelly). The Sweet Pig has maple icing and chopped bacon! The Cannoli had a ricotta cheese with chocolate chip filling, pieces of cannoli shell and sprinkled with powdered sugar.

Each one was better than the next and the best part was that since they are mini donuts you can eat six and not feel like you stuffed yourself.

From what I've seen they haven't been open very long, it's really fun as not only do they have really fun flavors but you get to watch as they assemble them. 

I'm betting this place is going to become really popular!

This spot is a hole in a wall joint with some high profile fans (like julia child's) and all for good reasons. I'm usually more of a flour tortilla girl but this place makes their corn tortilla fresh and it's the best I've had 

- La Supa-Rica Especial: roasted chile pasilla stuffed with plenty of cheese and adobodo (marinaded pork) and 3 corn tortilla at the bottom soaking up all the goodness. It's such a unique dish but seriously so good 
- Tamal de Venduras: their housemade veggie tamal  it's drenched in this beautiful cream sauce and it tastes like a comforting corn soup 
- Tacos: chorizo and adobado were good but the bistec was on the dry side

Overall a great meal but expect a wait since they make everything fresh. We came at 4pm on a Friday and there wasn't a line but still waited 30 min for food. Definitely worth it though

The food here is absolutely outstanding. I went with my boyfriend at the time and we got the chef's tasting menu. All of the food was so fresh and flavorful, and you could tell they really put a lot of effort into preparing it. The order of the food was also perfectly balanced by alternating richer dishes with lighter ones. The dishes we had, in order, were: 
1) boquerones (European anchovies) on crostini,
2) beet salad with apples, pistachios, and pickled vegetables
3) wagyu beef carpaccio with a taro chip and faux fish sauce
4) scallop crudo with carrot puree and yuzu sauce
5) snap peas with sesame seeds, duck fat sweet potato fries, croquettes, and red pepper remoulade
6) scallop risotto
7) sweetbreads
8) ahi tuna with arbol chile, avocado, pickled red onion, and taro chips
9) lamb shank with quinoa, apple chutney, and slaw
10) blueberry cheesecake with creme anglaise, caramel, and whipped cream with strawberries

Obviously the tasting menu is not going to be the same every time since they do use seasonal ingredients. The price is also a STEAL at $60 a person! You are not going to find a tasting menu of this quality at that price anywhere else in SB!

This is another one of those "Wait. Vegan? What?!" places that makes the carnivore in me spin around in circles. I love everything about the food here! It's a step up from Treehouse imo, in terms of both the flavor-explosion-in-my-mouth richness and the solid price points. I've yet to order a miss from here (but sadly can't say the same for Treehouse.)

Lulu's really experiments with food and makes it come alive with interesting textures. I got the banh mi bowl on my most recent visit, and was convinced the jackfruit was real pulled pork (YES, you read that right - JACKFRUIT!) I've also been trying to imitate the cauliflower bites at home, but still haven't been able to coat and fry mine up as crispy as the ones here. 

(I feel like this is less of a review, but rather a desperate request for Lulu's phenomenal secret recipes. Oops?!)

I can't recommend any particular dishes, because I've loved them all (yeah, it's pretty pathetic), so here's a list of everything just to make your mouth water: buffalo cauliflower bites (+ badass vegan ranch), tater tots, kale salad, sweet potato black bean burger, sweet potato falafel, power protein quinoa wrap, Thai crunch wrap, chipotle black bean burrito, banh mi bowl. 

Random notes
- easy street parking all along Grand (paid) and the side streets (free)
- great local beer selection (they've got tap options, cans, and bottles)
- food gets brought out to your table, but everything else (utensils, water cup) is self service 
- fast food prep, no matter if you're dining in or getting take out 
- the burritos are massive (see pic in comparison to my pen)
- love the outdoors patio seating.... Well, except for the bugs that adore my food just as much as I do :O

I got the Original Palestine shawarma per Yelp recs, and it did not disappoint. You can opt for chicken, beef, or a mix (my personal gluttonous choice.) The food came out surprisingly quickly (around 10 minutes for 2 Original Palestines.) The meat was sizzling hot from the grill, the tahini sauce and herbs were extremely flavorful, and the pita was filled to the max. No complaints here. This is officially my favorite food joint downtown now.

Update: came back again just for the pancakes and.... Yup, definitely the best in town. The compote served was noticeable less than last time though :(

I had the best brunch here. The double stacked pancakes were amazing! Each one was bigger than the size of my face, and the blueberry compote was excellent in flavoring - not too tart and not too sweet. My egg white omelette and potatoes were also done perfectly. The wedges were freshly fried up and crisped all over... just the way I like them.  My friend's shrimp and grits were apparently equally delicious. 

Everything else, from the layout and ambiance of the place to the rapid, friendly service gets 5 solid stars from me as well.

FYI: lots of street parking available everywhere

No pictures, because we snarfed up this pizza so dang fast.

This place has been on my list ever since I heard about its opening, and I was so happy when friends invited us to try it with them for a weeknight dinner. We arrived just in time to grab a table for four in the corner (one of the few smaller tables - though I certainly don't mind community seating if needed to get tasty food in my belly).

The interior is beautiful, simple, and inviting. I love that you can watch the chef work on the pizzas from pretty much anywhere is this (small) cozy space. 

The menu is simple and focused on quality over quantity - good ingredients, prepared well. The wine list and beer list is also small, but well-curated. I loved my rose!

The pizzas are big enough to be shared by two, or devoured by one hungry adult. I opted for the margherita and added prosciutto. The pizzas come out as they're ready, and mine was perfect. Delicious sauce, fresh basil, creamy cheese, and ultra-thin prosciutto, all on a chewy, thin, oven-baked crust. I somehow managed to control myself and only eat half, only because I wanted the leftovers for later!

Our server was friendly and funny, and the food and atmosphere was fabulous. This would be a great spot for a date, or an excellent place to take out-of-town guests for a quality meal that feels a little special (without being pretentious). Can't wait to go back!

Exo roast is LEGIT.

The warehouse-style building is trendy, open and relaxed - the first time I visited, I felt as though I was transported to Brooklyn or Chicago. Although it feels COOL to hang out here, it's not TOO cool - a welcoming and chill space to enjoy coffee, do some work, or meet friends.

Excellent options for coffee and food, including a spicy Chiltepin cold brew coffee, unlike anything I've ever tasted. Refreshing with a hint of spice at the end, and mixed with some cream, it even gives some chocolatey notes to the palate. 

Lots of interesting options to sample here, and of course, it all starts with a solidly roasted coffee bean. Food and bakery options abound, too - a little something for everyone.

I like hanging out here.

UPDATE (early 2017?):  Tacos saw another 25c increase to 2.99 each, but again, plenty of meat in each.

UPDATE (August 1, 2015):  Tacos saw a 25cent price increase (reflected below) ... but still overhwhelmingly worth it!
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I've only been here for lunch because it's not too far from work... wish I LIVED closer because this place is probably my favorite "dive" for authentic tacos.

I have tried their barbacoa, carne asada, carnitas, and el pastor tacos; and aslo their red chili entree.  All were very good, but the tacos were outstanding... and (now) only $2.75 each.

For every taco, the meats are grilled-to-order; they come piled high with LOTS of meat; guacamole, and pico de gallo (bascially a "dry" salsa comprised of chopped onions, tomatoes, cilantro and a few other things). All of this is included in the $2.75.  Their additional salsas (green, red, hot, mild) are also very good, but you won't need them because the taco is so good "as-is"!  Generally, 2-3 tacos will satisfy the average woman and 3-4 of these larger-than-average soft tacos will fill the average guy.

Ambiance is typical "dive" with very simple offerings for seating and tables.  The venue has approximately 7-8 tables indoors and 3-4 on the front patio.  Parking is ample/free in the form of a shared strip-mall lot that includes several other small eateries.

There are no "waiters" but the counter staff and chef have always been warm and friendly.  Drinks are fountain style (self-serve) and include one of my favorite guilty pleasures: apple soda.  They also have plain seltzer water from the fountain dispensers.  The salsa and fixings bar is readily self-serve with a fresh variety of sauces and pico de gallos.
I highly recommend this place.

Sadly Sports West has gone downhill and is in disrepair:

It's Just OK. Now I know why I got no enrollment fee and it's only 40 per month now, let me explain...

Honestly I'm staying a member simply because I live a few blocks away and one of my friends I grew up with is an incredible trainer there and it's only 40 bucks a month for me.

The men's locker room, showers, steam room, and dry sauna are super run down and deferred janitorial and maintenance seems to be the policy. The towels are super rough and like sandpaper. The Men's steam room has a broken door that is untrue to frame and the steam is out of order most of the time. The wood work in the dry sauna has got to be decades old, and is rotting and creaking and ready to break and hurt someone at any moment. The shower fixtures are unacceptable: some are only hot water, some are only cold, and most spray water in a way that is painful to the skin.

I have been a member (this time) for less than one month after being away for over 2 years, and I have to mention that nothing much has changed or improved over the years, in fact it's gotten worse. Some of the current staff, young kids, that run the front counter are rather brash or even rude in the morning, and don't make me feel welcome when I arrive. I even remember hearing one of them make a comment to his buddy that his meal time was being interrupted or something, and all I could observe is that this particular kid only wanted to chat with friends and eat. 

When I left that morning I had to wait around for several minutes to trade my locker key for my membership card and other members were also gathering around front counter looking for assistance as well before one of them yelled out. Then this male employee comes out with a mouthful of food and a bad attitude!  I'm like: your STILL eating? He looked at me like I just offered edification and said ALL I DO IS EAT! Then laughed it off like it was acceptable to be like that.

Some of the staff there are super unprofessional and some are just the opposite and very nice and friendly! So I'm not generalizing that the entire staff has a training issue, only most of them. So it's a like a dice roll or based on someone's mood that day. I'm considering getting a tour of Lakeridge Athletic Club, I hear it's super nice and I'd rather pay more and be happy than deal with a gym that won't repair or renovate or properly train their staff.

Thanks for considering my opinion and what is true for me.

Thanks for listening.

My son and I visited the much hyped Movie Tavern yesterday. We got there at 4:15 to buy tickets for a 4:30 show. I'm guessing we just beat the peak time (it was Friday) and wasn't crowded at all. The seats are great. My son was sold based on the seats alone. The show began promptly. I ordered a burger for me and kids meal chicken fingers for him. Both were ok.  (Definitely agree with the reviewer who described it as Applebee's-ish fare). Our waiter was efficient and friendly. The food arrived about 30 minutes into the show. Dessert came an hour in. I recommend ordering every course at one time. If movie tavern weren't so far it would be our new movie place. 4/5 for movie tavern. Go and see for yourself. It's worth it if only to experience the dinner and a movie combined phenomenon everyone is talking about.

My boyfriend wanted to take me to pod to celebrate my new job. He was pretty excited to go here since his coworkers have been heralding this place for months.  We arrived on Wednesday night and pod was pretty busy; we felt as if we'd traveled forward in time to this modern restaraunt. The hostesses greeted us and we were seated within 15 minutes of arrival. Our waiter was efficient. He was knowledgeable but curt; he had many tables but seemed to multi-task well. Our first course, the tempura sushi, was very good. We ordered macadamia chicken stir fry, which my boyfriend loved and garlic shrimp. I ordered the lemon cheesecake for dessert. It was simply divine. I recommend the pink martini although my boyfriend's Tokyo tea was just average. Overall I would return to pod. It would be cool to dine in one of the colored booths and sample more of the delicious items we saw at other tables and wizzing by in the hands of busy waiters. 4.5/5 for pod.

I'm giving el vez 3/5. I really wanted to like this place. I'd wanted to come here previously (this place was recommended by a coworker) but the 35-45 minutes wait always had me wandering to nearby spots for almost immediate seating and less hostess attitude. Due to the lack of a waiting area, you're forced to take a walk outside, which is annoying in the Winter months, or gather at the already crowded bar in the center of the dining room. So I made a 10pm reservation (the only one left) on a Friday night. Since we arrived at 9pm and I was quoted an hour wait anyway, I mentioned the 10pm reservation. Those must have been the magic words because the hostess was like "oh we can seat you now. " Huh? Ok. Anyway...at the waitress' recommendation we ordered the guacamole. It came with warm homemade chips and spicy house salsa. Both were good. We ordered shrimp and chicken tacos for two. Both were really good.  I thought the char flavor was a bit overwhelming but my dinner date was pleased. Margaritas were good. The restaurant has a laid back ambiance: think late 20 somethings gathering after work for celebrations in the booths etc so it was pretty loud. Not the ideal family or romantic spot. I probably wouldn't go here on a first date if you'd actually like to hear your date talking. Overall el vez was good just not good enough to go out of my way to return without a reservation or fight for a coveted center city parking space.

So we're back in Philly following my boyfriend's pre-birthday celebration in TX (home of some great restaurants) and I decided to make a reservation at R2L to make his "actually" birthday celebration just as special. I made a reservation last month and decided to call a few days before to make sure we got a window seat (as I had requested on the Open Table reservation). The hostess said she would try. Well, last night they delivered; we not only got a great window seat, we received complimentary champagne and a small dessert plate. So let me back up, we parked in the Liberty Place's parking lot (validated parking is $10 when you dine at R2L). We took the lone elevator to the 37th floor. We had to wait a few times because several people were going up at once. When we arrived the hostess took us to our seats. We had a stunning view of Center City. Our waiter greeted us with complimentary glasses of champagne and a lively "happy birthday" to my boyfriend. For starters we had the arugula flatbread. I enjoyed it although the center could have been crisper. My boyfriend ordered the seafood paella, which was huge. He had several large shrimp and lobster. We enjoyed it but thought it could use more seasoning. I ordered sides: potato skins, which were very salty and lobster mac and cheese, which was rich and delicious. We were too full to order dessert but the waiter brought out complimentary mini desserts for us to taste (and you guessed it, "happy birthday" was written on the plate). We had mini lemon sugar dipped squares (yummy) and small cakes. Overall R2L scores a solid 4.5/5. Service was impeccable and the view made up for any small food flaws. Food is a solid 4/5 for the price point, based on the large portions alone. R2L is worth a visit and offered the perfect romantic backdrop for me to surprise my boyfriend with his gift. Yeah, that was a moment :)

Against my better judgement, I visited Con Murphy's after reading Yelp reviews that consistently described the service and food as mediocre. Guess what? I received mediocre service and food. With such a great location, it's a shame that Con Murphy's doesn't deliver friendly and fast service. I was seated right away but my server was not very attentive or friendly. I ordered the cheesesteak, which was edible, but not one of the better restaurant variations I've had. I had to flag her down for more ketchup as she chatted with another server at the bar. The margarita was really good and only $5 due to their happy hour special. Another good thing, is that I got 15% off my meal for checking in on the Yelp app. Since I was dining alone, the view from Con Murphy's prime location at the corner of 17th & the Parkway made for great people watching. It's a shame that the view was the most exciting thing about my experience.

Ever spend 20 minutes waiting to get seated and then wait an hour for food that never makes it to the table? I have. What makes any backup in the kitchen worse is a terrible waitress. Our waitress never communicated that there was a backup in the kitchen. She could've come by to let us know and offer refills on coffee etc. We had to track down a manager to advise of the kitchen backup and even then she stated that our food had not even been cooked after an hour. Unacceptable! I cancelled the order so I can't even give a proper review of the food. What a way to ruin a Father's Day breakfast. Crossing Kitchen Bar off our restaurant list permanently.

I finally visited Alma de Cuba. I know, apparently I also finally crawled out from under the rock I'd been hiding under. My love and I made a 7pm reservation for Valentine's Day. We arrived a tad late due to snowmaggedon but the staff was accommodating and seated us right away. Our table was pretty congested on the second floor wedged between two other couples. Talk about awkward, praying my behind didn't slide across the neighboring table's ceviche as I headed to my seat. It was that tight. Now the tables on the third floor overlooking our area looked comfortable. In fact, I felt like the people sitting in those seats were giving us the "oooh we are so much more comfortable than you" stares. It was hard to hear anything the waiter said due to the close proximity to other shouting couples who were equally as frustrated trying to have lovey dovey conversations. On to the food: we ordered the appetizer sampler of FANTASTIC empanadas, bacon wrapped dates and tacos. My boyfriend had the Cuban shrimp and grits, which he thought would be spicier. The grits had a creamy almost mashed potato consistency but great flavor. I ordered the vaca frita which was tender and flavorful. My strawberry mojito was amazing but I wasn't a fan of the bitterness of the classic one he ordered. For dessert he ordered the chocolate cigar and I ordered the strawberry crepes. Both were ok. I thought the cigar would be sweeter and the crepes would be warmer. Overall a solid night with friendly service was had. I think I shouted "it was a solid night" to my boyfriend at some point near the end of the meal so that he could hear me. Happy belated Valentine's day :)

If I had one complaint about Crow and the Pitcher, and I don't since I found parking right in front of its doors, it would be the parking situation. But that's a center city problem. I had dinner with my former professor last night in celebration of my new job. The restaurant is small and cozy and would be a great date night spot or place to escape for a quiet drink or bite. I highly recommend the $11 cocktail, "the go getter." Check-in on Yelp and the cocktail is free with purchase. She and I ordered cheeseburgers. We did not try the cheese but yes they have a cheese cart as other reviewers mentioned. Let's just say the cheeseburger here is an elevated cheeseburger at $18 with bone marrow and it was delicious and perfectly cooked. The fries were really good but would've been better if they were hot; mine came out lukewarm. From the time we walked in, service was attentive and friendly. There are three cool basement restrooms with chalkboards in them (this is cool, it only sounds strange lol). There's also a private dining area down there. If I'm in center city (and I'm bound to be) I'll definitely check out Crow and the Pitcher. This place is new and definitely worth a visit. It would also be an awesome venue for any small gathering or private dining experience.

I'm reviewing the Hilton's events department only. I've attended several events at the Hilton City Avenue including a wedding and a few banquets and have been satisfied on every occasion. Most recently I attended a conference, which spanned several days and required the Hilton to execute quick room setups, continental breakfast, a buffet lunch and an evening reception. Randy, from the events department, is magnificent. He really helped to seamlessly coordinate our needs. The food was delicious. Breakfast was an average continental but the buffet lunch (chicken marsala, salmon and eggplant parmesan) and evening reception stations were fantastic. The evening reception included pot sticker, pasta, fajita, carving and dessert stations, which were also fantastic and still a cut above standard hotel fare. Well done Hilton.

Night Kitchen was A OK.  I purchased a father's day carrot cake from the bakery last month.  It was small for its $28 price tag but pretty moist and good.  My son enjoyed his cupcake as well.  Both were not the best we've ever had but Night Kitchen earns the additional star because my parents are still raving about the cake. Service was nice enough; the young lady who helped me with the cake was friendly and the only one to greet us (there were 3 people at the counter).  Overall, I am unsure if we'll return, as there are other better (and cheaper) bakeries in the city.

We roamed in here after being quoted a 45 minute wait at a nearby restaurant and were glad we did. The hostess seated us in less than 5 minutes. The restaurant was bustling, which is always a good sign to me (never trust a skinny chef). Our waiter was great. He made recommendations and wasn't pushy at all. We were there for over 2 hours noshing and talking and he was unphased. We didn't get that "hurry and eat so I can turn over the table" vibe.  He refilled drinks and kept it casual. So the food: all of the food is served family style. We ordered lobster Mac n' cheese (think rice not noodles so more of a casserole in my mind), open faced shrimp quesadilla and the hummus. I was dining with a pesco vegetarian and he was pretty happy with the menu. Overall I'd return as we enjoyed the ambiance without a pretentious vibe. 4/5 for continental  midtown.

Does Fogo de Chao need a 646th review? Well of course it does, so here it is. We celebrated my fiancé's birthday here. This was our second visit and we had a plan. We ate light all day to prepare and I made a 5 p.m. reservation to give our stomach's time to digest all that goodness. As usual, service was seamless since it seems that all of the staff is there to serve you. Our sides were never empty. We (read: me) went through those caramelized bananas pretty quickly. The salad bar was constantly replenished. The filet mignon was the standout and we always correctly received our medium cut requests. I didn't try all of the meat this time because part of my plan was to save room for the favorites (check out their menu ahead of time if you've never been). Overall we enjoyed a lovely evening and a happy birthday was had; however, it's nice when restaurants acknowledge the birthday person in some way, especially when it's mentioned in the reservation, and Fogo didn't. My fiancé still likes Chima better for some reason but we enjoy Fogo all the same. It's an expensive night out but worth it for special food coma-worthy occasions.

Yet again I'm wondering if I visited the same place as everyone else. Insomnia was just okay to me. I've had better cookies. To be fair though, I didn't try all of the flavors. I ordered the following cookies: snickerdoodle, white chocolate and peanut butter something or other. My boyfriend was impressed with the peanut butter specialty cookie and its warmth. I dont know, for 2.50 each I was expecting that cookie to rock my world but nope, not even a tremor. Ah well 3/5 for imsomnia.

Sabrina's was a solid 3 stars for us. My son and I visited on this snowy morning and found parking around the corner from the restaurant quickly. The dining area was pretty full but we were seated right away. Our waitress didn't introduce herself, but was efficient and friendly. A table runner brought water to our table without us having to ask. I ordered the challah french toast and my son ordered a short stack. He and I agreed that we'd had better.  The bacon was a little burnt and the scrambled eggs were overcooked.  With so many yelp and word of mouth rave reviews I left wondering if we visited the same restaurant as everyone else. 3/5 for Sabrina's. Maybe we didn't order the right things....

In honor of the GNO (girls night out), mom and I checked out Ruth's Chris for the first time. It's prime location right next to the Merriam, where we were to see the musical Fela, was great. Valet parking was quick and offered a slight discount to self parking in the Bellevue's parking lot. We arrived about 5 minutes early for our 5:45 reservation, checked our coats and were seated promptly. Mom ordered the mardi gras cocktail and I ordered a berry concoction based on the waiter's recommendation. I liked the mardi gras cocktail best and wished I'd ordered it too (cocktail envy). And speaking of our waiter...his name was Chris and he was pretty darn good. He recommended the barbecue shrimp appetizer, which we really enjoyed (the garlic bread on the side was divine). Mom ordered the bone in ribeye since she likes her steaks well done and doesn't want to lose flavor in the process. I ordered the porterhouse (medium-more pink than red) and it was excellent. The steaks came out sizzling on the 500 degree plates and were cooked perfectly. Our waiter brought out a few sauces for us to try. I especially enjoyed the peppercorn sauce. We ordered asparagus and mashed potatoes to share (the portions were huge). The asparagus was a little undercooked for my liking and the potatoes were a bit dry. Finally we shared an apple tart. It was one of the best I've ever had. I needed coffee to stay awake after that meal so I ordered a cappuccino, which was divine. We left with enough leftovers for a few days and were off to the show. 4/5 for a pleasant Ruth's Chris experience. It's pricey but a GNO with mom is worth every penny.

This review will echo other reviews so... you've been warned. I came to Raw on a GNO with my friend. She's a vegetarian and recommended this place as a middle ground for us since I'm her carnivorous friend. We were seated quickly on a Sunday night. There were only about 3 other pairs in the place (I didn't see the outside dining area but I hear it's really nice). I really liked the modern feel to the restaurant. Our server greeted us right away. He didn't introduce himself or recommend any dishes in particular; however, he did inform us of the specialty sushi, but $19 for 8 pieces seemed a bit overpriced for my taste. So we ordered a la carte. She got the veggie sushi platter and said it was great. I got the beef negimaki and shrimp tempura sushi rolls (6). So good I ate it all and happily didn't have to share :) Our cocktails were also pretty good. 4/5 for Raw. Yeah it's pricey for sushi but really really good.

We visited ooka on a Thursday night after hearing rave reviews from coworkers. It was pretty busy due to the holiday. The restaurant's ambiance was beautiful without being too trendy for kids. We were seated at the cramped communal table. My son and I were there for hibachi; the waitress said that if we sat on the hibachi side we'd only be able to order sushi as an appetizer. The sushi ended up being the star of the show. Hibachi was good (think teppan edo at Disney World, Benihana or any local Hibachi chain). Soup and noodles were a nice touch. Overall, ooka wasn't memorable enough to end my loyalty to the Hibachi chain's before 6pm $15 and under specials as the food didn't stand out enough to warrant the expensive prices. Service was just good but not great.

Pretty good spot for a quick lunch, though I found the menu hard to navigate. I came for a standard gyro sandwich but was given the choice between multiple styles (brunch-style, philly, italian...among others) and multiple options for meat. (I highly doubt the street vendors of Greece offer all these choices). I chose the standard Greek style called "Athena," with lamb as the protein.

The staff was friendly, and after submitting my order and getting a number, I sat at a large, blue countertop that had an open-air view of the street (for that good people-watching on a busy Saturday).

My gyro was delicious and large. Good quality meat. Fries were great too. But for $10 for the sandwich ($13 for the combo with fries/drink) it seemed a little spendy - I can get the same thing in pricey CA for a few bucks less.  Still, I'd go here again to try more items.

After seeing the ridiculous line for Brophy Brothers we spotted Endless Summer Cafe next door in a sweet location just above the Maritime Museum. 

Hmmm, let's see: Should we stand around for an hour-and-a-half to visit a four-star seafood place? Or should we just go to ESBC for immediate service and a table overlooking the harbor? Easy decision.

The staff was friendly and happy to see us, and a popcorn machine was generating snackables while we waited for food. My fish tacos were good, not fantastic, but they hit the spot squarely. And my IPA was ice cold. 1.5 hours saved and hunger satisfied. I'd go back.

= Boise Beer Tour (self-guided) - Stop 3 =

After taking a break at my hotel and then walking some more along the river, I checked Yelp and decided to angle towards White Dog to grab some dinner and another brewski (or two). The place was quiet for a Friday, and I had no trouble finding a seat at the bar. The staff was relaxed, uber-friendly and answered all my questions. I finally opted for a 4-beer sampler and a Beer & Bacon Burger, the latter being prepared by a food truck in the adjacent alleyway.

The beers in my sampler were all delicious and well-crafted: I was the least excited with the hazy IPA (it's a beer fad I'm quickly getting burned-out on), but I loved the Scotch Ale, the 5-hop IPA and the English IPA.  When I discovered they had some of the English IPA on nitrogen, I decided to get a pint of that and stay a little longer. It was by far my best beer of the night. (I stopped by the following night to have another, but they were out of it...dang).

As for the food, my burger was absolutely phenomenal, cooked perfectly and with some kind of oniony bacon-jam. It came with excellent, thick-cut fries as well. A 5-star meal.

Cool feature: White Dog has a 5-inch wide, metal rail embedded in the bar that is held at icy temps so you can sit your beer on it, keeping it from getting too warm. I've never seen this before, but it worked well (and it also made a fun, mini snowscape).

In short, I loved White Dog. It was a another, great Boise brewery "find," and so I was surprised (and a little sad) the place was not busier. I understand they are still "newish," and so hopefully they will gain a larger following over time.

= Boise Beer Tour (self-guided) - Stop 4 =

On my second night in Boise I decided to finally check out Bittercreek for dinner. Based on the Yelp reviews, it appeared to be one of the more popular spots in town. I arrived at about 6 pm on a Saturday, and it was absolutely packed to the gills, both inside and on the front patio.  But one of the few perks of dining solo is flexibility; and so I was able to squeeze into one open spot at the bar.

The tenders seemed a little harried and annoyed at first, but became more friendly as I chatted with them and made it clear I wasn't in a hurry. My neighbors at the bar were also friendly (a common occurrence in this town).

A huge and excellent beer list here with a lot of variety; though I didn't take notes.  Over the course of dinner I opted for two local beers, a session IPA followed by a nice porter. Tenders seemed knowledgeable on the offerings and provided tastes on request.

As for the food:
-- Polenta fries: ($7.75) Carbolicious! Being a polenta-holic, I had to get these after I spying them on the menu; they did not disappoint. My plate consisted of over a half-dozen, very large "fries" stacked like (and the size of) Lincoln logs. So so good and surprisingly filling. (5*)

-- Smoked trout salad: ($13.50) With greens, cucumber, egg, onion, capers, fennel. Basically a big plate of umami goodness. So filling that I couldn't finish it (though I partly blame those fries). The only downside was the salt level seemed high (4*)

I can't say I loved the extremely crowded, loud environment here, but I thoroughly enjoyed Bittercreek's offerings; and my visit raised some intriguing questions, such as:
-- What is the origin of their historic-looking building?  ..plus...
-- Why is there a full-sized statue of a tiger behind the bar? (perhaps an example of the famous Idaho tigers I've heard so much about?)

I hope I get the chance to come back again (maybe at a quieter time) to get some answers to these and other questions. Until then.

I hardly EVER write reviews, but I will take the time, sitting in my car, outside of Elsie's, to say this place is HORRIBLE!!!!! I work in a bar and I know when a bar is busy. pfffft, this place was practically dead; in yet, I (and this dude) stood at the bar for 15 plus mins, talking to other patrons, having any attempts of eye contact avoided (and when made just blatantly ignored). so I switched where I was standing 2 times to get Any bartenders attention; and I watched multiple people walk up to the bar, stand there 2 seconds and get served drinks. 

when I finally decide to say something (because the couple I'm talking to is saying how rude everyone has been to them and that I won't get any attention), I say "hey! you think it's about time we can get a drink? been here for over 15 mins." and pretentious beardo replies with "I'm busy." 

uhhhhh yeaaaaa, I'm a BOMB ASS tipper, being a server myself, and you can lick the crack of my Beautiful derrière if you think you'll get a cent of it. absolutely the worst customer service I've experienced Yet in Santa Barbara. way to bring the vibe Down Elsie's. left immediately. I'll go get service where my presence is appreciated. 

the neighborhood bar is AWESOME! and the press room was fun too. both a GAGILLION times better than Elsie's!

Snow Peas is one of the vegetables that I never refuse to eat when I was kid, Stir-fry with some sliced beef that doesn't required too much sauce that give you the nice fresh little undertone type of the sweetness that makes me go....Hum. 

Snow Peas Kitchen offer simple, solid food that just enough for me go ...yum as well. For the very first visit before I sat down I was concerned... " This is better not like the HotWok down the street..." sure it doesn't! As matter of fact its even better than some of the Asian food restaurants in the area., reasonable priced and the 10 mins drive from the house. for a night that my friends not feeding me, Snow Peas have my back!!

For those who still doesn't have the yelp app on your phone. You are missing the 10% off or the free pop...just saying...:)

This place is spacious but seem tucked in the heart of Tampa. It would be great for game night with the boys/girls and has good looking food. I haven't tried any yet but next go round definitely will be stuffing my face. 

My sweet bartenders recommended cinnamon on the rim of my cup when drinking seasonal beers. One of the best advice I've ever gotten from a bartender ( trust me I've had a lot ). It gives a rich experience that I would past on to the ones reading this so please try if you're a beer expert.

Really fantastic place for quality sushi!  Highly recommend the Tiger roll!  Our waitress recommended this and we're really glad she did because it was delicious.  
We also got the Volcano roll which is something classic that's served at most sushi places and helps to us compare to other places, this was also very good.  I wish I was more hungry so we could have ordered more rolls, just going to have to wait till next time.  
The baby octopus appetizer was average, I wouldn't get it again, it had a nice soft texture like chicken but it was cold and I would have preferred it warm. 
Nice comfortable clean seating and tables inside.  Sevice was fast and friendly, all workers wears masks. 
They have 2 outdoor tables available if you choose to eat outside.

Well presented, fabulous cocktails.  

You know the type of place: cooler than average glassware, Instagrammable takes on the classic drinks, ice is cut from a blocks, and ingredients you can't pronounce.  

I've never been at peak time.  I don't know how packed the little place gets or how long it takes to get a drink at 10pm on a Friday.  I don't know if your ex will be there or not.  I do know the people working there seem passionate about making great cocktails and cocktail culture.

Come through during a slower time like Sat afternoon, grab something like The Black Gates, chat up the bartender as they prep for the later rushes, and savour.  Your day can only improve.

In A Nutshell:

-Pho Kien Giang has huge bowls of pho.
-For what you get and the price you pay, you are definitely walking out a winner b/c you'll be both stuffed and light on the pocket book.
-This pho joint is in a strip of town that looks like has become the de facto "Vietnamese" area of Greater Tampa.

Overall, my wife and I were craving soup after eating a lot of fried food and seafood during a recent trip to Florida and Pho Kien Giang provided said nourishment!

The sushi here is so delicious that I pondered moving to Philadelphia after my first few bites. I will not need to move as the Acela Express is only a one hour train ride away from NYC. It would be worth the trek back just so I can eat here again. Especially when you sit in first class and can order free drinks on the way. I used to sit in the parking lot otherwise known as the 405 or 5 North Freeways for longer than that on trips from OC to LA to visit places I loved as much as Zama. And driving sucks compared to taking the train. There's no friggin waitress or comfort on the freeway. I'm lucky if I don't get cut off while being flipped the bird. That settles it. I'm going to start plotting my next trip. It's really that good! Plus, Philadelphia is a fun city.

I'm addicted to the Spicy Chirashi which consists of various chef's selection of sashimi over a bed of seasoned spicy rice. It's only available at lunch but the sushi chef (Kevin) was nice enough to make it for me anyway on an evening visit since I liked it so much.

I also really enjoyed the Kumamoto Oyster Shooter with Chili Daikon, Scallions, Masago, and Ponzu with Tabasco. I opt for a version without sake because I prefer it that way. And speaking of sake... I ordered the Koshi No Junmai Ginjo Sake and I recommend it if you like sake that is sweet but not too sweet and a smooth finish.

Here's the other stuff I tried, all of which was excellent:

Yellowtail
Scottish Salmon
Kindai Bluefin Tuna
& Japanese Unagi

Five star service provided by Mary and the sushi chef Kevin. Extra shoutouts for them because they made my sushi experience first class all the way.

I was so sad, when my favorite coffee shop, Roast Inc., was closing it's coffee shop portion, focusing only on roasting and cold brews.  I figured it was for the best for them, and I was glad to hear that they started to feature beans at good coffee shops like Edgehill Cafe, but I felt that something deep inside me was lost without getting to visit Brad and Lesa way down on Trousdale Pike.

How excited I was to read that they were opening their brand new place on 8th Ave. S., much closer to downtown.  I found the location, and watched it as they prepped the spot for weeks.  And when the Scene announced, out of nowhere that they were having an unofficial tasting, I could not wait to stop by.

And, not surprisingly, it's amazing, when you walk in, you're immediately greeted by these two very large tables, bearing small cards saying the wood for these tables were reclaimed twice, once from China, and then again from a Bowling Alley from somewhere in South Nashville.  They look just like bowling lanes.  Their counters are very open and inviting, and even their newest employees "get it."  They may not totally understand the roasting and flavor experience, but they are working hard, and I like that.  Brad and Lesa, as always, are pure sunshine, and they by themselves make 8th and Roast a worthy experience.

Their little gimmick (and don't take that the wrong way, I LOVE gimmicks!), is an open pour-bar where you can the hot water over the single origin beans yourself if you care to.  They clearly want to make you part of the coffee experience, and no one else does that, in Nashville at least.

This isn't a place where they get bags and bags of beans from some central roaster hundreds of miles aways: they roast their coffee themselves, and they work hard at it. It shows in every cup.  They don't cut corners and they don't settle for anything less than some of the best beans in the world.

I've raved and raved and raved over Roast Inc, and I can only imagine that this will bring a much wider audience to their wonderful products.  Nashville has gotten such a great selection of coffee places, but if I were to choose only one, 8th & Roast would be it without any hesitation.

This restaurant is so spunky and cute! I love the atmosphere and layout of this place! I had a great time meeting up with some friends at Verde. Our waitress was Esis and she was soooo sweet and charismatic!  I love going to verde because the food is consistent whenever I order my favorite, shrimp and pulpo (octopus) tacos. I was skeptical about first trying the pulpo because its octopus, but when I had it for the first time awhile back, it was delicious and now thats my main go to. Every time I go I always say to myself im going to try something different, but I end up getting the same order because its soooo good and consistent. 

Verde is a little higher in cost but not too high where you cant just sit down for lunch, so it's reasonably priced for what you are getting. For an appetizer we got the tamales, oysters, guacamole, and shrimp ceviche. Everything was full of flavor and delicious. For my entree I got the usual, shrimp and pulo tacos with a side of rice, YUM my FAVORITE. For desert my friends got the churros but I got the leche cake. That cake was amazing it was spongy like angel cake but with a light whipped frosting and berry preserves on top. YUMMMMM!!!

My bill came out to be around $39 for my entree, dessert, and of course a margarita. (Not including appetizers because we all shared) Not that bad! Love Love Love Verde. Ill see you all soon!

OVERVIEW:
On the bottom level of the new four seasons, but with enough of a great reputation of its own (from parent restaurant Vernick) comes a new modern seafood-based restaurant. The interior is clean, modern, and is more trendy and less intimate than the original Vernick. As a HUGE fan of Vernick, I had high expectations. I assume I came about a week or two after it first opened, so I wanted to keep that in mind and be fair when rating. We arrived at 5:30 on a Saturday without reservations, and luckily got one of the last remaining high tops. The bar completely filled up within 30 minutes, so I recommend grabbing reservations if you can. 

THE SERVICE:
First, the service. Everyone is very nice but as a new restaurant it seems like they were still getting the flow of things. Our server was super sweet, but she either checked up too many times on us or didn't return at all when we wanted to get the bill. Again, not a big deal as it seems like the staff was getting the small kinks sorted out. 

THE FOOD:
The menu offers a lot, but mainly seafood items which I really like. The menu is also aesthetically beautiful, it's this thick blue paper with the drink menu in a pocket on the back. I liked that they use shaved ice in the cocktails I saw, but didn't try any this time. So onto menu, there are separate sections for tartares, small dishes, large dishes, non seafood (pork/chicken/beef all offered) and veggies- plus more like raw fare etc- can't remember it all. We didn't want anything hot, but we did try several hot veggie items...here is my review:
1. Oysters - tried 2 each of the 3 east coast ones. They rotate I assume but our favorites started with an N. Sorry not useful lol, but all were fresh as one would expect. 
2. Scallop Tartare (from the tartare section) - served with lattice chips, great flavor and portion is decent (not too big) I would order again.
3. Mushrooms (from veggie section) really liked this dish! Great flavor and presentation.
4. Salt & Vinegar Potatoes - I am a big potato fan as long as there is flavor- these did it for me. 
5. Tuna & Foie Gras - small portion but delicious. Tuna was very fresh 
Dessert (all of which you can view in the glass refrigerator in the middle of the restaurant!):
6. Tres Leches cake - I've had this dish in many restaurants, here it is one of the best and you can pour the condensed milk to your liking. Stellar dessert.
7. Carrot Cake Pie - a dense carrot cake that has amazing flavor with a thinner layer of icing. As an icing lover, I still loved this dessert even though it had less icing because the flavor of the cake was so rich, perfectly sweet and embodied the epitome of carrot cake flavor. 

OVERALL:
As a fan of Vernick, and a lover of seafood, I was pleased to eat here and would return again. As a brand new restaurant, I am excited to see what others think and would want to try the other dishes as everything we had was great. I assume it'll get popular quick, so come here while it's new! Come for date night, catching up with friends, bringing the parents out, or just to eat some high quality seafood. As of this visit, Vernick Fish will be in my mental list of top 10 philly restaurants.

Finally after all these years we have a Trader Joe's here! Yay! Being from California originally, I have been going to them back there since the late 80's when they were still more of a wine and cheese shop. They have developed tremendously over the years into a great little market.

I attended the grand opening here this morning (third in line!) and it did not disappoint. The Lei cutting ceremony was so cool! They are a little bigger than the Baton Rouge store and the staff is very friendly and accommodating. I'm so glad I can go here on a regular basis now instead of a few times a year when I visit back home.

They offer a great variety of all sorts of things. And wine too, of course! 

As I expect, there will be many that do not understand the concept of the company/store. So, please read my side notes:

-If you are looking for local New Orleans or Louisiana products and seafood: This is not the store for you.

-If you are looking for national brand items: This is not the store for you. Most of what they sell is Trader Joe's brand.

BUT, if you like to try new things that are good quality and fair priced - This is the store for you!! Plus, Trader Joe's policy is whatever you buy, if for any reason you do not like it or are not satisfied, you can return or exchange the item.

I will be back for sure!!!

Who knew this gourmet poboy gem was hidden here?! All these years I thought it was just a seafood market. Thanks Yelpers! I read the reviews and checked out their menu and we have returned a few times now for take out.

Driving by, the place is very unassuming and small. Inside is a quaint and colorful restaurant, seafood market and bar. 

We generally call ahead and they have our poboys ready in about 15 minutes. The bread for their poboys is the kind with the seeds on top. Our favorites are the Roast Beef poboy (minus the horseradish mayo they are so fond of using) and The Cure poboy. The Cure is an interesting combination of hot sausage patties, over easy eggs and pepper jelly mayo...Yum!!  In addition, they have plate lunches, soups and salads, as well as fresh seafood and boiled seafood.

They have a small bar on one side and the other side has a few tables for those that would like to eat there.

The prices are reasonable and the staff is friendly.

*Note* - They are closed on Tuesdays. However, they are open on Sundays, which is even better.

First off, I highly recommend you make reservations before attempting to go here. Even then, you might not be able to get a reservation! They are always packed. The place is very small. It was formerly a Popeye's and the size is relatively the same.

On our third attempt at trying to go here since December we were finally able to get a table last weekend for a very late lunch.

They start you off with a loaf of bread and seasoned oil to dip the bread in. It was yummy. We split a Margherita Pizza. It was very good. I had a hard time narrowing down what to order. So many of the dishes sounded great. I love that they use fresh local ingredients. I ended up choosing the Fresh Frattura with grilled mushrooms. It was melt in your mouth excellent. My boyfriend got the Spaghetti and Meatballs. He enjoyed it. Our friend got the Penne Rosemary Chicken. It looked delicious. The quality of all the ingredients was superb.

I would definitely like to come back here again but it would be nice if they had more tables. They did add on a very small outdoor patio in front. But, the sides are not enclosed. They have two heaters out there. It seemed when we tried to go one of the other times, they were reluctant for anyone to sit outside even though they had a very large party taking up half of the inside of the restaurant. So we left.

*Note that they are closed on Sundays and the rest of the week they are closed everyday between 3 - 5.

I've been here a few times mostly for drinks. 

I took my little sister (14) for munchies around 9pm on a Friday night. It wasn't too busy, waited about 10 minutes to be seated.

We had the sweet potatoes tater tots with fries. The pot stickers. The bratwurst sliders with mustard.

The sweet potatoe tots were awesome. They went great with any dipping sauce and weren't to sweet. 

The pot stickers were really good and tasted fresh. You can tell they were hand made instead of frozen. I ate them alllll.

The bratwurst sliders were really good. Definitely needed the mustard to go with them as there is no sauce. Almost like it's missing something. They came in 2 and we're pretty good size.

The Port they have on tap is just too good. It's a crime. It's like chocolate coffee syrup.

The staff was very attentive and polite, although they had a full house. 

Will definitely go back for those tots.

My fiancé, my family and I have been happily visiting The Getaway for 3-years now.  Every experience we've had has been spectacular...until now.  For some unknown reason, we found it impossible to get service after we ate lunch today.  We enjoyed a late lunch with a great waiter named Jacob who was ending his shift.  He brought us a few amazing drinks before ending his shift.  We then decided to sit on a couple of Adirondack chairs by the dock.  At that point, all wait staff completely ignored us for HOURS.... We tried speaking with the very nice hostess three times, but she couldn't get a single waiter to acknowledge us or the other seven paying customers around us.  Finally, the hostess had to physically escort a waitress over to our seats to take our order.  It was all very bizarre.  Not sure if we'll be back...kinda irritated.

What can be said about this delicious tourist trap that hasn't been said before?

Cafe Du Monde is known for two things, hot fresh beignets and its famous chicory coffee. On any given day there are crowds of people covered in powdered sugar downing these little bites of heaven. It's definitely on the must try list if you're visiting New Orleans. 

Side note: used to be open 24 hours a day but closes at 10 p.m. since covid. Hopefully that will change soon.

One of my absolute must have breakfast spots when visiting New Orleans!

I don't know where to start on the menu. At this point I've made my way through most of it so here are some of the standouts.

Aebelskivers- these are a must have. They are puffed pancakes served with a choice of dipping sauce. Nutella and lemon curd are some of my favorite. 

Toast- prosciutto, honey, and ricotta is the best.

Chicken and waffles- perfectly cooked and served with cayenne butter. 

There are many other delicious items as well. Open 7 days a week from 8-3 p.m. Go! You won't be sorry.

Mother's is a New Orleans staple open since the 1930's. It has been featured on several t.v. food shows and has countless reviews. On any given day  there is a line out the door waiting to get in. Not to worry though this place runs like a top and the line tends to move quickly. 

While everything at Mother's is great there is one main reason to visit and that's for the FAMOUS FERDI SPECIAL. This is a ham, roastbeef and New Orleans debris on french bread. Both ham and roastbeef are made on premises in Mother's own butcher shop.

Mother's is sure not to disappoint!

I love tapas. I love getting to have a bite of dozen different things and experiment with new dishes every time.

The first time we walked into the most heavenly smelling restaurant, I was shocked it wasn't busier. The second time I realized, its taking people a while to catch on to this gem of soon to be hot spot.

The crab cakes were, again, heaven. Literally the best on the planet, EVER! That was our first dish and my mouth was watering for the rest of our delectable treats.  The rest of the evening progressed with dish after dish of heaven sent epicurean delights.

The second disk was sliders. You'd think that would be boring, but no. Cooked to perfection with little chunks of bacon and a sauce to die for, they were impressive in the way all the flavors combined to make a mouth-watering impact.

If you're not a Lobster fan, figure out some way to get the brown butter and sage sauce that comes on the Lobster ravioli. I'd be fine if they just brought some in a teacup for dessert. It's magical.

Next up was the Lamb with mushroom risotto. I love ordering lamb at restaurants to get ideas on how to make it at home. This had a demi glaze but sprinkled with a little chimmichurri sauce. Kinda awesome! And the lamb was cooked to perfection!

Here's where the concept of Tapas goes a little sideways. The venison lasagne. It was the size of my head. HUGE in fact! Totally a meal unto itself. Not that we were disappointed because its going to make a fabulous lunch today, but it's seriously large.

By this time we were stuffed and need to take a minute to digest... then out comes a tart delicious lemon berry graham cracker delite that just needed to be eaten. :)  We waddled out. With huge grins.  Great night, great food, exceptional service.  I predict the chef Kim Wells will be making that list of 10 best restaurants in the USA soon. She's creative and this menu has so much variety that I'll have to eat here a dozen times just to try it all.

Parking is easy at the garage, then take an after dinner stroll along the river... very romantic. I'll be back for sure.

It's a shame that you can't opt for zero stars. I had high hopes for this place. I went a month ago on a Saturday afternoon for a few cocktails with a friend and it was busy but not crazy. The service was decent at the bar. I was really excited because one of my favorite dj/artists rjd2 is a regular performer there. So I bought the tickets for the show on 7/11 and went with a friend, who happens to have the disability of only having one eye. Long story short, he went out to smoke and on the way back in he stumbled on the first stair into the place, hence only having one eye and not the greatest depth perception, and the goons working the door wouldn't let him back in. The show had not even started yet. So I went out to find out why they wouldn't let him back in and told them about his disability, but they just didn't care one bit, he was not coming back in.
