I started to get agitated with them as the show hadn't started and I had an open tab in there and they then pushed me out on to the sidewalk and told me to leave too. These thugs wouldn't give me my card back on my tab, then when they realized I wasn't leaving without it took 20 minutes and returned my card and tab was much larger than the 3 drinks I bought on it.  They refused to give me anything other than the credit card receipt so I couldn't even verify what they were charging me for. I will be disputing that with my bank. 


Overall I want to send out a huge FUCK YOU to Morgans Pier, and here are the reasons why I will tell everyone I know to never go to your sleazy establishment. Not only do you discriminate against people with disabilities but your door staff seems to get off on what little power they are given and are complete and utter assholes but you also tried to rip me off. Ill be sure that you get NONE of the money I had originally tried to spend there. I hope this review steers everyone away. The only thing you had was location. Buh bye

I want to first say that the bartenders were great! I should have eaten there but waited for my table.Unfortunately, I'm writing my first review because of a really bad dining experience. 7 waiters/waitresses walked around completely ignoring us. After waiting for 15 minutes, I had to complain to the hostess. The owner or manager noticed and said he would get a server right away. Another 5 minutes go by, we get the chips and told that our server is Jess. The same person notices that we haven't gotten served and Jim comes to serve us. A different manager comes to apologize saying Jess is mad at him and we should let him know if there is anything he can do for us. He was actually one of the folks who walked by and didn't see us fuming at our table. The food is extra delayed where Jim comes to apologize twice. On top of it, it was the worst Mexican food I've ever had. I'm never coming again. It you're looking for a better Mexican place I recommend plaza azteca in KOP or norristown- should have gone there. In addition, it's expensive.

I can scarcely find the words to describe this establishment after what they recently did for us.  My mother passed away just over a week ago.  The funeral luncheon was scheduled at Columbia Station in downtown Phoenixville.  The storm of last Tuesday came through - and knocked out the power at Columbia Station.  They phone at 6:30PM THE NIGHT BEFORE THE FUNERAL to tell me that our luncheon must be cancelled.  So - what do we do?  We call Jeff at the Kimberton Inn.  This professional man was so gracious and accommodating, it blew our minds.  Within TWO HOURS - he had the luncheon set up and ready to go for us the next day.
And WHAT A JOB THEY DID.  The room was beautiful - the food outstanding - and the service impeccable!  We received nothing but high praise & compliments from family & friends who attended the funeral.  They even personalized the menus to honor my late mother.  What a touch!
In the future, I will think of the Kimberton Inn and NOT the Columbia Station for events such as this.  Further, we will dine regularly at the Kimberton after this experience AND because the food is so good.
Hats off to Jeff and his team at the Kimberton Inn!!!!!!!

Went to lunch on a friday afternoon with my mom. We were greeted promptly with a cheery hello and welcome. They have done a very nice job on the design and remodel. 
Our waitress Sam ( I think), quickly approached our table and took our drink orders. She was very informative about the menu and gave us the perfect amount of time to look it over. We had one small glitch with our lunch......and THIS is where they could teach others how to handle such a situation. First Sam apologized (sincerely) took the plate and immediately told the owner and the chef. The owner came over and also apologized and thanked us for bringing it to her attention, removed it from our bill, offered us any other item we would like.    BRAVO!!
On our way out we were told thank you and hope to see you soon. We can't wait to go back mom wants to try the mac-n-cheese!!!

OMGosh I wish this place was close to my house.  It is so delicious!!! I ordered a fish taco, a shrimp taco, and a pupusa. The tacos were sweet due to the mango salsa but hot sauce balanced out the flavors.  The pupusas were SPECTACULAR!!!!!! I can't wait to go back for more.  The service was nice at this little spot.  



19/16

My boyfriend and I were seeing a realtor in the area so we decided to stop by for lunch.  I have been to the Truckee location so I knew what to expect......BIG delicious food!!!  My boyfriend had heard about the breakfast burrito and decided to give it a try with bacon.  It was decent size and he said it was fantastic!!!  I ordered something totally out of the norm for me and had the meatball sandwich.  I then had to choose from a long list of bread and I chose the house made jalapeno cheddar.  My sandwich was GIGANTIC!!!!  The bread was amazing, the meatballs were extremely delicious and very tender.  The marinara was flavorful and the mozzarella was not lacking.  It comes with black olives in it so if you are like me and don't like them, be sure to ask for none or you'll have to pick out like I did.  Luckily there weren't too many.  My sandwich was so large I ate it for three and half meals.  My one small complaint was there were many flies bothering us while we ate, however, that will NOT keep me from going back for that sandwich because I can't wait to have it again!! 



17/16

I've been here a couple times now and wow they have really good food.  The menu is quite large so a little hard to pick.  They have Chinese food and Pho.  Both times I went I had a soup of some kind.  It is a large bowl of which I couldn't finish.  
They have a large selection of drinks including smoothies and boba. I am looking forward to trying one on a future trip and to experience more of the menu.
With so few great places in Spanish Springs I'm glad this place is here.


20/2

As a Native Texan, I'm always leery of eating Mexican food outside of Texas. Anyone who loves Tex-Mex is always hesitant to branch out. I can tell you that the vast majority of my experiences with Mexican food outside of the great State of Texas has been negative.  Thankfully, Sopapilla's came through with a bang and gave us a great experience. 

First of all, this is not Tex-Mex.  Sopapilla's is a Mexican food with a New Mexico flair.  We started our meal with a chili con queso appetizer. It was very good. It was also free as a reward for checking in on Yelp.  The current promotion (7/2020) when we checked in was that two people from the same party had to check in on Yelp in order to get one free appetizer.  We did so we got a freebie. It was a really good chili con queso.  In addition, we both had two tacos each. I had a brisket taco and the original taco. My wife had the blue corn chicken taco and the shrimp taco.  We enjoyed them immensely. It was plenty of food as we arrived hungry but not starving.  Overall, we were quite impressed. It was a really good meal and not overly expensive.

Side note:  It is owned by the former bass player from the band Little Big Town, Steve Dale (this fact has zero influence on the rating). 

Bottom line - We were pleasantly surprised with our overall experience of eating Mexican food outside the state of Texas.  The New Mexico Mexican restaurant was very good. We will definitely be back when we are in the area. Bon appétit.

I started making a list of places that deliver near my office. When I was adding places to the list, I realized I never reviewed Juicy's! Whoops! 

I've been trying to steer away from bad food (my metabolism has slowed down as my age increased...interesting correlation, right?) Anyways, when I'm having one of those days that I want greasy, fatty food, this is my go-to place! A regular cheeseburger, fries and milkshake, of course, is what I always order. Yes, they do have more, but why try something else when their burgers are so good! They are juicy (hence the name) and they come with the normal lettuce, tomato, onion....I get mine plain though...I really have no major complaints here (other than they can be a bit slow during their rush hour, but who isn't). The food is always consistent and just your "good old hole in the wall burger joint."

I can't comment on the delivery fee since I've only seen them deliver to my office building. Plus, they are literally walking distance (1 block) from my office so I walk here most of the time versus getting delivery. However, it is nice to know they deliver for the days I can't leave the office.

- - - Unacceptable and Shocking Experience - - - 

We came here on Saturday night with my family and we were upset that we were seated in a corner next to a storage station where no table should be. The staff kept bumping into our table and my body, therefore I kindly asked to move to another table. We were then escorted to another table which we were satisfied with. However, the owner storms to the table and tell us the table is reserved and implied we need to leave. I was in shock at that point and asked him "do you really want us to leave?" and his response was "yes". 

As a military veteran who has served for this country, I felt that I was discriminated against by him. We were very upset and disrespected that we were refused service at this establishment. I should have read all of the Yelp reviews before coming to this place because we wasted our time to be insulted.

Lastly, when Valet got my car, they left the car running unattended in the parking lot and never informed us that the car was there.

Although, we were never given an opportunity to have a dining experience, I would not recommend this place to anyone.

Went here after reading all the reviews on Yelp. Excellent in every way. Great food, excellent service, family owned and operated, they did everything to make sure we had a good meal. Will definitely be going back.

I used to be a lunch regular. This place has really gone downhill. I used to overlook the obvious uncleanliness of the place because the food was good. Last year all of their bathrooms were out of order. How can a business function with no bathroom. 

Two weeks ago I gave them another chance and the service was abysmal. They were super busy at lunch, and they called in some kid to work. I watched him arrive, then go right in the kitchen and touch food without washing his hands!

Never again.

We came to celebrate a birthday. There were 8 of us so we had to wait a little bit for a larger table because we were not allowed to push 2 tables together. They were quick to bring water and take drink orders, however as the evening went on we found ourselves constantly asking for more water. 

We ordered about half the menu: the lamb, pork, calamari, English peas, home fries, succotash, steak sandwich, chocolate and citrus dessert. It was all amazing! I don't think you can go wrong here. What particularly stood out was the lamb and chocolate mousse. Perfect blend of flavors and textures. One thing to note is that you fill out an order sheet (like at a sushi restaurant) and everything comes as prepared (the waitress did warn us about this) So there was a little awkwardness waiting with some people eating and some not. Luckily we like to share. Also there was a considerable spread in the dishes we ordered at 8 and got the last dish at 9:30 (not including dessert which we ordered later and came out quickly).

We were hoping to get a candle or something since we were celebrating a birthday...but they didn't have any.

Our bill was ~$400 for 8 people with drinks.

I would definitely go again. It's a great little oasis in the quarter. I'm not giving it 5 stars (yet) because I think they have some room to grow in the service.

My wonderful wife and I stopped in here before some medical appointments. I got avocado toast which was wonderful. It had a nice sunny side egg on top and was way more than I can eat.  I enjoyed it in three servings. Thank you Blind Tiger!

Life is good with avocado toast!

We had a very nice meal here on a weekday evening! The food was amazing and the service was even better! We look forward to returning to this local establishment. 

Life is good!!!

We love Chicago hot dogs and this is the best place to get them! Just enjoy a proper hot dog with all the fixings!

Life is good!!

Hidden in a side street in Safety Harbor, we have here the best French food in Tampa Bay. The service is also on point. 

French onion soup? Delicious!
Escargot? Wonderful!
Steak frites! Perfect!

If you'd like a fine French meal or host a business party, which is what I did, this is the place!

I might be a foodie but I'm definitely not Cuban! Still, the service and food we had here was spectacular! The couple running the place were very gracious and their kids were full of life!

We had fried yuca with cilantro garlic sauce and a spinach empanada for appetizers. El freakin yummo to quote a famous yelper!

My beans, yellow rice, sweet plantains and fried pork main was beautifully presented and beyond delicious! Just add hot sauce and life is good!

We had a fantastic meal here hosted by Boon and Grace. The service was friendly and welcoming and we got to try so many new dishes, shared among the party. The cheese and raspberry blinchiki was my favorite!

We enjoyed our tasty crazy burgers here on a Saturday afternoon. The place was pretty busy with a wide variety of hungry and friendly folks of all ages! I didn't have to wait long in line and the lady who took our order was on point! 

Because of the large number of people waiting, I thought I might need to be patient but our food came up in only a few minutes! Nice!

I didn't really know what a crazy burger was but ordered them because of the name! It was crazy good with nice flavors! The fries were less exciting and could be crispier or have more salt. I have no complaints though because they were free and came with the burgers at a very affordable price!

Support your local hidden businesses and life is good!

I will fly with Jerome any time. You should too!

When you have an opportunity to sample real croissants (not the utter crap available at Publix or Panera), brioche, fruit tarts, and anything else Jerome decided to bake, do not hesitate. He only uses the finest ingredients like imported butter. Did you know butter in the US is actually 20% not butter (perhaps the remainder is water...)! In Europe or from a very few specialized small butter producers, you get 86% butterfat butter by default. In other words, more of the butter is actually butter and this difference, combined with other high-quality ingredients and then straight-from-France baking expertise, produces pastries that will simultaneously blow your mind and tantalize your tastebuds. 

The almond croissant I just finished was beyond delicious and also, huge! The other items we got (sorry, I can't pronounce them and I didn't write done what they were) were equally stupendous!

They do serve brunch until 3pm and then dinner later in the evening on weekends only. I mention this because if you arrive a little after 3, the kitchen is closed for the changeover and you will need to survive on pastry and espresso alone. Oh, the horror..! ;-)

We look forward to Flying with Jerome in the future for the amazing brunch menu and then again for dinner!

We had an amazing time exploring food from Venezuela. I'm here to tell you, it's delicious! This hidden restaurant is at the end of a tiny two story strip mall but inside, it's quite pleasant and even classy. 

We started with fried yucca that came with chimichurri and a huge bottle of awesome garlic sauce. Then we had massive Venezuelan empanadas they had meat, cheese and beans in them for a nice combination. 

For my main, I had cachapas which is a sweet corn pancake with yummy fresh cheese inside. In addition, it came with two medium-rare skewers of beef plus a helping of chorizo, all for a very reasonable price. I could only eat a small amount so I'm good for a few more meals!

My awesome wife had a patacon sklyper which is a fun plantain open faced sandwich which was also delicious. 

We definitely look forward to coming back here and trying even more Venezuelan items!

We ordered a Easter ham from here to support a local business. It was super delicious and well worth it. They delivered it right to our car when we pulled in. I'm enjoying some amazing leftovers right now! 

Thanks Epicurean!

This is a well known breakfast spot on the road along the beach. It's not actually on the beach but they know how to make a proper breakfast. 

Life is good with eggs and grits.
I thought Coney Island was in New York. Detroit isn't near New York so call me very confused! Still, the service and food we had were fun and flavorful! Hotdogs and chili and life is good!

We enjoyed a fine Columbian meal to go at this local spot in Clearwater. The food was very tasty and very plentiful! I've been eating it for three days. 

We came pretty early but plenty of other people came in too so it was good to see the business doing well! If you want some amazing chicharron or Bandeja Paisa or fried yuca or empanadas or all of the above, don't hesitate to come here. 

Life is good with Columbian food!

We had a wonderful meal which they kindly brought out to the car for us. The quiche Florentine was fantastic, fluffy and delicious served with a generous salad. My wonderful wife enjoyed her breakfast sandwich on a croissant with bacon plus a chai tea latte. We also got a avocado toast but I'm full so will eat it later. 

Life is good with local homemade food!

What an incredible beach bar experience! I found the place through yelp talk and life is good! 

The band was rocking! The beach was amazing! The food was good too! The service was great!

We can't wait to come back. For tunes and food and drinks on the amazing sand, this is the spot!!

We've enjoyed all of our taco meals here! They offer a huge variety plus indoor and outdoor seating plus drinks! 

What more can you want? Life is good with tacos!

I'm not an expert in Turkish food and I've never been to Turkey but we definitely enjoy Tazza! This quite tiny establishment has wonderful pictures of the owners family on the walls among native decorations. For seating, there are a very small number of tables that are a bit squeezed together plus two tables outside on the sidewalk. 

As for the food, their lentil soup is to die for and the kunefe dessert is quite unique and delicious! Both must be tried. In between soup and dessert, every Turkish specialty we've tried has been well prepared!

They also offer burgers, salads and a strange variety of pasta dishes (e.g. Louisiana pasta, fettuccine alfredo, etc) but we've never tried any of them. Perhaps they are popular also in Turkey but I have no idea. Do you?

We've had multiple business lunches here which everyone enjoyed! Order it Thai extra extra hot or super mild. Either way...

Life is good!

I've hosted multiple business events here and they have all been successful. The service and food have been excellent. Best of all, there is a nice assortment on the menu from sushi to seafood to steaks!

Life is good at Water Oak Grill!

Maybe my favorite overall meal of our Southwest road trip through three states! Maybe probably...but definitely five stars. Our first day in Tucson it was closed so lucky we were able to grab it before hitting the road. Didn't even know it was on Yelp's Top 100 Places to Eat in the US...now I know why. They make amazing breakfast burritos. Like the best ever. Wife and I shared one (with chorizo), and it was the perfect size. Especially when you're driving 5+ hours that day...you don't wanna over-burrito. That would be a rookie mistake. It comes with a red sauce on the side that the lady said was super hot. We didn't think it was THAT hot, but it was really flavorful and did bring some heat. 

And I can't forget to mention the drinks. We ordered a house cold brew and their horchata latte drink--AMAZING. 

A perfect breakfast.

This was my introduction to the Sonoran Hot Dog, and I don't know if I'll ever wanna go anywhere else now. It's so good. And hey so was everything else we tried from the menu, especially the Taco Yaqui, a chile relleno stuffed with meat, cheese, bacon, and mushroom. All the flavors! 

Check this place out if you're in the Tucson area. I know we'll be making a trip back for another Sonoran Hot Dog and more stuff from the menu. 

An easy five stars.

We feasted. 

This was a great change-of-pace meal while road trippin' through the Southwest. And most importantly, the BBQ is no joke. Some of the best I've ever had (not sure how much weight that carries from someone from the Bay Area...), as the meats were all rich with flavor and tender and lathered up in sauce. Sides were good too, especially the Mac n cheese and collard greens--only bummer was the cornbread that was a little bit on the drier side. 

Also, the value for all that you get is legit. I think we had three meats, four sides, and a drink for less than $30.

Okay, dope coffee shop in Santa Barbara, I see you. Was in the area and needed a little boost to get the day going. Happened to drive by here, and what a find! Space is really cool, big and open, with a marketplace type vibe and other food stalls--it was early in the morning, so those were all closed. Almost swooped a bag of beans to take home, wish I would've actually, but ended up just grabbing a nitro cold brew for the road. High quality stuff. Super smooth. 

Highly recommend if you're in the area!

#SupportLocal

A nice restaurant cafe to come and enjoy if you are ever staying in the Peppermill. They have an extensive menu and servings are big.  You will be sure to walk out with some leftovers. The waitstaff in the morning were a little delayed and so was the delivery of our food. My parents who had dined here before knew the wait would be long that they left us to go gamble. Not so great. Once our food was delivered we dined and were not visited until it was time to drop the check. Oh wells. Still like the convenience of the location. Especially since I was over the buffet.

Los Gallos Taqueria sits on the main drag of Downtown Reno. The place was pretty packed due to the Hot August Nights event and they did a pretty good job moving people in and out of the place. 

That's as good as it gets though. The food here is subpar. My S/O ordered a carne asada burrito and said that it was flavorless. The burrito was massive although it was filled with a lot of rice. I ordered two super tacos. They use tiny corn tortillas and filled with a crap ton of lettuce, like where's my al pastor meat? Lol. I did like that they have unlimited tortilla chips and salsa readily available for everyone. 

The interior is pretty run down. The walls are filled with Michoacan churches and culture. Dining area is clean and spacious and overall makes this place an A-Ok Mexican taqueria. We're San Jose, CA people so our expectations are a tad high. 

Solid 3 stars for me.

Loud, crowded, and small. The diner serves huge portions that will satisfy the locals and visitors of Reno. 

The Little Nugget Diner is like Red Robin on a lower scale. It's small, run down, and if you don't mind the smell of cigarettes then hell this would be a great place for you. They specialize in burgers, sandwiches, and wait for it... even breakfast!

The rundown:

Diced Ham and Eggs: Funny because the portions were so huge because it looked like they used a dozen eggs for this plate lol. It also comes with a heaping slab of hash browns. 

French Toast: 3 huge slices of toast for those looking to satisfy their sweet tooth. 

Chili Cheese Fries: This side is honestly enough to share with a big group of friends or two hungry people. Seriously, its basket sized fries and you seriously can't go wrong ordering it. Their chili was tasty and the cheese they use wasn't overpowering and the onions? Ugh, It was good. Real good. 

S/O found this place on a whim and it certainly was a good find - thank you!

If you don't mind the rough neighborhood, almost non existent parking or the traffic from all the street construction this is a pretty good place for wings. The place is a dump and people working here were really rude. I got the feeling it was because I was the wrong skin color. I really wanted to give this place 1 star or less but I did enjoy the wings. I tried 5 of the many flavors they had and liked all of them. I can't say much about the watermelon punch because I think they just gave me Kool-aid. This place could be so much more. Hopefully they will read peoples comments and make changes. I could overlook some things but never the service.

The reviews are true folks, Konan's BBQ is AMAZING. I was pretty surprised at the location that Konan's in since it's smack dab in the middle of a residential area. But sure enough, we could smell the bbq from down the street. We went in near closing time but there were still plenty of people ordering food. I ordered the chopped pork with baked beans and mac and cheese and it was heavenly! The chopped pork isn't exactly pulled pork but it's still deliciously tender. The tangy bbq sauce really pulled the flavors together. The sweet baked beans were perfect and the superb mac and cheese really made this a satisfying meal. Trust me, it's worth it!

One of Tampa's most popular restaurants that serves dishes with locally sourced ingredients. Ulele sits upon the Tampa river walk and is nestled between Water Works Park and Armature Works. I haven't yet been here for dinner but I enjoyed every lunch I've had here. 

From the ambience to the service to the food, Ulele surely does not disappoint. On my most recent visit, I came with a large party of 15 and our servers were extremely attentive and helpful during our meal. I enjoyed the gulf grouper sandwich and was pleased at the generous size of the fish. Afterwards, we enjoyed ice cream that Ulele makes in-house. 

Dishes here are a bit higher, but the service, quality and ambience adds to the amazing experience.

LISTEN. I read some of the reviews..eyeballed the pictures...got in the car and drove 30 minutes on a mission to experience all that is Caplinger's. 

I am like so confused by the high ratings on this place. Maybe I went on a bad day (Saturday around 7pm) that had the staff overworked, but it is highly unlikely I can find any love up in here. 

I love fish, I love seafood... I am deathly allergic to most of it, and have been known to sacrifice my insides for a taste of good crab. *side note* I am not full blown throat closing comatose shock allergic to ALL see food - mostly crab, lobster, and scallops (shellfish). So, if I were on the brink of total collapse after enjoying some DELICIOUS  seafood, I will crawl out the door on my hands and knees happy. 

THIS was NOT the case. Please tell me what you see in this place?? Should I go back again?? Feel free to inbox me, because I really want to know if I'm just being a picky jerk about Fresh Catch. 

Let me begin. Finally. 

Walking in the door, I stood in the "line" which happened to be the wrong line because there are two. One for carry out and one for dining in ordering?? I don't know actually because I am still confused about this. I walked around to the dine in ordering line, and we were in it for about 10 minutes. That was ok because it gave me time to take a few pictures. When We got through "the line", the gentleman told us a little history about the place, and that there is roughly 1 hour wait to be served. 

Hmmm... ok, so I asked if take out was any faster. He said, "no" and that they make, "all their food as the orders come in." 

Is it organized or progressive?...I am not so sure. It made me wonder how small the kitchen was, or if they had ample staff for the flood of orders coming in. The orders were being mixed up (names spelled wrong on call in orders) and this  led to an even longer wait. 

We ordered and got our drinks from a cramped up station that only one person could squeeze in at a time. I grabbed salt, mustard, ketchup etc... there weren't items available on the table. Which, would probably save on a ton of waste if they were - however, require more attention to the dining area. 

THE SUPER tiny dining area is frustrating at best-- for the entire hour and a half waiting for our food, we played musical chairs.  First having to wait outside - then standing near the smoked salmon, and finally to the high counter, then over to a small table. Needless to say, the exercise was great, but brought the excitement to eat way down. 

When we got our food, I instantly noticed the quality of the fried items being poor, more than likely due to not changing the grease. The hard darkened fry shell, did not coating the meat - which may have been water logged or frozen. The Mac was bland and greasy, the green beans were super salty, the corn was dry, and the potato fries were just not good. 

The one thing that I really didn't like was the fact that the oyster half shells were a little to warm for me. I always feel like something like this should be  served ICE cold. Totally cold. ICE COLD like the heart of Ursula when she wanted Ariel's voice in exchange for some legs, because Ursula sounded like she smokes e-sea cigs, and most Princesses didn't have match.com back then!!!!!! 

We still had six oysters and 8 cocktail shrimp. Yea, I did like the cocktail shrimp and sauce. 


I will go back to try some of their fresh catch, especially the giant tiger shrimp. However, I just don't believe this place is worth the price or hype. 

What to try: If you decide to go.. definitely try the cocktail sauce.

How to make Caplinger's Fresh Catch Healthy: They have a few options that *can't be grilled which leads me to believe almost everything else can be. Skip the sides, and sauces. Grab water to drink, and go without dessert. OR, take the option of buying fresh and cooking it yourself at home. Enjoy!

Coyote Crossing was a nice addition to Conshohocken when it opened about a dozen years ago.  The food was good and it was good Mexican food.  The chef left after a year, and my two subsequent visits were unpleasant, so I did not return for a good 5 years, until last night when friends indicated that they wanted to try it again.  Do not make that mistake.

Any decent Mexican food truck in California serves much better food at reasonable prices, and the food here is basically truck food.  Granted, the margaritas are excellent and the freshly made tortilla chips are good.  Everything else is unremarkable, at best, and do not expect reasonable prices to reflect the poor food quality, relying heavily on cheap carbohydrates.

The service is basically untrained, pushy and intrusively spotty, and the room inside has a decible level that makes conversation difficult.  In mild weather, the outside dining area is pleasant enough, but not enough reason to come here.

But the most galling and unacceptable aspect of this badly managed place is their attempt to squeeze money from diners for imagined orders.  I ordered a gin martini, saying house gin was fine for me.  The bill came with a $1 up-charge for Beefeaters.  We asked the waiter for some sour cream and hot sauce on the side.  He returned with two small cups with about one tablespoon of sour cream and a teaspoon of hot sauce.  We were charged a $1 up-charge for each of these.  When I complained to the manager, he replied that you always must expect to be charged for an ordered side dish.  These were not side dishes.  They were condiments, and are part of a normal meal.  If they served hamburgers, which they do not, they would charge for a slice of onion or ketchup.  You want mustard on that hot dog?  another buck.  Maybe pickle relish would go for 2 bucks.

Ridiculous!  And insulting as well.  Save your money and resist being treated like a sucker.  Bad food.  Bad service.  Excessive charges.  And an unpleasantly noisy environment.  Not my idea of a nice night out with friends.

WARNING: I will be cursing my a** off.

These guys are assholes who are cocky as sh*t for sh*tty a** cheesesteak. For one, their soggy a** cheesesteak is nothing but GREASE! And their meat is always chewy. To add to their crappy food, their customer service needs to change. 

You are in AMERICA where it is very diverse. How DARE you get rude with my dad who's been here since 1989 from Cambodia just because his English isn't "perfect." His English may not be perfect, but he damn sure can run a better business than you guys can. This is why businesses like yours WILL not succeed despite having gotten where you are today, it doesn't mean it'll last forever. P.S. MY parents ENGLISH may not be perfect, but at least they are intelligent and smart enough to learn to speak 4 different f***ing languages AND raise a successful family coming to America without a damn penny. Screw Geno's. A**holes.

Shells St Pete was by far my favorite restaurant in the immediate St. Pete Beach area we went to. Unpretentious and easy in and out I found Shells to be the most solid option for the goods near where we stayed. Service was spot on and dining outside is always a pleasure. I was a bit leery with all the 5-star reviews of this joint but accurate they were.

What I loved was the Shells seafood pasta. Creamy, decadent, and delicious and filled with a slew of seafood! Also enjoyed several $5 margaritas with that salty rim. My dining experience was probably one of the most enjoyable during our week stay. Solid joint for all thing's seafood and then some. Oh, I almost forgot, my most favorite dish almost even more so than my pasta... drumroll! The Clam Chowda! I had a cup then went back for a bowl... It was so rich and chucked full of clams! No wonder Shells claims to be the best!

Lees is great.  Lee himself is almost always present at the front counter with a very polite neutral expression his face.  Calm, in control and helpful.  He doesn't talk you to death but is definitely willing to make suggestions or give a bit of advice.

We usually get Seitan hoagies when we come here and the sauces they have to accompany it.

I'm not going to lie and say this food is groundbreaking - its standard diner fare but the place looks clean, Lee recently remodeled and it really looks great and the people that work there are always really laid back, polite yet not overbearing or over smiley.  When I lived in W Philly I came to Lees almost exclusively after having a few Bahn Mi hoagies over at Foo Wa and finding them a bit dry (perhaps remaining true to tradition, I can't say) and just not my style.

Lees is a great scene with good food at good prices.  Love it.

Beignets! Beignets! Beignets!

This is definitely a must stop when you are in NOLA. The southern style atmosphere welcomes you and the amazing staff keeps you happy. 

No wait needed to be seated, this is a find your own place to sit (every man for themselves) LoL 

It's hours of operation are 24/7 so make sure you come at the right time because if you don't waiting in line can sometimes take up to two hours. Lucky on my first visit, yes i said first (I came twice) I waited about 10 min total before I found a table and on the second time I did take out and waited less than that.  Once you are seated make sure you try and get the attention of an employee, there are tons of staff walking around and they definitely do there best to help everyone. 

Once you place your order if you are interested in purchasing merchandise you can place that order at the same time. The merchandise they have in stock is a good selection from Mugs, tees, coffee, and beignet mix, if you are looking for more you can always order online or check out any of the local Cafe Du Mond stores in the area, they are open till 5pm daily 

On my visit I had a couple (2) of beignets and a cup of hot coco, they beignets are constantly being made so they don't take much time to arrive to your table and they are always nice and hot, right out of the cooker. The hot coco was so flavorful and thick just how I like it, not like that water down stuff.  

Disclaimer: The powder sugar can and will get all over the place, so if you don't like to make a mess I suggest you don't attempt or maybe wear a bib lol 


Prices are very reasonable and they have combo deals as well.

If I could put negative stars I would! This place is utterly ridiculous. We just left about an hour ago for the following reasons:
1) Place is old: menus are falling apart and ranges are gross. If you're charging about $20/plate or more you can afford to get your ranges cleaned. I mean come on...
2) Salad has thousand island dressing and looks like the salad you can get from Costco in a big bag for under $2 we've been to a ton of Tepanyaki Grills and salad should be served with ginger dressing -I tried it and fiancé refused to eat it... What a waste
3) Onion mushroom soup is a joke... It tastes like cup of noodles soup with a few pieces of green onion and 2 pieces of mushroom... Gross... Another waste...

What did it for us was the service. Not by our waitress but by the owner! There was one couple seated to our right and then there was the two of us. Another couple came with their baby and the owner came to our table to seat them and "shoo-ed" my fiancé to move. Then he sat a larger group across from us and was pointing at a person and pointing at the chair for them to sit... How rude! And he was frowning the whole time! After this, my fiancé was fuming... If you're not grateful for your customers then you don't deserve any business.

We asked for our check and the waitress brought it and asked what was wrong but my fiancé didn't want to deal with the owner. They charged us $15.27 for two sweet teas we didn't drink, 1 untouched salad, 1 half eaten salad and 2 untouched soups. If you owned a restaurant and $70-100 ticket is about to walk out the door, wouldn't you go and try to fix the problem? We know our waitress told the owner because we saw her go up to him and he just walked off.


DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME AND EAT HERE!

We just finished eating at another Steakhouse and got much better service and food was so much better.

There's a special place in hell for me for not writing this review sooner.

This place is SUPER AMAZING!!! Thank goodness for Yelp, or else I probably never would have found it!!!

I came to Reno years ago on vacation and already had my trip planned out...I was all set to go to my most fave breakfast places of all time, Hash House. I was going to go there every day during my week long trip because I love their food. I had not been to Reno and was not familiar with the set up. They ended up being super busy, so I needed back up. I found Peg's and the rest is history. 

I stopped going to the Meadows Parkway location (is it still open???) and came here because this one never seems to be crowded, YAY!!!

We always end up ordering the favorites, Huevos Ranchero, Belgian Waffle, Burger and whatever their special is. Our food never takes long to come out, and when it arrives it was beautiful. The food looks almost too good to eat. The waffle was cooked to perfection and has that wonderful crispy outer layer and was soft and hot in the middle. I had them add bananas and walnuts, as well as whipped cream. The bananas were fresh (not mushy or discolored) and there were plenty of them. I could have done without the walnuts, they weren't chopped up or anything, just thrown on there whole. The waffle was just excellent and had a sweet flavor to it.

The Huevos Ranchero is THE BEST that I have had in a really really long time. There was a little bit of kick in the sauce, but not too much. The beans were great and the eggs were cooked to perfection. They had a bit of slaw served with it, yummers. They did forget to bring the tortillas out with ut, but did so immediately after being brought to their attention.

There was no need to ask for refills because gentleman who always seems to wait on us during every visit was always coming by to check on us. The service here was EXCELLENT!!!

I had walked in the door thinking that we would try it and then maybe go back to Hash House (try to find alternative parking) but after our meal here, we decided to come back HERE to Peg's. On our return visits, we were met with the same fantastic food and service. I am so glad that I found this place. My fellow Yelper's sure didnt fail me on this place.

I would HIGHLY recommend this place and from now on it will be a MUST for me while I am in town!!! 

(My pics, of course, aren't loading on review but they are on biz page)

Cool concept with a lot of unique homemade flavors...but a hot and muggy store that will have you asking for your scoops to-go. 

While I was finishing up my dinner at Smiling With Hope Pizza I searched up some places for a frozen treat...a respite from the Reno heat. Icecycle was in the same shopping center, they had a lot of interesting and unusual flavor combos, so it was an easy choice for me. 

I had hoped to satisfy my sweet tooth while simultaneously cooling off, but I ended up feeling like Tim Krizminski (Backdraft for you youngins) when I opened the door. All of the excitement I had felt about trying new flavors melted away, along with the skin on my face. The girl working apologized saying that they had X amount of machines running and that was the reason for it being so hot. It seems like if they know that then the AC should be lowered, I can't imagine those poor workers having to endure that day in and out. 

We ultimately settled on: Raspberry-Jalapeño Cornbread, Thai Peanut Sauce, Cookie Roulette and Captains Berry n Cream after sampling nearly all of their whacky combinations. 

Out of those flavors the Raspberry-Jalapeño Cornbread was the BEST...but the crumbly texture of the cornbread is sooo bizarre. I kept going back for a bite, even though it wasn't mine, because the sweetness from the raspberry/cornbread and spice from the jalapeño really complimented each other...that texture tho!!! The Thai Peanut came in second, if you want something different. I prefer my Thai Peanut on spring rolls, but hey, it tastes just like the real thing...sweet with a hint of heat. 

The Captains Berry, which was mine, was just ok. I went taste blind after a few licks. I was thinking that with all of their unique combos that it would've had some cereal pieces or fruit but no. 

Scoops during my visit were priced at $2 for Happy Hour vs their normal $2.75 price. One of our scoops (Cookie Roulette...maybe the name says it all) should've been even cheaper than that since it was not a full scoop. The girl scooped the bottom of the bucket and barely eeked out 1/2 a scoop, another flavor should've been recommended or an additional scoop added to make up the difference. 

I was glad that I tried it, you don't find flavors like Garlic Butterscotch or Sweet Potato Casserole everyday, but I prefer the creaminess and consistency of traditional ice cream shops. 

The shop has about 2 tables (if memory serves me) to sit, and besides ice cream they have a deli with a pretty extensive selection from what I saw of ice cream isn't your thing.

Smiling With Hope Pizza gives me hope...hope that there are still wonderful people out there, wonderful people like the Owners Judy and Walter. Walter, who earned his Masters Degree in Special Education, decided upon retirement to open this business to help those with special needs obtain job skills so that they could thrive and live their best life.   

I knew none of those things when I bookmarked this place before I set out on my annual Reno vacation. I wanted to add some new places on my rotation, pizza being a relatively cheap option that could feed a crowd was on that list and 'Smiling With Hope' seemed promising from their rating and pics. 

I almost didn't get to eat here due to their hours, open from 12-2pm and not re-opening again until 5pm just to close again at 8pm, but I managed to squeeze in a visit on my last night and my tummy and heart are so happy that I did. 

I arrived to an empty restaurant which felt a bit odd for a place that had so many reviews. It didn't take long for it to start filling up though and I would soon learn why. My party and I were warmly greeted by Judy, immediately I felt like family. She announced to Walter that we were there, like we had just stepped into their home. The owners along with 2 employees were on hand to help us 

Judy brought menus to our table and asked if we knew how ordering worked (you place your order at the counter and then they bring it to your table). She explained they have two different styles, traditional thin crust and then a deep dish. The thin is a round pizza and the deep dish is cut into squares. 

To start we ordered the garlic knots that I had seen in a lot of the pics. We asked for a side of ranch to dip them in and to my horror...they didn't have any. Ugh, how can you not have ranch for garlic knots??? I soon forgot about the ranch when Judy brought the little pillows of garlicky heaven to the table. Coated with butter, garlic and cheese...there was no need for ranch or any dipping sauce. 

For toppings, Garlic, Basil, Black Olives, Mushrooms, Green Peppers, Sausage, Pepperoni, Onions and Anchovies are all you're going to find here...but in this case less is MORE. 

We watched as Walter  personally hand stretched our dough as well as others while making small talk, hearing stories about him growing up in New Jersey. The aroma in the place was intoxicating as orders started to flood in. 

We ordered 2 pizzas: 12" NY Ricotta & an 18" pepperoni, sausage, green pepper & onion. It was love at first bite. I'm a sauce person, love mustard & ketchup on my fries, A1 on a fancy steak...but lemme tell you, I could eat that NY Ricotta all day. No sauce, just brushed with olive oil and topped with herbs and spices and the creamiest and freshest ricotta. 

The custom 18" was just as wonderful and more than enough for our small group. I kept noticing a little spice with each bite, at first I thought it to be the sausage but soon discovered it was the pepperoni. The veggies are sliced super thin so that they're not crunchy when you bite into the slice. The crust is thin, but does not get soggy...I know because I took leftovers back to my hotel and enjoyed many hours later. 

As we were dining, customers were coming in an out to pick up the or to-go orders. Some a lot of regulars from their convos and some first timers like myself...they were all treated like family. Judy was busy taking orders and helping people carry food to their cars. Their level of of hospitality is rivaled by none. 

Smiling With Hope is now on my permanent bookmark list and I will be back...in the meantime I wish them continued success.

'Wherever there is a human in need, there is an opportunity for kindness and to make a difference.' 

An unexpected act of extreme kindness was just what we experienced when ate at this restaurant. 

You see, we had been in town for a local festival that was cancelled abruptly by the recent virus going around. Having limited activity options, we gave up and came to this area in search for some good food. We had intended to eat at another place, On the Alley, but were unable to because of their seating situation. 

We left 'On the Alley' and had no clue where we would go next. Thats when the girl from On the Alley came running outside and said she would go up to Brophy's and inquire about us eating there. The only problem, in our mind, was access since one member of our group is in a wheelchair and Brophy's is located on the 2nd floor. Initially confused why the girl from On the Alley would go up there, we gave her the benefit of the doubt and waited for her return. 

In a moment that restored my faith in humanity, she returned w/ the Manager of Brophy's who said that she would be opening their downstairs restaurant JUST FOR US!!! That's right, the WHOLE DOWNSTAIRS that was closed to any and all would be opened just for US!!! As I write this I am still in awe of their generosity. I just cannot express how thankful I am...(I'm not crying, you're crying). 

As we settled in, the Manager brought us menus and waters along w/ some warm sourdough bread to start. We all decided on the Fish N Chips and a cup of Chowder, when in Rome...

I'll get to the food in a minute, but I want to shout out the Manager who not only opened up the place for us but who worked her butt off, not just running up and down to the stairs to put our order in, bringing us our food, refills on drinks and bread, worked in vain to try to turn the music on...but that she did ALL of that and with a genuine smile on her face. It really touched my heart. 

Hungry passerby-ers tried stopping in, but she ever so gently let them know that the restaurant downstairs was closed, but that they could dine upstairs. I'm sure they were confused, wondering why were allowed to dine there, but she didn't make it an issue. 

Our food arrived not long after ordering and wow...it was good. My opinion is unrelated to above and beyond service we received. Sure it helps, but had we not been in the situation I know I would've loved it just the same. 

The fish had a VERY light batter, fried to perfection and the fish was flaky w/ NO fishy taste...fresh. It was served w/ poppyseed coleslaw and fries. It comes 3pc to an order but that was just enough. I was able to take 2pcs back to my Hotel that night to enjoy for dinner and had the sauces to dip it in since she went and got us lids for all of the condiments. 

We were just a couple of humans in need, GOD presented an opportunity, and the Managers kindness made ALL of the difference.

I do-nut get the hype. These donuts have to be, by far, my least favorite donuts that come to mind in recent memory. 

I was excited to find a dessert place that was open so late while on my trip, and I loved all of the interesting flavor combos that they have here: Cherry Pie, S'mores, Mint Oreo, Strawberry Cheesecake and the classic Tang. 

I had been craving mint chocolate, but before I got my hopes up I called to see if they even had the Mint Oreo I spied in their pics. Girl on the other line said yes and asked if I'd like them to hold one for me (+1 Star). Loving that flavor combo in general, I said hold 2. 

Got there to an EMPTY store, with a small but decent selection to choose from. Service was not welcoming, they immediately asked ho front how many I was purchasing. Being a first time customer, I was not sure...I wanted to check out the selection first and expressed that. They said they need to know how to box them, being that I was the ONLY customer...how hard would it to be just to set them to the side and then box them when done??? 

Made a few choices after feeling rushed and then took a few snaps. Even made a couple of doodles on their adorable chalk wall. 

Got back to my hotel room and tore into the box, only to be disappointed by all but 1. The Cherry Pie was the best pic, and I usually don't like canned cherry filling. 

The Mint Oreo was a cake donut and it was terribly greasy and dense. The only discernible flavor was GREASE. The Oreo was not fresh and the Mint flavor was weaker than my Grandma. 

I took nibbles off of everyone else's, since mine was garbage. I thought maybe they'd be enjoying their picks, but the looks on their faces and grumbles said it all. The donuts ALL tasted old and greasy as well. The Strawberry Cheesecake had some sort of congealed blob in the middle that was sour and unpleasant. 

We agreed that these donuts were a complete fail taste and freshness wise and will not go back.

'Honey, I know, I know
I know times are changing
It's time we all reach out
For something new, that means you too...

Purple bean, purple bean
Purple bean, purple bean
If you know what I'm singing about up here
C'mon, raise your hand.

You say you want a leader
But you can't seem to make up your mind
I think you better close it
And let me guide you to the purple bean.' 


I reached out for something new while on vacation in Reno when I needed my caffeine fix and it led me to Purple Bean and the rest is Yelp history. 

Their menu is expansive, lots of froo-froo drinks- way more options than any other coffee shop in town and let's not even mention Starbucks (ok, I just did). Warm Apple Pie, Sticky Buns, Cherry Garcia, Snickers, Almond Joy, Hawaiian, Skittles Purplechino (Frapp) just to name a few. 

My favorite drinks, are the Warm Apple Pie and Hawaiian Breve Lattes. All of their drinks taste exactly like their description, but these two were my all time favorite. The WAP tasted like I was eating a slice that had just came out of Grandma's oven. The Hawaiian had equal parts pineapple, coconut and banana, all that was missing was the lei. 

The coffee was really smooth and you could actually taste it, which I've found isn't always the case at some of these types of shops. A lot of times they mask the coffee with all of the syrups and milk, but not here. You don't get the fancy art work, but you get the full bodied flavor in each drink. 

Their Purplechino's, which are their vs of Frapp's, are just as great as their hot drinks. My favorite was their Skittles. They were out of their standard lemon base so they used Cotton Candy which was fine by me cause it all tasted like the rainbow. 

I enjoyed all of their drinks so much so that I came here all but 2 days while I was on my trip. I started a stamp card and on my last day I was able to redeem a free drink. They also have a new featured drink every day of the week at a slightly discounted price. Worth mentioning, they don't only sell coffee but also muffins, cookies and smoothies. 

Only reason I took a star off (really only a 1/2)  is because when I had originally ordered the Skittles drink it came chock full of Skittle pieces blended in, pieces that you could still chew once sucked thru the straw. Another visit, there were no chewable pieces, they were all liquified. Then, I ordered a drink and they had to remake it (it was a different girl from the one who had been making my drinks) because it was absolutely flavorless. 

Employees are super chill and friendly. These girls work their tail ends off, on all of my visits it was only 1 working and they have to tend to inside as well as drive thru orders, but they don't skip a beat.

Ca-jing ca-jing make that cash register ring!!! 

Apparently the name is pronounce codge-ay...or so I was told when I walked up and was greeted by the barista. The whole time I had been pronouncing the 'j' as an 'h.' Anywhoo that's neither here nor there. 

I bookmarked after seeing a SB local post their pics. The featured drinks were unlike any other coffee offerings I have back home, glasses rimmed w/ rose petals and flaming marshmallows to name a few. After sizing up their menu that others were so generous to have posted, I settled on the Yemen...a hot coconut milk mocha, sweetened condensed milk, cacao, and whole milk topped off w/ a flaming marshmallow. What's not to love w/ that combo??? 

What I didn't love was the fact that you CANNOT order any of their 'Signature' drinks to go!!! What are they afraid of, that you're going to take the drink, break down their formula and then re-sell it??? Ok ok, I know it's not that deep, they probably can't do the flaming marshmallow part, due to some liability issue (y'all can thank the McDs coffee lady for that) but the fact that they wouldn't even make the drink w/ just the marshmallow dropped down in it is what really irked my nerves. 

I was told that I could just order a Mocha...really??? That's not what I wanted, but whatever. After a minute of looking the menu over again, I settled on a small hot Vanilla-Caramel Latte. To add insult to injury, the barista proceeds to ring up my order and then asks 'are you ok w/ our $2 cup charge.' So my drink is already costing about $5 and now I have to pay an ADDITIONAL $2 for what they call a 'deposit' in order to get my drink...in a CUP??? I felt like telling them 'f*ck the cup, just pour it in my hands for a dime.' 

In a moment of weakness, and frustration, I caved and paid the stupid fee so that I could get my drink and get on the road.

I enjoyed every mile back to Santa Maria, as I sipped my big ticket beverage. You see, the drink in that moment was worth the hassle and cost. Not worth it enough to visit regularly, I would def explore other options in town, but my drink tasted like I was drinking caramel corn and well that's good enough for me to at least consider a follow up visit in the future.

After having a festival cancelled on our most recent trip, we were hungry so we took to Yelp to find some local but easy eats. In the search criteria I marked 'Wheelchair Access' since a member of our party requires one. On the Alley was one of the first promising leads, so off we went. 

Much to my dismay, their 'Wheelchair Access' is only outside dining. They have a little enclosed area for inclement weather, but it was all taken. The girl at the counter, who had seen us struggling w/ the door and chair-helped hold the door for us, said there were additional tables...but they were uncovered, and w/ it drizzling it was not an option. 

She mentioned another restaurant down the way, but being unfamiliar w/ the area we weren't sure where to go. As we were leaving, she said that she would take us. 

When we arrived to Brophy's, right around the corner, she said she would be right back. She returned w/in a few seconds, with the Manager, who said they would be opening their downstairs restaurant JUST for US!!! 

Wow wow wow...this young lady went ABOVE AND BEYOND to help us out...and for that I will be eternally thankful. After our meal at Brophy's, I returned to give her a tip for doing the unexpected and for blessing us. 

I won't hesitate to return to this location next time for a dose of their warm hospitality, and to eat their delicious looking food.

My review for this place is LONG overdue, and I know it is only going to be a drop in the sea of the 3,240 reviews this place already has. *Note that this place is called the READING terminal market, yet it is pronounce REDDING. 

This Market is nestled between 11th & 12th Ave and Arch Street. There are several entry and exit points, one being right by the Hilton. 

This place is a foodie lovers paradise and overload!!! There is virtually something for EVERY palate. Want something fresh, hot, sweet, creamy, chocolate ears, something loaded with carbs to indulge your senses...they've got you covered here!!!

They have a LARGE produce section filled with an array of healthy options, I didn't spend much time in this section but everything appeared to be in peak freshness/ripeness. 

There is a LARGE selection of fresh meats (steaks, roasts, ribs etc) and what seems to be an even larger selection of mouth watering deli meats to choose from. We are talking stacks of piled high meats ready to be consumed in between two slices of bread, topped on a cracker with a cheese spread (that they have plenty of) or to just snack on a lone. 

If you do not want to make your own sandwich, they got you covered as well. You can walk over to another vendor that sells gut busting sandwiches such as: chicken Caesar, fresh mozzarella, chicken caprese, Pompeii etc. The sandwiches can either be purchase on loaves (better have a big appetite) or a more hand held option like ciabatta. A few steps over and you can purchase one of their ridiculously HUUUUUUUGE philly cheesesteaks, where they prepare the food in front of you. They also put on a show while they make it, which is kind of cool. Don't feel limited to just a traditional cheesesteak, you can get a chicken cheesesteak, pizza cheesesteak, broccoli rabe, BLT cheesesteak and on. You can also choose the cheese, be it provolone, American, or the east coats favorite cheese sauce. 

Next to the philly cheesesteak counter, they have pasta sheets that they will cut to your preference, while you wait for your food. You can pay at the same register. The pasta we purchased was seasonal, Pumpkin Pasta and it was terrific. 

If you meander to the left of the cheesesteak counter, they have a variety of comfort foods ranging from lasagna, spaghetti, Stromboli's, chicken parmigiana, and meatballs. 

Once you have quelled your hunger pangs, head over to their bakery section. There you can load up with cannoli's (filled to order), cheesecakes, torts, individual sliced cakes. Ever wonder what a chocolate shaped foot with almond toes, or Van Gogh's ear tasted like??? The also have a variety of caramel apples, plain, dipped in chocolate AND caramel or overloaded with chocolate chunks, marshmallows and drizzled in peanut butter. 

There are plenty of other delectable delights in this jam packed market, too many to list. Come hungry and with plenty of ambition. You could easily spend hours, if not a whole day here. Lines can be long at times, and some counters require you to take a number. It is worth the wait and weight ;)

Wonderful experience! I've been waiting for this place to open for awhile and couldn't wait to try it! 
They had a really good live band playing last night. The woman singing had a flawless voice! Super cool vibe. 
The bar and the bathrooms are decorated beautifully and very clean. The bathroom had this lotion that I need to go find now. Lol 
We were greeted by the owner. Really courteous gentleman that was very welcoming! We were happy to notice how passionate he was about his business.
Everything on the menu sounded really good so I had a hard time choosing. The tri-tip sandwich was recommended so I went with that. It was delicious! The sauce was a bit spicy so it had a nice kick to it. I loved that it comes with au jus.
Our waitress was also very attentive.
Overall, I would have to say the whole experience was awesome! The best part is I live nearby so I'll definitely be back often to support this genuine local business!

I'm just simply writing this review based on the birthday cake itself that they made for my cousin. I did not order it or deal with the bakery myself. I just wanted to tell you guys how amazing it was! My aunt ordered the Austrian creme cake. The cake was so beautifully decorated with a few raspberries on top. It was very moist and the chocolate wasn't overpowering, it was the perfect amount of sweetness. It was actually very light. The cake was very similar to the Josef Vienna cakes, but even better! We will most likely be ordering different cakes for upcoming occasions.

I'm really bummed to say I wasn't happy with my experience here, because I have been patiently waiting for this place to open. My mom and I ordered the NY Roni, Grandma's Pie, and the Mediterranean Lover salad coming out to like $22. Both pizzas were burned. I do have to say that the pizzas could have probably tasted awesome if they weren't burnt. The salad was wilted and old. Which also could have potentially been great if it was more fresh. Hit or miss, this was definitely a miss. I'm hoping this is just because this place just opened and they need to work out their kinks.

I have been here about 50 times. Ok, maybe not 50, but close! I get the buy one get one coupon with my players card. The prices have gone up a little since I first started coming here, but they are constantly busy and I'm sure all the traffic that they have coming through with the buy one get one they kind of had to up the prices for the integrity of the business. Either way it's still a steal if you have a players card! 
The food is awesome too! I have tried all sorts of things on the menu, but the fajitas have to be my favorite. Can't go wrong with the fajitas! Also, they bring you chips along with mild salsa. I like my salsa more spicy and if you ask they will bring you out a green spicy salsa. The fried ice cream is definitely my recommendation for dessert! It's delicious! 
I love this place and the staff is always so wonderful and friendly. Sometimes when it's very busy there is a bit of a wait, but it's worth it.

Wow. That's all I have to say. My wife and I were visiting from out of town and heard about this place. My only problem is this stuff is addictively good. So I may have to go back again and again.

The cupcakes are so delicious, so sweet, and there's such a variety, I wanted to try them all. I got the peanut butter one and the carrot cake. They were both really good. My wife also got the red velvet cupcake and that was her favorite.

If you're looking for a cute, desert joint with absolutely delicious treats, I HIGHLY recommend. With they had this place here in California.

I'm always skeptical when a place has perfect Yelp reviews - after finally trying this place out - I now know why! This food is amazing. It's incredibly fresh and the flavors are out of this world. The baba ghanoush is some of the best I've ever had. The falafel is great. Can't recommend this place enough!

Lots of GF options.

I've eaten pho in many cities and the options here might be the best value I've encountered. Also, we walked into a restaurant full of Vietnamese diners, and you know they know what's up. This soup is legit!

The food was just as delicious as I suspected. For appetizers we ordered the fried pork egg rolls, shrimp spring rolls, and shredded pork skin rolls. These came out very quickly and tasted incredibly fresh. The pork skin rolls were extra tasty, with their smoky meat, fresh herbs and rice noodles. 

I ordered the #12 - Tái, Gâù, Gân, Bò Viên, which is a combination of eye-round steak, marble brisket, soft tendon and meatball. The marbled brisket was my favorite and had just the right amount of fat in each delectable bite. The little balls of soft tendon were tasty, too! I do wish they provided a bit more fresh basil for me to garnish my soup with, but they more than made up for that with the incredible homemade hot sauce on the table. This complemented the complex broth perfectly and a dollop of it did not make my soup too spicy. I just couldn't seem to slurp it down fast enough!

Pho Kien Giang is a gem in Pinellas Park and rated so highly for good reason. I definitely plan on returning, the next time I'm in the area.

Our meeting didn't start until the afternoon, so we had time to grab a bite.  This place was on our walk to our meeting, so we thought we would give them a shot.

The help was really nice, and our waitress was real helpful.  She got us our drinks quickly and then took our orders.

She returned with the food faster than I thought was possible.  All orders in our group were 100% accurate.  Everybody thought their food was good.

My burger came with bacon, cheese, grilled onions and chips made in house.  $16 will get you that burger.

Will I return?  When I am in the area.

Listen up, Italians. 

I am Italian. I live in the neighborhood. I shop at the Italian Market every week. 

I know you are pretty upset that the Vietnamese moved in and then got more upset when the Mexicans moved in, but let's try to deal, okay?

I prefer to buy my produce from the Mexicans and Vietnamese. You know why? Because they are FRIENDLY--a concept that seems to be lost on many of you. 

Improve your attitudes and give us some service with a smile. It goes a long way. Plus, your produce isn't that awesome. It's good, but not awesome.

And if you don't like working with people, please do us all a favor and get a job that doesn't require you to interact with us. Maybe you can start selling stuff on Ebay from the comfort of your own home.

This is quite possibly the best Chinese restaurant I have ever been to.... 
Reasons why:

1. The food was light... Meaning that the sauces were not ladled in mass amounts onto my food, meaning I wasn't inputting tons of sauce calories into my system. My date and I both had different dishes (myself--the lemon shrimp, Heather H.--black pepper tofu (a great option for vegetarians I might add!)) that weren't swimming in sauce. The vegetables were also FRESH! Every carrot, celery, asparagus, onion, broccoli and pepper made a crunch as I took a bite, which means that the vegetables and my dish were made with the utmost care. Furthermore, the wontons! They weren't fried like other restaurants, but rather seemed to be baked, since they weren't greasy. I accidentally ordered some as an appetizer (8), only to receive 4 more later on in the meal (from both of our entrees). It's okay- I could've gone home and built a fort out of them if I didn't eat them all. :)

2. I fell in love.....with Bubble Tea. I had never tried Boba, and I had made a Resolution this year to try new things people! Furthermore, our server advised me on my tea selections... If I wasn't fond of a particular fruit, etc. then I should stay away from the traditional tea. I went with a Pineapple Green Tea added with Boba, and I'm tempted to draft this review at this moment and drive up to Castleton to go get more. That's how good it was people.

3. Prices! Reasonable... Not only did you receive a plate full of veggies, meat and sauce as your entree, but it also comes with steamed white rice and two crab wontons... PLUS soup! Each of our totals came to $15 for appetizers, entrees, and tea...A cost for deliciousness that was well spent!

4. Clean, quiet, attentive service. I'm tempted with every breath in my being to go back. 

5. FYI- check the hours! We went on a Saturday, and they were only open from 2-10pm.

I am completely appalled by the display of blatant racial discrimination I witnessed at this establishment last night. I was there with my husband's company's work party having a nice time, when all of the sudden an obvious altercation was happening at the bar- voices were raised and a crowd was gathering. A black woman from my group (I did not know her, but she works with my husband) came back to the table with a few others where apparently she had just been verbally attacked by a white woman at the bar. While leaning over the bar to reach for her drink from the bartender, the black woman apparently got too close to the white woman's husband, and the white woman began shrieking at her to get away from her husband. Shocked, the black woman replied- "I'm nowhere near your husband, I'm just getting my drink." and left to come back to our table while the woman continued to scream and gesture wildly, attracting the attention of everyone in the place, including management, who came over to talk to her. 

Several minutes had passed and our group was on to different topics, talking and laughing together when the managers came to our table and demanded to know "Who was involved in the altercation at the bar?" and then told the girl she had to leave, despite the fact that she hadn't done anything. Other people in our group instantly started taking up for her, insisting that she hadn't done anything to provoke the crazy woman at the bar, which we had all witnessed. Despite that, they told her she had to leave and she did, even though everyone else in our group was trying to convince the managers to let her stay. After one person asked why the couple at the bar didn't seem to be leaving, one manager replied: "They're leaving too. Our policy is that anyone involved in a fight has to leave." So the girl left and we stayed behind, still arguing that the couple at the bar was not leaving. 

After about 20 minutes of this, it not only became apparent that not only had they kicked out the black girl without even finding out from the countless witnesses what had happened, but they let the white couple stay and GAVE THEM FREE NACHOS! 

I also find it interesting that soon after mall security showed up- in the form of a retired black cop- the white couple was finally told they had to leave as well. The woman then stood up, swung her coat in the air angrily and shouted "God help her if I see her in the parking lot-" (then turned to glare at us) "Or any of her little friends!!!" Yeah. I think it was obvious the completely calm black girl was at fault here.

I'm so disgusted by how all this went down, and even if you take the racial discrimination factor out of the situation, management handled the whole thing poorly and acted like assholes to us when there was no need for it. Especially since my husband's company had just shelled out a small fortune to have their holiday party there, and management couldn't even hear them out. Revolting. We will not be going here again, and I highly doubt anyone in our group will be. If I were management at this Dave & Busters, I would be seriously scared about the backlash that this incident will cause when corporate starts getting all the outraged phone calls.

From one of the best chefs I have experienced, the food at K-Paul's  is fantastic, overtly yet genuinely Cajun.  Theres no other version of this cuisine can challenge the authenticity of the food at K-Pauls. And rightfully so, most of the recipes here were from the chef's long standing family traditions and cooking strategies.  The ambience? Casual, not chic, not formal like the grand dining establishments in  NOLA, yet you dine on tablecloth,  with whimsical Cajun recipes on paper.  Once you sit down, you are treated to genuinely attentive staff, deliciously unique flavors, you leave thinking you've got to plan your next trip back.

For this recent trip to NOLA,  I had to honor Paul Prudhomme with the dishes he's made that to me, were uniquely K-Pauls:

1.  Chicken/Andouille gumbo.  The gumbo here is peasant style, the roux darkened close to mahogany, and to brag about this serving, my small cup was loaded with chicken and  home made sausage, in this rich dark gumbo broth.  Can't have this anywhere.  This version is distinctly different from any gumbo I've sampled in the city and oh so soo good. 

2.  Blackened Twin filets (well only one requested this time) in debris sauce.  I loved the largesse to the plates at K-Pauls, and this dish proved distinctly Paul Prudhomme.  You don't get one filet mignon, you get 2;  the filet deliciously blackened with a developed debris sauce,  you'd swear you've had nothin' like it.  No steak knife provided here  for when I cut into the steak with my butter knife, I was treated to  the smoothest cut of a tender medium rare filet of beef.  You swipe that bite with the debris sauce and this combo was 2die4.  An Orin-Swift Zinfandel totally sent this dish to the clouds for me.

3.  K-Paul's version of Bread pudding with Hard sauce.  The bread generously seasoned with spices and custard only a Louisiana Creole can concoct.  It came baked in  a small ramekin, with a supremely delectable hard sauce (the liquor present to the taste buds but oh so complementary).  I am in love with this version.    I loved it so much I took another togo.


Paul Prudhomme passed away October 2015.   You are missed.   You've changed our dining landscape and planted Cajun cuisine on the world's culinary road map.  

I love this place and the people who work here.  For there is no other resto in this U.S. of A where one can say, "I've dined in an authentic Cajun restaurant where the food was made with lots of love." 


Visits:  More than 10, maybe 15

Tip:  The wine list is amazingly well put together with a nice range of French and California wines.  Be prepared, entrées are not skimpy and  can be shared with 2 people.    They make a really good, on point Sazerac here.  The blackened drum (fish) is famous here.  The bread basket is also famous:  you get different kinds of Cajun inspired breads with delicious butter.    If you don't have reservations and you don't mind the wait, they will not turn you away.

The restaurant was my dinner treat in NOLA and indeed it is a restaurant for a special occasion or every chance if you've got the gumption.  It is set in an opulent space, in the Sonesta Hotel.  The environment is so grand you feel as though you are eating in some palace with lots of butler looking wait staff who are attentive and obsessed with cleaning your table. The bar area is comfy and can be a hangout.  It is a dressy place but no fret,  a collared shirt and jeans with appropriate shoes won't make you feel out of place. For the ladies, well you don't need to be told, you know.  

First I was offered delicious amuse with bacon  flavors, bread with sugarcane seed butter, salt 

Louisiana Snapping Turtle Soup--  I loved the distinctiveness of this version, so different from Commanders, Arnauds and Omni's, my faves versions, but scrummy.  It had bold flavors of nutmeg and clove, the madeira was already in the soup as opposed to served bowl-side. I enjoyed this dish very much.   

Oysters R'evolution (with 3 sauces)--   This raw dish was very good but I didn't expect to get dino oysters.  I should have ordered smaller sized oysters as I prefer those.  I really loved the sauces made here.  The mignonette was really simple yet distinctive. 

Crab Beignets (4 remoulade sauces)--  This dish was beautiful and rich.  If you enjoy deep fried crab fritters, this is your dish. No scrimping on the crab, these were crispy balls of crabness dotting 4 to a plate.   It came with 4 sauces, the saffron remoulade being my favorite.  

Short Ribs (Tramonto's grandmother's recipe that he takes to all his restos).  This dish was sublime, a piece of deliciously cut short rib (sans bone), looking like a large brownie,  with a very interesting yet flavorful grapefruit sauce that sent me to a different planet.  Bite after bite, you understood how this recipe needs to live forever.  The dish is perfect.  2die4.   My photo died on the upload to Yelp servers but you can see other photos on Yelp of this geniusly executed dish.

Smores Soufflé--  20 minutes to order.  I like smores and this dessert is good, well balanced, served warm.  I would have liked to have been served a soufflé out of the oven with a 5 min wait not 20.

Dessert sampler-  This was a plate of teaser sweets that on some tables were served in a jewelry box

The dishes I sampled here are unique, bold and daring.  Yet whatever they did, it worked for me.   Loved it.  Coming back to try other items.

Visits:  1

Tip:  Early reservations are easy.  Dinner hour reservations take weeks to secure. The wine list is extensive and superb.   The gracious sommelier showed me her oldest bottle of sherry in the 1800s.  Want to try that next time.

Louisiana fried chicken is some of the best in the country.  Why Popeyes started in Arabi, Louisiana.  Fried chicken is serious in New Orleans.  While super hot Nashville fried chicken is pervasive these days, IMHO, fried chicken in NOLA is my fave.  I have been to 20 highly rated fried chicken joints in NOLA and hands down Li'l Dizzy's is the most delicious and perfect fried chicken I've ever had. It is lightly crunchy, garlicky, juicy chicken;  a couple of  drops of Louisiana hot sauce and I am  in fried chicken nirvana.  

Other dishes that are exceptional here? The seafood gumbo (light roux, with blue crab, two kinds of sausage and shrimp) is unbelievable as I've noted in past reviews.   The burnt ends of the bread pudding here is to die for too. The shrimp and grits is soulful. And, the rolls are everythang. Lol. I can keep going. 

Today I had what the owner, Wayne Baquet, calls bunk beans for the first time.  Cooked with shrimp, mild spices, it spoke of generations of tradition and love of Creole flavors and tightly held family secrets.  It was soo tasty and delicious, I ate three portions of this superbly made dish.  

Service is full of love and efficiency.
