Best of all,  the dishes described here (except for the  shrimp and grits) are part of THE famous buffet at $15.99 from 11a to 2pm.  Insane price for a SMH amazing meal. 

Visits: many

Tip:  Located in a neighborhood north of the French Quarter, this small family owned restaurant is open until 2pm daily. Breakfast is served also.

I love this place, its dark hallways, sexy vibe and comfy beds and rooms.  Love the capiz shell globes outside the reception area and gives guests warm dim light at night.   It's a W which is good.   I've come to appreciate how the W (Starwood/Sheraton) can take original old buildings and transform them to sensual environments.  I'm not a snob by any means but the artistry of W designers let loose on old buildings is to be admired.  They've done this really well in NYC also.  The Kimpton Group tries to unseat the W but Kimpton spaces look "put-together"  I must say the modern W Hotels are just ok, im getting tired of modern minimalist spaces these days  .  It's the old buildings transformed to a W "vibe" that makes it worth it for me.  

The W French Quarter  has so many nooks and crannies, different room layouts,  it lures one into coming back.    It's also a more intimate W than the larger ultra modern one on Poydras.    It's location is nondescript, in the Quarter,  down the street from one of my favorite restaurants, K-Paul's, and on my favorite street Chartres.  OK, OK,  it is my favorite hotel in NOLA, LOL.  It's just far enough away from the Bourbon St promenade  but close enough to partay when you are in the mood!    Get a room with a balcony if you are there during spring for the Jazz festival or in the winter.    I dont ever make it to Nawlins during Mardi Gras and I dont want to, LOL.   Nuff said.  

Note:  I give this business one less star because sometimes the staff have an affect,  as though you owe them the world during checkin.  I think the higher the price the more respectful the staff should be,  but Whatev..... being tactful & respectful here, I usually get what I want... smiles.

I've visited  NOLA classic restaurants in past trips, Galatoire, Arnaud, Emeril's (Delmonico and NOLA), Antoine's, Commander's Palace,  K-Pauls, Brennan's.  I wanted to try different restaurants this time as I'm sure there is a plethora in this food mecca.  Shannon, my friend thank you for your lists.  

So what was it like here?   It was like dining in an English salon or at Antoine's, antique tables and lighting fixtures surrounding you, its  a beautiful setting without the stodgyness or seriousness of a high-end NOLA restaurant.  The difference is the minute you sit down you are embraced with service-- attentive and friendly. 

I love NOLA.  New Orleans to me  is about supreme enjoyment of food one encounters nowhere else in our country. This restaurant embodies the paradox of New Orleans, classic and old yet bold and daring.  I love Nawlins for these reasons, its a classic Euro-American city but enjoys life and food immensely.    Back to the restaurant,    the vibe here is formal/casual.  I was welcomed by my waiter Erick and his backup Mareike.  Nice I get two wait staff but the prices to the menu were fair.   A Sazerac began my meal.  Always wanted one and voila it was on the menu. Erick explained the menu, the half bottles wine list and the Reveillon menu.  Considering the attention I'm getting and the Sazerac which appeared forthwith, downing this interesting drink  for the first time told me I had nothing else to worry about.  My waiter recommended a Reveillon dinner, prix fixe and came with 4 courses for a decent price.   I have a paranoia for prix fixe, from traveling in Europe, prix fixe to me means rip off the tourist  (especially in France and Italy).  Until I was told more about what Reveillon meant and that most  restaurants (its a X'mas/New Year's dinner NOLA style) have  Reveillon dinners did i relent.    A short description of a Reveillon dinner followed in the menu, the history and how it came about--- well DAMN sign me up!

This Reveillon was 4 courses for a good price and I proceeded to make my choices out of the selections on the menu.   First the bread came, warm and room temperature salted butter!!   I am happy.  First Course:  Crab Napoleon. Two pieces  of  panko crusted eggplant with  crab meat  in between. Amazing  .  A butter leaf salade with Gorgonzola and poached pears followed next.  Well made but the dressing was a tad subtle.   Then the filet came. I had ordered a Malbec to go with it. The filet came with the creamiest potatoes unctuous,  almost like a sauce in places and like very good mashed potatoes towards the center.  Strange concept  but very very good . On top was an 8 oz perfectly grilled medium rare filet with  nicely crusted Parmesan  cheese chip with mushrooms on top of garlicky spinach (stress on garlicky). The creamy potatoes and the meat were such an impressive pair, I kept eating them together.   I couldn't stop eating everything on my plate.   I was most impressed that each component on the plate had flavor:  i was expecting steamed/sauteed spinach and restaurant style mashed potatoes.  The Chef here made this Reveillon meal stand out and the people eating it like me felt special and served well.    I was soo full from this course,  I asked to take my dessert to go. 

My waitpersons  Erick  and  Mareike,   his warm attentive backup,  were checking up on me throughout the dinner.  Little did they know I was gonna write them up, LOL.  Thanks for the attentive service, both of you were stellar, thank you.  

In sum, a dinner here does not come with pomp  and ceremony as old Nola standards like Arnaud or Galatoire or Antoine.   While the food at these NOLA classics is superior,  so it is at Muriel's also.    One difference  is this restie wants to meet your expectations and anticipate your having to ask for something.   I adored the entire experience at  this restaurant.

Thank  you very much Shannon, for your recs on New Orleans.  They are on point and I'm trying lots of your restaurants while I'm here.  

Update:  So around midnight, I finally dug into the dessert.  Erick gave me not one but two squares of this killer Pain Perdu bread pudding with crushed pecans in this exquisitely buttery praline sauce.  I ate it all, LOL.  Im not a dessert person really.............right!

Away from the restaurants in the Quarter and situated on a narrow street in an old New Orleans neighborhood, Gautreau's is a small and intimate (for date nights) restaurant mostly.  Though I saw a family of six dine here ---so not strictly for dates or proposals.  Reservations are sought after because of its limited number of tables. 

I experienced one meal here and found the food to be very good, the service impeccable, and the owner checks in on each table to ensure that diners are content and happy.   

Would love to come back next time I'm in town. 

Tip:  The wine and cocktails lists are noteworthy.  It's an Uber ride from the Quarter/downtown

Food is good even though it is lacking consistency. Bakery section is really good. Here are my reasons why I am giving only two stars. Honestly this place deserves better rating other than the reasons mentioned below.
There is a bald guy with spectacles (glasses) and moustache who is at the counter most of the time. He is not at all good dealing with the customers.
Crappy attitude, dont answer the questions properly, arrogant, was not even interested in billing the customer when the customer offered to pay for the food ordered.
The worst part is the baldy was chatting with the other folks who work there and forgot to hand over the food to the customer even though the food was ready to be given for a long time. I had to go over the counter and ask for my order repeatedly.
No customer wants to spend money to get this kind of service.

Hope I dont have to deal with this idiot again if I go to this place again. All the other folks who work there are nice.

i love ramen, and this is by far some of the best ramen I've had in a long time. I came in during the week, and it was pretty quiet. They have a counter you can sit at or the usual tables. Parking is easy as they have a small lot, but if the lot is full, I can totally see parking being a hassle. Now, back to the ramen..

The broth...oh my god. So perfect. I could not find one fault with it. It was perfectly salty and flavorful. Then the noodles, so chewy!!! I love a chewier noodle, so if you prefer softer noodles, I would tell them when you order.  

Overall, I am so so happy I found this place. I will be a regular!!

When I say I LOVE Fresh Kitchen, I mean I LOVE it. Fresh Kitchen has a Chipotle style of ordering, and their locations have cute indoor and outdoor seating. I love how food accommodating FK is, and they really have something for everyone! Whether you're gluten free or have a certain diet, they have something for you, and it's ALL delicious. 

I highly recommend trying different things each time you visit to find what your perfect order is. 

My go to order here is: 6 bowl with double coconut rice, broccoli, tri colored potatoes, bbq chicken, citrus chicken, coconut sriracha sauce, white ginger sauce. The 6 bowl is a lot of food, so I always have leftovers! 

Also, I've had an amazing experience with all the employees at all the locations, but this location had the sweetest team! They were all friendly and welcoming.

WOW, is all I have to say. Some of the BEST breakfast I have had in a really long time. I came in on a weekend around 11:30 & the place was still pretty full. Although, there was no wait for a table. The parking was easy as there was a decent sized parking lot. The service was friendly and quick! The food:

Choco choco waffle: 5/5, would highly recommend if you can't decide between savory and sweet. It's the perfect balance between your typical sweet breakfast (half a waffle) and the typical savory breakfast (eggs, potatoes, and sausage/bacon). The waffle was soft on the inside and slightly crunchy on the outside. The strawberries were fresh & sweet. Loved, loved, loved the breakfast potatoes! 

Crepe: 5/5, amazing crepe! It was huge! The crepe was cooked perfectly & I loved the wide options of sweet and savory crepes. 

Service: 5/5, unfortunately I don't remember the name of our server, but she was so sweet! She was friendly and attentive. 

I cannot wait to go back here. Amazing, amazing place!

Excellent choice for out-of-towners looking for a great catfish meal! 

Hubs and I came out to Nashville for his dental school interview and really...really...really wanted catfish. We tried someplace downtown but the place was jam packed and the downtown streets was way too narrow and crowded for me. Buds was actually our second choice. It had to have been around 7pm when we got there...please don't hate me for this comment...but I was nervous with all this talk about racism in the south...it was just uncomfortable for a bit. I was actually much more nervous for my husband than myself...but THANKFULLY I had absolutely nothing to worry about!!! 
     We were seated within 15 mins and our waitress was Mekay. She was awesome! Super nice and emits southern hospitality through and through! We ordered the catfish plates and while we waited we had bowls and plates of pickles, hush puppies, onions and such placed in front of us. We weren't exactly sure what was going on and we didn't order this...but Mekay explained that these sides were free and all you can eat when you order meals!!! FREE FOOD?!? sounds good to me! (Our favorite were the beans) The catfish was delightfully most and flavorful and we ordered banana pudding that was served with a smile! Literally...it was served with a whipped cream smile. Too cute and so tasty! 
     After all our doubts we came to absolutely LOVE this restaurant! Mekay you are wonderful and we are so thankful to have you as our server! 
     Uncle Bud's...we will be coming back to see you again real soon!!! Hubs got his acceptance letter to Meharry Dental School so we will be regulars for at least 4 years

I will keep this brief but thorough. Cocktails - lovely and inventive (had the opportunity to taste a handful of them as our group all ordered something different). Atmosphere - perfect for the vibe they are trying to achieve - reminiscent of saloon, upscale enough to feel like you are actually going out, but relaxed enough to show up in jeans. Service - absolutely fabulous. Give them a try!

I usually don't review a place after only one visit so I can provide a more fair assessment; however, that's my rule and I'm comfortable breaking in now and again (and probably start with this same disclaimer). Sotto came in under the radar (at least under my radar) and is in a semi-secret location (all but tucked under the Walnut Street Bridge at 24th), so I feel like I want to give it a little well-deserved attention.

My GF and I caught a glimpse of Sotto while traversing aforementioned bridge. Not sure how or we spotted it. I wouldn't be surprised if we're developing a 6th new restaurant sense. We saw that it is a new Italian restaurant and were intrigued. We decided to try it for lunch and were both impressed.

We had an appetizer of roasted red peppers (with a nice coating of olive oil, garlic and herbs) and mozzarella and provolone. We followed that with a focaccia covered with tomatoes, mozzarella and prosciutto. Nothing fancy, but nicely prepared.

The lunch menu has a variety of pasta dishes, paninis, and pizzas, all reasonably priced.

Let me just preface this review by saying that I actually did come here. I'm not one of those people who post a bad review because of their recent publicity spectacle. The whole tipping thing? We'll never know what really happened since McCoy is not bothering with any sort of rebuking. All we know is Tommy Up's (store owner) story. So, on to the review.

I came here about a month ago while in town for a conference. After roaming around for two days hunting for Philly cheesesteak, a burger was a welcomed change for me.

Unfortunately, it appears to me that PYT committed the cardinal sin of pressing burger patties while cooking them. I sincerely hope that this is not how they treat all their burgers.  Sure, I showed up during peak meal time and the place looked pretty busy (though there was no line), that still does not excuse any cook from pressing down on their patties to make them cook faster but lose all the juice in the process. Maybe they were in too much of a hurry to get the orders out? I don't know. But the result of their pressing? What would have otherwise been a fine burger ended up with the thickness of something slightly thicker than a Whopper, but thinner than 5 Guys. Maybe it's just slightly below Red Robin's. The meat may have been high quality, but I wouldn't know since the pattie was dry. I didn't go back to see if this is how they consistently treat their burgers, but this is how things appeared to me on my visit.

The fries were nothing to write home about. Standard stuff that didn't look freshly cut. Similarly, their pickles were straight from a jar.

All in all, a completely forgettable experience. Luckily, I still tipped the standard 20% despite the utterly bare-bones service to avoid getting trolled in social media.
I go here at least once a week.  The black bean burger is my go to.  Always loving the special sauces. Great service and food!

This is a restaurant with a severe identity crisis. It aspires to be an upscale steak house among the dozens of seafood joints that dot the landscape of this resort community, but it's tucked away in a Marriott and, aside from a wall of windows affording a spectacular view, is cursed with a decor that betrays its mid-priced hotel dining room roots. It's slightly better than the faux-Western atmosphere most venues of this type embrace, but it's a long way from being elegant enough to justify pricing steaks - which are served with a simple salad but no sides - at $26 to $38. Besides, this isn't South Beach - neither the tot-toting tourists who flock here nor the seniors who comprise a large percentage of the local population are likely to part with bucks this big for a single meal. Although we had come for beef, we opted for more reasonably priced crab cakes - moist and mercifully light on the breading - with snow peas, and lobster with pasta in a saffron-infused lemon-cream sauce, and both were delectable. Still, while there's nothing offensive about the ambiance, it's not enough to lure us back . . . and certainly not for a $31 ribeye. If I'm going to pay that kind of money, I expect - at the very least - a server who's more of a cultured Jeeves than a kiss-my-grits Flo.

In his roundup of the best Tampa Bay dining spots of 2005, the food critic for the St. Petersburg Times cited this place as having the Crust Most Likely to Make the National Register of Historic Pizzas, which lead us to give it a try. Suffice it to say I won't be trusting any of his other recommendations or future reviews. Housed in a nondescript brick building nearly lost among the body shops that surround it, this joint has been making pies for some fifty years, apparently for a lot of very non-discriminating palates. The cracker-thin crust, with the texture and taste of a stale matzoh, was barely covered with a thin layer of odd-tasting sauce and a very skimpy sprinkling of cheese. The only award I'd give it is the Pizza Most Likely to Make a Grown New York Italian Weep.

Can not...

...write.

Too...

...weak

Lapsing into... food... coma...

4.75 Stars.
OMG - Have you ever had a meal that was such a calorie bomb that you literally felt all of the blood rush to your stomach to try and equalize what was happening in your system?

I seriously feel weak from my anniversary dinner at Union Trust.
Dh & I had a very romantic, dimly-lit, 5-star service (Fabian, you ROCK!), unforgettable meal here tonight.

I may need days to recover.

We started with cocktails/wine.  I had the Flyin' Hawaiian and with what little I normally drink (Being the Empress of the Arnold Palmer and all), after a few sips I was nicely buzzed and after one I was flyin'.  (2 might make me crash land.)

Once the buzz was on, out came our delectable apps.  A very good lobster bisque for DH and an icy-chilled crab cocktail perfection for me (better than Parc!).

We each had massive slabs of cow-on-a-plate.
He had the ancho-rubbed strip, garnished with salty (a bit too salty for me) finely-julienned frites.  I had a perfectly cooked cowboy ribeye (so huge I took over half of it home - and, I should mention DH took about 40% of his home.)  My major complaint (which nearly cost them a star) was the crust of the ribeye was WAY salty.  Not Arizona-desert salty, not inedibly salty - but noticably biting with salt.  Dommage!

Meanwhile the spectacular (and for $9 - $11 a pop they outta be) sides saved the meal.  Mac 'n cheese was enough for 4 people (again, half came home - which our kid will appreciate).  The crispy top gave way to bubbling, hot, melty-cheesey-creamy-yet-tender (not at all flabby) elbows.  (I had been expecting shells based on other yelp reviews - but got elbows.)

I love mac 'n cheese and the mac here is worthy!!!!  So good.

A platter of donut-like sweet, tender Onion rings - battered to perfection and (the only thing?) NOT salty.  Wonderful.  I lterally ate 1/2 of one ring and was satisfied.

DH also got a $3.00 dish of caramelized onions to go with his steak.  Not needed - but so tasty - with a light balsamic/demi sweetness to them.

The floor manager, our server (Fabian) and "bus" Valetin, were all on point with the service.  truly excellent.

Dessert (Come on now!  We have come this far - why not just succumb to the madness) was an I.V. of lipitor.

No, seriously - dessert DH had the s'mores (which did, in fact, look like a marshmallow-meringue hedgehog) atop a scoop of house-made peanut butter cup gelato.  The even wrote "Happy Anniversary" on the plate.  And put a little candle on it. Cute.

I had a latte (delicous Saxby coffee - not Peregrine, but fairly good stuff) with a few spoonfuls of Frangelico in it.

Basically everything - with the disappointing exception of the overly salted crust of the Cowboy rideye - was top-notch.

We hope to return again in about a year.
It'll take that long to recover my arterial walls.

Alcohol, caffeine, salt, fat and sugar.
A dietary disaster - but oh, so much fun.

back...

...to the sofa.

I feel a pleasant numbness coming on in my left arm.

Sally and Ronnie were our servers again and they KNOW what they are doing.

We had exemplary services and top tier food and beverage from the moment we walked in and enjoyed beverages at the bar (Frose all day! Plus pints of Guiness for the dudes) to the time we were seated in the main dining room. 

Seafood Wedge is delightfully simple and well executed.
Do not miss the perfectly tender seared scallops.  WOW!

My friend was celebrating a special birthday (30 again??) so they brought out a dish of white chocolate house-made (and so thick and rich) ice cream with "Happy Birthday" written on the plate in chocolate. 
An elegant touch and a surprise for the birthday boy.

I highly recommend Blue Bell Inn for any special occasion, corporate dinner or fancy date night.

This is a review for one of the many Nina's waffles & ice cream trucks.  Our company paid for the truck to come out to our facility in Plymouth Meeting, PA for about 2 hours on a hot summer afternoon.

Each employee had a choice of a waffle and/or ice cream or a waffle cone with ice cream.  Many toppings were available.  I chose the waffle (fresh, hot, liege style) with home-made espresso crunch ice cream and a drizzle of chocolate ganache.

The man who made them (fresh - to order) was lovely as well.

WONDERFUL and indulgent treat.

A great idea for a corporate event or large party - rent the waffle truck!

Walked in and waited.
And waited.
And waited.

12:30pm  on a Wednesday.  Busy dining room.
Not a hostess in sight.

Got a head nod from a busy waiter in the back but was unsure what it meant.
Waited some more.


Walked out.

WTF???

This review is based on service.  I had no chance to be greeted, seated or "eated".

Sad.

Horrible service, filthy bathrooms, mediocre food and just not worth it in any way.

Perhaps I should give them 1 star but the side order of brussels sprouts was good.

That ladies room was so nasty - they floors were awful and 2 toilets were clogged.

Yick.

I have lost my appetitie.

I contacted Pitruco about hosting a private event.  They were responsive and wonderful.  While my budget won't support it right now ($750 minimum for about 50 people at $15 per person), I will definitely consider them for future events. (The event I am having is for about 20-25 people only.)

If you are having a big graduation party or family reunion, it'd be so cool to have the Pitruco truck roll up and crank out fresh pies for your guests.

A gal's gotta dream...
Maybe some day Pitruco will come rolling up to MY driveway.

Cathy, our sassy server, was a delight.  She is a pro and has been here for about 6 years.  We sat in their outdoor "Covid Tent" on a busy Sunday morning at 11.  We got a table for 4 right away and juice/coffee/tea.

The eggs Florentine are terrific but they come with cheese.  Next time I will skip it and also get the copious amount of hollandaise sauce on the side.  A calorie/fat bomb for sure.  Too about 1/3 of it home.

Now I need a nap...

I'd skip Geno's and walk around the corner to Pat's - or better yet - go to Jim's.
Or Tony Luke's.
Or Pastificio's for the real deal.

Let me just add that I am NOT a cheessteak eater - I get a Chicken Cheesesteak 'wit Provolone and 'shrooms once or twice a year.

Geno's is filthy and to quote below - the owner is a racially prejudiced "ass clown".

I am so saddened and frankly I am angry.  
You know what - scratch the saddened.

I am angry.

In fact - I am mad as hell.

DH & I decided to have a late lunch (It was about 3:20) on a sunny Saturday afternoon and meandered into PYT.  There were about 5 clad-in-black young folk at the the hostess stand and before we were seated they said "cash only" (thank goodness they warned us - apparently the credit card machines were down).  This did not affect us - but the two tables near us had to write checks which were reluctantly accepted.

Things went from bad to worse once we were seated.

It was taking a long time to get out food (I ordered the PYT EAT BLT, DH ordered a double burger.).  Our male server came by (as if to ask "so, how is everything?") and I said, - any idea when our food will arrive?  He said "It will be here soon" and scurried away (I would bet money to quickly enter the order that I bet was never placed.)

15 minutes later a DIFFERENT male server plopped down the 2 plates and zipped off.

No cutlery, no napkins.

I called after him - no luck.  So I got up and followed him for a few feet and he turned around, apologized and got us some silverware.

OK, so we're eating - and then we see the table tent that says "A 20% gratuity will be added to your bill" (or something like that.

Well - we're a party of 2 (not 6 or more).  And we sure as hell don;t want to give them 20%.  

But wait - it gets worse.  So I'm eating the BLT and there's no avocado on it (which there is supposed to be per the brunch menu).  I'm hungry and I'm not bothered much - but they charge $2.00 to put avo on a burger - so I would like them to not charge me for it on my avocado-less BLT.

So the first male server comes over and assures me that I will not be charged for the avo and offered to bring a side of it - but I don't want it now (I am 1/2 way through the meal.).

So we finish eating - and we ask for a check.

And we wait.

And wait.

And we're pissed.

Nobody ever comes.

So we estimate our bill (sans 20% assholes!!!) and leave the cash on the table and walk the F out.  The ladies at the table next to us (who had the personal check fiasco) said it best.  "Because they are guaranteed a 20% tip for EVERY table - there is no incentive for good service."

I will never, ever, ever go back to PYT.
I was looking forward to the McThrill-made-famous Milkshakes, too.

The BLT was fine - very good.  Dh said the burger was fine.
The service (and loud, pumping, headache inducing music - we heard a club-mix of Dolly Parton's 9 to 5) is just freakin AWFUL!!!!!

Such an epic service-related fail.

5 stars for service from Emily (and the male manager and a pink-haired server who's name I did not catch).

Emily served our group of 9 ladies for a long-awaited and long-planned Happy Hour.

We got a large table (a few tables pushed together) in the back and ordered apps to share (delicious fried Brussel's sprouts and thick-cut sweet potato fries with 2 delectable dipping sauces - try the vanilla sauce).

Folks ordered their own drinks and dinners - but 4 of us had the pan-seared scallops with a creamy risotto.  DIVINE.

Our only complaint?  The $15 nachos (close to $20 if you want chicken) used to be an enormous platter - not anymore.   The nachos are still wonderful but you get much less - plenty for 3 people - but not for 9.

The 5 stars goes for the tremendous service including separate checks and rushing in a happy hour order (Iron Hill's Happy Hour drink specials end at 6 PM!!!!) for us.

So glad I planned my Ladies Night Happy Hour here.

Worse and worse every time we come.
The firt time we had a great 4 star experience.  This last time?  Not so much.

And do NOT get take out here.  No beverages to go (other than sugar-laden Mexican Sodas).  No Diet Coke.  No take out cups.  Bottled water (IF they have it) is $2.25 per bottle.

Plus they got my order wrong - and I called 45 minutes before I needed it.

They are clearly not well equipped for take out.

We had a corporate pizza lunch for about 40 people and brought in Anthony's salad and 15 pies including a very good Margarita pie, meatballs with roasted peppers and of course pepperoni.

They also had a cauliflower crust pie which disappeared so quickly that I did not get a chance to try it.

While I am not a big pizza fan, Anthony's is quite good. A nice alternative to the ubiquitous sandwich trays we usually get for catered lunches.

Good job!

Came here for my birthday dinner - just me and the husband (DH) - and poissoned myself on fresh sashimi (appetizer), Tuna Tartare (a bit oversuaced - heavy on the ponzu, but still tasty) and a delicious Salmon Belly, Cucumber hand roll.

Lovely food, decent enough service.
Best sushi around for the price (cheaper than Teikoku or Azie, closer than Sushi Nami).

Haven't been to Devil's Alley in years (try 5 or 6 of them) but stopped in for lunch on a not-so-busy Friday (It was 11:50 AM - so the rush had not yet hit) and had a great, basic cobb salad (I subbed Salmon for pulled Chicken) and it was terrific. 

The Honey Mustard and Blue Cheese dressings (I sampled both!) are very good and the lettuce was fresh and crunchy.

Service from the hostess (Alyssa/Alicia??) was outstanding, too.  She is young but been in restaurants for 7 years.  So kind.

We'll be back - and in less than 6 years, too.

Devil's Alley is still a good choice - even after all this time.
Keep it up!

This was my 4th or 5th visit to Harvest over the years and I still like it.  It's a bit steep on the prices for the amount of food but every plate is under 500 calories (unless noted otherwise) so you get the right amount of food.

I had the summer menu for lunch with a delicious Tuna tartar and a Crab/Shrimp cocktail.  All the seafood was fresh tasting and nicely plated and garnished. My friend had a cedar-planked salmon which looked terrific.  Salads here are always fresh.

A $6 cappuccino (ouch) was my dessert.

Very lovely place for a corporate lunch or a date night or girl's night out.

Had a nice evening here - but had to beg for veggies instead of chips (trying to watch carbs) for the $7 pico 'n chips.  They eventually oblidges with delicious cucumber, celery and carrot sticks.  PERFECT!

I wish you'd offer veggies on the menu as a sub for chips - I'd be willing to pay $2 - $3 extra for it.

But man, that pico (avocado chunks in pico de gallo) is terrific.

Great service.

Honestly - the food was exquisite my last time to Zama (in June 2017) with a colleague for a $100 (no alcohol, no dessert) lunch.  Sushi, salads, appetizers, all sorts of wonderful fish.

Delightful.

Every bite was perfection.

Wish I could afford to dine here more often.

3 star service (Danny is terrific but the food came out rather slowly and we were on lunch break)
4 star food - upscale "gastropub" type bar food.

I had been wanting to try Roots, and my group of 5 coworkers came for lunch - we only had an hour and lunch took easily 85 minutes.  Next time we will advise the staff that we are on a tighter time frame.

3 of the crew had burgers and they looked terrific with any toppings you could want - cheddar, bacon, fried (a little over cooked for my liking) egg.

I had the $10 lunch special of French Onion Soup ($6 on its own!) and a 1/2 sandwich (I chose the Chicken, Avocado and Pork Belly panini - yes, please!).  Both were scrumptious - albeit caloric.  Best of all?  The French Onion was not overly salted.  It was perfect.

I will return - but not on a day when I have a 1 PM meeting!
Great selection of beers - and a full bar ('natch!)

Omg! Came back to Shiroi after nearly 7 years and they treated us like celebrities.  The tuna lovers plate ($42, includes 2 pieces of chu-toro), naked tuna on crispy rice, oshi-tashi with bonito and succulent salmon tartar were all sheer perfection.

Swimmingly fresh.

Fabulous service, nothing "shi-shi" or hipster or fancy, just amazingly good sashimi, nigiri and maki.

We love you and sister-restaurant Doma, too.

Run, don't walk, to Shiroi Hana today!

5 star food and 3 or 4 star service for this update on Peter Mac's delightful La Porta on route 352 in Media.

Ate here for the first time in over a year and the late spring/summer menu is wonderful with crisp salads, pizzas, pasta and rich, flavorful entrees.

My pork cutlet stack with fresh mozz, spinach and peppers was so delicious and a generous portion.  I took about 1/3 home and enjoyed it the next day.

The bar was hoppin' on a Monday night and my Cranberry Moscow Mule was served icy-cold in the requisite copper mug.  Deeeee-licious.

Can't wait to come back.

I had an amazingly good first experience with Sweet Freedom.  I spoke to a very pleasant lady on the phone who put aside 6 vanilla cupcakes for my vegan teen's birthday.

When I came to pick them up they were boxed and ready.   I also wound up getting 6 more cupcakes in assorted flavors, chocolate, salted caramel and triple berry.

My kid loved them and shared with her friends.

Good vegan desserts are a blessing.

Thanks, sweet freedom, for supporting our animal-free diet.

Just OK - I had a salad bowl and the cucumber salad and baba ghanouj were fine - the rest (hummus, limp romaine, dry chicken and tough-mediocre "steak") was edible but blah.

Do not get the steak.  Not at all juicy.

I love this type of food and have tried 2 other local mini chains Naya and Cava and they were both better than Naf Naf.

I wanted to love it but it is just Meh.

That said they staff greeted me upon entrance (I came in early before the long-ass line)  and the cashier was very friendly and polite.

Might try it again but might now.

When it's fresh - that vanilla pound cake is simple, heavy and rich and DE-FRIKKIN-LICIOUS.  For $11 a pop - get 2 and freeze one.

So good.  A neighborhood staple and a "real" Philly treat.

Oh boy.  Where do I start?
Lots of things have changed at Fork.  Some for the better - but most are not.

Before I dive in - let me just say - or scream - this:

NOT GOOD FOR KIDS!!!!

Our fussy party of 4 included my not-so-fussy 8 year old - who has dined at many Philadelphia spots.  Before we went I saw "Crispy Chicken Nuggets" on the "Bites" menu - so I knew that was what we would get for her.

BOMB!  Dark meat chicken chunks in very pale (nearly white) tempura batter made the young lady frown almost instantly.

So we asked if the "Spaghetti al chitarra" (Homemade spaghetti with butter, scallions and crab) could be made as just spaghetti with butter?  What a fuss ensued - and after negotiations, yes - they brought her a small plate of home-made spaghetti DROWNED in butter.  And tried to charge $18 for it (which is the normal price when it comes with crabmeat.).

So disappointed.

OK - so "kids meal fiasco" aside - how were the grown-up dishes?
Not bad.  Salads were the stand out - my kale salad was terrific (Matyson's is better - as Fork's is a bit too vinegary in my opinion), and my friends split the "Roots" - a unique preparation of seasonal root veggies.

Appetizer pastas were SMALL and $15 - $16 each.  Yikes.

Our server is a great guy - and I just knew I had seen him before!
But the whole "not sure if we can make pasta with butter" thing just sat with me very poorly.

Even Ellen herself (the owner) cam out to chat with us - and I pretty much told her all of this.  I don't think it will matter one bit in the long run.
4 star food and 2 star (maybe even 1 star) service.

I won't be back. And there is no way I will deign to bring a kid in here.  (They made it very clear she was not welcome.

A fantastic find on an unseasonably warm November day.  Lentil Soup, Horiatiki Salad -topped with salmon - so perfect - and "greek" waffle fries.

Great service from Ian.

We loved that house-made pita, too.

Everything was so tasty and moderately priced.  Lovely!

Holy crap you guys, why didn't someone drag me here sooner? Hats off to my friend Erin for suggesting this gem of a place. I got the Irish breakfast drink with Jameson, butterscotch scnapps and oj (I could drink a gallon of those, OMG)! And the fried chicken slinger over perfect biscuits and gravy with an overeasy eggs and french fries. Legitimately that may very well be my most favorite meal of all time. I kind of don't want people to see this because I will literally be here every chance I get and be called that crazy yelp girl, but I don't care! I own it. Great live music and the waitress we had was hilarious and sat next to me to take my order. I'd be friends with the staff, and they know how to make amazing food and drinks so you should befriend them too! New favorite place, call me and take me back anytime.

In response to some of the complaints that this place's prices are higher than the average Korean spot: I don't see why Europeans/European food should have a monopoly on fancier restaurant vibes with higher priced menus- and they don't own "fusion" or putting imaginative spins on traditional dishes either! Don't non-white restauranteurs also deserve to make some money? 

Otherwise: I FREAKING LOVE THIS PLACE. I moved into an apartment building down the street from them 3 weeks ago, and since then have been there about 10 times. 

I'm a chef and am pretty hard to please. I always feel ripped off if I'm served something I feel like I could have made just as well as home. Like yeah, I am just a white gal and a relative newcomer to Korean cuisine, but I learned how to make certain dishes like Bulgogi from Maangchi's blog a few years ago, and have made it so many times since for professional gigs. Buk Chon's bulgogi is MILES BETTER. The overall flavor is of course the same, but it is a more interesting presentation: you can taste several more of the ingredients- so well-layered but subtle!!

I also have a big appetite, so was surprised to see some reviews complaining about portion size! The first time I went to Buk Chon for dinner, my partner and I shared the pork buns appetizer, and then both got an entree. This was WAY too much food. Several times since then, I have split two appetizers and the Bibimbap (my favorite!) with a friend. This has been the perfect amount of food. And it's SO NICE that the restaurant is cool with this- often "nicer" places insist on everyone order their own entree, or they'll add a fee to "make up" for the person or people who did not order their own. I'd actually be willing to pay more money for this now-routine of ordering a single entree, because all of them have always been so delicious!

Oh- if you go for lunch and order the discounted lunch special, the portions are smaller than when you pay full price at dinner. This is not unusual among restaurants I've been to in general.

Last thing: I also love the Chinese green tea and think it complements much of the food well. 

Every time I walk past and see someone(s) peering at the menu outside, I stop and encourage them to go in. And the same to everyone reading this!

Meh... The sandwich was dry and the meat was burnt. Hardly any taste. 

The wings were good but not amazing. 

The cook was in the back the whole time yelling out food stuff, super annoying. I get it is cute and unique but still, I don't want to hear all about why my fries are coming out.

The service was slow. The tables were dirty, just gross and grimy.

Like Mr. Chad below me, I had passed by Crescent City Steaks a million times. It wasn't until I heard Tom Fitzmorris talking about it on his radio show that I paid it any mind. According to him this is one of only three places in the city that serve grade A prime dry aged beef, the others being Emerli's Delmonico, and I think Domenica? From the stories I've heard Crescent City Steaks was once one of a few steak houses in that area, patronized by hungry gamblers going to and coming from the racetrack. I have even heard stories that Ruth's Chris got it's recipes and start from this place.

Anyway since I heard all that info over the past year or two I had been hyping this place up in my head. Imagining a utopia of steak, cut and served by beautiful seductive siren's manipulating all with huge slabs of well cooked rich flavored beef. And guess what? This all came true! Ok, not all of it, while certainly the staff is very attractive they are not steak sirens. 

Our table got a porter house for 4 along with some sides. I've never ordered such a large piece of meat before, I had no idea what to expect. I've also been disappointed so many times after I've hyped a restaurant up. The steak was absolutely cooked perfectly, like, I've never tasted a better steak ever in my entire life. In fact it was so good it has really changed my opinion of steak. Apparently they cook there steaks in like butter or something, on top of that it is dry aged meat which adds a really deep flavor to it. Like the steak was so tender and hot, I just wanted to shove the entire porterhouse for 4 in my mouth and stab anyone who wanted to take it away from me. As far as steak goes, you won't be disappointed, I've eaten many cuts of meat in my day, I'll say it again and again, this is the best steak I've ever eaten.

We also got a few sides, none particularly memorable, but they weren't bad. They also have a Hurricane here with actual fruit juice! None of that pat o's powdered/syrup mix crap. The wine and drink list is also very extensive.

The interior of the place is great, like clearly hasn't been renovated or changed much since it's opening in 1934, and if it was it was probably like 1944. Floors are tiled, it's got those metal tile things on the ceiling, and closed boths you can eat in! I've heard the closed curtain both thing used to be common among high end resturants back in the day. I suppose people now want everyone to see them wolf down some meat, I encourage you to hide that behavior in one of the booth areas. It's cool, and you'll probably never eat at another restaurant like it anymore. 

Service was perfectly fine, efficient, friendly, quick. 

Anyway only downside is, this place is expensive, but luckily it was my birthday, so I didn't have to pay. But unfortunately that cost will probably prevent someone like me from ever eating there again.

This place has won a james beard award, been on TV, and even has signs claiming it is "America's Best Fried Chhicken"!

Are you serious?

I have lived literally down the street from Willie Mae's for about a year now. So if this place was awesome, you bet I would have walked myself a couple of blocks to be a regular.

Unfortunately that was not the case.

First of all, let me explain what is extremely annoying about this place. This neighborhood for the most part is a working class Black neighborhood, and fairly residential. But every day you will see loads of tourists pouring onto this place like they found gold. I suppose they all think it is a spot that they only know, and everyone else is regulars. But I'm on to them. Anytime that situation is occurring I immediately become suspicious. 

More importantly the chicken. I wanted dark,  they gave me mostly white. There was so much breading I was horrified and full after a few bites.  The chicken was also extremely dry. I have been all over the south, eaten things who never would believe are cooked in America, and my friends, this is not the best fried chicken. The sides were decent at our whole table though.

Popeyes is better. Yes Popeyes!

If you are looking for something a little higher quality and local you could try, McHardy's on North Broad (take out only), Broad St Cafe, in the quarter Coops. Just don't come here, much better choices all through out the city.

I would also like to make an important point. Although New Orleanians certainly eat tons of fried chicken, and many places do it well. That is not the specialty cuisine of the region, traditional soul food is not what we are famous for down here. We have our own brand of New Orleans food, eat that if you are a tourist. Don't come here for "America's best fried chicken".

Just had my first visit, and first Juicy Lucy.

The previous restaurant in this location was pretty mediocre. In fact, there are quite a few mediocre (yet successful) restaurants in this area. With all of that in mind, and despite being ecstatic it was open, I was expecting Juicy Lucy's to be mediocre as well. Much to my surprise, it was far from it. 

The second I heard a burger joint was opening in Mid City, I immediately thought about how great of an idea it was. There are 3 fairly mediocre Mexican-themed restaurants, 4 Pizza/Italian restaurants, and a few higher end places within walking distance. I'm tired of all that crap--some of it's great, but if you live or frequent this area, you might get frustrated at a lack of variety. Which is why serving burgers is probably the best idea any restaurateur has had for this part of town.

Juicy Lucy's is probably one of the most solid restaurants I've visited in awhile. We had three people at our table, and everyone thought the food was pretty good and would come back again. I think for a brand new restaurant, in a brand new place, that few have ever heard of, that is pretty damn amazing. This place was good and smoothly landed me into a ground beef euphoria. 

The concept here is stuffed burgers, so basically they throw some cheese, and a variety of other things and wrap it in a ground beef patty. It comes out being a burger with a pocket of melty gooey goodness. They have about 5 or 6 different types of burgers to order stuffed, and you can also get a regular burger and pick your cheeses and toppings. Burgers come with a side, onion rings, fries, or sweet potato fries. For an added 2.50 you can get truffle fries! And of course, beer is served. 

The down side for me was the decor. It was kind of dark and drab, which put me into a tired mood. A mood that is hard to break regardless of how good the food is. I also think it would be great if you could choose what you want stuffed. Obviously the kitchen probably doesn't want to over-complicate things, but I'm sure you could let people mix and match some things quite easily. 

Go eat here, and eat here often. If a restaurant starts out serving solidly good food, it can only get better. I'm already planning my return visit.

I've lived in Hendersonville for about a year now and have been to a handful of restaurants but nothing has impressed me as much as Moby Dicky's. From the friendly staff, great customer service, unique scenery, and delicious food (especially seafood)... This is my new favorite spot. 

The restaurant is very small in terms of seating. While they do have outdoor seating, it was raining the day me and my family visited. Therefore a decent chunk of would-be-available seating was gone. The wait wasn't too bad though, considering how quickly they were bringing out food. 

My daughter (a finicky toddler) decided she wanted to try shrimp for the first time. Anyone with kids that age knows that a lot of the food you order ends up not being eaten. We didn't want to buy her a kids meal she wouldn't eat. Our waitress was kind enough to bring her a single piece of fried shrimp without question. My wife and I were stunned! My daughter liked it so much, we ended up getting her a kids fried shrimp meal. 

I ordered the appetizer lobster tail because I wanted to enjoy lobster but didn't want to splurge on the dinner portion lobster. Well as luck would have it, as I was trying to eat it, it fell on the floor. Now.. As gross as it sounds I was about to eat it anyway (I'm a guy and it was lobster!) Well a staff member saw it and said they would get me another. I didn't even have to ask!! A lot of places would have simply said "sorry about your luck." Again, my wife and I were amazed. 

Everyone's food was wonderful and I was surprised of the variety of items on their menu. The steak sandwich I got was one of the best I ever had. Heck, even the salad my wife got had some of the best croutons I've ever tasted. The key lime pie was also very delicious. 

My first time to Moby Dicky's was so good, I had to write this review. It is now definitely my go-to place in Sumner County!

Wandered in here while running some errands, so glad I did... it's one of the best finds I've had recently.

As soon as I walked in, I felt a nice breezy welcome by both the ambiance of the place and the servers. Clear high white walls accented by simple vibrant paintings and plain wood tables. The servers were punctual, helpful and very friendly throughout. I've found that Vietnamese places have a tendency to be somewhat tacky, but there was none of this here.

Ordered spring rolls, not excellent but good. The pho was delicious, basic beef green onions and noodles in broth. One of the servers offered me a lesson on how to use the sauces correctly, even though I am quite familiar with it. It was a nice touch. The drip coffee iced has a great kick but very tasty, thought about ordering a second...

There's a nice patio outside, hopefully I'll enjoy some good times there once the outside temp of St. Pete gets somewhere below the surface of the sun.

Westside St. Pete/Gulfport/Pasadena totally needs some diversity like this. Please give it a chance if you're in this neck of the woods!

Okay, so who doesn't like Jeni's. This location was nice and the staff was 
friendly. They kept the line moving and there wasn't much of a wait, even though there was a line. 

Now Jeni's have so many different and tasty recipes that it's ridiculous. Mind-blowing! The ice cream here is so creamy, flavorful, and lacks NOTHING! Also, if you have any type of dairy allergies,  don't fret, Jeni's got ya back...there's plenty of vegan options as well.

Side note: if you aren't in the area, you can always try a good ol pint of Jeni's ice cream at your local grocer.

A hidden gem restaurant my friends and I stumbled across and lucked into getting a table at despite how busy it was that Saturday night. We were a group of six people and somehow managed to get a big table inside a private dining room that was originally reserved for a private party, but I guess they cancelled last minute, luckily for us. 

The vibe was casual but the food was fancy/ elegant. I ordered the Fried Cauliflower in Thai Vinaigrette. Honestly I felt like the cauliflower could have been fried a little more as only a thin layer of the outside of the cauliflower was slightly crunchy. But I love cauliflower so I enjoyed the dish nonetheless, especially when dipped in the Wasabi aioli I had requested on the side, which definitely added a kick to the dish (I love spicy food). 

My favorite part of the meal though was the dessert, which I hear changes every night. I ordered the blueberry lemon cookie crumble cheesecake and it was really good! The plating of the dessert was also well-done and beautiful.

Service was also really friendly. So all in all, I would definitely want to come back here next time I'm back in SB.

I had high expectations but unfortunately Cafe Du Monde was such a let down that it really felt overhyped. The line was long but it moved fast. When I did reach the front to order though, I had a question about the coffee and the employee misunderstood me. But rather than answer my question, she tried to charge me double for two drinks, and then when I clarified, she blamed me and was pretty rude. 

Even more disappointing than the subpar service were the actual beignets, which were not made-to-order but were pre-sorted into brown bags that they hand over when you pay. Which means the beignets weren't hot. They were actually pretty heavy and doughy and hard, and not light and fluffy like beignets are supposed to be. Honestly I enjoyed the beignets from other local cafes better. So would I return to Cafe Du Monde? No. Definitely not. It absolutely wasn't worth the hype, at least in my opinion.

I had heard alot about Ruby Slipper so I was excited to try the popular New Orleans breakfast spot. We arrived soon after they opened in order to avoid the long lines/ wait. We were seated inside and our orders were taken. Service was subpar. Our waitress brought out the correct order for my friend but the wrong order for me, so it appeared she had taken down the wrong order. After finally getting my actual order, it seemed like our waitress forgot about us as I had to try to flag her down a few times to ask for hot sauce, etc. 

As for my food, I had ordered the one tomato two tomato benedict, and sadly my food was mediocre. Actually, to say it was mediocre is being kind. I really didn't like my Benedict at all. It was drenched in what I think was hollandaise sauce, to the point that the sauce overpowered all other flavors and tastes. My stomach also felt a little queasy the rest of the day. 

The only part of the benedict I actually enjoyed was the biscuit, which was good. Honestly I would have been better off if I just ordered a biscuit with maple butter to go. But at least now I know that if I return to NOLA in the future, I can pass on Ruby Slipper.

So incredibly disappointed in the experience we had here. Called in a to go order and gave us a 45 min to an hour wait time. Well about 20 minutes later I got a return call saying they didn't have some ingredient to make part of our order. We had to change it, and I was shocked that 20 minutes after ordering they were only just starting to make our food. They gave us an updated wait time of a full hour. We showed up to pick the food up about ten minutes after the suggested time to make sure it would be ready, but we still ended up waiting another 15 minutes in the car. Food smelled great and we were excited to get home to eat- such a let down! The meatballs are completely raw in the middle, not pink, completely raw. After removing the meatballs because I was scared to eat such undercooked meat, there was so little red gravy I couldn't even get the pasta coated enough to eat it. Pizza came like warm, but wasn't terrible. Can definitely get better Italian food at MUCH lower prices...like Olive Garden.

Why oh why did I not pay closer attention to the reviews of this restaurant?! My bad!
While in Santa Barbara for the weekend, we thought it would be nice to check out the pier at Sunset. We decided to eat at Longboards since it's one of a few places to eat at the wharf. I thought "how bad can it be? It's on the pier so the seafood has to be decent." Nope nothing decent about this place. It's a total tourist trap.
I ordered a bowl of clam chowder thinking it would be homemade. Wrong. It tasted like it was out of a can. My son ordered the salmon plate for $30 it came with a small piece of (previously frozen) salmon fries and salad. My husband ordered the chili (also tasted like it was out of a can). And my daughter had pulled pork sliders which wasn't anything special. I think we paid $130 (including tip) for that and 3 sodas. Such a rip off for the quality & quantity of food. I guess it was a pretty expensive sunset. LOL
If you find yourself in SB, I suggest passing this place by. You can find much better and less expensive food just a block up the street.

Located inside the Santa Barbara Public Market it was a bit tricky to find. They have a menu consisting of tacos, Tostadas, and a few sides. I thought the prices were pretty high for tacos, but totally worth it. Between 3 of us we ordered the sayulita (the wild shrimp tostada with mango, jicama, and cucumber), the Ensenada taco (beer battered fish), Al Pastor taco (marinate pork with pineapple salsa), Norteno (carne asada with beans, cheese, and guacamole), and the Tempura Cauliflower taco. They were all good, but the cauliflower taco was the favorite. And the portions are generous so we didn't even finish it all. There is a pretty impressive salsa bar if you want to add some extra flavor, but it isn't necessary because each taco comes with its own salsa or sauce to compliment the flavor.

Moved to Delaware from North Jersey. Thank god for this place because I'm really missing decent Italian food. Whatever I get is always good. The place is always super packed so there is usually a line of people waiting for a table and then people coming in to pick up their take out. It's confusing and a bit overwhelming if it's your first time at this place. You need to make your way to the register for assistance. The space is very tight. It's irresponsible and unfair for the two previous posters (who obviously know each other since they posted on the same day) to claim the place is racist. It actually has a diverse staff. The first time I was there, people were getting assisted before me because I was caught in the mix up and thought there was a line for the register and there wasn't. It's not anyone's fault, it's just is what it is for the space. Now I know and I don't have any problems and I'm in and out a happy customer. Last time I was in there was even a staff member by the door trying to assist people to make sure no one was getting missed.

Fantastic food with friendly service. This place is my go too for Indian food. I just tried the Buffett and is the best I have had in Tampa Bay. I have tried many Indian restaurants in the area and this is my favorite.
NOTE: they are starting to use non allergenic ingredients which can change the original flavor. Please specify that you are okay with him using original ingredients otherwise they will not use the peanuts or other allergenic ingredients.

I love First Watch. I love their menu and prices and I've never had a negative experience. I've gone to numerous locations and it's consistently great service and quality food. It's healthy but tasty. Pretty good portions, I usually have enough for a leftover meal. Never a wait time. Definitely check out FW!

A fun, hip restaurant to visit on a warm sunny Florida day! Located on Gandy (St Pete side), you can get here by car, bike, or boat! Convenient ;) While the restaurant is a hot spot on the weekend, it's not impossible to find a parking spot or table. I've never had to wait to find a table. The service is quite quick and my waiters have always done a good job of making sure we have everything we need. 
Loss of a star: I wish their bathroom was bigger and more private. The door is wide open for a breeze and lighting purposes (?), but it's really awkward when you're washing your hands and a guy at the bar is watching you lol. Sometimes, you just want to fix your hair and reapply your lipstick without guys around *shrug*. The prices are also high...cha ching. While the portions are adequate size, the pricing doesn't always reflect the portion or food item itself. I can get coconut shrimp elsewhere for $5 or so less then they have it listed for. Anyways, I enjoyed my tuna steak wrap and was relieved it came with chips (included). I really didn't want to have to pay more to add on a side and I don't like cole slaw, does anyone? I thought there was a nice serving of ahi tuna in the wrap, so I will splurge again ($18) and get their wrap next time I go. The margarita was also refreshing, I just don't know why it is $9.50.  Check it out because it is a fun time and there are kayaks and stand up paddle boards to rent. And the views are superb. Just be ready to pay more than the usual brunch spot!

5 stars alllllll around! Such a cute and unique place to dine at! Come on by for your favorite childhood dessert...with the addition of alcohol! Kid friendly just got adult friendly ;)! Enter into a dessert bar room, the next room is dimly lit with a small stage area where various musicians play (acoustic to edm on the weekend). The last room has a long table for a conference room vibe. A projector can be used for work or college projects. The employees are cool and friendly! My friend and I shared the beer cheese fondue (~$14) and the margarita flatbread (~$8), and both loved it. The sizes were perfect for sharing. For a more low key night, come any day but Friday or Saturday, those are their busiest days. Cannot wait to return back here!

Celebrated my birthday here with cocktails with friends. LOVE the atmosphere - they really went all out to create a cool, classy old-timey vibe. Lots of little touches from the velvet swags to the custom benches, the antique furniture and the metal rail in front of the bar.... But the real stars are the cocktails - hand crafted, classic cocktails with a twist. One reviewer didn't like the spanked basil in the Manhattan, but I loved it. The Old Fashioned was one of the best I've had and the VC Mule had so much ginger goodness I had to restrain from drinking it too quickly. If you're looking for cheap drinks to get smashed on quickly, this isn't your bar. 1864 is all about carefully crafted cocktails worth sipping slowly.

The grocery store that makes going to any others, suck. Gelson's is our closest market, and gladly so. Not trust-fund crunchy like Lazy Acres, Whole Foods funky nor Trader Joe's hipster, Gelson's fills the perfect niche. Here you find good quality, WHOLESOME food with an international, gourmet flare. Both the exotic and the staples happily co-exist.

Need Swiss appenzeller or raclette for a party or that perfect grilled cheese? They got it. Want to know what wine to pair with it? Ask the cheese lady behind the counter and browse their excellent wine selection. Wonderful flower department too, to surprise the wife.

Avoid lines at the deli counter by phoning your sliced-to-order cold cuts ahead. Need a special cake or pastry? The in-store Renaud's has you covered...AND they have the everyday nasty stuff you crave: Lay's potato chips, Coke Zero, Kraft mac 'n Cheese, etc. If the watchful manager sees any checkout line more than a couple people long, another opens. You genuinely feel spoiled. Sure, everyday prices are a bit more than other stores, but it's so enjoyable to shop at Gelson's - and worth every penny!

I gave Death & Taxes five stars because I think it's the best cocktail bar in the Reno/Tahoe area. I'm really surprised by the reviews that feel the drinks are expensive, I found them inexpensive ($10-$12) and I'm wondering what the other reviewers think these drinks should cost. Try drinking in New York and then tell me these drinks are overpriced...

Keep in mind, this is a cocktail bar. Not a dive bar, a pub or a sports bar and you'll be disappointed if you're expecting Death & Taxes to be something it's not. Dive bars, pubs and sports bars have their place and there's plenty to choose from, but D&T is a welcome breath of fresh air for those of us that enjoy cocktails and the experience. The drink menu is really interesting and their selection of spirits is top notch. Their mixers are either house made or sourced from small, high end companies. The bartenders were friendly, cared about what they were doing and made their drinks correctly with the right equipment.

It's a place where an adult can get an interesting cocktail or a classic standard, perfectly made by someone that cares about your drink and built with fresh ingredients and the best spirits. (Why would you go out for anything less?)

If you're sick of going out to bars dominated by vodka, crap like Alizé and those dispensing guns with buttons for sodas and mixers, then you'll find Death & Taxes to be a slice of heaven. 

On the other hand, if you think the hallmark of a good drink is big and cheap, or neon is an acceptable color in a cocktail then you might want to keep driving. I'm sure it's dollar PBR night somewhere...

This location is a real dive.  I phoned in an order for take-out.  When I got there, there was chaos among the employees.  It took five minutes to be acknowledged standing at the register.  I gave my name to the woman and she disappeared into the kitchen.  She was back out moments later, but did not give me any feedback on the status of my order.  I waited another twelve to fifteen minutes and they brought out the pizza.

It's not a bad pizza.  I just didn't like the atmosphere and service, so it's unlikely I'll be back.

I've been a customer at The Sausage Shop for almost thirty years.  Kent takes such good care of his customers.  He is also totally tuned-in to the local meat market.  I ask him for USDA prime brisket to smoke -- got it.  I want 1855 Angus Beef -- got that too.

Kent can tell you anything you want to know about meat and what's available.  Just don't piss him off.  That's a deal-breaker.

First visit at the new location for lunch.  They did a nice job inside, considering it was once a Chili's.

The lunch menu is pretty small, but they will bring a dinner menu if you ask.  We ordered a Caesar salad to split, and two 6-inch pizzas.  They split the salad onto two plates in the kitchen, which made it less messy at the table.  Also, the 6-inch pizzas are more like 8 inches.

The salad was excellent.  Perfectly dressed and the dressing is delicious.  The pizzas are excellent as well.  The crust is light and they get a good char on it.  The sauce is full of tomato flavor.

All-in-all, as good of a pizza as I've had in Tucson.

I ordered the cheese enchiladas, Christmas (Goyita's is a New Mexican restaurant), and my wife ordered the small combination plate.

She loved her taco, and the red chile on the enchilada.  Less enjoyable were the beans, rice and chile relleno, which had a really eggy coating.  I'll get to the green chile she ordered on the side in a minute.

From my experience, southern New Mexican food differs from northern mostly in the green chile sauce.  I've written in other reviews that southern seems to be more of a velouté with green chile, whereas northern is heavy on the green chile and slightly thickened.  I prefer northern, but have had some delicious sauce in Silver City.

I found the red sauce to be delicious.  It's spicy, but not too much.  The green had nice flavor, but, at least for my tastes, could have used a lot more green chile in it.

The beans and rice were not bad, but not great.  What I'd love to see is real New Mexican food here -- skip the rice, serve whole beans and posole, and smother the plate with chile.  That would make me feel like I was back in New Mexico.

Goyita's is a great restaurant and I'm sure they are going to do well with the great dishes they serve.
Yuck. The wings were just greasy, not tasty. They must have been cooked in oil that was 10 years old. The sandwich just gross - plasticy cheese, cold peppers, stale bread.

This is my personal favorite pizza spot.  We have places we go altogether but when it comes down to what I'm wanting and it's just me and my choice- hands down Scordato's all the way.   They have this eggplant, red pepper and zucchini pizza that also comes with an herb olive oil that I actually find myself really craving.  I've even had my meat loving man try it.  He'd ordered the sausage and onion pizza for himself (which he loved)  but he had to concede the flavors of my pizza were incredible.  He may even get that for himself next time which is saying a lot (because pizza for him must have meat).  
They have some really nice wines to choose from if you're eating in.   They even offer some local wines which I absolutely love anytime I see here.   Scordato's pizza is for someone going for flavor- definitely quality and they make incredible pizza.  I have had salads and other things too, never disappointed.   I absolutely love Scordato's!

If you're looking for great noodles and a ton of them, this is the place. I love going here on a cold day and warming up with some hot soup and freshly tossed noodles. Oh and the fried rice is amazing. 

I always get the beef or chicken and I'm never disappointed. For about $9 I can get the longest noodle I've ever eaten in my life. I just keep slurping and slurping and think I may never find the other end. 

I get it to go most times, but I have often eaten in here. It gets a little cold during the winter because it seems the door is constantly opening and closing with patrons rolling in to get some of these delicious noodles. However, eating in is a treat, as you can watch your noodles being made fresh right in front of you. These are simple dishes, but pack so much flavor. I like to throw a little spice in mine and turn up the heat, but they're great just as they come, too.

While your'e there, check out some of the great photographs on the wall. My friend at Natalie Hinds Studios has livened up the place with some photos of the tasty choices. 

For a special treat make sure you try the fluffy ice. I was very hesitant at first, but oh wow how creamy and delicous this is. I was with a group of five of my friends and I was totally not on board because for one, it was cold out and for two, I'm not a big fan of snow cones and that's what I figured it would be like, but I could not have been more wrong. It was very much like eating ice cream. I don't know how they do it, but I don't question it any longer!!

I grew up in NY with access to dumplings and high quality takeout. I moved away about 11yrs ago and just gave up on ever getting really delicious dumplings. Apparently, all I had to do was move to STL!  I'm new here and found Corner17 in a yelp search hunting for Bubble Tea (also really hard to find REAL tea - why!?).  After reading tons of reviews and looking at the menu I decided to give it a try despite the higher than average prices. It was so worth it, and now my husband and I order from here almost weekly!! This is not a 'Covid adjusted' review where I give 5 stars despite short fallings because times are hard. I mentioned the higher than average prices here because well - they are. But it's because quality food isn't cheap for restaurants to buy. If you enjoy getting fried little brown bits passed off as chicken - then go for your cheaper place. Every dollar is worth it here so do not be put off. If you just needed to read another reviewer saying that this place is worth it and go for it - stop reading. There's TONS of them and we all agree - Corner 17 is fantastic!

Some details for those who are crazy like me....

- The online ordering and pick up process is super easy! I've developed some anxiety about pick up after some bad experiences, but despite them being busy pick up was pretty seamless and the online ordering was as easy as any delivery site. I will note that pickup is not curbside and this place is popular. My husband gets to do the honors since I'm immune system compromised but he said it was clean, fast and has had zero complains returning despite the 30min round trip drive. 

- The drinks are prepared to travel! I ordered 3 teas worried they'd show up a total mess. Nope! They're in very high quality plastic cups that you honestly could wash and reuse a few times they're that stable. They have lids and those little mouth spout plugs. You also get to customize your level of sweetness and request add ins to make it the tea you've been dreaming of. If you're not a milk tea fan, the oolong super fruit tea is so good and the fruit sweetens it so much you don't even need to have sugar added. You've missing out if you don't try a drink from here! 

-The dumplings!!!!!!! God they are so good, they are scratch made, they are when they're supposed to be the fillings have complex flavors and their CHILI SAUCE!! it's what dreams are made of. Request extra, I would happily pay for extra if ever asked.  I will note that the chili dumplings are quite soft which threw my husband. I *think* this is how they're supposed to be and I love them, but if texture sensitive folks might take issue. If you only tried these in the past and they turned you off - they're the only ones that have that soft texture so try others!  

- We tried a few chicken and noodle dishes. The chicken is actual chicken, not those weird scraps that make you say huh- what is that? They're tender and flavorful, not chewy sauce delivery tools. The noodles are super fresh. They are softer than your typical take out joint because they're fresh. I only say this because it surprised me at first, but what a happy surprise! Again - that chili sauce - lord it makes me so happy and that TEA EGG! I'm a weirdo who orders a hard boiled egg every single time. The flavor is so cool I can't not. It's a great little lunch snack in the rare occasions I can control myself to save it. Try it. 

-Because 100% positive reviews always make me raise an eyebrow, if you put a gun to my head to come up with a complaint: The crab rangoons come with little sweet and sour sauce packets and it's never enough  if you really like to dip them. I really wish they'd have cups of sauce you could order to go with them, but I also understand that they aren't 'that' type of crappy americanized takeout chinese food so it's unfair of me to expect that. Seriously - may this be the worst offense lol this isn't barely a complaint and my blood sugar levels are thankful to them. 

Go forth and binge!

PS - Corner 17, if you're reading this....PLEASE add soup dumplings on your menu! Pretty pretty pretty please!!!!! I'll be your biggest fan and order them at least 1x a week this winter!!!

Dang! This might be my new favorite ice cream spot. Too bad it's 4 hours away :(.

My mom and brother have been raving about this place for a while, so I knew we had to try it on my next visit up to Brandon/Valrico. My mom told me about all of the crazy eclectic flavors on the menu. All of them sounded right up my alley. The Yelp reviews and pictures that I saw intrigued me even more. 

I tried so many flavors on my first visit to The Revolution Ice Cream Co. Each flavor was insanely delicious! I ended up settling on a scoop of Euro Trash and a scoop of Drunken Brownies. Euro Trash is Nutella ice cream with biscoff cookie crumbles mixed in. It was beyond amazing! Any Nutella fan has to order this flavor! Drunken Brownies is chardonnay caramel ice cream with brownie bits mixed in. Golllllyyy was that amazing! Seriously my favorite flavor of ice cream ever. It honestly tasted like a big warm, melty brownie with a scoop of the best vanilla ever on top. No idea how they got it to taste that good.

My little brother ordered Salted Caramel S'mores (salted caramel ice cream with a marshmallow ribbon and chunks of fudge covered graham crackers mixed in) and Eurotrash. I tried his S'mores ice cream and it was delish. My mom got her favorite flavor The Seaward (salted caramel, coffee, cinnamon and cardamom) and Ch2Hn (Chocolate Habanero). Both flavors were very unique. My boyfriend ordered What's up Nutter Fudger  (chocolate peanut butter ice cream with nutter bar chunks mixed in) and Chocolate Habanero. Oh man was What's up Nutter Fudger amazing!! The bf said it's the best peanut butter/chocolate ice cream he's ever had in his life. 

This place was too amazing. I cannot wait until my next visit!!

One, two, three, look at Mr. Lee
Three, four, five, look at him jive
Oh Mr. Lee, Mr. Lee
My heart is achin' for you Mr. Lee
'Cause I love your deli so

With apologies to the Bobbettes. 

The chicken steak is unparalleled in my extensive sample. The menu, while staying true to the beloved short-order grill, has enough surprising twists and thoughtful choices that I plan to eat my way through the menu--the Asian Fusion section is particularly alluring. The staff is charming and pleasant.

Needs Robert Irvine to come in.  Won't go there for another 20 years,.
rubber lobster.. over cooked crab imperial.. only good thing was our waiter Matt who was so wonderful.  prices are cheap but I'd rather pay more and get a good meal.. I'm spoiled by the restaurants in the city and south philadelphia.. can't believe that people actually wait in line to get a table.. I have to find a GOOD restaurant in delaware county .

Donuts have been fixed!
Every review from opening time should be taken with a grain of salt. I tried Batch (strictly for the donuts) the first week they were open and the donuts were BAD.  I was so bummed because I originally was filled with excitement to know a spot in Tucson would be doing something more creative than the cliche bacon maple donut. I thought Tucson finally had a trendy donut shop similar to Portland's Voodoo Doughnuts. Well, I was let down...
Until now! I'm really impressed that the owners of Batch saw the reaction from customers and did something about it. They now serve donuts from the best mom and pop donut shop in Tucson (Alvernon Donuts) and then add their creative spin as far as toppings go. One of my favorites is the Smores donut. I love the texture of the graham cracker dust on the marshmallows and the chocolate frosting is delicious. All this on a donut that is not too cakey or too oily. It's really fantastic. I also enjoy their key lime filled donut. It is really rich, but key lime is one of my favorite pies and this donut does not disappoint. 
So long story short, if you have tried Batch and were unimpressed, go back! If you have read bad reviews from early on in Batch's existence, give it a try anyway. The glaring defect of food quality has been addressed and these donuts are GREAT!

Desire was one of my favorites restaurant experiences during my New Orleans trip. Desire resides on the famed Bourbon Street and specializes in home-style New Orleans comfort food and fresh Gulf oysters. The congenial and upbeat staff really delivered top-notch service and made our experience very special and memorable. 

The Shrimp and Grits were perfection. I sampled about 4-5 different Shrimp and Grits dishes around NOLA and this one reigned supreme. The Cajun shrimp were plump, tender and  juicy and the grits were exactly as I like them -- perfectly seasoned, buttery, ultra rich and creamy and radiantly silky. I actually found the recipe for the Desire shrimp and grits online and will make my first foray into shrimp and grits cooking this summer. 

My dining companion ordered the Oyster & Shrimp Po' Boy, which looked like a fine choice. Fresh crusty bread laden with handfuls of fried shrimp and oysters. Can't go wrong there! 

You have to try the Deep Fried Peanut Butter & Jelly dessert. It came highly recommended by our server and I'm so glad she steered us to this one. It's amazing how a grade-school lunch classic can turn into such a devine dessert. It's warm, buttery and crispy served with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream. 

I love the feel at the Desire Oyster Bar. It has an old timey, traditional New Orleans feel with classy modern touches. The old tin ceiling, the black and the white checkered mosaic floor blend seamlessly with the beautiful modern architectural additions throughout the restaurant. French doors look out at all the conviviality of Bourbon Street so you get a front row seat to all the great live music and won't miss any of the action. 

Desires serves breakfast, lunch and dinner. The extensive menu includes a Jambalaya Breakfast Skillet, Bananas Fosters French Toast, Crab Etoufee, Fried Green Tomatoes, Crispy Alligator, Creole Gumbo, Po Boys, Crawfish and a host of other southern staples. If you're in search of authentic New Orleans classics with a fun atmosphere head over to Desire.

What a great place! I didn't actually go inside as they were closed but I watched the cats from outside the window for about 15 minutes. We happened to run into this cat cafe as we were heading back to the car in the nearby parking lot. Two adorable cats came up to me by the door and were just the sweetest little things. 

The next day I stopped by again to sneak another peek at all the kitties. This time it was open but you do need to make a reservation before coming in. This keeps a surge of people from coming in and ensures they maintain a relaxed and comfortable environment for the cats. 

What an great concept! Lounge and play with cats while you linger over coffee, refreshing beverages and light bites. The cats get socialization and companionship and potential owners can play and interact with the kitties before adopting. Of course you can just come in to visit and spend some quality time with some cool feline friends.
