I will have to make a reservation next time I'm in SB. I've heard wonderful things about this place and I can't wait to visit.

A culinary gem located in the Santa Barbara Public Market. This is my kind of place! Chef Velazquez brings the flavors from his Mexican homeland to Santa Barbara, paying homage to the fresh, simple street-style cuisine he grew up on.  Indulge in fresh, flavorful, elevated-yet-simple street food sourced from the local area. 

I ordered the Sayulita ($11), a towering tostada stacked with wild Mexican white shrimp, tomatoes, guacamole, onions, mango and serrano peppers, all dressed with a burnt habanero aioli. What a wonderful combination! Each bite offers a full breadth of flavors and textures (gentle heat from the aioli and serrano peppers, sweet crunch from the chopped mango, crunch from the crispy tortilla and juicy tomatoes and salsa fresca). This tostada isn't too heavy either but keeps you full and satisfied. 

My mom and brother ordered a couple of the Chicanos (shrimp quesadillas), a tasty mash-up of shrimp, market vegetables, fresh salsa and cheese on a housemade flour tortilla. The quesadillas are actually more like tacos. They come open-faced, not pressed. It doesn't matter because they were delicious and dynamite. Add some housemade guacamole for a nice zesty punch! 

Be sure to order a mimosa, sangria, wine-arita or cucumber fresca or lime fresca juice to accompany your meal. Sit back, relax and enjoy some awesome food and the dynamic and lively atmosphere at the SB Public Market.

Housed in the former Santa Barbara Fish Market, this Santa Barbara hot spot exudes local charm, historical significance and modern style. The space is warm and inviting with vestiges of the Lark's industrial past seen all around. The staff are personable, fun and attentive. Entrees range from $17-$42 but many can be shared family-style.  Enjoy an alfresco garden party on the lovely patio trimmed with delicate lights or cozy up under a heat lamp with a fleece blanket on one of those chilly Santa Barbara evenings. 

My friend and I shared several appetizers. The Rosemary & Brown Butter Cornbread served with a child honey butter was the perfect opener. You get a very nice herbal punch from the rosemary but it's very subtle and refreshing. My friend and I loved the wonderful marriage of rosemary and sweet brown butter. 

The Crispy Brussel Sprouts come garnished with medjool dates and sesame seeds and drizzled lime. They are crispy and crunchy with a touch of sweet from the dates. Our server warned us that the brussel sprouts are a good sized --they can almost double as an entree--appetizer so we swapped one of our entrees we were going to order for a salad. 

The Yellowtail Hamachi Crudo highlights some of the fresh summer seasonal ingredients bringing together compressed watermelon, shishito peppers, summer gazpacho, candied coriander along with some fresh lemon and basil. The enticing flavors are very well balanced.   

We shared the Little "Gems" Wedge salad featuring house smoked blue cheese, warm glazed bacon, spicy pecans all tossed in a refreshing herb vinaigrette. This beautifully oversized salad is dressed with so much fresh Santa Barbara bounty and is just so beautiful to behold. We really enjoyed this salad especially on a warm Santa Barbara summer evening paired with some wine. My friend picked up a nice Tempranillo from one of his wine tasting stops so we shared a bottle over dinner. There is a $25 corkage fee. 

The Hand Cut Pappardelle was excellent. So rich, robust and infinitely creamy. It's accentuated with piedmont white truffles, shaved parmesan, English snap peas and pine nuts. It looks small but it is so filling (2 of us didn't even finish it) especially when paired with one of their salads and an app or two. I would definitely order this one again. 

We shared a wonderful dinner at the Lark. This place is very popular so be sure to book your reservation. Valet parking is available as the parking fills up quick. It's a short jaunt to the beach so you can enjoy a nice post-meal evening beach stroll.

It's unfortunate that this coffee shop is suffering from bad reviews via people who don't know how to appreciate a place like this. Most of the negative reviews I'm reading are purely based on people not knowing the difference between Starbucks and a one-of-a-kind third wave coffee shop that serves incredibly high-quality drinks.

You wouldn't dare go to a five-star restaurant and ask the chef to hold three ingredients and add two you prefer. You wouldn't complain about there being three forks and not knowing which to use. You certainly wouldn't complain about the portion sizes on a four course meal. Why? Because this isn't Golden Corral. You don't smother your french fries in a sea of ketchup and pay $9 for all you can eat ribs. That might be what you are used to, but that doesn't mean all restaraunts operate in that fashion. 

Revelator is unique in that it's offering the best beans and ingredients to highlight their coffee. If you go to Stumptown in Seattle, you get their amazing roasters serving up their coffee. If you find yourself at Blue Bottle or Sightglass in San Francisco, it's the same high-caliber baristas pulling decadent shots and truly crafting your drink using their product. Revelator stocks the best beans from all over the world and lays them out for your choosing. Ok, ok... I guess it is a little like Golden Corral... but more like if the best chefs in the world were preparing the food. 

None the less, people should expect to pay a little more for incredible espresso being pulled through a thirty-thousand dollar machine. You should pay a little more for craft and precision. It's not even that much more expensive. A cappuccino at Starbucks would run me $3.10. I payed a whopping $1 more at Revelator for a cappucino that supremely destroys Starbucks. 

Which brings me to my last point...

If you don't LOVE the taste of GREAT coffee. DO NOT COME HERE! If you are absolutely fine with the "Super Dark Roast Arabica Robusto Blend w/ Six Stevia Packs" they serve at Thornton's gas stations, then you should totally go save some money and get your caffeine fix... FIDO is two doors down with average coffee and an incredible line! (ps. And insanely good breakfast I admit.)

However, if you want to taste coffee in ways you've never had it, using methods you've likely never seen, in an environment that's clean and inviting... you MUST visit this place!  I've traveled all over the country to some of the best coffee shops, and this one is in my top ten. The breakfast served here is healthy and tasty as well, albeit not a buffet.

Gyro's, feta and kalamata oh my!! This that gud gud!! Was out chiaaa heading back to sac after a long trip and wanted to get something to eat so we decided to check this place out. Yelp had good reviews so i was game to try it. 

When we pulled up, the parking lot seemed BUSY AF!! Lots of the patrons parking there were going to the steak house next door tho. To bad for them that they were missing out on some gud gud. When we walked in the first thing i noticed was that the lights were really dimmed, and the place had like an old school feel to it. 

Our waitress was koo as ish!!! Her name was Jessica, Jessica if u read this THANKS FOR THE GREAT COSTUMER SERVICE U MADE OUR EXPERIENCE PHENOMENAL!! Jessica was really helpful, and witty lol she really like to joke which i liked because me myself i'm a jokester so she really made me feel comfortable. 

If you check in you get a free dessert "awesome dude" is the name of the dessert its ice cream with baklava on top, its actually good AF! Ok let me talk about the food! We ordered the sampler that had a little of this and a little bit of that, Jessica recommended it and she did good, i hate to keep talking bout Jessica but she was such a good waitress i just cant stop!! She answered every question i had and gave me her recommendation which was highly appreciated. 

I ordered the lamb gyro that seemed to be cooked in a tomato sauce which was really flavorful and tender it was served with a side of rice and grilled veggies i loved it but the rice seemed plain and flavorless, this is why i'm giving it 4 stars. Mrs Nando V (Wife) ordered some type of grilled chicken sausage, idk how to spell it or pronounce it but it was hella fire. I wish i could give this place 5 stars. If i'm back in the area i will for surely come back. Jessica plugged it wit some dessert, good looking out Jess, come check this place out u will love it and they dont skimp out on the food, the customer service is on point!!

The good the bad and the ugly...dooooeeeeooooeeeeeooooo doo doo doo 

I have to admit I was really excited to be going as my health conscious GF Nancy was the one who suggested it and I love taverns especially when as badly hung over as I was. We both have admired the building and were extremely optimistic and hopeful about the experience

So the good...it's a tavern, the burger was fine...bordering on extra fine but you cannot order a less than murdered burger in Canada so not their fault, the fries were very good and the space is pretty darn nice.  I like the fish okay as well despite it being over cooked.  I would try it again but I'm not adverse to grease and am eternally hopeful.

The bad...everything was pretty greasy ( not bad for everybody...see above)...the service was off putting...the waitress actually came close to a WTF when Nancy ordered a " bloody caesar " I guess she hadn't heard the term before and she was obsequious and not in a bootlicking fake French sommelier kind of way but in a vapid " how are we getting along" kind of way.  The Caesar was crap. Truly insipid but improved with the addition of some Tabasco on the second and third rounds ( medicinal purposes) and the beer was a bit pricy but I guess the decor and location necessitates this

The ugly...we stared at "un bussed" tables throughout the visit...nothing was cleared from the empty adjacent tables for the duration of our visit  and it was a nearly empty Sunday afternoon so no excuse.  The Caesar in addition to being insipid was un garnished...what is uglier then a Caesar with no salted rim, no celery or spicy bean or some form of greenery...I mean this is where a good portion of the vegetables in my diet come from

Okay so we love industrial spaces and beer so I expect I will find myself there gain some day though Nancy said not her and she would give it one star but it was me that pecked this out so it gets 2 and the prospect of another chance

Gord

This is the worst $30 I have ever spent in my life. I ordered the roast beef debries, fries and a typhoon. The roast beef was very average no seasoning what's go ever. The drink was horrible. I won't ever be back. First time and last time

Ok, I really don't understand where others' lukewarm reviews come from.  It's *12.99*, for all you can eat with a ridiculous spread.  And the building is really nice.  That is as good as it gets!

They have sushi (and the good stuff at that... we're not just talking California rolls.  They have the usual suspects plus surf clam, baby octopus, octopus, squid, and lots more), frog legs, duck, roast beef, oysters, shrimp, crab legs (which would be enough to draw my brother alone), fish, tepanyaki, and more than I can remember.  Living in DC now it can be hard to find large quantities of tasty food at a reasonable price.  Anyone who lives within a 3-hour drive of Chopsticks has it incredibly lucky.

Nothing like an anniversary or special event to put a restaurant under intense scrutiny.  I picked this restaurant because of the good reviews, it was our 20th anniversary, and we had just come back from a 3 week trip where we travelled north and then all the way south in France.  I loved being able to walk in where I  immediately felt at home. I apologize I didn't get the gentleman's name behind the bar as he deserves credit. I asked to be seated away from the door as we get cold easy.  He smiled.  A genuine smile. That is unusual in a lot of places when we ask for something that isn't their plan, perhaps.  But, accommodating and polite, at the same time, started us out on a great evening. Next, Christina, our waitress took the baton and did her share to carry the evening.  She was so friendly and attentive without being oppressive or hovering.  She was prompt in bringing our drinks, was able to discuss their menu and informative when we asked questions, gave us time to ponder the menu and take our order.  The next part of our evening was the chef's outstanding abilities in preparing a dish called Pave' de Legumes which is a vegetarian dish that cried out with it's originality for me to order.  I have not had anything this unique or wonderful since 2001 in Napa. I have eaten in a 5 star Paris restaurant which left me "underwhelmed".  I am not trying to sound like a food snob.  I like diners as well as the next person. But there are times you want something really exciting to talk about in a restaurant and this was it.  Maybe I was just craving something really healthy and tired of "meat and potatoes".  The presentation of this dish was so pretty, I almost hated to disturb it.  I savored each bite and hated for it to end.  My husband thoroughly enjoyed his fresh grilled salmon on top of a bed of pureed asparagus with miso sauce.  I tasted it and it was very good.  I must add that because of all the reviews I read, we ordered the Pommes Frites with Sauce Original as an appetizer.  These were no ordinary french fries.  We could have polished them off but didn't because we wanted to save room for dessert.  We had Le Profiterole au Chocolat which was three puffs that were split and filled with vanilla ice cream, then topped with chocolate sauce and almonds.  Need I say more?  Well, I should say that I had the opportunity to pop my head in to say hi to the chef and his friendliness and attitude made me enjoy his food even more.  I had to tell him how happy he made me to eat the wonderful food he had prepared.  The other things that are important to me in my dining experience, wine and coffee or express after.  Both of these were the same caliber of the meal.  All the parts fit together perfectly for a good meal. Nothing was left out or unattended.  It was wrapped up all in a box, Perfect!  Thank you all for a wonderful memory.

I want to sing their praises for all to hear! In this time of Corona, they have been a bright light of hope and optimism in the midst of uncertainty.

They are open for takeout orders - it's easy and it's quick. Just go on line (or phone) and put together your order and pick it up curbside. 

I recently ordered their Easter Special of Bake-at-home croissants. They were easy to make and OMG I think I died and went to heaven delicious. It takes a bit of work, some time and patience, but so worth it. The croissants come out of the oven crisp and rich and so amazingly decadent yummy. The ready made pastries come frozen and vacuum packed. You just take out want you need, defrost, proof (rise in a warm moist place) and bake. The hard part is waiting for them to cool before you eat them.

I have been to the shop before the shut down and it is wonderful spot to have a nice cup of coffee and a kill your diet pastry. Everything is good, everything is made in-house and fresh. 

So to everyone out there - do your best to help keep a small local business afloat. Order, pick-up, take home. Couldn't be easier.

I have been a fan of Thali's for awhile now and finally had a chance to try Maya's. I was not disappointed.

They share the space with their sister restaurant (Thali) but the food is completely different. Well, not THAT different. They both serve vegetarian/vegan food with an option of gluten free. Both have lovely spicy delicious food for a reasonable price, and both have helpful and informative wait-staff to help you through the process and answer any questions. What is different is the presentation and the preparation of the chutney. The flavors and spices are also different. There seems to be mere emphasis on "bread" than on rice. They also do not have the Riata (Yogurt) . 

I opted for the Plain Dosa. I have never had Dosa before. It is like a crepe - a very thin, crispy pancake - but instead of being made out of wheat flour, it is made of fermented rice flour and lentil. Very yummy all by itself, as an accompaniment to the vegetable soup, and dipped in the tomato and coconut chutney. The meal becomes an exploration of spice and flavor and texture. The coconut chutney helps to cool your palate after eating some of the spicier fare. I just had water with my meal, but they have wine and beer available. 

I am looking forward to coming back and trying the rest of the offerings. The Poori and the Menu Vada look wonderful.

If you are expecting an authentic New York Deli experience, this is not it. 

I ordered a Reuben with a side of potato salad and while a generous portion, was not worth the price. The rye bread was very dry and tasted stale. The corned beef was bland and was just barely warm. The very thin slice of swiss cheese was not melted and the dressing was a small smear and hardly discernible. There was no sauerkraut anywhere on the sandwich. The potato salad was a bland mushy mess with no flavor. 

This is an order at the counter and take your "number" to the table kind of service. The staff were friendly, and our food was brought out to us very quickly, but no one checked to see if we enjoyed our food. The space is open to the casino and while clean, felt cold and antiseptic. 

The total for two people (two sandwiches, two mediocre beers) with tip came to almost $46. It definitely was not with the price. 

So no, don't think it was worth a return visit.

Finally! The new spot downtown has opened.

And what a great experience it was! The food, the service, the location, all were just what we had been hoping for.

They are still in their soft opening so there are a few kinks to get worked out, but it was pretty seamless for having been opened only three days. 

We decided to go with the small plates and were able to sample a variety of what they had to offer. We started off with the Charcuterie & Cheese Combo. A very nice sampling of cured meats and cheese, fruit compote and crostini. A nice paring wth our drinks. I had the Sierra Mule. A cinnamon flavored twist on the classic Mule served appropriately in a large copper mug. 

We then each chose two items off the small plates menu. First came the stuffed dates wrapped in bacon and crab cakes. The dates were amazing. The tender candy sweetness of the dates were offset by the creamy goat cheese and crisp, smoky bacon. The crab cakes were a little bit of a miss for me, but my dinning partners really enjoyed them. The crust was not quite as crunchy as I like it. 

Next were the Meatballs in sweet chili sauce and the Fillet Medallions with spinach and potatoes. The Fillet Medallions were hands down the all out headliner for me. They were tender, flavorful and juicy with a light reduction sauce. 

Our last pairing were Scallops on a bed of parmesan Risotto and Steak Tartar. The Steak Tartar was fresh and tasty. High quality prime fillet was used and it was amazing. My son dubbed it "Steak Sushi". With the fresh raw egg yoke, capers, mustard and cooked egg all stirred in, it made for an impeccable treat. I cannot eat scallops (sigh) but the others said they were fantastic. Our server kindly brought me a bowl of just the risotto. Oh my! Creamy and rich and piping hot. 

And it that wasn't enough, we decided to sample dessert. We had Chocolate Gelato (from The Eldorado), bananas Foster, and Profiteroles with a dark chocolate sauce made with Dorinda's chocolate. 

Servings were very generous and we walked away completely stuffed. Prices were reasonable for the quality of food that was provided. Items ran from $6-15. 

The only minor complaint was that the service felt just a little rushed at first. The dates and crab cakes came when we were still eating the Charcuterie. I think a little pause between servings would have made it perfect - time to sample and enjoy and digest a bit before the next round of deliciousness was brought. 

I am very much looking forward to coming back again. I think this will be one of our regular dining spots.

This used to be one of my favorite burger places, but alas, I feel there are better choices.

We have not been here in YEARS - I'm talking probably more than ten years ago. It really really really needs to be upgraded. The interior is starting look a bit frayed - ok it is looking pretty seedy actually. I don't need fancy but I do like clean. While I don't really think there was a health hazard, it looked unclean.

My cheese burger was just OK. It was cooked fresh with fresh ingredients and a soft bun that really held up to the juicy burger. (See how I worked that in?) But . . . . the flavor was disappointing. It was just bland. The cheese was generic American nice and melty, but very little flavor. I will say the portion was very generous and I was quite filled up after eating about 3/4 of the sandwich. The fries are decent. Served very crisp and hot out of the fryer but just a tad over salted. Nothing added nothing fancy, just plain fries.

I think this would be a better choice for take-out. Take it home to pair with a cold beer. So - it is OK. Not great, but OK.

Start spreading the news. 
Come in here today.
You want to be part of it. . . . . 

Ok, it's not New York, New York, but it's pretty good and we're so happy to have a new place Downtown that serves great food and good drink in a really cool space.

Red's (of Old 395 Grill in Carson City and The Little Wal on North Virginia) have opened a new spot right next to the Greater Nevada Field in the space which formerly housed Arroyo. 

The food - the fare is similar to what they have at the Carson Restaurant with a predominance of  Bar-B-Que and Mexican dishes. For lunch today, my husband had the Double Play Pork with a Dogfsh Head 60 IPA, I had the Salad 1868. All was very good. The shredded pork and ribs were deemed tasty and tender and came with sides and a choice of sauces. My salad was a upscale version of a taco salad with very tender smoked chicken, fresh greens, grilled corn, black beans, pineapple pico, and avocado, all served in a huge tortilla shell. It was smokey, spicy, crunchy with a hit of sweet from the pineapple. We came away stuffed.

The space is definitely visual overload. The theme is a mash-up of sports and cowboy bar. The pictures, and sports banners, and pieces of wagons, farm equipment and stage coaches adorn the walls and ceiling all evoking a much earlier age. High top tables in the bar area have Tractor Seat stools. The booths have red checked oilcloth on the tables. 

Staff are friendly and Matthew, our server, was polite and professional, took our orders quickly and checked in with us to see if all was to our liking. Everyone thanked us for coming in and made the whole experience feel welcoming. We assured them we would be back. 

These downtown blues, are melting away
I'm going to a brand new place today
Red's Broken Bat is here to stay.

I stand by what I originally posted while in the throes of chocolate intoxication - amazing handmade bites of pure bliss.

I have gone by here on numerous occasions and have resisted the temptation to stop and splurge. I finally gave in to my craven urges hoping against hope I would be horribly disappointed and not be tempted again.

Oh Dorinda, you siren of chocolate song, you purveyor of silken nuggets of phenylethylamine. How you call out to me! Your chocolates are amazing and I am doomed to be forever in your chocolate bondage.

The shop is lovely and in a perfect location along the tree-lined river walk in the elegant old neighborhood of the Powning Addition just west of downtown. It is also next door to hub coffee. With a great, shady patio area one can enjoy two favorite addictions in one place in a beautiful setting. 

I bought a four piece box of dark chocolates - sea salt caramel, peanut butte truffle, Caramel melt away, and marshmallow caramel - for $8.50. Yes it is expensive, but it is top quality with fresh ingredients. They let you sample before you buy and put your purchases in a classy little box tied up with a purple ribbon. 

So glad she moved here - otherwise I would have had to drive all the way to Truckee to get her chocolates.

Unique, tasty, and close to home.

This is a fantastic addition to our Downtown Food options. It is one of the best spots to pick up a healthy meal that is quick, clean and not the usual Tex Mex/ burger/ sandwich type place. 

This is really not fast food. When they are busy, it can take awhile to get your order, but the wait is worth it. My favorite is the Bulgogi, marinated beef, either as a "Classic" or "Top-Bab". With a cup of soup and a soft drink, it is a very filling meal. 

The staff are friendly and very helpful and always ask if you have been there before. The space is clean and modern. Seating is a bit limited and does not accommodate a large group very well. 

All items are available for take-out and they are now a part of Uber Eats. 

Highly recommended for a casual dining option.

Hands down the best place to order Pho! First of all, I was really impressed with just how cheap the Pho was! I was skeptical at first because I thought that for $9, I might be getting something basic, but after reading a couple more reviews, I decided that I wanted to see it for myself. 
So, I order Beef Pho for take-out and was told it would be ready in 15 mins. Upon arrival, it was already night time and the place hardly had street/parking lot lights so I felt weird getting out of my car alone. However, when I entered the restaurant, the restaurant was really bright and busy! There were so many people dining in that night that I was shocked. The waiter walked me to the counter to pay. 
When I finally got home and tried their broth, I was really really REALLY impressed with their broth! Even better, my mom, who's the most pickiest person in the world, was actually stunned at how delicious and spicy the broth was! The meat soaking in the broth along with all the veggie toppings were spot on! For my other order, I ordered fresh spring rolls and while the beef pho was really delicious, the spring roll was small in portion and the peanut sauce was not the traditional peanut-y sauce I'm used of! They could definitely improve on that, however. 

Overall, I enjoyed their food and will recommend to friends and family! If I'm ever in town and craving other Vietnamese food or Pho again, I will definitely go back and check this place out!

Blue willow is easily my favorite brunch spot in Tucson! We couldn't decide between savory or sweet, so we each ordered a savory meal and split a cinnamon roll pancake! The eggs Benedict was cooked perfectly and the potatoes were delicious. The chorizo scramble was also great!
The cinnamon roll pancake was an amazing texture and just the right amount of sweet!
The mimosas were self-poured, so it was easy to control the ratio of champagne:juice to ensure it was to personal preference. We can't wait to go back and try more on their menu!

I just have one thing to say. I'm not happy with the way I was treated this time. We are always here for Sunday football day but this Sunday we were treated pretty bad. 1st thing. The server took our order but then asked how we were paying, because we told her we were paying cash, she brought us our check before we even got our food or drinks. Like wow how rude is that! Then the server didn't even come back to check on us until our food was here and our check was paid! Like wow I've never been treated like this at Kilroys! Please retrain your waiter named Abrianna because customer service is definitely not her strong suit. 

Also was not given the 2 cent along with my change although it's petty it still should have been presented back to be to do as I please with.

RUDE!!!!! I can't believe how rude the guy on the phone was. Called and asked if they delivered to the Warehouse district and he said no. I said ok no problem. Then I thought of meeting the delivery guy halfway a few blocks away from their place and he said "no, we don't do that. Not gonna happen. Night" and he hung up on me! I was going to drive there if he had said no to my previous questions. But it doesn't or shouldn't hurt to ask. Then I'd never know! 

My feelings are actually hurt by how rude he was. Ouch.

BAD EXPERIENCE!

First time I've had a bad experience here. I usually try not to let little things bug me, but when it's one thing after another, sometimes I just can't handle it anymore!

So we (mom, dad, and I) came here the day before last and the wait was CRAZY! We were looking forward to eating here, but our stomachs were telling us to try again later. We come back yesterday and I really wish we hadn't come at all. 

We were seated rudely. The old ladies at the front are not so nice.

It's going to be tough to get me back in here. I wish I hadn't had such a crappy experience.

Some of the best sushi creations that have ever been tasted by my taste buds came from here.

When sitting at the sushi bar, always try to order from the specials menu - it is most definitely worth it.  The sushi chefs are always a pleasure - kind, professional and helpful with any questions you may have. 

The hibachi stations are okay, in my opinion. There are other hibachi restaurants in the area that are a little more spacious and accommodating for large parties.

My husband and I visited this restaurant yesterday. But let me tell you a quick story about GETTING THERE:

We [unfortunately] live in Baton Rouge, and we both had only one juice three hours before we left our house. Plus the one hour drive, we went four hours with nothing in our tummies. What made it worse on top of that? The endless traffic that caused our one hour trip into two. 

Ok, so now that you know exactly how HUNGRY we were, let's talk about SEED. 

I discovered Seed through Yelp, as I discover all great things in life (AKA FOOD). I walk into this beautiful, cute, clean and bright restaurant and I feel a huge sense of relief. 

The first thing I order is an appetizer and a drink. I was curious to order a cocktail because nothing makes me happier than a fresh, organic alcoholic drink, right? Well, almost nothing. I'm not an alcoholic, I swear. I just love fresh organic juices and alcohol is just a plus. So, I order a bloody mary. It was a smidgen too strong, and I say that because I wish I could have savored and appreciated the amazing tomato juice more without having to be overwhelmed by the alcohol.  

And I'm not lying when I say this, but 9 out of 10 times, I order better than my husband. But this time, he won. He ordered this Southern Fried Tofu po-boy. And I ordered the club sandwich and added some avocado. So I have to make it clear to you that at some point while visiting this place, you MUST TRY THAT POBOY. It's out of this world, and definitely one of the best po-boys I've had in my life thus far, and that's saying a lot. 

The staff is super friendly and chill. The ambience is simple and clean with local art on display, which I must say was super adorable. Whoever the artist is, I'm eager to find out because I'd love a piece. 

Looking forward to visiting again and highly recommended to people who appreciate clean eating. Note: IF YOU EAT LIKE SHIT, DON'T COME HERE. YOUR TASTE BUDS ARE SO F*ED UP AND YOUR BODY IS SO FULL OF TOXINS, YOU WILL NOT BE ABLE TO APPRECIATE THE CRAFT IT TAKES TO PUT THIS PLACE TOGETHER. 

Yours truly,

Cristy C.

This place is absolutely disgusting and filthy. The floors and coumters and tables are sticky to the touch. The food is bland and overpriced. The bathrooms smelled terrible and there were bugs crawling around. I cannot believe this place can pass an inspection to stay open!

This has to be the best reason to go to Pinellas County!  Every chance I get, I swing by Mazzaro's and order a #18 sandwich at the deli:  the Sesame Tuna Wasabi!  Okay, so I'm a Pescatarian and have not had their famous meat sandwiches, but I'm really okay with that!  This sandwich is amazing! On buttered and grilled sliced Italian bread, with generous portions of tuna and a creamy wasabi sauce, topped with sliced ginger and alfalfa sprouts - this is simply heaven.  The sandwich is pretty big, but I have to stop myself from gorging on the entire thing - which is not easy to do!!  And I want to definitely save some for later.  Delayed gratification is good for the soul.

While I go to the deli, get a number and wait to place my order, my hubby heads to the coffee counter, gets us 2 seats and orders us large cappuccinos.  We sip on the coffee while we wait for our order to be yelled from the deli, then I go over, pick them up, and head back over to our seats to enjoy the best lunch ever.

Going there on a Saturday is an experience.  If crowds make you nervous, then forget about it!  But if you want to truly experience Mazzaro's, then Saturday it is.  But get there before 2pm when they close.  Once your belly is full, you can then squeeze your way over to the bakery and grab another number to place your order for delicious Italian cookies or pastries.  I always order the Regina cookies and an assortment of their fruit-filled cookies.  Then we make our way over to the wine and cheese area to see how much trouble we can get in!

We never leave empty handed.  The soups and pastas that are in the refrigerated section just before the cash registers are a must!  We usually get the Pasta Fagioli or the Minestrone soups; they have delicious Lobster Mac & Cheese, as well as several kinds of Lasagna and other pasta dishes.

Parking can be a nightmare, but they have a HUGE parking lot, so even if you don't get to park close to the building, you'll still get a spot.  I consider it part of my workout since I usually waddle out of the building.

Don't miss out on this place!  Plan your day around it and you will never be the same again.

Anise has quickly become one of my favorite places to eat and drink. I am a huge fan of their late night hours and late night menu. I love the unique ambiance and the modern interior decor. Most of all, I love that it is conveniently located because all we need to do is take an elevator downstairs from Skypoint. 

I have been here three times in the past week! I have had many of the menu items here ranging from the Truffled Tater Tots with the Creme Fraiche to the Jap Chae. Everything I have ordered has been very good and you cannot go wrong with any of your food choices at Anise. 

The cocktails are fantastic, as well. Surprise...I have had a few of those, too! Some of my favorites are the Lychee Love Hotel and the Hibiscus Margarita. Anise also partners with some of the local breweries and features their beers on tap. 

We were here last late Tuesday night. John was our server for the second time in the past week, and was very friendly and attentive. I had just left a Yelp Steak Event, so I was pretty full and wanted something light to munch on. We decided on the Jap Chae with Tofu and the Tomato and Jalapeño flatbread. 

The Jap Chae, was very good, as usual. I decided to think outside the box and try the Flatbread, sans tomatoes, of course. I was pleasantly surprised. The Jalapeño bacon was not too spicy. I mean, seriously, how could I not want to eat bacon? 

We both had the Green Bench Brewing Sour Lager. I enjoyed it, as it has been a trend for me to enjoy all the sour beers lately. 

We still have yet to order dessert here, but I have a feeling that may change sooner than later. 

Once again, another no brainer, I will definitely be back.

#300!!

I normally dedicate every 50th review to one of my favorite restaurants, but I decided to make an exception tonight because this is sure to become one of them. I have driven by this place several times thinking it was sure to be yet ANOTHER sushi restaurant but I was so happy to find out they were specializing in ramen! 

Japanese Kitchen Dosunco just opened yesterday (7/28) and I love that they have been totally under the radar because we were able to get in for dinner and it wasn't crowded at all. Of course, I was very cocky walking in because I thought for sure I would be the first Yelp Elite to eat here. Lo and behold, Josh W was at a table with his beautiful family to the right of me and Mark P was sitting to the left of me!! 

The restaurant is simply decorated and very clean. We were greeted right away as we walked in by the entire staff like we were walking into a Japanese Moe's...and I loved it! 

I started with an Asahi beer. It was only $6 for the huge bottle and very good. My dining companion started with the Sake, which was equally good.

I ordered an Appetizer Sampler which consisted of Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken), Cream Coquettes, and Gyoza. Everything was so delicious, but the fried chicken was my favorite! 

Next, I ordered the Onigiri, which were the rice balls filled with Tuna with Mayo. The rice balls were very good, too!

For my entree I ordered the Miso Ramen. It was chock full of roast pork, ground beef, bean sprouts, bamboo shoots, green onion, and a seasoned egg. It was so tasty and exactly the ramen I had been craving since my favorite ramen joint had closed months ago. 

THINGS YOU NEED TO KNOW BEFORE YOU DINE HERE:

1.) They just opened and are trying to iron out the kinks of being a new restaurant. They are still looking to hire more staff and please note that English is not their primary language so please be patient with them.

2.) The food is here is MADE TO ORDER. If you are expecting to be in and out of the restaurant, you will be disappointed. Everything is delicious, is not pre-made, and if I must say so myself, worth the wait.

3.) Yes, the broth may bit a salty for some of you but it is soy based. But, I also am not a ramen expert and am a saltaholic! 

Definitely check Japanese Kitchen Dosunco out. Everything we ordered was so delicious that I will be putting this place on my weekly rotation. The staff was very friendly and did a great job taking care of us. 

Go get yourself some delicious ramen before the word gets out!

I always seem to forget about Tampa Bay Brewing Company because it isn't located on 7th Avenue, the main strip of Ybor. I like coming to their restaurant because they are always consistent with their good food and great service. 

Last night our server was Emily. She was very friendly and attentive, despite the restaurant being very busy from the craziness of the Snow on 7th Parade and it being a Saturday. 

It was a brisk night, so, I started with the gumbo. It wasn't too bad, it just needed a little more flavoring. To continue with the theme of comfort food, I ordered the grilled cheese sandwich off the kids menu (shhhhh!) with Tater Tots. Both were perfect for this rare cold night in Tampa. Most of TBBC dishes are good and you really can't go wrong with what you choose to order. 

The management staff is always helpful here. I have hosted parties of up to 20 people in their back room and they have always been able to accommodate me.

I have always been able to be seated quickly with not too long of a wait. The restaurant is very spacious so even when it is busy, you don't feel cramped. 

TBBC is always a great place to have a nice casual meal in Ybor with a wide variety of menu items if you can't quite pinpoint what you are craving. Oh yeah...their beers are pretty good, too!

I like this location which is conveniently located next to Amalie Arena. I also enjoy sitting outside on the patio when the weather isn't so blistering hot. The restaurant has stepped it up a notch by replacing the umbrellas providing little shade to diners with a roof complete with exterior fans. It also looks like the roof has been outfitted to install misters for those rare hot and humid days in Tampa. While sitting on the patio, you are also treated to a serene view of the Tampa Riverwalk. 

Unlike our fearless leader, CM Brett N., I do happen to like most of food at the Columbia. The menu at this location is limited and does not offer the extensive menu options like its sister locations. 

I am a creature of habit and I seem to usually order the same thing here: the Spanish Bean Soup and the 1905 Salad. I enjoy the heartiness of the soup filled with chorizo and garbanzo beans. I love the savory taste of the 1905 Salad Dressing. These two dishes are normally quick to come out of the kitchen. Normally...

The marginal service here is my reason for two stars. During my recent dining experiences at this location, the server has been extremely inefficient and inattentive. Servers were slow to greet the table, to grab drink/food orders, and  had to be reminded several times to refill drinks. A couple of orders were incorrect coming out of the kitchen. If you take a look at several reviews of my Fellow Yelpers, they express a common theme:  Bad service. 

I really like this location but service needs to be improved. Staff needs to be trained on timing, being more attentive, and how to be more efficient while multi-tasking. There should be a host or hostess that should be hired to alleviate some of the servers' tasks like meeting and greeting, menu distribution, and drink orders. 

For being Tampa's #1 restaurant on several Tampa Bay Foodie Lists, this location needs to step it up in order to live up to its title.

Pho Viet is a small Vietnamese restaurant that is located in a remodeled Pizza Hut. The decoration is minimal but the food quality makes up for the lack of ambiance. The staff working here is very friendly, efficient, and attentive. 

We started with the fried tofu and the veggie rolls (Gôi Cuón Chay). Both appetizers were very good. 

For my entree, I ordered the Superbowl of Pho Dac  Biet, the combination beef noodle soup. This massive bowl was chock full of meatballs, sliced beef, brisket, tendon, and tripe. It was delicious. The broth needed a little salt, but then again, I am a saltaholic. The Superbowl was so large that I had leftover pho for days! 

My friend order the Pho Ga, the chicken pho and she enjoyed her food, as well.

If you don't mind a minimally decorated remodeled Pizza Hut that serves delicious no-frills Vietnamese cuisine, this is definitely the place for you. The food is good and is worth the stop.

I have been frequenting Happy Fish for many years. I was sad last year to hear that former owners decided to move overseas. I used to eat here so much that I actually became friends with their son, Percy, and we still keep in touch, even though he has moved away, too. 

Luckily, the transition to the new owner, Kevin, has been a smooth one. Kevin has done a great job in taking over. He has totally remodeled the interior and it looks beautiful. Kevin's passion for Happy Fish is evident when he talks about his food and his restaurant. 

I have had most everything on Happy Fish's menu and you can't go wrong with anything you order. Some of my favorite appetizers are the Salchipapas (French fries and sliced hot dogs) and the Anticuchos (Grilled Beef Heart marinated in Steak Sauce). 

The lunch specials are a great value. I normally order the ceviche special which also includes their delicious Chcken Noodle soup or Papa Huancaina, which are potatoes cooked in a creamy sauce. The portion of ceviche you are served is huge. I always end up taking leftovers home and it is good for about two more meals for me.

Other entrees I enjoy other than the Ceviche Mixto are the Jalea Mixto (lightly breaded fish, shrimp, calamari, and mussels), the Chaufa (Fried Rice with Chicken, Beef, or Seafood), and the Lomo Saltado (Lean Beef). 

Although I try to stay away from soda, I have to always order an Inca Cola to wash my food down. If you have never tried one, you are depriving yourself. It is a delicious sweet soda with a huge caffeine jolt. 

Kevin, William, and his staff are very friendly and a pleasure to deal with. Sometimes, there may be a language barrier or two, but just be patient. Kevin cares about his customers and leaves the kitchen often to check in with his patrons.

I stopped by yesterday to assist my Yelp friend, Steve, with the UYE details with our Latin Crawl happening on 2/21/15. Kevin graciously treated us to a wonderful Peruvian dessert, Picarones. It was a pastry topped with a delicious sweet sauce that normally takes 4-5 hours to make. It was so sinfully good. 

If you haven't tried Happy Fish, it is a moral imperative in my book. You will definitely want to come back again and again.

I am so in love with Ulele, I decided to come back a second time.  We had a late reservation last Friday for 9:45 and it worked out perfectly since we were wrapping up First Friday at The Still in the Heights right down the road. 

We got there a few minutes early, so we were able to order some drinks from Javier at the bar. We ordered a Native Sun and a Pale Ale. I wasn't a fan of the Pale Ale. It was a little too bland for me. The Native Sun was refreshing but not my favorite. It may have been because I had been drinking sweet drinks prior to our arrival. 

I also asked Javier about the Wedding Beer that wasn't ready Opening Week. Well, before I even blinked an eye, Tim, the Brewmaster was standing right next to me ready to whisk me away for a taste of the first batch! Talk about feeling special! The Wedding Beer was ready but they weren't going to release to the public until the next day. I felt honored that I was able to try the very first batch! And let me tell you, the Wedding Beer is the best of all of the beers. 

Erin was our server and was very pleasant and attentive. We started with the Lobster Cake which was made from fresh, live, butter-poached lobster tail meat, cast iron seared, served with Cucumber Ginger Salad. I could not get enough of the Lobster Cake, it was so tasty. Jeff practically had to pull the plate away, so I wouldn't lick it. 

But ahhhh...the Crab Mac n' Cheese...was just pure heaven. I was so happy I got finally try it with someone who didn't mind the Crab in the Mac n' Cheese.  No offense, Dorene, love you! We practically inhaled the Mac n' cheese in less than five minutes. 

For my entree I ordered the Crackling Pork Shank, which was 1 1/2 pound of crispy pork shank with firecracker apple craisin chutney. Ummmm....wow. It was an unimaginable amount of meat! I am not a chutney fan whatsoever, but the pork was so tender and very delicious. I had leftovers for days! 

My date ordered the Waterworks Meatloaf made of Ground dry-aged strip loin, Cabernet garlic demi-glaze, served with white cheddar popcorn mash and Tobacco onions. Seriously? It was so good! I couldn't stop laughing because Jeff kept eating my mashed potatoes and when he found some on his dish, he was like a kid on Christmas morning. 

We decided to skip dessert and have some closer to home. Before we left, we walked along the Riverwalk. Lucky for us, it was a nice night and not too humid.  Make sure to plan time before or after your meal to walk along the Riverwalk, it is truly gorgeous.
 
No brainer here. Ulele is STILL five stars for me and I will definitely be back again and again.

Disappointed.

I was excited to try this place out after trying their pizza at the 2016 Taste of the Heights. Now that I think back, their stop was one of the ones towards the end and I may have been a little tipsy. 

I got to the restaurant and I just wanted a pepperoni pizza to go. A gentleman and a customer were at the counter and had no idea what they were doing with the register screen and took forever. Then, after ringing the previous customer up, he preceded to make his pizza. Ummmm? He couldn't have taken my quick order? 

I stood at the counter for at least fifteen minutes before anyone took my order. Another gentleman who had returned from delivering pizza, finally took my order.  I also ordered an empanada to try one out.

After what seemed like an eternity, my pizza was ready. A woman working handed it to me, but they had forgotten my empanada. I looked towards the kitchen and they threw in some sort of frozen one in. I asked her to stick my pizza in the oven to keep it hot. 

Finally, after another ten minutes, my empanada was ready. The woman handed me my pizza (WHICH SHE DID NOT KEEP WARM) and my empanada. 

I took a bite of the empanada in my car, and I almost vomited. The empanada smelled liked ass and was not cooked fully! 

The pizza was just as anticlimactic. It was cold and taste like cardboard. The only reason I gave them two stars is the fact that their pizza is priced inexpensively compared to other nearby pizza places.

STAY AWAY. FAR AWAY.

When I heard the name "Lee's Grocery," I was a bit skeptical. Then, when we reached our destination, I was worried about the neighborhood. But, wow...Lee's Grocery is a delightful hidden gem in the Seminole Heights area! Sorry Brett...I like using the clichés! 

Do not let any of your preconceived notions deceive you. Lee's Grocery is not a grocery store, but indeed a full-fledged stone-baked pizza joint with a HUGE selection of beer. The restaurant is clean with a spacious back patio. Oh, and did I mention that there is a lot of beer here? 

Like most places in Tampa Heights, Lee's Grocery bleeds the hipster vibe. I like it. But, what I love the most about this place is, the decor. There are albums and posters of various 80s bands that are near and dear to my heart, scattered throughout the restaurant. 

We ordered the wings and the "Bring the Noise" pizza which was chock-full of toppings. Both the wings and pizza tasted very good. And as for the beer, we started out with one of the ciders and ended up taking bottles of the Rekorderling Berry Cider and the St. Louis Framboise home. 

Jamie was the bartender tonight and was very friendly and efficient. 

I will definitely come back and can't wait to take my foodie friends here to experience this hidden gem.

Yay! Another Tampa Bay Area Brewery I can cross off my list...well, kind of.

After attending a prior event, I met my friends here. I am not too familiar with St. Pete so I was proud of myself for not getting lost. The brewery was packed and there were many cars in the parking lot, which, is not well lit. 

I entered through the warehouse. There was a comedy show going on and there were a ton of people out for weekday night. There is a giant Connect Four,  cornhole, and a ton of other fun games and things to keep yourself busy. 

I finally made my way into the bar itself and it wasn't too crowded. The vibe was great in here. There was a large group of people who were enjoying their beers and had also ordered pizza delivered in. My friends were playing Cards Against Humanity, which was just cracking me up! 

We sat at the bar and I tasted my friend's Beach Blonde Ale. And I sat there, and I sat there. Neither of the two women behind the bar never said a word to me. Ummm, hello? I was not too pleased. I wasn't feeling well anyways, but I would have liked to taste a flight or something. 

They weren't busy, so that can't be the reasoning for ignoring me. I wasn't even greeted "hello." 

I have had a couple of beers from 3 Daughters Brewery at several of the bars in DTSP. To be honest with you, I wasn't wowed with either of them. 

Would I come back? Hmmmm...not too sure. I am one of those people who is HUGE on customer service. Forgettable brews + bad customer service = probably not.

I was blessed to have been invited to go to not one, but two new restaurants in Tampa during their Opening Week in August. Lucky for me, Roux, was one of them. Roux is the birthchild of Datz's founders, Suzanne and Roger Perry. They have enjoyed the success of both Datz and Dough, and Roux will definitely be adding to that. There are still some kinks to be ironed out, though. 

The food served at Roux is Creole themed. The NOLA inspired decor is beautifully evident throughout the restaurant from the artwork to the tables. 

We had a late reservation for the evening and checked in at the hostess station. The restaurant was packed, so there was a minimal wait for our table. They informed us that they would let us know as soon as our table was ready. 

Of course, we decided to grab a drink at the beautiful bar while we waited. My friend, John, the General Manager of Roux, suggested the Vieux Carre. The Vieux Carre was made of a mix of Mitcher's Rye, Camu Cognac, Dolin Sweet Vermouth, Benedictine, and bitters. Wow...what a drink. It was quite potent and I was glad I was not driving!

The bar was gorgeous! Mark and Josh, our bartenders for the night, were easy on the eyes, as well! Mark and Josh were very friendly, attentive, and easy to get to know. One thing missing from the bar was a TV. There is space on the side walls to maybe install televisions later down the road, but the management decided against TVs at this time. 

We waited for over half an hour, and the hostesses had not yet updated us about our table. I took the liberty of talking to the hostess who then told me that they wanted us to enjoy our drinks but our table was indeed ready. I was disappointed at this. These hostesses should have let us know so we at least had the option of finishing our drinks at the bar or our table. 

We were then sat at our table. Like I stated earlier, the NOLA inspired decor is throughout the restaurant, including the tables. The bistro style setup was a little too close for comfort for me due the tables being so close together. I was not a big fan of Grandma sitting at the table next to ours listening to my conversation. So, quickly, we opted to sit at the bar. Besides, I would rather look at Mark and Josh instead of Grandma!

Upon returning back to the bar, we immediately put in our order because by this time we were starving. We decided to do several appetizers, sides, and an entree. We ordered the following:

Bayou Frog Legs which were buttermilk battered served with a mirlington slaw and a chive remoulade and a saffron remoulade. These were delicious! I haven't had frog legs in years and yes, they still taste like chicken!

Abita Beer-Battered Crab Beignets served with four remoulades:  saffron, cayenne, chive, and blanc. The beignets were a perfect consistency and very tasty. All remoulades were fantastic! 

Char-grilled Oysters which were served with Romano, Parmesan, and a the Roux compound butter. These were fantastic and we could not get enough of them. I wished we had ordered a full order, but we had ordered so much food as it is! 

Smoked Mac n Cheese - phenomenal! 

Benton's Bacon Brussel's Sprouts - very good with a good portion of bacon...yum!

Crawfish Monique a la Roux served with a shaved botargo, Louisana Crawfish, Sauce Monique, angel hair pasta, and Tasso ham. Incredible! Very rich and creamy and I love the pasta combined with the sauce and crawfish. 

All in all, the food was delicious! I am traveling to New Orleans later this year and this restaurant has made me even more excited for my trip!

We were entirely too stuffed to eat dessert, but we will definitely be back. In fact, lucky me, I will be back this Saturday for a Yelp Elite event!

Not really sure there is much else that can be said about the Hyppo. Enjoying Popsicles in the Florida heat and humidity is a win. 

You will be sure to find a popsicle that you will enjoy here. There are a myriad of flavors that customers can choose from. Did I mention that the popsicles were tasty? 

The staff is always pleasant and efficient here. The store is spotless because the employees are constantly cleaning. 

In addition to popsicles, the Hyppo also offers accessories that you can utilize to make your own! They also sell cute t-shirts, enamel pins, and other tchotchkes. 

My only gripe is that I wish there was seating outdoors. There isn't too much room outside of the storefront, so unfortunately this may never possible. So heads up, be prepared to take your popsicle to go.

Arepitas is a cute little Venezuelan/Lebanese Cafe located near the USF area. My Yelp brother from another mother, Jason C and my friend Dorene M, decided on this restaurant prior to a Yelp event at Busch Gardens.

The staff was friendly here and there were three people working but only one behind the counter. Jeremiah was very friendly and took time to explain all my food options, but I felt awful because a line was starting to form and he was the only one behind the counter.

You can choose to have your meal served in an arepa or a pita. I found this concept to be fascinating  since I had never seen Venezuelan and Lebanese cuisine paired together. 

I wanted something different so I settled on the Venezuelan Arepa with black beans, pulled beef, and white cheese. I had the fried plantains served on the side and not in the arepa. I get creeped out by mixing sweet and salty.  The food was delicious and was definitely a bigger portion than I had imagined. The arepa (as you can see in the picture) was stuffed full. 

I wish there was an Arepitas location close to me in South Tampa. I would definitely be back more often if I lived in the vicinity.

So far, Romi's Tacos is my contender for favorite tacos in the Brandon area. Tucked away in a non-descript shopping plaza in Brandon, it is easy to miss this hidden gem. 

I walked in and was greeted by Jesus who was very friendly and attentive. I ordered the Combo Special #15 of three tacos with beans and rice, and a drink. All combo specials are $8. Yes...eight dollars. Such a great value. 

I ordered my usual taco trio: chicharron, steak, and chorizo. I normally am not a fan of the soft chicharron tacos because of the weird consistency, but these were actually were full of flavor. The steak taco was also flavorful and the taste of the chorizo was a perfect "medium" in terms of spiciness. The beans and rice were also very good. 

I look forward to going back to try some of the other menu offerings including their soups and fried fish.

The trouble with the rise of cupcake shops opening is that most of them are just fluff and icing. I love frosting just as much as the next person, but there is such a thing as TOO MUCH icing. Sure the cupcakes are decorated beautifully, but how do they REALLY taste? 

At times, I have found many of Gigi's cupcakes to be dry. Are they trying to overcompensate for this with the enormous amount of frosting on the cupcake? 

GiGi's cupcakes aren't the worst, but they certainly  are not the best either. I do not normally question the prices of things if I believe they are worth the money. There are several independently owned bakeries in Tampa who bake a much better cupcake that are most certainly worth every penny.

Culver's was recommended to me by several friends and my boss, who loves bringing his son here. I am not a hamburger person, but I was in the neighborhood so I thought I would give it a try.

The line actually moved quickly and I found the "pick up" area for the food was interesting. The staff member who brought my food out to me was very friendly. 

I ordered the the original butterburger, fries, and the Wisconsin Cheese Curds. Although the fries were a bit undercooked, everything was good. The food was so good, I forgot to take some pictures. 

If I am in the neighborhood, I would definitely return. I am happy that this location and the one on Hillsborough are not located too close to me. It would be too convenient just to run through the drive-thru!

I had the pleasure of stopping by Big Ray's yesterday for lunch. Big Ray's is a "seafood shack" on Interbay Boulevard in a wee building that if you blink, you will definitely miss it. My rating is a 4.5 so I rounded up. 

I was greeted warmly by Lindsey and Ray, himself. I was a bit overwhelmed by the extended menu on the wall, but I decided to order the special, the Oyster Po Boy, which included one side. Lindsey recommended the onion rings so I chose those. Then I saw Cronuts on the menu board and all hell broke loose...

Food turnover was very quick and my Oyster Po Boy was placed in the cutest classic Shrimp Packing box. The onion rings were served in separately in another container. Both portions were very generous. The Cronuts were bite-sized and came five to a bag.

The Oyster Po Boy was delicious. There was a bit too much bread for me, but I am not a Po Boy expert. Maybe I will add extra oysters next time? I loved the onion rings. There were thin and salty, just the way I like them. I enjoyed the Cronuts, too. They were a perfect ending to my "fried festival" and I had some leftover to munch on for later. 

The restaurant is decorated in a nautical and fishing theme. There is minimal seating in the restaurant with a few tables and chairs. There is also seating by the window at an extended table. Because the building is located on a small lot, parking is limited, also. 

I will definitely return because I want to try the grouper cheeks and other menu items. If you want to stay away from the fried food, they do have salads. PS - if you eat like a child like I do, they also have corn dogs too!!!

Thai Island is one of my top three favorite Thai restaurants in Tampa Bay. Their food and service are consistently excellent. The restaurant is always clean and their staff is very friendly and attentive. I also love this restaurant because it isn't such a "scene."

Tonight I met my friend Alicia P for dinner here and we started with the Thai Island Special. This appetizer is perfect if you have no clue what to begin with. It is a generous serving of crab rangoons, corn fritters, spring rolls, and chicken satay. Everything was sinfully good. 

For my entree I ordered the Panang Curry with beef. It was highly recommended by several Yelp friends, so I knew I couldn't go wrong. It was definitely a solid choice. The portion was generous and very delicious. 

The only downside to Thai Island is the same with all businesses on Davis Island: limited parking. The secret is to park at the bank next door after hours or park on the side streets. 

Thai Island is a favorite for many of the residents of DI. Not only is this restaurant consistently busy inside, they have a strong take-out following. If you choose to dine in, you will see the steady stream of people picking up their to-go orders. I highly recommend this restaurant for a good Thai meal in South Tampa and I am sure a majority of the people who live on DI will agree with me.

I was craving a Banh Mi thanks to Rachel M earlier this week so I drove to the closest Vietnamese restaurant that was in the area. Well...apparently, I had stayed away too long because the restaurant had closed. 

Several doors down was First Choice, begging me to walk through its doors. I practically ran to it, like a lost child running back to her mother. 

Go ahead and make fun of me, I like to eat early. Call me old or whatever you like ha ha, but I despise crowds. Lucky for me, I had walked into First Choice right when they had just opened their doors. 

Getting early to First Choice is crucial. Crucial, because there is less of a wait. Otherwise, the line is out the door. No thanks. For those who know me, I have zero patience. 

What has not changed is that these guys are the BBQ Nazis like the Soup Nazi on Seinfeld. You better know what you want or else you will be in trouble! Don't be scared though, the staff is firm, but friendly here. 

Being a creature of habit, I always order the same thing here: sausage with baked beans and french fries. Mmmmmmm sausage!!!

As usual, the sausage was delicious. The fries were a bit soggy for me. And, the baked beans were good, but the cinnamon they added overpowered the taste of the beans. Next time, I plan to finally change it up with the sides. 

First Choice is definitely one of the best BBQ joints in this area. Their food is delicious and the portions are such a good value. The staff here is friendly and very efficient at getting you in and out of their restaurant. Tables are limited but turnover is normally quick. 

Ahhh...First Choice. I have missed you, my love. I promise it won't be two years before I see you again.

Oh. My. God!  This place is literally a hidden gem!!!!  I got a gift certificate from Restaurant.com and decided to give this place a try since I love Mexican food.  I was highly impressed with everything. I had the veggie burrito and it was as authentic as being in Mexico. It was perfect!  I also got an appetizer which was layered with fresh crab meat, avocado, tomatoes and lettuce.  My husband and I were literally fighting over it!!!  We also got dessert which was a vanilla cake. So, with 2 entrees, 1 appetizer and dessert, our bill came to $26!  I couldn't even use the gift certificate (min of $37). We plan on going back with some friends. It's also a BYOB which I loved!! We brought our own margaritas :)

Savory & Sweet crepes were amazing! Cafe con Leche was great, too. Cute place that a local took us to on our trip to Tampa, and we enjoyed it very much. 

I loved my Bon Curry Chicken savory crepe- very filling and interesting! The teens devoured their sweet crepes in 60 seconds or less. Nice atmosphere for smaller groups or for couples.

Overall a solid craft brewery in the Philly burbs. We arrived shortly before the rest of our party, so bellied up to the bar. I ordered two of the 4 oz. pours, because I like to change it up on the palate, when comparing beers. My only complaint here is No Flights Here- no more than one 4 oz. pour at a time. That's a little bit ridiculous, compared to say- every other tasting room in the country. Others have stated this, so perhaps they'll change their practice to meet a collective desire for flights. 

The beer was good, and changes often. Hophands was good. Saison Hands was my favorite. I rated everything around 4 stars on Untappd. The space is popular, but our group of five had no problem getting a table 6:30pm on a Sunday night. The space is industrial, but I found it more inviting than other tap rooms, and expected it to be much noisier than it actually was. 

The burger, made with Hophands mustard and whiskey dills was great. And the taco options looked awesome.

I bought some stickers which I'll make into magnets, and staff were very helpful and pleasant! I'll be back for sure.

Jenny H. gives a good representation of what's "supposed to" happen at Mother's, but it rarely is that "easy". Something akin to the Soup Nazi meets Cranky Motherly Love Service, is more like it. I ordered a drink. Do I have to ask for it? Yes, I do. Even though I was just chided for asking if I can help myself to water, I guess it's okay to ask for my cola that wasn't going to be gotten, otherwise.

Other diners asked us, once seated, if they would be getting their food delivered. Only because we had been waited on did we know. Have gotten the Ferdi before and it was awesome, but way too much meat for this li'l guy to finish. 

This visit was 2/3 ham po' boy with side of gumbo. Sandwich was exellent, and so glad I ordered the gumbo. Plan on waiting here, being confused or ignored, and not eating for the rest of the day!

I've been working week long Conferences in New Orleans for five years, and I'm no stranger to bars and restaurants here, and great service in New Orleans. The service industry is such a huge part of New Orleans, I've got nothing but admiration for the patience and hard work of servers. I had such a bad server experience at Backspace- it was bizarre, and seemed purposely directed, so much so that an acquaintance of mine also seated at the bar stepped in to call it out. 

After working 50 hours in 3 days at my Conference, I was super stoked to get a burger and a beer here after reading all the great reviews. Bellied up to the bar, asked for a menu, and ordered an Amber. It came in a plastic cup, which was the first strike when obviously dining in.  Then when I got my food, the bartender talked loudly about his bowel movements in front of me while I was eating, and joked about doing so. And here's when bad service felt like it was being done purposefully, I'm not a naive diner. My friend seated nearby comes to Backspace whenever he's in town, and called the server out (that's how obviously gauche the service was). 

New Orleans is great for its choices when going out, and I'm happy to Yelp about those great experiences, and spend my dollars elsewhere.

Monell's stole the 5 stars in my little black book of southern food! 

Monell's should be voted to end world hunger and make world peace along with turning everything into green meadows, chocolate, unicorns, and rainbows...

Monell's joins the people you don't know aka strangers into a family style dining!  After brunch, the couple you didn't know from Adam sitting across the table are your new BFFs... you've exchanged numbers and you're inviting them to your firstborns communion!   

What may have caused this happy-fear-not-love your neighbor feeling? I don't know, perhaps the owner sprinkled some magic dust on all the guests as they were so friendly welcomed in, perhaps it's the fact of immediately upon sitting having been served baskets and baskets of food, perhaps it's the secret recipe in the homemade biscuits, cheesy grits, potatoes, pancakes, bacon, sausage, fried chicken, apples, or the sweet tea! 

Whatever it is, it worked! We all left happy, our bellies full, well wishing everyone that crossed our path, spreading love and praying for world peace. 

Monell's you did it again and I Love You!

Wow what a view sitting on the edge of Clearwater beach
Eating a great dinner.Had a live band tonight playing sum old school music. Our waiter who's name was John was excellent.He made sure we had everything you needed for a excellent dinner.The house salad was very good , my steak was cooked perfect medium,great baked potato and a vegetable melody of carrots,broccoli n green beans. Great view and great music you have to try this place!!!!!!

This lil restaurant is right across the street from the beach.If you like playing cornhole they have it in front of the restaurant. I had the 1/2 lb of peel n eat shrimp very good,big shrimp also had the Baridi crab so sweet n delicious.they have drink specials throughout the night.
Great service got seated fast,Very good place to eat

Let's start off by saying no Air at all except inside we're u order,then off to the patio we're you sweat your arse off waiting for your food.
So it's all outside sitting,so while you wait your beer gets hott within minutes.
Now the food" tacos was ok not my kinda of tacos,I'm not into shredded beef,chips n a lil cup of salsa. Mehh 
Now the fish n chips was pretty good if anything I'd come back for them.
Had they had the air working out on patio maybe a 3.5 Star!!!!

Was craving some Mexican food so we stopped in here to give it a try. Glad we shared a taco first to see how it tasted.not my kind of food had no taste beans were bland.the salsa tasted like store bought. It was nice n clean plus the air was working but other than that not my kind of tacos!!!!

Giving this a 5 star rating it has everything hands down. If your looking to sit and relax after a day on the beach here's your place. Great cold beer and a great view to watch the sunsets. We ordered fish n chips it came out hot n crispy it was excellent. The fried shrimp was as good as it gets as well. Great service and friendly!!! So if your looking for a great place to hang out and to get a cold Beer look no further. 
Be sure to go on the 3rd floor to catch the sunset absolutely amazing!!!

This was the worst dining experience I've EVER had in my ENTIRE life.  Let me start off by saying I was a Groupon customer.  

We made a reservation for 7:30pm at the skybar (outside) and we got seated INSIDE at 9pm!!!  And the place wasn't even crowded.  It was a beautiful Tuesday night, and the skybar wasn't  even open.  So we got drinks at the bar while waiting for eternity.  Afterwards, they told us our Groupon couldn't be used at the bar.  #1 it doesn't say that on the Groupon, and I told them I had one when we sat down, and #2 DID YOU WANT US TO STAND THERE FOR AN HOUR AND 30 MINUTES?!!?  We had to remind them we had a reservation twice. 

Once we were finally seated, we were informed since our drinks were $15 each, they weren't covered because the Groupon was only for $14 drinks.  I demanded we pay the difference (OF ONE DOLLAR), they said no, then came back and said yes and acted like they were doing US a favor.  

The food came out pretty quick.  It was OK.  Honestly, the sushi rolls were small compared to prices and other sushi experiences I've had.  The sushi just wasn't that fresh either.

We were so excited to leave until they couldn't even split the check though they took both of our cards away and said they could.  If you don't like Groupon customers, then don't DO Groupon.  

It was a horrible experience from the moment we walked into the door when no one greeted us and we just stood there like hmmm how do we get a table?  

I can't even imagine how bad service is when they're crowded if they can't even handle 7 tables.  I would never ever come back here for any amount of money.

Break out the shades and make sure you're ready for a cool steady breeze. Ladies and gentlemen, Philly has a bad ass beer garden going on the 51st floor.  Talk about those magnificent views overlooking  all of Philly. From the Art Museum, Billy Penn over looking the Philadelphians, surrounding boroughs, down to the Ben Franklin Bridge. Yelpers, make sure you have that camera ready because, where ever you stand there is an incredible sight to be seen. 

It could be day or night you'll see it all with the hustle and bustle of the city coming alive. The bright lights of the city all around you, the trails of lights coming from the cars driving thru the evening all can be somewhat mesmerizing. 

I don't know a better way where one could enjoy a craft or two or three than here at the SkyGarten. I must say my first visit I was with Sari for a 4th of July event where they had an open bar with a buffet. The weather was kinda muggy, ok  it went from drizzling where it was bearable, to ok time to go inside. Inside you can also keep the party going with tables and a giant screen with something always on it. That is in case the weather decides to do a complete 180 on you, or maybe you don't want to get blown away.

In all this a great hot spot that keeps on getting hotter. Get in there and stand next to those skyscrapers, while giving a toast to Billy. I know I'll be back.

Find parking, take the train, or get yourself an Uber/Lyft  and just make a "B" line to Gran Caffe L'Aquilla! That is all you need to know, because what ever you get from here will simply be AMAZING! I see you are still looking at my review waiting for some more information than the whole "B" line shtick. I suppose a picture or 2 might stimulate your appetite to know more about Gran Caffe. Let's get serious now my Yelp family, serious like a kid to funnel cake serious. Get a glass of your favorite wine, because this will not be a short review. 

                                              ~Appetizers~  
*Polipo (Grilled Octopus) ~ This savory appetizer had me moaning I tell you. Picture getting punched in the face, but with out the pain that follows a punch. If perfection had a picture to follow it, this dish is it.
*Arancini ~ A decadent Sicilian dish, which is a lightly fried rice ball. A rice ball made in a ragu, which is stuffed with a mixture of veal and pork. All being held together with mozzarella cheese, laying over top their sauce mixed with peas for added pleasures. 
*Arrosticini Abruzzese ~ Your choice of either chicken or lamb with this dish folks. Lamb for the win, with their Calabrese dipping sauce that had a subtle kick to it. Honestly dipping it, or not, it's still badass.

                                              ~Our Meals~
The "Gelato" Pairings is something that needs to be taken advantage of it immediately. This is literally biblical, where you will be singing praises to the Gods above. The creativity, and uniqueness can not be described on Yelp. I implore you to order a dish from this amazing menu. Basically any dish from this sectioned off menu will be a winning dish.
                                              My Gelato Pairing
*Agnoletti al Tartufo ~ This elegant dish is homemade raviolis stuffed with veal, pork, onions with an herb that had me wanting to scream out obscenities with that butter sage sauce. The gelato that was paired with this dish is their black and white truffle gelato. You mix the gelato with your dish and you've just brought this to a whole new level of satisfaction.  Yelpers, this sinful combination, this dynamic duo will make you feel like you are having an affair. 1 word, 3 syllables. De-lic-ious... Delicious. 
*Insalata Pera ~ For a salad this larger than life dish of greens with fruits was on point. A fresh crisp succulent pear that just did numbers to ones taste buds, with the goat cheese mixed in there making me rethink how a salad should always taste.  
                                                   ~Dessert~ 
*Brioche con Gelato ~ This dessert is actually a gelato sandwich, with your choice of 2 scoops of gelato. I went with a Bacio gelato and an Amaretto gelato, being held nicely in a toasted brioche bun. To be honest this was ok, the brioche seemed a little too dry, and the gelato not so creamy. This is not a slam on Gran Caffe, with everything that have to offer, but it seemed a little off to me. I will say this though, their dessert menu looks amazing, with endless options. 
 
Unique dishes that will have your taste buds going into full tilt mode along with their weekly tasting menu. Their tasting menu is designed to bring you through different regions of Italy, experiencing the dishes from that region. If that doesn't raise an eyebrow you should checkout their happy hour menu, and specials. I feel Gran Caffe L'Aquilla is an establishment that needs to be a part of your rotation. The last few times I've been here the staff has always made sure I, or we have been fully accommodated. Hopefully you're seated in Corina or Anastaysia area, but if not, don't fret their staff will make sure you'll have the very best dining experience. I know I plan on coming back every time I come home to visit.

**Side Note** My Gelato Pairing was not an easy decision to make.

This is gonna be a fun review,  I'll see if I can work in some 60's and 70's slang in there too, I'm gonna do you guys and gals a "solid". 

Where in this   "cool city" of Philadelphia  can you find the best damn Old Fashioned I ask you? The Trestle Inn is the answer my friends, it really doesn't have to be an Old Fashioned by the way. This could be any of their well concocted cocktails where the libation gods would be impressed while saying "4-Sho". Well ok mind you there is one other place I know of in Old City that makes some pretty "blazin" cocktails, and their old fashioned is also on point.   

The Trestle Inn needs to be visited over , and over again. I am telling you there is something about this place that just makes you want to come back. With out trying to sound repetitive I'm gonna try to point out some of the reasons or give you the "lowdown"  why this place should be visited. 

"Here is the skinny" about the Trestle Inn !
~ I already mentioned the slew of beverages one could sip and enjoy.
~ It could also be that laid back atmosphere where the 60'and 70's retro look never left.
~ The "bunnys' " dancing , making you "feel that funk"  as you enter.
