The halibut was white and flaky and it cut into the buttery richness of the scallops. The dish was lightly seasoned as the seafood was the real star of the show. It was accompanied by a delicious risotto and was one of the best risottos I've experienced. 

The desserts were on point. Apple pie with cheddar cheese crust. Sounds crazy but it works! Salty malty ice cream pie is everything you want in a dessert. It's creamy, salty and sweet all at once. 

Last but not least...the cocktails! 
I do enjoy a good cocktail and GW Finns delivered. With many viable drink options I went with the Nola Fizz because it had everything I loved in it. Gin, St. Germain, thyme, grapefruit AND champs! Bestow my heart! It was simply a divine drink...so divide I needed 2 just to make sure I liked it.

The service:
Honestly, it was perfect. I can't think of one negative thing or anything the server could have done to make our experience any better. Our meal was paced perfectly. We were checked up on frequently, but not too much. Our server seemed genuine and spoke about the menu and food with both knowledge and excitement. GW Finns is a great place to have a special occasion dinner. I can't wait to return.

I  came here for lunch one afternoon looking forward to trying it and left hungry because I lost my appetite mid meal and here is why: 

I unrolled my silverware and there was cheese encrusted all over the fork to where the prongs were not even visible. Ok, strike one but not the worst I've seen so lets just grab another fork and move on.  

I make my way over to the buffet which was fried chicken and red beans and rice and I've heard good things about it so I was looking forward to trying it. They had quasi clean plates stacked on top of buffet line so I grab one and notice that there is rice matted onto the plate. Hmm...their dish washer must have been texting and drying because the dirty dish theme continues. Strike 2. 

Fast forward to new plate, new fork and my party of six are all back seated. Then my neighboring friend turns to me and goes, "is this what I think it is?" Yep, an enormous dead bug chilling in the middle of his red beans and rice. Now, this was no ordinary bug, this bug might as well had a hat and coat on because he was a hefty sucker. Clearly, he died from red beans and rice overdose or as I like to call them, red beans and flies. Strike 3. 

Judging from the other reviews it seems like I went on a very off day so I'd be willing to try it again, but long after this memory has been erased from my brain.

Since I live close to here, I was super excited to see another Thai restaurant open up since its my favorite food. Its a very small restaurant with minimalist decor. The size of the place is big enough for the area they are serving since its basically in a neighborhood. Great for those who work in Elmwood business park too! When we arrived at 1 on a Saturday only a few other tables were occupied so we were told to sit anywhere we liked. Since it was our first time we wanted to try a little of everything. So we got an appetizer, soup, and entrée. 

For our appetizer we chose the panfried chicken dumplings which were very good and flavorful. They could have been seared a little less because the bottoms were a little overdone, but still good nonetheless. The coconut soup was my favorite and think it could possibly be my favorite coconut soup, ever! The pad thai was good and very flavorful, more on the spicy side than sweet. Their lunch specials are fantastic! The portion was huge and only $7! They even have lunch prices on Saturday, nice! The prices for dinner still aren't that bad though. I thought the service was really good and all the girls working were very sweet. Our food came out pretty quick and they were on top of the refills. I hope this places sticks around because its nice to have a Thai option so close by! I can't wait to go back and try some other things on the menu.

I finally made it down to Willa Jean after hearing all the buzz around it. I know I'm in the minority, but the visit just fell flat for me. At first impression, wow, what a beautiful space! I'll give it to the designers, they did a great job.  It has a rustic feel and tons of windows allowing natural light. I liked that the staff all wore jeans and gingham plaid shirts giving it a laid back feel.  

We wanted to try a little bit of everything since it was our first time so we had 2 appetizers and each an entrée. For an appetizer we ordered pigs in the blanket, it had a very buttery dough so it was greasy and left my fingers slicker than a wet weasel on a linoleum floor.  It was ok. Next was the corn fritters. Again, ok. 

For an entrée I got the tartine sampler, which was a great way to be able to taste a variety of items. Unfortunately the bread was so chewy it was hard to break off in a single bite and it left my jaw sore from biting down so hard. My husband got the fried chicken sandwich which had a nice heat from the slaw, but that was really all you could taste. The chicken was very under seasoned and the batter slipped right off. 

I wanted to love this place so badly, but I was really underwhelmed. I will give the benefit of the doubt and try again for breakfast, but I'm not rushing to come back.

I am giving it 3 stars for atmosphere and the service was attentive and friendly.

I'm really digging these "food courts" that are trending. Mainly because I have ADD and want to try all the things. Pythian Market is a building with all the things jammed inside of it. Want a frozen drink? BBQ? pizza? Pho? You want it all at once? Noooo problem! 


My recommended vendors are 1908 for cocktails. The frozen Watermelon Paloma is so refreshing and a delight on a hot day. I think their frozen drinks rotate so you might not find that exact drink, but I think its safe to say all of them are likely delicious. 

Meribo Pizza was a delight and cured my case for the happy hour hunger pang. The ingredients were high quality on a thin crust pizza and I am here for it!

It's the perfect place to catch happy hour with a big group as it offers plenty of seating and many options to satisfy all your peoples.

I am so excited to have this restaurant in Rivertown. This area is going through a bit of a Renaissance and Gendusa's is a big part of that. It is a family owned and operated restaurant serving quality Italian food for a great price. They have daily specials that are amazing, my personal favorite being the filet served with a side and a salad for only $20. I also love their lasagnas both classic and eggplant (meatless) are fantastic options. The eggplant lasagna is so rich you won't miss the meat or the noodles. The Alfredo sauce is rich and creamy, but I typically like mine with a little more bite (read: Parmesan). Gendusa's is also BYOB so bring a bottle and get ready to dig in to some amazing food. The pizzas are also amazing. Thin crust, plenty of high quality toppings and made in a pizza oven to give it that perfect amount of crisp. I recommend fasting before you come because you will need to save room for one of their homemade desserts! Their praline cheesecake is the best dessert ever and I'm not that crazy about pralines. It's THAT good! 

Since it is locally owned and the owner is always at the restaurant the service is that you would expect from a mom and pop place, very personable and friendly! I find they always know a lot about the menu items and how items are prepared. Gendusa's has a family atmosphere and a very laid back and chill vibe, which is exactly what you want when you sit down for a good home cooked meal. Shh...just don't tell my Italian grandmother about this review.

As far as distillery tours go, Old New Orleans is the mack daddy ya'll.

-Very knowledgeable. Yes, you will actually learn cool stuff! About the rum making process, a little NOLA history, the background of the owner and how Old New Orleans Rum came to be.

-the tasting portion of the tour will give you a rum for your money...see what I did there....eh??
ok, seriously though, you get to taste all of the different rums and if they pour extras they use scare tactics and tell you they will throw it away if you don't throw it down your gullet. There's no choice, really. 

-our tour guide made goodies at his house using rum and let us taste his homemade desserts AND had the recipes ready for us when we asked. This guy is a pro! 

-This is a great outing for 21 and up locals and tourists looking for something fun. 

-Oh and its only ten bucks!
I'm from Florida and I always go to this market whenever I'm in NOLA. I recommend go here 20 mins after they're opened for fresh bakery, vegetables, and roasted pork/duck.

Nutshell:  simple, but super tasty food.  Super nice staff, chill atmosphere.  You need to stop in. 

I've literally been waiting for this place to open for like two months and finally made it in!  I did an early dinner, about 4 pm on a Saturday.  It was almost empty.  Its small, but still plenty of room to move around and the decor is really nice and calm.  Their music had me dancing in my seat.  Now for the food...the most important part.  Their chips are light and blissfully lightly salted (like Salt Bea salted) and the salsa is hands down the best I've ever had!  I ordered the chicken tinga burrito, which came with fries.  The fries are amazing!  Whatever seasoning they use is like crack.  The burrito is huge!  See photo.  The flavors are like authentic Mexican food, not super spicy or seasoned, but everything blends well.  My only issue is half the burrito seemed to be rice and the chicken seemed to be lost somewhere in there.  Otherwise, very very tasty.  They have a basic menu.  I'll be back for a torta for sure.  Definitely a great addition to the Princeton Heights area.

Nutshell: buckets of well made food, good prices, and very awesome service. Highly recommend a stop in.

First time in and I'm a fan! A friend and I decided on an impromptu Thursday dinner around 6pm. The guy working pegged us straight away as newbies. He was super friendly and gave us menus and told us to shoot any questions his way. He was super awesome throughout the visit, so shout out to him! (My bad for not getting his name) I ordered the flag burrito with chicken and my friend, the divorced eggs. Unbeknownst to us at the time, these are brand spanking new menu items off their Big Plate menu...big plate is right! The chicken was sliced and juicy, the beans were whole and not mushy, the flavors all melded together brilliantly. I got through about half the burrito and tapped out. It came on a bed of chips, which was nice to pick up all the bits that fell off my folk and looks way classier than picking it up with my fingers...which I would have done, I have no shame. They have a mini fridge of sauces and I personally was a big fan of the tomatillo one. The burrito has three sauces already, so I didn't need to add much else. The platter was $13 and with a fountain soda it rounded up to $16 something. Not too shabby. Aaaaand they have Ski!!!! Parking is a bit odd. Its on the corner of a residential one way street and a busy multi-lane street and its only street parking, but it seems to work. All in all a great experience and I look forward to getting back for some actual tacos!

You can't make a trip to the French Quarter without a visit to Pat O'Brien's. I was actually looking forward to coming here but then a chain of events turned everything upside down.

For merely convenience, my friends and I decided to order hurricanes and some food here before exploring the sights and sounds of the French Quarter. The hurricanes came out pretty quickly and the food shortly thereafter. As I started drinking my hurricane, I thought it tasted a little bit off but continued drinking about one-third of it because I was so thirsty from the day. I took the straw and mixed the drink around a bit to see if it would help with the taste. And then that's when I saw it- my heart skipped a beat as I saw not only one but TWO GIANT COCKROACHES in my hurricane drink! I was completely disgusted and lost any appetite I might have had that night. Heck, I don't even remember what food I ordered! I don't even know how both a bartender and waitress could overlook TWO GIANT COCKROACHES floating around in a drink! This was completely unacceptable!

The manager came over after we complained to the waitress. Unfortunately, the only thing he could offer was to take off the price of my ONE hurricane drink. Since I ordered the special souvenir glass, I had to pay for the glass. There was no mention of reducing the cost of the total ticket since we also ordered food. I was in no mood to venture around town that evening because I was still cringing from that terrible experience.

Maybe the worst of the worst days just happened to monsoon on my parade that day. Since then, I still have yet to return to Pat O'Briens for fear of re-living that horrendous ordeal again. I will gladly take a hand grenade over a hurricane any day.

When you find yourself in the city but need some fuel to power through the rest of your day, go get some MOJO! Mojo Coffee House is one of my favorite local spots in the city to grab some coffee on the go, study/work, or meet up some friends. 

Nestled in the lower garden district, Mojo offers plentiful indoor/outdoor seating. It's the perfect little cafe to stop by on a morning stroll down Magazine Street. Mojo has a warm, inviting and relaxed ambiance, as well as lots of character, making it a popular spot with locals and tourists.

The friendly staff here are usually knowledgeable and on point with drink recommendations. Although it can get busy at times, quality has not been compromised as I have enjoyed a plethora of drink offerings here (espresso, iced coffee, pour-over & drip coffee). To my surprise, the iced oat milk latte, rose lemonade, and sparkling elderberry lemonade were all really good! I love local coffee shops that have unique drinks, which makes them stand out from the rest! FYI, their coffee is ethically sourced and locally roasted in small batches. Looking for a snack? They also have a small menu of cold/hot items and fresh pastries.

Everyone needs some Mojo in their life every now and then. If you haven't already, please give Mojo a try and it might become one of your fave stops for coffee! Go get comfy, cozy and caffeinated at Mojo!

Hunker down y'all, Tsunami Sushi has arrived in the Big Easy and it's here to stay. Drop what you're doing and head down to the CBD for excellent sushi with a dash of Louisiana flair! 5-star food coupled with 5-star service in an upscale atmosphere makes for a great night out! 

It's incredibly hard to find high quality, fresh sushi here in the land of crawfish and so you can imagine my excitement when I found out that Tsunami was opening it's 3rd Louisiana location here in Nawlins! 
I've dined here for lunch and dinner and have always been 100% satisfied with the food and service. I always enjoy sitting at the sushi bar (which has an open kitchen concept) to admire the captivating work of the creative and talented sushi chefs. Make sure to sip on a deliciously potent cocktail while you dine too! I like to order the chef's special or whatever chef conjures up with those stellar sushi-making magic skills. My most favorite dish is the Sunflower, comprised of thin sashimi slices of seared tuna in spicy ponzu served with tobiko, masago, scallions, and quail egg. Not only is the Sunflower absolutely delicious, but it is also a beautiful piece of art and sushi perfection! 

Come on down to the CBD and ride the Tsunami wave- I promise it will be well worth it! You can even feast to your heart's delight with daily happy hour specials. I highly recommend Tsumani for the BEST SUSHI in New Orleans!!!

Calling all purist coffee drinkers- this is seriously the BEST ESPRESSO BAR for you in New Orleans! Take a break from exploring the French Quarter and visit Spitfire Espresso Bar, which is quietly nestled along St. Peter Street between Royal and Chartres. Jackson Square and Bourbon Street are both just a block away from this hidden jewel.

Simply put, what you see is what you get at Spitfire- no frills nor fancy decor because it's just freaking fantastic coffee! Locals flock here to get their espresso fix and continue on with their merry ways. There are a few bar stools along the wall for you to take a quick coffee break, but keep in mind that it's mostly standing room only as people order and take their drinks to-go. Everything here is made to order, so please be patient. There is a small menu: some specialty espresso concoctions with bitters, regional varieties of coffee for pour-overs, iced coffees, and a few espresso drinks. The bar itself is really the size of a walk-in closet and you'll have to see to it to believe it! 

On our first visit, we had the place to ourselves for about 15 mins until the line of people starting forming. Our barista was very friendly and knowledgeable, answering our questions with finesse as he diligently worked his crafty, magic at the espresso bar. I was in awe watching the meticulous preciseness of preparing the coffee (I even uploaded a video haha!). You can immediately see that the baristas here are very well trained and take pride in their craft. I got the cortado (yum- it packed a punch and woke me up from my lunch induced food coma) and a new featured "chocolate board" (espresso paired with 2 different gourmet chocolates). Noteworthy points were the chocolates featured on the "chocolate board" - Icelandic OmNom milk chocolate with sea salted almonds and locally made New Orleans Acalli dark chocolate. Both are handcrafted bean-to-bar artisan chocolates! At only $6 for the "chocolate board," you're able to enjoy espresso paired with unique, artisan chocolates that you normally wouldn't purchase at the store. (Each OmNom chocolate bar is $12 and Acalli is $8). In addition, we got an iced mocha latte, which packed quite a hefty caffeine punch along with the sweetness of the mocha. Spitfire definitely did its job in waking us up and gave us an energy burst to continue on with our French Quarter adventures. 

The vibe and ambiance of Spitfire made me feel like I was channeling my inner hipster and reminded me of days past when I enjoyed philosophizing with colleagues over coffee and cocktails. Come visit Spitfire Espresso Bar the next time you find yourself in the French Quarter in desperate need of a potently delicious caffeine-pick-me-up. Relax, enjoy the coffee, soak in the sunshiny day, and thank me later coffee connoisseurs.

Desire Oyster Bar is one of my fave spots on Bourbon Street for shucked oysters and appetizers to start off an evening of laissez les bon temps rouler! Even on a busy night, there are usually a couple of open spots at their oyster bar where you can actually see the oysters being shucked before you feast on them! I'm never left disappointed with my oyster feasting experiences at Desire! 

INSIDER TIP: Happy hour $1 shucked oysters and drink specials from 3pm-6pm :) Go early to grab a table by the window for people watching along Bourbon Street!

I've tried most of the other food fares on their menu but their shucked oysters are the real winners in my book. The oysters are always fresh and delicious! They're served chilled, with plenty of lemon and cocktail sauce. For apps, try a cup of gumbo, fried alligator w/ spicy La pepper jelly or the spinach-artichoke dip served with fried bowtie pasta. Use their fresh French bread to soak up the rest of the dip to enjoy all that goodness. Their poboys, fried seafood, and NOLA food fare are on point too mostly but again, the shucked oysters are the stars here! Obviously, no one does awesome charbroiled oysters like Drago's, so don't ever accept imitations, but there's been times I give in to the desires at Desire. Desire's chargrilled oysters are average at best and suffice to satiate that craving. Cocktails are overpriced here, as I would rather have a hand grenade or hurricane prior to dining here to get the most bang for my buck. If you have any room left, you should definitely try their amazing warm bread pudding, drenched in decadent bourbon whisky sauce too!

Service is prompt and friendly, and I never feel
rushed to dine here, even on the busiest of nights. I recommend dining during non-peak times for a better dining experience. Desire Oyster Bar will fulfill your desires for shucked oysters!

Head to District Donuts for a big win on deliciously decadent donuts! Carb and sugar lovers can rejoice here! (Disclaimer: If you're counting calories, avoid this place at all costs!)

This isn't your ordinary donut shop- it's a donut shop on steroids and all that pizzazz, with tasty sliders and addictive coffee brews. Breakfast, lunch and dinner can all be consumed here upon one visit or multiple visits. Pick your poison of beer or coffee to complement your snack or meal! But don't forget to bring your voracious appetite, and either a hammock or wheelbarrow for the food coma aftermath.

Cruising down on Harrison, you can see this location has an adjacent parking lot which was quite convenient. You walk in, get mesmerized by the psychedelic blue and teal floor designs, check out the menu and order at the counter. I admired the beautiful decor of this location- custom wooden booths with a splash of teal color on the back cushions. All of the staff members were friendly and helpful with menu recommendations.

Donut selections change daily and on my most recent visit, I fell in love with the cinnamon roll and chocolate peanut banana donut. The cinnamon roll had a cream cheese glaze, topped with bruleed raw sugar. After ordering, you can contain your excitement by watching a staff member flame the raw sugar on the cinnamon roll. The cinnamon roll was as good as any cinnamon roll should be! The bruleed sugar gave it a nice little crunch with every bite. The chocolate glazed donut was topped with peanuts and stuffed with the yummiest banana pastry cream. The flavors worked oh so well together and I regret not getting another one to bring home for a midnight snack. To seal the deal, the Vietnamese iced coffee was a great afternoon caffeine pick-me-up!

District Donuts is a must if you happen to be in the area and are in need of a snack/coffee/donut fix. Yes it is a little pricy for a $4 donut but remember that these are extraordinary donuts! I look forward to my next visit so I can try out some more of their sliders, kolaches, biscuits, and other donuts.

DONUT worry, be happy and DONUT let anyone ever tell you that you're less than incredibly amazing, yes I'm talking to you dear Yelpers :) !!!

Hooray for Gordon Biersch's atmosphere (especially the well-lit outdoor dining area) and plentiful drinks! Located next to Harrah's, this location is a great spot to meet up friends, grab some beers, and watch your sport of choice, as TVs are located both inside and outside the restaurant. Because of their prime location, they are often busy and service can be slow.

INSIDER TIP: Yelpers, don't forget to check-in to get your FREE GARLIC FRIES! 

Gordon Biersch is your average chain restaurant which offers pub food fare along with German beer (in-house brewed). On my most recent visit, our group ordered a few apps to share while watching the football game. 

Strawberry soda cocktail: Cruzan strawberry rum, triple sec, fresh-muddled mint & fresh strawberries topped w/ soda; I enjoyed this cocktail so much I had two- it was really light, fruity and refreshing! (5/5)

Blue crab & artichoke dip: I really couldn't taste much of the blue crab and it was more of a heavy, creamy and cheesy dip with subtle artichoke flavors. (3/5)

Fried calamari: The calamari pieces were pretty small. Nothing really stood out with this dish. (2/5)

Brewer's combo: grilled brats, soft pretzel & garlic fries; Personally the brats had too much of a smoky and charred flavor, which I did not like. The soft pretzel was fresh and warm. The garlic fries were extra delish! (3/5)

Gb chicken wings: traditional wings w/ spicy chili marzen, traditional buffalo or thai fire sauce; These wings were cooked to perfection and my fave app of the night! (5/5)

Ahi wonton nachos: diced tuna w/ teriyaki sauce over crisp wonton chips w/grilled pineapple, pickled ginger, green onions & toasted sesame seeds, drizzled w/ cucumber wasabi sauce & Sriracha cream; The wonton chips were too greasy for me and I wish the pieces of tuna were bigger; The overall flavors did not work well together. (3/5) 

The Fulton Street area is a fun hangout spot and I would come to Gordon Biersch again for drinks and apps while watching a game. Don't expect mind-blowing food or attentive service though. We dined inside and outside on the same night. The service we received inside was quite good but once we went outside, it unfortunately went downhill (our server outside really looked unhappy to be there and made it look like serving us was a big bother). Oh and the bathrooms were scary war zones that night too. Hopefully, management can help make improvements to make it better for everyone.

Finding yourself hungry in the French Quarter? All you need to do is go to Frank's to satisfy your appetite. Don't let the old, small size of the restaurant turn you away from feasting on some of the BEST muffulettas and New Orleans BBQ shrimp!

What sets this place apart from others is the hot, toasted muffuletta. Picture this: freshly baked, warm and sesame topped Italian bread generously loaded with slices of baked ham, Genoa salami, Swiss cheese, and Italian olive salad. The bread was just the right thickness to soak up the overflowing juices and held up to the very end of this ravenous devouring feast. Collectively, all of the meaty ingredients with the ooey gooey goodness of melted Swiss and tangy olive mix puts this toasted muffuletta above and beyond the traditional cold ones from Central Grocery. HOT & TOASTED muffulettas will always be a win!!!

Don't even get me started with their popular New Orleans BBQ shrimp. Just thinking about them makes me drool like kid in a candy shop. At a steep price of $25.99, the BBQ shrimp was completely worth it! Gargantuan Gulf shrimp piled high and swimming in a bowl of crack-alicious Cajun-buttery-BBQ sauce. Make sure to use the toasted, buttery French bread slices to soak up the crack-alicious sauce in all its glory and finger-licking goodness. You're gonna get down and dirty with these BBQ shrimp but no worries because you'll be given plenty of napkins. Trust me, you'll have to eat it to believe it!

Atmosphere was comfortable and a nice break from the busy buzzing of the French Quarter. For the best dining experience, be sure to sit upstairs and enjoy people watching. Service has room for improvement as our waitress wasn't the friendliest nor welcoming to us, but our food magically appeared quite fast, so it balanced out. We are not picky eaters and more than happy to just have good food on our plates. Remember the next time you visit the FQ, come to Frank's for the toasted muffuletta and BBQ shrimp- simply ahhh-mazingly delicious!

Calling all you gastropub addicts- stellar drinks, live music, and incredi-mazing international dishes make up the winning combination for Three Muses. We wandered in on a Saturday night after waiting forever and a day elsewhere with no success. Somehow things magically worked in our favor and we were able to get a table within 10 mins despite it being so busy!

I love being able to take my taste buds on a mini international flight. The small dishes (think tapas style) here each have a creative flair and you seriously can't go wrong with the variety of selections (gluten free and vegan friendly dishes are available too). We started off with the blue cheese stuffed dates which came out wrapped in glorious, smoky BACON with a balsamic reduction sauce(4/5). Sweet, savory and cheesy flavors were all wrapped in freaking BACON- how can you not devour such deliciousness?! It was a little too sweet for me personally. Next up was the Italian baked mac and cheese. This was the adult amped up version of mac and cheese- the creamy and cheesy goodness combined with the subtle crunch of the herbed bread crumbs was sheer deliciousness (5/5). The last dish of the night was the steak and cake (5/5). The all natural hangar steak was cooked to a perfect, juicy medium rare, resting atop a fresh Louisiana crab cake, with micro greens and béarnaise sauce. Everything in this steak dish had intense flavors and went very well together. You won't have to worry about leftovers because everything was happily and quickly devoured. Live music just made our dinner experience all the more amazing, along with our perfectly crafted drinks. At times, the music was loud, but music was meant to be shared and appreciated all over the world! 

I have to give a shout out to our hardworking server that night- he was swamped but managed to maintain his composure and provide quality service throughout the night. The restaurant is small but who doesn't mind cozying up to your SO or date in close quarters? Each staff member we interacted with was friendly and welcoming. For reference, you can make reservations in advance to avoid waitlist hassles.

If you find yourself in search of incredi-mazing food on Frenchmen Street, then you can count on Three Muses for a foodie-tastic culinary trip around the world to stimulate your palates. Be adventurous and leave behind the insane crowds on Bourbon Street. Follow your NOLA and run to Three Muses- you won't be disappointed!

For an exceptional and VIP experience, come have a drink at the classy, upscale Arnaud's French 75. The bartenders and waiters are dressed to the nines and some will feel rather underdressed at the bar. Not to worry though, you'll receive impeccable service regardless of your attire (although I recommend business casual). 

We met up with Houston Yelpers Emmanuel and his lovely wife, Jay and had the BESTTT night there!!! One drink led to two and then...well we made some fun-tastic memories! We had to stand by the bar at the beginning of the night, but as the crowd trickled out, we were able to lounge on the comfy chairs in the corner the rest of the evening. We even managed to find our way upstairs to the Mardi Gras Museum to see all the different regalia through the past years 1941-1968 (which btw, you should not visit at night when no one's around! There's just something about old creepy mannequins that reminds me of horror movies). The whole building itself has so much history and it was really interesting to look at all the old photographs adorning the walls.

When visiting an establishment with the name "French 75," it is obvious that you must try the French 75! (It was also Arnaud's fave drink!) A visit to Nawlins wouldn't be complete without enjoying an authentic French 75 cocktail. The French 75 is made with a fine cognac, sugar, lime juice and topped off with Moët champagne- a royally exquisite drink with historical significance. Bubbly bubbly makes the world go round- and how can you deny anything with fancy Moet champagne, which makes it simply divine! My second drink or was it third drink of the night was the Honi Makai- an equally exquisite concoction of anejo, rum, herbsaint, allspice dram, orgeat, lime and orange juice. I absolutely loved the dragonfruit-berry-grape -mint garnish, which made it such a visually appealing cocktail. The Honi Makai was a real treat- something that looked and tasted great!

Arnaud's French 75 is an old school lounge-cigar bar with nothing less than stellar service. The prices are steep but you're getting quality drinks with your VIP experience. It's a refreshing and welcomed change of scenery just steps away from Bourbon Street. I'd recommend a visit here to get away from the masses of people, and actually enjoy a perfectly crafted cocktail in an elegant but laid back atmosphere.

Seminole Heights' profile has been elevated by other restaurants that have come into our quaint 'hood over the past three years and I am so thankful for the "cred" we've recently received from previous naysayers that once told us that buying a house near Nebraska Avenue was ridiculous/stupid/scary/waste of money.  

Well color me ridiculous because I'm certain, we've made it now. 

Either by this new addition or by my outstanding ability to create run on sentences.  

Rooster and the Till is the bees knees y'all.  I have a short but inclusive list of what makes a good restaurant and readily checked off each as we enjoyed our New Year's Eve there.  And it was opening night.  What kind of culinary wizardry is going here to ensure it's patrons have a flawless meal on opening night?  

The owner greeted us and was incredibly friendly and helpful as we selected our food.  We ordered a cheese slate (AMAZING), the pork belly small plate (can't tell you, I draw lines at food with the word "belly" in them; my husband swooned though), and smoked mushroom small plate (AMAZING), the dishes looked incredibly and the two I tasted were delicious.  The flavors from the mushrooms were enhanced by a pork vinaigrette (probably from the belly....DAMN IT!) and pickled apple and raisins and the cheese slate was served with a sampling (a large sampling) of five cheeses. 

The interior was lovely, and was made more so by the fact it look less time to walk to the restaurant than it would have to start the car and drive.  I mean look at us, practically New Yorkers.  

Love it love it love it.  We didn't try their wines as it was New Years Eve and we had Bailey's and hot chocolate to bring us into 2014 at home.  But they have them, and they are sitting on the coolest wine rack I ever did see.

I think I like this place. :)

This place offers some of the better breakfast foods and sandwiches in the W. Philly area. The portions are huge. The prices are low. I definitely agree with Matt S about the area being overrun with unjustifiably higher prices for rather mediocre food. This place is definitely a refreshing change from such places. 

Also, the owner is also very friendly as you wait for your order.

I'm glad I don't live close to this establishment, it's just way too tempting, and I must admit that this is my first visit, but far from my last.

We've got errands to run in Reno, and so my wife is reviewing yelp for a new Reno experience for breakfast when she arrives at this listing, over 400 reviews and averaging four stars.  That's solid consensus among our yelp community and worth exploring further.

We arrive around 9:30 to a packed waiting room.  Some people think this is bad, and it can be, but it's a fast wait and proves to be well worth our time.  After about 20 minutes of watching food pass by I ask the hostess if the coffee is good, and she says that it is.  She then asks if she an get my wife and I a cup, and who are we to say no, heck, it's just over freezing outside and we've been on the road for 50 minutes.  It was good.

While waiting I read the specials board, and today they're offering a 'Hot Hot Omelet', it's a chorizo omelet with jalapeno's topped with a slice of pepper jack on top....zoinks was all I could say and so I never even looked at the menu.  It was served with a choice of hash browns or home fries and I was able to opt into the biscuit served with a side of gravy.  I haven't had biscuits and gravy in years....suffice it to say this was the only meal I had for the day.

My wife had the French toast of the day, and it was a salted caramel version with pecans on top.  My bite tasted like desert, and I noticed that my wife applied no syrup, she said it wasn't necessary.  She also had two cooked to order eggs with two slices of bacon.  As you'd suspect, I was able to help her out by eating one of her slices of bacon.  It was all in the interest of providing a quality yelp.  Yes, the bacon was good.

The service was also something to behold.  We were seated near the kitchen and able to observe the cooks cranking away the entire time we were there.  We never wanted for water and our coffee was refreshed multiple times.

For some there might be pitfalls, and they'd include a crowded room, staff moving quickly, people coming and going, a crowded waiting area, and some folks who were enjoying themselves for so long that they were clogging the pipeline of people waiting to be seated.  This is all to be expected when a place is doing good work.  If this bothers you, you might look elsewhere...

Again, and I mean this, we'll be back.

Rittenhouse takes the cake as the best hotel experience I've ever had. To say they outperformed would be an understatement. All I can say is it's clear that they value their reputation, and they certainly lived up to it.

I stayed here for my annnjversary via AMEX fhr, which comes with an upgrade. The upgrade I got however, was 4-5 levels above the room I initially had. The room looked like a luxury apartment on the upper east side of Manhattan and was absolutely huge. Fully equipped with dining room living room, kitchen, two bathrooms, bedroom suite and floor to ceiling windows. The most beautiful room I've ever seen. Later that evening, they even sent a complementary bottle of champagne and chocolate covered strawberries to the room with a happy anniversary note. #nailedit

The hotel itself has a classic feel with modern touches. The service is a reminder to days (before my time) when hotels went above and beyond to provide a personal experience for guests. From the check-in when the room wasn't ready and they took our bags and personally escorted us to brunch, to the remembering of your name by all the staff, this is the gold standard for what a hotel experience should be.

Bordentown for some reason still hasn't gotten the credit it deserves for its food scene. For years it's hosted some great restaurants and Under The Moon Cafe is one of them.

From the moment you enter, the hipster decor will grab you and let you know you're in for a unique experience. The walls are lined with interesting art and the restaurant itself is on the darker side. I came here for brunch on a Sunday and the experience was perfect.

I had an order of beef empanadas that were exceptional. Incredibly fresh, fried perfectly and came with a side of chimi churri. I then had the banana stuffed French toast which was delicious. It even came with more bananas on top. Also had a side of Mac n cheese which was also delicious.

In addition to great food, the service was excellent. It's also a byo, which makes for the perfect brunch. This place is definitely a must and one I'll be back to for sure.

I don't like writing bad reviews. I'm writing this one because I don't want someone else getting sucked in by the overall high star rating. Don't. Do. It.

I landed in New Orleans late in the afternoon. After a long day of travel, I needed something before heading off to a party for the night. Consulting my Yelp app, I noticed a German restaurant steps from my hotel. Jagerhaus had great reviews, and I love German food. What could go wrong? 

I walked in after viewing the menu outside. When I opened the menu I was handed inside, it was not the same. OK. The décor is very simple. It had an informal, deli type of feel that didn't fit with the menu prices.

I am a sucker for pretzels, so I ordered one along with a bowl of the soup of the day. I had wanted the bier cheese soup I had seen on the other menu, but chicken vegetable sounded fine. I also ordered a champagne cocktail which turned out to be champagne & cranberry juice. No strawberry garnish as advertised. Things happen.

There were only a few other people seated in the restaurant, so you would expect the soup to come out quickly. Nope. As I waited, people were coming in to order the various iced coffee drinks advertised. You would expect to see a coffee bar with an espresso machine, yes? Nope. They use powdered mixes, with instant coffee, the flavorings and cream mixed together in an envelope. The bartender just emptied the foil packets (from a drawer below the counter) into a blender with ice, turned it on, and poured them in cups to go. Calling themselves a full service coffee shop is quite a stretch. Moving on. 

About 20 minutes into the wait I saw them take a pretzel from the freezer and put it in the oven. Interesting. Still no soup. Most of what I saw happening from my bar stool were the cooks reheating various foods in the kitchen. That's acceptable in some cases. Not much, if anything I saw was made to order other than a couple of things coming from the deep fryer. 

Finally about 30 minutes from when I ordered (I had checked in, so I was watching the time), the pretzel and soup arrived. I have posted pictures of both. I guess I had expected a larger bowl of soup, and I certainly expected it to come out much more quickly than it did. The flavor wasn't bad, it was pretty good actually. The pretzel, well, look at the picture. It was a Super Pretzel. You know, the ones that you see at ball games that taste like paste? They charged around $5 for the nasty thing! It was horrible, but I ate a small part of it and asked for the check. 

I don't expect food to be authentic, but I do expect it to be good. This was neither. Do yourself a favor and go to Killer Poboys or Deja Vu on the same block. You aren't missing anything here.

Edit: I went back and gave 2 stars instead of my original 1. I didn't get spat at, or see anything creepy running around, but damn it! Is it that hard to at least buy pretzels from a local baker rather than use frozen Super Pretzels? At least ACT like you're trying to serve home made food. I think I made enough other points to warrant 1 star, but I was feeling guilty actually doing it.
Bad coffee. Bad service. Avoid at all costs! There are lots of better options in STL!

I came in here exclusively for a bubble tea. A coworker suggested them to me and told me I could call in my order so it was ready when I got there. I left early from work to run an errand and had to head back to work after my errand. I called and left my order over the phone (#4 - no changes). I walked in and someone pointed me towards the bubble tea counter. I told them I had called and they brought it right over. I was in and out in maybe 3 minutes?

The size and quality for the price was wonderful and having it so close to work is great! I need to try all their flavors now!

My wife and I have been huge fans of the Truckee location for years and wished that entire time that there would be an option here in Reno for fresh seafood. When they announced they were setting up shop here in Reno my excitement was sky high. When I saw the announcement they were open here in Reno I immediately knew I had Saturday lunch plans.

We arrived and were glad to have seen a tip re: entering from the back. That was a huge help. Do not be thrown of by the lack of signage from Virginia.

There's a few steps down from the parking lot as well as a staircase up. We saw a hostess so headed towards the street level entrance which has a door as well as a garage door wall which was open. As we approached the door I noticed customers seated with menus. This was a tad odd as the location in Truckee is a menu on the wall kind of place and thats what I was expecting.

We stepped to the hostess station and were asked if we wanted inside or outside seating. The weather was nice but slightly chilly so we opted for inside seating. The garage door was open so there was a chill coming in from outside but very pleasant.

We sat and were offered drinks and an appetizer order promptly. We opted for the Crab Cake app.

While we looked over the menu we also looked around and checked out the ambiance. It's clean and simple in its style and decor. 

We placed our entree orders and shortly after that the app arrived. The crab cakes were a bit smaller in size than most I am used to. The fresh lemon to squeeze on top was great because I like my crab cakes without aioli (this one being no exception). If I was hungrier, this may not have held me over until my entree arrived. I wasn't very hungry so this was the perfect size.

Then our entrees came and I was delighted. My choice was the Surf and Turf Slider. I was delivered two delightful sliders, a metal bucket of fries, cole slaw, ketchup and the bacon aioli that I asked for on the side. The sliders were generously apportioned with an entire lobster claw of meat on each slider. Under the claw meat was a piece of pork belly - perfectly seasoned and seared. The crisp lettuce and fresh tomato were great with the rich lobster and pork belly. The bacon aioli was great too but i still had half the container left after eating both sliders. I'm glad I asked for it on the side or it would have been far too much.

My wife enjoyed her crab roll. She said the portion is a bit smaller than those she's used to. She was able to hold the whole roll in one hand and said usually she struggles to manage a roll with both hands. She didn't like the cole slaw because it wasn't a creamy slaw. It seemed to be more of a vinegar / acid base. I enjoyed it for that reason however. Her crab roll was served with a salad and she said the dressing was light and perfectly complimentary to the richer crab roll.

The food aside, the service was impeccable. There was a challenging customer seated near us and every server in the building seemed to have tried to ease the customers negative attitude to no avail. They kept trying. I told our waitress she was incredibly patient and I was impressed by her prowess. She said 5 years in the industry had made her quite calm and patient. The food was good but the service put this over the top.

I would have to try more items off the menu before I could raise it to 5 but for being open only a few days i'd say they were cruising smoothly.

Overall, it's a breath of fresh beachside salty air to have good, fresh seafood in town.

Wow! These portions are huge. Coworkers decided to order lunch from here and suggested the nachos. I left off the jalapeños and they followed the request. I will say that I think she we ordered so many things other items were forgotten too. Mine had no pico but other orders did. 

Overall, if you can find a place to (double) park and grab your order, give this spot a chance. The nachos were huge, and delicious. I made it through only half the order before I gave up. They were definitely a fork situation because they were covered in so much yummy goodness they were a mess. 

Next time I'll try tacos or a burrito since the nachos were a great introductory lunch!

Visited this place while on a day trip to Philly from NY. I hade the original Philly cheesesteak with garlic Parm cheese fries. My mom has the chicken cheesesteak with broccoli and spinach. Both of us enjoyed our sandwiches, I've been here previously in the past and have never had a bad experience. My mom however, hadn't been here prior and is typically a picky eater when it comes to eating out.

Sump is, in a word, dope. 

Coffee is unappreciated as far as I'm concerned.  So much so that I, a coffee enthusiast, drink swill on the daily because well, its commonplace. 

Sump will enlighten you to what coffee can, and should be. 

Once upon a time I was lucky enough to travel to Central America where they spoil the gringos with some of the locally grown beans, brewed correctly. Makes you never want to leave, and when you do, long for the coffee you drank while you were there. 

I recreated those moments I spent drinking amazing coffee while i was at Sump.

If you love coffee go immediately. If you are not a coffee lover, Sump might just make you one.

A few side notes, Sump's logo is super rad. They don't have food. I would come back here with my laptop in tow to do some work. That's all for now.

I really like Russell's. If i was just evaluating the food, it would be 5 stars. But this place is a logistics NIGHTMARE during the lunch rush. You've been warned.

Lets talk about the good first. The baked goods. Whoa. Like whoa. I'm always skeptical when i see giant cookies, giant muffins and giant pieces of cake perfectly decorated. Bigger does not equal better, and sometimes the better they look..the worse they taste. Not at Russells. Every baked good I have had is ON POINT! The gooey butter cake is amazing. Its different than every place else. It has a more substantial crust. And they have rotating flavors. The peanut butter chocolate? Its very sweet, but oh so good. Horrible for you, but dang..worth. it. Also I recommend the giant cookies. Crunchy outside, soft and delicious in the middle. Very good.

Non sweet options include a solid selection of sandwiches and salads - along with a rotating soup. The ingredient are fresh, and i've not had anything i didn't like. I do call this the "ladies lunching place" though...cause its lady food. And filled with ladies at lunch. Who are, the ladies? I'm a lady, you're a lady..we're the ladies. (extra points if you catch that reference).

Anyway, now the bad. There are some issues that, if addressed could bump Russell's into 5 star territory. Russells used to be housed a smaller, more cramped space. When i found out they were moving to a bigger space..i was i excited. However, the new space is almost worse! Navigating around the bar where you order amongst the lunch crowd is awful. Also, when you have more than one in your party you each have to order. But you don't pay right away, you just place your order. But then after the last person puts in their order..you immediately have to go back up and pay in the order that you ordered. Confused? yeah, me too..and so is everyone else the first time they go. Its very bizarre and inefficient. 

Anyway, despite the face that you almost have to shank someone to get a table at lunch, i still go back. The food is just that good. Russells is opening a new location in the city soon too! I wish them much luck with that endeavor.

We were wandering around late near Bourbon St and my bf wanted to go to Court of Two Sisters but it looked like it was closed for the evening so we found Mambo's. There was a bit of a wait but this place has a rooftop patio where they were seating people too so the wait was short-lived. We asked for first available seating and was seated in the main dining room near the bar. They ask for proof of COVID vaccinations if you're dining inside so you better have them readily available. 

I really wanted fried chicken and while they had it on the menu, it was just tenders served with beans and rice. My bf ordered a cup of the gumbo to try and we went to town on the food. With Yelp check-in, we received a free dessert so I had the bread pudding. Service was okay and the place was busy for a Tuesday night in the French Quarter. For the most part, this place is a touristy spot which is why there's a line at the door. Reservations are recommended but not required.

My husband and I read the reviews before going here for an early evening dinner. 

Rule #1: if you see a bad review, look and see what else the person has reviewed. Anyone who gives Barrel 55 one star and Noodles and Company, Olive Garden, and McDonald's five stars....well, just sayin. Pocatello, Idaho is a culinary wasteland, so what does someone from there know anyhow? 

And then there are the folks that give EVERY review a one star. Stay home and cook your own food, I say. You can have your frozen dinner as you sit on your widening hips in front of the TV. Have as much soda and salt as you want. You will never be happy. 

That being said, we really enjoyed Barrel 55. The beer selection is outstanding. That is important. If your beer menu consists of Bud Light and 754 IPAs...then you have lost me. But this beer selection was great, a balance of several German beers, ambers, porters, some sours, and many offerings from local and regional brewers.
 
I had the salmon: Nice presentation of sockeye (might have been chinook) on a smoky plank with some roasted veg. The seasoning and sauce was excellent. 

My husband had the burger because...well he always gets a burger. He is the expert burger guy in Boise, though I wish he would splash out and get something more exciting. A burger does, in fact, help to bring out the best in a beer. It looked great, on a nice bun. 

I tried the fries when my hubby wasn't looking and they were very good as well.

The waiter was all about himself, telling us that it is his birthday and practically reading his resume to us. Ok. Just bring me my food and go away please. But I figure that bad waitstaff soon exits through the back door. The guy didn't make my food taste good. The chef did. Can't make a living by acting like an idiot waiter. We didn't do much in the way of tip, as not to encourage his bad behavior.

I've never written a Yelp review but I feel as if it's needed. The drinks were so gross I could barely take a sip and my food made me nauseous. Would not recommend. However very good looking restaurant. Would suggest the blind dog dog next door for drinks and the pizza across the street for food. The first place I've had to leave to get dinner after dinner. 0/0

No, thank you.

This was the very first spot my group ate at once we arrived fresh off the plane, and I was excited and STARVING for some good cajun food. Mother's did not deliver, sadly. Our Uber driver even said, "good-luck they usually have a line outside down to the end of the block most days." 

When we arrived...no line...

You get your menus from the entrance, look it over and order at the counter, and they bring your dish to wherever you sit. The lady at the counter looked pissed and annoyed at everyone. After that awkward encounter with her, we sat down and there were no napkins/utensils in sight. The first dish they gave me was my side order of fries. They were cold like...cold cold and stale, but I was far too hungry to even complain at that point. I got their 'special' po'boy, and it just reminded me of a cuban sandwich on soggy french bread. The first two bites were great, but the au jus sauce took over and before I knew it ..it was soggy french bread and mustard. Portions were huge, so that's a plus. My friends ordered the gumbo, and three of them said it was the worst gumbo they ever had. 

Maybe it was an off night, but I would not run back on my next trip.

I wish I could leave no stars.  After being in the service industry for 13 years, this may be the worst service I have ever experienced.  Attentiveness was at an all time low, no sense of urgency from ANYONE on the floor.  TO THE OWNERS: You should be absolutely embarrassed by the food/service that you provide.  You can taste the frozen quality of everything they serve, it's ridiculous.  I will never ever come back here and will proceed to tell ten more people to do the same.  I'm appalled.

If you read my reviews, I hope you understand that I view food as a spiritual experience and occasionally I encounter a meal that I think may have originated in a higher place.   Yesterday I tried Ginger and I think I went past the divine in to the sublime and oh my god, I don't know if I'll ever be the same.  

This is how it went down.  My family came along and we ordered ginger tea and it was warm,spicy, and refreshingly delicious. Now I can't do Thai with out doing the Tom Ka Gai and well my father in law may have summed it up when he quietly moaned "I think this is the best soup I have ever had in my life."   Next we ordered the duck noodle soup and I can't explain the rich depth yet delicate flavor of the broth.  Simply awe inspiring.  I am a green curry fanatic but our waiter (who incidentally made wonderful suggestions the entire meal) suggested that I try pineapple curry which was off menu.  Again, I think I may have added and crossed that off my bucket list in a moment of sheer bliss.   My son ordered Pad Thai which was quite good and my other children split a bowl of the chicken soup with udon noodles which kept them silently eating for unusually long time.  

The pause for me really is in that my taste buds were screaming for more and I found myself cursing the confines of my tummy.   My mind is still reeling, I'm counting down the moments to when I can visit again, there was so much I wanted to try.   For those of you who pride yourself on knowing the best Thai places in town, I would be surprised if this didn't make your list.

Overpriced cake with poor customer service! The one person in particular that has THE WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE, is the heavy set woman with the glasses. MISERABLE!  If you can't take the stress of owning a successful bakery, get out. 
Never again! And I will make sure that I shout it from the roof tops!

I'm completely baffled by so many positive reviews. I think people forgot to rate the pizza, and instead rated how cool they felt by going to PB. Simply put, this isn't good pizza. This is coming from someone who counts pizza as a primary food group - and has tried most places in Center City, a good chunk in South, all the ones in East Kenso/Fishtown/PR, Manayunk, Roxborough, etc.

This pizza...isn't good. 

The service is nice, albeit unhelpful. How a restaurant can be out of so many things in the middle of the day is beyond me..like cups. How are you really out of cups? How does it take 25 minutes for a pizza to go in the oven and come out of the oven? Why is the crust as thick as a slice of Ellio's?

 Their tomato sauce is watery (might want to try that tomato paste, fellas), their crust is as thick as a regular slice folded over, and the cheese is ok. The fresh basil on the Jane WAS top notch. This pizza makes Lorenzo's look gourmet, Lazaro's high end, and is on par with Ellio's. 

Pizza aside, I'm stunned by the amount of tank tops I saw on people who were making my food. I have no idea how that isn't an L+I violation, but I sure as hell don't want armpit hair in my food.

If you're in Fishtown, you're better off going to Aramingo's Best, or just going south and finding something - anything - better. Guarantee it'll have less armpit hair. 

Oh, and vegans - just go to Blackbird. Cheaper, better, easier.

We've tried and tried and tried again. At least they are consistent: the food is consistently mediocre and overpriced and the service is consistently awful. I should mention that we haven't been here in about 18 months,  so it could have improved.

I have eaten at the AZPC on the north east side of town quite a bit,  and it's one of my favorite pizza places. I was excited when this one opened out here in vail. It's true,  you can't beat the price of the lunch special (now $6), but the quality of the pizza is horrible. When it first opened,  I figured they were just working out the kinks,  so after the 3rd over cooked pizza I gave it a break for a while. About 6 months ago,  tried again and both of our pizzas had rock-hard crusts,  one clearly burnt. The slices you get with the special always seemed ok, so I gave them one last chance. The crust was like cardboard,  the cheese scant and it was dripping in grease. It tasted like a frozen pizza reheated. I will sadly never buy from here again. The people who work there are great and friendly,  and I've heard the owners are great people. Sad they can't get everything in the kitchen working right.

I never was a fan of bowling until I decided to bowl at South Bowl.

South Bowl is a one stop shop for fun! Its a great place to meet with friends, have a girls nite out or chill with your honey on a date.

I came to South Bowl with friends during the holiday season. South bowl has a spacious bar. It was three dollar Thursday so some drinks and appetizers were 3.00. I ordered the spiced pear punch and it was spicy with a nice kick.

We also decided to play a game of bowling which was 11.00 for about three hours. 

Overall the music was nice, the drinks were affordable and the atmosphere was great. I would definitely return to South bowl.

It was a cold snowy Thursday and we were experiencing our first snow storm for this Fall season. Then their was this determined yelper who embarked on a lifestyle change and had choosen this day awhile back along with friends to splurge on Relish dinner!

So yea, I was definitely determined to make it to Relish despite the nasty weather, I just knew I was gonna eat some fattening food and I didn't care if I was eating solo. I was gonna eat and eat good mmkay!

I made it safely along with a few others.It was 3 course Thursday at Relish and that's where your order an appetizer, main course and dessert all for 19.95. I had the kale and turkey sausage soup, which was so flavorful and delicious, just perfect for the snowy weather. For my main course I definitely enjoyed every crispy, crunchy fried goodness of the buttermilk chicken and lastly for dessert, I had a lemon pound cake which was light, fluffly and plain good!

Overall service was wonderful, staff was friendly, accommodating and kept us laughing. We was hoping to get the snow storm discount!!!... unfortunately that wasn't an option lol.

Thanks Relish!

I've heard so much about Dock Street Brewery since joining yelp. Surprisingly I grew up in the area at not once did I stop in to dine. I never even knew it was a restaurant until I joined yelp.

Nonetheless, I heard they were offering takeout and I decided to check their food out. I actually visited twice and service was good both times. They have an online website and you order and pay online.

Dock Street Brewery will call then call you to pick up your food and both times it took less than 30 minutes. 

So far I tried their fig jam pie and their Flammen pie. The fig jam was okay it had fig spread as the tomato base along with cheese and smoked bacon. Its the perfect sweet and salty however after a few bites I thought it was a little too sweet. The Flammen pie was pretty good it had smoked bacon, carmelized onions and herbs which I thought was delicious. The dough on both pies were fantastic and you can tell it was baked in an wood fire oven. 

Overall if I'm in the mood for some fancy pizza, I'll definitely check out Dock Street Brewery!

Yum Yum, I purchased the game over cheesesteak with a side of garlic parm fries and I was in lunch break heaven!!

Wow that cheesesteak took my lunch to another level!!. So Lee's Deli is a small store, on the corner of Baltimore Ave and they sell hot/cold foods. Lee's Deli also have a small area to dine in as well.

Lee's Deli been around for years and lately they have been known for their creative cheesesteaks. They have a Korean Bbq cheesesteak which has bulgolgi meat. They also have the rule breaker cheesesteak which has salmon and shrimp. They have vegan steaks and other food items as well.

That day I decided to purchase the game over, it had shrimp, chicken, broccoli and spinach. It was packed with flavors. My sandwich came with a sweet and spicy sauce on the side which added a delicious kick to the entire meal.

Overall the staff was very friendly, I was greeted with a nice hello and I also received a free carrot cake for using the ATM machine! 

I will definitely be back to try the Korean Bbq cheesesteak!!

2.5
Sighs in all my dramticness- yupp just made up that word lol. Sooo lets begin...

I dont know, I think based on my African American heritage and my grandmom who lived in a trailor home in Nathlie Virginia! I'm used to and been brought up on some good ole Southern cooking! So I think I place expectations a little too high when it comes to southern cooking espically with a restaurant called South!

So South seems to be a Southern and Louisiana fusion of food but it just wasn't good and the service wasn't good either. I orderd the catfish po boy and cornbread. My sandwich tasted bland the fish was too breaded, the remoulade was hardly there it was just boring. The fries tasted oily as if they placed the fries in day old oil. I originally ordered the hushpuppies but after waiting almost an hour they told me they couldn't get the recipe together so that's how I ended up with the cornbread for free which was nice.

The service seemed flustered, I asked the waiter for a straw cause I'm particular and he came back and placed the open straw on top of the table which almost rolled on the floor! Ughh no thanks! Then they never brought me back another one. Perhaps their skimpy with the straws?

Overall I expected more! Slow service and mediocre food!

As I was walking down Catherine st. In efforts to get to my car. I was intrigued by the rhythmic sounds of reggae music. My curiousity lured me into this wonderful small shop called hibiscus cafe.

Hisbiscus cafe is a vegan as well as health conscious store that sells vegan cheesesteaks, samosas, salmon platters and healthy smoothies. Today I decided to try the coconut delight smoothie. The coconut delight smoothie had cashews, moss, coconut milk, avocado, coconut oil and some other healthy ingredients. The wait wasn't too long and my smoothie was very good. It was creamy and it tasted sort of like an oatmeal cookie lol. I actually felt good about drinking it. I felt like I was doing something good for my body!

Overall thanks hisbicus cafe for the delicious smoothie. I look forward to returning and trying their other food items such as their salmon platters!

Five stars all the way!!! Wow just when I enjoyed my cheesecake from the cheesecake factory little did I know that I ain't seen nothing yet!

Yes ladies and gentlemen, The cheesecake lady is the perfect cheesecake. It taste like nana's cheesecake. Their cakes are definitely made with love and quality ingredients.

I ended up purchasing two flavors, I got the cinnamon roll and the strawberry shortcake. The cinnamon roll was my favorite. It had a thick cinnamon glaze and a small cinnamon roll on top of the cheesecake. Throughout the cheesecake it had pieces of cinnamon rolls and the bottom was a sugary graham cracker crust delicious!!

The strawberry shortcake was also yummy. It had a layer of cake and was topped with strawberries and a strawberry glaze as well as whipped cream.

These cheesecakes are rich, thick and creamy. The prices are kinda steep but worth it. There about 10.00 a pop but each slice is pretty heavy and can last awhile. The cheesecake lady offers a variety of flavors from banana pudding to fruity pebbles, make sure you get there early cause they run out fast.

This was a very neighbouring experience. Soon as I entered the small store, I saw to left and right of me, what looked like pictures of the staff family and friends as well as celebrities who have visted Koch's deli. 


I also saw the menu on the wall and they decided to name their hoagies after Philly Schools such as the Temple or Penn hoagie. They have this Special K hoagie which has potato salad, corned beef, turkey, pastrimi, swiss cheese and russian dressing. I was gonna try that but I figured I'll start basic and I got the gobbler which had all turkey meats, veggies and russian dressing. It was delicious and huge! you definitely can't finish it in one day!

Overall the staff was super friendly, the guy that made my sandwich was down to earth and he did a good job with explaining their selections.

Prices are a little steep but worth it. It's a treat you give yourself, I pretty much paid about 16.00. So if your in the area come to Koch's deli to grab a unique sandwich and have a unique sandwich experience.

I knew I had to check out Lucky's Last Chance after exploring their menu and discovering their creative burger selections.

After reviewing the menu. My heart was set on this one particular burger called the PB and bacon.Yupp peanut butter on a burger! I knew that I would probably like it because I enjoy sweet and salty food combinations.

The PB and bacon burger came with a double patty, it had peanut butter, fried onions, cheese and a jelly dip on the side. It was definitely delicious and huge. I enjoyed every bit of my burger. 

I also decided to order their fries and I don't know why I did that cause it was a complete waste. The fries tasted like it set under the light too long which I can't understand cause order and pick up took no longer than 20 minutes . It was just stale and tasteless. I was a little bummed about that being as tho fries are my ish!

Overall pickup and ordering was a breeze. I would order from Lucky's Last Chance. I just wouldn't get their fries again. Three and a half yelps!

Not much to say. Pizza was dry, bad and flavorless! Service didn't help either. I ordered a create my own vegan pizza with garlic knots and they only gave me the garlic knots. It's partial my fault. I just assumed they put everything in one box lol. I went home to discover they forgot the pizza. The cashier was apologetic however it still sucked! I was mad that I even went back for that nasty pizza that they could've kept! Smh

I like this yogurt beach location. I think the yogurt tastes the best out of all the fro-yo chains in town. The staff has always been very friendly here and I like the ocean motif. The only gripe I have about yogurt beach is that they don't label their flavors with potential allergens like u-swirl does. I have two kids with peanut allergies and not seeing the Reese's peanut butter cup flavor labeled with a "peanuts" disclaimer scares the crap out of me. I ask the staff and they're always happy to provide more information but I wish I didn't have to ask. My kids know to read the labels, when nothing's labeled as containing peanuts, they assume it's safe because that's how food labels works. Besides that: it's delicious, they're nice & the flavors are fun!

Malaga is perhaps the best authentic Spanish restaurant in the area.  It's phenomenal.  

Unlike Janelle R., I've never eaten lunch there (actually, I didn't even know about the buffet lunch -- so thanks for that, Janelle!), but I've eaten dinner there on several occassions, and I've never been disappointed.

Here's my list of the Top 3 things about Malaga:

1. The Sangria!  Holy crap!  I wholeheartedly agree with Janelle R.'s assessment of this stuff -- It ROCKS!  A full-size pitcher of the sangria will cost you $18.95, and it's completely worth it.  I've only ever had the red, but I'm sure the white is just as good.

2. The Paella A La Valenciana!  Holy crap! (Sorry to repeat myself, but seriously -- You've got to try this!)  This paella consists of "a combination of Shellfish, Chicken, Sausage, and Saffron Rice" and it's stellar.  And it's incredibly large.  I've taken leftovers home and eaten full meals for a couple of days afterwards.  (The poor homeless cats who live in/around the parking lot like it, too.  Especially the chicken.  Just ask my wife.)  Like the sangria, this also costs $18.95.

3. The Service.  I have to admit in many of my recent reviews for Yelp, I've been very critical of the service I have received at various restaurants.  That's only because some restaurants, like Malaga in particular, feature EXCELLENT service that puts most places to shame!  The waiters are friendly, jovial, and knowledgeable.  Heck they even like to sing from time to time.  (Speaking of service, several of the busboys and one of the hostesses are some of my ex-students, so you know that they're good!)

Malaga may be a little pricey, but most restaurants in the Chambersburg area are.  At least this one's worth it!

We just finished walking around the campus of Vanderbilt University, as we were walking back to our hotel downtown, we came across The Row Kitchen & Pub. We checked out the reviews on Yelp before going in and saw that they were pretty good. So we ate here for lunch.

The Row is about a couple blocks northwest of the campus (walking toward downtown). It is located in the West End neighborhood, described as upscale with many small shops and great (often expensive) restaurants.  The Row was an average priced restaurant ($10 burgers).

When you walk in, it kind of feels like you're walking into a barn, when you walk in to the left is a bar which extends to a big patio and to the right is the restaurant. We ate in the restaurant area. The walls are filled with giant posters/pictures of old country stars. Looks really nice inside.

I checked in via Yelp, rarely do that but glad I did. Upon check in, I received a free order of fried pickles. Reviews were raving about them, but since I am not a fan of fried pickles probably wouldn't have ordered them on my own. Anyway, the service was quick (we were only one of few parties there at the time). Our server immediately brought out the pickles. They were very thin strips, deep fried and really good (although a little too greasy) but that didn't keep us from demolishing them.

We ordered beers (the first two we tried to order were out- guess they had a crazy Sunday night). I ended up with a TN Brewworks Southern Wit and my boyfriend with a Jackalope Thunder Ann (it's an APA) both local breweries and both great beers.

For lunch I had The Row Burger it had pimento cheese, fried green tomato and a TN chow chow (a pickled relish made from a variety of veges). The tomato was barely noticeable as there was a heaping scoop of pimento cheese that took over, but it really made the burger. Very good. My boyfriend ordered the basic cheeseburger, it was a decent burger but nothing special. The burgers were a little overcooked for my taste but that was our fault for ordering them medium in steak of medium-rare (you just never know at a new restaurant which way to go). The fries that came with the burgers were just okay.

Overall the food and service were great. If in Nashville again, I would definitely stop by here to eat or just hang out again.

Rude hostess is all we will remember. On Saturday morning, March 9th, 2013 we visited the Limerick Diner for what we thought would be a nice breakfast out. While being led to the very back of the restaurant, we asked if we could have a booth up front. The older lady with long brown hair went ballistic. She rolled her eyes, led us to the front and threw our menus on the table. She then proceeded to go stand behind the counter and complain to one of the cooks about us. We could hear ever word. I laid into her, told her how rude she was, and we left. We will NEVER go back to the Limerick Diner because of this woman.

Not a place for kids or a pleasant experience. The owner/manager is very disrespectful and unprofessional. After our order, I was looking for a place to sit my family of five. By the fireplace, there are two sofa chairs and a small kid's chair by a coffee table. You would assume if there is a kid's chair, you'd be encouraged to sit there with your kids. As soon as we settled in, the owner came over and asked us if we would like to sit somewhere else with no explanation. Every parent understands you don't want to move around after you are settled in. Instead of an explanation, the owner stood over us and gave us a disgusted look. She then went behind the coffee bar and began to talk about us to her baristas. I know this because she was still looking at us with the same face as the baristas sheepishly looked over at our table. My wife followed up and asked if there was a problem to understand why this was our experience. The owner denied, deflected and made a personal attack stating that my wife has no customer experience. Really?

I can't comment on the coffee because after this experience, I asked for a refund.

My closing thoughts: 

The customer is always right, and you should do all you can to make their experience pleasant so they return.

Don't be disrespectful. If you don't want customers sitting in a certain area, make that clear and do this in kindness. If you truly are a "gathering place" make that clear in your arrangements and actions.

Great boba, lots of customization (sugar, ice, ect), tons of different flavors.  I was really impressed by this Tucson boba shop.  I'm a boba snob and this place lives up to my standards.  It's a bit on the pricey side but for a good cup of boba, I'm willing to sacrifice. They  hand you a sample of their seasonal tea at the moment which was wintermelon for the "holidays".  I had the roasted milk tea which was a nice change of pace.  Just a subtle hint of roasting.

Go!  It's a perfect afternoon pick me up!

Great food and excellent service. Although it's a tourist attraction, the prices are reasonable considered it's a prime location in front of the ocean with spectacular sunset view. 

I love their clam chowder and steamed clams. My wife liked their clam chowder better than the ones in Pismo Beach. She told me the soup has more clam meats and very smooth. 

The steamed clam with wine broth is a dish to die for. The clams are gigantic and the broth is so tasty that we could have drunk  the whole bowl of broth. The broth is great for dipping the breads. 

The two main dishes we had were fantastic as well. I didn't expect the crab and shrimp salad came with big portions of the crab meats. I could hardly finished the salad. On the other hand, the blacken halibut came in a right portion.  The sauce was delicious and the fish was tender and flaky. For a busy restaurant catering to tourists, they have done a good job on the food. 

Despite being a busy restaurant, we had great service from our server. She was attentive and kind. She checked on us frequently to make sure our needs were taking care of.  

We will definitely dine here again when we visit Santa Barbara next time.

I love this place!  I came here with a large (and loud) group to celebrate a friend's 30th birthday. We arrived with many wine bottles in hand.  The staff (including their friendly dog) greeted us and let us choose our table.  They immediately uncorked our wine and gave us the specials, but they didn't push us to order immediately.  Because of my food allergies, I ended up getting a pomodoro sauce with fresh herbs to go over some homemade pasta.  It was delicious!  I really didn't miss the cheese.  My friends went with the antipasto plate, gnocchi, and the chicken parm; no one was disappointed with their dish.  I skipped dessert, but everyone else split the cake and loved it.  We averaged around $25-30 after tip and we all took leftovers home.  It was a fantastic outing with good friends and food.  I will definitely come back!

Miss Rachel is beyond talented.  I don't understand how she makes half the things that she does, but her dishes are delicious.  We made reservations a month out for her "Dinner at the Pantry," which she does every Saturday night.  Basically, she only cooks for ten guests and they all sit at one huge-ass table.  Everyone that we met at the event was so much fun and we really had a great time...but I know no one really cares about that when they read Yelp reviews, so back to the food.  I got barbecue seitan tips on top of edamame puree to start.  It was completely amazing.  I really may need to start making mashed edamame.  My partner in crime had the poutine for his first course (yes, still vegan) and it was equally as good.  We both had the mushroom bisque and then I got the lasagna for my main course.  Instead of just plain noodles, she somehow used potatoes in it.  I'm an absolute carb whore, so I appreciated her inventive use of spuds.  Dessert was the cookies and cream ice cream cake, which was so good it should be illegal.  She came out to meet all of us at the end.  It's always nice to see your chef after a wonderful dinner and she was as sweet as could be.  

Whoever said that vegan food isn't good or filling or whatever needs to stop making excuses and try Rachel's food pronto.  I would gladly come back here in a heartbeat.
