I think that this is a good place to visit if you want a nice cocktail and a laid-back bar, but there is work that needs to be done with the food here.  I enjoy visiting plant-based restaurants, but there really weren't any dishes that I loved here.  The artichokes had an odd flavor and were difficult to eat, the chickpea fries were insanely salty, and tacos were difficult to share since there was only one of them on the plate!  First world problems, of course, but with the prices and the upscale vibe, I was hoping for a better experience!  Even though we paid a good amount here, I sadly left feeling pretty hungry.  I know they're still relatively new, but I really hope they can get it together and make some changes.  I would recommend skipping the food and stopping in for happy hour (Monday to Friday from 4-7) for their $6 cocktails at this point.

Great lunch yesterday at one of my favorites with a great staff that is always friendly and polite , bright and very clean dining room, and fresh and beautifully presented food. Decided on the Smokey Blue Sandwich that was excellent.  They cold smoke Mycella blue then pair that with a perfectly med rare roast beef that is on a multigrain bread that is accented with Worcester mayo, tomato and romaine lettuce.  Usually sandwiches come with salad or chips buy they had a great watermelon salad that was perfect with the blue cheese and the hot temperature outside.

Last month, my mom came down to FL for a visit and I whisked her off to St. Pete for some mom & daughter beachside R&R. It's an easy drive from Orlando, but after sitting in the car for a couple hours I was famished. I knew from my visit last year that St. Pete has a lot of great vegan options, but being a Monday and "covid times" I found the options to be slim pickings because lots of the vegan spots are either closed Monday/Tuesday or they were takeout only.

I opted for Leafy Greens because it didn't say on Yelp that they were takeout only, but when I walked in I saw it was actually setup for takeout only. Fortunately, the gentleman that was working that day, Anthony, was kind enough to let us have a seat and dine in. Before I get to the food, can I just say that Anthony made the whole experience for us. I never felt so catered to and welcomed anywhere. I felt like I was in a friend's home because it was just the three of us. He asked us what we would like and told us what he had available. He let us taste everything before preparing and was just so kind and wonderful. I was surprised to learn that Anthony is a volunteer working there too!

We opted to try the Thai Curry Soup and Lettuce Wrap Tacos. Both of which are totally raw foods which I'm still someone new to. Been eating vegan for over a year, but truly raw is another class in itself. The chilled soup was absolutely delicious with ginger, avocado, red bell peppers, cabbage, and zucchini. It was so refreshing! The lettuce wrap was made with cashew hummus, guac, red onion, cabbage, and featured a "meat" made from seasoned walnuts topped with cilantro and a spicy taco sauce. I believe this is their most popular dish.

While we ate, we learned from Anthony a bit about the history of the shop. It was totally raw and vegan for about 9 years, then started adding some cooked vegan items eventually. Construction across the street started to hurt business just before COVID hit so it was almost a double whammy for them. They've stuck it out and gone through a few changes, including adding some animal proteins and cheeses but still offer their raw and vegan staples.

This is definitely a place I will visit again if/when I find myself in St. Pete again. Please go support them and say hi to Anthony if you see him. He's an absolute gem. :)

I was visiting from Orlando and had done my vegan research for the area... Lotus was practically the top of the list of places I wanted to visit. 

I took my mom for dinner and was surprised at the menu even having looked on Yelp and their website ahead of time. There was way more variety and dishes on the menu than I expected. A bunch of different Asian cuisine, raw foods, smoothies, breakfasts, all sorts of stuff. And of course, ALL VEGAN!! 

I ordered the Singapore Noodles, a favorite of mine and this one did not disappoint. Their house made tofu was awesome! And fried up perfectly. I really enjoyed it. 

But my mom? I was a little envious of her dish. She got the eggplant tofu with rice. (It was my second choice between that and the noodles and I think she got it to be nice since she knew I wanted both. LOL) And thank goodness she did, because it was phenomenal. She Chinese eggplant was cooked perfectly (nice and soft, but not fall apart mushy) and the house made tofu was again a great addition to the dish. The sauce was delicious and I had a hard time not finishing the entire plate when my mom got full. Oh, and we also started with the Spring Rolls. We got two massive rolls that were filled with veggies and tofu and a delicious peanut sauce. The s'mores dessert I took back to the hotel was too much for me. There was a ton of graham cracker crumbs and the chocolate may have just been Hershey's syrup. Wouldn't get that again, but there were other desserts that looked great too. 

The location itself appears to be in an old Pizza Hut and isn't exactly fine dining, but I have been to very few vegan places that are. Sometimes the food served off paper plates in a modest little repurposed Pizza Hut is the best food. :)

Vegan donut and pastry lovers of Santa Barbara rejoice!! Breakfast Culture Club has your sweet tooth covered. I love the donuts here and I'm pretty sure it's the only place in town where you can get v donuts. They also have delicious vegan bagels and vegan cream cheese - yaasss! I must confess, I've tried every type of pastry they have here. If I had to rank them donuts are first, then bagels, followed by the banana nut muffin, and everything else is equally ok after that.

They serve Handlebar coffee and have many milk options, including my favorite almond milk. Also, on Sundays they have breakfast burritos! They have a vegan and non-vegan option. I opted for the meatless option which was delicious! It consisted of potatoes, tofu, onions, bell peppers, quinoa, and vegan cheese. 

To those complaining about the name, I actually really like it plus read the rest of it "Culture Club." It definitely has a lovely culture and vibe. I appreciate the art and cozy feel. The unconventional name is a good representation of the type of business this is - unconventional! I say this because there's not a lot of vegan businesses in Santa Barbara (compared to LA and SF), yet here is this little business bringing the minority delicious cruelty-free food and great service. Thanks, Breakfast Culture Club!!

IF your a tourist OR non regular customer....DO NOT dine here. Your not welcome. 

UPDATE....I researched if Roberto is the owner...google says your the Chef. The owner is Mindi....please read for this story. 

I've dined here at least twenty times. I have introduced out of town friends on business here, who have decided Ned since, my mom's best friend who's 80, my oldest son and his friends who visit. Three retired couples who we worked together and moved here from California. Not to mention my old neighbors south end of Reno. 

I used to live in Reno but moved and retired else where. 

Last night after a long retired work day...yes I stay busy. I decided to wrap up my two week work stay with my favorite dish. The linguini, shrimp, artichoke etc. delicious. 

I arrived at 625, sat at the only available seat at the bar. Three thirty year old women to my left and what appeared to be know customer to my right. The bar is small, as I've at there and in the dining room. 

I waited almost ten minutes to be offered anything. I was polite, asked for a wine list, and dinner menu. I ordered a glass of wine house, and my dish. Since the bartender offered bread to the three women, not me, I asked for bread when he brought my small pour glass of wine. 

While I waited, the bartender said someone bought the women shots of tequila...(probably was the manager), so the bartender had a shot with the three women. He was doing his best flirting. I drove to my favorite Mexican restaurant in south Reno. As always, 5 star food AND service. 

I called this restaurant at 720, Cecilia answered. I asked May I speak to a manager. She asked why twice. I asked now to speak to the owner as I've chatted with her several times and she's nice. Cecilia said the owner is busy. Then Cecilia said she is a manager. I laughed, said Cecilia can I speak to a manager. She said, "Jesus Christ what's your problem." I paused, knew this place had changed now from a year I was there last. I said thank you and hung up. 

I called back at around 8pm. Cecilia answered again. I told her, I called earlier and can I speak to the owner. Roberto identified himself as the owner. I said, are you really the owner? Two stars are for the quality of food, the Woman owner (ALWAYS NICE) the regular older woman hostess, the older guy waiter (I recognized him) AND the regular bartender who's trained everyone in town who wasn't there last night.

Terminate the unprofessional bartender who's behaved like that once before I saw. 

If I still lived in Reno, I'd drive to Johnny's from my old place in Damonte Ranch rather than your "restaurant." I dined at Johnny's over 12 times. That's my style. 

One more thing...please continue treating California customers and new faces like last night. You'll find that your revenue will drop. 

Also, you should have offered to make it up but didn't. 

My reviews are mostly 95% complimentary and I WANT others to visit.

I didn't deserve your treatment.

Elegance, Class and a Tantalizing adventure for your palette. 

My husband and I both have very demanding jobs, and when our Friday night rolls around, we like to share our time together over a nice glass of wine, a melt in your mouth dinner and good laughs. We have driven by Bricks numerous times, but never stopped. It was time to change that!

On Saturday morning I called the restaurant to make reservations, and had to leave a message being they are only open for dinner. I was initially nervous because in the experiences I have had leaving a message, you never  get your reservation. A few hours later, I received a phone call from a very lovely woman who was calling me back to confirm my reservation and assure me by booth I requested would be waiting for me. That was the first clue these people really had their stuff together. 

Upon arriving, we were sat immediately in a quiet booth tucked away. PERFECT!  We had bread service delivered and requested water. (In efforts to help the drought, water is served upon request) Shortly after that, we were greeted by Tootie, who offered a kind, soft smile, and asked if we had any questions on the menu. We told her it was our first time here, so she helped with our selections. Tootie took control of the entire dining experience by asking questions, offering suggestions, reinforcing our decisions while still providing professional, timely service. She was like the Pilot of our aircraft navigating us to our final destination. 

1st Course: Escargot 
Every "foodie" must try Escargot. It's a delicacy that has made itself widely known. I was excited and ready to do this. My husband on the other hand, started to get a paleness to him, asking the server assistant his opinion on it, and then googling the popularity of it. We took the plunge and when the plate arrived, the mushroom caps were soaked in a butter bath, the escargot was stuffed and topped with baked, bubbling bleu cheese. We took the first bite, and the only way to describe it was "Chewy, Delicious, Garlic Butter Sex". Mushrooms, garlic, bleu cheese and butter alone was enough to convince me, but then to add the escargot, it brought the entire dish to a full circle. 

Main Course: Seafood Thermidor 

Typically when you order lobster or seafood, you get a few little scrawny pieces on your plate loaded with vegetables and rice. Not at Bricks. My plate arrived with a small side of seasonal vegetables, a succulent lobster tail split, prawns and diver scallops all baked inside the shell of the lobster tail and then topped with Mornay sauce. I substituted the brown rice for lobster risotto, (You can never have too much lobsta!) and shared an add on of king crab legs with my husband. I felt like the great white shark under the ocean eating every little sea creature I could snag my teeth on. The seafood was so tender, so perfect. I mean, truly perfect. The king crab legs were steamed and served already shelled so you didn't have to cut your fingers up on those claws. 

My husband ordered the Filet Mignon, which was done medium-medium rare and served with a cabernet sauce dripping over the beef. His dish was served with tender vegetables and potatoes so smooth, there was not one lump. I honestly think those potatoes were smoother than a smoothie you would get a Jamba Juice. Again, another plate that did not disappoint. The filet was so tender, it was pure and not over seasoned so you can really get the flavors of the beef. The cabernet sauce was reduced perfectly, and the vegetables all vibrant colors which means they were blanched properly. 

Dessert Course: Chocolate Mousse & Crème Brule 

So as if we weren't completely stuffed out of our minds like a can of busted crescent rolls, we continued on to the dessert menu and selected a Chocolate Mousse and Crème Brule. When both dishes arrived, both just screamed decadence. The custard of the Crème Brule was flawless and creamy, with the notorious crust of torched sugar. The chocolate mouse was, well really indescribably tasty. The layers of chocolate just melted in your mouth as soon as you ate it. It wasn't too much, it was just enough. 

Overall, Bricks brings such a beautiful and classy dining experience to Reno. These days, people want the "Total dining experience" and that is what we got at Bricks. I can't wait to go back!

Visiting New Orleans with friends and Morrow's was recommended for their Cajun food. Ok cool, boom we decided to visit. We checked to see if there was a reservation process/waitlist. No problem, our party is still interested and expected a wait on arrival as it was fairly busy day. 

If you don't have time to read the details, here is the summary -- the experience was not ideal and basically sucked.  If Yelp allowed 1/2 a star!

For those that love details--Y'all ready, well here we go

Arrival/Check-in
On arrival there were host standing outside to greet guests and inform of the process and wait time.  BE WARNED there is not a waiting area, except
the sidewalk in front of the building. Initially on arrival, the guests in our party of four expected a wait time. We were told 1hr 30 minutes. TOTALLY our fault for believing them. They did give water to waiting guests every 45 minutes.  
At the time quoted we checked to see "how close" we were to being seated and was told there were 4 parties ahead of us. We then received a text that our table was ready. We went to be seated, the hostesses said "oops our bad we made a mistake and text you all too early". After 15 more minutes (1hr 45 mins), of waiting to be seated after receiving text, we inquired again and they said they would seat us soon, while another group walked up and had an exchange and walked in (will revisit this below). 

At this point we stay, because we're hungry it's late and really not many options. So we wait another 10
mins, (1hr 55 mins) and we see people who came after us walking right up and right to be seated -but behold it was after slipping the host money to go in, likely the table intended for our party. When our party and other parties who had been waiting approached, the host blatantly lies and says, she wasn't slipped any money, however, the guests who slipped her money and came after all other waiting parties, magically entered and was seated at a table. 
  
When called out for the BS, the hostesses lies and said, they didn't take any money and the guest opted to sit at the bar yeah ok "FAKE NEWS"
We saw them escorted and seated at a table. 
How misleading and rude.  I have no problem with a VIP list, however make it available to everyone and let the guests decide if they want to participate. Back to the seating at the bar, not one host ever told the guests waiting that we could sit at the bar as an option.  If we knew we had the option, I'm sure most guests would have dined at the bar.

After the hostess at the door was called out on their awful service and lies, magically we get a table. Total time to be seated 2 hrs 15 mins. 

Seating
Seating was limited and restaurant very full, some people were at a table after their meals just relaxing and passing time and guess what the party of four that "sat at the bar and didn't pay to enter" was comfortable at a booth right next to ours. Interesting! 

Ordering and menu
As soon as we were seated our waiter Delaney came fairly quickly to place drink orders and give us menu details. The menu was unfortunate and disappointing as it was limited, and the restaurant was out of corn muffins, red fish and red beans and rice. Delaney placed our orders probably within 20 minutes of our party being seated. I ordered the pasta with catfish. The dish was decent but expected it to have been stellar as it took about 45 minutes to come out. 

Manager check in
While we were dining, the manager and head chef came to check in on our experience and ask us how we were enjoying our meal. We began to explain to Chef Lenora our experience and she listened and went to investigate. After her "investigation" she returned with the same story the hostesses told us. When we told her we saw the money exchange her response was "perception is everything".
We didn't offer her an argument, and decided to just move on and finish our meal. Later in our meal she returned to offer us drinks on the house for our experience and we declined. She also offered a rain check on the drinks for the next visit. Unfortunately another visit is unlikely. 

For the owners and managers in case y'all decide to
care about the average customer experience, a couple of suggestions for improvement (free consulting)

1. Partner with services like Opentable for
Reservations or Waitlist on Yelp

2. Offer official VIP listing to move ahead of the line

3. On arrival suggest the option to sit at the bar 

4. Let waiting guest know that you're out of menu items before they are seated 

5. Buy software to manage analytics on food and kitchen supply  to automate supply ordering so you won't run out of menu items 

6. If celebrities and regulars are your most important customers close your restaurant to the general public during events like Essence

7. The waiters looked completely overwhelmed and exhausted, add more staff during extreme busy times.

I am a sucker for IG-worthy desserts (Don't judge me - technically I'm a millennial so can't help it) and adore soft serve so when traveling through Reno, KRĒM stood out as the best spot for a post-dinner treat. The idea is simple: Clear plastic cones filled with cake and sauce, topped with a tall swirl of ice cream. Their menu lists four curated options, or you can put together your own custom treat. There are four flavors of ice cream (I think this may change, but on our visit, it was matcha, ube, vanilla, and black sesame), vanilla or chocolate cake, and four sauces: strawberry, chocolate ganache, sweetened condensed milk, and red bean. 

My hubby kept it simple, ordering "I Love You So Matcha" off the "pre-set" menu. I like to make things complicated, so put together my own: chocolate cake and ganache + ube and black sesame swirl. They offer to add Pocky sticks but I declined....why?! Though they were consistently busy, orders were prepared within no more than five minutes. Conveniently, they are served with a spoon, so you can dig down past the ice cream into the cake and eat it all together. The cake was basic, but good. Fairly moist, with large crumb. My ganache sort of melded into the cake, so it was difficult to try it separately, but nothing tasted artificial, so I'm happy with that. I wasn't sure what my husband would think of the red beans, but he liked them! For the ice cream, matcha is not shy AT ALL - it is green and grassy, and if you love that tea, you'll be all about it. I found it a tad overwhelming for my taste, but again, it was natural, so no complaints. The black sesame ice cream was my favorite. It was sweeter than I imagined, with none of the bitter notes (that I enjoy!) usually accompanying sesame, but it did have good nutty flavor. The color is a stunning dark grey. Ube had no noticeable flavor beyond "sweet," but again, killing it in the color department with that vibrant purple. My one complaint: The ice cream almost hardened on the outside. Not unforgivably icy, but also not luscious and rich, almost like it had a base made entirely of milk or with added water. 

The interior is small, but there is enough seating for 15 or so people. It was clean, with self-serve water available. Employees were sweet as can be. At just under $7 per cone for good, if not stupendous ice cream, just own up to the fact that you want a cool IG photo (can't beat the "I licked it so it's mine" neon sign), and you still get a pretty decent dessert out of it, too.

Always a fan of ethnic cuisine, Kibrom's was a natural choice for lunch on a road trip home (side note, I always thought Boise was kind of lame, because, well it's Idaho (and before y'all start fussing I can throw shade 'cause I was born here!) but it turns out Boise is filled with a plethora of cool restaurants and businesses). I did not check where specifically Kibrom's was located, and it is not (even close to) immediately off the highway, so do not assume this will be a quick stop if you are on the road, too. But I don't regret my decision, even if it did lengthen my time in the car.

Kibrom's is Ethiopian food, with a generous menu featuring all manner of delightful-sounding entrees. What seems to be most popular, and if I could have talked my husband into sharing, I would have ordered, is their Family Meal, highlighting a diverse assortment of dishes. As it was, I opted for a variety plate, and ordered Dero Wot, White Tibs, Menchet, and Shiro. The price differs just slightly depending on if your choices are all meat, vegetarian, or a mix. Entrées are served on a giant platter over injera, with a simple acid-heavy salad in the center. I enjoyed everything, although was not blown away by any one particular item, in fact the salad was probably my favorite! My husband and I also shared a beef samosa, which we both LOVED. I do not eat a lot of fried food, but if I visited again, would order at least a couple of 'em. My husband also had a coffee, which was really more like espresso, being incredibly dark and strong, but he enjoyed the small serving, and felt that even with those characteristics it was not too bitter.

Service was brusque, though not unfriendly. It took about 25 minutes or so to receive our meals, even though there were no other diners present, and that felt a touch long. The interior is not much to look at, but was clean, and it is a large space, so would be a good spot for groups (not to mention then you could order EVERYTHING and try it all). You'll pay your bill at the front counter, and make sure to grab a couple of the candies up there, which are like fruity taffy things and yummy!

I came here on my last day of a little weekend trip I took to Tampa. I met up with a friend, and we had brunch. It's in a strip mall, so it's discreet on the outside, but the inside is decorated so ornately and you feel like you're in some sort of fancy smoking parlor in ye olde New Orleans. I was a fan. 

First thing's first, we ordered a half-dozen of the Char-Grilled Oysters (Romano, parmesan, Roux compound butter). They were very good. They were cheesy and buttery and oh so good. I could have eaten two dozen more. 

For my entree, I ordered the Alligator Hash (Crispy beer-battered alligator bites, garlic potatoes, sunny-side up egg, hollandaise and red "remi" remoulade). This was surprisingly good. I'm used to gimmicky fried gator on a stick when it's all chewy and stuff, but this gator was tender and absolutely delightful. Don't let the remoulade sell you on this item, though. It was almost nonexistent. 

I also got to sample the Crawfish Hash (Andouille and crawfish hash, garlic potatoes, sunny-side up egg and hollandaise). This dish was very similar. There were a TON of crawfish tails. More than enough to share. The sausage was a welcome Cajun taste. This was just so good. 

For dessert, we ordered the NOLA Style Beignets (Five light and puffy beignets covered in powdered sugar). These were objectively fine, but they were a far cry from what is offered in New Orleans. They were not light or puffy all the way, through. They were heavy. I mean, I ate them, but don't look for NOLA nostalgia here. 

Overall, this place was a delight. I'm used to New Orleans restaurants just shoving seafood boils and po' boys in my face, but this place offered a greater variety of dishes with great Cajun flavors. I was a fan. I will probably be back when I come to Tampa again.

After reading the amazingly positive reviews I had no doubt I would be experiencing Al's Finger Licking Good Bar-B-Que in the very near future and today the opportunity presented itself. If you know anything about me it's that I love good BBQ and can be somewhat direct and maybe a little harsh when it's come to reviewing these places, in my opinion Southern Style BBQ cooked on a real pit using wood is authentic and how cooking meat was meant to be from the beginning of time or at least since man discovered fire. There have been occasions when I've enjoyed smoked meats on mechanical devices that were developed either to speed up the process or feed the masses but the old school wood fired method that requires hours of patients is in a different league.

This place proves when you're passionate about something and willing to put in the work to make it successful the end results will be rewarding. What started in a garage feeding family members expanded into throwing a few extra pieces on the grill to feed a few neighbors it was apparent Al had the knowledge and talent to become what will be know forever going forward as a "Grill Master" this is not a self proclaimed tittle it's a fact. Once you experience this food that's a combination of southern style and soul food cooking you will know this is the real deal. After lunch I had the pleasure of meeting Jackie one of the family members here, it was apparent that her passion for serving only the best homemade dishes possible along with exceptional customer service is her number one priority and as impressive as this restaurant's accolades are it's all about customer service and the food. One look around validates the humble beginnings, one taste of anything here solidifies their place as one of the best BBQ joints if not the best in Florida. Demand has dictated a relocation is in the future as much as they love this location near 7th street in the historic district of Ybor City, so pay attention when you plan your visit. Now on to the food.....

-Pork Ribs- Fall off the bone tender, seasoned perfectly, smoked until a smoke ring and thin bark forms on the outside sealing in the all the juices. The flavor of the wood is intertwined with the seasoning to create a distinctive fragrance you get as soon as you get out of your vehicle in the parking lot so roll up your windows if you're in the path of the smoke. These are the real deal. 

-Smoked Chicken- Wow! Tender, juicy full of flavor all the way to the bone yet not dried out, it's really something magical. Warning this is smoked chicken not grilled perfect to pull apart and dip in your choice of sauces yes they don't bathe anything in sauce here you choose your sauce and how much of it you want, for me it doesn't need any sauce but I did dip a few bites of the chicken. 

-Smoked Pork Sausage- This maybe the most unique offering here and what sets them apart from every other BBQ shack in Florida, this special blend of meat and spice is going to be a hit with any pure sausage enthusiast smoked then chopped on the butcher block and piled high yes pour on the "hot BBQ sauce" on this one this is a real winner.

-Smoked Turkey- I love turkey and this turkey was moist, smokey and tender and oh for an added twist it came chopped like you would for a sandwich, different but delish.

-Collard Greens- Hand washed, chopped daily and cooked until tender. These aren't your average collard greens they are seasoned spicy and you will get a warning if you order them but not an apology so be ware of this, so simple so delicious and of course there's a bottle of pickled peppers in vinegars not the table to splash on top - oh and don't forget the cornbread it's old school and home made as well  served up with any order of collards.

-Blackeyed Peas- Seasoned mildly and cooked until they melt, Jackie assured me they were cooked from dried peas not frozen or canned there is a differences you know I could of eaten a bowl of these.

-Potato Salad- Mustard based sweet and tangy this is served like everything else here no pre-measured portion controls are in place here it's like fixing your plate at home when youve cooked your favorite dish.

-BBQ Sauces- Hot or Mild and these too are finger licking good.

There's really nothing more to say, if you're looking for good BBQ, you've found it...

Vieux Carre (Old Square) Pizza is a pizzeria, that caters to the crowds roaming Bourbon St. so don't be conned into thinking that the line out the door represents the quality of the product. This pizza is just okay at best, it does offer a very effective solution to offset the effects of the alcoholic beverages you've consumed prior to arriving here and can be used to extend you're ability to party late into the night if you find yourself lit up a little earlier than you planned. 

This crusty delicacy is served on paper plates and handed out when you place your order and hand over your money. The pizza is constructed on an assemble line and tossed into a conveyor belt oven where the cook time is synchronized with the rate of consumption so it's likely you'll receive a warm slice of pizza or slices depending on your buzz when you placed your order. It's likely the high ratings are based on this pizzeria's nostalgic location and the amount of time the reviewer spent bar hopping before arriving here. I ate one slice it wasn't bad but I could of survived without it...

Formerly known as Cheddar's Casual Café before ditching it's name and assumed the name Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen, this Irving, Texas based company has been quietly building its repertoire of recipes through local contests that invites the neighborhood's top amateurs to submit their tastiest side dish recipes for a chance to be featured on the casual-dining chain's menu. I chose the Cheddar's Club Sandwich and Fries, the club came on grilled buttered toasted white bread, I wasn't offered a bread choice so I don't know if this is an option, the fillings were fresh and proportioned to make this a nice lunch sandwich. The fries were just okay they were barely warm and actually kinda boring so a few will do. The service was exceptional and attentive even during the busy lunch hours which was very nice since everyone seems to be pressed for time. Over-all a great spot for lunch I would definitely return.

This is one of those rest areas that you just can't drive by, it's always a great place to stop even if only to get out and stretch your legs. The last few times I've stopped here it was very late and most of the restaurants were closing and the crowds were thinning out, other times it was if an event was being held here with a massive amount of people and long lines at each of the food vendors. It's a very large and well lit space and it seems to be staffed with an adequate staff to keep up with the sanitation but even with that said take advantage of the hand sanitizers and dispose of your own garbage please...

I was traveling through the area for business and had some time before my appointment and decided to grab some breakfast and thought this little café looked interesting. It's seems to be a local's favorite judging from the interaction between the staff and the few tables that had customers seated. The atmosphere is laid back and the restaurant was very clean and organized, I was greeted and told I could sit anywhere I liked. The staff here is very friendly and the service attentive, I was given a menu after taking a seat and my server returned immediately ready to take my drink and breakfast order.

My breakfast arrived after only a few minutes and looking at my plate it appeared to be just okay, the ham looked a little disappointing and after taking a few bites I decided to focus on the rest of the meal. I don't feel there is anything terrible here except I really didn't care for the ham, the rest of the food was just average at best. I don't know if I would go out of my way to stop in again but with the options in the immediate area pretty limited I might give them another opportunity if I'm in the area.

We decided to stop in for a few cocktails and to grab a bite to eat - rum runners and margaritas $5.50 damn Scott the bartenders are giving away the farm lol thank you sir they were delicious. Yes Virginia it is possible to get a buzz on well liquor - if you're wondering what's to follow well it's a really tragedy - humidity killed the individual packets of salt and pepper since we can't social distance using a real salt shaker someone needs to figure this one out, you can't serve homemade chips without salt.

The atmosphere - even with social distancing is manageable and not bad especially outside on one of the decks, everyone entering the property seems to be wearing a mask - the staff definitely did 100% of the time during our visit. If possible grab a table water side the breeze off the water really stifles the Florida humidity and provides a great unobstructed view.

Staff - very friendly and professional and plentiful even with the limited capacity rules in place everyone seemed to work together. The kitchen seemed to get the food out in a reasonable time and our server was on top of things so no complaints here.

Jack's Chicken Sandwich - We had the southern fried version and it was delicious a real quality chicken sandwich fresh ingredients and well constructed - I'd do this one again and again and again.

House Grouper Sandwich - We chose the blackened version - such a modest name, make no mistake this is deliciousness on a bun. The toasted bun makes it an exceptional choice if you like grouper.

House Chips - our we're served a little cold and I mentioned a number of times lacked seasoning so we thought they were bland - I could see that they have potential but I'd probably pass on the next visit.

Over-all we had a great time and a great meal and hope to return when we are back in the area - Good Job Capt'n Jack's...

Passe Aux Grilleurs (the passageway of the grillers), this quaint little town located on the southern most end of a barrier island and is the epitome of the salt life. If one was to try and describe this little beach town the words laid back come to mind.  This arty community is a real gem and surprisingly unspoiled, only 1 block wide by 31 blocks long its hardly a place you'll get lost in but it does offer some solitude, the white sands are filled with remnants of shells and the gentle waves are constantly replenishing the bounty if you're into collecting shells while walking down the beach. There plenty of options to get refreshments if you do end up at the beach...

We actually never walked inside the restaurant - the weather was much to beautiful to spend it inside, I guess the unofficial name of the Tiki Bar is "Rum Runners" a name so over used in my opinion, I think "outside bar" would be more fitting. Anyways it's located next to the pool and it closes at sunset and the single bartender walks back and forth so when's she in the tiki bar order up cause it may be awhile before she returns - the drinks are refreshing but unless you're a real light weight you may need to open a credit line to buy a buzz here. The view is great but the pool was infested with young ones and between the screaming kids and yelling moms I was trying every concoction this bartender could make to try and find my mojo to cast a spell to silence these frantic little people and their unassuming parents. 

I was staying at the hotel so I thought this place was a better option than Uber for a few drinks to watch the sunset. I guess since you can exercise the option to charge the alcohol to the room it's kinda like drinking free actually drinking here is free if you can justify in you mind that the room rate includes alcohol (only works if you have a buzz). If your looking for a place to watch the sunset this place is okay of course on this coast the worst place to watch the sunset is wonderful...

This is a local restaurant that I'd probably never dine at if it wasn't for getting an invitation from a few business associates that I came to visit here in Oldsmar. I was told they have a second location in Trinity but I'm not familiar enough with the area to verify it's exact location. We arrived here on a recent Tuesday a little before the noon hour the restaurant was surprisingly void of customers so we pretty much had a choice of seats anywhere in the restaurant which seemed a little strange according to my friends who frequently dine here so we grabbed a high top in the bar area and waited on our server.

The service was just okay especially considering it wasn't very busy, normally one would expect better but we weren't in any hurry so it wasn't an issue, after all it was Election Day so maybe that was a factor. We all ordered a variety of lunch salads I opted for the Ahi Tuna Salad blackened rare, it had an Asian flare and turned out to be a really good choice, lot of flavor with a variety of textures and trust me the lunch portion was absolutely perfect all the plates in our group were practically overflowing. I thought the quality was very good and the prices were reasonable I'd definitely return but probably remind the server that it's lunch service and everyone doesn't have more than an hour and a half to spare hmmm maybe this explains the lack of business...

All restaurants offering breakfast should ask themselves a few basic questions:

What statements are we making?
Who are my clientele?
Is serving breakfast appetizers pretentious?
How much of my breakfast revenue is generated by alcohol sales?
Do I really need more parking if I'm not turning tables?

Well the first victory here was getting a parking space within twenty five feet of the entrance - the second one was being seated immediately even though it's 9:00 AM on a recent Sunday morning with the outside temperature just a few degrees below 80 degrees Fahrenheit a block from the beach. It seemed most of the customers were tourists or temporary residents (snowbirds), believe me for a full time Florida resident this can be annoying at times, I guess I could be somewhat loud and obnoxious when I'm on vacation, well maybe not but it's no less annoying especially when alcohol is involved whether it early morning or late night. Maybe I should have participated in the Bloody Mary Bar.

Pardon me for the rant I was so distracted I almost forgot about the food - Chorizo and Cheese Omelette with pico de gallo and hot spicy salsa yeah baby this combination had me wishing there was a Mariachi band in the room, what wait... I ordered a biscuit with this I swear a biscuit shouldn't be a choice when ordering this combinación picante de amor exótico ole'.

Our server Jeremy was excellent - he did everything but juggle the condiment bottles and spin the plates on his head while break dancing, no really very cordial, professional and on top of things I mean everything from start to finish. The coffee was amazing it would make Juan Valdez proud if he wasn't a fictional character - rich, bold and McDonald's Hot - yes sip it at you're  own risk, maybe it's a secret brew and boiling gives it, its full-bodied aroma with a hint of smokiness that will delight the palette of the serious coffee drinker and all of this for under forty bucks including an appropriate gratitude. I wouldn't change a thing except for switching the biscuit out for a tortilla and drink whatever the guy from New York sitting at the bar was guzzling...

Great NYC Style Bagels are difficult to find anywhere outside the Big Apple, if you think otherwise it's been too long since you're last NYC experience, but sometimes you can find a good bagel that makes you think you've found one that can compete. The key is to getting your bagel fresh and that means you need to arrive early, although a good bagel doesn't need to be hot, it should be fresh, a bagel's at its best within 30 - 60 minutes of baking that means it's virtually impossible to get a good bagel anywhere other than at the location at which it's baked that's the attraction here.

So what's to like here?  - I'm not qualified to answer that question being this was my first visit but I can unequivocally say the bagels here are amazing, boiled and baked onsite daily so my sesame seed bagel was everything I expected - a thin crackly crust, a chewy but tender interior, and soooo delicious, oh yes I will return and no I won't get it toasted although I did witness some amateur requesting this as if they were at some grocery store or DD shop.

What a great find and lucky for us our visit here was perfectly timed with no wait, there's no doubt the crowds here can overwhelm this beautiful restaurant/deli and for good reason. If you're looking for a place with exceptional service and quality food do not drive past this restaurant. We were immediately seated by our very friendly and attentive server Kim, who explained the menu and made it clear they can do practically anything whether or not it's listed. The restaurant is a little loud, but the atmosphere is more festive than annoying they had a "master balloonist" walking around the restaurant making the kids smile with magical twisted balloon art providing latex hats and animated animals for all.

If you're a coffee drinker you'll be thrilled the coffee is very good and plentiful, the servers continuously roam the floor with pots of freshly brewed coffee offering to top off your mug or providing you with a cup to go. Everything we ordered was served fairly quick and hot, it was delicious I don't think I've ever eaten a better fresh made bagel, egg and grilled ham breakfast sandwich.

Traveling to the west coast from NSB is somewhat of a treat and is something I like to do a few times a year if only for an overnight stay - the trip is usually filled with some antiquing, some beach time and sometimes it's just finding a comfortable seat at a Tiki Bar over looking the water, but one can not live on Tequila and Vodka alone and it's always nice when you find a comfortable little restaurant / bar that's just a few feet off the street where you can do some quality people watching while enjoying refreshments and some finger foods. 

We arrived just past the noon hour and the place was nearly empty, and not having any historic knowledge to go by and not knowing this place had only been opened for three weeks we decided to give it a shot if only for a single cocktail. We grabbed two seats at the corner of the bar and we were immediately greeted by Vanessa who was tending bar like a pro although we later found out she had only just started with little to no bar tendering experience ( kudos to the owner for giving her a chance and to google for providing the mixologist training). She did a great job and has a great personality which can't be taught, and her innocence was welcoming so tip her like you mean it if she shuffling drinks when you stop in.

After a few Red Bull's and Tito's and some Hand Crafted Margaritas (yes this girl has talented) we decided on some calamari - which wasn't epic by any measure of the word but it was presentable and respectfully prepared for food service grub. We also ordered the 12" "New Yorker" pizza uhm... the crust was anything but New York but it was a really good pepperoni and sausage pizza on a great crust and quality mozzarella that will stretch for a mile (loved it).

The place began to fill up the later it got as the servers and hostess literally dragged people in off the street - that may be a slight exaggeration but they certainly solicited the passerby's and got results. We challenged Vanessa a little more and tried a few more creations that were move over-pours as we sipped on our regular concoctions and we even got talked into trying a hard seltzer in a slim can (not my thang but if you like hard lemonade type drinks you may enjoy it). We spent a few hours here at the bar waiting on our hotel room to become available - the location made sense, the service was exceptional, the cocktails were great and the prices were acceptable so who could ask for anything more.......

Felix's Restaurant & Oyster Bar is by far one of my favorite stops in New Orleans, this no frills oyster bar has timeless qualities that just aren't replicated anywhere I've ever been. The long counter bar is my preferred seating location, it seems eating oysters at a bar authenticates the whole experience and I swear they just taste better.

Now I've eaten oysters just about anyway you can imagine and I find its difficult to find a better oyster than one that's cleanly opened snuggled in a bed of crushed ice with a few shots of Tabasco, a smidgen of horseradish, a few saltines and a ice cold beverage, but the Oyster Rockefeller here stands up to any I've experienced, the extra large oysters are topped with a very spicy savory buttery chopped spinach mixture broiled on the half shell. If you want to go with oysters that are a little less jazzed up but can't stomach them raw I suggest the Char-broiled you won't be disappointed.

To the staff of H'ours Creole Smokehouse - Well Done!

This place definitely provides the locals a taste of New Orleans - I was born and raise west of NOLA so it was easy to identify the unique complexities of these perfectly executed dishes. There are many versions of these Louisiana favorites and although we do it a little different in Southwest Louisiana the flavors of the culture is indistinguishable and everything we tried was delicious - I wanted to try so many more dishes but that's for another visit being the portions here are certainly enough to share and probably will require a takeout container for most.

The staff here represents the character of this restaurant well, everyone here understands the meaning of customer service - we were pleased to have Shannon as our server she really exceeded our expectations, we never wanted or waited on anything.

Seafood & Sausage Gumbo: a bowl full of goodness - it all starts with a dark roux and patience. This gumbo was delicious, the texture and flavors were definitely created by someone behind the kitchen doors that has learned the art of making a great gumbo - folks this doesn't happen by accident there's a process that has to be understood before embarking on this adventure.

Grouper Pontchartrain: the quality ingredients are represented well here fresh clean pan fried grouper / Alaskan king crab / mushrooms / asparagus / delicate white rice all drizzled with a lemon, garlic butter sauce (absolument bien exécuté, l'assiette était la toile du chef).

Shrimp & Crawfish Étouffée w/ Soft-shell Crab: the soft-shell crab really should be a regular menu item (I want a half dozen to start lol) they are really that good - I was somewhat distracted by the crab but the rest of this dish stands on its own,  the large shrimp are so fresh tasting and cooked perfectly. The étouffée seasoning had the distinct undertones of the smoked andouille it was relatively mild for my taste but a few shots of Tabasco made the proper adjustment, this stuff is good - I'd say this is one of the more distinguished dishes on the menu and could bit well for the signature dish.

This is a beautiful restaurant, very clean and inviting - weather permitting you'd find me outside in the fresh Florida air. Oh I almost forgot to mention the jazz band on the porch was a pretty cool touch...

It seems it's more difficult to find a meal late on Christmas Eve than it is on Christmas Day itself, although most may be staying at home with family eating traditional grub or nestled all snug in their beds; while visions of sugar-plums dance in their heads I was thinking of a fresh made cheese burger loaded with fresh ingredients on a a toasted bun. Thankfully Burger Monger anticipated a few of us traveling and away from our homes and families would be needing something to eat and although we arrived right at closing time on their modified schedule this crew welcomed us in even though I'm sure they had plans on this holiday eve.

The restaurant had already been prep'd for closing but the grill and fryer were still ready for one more meal - a few burgers and fresh hand cut fries only took a few minutes and were delivered as the manager latch the front door while reminding us there was absolutely no need to hurry. It can be kind of awkward to be the last customers but we were treated as if we were the first customers of the day, now that's real customer service. Aside from the amazing staff I found the food to be outstanding as well and all freshly prepared exactly as requested. Although this isn't our tradition Christmas Eve Dinner nor will it likely be going forward it was a memorable one as they all seem to be unique in their own way and I was thankful for finding this place open after all - Twas the night before Christmas...

There's a lot to love here at Tikanis and I know I only sampled a small part of what makes this small restaurant successful. Covid-19 has impacted practically everything and I know during normal times this place would of been much busier. All the safeguards are in place to accommodate "dine-in" but it seems much of the business is still take out and delivery so wear you mask upon entering. The restaurant was clean and the staff was very friendly and accommodating and they took all precautions to ensure our visit here was comfortable by wearing their mask and minimizing their trips to our table.

We ordered a small Greek Salad to start and to share its adequate for two especially if your planning to order a pizza, the ingredients were fresh and the salad was made to order it would be quite filling for one person. I couldn't resist the crafted beer menu and our server was very descriptive with his recommendations, I am not a big beer drinker but the IPA's always get my attention especially when I ordering pizza. Like our server I can definitely recommend the "Atomizer" and "Life in the Clouds" especially since both were served ice cold in a chilled glass making them both easy to finish in this Florida heat. Okay since Pizza and Beer was going to be the choice for dinner before we left the campground we decided to let the menu lead the way, I was a little surprised to see they offer a deep dish option as well as some pretty awesome looking wings, but bringing left-overs back to the RV wasn't something we were interested in so we decided to go with a medium pizza to go with the salad. There are lots of good choices but it's the "green olives" that does it for us, hmmmm yes add some pepperoni and sausage but don't skimp on the olives since they really make the pizza.

Well since I'm volunteering my opinion I will tell you I think this place is something special, maybe it was the food and I know the food will keep people coming back but the staff and the beer choices makes it an easy choice as well if you're in the area, the interior decor is pretty interesting although I can't figure out the theme. After tasting the food its no wonder why so many people agree they do it right here....

I felt we hit a Home Run in Santa Barbara finding East Beach Tacos. Our original plan when we started the journey traveling up the coast of California was not to eat a lot of any one thing but to eat a little of everything so we could experience the culture and local specialities. We were very happy to find this little taco shop / recreational center while passing through town. 

Serving up delicious tacos is just part of what they do here but I will say  they do it all well and on a grand scale. The selection is huge but the dishes are simple, well thought out menu put together using fresh, quality ingredients all made to order. While looking over the menu board it was apparent that this place is extremely popular amongst the locals and definitely a destination for those traveling up and down the coast the steady stream of customers made it evident that these weren't first time customers.

We ordered the "triple play" two chicken tacos and one steak taco each of us having one chicken and we split the steak. These hand made creations aren't oversized by any stretch of the word but worked out perfect for us and actually there was plenty. I'd say if you're hungry and looking for lunch a triple play would be more than enough for one. The wait was a little longer than I expected being it was mid afternoon but that's the price you pay when it's all made to order so it wasn't an issue for us. I'd definitely stop in again on future trips. The service was outstanding and you're never gonna be rushed, once you decide step up to the window place your order and they will call your name when the food is ready - and please don't forget to pour on plenty of their hot sauces they are all delicious.

If you want to experience some old Florida charm in a city setting then you probably need to try out Big Ray's - the accommodations here are what you'd expect on a river bank restaurant a few small tables on the interior and lots of seating options outside, in the summer it will be humid and in the winter you'll have to deal with a little chill but everything here seems to be authentic this is by no mean a tourist trap, the local eat here so that in itself is the draw for me and the fact that I'm always looking for that perfect fish sandwich. Admittedly I can be sort of a food snob at times I have no issue putting down my hard earned cash for quality regardless of the setting so this kind of place appeals to me, it looks clean the customer service is outstanding and the seafood is what everyone raves about so it was a destination no doubt.

I wasn't going to let the opportunity escape me once I read about their fresh Grouper sandwiches, we like fried and blackened grouper so we ordered one of each to split and share both accompanied by those beautiful onion rings. Now my idea of the most bestest fish sandwich in the world is pretty simple and this place has all the ingredients to build such an iconic sandwich and forever be memorialize in my mind as the spot that can deliver it consistently. Although I think Ray's certainly builds a fish sandwich that make this place somewhat of an institution the construction of this sandwich was lacking in my opinion and may be that is just because I've raised the bar so high. I really enjoyed both but the for me the blackened was much better the seasoning was absolutely amazing, the fried one was a little bland but both delivered on the quantity and quality of the fish (maybe best ever in regards to the fish itself). I will take some responsibility here because I wanted to experience it as the founder of this place envisioned it and found it to be delicious but still not the fish sandwich I dream about. 

I definitely recommend this place to those of you who are uncomfortable trying to figure out where to get a really good fish sandwich - as for me I will customize my next one when I return. I want the blackened Grouper, on a well toasted fresh seeded bun with a slathering of tartare sauce on both sides, really fine shredded lettuce (not chopped like my first), a single slice of cheese, tomato and extremely finely sliced red onion. OMG I'm ready to make the drive right now - this place is really special, the staff is exceptional and the prices are in line with the quality no doubt about it...

Located inside the Intercontinental Hotel, Trenasse is what you'd expect to find inside a hotel of this caliper so it wasn't a stretch to expect this restaurant would be well managed and a beautiful addition to the over-all amenities of this property. 

Arriving just after 3:00 PM for Happy Hour was no accident after looking through some of the literature in our room. We were fortunate to find two open seats at the far right end of the bar which provided the best view of the restaurant and the lobby area and far enough away to mitigate any distractions from the busy afternoon hotel check-in process. 

Sitting at the bar provided us an opportunity to try an array of the offerings in smaller appetizer size portions that are priced very reasonable, being we weren't interesting in having a complete dinner service at this time of the day. The bar and kitchen staff worked well together interacting with all the customers and provided a fun and relaxing atmosphere. The food selections during happy hour are many and are presented beautifully on smaller dishes and arranged using the same care you expect in the restaurant. 

Raw Oysters - very large Louisiana oysters presented on the half shell, they were very clean and full of flavor sitting on a bed of ice served with all the condiments you could ever want.

Popcorn Catfish - bite size pieces of crispy fried catfish served on top of fresh greens in a cute cardboard bowl drizzled with two mildly spiced sauces with chopped green onion tops.

BBQ  Shrimp - grilled shrimp served in a classic spicy New Orleans BBQ sauce with a round of crispy French bread for dipping.

Muffuletta - a smaller portion of the traditional New Orleans sandwich with all the meats and cheeses you'd expect as well as the delicious olive dressing. 

Over-all a great place to start you visit to the Crescent City

I admit I've never eaten a waffle in this house and Burt's chili has never touched my lips nor have I ever listened to Francis Albert Sinatra belt out "New York New York" at 3:00 AM on the Waffle House juke box while sipping coffee from a ceramic mug on a stool at the counter or have I've ever traded useless tidbits of today's politics with servers named Agnes, Esther, or Ruby. Call me lackadaisical, indolent or slothful but I prefer the the hard composite booth in the corner facing the door while reading my laminated placemat menu that displays the demiurgic manipulated photos of entrées that have never actually been plated inside one of these cloned restaurants that mimics a shrine dedicated to the late night loner, the over the road insomniac trucker, or partaker of the last call from the jib joint down the road, of which I'm neither but I do like this place.

I like the grits, the eggs and bacon, the country ham and raisin toast served by a name tag wearing waitress that shows her years of service and who always offers up a healthy serving of honey, sweetheart or darling like a Hollywood script from the fifties and it doesn't matter if she's sixty-three or twenty-five the culture lives on. My vantage point provides me unequaled  people watching opportunities and at the same time shelters me from the views of the crusted waffle maker, the egg splattered oven doors, the greasy floors and dirty dish rags most likely use to wipe down the table top that props up my elbows. Yes I love these immune building venues and I've eaten at hundreds of them across the country and as unique as each may be they all look the same and the grub is consistence for better or worst....

Remembered Gendusas being really good but have to say I was very disappointed. We were seated outside which wasn't a big deal but our table was very wobbly so I was worried about my glass of wine.  We waited some time for our server. He took our order, brought drinks and we never saw him again. Other servers brought our food but it seemed my lasagna had been sitting. Had to ask other servers for drinks, etc.   very disappointed in my lasagna but no one ever asked how things were. Finally as we were boxing up the pizza our server finally came over. Asked if everything was ok and we said not really. He did not ask what might have been wrong just took our check. Other tables were being pretty well taken care of so I have to assume since it was just the two of us, we weren't worth the trouble and our tip reflected how we felt we had been treated. We had invited other people to join us and they weren't able to, and now I'm glad. I will not be back.

Fresh and delicious! I had read that Corazon Cocina was one of the top places to eat while in SB so we checked it out for lunch one day and came back again the next day! Located inside the Santa Barbara Public Market, in these COVID times, seating is still pretty plentiful and spaced out.

FOOD:
- ensenada taco - crispy battered fish taco with slaw and crema. Fish is so flaky and tender and that batter is so crispy when you bite down on it, yum.
- tia juana taco - shrimp and octopus taco. The octopus is probably one of the most tender and flavorful octopus I've ever had! This is what pulpo should be like all the time!
- chicana quesadilla - same size tortilla as the taco, and it's not folded in half or covered with a second tortilla (pretty much a taco with some melted cheese under the toppings). This was SO GOOD. The shrimp was super bouncy and fresh, paired with the fresh, sweet corn and salsa was amazing.
- burrito contramar - on the pricier side ($15) but pretty filling and comes with a side of chips. This was good, but not my favorite thing we tried, I thought some of the other items were more creative.

Salsas are available upon request and everyone here is super friendly and great - would recommend!

I live close to Sweet Eats so when I realized I had no candles for my husband's birthday cake, I figured I could run there since they have a large selection.  

Well to my surprise I was informed I couldn't buy candles if I didn't purchase a cake.  Are you kidding me?!?  What vendor refuses a customer?  I have been buying delicious cakes there since they have opened and have recommended them many times. 

Sadly, I don't know when/if I will return to Sweet Eats.  Won't let me buy candles, don't want to buy your cake!

I licked every finger during my meeting with Al. So, Al may I please ask you to forgive me. I mean what's a girl supposed to do when juicy, tender, delicious ribs just fall off the bone and the meat melts in your mouth? The baked beans were cooked to perfection,  Erika put her pinky toe in the spicy collards and you had my grandma's sweet tea. So please beg my pardon as I attacked my food like a savage. 

A quaint little house located in the heart off Ybor on the back side is where you too will find Al. It is not much to look at, but once you enter, you will forget all about the outside. I am glad I got in when I did because within minutes this places was swarming with hungry humans. 

The service was great! And the food was Ohhh Sooo finger licking! How's that irony!

My only critique is Al is only open Wed - Sat. So if you want a meeting with him, get there on an open day and early. And do not wear your Sunday best. Oh and please have positive table manners!

Geno's steaks is grrrrreat!!!!

4/12/20-I love to hear stories of heroic behavior. 

First, here's a review of a business I've never been to. Never tasted any of their products or met any of the staff. I can't even convey what's on the menu. Were it not for the name and here-say, I wouldn't know they made pizza. Hmmm???

A can tell you my wife loves this pizza. Ahhh! Well that's a finicky woman. If she likes something, that translates into fly like the wind over there and try it. It'll be great.

CHECK IT OUT:
Here's the best reason to visit. This man, Sabri, and his crew just built, baked and donated 270 pizzas to my hospital (Saint Mary's). In addition to feeding 1,000 health care heroes, he left a note of hope and encouragement for every one of them. What a fabulous gesture that must be rewarded. Cracks me up that he says his superpower is making pizza. Love it! 

So we have a local superhero that is incredibly selfless. Word is he makes great pizza and I'm told delivers them until 3am. Then I read where you can get $5 off your first order at pizzava.com.
Guess I know where we are headed this weekend. 

Thank you, Sabri! 4/20

What a great breakfast!!

Pros: Everything except the Cons. 
Cons: not open for Dinner!

First time caller, regular listener!  I'm going to make this my go to for breakfasts and lunches. I've not noticed this place as it's tucked back away from the main road a bit. But man it's worth the effort to find. 

Take a regular breakfast, stir in some creativity, fresh ingredients, a heavy hand for large portions and the finest fresh veggies and best tasting meats and you've got a top notch place called Amir Joe's. 

Prices are very reasonable. My wife had a "pick 3" for $7.99 if I recall correct. She had a large hash browns, small (their words. More like large) ham and cheese omelet and a biscuits and gravy. The biscuits appear to be pan made and are light and airy, but oh so delicious. 

Some of the best strawberry jam with my sourdough toast and my hash brown bowl was made with red potatoes and jalapeño peppers and chorizo. Dang it was delicious!!

Did I mention the Bloody Mary made with Sake?!  Yummy good!!!  Give it a try, and when you do, give me a nod...I'm the guy in the corner drooling over the menu, trying to decide what to order this next time.

I've never written one of these in my life, and I used to make fun of people who wrote scathing reviews. Until I went to Pizza Brain.

I can forgive any flavor bust, I get it. What I cannot forgive is bad service. Not because I feel any bit entitled, but because I have been behind the counter too. After waiting for 20 min, I asked in the sweetest way if they forgot my order because my patient friend had been waiting and her slice got cold (it also dropped on the ground after a rude female employee barged past with a tray, knocking into her). In response to my question, the cook guy jolted up and *yelled* back at me in an alarming tone, "Um, Everyone is waiting that long!" sounding as if he has to hold out the b-word at the end.  I was only confused about the 20 min lag between my order and my friend's. The cook made me feel so uncomfortable that I wanted to leave without my pizza, but I waited the full twenty five, maybe thirty minutes for my over-seasoned, over-priced slice. 

And for the record,  I do not care how alternative your shop is, there is such a thing as *inappropriately dressed*. I was offended at how unprofessional this cook was with his oddly cut khaki booty shorts and almost transparent sweaty graphic tee- the amount of exposed body hair and tattoos was just not what I want to see with my food.
I also thought not wearing gloves was violation of health code? Because no, I would not like to see you prepare my pizza behind the counter, wincing as I watch your bare hands and arms and imagine all of the bacteria/pathogens/arm hairs that might go into my slice as you take 25 minutes to prepare it.

What is worst is that the few horrible employees overshadow the one or two really nice, personable ones. I would gladly come back if they tweaked the staff but I'll stay far away from now on!

Honestly, I was excited to try GADCO after hearing so many good things from my friends and others on social media. I am a self-described donut enthusiast, so this seemed like a must-try in Indy. However, I found myself sorely disappointed. The donuts were dry (possibly over-fried) and flavorless. If I am purchasing a donut with a unique flavor or texture combination, I expect it to deliver, otherwise I can purchase something more satisfying from Meijer's bakery section. Unfortunately, these donuts failed to hit the mark. I have tried them a handful of times over the course of a couple of years hoping that I had just got them on an off-day, but they have never been worth the money or trip down.

Even more disappointing than these mediocre donuts was finding out about the inappropriate and unprofessional remarks made by the owners on social media. Completely tone-deaf and as tasteless as their donuts.

On a romantic get away from LA with my girlfriend I was sad to see that I thought there was a Ruth's Chris out here and it was closed. Lucky's came very highly recommended from the people at the Oceana when I asked where to get steak and lobster, so we gave it a try. 

I made a reservation for Wednesday night a day or two prior, and actually had to call the morning of to change the time... there was no one in so I left a message. I was pleased to receive a call back later in the afternoon. +1 star Lucky's, well done.

The ambiance of this place is excellent. +1 star. It feels very "rat-pack" olden days with a touch of class. We were seated immediately next to... let's just say a movie star. 

The server seemed busy so a young manager stopped by to say hello, we weren't in need of anything but it was nice to at least be asked. 

Service overall was good, however when we both tried to order Surf and Turf ($79 a plate) we were told they were "out of lobster." On a Wednesday. We asked to speak to a manager and "Leonard" came by and pretty much tried to do nothing to make the situation better other than suggest some other type of seafood similar to clams. No apologies, no offer to buy a drink, no offer for dessert, not even a handshake. Poor customer service Leonard, especially when someone is trying to spend $80 a plate. -1 star. The General Manager of a place such as this should know this. 

We both ordered filet mignon both medium rare. Mine arrived pretty close to if not perfectly cooked, however my girlfriends was medium well. We sent it back and the other younger manager apologized and was very professional about the situation. The steak arrived the second time correctly cooked. -1 star 

The mashed potatoes, and the asparagus were excellent. The steaks however were not in my opinion particularly good. It has a very "smoky" "woody" flavor, and it detracts from the flavor of the steak. It's never good when you have to order A1 for a $50 steak. -1 star

We asked to close our check and the "chef" sent us a dessert as an apology for the medium rare mishap. We weren't looking for dessert but it was quite excellent, and a nice gesture. 

Overall I might try this place again if we are in town, but go in with lower expectations and call ahead to make sure we can actually order what is on the menu. I think it is overpriced for what you're getting, but I have had much worse.

Incredibly overpriced for what they served. Ordered a hamburger with crab meat and fries for $17.  The hamburger had NO flavor, none.  Neither did the crab meat. the bun was falling apart because it was old or not stored properly. They didn't toast it or anything. They only gave me a handful of fries and half of them were undercooked. Definitely overpriced and overrated.

If you are an American Express Platinum member/card holder, you can get complimentary room upgrade, $100 resort credit, $45 breakfast credit and 4pm guaranteed late checkout.

This resort reopened in March 2013 after 8 years of renovation. There are 92 bungalows and suites on the property. The newly added bungalows are the ones that start with the numbers: 25, 28 and 29. 

Every room features a fireplace, espresso machine, fridge filled with all kinds of specialty beverages, and lots of closet space! And in the bathroom it features heated marble floors, an extra long pedestal soaking tub (made to fit a 6ft person comfortably) accompanied with a jar of bath salt and bath pillow that floats, a separate shower room with rain shower head, and double sinks.

Pretty much the only time I felt like leaving the room was to dine at the resort's restaurant which has a beautiful view that can be enjoyed best on the terrace. The food was great and reasonably priced! Some of my favorites were the Shepard's pie (hearty and yummy), Mushroom truffle risotto (truffles..mmm...), Lobster with gnocchi (great citrus and creamy taste), Beef tenderloin (so tender and juicy) and the Kobe steak and eggs (flavorful). 

The service overall was 4.5 stars!

Parking is complimentary for guests dinning at the restaurant and it is $35 if you are parking over night.

Some breweries definitely stand out over others. There was a different beer spot I visited with a few buddies back in July on the same day as Roy-Pitz and yet I felt the desire to write about this place first. Why? Well there's a few reasons that I can think of. Let's get into it.

For starters, Roy-Pitz Barrel House almost sounds like something that has nothing to do with drinking. Take out the word "Barrel" and you'd be hard pressed to figure out what Roy-Pitz is trying to sell. That mildly happened to us as I searched Yelp for breweries and didn't entirely understand the nature of Roy-Pitz until a little further research. But hey, they are in fact a living, brewing...um, brewery with quite a lot of character.

That word (character) is a great way to describe Roy-Pitz as the interior has an eclectic yet quirky style. Kraken/octopus artwork along the walls, succulent plants with labeled names on each table, barrel tops with original paintings, oh and the oddest image I may have ever seen in a bathroom (check the pics) just makes this place feel a tad different. Yeah, it does still give off the vibes of a bar or brewery with the way things are setup, but it adds some uniqueness which is nice to see.

It's also a pleasure (and another reviewable reason) to taste a few off-the-beaten-path beers. Roy-Pitz does just that with some normal styles while also getting exotic via way of sours. Sour Hound was just one of the mouth-puckering tasters that made up my flight, though there were also a few tasty varieties that beer drinkers know and love. Step Your Game Up (SYGU) was a hazy NEIPA that did the trick with plenty of smoothness on the palate which made it easy to drink. Nice job, Roy-Pitz.

Overall, Roy-Pitz Barrel House is kind of like your quirky cousin. Perhaps they're a little odd and a tad different, but you still enjoy spending  time with them. That's probably the weirdest comparison I've ever made for a brewery, but it works. So if you're looking for something out of the ordinary, give Roy-Pitz a shot. You might just write your review up sooner than later.

There's nothing like a tiny breakfast spot with a line outside to get you goin' in the morning. Welcome to Jimmy J's where my dad and I dined on a mid-morning meal on our recent NOLA trip.

That line is definitely not as bad as some I've seen before (Acme Oyster House...yikes!), but it still made me wonder how big (and how tasty?) was this brunch gonna be. We strolled down over to this tiny spot after Yelp did the trick in showing some high quality stars. I'd say things lived up to expectations almost fully.

That line/wait was probably only 20 minutes and once inside, I could see why it made sense. The place was tiny! Maybe 8-10 tables tops total. But it brought on a nice, intimately cool setting with jazzy pairings and actual designed skateboards on the wall. There was a tiny bar spot too for those seeking to start their drinking off ASAP. 

For me, I needed coffee. Now here's where Jimmy J's loses a little luster. No iced coffee to be found on the menu (I asked, just in case). Don't get me wrong, I'll take my coffee any way I can, but iced is the way to go and on a hot summer day, it would've done wonders. I mean Café Du Monde has iced coffee...c'mon Jimmy.

Beverages aside, the food did the trick. Well, at first I guess I was mildly skeptical. I don't know if it's just me, but when I think breakfast in New Orleans I want to see some interestingly infused dishes using ingredients and styles only found in the Gulf Coast. At Jimmy J's, there definitely were some menu items rockin' The Crescent City realm of cooking, but these were mostly for later dining (i.e. after breakfast). I did notice a special on the wall called Nawlin's Rancheros. Take out the black beans and put in red. Hey, good enough for me!

Results? Surprisingly delicious. With each bite my skepticism melted away. The fried eggs were cooked perfectly on top of a crisp tortilla with a bed of red beans and a few little pieces of decent chorizo. My father's French Toast Monte Cristo was also delightful as were his side of potatoes. Alright Jimmy, you make a good breakfast. We can be friends.

Overall, Jimmy J's is a quaint yet New Orleans-style spot, but mostly that comes from the decor. Food itself (for breakfast that is) won't lend heavily to the appetite of The Big Easy, but that's okay! You'll still get some quality morning grub, even if you'll wait a few minutes on line for it.

Looking for late night food love in NOLA? Go no further than Verti Marte. Like seriously, go whenever you want. My sis and I did just that last month on our trip to The Big Easy when our stomachs were rumblin' and the time was gettin' late.

Sure, you could dine on beignets til you're blue in the face, but sometimes you just need a massive sandwich after midnight. That's where Verti Marte comes in. Though the sandwiches are large and in charge, the place is a tiny hole in the wall. A little sign outside (and maybe a few inebriated people eating on stoops nearby) will give you the nod that you've made it. 

Once inside, it'll feel like a minuscule grocery store that, perhaps, your 94 year-old grandfather would visit to gather cooking materials. But in the back, that's where the magic is. A gigantic board of bread-based sammies, ones of all different types of interiors. Plenty of original concoctions while also featuring some local favorites.

For my sis, it was a chicken po'boy that her craving was looking for. Myself? I went with the muffuletta. Give it a couple minutes and your massive subs will be complete (even if mine wasn't technically a sub). Price-wise this wasn't the cheapest endeavor and it's a cash only affair so just be prepared.

With no where to really sit (unless we wanted to share one of those aforementioned drunken stoops), our sandwich consumption took place back at the hotel. That's when bites of scrumptiousness took place. Tasty chicken with all the fix-ins of a po'boy. As for my muffuletta, it definitely had the cold cuts going on, though the olive salad on top wasn't anything special (i.e. Central Grocery). Did the sandwich do the trick? Totally. But I'd go elsewhere for this specific option.

Overall, Verti Marte is nothing to look at aesthetically, but taste-wise it'll do the trick, especially at the wee hours when the alcohol has started to make that stomach rumble. Perhaps I didn't get the best possible sandwich, but that wouldn't stop me from a late night stroll back to Verti Marte to try my luck at one of their many other creations. Is it late? Then ya might as well join me. See ya there!
