Oyster is a word you'll find all over New Orleans and rightfully so. These babies are a whole lot different than the ones I'm used to seeing on Long Island. That's probably a good thing because then it bodes well for eating, like at Felix's Restaurant and Oyster Bar. This was the final dinner for my family and I on our recent NOLA trip and it did the trick, beyond just bivalves. 

Honestly, our original intention was to dine across the street at Acme Oyster House, but the line was something out of a Disney ride on a Saturday afternoon (i.e. long!). Felix's costed us just a couple minutes of waiting before we were brought into this bright white dining establishment. The front section almost felt like a classic foodspot in Manhattan. The back area opens up to a more large room that also had me thinking NYC seafood vibes, but you still felt like you were in The Big Easy (especially with a view of Bourbon Street from this section).

On to the menu which had a nice array of NOLA options, sandwiches, soups, gumbos, and (you guessed it!) oysters. Char-grilled started us off and these were delightfully delicious. More full in flavor than any I've previously munched on. Dinner had me torn so I went with the 1/2 po'boy (shrimp) and side (jambalaya was my choosing). Between the oysters and this main dish, there was a good chunk of time that passed by. Our somewhat locatable waiter told us the food would be out shortly (twice) before it finally made its way to our table. 

The wait was mostly worth it as my shrimp    po'boy had a nice fried breading and definitely hit the spot. The jambalaya was pretty strong in flavor (though not so much in spice). Everything was washed down with a great local brew (Hopitoulas IPA) which was on tap. It all added up to a reasonably respectable meal of sufficient pricing and enjoyable taste.

Overall, Felix's Restaurant and Oyster Bar is a solid option when looking for a solid meal in this loopy city. Though Acme was on the radar, Felix took the reigns and delivered enough to warrant a return trip if/when I find myself in New Orleans again. For now, I'll just have to tango with Blue Point oysters.

The idea of a courtyard usually lends my mind to some outdoor, grassy quadrant in the middle of a building. From now on, my mind will wander to a brewery instead. I'm all for this thinking so a big thanks to Courtyard Brewery for making my mind more beer oriented when thinking of certain vocabulary. 

This changing of the words occurred last month when I took a long and hot walk all the way from the French Quarter down to this unsuspecting brew-front. Really, if you didn't know what you were looking for (thanks, Yelp for the pics!) then you'd probably pass right by the place. What seems to be a loading dock turned brewery is what you'll find along with, I suppose, a concrete-esque courtyard area? There's a whole brick section of tables and umbrellas outside which could also be the courtyard in question, but on that sweltering June Monday in NOLA I had no plans on staying outside.

The fact that it was a Monday (around 11:45) probably led to the reasoning of why things were slow (I only saw three people come in during the hour and half I was there). Hey, I was cool with it because this gave me more time to take in all of the place. First the digs. A hodgepodge of chairs and seats made up the interior with a slab of wood behind the bar that listed the taps. Lest not forget the awesomely odd artwork (lounging gorilla painting and oyster wreath). 

From there, I took in the beer (one glass at a time!). Well, I didn't have full pints for each round as you can go with a half pour and still get a great bang for your buck (these ran about $3-$4, no flights by the way). I did get one full pint, but let's hold off on that for a sec. My first fractional brew was To Scatter Stars, an IPA with (count em!) 21 different hops. Not that I'm a master of differentiating bitterness, but regardless, this was a quality brew with great balance all around. 

The next half pour was Boss of Dead Souls, an IPA with citra and melba. I feel a little wrong with my initial Untapped score of the beer as my first few sips brought on a rather strong, almost grassy flavor that I wasn't expecting. As I continued to taste it, that flavor dissipated and created a solid, more mildly bitter taste.  After that, it was time to Preach! (Exclamation is part of the beer name). An imperial IPA that was deceivingly powerful at 8% ABV and was great on style and mouthfeel.

Heading backwards, we return to my full pour. I don't know if it was the heat, my current mood, or some Nawlin's Voodoo, but Unorthodox Interpretations was a godly beer. A Belgian blonde ale that delivered wonderfully in representing the quality and taste of this brew type. Writing this up now I can still taste it. I almost wish I went for a second glass of it, but there was too much I wanted to try (plus Courtyard has a large selection of New Orleans craft beers beyond their own). It just makes me want to return that much more (it's totally worthy of another sweaty walk in the sun!). 

Overall, Courtyard Brewery is a unique beer spot full of great suds for the sipping. It's laid back which you can tell from it's chill staff and jazz music that played throughout my time. Yeah, so it's not in the middle of The French Quarter and it is a bit of a trek away from the more popular spots, but it's a brewery that should be on your radar if you're in NOLA and looking for local quality craft. Maybe the weather will suit you better than it did for me and you can bask in the Courtyard-ish-ness taking place.

Want a beignet? Yeah, you know where to go (*cough* Du Monde *cough*), but wait! There is more than one way to get your beignet (I like the rhyme, sorry). Enter Cafe Beignet, which puts itself in a position to really live up to the name. How'd it go? Well after having breakfast at this Decatur Street location, I'd say pretty darn well (for the pastry, that is).

Ya see there are a few of these cafés, but for proximity purposes to the Steamboat Natchez, this spot worked the best for my family and I. Though it shouldn't be overlooked as the style of this Café Beignet was lovely. A corner spot with open air feel and a classy yet southern style to its aesthetics. The player piano in the corner did wonders to the vibe and made for a great breakfast vibe.

A few not so great things? Seat space. The tables are pretty cramped together so be ready to watch your elbows at most spots in the place. The other part would actually be the breakfast itself. It took forever to get the food and once we did it was, decent (that's about it). Beyond beignets (we'll get to that in a sec), my family and I ordered two veggie omelets, a western omelet, and Cajun hash browns. One of the veggie omelets turned out to be western instead and from those three omelets I didn't hear any amazing statements (Mom, dad, and sis). My own Cajun hash browns were also sufficient with pieces of sausage amongst potatoes topped with eggs. Nothing special.

I will give Café Beignet this: those beignets? They were top notch. A little more money than Du Monde's, but much larger and arguably fluffier and maybe (just maybe), depending on your mood and the way the stars are aligned, better than Du Monde *gasp!*. That and their iced café au lait was pretty legit.

Overall, this Café Beignet (maybe all of them?) isn't good for much more than coffee and definitely their namesake. For those two things (and the ambiance) I would definitely come back. Though for the purposes of this review and the "meh" that was most of the rest of breakfast, we're goin' 3.5, southward (ya know, because it's New Orleans).

Let me be useful first: the pizza here is thin crust and you can order decent sized slices which run about $2.25. The place is on the smaller side and very informal.  A lot of the people in here were clearly stopping by for a quickie. It's still nicer than a lot of pizza places; I just wouldn't plan on throwing your Dad's surprise 60th birthday here. 

Now let me just love: I like my pizza a little greasy (so embarrassing to admit). And that's what this place is: just a little fatty pizza loving that cures Saturday morning hangovers or satisfies after a particularly long run.

The pizza has been consistently yum, the service nice and friendly... I can't complain. It's exactly what I want my pizza stop to be.

Dad calls me and says, "Have you been to Pizzeria Beddia? I read about it in Bon Appetit. Best pizza in America, Knowlton says." So I'm all like PFFFFFT, hell no. "Best Pizza??" Is there such a thing?! It's like if I'm in a room with Sofia Vergara, Charlize Theron and Halle Berry and you're like "Which one is the most beautiful??"  It's a DILEMMA people. I'd cuddle them all. And to further compound my problems, I went to their website where in ALL CAPS like a bad OKCupid Profile (why are you YELLING?) they instructed me that they make a limited number of pizzas and there's usually a line and please start lining up at 4pm for $30 pizzas. Not sure my boss would be cool with me leaving work at 3:30 to go stand in a line, guy. And you know I'm not gonna win a pizza on a weekend.

So, I called my between-jobs loves-food-as-much-as-me friend and was like, "I have this really really good idea.... You stand in line by yourself and bring fifty dollars in cash. For PIZZA." 

Thank God she agreed. Chomping on two pizzas later: Arribiatta pizza whose humorous description on the pizza board has the word "ANGRY"-- i.e. the poops you will have later on. But, oh so happily spicy. You're like crying and smiling at the same time. And then we had a sausage with onions-- I could eat a hundo slices. 

After much contemplating and processing I knew why this place was a special five star pizza (for me): It's *not* brick oven pizza. I know that sounds weird but I think 9/10 of the philly pizza places I regularly frequent are all brick oven places. Pizza that tastes this great and it was made in a gas oven-- that's a masterful skill. Like finding out Halle Berry is almost 50. Yeah. Gorgeous.

Cuteness overload.

Not that it's bad - I just loved being in here every minute of it. 
It was about 6 minutes, if you wanted to know that badly. 
3 minutes to decide whether I should be good and get just one cupcake or be bad and get three. 
0.5 minutes to learn that this place is cash only. CASH ONLY.
1.5 minutes to use the ATM.
0.5 minutes to make the final decision - three cupcakes it is. hehe.
0.5 minutes to pay for the pieces of happiness.

I had to go to work soon after so I got to finally enjoy the cupcakes when I got home - 6 hours later it still tasted really soft and delicious. I don't even like cupcakes but these were definitely appealing to the eyes of a cold hearted non-cupcake lover. I didn't have milk so I drank wine with it. Still worked well. :D

PS: the Jewish apple streusel cupcake is to die for!!!! YUM
PSS: They were all $3 or $4 each. Not bad.
PSSS: VERY friendly staff!!! I couldn't have felt more welcomed. Thank you, I'm coming back just because how fabulous you guys were...AND because the cupcake is so delicious.

What a wonderful reminder of what it was like growing up in Los Angeles. 

Wings & Rice represents the quintessential neighborhood eatery, reminiscent of the fried chicken shops that were once all over Los Angeles. You will still find them there. 

The restaurant is fairly compact -- about one dozen tables, with a patio that is pet friendly. There is one table I noticed that is offered for reservations. 

Also, there is a single television set, which was tuned to sports. I get the sense that the owners are die hard Arizona fans, and it doesn't matter the team. The Wildcats, the Cardinals and the Suns each had prominent display. There is also a wall in recognition of those in military service. 

It takes about 15-20 minutes to get an order, and the restaurant seems to keep a steady stream of patrons. Seems lots of folks call in their orders as well. 

It is important to know that while wings and rice are, indeed, the popular menu items, the restaurant offers a pretty extensive menu: katsu, cheesesteaks, burgers, smothered fries, and more. They even have butterfly shrimp. They also have ice cream and sell Coke products. 

I went with a combo that came with wings and rice, which was topped with a Japanese sauce and served with a side salad. Hearty and delicious! Perfect picnic food! 

Other things to know: 

Lunch specials run 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and include a drink, fried rice topped with Japanese white sauce. You can get chicken wings, strips, a hamburger basket or a Philly cheesesteak. 

They have daily combos served all day, which will run between $10 and $14. 

Their platters include BBQ pulled pork nachos, a veggie platter and teriyaki chicken.

They also have sandwiches - Parmesan chicken, crispy chicken and burgers.  

Their sides are varied - celery and carrot sticks, cole slaw, stir-fry vegetables, steamed rice, cheese fries and more. 

As for the wings, you get a lot of choices: buffalo, teriyaki, cajun, Italian, orange, ginger soy, lemon pepper, honey mustard - tons of options there. 

They also have meal deals with 30 or 50 wings, which comes with baskets of fries and celery and carrots. 

There is a fried rice special for $6 on Mondays and Thursdays.

Bonus: Free WIFI.

Bring your parasols and lace gloves. 

This delicate, graceful bakeshop just opened on the popular University Boulevard. Aesthetically -- especially given its light, bright, feminine air -- the shop stand out in strong contrast to much of everything else offered in Main Gate Square. 

Woops! is a national chain, with most of its locations scattered throughout the Pacific Northwest. And its most popular menu item: the macarons. 

*Side note: Did you know that macarons and macaroons are not synonymous? They are not the same thing. For a brief description, check out: http://www.popsugar.com/food/Macarons-vs-Macaroons-8038818

Back to the macarons. Woops! offers them in so many different flavors: raspberry, lemon, pistachio, peanut butter, red velvet, chocolate chip mint, cookies n cream, Nutella even. And you can personalize your macarons. The shop had a few with the block A on display. Cost is $2.50 for one. Yes, a single macaron. That seems unnecessarily pricey. 

In addition to the macarons, the shop also offers croissant sandwiches (the brie and tomato is quite tasty -- but too steep a price at $6), rugelach, Belgian waffles, muffins and other items. 

The drink menu includes espresso, lattes, Americanos, organic drip coffee, mochas, chai lattees and iced tea, among other drinks. Prices vary between about $2.00 and $4.95.  

Also, the space is lovely for a quick sit with coffee or tea and a book. Maybe even a dessert after dinner with your loved one. It would be perfect for that, considering this place is dripping with gentle romance.

I couldn't quite understand why this place was so barren. Arriving for dinner in the middle of the week, the place is deserted. And by the time we left, only two other seats have been filled.

That sort of thing always makes me nervous. 

But I so enjoyed this little spot! They have about 18 tables and could very easily seat large groups of people. Nothing fancy or flashy. Modest digs, but delicious eats. This seems like the perfect spot for a casual lunch or for a casual dinner with family, friends or your volunteer group.

The service is prompt and attentive. We ordered the tofu spring rolls and fried canapés to share. I went with the duck Curry and my friend ordered a beef and mushroom entrée.

Prices are very reasonable. Most of the entrées fell somewhere between $7 and $9. 

Portions were hefty. We had enough for leftovers. I absolutely loved my duck curry. And I thoroughly enjoyed my friends entrée as well. Both had such deep and smooth flavors - a perfect marriage of spices and heat.

Great Scott! My goodness, that was good! 

So, yes, I've been to 47 Scott multiple times. I like the feel. I love the concept. Visiting this location, I feel like I am stalking in some back alley in a bigger city, like Brooklyn or Paris. Seriously, while inside, take a look through the front windows. It has an interestingly eerie, yet, romantic feel to it and, suddenly, you may feel transposed. 

Moving on in the conversation. 

Here, I am reviewing the brunch. 

I have been to many a locations in Tucson for a late morning breakfast/early lunch. Honestly, I am rarely impressed. I mean, come on, it's eggs. Maybe some bacon or sausage. A cup of coffee. 

I could have made that at home. 

But this? I wouldn't want to make it at home! I would rather pay 47 Scott to make it the way it does. 

Perfectly. 

We opted for the $1 (!!!) starter of grilled bread with olive oil. 

Folks, you can't find a better appetizer at $1! Really? $1? That's the price of, what, a Big Mac? But, trust me, you don't want the Big Mac. You want this amazing marriage of crunch-soft, warm-subdued, salty-sweet. And there is something so ridiculously romantic about dipping bread in fresh olive oil, which has been sprinkled with lovely grains of salt and black pepper.  ...yes, even at 10 in the morning in workout clothes. 

I went with the scramble with roasted red peppers, blue cheese and bits of bacon, fabulously called bacon lardons -- which only led me to think about lard. 

I'll let that slide. 

Listen people, try this scramble! Yes, this is a gratuitous endorsement. Served with that amazing slice of sourdough and the bed of kale, it was so delicious -- warm, luscious, soft, cheesy -- that I, and this is no lie, wanted a second serving! 

The cost for the scramble? $8. And worth every single stinkin' penny.

Whenever I visit Agustín, I think of the business partnerships it may have facilitated, the deep love it may have forged between people and the friendships it may have strengthened. 

So much has been said about Agustín. It's true. The space has an air of casual elegance. Think: stylized country living along the bay, but without the water and without the ridiculousness often characterized as "quaint." Agustín is powerful, stout, lovely. 

The food is glorious. Fresh. Rich. Tantalizing. Often locally sourced, and with a reverence for responsibility. Every dish, every single dish, is served with hyper attentive detail. Service has been iffy in the past, but improved as of late. 

Also important: Agustín's energy is delicate and precise. The place exudes a unique kind of energy, as though the restaurant were purposefully built and designed to celebrate the coming together of people -- and not just around its food and drinks. Even when the place is bustling with busy bodies, it demands a cordial interaction and compassion, but without the pompous elitism characteristic of too, too many places. Strangest thing. I rarely feel this way at establishments that rank comparatively in style. 

So, yes, it is fancy pants. It's the kind of place that demands proper posture and attention to etiquette. But, at the same time, it is not purposefully intimidating. 

So to all you lovers, new and well established; to those of you celebrating important accomplishments and others who simply want a decadent night of conversation, laughter and delicious eats; to the partners -- LGBT, straight and otherwise -- about to propose, I highly recommend that you give this place a go.

This used to be one of my favorite spots for breakfast. But I hadn't been to Bobo's in something like 8 years. Maybe more actually. 

Anyway, this is a famed Tucson institution. It's where local go and where locals take their visitors. The place is tiny, so expect a wait. And you may even find yourself seated with strangers. In addition to some booth seating, there are regular tables and also a bar. Open kitchen, so you can see all of the staff at work. 

I know people who will wait 30 minutes or more to dine here. Not sure why -- maybe for the allure of the place. The food is good, and the experience is nice (Great staff! Really, awesome folks work here). But, really...a 30-minute+ wait? Um, no. 

Anyway, I'm still a fan. 

Don't let the appearance scare you away. The food isn't swimming in fat. But it's not light either. Certainly bring your appetite. It seems the omelets and the (large) pancakes are the big sellers. I love their breakfast potatoes. Perfect shape, delicious consistency with the slight charring that MAKES breakfast potatoes. In addition to breakfast, they have an extensive lunch menu. Corned beef, grilled cheese, BLT, chicken livers, burgers, soups and salads. 

And they keep it simple here. Nothing too frilly or fancy on the menu.

I have been eating here for years upon years. When I cannot get off campus to Shere-E-Punjab, this is my go-to spot. 

And since the renovation of last year or so, the space and -- somehow -- the service have improved substantially. My favorite about the new space: gorgeous windows that let in natural, bright light, and I've developed quite the affinity for the bright green chairs there. 

What to know? 

This is a small, super casual and speedy restaurant. And, after placing your order, you can be sure that your food will be prepped and ready to go within 10 minutes or so. 

My favorite is the saag. Doesn't matter if you have it with chicken, paneer or whatever else, the dish always carries a lovely flavor, with a hint of mustard seed. Nice. 

But where are the issues? 

The place can get crammed very quickly during the lunch rush. That makes for too many awkward situations. 

Also, the veggie samosas and the tikka masala are strangely flat on the flavor. Just...not interesting at all. 

I hear the tikka masala is the most popular dish. How?! There is SO MUCH MORE going on with the menu offerings, I cannot believe the tikka is the go-to item here. The tomato sauce flavor is strong with this one. 

The bonuses?

I've had great luck with the curry and korma. The aloo matar and the biryani are also quite nice. 

And the Q-roll -- brilliant addition! It's yummy, spice-enduced flavor wrapped in a thin bread-like tortilla with crisp lettuce and this glorious sauce. Seriously?! Perfect for lunch. Try the lamb and haryali rolls. Yum-yum. 

Also important to note: You have the option of mild, medium or spicy. I tend to go with medium, but find that I often wish I had gone a bit more spicy than that. I was raised in Los Angeles. Tobasco sauce is a fun flavor additive. Dave's Insanity offers just an enjoyable rise. ("Give me the habanero, I say, or give me death!") So, for me, the spice often runs mild and dry at Kababeque. 

What else is important to mention? The favorite and enjoyable naan!

You have the option of plain naan, or a whole selection of flavorings, like cheese, japapeno, lamb, aloo and other naans. Seems the garlic naan is pretty popular here. I have not tried anything other than the plain naan. It's pretty amazing. The size of two adult faces for a little more than $2. Nice pricing there. 

So, yes, highly recommended, especially if you are on campus or visiting campus.

Tanias 33, located in a gritty lot in Tucson's famed Barrio Hollywood, has all the allure of a local, well-oiled (but not greasy) and heavily vetted establishment. 

Don't be discouraged or put off by its appearance. The place has, like, zero curb appeal. Tanias is like that popular aunt you never get to see until it's time for family holiday cookouts. And when she arrives, she comes with the best homemade tamales and flan. Seriously, once you skitter past the trash-littered parking lot and move inside, you feel transposed. 

I'd heard great things about Tanias. I've also read a great deal about this spot, known and revered for its massive burritos, soup selection and combination plates. 

This shotgun-style restaurant has five tables. Yes, only five tables. The largest one could easily seat 10 adults. There's no waiter service - they call your name and leave your eats on the counter. At the end of your meal, just leave your plates on the table, or put the tray on the far end of the counter, completely opposite the cash register. 

Now to the food. 

The menu is quite extensive and very inexpensive. 

For less than 10 bucks, you have a choice of custom combination plates, which come with rice, beans, chips and a drink. You have the choice of two items: flautas, enchiladas, tacos, tostadas or a tamale. Huge portions! 

You can also go for a breakfast plate. They serve chorizo, chilaquiles, machaca and huevos rancheros. 

For your burritos, you have the option of red or green chile beef, chicken, carne asada, birria, barbacoa, nopales - so many other options. Want to add beans and rice to the side - that will be $1. Same for adding chips. 

They have about one dozen soups, or caldos, including albondindigas, cazuela, chicken and rice, menudo, pozole and also vegetarian options. Comes with lime, cilantro, onion and salsa. I saw an older gentleman come in, order a cup of soup and eat it solo. He looked pleased as peaches, and was gone in less than 10 minutes. Later, I saw a fella sitting in his construction van out front, eating a burrito and listening to Christian talk radio.

Other items on the menu include cheese crisps and taco salads. Plus, they have numerous options for vegetarians. 

Also, they sell aguas frescas at $3 each - horchata, coco, Jamaica, limonada, melon, tamarido, mango and others. 

I went with the carne asada burrito with a side of rice, beans and chips. Goodness me! What a heaping serving. Carne asada was delicious - nicely prepared with a nice char, but still soft. Huge chunks, too. With the burritos, they come with just the meat, then you choose three free add-ons. Mine included guacamole. Score! I cannot stand guacamole that doesn't state like avocados. Tanias serves it guacamole a bit on the chunky size - will large scoops of avocado flesh. 

They also sell lollipos, masa and tamales to go, chips in bags and a number of other items for you home cooks. Also, there is a single, unisex (thank you!) restroom is available for customers. Granted, it could use some toilet tissue, not just paper towels. But, anyway, cool little spot. I am glad I finally had a chance to check it out.

Wok&Roll is one of the fairly new restaurants on the scene, having opened about six months ago. I was impressed. 

The restaurant has an open and comfortable feel. Word on the street is that this was once a Sizzler's steakhouse. But it feels completely different. 

I like the light motifs on the walls, which complements well with the dark wood vinyl and brickwork. It gives the space a slight feel of sophistication unlike many buffets, which, quite honestly, are too often dank, sticky pits -lowly culinary hangouts. 

So, yes, I appreciate that Wok&Roll was some brightness to it. The benefit also comes from a couple of skylights installed. Great idea there. 

You get the option of sitting in the booth near the buffet lines, or on the other side, which has a nice barrier wall that helps to drown out the sound from the buffet. There is also a back room. 

I appreciated the immediate greeting from a host, who provided a booth seat promptly. Also, the service is very attentive and kind. Christina, who served me on my first visit, is especially helpful.

For us introverts, there's a warning. The place gets pretty busy, and while the acoustics do a pretty good job muffling the noise, you are bound to run into folks who are entirely too loud and fall to the lower end of the scale when it comes to manners. This seems true of most buffets - why is that, I wonder?
 
Now, to the eats. 

I went for the Sunday buffet, which costs about $16 (they only serve the dinner buffet rate on Sundays). You can also offer from the menu, with sushi starting in around $2.50. 

The buffet is staffed by two sushi chefs, which replenish the boards on the regular. You have the option of sashimi, nigiri and rolls. I found that the sushi was pretty good! Pretty good. Sure, the salmon wasn't bursting with luster, the wasabi wasn't spicy and the boards could have used a quick wipe down - as some were caked with sauces. But most everything was tasty. The rice was prepared well, too - not dried out at all. 

The variety is great. There are several rows of hot food with offerings that include baked salmon, rangoons, chow mein, lo mein, honey chicken, beef with broccoli, pepper steak, crab legs and several soups. I love that they clearly mark the names of their food! Also, their steamed rice has an especially light and fluffy flavor. Very good! 

Also, Wok&Roll provides an entire section devoted to salads. They also have fresh fruit. And they have ice cream. And they sell beer, wine/sake. Nice spot!

This darling, charming restaurant looks like someone's extended dining room. It's cozy, comfortable and inviting with attentive and helpful service. But it is not sizable -- seems like it could only comfortable seat about 30 or so people. 

Interesting: The hostess/server will reserve tables in advance and without request for the anticipated larger groups.

On the menu are items the restaurant boasts are made in house and from scratch. 

Among other options, you have the choice of sour rye soup, beet soup, chicken and pork cutlets, veal schnitzel, potato pancakes, kielbasa and Reuben sandwiches, vegetable salads (with apples, carrots, eggs and potatoes), broiled salmon and desserts like cheesecake, kolaczki and crepes. Polish Cottage also cares the obligatory, all-famous pierogies with several different options for fillings. 

We were first-timers, so we opted for the dinner for two which, at $34, came with two stuffed cabbage orders, two sausages, a beef stew, two buns and eight pierogies. You get two choices for the pierogies, so we asked that our dumplings be stuffed with potatoes and cheese, and also beef. For dinner, the serving size was able. A great amount of food for the both of us. 

It was my first time eating pierogies and I found them to be just OK. They were served with sour cream (interestingly served in a to-go container instead of a more sustainable option), which did not enhance the flavor. Of the two, I like the one stuffed with potatoes and cheese the best. 

What I loved, loved, loved, however, were two dishes: the stuffed cabbage and the stew. 

The cabbage roll is full of pork and rice, then smothered with a tomato sauce. It was quite delicious! Not rich, but certainly not flat in flavor. I loved that, despite the filling and topping, you could still distinctively taste the cabbage. And the cabbage held its form pretty well, indicating that the dish was made fresh. 

The stew -- I need that recipe! It contains cabbage, beef and I don't know what else. Luscious, deep flavor! I was stuffed, yet found myself wanting another cup of stew. 

On the drink menu, you will find Bulgarian and Romanian Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay. There is also a Serbian Riesling and a Tsantali Blanc from Greece. There's also a dessert wine from Croatia. All reasonably priced at less than $6 per glass. There is also a selection of Polish, Slovak and Russian beers. 

All in all, a wonderful experience! And having held the Polish Cottage in my bookmarks for years and years. Don't wait that long to give them a try.

Cannot believe I haven't left a review here!

I've been eating at Gee's for years! Many, many years. I wasn't raised eating dim sum -- in fact, first time I enjoyed it was at a sizable restaurant near Seattle's International District sometime around 2003. 

I remember being enthralled! I found that I loved the concept of sharing, and of having ample access to smaller samples/servings of food. The gelatinous sticky rice had me sold. I would eat dim sum for life, I pledged. 

Then, I would return to Tucson where decent dim sum is in short supply.

Very short.

The quality at Gee's is certainly no where near that of the dim sum I had in Seattle and that I also have had in Los Angeles, Phoenix and, strangely, Houston. But it is good. Consistently good.

Others have written about the poor quality, but I have seldom had bad luck in this area. Usually when a dumpling had dried out a bit. Or when the flavor was slightly off on a dish. I haven't had major problems as of late -- only that the sweet soy sauce served with the cheong fun was a bit too salty on the last go. 

My worst luck is with the service. Usually not being able to find someone when we need an extra plate, or some mustard sauce, or want to close out or check. And the carts can run low after the noon hour. But I'm still a huge fan. 

Also, Gee's serves dim sum during the weekday through 3 p.m. -- bonus! That alone gets them an extra star.

Formerly affiliated with the Marriott, the location has rebranded itself as the Tucson University Park Hotel. 

It doesn't seem like much has changed in the transition. 

The hotel pushes right up against the border of the University of Arizona, making it the go to place for athletic teams and their fans, people visiting for University business, prospective students and their families and, come Commencement time, graduation-ready folks. 

The 9-story hotel has a pool, exercise room, a lazy river in the lobby (small one; not for you and your bathing suit), restaurant and banquet halls and meeting rooms. It is right off of University Boulevard, the popular strip leading up to the UA, and not too far from Fourth Avenue or Downtown. This means you will undoubtedly hearing the "wooo" crowd yelling and screaming while attending the nearby bars and restaurants. And, yes, late into the night. 

Parking is locating a half block away at Main Gate Garage, or you might get lucky with street parking. But that is not ideal for a hotel stay, because it is metered. 

The rooms are sizable and comfortable with down pillows, though they turn all pancake-like shortly into the evening. Lots of fluffing required. Rooms are standard with a few lamps, a desk, flat screen TV,lounge chair and nightstands along with the bed, which is quite short. That's helpful for people relying on mobility aids. WIFI is included, though it can be spotty around dinner time until midnight. 

The pool, which reaches 5-feet in depth, is heated and comfortable. Jacuzzi is adjacent, and has a decent amount of strength with a timer that can run on 15 minute increments. Good amount of chairs for lounging, too. However, the pool brushes right up against a University building. So, while you are hanging out in the pool during the days, you may be seen by curious neighbors and walkers by. 

On site dinning generally runs 6:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. The Saguaro Grill offers a lunch buffet and a full suite of breakfast offerings. The happy hour runs during the weekdays, 4-6 p.m., with specials on food and drinks. 

Room service is swift, but does not offer fare that competes well with the surrounding area. You get the full range of offerings: frittatas, continental breakfast, an All-American option, broken yolk sandwich, pancakes, huevos rancheros, French toast, salads, wraps, wings, tacos, calamari (found it to be a bit too salty), burgers, New York strip steak, shrimp linguini, cheesecake, ice cream, creme brulee and more. There is also a kid's menu, but with fare like pizza and chicken fingers. 

As for discounts, inquire about the government, AARP and senior discounts for those 55 and older.

I have known about Pat's for probably a decade. Had never been.

If I am going for a hot dog, I am more interested in the Sonoran hot dog, or in making them at home. Preferably with hotlinks instead of hotdogs. 

Yeah. Eating hot dogs out just isn't a part of my repertoire.

But this seems like one of those Tucson institutions that requires your presence at least once.

Pat's is steeped in that old school vibe. It's a cheeseburger and hotdog stand that draws people in droves primarily for it's chili and its massive bags of french fries. 

Seriously, you can almost imagine people in the 1960s inviting each other out on late night dates, then sitting on the curb eating their chili hot dogs and drinking sodas.

I went for a plain hot dog and fries. The hotdog was fairly uninteresting. Moderately interesting, really. I've had better plain hotdogs at Wienerschnitzel. 

The french fries are pretty good. Humongous bag! I couldn't finish them off. Decent amount for two people, for sure.

There isn't sitting inside, but there are several metal benches on the front patio.

And keep an eye on your food - there are bound to be interactions with the urban wildlife. Mostly sparrows and doves. ... Though I did also hear a rooster.

Be forewarned: this place proudly proclaims that it is a non-gourmet restaurant. Don't expect to see lardons, canapés and eggs Benedict on the menu.

For a moment I thought, "Why did I bother getting dressed? I could just come in my pajamas and no one would mind." Just kidding! But seriously, this place takes pretentiousness out of the most important meal of the day. 

The first thing I noticed when I walked into this place was that it had somewhat of a cafeteria feel to it. Actually, the very first thing I noticed was that amazing decades-old industrial sized mixer in the window. Freakin cool. And the restaurant has all kinds of antique-ish ornaments and trinkets. And they even have a book exchange going. How amazing is that! 

It's worn in. It's family-style. All the decorations remind me of a grandmother or great-grandmother's house. And all the servers were briskly moving around calling people tell-tell nicknames like honey and darling and sweetie.

Reading the menu was comic relief. Do take the time and give it a full look over. It's food convergence to the extreme. They have American, Greek, Mexican and Italian dishes. I probably missed some other culinary regions represented. They put gravy on so many things that seem not to call for gravy at all. They even have this burger that's actually a breakfast sandwich but doesn't quite fit on the breakfast menu. 

I felt like a traditionalist. So, I went with the Denver omelette and my friend ordered the breakfast veggie dish. When the server took her order she mentioned rarely getting that request, and then asked to see the menu. Ha! 

I was terrified that everything was going to be drowning in grease. But I found that my omelette was both bulky and light. The eggs were extra hardy and there were plenty of vegetables included, but the meal didn't leave me with that disgusting sticky feeling after I ate. I also enjoyed the grits. It is so hard to find grits on the breakfast menus in Tucson! They had a tad bit too much butter, but otherwise were delicious. The toast was the only disappointment, cooked about 30 seconds too long. My friend enjoyed her meal as well, and we were both impressed with the broad range of vegetables included in her dish. There was even broccoli and cauliflower! What a treat.

All told, our breakfast cost less than $20. And I was surprised to see that they have a working class special where you could get a full breakfast for under $2. So, good find! I look forward to my next visit.

I feel like I have been waiting my life for a theater like this. Well...my adult life. 

Roadhouse has something for just about everyone: vegetarians, those who are gluten-free and your general glutton. I love the concept -- arrive early to have a pre-movie toast either in the bar or on the patio, then order your eats before the credits finish rolling. But be forewarned: the bar is very bright, busy and loud. 

The magic happens inside the theatre, but because the employees must work in near darkness, there's bound to be some hiccups. Like, receiving a burger you never ordered, or finding that your water was never delivered. Whatevs -- folks here are pretty laid back and chill, but with forward customer service. Not satisfied with something? Cordially let them know, and they will be more than happy to take care of the issue on the spot. 

And FYI: I never, ever saw a single person act like a douche to the staff, or anyone for that matter -- so kudos to mild-mannered adults! 

Besides the very minor mix ups with orders, it's a pretty seamless operation. 

I found that the nachos were delicious as-is. No need to add the cheese sauce, or the ranch-looking dressing that comes on the side. Perfect crisp on the chips, and ideal amount of toppings. 

The pizza is also quite delicious for a theatre. It all certainly tastes fresh and not at all frozen or premade, which is pretty cool. And everything is served on actual dishes -- even the popcorn. So fancy! 

And the lounge chairs. Yup, you can kick up your feet and lean back. Total Lazy Boy style. But please do not remove your shoes. Apparently this is a big no-no in Roadhouse-land. 

Great, now I'm spoiled!

Omar, you were damn right. The oysters here... unreal. 

Just to be clear, I'm not a gigantic fan of oysters. I can't sit down at a table and enjoy dozen as I'm usually satisfied with two or three before moving on to something else on the table. Oysters have never been a meal for me but rather a gateway to bigger and better things. Well, when it comes to the charbroiled oysters from Drago's, I'll gladly dive in for seconds. Hell, give me thirds. 

This review speaks for my table of six friends who all were in total agreement when stating that these were the best oysters that we've ever tasted. Granted we didn't go for any raw suckers, but the famous charbroiled are where it's at anyway. Oh, priced right too! I'll certainly be back!

The price is right, but the food is just wrong!

At 3:30 in the morning with enough booze in my system I can stomach the steak and eggs for $6.99, but the French dip at lunch had nothing on one of the 200 McDonald's hamburgers I had in my hotel room bathtub. Yeah, we filled a bathtub with 200 hamburgers... long story. Anyway, the bun was soggy (before being dipped) and the meat was fatty and kind of an odd shade of pink.. only in Reno.

Okay, more about the slop they're serving. Cravin' some Asian? You're in luck... or are you? Yes, they do have an Asian inspired section of the menu and yes I dared to go there. I ordered some kind of jazzed up fried rice with shrimp, chicken, pork, spark plugs, ear wax, toenail clippings, pencil shavings - who the hell knows what was in this?! Tasted like the "chef" dug deep into his bag of tricks to serve me up something special, and boy was it special. No thank you, I do not need a box for the remaining 95% of my fried rice but thanks for the offer.

Horrifying experience.

It was my birthday and I learned when you're in New Orleans, people pin money on you to celebrate. 

My group heard a band playing so we walked up to this place. The guy checking IDs at the door said, "Oh, it's your birthday."  He went to open his wallet and gave me a card. I said I didn't understand what he was giving me. His reply, "It's a food stamp."

I complained to the manager and she didn't believe me.  I'm at an absolute loss.  What would I gain by making up something like this?

Cannot believe what this employee did and that this is how this establishment treats customers. 

I took a photo of him, because he wouldn't give me his name.

I might be bias, but Peruvian food is the BEST. FOOD. IN. THE. WORLD. 
When the owners of Villa Peru, in Phoenix, moved their location to Tucson, I was ecstatic! This place is very mom and pop, and it shows through the heart and spirit they put in their food. Keep in mind that this place take a monden twist on Peruvian food, so if you're a traditionalist then you might not like this place. Regardless, try it. They imported most of their furniture from Peru, and they import all their ingredients from Peru too. It's also organic, so BONUS. I would highly recommend getting the ceviche. You'll never want to eat ceviche any other way- it's the BEST! Sorry, Mexico.

My best friend highly recommended the grouper and it's one of her favorite seafood places to dine in whenever she's in the area.
We dined in on an early Saturday evening. It wasn't jammed pack yet. I really loved the the atmosphere and very laid back. It's like a tiny shack, but when you walk inside, it's pretty cool!
Our server was very friendly and attentive. I started off with the crab cake appetizer then we ordered a Spanish Brut (bottle for $21.00). For dinner we both got the grouper (grilled) with a side of baked potato (my friend ordered the yellow rice) and side salad.
The crab cake was so delicious! I ate the whole thing! Loved the sauce that was drizzled on the crab cake. When the grouper came out, we both enjoyed it! It didn't need any tarter sauce because it had already had great flavor and was not dry. 
A great experience and I highly recommend it!!!

How convenient to have a bar and grill on the beach. My friend and I went for a sunrise walk and she highly recommended coming here for breakfast. You can dine in or out on the picnic tables where you can leave your flip flops off! How nice is that?
We had a simple breakfast -2 eggs (scrambled) with applewood bacon and home fries. We also got a coffee and orange juice. For $22.00 you cannot beat a good solid meal and the beach view! Our server was very friendly and attentive. However they were having a problem with their system, so we had to pay cash (or choice of using the ATM inside which we get a discount if we did). 
Other than that, great food and experience! Love this place!
Warning!! Seagulls are very aggressive, when dining out, please watch your food.

Highly recommended by my best friends aunt. Whose been coming here for years. This is her go to breakfast spot and I can see why. They've been established since 1989 and you can tell when you walk in. It's a small cute diner! Love the nostalgia decor and pictures hanging on the wall. It's definately tight and not spacious. But I noticed they are quick to clean the tables.
You walk in and sit anywhere you like. We were waited on right away! I started off with a coffee (love their old school coffee mugs). I ordered the build your own omelet which (3 eggs) their own herb seasoning in it I wanted cheddar cheese and bacon. My side are the home potatoes and croissant. I also ordered another side of bacon. My friend ordered the same thing except no cheese stuffed with ham and bacon. 
They are super quick with filling up your waters and coffee! 
We got our food right away. The omelet was definitely stuffed with bacon and cheese! They were not bashful! Plus I love the herb seasoning! Did not need to add salt or pepper on my eggs or potatoes! I ate all of my potatoes! So good! Plus the bacon was not greasy! I saved the best for last... The croissant... Super puffy and fresh! Yum!
Literally, I was stuffed and left with a smile on my place. 
I had an awesome experience and highly recommend everyone comes here!! They also serve lunch which I am curious to try the next time I come back.

I grabbed a big breakfast here to start my day off on the right foot and was not disappointed! The hostess was friendly, atmosphere was quiet and clean, and service was nearly spectacular. 

Food-wise, everything I had was above average. Their banana pancakes were stuffed with nanners, and scrambled egg-whites, along with homefries wit onions, were worth ordering again. Coffee was well portioned in a large mug... I've noticed some diners skimp here, which makes constantly asking for a refill taxing, and at times, costly. 

With this diner in such close vicinity to the Red Robin diner just a few blocks down, there is no need to visit RR, which lies well below the quality you'll receive here.

Went for lunch based on Yelp reviews. Really liked it!  Had number 6 in stone bowl. Very generous portion. Friend had the sweet potato noodles with tofu. She was skeptical but really liked it. Very good service. Owner was very patient to teach us about the food and checked on us. Will be back!

A lot has been written about how Cin Cin is a "typical" Chestnut Hill restaurant. I suspect those reviews were written by people who don't live here. We do not all live in big houses and drive Jags or Range Rovers. A lot of us live in 60-year-old row houses and drive 5-year-old Hyundais.

In fact, just about every stereotype you can think of to describe us "Hillers" gets knocked down pretty quickly if you spend any time at all here.

So the first thing I'd like to say is that Cin Cin is not a "typical" Chestnut Hill restaurant. That's because there IS no such thing as a "typical" Chestnut Hill restaurant. We have a few shot-and-beer joints, a truly world-class neighborhood bar (McNally's), a couple of pizza joints (only one of them, Fiesta, is worth a visit), a few Chinese places, a quirky little side-street cafe, an Italian place, a Persian restaurant (good, but wish it was better), a sit-down French bakery, a truly killer sandwich shop, a seafood restaurant ... and I could go on, but I can't think of one that would fit the stereotype. Our restaurants generally are not all that expensive (I've spent more at the Cheesecake Factory in K of P), and I really can't think of one of our restaurants that I would describe as snooty.

Anyway, the review. We started going to Cin Cin when my daughter was in grade school. She's old enough to have a nice glass of wine with us now, and we still go there, usually 2-3 times a month. Henry Lee, the manager, greets us by name. (Once, when our daughter was about 16 and feeling a bit under the weather, my wife and I went there for a quick bite on a Friday night. Henry asked where she was. When we told him she wasn't feeling great, he came out with a big bag of chocolate-dipped fortune cookies for her to eat when she was better. We've never forgotten that. Henry is a mensch.)

And yup, sometimes we have to wait, even when we've made a reservation. It's because Cin Cin really is that packed most of the time. And what does that tell you about how good Cin Cin is? It's well worth the wait.

The kitchen is super-fast, the servers get it right every time (they've had the same waiters for years), busboys clear and reset tables like it's a magic act, and the food is delicious and unlike any standard-fare Chinese food I've had anywhere in the U.S. The only place I can think of that comes close is a restaurant (now closed, I think) called Germaine's in Georgetown.

A couple of reviewers have described Cin Cin as pan-Asian, and I think that's right. It's billed as French fusion, but in all the years I've been stuffing my face there, I've never gotten that part of it.

There's a good deal of attention to detail at Cin Cin. At most strip shopping center Chinese places, one dish pretty much looks like the next. You could easily confuse the stringy, fatty chicken with the stringy, fatty pork. The sauces are thick, gloppy and unappetizing. The veggies are droopy and almost unrecognizable as veggies, heavy on the cheap-o water chestnuts. (And is it just me, or do all of those joints smell like someone just lit a giant Sterno can?)

At Cin Cin, the animal protein is all (gasp!) recognizable as shrimp, pork, beef, or however it's described on the menu. And the meats aren't all one big mass of gristly, cheap connective tissue--they're prime cuts. The veggies are crisp. Every sauce is different from the next. Everything on your plate is fresh as it can be. And the presentation? You're afraid to eat it because it's so dang pretty. (Without being fussy.)

The building itself (they used to park ambulances there before Cin Cin 's owners bought it and gutted it) is just pleasantly and tastefully attractive. Not overdone, and no cheesy butterfly fans and red lanterns.

I highly recommend the cheesesteak egg rolls (yo, Adrian, it's a PHILADELPHIA Chinese restaurant), the shrimp with honey walnuts, the crab cakes in a terrific mustard sauce, and the sake wild-peppered chicken. (By the way, when you see those two little stars indicating "very spicy," they absolutely mean it. Eater, beware.)

A few folks have commented about the quality of the desserts. I haven't had anything there that I haven't liked a lot. The fried banana is very good, maybe the best. But somehow we always wind up with dishes of green tea ice cream. Yum.

In contrast with strip-mall Chinese restaurants, which have menus that go on for page after page with loads and loads of choices (that somehow, mysteriously, all taste like kung pao chicken), Cin Cin has far fewer choices ... but what they DO have is just plain knock-your-socks-off superb every, every time.

We went for dinner tonight. I didn't love the hummus. The chicken shawarma was over cooked/dry/overly charred. The gyro platter was pretty decent. Overall I was unimpressed, but I wouldn't write the place off entirely. It was a random Tuesday night and they seemed oddly  busy.

I was so disappointed coming here especially after reading decent reviews. I've never had such terrible service in my life. We waited about 20 minutes before our server came to get our drink order. Our drinks took another 15 minutes before coming to the table. After ordering our food, they forgot to bring out our house salads that we asked to get before our meals. One of my friends asked for his second beer(happy hour 2 for 1) when we finally got our food and the server kept forgetting and he ended up getting it AFTER we got our checks. Our server was rude and acted like she had no idea what we were saying or ordering. Apparently you pay up front but your server won't inform you of that. We went to the restrooms and they were filthy. I wish I would've used them before I ate, I would've walked out. The food was okay. Nothing great especially for being the price it was. Having worked in the restaurant industry for years, I never thought I would run into service this bad.


& another hilarious thing to add; I asked for flour tortillas to come with my meal. When the food came, no tortillas. My friend was given three or four CORN tortillas. I asked the server if I could have some flour ones like I asked and after a minute of her pretending not to understand me, she got an attitude and told me to just share the tortillas my friend got with her meal. Amazing right?

I am a huge fan of The Listening Room. The concept is simple: arrive before showtime, pay the cover, get a table, order food and drink and listen to great tunes! But to break it down for you, here are the basics for a fun night at TLR:

1. Valet! It's so easy to park there, beause valet is close and super fast. Whee!!
2. Get there early. When you check in at the ticket counter, you'll get a table number. The earlier you arrive, the better your seat at the show!
3. Grab a drink at the lobby bar and wait to be seated. Once the doors open,take a look at that beverage - is it low? Grab another...you'll see why inside.
4. Go to your table and hang out. There is sort of a mad dash among the servers to start greeting guests and taking orders. See how smart you were, though? You have a full drink (perhaps one of their exceptional craft beers?) and you are just peacefully reviewing the food menu. Ahhhh
5. Enjoy the wonderful food! Orders arrive quickly, and the food is a step up from basic pub fare. We love the portobello mushroom sandwich, fries, Brussels sprouts with bacon, chicken fingers and salads. 
6. Marvel at the talented musicians! They typically play in the round with each songwriter playing a song followed by the next one doing the same. You'll hear a variety of artists - enjoy the ride!

So, that's it...pretty simple! Have fun and keep this on your rotation in Nashville!
We always eat here! This is as authentic and fresh as it will get.  The charbroiled fish is excellent and the lamb is an all time favorite. The service is great.  They treat you like family.

My order's been wrong 100% of the time, meaning they've got my take out order wrong all 3 times. This poor attention to detail would make me horrified to use them for catering. The first time there were several small things wrong (raw onions on side instead of fried onions in sandwich, no dipping sauce for wings, etc.). The second time I ordered take out, I spoke verrrry slowly and and clearly. My husband got home with the food and we realized they forgot his entire meal, a dozen wings. He called and they told him to come back for his food, exhausted after work, he asked for a refund to be put back on his card. He had to provide all of credit card information over the phone--hopefully the refund will show up. When my husband noted (nicely) this was the second time this happened to us, he was rushed off the phone without empathy.

I gave two stars because the food is decent. If I chose to order from them again, I'd literally check my entire order extremely thoroughly before leaving the establishment. Unfortunate. Who wants to do that?

In my humble opinion and having traveled the world to compare, there are only two sushi places worth going to in Tucson and Yamato is one of them. 

Yamato doesn't have good sushi, they have SUPERB sushi. Sushi that never ever disappoints. The kind of fish that melts in your mouth and is always, always fresh!

It's a small, simple, QUIET place so if you get there when it's crowded, you'll have to wait and staff will give you a wait time as well for sushi prep as the only person making it is the owner (hence the beauty and perfection of this place). 

Tucson people, if you want quality sushi, every time, there is no other place but Yamato.

Not just your typical Irish pub! Loved the atmosphere in this place. It was so packed for a Tuesday night and there was such a wide age range that came out to take advantage of the 35 cent wings and awesome drink specials. The wings were a nice size and had a yummy sauce. I had also had the shepherds pie which was good but over seasoned. They played a variety of music tailored to the crowd while showing an array of sports on the t.v.s. It was nice to sit in here and relax after work with good food and friends and a refreshing Blueberry Lemonade!

I'll admit Thai food is new to me, but I have a feeling I'll be having it more often after my experience at Thai Orchid.  We went on a Saturday afternoon and got seated right away.  The waitress was very friendly, and concerned for my wife when she ordered the spiciest thing on the menu.  She doesn't know my wife very well :)  I ordered the drunken noodles, which was had 2 peppers next to it, denoting the spiciness.  It was pretty damned spicy, which I liked, but I was actually sweating!  The taste of the dish was DELICIOUS!  Yes i just yelled that.  Overall, I give this restaurant 2 thumbs up, and will definitely be returning.

Okay, this is probably my favorite business in my area.  There are so many great things about it, I don't even know where to start.

The ice cream is freshly made every day, and they always have vanilla, chocolate, and a flavor of the day (changes every other day).  It's extremely smooth, and delicious.  You can see it being made in a machine right behind the counter, which my friend described as a portal to heaven!  I agree :)  The other ice cream choice is something called a yodeler, which is a GIHUGIC cookie sandwich with whatever kind of cookie/ice cream combination you want.

The toppings selection is great, and the sauces are also homemade every day (hot fudge, dark hot fudge, chocolate chip sauce, caramel, marshmallow, PEANUT BUTTER!!!).  There are plenty of candy toppings to choose from too (I usually go with peanut butter cups).

Zwahlen's makes all their own chocolate/candies and they have a pretty big selection.  The best part are their apples though.  They weigh about a pound each, and are covered in caramel, something else delicious and a chocolate(s) of your choice.  Dark Chocolate Peanut Butter is once again my favorite apple.

There is usually a line, but it moves quickly.  The staff is friendly, and pretty quick.  You can even sit at a table and wait for your ice cream to be brought to you, which is nice.  Best of all, the place is family owned, and thriving as far as I can tell...a rarity these days.

I'm glad to finally try this restaurant, just a short hop down Elysian Fields from my home. I was going to a little conference at UNO and lunch was on our own, so my co-worker and I went here. I had done my Yelp research, so figured this was a good, close option, and it was. 

I had the grilled fish sandwich and chose the "Elysian Peels" potatoes for my side. Both were quite nice. The Elysian Peels are a bit hard to describe they have more potato meat  than fried potato skins but less than...oh, lord, those baked/fried slices of potato that are thicker than fries. I'm having a brain freeze and can't remember exactly what they are called. Anyway, they were hot and crispy. The sandwiches are on brioche buns, which can add grease but worked great with grilled fish.

The service was good. The server was very nice and she was very attentive with water and iced tea refills. I'm looking forward to trying Munch Factory again.

Awesome food and drinks!! The calamari is a favorite as is the Strawberry Balsamic Salad with Salmon. The salmon is always cooked perfectly and the Balsamic dressing is always so good. The servers and bartenders are awesome!

The Brio Old Fashioned is fantastic!

Hanging out in Philly and wanted to try Lee's Deli after following a foodies post. Stopped by and they were preparing to close. Allowed me to order the shrimp, fish and veggie hoagie. The owner is so nice and the restaurant is clean. The owner advised they usually close on time but the grill is still hot. Ordered onions ring with special sauce on the side. 

The food was so good along with the customer service. Food very fresh and the menu has so much variety. I'm glad they cater to vegetarians.

They also have dessert. I was eyeing the carrot cake muffins with icing and the owner gave us 2 free. They were delicious and the icing was so good. I can't wait to enjoy another when back in Philly 

They also serve breakfast but are closed on Sunday. Everyone needs a day off to reset. 

Wide variety of beverages which I didn't buy. They were offering free can sodas and chips with certain items. 

I will definitely stop by when I visit Philly

We can in with a coupon I just purchased and when we were seated I told our waiter that and he offered to have us keep the coupon for the next time because he said it was happy hour (all day on Sundays). So we did, we had some two-for-one margaritas and were shocked when they came out and were delicious as ever! Gino, our server explain that they use house mix and it's not pre-made and you could definitely tell this was the case. 
He was very confident on his menu recommendations which I appreciated. We listened to what he told us to get and were NOT disappointed! We loved the tortilla soup, the entrees (which were big enough for leftovers to take home), and the service was some of the very best we have had and that is saying a lot. To have someone seem like they really care about your meal and dining experience was refreshing and it doesn't happen as often as it should. That being said, I cannot wait to go back and use my coupon I saved! 
I highly recommend for a relaxing atmosphere, great service and killer authentic Mexican food!

Sure, social distancing, masks are required, hand sanitizers, and instruction on how to wash your hands posted on the restroom walls...

BUT... we had several harrassing 'reminders' from the casino floor staff repeatedly admonishing customers to keep their masks on. Drinking? With a mask please. 
Smoking.  Must have mask on 'between puffs' we were told.

Not a fan of this very older crowd casino.  The bartender this morning at the bar by the front desk never washed his hands in the hour we sat at the counter. And the bloody mary he made us was so spicy it was undrinkable. 

Stayed at the adjacent motel which has a high Booking. Com rating but : unsavory clientele, no in-room Kleenex, no microwave.

Pluses: nice big TV,  golf channel, fridge and pleasant efficient front desk staff. Especially props to Amanda who allowed an early check-in. 

Housekeeping staff excellent, at least in this room. Trash removal and fresh towels. Bed made on our second day.  Soaps and shampoos provided both nights.

Its been ruled unconstitutional for the governor to tell you that you have to wear a mask.  It's only a suggestion. 

What happened in Vegas that made the Covid count so high was that the tests weren't processed for a few days, and then when they were, it appeared that a tremendous spike had occurred.  

Say goodbye to Reno and Vegas as both these gambling bergs are going downhill fast, as well as all Nevada with the shortfall in revenue this state is experiencing. 

Its the end of freedom and good times. Look at it as a tax: just as alcohol and smoking are taxed (because they are 'bad' for you), we will forever be forced into teeny plastic partitioned off slot machines.

No table games. No roulette.  No craps. No poker.

Killer 10 out of 5 star pizza BUT sadly killer on the wallet! I think they know it's killer on the wallet because they've given us a few free pizzas.. especially when our bill is been over $150. Yes $150 for 4 pizzas and drinks! My brain says RIDICULOUS but my stomach says OMG MUST EAT MORE, so obviously in this mind over stomach struggle the stomach has won and we have returned a kagillion times. I'm pretty sure that when our wallet is empty they will continue to give us free pizzas. Bahahaha sob sob sob 
Def the best pizza on planet earth, and possibly in the galaxy! seriously there is no comparison, nothing in Philly, NY, or even Italy.. well maybe Italy.. but you get my point!!

Mercury is in retrograde and I'm blaming everything out of step on the stars, and that includes our visit to Pub & Kitchen last night.
I have had many delicious meals at Pub & Kitchen over the years, and especially love their burgers, so I'm hoping this is just a blip and everything will be back to normal next week. 
Last night we stopped in later in the evening after dinner for cocktails and small bites, and had a pretty disappointing experience. 
We ordered cocktails, beignets & fries. The beignets were brought out 10 mins before the drinks arrived, and after eating one my friend noticed a curly white hair stuck to one of the beignets, OMG. We gave it back to our waitress who brought us a new one. The beignets were heavy and doughy, could have been better. Our cocktails finally arrived, they were all delicious, yet they were sliding down the table because it was on a slant due to the uneven sidewalk, we decided to cover the table with a cloth napkin and put the cocktails on top so they would stop sliding down the table. The fries and sauce were DELISH and we ordered another round of yummy cocktails. Our waitress, while clearing old glasses inadvertently knocked over one of the cocktails and the fries sauce, she quickly cleaned up the mess, fortunately the napkin I had put on the table to stop the drinks from falling off had absorbed the spilled drink. She brought out a fresh cocktail but forgot to replace the sauce for the fries. At this point we asked for the check. 
It was an out of the ordinary visit, and I'll definitely be back when mercury is out of retrograde to enjoy a burger and more of those delicious cocktails!

Another lovely evening at the awesome Friday Saturday Sunday! Went tonight with some friends and enjoyed my favorite cocktail Control State! Had the pleasure of meeting the owner Hannah tonight too, charming lady! Will be back soon!

"DO NOT DRINK THE LIQUID NITROGEN AT THE BOTTOM OF THE MUG OR YOU WILL DIE" Says the card they make you read when you order Dragon Breath. Gulp!!!! Of course I wonder if it's legal to be serving it as they do; puff cereal in a mug doused with liquid nitrogen that sits as liquid at the bottom of the mug. They give you long wooden spears to stab the puff cereal. It was a cool experience to have the cereal coated liquid nitrogen smoke out of your mouth, it was a big hit with the kids, and there was lots of snap chatting. They also had a kitchen aide mixer at the front desk making liquid nitrogen ice cream with smoke flowing out of the bowl, like a potion. They've got their finger on the pulse of the food trends, and this cleverly sets them apart from their big rival Franklin Fountain a few blocks down. The shop is cute with a video game machine and big Market front windows. Check it out!

Embarrassed to say I've walked by this restaurant numerous times and had no idea it was there. It wasn't until a recent Philadelphia magazine article about the owner couple George & Jennifer Sabatino divorcing that I discovered it. Also, Craig Laban gave it a very good review! George is the chef and he is leaving soon to begin a new venture. 
At the busy corner of 19th and Chestnut, diagonal from CVS and above Snap Kitchen there is a low-key brown door that leads you to the second floor restaurant. 
Aldine has a lovely interior, with dark wood, tin ceiling and giant windows. Waiters are all in black and very attentive. The bartenders are both bearded mixing away under 3 giant hand blown pendant lights. There is a modern antique feeling in the restaurant with special details like vintage lightbulbs that show the wires.
Bummer that Target opened across the street, we had a view of people shopping on the second floor at 9pm! A shame for Aldine that Target moved in, it detracts from their lovely atmosphere. Aldine may want to consider some type of blind for their Chestnut facing windows.
We were four for dinner last night, during restaurant week. The three appetizer choices were: beet salad, chicken liver mouse, and cauliflower soup. The mains were: butternut squash pasta, skate, and beef. Dessert options were ginger panacotta and chocolate cake. 
Everything was delicious, my favorite was the skate!! Wow it was delish and beautifully plaited, garnished with watermelon radish and mustard seeds every bite was bursting with flavor! I will come back for that skate, amazing!!

Love the interior hardware store look of Honey's with vintage hanging paint signs, shovels displayed on the wall as if they were in a Tractor Supply store, and vintage electrical car tools under the glass on the tables you eat on. It makes for great conversation and a fun vibe. Perfect brunch for posh urban farmers.
We've eaten here a bunch of times, with family, and friends, big groups and small. The food is always great! My personal faves are the eggs Benedict, and the huevos rancheros. The plates are abundant, and always leave you content.
The service is excellent too, we have always had very attentive waiters and waitresses. The host is great too, calm and patiently attending to the brunch peeps on the long wait list and anxious hoverers. 
We will have to try their other location in Northern Liberties next!

Life changing inventions: the wheel, the telephone, the steam engine, television, the lightbulb, and of course.... the chocolate chip cookie sandwich pop (with a vanilla sprinkle center) from the Lil' Pop Shop! 
Lil' Pop Shop has a great Rittenhouse location with a hip wallpapered and sizable indoor seating area. The pop flavors are unique and refreshing, they use cane sugar and natural flavors, and source as many ingredients as possible locally. 
At this point, nearing the end of the summer, we have tried just about all of the summer menu flavors: Vietnamese coffee, raspberry lime, green tea with mochi , chocolate with salted caramel brownie, garden mint chocolate, coconut hibiscus.. 
I am still dreaming their new genius invention, the ice cream sandwich pop! They only had one ice cream sandwich pop left when I went last night (I had tried to order it last week but they were sold out), I watched it like a hawk as we waited in line, and was sending telepathy waves out to all around me not to order it because it was reserved for ME! Finally at the glass counter I strategically placed my order before the rest of my family, there were cries of unfairness from my children who when they saw it immediately wanted it. Repressing my maternal pangs I stood my ground and they were forced to chose a pop from the standard menu. 
It was as good as I had expected, and I was glad I had fought for it. I savored every bite, occasionally closing my eyes after bites to create jealousy from the rest of the fam. Half way through my pop a wave of sorrow overcame me that my little chicklets were not able to enjoy this new delicacy, so I caved and very generously gave them all a bite. And the Mom of the year award goes to...

A little bit of Paris in Rittenhouse Square. I have eaten at Parc so many times I can't count! Today it was a snow day (weekday) lunch with the family. I have been numerous times for breakfast, coffee and croissants, eggs.. many lunches with friends, my fave is the French onion soup and salad lyonnaise. Although other lunches I've loved have been the croque madame and salad nisoise..and my son loves the mac and cheese. The bread basket is the best in town and we fight over the baguette slices. I also regularly buy baguettes from the front desk for $3, (at least every other week) great with dinner at home. The cheese boards are always yum, although no matter the restaurant they often have cheddar which I always request to switch out, because ... come on!!!! We've had Christmas Eve dinner at Parc a few times too, and other dinners too. Steak is a fave, and the burgers too. Oh, and the fries! You must order the fries!!! And they know to bring it with mayo!!! Only one dining experience I had a Parc did I have to ask the waiter to take my plate back to the kitchen, it was a tough chewy steak, they redid it and it came out late after everyone had finished their meal, so they didn't charge me. Hey, it happens. The pot de creme was my fave dessert from 5 years ago, they took it off the menu and I've been in mourning ever since. Parc is Steven Star's faux Parisian brasserie recreation, which takes me back to my childhood living in Paris where we lived in an apartment above a very similar looking brasserie called Le Scossa, where I had chocolate mousse (like Parc's pot de creme) whenever I was allowed! Definitely try Parc, it's the closest you'll come to Paris while in Philly!

2 days after my earlier review, Erik The manager reached out via private message on Yelp to refund $34 (the difference between the $59 reservation charge, and the $25 walk in charge), which he promptly refunded today. Glad to see management is so responsive, and we look forward to visiting again soon. I've upgraded to 4 stars, for attentiveness to address the situation and good customer service.

Mustaches + souvlaki = Moustaki ! Cute well designed graphic logo and fun modern interior with blue metal chairs and rustic wood table tops. Just a few steps from The Franklin Institute, it was the perfect spot to have lunch after visiting the Terra-cotta Warriors exhibit. Moustaki is a new restaurant that opened in the last few months, use to be a pizza joint. They decided to keep pizza on the menu for customers who will miss the old pizza place, ha. Great classic Greek menu, authentic gyro sandwiches with French fries wrapped inside. Friendly staff, unfortunately not in my residential neighborhood, but will definitely be back after my next Franklin Institute show!

Gem of Philly, a must for locals AND tourists! Filled with local produce, Amish farmers/Pennsylvania Dutch, freshly baked goods, hand churned ice creams, a small chocolate and candy factory showing their mold making techniques, artisan cheeses, fresh fish & meat, book vendors, spice shops, and soooooooo much more. Two of the merchants are even descendants of original vendors from the 1800's, how cool is that??!! Reading Terminal is great for grocery shopping, and lunch.. although it does get quite overwhelming with crowds at lunch. During the holidays they have a giant train display complete with tracks and train cars whistling and zooming around, RT also has lots of festivals and fun events for both adults and kids. I'm not going to list my fave food and market vendors because I love so much that is here and they would all be on the list. An awesome market, highly recommend!! Ah yes, I can't forget to tell you about Philbert! Philbert is the lovely 3' plump bronze piggy bank sculpture in the center of the terminal, he collects coins for charity. Eric Berg is a VERY special local Philadelphia sculptor, whose work is all over the city in major parks, the bear in Fitler Square, the dragon at Drexel, the vine covered cottage gate in Rittenhouse square, the sphere at Pennsylvania hospital and so much more. Reading Terminal is a gem, go!

So I decide to go for Happy Hour and check out the new place, it's around 3 PM on a Wednesday and I go to the open air bar on the top floor, very nice. I'm shocked to find beer being offered for $2.-!  As I relax I notice there are no less than 9 service people milling about and a total of 7 customers.
Anyway I ask for a wine by the glass list, the bartender leaves to get it and never returns, odd. Another bartender brings me the list and says I should check out the restaurant bar on the street level that also offers a happy hour but is completely different. Intrigued, I head downstairs and sit at the bar, a young bartender greets me and says "I guess your part of this private party?" I say No I am here for Happy Hour to which he promptly replies: "This is a private party  so you need to leave."
That's a nice first impression don't you think?

The Santa Barbara farmers market on Saturday is one of my all time favorites!  The fresh sea air mixed with the smell of flowers and produce is simply intoxicating!  Every time I visit this market, I want to move to Santa Barbara just to be close enough to shop here every weekend!  

I have been coming to this farmer's market for over 25 years.  It's my happy place and escape from the stressful city life.  The produce and flowers at this market is super fresh and often better and more unique than other farmer markets in LA because many of the growers are nearby.  

I typically walk up and down each aisle at least 2 to 3 times to scope out prices, quality, and to make sure I'm not missing anything.  The vibe here is very relaxed and very family friendly. 

Some of my favorite things to buy here include olive oil, whatever fruit or vegetable is in season, and ver jus.  It's easy to go overboard here!  

Parking is never an issue because there's lots of street parking and a public lot nearby.

Stopped in here before our concert down the block. We were able to find seating at the bar. They had the movie Jaws playing in the background. I was really excited to watch a movie while eating a huge pretzel. Prices are really good. They seem like they're known for their old fashions since I saw the bartender make like ten while sitting there. 

I would call this place a little hipster-ish. It reminds me of a couple of bars in Astoria, NY that I've been to.   I love a good place with outdoor seating. Overall I would probably come back here to watch the game (which I don't really end up watching, my husband does). The person next to us ordered wings... I didn't think they looked very appetizing, I might be up for trying them though.

Wheewww I wasn't expecting the Spicy Garlic to be spicy. So many places call things " spicy" it turns out they only added a little paprika. Not this place... the Spicy Garlic is actually spicy. It could use a little more cheese though. I wasn't expecting it to be pretty much cheese-less.
