The Radicchio is really good. I love mushrooms and balsamic vinaigrette so this is perfect for me. It's bursting with flavor. I'm not entirely sure what I was eating.. I just keep shoveling it in my mouth. 

I love their crust. It's that coal oven texture and taste but the end of the crust is fluffy. Nice touch. 

Decently priced for what you get. I've only tried their food truck location. Apparently you can call ahead of time and they will get your pizza ready for you. All you have to do is pay and pick it up from their truck. 

I don't think I have ever seen a pizza food truck before.
I was very intrigued. Customer service was great.

Great lunch special 3 rolls and a soup or salad for around $17. You can't beat that. 
I ordered through Grubhub. My food arrived fresh, well packaged and was not missing any items. 
I was really impressed by the spicy salmon roll and spicy tuna. 
Normally, when I order spicy sushi it isn't that spicy or flavorful. I was surprised to find both rolls had a nice kick to them.

Went here for dinner on a Monday night. The kitchen was open until midnight. Ordered the wings (extra spicy) and jalapeño poppers. The poppers were a little on the cold side, I'm not sure why or how.  

The wings were once again, amazing. The extra spicy is very very very hot, which was kinda refreshing. I struggle to find a place that serves extra hot wings. 

Great service at the bar.

I took my daughter and husband here after we went ice skating.

It was 11pm on a Thursday. We waited about 10 minutes to be seated at the counter. 

What an experience. I'm so glad that we were able to grab 3 seats and enjoy our cheesesteak and cheeseburger. 

I'm convinced they gave my husband the wrong steak last time or my husband just ordered it wrong. (See my last review) 

I ordered the same thing I told him to order last time and I got a totally different product. Everything blended together perfectly. I'm so happy that I gave this place a second chance. 

Their cheeseburgers are amazing. They're huge and decently priced. 

Our waitress was super friendly and quick. We ordered a cheesesteak, cheeseburger, carrot cake and cheesecake. The desserts are a must. My husband hates carrot cake but loved their carrot cake. 

If you want to try this place out, go later at night. You'll be able to grab a beer, food and sit without all the people behind you.

No, just no. I don't know why I keep giving Iron Hill a chance. We ordered the Fish & Chips and Cheesesteak Egg rolls. 

For starters, I had to send the fish & chips back, they drowned the plate in salt. I was literally chewing on rock salt. The portion looked like something you would give a child.  $19 for two fish sticks, overcooked fries and enough salt to medically raise your blood pressure. 

Cheesesteak Egg rolls were mediocre, flavorless and cold.

1st popcorn was drenched in their coconut oil. When I say drenched.. I mean the middle of my bucket was soaking wet. I can't have butter because I get severely ill. Originally I thought they added butter even though I said at least 3x no butter. Management apologized and reassured me that this was just their coconut oil and that it sometimes spills over. He went to get me a new bucket, then he came back to inform me that the oil did spill over into the bin. Who knows? The situation was solved, back to my movie. 

Fast forward 35 minutes later... my husband goes... there is HAIR in the popcorn!?!! I didn't hear him at first...so he grabs my hand and puts the hair on my hand. FML this hair was just in his mouth and now it's stuck to my hand. 

So I go back out a second time to speak with someone. Now I'm laughing, I'm so mad that I'm laughing. I've missed major plot points in my movie and now I have this plastic looking black hair greased onto my hand  

The manager did not have black hair. Remember he was the one who got me a new bucket?!? Soooo the hair was actually in the popcorn bin. I have blonde hair and my husband does have black hair.. but this wasn't his black hair...this was double the length and it looked like wig hair. The manager stated that they were going to dump the entire bin of popcorn and clean it out. 

All I asked for was my popcorn to be taken off of my bill. They also gave me two movie passes. Thanks, but no thanks. I'm a AMC stub member. I don't need their passes. 

This was a huge waste of our time. We only came here because AMC wasn't playing the movie at a time we could attend. 

Now.. for the actual movie theater. The screen is lovely, it's huge, great quality. The seats recline pretty far back. The tables seemed cleaned. The bathrooms were a mess. 

We actually were the last people to get our food out of the entire theater. I had to ask someone else to get it for us. All we ordered was popcorn. Here is everyone around me getting their cooked food and still no popcorn. 

Also, they left the top light on above us. I was told that it would go off after they were done serving everyone. It didn't. 

Overall, Management was very friendly and I appreciate their honest effort to try and make things right.While leaving we were handed 4 more passes so 6 total. I gave them all away, this just isn't the place for us.

My husband and I went here for restaurant week. I really enjoyed their preset menu and the array of choices they had to offer. We each order the $35 four course dinner. The only compliant I had for the night was the dessert. The ice cream was frozen and then it must have been melted to only be frozen again. So in other words... it had freezer burn on it. 

The typical menu is pretty pricey for the amount you actually receive. I almost fell off my chair when I saw the persons vindaloo next to me. $22 for a personal sized dish? Maybe it's just me, or the fact that my husband is south Asian... but this is highest vindaloo dish I have ever seen. I dine out in NYC frequently and I have never seen it priced this high. 

Anyways, service was amazing. Everyone worked together.. my table was constantly cleaned and each course was packed away neatly in a bag.

I do wish the dishes brought a little more heat. I asked for extra spicy (knowing that they would maybe add a couple of chili flakes.. based on the other reviews). When my food came out, my server asked if I would like hot sauce? Once again, I almost fell over. I have never had an Indian place ask if I wanted hot sauce with my dish. It's normally the exact opposite. 

Overall, this place is for people who want to try Indian flavors without actually trying the real dishes. Bring your friends or colleagues for a fancy dinner with amazing service. 

I wouldn't bring my in-laws here. They would be very confused.

Stopped in and grabbed a homemade cheese burger and fries
Awesome burger and fries done perfect.
Real ground beef Patty,not the frozen crap others use
Mr Lee is very nice and the service was quick and excellent.
Will be back again to try the other dishes!

The food is pretty good here, but the profanity-laced shouting experience I had here tonight was embarrassing and should never be tolerated at any dining establishment.

I guess I came in about 20 minutes before close and they were getting in produce for tomorrow. Literally as soon as I walked in the woman working behind the assembly line had a meltdown, cursing at the delivery boy whose boxers and underwear I could clearly see because he wasn't wearing a belt.

I ordered my food, and that much went alright, until I asked for regular tzatziki on my bowl and then asked for spicy tzatziki on the side. The same woman who was cursing at the delivery boy told me she was just going to put both sauces on the side, which wasn't what I asked. So I just got the regular tzatziki. 

I paid for my food and sat down to eat, and the shouting and cursing continued. I was the only person in the restaurant at this point, which all of these people recognized. 

Three of the workers here apologized for their language and then carried on shouting and cursing about the produce. 

I left before even finishing my food because I was so appalled. Save the drama for when the doors are closed and you don't have customers coming into your restaurant. And put a belt on so I don't have to see your underwear.

It was just trashy, honestly, and signified a severe lack of respect for customers. If you're having a bad day, I get it. We all have our setbacks and personal issues. I'm not immune to that. I actually came here BECAUSE I was having a bad day and just wanted a nice casual meal. And then I had this experience.

I'm only getting to go from now on.

I have been to the Rollin' Oats in Tampa and always really liked the selection but never made my way over to the St. Pete location.

I love this location much more than the Tampa one. It's cleaner, a little bit smaller, and the people are much friendlier. The selection is basically the same, but the layout here seems a little bit more organized than the Tampa location. There's also a yoga studio above the market which is awesome.

This is the place to go if you are looking for natural items and organic foods. Even their prepared items are delicious looking and you'll find a ton of gluten-free and grain free items here. 

I'll be back for sure!

Yesterday I surveyed my Facebook and asked my friends if Trader Joe's lived up to the hype. I had quite a few people comment and all of them said yes, so I stopped in after hitting the gym. 

I was pretty excited to come here after hearing so many good things. The store itself is small and there are not a lot of parking spaces, but considering the intense rain and the early hour I went, I easily found a spot. 

An employee gave me a cart and into my first Trader Joe's I went. The first thing I saw were the beautiful flowers and WOW they were also beautiful, inexpensive flowers! I did not get any this go around but I love having flowers in my house so I will definitely buy some in the future. 

Next up was the produce section. All of the produce looked fresh and delicious. And again, CHEAP! Like, cheaper than Publix. And I really love Publix, but where else can you buy organic kale for $2? Nowhere, that's where. 

I was able to sample some of TJ's famous cookie butter and yes, it is as good as everyone says it is. The crunchy kind appealed to me more than the regular kind since I could taste the gingerbread in it. So I got a jar! My first jar of cookie butter. I feel warm and fuzzy inside just thinking of it. 

TJ's has a good frozen food section with a lot of Indian and Italian options. I did get some of the frozen Indian food and am excited to try it! 

Checkout was speedy and the service was friendly. I am really happy there's a Trader Joe's here. I think it might just be my new grocery store!

I find the rest of these reviews to be a little odd but I guess Ciccio's restaurant chain is more prominent in Tampa which is why people there know what to expect when they go to a CRG restaurant. 

Anyway, I like Fresh Kitchen. I liked it in Tampa, and I like it here, too. It seems like all the kinks the place had in Tampa seem to have been worked out in the St. Pete location, which means the portion sizes have been fixed and the food is still fresh. 

The concept is a "healthy" style bowl with greens, vegetables, meats and dressing/sauce. I usually get the kale salad with broccoli or cauliflower, but the rest of the vegetables that I've had have been pretty on point too. Sometimes they are not cooked thoroughly, however. 

The meat here is pretty solid. I especially like the chimichurri chicken since I don't recall that ever being on the menu at FK's Tampa location. The sauces are all great too. The coconut sriracha is always a winner. 

This place gets packed at lunchtime but the line moves quickly which is a relief. The employees here are always more than happy to give you a sample and have always been friendly when I have gone in. 

Prices are slightly higher than Chipotle or Moe's, but I think you're getting better quality food here. 

Parking is a total nightmare however and sometimes you will have to park in the neighborhood. That's really my huge complaint and the main deterrent from going to FK regularly.

New to Indianapoils by way of St. Louis.... The best bbq in Indy, Sugarfire Smokehouse. As a native of StL, I am excited to have them.  I've long thought the bbq scene in Indy was lacking great bbq.. that has now changed.  Not to mention some competition coming from up north soon (cannot remember the name of the place coming). 

Sugarfire has something for everyone.. brisket, pork, burgers, ribs, a ton of sides.  One of the better things... they have daily specials that bring a ton of variety.   

Couple things I noticed.. they do not have beer yet, but it said its coming soon.  Not sure if they will have liquor or not.  Once this place gets busy, expect to be waiting outside as there isn't much of a runway between the counter, line and door.  They also do not have traditional soda selections, coke, pepsi, etc.. they have some smaller brands.  I'm not a huge soda guy, a cola is a cola to me..  

Do your stomach a favor and swing by this place before it gets too busy and you have to wait.

The brisket, moist, is the way to go.  It had a bit of crust on it, just enough fat and amazing taste.  Some of the better brisket I've had, especially around Indy.  They had bacon wrapped bacon as a special.. pretty good but too much for me with the brisket I already had.  Will be back as I have time!

I may not be a coffee drinker, but I damn sure know a good coffee house when I see one. The first good sign is that the place doesn't really care if you enter it or pass it by. But when you do enter the unassuming door, you feel like they are happy that you've arrived. The next good sign is that it smells so good, even a tea drinker is tempted to get a cup. The third sign is that the decor and music is not too quirky, but instead hits that sweet spot of just weird enough. 

HG has all of this and more. I was nearby and had 45 minutes to kill and Yelp pointed me here. The front door was barely noticeable as a business, but once inside the cool and somewhat dimly lit room I knew I was in the right place. My perfect iced tea hit the spot, and as I took a vintage chair and admired the artwork all around me, I felt quite comfortable. It did not hurt that one of my favorite Talking Heads songs was playing in the background.

The barista on duty was very friendly and the food at the counter looked appetizing, they also make a few items to order. A Yelp checkin here gets you $1 off the baked goods. Do you really need to go to another Starbucks; probably not. Come here instead

It took waaay too long for me to finally visit this creamery. I didn't get to their short lived Princeton location in time. I was steps away from this location twice in the past few years, once just a few months ago. But on those occasions I had just finished large meals. I almost tried the Lahaska location yesterday, but when we entered the case was depleted to about 9 flavors. I called up this one and was assured a better selection. 

Matt was the server on duty and was only too willing to provide samples to aid in our selection. That may have only added to my indecision. It took some intense deliberation choosing between the pistachio and salted caramel. But I'm confident that the pistachio will be a part of my next visit. 

The caramel may have been the best example of that flavor I've encountered. Although there was no vein of it, the dark color suggested it was deeply infused into it( and it was, with bits of crunchy caramel too) but the big surprise was the milk chocolate, in spite of its name and lighter color, this was a dark tasting version with little bits of undissolved chocolate. Both were very creamy and NOT overly sugared. For the area I think it was a good portion to price. The shop is very cute too, a few seating areas inside and some outside  as well. The only drawback I can see is the metered parking, there are spots very close to the business, but those will likely be filled on weekends. My next visit will include a waffle, if I can manage to not overeat prior.

Trish found a Groupon for this place so we decided to give it a try. Located in a small strip mall, the interior was average and clean with about 15 or so tables. Fusion restaurants are kind of a gamble, with trying to cook several types of cuisine, inevitably some come out better than others. This was in fact our experience here as well. 

Our specialty roll( can't recall name) was very good, it was a pimped out  shrimp tempura but with avo and spicy tuna added to the top. In hindsight we should have just stuck with sushi. But Trish craved Udon, and I some Mu Shu. We both selected chicken as the protein and both regretted it. While the rest of our dishes were average, the meat was below that. Funky texture and taste and detracted from the overall taste. I like my Mu Shu with pepper oil, and this one was excellent, pancakes however were a bit stale and did not roll very well. 

Our servers were friendly and funny, and for the savings( $15 for $30 worth of food) we might return for an all sushi feast.

I thought I had reviewed Enzo's after my previous visit which was near the holidays. I even kind of remembered the words I used, and the overall rating. But I was mistaken and my memory lapses might be something to keep an eye on. Last night's experience further strengthened my opinion that this is 4 star dining, with prices to match unfortunately. 

This recent meal was possibly my 5th here and might have been the best. I took advantage of a Friday night Lenten menu that gives the diner app, salad and entree courses for $30. A few apps sounded good but I had to try the Dijon mussels, great bivalves, small but tender and sweet. The sauce was white wine and light mustard and even had some crisp broccoli in it. Very good. Caesar salad was fresh but standard. My odd choice of fish and chips in an Italian joint proved to be a great one. This lightly breaded haddock in a mild beer batter was probably the best I've had in many years. The house made chips were ok, they would have benefited from a light salting as they exited the fryer. My aunt almost always orders the tagliatelle with chicken and figs. She loved it. On our last trip I had incredible braciola and an earlier one featured a great seafood pizza. So good that I want to try other pies here but haven't gotten around to it.

Service is very good and on our most recent visits we had a great waiter. Both times his recommendations were perfect. If I had one gripe it would do with prices.  A haddock special from last nights menu was priced at $32, my great braciola was in this range too. This is not an expensive fish, nor cut of beef. Both should have been at least $5 less in my opinion. This is not enough to detract me from coming, but I try to avoid the costlier dishes. Yelp checkin offer of 10% off is much appreciated.

With 2 visits in 2 days it's safe to say that I'm a fan. And the second and Saturday night trip was more like 5 stars with great company, great food and a cool duo named Mama juice box performing to a half full house. Truth be told they made this night with diverse song selection and quirky but soulful arrangements of said selections. 

Sampled on our first trip was the local sour( Manayunk backflip) the creole cabbage soup and fried chicken sandwich. The sandwich was good, perfectly fried breast with chorizo sauce slathered on it. It was messy, after hoisting it once or twice I resorted to utensils, the chorizo sauce was amazing, I was picturing other things it could be used on too. 

For the second visit we went with a grapefruit beer that was very good, hummus plate and steak sandwich. The house made hummus was incredible, served with cuke, olives, feta, tomato, roasted red pepper and pita wedges. The steak sandwich was very good too, nice crispy roll and onions, and served with a beer cheese sauce( on the side for me) I'll get this again for sure, probably on our next time there. 

There is just a really chill vibe here, small and long building, blackboard sighs advertising specials, tap choices and upcoming events. A very nice abs dog friendly outside area. Lastly the staff has been super nice too. I can see why locals love this place; we'll likely be regulars too.

We finally made it back after our first visit more than 2 years ago which was dessert only. On that trip we ate outside due to a live performance happening and the fact that to eat inside we'd have to order off of a very specific menu. It was late summer and evening, so sweets in the fresh night air was a perfect choice. From that first time on we had been trying to get back for a proper meal. This past weekend our schedules aligned and we went to celebrate T's bday. 

The decor is very cute, with many antiques and ornate tin ceiling. But to be honest, the 2 seater tables which happen to ALL be the old fashioned pedal sewing machines are not comfortable for patrons with long legs and torsos. We were first seated near the center of the room, and without pushing my chair far away and into traffic I could find no way to get either leg under it. I asked to be moved but it was the same type of table,  due to a different chair and location I was able to place my extremities on the outside and straddled it the whole time I was there. 

We studied the online menu but still had a hard time deciding among all of the options. Trish went for the risotto of the day( wild mushroom) and I ordered the gnocchi dish. To share we selected their spinach salad and from the tapas menu the tortilla espanol.  First came an excellent olive and herb bread along with olive tapenade to spread on it. Normally I'm not a fan of either but the spread was more pesto tasting than olivey. The bread was phenomenal, no bitter taste and very dense. The tapas dish was comparable to a potato quiche, served with a tasty pepper aioli, even T, who is not a potato fan enjoyed it. Our salads were thick neatly stacked rounds of fresh spinach that were topped with Asian pear slices and goat cheese and spiced pecans and very little dressing. Both portions were of a nice size that caused me to wonder if this was 2 salads( happily it was not) The risotto was perfectly cooked and flavored with large mushroom pieces and a drizzle of truffle oil, very good. And the gnocchi dish was just as good if not better, tender slices of chicken in a mild Gorgonzola sauce with cherry toms and spinach mixed in. We agreed that we would order either or both again. 

We skipped dessert this time because they were out of the peanut butter pie, but I regret that now and should have ordered one of the crepe cakes. Dessert really is a must here.

Based on food and decor alone this review would be verging on 5 stars, but service was a bit spotty. We were asked for our order a few minutes after being seated( at second table) and needed a bit more time to decide. We were ready a few minutes later but our server took many more than that to return. They were not short staffed, in fact there must have been at least 5 employees working the front of house. At the end of our meal our check was wrong too, we were probably given one from a different table. It seemed to take another several minutes to correct this. Lastly, and I feel old saying this.... but when I'm in a " better" restaurant with an attractive female, I do NOT think it is good service to be addressed as guys. This happened several times and by most of the staff. If I'm at a bar with a buddy it's ok, on a romantic dinner date it is not.

Overall we were pleased with our meals and with the ambiance that the owners created in this restaurant. Much thought went into all of it and the food coming out was nicely done too. We are planning on returning, but it would be nice to see the service match the food and setting. 4.2 who knew I liked olive bread and tapenade Yelps

My first visit to this brewery/ restaurant and I'm close to being a fan. We were here to celebrate a friend's birthday and it seemed like all 12 or so of us were satisfied with our food and experience. 

It is a large and open space, both dining room and bar area, with some outside seating available as well. If I were to revisit( a good chance I will) I'd probably opt for bar area, especially during happy hour since those specials are not offered in dining room. Trish made the reservation for our group and ran into one glitch, the day of the event our 5:30 was changed to 5:00 by the restaurant. This was supposedly to accommodate another party at 7. We were not rushed out when that time approached but we also saw no sign of another party. 

I first perused the beer offerings, there seemed to be at least 10 on draught and some earlier offerings in cans. I selected their blueberry Hefeweizen and enjoyed the crisp flavor on this warm night, even though little to no berry taste came through. I would probably try something else next time. The food menu was possibly too large( in my opinion) with sandwich, pizza, apps and entrees offered. I was very hungry and 75% of the menu appealed to me, so I went to our excellent server Frank for his advice. He suggested a few dishes and I thought my beer choice would pair nicely with the pan roasted chicken entree. It proved to be good advice, a nicely cooked Frenched breast with the skin crispified served with what seemed to be local asparagus and mashed potatoes. The fowl was tender and juicy still, the pan sauce was lightly citrusy and herbed, it was good but could have been better if reduced and thickened. The mashed were ok, and probably the weakest link in the dish. I had an add on Caesar salad that was fair and overpriced( as add ons go) at $6. Trish went with his advice and ordered a shrimp and scallops special, she loved it and I have to admit, they are sourcing quality crustaceans.

Most others in our group ordered burgers and we heard many good things. Surprisingly no one else tried any beer. We brought our own bday cake and were not charged a plating fee. Beer aficionados should consider joining their reward program, for a $15 one time fee you are entitled to a special glass that holds 22 oz for the price of a pint, along with other perks and incentives. Great place for gatherings, let's go with 3.75 ongoing research Yelps

Can you still be a fan when there is little desire to return to said business? That is the question I was wrestling with when thinking about this review. In the end I decided that yes you can. 

Things started out poorly when we had to wait 20 minutes past our reservation time to be seated. But we were ushered to a nice window table and the vibe in the restaurant was uplifting. We liked the decor, kind of rustic Italian, dark unfinished wood with photos of Gumbas. We were greeted immediately by our server Andrew who fit the role perfectly with his Italian accent.

The menu is primarily old school dishes, your parms, vodka sauces etc. I was torn between the night's special pork Osso Bucco and the Italian gravy. In the end I choose the later to sample the various meats. The spareribs were good but messy to deal with, sausage was ok, brasciole was very good, and the meatball may have been the best I've had in a restaurant. The red sauce was very thick and flavorful and the rigatoni went nicely with the dish, though with a bit more pasta I might have taken w doggie bag home. Trish ordered a seafood in vodka sauce dish, I tasted it and thought it was pretty good, and it seemed to have a nice amount of shellfish in it. Salads came with the meal and were better than average, bread was nothing special but worked to sop up sauces.

Just like the dishes, the clientele is primarily old school as well. At one point I think we were among the youngest diners. Glancing across the street we saw the young hipsters lining up for another Italian joint, but no lines here when we exited. With several other nearby options for this type of cuisine, and my current favorite being one of them, I can't see us coming back soon. But if your parents or grandparents want a nice BYOB spot with slightly overpriced familiar favorites I think they would be fans. 4 the meatball earned that fourth star Yelps

I'm pretty fortunate to live super close to a business that has been doing what Han is doing here and at his other 7(?) locations, but they toil in a bit of obscurity. They keep the menu more traditional, and offer many more dishes. At Han I get the feeling that everything has been distilled down and polished, which is not necessarily a bad thing.

With the glowing reviews we did not know what to expect on a Saturday afternoon visit. This must not be a busy time for them, only one third of the tables were seated. From all indications those folks were enjoying the food. The manager came over and explained the menu, we probably would have deciphered it anyway. He seemed eager to make a good impression as did our server Alex who was very good throughout.

We knew enough to order the DanDan noodles, and agree with all who have cited it as a must have. And a pretty low cost too. They lowered the heat so Trish could share it, while providing me with chili oil to spice my serving back up. Fried dumplings were very good, but I would consider going without next time to try something else. Our shared entree of 3 cup chicken was ok. This is perhaps the menu's least spicy offering, but maybe a choice for the less adventurous. If you are not a fan of dark meat chicken this dish may not be your thing either, it is served in a mellow soy, garlic, ginger, basil and 5 spice sauce.

We agreed another visit is on the horizon, although I wonder if a different location might reveal more depth. As it is, this one is  convenient for us, so we'll return. Here's looking forward to my next taste of those noodles.

Oh Trenton, even though you are the state capital, you are tiny as far as cities go. But you are certainly broadening your food frontiers. Now along with great Asian and Latino choices, not to mention Eastern European, you can boast a very interesting Trinidadian spot. But in the interest of accuracy, the place is technically situated in Hamilton. In recent years the boundary between the 2 localities has been somewhat blurred I will admit.

Thanks to a review by intrepid Yelper Gerald S., this place was on my to do list. A desire for something completely different steered me here finally. Upon entering I was enchanted by the aromas. All chefs were busy in the kitchen so I was not pressured into making a rush decision. I decided on a double, the boneless chicken roti, and a dessert in the small case intrigued me. The owner says it is called cassava bone, and looks a bit like pumpkin pie( it contains cassava, coconut and a small amount of pumpkin)

The roti was tasty and very filling, I was pondering that this is a perfect chilly weather meal, esp for a meat n taters type of hunger. The seasoning was interesting and I did like the roti part of it too, and found that the powdered chick peas in between the layers to be a tasty if somewhat messy treat. The double was even better, I would considering buying several and freezing to use as a side dish or snack. The dessert was pumpkin pie-esque, but with hints of coconut. I imagined how good it would be with a nice scoop of vanilla ice cream or whipped cream, sadly, I had neither

Roy, the owner is very friendly, and very confident in his food. He was sure that I would come back again, and I think he is right. Even though the menu is small, there were still several items I was curious about. I'm thrilled to have been able to sample such an exotic cuisine only a few miles from my house, 4 hot Yelps.

Mikonos is probably the grandfather of all the newer Greek restaurants that have been sprouting up as of late. I was aware of them, but have no good excuse as to why it took me so long to visit. I'm glad we picked this for a late lunch date, and we both agreed it's worth revisiting. 

We started with the grilled octopus, it was served in a light and lemony vinaigrette with slivered red onions and a few greens tossed in. The octopod was tender and tasty, and really big enough for 4 to share. My dining companion chose the mixed gyro platter and she thoroughly enjoyed. I veered away from my usual kebab or gyro choices and went all in with the pastichio, my first time ever trying this. I was happy I did, although similar in form and structure of lasagna, this was very different and very good. I would order this again for sure. The lemon potatoes that everyone raves about were good, but I'm not sure worthy of a cult following. The chopped Greek salad that came on the plate was fresh and a nice contrast to the creamy and rich pasta dish. Not wanting the great experience to end we shared the "G" dessert and my companion also had the Greek coffee, which was so strong it could be said that it would curl your toes. The dessert was very good, filo dough encasing the custard and a light syrup drizzled on it. A great ending to a great lunch. 

As another reviewer noted, this location appears to have been a standalone fast food place, but once inside much care was given to make it their own and with a Greek flair. Our server was friendly but gave us plenty of time and space which was appreciated. I'm looking forward to my next visit already.

This may upset some old time Bordentown locals, but I was never a fan of the Farnsworth house. I like OTP more, and it suits the town better as well. It took me awhile to finally visit but I know I'll be back. 

I came with a friend who lives in town and has be telling me good things about it. Several items looked good on the menu, but I was trying to eat a bit healthier today so I went with a wedge salad and the mahi tacos. The tap list held about 25 options, and their mixed drinks are good here as well. I found a cider to try and enjoyed it. Our food came out very quickly, salads and mains together. But that was not a problem. I liked my wedge, I crave this salad about once every 2-3 years, this one satisfied that craving. The tacos were good too, blackened fish but not over cooked, or over dressed in the flour tortillas. It came with very good thin sliced but long fries, I've never seen this style but I like them a lot. My friend had the grilled cheese with brisket, that looked great too. I'll probably try a more bar food item when I return, perhaps a burger. With indoor and outdoor seating options and a good bar, I think this is my first choice for casual dining in Btown, and the menu does provide more than just standard bar bites. I'll be back.....

Gift certificate 4 stars

After mulling this one over for several days I felt my lone experience here was worthy of the fourth. Helping the rating was the perfect Sunday that we chose to visit, weather and otherwise. And I'm definitely a fan of the building, decor and location right on the canal. Inside rustic would be a good descriptor with many exposed beams and brick walls, and an open kitchen smack in the middle of the main dining room. The outdoor patio along the tow path was a perfect spot to enjoy a weekend lunch, and certainly affected the food in a positive way. 

We started with an excellent and slightly different take on a Caesar salad, the goat cheese added a creaminess and cut down on the sharpness of the Italian cheese, we'd definitely order again since it was a good portion to share. Trish went for their quiche( garden vegetable and cheese) of the day, a good choice and full of flavor with light and  fluffy eggs and a good crust. I had mahi tacos and while they were good would select something else if I returned. The fish was fine and cooked to a nice blackened turn and the pepper and mango salsa was equally good. The problem was with ratios, too little fish and too much salsa. The onion rings that came with it( odd I know) were excellent and would be better paired with something else. We both loved these. We finished with 2 desserts and the standout was definitely the chocolate peanut butter cake. The layers of cake were moist and dense and the icing layers just lightly sweetened. This was a shareable slice too, maybe for more than 2.

The reason I had to consider this for longer than it normally takes me is twofold. First and biggest are the prices here( literally) burgers for $20 and fish tacos close to that seems high to my budget. Second was the realization that this cuisine, for the most part, is easily reproduced in many home kitchens. But for folks on vacation or just splurging on a meal out( and this is an expensive town/ area) it might satisfy. Slightly rounding up to 4 individual results may vary Yelps.

Come here on a warm Black Friday and you will see how easy it is to be a fan, and also how many other fans this place has. It seemed as though many folks had the same idea this year, which is to avoid malls and big box stores to shop local or small at least. 

I heard about the holiday lights and had great memories of coming here as a child. So I took this opportunity to share it with Trish. We both were thrilled with all of the lights and sights. And by all indications the many people here did as well. Though to be honest, even with the crowds it was easy to browse in any stores that we wished to.

It is too easy to just say that this is a tourist trap. While that may be true it is still very cool. The buildings are all rustic and not cheesy at all( except for the cheese shop) There are shops to suit any personality. Are you a drinker? There's a wine tasting room and a local spirit tasting room( I want to go back for that one) Are you a bibliophile? A nice book store, and books to be found in other stores too. Have kids or are a kid at heart? A sweet toy store. Foodie? Several specialty food shops. I could go on, but probably don't need to.

We both enjoyed it so much, but due to time constraints had to forgo some areas. I know we will return again, and there is a good chance it will be soon to take in the lights before the season ends. This is a fun place for all
ages, and should be on your to do list if you've never been. 4 Lahaska Yelps

I've been waiting to try this place for several years. The closest I came was sampling their food at the last 3 Epicurean events held at GFS. We planned ahead on being nearby on Black Friday, so I called for a reservation days in advance. The only option left was to sit outside on their deck, with warm weather expected and the knowledge that they had heaters I went for it. 

We arrived on time and were informed we could sit inside due to a cancellation, but after walking out onto the skate we decided to dine open air. The interior would have been nice too, quirky and cute touched abounded. But there is something special about fresh air and food, and the heaters made it really cozy out there.

They offer 3 course menus which start at $28 on week nights and then $32 on weekends. Some of the options have a slight up charge, but there are still good choices if you want to stay at that price point. Trish selected sweet potato nachos and a seasonal gnocchi dish that contained spinach and pumpkin. The nachos were very good, definitely not your typical messy dish. Each component contributed to the whole, and a nice size even for sharing. The pasta was very good too, nice cheese sauce and perfect bite to the doughy pillows.

Our excellent waitress Meghan recommended the crab cake, I informed her that while I love me some CC's, I'm also a snob and hardly ever like them unless I am near the Chesapeake. She told me she is as well, ok I'll bite. I also ordered the baked Brie. Both of these had slight uncharged, $2 or $3 each. The cheese was very good, gooey and topped with cooked apple and pumpkin seeds. I was pleased with the large amount of toasted bread that came with it, 8 or more crunchy and seasoned slices and just the right amount to use up all the Brie. The crab cake was one of the best I've had in years( in this area) and to be honest may be the best I've tasted in the Pa area. It was topped with a delicious avocado and corn salsa and served on top of a tasty and bright carrot sauce. The mashed potatoes that came with it were fair but only slightly warm, and the seasonal veggies were grilled perfectly.

We shared our desserts, a perfectly executed and larger than average creme brûlée and a chèvre brownie that was divine. These desserts would be in the $10 range at other nearby spots. All items on the menu are available a la carte, but  get the 3 course. This restaurant has a very interesting origin story, and that was one of my original reasons for wanting to try it. I now think that the food tells its own story. As I was considering my review I knew it was at least 4.5 stars, but as I pondered the other options in this town, and the price to quality ratio of this BYOB, I knew I had to go to 5.

We were getting hangry for lunch but knew it had to be a light one based on dinner plans. Neither of us had been here but we were both curious after passing by many times. This seemed to fit our needs and was very close. 

We walked in on a Friday just about 1:30, not a large crowd but perhaps half full. A darkish and hardwood prolific ambiance, possibly even romantic. We both liked and hoped food would be as attractive. The prices are on the high side but many menu items sounded tasty. We agreed on a few and asked the waitress about a special, the chicken salad stuffed avocados. Based on her description we ordered that, a flatbread and the crab dip. 

The salad arrived first, this was a portion suitable for 3, 3 halved Avos stuffed to overflowing with very good chick salad, with fresh baby romaine leaves dressed up somewhat Caesar - ish. Very good and something we'd get again. Just as we were finishing both other dishes arrived, we would have preferred them to
Be spaced, but didn't specify. The margarita flatbread was ok, not as flat as some with herbed dough, fresh mozz and fair toms. The crab dip was excellent, real crab in a perfectly browned on top cheese sauce. The pita chips we very good as well. 

After such a nice lunch here we are planning on going back for dinner.  This seems like a good choice for special occasion, date night or a splurge. Oh, and the swanky framed TVs in the men's room turned to financial news was neato too.

I'm a sucker for this type of business. I love it when farmers and their families find ways to make their life easier and still hold onto the land. And places like this build great family memories too. Although based on other reviews the operation has scaled down somewhat, they also seem to be paving the way for other more adult experiences. 

We came for the ice cream but had to venture inside to see what was available here. With Apple season well underway they were showcasing a few varieties of local offerings, can't remember exact price but it was under $2 per lb and the fruit looked nice. They also had a good selection of other produce just over supermarket prices, still some local toms too. A decent cheese case with several DiBrunno Bros offerings among other things. A prepared foods case looked promising but our late evening visit was not the time to try anything. A brownie was agreed upon and it was pretty good. We skipped the gardening store if it was even still open. 

My biggest surprise was the bar. It was packed, but this was a Saturday and it is kind of small. Had I not had a few glasses of wine prior to arriving I would have ventured in farther to whet my whistle. Website research confirmed what I sensed, they only serve local beer and wine( see site for listing) Food can be brought in from store( yup, I'm thinking cheese and crackers or other snacks) but eventually they plan to do bar foods as well. 

I know I will return here, I hope it's for a festive event( Xmas lights or pumpkin activities) but even if it's just to enjoy an ice cream in a rustic environment, I will bask in the feeling that this simple act has been enjoyed and will be enjoyed by many others.

There's nothing wrong with pound cake, but I just can't get as excited over it as most reviewers of this place do. Maybe it's a Philly or S.Jersey thing, somewhat akin to this regions love of cutlets?

To date I've tried their chocolate frosted pound cake and a vanilla frosted birthday cake. The latter was decorated very nicely and guess what it was made with? If you said pound cake you are correct. Sadly though, the recipient of this cake is a chocoholic, and the purchaser inquired if it could be chocolate frosted, they were told that the bakery does not do that.

The pound cake itself is very good, but it is pound cake. I would prefer to use my dessert calories on something else. The frostings are also good, but not great. I would take a buttercream one of any flavor over their offerings. In the future I would like to try the butter cake, but I don't think that would sway my 3.5 Yelp opinion

At 1st glance the market seems like a mini fortress complete with a set of steel bars lining the door and windows. As I start to read the exterior signs on the building I see international food, Western union, Asian market, 24K jewelry, Thai and Lao café. Now I'm really intrigued and definitely got to check this place out.

When you walk in it looks like your typical Asian supermarket with aisles stocked with dry goods like ramen, snack chips, can goods and your typical Asian supermarket fare. As you walk towards the rear of the store to your right you will discover this little gem of a restaurant.

The menu has pictures which is always a good visual to give you an idea what your plate should look like. I was impressed with the menu and the many varieties they offered and was going to order more than two people could humanely eat, so it took a lot of inner chi, mental anguish and my buddy yelling at me to stand down.

We did order the following:
1. Paneng chicken wings as an appetizer, delicious savory thick curry that is "Finger licking good!" Sorry Colonel Sanders! :) my only gripe for this dish is the wing tips are left on. 
2. Deep fried pork intestines - I loved this dish, crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside, it may be a little funky for some people to try, but once you do, you'll be hooked! Just think of it as Asian calamari. 
3. Red curry with beef - Thick curry with beef, vegetables and basil that was sweet and delicious. I can taste the coconut milk and palm sugar. Good thing we ordered two big bowls of rice since we made sure every grain of rice soaked up all that curry yumminess!
4. We washed everything down with Thai ice tea and fresh coconut juice served in the shell itself.

King Market may be classified as a "Dive" by some people but the food is far from it. The portions are generous, the price is a steal for this type of cuisine and the service was spot on. The market may be called King, but the real King and Queen is the restaurant. I am all pumped and ready to go back next time I'm in town!

Not many chinese restaurants to choose from in the King of Prussia area offering legit Chinese food. This place is pretty good and located in a strip mall area made it convenient to find with ample parking.

When we 1st walked in 90% of the diners were Chinese which is a great sign! I figured the food should be pretty decent and with such a huge Chinese clientele.

We ordered the spicy garlic pork belly, Dan dan noodles, shitake mushrooms with Shanghainese bok choy, mixed seafood and meat platter, fish with pickled cabbage soup, fried tofu, brisket casserole and bowl of hot and sour soup. Everything was seasoned and cooked well. The use of peppercorns and spices were subtle without being too overwhelming in there spicy dishes.

The residents of King of Prussia should be ecstatic to have an Authentic Chinese restaurant among them offering the real deal szechuan cooking without charging you an arm and a leg for it.

NOTE: If you pay in cash they won't charge you tax. So keep that in mind especially if you have a big order and appetite that day.

I came here tonight with some girlfriends from my gym. The wait was quoted at 45 minutes, but they were able to seat us in a booth almost immediately. Super friendly from the beginning in terms of service. 

I got three different tacos and street corn with a mango White Claw. Let's discuss these tacos. The jerk chicken was great! There was another one that was hot chicken or something along those lines, and I'll be dreaming about that bad boy every night till I get another one. So good! Then I got some other one. I totally forgot what my third one was called. My friend had the burger taco and the breakfast taco. She seemed as impressed. 

But wait! There's more!

That street corn! It was SO GREAT! I spent like $31 on tacos and drinks. Oh! And also chips and salsa. Just for one person. It was completely worth it. The chips and salsa came with mango salsa, a spicy red salsa and another verde type salsa. They were fine. The real stars were the tacos and corn. My fiancé hates vegetables or I would bring him, but I'll have to figure out who I'm taking cause I need this place in my life!!!

Bold prediction: Pearl Diver won't last a year

...unless they make some swift adjustments. This island-themed, supposed retreat recently opened to much hype and anticipation. But based on my first visit and after reading other reviews, the post-launch buzz isn't looking good.

First, the location is a bit of a challenge. It's on Gallatin Road, about halfway between Five Points and Fox Club/Mickey's/Walden. It's sort of on its own. And parking is very limited.

Second, and certainly most memorably for me, the entry/waiting list/line (whatever it is) situation is just an absolutely confusing disaster of a poorly thought out procedure. We walked in to find a waiting room(?) with what appeared to be a line. We gathered that there was a bit of a wait to get in (which is not a foreign concept, so no beef there), but we didn't see a host stand or anyone who appeared to be managing entry. So, initially confusing. After a few minutes, we realized that the woman wearing the hip dark green romper was in charge of letting people in. After explaining that there was a bit of a wait because they want to make sure that everyone has a comfortable experience inside, she proceeded to let three people skip the line and enter because they were friends of the owner. So whatever make-believe, good-vibes policy they're touting was just killed for me right there. Eventually, three of us got inside and grabbed a big booth in the front room. 

Soon after, we noticed that two of our friends had arrived and were waiting in the waiting-for-the-sake-of-waiting line, and I walked up to let the host/bouncer/romper person know that the two guys we were joining us in our booth and asked if they could join us rather than having to wait and stare at us from the waiting room. As expected, the answer was no and that everyone has to wait until there's enough room inside -- even though the room wasn't that crowded and our friends were just going to be sitting down in the booth with us.

At this point, romper bouncer started to get a little mouthy and patronizing, to which I (*ahem* the customer) took exception. She explained that the policy wasn't pretentious and that it's designed to keep people happy. As an added bonus, she also explained that she's the least pretentious person because she lives in an airstream trailer (note: basically the most pretentious thing I've ever heard). After engaging in a bit of a back-and-forth, frustrated, I eventually walked back to the booth, and our friends were eventually allowed to join us. And I say it that way, because apparently as soon as I walked away from the door, bouncer romper told my friends that 1.) it'd be a bad idea for me to come back to the door again, and 2.) she'd still let them in despite my actions.

Alright. We're all inside, and eventually, we calm down after debriefing the door fiasco. I'll try to keep it brief from here on out, but I've got a lot of notes left. Besides, we're on island time and in no hurry. Maybe a list will help:

1. Two of the three drinks I tried were horrible and overpriced, also noting that they charge $10 for a michelada (yep, beer and spiced tomato juice).

2. It was 85 degrees out and humid AF having just rained, yet all the garage doors were open. The climate of this "oasis" was disgusting.

3. Two one-seater bathrooms are not enough for a place of this size. Additionally, the blue lights on one of the unisex bathroom doors and pink lights on the other are confusing. Perhaps this is intended to be a clever social experiment to see if men use the blue light door and women use the pink light door, but the restroom line would run more efficiently if both were clearly indicated as unisex rather than suggesting gender-specific rooms. Just another detail that wasn't well considered.

4. Two weeks in, and the paper menus were already falling apart, which just resonated with me as cheap.

5. One bartender took my order by standing about three feet behind the bar, arms folded behind his back with very erect posture, and then raising one finger to his ear to indicate that he was ready for my order. How arrogant!

The decor and lightning are beautiful, and I've been reading about what the owners are trying to pull off. But relaxed, island retreat is definitely not what I experienced. If they can be bothered to listen to their customers, my recommendations are:

1. Figure out your door situation -- what is your procedure and policy, and how are you going to clearly convey this to potential customers in a way that is straightforward to understand? This is the first impression. Keep it simple, and get it right.

2. Based on my experience and others', it's already time for an all-staff lineup about providing customer service. Set clear expectations, and cut the fat if your employees aren't getting it done. This is incredibly basic and fundamental to your industry. Arrogant, patronizing service won't cut it.

I'll take the host's advice and will skip coming back to the door.

I'll admit that due to my profession, I can't "turn off" my management mentality and I'm almost always taking note to everything pertaining to my dining experience; if the hostess is engaging, the cleanliness of the store/restrooms, how efficiently the serve staff is working and their demeanor towards customers, the server's interaction w/ fellow employees and kitchen staff, the quickness of my drink and food order, the plating of the food and the quality/taste that accompanies it, and how all of the above compares to my establishment.

That said, Silo was great.

Our server was excellent; she was genuine and knowledgeable, on point and accurate, attentive but never overbearing.  My Bloody Mary was brought out within 2 minutes of ordering it; the grapes on the lime skewer threw me off but otherwise it was a "unique-in-their-own" tasting cocktail.  The kitchen was very busy (it can be seen from the dining area) but that wasn't shown on my plate; the Pulled Pork Benedict was garnished with ripe honeydew melon and featured two perfectly toasted english muffins with juicy, seasoned and perfectly trimmed pulled pork, topped with two poached eggs (one of which was a little under-done but I'd take that over overcooked ANY day), and a jalapeno hollandaise which was spot-on some of the best hollandaise I have ever had.  I might consider calling this my favorite Benedict in Nashville.

The host stand seemed busy socializing, as there were always 2 girls and at least 1 gentleman at the stand (both at the time I arrived and when we left.)  I was meeting someone and instead of being escorted to the table, I was "pointed" to my party.  This was the only downfall, but again, I'm judging from a management standpoint and I have trained hostesses to do otherwise.  I won't fault Silo for this.  The ambiance was great, the noise level manageable (I didn't hear any music, only a full dining room talking), the main dining room was well kept and our table was very clean/stocked.

This was my first visit and I would absolutely return.

Looking back at my previous reviews from 3 years ago, I know the restaurant has gone completely down hill since! The service is absolutely horrible. During my last, and I mean last ever, visit, there were 3 servers in a small section, and no one could get anyone's attention. The food also isn't what it used to be. Yes, their crazy burger concoctions may sound good, but are actually impractical and unappetizing. With so many better restaurants nearby, forget PYT.

Oh, Elliot's. I love thee. How do I love thee? Let me count the ways:
1) house-infused vodkas that lead to endless combinations of tasty cocktails
2) huge delicious portions for incredibly fair prices
3) many healthy options (poached pear salad mmmm)
4) the atmosphere is just right for watching a game, going on a serious date, or stumbling in at 1 a.m. completely toasted

And the main reason I love Elliot's? Every time I bring my boyfriend, he gets all romantic. I have cross-checked this phenomenon with some friends and the same thing happens to them. So I don't know if they pump it through the vents, lace the parmesan garlic fries, or infused all their vodka with love potion number 9, but there's something so wonderful about Elliot's that it makes men romantic. Thank you, Elliot's; I love you!

Wait... is Elliot's making me romantic... for Elliots?

Sucks. Sucks. Sucks. 

SMALL. SMOKEY. DIRTY. SCUM BAG. GROSS. 

After visiting Vegas, Mohegan Sun, Pechanga, & other International casino's, this pathetic Tampa location should have it's tail between it's legs. 

It's filthy. Literally dust and grime wherever you sit or stand....Dirty carpets...FILTHY bathrooms...ALL bathrooms...FILTHY...

No COMPS...No free cocktails as you play, no complementary players club buffet or discounted rooms compared to the other casinos. 

Not to mention the huge ATM & Valet fees. 

YUCK! Wish there was a negative star scale! 

Get your act together Seminole!

I'm so happy this place exists! Got a chance to try it tonight for the first time and I have to say, their style and flavor is on point. Vermicelli bowl and rice paper rolls were so good. What a great addition to the neighborhood. I love the combination of a casual feel and excellent food. Everything tastes clean and fresh with no shortage of flavor. Furthermore the prices are very reasonable. I will definitely be back.

You know what sucks even more than being STUCK in a non-moving drive-thru line for HALF an HOUR? Pulling out of said drive-thru line to find THE WRONG ORDER in your bag.

This is the second time this week that I've been trapped in that line, although tonight was way longer. No, I didn't learn my lesson the first time because IT'S McDONALD'S! You'd think that if any fast-food place -- shit, no -- any RESTAURANT chain on this planet would basically have their shit together it would be McDonald's. So last time I chalked up to a fluke.

So last time after about fifteen minutes in the drive thru, i get home and my Pico Guac Burger had no lettuce. Okay no biggie. I was sad but I lived through it.

Tonight I ordered the Pico Guac burger again - on "Artisan" bun, a large fry and a cheeseburger (for my pup who's been under the weather today). Thirty minutes after placing my order I get to the window and am handed a cup and straw.

"I didn't order a drink..." says I.

"You didn't order a small ice water?" says she.

"No."

"Did you have the Pico Guac Burger and a cheeseburger?" says she.

"Yes. And a large fries."

She hands me the bag and because the entire population of south Reno was in line behind me, I took only a second to look in the bag to make sure I got my three items. One. Two. Three. Yep.

Get back and open the box to find a sesame seed bun with a dried out hockey puck, two desiccated pieces of what may have been Bacon about twelve hours ago, and a smidge of barbecue sauce.

And a plain hamburger with no cheese.
(My dog's name is "Nacho", okay? Cheese is like, his THING).

So not only did I not get my Pico Guac Burger my boy didn't get his cheese.

I also got zero napkins. But whatever.

You'll notice I don't often review fast food joints because, well, they are what they are, right? I mean I don't go to Arby's and bitch that their sandwiches aren't made of filet mignon with a side of ribeye.

But, and especially after reading other reviews of this place, this fast food joint needs to get its shit together.

Will I give this McD's one more chance?

You bet! Tomorrow, when I go in to see the manager and get the meal that I ordered tonight.

By STL standards, Nudo is a 4, maybe even 4.5. By CA or NY standards it would be a 2.5. 

Tucked away in a Creve Coeur shopping plaza, this restaurant has a small storefront but no shortage of noodle soups. There is something here to suit any palate, despite the limited menu - 7 apps, 2 sandwich, 4 pho, and 4 ramen options (including 1 vegetarian). 

My go-to dish at any new ramen shop is pork tonkotsu, which is called the Classic Nudo here. I figured it must be on a whole 'nother level, since it was so good that the restaurant is named after it. FYI I had to ask since this info wasn't anywhere on the menu, but the Classic comes with 3 slices of chashu pork, menma (bamboo shoots), half an egg, nori (seaweed), scallions and sesame seeds. 

The ramen itself was chewy, with a good bite to it, but at the same time there was also a staleness as if it had been packed and preserved for some time. For a restaurant whose name is a play on the word noodle, I expected fresher ramen.

The broth had the rich, cloudy appearance of a good tonkotsu, but I daresay it looked better than it tasted. There was no depth of flavor or discernible richness from boiled pork bones, and after a while all I could taste was salt. 

The pork, while a generous portion, was on the dry side and tasted quite plain for meat that's supposedly marinated and braised. It's also possible that the saltiness of the broth was overpowering all the other flavors in the bowl. The egg, however, was cooked to perfection!

I can certainly appreciate the effort the owner has put into this restaurant, as well as the fun mixed-Vietnamese-and-Japanese concept, but the ramen missed the mark for me. For $12 a bowl (+$2/add-on) it's not a bad deal, though I probably won't be going out of my way to come back anytime soon.

I can't even give this place a star. We attempted to come in with a party of 12 on a Saturday afternoon at 4pm and were told by the manager that "they do not accommodate parties our size". After asking the manger if she was serious, as the entire place was empty, she precedes to escort us out the door. 

Now, as a bar owner myself, I would NEVER turn away business. This woman has no idea how much money she just turned away. 

If I was the owner of this business and knew this happened I would be beyond pissed off. 

I will NEVER give this place another chance, and I am in New Orleans at least 5 times a year.

This hurts. It hurts so much to be leaving such a low rating at such a beautiful restaurant. I absolutely loved my experience in Orlando, the service as well as the food.

Unfortunately my visit at the Tampa location upsets me. It hurts me so much. I was really excited to go back to Texas De Brazil and wanted to share something new to my mother. I'm absolutely embarrassed that our dinner today was just disappointments. 

Let's just start out with all the problems... For some reason our reservation for OpenTable was canceled? Uhh.. okay. Easy fix because we arrived early enough for dinner. After that I thought it would be smooth sailing and excitedly explained to my mom the concept. 

We got our drinks and we are ready to head off to the salad bar. Things are going smoothly and everything is fresh and delicious! Yay! Here comes the meats! So we dig in and yikes, the meats are super salty... almost like licking a salt rock. Hmm.. I was hoping that maybe it was just the crust and that's were all the salts were... so I was being hopeful as more meats come along. Nope. Nope. Too salty.

So at this time I'm observing my waiter as he is just chilling in the corner with another server. Alright, cool. My drinks are running low and I don't know if sodas are refillable, but he never came by to ask if I ever wanted another one. A different server had to refill my water... Alright... (My server only asked if I needed more water as we were paying for the bill.. man awesome timing huh?)

Anyways.. back to the meat. I think the last piece was when I got a filet mignon that was RED like.. it was uncooked. Now I'm cool with rare, but this was uncooked and scary looking. I handed it over to my boyfriend and even he didn't touch it. 

I guess that ends our dinner. A party of 3, waited to be seated, settled in, ate and waited to pay our bill within 1 hour. That's the fastest dinner ever... at an place with endless food. What a waste, especially at roughly $50 per head. Yikes. 

I know this review is just upsetting... I hate writing it, but honestly I couldn't leave Texas De Brazil with a smile. I was over overall disappointed, with the meats and also the service. If it wasn't for the salad bar we probably wouldn't have ate anything. For the salad bar, you received 2 stars.

Man, it still hurts. Now my Texas De Brazil experience is forever ruined.

Honest thoughts? I have had better.

I agree with Coty that Arirang is really expensive and Korean food is overall an expensive cuisine in Tampa. 

We (boyfriend and I) started with an appetizer of Seafood pancake, which came out not as crispy or flavorful as Sa Ri One (the best in town in my opinion).  It was soggy and the flavor was just off. 

We shared an order of dolsot bibimbap and wang galbi (which was a freaking $30 for the smallest portion ever). The dolsot bibimbap tasted plain even with the pepper sauce. I barely ate my portion. The galbi was what disappointed me the most, for $30 I expected a plate of delicious galbi but what arrived was skimpy dull meat.

So you could say.. I was disappointed because the bill was hefty for a not so delicious meal.

The service (whom I assumed was the owner) was nice and I enjoyed the cinnamon tea at the end of the meal.

I really wish I could like this place because it's such a mom and pop's restaurant, but sadly flavorwise and bill wise I would rather visit Sa Ri One which is closer to me.

I absolutely loved this place the moment I walked in. It's a very airy and comfortable restaurant set up like a cafe. There's French and Vietnamese dishes to pick from their menu and I must say the egg rolls and pho is the best I've ever had at any restaurant. 

I really recommend this place! The interior is very adorable and I felt like I was able to relax here. The waitress are pretty nice and the food was served up fast and hot. It's honestly the best place I've been to recently and wish it was closer to me. 

Check this place out!!!

The casino employees were VERY helpful.  Anytime we needed to find something they would actually take you directly to the slot machine, bar, etc.  I was very impressed with everyone we met.  4 stars for the employees!

This comment is directed at the casino management...who the hell raises the valet parking charge to $20?  My Mom is disabled and always used the valet for $5 until this time when as of 1/1/2015 you raised it to $20.  I can understand raising it to $10 but $20 is highway robbery.  I REFUSED to let her pay that extortion rate so we slowly walked from the handicapped parking to the casino.  She used to come here twice month so I doubt she will ever be back.   Zero stars for management!

I was on board with your Kenosha, WI  casino until this entire valet incident.  If this is how you run a casino then I hope you don't get one in Wisconsin!

FIVE STARS ALL DAY

This place is within close walking distance from my apartment and is generally amazing.

It's the bee's knees. 

I was pleasantly suprised to walk in around 8 am this morning (8/18) and find only a small line. Often the line is out the door. I ordered an everything bagel (made in house like all their bagels) with bacon, egg, and pepperjack  cheese. 

It was AMAZING!!!

I have never been let down by this place, not even slightly. They are the real deal, so amazing. 

The bagel is so fresh, just the right amount of chewy and the perfect amount of "everything" toppings. The bacon, egg, and pepperjack were also very nice. 

Overall this is, in my opinion, the best place to get a bagel in Nola. I will definitely be back soon! Highly recommended.

TERRIBLE SERVICE! This place just opened this past weekend in our neighborhood, we've been watching the place for months in anticipation of a great seafood restaurant but we were sadly disappointed. The place seemed packed by the wait at the door which is to be expected but when the hostess walked us to the table, the restaurant had huge open spaces (for the live band?? MIA) which made it look like it was still under renovation. The tables were so crowded together so that our chairs rubbed against the back of the neighboring tables chairs - Irritating! We waited 8-10 minutes just for our server to come greet us and take our drink orders. Another 10 for him to come back with half our drinks then another 5 for the rest. Ordered appt, shrimp legon, crab dip, and crab fries. Along with our meals, fisherman's platter, and a pot of snow crab legs. I wanted a steam pot with king crab legs, but they were out of all crabs but snow crab. Not happy. Took about 30 mins for apps to come out, while we continually had to chase down our server to get refills. (While there's 10-15 other servers standing around looking bored) finally our meals come, after about 15-20 more minutes of observing bored waiters and scraping my neighbors chair, the moment we've been waiting for, been craving seafood all day! DISAPPOINTING! Fishermans platter is small and cold, not the huge platter we were dreaming the most expensive thing on the menu would be. My pot of snow crabs that the waiter told me came with sides of corn and 'others' was 4 semi cleaned crab leg sections. Had to ask for the sides, waiter told me corn would take 20 mins would I like fries? There was two crackers on the table, no hammers, no seafood forks, no extra napkins, no buckets for shells. I guess i expected a 'crabhouse' to have those. Our entire dining experience was close to 2 hours long.  All in all this place has potential but needs to work out all the kinks first, like the terrible service. The food wasn't bad but definitely needs some finesse. I expected much more. I would try aj Stephens crab house again but not for at least 6-12 months.

All the loveliness and great customer service of Sup just up the street.

Had lunch here with a friend today and it hit the spot. The crepes were just delicious: I had the farmhouse and the nutella crepe for desert. It was all fairly priced: $1.99 for crepes ala carte, with the whole spread two crepes and a salad mine was $5.99. It did not disappoint at all. I am not really a lunch person so when I eat lunch, I always prefer it to be something light but filling. Crepes are just the trick. 

The customer service today was outstanding. They really bent over backwards to make sure we were having a pleasant experience. Great addition to the mid-town area, which is getting increasingly better by the moment. Recommended for lunch or breakfast.

Before I ever thought I'd end up living in New Orleans, I watched Top Chef. Apart from adding a whole bunch of restaurants to my 'must visit' list, I made a mental note to go and eat at whatever restaurant Nina owned. I had a few reasons for liking Nina so much, her plates always looked delicious, they sounded really interesting and she also came across as genuine, passionate and just...nice. Obviously TV is edited and produced in a certain way but it's hard to argue that she didn't come across really well. Anyway, fast forward a year and I'm moving to NOLA and what's more, Nina never left and she's opened her restaurant. I've never made a booking so quick!

First impressions are good, the OLD No.77 is cool and funky, adding to the excitement as you sit. We ordered cocktails (CL Pimms Cup & TCB Sour) as we decided what to order. It's a really interesting menu, with a few things I hadn't tried before as well as some things I had only seen on TV. Our server was top notch, recommending the conch croquette and jerk corn as appetizers. As we finished ordering, bread service arrived. As it's often the first bite of food you have in a restaurant, it can set the tone for what's to follow. This was heavenly. The bread was light and fluffy and still warm, coming with herby butter that melted on to the dough. Quite a bite.

I wasn't at all familiar with conch (unless the Lord of the Flies counts?) but it's delicious, served with a pickled pineapple tartar sauce. The corn might even have been better, served with Aioli and crispy chicken skin. Large plates arrived in due course. The goat curry with sweet potato gnocchi and cashews is excellent. It's a milder curry than I expected but that's probably no bad thing. The goat was incredibly tender and each spoonful was fantastic. My mouth is watering thinking about it. Also, I managed to not spill any curry sauce on my white shirt, which was nice. I'm getting good at using spoons. The Drum was probably a little less successful, it's still very good but probably falls a little in comparison to the other dishes.

At the end of meal, after paying, we debated where to go for a night cap. That was a pretty easy choice too...we sat at the bar, and enjoyed a couple more drinks taking in the view to the kitchen. A pretty nice place to be. Overall, a bill of $75 before tax (Pimms cup $8, TCB sour $9, Conch $6, Corn $5, Drum $24 & Goat $23) was pretty good value given the quality, variety, portions and ambiance. On the whole, it's actually pretty easy to give this five stars. Now, when to go back...

My nephew had taken my here for happy hour and we definitely made sure to make the best of it!

This restaurant is within close proximity to the West Edmonton Mall, so we had walked a few steps to get to this place.

Pros:
- The interior is really nice. Definitely has a nice modern sultry feel to it. Great for business lunches or intimate dinners.
- Their happy hour menu had many options for definitely better prices compared to their full price. Although the portion size may be smaller, it makes for great snacking.
- Truffle fries are pretty good and addicting!
- They have a unique beverage menu.

Cons:
- Service can tend to lack due to how big the restaurant is.

I had tried their frose, which is basically a sweet frozen rose and it was perfect. Not so sweet, but not so dry either. My nephew got their peach bellini, which was also good but may have been a bit sweet for me.

So here I am, in Canada. wondering where to get some good breakfast at. Luckily my nephew, who actually lives in Canada, knows a few. So here we went venturing into Whyte Ave.

This spot is a bit hard to find, but its inside the same building that contains Blush Lane Organic Market on Whyte Ave. It's on the left side, also with De Capo.

Pros:
- Interior is very hipster-esque, but homey nonetheless. Lots of interior, as well as exterior seating available.
- Menu is simple and straightforward on a tiny clipboard: you have a small menu of breakfast foods (Crepes, Waffles), non-breakfast foods, alcoholic beverages (wines, their concoctions) Hot and cold espresso/tea drinks. They also have milk alternatives as well (yee!)
- Service is quick, attentive, and very helpful.
- Accepts card and cash.
- Parking is available at the side of the building, or street parking.

Cons:
- Quite pricey for the food you will be paying.
- If you're lucky and you come in on a slow day, your food will probably come out faster.

I got the waffle that consists of a side salad, fruits, poached egg, and your choice of meat (sausage, smoked salmon, ham). I liked that the portion size was appropriate for one person, and that they are considerate of whether or not a customer has any food allergies. You can also choose how you want your poached egg cooked, and you can substitute the side salad for potatoes. Hoping to come back one day to try their other options!

Ah yes, an A-OK Dim Sum spot in Canada. We've been brought here several times by our Canadian relatives, and after having different kinds of dim sum back in the states, I can honestly say that this place is... A-OK.

Pros:
- Large interior with many tables. It's a great spot for large parties. 
- They have the carts!! Best part about dim sum are the carts ~ 
- Food comes out pretty fast. 
- Definite favorites are the siu mai, pork dumplings, and such. I'm unsure if they serve the XLB (xiao long bao) but if so then I should invest on trying it in the future. 
- They take reservations, but i think you have to have a certain number of people in your party for them to actually take it.

Cons:
- Gets a bit cramped due to the large tables. 
- Workers aren't super friendly and may brush you off, even if you try to get their attention. 
- They're EXTRA busy during lunch hours and weekends. Don't expect to come in and have a nice quiet lunch. It gets crowded, and it's pretty loud.
- Location doesn't have the best parking available. The lot is small and gets cramped. 

Definitely one of those spots where you go to if you really need to get your dim sum cravings in. But otherwise, I'm pretty sure there are better places elsewhere.

My interpretation of Hattie B's heat levels...

Southern - Why are you in a Nashville "Hot" Chicken joint, fool?
Mild - I bet you think black pepper is spicy.
Medium - Poseur.
Hot - It ain't *that* hot. Don't brag to your girlfriend.
Damn Hot - It hurts so good!
Shut the Cluck Up!!! - For masochists and those who wish to engage in self-loathing only.

Do yourself a favor. Order a heat level up from where you think your tolerance level is. Get some blue cheese on the side to help cool your palate, and push your boundaries a bit. Yes, you'll be uncomfortable for a little while, but you won't die. Really, you'll live to tell the tale.

Seriously, it's called "HOT" chicken for a reason, folks.

If your chosen heat level does make you uncomfortable, relax and sip a beer or a sprite, the discomfort will pass. And then you'll have the self-satisfaction of knowing you ate Nashville Hot Chicken that was actually, you know, hot.

Did I mention the chicken is delicious? Oh, yes it is. It's excellent. It's worthy of the hype, and the long lines.

One last thing, order the bone-in chicken. Only boneheads (pun intended) get the boneless chicken. I don't care that boneless chicken is on the menu. Nashville Hot Chicken *is* bone-in fried chicken. You ain't at Chick-fil-A.

Very cool new place in Southwest St Pete. Not on the beach or downtown but a great choice if you're in the middle areas and easy access off of I-275.

Indoor and outdoor bars. There are also some tables in a cool sandy area overlooking the marina. We prefer the outside bar as a place to enjoy an afternoon watching the boats come and go. 

Cocktails are well-made, strong, and reasonably priced. Pain Killers actually have Pusser's Rum which is rare these days but I won't drink them any other way. 

We had the chicken tenders in the coconut batter which was excellent....moist, succulent and tasty. 

We also had the banana bread ice cream sandwich which was STELLAR!! Seriously... get this fantastic treat!!
