Parking shares with the marina so it can get crowded at times.

Staff was friendly and accommodating throughout. 

Bathrooms were very clean and spacious. 

Overall recommended!

Great SpeakEasy, one of the few in the Bay area. And excellent mixologists behind the bar! This is a must stop in Tampa for some cozy cocktails. They are open late but the limited seat bar fills very fast and you definitely want to call ahead to get reservations for any of the tables...  and the password!

The staff has always been excellent. 

The parking is valet only unless you find a random spot along the local streets.

The cocktails and food are priced on par with a high quality speakeasy but not ridiculous for what you're getting.

Highly recommended!

This place is great. We had the Mae half of our baby shower her whole the wife had hers across the way at Brio.

Anyways... Come here during Happy Hour for the $5 beer and bourbon shot special! Best deal at I.Plaza. 

Staff has always been cool. Love the kilts all around. This is probably the best bourbon and whiskey selection in town, but they can get pricey. 

They have a 'serve yourself' beer tap area on the second floor but never used it.

There are private rooms and patios which are great for events.

My only complaint... and this is minor... the bathrooms are on the second floor. So.. they force me to work off calories to relieve. Maybe that's a good thing?!?

We wanted to step out of our norm for burritos in Tampa as I'm always on the hunt for something close to the incredible and original Mission-style burritos of San Fran.

This place is very close and they execute well. 

When in a new place I like to try their signature dish which in this case is the Signature Crazy Burrito. In the full size offering, it is huge and most likely more than enough for any person. I finished half. At $11 it is pricier than the chain store offerings but it is a monster! The Junior Crazy Burrito seems like the perfect size and you can save $2. It was great in flavor but I would recommend against the chorizo as it made the experience a bit too salty for my taste.

Our group also had the California Burrito which comes with fries in the burrito. Very unique, but tasty. 

We also got the Baby Burrito for our 5 year old and it was more than enough for any young eater. $7

5 of us ate for a little over $50 with tip (burritos only, no drinks, no apps).

They have a small dining area for in-house eating although we took ours to go. They have mild green sauce and spicy red sauce perfect for flavoring the burritos. 

If you're tired of the chains (Chipotle, Moe's, Qdoba) give this local spot a try.

Note for Crazy Burrito: Put your menu on your website! :)

This place is a cool local hangout. While the tourists are out at the beach spots, the locals come here for great smoked food, strong drinks, and cheap beer. 

The ambiance is that of an open air 'tiki' style place with a cool breeze blowing off the waterside canal. Very chill and inviting. Staff is friendly and timely. 

The food is smokey goodness. The wings and Big A$$ burrito are favorites and recommended. The Angry Peppers are the signature app. Big peppers stuffed and fried. Careful though.... it's like Russian roulette and you might get one with some seeds that will light you up!

Prices so far have not taken the Biden jump so come while it's still affordable. This might be the last place around with a $2.50 beer and wings that haven't gone to "Market Price"!!

Great German beer selection! The food menu is brief but tasty and the staff is always friendly and attentive. There is a cool patio on the back of the restaurant if you want to dine al fresco. Small plaza with plenty of parking. Definitely worth a try if you're in the mood for some liters of beer and wurst!

Stopped in for some breakfast sandwhiches... and they didn't disappoint! 

Food:
Large portion breakfast croissants that run about $7-$10. We also had the quiche which was $8.50 and tasty but not overwhelming. Menu is rather limited compared to other breakfast stops but enough for everyone to find something. Omelettes are around $10-$12. 

Drinks: 
Coffee/Espresso/Latte drinks are around $3-$4.

Service:
Friendly and busy on weekend mornings. 

Ambiance:
The seating area is small and can get crowded. 

Take Out:
They have a pastry display case with baked breakfast selections and desserts. 

Parking:
Plenty! It's in a small strip mall with a bar, another restaurant, a convenience store and some other miscellaneous. 

Overall:
Good place to try and food was good. I'd like to try the omelettes next time to give a better review of the menu. It was good, just not outstanding.

This is quickly becoming our goto and favorite sushi place in Tampa. 

The service is outstanding... very timely, personable, attentive, and accommodating. The staff has been awesome!

The place has been fully redesigned from the previous restaurant... BUT... they kept the very cool chabudai short tables for seating near the sushi bar. Take off your shoes and chill like it's your living room with your own sushi bar.

Happy Hour is great! Pork belly skewers are on point for $2.50 and Kirin pints at $3, $5 hot sake can't be beat. There are other specials for sake, apps, etc but I'm hazy on what they were. 

Sushi is outstanding! Presentation, taste, price are all perfect! 

Parking can get tight as there se wonky a few spaces but street parking is available on the side street and there is a huge lot for Press Box next door if you want to be sneaky. 

Do it!!

I've had a couple of opportunities to explore Casa Santo Stefano and I have been very pleased on both occasions. 

Menu/Food: The menu is excellent for both lunch and dinner offerings. The prices are great for the area and the ambiance. 

Drinks: The beer is a bit pricey but the specialty cocktails are excellent. 

Atmosphere: Stellar. Simply stellar. The main dining area offers seating that surrounds the kitchen. Yes, they cook/prep out in the open. It is incredible! It feels like you're eating in a large Sicilian home! They even have dining service ON their prep tables! The main floor bar is a tucked away little gem and perfectly decorated. 

Then there is the upstairs patio and bar. Truly amazing!! Great views! They even offer cigars if you're an aficionado. (Opus X is available!)

Staff: Awesome staff. Friendly. Courteous. Timely. Excellent!

This place is our new GoTo!! You need to try it if you're in the area!!

Absolutely stellar dive bar. This is my #1 in all my travels of dive bars around the world. 

Crazy, incredible ambiance, wonderfully abrasive bar staff, and cheap STRONG drinks!! The perfect mix for the Number 1 Title of Worlds Best Dive Bar. 

Also, they do have side parking which is useful at this beach location. 

BEST DIVE BAR EVER!!!

Always a great experience at Culvers! The custard is excellent, the burgers are some of the best around, and the prices are right. The staff here is friendly but this place can get busy and they can get overwhelmed. The parking lot is usually full and there are usually cars lined up around the drive through so plan ahead.

I hate to call this fast food because that would put Culver's in the category with McD, BK, and Taco Bell... and those don't even compare to Culver's. Rather, this is an Quickly Prepared Eating Experience.

Come grab a burger or get your kiddos some frozen custard (ITS NOT ICE CREAM) on the way home. Oh, and the root beer is incredible, best as a root beer float!

If you haven't been to a Culver's yet, definitely put this on your list!

Sushi chefs are not the same. Quality was less than normal and certainly took quite a bit more time to serve. Almost 15 minutes to pay my check. Seemed like the service members were the same and the capacity was reduced to the 25% so why the delays?!?!? Love this place but the service should be as good or better given the reduced volume.
Incredible response and handling of the virus issues. Happy to have them back again. The place is energized and dialed in. Staff and management are on point. Food is fast and tasty. Keep it up!!

All I have to say is this; the long drive is worth the pain. A friend of mine recommended me this restaurant few months ago and I finally decided to give it a try. First of all, I hesitated to come because of the distance but after reading all the reviews my stomach screamed from far away GO, YOU HAVE TO GO and there I was driving for 2 hrs and 35 minutes to get here. Was it worthy?? Hell yeah!!! The food was delicious. The meat was melting in my mouth; super tender and flavorful. The portions big enough and the prices were not that bad either. I was impressed for their customer service. The staff was super friendly and our waiter exceeded all my expectations of great customer service. I honestly didn't order from the menu. I asked the waiter to bring us the favorite and most popular dishes in the menu and boooooy, we didn't get disappointed me. Everything was perfectly cooked. Beautiful presentation. And the variety of the menu was awesome. If you're vegan, you'll enjoy it too. They have everything for everyone. How cool is that?? I didn't regret spending Christmas eve dining in this restaurant. Best decision ever. The only issue?   we had problems getting a reservation. We tried online, all booked, we tried on the phone, no answer.......we just showed up one hour after opening time and we were lucky to got seated right away. Besides that; Awesome experience!!

Cutting to the chase because I'm writing this from my phone... 

This place is crappy. It wasn't even busy. 

1. Wait staff. I had to ask to order my food. Then I had to ask for a refill. However, the people next to us got excellent service. Instant irritation. 

2. Food. I ordered a distinguished gentleman. MEDIUM.  MEEEEEEDIUUUUMMMMMMM. NOT BLACKENED. NOT WELL. It came out with really charred edges. Tasted it... It was well done. Sent it back... (keep in mind I am STARVING. Next level hungry) It came back AGAIN CHARRED. 

3. Management. A manager came out to address the twice sent back Kobe beef burger. It was pointless interaction. Her solution was to "talk to the kitchen. " If your kitchen doesn't know what medium is. Forget talking to them.  Re-TRAIN THEM. 

4. Crowd. The person next to me was giving me dirty looks because I WAS NOT PLEASED WITH MYYYY FOOD I WAS PAYING FOR. EVERY TIME I SPOKE WITH THE WAITRESS, they stopped everything they were doing to hang on to every word I said. Very VERY CREEPY. 

SAVE YOURSELF THE TIME AND ENERGY. GO TO SQUARE 1 where the burgers are not pre-cooked. I have not had a dining experience this bad in an extremely long time. Don't bother with them. Bad wait staff, inexperienced managers and the patrons are awful, too. They could've easily put a fast food joint here that would do better. Never EVER going back. Ever. 

Go to World of Beer across the street for a Chimay Burger and 100xbetter service.

The positive reviews surpassed my high expectations of this restaurant! We found Stanley on a chance while walking in the rain through Jackson Square. Wait was a little bit, but the bar next door offers a great selection of drinks while you wait. While the rest of my group are Bloody Mary drinkers, my best friend and I are not and we've never been a fan. However, their Bloody Mary was soo good that we had one ourselves. It was especially good with the pickled green beans they served it with. 
With the long wait at the bar and a couple Bloody Mary's later, we ordered a little too much that the plates almost didn't fit at the table, but everything was worth it. 
Here are the must haves:
Breaux Bridge Benedict (best dish of the table)-  Boudin, Smoked Ham, American Cheese, Poached Eggs, and Creole Hollandaise 
Egg stanley
Jambalaya
Banana Foster French Toast- everyone's favorite

I see why it has such great ratings and why it's so hyped! Will be back when I return!!

One Mojito, Two Mojito... and a whole lot of solid ales on tap!    Awesome spot to either just sit back with a group of pals and nosh on tapas such as  brushetta and Brie, Jalapeno Poppers wrapped in bacon, or a Cubano sandwich,  and a whole lot of awesome drinks such as the Red Mojito, which had just the right amount of zing to get the party started for this lass.

Friendly staff , great waitress that was able to keep our tabs organized and able to keep our very large parties orders straight. 

I also love that it's a dog friendly pub, as we walked in a man was there with his Husky who was content to lay at his owners feet, but was happy to be petted by passing guests too.

They have an eclectic urban vibe going on, art work hangs on the walls, they have padded bench seating, as well as wood chairs, that line the left side of Reds when walking in, and if you like to sit at the bar, just mosey on up and grab a stool. 

If I had one suggestion my to my friends at Reds, it might be to get some seat covers in the restroom, maybe they were out of stock, after all they had quite the line waiting to get in, so I'll give them the benefit of the doubt.

All in all, I had an outright fabulous time, it helps that I love the people I was with... just add good drinks and some nosh worthy tapas and you've got yourself a solid hit! 

Thanks Reds Bin 211 you rock!

This place seems to slip my mind, perhaps it is the complete lack of curbside appeal.

If you like sushi served by a very good staff then do yourself a favor and look past the outside.

I have eaten here several times and have enjoyed it every time.  The food is great, the menu diverse and the staff is very friendly and knowledgeable.

The chef does a great job when trusted to  "just feed me" - That is the course a friend and I (a local chef) took several months ago - cheap?  No..but the plates just kept coming - each one better than the one before.  He asked us ahead of time how much we were willing to spend and we told him to try to keep in under $75.00 each (not counting booze of course!) so he had quite a bit of leeway considering their reasonable prices.  But oh the stuff he created for us!  He told us that he cannot do that on busy nights but enjoys it on slower ones - most of the "rolls" were just two bites and one plate just rolled right into the next thing.  We spent about 2 hours had not only great food but a great time.  You just won't find this at a "chain" restaurant!

Stopped in this evening and had another very nice experience - ordered the Volcano roll and then left the rest up to the chef depending on what looked good to him...he choose white tuna and a scallop hand roll.  The Tuna was good and had that "bite" that good white tuna has - the temp was perfect as well -- not too cold, but just right (Good sashimi is not supposed to be ice cold contrary to popular myth).  The Scallop filled the entire hand roll and was very good.
The volcano roll was a little too sweet for my taste - was hoping for a little more spice - but still good.

Worth the trip from across the river even.

PS,,,they do have that "secret" Korean menu available as well - just ask!  It's in English also btw....

Decided to give this place a try after looking up places for tasty drinks and appetizers. 

The boyfriend and I went for happy hour which is Monday-Friday 4-6. I had the house made sangria and he had this ginseng tea infused gin cocktail, the ginseng tea drink was fire  but I wasn't a huge fan of the sangria only because I like my sangria to be more wine forward and than fruit juice, it wasn't horrible but just not my favorite.

For appetizers we tried the steak tacos and the bacon wrapped dates, both were delicious  . Portions are small for appetizers so make sure you order different plates if your hungry. Appetizers are o my $5 for HH which is reasonable but the restaurant prices for dinner seemed a little high. 

Location is right by the river in midtown so it's a super cute location but downside is parking and it's super small inside. My advice is get an Uber so your not circling to find a spot to park otherwise I think it's a great spot for a date of catching up with friends and affordable if you go during happy hour.

Restaurants in the burbs are not in my regular rotation of places to visit.  However, exceptions may be made for get togethers with friends -- especially for locales that are close to Septa train stations, as the Fermentaria is (a couple of minutes from the Ardmore station).

They've got an interesting and substantial beer list -- even when one excludes the numerous IPAs on that list.  I tried a couple and enjoyed both.  And would be happy to return to try more of the brews.

The food options include typical pub fare, but done much better than average.  I tried the fish tacos (thankfully made with an Atlantic pollock, rather than the now-ubiquitous tilapia).  The order comes with two tacos, topped with freshly-fried fish goodness and heaped with a colorful variety of veggie and cheesy toppings.  They were yummy and filling.  

Our server was friendly and had no problem tracking and providing separate checks, which makes it sooo much easier for people in a large group to come and go and pay in accordance with their schedules and such.  So much easier.  And a definite mark of professionalism.

The prices are reasonable.  The space, which is huge, seemed a bit cavernous, especially on an only mildly busy weeknight.  The bathrooms have awesomely original artwork worth checking out (well, at least the men's room does).

At last, the doors have officially open to a warm and welcoming coffee shop in Kennett Square! The shop is very unique offering ample seating for 2 to 4 guests at beautifully hand crafted tables. Two window seats with barstools are also at the front of the store which overlook State Street as well as little tables on the sidewalk out front. The menu is impressive and offers breakfast, salads, soups, sandwiches and even a kids selection for warm drinks. Three coffee flavors plus a house blend is sure to treat any coffee lovers taste. A full selection of teas, 12 to be exact, from local tea Artisan, Mrs. Robinson's Tea Shop are available for those who indulge in specialty tea. Espresso available as well. All menu items are available Togo which is very convenient since I was able to take home some items for the family! Hours of operation allow for all to enjoy between 6am and 8pm Monday to Thursday and until 9pm Friday and Saturday. Be sure to bring plenty of quarters for parking for once you come in you won't want to leave! Bravo Philter Coffee!

My husband and I live just a few min away from the Summit Sierra mall where this is located.  We have seen the new Miguel's open for some time but have never had the desire to go in, because we are such big fans of Murrietas. Today was The day! 

We walked in and there were about 8 people in the entire restaurant with about 10 people working. We were greeted right away and taken to a booth in the bar. I thought that was kind of strange... Didn't mind too much. Immediately after being seated a young man came around and gave us chips and salsa. At first glance it looks like every other chips and salsa you would get. However the salsa was fresh and made from scratch. Super tastie with the PERFECT amount of heat. They get all of their ingredients fresh, not frozen, so this will taste different every time you come in. If the jalapeños are grown a bit more spicy... This will effect the taste of the salsa.... The chips were made from the taco shell and nice and fluffy. Not like those thin frail chips you would get from Chili's or another Mexican food restaurant that's trying to save money by buying or cooking cheap versions of chips. The chips are not salted which we love! We were there about three minutes and ate all of our salsa! Within two minutes another man came around and filled our salsa up from a water pitcher filled with salsa. This happened about four or five times throughout our visit!  I can't tell you how much I appreciate that because of the drought where in the additional dishes and the additional space on the table just don't make sense. 

Usually when my husband and I go to a Mexican food restaurant on a Sunday we will get a beer and some nachos and split them. Today I didn't feel like a beer so I got an iced tea which was delicious. No sugar you can tell it has been just made. My husband ordered A large beer that came in a few different size options. He got the large one, it came in a frosty mug! It was fresh not something that had been sitting in an old Keg. 

While we were waiting for food which only took a few minutes, we were able to look around the restaurant and check it out. We found even though it has been remodeled there were still a need for some upgrades and maintenance such as a rip in the seat of the booth I was sitting in.

When the order of supreme nachos came they were much smaller than what we are usually used to. However the taste definitely made up for the quantity. This dish was layered with beans that were made from scratch, hamburger meat that I think had Cumin in it, fresh made guacamole, fresh tomato and those amazing chips! This also came with some sour cream... That tasted more like Crema then sour cream but had a nice tangy flavor. 

We polished that off , taking our time and appreciating all of the layers and layers and layers of flavor. I don't know how they do that!! The chips NEVER got soggy and yucky! They stayed crisp and delicious the entire time! 

After we split the nachos I was stuffed and wasn't ready to eat anything else. However my husband wanted more. So he ordered the number one with a cheese enchilada, a chili Relleno and a taco that came with rice and beans.

This plate came out smoking hot and with all fresh ingredients. At first glance it looked like a big plate of "mess"... But ohh what a awesome mess it was! The cheese enchilada came with a GRAVY!!! instead of the usual enchilada sauce. They do have the "green" and "red" typical sauce.... But dear god! After having that, IM RUINED FOR LIFE! I will only go there for the cheese and onion enchilada, rice and beans for now on! Sooooo good! 

The service was great! The drinks were great and the food was wonderful. 

I gave them 4 stars instead of 5 for a few minute reasons:
1. It's needs a bit of up keep. 
2. I asked for no sweetener with my tea and they brought me the sugar tray thing anyway. ( they did leave the lemon off :) 
3. The young buss boy would come over and remove plates and what not, without checking in with us first or saying anything at all
4. The taco meat tastes of Cumin, my husbands not a fan of cumin. 

Other than that, they have a HUGE menu - open Tuesday - Sunday, have a great happy hour,that has super fries ( like the super nachos we had ) ... I HAVE to go back for that and the amazing Margaritas I keep hearing about :) 

We will be back!

I have been here a thousand times through umpteen million diets! Now that I have decided to make a life change.... and have gone dietary vegan... this is my go to food source, until sprouts opens ( closer to my house ). As I was walking out of the store... I saw VEGAN DONUTS! oh lord! Are you kidding me right now! I have died and gone to heaven. I ordered the maple for 2.00 and ate the entire thing before I could get to my car in the parking lot!!!! Amazing! Thank you Whole Foods for supporting the Vegans. 
Came back today to get one Donut of each kind to do a donut taste test. THEY CHANGED! WHAT !! Noooooo, I have posted the before and after ... totally different flavor and totally different texture. I don't like the new ones, so if they don't change it back.... I won't buy them again :( yuck!

OK here's the skinny!

Parking here is super super simple because it's an outdoor strip mall. The signage on the outside is clear clean and it's easy to find.

When you initially walk and it seems pretty dark. You have a hostess station to your left that seems a little outdated. When you're greeted by the hostess she asks if you want to sit at the bar or a table. We chose to sit at the bar because we were going to do all you can eat sushi.  

Dinner Menu 
Option A ( without appetizers and Desserts ) 19.95
Option B includes one miso soup, edamame, drag salad, gyoza, mussel, ice cream,and Bogo hot sake ( Mon - Thu ). 

So basically I was looking for the soup only and a couple of long rolls. You don't have the option to do that under option a or B. So we both just got option a. When you sit down at the bar you have a large water glass that is filled with individually paper wrapped straws... I thought that was really weird?, And then your usual set up in front of you.

Our sushi chef didn't even acknowledge we came in. We had to ask him for a couple of rolls that were on the menu... And he never looked up once. He continued to speak in Spanish back-and-forth to the other sushi chef that was there, which I find incredibly rude. 

I didn't think any of the rules for anything special... Actually under par if you ask me. The roles were small and pretty much every single rule included cucumber. Because there was nothing particularly good about any of the rules, I asked for a side of "JP sauce "which is kind of like Suraci mayo. When I asked him for it he didn't knowledge my request, mumbled something in Spanish, then squirted this JP sauce into a little dish and put it up on the counter for me to take. At that point we finished what we ordered and we're ready for the check.

Our waitress/hostess... One and the same, was nowhere to be found. However I do want to say that she did check on us a few times throughout our meal. Just wasn't around at this time. So another waitress came over and was leaning across the table to my right speaking in Spanish to both of the sushi chefs this went on for a few minutes until I interrupted them and ask for the check. This waitress acknowledge my request but never came back with the check. When our original waitress came by we asked, again for the check! We paid and as we were leaving our sushi shaft looked up and said "thanks for coming in, will see you next time! ".

I will tell you from the sushi they offer, the darkness of the restaurant, the lack of flexibility with the menu, and the overall vibe and feel of the restaurant we will not be back without some serious changes.

This location is in an outdoor mall, right next to the movie theater!! The ambience, the food, and the service definitely has room for improvement.

My new favorite ASIAN SPOT!!! Wow the flavors are good! And the prices are RIGHT! They have a sister location on south meadow Called La Mint .... same basic menu.

Parking was super easy. We were seated in a booth right away.  Drinks and appetizer order was taken within minutes. 

The staff was super easy to work with on Vegan options and they have tried almost everything on the menu! A ton of vegan options here :) 

The restaurant has a clean, trendy feel with a full bar and an outdoor patio. 

The beer is cold and wine is fresh. 

The food is the star here. Layers and layers of fresh made  foods and flavors! We had the tofu fresh spring rolls... made FRESH! , tofu curry and war wonton soup with a beer and a glass of wine ( total of $44.48!!!) awesome value if you ask me.  The war wonton soup was delicious! Light and fresh wontons, textured and delicious flavored broth with all the veggies :) and the peanut sauce with the fresh spring rolls was spot on!! 

And when you have leftovers, and you will :) they take it away and box it up for you.... I LOVE that! 

You have to check this place out.  Lunch, happy hour or dinner!! They have you covered for sure! YUM!!! We will be back .... and we are going to try your sister location la mint next! 

Way to go Asian kitchen and bar!!!

This place is awesome! Open ... Clean....60 + beers on tap! We popped in early to see if we could check out a few beers before lunch.. The door was open so we went on in. The staff was super nice and gave us the Low down on coming back in when they were set up. They are doing the soft opening tonight and the grand opening next week. So stay tuned for more pics and more of my review :) so far!! I love what I see :)

Every time I go to Roberto's they ALWAYS get my order right..... except this time. 

Parking is simple ... plenty of room. There are tons of windows so you have lots of room to watch folks walk by. 

Bathroom was a mess AND you need a KEY! to get in. I hate that! 

There were THREE people in the restaurant! My to go order is simple. Veggie burrito with no sour cream or cheese. I received a Luke warm burrito with no rice and cheese. I'm a vegan and I told the cashier that.  So I take one bite and can't eat the rest! I'm on a time schedule... that's why I got it to go! As I was walking out , I looked for napkins... oh that's right! You HAVE TO ASK FOR THEM! 

I will enjoy my other Roberto's Locations but not likely be back to this one :( BUMMER!

So disappointing! I really try my best to find the best in all my reviews. But.... I have to say..... totally a let down :( 

A few days I had the GREAT PLEASURE of going to SOHO Sushi Burrito in Las Vegas and had some unicorn dream about this place being similar. Boy was I wrong. 

Here we go - first ..... Parking here can be a challenge because public house is right behind it and takes most all of the parking. So pretty much your restricted to street parking. 

When you walk in, there is a pungent smell..... not quiet fishy..... but there is defiantly something in the air. The place and employees are clean. Both very important. They have have a "junk bucket" with pens and paper and junk in it, by the register.... I don't like that. Put it under the counter where I don't have to see that. For someone that eats with their eyes..... that's not something I want to see. 

The ordering process was less than desirable. Basically you have the option for a bowl or burrito. A prebuilt option or a build your own option. The menu says you can have an rice ( I wanted the purple rice ) but we were never offered one and the guy behind the counter just put white rice on our burrito and moved it down the line. There was no one in front or behind us. Im not one to waist.... so I just went with it ( totally unlike me ). Because I'm vegan I asked if they had any other options besides tofu for my protein, explaining that I'm vegan. The girl behind the counter proceeded to tell me that they have a sweet egg option. So she obviously did not know what vegetarian or vegan means!... It's pretty simple if you're in the food industry be clear about dietary restrictions and options... She did however know what was gluten free. Unfortunately I don't have a gluten issue or this might of been a better experience for me.
After adding all of the veggies that I wanted to add I asked to add avocado, this was a sixth of an avocado! The three smallest pieces of avocado I have ever seen put on any item ever...all for very cheap price of one dollar. Wanting to be sure the wonton chips were vegan I asked... No one knowing, I suggested someone read the ingredients on the package that came in... The guy behind the counter said well I guess it would matter what they were fried in.... I said well no not unless they were fried in lard?... Anyway he came back later to tell me that he read the instructions on the fried onions... Telling me that it's basically the same thing and that I was clear to eat them. So I give him credit for at least trying to help.
So for $25 we sat down to eat one orange soda and two burritos.

So to eat there you get a tray for all of your food... I know additional plates or placemats or anything... Your burritos just wrapped in a paper wrap. I guess were supposed to eat over a napkin? Maybe?? I don't know. So after we sat down I went back to the register to ask for an additional paper placement so I can eat my food over something... The woman said oh yeah go ahead and grab it since my hands are wet! I reached over the counter and grabbed one as she instructed me!  They got back up back to the counter to ask if they had any ginger... They have that pink pickle kind of ginger... Not that yellow clear fresh normal looking ginger. Just for those of you that are ginger fans.

Anyway as I begin to unwrap the paper from my sushi burrito I noticed that the seaweed wrap ( nori ) literally has holes in it and is falling apart! You'll see that my photos below. They are used to use a lesser grade wrap to save money ?? Biiiiig mistake on their part! When I mentioned this to my husband he said they DONT HAND ROLL THEM! ok.... wait .... whaaaaaaat! Moving on. 

My build your own was designed to be vegan .... having tofu in it. The tofu was absolutely horrible. The other ingredients however we're pretty fresh for the most part and a jalapeño that I got was an absolute top 10 spicy! I husbands sushi burrito on the other hand was pretty bland with no flavor in the spicy tuna. It looked like canned tuna with Siratcha in it... and the shrimp.... since when do shrimp come in rectangle shapes??? They don't even have KIMCHI! Whaaaaaaat.... I know... blew my mind too! 

Overall..... I won't come back again unless they can pull it together with the service , food and especially the nori. 

Sorry guys! I was really pulling for you.

I came to this location because GLB said that it had vegetarian and vegan options. However... They don't have any vegetarian or vegan options. Maybe in November they said. They only have Chicken beef and pork stock. They don't have anything vegetarian or vegan on the menu at all.  I will definitely be going to check it out when they do have those options available... And will revise my review at that time.

I love this place...... what can I say.... lol. 

I messaged them to ask what the deal was w the vegan pizza. They got back to me super fast! 

I went down to pick up some pizza kits for a Yelp event I was doing and they.... of course we're super accommodating, quick.... but not "Rush-ie" if you know what I mean. They even had an order of 45 pizzas in front of me!! And they still had a smile on their face and a kind word to say! 

The pizza was awesome, and because it was so easy for me to get in and out... I bought 7 chocolate chip cookies to support these guys even more! Lol. 

Super clean!! Parking is easy, ordering is easy, staff is easy ( not that kind of easy ... get your mind out of the gutter! ) easy to work with!! Lol 

Thin crust , good fresh veg.... I'll continue to come back year after year :) 

Great job RENO TEAM!

For stars for effort! This place is up off of pyramid highway in sparks.. It's up in the Walmart shopping center. The location has been open since December 2015.... Who knew? Parking is super easy and there is lots of space. 
When you walk in it's very clean and free of any one particular food odor. There were about 15 people inside already and more just pouring in. 

You are greeted immediately by the owner or one of his extremely nice staff.  We were seated right away and offered to get a drink order done. They have a nice big menu with Mexican and American food to offer. Half of my group got breakfast and half of my group got lunch.  The food came out within 10 minutes and everything is piping hot.
I ended up ordering the chicken Caesar wrap with french fries. My french fries were super hot and sprinkled with some amazing seasoning. The French fry is a combination between a regular french fry and a steak fry. Super delicious and super hot. My chicken Caesar wrap it's self was perfectly balanced with sauce to lettuce to meat. It wasn't too dry or too wet... It was just right. However, the texture of the chicken was a little chewy and a little gummy and it was waaay over seasoned with garlic. I was able to pick the chicken out and eat around it just the same. 
I wasn't going to say anything because every single person at the table was happy with their meal and everything looks fantastic! However when the owner came over to ask if I wanted a box, I told him no. He seemed concerned on why and inquired if everything was ok?  I explain the situation above. He insisted on removing it from the bill and comped my entire meal! I ask him not to do that because I was happy to pay for it, totally 100% out of my normal character, but he insisted and said it was the right thing to do!NOW THAT IS WHAT I CALL SERVICE! 

When it came time for us to pay the bill, my iced tea, side of ranch ( I don't know if they charge for that... And it was super good ) and my meal were completely removed. I asked to at least pay for the iced tea, he insisted on removing  the entire thing, apologized and apologized. He told me " we are better than that! Please come back to let us show you". 

Because of his outstanding customer service I WILL BE BACK to try the shrimp enchiladas that my girlfriend said were phenomenal and or the taco salad that equal.

WATER SPRINGS!! you should teach some of the other places in town ... How to treat a customer :) outstanding job! I will be back with friends!  Thank you for getting giving me the opportunity to do that :) GREAT JOB!

BOISE: I just got my world rocked by this top-rated little German fusion gastropub.  Come get yours rocked as well.

Ambience (4 stars): Cool, new, clean exterior with a trendy looking front and outdoor patio.  Long tables, communal goodness.  Parking was difficult.  I think I parked in a briar patch out back.

Service (5 stars): Super nice, super chill waitress who even had a sense of humor.  Sense of humor earns like +4 service stars every time for me; super underrated.

FOOD - tried two dishes, both were mindblowers

"Cheesysteak" 5 stars: wow! Delicious, moist tender ribeye, peppers, perfect bread, beer cheese, onions, lip smacking good.  Eat this 

Currywurst (5 stars): curried ketchup atop amazing sliced brat atop awesome house fries plus flavorful sourkraut=bliss.  I couldn't believe how complex and engaging the flavor was.  Highly recommended!

I'm half-Korean (mother) and have lived in Korea for short time. Also been to many Korean restaurants in NYC, Bay Area, etc. 

I was excited to try a Korean place, the first one I've seen in New Orleans. (I've tried one in Metairie, which I thought was actually better.)

The Good
Despite being in an old Taco Bell, the servers make the place feel homier than expected. Most were young and had that endearing (more so than annoying) lack of confidence and skills that I'm sure they will soon acquire. 
Service was quick, frequent and personal. 

The Bad
The food wasn't good. It wasn't bad. Not authentic though and not anything I'd order again. And I ordered some staples. 
Mondoo: I really like the way these were cooked, crispy on the outside. But the filling was kind of mush with no real taste of anything. 
LA Kalbi: BBQ at our table, these looked okay raw but I could tell they wouldn't be that good. Not super fresh. No real taste when I ate them. 
Sam Gyup Sal: One of my favorites in general. Here, it was basically unseasoned bacon. The slices of pork belly are usually not long, thin strips and not as streaky, more fat/meat/fat, short, FAT pieces of pork belly.
Server cooked at our table and that was great, but was there the whole meal. Even though she was really nice, I was there to eat with my gf, not my gf and the server. Usually, someone puts the meat on, checks on it, there longer when needs to be and leaves when done. 
Rice was long-grain American rice. Banchan was not good. Kimchi was super weak. Pajeon was so plain. 

Would I go again? 
I'm half-Korean and I'd like to try to support this new business and their employees who were all SO nice. I'll give them one more try and see how the soups are. I love sundooboo jigae, though i have to say, my expectations are low.

I almost couldn't find this place but it is to the right of Zocalo, and it really is a hidden gem. Its subtle signage is an intentional choice of the ambiance of this place. A tucked away pizzeria that should change your views on what brick oven pizza is all about.

We began with a Caprese from the Antipizza menu, and lord it was good. The restaurant itself is supplied by a small farm (Sleeping Frog Farm near Benson) and the ingredients are amazing. Using Heirloom fruits and vegetables for their meals makes this special and unique experience. 

Sitting at the "Farm" table I feel your less inclined to rudely pull out your cell phone and face book away your precious time with the friends you bring. Stay in the moment and appreciate the vinyl music, they will even play yours if you bring it. Keep it classy though, I'm not sure if they will play your Megadeath album. 

For dinner we indulge in the FUMO- a pizza with goat cheese, cherry tomatoes, capers, red onion and salmon. The combination was unique to me and so delicious. We met the owner Ari, who was very friendly. Nice to have a pizza joint that you are anxious to go back to. 

So park in the shopping center and find your way back to Falora. :D

First time here ... Grew up in this neighborhood and never tried it until today.. Just left the gym and was looking for something tasty but no too heavy.  Owner told me to try the chicken cheesesteak with shrimp and spinach and fried onions.  It was MADD good especially with the sauce that comes on the side.  I will definitely give this place another try.

Budweiser is an American icon and makes one of the most popular beers out there in many forms. I have partaken of my share over the years and now have taken a shine to the Bud Light Lime brand for my thirst quenching go to in the hot summer months. Nothing tastes as good after a lawn mowing. Almost makes me look forward to mowing the lawn sometimes.  

Budweiser stands for America and America stands for Budweiser. Cheers!

Just like John L H before me today Yelp removed my review for some reason so I'm back to put my vote in for a true American icon bucket list place. 

If you whine about this place then I laugh in your general direction. Either you think your too good or hungover is my guess although this is a great after partying place pick me up. Coffee and sugar! 

Been here countless times and the Cafe Au Lait is still one of my favorite cups of joe. I measure all other Au Laits against this one. And the beignets will ALWAYS leave you sporting some white powder. 

The atmosphere is bustling and jazzy and if you are looking for 5 star service stay home. It is part of the charm here. 

Right on the river and across from Jackson Square it is perfectly located and deserves 6 stars. The romance of New Orleans is in this little area far away from the stench and filth of Bourbon. 

A must visit. Trust me.

I reviewed my previous review when I saw one of friends visited and was surprised at my score being only 3 star here. Not ready to go 5 star yet but after a few more visits after my first review I certainly can say with certainty we got us a winner here. Son loved the burgers, even for breakfast and I stick with eggs. 

We got in the habit of paying it forward here, especially around the holidays to continue a  Waffle House tradition. 

Will stop in again sometime when we hit the area.

Dots hits the spot. So stop at Dots. Pick it up and trot.

A little or a lot of just about everything food here. We ate a hot cheesesteak and I do mean hot meat and  pepper sandwich here at one stand and had to hightail it over to the ice cream stand to tame the flames. Great spot to people watch, shop and get your eats and drinks on. 

Highly recommend this stop on your downtown Philly tour.

The food was not good. I was really surprised this place got such great reviews. The food isn't ok, it's actually bad. Bad flavor pairings, mushy bread. Worst than bad bar food. I'm definitely disappointed I spent so much on food I didn't enjoy. I'd rather eat at Applebee's and I haven't eaten there in 13 years. I will never eat here again. The drinks are good though.

There's not much I can add to the 2,000+ glowing reviews of the hot chicken here. The crispy exterior, the moist and succulent interior, and the great flavor despite the heat index, all make this gut busting treat worth the wait in long lines. 

For a side, you just can't go wrong with the pimento mac and cheese. Since you get two sides with your chicken, let the second one be the cool cole slaw. You may need it after a few bites of the "hot" and "damn hot" (those are spice levels) varieties of hot chicken. 

Make sure you save room for dessert, for the banana pudding here is some of the best I've ever had. The rich, velvety pudding is strewn with crunchy nilla wafers and topped with a light and fluffy meringue. 

This chicken dinner most certainly is a winner!

I had no idea who Chef Maneet Chauhan was until I first dined at this restaurant, but I'm now a fan. People who are fixated on "traditional" and "authentic" Indian food may not like this, but it really is the creative spin on Indian recipes that has me enamoured with the menu here. 

In keeping with the trend at most modern Indian restaurants around the US, the appetizers here are much more interesting than the main dishes. The naanzanella salad combines the heat and tartness of green chutney with the sweetness of lychees and strawberries; the creaminess of the yogurt dressing comes together with the crunchiness of the chana jor garam to create a textural delight. The bone marrow, served with naan "crostini" has a tasty tamarind glaze, and is covered with tender pulled beef shank. 

The hot chicken pakora is, perhaps, the only item I would probably not order again. The ghost pepper sauce is an instrument of self-torture.

The star menu item, of course, is a dessert! The gulab jamun cheesecake is everything I had ever hoped for in a sweet dish. Slices of gulab jamun are embedded within and strewn on top of the creamy New York style cheesecake. This has to be among the top 5 desserts I've had in the past decade.

It wouldn't be fair to compare the offerings at Yats to Cajun food in Louisiana or even Texas, but for Cajun / Creole fare in Indiana, it is pretty good. Set up like a fast food restaurant, you seat yourself, place your order and pay at the counter, and they bring your food out on disposable plates. 

The crawfish chili cheese etouffee was tasty and had a nice kick, but there were literally three pieces of crawfish in it. The chicken maque choux was nice and creamy, but was a tad too sweet. 

The menu is updated daily on a chalk board, and the service is cordial. A perfectly A-OK experience that I wouldn't mind repeating if I were in the area again.

I generally avoid restaurants on Bourbon Street, but Saints and Sinners has a very interesting version of crawfish pie, which keeps drawing me back. It really is a crawfish risotto sanswiched between puff pastry shells. Unfortunately, consistency of quality seems to be an issue here. While I have thoroughly enjoyed the crawfish pie on most of my visits, my most recent experience was not as good. The kitchen seemed to have gone overboard with the seasoning, rendering the dish overly salty, and the quantity of crawfish was less generous than usual. 

The crawfish mac and cheese is rich and tasty, the crowd is interesting, and the service is gracious and attentive. 

In terms of its interior decor, it seems like Saints and Sinners is trying to be a couple of very different things all at once. On the one hand, it claims to hearken back to the days when men went to bordellos to seek carnal pleasures (the walls showcase all of the gaudiness of a classical brothel, and there even is a stripper pole in the dining area!); on the other hand, it also is a sports bar with large TV screens showing football games. I wonder if I'm the only one who finds the two concepts (adult entertainment and sports) mutually incompatible.

I continue to go back, hoping each time to catch them on a "hit" day, rather than on a "miss" day with respect to the preparation of their crawfish pie.

At the risk of sounding like a big city snob, I will state that I would never have expected to find such fantastic Sichuan food in suburban Pennsylvania. King of Prussia seems to have every single chain restaurant I know of, and most of these are in or around the King of Prussia Mall. Hidden away in an unremarkable shopping plaza is Pin Wei, the rightful claimant of cliched titles such as "hidden gem" and "best-kept secret". 

The food is numbingly spicy and full of deliciously complex flavors. The Chengdu prawns and the dry pot rabbit are easily my favorite dishes. The Xinjiang chicken has a relatively low heat index, and is a hearty stew consisting of chicken and potatoes. It is from the Uyghur part of northwestern China, and is an amalgamation of Turkic and Sichuan culinary styles. 

Service is polite and attentive, but not overly convivial, which is perfectly fine by me. If you're anywhere within thirty miles of King of Prussia, I would recommend Pin Wei over any other restaurant near you.

Trenasse was the reason for my recent trip to New Orleans. Until recently, the Louisiana Crawfish Pie was offered only on Wednesdays as a lunch special. My previous trips to NOLA had all been weekend trips, so I had not been able to try the crawfish pie here. I planned this particular trip, flying in on Tuesday night, specifically so I could be in New Orleans on a Wednesday and come to Trenasse for their crawfish pie. I came in on Wednesday only to find out that this much coveted and once evasive dish is now available every night on the dinner menu, and a mini version of it is available on the daily happy hour menu (3PM to 6PM). Now I can have this piece of deliciousness on my future weekend trips too!

The crawfish pie really is the best I've ever had. Flaky crust filled with a spicy and creamy pepperjack cheese sauce and a generous quantity of crawfish, served on a bed of grits. This dish alone merits five stars. The other dishes were good, but completely eclipsed by the scrumptiousness of the crawfish pie. 

I've already planned my next trip to NOLA; the Louisiana crawfish pie Trenasse will have to be my first meal (and, perhaps, my last) on each trip!

I've eaten at Datz before in tampa but it was only once and a very long time ago. So this was essentially a new experience for me. We decided that it would be a good idea to have 9 of us come here for a family day. The table was LOADED with food. One thing I love and hate about Datz is they do NOT do small portions. For the price and what you get 10/10 worth it. But also for some of us at the table we are plain people and for what it's worth they worked with our dietary needs very well! For the rest of us who were willing to be brave, this menu offered multiple things to try that may be outside of the realm of norm. From donut burgers and burgers with fried mac n cheese as the bun. We will be coming here again maybe with more of an appetite.

Thanks, Pod, for making eating here such a delight for a vegan like me! I am so happy with the amount of choices that I can make on the menu, and the fact that they will make a few things vegan for me upon request! 

When I ate here a couple of weeks ago, I told my server I was vegan, so she made sure to veganize my side order of roasted asparagus (I think it normally has fish sauce in it or something). It was quite delicious, as was the Vegan Stephen sushi. I almost sent it back because I thought it was fish when it arrived. The tomato looks suspiciously like raw salmon! But, no, all vegan here, and full of fresh vegetables and stuffed with tempura'd veggies. Delicious! 

For lunch today, I decided to go with an old standby: tofu lettuce wraps. These are very decadent. Deep fried tofu in a sweet and savory Asian sauce, with sprouts and onions, a side of peanutty sauce and some fresh butter lettuce leaves. I love that you can roll them up yourself. Fun lunch. And delicious. Thanks, Pod!

I'm definitely going to be sad to leave behind the very vegan-friendly Bacio, when I move away from the area. For now, this sweet little BYO is just a 15 minute drive from us and we will take advantage of it as much as possible. 

On my first trip here, the very friendly waiter told us that basically everything on the menu could be made vegan. I'm definitely going to make my way through the entire menu eventually. For our first meal here, we each started with the arugula salad with pomegranate dressing and fresh apples, hold the cheese. It was fantastic. For my main dish, I ordered the veganized sweet potato gnocchi. It wasn't really gnocchi and it was a bit on the soggy side but the taste was pretty good and their homemade sauce was fantastic. On my second trip, we each had the vegan caeser which was probably the best caeser salad I've had anywhere. I decided to order the veganized eggplant parmesan. This time, my main dish was superb. It took a little extra time as the chef explained that he had to make my dish from scratch in order to make it vegan. The cheese on top was Daiya mozzerella, which is by far the best vegan brand of cheese out there. My husband ordered the fresh spaghetti, but I'm pretty sure it wasn't homemade pasta, which was kind of a bummer. We finished off our meal with a couple of delectable vegan cannolis, even though I was busting at the seams.

I love this place: love the staff, love the food, love the atmosphere, love the fact that it's BYO. We'll be back. Soon.

At a donut shop where the focus is on innovative ingredients, it's surprising that my favorite was the simple honey almond. I sampled all nine donuts on the menu. After one bite of each, I had a sugar high for hours. The honey drenched donut was by far the best tasting of the bunch. A distant second was the hot and fresh Indian spiced donut. As far as I know, Philly doesn't have any real donut shops that serve them fresh out of the fryer. 

The demand for this place has made for long lines and early sell outs. If you manage to get there in time, I'd suggest ordering a couple of the honey almond donuts and a hot coffee, which is also delightfully rich and not at all acidic.

If you want an excellent vegetarian or vegan meal for a great value, drive out to Southampton for Blue Sage. I can't believe it took me this many years to finally check this place out. I called them last night at around dinner and couldn't get through a few times (got the busy signal). Finally got through and they were able to squeeze us in for a reservation for two at 8pm. The restaurant was completely full, aside from our little table, when we arrived, and the pace never slowed. The secret's out, apparently.

There are only a few items on the menu that are strictly vegan, however they can make any of their items 100% vegan if you ask (they call it "dairy free" instead but I guess they don't use eggs in general). Before we got our started, our red wine bottle was opened (BYO!) and we were given a small basket of delicious chewy sourdough bread and a small dish of spicy bean dip. We ordered the corn and avocado Tartare to start and it was fantastic. Loads of corn, diced avocado and tomatoes in a sort of savory salsa was served in a large cocktail glass surrounded by what tasted like homemade taro chips. We ate every last kernel and basically licked the plate. Next, I had the Pan Bagno sandwich for my main dish. I could barely eat half of it, it was so gigantic, and at around $12, a real steal. The chickpea cakes were similar to tofu in consistency which was surprising and nice. The "artichoke-oil cured tomato tapenade" on the fresh crusty, toasted baguette was wonderful. It was served with a very fresh salad of bitter greens, almonds and sliced grapes. I had a couple bites of that, but I was getting pretty stuffed. We decided to opt out of dessert. Two out of four of the desserts were vegan, and sounded really great, but we just couldn't manage to eat another bite and we were both bringing doggie bags home already. 

Our total bill for an appetizer, a sandwich and an entree (my husband ordered the pumpkin risotto) was around $40. Seriously. It would have been less had he ordered a sandwich, salad or any of the other less expensive items on the menu. After we got used to some of the more expensive veggie restaurants, this place was such a breath of fresh air! I think they could easily expand as they were doing such brisk business the night we were there. Our waitress and the entire staff could not have been nicer or more helpful. I look forward to more meals here.

After seeing many people post about Nudo House over the past few days I decided to go for lunch today and bring 4 coworkers.  When we first arrived there was a line out of the first door, however we were pleasantly surprised when we realized it was moving very fast.  It took less than 5 minutes to place our order.
To get a feel for the new restaurant I decided to try the Classic Nudo and Crab Rangoon.  After ordering I grabbed a drink and found an empty table.  The staff were very fast to clean up tables after people left so finding one was not an issue.  Once we sat down it took around 10 minutes for our food to start arriving.
My Crab Rangoon arrived first.  Unfortunately it was a bit cold, but it tasted extremely good.  I really enjoyed the fact that there were chunks of crab (not sure if it is real or imitation) inside of the cream cheese.
My ramen was brought out about 5 minutes after my crab Rangoon.  It was extremely hot, and extremely tasty.  I thought there was a generous amount of meat inside of the Ramen, and the perfect amount of noodles.  The flavor profile of the broth was very complex and in my opinion that is the mark of good ramen.
I found the prices here to be a bit odd.  I thought $12 for ramen was a very competitive price, especially considering the quality of the ramen.  I thought the Crab Rangoon was overpriced a bit though at $4 for 3 pieces.  I think I would recommend lowering the price a bit or increasing the size to 4 or 5 pieces.  While it was very good I have a hard time paying over a dollar per piece.
Needless to say I really enjoyed my meal here.  Not only was the food great but the staff was very friendly.  The only complaint I have from my visit revolves around the cold Crab Rangoon.   I have no doubt that if I would have brought that issue up with an employee they would have fixed it.  I give Nudo 4.5 out of 5 stars, and since I round up a full 5 out of 5 star rating.

I was really sad when India Palace closed their old location.  I really enjoyed eating a good Indian buffet while overlooking the airport.  The new location is right next to another Indian restaurant that I enjoy and I am worried only one of the two will survive.
When I went here for lunch they were absolutely packed.  I once had to wait almost 5 minutes in line to walk down the buffet line.  I thought the selection was pretty good, I wish they included Mango Lassi like a few other buffets in the area do, but that is just me being picky.
The old location had a really good dinner.  I am hoping this is true at this new location as well.  My old go to dinner order was the Goat Pickle.

I have never had a bad brunch at The Blue Duck.  Not only is the food good but the staff have always treated us great.  The Duck Gees Benedict is my go to order here, however I also really enjoy the burgers.  This last visit I opted to ignore the dessert and order a blueberry muffin instead.  That was an amazing idea, it was the best Blueberry Muffin I have ever had.
I really need to try them out for dinner one of these days.

The food at lolita is good, but good food should be the norm at a restaurant especially when you are paying around $25+ per entree. There are other things about this restaurant that makes me not want to return:  

We arrived at the restaurant around 6pm when it was completely empty, except for 1 table. The servers and hostess clearly saw that we had entered the restaurant, but took all the time in the world to greet us. When we told them that we were a party of four and waiting for 2 more guests, the hostess told us that it was their "policy" they could not sit us until all members of the party arrived. So my husband and I stood amongst the empty tables, annoyed with the hostess's attitude. 

When we were finally seated and read the menu, we noticed that the restaurant also had a "policy" of $18 food minimum per guest. On top of everything else, this restaurant is cash only.  Considering that each entree was $20+, this policy was obviously not that difficult to meet. But what if a customer was not in the mood to order an entree and just wanted an appetizer? 

A good restaurant should not place restrictions on how a customer should spend their money.

Definitely a fan of this new brunch spot. The space is large and open with simple decor. I ate here on a weekday and there were lots of tables, but I imagine it gets crowded on the weekends since it is in a great location.

Everyone working here was very friendly and service was great. The menu is large and has a wide range of things to pick from. They also had a few specials of the day. 

Everything sounded good, but I went with a mushroom and goat cheese omelette. It was delicious and overflowing with lots of seasoned mushrooms and cheese. Eggs were fluffy and well made. I also really liked the potato hash and side salad it came with, which was well dressed. I got a side of bacon which was really delicious- I think it was caramelized with sugar and I'm here for it. My friend also enjoyed her beet and gouda salad. 

Prices were reasonable and a perk is that it's BYO and they take credit cards! Much better than some of the other brunch places in the area. I'll definitely be back!
Always have been overpriced and arrogant. I've tried them 3 times now and I'm done trying. Also, $40 minimum on cards at the bar is insane.

Trust the nose!

During my Reno trip, I stumbled into Salty-Savory-Sweet Spices and Teas by chance. With my first step into this quaint family owned shop, I was hypnotized with the fragrance of spices and teas. Wall to wall jars filled with every kind of spice, mixes and teas with the majority of it made at their shop. 

The owners, Lindy and Brent were so helpful and friendly. Since I've been practicing my grilling skills at home, I knew finding some dry rubs would enhance the flavors of my meals. I could have bought half of the store but decided on these mixtures:

Kansas City BBQ
Smoked Peppercorn and Sage Rub
Aglio Olio E Pepperoncino
Rosemary Garlic Rub
French Lavender

These mixture could be purchased by pre-made jars or weighed by the ounce. Since I didn't want to purchase too much, I had her package a few ounces in the baggies to enjoy at home and gave away as gifts.

The personalized service outstanding and I look forward to visiting their shop to pick up more rubs on my next trip to Reno!

If I could, I'd give this place ZERO stars for a number of reasons.

On my initial visit, I came here before dinner time and decided on the regular size poke bowl $10.50 which included 3 proteins, base, side, sauce and toppings. The size of the bowl was clearly smaller than the other poke places I've tried throughout the West Coast. It was obvious the owners were purposely using a smaller container to restrict the amount per serving. I found it to be insulting.

For the base, you can select from white rice, sushi rice, brown rice or salad. My bowl had the half salad and sushi rice which was a poorly executed given the delicate flavors it is known for. 

From the protein choices, I picked two servings of the salmon and one of the tunas. These cuts could have fooled me because the tuna did not have a fresh flavor and the quantity was very skimpy.

They did a good job of adding your bill quickly by charging extra for crabmeat, avocado, masago and seaweed salad. The young guy who helped me didn't seem too eager to help either.

What's so odd is these bowls are usually filling but when I finished it here and was still hungry. Because of the lack of food, I was very troubled and decided not to return because I did not think it justified the cost, quality and the amount of food.

But .... it doesn't stop here.

Since I decided that I would never to eat here again, I came back to try their boba milk tea on a different day, and that was the worst experience ever. 

The boba drinks has it's own ordering counter and other people and myself stood in line waiting to place our order. A female employee from PokeMee had to run over and take all of our orders and then return back. It lead to only one girl who was making the drinks. When I finally got up to order my large rose milk tea $5.26, I had a couple questions and the staff was clueless on all her drinks. She had to ask the other staff who didn't speak English and at that point I knew this was going down hill very quickly. 

After waiting over 20 minutes, the drink was no where in sight and the people in front of me who were waiting didn't get their drinks either. At that point, my time was lost and I went to the poke cashier and asked for a refund. He shrugged his shoulders as if I was speaking a different language. Another girl stepped in to assist with the drinks which they should have done way earlier. I asked for a refund and instead she asked if I would prefer to upsize my drink. I declined because I didn't think it was fair for me to get my drink before the others who were ahead of me and insisted on my refund. She said her manager wasn't around and couldn't authorize a $5.26 refund. You're kidding me?? Finally, the manager walks in and I requested my refund due to the poor service and basically wasting my time for a drink that was nowhere insight.

He said his staff are students and it's finals time so he needs to hire more people. Okay, I'm totally for employing students because I was once a student myself but running a business you need to cover all your bases and that means having a sense of quality control.

Disappointing from first to last experience. Small bowl size, stingy protein servings, extra costs, staff not able to converse with diners left a horrible taste in my mouth.

Oh boy, a banh mi joint in Norristown?! GTFO! I've been hype about this place since I drove by it the first time months ago!

So of course on their opening day I bought 3 $5 footlongs (the special for the soft opening). One was the classic, another was the pork banh mi and the last was the meatball banh mi. 

Yes, I tasted all of them within minutes and my conclusion is: All of the sandwiches were super delicious and flavorful and the bread was on point. The only thing I'd probably want them to add is a bit more meat and a lot more daikon and veggies. The bread to meat ratio was a bit off to me...there was more bread than meat but then again, this could 100% be attributed to the fact that I'm a fatty patty. 

As far as the interior goes, it was spacious and modern however the walls lacked decoration but I'm sure they'll be putting things up in no time. 

Seeing that today was their soft opening, I'm really looking forward to coming back here in the near future to see what else they have in store and of course I'd rather drive 15 minutes vs. 40 minutes into Philly to fill my viet hoagie cravings.
No website to compare rise in prices. Burger was undercooked and waitress short with us.  New place in congested area with less parking. I'll go else where. Never again!

I have visited this restaurant before and I wanted to give it a better review. My husband ordered the roast beef sandwich and it was very dry. When he asked for more gravy he was told the chef doesn't make it that way and they don't have any gravy. WTH? I ordered a pizza with onions,mushrooms, and salami and it was oversaturated with onions and little sauce. The service was slow and we left terribly disappointed.

I don't know if we will return.

5 Stars for what it is, and 5 Stars for what it's going to be. Does that mean I can give 10?

For the longest time I followed that the owner of South Philly Tap Room was going to open up a cafe that hook up delectable coffee offerings from one of my favorites, Counter Culture (http://mealticket.blogs.citypaper.net/blogs/mu/2009/05/05/first-look-at-brewultimo-coffee/). and even better was the fact that it wasn't only going to offer one of my favorite vices, it was going to offer TWO of them by doubling over as a beer store as soon as it procured a liquor license (http://ultimocoffee.wordpress.com/2009/01/23/meal-ticket-round-two-keeping-tabs-on-brewultimo-coffee/). And while one of those goals is still a work in progress, the coffee shop is very much alive and might just be one of the best in the city.

as soon as I walked up one of the South Philly roads that is less traveled for me and saw my destination, I became enamored by it's outdoor seating and garage door that opened to combine the outside with the in. the incredible decor expanded with church pews and antique window fixtures hanging indoors. I also made note of the many refrigerator units that will one day hold mass quantities of delectable beer.

The iced chai that I initially order made for the perfect relaxed wake up call during a hot day. and the coffee that I ordered afterwards embodied a dark richness to it's body that was fully accentuated by the drip method that they utilize. and the lemon square that I ordered along with it was sheer perfection. 

Overall the staff were friendly and extremely accommodating, and the atmosphere made for the perfect environment to have our book club in. It looks like Ultimo is a place that I'll be visiting for a long while to come!

My name is Bill McThrill Esquire the Fifth (well at least some of that isn't a nom de plume). Yet  anytime I step foot into Butcher and Singer I can't help but be whisked away into the time of Don Draper and the era of Mad Men.

Seriously though how priceless is the interior and every step of the service in this piece of luxury? If you think for a second that you've experienced a second of the classy high life of Philly without stepping in and sampling the meat mansion that is Butcher; then you'd best be thinking again fool. Although it does manage to deliver just fine when I walk in on the business casual front during lunch time for that extra gold star.

But the main purpose of this silly review is to cover the one key ingredient of Butcher and Singer that no other piece of the Philly luxury delivers so successfully. The Butcher Burger is so simply done, yet executed with a simple (read: not overboard) amount of the finest ingredients to make it perfectly flawless. And that makes this top of the line steakhouse (I actually like a Starr restaurant?) one of the best places to grab a burger in Philly!

**Disclaimer** - This review update has nothing to do with blogs that I could care little about, How I feel about credit minimums (no sir I don't like them), or how a certain worker composed himself on a certain fustercluck of a talk thread that I'd rather not look back on (And for the record he definitely could of composed himself a WHOLE HELL of a lot better).

You see this update is about everything that I look for personally when I look for a good coffeehouse. When I look for a good coffeehouse I search a good vibe and atmosphere that perfect for getting some work done, an impressive variety of drink offerings, delicious food offerings, board games to play and house books to read, and a variety of fantastic art on the wall (and there's always bonus points for a cute house dog). And when I came back to Chapterhouse for Book Club I got to revisit how much of these things it has to offer, and that's exactly why I enjoy it thoroughly (too bad the dog wasn't there!).

And for what it's worth, while I'll agree in a heartbeat that Christopher needs to step away from things like talk threads so that Shannon can be the voice of mediation when a situation arises (just saying since she definitely does the better job of it), I will stand by the fact that I have had good service from him in the past. He goes the extra mile by making sure that your not allergic to any ingredient in the more involved drinks, and goes the extra mile with his preparation. And while he might of seemed a little more distant every time he heard the mention of Yelp (not to say I don't particularly blame him given the fustercluck that I'd rather not talk about) during the Book Club, he didn't miss a beat. And it is things like that that I appreciate.

When I first heard about Loco Pez I was picturing a fine lavish cantina that delivered fresh and delicious tacos and guacamole with strong margaritas. But walking in and seeing a chill neighborhood dive bar that delivered all of those things made it even better!

From the crazy Pez dispenser collection that the Fish is partly named for and the eclectic art throughout, to a solid brunch offering and dollar taco night, Loco Pez is a fun and inexpensive occasion every time that you go. And that's why the cash only bar has been given the designation of being a perfect cheap date location on more than one occasion (http://philly.thedrinknation.com/articles/read/6461-Cheap-Date-Loco-Pez-in-Fishtown).

The bar is fully loaded with plenty of local beers on draft and in bottles and cans. And it offers 25 tequilas making making it a perfect spot for fresh made cocktails with Latin flare. As a result of this its a given that they make some damn good margaritas, but I quickly learned to prefer going on the road to El Dorado with its Espolon Blanco, Mezcal Joven, muddled grapefruit, habanero, lime. but there's also a couple of Sangrias, mimosas and bloody Mary's for brunch, and Micheladas for the perfect beer cocktail with a kick.

With so many taco, burrito, enchilada, and quesadilla options available its near impossible to choose what you order. especially when you add inexpensive Americano goods like a chili dog and burger with waffle fries into the mix. but with options like chicken, shrimp, fish, seitan & spinach, and soy chorizo or regular w/ potato to fill your order with; your belly is happy no matter what you choose. Especially if you get a side of ultra fresh guacamole with chips.

Although it's been a good couple of years since I've eaten a cheesesteak I figured I know enough about these places to get some good facts across. so here goes:

1) Unless a long and obnoxious line takes you to a roller coaster, the concert of a lifetime, or a truly epic event, it probably isn't going to be worth waiting in. So if you see a long line for a sandwich don't bother, ESPECIALLY if you're waiting for this pile of junk.

2) Most real Philadelphians find wiz to be quite disgusting. Hell it's probably toxic in nature. Fortunately though if it's a legit cheesesteak establishment you should be able to order yours "wit" American or provolone cheese.

3) Contrary to popular cheesesteak ordering belief, "wit wiz" actually isn't English. So will you please stop being an ass clown Joey Vento?

4) Fact of the matter is that unless we're drunk enough to the point that we end up regretting our food choices the next morning, most real Philadelphians don't bother with Geno's or Pat's. Go to Tony Lukes, Steaks On South, John's Roast Pork, hell ANY other sandwich shop here that serves a cheesesteak, and you're bound to find something a lot better. And you might not even have to bother with a line or a server with bad attitude while you do so.

so do yourself a favor and don't believe the hype that comes with this place.

An incredibly solid four for now, but I can see them very quickly getting that extra star once they get the credit card system up and running (tomorrow!) and the staff overcomes the first weekend hype and starts to find their footing a little better. But holy hell is P.Y.T. quite the happening burger joint to go to!

If you're on the Mojito, Paperstreet, or any other mailer that Tommy Up sends out; or you're an avid reader of Philebrity, then just like me you have been dying to sink your teeth into a P.Y.T. Burger for a good 2 months now. So when I finally got the word I've been waiting for that it was opening this weekend I was ready to go with anticipation, but decided to wait a bit and check out the Sundae party that the Piazza hooks up (not enough dancing!). It was still so packed that it took a few attempts to score an outdoor table. But the fifth time was the charm and we had the chance to enjoy a double dose of DJs, order up a round of burgers, and some ALCOHOLIC MILKSHAKES!

To quote Jules Winnfield from Pulp Fiction "Mmm-mmmm. That is a tasty burger.". And the P.Y.T. Burger was very worthy of that moniker. It was a good sized patty that was fully loaded with bacon, lettuce tomato, American cheese, and special sauce on Potato bread. It came with a side of chips and a pickle spear, and I'm very happy to report that it was only $8. BUT you can double up to the Royale and have it with 2 patties for $10, or TRIPLE up to the the Big Mic and have 3 patties for $12. you can also do a side of fries for as little as $2, and a side of onion rings for as little as $3. so P.Y.T. hardly breaks the bank, and since it stands for Pick Your Toppings they give you PLENTY to choose from. of course you can also go veggie with 2 different veggie burger options, switch it up to their grilled cheese, or do some lobster fish sticks!

Their Milkshake brings all the boys to the yard, and that's right McThrill actually went there for a review! But they were so damn good that they were worth reliving a horrible song over. my friend ordered a milkshake that blended chocolate ice cream with Patron! and I ordered up the Double Espresso Milkshake which blended espresso ice cream, with fresh espresso beans, and espresso vodka! It's such a simple and incredible idea, that I'm seriously surprised that no other spot in Philly (or anywhere else?) does it, and it was well worth the $10. you can also get all your standard milkshake favorites for $5.

Congratulations Tommy Up because you definitely have a place that lived up to the hype considerably, and was well worth the wait. And it definitely goes without saying that P.Y.T. is a place that I plan to hit up on a regular basis. Nicely done indeed!

I came, I saw, I had a whole room doing gang vocals to "Livin' on a Prayer" by Bon Jovi!

For a fun filled karaoke party with plenty of sushi and shochu it doesn't get much better than Fuji Mountain. The party room well accommodated our party of 20+ and came with comfortable red couches, good lighting, its own bathroom, and a nice sized video screen. Along with plenty of shochu and sake options the drink menu yielded a decent variety of wines, cocktails, and beers like Kirin Ichiban and Dogfish Head 60 Min IPA for decent prices. And the food menu touted the decent sized portions of the sushi, dumpling, and noodle dishes that you'd expect.

The one issue I could give was that the karaoke book was listed by song title instead of artist, making them harder to navigate through. I was also sad to see some essential songs that you'd expect to see in such a book like "White Wedding" by Billy Idol and "Psycho Killer" by Talking Heads missing. And while it was completely weird and perfectly random, I did love the odd vignettes that played during the songs, and wondered what romantic yet tragically awkward situations we could lead the characters in them through. 

Whether you're someone who just likes singing along to the chorus with a bunch of people, or you prefer to belt out the high notes of "Don't Stop Believing" by Journey (guilty!), Fuji Mountain is a whole lot of fun.
