Mike Solo,the people behind Bodhi Coffee, and Felicia D. joining forces to make this place possible? The Queen of Awesomeness holding it down at the cash register and welcoming you as you enter? Hell with people like this behind it FD could peddle snake oil and it would still seem like a revelation!

But fortunately for all mankind FD peddles something so much better than snake oil. We're talking a custom blended coffee from PT's out of Topeka (thanks for the info Blake!). Combine it with fried chicken recipes that The Colonel couldn't even dream about, and add in fancy donuts made by ROBOTS; and you have yourself the new trifecta of glory!

Like many, many people I knew the bulk of this months beforehand (and had even planned to camp out for the opening at one point. Fail!). But upon reading tweet after Facebook post about product selling out as fast as lightening, I figured that it would be best to wait a bit so I could truly savor the moment.

It finally came today and the queen was as awesome as ever when I entered. Since it was one of moments where I was tempted to order one of everything I opted to just go for a 1/2 dozen of the fancy donuts so I could try one of each and have a bit leftover. And pending tomorrows breakfast (or the aftermath of this review if I can't hold back temptation) it just might have been the best worst decision ever.

Between the glaze, the freshness, and the un-overbearing filling inside each bite is sheer perfection. And there's no Dunkin necessary because each bite is pure flavor country. Both the Key Lime and the Blood Orange yielded the necessary fruit flavor, while the Chocolate Raspberry was the perfect taste of decadence. But the Nutella-Tehina Pomegranate was the clear winner for offering the perfect combination of each flavor sensation.

Believe the hype, because after just a couple of weeks Federal Donuts has more than earned its spot towards greatness!

For fanciful yet unpretentious dining, and a restaurant with a well rounded bar selection and an impressive selection of cheeses on the Main Line; It really doesn't get much better than Savona. I learned that before but it took a successful Mother's Day brunch to rekindle that memory.

Tucked away in an unsuspecting corner of Gulph Mills Road, Savona is an intriguing restaurant in an older building with an updated a modernized decor, especially were it counts in the dining room. the bar featured an amicable selection of brews from the likes of Dogfish Head, Yards, and Ommegang; as well a a satisfactory cocktail list. But in the tradition of brunch I opted for a Grey Goose Bloody Mary which yielded a subtle spicy kick.

Whether it was a cream of goat cheese in a crimini mushroom soup, pecorino romano in a risotto with bacon, or a parmesean reggiano melt in a Tuscan white bean soup; I was really in awe of the ways that cheese was utilized in the menu. And they succeeded in the rare task of opening a monger like me up to some previously unheard of varieties like Creme Royale and a smooth but slightly salty triple creme goat cheese that I really wish I could remember the name of. Overall the farm to table food menu was very thought out and featured some well played twists. The aforementioned mushroom soup might have been the best that I've ever had. And my eggs Benedict with asparagus and a smoked Scottish salmon was one of those rare egg dishes that had me wanting to lick the yolk off my plate. and my mom and dad were satisfied with their blue claw crab scrambled eggs.

Really the only flaw to this successful brunch was that it was a brunch menu that they only offered on special occasions like Mother's Day. But it definitely impressed me enough to check them out on a regular dinner or lunch. And they definitely have a variety of other special occasions like cooking classes and beer events.

1/2 burger and veggie burgers on Monday and Thursday!
Taco Tuesday!
Pierogie Wednesday!
$1 PBR pounders on Friday and Saturday nights!
Crafts day and other theme events on Sundays!

Tattooed Mom is indeed a bar that gives you an abnormal excuse to be happy everyday of the week! Grant it Sugar Moms does too, But I feel that Tattooed mom does it with less smoke and pretentiousness. It also doesn't do it in a basement and brings out a better crowd.

I should have bought that up in the last review. But hanging out with 20 plus of the Yelp crew, eating Unicorn cake, basking in all the incredible figurines and artwork, and encountering an incredible server named Bobby has helped me up my love for Tattooed Mom.

While you can definitely do it there, this isn't the cafe that I would go to for coffee and getting work done. they do have an abundance of Lavazza coffee, but I've always found there something to be off about the brand (their better for espresso). And aside from the outside seating arrangement that gives you the chance to watch people playing in a park, and fools getting ready to line up at Geno's, I found the seating to be kind of scattered. But this is by far the place to go for espresso, dessert, chocolate, and chillaxing outside the Italian Market.

When I first came in I saw Rene whipping up a drinking chocolate concoction for a customer that was the stuff of decadence. It was filled with so many different varieties of chocolate syrup that I lost track, but It also had some raspberry amaretto for good measure. it definitely looked beyond impressive. When my turn came I was craving a Canolli even though I was in a French cafe, and holy crap did I get one. the inside was a traditional blend of ricotta and marscapone, and the outside was uncharacteristically drizzled with cocoa, chocolate syrup, honey, pistachios, cinnamon, and then some. The traditionist inside of me might of been calling blasphemy, But the rest of me was greedily devouring it without paying him any mind. I also quickly noticed that Rene was a friendly and entertaining person to watch while he prepared your order.

Upon checking out their website I'm learing that they make their Tea using a syphon, offer good tips on how to make espresso, and offer a decadent sounding Cappuccino Brulee! So apparently I have a lot more reasons to come here.

Since I'm living in West Philly I never thought I would ever consider making the effort to hop on the trolley for another Ethiopian Restaurant. after all I'm living in Philly's mecca of Ethiopian food! But I stopped in Almaz to give their Hot Chocolate a try, and I might just be tempted to become a turncoat. 

I made note of it's inexpensive food options, and it's superior coffee varieties. And If I didn't stop in for brunch at a spot earlier I would have definitely stuck around longer to try them out. But the service here was unbelievable. the people who worked there really had a lasting knowledge of who a lot of their customers were (Soon I will be among them). and made a point to keep anyone satisfied even if they were 
just stopping in for a cup of coffee on the go. The hot chocolate was amazing. It might just be the best I've had in Philly (need to hit up Cafe Pier One again just to double check).

so to recap amazing service, inexpensive Ethiopian food, and incredible coffee options. throw in the free Wi-Fi, and sweet looking balcony spot that they have going and I'm sold!

Out of two experiences I've only been in for Happy Hour thus far. But its fairly easy to give 4 stars to one of the best happy hour deals in all of Philly.

Bru Craft & Wurst first had me intrigued with the solid beer menu, German influenced sausage menu, and close proximity to McGillan's. But it took a pre-gathering before the Scratch Biscuits Elite Event to get me down there. When we did I knew it was going to be for happy hour, but I had no idea that it would feature $4 drafts from some of the best breweries out there including Ommegang, Jolly Pumpkin, Firestone Walker, 2SP, plenty of German brews to go with the theme, and then some. Add in $5 for select wurst sandwiches and appetizers, and its pretty easy to satisfy your appetite while you're sampling some of the best beers out there.

Outside of happy hour its still pretty easy to delve into that near flawless beer list at a reasonable price for what your imbibing on. Plus you definitely want to savor starters like currywurst and bavarian pretzels with a smoked gouda fondue, small plates like mussels and short rib mac & cheese, and mains like doner kebab or a mixed wurst plate of 4 assorted sausages. Happy Hour has only given me the chance to chill barside and pick the brains of the spot on bartenders. But Bru also has enough room to fit roughly any sized party during its other not so crazy hours, touts and interesting decor, and has a pour your own beer system with a decent selection if you'd rather not feel overwhelmed by their epic list.

Philly is filled to the brim with standout BYOB restaurants that feature eclectic and elevated menus, but in the suburbs the options are few and far between thus making them harder to find.  But it was my dad who impressed me (I taught him well!) by finding this crown jewel of a BYOB in an unassuming Havertown neighborhood, and it was Edgewood that managed to deliver an impressive dinner for my mom's birthday.

The interior is roomy and comfortable decor with plenty of booths that can hold up to four. It also has an inviting decor with an open view that allows you to catch a glimpse of the kitchen staff at work. Upon arrival we were quickly welcomed, had our bottle of wine opened, and where presented with a menu of delectable options that were hard to choose from. while wild mushroom risotto fritters and and short rib flatbreads sounded like winning appetizers; we were instantly drawn to the cheese plate which featured brie, burrata, gorgonzola, and accompaniments like toasted almonds, fresh honey, and a delicious apple raisin chutney.

with options like porterhouse style lamb chops, southern fried chicken, jumbo lump crab cakes, and bacon wrapped filet, any entree is a good decision. But I was especially drawn to and ended up ordering right with the shrimp and crab scampi with angel hair pasta, roasted tomatoes, and baby spinach in a pinot grigio broth.Choosing dessert would have also proven difficult if they hadn't of featured a 3 for $20 dessert sampler. My folks were satisfied with their vanilla creme brulee and honey ricotta cheesecake, and I was especially tantalized by the molten chocolate lava cake with vanilla ice cream.

Overall Edgewood is a BYOB that can contend with those standout city ones. But it remaining on an unassuming suburban block gives it a solid hidden treasure status.

Hands down the best restaurant in the West Passyunk proper, even during these crazy Covid-19 times!

I kind of knew that before even setting foot outside of it (because of Covid-19) given the credibility of the couple owning it and the overall labor of passion that they put into their Mediterranean BYOB. If you know good greek food in Philadelphia from the past few years, then there's a very good chance that you savored the incredible food that Bobby Saritsoglou made at Opa. But when he stepped down from there in 2019 he did so to open his dream restaurant with his wife, who's a co-founder of one of my favorite places Philadelphia AIDS Thrift (https://www.phillymag.com/foobooz/2018/08/15/stina-bobby-saritsoglou/). And from the well rounded Mediterranean menu mostly made from the Morello Forni wood-burning oven they brought over from Italy, to the lavish interior filled with vintage art and tchotchkes, to how they try to give back to their surrounding community (https://www.phillymag.com/foobooz/2019/05/28/stina-restaurant-menu-pizza-south-philadelphia/) every inch of Stina houses their passion and it shows in the execution.

When I visited my cousin during a Labor Day weekend social distance rendezvous in Philly, I was surprised to see a reservation on Resy that fit our small group of people and was amped up to try it. And even though my very aloof group managed to double in size in happenstance during our commute, Stina was beyond accomodating and able to fit in all of us. The outdoor seating was cozy and perfect for a late summer evening and the cheap booze store across the street makes BYOB very doable when you don't properly plan for it.

When you encounter a menu like Stina's you find yourself enticed to order ALL THE THINGS! But we settled for and enjoyed sharing the following:

Fire roasted cauliflower: charred to perfection with Baharat spices and drizzled with an incredible tahini sauce.

Loukaniko sausage: Absolutely loved the traditional greek sausage, but gigandes beans slow-cooked in tomato and sunny side up egg that accompanied it also might have been the real Allstars of the dish which says something for the overall quality!

Spanish octopus: slow cooked for three hours, then served with an olive tapanade, almond romesco, black garlic purree. This dish might have just been the best one that I've had in all of 2020!

Spicy Sopresseta Pizza: When a restaurant imports a wood-fired oven imported from Italy for it, its a given that you need to try their pizza! and the spicy meat paired with the drizzled honey and semi-soft fiore di latte cheese was an absolute revelation!

One day I'll be able to visit and take in the restaurant's interior with all of its vintage art and many reclaimed wooden doors within it while enjoying a good meal. But until then it's a definite must for pick up and delivery the next time I'm in South Philly (the only options for now).

Sometimes its stupefying to believe that the original Foodery location is a place that I've been enjoying for 20 years now (and that it's been roughly 14 years ago since I reviewed it on here - https://www.yelp.com/biz/foodery-philadelphia). But in its multiple locations its definitely evolved from the tiny corner store that's a beer and sandwich haven, to several places that deliver the same in a much larger package.

But when it comes down to both deli counter and beer selection, the Roxborough location might just be my favorite, and not just because it also let me scoop out some popcorn to go during non-Covid-19 times.

Even in the slightly larger NoLibs location, past Foodery locations have boldly crammed specialty groceries, a deli counter, and fridges stocked with ALL THE BEERS into some seriously crammed situations. But that isn't a problem in this one which is by far the largest I've seen (without setting foot in the Phoenixville one yet). Because of that everything is placed in areas that make sense while also tossing in things like a section for large bottles, ALL THE SNACKS, and an impressive growler fill station.

My favorite sandwich is definitely the Diablo with its buffalo chicken, pepper jack cheese, avocado, and chipotle mayo that delivers a spicy kick that doesn't border on overkill. But I've also enjoyed the Hot Toastee with its tavern ham, swiss cheese, honey mustard, apple, and pecans on a toasted sourdough.

The main event by far is the epic beer coolers, and whether you're looking for hard to find imports, well-liked local brews, noteworthy seasonal brews, ciders and seltzers, hoppy beers, chocolate stouts, or other, you're bound to find it!

When Cherie was in town for a visit (McThrill Loves Lamp!) I just had to get together and catch up (And I still need to find Severa on here. I'm such a slacker!). And when she suggested meeting up and Farmicia I was doubly psyched because it was something that I've been meaning to do for ages (see the I'm a slacker part).

Dinner wasn't without it's flaws so I'll get those over with first. on the good they had a burger that could be worthy of rallying up another majestic orgy of burgers and came with farm fresh local bacon and cheddar cheese and was super sized alongside a fresh cut side of well proportioned fries. as you can imagine it would have been the stuff of sheer and absolute perfection.... If the bacon wasn't burnt around the edges. It would have been a contender for best burger I've ever had, if the mishandling of innocent bacon didn't leave me feeling a little hollow inside. For another considerable flaw while the one beer that I ordered was exceptional, the 2nd flying fish that I ordered flew the coup. it wasn't on the check either but still! lastly rather then come with a traditional kind of sauce that it usually does, the calamari came with a mix of Tabasco and ketchup, which was sort of odd.

The above are enough to merit 3 stars, however everything else was exceptional enough to the point that I can't grade below a 4 (And Aaron and Meredith call McThrill too nice yet again!). It had fresh baked bread from Metropolitan Bakery, and extra fresh coffee. It had a great selection of wines, specialty tonics, and beers, yet is cool enough to double over as a B.Y.O. Wine place every night. Even though he forgot my beer, our server was otherwise attentive and dead on with his recommendations. I came close to having what might have been the best burger I ever had (poor bacon!). the cheese plate and desserts where quite exceptional. and you could take home and eat the apple centerpieces! So overall Farmicia had enough for me to enjoy in all of the right places.

My first Fermentaria review came when it was still fairly new and going through some menu pains. After two years of living a block and a half away, 45 check ins at present date, and hosting a successful UYE within (Next one coming TBD Spring(ish) 2018!), its fair to say that I've been there enough to warrant a review update. But it took a weekend gathering with a group of other Yelpers, and taking a bite out of one of the best chicken sandwiches ever (!!!), to realize just how long overdue it was!

While the original menu I covered featured a number of the brilliant tacos that they still have today, it also had oysters and shared plates that just didn't fit the bill no matter how good they were. But since then they changed them up with delectable snacks like pork belly buns and braised beef empanadas, sabdwiches like a banh mi style veggie wrap and the best burger on the Main Line (with whisky dill pickles and candied bacon!), a killed brunch menu, and damn good fried chicken with pickled apple butter and chili honey! With incredible tacos like brussel sprouts with bacon jam and sriracha ranch dressing, and salmon with fried rice and orange ginger; they still very much manage to stay a main event!

Add in the forward thinking beer that they've always been known for, and the mad cap special beer releases that they throw, and Fermenteria is as good as always!

During my last review I failed to mention a lot of the food, which is a shame since it's probably my favorite thing about Ole. So considering I'll probably be devouring one of their epic sandwiches and enjoying one of their Iced teas (free refills!) before I take to the streets for First Friday, I figured I'd give it a noble do over.

I recommended the European Grilled Cheese Sandwich last time. And with with 4 different kinds of cheese melted down together it certainly doesn't disappoint ever. But they also have an amazing sandwich that hooked up brie with apples! and their chicken salad and tuna salad is pretty impressive in their own right. while you can choose between free chips or a salad to go with your meal, you'd be foolish not to go with the homemade Greek salad!

And to think all of this time I failed to realize that Ole was a La Colombe coffeehouse. But really that's OK to me, because that only makes it the most distinct and pleasant one of the bunch.

Thanks for the tip Meredith. HOLY CRAP does this place know how to make a sammich! they are hands down the best Jewish Deli in Philly and give great service every step of the way. and not only did the sandwich maker make my sammich to perfection, he was friendly and cool enough to tell me some things about stuff on my street that I had no idea about.

If you like your sammiches piled high with meat than this is by far the place for you. their catchphrase is "More Meat for Less Bread" and their dead on. The turkey pastrami was piled high on my potato bread. The lettuce was fresh and came from a good sized head. the hot peppers and fried onions hit the spot. and the cooler had awesome sodas from Jones and Dr. Browns (The celery soda was better than I thought it would be.). Next time I come here I'm going to have to order the Whitefish sammich so I can report back to Aaron (and I might just have to pile on some nova lox in the process). And I'm going to have to go for one of those awesome sounding blintzes too. SAMMICHES!

It's long been established that I consider the Tired Hands format to be the perfect way to construct a solid micro brewery, and in a lot of ways many other Philly breweries would agree since they've picked up people who've worked there to manage aspects of their beer operations. But outside of Ardmore I've been looking for the micro brewery that has come closest to delivering similar results in the Philly proper for awhile now! But between the beers, food, customer service, and abstract art/personality that they featured; Crime & Punishment proved to match all of my considered requirements in just a single visit!

Crime & Punishment first had me with a chalk drawing of a kielbasy (hot dog?) man ushering in 2018 by the door, and continued such win with bathroom signs that warned you not to flush away hopes and dreams. But beyond that point it also featured a dynamic pale ale heavy beer list that also delivered rarer varieties like oatmeal stouts, Berliner weisses, and Grodziskies. Much like Tired Hands all of the above weren't beer flight friendly, but their 2 size options did ensure for pours that matched your preference.

Another key thing for what I consider to be my best brewpubs is the food menu. and between the squash salad with pumpkin seeds & dried cranberries, and the beet salad with almond crumble and goat cheese; Crime & Punishment is one of those places that has the rare designation of being able to win friends with salad (Homer Simpson be damned! - https://youtu.be/wx59zLqBRuI). But they also featured winning things like pierogies, charcuterie boards, and a Kielbasa sandwich that featured some of Czerw's finest. Being the former cheese monger that I am; the only caveat with the menu I could give was that the brie, Danish blue, and marbled Irish cheddar that came with the cheese plate made it a little too basic bitch to be considered artisanal. But with a little love to some local cheese makers, and the continued application of the wonderful spreads and nuts that it came with, you have something that could be remedied fairly easily.

Slight cheese board oversight aside; Crime & Punishment allowed me to take a Space Race to The Grod Inquisitor, and delivered enough of a ride to have me wanting to visit the extremely outside of my reach Brewerytown for more. Especially during their weekday happy hour that features $2 off beers and food specials from 4-7 PM!

Birthday Dinner Review!

Despite living on East Passyunk Ave for years, Will BYOB was one of those places that alluded me before it closed over the summer. But Christopher Kearse was one of those chefs that I admired at a distance, and when I first read about the modern French Cuisine that he was bringing to Forsythia (https://www.phillymag.com/foobooz/2019/08/07/forsythia-chris-kearse-old-city-philadelphia/) my minds eye bookmarked it as a future place to indulge upon. And when my better half surprised me with a birthday dinner here over the weekend it delivered all of the good that I expected and more!

With the fire that ravaged the 2nd block of Chestnut Street a couple years ago, seeing a brand new restaurant open up and doing well was a good sign of hope from the get go. And Forsythia was packed, and moved like such a well oiled machine, that it also didn't feel like a restaurant that has only been open for six months! 

Whether it was through offering up spot on recommendations, or through providing humorous anecdotes and a positive attitude, service was at some of the best that I've seen! For cocktails my On Your Mark hit the mark with its Makers Mark, absinthe, and chocolate & chili bitters. And my better half approved of her old fashioned style Rye Fever with Old Overholt Rye and yellow chartreuse. Toss in beers from the likes of Unibroue and Stillwater Artisnal, and it had an amicable list for drafts and bottles/cans.

For ordering food our main server made the spot on recommendation that we order 6 - 8 dishes from the restaurants very inspiring menu. And with a plentiful assortment of French canapes, small plates, vegetables, pasta entrees, large plates, and specials this proved to be a very wise and delicious decision. 

If you've looked at my photos then you'll already identify our meal as a tantalizing assortment of food porn. But here's a more descriptive assessment of our meal:

Pumpkin Soup: combine fresh pumpkin with a cranberry mousse and crispy grains for one of the best cold soups I've ever had!

Cassoulet - this French classic was exceptionally elevated with blood sausage and a red wine soaked poached egg!

Sunchokes - almost like brussel sprouts, but such a good revelation with the horseradish and BACON MARMALADE that came with it!

Whole roasted hen of the woods - a new favorite mushroom of mine prepared perfectly with smoked ricotta, Madeira, and sumac spices.

Uni carbonara - a contender for my favorite dish of the night with its creamy uni, crispy pancetta, and salty pecorino cheese!

Rabbit Boudin - a special of the night that was AMAZING with its tender rabbit sausage and cheesy grits.

Duck A L'Orange - This classic got elevated with red cabbage, hibiscus, and cara cara oranges.

Napolean - a classic dessert taken to a next level with white chocolate, tahini, and a red caramel. 

From start to finish it was an incredible experience that already has me thinking about more meals here!

I've heard constant legend of the pizza creations that Vetri has been able to concoct at his other establishments. Unfortunately the sheer fact that I've always been in awe of his many pasta, meat, seafood, salumi, and then some that his other menus have to offer have also attributed to his pizzas constantly alluding me. So when I found out that he was set to open a pizzeria in Fairmount I was absolutely smitten with the fact that I'd be able to try the bulk of his pizza offerings without being overwhelmed by the slew of other options. And overall it delivered a plentiful assortment of greatness.

Upon entry I noted the roomy interior with plenty of unique seating options. And I instantly loved that my dining partner had chosen the side corner spots that gave us a grand view of the pizza over and the process of preparing the many pies that it created.  Upon seating we were welcomed with the extra attentive service that Vetri's restaurant are known for. From bottled cocktails and wines by the tap or carafe, to an eclectic assortment of beers by the bottle or cans, the pizzeria definitely has the assortment of libations. And we were satisfied by the Sly Fox Helles.

Much like Osteria, Amis, and others, Pizzeria Vetri utilizes the finest and freshest of ingredients alongside the most authentic of traditional Italian pizza cooking methods to create some serious pies. And if you go with 2 or more people its the perfect opportunity to share to your hearts content. The Salsiccia offered the perfect blend of fennel sausage and roasted fennel with mozzarella and tomato sauce. And my companion had an incredible special pie with a bit of eggplant, mozzarella, tomato sauce and potato. With pies like that, a traditional Margherita, a proscuitto crudo with buffalo mozzarella, and then some there are reallly no wrongs choices.

Add in an impeccable calzone, plenty of salad options, desserts like soft serve ice creams, and after dinner limoncello; and there are plenty of reasons to love here!

When I'm in Chinatown and in dire need of a caffeine fix for over a decade the winning and right answer has always been going to Ray's (https://www.yelp.com/biz/rays-caf%C3%A9-and-teahouse-philadelphia-2). But whenever I had that same fix and Ray's was closed, the answer almost always seemed to be giving into convenient store coffee and remorsefully lamenting in the key of Lemonheads (https://youtu.be/hFYFj5q8_Qk).

But the beautiful thing about going on food adventures with fellow Yelpers is that whenever life presents you with one of those problems, another member of your group always seems to have that perfect solution! Such an occasion arose when my suggestion for the pure coffee nirvana of Ray's led us to closed doors, and Kana led us to A La Mousse and some of the best coffee and dessert options that I've ever seen on one single menu!

When a stacked coffeehouse menu gives you matcha, milkfoam, and MILKSHAKES on top of the usual coffee and tea offerings you'd expect, you know that ordering the right beverage for the occasion may prove quite difficult. But since my brain was in need of a sweet awakening going with caramel espresso macchiato seemed like a no brainer. And from bitter of the espresso to the sweetness of the caramel, and the foam leaf on top, it was sheer perfection to the last drop!

As you've might have gathered from my Sugar Rush list, dessert is one of those things I prefer to avoid, but oftentimes can't resist. But when you see as many sweet sweet delicious cakes A La Mousse has gazing at you, they definitely get pretty damn hard to resist! Especially when you see one of your all time favorites cheesecake presented in baked matcha form, and served a la mode with a Guatemalan Ripple Ice Cream! the tempting picture of the green beauty I took does how delicious it truly was little justice. And it definitely has me craving more just thinking about it!

Birthday dinner review!

Like most Yelpers in the know I've had the chance to talk with Chef Sam and get a genuine feel for his passion for cooking and extensive recipe knowledge. And it got to the point that following him and Sycamore on Facebook has led to me seeing some pretty tantalizing food porn. So when it came to deciding where I wanted to enjoy birthday dinner with my fam this year, I couldn't think of any other place. And in the end I'm far from being biased in saying that it was hands down one of the best meals I've ever experienced!

When I first walked in I was instantly drawn to the fine wooden decor, and I became even more amazed when I learned that the owner crafted all of the elongated tables and chandeliers with their own hands! And our server was spot on and proved to be extremely knowledgeable throughout the evening.

You know a menu is impeccable when you literally want to order every single thing on it. So you can imagine how impossible rounding it down was, although things like the farmers plate which hooked up 3 cheeses and 2 charcuterie items helped a little. The dry steak dusted with porcini mushrooms was amazing, and the Sopresseta salami was the perfect antithesis. as a former cheese monger I can assure you that a place is real deal when it has things like Epoisses and Idiazabal on its cheese plate selection; so seeing them available had me sold.

Appetizers consisted of the so simple yet so addicting egg and medley of wild mushrooms on toast (which is what I've been dreaming up as the perfect breakfast ever since!), and the new tuna tartare that Sam was testing out for the chef's menu and hopefully decides to keep for a long haul since it was amazing. the main course of scallops with chorizo, potatoes, and chard in a port wine reduction was as impeccably delicious and masterful as it sounds.

For dessert I was mad tempted to go with the pumpkin flan. But since the Budino offered graham cracker crust, rum, and BACON, it piqued my curiosity. And since a wise man once said on Facebook, "Either you love Bacon, or you're wrong."; it turned into something that I henceforth couldn't resist. Since I was expecting the rum cake forged by the GODS; I was little surprised to find that it was a pudding, but i can only summarize it by saying.... WoW!

For the extra special touch I was given a plate of cookies (which I apologize for not finishing, but as this review shows I was that well fed!) and a candle to blow out for my birthday. And its extra touches like that which managed to shine throughout that make Sycamore one of places to watch and get down to already!

Pizza in Philly is one of those fantastic things that have managed to get better and better over the years. But still after all of these miraculous and delicious pies and slices, I can't help but marvel over those spots that serve a near perfect pie as quickly as possible.And when it comes down to it, &Pizza might be the spot that does it best!

&Pizza first had me hooked with its majestic use of the ampersand!  It was also pretty easy to marvel over the huge interior and awesome bike mural within. But I also savored the prospect of delicious iced teas and pies that utilized ingredients like bacon and shrimp served extra quick! Especially once you look at the heart of the matter and see that they utilize organic dough, ingredients that are free of MSG and high fructose corn syrup, and utilize ingredients that are fresh and locally sourced as often as possible!

Before ordering pizza I'm always wowed by the selection of jarred iced teas that contain flavors like spiced Thai and lemongrass white peach. &pizza is one of those fast casual spots where its pretty easy to go rapid fire with ingredients and create the pizza of your ultimate dreams (or nightmares). But the signature pies are pretty extraordinary when you factor in options like  the mushroom, goat cheese, and fig balsamic topped Moonstruck; or the chocolate/hazelnut peanut butter, bacon, and banana topped homage to Elvis. The Maverick is an absolute must for meat lovers since its loaded with Italian sausage, salami, and pepperoni. But the best might just be the Farmer's Daughter with egg, Italian sausage, and hot sauce!

Inexpensive Turkish food? an amazing coffee house vibe that doubles as a quaint little BYOB when you need it to? Excellent service from friendly people? Those are the things that I found the first time that I visited and I'm totally sold!

I've walked by here on several occasions but never found the time to stop in and give it a go. So after getting my haircut at Jeremiah's new Alley location (the spikes are back!!!) I made a point to give it a try. Despite the impressive looking veggie dishes that were ready to serve (zucchini pancakes, eggplant salad w/ Turkish bread, spinach pie!), I was really craving a sandwich. While I normally don't dig salami and kaiser rolls, they managed to make it immaculate. it could be that the addition of both mozzarella AND provolone helped immensely. But it was probably the fact that Turkish beef salami was like no salami that I've ever had. not bad at all for $5.

A+ on the service too. I had my extra strong Turkish coffee (love!) in the blink of an eye, and the server was quick on prepping my sandwich. he was also kind enough to let me try one of their incredible Baklava (more love!). I'm hooked!

This shop just opened.  Incredible variety HOWEVER, $20 for a dozen donuts is absurd.  There are many other places in Tucson that have donuts that are as good or better (LeCaves!!!) and are half the price or less.  Sorry Amy but I don't care how much variety you offer, you won't see me back.  It would be nice if you posted your prices or are you afraid people will turn around and leave??????

Great pricing and AMAZING pizza!!! Must go to if you're in the area.  I didn't think too much of it before I went inside, since we don't have any in California.. but man, this is DAMN GOOD PIZZA!!! :D awesome pricing too

When I heard about this business, I knew I had to take my mom. We pulled up to the VW bus, she saw the signage with the business name, and about died laughing. Friendly staff helped us select the Mac & Cheese Weenie (exactly what it sounds like) and the secret menu Hot Southern Mess (pimento cheese, slaw, Tennessee chow-chow), total under $10. Note these are smaller dogs, two would be closer to a meal size for a single person.

The eats are decent, and I like that the buns are soft and many of the toppings are made in house, like the cheddar mac and the piemento cheese. I do think the hotdogs themselves could be a bit better, as a few other reviews mention, but I like the business regardless and would stop by whenever business brought me to East Nash. 

Note that they offer brunch dogs on Sundays as well as some amazing-sounding daily features, wish they'd had the Greek or Buffalo specials when I stopped by!

Morning, noon, or night, D+D is great for a bite! Cute country cottage location, sweet and savory menu options, friendly staff. As the name implies, you can get donuts or hot dogs here, and I had to try them both.

DONUT: They're a unique brioche style donut with a 15 hour preparation time. Don't worry if you don't come by in the morning, they also make a fresh batch in the afternoon around 5 or 6 and you can reserve specific donuts in advance through their social media. The Sweet Baby Jesus, with creme brulee crust and raspberry-cayenne filling, was such a treat! I'm not much of a donut fan, this was my mom's pick, and it was such a unique find.

DOG: Opted for the Chili Queso dog, which was tasty. Upon ordering this item, we were assured all items are organic when available and the queso and chili are both made in house and buns are baked daily. The dog itself was well-sized and easily shared, and the queso was my favorite part. Dogs come with a side, highly suggest upgrading to truffle fries for +$2, they were crispy and delightful. They also offer an elote side, which we added on, and that was just okay. 

Service was friendly, food was tasty, and the shop itself is super cute. Utilize the outdoor seating if the weather is nice, check IG for daily donut/dog specials!

Synopses of my 1st review: Good pies, yes. Bad service.

As a self described foodie who has had pizza around the world, I profess that I enjoy the "creative" palate used to design the menu.  However I cannot stop wondering if even amazing pizza is worth selling ones soul to the hipster devil...

I've come to realize that I am not alone in this 'sea of faceless reviewers' as Brian D (the owner) puts it.  Take a minute Yelp community, and read some of the ripping,  snark filled owner comments on negative, or even less than stellar reviews. 

After recently reading this article 
http://www.huffingtonpost.com/kelly-maclean/surviving-whole-foods_b_3895583.html
I have come to understand the owner's comments, and in fact appreciate them as monuments to what a narcissistic, pseudo-artistic personality can truly create. indeed, Namaste.

Perhaps this is a new kind of viral marketing campaign, and that might explain why they take such great lengths, editing their comments up to a dozen times.  This may be genius at work. Get everyone to hate you, and then your business is bound to succeed.  Kind of like a hipster Howard Stern of pizza, Brian D has perfected ironic toned hate rants against his adoring fans.

The really sad thing is that I like little babies, but refuse to go anymore due to the black hole of pizza arrogance next door.  

Perhaps my review will spark an ego driven war with Brian D, if it does, all I can say is Namaste.

This was a tale of two restaurants - the one that was absolutely amazing, and the restaurant that was ... "heh".

Unfortunately It started off on a bad foot when we arrived and waited at the check in desk where one is usually greeted by the hostess only to find no hostess.  We waited...and waited...and waited.  I finally wandered into the dining room and asked one of the servers if we were supposed to sit ourselves.  He stated that someone should be there any minute to help us.  By the time the hostess showed up there were about 15 people behind us.  

But, it did get better.  The service by Abigail was on point and she was really hustling.  She took our orders, got our drinks, and checked on us throughout our meal.  She was a great employee and did a great job. 

The Good:  Get their Queso.  It's a blend of cheese, green chili, and ranchero sauce ($8.49), and be sure to add the seasoned ground beef, guacamole, and pico de gallo for $1.00 more.  It had great taste, great texture, and a nice bite to it.  It's Excellent!! 

The Not So Good:  I ordered their Steak Burrito ($13.69) which was touted as a flour tortilla stuffed with grilled steak and Jack cheese topped with Hatch Green Chile sauce.  Having just moved back from New Mexico to Florida, the thought of great Hatch Green Chile sauce had me hooked.  Sadly, the Hatch Green Chile sauce in Lutz Florida is not anything near the amazing Hatch Green Chile sauce in Las Cruces, NM.  I found my burrito very disappointing. Additionally the steak was over salted (IMO).  I would not order their burrito again.  

Poor greeting, offset by great service, followed by an excellent appetizer, only to be finished by a disappointing entrée leads me to only 3 Stars.  I would suggest the cook take a 3 month sabbatical in New Mexico and discover what true Hatch Green Chile is all about.  

I recommend you give them a try and draw your own conclusion.

This is a traditional Irish Pub in a renovated house.  Irish themed pictures and items adorn the walls.  The menu has just about every Irish dish I'm familiar with. 

I ordered their classic fish and chips.  The fish was very good - thick, flaky, hot, tasty, (and not greasy).  An ice cold Killian's Red complimented the meal nicely.  For dessert, Patsy's Peach Cobbler didn't quite hit the mark.  The peaches were good, but the cobbler was not what I consider great. 

The employee was friendly, polite, and helpful.  I would recommend you check this place out.

I want to give this review 5 stars. The food was amazing, the service was great-- until we were asked to leave. 

We were a party of 12 celebrating a birthday and were seated in the private room in the back. It was nice to have our own space, separate from the rest of the restaurant. 

We ordered a couple orders of lobster mac and cheese, crab Napoleon and crab cakes for the table. I only tasted the Napoleon and the Mac and cheese. The Napoleon was delicious! It was crab and avocado with a chili sauce served with crispy wonton chips. The Mac and cheese was okay. The lobster tasted a little rubbery and the Mac was not cheesy enough for my taste. 


For the main course I ordered a petit filet, which came with scalloped potatoes, green beans and a salad. My dinner was excellent. My filet was cooked beautifully and the scalloped potatoes were delicious. 

Then I also couldn't resist a creme brûlée when the dessert menu came around. It was perfect! I also tasted the coconut cake and the Godiva lava cake. 

So my disappointment comes down to this-- we ordered a lot of food and wine, and I can promise you the bill was not cheap for 12 people. And at 9:30 on a Friday night, the sommelier asked us to leave. We were still drinking coffee and some were still eating their dessert. I couldn't believe that a steak house inside a casino that is open 24/7 would ask paying customers to leave.  The restaurant had otherwise emptied out and we were the last guests, but 9:30?! That left a bad taste in my mouth.

This place is a little too Birdcage for me.... but I have to admit the cupcakes are fantastic.  I work in the city and live in the 'burbs so I pick up cupcakes for my wife occasionally.  This place wins by a mile vs. Flying Monkey.  They do a red velvet cupcake extremely well.

What a cute beachside food shack. That's a bit of a stretch, it's a small but the grounds it sits on is huge. Lots of picnic tables a sand pit for the kids. There's a stage out back and 2 adults only sections. This place is perfect for a late lunch, it's Situated right next to the train tracks, so you can feel the ocean breeze, hear the waves crashing and watch the pacific surf liner come by. 
The food is pretty cheap, burgers for $6, 2 grilled shrimp tacos for $10. The shrimp was juicy and piled high with cabbage and avocado. A side of chips came with it too!
I loved this hidden gem! Great spot! Check it out!

Trendy donut shop in a trendy neighborhood, one that lives up to its hype. 
The donuts are creative and taste amazing! What is it about the food in New Orleans? All tastes soo good!
We came in for a brunch-ish type meal. The breakfast sandwich's are made fresh and are served all day. 
They offer a breakfast menu with more options but it's offered at specific times. 
The coffee is cold brew and is on draft! 
The brown butter drop was so rich and delicious! I could have had two!
Great place to grab a bite to eat and then explore the neighborhood and it's quirky shops.
Check it!

There are plenty of Cajun creole style restaurants in the French quarter and some are over the top with hype! With that being said, I didn't care which one I ate at, I just didn't want to wait an hour in line. So the "other" place across the street had 45 min wait, and no wait here. DONE! The hostesses were very friendly and walked us to the bar upstairs. The restaurant has a large dining room and an upstairs bar with additional dining tables. Also, if you can request this do it, there is a bourbon street facing patio, to sit and watch all the crazy shenanigans. 
The food was fantastic! 
I tried blackened alligator! It was interesting, has the texture of pork but leaner. Washed it down with an Abita. Next up was the bayou platter. A trio of southern soup-ish hearty dishes. The red beans and rice were crazy good! 
I absolutely loved eating here and complexly understand all the hype. Worth the dollars and the small wait time. 
Check it out!

This is THE spot for breakfast/brunch! They aren't open past 2pm, so everything served here is in the breakfast/ brunch category. 
Be aware! This is a very busy location! Make sure to make a reservation through yelp to get sat much quicker. I sure did! When I arrived I was sat right away. As I walked through the dining room I could see the many delicious plates. My server recommended a slew of dishes, all sounded just as scrumptious as the next. 
They have a Benedict sampler. Make sure to try it! They have a creative take on eggs Benedict and the biscuits they use are just the fluffiest ever!! Also, the pain perdue topped with the bananas foster is amazing!! The caramelized bananas are so good! 
This spot came highly recommended by locals and they did not steer me wrong! Make sure to check this spot out!!

Cup Café is super popular for weekend brunch, if a huge crowd waiting for tables on a recent weekend mid-morning was any indication. And with good reason, as you'll find big portions of comforting, carbolicous fare at reasonable prices.

When I saw how busy the café was when I drove up, I immediately phoned my order in for takeout instead, so as to preempt any wait I'd need to endure once I entered the venue. And the Southern biscuits & gravy platter didn't disappoint. So much food, in fact, that it came in two boxes. One for a two huuuge biscuits that were delightfully drowning in a sea of delicious gravy, and another for two eggs, two pieces of bacon, two sausage links, and potatoes.

Fortunately, I didn't die of a heart attack, since I've lived to tell the tale. It was all a welcome part of a "cheat weekend" from my diet where I've lost 20 pounds since the coronacrisis began. Thanks Yelpers for yet another worthy local find!

Consider this a 4.5 star review.
Tried out this new spot in town. Was very excited to see a new place open where the old Nugget once stood. They offer a  variety of seafood items as well as burgers, fried chicken and a wild mushroom pasta. 
We started off with ceviche. It was very flavorful with avocado, jicama and cucumber but I felt it could have used a little more fish. It was served with freshly made tortilla chips. 
Next we tried the grilled mussels and they were fine. 
I had the shrimp/chorizo and grits. Amazing flavors but the grits were very runny. I had to ask for a spoon because they were impossible to eat with a fork.

The hostess Maggie was very friendly and our waitress Antoinella was pleasant and very attentive. We really liked her even though she would not share her cheesecake recipe with me. LOL.

 We will definitely be back and look forward to bringing our out of town guest there as well.

Absolutely atrocious treatment from the beginning. We come to the area almost weekly to visit other restaurants. Watching this one under construction caught our eye. We decided to come in today as a family (6 in total) to see what they're all about and to celebrate our daughters orchestral performance this evening. 

Well, we step inside and the place looks amazing! Very swank with an open layout and a nice warm feel. The staff looked sharp and greeted us with a smile. 

The hostess asked if we have a reservation and I advised we did not. She apologized and said that today (May 3) they are only taking reservations. I asked if any reservations are available and she said no. We should have walked away...

Trying to be savvy, I went to OpenTable and saw appointments available all evening beginning immediately. So, we set one and re-entered the building. This time there was a different hostess. I explained what was previously told and let her know we set a reservation. She kindly said that our table was being prepared as she began speaking with other staff members about the table that we are to be seated at. 

After a few minutes we were greeted by a bearded manager (compliments on the beard!) that explained that the wait will be 30 minutes because they are in their opening week and want to provide the best experience possible; the kitchen isn't ready for a party of 6 at the time. His explanation wasn't too direct, so I felt compelled to ask: 
 Me: So, are you telling me that it is a 30 minute wait or asking me to come back an other time?

 Manager: Oh.... I mean, you can wait if you really want to... um, yeah.... just let us know.

 Before I could respond I get a notification from OpenTable that the restaurant cancelled my reservation. The sinking feeling that came over me told me just to walk away, and we did. 

 Tons of misses from the first interaction. I don't expect perfection, but I truly feel that they didn't want to serve a family of 6 considering the average party size was 4 or less of business looking 30-40 somethings. Lots of lessons to learn in customer service and communication. When you get better, maybe we'll give you a second chance. Until then...

I love this place! We were so glad that during Covid they were still open. We sat outside where everyone was socially distance and staff was wearing masks! Even though it's hot as heck, they have fans that make sitting outside enjoyable. 

We started with the peel and eat shrimp. Always my favorite. Seasoned perfectly and the portion is always generous!

For dinner, I went with the shrimp scampi. All I can say is, YUM!! The delicious garlic and lemon flavors won me over after my first bite. I couldn't stop eating it! The portion was HUGE and there were so many shrimp in this dish I was sharing with others, which usually I refuse to do because I want to eat every last bite myself 

My boyfriend went with the blackened grouper sandwich. I'm pretty sure the fish fillet was a foot long! It was cooked perfectly and we loved the homemade tarter sauce it was served with! The fries were hand cut which are always the tastiest!

We had a wonderful time and can't wait to return!

In my humble opinion, this is the best Korean food available in the Nashville area. 

Baseline: my sister in law is Korean and makes some mean Korean food. This is the only place she'll go to for Korean food. She introduced me. The only better Korean food I've had was at Kimchihana in South Plainfield, New Jersey. Not a white face in sight except for my man---all Korean patrons and large large parties of patrons. It was always full. 

Ridiculously good Korean food. 

The standouts:

Seafood pancake--ask for it thin and extra crispy. Otherwise they'll make it chunky with too much flour--that covers up the very generous portions of seafood. 

House made kimchi-you can buy this in quarts and take it home. 

Galbi--garlicky crosscut ribs.  Arrives at your table super hot to the touch. Gnaw on the cartilage and slurp up the charred marrow. 

Spicy pork--this is similar to Bulgogi but oh so different. It has been marinated in asian pear until the meat is fork tender. Swimming in Gojujaru -- the ubiquitous Korean roasted red pepper -- savory and perfect with a bite of steaming hot Korean rice. 

Yukaejang--red spicy soup with beef and bracken -- it will warm you thoroughly. Not sour like the kimchi jigae, but savory and deep with pieces of shredded beef, enoki mushrooms, and sprouts. 

Boodaejang--spam stew.  This recipe was developed around that infamous American potted meat. It also has "sausages" (actually hot dogs), quarter sized rice cakes, on a bed of curly ramen noodles, kimchi, all in a flat paella-styled hot pot. This is spicy hot and warming.  Salty goodness.  This soup is just WRONG on paper but in real life, well, you've got to try it. I loved it even more 2 days later.

Kimchijigae--pretty well done here. This is the infamous kimchi soup--where all the super far gone kimchi go b/c old kimchi never dies. When it's too sour to eat, it's right for kimchi soup. But don't be fooled into thinking it might be just sour soup. There are layers of flavors:  deep roasted Gojujaru, silky fatty pork belly, and toothsome sour kimchi.  All that action could be a bit much if it weren't for the relief you get from the soft chunks of semi-firm tofu. 

Good selection of standard Japanese beers. Why no Korean beers?

The soft spots:

Hai Woon Dae suffers from location. It always looks a little deserted in the parking lot but don't be fooled. They have a lot of foot traffic here for dinner--I've been twice for lunch and they were decently busy. 

Location.

Location. 

Bulgogi is not my favorite here but if you have little guys, it is not spicy and kids usually love it. 

Dumplings--a little thick but will do if you're jonesin' for some mandool. 

Final Tip:  The friendly ladies who will take care of you on your visit eat their own cooking. Ask them what they're eating and what their favorite dishes are and try it. The worst that can happen, you don't like it and you're out a little money.  You could also get your mind blown and find a new favorite Korean dish.  That's priceless.

I admit after reading some of these reviews I was a little hesitant about eating there. However I was meeting old friends and decided not to create waves so I went thinking I should just prepare for the worst but hope for the best. 

To my surprise It was better then the reviews. I guess you cant please everybody all of the time and it seems the people who are the unhappiest usually are the ones that express their feeling "Let it be known" kind of attitude. 

Now for the review - 
The waitress Kristin S. was just as bubbly, friendly and knowable as they come - She was awesome taking care of our needs.  Five Star *****

The meal  - I ordered the Shrimp  Deal - 10 Gulf shrimp  with 2 sides rice and a salad

The presentation on the plate better than average Four Stars ****
The taste was also better than average  Four Stars ****

What I thought was disappointing but maybe that's because I am a big eater the size of the side I ordered (the rice) wasn't enough to fill you especially since there was nothing to fill you up at the table - hot bread etc. Three Stars ***

My bride also split an appetizer The Crab cakes which was cooked and seasoned perfectly but again - the two crab cakes were very small. 

Pricing - was a little high for the size of the servings but I am sure it co-insides with their expenses -  

Overall I give it 3 and 1/2 stars which is not an option -

 I would recommend to a friend and probably will go back again but will order a couple of appetizers for the table

I have been coming to Sitar since I was like 6 years old....so I might be biased? Either way, this is hands down the best Indian place in the city. My dad is from southeast asia, so I have high standards when it comes to Indian food and Sitar fulfills all of them.

One thing I love about this place is that it has a homey and family vibe to it. If you are a "regular" then they know you and appreciate your business. My family and I have a special table there. As soon as we walk in, they seat us there and bring us out our favorite appetizers. Now obviously this is special treatment since we are loyal customers, but I've seen them do similar things for other people. The servers have the mindset that they want to serve you.

You know how they say that hole in the wall places are the best types of restaurants to go to?? That is how Sitar is. It's the oddest building, I think it used to be a house or something. But don't let the shabby appearance stope you from indulging in a wide variety of Indian delicacies. I'm hungry just writing about it now.

If you decide to treat yourself and go to sitar, you have two options. (1) Go to their lunch buffet (2) Eat there for dinner

If you have never had Indian food before, and when you hear the world "naan" you think you misheard me saying "Hey maannn" then go to the lunch buffet. You will be able to try a wide variety of different types of dishes and ultimately see what your taste palette and stomach agree with. 

If you are a lover of all things Indian Cuisine and know what you like then I suggest going for dinner. The food during the evening tastes better. My family (4 of us) usually order....two orders of chicken tikka masala, one order of the mixed grille (it comes out with kabobs, chicken, fish...sooo yummy), a couple orders of samosas and pakoras, some type of dal and four naan. Three entrees here will easily serve 4-5 people. 

Ok, that was a long review. If you actually got to this point then good for you! Go eat Naan now!!

Exquisite. Authentic. Just go here!
I tried out this new restaurant in the former location  of Umbria last night. I'll admit I'm not generally excited about going out for Italian food because it is one of the cuisines I cook a lot at home and after living many years in Europe, I'm usually disappointed by Americanized Italian food.  Well, thankfully I didn't let that keep me away. The restaurant is absolutely wonderful. The ambiance is dark and romantic; it feels very sophisticated, yet not snooty. 
You are welcomed by homemade bread, ready to eat as is or dipped in the heavenly olive oil, salt and Balsamic vinegar. 
Similar to restaurants in Italy, the pasta is considered a "first course" to be eaten before the meat or fish course, but the five people in my party ordered only pasta and the portions were ample enough to stand alone. All of the pasta is made by the chef, and each dish is prepared when you order it, which means you can ask the chef to tweak it to meet your preferences/dietary needs. The other side to that is that you may have to wait a little longer for your food to come out, but with the lovely ambiance and bread...who cares!!
I had wild mushroom ravioli with truffle oil. It was TO DIE FOR. I got nibbles of everyone's dishes and each one was as fantastic as the other. I had a crème brûlée done perfectly and my friends seemed to enjoy their tiramisu.

This is very close to my experiences eating in Italy. If you are looking for the Olive Garden, keep walking. If you want high quality, authentic Italian food, run to Trattoria Moma.

It is reasonably priced and BYOB as well!

Bravo!

Great place to stop for a quick bite while driving up the coast. However - beware if you are planning to go here for a bathroom break - there was just one stall and a huge line of people to use it, including people who seemed to be just hanging out at the beach and/or looking for a place to change.  My bf was able to line up, order food, and have it brought out before I made it to the front of the bathroom line. Definitely a beach spot vs a sit down spot, so adjust expectations accordingly.

That being said, the tacos were great!  I had the grilled fish tacos and onion rings.  The burgers and sandwiches looked good as well, but I can't opine as I only had the tacos.

*** 4.5 stars ***

Julia Child's favorite taco spot is definitely worth a stop. Is it worth an extra trip or an hour in line? That debate is still out to the jury but if you are in Santa Barbara and are craving some good, hearty Mexican food, this is your spot.  If you time it right, like we did, you'll only need to wait in like for 15-20 minutes. We seemed to arrive just before the lunch crowd, just before 11:30 am.  We were in and out in about an hour.

The line is outdoors and people mostly stay distanced. There are some standing tables behind the restaurant in a large open space where you can eat (bring a picnic blanket if you have one!).

We tried a bit of everything - tacos, quesadillas, tamales, soup... all was good, but I have to say the stand out and must get item is the Super Rica Especial - roasted chile pasilla stuffed with cheese, served with 3 homemade tortillas.  Everything is good, though. I found the meat quality of everything here to be higher than other Mexican places that I've been in Santa Barbara. It tasted authentic and was not too greasy.  Definitely not healthy by any means, but I didn't feel sick at all after eating all that food. We definitely ordered more than we needed to for two, but it was worth it to get to try so many different things, especially since the line that formed after we ordered was probably an hour long.

Would I wait an hour for this? Perhaps if it was my first time coming here and I was seriously craving some good Mexican food, but probably not upon return.

*** 3.5 stars ***

NOLA is touristy, so my expectations were low, and I was pleasantly surprised.  In any other city it would be a solid 4 stars, but this is New Orleans and the competition is tough (there never seems to be enough meals in the day when I visit this city), and it's also on the pricey side.

It has an upscale vibe and made for a good family meal around the holidays.  They also had my favorite Italian wine on the menu (Zenato Amarone) so they get immediate bonus points for that.

We shared a few appetizers, all of which were good, but nothing I would say is a must order (except perhaps the Jalapeno Cornbread):

JALAPENO CORNBREAD - aforementioned.  I happen to be a huge fan of jalapeno cornbread and would always order it, and there''s no exception here.

MISS HAY'S STUFFED CHICKEN WINGS (homemade hoisin dipping sauce  chopped peanuts) - sounded better than they actually were. Good, but not great.

LOCAL LOUISIANA CRAB CAKE (creole corn maque choux  green tomato chow chow) - good, but pretty standard as far as crab cake goes in New Orleans.

For my main, I had the GARLIC CRUSTED DRUM (brabant potatoes  crimini mushrooms  bacon  haricot verts  sauce beurre rouge) which I can definitely recommend. I think the mains are more impressive than the appetizers here.  Someone I was dining with had the HICKORY ROASTED DUCK, which was really impressive. It was like a full duck - I've never seen anything like it. I tried a piece, and it tasted as good as it looked.

All in all - touristy but good. Not the best restaurant in town, but it holds its own.

I just love the vibe of this place. It's like a hip, modern diner serving Asian fusion style food.  And love that they serve food super late - I always seem to end up here, well super late.  After having a drink at 1 Tippling, we walked down to Continental (around 11 pm) because they were no longer serving food at Tippling (they stop at like 8 pm).  

Even though it wasn't on the menu, they made me an old fashioned that was actually better than the one I'd had at Tippling.  My friend ordered the fries and quesadilla, and the fries were insane. I don't remember them always being so intense, but they are super skinny almost like potato sticks and served as a huge mound with a wasabi mayo that clears your sinuses.  Definitely share these. I wish they were a bit less thin because they weren't that easy to eat and were a bit unsatisfying, but still very good, and definitely has that "wow" factor in terms of presentation.

I was pretty disappointed by Mother's.  I had heard such great things about the po boys that I expected to be blown away.  But, alas, Mother's is in last place of the po boys that I've had in New Orleans.  Johnny's was better, but 801 Royal was the best. I still need to try Killer Po Boys, but I'm sure it's better than Mother's.

I had the grilled shrimp po boy and I just wasn't a fan of the seasoning... it seemed cheap and was overwhelming and didn't taste very good. There wasn't much else on the po boy except the shrimp, and the bread wasn't anything special, so it was hard to get through.  My bf had the famous ferdi special, which he also didn't enjoy. All he had to say about it was "it was a lot of meat".  We didn't hate our po boys.. but they did feel like a waste of a meal in this city of fine food.

On a positive: the fries were pretty good, but aren't they always?

Pretty disappointing as far as Cajun food goes, especially considering this is New Orleans, but for being in an airport where there aren't any better options, this will do.  It's not terrible like you might expect from the other reviews, it's just not great.  I had the jambalaya which didn't have a whole lot of flavor and was just kind of forgettable, but it still did the trick when I was hungry and waiting for my flight. This is an airport, so temper your expectations. The Bloody Mary's are good, so get one to wash down your food and all will be good!

We stopped by Taqueria Cuernavaca for some quick, authentic Mexican food after a day of wine tasting in the area.  The COVID-19 set up with tables in the parking lot is actually quite nice and I preferred eating where we did more than I would have enjoyed indoors during "normal" times. Maybe they can keep some al fresco dining tables post-pandemic but I digress.

The food...

The tacos were solid. We tried the chicken, al pastor, lengua, and carne asada which each come on two corn tortillas.  While quite good, these did not blow me away.  The guy working at the counter said that al pastor is the one that "most people like the most" but he personally liked the chicken the best. I agreed with him, my favorite being the chicken, but that is personal preference. All were good, but lengua (tongue) is just not my personal jam.

The sopes were outstanding. We tried one of each - chicken, vegetarian, and chorizo. I've never had sopes before so I have nothing to compare them to, but the homemade corn shell that the meat sits on was thick, crispy yet soft, and wonderfully indulgent and delicious. I enjoyed all three equally - the mix of flavors from the meat combined with the corn shell are near perfection.

I really wanted to like this place since some of my usual coffee haunts downtown get packed towards the end of the semester, but I won't go back to Brewd again. I ordered a mocha and cinnamon roll; the mocha was nauseatingly sweet and I couldn't even taste the coffee, the cinnamon roll was stale (it was wrapped in saran wrap so maybe it old?). There is a big cross hanging near the bathroom and new testament sayings in the bathroom, which made me feel unwelcome as someone from a different faith. The wi-fi was spotty, and the whole vibe just wasn't that cool. If you're downtown and looking for a good coffee or a spot to chill this isn't the place for you.

I went in for something sweet and I wanted to try their macaroons as they are one of the only bakeries in town that makes them, but I was really off-put. They seemed to be running low on their baked goods, which was kind of strange, but not a deal-breaker for me (for all I know, they restocked after I left or something). The macaroons were fine.  They were properly prepared which was good, but the filling was a bit too sweet for my taste. The pistachio flavor was good but the coffee flavor was terrible. The problem is that the customer service was not good.  The man who worked there (he was a bit of an older gentleman) was very, very rude. I am not sure if they were busy or what, but I did not leave with a very good impression of this place.  

I did only stop in once though, so in all fairness, I will probably stop in at another time and try them out again.  Perhaps it was just a stressful day.  If the customer service is any better when I stop in again, I will change my review.  But for now, I am sorely disappointed because I had high hopes for this place! There are so few places in Boise that have any French food at all.  I am hoping next time is a better experience.

UPDATE: So I went back and the customer service improved, but just a bit.  They seem to have no problem treating customer like an inconvenience, which is kind of irritating. I really wanted to like this place, but they are just so rude.

They're also really small and not in a nice location. If I'm going out for something sweet and indulgent, I want to be able to sit in a nice area and enjoy it, not in a weird shopping outlet. Especially not for $2 per cookie. There are definitely nicer bakeries in Boise.

A new adventure and a winning one at that.  I knew some of my most trusted Yelp friends gave it high-marks,  but I was still pleasantly surprised. I already know that I will be going back to experience the Roasted Cauliflower and Brussels Sprouts, plus the Spaghetti with Meatballs and the Lasagna. Seeing them pass by our table made me want to change my original order. 

As we glanced over the menu, we were served warm complementary bread with olive oil and finely grated Parmesan cheese. The bread was so soft and flavorful, I had to resist when they offered to bring us more. Yes, we ate every bit of the original serving and would of loved more, but had to say  "No".  I liked how they served the olive oil and grated cheese in separate little ramekins. It made the dipping of the bread easier then smearing it on a plate. 

Since this feast was a birthday celebration, I let the birthday man choose the appetizers and entree. He had us start out with Mussels and Calamari. Good choices, I was going to select the Mussels as my entree if I were picking on my own. Their Calamari is flash fried and was done so perfectly. I like the presentation, they do a dollop of tomato sauce on the plate then place the Calamari on top. However, I always do not like to dip mine in the sauce and with this presentation it was unavoidable.  Next time I will remember to ask for the sauce on the side. 

The mussels were served in a black cast iron pot, that was extremely hot. I know that because, I touched it - ouch. The reason we ate our entire serving of bread, is that we dipped it in the white wine broth that our mussels were served in. A couple of the mussels were overcooked, but all were open. I hate it when you order mussels out and two or three in your pot are still closed. I just hate to see a mussel go to waste. 

The 50 year old wanted pizza, so we shared a Sugo's which would be a meat lovers dream. It is a simple pie. It has minimal tomato sauce, that is covered in sausage, pepperoni, bacon and hamburger. Then topped with Mozzarella Cheese, that  was so gooey and  stretchy good. They probably should have gotten 5 Stars just for not using provel as their cheese. 

When our pizza was served, we were ecstatic that it was actually cut in pie slices and not those stupid little squares. It was so huge as others have mentioned, we each only ate two slices and had four slices to take home providing each of us lunch for the next day. 

The ambiance is a vast open room with a view of the kitchen. It is kind of fun to see the worker bees creating their masterpieces. I like the garage door that can be opened when the weather is permitting to connect the patio with the main dinning room. Our server Alicia was attentive and charming. I like it when a server ask you to return and tells you when they work so she can serve you again.  I shall return and I will be sure to request her as my server.

We all know, or at least most of us know Egg is an excellent place for breakfast. However, in this review I want to give a shout out to something on their menu that most folks would not think to order and that is, a burger. 

Yes, a burger. It is simply listed on the lunch menu, as The Burger. It is served after 11 AM and comes with LTO (lettuce, tomato and onion) & Fries. It is a thick patty, hand pressed and prepared to your liking. I choose medium rare and it was done perfectly. I cut mine in half for easier handling while eating and the inside was a beautiful pink. 

I opted to add cheese and bacon to my burger. The bacon was thick-cut, crisp and extended well beyond the bun. I cut the excess off and munched on it in between bites of burger and fries. Mentioning the fries, they are made in house and seasoned simply with salt and pepper. 

This is now one of my favorite burgers and it's from a place known for eggs. I think the next time I have a burger here, I'll have them top it with an egg. 

I'll be back? - Yes

When: January 16, 2018
Why: Wanted to see if the burger was as good as it is at Spare No Rib.

There is nothing Pint Size about this new bakery on Watson except their size. The flavor of thier baked goods is totally HUGE. Today I taste tested their scones, brownies and cookies and all three of them should have near by coffee shops and bakeries shaking in their chef hats. 

I love scones, the one I tried today was a savory Asiago Cheese and Artichoke. This scone had a perfect light crunch outer crust and the most moist inside I have ever seen in scone. It would be a perfect accompliment to a salad, chili or bowl of soup. I enjoyed mine with a nice cold glass of milk at home and was totally satisfied. 

A must for everyone to try is the Cranberry Crunch cookie, it has potato chips in it and taste fabulous. I think I'm going to go get another one after writting this review. 

My brownie today was the Blondie,  which was the first to disapper from my plate.  That alone should tell how good it was. 

They serve Kaldi's coffee, are closed Sunday and Monday. The staff is super friendly and if you get to meet Christy the owner and baker, you'll love her.  I am so glad they are in my hood and within walking distance. They have a Loyalty Card that can get you $5 of free baked goods. Everytime you spend $5, they'll punch your card and once you have 10 punches, you get the $5 free. I plan on filling my card up very soon. 

Pint Size Bakery is a great addition to my hood.

Thanks to social media, Adam's has been teasing me with their Brisket Burger. Every time, I'd be at work or out of town. Today, when I saw the announcement, it was lunchtime and I drove right over to get mine. 

The burger was thick and covered the entire bun. If you want cheese, you're given the choice of having it placed on top, or injected inside. I choose to have mine injected. It was so cool, when I took my first bite cheese oozed out. There was so much cheese. 

When it came to choosing my bbq sauce, I opted for no bbq sauce. I wanted to taste the true flavors of the smoked brisket in the burger. Yum. When I got home, I did add a nice slice of onion and a few hot pickles to compliment the big burger. 

The brisket burger special came with two sides. I choose my two favorites at Adam's, their Pit Beans and Cole Slaw. The Pit Beans were a perfect pairing for a smoked burger. Don't get me wrong, the cole slaw was good to, but the pit beans were just better. 

The staff is great here. They make me feel like Norm on, Cheers. They know my name, always use it when speaking to me and thank me for coming in each time I visit. 

I'll be back? - Yes. They make my favorite ribs. 

When: May 30,2019
Why: My first Brisket Burger

BLT's = Breakfast, Lunch and Taco's. I've already experienced their amazingly delicious breakfast. When it was time for National Margarita Day, I thought I'd check out their tacos. 

I still came during breakfast hours, so I ordered one each of their breakfast tacos. My favorite was the Steak n' Egg. It was a corn tortilla filled with flank steak, pepper jack & cheddar cheese, onions, peppers and of course, eggs.  There was so such filling, they also need to double up on the tortilla wrap. 

The other two tacos were equally as delicious. I'd say the Sunrise came in second for flavor. It had a filling of; eggs, bacon, avocado, roasted tomato salsa, pico de gallo. It was also served in a corn tortilla. 

My last taco was the Chorizo n' Egg. It was the most simple of the three. A typical flour tortilla stuffed with; spicy chorizo, eggs, potato and white cheddar. It was good, but for my taste buds, it was definitely the bronze medal winner. 

Of course, with it being National Margarita I had to have a Margarita. Ordering one so early in the morning took the bartender by surprise. Once I told him it was, NMD, he totally understood and made me one from scratch. I love it when I see and hear a shaker being used for a Margarita. Those that come straight from a bottle are nasty. 

Friendly bartender, refreshing Margarita and overly stuffed taco were a great start to my celebration of National Margarita Day. 

Chances of returning? - I see a UYE in the future. 

When: February 22, 2019
Why: 1st Stop on National Margarita Day

I was looking so forward to my first visit Crown Candy Kitchen, after-all I have lived in Saint Louis for 33 years and had never gone. When it was featured on the Food Network for the Heart Stopping BLT, I knew I had to make time and go. I knew as soon as I walked in I had not missed much those past 33 years. 

The building outside appears so run down, we were not even sure they were open. At first I was surprised to see parking meters, in such a dilapidated neighborhood. Once inside the ambiance did not improve. The floor was in need of being replaced and the booths could use a fresh coat of paint. To be honest, the entire place felt claustrophobic and dirty. I was willing to over look those details and consider it character if the food was good, but it was horrible. 

My Heart Stopping BLT was heart breaking. The bacon was cold, rubbery and chewy as hell. I was expecting hot fresh off the grill bacon and it was far from it. Actually it tasted as if it were fried the day before. I've had better malts at Steak - n - Shake. I took a bite of the SO's Ruben and thought the Corned Beef was fatty and the sandwich had to much Thousand Island Dressing. 

I could go on about the limp potato chips, warm pickle and lackluster service, but I have got to shake this negative experience and move on. Thank goodness, we had Yelp Mints in the car to rid our mouths of the horrible after taste we both had. 

This is a tourist trap and I am embarrassed that it is representing my hometown.

Opening Day & they nailed it!

I can already tell you, this is going to be the place to meet your friends, before and after a STL Cardinals game. The bar selections and the food are top notch. 

I always judge a bar by their ability to make classic cocktails. Today, I tested them with a Manhattan and an Old Fashioned, two favorites. To my surprise, they were made with extreme care and professionalism. I'm tempted to say, the Manhattan was one of the best I've had in 2019.
