Another go to for me when seen on a menu, is Fried Green Tomatoes. 
Theirs was prepared with a thick, crisp crust and the green tomato still stayed firm. Nice. The tomato jam and the tomato aioli were nice accents to the flavor. When reading the menu, I questioned the ricotta in my head, but was proven wrong. To swirl my bites of the tomato in the ricotta before eating, added to the flavor. 

I knew my eyes were bigger then my stomach, but I could not resist. I wanted it all. I ordered the Sampler Platter and got it all. It consisted of; 3 ribs, brisket, pastrami, pulled pork, turkey and 2 Smoked wings. Of course I did not eat it all, I have a fantastic lunch for working OT tomorrow. 

Brisket - Best in the city. 
Pulled Pork - Moist & Flavorful 
Turkey - Seasoned well & fork tender. 
Pastrami - I am in love. Replaces my old time favorite from Soulard. 
Ribs - Dry Rub, thick & meaty. 
Smoked Wings - LARGE & meaty. Not a fan of the tips still being attached, but I dealt with it. 

Sides: Mac-n-Cheese and Pit Beans. The Mac-n-Cheese reminded me of Grandma. The Pit Beans, were just okay for me, but I'm sure others will love'm. 

Service was top notch. Ben has recruited an incredible staff. 

Chances of returning? - Hell, yes!

When: March 1, 2019
Why: Opening Day

Breakfast is being served in Creve Coeur and it has landed itself on four of my Yelp list. Yeah, it was that damn good. If it were closer to my home, I'd have it in my regular breakfast out rotation. Now it is in my special occasion breakfast rotation and I cannot wait until the next special occasion. I may have to make one up, just so I can go again real soon.

What is a weekend breakfast without a Bloody Mary? I don't know, I've never experienced one. If a Bloody Mary is available, I'm going to enjoy one and maybe two. A spicy mix, a peppered rim with a pickle spear and olive garnishes had this Mary going down smooth. 

I'm a big fan of any type of Benedict, so I tried OSC's Traditional Benedict. They gave theirs a little different twist, by using Whole Wheat English Muffins and Maple Ham. It then is topped off with a Lemon Hollandaise. I'm a fan of whole wheat, so this was a big selling point for me and who doesn't like a slice of Maple Ham over Canadian Bacon on a Benedict. You have a choice of fresh fruit or House Potatoes as your side. I went with the potatoes when I found out they were small red potatoes with the skin left on. These small potatoes were cut it quarters and fried crispy on the outside, leaving a soft hot meaty inside.

My dining partner is a fan of slingers. Normally he likes those served with chili on top, but he ventured off path and enjoyed,The Country Slinger. It consisted of:
Two Buttermilk Biscuits, Maple Ham, House Potatoes, Sausage Gravy. He liked it and I can tell you from the bite I sneaked, I will be back to order their biscuits and gravy. 
The biscuits were flaky and the gravy is what you'd expect from a farmers wife.

Now I just have to decide what I'm going to have on my next visit. Should I have an order of those amazing biscuits and gravy or try the Crab Cake Benedict? So many decisions to make.

Three visits = 3 Stars.

What impresses me most about Yolklore is that they are very eco-friendly. I like that they use their dirty trays for composting. I try to recycle as much as I possibly can, so when I see businesses doing something for our environment, I'm impressed. 

Food wise, I like their crispy potatoes and for quick serve counter food, they do a very good Biscuits and Gravy. The buttermilk biscuits are flakey and moist and the Sage Sausage Gravy is seasoned well. As I have said before, I was raised on a farm and I know B&G's. These receive a former farmers seal of approval. 

I've eaten; Classic Breakfast, Johnny Ham Hands and their Nest Egg. Out of the three, I'd say the Classic Breakfast was the best. It truly is a classic breakfast. It has two eggs your style, meat of choice, a biscuit with sage sausage gravy and their famous crispy potatoes. Having this breakfast, you will not go away hungry. 

Johnny Ham is a Plain Jane ham sandwich, nothing really impressive. The Nest Egg was a major disappointment. The biscuit shell was hard and tough, my eggs were under poached and the bacon was equally as tough as the biscuit shell. 

What holds them back from getting a fourth star is their customer service. I'd highly recommend the staff go visit other businesses similar to theirs and see how counter service should be done. The staff here is cold and very unfriendly. On one of my visits, I was the only person there and on the other two visits had two and three other diners and they arrived as I was leaving. So being overly busy was not the excuse for providing cold inattentive service.

Also, with large windows and an open view of the kitchen, the cooks should be aware that all eyes are on them. Some things should not be seen. 

Well I return? - If a friend wants to go, I'll give them another try. Otherwise, I have too many other breakfast cafes closer to home. 

When: August 5 & August 8, 2016 and January 23, 2017
Why: Breakfast, of course.

I am a BIG fan of Brunch. Unfortunately, I work every Sunday. So, I am constantly on the search for a restaurant that serves it up on a Saturday. Lucky for me, Big Sky Cafe does just that. 

Kyle greeted me as I entered, and I told him I was dining alone and didn't mind sitting at the bar. He obliged me and escorted me to a very colorful tiled bar. As he got me situated, he offered me coffee, which I accepted. I told him, no brunch is complete without a Bloody Mary and I would like one of those, too. He recommended, Tito's for the vodka and that was just perfect, since it's my favorite. 

As he greeted other guest, I studied the menu and sipped back and forth between my two beverages. When Kyle returned, I told him I had narrowed it down two entrees. I was torn between, Big Sky Benedict and Cornbread and Jalapeño Gravy. Without missing a beat, he recommended the Cornbread and Jalapeño Gravy. We just meet and he knew me so well. I am a fan of jalapeños and as a farm boy, I love biscuits and gravy. Putting the two together, made for a winning combination. In addition to the house made cornbread and the tangy, spicy jalapeño gravy, it had Geisert Farm, Smoked Bacon and a fresh farm egg. 

What kept BSC from getting 4 Stars, is the cornbread was a little on the dry-side and I did not enjoy the Bloody Mary mix that they used. Otherwise, it was a good Saturday Brunch and Kyle offered excellent customer service. 

When: February 15, 2020
Why: Saturday Brunch

Welcome to my neighborhood, Knead. I wish you much success, but I am not impressed. I've been to your establishment three times and not one of them wowed me. 

Your variety of selections are extremely limited and those that I have tried were just okay. They are nothing that I'd rush back to have and I can walk to your establishment. Being a bakery, I was wanting to be blown away with your bread, donuts and morning buns. Even your sandwiches on your own house made bread are nowhere worth the price you are charging. 

Also, your staff is not the most friendly. They were not engaging, nor did they provide the type of service that would encourage a repeat customer. Being a new business, I was not even thanked for coming in. 

Again, I am glad you are in my hood. I'll let you get acclimated to being a new business and revisit you after the first of the year. Perhaps it was grand opening jitters that I experienced. Everyone else seems to think you are the cats pajamas. 

Will I return? - I'll give them a 4th chance

When: November 29, 30 and December 2017
Why: In my hood, I want them to succeed.

If you are on, The Hill and need a cup of Joe to keep you going or to start your day, Shaw's is the place to go. They are by far the absolute best coffee shop on The Hill. I myself have been known to stop by for an iced coffee, just simply because I am in the neighborhood. 

They've been serving, The Hill and STL community for over 20 years. What I like best is that they do their own roasting and do it multiple times during the week so the coffee is always super fresh. 

The Baristas also help with the weekly roasting, so they have a true love and knowledge of the coffee bean. A good barista is like a good bartender, so be sure to tip accordingly. 

When: March 5, 2021
Why: A morning cup of coffee.

Before writing this update, I removed John Donut Co from my No-No List. It has been over two years since my first John Donut and I thought it was time to revisit. My last review was based on a box of donuts brought in by a coworker, so I missed out on the ambiance and customer service that is offered at JDC.

When experiencing a donut shop, I use my three classic donuts as a base for judging. They are the traditional Glazed Donut, Apple Fritter and the Chocolate Long John, or Chocolate Bar depending on which name you grew up calling it. The Apple Fritter was good, but the best in my humble opinion Donut Drive-In still is the best. I grew up calling it a Chocolate Long John and thought this was above average, it goes well with an ice cold glass of milk. Their Glazed Donut, is a true classic. In my earlier review I stated Homer Simpson wouldn't eat them, I now stand corrected. 

Not stereotyping, but I am surprised I did not see any policeman at JDC. It's a great location in Soulard. It is off the beaten path in the industrial area of Soulard, but still easy and safe to get in and out of on a busy day. It's not in my hood, but when in the area and craving a donut I'll be apt to return. If you decide to go remember as most donut joints, it is cash only.

New location, same great smash burgers! 

National Cheeseburger Day was a great day to have a Grand Opening. Upon entering their new location, I could immediately see why they re-located. There was many more tables for diners, a nice patio and best of all - a craft brewery in the same space. 

One upside of the new location is a larger kitchen and grill. Our burgers came out extremely fast. I barely had my beer from the bar and our delicious smash burgers were being served. The only downside, is that the lines to order your burger and fries is still extremely long. If you're coming for a work lunch, you'll be pressed for time. We waited in line close to 40 minutes, so I recommend you get yourself a pint or a flight to enjoy while you wait your turn to order. It is well worth the wait. 

My smash for the Grand Opening was, The Lumberjack. It's made with two patties; one beef and one pork, with two cheeses; American and Pepper Jack. Then it was topped with my favorite toppings which are so simple; bacon, ketchup, mustard, onion and pickle. I don't need fancy toppings on my burger. Lumberjack is a classic. 

The staff was friendly. A nicer touch to the new location is runners delivering the food to your table instead of getting a text from the kitchen. Having a table marker is so much better then a text. 

Congratulations on your new location, Mac. I think you've got a winner. 

I'll be back? - Yes, I'm a burger addict. 

When: September 18, 2019
Why: Grand Opening Lunch

So glad I can come back and sit at my corner of the bar at Stone Turtle. I had to giggle how they had areas marked off with blue tape so customers would not sit at certain areas at the bar. They're taking the social distancing seriously. My usual stool was available, so I was a happy drinker. 

One of my favorite summer drinks is a, Boulevardier. The Compari makes a refreshing cocktail to sip while visiting with a good friend. Norma my BFF enjoyed a, Aviation. If you're a fan of Gin, you'll love it, too. 

We both needed something to nosh on, while we enjoyed our cocktails and chatted. Norma knew immediately that she wanted the, Pork & Cashews. I gotta agree with her, how can you go wrong with a salty mixture of pork belly & cashew nuts. Yum-Yum. 

For me, I went with, Tiger Roll. It was my first time and it will not be the last. They were f-ing amazing. The serving size was, 3 rolls. If you order these on my recommendation, I suggest you do a double order. Because, I'm telling you now, you will not want to share them. 

These rolls are wontons stuffed with; spicy crab, shrimp and cream cheese. Then for dipping, they're served with a Cilantro Jam. I'm one of those people who thinks, cilantro taste like soap. However, this jam won me over. It provided a nice splash of extra flavor when you dabbed it on your wonton. 

We needed a second cocktail. For me, I had to have my all-time favorite, a classic, Manhattan. If you've read my previous review - they do them right here. I loved it and I had it on the rocks. Norma, got a little adventurous and tried a, La Socialista. It was a perfect blend of; Rum, Blood Orange, Lime Juice and Vanilla. Rum and Vanilla for me personally is always a winner. It must have been good, she finished it before I finished my Manhattan. 

The staff were all wearing mask and I as I stated in my opening, they were on top of the social distancing. So they get a big, Thank-You for doing it safe. 

Will I be back? - Yep, it's one of my favorite Dogtown bars. 

When: July 1, 2020
Why: Getting out of the house.

I'm bad, I cannot believe I have not updated my review over the last 11 years.
So, I am raising them up to 5 Stars and it is well deserved. 

My go to order here at  Lester's is always the chicken wings. I like my wings extra crisp, so they oblige me when I order them, extra crispy. They do it, without drying them out. They're crispy and the meat is still juicy. The wings are seasoned so well, I never use any dressing for dipping. If you do, they offer both, Blu Cheese and Ranch. 

To accompany my wings, I order a small house salad and that is when I order the Blu Cheese. Many restaurants I have the dressing served as a side, but I trust Lester and they do not over dress. They toss the lettuce with just enough dressing to provide a light and flavorful coating. 

My recent visit, I was fortunate to have Deborah as my server. She is a delight and for those of you who do not know her, she has been there since day one. This lady knows her stuff and is attentive to your needs as a diner. 

Dining during the pandemic, I was pleased to see hand sanitizer available and tables marked unavailable to provide social distancing. They even had the statue of Stan the Man wearing a Cardinal face mask outside at the entrance. 

In addition to the wings, I love their pastrami.

Damn, it!! I want to give you 5 Stars, but can't and yet you deserve more then 4. Yelp has got to figure out a way for us to give that 1/2 Star when a business is fluctuating between two stars.  

The food here amazes me, it is so simple and yet so very good. It truly reminds on the convenience stores in the French Quarter with small kitchens in the back. There is no fancy presentation here. It is quality Cajun, Creole, and Comfort Food served in a tin pan dish that you'd eat out of on a camping trip and I am totally fine with that. 

Our most recent visit, we shared a Captain Dee's as an appetizer . Three crispy cakes that were fried crisp on the outside and yet the seafood inside was moist. Out of the three, the crab was our favorite. Then it would be the shrimp and salmon. They were served with a portion of Arugula in the center. It would of been a nice touch if the arugula was tossed in a simple vinaigrette. This could easily be a light lunch. 

Having started a Slinger list here on Yelp, I ordered The Sink. It just felt like a breakfast for dinner night. Two fluffy biscuits (and I do mean fluffy), two sausage patties, tater tots, two eggs over easy, sausage gravy & topped with diced jalapeño bacon, white cheddar and pepper jack cheese. Be still by beating heart. Wait I think my heart did stop after eating this, but it was so worth it. The gravy was rich and creamy and covered the entire entree. The spicy sausage and the jalapeño bacon were the perfect accent. This may be a different twist to the traditional Slinger, but it is still worthy of a spot on my list. 

My dining partner, Brad ordered wisely. He selected the 4 Horseman, which gave you a sampling of four different entrees. In two different tin pans, were sampling of; Étouffée, Jambalaya, SBR (sausage, beans & rice) and Seafood Gumbo. These servings were so large, that two adults could of shared. We differed on our rankings of which one we liked best, but agreed all four were pretty damn amazing. The Seafood Gumbo and Jambalaya were defiantly the shining stars. 

Parking here is not my issue, I have the most amazing Parking Angel, that always makes sure I have Prince Parking. My only disappointments were that there is no liquor  license yet and the slow service. I know the license is beyond your control, but I really wanted a drink and can't wait to see how you prepare a Bloody Mary. The service  you can control and it just needs a little adjustment. Our server was bubbly and friendly, but got easily sidetracked. If I had that Bloody Mary, I most likely could of cared less. We probably all suffer from ADD now and then....LOL 

Get that liquor license and your guaranteed 5 Stars.

Those who say the best Italian in STL is on, "The Hill" is totally wrong. This place in Clayton is amazingly delicious. It is tucked away at the  back-end of a small strip center just off Wydown. The small boutique size makes it intimate and almost romantic. 

I meet up with fellow Yelper, Christal for lunch on the Tuesday after Labor Day. Our luncheon was 12:30pm, towards the end of their lunch rush. I arrived first and selected a table on their small patio. Being a dog dad, it was nice to see they had water bowls making the patio pet friendly. 

We started out with some Cauliflower Hummus. In addition to the crostini, they offered a basket of soft Italian bread dabbed with garlic butter. This worked out great, because I preferred the crostini and Christal wanted the softer bread. I enjoyed the uniqueness of the cauliflower hummus. In addition to the hummus, the plate had a small spinach salad with pine nuts and balsamic dressing. It was a nice touch. 

For my entree, I channeled my inner child and ordered a half order of spaghetti and meatball. I choose the chicken.The ground chicken was blended with breadcrumbs. It was moist and tender. Noodles were prepared to a perfect al dente. I don't think Italian food can really be classified as a comfort food, but this Southern Italian Southern food, brought me comfort this afternoon. 

No booze for me, I enjoyed a tall refreshing glass of ice tea. Christal was having a rough day at work and enjoyed a glass of red wine. I found it odd that it was not served in a traditional wine glass. It was served in a small juice/water glass. I thought it was perhaps because we were on the patio.  Then the table next to us ordered a bottle and did have a traditional steamed glass. Just weird. 

Our server was professional and very knowledgeable. He described their food and recommended wines for Christal like a true pro. 

Will I return? - Most definitely. 

When: September 5, 2017
Why: Italian lunch with a friend

Are we having fun yet? If you're at Mission Taco Joint, you'll never have to ask that question. Because from the moment you enter the door, the party begins.  The entire staff here is always cheerful, friendly and truly go out of their way to make sure you enjoy your time at "The Joint".  In addition to the good food and booze you can feel a positive energy generated through out. 

We arrived almost at peak dinner time and had a small wait of about 20 minuets. Which I did not mind at all, it gave us time to enjoy a Mission Margarita at the bar. We told the bartender, that we wanted "the best Margarita" and he delivered.  Not only are they one of the best Margaritas in town, but watching them be made is a show in itself. James Bond would love'm, because they are "shaken, not stirred". 

Once seated, we were greeted by Betsy who remembered us from our last visit. Gave us a warm fuzzy feeling. We were glad we had her again too, she's a great server.  We quickly ordered Chips and Salsa, so we could munch while be debated what would be our new MTJ experience. Don't be cheap  order the C&S, you'll understand the difference in what you get at other places "free". There is no comparison, these chips will make your taste buds dance. 

I would have loved to experienced the Carne Asada Fries again, but the Crab Taquitos were calling out to me and I am glad that I listened. Crispy tortillas stuffed with Blue Crab Meat, Roasted Corn and Spicy Avocado Sauce. Don't worry about dipping or smearing them in the garnishes on the plate, they are perfect just the way they are served. I can see myself ordering these again with a small side of the Roasted Street Corn as my main entree.

Speaking of Street Corn, their large order is enough for three people to share. We both enjoyed a good serving and I still had enough for lunch the next day. Having it for lunch was a real treat, I tasted it cold before reheating and it was so damn good, I ate it cold. I would love to do a side by side taste test of Mission Taco Joint and Milagro Street Corn to see which one is really the best, because I think it is a close tie. 

Earlier the young couple next to us at the bar were enjoying a Piscojitos, so when we ordered our second round of drinks we switched over. Only thing that could make these possibly better, would be a sandy beach and a sexy cabana boy or girl. 

The SO continued his quest to experience all the tacos on the menu. The only one I got to get a bite of was the Nopales. Yummy, Yummy. Who knew cactus could taste go good, when served up with goat cheese and roasted jalapeno salsa. I'll be ordering one of these soon. 

I also learned on this visit, I should of paid closer attention in high school Spanish instead of being the class clown. I ordered the Chorihevo, which is one of their featured Tortas and I was disappointed. No fault of theirs, the flavor was outstanding and would make a great breakfast sandwich with the sausage, fried egg and pickled jalapeno, and smashed black beans. I just was not expecting it to be served on a very large bun. Again, I stress GREAT flavor, just not what I expected or wanted.  The Chili Crusted Potato Fries that were served with my Tortas, were seasoned well and a perfect accompaniment to the Tortas. Next time I will ask that mine be done a little crispier. 

Now on the next visit, I shall start my quest of experiencing ALL the tacos. Only because, this is a TACO joint.

I would have never discovered The Post if were not for a talk thread on Yelp. Everyone was sharing their favorite places in Maplewood and several mentioned The Post. I became curious, so one day I checked it out and now know what all the excitement is about. In fact, I already established myself as a regular with check-ins on my iPhone. 

The Post offers some very good bar grub. I will say, they are #1 in my book for wings. Their wings are good size, meaty and very juicy. What I love is they offer for an additional 50¢ to bake your wings. After your wings are done like normal wings they give them a ride through the pizza oven. This bakes their fantastic and flavorful sauce into the wings and it also makes them less messy while eating. 

On our first visit I was surprised to do my iPhone check-in and get a 20% off coupon on my entire bill. Now that is one hell of a Yelp deal.  We chowed down on wings, cheeseburgers and fries. I love bars that offer my favorite cheese on their burgers. No, I am not talking provel. I am talking about pepper cheese for that extra bang of flavor.  Our drinks of choice  were soda which gave us another surprise, they are served in plastic tumblers that you get to take home. When I got home, I washed mine and placed it next to my other souvenir glasses from the 2006 World Series and 1983 Miss Universe Pageant. I have a very varied collection. 

The next visit was a dinner to experience their pizza. I have a hard enough time choosing my topping, now at The Post you need to select you crust. The Post offers 8 different types of crust. We choose Parmesan Peppercorn to complement the "Kitchen Sink"  toppings. We ordered a small size and it was enough for two, with enough leftovers for a next day lunch for one. 

My only complaint about The Post is that there are not enough TVs to watch a sporting event. Ha Ha - just kidding. TVs are plentiful, and you have a great view from any chair or bar-stool in the restaurant.  Young ladies if you are looking for a hot man, go to  The Post on game night you will plenty to choose from. However, to get their attention from the TVs or their lap tops and fantasy teams may be a challenge.

You've heard the expression, "Don't judge a book by its' cover". Well, I am hear to tell you, do not judge a taco shop by its name. I have been ignoring Fuzzy for a long time and now I regret that I didn't give them a try earlier. I was expecting a Taco Bell type restaurant and that was the furthest thing from my experience. 

Fuzzy may not offer table service, but the quality of food exceeds some of the better known Mexican restaurants that do. As you enter the taco shop, you place your order for food and alcoholic beverages. Yes, Fuzzy has booze and their frozen Margaritas will give you a brain freeze and kick your ass. I was amazed how strong they were. I'm normally not a fan of frozen drinks, but this one is one of the best frozen Margaritas I have ever enjoyed. 

After placing your food order, you move on to the next counter around the corner. Sometimes you are given a vibrating beeper or you just wait until your number is called out. They hustle in the kitchen and our food was prepared in minimal time. 

There are no free chips and salsa here and I like it that way. So many times when a restaurant does offer them, you munch and munch until you are to full to enjoy the entree you ordered. We ordered Chips and Queso and the portion they served was the perfect size for two. Both of us liked how they sprinkled the chips with chili powder. The queso is thick and clings to the chips after being dipped. 

We both ordered Taco Plates which comes with two tacos and two sides. We both ordered Tempura Fish and would rate it second best in the city. Our second tacos were Fajita, one beef and one chicken. Both were tender and seasoned well. Sampling each others, we agreed the beef was the best. 

As side dishes, we both selected the Cilantro Lime Rice which was way better then the traditional Mexican Rice you get at the budget Mexican Restaurants. I had the Refried Beans, which again surprised me with the quality. However, my friends Borracho Beans will be what I will order next time. They were spicy and the perfect side dish for tacos. 

Next time I want inexpensive Mexican food, I'm driving past all the local little El and Del blanks and going straight to Fuzzy's Taco Shop. I take better food over table service any day. 

Also, for all my single lady Yelpers, there were a lot of hot single men dining alone at Fuzzy's. 
I'm just saying.......

When: September 4, 2015
Why: Dinner

I've always been a fan of OBB and I am even more so now that I live less than five miles away. Living so close makes it easy to swing by to fill my growler to grab a variety of 4/6 packs of cans. Why buy it from a third party, when you can get it directly from the brewery. 

For me, OBB is also a great place to go for lunch on my days off. For example on St. Patrick's Day, I got to enjoy, Corned Beef and Cabbage for only $10. It was delicious, but I was so tempted to order the Burger of the Week. It was a half-pound steak burger with jalapeño cheese sauce and onion straws. I thought to myself, St. Patty's is a once a year thing, that steak burger will be offered again. 

I also, enjoy their daily specials. I'll share them with you, so you too can enjoy them. 
Monday - Fill 64 oz Growler for $10
Tuesday - Double Cheeseburger with Fries $7
Wednesday - Boneless Chicken Wings $9 
Thursday - 14" Pizza $14 or $20 with a pitcher or 4 Pack
Friday - Fish n Chips (Fries and Hush Puppies) $12
Saturday - Fried Chicken Sandwich - $10
Sunday - Vegan Special 

So as you can see, they've something for everyone. 

When I moved from STL, I did it with 4 cousins and after we were done in record time, I brought my crew here for dinner. We had a fun time celebrating my move. We enjoyed a lot of booze, appetizers and a variety of entrees. 

The crew here is always friendly and during the pandemic they have offered curbside to-go, patio seating and now are able to offer inside dining with social distancing. 

Hope I don't develop a little beer belly, now that I live close to a brewery. 

When: Numerous Visit - Oct 23, 2020 was my moving celebration
Why: Supporting a local brewery

I was shocked today to learn that CJ Muggs is a local business and not a chain. I knew we had two in the Saint Louis area, so for some reason I just assumed it was a chain. I have never been so glad in my life to be wrong. It is similar to a TGIF or Houlihan's with hometown ownership. 

After dropping more $'s then I normally do for tennis shoes, I wanted to save some $'s on lunch so I flipped through the Entertainment Coupon Book and found one for CJ Muggs. It was a BOGO which would give us a savings of $8. 

We were strong and skipped having an appetizer. I stuck to being good on my diet, and enjoyed the Smoked Salmon Spinach and Field Greens Salad. Spinach, mixed greens,  crumbled blue cheese, toasted walnuts,  roasted red and yellow peppers, al dente green beans topped with a nice size piece of smoked salmon and tossed in their strawberry vinaigrette. It was a nice mix, but they were heavy handed on the dressing. I would also recommend breaking the salmon up to make it easier to enjoy. 

The SO enjoyed a small house salad with blue cheese dressing, which was just a typical small dinner salad. Then he enjoyed a half size of Muffalato with their house french fries. They did a great job on the Muffalato. It may not be Blues City Deli, but when in Clayton it will do. Their fries were made in house, I love it when fries have the outer potato skin on and are fried crispy. 

Service was good, our waitress was friendly and chatty making our first visit enjoyable. I think on our next visit we'll check out their location in Webster Grove and see which one is the best of the two. After all, I have more BOGO coupons.

I disagree with Brian M., I highly recommend getting an appetizer. Especially the Fried Pickles, they are the best I've ever had and I love Fried Pickles. However, Brian is right about the entree sizes are huge and you will have leftovers, which make for a great lunch the next day.  Just use some self control when ordering and if you have room for dessert you are a better person then I. 

We did a road trip over to IL for lunch, we'd been talking about going to Lotawata for their Chicken Fried Steak, which is a real heart stopper.  When we arrived we were disappointed that it was not offered on the lunch menu and we didn't want to order the main entree, because we knew it was too huge.  Nonetheless, we found other heart stopping lunch specials that satisfied our Lotawata craving. 

First I must tell you about those amazing Fried Pickles.  The serving was enough for a party of four, but some how we managed to eat almost 2/3 or the serving. I just couldn't stop munching and dipping them in the Spicy Ranch dressing. They take a Dill Pickle Chip and roll it in their homemade breading, just coating the chip enough for flavor. I like to be able to see the ridges in my pickle chip and I definitely could here. Then they fried them to a rich golden brown, allowing the pickle to still have its' own snap. These were tasty, tasty. 

The BF enjoyed a Fried Seafood Plate. You can tell it is a Southern restaurant, almost everything is "fried".  His plate was covered in fries, small shrimp and huge pieces of white fish. Plus, he had Hush Puppies and Cole Slaw. The fries were crispy and seasoned, he could not finish them due to the huge amount served. The menu said the plate came with 8 shrimp, but he had over a dozen. Did we get more because they were on the small size or did someone in the kitchen lose count? The fish was truly southern fried, crispy spicy and flavorful breading around a moist piece of fish. 
These Hush Puppies were better then my dad's and he made a mean and tasty Hush Puppy in his day. 

I opted for the Chicken Fried Chicken which came with only one side. Like I could of eaten a second one. It was a large Boneless Chicken Breast rolled in breading and fried to a flakey golden brown & topped with homemade country gravy. As my side, I choose Mashed Potatoes so my entire plate was covered in the rich country milk gravy. I cut my breast in half and divided the potatoes and instantly had my lunch for work the next day and I was still stuffed to the gills. 

Brian M. is right about the bread and butter, it is amazing. When I asked for a to go vessel to  pack my leftovers, the waitress brought us a bag of fresh bread and butter to take with us. We still had half of our original serving on the table and we were going to take it home. Guess no one goes home hungry from here. 

The service was down home friendly and be aware of the ice tea. They offer true Sweet Tea from the South and it is sweet. For those of us who like to save a calorie or two they offer the "Rainbow of Sweetness" all three of the artificial sweeteners; blue, pink and yellow. Also, you'll get a laugh when the waitress ask the classic question, "Did you leave room for dessert"  

I'll be back, we'll be back and may order the Chicken Fried Steak and share it. 
I know I gotta have my Fried Pickles.

Twisted Ranch, surprised the hell out of me. I'm not a "ranch" person so, I was in no hurry to go here. When I saw that there was a UYE on a Saturday that I was off from work, I thought, "why not give it a try". I was expecting chicken tenders, wings, salad and plain ole Ranch dressing. WOW! I had no idea there were so many different flavors of Ranch dressing and that it went with so many other foods. 

They immediately won me over by having Fried Pickles. It came with two different Ranches for dipping. Being a fan of Jalapeños, I choose Jalapeño Popper and I don't remember. However, I can tell you I loved the Jalapeño Popper one. The coating on the pickles was coarse like bread crumbs, not a finely ground powder like many other places. I loved the texture, it made them stand out from the typical fried pickle.

For my entree, I went the safe route and ordered; the Twisted Ranch Burger. It was a 1 /2 lb prime ranch seasoned ground beef patty, grilled and garnished with lettuce, onion, tomato, pickle, choice of cheese. For me the cheese was Pepper Jack and for my ranch, I had to repeat Jalapeño Popper. All of this was served on a warm brioche bun. I like my burgers medium and they got the temp, right. I think ordering medium is more difficult then well done or rare. I recently went low-carb and I now dream of the fries served here and it ain't no nightmare, it's savory dreams. 

Now let's talk cocktails. I started out with The Grinch, since it was the holidays and I had done some serious shopping before my arrival. I'm no Grinch, but I just had to try this green drink with a peppermint garnish. It was like the punch at a school dance, after one cup you've had enough. I then moved on to a very flavorful Bloody Mary, that spiced things up after the sweetness of the Grinch. 

Our server Robin, was a rock star waitress. We were a large group of 12 and she didn't mind splitting checks and she kept everything straight and organized. The kitchen also did a great job getting the food out to the table in a timely manner. 

My experience at this UYE was so positive, I will be returning to the Twisted Ranch to try other items on their twisted menu. I learned that Ranch goes well beyond the Buttermilk at Hidden Valley. 

When: December 12, 2015
Why: UYE Luncheon

Picture this; 18 foodies from a social website called Yelp having an International Supper Club meeting at Mango. Now imagine, these foodies being divided up into groups of 9 and seated at tables that are perpendicular to each other. As a final visual, give these hearty partying foodies only one waitress. Can you guess what you get? 

You get one hell of a fun night and a waitress named Kelsie who I bestow the title of; "Best Waitress of 2011". When we were seated and I realized Kelsie was going to be waiting on our entire group alone I thought to myself, this is going to be a disaster. Miss. Kelsie proved me wrong, she is one top notch professional waitress. She treated us as if we guest in her own home. 

Kelsie worked our tables making recommendations and taking our orders as if she were a socialite working a charity fund raiser. She knew her menu product and asked open ended questions to figure out which items would be best for each foodie. 

She had me starting my night off with a Mango Passion Fruit Martini. I could have had more then one, but I was my own designated driver so I had to refrain from saying, "more, please". When my main entree arrived, I switched over to a glass of Sangria which they are famous for and rightfully so. 

I started my feast off with Aguadito Pollo. I enjoyed a dinner size cup, which was a hearty portion. It is a homemade soup of grilled chicken, rice, vegetables and Peruvian spices in a citrus-herb broth. A very creative and flavorful soup. 

I love mussels, so when I saw Choros Sudados on the menu I knew it was meant for me. Nothing fills me up like a big bowl of steamed mussels in white wine and good French bread to soak up the broth. 

When it came time for dessert i was already fairly full, but Kelsie told me I had to try the Torta Chocolate.  I had to listen to her, she hadn't guided me wrong all night. 
So I ordered it along with a side of vanilla ice cream. In my foodie world chocolate cake with fudge icing needs either ice cream or a big glass of cold milk. Kelsie informed me that the cake was a family recipe. To be honest, that is what sold me on trying it over the Flan. The cake was moist and I wish I were in the family so I could get my hands on that recipe. 

Mango and especially Kelsie a big hearty thanks for making our International Supper Club so awesome. I'll be back and you can bet your last dollar I will want Kelsie as my waitress.

GM+T will easily win every Best Fried Chicken poll for STL in the coming future. We've all loved Rick's chicken from other restaurants he has been chef, but this is by far the best he has created. 

His creative ability to take a marinade + a dry rub to produce an extra crispy, juicy and flavorful chicken. To have a true comfort meal, I added some traditional Southern sides; slow cooked field peas, macaroni & cheese and cracklin cornbread. 

The macaroni and cheese was made with white cheddar and Gouda. I would've never thought to put Gouda in a mac & cheese, but it made it so rich and creamy. 

I could not resist dipping my cornbread that was made with pork renderings and topped with a caramelized honey glaze into the slow cooked field peas broth. Come binding the two was a treat within itself. Telling you that the peas are made with salt cured bacon, is enough. It is as if your southern grandmother prepared them for Sunday dinner. 

I did start out with an appetizer, their fried green tomatoes. Fannie Flagg would be proud and jealous of these  delicious treats. I loved them and I do not like red tomatoes. I only eat fried green tomatoes. 

The service is in true Southern hospitality style. Rick and his team know how to do it - they nailed it on opening day. I can't wait to return. 

Will I return? - I gotta try the catfish

When: September 13, 2017
Why: opening day lunch

We had a plan, to arrive at Bogart's when it opened to have a fabulous BBQ lunch on site. Our plan backfired on us, because I did not check to see that they opened at 10:30AM instead of 11:00AM.  Who wants lunch at that time of the morning? Obviously a lot of people. When we arrived at 10:45AM, all the tables were filled and the line was ready to go out the door.  We got ours to go and enjoyed it at home. 

In the Stevie B taste test, Bogart's wins the best BBQ in the city. I love their Brisket! I can enjoy it with just the rub or with their sweet sauce. If you love your BBQ hot and spicy, they have a sauce that is perfect for you. Their hot sauce will leave you with that burning feeling. (I'm a wimp, I mix the sweet & hot)

As usual, our sides were their amazing Pit Baked Beans and Deviled Egg Potato Salad. If the Golden Retriever who wants to sell the Bush's Baked Beans family recipe can get hold of this one, I will gladly pay him for it. The smokey flavor and thick texture, make these my favorite baked beans.  As stated in my previous review, all I want to say about the Potato Salad is, "more, please.".  The mixture of deviled eggs and potato make a farm boy happy. 

A trip to Bogart's is not complete without taking a pound of their pastrami home. This time we could not wait, we were eating from the container on drive home. Peppery, smokey, juicy and tender. Jewish deli's should be jealous. 

What sets Bogart's above Pappy's is the customer service. The staff here is friendly, upbeat and charming. They go out of their way to make you feel comfortable and welcomed. When you are there, you know that your business is appreciated.

Shhhh.....we gotta keep this a secret. The Happy Hour, at Bartolino's Osteria, is top notch. They celebrate HH, 3-6 PM, every Monday thru Wednesday. On Thursday, they celebrate Happy Hour 3- Close in the bar and on the patio. Now that is how HH should be scheduled. 

In addition to discounted adult beverages, they have a special bar menu offering super deals on a variety of finger foods. Some of the most popular are; Toasted Ravioli, Pizza Fries, Crab Cake, Lobster Rangoon, Mini Cheeseburger and a One Topping Pizza. 

The bartenders are old school. They free-pour their creations, making them extra strong. Many of the patrons sitting around the bar are regulars. It's almost shades of Cheers. They all greet each other by name as they position themselves on a bar stool. Don't worry if you're not a regular, they're all extremely friendly and welcoming. 

Will I return? - Yep, I love a good strong cocktail. 

When: July 2, 2020
Why: HH - Out running errands and day drinking with a friend.

It's amazing how a year and a pandemic can change things. My most recent visit wasn't what it use to be. I truly was disappointed. 

A friend and I were out running errands on a Wednesday in December and stopped by for lunch. We were seated on the back patio. I stopped to use the bathroom before joining my friend on the patio. When I entered the patio, I was hit in the face with a strong odor. The bathroom I just used smelled better then the patio. I have a sensitive nose. It didn't seem to bother my friend, so I kept it to myself, but it did effect my experience. 

We each had a draft beer to accompany our sandwiches. I had the Cheesy Bacon Burger and my friend had the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich. Both of our sammies came with a side of fries. Both of us enjoy crinkle fries, so we were pleased that is the type Seamus serves and their position is always generous. 

My friend was pleased with her Buffalo Chicken, but my burger was not up to the level I am use to getting at Seamus. The grade of beef seemed to be different and my burger was over cooked. I also could not get beyond the odor, I should have spoken up and moved inside. 

In closing, I'll say the customer service wasn't what it normally is, but it was obvious they were short staffed, so I will not judge them on that. 

I haven't given up on Seamus, I'll still go back and hope for a better outcome.

St. Louis Magazine did an article on, "5 Items Under $10 to try this August" and TOD was featured. The featured diner special, was their Ying-Yang. You ask, what is a Ying-Yang? It's a classic, Slinger with both Chili and Gravy on top. Yes, instead of having to choose your favorite topping of gravy or chili on your Slinger, Tiffany's gives you both. 

What also surprised me, is I got to choose my meat. I didn't have to have the usual hamburger on my Slinger. I got to choose between, sausage, bacon or the traditional hamburger. I went with, sausage. My two eggs, I had fried hard. When having a Slinger, i don't want a runny yolk. 

The Hashbrowns at Tiffany's are homemade. They make them from scratch, everyday. That's true dedication, if they have the patience to boil, peel and grate potatoes daily. That's true diner love. You can't tell under the gravy & chili, but it was perfectly divided. Each side of my plate had an egg, sausage patty and a serving of the delicious hashbrowns. 

The coffee that TOD serves, is from their neighbor down the street, The Living Room. That guarantees you a good strong cup morning brew. It's always nice to see local businesses supporting each other. Another local biz that TOD supports is, Happy Dog Hot Sauce. I've always been a fan and was excited to see that they sell it as a retail item. The server/cook told me it is a favorite of their customers and that is why they decided to start selling it. 

TOD, is a true diner experience. There are no booths or tables. Everyone sits at the counter and watch your diner comfort food be prepared right before you. The crowd itself can be entertaining and the regulars will include newbies in their conversations. 

If you haven't been, I recommend a visit to Tiffany's Original Diner. After dining there, you can tell your friends you had, "Breakfast at Tiffany's". 

I'll be back? - Yes, I want to try a burger. 

When: August 7, 2019
Why: St. Louis Magazine article. 

Notes: Free Wi-Fi and Cash Only, but ATM on site.

I guess every restaurant has a bad night. If this is true, then S+S had one last night. 
I'll admit, for a Tuesday night they were packed at 6:30PM and many of the tables were large parties. Our table was 10, next to us was a party of 14 and in the next room I could see tables of 6 and 8. However, that should not have effected the quality of service and food, but it did. 

As an appetizer I ordered the Smokey Wings to share with my friends. They were huge, meaty and definitely smokey. For some of my friends who tried them, they were too smokey, but they tantalized my taste buds. 

For my entree I choose the Brisket Plate which came with two sides. Eating low-carb, I selected the cole slaw and green bean and tomato salad as my sides. Their GBSS is always a winner for me. The cole slaw is a vinegar base which I favor over a creamy dressing. It's a simple slaw, cabbage only and the dressing, which makes it an easy accompaniment to BBQ. 

When ordering Brisket, I like the fact that they give you three different options. You can choose from; lean, fat or burnt ends. They even allow you to mix two of them. 
In the past, I have always loved their fork tender brisket. However, tonight when I ordered the lean and burnt ends, my brisket was dried out and tough. I had to apply pressure and saw like movements to break it into pieces. It was also overly SALTY. 
Salt may be in your name, but do not make it the primary flavor that I taste. 

I promised the roomie I'd bring home a plate for them to enjoy and almost backed out on my promise after eating my meal. I stayed with my promise and brought him home brisket with baked beans and mac-n-cheese. To my surprise and delight, his brisket was the fork tender that I had experienced on my earlier visits to S+S. As in my previous review, both the mac-n-cheese and pit beans are winners. I also, brought home a slice of pecan pie and in the words of my roomie, "This Pecan pie would make any Texan, proud." Which in translation is damn good.

Service was friendly and they were willing to separate all the checks, which is always a nice gesture to a large group. However, service was slow, orders brought out by a variety of different servers and orders were mixed up with different sides. I think most of the problems tonight were in the kitchen, dealing with a full house and several large groups. I'll keep the issue with the bartender to myself, but it was a major flub up. 

I know S+S is better and am also confident they'll be back up to 5 Stars on my next visit. I hated to take them down a couple of stars, but had to be honest.

Cute and simple cafe. Not only do they offer hand brewed coffee, but you can get a shrub cocktail or a mimosa to start your day. 

I was impressed with the pour over, Chemex preparation of my coffee. They use Perc Coffee which is out of Savannah, GA. It's a decent coffee, but with all the great coffee roaster here in STL, I wish they supported another local business. 

As of now, the pastry offering are minimal. However, I must say they are very good. I was surprised to find out they are done in house. I devoured a Spinach & Feta Croissant and thought it was from a popular French bakery out in West County. It was that good. 

The only negative I will comment on, is the service. The staff was not friendly or engaging. 
In fact as I watched them during my visit, they hardly smiled. They almost were robot like. 
Smile, engage and encourage me to return. It's a great place, if they kick up the customer service. 

Will I return? - Yes, I'll give them another try. 

When: November 2, 2017
Why: Morning Coffee

Not my shot glass of vodka and I love vodka. How this place was selected as one of the best 100 restaurants in STL is beyond me. The only thing that saved it from getting a two star rating and being placed on my Terrible Two's list was the $1 off my cocktail for checking in on Yelp and the fact that the Pork Pelmeni which Ian Froeb recommended was actually good. 

What I did not like was the odor that hit me in the face as I entered. It was not a just freshly cleaned smell, it was an unpleasant scent. I just ignored it and took a seat at the bar. Which was a big mistake. I think I would have been better off at a table. Not only did I have to brush away fruit flies, but the bartender was busy servicing the tables more then she was the bar. At first I thought it was strange that she kept rushing me and pushing me to order everything at once. She also seemed put out when I asked questions about the items on the menu.  Then I realized, she was hustling and working the bar and both sides of the restaurant as a server. 

Here's the run down on my order:

New Old Fashioned - I've had better, but can I really complain about a $5 cocktail. 

Brussels Sprouts Salad - The bacon was rubbery and the burnt honey vinaigrette was bitter

Pelmini - Good pork flavored Russian style dumpling. Saved them from only getting 2 Stars

The fruit flies were a big distraction, having to wave them away constantly. The bartender even waved them away from my area. I gave up on eating my salad when I saw two resting in my salad bowl. 

I also felt sorry for the bartender/server. They were way to busy, to so understaffed. If she wasn't so rushed to do everything, I'm sure she'd been more attentive. 

When: August 9, 2016
Why: Lunch - STL 100

Oh, Happy Day! I have been waiting for this new location to open and I was so anxious, I was one of the first to arrive on opening day. They informed me I was the first to sit at the bar and that is an honor I will cherish for ever. This location is much larger then the Clayton location, but still has the same decor and feel. 

This morning I made it an avocado themed breakfast. I started out with avocado toast. I call it my breakfast appetizer. It's so simple and yet so delicious; wheat toast, feta, cilantro, lime, cracked pepper and smear of avocado. Yum-Yum. 

Next was my entree, Avocado and Spinach Benedict. It was a traditional English Muffin topped with avocado, sautéed spinach and two poached eggs with hollandaise sauce. I consider this a healthy breakfast - LOL. In my humble opinion, Half & Half has the best hollandaise sauce. 

I like that they serve Blueprint Coffee, which is a local roaster. It's nice to see local businesses supporting each other. I try not only to shop local, but to eat local too. 

The staff was professional and friendly. I liked how they were asking everyone their names, so they can learn and greet their future regulars. 

Will I return? - I'll be there tomorrow for breakfast again. 

When: September 5, 2017
Why: Breakfast on Opening Day

When I saw that another Mexican restaurant was opening near my house, I rolled my eyes. I already have four. Do I really need a fifth one? Last night I went to One Way Cafe and Bar and answered my own question. Yes, I do. I was totally surprised by the quality of food at a very affordable price. 

As other reviewers have stated, the chips and salsa are average. Hey, they're complimentary so average is good. To kick it up little I ordered a side of Cheese Dip and that made mine more enjoyable. Next time, I will try the Guacamole. 

My server was attentive and very chatty. When I arrived, I was craving Nachos. However, as we talked he recommended the Tamales and said he preferred the beef over the chicken. I went with his recommendation and he gave good advice. What makes their tamales unique is that they wrap them in banana leaves instead of corn husk. It gives them a slightly different texture and flavor. 

Driving by you can miss it, as it sits back from the other buildings. It is smack dab in between Midwest Money & Hampton Shoe. The restaurant is small and intimate with a larger patio when weather is permitting. 

The staff is extremely attentive and friendly. I was impressed that they talked about their menu and described their offering. It was obvious that they are proud of what they are doing. 

 I'm looking forward to them obtaining their liquor license, so I can enjoy a Margarita. Until then, I don't mind drinking a diet Coke. 

Will I return? - Yes, and I'll pass three other Mexican restaurants to get here. 

When: November 1, 2017
Why: Dinner

Yippie! I am so glad that Kevin's Place relocated closer to my home. I heard such great things about his pizza, but never went down to Cherokee to experience his masterpiece of a pizza pie. Now that he's only a mile and a half from my home, my waistline may be in danger. 

I was craving pizza for lunch and wanted to experience some place new, so I did a search on Yelp. Yeah, Yelp of all places of informed me of Kevin's new location. Seeing how close he was to my home, it was a no brainer to head on over for lunch. Kevin's Place has a small dining room and a good sized patio to enjoy your food. 

Reading reviews, I discovered they all raved about the wings as much as they did the pizza. So wanting the full experience, I had to have an order of them as well. I had my wing prepared, hot & sweet. The sweetness, toned down the hotness. They were flavorful and meaty. I like my wings to have equal portions of flats and drums, but my order was 2/3 drum and 1/3 flats. Since, I favor drums it was okay. 

My pizza was the bomb. I can easily say it is in my top three for quick pizza delivery pizza. It was a typical thin crust pizza and it was nice and crisp. I had mine topped with sausage, jalapeños and onions. It was so good, I couldn't control myself. I ate all of it, except for two squares. I really was hoping to take more home. At least, I took half the wings home for the afternoon snack. 

The small dining room is kinda cluttered, so don't judge by looking at the decor. If you do, you'll be missing out on some of the best pizza in the STL area. Only downside of dining at Kevin's is no booze, but I can suffer through that. His pizza is that good. 

I'll be back? - Absolutely. 

When: August 8, 2019
Why: New pizza experience.

Can I have a drum roll, please. I have reached another milestone on Yelp. My 5 Star review of Juniper, (A Southern Table & Bar) is my 1000th review. I could not be prouder, to have this amazing restaurant that is ranked 14 on Ian Froeb's STL 100 List, as my 1000th. I've eaten and drank here numerous times, without a review. So it is now time, to sing their praises. 

I've enjoyed a meal at one of the tables, but my favorite place to sit by far is at the bar. I enjoy watching the bartender mix and serve the handcrafted cocktails. So many times, I have caught myself saying, "That looks good, I'll have that next." I've enjoyed; Hollywood & Vine, Keep The Change and a Moscow Mule. However, my favorites are two true classic cocktails; a Manhattan and Old Fashioned. You can call me "old fashioned", but I am still a fan of the good ole classic cocktails.

You may scratch your head and wonder way you should pay for a Breadbasket, but once you order it, you'll understand. All I will tell you, is be sure to order the Angel Biscuits and Hush Puppies in your mix. The biscuits will be light and fluffy as the clouds from which angels perch and your in a Southern restaurant so ordering Hush Puppies is just common sense. 

Next let's discuss those small plates for sharing. If the Pork Ribs with Sea Island Red Peas are available, go for it. Again common sense will come into play when ordering; Fried Green Tomatoes or Fried Pickles. If you are lucky enough and both are on the menu at the same time, don't try to decide which one to get - get both. My last visit, they said it was going to be another week or two before they had local green tomatoes. I can't wait, but I will. In the meantime, I scarfed down some amazing Fried Pickles. I enjoyed the light dusting of seasoned breading barely covering the pickle, so the green color of the pickle showed through.

Another great Small Plate for sharing or keeping all to yourself is the Deviled Eggs. Sit me at the bar, with a Old Fashioned and a plate of these Deviled Eggs and I'd be in heaven. For me, that would be perfect "Happy Hour". 

Entrees here are referred to as the, "Main Attraction" and every time I come I get the same damn thing. When I enter the restaurant, I swear I am going to try something new, but when I order, "Fried Chicken" comes out of my mouth. One of these days, I am going to surprise myself and say, "Fried Catfish". Any way, the chicken is crispy, juicy and definitely southern comfort food. The chicken comes with mashed potatoes & gravy and a vegetable. I've had green beans and asparagus. Both were good, but for my farm boy roots, the green beans was the best match up. They also, change the gravy from time to time. I've had a traditional brown gravy and once I had a spicy red tinted one that gave a nice twist. 

It is sad to say and I am also embarrassed to admit, I've never had a dessert at Juniper. By the time the evening & meal are coming to a close, I am overly stuffed and do not have room for another bite. I think in the future I need to not have a small plate, so I can finally have something sweet to write about. 

I have always found the service here to be appropriate for a Southern Table & Bar - it is down home, Southern Hospitality. When packing up your to-go vessel which is eco-friendly, they write the date and Juniper on the box, too. 

When: Numerous - most recently, June 28, 2016
Why: Comfort Food

Let me begin by saying, I am not a fan of Indian cuisine. Or should I say, House of India has won me over and changed my view of Indian cuisine. I think I've just been eating at all the wrong Indian restaurants. I always been hesitant in my ordering, but loving lamb I felt safe ordering their Lamb Krahi. 

Lamb Krahi is stir fried with fresh bell peppers, onion, tomatoes, ginger and spices. I ate most of my entree without adding the rice, because it was so filling and flavorful all by itself. I did enjoy the rice, it was perfectly prepared. Many other Indian restaurants have always served me rice that was over cooked, dry and sticky. HOI served rice that was moist and flakey, making it a perfect accompaniment to and entree. 

Our group of 13 (International Supper Club) did not phase the server. He didn't mind that we wanted 9 different separate checks. The kitchen even kept the flow of food to our table consistent, so we were all eating together and not in shifts. 

A big thanks to House of India for showing me the true way Indian food should be served and prepared. Next time a friend suggest that we go out for Indian food, instead of trying to convince them to go somewhere else, I'll recommend we go to House of India.

What do you do when you've had a rough day at work and you don't have the energy to cook? Go out? That's what my plan would be, but I didn't even have the energy to dress up and put on a pretty face. So, Louie's came to my rescue with delivery. 

We ordered an appetizer of Lemon Pepper Chicken Wings and a small Chicago Original Deluxe Pizza. The LP wings were a nice change from the typical hot or BBQ wings. They had a tangy taste, blended with pepper. They were not as good as Jefferson Avenue Bistro, but were a good accompaniment to our pizza. 

When you order a Chicago style pizza from Louie's, they'll ask if you want the sauce on bottom or top. Being a STL man, I always say "bottom".  I've tried it on top, but prefer my ingredients on top of the sauce. The original deluxe is my favorite ingredients so it makes it so easy to order instead of creating my own. Chicken, spinach, bacon and tomato are some good healthy choices. We ordered a small and had two slices left over for a work lunch the next day. 

When ordering for delivery or carryout, the staff has good phone etiquette and customer service skills. If you opted for delivery, the drivers are clean-cut and friendly. A bonus of picking it up yourself is a Yelp check-in "prize". You'll receive a FREE 32 oz soda. That is more soda then I drink in a month, but you can get one for just showing some Yelp love. 

The only reason I am lowering my stars from 5 to 4 is the fact that I am getting more stingy with my 5's. I'm still a BIG fan of Louie's, I just don't think it is as good as it gets.

Seriously, I cannot believe I have not updated my review until now. I've bee eating here on the regular for four years. It goes to show how we get so comfortable going to our faves, that we forget to give them a shout out. So here it is, "Hey, Vinnie. I'm giving you that well deserved 5 Stars."

My go to when I do not want to cook, or just want a simple salad for dinner is a Large Greek Salad with Gyro Meat. It is huge and fills me up. They're not stingy with the Gyro Meat that is place on top of the salad. I could go for a little less dressing, but I always forget to tell them to go light. That's on me, but it is one of the better Greek dressing in the neighborhood. 

Another of my favorites is the Reuben Sandwich. If I remember correctly it use to be an occasional daily special that has made its way on to the regular menu. Mentioning daily specials, that is one chalkboard you need to take note of when ordering. Tonight I finally made it here to experience their famous, Cheeseburger Cheeseburger. 

The Cheeseburger Cheeseburger is flat grilled, diner style. It is two patties, both topped with American Cheese and then topped with thinly sliced white onion and dill pickle chips. I ate half of mine with not ketchup or mustard. The simple seasoning of salt & pepper was enough. For the last few bites, I did add ketchup. Simply because I am a ketchup freak for my burgers. The bun was also lightly toasted on the grill. 

If you are super hungry, order the famous Vinnie's Fried Potatoes. They are Baked then fried and tossed in parmesan cheese and Vinnie's seasoned salt. The serving is so massive, be sure to have a friend to share them with. 

Service is neighborly. The staff is always ready to chat while they prepare your order. I'm so glad this #smallbusiness is succeeding in my hood. 

Will I return? - I support my hood. 

When: January 2, 2018
Why: Burger Time

Some times it pays off to be a single diner when going to one of the newest and hottest restaurants in town. That way you can sneak in without a reservation, sit at the bar and experience what some are waiting weeks to do with a reservation. That is exactly what I did.

I went on a Sunday night and was able to snag a single seat at the bar next to the wall. Yeah, it was a little cramped, but I was comfortable and it was a great spot to watch all the bar activity. Another advantage of sitting at the bar is service. With multiple bartenders working, those seated at the bar receive endless and attentive service. I'll say, the service was sensational and extremely friendly. 

I'm normally a vodka man, but I started out with Cocktail #69 (giggle). I just had to see the Torched Rosemary garnish. I found the mix of whiskey, lemon & lime, Big O and egg to be a refreshing classic cocktail. It's one of those that you can sip, relax and totally enjoy.

I was wanting a light dinner, so I went with their Crispy Chicken Wings and a side of Roasted Cauliflower. Both dishes were top notch. The wings were simple, no messy sauce coating the wings. They were what they were called, Crispy Chicken Wings. They were served with a little cup of Chili Mustard Butter for dipping. Myself and the group next to me liked the wings so much, neither of us used the sauce that much. It was good, but the wings stood by myself as well. 

So many popular restaurants are serving Brussel Sprouts, which I do love, but it was great to see Olive + Oak go in a different direction. O+O offers Roasted Cauliflower and Charred Broccoli. As stated, I ordered the Cauliflower and am looking forward to my return visit to try the Charred Broccoli. It is good to see more restaurants are offering vegetables as starter and side dishes. We all need that extra push to eat our veggies. 

I closed out the night with a Cocktail #51. This one is made with vodka, my liquor of choice. It also had Rose infused Dolin Blanc and Lemon Bubbles. I don't want to sound sexist, but I should have known with a rosebud garnish, this drink would be more popular with the ladies. It was refreshing, but not a repeater. 

I'm confident Olive+Oak is going to be a great place for Happy Hour and dinner with friends. I cannot wait to return and try the; Kale Salad, Blue Crab Gratin, Gnocchi with Lamb Ragu and the Seared Jumbo Sea Scallops. I'm also looking for someone to go and share the 34 oz Prime Cowboy Ribeye. Any low-carbers want to give it a go? 

When: February 21, 2016
Why: Dinner and checking out the new hot restaurant

Hooray, for Gus's! I attended their soft opening and have been back a couple of times so I can honestly say, "I am a fan." 

Gus's fried chicken may be world famous, but it may take awhile before it is St. Louis famous. After all we are in the Show-Me-State and the people of STL love their Hodak's and Porter's. I personally think Gus's is far beyond those two in quality of fried chicken. They out shine them in seasoning and flavor. Gus's pieces are juicy on the inside and crispy on the outside, the way Southern fried chicken is suppose to be. Also, the size of the pieces will not disappoint you. When referring to pieces of fried chicken, size does matter. 

For some taste buds, Gus's may be to spicy. I'll admit, as I enjoyed my chicken I did have to blot little beads of sweat on my forehead. To me, that is a sign of a good spicy chicken. My friend who dined with me once, said it was too spicy for her and that she'd most likely not return. Me on the other hand, Gus's will most likely be my go to for fast fried chicken. 

On two different visits, I tried a couple of their appetizers and both of them did not disappoint. 
I am a huge fan of Fried Pickles and was impressed with the thick breading that they used on the dill spears. I am so use to seeing fried pickle chips, that it was a pleasant surprise to see spears. The breading was crisp and when you bite into the pickle, it was extremely warm inside...again, nice touch. 

The second app I tried was a true Southern delight; Fried Green Tomatoes. The slices were thick and they had the same bread coating as the Fried Pickles. I know that makes it easier in the kitchen, but a difference in coatings would have set these two apart. However, they were still an excellent choice and I am glad Fannie Flagg wasn't with me, because she probably would not have shared.

Each time I've gone, I've had the same sides. I know, I need to try the others, but the Mac-n-Cheese is so good. It reminded me of some of the mac-n-cheese I enjoyed as a child at family picnics. The cole slaw is good, but being a pepper man, I had to add a few shakes of my favorite spice. 

In closing I'll give a quick shout out to their sweet tea. Usually a Southern restaurant makes the sweet tea overly sweet, but Gus has tweaked it just right. Also, what is a Southern dinner without a slice of pie? It's a dinner that is not complete, so order up and enjoy a slice of Pe-can pie, because u-can. 

When: Multiple Times
Why: Fried Chicken

What do you do when you literally have eaten everything on the menu? You check and see if there's an off the menu special of the night. That's what I had to do the other night and the kitchen at PS knocked it out of the park with their special. 

The special was a Ribeye and they did it equally as well as any steakhouse in the city. They prepared it to my requested medium-rare and served it with Fingerling Potatoes and Green Beans. It all was delicious and as always my Manhattan was a perfect pairing. 

PS never disappoints me, with food, cocktails or service. I cannot wait to see what they do with The Bellwether. I'll have two great places to frequent. 

I'll be back? - PS is my go to in STL. 

When: February 27, 2019
Why: Late Dinner

My love affair with Spencer's Grill has continued on. They offer good food at a great value, served by some of the perkiest and friendliest staff. I have almost eaten my way thru the entire menu, if I haven't enjoyed a listing one of my friends dining with me has. 

As promised in my last review, I've been back to try the diner style burger. There just is something about a grill seared burger from a diner. It is simple and full of flavor. I enjoyed a Double Cheeseburger with lettuce, tomato and onion. This burger was better then those I have had at Carl's Drive In. The fries served as a side were well seasoned and extremely crispy with a hot and soft inside. 

My favorite breakfast at Spencer's is one of their omelettes. They are made with only two eggs, which in my opinion is large enough. They are also filled with the appropriate amount of ingredients. So many other places, over produce omelettes and I am unable to finish my order.  Here, I clean my plate and feel totally satisfied. 

I must also let pancake lovers in on a little secret, Spencer's serves them up with a twist. Here you can order them crispy and they'll come to you with crisp edges. I don't know how they work their magic, but it adds an extra kick of flavor. 

In closing, I just want to give an extra shut out to the wait staff. They are all exceptionally friendly and well trained. They work as a team and make sure everyone is treated as if they were family or a personal friend.

#curbside #togo #pandemic

Nailed it! 

Let's be honest, yes I would have rather been sitting at the bar with a Margarita enjoying my chips, hot salsa with a side of queso. However, taking my carry-out order home and enjoying it with a classic episode of Law & Order was just as enjoyable and delicious. The carry-out Margarita, surprised me. It had the same refreshing taste, as if it had just been shaken behind the bar. Of course, I gave mine a good stir before pouring it over ice at home. 

I also enjoyed two of my favorite tacos, Hot Chicken and Baja Grilled Fish. When I saw that the to-go vessel held three tacos, I felt guilty not ordering a Portobello as well. My ride home is approximately 5 miles. The tacos were still as warm as, if they were carried out from the kitchen and placed in front of me at the bar. 

The process of ordering on-line was simple. I was out running errands and decided I wanted Mexican for lunch. So I drove over to Soulard, parked and ordered on my iPhone. After completing my order they gave me approximate time it would be ready and when it was being bagged up, they sent me a text message telling me it was ready. So easy and well organized. 

To make it safe for everyone they have signage up encouraging everyone to stand 6 feet apart while waiting for you order. They even took it a step further and have marking on the sidewalk for those who do not know the difference between 6 inches and 6 feet. 

Will I return? - Hell, yes. Curb-Side or Dine-In 

When: May 8, 2020
Why: I worked Cinco De Mayo and needed Tacos.

OMG! The "Famous" Slider Mary is meal all by itself. It's a spicy hot Bloody Mary and has an, The All American slider as a garnish. That is right, a Slider is perched on a skewer towering high above your cocktail. Order a side of Fried Pickles, Parmesan Fries or Fried Green Tomatoes and you've got a light lunch. However, that is not what I did......I ordered more. 

By chance I walked in on opening day.......a surprise to me, but it was a delightful surprise.  After being served one of the best Bloody Mary's and sampling the beef slider, I had to have more. I ordered the Slider Plate, which allows you to enjoy two regular sliders and 1 regular side. Being the King of Fried Pickles, I paid an additional $1 upgrade to have pickles instead of fries or house chips. The pickles were traditional dill pickle chips and only lightly dusted with a seasoned coating. I really liked that the taste of the pickle dominated the flavor instead of the breading which happens at so many other restaurants. 

Now, let's talk sliders. The menu has a variety of beef sliders, just like any burger bar, the only difference is they are "sliders". They also had multiple chicken sliders, veggie sliders and for those who need gluten-free, they've got you covered as well. Since, I had the All-American with my Bloody Mary, I opted for The Classic Ruben and Nashville Hot Chicken as my two choices. 

The Classic Ruben was the perfect size to go along with my fried pickles. It was served on a small pretzel bun and the corned beef is made in house. They topped it with big eye swiss, sauerkraut, caraway and 1000 Island Dressing. I love a good Ruben and this one hit the spot. 

My Nashville Hot Chicken, surprised me. It actually lived up to its' name, "HOT". It may have had a burning sensation to it and definitely had me wiping my brow, but it got my curiosity up on how good their chicken wings may be. The Nashville Hot Chicken was hand breaded fried chicken, the piece was huge and hung out on all sides of the white slider bun. It was topped with coleslaw, pickle and that hot and tasty Nashville Secret Hot Sauce. 

The service was extremly friendly and welcoming. Slider House is based in Nashville and it is apparent that they have brought Southern Hospitality with them. In addition to my server being bubbly sweet, others stopped by to get my opinion on the Bloody Mary and Fried Pickles. 

This is going to be a great place for lunch, Happy Hour and business luncheons. It's going to be a restaurant for everyone, but this is definitely a mans restaurant. I see the Slider House being one of the Hot new openings of 2016. 

When: February 24, 2016
Why: Lunch

The angels were definitely singing the night I dined at Twisted Tree. I will be honest, if it were not for the stellar review from Joan G., I may have never tried TT. I hate to admit it, but what kept me away was the fact that  a steakhouse was connected to Syberg's. I questioned how a restaurant known for its chicken wings, and being a sports bar, could prepare a high quality steak? I learned my lesson on being judgmental very quickly. They can do it very well. 

I arrived around 6:30 PM on a Saturday night without a reservation. As my usual protocol, I informed the hostess I did not mind sitting at the bar. She directed me to the left side, where 4 stools were awaiting and told me to make myself comfortable. As I selected my throne for the night, I was cheerfully greeted by Lindsey one of the multiple bartenders working that evening. She took my order for a Manhattan and quickly began to prepare it before my eyes. Her skills were fast and masterful - I enjoyed my Manhattan so much, I had two that evening. 

When she presented me my cocktail, she asked if I'd be dining at the bar. When I replied yes, she immediately set me up with a white linen place sitting. I knew I wanted the infamous onion rings, so I placed my order for them. When they arrived, they totally lived up to their reputation. They're light, flakey, crisp and the seasoning is like no other onion ring. I normally don't dip my onion rings, but they presented a buffalo sauce and ketchup for dipping. Most of the rings I ate without dipping, but the buffalo sauce provided an extra kick to those that I did dip. 

As I munched on the rings, Lindsey and chatted about her favorite sides. I told her I was famished and most likely would order two sides. An extra side with an entree order is only $3. When you see the size of the serving, you realize it is a steal of a deal. I also had the option of not having a salad and enjoying the two sides. I was a glutton and wanted it all. 

For my entree, I ordered an 8 oz Prime Rib, medium rare. I also enjoyed; Caesar Salad, White Cheddar Potatoes Au Gratin (a Lindsey favorite) and Fire Roasted Brussels Sprouts (my favorite vegetable). The prime rib was prepared to my requested temperature. It was so tender, my steak knife slid through it like a warm knife through butter. I then tried just breaking off a bite with my fork and it again was simply done. It was capital T - tender. 

Both side dishes were, killer good. I will always order Brussels Sprouts when I see them on a menu. These are definitely prepared well. They had that crisp fresh texture. They were not over cooked or under cooked - they were just right. I am so happy that I listed to the bartender and tried the Au Gratin potatoes. She also recommended the mashed, but I choose Au Gratin, because of the White Cheddar. Go with one of these potatoes, you can get a Baked Potato anywhere. 

Once again, my eyes were bigger then my stomach. I had enough food to take home and make my co-workers jealous with an incredible lunch the next day. To be honest, I still came home with some Brussels Sprouts and Au Gratin Potatoes from that work lunch. No worries, the sprouts made a flavorful frittata and the potatoes became breakfast potatoes. 

Even though I was stuffed and didn't clean my plate, I had to have dessert. I love Wedding Cake and had to try theirs. I had seen so many pictures on Yelp and everyone raved how good it was. Everyone was right, it hit the spot and satisfied my sweet craving without being overly sweet. It a great way to enjoy one of your favorite cakes, without getting married or going to wedding. Yes, I had left-overs and I took them to work and finished off the slice of cake with my morning coffee. It may not have been the healthiest breakfast, but it was damn good. 

A highlight that makes Twisted Tree stand out above the other upscale steakhouses is that; a salad and one side is included in the price of your entree. Everything is not A la carte. That is a win-win. 

Will I return? - I'm a meat man, so that answer is, YES!

When: December 2, 2017
Why: Dinner - Super Belated Birthday with Gift Cards

The envelope, please and the winner of best Fish Fry of Lent Season 2019 is, Edibles & Essentials. At least in my opinion it is.
