Every Friday during Lent, E&E had their food truck, Essentially Fries parked out front serving up the absolute best fries and fried fish. With a food truck that specializes in fries, you already know the fries are going to be good. Well, let me tell you they can also fry up some crispy, flakey and flavorful fish. I had a lot of fish this Lent season and even though this was my last on Good Friday, it was also the best. I wish they'd do this at least once a month. If they did, I'd be here. 

After ordering from the food truck and paying at the food truck, you could go inside and enjoy your meal. I enjoyed mine with a couple glasses of white wine. 

The staff here is always so friendly and engaging. It may be order at the counter and take a table marker, but the service is still top notch and attentive. 

I'll be back? - Absolutely! 

When: April 19, 2019
Why: Lent - Good Friday - Fish Fry

Have you ever put something in your mouth and your taste buds instantly make your eyes pop out of your head? I am fairly certain that is what happened to me this morning, after taking my first bite of a glazed twist from WFD.  I hadn't even bitten down , to take a bite and the buds were already, singing praises. 

I took my first bite at the stoplight, before entering on to 44 east and immediately tossed it back into the bag. This was not a donut to eat while driving, it was a donut to enjoy with a hot cup of coffee or a cold glass of milk once I arrived to work.  I kind of always thought a glazed donut was just a glazed donut, nothing special to write home about and now here I am writing about one on Yelp.  It was moist, had a unique sweetness to it and I scratch my head in wonderment if they use buttermilk.  

In the Homer Simpson guide book to eating donuts, I think it is rule #4, you should never just order or eat just 1 donut. So not wanting to break one of Homer's rules, I also enjoyed a Chocolate Long John.  The John was good, but not as amazing as the glazed delight. It did have an ample spread of chocolate from end to end and side to side, giving it an edge over other donut shops within the city limits. 

I was disappointed that they do not serve my favorite "donut holes", but with a glazed twist like the one I had this morning I can forgive them.  Plus, the couple who were working the early morning shift (5 AM) were picture book Grandma and Grandpa. 

If you think there is no dough ($) to be made in donuts, take note of the Mercedes Benz in the parking lot with a personalized license plate - DONUTS. 

WFD is now marked off my Yelp Bucket List and I recommend this STL jewel to everyone.

Psst, come here and I'll tell you a secret. No, come closer I've got to whisper it or everyone will know. Some of the best Italian in Saint Louis is not on The Hill, it can be found on Lindell near SLU. 

I will be honest, I may have not ever discovered Vito's if it were not for my Chicago Yelp friend, Lupe D.. She had Living Social Coupon she was not going to be able to use and shared it with me. Wow, it goes to show Yelp friendships can extend beyond your hometown.

We begun our Vito's experience with Calamari Fritti and it was a great way to start. 
The pieces were huge and covered in enough breading to get a crispy texture. They were served with a side of freshly made marinara sauce, but I enjoyed mine with a fresh squeezed lemon. 

Next was Crispy Caesar Salad and fresh hot baked bread. The bread was so warm when served to our table, that the butter melted easily. Making it a perfect complement to our salads. Vito's uses only the hearts of romaine for their Caesar Salad and combined it with Crunchy Croutons and Shaved Parmigiano Cheese. My tummy was content at this point, but we still had more to come. 

Our entrees were Parpadelle Bolognese and Linguine Con Vongole, both were superior to fare I have had recently on "The Hill". The Parpadelle had a rich Marinara sauce combined with ground beef and peas. They then topped it with fresh shaved Parmigiano. My Linguine Con Vongale was absolutely perfect. I was amazed at the large number of littleneck clams that they tossed in white wine, olive oil, fresh garlic, lemon and parsley. Both servings were large enough for two to share after having a salad. 

Our server was friendly and attentive to all the tables around us. Taking note of the other food being served around us, we know that we will be back for more great food at Vito's.

Yippie! I no longer have to drive over to Belleville to enjoy the best Pork Steak in the metro area. Now that the Beast has opened in The Grove, their Pork Steak can be billed the best in the state of MO. 

Their Pork Steak is so delicious from the seasonings of the dry rub, there is no need to use any sauce. It is also so tender, there's no need to use the steak knife that is provided. I was able to pull and tear it apart into small bite size pieces without using the knife. 

The sides are sold separately. To accompany my huge pork steak, I choose; Bacon-Mac and Brussels Sprouts with Belly. How could I go wrong with either of these. The Mac was rich and creamy with cheese and then adding bacon made it even yummier. The Brussels Sprouts were crisp and served with pieces of pork belly. What a great way to get your green vegetable in for the day. 

The restaurant is order at a counter and find a seat with a table marker. Runners will then bring you your order on sheet trays. Ambiance is retro contemporary minimalist (if that can be a thing). The staff is friendly and attentive, very similar to that of the original location in Belleville. 

I'll be back? -Yes, I love that Pork Steak

When: June 15, 2019
Why: Grand Opening

The Mack is truly a hidden jewel in South Hampton neighborhood. I would have never discovered the diamond in the ruff if it were not for Mark S. telling me about it in a Hamburger talk thread here on Yelp. Thanks Mark, for expanding my burger world. 

We went for lunch yesterday and had a totally enjoyable meal. When having a burger for some silly reason, I always need to start out with an order of chicken wings. I always get a giggle when a menu says, "Our Famous Chicken Wings". The Mack, lives up to that boast. Their wings are crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. They have just the perfect amount of spice and kick.

After the wings,  I had a Half Pound Burger with Pepper Jack Cheese and the SO enjoyed The Southside Burger. Both were charbroiled to perfection and I love it when a burger is hand pressed. There is something, about a burger that isn't perfectly shaped that seems to add flavor. 

My burger was topped with rings of white onion, lettuce and a slice of tomato that made it perfect. It was as if I were enjoying a juicy burger at a backyard cook out. 
The Southside Burger was topped with Cheddar Cheese, Crispy Onion Rings and BBQ Sauce. Both burgers were huge in size, so huge that we had to take some of ours home. When they brought us our box to take our leftovers, I was pleased to see that their container was Eco-Frinendly. 

They offer two kinds of fries to compliment your burger; "traditional" and "waffle". 
The traditional were slender, crispy and had a seasoning similar to Lawry's. which is A+ to me. The waffle fries were huge and I loved how they held the ketchup when dipping. 

Their server did a great job of waiting on the tables and serving the bar, she is trained well. By that, I mean she is trained like Pavlov's dog. When food is ready, the kitchen pushes a buzzer that you can hear behind the bar and off she goes to retrieve it. I found it funny and when I shared my laugh with her, she laughed too. She commented that she never thought of that, but it was so true. 

I am a new fan of The Mack and it is being added to 3 of my lists; Burgers, Wings and Eco-Friendly.

Did St. Louis really need another craft beer taproom? Of course, we did. 
A city can never have too many brew hubs. Especially when the city was just named #1 for Best Beer Scene 2018 by USA Today. 

BHT is tucked away and kind of hidden on Oakland, but it is a great addition for the city and area. So many restaurants have come and gone in this space, but I think this one is going to make it. 

During my first visit, I was alone and sat at the bar for lunch. The bartender was attentive and helped me select my Flight of Four Beers. My favorite of the four was one she suggested, KeyBilly. I'm looking forward to coming back and trying their Chicken Wings which are made with the same beer. 

Talking with the bartender, I mentioned I was a fan of lamb and she then recommended the Lamb Burger. I'll admit it was not as good as 5 Stars or Scottish Arms, but for the price I was damn impressed. I'd definitely order it again. No fries here, all burgers and sandwiches are served with a side of Brew Hub Chips. They are house made and crisp. They're a nice change from the standard fries at bars. 

As stated, the service was attentive and friendly. They have free Wi Fi which is great for those of us who are addicted to social media. Gotta stay connected to; Yelp, Untappd, Instagram and Twitter. 

I'll Be Back? - With a friend in tow. 

When: March 13, 2018
Why: Lunch at the Bar

I cannot believe that I have not written a review for Corner Bistro - I've eaten here so many times that I have almost experienced the entire menu. I guess I thought all the pictures that I have posted, were my review. After all, they do say that a picture is worth a thousand words.

Since I've eaten here multiple times, I am just going to list some of my favorites:

Bistro Burger - A hand pressed burger, topped with Applewood crisp bacon, cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion and what I can only assume is a secret Bosnian spice. The flavor is unique and makes the burger stand out from a typical American hamburger. It was served with crispy fries and a little cup of ketchup. 

Spicy Chicken Wings - Ooey Gooey Spicy sauce covered the entire wings. Finger licking good and good thing they have paper napkins over linen, because you need to use serval to keep fingers clean. 

Ham & Cheese Panini - Puts Panera Bread to shame. Thinly sliced ham, smoked cheese, roasted red peppers, lettuce, tomato and mayo on a Ciabatta bread. The sandwich is crisply toasted on the outside and the ingredients on the inside are piping hot. A side of crispy fries makes this a winning combination. 

Their pizzas are some of the best in STL. You'll be surprised how tasty they are and they do not use provel. 

Chicken & Mushroom - Freshly sliced mushrooms and diced white meat chicken. 

Meat Lovers - Hamburger, pepperoni and bacon. The perfect combo of meat. 

Buffalo Chicken - (My favorite) A zesty cheese pizza topped with chicken tossed in buffalo sauce and drizzled with ranch dressing and more buffalo sauce. Totally different and worth the experience. 

I also give a thumbs up to the house salad and Bruschetta.

I've dined in and I've called ahead for carry-out and every time I have been pleased with my meals. The service at times can be slow, but that has never bothered me, because the food is that damn good. The dining room inside is small, but when the weather is good the patio almost doubles the amount of tables available. 

I want this place to continue to succeed, so I recommend it to all pizza lovers. I just hope it doesn't get so popular that I cannot get in to enjoy one myself.

It was time to bring a busy day, to an end and we wanted to relax, nosh and drink. We thought it would be a great time to try Retreat Gastropub. Being a Sunday night, it wasn't very busy when we arrived, but the hostess was sitting everyone next to each other. She placed us in a corner deuce. We felt cramped and the table next to us was having an intense conversation, so we opted to move to the bar for more comfort. 

Once seated at the bar, I ordered a Manhattan and my friend had a Southside. My friend enjoyed her Southside, but I must say the Manhattan was the worst one I have ever had. I couldn't wait to finish it, so I could order a Paloma which they did well. 

We grazed through our small plates, ordering them one or two at a time. Brussels Sprouts is a favorite vegetable for the two of us, so we knew we had to start with them. Undercooked and minimal flavor. Next we moved on to chicken wings and fries. Both of these got thumbs up from both of us. I preferred the parmesan aioli over the smoked tomato sauce served with the fries.  The chicken wings were deep fried and we choose the garlic herb butter over buffalo sauce and I recommend that you do the same. 

The night ended with Candied Bacon and Pork Toasts. You really can't go wrong with crispy bread, goat cheese (my favorite), braised pork and micro greens. I'll order this again, but I'll have them hold the micro greens, they just didn't add flavor to the toast for me. The Candied Bacon was a big yawn and proved to us that ordering the bacon dish is not always a good choice. 

The atmosphere is casual and relaxing, a little loud, but you're still able to have a conversation with ease. I want to come back and hopefully raise my rating once I try the Mac-n-Cheese, burger or veggie sandwich. Also, instead of a house cocktail, next time I'll enjoy a cold craft beer. 

When: November 8, 2015
Why: Dinner

Taco Circus's new location is definitely a three ring circus. The main ring of course is the bar area, with the other rings being a large dining room and huge colorful patio. I attended their soft opening and was luck enough to snag a seat at the bar and had a prime view entire show. 

Let say first, I was impressed that all Margaritas are made from scratch. There are no mixes at this circus. I enjoyed a House Margarita and it was as fine and strong as a top shelf at many other local Mexican restaurants. I can't wait to go back and try the Circus Margarita and the Mexican Martini. The gentleman next to me had the martini and he raved about it. 

To accompany my Margarita I had an order of chips and queso. They claim the queso blanco is the creamiest in town. I cannot confirm that, but it was thick and would cling to the thick chips making the dipping so much easier.  The chips were thicker then most and also a little more salty. I may hold the salt on the rim of my Margarita, but I'm a saltaholic, so I enjoyed the extra salty chips. 

My main attraction was a Steak Quesadilla. They take two XXL 12 - inch tortillas and filled them with Skirt Steak and Cheese. It was so huge, I had to take half of it home. So this is a dish that could easily be shared. It was seasoned well and had plenty of cheese oozing out and around the good sized pieces of steak. 

Considering it was a huge crowd and a soft opening, I think the staff and kitchen did a good job keeping up with the high volume. I'm looking forward to future visits once they have officially opened their, "circus". 

I'll be back? - May be my new go to for Mexican. 

When: September 12, 201
Why: Soft Opening at new location.

We were totally blown away with our first visit to The Block. I will say, it is by far the BEST BURGER and Best Mac - n - Cheese in the city. Both of these menu items were totally off the charts.

Our lunch started with two salads; Asparagus Salad and Block Salad. I enjoyed a small Asparagus Salad, which was the perfect size to enjoy before a Block Burger. I'm confident that a large would be a meal by itself. Which would be a dream for a vegetarian. It was not only grilled asparagus, but it also had mixed greens, roasted beets, goat cheese (my favorite), toasted walnuts and tossed in a balsamic vinaigrette . 
The BF enjoyed The Block Salad which was not your typical chef salad. It may sound like it, but when you add their bacon, smoked ham, smoked cheddar to greens, tomato, egg, red onion and toss it with a Buttermilk dressing it becomes a culinary masterpiece. He too, enjoyed the small size. Again, the large would be a perfect meal for someone who is watching their weigh or just wanting a health choice for lunch. 

Now let's talk about the two items that are taking the #1 position on two of my Yelp list. The Block Burger was a huge 8 oz. grass fed beef, grilled medium and topped with farmhouse white cheddar. It was the most juicy, well seasoned and grilled burger I have had in a long time. I do not know what kind of grass those cows were eating, but it made that burger the best. If that wasn't enough, the Garlic Herbed Fries were the perfect accompaniment with a little cup of ketchup. 

I had heard so much about their amazing Baked Mac -n - Cheese, that I had to have some. Since we both had salad and entrees, we ordered a small so we could experience a little bit of heaven. It was rich, creamy and baked in a little cast iron casserole dish to give a perfect crunchy top. The table of three next to us, ordered a large portion and it was perfect for sharing. It would of been enough it they had a fourth. 

Paula Deen may be in need of some comfort food right now and I know what would make her feel better. A healthy portion of the Shrimp & Grits at The Block. Their grits can put a smile on any Southern Belle or Gentleman. Add 4 huge shrimp on top of the cheddar grits and you've got a great lunch. 

My only negative is that we arrived early for lunch early and as others arrived they clustered them around our table. They had everyone on top of each other. In a large dining room, it made us feel cramped. However, making 7 of my list and a cute water faucet  that resembled a old fashion water pump in the men's room gives them a solid 5 Stars.

It's been almost two years since my last review of Olio. Since that time, there have been staffing and management changes and when that happens the atmosphere of a business also change. Olio is still a relaxing and comfortable place to enjoy a masterfully created cocktail, but it no longer has the warm fuzzy feeling it once had. The service has almost become, cold and stiff. It is still very professional and attentive, just not as welcoming as it use to be. For that reason, I need to drop them down a star. 

I do agree with Ian Froeb that Olio is definitely one of the top 100 restaurants in St. Louis. However, I disagree with on the must have item. I do enjoy his recommendation; King of Kings hummus, served with pieces of both pita bread and baguette. The portion is huge and will have a low-carb eater, forgetting their ways until the bowl of hummus and basket of bread are empty. 

My recommendation of the "must have" is their egg salad and you must add the white anchovies. The creamy egg salad is served on slices of baguette with those salty little fishes resting on top. This is by far the best egg salad in the St. Louis area. If they sold it by the pound like a deli, I'd be an addict. 

What makes their service stand out is that when  you're seated at the bar and your order is ready, they do not just sit it in front of you from the bartenders side of the bar. Which would be the easy and quickest way. They walk around and serve it from your back and to the left side. That fine dining etiquette, making them a class act. 

I hope the warm fuzzies come back, because I love a good cocktail & their egg salad. 

When: March 22, 2016
Why: After Work Cocktails

The Top Ten Reasons to Love Carl's Drive-In

10. Fries and Onion Rings from a bag.
9.  Soft Grilled Buns.
8.  Counter Seating Only - Small & Cozy
7.  Biodegradable China
6.  Prompt Service with Attitude
5.  Nostalgic Ambiance
4.  Milkshakes in only two flavors
3.  Foot long Hot Dogs
2.  House-made Root Beer in Frosted Mugs

And the number 1 Reason:

The Best Flat Grilled Burgers in Saint Louis!!!

WOW! I cannot tell you how excited I was waiting for the Copper Pig to open. Now that it has opened, I am sad to say, it is the winner of a Stevie B Yelp Award. It is the winner of; The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015. They disappointed me with; food, cocktails and service.

Let me start off with the positive points that saved them from getting a 1 Star Review:

1) Linen Napkins - They're always give a nice upscale feeling to any restaurant. 
2) Eco-Friendly To-Go Vessels - Thinking of our planet. 
3) French Fries - European style fries & a little cup of ketchup. 
4) It's in my hood - Brings variety and vitality to the neighborhood.
5) Girl with water pitcher always made sure your glass was full. (Also see negative point)*

Now the reasons why it was The Absolute Worst Meal at a Restaurant in 2015:

1) Service - Very rushed. We ordered cocktails and three appetizers. When our drinks were served, waitress asked for the rest of our order. We stated we wanted to wait until our small plates arrived. Later when the small plates arrived, she again asked for order. When we ordered a second round of drinks, she responded, "I meant your entrees". The time we were there, it was obvious they wanted us to eat, drink and go as quickly as possible. 
2) Deviled Eggs with Bacon Chips - Had the taste of refrigerator.
3) Crispy Brussel Sprouts with Miso and Bacon - Bacon dominated the dish with Brussels Sprouts that were undercooked and hard. Dish was overly salty. Good thing for the water girl. 
4) Beet Fries - Tasteless. I love beets and these were flavorless mush. I think they were prepped to far in advance. 
5) Bulgogi Cheesesteak - Tough and hard to chew. Disassembled sandwich to see if that would help, but it was the actual beef that was making it tough and chewy. 
6) Board Burger - Mealy burger, with a grey tint. My friend said, it resembled a burger patty from McDonald's. Her dog wouldn't even eat it when served the leftovers which were the majority of the burger. (Take note of photo)
7) Cocktails - Weak and unprofessionally prepared. Obvious their bartenders are more comfortable opening beer bottles and pour a draft beer. No skills in a well crafted cocktail. 

After leaving CP we went down the street to another establishment and ran into several other diners who where at the CP as well. We all compared notes and were in agreement that they have a lot of improving to do. 

I hate for a business in my hood to be on my Terrible Two's List. So I'm going to give them a couple weeks to work their kinks out and hopefully they will. Then I'll revisit them again and hopefully be able to raise my rating.

When: November 12, 2015
Why: Belated Birthday Dinner

It may not be original, but DAMN, The Dam is good. In fact, it is real good. The concept is smart. They offer easy carryout, a small dining area and my favorite option, go next door to The Amsterdam to enjoy a beer and have your food brought over when it is ready.

Their burgers are made with premium Black Angus beef. It is fresh, never frozen. Having been raised on a Black Angus farm, I appreciate it when I see a restaurant promoting Black Angus. Especially when it is  antibiotic and hormone free. 

My burger of choice today was, The Dam. It's a two beef patty delight. One was topped with American and the other with Swiss. They were then placed between two slices of grilled Sourdough bread that had smears of their special Damn Sauce. I added grilled onions for a mere 75¢. It was perfect!

My friend and dining explorer, skipped the burgers and went for his favorite sandwich, The Muffalata. When ever he sees a Muffalato on a menu, he loses all self control and has to have one. The gentleman taking our order, told him that theirs was not the typical round Muffalata and he was comfortable with trying something new. Once it was served to him over at The Amsterdam, he declared it was the BEST Muffalata  he has ever eaten. I got to sneak a bite and I must say, I liked it better then some of the better known deli's in town. 

We shared a order of Belgian Style Fries. I liked that their menu stated, extra crispy. It saved me having to make that request. The small order was enough for the two of us to enjoy with our huge sandwiches. 

The staff is friendly and as stated above, they are willing to deliver your order to the bar next door. 

When: 30 Jan 2014
Why: Lunch

Last year when Ian Froeb announced his STL 100 and Niche was #1, I couldn't wait to go. 
Before I knew it, Gerard was announcing it's closure and I didn't get a reservation in time. I missed out on experience Niche. So when, Sardella landed on the list for 2017 at #6, I wasted no time and went immediately. When I say immediately, I mean I went Saturday night right after his list appeared in GO! Magazine insert to the week-end Post-Dispatch. 

I arrived around 5:45 PM and took a seat at the bar. Dining alone, you can always find a spot at the bar. I started off with one of their signature cocktails; Welcome to Heartbreak. It was a delectable bourbon cocktail, that I was able to sip and enjoy as I relaxed at the bar. I then debated with myself if I wanted Mussels. It wasn't a serious or long debate, I ordered them. 

Their Mussels are listed under, "Small Plates", but my bowl of mussels was huge. They were prepared with; white wine, Creme Fraiche, Thai Chili and Smoked Paprika. Along side these succulent mussels, was a ginormous slice of toasted bread that i used to soak up the mouthwatering broth. Serving size is perfect for sharing, or as a complete light meal for one. 

Since I knew I was coming, I held back all day on eating, so I could feast. After my mussels, I ordered; Gnocchi of the Sea. It is what Ian Froeb says is a, "Must Order". It was scrumptious. I'm a big fan of Crab, so when it was Ian's must order, I was game. Seasoned  with tomato, Chili and Bone Marrow. It's listed as, "Pasta", but the serving size is definitely a "small plate". 

My second cocktail was a, Manhattan one of my favorite Classic Cocktails. Damn, was it good. I always love it when a bar, uses a single large ice cube for my Manhattan. It's  the attentions to details that make a dining experience complete. Sardella pulls out all the bells and whistles on the little details. In addition to the large cube, they offered up cloth napkins, a seafood fork for my mussels and a USB slot under the bar for charging. With the attention to these details, you'd think they'd take notice of the bowl they served my Mussels in. It had chips in the enamel and should be tossed. However, the flavors were so strong, I'm overlooking it and still giving them 5 Stars. 

The bartender who did double duty as my server, was charming and warm. He made me feel comfortable dining at the bar, as we chatted the art of making drinks and their garnishes. 

Will I return? - Gotta experience breakfast and lunch

When: March 4, 2017
Why: #6 on Ian Froeb's STL List 2017

Farewell, Joanie. A friend organized a party at your Pizzeria, so we all could say good-bye. I had never been, so it was a first and last time for me. 

Being on a diet, I didn't order pizza. I enjoyed a Caesar Salad and their house made dressing was top notch. I also had an order of Buffalo Wings, that was a special that evening. For pizzeria wings, they were pretty tasty. 

Our server was accommodating and friendly. She said business had jumped up drastically, since the closure announcement. However, it's still too late to save the business.  

It's sad to see a local business close, especially one who had been open as long as Joanie's. However, from my one visit, I could tell it hadn't changed much since it's opening and perhaps that was the downfall. 

When: February 5, 2020
Why: Announced Closing

St. Louis Union Station Soda Fountain is the perfect spot to have a quick lunch/bite before or after riding, The St. Louis Wheel. 

Our party of three arrived at noon and there already was a wait for tables. Over half the restaurant was filled with convention attendees. It was easy to spot them, they all had lanyards hanging around their necks.  Even with the crowd, our wait was not long. 

Normally, I like the coziness of a booth, but today we were seated at a four-top table in front of the actual soda fountain. It was a great show, it was fun watching the, to use a classic term, "soda jerks" make all the sweet treats. Numerous times we were asking our server, "what's that?".
They all looked so delicious. For our sweet treat, after our lunch we ended up enjoying, The King. 

Now let's talk about the real reason we came here, our lunch before riding The Wheel. I ordered the Single Grilled Cheeseburger and my cousins enjoyed, Fried Chicken Sandwich and a BLT. To accompany our sammies, we all shared two sides; Crinkle Fries and Onion Rings. 

I enjoyed my burger, which was loaded up with the typical, LTOP. A single was enough, I could not imagine eating a double along with a side and one of the sweet treats. My cuz who had the Fried Chicken Sandwich said it crisp, moist and flavorful. She normally doesn't like mayo and had them put it on the side. When it arrived, it was a flavored mayo in a little cup and she liked it. Her husband, enjoyed the BLT. He said the applewood smoked bacon was a flavorful twist on the classic sandwich. 

We were so glad we all shared the our sides. The portions are plentiful and enough to share. The crinkle fries (my favorite style) were crispy and seasoned with just enough salt. The onion rings I found out are not made it house, but I'll tell you that they were pretty tasty for being a frozen product. It could have fooled me, they were that good. 

The dessert, our finale was a delicious sweet treat. As I stated earlier, we went with, The King. It was a delightful mix of sweet and salty. It all centered around a big scoop of peanut butter banana ice cream, surrounded by sliced bananas and covered in peanut butter sauce, topped with bacon and chopped peanuts. A sundae is not complete without the whipped cream topping and maraschino cherries on top. 

Eric our server was a delight. He was honest with his recommendations and didn't mind splitting our checks and that we shared our sides and dessert. I was also impressed that one of the managers was hands on assisting all the servers. She even took time out twice to chat with us about our first visit. The floor captain also came over and thanked us for coming in as we were getting ready to leave. Overall, very friendly staff. 

When: January 9, 20202
Why: Lunch before riding, The Wheel

Thanks Sugarfire Smoke House for making my Memorial Day lunch a success. The 10 oz Brisket Sandwich was a true classic and your Brisket Cheesesteak put all Philly Cheesesteaks to shame. Philadelphia should be scared. 

We shared four sides; Potato Salad, Baked Beans, Creamy Cole Slaw and Pasta Salad. The portions were so huge, we took most of them home to enjoy with the Brats we grilled at home that evening. However, we ate every bite of our sandwiches. I truly love your cole slaw and baked beans. I'd love the recipe for both, but know I'll never get them. 

No matter how busy and slammed you are, your staff is always friendly. They  take the time to make sure all diners are greeted appropriately and make small talk as place your order. I always feel welcomed, which in addition to the great food is why I keep coming back for more. Give me some Sugarfire!

Great addition to Maplewood and a great place to enjoy a beer or two or three. They not only have a large selection of beers, but they have whiskey and wine as well.  The atmosphere is minimalist, very stark and simple. As Kelly B., pointed out it is cute and cozy. Their serving hours are limited, Tue-Thu they are open 3PM-10PM and on Fri & Sat they open at 12PM and stay open an extra hour, closing at 11PM. 

SPC has a very friendly staff and the ones we spoke with are very knowledgeable about the brews they are serving. I'd recommend SPC as a great place to start your evening out or as a relaxing place to enjoy a beer after dinner on the main Manchester drag in Maplewood. 

Warning: Be aware of a step marked only by a strip of lights on the floor, leading you into the bar area. Several patrons arriving misstepped and stumbled while we were sitting at the main bar. No one got hurt, they just shook it off and laughed. Kind of embarrassing when you do misstep and you are sober. 

Hope they add some type of munchie soon, so you can stay longer and enjoy the LARGE variety of beers.

When the most positive thing I can say about a new restaurant is the ambiance, "Houston, we have a problem." They've created a very beautiful space to relax and enjoy your meal. However, the most important points of a restaurant, food and service fall short.

I heard some great things about CSS, so when I was in Creve Coeur at lunch time, I stopped by. Being a lone diner, as my usual, I choose to sit at the bar. Looking over the Signature Cocktail list, they had one of my favorites, Smokey Old Fashion. How could I resist? I should have. It was weak and bland with no smokey taste or garnish. However, I did like the water being served in a Cobalt Blue glass. 

After reading the entrees, I choose their Mixed Grill, but was told it was sold out. They wouldn't have it until dinner, after they received their delivery.  Bartender explained it was very popular and they sell out of it regularly. I then choose their Crispy Catfish Sandwich with Fries. 

Since I was doing a sandwich and not a full entree, I decided to add an appetizer to my lunch. I was torn between the Crab Cakes and the Tempura Green Beans. I asked the bartender and she informed me the crab cakes were really good and were another of their most popular items. I went with the Green Beans, because I wanted a green veggie. 
They were crisp and very lightly coated for a tempura item. The sweet and spicy sesame syrup served as a dipping sauce was delightful. 

My crispy catfish was an extremely thin piece that was dominated by the bread. I did like the hot peppers as a topping to the catfish. When I choose the sea salt chips as my side the bartender informed me they no longer did them and it was fries. When I asked what type of fries, she replied, steak fries. I love steak fries, they're my favorite. So, I said yes to fries instead of the side salad. 

Bartender needs to be educated on the difference in fries. When they arrived with my sandwich, they were Hand-Cut Fries. My second favorite, so I was to upset. However, some thick cut wedges of fries would have been nice. 

Service was not that attentive. The bartender was busy talking with the manager on duty. She was friendly, but considering I was the only one at the bar and the restaurant only had three other tables, you'd think the service would be spot on. 

They're new, I'm sure they'll overcome these little details and bumps. 

I'll be back? - For dinner, I want to try the Mixed Grill

When: May 17, 2019
Why: Hot & New and Lunch

#curbside #togo #pandemic

Applause to, The Blue Duck for their well organized #curbside service during the #pandemic. The process was so easy. I placed my order on line, paid with a card, included my tip and drove over to Maplewood. Once I arrived, I called to let them know I was there and they brought my order out. They placed it on a table, I then picked it up and went home with a juicy delicious slam burger. There was no touching or contact. We were both gloved and living the life in a pandemic world. 

In addition to my slam burger, I also had an order of Tortilla Chips (house made) with Queso. I got these to enjoy the next night during a virtual UYE Happy Hour. Of course, I had to sneak a few while they were warm and fresh. It was a challenge not to devour them all right away, they were that good. However, I'll let you know they were just as tasty the next night with a little warm up in the oven for the chips and the queso did a quick spin in the micro. 

This weeks Slam Burger special had my name written all over it. I'm a sucker for Mexican food and I love a good juicy burger. It was called, the MoMex. They started it out with 8 ounces of house ground chuck with melted white cheddar. Then it was garnished with; bbq sauce, refried beans, house made chorizo, shredded iceberg, tomato, onion and my favorite food accessory, jalapeño. All that goodness could not be put in a regular hamburger bun, it had to have something special. It was all stacked inside a, Green Chili Brioche Bun. OMG! This burger prepared medium rare was kick-ass. This fat boy who has been dieting during this lockdown was in heaven. We all need to cheat once in awhile and being a bad boy this once was so worth it. 

Thanks, Blue Duck for providing your amazing and delicious food curbside during the pandemic. It is making life so much more tolerable. 

Will I return? - Can't wait for this lockdown to end so I can go inside. 

When: April 22, 2020
Why: Curbside - Burger Fix

Three Dog Night had a popular song that hit number 1 on the charts in the 70's. It was appropriately called "One". In the lyrics, it stated, "One is the loneliest number that you'll ever do". That may be true in love, but when it comes to dining sometimes you just want to dine alone.  If you do, avoid HWK. 

Not once, but twice I have been turned  away when wanting to dine here as a single person. The first time when I called to make a reservation, the young lady who answered informed me they preferred not to sit single diners at tables and that I'd have to eat at the bar.  At first I was content with that arrangement, but then she continued to tell me that  those eating at the bar can not select from the entire menu. At that point, I decided not to make the reservation.  I wanted the true HWK experience. After all the reviews have been amazing. 

The second time, I stopped in for early lunch while shopping the main drag in Maplewood.  Once again, I was told I'd have to sit at the bar and order from a "limited menu". When I asked if I could be seated at one of the hightops in the window, she told me she needed to save those for parties of two. The kicker came when I asked if they were already reserved and she said, "no".  I ate else where that day. 

What I do not understand, is why can I go to Chicago dine at such top restaurants such as; Girl and the Goat, RL, The Pump Room, Table Fifty-Two, The Purple Pig, Frontera Grill and The Publican and be welcomed with open arms. Many of the chefs at these restaurants have been on Top Chef and published cookbooks.  How is it that their establishments are welcoming to the lone diner, yet a small Maplewood restaurant is not?

I understand they have a small space, but if you are going to sit single diners at the bar, let them order from the entire menu. Before posting, I shared this review with other friends who are single diners and being women, they said for them they would not feel comfortable eating at the bar and would not eat here if a table was not an option. 

Disclaimer: I did dine here as a couple opening week and was not impressed. I contributed that to opening week jitters and wanted to give them another chance. It is a shame that I have not had that opportunity.

Absolutely delicious.  I had the brisket bbq sandwich with the local greens, amazing!!! Before the group of us headed back to Atlanta we had to stop by and try the hot chicken. Also amazing!! In addition, the fried pickles, cheddar grits, white bbq sauce were all amazing. So ultimately this place is ... amazing!!!!!

It is no exaggeration when I say that Lolita delivered the worst customer service experience I've ever had - I'm talking worse than Mickey D's cashiers at 3 AM on a drunken morning. At least those people smile and ask if you want fries with your burger. Lolita people basically sneer and look down their noses at you.

I'm sorry that we've inconvenienced your customer service Lolita by not being the perfect customers. And by the perfect customers, I'm sorry we didn't come at a time that was convenient for YOU to seat us. 

I get that usually you would prefer we have everyone ready to be seated before we sat down. And we did. But if one of us changes our mind and decides to swap with someone else from another table, that person should certainly have the freedom to do so. How does it inconvenience you in anyway to serve a different person in the SAME seat? Are you that confused that such a small transition totally throws you off your game?

Apparently so because you proceeded to yell at us. May I remind you that in the business of hospitality, the last thing you do is yell at people??

Don't act so shocked when we didn't tip you very well. We didn't pay to get yelled at. But of course you obviously thought we did because then you DEMANDED more tip? Excuse you? You yelled at us, threw a hissy fit, served us food that is marginally better than my lean cuisines (and even that's a generous comment), and margaritas that could have been mistakened for powdered mixed koolaid. 

Lastly, when we expressed our disappointment and terrible experience to the manager, he dismissively said "that's fine by us".

At first I could only laugh incredulously but now I'm just pissed.

By George! Is a good pizza and Italian food restaurant in the Reading Terminal Market in downtown Philadelphia.  Their prices are reasonable and staff is friendly.  During lunch they are busy so expect to wait a bit.  They offer a great variety of food and pizzas!  Their tomato deep dish is great.  Definitely a place to checkout!

Pietro's Pizzeria is a small Italian restaurant in downtown Philadelphia.  It's has a nice atmosphere with pleasant staff.  The restaurant itself is very narrow but long.  The lighting is dim, so use your phones to read the menu.  It's has a bar section as you enter and seating just a few steps above.  The menu is decent with lots of traditional Italian dishes as well as a variety of pizzas.  They do have a number of vegan options to choose from which is nice.  The prices are decent for the amount of food you get. I'll definitely come back and try a few other options.

The Tasty is a small local neighborhood diner with vegan options.  Did I mention small!  Also the staff was not that friendly.  After receiving my order, not once did someone ask me how my food was!  Also I noticed a sign asking everyone to bus their own tables!  Wow... talk about lazy!  The food was okay, not anything special.  The prices seemed a little high for the quality and portions of food.  I'm most likely will not be returning!

Sky Asian Bistro is a nice restaurant in the Philadelphia airport between terminals B & C. They have a decent menu for airport food. Prices are high, but not surprising since it's in an airport.   They have both dine-in and takeout.  What's really nice is their airport employee menu which offers a few items at about half the prices as their full menu.  I've eaten there a few times, the quality and taste are great.  I will continue to eat there!  Highly recommend!

Reading Terminal Market is a huge indoor food market in downtown Philadelphia.  There are hundreds of stalls that offer all kinds of foods from meats to fruits, vegetables and pastries.  If you are hungry this is the place for you.  There are also vendors that offer vegan and vegetarian options as well.  Tons of food to choose from.  Beware, it's crowded.  Parking is difficult as well.  There is very little street parking, however there is a city parking garage which fills up quickly.  Also don't forget to get your ticket validated at the market, otherwise parking is very expensive.  With validation 3 hrs. max for $5, otherwise your looking at about $10 an hour.  It's definitely worth going if you are hungry!

I have been wanting to try this Thai restaurant for awhile now and I ordered carry out which I wouldn't typically do for my first time but I ordered the Thai Kitchen Sample, Hot Chicken Pad Thai, and Steam vegetables!
The vegetables were so fresh with no oils or seasoning!
The Kitchen Sample was absolutely Perfect it you Enjoy trying new foods! My favorite part of the sample were the Shrimp Blankets!! My favorite Part of the meal was absolutely the Crab Rangoon! 
The pad Thai was literally Life changing and I'm
Soooo excited we got it! Get the Thai hot on the side and make it spicier if you're into that! can't wait to go back!!!

I'm sure I'd give this place a better review if they didn't completely diss us by hitting the panic lock to the front door when my boyfriend, friend and I tried to eat here. I'm not sure if its because we're white or because my boyfriend looks like he can put away some serious chicken but either way it was so effed up that we're still LOLling about getting barred from eating here. Wtf guys?

This place is adorable! I came here on the weekend and there was some kind of event going on. In addition to the beautiful selection of plants, they had some other vendors selling beer, chocolate, dainty jewelry, and some other miscellaneous things. I love the idea of this coffee house. There's a section that is outside of the greenhouse where you can sit and do work. There's free wifi. I initially planned on staying here to do some work while drinking my coffee. However, it was too humid there so I just ordered my coffee and left. 

Coffee was great! I ordered the vietnamese iced coffee and it was great. Very relaxing vibes and good coffee. What more could you ask for! Love this place.

I'm sorry to everyone that loves this place in advance for the one star.  My experience here was at the end of Oct. 2007 so maybe things have changed....I'm a nice person...I really am and it would take a lot for me to give a place 1 star, but here's my two cents.

This place looks cute, has a friendly atmosphere, and I was totally digging the organic take on the food.  

BUT here's when organic/environmentally friendly crosses the line for me....

I was enjoying a nice overpriced dinner with a guest.  We thought for the price the food is just okay, we've had much better elsewhere.  I had salmon and he had a fillet.  We were seated downstairs, and towards the end of our dinner I see IT.  What is IT you ask?  

A HUGE cockroach the size of half my hand crawling up and down the wall above my friends head!  HOLY CRAP I told him to get up because it was crawling towards him.  The two of us stood up away from our table and just stared at it not knowing what to do.  We called the waitress over and told her dude you have a fat ass cockroach crawling on your wall.  By then the cockroach had walked up the wall into the shelf where they stored all the glass cups.  So it was in there mingling with all your cups.  The cups are also placed upside down so I'm sure it touched all the rims.  She apologizes to us and that's it...nothing...we didn't get our dinner comp-ed...we didn't get a discount...and the kicker...

NO ONE WASHED THE CUPS where the cockroach walked all over...

What are they trying to do?  Conserve water?!  I think in this case it would've been okay to not save the earth for the sake of sanitation.

(heard there is a new owner/chef..if that's the case i would try it again)4/18/2017
Not the best, not the worst. I did enjoy my meal however the chef would not accommodate me when I asked for just a plain side of pasta instead of to side items. Nobody ever tells you know to that. And fact I found out through Facebook the chef has a major attitude. 

Update September 28th after finding out about the criminal activity of the owner threatening people including a woman who gave a bad review, I will never step foot in that place again. I saw firsthand the threatening messages he sent people. Shame on you.

This place was awesome. I was going on and on about being hungry so we ended up eating here. First of all, not many parking spots out front but plenty of near by street parking. This place is so packed in order to be able to get a parking spot, you'd be a lucky duck to be coming when someone is leaving or you're here as soon as they open their doors. 

When we walked in, it was so packed and every single table was occupied. We had been waiting about 5 minutes or so when two people were getting up from the bar so we sat down in front of the kitchen and grabbed some menus. The waitress was extremely friendly and out food came out quicker than most places with this many people ordering food at the register, tables and calling every other minute. 

First, I want to say how cheap this place is..we spent $20! For twenty bucks each of us had Cubans to take with us and were beyond full walking out the door. I ordered the omelet with chorizo, bacon, Swiss and American cheese, onions and peppers. Just... goodness in egg form, I tell ya.. Just the right amount of everything. No ingredient overpowered another. You tasted everything in every bite. I was so impressed by this omelet. The waitress also brought some Cuban toast. I decided on some Cafe con Leche to drink - which was made perfectly and paired well with the breakfast. 

Looking around, you can see all of the famous people who came and went. Since President Obama had been here, I decided to get the Cuban (honey Cuban) he ordered to take with me to eat later since they close fairly early. 

Best Cuban I've ever eaten! Tampa is my new favorite place for this sandwich.

So, the second day of our girls trip was starting and we needed good eats. We wanted a good authentic New Orleans breakfast so after seeing the reviews, we decided to go here. We thought we were in for a treat but this turned into the worst breakfast I had ever had. 

First, the food took a while to come out. Then when it did, my friend got the wrong omelet. She bit into it and told the waitress it was wrong. They took FOREVER bringing out the correct omelet. Then when that came she said it was nasty. We spoke to the manager and she then recommended a third dish. My friend said this was better than the Mexican omelet but not the best. So, out of three tries, the amigo breakfast but the best - but it was still mediocre. 

I got the catfish and grits. The grits were plain underneath, no butter, salt or pepper or cheese. The fish was barely seasoned and the sauce on top was not enough. I had to ask for extra to try and her some flavor. When I mentioned to this manager, she said she knew the seasoning was low on the food and that was HER number one complain. MA'AM.. Smh

Lastly, my sister got the meal with three different biscuits and she for hers comped because it wasn't good, either.

All in all, I wouldn't even recommend this place. Hopefully, they make some necessary changes in the future. I have never had a breakfast so bad before. Try anywhere else! I urge you.

One of the worst restaurants I've been to. I had already written a review on Google, but apparently it had been deleted. 

Service: 2/10
Came here with two of my friends. Newly moved to the area and wanted to try the food nearby. Terrible decision. Food took 45 minutes to come out. When it did, some of them were cold, others were piping hot. Took 15 minutes to just try to pay the bill. Tried to flag someone down to pay. The owner had spent 5 minutes talking to a table, looked directly at us, and then proceeded to keep talking. She didn't even at least signal to someone to look our way.

Food: 4-5/10
Uneven delivery of items. Most of them cold, 2 of them hot. Food is as good as Panda express, which to me is a solid benchmark.
For comparison, I'd give the Hot Wok down the street a 6-7/10 simply because their decent price matches the taste of their food.

Price: 1/10
Overpriced for mediocrity.

So far, I'm liking the new location and most of the ambiance.  I did not spend any time in the outside bar, but inside, the new trendy, sleek look is cool, spacious and all brand spankin' new.

The night I went was on a Tuesday, it was the first night they started Open Mic Night again.  And it was great!  A little speaker/sound tweaking is all it took, although the outside speakers were fuzzy.  Not sure if they need to be replaced or just adjusted.

I had the classic Philly Cheesesteak.  The same one they made on the island.  And when I mentioned to Bondo that's what we had and was just as good as it used to be, he was so proud and told me he made sure to train them (even with a video) so that it wouldn't lose what was so special about it.  I really liked it!

The bar could be a little more English-authentic.  But overall, it's a great bar.  Unfortunately, I'm not happy with the cider selection and ended up with a Hoegaarden.  Next time, I'll dig deeper for something a little less popular....I mean, they do have (or had) hundreds of beers!  What happened to the Wall of Foam? I wonder.

There were a lot of people in there on this Tuesday night.  I sure do hope it can keep it's island-like neighborhood feel like it used to.  There did seem to be quite of few of the ole regulars, but also new folks.  What was great about the old location was the varied mix of people.  I think (and hope) this new spot will still maintain that mix.  Will be coming back again and again!

This review is for dockside take out. I loved this experience. In fact it was so fun and enjoyable I would do this every day if I could.

Some friends and I were kayaking through harbor island and around to the aquarium and saw a sign on the outside of their dock that said call for dockside service. We thought how much fun would that be!?
Let's do happy hour!

We weren't sure if they would even deliver sangria to the dock but when we showed up on our kayaks we called them ordered a half gallon of sangria delivered to the dock we were excited. Because they DO!

When the server came he wasn't sure what to think because he had never seen anybody show up in kayaks before LOL.
We thought it was pretty funny too.

We had also ordered some tapas. We got crab croquettes, we got black bean cakes and we got empanadas.  We kinda went all out!

The half gallon was the star of the show. They bring it in a plastic container and the fruit on the side. And they bring large plastic cups. Don't forget to put the fruit in!

Although pretty much everything tapas they serve dockside is fried, it's fun to do. And although I can't realistically do this every day, I can justify doing it every month or so. Definitely doing this again. So much fun!!

I came here for lunch spontaneously one day with a couple friends.  We sat outside in the beautiful courtyard.  I wish I had taken a photo of it but once we ordered our cocktails and they arrived, those became the topic of conversation!

I had a sangria and it was wonderful, the fruits were all lovely and the flavor of the drink itself was very nice and refreshing.  A friend had a bloody Mary and it had a huge shrimp in it and the whole thing looked like a meal in itself!

The staff were very nice and attentive, they filled our water without asking and were on top of everything.  As they should be.

We ordered some guac to go with our chips - this would be the only thing I drop a star for.  Although a decently large portion, it was $8!  WHAT?!  I had a tiny bite of it and they split it across 2 bills without asking.  The bite was a good bite but certainly not worth the $8.  I wouldn't order that again.

The meals came out and were large and very tasty.  I had the tacos one with chicken and one with beef, one soft, one hard.  Both were very good.  I would totally get these again!

There is no doubt I will come back!

I was lured by a friend to attend a singles mixer...had no idea it was in the private room in the back (behind double doors) and it was a speed dating event!  HAHA

I was late, happy hour ended at 6:30, I rushed to review the limited happy hour menu and was super happy to get a sangria and a carnitas taco and quesadilla pollo.

Luis, our server, was super nice, quick and attentive.  He brought me my sangria and it was lovely.  I ordered another later (just with less ice!).

My carnitas taco came and it was soooooo good......and the quesadilla was a lot larger than I thought it would be.  I think the food here, from the taste I had, was a perfect teaser for me to return because I enjoyed it all!

Besito also has an outdoor area, I think I would enjoy dining out there.... will return! Hopefully soon!

I've been here just a few times and each experience has always been spectacular.
This small unassuming spot in the corner of the Bayshore Plaza on MacDill is truly great.

First, when you are greeted by Spartaco, you know right off the bat you are going to have an interesting time.  The number of specials spouted out are almost as many as the items on the menu.  We always seem to order off the menu, the specials are just too great to pass up!

On our last visit, it was our anniversary.  I asked if there was a special anniversary table for us and was told there was a special wait.  That is very typical.  Expect to wait.  But no worries, the wait is very well worth it.  And head on down to Bianchi's for a glass of wine and they will call when your table is ready.  Great partnership there.

Once seated and our favorite appetizer of pear and cheese pasta "sachets" (but don't say that because that's French and this is NOT a French restaurant, Spartaco will certainly make sure you know that!  ;)) and cheese filled gnocchi, WOW, what a great way to start.

My husband picked a Super Tuscan wine to go with our entrees, him the linguine with white clam sauce and me the veal piccata (no capers please!).  Both dishes were fabulous, as expected.

Toward the end, we were asked if we were interested in dessert.....sure wish we had room.  But then Spartaco brought us each a flute of Moscato.....so good I thought it was a sweet Riesling..... and when we asked what this was for, he said "it's part of the plan" which was quite a surprise for us.

We were brought out a plate with cream puffs and cannolis and gelato.  WOW.  We couldn't NOT eat it!  And it was so wonderful.

Spartaco really helped make our anniversary dinner fun and special.  We are definitely sold (again) and will be making it a more regular spot to dine.  It sure had been way too long since we had been.  That will change!

K-Paul's has been a favorite of mine for years. While in the French Quarter I always make a point of having at least two meals at K- Paul's Louisiana Kitchen. They are exceptional. Chef Paul Prudhomme is man who loves food, and knows how to run a restaurant. His hospitality back in the eighties has kept me going back for more.In 1985 we were invited into his kitchen where he and his wife K talked food with us for more than an hour. -- I left that kitchen a serious foodie.   

Now for what we had--for 6 people
Drinks 

Cajun Martini's served in a mason jars. They kick butt.
And are made with Jalapeno's, so they're hotter than hell.
They limit one per person. Think about--it's a mason jar.
 
Pomegranate Martini  
  
Creole Mary- spicy

K-Paul Cosmo 

 One Bottle of Decoy Meritage
  
First courses
Salad -with green onion dressing (created at K-Paul's ) 

Gumbo

 Complimentary basket of 4 different house made breads 
Yeast rolls
Corn bread muffins
Molasses bread 
Jalapeno cheese  bread.
  
Complimentary
Special sausage appetizers
Special curry appetizers.  
Both were amazing 

Main courses
Crawfish Etouffee -Everyone that had it, loved it. Spicy... but not like once was. 
It used to make my eyelids curl. 

Jambalaya- another hit. 

And my Blackened stuffed Pork Chop. 
Let me tell you a little bit about this pork chop. 
It is stuffed with ricotta, Asiago, Mozzarella and Caclocavello cheeses, and fresh basil, then it is seasoned and blackened in a cast iron pan, and served with a Marchand de vin sauce of Prosciutto, red wine and mushroom. Even the words "food orgasm" doesn't cover this one. Not descriptive enough. 

Desserts
Bread Pudding 
And special cupcakes--I liked Lainie's better

 K- Paul's Louisiana Kitchen is always a 5 star experience for me. 

I'm closing my eyes and imagining I'm back on Chartres Street.

Overdue review, I really need to be better about stuff like this, especially a place that is so deserving of a five star review. This place hits all the notes for me. It's not fancy, it's family run, it's stood the test of time because the food is really good. 

I love a good local place, with friendly people that know how to show an out of towner some good old fashioned hospitality. I was lucky enough to get one of the last available corner tables during dinner time, apparently they were holding the spot for someone that wasn't there on time, so my wait wasn't a long one. Big open room, reminded me of Club Lucky here at home. A good mix of people, young, old, couples and families. Everyone breaking bread and having a great time.

I had a glass of the house red, salad and the manicotti special. If you get the salad, do get the house made blue cheese dressing, you will not be disappointed, the three different sauces on the manicotti is a nice touch, however I think I prefer the traditional red the most. Even the bread was a treat.

If you're looking for a quiet romantic restaurant to gaze into your lover's eyes, this isn't it. But if you're looking for a great meal, it is. Of course you can still do the eye thing if you want :)

You have a few choices if you want BBQ in the vicinity.  Red, hot, and blue attached to the Holiday Inn and Famous Dave's a mile or two down the road.  Red, hot, and blue has declined significantly over the years while Famous Dave's is too much of a dining ordeal.  

If you want a good value with little to no fuss, I'd go to Whole Hog.  Order at the counter one of a number of options and they'll have it ready for you.  The portions are generous and plentiful.  If you're in the area, give them a try.

Ugh, Reno, come on buddy help me out here! I can't be the only local who had the worst food here, can I? 
I came here at the end of April with my husband for date night. We were seated right away and I didn't even need to look over the menu because I had been stalking food pictures of Zozo's online. I decided on cheese tortellini with creamy pesto and a side salad with their house dressing. The salad arrived to the table and it was swimming in dressing, so much so that I tried to move most of the lettuce off to the side and that is when I found the soggiest, old black lettuce all mixed in. I put my salad to the side, and even though the owner (the man behind the bar - I am assuming is the owner based on other reviews, pics) passed by my table several times, no one stopped to ask if there was an issue. Finally, our server came back to the table, apologized, offered me soup instead (sorry, if I wanted soup I would have ordered that), and then took my salad back to the kitchen. The food arrives and it is so so so bland. The house bread was simply hot dog buns! (I am not even kidding, I wish I had a picture to show you)
I had to order an additional side of marinara sauce to make my tortellini have any flavor at all and in the end it was just soggy, over cooked and bland.
We asked for our bill, of course we were charged full price for our meal even though we were unable to eat it, so instead of making a big deal we just paid and left. 
I hope my experience helps someone out there who has taste buds because Zozo's is definitely not the place for you! If you love bland overpriced food - maybe bring grandma with you.

Updated review for 2019: 
Yesterday I stopped by, my husband was craving something sweet and we were in the area so we decided to try these donuts again. 
The selection for vegan donuts was amazing, we ended up with a half dozen between us two, so it's true, you eat with your eyes. 
My selection was : chocolate round donut, French toast, and an apple pie. Oh my gosh that one was amazing! Galen, if you're reading this, please make this one again on Tuesday!! 
My husband had a glazed, French toast and an apple fritter. 
The gal who helped us out was super friendly, and I believe the owner, Galen, who checked us out at the register. 
We got home and tried our donuts, not expecting much from our previous visits and we were wrong! These donuts are good! Puffy, not overly sweet, perfectly dressed or glazed, the chocolate was smooth and not gritty at all... these donuts are amazing!! I think the owner has really listened to some of the complaints and made a few changes and because of that, I added a star and updated this review. Go try them again if you haven't had them in awhile, and if you've never been, GO!!! 







I want to like holy Schmidt donuts more than I do but I just don't. Keep in mind I have only had their vegan donuts sold on Tuesday, maybe their regular donuts are better? For me, the best donut they sell is their vegan French toast, it's crispy on the outside, fluffy in the middle and the glaze is perfect. Every other donut I have tried from here has not been that great even though they look amazing. Their vegan chocolate is a little too on the dark side, it has been gritty every single time I have tried one and that bums me out! My husband always gets a "fritter" always made with different fruit (not just apples) but the fritter is always just dough, no fruit! We actually stopped coming in because they had donuts with cereal labeled as vegan, but the cereal that was used as a topping is not vegan! Fruit loops contain lanolin which comes from sheep! Red food dye used in cereal is not vegan either! 
The employees here can vary from very helpful to "what do you want" so sometimes we feel welcome and other times we just get our donuts and go. 
The location is cute, there is always parking available. If have kids you could take them to the discovery museum next door and then take them for a special treat after at the donut shop. And they stay open late. 
I really just wish that businesses who offer vegan options do their homework on animal containing foods before they offer them as vegan options.

Great Full Gardens is one of our favorite restaurants in Reno, and now they have this location in Sparks. 
If you're familiar with the midtown or south reno locations then this place will make you feel right at home. They all share the same menu, and whether you're vegan or paleo or just love food, they have something for you. 
They serve elevated water on all the tables which is magnesium enriched and super amazing for you. They also support local farmers and small businesses, while keeping the foods organic and non GMO. 
Yesterday we tried this new location and even though we had a small hiccup with our order, they were more than accommodating to fix what went wrong. Our server was Dwight and he did an wonderful job checking on us and making sure our order was correct. 
Our order: jackfruit tacos with jalapeno aioli and the jackfruit bbq sandwich with quinoa. These two dishes are always so good, you wont miss the meat at all.  We also had the magic mushroom blend with oat milk- I've been thinking about it all day. (Organic cacao, medicinal mushrooms (chaga, reishi, lion's mane, turkey tail, cordyceps), organic maple syrup, choice of milk. Immune modulating, anti viral, brain health.) I will seriously be coming in more often just for this drink. 
Juli is the sweetest lady ever, she walked around and made sure everyone was happy with their orders and shared her vibrant energy with everyone. 
The best part about this location aside from the super cute mural painted inside, is the fact that it is bright and open and spacious. It feels less crowded than the midtown location and since it is still rather new, there was no wait at lunch time for us yesterday!

I order the combination fried rice most likely the onion fried rice. I had more onions then meat in the rice. I thought this place would actually taste like authentic Chinese food but it didn't. The rice didn't taste like nothing at all, if it wasn't for the duck sauce i would of have gave a 1 star rate. I'm very disappointed.

We came just for the casino. Here is our experience:
Walked in, saw security guards near what looked to be where you enter the casino floor. Confused, we stood and watched what other people were doing and determined we should get a players card. We go up to the players counter and are informed that just going into the casino floor costs money (!!!). It was $10/person for 24 hour access. But you get that money back in a gift card to spend on food (what even is the point ). Side note- from what I understood from the players club lady, you don't have to pay to use the casino if you stay in the hotel. So we get our cards and go scan them by the security guards. The guard asks to see our cards and our IDs so she can scan them...what's the point in any of this!! 
On the casino floor:
The actual gaming area in TINY!!! I guess I should add that we went on a Saturday night. I know casinos are crowded on weekends, but this was ridiculous. By the time we left, which was about an hour after arriving, there were literally no open machines. I'm personally not interested in spending any sort of minutes longer than a couple to wait for a machine. When we left, I tried to cash out my tickets on the cash out machines but was told to go to the actual cashier. Annoying since it's in the back of the casino. 
Spending our "gift card":
There are 3 "restaurant" choices outside the casino floor. Asian, burgers, and Italian (pizza). It's really, really over priced - probably because they want you to spend more money than the obligatory $10. We opted for Asian. I got general tso chicken, husband got pad Thai. Each entree was $16 for a small plate that would cost no more than $12 at any Asian restaurant. Also, it wasn't even good. 

Never going back.

If you're in for a night of drinking excessive amounts of alcohol (and, c'mon now, who visiting New Orleans, especially Bourbon street isn't doing that), you'd better have something to eat planned out.  Fortunately for you, Vieux Carre Pizza is right off Bourbon street and has pizza by slice, hot, ready and waiting for you to devour.

The best part is, they don't just have cheese or pepperoni ready for you, they've got some damn good other choices too!  I'm talking slices of "Bourbon Special" pizza (chicken, spinach, pesto and feta) or "Meat Lover" pizza (Pepperoni, Canadian Bacon, Sausage) ready for you to grab, eat and fuel your drunken shenanigans for a few more hours.

The staff here get you in and out pretty quick too (essential when you're on Bourbon street) and at an average of $4.00 per slice, it's easy on your wallet too (Hooray for you! Now you afford a refill on your fish bowl full of alcohol!)

So this is one of those reviews every seasoned Yelper hates writing. When you five star a place and realize that 1,794 others have already discovered probably everything amazing about the place you're about to Yelp. What can be said that already hasn't? Allow me to do my best....

When people hear you're traveling to New Orleans (NOLA when Yelping), you'll hear literally EVERYONE tell you that you MUST visit the cafe in the French Quarter for beignets and coffee (you know the place I'm talking about).  I'm here to tell you forget all that. No. Seriously.  If you're TRULY looking for a "life changing experience" in the form of a bite of something deep fried, sweet and "to die for", head over to District Donuts. 

OK so, on the the review: The donuts here are HUGE and of the HIGHEST quality. They are also, anything but boring. Creations such as "Funfetti", "Turtle Cheesecake", "Nutella Mousse" and "Chocolate Raspberry" are available to entice you (and if the names don't tempt you, the way they look will).  I tried four donuts on my visits (yeah, I know) and all four were superb. However, the one which stood above all else....

The Monte Cristo donut!!! When it was presented to me (this one is made to order), I heard the "Ahhhhhhh" in my ears.  A tear formed in my eye, as my gaze was allowed to catch such a thing of beauty. After staring at it for a few moments, just appreciating its beauty, I cut into it, sad that I defaced such a masterpiece, but glad I was about to taste something so heavenly mere moments later. The smoked ham and havarti cheese gave it a savory aspect which married so beautifully with the sweetness of the powdered sugar (again, get your powdered sugar fix here instead of elsewhere) and slight tartness of the raspberry preserves.  Damn, this doughnut started my day of right!

My wife and I plan on visiting NOLA again without the kids (so we can engage in some Bourbon street shenanigans).  Rest assured, District Donuts will be on my "must do" lists.

Tried Bricks for my husbands birthday. Everything was excellent.  We took our time and they did not try to hurry us at all. We tried the abalone as an appetizer first. Although it's pricey, it was a worthwhile splurge. The martini's were perfect ( be careful though, they are doubles!) I had a salad with grilled goat cheese that was wonderful. The pasta was the only thing I can say was just ok. Desert was great too! We would love to go back again!

Terrible experience and apparently as I read through the reviews I wasn't the only one.  The manager/hostess have some serious customer service issues here.  First of all they told my friend on the phone (30 yr old) that this wasn't a place for your friends to sit and drink all night long.  For heavens sake it was her 30th birthday.  She wanted a few more than 6 people there and they were already giving a bad attitude.  Well anyways she didn't care and wanted to eat there.

So when we got there a few people were late.  They had a problem sitting our almost complete party.  Instead they rather let the door and hallway get crowded.  Then as we hassled to get them to seat us the manage had some nerve to tell us we had to be out by 7:30.  Correct me if I am wrong, but aren't paying customers allowed to enjoy themselves and not feel rushed?  After all we did spend over $500 dollars.

Well anyways, that's not all, one of our friends accidentally let out a semi loud laugh.  It was only one laugh and the hostess had the nerve to come and tell her to be quite because people are complaining.  Meanwhile it was only a minute after she laughed.  So I don't know but I think the hostess complained and blamed it on the customers.  

Anyways, I felt rushed I felt stressed and even though the food was good I was very annoyed and pissed off.  The manager and hostess ruined this experience.  And because of that I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone.  The only good thing I can say is that our waiter was very nice to us.  I was sure to thank him on my way out and then have my words with the manager.

I don't normally write bad reviews so trust me and avoid this place.

Today is the fifth time we have visited we got there and there is a bit of a wait, however we had the mind set to get reservation for five people at 8:30am on a Sunday Father's Day, so we expect it to be busy.  The wait is huge like seven to eight parties waiting for tables, so we were lucky they got our reservation correct and were seated at 8:30, no wait.   

We sat inside where there were, I  counted Seven tables open and five open spots at the bar.   We ordered at 8:50am mark, it took the food server twenty minutes to take our order

The server came back to the table to make sure her had our order correct and came back again to make sure our order was correct and he can back a third time  to tell us there was no shrimp and grits, and then came back a fourth time to make sure he got the veggie omelet right.   

Our breakfast arrived 9:40am an hour and ten minutes after being seated.  I believe the kitchen was running slow, however our food server was awful, he was a crappy food server, he spoke really fast and was hard to understand, he kept getting our orders wrong.

Sad part is after the long wait our orders were still wrong.   What a joke!  

We like the food, service is crap!

This place does Bosnian right.  When I say that, I don't just mean the food.  EVERYTHING in this place is done well.  The restaurant is beautiful and spacious.  The food is not only delicious but looks beautiful.  Even the wait staff seems like you are actually eating dinner in Sarajevo.  The sheer attitude of the place is Eastern European.  

I had the cauliflower schnitzel...it was nothing short of melt in your mouth delicious, my friend tried the cevapi, a spicey Bosnian sausage and after practically licking his plate, said it was so good he wanted to order more to bring home with him.  I have to say, the goulash that the woman next to me ordered made me long for my days of beef eating and steamed and smelled like it came right out of Budapest...

I had no idea we had restaurants like this in St. Louis.  I had no idea we had restaurants like this west of the Danube for that matter.   If you are looking for a totally different type of dinner experience and looking to be filled up with what can only be described as some of the most comforting foods in creation, you have to check out Grbic.

The owner Rachel was very rude to my girlfriend and gave her terrible customer service. She went in to do some homework and study while getting some work done. Before she could get settled in the owner went up to her and demanded that she needs to buy something in the store before receiving the WiFi password. She felt discriminated against and felt racial intents as she felt singled out amongst a group of other people sitting down without having bought anything. The owner talked her in a very disrespectful manner and made her very uncomfortable. 

 After the conservation my girlfriend went up to the owner and confronted her about what she said, the negative attitude and terrible customer service she was providing. The owner later called the police for confronting her and kicked her out of her establishment. Would recommend not coming to this place as the owner is unprofessional, over dramatic, racist and discriminative.

The newest addition to the Mercer Building and the successor to the Roast Coffeehouse space, Rostizado opened its doors to the public on August 11th. The restaurant is the latest venture of the Tres Carnales trio: Daniel Braun, Chris Sills, and Edgar Gutierrez. While Tres Carnales has a brighter, more casual atmosphere, Rostizado is its grown-up counterpart. The modern Mexican rotisserie restaurant specializes in roasted meats offered in a classy, low-lit dining space. The eclectic Mexican touches are still there, but they sit amongst darker wood elements-a distinct difference from the bubbly, colourful Tres Carnales.

I attended their VIP media event recently and everything was great. We sampled the albondigas, meatballs made from veal, pork, beef, and rice, tossed in tomato and warm chile de árbol salsa. One bite of these meatballs unveiled a variety of herbs to complement the meat, followed by a spicy sucker punch to tease those tastebuds. They were so good, I went back for seconds and had to stop myself from diving for thirds.

The gorditas with pancita (braised pork belly) had a unique combination of savoury and plenty of lime, all tempered by the fluffy corn flour gordita. The queso fundido gave fungus-lovers the taste of wild mushrooms paired with smoked gouda, monterery jack cheese, poblano chile strips, and sauteed onions. For those who prefer subtle, rich flavours, this one's for you. Slow roasted and flavourful, the rosti puerco (roasted pork) slices sat atop a tortilla, paired with pickled red onion, avocado, and parsley.

And the churros-oh, the churros. I would order this dessert in a heartbeat. The chefs served them up fresh, hot, and overflowing with sugar. The insides were still soft, though the exterior had been fried to a perfect, golden-brown crisp. Delicious, sweet, and well worth the third trip through the line.

Rostizado has definitely raised the bar. I look forward to returning soon and trying one of their roasted meat platters, which are served with roasted potatoes and tortillas. Oh, the meats! The flavours!
