Our server was friendly and attentive, though she seemed a little bit inexperienced (clearing a wine glass before it was empty, checking in a little too often, etc.)

Onion rings were pretty tasty. Nothing unusual, just extra crispy goodness with a chipotle dipping sauce.  The portobello sandwich was tasty, if unimaginative. And the pour-over coffee is good.

Some good local/regional wines by the glass at reasonable prices and a good by the bottle beer list. I was especially pleased to see that a large portion of the wine by the bottle list is available by the glass with a two-glass commitment. I don't think anyone else in Boise does this and I was really pleased to see someone giving it a shot. I hope it works out. 

Three people at our table really liked the Butter Cake. I thought the texture was off, a bit bread-like, as if the batter had been overworked. I really enjoyed the Chocolate Lava Vault.

The bad:

I have never in my life sent back a dish until this meal. The butternut ravioli was inedible. Two other people at the table tasted it and had the same reaction. The sauce was weirdly sweet and apple-saucy. The wilted greens appeared to be baby salad greens instead of something hardier and more appropriate. They added a slimy texture but almost no flavor. The raviolis themselves could hardly be tasted under that foul and overwhelming sauce. The floor manager (at least I think she was the floor manager, she didn't introduce herself) came over after the dish went back to see if I had any feedback for how the dish could be improved. It seemed like it wasn't the first time this had happened. 

There was not a special, or if there was the server didn't tell us about it. 

The apple-barrel chicken underwhelmed the two at our table who shared it.

The disappointing:

Why can't a restaurant in Boise try something new? It is almost as if the menus from Bittercreek, 13th Street, Solid, Bardenay, Berryhill, Bungalow, City Grill, and half a dozen other restaurants over the last few years just got jumbled up and reprinted. This is the same un-inspired, semi-casual, might-as-well-have-gotten-your-recipes-straight-out-of-Bon-Apetit-in-2001 fare that has plagued Boise ever since the invention of the spinach salad with pear, gorgonzola, and walnuts. 

And I'm not sure what farm-fresh and local means to Fork, but to me it doesn't include tomatoes in Idaho in April.

I like crepes.  Seriously.  Most of the time, I'm wary about going to a new place, but I was certainly game to try me some crepes.

The floral walls were a little disorienting, but the place was homey, and it was crepes!

No point in beating around the bush.  These crepes are great. Absolutely amazing.  You get to pick what you want in them, and you pay by the filling - which can start getting pretty expensive.  I ordered 2 fillings - chicken and mushroom.  I'm not sure which one of the toppings won the little topping death match to get to provide the cream sauce, but I don't care - it was delicious.

I was a little surprised at the size - I'm used to seeing those giant triangle shaped crepes with the filling busting out both ends.  This was a small flat square thing that appeared to be made out of some kind of healthy whole-grain batter.  If there's something I can't stand, it's healthiness, especially in the form of whole-grains.  I want partial to no grains, damn it!  Still, like I said... delicious.  If you're like me (and you're probably not) and you still would rather get your turkey on white, rather than rye, you still won't mind this disturbingly brown crepe.

You might mind the serving size, though.  For the cost, it really feels like you should get more.  But what it does is makes sure you have room for a second crepe - because you don't want to leave without having a sweet crepe as well.

The first time I went, I had strawberries & nutella - which didn't stand out too much from strawberry & nutella crepes I've had elsewhere.  The second time, however, I had brown sugar, which was really, really good.  I didn't know how they could make a dry crepe and a dry sugar into a tasty dish, but the brown sugar was heated and melted and made into some kind of crepe wonder paste, and.... yum. 

For those of you keeping count, while I did go twice, I had the same savory crepe both times.  That chicken and mushroom thing was one of the best things I've ever put into my mouth (apologies to all previous girlfriends) and I saw no reason to mess with a good thing.  I'm a creature of habit.

Everyone else appeared to enjoy what they had as well, thought one of my friends learned that 'Roquefort' is the same as 'blue cheese' which he is 'allergic to'.  Damn those frenchies for being so fancy with their words.

The did have wine as well, which others appeared to enjoy.

I love this place and will be going back.  Not the cheapest place, but won't break the bank either, and good for any time of the day.  if you're in the mood for a good dinner and a good dessert in one place, or a nice brunch, it's a great place.

Bea Arthur. I don't know who you are, but this ice cream that is named for you is fabulous. My softserve vanilla is injected with sweet sweet sweeeet dulce de leche, and dipped in wafer crust. My childhood memories of chasing the ice cream truck and getting rainbow sprinkles has been obliterated. My ice cream craving is bigger and gayer now.

OMG, where do I even start with Mazzaro's? I love, love, love it! Probably the #1 place I miss in St Pete, having moved to Miami a year and a half ago. 

Fresh seafood, butcher, organic produce, gourmet cheeses, a mix of fine and reasonably priced wines, homemade FABULOUS pasta, delish Italian cold cuts, olive bar, ready made foods, sandwich counter --outdoor seating, bakery, decadent desserts... It goes on and on. 

Not to mention the old fashioned, refurbished, hand-cranked deli slicer that they use for their top notch prosciutto which transports you to a simpler time and provides pitch perfect slices.

Another unique feature are their premium aged steaks which they do in house.

With every visit, my eyes get all googly and it is hard to resist buying EVERYTHING! I've never come here with a plan, it's more like you come in and choose a little of this and a little of that and the next thing you know you are having a FEAST! It is too hard to resist.

I know plenty of people who make the drive from an hour away for the sole purpose of mazzaro's, and with very good reason. I really don't think there is any place quite like it in the state of Florida.  

Beware though of their hours. I believe they close around 4 on weekdays and are not open Sundays. If you are here around Valentine's Day, Christmas or any other major holiday be prepared because it will be a madhouse!

The chicken cheesesteak is the best in Philly! (Regular cheesesteaks are good, but Lee's chicken cheesesteaks are the real draw) 

Mr. Lee also has great carrot cake as well as an impressive variety of sodas. The restaurant has recently been renovated which is nice. 

Definitely a spot to check out in West Philadelphia.

Been here a few times already since it opened since I live across the street, and they have really good mexican food if I do say so myself! But beware the HUGE serving sizes! The plates are literally bigger than your steering wheel and if you order a burrito, it stretches from one side of the plate to the other, no exaggeration. It will probably last you a weeks worth of food, so I do recommend sharing haha. Really good quality tasting food and their desserts are yummy as well. Its great for a late night hang out since they do have a full bar or just a nice lunch or dinner with friends. :) The manager was super friendly and you can tell he really cares about the restaurant and how the customers are treated. Service is really fast and the waiters are also very friendly. The prices are super decent for what you get. If you're looking for a delicious Mexican restaurant, check this place out!

Went here years ago when it was new and returned again tonight. I'd forgotten how great it was but quickly remembered. All the food is delicious, obviously fresh, and abundant. Staff is very nice, warm, and friendly. Location is clean and well kept. We will definitely be back soon but next time we'll remember our wine (it's BYOB). I hear their lunch buffet (weekdays) is great but haven't yet tried. Only wish is for falafel.

Mmmm.....

The cupcake phenomenon hitting this city is mildly amusing, but it does make me happy since it gives me an excuse to try them all. 

The flavor list is delightful, I only tried the vanilla bean cupcake with chocolate frosting but was very impressed! The cupcake seemed very homemade, which to me signifies real flavors, real butter, great dense texture, and love of dessert. 

Cupcakes cost $3, Coffee $1.75. They also serve homemade hot chocolate I am looking forward to trying. 

The owners definitely are trying to find their niche by adding decor to the top of the cupcake. Mine came with a lovely lacy chocolate decoration. Even more fun are the kitschy cupcake cabinets and furniture inside the store. 

My only complaints are that there is not really a place to sit, so they are mostly for takeout, and they use too much packaging in order to preserve the beauty of the cupcake. 

Looking forward to trying many many more cupcakes there in the future.

Do you know how challenging it is to find somewhere I can get a dairy free milkshake with whipped cream? It's hard! Enter Gordon's Milkshake Bar, where dairy free and vegan folk have options for a good, old fashioned milkshake. (Or a new fashioned boozy one, if you like that sort of thing.)

I made my first visit to Gordon's on what most would call an inopportune day. It was 12 degrees out. Yeah. And this was, in fact, during the pandemic so indoor seating--limited as it is anyway--wasn't open. I knew all of this ahead of time and chose to go, so I was prepared ahead of time. 

So I'm sitting outside on a bench, bundled up winter-style and sipping a dairy free (and gluten free) chocolate peanut butter milkshake. The verdict? Delicious! The shake was really tasty and being able to have df whipped cream on top made me feel special. Like I said, hard to find sometimes. The price point was a little on the high side for a milkshake, but for a once-in-awhile treat (and a dairy free one at that) on Mass Ave, it's about what you'd expect. The portion size was pretty good, too. 

The staff was friendly and patient. The shop was clean, as was the bathroom. The menu has plenty of options for everyone. Gordon's is a keeper! I'll definitely come by again... maybe even on a warm, summer day. ;)

Go early at opening because at 12PM, nearly everything was sold out. We didn't get our our urchins.

Tip: Order a bunch of cold items, and carry them to eat at the benches right along Harbor Walk outside the Santa Barbara Yacht Club for a mess-free picnic and a gorgeous view.

Smoked salmon candy peppered - Must order! Delicious, sweet, chunky, and fluffy. We were lucky to snag the last handful, and inhaled this in less than a minute.

Salmon poke - Average, plump, juicy. 

Baby octopus - More like toddler octopus. Identical to the cold octopus appetizer dishes at the dim sum restaurants but much bigger. 

Seaweed salad - Pass, lacked flavor.

Reminder: Crab cakes are taken home to finish cooking, not ready-to-eat.

Everything you would want from a diner!  Generous portions of high-quality food, clean & comfortable atmosphere, speedy service and some great specials!!

Diners usually serve generous portions with speedy service.  But from my experience the food quality is usually average.  NOT here!  All of the food here is clearly a step above - refreshingly deliciously & satisfying!

My grilled blackened chicken sandwich was great!  Flavored just right and moist! All of the other food including the chicken soup and the pickled beets were without a doubt above average.  Even my chocolate pudding for dessert was so darn good!  I was really impressed and just hoping for a good meal, but I got more!

They have great specials here too for $8.99.  If you get the sandwich special like me it comes with soup or salad, fries or any side, coleslaw, a drink, and a choice of desserts!  If you prefer an entrée for the same price, you also get soup or salad, drink and any dessert with your entree!  

If you have a little time to eat and don't want fast food and you are looking to stop along Route 168 that connects the New Jersey Turnpike with Route 295, this is your place to stop!

A beautiful shopping and strolling district loaded with stores, restaurants, bars, but beware some stores only offer credit. 

OK first thing I have to say right away, you can buy alcohol and walk around store to store drinking it! Did you get that? You can go to a microbrewery, winery anywhere and buy a draft beer or a glass of wine and take it with you and walk around and shop! This begins in the morning by the way.  That almost deserves five stars right there!  LOLL 

The next thing I want to point out is the not so good stuff. Just beware some of the stores there will not give you a refund. They will offer you store credit. Which at first sounds fine except that keep in mind the stores are not located throughout the state. They have other stores throughout the state where you can get store credit but it may not be a place that's either convenient or a place that you would wish to shop at so you need to check out the return policy before buying anything from any store if it's expensive!!!  Don't forget that one!!

OK now that I got that out-of-the-way, which is also the reason for taking one star away, I'd love to get to even more great stuff!

There's nothing not to love about this place! A couple of blocks filled with lots of fun and interesting stores, bars, restaurants, breweries, wineries with a beautiful courtyard and gardens in the center of the complex! Absolutely gorgeous layout!   If you spend an entire day browsing through stores it may not even be enough! They have hotels there as part of peddlers village and it may not be a bad idea to get a room if it's your first time or if you want to really have a fun night after shopping!

I want to point out for you pandemic turned frequent alcohol drinkers like me that the micro brewery and winery are both outstanding! And I recommend working both of them somehow into your daily plan! We usually don't drink until night time but we had our first drink at 11:02 AM at the winery store LOLLLL.   Well let's just say that was the beginning of a fun day of shopping and drinking with friends!  

I highly recommend going here as a great way to spend a day or maybe two. In my case we got a hotel room and did not regret it! Keep in mind there are additional restaurants just a block or two outside of the immediate peddlers village area that may offer different food or even better food in some cases. And if you've been here before no harm in going back again and again, I've already gone there twice and we're planning our next trip now!

My latest obsession? Nashville!  I'd always wanted to go and thanks to a conference there this year, I finally got to go and this town does NOT disappoint.  Its easy to see why its growing like crazy.  I hear the humidity is crazy in the summer but during this visit in early May, it was perfect!

We scored a great tip from the AirBnB one of my team members was staying at, they highly recommended Sky Blue for breakfast and for that, I'm grateful.

This is a great little restaurant primarily in a residential area, across from a park and what appears to be a school on the other side.  It's the type of place brunch was made for with your cool adult friends.  They put out a great pot of coffee to take the edge off while you wait for your table to open.  Use this time to make a new friend, learn a new POV, or just enjoy the dew on grass across the street and grab a seat on the benches.  

This is a small business as, maybe 30 people fit which is amazing as the kitchen is smaller than what I have in my home.  Regardless, the service was excellent, the food was very good and the portion size was large enough for a Tennessee Titans lineman (only if he was hungry).  

The table ordered a variety of plates, a burrito, a skillet with avocado and egg, and I ordered an amazing French toast/pancake sandwich with egg and sausage and then I smeared Nutella all over it.  Growing up as a twin with two additional younger sisters, food was a premium and it never went to waste.  I really needed my twin brother along on this morning to help finish off my breakfast.  I don't leave food often but there was no way I could finish it but it wasn't from a lack of trying.  

Interesting art on the wall to purchase, bench seating to have small talk with your neighbors, and a cool morning to soak in a touch of Americana in the middle of America.  Nashville, you're awesome-and Sky Blue is part of that!

Legend, icon, hero, idol, rebel, convict.  Johnny Cash

This is a small but dynamite museum.  Absolutely enjoyed every minute taking a tour of this American original.  The museum is filled with his artifacts, handwritten liner notes, personal artwork, outfits, and walls of his hit records-what an amazing career!

We toured the Museum of Country Music the day before we went through this tour and IMHO, this one is a 10th of the size and is twice as good.  You actually get some meat on the bones of who Johnny was, what his life was like, his successes, demons, and loves.

The museum has a great little eatery and a wonderful gift shop with reasonable priced Johnny memorabilia.  

Located right off the magnificent Broadway, the Johnny Cash museum is not to be missed if you're visiting Nashville

I've been jonesing for some good pho for weeks now.  I saw Pho Manchester on Yelp a while ago, but wasn't able to make time to get down there until today for lunch.  My spicy veggie & tofu pho was AMAZING!  It was on par with some of the best I've ever had, including during my business trip to Vietnam a year ago.

The gentleman who served me was super nice, and genuinely happy & extraordinarily helpful when he learned I was a new customer.  He was concerned the "Asian spicy" might be too much for me.  After some convincing, he cautiously went ahead with the order.  I like spicy food, and this pho had just the right amount for my taste buds.

Don't shy away from the place because it's small.  It is well worth the visit.  I strongly recommend it to anyone who enjoys a good bowl of pho.  Delicious.  Without question, Pho Manchester is now on my short list of favorite places to pick up takeout on the way home from the office.

I can't believe we just finally made it here.  We live less than a mile away.  I am sorry that I didn't make it here sooner.  Food is so good, so fresh, and for such a small spot, it's perfectly set up inside.  I had the salad without meat, and my husband had the quesadilla.  We didn't want a lot of food, so we thought we'd order light. Ha!  The salad was huge, the veggies were grilled perfectly, and his quesadilla was big and perfectly crisp. We actually took a to go box.  I ordered horchata because I haven't allowed myself that luxury in years.  It was just as good as I remembered.  A little light on the cinnamon, but good. The salsa bar had all over our favorites and each one was yummy.  We were bummed we didn't see the pupusa sign until after we placed our order, so next time we need an inexpensive and easy dinner night, pupusas will be had!

The ramen sucks. I didn't drink the broth.

I'm sure there are better things to order here but honestly The Black Sheep should do the Santa Barbara community a favor and 86 the ramen from the menu. It's one of the worst things I've eaten in Santa Barbara. My review was supposed to be amended for Santa Barbara Asian food standards but that whole thing went out the window when I tasted the thing.

The broth tasted like vomit. I thought I was crazy so I asked Ashley E. who confirmed my suspicions. I guess it's kind of cool you know, because I don't really like the taste of vomit when it's coming out so I got to find out it's not pleasant going in either.

Noodles were soggy, ingredients were totally different than the description wtf. the egg was probably the only thing ok and it was ok. The pork was good although there was not much of it. I had a chunk of pure pork fat, maybe that was intentional but I didn't think it tasted good.

I liked the Zombie Romney painting on the wall.

Needless to say I did not drink the broth.

One will not find many options for Korean BBQ in Santa Barbara. Kimchi Korean BBQ will get business for this reason but for being mediocre Korean BBQ it is ridiculous how much they charge - even more ridiculous is now AYCE is the only option. This restaurant has changed ownership twice since last year, and yet despite all this I kept an open mind and I can now declare with confidence that this place blows.

The Korean dumpling is disgusting. Just don't, I only had some because of curiosity but they are not good. 

Eat here if you must but I would rather drive to Santa Maria or Oxnard for better options. I would drive to LA if I wanted to be 100% happy.

This is a finely run establishment. The quality and attention to detail isn't missed at all. 

I had a chicken burrito and the chicken was amazing, like how often does chicken taste so good? The rice and beans were so so but there's enough chicken in the burrito to carry it taste-wise. 

I'll be back for the torta! And I'll yelp it. ;)

Terrible food and unacceptable service for a steakhouse that considers itself a fine dining establishment with lofty $40+ per patron prices. I had an over-salted and over-cooked filet that was completely inedible, a boring over-cooked baked potato, and chowder that was nothing to write home about; honestly, I've had better out of a can of Campbell's.

We had a problem with our order; it took forever to get our server or bus boys attention. Took forever to get what was clearly an already prepared fruit bowl for dessert. Took forever for the bill. They had the audacity to charge me $10 for a dessert that the server and busboy had previously conveyed would be complimentary; This, due to the mess up on my overly salted and in edible disgusting steak. Nice try Scott. Your attitude was absolutely dreadful and uncalled for in taking care of this matter. I don't care if you've worked there for 10 years or 30, the patrons are the reason this restaurant exists; they are the reason you continue to be employed there. I suggest management take this into consideration the next time you neglect to apologize to your customers or storm away with such a staunch attitude!

This was by far the absolute WORST dining experience I've ever had.

I don't recommend it. There are far better restaurants in the area.

Since I was in New Orleans, I had to have a beignet. Why not go to a place with the name Beignet on its sign?

As with a lot of places in the French Quarter, it's basically a tourist attraction. 

I was there at 10 am on a Tuesday and it was packed. No open tables and people waiting for them.

I decided to get my beignets to go. An order is three for $3.99. One would have been more than enough but it's probably not worth their while to sell just one.

I waited in line for about ten minutes to place my order and then waited about another fifteen minutes for the beignets. The thing is, it's so packed there's no place to wait for your order. You just have to find a place to stand and hold your sign with a number on it. 

The beignets were just OK. On the doughy side. One of them was super small, about a quarter of the size of the other two. Good thing I had my fill after the first one.

The breakfast food looked pretty good. Again,a very touristy place. One and done is plenty.

A friend and I decided to check out the Cajun Cannon Restaurant for lunch. I had read the few reviews on Yelp which were encouraging, so I was looking forward to the experience. I also love Bobby Hebert, the pride of Cut Off, Louisiana and South Lafourche High School

The space is oddly designed. You enter a little right of center and are facing the bar with the hostess stand on your right. There are two dining rooms, a smaller one to the right and a larger to the left. The décor is pretty pedestrian, rather dim and uninspiring. My guess is very little was spent comparatively speaking on remodeling what was Carmine's. The high top tables and booths in the small dining room were drab and uninviting.  There are a fair number of TV's, most of them tuned to news channels, FOX and CNN. One TV tuned was tuned ESPNU. Wall decorations consisted of Bobby's newspaper clippings, Saints stuff, etc. The music was Farrell ("I'm Happy, etc.") and other pop tunes. In sum, not your average sports bar, and not very inviting on any front.

The food was what I expected. My dining companion and I ordered a cup of seafood gumbo and split a seafood platter. The gumbo was above average, with good flavor and consistency. It is served with a back fin of the crab crawling out the bowl, a nice touch. A bowl of rice on the side would have been another nice touch. It would also have been nice to get more than one pack of crackers and to get a decent brand of crackers. Premium saltines are the only way to go. When will restaurant owners get that.  But I have no complaints at all about the gumbo. 

The seafood platter was more than enough for two. It consists of 4 each of oysters, shrimp, and catfish,  a mound of fries, plus a small cup of coleslaw which I forgot to taste. (My bad cuz I love coleslaw.) The fries were frozen batter fries, well fried and crispy. The seafood had a medium breading with a little kick of pepper and was cooked correctly although the catfish was a bit greasy, and I detected a hint of too old oil. I would say it was not at all a bad effort, but there is better fried seafood in New Orleans than this. I also think  fried seafood should be served atop buttered white toast, a throwback old school way to do it which I think Bobby would appreciate since he's an old school kinda guy.  But alas no white toast.

The service was fine. The servers are all extremely young girls dressed when we were there in little baseball outfits, cute but not tacky or cheesy. Our server was Christina who was a cute little girl, a real doll, and a good server. My only complaint here was the timing of the food coming out. The gumbo came out a few minutes after we ordered. Not unusual at all. But we were only 3 spoonfuls in when the seafood platter arrived. I'm not sure if they do it that way on purpose, but, regardless, I think there needs to be a gap between the gumbo and the main course. It also smacks of fried seafood sitting around the kitchen waiting to be piled on the plate. 

Some of the other menu items looked more ambitious than what we ordered, and I would be interested to try them. This place was just good enough to merit a return.

The GF and I visited this place on the first Friday of Lent after a late afternoon jaunt downtown. We had been here once before and really enjoyed what we had. We were hoping to order a noodle dish which we hadn't experienced the last time, but, alas, there were no seafood noodle dishes though there is a vegetarian one. 

So we ordered the mussels in green curry as an appetizer and a catfish special. The mussels were fabulous, steamed in a beautiful coconut curry sauce/broth and served with a  great sticky sesame rice. We split the small portion which was enormous and a great value. Now for the catfish. The catfish was fried in a beautiful wet batter (I think) which was wonderfully flavorful and perfectly executed. It ain't as easy to fry catfish as some might think. It was served with a refreshing side salad with basil and cilantro as the predominant herbs and a little shot of coconut milk. Here's the bad part. The fish was so spicy I couldn't eat it. The GF, who has a higher tolerance for heat, barely made it through her small portion. I brought half of mine home and gave it to my daughter who couldn't handle it either. It's such a shame when too much heat makes a perfectly conceived dish inedible. In defense of the chef, I will say I don't handle heat well at all. Funny thing is the waiter, a real good guy, did say it was spicy but said it was mildly spicy, about 5/10 on the heat scale. I gotta say, my friend, if that's 5/10, then 10/10 would be a great tool at Guantanamo.  

Now all of the dishes are not spicy, most not at all. Last time we had delicious calamari, chicken wings, and a great rice bowl. And if you can handle the heat, maybe the catfish is for you. As I said, it was a wonderfully conceived and executed dish. Funny thing is, we have been there twice now and still have had neither noodle nor pie. Next time!

First there was the hamburger invasion, then the pizza invasion, and now barbecue is all over New Orleans. Unfortunately, the barbecue places have often been short-lived. Hopefully Blue Oak Will change that trend.

We came here one early Friday evening after a July rain storm. The place was crowded, but we were able to order quickly and get a seat at this order at the counter wait for your food establishment. I had heard a lot about this place from several friends and was anxiously looking forward to trying it out. I can promise you it does not disappoint. The concept and the layout are both great. It is an extremely well-run establishment. And the food was well above average. 

I had the brisket and grilled sausage sandwich with coleslaw and a side of macaroni and cheese . The girlfriend had the brisket plate with brussel sprouts and a special side which was a watermelon salad.  The the brisket and sausage along with the barbecue sauce and coleslaw on the sandwich all played well together. The bun was not neglected as it is in some places like this. The bun was a beautifully baked bun from Laurel Street Bakery. It held up well to the mass of ingredients inside of it. A lesser bun would've completely fallen apart. The brisket on the plate was perfectly tender without being dry.The sides were great too. The macaroni and cheese was the star. It is good for so many reasons-the wonderful texture, the perfectly gooey cheesiness, the heavy garlic flavor tempered by the fact that the garlic is roasted not sautéed or raw. The watermelon salad was nice and refreshing actually serving as a palate cleanser. The brussel sprouts were nicely done, overly dressed, perhaps, with what appeared to be some type of preserves like fig or maybe pepper jelly. Not bad just a little overly sweet.

The girlfriend and I will definitely come back to this place. The chicken looked awesome, particularly the chicken wings. But my guess is that no matter what you order at Blue Oak you won't go wrong.

I had been here once before for drinks, and my girlfriend had been here twice, with me and once for dinner. She raved about the food, so we came here for Valentine 's Day. She looked stunning in a purple dress and super high heels. My heart skipped a beat when she opened the door to let me in. She looked that good. 

After chatting with a friend who happened to be at the bar, we sat down and scrutinized the menu  and wine list. We felt like red wine, so I ordered the Copertino which turned out to be a great choice, medium heavy, with fruit and spice and not too tannic. A great buy at $40. The wine list was a little pricey in my book with only a few bottles in that range or less. 

The menu is divided into several sections - snacks, appetizers, small plates and entrees. Surprisingly, there were only 4 entrees. I came specifically to try the chicken which is prepared sous vide. What I didn't know was there were other dishes prepared sous vide as well, so we ordered the chicken and the pork chop. To start we ordered the smoked fish spread which is served with grilled lavash which are very tasty in and of themselves. The fish dip too is excellent, very light, almost like velvet, and smokey.

The entrees did not disappoint. The chicken consists of a boneless breast and thigh served over greens and mushrooms. It was perfectly cooked with skin like a cracklin'. The pork chop too was awesome, served medium, with what I would call an apple gastrique  which was phenomenal. The chop comes with celery, a little weird but tasty. 

The ambiance of the place needs to be mentioned. It's a beautiful place with a gorgeous ceiling and stunning stained glass windows, befitting of the church it once was. The wait staff and management are both top notch too. Joe, the general manager, stopped by the table. He remembered us from last time. The bar had been busy so he hustled down a bartender to get our drinks. A prince of a guy. And Chloe our server was the best although I'm a little biased in her favor because she said we were the cutest couple in the place. A doll she is. 

I predict Vessel is here to stay. It was bustling with a very chic crowd. I know I'll be back!

Well since I'm the Duke, I guess I should review it. This is a dive bar in Metairie that I never would have gone to except it is close to work and has been on the regular rotation where I work. It's a great place to go espeically on a nice day when you can sit on the patio. Inside is a little ... well divey, and the smoke can get in your eyes. But it is what it is. The drinks are very well priced and are generous pours. Finally the food is way above average. From burgers to gumbo, Jason, the owner and head chef, knows his way around the kitchen.

Great BBQ place with a really good and traditional menu with a few wrinkles thrown in like grilled cabbage. I have been twice and enjoyed both meals. The first time I had the brisket sandwich, frites, and coleslaw. The second, I had smoked chicken, brisket, coleslaw and beans. I also had 2 big bites of the pimento cheese burger. All dishes were excellent. The fries may be the best in the city, the coleslaw is spectacular, and the burger rivals any in the area. The great thing about the sandwiches is the bun is not an after thought.  Nice beer list as well. You won't go wrong here.

This is perfect example of why reviewing a restaurant based on one visit is not a good idea. I dined here about 2 years ago and was anticipating an awesome meal based on the reviews by critics I respected including those who work for a little outfit called the James Beard Awards. And, unfortunately, I was underwhelemed by my meal.

 I returned a few days ago and had one of the best meals in recent memory. For an appetizer I had the seared sea scallops with crawfish tails with artichokes, fingerling potatoes, corn and andouille. As some may know, I'm a big scallop fan, so I'm always interested in different preparations of them. This one came, I believe, with a foie gras based sauce. Weird, but man was it delicious. For an entree, I ordered the halibut which was  finished with what I thought was a beef based sauce, also a little out of the ordinary. Sauces are the difference between home cooks, mediocre professionals, and the pros out there. Sue Zemanick is such a pro. Her sauces turned these 2 dishes from good to excellent. I can cook halibut as well as the pros in Gautreau's kitchen, but I cannot make  sauces like those. I also tasted the seared duck breast which was nice, but I must say I'm not a fan of medium rare duck. For dessert, my 3 dining companions and I split the rhubarb tart with strawberry jam and creme fraiche ice cream and the blackberry shortcake with meyer lemon cream. I loved them both, but the tart was superb, a not too sweet tart, almost a sandwich with semolina cake as the bread. 

The space is as I remembered--small and quaint, a little stuffy and pretentious (well, it is next to Newman), but warm and friendly nonetheless.

I am so glad I returned to Gautreau's and will def be back.

I have been to Mopho several times and have usually enjoyed my experience. 

My first time here was for dinner not long after it opened and was all the rage. It was dinnertime and the place was packed, noisy and lively in a good way. My dining companion and I ordered a drink at the bar and waited for a table which took about 45 minutes. Lately the place is not so crowded since the newness has worn off and, of course, there are so many new places opening every week it seems. But the food here is usually good. My 2 favorite appetizers on the menu are the chicken wings and the oysters though I was not as impressed with the oysters as others have been.  For mains, I've had a few specials like the fish which is great and the duck leg, also delicious. The pork belly rice bowl is also a favorite. 

One criticism is lack of consistency. The last 2 times I dined here, I ordered the pork rice bowl. The first time, there was not a lot of meat which I noted to my companion. Good stuff, but a little skimpy. I ordered it again 2 weeks later and the bowl was packed with pork. 

The service here is usually good but can be uneven as well. One particular good experience was a weeknight visit when my dining companion and I got stranded by a huge rainstorm when we were leaving. Rather than get wet, we decided to sit at the bar and have another glass of wine which turned into a tasting event with the delightful bartender. It was a fun time.

We tried Lee's out during the Baltimore Avenue Dollar Stroll. I had some fries and he had their Buffalo chicken cheesesteak.. Both were really good. The other day we were trying to figure out what to eat for a snack and I suggested Lee's. 

Check out the pics for all of their options for food. Burgers, vegan food, breakfast, lunch whatever you want.. We like that the menu has something for everybody.  Luis had their Buffalo cheesesteak again and said it was good but the Buffalo sauce they use is a bit thin so it makes the roll soggy. 

We sat in the car to eat because all of the booths were taken. I really wish they had more than four booths because we'd love to sit down and eat. Mr. Lee is friendly and probably knows most of his customers. The cooks in the back are always in  good spirits as well.

We came across a Groupon for Shanks the other day. Saturday was a BEAUTIFUL day and awesome to grab steaks and enjoy the weather outside.  

Shanks is located on Delaware Avenue /Columbus Blvd and can be easily missed if you don't know where it is. 

Has a similar setup to Pat's and Genos (small, order at counter  ,outside seating).  We ordered two Wiz Wits (cheesesteaks with onions)  two orders of fries and two sodas.  The place wasn't packed but just had large groups of people ordering 6-7 steaks at a time.  So we waited 25 minutes for our food.  I do believe they were short staffed because the cashier was helping the cooks. 

The steaks were good! I like that the meat was chopped and not in huge slabs. Nice amount of wiz and onions. Now the fries? We wouldn't buy those again.  The fries were shoe strings, cold and tasteless.  

Regularly, they sell steaks for $9.75 and comes with a fountain soda.

Stopped in today for a cup of java with a friend. Reminds me of someone's grandma's house turned into a cute little Cafe. Coffee was good. It was around 1pm and I was surprised to find that the  coffee wasn't stale. Plans were to sit outside but the uncovered tables with the sun beaming down in 90 degrees wasn't exactly inviting so we took a walk to Cedar Park under some shade.  

We decided to come back for lunch an hour later. Place  is a little small in the front but I tend to like establishments like this. Kinda has a community /homey feel to it and no one feels like a stranger. We waited a minute or so for a table in the back. Felt like I was sitting in my grandmother's dining room. Loved the  setup and ambiance. Cool artwork on the walls. Bubbly waitress gave us the specials, a carafe of cool ice water and let us be for a few to peruse the menu. 

Unlike some reviewers, I thought the prices were pretty reasonable. Sandwiches, soups, salads and burgers. Variety but not overwhelming where you're taking fifteen minutes to decide what to eat. I usually don't drink water at restaurants because it always tastes like tap water or has a kinda "mineral" after taste yuck! But this ice water, was cool and refreshing with no tap taste. Menu in hand,  I had no clue what I wanted. I wanted to try something new so I went with the flank steak sandwich. My Date had the gazpacho and a sandwich. Can't remember which one though. He liked the  gazpacho but said it needed salt. 

Food came out in less than ten minutes.. Good thing because I was hungry. My sandwich was on this super soft sourdough bun.. Amazing texture and taste. Came with a side salad of red leaf lettuce, tomatoes, carrots and radishes. Red pepper dressing. I gave the side eye to the tiny container of dressing but to my surprise, it was just the right amount! My steak sandwich was great.  Steak was cooked well done, I do prefer a medium.. But I enjoyed it nonetheless. One small gripe was just that they give you a single napkin. Literally just one lol. I'm use I could have asked for more though. 

I'd definitely come back here for lunch. It's a small place and I'm sure the wait times are crazy on weekends so it'll be a weekday thing for me. Oh yes,  it's BYOB.. So bring your bottles.. Cheers!

How can you not love a place with beer names like these?

Dew Me Now

Pecker Wrecker

Titches Wit

Nice Rack

Conan The Brewbarian

Dumb Blonde

I visited Cool Springs yesterday, grabbed a seat at the bar and chatted with the personable mohawked bartender. I asked if they sold beer by the flight or in a sampler, and he said they offered a ten beer taster for eight and a half bucks.

A few minutes later, I had ten small glasses lined up in front of me ranging in color from apple juice to black coffee.  I really liked the first one- a mild lighter blonde, I also liked the mango IPA, and the orange & citrus of the Tiches Wit.

I had such a nice time, soaking in the atmosphere, chatting with the staff, and sampling the very impressive beer selection..

The West End is a New Orleans neighborhood just south of Lake Pontchartrain. Seafood and boating are big influences here, and I saw quite a few suburban looking single-family houses and some condominium complexes as we drove around.  

No doubt, Two Tony's is a favorite of the nearby residents. It most definitely has a "hometown feel", the bar and lounge are very welcoming, and the food is both very good and very fairly priced.

I was visiting the local chapter of a professional organization I belong to and attended their monthly dinner meeting at Two Tony's. They did a wonderful job feeding our party of 30. We had a group choice of seven meals (!) and the dinners were cooked to order.  

The choices were Chicken Parmesan, Eggplant Parmesan, Manicotti, Shrimp Fettucine, Grilled Chicken Salad, Spaghetti and Meatballs, and a Catfish Poboy. 

I went for the Poboy (fried thin-cut catfish in seasoned corn flour breading - $8.95) "fully dressed" which I learned means with lettuce, tomato, pickles, and mayo) for a mere $0.75 surcharge. 

It was an enormous sandwich on what seemed like half a loaf of Italian bread with plenty of fish fillets and the fully dressed add-ons. It was excellent! The bread, the fillets, the dressings -stellar.

It was nice seeing a different kind of New Orleans restaurant -a place the locals enjoy and where tourists (except for us) were pretty scarce.

Let me preface this review by stating that I love the building. It's rustic, yet upscale. Vast, yet cozy. And the delineation of space is quite nice. Although I haven't been able to properly enjoy the rooftop patio due to the season, I do think this is one of the best al fresco dining spots in all of Reno. 

Now onto the heart of my review: The food and service are quite simply lacking. I sense that there is some effort being put forth by the employees/owners/operators, but the end result is less than accomplished and needs some serious fine tuning. 

My initial dining experience occurred in Mid-October, just after the opening. I was with a party of 5 friends. We were sat in the section of the restaurant to the left of the wraparound/dual bar. This area has more of a pub/sports bar type vibe with flat panel TVs, paper towel dispensers in place of cloth napkins, and at least on a busy Friday evening, a slightly rowdy type vibe. Not being a snob, that works just fine for me. I enjoy a sociable, lively atmosphere when out with friends so I found the overall people watching and ambiance enjoyable.

Upon glancing over the menu with friends we all selected a few different beers to try. My personal favorite was Saison of the Witch, but as with everything, tastes may vary. I found it very much to my liking and stuck with it for the remainder of my meal. One of my friends isn't a drinker so he asked for an Iced Tea. A simple enough request. Well, apparently not. He was initially told no Iced Tea was offered, then told they only had a "fancy" Iced Tea in a large bottle, then told that they do in fact have plain ole Iced Tea. Imagine his/our surprise when a large bottle of tea showed up (something like $5-6) at the table. To the server's credit, she did comp us for the tea since he was expecting a $2-3 glass of tea and not a huge bottle.  

We then proceeded to order some appetizers/menu items to share. We selected the Mac-n-Cheese, The Spaniard Flat Bread, the Cheese Plate, and some sort of fried Potato Poppers w/ Aoli . The dishes came out relatively quickly given the amount of business in the restaurant. The Mac-n-Cheese was okay, but most of us agreed that the flavor of mushrooms (an interesting addition), overpowered the dish. The Potatoes were utterly flavorless, but had a nice crisp fried outer layer. Sadly, the mayonaisy dipping sauce did nothing to enhance the flavor. The Flat Bread was more of a traditional thin crust Pizza (round in shape and w/ a sauce) than what I typically associate w/ Flat Bread. The flavor was good, but it was too soggy in the middle. The Cheese Plate was absolutely dismal. It had 3 pieces of cheese about 1/2 the size of a large egg along with a very small bit of nuts, and some sort of sweet honey/jelly concoction. The flavor of each was enjoyable, but it was so ridiculously tiny given the price. I can't imagine there was more than $4 worth of food on the plate, even if it was good cheese. 

Still hungry, we then proceeded to ordering a Steak and a Burger. The Steak was the best part of the entire evening. It was flavorful, not too tough, and cooked as ordered. The Burger was unremarkable. It was good, but the flavor profile lacked distinction. It doesn't hold a candle to Midtown Eat's Bison Burger IMO. 

We all left disappointed, but a couple of us agreed we would return again after they worked out the kinks. 

My second visit occurred this past Sunday. My friend had dined there the preceding Thursday and raved about his experience so I thought it was time to give them another shot. We arrived at around Noon for Brunch.

After a bit of deliberating and speaking with the friendly waitress, I selected the Chicken and Waffles (a guilty pleasure), and my friend ordered the Duck Hash. We got a Dutch Baby Pancake to share. The food arrived quickly, but with little flair. I've seen food at Denny's with better presentation (no joke). My dish was simply a Waffle w/ a sizable breaded/fried Chicken Breast on top. A bit of greenery would have helped. Syrup came on a separate trip a moment later. I then noticed that I didn't have butter, but given the richness of the dish, it didn't really matter to me. I proceeded to pour on some syrup and dig in. The Chicken was fried to perfection and quite good. The Waffle on the other hand was barely cooked. The outer edges were soft and the center was mushy and almost raw. After about my 4th or 5th bite, I noticed I did in fact have butter, but it was buried under my Chicken. My friend's Duck Hash had a great flavor, but was also VERY mushy. The potatoes/hash were lackluster in every way (seasoning/preparation). Our miniature Dutch Baby Pancake barely got touched and was wet and cold in the center. The pecans and chunks of apple did nothing to flavor the dish and it didn't come with a lemon to squeeze on top which I found odd (I've never seen a Dutch Baby w/ out lemon). We mentioned it to the server. She apologized, but still charged us for it.

Is it appropriate to start a review with a thank you? Because thats what I want to say to the proprietors of this fine establishment. Taking a beautiful, historic train depot and turning it into a distillery and restaurant must have been a huge undertaking, but they did it and did it well. Preserving the historic detail of the building while modernizing parts that needed addressing is a tricky balance, but they pulled it off. I especially like the vault safe in the bathroom and the huge blown up map of the grounds from when it was a train depot on the front dining room wall - fun! Ten years ago this would never have been thought possible in Reno. 4th Street was a dead zone and the sure bet was on spending your money building in the burbs. Very, very few had any interest in downtown. Post Recession era Reno and it's once again cool to be in downtown/midtown, and I personally could not be happier. This is the type of development we've been starving for as a city. And I hope it continues.

Onto the food...

I've now been here 5 times and each time I come away impressed with the quality and the general depth of flavor. The duck sliders are a go-to favorite, and their fries are crispy, delicious and served with a very good house made ketchup. I'm a Heinz man myself, but this stuff is so yummy they should consider bottling it and selling it alongside their Whisky. On my two most recent visits I have become a huge fan of their brunch. We've tried the pancakes, biscuits and gravy, chicken and waffles, and breakfast tacos. Each was amazing in its own way, but the biscuits and gravy and chicken and waffles were real stand outs for me. The best part? $10 bottomless mimosas! It's easily the best deal in all of Reno. I suspect that once more people find out about their brunch the prices will go up. Such is life - this place deserves to succeed. In an area that sometimes feels rife with mediocre dining options, The Depot stands out as something special.

This... this is not Italian food. It is more like food with an Italian flare. 

First, the bread. Italians and Italian food are all about family and sharing. This does not mean nickel and diming you and making you pay for bread like Pia's. The bread was slightly under cooked and didn't have enough salt in it. For $5 a loaf, it sucked. The Olive Oil provided also was subpar. 

Next, there was one fish option on the menu - Salmon - and it was a weekly special. No Branzino or any other fish since you are in Florida? There were only four options if you wanted chicken or veal. Otherwise there was the $30 beef option. 

The pasta which was touted as made in-house was a bit mushy and not very good. The meatballs had no flavor and were most likely Veal that had possibly been frozen. My salmon was extremely over-done and was as crunchy as a cracker. 

Overall - the food was decent if you haven't experienced real Italian food and kept your expectations low. But for the price you should go elsewhere.

We ate here for lunch yesterday and had the lunch buffet. We have been here many times for dinner and always had a good experience, so we decided to give the lunch buffet a shot and I'm so glad we did! There was such a great variety of both hot and cold greek/mediterranean options to choose from. On the hot bar there was 4 main dishes: a seafood stew with different fish in a seasoned cream sauce, greek meatballs (so good!), traditional greek moussaka, and some type of grilled chicken souvlaki. I tried a small sample of each and all were very good. There were also a couple of different pita pizzas and seasoned pita fries. My favorite offering was the wide variety of chargrilled vegetables including eggplant, zucchini, red peppers, green peppers, red onions and mushrooms. All were grilled to perfection, perfectly seasoned, and tasted great. They also had a lot  of cold options such as greek and house salads, a greek village salad with tomatoes, green peppers, cucumbers, red Onions, olives, salonika peppers, feta Cheese and house dressing (awesome), coleslaw (exceptional), fresh soft pita bread, and some tzatziki sauce that was hands down the best I have ever had! There were other options too that I just can't recall, but everything that I tried was very good.

The buffet was $9.99, and for the quality and quantity of food I think it is an exceptional value. In fact, the one woman in the buffet line commented "this shouldn't be so exciting, but it is!" I totally agree! The only thing that was a little disappointing was there were no dessert options on the buffet. I was hoping for maybe one choice like a baklava or karidopita, but no such luck. If you want to order these in addition you can, so not completely out of luck. All in all, a very satisfying meal. I will definitely be back for lunch again soon.

**** 4 Stars for Greek/Mediterranean food ****

Dear GOD, what a ripoff!  I LOVED the decor of the place and wanted to check out their cupcakes.  I walked in and ordered the chocolate-amaretto cupcake and the Twix cupcake.  The lady that helped me said that the Twix cupcake with vanilla cake was her favorite, and boasted that they made their own caramel.  (Is that really a selling point?  I had already expected housemade caramel. It's not like it's difficult to make.)

When I arrived at the counter, the saleslady said, "That'll be $9 please."  I damn near had a heart attack; they were pretty small cupcakes.  Without the frosting, they looked like homemade school bakesale cupcakes-- flat as hell.  Nonetheless, I held out hope that they were worth it.  Not the case, unfortunately.  Dry, dense, and boring.  The frosting on the chocolate-amaretto was hard and tasted nothing like amaretto, and the Twix was a dry plain cupcake, topped with buttercream, a drizzle of caramel, and a couple of Twix pieces.  $4.50?  Really??  I'd be more than happy to pay that much if it were a great cupcake, but it's not even good, let alone great.  Very disappointing.    :(

Disappointing. 2nd Visit. The place was crowded but we were still sat immediately. The server was pleasant and informed us that certain items would take 45min long to cook. We said ok and ordered apps immediately. They came out in 10min. She checked on us and we told her the rest of our order. Almost 1.5 hours later still no food. We ask her about it she says...let me check on it. Comes back and asks what was it that we ordered. We told her and she said ok. Needless to say and quite obviously we didn't get any food until almost 2.5 hours after the initial order, and one item was wrong!!! Long story short this experience wasn't very good at all. A manager table visit or some sort of comp would have been appreciated. We received none of that. We should have just laid for the drinks and apps and left. The sad part is that, the server seemed oblivious as to how to handle this situation. Will likely avoid this place for a while or maybe just go for drinks. A true waste of a rare Sunday night off with the fiancé.

We had a great experience at Angel Oak, the ambiance set the mood for a great post valentines date night. The staff were very attentive and explained the entire menu throughly. They answered any questions we had and the provided us with great service the entire night. Only minor negative was that our cocktails came slightly late. Our server assured us they haven't forgotten and were just a little busy. 

Our entire meal from the crab cakes, the albacore pasta, the dry aged NY Steak, sides and our baked Alaska were all highlights. Its definitely something to look forward to if we do come back.  From the seasoning, presentation, service and efficiency it was all 10/10 in our book.

Carpinteria, CA

5 star Teddy's Tavern Burger $16.00 * this burger alone was worth the visit

100% grass fed beef topped with lettuces, tomato, crispy shallots, thick cut bacon, white cheddar, candied jalapeno mayo

Fantastic burger ordered medium, flavorful, juicy, ordered with no salt which was perfect.  Loved the butter lettuce on the burger.  Served with a side of ketchup and delicious ranch dressing, this burger made it on the list of favorite burgers I have tried.  Liked, not loved the fries which were salty and tasted frozen versus fresh but I could be wrong...nevertheless they were good but scant on the plate.  We could not really taste the candied jalapeno mayo and were wondering if they even added it to the burger.  We would have liked to have tried some of the mayo on the side but by the time we thought to ask, we were not able to flag down the wait staff to even ask. The ranch and ketchup were also great condiments paired with the burger.

3 stars service  Service was slow, very slow when first seated, it took about 15 minutes for someone to even come to our table for our order.  I think it may have been an anomaly as I later found out their ordering system had crashed.  Once someone finally came to our table, food came out in a timely manner but we were only checked on once during the meal.  I understand staffing, and getting up and running again, so I chalk it up to part of the learning curve of being super busy again.

We sat on the outdoor patio early evening and it was a little breezy and cold, so eating our food before it got cold took preference over a photo shoot of this above average burger creation...but a few others have captured it on yelp photos.

It's a very rare occasion if you see a mexican food joint in my list of "Check In's" but when a place has all the rave reviews on "Yelp" and non "Yelp" friends tell me this is one of the go to spots in "Reno" for good mexican food..I knew I had to drop in, try it out for myself and of course leave my mark in "Reno" by leaving a review. And of course being still "inebriated" from partying a few hours was a big incentive to go here. Here is my review of Roberto's Taco Shop.

July 30, 2016 Saturday - 1:10 p.m. 3 hungry, simi drunk, guys needed something to eat to prepare for another fun filled day and night.

Atmosphere - 4/5
Food - 5/5
Service - 5/5

Background - Reno Yelper "Paul S." is really the reason I bookemarked Roberto's Taco Shop. And being in "Reno" every so often, I figured why not start visiting some of the places I've bookmarked. My homies agreed. 

Atmosphere - The spot has indoor and outdoor seating. Not too much, not to little. You could tell the set up is catered toward the college crowd. A nice place with big windows to take in the surrounding scene.

Food - My buddies got the Carne Asada and Carnitias meal plates respectively. I got the Carne Asada Fries that a lot of "Yelpers" seemed to have enjoyed here. I too am one of the many. My fries were prefect in every way, the carne asada was tender and the fries crisp. The fresh guacamole and sour cream and  dollop of refried beans just added to the overall balance of the dish. My buddies Carnitias was on point! The best I've propabubly had in a while.

Drink - I had an Hibiscus Agua Fresca. It was refreshing, especially seeing this was a hot day.

Service - The service was prompt and good. The cashier was glad to answer the few questions I and my homies had for him. 

Future - Without a Doubt!

Now It's now been a little while since I've been to "Reno" because of the current situation at hand, but I been having this review waiting for such a time. Downtown Reno is changing, and with it some things that I've loved has come and gone. And when staying at a Casino/Resort a main part of the attraction is not just the slot machines and bars, "Food" is a big incentive. I personally like eating where I stay. With the now closure of "Flavors The Buffet" in the Silver Legacy, that leaves just "2" buffets in Downtown Reno (Not speaking for the buffets at Atlantis & Peppermill which is Midtown), "Carvings Buffet"  inside Harrah's (See my review) and " The Buffet" inside Eldorado. Now I'm going to let you know why in my opinion, "The Buffet" is the one, hence the name.

"The Buffet"
Location - Eldorado Reno
Food - Various
Price - $29.22

The Buffet:
So I actually had the chance to go to Reno back in March and lucky me it was before the current shelter in place. I went Sunday the 9th I had saved my appetite just to visit "The Buffet" after reading some reviews and decided it was where I wanted to go. This buffet serves breakfast, lunch and dinner and have different prices and themes for the offering each day. Sunday happens to be the "Mexican Buffet" for the Dinner hours and based off your membership level, the price varies. For me being a basic member, the price was $26.99 which comes out too $29.22 with the added tax. 

If you're not too familiar with the Eldorado, this buffet may be kinda tricky to find, but lucky for me throughout the years I've always known where it is.... although this time happened to be my first ever visit. Just up the escalator, past the wishing fountain and "Roxy" and you'll see this establishment. So "Mexican Dinner" night at a Casino Resort, sounds good right? Well, it was delicious. Usually at buffets you kinda get what you pay for, if you're a regular at a particular one you like, then you know. This was my first time here and I loved the menu and the offerings. The stand out dish for me was the "Chile Verde" which was made with spare ribs and captured everything I like about this dish in general. They had other fair that I sampled, but I did also partake in BBQ ribs, which was tender and amazing mushroom ravioli accompanied by the mushroom sauce....yes. even though it was "Mexican Dinner" night, they did still have Prime Rib and other carving table options and Asian Food offerings. All which were delicious and I did partake in some dessert. Cool thing about this buffet although I didn't get any because my lactose sensitivity, they have housemate gelato here. It looked great, perhaps next time when I have my lactaid with me.

In Closing:
I would recommend "The Buffet" to anyone looking for a great place to eat with an array of options. If you're a member of the Eldorado Resorts (Eldorado, Silver Legacy, Circus Circus) "One Club" card program and have one of the various different card levels your discount could be greater. I personally consider this place my buffet of choice from now on. I personally can't wait till the nation opens back up, of course in a timely mannor, and I can go back to the "City of Reno" and when I get hungry...."The Buffet" will definitely be on my places to eat list.

Well, sometimes going against the grain totally backfires. It happens and it's completely normal, just apart our human nature (Tell me Why, Why) and that is just how it is when your options become limited in a place where your options shouldn't be..limited. I don't know why I would not get what everyone else was getting when it's literally the "Star" of the show, but being a rebel is sometimes what being apart of the "Yelpire" is all about. I sometimes like to follow the beat of my own drum, but at times I make "Awful Awful" decisions and I regret them. This night I did that and let me tell you why before this little intro starts to go on and on..

Saturday September 1, 2018
Location: Little Nugget Diner, Reno NV
People: 1 Adult

Story:
It was day "2" of a fun labor day weekend in Downtown Reno. In all that fun time one does get hungry, but "2" of my options for the evening were closed and it was quite a shame that it was. I didn't let that halt my quest for a good meal, I knew that I wanted some "wings" and pretty much all my options was pretty much done except for the good ole home of the "Awful Awful" so after looking at some pics and reviews on "Yelp", my mind was made up and I decided to go inside and give "The Little Nugget Diner" a shot.

Service/Hospitality:
When I went inside I was greeted by a fry cook, he gave me sometime to look over the menu and then I told him what I wanted. As he went to cook my order, a waitress come over and resumed where he left off by ringing me up. I wouldn't say that the service was over the top, but it was decent for what it was worth. I didn't feel out of place being there which is a good thing, I didn't expect anything more than the service I got to be honest.

Food/Cleanliness:
I'm not going to sugar coat things, the place was pretty filthy. This place needed some serious cleaning. The counter was oily, had crumbs and plates and such left from other diners. The floor needed a good sweeping, and just some average good ole TLC overall. In spite of this very "BIG" factor, I was hungry and I decided not to order the famous "Awful Awful" and go for the "Basket of Wings" $11.50. They don't offer but 3 sauce options here, Mild, Hot, and Nitro. I'm not into hot wings so I went with the mild option, the meal also came with their famous seasoned fries. The wings were overcooked and the mild sauce wasn't mild at all. The fries were soggy and very oily, they honestly should have let these drain some of the oil a little bit. I honestly didn't finish this whole thing and ended up throwing it out and going somewhere else and getting myself a bite to eat. I was pretty upset with myself that I didn't get the famous "Awful Awful" as it seemed to be what they do right here.

Overall:
I wasn't too please with my experience here, I would say that I'm not going back but I really want to try that "Awful Awful" burger and that alone is the saving grace of this place for me. I may have to be more drunk I guess to be able to tolerate this place a bit more the next time I go. But I will say at the same time I could see why this place gets the customer base it does, huge portions for a not so huge price. Hopefully next time I have a better time, and at least "2 Shots"

October 27, 2019

"Mel's Diner" definitely not "Tom's Diner" if that was ever really a place anyway....Duh Duh Duh Da Duh Duh Duh Da..you should know how it goes. I've been to a few diners in my time and all of them certainly aren't created equal. This would be the third Mel's location I've visited and quite frankly....this one provided just about the same experience that I've had at the other two I've visited. I don't think my standards are high or anything, but just for me something is common at all the locations I've visited. I'll tell you what it is..

Mel's Diner (Sands Regency):
This particular location is inside the "Sands Regency" in Downtown Reno. It's a pretty easy find as it's well marketed throughout the casino itself and postered ads around town. When entering this location via through the casino itself or it's own personal entrance, you'll notice the usual scheme that is the general one between locations. You'll also notice memorabilia and cues to the area the location serves. All the tables have the little jukeboxes on it as most locations does, and it's well lit. What is common with these locations in my experiences is...."service" and "consistency". This location is no exception. 

How does one, go and sit down and wait to be seated and 3 people that aren't following the rules get seated and served before said person? Yea, this has happened to me 3 different times at 3 different locations. Plus also how does one get seated after mentioning they haven't been seated and get seated at a dirty table, and then a person comes to clean it as you're sitting down reading your menu? I really could go on but it would further dive from the general review. On this particular visit after finally getting a really great waitress named "Elizabeth" (breath of fresh air from the nonchalant hostess) I decided to order a combo called "The Bomb" $14.59, which is a large Ham Steak, served with Eggs (Prepared your way) and Potatoes (House/Scrambled) served with toast, english muffin or hot cakes (pancakes). 

I was only given 3 pieces of toast....okay, my ham steak was pretty good for what it's worth. First time honestly having one, was a bit to....hammy for my taste, I'll save the ham for Thanksgiving or Christmas. My eggs were cold, don't know how seeing it was fresh from the kitchen, something all these locations have had j  coming with my orders. And that leaves me to my conclusion....

Overall:
3 stars, yes still 3 stars, and that's mostly because of the service from my waitress. I like diners, I'm just not a huge fan of "Mel's Diner" so I think this will be my last time visiting one. Just okay food, and blah service isn't my thing. But I'm just one "yelper" results vary from person to person.

October 27, 2019

"AYCE" always the best way to go if you're an indecisive person. Always something for everyone in one spot, you really can't go wrong at a buffet....or can you? Buffets, especially when being in the heart of a hotel/casino. As I make my way down the Virginia and Sierra St stroll, "Carvings Buffet" was another one I haven't visited. Being I'm now a member of the Ceasers Rewards program, I decided to go seeing I had $2.00 off. Let me tell you why it "was" and "wasn't" worth my time.

Carvings Buffet:
Carvings Buffet is located inside of Harrah's on the second floor. The set up of this buffet is pretty nice, having a line for regular guest and a separate one for members of the Platinum and Seven Star Ceasers Rewards program. Being this was the Sunday dinner time, the price of the buffet was $23.99 for Adults, with $2.00 off for rewards members. Seating inside is either booth or table seating, and all the food offerings are organized by the types of cuisine (Dessert, Asian, Mexican, American, Salad, Italian). I arrived about 30 min after they opened so the food was still very fresh. As I mentioned earlier, the experience "was" and "wasn't" worth my time. I'm going to tell you why..

"Was" - The price was pretty decent as far as Casino buffets go. They had a pretty good variety of food to choose from. The service is pretty good, and there is incentives to eating here.

"Wasn't" - The food is flavorless, not enough of items being set out at one time (not that that's a super bad thing). Crowed food stations, and not enough staffing for effective crowd flow and control.

Everything I had literally had no flavor at all. The dessert was the only thing with flavor..but that's not saying much because it's dessert. I only ended up eating one plate of food as it didn't really end up living up to my food standards for taste, although the quality was very presentable. 

Overall:
I'm glad that I got to try out "Carvings Buffet" I came, I saw, and I can now cross this one off my list. I think I won't be returning though, there are more buffets in Reno. With so many options around it's kinda disappointing that this experience wasn't what I had hoped. The service was top notch here though and I did feel welcomed. So, I would say that everyone's entitled to their own opinion, so if you do decide to vist here, really come with your own mind. Because buffets always usually are hit or miss, some people may love it, others may dislike it.

With buffet's you really have to not build your hopes up. What I like and dislike about buffet's is the "AYCE" (All You Can Eat) aspect. I'm not a buffet guy anymore honestly. But when you're looking for a deal and just a plethora of options, it always turns out to be a decent option. One thing about buffet's that tend to bug me is "timing" because they like to charge for certain menu items and such. When it comes to "Flavors The Buffet" there is no exceptions here. Allow me to tell you about my experience.

Friday April 20, 2018
Location: Flavors! The Buffet (Silver Legacy) Reno, NV
People: 2 Adults

Story:
It was my birthday weekend, I was pretty stoked and excited to not be at work on a Friday finally. I was so excited that I didn't eat nothing as I wanted to save my appetite and eat when I got to Reno. My homie and I decided on a buffet as we both could get something we want. As usual I turned to "Yelp" in helping me choose out the buffet's in downtown Reno. "Flavors The Buffet" was the closer option, so we choose this place for lunch.

Service/Hospitality:
The service here was very.."blunt" everyone seemed like they hated life this day. No smiles, rolling eyes, staff conversing with one another, not very attentive. Plus when I had a question for the guy at the register, he just looked at me like he didn't want to talk to me and sighed and answered my question. Not a good first impression at all, made me feel like at burden instead of a patron.

Food/Cleanliness:
Well, first off this is a "buffet" so the food was rather....standard. I always like to go to carving stations and get me a slice of prime rib and other roasted meats and sausage when available. The guy at the carving station was being rather "Stingy" with the cuts of meat I selected. I got a slice of prime rib which was a nice "well" for the cut selected. The sausage was pretty good as well from the carving station. They had a variety of food from American fare to Asian Cuisine. I had some broccoli beef that surprisingly was pretty good. I also had a little cup of ceviche that in my personal taste wasn't to my liking. 

They had touted the time when my homie and I went as the "Seafood Buffet" time $27.99 but I later found out if I didn't want the seafood I could of payed the regular $13.99 price. So, I ate a few crab legs to somewhat get my money worth. Honestly for this being a seafood buffet it was pretty sad honestly as the selection was really limited to crab legs, fried calamari and steamed mussels. Other than that, the place was pretty tidy, although it did take a while for a person to come and clear tables.

Overall:
No wonder I liked the now closed "Courtyard Buffet" because this place honestly doesn't compare. You can't use comp here and the service is just pretty bad. I will totally pass on this buffet and leave it to just this visit. Paying $60.61 for mediocre food isn't my idea of a good time, also I don't like the fact that I had to pay for something I really didn't care to have. I wouldn't recommend this place, but to each is their own. All I would say is get there before 4pm or remember to tell them you don't want the seafood of you want a better price.

I travel globally for business and my wife is a chef. When I'm entertaining colleagues and customers I stay far away from chain restaurants and typically pick places with a unique vision. 

2 colleagues and I were in Pinellas on business and I had heard about Cuvee 103 from a friend so I brought them there. Right off the bat, the Beet Carpaccio appetizer was delicious, featuring thinly sliced roasted beets topped with winter greens, goat cheese, and walnuts. Frankly, I had never tasted those combinations together and they worked very well. My colleagues both had a flight of three exception wines. 

For the main course, I had the Sausage Stuffed Pork Tenderloin, which arrived perfect temp., perfectly plated and was yet another new and delectable treat for me. My colleagues had the Chicken Pistachio Tortellini, and that night they were making a Flounder Ciappino. My friend that had the Flounder, who is a fish fanatic, (He lived in Japan for years and generally hates the way that American Restaurants treat fish) found this to be outstanding. This is a lively space, with inventive and delicious food paired with top notch wines. I look forward to going back whenever I'm in the area.

I finally tried Kevin's Place! I've heard of his amazing pizzas and somewhat smart attitude, and I was not disappointed.

The first time I called was for a delivery order. Kevin answered and I ordered my pizza, sausage and pepperoni. My spouse asked me to order some wings too, so I asked for some naked wings, but I had no idea what flavor. I felt a little rushed by Kevin, and ended up ordering the naked wings with sweet and sour sauce which I later found wasn't really what my spouse was wanting (oops).

Kevin himself delivered the pizza! He was actually very pleasant.

My spouse and I started with the wings. They were phenomenal. I was super impressed at how perfectly they were cooked and how delicious they were. I would at the moment say they are my favorite wings in town. I didn't expect the pizza to be thin crust, but it didn't matter to me, I was just really excited to try out his pizza. The pizza was really good, just like others had told me. I really like the flavor of the crust, and the toppings tasted fresh!

I'm definitely a fan. We actually ordered wings and pizza again the next week. Just as delicious!

If you are a pizza or wings fan, Kevin's Place is one to checkout! You won't be disappointed!

I admit it. I made a mistake.

My wife and I came here for dinner one night. She didn't know what to expect, so the easiest way to explain it was Chipotle but Italian. We went on a weeknight, so the place was pretty empty; we basically had the whole place to ourselves.

The employees were very friendly and helpful. I ordered a large with house-made pasta, pumpkin seed pesto, chicken and pulled pork, crispy garlic, and grana padano cheese. Almost the same thing I got last time, but with different proteins. The reason I got the pasta again was because I felt like it was overcooked last time. I was actually wrong. I watched as the cook checked the pasta by tasting it and brought out fresh pasta for my bowl. I was just not used to this type of pasta. It's a little denser than what I'm normally used to, which lead me to believe it was overcooked. That being said, everything else was just as good as I remembered last time. Though the chicken was the star of the night. It had just come off the grill and my wife and I kept telling each other how good the chicken was, moist and well seasoned.

I ended the meal with a matcha gelato pop. I've never had a gelato pop before, but if they are just as good as the one I had, I'm a fan! I especially like that it was partially dipped in chocolate, that really added to the enjoyment.

Definitely will be back again for lunch or dinner!

My co-workers and I checked this place out for lunch the other day. I was a little hesitant seeing the mixed reviews, and being the only one of two tables in the restaurant didn't help. Regardless, I shouldn't have judged a book by it's cover.

Like others have mentioned, the staff isn't particularly friendly, but that's okay. Our server did a good job filling our waters and got our food right, that's really all I ask.

I ordered the beef hot pot after reading Yelp reviews and looking through pictures. I was certainly not disappointed. The dish was a cross between stir fry and bibimbap. The dish was very flavorful. I really enjoyed the beef, vegetables (besides broccoli), and the sauce that was used. My co-workers even got a taste since I gave them the broccoli... I'm allergic to broccoli (Okay, that's a lie). Everyone of my co-workers told me they regretted not ordering the hot pot. Oh and I absolutely loved the charred bits of rice on the bottom!

I was pleasantly surprised by LemonGrass. I'll be back again for more hot pot!

Okay this place is great. No wonder during pre-pandemic times I could never get a table!! I've gotten takeout twice since the world ended, and it's been ready in half an hour and is piping hot. They remembered everything in our orders, which is impressive because I ordered enough for 5 people both times when there's only 2 of us.
