A lot of the things can be spicy, but it's so good. Just watch out for the peppers lurking in the sauce, and you can escape unscathed. They serve very generous portions of white rice with all of their entrees, but don't forget about the apps. Get the chicken 65, or don't even bother coming here. And if you want something even better than naan, get 10 orders of malabar porrota to soak up the sauces!

Found this lil gem in downtown Wilmington on Market Street. Nice quaint atmosphere. The service was very welcoming and explained to us what was offered by the establishment since it was our first time being there.  I highly recommend the fried pimento cheese. It's so delicious. The Brimley Shake was to die for and the FTC burger did not disappoint. I look forward to visiting this establishment again.

From start to finish, this was an excellent meal.

The Service:

My server, Danielle, was very cordial and accomodating. She allowed ample time for me to scan the menu and gave a great second opinion on my choices. She was so nice that on my way out she actually gave me an ice water to go. As hot as Florida is right now that was a godsend.

The Food:

I started with an order of Cheddar Brisket Risotto Balls. These panko crusted delights were warm and cheesy inside, with the brisket complementing the other flavors. Definitely comfort food. They serve'em with barbecue sauce on the side that's great for dipping.

I really struggled with what to choose as my entree. There are so many unique options on the menu! In the end I went with the Lobster Mac & Cheese. 
As a hardcore mac & cheese lover I have some pretty high expectations for any dish labeling itself as such. 

Imagine my surprise when I saw Danielle bring out a large, piping hot bowl of the stuff, complete with big chunks of lobster peeking out from underneath the noodles. Oh hell yes. It was on.

I am happy to say that my tastebuds were just as pleased as my eyes were. The sauce was just the right consistency for me. Not soupy, but not creamy either.
The dish is made with havarti, Maine lobster, and green onions. When combined with tender noodles, this bowl creates mouthful after mouthful of the culinary equivalent of love.

The price was a bit high for someone in my tax bracket, but my lunch was well worth it. I will certainly be back to try more items from Clear Sky's tantalizing menu.

I was looking forward to FINALLY trying Blue Willow only to have my expectations totally torn down. Why does everyone like this place so much? 
Let's start with our waitress. Jessica is the name that was on my bill, however I'm not sure if that was actually HER because she never introduced herself. She just walked up and asked what we wanted to drink, waiting impatiently as we decided. She was incredibly rude when we told her we wanted to wait for the rest of our party to show up before we ordered our food. She never once came back to check on us. She didn't give us straws for our drinks, she never filled up our water glasses unless we asked (and when we did, we had to ask multiple times), and she never brought one person in our party his lemonade (and then proceeded to try to charge him for it). 

Onto the food... I'm sure Jessica didn't think I'd notice that she gave my food to the wrong table, setting it down in front of a girl and walking away, only to go back to the table to take it back. By this point, the girl at the table had already touched my toast. So Jessica sets my plate back on the tray with everyone else's food and just takes off the toast, serving me my omelette with just the side of fruit. Then she tried to give me a side of bacon which I never ordered. Two of the people in my party have worked in the food industry and informed me that they should have completely remade my order because it was put on a different table AND the person sitting at that table touched it. 

My omelette was cold in the center and had very few green chiles. The fruit was pretty good though, so that's a plus. Another plus is that the birthday girl enjoyed her breakfast burrito. 

After this experience, I am completely turned off by the Blue Willow. I wanted to take my husband here but he doesn't even want to go after hearing about my experience. We will definitely be sticking with Prep and Pastry.
We ordered Pad Thai, shrimp rolls, fried dumplings and fried pork chops. It was staggeringly good.  I would not hesitate to order, nor would I hesitate to recommend it to others.

-- BASED ON DELIVERY ONLY --

NOTE: I've been meaning to give this another shot. Will happen soon; look for an improved review!

With that out of the way, I will say that it was delivered promptly and the person on the phone was very friendly, which is always nice. However, the food was nothing more than mediocre, especially for the price. Two pasta dishes ran us 36 bucks (40 with tip). 

Delivered in a tin container, which always changes the taste. Sauce was bland and thin. Chicken was tender, but also bland. In fact, bland is probably the best way to describe the dish. The meal was so bland that I can't even write something that's exciting. So, here is a bland review for a bland meal. 

If you're looking to eat something good, I'd recommend ordering elsewhere; if you just want something and don't need flavor, go for it.

One of my big pet peeves at restaurants is ordering food that I can make at home, so I basically never go to delis; thanks, but I'm pretty sure I have the ability and epicurean creativity to put together meat, cheese, bacon and vegetables with mayonnaise. To be honest, Adriana's on the surface is no exception to the rule. 

However, there's something awesome about this small sandwich shop on The Hill. Their spinach and beef soup is only okay, and the only interesting thing about their famed Italian beef sandwich is that it intriguingly got better with each bite (starting from "eh" to "hey, this is pretty good."). 

Their Italian grandmother, however, is awesome. 

I originally got the large sandwich and soup, and she looked at me and said, 'no." I thought she meant she was out, until she said again "No, its too much food; you'll kill yourself trying to eat it all." I jokingly replied that I was a big boy that could handle it, and she again looked at me and said "No, I'll let you have the small sandwich and soup, or just the large sandwich, but not the large and the soup--that's ridiculous. You're mother would have a fit if she saw you trying to eat that much food." 

You know what? Normally I would be mad at a purveyor attempting to tell me what I should and shouldn't do, but then again, I've never had a small Italian G-Ma telling me what to do--I'm Taiwanese people, we're programmed to listen to our grandmothers. Also, in this case, she was trying to save me money, which Taiwanese people are also big fans of; bless you Grandma for trying to save me money in these tough economic times--lord knows we could all use more Italian beef sandwiches. 

Anyway, she was right; I finished the small sandwich, but I couldn't finish the soup. I love you, Italian Grandma.

I've always been intrigued by "food wars," more specifically, by the people that perpetuate them. "Gino's is better! Pat's is better! (to be honest, I think both are "eh," there's far better to be had in the City of Brotherly Shove, but I digress)" 

Though more of a food scuffle than an all out war, I've been intrigued by the infatuation some people have with The Cupcakery and Jilly's. I've been a passive fan of The Cupcakery since they opened, but had yet to try Jilly's, namely, because I had no idea where it was and never bothered to Google™ it. 

Until now. *cue ominous orchestral arrangement*

Jilly's is okay. The lady behind the counter, who I can only assume to be Jilly, was extremely proud of her product, basically, to the point of annoyance. When I told her I'd never been there before, she said, "these will be the best things you've ever tasted."

Uh, sorry lady, I've tasted bacon. 

I ordered the Red Velvet cupcake, which tasted like it had been sitting out all day. When she came by to ask how everything was, I told her, "fine, the cream cheese icing is good." Her reply, "have you not had red velvet cake before?" Bitch, don't you know how to take a silver-lining-compliment? I tried to tell you something good about your product, and then you insult me by asking if I've had red velvet cake before? I can't wait to come home and passive-aggressively complain about you via my online review community...

Anyway, to be fair, my friend had some kind of chocolate cupcake, and it was definitely good. And I can't blame Jilly (assumably) for being passionate about her product--I'd rather have someone that's passionate about what they do over someone who's blase about the whole thing any day of the week; I think she just annoyed me because a.) I'm an ass, and b.) they're just fucking cupcakes. 

Overall, I wasn't too impressed with the place. I don't know which came first--The Cupcakery or Jilly's--but Jilly's just had this cheap feel to it for me; like a second-rate version of The Cupcakery. Also, Jilly's seemed way more expensive than Cupcakery--two cupcakes, and two glasses of milk (yeah, I know) ran somewhere around $14 dollars. AMERICAN. 

If you're going to charge me that much and also tell me that it's going to be the best thing I've ever tasted, you better make sure it's not stale.

I'm pretty sure I've mentioned this before, but I was once told two rules about restaurants--never eat at a place known for it's view, and never eat at a place that's named after the owner. Should've listened.

Vin de Set is visually appealing. The outdoor patio is nice, though I don't understand why people think the view is great; I've never found the commercialized section of Chouteau to be especially "breathtaking," but hey, to each their own, I guess. 

So, the actual restaurant is nice, which I'm assuming is done to mask the horribleness of the food/service. We had the steak tartare and escargot to start--both decent dishes. It was followed up by both soup and salad that were definitely underwhelming. We then had both the Mahi Mahi special and the Steak au Poivre (our server told me it was the "best thing on the menu"). 

The Mahi was extremely dry, but edible. The Steak au Poivre however was one of the worst things I've ever eaten. Firstly, there was no peppercorn encrustment, which I believe to be the exact definition of a steak au poivre. Secondly, I ordered the steak medium rare, and when it came out--though cooked medium rare--the center was a unappetizing grayish-brown, an immediate sign that the steak was frozen and then thawed to cook. Now, I don't mind if a restaurant does a frozen steak--I order steaks that look like this one all the time; the only difference is that it normally costs $7.99, comes with eggs and a side of hash browns, and I'm too wasted to even care. To pay $24 for this is a joke. It was so terrible, that I actually sent the dish back, something I have never done. 

Over this entire time, I have attempted to be courteous and understanding: I apologize for not enjoying the entree; when she totally forgets my soup, I note there is a possibility I may have been unclear in my order, etc. but the service at this restaurant is totally unacceptable, and only added to my frustration. We had no water refills, EVER. The waitress did not change our silverware or offer us replacements when she bussed the table (which I'm fairly certain she did only because she had to make room for the other food), when I asked what the best things on the menu are, she told me the most expensive thing on the menu--one of my biggest pet peeves. I don't mind paying a premium price for a premium product, but don't fucking tell me the most expensive thing on your menu just to try and boost your tip, especially if a.) the food is fucking dog shit, and b.) your service is terrible. 

When I pushed my plate away, she obviously was trying to hide from our table because she knew something was wrong. There were two other tables around us, and she kept circling to try and avoid us. When she finally came over, she apologized and said she would take it away and off the bill. When the bill came, the dish was still on the ticket. When I asked her, she responded with "I'm sorry, I completely forgot." Quit bullshitting me, lady. It's not like you were so busy you forgot with your whopping three tables. You were trying to see if I would pay and still tip on the total. Fuck you, the only reason I gave you fifteen percent is because I'm a dick, but I'm not a fucking DICK. If I didn't have a conscience, I would've tipped you nothing, and taken a butter knife as compensation for your terrible service and worthless food. And if all this wasn't enough, as we were leaving the hostess barely looked up and said "bye." I've had warmer good-byes from American Eagle shirt-folders. Even the lady friend, who gives everyone the benefit of the doubt--probably because she's dating me--said that the girl was ridiculously rude.

If you can't tell by now, I don't think Vin de Set is very good. However, to end on a good note, their drinks are ridicu-cheap. Goose on the rocks at $6.50? Amazing. Too bad the service will be so shitty that you'll only be able to get one before you leave in frustration. 

I'm back, people. I missed you.
Great ambience.  Outside patio/bar has a great setup. The servers are super nice & friendly. Nice venue to watch live music. Their fried pickles are a must!

This is a smoker's paradise. The second hand smoke in this place is so thick. There is no break from it. Even the so called non-smoking area is filled with secondhand smoke because the whole place is one big area. The non-smoking area is not sectioned off with anything to keep the smoke out. I really felt like I was going to get emphysema. I went outside for some "fresh" air and found that many smokers came outside to smoke. I just could not catch a break.

A former boyfriend once worked here and he gave me the scoop on all the best menu items (the scallops folks!). I fell in love with this place (not so much the boy but he was very sweet) and dine here a few times a year. My most recent visit was this last Sunday. They started their Devour Downtown menu early. Lucky me!!!! I had the braised beef. It was incredible in both taste and value. For $30 I dined on that fall-apart tender piece of meat, Italian wedding soup and cannoli. 

For those that have never been to Iozzo's but have been to Mama Corolla's.... Let me try to sway you to visit downtown instead for Italian fare. (Sorry Mama C lovers.... there's gonna be a bit of bashing here.)

1. I don't have to deal with the crowds and no reservation policy that makes going to Mama C's an 'event'. I'm 34 GD years old and don't have time for 'events'. 

2. Although I love Mama C's kitschy decor, I like the exposed brick and murano-esque overhead lighting of Iozzo's much better. It has a warm feeling without being to gritty. (Aka no plastic flowers or grapes)

3. The menu at Iozzo's has more options for the lactose intolerant crowd. Translation: more seafood. 

4. Iozzo's has a deep history in Indy. 

5. Iozzo's outdoor patio is lovely. I believe they have movie nights out there in the summer. 

6. Iozzo's bar is far superior in esthetics and drink options. Less cheap chianti and more upscale wine from home and abroad. 

7. They have a diner's club that's pretty legit. $30 yearly fee gets you all sorts of discounts on glasses/bottles of wine, first access to special occasion dinners etc. 

Reminder that this place isn't Fazoli's. You're walking out at least $30 per person minimum (drinking water, no apps). This is why Devour is so awesome.... Such a deal! This is your chance to try Iozzo's for the next week or so.

To give you an idea of how I truly feel about The Cake Bake Shop, I give you a scene from the classic movie, Clueless:

Tai: Do you think she's pretty?
Cher: No, she's a full-on Monet.
Tai: What's a monet?
Cher: It's like a painting, see? From far away, it's OK, but up close, it's a big old mess. Let's ask a guy. Christian, what do you think of Amber?
Christian: Hagsville.
Cher: See?

After hearing much a buzz surround this establishment, I decided to pop in to grab a few macarons for a friend's birthday this past Saturday. Immediately I am impressed with the exterior of the building. The building is a crisp white with an iron fence draped in beautiful garland. My heart pounds in anticipation for a few sweets.

As I walk through the front door I am greeting by a very long queue. I don't notice the stunning decor until I am at the very back of line, almost to the private room that is about to hold a birthday party. So tres chic! Totes adorbs! This room has a beautiful, large wood table and lovely white and pink decorations. Balloons abound. It looks like something out of a magazine. At this point I am thinking, the sweets from this place are gonna rock my world.

During my wait in the queue I am eyeballing the heck out of some very tall cakes on the counter..... red velvet, carrot and a raspberry filing cake. I decide in addition to macarons, I must have cake! I felt like bursting out a Marie Antoinette quote, just to make this little moment in faux-Paris feel more real.

Thirty minutes later, it is finally, finally my turn to order my sweets. I order:

6 macarons
1 slice of white cake filled with raspberry
1 hummingbird cupcake

The girl behind the counter responds, "Six macaroons?"

NO. NO. NOOOO!!!! My dear precious girl those are macarons!!! There is a distinct difference. I wanted to educate her, but for a place that prides itself on French influence their staff should know this. Here's one of many articles you can find on the interwebz that explains the difference:

http://shopruche.com/blog/difference-between-macarons-and-macaroons/

Alright, now we all know what a macaron is. Back to my order. My total comes to $38?!?! Excuse, me. WHAT? That means for each item I paid $4.75. I would know the exact price of each, but I didn't get a receipt. I asked them to print it rather than email and it never made it into my goodies bag. This leads me to my biggest complaint about the Cake Bake Shop....

How the hell do you know how much stuff costs here? The prices are not published online (expect for the drink menu) and they are not printed on those adorable little labels next to the items in the counter. Oh, there must be a reason why and I think I discovered it.

So, I leave feeling like I just got stabbed in the wallet by the Eiffel Tower, so big of a weapon that I didn't see it coming. At this point, the only thing that will make me feel 'ok' is a mouth orgasm from a bit of that cake.

I share my sweets with a female and male friend later that evening. The macaron was just odd, and it had glitter on it. Rosehips or rosewater as an ingredient, maybe? Not very flavorful, and not a perfect macaron either. They should have a crisp shell on the outside and a chewy inside. These were very flat, not very puffy at all, so you didn't get the distinct texture bite like a normal macaron.

The let down continues with the likely $10 piece of cake I bought. So it's a white cake with raspberry filling. The cake isn't moist, and has zero flavor. My friend described it as 'like eating air'.  The filling was the only decent part. 

To wrap this complaint fest up I leave you with two warnings about bakeries:

1. If they sprinkle glitter on everything, it's probably because that's all they've got going for them. I don't need glitter in my frosting. I'm not five.
2. If they claim to have master bakers behind the counter, yet these bakers don't have a bio on the website.... yeah, not looking very legit.
3. If they don't have pricing signage. It's because they know they can't stand behind their pricing or  they are the for real Louis Vuitton of the baking world.

I have yet to eat my hummingbird cupcake, so this review could be updated.

Come to this place for the ambiance, maybe a small cookie and for a mimosa for a special outing. Don't come here and treat it like a real bakery where you order a few things... like oh, Rene's down the road. Read my review if you want to know more. They have phenom macarons there that live up to perfection standards and you won't leave feeling buyers remorse.

On our last day in New Orleans we visited this breakfast spot. The decor is super cute and almost feels like you are taking a step back in time. Breakfast was really good and the service was great too. I wouldn't say the breakfast was anything special but the experience is what made it special.

We were looking for a traditional type of New Orleans breakfast while on vacation and we were not disappointed. The Trolley Stop cafe was really bustling when we got there but we were warmly welcomed and seated right away. The breakfast overall was flavorful and a hearty portion. Grits were cooked to perfection. Home fries were a little weird but I guess they just had a different take on traditional home fries. The waffle was fluffy and the banana on top was fresh. I will definitely head back when I'm in town again.

The hype is real with this little corner store. Don't be fooled by the looks of the store. Located directly across from the the LaLaurie house featured in American Horror Story (also known to be the most haunted house in NOLA), it would be easy to miss this store, but on our walk to the Frenchmen Quarter, we saw so many people eating sandwiches right outside this convenience store, so we knew this had to be a good place. 

We ordered a muffaletta and a po boy. These sandwiches were no joke and could be shared by at least  two people. I'd HIGHLY recommend the All that Jazz po boy. It was so good, unlike any other po boys we had in the neighborhood.

I'm so glad I found this little gem in NOLA!

$6 cold brew? Ouch, my wallet hurts. But, I had to give it a try. The coffee itself was good, but for it just being steeped coffee, it was really hard for me to fathom the fact that I had just dropped about $15 (tax and tip) and two cold brews. 

The place was super packed on a Saturday, but they did have tons of seating available outdoors, and it was dog friendly. 

It looked like they had a lot of unique drinks, but I'm trying to cut down on unnecessary calories, which is why I opted for cold brew. 

The actual aesthetics of this place are super cute though. Would be a good place to open up a laptop and get some work done.

We came here while on a recent visit to SB. It had some really awesome photos online and it looked like it had a cute patio area, so why not? 

We ordered the brisket, burgers, some wings, and fries. The burgers, wings, and fries were a hit, however, I think the brisket could've used a little more fat. It was on the drier side and needed to be accommodated by a lot of BBQ sauce to give it some juiciness. 

The patio was super cute and perfect for a summer day. The tables were spaced out, keeping social distancing in mind. They do close earlier than  I thought they would, so I'd just double check to see what time they're closing on the day that you decide to visit to make sure you relax while dining there.

This place is located inside the Handlebar Coffee Roasters towards the back. While looking for places to eat in SB, I found this place on a few SB blogs. I'm a bao fan, so I knew I had to give this place a try. The price points of each bao was very reasonable, so we ordered a handful. 

We ordered the mushroom bao, pork belly bao, and the crispy shrimp bao to share between the two of us. We didn't want to to order much more since we were only really here to taste it (we had plans to eat by the wharf later). 

Out of the three items, to my surprise, the mushroom bao ended up being my favorite one. It had so much flavor and was just overall delish. It just so happens that the mushroom bao was also the cheapest. The pork belly and crispy shrimp were good,  but the mushroom was hands down the bao for me.

I was really curious to try this place out as it received five stars on Yelp. I also have been on paleo and was craving something carb based, which I know this would've fixed that craving. 

Since we weren't in SB for very long, we decided to take a dozen of these empanadas to go. 

They sell half frozen and fully frozen empanadas to go, so you can enjoy them as fresh as possible. We ordered the half frozen, so the cook time was cut in half at home. 

These empanadas are some of the best that I've had. My favorite were the hongos, which were the mushroom based empanadas. 

Next time I head up to SB, I'll definitely be grabbing some to go again or eating some there.

Ordered 1 wiz wid, and 1 wiz widout.

The guy at the counter gave me an attitude throughout this whole process. I got my money ready, I placed my order, basically one with wiz and onions and one without the onions for my pal who can't have onions at this time due to recent abdominal surgery. I don't know the details of his operation but doctors told him to stay away from onions and other foods. I think it's because of the acidity or something. I don't know, don't care and I'm not a doctor. With that said, the guy at the counter from Geno's kept busting our chops and mocking us about how you can't have a philly cheesesteak without the onions. He kept going on and on, his mouth didn't stop just like the owner Joey Vento.

So I let this jerk finish up our sandwiches, I paid for it and handed him back the cheesesteaks he made and walked away from the window.

Verdict - Fuggedaboutit! Where I come from, we don't take shit from nobody! We're American born too but these guys at Geno's tend to discriminate against foreigners and people who they think are foreigners but are not. We're the ones traveling the distance and paying for their product. Show your customers some respect if you want our cold hard cash! Without us, you wouldn't have any dough to pay for your tacky light displays.

Underwhelming market place styled facility with limited seating and rude service. 
Great sales pitch by the little high school youngster behind the counter. 
Here's how his sales pitch went..
 "If you order tacos then you get soup at a discounted price."
Ok.. that's cool. "I'll take that". 
Then he asked if I had a card. I said no I'd like to pay cash. Then he said you have a resident axxess card. I ask what's that. Then he tells me, "you get a discount if you live here."
What's with that??? I didn't see that anywhere on the menu or on the counter.
So The Outsiders like us don't get a discount. I even asked, "Can you make an exception and give us a discount card since we're out-of-towners?"
With a nice little smile on his face, he said no.
This guy behind the counter was all happy and cheerful till I said I was from out of town.
WOW... then his whole demeanor changed. We were instantly marked to have crappy service... and crappy soup.
So we ordered the tortilla soup. When we got it, their soup was horrible. What did this guy do empty their kitchen sink water in the bowl.? It was all watered down and just three pieces of very small chicken in the bowl. Horrible.. Just horrible..
Let's see now...
You stand in line to order, you then wait for your food, once it is done you walk up to the counter get your food and go sit down.
And it's not like you're coming to a very fancy restaurant to pay very high prices for tortilla soup.  Almost $10 a bowl.
Good luck finding a seat to eat your food. They only have 2 tables assigned to the restaurant and there is about 10 restaurants inside of this big huge building.

118 miles, 2 hours and 25 minute drive, 96 years old today

Not me...however I feel like 96 years old
For my precious mom, I thought I'd travel to Santa Barbara.
A perfect day, a 75 MPH cruise along the coast
Spur of the moment decision and I can beat the bullet train.

I did get lost in Santa Barbara, and went past the place
After several times..I looked and saw the name Bouchon 
I had hoped my Yelp buddies were right on with this place
I loved the beauty of the entrance, and well decorated tables

I could see that this was going to be a pleasureable evening
The hostess lady asked, how many. Oooh...four of us.
She asked, "Do you have reservations?"
Oooh wow...should I lie?  Well...aaah no!

We drove up from the L.A. area to have a wonderful meal. 
The lady looked at us, and my mom in her wheelchair,
And made an exception, providing the table would be clear at 6:30
Not a problem.  We're all fast eaters.

We arrived at 5:00 p.m. and the menu was impressive.  
We had waiters and waitresses all around our table
Catering to our every needs.  Nice entree of warm fresh bread
It tasted so great with the butter...like momma just cooked it

The Wagyu steak was so delicious and tasty too.
I don't know what Wagyu is??? Is that the tail wagging at you??
Roast tail Wagyu.....  Aaawe; who knows, who cares.. it was good
And the desserts were magnificent. ...

A small birthday special with one candle on it for mom...
I'm sure 96 candles woulda burned the place down..
It was free... But for a bill over $200.00...I'm glad it was.
Excellent place and superb service.. Now for the ride back home.

Happy 96th. birthday mom.  You're very special to me.......

I was excited when I saw Morrow's, a black-owned restaurant, pop up in the neighborhood I grew up in! It sits on a St. Claude corner and you can't miss that pristine white building. 

The inside looks just as sophisticated as the outside, I must admit. I'm a big fan of spots placing neon lights on their walls and Morrow's doesn't disappoint with their frosted "Morrow of the story..." light behind the bar. When you get there, you'll see!

I stopped by Morrow's for quick dinner, so I only ordered Pasta Lenora, with Guff shrimp sautéed in a rich Alfredo sauce, but it was super delicious! Very saucy noodles with plump shrimp and cheese on top. Definitely the perfect Cajun twist to your typical Alfredo. Can't wait to go back and try their drinks!

It seemed like no business was ever successful in this location until Luciana's opened up.  On opening day I noticed that he parking lot was packed, and it really hasn't slowed down since!  I checked out the reviews and several of them seemed pretty fishy (yelpers with only 1 or 2 reviews and no picture giving the place 5 stars).  However, I decided that I wanted to see for myself.

I have been to Luciana's twice, once on a weekday evening for dinner and once for a weekday lunch.  Lunch service was much quicker which I expected because the place was less crowded.

The menu is pretty standard.  They have all of the Americanized Mexican food you know and love.  Start off with a bowl of their queso if you don't plan on living past 45, because it is dang tasty.  Their chips and salsa are also pretty good, but the salsa is a bit runny for me.

Prices are on the higher end of reasonable.  I have been satisfied with my orders during both of my visits.  Fajitas, quesadillas, tacos and the like all have been pretty dang good.  It is what it is though, don't come here expecting a super authentic meal and you'll be happy.

I'll be back!

Two words: NOT READY

I really REALLY want to like this place.  Sure it is yet another brewery trying to make its way in Indy, but I'm willing to give any place with proximity to the Monon and a beer list a try.  When I visited with a friend recently I was simply surprised that this place is open.  It is not at all ready to be.  

This place has the feel of a restaurant that opened out of desperation.  They don't have any of their own brews.  Sure they have their brewing equipment up and waiting for the proper legal paperwork to start brewing, but they don't have anything of their own.  Their bar boasts tons of taps, but only 5 beers were available.  Happily all local, but the options were very limited.  

The ambiance is cold and sparse.  It needs nearly twice the tables and chairs to fill the brewery.  It reminds of that first house you move into where you only have enough furniture to fill half of it.  The bar was made from a cheap laminate.  Honestly, if you want people to enjoy your brewery there needs to be some serious money invested, and it seems like this place just doesn't have it.

Now I could forgive bad ambiance, absent service and limited (and overpriced) menu if the beer was killer.  No beer?  No bueno.  If I'm going to pay 12 bucks for a sammie, it better be washed down with an awesome local brew I can't get down the street at the Aristocrat for cheaper.  

This place has potential, and I'm hoping it lives up to it otherwise this place is going down faster than my $5.50 ales.

This review is unfortunately going to be about the damage a simple misunderstanding can cause. First I will start off by saying that the food was excellent. The steamed buns, Crawfish and cabbage were top notch. Our server was very sweet. 
After we finished I said to my counterpart, "this is our new spot"...... but then things changed. 

See, when we walked in, there were only two other people dinning in and I made a joke about if they could "fit us in". This joke was actually aimed at us since we called prior to see if they had room. Apparently the chef didn't know this little detail. Apparently the chef took offense. 

When we were leaving we thanked everyone as we walked out and the chef screamed back "yea glad we could FIT YOU IN!", to which I was like ok weird but no big deal. But then as we walked to the car we walked past the kitchen, which the door was open, and heard them talking "s" about us and the joke I made. They didn't seem to care that we could hear them ragging on us. 

This sucked since we really enjoyed our dinner there. I hope they read this and know I wasn't making a joke about their empty restaurant. To be honest, I love a quiet empty restaurant. 

So this is just a warning about how a little misunderstanding can totally flip an experience upside down. 

The food was great though.

This is our second time ordering from here. Both times have been very fast and nearly perfectly accurate. This time they did make one of my vegan rolls non vegan. The miso soup is delicious.  The spring rolls are so crispy, and vegan. The star of the spring rolls is the sweet and sour sauce they give you. It's yummy sweet and the perfect accent.  The edamame arrived crispy and salty just right. The pot stickers have been great both times.   

This order we got Donald Duck, Crystal Shrimp, Spicy Scallop hand roll, snow mountain, rukki roll, krab mix bowl, tempura veggie rolls, salmon sake, yuppie, mussels, edamame, miso soup, and spring roll. My ex husband said he prefers Ijji's muscles. We all agree the spring rolls are divine. We got the Krab mix bowl simply because we didn't know what it was. Turns out it's just the Krab toppin in a bowl. My husband put it on top of his donald duck.  The first time my vegan yuppie and vegan tempura were perfect. This time the vegan yuppie had cream cheese, and sprouts and weird things so I couldn't eat it.  The edamame was delicious and the miso was wonderful both times. My son was confused that his crystal shrimp had Krab. The menu said it, but most places don't have crab in them. All together both orders were good and we would get them again. Delivery was flawless and fast.  The food was wrapped and contained well.  I wish they had more vegan offerings though.

I love everything about this place. The staff is all so welcoming. Our favorites are Will and Gurpreet. I've had both their gluten free crust and regular. Both are terrific. I love that they will make the gluten free in a separate area, with different gloves and make extra sure there is no cross contamination.  I'm vegan and my husband is lactose intolerant. They offer the Daiya vegan cheese which I prefer since I'm allergic to soy cheese.  Their sauce is all fresh and their toppings are always fresh, bright and vibrant. The crust is thin but also crispy and delicious. Their Garlic knots alone are worth a trip to My Pie. Rolled in fresh garlic, parsley, and olive oil. I cannot recommend My Pie enough. It's hard to find places that are so understanding about food allergies and intolerances. If I ask questions they make sure to get the label and triple check before answering me.  There has been a line a few times, and every single time it was with the wait. Pro tip. Get the garlic and olive oil under your pizza sauce. Yummmm

Update. Always add the fresh basil.  Took it too a whole new level of delicious!!

Went for my sons birthday this week as he loves lobster. He was thrilled.  The lobsters were huge and halfway through he announced that he couldn't finish it all. This never happens, someone finally found a portion big enough for him. My husbands rib eye was perfect. My parents rib eye and filet were also great. My little guy didn't love the Alfredo, it was a little pungent for him. The fresh bread was devoured many times over.  I ate nothing. There was nothing for vegans besides a dry baked potato, steamed string beans, or dry salad.  The bread was possibly safe but I refrain from barley.  Very clean, polite staff, quick service.

Wow! I've eaten here before but tonight I ordered food to be delivered to work for dinner. Let me stop you here, yes this is all for one person, yes I was more hungry than my stomach, yes I acknowledge this is an obscene amount of food and many bad choices were enjoyed tonight. Some of you know my son passed away in February. He wanted to be a chef and was a foodie like me. Our last date was a Yelp event, and I've barely eaten since he passed. I need to start this review by saying this meal was the first true food joy I've had since losing Brandon. It was that good, and I felt the love in the ingredients. 

I wanted to try something new so I got the samosa chaat and aloo tikki chaat, and aloo tikki. I was pleased with the packaging for delivery. Anything that could spill was wrapped in plastic wrap and spill proof. It arrived warm and in perfect condition. I wanted to eat at home, but was curious so I rummage in my bag for a treat. I came out with the aloo tikki. Oh boy! So good. It was kind of sweet which was awesome. The samosa are the best I've had in months and as always their dosa is amazing. The samosa chaat was great but the aloo tikki chaat WOW. The aloo tikki turned into a sauce soaked tasty little dumpling under the chickpeas and I am in love. Of course this is all fire hot and I'm vegan which means I don't get the yogurt sauce. I was stoked to remember I had some plain vegan yogurt in the fridge. Drizzled that on my chaat and commenced eating with only mild pain. 

India Kabob was not skimpy oh the sauces and gave me two big sized mango chutney plus 3 of each other sauce. A lot of care went into my food. 

I can barely breathe because I've eaten so much my stomach is trying to jump out of my body and run away before I attempt to eat any more. I am so pleased with this meal and would definitely order take out from them again.  

Also I should mention, this entire meal is vegan.

Huge slices with decent prices. This place does really seem to be a little hidden considering I've been visiting and staying in this area for years and only just now found it and tried it. The pizza is good and I have no complaints. Friendly and fast service. Not a lot of room to sit inside BUT there are tables set just right outside that are usually open. I'll definitely be back when I am craving pizza :)

I should start off by saying I'm not even a big fan of seafood. I like a few select things, but generally this isn't where I am going to spend my money, but I can still find something if someone else wants to go. 

I've had a crab sandwich here in the past which I was not very happy with, but again I'd attach that to me just not being a fan of seafood and going a little too far out of my comfort level too fast. This last visit I got the salmon caesar salad and was MUCH happier. I do like salmon quite a lot, and they give you a big block of it. They don't skimp out on it, it was almost more than enough. Everything was super fresh and I was very pleased with it.

My favorite though was the Malibu Mojito. Absolutely delicious and I think I would go here again just for that lol I recommend trying it to anyone who likes mojitos, it's a nice take on it (though it does get sticky but it's still absolutely worth it I promise).

I've also attached photos of the clam chowder and oysters my man got. I was too scared to try the oysters though so I have no comment :x he's always been happy with them though!

Overall it's always been a decent experience here. I just have to keep in mind seafood *generally* isn't my thing so I am not the best to judge, but the service has always been awesome and I would still go again and just make sure to stick to what I already know I like.

Their BBQ Pizza = AWESOME!!!

Love the setup at this place. I'm always a fan of outside seating but sadly it was way too hot to sit out there but it's nice to know it's there when we come back. 

The girl who took our order up at the counter was very nice and patient while we considered what we wanted. They have a lot of pizza options so it's hard to decide what to try, but of course I wanted the BBQ. It's one of the best BBQ pizzas I've had and I already want to come back for another!

The wait for the food didn't seem too long and was nice and fresh when we got it. They didn't have parmesan out but they have it if you ask for it!

100% plan on coming back here for more pizza when I'm in Reno :)

First of all, no reflection on the restaurant itself and this isn't reflected in my rating, but this was the first place that popped up on Yelp while searching for "BURRITOS" and there are no burritos. To be fair we were in a hurry so we didn't double check the menu, but c'mon Yelp!!!

I didn't end up ordering or eating anything from here but my boyfriend still decided to try a few tacos. 

You order and pay at one counter then take your receipt to another counter where they will make your food. They have signs up stating not to sit down and risk missing your order because they're not responsible for someone else taking it. Fair enough I guess. It wasn't packed and still seemed to take a long time for the tacos but it wasn't the absolute worst. 

My boyfriend's review is that it's just "A-OK". He said it's not his first choice, he'd rather go to one of our fave spots or try out another new place before coming back, but that he'd maybe come again and give the drive thru a try since he didn't like the ordering set up inside or the wait, but the tacos themselves were A-OK.

I have only been here twice so far but I absolutely love this place. First time I came in I got a few tacos (wanted to try the steak, chicken, and chorizo) and all were perfectly delicious. This last time I went in I got another chorizo taco and I tried the carne asada torta which I was also very pleased with. It was about double the size of the torta's I have tried in the past, which I will admit has only been a couple, but I couldn't even finish it (which while I hate wasting food this is better than not getting enough). Everyone is always friendly and there are so many other items on their menu I would like to try and plan on making this is a regular place I eat at when visiting Reno.

Not my first time at In-N-Out but this was my first time at this location. It's crazy how they all look pretty much the same, but in a good way! Sometimes it's more comfortable to have everything be so familiar. I've always been a fan of their burgers so no complaints from me there. 

Location was clean, service was friendly, and we got our food pretty quick considering how packed it was when we went (right at lunchtime). 5 Stars from me, would come again!

This place is outside and you walk up to it to order and there's a pretty good sized outside seating area.

I'm not a bubble tea pro but I have enjoyed it every time I've gotten it. Here I decided to try the strawberry fruit tea with popping boba. I think this was my first time trying the popping boba anywhere and I realllllly like this more than the normal boba! 

My boyfriend got the honeydew milk tea which was sooo good and I really preferred this over mine after trying it but both drinks were tasty and I would love to come back!

**They do not accept credit cards for payment**

WinCo was my store back in the day (2010-2012) but I still totally forgot about this. It's usually just easier to swipe my CC instead of my debit and trying to remember the pin, but thankfully I only recently changed it so I could still remember and be able to pay lol but thought it's worth mentioning!

I've recently moved to Reno and had to find where my go-to grocery store was gonna be. I was absolutely shocked (in a good way) the first time I shopped here and saw what my total was. It was sooo much less than what I have been spending at other grocery stores before I moved. It was such a relief, because I really thought I'd have to cut back on my healthy food/produce in order to save money but now I don't have to worry about it at all.

All the produce I've bought and eaten has been perfectly fine too, so I'm not sure how they're able to sell it for so cheap in comparison to other stores but I'm not gonna ask questions, I'm just grateful. 

The first time I stopped in this location it was packed and pretty overwhelming to a point I thought I might just shop elsewhere to avoid it, but my second trip I went in the morning and it was so much better, so I am just going to stick with early mornings from now on. Morning's just seem to go so much smoother and quicker. 

I also tried some of their sushi recently and it was a good treat! It wasn't as good (imo) as my favorite sushi restaurants but for something you can just pick up while getting groceries, it was pretty awesome!

Cashiers so far have been super friendly and I like that automatically you pack your own bags, since I tend to use my own bags and occasionally a backpack which is sometimes awkward to ask someone to pack for you. 

I've used self-checkout once and that also went alright. I even got refunded for using my own bags, but I don't think I did when I wasn't using self-checkout. Not a big deal at all, I'm still getting used to this as I've never been "refunded" for using my own bags until I moved here from Oregon, but I thought that was nice. 

Overall, this has won as my new go-to grocery store. here in Reno No doubt about it.

Giving Noboru 2 stars is my way of being generous. 

I went for dinner over the weekend with some friends, and we were very disappointed. Considering the price for dinner, we all had expected a lot more.

At first glance, it appears as though there is a lot of sushi. However, after a closer look, we realized there actually was about 5 different types of sushi all with slight variations. For example, there was a shrimp roll, shrimp tempura, spicy shrimp tempura, shrimp tempura "sandwich", and shrimp tempura with a special sauce. I'm sorry, but that is not a good selection!

After we ate some sushi we decided to try some of their other dishes as well. The sesame chicken was pretty good if it was fresh, if it sat out for more than 15 minutes it would dry out and become hard to chew. Also, the fried rice was really bland and had a awkward texture. 

I know people go to Noboru for the dinner, but not the dessert, but since they had dessert we had to try it. On Noboru's website and Facebook page they advertise chocolate covered strawberries and even crepes! We saw nothing of the sort. There were miniature cookies which gave one of my friends and I a laugh because they were advertised as "homemade", when they clearly came from the nearest Acme. They also offered 3 small pieces of jello in a bowl, some fruit, mini cakes, mini brownies, vanilla soft serve ice cream and tart frozen yogurt (which, as a major fro yo fan, I was very disappointed in).  The only dessert item that my table semi-enjoyed were the brownies. 

Finally, I do have to say their cold veggies were delicious! I read some reviews prior to going, and one reviewer mentioned how great the asparagus was. I'm so glad I read their review and made sure to try the asparagus, because it was by far my favorite item there! My only suggestion would be that, while good cold, it should be served warm. I had one piece that was under a heat lamp and was so warm and delicious!

Overall I would say, avoid Noboru unless you really like shrimp and overpaying for food. It may have been the cleanest buffet I have ever been to, but no matter how clean a place is, if the food is not good then it is not worth it!

On the recommendation of a friend who's moving into a nearby neighborhood we gave this pizza joint a try. It was honestly up in the air between pizza, barbecue or sushi. I'm so glad pizza won and I'm so sad I live 30 minutes away. 

On a Sunday afternoon this seemingly small restaurant is actually quite a nice size and has plenty of tables for families and gatherings or intimate lunches/dinners. Even a bar style seating area to have a quick bite and go. Parking is plentiful so no worries there. I was very surprised at how busy they were for lunch. The ambiance is comfortable and casual. Definitely has a "homey" mom and pop feel. That was solidified for me when I last minute added a Greek salad to the order and the cashier (son) said his mom was on it and should only be a couple minutes. Dad was actively making pizzas. So stinking cute. His service was so friendly and genuine. It is easy to tell this family truly has a passion for their cuisine and loves what they do. It's infectious. 

Ok, so the food. THEIR TALK WALKS THE WALK. I never really believed the whole "oh New York has he best pizza" thing until I went to New York and just so happened to have the best pizza I've ever eaten in my life there. Maybe the fable is true. Maybe it's the water. I don't know. Now I've been to Amici's. I don't have to fly to New York to have my favorite pizza, I can drive 30 minutes. If you're Italian and you try their pizza you can tell how legitimate it is by the sauce alone. THE SAUCE MAKES THIS PIZZA. The thickness, the amount of herbs, the perfect balance between sweet and savory. It's a golden recipe. The cheese to sauce ratio is perfect and the crust doesn't flop under the weight of the ingredients. We were ordering to go (pick up only no delivering) for a group of friends and we ordered a large Hawaiian ($16) and large pepperoni and mushroom ($14). A geek salad ($9), caprese salad, and garlic knots ($2-3). The portions are generous and the flavor is all there. I personally feel the price is spot on. I would pay that and then some for this pizza. The Greek salad was good. Not the net I've ever had but very good and easily fed 4 of us in addition to having a slice of pizza. It was authentic with the home made potato salad. Garlic knots are killer and a must order. I mean their understanding of savory and complimenting herbs is amazing . You can really taste it in their food that they've been doing this a long time and know what they're doing. Seriously some professional home chefs. 

Their menu is large and has a wide variety of appetizers (mussels and clams in white sauce), pasta and main Italian dishes. 
I can't wait to go back and try EVERYTHING and I can't wait to have all my loved ones who come visit me try this pizza with me. 
Because that's what I felt when I ate it. Love.

Das Essen hier ist Bombe Diggity.
Translation: The food here is bomb diggity. (Oh, yeah.)

Seriously, and the service is equally great. I love the home-y feel of the place coupled with the fact that it's run by a gorgeous mother and daughter team: the Brummis'.

Santa Barbara lacks a lot of authentic European eateries, but Brummis totally makes up for that.

+Grab a few of your friends and sit at a table.
+Show up with minimal expectations. Seriously, it's a brewing company (a step up from a pub). Relax.
+Get a beer sampler. Share it (or don't). Pick your favorite(s), order a pint of it.
+Order a burger, some parmesan fries, and some fish & chips. Share (or don't).
+Laugh, chat, chill, drink, eat, tip your waiter/waitress.

Now quit yer whinin'.

I can't tell you how much I love this place. So much. Just... so much.

The food is extraordinary. Some of my favorites include:

+Pappardelle alla boscaiola (Flat ribbon pasta with porcini mushrooms, pancetta, light tomato cream sauce). Incredibly addicting.
+Ziti al ragu di olive e capperi (Short tube pasta with ragout of olives, capers, fresh tomato, chili flakes, and pecorino cheese). I love sopping up the ragu with the endless amount of bread they provide.
+Ravioli al burro e salvia (Pasta pillows filled with spinach and ricotta with browned butter and sage sauce). I don't know what they put in here, but you'll be dreaming about that browned butter and sage sauce that night. 

They're very good about specializing your order and omitting whatever you don't like.

This is located on the outer edge of Ybor city iff of highway 60. I was here for the grand opening night. 

They have a good selection of craft beers some comparable to cigar city and other local breweries. 

The facility is a large two level building with a brewing on one side and the bar area and a large portion of the other. The setting/atmosphere here is a rustic/industrial. The antique decor adds a lot of the charm. The second level has been reserved for private parties/events, but has been opened to the public for certain events throughout the year. The tours are worth going to. We even went to the Halloween tour which featured a haunted brewery scene with acting.

More recently as of summer 2017, the popular local restaurant Stein and Vine (one of my favorites) has opened up a location here! It just keeps getting better and better!

This is another new addition to the Seminole Heights neighborhood on N. Florida Ave. This is within walking distance from a few other hotspots such as, The front porch, The C House, etc. The menu items are more Latin themed. The environment is more casual than originally advertised.

I've had the Cuban and the Lechon sandwiches. They are both amazing! The drink choices are good too. Parking is relatively limited on high peak times. Seating indoors and outdoors are limited also. Another unique feature about this location is that they have shuffleboard.  Kind of weird to me, but I guess this will catch on if you're bored here.  Like mentioned before the vibe here is very casual and relaxed. The service here has been quick and friendly with us.

It's worth a stop by if you happen to be in this part of town.

This has replaced the old Hooters that used to be in Channelside downtown Tampa. I went here on the first Friday after its opening and let me tell you, I was impressed already by the smells (aroma) alone! 

A group of us had a reservation for outdoor seating. There's seating inside also, but there's plenty of seating outside for the view. The wait staff was friendly and helpful. The scenery inside is beautiful with Mexican themed decor and wall art. I was excited to know that they had margarita flights. They have tequila flights too. I ordered the Korean beef barbecue tacos (they come in a set of two). Unfortunately, they couldn't mix and match the tacos. :( I still enjoyed them thoroughly as they were delicious A.F. 

They have paperless menus via QR codes available, though they do have regular menus if you prefer that. This neighborhood just got a little bit more awesome.

I'm glad to have found this hidden gem in the Riverview neighborhood off of a small residential street from Gibsonton Drive. This overlooks the Alafaya River and you can get beautiful sunset views in the evening depending on the time of year.

I've ordered the margaritas here and they were pretty tasty. They were $5! I ordered the Alafia burger which is normally $9.50, but requested to add bacon to it, which was recommended as a "game changer". They give you an option of chips, potato salad, or coleslaw for the side and it also comes with a pickle wedge. I chose the potato salad for my side. The potato salad was good. The burger I had was very good with the bacon included. Unfortunately, I realized that the bacon is an extra two dollars. It was delicious though, but I'll hold off on the bacon if come here another time. Overall, they have good prices for everything. They have plenty of seating outside with a nice view of the river. 

Our waitress was very friendly and responsive. She was able to provide us good suggestions from the menu when asked. I could definitely see coming back here again. It was a good visit.

I remember back in the day when the owner used to run this place from the inside of the gas station across the street. Sometimes, the lines for the food would be almost out the door. His smoker used to be out in the front of the gas station just like it is now off of US 301.

 I was so happy to see that he had finally decided to move on into his own space last summer. I finally had a chance to step in to buy some dinner and it was filled with the same wonderful smoky, seasoned smells, but this time accompanied by festive old school reggae music playing in the background (Shaba Ranks). This location is mostly used for pick up orders with very few seating though.

The menu has not really changed much since his last location.  The only item I saw missing at the time I was visiting was the ever so delicious smoky pasta salad. This is one of my favorite due to the fact that it has a smoky flavor also and some extra seasonings not typical of most pasta salads makes it so special. 

I didn't see him back there this time. Now he has other staff running this place. If I'm not mistaken, I believe it was his wife running the front that night. I recognized her from their business Facebook page. :-) 

Though this is a barbecue place, the seasonings are very Jamaican. He is very famous for his jerked chicken. It's the real deal guys!

I plan on making many visits here in the future. I would recommend this place to anyone looking for high-quality barbecue and authentic Jamaican jerked chicken.

This is a hidden gem everyone should try. They offer hot pot and Korean BBQ all you can eat. It's super authentic food that is of great quality. I highly recommend just spending the extra money and doing both the All You Can Eat Hot Pot and Korean BBQ, you won't be disappointed. 

On top of the amazing food and unique experience, their service is top notch. They are very attentive when it comes to clearing plates, changing out your bbq grill, and making sure your hot pot has enough brother. 

I absolutely love this place!

I came here for the first time with a friend then again with my sister. Hands down best sushi roll I've ever had is the Crab Rangoon Roll. SO, SO good!! My friend and I had ordered 4 different rolls and then decided next time we'd just order 4 of the Crab Rangoon roll. It is delicious! Also shoutout to this place for having an amazing kids meal that isn't just junk food like most places. My toddler got grilled chicken (you can get it without the teriyaki sauce or with the teriyaki on the side if your kiddo is like mine and doesn't like too much flavoring on their protein), a very nicely cut up mandarin, and some fries. I had to stop myself from eating her plate because it looked delicious! The decor and vibe inside the restaurant is welcoming and casual. I'm sure I'll be back again for more crab Rangoon and a kids meal!

3.5

I was in Green Hills and a bit hungry. I wanted to eat somewhere that didn't break the budget, was new to me and close by. Oh, it was raining. Did I mention that? It was raining so I didn't want to travel all over God's green earth in search of sustenance. A quick check of the Jelps and I discovered that Greek Cafe was one of the best reviewed restaurants in Nashville. I was shocked. I'd sort of noticed it as I sped up and down Hillsboro but I'd never really paid it much attention. That was about to change.

My crew walked through the door and was pleased to note there weren't many people in the restaurant. Yes, such was a selfish response but I'm being honest. We were hungry and didn't want to wait. As I looked over the menu, I noticed two things: 1.) There was a discount when paying with cash and 2.) there was a special of the day. Done and done. The special was a platter of pork, chicken and lamb atop rice and served with choice of salad and some pieces of pita. The fellows behind the counter couldn't have been nicer. They have service down to a science. They scooped a generous portion of yellow rice on to my plate, asked which of Greek, Caesar or tabbouleh I wanted and, then, proceeded to load my plate with meat, finally asking me if I wanted onions (yes), olives (yes), feta (yes), tzatziki (yes), and other toppings. I, literally, had to use some muscle to carry my tray to the booth.

The rice was delicious. It's very easy to screw rice up -- especially when made in large quantities -- but this was wonderful. I could have eaten a bowl of it by itself. I was, equally, impressed with the meat. Plentiful, seasoned and distinctive in taste and texture, every bite was a delight and showed off the cook's skill on the grill and spit. I wasn't crazy about my Greek salad. The lettuce was a bit wilted and despite the oil and feta, it was rather lifeless. I should have gone for the tabbouleh. Likewise, I was not at all happy with the tzatziki. After the wonderful taste of the meat and rice, I was surprised at how much I disliked the tzatziki (usually a favorite of mine). But for the powerful flavor of the meat and rice, the sauce could have ruined the plate and that would have been a shame.

The cafe looks as though it's been there for a while. We noticed parts of the ceiling bowing slightly and there was some water dripping from above. Oddly enough, neither bothered me much. This isn't haute cuisine. This is accessible comfort food, served at a very reasonable price and in great abundance. I didn't have a 5-star experience but I think I made some poor choices. It's easy to understand, though, why Greek Cafe is so beloved.

With all the changes that have taken place in Nashville since the time I first lived here, it's nice to know that Calypso Cafe is still alive and kicking. Granted, the Vanderbilt-adjacent location I used to frequent is no more but that just gives me more reason to venture out to other parts of the metro and see what's happening. 

On a busy mid-Spring Tuesday, I found myself in Berry Hill and very hungry. I thought about driving home and making lunch from the food I had in the fridge (responsible) but, instead, I gave in to my impulses and stopped in to Calypso Cafe. I've been ordering the same thing here for [redacted] years but I decided to change it up a bit. For my meal I ordered the black bean salad and rather than fruit tea, I ordered the hot spiced tea. Both were fine choices. Like most other things at Calypso, the salad portion was extremely generous. It's not going to win any James Beard awards but this is island comfort food. It's supposed to give you a food hug -- and it does. My plate of tortilla chips was slathered in black beans, red onions, lettuce, cheese, tomato, bbq chicken, and bbq sauce. Yes, it sounds like a ridiculous 'salad.' Yes, it's extremely satisfying. Yes, I'd order again. The revelation of the meal was the hot spiced tea. Long have I been a gluttonous fan of Calypso's fruit tea. It's addicting. But this hot spiced tea was eye-opening. With a taste I'd describe at 'Christmas in the islands', I found myself trying to balance savoring the drink and wanting to gulp it down as fast as I could. My only regret is that it's not a bigger serving. With colder weather on the way (I think), put this drink into your rotation. One thing I liked about this location was the music. I never really noticed music at the other locations. Maybe it was due to the fact that the dining room was, mostly, empty but island jam after island jam accompanied my meal and made me wish that the islands had their act more together for I would, surely, move there and spend the rest of my days relaxing.

Until that time, I'll have Calypso.

4.5

Eastland Cafe might not get the press/attention of some of its neighbors or comparable restaurants in the city but, trust, it's serving up some excellent food, satisfying cocktails and engaged service -- all in an environment you're going to want to experience. It had been on my to-try list for months and I'm glad that I had the opportunity to go there. Parking's a breeze (street or nearby lot) so don't let that be a deterrent (and, please, don't park across the street).

Once you walk in, you realize that the space is a bit bigger than it appears from the street. This allows your group of six (or so) to be as comfortable as you might be on a date. It's homey and inviting but doesn't sacrifice ambiance for either. As is my custom, I began the evening with a cocktail before delving into wine/beer. As an homage to my many years in Chicago, I opted for the Violet Hour: gin, lemon, simple syrup, and lavender bitters. Unsurprisingly, it was a floral yet muted beginning to the evening. I'm not the world's biggest gin fan but I found myself intrigued by this cocktail. I'd, gladly, order it again. As I sipped my cocktail and took in the mood lighting, our waitress brought out a hot bread basket with chimichurri. Pace yourself on this or else it's game over. Because we weren't carb-loaded enough, we ordered the chitarra pasta -- which I liked saying because, Thundercats. It's an addictive melange of: red bell pepper emulsion, sun dried tomato, garlic, shallot, chile, and tapenade crouton. Incredible.

For dinner, I thought I'd slow it down with a beer and some comfort food. I was looking for a barleywine but there wasn't any on the menu. I didn't hold it against them. Nashville is still getting its footing when it comes to beer. I 'settled' for a bourbon barrel ale to accompany shrimp & grits. Yes, I came to a restaurant like Eastland Cafe and ordered shrimp & grits. And, you know what? I'd do it again. These were ridiculous. Even though I am a native southerner, I am relatively new to the world of grits. I blame Cream of Wheat and early school days. Now that I know the warm hug of properly-prepared cheese grits, it's a new story. Not only did the plate have an ample amount of sweet & meaty shrimp, the grits were a star in their own right (and not just a side show). To the cheese grits add a healthy dose of mushrooms, green onion and lemon... and, man... don't even know. Again, coupled with my beer, it was the perfect pairing for a cold evening.

But, if I was going all in, I couldn't just stop there, right? I had to have dessert. I had to have the granny smith apple donut. I mean, it's apple rings (healthy) fried in a cinnamon dough (donuts) and served with caramel ice cream/gelato/I don't know. My eyes had glazed. My ears weren't functioning. All I knew is that I had to eat every morsel of food on that plate. All else was inconsequential. After dinner, I barely made it home before popping my top button on my pants and passing out. 

Yeah, Eastland Cafe needs to be in your rotation.

I've reviewed the other two. Might as well make it a clean sweep. This is a pre-lockdown experience.

With its generous size and quick-moving line, I wondered if the west (Sylvan Park or nah?) location was the de facto locals Hattie B's. By reviews, it's the second-most popular spot but by the people I've seen in the dining room, it seems to have the most 615ers. I chalked that up to the fact that it's the farthest from Downtown. To come here, you've got to really want to do so. You don't show up by accident -- especially when there are spots closer to the hotel/AirBnB madness. I could be wrong.*

What I'm definitely not wrong about is that naked/grilled tenders are the way to go. Since developing my gluten-problematic gut, I've had to think long and hard about many of the food/drink items I used to consume without worry. So, unless I was *really* determined, hot chicken was a thing of the past... unless it was grilled instead of fried. Now, I have no illusions that Hattie B's has a GF kitchen. Even ordering grilled tenders is likely to result in cross contamination. But the heart wants what the heart wants, y'all. One tenders plate to go later (hold the bread) and I was in the wind.** 

The tenders were as jumbo as their breaded counterparts. With no breading to hide it, I tasted more of the spice and had the ability to savor the flavor. The fries and black-eyed peas were the same as they ever were. If this isn't your first time at the Hattie B's rodeo, you know what to expect. The naked tenders were a welcome surprise and on a mid-fall Saturday night when I just wanted comfort food, trash TV and had nowhere to be for a while... they did me quite nicely. Maybe I was the last to know about the naked/grilled tenders. In case I'm not... you're welcome. Also, if you live in town, this is the Hattie B's*** you'll want to patronize.

*I'm not wrong.
**Order online. Pick up. Leave. No fuss.
***I still have issues with the brand/appropriation.

2.5

The good things to start: the employees are wonderfully nice. Everyone from security to the door guys to the bartenders... super nice. I think many of the problems I had/have with The Valentine are due to the fact that it's new. BUT if it's open to take my money and is located on Broadway (ground zero in the tourist traffic game), I think it's fair to expect that it would have its act together from the very beginning.

I came here with a good friend in late spring. I was excited to spend time with her and to show off a new business. She, being from TN, was dubious about going out on Broadway but she indulged me. I left with egg on my face. We walked in to find a, largely, empty huge space. 'Well, it's Sunday so maybe it needs some time to amp up.' Thing is, even though it may be Sunday, it's still Broadway. Most establishments weren't hurting for a crowd. We walked in and thought about getting a bite to eat. The menu, at that time, wasn't quite ready. We'd thought about having salads and sandwiches. At the time, though, all they had to offer were chicken tenders and pretzel bites. Hmm. Okay. Drinks. We're in a bar. We'll get drinks. I got a Stiegl Grapefruit and my friend ordered a white wine... which came in a plastic cup and was a small pour. Hmm. Okay. We tried to make the best of it (the bartender was very sweet as she apologized about items that were unavailable) but as we started talking, the band started up. I hate to yuck someone's yum but this band was not the most talented. But they were loud. Very loud. The emptiness of the bar didn't help the noise or talent level. Wanting to escape the madness, we tried to salvage our time there by going to the roof. Since it was such a slow night, the venue was closed past the second floor. I get it. I do. But rooftops are Broadway bars' bread & butter in food weather. After the first floor, the rooftop should always be open. My friend, patient and sweet as she is, was nearing her breaking point. We gulped our drinks and took off to see what else Downtown had to offer.

Despite the abundance of local pizza places, I was told time and again that I *had* to eat at DeSano. I'm happy I came to check it out. I had a good experience and I'll get to the meat of it in a quick bit. I just hope that for as many people who rave about DeSano (and, again, it's quite good) that they spend as much time and energy trying out and patronizing the pizza places that were here before Desano was. PSA concluded.

My assistant and I were in the area getting the notes on an event we were producing (I can't believe Living The Yelp Life came together in just a little over a month; you're welcome) and needed to get some lunch. Realizing that I was close to the site of so much pizza joy for many of my acquaintances, I took the chance to pop in for a pie. Desano is deceptively big and depending on which you enter, you'll have a different experience. One side is tables, kitchen and industrial seating. The other side has all that and a BAR. Choose wisely. We sat on the kitchen side but our drink needs were met by the large cooler in front and in back of us. If you're into beverages (not just booze), you're going to to want to spend some time looking at all the selections. Because it was late spring, I availed myself of a Stiegl Radler grapefruit. It's always a good choice. Feeling adventurous, we opted for the special pizza of the day. It only came in one size so that was one less decision to make. This is a good thing.

We sat ourselves at a communal table and set about planning and prepping. Before too long, our number was called and the pizza was up. This specialty pie was a saucy number: peppadew-based sauce, not much cheese, shrimp, garlic, and peppers. It... was very very good. Between two people, it was an easy split but most overweight Americans (no shade, just truth) could probably handle one on their own. The pepper-based sauce was a sweet take on a tomato sauce and I was impressed with the generous portion of shrimp on the pie. This wasn't a 'two pieces make an order' sort of boondoggle. This wasn't your post-Little League game sort of pizza pie. This was on the fancier side of casual. 

I definitely understand why DeSano has made such a positive impression on so many. I'm not always in this part of town but when I am, I have to admit that I have somewhere new to put into rotation. Score one for the power of Yelp reviews to inform and shape business decisions. Whaddya know? The site works!

Admittedly, Hermitage Cafe is probably best experienced when not completely sober. And, yes, the odd hours *are* correct: they open at 10 pm. But, dangit if there doesn't come a time in life when you need exactly what a greasy spoon can do for you. It's as American as apple pie and the HC is as Nashville as... well, Nashville.

You know the story by now: old gas station, set on a hill south of downtown (it took me a while to do the SoBro thing; if you think 'Rutledge/Rolling Hill' is coming out of my mouth any time soon, you have another thing coming), dedicated to diner hits. It is what it is. It's even managed to resist a hipster makeover (although it did get a good cleaning). So, if you're three sheets to the wind and want* a localized Waffle House experience, you know what to do.

I knew what to do. Somehow I held it together enough to note that I needed protein, grease and more protein... and no bread. Well, Hermitage Cafe is not the place to go if trying to maintain a GF diet. But you should know that already. Even if you sacrifice the addition of a delicious delicious biscuit, there's no way that griddle isn't laden with gluten. If you have dietary issues, try to avoid. I write 'try' because if you're here, odds are you're tanked and not thinking clearly. Where was I? Oh yeah: ham steak. I ordered a ham steak (complete with that o ring bone), scrambled eggs and homefries with cheese & onions (extra charge). To go. I hopped in my awaiting ride, came home, mixed everything together and devoured the salty, savory mix/mess. It's not pretty. I paid for it the following dayS. I knew what I was doing. Odds are, it'll happen again. It will happen to all of us. You know why you're here. Don't act brand new.

*'Need' is probably more accurate.

I finally made it in to Adele's and I am kicking myself for having taken so long to experience it. Even though it's a Gulch mainstay, the location and build out makes it seem a bit as though it's by itself on the mountaintop. It's a nice dynamic and adds a bit of mystery to an area of town that's known for congestion. Plus, if you can create that sort of ambiance outside of a former garage, more power to you.

Once you walk inside, that airy 'Olympus' feel resonates even more strongly. What I had previously chalked up to Instagram features, I came to realize, was real life. The light really *is* that favorable here. Again, what could have been industrial and cold comes off as being quite warm and relaxing. Kudos to the designers. You did an excellent job. Coming here, you're in the mood to dine, not just eat.

Had I not been here for a lunch work meeting, I would have availed myself of an adult beverage. But, I needed to be coherent so I opted for an unsweetened tea. I would have preferred an Arnold Palmer (RIP) but Adele's didn't have any lemonade. The drink came in a Tom Collins glass. I know that glass choice tends to be controversial, so I wanted to prepare people for it. The lunch menu has recently changed so even if you were familiar with the offerings, come back in and see what's new. We started with the kale salad because duh. There's a reason it's mentioned and photographed so often. My goodness. It's a work of art. It seems simple enough -- kale, pecorino and anchovy dressing -- but the execution is so spot on, so comforting... To begin, the kale is wonderfully massaged. Kale is a rough piece of roughage. If it's not massaged properly, nothing about it is pleasurable. This kale was a delight. Adorned in a marriage of salty, savory cheese and anchovy, each bite is better than the last. The kale salad sounds basic but it's fantastic. Order it. Buoyed by the beginning of my meal, I was very excited for my main. I ordered the Moroccan Eggs. It's a new dish and it's one that, I think, will be quite popular. In a scalding hot personal skillet, the kitchen combined egg, polenta, chili, goat cheese, and tomato into a just-enough-spicy, deceptively filling dish. It's a very successful lunch offering. And the meal wouldn't have been complete without a taste of the JW potatoes. What's not to like about fried potatoes? Get 'em and split 'em.

Adele's is a brilliant addition to Nashville's culinary scene but that's to be expected of a Waxman restaurant. There's a reason why he exists in rarefied air in the food world. Travis McShane has executed a wonderful journey for the eyes and belly at Adele's. It may have taken me a minute to come here but it won't take me nearly so long to return.

4.5

Who would/could have predicted that seafood in Nashville would be a trend? Not me, but I'm not complaining. Sea Salt is a nice shot in the arm to the culinary landscape in Music City and it's doing a nice job bringing the heat to Downtown as the previously ignored part of the city experiences a wondrous rebirth. While the cowbros and woo hoo girls troll Broadway, local biz owners have been steadily and quietly re-creating a Downtown Nashville locals can be proud of.

Let's start with the building. There's a wealth of gorgeous old buildings from 2nd-6th and I am here for them gaining new life. The Sea Salt building is the former home of a famous blues artist and the owners have added their own touches to the historic location. Actual sea salt adorns the main dining room, as does wrought iron, exposed brick, high ceilings, and nooks & crannies. Genuine farm equipment (hand tools) dot the walls and tell a story (the wares come from the family, not eBay). With Sea Salt only being around for a week (!), I was very impressed by the number of covers I witnessed while there. Granted it was a Friday night but the place was packed. The room had a wonderful energy and people seemed to be in great spirits.

To the spirits in the air, I added some spirits to my belly. The bar program is legit so spend some time coming up with a game plan. I started the meal with a Corsair Collins.
