We were led to a private booth in the back. I quite liked it. It's a two top (I supposed you could squeeze four if all parties were *really* skinny) just off the bar that offered a nice bit of privacy. Just as we were getting settled, Wayne, our waiter, came by to welcome us and introduce us. He was a fantastic server. Not only did he know the menu well, he was a fun conversationalist and added to our dining experience. I would ask for him. Study the menu beforehand but have backups. etc. has already had some stock issues (as a wine I was contemplating was unavailable and the pastrami for the duck breast appetizer was nowhere to be found). Foregoing cocktails (the gin looked surprisingly good), we opted for a bottle of wine. The Melee Grenache was a nice choice (served at a chilly 51 degrees, as it warmed so did my appreciation of it) but overpriced. It was a special occasion and I was expecting a markup but know that a bottle of it will cost you twice what you could get it for at a local wine shop (damn you, beer, for having so many carbs!). 

Since we were without the duck breast app, we opted for the scallop crudo. It's a visually stunning plate. Six scallops come atop roasted poblano pepper orange oil and accompanied by black lava salt. For each bite, I'd recommend pairing the protein with the mustard seeds and orange segments. Despite trying to avoid carbs, I couldn't resist the temptation of the watercress tempura (the health cancels out the fried aspect, right?). I'd thought about ordering the tuna but I avoid asparagus like the plague (horrible, horrible vegetable). Instead I went for the lamb. Again, what a pretty plate. My meal came with a healthy portion of medium-to medium-rare (a little bloody for my tastes but I ate it all; perhaps ask for medium-well to get medium?). The meat was above a drizzle of ginger masala and served with pea mint chutney. I tried to avoid the crispy coconut potatoes... but, c'mon. They were made even more decadent/addictive with the smoked date yogurt (which had a thicker consistency than you might think). The okra was an afterthought but props to a grilled, crisp version of the vegetable which is way too often slimy and gross. I fought the temptation to get dessert even though the chocolate panna cotta and grilled pineapple sorbet fought for my love.

etc. provided us a lovely evening with good food in a pretty setting. When going out to eat, that's, pretty much, all you need. I'll be curious to see how the menu develops in the future but for an initial effort, it's quite good. Welcome to Nashville.

Is there a secret to getting past super angry owner/hostess?  We've been 3 times and I swear she gets angrier each time.  All 3 times her attitude was so off-putting I had no desire to try and enjoy our meal.

Luckily the excellent service would make up for the angry owner, right?  Wrong.  I am convinced they do not care about repeat business here otherwise they would put some effort in.  

The food is ok.  I haven't had anything spectacular..  or bad.

The perfect meal. Seriously. My friends and I dined at Suraya on a rainy Tuesday. There is a free parking lot directly behind Suraya that made parking a breeze. The restaurant is self is surprisingly large with ornate decorations that contribute to the ambience. 

We decided to go for the tasting menu which is $58 per person. I think this is a great choice if you have never dined at Suraya before or aren't familiar wIth Lebanese food. It includes a variety of dips to pair with the house made pita. These dips/spreads can be used on various other courses over the evening. My personal favorite was the labneh which is a yogurt based spread; it is rich and creamy with a unique flavor. The baba ganoush was also excellent. Each person then chooses another "mezza" (appetizer)--definitely an advantage of dining with a larger group here as you get to try more! My favorite was the fatteh which is a chickpea dish. This is honestly incredible with both sweet and savory flavors. 

For an entree, I chose the kawarama. Entrees are smaller serving sizes but considering how much you will have eaten by the time the entree comes out, it's the perfect size. My kawarma was cooked perfectly and paired well with the dill yogurt and pomegranate salad it was served with.  The final part of the meal was dessert. At this point, I was really full but still managed to enjoy the kanafeh which was a cheese based dessert. This is a bit rich to end with, but the flavors are perfect. It took us almost three hours to dine at Suraya which makes it the ideal spot for a special occasion or to catch up with friends!

This used to be one of my favorite restaurants in stlouis but I moved out of state and decided to come back a couple years later .. only to be extremely disappointed. 

My favorite thing used to be the mashed potatoes. I would order them all the time and even just get orders to go because it was THAT good. ... when I was ordering food, I asked the waiter if the recipe has changed and she said no.. however the new mashed potatoes were Not good!! It was chunky and NOT smooth like before. The taste was bland! Honestly tasted like microwaved mashed potatoes from the dollar tree. I remember it being so heavenly and flavorful and this time it was just ... no it was so bad I had to stop eating after a couple bites. I was looking forward to these so much!! Flew in from California with full excitement JUST FOR THIS!! Im beyond disappointed and sad at how bad they were. . 

I noticed the menu itself changed the items since I had last been here which is fine.

We also ordered the avocado and chicken apps, stuffed mushroom??, calamari and the margarita flatbread

The avocado and chicken appetizer / $5 dollar option for happy hour was probably my favorite thing all night! It was super good and unique! Never tried it anywhere else.

The calamari was good, i really loved the sriracha sauce that it came with!!! The taste of the calamari was different than what I used to order here but this version was still good.

Personally I'm not a fan of the flat bread or the stuffed cheese mushrooms. Everyone else thought it was good but personally I didn't like either one. The pizza tasted kind of bitter, as did the mushrooms. 

I also tried the blueberry lemonade drink. It was super fruity and filled with a tremendous amount of blue berries. Definitely a new drink to me. 

Customer service was my fav. I think her name is Jessica?? . She was hilarious and Easy going, i seriously enjoyed her being our waiter!!

We live in Franklin and for several years my wife has included this as her favorite local place to eat & hang, so read my review carefully as my wife and I have different opinions. 

The food is not all that is cracked up to be and a the kind of prices they charge, my expectations always exceed the delivery. 

For Franklin this is a very nice place to have in town, the environment is terrific, parking is problem - only on street parking and no valet. There is a parking lot on the back side and if you are a fast runner and adept at running with an umbrella, you might make it to the back door on the top stairs 1/2 way wet in a rain storm. So if you are not up for this kind of adventure, be patient and circle the block until you find a place, it usually only takes 15 minutes or so. 

The atmosphere is great and they have two bars - an upstairs bar and a downstairs bar. Down Stairs is more comfortable, but for obvious reason, it also fills up quickly - but upstairs is real nice also. 

Th service staff is real nice, they are a tight not group and always provide solutions and they all believe in the concept. 

HOWEVER - i cant get by the taste and quality of the food. My wife surprised me the other night with take out and she refused to tell me where it was from, She wanted me to have an open mind in my evaluation. She knew i had so many bad meals that if she told me where it came from, that i might be predisposed to just give a negative assessment. So she suggested i "just try it" an tell her what i thought, without knowing where it came from. So with that in mind the experiment began. I had a grilled Hanger type steak with grilled shrimp - shrimp were OK, but the steak was so bad that after two bites i stopped eating. My wife, then decided to try it since she could not believe me. After one bite, she also stopped eating. the steak was bitter, from too much vinegar and it was TOUGH. I ate the shrimp and concluded my effort. 

My wife tried the fish, it was soupy and although better than the Steak it wasn't great and we decided that the fish was the winner, but the bench was set pretty low. 

Finally she told me where the food came from and we both agreed it was an honest negative assessment and no partiality for previous bad results. 

The place is nicely designed and the service is great, its just the quality and recipe of the food really needs some attention. So keep in mind that My wife really likes the place and maybe my taste for things is not the only authority. 

good luck

We probably should have read some reviews before ordering sammies to go because my husband and I certainly could have filled our bellies and then some by just splitting one sandwich. However, we didn't read anything in advance and ended up with two HUGE sandwiches. The cashier taking our order pointed out the most popular options which are highlighted in boxes on the menu but I went with her personal favorite- a cheese steak with some additions and substitutions. I'm super happy that I did because it perfectly hit the spot upon initial consumption and as leftovers a couple of days later. We did have a bit of a wait since we ordered 2 warm sandwiches and there was a bit of a line ahead of us but we throughout enjoyed the food and customer service throughout our time here. I'm sure we'll order more in the future.

Let me start with the place is beautiful.  Staff and servers were great! Beautiful gift shop to browse through or buy while you wait.  The patio looks like it'll be amazing during the summer months.  

Ok...so for the food... honestly it was ehhh. I'm Mexican....so any Mexican place I try...I start with the basics.  Tacos, enchiladas, tostadas, rice, beans, etc. If you can't do the basics...well it's just that... the basics.  ALL was BLAND. The best I could do was add salt. 

Let me add that a few days ago I had the stomach flu and all I wanted was soup. I saw that this place was open and had my fiance go pick me up some Caldo de res (beef soup) like my mama makes. I gotta tell you you it was close. Almost but not quite like Doña Aída makes but very good. Which is why I was so excited to try this place in person!

Sad to say I was disappointed. Left the place with half the food left on my plate.  The beef taco and beef tostada shells were pre-made (like you would buy off the shelf at Schnucks) and the beef had no seasoning at all. The beef enchilada was dry as well. Rice and beans were ok. 

I'm willing to give this place another try because their soup was great,  the people were great and the ambiance was beautiful. It was suggested that I try a few other things on the menu so I'll definitely post an update when that happens. Til then I'll unfortunately have to give it 2 stars for now.

First time to Kibroms - never went to the previous locations. Super psyched that it is close to us. Loved the food - first Ethiopian food in quite some time. My wife and I each got a 2 item combo plate, but now I wonder if it would be better for us to split a single 4 item combo plate instead. The boys generally loved the beef white tibs (#2) and one of them loved the lentils (#18 & #19) but neither liked the injera. Pretty busy which was awesome to see.

Rough spots: picky eater kids will be kind of out of luck. It would be good if they at least offered some plain unseasoned rice. Also, napkins were small and not on all tables. But generally a great eating experience! Can't wait until the next time!

Love this place!!! 
If you're looking for  an intimate but casual dining experience this is it. The staff are incredibly friendly and the food is amazing - fresh ingredients - fresh pasta - amazing desserts... do i need to go on? You can watch the chefs work their magic in the kitchen (it's open to the dining area.. you can watch them make pasta!) and there's even a little booth in the back if you require a bit more privacy.. 
If going with a larger group I would definitely make a reservation, and it's also BYOB.. 
Be prepared to overeat and then still squeak in dessert (trust me, you'll want to)!!

Spent 40 bucks on a Togo order. I order spicy noodles with chicken, PCU with chicken, Panang chicken, and Kha tofu. 

I first ate the soup when I got home and it was amazingly too sweet for me. Also, they left the dry herbs which I had to pick them out as I ate a few bite. 

Then, I tried the Panang which was flavor less. It just tasted purely like coconut milk and rarely any curry flavor .. 

Next, I just took a spoonful taste of the rest of the food and it was just as flavorless .. The "spicy" noodles was mild and all you taste was the veggies. The PCU noodle felt like they poured soy sauce and called it a day. It was just not Thai.

I'm giving 5 stars because the food was fantastic.  The start was a little rocky though.  The hostess sat us, gave us menus, and we started the "what are you getting" dance.  The love o my life takes forever and a freakin day to order.  F-O-R-E-V-E-R.  So after 15 grueling minutes the server comes and takes our order.  W ask him questions, he answers and assures us that we have made excellent choices.  Five minutes later he comes back and apologetically tells us that we had been given the dinner menu at lunch time and the entrees we wanted were not available.  OK so now I'm a wee bit peeved but we figured out new meals, did a few deep breaths, and ate a lot of salsa and chips.  Which are amazing by the way.  Like I asked if I could have the recipe amazing.

This is an extremely gluten free friendly restaurant.  Quite a bit is naturally gluten free and they seem well educated on the entire subject.

On to the meal!!!  The full round up of what we got included cochinita pibil street tacos, chicken tinga tacos, grilled baja fish tacos, cilantro rice, charro beans, and street corn.  Everything was excellent but the close your eyes, sit back, and thank heaven you're eating this award goes to....fish tacos and street corn.   So delicious.  Everything was fresh and seasoned perfectly.  

The fact that I'm more than willing to schlep to Webster Groves for tacos and corn should clue in that this place is awesome.

I came here last week with a friend as we walked around and reminisced about the UA area and how much it has grown since we were in college. 

This is a new place that I was unfamiliar with, and located just past some new student housing, making it a prime location. It's decorated with a nice modern style that isn't really my vibe, but it would probably be a nice hangout spot for many if we weren't living amidst a pandemic. 

I ordered an excellent grapefruit flavored green tea, that had a fresh grapefruit wedge inside the cup, which added an extra zing to the otherwise bland tasting tapioca pearls. 

My friend ordered the Jasmine Milk Tea, and had a lot of excellent things to say about it. In particular, she enjoyed how it wasn't too sweet. 

The customer service was great! The woman at the counter was a gracious hostess, and helped us pick out the right drink for our palates. The price was also right, as the offerings here were similarly priced in comparison to other places in town. 

That said, this place is well worth a visit,

I came here because I had some friends who praised their pizza to the high heavens. So I just had to try it upon the realization that I was just a stone's throw away one weekend afternoon. 

However, I ended up not ordering pizza, as I was enticed by the choices offered in the choose your own bento box. I chose to get the eggplant parmesan, coupled with a caprese salad, a traditional salad, and the piece de resistance; a healthy slice of cheesecake, (all for 12 bucks I might add). 

Their sauce game is strong. In fact, I would argue that they have the best pasta sauce in Tucson. The amount of sauce in my entree was perfect. In fact, it closely resembled the one I had during my visit to Siena, Italy a long time ago. 

Everything else was pretty standard. However I was puzzled by the fact that they did not include a piece of bread with my entree. I had to ask for it. Thankfully, they provided it at no charge. 

That said, I intend to go back very soon to try their pizza.

I decided to visit this place on a Friday morning just before 9 a.m. while visiting Reno.

I was able to easily find side street parking directly across from the coffee shop and it was only about a six minute drive from our hotel downtown.

They have 8oz, 12oz, and 16oz cups available so I opted for an 8oz mocha with two shots today. The 8oz and 12oz sizes come standard with one shot, but you can get the second shot for free with your Yelp check-in. The coffee was super good! It tasted balanced and the coffee had a unique flavor. 

The walls were made of exposed brick and the seating area is pretty large. The ceiling also was exposed which gave it a slight industrial feel. The staff was very friendly.

I would come back if I was in the area again and wanted coffee.
I love this place but unfortunately it is completely closed down and fenced off with a for lease sign posted. Bummer!

We finally made here! We went for happy hour and it was awesome. They have 1/2 off bar snacks, $2 off drafts from 5-7pm. On Tuesdays, they have $2 tacos, $2 tecates, and $5 margs.

We sat at the bar and it wasn't too crowded when we went. The bartender was training someone new so we didn't have the best service but the bartender was still friendly.

We got:
Korean Wings - delicious with a hint of spicy.
$2 tacos - beef and chicken. They don't do plain tacos, the beer one had a special sauce and crispy chips on top. the chicken one was fried chicken with a spicy sauce and toasted coconut. The beef taco was better then the chicken.
fried eggplant bites - AMAZE. SO GOOD. i could not stop eating them!
grilled cheese - they have a specialty grilled cheese everyday. they had the pork roll, egg, and cheese when we went and the BF loved it. It comes with fries and a special sauce to dip. It was good but i couldn't make out what the sauce was!

We cannot wait to go back. Definitely an expensive happy hour but we love this place more then SPTR (south philly tap room).

For all the years I've lived in Reno, I've never been here.  I've been a fan of pho for a few years now and just came into this restaurant for the first time. I will tell you it is busy! The business hours are great! Open until 3am?! The majority of places around here that serve pho are closed by 9 or 10pm. I suggest getting an order of spring rolls for an appetizer. They're sooooo good especially when you dip them in the peanut sauce they are served with. I ordered the rare beef pho, the regular size is pretty sufficient for me. I added my hoisen sauce, siracha, and all the additions they bring with it. Let me tell you, SO GOOD!! We sat down with no wait at all and left fairly quickly as well. I will be coming back here for sure!! I may become a regular in fact.

The service here is terrible and they are racist to asians. They forgot to put onions in our sandwiches. When we went back to the counter to complain, the woman in the back told us we were wrong and started yelling at us, and SLAMMED the window on us. Terrible service. 

Also, the meat has no flavor. Geno's has a better cheesesteak than this place.

My favorite spot for an acai bowl or healthy smoothie! 

I order the Mean Green smoothie and change it to Vegan Protein and it is my ultimate go to when I want to tackle the day. It also cures my hangovers so a win win in my book.

Their acai bowls are delicious too and the dragonfruit option is another goodie.

Everyone that works here is always super attentive and friendly. Can't recommend Enerjuicer enough!

After coming to Bacara for almost 10 years, I can't believe I'm changing the review from 5 stars to 3. I was literally just put in a room with what looks like black mold. Huge spot underneath the TV. The first thing you see coming in. 
Look, it probably isn't, but the big spot is unsightly and makes you think this is black mold, so it's halfway bad already. 
I'll let you know if I die.

It is the evening of July 15, 2011. The plan for the night is to go out with friends to Ciro's Speakeasy. Shoes are shined, suspenders are fastened, shirt and pants pressed. 

On the way out, I grab the fedora and the U gang are all ready for our first experience of absinthe.

Upon arrival to the address, Ciro's is well hidden, located at the bottom of a residential building. I stand outside smoking a cigarette not knowing what to expect.

Cigarette is finished, so I step in Ciro's. In that very moment, I feel as if I traveled back in time to July 15, 1925. The speakeasy is intimate and dark with jazz playing in the background. I feel at any moment Al Capone could walk in the joint. I await anxiously.

In the mean time, we get a round of absinthe to ease the anxiety over the possible arrival of the most notorious gangster. The absinthe arrives and we watch it is prepped with melted sugar and a water drip by our vixen waitress. We down our powerful black liquorice liquor and are informed that Mr. Capone will not be coming to Ciro's on this night. We are all at ease.

Our group of gangsters and gangsterettes is so large and menacing looking that they quickly accommodate our group, moving us to the back VIP room.

Here, the alcohol and loud laughs continue to flow freely. On the next round of drinks, I glance over at the waitress and order a Tryst. It is made with absinthe, gin, and cucumbers; what an absolute delight. It is light and refreshing.

The new guy in our gang, Brian, passes out because he cannot handle his absinthe. I finish his absinthe for him and then proceed to order myself a Bramble. Another gin drink that contains blackberries, It is absolutely made to perfection. I casually sip on my Bramble while sharing the delectable duck fries and truffle popcorn with my gang.

After a classy night of drinking, we stroll out and I tip my fedora to the bartender for truly being a master mixologist. I step out and immediately teleport back to July 15, 2011.

So that is how it feels to be in a speakeasy during the Prohibition period. What a night.

What would be a proper slogan for this place?

MacDintons: I am only Irish in name and nothing more.

OR

Macdintons: I am a terribly overrated, overcrowded college bar

OR

Macdintons: Home of the diluted alcoholic drink

Hmm... after careful deliberation, the winner is all of the above. Yes, Macdintons: The overrated, overcrowded college atmosphere Irish bar that is only Irish in name and wildly popular for serving diluted alcoholic mixed drinks.

Save your money and just go for shots here. Seriously, I think i drank coke on the rocks. I would not be surprised if I was drinking RC Cola from Winn-Dixie they are so cheap.

The ambiance reeks of a college bar, so be warned, but if that is your thing then you might like this bar. It really has no Irish pub charm, so if you are looking for that, look elsewhere.

Its saving grace is the big patio area.

I wold prefer not to come back to Macdintons again.

FYI: If you leave your card over night, they will destroy it. You are warned.

pizza week - stella's answer to philly restaurant week is actually a solid deal.
you get to choose a starter (an app or a salad or a soup), a pizza, and a happy ending (gelato) - all for $25. 

my sister and i took my mom out for lunch, and between the three of us, we chose the arancini and the marinated olives for our starters - both were delightful.

we had a difficult time narrowing down our choices for pizza - they all sounded great.
we decided on the quattro formaggi (sauce/4 cheeses), the pepperoni (abbruzze pepperoni/mozz/sauce) and the san daniele (proscuitto/smoked mozz/arugula) - they were delicious. (i think the arugula might have benefitted from a post-bake drizzle of olive oil, but that might just be me)

i would love to try the pistachio, the mushroom, the zucchini, the pancetta, the tartufo, and the piccante pizzas...damn you, stella - STELLLLLAAAAAAAAAHHHH - you make me sound like a glutton!

the crust is a tender and delicate version of chewy - nice and thin and tasty, it was beautifully spotted with char (this is a good thing). the toppings were delicious, and generous...we ended up eating only half of all three pies, so home the rest went

the honey-mascarpone gelato was delicate and delicious, and the stracciatella was generously veined with chocolate - nice for 3 to share.

they make a good espresso here - italian-mamma-approved.

for my 100th, i am happy to review sycamore, named in honor of the historic and stunningly beautiful sycamore in town (the sycamore is my favorite tree). i had the pleasure of dining here with two of yelp's very own lovelies, Blake and Michelle, and enjoyed a fabulous meal, good wine and great company. 

from the original architectural details to the color scheme, materials, and lighting used throughout - this intimate space is beautiful to behold. 

we know the very talented young chef, yelp philly's own Sam J, and we met the congenial owner who spoke about the space and about their mission/philosophy - this sort of thing interests me immensely, maybe not of great concern to everyone though. their attention to detail belies the fact that they have only been open since june of this year (i absolutely love their logo and the font they use) kudos to our server Elle who was adorable, professional, friendly and on point in anticipating our needs. 

amuse bouche was a divine shot glass of warm and velvety potato puree/soup with a trickle of truffle oil. 

the cheese platter was phenomenal - four cheeses, each better than the next, accompanied by bread, honey, house-brined olives, and incredible drunken raisins. 

for the next course we enjoyed the baby arugula salad with roasted squash, cranberries and goat cheese, and the pancetta, caramelized onion and goat cheese tart - i would have licked the plates clean had i been at home 

for entrees - i tasted the boeuf bourguignon with herbed mashed -  comfort food at its soul-satisfying finest; my seared scallops with maple glazed pork belly was a winning combination of sensuous flavors accented by baby bok choy and shiitakes and a brilliant sour apple salad; and my taste of the beautiful vegetarian tagine of butternut squash, couscous, apricots and nuts seemed custom-made for Blake's sophisticated vegetarian palate. the dishes were beautifully presented and were simply brilliant! 

the desserts are all made in-house: the flan was sublimely delicious, the pumpkin cheesecake with rum caramel sauce was comforting without being heavy, and the banofee tart of perfectly ripe banana coins, dulce de leche, and whipped cream was decadent. 

lansdowne is lucky to have such a place and i highly recommend sycamore...they have a lovely menu planned for new year's eve hint, hint!

First, I have to say how much we love this place and that we really enjoy food here! Especially the Lemongrass wings as well as the Chocolate Tart with Condensed Milk ice cream! Oh, their ribeye (pho), great quality!

We had quite an experience last week at this place. We ordered the Wok Fried Ramen and it came out the way we did not expected. Needless to say, the dish was a little too small and messy to eat, and it was a little pricey for an entree. (See my last updated review). We expressed how we felt last week to the Manager/owner (Jeff) and he was handling it professionally.

Anyhow, we got a response from the same manager/owner few days later through here.  He stated that he tried the dish himself and felt the same way we did. He also mentioned that him and the head chef were trying to improve this dish. Therefore, he would like to invite us back for a try again.  So we went tonight......

The dish was such a great improvement! They put that as an appetizer now with more reasonable price. Originally, there was a whole crab in this dish and it was too messy to eat. Also, it was a little too spicy to even taste the freshness of the crab. (See original picture posted) However, the new improved version was so much better. They use crabmeat instead of the whole crab and it's less spicy which brings out the flavor and freshness of the crabmeat. I love it and will order it again next time!

I have to say that our experience this time was so much better, and the fact that they would take such constructive criticism to continuously improve themselves has truly led this place to succeed. During this visit, our server was so friendly and appreciative for us to give a second try.  I am truly impressed!  This is my regular restaurant now! 

By the way, next time you go there, try their roasted Brussel sprouts appetizer. It is so crispy and perfectly seasoned. The dipping sauce for this dish is a winner!  It reminds me of eating fried calamari! Who says that vegetables can't be delicious?!

PROS: TACOS AL PASTOR (pork and pineapple)! I order this for delivery ALL THE TIIIIIME! it's so delicious. I was skeptical at first because I wasn't sure what fruit and meat mix would be like, but it's the perfect balance and combination of flavors. mmMMMM. Also, I ask for their spicy green and orange sauce and it is just perfection. Delivery is fast too, about 45 min considering the distance. Very pleased and will always order from here for my taco craving.

After reading all the great reviews on Yelp about Jack's, I knew I had to pay it a visit on my trip to Tennessee.

{Ambiance} Laid back. Lots of pictures of celebrities who ate here on the walls. 

{Service} The set up is cafeteria style. When you enter the restaurant, place your order with an employee behind the counter. They were kind and quick. Once your plate is set, pay the cashier at the end of the line and seat yourself. There are plenty of seats on the main floor and upstairs. Silverware, straws, BBQ sauces, and drinks are within your reach on BOTH floors. Paper towels are available on each table (love it!). 

{Food}

Combo Plate (any 3 meats)- We chose Beef Brisket, Pork Shoulder, and St. Louis Style Pork Ribs. After taking my first bite, I noticed that the food was not all that warm. It wasn't cold, but it would have been nice if it was warmer. The Beef Brisket was not bad, but it was a bit tough in some areas and lacked flavor. The Pork Shoulder and Ribs were a bit more flavorful but still tough. None of the meats were juicy or tender. 

The Combo Plate also comes with your choice of 2 sides and corn bread. We chose Potato Salad and Apples. The Potato Salad was tasty but very watery. The Apples were amazing. They were warm, aromatic, and cooked with loads of cinnamon and sugar. Yum! This was probably my favorite dish on the plate. The corn bread was delicious too. It was fluffy and not too sweet. 

Beef Brisket Plate- Once again, the brisket was not bad, but it was a bit lacking in flavor and wasn't as juicy as some of the other briskets I have had in the past. This plate also comes with 2 sides and corn bread. The sides we chose were Baked Beans and Mac & Cheese. They were both warm, packed with flavor, and prepared well. 

There are 3 sauces available for your meats (ie. Tennessee "Original" -Tangy Vinegar, Texas Sweet Hot -Tomato Base, and Kansas City Mild- Sweet & Smoky). They were mouth watering and had the perfect consistency. Pouring any one of these sauces on top of your meat will definitely add a lot of flavor. I would have still liked the meat to be flavorful on its own and without all the sauce. 

Note: They charge 25 cents for water cups. 

{Price} Combo Plate $13.99, Beef Brisket Plate $9.82

Four stars on Yelp and a long line has got to mean this place is off the chain right? The BBQ at Jack's is good, but I wouldn't say I'm a fan and that I would come here time and time again.

Came here Christmas Eve.

There are a few parking spots in front of the restaurant, it is a bit tight. There was a short line outside the restaurant when we arrived, which continued to grow as we were eating. The cashier was quick and friendly. We met the owner, who is just the sweetest and so down to earth. Indoor and outdoor seating is available. There is some counter seating as well. 

The food came out fresh and in no time. Everything we tried was delicious. Packed with flavor and the price is right. My favorite tacos were the Fish, Pulled Pork, and Fried Avocado. There is a spicy green sauce bottle near the cashier that is delicious, definitely try it out if you want to add a spicy kick to your tacos. The Elote (grilled corn w/ cheese and spices) and Sweet Plantains are amazing. The prices are reasonable.

You will leave happy and full. Oh yea, and Guy Fieri was here :D

Yum yum in my tum tum...

Came here on a Friday at 2:30 pm and there was a long line. You know a place is good when there is a line out the door. 

Indoor and outdoor seating available. It's a bit of a squeeze in here especially because it's so crowded. Restrooms are available to your right upon entering. The menu is straightforward and displayed on the wall behind the cashier. 

Ordered the Mild Small White Chicken Plate. It comes with 2 sides, tried the Pimento Mac and Cheese and Baked Beans. Your chicken is placed on top of a slice of bread and then topped with pickles. The Mild had a light kick to it. It was seasoned well. The skin was so crispy and the meat was incredibly juicy. Portions are generous here. The sides we chose were delicious and prepared well. Especially the Pimento Mac and Cheese. They also have Ranch or Blue Cheese dipping sauces. You have to ask for it. They taste homemade, the ranch was my favorite.

Employees are really sweet, funny, and friendly. I definitely recommend this place if you're in the mood for southern fried chicken or hot chicken.

Whenever I'm in Philadelphia, the highlight of my trip is a visit to Geno's. I have not tried Pat's yet (across the street). The line for both of these places are always long, so for some reason or another (Oooo look at the pretty lights) I've just always stood in front of Geno's. 

I remember the first time I bit into of one of their cheesesteaks. I took a good look at it and was very confused. It looked nothing like what I had been eating for my 26 years? It didn't taste like it either? So WAIT, is this how a Cheesesteak is supposed to taste like? Because this tastes so different and good!

{Bread} Light, fluffy, and fresh. Holds the meat, cheese whiz, and onions in place.
{Meat} Not greasy. Not salty or over seasoned. Thinly sliced. Juicy. Though, I wish they put MORE slices in there.
{Cheese Whiz} Oh so cheesy. A bit salty. Holds the sandwich in place.
{Diced onions} Bits of chopped sauteed onions complete this sandwich. 

It's simple. Everything on the sandwich seems to highlight one thing- THE MEAT. Compared to the "Philly Cheesesteaks" I've had in the past, this was lighter and flavorful. One could have eaten 2 of these with ease. Yes, its pricey. But since I only come here once in a blue moon, I guess I'm willing to fork out some cash for an authentic Philly Cheesesteak.

Now I've got to try Pat's...

Hot diggity dog.

Cute hot dog joint. Love the laid back ambiance and decor. The cashier was friendly and quick. Once you've placed your order, there will be a number on your receipt. Another employee will call out your number and bring the food over to your table. She was very sweet as well. 

Restrooms are in the back. Plenty of seating is available but I can see this place getting super packed on certain nights. The hot dogs are well prepared. The bun is soft yet holds everything together. Quality ingredients are used for their toppings and we enjoyed our choices. They have a lot of different types of hot dogs, which is fun and unique. They even make their own chips which comes in three different flavors (plain, salt & vinegar, and buffalo).

I'm glad we dropped by.

They're biscuits. How good can biscuits really get?

{Ambiance} Homey. Laid back. Loads of celebrity pictures on the walls. We arrived at around 9 am on Wednesday and there was no wait. By 10 am there was a bit of a wait. Not a huge line though. I believe you are given a buzzer if you have to wait for a table, so you can browse around the gift shop to kill some time.

{Service} The moment we entered the doors, the hostess was welcoming and friendly. Our server Dee was attentive, offered suggestions, and was more than helpful. She brought us extra napkins, our water cups were always full, and she made sure we had plenty of biscuits throughout our meal. 

{Food} 

*A bowl of butter and half & half sits on each table. How convenient. 

Complimentary Homemade Biscuits and Preserves- The most memorable biscuits ever! Warm, light, fluffy, and slightly buttery. They weren't extremely buttery or salty like some of the others I have had in the past. Three types of preserves come with your plate of biscuits: Peach, Blackberry, and Strawberry. The biscuits are delicious on their own but the preserves are so well made, you will want to buy a jar of it to take home. Two simple ingredients go into their preserves, sugar and fruit. 

Southern Sampler Breakfast - Includes Country Ham, Bacon, Sausage and Eggs. All Breakfast Platters come with your choice of grits or potatoes. The Ham was flavorful but really tough. You will be chewing for a very long time. The red eye gravy was flavorful. The bacon was savory, crispy, and slightly salty. The sausage patties were warm, tender, and seasoned well. The eggs were cooked perfectly, just the way I ordered them- sunny side up. The grits were warm and comforting but a bit too watery for me. 

French Toast- Hearty slices of Texas toast with loads of cinnamon and sugar. It comes with syrup, but they were delicious on their own. 

Hashbrown Casserole- Potatoes + Cheese = winner

{Price Range} Breakfast Plates/Platters $6.95-$13.50, Supper Platters $9.95-$16.95

When thinking about the biscuits at Loveless Cafe, words such as "amazing" and "mind blowing" come to mind.

Delicious Coffee. Done.
Jeni's Splendid Ice Cream. Yes.
Las Paletas. Got it.
Quality goods. Yup.

4 stars just for that! We were in the area and it was a chilly day. Looking to warm up a bit, we came across Hot & Cold. Very cute coffee shop. Love the local art work on the walls. As the store is named, this place offers Hot beverages and Cold desserts. How lucky is Nashville to have this place?! My favorite ice cream and paletas under one roof. 

Employees are friendly and quick. Store is neat and organized. Napkins, honey, sugar, lids, and coffee stirrers are on a side table. I ordered the Mocha and it had a deep flavor. B got the Hot Chocolate and absolutely loved it. It comes with your choice of a homemade marshmallow. The marshmallows are from The Bang Candy Company. Another plus! Their marshmallows are excellent. 

I love that Hot and Cold brings some of the tastiest local treats under one roof.

I heart Fido.

If only there was one closer to me. I'd be a regular. I'm thankful that they have free parking behind their restaurant! Line up and place your order with the cashier. As you're standing in line, you will see a plethora of delicious baked goods calling your name. Once you've placed your order, you will be given a table card with a picture of a dog on it. Love the attention to detail. 

I appreciate that they display local artwork on the walls. They can be purchased. Employees are quick and friendly. Our food came out in no time. The dishes looked delicious. Everything we tried was seasoned well, not oily and light. The price is reasonable for the quality ingredients used in their dishes. They use organic and local ingredients. Their Local Burger is delicious, the bun held everything together and the meat was juicy and flavorful. The Pink Radio Cake was very cool. A cake made with beets! Surprisingly, you can't taste the beets. I love that no artificial color was used. 

Can't wait to come back!

Pastrami!

Located inside the Reading Terminal Market, this place makes a mean sandwich. Employees are friendly and quick. Our order was neatly wrapped. Seating can be difficult to find on weekends but eventually a spot opened up. Tried the Famous Reuben with Pastrami. Comes with your choice of bread, cole slaw, Russian dressing, and Swiss cheese. One sandwich can definitely be shared between two people, they are generous with the portions. The pastrami was melt in your mouth good. So flavorful and tender. Everything in this sandwich came together so well. 

Highly recommend paying Hershel's a visit.

Smooth. Creamy. Not too sweet. Packed with flavor.

Yes, this place is legit. The store is adorable. Loving the decor. Indoor and outdoor seating is available. The lady who helped us was friendly, quick, and helpful. Parking can be a bit difficult to find depending on what time you come. There is a lot nearby but you have to pay. We found street parking in a neighborhood nearby that was free.

The selection is nice. There isn't a big variety of flavors, but what they offer is incredibly tasty. Quality ingredients are definitely used. Some of my favorites were Coconut, Strawberry, and Dark Chocolate. A small cup can hold up to 3 flavors.

Cute gelato spot.

Why are your Popsicles so good? I'm addicted to them.

Are you happy now?

With so many flavor options to choose from (ie. Avocado, Pumpkin, Banana w/ Chocolate Chips, Green Tea, Rice, Hot Chocolate w/ Chili, Lime, Grapefruit, Plum, Cantaloupe, Pineapple Blackberry, Chocolate Strawberry, Hibiscus, Cucumber w/ Chili, etc). There is something here for everyone. 

The shop is small. There is a small bench outside and inside the store. I'm not sure if there is a parking lot near by, but there were a few spots available along the street near the store. The ladies behind the counter (I believe one of them was the owner) are friendly and quick. Mexican Caramel was not listed on the menu board that day, but when I asked for it, the kind lady told me she'd go in the back and grab me one. How sweet. 

We decided to try the Mexican Caramel, Pineapple Blackberry, and Cantaloupe. The Mexican Caramel was creamy. It tasted like dulce de leche ice cream but much lighter and not as sweet. The Pineapple Blackberry had pieces of pineapple and blackberry seeds in it. The Cantaloupe was not too sweet and had a lovely fresh cantaloupe flavor. The popsicles here are smooth, light, and refreshing. The flavors are so well blended. They are cool but not too icy. 

At $2.50 per gourmet popsicle, I am more than just a fan of this place. 

The next time I visit Las Paletas, I'm going straight for the Rice Popsicle. One of the employees told me it tastes like rice pudding and has actual pieces of rice in it. What! ::Drool::

In the mood for a light and refreshing treat? Look no further, Las Paletas is where it's at.

A great find.

Fox's Donut Den has a very old time feel. The employee was friendly and helpful. Plenty of seating is available. In addition to donuts, they offer cookies, bagels, muffins, sausage biscuits, coffee, etc. 

We decided to try an Apple Fritter, Old Fashioned Cinnamon Donut and Glazed Donuts. The Cinnamon Donut was on the dryer side but it had loads of cinnamon flavor. The other donuts had a wonderful texture. They were chewy, gooey and sweet. Very fresh and a good size. Total for the 5 donuts and Apple Fritter was about $6.30, not bad.

Recommended for any donut lover.

Jennie M and I headed over to The Marc optimistic that they may be open on Remembrance Day... We wandered inside only to learn that they were not open for lunch.  But they were going to be open for dinner that night!

So, we headed elsewhere for lunch but ventured back later that night (post elite-event).  Our party had grown into to three and we called ahead to make sure they could accommodate us.  Luckily, the answer was yes!  We strolled in around 9pm and were greeted warmly by the staff.  

As I'd noted earlier, The Marc is one large open room, but it's tastefully decorated and has a cozy feeling to it.  The dinner menu is limited, but there's likely something for everyone on it...

We started out with some olives to munch on in addition to some fresh bread...
It did take awhile to order and get our food, but it was well worth the wait, and we weren't in a rush.  I had Manhattan Clam Chowder and a Caesar Salad and cleaned both my bowl and my plate!  I also did some damage to the side of frites we ordered for the table. My dining companions seemed to enjoy their meals as well... 

Needless to say, I think we were all pretty full after our meals, but our waitress talked us into sharing dessert - a chocolate turtle pie of sorts that was the perfect sweet ending to a wonderful day!  The Marc is definitely a dining experience to remember and visit again in the future.

Thank you Sue, aka our "Asian Goddess" server extraordinaire for going above and beyond to take such amazing care of our group tonight!  Your fun enthusiasm and vibrant personality really added to the experience for all of us!  It's also worth mentioning how accommodating you were to the one in our group with dietary restrictions.  

But enough about Sue... the real hit of the evening was the five star worthy food!  I gave up on taking pictures after only a few, but my fellow yelping companions added a bunch.

Seriously, this was some of the best sushi I've had in a really long time.  From one appetizer to the next, to the salads and the rolls, and the sashimi too... so much food and every single bite was amazing.  

The ginger dressing here rocks... go for a salad with ginger dressing over the other salads if you are not sure which to choose.  And a few things not to miss:

-Hamachi Jalapeno
-Crispy Spicy Tuna
-Uni & Fresh Scallop Handroll
-Hawaiian roll (if you like a little kick)
-Tempura Lobster Roll
-Sashimi of any kind

Well, those were my personal favorites, but honestly, I'm sure you can't go wrong here!  There is also a full bar and very moderately priced wine. 
 
If I find myself anywhere near Ybor in the future, I'll definitely be returning to Samurai Blue!

Unfortunately my dining experience was humiliating; for my son. I am the Mother that dined at Muriel's Saturday evening with my husband and son who has brain cancer. Ross has Glioblastoma (Stage 3) Ross is 34 years old. Ross had surgery in September and has been undergoing chemotherapy and Radiation for four months now. His type of ca...ncer is terminal. There is no remission, there is no cure..as of now. Ross has not been able to eat much lately. Food tastes strange to him. Saturday night my husband and I dressed and decided to see if we could coax Ross into dinner. My husband's family have had the same apartment in the French Quarter since the 40's. We now have the apartment. My son lives downstairs in another apartment with his girlfriend. We are very familiar with what is good to eat in and around the Quarter. I had wanted to eat at "Coops" ( Great place, laid back) Ross wanted Muriel's. He wanted the "Midi Salad" and the "Shrimp and Goat cheese Crepe". We headed out and walked to Muriel's. Upon walking in the Hostess was very polite...until she went to seat us. At that point she asked Ross to remove his hat. I told her the situation; Ross's head is scarred up, his is missing clumps of hair and has been very cold, even if it's warm outside he stays cold. She seated our family, and I thought that was the end. Ross went straight to the restroom and was violently ill...again. Ross came back to the table and the waiter approached. He asked Ross to remove his hat. We told him a short version of what was going on. The waiter apologized and never said another word about it.  (I applaud the waiter) . Several minutes after the waiter took our drink order, I noticed the Hostess ( the same one that I spoke to about the hat situation). speaking to the Matre D. She was gesturing to her head and pointed to Ross. The Matre D then proceeded to walk over to our table, place his hand on Ross's shoulder and ask him to remove his hat. (The hat Ross had on was a beanie cap). My husband; Wade then stood up and addressed the situation. We were furious at this point. My husband DID stand up and he DID tell the Matre D what the situation was. The Matre D kept going on and on about the situation with the hat. My husband told the Matre D "To let it the F___go". Under any other circumstances we would have left. But Ross was finally wanting to eat something. We stood our ground. Ross looked at my husband and I and apologized. My step son, my husband's son apologized to US! I wanted to cry. I wanted to cry for every cancer patient, cry because Ross kept apologizing to us. Why..because Ross thought he was embarrassing us. So Muriel's as you remove your posts and your reviews because you do not want to own up to what you did..I hope you too feel shame. Shame for humiliating a former Dean's list LSU student. A member of your community, a man that helped rebuild NOLA post Katrina, a man whom the locals love, a young man that just wanted to eat your salad and crepe. Was the food good? Ross loved it. So I thank you for having something on your menu that he wanted. As for me, I will never recommend your restaurant again. I will tell my friends and family to stick to "Mr. B's" and " The rib room" for an upscale dining experience both places have an awesome wait staff, and the Matre D: Allan is at the 'Rib Room" he is a wonderful compassionate man). and "Coops" for a laid back experience. So delete my post Muriel's....My next step is the Times, and The Gambit.

I have had many wonderful evenings at Bacchanal, which is why I'm so very surprised that I've yet to write a review! The staff is always super helpful with wine and cheese selections, and though I've yet to try food from their kitchen, I've been with groups that have and they had nothing but wonderful things to say about it. The prices on their wines and cheeses are so incredibly reasonable I don't know how they do it! After purchasing your booze you head to the backyard where there are plenty of mismatched tables and chairs to choose from. Every time I've had the pleasure of coming here they had a live band that was playing some killer mood music, torches lit, and lots of seating. They really know how to create a nice atmosphere. There is a cocktail bar if beer and wine aren't your jam, and be sure to bring cash or be prepared to use the ATM if you want something from the kitchen  because the counter you order food from is cash only. But whatever you do, don't pass up on Bacchanal.

The food was good but a little pricey . Our waiter was excellent. The manager is a rude little man. Spent 900.00 on dinner and manager complained we were taking to long. We were there for 3 hours and ate and drank the whole time. I won't take up any space in there dining room ever again.

BYOB. Amazing veal n chicken, cooked to perfection. Pasta was kinda nondescript. Best cannoli I've had in a while (skip the tiramisu). Great napoleon too.
Things are made fresh so order early (w/ antipasto) n take ur time.

Here are some positives to living through a pandemic. Take-out done right. A business that protects their workers and the public (wearing masks and gloves before the Mayor mandated them). 

We've worked hard to support local businesses, and we've had mixed results. Pizza Luna rises to the top on a number of fronts, hence the five-star review with only two visits. Two! 

Both times I ordered over the phone, as we prefer to pay in cash. No problem there, I didn't feel rushed. Accurately took my order and repeated it back to me. The honey went to pick it up.

Both times their pizza bianco. Yum, yum, yum! Just a hint of fresh garlic, the fresh basil is a dream in every bite, a crust that's chewy, not crunchy (it peeves me to no end to get a crunchy crust), hearty but not heavy, and four types of cheese. (fior di latte. trust me, you won't regret it. we also got manchego). We add some mushrooms and voila! An easy and reasonably priced dinner. A small is a good size for the both of us, one time with leftovers (really great cold the next morning) the other time we gobbled it up. 

I'm glad we found a local business that does pizza right. I'm a Manhattan, born-and-bred New Yorker, and a bit of a pizza brat. Enough said.

I love this new fancy pizza spot.

To start with the ambiance is great. The tables and all the woodwork inside is absolutely beautiful. The community tables are pretty cool but I also love the table that can seat six by the window where you can sit in the window seat. Totally fun.

I've been here twice now and both times the food was great. The first time I went with 5 people and we got 3 pizzas and 2 salads. Probably a little overkill, but none of us went hungry! The second time I went with 4 people and we got 2 pizzas and 1 salad and it was perfect.

I'm totally loving both the Arrosto and the Cura pizzas. The Arrosto is amazing with really unique flavors probably brought on by the truffle oil. As far as salads I love both the Butter Pecan which has these big tasty apple slices and the Kale which includes kalamata olives and artichoke hearts,  always favorites.

The service the first time wasn't terrible but it certainly wasn't seamless. The second time about a week and a half later they'd clearly gotten it together. They got us drinks right away, anything on the menu that they didn't currently have they stated as they handed us the menus (nicely) so that we didn't have that in mind to order only to find out we couldn't later.

The owner is so nice. Both times we've been there he's been going around checking on tables and asking about food. He was walking down the sidewalk as we were walking in this time so he walked us in and helped us find a place to sit. He clearly really wants to make this place great and I'm happy to return to it again and again.

Cantina Laredo deserves more than 3.5 stars. I have been here just a few times and have enjoyed each experience. 

Kay X introduced me to Cantina Laredo for a Yelp brunch and it was amazing. They have great omelettes. I had the fajita omelette and I'd recommend it. 

Another experience here was for a Yelp happy hour hosted by Steven B. The specials for happy hour are really good. I had the ahi tuna taco which were 3 for $5. A very good margarita was just $5. Happy hour runs from 4-7. 

Cantina Laredo has a chic decor with reasonable prices for being in Clayton. Service has always been on point and they validate parking tickets for the garage. 

Check out Cantina Laredo if you're looking for a good meal at a fair price in Clayton.

This is my 100th Yelp review and it might as well be a 5 star review as I enjoyed my dinner last night. I went to Sauce on the Side for my first time last night with my mom. This location has only been open a week. They did a nice remodel of the store. There are nice wood floors and the bar has a beautiful marble counter.

Right by the entrance are paper menus rolled up nicely and ordering is done all at the counter (where there is another large menu on the wall behind the bar) and the food is brought to the table. Silverware is wrapped up in linen and stored in a container on the table. The restaurant seems to be staffed very well. Workers were diligently cleaning tables right after customers left as well as greeting people as they came and left. 

We shared all the food we ordered which was the duke calzone and the beet salad. Both were delicious. After we finished the main course, we split the banana and nutella calzone for dessert. Dessert was truly the highlight. I don't know if it's because I generally try to avoid desserts and haven't had sweets in a long time but this calzone was amazing. Highly recommend.

Although we stayed with ice water for a beverage, there looks to be about 50 bottled beers available as wells as about 5 on tap. 

I have a feeling this place will do well with the Clayton lunch crowd. I am glad they opened a location in my hood.

This is by far the finest restaurant I've ever experienced in the entire Tampa Bay Area. In fact, the entire Southeast Region of our country!

I'm not sure where to start...

There is nothing stuffy and overbearing about Rocca. It is comfortable but elegant in a casual sort of way. Anyone would feel welcome here from a layman to the most elite businesspeople. It is a testament to well-trained staff that they can treat everyone respectfully and with a kind and welcoming manner. 

Backtrack - complimentary valet so there's no going crazy with the anxiety of finding a space in the parking lot at Armature Works parking lot, by the way!

Moving on...we ordered almost every single appetizer now in our 2 visits. Yes, I waited to write because it was hard to imagine that the perfection was truly real after one visit so I wanted to make sure I wasn't imagining it and went back. Yes. It's true. Perfection can be found in Tampa and it's at Rocca!

Apps: the beet and ricotta dish is mouth-watering with the balance of flavors and acidity enough to make you want to stop there - but don't! Lordy, don't stop there! The mozzarella cart is a standout and we were in heaven with the heirloom tomatoes tasting like they'd been picked out back just for us!

We really all wanted to try the pastas the first time so we passed on proteins and made up for it the second visit. I'm a big fan of the gnudi. Big. Fan. 
Our friends are like us so we shared it all - can't go wrong with friends like that. Each and every pasta and protein was better than the last - the huge ravioli piece with egg and ricotta inside is delicious and so cool! 

I can't remember all the names of the dishes and some elements changed from the first visit to the second which I found amazing - Chef Bonsack is constantly reworking what is already excellent but he is such a perfectionist and anyone would be  lucky to have this experience! 

Wow! I could do a commercial...I just need a menu to have the correct names! Just know you can't go wrong with ANY choice. That's never happened before - truly a remarkable dining experience. 

Just go!!

I have been coming to Queen of Sheba for years for dinner and have always enjoyed the Queens Eight Platter. What a fun way to sit with friends or on a date and enjoy great food in a very fun way!

The Queen's Eight: It is $15 per person and is a sampling of different types of chicken and beef dishes along with yellow and red lentils and some vegetable dishes. It is served with Injera, which is hard to describe but comes rolled up and you unroll it and tear off a piece that is thin and spongy made from the world's smallest grain! It is used in place of utensils to dip in the various meats and veggies to pick up and eat, but if you're a purist and won't join in, they will bring you a separate plate and fork so you don't have to share and they never blink an eye. I'm sure many people do that!

Many people also assume Ethiopian food is spicy and they couldn't be more wrong. There is nothing spicy at all about it. In fact, there is something very home-cooked and like comfort food about Ethiopian cooking. When I'm having a bad day I could always use meatloaf and mashed potatoes or Ethiopian food. Seriously! It gives you that same feeling. The restaurant does also, since it is calm inside and for some reason people seem to keep a low voice. Why? I often wonder, but I do the same thing! Huh.

This last trip my daughter and I went for lunch and guess what I found out?? All of the food on the Queens Eight platter are offered on a lunchtime buffet that is only $9.95 per person! Yippee!! We certainly got our monies worth and I learned that I can get my favorite food almost all day!

Queen of Sheba offers African wine, which is delicious!

Even though there are currently 11 other locations in the New Orleans Metropolitan Area, the one at the French Market is the original since it was established back in 1862. 

This place is a major tourist attraction; as whenever you mention to people that you're going to New Orleans, they will recommend Café Du Monde. If you want to avoid Bourbon St. with all of the alcohol & gorging on fried food, but prefer to enjoy a cafe au lait & a beignet instead by experiencing the atmosphere of the French Market & Jackson Square, then this place is for you!

Since Café du Monde is a tourist attraction, this place is always crowded. They are open 24 hours a day, so you have the flexibility to avoid their peak hours & weekend crowds. They are closed on Christmas Day, or whenever there's a threat of a hurricane. 

I really liked Café du Monde, but maybe with all the hype, it took away some of the luster of this place; but I still highly recommend making a trip down here if you're already down in New Orleans. Café du Monde is a gorgeous place to be at on a nice comfortable late evening in the French Market.

Smiling with hope pizza is located in a strip mall off lakeside dr. This used to be another pizza place , but i cannot remember the name.
Smiling with hope pizza is special. There mission statement is as follows, To create hope and meaning in the lives of people with disabilities. For a business to put love before the mighty buck is awesome.
I am disabled, not mentally but physically. I like to think of myself as normal, but I am constantly reminded of my disability by the stares and difficulties both my wife and I struggle to have a "normal" day.
When I heard of this pizza place that employees special needs kids, it made me smile. Life is difficult for them, and the disabled and special needs kids are looked at like a second class, not able to work, not able to think,, they might embarrass themselves or you. 
When I entered the restaurant, I saw true love, felt true love. There were smiles everywhere, laughing, and kids that loved good pizza.
The pizza is true ny style, thin crust. It was cooked just right. I ordered the pepperoni pizza. The pepperoni had a little spice, and curled up when cooked. It was not paper thin slices, but somewhat thick slices. The mozzarella cheese was fantastic. I do not know if it was freshly grated, but it sure packed alot of flavor.
There hours are kind of weird, so just make sure they are open when you go. 
I definitely will be back!

Jasmine is located in South Reno on Double R Blvd.
They are located in a business/residential area.
Parking was no problem with plenty of spaces available.
The lunch crowd was a mix of workers, businessmen in ties, and  some families.
This is a higher end Chinese,Thai and Sushi restaurant, with the waiters in ties and the decor and presentation lending itself to high end.
The one thing that was not high end was the pricing. Very competitive to other Chinese restaurants.
My wife and I started out with spring rolls, then moved on to hot and sour soup and last but not least, Jasmine Chow mein.
The spring rolls were delicious, packed full of flavor.
They make there own rolls, fry them and serve them with homemade sweet and sour sauce.
The hot and sour soup was good in flavor, not to spicy but a little gelatinous for me.
The chow mein was fantastic. It came with beef ,chicken, shrimp, tofu, water chestnuts and yummy fresh noodles.
Getting back to the presentation, the chopsticks were not wood stuffed in a bag, but we're plastic and resting on a holder on the table. Nice touch.
Service was excellent.
If in the area we will be back.

Blaze was represented at the NOLA Yelp Krewe de Vieuxing party on 1/23/16 and I was lucky enough to get a coupon...once the parade was over the children wanted to try it out because of the coupon...I was game so we headed on over...

Walked in and they had a number of patrons but we were able to order immediately...went with a Meat Lover's and another that was half White Top and half pepperoni and black olive...

After placing the order the pizzas came out PDQ (pretty damn quick)...I'm personally a huge fan of thin crust and found these pizza crusts to be very good...

My drawback with this place is the fact that they are real light on the toppings...The daughter loved her White Top and I tried a bite and have to tell you that was a very tasty pizza and I'm in no way a fan of white pizza...the son liked his but wasn't blown away and I agree with the son's assessment...

However it did the job for a reasonable price and I'd recommend the place to anybody craving pizza and wanting a quick sit down meal...

Had this location bookmarked and figured since had the kids with me in NOLA we'd give it a try... kids love pizza...

Found it easy on St. Charles, parking was a breeze, found street parking right in front of St. Charles Tavern... when we walked in about 6ish on a Saturday just a couple of people at the bar but we were the only diners..

Lotta pizza for the price.... me and the boy split a medium Meat Lovers and it was plenty for a 16 year old boy with me, the Dad, not having to worry if he was gonna plow through the whole thing.... the baby girl wanted to try white pizza and I was happy that any pizza was offered by the slice... she went with a white slice with bacon and fresh basil and really loved it...

However, in my humble opinion, the kids really loved the Garlic Bread with Red Gravy appetizer...I was lucky to get one piece of that garlic bread! 

Our waitress, didn't get her name but she has 2 6-shooters tattooed on her upper chest, was excellent, friendly and timely... plus the Leinenkugel Summer Shandy they were offering on tap hit the spot! 

All in all one helluva enjoyable stop and meal and brought it in for a damn reasonable price!

Ordered takeout during these quarantine times.
My girlfriend and I ordered a pizza cheese steak and the wing platter (with two sides of potato salad and garlic parm fries). The cheese steak quality was amazing and fresh. The wing platter came with 2 more wings than advertised and really enjoyed the potato salad/fries as well. The owners are very nice and even added a free piece of cake because I used the ATM to take out cash. Great first visit and will be back!

Oddly enough, the older I get the less I like cream in my coffee.  Sugar or anything sweet was nixed a long time ago.  However, just because I like black coffee doesn't mean all black coffee is created the same.  If you try a pour over from Slow By Slow, you will see what I mean.  I recommend the Uganda, it's amazing!

Hi Greg (the owner),

I hope you had a better evening than my mother, boyfriend, and I had at your restaurant. We were enjoying our second round of drinks and awaiting dessert after a delicious meal when you rudely interrupted us. You offered no courtesies such as 'hello' or 'how is your meal?'. Instead, you proceeded to tell us that you needed to flip the table so that the restaurant could serve more patrons because your wait staff needs tips to pay rent. When my mother informed you that we were not done our meal, you essentially repeated yourself verbatim. 

Greg, here are a few things to consider. Firstly, if you are so concerned about your waitstaff's ability to pay rent, how about you pay them a living wage? That way you don't need to harass paying costumers that up until your tactless intervention were enjoying their evening. 

How long have you worked in the restaurant industry? If I had to guess, I'd say less than a day because you have no clue how to speak to costumers. That's a shame because the food and staff (shoutout to our server Jeff, who rocks) are pretty cool. Since it's your first day on the job, I am happy to give you free advice, no tip required. Harassing and guilting customers into giving up a table before their meal is over is not a good idea. I know, I know. That's intuitive for most people. But occasionally people forget. I hope you don't.

Like they need one more great review, huh? 

For the last 10 years, my Belfast born husband has only wanted sausage rolls.  

MacNivens caught his eye and we finally got in there today.

Super cool vibe and a good "pub" feel.  A lower ceiling and a roaring fire would make it a true, cozy, public house.  

We started with the Scotch Egg.  It was my first Scotch Egg and I loved it.  Pip said they "nailed it!"  It tasted great without the accompanying spicy mayo.  Turns out, this aioli is pretty tasty with the fries, so hang onto it.

I got the Angus Burger, which is different - but delicious.  I can only describe it as a "giant meat crepe."  It arrives covering your entire plate and you get to fold it up, which results in many tasty burger layers.  I enjoyed the interactive part of folding it.  I added sauteed mushrooms and bacon to mine, but let them keep the cheese.  

Pip ordered the sausage rolls (2) w/ beans and chips.  He was in sausage roll heaven.  It met his needs, saying it was 98% right on.  The taste was a hit.  A little less pastry and looser sausage crumble and the texture would have been spot on.

When we got there, one of their desserts caught my eye, but I couldn't make it through my huge burger and load of fries.  Next time, I'll plan accordingly.  

Our server was a cute hipster in skinny jeans.  He took great care of us.

I can't wait to go back!

We have been here numerous times and always loved it. Today was very very different!!!!!! We were rushed through our brunch by our waitress. She kept asking if we were done. We had a couple cocktails and we're actually still eating when we were asked to move so they could seat another table!!! WTF!! ?? We were there a total of 40min that includes ordering and waiting for food. If I wanted a fast food place I would have went to one. They were obviously understaffed, so their poor judgment became our problem!!! Not cool!! Then I got up and gave the waitress my card to pay and she continued what she was doing?! I told her "now I'm in a hurry". Don't make me wait after you ask me to leave..  Listen there are alot of places to eat in Reno.. and we will be going elsewhere for a long long time... F@#@**CK this place!

I thought that the owners of the Korean run Oishi could bring a good Korean restaurant to the area.  The bulgogi I had was decent, a bit steep at $26.  The beef had a good spice, not too overpowering, and the gochuchang dipping was good too.

the banchans i got with the bulgogi looked like stuff you can buy from the freezer of H-Mart- they were shrimp shumai, pot stickers and a cold tamago omlette.  what the heck? No kim-chee or vegetable banchans to go with the $26 entree?  guess my hope that a real korean place coming to town was squashed pretty quickly.

My wife got the ramen.  Ok, not korean, but it's here.  and it's awful.  I had no expectation of it tasting like Ippudo in NY or even the new ramen joints in philly, but come on.  The noodles were "oodles of noodles", the broth totally salty-but-bland and tasted like it came from a ramen package.  bean sprouts and pork thrown on top of a 50 cent ramen package, just like I made after coming home from school.

On a positive note, The korean fried chicken with yuzu shio flavor was also bland, no yuzu flavor found, however the chicken itself was very crispy. the service was good and the atmosphere is nice.

Overall, I'm sure this will be a hit with people who like oishi (dumbed down mediocre expensive "japanese" food in a swanky atmosphere), but for people who want non-bland, real korean food can look elsewhere.  I think in the general area, Mirim near the oxford valley mall has the food at this place beat significantly.

Gave this place a try after reading a lot of reviewers praising this as the best Indian place in Nashville. I loved the cozy, mom and pop shop feel and the service was really great but that's about as far as the positives go...

So I ordered the dinner combo that came with an assortment of charcoal fired meats like chicken tandoori, chicken tikka, seekh kabob, and shrimp. It also came with a side of soup, naan bread, and rice. Pretty awesome deal for $16. All the meats were nice and juicy but I felt like I could've eaten this at any restaurant - the marinade was lacking and didn't have that spicy, savory flavor that's unique to Indian cuisine. So I asked for a side of their curry sauce to spice things up but that was also disappointing bc it was like a thick paste. And lo and behold I later found a piece of rubber inside my naan... GOOD LORDT. 

I feel bad for leaving a poor review for a local business and I'm sure they have other solid meals on the menu. Tbh the rubber situation wasn't that big of a deal to me, it was the lack of authenticity in the flavors that makes me hesitant on coming back again :-/

Everyone who visits Nashville is told to go to S&H because it is THE best BYO pizza place in the city. I love this place even more because the owners are known to give back to the community by employing neighborhood residents, giving complimentary pizza and cinnamon rolls to students who meet their reading goals, starting eco-friendly initiatives, etc. THIS PLACE IS TOO PURE FOR THIS WORLD T_T

Anyway, the name of this place refers to the size of your pizza: slim is 10" ($10) and a husky is 16" ($14) which is served like a flatbread. I got the husky and was able to finish it on my own without feeling too full mainly because the dough is really thin and obv because it was SO GOOD. Try out their unique selection of protein toppings like salmon, shrimp and philly steak!!!

I heard the white sauce is to die for so I'll be coming back for that :D

California has In N Out, New York has Shake Shack, and here in the south, we have COOK OUT. This North Carolina based fast food chain developed a massive cult following for its OUTRAGEOUSLY CHEAP prices for good quality char grilled burgers, bbq and milkshakes (40+ flavors!!!) 

I got the Cook Out Tray which includes a burger, 2 sides and a large drink. ALL FOR 5 BUCKS. I got the spicy chicken burger, slaw and hushpuppies which are fried cornbread balls and WOW they were so good, prob the best part of my meal. It's sweet and soft like mozzarella cheese.

I was still hungry and went back to get a 6 piece chicken nuggets and fries LOL. I didn't really like the nuggets but can't expect much from a $1 meal. So in total I spent $7 on two meals. And a thousand calories. What a time to be alive.

I love this place. I drove 30 minutes just to come here, the bread is amazing and it was my husbands birthday so I thought it would be the perfect place to get a last minute desert. Cheese cake is his favorite. I bought a whole one and brought it home adding some strawberries and chocolate sauce. The kids ate first, and everything on their plate. I served up mine and spotted the mold. Upon further investigation I saw the bottom was covered in mold and also a date sticker.. for October 4th! (This was on October 20th). I brought the cake back in (an hour round trip drive) and quietly told the lady at the register. She was very apologetic but didn't seem to know what to do so I asked who was in charge. The lady she called over told me that wasn't possible (really?! I'm standing here holding a moldy cake with a date on it?!) . Finally someone else was called over and I was given a refund along with a bunch of excuses.  I'm very disappointed to say that I don't think I could bring myself to go back here again..  yelping another bakery now.

I have been a customer here for several years. As a mother with small children I have always been grateful that they deliver to my house. Last week my youngest was home sick all day so I was unable to go grocery shopping.. No worries! Our lovely local pizza place to the rescue! No. They told me that they don't deliver any more than 8 miles out and haven't since October last year. (I've had several deliveries since then and nobody ever told me that they won't be able to delivery out here anymore). I was then given the phone to the "boss" and I pleaded my case. Surely they could deliver this one last time?! I was told "that's the way it is" , according to their system I am 8.01 miles away (I did it on maps from my location and it told me 7.9 miles). We had crackers  and peanut butter for dinner. It's a shame, I would have still gone regularly for pizza night with the kids but I can't spend my money somewhere that does not value their customers. Very disappointing.

**** edit update****
Although it doesn't change my experience that evening I did receive an honest message from them following up...


Rachael Mae Day
Hello Mercedes. The night of your call, Jody took it upon himself, after work, to drive and clock the mileage to your house, considering phones and electronics aren't always correct. We are sorry for any inconvenience. We were wrong about mileage, and you shouldn't have further problems ordering, if you choose. Thank you for your support.
Wednesday at 11:03am · Sent from Messenger

I'm a born in Philly resident of over 3 decades and not once had I tried a cheesesteak from Max's. What's wrong with me?!? Anyway, I ordered a chicken cheesesteak, my friend got a cheesesteak.  Each cost about $8.75. We also ordered a smooth bitch (mixed fruit, slushy, pink drink) I thought was too strong but I guess as it melted it watered it down. It was pretty good.

My friend said her cheesesteak was good. I'm going to say my chicken cheesesteak was bangin! So far the best "chicken" cheesesteak I've eaten. Mayo, fried onions, salt and pepper with provolone cheese.

There was no long wait. I came around 4pm on a Tuesday. We ate in the restaurant/bar. There's a jukebox and I could tell there were some 80's and 90' hiphop heads. Cool place for afterwork, but no happy hour specials until 5.

Steve's hot dogs in tower grove has so many great aspects. Obviously the hot dog combos are great. Naturally, I ordered the hawaiian style dog because bacon, pineapple and bbq sauce. 

Right next door to Steve's is a retro bar called Tick Tock Tavern where you can get an adult beverage to pair with your dog. The two establishments are totally friendly with each other so feel free to bring your dog to the bar or your drink to the dogshop.

If you're hungry on a Sunday, head down for hot dog brunch! Only $15 gets you all you can eat dogs and mac n cheese. There is chili to smother your puppy too if you're in the mood.  For the brunch they have live acoustic sets from local acts such as Bruiser Queen, Music Embryo and Steve Ewing, himself! Its a great way to spend a day. 

This street corner just east of Grand blvd has a great vibe and good eats. Go check it out!

Right across the street from the Ocean, 1 block away from the coolest park ever, and kitty corner cross the street from the Pier, we decided to stop here for a late lunch after playing at the park. 

We stopped in apparently at the change of shift around 2:30pm, we were seated at the front window with an ocean view, before the late afternoon lunch rush began...... I noticed that people that arrived after us were having their orders taken and served their meals before our server ever arrived to take our order. 

Finally Cindy our server arrived and when I mentioned we have been waiting 20 minutes and people were being served and eating who arrived after us she said it was the change of shift and asked if we needed a few more minutes to decide..... Decide? on what? going to another restaurant?
