We ordered the fried calamari (excellent) and fresh red snapper cevechi (excellent) as starters, my road trip warrior had a spinach salad that she said was excellent and the toddler and I had bowls of clam chowder with big chunks of clams in a flavorful but watery base, and the best tuna fish sandwich I have ever had. It was to be a tuna melt but I forgo the cheese and they grilled the tuna salad and served it on sourdough toast. I think I want all my tuna fish sandwich's grilled now. 

Service lacked big time but the food was surprisingly awesome, very kid friendly restaurant and accommodating with color crayons and coloring menu. I thought it was reasonably priced for location and food quality. 

I could tell it is a big hit for locals, while we were there the hostess was taking phone calls for reservations non stop.  If I was a local..... It would be a place I would frequent in hopes of better service.

THE WORST SERVICE I HAVE EVER ENCOUNTERED. This is no exaggeration - I've had better service at a McDonalds drive thru. 25 mins for an adult milkshake on a slow day w/o any explanation? I live in the Piazza and have eaten out at pretty much every place in a mile radius, but seriously, waiting over an hour w/o a crowd on a rainy Sunday afternoon w/ no crowd for a cheeseburger? The decor is awesome, great atmosphere, food is very good but I will not step foot back in this place just b/c the place is run by teenagers who must be trust fund babies, think they run the place and believe they are cooler than they are (I've actually met a guy who bartends there at another bar who was very cool so I can't say everyone is a Dbag who works here). I ended up speaking directly to the owner b/c the service was so bad that day and management was run by an immature asst mgr who needs to find another line of work. He ended up telling me his wait staff was still "green" - this after they'd been open a year,and btw dude, telling a patron your staff is green & expecting us to accept that is ridiculous. I'd like to recommend the place and go there again if it wasn't for some of the staff who works there .. esp since its in my backyard. In the meantime, unless you only care about hanging out in the "it" places don't bother unless you want to have the same frustration ... there are plenty of other places around here who care about your patronage.

You know what I like? Really good, unique drinks. 

You know what else? A really cool atmosphere, unlike anything I've found in Tucson until now. 

And, another thing I like? When people remember my name.

Scott & Co delivered all three of these things last night. 

A couple of girlfriends and I decided to get a really, really good drink. They had been to Scott & Co before; I had not. 
I arrived first, and was not worried by the drink menu. Granted, there were words that I had never heard of (not to mention had no clue how to pronounce), but my girls had been there before so I knew they could help me out. 
They arrived, and glanced at the menu only to realize that they had changed their menu. We asked about it, and the friendly (albeit BUSY) mixologist informed us that they changed it for Spring. 

I love seasonal menus. (And I don't blame them for not being able to predict the cold rain of last night when agreeing on the Spring menu). 

We chose our drinks, with some help from said mixologist, and enjoyed the beautiful, dark, exposed brick ambiance while we waited. 

Our drinks came, and mine? Mine was delicious. 

It would be AH-MAZING on a warm day. Even on a cold night, I was in heaven. 

I had chosen "Lolita's Cup," which is vodka, red wine, cucumber syrup (makes it SO refreshing), tonic, and possibly something else that I can't remember. 

It was delish. 

My girlfriends each loved their drinks as well. 

Travis, the owner, came over to meet us, and I love when someone takes the time to remember names. Like, double checked that he had our names correct, and then remembered them (correctly) when he thanked us later, as we were leaving. 

It's a little thing, but it leaves an impression. 

The $8-10 drinks? Worth every penny. Plus, it's a great excuse to go downtown and explore. 

Will I be back? Absolutely. Possibly to check out their Tiki Thursdays, which seems interesting. 

Seriously... go check it out. You won't be sorry!

Definitely agree with all of the other reviews stating this place is overpriced! I wish I had read the reviews before setting foot in their establishment. And another face palm for not looking at the pricing on their menu. That was my two mistakes. 

But for them servicing Thrifty brand ice cream I do believe their pricing is a bit much. Being located on the pier and in Santa Barbara county I don't doubt that their store rent must be expensive. Still, $16 for 3 scoops of ice cream and a few toppings really is a lot when you think of other places that charge significantly less!

If you're willing to pay a premium to enjoy some ice cream with your family on the pier then this is def your place! Just wish it was maybe higher quality ice cream - even dreyers would be a step up from ice cream you can purchase from rite aid and get a whole tub for the same price you pay at their store. 

Just be aware of the pricing when buying from Great Pacific Ice Cream!

A family member order us some meals for our family due to having a newborn and the times of COVID. It was Ordered through Grub hub I believe and everything was seamless, on time and delicious. We ordered the Salmon dinner and the BBQ pork W/ Gouda Mac n cheese family of four dinners. They came with a medium sized salad, pound cake and all the fixings (sauces and dressings) that can come with that. The salmon came with a side of mixed sweet and regular potatoes and some green veggies like broccoli. We ordered it a second time and got asparagus. It was all so good. The Mac n cheese was good, but for me I preferred it without the pork on top that comes as a one pan dish or casserole. Which we got a Mac n cheese family dinner. Y'all it was a full pan of it! My whole family enjoyed the meals and we ate on these foods for a couple days/meals. 

The second time of my delivery, our food was hot and and apparently right out of the oven. As it was a little late. The restaurant and grub hub delivery person both contacted me and adjusted our time accurately by only 20minutes. Not bad at all. 

We also got a side order of the garlic fries which is one of my husbands favorites. We love this place and will continue to recommend. 

Service obviously cannot be counted but just the communication factor is definitely a leg up. I can't wait to return to this establishment. Due to COVID we prefer to remain at home, but luckily this has not stopped us from enjoying their meals. We had Kitchen 519 for a date night during pregnancy. So it's safe to see we will be back. Their tacos are yum! Sorry no pictures. There were way to many people (my household) and too much food to get a solid shot on a whim before everyone dug in. 

The family meals run about $55+ give or take plus any delivery fees and taxes and tip. But it's worth it. I hope to keep this in mind again in the future.

Go and buy buckets of the Parmesan garlic spread. Dip it in breadsticks, crust, on your friends, or on whatever. It is unreal!!!  Cheese Louise is our go-ton pizza here. We love the ricotta on the pizza. Also, this location has the nicest staff. They are so responsive and always check on their costumers. Love this location.

This is a hard review for me.  We decided to have lunch today.  Valet was on point and the staff around the grounds were top notch.  We dined at Malibu Farm.  The food was great.  My cheeseburger was easily in the top 3 I've ever had.  I'm not a fan of Russian dressing so I opted for their lemon aioli & stone-ground mustard.  The burger temperature was exactly how I ordered it and the bun was perfect.  My wife's salad was crisp & flavorful and the other dishes served were great.

So why the 3-star review you ask?  Well, the main reason for our visit was lunch and one would expect the service in the restaurant to match the food quality and overall service of the entire grounds.  I would hold a property of this caliber in higher esteem when it comes to food service at its restaurant.  We were seated for 10 minutes before our server even came and poured water and just asked if we had questions and were "ready to order".  I put that in quotes to highlight the verbiage used.  That's what you ask in Denny's - not here.  I also ordered an iced tea.  It was nothing special but wasn't cheap.  So you might expect that an iced tea served in a 14 oz Collins glass would never be empty.  Well, in actuality, it was never filled again.  Not even when I noticed everyone in our party had empty water glasses and I had to ask for more water.  A place like this should never have an empty water glass.  Also, I would expect dishes to be cleared before a check is dropped.  That's just upper-end dining etiquette.

I'll conclude with this - This property is spectacular and I would expect my 3-star review to be lost in a sea of 5-star reviews in pretty short order.  But I see the manager actually looks at these and that's fantastic.  These growing pains will he worked out.  We will certainly be back but you need to step up your service game in this restaurant.  Thanks for the great burger.

Update: tried Raju gari Goat pulav over the weekend and it brought back memories...finger licking good.

New Best Indian food we have been craving for in Saint Louis metro area. Try the Ulavacharu Biryani...yummy and you won't find it around anywhere :)

This place was one of the stops on the Dine the District food tour today.  We were curious to try as we have never eaten here.   It's a place that specializes in hot dogs but they were serving samples of pizza.  We saw that a fresh pie had just come out and part of it had sausage on it.   My husband asked for a cheese piece and I asked for a piece with the sausage on it, thinking that would be different.   The pizza was cut into squares.  The girl serving apparently thought it would be comical to give me a piece of the sausage pizza that was about an inch wide.   My husband's piece was about 2 inches wide.  I can tell you that we will never step foot into this establishment ever again!   The pizza was mediocre and nothing that I would pay for.

I am so glad that I came back to Winslow's Home yesterday. Still haven't tried their food (which looked FANTASTIC btw) but their wine selection is pretty damn affordable. A bottle of good Merlot for $15? Sold! 

The staff is incredibly nice, too. Arrived around 3:30 to set up for Office Hours and they just let me do my thing until folks arrived at 5. No one bugged me to order food or drink and they didn't even flinch when I started blowing up Yelp balloons right there on-site or when I decorated a table full of Yelp schwag. 

One small issue - I ran a tab for the day and wasn't able to tip the staff on my card! Oh no! So please bring cash to tip these kind folks when you visit. I will be sure to drop by soon and make up for not tipping last night!

Yes, Crown Candy is open on Sundays. Get there before noon and you won't have to wait in line, either. Yes, this means I am encouraging yelpers to skip church AND eat an incredibly unhealthy meal. I am so going to hell for this review...

Anyway, the line was non-existent so we were able to get a booth right away. Service was a tad slow this time around, but once we ordered, food came out within 10 minutes. Damn that's quick! And as always, the bacon was piled high and slathered in Miracle Whip. Mmmm mmmm good. The BF ordered a bacon turkey melt and was able to snag some of my overflowing bacon and add to his sammie. 

For dessert, we indulged in some original Crown Candy ice cream. A giant chocolate shake is probably the best way to wash down several pounds of bacon. The BF downed a double scoop cone. So good! 

Still one of my favorite STL spots (when the line isn't wrapped around the corner) and I love taking out of town guests here.

Hell to the no on this dining establishment! Seriously, E-ville, I expected more from you...

As a former resident of Edwardsville, it's really cool to see all of the new development happening 'round town. It's been several years since I've lived here and the amount of change is monumental. We did not have an Old Navy, Dierbergs, Qdoba or Peel Wood Fire Pizza back in my day... and I'm not *that* old!

With all of the new development, no one mentioned to me that Hwy 159 has been re-routed through town. Seriously? How do you change a major highway like that? And very few of the new businesses mentioned above have claimed their businesses on Google maps, which makes it next to impossible to find them! 

Needless to say, I had a very difficult time finding Peel Wood Fired Pizza last night, and when I called up for directions (twice!), the gal on the phone wasn't very helpful. She was nice, but not helpful. It took me 30 minutes of driving every possible route around town to find this damn place. So I came in here with a bad attitude... I'll give you that.

However, the black cloud over my head (think Grumpy Bear) could have easily been lifted had I received good service or a really great meal. Neither of those things happened. Without going into too much detail, here are my complaints:

1. Dinner salads come piled up on an 11" plate (the same exact plate as the 11" pizzas). Who needs that much salad? And why didn't the server ask me, "Are you really hungry? 'Cause our dinner salads are ginormous." Salad doesn't save well, people, so I had to waste at least 5" of lettuce. And it was a total waste of money, too.

2. I asked for bread and butter since eating that much salad could blow anyone's colon out of this Earth. It cost an additional $1.50 to get bread. Without butter. When I asked for butter, my server told me that they didn't have butter. Say what? You are a restaurant; therefore, you have butter.

3. My Pinot Grigio was watery and tasted cheap. 

4. Our waitress was overwhelmed and you could tell. A good server, no matter how overwhelmed, doesn't show it. Or they get someone else to cover their table. Or a manager pops in to apologize for the crazy night. 

It was a total bummer to drive 45 minutes each way to have such a disappointing meal. I will *not* be coming back anytime soon. But I am interested to try Fond and a few other E-ville spots that have been highly reviewed on Yelp. I'll just make sure to map out my route ahead of time and cross my fingers that it's correct!

Here's my tally for Noble Pie in Midtown:

1-star: For a kitchen open late night on a Wednesday. Lots of tasty eats until the wee hours of the morning.

1-star: Trevor at the bar, he's a gem. Personable, never looks stressed out. Makes a mean cocktail, too.

1-star: Frachos, aka FRENCH FRY NACHOS. Yes, it's a thing and it's served at Noble Pie. I enjoyed the house meatballs as well as some garlic knots. 

1-star: A relatively sophisticated wine selection, considering it's a wing/pizza place open late. I enjoyed a Montepulciano with my meal. Pairs very well with Noble Pie's meatballs.

1-star: Always an interesting crowd. Locals, visitors, even National Geographic Channel stars come through the doors. Great people watching and even better interactions.

If Noble Pie was in Denver, I'd be here a lot more. And I'd likely weigh an additional 20 lbs.

This was the first weekend I've had off since January - no lie! So, of course, Mike T and I wanted to make a weekend of it. One of the first things on my "to do" list was to make a dinner reservation at Brasserie, as I'd read so many great reviews on this newer restaurant. 

I'm a little embarrassed to admit that I used to live across the street from Niche and never actually dined there. It always seemed to fancy and expensive... So I didn't go into Brasserie with any preconceived notions about what a Gerard Craft restaurant should be/taste like. 

Our server was great, very personable. We are pretty sure he is the guy who was featured in the RFT's article about all of the tattooed waiters at Craft's restaurants. Regardless, he did a great job of explaining both the wine menu and our dinner options. 

Unfortunately the bottle of bubbly that we wanted was not available, so we had to upgrade from a $28 to $37 bottle of champagne. Not a big deal, and although it was a Rose, it wasn't especially pink or rosy, which is a good thing. 

I ordered the $30 prixe fixe menu and Mike ordered the short ribs. My salad greens tasted especially fresh and I liked the goat cheese on a cracker served with them. And my coq au vin was amazing! I could eat that all day. Mike said his short ribs were more like pot roast, which is fine. Just not what he expected. 

Also, it was VERY warm in the restaurant, which made eating rich food a little laborious. I'm normally cold in most situations and was sweating inside Brasserie, which is too bad because it was a lovely night outside and they could have easily opened a window and aired out the place. Both of us were pretty uncomfortable and didn't finish our entrees or dessert (which were also very good!) because we wanted some fresh air! 

I would love to go back and give Brasserie another try. Perhaps sitting outside would be better? Again, our food and service were great but the environment kept it from being a 4 or 5-star experience.

You had me at ranch, aka the glue that holds all Midwestern people together. 

When I found out there was a restaurant dedicated to one of my favorite condiments in St. Louis proper, it was bookmarked for a future visit. Heck, you might even say it's what prompted me to book a plane ticket to the Lou. And it was definitely one of the first stops made after getting off the plane.

In addition to the traditional classic ranch dressing, Twisted Ranch offers several different flavors, including sriracha, buffalo and Greek. The latter goes well inside a chicken gyro, that's for sure.

As with most restaurants in this part of the country, portions are quite generous. Two can split one dish and be satisfied. Unlimited refills on your soda, too.

Overall a nice, casual foray into the world of ranch dressing.

OK, it's no secret that I like wine. Red wine. A lot. :) So it surprises and saddens me a little bit to discover Ernesto's right before leaving town. It's so close to my house (tucked away in Benton Park on McNair) and a perfect little happy hour spot. 

Last night they had a $5 happy hour wine special until 7 pm. Hefty pours and hearty wine - that's enough for me to brave the slippery sidewalks on a cold winter evening. In my world, wine and cheese go hand-in-hand and Ernesto's offers a wide variety of plate selections. Their summer sausage is sooo good! 

And after a small bite, why not stick around for dinner? The cheeseburger sliders smelled divine, but I opted for the seafood pasta. The mussels were cooked perfectly - smooth and buttery. The plate was huge and I couldn't eat it all (shocker!) but I enjoyed every bite thoroughly. 

If you're bored with the typical Chad-like happy hour hole, definitely hit up Ernesto's. It's in a cute little 'hood, the drinks are delish and it's a little off the beaten path.

For the record, I would much prefer to spend my time and money at a local restaurant rather than a chain. But there are times where I do crave some Applebee's, Red Robin or P.F. Chang's. I'm not proud of it, but my therapist said I no longer need to feel shame about my choices in life. When I do get a craving for something homogenous, Elephant Bar would NOT be a place that I'd pick again.

After a long day at the West County Mall, both my boyfriend and I decided to grab dinner at Elephant Bar. I'd been there before for happy hour and had their appetizers. Their lettuce wraps and egg rolls are just fine. Nothing special, but for half price during the week, a girl can't be too picky. 

Dinner at Elephant Bar is a whole other story! Per my boyfriend's request, I ordered the Shrimp Adventure. Keep in mind that anything one orders at a chain with the words "Adventure", "Explosion" or "Ultimate Feast", know that the meal turns out to be nothing of the sort! It was basically shrimp battered and fried in three different ways. With some sad looking sweet potato fries on the side. The lamb shanks that my boyfriend ordered were dry and served with a gelatinous gravy. Blech!

Maybe if I had ordered the orange chicken or lettuce wraps, the meal would have gone a little bit better. But we left that night feeling disgusted- both with our food and what we paid for it. A total waste. When deciding on where to eat, we usually joke about going to Elephant Bar because the meal was just so bad.
Anyplace that serves a tiki drink in a ceramic Shamu mug or a hallowed out pineapple is more than OK with me! Sit at the bar, make friends with the cool 'tenders and you're in for a special treat.

Get there early for Saturday brunch and you'll have a fabulous time! 

A few gal pals and I flew into Santa Barbara airport and beelined it for State & Fig for some bonding and brekkie. It was a delightful way to get our vacay going, with bottomless mimosas and countless egg dishes. For $15 you can have the standard OJ mimosas, or for $19 you can get more exotic flavored juices like pomegranate. 

Even though it gets crowded, especially on the patio, our server never looked frazzled nor did he rush us out of our prime patio seat. That's so appreciated, kind sir.

With a slight buzz and a full belly, we departed State & Fig and traveled to Ojai. Not a bad way to start the day. Not bad at all!

Wow. 

I've always loved the Tower Grove/Botanical Heights neighborhood, but Olio makes it that much better. How things have changed in STL over the past 4-5 years! 

From drinks at the bar to a lovely fall dinner on the outside patio, this experience was pretty damn awesome. Bonny Doon rose on special? Yes. Famous egg salad? Uh-huh. Hummus? Mmm - and that's just the starters. Portions are on the smaller side by Midwest standards, but plenty of food for three people to appease their initial cravings.

For the main, I split the Chicken Tagine and it was the most tender meat I've had in awhile. Chef Ben Poremba obviously has spent some time in the Middle East... the menu states that there's "nods" of the region in his cuisine, but I'm going to suggest it's more of a hand raised in the air. 

Dessert in a pie? Skip it. I was imagining a mason jar with fresh crust and fillings, but we got a little cylinder with pudding. Something you could find at Walgreens or a corner store. But that didn't damper the rest of the meal at all. Everyone at the table left happy and full.

Torta Cubana. End of story. 

Just kidding, my story starts with a venture into the Bella Vista area on a Sunday night. I was on searching for something other than Vietnamese food. I stumbled upon a restaurant that I can't imagine pronouncing correctly the first ten tries. I walked in and asked if I could see a menu for take-out and the gentleman, John, sat me at the bar. 

The place is pretty roomy. Nothing fancy here, tables and chairs with Spanish music playing. I asked John for recommendations and he immediately pointed out the Torta Cubana. Before I left, I received a history lesson and learned how to pronounce the restaurant's name; Ees-tah-see-wah. 

This football-sized sandwich is no joke. I unwrapped the foil and was immediately impressed with the presentation. I don't know how they did it but they managed to cram 12 ingredients in between two slices of Bolillo bread. What's more amazing is that each ingredient is layered neatly, and you can see each layer. It looked like a sandwich you would see on TV! Everything about the Torta was excellent. I cannot wait to go back to try the rest of the food at Iztaccihuatl.

HiFalutin is one of my favorite restaurants in Tucson and every time I have dined there, I have never been disappointed. Between the western decor, the friendly service, and the dependably delicious food, HiFalutin is a treasure. 

The restaurant has a theme and it's western steakhouse and the decorations are thorough, consistent, and genuine. There's a main dining area, a patio, and a bar area. In the main dining area, you can get a peak into the open concept kitchen and observe the chef crafting the meals. If you're in the mood to catch a game or be up close to the live music they have on the weekends, the bar is a great go-to spot. Overall, the vibe of HiFalutin is warm and cozy, making you want to settle in for a while. 

The food has always been on point every time I've dined here. Instead of traditional bread, they give you blue corn muffins with butter and they are so amazing. Be prepared to ask for several refills! The bar has several options to wet your whistle. During my most recent visit, I went with the full moon beer, which is kind of like a Blue Moon. They also had an IPA and kiltlifter on tap. My brother and his partner each got the prickly pear margarita and it was delicious! For my meal, I got the tomato basil pasta with shrimp. The dish is one of my favorites at HiFalutin. In past visits, I've had the salmon and it too is delicious. Some other dishes my family got were the fajitas, the tacos, the pot roast, and the turkey sandwich. All were great--with one minor issue: my brother was unhappy with the fact that the pot roast comes with cubed potatoes which is a big change from our familial preference for whipped potatoes. 

The service is always friendly and efficient, no matter how busy they are, so no complaints there. My only issue with this most recent visit was that it seemed like a few things needed some upkeep. We dined in the bar area and the chair I sat on was broken so I switched it out for another. Weirdly enough, the same thing happened to my brother. The napkin I got had a hole in it, which isn't the biggest deal in the world, but it shows that some things are being overlooked. 

Overall, this is an excellent restaurant that I will continue to return to again and again and I highly recommend it!

Wow! This place is a hidden gem. My friend and I dined here last weekend and I wish I had known about it sooner! 

First, the setting. It's absolutely gorgeous. The bistro sits amongst the beautiful Tohono Chul Park setting, so you get to enjoy beautiful flora and fauna of the Sonoran desert. On top of the beauty, it's so serene and quiet. And I love the architecture. A Spanish colonial style that's a bit rustic. We dined outside and it was just divine. Perfectly shaded. Beautiful scenery. 

Next, the food! The selection is unique and extensive, so I had a hard time deciding. I went with the chicken and waffles. Wow. I love how it comes with watermelon and I love how the waffle is made with blue corn flour. I devoured the whole thing. My friend got the prickly pear chicken and loved it. We both also enjoyed a prickly pear lemonade. The arresting fuchsia color of the drink alone makes it worth getting, but it's also delicious. Very refreshing. 

Service was perfect. Helpful, but not over imposing. Very relaxing. I think our server's name was Trevor. 

If I'm gushing this much, why just 4 stars? Well it's a bit pricy, so keep that in mind. My dish was $17.75 and the prickly pear lemonade was $4.75. So with tip I paid almost $30 just for myself for a lunch with my gal pal. The food is good and the atmosphere is just wonderful, so it's definitely worth it every once in a while! For the cost though, I can't justify coming here on a more regular basis. 

Other than the cost, the place is perfect! Plus you can eat at the bistro without paying entrance for the park. Highly recommend!!

Terrible service and the food isn't worth coming in for. 

You can find better food at other burger joints. 

They don't serve anything special that you can't get at another location.

Mmmm I'm still thinking about the steak tartare from last night. I loved everything about Le Cheri, from it's location in the beautiful Art Alliance building to the impeccable service and of course the food. 

My friends and I ordered 4 different appetizers to share: escargot, gravlax, raviole cream cheese and the tartare.  All were very good but my favorite by far was the tartare.  It's so good that it rivals Vernick's. 

My bourguignon was absolutely delicious: melt in your mouth beef over fresh housemade pasta. I sampled the mahi mahi over pomegranate seeds (also delicious) and the quenelle.  My friend who ordered the quenelle thought that it, and the accompanying rice were overwhelmingly salty but I thought they were tasty despite all the salt.  For dessert I chose the banana bread pudding with chocolate ice cream which was definitely the best one of the night (compared to the ginger creme brulee, pineapple tatin and the pear & chocolate charlotte). The complimentary macaroons & marshmallows were to die for.  

One appetizer, main plate & dessert per person plus 2 bottles of shared wine came out to $75 pp (including tax & tip) - really pretty reasonable for what you get.

I've had pho in New York and Chicago, and this is at the top of my list for the best pho. The broth has a depth and rich flavor with meat that is tender and not chewy.

I always order #10 large, and it satisfies my craving and appetite for the entire day. Great before or after doing a major day of walking or activities. A large bowl is just 75 cents more than the small, and a small is plenty big for most people.

Do yourself a favor and order spring rolls and a Thai iced tea. They make the rolls fresh and the cold tea is nice, sweet, and cold.

My go to spot every time I come back to Florida. It should be yours too if you care about a good, rich broth.

This location is located inside of the Peppermill where we were staying for our girls weekend.

Pros - 

1. Excellent service, upbeat/friendly server.
2. Huge portions.
3. The bar is ALWAYS open. HAHAHAHA

Cons - None

This place (food wise) reminds me of a cross between Mimi's Cafe and Black Bear Diner, as far as options, quality and presentation. It was just ok for me and the service really stood out.

I'm never coming here again! The food is just too good. The omelettes, pancakes...even the sausage patties make your taste buds tingle with every bite. What do they have,.... Emeril cooking back there? Did a UFO start this company and make a menu based on ingredients from Mars? If I went in the back would Will Smith have to wipe my memory with a neuralyzer?

I'm never coming here again because even the coffee is good. Not too strong or too weak and it's definitely not cheap Folders-like coffee.

I'm never coming here again because the presentation is too good. When you're walking in and you see the food on other people's table, your brain gets sensory overload. The eggs, Bloody Marys, breakfast plates, ...it's like they're pictures in a food magazine. But I'm always leery when the presentation is too good because the taste rarely matches how it looks. But I'm never coming here again because the taste is actually, believe it or not, better than the presentation.

I'm never coming her way again because the service is great. Oh, how annoying it is when the server keeps coming and bothering you. Re-filling your water when it's not even half down. Or when you need to flag them down. I can't take it, the servers here are all knowledgeable about the menu and know exactly when to come. 

If you want my advice, stay away from this place. Nobody should be that good. There are at least three other breakfast/brunch places in this shopping area and they are empty compared to here. There's a 30 minute wait here on weekends. Try them instead. One bite of Broken Egg and you're hooked for life.

Decided to give this place a try as I was heading to Jazzy's BBQ for lunch, two blocks away on the other side of the street. Glad I did! The most recent reviews range from people being highly impressed to sorely disappointed. Most of them complaints had to do with the sides but I since I only go for the meat when I eat BBQ, it's a non-issue for me. 

I got the Three Meat Sampler and really liked the taste. All three meats were moist, flavorful and not too smoky. Same goes for the look, texture and seasoning. The moistness and juiciness of the meat sold me. Jazzy's is good but their meat is a little drier than Mission BBQ. As a side note, I like the way they put your food on brown butcher paper like most Texan old style places do it. It makes the whole experience seem more authentic, even though Mission BBQ is actually a small chain based in Baltimore. 

The restaurant combined modern decor with a slight western feel. I like how they have very large windows with good lightening (believe me, many places get this wrong and end up with an interior that feels to dark).

Customer service wise, Mission BBQ is awesome. You can tell that they put a lot of effort into this. They go out of their way to make sure you're happy. There are no waiters/waitresses and yet an employee approached me as I was eating and offered to get me a drink because she noticed I didn't order one. That's attention to detail! As I was leaving I got into a brief conversation with the manager, Steve, who showed me the pit where they smoke the meat for events. It's always a plus when you see the manager is a down-to-earth, friendly person who is working alongside his employees instead of sitting in the back room.  

I almost took of a star because they charge charge you a more for their food than others and give you smaller portions. Value wise, this place doesn't stack up as high as other places. For $14, with no sides, I wish I could have gotten a little more meat. But I don't want to imply that Mission BBQ is a rip off either. 

Overall, I like the look of the place, the customer service (usually don't factor this in much but their's is excellent) and of course, the food. They definitely have earned a spot on my rotation for places to eat for lunch or early diner.

I love the whole feel of Irish bars so I end up here almost every time I go to Ybor Town. It always seems to start or end here at James Joyce. Its a nice medium sized bar with an great beer selection. Love the pinaaple cider (even though they ran out the last time).

Like all bars the atmopshere can get crazy on weekends. Doesn't get too crazy though, as the most you'll see is a leprechaun giving a lap dance to two women in the middle of the bar. Seriously, it's pretty mellow and laid back for the most part. Because it's a block off 8th street, it doesn't get as packed as some other bars get so its pretty easy to walk around. 

Overall, James Joyce is a pretty chill bar with a killer draft beer selection. One of my favorite spots to go to in the area.

The Good:

For $10.99 during lunch, you can eat as much sushi as you want. Don't get this confused with a buffet, because you pick what you want from the menu, and they bring it out to you. Each time you want another selection, you have to order it from your server. You can choose any type of roll you want on the menu. The selection is awesome! I counted 31 types of sushi alone that you can pick from and that doesn't include the Hibachi section (not included during lunch only diner).

The food is the selling point for me but I'm also a fan out the semi-authentic Japanese decor and kimonos all the servers wear. They look a lot more comfortable than standard uniforms I see waiters and waitresses wearing.

The Bad:

It takes a while to get your food, especially when it's busy. The wait time will be at least 10 minutes once you order your next plate. It's somewhat understandable b/c they have to hand make each roll but it doesn't make it any less annoying. 

I've found that it's better to order plates things at a time due to the wait time. If you order one plate at a time, you'll be looking at 30 minutes worth of wait time just for three items. 

The Ugly:

Finding the place! It's off highway 19 and there's only one way to get to it. It's next to Costco. It took me a couple tries to find it because it's not in the main part of the mall area. 

Overall, I'm pretty impressed with this place. The sushi is a 7 out of 10 but you want try a bunch of different types. The service is good but slow. Once you consider everything, including price, it's a pretty good spot for lunch or dinner, especially if you like Sushi and semi-authentic Japanese food.

Fantastic Jamaican food! Everything is made from scratch and oh, so good. I would consider myself someone a connoisseur of jerk chicken and I can definitely say this restaurant gets an A+ in that department. The spices are perfect. Besides the meat, the sides aren't bad too including the rice n' beans, cabbage and macaroni n' cheese. Great beef and chicken patties as well. The inside is small but they do a lot delivery business in the area. When you eat-in, you see Uber Eats drivers coming in and out every 10 mins. Huge fan of this place and come here at least 3x per week. Good for lunch and diner

Review For Sunday Buffet Only: $58.85 with tax

Brunch Buffet At OysterCatchers is Sunday 10am-2pm. They stop seating at 2pm but you can still stay and eat until about 3:30pm so there's no rush to leave exactly at the time the buffet officially closes.

-Unlimited champagne and bloody Mary's.
-Custom omelette station
-Custom pasta section
-Oyster, shrimp and muscles bar
-Sushi bar (small selection)
-Waffle bar
-Desert bar
-Seafood bar
-Prime rib
-Everything in between

This is the unlimited premium buffet. You must valet park ($8.00) and it gets really busy so you might want to make a reservation in advance. You don't have to (I always forget) but just know you'll get a table outside. Not a problem in the winter but a problem in spring and summer months when it's 100% humidity outside. As I'm writing this sweat is pouring down my face onto the computer screen even though the food and atmosphere are great.

I am very picky about my barbecue. Always have been, always will be. I randomly found this place on Yelp and, having never heard of it, had to give it a try.

The restaurant looks like you would expect it to, concrete floors with a pretty utilitarian ambience. Perfect, I'm here for the food, not the environment. The service was quick and clean, one of the advantages of BBQ is that it can is that it just can't be made to order. 

The pulled pork was solid and is my yardstick for a barbecue place. Not charging for slaw, a required condiment in my book is a HUGE bonus. They had some great drink specials that made it 11 bucks (plus tip) for a sandwich, two sides and a good IPA. I can't see how you would beat that. 

They've got a solid selection of aides; the mashed sweet potatoes are the best of their regular sides that I had. The slaw is similarly excellent and is house made. I don't think I'd go for the potato salad again, it didn't strike me as particularly special. 

Overall this is a solid BBQ place one of the best in New Orleans, a welcome addition for a city that while known for his food isn't exactly on the barbecue atlas.

There are Peel people and Dewey's people when it comes to who has the best pizza in the area.  I love them both for different reasons.  Peel wins the appetizer category with their Involtinis.  Pizza dough wrapped around prosciutto that comes with sipping sauces.  I'd fight a small child for the last one of those on the serving plate!

Peel also has a good selection of beers and tasty deserts cooked in their wood fired oven.  The pizzas in my opinion are very good but not quite as good as at Deweys.  Mainly because they have funkier toppings.  But if you like things such as broccoli and turkey on a pizza, you're gonna love Peel.

The service is always good and they have a decent little outside area.  The wait for a table isn't as bad as it used to be either.  Definitely worth a trip to either Edwardsville or the much larger O'Fallon location.

Bobby's is the best frozen custard in the greater St Louis area (sorry Ted Drews).  They have a fun throw back to the 50s style.  The line moves super fast so don't worry if it looks long.  They have outdoor seating only and have done a good job adjusting to Covid 19 limitations.

Bobby's is dog friendly so take your furry friend along and order them a Pup Cup (low sugar vanilla in a bow).  They will love you forever and you'll get to laugh at them pushing the bowl all over as they lick their treat.  They also do specials that frequently involve mixing baked goods like pumpkin pie from a local bakery in their concrete.  So good!

If the world ever gets back to normal they do free concerts on Sunday evenings.  Expect a crowd then.

Amazing food for a great price. I've been a customer here since I was a child, and the place has evolved beautifully. Customer service is always warm and inviting. I usually get the rice with chicken shrimp and veggies, but everything on the menu is delicious. All ingredients are always fresh and made to order.  Always one of my first choices when I'm really hungry and in the area.

WELCOME TO BAYONA! The Quarter's best fine dining-themed circus. 

Step right up and take a seat. Let the aloof waiters set the mood. I hope you brought a poncho! Now's the time to pull it on: the wine flows freely everywhere but in your glass, making a Pollockian masterpiece of your tablecloth. If you're lucky, they may extend their artistry to your dress shirt by opening a bottle over it, as they did for one of my dining companions. 

Oh, you didn't want your memories of Bayona on your shirt? How unappreciat... I mean, please leave your information with the host stand, dry clean your shirt, mail the receipt, and (maybe) you'll be reimbursed: At Bayona, they exemplify "service."

The manager, you ask? The manager is part of the experience, silly! And he makes Ed Debevic's look like Mister Rogers' Neighborhood: 

Manager S. (ask for him by name!) starts the encounter reasonably, but--when you step aside with him and suggest that a comped entrée for the victim/art patron might be in order since, you know, he expected to pay for fine dining but instead is without a dress shirt for the night--you realize that you're still in Alice's Wonderland, and S. will insist that you're the crazy one. "Intoxicated!" Never mind that the only alcohol you'd had since waking was the maybe one glass of wine his restaurant served you when the waitress wasn't watering the tablecloth or your shirt with your bottle: if you don't sit down, Manager S. will call the police. 
 
Suffer through the performance or go to jail: those are your options. 

Following my S.-perience but still before our entrées arrived, our guest of honor, still in denial that we were actually at the circus, went, himself, to talk with the manager. Manager S. told him our options were to leave or stay, and when we chose to leave, ran after us calling the police. As we waited for S. at the front door, S. let loose a racial epithet at our guest of honor, perhaps as compensation for the waitress's spill. 

Wanting to get on with our night, we ultimately paid over $400 for the whole experience, including the entrées we hadn't received. (We demanded they pack those entrées for us. They left out one, so they still shorted us not only in service but also in still-unwanted food.) New Orleans' finest--about six of them--arrived shortly thereafter, heard our story, talked to S., and then left, handcuffs empty. 

One star for falsely promoting itself as a restaurant. Performance art is great, but not when I'm hungry. 

N.B.: Manager S.'s full name omitted for the sake of internet anonymity. Mr. Rogers, rest in peace, probably would have wanted it that way. 

And, again in Mr. Rogers' memory, I'll mention that the host stand staff were pleasant, so props to them. One of them should be promoted to manager.

We have always driven by this place, and saw the lines of people waiting to get in, so we decided that we need to try it out someday. 
The parking lot was small so parking can definitely be an issue. 
We were lucky that we were seated right away and there was no lines but the place was still packed. 
Deciding what to get was pretty tough as the menu choices were pretty vast. I decided on the chicken and waffles benedict, which I was able to pick a side of pancakes, slices of tomatoes, fruit, or home fries. 
We got an basket of complimentary Danishes that had a variety of sweets. I have to say this was one of the best chicken and waffles Benedict I ever had. The eggs were poached perfectly and the chicken was crispy with a perfectly made waffle that wasn't hard and not to soft. 
I definitely recommend the place to go...fast and friendly service with good food!

It's often a challenge to find good Greek food in New Jersey, but this Mercer County spot fits the bill.

Out with a friend for an early dinner on a balmy Sunday evening, Mikonos offered up quick service and a menu of familiar eats (gyro, souvlaki, moussaka,et al) with some less common choices (a wide range of lamb dishes, stuffed eggplant). 

We both kept it simple with a gyro platter: the plate was overflowing with wedges of warm and chewy pita, nicely tart lemon potatoes, and strips of well spiced, just-charred-enough lamb/beef with an appropriately tangy tzatziki on the side. More than enough food for two meals.

Bourbon House is a more casual outpost of the Brennan restaurant empire (including Commander's Palace, Brennan's, and the neighboring Dickie Brennan's Steakhouse). It also doubles as the hotel bar and restaurant for the Crowne Plaza where I stayed.

I dropped in for a quick beer and a bite to eat. The menu is mostly modern Creole cooking, with the crawfish and tasso boudin ball not to be missed: crawfish, spicy tasso ham, Creole cream cheese and rice formed into a ball, fried, and served with a tangy sauce.

This trip to the beach nearly killed me, so it only gets 4 stars. Beautiful beach and seashells galore. But not worth the terror of nearly drowning.

After paying at the meter to park ($2.50/hr), I headed out onto the beach. I found it more crowded than I had expected from what little traffic I had experienced, but it was also a Saturday. I was there for some shelling anyways and had plans to beachcomb my way down to the end of the beach, to the retaining wall. 

I hit the jackpot, down by the retaining wall, and found lots of great shells. Afterwards, I decided to walk back up the beach a short distance and go cool off in the water. I know better than to go into water near retaining walls and channels, due to dangerous currents. There was only a couple people down at the end, up on the beach, and I wanted to enjoy the water where it wasn't crowded and it was quiet. That almost ended up being the last bad decision I've ever made. 

I didn't even go out very far before I laid back to float on my back and relax for a bit. After what seemed like just a few seconds, I felt myself being pulled into a current and when I opened my eyes, I saw that I had been very quickly pulled right back to the end of the beach and the current sucking me in was just getting stronger and beginning to pull me down the retaining wall of rocks and out towards the channel. I couldn't get ahold of the rocks I was being dragged along and slammed into well enough to climb up and out of the water. I'm a very strong swimmer, but there was no way of swimming out of this and I was fearful that if I went along with the current and allowed myself to be pulled into the channel, I would drown. 

A man appeared out of nowhere and jumped in to save me. I am so extremely grateful for the big, muscular man named Dan that scooped me up like a sack of potatoes and took me to land. He said I was just about to be sucked into a spot in the rocks that whirlpools and would have sucked me under. This is an extremely dangerous spot, and there's not a single sign warning of such. I know locals understand the dangers of channels, inlets, rip currents, etc. But others often do not. I'm still mad at myself because I knew better, but I really did think I had moved far enough away to be safe before entering the water. Children should absolutely not go anywhere near the end of this beach. 

I'm looking forward to going back on a weekday morning for some less crowded shelling time. But I'm never going in the water, past the restaurant that meets the shore, ever again.

We had a really great lunch experience! They were only seating people every other booth, and we greatly appreciated that. 

Our waiter was very attentive and friendly. Food was great and the lunch menus prices and serving sizes were perfect. My daughter and I both had to take home leftovers.

My daughter and I were in search of a new sushi place to try. The photos of a few of the rolls on Sushi Boss' Yelp page really drew us in.    Wow! They really are very generous with the tastiest ingredients in their rolls!

A super friendly woman greeted us as soon as we walked in and described Sushi Boss as being "the Subway of sushi." While they had a list of sushi rolls and poke bowls, they also have build your own options. What I found really interesting is that they also offer the option to have 2 different rolls combined into one for a specialty half/half roll. Your entire meal is made right in front of you.

Prices are really reasonable and they have plenty of options. Checking in with Yelp scores you a free Miso soup! They also have a great offer to add on one of many sides and a drink from their large drink selection. 

We were both thrilled with our rolls. They were absolutely delicious, and we both regretted eating the last pieces. We were so overly full, but they were to tasty to waste. Neither of us were able to eat much of the edamame we had ordered because our rolls were so filling. 

Worth noting, for those with a partner who never wants to go to sushi joints. They offer sushi that's made with red meat, cooked obviously...and it sounds delicious.

This is a pretty good little burger joint. My teen dream, Marky Mark, is affiliated so...5 stars. 

Stopped in with my daughter and grandbabies for lunch. We didn't have a wait to be seated and our waiter was friendly and attentive. 

We shared a tasty Flight Of Tots while we enjoyed our cocktails and waited on our burgers. My cocktail wasn't really what I was after, but ok. I wouldn't order it again. 

The burgers were delicious. I can't argue that. However, it may be my sensitivity to certain textures, but once the buns on my burger became soggy about halfway thru eating, I was done. My burger had a lot of good stuff on it that could cause that to happen, so I don't think it was an overly greasy burger issue. 

The descriptions on the menu really gave me a chuckle, like "government cheese." There were several items on the menu that I'd like to go back and try. It sounds like Jenny has really good tastes, because all of the menu items deemed as "hers" sounded really tasty...and more on the healthier side of things.

It was a cold rainy evening with nasty weather forecasted so even though I was concerned there was only one car in the lot when I arrived, I gave it a shot. 
There were a few issues:  
* had to ask for silverware. 
* then had to ask for a napkin 
* my milk wasn't really cold and only 3/4 full. 
* my soup wasn't hot nor really warm- just lukewarm. 
All of that aside, the meal was called a mini meal and it was a great value at $9.99. Soup, roll with butter, entree with a huge side of pasta. Brought the pasta home for another meal. 
It was a run of the mill diner meal that was comforting on this nasty weather night. 
* Final issue was having to wait for my check while my server with her back to me finished her dinner seated at the counter 3 feet from me. I Consider this an issue because 3 other servers were standing around, facing me with my plate pushed away and no one volunteered to deliver a check to someone who was obviously done. Cmon folks there were only 2 other customers !!! 

This place is no way as good as the LLANERCH of old, Pre 2010 but it's ok and I'll try it again sometime And  hopefully be able to add more stars.

Disclaimer: I may be biased because I've been coming here on and off for 30 years. 
Believe me with the gazillion dining options in the City,Delco,
Montgomery and Chester Counties I always return to my roots for fabulous food at great prices. 
Over the years my forays here have included dates in my 20's to dining with the husband, bringing our daughter in, in a car seat where she was wide eyed with all to look at and being fawned over by everyone around. Later they gave her Shirley Temples and many times never charged us. 
My daughters Times  here went on to in to include her first time dining alone with friends as a teen, various special occasions including many St Patrick's Days for Ham and Cabbage. We also had a small gathering here after my husbands funeral in 2006 and it was handled tastefully and lovingly. 
The feminine offspring is now 25 and still likes to come here with me. Millennials  aren't going to hang here but trust me they sure like eating here. 
I have easily turned a hundred people onto Erin and all are now reg's
Today was my Prendie girl's quarterly friends luncheon. 5 of us ate and moderately drank for an 1.5 hrs of fun. No one rushed us out. In fact I have never felt rushed here. You are treated like family here. 
If you need convincing about how reasonable the prices are today I had: 
-Seven Seas soup- full of seafood in a beefy broth -- Devine 
- Veal Parmigiana. They called it lunch and yet it was huge and I am taking it home where it will be at less 2 more meals.  Served with a large side of spaghetti and home made coleslaw like your Nanna used to make!
- Dessert was a Creme de Menthe parfait. Also huge. 
- But the best part was my Grey Goose dirty Martini for only $8.50. Served in a retro glass and one was enough for me to have fun. 
The grand total for this huge meal with a libation was $24.62 !!!

Sunday, November 25. 

About 13 of us who Brunch on Sunday's were lucky enough for fellow Yelpie Alexandra K. to have chosen Bar Hygge when she hosted this event. 
Our server was devine in that she complied with our separate checks request. It's just easier that way for us. Even with separate checks they did add the tip but most of us I believe left her more because she was a fabulous server, along with a food runner. The reception area was staffed by a lovely young lady too. 

Zagat states " Hygge' is Danish for 'cozy camaraderie".  Well, They have that nailed here.
The conversations was able to flow well due to the long table ending at a banquette type area on which 5 were seated facing the table. The minimal times where I wasn't talking I looked around and saw that everybody was having a good time and everybody was enjoying their cocktails. It was a chill yet warm vibe also due to the huge picture window bathing our table in gentle light. 

A short stop at the bar to change a bill to facilitate quicker payments allowed me to meet the friendly bartender Who has been here from the beginning-  three years. He was conversant and friendly While never missing a beat while Simultaneously making cocktails.
I apologize to the anyone reading this review But I'm totally blanking on the names of the bartender and a server. They were very good.

My menu: 
- Bloody Mary
- Eggs Benedict w Pork Belly. 

The bloody Mary was a step above the standard American bloody Mary. It was slightly darker due to the spices being a little stronger. Spices lined the rim giving it that extra kick along with making the glass pretty. 2 cubes of provolone with a razor thin slice of prosciutto( I think)  wrapped around them took this Bloody Mary to the next level. 

I have a favorite saying "Everything is better with bacon".  At this brunch  I'm changing that to everything's better with pork belly. My entree was 2 perfectly poached eggs atop spinach and pieces of pork belly. 
Can you say " Delicacy Heaven?"

I can't wait to bring friends back here. Loved it!!!

I can't believe it's taken me this long to write a review of Pho 75. 
The reason I haven't is because I can't say anything  different than anyone else has said in a very positive way. It's family run. The service is great and attentive. The food is great. There is ample comfortable seating in an albeit plain  interior. 
The Tea is free!!!   
There is one large overhead TV and this time when I visited Eagles banners were hanging from the ceiling.
It's cash only and I don't blame them because they're able to deliver a good product very inexpensively. If they took credit cards that wouldn't be the case.
Plenty of free parking.

I wasn't sure if I could be objective having come to Pica's for 40 years!!!! But after 5 years as Yelp Elite I had to. 
Coming here as a teen we usually got 1 pizza pie with the cheese on the bottom, sauce on top and split it 6 ways. We'd all at least get a Coke but we were so broke we weren't helping the Pica's pay off the mortgage with our business. They never seemed to mind. The Pica's were "old school" in that business was business and every customer was treated well. And the really cool thing in High School was to get a job at Pica's. I never worked there but friends did and to hear them tell it then, it was a great job. 30 and 40 years later my friends and a sibling talk about it as if it were the Holy Grail off teenage employment. I attribute this to the Pica philosophy. AND, When Tina Fey was on Fallon, he remembered her love of Pica's and surprised her with one of their pizza's live on the show!

Fast forward to me as a 20 something able to buy a meal with new friends. We'd stop by for pizza dinners and their famous escarole soup before going out clubbing. Hopefully we were never too obnoxious but none of us ever felt like we weren't their best customers. We were living it up! Except when we ran into our parents or their neighbor friends. LOL 
You see, everyone loved Pica's. Great food and service so you were bound to run into someone. The same is true today. Everytime I visit I see families and friends who have been coming for decades. You don't get repeat business if you don't have the key to success in the restaurant industry. Namely, treat you customer well and fill them with great food and libations.
Heading into the early 1990's and I have a fiance and eventually my husband who became as hooked on as I on this wonderful, old school, authentic Italian restaurant.. Both of us cringed when they remodeled it in the early 90's. Would it retain the old world charm? The answer is yes! The oak that was blondish when installed is now a little darker and I like the warmth it imparts. Makes you feel like you are at your Nonna's place. We welcomed Baby Elizabeth in September,1992 and she has been going there every couple of months since she was 3 months old. The frequent times she's dined there as an adult she loves the fact the portions are so generous she always leaves with leftovers(Reminds me of broke me at the same age).
Honestly even though their menu is extensive and full of choices I've had everything at least 3x so I can't recommend one thing.Everything is s good. They have every Italian dish you can think of. Their seafood is really good. Excellent meat and veal choices too. Soups= Yum!

 Thus far in 2018, I've been there 4x. I especially like their Prime Rib night.  What I can tell you is this...you will love what they bring to the table as a "welcome". Really great Fresh Italian bread that will be warm. Plus a dish of roasted peppers in olive oil.  
 
Manga!

Northern Delaware, Represent!!!

I live close to PA/DE border and for years worked in DE but have been remiss in trying" below the border" spots.My special gentleman friend has become a Yelp convert so when he saw over 4 stars for this Italian Restaurant/Pizzeria in a strip mall off Naamans road( rt 92) He said "Lets go".  This place is so cute and the food is really good so C'mon Philly peeps, take the 30 minute drive from Center City. And no tax! 

Yes it is a pizzeria. And yes when you dine on the restaurant fare you are basically seated in a pizzeria like environment. But don't let that dissuade you.The seating is very comfortable. The menu and the food are great! I've dined in South Philly/NYC many times and the taste here is reminiscent of those venues with its authentic, excellently crafted menu items. Everyone here seemed to be enjoying their meals. The atmosphere and vibe is homey here. When you taste your entree you imagine someone's grandma was in the back making it just for you. 

 Both of us had Chicken Piccante which came  with a side salad and nice, flat Italian bread and butter. 3 slices of chicken breast in a mellow lemon butter sauce  topped with capers atop a bed of spinach. The chicken was accompanied with pasta that tasted fresh. The sauce was just perfect in that you could taste all 3 but it was not overwhelmed by the flavor of just one. A perfect blend. 
Our wonderful experience was complimented by warm Italian dinner music.
Premium beers were incredibly reasonable priced.House wines are a good price too.

Luckily we arrived at 5:45 because there were no seats by by 615 on a Monday night.  When we left at 7 there was literally a line out the door  spilling onto the walkway so the locals know about this place.On a Monday night!!!!  The locals might want to keep it a secret but I am passing the secret on...You won't be disappointed if you stop here for dinner. 


.

Visit: Sunday April 2, 2017

Incredible place to get just a piece of cake, pie or pudding. Or take a variety of items home. 
Everything is so beautiful inside of the display cases that I remarked to our group that was on a culinary tour of the new Chinatown , that for the next birthday instead of a bakery cake I'm going to come here and get a variety of items and serve them buffet style for the birthday celebration. 
Besides the six of us who split slices of mango and matcha mousse cake as well as a green tea-i-misu cake we noticed people just popped in for a piece of dessert and a cup of tea or coffee. 

My friend had told me that the owner, a Chinatown business person had hired a French pastry chef. Chef does a fine job on interpreting all of the normal staples but I particularly enjoyed his interpretations of Asian desserts. 
Bringing the point home even more, I heard a French accent while I was in line and I turned to talk to the gentleman. We talked for a few minutes and he remarked on how beautiful everything looked in the case. He also told me he had tried 2 desserts and I have to tell you this Frenchman was really really impressed.

 I was lucky enough to meet the owner Jack who thanked us for coming in that day. No, Thank You Jack for giving us something totally new to do in Chinatown

Service: Impeccable. 
Ambiance : Perfection, inside and out. 
Meal: Fabulous. 

For our visit on Thursday at lunchtime we opted to sit outside on the covered porch that overlooks the parking lot. Don't let the parking lot dissuade you from choosing this space because you're high up enough that you see the trees around you and not cars. The tables were amply spaced apart giving us plenty of room to stretch out, converse as old fiends do and enjoy our meal without having to listen to other's conversations. The table and seating are comfortable. But the real gem is inside where you have beautiful tables and two beautiful bars where I have gone for happy hours and enjoyed. Downstairs is the wine cellar with beautiful seating in a large room and a couple of more private rooms. It'd been a few years since I had seen the wine cellar dining area and a nice gentleman gladly gave us a tour of the main room as well as the small rooms within the wine cellar. The tour was so nice it reminded me that it's been a years since I had a birthday party and I'm now considering doing Tecca for my next birthday.
See what great customer service gets you?

I've eaten here before and enjoyed it but this is my first review. Today we both had salads
- I had the shrimp arugula salad which had shaved fennel and four large meaty shrimp with a delicate creamy dressing they complemented the salad. 

- I have forgotten what my dining companion had but he did enjoy his salad equally as well as I did. 

He had a gin and tonic and I had an unsweetened iced tea and both of us enjoyed the beverages. Both of us felt the service was attentive and very pleasant. And Both of us remarked that we will definitely come back again this summer and most definitely in the winter.

I come here specifically for the Vietnamese sandwiches (banh mi) and BBQed pork. Don't be intimidated by the unfamiliar meat that's dangling in the window or the man with the machete-like butchers knife chopping away at said meat - that pork and duck are to DIE FOR. No joke. Be adventurous and ask for half a lb of pork - promise you will not be disappointed! 

And who can complain about a $2.50 sandwich? It's got mayo, pate, several different cold cuts, meat balls, cucumber, cilantro and jalepenos. DeeeeeeeeLISH! I always get extra for an easy lunch or snack later in the week. I've yet to meet a person who hasn't loved this sandwich. 

Like other reviewers have said, the produce section is solid. Lots of fresh Asian greens and plenty of familiar staples (onion, garlic, bell peppers, etc) - all priced a bit less than Rouses. 

Other personal favorites are:
- Udon noodles - cook in chicken broth with shrimp and garnished with bean sprouts, green onions and cilantro - cheap and satisfying meal!
- Young coconut juice
- Grass jelly drink - I still don't know what grass jelly is, but it sure is tasty!
- Frozen potstickers
- Ramen galore! Every brand and flavor your heart could ever desire. 

I wish we had this market or even a mini version of it within the actual city of New Orleans, but for now, I'm willing to make the trek over the bridge to get my sandwiches and BBQed meats.

This place is just lovely! Very quintessential upscale New Orleans with the exposed brick, ceiling to floor curtains, lush green ivy dangling from above, chandeliers, top notch service and the perfect location in Jackson Square. 

I ordered from their fixed priced menu, which is an absolute steal! The bayoubaise was huge and delicious, perfect for a seafood lover. The flourless chocolate cake was the perfect way to end the meal. Unfortunately the gorgonzola cheese cake was a complete miss; there was something about the flavor and texture that were completely off for me; would not recommend. My husband devoured his turtle soup and duck, which I take as signs of approval. From the few bites I was able to swindle, I could tell he ate quickly to minimize sharing with me. 

Overall, it was a really fantastic dining experience. I often assume that food in the French Quarter will be awful and overpriced due the tourist traps but Muriel's was exceptional.

A place that truly captures the spirit and magic of New Orleans. The kind of place I take guests to give them a truly authentic experience. Use your rose-colored glasses if you come during the day; it's hard to fall in love with mis-matched lawn furniture. But at night when the tiki torches are lit and the place is buzzing with chatter and live music and the air smells of all sorts of yummy foods - it's hard not to be caught in the spell.  Grab some vino and embrace the moment. 

Food is cash only. Super annoying but at least there's an ATM. This weekend we had the ahi tuni with watermelon. Amazing. Asian broccoli. Amazing. Ceviche. Amazing. Crab with sweet zucchini bread. Super amazing. For lack of a better word, food was simply amazing. And affordable. 

This is one of those places that makes me think: gosh I'm so lucky to live in this wonderful city. No one has it better than us!

Cafe Du Monde is a must stop when in New Orleans or even when passing through New Orleans. It's that one place, above all others, that you must go.

First things first, before you go, grab cash as you're not getting anything with your debit or credit card.

Usually it's crowded beyond imagine, but due to recent events the place was essentially empty. So empty that you're not even allowed inside. It's a walk up counter where you order and they grab everything for you.

But regardless, the beignets are so good. The perfect full consistency. Tons of powdered sugar. An order is three and will run you a couple of bucks. All totally worth it, even if you're on a diet. It's worth the break. Plus you've got to get the frozen coffee. It's delicious.

If you're lucky, there won't be a line. But if there is a line, get in it, it'll be worth it, I promise. This place is an institution. You've got to give it a try at least once. And your taste buds will thank you, trust.

I'm a fan. I'm a fan. I'm a fan. I'm so happy a friend told me about Naked Farmer, and I'm even more happy that it's not far from where I live.

I recently moved to the area and unfortunately am on a diet trying desperately to get off my quarantine weight, lucky Naked Farmer is here to help.

Naked Farmer is a build your own bowl concept with fresh and locally grown foods.

You get one base, two sides, and a protein. I believe my bowl was $13 and some change. I got the farro with winter green vegetables, broccoli and sweet potatoes and the rosemary chicken. Then when it's all said and done, there are sauces! I tried two- the cider vinaigrette and the garlic aioli. If I had to be uber picky, I did think the chicken was a little dry, but the dips helped out. I loved the cider vinaigrette. That will be my go-to for certain.

the bowls are decently sized and the protein is evenly portioned out for each person who comes in.

The staff was really friendly and walked me through the process and just were really great to talk to.

Whether I'm watching what I eat or not, Naked Farmer will be a place I frequent here in DTSP. The food is phenomenal.

I had been to Philadelphia once before, but never ordered a real "Philly Cheesesteak". Campo's was near where I was staying so this was where I popped that cherry.

The inside is small with some two and four-top tables, but they also have some outside seating on the sidewalk. I liked the huge window that was open to get the fresh air because it was hot that day so I needed it and it didn't feel like the place had any a/c at all.

The line is a pain here because it starts to get long and go out the door so you have to loop yourself around, walking by the register to walk back to it and the space you're walking through is tight quarters so again, on a hot day, isn't fun.

IT'S CASH ONLY. They do have an ATM onsite though.

I ordered "the works" a Philly with provolone, mushrooms, onions, and green peppers. The sandwich was around $11. When it came out I was a little underwhelmed by the size of it. I'm used to spending that amount and getting this huge sub/hero/hoagie/etc, but this wasn't that. It tasted fine, but it wasn't overloaded with any ingredients. The bread was the best part in my opinion.

Not a bad place overall, but I'm going to try my Philly elsewhere next time I'm in town.

So I've finally got around to writing a review about this place. Long overdue. I've been a fan of theirs for about a year strong. I was hooked from my very first visit. I've never had a bad experience. They are great at what they do. They provide friendly service and great wing. There's a ghost chili pepper infused wing sauce they have that is sure to knock your socks off! This place is located directly across the street from Tulane so be wary of the times you order. My favorites are the hot boy wings and the Korean BBQ wings. They have steak fries which I love. Their fries aren't hard like traditional steak fries which is nice. They have plenty of parking depending on the times you frequent the establishment. It's hard to find parking nearby if the parking lot is packed tight. As far as wings go they may be the best in the city.

There are three Noble Pie locations in Reno. The summit location is my favorite! 
The location is a little farther from town but is the newest, and in my opinion, the coolest location.
This place can get very busy. I have been here during a dinner rush and wait times for food and drinks can get as long as 30 minutes. However, it is well worth the wait. 
If you have never had Noble Pie, I would recommend trying a custom pizza by the slice and some of their wings! I usually don't enjoy bone-in wings, but the ones at Noble pie are worth it! They are extra garlicky! So I recommend you bring some gum/mints for after.
I love sitting at the bar at this location. The bartenders are always fun to talk to, the music selection is always on Point, and I love being able to people watch. 

So why do I think this Noble pie location is better than the others? Well I think it all comes down to their cook. The pizza at any Noble pie location is delicious, but the crust is slightly different. The cook at The summit location cooks the pizza a touch longer and it makes the crust much more sturdy! That way you get a nice slice that won't flop over and make you lose all of your toppings. The cook here also backs your toppings under the cheese! Delicious! 

There is ample parking at this location, because it is located in a large outside mall. 
However, I recommend coming before the dinner rush, as seating can become limited and wait times can increase. 

No need to dine in. You can call for to go orders and pick up.

Simply Magical...

This indoor market is remarkable. There are endless aisles lined with everything from baked goods, confections, restaurants and shops. There is truly something for everyone here.

Been to Philly several times and never visited this gem. Most certainly worthy of a day trip. Be sure to visit on a very empty stomach. Do note that the market is mainly comprised of foods. 

Don't make the mistake we made and pay major for parking. Find the lot just across the street and pay for four to five bucks with ten dollar purchase.

Good! Who doesn't love Halal Guys? I was a little nervous about giving this location a try due to several mediocre reviews, however, I'm glad that I gave it a try because the food was phenomenal. I requested the falafel and they made it fresh so it took about 6 or 7 minutes to cook. Our food was great! The young lady was a little heavy handed on the white sauce, but it was all good. The indoor seating is limited, but they have several tables on the outside. This location is in the Target Plaza and we happened to see it on one of our Target runs. Would totally visit again.

HOMOPHOBIC, VIOLENT, ABUSIVE OWNER
It makes me sad to write this review because I used to love this place. However, last night I had the misfortune of meeting the owner for the first time and I will not be going back. He was very drunk, angry, violent, crude, and abusive.
Here is what happened:
It was the night of mardigras itself. My friend was absentmindedly smoking a cigarette as she handed her id to the bouncer at the door. The door guy was super friendly, smiled, and let her through. As soon as we got in (the bar was completely dead, on fat tuesday, btw) the owner stumbled over to her and loudly and aggressively told her "you can't have that in here! Get out!!" She calmly responded "I'm sorry! I didn't realize, the bouncer didn't say anything so I assumed it was ok" "Get out! Get out of my bar!" the owner screamed.
My friend, by the way, is gay and I am fairly certain her appearance had plenty to do with the owner's nasty behavior.
My friend responded: "Hey man, what's your problem? I'm leaving, you could at least be nice"
At this point the owner threw himself at her. He was physically, violently shoving her towards the door, screaming "you're a little A$$HOLE, that's my problem!"
By now the friendly bouncer had come back inside, hearing the commotion. After assessing the situation he gave us a rueful smile "Well, he's the owner". He couldn't do anything, of course, but he kept his hands off my friend which I appreciated. He seemed accustomed to such outbursts from his boss, which is horrifying.
Not realizing my friend and I were there together, the bouncer took the opportunity to pass my question about eating food in the bar on to the owner. The owner responded: "F*CK NO! Get them out of here!!"
Needless to say, we left and found a different bar. On our way back later that night, we walked past the bar owner standing outside of his bar. My friend approached him and, remarkably calmly, said "That's not right what you did before, man. You shouldn't lay your hands on a customer like that, it's bad for business." He screamed obscenities at her down the street as we walked away.
I know he's right that you can't have a cigarette in the bar, but the policy is not the issue, it is his treatment of my friend which is the issue. 
tl;dr
DON'T GO HERE
the owner is
1) Violent
2) Homophobic
3) aggressive 
4) rude
5) very drunk on the job

Very large, and loud, sports bar inside Opryland Resort. TVs or projectors literally everywhere you look. Impressive.

Hubby and I were lucky enough to snag two seats at end of the bar. Others were waiting on tables even though many were open. ? People actually seated at tables seemed to have difficulties with getting good service, as I saw many a staff being waived down pretty consistently. We had stellar service at the bar, so I guess that's the way to go if you're a small party. Otherwise, well...good luck. ;)

We each ordered some local suds and perused the [only available] late night menu. Bacon Cheddar Burger (note: they only cook one temp, medium, because it has two [very] thin patties we were told) for him and "Tennessee" Cheesesteak for me, 16 bucks each with fries. Food came out quickly. Burger was very marginal and actually on the smaller size despite how it looks on the brioche bun. Merp. The TN CS on hoagie was really small (think fit in the length of my hand); however it was mighty tasty. Juicy, tender, flavorful shaved ribeye with grilled veg and white cheese...yum. 

Overall: You kind of know what to expect from these kind of "resort" joints, but there was still a bit of sticker shock. Two plates and a couple of beers each @$9-11 a pop =~$70 tab. Wowza. The steak and friendly lady 'tender bumped the experience up to a solid 3 star from me. Cheers!

A better sign for this place: "Elegant service elsewhere." So true. 

I used to love Franks. My parents took me here often. Great home style cooking. Real waitresses with sass. A nice friendly place with good food, food enough for heavy eaters. 

Sadly I returned as an adult.

I know there is probably a lot of good stuff about Franks/Franciscos. I would give it higher ratings but.... I had the worst experience with a waitress there a few years ago. And I won't go back. I don't care if that waitress is gone or whatnot, because a horrible experience like that is inexcusable for repeat business. Someone can have a bad day here and there. But this waitress really messed it up.

My buddy and I popped in for breakfast and a surly, pissy waitress finally came over to get our order. It was obvious she was having a very bad day. Guess what? All of us do. And I don't ever take it out on the people I serve. She snapped at us for asking where our ice teas were, and told us to get them ourselves when she put them on the counter. The order took forever, and she barked at us when asking for the bill. I have had moments where service is slow, orders are forgotten, but I've never had a waitress in my life "You'll get your damn food stop bothering me."
