Being a timid and polite person, I actually tipped her. And I never returned to Franks. No excuses.

**UPDATE** 
Re: the OWNER'S remarks below, way to value customer feedback! Like I said, the food has gone downhill the last couple orders. I didn't Yelp when it was ok, b/c it wasn't *that* noteworthy. But sure, personally attack me and say it's b/c I'm "lonely"; that really makes sense and is a mature response. More like the last few times when I've chosen OTHER & left $1, the bell wasn't rung as if the deafening silence is there to "shame you". That's a pretty BS excuse about the POS company being to blame as you can have it customized, dear. Self-absorption? You're really laughable! Nah, try the fact that the last time I ordered, consumers were unable to pay with a card. Dark soul?? B/c I have a complaint?? Good god, grow up and learn how to take feedback; positive AND negative. 

Started out great when they first opened, but the last few times were sub par with the cheesesteak & fries. What I find insulting, however, is the default tip amounts when paying by card. If memory serves correct, the defaults are 20%; 25%; 30% or Other. Are you kidding me?!? Did someone come to my table, take my order, deliver it, refill my drink, bring me my check, and process my payment?? Or did I place an order myself, hand the cashier my card (easily resolved if you enabled paying online), and walk back up to the counter when called?? I find this insulting as a former server in the biz that counter folks find themselves entitled to tips, let alone more than a buck or 2 for perhaps going above and beyond somehow. I highly doubt they're making the $2.13/hr I did to constitute the need for tips. Lord knows I don't tip my cashier at Wendy's, the checkout line at the grocery store, or my gas attendant! Get over yourselves, kiddos!

What a wonderful, hidden little gem in Santa Barbara! I honestly don't understand why this hotel has such crappy ratings! Quiet, cozy....just lovely, lovely.

HOTEL ROOM, GROUNDS AND AMENITIES

Our first room was a darling of a room (#803), which felt more like a little cottage in the woods. I loved the old fashioned bath tub, the small little outdoor patio (where we drank morning coffee), the fireplace, hardwood floors, and HEATED bathroom marble floors. 

Upon our arrival, I noticed the letter "H" on the bed pillow, which I found out was for our last name! What a delightful little surprise. The bellman gave us a wonderful detailed tour of the amenities of our room. 

Beautiful windows, well lit rooms. The furniture pieces were so simple, classy, and beautiful. 

Our second room, #2803 (we loved the hotel so much, we decided to stay for a second night but had to be moved due to a wedding party in our building), was actually an upgrade! Located further away from the lobby, restaurant, and things, it was so quiet and romantic. We had a small balcony overlooking the hotel grounds and can see a little bit of ocean too. We enjoyed the fireplace and lounge chairs while playing Scrabble and drinking wine.

We thoroughly enjoyed the oversized tub and you MUST try their amaaaaazzzzzing bath salts. Sadly, they don't sell it at the hotel. :(  (Dear Management, if you're reading this and decide to sell those bath salts one day, let me know!!!)

The hotel grounds are quiet, cozy and quaint. Simple trees, flowers, a wishing well, a pond with coy fish and turtles, a few fountains. Wonderful landscaping. We also liked the little piggy banks!

GYM: I didn't use it but took a peek. Great, brand new equipment. Downstairs from the pool.

POOL: Perfect temperature (heated pool). Great pool side service. NO JACUZZI. No loud music. Just simple loud chairs. Simple relaxation.

Note that the pool and gym are NOT connected to the spa like most hotels! The spa is all by itself by the front desk and restaurant. So it's not an easy thing if you wanted to make an afternoon of it.

BIG TIP:  OMG, you MUST try their battery-powered bikes!! EEEK! We took it out twice during our trip and just had a friggen blast!  The battery enables you to get up those hills. There are only 4 at the hotel so I suggest making reservations. There are no reflectors or lights on the bike so come back before sunset. We made the mistake of taking them out till way past sunset, and it was super scary on the way back because many of the streets don't have lights.

SERVICE

Even better than the Four Seasons. Better than some super luxury hotels in Vegas. Service at this hotel is just second to none.

From the bellman desk, to the front desk, to even engineering, they were just spectacular.  They all try to make an effort to know your name and try to remember you and say hello. My last name is not easy but I still appreciated their effort.

The valet guys (bellman desk) are incredibly personable, fast, and sweet. I have no idea why some of the Yelpers are dissing these hard working dudes!

Whenever you call for anything related to room services, they show up at your door within less than 10 minutes. I loved that. They were so on top of it!

A couple of standouts in terms of service:  

First, we really love Marie (maybe it was Kate or even Marie and Kate???). One of the girls spent so much time with us on the phone while we were driving around trying to find a store that sold bottles of wine at a late hour. In our case, we were trying to find Ralphs.

Second, there was another woman (again, I want to say it was Marie or Kate) who came through for us in scoring a room for our second night at the rate we wanted. I asked that they match our first night's rate and give us a comparable room in the same category and she totally did that.

Third, on the Sunday morning we were scheduled to move rooms, we discovered that the second room had no patio, no fireplace, and appeared to be smaller. Again, another female employee (or maybe it's the same one!) helped us into a room with similar amenities, which turned out to be an upgrade but she gave it to us for the same price. 

SPA

My massage was mediocre. The spa amenities were actually fairly lacking. There's only a steam room and locker room. Nothing else. No jacuzzi. No nuthin'.

And, it was EXPENSIVE. I'm used to paying $150/massage plus tip. Here it was $180 plus 22% service charge. Ouch. 

I would skip the spa.

RESTAURANT 

With the exception of the RIDICULOUSLY tasty beef shepherd's pie, the food here is meh and super overpriced. Here are a few notes:

- Don't order the pot of coffee. It'll cost you $8 and taste terrible. You're better off drinking the free Kourig in the room.
- The kale salad is not really all kale. In fact, it has very little kale.
- The caesar's salad was not good.
- Service was good but terribly, terribly slow at the restaurant. 

Will I be back?? YES.

Good for the late night munchies and when you don't want to stop drinking. Dive bar atmosphere, cool employees, and full food menu and full bar. 

The only complaint is that the Po'Boy bread was stale. Aside from that the fried catfish and fried crawfish are okay. The chili cheese fries are thick enough to cut through the alcohol in your stomach.  

Cash or credit card..

This was a solid diner meal with a few extras. We'd called ahead to waitlist so it was not that long a wait. They were pretty busy on a rainy Sunday afternoon. 

You could order breakfast or lunch. Most of our group went with lunch and one chose a breakfast combo. Service was very good. It took a bit to get our food but as I said, they were packed.

I tried their fried chicken sandwich opting for no pickles and ranch dressing on the side; upgrading my fries to an order of onion rings. The small sandwich came with lettuce on a soft bun but I deconstructed it and only ate the chicken which was quite  good. The onion rings were very good and a large portion. I made sure to save room for dessert -- one of their famous pies.

Others in our group had burgers and liked them. They have kids menus for smaller portions too. The breakfast -- eggs, sausage, potatoes, and toast -- was scarfed down. Even the bread was good. My husband had their hot dog with chili and jalapeños and liked it too.

For dessert, we tried two of their pies -- the butterscotch and the coconut cream. I didn't even get to try the butterscotch, but it must have been good as nary a crumb remained. The coconut cream pie that I shared was amazing -- light and fluffy meringue on a cream filling loaded with coconut flavor and bits. 

Bottom line? Even if you don't want breakfast or lunch -- come for a slice of pie. Double yum!

This was an exceptional dinner experience. Top notch service. White tablecloths. Black napkins (chosen for us when they saw we were wearing black). Delicious food -- everything we ate was wonderful. In spite of the drunk women a couple tables over who were quite loud and obnoxious. I gather this is common. 

My girlfriend had eaten here previously and recommended it to us awhile back. So we made reservations in anticipation of our visit. Reservations are recommended even mid week. They have a dress code -- the most important part is wearing a collared shirt. They're supposed to not seat those in shorts or flip flops, but they did do so anyway for some conventioneers.

I began with a wedge salad trio (triple ice berg wedge). This was a plate with three small wedges of lettuce. One was topped with a large shrimp and a creamy basil dressing; one with crisp bacon and chunky blue cheese with blue cheese dressing; and the last with halved grape tomatoes and a thousand island dressing that tasted like a thick ranch. Super good. I gave one of the wedges to my husband to save room for my entree.

He started with the seafood gumbo. It wasn't a huge portion, but the dark roux base was rich with a spicy white pepper under base. It has shrimp, crab, and oysters in it. They did a nice presentation. The bowl was delivered with a small mound of long grain white rice in the center. Then they poured the gumbo over it at the table. 

For my entree, I had their fried soft shell crab. It was one of the largest and meatiest ones I've ever had. The batter was very light. It was served on top of a corn spoon bread that was surrounded by additional crab chunks and a mix of corn, baby okra, red peppers and tomatoes stewed together (a maque choux). Just wonderful.

My husband had another appetizer as his main dish. He had their version of shrimp and grits. It was New Orleans bbq style shrimp deglazed with local brew Abita amber and goat cheese grits. He said it was rich and creamy. He ate up every bit. 

We did look at the dessert menu, but were too full to indulge. This restaurant is a keeper.  And we will look forward to coming back when next in the area.

This was a disappointing dinner experience especially since it had been recommended by a friend who is usually right on... 

First off it was excruciatingly loud. Uncomfortably so. We could not have a decent conversation and barely heard the explanations by the staff of various menu items. Service was quite good, though. It was the food that was just ok.

One item stood out as being very good and innovative  -- their rabbit and chicken liver pate. It was served in its own little jar topped with aspic. On the board were dollops of grainy mustard, pickled watermelon rind, apple chutney, and half sour pickles. Thin toasts came on the side. 

The cup of crab and corn chowder was just okay. They reheated it for me as the first time it was just barely warm. But I've had a better version at bonefish grill of all places. 

My entree was their drum fish. I ordered it almondine. It came fried with a light coating. But it was dry and topped with only 4 little almond slivers. I was hoping for the traditional brown butter sauce with almonds.... The fish was served over some root vegetables that had an off putting flavor. Not sure if it was the spice used or what,  but I didn't care for them at all. 

My husband ordered their featured pork schnitzel. The portion was large, but it too was overcooked and dry. Luckily there was some sauce on the side which he used to make it edible. The fries were cooked well done as requested. 

In a town where even a bad meal is usually good, we felt we'd waisted our evening. The seafood towers going by did look good though... as did the burger the kid next to us was served. Maybe we ordered all the wrong items? Now we know...

Christmas Day is always a challenge finding an open restaurant. We were a party of six and unfortunately, they only took advanced reservations for parties of 8 or larger. On arrival we were told 25 minutes, but the air was an hour and fifteen minutes. The kids were a little antsy by then.

That being said, we'd had plenty of time to read the menu and decide what everyone wanted to eat. When we were finally seated, we ordered everything at once. 

They forgot my husband's soup. But the egg roll came fairly fast and it was okay.

The entrees came shortly after that and they were wonderful. My husband cancelled his soup when they brought his entree. Unusual for all to like all dishes orders. The kids had the children's meals -- sweet and sour chicken and honey chicken -- and they liked them as well. The Singapore rice noodles had a touch of a curry kick. The noodles were perfectly cooked. The General Tso's Chicken was not very spicy which was perfect for this that ordered it. They also had some chicken low menu which was very flavorful -- not greasy. I felt I got the standout dish - orange beef. This was a huge portion of beef caramelized in orange sauce which was sweet but not cloyingly so. Lots of pieces of candied peel were included too. On the edge of the dish were several pieces of broccoli and a small side dish of white rice. I didn't even dent the rice nor get to the broccoli. It was a tad spicy but not much at all. You can request spicier if you desire.  

Would we come back? Yes. But we'd make sure to come earlier or very late -- if it's Xmas or adopt two more people so we could make a reservation.

Service was excellent and friendly. Came here for dinner with family over the holidays. 

Everyone liked their food. And we got a variety of items. 

We ordered their crispy chicken wings (they looked wonderful); the pork chasu bun appetizer (with a nice soft "bun"); a house salad (with fresh crisp lettuce and a tasty ginger dressing); a kanisu salad (a large portion; with krab, masago, and avocado over cucumber); We also had a variety of their ramen dishes -- with miso; spicy; with chicken broth and pork broth; with chicken, with pork; with shrimp. I had their yuzu shoyu -- a chicken broth base -- with shrimp. I think it would have been better with pork or chicken, though there was a lot of shrimp. And a lot of noodles and bamboo shoots along with seaweed, fish cake slices, and a half boiled egg.  I asked for added bok choy but they gave me regular cabbage instead. No problem, I like cabbage too. The bowls are large and had we not been staying at a hotel, I would have taken leftovers home. 

As they'd opened during 2020 (at the beginning of the pandemic), we'd never been here before. Hope they are successful and stay, as I'd like to try a number of their other menu items (appetizers; rice bowls, too).

This was a very good fast casual restaurant. It's Greek food -- better than some sit down full service places here. 

You order and pay at the counter. They give you a number and then bring your order to the table. It is served with plastic ware and on disposable plates... 

We came with some family and everyone -- even the kids -- found something they liked to order.

We had a cup of their lemon chicken soup. It was quite lemony and served piping hot (it was cool out). It didn't even need any salt, as this type of soup usually does, but there was more than enough lemon for flavor. There were even nice chunks of chicken along with the rice in the broth. 

We also shared a gyro platter with Greek salad. The salad was fresh with olives, feta, beets, tomatoes, green peppers, etc. I liked the dressing on it as well. There was lots of gyro meat on top of the salad and yellow rice (with veggies mixed in) -- so the portion was certainly large enough to share. A small container of tzatziki sauce and pita bread wedges, too, also came with the plate 

I'd certainly come back here again in the future. Prices were reasonable and the food was tasty.

More like 3 1/2 stars...

This is a relatively new branch of the chain. They are known for their individual pizzas and salads. 

We came with family and for kids this is a great option to design their own pizzas with toppings of their choice. 

The pizzas we had were pretty good. They have suggested classic combinations or you can choose to make your own. The regular size 11" dough base looks exceptionally thin when they first place it on the pan. Don't be fooled as it puffs up fine in the oven. For very young kids or small eaters, they also offer a min pizza at only 6 inches. For those that like a LOT of dough you can get a double thick crust. They also offer a gluten free option but the disclaimer notes that since they only have one serving line, it's really not fool proof. So if you really have a gluten problem, skip this place.

The reason for the less one star is due to their organization. A long line was held up by the first person you come in contact with. It's like a game of forty questions. Then if you're doing "make your own" pizza you answer the toppings questions all over again once you've seen the actual toppings in front of you. So, they need a better system moving the line along.

Once you order however, your pizza is delivered in a fairly good amount of time.

We all liked our different pizza varieties. Some got white sauce, most got tomato sauce as a base. And a complete variety of toppings which are all at the same price. They even offer anchovies. 

In addition to pizza, they have salads. Some classic varieties or make your own. Again, a mini version and a large version. Can't decide? They have a salad on top of a pizza crust! 

They have a couple starters -- one like a garlic bread called "strips" and one like a dessert with cinnamon. The boys liked their garlic strips dipped into pesto. And they even have a cake for their one official dessert. 

If you're looking for a casual venue for dinner at a reasonable price and have kids in tow who like pizza, this is your kind of restaurant.

We were on the way to visit family and stopped here for lunch. Their specialty are boils -- and the presentation is dramatic. Large puffed up with air plastic bags that are filled at the bottom with seafood in a sauce of your choice are presented to the table. You order by weight and the menu is done so they can change the prices to reflect market conditions. 

We didn't have the patience or time to try one of their seafood boils. And I didn't want to smell like garlic butter or Cajun seasoning. So we tried another portion of their menu -- fried seafood baskets. 

We wanted a combo of two types of seafood, but that wasn't offered on the menu. So I ordered their fried oysters and he ordered the fried shrimp and we shared. The fried orders come with a choice of one side. I chose their onion rings and he chose "potato" (it's singular on the menu). 

The food came out in a reasonable amount of time. The oysters were a bit small and tasted preprocessed and pre breaded. They were okay. The onion rings were barely okay. On the other hand, the fried shrimp was wonderful -- delicious in a light flour batter. The "potato" was steamed in sauce and served in a small plastic bag of its own. He opted for a combo of the sauces; the boiled potatoes (2 small ones) were drenched in sauce. 

They also have a separate section of steamed oysters (and scallops) so maybe I'd try that next time we are in the area. The menu has calamari, gumbo, sides, and even salads, along with a couple desserts. 

Service was good. Every booth was occupied so they are certainly popular.

We came here for lunch as the yelp reviews were good and it wasn't too far from our hotel.  I'm glad we got here a bit before lunch hour as they were already full and saying it would be a half hour to forty five minute wait. We opted to sit at the bar which is open seating. 

The restaurant is actually located on the corner and the entrance is on Girod Street. There are tables, the bar seating, and a counter along the windows. The bakery is what you see first when you enter with a number of enticing cookies and small cakes. They even ship their coffee too. 

The lunch menu is small but innovative. Every item is beautifully plated. You can see the chef's creativity in the combo of ingredients. 

My husband chose their meat loaf sandwich. It was a thick slice with a bit of tomato jam and mayo with fried onions on top all served on an onion roll. I opted for their bbq shrimp toast which turned out to be whole peeled cooked shrimp on top of melted burrata cheese on a grilled piece of sourdough bread. It was served open faced on a bed of NOLA style bbq sauce -- perfect for dipping. This bbq sauce is the kind with a base of butter and Worcestershire. So good. I ate it with a knife and fork. The sharp steak knife provided was French and had the cutest little fly design on the handle where you could rest your thumb while cutting. 

They also have pimento cheese, poutine, and an artichoke dip to start; plus a soup and 3 different salads. The burgers looked good. My second choice which I almost ordered was a fried chicken sandwich with Serrano slaw... Guess that's for next time. 

If we hadn't been so full, we would have tried their jarred banana pudding (my husband's favorite). Or maybe their sweet cornbread which comes with butter and cane syrup. It's listed under snacks, but would make a good dessert.

I really don't like writing negative or even so so reviews m, but I was so disappointed in our recent visit here. 

We'd come when they first opened. It had been pouring rain and we were able to linger over our food. That's one of the reasons I remembered how good  everything was.

This time we were looking for a quick bite and decided to stop by on the way back to our hotel. 

I got their regular burger wrapped in a lettuce "bun". The burger was okay and it had almost a quarter of a head of iceberg on either side of the patty. 

I had some of my husband's fries -- they were anemic, undercooked, and just blah.

For a drink I ordered a small vanilla shake. It came with some nasty tasting whipped cream on top. I appreciate that it was dyed pink for breast cancer month (I'm a survivor) but this tasted awful. I scraped it off. The shake itself had barely any vanilla taste. Last time it was over the top with flavor. This tasted like a plain base to add stuff to...nothing more. 

Would I come back here? No. Would I recommend you try it? No.

We came here at the suggestion of some family members with a group including a couple kids. It's a little bit out of the way, but I can see how during warm weather or during the day it would be nice to be lakeside, listening to some live music, etc.

As it was a cool and windy evening, we sat inside. The setting is very rustic. Jeans were certainly appropriate dress. 

Service was good. And the place was busy. Prices aren't too expensive. Our group ordered meatloaf and burgers -- both pretty good. One person had a salad -- just okay; I had a blackened grouper sandwich (passable) and the kids got children's meals which looked a bit skimpy for growing boys. 

I think burgers are the way to go based on our table comments. I definitely wouldn't order the fish I got again. And I'm not quite sure what their specialty or strength is -- I couldn't tell by the menu. It's a bit of a mash up. 

We enjoyed our visit because of who we were with... not because of the food.

We came here tonight as a group of twelve -- having been joined by a family of 4 who are neighbors of our kids/grandkids. 

Luckily we had early reservations -- they don't seat you until the whole party is present, but even though a few people were a few minutes late, it didn't take any time at all to seat us at our own private table. 

First, we gave our drink orders, and our food orders. After we received our drinks, we were served our onion soup and salads. The thin beef broth with onions and a few mushroom slices was served very hot. The salads were crispy iceberg lettuce with ginger dressing. I liked both of them.

Then the actual chef appeared with his cart to begin cooking on the flat grill. If you've been to this type of restaurant, you know there are a number of levels of skill. We were lucky tonight to have a very good, very skilled chef with a wonderful sense of humor. He laughed at all his own corny jokes and charmed the four young boys in our group -- all of whom had never been here before. 

As usual, we had fried rice to begin with, then mixed vegetables, then fried noodles, and finally each of us received our entrees. My husband and I chose the shrimp and steak combination for our "meat".

We've been to Kobe and other similar places many times over the years. I have to say that everything we had this evening was excellent. The portions were huge -- even the kids menu items. The shrimp was flavorful. Our steak was very tender and cooked to the temperature exactly as ordered. Some in the group got boxes to take food home. 

They were very accommodating handling our bills as well. We needed 3 checks and not everyone was sitting side by side. The bills came out perfectly. They also didn't rush us from our table - and there were people waiting. Another nice touch.

I'd definitely recommend this restaurant for any group and would be comfortable returning in the future.

I'm from Florida, and every time I visit family in St. Louis, we have to stop by Pappy's. The ribs, corn, and sweet potato fries here are superb. The ribs are tender, the corn is deep fried, and the sweet potato fries are caramelized with brown sugar. Since I only visit this state like once or twice a year, I don't get to come here often, so I don't know what the other meals are like. However, the ribs, corn, and fries are more than enough to make me want to come here every time I visit. The only thing I would gripe about this place is the sauces they offer.

I also prefer this place over Sugarfire Smoke House, even if it's a farther drive to go to Pappy's and Sugarfire is only 5 minutes away from my family's place. Sugarfire isn't bad, though. I like it also, but Pappy's is a little better. I would rate Pappy's a 9/10 (not a perfect score only because of the sauce) and Sugarfire an 8/10. 

One more thing... they used to get really packed, but they recently opened a new section, so people don't have to wait as much for a seat any more. It was pretty cramped back then. It's not big by any means, but if you go too late you'll have trouble finding a seat AND miss out on the ribs because they only have a limited supply. Once they're out, they out. Get here before noon to be safe.

Whoever said the wait is nothing like Pappy's is a liar! It was about a 45-minute wait on a Saturday. The place is much smaller than Pappy's, so even if you make it through to order, it is hard to find a seat with the very limited seating. Parking is also a hassle for this area. 

We ordered "The Full", which came with a full rack of ribs, 1/4 pound of another type of meat, and 2 sides. 

Ribs: very tender like Pappy's, if not better. This should be the reason you come to this place anyways. I find the sauces a bit better than Pappy's. 

1/4 lb meat: we got the beef brisket, and it was unlike any other brisket I've tasted. It was super tender and very delicious. It's pretty close to the brisket they serve in Texas.

Sides: get the beans!!!! OMG. These were freaking awesome! I'm so glad we listened to a customer who waited in line with us when he recommended this side. The other side we got was the pork skins, which weren't great. I had high expectations for these (maybe because I was ignorant and believed they were going to taste like crispy skins they serve at Chinese restaurants), but they were just typical pork rinds. The customer suggested the slaw, and I think we should have listened to him.  =/

I was a bit skeptical on Indian food, but when I saw the amount of ratings this place had, I decided to give it a try.  The service was satisfactory, and the food was enjoyable. We had the Samosa as the appetizer. It is a type of pastry that has shredded chicken (or pork) inside.  I highly recommend this.

I came with two other people,  and we decided to share our meals.  We ordered:

1.  Chicken Korma (mild) -  lightest of the three entrées with creamy sauce.
2.  Chicken Tikka Masala (mild) -  you taste more of the flavors in this one.  There's actually another dish similar to this one (Chicken Tikka).  The Masala one has the chicken taken out of the skewer and mixed in with a creamy sauce (as explained by our waiter). 
3.  Vindaloo (medium spicy) -  this one had the most kick,  perhaps due to the spice, but it also had stronger flavors than the other two dishes, and it wasn't as creamy. The waiter said if he had to rate the level of spiciness from 1-5, this dish comes regularly at a level 3, and that's what my friend ordered, since the waiter claimed that this dish was the spiciest one of their menu. However, it didn't seem that spicy to me. It's like having a spicy chicken sandwich from Wendy's.
4. Naan (type of bread) - this is not free. However, I would recommend this to dip in the Chicken Korma or Tikkia Masala sauce. Also, eat this while it's hot!

If you're in the mood for something light on your stomach, I would recommend the Chicken Korma. That's what I had. My friend even kept dipping his naan in my dish, instead of his Masala. If I had to go again, I would go for the same thing.

Please keep in mind that there are retarded writers who give *explicit word* reviews. Most of the complaints were based on take-outs and the slow delivery service. I don't believe in Chinese take-outs or delivery anyways (only makes the quality go down). However, if you eat at the restaurant, the food comes out quickly (4 of our dishes came out in less than 10 minutes). Moreover, if you look at the other reviews those idiots gave for other restaurants, you will see that about half, if not all, of their reviews on Yelp are just complaints.

The only person I would say is somewhat legit is Connie C., a fat person who says she "hearts" food and eats at a lot of places. She was upset with this restaurant for not having enough food when the dim sum cart came to her table. They served this style of dim sum at the old location, and they have stopped since they moved to Brandon.

MY REVIEW:
The food here is comparable to popular Chinese restaurants (popular as in the restaurants that Chinese people know to go to for authentic food), IF you order the right dishes. I'm Chinese, and I have gone to many Chinese restaurants in Florida, other states, and Hong Kong. Not to brag, but I can say I know as to which dishes are good and which taste bad. The walnut shrimp, fish with black bean sauce, fried calamari, General Tso chicken, clams with black bean sauce, Hawaiian pork chops, Singapore noodles, and the beef chow fun are tasty. I haven't been there enough to try the other dishes, but what I have tried so far has been good. You should also look into the Thai tea, which is what I always request when I go there.

We chose Home Plate based on all the wonderful Yelp reviews and we were not disappointed.

Located behind a 7-11 in a strip mall where if not for GPS we would of thought we were lost.

When we first walked in we were welcomed with an amazing smell of freshly grilled burgers.

The gal who was taking the orders was so warm and friendly. I wish I would of gotten her name. She handed us a menu which was not as overwhelming as they have a pretty extensive menu printed on the wall behind the grill and a specials menu as well.

They offer burgers, fries, pizza and other types of delicious sounding sandwiches as well as milkshakes. They suggested the tri tip sandwich which was highly recommended by other yelpers.

We all chose the savory brisket burger instead which the chef described as a blend of 3 types of beef.

Served hot and freshly grilled with your choice of special sauce, tomato, grilled or fresh red onions, fresh iceberg lettuce on a warm toasty brioche bun. Cheese and bacon was also an option. I chose all of the above except the grilled onions and may i say it was one of the best burgers I have ever had. 

I also ordered the spicy fried green beans and wow those were delicious as well. Slightly spicy and crispy and served with a side of ranch. The serving is not large but was just the right amount considering I was having that amazing bacon cheeseburger. Lol!

We also ordered milkshakes and we are glad we did. They had the usual vanilla, strawberry and chocolate but also had a white chocolate version which I've never seen anywhere else so we ordered one of those as well as a vanilla and strawberry. May i say they were all delicious but the white chocolate one was over the top yummy.

I live quite aways away but any time I am in that neighborhood again I am planning on going back and maybe trying something else or certainly having that savory brisket burger again.

 I highly suggest the Home Plate as your next dining experience.

Cute shop but not really sure if the drinks are on point. 

Came here for a change of scenery from the every day work from home dullness. 

Found parking on one of the side streets and were able to walk on site without issue. Inside, masks are enforced and when we went, indoor dining was not an option. 

Overall, it's a nice little shop aesthetically, lots of windows and charm creating that cozy corner coffee shop vibe. The workers were very polite and allowed us to take our time going through the menu and making our choices. We got a latte and a cold brew and a muffin to share. Nothing too spectacular from the drinks or bakery item. I also noticed that they have other local areas' items for sale - like quiches and bagels. We had arrived here late afternoon, so all the bagels were all sold out, so coming here in the morning may be a better idea. 

We sat outside while dining, and I found it surprisingly chill. The outdoor space is a pretty spacious and even though the street is pretty busy with foot and car traffic, we didn't feel too confined. 

COVID review: masks required while inside but can take off when seated at their outdoor seating. There are many areas where you can use sanitizer and they have a station with paper towels and cleaner to use to wipe your area down when you leave. 

Might give this place one more whirl and aim for a morning time visit but not itching to go back for the time being.

Great find! 

I've made my away around Chinatown in Philly and though I've found great options - haven't really experienced the same level of Asian-fusion this side of Broad!

SUGA is in the heart of Rittenhouse, so it'll be hard parking wise if you're driving in. I had to park south and take the walk up (which actually wasn't a big deal since it was a nice evening weather wise.) I would advise to prepare for parking if you're driving in and have made reservations. 

Inside it's modern, but subdued. There's a bar that meets you on the right walking in, and there's small tables to the left. When I arrived, the hostess led me up a small set of stairs and towards the back where my party had been seated. 

From the drink menu, I ordered their ginger lotus drink - delicious. I liked how smooth it went down without leaving a alcohol after taste. 

For starters, we had the options of vegetarian dumplings, a charcuterie board of nuts, beets, etc., and small goat cheese won tons. Each item was great. I really enjoyed the goat cheese won tons, and the small bites were a great way to coat the stomach. I enjoy it when the veggie friendly options are plentiful. 

For my entree, I chose the charred cauliflower and ordered the side of charred brussel sprouts - SO good! The cauliflower was tender and easy to cut down to bite sized pieces. The brussel sprouts were a nice accompaniment - they were well bloomed, so they took on the seasonings well. The charred veggies each had a sweet and sour sauce to them - which really paired well with the charred bits. 

For dessert, I ordered the coconut tapioca with mango sorbet. Really refreshing and I love the texture differences that occur when spooning together the tapioca and the sorbet.

The service was really pleasant. They had a few servers always ready to help and our water glasses stayed full (and us hydrated haha.)

Definitely looking forward to my next trip back!

Farm to table - serving good eats! 

Came here on a weekday with some friends for a late dinner. The trek to get to this location was a bit rough - I was traveling from the city during rush hour so took about 40 minutes to reach. 

The restaurant is located in the KoP Town Square portion of the mall district. There is plenty of surface lot parking available. The whole area is fairly new so everything looks shiny and bright. There's also a small courtyard with seating which would be nice on warmer days to enjoy.

Inside the space, it's a bakery/coffee shop on the first floor and the full dining space on the second floor. I checked in with the hostess at the counter after taking the stairs, and then was led to where my party was seated. 

It's a nice hip atmosphere, with good lighting and comfortable furnishings. Our server was ready to offer drink orders and handed me a menu as I sat down which was nice since I was looking forward to getting started. 

I ordered the farmers salad to start - filled with avocados, dates, tomatoes, grapes, almonds, olives - topped with parmigiano-reggiano, and all tossed with a sherry vinaigrette. This was so good! I really enjoyed the mixture of vegetables, fresh and decent portions. The sherry vinaigrette was a nice touch, added good flavor to the whole dish. 

For my entree I ordered the cauliflower steak. The steak was roasted very well - and it fell off the branches easily. It was paired with apples, farro, sautéed greens, and a buckwheat salad. The steak was topped with a tomato glaze. This was awesome! I finished the whole plate. Each bite had great flavor and the portion was perfect, not too much - just enough! 

For dessert, they didn't have any eggless options available. When I inquired, they first served me some ice cream thinking it didn't have any eggs. However, the server had to rush back and let me know that there were egg products used in the making of the ice cream, so I was left with berries. I wish this wasn't the case and am hoping they can include something on their dessert options that's veggie friendly and without eggs. 

I liked the service, our waitress was always good about refilling our waters, and she apologized a few times about the ice cream mix up. I appreciated her diligence. 

Overall - great dinner and a solid option for lots of different cuisines.

Nice find just north of City Hall. It had a decent selection of beers and wine. The atmosphere was fun but subdued. Nothing too hyped up but if you're looking for a good selection of drinks in a spot to hole away into and get away from the more crowded areas of the city - it's a great option! 

Being away from the main action of the city has its advantages. There was ample street parking just steps away which was handy given how windy it was outside! 

The proximity to City Hall is also nice since the Winter Garden was in place at Dilworth Park. If the weather was nicer we would've walked there to check out the different shops. Great location since there is always something seasonal set up at Dilworth Park. 

Would recommend for a night cap or happy hour for sure!

Disappointed. 

This place has been getting good reviews and I've dined in (pre COVID) once before and walked away with great service. 

Tonight was different. My girlfriend ordered take out for us through Caviar and we specifically ordered off their vegan menu. The ordering process was smooth and the turn around time was about an hour - no problem.

We received our food (contact free) within the specified time limit and were excited to chow down. We started to plate our food and noticed that our Tom klong soup had shrimp in it!! We're both vegetarians and this was simply unacceptable. We lost our appetite and also our trust in the establishment. 

Calling them to report this did result in them promising to refund us the cost of the order but our dinner was ruined and we were left hungry. 

It's a shame as we did want to continue to support local businesses during the pandemic. I would advise to proceed with caution when ordering for vegan items. 

Attaching pictures of our receipt of all vegan items ordered and the shrimp containing soup that was delivered to us.

The iconic Philadelphia Art Museum definitely delivers. It's a great way to learn about different art periods and cultures along with being exposed to new offerings that are unexpected but definitely welcomed!

Walking in, the entrance is exceptional. You walk up the steps (yes THE famous Rocky steps) and have a moment to peep the view once you make it to the large landing. Walking in the workers are very welcoming and guide you in so you can register as well as offer different tidbits on the current exhibitions. I really enjoyed the Japanese Tea Garden and Indian exhibit!

I recommend going on a weekend day so you have a good amount of time to peer through the galleries. There are also additional locations you can visit which are accessible via a Trolley! Definitely try to stop by the Perelman Building!

Have fun meandering at this must see Philadelphia site!

All the dogs, all the time! 

This place is nestled at the beginning of UCity. It could be a bit tough parking wise so plan accordingly. I parked a few blocks away and walked over but wasn't too much of a hassle. 

Inside it's cozy, sectioned off into separate rooms along with a large bar area at the opposite end from the entrance. Each room is decked out in dog masterpieces - and depending on the room, the artwork is themed accordingly. It's like walking through a different gallery per room - conversation pieces for sure!

It's a farm to table joint with a nice selection of vegetarian options (yay!) We ordered their hummus for the table - served with kalamata olive tapanade, pine nuts, and fresh grape tomatoes, and I ordered the beet and arugula salad for my meal. It was hearty but not heavy. The salad was tossed with an herby crème fraiche which was a nice savory accompaniment to the sweetness from the beets. 

I thought the portions were perfect - I didn't end up leaving anything on the plate! The ingredients tasted fresh, and overall it was a great dish to enjoy (albeit nothing extraordinary.) 

The service was great, our waiter was quick with delivering out our food and he refilled our water glasses plenty. For the wallet, I thought it was a bit on the pricier side but it wouldn't stop me from coming back. I'm hoping when the weather gets better, we can return and take advantage of their outdoor seating. They also have a pretty decent drink menu - something else to explore for later! 

Enjoy!!

Nice little spot for lunch or dinner in South Philly. 

Came here for a work lunch and was treated well by the staff and the food was a solid - portion and flavor wise. It's pretty easy to find and seems to be a neighborhood favorite. 

Upon entry, we were greeted and were readily led towards the back to our seats. I liked that they were able to accommodate our large group without a reservation. We were all served water quickly and placed our orders soon after. 

I got the house salad and they were able to move a few ingredients out and put others in to make it vegetarian friendly. The food came out fast and ready to eat! The atmosphere is relaxed and casual and can see this as a nice happy hour spot after work or a place to meet up for drinks. 

Parking in the area is tight but can be found in the surrounding streets. We had taken a walk from work as it was a decent afternoon so not too bad to get to on site. 

Enjoy your time!

Brunching is a habit - and this place appeases that disposition in all the right ways!

Came here for brunch on a Saturday and turned out to be a great experience. We had made reservations prior and the table was set for us upon our arrival. The standard brunch drinks along with solid mocktails were flowing. We had some mimosas and even tried their acai feaux-jito!

I ordered a savory dish full of hummus/pita/side salad. My companions ordered their version of the french toast/(vegetarian) monte cristo, and a vegan burrito. 

Everyone enjoyed their food and drinks thoroughly. The food was fresh and well prepared. The serving sizes were great, and I felt satiated without overly full at the end. 

The parking is tight in the area. We parked a few blocks down and made the walk over (the weather was great!)

Will definitely be back for another brunch time adventure!

Morgo's is a solid spot on the water!

With COVID looming on, needed to find somewhere to enjoy a nightcap. Morgo's was great choice to sip on hot drinks while enjoying the view. 

Walking in, we have to show our ID to the bouncer and once cleared, we're met with host station who checked us into our reservation and led us to our table. The space is all open. Some parts are covered, especially the large bar in the middle. The spot and makes for a great all season hang. 

We were seated closer to the water and distanced appropriately from the rest of the patrons to align with the COVID restrictions in place. Everyone working was wearing masks and practicing distancing as best as possible. We were allowed to have masks off at the table but if getting up from the table, we are to have our masks on. 

It was a chilly night so we dressed warmly. Unfortunately, given the open nature of the area, outdoor heating not an option (or so we were explained), so be sure to bundle if coming in during the colder months!

Had a good time and hoping for more here in a more pandemic free nature!

I disagree - Charlie is a Saint!

Great experience last night at this spot. The place appealed to me for their vegetarian friendly options, and has been on my radar for some time. 

It's located right where all the other action is east of Broad Street. Be sure to plan for parking, and call ahead for reservations if you remember. I parked a few blocks south and walked my way up. We were only a party of two, but still ended up waiting a good 20 minutes at the bar before having our table set up. At the bar, we were able to get the attention of a bartender, and he personally stepped out to hand over a bar menu as well as take our order - super awesome! 

You can tell this is a fan favorite, there were lines for a table, at the bar, and even to get service. The last detail is what dings this place from being a full 5 star experience for me. It took more than 20 minutes after being seated (so around 40 minutes since entering the place) before we were presented with menus - and that's only because we had to inquire to have menus brought to us to begin with! That aside, it was busy, and many celebrations were happening so it's still worth the experience, just be vigilant in case the service overlooks you. 

Once we had the food options available, we ordered a few of the plates - the avocado toast, Korean tofu, cauliflower steak, and potato gnocchi. Overall the food was really tasty! We both agreed the avocado toast and the Korean tofu were our favorites. There was a depth of flavor with good use of the ingredients to really let the food shine. There was also this side of rice on the cauliflower dish that stole the show. It was really well developed, with surprise ingredients like raisins - I'm hoping it makes it's way as a main item. If the gnocchi was called something else, our opinions of it would be different. It was more fried than doughy, so it felt like we were eating some expensive french fries. The plates, tables, and portions are small - but shareable for two. 

Overall, I liked the experience, and the story behind the name still eludes me but the intrigue is there. Looking to find my way back here another time to crack that case!

Pizzeria Beddia gets a lot of hype and for the most part it delivers!

Located in the trendy Fishtown neighborhood, the façade is a mix of its previous open air space at the entrance followed by a new, covered, and formal dining space. It's a nice nod to its roots and also it's future.

Of note, reservations are recommended. We had a 9:15pm reservation. We checked in on time but weren't seated until 9:40pm. The service staff were aware they were behind and did their best to keep on schedule. We ended up grabbing some wine and hung out in the outside space. There are heating lamps and picnic tables outside, but it is limited. Since it was a Friday night, for our purposes, it was standing room only. 

Inside is open, light in color, and bright. There are booths available towards the back and a large bar when we first walk in. It is rather raucous inside and the acoustics didn't help, as some times it was hard to hear each other. 

Once seated, our waitress was quick to offer us drinks, the menu, and to recommend an appetizer as it would take a bit for pizza to come out (each pie is baked fresh.) 

The menu is pretty diverse (for a pizza place), with options for many different diets. They also had a special running that night. We ended up ordering the special - a white pizza with shallots and kale, as well as their "angry" pizza - which we were warned was spicy (made with Serrano peppers  in the sauce!)

For an appetizer, we ordered a cheese platter. The appetizer was pretty tasty but the bread it was served with was ill proportioned. The waitress did give us another bowl of bread to help balance it out. 

Once the pizza came out (took about 25 minutes), it was warm and ready to be devoured. The white pizza was very savory but a little heavy on the finishing oil! The amount of napkins necessary does not exist! The "angry" pizza lived up to its expectations - spicy but SO good! 

There were four of us and the two pies definitely left us full with spare slices left. I liked that they hand out aluminum foil when wrapping up to go containers - environmentally friendly. That being said...the pizza is pricy so I'm sure they could afford to option actual boxes to use as to go containers. 

We ended up ordering their espresso ice cream - which really cleansed the palate! We just ordered one helping and extra spoons - it was enough for all of us without feeling like we were in a food coma! 

The service was good and the food was delicious so definitely a place to try and even return to. It is on the pricier side for a pizza parlor, and the wait times can be lengthy - it's not an easy option for pick up and go :(. 

Enjoy!!

This place has been on my radar for some time and it did not disappoint!

I made a brunch reservation via OpenTable and was glad I did! When I got there, a crowd of walk-in patrons had developed deep waiting for a table to open up. I arrived 10 minutes early for my 1:45PM reservation and it was just about ready. While waiting, I had a chance to look around their "market" area at the front end of the restaurant. Their market section is full of great treasures, including their signature cookbook, all sorts of spreads and spices, and a full coffee bar! 

The motif inside is hip, trendy, Middle East breezy. There's intricate tile work interspersed with light colors in  an open concept layout. The place fits well in the Fishtown neighborhood - upscale and relaxed without trying. 

We were seated towards the front middle which was a nice area to catch waiters without having to hail them from an inside corner and it gave us a good view to people watch. 

The menu is full of veggie friendly items, and I took full advantage - ordering a flat bread with cheese, veggies (including the Philly staple "long hots"), over a light tahini sauce. I also ordered their Lebanese chai on ice with almond milk - refreshing (a little sweet but it balanced my savory dish well.) The portions were perfect - nothing on the plate left and I felt satiated but not induced in a food coma. 

A note, there is parking on site! That being said, the lot was under construction when we were dining so I still had to street park (which was fairly easy to find for a Sunday afternoon.) 

The service was really great! Our waitress checked in on us plenty and she was able to address a lot of our questions about the menu. 

I'm really excited about this place and already looking for another excuse to head back!

Wow.

I hardly write reviews anymore and five stars is definitely generous.

I missed the Yelp brunch event today because I was already attending another event in Tampa, but was not interested in the restaurant there. Instead, I wanted to finally cross Filipiniana off my list because I had been to Saigon Deli many times.

They are the Filipino version of Jimmy John's! Everyone was so eager to help. I ordered the beef menudo (weekend special) and a pair of cheese cupcakes to go.

I had just finished signing my e-bill and my food was packed and ready to go. Finishing eating just now.

Omg. The beef menudo tastes like the carnes con papas my Cuban friend used to make me. And the cheese cupcake tasted like pound cake.

So glad I finally tried it! I could come back next time I make it over the bridge.

My family and I came to Smiling with Hope Pizza because a friend of mine heard it was delicious, but most importantly the vision behind this special place. 

Immediately upon walking in you feel right at home. All the staff have big smiles on their faces and are working hard to make the most incredible food! Although I have never been to NY and had the traditional pizza, I imagine this is how it would feel and taste. =o) 

Placed around the restaurant is their Mission Statement: To create hope and meaning in the lives of people with disabilities. I will always hold this place dear to my heart for having "pizza with a social cause." The gentleman who was our server was so adorable, polite, and prompt in all aspects. 

Looking at the menu, my husband and I immediately decided to order all the food....LOL, okay maybe not all the food, but that is what it felt like! We ordered the traditional NY pizza (cheese), garlic knots and dark chocolate dipped cannoli's. 

My family and I thought absolutely everything tasted incredible. Have you ever had something so good, that you just want to eat more and more and more? Well this was my experience. We started with the garlic knots, which by the way came out immediately. I was not entirely prepared for the fact that the garlic knots were cold and not hot. This is something different for me, but WOW were they great, especially dipped in the most tasty marinara sauce. I literally had to stop myself so that I would have enough room for the pizza and cannoli. 

When the pizza came out it was huge and beautiful! I like cheese pizza, don't get me wrong, but I usually like things on it. So personally I was not as excited about this pizza until I took a bite. Holy Moly, did they change my perspective on cheese pizza! Again, so amazing that I had to force myself to stop eating so I had room for desert. 

Now to the cannoli, which I am not even sure I can do justice in words. The dark chocolate, filling, and shell each had an amazing flavor that added to this delectable cannoli. It is something that is a must try if you stop by. My husband stated that not only was everything delicious, but he would come by just for the cannoli! 

Overall, such an amazing place with an amazing purpose. Thank you for all you are doing in our community and I wish you nothing but the best. I know for sure we will be back again!

The reviews about the lady with the black hair were all true.  I told her what I wanted in the bakery case, she didn't listen so she asked again. I then asked what was warm and she very rudely said,"we are busy."  I was the only person in line and they were not busy.  The coffee is good but the scone was doughy.  On occasion we'll pay $16 for two lattes and a scone, but not again here considering obvious rudeness.

I was a patron there this past week when a group
Of white men walked in strapped with multiply guns each, wearing shirts saying "tranny for law, rebellion is duty" 
I actually had a gun too,  wasn't flashing it like I was out of the show "peaky blinders" and wasn't wearing a shirt that is offensive to other peoples lifestyle that is not hurting anybody. This is why we can't agree on the gun laws because some of us are respectful and responsible and some of us act like ignorant babies that feel the need to hurt others to feel better about themselves.  FYI, the food was amazing,bloody's and mimosas on point!!! Love the glassware!

Amazing atmosphere with an inviting patio serving cold beer, warm pretzels, and German-style pub fare. Das Bevo has been restored its historic glory! 

The atmosphere is what sets this place apart and reason alone to check it out.They have bands on the patio regularly, custom fire pits, and an old school fire truck for photo ops. Inside it's a European beer hall, with mahogany wood bar, and event space downstairs. History note: The Anheuser-Busch family commissioned the mosaic tiles in the far end dining room from the 1904 World's Fair.  

Beers are $6-7 and food is $13-20. Not cheap, but you are really paying for the atmosphere. I tried the German board - two sausages, kraut, spicy mustard, warm pretzel, and cheese sauce. The best "value" if your hungry and it filled me up. I wouldn't go for the food alone but overall no complaints. Great spot for a group. 

For a unique experience, Das Bevo is a destination for friends, beers, and good times.

A wonderful quaint restaurant away from the hustle and bustle of the French Quarter. Casual, but stylish, boasting old world charm and attentive service. The menu is all about the classics, which is exactly what we came here for.

Since we couldn't decide between the Crawfish Etouffee, Jambalaya, Laurie, or the Omelette, we order all four in a form of a Crawfish Dinner. Served with a salad. The most striking thing was that the crawfish was perfectly cooked in all four. Supple, juicy, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. My personal favorites were split between the omelet and Etouffee, but I would be just as happy having the Jambalaya with it's aromatic rice or the Lauri. Basically, I just love crawfish! 

The preceding salad was drowned in dressing, but the veggies were fresh and crisp. Additionally, we ordered a fried Soft Shell Crab, which was soggy, but quite flavorful.

I booked a flight to New Orleans after seeing this place on Travel Channel. Best Fried Chicken in America? I'll be the judge of that. Lots of places make fried chicken, but it's easier to do wrong than right. My expectations were very high, and I had no interest in lowering them. Nothing less than exceptional would do.

Located a mile from the quarter near no other attractions, this is something a tourist must really want. A trolley ride and a 10 minute walk through lower class and sparsely shaded but friendly neighborhoods will get you there. Or, you can take a cab if you aren't up for taking in the local feel. I expected a line around the block, but we beat it by arriving before noon. It's a nondescript white building with plain tables, plain chairs, plain everything.

We were directed to wait in a row of seats to be called upon. They just seem to remember the order you showed up in. There's a lot of things on the menu (even salad), but you know what we came for. I ordered a 3 piece meal with a sweet tea. I sat quietly sipping tea, while trying not to stare at anyone else's plate.  One bite triggers emotions stemming from places deep down in places you don't talk about at parties. It's part food, part religious experience. Perfectly moist to the center. Impossibly crispy. Packed with flavor. Why do people people do heroine when they can go to Willie Mae's? Why spend 2 months salary on a wedding ring when there's deeper love waiting for you for just $10?

OK, I've gotten off track. Let's talk sides. The read beans, peas, and mac and cheese where good. They just suffer the fate of being on the same table as the chicken. I'll cop to this being the best chicken around. The sides are a 4 star. The chicken is a 7 star. Go. Now.

Finally getting around to trying some of the new places that recently opened up. Today we went to An Asian Kitchen and Bar occupying the space that was once Cafe de Thia. 
The interior has undergone a few changes. The dripping fountain is gone replaced by a wood Island decorated for Christmas and the colors are much warmer. 
The menu is extensive covering Vietnamese, Chinese and Asian fusion inspired dishes. The spring rolls are available in several ways and are beautifully present with some of the best peanut sauce I have had in ages. 
My Korean style beef short ribs were outstanding. Served with a small bowl of delicately flavored broth, rice and a garnish of salad vegetables. My ever lov'n had the chicken and eggroll vermicelli bowl and was happy with his choice. 
There is much to go back and sample and our waitperson was excellent.

I'm basing this review solely on the happy hour experience we had! Wow amazing! I think this is one of the best happy hour spots Tampa bay has to offer to be quite honest! You can't beat it! This upscale restaurant has a happy hour menu that changes daily. 

My husband enjoyed sitting at the bar enjoying our $2 beers and $3 cocktails! I couldn't believe they had TBBC Moosekiller 12% on draft for only $2 for 5oz! Wow deal of the century! My sangria was also very well made and packed with cinnamon which I prefer!

We ordered the charcuterie board $5 and added 2 cheeses to pair with it (not on happy hour menu only $10) The meats and cheeses were delicious and everything paired very well together. 

The service was excellent, loved the decor, and love this place! Can't wait to come back for some more epic happy hour deals and even dinner if I'm feeling fancy

Met up with with some family and a friend of ours to try this place out. At first you ask yourself why in this dumpy and abandoned shopping mall? But it appears they are working on putting more businesses in here as they should as its a great location. Kind of funny that there are 2 churches next to the brewery but that has nothing to do with the brewery. 

Okay, so when we walked in I was amazed with the amount of space they have for people to enjoy their beers inside and brew beer of course. Loved the art work and murals around the whole brewery. I got a flight of the pale ale, stout, fish water, and the rays. My favorite was the fish water. It was well balanced and delicious! This place just opening has a lot to offer and lots of potential! It's also dog friendly too! Living only 15 minutes from here I look forward to coming here more often!

This was my 3rd visit to Johnny's and I didn't previously review based on that I went there during events so due to the number of people there I didn't feel a review would be fair based on it having a limited menu and slower ticket times. I did remember reviewing the full menu so felt they were worth a visit under normal circumstances. 

We sat at the bar and well, the bartender seemed super annoyed to be there and doing her job. Not just with us, I watched her interaction with others and just thought how I wished we would have sat at a table instead. She was killing the vibe. We ordered are drinks and an app after several minutes of no interaction with her only for a kitchen staff member to come out and tell her they didn't have all the ingredients for it after 10 minutes of it being placed. We ordered the Reuben Egg Rolls to replace it. The people next to us left and suddenly her attitude did a 180. Okay so we narrowed down the problem but still, she wore everything on her face which isn't good for the service industry. 

The Reuben Eggs Rolls came out and we were both surprised. I was expecting an egg roll not a burrito. This could be an entire meal. They were very good and super hot! 

Ben ordered the buffalo chicken flatbread that I think was named something with Johnny in the name. It had a blue cheese sauce and crumbles on it too. I ordered the fish and chips. There were two thick pieces of cod, chips and coleslaw. Everything we ordered was large in proportion size and we both had to get togo boxes. With the pricing, it was surprising and 100% worth it. 

It is worth a stop in for sure for the for sure.

We had been waiting to try this place out for months but you know.... COVID. Finally, we got the chance but sadly this experience wasn't the best. 

The Poke Chips were good, spicy but good and the fish was very fresh. 

I ordered the Chicken teriyaki bowl with brown rice. One thing I thought was unusual was that the rice bowl came with lettuce but I ordered it as is to try it. Sadly, when I got my bowl, the chicken pieces were big but extremely overcooked, dry and stringy. I did try to eat around the chicken for the other items but there was just something off. I decided to not continue to eat and waited for someone to come by. 

Ben's Pho flavor was unique in taste, not bad but not like any other Pho either or us had had before and we couldn't figure out the flavor difference. 

Finally, someone did come by to ask about our food and I quietly mentioned how the chicken was inedible. He offered to take it away and make me a new one but at that point, I was just not in the mood to try again during this visit. He also offered to refund that part of our meal. 

While Ben finished, I assume the owner came by to check on us as well as he had heard about the situation. I appreciate that and he again, offered to make me a new bowl. 

The customer service says a lot.

I am giving this a 3 based on the hopes that other items are better and the place is really cute and I wanted to like it so badly.

With the name The Stone Soup Company, you'd think there would be a lot more soup options, I was surprised to see that there wasn't and the huge menu was almost everything but and the menu is HUGE. There really would have only been one, maybe two other soups that I could consider and was surprised to see some "big ones" missing. 

We went while in Ybor because Ben loves French Onion Soup and I had been wanting to try the place from coworkers reviews. Sadly, though the soup looked great when it came out, it just wasn't there. There were plenty of onions, which they leave in long slices which kinda made it difficult to get a spoonful but also the flavor was really just bland and off point. We actually didn't even finish the bowl that we ordered to share together. 

But like I said, the spot is very unique with awesome artwork and decor, but just not at all what I was expecting and disappointed that a classic like French Onion was so off the mark.

Yay Ciders! A place for me! I was pretty excited for this spot as it was my first cidery that I went to and it was finally all about me vs Ben. LOL. I discovered them when we were at the hockey game the night before as they had a booth with local brewery options where I choose Tiki Tonik.

As this was my first time getting an all cider, I was taken back a little by the cost of the flight but now have learned that is pretty normal. On my flight I had Lil' Blondie, BTC - Bourbon Tart Cherry, Resolution and Striptease but was given little tasters of WeHo, Six One Five, and Bob's Your Uncle.

It is probably a good thing that I don't live close to Diskin or have found them in any stores around here because they have some really great, solid ciders that I would probably have in stock at home.

I stopped by during a leisurely afternoon wandering State Street. It was at 3:04 (the timing here is important) and was seated in a pretty empty restaurant. When my waiter came, I asked for the happy hour menu. He seemed confused and said he had to check if it was 3pm yet. He came back with the happy hour menu and I promptly ordered 3 items - the spicy tuna/salmon roll, lobster slider and 3 oysters. 

Thirty minutes pass and no one checks in on me. I don't mind too much as I have no plans and am content reading my kindle book. At around 3:40, my waiter comes back and apologizes that the kitchen is running behind. Now looking back, that's off as there were only 3-4 other tables with people but whatever.

At 355 my waiter peeks out at me on the empty patio and remarks that my food has not arrived. Now I am getting slightly annoyed, so I ask for my check even without food on the table as I didn't want to be held up any longer by that.   He brings a check and it is full (not happy hour) price. When I ask him to correct it, he seems surprised as he didn't think I had ordered happy hour. Which is concerning as happy hour started at 3 and now it was already almost 4. 

I tell him - you know what, I hate to do this but it's been a long time and I'd like to go on with my day so can we just cancel the order since the food is nowhere to be seen and what was planned as a light afternoon snack is now encroaching on my dinner plans. He says he will check with the manager to see if he can get things to go. Not what I had in mind but I am really just over it at this point. 

He comes back with my 3 oysters and says the manager says that the $6 oysters are on the house but he can't give me happy hour prices because it is now a to-go order (thereby costing me twice as much). Here is where I start to get mad. I point out that I had no intention of getting a to-go order but after an hour here with just a glass of water, I just want to leave. 

I ask for the manager who makes no apologies and indicates that she already gave me free oysters so what more the did I want?  I tell her that I would expect something substantial to eat after being here almost an hour. She then noted that my order was just entered at 340. At this point, I lose it. I note that her waiter blamed it on the kitchen at 340 and that I had been sitting here for 30 minutes  before that. So he was not telling the truth.  And if I truly ordered at 3:40 why is there any debate as to whether it was happy hour or not?! She says he seems to be "flustered" today. 

Finally I just hand her a $20 bill and tell her to charge me for the oysters I ate so I don't "steal" any food and to just let me go. I do not want anything more from here. I then take my change and leave. As I walk out, my waiter walks by with my food. I can't believe I spent an hour plus in an empty restaurant and left hungry. 

I have never raised my voice in a public establishment before. I may whine in private but I hate public confrontation. This was a first. It was a hiccup in what was otherwise a great afternoon.

The place looks soooooooooo pretty you can't help, but to peek in! Can you tell I have two little girls? I honestly thought it would be a place for them, and I was partly right! LOL 

Once you walk-in the center of the bakery does have some pupcakes displayed which threw me off into thinking, "gosh if I took one home and ate it for myself instead of my yorkie, it's o.k. as long as no one knows right"? The lady behind the counter as if reading my confused mind replied only the center had the pupcakes and the rest were for humans! After purchasing the strawberry cake in placed into a cute cup: I still couldn't consume it right away since it's so pretty so I took a picture of it! 

Would go back!
Amazing international selections everything from wine to coffee, deli, bakery, fresh made pastas, gourmet cheese, chocolates.

Gosh sometimes you can take a place for granted and the day you ask for beef tacos and they say sold out is the day your in tears!  Well this is a favorite place of mine,  yeah I like that they're open early so I can have breakfast I love that I can pop in for lunch or a snack or even dinner. The menu here offers so many choices and everything is freshly made.  I have enjoyed so many dishes from the tamales, to tacos and the enchiladas. The charro beans are the BEST I have found in south shore outside of going to Wimauma.  The atmosphere is warm and welcoming and I love the samples, I still can always find something new from a sauce to a drink.  The house chips are plentiful and complimentary and the house salsas are also very flavorful.  Overall a great dining experience from food to atmosphere.  A+

Finally made my stop in here; I have my favorites so it's hard to break the habit and make room for a new comer!  So the owners are Lithuanian and this one cake is my weakness it's graham crackers, condensed milk and some others spices and goodies not named.  Lol even the vegan option is delicious!  So glad I did though I got a lot accomplished this morning from my matcha latte sweetened just right made with my creamy oat milk preference to the chocolaty croissant ice since added to my rituals.  The decor is hip and industrial reminiscent of my recent visit to NYC.  The spot has lots of good vibes from the free wifi to the abundance of seating options both indoor and outdoor.  Even the circulation of air movement with plenty of fans !  Def a worthy stop in and be sure to sign up for rewards program it's so simple and after 5 visits your next one is on them!

Tonight 2/13/2020, Thursday night didn't go very very originally made reservations for 10:30 for a party of 8p and then our party size decreased by 1/2 to 4p.  So we decided to try to come earlier 9:30pm and see if we could be seated.  Turned out that 1/2 the restaurant was empty and there was 3 empty booths and a empty table.  So we asked if we could be seated and the hostess explained that those tables were no shows and they would not open the tables and would keep them empty.

I come here mainly for lunches when it suits me and always have to enjoy a mojito or the freshly made sangria done table side.  The staples for me vary a bit but on my last visit I went with a Cuban sandwich and the 1905 salad.  The atmosphere here is amazing it sits on the water there is a nice sized outdoor patio that you can see the river and enjoy the sights.  Service has always been great during lunch and I recommend the sorbet.  Very flavorful and refreshing.  It connects to the Tampa Bay History museum and with easy walking distance of channelside.

I truly love sharing this wonderful restaurant it's the closest to what I would make myself for a special dinner or around Holidays.  Many of the favorites I grew up with I don't make as often due to amount of time it takes to make some of these dishes.  I think most people forget that the cabbage rolls or pierogi and many other dishes take a long time to create.  Yes they are prepared as much to order as possible and some are made as larger batches that day.  
So if one takes notice all dishes are made to order and flared with care and attention.  Still way homemade and fresher than a bag of frozen machine made pierogi.  The ingredients are always fresh; the food always made from scratch and to your liking like vegan dishes too.  

Service is always warm & friendly and seating is modest and comfortable.  I enjoyed the beef borsht which is a tomato and cabbage based type of hot soup with tender chunks of beef, orders of pierogi as more commonly known fillings include cherry(dessert choice) potato, or what I ordered this visit the cabbage & cheese vareniki.  Also seen as pierogi to most are meat options for fillings like pork, beef or lamb pelmeni, and a more common breakfast item the salmon (potato pancakes)draniki.  Finished with a lovely Napoleon a flaky layered dessert with sweetened cheese but not too sweet.  
Truly authentic Russian/Ukraine cooking and always a pleasure to dine with.  Staff is wearing masks & gloves as needed with sanitizing between customers.  You may BYOB; with a $10 opening charge.

Delicious if you're in the mood for Peruvian food this is it.  Food is traditional you can always call ahead there's a few boots a little bit of a smaller set up and a bar area. Some other spots have dance floors but the food is definitely worth it here.

Me and some girlfriends stopped in here for a few sweets !! Cute walk up, they offer Japanese style street soft serve in a adorable taiyaki cone.  Alongside shakes & cookies.  They have a delicious Nutella stuffed cookie that is salted chocolate chip with Nutella sandwiches between.  Fruity pebbles, gummy worms , CBD chocolate chips salted chocolate chips cookies are among a few favorites to choose from.  Sleazy brownie sounds like a dream or a damnation haha with its layers of cookie dough, Oreos and brownie batter.

Came for a girls lunch and we just enjoyed the food, drinks, and the vibes.  We ordered clam chowder 
To start with it has a great presentation came out with two little necks in a thick and creamy base.  My girlfriend order soup and salad and ended up with full dinner salad.  I initially ordered the skirt steak wrap and unlike a steak you can't see the marble edge of grizzle until you bite into it.  So I couldn't enjoy the lettuce wraps after having to spit one into my napkin, my gap reflex kicked in.  I decided to sent it back and our waiter was so understanding brought k we the manager and we choose the spinach, gorgonzol,, dried cranberries walnuts,  salad.  I added the blackened scallops for a addt'l $16.  The service is wonderful our waiter graciously accept the changes and adjusted our checks.  Everything was greet in presentation and taste and temp.

Surprisingly for all the bad reviews I think I waited long enough to try the food here.  Me and a couple of girlfriends met up for Thursday night dinner and drinks. Made a reservation ahead of time so it was very smooth a check in got seated right away cute little table on the deck facing the river. Even had one of those coconut umbrella for shade great vibes here felt like you were in Polynesian Island. Lots of neon lighting trimmed the deck and the water fountain wall was nearby.  
We sat behind the live music stage and couldn't hear his name but he played a mix of country and rock.  Enjoyable to have live music again!

Ordered the island time dockwich $13.99  asked for a bun less burger to be on that and a side of watermelon. Very pleased with my food another friend of mine had the peel and eat shrimp which is also seasoned really well I wasn't in the mood for the messiness of that especially with my manicure. 
Our waitress was very attentive tho not too talkative; but I think that's because she was very busy being stretched between the deck at about eight tables at that time. I ordered a few of the sneaky rum runners $10 which I get the sneaky part now very tasty!  Definitely will come back!

This place was either a coma from sugar or the liquor !!!  Such a cute place from burgers to steaks and milkshakes this is what many would say is a burger and milkshake spot for all.  If your celebrating a birthday then definitely a fun experience with the whole staff groove and shake it with a dance party.  The place comes alive with lights flashing and the staff join in the party to celebrate with you!  We had a great time celebrating here from the fun drink goblets and sugary candy toppings, the fantastic presentation.  Can't go as high a 5-stars mainly due to some hiccups w/ a few things but plan to return for sure and hang with some friends again.
