Service is always downhill at the bar and the table wait here is extremely long.  Bartender tonight was unbelievable for Thursday.  She didn't even put my order in at all and then when I asked about it 20 minutes later she said we don't have any of those things you ordered !! Wth? 
So I asked her a simple water and the next thing she did was take another bar order.‍ How rude.   I then decided to leave and then 29 minutes later I find out my water was delivered to another friend that was still at the bar.  Really M.Bird ??? Unacceptable

This restaurant wasn't so accommodating after we arrived to get our order they weren't expecting us and we had to go inside and wait some.  Also upon my check in I tried to use a yelp offer and they refused to honor it because I wasn't not dining in ! Wtf?  Really it's a pandemic and would allowed me to use. 

Then to make things worse they don't even bother to keep their Hair out of my food . Do Not Eat here 

I won't be back

PYT definitely has a lot of variety I'll give them that but the food here is just medicore. Ordered a PYT burger and yes it was juicy but it lacked flavor. They put way too much mayo on the PYT burger.. it was literally going all over the place (it actually didn't even say on the menu there was mayo). The waffle fries that came with the burgers were at least decent but still not worth the $12.

The service here is subpar - it's slow and our waiter was not attentive at all. He pretty much just took our order and gave us our food and that was it. We had to get up to get the check and pay.

Bathrooms here are pretty disgusting. There is also only one co-ed bathroom with multiple stalls which can be a bit uncomfortable for some. Don't think I'll be coming back.

I have been here several times, but this was the first time since they've been under new management. I usually go to Petra or Zeko's, but this was more along my route. The new decor was quite a pleasant surprise. The dine-in part is small but can easily accommodate a medium-sized party. The service was generally good. Keep in mind that they automatically add a 15% tip to all checks!

Now on to the food, I ordered the chicken kofte. The accompanying Greek salad was fresh and flavorful. I sometimes find that Greek dressing ends up being mostly oil, but this one had a good citrusy zing. The kofte itself was served on rice with a yogurt sauce. The kofte were very flavorful and had a pleasant tang. The texture was tender and complemented well by the chopped, aromatic vegetables inside. I will definitely plan to come back and try some other dishes. They have a large menu with everything from wings to Cajun pasta, and the prices are very affordable.

Matzo Ball Soup. Say that with me, please. Matzo Ball Soup... ohhhh yes!!

I've been wanting to try this place for a while now, but since I rarely find myself in casino's, I just kept forgetting to go check them out. My daughter and her family came into town and stayed at the Atlantis, so after an afternoon of swimming in the pool, we decided to take the kids and go eat. 

What took me so long, to come here????

I ordered the matzo ball soup and a half egg salad sandwich on rye bread, toasted... O.M.G.!!! So simple, and so TASTY!!! Their soup tastes like they get up in the morning, pour a ton of love in the pot and slow cook it all day so it can extract all of the goodness it can possibly muster. The matzo balls are so delicate and perfect, I caught myself more then once closing my eyes and savoring the bites... quietly saying out loud "Mmmm!".  Must. Have. Again.!!!! The food is so simple, yet delicious!!!

Our server was super friendly and outgoing, you can tell that he REALLY loves his job... no one can fake it that good! LOL  I wish we had gotten his name, I'm sure he gave it to us but I was too distracted and admit that I'm a very bad person for not remembering.  :-(  I really think that more people should be going here though. They are THAT good, and they have plenty of seating. Take a group, go have great food with excellent service!!

I almost gave this rating a 4-star... but the more I think about it, no. They really truly deserve a 5-star. They are THAT good!

I was checking out Reno Foodies yesterday, on Facebook... someone posted a photo of the most gorgeous looking bread, and credited it to Rounds Bakery. That led me to check them out here on Yelp... and the pictures... and the reviews... and they're RIGHT around corner from me!

That's it... make the daughter get dressed, slap a leash on the dog (he loves car rides), walk out into the wonderful rainy morning air... we're OFF!!

I find Rounds very quickly, and in we go. The smells when we walked through the door... heavenly! We were immediately greeted, but not rushed when we took our time checking out the menu boards and looking at the pastry case. Ohhh the smells that were taunting us, YUMM!! I love the smell of coffee, and that was wafting through the air along with the smell of fresh bread... it was amazing!

I finally settled on the "Black and Blue" on a Jalapeno Cheese bagel. My daughter got the "Ultimate BLT" on a plain bagel. Then we ordered pastries and drinks... and off we went, home with the dog to enjoy our new discovery.

The Black and Blue... while it was good (I love blue cheese!), I liked my daughters Ultimate BLT much better (we swapped halves of our sandwiches). The creamy spiciness of the sriracha mayo, the hard cooked poached egg, the mouth watering bacon, the avocado my daughter had them add... all DELICIOUS! Thinking about this even now, makes my mouth water!! We'll be going back, and trying the rest of their menu, one sandwich at a time... I wonder if they make Pretzel Bread there.... hmm...

Cheers!!!

I found this place on Yelp and decided one day a month or so ago, on a whim, to check them out. There is almost NO places in Reno (that I can find) that has fresh Dim Sum. 

It's a little hole in the wall bakery, and the owner is really friendly! When we walked in the first time, it smelled SO good inside... and when I commented on it, he told me he had been in the back making his lunch! LOL I want some of what he was having!!

Because of the whole COVID-19 thing, they appear to have a lot of their stuff down inside, but oooohh man!! They have a huge variety of Chinese Buns! I didn't take any pictures the first time I went, and today my daughter went in for me, so again I didn't get pictures of the buns... but we had tried the BBQ Pork, Curry Chicken and Teriyaki Chicken buns. They were so good!!

Tonight we just got the Mushroom Shu Mai, and the Shrimp Shu Mai. So tasty, my mouth is salivating as I write this! I just knew I had to get this review out right now, so I stopped stuffing my face long enough to praise this wonderful tiny slice of Heaven in Reno! 

If you haven't been here, DO IT!! We knew what we wanted so called ahead and ordered it. They have other Dim Sum options as well, these two just happened to be our favorites and since we were making Chinese Black Bean Clams for dinner, we caved in to the yummy!! LOL

Having read that they were not brewing yet kept me away for a while. And I am sorry that I stayed away so long.

Now I have been twice and so happy to say that this place is great. The space is huge. On one of my visits there was a meet up for a bike ride going on with a whole lot of people but there was still plenty of room for more. I would be tempted to put up a wall and limit the space some but all in all I didn't feel at all uncomfortable. 

There is a shuffleboard game, pool table and even a throw back Pac Man machine. I really hat the blue guy in that game.

The tables and chairs are roomy and comfortable. My first visit was on the return from a long bike ride on the Monon. (some bike parking would be a nice improvement). We were not interested in a big meal and were hoping for something small. We started with a Gazpacho (special dish for the day) and it was really super. And then, wow, were we happy when the charcuterie and cheese plate was brought to the table. It is server on a dark gray slate that just makes a great presentation. The Capocollo was phenomenal.

The Capocollo was so good that I made it a point to visit again the very next weekend. I had the Italian sandwich and again the Capocollo was the star. 

The beer offering is craft and a wide range to provide beer for all tastes.

If you haven't been to Bent Rail then I encourage you to visit and judge the place for yourself as I finally did.

Heard good things about Relais so off we went.  Met all expectations, the fresh salad tasted as if had just been picked, and it probably was, since they source locally.  The wild salmon was cooked to perfection.  Stellar service delivered by a capable caring staff who made sure we were well looked after.

What a great dining experience.  They are open for lunch on selected days and luckily today was one of them.  Started with the manhattan style lobster chowder and so different from other places it was literally swimming with lobster including whole claw meat as opposed to the salty lobster whisperer and not one mushy potato to be found.  Awesome! The wedge was chunks of blue cheese and large pieces of bacon on really crisp lettuce as opposed to the bacon bit whisperer which also sucks. Awesome twice! The ahi salad had so much flavor we are thinking why don't we come here more often, well duh we live in Tahoe.  Seriuosly service was awesome, thank you Mike, and it was a fabulous meal from start to finish.

TL;DR -- Messed up our wedding reception big time. Terrible communication. No leadership, no one took responsibility, no one made it right. Terrible experience.

My bride and I booked the private room at 360 Bistro months in advance for our small wedding reception. We had been there previously to try it out, and their food and service were top notch (if exorbitantly expensive), so we thought it would be a sure thing.
Let me start by saying, anyone who has ever been married or planned a wedding knows that there is so much that goes into it. So much planning, so much money, and when things don't go right it can be heartbreaking. Thus begins the tale of our experience at 360 Bistro.
About a month out from the wedding, my bride calls 360 to just make sure everything is still good to go. They inform us that the person we had been dealing with no longer works there and they have no idea what we are talking about. So we showed the the correspondence between us and them and they agreed to honor the terms. It seemed like crisis was averted. Fast forward to the night of the wedding.
We arrive post-ceremony to find that they had booted us out of the private room. No call, no email, no communication of any kind. They not only did not have us set up in the private room, they put us back in the corner in the server's prep area. They didn't even have enough tables or chairs set up. So here we are, us and our wedding guests wondering what in the heck is happening. Immediately we begin to ask what is going on. The manager never came to us to talk to us. She simply ignored that we were there. The wait staff tried desperately to cover, but they knew it was wrong. They stuffed us in to this tiny corner where I didn't even have enough room to pull the chair out for my bride to sit down.
Appetizers were already supposed to be prepared (we specifically asked and had someone come early to make sure they were ordered), they weren't. So all of us had to wait for those. The food was delicious as we knew it would be and the servers, while it appeared that they had never been to a wedding or hosted any sort of party there ever, did an admirable job with the debacle. On top of all of the aforementioned gaffes, they informed us that they would be charging us $2.50 PER SLICE of our own wedding cake that we brought which was not previously disclosed to us. They then proceeded to take the cake without even asking us and cut it into GIANT pieces. This was a cake made to serve 40-50 people. They cut it into 20 slices. Hundreds of dollars down the drain as no one could finish their cake. To top it off, they did not leave any for my bride and I to have! Imagine having to console your new wife who is in tears over all this, and not a manager in sight to even apologize for confusion.
To end the night we asked for some satisfaction. We were told succinctly that we would not be receiving any sort of discount and were required to pay the full price. After the huge amount of money we spent, one would think we would get at least an apology from the manager. We did not.

As you might imagine, I will not be patronizing their establishment again and will actively encourage others to dine elsewhere.

More like Bison Bitch's, what an awful experience. 

I was so excited to spend time with my friends after a long work day and watch the U of A game, waitress 'lost' our food order. After 30 minutes we checked in on status, bartender said he will look into it, 20 minutes later we follow up with bartender who tells us they lost our ticket. An hour and a half later we get 2 orders of nachos. When I asked the waitress and bartender if they can make it up to us, the bartender immediately starts screaming at me and says "just for that, he won't help me".

I asked to speak to the manager to which he replies: he is the manger (which he isn't). After a 5 minute screaming match I walk out to the main bar area and ask to speak to a real manager and to explain how I was treated. The manager comped one of our orders but I was so furious I left without eating my dinner.

I will never return, terrible service no apologies for terrible treatment. I never want to be yelled at by a little man at bison bitch's again.

A friend suggested that we share dinner and indulge our mutual love of excellent meats, so we headed over to Texas de Brazil for an exceptional dining experience.  The atmosphere is elegant, with nice lighting that's perfect for a romantic teta-a-tete dinner :-)

They charge a single, surprisingly reasonable price for both the salad bar and limitless helpings of all their incredible meats.  While the salad bar is elaborate enough to be a meal by itself, I suggest that you go easy here and save room for all the MEAT!!

Once you're seated in the dining area, servers dressed like Brazillian Gauchos walk around carrying a huge cross-section of meats, which they'll cut to your size and doneness specifications.  The meats available include Parmesan chicken, flank steak, sausages, filet mignon, lamb, and many more!

Tip: They provide a disk on the table which will theorically control the arrival of new meat offerings.  Flip the disk to red for stop, and green for go :-)

This is a restaurant where you need to make sure you come hungry because you will leave so full you will need to go for a walk!

We went to Happy Fish for dinner recently and were absolutely floored by their incredible Peruvian food!

Tucked away in the corner of a strip mall, the venue's atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the service is first-tier.  Our server was attentive, polite, never overbearing and always smiling. He explained many of the dishes to us, and gave us some spot-on recommendations.

We shared the veal hearts appetizer, and two entrees - the mixed sea food main course and the seared tuna.  Everything was fresh, wonderfully prepared and completely delicious!

I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this place, and look forward to returning :-)

The chicken wings are really fatty tasting. I ordered take out and the order was wrong. They were out of the watermelon drink so I got some blue drink that was really sugary and not what I wanted. I got cheese fries and no cheese was on my fries. I also got no ranch dressing for my wings. I ended up throwing my meal in the trash. Won't be back.

What is going on here is a tragedy. 

I visited this place last summer for a "happy hour" type of event with half off appetizers. The appetizers  (3) that I ordered all tasted stale, like they were made yesterday and hence the whole "half off" deal. 
I was soo disappointed. My mango mojito (or was it peach) was on point tho.
I vowed not to return because I was just turned off by the food.

So they changed the name and the management and so I figured let's give it another go...uhm, big mistake.

1) I ordered regular margarita...tasted salty. I asked for my nice waiter to add some pineapple or ANYTHING to make it better, he gave me a little cup of the sour mix thing that margaritas are made of...so I just added it to what I was drinking which made it a bit better.
Now it was hot as balls in the place and for some reason or the other my ice was melting really fast in my drink...so I ended up with a warm'ish drink. 

2) I ordered a virgin pina colada next....i can make better with my home blender...but I guess that's not their fault that I'm Queen of Pina Colada making

3) Cornbread....I actually enjoyed this because it was sweet. However, it wasn't baked evenly OR there was something wrong with the way the fat/butter settled in the mix. Some parts looked saturated with fat/butter/sweetness...and other parts were nice and dry like a bread/cake should be dry. Either way I ate it cause it was sweet.

4) The biggest disappointment- MY entree. I went with the short ribs. It was 60-70% fat...the kind of fat that you can see and you just wanna cut off cause it's just all white and soft and ek! 
I was partially grossed out, partially just annoyed at the work I was doing to avoid a mouthful of fat.
My friend had the rack of lamb which I didn't want to order cause I thought THAT would be fatty...BAD decision. The lamb was actually very good (I tasted hers)...so if I have to recommend a dish, I'll say the lamb. 

So at the end of the day...I just don't think this place cuts it. Maybe my taste is just way up there (I really don't think so). I guess if the prices were 80% less I wouldn't be soo disappointed but with the price I'm expected to pay, I really thought the food would be a bit better but it's not. 

I don't know...I wish the place well.

Honestly, I believe Nina's could have went outside, put dirt onto my waffle, and I would have given this place five stars...  The liege Belgian waffle was possibly the best liege waffle I've ever had.  It's not called Nina's Ice Cream and Waffles, no they know what they are selling.  This is Nina's Waffles & Ice Cream.  

We're helped by friendly staff and they offered some suggestions.  I love ordering freshly made waffles, but at the same time, I absolutely hate the wait.  This place had it down to a science.  Quickly, my waffle was in a paper bowl, with mad crack ice cream scooped on top.  I haven't mentioned yet about the amazing waffle smell this place had, but it was so much better right in front of my face.  I took a bite of the waffle and was so happy.  The biggest high of the day for me.  Super impressed.  

I'm kinda depressed as I write this though, because I will never truly know how good their ice cream is and I'm not sure if I care.   This place is so far away from me, and we will make the drive back, but I will never be able to just get ice cream.  Some times I want a milkshake, some times I want a cone...  Not here.  I want that waffle first and they can put whatever ice cream they want on there.  The warm waffles with that cold ice cream was magical in my mouth.  They know they are on to something here.

I've had a Po'boy here, but let's not talk about a meal I've eaten here...  Let's discuss me ordering King Cake's every year.  I have a King Cake shipped from the New Orleans area every year.  Okay, almost every year...  My wife is going to read this and tell me I didn't order one when I was two years old... Back to the King Cakes... I wasn't fully feeling them in recent years, so I've tried some other places and even made my own last year.  This year, I was talking to co-workers and thought about local places.  I knew a place in Reading Terminal Market, didn't recall the name, but after some quick yelp searches, remembered it was Beck's...  I reached out to them and inquired about the King Cake on Instagram.  After a small conversation, I placed an order.  On the day to pickup, there were a lot of King Cakes there.  I was given mine and I got a quick peek before paying.  

"Wow" was seriously my first thought.  I think every company from New Orleans ships with FedEx, along with special FedEx boxes.  They're almost all the same...  None, that I've found, were this large.  Those are smaller, I'm sure for shipping reasons, and sometimes filled with custard, but this was so much larger.  

I personally loved the flavors so much more.  The sugar topping, which is usually too much for me, was more balanced on the Beck's King Cake.  I enjoyed the more brioche like center.   The only complaint I received, was that someone said theirs didn't have a filling in it...  I think they wanted custard...  Which another co-worker won't eat, because he doesn't eat cream cheese...  Even though I don't think there is cream cheese in the Bavarian custard we sometimes get?  I don't like people...  Why do I get these things for everyone?  

Forgetting the "extras" that goes inside, this was a fantastic King Cake and probably the best value I've gotten.  These cakes were decorated nicely too.  You can do that when you aren't depending on FedEx to ship...  I can baby, get it, this cake filled with a baby, all the way back to the office in my car.  I wouldn't be surprised if this is the place I go for now on...  It's more work on my behalf, but I think it's worth it.  I'll just get a tub of custard and fruit fillings and let people dip in the future...  Just to shut them up...

I fell in love with this place in 2000 or 2001, a few years before the movie National Treasure, had a chase scene here.  The Reading Terminal Market was the first place where I learned you didn't need to buy everything from a grocery store.  I ordered amazing meats at the butcher and bought fresh produce.  Over the years, when I worked close by, I frequented this place multiple times a week and there are always great places to eat.  

I've been here for private parties, weddings, and just whenever I can get the chance.  DiNic's is one of my favorite sandwiches in the world, so I spend most of my time there.  I love the Pretzels in the market now too.  So buttery good.  Check this place out if you are in town.  A ton of tourists join locals here, but it's worth it.

D'alessandro's is absolutely legit. A no nonsense small corner joint serving up huge, soft hoagies filled perfectly tender and juicy beef. Actually filled is an understatement. These things pack a load of meat. The toppings are numerous. While most places are traditionalist, D'alessadros gives you the freedom to add all types of extras. The fried onions add the perfect balance of sweet and crunch. 

Ok I have a confession that hopefully won't get me shunned: the first cheesesteaks I ever had in Philly were at....Pat & Geno's. In my defense, I knew they were tourist traps before I made the leap. But sometimes you do things for the sake of ticking the box on the bucket list. For what it's worth, those were terrible cheesesteaks. 

Easy to see why this is a Philly fav: Super speedy service, fair prices, and food quality beyond reproach. Now, if we could only get rid of that whole "cash only" thing....

I love seafood. All seafood...fish, shrimp, crabs, crawfish, shoot I even like alligator.  The one exception to this has always been oysters. I never did enjoy them cooked anyway...fried, smoked, boiled or raw. Nope. No dice on the oysters.

Until someone convinced me to try them at Drago's. The charbroiled oysters are one of the most delicious things I've ever had the pleasure of tasting. I was in heaven eating them and have been back several times since that first time to order them again and relive that first time I had them.

Let's face it, if you were a hater of all things oysters and Drago's completely changed your life...err...mind about oysters, well then you've got to admit that they know what the heck they are doing and they do it damn well.

For charbroiled oysters, Drago's is the best. There is no comparison.

I LOVE me some breakfast food. Love, love, love. It's the most important meal of the day and my favorite. New Orleans has a lot of great restaurants but the great breakfast places are few and far in between, I find.

Hello, Wakin' Bakin' and welcome to my world! Unpretentious and friendly service had me from the start. The food sealed the deal.

I just love this cozy (read-small) restaurant. It's flipping awesome. Walk in and order at the counter and grab a cup of coffee and utensils at the little coffee/utensil station and have a seat. Your food will be brought out soon to you. Smile and dig in. It's goooood!

The hash browns are amazing and the breakfast club was out of this world. Turkey, ham, tomato and bacon topped with Swiss and fried eggs? SOLD! 

Oh, did I mention they are super affordable? Like I said, welcome to my world, Wakin' Bakin'. I know this will be a really great romance between us :)

The only thing that I like about Pat O's is the piano bar. Spending a few hours in there is fun and very entertaining. The pianists really know their stuff and get the crowd going. That is awesome.

Everything else is not. It's crowded. I hate crowds.

The signature drink is a Hurricane. I hate real life hurricanes and I hate the Hurricane drink just as much. Would you like to wake up with the worst headache of your life? Drink a couple of Hurricanes. 

They have bathroom attendants. I hate bathroom attendants. I can get my own towel to dry my hands off, thankyouverymuch. 

It's filled with college guys who think they are God's gift to women. I hate college guys who think they are God's gift to women.

All that being said, it should be on a bucket list for anyone coming to New Orleans for the first time. Stick to the piano bar, though.

I have to admit the idea of a fancy hot dog joint seemed pretty silly to me. I hadn't  bought into the hype until yesterday when heading to another place only to find them sold out and closed. 

I love the funky and colorful decor of this place. It just puts me in a Caribbean state of mind. But instead of having a cheeseburger in paradise I was having a hot dog in paradise. Ha.

I ordered the alligator sausage dog and had it dressed "chefs choice" which is where you trust the chef to top your dog with a perfect mixture of toppings which turned out to be great choice. Interesting side note about ordering it chef's choice. My friend and I got the same alligator sausage and ordered them that way and they came out two different ways. When our waitress came to the table with them she sort of sized us both up and then decided which to give me and which to hand to my friend. Definitely a different kind of dining experience, but so fun!

One more thing. WHITE TRASH FRIES. Get an order to share and prepare to fight over the very last deliciously covered fry. Trust me. They are worth every calorie.

I've got mad, mad love for the Rouses chain in general. My grandmother worked and retired from the very first one opened in Houma. I have so many fond memories of visiting her while she was working behind that bakery counter. That store to this very day is still my favorite one. This location is giving it a run for it's money though.

This Rouses is super cool! Oh my goodness. I was surprised seeing it in the Quarter and was in awe walking in. It looks tiny but it's not. It's got everything you'd find in your neighborhood Rouses. I love the narrow aisles and the liquor behind the counter. It feels like an old timey drugstore. I love it!

This would be the perfect place for all the ingredients you need for a fabulous Bloody Mary. Or dinner. :)

Boiled shrimp, corn and potatoes. Awesome.
Onion rings. Awesome.
Shrimp Poboy. Awesome.
Atmosphere. Awesome.

You get the point. This place is badass. The food is excellent, the service is so friendly (like you're in a a family member's kitchen) and the no frills atmosphere really kind of adds to the entire experience. It felt like home. I was in very good company with my Westbank tour guide and I loved every moment. 

Seriously one of the best meals of my life.

How awesome is Mojo? When the line is usually out the door every time you pass by, I would geuss that it's probably pretty damn awesome. I was right.

The vibe is laid back and cool, the baristas are friendly and helpful and it seves the best iced coffee I have had. I have also had a few chocolate flavored frozen coffee from here and those were fantastic too. 

I love all of the local art and locals publications that you can look at while waiting for your order. I love that Mojo is local itself. I love how affordable they are. I love all the cute outdoor seating on people watching heaven Magazine Street.

One big con...it's small and always crowded. If you so much as think of wanting some elbow room, you'll probably hit the person standing next to you. But, hey, you may not mind that. I just happen to dislike people invading my personal space.

Stop in and give Mojo a try if you haven't. It may become your new favorite coffee shop.

So there's this guy in my life. He's sexy and funny and is pretty much every girl's dream come true. But there was one little thing wrong. He kept trying to introduce me to Vietnamese food. I was all like "look, Mr. Fantastic. It ain't going to happen." And he was all like,"look, woman you need to broaden your horizons or else."

WHAT WAS WRONG WITH ME!?

I didn't know what I was really missing out on until we went to Dong's. We had a bahn mi here (roasted pork for me) and that was great but what blew me away was the pate chaud. Oh. My. God. Picture this...puff pastry stuffed with grilled pork and onions. I am still dreaming of that thing. I'm not even kidding. And the varieties they have was pretty much astounding. Chicken and grilled onions, chicken and water chestnuts, grilled pork, shrimp. Just stop reading and go get one now! Get several. That thing was so freaking good I wanted to go back in and buy like ten more but I didn't want them to think I was a cow. 

Writing this review makes the craving worse. I'm going there today! Don't buy up all of my pate chauds!  

By the way, they have beautiful cakes. And now I want one of those too.

It seems like everyone is jumping on the BBQ craze that has been taking over New Orleans and I am very ok with that. Bring on the smoked meats! 

While I pledge my BBQ allegiance to The Joint and NOLA Smokehouse (RIP) Blue Oak is bringing something just as good and a little extra to the table. 

We went around 1:30 one afternoon for lunch and not only did they still have brisket (yes!) they weren't out of anything, which we were a little worried about. We ended up choosing the brisket plate which came with two sides (mac and cheese and potato salad were our choices) and we were just going to split that but I couldn't stop looking at the brisket nachos on the menu. When I inquired about them the guy behind the counter pointed out a table that had just ordered them and I was sold. Ok, I love bbq and I love Mexican style food and just the thought of those combined peaked my interest. Well, I was not disappointed. They were loaded with tender, perfectly smoked brisket, jalapeños, pico de gallo, queso and bbq sauce. They were out of this world delicious! My only complaint is that I wish they had layered the toppings a little more since we were left with some empty chips on the plate after devouring the top layer. 

The brisket plate was very good. My guy got a combo of lean and regular. Very good, no complaints here or from across the table. I was a little underwhelmed by the sides, but really the focus should be on the meat here and they are firing on all cylinders in that category. 

Try the brisket nachos! I know I'll be back for those again.

I'm hating writing this review because I expected so much more. 

I'm a huge Breenan's fan but you guys...this place disappointed like no one's business. This was a Christmas celebration for us and it just fell flat. Way flat. 

First of all, we came here specifically for the turtle soup. Not on the menu. Huh? Apparently there is a turtle shortage. This was my first time hearing this and since I'd been looking forward to the soup all week I was a little more than let down.

Secondly, I have to echo the sentiments of my friend Charles. H. "WHY ARE WE WAITING?" We are locals, we don't expect special service by any means, but seeing tourists treated like royalty while the people in your backyard are more than willing to spend their hard earned dollars, and, may I mention way more often than tourists ever will is very off putting. We waited for the wine for much too long, waited for each course for a little longer than expected, the check arrived 15 minutes after requested and were ignored by our waiter for long stretches all throughout our meal.

We ended up getting the Reveillion menu. The soup was spectacular but as for the other courses. Ehh.

Ok, ok. I so get the hype now.

I could shuck oysters, peel crawfish and devein shrimp by the time I was 5. My grandfather was a fisherman, so that's just how it was in my family. By the age of 10 I could fry frog legs and cook alligator. I'm southern Louisiana through and through y'all.

One day my dad got a BBQ pit with a smoker and started experimenting with smoking a brisket. It took a few tries but he perfected brisket and still to this day is the best I've ever had. 

The Joint comes very, very close to my dad's brisket and that's really saying something. The brisket here is sooooo tender and juicy. Oh wow. I just loved it. I loved the three different sauces on the brisket...the mustard-y one being my favorite. Did I mention the sides? The potato salad is really good and the green salad comes with some sort of dressing that I'd knock down someone to get more of.

In the seafood paradise that is New Orleans, The Joint is a welcome change and does it very well. Nicely played, The Joint. Very nicely played.

Oh how I love The Rusty Nail. This bar in the awesome Warehouse District is the the bees knees, y'all. The front area of the bar is pretty crowded but the patrons are cool as hell and if you get a little claustrophobic up front, there's a super cool area in the back with a bunch of tables where you can sit and chat with new friends and old ones. 

The drinks are cheap, the Bloody Mary is spicy and strong and full of those luscious green garnishes y'all know I love.

Even better...there's a huge outdoor patio filled with lush, tropical plants and trees and plenty of seating for everyone. Do yourself a favor and check this place out. I'm sure you'll love it like I do.

Oh, and speaking of the bees knees... the last time I was there I could have sworn I saw a very tall beekeeper molesting a tree. It was very strange, to say the least. I guess it could have been those bloody Mary's, but I really don't think so. It was so real. That poor tree. Bad beekeeper!

I absolutely love Greek food. I could live on hummus dipped in pita bread alone and die happy. Don't even get me started on chicken shawarma stuffed into said pita bread and filled with yummy lemony hummus. Oh. My. Goodness.

But I have to agree with Harry here. The food is great but the service is really crappy. It's just bad. Walk in and seat yourself. A sign up front says a server will find you. Ok...when she/he finally does they will promptly forget about you. That's at least what happened to us. When the food came out I was already needing my drink refilled (water) and she came back to the table not once, not twice but three times forgetting the water pitcher. 

Parking is definitely a challenge but I'd overlook that to eat here again. But I can't overlook bad service. We won't be back.

I'm sure that the pizza here is great. I will never know, though. That's because Slice Pizzeria has a BBQ shrimp poboy that's out of this world delicious and has ruined me for all other BBQ shrimp poboys. This poboy should set the standard for all other BBQ shrimp poboys. It. Is. So. Good.  So good, in fact, that I am doubtful that I'll ever order anything else here. It is garlicky and spicy and it also has lots of black pepper in it. You might want to check to make sure you're not walking around smiling like a fool at everyone with black pepper in your teeth like I did the first time I had it.

Just go. Order the BBQ shrimp poboy. I have plans to go there this week.  I'll bet you can guess what I'll be having. :)

I went to Juan's on Monday. It's Thursday and I'm still thinking about it. It's like that man (or woman) you can't get out of your head.

For me, parking wasn't too bad since I arrived early and I had a mighty fine gentlemen guiding me. The lot is small and spaces are limited so keep that in mind.

I ordered a Western Burrito with chicken. Let me just say that this burrito can stand alone as being the best burrito ever...(sour cream, salsa, green peppers, onions, jalapeños and cheese? Hell yes!) but get it "wet". The red chili sauce, tomatoes, sour cream and melted cheese only make it that much better. 

Service was friendly and prompt. The food was incredible and I can't wait to go again.

Dear John,
You let us down. You know if you read my reviews I love all things Besh-but gosh I didn't love this place at all. I was soooo excited for King cake season to arrive and rushed to Willa Jean for their bananas foster version. 

First, the positive. As May pointed out the people who work here are very sweet.

Now for the bad...
It was not good. $10 a slice is ridiculous. For $10 a slice I expected it to blow me away. It just wasn't good. It was dry and tasted like my grandmothers banana pudding...which is great but I wouldn't pay $10 a slice for it! Save your money

Not impressed. Won't be back.

There is nothing, and I mean nothing, that a king cakes from Gambino's does wrong. Nothing.
 
They are not (rhymes with wussies) 
There really is nothing sadder than when bakery A won't put the damn baby in the king cake. Are you kidding me? Part of the fun of eating the king cake is to see WHO GETS THE BABY!! Who wants to stuff it themselves? Not I. It just plain takes the fun out of the pure joy that is eating the cake and finding the baby.

Speaking of plain-
A good barometer for how good a king cake does all of their other filled cakes is to first try the plain cinnamon one. If's it moist and has a good icing to dough ratio, it's perfect. It's gotta be sweet, soft and almost melt in your mouth. Bakery A please stop slathering your too sweet icing all over your dry ass king cake. It ain't working sweetie.

You've probably guessed by this point that Gambino's stuffs the baby. Major props to you, Mr. Gambino for not being a wuss. And secondly, their plain cake is perfect. OUT. OF. THIS. WORLD. Moist, delicious, perfect icing to cake ratio. As for Bakery A, well I'm looking at you (rhymes with Mouse's)

King Cake purists, get yourself a Joe Gambino's king cake. You can thank me later.

First of all, Cafe Beignet is so much fun to say, right? Cafe Beignet! I love it!

I wanted to try some of the city's other beignet offerings and this one looked promising so in we went.

I absolutely love the open air space! It's situated right on the river, so you get that nice breeze coming in. There is also a player piano which some people think is creepy, but I really love them! This charming little bistro also boasts a beautiful full bar and has a menu that goes way beyond beignets, so if those little pillows of heaven aren't your thing, you're sure to find something here that is.

As for the beignets, they were absolutely delicious! They are satisfyingly crispy on the outside but soft and dense inside. 

I'll be back to try their Crawfish Omelette. And the Mushroom Omelette. And most certainly the Andouille Sausage Omelette...

Domilise's poboy shop is totally trying to steal my heart. I'd let him have it glady and never stray with another poboy shop in the city, if it weren't for but a few minor details.

First the good. I ordered my usual shrimp Poboy and it was great.  The shrimp were seasoned to perfection and plentiful. The batter was just right...not too thin, not too thick. If you order it dressed they put ketchup and Tabasco on it along with lettuce, tomatoes, pickles and mayo. Hello!?! You had me at Tabasco. They don't put too much on it, just a dab. In fact,  I had to add more ketchup and a lot more Tabasco on it..but I appreciate that they already know that Tabasco and ketchup on a shrimp Po boy makes it freaking spectacular. Kudos to you Domilise's. I also love the fact that they split their poboys into three quarters instead of half.

Also love the divey and casual atmosphere here and looking at all of the New Orleans memorabilia on the walls. Speaking of New Orleans, behind the bar there's a Manning shrine. Now don't get me wrong, I'm a Saints girl all the way. But you better believe if Peyton or Eli are playing (and it's not against us) I'm rooting for my New Orleans boys. And who doesn't love Archie Manning? 

Now for the not so good. It's very small in here. There are only 5 four top tables. There's seating at the bar, but probably no more than ten barstools. I can imagine it gets very crowded. 

The other thing? It ain't cheap. A whole shrimp poboy was $15. Come again? You heard right. $15! That's outrageous. I mean that Shrimp poboy was good but it wasn't THAT good. Like my friend pointed out, that's just a few dollars less than the three course price fixe menu for lunch at many of our upscale restaurants here in New Orleans.

Sigh. So while I have found one of the best shrimp poboys in New Orleans, it would put a serious dent in my wallet to eat here as often as I now want to. *sob*

The search continues for the perfect shrimp poboy at the perfect price. Stay tuned friends.

I don't care where you're from or why you'd be up at breakfast (judge free zone here all the way) but get your ass to Ruby Slipper.

First of all they are local. One of the first resturants to open after Katrina. The name comes directly from the spirit of New Orleans. We will not waver, we will get past this and we know this is our Home Sweet Home.  Make no mistake about it, New Orleans gets in your very being and STAYS there. I could wax poetically about my beloved city but this is a restraunt review.

I'm definitely a creature of habit and normally get the eggs Benedict so I ordered their verision which was  the eggs Cochon. Ummm. Hello, breakfast of my life. If you were a man I would probably propose. This is definitely a must have! It's so tender, flaky, spicy all at once. Perfection, y'all. I mean really. I ordered the mixed fruit as a side and again was blown away.  It was sweet and juicy and oh so fresh.

If coffee is your thing (mine really isn't) theirs is on the weak side, but still all in all I highly recommend Ruby Slipper for a great breakfast.place. Just jet your self over there. You are welcome.

What a super cool and fun experience this was! My sister from another mister Ms. Libby V. herself http://www.yelp.com/user_details?userid=vazTanfeJwjbokWZrGpNzg invited me to do this with her while she was in town and I was so excited. I already know how to cook the dishes that they demonstrated for us, so I wasn't really sure what to expect.

First of all, our instructor (Harriet) was classic old school New Orleans. Charming, funny and so darn cute. She has that thick Yat accent and said things like zink (sink), mynez (mayonnaise) and dawlin' (darling). I just loved her and wish she was a part of my family. I really felt like I was sitting in her very own kitchen watching her cook and listening to her hilarious stories.

She made chicken and andouille gumbo (oh.my.goodness.), jambalaya, bananas foster, and pralines. We were even served pitchers of Abita Amber and sweet tea as well as coffee and lemonade. 

Harriet gave us lots of lessons of the history of New Orleans and it's food as well as our culture and she definitely knew her stuff. I learned so much and was captivated listening to her.

This is a must do for sure. For visitors definitely, but I think locals will get so much out of it, too. If you get a chance to, please go. In fact you really should make it happen as soon as possible. It was wonderful. I'm already planning my second trip.

You guys. This place is awesome. It's casual and cool and decorated with an ocean theme. Hello, perfection.

I had the blue crab bisque to start. This is seriously one of the best crab bisques I've ever had. It was thick and delicious-full of crabmeat. All too often I'll order crab bisque and get some watered down, barely any crab in it version that I have to doctor up with salt, pepper, Tony's and Tabasco. Not here. It was so good I was scraping the bowl and had to stop myself from licking it. No kidding.

For my main dish I ordered the crawfish pie. Another great choice. The crust was flaky and mouthwateringly delicious. It was spicy and full of crawfish. I'm not easy to please when it comes to crawfish but this dish had my Cajun self whimpering. 

Service was awesome and it wasn't too expensive. I'd go again in a heartbeat.

Let's talk about shrimp and grits. If you're from the south I'm willing to bet that you've had shrimp and grits at some point in your life. Right?  Of course! 

However, if your southern ass has not had Surrey's shrimp and grits, well then you might as well just say you've never had shrimp and grits...period. 

Surrey's shrimp and grits are the thing that dreams are made of. The grits are buttery and creamy. The shrimp are perfectly cooked and seasoned. The bacon is crisp and delicious. The sprig of delightful smelling rosemary is like the icing on the (perfect) cake. I've had shrimp and grits several times throughout my life, but none even come close to the perfection that are Surrey's version of this dish. 

Go to Surrey's. They have lots of really yummy things on the menu. But order the shrimp and grits.  You're welcome.

A good ol' summer BBQ seems like a thing of the past...... with the 'Rona running rampant, it's hard to get that warm feeling again. Since BBQ for one is a little lackluster, I decided to call on Baby Blues BBQ  Philly. 
BBQ can be tricky, it has to be tender, smokey and in my opinion, plentiful. Nothing is worse than tough BBQ. 
I ordered the barbequed beef brisket, baked beans, chicken smoked rice, collard greens and cornbread. The brisket was tasty, tender and juicy but not fatty. The BBQ sauce was delicious, but not enough to go round. The collards were fair and the baked beans were very good. 
I ordered chicken smoked rice and it was good and even though the cornbread was tiny, the flavor was great. All in all, it was a decent, filling meal and if they would have supplied more of that delicious BBQ sauce, I would be wiping it off my cheeks right now.

I GrubHubed some food from Tampopo today. I felt like some Asian food and after checking out their menu online, I decided to give them a whirl.
I ordered the Spicy chicken bowl and a order of pan fried pork dumplings and a side of Kimchee. The delivery was quick, and I received all the necessary utensils to enjoy my meal. The Spicy chicken was delicious, sliced into bite sized strips with a tasty sauce, the sauce wasn't that spicy but the chicken was grilled perfectly. I enjoyed that it wasn't too soft and it felt like you were having real chicken.
The dumplings were tasty, tender and a little bit on the smaller size, but very flavorful. The kimchee was good, with a satisfying amount in the container.
My meal was as promised, the only criticism I have is the spice level was kind of PG-13. I'm looking forward for my next experience with Tampopo.

Lee's Deli is a small neighborhood spot with an international flair. They have food from Asia, Hawaii, Mexico and of course, Philly. They have a small seating area and a good experienced server. The menu is so divers, I couldn't wait to dive in.
I ordered the spicy Thai red curry chicken soup for starters and the beef fajita which I asked for avocado and bacon and spicy mayo on it. The experience of the cooks showed, they didn't bat an eye when presented with the order. 
The Thai curry soup was good and flavorful, but not spicy enough for me. The fajita was perfect. The steak was to my likings and the avocado and cheese melted into a gooey center, wrapped in a crisp tortilla. 
To round out the meal, I ordered a toasted cinnamon roll and a cup of coffee. I had a pretty good dining experience for it to be a corner sandwich spot, and I think I saw
 Loco Moco on the menu....... like Arnie says
"I'll be back"

I've been driving past this restaurant for years and I never stopped in because the restaurant that was there before them was not very good. It was late, late one Friday night and I was coming from a friends party in Doylestown and please-no of fence but to me suburban parties usually leave me hungry, they don't throw down like we do in Philly. 
I was driving down Wyncote ave heading to Germantown when I past Jamaican D's and there was a guy outside jerking the Hell out of somebody's Chicken, I could smell it a couple of blocks away! 
I parked and went inside and the small takeout place was very clean with the food on display in technicolor right before your eyes in a large food warmer. The foods were so colorful with an over abundance of fresh Veggies. There was Curry Chicken & Goat, Ox Tails, Stew Beef & Stew Chicken, BBQ Ribs and every side order known from Plantains to Steamed Cabbage. This is my second trip here and so far the food has been excellent! The portions are-say it with me "L-E-G-E-N-D-A-R-Y"! 
There's also a Rasta DJ spinning Discs and selling his own mixed Dance hall, Soca, and Reggae Cd's, so you can get your groove on while your getting served and you can even keep the flow going if you buy a disc and continue while chomping on some pretty good grub. Just don't try to eat it all at once, half of it will taste even better tomorrow.

Not much I can add to the many,  many reviews of this iconic Chinatown restaurant except what I love to eat here. Sang Kee is a great noodle house and their Peking duck is stellar.  
I go there mostly for 3 items,  the duck noodle soup  (with ginger and scallions), the sliced roast pork and the duck rolls. The soup is delicious,  crammed with roast duck,  noodles in a savory broth. The ginger and scallions make it perfect. 
I order the roast pork and ask them to smother it with the duck juice and dip it in spicy Chinese mustard.  
But the duck rolls are the star of the meal, Peking duck sliced with slivers of scallions,  a swipe of hoisen sauce and rolled up in a flour tortilla,  I could eat them everyday if I could. 
So that's it folks, try these items and you'll be looking for a hard to find parking space, avoiding the nefarious PPA, standing in a crowded takeout space and salivating while they prepare a unforgettable experience.

I haven't ate here in 6 or 7 years and I was still craving spicy food, so I decided to GrubHub them. I ordered the samosas with meat and the garlic naan and the chicken tiki masala. I know, I know, no creativity in the ordering, but these are my favorites. 
In my last 2 reviews I complained about the spice level of the dishes I ordered. Well I ain't complaining no more! If you're like me, you love spicy food and New Delhi got something for you. They straightened me out quick fast and in a hurry. 
My delivery was prompt and still hot and all the necessary utensils, and sauces and even included a plate. 
The samosas were delicious, large and stuffed full of meat, the pastry wrap was crisp and tasty. I really liked the fresh spicy salsa on the side.  The garlic naan was toasted just right and after I slathered it with melted butter it was irresistible.
Now, back to the spice level, when I ordered the chicken tiki masala they offered many spice levels, mild, slightly spicy, moderate spicy, extra spicy to name a few. I chose spicy, which was just below extra spicy.  The dish was good, creamy and hearty chunks of white meat chicken and fresh veggies, the sauce was hot..... hotter than July as Stevie sang. I no longer crave spicy food, they put out my fire with a nuclear spice bomb!
 It left me wondering what extra spicy was like.......
It was so spicy, I was comatose for a couple of minutes, when my head cleared I began to feel the burn and the benefits of the spice. My nose, throat and sinus were cleared, my vision was a little sharper, I had to turn down the TV because it sounded too loud and the more I ate, the more heightened the experience got. 
I'm not saying this will happen to you, but I have always been a fan of spicy foods and the reactions I received. Whenever I need a fix, I know where to cop.

It's great to see that some things never change. I have been eating at Ishkabibble's on South St. for longer than I want to admit.
I have been eating there since the glory days of South St. when it truly was the hippest street in town. 
I love their cheese steaks, especially the chicken cheese steaks the cheese fries and my favorite non- alcoholic drink, the Gremlin, which is grape juice and lemonade mixed. 
Ishkablbble's has something you don't see much of these days, a window you can walk up to, it makes things easier and more convenient. They have seating inside, but it's a sardine can, better to be outdoors and taking in the drama of South St. 
Back in the day they had a lady working the outside counter who I called "Mom". She was a real character that earnen her place as one of South steets iconic personalities.
I would be across the street conversating with a South street regular like Shamus or Mikey Wild, and all I had to do was wave or nod at Mom and my favorite meal was on the grill. 
I usually ordered the same thing, chicken cheese steak, cheese fries and a large Gremlin. 
By the time I sashayed over there, Mom had my food on the counter. The chicken steak was meaty, made with big chunks of chicken breast with onions and peppers, the fries were very crispy and remained so even after it was drowned in rich, gooey cheese. An ice cold Gremlin washed it down nicely.
I'll never get tired of that.

Shia Lan Kung is a late night, old school restaurant that serves tasty food in the speed of light.  I sobered up many a late night here over the years.  
They offer a really huge menu with all of the traditional favorites. Everything I've tried here over the years has been pleasing to say the least.  There's a saying in Hawaii,  and it goes like this:  "The best Chinese food is not on the menu" so sometimes I invent a dish.  
You should have some knowledge of how Chinese food is constructed or you could be laughed out of there.  There is one dish that they prepare so excellent, I wish I could experience it. I have a severe allergy to crabs,  but I know if I want to thank or impress a young lady or aa co-worker,  I order what everyone calls "Big Crab". Actually it a big Dungeness crab sauteed with ginger and scallions.  There must be something in the water they drink because all the ladies I know go ga ga over "Big Crab". 
Stop by Shiao Lan Kung and try it, there's no set price for it because the bigger the crab,  the bigger the price.  Whatever it cost, it ain't enough.

Fat Jack's BBQ is my kinda place. The first thing I noticed about Jack's is the giant silver smoker positioned in the front of the parking lot. As I passed the smoker, I got a huge whiff of the rich BBQ flavor. 
I stood there for a few minutes taking it all in. I tore myself away from the intoxicating smell and went inside Jack's to order some BBQ before I passed out.
Fat Jack's has a unique menu because it's not all just BBQ'd meats. Of course there are ribs, chicken, pulled pork, sausage and beef brisket. Fat Jack's adds a twist to the BBQ game by creating a number of selections with different sauces and rubs, adding peppers and cheeses to give you a more chef quality meal.
I chose the"Hellfire sandwich" because I love spicy food, it had beef brisket, pull pork and pulled chicken with a spicy BBQ sauce, cheese, grilled onions and jalapenos. The sandwich was delicious, thick and meaty though I thought it could of used more heat to suit me. 
Service was good and I especially enjoyed the decor of the restaurant. I left the restaurant satisfied and I took one more look at the big silver smoker in the parking lot filling the sky with beautiful 24 hour BBQ flavor. Right then and there I decided to come back late one night, bring along a chair and sit there with a beer and a good cigar and watch the traffic go by while taking in all that BBQ goodness!

Isgro Pastries has 2 truly great things about them and 2 extremely bad things about them. The great things are: 
1 Isgro has many delicious baked goods. 
2 Isgro is open late.
The bad things about them are:
1 Isgro has many delicious baked goods. 
2 Isgro is open late. 
Depending on your priorities,  it may work for you,  it works for me because quoting a friend "I'm not in it for a long time,  I'm in it for a good time "
And if you enjoy delicious,  well made traditional Italian pastries,  then Isgro's Pastries is the place for you.  I love their Neapolitan pastry,  the creamy cheese cakes,  cookies,  delicate cannoli's  (especially the chocolate ones) and a wonderful Italian style rum cake. The rum cake is silky smooth with a delicious icing and gently soaked in smooth rum. Some folks aren't used to wet cake,  but for me it was a revelation.  Along with a Thai herbal cake, they are my favorite birthday cakes 
If you go to Isgro's Pastries I dare you to go in there and not want to purchase something,  if you don't you ain't human.

Parx Casino is the other Philadelphia casino even if it's in Bensalem. It's located where the former Philadelphia Racetrack was years ago. The horse racetrack theme is throughout the property, with a huge horse's head statue in the front of the casino. 
Parx is big and plush, very modern in design. Lots of comfortable chairs, big screen TV's, restaurants and of course slot machines and gambling tables. It's very warm and colorful.
I'm not much of a gambler, I had come here with some friends from Chinatown, I played slots, lost a few at the blackjack table and finally settled on playing video poker. I won. Finally, I invested 2 or 3 bucks and came away with $67.50.  Guess what I did next? I sat at the bar had a couple of beers and at the Liberty Bell Gastropub and I ordered some raw oysters on a half shell and dosed them with lemon juice and hot sauce. They were fresh, but kinda puny for $4 bucks a pop. 
I waited for my friends to lose their hard earned cash until they were ready to go. I still walked out of there with almost $40 bucks more than I came with and all in all I think I was lucky.

There's a new hangout in Chinatown, and the eye candy is smoking hot!!  I was invited to a soft opening of this new club / restaurant/ Karaoke club in Chinatown. TANGO is a stylish new spot that hasn't opened yet and I was invited by some friends to check the spot out.  First there is a extremely well dressed doorman to greet you when you enter TANGO, upon entering the place, its very modern and fresh. The building is very long and narrow, it must run about 200 feet deep. It start with a long red acrylic bar, there are some tables and booths,  followed by a huge, open kitchen. 
 We sat at the bar and a beautiful friendly young lady named Tikki greeted us and she was so sweet and her outfit conjured up all the Mystikal secrets of Asian women. Assisting her at the bar was Jose and the two of them try their hardest to please everyone and they succeeded with style. I ordered a bottle of orchid Apple cider and some Thai crispy chicken wings with a dipping sauce.  They were very fresh and delicious and the crunch was intense.
 I went upstairs to check out the club portion of the restaurant and Wow! Upstairs there was a huge bar with 3 bartenders, 6 karaoke rooms complete with a hostess and bottle service. I counted 37 huge flat screen TVs with a huge projection screen that doubled as a huge window overlooking Arch Street. All the karaoke equipment was state of art and everyone seem to be having such a great time. TANGO Is a great addition to the bar scene in Chinatown and now you can go bar hopping all night long but I think you will spend most of the time here at TANGO.

I once witnessed the strangest bar argument ever. I was enjoying an adult cocktail at a bar in Chinatown and 2 guys were going at it arguing about who's food was the HEALTHIEST. A strange argument to say the least. one guy was Thai,  the other one was Vietnamese. I don't think either guy won the argument, but it was refreshing to see someone bragging about how healthy their native food is.
Vietnam restaurant is a lovely place, very well decorated in a nostalgic Vietnam style. The menu is very creative and contains most of the classic Vietnamese dishes and a few other Asian specialties. 
I ordered the Cha Gio which is pork spring rolls, crispy with lots of meat and an accompanying sauce along with a nice salad and fresh Thai basil. I guess this is what he meant by healthy. If you order this make sure you wrap the spring roll in a basil leaf..... delicious.
Next I had the Chicken gree papaya salad, chunks of chicken with lots of vegetables and heaps of shredded green papaya. It was fresh and tasty, but I felt it needed some heat so I added some red chili oil and it was complete for me. I tried to make this dish at home, but I couldn't figure out how to shred that hard ass papaya.
For my main course I ordered the Shaking Beef which is chunks of sirloin steak seared with fresh watercress, red onion, tomatoes and a soy vinaigrette. The steak was a perfect medium rare and it is served with a bowl of steamed rice. No room for dessert and I guess that keeps you healthy.

I'm from West Philadelphia, born and raised, eating soft pretzels and Italian water ice is how I spent most of my summer day......... A little ad-lib for ya.
In Philly, we love our soft pretzels, squirt some mustard on them (not yellow please) and you have a snack that stays with you. 
I can't tell you how many pretzels ive eaten over the years, that would be like counting the stars in the sky. I like the pretzels they make at Philly Pretzel Factory, fresh and soft with the right amount of salt. I use to prefer a tougher chew on the pretzel, but as I get older the soft ones are easier for me to process.
I like their regular sized ones and the mini pretzels most. The pretzels with the hot dog inside is a great idea, but there's some slimy substance inside the pretzel that skives me out. 
They have good service and it's pretty cool watching them make the pretzels before your very eyes.

Restaurant week. I hate restaurant week. But that's what it was when I wanted to stay close to home and see the sunset at the beach while also allowing the family some dinner... Just as I was describing to my sister the Jimmy Buffet-esque music I hoped to hear at a nice beachside joint, we approached to the sounds of the man himself. Decision made.
To complete my Floridian dream, I decided to order the grouper sandwich. It was superb. The service was also surprisingly on point. Fast, polite, even jovial at points. (I think Dan was our server?) Plenty of places can't get that right when it's not restaurant week.
Sis had the steak salad. I had 2 bites and realized I had ordered wrong. That steak was awesome.
Next time, I'll starve all day to save up calories for dessert.

Okay so this place is just fantastic! There is no skimping on the flavor. The price is pretty reasonable as well. 6 people for lunch with a tab under $100. 

I had the salmon special of the day. It was beautifully cooked! Crispy and flavorful on the outside but moist and perfectly cooked on the inside. There was also a tomato sauce (not sure of the Italian name for it) but it reminded me of a cacciatore sauce. It had tomatoes, olives and capers in it. I'm also doing the Keto thing so I was pleased that they were able to give me a double dose of veggies in exchange for the mashed potatoes that were on the side. I was expecting the veggies to be a broccoli/carrot combo like you get at most restaurants but what I got instead was perfectly cooked squash, zucchini and eggplant... holy wow was it fantastic!

The other people at my table had the Chicken Parmesan, Pumpkin Sausage Ravioli (I tried a bite... was off the hook amazeballs!) and Mushroom Ravioli (also sampled... the chefs are wizards of mega flavor!) It was one of those lunches where it was awkwardly quiet because everyone was stuffing their faces! 

We were there celebrating a birthday and the waiter brought out a piece of mouth watering tiramisu with a candle in it... it was a sweet gesture! 

This is the second time I've eaten at this restaurant for lunch and the second time I left impressed. 

One thing to mention is that they have perfect portions for lunch. No to-go box needed. You can eat everything on your plate and be comfortably full.

I know Tucson must be looking for "fancy" places to eat or I feel like this place would never make it. The food is pretty good but they way they treat you here guarantees I won't return again. I've been here twice- once for a birthday and once to celebrate Valentine's day. Both experiences were overpriced and the waiters were snotty/nasty on both occasions. My friends brought my birthday gifts the first time I came here and the staff acted like we were tiny children or something. Even the hostess was a jerk.

As for my vegetarian friend.. well, she didn't have a very great eating experience here either, so if you don't eat meat you might want to skip this place all together.

I get why people like the food but it's really not worth being treated crappy because you don't live up to the restaurant's standards. Bleh.

Came there on a Saturday Night and it was packed, not a problem! I asked for a seat for three, the person at the door said he would take care of it. After 30 minutes of waiting I ask another worker about the seating. She points to the hostess and do the 30 minutes was a waste of time. After reserving a seat they said it would take another 30-40 minutes. An hour later, we ask the hostess how much longer. Apparently asking how long the tables will take will get you kicked out of the place. 
Cons: everything. The workers are rude and obnoxious. I called the place to speak to a manager and they said he wasn't available. I called 10 times throughout the night, it's a horrible establishment. Place is run down .

Had lunch here on my first visit, and was pleasantly surprised at their lunch specials.  The pan roast and pacifica sandwich combo with fries was a very good value in terms of portion and flavor.  Really, really good.  The space, albeit inside the Peppermill Casino, is right by the north entrance, so one does not actually have to go through the smoky casino to get to Oceano.  The dining area itself is bright, well-appointed, and with ample seating all around.  My favorite feature of the space are the two gigantic screens that show high-def photos from all over the world.  
My first lunch experience stuck with so much so that I couldn't wait to take my hubs there.  He loves pan-roast and I thought theirs is as good, if not better, as the pan-roast from another casino restaurant in town.  He ordered the lunch combo and was very happy with it, as I expected.  I went for the soup and salad combo (clam chowder and huge house salad) and was very pleased with it as well.  Unfortunately, the lunch special pricing is only good on weekdays.  Our server was Lissa, and she was excellent.  She anticipated things that I might have to ask for (side of ranch, extra spoon, lemon).  Overall, a very enjoyable lunch in a clean, bright, spacious setting, topped with friendly and efficient service.  
P.S.  They have a sushi bar that I am looking forward to trying one of these days.

Came here per a birthday celebrant's wishes.  I've been here before and although I enjoyed my past experience, I prefer the other spas in the area.  It's mostly because of space.  I feel the facilities here are cramped, especially the ladies' locker room.  The sauna and steam room in the ladies room are also tiny and you can literally bump other users, and because it's right in the middle of the lockers, the 'noise' carries inside, and you're literally listening to conversations right outside.  Not very relaxing.  The waiting room is also very small, with only 5 seats.  The amenities are meager and because it's right by the entrance to the ladies' locker room, it's not very ideal for peace and quiet as well.  The rest of the facilities are co-ed and are spread out.  You have to walk hallways to find the Laconian and Brine rooms.  To get to the jacuzzi, you have to walk in front of the gym.  Once there, good luck finding a lounge chair, as there's only a few, less than 10.  And to go to the pool, you have to go outside the entrance to the spa and mingle with non-spa guests.  Kids are welcome there, so as you can imagine, it doesn't make for a very relaxing spa experience.  
I did enjoy the treatments and the treatment rooms.  But these are tad too pricey, and since we were there on a holiday, they did not honor the local discount.  Overall, it was just ok.

Omg, I LOVE THIS PLACE!  I don't know why I haven't been here sooner.  Ok, I do know why ~ it's quite a drive from our home, but heck, I wouldn't have minded the drive had I known it was gonna be this good.
We came here for breakfast.  We decided, instead of eating somewhere after a hike, we would eat first and then go hike.  I checked the trusted Yelp, and Creme popped up.  They open early, so we decided to go there.  I'm so happy we did. 
It's a small, yet cozy little place.  There was a fair amount of people there, but we got seated right away.  We were greeted warmly by someone from the bar and by our server.   
To start, I was torn between the french press coffee (from Blind Dog, for those who want to know) and the Mexican Mocha.  I don't think I've had Mexican Mocha before, but when the server said it's essentially mocha with a dash of cumin, I had to try it.  I liked it a lot.  It may be a tad sweet, but the heat from the cumin kinda offset it a little bit.  I had to slurp it to the very last drop because that's where all the cumin ended up.  
Then, there's the crepe.  I love crepes.  And Creme has them, and theirs is so good!  I ordered the seasonal special savory crepe (breakfast sausage, sauteed mushroom, kale, fennel, and topped with a fried egg).  I mean...so delicious!  It had everything I wanted and needed to get me fueled up for our hike.  Hubby had the breakfast sandwich (two scrambled eggs, cheddar cheese, leeks, mushroom and your choice of meat).  It looked good, but he wasn't sharing, not even when I pulled the 'I had to taste it so I can review it on Yelp.'  Oh well, I will just have to order it when we go back.
Finally, the service.  I liked that I could see the chefs busy themselves in the kitchen.  The place was starting to fill up, but the servers remained friendly and warm, and didn't rush us out of there, even when we offered to get up before the check came, so that they can seat the people waiting.  It just gave off this super relaxed, neighborly atmosphere.  We got the feeling that we were regulars, despite the fact that it was our first time there.  I liked that.  I liked that a lot.  I can't wait to go back!  Go give them a try!

After a night of enjoying an amazing sunset and snowshoeing under the full moon, I say nothing would cap the night better than a juicy and tasty burger.  I didn't realize they recently opened at the Summit shopping mall in Reno, but am glad that they did.  It's always good to have different dining options while in the area.  Nothing seems to last for very long, so hopefully this business fares well.
It was quiet for a Saturday night, but we were informed that we just missed the rush.  The server informed us that sometimes, the line snakes outside.  Very encouraging to hear!  But on this night (around 8 pm), it was just me and 3 others.  I had the turkey burger, hubs got the elk burger special, and our friends had the regular cheeseburgers with fries.  Table consensus:  everything was good!  Mine was cooked perfectly ~ juicy, tender and tasty.  The bun had a tinge of sweetness to it, which enhanced the burger.  It came with a good portion of lettuce and tomatoes.  I believe the dressing was their version of a thousand island, which was very good! (none of that ketchup/bbq nonsense).  I skipped the fries, and could do without it.  Too much!  I did like that they have an 'open condiment' area, where you can just grab more pickles, banana peppers, ranch and blue cheese dressing, etc.  They have a good beer/wine selection, but we didn't have any.  One of our companions had a milkshake and he was very pleased with it.  
Service was friendly and fast.  The place is clean, and there are plenty of seating.  There are also a couple of TV monitors to watch your favorite games!  Would love to stop by here again, either before or after working off some calories outdoors!

I'm no expert on Korean food, but thankfully, the staff at Bab Cafe were so accommodating and they patiently walked us through the menu.  I love that the menu is simple enough, but sounds very interesting.  This is not your typical Korean AYCE BBQ place.  Instead, there were at least 3 choices of 'bowls' and they differ according to the type of veggies that they come with, and how the veggies were prepared (sauteed, fresh, or steamed).  Each bowl comes with rice and a cup of miso soup, and a small bottled water.  You choose your protein (chicken, beef, pork, or tofu), and some add-ons, if you are so inclined.  They also offer a few side/appetizer dishes.  I opted for Kimchee (it's a Korean cafe after all).  i could've easily picked the wings or the japchae, but i noticed the size of the bowls and decided it might be too much for me and hubs to finish (it was!).  Maybe next time.
I had the bulgogi (beef) and hubs had the top bab (chicken).  Both were delicious, and as hubs would say 'hit the spot'.  I personally think my bowl was bigger portion than expected, but I'm not complaining!  I want to say, the bowls are not overwhelmingly seasoned, which was perfect because they have sauces on the side that you can help yourself with (hot korean sauce, teriyake, and spicy mayo).  My favorite is the hot sauce.  It has a real kick to it, but really elevates the flavors of my bowl.  Also, the kimchee was on point.  I could snack on just the kimchee alone, but it went perfectly with the bowl.  I'm glad I ordered it as a side.  I saw there's a kimchee fried rice on the menu.  I will have to try that next time.
Overall, a wonderful first time experience.  It was the perfect pre-movie dinner because of its location.  It was a no-fuss, easy, quick but super delicious meal.  I'm looking forward to my next visit already!
Pro-tip:  They still have the Buy-One-Get-50off-on-the-second-bowl Grand Opening promo through end of June, so stop by when you get a chance!

Re: Response from Lolo's:
1) Yes, you DID apologize and offered to refund, but I never said it was fine.  We spoke over text, and I preferred it that way so I can document our conversation.  I "just" wanted the refund so I could be done with this transaction vs your having to send food and go through the process again. 
2) As I've written below, my complaint was not ONLY the wrong order; it's the 2-hr delay in the agreed delivery time, the 4 missing items (chicken bbq, lumpia, cole slaw and beans), and one of the items actually delivered was wrong (fried fish, instead of escabeche lapu-lapu).  I did not say I liked your food in any of our messages. 
3) I live 8 miles away from Lolo's (per googlemaps), NOT 20 miles as you pointed out below.  I ordered 2 bundles to make it worth the delivery, and I left $20 tip for your driver, for the convenience.  You're the one who set up the pricing, so I'm not quite sure why you're telling me how much money you made on my order.  
4) No hard feelings here either.  I do hope to find restaurants that will deliver what I ordered, and deliver it at somewhat reasonably close to our agreed time.  I don't remember asking for anything else beyond that.  I've had food delivered before and I haven't had any issues.  They were not always perfect, but the difference is ~ they gave me a head's up if the order was running behind.  They never had to deliver without any of my order yet, but I suspect if they can't deliver something, they would have probably asked if I'd be ok with the substitute.  At least, I would have had to agree to the substitute, or be made aware that half of my order will not be delivered.  Lolo's Easter menu mentioned "no substitutes".  It would've been only fair if that's true in fulfilling orders as well, in my humble opinion.
I based my review on overall experience, not just food.  Food reviews can be subjective and I prefer sticking to the facts.  If the complaints I mentioned here are considered tiny, then perhaps we can all agree it depends on one's point of view.  

To participate in Yelp's Big Night In, I decided to order from Lolo's for Easter.  They had 4 "bundles" to choose from, each supposedly good for 4 persons.  Even though there's only me and hubs in isolation, we couldn't agree on which one to order, so we picked 2 bundles!  We thought, hey ~ let's support the business, and we'll have leftovers for days!  Win-win, or so I thought.  I placed the order through PM on FB, and requested delivery at Noon, on Sunday.  Delivery was "free", as long as we tip the driver.  Ok, no problem.  Sunday morning, someone called to get my payment/credit card info over the phone.  I also confirmed if we are still on track for Noon delivery, and was assured that's the case.  Ok, cool.
Noon came and went.  I waited around 20 minutes or so before texting, calling and PM-ing Lolo's to check on my order.  Finally, got someone to answer and was told "finishing up your order now and your food will be out the door shortly."  Cool.  
ONE AND HALF HOUR later, the food finally showed up.  That's almost 2 hours from agreed delivery time.  By this time, we gave up waiting to have it for lunch and resigned ourselves to just have it for dinner.  But when the food DID show up, they looked suspiciously less than what I anticipated.  Remember, I ordered 2 "bundles", but I pretty much got HALF that.  And to make it even worse, when I opened the containers, not only were we missing half our order, we were also given the WRONG one.  We ordered BBQ chicken, pork BBQ, coleslaw and beans (bundle 1), AND Escabeche Lapu-Lapu, pancit bihon, lumpia and rice (bundle 2).  
What we got:  Deep-fried fish, pancit bihon,  pork bbq, and rice.  I can only guess that the deep-fried fish was supposed to be excabeche?  I know I haven't eaten escabeche in a long time, but from what I can remember, it's the Filipinos' version of a sweet and sour fish.  Obviously, we're missing the sauce.  Any sauce!  The pancit bihon is soggy, and mostly noodles ~hardly any meat or vegetables in it.  The pork bbq has a funky taste, akin to stale meat or sauce that's been sitting too long, i can't be sure, but I'll skip it.  
Naturally, I reached out to Lolo's to at least get some of my money's back.
