I was told there was some kind of trouble with the fryer, not being able to supervise, a new delivery person, etc.  It's hard to be understanding of these reasons when this was a PRE-ORDER.  They knew what orders they have to prepare, and when they're expected to deliver.  I understand problems come up, but the least they could have done was give their customers a head's up.  That way we wouldn't have expected food that was never going to be delivered, as well as have the chance to refuse the substitute.  I believe this is a basic customer courtesy, and I feel Lolo's failed to show me some.
So overall, as much as I would've wanted to support this business, I sadly can't recommend this business at this time.

Guidos Pizzeria & Tapas is located on The Hill with every other Italian restaurant. However, they stand out from the others I've been too. From the outside, it appears to be a small place but when you walk in there's 3 sections. The full bar with barstool tables, dining area and in the back, a larger banquet area. 

This was my first International supper club event and not only did I enjoy the food; but the company as well. Our waitress Donna was awesome! If I can remember your name 4 days later, you have obviously left an impression on me; it was a good one. Donna was able to keep up with the large group, no orders were sent back, she interacted with us, showed her great personality and checks were correct. Kudos to her!!!! 

I ordered the Guidos signature salad, Cordero Lollipops (tapas), white sangria and steak sandwich (to go). I could probably eat this salad everyday minus the artichokes. My lollipop lamb was cooked perfectly with mint jam and mash potatoes. The white sangria was the best I've ever had. I was tempted to get a pitcher but I also needed to drive, so 2 glasses was enough. The steak sandwich came on cheesy garlic bread with fries. Which was a to go order for the kid, who enjoyed it. 

At the end of the day... Yes, I will definitely return!

Polite Society located in Lafayette Square; probably would have never visited if it wasn't for Mr Steven B! So happy he put this brunch together. 

The ambience is warm and inviting for brunch, lunch and dinner. If you're seating at the bar or enjoying company who can pass of the bottomless mimosas?!? Well at least not me! The staff; from the bartender to our waiter (Josh) and even the Chef (Tom) were welcoming and on point the whole time we were there. Have you ever had fried but yet tender wings before?!? Oh... you haven't! We did and they were delicious. The aroma alone would make your mouth water. Complements of the chef. Our glasses stayed full of it was water or a specialty drink. The service alone gives this place a thumbs up. 

I've never had poached eggs before so I took the chance of ordering a eggs Benedict. Oh joy... happy I did. Poached eggs sitting on top of crispy bacon and English muffin and a side of potatoes. Everything was seasoned to perfection. So many options on the menu but everything was just enough to fill you up. 

At the end of the day... yes I would go back!

Stoked to find a decent bagel spot even though I'm a good 25 minutes from K&A (for now...).  

I'm so picky about my everything bagels.  

I cannot stand when 
1) places don't put enough crunchy "everything spices" (not sure of the technical term) 
2) places don't put salt on their everything bagels (hello? Did I not order an EVERYTHING bagel?
3) places only put "everything spices" on ONE side of the bagel 

K&A checks off all of my picky checkboxes!! Finally!  I came here twice in two weeks with my daughter and each time the bagels were perfect!  

There are so many horrible bagel shops in south Jersey. K&A joins that elite club of about 2 other bagel joints that are worth the drive.

After leaving the Voorhees Diner I was torn between 1 and 2 stars. A few hours later when my husband and I were feeling sick to our stomachs my decision was easy. 

We stopped in after dropping off our pup at the kennel and before heading out on a road trip. We're not in the area too much during breakfast time and saw that they were now open for business after a very long remodel. I was excited to try it especially after seeing how nice it looked on the inside. Everything was very upscale and fancy. Unfortunately this does not translate to the quality of their food. 

We sat at the counter and it took about 10 minutes for our waitress to come and give us waters and take our order.  We both ordered 2 eggs (mine over-easy, his scrambled), hash browns, and rye toast. I ordered scrapple (asked for it to be cut in half and deep fried since I like it really crunchy) and my husband ordered corned beef hash. 

It took about 30 minutes for our food to come out so needless to say we were already annoyed before we took a bite. My scrapple was cut in half but a complete mush. I waited for our waitress to come over but she never did so I flagged down a man who was standing 5 feet from us behind the counter the whole time (seemed like some sort of manager). When he came over I started to explain my scrapple issue but before I could finish my sentence he took the dish and without saying a word took it back to the kitchen. He never came back over to us, went back to his post, and I didn't see my scrapple again. Ok, I guess I was better off without it anyway. 

Hash browns were barely cooked and reminded me more of mashed potatoes. My husband kept finding egg shells in his scrambled eggs and did not like his corned beef hash at all (it was barely warmed). 

It took 10 minutes after we were finished eating for our waitress to finally come over. I explained to her what happened with the scrapple and the rude gentleman and she felt horrible. She apologized several times and asked many times if there was anything else I wanted. We just wanted to get out of there!! So even though I barely saw her, she was very apologetic about what had happened and she definitely seemed rather embarrassed (hence my back and forth between 1 and 2 stars). 

Two hours into our road trip and we felt horrible! I'll be sticking to my usual south jersey diner spots from now on. Eat with caution at the Voorhees Diner!

One of my favorite bars to go to in Philly. The vibe is super nice and chill, especially during the summer time. The patio area with the lights and hanging vines definitely creates a relaxed ambience. 

The menu for sips is (5-7pm Wednesdays during the summer) pretty good - $3 beers, $4 wines, and $5 cocktails. They also have decent food for around $5, I think. The cheese curds are my favorite. The sliders are average. Tacos are not bad either, but kind of small. The spicy chips aren't that great. They're a lot spicier than I expected. The wings were also a little disappointing. They were sweet for some reason, but it wasn't because a sauce or anything, so it was kind of weird.

I normally go here for dim sum once in a while, but the service has gotten so bad. We asked for two glasses of water and that took about 20 minutes to get. We ordered a dish twice, and it never came out.

I'm used to okay customer service at asian restaurants, but this is just ridiculous. When I paid the bill, I didn't put any tip since I have cash. The lady in the front said "the tip is on the table right?" Soooooooooooooo rude. As a customer, it's up to me to give tip or not. You don't need to remind me, that's an optional thing. I got upset and handed her the receipt, and she tried handing it back to me and "forcing" me to give tip. I was half tempted to not give tip at all, but that would be unfair to the servers. Never coming here again. Same food and better customer service at ocean harbour.

I wanted to try out Relais de Paris because I had read some good reviews, and it was even better than I expected. I had the steak frites, which came with a simple but delicious salad, perfect french fries, and one of the most tender steaks I've ever had. The sauce was flavorful and really enhanced the steak. I would absolutely recommend this restaurant!

Solid, especially among the Korean restaurants in Cherry Hill. Formerly known as Sammy Chon's, Dolsot House offers a pretty extensive repertoire of Korean staple dishes, from soups to Korean barbecue, although you won't have the grill in front of you. Located in a small strip mall, the outside is fairly unassuming, as is the inside, but the food is very good, so don't let the austere vibe deter you.

I've only ever come during lunch with my family, and I have to say the lunch specials are pretty bomb. You can get a bento box with your choice of meat, pickled vegetables, jap chae (potato noodles), rice, and salad, all for around $10. The creamy sesame dressing that comes with the salad is pretty great, and something I haven't seen before. My go-to is the dweji bulgogi (spicy pork), and while it's not scaldingly spicy, it does pack a bit of a punch, so beware if you can't handle spicy food well. 

Another lunch special is a large bowl of soondubu (tofu stew) or nengmyun (cold noodles), with your choice of grilled meat (I typically go for the Kalbi) for around $15. The portion of grilled meat is usually pretty substantial, so you should only order it if you're really hungry. As for other dishes, I highly recommend the haemul pajun (seafood pancake), since it's absolutely enormous and only around $9. You'll be hard-pressed to find a pancake that big with that much seafood for that price anywhere. For those of you who really like Korean fried chicken, their wings have been solid every time we've ordered them. I typically go for the soy garlic or honey sesame, since they're the most flavorful in my opinion.  Comparable to Bon Chon, and at a better price, I believe.

Service is a little slower when it gets busy, but they're very accommodating and friendly. I think it's a function of not having enough people to cover the entire restaurant when it's full. At the end of the meal, they give each person a mini bottle of Yakult, or Korean/Japanese yogurt drink. It's kind of sour and sweet with a very unusual flavor, so it might not be your cup of tea, but I grew up drinking it, so I highly enjoy the fact that they give this away at the end of the meal. Prices are cheap for lunch, but I'm not entirely sure if I would come for dinner. Just can't tear myself away from that bento box. 

I'll definitely be back during lunch hours when I'm back in Cherry Hill.

Yeah, I've completely bought into the hype, and I have no regrets. My friends (and the rest of Yelp) raved about this place, and after trying, I completely agree with them.

Had the fortune of being able to do Hattie B's twice during my 3-day trip to Nashville: once at a pop-up stand during the Music City Bowl, and another for takeout dinner on New Year's Eve. The pop-up only served tenders, but holy cow, those tenders were really great. The chicken had soaked just enough in the hot sauce, and there was still a crisp, despite the tenders being "wet" (heh), and dipped in the ranch, it was unbelievably good. It was that experience that made us realize that we had to try it for real the next day. The thing was that some people in our party also wanted to try Edley's BBQ for dinner the next day too, so we came a simple agreement: do takeout for both. Bang bang, and we're done.

Pro-tip: Do the to-go online ordering. It'll make your life so much easier, and it's really convenient. We did a massive online order and walked in and out without have to wait at all. And it was still absolutely delicious despite sitting in the containers for about 15 minutes. We managed to get more tenders, 2 large dark meals, and 1 large white meal. I usually prefer dark meat, and I have to say both types of meat were really good, especially with the pickles, white toast, and dressing that they gave us. Hoo-wee.

I can't speak too much about the service, but the people behind the counter were very kind and patient (I feel like you'd have to be with those crowds), and from the looks of it, they were very efficient with churning out orders to the masses of hungry people. Prices were very reasonable, with most meals being about $12-18, and easily very filling ones. The value, therefore, is definitely great.

A must-visit when in Nashville, but you didn't need me to tell you that.

I've never really been out at the bars in the suburbs of South Jersey, so this was a sort of strange experience for me, going out to a bar in the area where I grew up. It's just a little strange to go out drinking in the context of the area you spent your formative years. So Iron Hill is the only bar I've ever been to in South Jersey, and to be honest, I really liked it. Anyways, sorry for the life story.

Came in recently to watch the Eagles game and enjoy some bar food and beer. It was a good time, minus the Eagles being a dumpster fire this past season. But I digress. The place is split into two areas, a bar section with TVs, and a main dining room. Both are pretty spacious, so you can't go wrong. The full menu is available for both sections, so don't worry about a limited bar menu.

We went with a pitcher of the White Iron Wit (similar to Hoegaarden), which was only $14. Not sure how expensive that is in the realm of bars in the area, but given that we were used to New York prices, this was a welcome sight. We also went for the buffalo wings, which were huge, delicious and also a pretty good price, as well. In general, the menu is pretty extensive, so there's a lot you can try here. Nothing too crazy, but all the dishes we saw being brought around looked good.

Service was okay, but sort of uncomfortable since our waiter was being a bit too casual with us. I actually thoroughly enjoy when chatting up small talk with the waitstaff, but it kinda resulted in our food and drinks coming out late, and our waiter almost forgetting about bringing it out. Nonetheless, it wasn't enough to ruin the experience, and it ended up all right in the end.

Easily now my go-to sports bar in the area. Will definitely be back, should the opportunity for sports-watching present itself when I'm back visiting my folks.

Really good, and I liked the mix of Jewish and Asian cuisines. Pretty much perfect for me. I'm a huge fan of the Cooknsolo restaurants, mostly because of the concepts Chef Mike Solomonov puts out.

What we ordered:
- Potato latke with beef tartare: Everything you love about beef tartare, while adding a crispy, yet potato-y "crudite" underneath. Really good.
- Brussels sprout caesar: Quite delicious with the bitterness of the sprouts and the richness of the caesar. Also made us feel better about including vegetables in our meal, ha.
- Corned pork belly reuben: Portion was on the smaller side, but the bite of salty, corned pork belly with the pickled green tomato is an exceptional one.
- Veal Schnitzel tacos: Quite a nice blend of crispy, chewy, salty, and crunchy textures, and the meat was excellently prepared. 
- Hungarian duck, complete with fixings: Delicious, and expertly prepared. They don't actually do the real traditional slicing methods found in Chinatown, as the cuts are a lot thicker, but with all the sauces and the schmaltz rice, the dish is excellent. 

Service was a little spotty throughout the meal, but the food really just made up for it. It wasn't quite that busy on a Friday night, but for some reason, it took us a while to get our dishes and get our drinks refilled. Nonetheless, the waitstaff was very pleasant, and were quick to get us our things once we asked them. Prices are easily on the higher side, but the value is there, since all the dishes we got were really great.

Overall, Abe Fisher definitely met my high expectations. I'll have to come back to try that large-format short rib feast, as that seemed like it was a pretty filling and delicious meal. After really enjoying Zahav, Federal Donuts, Dizengoff, and now Abe Fisher, I am almost convinced that Mike Solomonov can do no wrong.

We came here for a rehearsal dinner, with one of the large rooms booked upstairs. First thing I noticed was that this place is a MAZE. It was hard to navigate the upper levels, but a really great experience, overall. Arnaud's history pretty much speaks for itself, but in the wake of the recent revamp, I have to say that the upholstery looks great. Not only that, it's a pretty calming, yet active oasis from the craziness that is Bourbon Street.

We had a set menu which gave you a choice of seafood or steak as the main course. Started out with the Shrimp Arnaud and the crawfish bourgeois. I gotta say, I love crawfish, and it's pretty great when all the work of crawfish is done for you. I also got to try the chicken and andouille gumbo, which was delicious and rich.

As for the filet au poivre, the flavor was delicious and peppery, and the asparagus and potatoes were all cooked perfectly. A relatively simple dish, but executed quite well, especially for a party of 80+ people. The famed bananas foster presentation was pretty great, and not only that, they tasted pretty delicious too.

Service was very attentive, with an old school flavor. Our server was very friendly and professional throughout, and got us our drinks and food with great efficiency. 

Overall, definitely worth a try for a drink in the lounges and a nice meal. Our experience overall was great, and would definitely come back for a nightcap next time we're looking for an escape from the chaos of the French quarter.

Our first stop for food in Nashville, and our first experience with hot chicken in Nashville as well. We were hanging out and listening to some live music nearby (duh), and were looking for a place that was open past 10 and had more than just alcohol. After looking up the Stillery on Yelp, we went for it. They also had live music playing, but we didn't know exactly where they were playing, since it was on the TV. 

Hot chicken sandwich was very solid, and the fries were crispy and delicious. There's always got to be a balance with hot chicken, so it remains crispy but has enough hot sauce to give the entire thing flavor. Brussels sprouts were a bit overcooked, but still decent overall, as there was a bit of a crisp on top to counter the mushiness. The pizza they had looked pretty good too, although most of us went for sandwiches because of the prospect of getting those fries.

Prices were very reasonable, with our meals only being about $14, and the waitstaff was very kind and patient. It was a little cold outside, so they ended up moving us to a booth further indoors after the previous party had left. Pretty cool that they were willing to do that with more parties coming in. 

Overall, a really good place with solid food in the throngs of tourists near Broadway.  Good for both larger parties as well as small groups, and a good spot for some late(r) night eats.

Warning - don't be tricked in to thinking that you'll have a great burger here because you won't.  I was looking for a classic, great tasting burger, and ended up with a cheap and bland burger that I really didn't even finish.  The place is a classic dive and so the burger could be a good dive burger if that is what you're expecting or looking for or if you've had too much to drink and it's like two in the morning.
But I guess that I'm a bit of a food snob and was expecting to get my burger on.

Great classic burger with good fries and onion rings along with a tasty shake.  Talk about calorie overload, save up for the day and then go here to indulge and enjoy.  They have a good selection of different types of burgers, ranging from fish to turkey to bison, along with all the usual ones.  I particularly like a double cheese burger with bacon.  Note that they also have a food truck so keep your eyes open for it.

This bakery or sweets shop is a bit of old and also a bit rustic but then again it also has live entertainment at times.  Net, it has a unique mix for a donut shop basically.  The donuts and cakes are pretty good but also a bit heavy.

What a great name but tough to live up to.  You have to have really outstanding grilled cheese sandwiches to have a name like "Grilled Cheeserie."  However, I found the grilled cheese sandwiches lacked that rich and creamy cheesy yumminess.  The pimento mac & chee was pretty good and the B&B of Tennessee was better.  Overall, solid grilled cheese sandwiches.

I've been back to the Sunday brunch at Sterling's Steak House in the Silver Legacy Casino several times.  It is definitely the best brunch buffet in all of Reno.  The food is prepared in small enough quantities that it is fresh, not over cooked, and very flavorful.  They have steak, shrimp, fish, lamb chops, and roast beef and ham along with the normal breakfast items such as made to order omelets and of course the usual sausage, bacon, eggs benedicts, and lots of fruit and pastries.  The desserts are good too.

The deli that Tampa is missing!!!

What a place! I mean I don't know where to start so I'm just gonna go by what see from the moment you walk in.  Immediately to your right you have a buffet of olives... I mean I don't know where else this exists.

Next you see a whole fresh fish section.

Directly across from this is a fridge of pre-made food which is all wonderful.  

My favorite room comes next... A wine room where there are ransoms wine tastings/sampling.

Next you enter the main area where you can order some of the best sandwiches ever, pre-made Italian food, fresh made pasta, desserts, and some of the best coffee I've had.

Even if it gets busy, max wait for food is 20-30min which isn't terrible (hard if you go for lunch during the week).

Just go and be amazed!

If I could give them a 0 star I would 
I was with a big group of all doctors going to this restaurant past weekend , so let me tell you about my experience 

1) we had a reservation for 8.45 by the time we were at our table it was 9.25 

2) we had no waiter so the hostess comes to help she has no idea about the wine list , no idea about the specials for that night, whatever questions we asked she said " let me go ask and come back " so you can imagine our frustration 

3) finally they give us a waiter and all the story starts here , this guy comes start taking the orders in a very bad attitude, mumbling " oh I'm gonna die " " oh I'm gonna kill myself " and when our friends are asking questions about the menu we hear him mumbling " oh shut up lady " we were shocked and kind of scared , then he goes behind my head to take the order from the person next to me i hear him back of my head saying that " oh I'm gonna die , I'm gonna die " and I hear he broke something , I was so scared that I didn't even look back and my friend who was sitting in front of me tells me he broke his pen 

4) he goes to the last dr to get the order he starts cussing us out in Spanish that Dr very nicely tell him " sir you can not use bad words " and he replies " yes I can " 

So when he did that, it was the last Straw for our group. we called the manager and told him we think he is high or something and we don't want him to serve our table 

5) manager just apologizes and put him back to serve another table " heyyyyyyy didn't we just tell you he might be high and he looks dangerous? And he broke the pen on top of our head ? """""

6) manager puts someone else in charge this new lady brings our food and one of my friends asks her very nicely , " excuse me , do we have a side dish as well ?" She replies " I have only two hands lady "

So we finally chewed down our food ask for the bill and this manager doesn't have decency to at least say , " you know what your desert is on us " so nothing,

I think this was the worst restaurant experience Ive ever had in my life

I met a girlfriend for lunch. We arrived early, and that was probably a good thing, 'cause the place filled up quickly.

Our server, Lance, was spectacular, repeated our orders to ensure accuracy. And he was very friendly.

I had an OLD coupon for a free pizza, and it was honored without a blink of an eye. BINGO!! Thank you, Pi!!

We decided to split a small simple salad: field greens, marinated red onions, grape tomatoes, croutons (which we declined) and parmesan with a red wine vinaigrette.

This was just the right amount knowing a large pizza is coming up. 

And it was a good salad. So fresh and crispy.

We split the pizza: I got The Hill. I can't remember what she got.

But we were both delighted with our pizzas.

We both ate one piece and took the rest home.

It was a delightful lunch!

My great friend and I met for lunch September 30. I arrived early -- to get a parking spot in their small lot behind the restaurant.

Burnt ends are only available on Wednesday.

The cash register guy was incredibly personable. When I told him I only wanted meat, HE GOT IT and offered some choices. I also said no bread.

My friend got a burnt ends sandwich with pit beans and potato salad. The pit beans looked rich and flavorful. The potato salad looked mustardy, but not too much. They both looked solid. He said they were good.

Other sides: coleslaw, Billy Goat chips, applesauce and pasta salad.

I got 5 ounces of burnt ends and 5 ounces of tri-tips. With a Diet DP for ~$18.

I tried all three sauces: Carolina Vinegar, Cranberry Cayenne and Sweet Jane.

The meats stood solidly on their own without sauce. I don't like sauce, because it masks the meat flavor.

Nonetheless, I liked the Sweet Jane best, followed by the Cranberry Cayenne. The Carolina Vinegar was too spicy for me.

The burnt ends were fabulous, meaty, tender and luxurious. The tri-tips were sliced thin, rare, juicy and flavorful.

Lovely attendant monitoring tables to remove plates, etc. She was very kind. Brought us to-go vessels WITH, if desired, little covered cups of sauces. I got the Sweet Jane and the Cranberry Cayenne to take home with my meat.

And she offered us a dessert. A metal pig sculpture dressed for the season and filled with "fun size" candy bars. I snagged a KitKat. He snagged a Three Musketeers. Her (the pig) seasonal garb was a Cardinals uniform.

They've got sandwiches; plates; combos; carryout combos; BBQ salad; meat by the pound; and sides by the pint, quart or gallon.

Meat offerings include: pulled pork, smoked salami, turkey, chicken, brisket, tri-tips, ribs and burnt ends (Wednesday only).

My to-go vessel was enough meat for two additional meals.

My college chum and I stopped in around 10:30 a.m. and were seated promptly.

This is a lodge kind of look -- a little rustic, a little homey. Hours are 7 a.m.-2:30 p.m.

They begin lunch service at 10:30 a.m., so we had our choice of breakfast or lunch. I was eyeing the Reuben, but then decided to go with breakfast.

My college chum got a short stack (4) of banana pancakes ($6.95) and added nuts (+$.95), and an order of bacon ($4.75). Bananas are in the batter, as well as sliced on top.

It looked beautiful. And the bacon looked nice and crispy. She liked it all.

I got the spinach omelette -- with tomatoes, mushrooms and feta ($10.95). It comes with pancakes, but I don't like pancakes, so I asked to sub extra-crispy hash browns (+$1.75). I highly disliked that hefty upcharge for potatoes.

Both the hash browns and the omelette were served on separate platters. I've never seen such a huge omelette.

Both were quite tasty. The extra-crispy on the hash browns was delightful with crunchy-crunchy on the outside and some soft, delicious potatoes on the inside.

The omelette was full of luscious flavor. All ingredients were in great abundance and blended well together.

Service was attentive and friendly.

My incredibly heavy to-go vessel lasted three more meals. I added a little more feta and some kalamata olives to the omelette to spruce it up.

Dang. It's been here since 1913, and I've never been.

My husband took our children every Easter season to pick out a chocolate animal. Invariably, every year, someone came home with a pig. When you can get only one piece of chocolate, you want it to be big, and you want it to be solid (not hollow).

My great friend and I came for lunch today, timing arrival to avoid crowds and lines, part and parcel of Crown Candy Kitchen. And we got a fabulous parking spot.

We arrived at 10:40 a.m. They open at 10:30 a.m. We got a two-person booth right away. Water served immediately. Menus at the booth.

Please note: no separate checks.
 
Tammie was our great server. We needed a few minutes to decide on our order. While discussing and contemplating, a guy in the booth across from us (of course, he heard our conversation), lifted up his BLT to show us the bacon depth. Gads, there must be a pound of bacon on that sandwich. And he showed us the half he hadn't eaten yet.

He got a grilled ham-and-cheese sandwich ($6.99), which comes with chips and a pickle; and a chocolate-banana malted ($5.19).

I got a large chili ($4.99) -- with cheese and onions (+$.99) -- and a hot fudge shake ($5.19).

All their shakes and malts are 24 ounces. You are delivered one of those old-fashioned glass sundae containers with a straw and a spoon. The beverage comes in the metal container used to create your confection.

Their chili is no beans. I like that. The cheese and onions were massive. The chili is sooooo good. Hefty. Spicy, but not hot. Thick and rich. I ate about 1/4 of it. Comes with three packages of oyster crackers.

The hot fudge shake was stellar. So rich, so wonderful, so fudgy. I drank perhaps 1/3 of it.

My great friend ate half of his sandwich. It was so big! And drank half of his malted.

AND, he gave me his pickle . . . which was divine!!

We left with a lot of future meals. And when we walked out, there was a line of diners.

We timed it well.

I had lunch here last month with my college chum.

The place is beautiful and so well appointed.

But THEY DO NOT SERVE DIET SODA!

I was so put out with this announcement, that I almost upped myself to going to the quite convenient QT to get my own diet soda.

Keep in mind that they offer sweetener for coffee or tea. But they don't offer diet soda.
Figure that out..

My college chum got the turkey burger with fries.

I got the Prasino burger with French onion soup.There were other options available as the side with the burger, but they weren't on the menu and were recited by our server -- which makes me think they may vary from day to day.

The soup was delicious and would have served as a meal in and of itself. It was served in an iron casserole with great broth, nicely cooked onions, very large croutons (really pieces of French bread) and cheese (maybe Swiss or Gruyere).

The burger was great-tasting, cooked perfectly meduim, and the tomato jam was quite nice.

My college chum said her turkey burger was fabulous and was so good and moist, it could have passed as a meat patty.

The food was good. I can live without the pretentious crapola . .  and if I go again, I'll stop into the QT for a diet soda.

My college chum and I met January 2 for lunch. We had great service. We both drank water.

She got two pancakes with extra syrup ($6). This may sound like a small meal and it did to me, until I saw the size of these pancakes. They were the size of the plate!

I got an omelette ($9.95) with roasted red peppers, caramelized onions, white cheddar and turkey sausage. The omelette comes with four additions. I opted out of toast and hash browns. And got a fruit cup.

More than four omelette additions cost 50 cents each, with plenty of additions available.

And there are premium additions: smoked salmon and lump jumbo crab for $2.50 each.

This was a lovely meal, and we got a chance to catch up, without any pressure to leave.

She liked her pancakes.

My omelette was PERFECT! The roasted red peppers and caramelized onions were such tasty additions. And the turkey sausage was small pieces scattered about -- which gave me a piece of turkey sausage in every bite. Great composition. And the eggs were beautifully done.

My fruit cup was ridiculously fresh: blackberry, raspberry, kiwi, grape, honeydew and pineapple. What a glorious mix of fresh fruits.

I took home half of my omelette and half of my fruit cup, which served well as lunch the next day.

I met a girlfriend Tuesday for dinner.

The tables are very close, so I listened to two couples talking about dental implants, with massive details, before my dining partner arrived. I could have puked. Not a good way to start a special dinner.

After listening to all that, gol dang, I needed a cocktail. I got a dirty gin and tonic with olives. It was not nearly as dirty as I would have liked.

Tom was our stupendous server. I ordered arancini for us to share. The order is three balls, but Tom said they can sell by the ball. So I said, just give us each one ball.

These weren't so good, and they were sitting in the sauce, so the bottom would get soggy. I've had arancini one other time -- at Pan d'Olive -- and they were made with potato, not rice, with steak and gorgonzola. With dipping sauce on the side.

These were made with rice and some gooey cheese that messed it all up. Plus the bottom of each ball was getting soggy in the sauce. The sauce needs to be served separately for dipping. It should be your option.

My dining partner got a stack salad, which was gorgeous. And she shared. Dang, that thing was good. Layered tomato, flash-fried eggplant, buffalo mozzarella topped with roasted bell peppers, basil and balsamic reduction. Holy cow!! It was amazing!!

Entrees: She was excited that they make their own pasta and got the tagliatelle bolognese ($19) -- meat sauce with parmesan reggiano.

I got veal piccata ($23), which was fabulous with capers and a lovely, creamy sauce.

What a stupendous dinner, great dining partner, fabulous service from Tom. I just wish their tables were farther apart. I have no need to hear somebody else's dinner conversation.

Good Frank Sinatra music.

We both took home another meal with our leftovers.

This is how The Blue Owl does reservations: they don't take reservations, except for parties of 5 or more. For smaller groups, you can call the morning you're going, give your name and approximate time of arrival. Check in at the hostess station when you get there, and they fit you in.

My college chum and I arrived at 11 a.m., and were seated right away. The place was bustling. We opted to sit on the veranda, which was covered and well-ventilated with many ceiling fans.

Our server was delightful, efficient and helpful. She kept our iced teas filled, and we had a decanter of water at the table.

We both got the Terrific Trio: you pick three from salad, soup, quiche, sandwiches and dessert.

She chose 1/2 Cobb salad, 1/2 Reuben and the Caramel Pecan Levee-High Apple Pie.

I chose 1/2 Cobb salad, a cup of Canadian cheese soup and 1/2 Reuben.

All their salad dressings are homemade. She got Thousand Island. I got bleu cheese, and it was fabulous.

The Cobb salad was HUGE and full of bacon, chicken, black olives, bleu cheese chunks (not crumbles), tomato and lettuce. The flavors were lovely and so fresh. I do not know how this was 1/2 a salad. I ate half, then moved on to the soup.

The soup was thick and creamy, full of mashed up potatoes, celery, carrots and onion, Canadian bacon and cheese. For all of that, it was not chunky, but amazingly smooth. And delicious.

The Reuben was terrific. I've never had such tender and tasty corned beef. The marble rye was toasted. Good amount of Swiss cheese. It was a little light on the sauerkraut -- for my taste -- but I love sauerkraut.

And it came with a tasty, crunchy pickle spear! YUM!

My college chum didn't eat her pickle, but I didn't notice that until the server was taking her plate away. I almost grabbed it. But I do have some modicum of couth, so I restrained myself.

Her Caramel Pecan Levee-High Apple Pie was the largest dessert I've ever seen. She loved it, and took more than half of it home.

I took half of my salad and half of my sandwich home. Our server was kind enough to bring me two to-go vessels, so the dressing from the salad didn't get into the sandwich. And a bag for easy carrying.

And she brought us to-go iced teas!!

Service was spectacular, and it was just a delightful experience with fabulous food!

My girlfriend and I had lunch Thursday. We both opted for the lunch special: $12.95 for half a salad and a small pizza.

Molly was our fabulous and friendly server. She had a shadow, who I presume was a trainee.

My girlfriend got the Fried Artichoke salad and the Margherita pizza.

On the pizza, she had her choice of San Marzano tomatoes, fresh basil and Mozz; OR EVOO, cherry tomatoes, fresh basil and Mozz.

She went with the San Marzano version.

I got the Fried Artichoke salad and the sausage pizza: fennel sausage, caramelized leeks, fontina cheese and pine nuts.

We were provided a beautiful piece of bread with olive oil. It might have been sourdough, but we didn't touch it.

This half-salad was the hugest half a salad I've ever seen on a beautiful rectangular white plate: fried (but not breaded) artichokes, pistachios, goat cheese, asparagus and spring mix with a balsamic vinaigrette.

Whoever devised this salad is a genius.

The play on textures and tastes was spectacular. I think the artichokes were fried for texture because if they had not been fried, they would have been soft.

However, I think the frying took away some of their flavor.

Three beautiful spears of asparagus overlaid the entire salad, necessitating a knife situation. I was raised to NEVER take a knife to a salad.

I had to ditch that concept, or I would have had asparagus spears hanging out of my mouth like fangs.

The pistachios added a great super-crunch.

The goat cheese was not too much. I know goat cheese is all the rage, but it is a potent-potent cheese. If you add too much, you've over-powered the dish.

I was glad to see a spring mix and not all arugula, which is too peppery for me. The spring mix was fresh and lively.

And the balsamic vinaigrette was just perfect for this salad, without too much balsamic (which, again, is an aggressive flavor).

Now that I've dissected the salad, let's move on to my pizza.

The crust was crunchy, yeasty and flavorful.

The fennel sausage was prominent (as appropriate) and had a great flavor.

Caramelized leeks -- I know they were there, but they didn't shout out to me.

Fontina cheese is a good-melter and noted for its earthy, mushroomy and woody taste. There are milder versions and this may have been one of them.

I love pine nuts. These weren't toasted. When pine nuts aren't toasted, they're waxy. And that's what I got. But they provided nice crunch.

I ate all the salad, which could have included the plate. But I'm not confessing to anything.

After that, all I could eat was two pieces of pizza.

I took four pieces of pizza home along with the bread they provided with our salad.

This was two more meals. The bread was great and had a touch of either kosher salt or sea salt on the top, which was wonderful.

Ben S. and Charleen S. provided another dang-bang Dim Sum UYE February 1!! This was the 7th annual, and the second time I've been able to participate.

I loved everything I ate, but I don't know what I ate. I heard names but there were so many dishes on the Lazy Susan, I didn't know which was which.

It didn't matter. We had a lovely, sumptuous meal. And everybody had a good time.

I liked the vegetables: carrot, cucumber (?) and something else -- very tasty and crunchy -- on a plate with thin-sliced pork, which was very flavorful.

Most of the other things were in bundles, so I didn't know which were which -- but I ate 'em and liked 'em. And I got full fast, 'cause there was a lot of dough involved in most.

I especially remember a scallop/shrimp bundle that was incredibly fresh and tasty.

And a soup meatball you had to let cool a bit, and then pop it in your mouth all at once -- to get the meatball AND the soup. Holy cow! I was glad somebody told me how to eat this thing. It was terrific as one bite.

Thanks to Ben S. and Charleen S., and Wonton King for accommodating our group. These folks are glorious and happy to serve!!

I met yesterday with former co-workers -- like about 17 of us.

It was a great little unofficial reunion. Service was spectacular. I put my drinks on a card, and they didn't mess it up. A couple folks ordered appetizers. And the spinach-artichoke dip was a winner. It is pretty amazing.

My girlfriend and I returned January 11. We were offered to take any table, so we did.

She got a salad and the Roberto pizza: brown butter, EVOO, roasted Sicilian potato, wild mushroom, pecorino, fontina, goat cheese and toasted pistachio breadcrumbs.

She ordered to take home: seafood pasta --  mussels, clams, whitefish in a tomato broth.

I got a salad and the Papperdelle pasta.

To take home: Gemelli pasta.

The house salad is just plain-old good, like ridiculously good: mixed greens, Italian peppers, mozz, olives (with pits).

We both took home half of our salads. It wasn't because we didn't like them. It was because we had to stop eating to have room for the entrees.

Her pizza came out first, and she offered me a piece. Glory, crazy . . . pizza like I've never had before. Crusty-crunchy-flavorful ultra-thin crust. Toppings were such a fabulous blend of the three cheeses with the wild mushrooms and potato, and crazy-ass pistachio breadcrumbs. I'd get that on a carryout in a New York second.

The Papperdelle was perfect -- categorized as a ribbon pasta, it was so thin and wide, it held sauce perfectly. The sauce was a light tomato sauce with roasted red peppers, pistachios and itty-bitty meatballs that tasted so well of fennel. So tasty.

The Gemelli pasta is a wonderful stretched-out corkscrew that holds and retains sauce, which was a meat-thick tomato sauce. It was a wonderfully balanced dish.

We left with lovely to-go vessels. For $51 (without tax or tip), I got 8 glorious meals.

I went today for lunch with a girlfriend. We arrived around 12:15 p.m. It was not crowded. The bartender looked at us. I don't think he said anything. If he did, I didn't hear it.

Someone (hostess? server?) came over to seat us at a hightop for two in the bar area. And she brought us water.

Service throughout was painfully s-l-o-w. And I mean REALLY SLOW! Our server NEVER looked at me, just at my dining partner. He seemed so, so timid.

We ordered chips and guac for $3. Chips and salsa is $2.50 or $2.75. 

The guac was terrific. It's not just smashed avocado. There's pico and queso fresco. The chips were not salted. They were tasty and well-crunchified. But a little snap of salt would have been helpful.

We both ordered the same thing: one grilled fish taco ($2.50) and one carne asada taco ($3). We both wanted the roasted duck taco, but they were out of duck. How does that happen on a Tuesday at lunch time?

All tacos are served in house-made corn tortillas. If you want sides, they're a la carte.

The fish taco can be either wood-grilled or fried. We both got wood-grilled. It comes with chipotle baja sauce, cabbage, pico and queso fresco. But I don't know what kind of fish it was. We both suspected tilapia.

The carne asada taco was grilled flank steak, baby arugula, creamy avocado serrano sauce and queso fresco. The flank steak was rare to medium-rare.

The tacos were good. They both had plenty of protein, nice flavor, good unique sauces. I would call them small.

We were finished eating for quite some time . . . nobody asked how the food was, nobody asked if we were done.

Our waters were never refilled. We each got one refill of tea/soda, and sat without beverages for quite a while.

Once the bill came, it sat and sat and sat after we quickly put our money in the folder. $12 apiece (which includes tax and tip) for two tacos, guac and chips. And 90 minutes of our time.

The place looks good! Not overdone. Good colors.

My college chum and I came for lunch August 14.

I followed Tom J.'s cue and ordered the goat soup. Dang, it was good. Wonderful vegetables, great tender meat, lovely sauce. I did the lime squeeze, the onions and the cilantro --  skipped the jalapenos.

Then, I ordered Huevos Rancheros.

Then, when I checked in on Yelp, I got a free taco. I wanted a fish taco. That was not included in the free taco offering, so I got a free beef taco.

This was one big dang lotta food.

The eggs in the Huevos Rancheros were PERFECTLY cooked. Oozed tasty yolk.

So much food. I took home at least half of my soup, half of the Huevos Rancheros and the entire free beef taco.

This is where it gets ugly. My college chum noticed this rating in the window.

Le Tejana Taqueria has a Grade B rating (82%) from the St. Louis County Health Department: http://www.decadeonline.com/insp.phtml?agency=STL&violsortfield=TB_CORE_INSPECTION_VIOL.VIOLATION_CODE&record_id=PR0002712

The routine inspection was July 29, 2015. You will notice (in red) that some of the violations are classified as critical.

I'm sure they'll get re-inspected, but I don't know the timing on those things.

Last ugly thing, in my reheated goat soup -- which was still tasting quite fine -- I found three large bones. At least if the bone is large, you're probably not going to swallow it. But you could break a tooth. So, I had to stop eating it.

And then I got rid of the rest of it.

I got a two-seat high-top . . . happened to be in the bar area, so I got to enjoy "Happy Hour" prices on beverages, which is 3 p.m.-6 p.m. Not geared to the worker-bee. Who on Earth is doing this afternoon Happy Hour??

I ordered the "regular" burger, which was two patties with lettuce, tomato and red onion. I was offered cheese, and accepted. No mention of the upcharge. But there it was on the bill.

The ONLY side offered is fries, so I asked about other choices. Yes, any of the sides can be had with your burger. I chose the macaroni and cheese. Well, hello, that was an upcharge as well . . . said upcharge not mentioned.

I understand upcharges, but please tell me.

The macaroni and cheese had Cheetos on top -- a comical and unexpected tasty crunch. It was served in a jar. There was plenty of cheese with the macaroni, it just wasn't all that cheesy-tasting.

He didn't ask me how I wanted the burgers cooked. They were done . . . as in DONE -- both patties. Dry. Cheese was on one patty.

No condiments on the table. None were offered.

There were lots of families and children this night. It was rather loud; no big deal. The atmosphere is pleasant and inviting.

Their draw is the beer taps at some of the booths. I'm not so sure it's necessary to encourage additional drinking. Besides, unless you're an expert beer-drawer, you pay for the foam.

My dear friend and I came for lunch at noon January 10. Service was spectacular.

We both got the cod sandwich special for $10 that came with cole slaw.

He got the whole fried cod sandwich. I got the grilled cod without bread.

The cod was fabulous, so fresh and tasty. The cole slaw was vinegar-based, incredibly good-tasting.

This is the first time I've left a restaurant without a to-go vessel.

Thanks, Sarah S. and Anthonino's, for a tremendous International Supper Club get-together August 24.

Eleven or 12 of us were gathered in this great place that has been redone since my last visit. It was great before. It's greater now. And it felt much bigger. I'd also say a little fancier.

Everybody ordered what they wanted, and our server was a champ at keeping separate tabs (except for couples). They did an excellent job at that.

Some apps were passed.

I got the House Salad and added gyro meat. What an incredibly filling meal. I might have been talking too much, 'cause I took home probably 2/3 of the salad.

Great camaraderie with all the Yelp diners.

I was a little worked up, because I'd just had an unplanned biopsy earlier in the day. I hope everyone was patient with me.

As it happens, I was at Anthonino's the Monday prior with a girlfriend, August 17.

We sat at the bar waiting for a table, but it was a short wait.

Taylor, our server, was so fun and on-point!

I got the Palermo Chicken ($17) -- Charbroiled, topped with lemons, capers, Sicilian olives and white wine butter sauce. It comes with salad, and pasta or vegetable. I chose the vegetable (tomato, zucchini, carrot).

The chicken was m**st, not overcooked and the vegetables were amazing. Who would think that combination of vegetables would be good? But it was.

The salad was delicious.

I took home two more meals from this visit.

I met girlfriends for dinner Friday. I was waaaaay early and was seated in the bar at a table for four.

My box from Pie Oh My was welcomed, which was a good thing, since I thought I needed to leave it in the car, which would not have been good.

Meg was our glorious server, and she did a perfect job with check-ins and beverage refills.

Chips and salsa were fabulous, and each diner gets their own saucer for spooning salsa from the jar.

One dining partner got the Pollo en Pepian Dulce ($16.95), a Guatamalan dish: grilled chicken breast with a sauce of ground pepitas (pumpkin seeds) and sesame seeds, red bell peppers, tomatoes, onions and garlic stewed in a bitter orange and cinnamon-infused chicken broth, served with white rice, grilled asparagus and garnished with roasted almond slices and Pisco bloomed raisins.

The other dining partner and I got Aji de Gallina/Aji de Camarones ($17.95), a Peruvian dish: grilled chicken breast or eight large shrimp covered in spicy ancho, habanero and citrus cream sauce; served with saffron rice and garnished with slices of hard-boiled egg, kalamata olive and slivered almond.

She split hers as half chicken, half shrimp. I got all shrimp.

This had a little kick to it, but it was a beautifully composed dish. I cut all my shrimp into little pieces, along with the hard-boiled egg to be sure to get some of everything in each bite.

A fabulous dish with juicy and flavorful shrimp, a complex creamy sauce that blended so well with the rice, egg, brininess from the olives and lovely crunch from the almonds.

I really don't know how all these ingredients went so well together.

My hefty to-go vessel lasted four more meals.

Two words: lobster bisque.

Yes, at a deli. Their regular soups are lobster bisque, matzo ball soup and chicken noodle soup. Today, they also had minestrone.

I perused the online menu numerous times before my girlfriend and I came for lunch. Be apprised, there is much more to the menu in the store than what you find online.

Order as soon as you walk in the door. Get a red-and-white boat of those delicious pickles, or take a whole crock of pickles to your table. Select a table. They'll call you to the counter when your order is ready. And that's when you pay.

For $5.16, I got a HUGE bowl of incredibly rich and tasty lobster bisque. Had I not been in public, I would have licked the bowl.

My girlfriend got the Rachel, as she did last time we were here.

We went a little earlier than our previous visit, and parking was more than tolerable. That will be our tactic on our next lunch.

This place opened Saturday. It's open 11 a.m.-7 p.m. every day.

I went for lunch today. It's clean and new with cheerful colors.

You order in the back, then make your way up to the register while they make your food.

I got a vegetable samosa ($1.50) and a gyro salad with lamb ($8.99).

The folks in front of me got gyros, and there is a whole array of toppings from which to select. They got feta, cilantro, white onion, lettuce and tomato. Those gyros were quite large.

The vegetable samosa was fresh, crispy and hot. The filling was abundant, and the spices were spot-on.

The gyro salad was huge with beautiful greens (no iceberg), tomatoes, red onions, croutons, feta and plenty of lamb. He put some white sauce on as a dressing, and I asked for an extra container of Tzatziki. That just made it perfect.

I usually don't like croutons on salad, but these were itty-bitty and gave a nice little crunch factor.

Sami, the proprietor, was at the register, so I talked to him a little about the store. He is extremely friendly and thanked me for my patience, although there was no delay.

The salad is lasting two meals.

My girlfriend and I went for lunch. We both got a plate, which includes two sides and a popover.

She got pulled pork ($12). I got pulled chicken ($11). We both got the same sides: white cheddar cracker mac, and green bean and tomato salad.

They had three sauces on the table: My Sweet Bestie, White BBQ and Mustarolina.

I tried them all on my finger. They were fine.

But the chicken was great by itself. Moist and smoky.

My girlfriend's pork was infused with tarragon. I found that interesting for a smoked meat. She found it awful, as she HATES tarragon. She gave me a taste of if, and it was full of some herb, and I didn't care for it.

She didn't eat it.

The sides: the white cheddar cracker mac tasted OK, but it was dry. Too much topping.

The green bean and tomato salad was good.

And the popover . . .  I have no idea what it was. I took a taste, and that was it.

Service was incredibly slow. Yes, he came by to fill my water glass.

But it was an agonizingly long lunch.

I took home half of my chicken and half of my macaroni.

I met a HS girlfriend for late lunch (3:30 p.m.) Thursday, January 10.

We had excellent service. And . . . as it turns out . . . we were there during Happy Hour. Who knows when Happy Hours are these days?

The chips are incredibly thin. In fact when they came to the table, I thought they were potato chips. But they were good. Coulda used a splash of salt.

The salsa was thin and drippy, so get a napkin in front of you, or you're gonna spill it on your clothes. The taste was OK, but not great.

I ordered Barbacoa Street Tacos ($12 for three). They were double-tortilla'd. I did not appreciate that AT ALL. And it was not mentioned on the menu for the Street Tacos.

The taste was fine, but the cabbage was overly large strips for being a crunchy item, and the cilantro was over-generous. The meat was kinda smooshed into the bottom of the taco, and it ended up being like a paste, so that texture was crappy. The taste was OK.

Met my college chum for early dinner Friday night. Not too many patrons for the duration of our visit.

Our reception and the service were quite nice throughout. Water refills were always at hand, as was plate-clearing, offering of dessert and delivery of to-go vessels.

We ordered meat samosas for appetizer ($3.95) -- triangular pastry filled with ground beef and spices. Two sauces were served in a condiment caddy -- one green (quite spicy) and one maroon (less spicy).

We selected the samosas for two reasons: description and the order comes with two -- figuring that wouldn't be too much of an appetizer!

These things were huge! Extremely crunchy on the outside and tasty meat/spice soft on the inside. After I tried both sauces, I just ate my samosa naked. It was quite flavorful, and NOT spicy hot.

I would not call the outside a pastry as I know it; I'd call it more like a hush puppy outside (but harder), but not cornmeal like a hush puppy. The menu did not call these deep-fried (as it did for other appetizers), but my guess is they were deep-fried.

Entrees:
Chicken curry ($11.95) -- chicken cooked in tomatoes and spices
Lamb sagwala ($12.95) -- lamb cooked in spinach and herbs

Heat: we were offered a scale of heat beginning with medium, then spicy, very spicy, hot, and on and on.

I opted for medium for the lamb sagwala. She opted for one step above medium for the chicken curry.

She got garlic cheese naan ($4). I got garlic naan ($2.50).

We got a lovely share platter of rice garnished with peas. Great presentation and nice thought to spiffing up the look of a white platter full of white rice.

Our entrees were in individual casserole dishes.

She liked the chicken curry, but said it wasn't as thick as she liked. The taste was fine. But I did notice that it looked a little runny. She loved the garlic cheese naan.

I tried her chicken curry, so I understand about the consistency, but the flavor was delightful, albeit a bit spicy for my palette. But it didn't make me delusional.

The lamb sagwala was spectacular -- thick, lucious, deep flavor, wonderful mixed with some rice, or I could have eaten it by itself.

The garlic naan was the garlickiest I've ever had -- and that's a good thing!

We were both stuffed, and half the food was still sitting on the table. I got it all, since she was eating out all weekend.

So we put our food in the styrofoam containers, wrapped the naan in foil, and I'm trying to open the plastic bag to put it all in. It wasn't happening. The guy who took our orders came by, gently took the plastic bag from my hand, smiled big (which he hadn't done the whole service), and opened that derned think in a New York second. Then he smiled bigger as he put all our containers in the bag and tied it in a knot!!

Yippee!!

High school girlfriends met for Happy Hour March 15. Happy Hour is 4 p.m.-6 p.m.

Bob was our friendly and informative server. While we were struggling with the menu (everything sounded delicious), we ordered beverages. One got a lager, one got a take on a mint julep, one got Brut champagne, one got a special Juniper cocktail, and I got Ratsalad beer -- brewed by 2nd Shift Brewing in New Haven, Mo.

I couldn't help it. The name was too funny. Bob offered me a sample first, to see if I liked it. It was a little hoppy. Not too hoppy for me, but one of our party tried mine, and it was too hoppy for her.

When I ordered my second one, I giggled. And it wasn't from the beer. It was from the name.

We got a complimentary Labneh with Benne crackers, which was incredibly delicious -- all homemade in-house. So, we had that to snack on while contemplating the menu.

Our appetizers were: deviled eggs (two kinds), chicken and waffles, mushrooms on toast (Ozark Forest mushrooms with cheese curds and Missouri pecans), hoe cakes (scallions, kimchi, crispy head cheese, Stl bbq) and BLT.

Since we were sharing all appetizers, we asked Bob to have them cut everything into five pieces, which was accomplished beautifully.

Appetizers came out rather in shifts, which was just fine for us.

Holy cow, was this food good. I can't even say which one I liked best, but the deviled eggs did stand out. But I just LOVE deviled eggs. For me, #2 was mushrooms on toast.

We had our own little plates as we passed appetizers, and all plates were brimming with delicious food. And it was all so beautifully presented.

This is a gorgeous facility. All wood is repurposed barnwood, including some sliding doors and all the tables. Bob told us all about the facility, where they cater for private parties (next door), including a conference room upstairs for smaller private get-togethers.

When Juniper moved in, it was empty. It was nothing before, so they built from the ground up, from the brick walls in -- you get the picture.

Bob also told us about the brick walls, which is a St. Louis history lesson in and of itself. He was a fount of information, and it was all interesting.

We had a great time, great company, great service and great food.

My girlfriend and I came for lunch October 13. Order and pay at the counter. They bring the food to your table.

We split a large Greek Salad ($7.50) -- Iceberg, kalamata olives, cucumber, pepper, onion, feta, tomato, pepperoncini and homemade dressing. It came with two pitas that were fresh and tasty.

And we both got the Colossal Gyro ($8.50) -- Gyro meat, onion, tomato, tzatziki, lettuce and feta in a pita.

The Colossal differs from the Traditional ONLY with the addition of lettuce and feta, and I HAVE TO HAVE FETA ON A GYRO.

The salad was fresh, and the dressing tasted like Italian. Good flavors.

The gyros were STUFFED, and the feta was plentiful. I knife-and-forked it. It was just that perfect blend of ingredients where they all hold their own and you can taste them individually, and yet the entire thing is greater than the sum of its parts. Just delicious.

I took the leftover salad home, and we both had a to-go vessel of our gyros -- kinda massive.

I had three more meals, and the pita never got soggy.

The restrooms could use some spiffing up. There's a nice patio on the side.

College chum and I went for lunch Tuesday. Plenty of folks in the house.

This place is a nice redux from former occupants. More vibrant and more exciting.

She got the roasted mushroom pizza ($12). Shitake, oyster, portobello mushrooms with garlic, fresh herbs, goat cheese, and a provolone-mozzarella blend.

I got the lobster and crab bisque ($5).

And the Beer-Cheese Sandwich ($12), which included sirloin, beer cheese sauce, lager-braised onions and peppers on a Hoagie.

After eating this incredibly rich soup, which was wonderful, I wasn't really inclined to eat much else.

Except for the incredible dill chips set lovingly aside of the sandwich. They were stupendous.

So I picked at the sandwich and the homemade fries that came with the sandwich. Everything was good, I just was full from this rich soup.

So, I took home MOST of my sandwich and the home-made fries.

Together, I had three meals.

My friend and I were going to Peno for lunch January 17. Unbeknownst to us, Peno is no longer serving lunch. We stood there thinking about what's close.

I knew Protzel's was sorta close, but it was a mere two doors west on Wydown.

So we walked there.

We both got the same thing: small rare roast beef sandwich with mayo on an onion roll. And YES!!!! I ATE THE ROLL!!

You pay when the food is ready. And there were PICKLES!!! The big spear looked so inviting, I asked for a second, and it was happily added to my plate. We both drank water.

We sat at a table (probably only three in the house, but numerous stools at counters).

We had a lot to talk about, so it ended up being a two-hour lunch -- at a deli!! It was so fun!! And we were never rushed or encouraged to leave. And it wasn't packed. There was plenty of activity, but it was takeout.

It is amazing the deli, sandwich, salad offerings at this place. And so many types of soft drinks. And grocery items. They've packed a lot of stuff into this small space. It's not fancy. It's GOOD!!

I'd go again in a New York second and probably get a Reuben with extra pickles on the side, of course.

We both took home half of our sandwiches.

My girlfriend and I went for lunch July 30. Her suggestion. We sat at a booth in the bar. Quite close to the restroom. Kinda a plus.

We both got the prime sirloin meatloaf, which comes with fries. I should have asked for broccoli. Fries only last for -- you eat four or five, and then you're done. They were fine. Shoestring-style.

The meatloaf was incredibly rich. It was a mound -- not a loaf. And covered with ketchup.

I was not blown away with this meatloaf. For one, it was too rich. I took three bites and was done. For two, the overwhelming ketchup was waaaay too much.

Leftovers were better, 'cause I added A-1.

I think I found out what service is like at Jimmy's when you're two women dining, not drinking and using a LivingSocial coupon  -- thanks to Nicholas. Or maybe that's how he is with all patrons.

We got great food. We were not well-attended at any time during the course of our two-hour dinner in the bar area. That's where we were seated. And we had a reservation.

The bread basket wasn't refilled and the only reason we had water refills was there was a bottle of water on the table. And he never came by to see how the food was.

Nicholas made it clear that we could not order any appetizers during Happy Hour that would count on the coupon. That's different from how it worked last time I was here with a coupon. So, does each server get to make their own rules for these coupons?

My dining partner got the Grilled Roast Pork Loin ($18.95) --  With sage-roasted fingerling potatoes, sautéed napa cabbage and bok choy, pancetta bacon vinaigrette, pickled beets and horseradish creme fraiche

I got the Roasted Chicken Fettuccine ($18.50) -- Pan-roasted squash and zucchini, bacon, artichoke, pulled roasted chicken, roasted bell pepper cream sauce and parm

After we ordered entrees, Nicholas said we could now order Happy Hour appetizers, since we ordered entrees. Well, thanks for that. I think that timing was waaay off!

The chicken fettuccine was fabulous. Huge pieces of juicy and tasty chicken, an abundance of vegetables and not a pound-ton of fettuccine. Great proportions. It would have been a bit better if the chicken and the artichoke hearts were cut up more in proportion with the other vegetables, so you could get some of everything in one forkful.

For dessert, we shared the Granola Apple Crisp ($7) -- Oatmeal granola crust, sliced apple and streusel topping, served warm, topped with cinnamon ice cream with candied walnuts and caramel sauce

My dining partner asked for a separate plate, so we weren't double-dipping. They brought out one plate and one spoon for her. I got nothing. Somehow the concept was lost. I had to use the HUGE serving spoon to eat my dessert.

This was really good. Rather deconstructed on the plate -- a little of this here, a little of that there. Very attractive.

When it came time for to-go vessels, my dining partner wanted to put her own food in her container. So, she asked for him to bring out the containers, instead of boxing it in the kitchen. He absolutely did not want to do that. And it took a bit of talking to accomplish this simple request. I don't understand why that was so challenging.

We both had hefty to-go vessels, once they were brought out for us.

I am very, very, very sorry for this review. And I wish I had been in circumstances that it could have been addressed at the table. But I must explain.

We had a celebration luncheon (celebrating ME) that included the office regulars (the 4 of us), my director and my vice president.

The 4 of us arrived first and were informed that the reservation had been changed to 5. Well, that's not what we understood. So we had to stand at the hostess station while they changed the table from 5 place settings to 6. And we were right. There were 6 of us. So I don't really know what the mix-up was.

I chose the wrong entree. The goat cheese torte. It came with mixed vegetables and a salad with a skimpy goat cheese torte my vp couldn't even see until I turned the plate totally around. Everything was touching and getting mixed up. That wasn't really the big problem.

The big problem was, the torte had a sour (mold) taste. I could not eat it. Didn't know if it was the goat cheese or the goat cheese gone bad. And I was embarrassed to say anything with both my director and vp sitting right there. So I said nothing. And I DO like goat cheese.

I should have gotten the Hot Brown or the crabcakes or the Burger Meister, or just about anything else.

We had to ask for a basket of bread. Menu says so. Shouldn't be like that at such a fancy restaurant. 'Cause were were waiting for luncheon partners, us 6 having come in three cars. But beverages were replenished quickly.

Lunch orders were:
#1 -- Club sandwich (she skipped the avocado). She chose salad as her side. It looked fabulous. The sandwich was soooo thick.

#2 -- Vegetarian sandwich. She chose slaw as her side. There was portabella, asparagus spears arranged perfectly like little soldiers sitting flat in a good-looking sauce/spread that kept them in place, roasted red peppers. Other stuff. She ate half, loved the slaw and gladly took half her sandwich home.

#3 -- special fried oyster BLT. She chose macaroni and cheese as her side. I believe this was an upcharge, but Connor (our server) didn't mention it. Sandwiches are offered with side (included with sandwiches -- no extra charge) of slaw, fries, green salad or potato salad. The side she chose was listed at the bottom of the menu in the section called "Sides." I didn't see the bill, but I'd bet it was an add-on. And that wasn't mentioned.

The sandwich was immense. The macaroni and cheese side was immense. She was a-cluckin' about this wonderful lunch. And said the bread with the sandwich was fabulous, too!

#4 -- Vietnamese stir fry with shrimp and scallops. She got it with brown rice and ate every bite.

#5 -- Hot Brown, famous from The Brown Hotel in Louisville invented by chef Fred Schmidt in 1923, http://www.brownhotel.co....  . This is only the second time in my life I've seen Hot Brown on a menu. The other time was at the Timber Creek Grill on Highway K just off I-64 in St. Charles County.

It's an open-faced turkey sandwich with sliced tomatoes and topped with an abundant amount of tangy cheese sauce (like a rarebit). I forgot what side he chose. But he said it was all great!

And then there's #6 -- me.

I added a star, because everybody else really enjoyed their food.

My girlfriend and I have been wanting to try Carl's for quite some time. Every time we think about going, it's Monday, when Carl's is closed.

We went today. Not wanting to get into a crowded diner or having patrons standing behind us waiting for us to vacate our stools, we went early -- arriving about 10 minutes before Carl's opens at 11 a.m.

Watch which door you use. Once you're in, you cannot get to the other side without exiting, walking around the building and entering on the other side.

Rather varied menu: burgers and cheeseburgers (single, double, triple), footlong hot dogs, chili, pork steak, tamales, Reuben dog, grilled cheese, fish and chicken. Fries and onion rings.

Just about anything you get ON your food costs extra: lettuce and tomato, grilled onions, and cheese sauce. Ketchup, mayonnaise and mustard are NOT extra.

My girlfriend got a double cheeseburger with ketchup, mayonnaise and tomato; fries; and a bottled water.

I got a double cheeseburger with mustard, grilled onions, lettuce and tomato; and a large diet DP -- $7.30.

Our lunches came up pretty quickly. They were working diligently.

Our server was friendly. The three women cooking, pulling root beer and taking carryout orders over the phone didn't say a word to anybody, except themselves.

You can watch them working on the flat-top and frying the potatoes and onion rings, both of which are frozen.

The burgers were A-OK; served on itty-bitty paper plates. A lotta bun. I could have used a triple. Crispy edges, but actually, the entire burger was crispy . . . not just the edges. I like crispy edges, but I don't want the whole burger to be crispy like a potato chip. It was so crispy, I didn't taste much meat flavor.

I would say these patties are two or three ounces each.

My girlfriend ate some of her fries. It was a reasonable portion. I tried one. It was A-OK -- not those atrocious crinkle-cut frozen fries, but a variation ALMOST verging on a steak fry.

This is not a place to linger. You get a stool (16 are available; eight on each side of the grill/food prep area). Order your food. Eat your food. Pay for your food. You're done, and you exit.

If you need to use the facilities, you have to tell them. At the back of the building, there's a red door that is locked. They have to let you in.

I was so glad it was a flushie. We didn't know what to expect: an outhouse or a Johnny-on-the-Spot.

I'm not from St. Louis, so I have zero nostalgic memories of Carl's. I know Carl's has been around a long time. And probably will be around for another long time.

It's cash only.
.

My good friend and I came for lunch August 2. Our strategy was: arrive at 11 a.m., just when the place opens.

I got the right door this time, and I was the first to arrive. But I let others in when the doors opened, because my good friend wasn't there yet.

My friend came virtually on time, but he had gifts I needed to put in my car. A beautiful zucchini, a fabulous home-grown tomato and a great book to read.

The line hadn't expanded exponentially, so we were in good shape.

We both got a combo meal -- two meats, two sides and a beverage (~$17).

He got turkey and ribs (four bones), potato salad and baked beans. He opted for water.

I got ribs (four bones) and brisket, cauliflower salad and green beans -- and five pickle spears. I cannot do without those dang dill pickle spears! I opted for diet cola.

We both enjoyed our food. The ribs were toothsome, tangy and tasteful. I ate them naked. My friend tried a couple sauces and liked them both.

These are not fall-off-the-bone ribs, thank goodness. Those are backyard barbeque or crockpot ribs.

He liked his sides. I didn't taste them.

The cauliflower salad was ingenious: a greenish vinegar-based thin dressing with red onion, white onion, black olive, green pepper and a small-dice white cheese (but it coulda been tofu) along for the ride with the cauliflower.

This was such an amazing amalgam, and it was perfect!! WHO thought this up?!?!

The green beans were beautifully tender-crisp and well-seasoned.

The pickles were perfect, as always.

He took home his meats. I took home all my couldn't-eat-it-here, including two pickles. I got two more meals out of this outstanding array.

And I refilled my diet cola on the way out.

November 25, for Thanksgiving, I went for cakes.

German Chocolate and Carrot. I needed to walk them out of the store, so I needed to buy what was on hand. No custom ordering.

They have three sizes: small, medium and large.

Happily, they had a medium of both cakes. We have had these cakes before, when I got them for 2016 Christmas. They are deliriously, wonderful, moist, tasty and incredibly beautifully decorated cakes.

On Thanksgiving, these cakes were winners! They beat out the homemade pumpkin pie. Beat out the homemade pecan pie.

Dang good winners!!

Office birthday lunch today, party of 8. Birthday person gets to pick the place -- it's a rule. Parking is nasty if you park right in front of the restaurant, because you'll be backing out onto Manchester Road. Not necessarily the best idea!

Cute place. When you walk in, you're right there in the bar. I never saw a hostess station. So, if you have to wait for a table, I don't know where that's done. Lots of little rooms and what looked like a large sunroom.

Seated. Got beverages. Server left us alone for at least 15 minutes -- to contemplate a ONE-PAGE menu.

Pizza's supposed to be a specialty. NOWHERE on the menu is there a list of the toppings available. Hello?! Give me something to work with!! Somebody orders mushrooms on pizza. She asks, "Canned or fresh?" Hmmm! That portends trouble!

I got (as did 3 others) the lunch special for $9.79: 9-inch pizza (1 topping), salad or soup, and soda. I chose: sausage, salad and Diet Coke.

Somebody wanted a Margherita pizza -- server didn't know what that was. That portends trouble!

Salad was greens, provel, 2 grape tomatoes. I have no idea what the dressing was, but it was all tasteless. That was trouble!

Pizza was edible -- but just barely. Topping was sparse. It seemed, and looked, overcooked. That was trouble!

Two at the table got pasta con broccoli. The sauce looked redder than I would have thought it should be for this dish. The broccoli was sparse. And the portion was meager, even for a lunch portion. And we had a guy at the table who gobbled up his dish in no time flat!

The person who got the Margherita pizza said it was truly the worst pizza she'd ever had in her life. It didn't seem like it was fresh basil they put on it. It looked like spinach. She said it was in slimy lumps throughout the pizza.

The winners at this meal were the two who got salads: one got the spinach salad; one got the chicken Caesar salad. Both enjoyed their dishes.

We WERE well-hydrated!

We sat, and we sat . . . finished with food, some needing boxes . . . and we sat, and we sat.

This disaster took TWO HOURS!!!

At least we backed out onto Manchester Road and lived to tell about it!

Drive-through Saturday. Cheese quesadilla and beef burrito. Nothing special. And no sauce, no offer of sauce, no sign of sauce anywhere.

The menu is plain-old pedestrian Mexican food.

Cost nearly $13. Isn't that expensive?

Lasted two meals. Used my own sauce at home.

Window woman wasn't friendly.

Loved everything about this place.  Work close by and have been anticipating the opening so was excited to try with the family. You must order the cornbread and the Shrimp and Grits (Savannah style) were outstanding. Great service and suggestion from the staff.

 Great outdoor area that I hope they are able to utilize somehow with our harsh winters.  They said they are opening lunch in a week or so.  Will definitely be back.

We went here today for breakfast and felt the quality of food and service was excellent! It is in the Schnuck's plaza opposite Crazy Bowls & Wraps (Olive/Mason). I had an egg white omelet and my fiance had the biscuits and gravy. Both were great with really excellent. I love the quality of accompaniments (house made apple butter or strawberry vanilla jam) as well as side dishes (low fat cottage cheese, kale salad, roasted mushrooms). I'd love to come back for lunch and try their bison burger or lamb burger. They have a full bar, wait staff service and an outdoor patio. Tom, a co-owner, has amazing restaurant experience and we know this will be a success.

So incredibly RUDE. DO NOT GO HERE. The staff has NO class. WOW! I will NEVER come back to the place again. They have the worst customer service I've ever experienced. It was my sisters birthday and I made reservations. I was the first one there and decided to grab a drink at the bar. Ordered a dirty martini and the bartender made me the drink and then I sat there waiting for the rest of my party. While I was sitting there I noticed the bartender staring at me and then he came up to me and said 'did you like your drink?' And I said yes thank you. (Not realizing that he was WAITING for a tip, even though I was still sitting there!) Normal customers tip when they leave the bar, which is what I do! He then proceeded to tell the other customers at the bar 'people don't appreciate good drinks around here'! So I left a 25% tip and said thanks! We then went to our hibachi table. Excited bc it was my sisters birthday and ready for the fun to begin! 

Well...let me tell you...if you want a fun bday dinner don't go here. The chef we had was miserable! I was expecting some 'hey, ho, heyyyy!' Throw a shrimp in your mouth and do some fun tricks. He literally didn't even crack a smile. Just made the food and that's it. We then asked the waitress if we could get saki bombs and she said 'can you wait I'm  too busy'. Understandably we said 'it's ok whenever you get a chance'. Like we were bothering her! 

Then a waitress was walking by and dropped a glass right by us. The glass went RIGHT into my sisters shoes and we had to dump it out! Literally DUMP GLASS OUT of her shoes. I get that it was an accident but they showed no remorse or concern! Not even an 'oh my gosh I'm so sorry'. 

To top it alllll offf! And this is what made me write this review in the first place. My boyfriend left a 15% tip on our bill! WHICH IS REASONABLE considering the service that was given to us! The waitress literally RAN after my boyfriend and said 'why no more tip?' And my boyfriend said 'because the chef was horrible and we came here for an experience and we didn't get that' and she said 'well we split tip and it's not enough'  WHAT?!? You got 15%! On a SHITTY service! You should be happy! My boyfriend rolled his eyes and left 5% more because he felt that THEY need it more than us! 
But I've NEVER been to a restaurant where the wait staff DEMANDS more of a tip. Here's a tip....why don't you tend to your customers and you will get the tip you DESERVE!
