Never in my life will I return To this shitbag of a place. DISGUSTING service and you should be ashamed  with how you service your customers. I don't know if it's a culture barrier but you ALL need to learn some manners and CLASS, because Lord knows you need it. I'm appalled how you think it's acceptable to RUN after your customers and question the tip. So unethical. Especially when we left you a 15% tip! Thanks for ruining my sisters birthday dinner. We will never return!

Let me preface ths post by stating that I am a louder than average energetic Father of 3 sons (5, 3 and 2).

I have enjoyed the Bistro as one of town's few breakfast options for our early schedule.  We are typically one of the first customers on Sunday at 7:45am/8am.  The people are usually very nice, professional and the food is good.  This used to be one of our favorite weekend rituals.

This morning we (me and my 3 young sons) sat at a table and everything seemed normal until the end of the meal.  2 things happened.  #1 - I ordered yogurt and it was a more traditional Greek yogurt than supermarket Greek yogurt (apparently).  And the granola had a strange spiced/herbal taste to it. When I complained, the manager Nick made it a point to  have an open debate and aggressively tell me how I did not know Greek yogurt and that I was wrong for not liking it.  And #2 -Minutes later a table next to us (older couple) shouted as we were leaving "thank God. You and your kids are so annoying"  To which I responded "have a great morning" and left a little embarrassed and a little annoyed.  Baffled as Haddonfield folks are typically very friendly and understanding of kids/volume.

I state this because I decided to call the manager back after an hour upset that he felt the need to tell me off and lecture me about yogurt.  This is where things go south.  He barrages me with derogatory remarks about me and my family and how he cannot stand us.  He goes on to tell me that all the customers always complain (I haven't ever experienced this before and we have been there about 30 times).  He goes for the jugular by stating that we have no common sense on how to behave in public (as if we are animals).  At this point I am flabbergasted and tell him that he could have simply pulled me aside if he felt me and my family ended to quiet down.  And that this is the first time anyone has lectured me from a restaurant that I loved.  His response "there's af first time for everything and don't come back ever."

Done.  And I will make sure all my neighbors and social media outlets are fair warned.  Completely unacceptable to thrash a customer and his kids.  A simple warning if the noise was too much would have been nice but the rest of his anger filled insults are not acceptable regardless of how miserable a morning he was having.  He felt a need to hit personally.

Sorry the lack of common sense is on the manager.

My husband and I ordered takeout from here a few nights ago because Thai is my typical pre-test good luck meal. Frankly, I've tried just about every Thai restaurant in New Orleans, and this one blows them all away in the flavor category. Inside the restaurant seemed like a really fun vibe as well!

We got an order of pad Thai (duh), which was so flavorful, just a hint of sweet (not overly sweet like some places), savory, not fishy-so well balanced. We also tried the crispy pork with kale and fried egg (this was so delicious, but they did forget to put our rice in the bag unfortunately so we were a little sad about that), grilled pork shoulder (rich, crispy, sweet goodness), and the khao soi noodle soup (awesome flavor, didn't break, with yummy big chunks of meat).

For spice level, we got regular on the pad Thai, which was perfect for me. We got spicy for the soup and my husband enjoyed that-he loves spice though so may try the Thai spicy next time.

Goes without saying this will be our new go-to for Thai. Only wish they delivered!!

We came here last night with a few friends from out of town. It's beautifully decorated inside, moderate lighting (usually like a little more sultry for evening dining), kind of hustle/bustling/busy, and definitely quite warm (thighs sweating on the booth cushion ). However, the service was awesome-thanks Brian! And the food and drinks were yummy.

I got a mocha martini (like a tasty smooth alcoholic Yoohoo), and my husband got an Old Fashionthat he enjoyed. To eat, we got the wedge salad (light, fresh, flavorful), bbq shrimp (so tasty, could have drank the tasty marinade in the bottom of the bowl-maybe ask if or extra bread to sop it up?), chargrilled oysters with gruyere and pancetta (so rich and delicious), and Brie burger (holy yum! Crispy fried Brie, cooked perfectly medium rare, and added the thick crispy bacon and and the fries were awesome)

Overall, we enjoyed ourselves and will be back.

Although I am not vegan, I have had plenty of vegan cupcakes before and have made my own.   These cupcakes were overpoweringly sweet, expensive (about 40 bucks for a dozen), and the woman working here was quite rude.  

When I came into the store she didn't bother greeting me or getting up from her seat a few feet behind the counter.  I told her I was ready to odrer...I picked out about 10 cupcakes and was considering what to get for the last few.  Not only did she not offer any suggestions, but she huffed and returned back to her seat behind the counter telling me to let her know when I was actually ready.  2 seconds later I told her I was ready again and she begrudgingly got up...I told her which ones I wanted and took a slight pause b/f telling her my last choice when she huffed again and told me again to let her know when I was actually ready.  "I'm ready!  I'm ready!" and I just picked any old cupcake because I really wanted to get out of there.   And 40 bucks later, I am never going back here again.

I am still not sure why I ever mourned the Dickey's BBQ place that closed that was in this location?

At a recent Yelp event I heard from many people that this place is some of the best BBQ in the STL, so I had to go and try it. Especially Stephen W. who said he was basically the Ambassador for this Place said I had to go, which I would have told him I was going but he still hasn't accepted my stalker oops I mean friend request. Anyway...

This was a spur of the moment visit after Running a 10k 
the day before. So you can imagine I was hungry. We decided to go and I was not sure what to expect mainly because shame on me I hadn't really read any reviews yet on it. We brought our Kids too, and that is a real test of any establishments ability to deal with Chaos, take a 4 year old and a set of 2 year old twins to eat there. 

Right away you walk in and there was a sign on the wall that was hand written that said 15 minute wait. I assumed that meant that if you are standing here reading this there will be 15 minutes to wait before ordering. Luckily we walked up around the corner and there was about a 4 minute wait and that gave us time to look at the menu and take note that the Excel brand of soda they serve is High fructose corn syrup free and uses pure cane sugar. That is a big deal to me and made me feel good about the place right off the jump. 

Next we got lost in the menu... wait I mean the 2 menus all scattered of painted on the walls and pieces of paper taped with sides listed. It was kind fun though not like a lost for days not understanding what the heck to order or conflicting prices. 

I loved the next step you basically got your food on a tray with Brown parchment paper laid out on it. This made me smile and catered toward my eating style of lot of space to mix sauces and what not. 

I ordered the Brisket, which was cut right in front of me. I wish he would have weighed it because at first I thought it wasn't a lot but then I was thinking maybe I got more than I should have because I couldn't eat it all. The brisket was good but not as moist as I would have expected, but it was so delicious with all the sauces that it didn't matter. I also got the fresh cut fries (the Bomb) and the Gumbo, which was the show stopper. I loved it and would be back for a huge bowl just on its own.

My wife ordered the turkey, coleslaw and fries. Her turkey was so moist and full of flavor. The Cole slaw wasn't anything special but my 4 year old ate it before her burger.

My 4 year old got a "kids" burger which looked like a regular burger. She didn't eat it but ate all her coleslaw and meats we gave her from our trays. The burger was good, but I think the spices on it were to much for her.

The sauces were excellent and I liked the big squeeze bottleful of sauce, made it easy to get as much a you wanted. Like some have reviewed the bottles labels were a bit worn and I couldn't easily tell what some said, so I just tasted them all, yet another great thing about the tray lots of room for sauce. Surprisingly the Coffee sauce was actually really good and my wife liked the Autumn orange and Hana lulu sauce. I did ask if there was HFCS in the sauce and they said the base sauce they use has it in it. I am at this point not ultimately concerned with the condiments. I know I could be but all in all they have less bad stuff overall. And they have Grass fed beef burgers!!

So to wrap it up. Yes it is amazing, No it may not be your favorite, Yes it can still be my favorite, its effing delicious, you may not think it is effing delicious, that's ok, more for me.

If I could rate this experience less than one star, I would. Never in any of my restaurant experiences have I been made to feel this uncomfortable. We were at this location on December 2nd around 9pm. We were at the location for a birthday party with a party of six. The hostess I spoke with, Ellie , at first refused to seat us because our party was too large. I asked if our party could be split into half or a smaller group because we went to this location specifically for a special occasion. The hostess again refused to serve us and said we could order Cake to go. I asked her if there was any possible way to seat us because we drove at length to get her. She finally said that she would see what she could do. She then proceeded to pull over three other people working and begin to literately gossip about our party. The servers were all staring at our party and laughing while rolling their eyes. The rest of the evening was extremely uncomfortable because we were the last in the shop to be served. When we walked up to see the cake selections another sever (not sure of her name but she had blonde hair and black glasses on) was talking to another male about our party and how "annoying" our party was. To add insult to injury, the hostess Ellie, continued to talk about the clients in the shop and our party the rest of the evening with the other staff. It felt more like a gossip session than a relaxing evening out. I find this kind of service extremely upsetting especially after we have heard such great things about this shop. Needless to say I don't think we will be returning to this location due to the way we were treated on our first visit. I've always highly recommended this place to people visiting Indianapolis based of off reviews but sadly can no longer do that.

Update: after voicing a concern via twitter the account proceeded to block my twitter account. Nothing I said was rude or out of line from a normal customer concern.

I've waited quite a while to review Frieda. I wanted to learn a lot about it to include in my review. Frieda is a great spot to get lunch solo or with friends/colleagues, study quietly, or join a group. Let me elaborate:

Frieda offers a menu of fresh breakfast, lunch, and pastry items. You can get a sandwich, wrap, or salad or opt for a frittata or soup. Their pastries are made on the spot, often in view of the cafe. I love watching them make their cakes and sweet delicacies. There's quite an art to it. My favorite sandwiches are a toss up: some days it's the curry chicken wrap; others it's the turkey with their delicious Frieda chutney. I've become such a regular that the staff greets me warmly and knows I'll be asking for a hot chai latte. Oh yes, their looseleaf teas and lattes are great as well!

Their motto is CONNECTING GENERATIONS. This is the second part of Frieda I was curious about. I didn't understand, so I asked staff to explain. They offer a great space for people to come and play games. There's frequently a table or 3 of ladies playing Mahjong around 1 PM on weekdays. They also have sign-up sheets on the front wall near the door. They have a movie club, book club, German- and French-language clubs...really, this place has it all. They wanted to open a space where people could come and meet others of all ages and interact. They also have a great program where senior citizens make the pastries and jars of jelly. Frieda pays them fair wage. Now, who can't get behind a mission like Frieda's?! I love the place. 

Frieda is nestled on Walnut Street between 3rd and 4th Streets. It's next to the Polish American Cultural Center. Check it out.

My review remains about the same. An important update: their lunch menu is smaller than it used to be. It includes about 10 varieties of pizzas and a limited non-pizza section. The non-pizza section omits the sandwiches now. This is important, as their Brick Oven can bake only 4 pizzas at a time. If you go to lunch with a group and all order pizzas, they'll arrive 4 at a time.

The space manages noise extremely well. They have music playing near the back, but it doesn't drown out conversation like it does at other restaurants. The space has a lot of sound absorption. This is an ideal location if you'd like to have a meaningful conversation with your table.

Yum yum yum to everything at this place.

The food is out of this world. It's so amazing to see a vegan/vegetarian restaurant do literally everything well. Everything we ordered was delicious. For our entrees we got the Patty melt and kimchi and holy shiite, I can't wait to eat it again.

They also have amazing seasonal kombucha! We got the passion fruit, safflower, and basil and it was awesome. The basil really cuts that apple cider vinegar taste most booch's have!

One thing that really stood out was how much they seem to value their employees, and you can tell people loved their job. I have never seen a restaurant, business, etc. put this type of respect on display (see the faces of graze photo).

We will definitely be back!

I'm giving Old Castle a solid five because not only did they make us feel like a million bucks up in there, they delivered on good, wholesome, traditional German American fare without breaking the bank.  You can get all sorts of mains on their lunch menu under $10 you'd never see anywhere else.  They've got the right beers.  The right attitude.  Food's good.  What more could you ask for?  

We'd been here once before and they were too busy to serve us; but they'v expanded, growing into and opening up next door as well.  Nevertheless, we came back because something about them sounded, smelled so good; the way they treated us when they sent us away.  All bespoke of who they are and what they do.  

To me, German's mostly not unlike Mexican or so many other foreign comfort foods; food of the poor.  So it should be cheap.  A few hot dogs (and I know they're a bit more than that) and pasta (spaetzle) shouldn't ever be more than a few dollars but most German places try to hold sway over a wallet but not Old Castle so much.  First time I've felt that way in a long time.  Good stuff.

btw, we drove up from Orlando just because.

Easy solid five for that hot pastrami sandwich! God damned God damn. Absolutely Loved it so much it's become something of a benchmark and none of the others since have been as good. None of them! It's a damn shame I live so far away and can't put them on my regular foodie hit list. I miss that sandwich, man. Right up there with Katz's.

Otherwise everything else was pretty good. Friendly helpful attentive service. Happy happy happy.

Easy four or more. Was sort of slow when we popped in to see what's what one day in the middle of the week but was fun. Solid hospitality. Enjoyed the beers so's all well.  Hung out at the bar, played around outside, was fun. Was well tended with warm hospitality.

Was good. The place the space was nice and our waitress was sort of over-the-top but not overwhelming though almost. She deserves five stars all-day-long!

Interesting tapas and Italian eats, curious food stuffs. Salad was really good.  Meatballs were dense, with a wonderful gravy; like my mom makes, not full of binder like so many seem to want. They do the bread and the oil. Nice touch. Who makes a taco pizza? I went in on it for the novelty of it but should have gone with one of their mainstays.  Liked it, didn't love it.  Ate all the leftovers, so there's that. lol.

Enjoyable and would definitely return.

I'm from the land of theme restaurants so it takes a lot to impress me but I'm also a car guy and would have been happy at hello!  

Honestly expected to be disappointed thinking this was just another tourist trap but was wholly satisfied by a thoroughly enjoyable experience with colleagues.     

Was in on an off night and went in on that Guinness soup, which was pretty awesome, one of the burgers add onion rings, and those original nachos too.  What a fun and immersive experience.  Waitress was super friendly.  

Easily a solid four swayed on up to five with the fun and creativity factor.

Bumbled upon this place a few years after venturing in on a foodie adventure with an X.  Was fun and a good respite ripe with beers and respectable food stuffs.  Was one of three lunch covers and the server was unabashedly personally recovering from a hangover which was cute and wasn't.  I don't know that I'd travel here but when nearby, fun fun.

Was talked into a banger sammy which I wish I hadn't, but was decent enough alright okay.

Easy solid 5 for some of the best comfort food I've had in a long time. Happy friendly attentive service. Nice craft draft and excellent cocktails. They really feed you here.

Exactly the kind of experience I've been looking for in so long I can't even remember. Delicious.

Easy four or more for this nice locals sports bar spot that's as old as me, since 74. You know, sometimes you wing a thing and after a foodie snafu somewhere else we lucked out and ended up here and I'm so glad we did.

Everyone was very friendly and nice; attentive. Hospitality's warm. Weather was beautiful for the outside seating though we chose inside. Was all private, supper club like.

Bison burger was pretty good and cooked to temp which back home would be a miracle. Plenty of side choices like steak fries, tots, chips, curly fries, and more; thank you. And the "famous" turkey chili's no joke, so good we actually bought a quart for take-away and I don't think it's going to make it through the night.

Wish I were a local to make it my mainstay.

Mnmmm.... really wanted to like em and was so very hopeful going in this would be our best of "quintessential" St. Louis BBQ experience but we were unfortunately early one lunch and the ribs were just okay, alright, with fewer spots of tender than tough ...enough to just not really like them enough as hoped. Was okay though, they weren't bad, just not excellent is all.

Hey, sauces were good. Concept's familiar. Hospitality was off but they just opened so maybe they weren't all geared up for the queue which is also probably why the ribs weren't so good either; prolly from the day before methinks.

Anyway, I know they're better, just didn't get it when I went.

....so far as the comment from Management goes, we still ate them ...and the leftovers. Wasn't excellent but also not worth complaining about on the day is all.

So I Loved Blue Ducks food, let's be straight.  Food was fantastic!  Slamburger and bacon fat fries were delicious but we found the front of house crowded and confusing. Not sure what's with the hostess taking orders so we thought we bypassed all that, sat at the bar, but ended up with a sufficiently sufficient bartender. Asked about duck fat fries, got a snappy response. 

Lunch was a little much, about $100 for the two of us. A burger, chicken sandwich, two cocktails and two beers usually runs us about 60-70 bucks. $$$

I've been to Blue Moon twice since they opened.

The wait staff has always been very friendly and the atmosphere is comfortable.  

Great waterfront views and a relaxed decor.

Maybe it's because the place is new, but there was an awful lot of staff milling around doing nothing and there were a few times where we waited quite a bit for service considering how many people they had on hand.

They have no happy hour specials and the liquor is insanely priced: $22 for two shots of patron silver.  Really?!  Stick with beer.

The food is good, but not great.  Again, their pricing is off the mark.  And, who puts fish tacos on a hard shell?

The management was not receptive to suggestions and in the end, that may be their downfall.  Don't check on my table or ask how my meal was if you can't take constructive criticism.  Also, go to other marina restaurants in the area and see how they do it.

I'm hoping at some point I can come back and improve my rating.  I'm excited by new places on the west side and want them to succeed.  However, based on the experience I had last night, we won't be back for a while in the hopes that they get their act together.  

It's really unfortunate too because we were going to try the inaugural brunch this upcoming Sunday with some friends/potential new customers.  Now we're not.

Okay so any reviews prior to this past week should be ignored. No not because my palate is amazing but because the restaurant recently had a makeover as part of a hellish tv show. The menu is paired down to one page and the service is attentive. The food was mouth watering and done correctly. I had the bruschetta as an appetizer and it was one of the best I have

I really don't understand how anyone can like their Philly Cheesesteak. I guess I will avoid all food recommendation from those reviewers . 

Now seriosly, this was the worst cheesesteak I ever tried. No flavor whatsoever. Even the fries were bad. 
Not to mention they charge way to much. 
And what's up with the system of ordering steak on one window and fries and soda on another. Doesn't make much sense. 

This is my first one star review...  And the reward goes to...  Geno's steaks!  Congrats!

What's not to love about Trader Joe's? Great prices, vast selection and amazing customer service! This was actually my first official visit at this location. I went to their location in Knoxville, TN while I was in college but would only get a few items. I decided to read a few blogs from people who shop regularly at TJ's to figure out what the "must have" items are. I selected a couple bottles of red wine, chicken jalapeño sausages, orange chicken, chicken pot stickers, carne asada, a sirloin taco kit, dark chocolate peanut butter cups, dried mango and soyaki sauce. I've had the soyaki sauce quite a bit and it's delicious to marinate in salmon or chicken. 
They carry a couple of my go-to items from Kroger at a fraction of the cost. 
I foresee myself making a stop here once every few weeks. Highly suggest checking this place out!

Ripple Bagel & Deli used to be my hangover cure when my husband lived within walking distance while we were still dating. Now, it's an indulgence that I don't get very often since we live farther away. I always get the Big N on a jalapeño or everything bagel. It's delicious and messy and everything I want in a bagel sandwich. My husband recently tried the Loxy Lady and enjoyed it. You can order ahead online and leave certain ingredients off or add whatever you like. You can also choose what kind of bagel you want. If you haven't been, you need to check this place out!

Just month later and prices are higher. The drink I liked (Hong Kong Latte) is more expensive now: $3.75 plus $0.75 for soy/almond milk! It was $2.99 and it was acceptable. Haven't tried it again but I hope it's not so sweet anymore.
The selection of products is still poor. For example, I went in to look for Stevia and Manuka honey. They didn't have it.
I came back to give another try and see if I can find some reasonably priced and delicious vegetarian dish that is also healthy. But nothing. Only two vegetarian soups (sour tomato soup and sweet corn soup) $5 for smaller cup. Falafel burger (with white bread) for $10 and eggplant sandwich (white bread again) for $8.50 (tax incl).
Why don't you have multigrain or rye bread? - "We are working on it", they said.
I decided to try the Eggplant sandwich with caramelized onions and goat cheese - I think it was kind of sweet, little bit bland, little burned and pretty oily. I would rate it 3/5. My husband said it's tasteless.
I also noticed that some employees have "It's not my department - ask there" attitude. Not a big deal though, as I understand each employee responds for his own "area", but I always notice such things in hospitality industry.
While I walked around I noticed so many people, all eating white bread burgers and fries. I mean, if you like this type of food, go ahead but this place is not for me. Looks like expensive, higher quality "junk food".
Also their ice cream options are limited. No chocolate, peanut butter or hazelnut ice creams! Last time, I was there it was only vanilla ad tiramisu left, the rest was empty.
3 stars because of the location and their delicious (and expensive $7) healthy smoothies. They are really good. I loved the "Mojo Enhancement" with banana, strawberry, ginger, dates, cacao powder and cashews. So good!
They also have some nice pastries upstairs that are pricy but really tasty. Their mini cheesecakes are a rip off. So small and cost $5, and a simple cupcake $4 (!!). Insane prices.

We came here mainly for the 75 cent happy hour oysters! I made reservations before we arrived in NOLA specifically during the HH time. We found that we didn't really need them since we came on a Wednesday and it looked like they weren't too busy. 

Service was great - our waitress was extremely friendly and attentive. We ordered two dozen oysters and shared the jumbo louisiana shrimp "en cocotte" which had roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausage. The oysters were delicious - I had gone through about 6-7 until I saw what I thought was a red vein on my oyster... yikes, it wasn't that at all. I picked it up with my tiny fork and I couldn't believe what I was seeing... the little thing wrapped itself around my fork. It was a tiny little red worm. I found another one on another oyster. That was it for me, no more oysters for the rest of the night. I called over our waitress who then brought over the manager. He informed us that their oysters come fresh and that these worms are naturally found around the oyster shells, but not normally when they are plated at a restaurant. I asked if I could eat them since I could potentially have eaten one already without knowing and he said no. This worried me at the time. But I did some research online and it seems as though these worms are probably harmless. Nobody really wants to see a worm during their meal, c'mon... honestly, I just think the oysters weren't properly shucked and thoroughly cleaned before plating. 

I appreciated the offer for a new set of oysters. I declined, but my boyfriend agreed (not sure how or why) but was super careful eating them. They also gave us fried oysters on the house. The appetizer & two dozen oysters were taken off the bill so we only had to pay for the shrimp entree we had ordered. 

I guess that's the risk when eating anything raw.. lol. No more oysters for me, I'm sorry.

So glad we stopped by to try this place on our trip. It was probably one of the best meals we had! A line started forming outside the door quickly after we were seated (we came a few minutes after opening) and most people were carrying luggages (I assume they went straight here after their flight or are enjoying this as their last meal in NOLA!) 

My boyfriend and I both ordered their fried chicken which came with 3 pieces of chicken (white meat) and a side. I got a side of mac and cheese and he got their mashed potatoes. Each plate also came with a side of what were the most delish peas I have ever had! The sides were so good... thinking about it right now makes my mouth water! The chicken itself was yummy, especially with the hot sauce. I really loved how light and airy the breading was!! 

A must try in NOLA.

I really wish I had the appetite for AYCE sushi, I really do. So many things I would've liked to try but I get so full so easily.. We opted out of AYCE because I knew it wouldn't be worth it getting AYCE unless I was super super hungry. We sat at the bar and gave our orders to the sushi chef. He was super friendly and always made sure we got what we needed. We had only ordered three things - their Mt. Rose Roll (tempura shrimp, hamachi, salmon, scallop, spicy kani, green onion & unagi sauce), Godzilla Roll (yellowtail, deep fried in tempura, topped w/ unagi & sriracha sauces, sesame seeds and green onion), and their seared tuna which was topped with ponzu and unagi sauce. Everything we ordered was SO good. The seared tuna and Mt. Rose had to be my faves!! The fish was so fresh. Mm!!

The rolls here are a whole lot cheaper than most sushi places I know. Really affordable! I'd definitely come here again if I'm ever in the area again.

I rarely enjoy going out to eat for breakfast, but wow did the bananas fosters french toast really impress me! I never get anything sweet for breakfast and usually stick to something safe like eggs so this was a first. Something about the texture and flavor of the french toast was very nostalgic - it reminded me so much of the bread my grandma used to dip in her hot coffee every morning. It was perfect and not overly sweet. One of the best french toasts I ever had. I didn't get to taste the crab omelette, but it looked decent! I would've loved to try their shrimp and grits!

I have been here several times for several reasons.   

The staff is friendly and everything is face to face.  Drive thru order is not thru the speaker & they always ask your name for that personal touch.

I have been trying to eat less processed food, so having a place like this seems to help me when I fail at packing my lunch...  because I will totally get their White Albacore Tuna salad.  I love it. 

Now they also have things that aren't as 'healthy', but regardless of what you get, it is as they are named.  It IS fresh.  Not sure why the name on here says wow that's fast, because the sign says wow that's fresh.

The toffee dip for the fresh apple slices is like dessert, the apples are put in orange juice (like my mom used to do)  It keeps the fresh apple slices from browning.

The burgers may not look as large as you expect but trust me, it's fresh & filling.  The fries are fresh cut potatoes with the skins, like you would make at home.  And as hardly any other drive thru food places (in Brandon) have hot dogs with sauerkraut, you can also get that here. 

It is a place I will return to again often.

I wish I could give this place infinite stars. We came here on a Friday night, around 7 PM. We were seated immediately. I ordered Chicken Parmesan and garlic knots.  After our order, there was an influx of customers, so we had to wait a bit (small place). But when the food came......wow! The Chicken Parmesan was absolutely perfect.

For $13.50, you get a huge piece of chicken breast, breaded perfectly, surrounded by sauce that is to die for. On top of that, it was layered with one of the best mozzarella cheeses I've ever had in my life. Service was excellent, no faults in the entire meal, and even though I ate a huge slab of chicken, cheese and sauce, I was ready for more. 

Not to mention, I was in here once before and forgot to check in. But, I had the pizza on the previous visit. The pizza is pretty amazing too. Very nice flavor, great crust and perfect cheese. 

I can't say enough about the quality of food here. It was simply amazing. I will be back so fast, their heads will spin.

Bluebeard is an Indianapolis American restaurant located near the hustle and bustle of downtown Indy.  

My family and I were in town and down the street at the convention center as my daughter had a huge cheer comp. Saturday after she finished day one of performing wee arrived to this establishment at around 240pm. 

Very small and cozy inside. Not much seating. We were the only visitors at the time and were told "no worries but the kitchen closes in 20 min". We assured them we are fast decision makers and shouldn't be a problem. 

The decor here on the inside is very sleek and quaint. On the outside you have some really cool murals. Including one in the rear of a face tatted Dolly Parton with her hit songs. Yes you read that right. And yes it is glorious. 

We placed our order fairly quickly. The menu said lunch but most options were breakfast food. So maybe this is a brunch place primarily (maybe just  on Saturday)?  We are fine with that though as we are the type who will eat breakfast for dinner by choice. So no biggie. 

My two daughters with us (are 11 and 1 year old) split a grilled cheese and spaghetti. The grilled cheese looked very visually pleasing. So of course I sampled it. And it was tastefully pleasing as well. Good sandwich. The spaghetti was interesting. Neither kid cared for it. Me and the wife tried it and it is good. But very unique in that it has like a lemon flavor to it. So I can see where kids expecting traditional spaghetti may turn there noses up at this item. 

My wife order the big a** B&G (biscuit and gravy with and egg) and a side of Brussels sprouts. Weird combo right? She 9 months pregnant so we will let her slide. Anyways, she loved both. Said both top notch. The Brussels sprouts side was in a huge bowl and enough to feed a person alone. 

I personally  got the quesadilla which once again was breakfast style only. Egg and chorizo. I will say it is by far the best breakfast quesadilla I've ever had. Nice and cheesy and just a great taste. 

Overall we had a wonderful experience. Great food and our server was super kind and recognized my daughter was in town for a cheer comp and really hyped her up and cheered on her success. Which made her feel good! My only complaint is something that if you don't read the small print on the menu you wouldn't know about. They charge an automatic 5 percent Kitchen gratuity. Very strange and I've never had a place do that before. Something so unique and obscure I'd really like to see signs posted on larger lettering. I fear that people would get angry about feeling bamboozled and it may cause someone to take it out of a waiter/waitress tip which wouldn't be fair to them. Outside of that this is a 5 star experience for us and we were very satisfied.

Went on opening day, and it was fantastic! Very happy to have a seated option both near to, and from the same people as HipCityVeg. Rittenhouse is getting really great for vegan options! The menu has a lot of choices, with sopas, empanadas, sandwiches, and tacos all making an appearance. 

We started with rellenos where there was "beef" (a very tasty plant-based version) in plantains. For mains, two of us went for the cubano, which was delicious (loved the tempeh) and another got "pescado" tacos. If the appetizer was a little small (but fancy), the mains were a perfect size. 

And since it was my birthday (yay! me and the restaurant share a birthday now!) we also got flan and tres leches ... the tres leches was particularly fantastic, very coconut-y but I love coconut. Would definitely recommend and definitely plan coming back!

I'm sooooo happy this is here! A fantastic location right on the corner of the park. There's a counter inside with lots of baked goods on it, so you can grab an iced coffee or tea and go for a walk in the park, or there's seating as well.
 
I went here for a mid-week brunch and tried the biscuits and gravy, which were fantastic. I also had a hibiscus tea and a chocolate croissant to round it off. Everything is vegan and good!

I'm so excited they're open! They do take cards, so no worries there, and the staff are really nice and kind. Looking forward to frequenting The Tasty!

For months, I've watched streams of posts in my social media feeds of the Cake Bake Shop and was really excited to check it out. I made a reservation for two on a Friday evening. I assumed when they took my credit card information to hold my reservation that they may charge a fee for canceling. It's a small place so I get it - you want to keep the tables full - but I was a little surprised to learn the fee was $20 per person. It seemed pretentious for a couple slices of cake, but I was still looking forward to our visit. 

There isn't much onsite parking - 5-6 spots - but we were both able to find street parking nearby. It's a really cute shop with lots of sparkles, tiaras, and pretty pink things. The desserts are beautifully displayed and there seem to be nearly as many staff as there are tables to seat patrons. I got the feeling by the end of our visit that it was the ambiance you're paying for because the cake, at $12.50 per slice, was good, but it didn't blow me away. 

Cake Bake Shop is the type of place you treat a young girl to on a special occasion, which is why I was there, but you can find great cake for less if you're just wanting to pop-in to please a sugar craving.

This downtown location is very accessible for the people who work in the thousands of offices in this area and everyone who visits. The line is not too bad,15-20 minutes or so and you'll sink your teeth in some awesome BBQ, ribs, brisket or whatever you prefer. They are not sweet (as most of the BBQ is), it's St Louis style BBQ and it's good. Can you find better in this town? Maybe, but between the proximity, fast line and quality - this one comes very close to the top, try it. Their service is super-fast, they know what they are doing and how to maximize the number of customers they get at lunch, they figured out how to fit this whole thing in an 1 hr lunch break and it works great. But come sooner if you can before the like gets worse, it's close and walking distance to pretty much anywhere in downtown.

Great place to try a "St Louis style' pizza, walking distance from pretty much anything in downtown. It has a corner joint feeling, not the place where you would stay too long, they don't serve beer or anything that would keep you here longer than just eating lunch. It's in a hotel, next to some fancy bistro and the restrooms are in the reception area. So order your pizza first and then take care of other stuff, it might take about 15-20 min till you get it. It's a thin crust, Provel cheese pizza and it might taste odd at first, but it's good in the end. The small one is enough to share for 2 people, enjoy!

I have been wanting to go here for months, and it did not disappoint!

When you first walk in the place is absolutely charming.  There is a nice little faux fireplace and a really cool "cottage" looking area where the bar and the servers station is located.  Really quaint and homey feeling!

The menu is one of those that you read over and then want more food than you are going to be able to eat.  We had the cabbage rolls and every kind of pirogue they had to offer.  Best cabbage rolls I have ever had and the all of the pirogues were great.  The sweet cheese pirogue is almost like dessert.

And the best part is damn near everything is made from scratch, right there at the restaurant.  You can totally taste the difference.

The servers were very friendly and attentive and the prices were so low I thought they forgot something on our bill.  $25 for drinks and our food!

I will be back and I will bring friends!

Lulu generously took me out to dinner here so we could celebrate being fabulous and unemployed. The gorgeous, dark, retro space made it the perfect place to speculate about this season of Mad Men as well. 

The service was nearly perfect. The fact that Lulu knew many of the staff members made for a warm, friendly experience. Alina was a wonderful server- she made great recommendations, made sure we did not feel rushed and went out of her way to accommodate our sharing of dishes. 

To start, we had the fried oysters and shrimp cocktail. The shrimp were divine, perfectly sweet and fresh. I loved the extra horseradish on top of the cocktail sauce, the extra heat and beautiful presentation made it stand out among the many versions of this dish I have eaten in my lifetime. The oysters were also amazing, the flavors of the sauce and the roe really enhanced their sea essence. I'm usually more of a fresh oyster girl, so these were a revelation for me. 

We also split a salad of tomato and vidalia onion, which had a creamy dressing and a generous dose of blue cheese. I could have eaten this everyday for the rest of my life, but then again I'm a vidalia addict. 

For the main portion of our meal, we both had the petit filet mignon. I cannot tell you how perfect this meat was. Besides being tender and beautifully medium-rare, the sear added so much to the flavor of the beef. Our side dishes included creamed spinach, which was tasty, but a bit salty for me. I knew it would happen eventually. Steven Starr, I'm going to beat you with your salt lick. We also had the stuffed hashbrown, which I really enjoyed. It reminded me a bit of a spanish tortilla, but creamier. 

For dessert, we opted for the chocolate cake and baked alaska. While the cake with its boozified cherries was delicious, the baked alaska was unbelievable. It is one of those dishes that I've always wanted to try, but I'm too timid to make it at home and it is rarely offered at restaurants anymore. The ice cream wasn't overwhelmingly flavored, which was great because I'm weird about banana flavored things. The toasty meringue made it one of the best things I've ever eaten. Seriously. 

For drinks, my tom collins was divine and the sidecar was dangerous.

Love. It.

Imagine my excitement when my favorite Philly couple showed up on my doorstep with get-well cupcakes. I must say I now believe in the healing power of cupcakes, especially ones from Brown Betty.

Honestly, this place wasn't even on my list of places to try because I've been so satisfied with Flying Monkey. But Brown Betty's cakes are a little better and definitely a bit different in style. These cupcakes have a less oily crumb, I feel like the cake could stand on its own better than Flying Monkey's. Also, although the frosting is sweeter, the cake-to-frosting ratio ensures they are not too sweet and are suited to an adult's palate. 

These cupcakes are quite large. I was determined to eat all four of mine before Chad got home and ended up consuming not even a quarter of each. Here's what I had:

Red velvet - excellent and I'm super picky about this type of cake. I could actually taste the cocoa in it, which I was very happy about because red velvet is too often just a vehicle for cream cheese frosting. The cake wasn't too red, which I was grateful for because I try to avoid food coloring. 

Pineapple - really good if you love pineapple and dislike artificial flavors.  I can honestly describe this cupcake as juicy, in a good way.  

Chocolate - I could not believe how much I loved this cupcake. It tasted like it came out of my mother's kitchen! This cake proved to me they bake with love. 

Sour cream - the surprise favorite. I'm a big fan of yogurt cakes, but I would never have selected a sour cream cupcake on my own. I was impressed with its flavor and moistness, they are definitely using good quality ingredients. Even Bug enjoyed a little of this cake, she showed her appreciation with atomic kitty farts the rest of the night. 

I was very, very impressed with my cupcakes. I'll definitely be stopping by to try the strawberry, lemon and almond flavors.

Location is the key to this hotel. Everything else pretty much sucks. It's run by kids who couldn't be nicer but don't know what the hell they are doing. We weren't able to check in when we arrived, they were delayed over 4 hours.  Don't get room 227. It's right be the gym and all you hear is pounding and treadmills running all morning. Not my favorite Starwood property.

I can't recall any time in my life, sober or not sober, where I have been so revolted watching food being prepared that I literally had to leave because I feared I would throw up all over the counter. The people cooking food are dirty, their shirts soiled in grease, the floors covered in old food and garbage, a gross grill with everything frozen being thawed out on it, the butter dispenser, dirty waffle pans, the smell... When I saw the grease bin being cleaned from the grill, I threw up a little in my mouth. And I was sober. 

This was and is the most horrific display of unsanitary food preparation I have ever seen in my life. After 40 minutes I left without eating anything, ran home to my hotel gagging the whole way and took a shower to get the grease smell out of my hair. That's how bad it was.

Love this place, and have loved it for years! Met with friends recently who had never been here, and thought, "How do you live here and never eat here?" You have to eat here at least once! They have amazing dinner dishes, and sushi dishes - really something to please any palette. The food & drinks are delicious, but they're the whole package: party type atmosphere with the music, interesting decor, and wonderful staff. Great place for a small group, or even a really fun date night. 

The specialty cocktails are interesting, and very good. Try one if you're in the mood for a drink. I tried one with Japanese whiskey and rosemary - tasty. 

My husband ordered the Holy Shishito Peppers and Tuna Nachos. The peppers are definitely hot, but not so hot that you can't handle them if heat is your thing. The Tuna Nachos is one our favorite dishes here; the flavors are just amazing together and the serving is large enough to replace a roll or two. 
 
For my part I ordered the sashimi appetizer along with the rice paper roll, and everything was so fresh. Absolutely delicious! 

I think our friends ordered the yaki soba, and beef tatki (& an app I can't remember). They loved every bite! Very thankful that we'd brought them in for a fun time with tasty food.

I sat at the bar and ordered a slice of Wicked Garden a White Pizza and the Pineapple Mojito for their Thurs $5 house cocktail special. Delicious pizza, delicious drink, and delicious memories. I remember the novelty of this place when it first opened. I lived in the neighborhood and was a regular as soon as they opened. I could order a cheap, single slice of whatever I wanted - didn't have to share or order a whole pizza or pick off stuff I didn't want from my own pizza.  And the drinks were always affordable, too. Fast forward over a decade and they're still selling great pizza by the slice - affordable pizza and affordable drinks on the street car line. In a neighborhood that has definitely changed, they've been a constant. When I checked in I noticed I'd never reviewed this place. Something to be said about places you visited pre-Yelp and then forget to review! 

It was really nice to see they still have that great neighborhood feel. Staff was very pleasant to everyone coming through the door and doing the best they can in this new understaffed world. Making sure everyone had refills, napkins, hot pizza, cheese & red pepper if they needed. Sometimes its the small stuff that still makes it worth the visit. Best slice of pizza for miles around, and great for a quick dinner or snack.

DESERVING OF EVERY STAR ON THIS FIVE STAR REVIEW! 

Favorite things: Nero Rose, avocado tacos, roasted cauliflower, steak & fries, and meat & cheese plates; great service every visit; indoor & outdoor seating year round.
Least favorite thing: parking, but I'm used to it in this city so I deal. 

How have I never written a review for this place? I try not to give 5 star reviews unless it's a place I've been to multiple times, that has proven stellar service and products/food every time - this place is for real. I've been a patron since they opened, and have gone at least once a quarter since then. Even on visits when it wasn't 100% (which is rare), there's nothing to complain about here. Rarely have I seen a business with so much repeat business, and so much success. They deserve it! 

Amazing prices, great selection, constant Happy Hour / deals, delicious food, nice service (even in a crowd), and perfect ambiance / atmosphere inside or out. I end up here at different hours all the time with a variety of groups of people, and the standard of service is always the same. I've come here with a large family group mid Saturday, for a Happy Hour meeting with coworkers, for a fun Happy Hour with friends, for a quick lunch, and for numerous dinner dates with my honey. Never am I disappointed. I've tried almost everything on the menu and it's all delicious. This is one of the few places I can actually even eat almost everything on the menu! Double points for that since everything is fresh, and there's a ton of veggie and small plate options. I cannot say enough about this place, so I'll just say, worth this five star review hands down.

I'm devastated to report the awful customer service I received today. I can safely say it is the worst I have had in my whole life! 


Hubby and I came here and ordered breakfast this Sunday morning. It took a while for food and my daughter finished her baby food before our meal even got to us. When our food finally arrived my husbands order was incorrect (I can attest to this even though the owner stated it was right - ummm, isn't the customer always right?). My husband asked him to take the potatoes back and leave the rest of the food since we were on a time crunch with the baby and all. He agreed, but when my husband got up to retrieve something from inside the restaurant (we were on the back patio) he snuck the plate away. My husband caught him inside, asked for the other food back, so... Here's the kicker... The "chef" threw the plate down on the counter. My husband asked him what the problem was and he replied "$&@! You!" Right in front of the owner. 

Hubby looked at the owner, flabbergasted, and the owner just played it off as if it was my husbands fault for wanting his order to his liking. Insane! Awful experience, insulting behavior, they don't deserve our money nor do they deserve other business if this is how they treat their customers. Bring Oscar and Jamie back!

P.S. The original review was about our experience with the previous owners!!!!

Remember that hotel room in Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas?  That's my husband and I on "date nights", which are few and far between.

Not tonight, though.  We kept it classy.

This swanky, crepuscular millennial enclave is located on a lesser known side street downtown. The ambience is definitely trendy, without having prices that whisper "I'm charging you a couple of extra bucks for the pleasure."  Even though we had a good ten years on the rest of the crowd, no one was eye balling us.

The cocktail menu was brief but imaginative; I chose something margarita-like that was a step up from the Kirkland version that I usually make at home.  I was actually most impressed by my husband's pick, the Brick House Old Fashioned.  I have no idea what was in it, but as I sipped it somehow I longed for Sterling, Don, Peggy and the rest of the crew.  I tasted a hint of ginger, but my husband announced gleefully that that was the bacon washed rye.  As a vegetarian, somehow it never occurred to me to check the beverage menu for meat.  Anyway, the drink was interesting enough for me to question my porkless ways.  

My husband ordered the steak frites, after Googling the correct pronunciation - it's not free-tays, in case you ever need to know - which he was satisfied with.  I think he's just more of a filet mignon guy.   For my entrée, I devoured the mustard crusted salmon and grilled asparagus. I instantly regretted that I doused it with lemon; I don't think it needed it.  As it was, I'd still have to say that that was the best salmon filet that I've enjoyed in my fairly limited dining-out experience.

I've lived in Tucson since 2002, and have only ventured downtown after sundown once, to hit up Downtown Bail Bonds...don't ask...I'll save that review for another time.  Thanks, Yelp, for leading us back.

We only had tacos here but hands down one of the best we've had in the city! Lean, generous portion of meat, overflowing cilantro, warm taco shells that don't fall apart and most importantly, no soggy oil at the bottom! Flavors are spot on and we were completely stuffed! 

The mild salsa is a little too spicy for me so be careful to not put too much. We would've loved it a bit more if the radish were pickled like the Guapos Tacos truck, but $7 for 3 massive tacos, we're not complaining.

We'll definitely be back to try other dishes!

I absolutely love a good breakfast, i can eat it any time of the day. Woke up this morning unable to drive myself somewhere for food because my car is in the shop, had the biggest urge for breakfast and although i am walking distance from Ruby Slipper, i wanted something different. 

Discovered this little gem, and it turned out to be an enlightening experience. What did it for me was that this place delivered. What a perfect solution to my ail! 

Ordered the pancrepes with sausage and a queso burrito. Didn't quite think the pancrepes alone would be enough which is why i added the burrito, but i am typing this review as my burrito sits in the bag. The pancrepes came with scrambled eggs and your choice of bacon or sausage. It tasted like a real home-made breakfast, it really hit the spot. 

Delivery was fast and on point, food was still piping hot and got here in about half the time they said over the phone. 

Glad i discovered this place, definitely my go-to breakfast joint when i'm feeling lazy/hungover :)

I had a really good experience here. There's a lot to like about this place. The decor being one of my favorite things about this new restaurant. I love the high, exposed ceilings which are met by brick accented walls, spotted with some really cool art work. When you first walk in there are these cool, not-so-little couches in the front window, ideal for a group having some coctails. 

About the coctails, they're magnificent. There's also the noteworthy bar that you come across before entering the dining area. I came here once when it was a burger joint, but they've done well with the place in its new venture. You also wanna note it's only street parking around here, i recommend coming after 6pm so you don't have to pay a meter.

I ordered the Kyoto coctail which was easily the best choice on the drink menu, but it'll hit you for $15. I'd say it's worth it tho, for sure. Our server, Kayla, was simply thee cutest thing! Such a delight having her at our service.

My date had the curry udon noodles, which are SPICY y'all, but SO good! I think I enjoyed her dish a little more than mine, but that's not to take anything away from what I had. My order was the rebellion ramen. It was pretty tasty, i didn't finish it, but it was only because my lunch from earlier weighed heavier on me than expected. I didn't know what to expect but the first taste I got from the ramen was cabbage, granted I saw it as one of the ingredients, i just did not expect it to be the first, noticeable taste from it. Once I mixed everything together a bit, it was smooth sailing.

Neither of us did apps or dessert, i think we both weren't that hungry, but the meal only came out to about $60 which wasn't bad at all. Definitely going back and next time there will be room for dessert.

Ok so I was wondering if this was in place of the old Wow Cafe, and it is. I don't recall seeing any renovations being done here at all, but it is tucked away in the corner of the tiniest shopping strip in Mid City. 

Anyway, i came here for the chicken and waffle with the side of brussels. Both were amazing. The sandwich was pressed nicely and blended well with the cheese and the chopped chicken. The brussels were a lot like Cochon Butcher's. They taste almost exactly the same, in fact. Get the brussels. Oh! The sauce that comes with the waffles compliments it SO well; kind of sweet with a hint of something i can't really put my finger on, but i was like, 'yeah'.

The place was a bit busy, thats always a good sign. Also the smell upon walking in reassured me that i was making steps in the right direction. Friendly staff and quick service. Call ahead and have your order ready for pick up or kick back in the nice ambiance. Too bad there's no outside seating for enjoying those perfect Mid-City days.

I'm a fan.

Definitely a must if you're thinking about it. At no one's behest did I show up here, it was a rare hankering for something out of my usual and since I was in Kenner (far from my usual) there were an abundance of options. Something told me I wanted Indian food so the search began. There was a couple places I was torn between but decided on this one. I find it difficult to believe I could have made a better choice.

The place sits in the middle of a strip mall, not much aesthetically. Let that be no deterrence. Where they may lack in decor, it's made up for in their dishes. Since it was only me, I had the butter chicken and garlic naan; simply phenomenal. I was unsure if I would be able to finish it all but it was so dang tasty I couldn't leave nor embarrass myself by requesting a to-go box. I had to let them know how much life the food gave me. By the time I was done with it, the dishes seemingly could've gone straight back on the shelf.

No doubt about it, the food here is bangin. I'd definitely be willing to make the trip out this way for this again, great job!

We are very enjoyed our all you can eat experience in Atlantis Sky Terrance Sushi Bar even we have to wait for 2-1/2 hours for our sets in the very busy Labor Day Weekend Saturday.

This is not a buffet, but make after order all you can eat restaurant. They are mainly sushi rolls in the all you can eat menu only. Long rolls, hand rolls, and nigiri. Make sure you are hungry! Lol!

The rolls are very fresh and many choices of fishes for nigiri. The best I like is the Salmon Skin Hand Roll. This is a much try when you are there!

The parking log is huge but it is part of the Atlantis Hotel and Cosnio. It is always very busy. I have no problem finding a parking. But you may have to walking a little bit longer in the parking lot. The park lot is safe and clean.

My roommate and I have almost finished an entire cream cheese king cake from this awesome gem in NO East (way out on Chef) within the last 24 hours. Definitely the freshest, yummiest king cake I've had. The icing on top is light and fluffy - not goopy, sticky and heavy like most, the sugar adds texture and somehow actually tastes good not just like food colored granules. And the cake is moist and delicious - not dry or overly sweet. While I'm a new resident, I've had my share over the years and I believe their king cakes must be one of this city's best kept secrets. Plus, at $12 they are even affordable!

Not to mention, I am uber excited about my new gig at a school out in the East this winter cuz I get to have their slammin' banh mi sandwiches for lunch at least once a week. They fill their freshly baked baguette on premises (which you can buy 3 for $1 while there to make your own sammys at home) with a smear of butter-tinted mayo, nice hearty slice of cucumber, healthy handful of carrots, full sprigs of cilantro, several slices spicy peppers and delicious meats (I always get the grilled pork). I love me some banh mi, and this is about as good as it gets. $2.85 is average price, but head and shoulders above others I've had in NOLA and elsewhere.

Make the trek out to the East, it's worth it!

Dear bartender-who-looks-like-a-skinny-santa,
Thanks for making me feel like poop for no reason.

I was visiting SB from another county and my brother sent me along with a growler to refill that he'd purchased (from the Brewhouse) just this spring. I walk into the establishment, proud of my nifty glass jug, and excited to try the oft-talked about Habanero Pilsner. I saunter up to old Santa Claus, with expectation in my heart, and ask how I can get more liquids in my growler. Santa peered at me severely, as though he was studying me over his reading glasses or a republican newspaper, although he had neither. He informed me that they don't refill growlers anymore, in a tone that conveyed to me that I must have just kicked his dog, or smooshed his birthday cake.
He said it with such finality that I was unsure how to proceed. I was confused about the information he'd just given me, and I didn't want to return home empty handed. I assumed they could no longer sell alcohol in un-sealed bottles, and surely a BREW HOUSE would have sealed bottles to sell me. When I inquired, I got the same pissy attitude from Santa. Thanks Santa! Thanks for nothing! We were going to have a drink when we stopped over, but you made it clear that you really didn't want me to drink anything you had, or have fun, or feel like a human.

Unsure why the attitude and lack of information. Unsure if prejudiced, or just a jerk? :/

Maybe he thought we were undercover cops?

I skipped in there like Little Red Riding Hood with a basket for granny, and was un-pleasantly surprised to be eaten by the big bad wolf; with no beer to boot!
Obnoxiously long lines and mediocre meat and bread combine perfectly to provide the visiting tourist with the wrong type of unforgetable experience (Pat's across the street isn't much better).

I was really excited to check this place out, and I'd give it a one star if I hadn't remotely enjoyed the drinks (I am a bourbon snob and the Southern Belle was very enjoyable).

We were being rushed out of the place due to reservation times, when our server was completely overwhelmed and couldn't tend to his 8+ tables. I had read reviews before and saw the place doesn't staff appropriately, so I should have known better.

The manager we tried to talk to was incredibly dismissive - couldn't even catch his name, but tall guy - and he almost talked to us in a condescending tone. Then he pulled down his mask, because I asked him to repeat himself, and I couldn't believe it. We are in a pandemic, and this place obviously doesn't get it.

Good drinks, cute view, subpar service and management. Better tapas-style restaurants in the city for half the price and none of the attitude.

We've taken to stopping here on Saturday afternoons when the place is empty save for one bartender prepping for the day's adventures. At such times we get the inside scoop about the business and craft. On our last stop here I was given an in depth explanation on just how they get these perfectly clear ice cubes, which in my experience is a rare sight indeed. Hint: there is a chainsaw involved. What drew my attention initially to this location was the business name, but the reason to keep coming back? Classy, exquisite cocktails, the best I've had anywhere (sorry Bottle & Barlow). Another jewel in Midtown Reno's crown, Death & Taxes is top notch in every way. 

My favorite cocktail is the Black Gates (what whiskey sours strive to be, with gunpowder green tea bourbon, Islay Mist, Drambuie, lemon, and cardamom), after which I favor any of the drinks under the whiskey section of their menu, which is divided by spirit. These drinks are insane, all made with quality hand-made ingredients, syrups, juices, herbs, and an impressive bevy of spirits, presented in sublime fashion: some with little curly orange peels, or a spiral of candied, dried apricots, or with sprigs of lavender, or perhaps with crystal clear ice cubes, all nestled lovingly in multifaceted glassware. I suppose at times I felt as if I was drinking art. Pinkies at the ready!

Fancy doesn't mean weak pours, so don't make that mistake. Two of the cocktail menu items will easily cost you $20-$30, and you'll be feeling it in places other than the wallet. Gathering oneself up and emerging from the dark cavern out into the sunlit Reno streets can be a shock as well. I enjoy the gothic lighting in here but I could see it not being everyone's cup o tea. Bottom line, this is a fantastic place to be as the drinks and the bartenders are perfection. Death & Taxes is a highly recommended must!

See my pictures for other tasty cocktail examples. My other two recommendations after the aforementioned Black Gates would be the Bonaparte (Larceny small batch bourbon, peach, house-made Amaro blend, cardamom), or the Penicillin (brown butter scotch, ginger honey, saffron, lemon). They also have a SWEET BEER LIST!

Note: Street parking. Hours are a bit funky. D&T doesn't open until 2 pm weekdays and Saturday, and not until 5 on Sundays.

Ok...finally got around to visiting their new location (they recently moved).

They now have seats to chill on and it's a cute set up...but I'm about to lay down some critiques:

1) there's no WiFi (they should really look into offering that for customers)
2) there are a few "desks" and chairs, sorta like old school furniture. It's cool but not comfortable
3) the music during my visit has been rap/hip hop...with vulgar language at times...lots of "F bombs" and even that "N word" whoa (I don't mind the music but for a business, ehhhh)
4) my latte wasn't great, not bad...just not my fave

I'll be back, I like their look and feel somewhat, they did JUST open up here so they probably still need to work out a flow. There are 2 registers which can be helpful but customers don't know where to line up. 

When I walked in, I was the 3rd customer...I knew this but the guy behind the counter asked if I was ready to order. I told him, "thanks but it's actually her turn." It wasn't an issue but you can see where that could create tension.

I'm all for a new coffee shop where I can chill a bit and catch up on work. Maybe they're not looking for that here...perhaps they like the quick in/out approach. It's their business, they can do what they like...I'm just sharing some feedback.

Details:
After moving to Saint Louis, me and my partner were on a mission to try all the local coffee houses in the area. Sump was on our list and recommended by some friends and even our neighbor. We went to order and encountered a rather snobby barista who took our order but seemed to challenge our method of ordering. Nevertheless we ordered a cappuccino and a latte. We were prepared to pay but told we could pay later.

We go to find a seat and there's a variety of seating surfaces, many looking as if they belong outdoors. Interior decor is kept at a minimal and it borders second hand store and somewhat pirate ship-like. Our order arrives and it looks pretty, I sip my cappuccino and find I need a little sugar. My partner does the same to his latte and goes in search of a prep station. He comes back to our table and tells me, "There's no sugar." A bit puzzled, I go up to the bar and ask for sugar where I'm told; "We're not trying to be pretentious or anything...but we don't have sugar." I was surprised. I've been to some pretty pretentious coffee shops and all of them had sugar. I stood there and another lady walked up to confirm this while adding, "We roast our beans lightly so you can enjoy the flavor."

Ok...I get that but I felt like it needed some sugar so I explained that and the lady then remarks, "I feel as if you're telling me how to do my craft."

So first, this is coffee...and oh yeah, I'm a customer. I'm a guest. My palette isn't yours. She then says, "You don't have to pay for them in a rather snooty tone." Well of course not, but that wasn't the point. We made a trip to experience this place and we'll never return...not so much for the lack of sugar but because of the terrible service.

I've been (unsuccessfully) looking for good croissants all over town (please give me more recommendations). Frieda is one of the rare places that made me swoon over their chocolate almond croissant. Get this if it's the one thing you're getting here.  
I also got a side of the multigrain toast and chorizo with the cortado. Absolutely delicious sausage and perfect coffee! Attentive servers and super chill vibe. I imagine I'm going to be trying a lot of their bakery items on a regular basis. 

The only minor complaint I'd have is that the table was a little sticky.

Had been hearing raving reviews about Stina and luckily found a 7:15 slot on Resy. The two of us reached at 7 and waited happily, hungrily, patiently watching everyone eat. Our table wasn't available by 7:15. Neither was it available by 7:30. By 7:40 our stomachs were protesting, and finally got our table then. The staff apologized to us about the delay (I understand it's not their fault if people don't finish dining on time, but that's the only reason I'm docking one star off). 

We ordered all at once  - fire roasted potatoes, octopus, merguez pide. They started us off with the fire roasted cauliflower, compliments of the house for the delay. 0.5 star up for that, but I'll still round off to 4, because I'm sure the next visit will make it 5. The cauliflower was a beautiful roasted half, that sadly didn't match up to its looks. The outer char was amazing, but we felt the cauliflower was more than crunchy, almost raw inside, and didn't do much. One of the best looking dishes of the night though. 

Next came the merguez pide and potatoes. Wow. Blown away. One of the most unique dishes I've had in a while - the lamb sausage is spicy, savory with the perfect burst of cheese and delicious dough. Highlight of the evening, that made me forget my previously grumpy self. I will definitely have this again, and very soon. The potatoes were delicious - slight citrusy taste with some greens, and a more than hearty quantity. The octopus (priciest item on the menu) was charred to perfection, but you could live without it. 

We'd hoped to try a pizza but all this food was definitely more than enough for two famished people. We still did dessert - citrus cheesecake, that I had no intention of having but claimed 50% of after a bite. 

I'm sorry for the 4 stars Bob, I promise I'll make it up the next time.
Ordered a molten chocolate lava cake via Grubhub and it was absolutely delicious! Will be trying other things from here soon

Updating another 5 star review. 

We went in starving for a late lunch and ordered: 
Crispy spring rolls - arrived quick, tasty and filling with a great dipping sauce (ask for the spicy sauce and chili powder)
Drunken noodles - an ever favorite. SO much flavor, it was hard for me to stop eating continuously for the first 5 minutes
Grilled salmon in green curry (weekend special) - this blew us away. Amazing depth and flavor, with a unique combination Brussels sprouts, asparagus, peas, chopped shrimp and tender, buttery salmon grilled to perfection. I hope they have this again, I'd rate it as the top dish here, and I love all their items 
Matcha creme brûlée - I normally tend to not think much of Thai desserts, but JJ managed to exceed expectations there as well. The matcha was not overwhelming but added an interesting element to a perfect creme brûlée

5 stars, again. Cannot wait to dine here and try more of their specials (and regular items as well) 

Best Thai in Philly for me, period. 

I'm a regular red curry customer here, never disappointed me. I first had it when I was looking for apartments in this city back in Feb. Has been consistent so far. 

This evening, I went in with the intention to pick up but asked them to serve me there instead. Sat with a book and enjoyed the Tom Kha Gai (good flavor) and Pad Thai with shrimp (exceptional). The Pad Thai sauce was slightly sweet but it was really well made and bursting with flavor. 

I see no reason why JJ Thai won't continue to be my favorite Thai joint for years to xome

Great food. However, they got my Grubhub order modification wrong and the follow up after that made me lose any interest in wanting to order again. 

I was sick and wanted to have fish. They have something called Shrimp Moilee on the menu, which I'm familiar with. I called them up and the lady who received my call told me they could make the same dish with fish if I added a note to my order on Grubhub. She also took down my name and said she'd personally monitor it. I was amazed at such graciousness for someone ordering delivery. 

The food came before the estimated time - only for me to find it was shrimp despite my note and having called them. I called back and spoke to the same person. She asked for my name and said  she got too busy to monitor it. She apologized and assured me that she would make sure she would keep on top of things in the future (for who? Not me definitely). 

I was offered a free entree and a discount - is what my expectation was. But nada. She just reiterated her apologies. 

Despite liking their food a lot, I'm terribly disappointed with the customer service. And the 7-8 big pieces of shrimp on a night when I was craving some fish! 

Good food AND good customer service might be asking for too much, no?

My friends and I were harassed at this establishment last night. After I presented my AZ drivers license the bartender handed it to the manager, who hadn't spoken to us whatsoever at this point, came up to me in a hostile manner and accused me of presenting a fake ID, I am almost 25, I don't need to be walking around with a fake.  I never even had one when I was underage . My friends and I were thrown off by behavior but didn't want that to ruin our evening, as we had been planning to pay this place a visit for the past few weeks. The bartender even began to treat us differently and rude also. I told the manager i could show him my passport as well, and for some odd reason he said that they already told me they were going to refuse me services and to stop trying. He was yelling from across the bar while other customers were there. At this point he was even more hostile. I told him that I didn't know what to say because that was my id and I've never had this issue. He rudely told me he's s been working in this field for 15 years and can spot a real from a fake with ease. 

 Feeling quite disappointed, i stopped trying. I didn't want to ruin the evening for my friends. One of them still ordered wine. Which the bartender dryly gave to her. My friend proceeded to leave them a negative review. 5 minutes later the owner of the establishment came up to us and in a belligerent manner, started telling her to take down the review or leave his business. My friends tried to explain how i was of age and i was falsely accused, however he became even more angry and was talking over them and cussing at us. I was shocked by the situation. He told us that we were breaking the law and that he didn't care for social media. In his words "this social media crap is bullshit." At this point my friends and the owner were yelling at each other. 

My friends and I left accordingly and in a cooperative manner. We didn't damage anything. 

I understand that you are trying to stand by your employees (Which was his son btw I'm sure), but he could've at least heard us out or not act as hostile for doing nothing. 

Father And son need to take some business etiquette courses. The location has a lot of potential, but with the work personnel and management they have running it. It will not go anywhere

I've never in my life written a review or left a comment but this behavior has to be exposed. Cannot allow them to treat anyone else this way. So.much for the hot new  Tucson hangout

P.S. I decided to go out downtown afterwards instead and I was able to get in to other bars with no problem

Came here for my birthday breakfast and I love it! The decor is welcoming and warm. You walk in and everyone is all smiles. I didn't know what to expect because we stumbled on to this gem while running early morning errands on my birthday. Apparently, this is was a restaurant named Kimmies and had been open for some time but renamed Cup Cafe. Not sure the back story here but I can't believe I'm just now trying this place for the first time.We decided to share a short stack of buttermilk pancakes and the southern biscuits & gravy platter. Both were eggxellant choices

The pancakes were fluffy and delicious. The flavor is so good you can eat them with or without syrup. The top it with powdered sugar so if you are not a fan let them know. Personally I love it. The dish that really shined was the southern biscuits and gravy platter. 
Literally homemade biscuits!! Like real ones and you can certainly tell. Many places claim to make homemade biscuits but the size shape and texture is telling and I guess everyones definition of 'honemade' is different. The sausage gravy was delicious. Savory, salty goodness with just a touch of sweet in there. Hands down the best biscuits and gravy that I've had at a breakfast spot in Reno and Sparks. 
Eggs were perfectly cooked. Bacon was a delicious cherry wood smoked flavor. The platter is just that, a platter! It is massive, shareable and reasonably priced. To top it all off I had a delicious mimosa, fresh squeezed juice would have put me over the top but good nonetheless... a girl can dream. The service is fast, friendly and good. This place is a definite must try if you are a breakfast person.

First of all... Very friendly!  I mean very friendly!!  These are the type of guys you want to succeed in a small business.   They are proud of their product and it shows.  This is a great place to stop before or after a movie and get a slice or a whole pizza. The restaurant is a little small but is great for take out or delivery.  Now about the pizza. It's pretty darn good. And the guys will help do what ever you want not like a chain pizzeria.  For example we got a giant 28 inch pizza quarter pepperoni quarter cheese and half supreme.   And everyone loved it!  And yes I know I'm known for typos but the 28 inch was not one of them.  So I definitely will try them for delivery.

In the heart of downtown Boise the Fork is truly one of our best overall restaurants!  A must try if your local or from out of town..  Can't go wrong with the Fork!  The vibe of the restaurant is awesome! And the customer service is top notch.  They just get it!  From water when you are first seated to great recommendation  on drinks and food selections. The servers are very passionate about what they are serving.  All the food is top notch and sometimes for everyone in your party including the kids.  Only this is the main dish selection is a bit limited.  Overall this is a wonderful restaurant that I highly recommend for everyone to try..

Was here recently for a late lunch. They close at 3pm, so we just about made it. With that said, the restaurant was packed - it is new after all! And a very welcome addition to Newtown breakfast places. 

Inside is open and light. Looks very similar to the one in Warrington, with light blue colored paint on the walls and white trim everywhere. The waiting area is rather small, but there is a large area outdoor that can be used for waiting. There is also a coffee bar, I assume it's first come first serve seating but can't be sure.

The menu is also similar if not the same to the Warrington location.
