My party and I arrived on time, and were told that there would be a 25-30 minutes wait, despite our reservation. We were given the option of eating outside (in the mall parking lot) in 92 degrees (RF was 96) heat. 

We left.

It's good, but I do not get the hype. 

I have had the beef with falafel several times. It's tasty and reasonably priced. But it's not that special, IMO. I always get extra white and hot sauses. The hot sauce is definitely hot. I don't really like their fries. 

I always go at off-peak times, so lines have not been an issue. One of best things about it, and the main reason I keep returning, is that it is open until 11pm, which not many places in the area are. 

I wish it felt more conducive to sitting down and eating rather than people using tables to prepare toppings and condiments.

There are definitely 2 other local places I prefer for this type of food, but HG is quick, cheap, and decent.

If you love local craft beer and great food, then this is a must stop when in the Tampa area. Every beer I've had here has been excellent and the food is equally amazing. 

Cool casual atmosphere, good for an afternoon lunch date or big event on the weekend. The pub has a beautiful bar that grants you views of where they brew the beer. They have an outside sitting area that allows you to enjoy the awesome weather Florida has. 

Can't wait to go again and Ill be back with friends!

Nice decor but thats where it stops. Food was not good and service was lame at best. 

They sat us at a broken table and we had to wait 10 min before a server came by. We mentioned the broken table but they didn't seem interested in correcting the problem. So I go to the host stand and say we need a new table. 10 min later we get a new table. Literally 10 more min go by and not one server domes by ( BTW the host that moved us from the broken table sat another family at that table 3 min later) I had to go back up to the host stand to get someone to come to our table. 

Once we got a server ( who had pasted our table several times prior), things started happening. We got our drinks and table side guacamole. 

The table side guacamole was not that good. I've had better that was premade. My wife had the Gaucho platter. It was over priced, poor presentation and dry. I had the chicken Chimichanga which was equally disappointing. Presentation was good but it lacked flavor to include the rice and beans. 

Margaritas were well made and the modelo was ice cold

Overall, not impressed. Will not go again and will only recommend for drinks and hanging out

It was our final night visiting my in-laws in their winter condo and time to try the most yelped about pizzeria in Green Valley. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/1s8WJM2zbUScgZ-7HlMXuA?select=1Gas_rP6jY5-uJnwdaSfqw

We got takeout for a total of about $50:

* Large veggie pie minus green pepper http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/1s8WJM2zbUScgZ-7HlMXuA?select=5RUBJ-XdJ__xEMn4pw1__A
* Large spicy sausage, olive, and onion pie http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/1s8WJM2zbUScgZ-7HlMXuA?select=_KroEfxB7IRl0kMUwKLwEg
* Slice of cheese pizza http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/1s8WJM2zbUScgZ-7HlMXuA?select=4EAF9mxm02rr87l1KCUyBQ

On our 4-year-old's random number scale, the pizza is "200 good," beating the previous high by 100. He practically inhaled most of his cheese slice during the car ride home and said it was better than the previous pizzeria we tried. I was relieved he didn't object to the flecks of green (oregano?) on his pizza. Perhaps it was a good thing he'd had a light lunch.

Most noteworthy to me was the delicious crust, which was just right. Tougher food critic Mr. L and my in-laws gave it high praise, 4 and 5 stars respectively. My mother-in-law's only complaint is that the pizzeria can get very crowded, but it wasn't when we stopped by. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/1s8WJM2zbUScgZ-7HlMXuA?select=OPPmD9qheduvmL1NUeP3VQ


Two Girls doesn't make my favorite Margherita pizza and our veggie pizza didn't seem the most balanced, but it was still good. 3.5 stars and rounding up.

Coming from the San Francisco area, I'm a little spoiled when it comes to vegan and vegetarian restaurants. While this place didn't blow my mind, it was nice to find a vegan restaurant, even though I'm not vegan. I didn't expect to find a restaurant like this in a strip mall in Tucson. 

The name "Lovin' Spoonfuls" threw me a bit. To me Lovin' Spoonfuls conjures images of someone lovingly (well, minus the "g") feeding spoonfuls of tapioca pudding to a person in a retirement home. Not very sexy, but a name is one thing to one person, and entirely something different to another.

After a bit of consultation with the friendly owner, Peg Raisglid (who interestingly enough has a Ph. D. in Chemistry), we settled on:
 
* Linguini with Italian Meatballs for Mr. L - Linguini pasta topped with a zesty tomato sauce and savory herbed meatless meatballs. Served with warm garlic bread. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/szad9yEwckNw0P3L5FGyNQ?select=2UU3KeT7SiJjtpzd-Ndozw 

* Country Fried Chicken Platter for me - Crispy fried soy chicken with savory stuffing, mashed potatoes, gravy and steam grilled vegetables. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/szad9yEwckNw0P3L5FGyNQ?select=vkvPAzC_jJNZGduh_JNEYg

* Pumpkin squash and Moroccan lentil soup specials of the day http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/szad9yEwckNw0P3L5FGyNQ?select=CdEdnENg-TDW4XI99RiG9w 

* Spicy house herbal iced tea

I liked my husband's linguini and meatball dish better than mine and stole a few bites. My dish was pretty good too, but the stuffing was crispy (not in a good way), the potatoes lacked flavor, and the steamed vegetables were not cooked perfectly. I don't usually go for fake meat, but I knew this fried chicken was a popular dish, and was interested in trying it.

A house salad came before our entrees, and I enjoyed it and the homemade dressing with it. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/szad9yEwckNw0P3L5FGyNQ?select=W3LweKJVS0AkFdHVSdHKDw

The restaurant got pretty busy while we were there, so it seems there is a desire for vegan food in Tucson. The customers order at the counter, and then the food is brought to them fairly quickly. There was a microwave visible behind the counter, which I hope wasn't used on our food.

The customers in here looked generally more fit and trim than those we saw in other mainstream restaurants, perhaps as a testament to the vegan lifestyle. One couple in line couldn't stop kissing each other, which I doubt had anything to do with the vegan diet. My guess is they hadn't been together long, or maybe it was the name of the restaurant that got them in the mood. 

Overall, I like this restaurant, despite my reaction to the name and a few hiccups with the food. 3.5 and rounding up.

This place embodies my dreams of the little neighborhood coffee shop I would venture to after a weekend morning stroll. It's part hipster, part metro, and a whole-lotta delicious. It's one of those places you don't want to tell people about because you want to keep it "your little secret," but then you realize that you're just being selfish and that you should share their amazingness with the world. 

The coffee is complex, their lattes are little works of art, and their teas make you feel special. The fact that they serve High Street breads and pastries is just over-kill. Their sandwiches are thoughtful bundles showcasing local ingredients, so they change seasonally. I was drooling over their ricotta toast with honey and their new peanut butter toast with figs just yesterday when the customer in front of me ordered them. I was seriously disappointed I had already eaten breakfast.

They're not your standard study cafe so don't expect to unload all of your study paraphernalia out onto the tables. It's more of a destination for serious drinks, delicious bites, and good conversation.

Was in philly for 2 nights & was highly recommended this place by a friend who used to live in the city and wow - this was AMAZING. 

My favorite pasta dish & gnocchi so of course, I ordered this amazing piece of art and I can't wait until the next time I'm in Philly so I can return & order this again!

- Gnocchi +5/5
The texture, amount of cheese, flavor, & everything was s-p-o-t o-n. The pasta was cooked perfectly & the dish it self came out so pretty quickly which was really impressive. I would come back over & over and just order this single dish. While the portion was perfect for me, I stand at 5'0 and would recommend ordering a couple more plates if you're with a friend/group. 

- Honorable mentions: The gelato sampler.
I was too full to try this & will definitely order this next time I return! The waitress also highly recommended this & from some research online, some claim that this is the best ice cream in the city!

The service was impeccable, the vibes were amazing, & the overall experience was so great. Thank you, gran caffe!

Don't be deceived by the long lines, they go by so quickly! When I went on Sunday morning, the line wrapped around to where you pick up your donuts towards the middle of the store & we got our donuts within 10 minutes!

MUNCHIES:
- cinnamon bun +5/5
Wow, this was amazing. I'm salivating right now thinking about it. It was so soft & so yummy so definitely get here early (before 10/11am) since I heard it runs out!
- horchata donut +3/5
I love horchata flavored anything but while the outside of the donut was amazing, the inside filling was odd and ruined the taste of the overall donut. 
- red velvet donut +4.5/5
My bf loves red velvet flavored things & loved this! The generous amount of red velvet cake on the top is a huge plus. 
- buttermilk drop +2/5
Apparently these are popular but my bf and I thought they were really bland.. we didn't see what the hype was about, honestly. :/
- kolache +5/5
This was my favorite out of all the things that we ordered. It was savory, warm, & just so good! Definitely ask them to warm it up for you. 

Overall, I'd say this place is a spot you need to stop by when you're visiting NOLA. & when have donuts ever not brought you happiness? ;)

Need a place to escape from the greasiness/butteriness found in most NOLA dishes? This is the spot!

FOOD:
- Beet salad +4/5
The presentation for this is AMAZING. The colors are so lovely & it tastes really yummy tho! Just remember that this IS a salad though, so if you're craving something more savory/heavy, refer to the next 2 options.
- BBQ shrimp toast +4.5/5
My bf ordered this & destroyed it. Enough said!
- Chicken & biscuits +5/5
Our friend ordered this and inhaled it, while mumbling mid-bites on how delicious it was. So... he'd highly recommend it hahaha.

SERVICE:
- Our initial server was so lovely but her replacement was subpar& quite rude. From rolling her eyes to tapping her toes when my friend took longer than usual to order, she was really unprofessional. I used to be a server myself so I'm not trying to be hard on her but really, she - this angry looking, short blonde - could've honestly been nicer.

Overall, a great place to visit while in NOLA. The blonde just needs some lessons on how to treat others.

Sometimes you really have to do things that you really don't want to and today is the day i do so with this review of 7th and Grove.

Having to choose between getting one of their benedicts or their French Toast is probably about as difficult a decision to make as it is for someone to decide which 1 of the 28 selfies they took to post.

I was more in the mood for eggs but couldn't pass up the chance to try their illustrious French Toast, so getting both and sharing was the only way to go about it.

*BANANAS FOSTER FRENCH TOAST $14 (Sliced Bananas, Vanilla Bean Ice Cream, and Toasted Walnuts with Foster Sauce): just look at it. There's so much going on but everything comes together well and it has just the right level of sweetness.

*EGGS STANLEY (Benedict) $16: this features Cornmeal-Crusted Oysters, Canadian Bacon, and Poached Eggs that gush out yolk the moment your fork pierces it. 

I can't think of a more ideal sweet and savory brunch in Jackson Square than this. You don't have to worry about getting to Stanley just in time for breakfast either, as their full menu is available all day.

Friend: "did u get all that jizz?"

Me: eww, umm no, I wasn't on Bourbon Street

(when your friend texts you and ignores the autocorrect recommendation for the "All That Jazz" sandwich)

I didn't get All That Jazz, as I went with the SHRIMP PHILLY and will never second guess that decision! It's sooo good that you don't need to be drunk and have it at 2am to enjoy it. This style of sandwich couldn't be more different than the one I had at New Orleans' other top deli, Cochon Butcher, but somehow it was equally, if not more, satisfying.

The Shrimp Philly, served on a lengthy french roll, is comprised of grilled shrimp, bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, cheese, and "Wow Sauce." The mushrooms and sauce are the difference makers. This thing gets messy but is well worth the 17 napkins used.

Verti Marte is cash only, open 24 hours, and inside a convenience store located just across from the so-called haunted Lalaurie Mansion. You get the idea - charming AF.

My wife and I had a fantastic lunch at Alésia.  The place looks great, very light, bright and trendy.  But for having such an upscale feel, the prices were very reasonable.  

We started with the summer rolls, which were very fresh tasting, with shrimp, pork, rice, and a touch of mint.  We had a carafe of their organic green tea with citrus and ginko.  It was not overpowering, but had great flavor and really complimented the summer rolls as well as the rest of the meal.  

We are both big fans of Pho, so my wife ordered that and I got the bánh mì.  My sandwich was excellent, with pâté and salami going nicely with the spice of the jalapeño.  My wife's Pho was good, but didn't come out hot so she sent it back for a reheat.  Being summer in Florida, I'm sure not everyone wants piping hot soup, but that is how my wife likes it, and they were very pleasant about doing it.  The Pho had a bit of sweetness to it which was different for us, but we did quite like it.  

We are looking forward to going for breakfast soon, since their morning items look excellent, and different from the usual choices.  We are also hoping it will cool down soon so we can sit outside in their lovely courtyard.  I would highly recommend going to Alésia as soon as possible.

On my last afternoon in NOLA before my flight home to LA, I wanted to cap off my indulgent eating with a iced coffee. Spitfire Expresso Bar specializes in pour overs but  a cold drink is a must in the New Orleans humidity.

The Tres Flores (expresso, lavender infused milk, orange blossom simple syrup, and rose petals) outrivals ANY specialty coffee drink I've had in the West Coast... The coffee beans even had floral notes. It is simply the BEST and most unique latte I've ever had and priced fairly at $6.

The cashier and barista were a pleasure to talk to. The barista wanted to check out all the LA coffee places as a gift to himself after graduation and I shared with him all my favorites.

Vegan/vegetarian new restaurant in Lutz shopping center.  The center is busy as it has many other establishments but there is a decent amount of parking.  

I ordered a "chicken" buffalo wrap.  I was very surprised to find out the chicken is made with mushrooms and egg whites.  It tasted just like a chicken nugget. I was impressed and would order again. The corn chowder although fresh and overwhelming flavor of only dare I say corn and heavy cream. Although I know cream was not used those are the only two flavors I could pick up on.  

The Americano I had was good, nothing special.  Not quite sure where they source their beans and blends from.  

Nice option for a simple lunch if you are in the area.

If you're looking for a lively, energetic restaurant to have a dinner date, this is a nice start. My husband and I tend to scoot in and head straight for the bar to order small plates and appetizers, especially when the restaurant is uber busy. I was very surprised when Ulele came up when I searched local breweries.  Come to find out, they have about 5 beers that are brewed in house,  and let me tell you the Wedding beer is phenomenal! Mildly balanced with a slight fruit and floral note. .very very good! 

For appetizers we enjoyed the octopus carrpaccio, crispy okra fries with homemade ketchup and fresh green beans. Odd combos, but that's how we roll! All were decent and fresh but we really just enjoyed the libations and atmosphere the most.  

I will definatly return and venture a little more into the menu next time

Hands down so worth this being one of the first meals actually at a restaurant since the dreaded "C" word.  

We've seen all of the reviews about masks and social distancing so I'll skip right to the experience.

Ambiance is down right gorgeous.  Natural stones and bright blues that one may see while traveling abroad. The menu is lite and decently approachable. We both couldn't pass up the Psomi bagel.  Everything bagel, shaved red onions, sprouts, tomatoes and cucumbers.  All piled high on top of one of the best bagels I've had in Tampa.  I wish I could have ordered many to go but we were too late.  

Our mimosas were delightful.  Our service was refreshing and appreciated.  All in all the best meal out I could have imagined for the start of a girl's day.

Pro Tip: Don't sleep on the appetizer trio.  The yellow lentil dip is SO worth it!

What a phenomenal meal.  

My daughter and I enjoy an annual trip to Clearwater Beach each year. We always try a new restaurant for dinner where we can dress up enjoy. Although this is a nice restaurant I did not feel it was too pretentious. There were lots of lively patrons at the bar laughing enjoying having a good time. It is white cloth table top and over the top service but still approachable.

We started with the crispy calamari for an appetizer. This was a huge portion and absolutely delicious. You are also serve to small dinner rolls well that nice mango butter that complemented it very well.

I went for the sea scallop special. I unfortunately cannot recall each detail of the dish and all its components however it was spectacular and again a very large portion. My daughter splurged and went for the filet. Very enjoyable as expected.  

I would absolutely recommended this restaurant for anyone wanting to celebrate a special occasion or just expecting to have a nice meal.  I hope to return next year.

I can't quite figure this place out.  When entering we noticed it was super busy.  I'm glad everyone was out and about having fun. The bar is at the front of the restaurant right by the door.  Lots of patrons watching the football games.  You have to pass through this area to get to the diningroom or to the outside patio.  I get from the vibe that the bar area is a bit of a locals hangout..cool, this is my kind of spot but it had an odd vibe.  

We were sat inside in the dining room almost right smack dab in the middle of some sort of celebration.  Birthday? Family reunion? Again, odd.  Wish we weren't right in the middle of their party. 

The oysters were THE highlight for me.  Omg so fresh and the toppings were so inventive.  I can't remember the names of the dishes but oysters with fresh jalapeno..yes!  Oysters with vodka and cavier..yes! I would go back just for the these. 

The main dishes were just ok.  My pasta was uneventful and my friends was also just blah.  It was definitely missing something.  The burgers at the table were fine, not memorable.  

Prices aren't cheap but in the area it's a decent option.

Local homemade goodness! 

This family owned establishment just recently opened its brick and mortar after having several pop-ups over the years. You can tell this place already has a following. During breakfast on a Saturday morning there are lots of patrons in and out ordering their goodies to go as well as dining in.

I like the area of Ybor this is in. It looks like there's going to be some revitalization and the outside as well as the inside of this new restaurant is adorable. 

Obviously you're going for the flan however don't miss the Cuban sandwich or the fried cheese. I'm telling you both are must get. My eyes to keeping coffee was also delicious. I loved this breakfast and can't wait to return.  Well done.

I thought Whiskey Cake was great. 

The setting is beautiful of course. We were lucky enough to pop in during Happy Hour. Unfortunately/fortunately I was so involved in conversation with my friend I didn't catch the hours. Brandon was our bartender at the outside bar. He informed us all of the house made juices (except Cranberry) which was funny. I couldn't believe the Happy Hour options. Approximately 6 different crafted cocktails and the same amount of light but options. Our guava forward cocktails were light and delicious. We enjoyed a creative cheese board with black truffle havarti, black forest ham, local honeycomb and house made pimento. It was delicious and all for $5!

Day 8 and they're doing great. I can't believe this establishment has only been open for 8 days and is running so smoothly. 

I stopped in for lunch and had a quick seat at the bar. Both bartenders were super personable and really added to the experience. They have so many drink options. All with fresh juices made in house. I thought it was interesting that they had three decanters hanging in the middle of the bar, each with a wonderful sounding cocktail. One was an apple cinnamon rum yum! There was a hibiscus infused mezcal and the third one escapes me. I enjoyed a Palermo which was nicely balanced with grapefruit juice and tequila as well as a margarita named Salt Aire.  I asked for mine without the salt foam but next time I'm going to give it a go. Both cocktails were very nice.

I really wanted to try a noodle soup with miso broth and shrimp however, I went for the three taco and one side lunch for $10.95. The spicy cucumber salad was delightful. Needed a little bit of salt for my taste but spicy yet refreshing. My favorite taco was the jerk chicken which was flavorful, balanced and I was so delicious. Author did the angry pork taco and spicy korean BBQ. Both were memorable.

$28 before too for lunch but I'm A ok with that as it was a very enjoyable luncheon.  I can't wait to return.

Fantastic option for a special occasion. This is the type of restaurant that you should branch out and go all out to sample many menu items. 

Reservations are recommended. I called the day ahead to get a 6:30 p.m. at the cooking bar. There are lots of servers food runners so it's a tight fit in some areas however it almost adds to the atmosphere. I love being able to watch the line cooks and the sous chefs do their thing. I was mesmerized.

My husband and I went ALL out with a $80 bottle of Barbera from Italy. Our awesome server used a decanter for us. It was a delightful wine. I'm glad we splurged. Speaking of splurging with the $80 bottle of wine we also ordered $120 worth of food. Were we hungry? or where we really excited about all of the menu options? I have no regrets.

3/5 sea bass with glass noodles and panang curry. The curry was a little too light in flavor and the bass was almost not cooked long enough. It was very chewy. I would skip this one.

5/5 Cobia collar bone. The presentation was stunning. The broth with a limey sweet flavor was perfect with the perfectly crisp fish that was lightly coated in rice flour. I will forever remember this dish.

3/5 grouper cheeks with roe, collard green mayo and dusted onion ash. Nicely done and the presentation was beautiful but the grouper was a little bland. Although it was fried perfectly. I may skip this one as well next time.

5/5 gnocchi with short ribs. I want more of this right now. Perfectly pillowy gnocchi with smoked ricotta need I say more?

4/5 oysters were $3.75 a piece so I only ordered two. They needed more acidity. There was a cherry ponzu sauce which sounded promising but did not lend much flavor and an overwhelming addition of sesame oil. Not my favorite.

5/5 foie gras was served with crisp marinated pear cashew Nutella and Huckleberry jam. When mixed together it almost tasted like a PB&j sandwich absolutely phenomenal and very memorable. 

I am so excited about the experience we had it rooster and till and for many special occasions she come can imagine us revisiting again and again.

I'm really pleasantly surprised actually. Have eaten here before and do typically like this as a lunch option but I typically frequent one of the other Frenchy's locations. I've got to admit, this is a close 2nd for me.

Not a lot of shaded or should I say interior seating so we grabbed a seat at the bar. There's lots of seats outside under umbrellas but it's seriously too hot in the summertime.

I always get the shrimp diablo. I highly recommend this dish with rock shrimp, creamy blue cheese and spicy sauce. Nice toast to soak up all that awesome deliciousness. I tried the fried corn..yummy! Get this too. The fried clams are well, fried clams. Surprisingly, I enjoyed the grouper eggrolls. They are made southwest style and if I'm being honest I did not taste much grouper at all but the flavor was overall pretty good. 

The two gentlemen bartenders we're great.  Service with a smile.

As background, my wife and I almost always eat Asian foods at home and when we go out. When in China and Hong Kong, hot pot is a routine and something we look forward to. Here in the US there are not too many but in China they are not only popular but they are "the" spot to go with family and friends.

We had seen the sign for Hippot Shabu Shabu while they were developing the site and were looking forward to its opening. There are various restaurants that say they have hot pot but none really recreate the hot pot of China, at least in the Philly area. 

We were in San Francisco the previous week and visited the Little Sheep branded hot pot restaurant. That one was headquartered in China until its recent acquisition by the US based YUM Brands. I say this only because it is a good comparison of a China based hot pot restaurant chain re-deployed in the US under the Chinese branding. 

So those are my points of comparison.

We were in Chinatown shopping on 9/6/2014 when we thought we would check on the Hippot to see if it had opened. We were happy to find it had and latter found out that they had just opened that day. What luck! We arrived about 7:00pm and it was packed. We had a twenty minute wait which was fine and the staff were very pleasant, checking on us and providing us with assurance we would have a table soon, and we did.

The menu is easy to follow and provides a wide array of food. Now if you are not used to hot pot the way it works is that you pay for a hot pot which contains a "soup" (my words) or base that can be herbal or spicy. You can get a split bowl which has two sections containing each type. Next you order meats, vegetables, dumplings and noodles. These are delivered raw. You then drop in what you want to eat into the bowl and let it cook. When you take out your food from the pot you can dip it in sauces and eat. 

As you enter the restaurant you will see it is very stylish in a subtle way providing an upscale and modern Asian feel. It is a nice departure from the more plain or gaudy restaurants in Chinatown. It can handle couples or large groups easily and is well ventilated so the steam of the hotpots doesn't linger too long. To the rear of the restaurant is the self serve sauce station. They had a wide variety of sauces and herbs that you can mix and match to your liking. I kept it simple though you can head in many directions and be happy. 

As I mentioned earlier, there is a wide variety of food, greater than others we have seen. We kept our order simple, order lamb, Taro, Enoki Mushroom, Tofu Skin, shrimp dumplings, and spinach. All was fresh and high quality which is something you can tell with hotpot since the food is raw unlike most any restaurant that smothers food with sauce and cheese. 

The staff were very helpful and attentive to all the guests. There were some day one confusions but nothing of substance and anything e encountered was quickly resolved with friendly apologies. Whatever kinks they had on the first and well attended day were minor and will be quickly worked out. 

All in all, Hippot Shabu Shabu is one of the best in Philly and the only hot pot restaurant that can compete on a level with those across the country and even in China. We definitely will be back and back often.

Stopped in for lunch today with my friend and really had a wonderful time! 

The service was amazing. I drank the peach sangria - yummy! But a little on the sweet side. But I drank the whole thing, so I'm not complaining ;-) 

The bread and butter is a great starter, but try not to get full off of that. 

I ordered the open-faced short rib and white cheddar cheese sandwich that came with home made potato chips. The chips tasted a bit stale, but I didn't mind as I was watching my carbs anyway. The short rib Sammy was sooooooo good!! Perfectly seasoned & tasty. I would definitely get that again. 

As we were paying, the sweet server overheard me mentioning my birthday & made some adjustments to the bill. She also gave a us free dessert. 

The biggest surprise was a handwritten card that manager gave me that had a birthday wish and a free appetizer card for my next visit! Yay!!!

I will say this place does have good food but the service today was horrible. It took over an hour for us to get our food. This is subs and french fries were talking about not steak and lobster! Absolutely ridiculous for it to take over an hour to get served. Management just kept saying sorry and that they only had one cook. I understand things come up but still not a good enough reason for it to take this long! I will not be coming back here anymore!

I've had my eye on this place for awhile and I'm so glad I didn't wait any longer to try it! 
On a Thursday night there was a 30 minute wait but open spaces at the bar. 

The service was quick and helpful. Chips & salsa come to the table for free and the tortilla chips were warm and crisp. 

House margs come in frozen or on the rocks.

Empanadas trio appetizer was amazing. They were fried perfectly and the chicken, cheese and steak fillings were seasoned and cooked perfectly too. 

Ordered the 3 tacos mix & match. If you're feeling adventurous they have a grasshopper taco! Honesty it was better than the fish and the pork belly imo. The fish was a bit bland and the pork belly should be fatty and crisp and it was not. The grasshopper is definitely novelty but tastes a bit like sunflower seeds? Go try it. 
Hands down the best taco was the octopus! Definitely get this...maybe x3! 

Pro tip: Half price margs on Tuesday & Thursdays!

This restaurant's niche is it bills itself as a fine dining establishment that serves massive portions. What most people realize in going here is that you're basically paying for almost two platters worth of food on one plate and that the size of the appetizers and entrees is reflected in the cost. 

Seven Stars Inn holds an unflattering distinction as being the 2nd worst dining experience I have ever had in my life (#1 is held by a TGI Fridays). Sadly, the unbelievably bad experience had nothing to do with the food, which for the most part was pretty good, and had EVERYTHING to do with our server and the host. Just thinking about the dinner our party had here makes me angry.

I should qualify this review by stating that the dining experience I'm writing about happened a while ago - before I learned about the existence of Yelp. Normally I wouldn't bother writing a review so long after the fact, but the story is so incredible and this restaurant so badly ruined what was supposed to be a special evening out (retirement celebration) that it still brings back memories for everyone that was in our dinner party.

Our waitress gave our party of 8 the worst service I have ever witnessed at a "fine dining" restaurant. To start things off her demeanor was a tad cold, at least towards our table. Throughout the evening various things occurred that irked us about the service we were receiving, including receiving some drinking glasses that had large chips at the rim where you put your lips (EEK). However, nothing compares to the lack of attentiveness she gave our party. We watched during the 2+ hours we were here while she zipped around to other tables of diners refilling drinks, clearing plates, checking in to see if everything was ok. All things she was REPEATEDLY negligent in doing for our table. 

Not too long into our dining experience a number of us were getting annoyed at the lack of service we were receiving and we are NOT a demanding bunch. So I decided to go have a talk with the host. The host was a middle aged gentleman who sat on a stool by a podium and resembled Jesse Ventura with glasses. I told him what had happened thus far and he said that he would take care of it. About 45 minutes after my first visit to the host it was clear that nothing had changed. Our plates were not being cleared, our drinks were not being refilled, more rolls and butter were not being brought out, and all while we watched our waitress serve other tables in an efficient manner. We attempted on several occasions throughout the night to get her attention as she was walking nearby coming from other tables and unbelievably most of the time she wouldn't even look our way. On at least one ocassion she looked right at us as several of us were gesturing to get here attention and she just kept right on walking. We were dumbfouded. It was as if we were lepers. 

I paid my second visit to the host almost 2 hours into our dinner. Once again we had been sitting with empty dinner plates and empty drink glasses for roughly a 1/2 hour and the waitress was still ignoring our table. On this visit to the host he seemed less interested in what I was telling him and the way he responded didn't inspire confidence that anything was going to be done. A short while after my second complaint to the host the waitress finally visited our table and cleared our plates - I think this was just coincidence. She once again disappeared and now we were left sitting with no offer for coffee or a dessert menu. After 2 discreet complaints by me to the host regarding our waitress's chronic inattentiveness (among a few other things), it was clear that nothing had changed. After sitting idle for another 15 minutes we collectivley decided to just give up and end the evening early by getting the check because we didn't feel like waiting another 1/2 hour for dessert. 

As we walked through the foyer I paid my 3rd and final visit to the host. I told him that I wanted him to know that we got tired of waiting for our server and were so disappointed with our service that we decided to skip dessert and just leave. I also mentioned to him that my comments to him had changed nothing and that our waitress had been ignoring us all evening. His reply to me was a flippant, "we'll make it up to you next time." I was so flabbergasted at his response to me that I just walked away. My thought and what I should have said to him was "Oh really? How are you going to do that, by giving us the service we should have received tonight on our next visit?", but I was left speechless by his response. So this is the type of service you can expect from a $400 night out at a restaurant that bills itself as fine dining!?! 

As someone who eats out often I realize that any restaurant can have an off night but that wasn't the case here. This was blissful ignorance, lack of courtesy and blatant disregard for the customer. No one in our party of 8 has ever gone to this restaurant since.

Did you know that Theo's does thin crust pizza?? I love pizza but hate the super carb load, but with Theo's thin crust pizza I can have my slice and eat it too (bad pun, I know). You can make any pizza a thin crust, and they do a great job getting that perfect crisp. It reminds me of the thin crustiness of my native New York pizza. There's also an option for gluten free. Throw in a box of wings and their special creamy Italian wing sauce, which pairs perfectly as pizza dipping sauce.

Terrible from start to finish. Poor service at the bar, the food that came out was not cooked properly and the restaurant was not very clean. The TV was blasting a right wing news channel that was giving everyone a headache. The server kept mixing up our drink and food items then washed dishes splashing us with dirty water at the bar. Such an odd experience. The Deanie's on Magazine is the opposite experience FYI.
Someone told me is was good so I decided to come and try it out. Is not as good as I thought so I won't come here again. I always got to the Eldorado is a lot better

You know some places never really live up to their hype. And wow was this one hyped up. I was like ok, ok, ok I know it's like the brother of Datz or something, which is incredible, so I bet it's good but it probably isn't THAT good... and OMG Roux just BLEW me away. Superior quality, superior taste, superior service, it was hands down the best dining experience I've had in Tampa to date. 

I really owe a big portion of our experience to our waiter, Adam. He really made the night one of a kind. He was funny, energetic, and there for us whenever we needed something. I didn't know what a crawfish was and he went to the kitchen to literally bring one out to show me. My bf and I were having a disagreement about dessert -- he wanted bananas, I wanted bread pudding -- so he had the kitchen put bananas on the bread pudding. GENIUS.

I should probably mention more about the food.

We started with the Gator bites. Like chicken, but BETTER. And with that side sauce that added that special little kick. MAGNIFICENT.

Entree. Andouille crusted wahoo is WHERE IT IS AT. And those grits - boy am I a fan of those creole cream cheese grits. I never knew I even liked grits. FANTASTIC.

And the bread pudding with caramel and vanilla ice cream on the side - come ON. If you're a hummer and dancer at the dining table when you start eating something delish, like me, then you're going to be singing and dancing all the way back to the car. 

You know what -- put down your phone, stop reading this review, and just GO. I've never talked this much in all caps EVER IN MY LIFE. You can thank me later ;)

We have been going to Jake's for over 15 years and have genuinely enjoyed our time there every time, until last night. We have celebrated birthdays, graduations, and anniversaries there and true to form were there for my mom's birthday on Saturday night. 

We were greeted by Cosmo and shown to our table and promptly had our drink orders taken. We were given a comfortable amount of time to select food and after giving our order only had a short wait until our appetizers and eventual dinner arrived. 

From dinner on the service went downhill quickly. They were inconsistent and flaky; the older blonde expediter/waitress cleared all plates at the table and told me she would be right back to clear mine; 30 minutes later I finally flagged down our waitress (younger brunette woman) and asked her to clear it.

She took our coffee/tea orders and disappeared only to return 15 minutes later with the beverages. She asked if we wanted to look at the dessert menu, and although we did (we were planning on having some birthday profiteroles) we declined and 10 minutes later got the check. Good food but absolutely terrible service; especially when the bill was $250+. Total seated time: 2.5 hours.

We politely told Cosmo on the way out how terrible the service was and although he genuinely seemed concerned (and tried to offer drinks and dessert on the house) we just wanted to get out of there. I would never recommend this place for a special occasion and will seriously caution my parents against doing the same. 

How the mighty have fallen.

I came here for their famous lobster roll and added a clam chowder as well. It was a perfect amount of food. For $16, you get a GENEROUS amount of lobster in the halfwhich! If you're extra hungry they offer a foot long but for me, personally, the portion I got was enough along with the chowder. 

I don't come here often because it's a tad bit out of the way for me but I was also recommended to try the fried haddock from someone who really knows his seafood. I'll have to try it next time! 

PROS: The lobster roll hype is real. They have an app where you can earn a free meal with visits. They have weekday specials (the same person told me Monday is an awesome special). 

CONS: location for me

COVID Quarantine Takeout!
You can park by the comedy club (I didn't find it so I just pulled to the side up front) but if you're having trouble, the owner told me over the phone he could bring the food out to me. I thought that was very nice! 

I came here on Sara M's recommendation on the Koa Soi, a yellow curry with peas and carrots. I got a side of pork belly and.. who doesn't love drinking Thai tea with your meal? 

I'm usually a huge fan of Panang curry, so getting yellow curry this time was out of my comfort zone. It's definitely milder and the flavors are more subtle. I added my own extra pepper flakes to it, but I still thoroughly enjoyed it as well as the fresh noodles. By the way.. Did you notice the SIZE of my meal?! HOLY COW that could last me 3 meals if I was portion controlling! That's the best part about getting this as takeout. You can mix a small portion of your curry and noodles together and save the rest of the separated ingredients for the next day so that the noodles don't soak up the sauce and mess up the texture if you're saving some for later.

The pork belly was great! I'm very picky with pork belly and I loved the way they seasoned and cooked this. There were tender pieces as well as charred and crisp pieces that played a great dance of texture on the senses. Some might complain that the slices are too thin, but I loved it that way because it was a nice balance of meat and fat. The dipping sauce wasn't soy sauce; it was a kind of hoisen sauce that paired well with the meat. 

TIP: I asked for my Thai tea without ice so that it doesn't melt on the way home! I just added ice at home. 

Also DO NOT TIP! These takeout containers aren't the best for liquid so try your best to secure it well in the car the first time. 

I noticed they're currently having family-style entrees where you pick 3 entrees for $36 that serves about 4 people (comes with white rice.. can upgrade to fried for extra $$). Lets be realistic here.. it probably serves like 5-6 people with their portion sizes!

We continue to be sad about the way this little village is run.  This is a pure tourist trap.  The stores here are terrible.  It is all junk and stuff you can buy at home.  The few good restaurant have left.  This place is not kid friendly at all!  

They do not cater to locals.  I spoke with their marketing director, who basically told me they do not care if locals come or not.  They are out to get people here once a year and get as much money from them once they are stuck here as possible.  As a child, I remember coming here and it was so romantic.  Things have changed greatly.  There is a reason the outlets across the street have not thrived.  In fact, they've had a problem finding tenants to stay.  It is such a shame.  We live 2 miles away and choose to go to Flemington for our shopping.  

It is a shame, because we would love to spend our money at PV, but don't feel welcomed.....

Such a shame and such a waste of a beautiful place.  It is always clean!!!  I can say that and the few restaurants are good as well.....   but overall, we are very disappointed in their business practices in the community...

I had no idea that BJ's Nevada Barbecue would turn into a favorite brunch location, but that's exactly what happened. Of course I had been here for ribs, but discovering that they also served brunch was a surprise! And have you tried those cinnamon rolls?!?

The staff here is so friendly and service is quick. The food is delicious and you get a good amount for your money. It's obvious that BJ's is a favorite with locals. 

Thank you for a wonderful dining experience! I'll definitely be back!

As excited as I am for Beddia's latest accolades I am also fearful of all the silly people who will now try to tarnish the reputation of this fine establishment because they are entitled babies. No, there's no phone. Yes, there is a chance you won't get pizza because people are lining up for pizza now. Yes, he only makes a certain amount each day. SHUT UP! Seriously, stop complaining. That's why it's good. If you read the article on Bon Appetit and all you understood from it was that you were entitled to eat the pizza, then I question your reading comprehension. 

The hours aren't bullshit. They open at 5:30. If twenty people line up before opening and 14 people buy two pizzas, crazy stoner Barry buys three, and the nine others get one each, that's forty pizzas. That is not bullshit. That's some standardized testing next level pizza math.

Ideal lunch spot for a birthday celebration today!

Sat outside under a heater with a glorious view of the marina. Could it be any more beautiful?

We start with the gargantuan bowl of clam chowder ... and I kid you not, this is the BEST clam chowder on the planet. I am from San Francisco and I've had my share of this stuff. THIS IS THE BOMB. Come here for the clam chowder. From wherever you are in the US of A. You will thank me.

We also have the crab and shrimp salad, the ahi poke salad, the calamari with fries and the seafood pasta. All of the dishes take our breath away when they arrive - beautiful presentation and a plethora of seafood. YUM.

Service is friendly. Prices are fair and beyond reasonable. What is not to love?

25 years ago, when I lived in the Pie Allen Historic District, there was a restaurant at this location called 'The Eggroll House'. It claimed to be French Vietnamese food and had the largest, best, most amazing eggrolls I've ever had the pleasure to eat.
Now it's the China Pasta House and has some of the most amazing noodle bowls I've ever had the pleasure to eat!
My mister and I were looking for an inexpensive restaurant for a quick dinner and he suggested we try this establishment. He had the Chicken and Cucumber Noddles ($7.24) and I had the Vegetable Noodles ($6.74). What we received were enormous portions of noodles, in my man's case chicken, shredded cucumbers, cilantro, mushrooms, and spinach. Both bowls had a peanut sauce that when tasted on it's own was rather salty...but mixed into the noodles it was just perfect! I tasted my guy's chicken and thought it could have used a little flavor, but the meat was tender and there was a lot of it!
I don't think the adorable little woman manning the counter spoke much english. but she was eager to please, gracious, and attentive.
The only reason I didn't give China Pasta House 5 stars was the restroom. I had to walk through the kitchen (which was spotlessly clean) to get to it and once inside it was a nightmare flashback to cross country gas stations restrooms. Grimy dirty and dimly lit.
It's no Eggroll House, but it's good, yummy, plentiful food and we'll return to try the big, steamed buns that were displayed in a steamer at the front counter!

Today was my 10th or so time eating here and it's always the BEST Jalisco style mexican food I've ever had. Their food has always been consistent in flavor, amount, quality, and presentation.
We've tried many different offerings  (I had their beans as a side today...perfect!) and I always seem to get their Pork Al Pastor taco. I've tried recreating the flavor at my home, and while mine may be good, the way this place makes theirs is so much better! Flavorful, moist, slightly sweet, and slightly spicy...I want to go back and get another one!
I'd never use a word like, "...mediocre." to describe this stout example of good Sonoran mexican chow. I would, however, use such adjectives as, "authentic", "satisfying", "homemade", "incredible", and "outstanding"!
We'll be bringing our friends here soon to experience what we've been raving for months about!!

This place offers sizable portions of very fresh Mexican cuisine.  It's open late and offers quick, no frills delivery at reasonable prices.  There are plenty of places hoping to compete in South Philadelphia, but only one or two are really in the same league, I've found.  My only complaint is that the guac is not as flavorful as I'd like.  I prefer a potent guac and theirs is more about the mild flavor of the aguacate.  However, their pico de gallo and salsas definitely make up for that.  Long story short, if I'm jonesing for tacos, this is probably where you'll find me.

I have been to this place 3 times now.  I first went there with my wife.  We had a very good experience.  Food was very good but not great.  The atmosphere was excellent.  Our waiter was very attentive but not intrusive.   We had one little issue with one of our entrées and they went out of their way to make it right.  We spoke with Amy for about 20 minutes at the end of our meal.  She was personable and seemed truly interested in our opinion of the restaurant

We enjoyed it so much we went for our youngest sons 6th birthday,  bringing along our 3 children and my parents.  What an amazing experience this time was.  My parents, who came from about 45 minutes away,  couldnt help but rave about the place,  the food,  the service,  the atmosphere.  Now that they are older,  they go out to eat alot and couldnt wait to come back.

And they didnt have to wait long because we came back just two weeks later for our older sons 12th birthday.  They allowed us to bring in our own cake,  and let us bring in our own desert to surprise my wife whose birthday was the next say.

Ive had the mussles in red all three times i was there and they have been amazing all three times.  I have had the crab soup twice.  First time was good,  the second time was amazing.  

A review good or bad will not sway me as to whether or not i spend my money in a place.  Nor will an owners response to any review.  How they choose to deal with things is their business.  I am a free thinking person and can form my own opinion from my own experience.  And from my own experience,  I am happy with AJ Stephens. Also from my experience,  when something wasnt right with my dinner experience here,  they owners and management of this place went above and beyond to try to make it right.  

Not every restaurant will be perfect night in and night out.  How they deal with those issues separate the good restaurants from the bad.  When i have brought my issues to the attention of the people at AJ Stephens,  my issues were resolved.

Also,  i see the reviews and people attacking this place for the owners response to a bad review.  Although as a business owner i would never response to a negative review this way,   i have read all the reviews of this place and have seen the same owners response to other negative reviews with class and dignity,  apologizing and asking them to come back in so they can try to make it right.  The difference with those reviews and the one where the owner lashed out at the reviewer is that those one had constructive criticism,   specific issues listed and exactly what they didnt like.  The review in question was nasty,  attacking with very vague issues that seems like it had an anterior motive.  Like i said,  i would never respond that way but as a business owner,  i have wanted to.

This is such a nice, elegant place for dining that we make it a point to come here for happy hour and/or dinner.

It's well known to the locals for its tasty dishes and drinks; attentive and friendly service, as well as elegant ambience. Although the prices are on the high side, the quality of food, service and ambience are well in line with the best of fine dining standard.

DETAILS, Details, details...

A few days ago, my wife and I enjoyed our happy hour in its nicely appointed lounge, followed by a wonderful dinner.  The friendly hostess warmly greeted us and took us to a corner table. We liked the relaxing, luxurious ambience with soft, dim lights. Near our dinner reservation time, 6:15p, the charming hostess ushered us to a great corner table in the dining room. The medium size, elegant dining room was still half empty then, but it'd  soon be completely filled up.

During my Happy Hour earlier, I had a delicious, vodka martini with stuffed olives. It was so tasty that I had another one at dinner! We also shared a bottle of wine over apps of (1) Beef tartare and (2) Kale salad. Both apps were very appetizing. The beef tartare was tender and was bursting with flavor in every bite! We liked the complimentary warm cheese puffs a lot, too, which were light, and super delicious with salted butter. 

Our main courses were (1) 12 oz Ribeye and (2) Chilean sea bass. 
- Interestingly, our server brought out a box of steak knives to choose from! My wife took a feel of each knife and picked a German crafted one.  She loved it as it cut her steak like butter, which was cooked exactly to her liking. My Chilean sea bass was fresh, flaky and flavorful! Yes, we happily shared them. 

We also shared three tasty sides of Fried baby artichokes, Garlic meshed-potatoes, and Creamy spinach. We were so satisfied and FULL that we had to skip desserts all together this time! Believe me, this almost never happens! 

Our server, Glenn, and his crew were just delightful, attentive but not overly so. Our water glasses were kept full, and the finished plates were cleared discretely. They saw that we loved the cheese puff, and offered us extra without our asking. 

We totally enjoyed our dinner experience, and will be back next time in town. This place is already well known to locals. So, if you love fine dining, Barclay Prime would be a good place to go to, when you are visiting Philly. 

By the way, if you like taking a leisure walk after a satisfying meal, the beautiful Rittenhouse Square Park is right across the street from Barclay! We did! 

October 2015

First impressions while driving to Danny Boy: Are we in the right place? Man, it's dark out here in the suburbs! Holy crap did you see that house we just passed! Maybe I should have worn something nicer then flannel? 

Walking into Danny Boy: Impressive! Loved the architectural details: large Irish pub style doors, beer bottle lighting, large garage doors that will provide an indoor outdoor feel in warmer months, a large stone-top bar that goes on for miles, lots of shiny stainless steel, sexy looking fermentation tanks that want to be seen and can be seen. 

Beer is excellent! Loved the Danny Boy Black IPA & Boston Asphalt (Black IPA aged with Jameson Chips). I am not a huge Witbier drinker but the Miss Ginger Witte surprised me. I can see myself easy drinking that tasty beverage in the Summer. 

I admit, I felt the location was a little odd (at first) in the heart of Village of West Clay however, I love the sense of community. It makes me wish we could all have breweries, in our neighborhoods, in the suburbs. It would be a great way to get to know our neighbors or have those hard conversations. Hey Jim & Susie, we've been meaning to talk to you about your lawn gnome collection. It may be getting out of hand. Let's meet over beers at our neighborhood brewery to discuss? First round is on me. I am sure that conversation would go much smoother. 

The staff are very helpful and friendly. They did a wonderful job opening night taking care of guests (they were packed). Can't wait to come back on a normal night. 

Notes: Love the upper level where families with kids can hang out. Downstairs is for 21 and older. Food is available for purchase. Greeks Pizza (across the street) will deliver to Danny Boy. In warmer months the garage doors will open to provide pet-friendly patio seating. 

I agree with Ian B. the hard part is getting there but once your there you won't want to leave.

I'm always on the hunt for healthier fast options for lunch and OMONI sure fits that bill. They have created two menus one for those in a time crunch and one for those that have time to settle in and stay awhile - smart thinking OMONI. For example, I ordered the #6 Bibimbap served in a hot stone bowl which took a bit longer to cook and prepare however if I was in a hurry I could order #1 - same dish without the bowl. 

Topping, sides and seasonings - so many to choose from! I admit, I get a little sweaty with food anxiety trying to pick from a cornucopia of selections. I personally wanted to try all of the house made kimchi options (radish, cucumber, cabbage) however I was thankful to read the list of recommended toppings/seasonings for my dish and went with the basic suggested 4 and added kimchi....because I need that kimchi! The lady behind the counter was also very friendly and helpful with recommendations which made the "Chipotle made your way" style ordering process easy. The bowl came piping hot and the serving size was large. I also really enjoyed my Jujubee tea with little bits of plum.  

There is a beer menu with about 4-5 selections for those looking to partake in an adult beverage. I would love to see some outdoor seating added as they do have the space for it. They definitely could use a sprinkle of signage visible in front of the strip mall area/near the overpass. As others have mentioned it's difficult to find and you wouldn't even know the business was there unless someone told you about it or you discovered it on Yelp.

Note: the story behind this business is beautiful, for some warm fuzzy's read about it on their website: http://omonigrill.com/About-us/.

Went here for the first time a few weeks ago. Needless to say I won't be going back. Quick 3 reasons

1. Rude, arrogant ownership. I tried asking him for suggestions and he wouldn't even acknowledge me. No smiles, no thank you. Just an awkward experience from start to finish.

2. Complete ripoff. I paid around $11 for a sandwich and drink. The sandwich was a abomination (the "Tucson", which is turkey, green chile and Swiss). I've seen thicker pancakes than these things. There was probably 2 pieces of turkey and a tablespoon of chile. 

3. There are better options nearby for less money. Save yourself some cash and some sanity, go to Baggins down the street. Even jimmy johns is better. 

Note to ownership: if you think you can survive in this market with rude service and subpar quality you are only kidding yourself.

Missing some comfort Vietnamese food from home, we stopped by here after coming back from Orlando. We were here on vacay and was in need of a nice homey dinner and found this place. The restaurant was pretty big inside, not too crowded on a weekday night. 

Service was pretty quick and lucky us because we were starving. We went with a bowl of pho, chicken fried rice, and stir fried veggies with tofu. The stir fry had a sweet sauce with broccoli, carrots, and tofu. It was balanced out perfectly if you eat it with white rice. The pho broth was sweet but not as flavored as I'm used to. 

Portions were pretty big. We didn't finished everything so had it packed for to-go back to our hotel. It ended up being breakfast the next day, still tasted good. Overall, it was the comfort food we needed.

Run down hotel. It looks good on the website but not in person. People here are unprofessional, rude, disrespectful and bad management. This shit hole will not last. Everything about this hotel is wrong and the people that works here dont give a damn about their jobs. THUMBS DOWN FOR ME!!!

Put my name on a barstool because I'm about to become a permanent fixture here! 
Usually I would be weary of eating at a restaurant on its opening night because they usually have a lot to work out, but I don't have anything but amazing things to say about the food. We tried a bunch of things tonight.. 
Shrimp scampi and fire roasted shrimp - I preferred the shrimp scampi flavor wise but the shrimp themselves are so tasty, fresh and jumbo!  Margherita pizza - very good, New York style vibes. Linguini and clam sauce - amazing - I inhaled it. Tiramisu - literally one of the best I've ever had. 

The menu has so much VARIETY, you can eat here whether you want to eat comfort food OR healthy food. There are a lot of veggie options for vegetarians/vegans. I love how many options of seafood there are! I love that they are small plates so you can try a bunch of items! You can build your own pizza's and pasta! They have very unique handcrafted cocktails. I am so excited that this has opened up in my neighborhood and highly recommend everyone to try it!

Simply put. B&S blew me away. It is now my go to steakhouse in the city (until I finally try Barclay Prime to see if it matches the hype). Everything about my experience was perfect and more. 

I have little to no words regarding how to describe the steak. Let's just say it was in my top 3 steaks (yes, I have a top 5) I've ever had. The other two were not in Philadelphia. 

Service was perfect. A friend and I split a bottle of wine and she came around to pour any time the glass neared empty. She knew the menu inside out. Desserts (I believe) are all made in house. 

It's obviously pricey for those who may be watching their wallet but it's worth the trip if you go. A great night all around.

Points for: Food, service, wine, everything.
No negatives.

The first rule of Sushi Club?  That no one talks about how many times I sent those wipe off menus back with more rolls and apps aaaaaand...yeah.  We won't talk about that. 

Having visited the Westside location, I was PUMPED to learn that they were adding a location up north!  

Truth be told, Sushi Club totally caters to those who prefer 'non-traditional' rolls full of cream cheese and tempura and deep fried goodness and a TON of things all in one roll.  If you are a sushi purist, you may wanna steer clear and hit a place like Sakura (our fav, honestly).  However, for less than $25 at Sushi Club you can eat to your heart's content - that's right - all the miso soup, salads, crab rangoon, gyoza, rolls, and even dessert you want - all for one price (changes depending on the day of the week and if it is a holiday).  PRO TIP: Pay close attention to how many pieces come in each roll - some have 3 and some have 8 - and you are charged if you leave more than 7 pieces on the table ($1 per piece) - so don't let your eyes get bigger than your stomach!  

Long story short - Sushi Club is PERFECT for that girl's night or date night when you just wanna sit and chat and keep ordering whatever the table thinks sounds good without worrying about how much it will cost or splitting the bill evenly. Service was good.  Is it my favorite in town?  Naw.  But for the value and sheer gluttony of it - 5 stars.

My husband has never had a proper milkshake.  GASP!  ...because he has a true dairy allergy.   This all changed the night we went in to Gordon's Milkshake Bar and he found out what he has been missing all these years. Hooooooray for Vegan options!  We did not opt to partake this visit, but you can also make your milkshake BOOZY!  Or add CBD!

Located on Mass Ave - roughly between Boomerang BTQ and Homespun on that same side of the road - Gordon's has a great variety of pre-made/pre-determined milkshake recipes on the board, and they will adjust these according to your wishes.  All orders are hand-made on the spot and in sight.  You can also opt to just get scoops of ice cream or make a sundae  - you do you, boo.  While the prices seem a little high (I think we paid about $18 with tip for 2 shakes), I assure you that you get a LOT in your end result.  Our shakes were HEAVY and chock full of mix ins.  We each enjoyed our selections and we cannot wait to go back and try another round. 

Now - if you hear nothing else, hear me on this.  GO HUNGRY.  We thought this would be great for dessert (and it IS), but we were wayyyy too full when we got there to truly enjoy this massive shake.  We each only got through about 1/8th of it before tapping out.  Do yourself a favor and have an ice cream for dinner night and just enjoy.

Since my last review I have gone through the drive through several times to get my own meal.  Roast beef is okay as are the other sandwiches, but of course I check my order before pulling away.  Realistically I would rate them 2.5 stars if possible.

Good breakfast choices, some of which are available later than normal break fast time.  I haven't tried much of the lunch fare other than the chili which I thought was very good.

Staff is friendly and accurate.

Picked up burgers and chicken sandwiches for 3 people along with fries.  The fries were okay, average, as good as most places.  1 person enjoyed their double cheeseburger.  I had a bacon double cheeseburger plain, and found it a bit overcooked and tasted a little strange.  The person with the chicken sandwich was a fan.
 
The size of the sandwiches were impressive.  Next opportunity I will try one of the other items on the menu.

I hadn't been to this Mexican restaurant before, so I decided to give it a try for lunch.  Parking lot was not a problem and most of the tables were empty.
 
After being seated it was the standard routine of menu, drink, setting fairly quickly.  I had a taste for fajitas, as I had not had them in a while, so I ordered the dinner version.  While I waited for my order my server brought my drink (Pepsi products) and chips and salsa.  The chips were a little greasy.  Not bad, but not the best I have had recently either.
 
The fajita platter arrived after a while, and it was so hot that the steam obscured the pictures that are included.  As I am apt to do I tasted one of the pieces of chicken and one of the pieces of meat via fork to get a sense of the taste without all the rest of the add ons.  I can say that both tasted very plain, no sense of seasoning at all.  When wrapped with the lettuce, cheese, and rest the overall tasted was good, though not great.
 
My server was friendly and attentive.  Overall experience was not bad, but their are better local choices.

I am reviewing the Chili's on West Brandon Blvd, near the Sam's Club.  I want to be clear because I have been to the Chili's in Valrico on SR60, and my impression was so bad this is the first time I have been back to a Chili's in a few years.  I didn't know what to expect, but I had fond memories of enjoying this particular location in the past.
 
About 1:30 PM on Thursday afternoon I arrived to the parking lot, and it took a few minutes to find a spot.  The restaurant had a fair amount of empty tables, perhaps about half full.  I was seated at one of those half booths, with a booth seat on one side and two chairs on the other.
 
My server came over quickly, gave me the main menu and two other special menus.  She took my drink order which was a Coca Cola.  She quickly brought over the Coke and a large basket of chips and bowl of salsa.  After my experience the prior day, I appreciated the rich full flavor of this fountain Coca Cola.  The chips were thin, crisp, and very fresh, and the salsa was just the right amount of zesty to fit my taste.  

I spent a few minutes looking at the menu, and then noticed the table flyer which listed a "3 for $10" deal.  I chose the beverage, salad, and bacon cheese burger as the three items.  The chips and salsa are one of the alternatives to the salad, but I was already getting those for free.  Anyone who is a member of Chili's club gets free chips and salsa on every visit, but if you aren't you can quickly sign up at the table and it is good for that visit as well.
 
The house salad was fresh and tasty, the wine vinaigrette very tasty.  The cheeseburger that I ordered cooked medium, was done exactly right.  You will see in the attached photos that there was a generous amount of bacon.  In essence, it was prepared perfectly, and one of the best bacon cheeseburgers I have had in quite awhile.  The french fries which accompanied the meal were also very tasty.  I looked up the prices of the individual items in the menu, and if not for the "3 for $10" deal they would have cost me twice as much.
 
I was stuffed, but couldn't resist ordering the Skillet Chocolate Chip Cookie for dessert.  This is a freshly baked chocolate cookie in a small pan, topped with vanilla ice cream, and drizzles of chocolate syrup.  Absolutely heavenly.
 
All in all, one of the best meals I have had in a long time at an unexpected place.  Note that this is  a Sports Bar at heart.  Not a tremendous amount of screens, but the music was a bit loud.

I've tried the other BBQ places in the area and couldn't find ribs that I really liked.  Thought I would give Smokin Pig a try as I was in the area.
 
Ordered Baby Back and St Louis ribs to go and some lean Beef Brisket.  The St Louis ribs were excellent.  Very meaty and very little fat.  This was a surprise to me as other places I have been to this might be the normal description of Baby Back ribs. $24.25 a slab.  You can also order as a dinner plate which includes two sides.
 
The Baby Back ribs were a bit of a disappointment.  Not much meat and more fat than I am used to.
 
The Lean Beef Brisket was cut into 3/8 inch slabs and was very good, the best I have had around here.
 
Sides I ordered were fries and Mac and Cheese.  Both were okay, though I was a little surprised that the Mac and Cheese pasta was shells.  No complaint about that, in fact was a nice change.  Texas toast was also supplied.
 
Prices were about 15 - 20% higher than what I am used to, though certainly worth it for the St. Louse Ribs and the Brisket.  There are a variety of other things on the menu, though on my next trip I'll probably stick with the St. Louis ribs since they were so good.
 
The staff was really friendly, and even carried the food out to my car for me.  4+ stars, I will be returning.

This time I went with 2 other folks this afternoon at about 4 pm.  Parking was plentiful, and there were many tables to choose from.  We were greeted immediately, and approached by our server as soon as we were seated.  All in all service was excellent.
 
I ordered a NY Strip Steak, medium, cooked Pittsburgh style.  It was done appropriately, and served in a timely fashion.  The reason for decreasing my rating from my last visit was solely the fact that the cut of beef was not as good as last time, too much fat to have to trim away.
 
An overall enjoyable experience.  The other diners had desserts which they thoroughly enjoyed.  I will continue to try this location in the future, though perhaps will try a different cut of beef.

Placed a largish take out order from Shells this evening.  Gave them plenty of time as I said we would like to pick up the order in 1 hour.  We ordered several different things:  shrimp pasta with $4 extra shrimp, Buffalo shrimp with $4 extra shrimp, Fried shrimp dinner, child's cheeseburger, child's chicken tenders, shrimp mezzo mezzo with $4 extra shrimp, and a bacon cheddar burger specified with just cheese (no lettuce or tomato)  and the bacon on the side.
 
First the three mistakes:
 
the cheeseburger patty sat on top of a slice of tomato that wasn't supposed to be there.
 
We had asked for packets of ketchup that were not included.

The menus listed that all child meals include:  apple sauce, teddy grahams, and a soft drink.  Since we ordered two child meals there should have been two of each.  In fact what we received were 1 apple sauce, 1 teddy grahams, and no soft drinks.
 
On the plus side, everything we received was cooked to order.  The shrimp dishes were very good.  I expected a bit more shrimp than received in the dinners where we added an extra $4 shrimp.

The meal was ready at the time requested.  The rating would have been 4 stars, if not for the mistakes and missing child dinner items.

I hadn't read any reviews prior to stopping at this Mexican restaurant.  It is in a part of town I usually only drive through after a doctor appointment, and I just happened to be really hungry as I was passing by.  It turned out to be a very fortuitous change event.
 
This relatively small center has several stores, including another restaurant.  It was fairly early for dinner, so I had no problem finding parking.  On entering I saw that most of the tables were still empty, yet there were several servers wandering around looking like they were anticipating a dinner rush.  This turned out to be true, and by the time I finished eating, many of the tables and booths and bar stools were occupied.
 
I was cordially greeted on entering and seated at a table of my choice.  My server immediately brought over a place setting and menu, and took my drink order.  I tried to capture most of the menu in attached pictures, and you will see it is extensive.
 
After bringing my soda and water, I also received a bowl of tortilla chips and a bowl of salsa.  The chips were hot, fresh, and crispy, just excellent.  I ended up ordering an appetizer, Nachos with Beef and Beans.  The order of Nachos was huge, and could have easily served as an entire meal for one or two people.  My server informed me that he would wait until I was done with my appetizer before bringing out the main course.
 
I had ordered combination #11:  one beef burrito, one taco, and one enchilada.  The taco was on a separate smaller plate, while the burrito and enchilada shared a plate, which I was warned was very hot.  Given this information, I dug into the taco first.  Scrumptious.  This was no Taco Bell taco by any means.  After finishing the taco I began to work on the burrito and enchilada, having some of one and then the other.  I wanted badly to sample everything, and knew there was no way I could finish all the food.  In the end I was able to eat about half of everything that I had ordered, and I shouldn't have forced myself to eat that much.
 
This is one of the best Mexican restaurants I have had the pleasure to eat at, and definitely will return.
 
A couple of things to note.  As stated on the menu, the soft drinks have a maximum of 3 free refills.  The bowl of chips that are brought to your table when you are seated are free, but refills of chips or salsa are extra.

My first time here, and I was expecting a dive bar.  Unexpectedly it is a large well laid out and furnished Sports Bar.  Those of you that read my reviews know that I am on the lookout for the best fresh fried shrimp Tampa Bay has to offer (though I have been limited to traveling the Brandon area of late), so I was interested in hitting this establishment because of the 35 fried shrimp dinner they advertise.  It is a special on Tuesdays, where the price is reduced by $1.50.  However, I splurged and went for a late lunch on Wednesday.
 
I entered and was seated at a table immediately.  The place was 95% empty, and there only seemed to be one server running around.  The menus are at the table, so the only thing my server did initially was to remove the 3 extra place settings and take my drink order.  Only Pepsi soft drinks here so I ordered a lemonade.  It was delivered rather quickly, and it tasted rather strange to me, but no other real choices I could make.,
 
I ordered the 35 shrimp dinner and substituted french fries for the coleslaw.  It took about 5 minutes and my dinner plate was delivered to my table.  For a 35 shrimp dinner I wasn't expecting jumbo shrimp, but neither was I expecting small to less than small shrimp.  As is the way with many places, these were small shrimp with oodles of breading to make them look larger.  These were obviously from a large restaurant supply frozen breaded and thrown into a fryer for a few minutes.  Nowhere near as good as if I had bought Mrs Pauls or SeaPak from my local grocery store and cooked them myself.  I really shouldn't have expected anything different.  I suppose now a days if you want passable food, you need to pick something off the menu that has to be prepared and cooked from fresh ingredients.  I didn't expect much for going in, and in that respect I wasn't disappointed.
 
My server was friendly and sporadically attentive.  My lemonade was refilled without having to ask, except for the time my glass sat empty for about 10 minutes as the staff were having some kind of discussion just outside the kitchen.  My server brought my check along with a Styrofoam cup of lemonade to go.  I was not asked if I wanted dessert, which I did not anyway.
 
If I was able to drink alcohol or liked a sports bar atmosphere this would probably be a good place to gather with friends and watch the game.  I will probably return again some quiet afternoon and try one of the things that takes some effort to cook.

3 stars for an upper scale sports bar, 1.5 stars for food and service.

Decided to stop by on a weekday afternoon at about 4 PM.  The restaurant was mostly empty, so I was greeted and seated rather quickly.  My server was friendly and pleasant and handed me a menu and took my drink order.
 
I decided (bet you can guess) on the fried shrimp platter.  My Coca Cola was delivered in a minute and the food was brought around 10 minutes later.  The shrimp tasted fresh, perfectly breaded, and perfectly cooked.  They were large shrimp and just delicious.  My side of fries was average.
 
For a rather empty restaurant my server could have stopped by a little more frequently to refill my soda.  I found the meal heavenly, if not a little expensive, though certainly worth it.  The next time I decide to splurge on lunch, the Crafty Crab will definitely be one of my top choices.
 
A well deserved 4 stars.  Slightly better service, slightly more shrimp, and slightly lower prices would have made this a 5 star review.

I realized I had a long expired Groupon coupon for Square 1 Burgers.  It was a good deal at the time, $8 for $16 of food.  But, your original spend part never expires, so it was still worth $8.  So I headed on over to Square 1 on Providence about 5 pm.
 
The place was very empty except for the bar, where there were several patrons.  The hostess tried to seat me in a both near the bar, but the music was so loud it was annoying.  In stead I asked for a booth as far away from the bar as possible, which was much more bearable.  My server came by quickly with a menu and place setting and took my drink order (no Coca Cola products, so water please).
 
I ordered the All-American burger, medium, blackened, and substituted cheddar cheese instead of the American Cheese, with the free side of fries.  In a bit over 10 minutes my order was brought to the table.  It was as ordered, except that my medium burger was overcooked for even a well done order, making it a bit dry and tough.  When the server came by several minutes later to ask how everything was, I showed her how well done the hamburger patty was.  To her credit she went and told the manager, who came by and offered to have another one cooked for me.  I declined, and the manager came back again in a few minutes to apologize once more and hand me a card for $10 off a future order.
 
It's been several years since I had been to Square 1, so I can't really say whether this is indicative of all their care in food preparation or not.  The French fries were a bit over cooked as well.  I have never made this particular complaint about a restaurant, but the water tasted kind of funky.
